11100219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100219.value: Cochlear implants (CI) enable many profoundly hearing impaired patients to understand speech, but they fall short of providing normal hearing in important respects. In particular CI users cannot process, so-called interaural time differences (ITDs) which arise when sound from one side arrives at one ear a fraction of a milisecond earlier than at the other. ITDs are an important cue to sound source direction. A lack of early binaural experience is often blamed for the inability of CI users to hear ITDs, but recently our lab has shown that neonatally deafened animals without any early hearing experience localise ITDs perfectly well when given precisely synchronised binaural electrical stimuli. Imagine a child recently implanted binaurally with CIs. She needs to pay close attention to amplitude modulation (AM) in sounds as she learns to process speech. At the same time, she also receives useful interaural level differences (ILDs) – another spatial cue more readily accessible with current CIs – which provide information about where the speech is coming from. This brings advantages of spatial attention, and even spatial unmasking (Hess et al. 2018), making hearing in background noise much easier. However, the ITDs delivered by current CIs are uninformative and incongruent with the ILDs. They are a nuisance factor that the child needs to learn to ignore. An insensitivity to ITDs is therefore probably not due to a lack of early experience, it may instead be actively acquired in response to inappropriate stimulation following implantation. We will test this hypothesis with experimental animals, to test whether these phenomena unfold as we have suggested here. We will compare experimental and control groups of neonatally deaf rats fitted with binaural CIs in young adulthood. Both groups will be trained in AM detection to train them in a key auditory skill which has been shown to be important for speech processing. One group will receive additional congruent ITD and ILD cues, as a normally hearing person would. The second group will receive informative ILDs but uninformative ITDs, replicating current clinical CI processors. We predict that, over a training period lasting several weeks, the animals receiving congruent ITDs will not just hone a high sensitivity to ITDs but also come to perform better at AM detection than the group with uninformative ITDs, which will lose their innate ability to process ITDs and learn more slowly. We will test these predictions with behaviour and electrophysiology experiments. 人工耳蝸植入（CI）非常有助於幫助深度聽力受損患者理解言語，但在某些重要方面遠遠不能正常聽力。尤其，CI用戶不能處理一類重要的空間線索：耳間時間差（ITD），即來自一側的聲音到達一隻耳朵和到達另一隻耳朵小於一微秒的時間差。CI用戶無法聽到ITD往往歸咎於缺乏早期的雙耳聽覺經驗，但最近我們的實驗室已經證明，在沒有任何早期聽力經驗的新生耳聾動物在給予精確同步的雙耳電刺激時完全可以很好地定位ITD。 想像一下，一個孩子最近進行CI雙耳植入。當她學會處理語音時，她需要密切關注聲音中的振幅調變（AM）。同時，她還獲得了有用的耳間水平差異（ILD） - 當前CI更容易獲得的另一個空間線索 - 提供有關語音來源的信息。這帶來了空間注意力的優勢，甚至能抵銷掩蔽效應（Hess et al., 2018）。然而，與正常聽力狀態不同，當前CI提供的ITD與ILD並不一致。相反，當前CI提供的ITD是一個令人困惑的麻煩因素，孩子需要學會忽視。因此，對ITD的不敏感性不是由於缺乏早期經驗，而是在植入後對於不適當的刺激的反應。 我們將複製剛剛描述的場景於實驗動物，以測試這些現像是否真的如我們在此處所建議的那樣產生。我們將比較在年輕成年期配有雙耳CI的新生耳聾大鼠實驗組和對照組。兩組都將接受AM檢測培訓，以培養他們的關鍵聽覺技能，這對於語音處理非常重要。一個小組將獲得一致的ITD和ILD提示，有如正常聽力。第二組將接收信息豐富的ILD但無意義的ITD，複製當前的臨床CI處理器。我們預測，在持續數週的培訓期間，接受一致ITD的動物不僅會對ITD具有高度敏感性，而且在AM檢測方面的表現也會優於對照組。接收無意義ITD信息的對照組將失去其天生的ITD處理能力， 學習亦比較慢。我們將通過行為和電生理學實驗來測試這些預測。

11100219.label: Realisation of objectives
11100219.value: The project objectives have been realized as planned and described in the original proposal. The results of the main study are described in detail in the draft manuscript entitled "Impaired binaural hearing in cochlear implant patients – Is it caused by lack of experience or inappropriate stimulation?" which is attached below. That manuscript requires some minor editing and polishing before submission for publication, likely by the end of July 2025 if not before. In addition to the main study described in the attached manuscript in preparation, we were also able to spin out a further paper documenting interaural level difference sensitivity in cochlear implanted rats which has been published in Scientific Reports, and to finalize publication of a major study into envelope and pulse timing ITD sensitivity which was partly supported by this grant and partly by another GRF funded project (11101020) in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Science (PNAS). We also published a review paper together with a number of other groups working in this area.

11100219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100219.value: bilateral CI users often struggle with spatial hearing, particularly in detecting interaural time differences (ITDs), a key cue for sound localization. This limitation is especially pronounced in individuals who are prelingually deaf. While biological factors may contribute, technical constraints of current clinical CI processors are increasingly recognized as a major cause. The devices predominantly encode sound through the amplitude envelope of electrical pulses, failing to preserve precise temporal information of the pulses. In this study, we investigated this issue using our established animal model of neonatally deafened, bilaterally CI supplied rats. In a two-cohort design, one cohort received informative pulse timing (PT) ITDs (PT+), while the other received randomized, non-informative PT ITDs (PT−), simulating standard clinical processors. Both groups were trained in an amplitude modulation detection task with passive exposure to ITDs and interaural level differences (ILDs). The rats achieved good AM detection thresholds, further supporting the utility of this model for studying CI hearing under behaviorally relevant conditions. PT+ rats consistently developed robust ITD sensitivity, while PT− rats displayed more variable sensitivity, with most rats initially showing low ITD sensitivity. However, following targeted ITD rehabilitation training, the PT− group exhibited marked improvements, ultimately reaching thresholds comparable to the PT+ group. A perceptual weighting task further revealed that PT− rats began relying more on ITDs after training, an effect not seen in PT+ animals. Overall, our findings suggest that ITD sensitivity may deteriorate or fail to develop behaviorally if bilateral CIs do not deliver informative PT cues. In contrast, when rats were provided with coherent and usable PT ITDs from the outset, they achieved good ITD sensitivity at clinically relevant stimulation rates. Importantly, targeted rehabilitation may not only enhance but also restore ITD sensitivity in CI users who initially lack access to meaningful temporal cues. Overall, the results support the hypothesis set out in the original research proposal and provide strong evidence that some of the poor outcomes in patients fitted with CIs are likely due to a form of mal-adaptation of their auditory pathways to stimulation patterns that fail to deliver accurate temporal fine structure information to the auditory nerve.

11100219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100219.value: This research strongly suggests that improving temporal coding in cochlear implants by aligning the timing of electrical stimulus pulses with temporal features of the sounds to be encoded is bound to lead to better patient outcomes. The next step required to build on this insight is to develop specific multi-channel coding strategies which realize such temporal coding without degrading place coding for spectral information. We will pursue this in follow-up projects in collaboration with academic partners in Germany and in the UK as well as with industry partners in Austria and China.

11100219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100219.value: The normal, healthy human ear analyses incoming sounds by systematically decomposing sound waves into vibrations of different frequencies along the length of the basilar membrane of the inner ear. The vibrations along the basilar membrane are then detected by microscopic "hair cells" which trigger neural impulses in the auditory nerve in lock step with the ebb and fall of the mechanical vibrations. The pattern of neural activity in the auditor nerve is therefore both "place coded" as nerve fibers from one end of the basilar membrane will respond to low frequencies and those from the other end to high frequencies, as well as temporally coded because the timing of nerve impulses become "phase locked" to temporal features of the sound waves with a precision of a few tens of microseconds Unfortunately, cochlear hair cells are easily irreperably damaged - a common cause of deafness. Cochlear implants bypass damaged hair cells with direct, place coded electrical stimulation, but they typically do not pay much attention to temporal coding. In this study we used animal experiments on rats to show that this failure to provide very precise temporal codes in cochlear implants likely leads to deficits such as poor binaural spatial hearing.

11100519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11100519.value: 神經系統損傷是導致運動功能障礙的主因之一，現今並無有效治療方案。與中樞神經系統（central nervous system；CNS）不同，周圍神經系統（peripheral nervous system；PNS）的周圍神經具有一定的再生能力，但其再生速率頗慢（每日1毫米左右）。人類的皮層脊髓束（CNS）及坐骨神經（PNS）包含長度超過1米的軸突。軸突（構成為神經）再生是一個需要極高能量的過程：需要將線粒體從細胞體運送至再生中的軸突，牽涉長距離的軸突運輸，其中局部能量消耗成為軸突再生成功的關鍵。 線粒體是神經元的能量泉源，並經常進行線粒體融合、裂變及雙向的軸突運輸。愈來愈多的研究顯示有缺陷的線粒體動態是各類神經系統損傷的常見病理機制，而與線粒體融合及裂變有關的基因突變與神經退行性疾病的發展有著密切關係。線粒體通常於沒有受傷的軸突是維持靜止狀態的，而快速的軸突運輸只能於再生中的軸突中觀察得到。大量的線粒體會於神經肌肉接頭聚集，而成功的肌肉神經再支配亦成了運動功能恢復的關鍵。於年輕的CNS神經元軸突上的線粒體具有高度的移動性，可進行雙向移動，以滿足生長中的細胞對能量的極高需求。不過，隨著神經軸突越趨成熟，線粒體的移動性亦因而減低。有關的研究構成了是次研究實驗假設的基礎：線粒體的低移動性與成年神經元的再生能力下降有著不可分割的關係，而提高線粒體的移動性可成為提高神經軸突再生的治療目標。 為了測試我們的實驗假設，我們首先證明一個已知與軸突再生有關的基因（regeneration-associated genes）熱休克蛋白-27 （heat shock protein 27；Hsp27）不僅加快神經軸突再生的速度，亦能提高線粒體的軸突運輸速率、增加線粒體的大小，及線粒體融合蛋白於再生中軸突的定位。我們亦證明一種能於市面購買的線粒線融合的激活劑M1可有效增加線粒體的大小及融合，以及提高線粒體於再生軸突尖端的軸突運輸速率。更重要的是，M1於體外細胞培植及體內實驗中顯著增加了受損PNS神經元的軸突再生速度。 此研究計劃旨在測試M1用於治療嚴重PNS及CNS神經損傷的醫療潛力。我們首先優化M1用於治療PNS神經損傷的治療模式，以測試M1能否於重覆周圍神經擠壓損傷（即嚴重周圍神經損傷）後促進功能恢復。我們亦會使用體外培植的視網膜神經節細胞（retinal ganglion cells）及體內視神經損傷的動物模型，以測試M1於中樞神經損傷的醫療潛力。最後，我們將會以活細胞成像去測試M1能否於損傷後保存PNS及CNS神經元的線粒體膜電位（mitochondrial membrane potential），用以闡明M1的潛在機理。是次研究旨在通過調節線粒體於再生軸突的動態，為建基於線粒體的治療發展提供見解，用以促進神經軸突再生及功能恢復。

11100519.label: Realisation of objectives
11100519.value: All Objectives were completed. Figures/References are attached in Part C/Section 11/Other Impact. We published the results generated from current GRF together with additional experiments in a prestigious Journal - Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) in 2022 (1). We performed additional experiments such as inflammatory responses after M1 treatment and sciatic nerve crush and optic nerve crush (ONC), ex vivo time-lapse imaging of mitochondria in sciatic nerve, tracing long-distance regenerating axon projections from optic chiasm to multiple subcortical visual targets after ONC, local field potential (LFP) recordings in the superior colliculus (SC) following optogenetic activation of channel rhodopsin-2 (ChR2)–transduced retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) after ONC, visual function tests including pupillary light reflex and looming visual stimuli, expression profile of key mitochondrial fusion proteins and axonal transport machinery proteins in the retina after M1 treatment, the identification of key mitochondrial fusion protein (AAV-shRNA knockdown experiments) that are responsible for the promoting effects of M1 after ONC, and synergistic effect of M1 with PTEN. M1 treatment enhanced the intrinsic growth capacity of injured DRG neurons (1-5) by promoting neurite outgrowth with its maximal effects at 2.5µM (44.2% increase) (Fig. 1A-C), without affecting cell survival (Fig. 1D). Direct application of M1 (20µg/day) onto the injury site significantly promoted (65.8%) in vivo axon regeneration after sciatic nerve crush (SNC) injury (1, 3, 5) by using sciatic nerve pinch test (Fig. 2A-B). The in vivo promoting effects of M1 were further validated by immunostaining of SCG10 (marker of regenerating axons) (1). We detected prominent SCG10 immunoreactivity in the far-distal region of injured sciatic nerve in M1-treated mice (Fig. 2C). By intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of M1 at 10-20mg/kg for 3 consecutive days after SNC (Fig. 2D), which induced maximal growth-promoting effect (increased by 48%) (Fig. 2E) to an extent that was similar to direct administration of M1 onto the injury site (Fig. 2B). Mice received i.p. injections of the optimal dose of M1 (15mg/kg) or vehicle for 21 consecutive days, sensory and motor functional recovery were evaluated on every alternate day post-SNC (Fig. 3A). In M1-treated mice, sensory function was fully recovered at day 17 post-SNC, 2 days earlier than vehicle-treated mice (Fig. 3B). M1-treated mice showed an early initial (reaching score 1) and full toe spreading reflex at day 16 and 21, respectively, which was 2 days earlier than vehicle-treated controls (Fig. 3C). M1 treatment did not alter immune cell profiles (Fig. 4) and gene/protein expression of inflammatory cytokines in injured DRGs (Figs. 5-6). In the central nervous system (CNS), M1-treated primary RGCs exhibited much longer neurite outgrowth than controls (Fig. 7). We then compared the promoting effects of M1 with one of the well-known RAGs such as Pten-/- (6, 7) and their synergistic effects in axon regeneration. M1 was intravitreally injected on a weekly basis due to a decline in the M1 availability in the retinae (Fig. 8). Cholera toxin subunit B (CTB) was injected intravitreally to anterograde label regenerating axons, and tissue-cleared optic nerve was then imaged with confocal microscopy (Fig. 9A). M1 treatment alone enhanced axon regeneration after ONC, and Pten deletion further enhanced the M1-induced optic nerve regeneration 2 weeks after ONC (Fig. 9B-C). M1 treatment significantly promoted RGC survival as evidenced by immunostaining of RBPMS (RGC marker) (Fig. 9D). More strikingly, M1 induced sustained and long-distance axon regeneration 4 weeks after ONC. In M1-treated mice, several CTB-positive regenerating axons regenerated the entire length of optic nerve and reached the optic chiasm (>4mm), While no axons could reach 4mm distal to the crushed site in vehicle-treated or Pten-/- mice (Fig. 10A-C). M1 treatment, Pten-/- or Pten-/- + M1 mice showed a significant increase in RGC survival (32-35%) (Fig. 10D). M1 sustained long-distance axon regeneration into different brain visual targets at 6-week post-ONC (Fig. 11A). In both M1-treated and Pten-/- + M1 mice, we observed substantial reinnervation of regenerated RGC axons into the hypothalamic suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) (Fig. 11B), optic tract (Fig. 11C), the ventral (Fig. 11D) and dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus (Fig. 10E), olivary pretectal nucleus (OPN) (Fig. 11F) and the brachium and zonal layer of SC (Fig. 11G). Quantification of CTB-positive regenerating axons confirmed the reinnervation of multiple visual targets (Fig. 11H). No CTB-positive regenerating axons were detected in controls (Fig. 12). To examine if M1 induced restoration of neural activity and visual function recovery, we performed LFP recordings at SC upon optogenetic activation of ChR2-transduced RGCs 6 weeks after ONC (8) (Fig. 13A). Upon focal laser stimulation to the AAV-ChR2-mCherry-transduced RGCs, M1-treated and Pten-/- + M1 mice showed a substantial increase in eye-evoked LFPs (82.1-97.2µV) vs controls (13.8±1.6µV) (Fig. 13B-C). Substantial innervation of regenerating axons into OPN and SC led to a restoration of visual functions such as pupillary light reflex (Fig. 13D-E) and looming response (Fig. 13F-G) in M1-treated and Pten-/- + M1 mice. We ruled out the possibility of intraocular inflammation in M1-induced CNS regeneration (Figs. 14-17). There were no spared axons beyond the crushed site after ONC (Fig. 18). M1 is a mitochondrial fusion promoter (9), we observed a 25% increase in mitochondrial size in axotomized DRG neurons after M1 treatment (Fig. 19A-B). M1 treatment promoted the localization of mitochondrial fusion proteins OPA1 and MFN2 towards the filopodial protrusions and colocalized with actin at the growth cones (Fig. 19C-E), and increased mRNA and protein expression of OPA1 and MFN2 (Fig. 19F-G). Next, we performed live-cell imaging on cultured DRG neurons stained with MitoTracker Red (Fig. 20A). Kymograph analysis of mitochondrial movement suggested that M1 enhanced the motile pool of mitochondria (Fig. 20B) without affecting mitochondrial density (Fig. 20C). M1 increased the time that mitochondria spent in motion (Fig. 20D). In M1-treated neurons, the average mitochondrial velocity was increased by 62.5% (Fig. 20E) and mRNA expression of key genes involved in anterograde and retrograde axonal transport were increased significantly (Fig. 20F). To visualize mitochondria, AAV2/9-mitoGFP expressing mitochondrial matrix-targeted green fluorescent protein was injected into the sciatic nerve and ex vivo time-lapse imaging was performed (Fig. 21A). We observed a 22.4% increase in mitochondrial size after M1 treatment (1.44±0.02µm) vs controls (1.17±0.02µm) (Fig. 21B-C). Kymograph analysis (Fig. 21D) revealed that M1 treatment increased the motile pool of mitochondria with no effects on mitochondrial density (Fig. 21E-F). M1 treatment led to an increase in the time the mitochondria spent in motion (Fig. 21G) and a 2.89-fold increase in the average mitochondrial velocity (Fig. 21H). Mechanistically, M1 up-regulated mRNA expression of key machinery for mitochondrial fusion (Opa1 and Mfn2) in the retina (Fig. 22A-B). We therefore silenced the gene expression of Opa1 and Mfn2 by intravitreal injections of AAV2-Opa1-shRNA or AAV2-Mfn2-shRNA (Fig. 22C). Intravitreal injections of AAV2-scrambled (scr)-shRNA (tagged with eGFP) preferentially transduced RGCs (Fig. 22D). Endogenous OPA1 and MFN2 were ubiquitously expressed in RGCs at ganglion cell layer, with limited expression of these proteins in other layers of retina (Fig. 22E-F). The mRNA expression of Opa1 or Mfn2 was markedly reduced (84.0-87.1%) in the retinae two weeks after intravitreal injections of AAV2-Opa1-shRNA or AAV2-Mfn2-shRNA (Fig. 22G-H). Silencing Opa1 or Mfn2 completely abolished the growth-promoting effects of M1, suggesting that Opa1 or Mfn2 is required for M1-induced axon regeneration (Fig. 23A-C) and RGC survival (Fig. 23D).

11100519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11100519.value: The current study demonstrated for the first time that M1 could promote long-distance axon regeneration after CNS injuries, the research team assessed the extent of axon regeneration in M1-treated mice at 4 weeks after injuries. Strikingly, most of the regenerating axons of M1-treated mice reached 4mm distal to the crush site (i.e., near optic chiasm), while no regenerating axons were found in vehicle-treated control mice. In M1-treated mice, the survival of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs, neurons that transmit visual stimuli from the eye to the brain) was significantly increased from 19% to 33% at 4 weeks after optic nerve injury. It exemplifies that the M1 treatment sustains long-distance axon regeneration from the optic chiasm, i.e., midway between the eyes and target brain region, to multiple subcortical visual targets in the brain. Regenerated axons elicit neural activities in target brain regions and restore visual functions after M1 treatment. To further explore whether M1 treatment is able to restore visual function, we challenged the M1-treated mice with pupillary light reflex test at 6 weeks after optic nerve injury. We found that the lesioned eyes of M1-treated mice restored pupil constriction response upon blue light illumination to a similar extent of the non-lesioned eyes, suggesting that M1 treatment is able to rescue pupil constriction response after optic nerve injuries. In addition, we assessed the response of mice to a looming stimulus, a visually induced innate defensive response to avoid predator. The mice were placed into an open chamber with a triangular prism-shaped shelter and a rapidly expanding overhead-black circle as a looming stimulus, and their freeze and escape behaviours were observed. Half of the M1-treated mice responded to the stimulus by hiding in shelter, showing that M1induced robust axon regeneration to reinnervate subcortical visual target brain regions for complete recovery of visual function. To this end, our proof-of-concept study has provided important preclinical evidence that mitochondria-based therapy is an attractive approach for repairing nerve injuries. One paper was published in a prestigious Journal - Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) in 2022. We presented the work at the largest Neuroscience Meeting in the US in 2020 (switched to online mode due to the pandemics). After completion of this study, we have filed a patent in the United States Patent and Trademark Office, entitled “Unraveling the therapeutic potential of a small molecule activator of mitochondrial fusion and mechanistic role of mitochondria in axon regeneration” (reference number US 63/081,371 with its filing date on 30 September 2020).

11100519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11100519.value: Currently, there are no effective therapeutic invention to improve clinical outcomes and to promote visual function recovery after optic nerve damage. Our study revealed that M1 could promote mitochondrial dynamics by increasing the mitochondrial length, motility, and transport velocity which induced robust axon regeneration and restoration of visual function in the adult mammalian CNS. Our findings also support the development of non-viral mitochondria-based therapeutic opportunities directed at modulating mitochondrial dynamics for sustained axon regeneration after CNS nerve injury, will spur new scientific investigation and help develop new therapeutic strategies. We hope that you share our excitement regarding this major transformation in our understanding of using a mitochondrial fusion promoter small molecule for treating nerve injuries. We have provided important preclinical evidence that readily available small molecule M1 could be used for further clinical trials. Several clinical studies demonstrated the feasibility of intravitreal administration of drugs in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration and retinitis pigmentosa. Administration of M1 might represent a viable and non-viral therapeutic strategy to promote CNS repair and thus further investigation is warranted to evaluate the potential clinical application of M1.

11100519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11100519.value: Long-distance axon regeneration and function recovery after injury to the adult mammalian central nervous system (CNS) remain challenging. Axons, which are cable-like structure that extends from a neuron, responsible for transmitting signals between neurons as well as different brain regions. The first step for successful axon regeneration is to form active growth cones and activation of regrowth programme such as synthesis and transport of materials to regrow axons. These are all energy-demanding processes, requiring an active transport of mitochondria (powerhouse of cells) into injured distal axons. Retinal ganglion cells in the CNS fail to regenerate their axons after optic nerve injury, resulting in permanent vision loss in patients. Here, we identified M1, that enabled long-distance axon regeneration through the entire length of optic nerve and reached multiple visual targets in the brain after optic nerve crush injury. Such robust axonal regeneration elicited neural activities in the most distal target brain region after optical stimulation, resulting in a complete recovery of pupillary light reflex upon light stimulation and restoration of response to looming visual stimuli (innate defensive behavior). Our study identified a small molecule that could offer hope for patients with optic nerve damages such as glaucoma-related vision loss.

11101019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101019.value: 多发性硬化症是中枢神经系统中最众所周知的脱髓鞘疾病，然而最近的研究发现，其他中枢神经系统疾病，如阿尔兹海默症，也存在脱髓鞘的现象。少突胶质细胞是一种神经胶质细胞，它们在轴突周围形成髓鞘从而绝缘化，以提高神经传导速度。如果少突胶质细胞受到大脑损伤的损害，则会诱导脱髓鞘，导致神经元活动的减少以及神经变性。然而，与神经变性不同的是，脱髓鞘伴随着自然修复机制，即髓鞘再生。越来越多的证据表明，位于脑室下区的成体神经干细胞会增殖并迁移到附近的脱髓鞘区域以响应脱髓鞘病变。然而，成体神经干细胞是如何识别脱髓鞘病变，迁移到病变区，并分化成少突胶质细胞？这在很大程度上是未知的。 我们在离体和体内实验中的初步数据显示，昼夜节律钟不仅在脱髓鞘病变区发生改变，而且在脑室下区也发生了变化。昼夜节律钟是一种内源性振荡器，存在于大多数细胞（包括少突胶质细胞）中，以产生从分子到行为层面的日常生物节律。分布于各个区域的昼夜节律钟，通过转录调控数千个时钟调节基因，来控制不同的细胞过程。我们观察到的有趣现象是，昼夜节律钟首先在脱髓鞘病变中改变，然后在脑室下区中的神经干细胞中变化，导致了脑室下区中的神经干细胞的增殖和迁移的增加。这暗示了脱髓鞘病变区中昼夜节律钟的改变与脑室下区中神经干细胞特性的改变有关。 根据我们的初步结果和以前的文献，我们假设脱髓鞘改变了病变区中的昼夜节律钟从而改变了一些细胞过程，这导致了信号传送到脑室下区引起神经干细胞特性的变化，以向脱髓鞘病变区提供干细胞从而启动髓鞘再生。为了测试这一点，我们将集中于两个主要目标：1）识别在脱髓鞘病变中依赖于变化的昼夜节律钟的细胞过程，这些细胞过程通过传递信号到脑室下区，以准备髓鞘再生；2）理解成体神经干细胞中的昼夜节律钟如何参与调控干细胞的特性。从这个项目中，我们将提供证据说明：不同神经细胞中昼夜节律钟的动态变化能通过神经细胞网络协调大脑功能。

11101019.label: Realisation of objectives
11101019.value: At the beginning of this study, we hypothesized that circadian clocks are altered in the demyelinated lesions to change cellular processes, and this sends signals to the SVZ to recruit adult neural stem cells (NSCs) to start remyelination. Based on our preliminary results, two major questions were raised to prove our hypothesis: 1) Which cellular processes are affected by the altered circadian clocks in the demyelinated lesions to recruit adult NSCs for remyelination? 2) How do circadian clocks in adult NSCs control stem cell properties to proliferate, migrate to the lesions, and differentiate into oligodendrocytes? To answer these questions, we designed five main experiments under Objectives 1 and 2. Objective 1: Identify the altered circadian clock-dependent cellular processes in the demyelinated lesions which send signals to the SVZ to prepare remyelination. Experiment 1) Identify cellular processes under the control of the circadian clock in the CC. As proposed, we performed bulk RNA-sequencing analysis in the corpus callosum (CC) of control and the circadian transcription factor Bmal1 knockout (BKO) mice. We identified multiple secretory molecules, such as Sfrp isoforms, as BMAL1 target genes in the CC and validated RNA-seq results in the same experimental condition by qRT-PCR. These results were presented in Figure 2A-C and Figure S2 of Huang et al. (please refer to https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108394). Experiment 2) Identify the altered circadian clock-dependent cellular processes in the demyelinated lesions. Multiple secretory molecules (including Sfrp isoforms) were identified as BMAL1 target genes in the CC, meaning circadian clocks are involved in cell-cell communications by secreting proteins. To prove this, we performed the proposed experiments in the CC of normal-diet and 4-week cuprizone-treated mice at different circadian times, CT02, 06, 10, 14, 18, and 22. We observed that the expression of secretory molecule Sfrp isoforms was induced in the demyelinated CC compared to control, and their expression oscillated across a circadian cycle. We also confirmed that circadian clocks in the CC were altered in the demyelinating lesions compared to the control. This supports that altered circadian clocks in the demyelinated CC induce the Sfrp expression, thereby communicating with other cells. These results were published in Figure 2 of Huang et al. (please refer to https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108394). Experiment 3) Examine whether the demyelinated CC sends signals to the SVZ to change circadian clocks in adult NSCs to prepare remyelination. The proposed experiments were performed to examine communications between the demyelinated CC and the subventricular zone (SVZ) of the lateral ventricle with in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo systems. BMAL1 activities were induced by altered circadian clocks in astrocytes of the demyelinated CC, followed by reduced BMAL1 levels in the SVZ. SFRP1/5 that are secreted by astrocytes in the demyelinated CC could mimic reduced SVZ BMAL1 levels by the demyelinated CC. Reduced SVZ BMAL1 resulted in increased oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) in the SVZ, and then OPCs migrated to the demyelinated CC to differentiate into oligodendrocytes. These results were published in Figures 3, 4, 5, and 6 of Huang et al. (please refer to https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108394). Objective 2: Understand how the circadian clock in adult NSCs is involved in controlling stem cell properties. Experiment 1) Examine the effects of Bmal1-/- on the proliferation and differentiation of adult NSCs. To examine BMAL1 effects on the proliferation and differentiation of NSCs, we performed the proposed experiments in not only demyelinating lesions but also neurodegenerative conditions, which affect BMAL1 levels in NSCs of the SVZ and the subgranular zone (SGZ) of the hippocampus. We found that reduced BMAL1 in NSCs of the SVZ and SGZ accelerated differentiation into oligodendrocytes and neurons. However, BMAL1 effects on cell proliferation were brain region-dependent: no effect on NSC proliferation in the SVZ but induced in the SGZ. These results were published in Figure 4 of Huang et al. (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108394) and Figures 2, 4, and 5 of Zhang et al. (please refer to https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2024.108829). Experiment 2) Further identify other cellular processes under the control of the circadian clock in the SVZ. We performed bulk RNA-sequencing analysis in the SVZ of wild-type and BKO mice. We identified cellular and molecular processes in signal transduction, mitochondrial respiratory chain, behavior, and translation as potential targets of circadian clocks in the SVZ. We also found that BMAL1 in hippocampal neurons is involved in the regulation of neuronal activity via communications between BMAL1 in the dentate gyrus, CA3, and CA1 neurons. These results were published in Figure S3 of Huang et al. (refer to https://doi.org/10.1016/j.celrep.2020.108394) and Figure 3 of Zhang et al. (please refer to https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2024.108829).

11101019.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101019.value: This project discovered that pathological conditions (demyelination and neurodegeneration) in the brain alter local circadian clocks in the lesions to signal NSCs of the SVZ and SGZ using in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo systems. Parts of the findings were published in Cell Reports in 2020 and iScience in 2024 (please refer to Part C: Research Output, 8, No. 1 and 2). In addition, we presented our findings at the international conference: the Society for Neuroscience (SfN) Global Connectome in 2021 and Society for Neuroscience 2023 (please refer to Part C: Research Output, 9, No. 1 and 2).

11101019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101019.value: This project identified molecular mechanisms controlling abnormal circadian clocks in brain pathological conditions (demyelination and neurodegeneration) with experimental systems in vitro and ex vivo. Then, we confirmed whether our findings were observed in animal models of demyelination and neurodegeneration. This strategy helps to facilitate the finding of reactive astrocyte roles and their related mechanisms in brain pathological conditions. Furthermore, we combined what we found from this project with our knowledge about circadian clocks in other central nervous system cell types from different projects in our lab. Understanding neural cell networks in physiological and pathological conditions is important, thereby helping to understand glial cell damage and neurodegeneration mechanisms and finding potential therapeutic targets and treatment strategies.

11101019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101019.value: All living organisms on the Earth show daily rhythms in various biological processes, such as a rest-activity cycle across a day and daily repeated sleep cycles. These rhythms, called circadian rhythms, are essential to orchestrate brain functions to maintain health. Although circadian rhythms show the same cycle as the Earth’s rotation, they are generated by endogenous molecular machinery called circadian clocks at the molecular and cellular levels rather than light-dark cycles from the environment. Most cells in our body have their own circadian clocks that produce thousands of proteins with daily rhythms. These proteins cooperate in running biological processes according to the times of the day. This study discovers that circadian clocks are dynamically changed in various brain cell types in response to insults, their consequences, and their effects on brain repair. So, this finding helps us understand how circadian clocks in brain cells are important for brain functions and how they work together to repair brain damage.

11101519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101519.value: RNA G-四鏈體（rG4）結構已顯示在基本生物過程中具有無數的功能和調節作用。最新發現揭示了非編碼RNA中rG4s的形成及其對基因調控和RNA代謝的影響，突出了研究rG4s在非編碼轉錄組中的重要性，並設計了靶向它們的分子工具。 rG4結構的知識 - 尤其是它們在非編碼轉錄組中的普遍性和位置，以及它們的結構特徵 - 是進一步探索rG4生物學和開發靶向和基因操作目的的新策略的兩個關鍵方面。 我們小組在研究rG4結構和功能方面有著悠久的歷史記錄。最近，我們揭示了前體和成熟microRNA中rG4s的形成，並證明了它們在microRNA生物發生和轉錄後調控中的作用。此外，我們開發了rG4-seq並將其應用於富含polyA的RNA，以鑑定人類轉錄組中的數千種rG4，其中一些來自長的非編碼RNA，如NEAT1和人端粒酶RNA（hTR）。在這個項目中，我們將改進rG4-seq以繪製人類非編碼轉錄組中的rG4s，開發可與rG4s選擇性相互作用的L-RNA適體，並研究使用L-RNA適體干擾rG4-的潛力。蛋白質相互作用以及基因活動。 與Ting Fung Chan教授合作，我們將調整我們最近開發的rG4-seeker來分析來自非編碼轉錄組的新rG4-seq數據，這將允許詳細檢查非編碼RNA中的rG4結構基序。 一種特異性感興趣的rG4候選物位於hTR的5'末端，這是與端粒維持和癌症相關的RNA。使用生物物理和生物化學測定的組合，將表徵hTR rG4的結構特徵及其與L-RNA適體的相互作用。 與Julian Tanner教授合作，我們將優化L-RNA適體選擇方法，分離可與hTR中的rG4結合的適體，並測試它們對乾擾rG4-蛋白結合和基因活性的影響。還將研究如上所述的非編碼RNA中的其他有趣的rG4。 通過結合我們的跨學科專業知識和獨特經驗，我們將揭示rG4s在非編碼轉錄組中的全部功能，揭示針對rG4s的新策略，以及將為rG4在非編碼RNA中的作用提供有價值見解的重要發現，進一步提升我們對rG4生物學的認識。

11101519.label: Realisation of objectives
11101519.value: We have successfully achieved the project objectives and reported original research findings, and in addition to that, during the course of this project period, we have obtained new research insights that led us to explore a few associated ideas on RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s) (see section 6.1), which altogether yielded a number of high-quality research outputs, and these results are useful for further development of the research in our lab and the related research communities (See section 6.2). In summary, we have published 33 publications, including papers in prestigious journals including Nature Communications (IF 16.6), Nature Protocol (IF 14.8), Nucleic Acids Research (IF 14.9), Angewandte Chemie International Edition (IF 16.6), JACS (IF 15.0), Genome Biology (IF 12.3), ACS Applied Materials and Interfaces (IF 9.5), Briefings in Bioinformatics (IF 9.5), Cell Reports (IF 8.8), Analytical Chemistry (IF 7.4), etc. Moreover, several awards/patents have been received, several invited talks have been given, a few PhDs and undergraduate have been mentored, strong collaboration networks have been established with top institutions in Hong Kong and around the globe, and we have received some press and media coverage (see part C). With regards to research findings and realization of objectives, we have performed rG4 mapping and analyzed transcriptome-wide rG4-seq experimental data, and examined the formation and roles of rG4 on non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) and messenger RNAs (mRNAs). Also, we have developed tools to target some of these functionally important rG4s. Moreover, we worked on transcript-specific assays, and we reported an experimental protocol describing in detail the procedures involved in the preparation of in vitro transcribed RNAs, buffers, and reagents for RTS and SHALiPE assays, as well as performing RTS and SHALiPE assays, to examine the formation of rG4 and reveal the rG4 structural conformation at nucleotide resolution in vitro. Regarding the transcriptome-wide mapping of rG4, we improved the outcomes and false-positive discrimination in rG4-seq experiments using a bioinformatic approach. By establishing connections between rG4-seq library preparation chemistry and the underlying properties of sequencing data, we identified how to mitigate indigenous sampling errors and background noise in rG4-seq. We applied these findings to develop a novel bioinformatics pipeline named rG4-seeker, which uses tailored noise models to autonomously assess and optimize rG4 detections in a replicate-independent manner. Using rG4-seeker, we identified novel features in rG4 formation that were missed previously. More recently, we developed rG4-seq 2.0 by introducing a new ssDNA adapter containing deoxyuridine during library preparation to enhance library quality with no gel purification step, less PCR amplification cycles and higher yield of PCR products. We demonstrated that rG4-seq 2.0 produces high-quality cDNA libraries that support reliable and reproducible rG4 identification at varying RNA inputs, including RNA mounts as low as 10 ng. rG4-seq 2.0 also improved the rG4-seq calling outcome and nucleotide bias in rG4 detection persistent in rG4-seq 1.0. We further provided in vitro mapping of rG4 in the HEK293T cell line, and recommendations for assessing RNA input and sequencing depth for individual rG4 studies based on transcript abundance. Overall, refined transcriptome-wide G4-ome methods with low input RNA requirement, as well as improved bioinformatics analysis pipelines have been developed, which will facilitate the investigation of the landscape of RNA structure elements and dynamics of G4 motifs in human and other species. We have applied these methodologies to study the rG4s in different species, including human, mouse, plant, bacteria, and plasmodium. In particular, we investigated the formation and role of rG4s in ncRNAs. Using comparative sequence and biophysical analysis, we reported that MALAT1 lncRNA contains conserved rG4 motifs, forming thermostable rG4 structures with parallel topology. We also showed that rG4s in MALAT1 lncRNA can interact with NONO protein with high specificity and affinity in vitro and in nuclear cell lysate, and we also provided cellular data to support that NONO protein recognizes MALAT1 lncRNA via rG4 motifs. Notably, we demonstrated that rG4s in MALAT1 lncRNA can be targeted by the rG4-specific small molecule, peptide, and L-aptamer, leading to the dissociation of MALAT1 rG4-NONO protein interaction. Altogether, this study uncovered new and important rG4s in MALAT1 lncRNAs, revealed their specific interactions with NONO protein, offered multiple strategies for targeting MALAT1 and its RNA–protein complex via its rG4 structure, and illustrated the prevalence and significance of rG4s in ncRNAs. Also, by using computational prediction, we found a dozen of rG4s were identified in lncRNAs, providing lncRNAs rG4 candidates for future studies. Besides long ncRNAs, we also studied the formation and role of rG4s in microRNAs. We identified and characterized an RNA G-quadruplex (rG4) structure motif in the human microRNA 638 (hsa-miR-638). We investigated the formation and role of this rG4 in vitro and in cells, and revealed that it inhibited the miR-638 and MEF2C messenger RNA interaction and controls gene expression at the translational level. This novel finding highlights the significance of rG4 structures in miRNAs as critical modulators of gene expression, and using computational prediction, we reported a hundred of rG4s were identified in miRNAs, providing miRNA rG4 candidates for future examination. We presented a novel method rG4-SELEX to identify rG4-specific binders that can effectively suppress rG4–peptide and rG4–protein associations. Using rG4-SELEX, we were able to develop L-RNA aptamer that can specifically bind to G4 target of interest, and interfere with G4-mediated association and gene activity. Notably, we have developed L-Apt.3-7, L-Apt.4-1c to target TERRA rG4 and hTERC rG4 respectively. For L-Apt.3-7, the aptamer was shown to be selective to TERRA rG4 but not to other G4s or non-G4 tested. For L-Apt.4-1c, it was reported to be generally selective to many of the rG4s tested, but not to dG4s and non-G4s. As such, both L-aptamers have utilities for different applications. For example, we have demonstrated that rG4s in MALAT1 lncRNA can be targeted by the rG4-specific L-RNA aptamer L-Apt.4-1c, leading to the dissociation of MALAT1 rG4-NONO protein interaction. In a separate study, we have developed a novel L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt.8f that strongly and specifically recognizes the APP 3’UTR rG4 motif, which in turn suppressed the APP reporter gene and native transcript translation in cells. This result showcased the potential of controlling APP gene expression via targeting the 3’UTR rG4 motif. Other new L-aptamers were also developed to improve the binding properties, biostability, as well as the target diversity.

11101519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101519.value: The major findings and research outcome are as follows: We have developed a bioinformatics pipeline named rG4-seeker. Using rG4-seeker, we identified novel features in rG4 formation that were missed previously. This work was published in RNA biology (IF 4.1). Also, we developed rG4-seq 2.0 by introducing a new ssDNA adapter containing deoxyuridine during library preparation. We further provided mapping of rG4 in HEK293T cells. This work was published in BMC biology (IF 5.4). We have applied these methodologies to study the formation and role of rG4s in different species. Those works were published in Nature Communications (IF 16.6), Genome Biology (IF 12.3) , Angewandte Chemie (IF 16.6) , mbio (IF 6.4) , Nucleic Acids Research (IF 14.9), Cell Reports (IF 8.8). We identified rG4s in long non-coding RNA MALAT1, revealed their interactions with NONO protein, and offered multiple strategies for targeting MALAT1 and its RNA–protein complex. This work was published in Nucleic Acid Research (IF 14.9). We also identified and characterized an rG4 in the human microRNA 638 (hsa-miR-638), and revealed that it inhibited the miR-638 and MEF2C messenger RNA interaction and controls gene expression at the translational level. This work was published in Chemical Communication (IF 4.9). We introduced rG4-SELEX to identify rG4-specific binders. Using rG4-SELEX, we developed L-RNA aptamer that can specifically bind to G4 target of interest, and interfere with G4-mediated association and gene activity. These works were published in Angewandte Chemie (IF 16.6), Nucleic Acids Research (IF 14.9), Nature Protocols (IF 14.8). Moreover, we have developed another L-RNA aptamer that recognizes the APP rG4, which in turn suppressed the APP translation in cells. Other new L-aptamers were developed to improve the binding properties, biostability, as well as the target diversity. These works were published in Nucleic Acids Research (IF 14.9). Our findings and reputations have attracted journals to invite us to write reviews, and we have highlighted the above-mentioned major findings and acknowledged the RGC funding in them, including Trends in Biotechnology (IF 17.3), Nucleic Acid Research (IF 14.9), Science China Life Sciences (IF 9.1), etc. All info can be found in part C. Other relevant research activities: We have also published other research articles, including Nature Communications (IF 16.6), JACS (IF 15.0), Briefing in Bioinformatics (IF 9.5), and etc, on research topics that are relevant to this project, and acknowledged the RGC funding. All info can be found in part C.

11101519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101519.value: There are at least 3 potentials for further development of the research. First, we have identified hundreds of rG4s in the ncRNAs, however, only a handful of cases were studied so far. In the near future, we will investigate other rG4s in the ncRNA on our list and explore their formation and role in cells. Also, we plan to examine the protein interacting partners of MALAT1 rG4 and decipher the molecular basis of this rG4-mediated regulatory mechanism. Similarly, other ncRNA rG4s can be explored and investigated using the strategies we developed. Second, we have showcased ncRNAs such as lncRNA, miRNA rG4 examples from this project, and next we plan to investigate more rG4 candidates in mRNAs as well, and examine their effect on translation, splicing, protein interacting partners and their underlying biochemical mechanisms. Last, with these rG4 being demonstrated to have a critical role in cells, we plan to develop novel rG4 targeting toolsets such as rG4 targeting L-aptamers and peptides to achieve gene control via selective recognition of the rG4 of interest. These are ongoing research in my laboratory, and once promising preliminary data are generated, we will apply for funding support in RGC and other agencies.

11101519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101519.value: G-rich sequences in RNA can form special structure motifs referred as RNA G-quadruplexes (rG4s), and in this research project, we have investigated rG4s in non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) such as long ncRNAs and microRNAs (miRNAs). We have first developed transcript-specific and transcriptome-wide methods to map rG4s, and illustrated their formation and roles in human, mouse, plant, bacteria and plasmodium. As some of these ncRNAs, such as MALAT1, and miR-638 rG4, are associated with human diseases such as cancers, these findings supported that ncRNA rG4s can be an important RNA structural element to regulate biological functions such as gene regulation, and rG4s in ncRNA can be a promising drug target for preventing and controlling disease development. We also developed new methods and reported rG4-targeting L-RNA aptamer tools to recognize rG4 of interest, and these L-RNA aptamers can interfere with rG4-protein interactions and control rG4-mediated gene expression. As research on rG4 is currently underexplored, our original data open new doors for future studying and understanding of rG4s’ functions in biology and diseases, which will stimulate further development in biological and biomedical applications.

11101619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101619.value: Pseudomonas syringae, the leading cause of crop diseases world-wide, uses type III secretion system (T3SS) to invade host plants. T3SS of plant pathogenic bacteria is induced in the plant and minimal media (MM). Although a number of components regulating the T3SS gene expression have been identified, how bacteria sense the environmental conditions and further transduce the signal(s) to the known regulatory components remain largely unknown. We have recently found a novel protease system RhpPC as a major regulator of T3SS in P. syringae. In our previous studies, we found that RhpPC was localized to the cytoplasm and regulated the in vivo protein level of HrpL, a key regulator of the T3SS genes. We also have done a transposon-insertion mutant screening, and identified osmolarity-sensing two-component system histidine kinase EnvZ as a regulator of rhpPC. We propose a novel signaling pathway of osmolarity-EnvZ-OmpR-RhpPC-HrpL-T3SS, whose verification is the focus of the proposal. Genetic and biochemical characterizations of RhpPC-pathway is the first step toward identifying signals to which the T3SS responds, and toward the development of new strategies for disease control based on T3SS manipulation. Our long-term goal is to leverage the outcomes of the herein proposed studies to develop better therapies against P. syringae infection. 丁香假單胞菌（Pseudomonas syringae）是全世界範圍內農作物最重要致的致病菌之一。丁香假單胞菌使用類似於注射器狀結構的三型分泌系統（type III secretion system，T3SS）對宿主植物進行侵染，進而造成巨大的經濟損失。植物病原菌的T3SS在植物和基本培養基（minimal media，MM）中被顯著誘導表達。儘管調控T3SS基因表達的很多調節組分已經被確定，但是細菌是如何感受外部環境變化以及如何进一步将信号傳遞到已知的调控元件仍然未知。我們最新發現了一套新的蛋白酶系統RhpPC,其可以做為丁香假單胞菌的一個主要的調節子。在前期研究中，我們發現RhpPC存在於細胞質中，而且可調控體內T3SS關鍵調控蛋白HrpL的蛋白表達水平。我們通過轉座子插入突變的篩選方法篩選到了滲透壓感受雙組分系統（EnvZ/OmpR）中的組氨酸激酶EnvZ可以作為rhpPC基因的一個重要調節子。我們提出了一條新的信號調控途徑：滲透壓-EnvZ-OmpR-RhpPC-HrpL-T3SS。RhpPC調控途徑的遺傳學和生物化學表征是確定T3SS感受信號的第一步，該研究將為开发由T3SS引起的疾病控制提供新的研究策略。我們的長期目標是利用本研究方案提出的研究結果开发更好的治疗方法，以对抗丁香假單胞菌感染。

11101619.label: Realisation of objectives
11101619.value: Objective 1: To determine if RhpP directly degrade HrpL to repress T3SS. RhpP acts as a protease and directly degrades HrpL protein, the master regulator of T3SS, and that RhpC inhibits the protease activity of RhpP. We have shown that a lower level of HrpL protein in the ΔrhpC mutant than in ΔrhpP and ΔrhpPC strains, which is consistent with the lower T3SS gene expression in this strain. To explore if the reduced level of HrpL protein in the ΔrhpC mutant could be due to degradation of HrpL by RhpP, we purify HrpL-FLAG and RhpP-FLAG. In the presence of PBS buffer only, HrpL-FLAG is stable. However, the level of HrpL-FLAG is significantly reduced after incubation with RhpP-FLAG. The reduction of HrpL-FLAG is much suppressed when EDTA, a metalloprotease inhibitor, is added with RhpP-FLAG, or when HrpL-FLAG was incubated with RhpPH279T, a RhpP mutant of the protease active site. These results indicate that RhpP is an active metalloprotease for HrpL. Co-incubation of RhpC with RhpP stabilizes the HrpL-FLAG protein, indicating that RhpC blocks the RhpP protease activity. Objective 2: To examine whether rhpPC is directly regulated by EnvZ/OmpR and osmolarity. OmpR directly binds to the promoter of rhpPC and regulates its transcription. We have proved that many T3SS genes are up-regulated in ΔenvZ, which is consistent with the negative role of RhpPC in T3SS. Osmolarity also regulates rhpPC. In addition, another transcription factor PSPPH_3618 can also directly interacts with the promoter of rhpPC operon. The transcriptional level of rhpP is significantly lower in ∆PSPPH_3618 than in the wild-type strain in KB and MM. PSPPH_3618 is functionally crucial in bacterial virulence, possibly through its implication in modulating T3SS genes, the rhpPC operon and a T3SS effector AvrB2 known to enhance bacterial virulence. Objective 3: To study what is the structural basis of the regulatory function of RhpP and RhpC. We found that when RhpP is present alone in the phaseolicola pathovar (Psph). It interferes with the induction of the T3SS genes and bacterial virulence, and the presence of RhpC represses the negative effect of RhpP. The rhpP-FLAG gene expressed by the pHM1 plasmid produces stronger protein signal in the WT Psph strain than in the ΔrhpC mutant, suggesting that RhpC stabilizes RhpP in the bacterium. To explore whether RhpC physically interacts with RhpP, we perform protein pull-down assay and find that RhpP-FLAG is specifically pulled down by RhpC-GST. Mutation of the active sites of RhpP does not interrupt the interaction with RhpC and has no effect on the RhpP protein translocation to the periplasm. In addition, RhpC consists of 99 amino acids that form a clear secondary structure of β-β-α-β-β-β-α and four long β-sheets are antiparallel in space. Due to its stable secondary structure and antiparallel β-segments, the protein is stable and forms a binding surface for interaction with other molecules such as ligands, proteins, or nucleic acids. RhpP is a bigger protein which consist of 356 amino acids, whose secondary structure is more complicated and has 9 α-helixes. The protein showes highly similarity to peptidase family M4, which has the ability of metalloendopeptidase.

11101619.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101619.value: The type III secretion system (T3SS) is a key determinant of the virulence of the model plant pathogen P. syringae. Here, we identify the bicistronic genes in the rhpPC locus of Psph act in a coordinated manner in regulating the T3SS gene expression and pathogenicity. rhpP encodes a metalloprotease that can directly degrade the key T3SS regulator protein HrpL. rhpC encodes a chaperone that directly inhibits the RhpP activity and mediates translocation of RhpP to the periplasm. In addition, we found a new master regulater, PSPPH_3618, which can regulate T3SS by modulating T3SS genes, such as the rhpPC operon and a T3SS effector AvrB2 known to enhance bacterial virulence. The coordination between rhpP and rhpC reveals a new mechanism regulating bacterial pathogenicity and may provide an important target for controlling bacterial pathogens.

11101619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101619.value: Since rhpPC is important in regulating T3SS, its upstream signaling pathway is key to fully understand the RhpPC-mediated regulation of T3SS. To further understand the upstream signaling pathway of rhpPC in P. syringae, we will try to find more regulators that can directly regulate the rhpPC operon. To test this, we will perform a in vivo pull-down assay using the rhpPC promoter following mass spec analysis. We predict that this/these regulator(s) can be important factor(s) for P. syringae virulence, which will be tested in field study in the future. Although EnvZ/OmpR have been characterized as a key osmolarity-sensing TCS in E. coli and other bacterial species, their role in P. syringae is still unknown. We plan to test if envZ is important to sense osmolarity in P. syringae. We expect that EnvZ senses osmolarity signal and then regulates rhpPC, which responds to osmolaric changes. RhpP is induced by high osmolarity, thus degrading HrpL and inhibiting T3SS. Based on all the results, we can further understand the molecular mechanism of RhpPC-mediated signaling pathway of T3SS in P. syringae.

11101619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101619.value: P. syringae is the causal agent of bacterial speck disease in many staple crops and fruits worldwide, leading to a reduction in yield of up to 80% in severely affected regions. Many plant bacterial pathogens including Pseudomonas species, utilize the T3SS to deliver effector proteins into plant cells. In this study, we discovered that the bicistronic genes in the rhpPC locus of Psph act coordinately to regulate the T3SS gene expression and pathogenicity. We also revealed that RhpP directly degrades the key T3SS regulator protein HrpL. As a master T3SS regulator, PSPPH_3618 plays a crucial role in regulating the virulence of P. syringae. Our research not only showed a new and key regulatory mechanism of T3SS, but also provided new insights to leverage the outcomes of the herein proposed studies to develop better therapies against P. syringae infection.

11101919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11101919.value: 當細胞開始生長並以不受控制的方式分裂時，癌症就會出現。最近的基因組學研究表明，癌基因和腫瘤抑制基因的體細胞拷貝數改變和DNA突變是腫瘤發生的關鍵驅動因素。有趣的是，在許多類型的癌症中也發現了編碼染色質修飾因子和表觀遺傳因子的基因中的大量突變，突出了表觀遺傳學在癌症發展中的關鍵作用。 我們之前已經闡明了驅動突變的作用;小兒腦癌中組蛋白H3 K27-to-M錯義突變。 H3K27M突變體組蛋白表現出顯性負效應，其抑制賴氨酸27處H3的二甲基化和三甲基化，導致基因表達的顯著變化，包括腫瘤抑制因子p16INK4a的表觀遺傳沉默。為了探究額外的組蛋白突變是否可能在其他疾病中發揮作用，我們分析了“癌症基因組圖譜”（TCGA）和“cBioPortal”數據庫，並在包括乳腺癌在內的一些癌症中鑑定出組蛋白H2B E76-to-K錯義突變。肺癌。 H2B的谷氨酸76（H2BE76）在酵母與人之間是進化上保守的，並且人核小體的結構分析顯示H2B E76殘基是其與組蛋白H4的直接組蛋白間相互作用所必需的。在293T中使用瞬時轉染方法我們的共免疫沉澱測定證實H2BE76K突變削弱了H2B與組蛋白H4之間的相互作用。有趣的是，我們還發現這種突變顯著增加了H2B與組蛋白伴侶NAP1L1 / 2的結合，但減少了與SPT16的相互作用。為了在生理水平表達突變組蛋白並模擬患者情況，我們使用CRISPR-Cas9方法並敲除乳腺癌細胞系MDA-MB-231和MCF7中的H2BE76K突變。我們的細胞分級分析和單核小體IP顯示，E76K突變改變了H2B的核輸入和沈積到染色質。此外，與同基因野生型CRISPR對照相比，表達H2BE76K的CRISPR敲入系具有增加的集落形成和細胞遷移能力。更重要的是，我們的RNA-seq數據揭示了H2BE76K突變細胞中300個差異表達的基因。基因本體分析表明，許多這些基因與癌症途徑有關，進一步支持了H2BE76K突變可能在癌症中發揮關鍵作用的觀點。有趣的是，我們發現表達H2BE76K突變組蛋白的細胞對酵母模型中的DNA損傷劑和DNA複製抑製劑敏感。該數據顯示，除了改變癌症途徑中基因的表達外，H2BE76K突變還可能導致基因組不穩定並可能進一步推動癌症進展。 我們假設H2BE76K是癌症的驅動突變之一，它通過改變染色質上的生物活性：DNA複製，轉錄和DNA損傷修復。在該提議中，我們的目的是確定這種突變如何影響染色質功能並破譯癌症中H2BE76K突變的機制。我們的目標是1）闡明H2BE76K對H2B核小體位置和轉錄的影響，2）研究H2BE76K在DNA損傷修復和DNA複製中的作用3）解讀造成H2BE76K表達細胞致癌特性的基因和途徑。 通過完成該項目，我們將揭示癌症中H2BE76K突變的臨床相關性和分子機制，並通過將基因突變和表觀遺傳基因調控與癌症發展聯繫起來，在該領域取得重大突破。從這項工作中獲得的知識將轉化為治療患有這種錯義突變的患者的新策略的發展。

11101919.label: Realisation of objectives
11101919.value: Objective 1) Elucidate the effect of H2BE76K on transcription We first employed the CRISPR-Cas9 technique to knockin the E76K mutation with a FLAG tag in the H2BO gene of breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231. After validation and confirmation of the clones by Sanger sequencing and western blot we selected two H2BE76K knockin lines and two wildtype isogenic control lines for all the subsequently experiments. We first performed FLAG CUT&RUN sequencing to investigate the genomic distribution of the E76K mutant H2B. Our data showed that the gene body localization of the E76K mutant H2B is significantly higher than the wildtype H2B, while the intergenic and promoter enrichment is reduced by the H2BE76K mutation. We further performed RNA-seq and correlated the RNA-seq results with the FLAG CUT&RUN data. Our Gene Set Enrichment Analysis results showed that the genes enriched with the E76K mutant H2B are correlated with higher gene expression, indicating the effect of H2BE76K mutation on gene expression. We further performed a transcription elongation assay to investigate the effect of the E76K mutation on the transcription elongation rate of one of the E76K-H2B target genes "ADAM19". We treated the E76K mutants and wildtype cells with DRB (POL2 inhibitor) and then released the cells into fresh medium. Total RNAs were collected at various time points and RT-qPCR were performed to determine the amount of pre-mRNA of ADAM19. We examined multiple intron-exon junctions of ADAM19 and our results demonstrated that the amount of ADAM19 pre-mRNA is higher in E76K mutant cells compared to isogenic wildtype controls. A control gene "TMEM241, with similar gene size but is not a target of the E76K-mutant H2B, did not show difference in transcription elongation between wildtype and E76K mutant cells. These results demonstrated the positive effect of H2BE76K on transcription. We have completed (100%) the objective #1. Objective 2) Investigate the effect of H2BE76K in DNA damage repair and DNA replication Using the CRISPR-Cas9 generated H2BE76K knockin cell lines we first treated the cells with various DNA damage agents including camphothecin (CPT) and methyl methanesulfonate (MMS) at different time points and collected the cells and lysates for immunofluorescence and western blotting analysis. We detected the protein levels of DNA damage markers gamma-H2AX and 53BP1 and we did not see difference between wildtype and E76K mutant cells upon DNA damage induction. Our gamma-H2AX and 53BP1 immunofluorescence staining also did not reveal significant difference between wildtype and E76K mutant cells, these data suggested that the H2BE76K mutation does not affect the DNA damage repair. To test the effect of H2BE76K mutation of DNA replication we treated the cells with thymidine analog 5-bromo-2 deoxyuridine (BrdU). We pulse-labeled the cells with BrdU for 1hour and the fixed the cells and denature the double-stranded DNA for immunofluorescence staining. We used the anti-BrdU antibodies for the detection of the incorporation of BrdU in the genome and our data revealed that there is no significant difference between wildtype and E76K mutant cells on DNA replication. These results collectively revealed that the H2BE76K mutation has no significant effect on DNA damage repair and DNA replication. Though the data is negative, we have completed (100%) the objective #2 and proved that the H2BE76K mutation mainly alters gene transcription but not other biological activities on the chromatin (see objective #1 and #3). Objective 3) Decipher the genes and pathways that are responsible for the oncogenic properties in H2BE76K expressing cells Based on the RNA-seq and CUT&RUN sequencing data from objective #1, we have identified dozens of genes that have the enrichment of the E76K-mutant H2B in the gene body. Among these candidate genes we focused on ADAM19 (A Disintegrin And Metalloproteinase 19), an enzyme which has previously shown important in remodeling of the extracellular matrix and cell-cell / cell-matrix interactions. However, the role of ADAM19 in breast cancer is not well documented. We performed oncogenic assays on our H2BE76K mutant cells and compared with the isogenic wildtype control cells. We showed that while the cell proliferation and cell migration ability is not changed in the E76K mutant cells, the H2BE76K mutation significantly increased the colony formation ability. ADAM19 is overexpressed (>2-fold) in the E76K mutant cells and the knockdown of ADAM19 in the E76K mutant cells significantly reduced the colony sizes of the E76K mutant cells. Interestingly however, the sizes of the colonies of the ADAM19 knockdown - E76K mutant cells are still larger than those of the wildtype isogenic control cells. On the other hand, the overexpression of ADAM19 increased the colony formation ability of the wildtype cells, indicating the functional significance of the expression of ADAM19 in controlling the colony formation property of breast cancer cells. We have also tested other E76K target genes such as PAK1 and TRPS1, which are known breast cancer drivers. The knockdown of PAK1 and TRPS1 severely affected the viability and thus the colony formation ability of both the wildtype and E76K mutant cells. These results revealed that the H2BE76K mutation affects the oncogenic properties of breast cancer cells through multiple genes and pathways. We have completed (100%) the objective #3. Most of the above results have been published in a research article in Journal of Biological Chemistry in 2021.

11101919.label: Major findings and research outcome
11101919.value: We have elucidated the effect of the H2BE76K mutation on gene transcription, DNA damage repair and deciphered the mechanisms by which the mutation increased oncogenic properties through altering gene expression. We employed the CRISPR-Cas9 approach to knockin the FLAG-tagged H2BE76K in a breast cancer cell line MDA-MB-231. Using the E76K mutant cells and the isogenic wildtype control cells our FLAG CUT&RUN sequencing data revealed a specific genomic distribution of the E76K mutant H2B which is significantly enriched in the gene body compared to intergenic regions. Genes enriched with the E76K mutant H2B had elevated gene expression in and are enriched in various cancer pathways. The knockdown of one of the H2BE76K mutant genes, ADAM19, reduced the colony formation ability of the mutant cells while overexpression of ADAM19 elevated the colony formation in wildtype MDA-MB-231 cells. We further showed that the presence of E76K mutant H2B increased the transcription elongation of ADAM19, revealing a role of the H2BE76K mutation on gene expression. Though the H2BE76K mutation does not affect DNA damage repair, our results indicated that the H2BE76K mutation might affect the development of breast cancer via modulating the expression of target genes and subsequently cancer properties. The above data was published in journal "Journal of Biological Chemistry" in 2021. We have completed all the 3 proposed objectives.

11101919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11101919.value: Based on the findings generated from this funded project, we are currently investigating how the E76K-mutant H2B is deposited to the genome at specific regions. We are also performing a CRISPR-Cas9 genome wide gRNA screening to identify gene targets that are essential to the E76K mutant cells. Furthermore, we have generated a H2BE76K gene knockin mice. This knockin model will be crossed with breast cancer mouse model (e.g. MMTV-Neu / MMTV- PyMT) to elucidate the effect of the H2BE76K mutation in cancer development in vivo. Data generated from the above on going experiments will be used for applying another GRF grant in the future.

11101919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11101919.value: The histone H2B gene was found frequently mutated at position E76-to-K in breast and lung cancers. This H2BE76K mutation weakens the stability of nucleosomes, alters gene expression and promotes colony formation. Using breast cancer cells expressing the E76K mutant protein as system we showed that the E76K mutant H2B has specific genomic distribution and genes enriched with the E76K mutant H2B proteins have elevated expression. The depletion of one of the E76K target genes, ADAM19, resulted in reduction of colony formation ability in breast cancer cells. Collectively, our data demonstrated the effect of H2BE76K mutation in cancer property and our work provided a foundation for the future development of therapeutics for patients harboring the H2BE76K mutation.

11102119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102119.value: RNase III is a family of endoribonuclease specific for double-stranded RNAs (dsRNAs). RNase III class gene is ubiquitously present and plays critical roles in important cellular pathways e.g. RNAi in eukaryotes and CRISPR in bacteria. In bacteria, RNase III could cleave both structured single-stranded RNAs and long dsRNAs formed by intermolecular base pairing of overlapping sense and antisense transcripts. The later function is starting to be appreciated because wide-spread and often low abundant antisense RNAs (asRNAs) were discovered by deep sequencing technology. We have invented an unique method of stabilizing and characterizing otherwise highly unstable RNase III degradation products of dsRNAs in bacteria. The PI discovered that ectopic expression of p19 siRNA binding protein, found in plant tombusvirus, could stabilize a RNase III-dependent and ~21 nt siRNA-like RNA species (named ‘pro-siRNA’ for ‘prokaryotic siRNA’) in bacteria. We found pro-siRNAs arise from across the entire genome and plasmid in E. coli, consistent with previous observations that pervasive asRNAs are processed by RNase III in bacteria. Importantly, the abundance of pro-siRNA suggests an underestimated extent of RNase III processing on bacterial transcriptome and pro-siRNA sequences reveal the targets and a large number of exact cleavage sites of RNase III. Those new information provide an unprecedented opportunity for exploring detailed molecular mechanism and biological significance of RNase III regulation in bacteria. This project aims to unravel key factors that determine RNase III processing and functions of asRNA in bacteria. We will apply the pro-siRNA technique to profile RNase III target genes and cleavage sites on genome-wide scale in representative bacterial species including E. coli, S. Enteritidis, and L. monocytogenes. With multiple datasets on RNase III regulation and processing from various bacterial species, advanced bioinformatics and comparative genomics will be employed to identify preferred sequences and features of RNase III processing and conserved asRNA-regulated genes in multiple bacterial species. In vitro biochemical assay and substrate sequence mutation experiments will be performed on selected RNase III substrates to discover and prove sequence selectivity of RNase III. Furthermore using carefully designed genetic experiments, we will study the functions of asRNA and RNase III cleavage for a specific class of asRNAs, termed ‘excludon’ in L. monocytogenes, because excludon-like loci are among the most abundant pro-siRNA producing loci in E. coli. Our findings would contribute significantly to the understanding of RNA regulation and processing in bacteria and may unravel novel mechanism for regulating virulence genes.

11102119.label: Realisation of objectives
11102119.value: Understanding the molecular functions of antisense RNA (asRNA) is an emerging topic of molecular biology and genetics for both prokaryotic and eukaryotic species. We invented a novel method of using ectopically expressed p19 proteins (a small dsRNA binding protein) to capture RNase III degradation products of paired sense and antisense transcripts in vivo in bacterial cells. This method can survey functional asRNA generating loci on a genome-wide scale and can identify RNase III cleavage sequences because RNase III, an dsRNA specific endonuclease, is responsible for making those small dsRNAs. The functional relationship between RNase III and asRNA has been investigated by this project. Laboratory strain of E. coli was used as the model organism initially and then this project has expanded into studying asRNAs in important bacterial pathogens including Salmonella enterica and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The molecular mechanisms of gene regulation by both asRNA and RNase III have been investigated extensively at selected gene loci to unravel the biological functions of asRNAs. Objective 1: Apply p19 ectopic expression and pulldown technique to survey RNase III generated pro-siRNAs in representative bacterial species. Results for this objective: We have completed the mapping and categorization of RNase III-cleaved asRNA loci in three model bacterial species: E. coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Salmonella enterica. asRNA generating loci in both multicopy plasmid and genome have been identified by deep sequencing of p19-capture small dsRNAs from the three bacterial species. The small dsRNAs are shown to be dependent on RNase III, encoded by rnc gene, and are resulting from paired sense and antisense RNA transcripts. In particular, bacterial plasmids can produce very abundant overlapping sense and antisense RNAs in all three species. pro-siRNAs are also generated from nearly all bacterial genes but the abundance varies greatly. We classified various types of asRNA loci based on the relative position of asRNA to the sense mRNA. Using abundance ranking, we selected the loci with the most abundant pro-siRNAs as our candidate for further functional studies. The survey of E. coli asRNAs have been published in mBio (Huang et al., mBio, 2020). A part of the results of asRNA survey in Pseudomonas aeruginosa has been published in mBio (Hua et al., mBio, 2022). The asRNA study in Salmonella enterica is in preparation for submission (Chan et al., 2023). Objective 2: Advanced bioinformatic analysis to identify RNase III preferred sequences and/or features and confirmation by biochemical tests. Results for this objective: Bioinformatic analysis was performed on p19-capture small dsRNA datasets. We first annotated RNase III cleavage sites based on the known character of the 2-nt 3’ overhang at RNase III cutting site. Surprisingly, distinctive GC enrichment pattern has been identified from p19-captured dsRNA dataset. A clear GC distribution pattern was observed at the RNase III cleavage sites and a weak preference of high GC sequence by the p19 protein. Our findings strongly support that RNase III has strong sequence specificity at the cleavage sites, likely due to specific biochemical properties of RNase III protein. We also investigated if this sequence specificity is conserved in all bacterial species. By comparing pro-siRNAs isolated from various bacterial species and cloning RNase III from multiple representative bacterial species into E. coli, we have identified certain preferences of various RNase III homologs. Using RNase III in vitro cleavage assay followed by deep sequencing of the products, the sequence bias of E. coli RNase III has been confirmed. The data on RNase III sequence preference and validation in E. coli have been published in mBio (Huang et al., mBio, 2020). Other results are being prepared for publication. Objective 3: Understand the impact of asRNA and RNase III processing on gene regulation at putative excludon loci in E. coli. Results for this objective: In E. coli, we selected gene loci with abundant asRNA transcription have been studied by molecular genetic method, biochemical assay, and quantitative proteomics. The candidate loci include small non-coding RNA genes, like ryeA/ryeB, Spot 42, micA and ldrD, and protein coding genes including tpx, rsd, asd, and cspD and they are all the top loci from p19-captured dsRNA sequencing datasets. In summary, we found that at all loci sense RNA half-lives are affected by RNase III presumably through asRNAs. mRNA and protein abundance were only affected at certain genes, including cspD in E. coli. Our published paper (Huang et al., mBio, 2020) suggests although asRNAs are widespread, they appear to regulate RNA degradation and turnover, asRNA regulation of sense mRNA expression on the protein level is uncommon. We also extended our study on asRNA functions in both Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Salmonella enterica, two important human pathogens. In Salmonella, rnc mutants have been made and those rnc mutants have significantly reduced infectivity comparing to WT. In this study, the relationship between Salmonella virulence and rnc gene which encoding RNase III ribonuclease was being investigated. The rnc gene was knockout from the genome of Salmonella strains and carried on different assays to determine its changes on the virulence expression. The result showed that rnc gene played an important role on the expression of superoxide dismutase SodA, which was an essential determinator of Salmonella survival under the stress of host immunity. On the order hand, we discovered that the double stranded RNA from Salmonella could trigger immune response of the host. Our experimental results suggested that the high expression of rnc gene could help Salmonella to evade from clearance by the immune system of the host. The discovery of the function of rnc in high virulent Salmonella shall facilitate development of novel antimicrobial treatments based on suppression of virulence expression and survival fitness. Publication for this work is in preparation (Chan et al., 2023). In Pseudomonas aeruginosa, we found novel antisense cryptic promoters using strand-specific RNA sequencing. A portion of the protein coding sequence-binding transcription factors regulate the transcription of asRNAs. Certain transcription factor, like RhpR, plays a key role in mediating cryptic transcripts within the coding sequence. Our findings suggest that RhpR influenced the translational efficiency of binding genes. We also profiled pro-siRNAs in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, which revealed a broad range of genes that potentially be regulated by asRNAs. Our study revealed regulatory mechanisms of CDS-bound transcription factors and the complexity of bacterial transcriptomes and RNA regulatory roles for antisense RNAs. Results of transcription factor regulation on CDS-associated asRNA in Pseudomonas aeruginosa has been published in mBio (Hua et al., mBio, 2022). In summary, this project has revealed novel asRNAs in multiple bacterial species and functional models of asRNA regulation on mRNA translation, RNA decay regulated by RNase III, and host innate immunity.

11102119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11102119.value: A summary of the major findings is listed below. Details can be found in 5.3 and our publications. 1. We produced datasets on numerous asRNA loci in E. coli, Salmonella enterica and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. We have completed the mapping and categorization of RNase III-cleaved asRNA loci in three model bacterial species: E. coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Salmonella enterica. The amount of candidate asRNA loci exceeded any previous datasets. (Huang et al., mBio, 2020; Hua et al., mBio, 2022). 2. We demonstrated GC bias pattern of RNase III cleavage sites and the sequence preference of RNase III from multiple bacterial species. RNase III has clear GC preference and there are also differences in the biochemical functions of RNase III from different bacterial species. (Huang et al., mBio, 2020) 3. We identified and experimentally proved a few examples of functional asRNAs regulating sense RNA decay and protein translation in both E. coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. (Huang et al., mBio, 2020; Hua et al., mBio, 2022). 4. We identify the role of certain transcription factors in regulating cryptic promoters within the coding sequences that lead to the transcription of asRNA. (Hua et al., mBio, 2022). 5. Our study revealed the importance of RNase III and asRNA regulated gene loci in the pathogenesis of Salmonella enterica and the role of bacterial dsRNAs in host innate immunity. (Chan et al., under preparation).

11102119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11102119.value: Through this project, we proved that our unique small dsRNA (pro-siRNA) capture method is feasible for asRNA identification in multiple bacterial species. This method can be extended to other bacterial species, especially those pathogenic species, for the identification of novel asRNAs that regulate pathogenesis and drug resistance. For example, we could use plasmid mediated antibiotic-resistant bacteria to explore asRNA function in regulating plasmid since we found plasmid is the most abundant source of asRNAs. Secondly, we have identified a wealth of genomic loci that are potentially asRNA regulated in three bacterial genomes and only a few selected loci have been studied experimentally in the current project. We could continue to explore the functions of asRNAs in other important genes. Thirdly, our results identify an important role of RNase III in regulating dsRNAs in bacteria. Since dsRNAs are potent immune inducers in mammalian system, we believe that the asRNAs in bacteria may play a role in affecting the innate immune system of host cells. Our ongoing work is exploring the asRNA-mediated dsRNA immunity in Salmonella.

11102119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11102119.value: RNA plays a central role in regulating gene functions. In recent years, we began to realize that the diversity and function of RNA are much more complex than known before. Especially, non-coding RNAs are found to be widespread in the genome, especially in bacteria. We use a novel method to capture functional non-coding RNAs that could potentially regulate important genes. Our findings offered a most detailed view on the landscape of non-coding RNAs that are located opposite to and near functional genes in both model and pathogenic bacteria. Among the many novel non-coding RNAs, we proved some are important for regulating bacterial growth and infection. Our findings may lead to novel RNA-based approaches to fight against bacterial infection.
