11102719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11102719.value: Sirt5 is a mitochondria-localized enzyme that belongs to a family of NAD+-dependent HDACs. It can modulate protein activity through desuccinylation, demalonylation and deglutarylation mechanism. Biological studies have shown that Sirt5 is involved in regulating diverse biological processes, including tricarboxylic acid cycle, reactive oxygen defense, fatty acid metabolism and apoptosis. Recently a number of studies have shown Sirt5 is associated with promoting cancer formation. Due to the important roles of Sirt5 in biology and cancer, it will be highly useful to develop chemical tools for detecting Sirt5 activity in living cells. In this proposal, we will employ molecular self-assembly approach to develop peptide-based tools to detect Sirt5 activity in living cells. Molecular self-assembly has found wide applications in cellular activity control, biomarker imaging, drug delivery and other areas. Mimicking nature’s ability to orchestrate a high level of self-assembly in living organisms is fundamentally important and technically challenging. The engineering of self-assembly in living systems demands precise control over molecular forces in complex cellular environment. Our approach is based on designing peptide precursors that can selectively respond to Sirt5 and self-assemble to form nanofiber. We will first develop a succinylated peptide microarray to investigate the substrate specificity of Sirt5. After identifying the peptide substrates with the strongest activity, we will synthesize the corresponding NBD-linked peptide precursor for Sirt5-triggered self-assembly study. In the presence of Sirt5, we expect the soluble non-assembling peptide precursor to be transformed into self-assembling building block, leading to the formation of nanofibers and hydrogel. At the same time, the environment-sensitive fluorophore NBD in the peptide can produce bright fluorescence due to the hydrophobic environment of nanofibers. After proving Sirt5 can induce nanofiber formation in vitro, we will next investigate whether the peptide precursor can be used to image Sirt5 activity in living cells. Co-localization experiments and SiRNA assay will be conducted to further validate the roles of Sirt5 in catalyzing nanofiber formation. In the last stage, we will adopt fragment-based approach and synthesize a small molecule-based inhibitor library. After obtaining the inhibitors, we will employ hydrogelation assay and cell-based assay to screen the potent hits. Through our interdisciplinary research encompassing organic chemistry, peptide microarray, self-assembly and molecular imaging, we hope to generate new chemical tools to facilitate research on Sirt5 and generate useful inhibitors to aid in drug discovery.

11102719.label: Realisation of objectives
11102719.value: All the objectives have been successfully accomplished by the completion date. Initially, suitable peptide substrates for Sirt5 were identified, and NBD-containing peptide precursors were synthesized for the study of Sirt5-triggered self-assembly. In vitro hydrogelation experiments demonstrated the transformation of the peptide precursor into hydrogels. Subsequently we investigated whether the peptide precursor can be transformed into nanofibers in living cells. Fluorescent imaging experiments showed that the fluorescence is mainly localized into mitochondria, which corresponds to the cellular localization of Sirt5. TEM imaging experiments revealed that nanofibers can be selectively formed in mitochondria. Furthermore, our hydrogelation assay can be used to assess the inhibition potency of Sirt5 inhibitors. The self-assembled nanofibers were found to attenuate mitochondrial activity and significantly enhance the cancer cell killing activity of various drugs, including dichloroacetate (DCA), cisplatin, and paclitaxel (Taxol).

11103619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103619.value: Young-onset colorectal cancer, defined as arising in people younger than age 50, is a growing threat of health worldwide, with estimated increases of incidence in a decade by about 90% and 140% in western and eastern world, respectively. Conventional colorectal cancer risk factors such as obesity, alcohol consumption and smoking have been extensively investigated, yet no compelling explanation has been identified for this epidemiological trend. More importantly, the etiology and underlying biology of young onset CRC are not understood. Although the pathogenesis of hereditary CRC syndromes has been well characterized, they only account for a small fraction of early-onset CRC, and therefore, cannot explain the rapidly increasing incidence, more aggressiveness and relatively poorer outcome. So far, no biomarker is available for effective prediction of high-risk young-onset CRC patients, and as a result, these patients were overtreated with significantly more adjuvant chemotherapies at all stages, but only received minor gain in survival. Elucidating the biological mechanisms in relation to clinical outcomes in young-onset CRC is critical for selection of patients for more optimized clinical management and individualized therapy. Colorectal cancer is a heterogeneous disease, which can be subdivided into four consensus molecular subtypes (CMSs): CMS1-MSI, CMS2-canonical, CMS3-metabolic and CMS4-mesenchymal. In our pilot study, we unveiled that young-onset CRC is also a biologically heterogeneous disease comprising the same four molecular subtypes, but the prevalence of CMSs is different from late-onset CRC. More specifically, we found that the observed poor clinical outcomes in young-onset CRC were not due to age per se, but higher prevalence of CMS4-mesenchymal subtype, known to be associated with poor relapse-free survival and higher risk of metastasis. Furthermore, we provided evidences to show that the higher prevalence of CMS1 in late-onset CRC may be potentially due to DNA hypermethylation and mutation burden progressively accumulated during aging. In this proposal, we aim to comprehensively dissect the age-dependent heterogeneity of CRC by integrative analysis of multi-omic and clinical data involving over 7000 patient samples across 9 public datasets and 2 independent in-house clinical cohorts. Our 1st objective is to perform comprehensive clinical characterizations of young-onset CRC based on a multi-center cohort study. Based on curated public datasets, our 2nd objective is to systematically delineate multi-omic molecular properties associated with each CMS in young-onset CRC. To robustly identify high-risk young-onset CRC patients, our 3rd objective is to develop a probabilistic model that integrates age-specific prevalence, molecular subtyping and subtype-specific recurrence risk prediction. 早發結直腸癌（患者年齡小於50歲）已成為世界範圍內日益增長的健康威脅，其在東、西方的發病率預計十年內將分別增長90％和140％。傳統的結直腸癌風險因素諸如肥胖，酗酒和吸煙在文獻中已有大量報導，然而這些因素並不能有力地解釋其流行病學趨勢。更重要的是，早發結直腸癌的病因和潛在的生物學機制尚不明確。儘管遺傳性結直腸癌綜合症的發病機制已經被熟知，但其僅佔早發結直腸癌的一小部分，因而並不能解釋其迅速增加的發病率、更高的侵襲性和更差的臨床結果。到目前為止，尚缺乏有效預測高風險早發結直腸癌的生物標誌物，導致這些患者普遍接受過度的輔助化療，卻收效甚微。因此，闡明與早發結直腸癌臨床結果相關的生物學機制對於實現更為優化的臨床管理和個性化治療至關重要。 結直腸癌是一種具有高度異質性的癌症，並可被劃分為四種共識分子亞型（CMS的）：CMS1-MSI型或免疫型，CMS2-經典型（標準），CMS3-代謝型（代謝）和CMS4-間充質型（mesenchymal）。本課題組前期工作發現早發結直腸癌也是具有高度分子異質性的疾病，且擁有相同的四種分子亞型，但是其各種亞型的發病率卻和遲發結直腸癌存在顯著差異。具體而言，我們發現早發結直腸癌較差的臨床結果並非源於年齡本身而是由於富集了較高比例的CMS4-間充質亞型的患者，而該分子亞型已經被證實與高復發和高轉移風險相關。此外，前期研究結果還表明遲發結直腸癌中CMS1-MSI型患者的高發病率可能與衰老過程中所逐漸積累的DNA甲基化和基因突變負荷相關。 本研究旨在通過對來源於9個公共數據集和2個獨立內部臨床數據集的共計超過7000例病人樣本，經多組學數據和臨床信息的綜合性分析，實現對早發結直腸癌與年齡相關的分子異質性進行全面剖析。我們的第一個目標是基於多中心隊列研究對早發結直腸癌患者的臨床特徵進行綜合表徵。基於公共數據集，第二個目標是系統性描繪與早發結直腸癌中每個分子亞型相關的多組學分子特徵圖譜。為有效識別高復發風險早發結直腸癌患者，第三個目標是建立一個綜合年齡特異性發病率、分子分型概率分佈及分子亞型特異性復發風險的概率模型。

11103719.value: 三陰性乳腺癌是一種高侵襲性的乳腺癌，化療是主要的治療選擇。不幸的是，化學治療劑通常對患者具有高毒性。因此，有迫切需要研發新的治療靶點。最近有研究顯示，超級增強子在上調癌症驅動基因的表達中起重要作用。然而，超級增強子在不同乳腺癌亞型中的功能, 及其在腫瘤發生中的具體機制尚未闡明。使用生物信息學方法，我們發現了三陰性乳腺癌的超級增強子和其調節的基因。我們初步研究顯示三陰性乳腺癌的超級增強子能調節TCOF1的表達。目前尚未發現TCOF1在癌症發病機制中的作用。在本研究計劃中，我們 將剖析TCOF1在轉錄子集翻譯中的作用，以及該轉錄物如何賦予癌細胞生長和存活的優勢。之後，我們將研究超級增強子和Akt3對TCOF1的調節作用。最後，我們將使用異種移植模型研究TCOF1的信號傳導。

11103719.label: Realisation of objectives
11103719.value: All project objectives have been addressed, and we have identified TCOF1 as a novel cancer gene in promoting triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) growth and determined the upregulation of TCOF1 by TNBC-specific super-enhancer. As set out in Objective 1, to assess the role of TCOF1 in spheroid growth in different subgroups of TNBC, we performed knockout studies in a diverse set of TNBC lines. In addition to BL1 line (MDA-MB-468) and BL2 line (HCC1806), we analyzed two additional BL1 lines (HCC1937, HCC1143), one M line (BT549) and 3 MSL lines (Hs578T, MDA-MB-436, MDA-MB-231). Interestingly, whereas TCOF1 depletion had potent effect on spheroid growth in basal-like TNBC lines, it had no effect on mesenchymal-like spheroids (Fig. 1). To determine the effect of TCOF1 in regulating TNBC stemness, we tested the effect of TCOF1 on ALDH activity. Knockout of TCOF1 markedly decreased the percentage of ALDHhigh population in TNBC spheroids (Fig. 2). In the TCS model, loss of TCOF1 function resulted in the downregulation of rDNA transcription, we therefore examined the function of TCOF1 in ribosome biogenesis, as set out in Aim 1. We have quantified levels of 45S and 5S ribosomal RNAs (rRNAs), as well as performed immunofluorescence to exam the integrity of rRNA in TNBC cells. Our data showed that TCOF1 knockout did not lead to reduction of 45S or 5S rRNA, nor impair rRNA integrity in TNBC cells (results shown in mid-term report). We have also performed ribo-seq to examine if TCOF1 selectively regulates the translation of distinct subpools of mRNAs. Our ribo-seq data and validation experiments did not point to TCOF1 as a major player in regulating protein translation in TNBC cells, instead by performing RNA-seq, we observed interesting regulatory function of TCOF1 in modulating mRNA levels of genes involved in cancer stemness. Among the TCOF1-modulated candidates, KIT, FZD8 and NOS2 have been reported to modulate cell differentiation and/or stem cell maintenance. In addition, high KIT mRNA expression in basal-like breast cancer is correlated with shorter overall survival. We, therefore, focused on testing if these genes mediate the effect of TCOF1 in TNBC stemness. RT-qPCR confirmed that mRNA levels of KIT, FZD8, NOS2 were decreased upon TCOF1 knockout. Immunoblot analysis shows that TCOF1 depletion led to reduced KIT and FZD8 protein expression in MDA-MB-468 3D spheroids (Fig. 3A). Downregulation of KIT was also observed in two distinct TNBC lines, HCC1806 and HCC1143 (Fig. 3C). Next, we overexpressed HA-TCOF1 in TNBC cells, and observed upregulation of KIT protein expression (Fig. 3C) as well as mRNA levels (Fig. 3D). Agreeing with these findings, expression of KIT is positively co-related with TCOF1 expression in a gene expression dataset of 55 TNBC samples from lymph node-negative systemically untreated patients (GSE7390). The expression of KIT and TCOF1 in normal breast tissues is also positively co-related (GEPIA, n = 178). We then examined the effects of TCOF1 on downstream pathways of KIT, and our results indicated that phosphorylation of KIT, AKT, STAT3 and ERK was inhibited upon TCOF1 knockout. Conversely, overexpression of TCOF1 resulted in activation of these known downstream molecules (Fig. 3C), supporting the notion of increased KIT signaling in TCOF1-overexpressed TNBC cells. As the role of KIT in breast CSC properties has not been reported, we first examined if depleting KIT had any effect on TNBC stemness. Knockout of KIT impaired mammosphere formation as well as self-renewal ability (Fig. 3E). To explore this further and evaluate whether KIT is a downstream target of TCOF1 in CSC maintenance, we overexpressed KIT in rescue experiments. Whereas overexpression of KIT alone had no effect on mammosphere formation, impairment of mammosphere formation ability by TCOF1 knockout could be rescued by KIT overexpression (Fig. 3F, 3G). KIT also rescued the ratio of secondary to primary mammosphere numbers (Fig. 3H), indicating that it mediates the function of TCOF1 in self-renewal of CSCs. Interestingly, overexpression of KIT does not rescue the growth of TCOF1-depleted spheroids nor cells cultured in 2D, demonstrating the specific role of KIT in mediating TCOF1’s function in CSCs. We have also examined whether FZD8 or NOS2 is a mediator of TCOF1 in regulating CSCs. Overexpression of FZD8 or NOS2 did not rescue mammosphere formation impaired by TCOF1 knockout in TNBC cells. These findings indicate that KIT, but not FDZ8 or NOS2, plays a crucial role in TCOF1-mediated CSC regulation. In Aim 2, we evaluated the association of TCOF1 mRNA expression with patient overall survival in various clinical datasets. In addition, in a panel of breast tumor lines, protein expression levels of TCOF1 are higher in TNBC lines as compared to luminal or HER2-overexpressed lines (Data shown in mid-term report). These observations were further validated by immunohistochemistry (IHC) in a cohort consisting of 37 primary breast cancer cases, in which higher percentage of TNBC patients had high staining intensity of TCOF1 compared to non-TNBC cases (Fig. 4). We next examined the functional role of TCOF1 super-enhancer in TCOF1 expression and TNBC growth. We deleted e1 region of TCOF1 super-enhancer using Crispr/Cas9 system, and verified deletion with PCR (Fig. 5A) and DNA sequencing. Deletion of e1 resulted in marked decrease of TCOF1 expression (Fig. 5B), demonstrating that TCOF1 is a target gene of super-enhancer SE324. Furthermore, deletion of e1 region led to reduction of spheroid growth (Fig. 5C), whereas overexpression of TCOF1 rescued the phenotype (Fig. 5D), indicating the functional importance of TCOF1-associated super-enhancer. JQ1 is a BET inhibitor which shows promising anti-cancer potential in various cancers including TNBC. To examine its effect on the binding of BRD4 to TCOF1 super-enhancer and TCOF1 expression, we performed ChIP-qPCR and immunoblotting in JQ1- or DMSO-treated breast cancer cells. Treatment of TNBC cells with JQ1 potently reduced the binding of BRD4 to the super-enhancer as well as TCOF1 protein levels (Fig. 5E). In contrast, JQ1 had no effect on BRD4 binding or TCOF1 expression in luminal cells (Fig. 5E). Taken together, our findings uncovered TCOF1 as a novel oncogenic gene regulated by a TNBC-specific super-enhancer. As set out in Aim 3, we extended our studies in vivo, in which TNBC cells with TCOF1 knockout were injected orthotopically into nude mice. Depletion of TCOF1 in basal-like MDA-MB-468 cells resulted in a profound decrease of tumor growth (Fig. 6A-C). TCOF1 knockout in another basal-like TNBC line HCC1806 had similar effect on the inhibition of xenograft growth (Fig. 6D-F). To assess the degree to which TCOF1 regulates tumor-initiating ability, TNBC cells derived from spheroids with or without TCOF1 knockout were injected into mammary fat pads of female nude mice at limiting dilutions. Mice injected with TCOF1 knockout cells showed decreased tumor incidence and significant lower frequency of tumor-initiating cells compared with other subgroups (Fig. 7). On the other hand, there was no significant difference between dox-treated and dox-untreated control groups. Taken together, these data demonstrate an important function of TCOF1 in regulating CSC self-renewal and tumor initiation.

11103719.label: Major findings and research outcome
11103719.value: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is aggressive and has a poor prognosis. Currently, chemotherapy is the major treatment option but the clinical benefit is limited to a subset of patients. Key genomic alterations associated with different subtypes of breast cancer have been comprehensively studied. However, deregulation of epigenome in different breast cancer subtypes remains poorly characterized. We previously performed an integrated epigenomic and transcriptomic profiling to identify TNBC-specific genes driven by super-enhancers. In this project, we uncovered a TNBC-specific super-enhancer proximal to TCOF1, a gene which plays a key role in ribosome biogenesis and is implicated in a craniofacial syndrome. The role of TCOF1 in cancer has not been reported. Using in vitro and in vivo studies, we provided evidence for a critical and novel function of TCOF1 in driving self-renewal of cancer stem cells in TNBC. We found that TCOF1 is overexpressed in ~32% of TNBC, and upregulation of TCOF1 is a predictor of poor survival in breast cancer patients, indicating its clinical significance. Our data showed that basal-like but not in mesenchymal-like subtype of TNBC shows dependency on TCOF1, highlighting the importance of identifying distinct drivers for different subtypes of TNBC. Furthermore, we uncovered a key and novel function of TCOF1 in upregulating KIT expression to drive cancer stem cell self-renewal. The majority of data collected from this study have been summarized and published in Nature Communications and British Journal of Cancer (refer to Part C).

11103719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11103719.value: This study has greatly advanced our understanding in the role of super-enhancer and TCOF1 in breast cancer stemness. The funded work provides the foundation for identifying more super-enhancer-driven oncogenes that play critical roles in various processes driving TNBC growth and progression. In addition, the funded project allows us to explore the molecular mechanisms by which the super-enhancer is upregulating TCOF1 expression. We have explored and discovered a transcription factor that mediates the super-enhancer’s activities. Targeting TCOF1 or its regulator may be a new therapeutic strategy for TNBC patients.

11103719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11103719.value: Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype of breast cancer with poor prognosis. We have recently uncovered a potential mechanism that TNBC cells utilize to promote the stemness and growth of tumor. The objective of this proposal is to decipher this mechanism in breast tumor growth, with a long term goal to discover more effective therapeutics for breast cancer patients. It has been shown recently that super-enhancers, located in certain non-coding regions of the genome, play an important role in regulating expression of cancer driver genes. Using computer-based analysis, we have identified a TNBC-specific super-enhancer located close to a gene named TCOF1. In this funded study, we showed that TCOF1 plays an important role in regulating TNBC growth. We further identified KIT as a specific downstream target of TCOF1. Our studies have provided insights for developing treatment strategies targeting TCOF1 signaling.

11103819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11103819.value: 感光细胞死亡引起的视网膜变性是导致不可治愈失明的主要原因。感光细胞工作需要大量能量，因此它们的代谢非常活跃，尤其是氧和糖的代谢。然而，当氧或者糖代谢不能维持良好的平衡，感光细胞的功能和存活会受到影响，导致或者加快视网膜变性。Txnip蛋白是一个调控和关联氧和糖代谢的关键蛋白，然而其在感光细胞中的作用还没有被仔细研究。在这个项目中，我们将研究Txnip蛋白在感光细胞变性中的作用和受到其调控的下游信号通路。这个项目的成果可能会让我们更好地理解遗传性视网膜变性的发病机理，并且或为该类疾病的治疗指出新的靶点。

11103819.label: Realisation of objectives
11103819.value: Objective 1. To confirm whether Txnip suppression prolongs photoreceptor function and survival We crossed rd10 with Rho-Cre;Txnipfl/fl mice to produce rd10 offsprings with Txnip homo- or heterozygous deletion specifically in the rod photoreceptors. Rod-specific Txnip deletion provided an alleviation of the rd10 rod degeneration process, which was evident as a thicker ONL at p24 as shown by OCT in-vivo live imaging. The statistical calculation revealed a significant increase of ONL thickness in rd10;Txnipfl/fl;Rho-Cre and rd10;Txnipfl/+;Rho-Cre compared to rd10;Txnip+/+;Rho-Cre controls. Moreover, the morphological rescue was also accompanied by a functional rescue at p30 as demonstrated by a better electroretinography (ERG) response. There was a dose-dependent effect of Txnip zygosity on the scotopic waves, where rd10;Txnipfl/fl;Rho-Cre mice had higher scotopic a- and b-wave amplitudes compared to rd10;Txnipfl/+;Rho-Cre or rd10;Txnipfl/fl;Rho-Cre controls. In photopic conditions, the rescue trend persisted but did not reach statistical significance, suggesting that the rescue effect is rod-autonomous, with a possible secondary rescue in the cones. Homo- and heterozygous Txnip deletion preserved the visual acuity as assessed by an optomotor assay. Histologically, dying rods can be identified by the shortening of their outer segments (early phase) followed by the mislocalization of rhodopsin immunoreactivity from the outer segments to the soma. Homo-and heterozygous deletion of Txnip in the rods ameliorated the rod degeneration as can be seen from thicker ONL, better preserved rod outer segments, and less somatic rhodopsin mislocalization. The cones, which do not degenerate yet at this age, retained their morphology, despite the shortening of their axons amid the ONL collapse. To translate these findings into the development of RP gene therapy, we constructed adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) carrying a short hairpin RNA against the Txnip gene to knock down its expression in the degenerating rd10 retina. The most suitable promoter to selectively target the rods would be the rhodopsin (Rho) promoter. The AAV-Rho-Txnip-shRNA can effectively downregulate TXNIP expression in the rd10 retina. Unfortunately, we observed a toxic effect on the rod and cone photoreceptors when AAV-Rho-shRNAs were delivered subretinally into the rd10 mouse retina. We then opted to use the human rhodopsin kinase (hRK) promoter which is relatively safe, but less selective, as it drives the transgene expression in both rod and cones. The eyes of the neonatal pups were injected subretinally with AAV-hRK-mCherry-Txnip-shRNA or non-targeting (NT)-shRNA. At p30, there was a robust electrophysiological rescue as shown by the b-wave during scotopic and mesopic conditions, but too minute to be seen in the a-wave. Similar to the results from the triple transgenic mice above, the rescue effect of Txnip knockdown diminished during the photopic condition but can be translated into behavioral phenotype as shown by optomotor assay. The rescue effect was transient, as the degeneration still progressed over time, and another ERG test at p50 only showed minimal and noisy ERG response in both groups. Objective 2: To determine whether Txnip suppresses Glut1 and glucose intake in photoreceptors A stable Txnip-expressing 661w cell line using a lentiviral system was established to examine the downstream effects of Txnip upregulation. Using 2-NBDG, a fluorescent-tagged glucose analog, we compared glucose uptake of EF-Txnip vs. EF-empty. A group of EF-empty with high glucose (35 mM) addition was also included as a positive control because glucose and 2-NBDG will compete for the glucose transporter occupancy. Txnip overexpression significantly decreases glucose uptake into the 661w cell. We then asked whether this glucose uptake reduction would consequently decrease glycolysis. To test this, a Glycolysis Stress Test using a Seahorse apparatus was performed. EF-Txnip, as expected, exhibited a lesser glycolysis activity compared to the EF-empty. In the Seahorse curve, EF-Txnip consistently displayed less extracellular acidification rate (ECAR, a reflection of glycolysis) at all measurement points. It was found that Txnip overexpression reduced the basal glycolysis, glycolytic capacity, and glycolytic reserve capacity. The immediate question that arose was whether Txnip-overexpressing cells also decrease oxidative phosphorylation proportionally to the glucose uptake and glycolysis inhibition. We utilized the Seahorse MitoStress test to measure the oxygen consumption rate (OCR) dynamics at the basal state and during mitochondrial inhibition. Interestingly, we observed that Txnip overexpression induced an increase in the global OCR as seen from the Seahorse MitoStress curve, with a significant increase in all parameters tested: basal respiration, maximal respiration, oxygen for ATP synthesis, and spare respiratory capacity. While it was expected that Txnip overexpression would reduce global OCR due to the inhibition of glucose uptake, pyruvate oxidation, and glutamine deamination might compensate for this by directly providing the mitochondrial fuel in the Krebs cycle, thus reflecting the metabolic shift of Txnip-overexpressing cells. However, since rod photoreceptors are reliant on glycolysis for their function and survival, this metabolic shift can be detrimental to the degenerating rods. Objective 3. To test whether Txnip inhibits Trx antioxidant system and activates the pro-apoptotic ASK1-p38/JNK pathway in photoreceptors TXNIP is a pro-oxidant protein via its action in inhibiting thioredoxin (TXN). We tested the oxidative stress level in TXNIP-overexpressing cells by MitoSox Red staining followed by flow cytometry. As expected, Txnip overexpression significantly increased ROS in 661w cells. Finally, since TXNIP is also pro-apoptotic, we examined the effect of Txnip overexpression on the apoptosis rate. Using an Annexin-V assay, we observed an increase in the apoptosis rate when Txnip is overexpressed in 661w cells. Brought together, these results indicate a detrimental metabolic shift and aberrant cellular responses against Txnip overexpression, which may result in the worsening of the degeneration process in vivo. Thus, we were provided with a rational reason to downregulate Txnip in an animal model of RP with an expectation to see a rescue or delay in the photoreceptor degeneration. To confirm the findings in vivo, we measured the total antioxidant capacity of the rd10 retinas when Txnip is deleted in the rods and compared it with the capacity when the Txnip gene is intact. The experiment was performed at the onset of degeneration (p18), where the number of rods was still similar across groups. We observed an increase of antioxidant capacity in rd10;Txnipfl/fl;Rho-Cre and rd10;Txnipfl/+;Rho-Cre retina compared to rd10;Txnip+/+;Rho-Cre, which may be the main rescue mechanism of Txnip deletion.

11103819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11103819.value: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited retinal degenerative disease that currently lacks a curative treatment. Thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP) is a versatile protein involved in various functions, including oxidative and metabolic stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. Its expression is highly responsive to different stressors, making it a potential target for various human pathologies, including RP. In this study, we have identified TXNIP as an upregulated protein in dying rods of multiple mouse models of RP. Upregulation of Txnip led to increased apoptosis and oxidative stress, as well as a shift in photoreceptor metabolism towards a less glycolytic and more oxidative state in a photoreceptor cell line. Through transgenic knockout and AAV-mediated knockdown approaches, we observed that reducing Txnip improved the structure and function of degenerating rod retina. This improvement was partially attributed to increased antioxidant capacity and restoration of the NADPH/NADH ratio. Interestingly, when Txnip was overexpressed in cones while simultaneously knocking down rod Txnip, we observed a more consistent and robust rescue of visual function and photoreceptor survival compared to independent treatments. This discovery highlights the opposing effects of TXNIP on rod and cone survival and provides insights for the development of a novel and effective therapy targeting TXNIP for the treatment of retinitis pigmentosa. Based on our findings, we believe that TXNIP is a crucial player and a potential target molecule for RP therapy, showing promising translational potential. We are currently preparing a manuscript for publication (as mentioned in item No. 5 of Part C, point 8). Additionally, the PhD student, Alva SUPIT, who conducted this project, submitted his thesis (see Part C, point 10) and obtained his PhD degree in July 2021. Furthermore, this grant has supported two side projects, resulting in the publication of two papers (listed as item No. 1 and 2 in Part C, point 8), and in both papers we acknowledged the support of this GRF grant. With the assistance of this grant, we have actively participated in several collaborative research projects and published four papers as co-authors (listed as item No. 3 and 4 in Part C point 8, and two papers reported in the mid-term report).

11103819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11103819.value: Due to the heterogeneity of causal gene lesions in retinitis pigmentosa (RP), it is currently not feasible to implement specific gene supplementation therapy for each individual patient. However, the combined treatment with AAV-RO-Txnip and AAV-RK-Txnip shRNA offers a potential gene-independent therapyfor RP patients whose mutant gene cannot be identified or is too rare for gene supplementation therapy. To further advance this research, we will seek collaboration with ophthalmologists to obtain clinical samples from RP patients. These samples will allow us to confirm the level of Txnip changes. Additionally, we aim to test the safety and efficacy of combined therapies targeting Txnip in other animal models, such as dogs, as part of our future investigations. Given the involvement of Txnip in various stress conditions, we also wish to collaborate with other laboratories to examine its expression changes in neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer's disease. Furthermore, we aim to investigate whether Txnip could serve as a therapeutic target in other disease contexts. By expanding our research scope, we hope to contribute to a better understanding of Txnip's role and potential applications beyond retinitis pigmentosa.

11103819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11103819.value: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is an inherited eye disease that causes the retina to degenerate over time. Unfortunately, there is currently no cure for RP. In our research, we focused on a protein called TXNIP, which is involved in different cellular functions including responding to stress and controlling cell survival. We discovered that in mice with RP, the levels of TXNIP were higher in the cells of the retina that were dying. When we reduced the levels of TXNIP in RP mouse model's retinas, we saw improvements in the structure and function of the damaged retina. This improvement was partly due to better protection of the cells against stress and a restoration of their energy balance. We also made an interesting observation when we increased the levels of TXNIP in cones while simultaneously reducing it in rods. This combination treatment resulted in even better preservation of vision and cell survival compared to treating the cells separately. Based on our findings, we believe that TXNIP could be an important target for developing new treatments for RP. By targeting TXNIP, we may be able to protect the retinal cells and improve vision in people with RP.

11200219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200219.value: The decision criterion plays a crucial role in selecting optimal portfolios that best fit investors’ investment expectation and risk attitudes. There are two main schools of such decision frameworks in the literature: the framework of expected utility maximization, based on Von Neumann-Morgenstern utility theorem that is derived from the assumed preferences of rational decision-makers, and the mean-risk framework pioneered by Markowitz, in which investors seek to strike a balance between risk and return. Despite its scientific rigour based on the justifiable axioms of rational behavior, the expected utility maximization framework is not widely adopted by practitioners due to its abstract nature and global assessment requirement. Mean-risk optimization on the other hand is popular in investment practice due to its clear intuition to practitioners, but suffers from several theoretical deficiencies, in particular the notorious time-inconsistency. In this project we propose a novel risk-potential portfolio selection framework which possesses both desirable theoretical features, including monotonicity and time-consistency, and straightforward financial intuition. We argue that investors should always set a target in investment and care about minimizing the possibility of falling short of the target and maximizing the possibility of exceeding the target simultaneously. We then define the two performance measures, i）Risk: lower partial moments below the target, and ii) Potential: upper partial moment above the target. Under a realistic premise that investors only need to provide their investment targets and the desired trade-offs between risk and potential, we can translate such investment parameters into a corresponding stochastic control formulation. In this research, we will proceed to show, building on our preliminary investigation, that our proposed risk-potential portfolio selection formulation is analytically solvable and computationally tractable, although the problem formulation is nonconvex in nature due to its inverse S-shape objective function. We will derive its wellposedness condition, and obtain its optimal investment strategy. We will then study the distinctive features and prominent properties of our framework, and compare it with various existing portfolio selection formulations, including the dynamic mean-variance formulation, dynamic mean-CVaR formulation, and dynamic behavioral portfolio selection under cumulative prospect theory. Our contributions in this research will advance the state-of-the-art and directly improve investment practice by i) connecting the objective function in investment models with the lower and upper partial moments associated with an investment target which are easily comprehensible by market practitioners, and ii) making the resulting investment models computationally tractable, thus offering investors more valuable guidance.

11200219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200219.value: This research project introduces a novel framework for asset allocation that is particularly relevant for robo-advisors. The framework involves a set of utility functions that combine the benefits of traditional mean-variance analysis with enhanced features. It allows for intuitive investment objectives and straightforward optimal strategy calculations while addressing issues related to consistency and non-monotonicity. Key components include target wealth, potential-aversion, and weighting parameters, which lead to time-consistent strategies. The framework distinguishes between risk (below the target wealth) and potential (above the target wealth), offering a comprehensive view of portfolio performance. Numerical examples indicate that lower potential-aversion parameters result in improved risk and potential, given constant expected wealth. Overall, this research contributes to a more sophisticated understanding of asset allocation and investment decision-making.

11200319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200319.value: A holographic projector is a new type of image projection system that has significant advantages over existing ones. From the hardware point of view, a holographic projector is not much different to a traditional projector, but instead of directly projecting an optical image, the reconstructed image resulting from the digital hologram is projected. The digital hologram of an image can be generated through numerical computation. In comparison with current image projectors, a holographic projector is brighter, and does not require any lens for focusing. In addition, the projected area can be resized, or moved to different locations simply by modifying a few parameters in the generation of the digital hologram. As such, size of a holographic projector, as well as the cost and the power consumption are much lower than that of a traditional projector. Despite the numerous advantages of a holographic projector, there are 4 major factors that have prohibited it from being utilized, and replacing existing projectors in practice. First, the quality of the image projected by a holographic projector is far from acceptable. This is fatal in the context of image projection as the quality of the projected image is a major concern. Second, the projected image is heavily contaminated with noise, which again is not acceptable in practice. Third, similar to existing projectors, the display area is restricted. Fourth, existing methods that are used to improve the image quality require heavy amount of computation, implying the need of high speed processor(s), higher cost and power consumption, hence defeating the advantages of the holographic projector. More importantly, even with the incorporation of such improvement, some of the aforementioned disadvantages are still not overcome. This proposal aims at the development of a new type of holographic projector to overcome the above-mentioned problems. The proposed holographic projector is based on a novel method that enhances the image quality (as well as lowering the noise level) through an optimization algorithm and high speed spatial filtering, as well as widening the projected area. The Principal Investigator has obtained some positive proof of concept with numerical simulation, and hope that the funding can be utilized to realize develop the proposed holographic projector. All in all, the proposed holographic projector to be developed has the following advantages: • Higher optical efficiency (i.e. brighter) • Low power consumption. • Computation efficient in the hologram generation process. • Does not require focusing lens. • Enhanced projected image quality. • Reduced noise contamination on the projected image. • Wide display area. 全息投影儀是一種具有重要意義的新型圖像投影系統 優於現有的優勢。從硬件角度來看，是一台全息投影儀與傳統投影機沒什麼不同，但不是直接投影在光學圖像中，投影由數字全息圖產生的重建圖像。可以通過數值計算生成圖像的數字全息圖。與當前的圖像投影儀相比，全息投影儀更亮，並且不需要任何鏡頭進行聚焦。此外，投影區域可以調整大小，或只需修改生成中的一些參數即可移動到不同的位置數字全息圖。因此，全息投影儀的尺寸，以及成本和功耗遠低於傳統投影機。 儘管全息投影儀具有眾多優點，但有4個主要因素禁止使用它，並在實踐中取代現有的投影儀。 首先，全息投影儀投影的圖像質量遠非如此可以接受的。這在圖像投影的背景下是致命的，因為投影的質量形像是一個主要問題。其次，投影圖像受到嚴重污染噪音，這在實踐中是不可接受的。第三，類似於現有的投影儀顯示區域受限制。第四，用於改善圖像的現有方法質量需要大量的計算，這意味著需要高速處理器，更高的成本和功耗，從而打敗了它的優點全息投影儀。更重要的是，即使加入了這樣的改進，一些上述缺點仍未克服。 該提案旨在開發一種新型全息投影儀克服了上述問題。所提出的全息投影儀是基於的一種提高圖像質量（以及降低噪音水平）的新方法通過優化算法和高速空間濾波，以及拓寬投影面積。首席研究員獲得了一些積極的證據概念與數值模擬，並希望資金可以用來實現開發擬議的全息投影。 總而言之，擬議的全息投影儀待開發具有以下優點： • 更高的光學效率（即更亮） • 低功耗。 • 全息圖生成過程中的計算效率。 • 不需要聚焦鏡頭。 • 增強投影圖像質量。 • 減少投影圖像上的噪音污染。 • 寬顯示區域。

11200319.label: Realisation of objectives
11200319.value: 1. General comment on progress As report in the midterm report, favorable progress and results have been attained to meet the original objectives of the GRF proposal. The following is a recap of my previous report. To begin with, a solid foundation has been developed on the theory and algorithm to enhance the quality of hologram projection. What has been achieved followed the original objectives, and also inspired the remaining stage of development of the GRF project. Similar to my previous strategy, I have continued to collaborate with international researchers working in relevant area. In this respect, I have shared my research experience with them, and at the same time also adopting some of their ideas and methods in my works. Following the collaboration, I am pleased to say that we have managed to published our join works in international journals with reasonable high impact factors. 2. Foundations established in the first stage of the GRF research (recapped from midterm report) In the first stage of the project, as described in the midterm report, I have developed a novel method known as “Time division comb filtering” (TDCF) [2] (please refer to Section C: Research Output). This method is used to generate a phase-only hologram which can be displayed with a single phase-only spatial light modulator (SLM). Briefly, the source image is first down-sampled (with a sufficiently large down-sampling factor) with a grid-cross lattice and converted into a phase-only hologram. A hologram generated with this method is referred to as a sampled phase-only hologram (SPOH). The reconstructed image of a SPOH is good, but due to the down-sampling, the non-sampled points lead to a sparse image with lots of empty voids. The TDCF method overcomes this shortcoming by rapidly displaying multiple SPOHs, each being a slightly offset version of the original one. Using the persistence of vision of human eyes, the reconstructed images of the SPOHs are averaged out, resulting in a low-pass comb filtering effect that partially filled the empty voids of the non-sampled points. As shown in the figures in [2] on the evaluation of the method, the comb-filter has filled up the voids to a good extent and leads to a more solid reconstructed image. This stage of development partially fulfills objectives (1), (3), and (4) of the GRF proposal. Further enhancement is expected. 3. Development in the second (final) stage of the GRF project: LRDS+AIA holograms Subsequent to the first stage of development, I have discussed with Prof. J.P. Liu of the Feng Chia University on the possibility of further enhancing the quality of the SPOH and decreasing the complexity of the optical setup. We observed that regular down-sampling patterns are generally easier to recognize and hence more prominent to the eyes as compared with random patterns. We also noted that digital micro-mirror is more economical than a grey-scaled SLM. In our method, we first applied a localized random down-sampling (LRDS) mask to down-sample the object function and generated a binary CGH by direct sign-thresholding. This is similar to the SPOH that is adopted in the first stage of the project, but the regular grid-cross lattice is replaced with random lattice. Next, SPOHs of the same source image are generated in the same way, each based on a different LRDS mask. In the formation of each LRDS, the adaptive mask removes the object points at the region with stronger reconstructed light. Subsequently, the multiple LRDS holograms are displayed in rapid transition on a digital micro-mirror device (DMD), a process known as adaptive intensity accumulation (AIA). Our findings have been published in [3]. As shown in the evaluation in [3], the reconstructed images of adaptively accumulating multiple LRDS holograms are good, and increases with larger number of LRDS holograms. In addition, the computation loading is mild and the method is suitable for practical applications. This part of the work further enhances objectives 1, 3, and 4. 4. Development in the second (final) stage of the GRF project: Optimal sampled phase-only hologram (OSPOH) The TDCF and the LRDS+AIA methods both serve to enhance the quality of the SPOHs, but they require generating multiple SPOHs of the same source image. This leads to increase of the computation time, although it is not too far from the mark in practical applications. These two methods also require displaying the holograms at high speed, which requires the use of high speed, and more expensive SLM. To overcome this problem, I have developed a new method known as the optimal sampled phase-only hologram (OSPOH) [4]. My research collaborators have also inspired me with good ideas and suggestions in the course of development. The method is outlined as follows. First, a sampled phase-only hologram H_P (m,n) is generated based on a down-sampling lattice D(m,n). The source image I(m,n) is down-sampled with D(m,n) to a down-sampled image I_D(m,n). Mathematically, we have H_P (m,n)=arg[I_D (m,n)*f(m,n;z_0 )], (1) and I_D (m,n)=I(m,n)×D(m,n). (2) The down-sampling lattice D(m,n) is comprised of a small periodic based unit B(m,n) of size τ×τ, where τ is the down-sampling factor. Each element of the basic unit has value of either +1 or -1. Denoting the modulus operator as ‘%’, Eq. (2) can be rewritten as I_D (m,n)=I(m,n)×B(m%τ,n%τ). (3) The quality of the reconstructed image is dependent on the down-sampling lattice D(m,n), which in turn is depending on the basic unit B(m,n). It can be inferred that for similar type of image contents, there should exist an optimal lattice/basic unit that results in the best reconstructed images. To deduce the optimal sampling lattice, a source image that is typical amongst its class is selected. An iterative process is conducted to find the optimal basic unit B(m,n) that results in the SPOH of the best reconstructed image. Briefly, the basic unit is modified in each iteration to evaluate whether the fidelity (in peak-signal-to-noise-ratio or PSNR) of the reconstructed image of the SPOH is improved. If affirmative, the new basic unit is retained, otherwise the previous one is taken for the next round of iteration. The process continues until the fidelity of the reconstructed has reached certain level, or terminates when the maximum allowable epochs has elapsed. As shown in [4], the reconstructed images of the OSPOHs are of high quality and similar to the original ones. A definite advantage of this method, as compared with the TDCF and the LDRS+AIA methods, is that only a single hologram is generated for each source image. Hence the OSPOH can be displayed as a single frame (at normal frame rate) on a phase-only SLM. This decreases the computation time and the complexity of the display unit, as compared with the two previous methods. The OSPOH method developed has fully met objectives 1, 3, and 4. 5. Development in the second (final) stage of the GRF project: Widening projection area To fulfill the second objective of the GRF project, the projection area is widened by multiplying an off-axis plane wave to the phase-only holograms that are generated with the TDCF, LRDS+AIA, or OSPOH methods. The angle of inclination of the plane waves along the horizontal and vertical directions steers the projected image to different areas on the display screen, hence widening the display area.

11200319.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200319.value: In this project I have developed three methods for generating phase-only holograms that can be displayed with a single spatial light modulator (SLM). The displayed image can be projected onto a screen with high optical efficiency, and with the focal plane adjusted through varying the depth parameter in the computation of the hologram. As such, the projection is lens free, removing the need of using bulky lens and mechanical parts for focusing the projected image. In addition, the projected image can be steered electronically (through adjusting two angular parameters in the computation) to different off-axis locations on the projected area, hence widening the projected area. The three methods are known as Time Division Comb Filtering (TDCF), Local Random Down-sampling Mask + Adaptive Intensity Accumulation (LRDS+AIA), and Optimal Sampled Phase-only Hologram (OSPOH). The TDCF enhances the holographic projected image through a filtering mechanism that is formed by rapidly displaying 2 or more offset sampled phase-only holograms (SPOHs). In the LRDS+AIA method, multiple SPOHs, each adopting a different down-sampling lattice that is adaptive to the contents of the reconstructed image, are displayed rapidly. Both the TDCF and the LRDS+AIA methods are based on the persistence of vision (POV) of human eyes in averaging different SPOHs of the same source image, leading to reduction of speckle noise and other imperfections (e.g. sparsity due to down-sampling). The OSPOH generates a phase-only hologram through a down-sampling lattice that has been optimized. Generating the optimal lattice is a one-off process, and the quality reconstructed image is of high quality. Performance of the OSPOH is the best amongst the 3 methods that have been developed in this GRF project.

11200319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200319.value: As mentioned in 6.1, performance of the OSPOH is the best amongst the 3 methods that have been developed in this GRF project. However, it is highly possible that the 3 methods can be integrated in certain ways to further improve the quality of the holograms. For example, TDCF can be applied to the OSPOH to suppress the speckle noise of the coherent illumination. The AIA method can be used to fine tune a small number of OSPOHs, and display them rapidly to increase the quality of the reconstructed images.

11200319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200319.value: Is it possible to have an optical projector that is of the size of a laser pointer, and which can project a wide and bright image? Optical projectors to date are usually bulky as lens and associated mechanical parts are needed to focus the projected image on the screen. The location of the projected image is fixed on the screen, and can only be moved to other places by changing the pose and location of the projector. In this GRF project, a holographic projector has been developed that does not require any lens or mechanical parts for focusing the image. In addition, the projected image can be electronically steered to different places through simple computation. The outcome of this project suggests the possibility of implementing a small, light-weighted, and economical optical projector that can project a large and bright image.

11200719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11200719.value: It is well known that nanograined metals (NMs) have a great potential as the next generation structural materials because of their high strength due to grain size refinement induced strengthening, as manifested in the Hall-Petch law. However, the abundance of grain boundaries, which are simply planar defects, could be problematic and cause issues, such as poor thermal stability and low fracture toughness, for the application of the NMs. To mitigate these issues, there was a surge of interest recently to transform a regular grain boundary into an ultra-thin amorphous film. To achieve this, the prior efforts were mainly focused on alloying a proper element into an existing NM, which could subsequently segregate into grain boundaries and cause amorphization therein. While this approach was already demonstrated to be effective on a few binary/ternary alloys, however, it is difficult to be extended to the multicomponent alloy systems with functional applications, such as Fe-based soft magnetic alloys, or the multicomponent alloy systems with economic advantage, such as Al-based alloys, owing to the increased chemical complexity in these systems. In this project, we propose several strategies to develop nanograined multicomponent alloys with an intergranular amorphous phase. In sharp contrast to the prior approach, we will start with a multicomponent metallic glass system as a template to develop the desired nanograined alloys. Through a well-designed protocol entailing ultrasonic excitation and thermal treatment, we are able to tune the properties of the intergranular amorphous phase in a systematic way, such as its thickness, composition, strength and the plastic flow ability. Once the project was funded, we will achieve the following goals through the combined efforts from experiments, theoretical modeling and atomistic simulations, which include (1) to understand the thermodynamic/microstructural mechanism for the formation of a nanograined structure in a metallic glass, (2) to understand the micromechanical mechanism to overcome the strength-plasticity trade-off in the obtained nanograined alloy, and (3) to provide the protocol that could enable people to develop the nanograined multicomponent alloy with a controlled intergranular amorphous phase and therefore desired properties. The outcome of the proposed research is expected to strengthen the position of Hong Kong as a hub in the fundamental research in metals and alloys, which could benefit the local manufacturing industries within the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area in the long run. 晶體合金強度通常隨著晶粒尺寸變小而增加，這通常被稱為霍爾佩奇(Hall-Petch)效應。由於此效應，納米晶合金相比普通合金而言通常具有較高的強度。然而大量晶界的存在也帶來納米晶合金的其他問題，比如較差的熱穩定性和較低的斷裂韌性。為了解決這些問題，現在一個通常使用的方法是通過在納米晶合金中加入新的元素達到界面偏析，從而達到界面非晶化。一般認為，非晶化後的界面能夠改善母合金的熱穩定性和斷裂韌性。然而，由於原子擴散在多組元合金中的複雜性 (比如鐵基和鋁基合金)，界面偏析方法通常應用於二元或者三元合金。在本項研究中，我們提出使用超聲和熱處理來通過非晶合金作為母合金在多組元合金中生成具有非晶晶界的納米晶合金的方法。結合試驗，理論和模擬，本項研究的結果旨在理解和製備高韌高強的複雜納米晶合金。

11200719.label: Realisation of objectives
11200719.value: Objective 1: We have achieved successful fabrication of nanocrystalline alloys by utilizing a Al-Y based metallic glass and employing thermal annealing techniques. Notably, we made an intriguing observation that the Al-Y metallic glass exhibits significant chemical heterogeneity, leading to the clustering of Y atoms, even in its pre-annealed state. These Y clusters serve as nucleation sites for the formation of nanocrystals during the thermal annealing process. In line with our proposed methodology, we conducted an extensive characterization of the resulting alloy's nanostructure. This involved subjecting the alloys to annealing at various temperatures and durations, followed by comprehensive thermal analyses and elemental mapping of the resulting nanostructured Al-based alloys. Additionally, we investigated the evolution of the nanostructure over different annealing time periods. The presence of chemical heterogeneity and the utilization of thermal annealing techniques have provided valuable insights into the formation and manipulation of nanocrystalline structures in the Al-Y based metallic glass system. These findings contribute to our understanding of the underlying mechanisms governing the development of nanocrystalline alloys. In addition, within the scope of this project, we employed an innovative approach utilizing ultra-fast nano-calorimetry to investigate the influence of chemical heterogeneity on stress relaxation behaviour in the Al-based metallic glass, both before and after crystallization. Notably, our results revealed the presence of a distinct and pronounced fast beta relaxation peak, alongside the conventional slow beta relaxation peak, as observed in the dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) curve. Intriguingly, this fast relaxation peak could be eliminated through thermal annealing. We further discovered that the stress relaxation behavior plays a crucial role in both the crystallization and deformation processes of metallic glass and metallic glass-based composites. Nanocrystals tend to nucleate in regions where atoms exhibit higher activity compared to their neighbours, thereby serving as preferential sites for crystallization during thermal annealing. By carefully controlling the thermal annealing process, we successfully achieved extensive nanocrystallization within the Al-based metallic glass. These findings shed light on the intricate relationship between chemical heterogeneity, stress relaxation, and the formation of nanocrystalline structures in metallic glasses. The ability to manipulate and control these factors contributes to the development of advanced metallic-glass composites with tailored properties and improved performance. Furthermore, it is important to highlight that we have introduced a novel fabrication technique called polymer surface buckling enabled exfoliation (PSBEE) for producing nanocrystalline Al nanosheets or nanomembranes. In addition, we have employed machine learning methods to facilitate the discovery of new Al-containing metallic glasses, with the support of this project. One notable achievement is the development of a novel Al-containing metallic glass system, namely Al-Co-Zr-Hf. When compared to conventional Zr-based metallic glasses, this newly discovered metallic glass system exhibits remarkable chemical heterogeneity. Objective 2: Additionally, we conducted a comprehensive characterization of the properties of the Al-based amorphous nanocrystalline alloys using various techniques, including transmission electron microscopy (TEM), 3D atom probe tomography (3D APT), X-ray diffraction. Furthermore, we employed DMA, regular tensile tests, atomic force microscopy tests, and microcompression tests to further investigate the properties of these alloys. The DMA tests provided insights into the plastic flow behaviour of Al-based metallic glasses and their correlation with the observed properties. We extended our findings to a broader range of metallic glasses, including high entropy metallic glasses that consist of multiple principal elements. However, in the case of regular Al-based metallic glass, we did not observe significant strain hardening under tension, even after the precipitation of nanocrystals following thermal annealing. This finding highlights the unique behaviour of Al-based metallic glasses and suggests the need for further exploration and understanding of the underlying mechanisms governing their mechanical properties. Objective 3: In order to gain a deeper understanding of the atomic-level mechanisms underlying plasticity in amorphous nanocrystalline alloys, we conducted extensive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Our simulations focused on the evolution of local atomic packing, von-Mises strain, and atomic-level stress within our atomic model. For example, we obtained typical mappings of these properties around a 5 nm nanocrystal at different applied strains (εapp), namely 0%, 8%, and 15%. Initially, at zero applied strain (εapp = 0%), the interface between the amorphous and crystalline regions exhibits diffusive behavior, with a transition layer of approximately one atom size. As the applied strain increases to 8% and 15%, we observe evident local structural rearrangements occurring around the diffusive interface. These rearrangements result in the reshuffling of atoms, resembling a local order-disorder transition, and consequently lead to local boundary migrations into the nanocrystal. The mappings of von-Mises strains at different εapp clearly indicate that deformation is primarily accommodated within the amorphous interphase. In contrast, deformation in the nanocrystal is concentrated primarily at its boundary, where the local reshuffling of atoms occurs. This phenomenon promotes deformation compatibility or co-deformation, enhancing the ductility of the material. However, it is important to note that this co-deformation mechanism begins to fail at εapp = 8%, resulting in void nucleation at other locations. Throughout the deformation process, the overall local short-range order, such as crystal-like order, within the amorphous interphase remains mostly unchanged, regardless of the applied strain. These observations provide valuable insights int the atomic-scale behavior and mechanisms that govern plasticity in amorphous nanocrystalline alloys. Objective 4: Our findings demonstrate the valuable insights that can be gained from analyzing the dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) curves of metallic glasses, including Al-based metallic glass, to optimize processing routes and enhance the strength-plasticity synergy. However, these results also emphasize the critical role of chemical composition and the resulting chemical heterogeneity in achieving the desired synergy. As part of this project, we have made significant progress in developing two machine learning methods to identify Al-containing metallic glasses that can serve as ideal amorphous templates for the formation of amorphous nanocrystal composites. The first machine learning method adopts a forward design approach, establishing a link between the chemical composition and attributes such as glass-forming ability and other physical properties. The second method employs an inverse design approach, establishing a correlation between the mechanical properties, primarily hardness and elastic modulus, and the chemical compositions of metallic glasses. Through these approaches, we have successfully identified novel Al-containing metallic glasses with promising properties. By leveraging these machine learning techniques, we have made significant advancements in the discovery and design of Al-containing metallic glasses, paving the way for the development of improved amorphous nanocrystal composites. The combination of experimental and computational approaches has proven to be a powerful tool for materials discovery and has the potential to revolutionize the field of metallic glass research.

11200719.label: Major findings and research outcome
11200719.value: By subjecting Al-based metallic glasses to controlled thermal annealing at temperatures linked to their dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) curves, we can induce the formation of extensive nanocrystals within the amorphous matrix. The presence of these nanocrystals can be attributed to the activity of "active" atoms, which contribute to both fast and slow beta relaxations observed in the DMA curves. When the size of the nanocrystals is small, below 10 nm, the deformation of the amorphous-nanocrystal composite is primarily accommodated by the amorphous matrix, while the nanocrystals contribute to mechanical strengthening. However, in the case of regular Al-based metallic glasses like Al-Y based metallic glass, the resulting amorphous-nanocrystal composite still lacks the ability for strain hardening under tension. To address this limitation, novel Al-containing metallic glasses, such as high entropy metallic glasses, have been developed using machine learning techniques. These newly discovered metallic glasses exhibit unique chemical heterogeneity, making them ideal candidates for serving as amorphous templates in the formation of amorphous nanocrystal composites. Furthermore, they demonstrate distinctive behaviors in mechanical dynamic analyses and exhibit enhanced deformability compared to conventional metallic glasses. The combination of machine learning-driven discovery and the utilization of unique chemical heterogeneity has opened up new possibilities for developing advanced metallic glasses with improved mechanical properties.

11200719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11200719.value: We are actively advancing the development of the machine learning models that were initially created with the support of this project. Our aim is to extend the applicability of these models to explore entirely new metallic glass systems. One of the current challenges we face with traditional Al-based metallic glasses is the limited availability of data. To overcome this limitation, we have amalgamated data from various classes of metallic glass systems, including those based on Al, Zr, Cu, and Co. Through this comprehensive data analysis, we have made a significant breakthrough by discovering a hybrid or high entropy metallic glass. Remarkably, this new metallic glass exhibits tensile ductility even at room temperature, a characteristic that was previously elusive in Al-based metallic glasses. The observation of strain hardening behavior in this high entropy metallic glass has garnered substantial interest, leading to the acquisition of further funding. This additional support will enable us to conduct an in-depth study and exploration of the unique properties and potential applications of this strain-hardening high entropy metallic glass.

11200719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11200719.value: Amorphous metals, also known as metallic glasses, lack a crystalline structure and typically exhibit brittleness at room temperature, which has limited their use as structural materials. Overcoming this brittleness is crucial for harnessing the full potential of metallic glasses. One effective approach to enhance their toughness is by utilizing metallic glass as a template for the formation of amorphous nanocrystalline composites through controlled thermal annealing. In this project, we focused on investigating the application of this approach to Al-based metallic glass. Our research has provided significant insights into the underlying deformation mechanisms in amorphous-nanocrystalline composites. By studying these materials, we have gained valuable knowledge about how their properties can be tailored and optimized. Furthermore, as part of this project, we have developed advanced machine learning tools that enable rapid identification of the chemical composition required for Al-containing metallic glasses to serve as effective templates in the formation of amorphous nanocrystalline composites. These tools streamline the materials discovery process and facilitate the design of novel metallic glass systems with enhanced properties.

11201519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201519.value: This project will develop statistical methods that utilize the Gaussian process (GP) model to perform robust parameter design (RPD) with multiple loss functions that measure the quality of multiple responses, and noise factors that have probability density function estimated by a kernel density estimator (KDE). Due to the widespread availability of computers and physical modeling software, computer models, also called simulators, are increasingly used for designing engineering systems. These models are often computer codes that implement numerical algorithms, notably the finite element method, to solve partial differential equations (PDEs). Due to the complexity of engineering systems, simulators for such systems can be time-consuming to run. To circumvent this difficulty, an emulator constructed with data obtained by running the simulator according to an experimental design can be employed. In design of engineering systems, there is always the need to study multiple responses with quality level measured by several loss functions (or equivalently, desirability functions), and input factors can often be classified into two types, i.e., control factors and noise factors. Control factors are inputs set by designers while noise factors vary randomly in the actual system. The average quality level is quantified by the expectation of the loss functions with respect to the distribution of the noise factors. Note that it is not always easy or desirable to combine all loss functions into a single objective function. Thus, it can be preferable to seek the Pareto frontier, which is an idea that has been scarcely considered in RPD. Moreover, it can be important to use a realistic estimate of the noise distribution than simply assuming the noise factors follow some standard distribution such as the normal distribution. This project will develop an approach based on the GP model to seek the Pareto frontier for multiple expected loss functions for RPD with time-consuming simulators. Our approach will assume the noise factor distribution is estimated from data with a mixture normal KDE. We shall develop analytical expressions for the posterior mean and covariance functions of the expected quality loss vector using appropriate modeling assumptions so that computations are simplified. We shall use a model-based approach to solve the experimental design problem posed by the nonstandard distribution of the noise factors. Finally, we shall develop an expected improvement (EI) criterion for seeking the Pareto frontier via sequential experimental design together with a fast and deterministic way to compute the criterion to ease optimization. 该项目将开发一种基于高斯过程（GP）模型的统计方法来进行具有多个损失函数以衡量多个响应质量的稳健参数设计（RPD），并采用核密度估计（ KDE）来估计噪声因子的概率密度函数。 由于计算机和物理建模软件的广泛可用性，计算机模型（也称为模拟器）越来越多地用于工程设计系统。这些模型通常是用于实现数值算法，特别是有限元方法的计算机代码，以求解偏微分方程（PDE）。由于工程系统的复杂性，用于此类系统的模拟器运行起来可能非常耗时。为了解决这一难题，可以采用由根据试验设计运行模拟器从而获得的数据来构建的仿真器。 在工程系统的设计中，通常需要研究具有通过若干损失函数（或满意度函数）来衡量质量水平的多个响应，并且输入通常可以分为两种类型，即可控因子和噪声因子。可控因子是设计者设定的输入，而噪声因子在实际系统中随机变化。平均质量水平可通过损失函数对于噪声分布的期望来量化。注意，将所有损失函数组合成单个目标函数并不总是容易的或适合的。因此，更好的方式是求得帕累托边界，而且这种方法在RPD中几乎没有被考虑过。此外，使用噪声分布的实际估计比仅仅假设噪声因子服从某些标准分布（例如正态分布）更重要。 该项目将开发一种基于GP模型的方法来寻找基于耗时模拟器的具有多个期望损失函数的RPD的帕累托边界。我们的方法假设噪声分布是根据混合正态KDE的数据来估计的。我们将使用适当的建模假设来给出期望质量损失向量的后验均值和协方差函数的解析表达式以简化计算。我们将使用基于模型的方法来解决由噪声因子的非标准分布引起的试验设计问题。最后，我们将开发一个期望改进（EI）准则，通过序贯试验设计寻找帕累托边界，同时以快速和确定性的方式计算该准则来简化优化过程。

11201519.label: Realisation of objectives
11201519.value: Objective 1 has been addressed in Articles #1, #3, #4, #5, #7, and #8. Article #1/#3/#4/#7/#8 considers the problem of robust parameter design (RPD) via time-consuming simulators. In this problem, there are two types of real-valued inputs that are fixed in each simulator run called control factors (inputs whose values in the real system are decision variables) and noise factors (inputs that are random in the real system), and the objective function, whose minimizer is the optimal value of the vector of control factors, is an expected quality loss (EQL) of one/multiple output(s)/response(s) of a simulator. The EQL of one/multiple output(s) is the expectation of the loss for the output(s) (given by a real-valued loss function evaluated at the output(s)) with respect to the noise-factor distribution (joint distribution of the noise factors in the real system), where herein, loss refers to quality loss and an output refers to a real-valued output. Article #1 proposes an analytically tractable Gaussian process (GP) emulator/model/surrogate of multiple outputs of a simulator with internal noise factors (each such factor is a deviation from a nominal value given by a control factor). The model is applied to predict the expected quadratic quality loss (EQQL) of one/multiple output(s), i.e., the EQL of one/multiple output(s) with loss given by a quadratic loss function. Article #3 proposes the shifted log loss GP (SLLGP) emulator, which models a shifted log transformation of the loss as a GP, for predicting the EQL of multiple outputs with loss given by an arbitrary loss function. The SLLGP emulator is equipped with an analytically tractable approximation to the EQL's posterior distribution, which makes computing its EQL predictions inexpensive, and it predicts EQLs better than alternative emulators (e.g., a GP model for the loss). Article #7 proposes an analytically tractable bi-fidelity GP emulator, called the autoregressive SLLGP emulator, that extends the SLLGP emulator in Article #3 to bi-fidelity simulations. Bi-fidelity simulations comprise simulations at two fidelity/accuracy levels, called the high-fidelity (HF) and low-fidelity (LF) levels, and a bi-fidelity emulator/model/surrogate utilizes data on the HF and LF simulators' outputs (HF and LF outputs) to predict quantities depending on those outputs. The autoregressive SLLGP emulator outperforms alternative emulators in predicting EQLs of HF outputs. Article #4 proposes an analytically tractable GP emulator of multiple functional outputs for predicting the EQQL of those outputs in multi-functional target RPD. Article #8 employs a standard GP model for each output and derives an analytically tractable formula for the posterior mean of the EQL of an output that works for certain loss functions. Article #1/#3/#4/#7/#8 approximates the EQL via a quadrature formula (a weighted sum of the loss at finitely many points with points and weights obtained from a quadrature scheme for computing expectations with respect to the noise-factor distribution), which is an approach that works for most noise-factor distributions. This enables the emulator/model proposed/employed in Article #1/#3/#4/#7/#8 to be used for predicting EQLs in RPD with most noise-factor distributions, including mixture-normal distributions. Furthermore, an independent version of the emulator/model proposed/employed in Article #1/#3/#4/#7/#8 can be used to predict each element of a multivariate EQL, i.e., a vector of EQLs. Lastly, Article #5 proposes a bi-fidelity GP emulator, called boundary modified autoregressive GP (BMAGP) emulator, that improves the standard autoregressive GP emulator by incorporating boundary information, i.e., information that a HF output converges to an LF output as certain inputs to the HF simulator converge to zero. The BMAGP emulator can outperform the autoregressive GP emulator in predicting EQLs of HF outputs. Objective 2 has been addressed in Articles #1, #2, and #6. Article #1 proposes an initial experimental design (IED) for building GP emulators for RPD with independently distributed internal noise factors. Article #2 proposes methods for generating Latin hypercube designs (LHDs) in hypercube design domains that perform well in terms of the expected entropy criterion, i.e., the average of a GP model's entropy for every projection (every subset of inputs). These designs, called maximum expected entropy transformed LHDs (MEETLHDs), have good GP-model-based properties in all projections, i.e., they perform well for constructing a GP model to predict an output/loss as a function of any subset of inputs. Thus, MEETLHDs are useful IEDs for RPD when the inputs (control/noise factors) with nonnegligible effects on an output/loss are unknown a priori. They are suitable IEDs when the noise factors have independent distributions such as independent mixture-normal distributions, as certain hypercube design domains are apt in this case. Article #6 proposes an algorithm for generating IEDs (specifically, LHDs) with good space-filling properties. Objective 3 has been addressed in Articles #1 and #8. Article #1 proposes and compares three acquisition functions (AFs) for minimizing the EQQL of multiple outputs via a Bayesian optimization procedure (BOP), and develops efficient methods for computing the AFs. Note that a BOP is a sequential-design scheme that finds an optimal point by adding an experiment-design point, chosen by maximizing an AF, in each of finitely many iterations. In Article #1, the EQQL of multiple outputs can be taken as a weighted sum (with positive weights) of the elements of a vector of EQQLs (a multivariate EQL) that are each the EQQL of an output. In this case, the minimizer of the EQQL of multiple outputs is a point on the Pareto frontier for the elements of the vector of EQQLs, and a proposed AF can be applied to minimize each of multiple weighted sums of those elements (with different positive weights) to find multiple Pareto-frontier points. Article #8 proposes a theoretically justified AF for a BOP for solving the problem of minimizing the EQL of an output of a simulator subject to an upper-bound constraint on the EQL of each of a few other outputs of the simulator. A unique optimal solution to this problem is a point on the Pareto frontier for the EQLs of the outputs (EQLs in the objective function and constraints), and multiple Pareto-frontier points can be found by solving multiple versions of the problem with different upper bounds in the constraints via the proposed AF.
