11201519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11201519.value: In this project, novel GP emulators, IEDs for constructing GP emulators, and sequential design methods based on GP emulators (BOPs to be specific) are developed for RPD with one or more EQL objective functions via time-consuming simulations. Major research outcomes of this project are discussed below. Article #1 proposes and compares three AFs for minimizing the EQQL of multiple outputs via a BOP. Accurate and computationally efficient methods are developed for computing the proposed AFs, and theoretical justifications are provided for two of those AFs. Article #8 proposes a novel, theoretically justified, and computationally efficient AF for a BOP for minimizing the EQL of an output of a simulator subject to an upper-bound constraint on the EQL of each of a few other outputs of the simulator. The AFs proposed in Articles #1 and #8 allow points (values of the vector of control factors) on the Pareto frontier of finitely many EQL objective functions to be computed efficiently with theoretical guarantees, and the AFs are found to give BOPs that outperform existing BOPs. Articles #3, #4, #5, and #7 propose novel GP emulators for EQL prediction in RPD. The SLLGP emulator proposed in Article #3 models a data-based shifted log transformation of the loss as a GP. It predicts EQLs better than alternative emulators that model fixed transformations of the loss as GPs due to the added flexibility provided by the data-based shifted log transformation. The SLLGP emulator is computationally efficient since (i) analytical formulas are available to facilitate computation of estimates of its parameters, and (ii) it uses an analytically tractable approximation to the EQL's posterior distribution. Article #7 extends the SLLGP emulator to bi-fidelity simulations. Article #4 proposes a GP emulator of multiple functional outputs and applies it predict the EQQL of those outputs in multi-functional target RPD. Computationally efficient analytical formulas for computing estimates of the proposed emulator's parameters and the proposed emulator's predictions are obtained via Kronecker product matrix algebra formulas. Article #5 proposes a novel bi-fidelity GP emulator, called the BMAGP emulator, that exploits boundary information to improve the standard autoregressive GP emulator's predictions of the HF output(s). Lastly, Article #2 proposes methods for generating LHDs that perform well in terms of the average of a GP model's entropy for every projection. Such LHDs are good IEDs for constructing the GP model when the inputs with nonnegligible effects on the output(s) are unknown a priori.

11201519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11201519.value: Two topics have potential for further development. First, it is of interest to extend one of the AFs proposed in Article #1, which is developed for finding the minimizer of the EQQL of multiple outputs, to obtain a new AF for finding, via a BOP, the minimizer of the EQL of multiple outputs with loss given by an arbitrary loss function. This new AF can be used to minimize a weighted sum (with positive weights) of EQLs that are each the EQL of an output with loss given by an arbitrary loss function. Thus, the new AF can be used to find the Pareto frontier for EQLs that are each the EQL of an output with loss given by an arbitrary loss function. Second, it is of interest to develop a BOP (together with its AF) for the problem of minimizing the EQL of HF outputs in RPD via time-consuming bi-fidelity simulations. This BOP and its AF can be developed based on either the autoregressive SLLGP emulator proposed in Article #7 or the BMAGP emulator proposed in Article #5.

11201519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11201519.value: Robust parameter design (RPD) via time-consuming simulations with one or more expected quality loss (EQL) objective functions is an important class of engineering problems. This project advances the methodology frontier for such problems in three areas: (1) Gaussian process (GP) emulators/models for predicting EQLs, (2) initial experimental designs for RPD, and (3) acquisition functions (AFs) for minimizing EQLs via certain Bayesian optimization procedures. For (1), this project proposes an emulator that models a data-based shifted log transformation of the loss as a GP and a bi-fidelity version of the emulator, which both predict EQLs better than alternative emulators that model fixed transformations of the loss as GPs. For (1), this project also proposes a computationally efficient GP emulator of multiple functional outputs for multi-functional target RPD, and a bi-fidelity GP emulator that improves the standard autoregressive GP emulator with boundary information. For (2), this project proposes methods for generating Latin hypercube designs with good GP-model-based properties in all subsets of inputs. For (3), this project proposes theoretically justified and computationally efficient AFs for minimizing the EQL given by a quadratic loss function, and for minimizing the EQL of an output subject to upper bounds on the EQLs of other outputs.

11201919.label: Project Objectives
11201919.value: Isogeometric collocation methods for PDE-based analysis suitable parameterization: Given a complex CAD model, we investigate collocation methods for constructing an analysis suitable parameterization of the computational domain through the solution of partial differential equations. Structured constraints for PDE-based analysis suitable parameterization: We also design various structured constraints for integration in the collocation system of equations for achieving desired properties of the resulting parameterization of the input boundary representation. Field-aligned parameterization for accurate and fast converging isogeometric analysis: Based on the constraints developed through the project and posterior solution error analysis, we further investigate methods for producing field-aligned parameterization with appropriate control of local degrees of freedom for producing accurate and fast converging field solutions. Application of the developed algorithms for isogeometric thermal analysis: The developed methods and related algorithms on analysis suitable parameterization will be applied for isogeometric thermal analysis and simulation of several 3D/4D printing processes. Various case studies will be produced for testing and verification.

11201919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11201919.value: Isogeometric analysis (IGA) is an active field of research for integrated design and analysis of engineering objects using the same set of basis functions for computer aided design (CAD). However, the present CAD industry is not entirely compatible with the concept of isogeometric analysis and not all CAD models can be directly used in isogeometric analysis. One often needs to construct an analysis suitable parameterization of the computational domain from a boundary representation (B-rep) model for isogeometric analysis. Construction of spline surfaces or volumetric spline models with given boundaries is one of the classical problems in computer aided geometric design. In connection with analysis suitable parameterization for IGA, the topic re-attracted much interest in recent years. It is still a challenging problem especially for parameterization from a complex input boundary representation. This project investigates alternative methods for analysis suitable parameterization of computational domains from input boundary representations using isogeometric collocation methods with structured constraints for achieving desired parameterization. The methods are based on isogeometric solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) with boundary conditions being the input boundary representation plus structured constraints that can be specified either over the boundary or inside the computational domain in meeting desired properties. While the resulting parameterization will be for isogeometric analysis, the PDEs will also be solved using one of the general methodologies of isogeometric analysis, namely isogeometric collocation methods. Additional structured constraints will be designed and implemented in the system of collocation equations of the PDEs for achieving desired properties of the resulting parameterization. The project will also investigate field-aligned parameterization by applying structured constraints based on extracted structural shape information of the input boundary and a posterior analysis of solution error distribution. Main areas of research in the project include (1) the development of a general framework on isogeometric collocation methods for parameterization of computational domains using NURBS and subdivision schemes, (2) design and analysis of structured constraints for achieving desired properties of resulting parameterization, (3) field-aligned dynamic parameterization with desired distribution of degrees of freedom for application specific solutions, and (4) application of the resulting parameterization in thermal analysis and simulation. The proposed research will contribute to isogeometric analysis with added capability and flexibility in handling a wider range of engineering objects and solutions to several key research issues of isogeometric analysis. It will also contribute to future CAD technologies compatible with isogeometric analysis. 等幾何分析（IGA）的基本思想是用與計算機輔助設計（CAD）兼容的模型或基函數進行後續工程分析。然而目前並非所有CAD模型都可以直接用來做等幾何分析，對於目前工業界通用的以邊界表示（B-rep）的CAD模型，通常需要在其計算域構建一個適用於等幾何分析的參數化模型。給定一個以邊界表示的CAD模型，該項目研究基於偏微分方程（PDE）求解而生成的適用於等幾何分析的參數化模型。其PDE的解也將使用等幾何分析中的配點法來產生。在PDE求解過程中的邊界條件為其計算域CAD模型的邊界表示（B-rep），同時在PDE求解的配點方程系統中還添加了為實現參數化所需一些屬性而特別設計的結構化約束。該項目的主要研究領域包括（1）建立一套基於等幾何配點法PDE求解的用有理樣條和體細分對計算域進行參數化的求解框架；（2）研究各種以實現參數化所需特性的結構約束及其設計；（3）研究適用於一些情形下具備與解相關及自由度分佈可控的動態參數化解決方案；及（4）將如上研究結果用於購建在一些熱系統分析和模擬中所需的適用於等幾何分析的參數化建模。該研究項目將提供等幾何分析中一些關鍵技術及解決方案，有助於提升等幾何分析能力及靈活性，從而用於更廣泛的CAD模型等幾何分析。它還將為實現未來與等幾何分析兼容的CAD技術做出相關貢獻。

11202019.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11202019.value: 投资组合优化的协同式神经动力学方法

11202019.label: Project Objectives
11202019.value: In face of nonconvexity and discontinuity of some performance indices and constraints, our first objective of the proposed research is to develop collaborative neurodynamic systems for solving portfolio optimization and related problems with nonconvex and discontinuous risk measures based on our recent findings on collective neurodynamic approaches to global optimization. In presence of discrete decision variables such as binary or other integers due to confined cardinality or round-lot integrity in asset holdings and transactions, our second objective of the proposed research is to develop collaborative neurodynamic systems for portfolio optimization with mixed-integer variables by extending our recent findings on neurodynamics-based global optimization to combinatorial optimization. In view of multiple-facet nature of portfolio selection with multiple conflicting objective functions such as expected investment return versus market risk, our third objective of the proposed research is to develop collaborative neurodynamic systems for multi-criteria portfolio selection with more than one objectives with considerations of risk behaviors of investors by means of adaptive scalarization and multi-attribute utility functions based on our new findings on collaborative neurodynamic approaches to multi-objective optimization. In pursuit of maximal accumulative wealth or minimal index tracking error in long-term investments, our fifth objective of the proposed research is to develop collaborative neurodynamic systems for multi-period portfolio selection with wealth dynamics modeling and receding horizon optimization based on the state-of-the-art results on adaptive dynamic programming and our recent findings on neurodynamics-based nonlinear and robust model predictive control.

11202019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202019.value: 从学术和经济的角度来看，投资组合的选择对金融投资具有重要的意义。在过去的60年里，投资组合的选择被广泛的探索，至少五位诺贝尔经济学奖获得者的工作显示出了这一点。作为现代金融学的基石，马尔可维茨开创性的均值-方差分析为投资组合优化提供了一个优美的框架，投资回报和风险都是量化的。尽管均值-方差理论具有重要的理论意义，但它并不完美，因为它的一些假设是不现实的。由于投资者对收益和损失的风险行为通常是不对称的，潜在的概率分布是非正态的，方差不是捕获收益/损失风险行为的理想风险度量。虽然有几种方法比较合理，但一些方法的不确定性和不连续性对投资组合的数学和计算优化提出了巨大挑战。 与金融领域的投资组合选择研究相比，科学与工程领域的人工智能研究已经活跃了几十年，近年来由于深度学习的成功而变得非常流行。作为神经网络研究的一个分支，神经动态优化已经发展成为一种并行和分布式的优化方法，并且已经开发出许多用于解决各种优化问题的回归神经网络。我们最近的研究结果表明，由多个神经网络组成的神经动力系统与群智能规则相协作，对于有约束全局、多周期、多目标优化具有较好的效果。结果推广到二级优化和组合优化。神经动力优化与投资组合管理相结合，将取得丰硕的成果和重大突破。尽管神经动力学优化研究取得了一定的进展，但基于神经动力学的投资组合优化在金融工程和管理的深度和规模上具有明显的复杂性，值得深入研究。 在本研究中，我们将在神经计算的基础上，对投资组合选择的智能方法及相关问题进行系统的研究。该项目将由五个连贯的部分组成，重点是在五个主要环境中研究和开发协同神经动力方法来优化投资组合。拟议研究的预期结果包括新见解、收敛模型、创新方法和组合优化的集成系统。基于神经动力学的投资组合优化智能系统将成为机构和个人投资者可行的问题解决工具。预计该项目的成功完成将大大推进投资组合优化理论和实践的前沿。

11202019.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202019.value: In this project, numerous computationally intelligent methods were developed for financial engineering in general and portfolio optimization in particular. Specifically, neurodynamics-based robust portfolio selection was addressed in the minimax and biconvex frameworks ([4], [21] in Section 8; [2], [5] in Section 9). In addition, cardinality-constrained portfolio selection based on collaborative neurodynamic optimization was investigated ([11], [15], [48] in Section 8). Moreover, decentralized portfolio selection based on collaborative neurodynamic optimization and cooperative-competitive multi-agent systems was addressed ([21], [23] in Section 8). Furthermore, portfolio optimization based on various risk measures and performance indices was investigated ([23], [46] in Section 8). In addition to active portfolio selection, index-tracking approaches to portfolio selection in multiple investment periods were also developed based on clustering and regression of historical financial data ([4] in Section 9; ([47] in Section 8). More results are being obtained along this line of regression-based index-tracking approach. In this project, many new neurodynamic optimization and evp;utionary optimization approaches were also developed to solve nonlinear programming and mixed-integer optimization problems in portfolio selection ([1], [6], [12], [27], [29], [31], [33]-[38], [42], [44] [45] in Sec. 8). These methods were extended for solving several problems related to financial data analysis, such as data clustering ([13], [17], [39], [41] in Section 8), classification ([7] in Section 8), regression ([22] in Section 8), sparse data processing ([2], [16] in Sec. 8 and [1] in Sec. 9), feature selection ([3], ]9], [20], [24], [40] in Section 8), feature extraction ([2], [14]), computational games ([43] in Section 8 and [7] in Section 9), hash -bit selection ([8] & [19] in Section 8), and other logistics-related optimization problems ([3], [6] in Section 9). Furthermore, in-depth neurodynamic behaviors were analyzed theoretically ([5], [10], [18], [25], [26]. ][28], [30], [32] in Section 8) to facilitate the further design and applications of neurodynamics-based portfolio optimization and other financial engineering tasks.

11202019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202019.value: Many avenues are open for further investigations. In addition to the results reported in the published papers, we are presently investigating new collaborative neurodynamic approaches to cardinality-constrained portfolio optimization based on heterogeneous neurodynamic models (e.g., discrete-Hopfield networks and projection neural networks). Moreover, we are working on stock index tracking for multi-period portfolio selection via neurodynamics-driven Gaussian regression with temporally weighted historical data. Furthermore, we are developing an enhanced version of optimization-based index tracking by minimizing risk-adjusted returns subject to one-sided index tracking constraints. In addition, we are also developing a new class of collaborative neurodynamic optimization approaches for global and mixed-integer optimization based on Bayesian optimization to be used for intelligent financial engineering problem-solving.

11202019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202019.value: Portfolio selection is of great interest for financial investments from academic and economic points of view. Over the past six decades, portfolio selection has been extensively explored, highlighted by the works of at least five Nobel laureates in economics. As a cornerstone of finance, modern portfolio theory is featured in Markowitz’s ground-breaking work on mean-variance analysis, which provides a formal framework for portfolio optimization with quantified investment returns and risks. In this project, systematic investigations were performed on intelligent methodology for portfolio selection and related problems. The project consists of four coherent parts aiming at four objectives and focusing on the research and development of collaborative neurodynamic approaches to portfolio optimization in four major settings. The outcomes of the research include new insights, new neurodynamic models, rigorous theory, innovative methods, and integrated systems for portfolio optimization. The results obtained in this project would significantly advance the frontiers of portfolio optimization in both theory and practice.

11202119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202119.value: Mobile robots are populating the structured environments, thanks to the progress in sensing and computation. However, the continuing effort of advancing mobile robots beyond manufacturing plant is yet unsuccessful. While moving into the everyday world that human inhabits -- shopping malls, canteens, or train stations, the current generation of mobile robots suffer from their limited navigation abilities in cluttered and uncontrolled human environments. The dense human environments pose three main challenges for mobile robots. 1) The robot may get lost, i.e., cannot accurately localize itself in the scenario due to severe occlusions in the crowd. 2) The robot may get frozen, i.e., cannot make progress toward its goal by getting stuck in the crowd. 3) The robot may behave intrusively, i.e., cannot coordinate well with nearby humans but frequently interrupt the crowd flow. These difficulties lead to the mobile robot's poor performance in dense human scenarios. In this project, we propose a novel deep reinforcement learning based framework to simultaneously solve the three challenges mentioned above. First, we enhance the robot's mobility and unfreeze the robot by using a local navigation policy optimized using the deep reinforcement learning. The learned policy also naturally considers the coordination between the robot and the crowd. The excellent local mobility will then play a central role in the robot's recovery strategy when the robot is getting lost. In particular, the robot will attempt to regain its localization certainty by adaptively approaching a set of recovery positions in the scenario, which are not only rich in visual features but can also be easily reached in the dense crowd using the learned local navigation policy. Finally, we endow the robot the ability to obey common sense rules and comply with social conventions. In particular, we use a recurrent neural network to predict the trajectories of the robot's neighboring agents, which are then used to define a suitable reward function for optimizing the navigation policy, where the hyperparameters in the reward are determined using inverse reinforcement learning. To the best of our knowledge, our method is the first approach in the world that can get the robot unlost, unfrozen, and unobtrusive in an unstructured scene with dense human crowds. It also fruits into new insights of theory and analysis about the optimal interaction between a robot and a dense crowd. We evaluate our method in both simulated and real-world environments and demonstrate that it outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches. 移動機器人目前在結構化環境中得到了廣泛應用。但在復雜的人群環境下，目前移動機器人的應用面臨極大的挑戰：移動的稠密人群使得移動機器人的傳感、定位、導航等模塊都不能有效運行。 本項目中，我們將使用新的深度強化學習技術解決移動機器人在稠密人群中的三個主要問題。首先，我們使用深度強化學習訓練的移動策略提高機器人在人群中的移動能力，能夠在流動的人流中自如穿梭。其次，我們利用機器人的良好移動能力提高了機器人在定位丟失的情況下的自主恢復能力。最後，我們使用循環神經網絡使得機器人能習得與人群協同移動的能力。

11202119.label: Realisation of objectives
11202119.value: All the objectives of the project have been accomplished and presented in 35 publications. Objective 2 [100%]: we have developed a localization recovery strategy for optimally balancing the benefit of regaining localization certainty and the overhead of navigating through dense crowds. Objective 3 [100%]: we have developed inverse reinforcement learning for optimizing the navigation reward function to enable the robot to obey common sense rules and comply with social conventions. Objective 4 [100%]: we have implemented two systems and testing benchmarks for getting robots unfrozen, unlost and unobtrusive in dense crowds. 11202119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11202119.value: 1. This project has generated three PhD dissertations. 2. We have published 35 papers under this project, comprising 26 journal articles and 9 conference papers. 3. We have constructed two prototypes of physical robots in crowded environments. One system is a quadruped dog robot designed for COVID-19 social distancing monitoring. This work was featured in IEEE Spectrum. The other is a mobile robot system that can autonomously navigate in the crowded open spaces of a university campus and park for over an hour without human intervention. 4. The publications listed in 2) address the following objectives: Papers 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 18, 21, 22, 27, 29 focus on developing policies optimized with Actor-Critic reinforcement learning, corresponding to Objective 1. We have also extended these techniques to tasks beyond navigation, such as robotic manipulation and human-robot collaboration. Papers 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 16, 21 address the issue of uncertainty in navigation, a primary obstacle preventing robots from recovering from localization failures. The developed techniques have also been applied to provide high-precision object detection in manipulation tasks, as seen in Paper 19. Papers 3-5, 9, 22, 26 explore the use of inverse reinforcement learning (iRL) to ensure robots adhere to common sense rules and social norms. Our initial forays into this area suggest that the same techniques could be valuable for human-robot collaboration, particularly in using iRL to discern human intentions. Papers 4, 5, 7, 27, 28, 29 describe the development of prototypes for robots navigating dense pedestrian crowds. As mentioned in 3), we have developed a quadruped dog robot prototype to test our system. Papers 1, 15 discuss the development of tactile sensors, which serve dual purposes. Firstly, mounted on the quadruped robot's feet, these sensors provide force feedback when navigating uneven terrain. Secondly, when extending our RL and iRL techniques from navigation to manipulation, we found that high-resolution tactile sensors are beneficial for various tasks. Papers 12, 20, 23 address a fundamental problem in navigation: the rapid generation of collision-free trajectories. These papers offer robust solutions as the low-level planner for complex navigation systems. Papers 24, 33 tackle the perception challenges encountered when navigating in dense crowds. Papers 17, 25 address the complex issue of manipulating the motion of dense crowds in proximity to the robot. Papers 30-35 provide essential machine learning tools necessary for the success of our learning-based navigation systems.

11202119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202119.value: When testing our navigation system in an open-world environment with a crowd, we discovered that it's crucial for the robot to comprehend text-centric semantic information. This includes 2D venue maps, directional signs, business signs, and so on. We are developing a novel text-aware exploration method that can perceive and recognize text in the environment and use venue maps as a form of prior knowledge. Firstly, we propose a text understanding method designed to accurately detect and recognize signs within the scene. This method includes a diffusion-based scene text retrieval approach and a 2D-to-3D semantic fusion strategy. Following that, we've designed a venue map-guided exploration-exploitation planner. This planner is intended to strike a balance between exploring unknown areas and exploiting known areas for precise signage recognition. We will conduct experiments in large-scale shopping malls to demonstrate the superior efficiency of our method in terms of signage coverage and recognition accuracy. Our approach is expected to outperform traditional exploration methods and the current state-of-the-art scene text spotting techniques.

11202119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202119.value: Mobile robots are becoming more common in places like factories, but they struggle when they try to move into busy, everyday places like malls or train stations. The problem is that these robots can't navigate well in crowded, messy spaces. They might get lost, stuck, or even get in people's way. This research project aims to fix these issues by using a smart learning method called deep reinforcement learning. It helps the robot move better in crowded places, find its way if it gets lost, and act in a way that doesn't bother people around it. The team also makes sure the robot follows common sense and social rules, using a special kind of computer brain (a neural network) to predict what people will do and how the robot should respond. The project is important because it's the first to make robots work well in really busy places with lots of people. It also teaches us more about how robots and people can get along best. Tests in fake and real-world places show that this method works better than anything else out there.

11202319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202319.value: The human visual system has no difficulty in achieving various perception tasks such as moving object detection, action/event recognition, etc. These tasks have been active computer vision research topics in the past decades that have led to numerous deterministic systems utilizing hand-crafted features been proposed. Recently automated visual perception systems have advanced rapidly through the use of deep learning resulting in many architectures, often each comprising of a model specially designed for a specific application. For instance, a convolutional neural network (CNN) can be used to group image pixels into meaningful regions, or a two-stream network has been developed for human action recognition through parallel processing of spatial and temporal image data. CNN is inspired by the connectivity of neurons of the human brain, and each neuron only responds to a small receptive field. The essence of various CNN architectures is feature extraction. Some studies have demonstrated that the features extracted by CNN are better than the hand-crafted features for recognition. While the goal of computer vision is to infer the meaning from image or video by machine, no part of CNN can be considered as resemblance of the human visual perception. In the human eye, the retina contains photoreceptor cells, each of which senses light and translates optical information into neural impulses. The photoreceptor cells are not distributed uniformly. The fovea, located in the center of retina, contains closely packed photoreceptor cells. Most of them are parvocellular cells (P-cells) which are sensitive to different wavelengths of light and create chromatic perception with the highest resolution. At the peripheral of the visual field, the photoreceptor cells (mostly magnocellular cells, M-cells), are more sensitive to achromatic motion information. We propose a foveated model that mimics the human visual system. It is a sequential process simulating the awareness of motion followed by the extraction of detailed information. Experimentation will first be performed applying the model on traditional computer vision methods. The concept of foveated vision will be integrated with deep learning. The parallel inferencing framework can best simulate the simultaneous analysis of multi-modal visual signals in the brain. Through these experimentations, we will demonstrate the improvement and applicability due to embedding of the foveated vision model to deep learning on computer vision research. Comparison will be made with state-of-the-art methods on benchmark datasets. To investigate the correlation of the foveated model with subjective evaluation, specific quantitative measures will be proposed and verified.

11202319.label: Realisation of objectives
11202319.value: Refer to objectives 1, 2 and 4: The human visual system, consisting of the eyes and brain, can perform various perception tasks. The retina receives sensory signals from the whole visual field. When a human observes a moving object, by fast movement of the eyes (saccadic moves) he/she can fixate (focus the gaze) on the object. By doing this, more information (color, high-frequency) of the object can be obtained whilst redundant processing of the peripheral visual field can be dispensed with. It is natural that such normal viewing can be modelled as a sequential process. We propose a model that mimics the human visual system. It is a sequential process simulating the awareness of changes (e.g., moving objects) in the image followed by the extraction of detailed information (e.g., color, texture) of the targets. Detection of visual change or anomaly in the image sequence is a common computer vision problem that can be formulated as background/foreground segregation. To achieve this, the background model is generated and the target (foreground) is detected via background subtraction. We propose a framework for visual change detection with three main modules: background modeler, convolutional neural network, and feedback scheme for background model updating. The background image frame and individual frames of the image sequence are input to the convolutional neural network for background/foreground segregation. For long-term analysis, maintenance of the background model is needed. A feedback scheme is proposed that can dynamically update the colors of the background frame. In the next investigation, we study the problem of image enhancement. We propose a model based on traditional computer vision approach. Computer vision applications usually rely on the features extracted from input images with good visibility. Image acquisition systems may produce degraded images with low contrast or distorted colors. For instance, bad weather (haze, fog) can cause images captured outdoor with low visibility. Haze removal, with the recovery of image radiance, ensures reliable features extracted from images and the image processing algorithm can achieve optimal performance. Inspired by the concept of image dehazing, we propose an image enhancement method that can be used to improve the visibility of the images. To evaluate the performance of the image enhancement method quantitatively, we propose to utilize the enhanced images for 3D model reconstruction. Our analysis finds that when fed into the photogrammetry software, the images enhanced by the proposed method can reconstruct 3D scene models with sub-millimeter mean errors, which are much better than those with the original degraded images. Refer to objectives 3 and 4: Afterwards, the concept of foveated vision is adopted for the research in machine learning-based image processing algorithms. Visual information processing has advanced rapidly through the use of deep learning – one branch of machine learning. We propose a deep learning model for image enhancement via image dehazing. The framework is based on the conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN). Our proposed model is improved with two modifications. We strengthen the analytical power of the network via the adoption of convolutional blocks with progressively more layers. Moreover, the entire dehazing framework is enhanced with the utilization of a new activation function in both the generator and discriminator modules. To evaluate the performance of the proposed image dehazing model quantitatively, various image dehazing datasets are employed for comparative analysis. Our proposed model outperforms other hand-crafted and deep learning-based image dehazing methods. Moreover, we utilize the dehazed images for target detection using the object detector YOLO. We demonstrate that the objects detected in images enhanced by our proposed dehazing model are significantly improved over those detected in the degraded images. Refer to objective 3: We continue to propose more deep learning-based models for other visual information processing problems. After studying the research on monocular 3D target detection based on pseudo-LiDAR data, we realize that the main limitations are due to the inaccuracy of the target position and the uncertainty in the depth distribution of the foreground target. To deal with these problems, we propose a monocular 3D object detection method with two innovative solutions. The first is a novel method based on joint image segmentation and geometric constraints, used to predict the target depth and provide the depth prediction confidence measure. For the second, we utilize the target scale, normalized with the Gaussian function, as a priori information. Next, we propose a deep learning model for micro-expression recognition. Humans show micro‑expressions (MEs) under some circumstances. MEs are a display of emotions that a human wants to conceal. MEs are typically of short duration and low intensity, it is hard to extract discriminative features from ME videos. Moreover, it is tedious to collect ME data. Existing ME datasets usually contain insufficient video samples. In this paper, we propose a deep learning model, double‑stream 3D convolutional neural network (DS‑3DCNN), for recognizing MEs captured in video. The recognition framework contains two streams of 3D‑CNN. The first extracts spatiotemporal features from the raw ME videos. The second extracts variations of the facial motions within the spatiotemporal domain. To facilitate feature extraction, the subtle motion embedded in a ME is amplified. To address the insufficient ME data, a macro‑expression dataset is employed to expand the training sample size. Supervised domain adaptation is adopted in model training in order to bridge the difference between ME and macro‑expression datasets. Finally, we propose a deep learning model for facial expression recognition (FER). The detection of facial muscle movements is crucial for FER. However, extracting these facial motion features is challenging for the following reasons: (1) without explicit labels of motion for training, there is no guarantee that convolutional neural networks (CNNs) can extract motions effectively; (2) compared to human action recognition, some facial motions are more subtle and thus harder to extract; and (3) the use of optical flow to extract motion features is time-consuming when using a commonly-used camera. In this work, we propose a Multi-Scale Correlation Module (MSCM) together with an adaptive fusion. Firstly, large as well as small facial motions are extracted by MSCM and encoded by CNNs. Then, an adaptive fusion module is used to aggregate motion features. With these modules, our recognition network is able to model both subtle and large motion features for video-based FER with only the RGB image frames as input. In summary, we realize all four objectives as mentioned in the application. We propose deterministic and deep learning-based computer vision algorithms to address various visual information processing problems: • Deterministic algorithm for image enhancement • Deep learning model for moving object detection via background subtraction • Deep learning model for image dehazing • Deep learning model for monocular 3D object detection • Deep learning model for facial expression recognition • Deep learning model for micro-expression recognition The models generally adopt the sequential framework, mimicking the human visual system to process and infer the visual signal first globally and then focusing on the details. For each proposed model, we adopt specific quantitative measures for performance evaluation and comparative analysis. We also evaluate the proposed models on some practical image-based applications, e.g.: • Evaluate the performance of the image enhancement method on 3D model reconstruction of building and construction site • Evaluate the performance of the image dehazing model on detection of targets (pedestrians, bicycle, car, bus, truck) in road scene images

The quantitative results show that our method outperforms many deterministic algorithms and deep learning models. Our analysis finds that when fed into the photogrammetry software, the images enhanced by the proposed method can reconstruct 3D scene models with sub-millimeter mean errors, which are much better than those with the original degraded images. The visual results of 3D model reconstruction also demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method. Refer to Ref. [2] in Part C: Our proposed deep learning-based image dehazing model outperforms other hand-crafted and deep learning-based image dehazing methods by 2dB or more in peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR). Moreover, we utilize the dehazed images for target detection using the object detector YOLO. In the experimentations, images are degraded by two weather conditions - rain and fog. We demonstrate that the objects detected in images enhanced by our proposed dehazing model are significantly improved over those detected in the degraded images. Refer to Ref. [6] in Part C: We propose a deep learning model for FER. Experiments on two datasets, AFEW and DFEW, show that the network achieves state-of-art performances on the benchmarks.

11202319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11202319.value: We have mentioned future work in the published papers. For instance, in the research of monocular 3D object detection (refer to Ref. [3] in Part C), we would like to conduct more experiments on other datasets, such as nuScenes. Other research directions include training an occlusion-aware segmentation, and improving the inference strategy of depth prediction. One journal paper is submitted to IEEE Access. We also discuss further research in MER (refer to Ref. [5] in Part C). Since 3D convolutions contain a large amount of parameters and require high computation costs. we will investigate a computationally efficient framework for MER. For instance, temporal modeling in video sequences using a pooling technique can achieve fewer parameters, thus requiring less computation. We observe some failure cases in our FER model (refer to Ref. [6] in Part C). Some videos might contain very few useful motion features (e.g., still faces). This suggests that a more effective algorithm should learn to estimate the necessity of extra motion features, to avoid introducing noise. For example, we can treat neutral and sadness differently from other classes and use a distinct image-based binary classifier to classify these two emotions, based on the failure cases analysis.

11202319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11202319.value: The human visual system consists of eyes and brain. The retina receives sensory signals from the whole visual field, follows by focusing the gaze on target (e.g., moving object). Computer vision algorithms mimicking human visual system can be modelled as a sequential process. We propose a model based on traditional (deterministic) approach utilizing hand-crafted features. Then, the concept of foveated vision is adopted for deep learning-based image processing. A number of deep learning models are proposed – moving object detection via background subtraction, enhancing images via dehazing for 3D model reconstruction and road scene object detection, image-based 3D object detection, facial expression recognition, micro-expression recognition. Each proposed model is evaluated quantitatively on publicly available and custom datasets. We also compared our proposed models with state-of-the-art methods using evaluation metrics. Moreover, we assess the performance of our models qualitatively by examining the visual results. We collaborate with academics in another department of CityU, mainland university, and UK university. We also collaborate with commercial companies and research centre in transferring our proposed method to practical applications. We support and provide research training to PhD student, MSc and undergraduate students. The project produces 6 peer-reviewed journal papers. One journal paper is under review.

11202419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202419.value: There is a great need for a secure and fair platform for people to trade their under-utilized computing resources. On one hand, there are many institutions or individuals that have a lot of unused storage capacities; on the other hand, there are many users that have a large amount of data looking for storage. Peer-to-Peer (P2P) is an ideal model for building such a large-scale distributed storage system. However, traditional P2P systems are notorious for their insecurity and unfairness. The principal goal of this project is to use the emerging blockchain technology to develop a framework for secure, fair and verifiable P2P storage systems. The objectives of this project are three-fold: 1) Design an efficient and secure blockchain-based P2P framework for storage systems equipped with search capability over encrypted data. 2) Design a file index structure that can support dynamic file updates and yet achieve efficient search operations in this blockchain-based P2P framework. The system should also preserve forward-security for update operations. 3) Design a verification scheme to verify the correctness of search results and an auditing scheme to ensure the integrity of the data for the blockchain-based P2P framework. 我們迫切需要構建一個安全且公平的平台供人們交易其未充分利用的計算資源。一方面，有許多機構和個人擁有大量未使用的存儲資源; 另一方面，有許多用戶迫切尋求存儲空間來存儲其日益增長的數據。點對點（P2P）是構建這種大規模分布式存儲系統的理想模式。然而，傳統的P2P系統因其不公平性和不安全性而臭名昭著。該項目擬通過使用新興的區塊鏈技術構建一個安全，公平且可驗證的P2P存儲系統。其中的主要研究目標有三個：1）基於區塊鏈技術，構建支持加密數據搜索的P2P存儲架構。2）設計支持動態文件更新的密文索引結構，以實現在此P2P存儲架構中高效的加密搜索和更新操作。所設計的系統還應保證文件更新操作的前向安全性。3）設計實現適配與此P2P架構的驗證和審計方案，以確保搜索結果的準確性和存儲數據的完整性。

11202419.label: Realisation of objectives
11202419.value: The project has three objectives. They are all fully achieved. Summarized below are the achievements under each of the objectives. Objective 1. Design an efficient and secure blockchain-based P2P framework for storage systems equipped with search capability over encrypted data. The focused research issues include development of security analytic model and security analysis, distributed consensus and useful PoW, etc. Achievements: 1) Developed a decentralized public auditing system for cloud storage by using blockchain. Public auditing schemes for cloud storage systems have been extensively explored with the increasing importance of data integrity. However, existing auditing schemes rely on a centralized TPA, and they are vulnerable to tempting auditors who may collude with malicious blockchain miners to produce biased auditing results. We propose a blockchain-based decentralized public auditing (BDPA) scheme by utilizing a decentralized blockchain network to undertake the responsibility of a centralized TPA, and also mitigate the influence of tempting auditors and malicious blockchain miners by taking the concept of decentralized autonomous organization (DAO). This work was published in IEEE TCC 2021. We also developed a Privacy-preserving Online Ride-hailing System without Involving a TPA Server. This work was published in IEEE TIFS 2021, a top-tier journal in the field; 2) Developed a Privacy-Preserving and Federated Crowdsourcing Framework by Using Blockchain (PFcrowd). PFcrowd system allows different crowdsourcing systems to perform encrypted task-worker matching over the blockchain platform without involving any third party authority. The core idea is to utilize the blockchain to assist the federated crowdsourcing by moving the task recommendation algorithm to the trusted smart contract. To avoid third-party involvement, we first leverage the re-writable deterministic hashing (RDH) technique to convert the problem of federated task worker matching into the secure query authorization. We then devise a secure scheme based on RDH and searchable encryption (SE) to support privacy-preserving task-worker matching via the smart contract. This work was published in IEEE International Workshop on QoS 2020; 3) developed a series of works that deduplicates data among edge nodes, offloads interactive rendering tasks to edge nodes, and schedules remote rendering tasks at edge nodes. This series of works were published in IEEE Trans. Serv. Comput., IEEE TPDS, and IEEE Trans. on Cloud Computing, respectively. Objective 2. Design a file index structure that can support dynamic file updates and yet achieve efficient search operations in this blockchain-based P2P framework. The focused research issues include forward-security for update operations, parallel search structures and algorithms, efficient information retrieval from the blockchain, etc. Achievements: 1) Recent work on Dynamic Searchable Symmetric Encryption (DSSE) schemes has focused on the direction of forward-privacy, requiring that newly added data cannot be linked to previously query results. However, due to the complexity of forward-privacy updates, existing schemes can only address an honest-but-curious server. It is difficult to verify updated results while preserving forward-privacy. We developed a scheme that resorts to the emerging smart contract as a trusted platform to store digests for public result verification, and carefully crafts dynamic query protocols to enable encrypted search with forward-privacy. In our design, indexes are collocated with encrypted files and stored at storage-servers, which makes the blockchain light-weighted and search operations more efficient. Moreover, we proposed a hybrid index design to support efficient files deletion. By using our blockchain-assisted primitive, the property collision between dynamic result verification and forward-privacy can be solved. This work was published in IEEE Trans on Dependable and Secure Computing (IEEE TDSC 2023); 2) Developed a metadata-hiding data analytic system with end-to-end policy controls, which enables search and data analytics over encrypted data. This work was presented at ACM CCS, one of the top computer security conferences in the world. We also designed a certificate revocation framework for named-data-networking, which is published in ICN 2022, a top conference in the field of Information-centric Networks. Objective 3. Design a verification scheme to verify the correctness of search results and an auditing scheme to ensure the integrity of the data for the blockchain-based P2P framework. The focused research issues include reducing the on-chain storage cost for search results verification, minimizing the size of Merkle tree for storage auditing, prevention of replay attacks, etc. Achievements: 1) Developed a publicly verifiable encrypted search scheme that preserves forward-privacy by using blockchains. It can help to support the update of searched databases. This work becomes part of the publication materials of IEEE TDSC 2023; 2) Developed a new blockchain system, “Occam: A Secure and Adaptive Scaling Protocol for Permissionless Blockchain”. Blockchain scalability is the core issue for public blockchain platforms and many blockchain protocols have been proposed to increase the transaction throughput while guarantee the safety and liveness. However, existing protocols cannot dynamically scale the transaction throughput to fit network needs. We proposed Occam, a secure and adaptive blockchain protocol for the permissionless setting. Occam adaptively changes the transaction throughput by expanding and shrinking according to the transaction demand in the network. We introduce a dynamic adjustment mechanism of mining difficulty and a computing power load balancing mechanism to resist various attacks. This work was published in IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems, 2021, a highly competitive conference in the field.

11202819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11202819.value: A networked sensor system (NSS) consists of spatially distributed autonomous sensors to cooperatively monitor physical or environment conditions. Networked sensor systems (NSSs) can provide a powerful tool to capture the dynamical behavior of many real-world engineering systems such as smart grids, multi-robot localization and internet of things. In most applications, the monitored physical process is nonlinear and the disturbance noise is unknown but bounded (UBB). In fact, it is not easy to realize real-time communication of complete information in NSSs due to the constrains of communication bandwidth and sensor energy. This project aims to develop nonlinear fusion estimation algorithms of NSSs that can be used by a group of sensors to carry out prescribed tasks efficiently under UBB noises and incomplete information. Designing nonlinear estimators under UBB noises and fusion criteria for nonlinear systems are the most fundamental problems in fusion estimation. However, most of the existing nonlinear fusion estimation methods requires knowledge of the statistical property of disturbance noises. The existing linear fusion criteria may not reflect the real correlation between local nonlinear estimates because of the complexity of nonlinear dynamics. Notice that the statistical information of noises is difficult to obtain accurately in most practical systems, while UBB noises can be easily satisfied in practical applications. Hence, learning-based fusion strategies will be studied in this proposal to design efficient nonlinear estimation/fusion criteria under UBB noises. Bandwidth constraint and energy consumption are two of the most concerned problems in NSSs. Incomplete information caused by bandwidth and energy constraints will degrade the system performance seriously. It is necessary to design compensation strategies to minimize the information loss for NSSs. In particular, the complexity of nonlinear systems and unknown statistical information of noises do bring inherent difficulties in designing nonlinear fusion estimation schemes for NSSs. Hence, dynamical quantization fusion methods under distributed dimensionality reduction will be designed in this project to satisfy the limited communication capacity. Also self-triggered schemes for the nonlinear fusion estimation will be developed to save sensor energy. In particular, the developed nonlinear fusion estimation framework in this proposal will be applied to the monitoring and supervision of power grids described by IEEE bus models. The theoretical results generated in this proposal, if well accomplished, will lay a solid foundation for the development of estimation fields of nonlinear fusion, and also provide a fundamental investigation of nonlinear fusion estimation for NSSs. 網絡化多傳感器系統是由大量以協同監測物理環境為任務的空間分佈自主傳感器組成。網絡化多傳感器系統(Networked Sensor Systems, NSSs) 可以提供強而有力的工具以獲取諸如智能電網、多機器人定位系統和物聯網系統等實際工程系統的動態過程。在大多數實際應用中，被監測的物理系統動態過程是非線性的，且擾動噪聲是未知但有界的(Unknown But Bounded (UBB))。事實上，由於通信帶寬和傳感器能量的約束，在NSS中很難實現完整信息的實時通信。為此，本項目將針對帶有不完整信息和有界能量噪聲的NSSs提出一套非線性融合估計方法。首先，UBB噪聲下的非線性融合估計器設計和非線性系統的融合準則設計是融合估計領域的基礎性問題。但是，大多數非線性融合估計方法都需要知道擾動噪聲的統計特性，而非線性動態的複雜性使得線性融合準則可能刻畫不了局部非線性估計之間的真實關係。注意到噪聲的統計信息在大多數實際系統中很難準確獲得，但是在實際系統中的噪聲很容易滿足UBB。因此，本項目將研究如何基於學習的融合策略以設計UUB噪聲下高效的非線性估計和融合準則。其次，帶寬約束和能量消耗是NSSs中最受關注的兩個問題。由帶寬和能量約束所導致的不完整信息將嚴重降低系統性能，使得非常有必要設計補償策略以盡量減少NSSs的信息損失。注意到非線性系統的動態復雜性和噪聲的未知統計信息將為NSSs的非線性融合估計設計帶來了內在的困難。因此，本項目將設計分佈式降維融合下的動態量化方法以滿足有限的通信帶寬，同時將提出基於自觸發機制的非線性融合估計算法以實現節能。最後，將基於IEEE-Bus模型的電力系統實時監測來驗證本項目所提出的一系列非線性融合估計方法。如果本項目所期望的理論結果可以圓滿完成，將會為非線性融合估計領域的發展奠定堅實的基礎，也為NSSs的非線性融合估計提供了基礎性的研究。

11203519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203519.value: This project aims to improve the effectiveness of complex system maintenance through innovative adaptation of ‘importance measures’. In particular, we examine the problem of effective prioritisation of maintenance resources by identifying the most critical components in a complex system to be selected for maintenance. This is of growing urgency for complex real-world systems such as power networks, traffic systems and infrastructure, where the asset owners are experiencing ever-tightening operational and maintenance budgets. Although ‘importance measures’ have been a topic of considerable interest in the reliability community, their use in supporting maintenance decisions for complex systems have been impeded due to some fundamental flaws. Firstly, in most complex systems, component failures and degradation are not independent, and these behaviours of a component are also influenced by other components in the system. Further, the availability of resources (e.g., personnel, spares) has a significant influence on the components to be selected for maintenance. These two issues – which are insufficiently explored in the extant academic literature in the development of ‘importance measures’ – is the focus of this proposal. The novelty of the proposed research is two-fold. First, this project will develop importance measures specifically designed for condition-based maintenance, incorporating the dynamic and stochastic nature of component degradation and also importance measures that explicitly considers the dependency between components in a complex system which is new to the existing literature and important for practical decision making. Second, we will develop a technique that exploits the new importance measure to optimise condition-based maintenance with the multiple options for intervention including opportunistic maintenance, especially a procedure based on importance measures that allow joint analysis of maintenance and spare parts optimisation. The proposed research project developed through our collaborative effort with the research group at Univ of Cambridge has clear practical impacts on industrial applications across different sectors. The maintenance-oriented importance measures developed through this project will guide the selection of components for maintenance so that the system performance can be improved in a more effective and cost-efficient manner. By facilitating the identification of the parameters that exert the most significant influence on system performance, asset managers can use these importance measures to make decisions that ensure their investment in maintenance delivers maximum value to the organisation. 该项目旨在利用重要度理论，提高复杂系统维护措施的有效性，尤其是通过正确地选择复杂系统中待维护的关键部件来研究维护资源的优化问题。对于现实中的复杂系统，如电网、交通系统和基础设施等，随着系统进入老化阶段，维修优化问题越来越紧迫，然而多数企业面临着日益紧缩的运营和维护预算。虽然重要度理论一直是可靠性领域的热点课题，但用于支持复杂系统的维护决策时，现有方法有很多局限。首先，在大多数复杂系统中，部件故障和退化不是独立的，部件的退化也受系统中其它部件的影响。此外，资源(如人员、备件等)的可获取性对于待维护的部件有很大影响。现有的相关文献对这两个问题的探讨尚不充分。本课题的创新性主要有两方面：其一，本项目将提出专为视情维护设计的重要度，同时考虑动态和随机老化特性并明确考虑部件相关性。这方面在现有文献中没有同时考虑，且这个研究对实际决策具有重要意义。其二，我们将所提出的重要度概念用于视情维护决策，同时考虑多种维修策略的结合，例如机会维修；进一步利用重要度理论对维修策略和维修备件进行联合分析优化。在我们与剑桥大学研究小组的合作基础上，本课题将针对不同行业的实际应用做这方面的研究。本课题提出的以维护为导向的重要度将有效协助优先维护部件的选择，利用更有效、更经济的方式提高系统可靠性。通过有效地识别对系统性能影响最大的参数，资产管理人员可以利用这些重要度制定决策，确保其维护投资的收益最大化。

11203519.label: Realisation of objectives
11203519.value: Although the project was affected by the pandemic, we have carried out the research in line with the proposed research tasks and fully achieved the objectives. The project team members published several good papers, and we also presented our research at international conferences (some online). We have also initiated collaboration with industry. With regard to international collaboration with Prof Parlikad at the University of Cambridge, a visit was made last year after the pandemic. A research student will visit him this year to continue with the collaboration. Below is a summary of the research done to achieve the project objectives, as in the published works. In addition to these papers, new research ideas are developed, and some are in preparation for additional research papers or grant proposals. Objective #1: To develop importance measures for dependent components in complex systems In the paper by Ling, Kuo, and Xie (2023), following a short preliminary overview of reliability-based design optimization (RBDO) as well as the traditional strategies, this paper sets out to review the state of the art of how surrogate models have been explored to streamline RBDO through a systematic study, outlining their respective advantages as well as disadvantages, and discussing the bottleneck problems that need to be solved. It is related to all objectives as it contains many basic results. In Zhang et al. (2023), we focused on applying the STPA method to the CAES system to identify potential hazards and provide clues for practitioners in risk management. The CAES system is a complex system leveraging two separate processes, the charging and discharging process. To meet the specific operating conditions, a multi-component structure with multiple energy forms is involved in the process and is subjected to high temperature and high pressure. As a result, the CAES system usually operates under off-design conditions, which brings difficulties to optimal system operation and control. Compared with conventional hazard analysis methods, STPA satisfies the need for complicated modern systems where accidents occur due to faulty single components and inter-component communication mismatches. Therefore, more potential causes of accidents could be captured. In the paper by Yang et al. (2023), we proposed a survival signature-based reliability framework for an imprecise multistate system (IMSS). Systems with complex configurations usually cannot be decomposed into combinations of series and parallel systems. In addition, the rapid growth of dimension makes the evaluation procedures of current reliability estimation methods tedious. The survival signature is introduced to address these obstacles by allowing the separation of topological information and probabilistic information for complex systems consisting of multiple component types. Besides, some key parameters in the system model cannot be precisely determined due to a lack of field test data and the inevitable bias in prior knowledge. This research defines the survival signature for IMSS and establishes the corresponding multistate survival function. An approximate Bayesian computation method is then developed to calibrate the unknown imprecise parameters for a better reliability evaluation result with less uncertainty. In collaboration with Univ of Cambridge, Zhao et al. (2022) presented a study of an evaluation and maintenance strategy optimization approach considering system risk. System performance is defined by the number of functional assets similar to components, and the penalty cost is measured by the loss of performance in the form of a ranking. A Bayesian framework to dynamically update unknown parameters in a Wiener degradation model. Based on the Bayesian parameter inferences, we propose a short-term value-based replacement policy to minimize the expected cost rate in the current planning horizon. Objective #2: To extend importance measures through dynamic time updating with maintenance policies Some of the works described earlier are also related to meeting this objective. In addition, there are some other works that are more of an extension of earlier ones, considering the dynamic nature and maintenance policy, as described in our original proposal for this objective. Zhang et al. (2023) describe a general and robust optimization for joint system design and maintenance scheduling in high-consequence systems. The existing importance measures and procedures often results in significant losses due to redundancies. To fill this gap, we consider an integrated optimization of system design and maintenance scheduling for multi-state high-consequence systems in which the component’s degradation is known with limited distributional information. We utilize the framework of distributionally robust optimization to provide a risk-averse decision to decision-makers even under the worst realizations of random parameters and develop a two-stage integer distributionally robust model with a moment-based ambiguity set to determine the system design and maintenance scheduling simultaneously. In Bai et al (2021), we considered the severity of power grid disasters, and an improved power grid resilience measure and its corresponding importance measures are proposed. The recovery priority of failed components after a disaster is determined according to the influence of the failed components on the power grid resilience. Finally, based on the data from the 2019 Power Yearbook of each city in Shandong Province, China, the power grid resilience after a disaster is analyzed for two situations, namely, partial components failure and failure of all components. The result shows that the recovery priorities of components with different importance measures vary. This paper proposed an important index, the Cost-Informed Component Maintenance Index (CICMI), for optimizing preventive maintenance policies. It then applied the CICMI to analyze series-parallel and parallel-serial systems. Some propositions of the CICMI were given for different policies, such as group failure and simultaneous maintenance. Considering the cost constraints, this paper optimized the number of components for PM and maintenance policies. Objective #3: To develop a procedure for industrial implementation As we had different scenarios, we developed different implementation procedures. In each of the works described earlier, we have either procedures or numerical examples using real systems or based on real scenarios. We have also worked with companies to study the effect and further modification of the procedure for specific applications and discussed possible further implementation and projects in future research. We have initiated discussions with software companies to see how general procedures can be incorporated into the existing software. For example, in the paper by Bai et al. (2021), an implementation procedure is developed and applied to a reactor system to illustrate the applicability and the positive results. The paper by Han et al. (2021) incorporated some of the research in this project into real-world scenarios, and procedures were developed to show the implementation and results. This led to further research in this field, and it is already a highly cited paper in the Web of Science. In summary, the project objectives are achieved with many publications in the top journals in terms of reliability. In addition to the research outputs, PI was invited to deliver talks at some major international conferences, including the leading reliability conference, Mathematical Models in Reliability, held in 2023 in Spain. A few related sessions are organized at other conferences. Several graduates who worked on the project have secured faculty positions at major universities or leading companies in mainland or overseas.

11203519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203519.value: In this project, we have carried out specific studies on the importance measures of system components in some realistic scenarios. The existing importance measures are based on different assumptions that may not be true. Component dependence is an example, although it is difficult to model different types of dependence. Anyway, a number of studies have been carried out, and some important measures for dependent components in complex systems have been studied. A survival signature-based reliability framework for an imprecise multistate system has been developed. Systems with complex configurations usually cannot be decomposed into combinations of series and parallel systems. The survival signature is introduced to address these obstacles by allowing the separation of topological information and probabilistic information for complex systems consisting of multiple component types. Another direction is the use of importance measures for decision-making. A new importance index, called Cost-Informed Component Maintenance Index, has been developed to optimize preventive maintenance policies, which is useful in maintenance decision-making. Furthermore, we also utilize the framework of distributionally robust optimization to provide a risk-averse decision to decision-makers even under the worst realizations of random parameters. A number of application studies have also been carried out to show its applicability. We considered for example, the severity of power grid disasters, an improved power grid resilience measure, and its corresponding importance measures are proposed. The studies have shown the usefulness and advantages of the approaches developed in this project. Although the pandemic affected the project, we immediately resumed the visits and face-to-face meetings. PI visited co-PI at Cambridge University, and a student was later sent to spend a few months working with the team there. And new results beyond the scope of the project are also expected soon.

11203519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203519.value: We have identified several different research directions. One example is the study of component importance in dynamic systems, such as those in flexible manufacturing systems or telecommunication systems how the idea of ranking components or subsystems for AI-system is another challenge. There is also a lack of research for systems that consist of both software and hardware in general. Some ideas are in the new proposals we are preparing, and we are also discussing with our collaborators to see what to focus on in our further research. We are also talking to industry partners so that the research can be of more direct industry relevance.

11203519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203519.value: For any complex system, some components should be given a higher priority when we decide to improve the system further or find the failed component that led to system failure. Component importance measures are developed for this purpose. However, the existing importance measures are usually based on different assumptions that may not be realistic. One example is that components are usually dependent. We have carried out research to incorporate different kinds of dependence to make more cost-effective decisions. Different maintenance actions can be taken on different components, and how that affects the importance of each component is another issue. Considering the cost and risk, we have presented several theoretical studies in this project. Furthermore, we have applied our research findings and results to different real systems to show their usefulness and applicability.

11203619.label: Project Objectives
11203619.value: To study human visual attention modeling for human gaze tracking. A visual attention model will be proposed to generate focused object regions to recover tracking errors. A bottom-up scheme is to be studied in the initialization stage while a top-down one will be utilized in the tracking stage; To extract suitable features for the tracking task via deep learning. Some typical tasks will be tested to assess the performance of the system including robotic task teaching by human demonstration and human-robot cooperative assembly tasks.

11203619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11203619.value: Collaborations between robots and humans are becoming increasingly important for many robotic applications. In interacting with human, a robot needs to know the reference objects and the physical locations. Gaze tracking can be useful for communicating human intentions to the robot in such cases. However, tracking an object via estimating the 3D points of gaze (POG) in space is very difficult to achieve using a gaze tracker alone. To solve this problem, we propose to explore human visual attention mechanism for use with a gaze tracker to achieve robust object tracking for human-robot interactions. The tracking here needs to address several challenging issues including background cluttering, occlusions, and rapid object pose changes. Focusing the most relevant parts in the scene quickly and learning useful image features automatically will solve these problems. This project aims to develop an attention-driven object tracking method with deep feature learning. Here the visual attention controls where to look, whereas the deep feature learning conveys what is seen. To find the focused region in which the target object may lie, we propose to utilize bottom-up visual attention with a gazer tracker in the initialization stage. In the tracking stage, on the other hand, the top-down visual attention model will be adopted. It is proposed to adapt and fine tune the pre-trained deep model for tracking, in which some layers will be responsible for extracting view-invariant features for semantic segmentation, whereas some other layers will extract view-variant representation for recovering the object pose. The visual attention module will output a small set of potentially relevant candidate regions to be evaluated by the image features learnt. Hence, robust object tracking can be achieved. In this project, the gaze estimation is responsible for providing the initial location of the object of interest on the 2D image via the gazing direction extracted from the gaze tracker. It is the task of the visual attention and deep feature learning based tracker to locate and track the target on-line for interacting with a robot. The output of the project will be a robust gaze guided tracking system for communicating human intentions with a robot. This will be useful for robot to take part in tasks in assisting human collaboratively by following human intentions, which will benefit robotic applications in general with the new type of human-robot interface enhanced by the gaze guided tracking system. 机器人与人之间的协同合作在许多应用中变的日趋重要。为此，本项目旨在探讨人的注意力机制以实现鲁棒的注视跟踪，探索意图理解和眼控指令的凝视交互模式。 根据可穿戴凝视数据，应用深度特征学习， 建立自主标定方法，保证非理想情形下凝视测量和估计的可靠性；针对主动自发的意图理解交互模式，从由上至下和由下至上的注意力机理，研究注意力状态识别和意图表征的问题。形成有效的眼控交互机制。针对视觉注意力驱动的人机协作任务，进行相关实验。本项目的研究也将对探索人与机器人间的新的交互方法有所贡献，研究成果将为人与机器人自然交互过程中使机器人更有效地提供其协助作用，使机器人获得更广泛的应用。

11203619.label: Realisation of objectives
11203619.value: In this project, the proposed objectives are mostly well realized, through extensive studies conducted and implementation efforts made. Objective 1 has been studied to the depth. Related to modeling of human visual attention for human gaze tracking, a bottom-up scheme is studied at the initial stage of the research. To this end, we have achieved a systematic solution for salient features and object detection. This addresses the three aspects of the problem with a unified framework: modal-specific representation learning, complementary cue selection, and cross-modal complement fusion. With the cross-modal heterogeneous representations disentangled explicitly, the cross-modal fusion process has less uncertainty, while enjoying better adaptability. We shift the attention of RGBD Salient object detection from designing complex cross-modal fusion connections to reducing the fusion uncertainty. We develop a cross-modal disentanglement framework, which takes the first step to answer the question of how RGB and depth complement for saliency detection. This framework also allows better cross-modal selection adaptability and fusion sufficiency, which is verified by extensive experiments. The proposed multi-modal fusion network achieves large improvement than state-of-the-art methods. For different scenes, the disentangled representations allow the fusion module to easily identify and incorporate desired complements for informative multi-modal fusion. This work can be expected to inspire future works to advance the dissection of multi-modal fusion, and from this perspective, to improve the fusion sufficiency. The results will benefit salient object detection with the additional saliency cues. To learn discriminative modal specific features, we propose a hierarchical cross-modal distillation scheme, in which we use the progressive predictions from the well-learned source modality to supervise learning feature hierarchies and inference in the new modality. To better select complementary cues, we formulate a residual function to incorporate complements from the paired modality adaptively. We propose a new cross-modal transfer learning scheme, an explicit cross-modal complement selector, and a sufficient cross-modal cross-level fusion pattern. Furthermore, a top-down fusion structure is constructed for sufficient cross-modal cross-level interactions. This resembles a kind of mechanism in human attention, the top-down approach. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed cross-modal distillation scheme in learning from a new modality, the advantages of the proposed multi-modal fusion pattern in selecting and fusing cross-modal complements, and the generalization of the proposed designs to different tasks. We implemented the attention model in guiding combination of RGB and depth modalities. The challenges are addressed with a novel framework developed to adopt the task-understanding knowledge of the RGB-induced saliency detection network to depth modality and fuse the deep representations of both two modalities adaptively to obtain the final saliency map. In studying issues related to tracking tasks via deep learning, we proposed a multi-view attention-aware network. The attention mechanism was used to boost the complements in different streams for better joint inference. Comprehensive experiments conducted showed superiority of our model over state-of-the-art methods as well as the efficacy of our framework. The insights gained from this work will allow us to learn better representations from other new modalities and enable sufficient fusion for other multi-modal systems. With the salience-based bottom-up approach and a top-down fusion structure constructed for cross-modal cross-level interactions, Objective 1 and 2 are well explored and research goals are mostly achieved. The top-down approach paves the way for object detection and tracking in the subsequent works. The Objective 3 aims to achieve pose tracking for robotic manipulations by incorporating depth information in visual sensing. This is needed for robotic manipulation tasks, where depth information is to be used to reconstruct 3D object pose. For this purpose, we proposed a new hardware setup for gaze tracking, where an RGBD sensor is deployed and integrated with the gaze tracker, to reconstruct dense 3-D environmental structures. With this system, we propose a flexible framework to remove the explicit user calibration and achieve a more robust 3-D gaze estimation in room-scale distances. During the calibration data collection, 3-D eye models are studied according to eye images. Meanwhile, the bag-of-word (BoW) algorithm is employed to compute the similarity of the scene image pairs and eliminate redundant figures. Saliency maps are then generated from the selected scene images, and the geometrical relationship among the scene and eye cameras is obtained through aggregating 3-D salient targets with eye visual directions. We choose those salient regions whose salience value is higher than the threshold as our potential 3-D target data. Through the aggregation, the transformation relationships among the scene camera and two eye cameras are obtained. The 3-D Point of Regard (PoR) can then be obtained by determining the point in the reconstructed scene, which is closest to the transformed gaze vectors. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed 3-D gaze estimation framework achieves robust performance in the room-scale area, both indoors and outdoors. With our developed hardware of depth integrated gaze tracker and the PoR estimation framework, Object 3 us fully achieved. In order to implement Objective 4, we have built two gaze trackers. We first built the hardware system of a head mounted gaze tracker of our own. We propose a flexible calibration framework to accurately learn the relation between the pupil center and POR projected from different depths. Adopting a new gaze data acquisition approach to acquire densely distributed calibration points in a wide field of view, a nonparametric model is applied. To improve the robustness of the learning process, a distraction detection method is also introduced to detect the outlier training data. To reduce the parallax error, the epipolar geometry of HMGT and user’s eyes is recovered by calculated virtual parallax errors. Thus, POR unaffected by the parallax error can be estimated as the intersection of two epipolar lines inferred from both eye images. To meet the need for 3D tracking for robotic applications, a new type of gaze tracker is developed with 3D gaze estimation and auto-calibration method proposed in this study. In this system, we employ an RGBD camera as the scene camera to acquire the 3D structure of the environment. The automatic calibration is achieved by uniting gaze vectors with saliency maps of the scene which aligned depth information. The 3D gaze point is determined through a point cloud generated from the RGBD camera. Related to motion tracking, we also studied efficient tracking with event based vision and have set up the basic modules for tracking applications. For object detection, we introduced an adaptive motion-agnostic encoder which can extract indistinguishable semantic information behind event signals under various motion conditions by encoding events with integration block and adaptive motion-agnostic filter. The differentiable and continuous properties of the encoder allow us to learn its parameters with CNN’s blocks, which makes the encoder more robust than traditional handcraft descriptors. The performance of our proposed method in motion consistency and inconsistency evaluations shows that our approach outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of accuracy and motion robustness. With the two types of gaze tracking systems built, and the methods related to motion tracking developed, Objective 4 is investigated to the depth.
