11203619.label: Major findings and research outcome
11203619.value: In this project, we investigated gaze tracking for robotic applications. Two types of gaze tracking systems were developed. The first one consists of a scene camera and two eye cameras [Patent 1]. For this setup, the problems in tedious calibration and parallax errors are solved with a new calibration method [Patent 1]. The user is only required to change his head pose while gazing at one calibration marker. This results in a flexible calibration method. The second gaze tracking system employs an RGBD camera as the scene camera [Journal 4, 6]. In this system, 3D eye model is built on the eye images to determine gaze vectors [Conference 1, 3]. The 3D gaze point is obtained through the calibrated gaze vectors, and the point cloud is generated from the RGBD camera. The set up system also presents a significant improvement in depth measurement, which is sufficient for tracking users' visual attention in real scenes for robotic applications. A special feature for this type of gaze tracking system is the auto-calibration capability enabled by the setup and methodology developed. In exploring human attention mechanisms, we have found a systematic solution for salient features and object detection [Journal 2, 5]. We shift the attention of RGBD Salient object detection from designing complex cross-modal fusion connections to reducing the fusion uncertainty. This shows the bottom-up approach for human attention. We use the progressive predictions from the well-learned source modality to supervise learning feature hierarchies and inference. A top-down fusion structure is constructed. We implemented the attention model in guiding combination of RGB and depth modalities. A novel framework is developed to adopt the task-understanding knowledge of the RGB-induced saliency detection network to obtain the final saliency map. A multi-view attention-aware network was developed. In addition to the tracking by gaze trackers, we also studied efficient motion tracking with event-based [Journal 1]. An adaptive motion-agnostic encoder is introduced which can extract indistinguishable semantic information behind event [Conference 2], which allows learning the parameters with CNN’s blocks. As side products of the study, we have developed a method for accurate alignment for MEMS based motion [Journal 3] and micro-grasping in 3D space [Journal 7]. The tracking method studies also contributed to an award as part of generic motion estimations (Impact 2).

11203619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11203619.value: In this project, we investigated gaze tracking for robotic applications, with two types of gaze tracking systems developed. The first one consists of a scene camera and two eye cameras. The problems in tedious calibration and parallax errors are resolved with a new calibration method developed, where the user only needs to change his or her head pose while gazing at a calibration marker. This results in a flexible calibration method, which shows high potential for further development in gaze tracking applications. The second gaze tracking system is a low-cost HMD where we adopted an RGBD camera as the scene camera and two IR cameras as the eye cameras. This system presents a significant improvement in depth measurement, which is sufficient for tracking users' visual attention in real scenes for robotic applications. A special feature for this type of gaze tracking system is the auto-calibration capability enabled by the setup and methodology developed. The prototype developed here will invite more explorations of such type of gaze trackers. With attention guided combination of RGB and depth modalities in studying visual attention, both salience based (bottom-up) and model guided (top-down) approached were studied for vision processing and tracking. The insights gained from this work will allow us to learn better representations from other new modalities and enable sufficient fusion for other multi-modal systems. We plan to extend studies and applications of the gaze tracking systems and methods for more robotics project applications.

11203619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11203619.value: Interactions between human operators and robots are important for robotic applications. In this project, we investigated the use of gaze tracking to extract the intentions of human from their eyes, to provide a new means to pass human commands to robots. Two types of gaze tracking systems are developed. To overcome the drawbacks of tedious calibration and lack of 3D functionality of the existing gaze trackers, a new calibration framework is developed where the user only needs to change his or her head pose while gazing at a calibration marker, making it easier for the user to use a gaze tracker in practical applications. We also developed a new low-cost gaze tracker, employing an RGBD camera as the scene camera. This setup system brings significant improvement in depth measurement, which is useful for tracking user visual intention in 3D for robotic applications. This gaze tracking system allows automatic calibration by the system itself. Together with the study in visual attention model learning, the methodologies explored will be useful for enhancing human-robot interctions. The systems and methods developed here will have its impact on the applications of gaze trackers in human-computer interface in general and in human-robot interactions in particular. As robots are now finding wider and wider applications, the new way to interact with robots through users eyes provides a promising alternative for teaching robots to work.

11204119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204119.value: 本項目旨在實現超聲波功率傳輸鏈路的小型化，從而對植入體內深處的亞毫米（mm）級生物醫學設備進行無線供電。結合我們在微系統和壓電器件方面的專業經驗，我們的研究重點將專注於氮化鋁壓電隔膜結構。本研究的首要目標著眼於無線鏈路的接收器終端，分析器件的幾何結構，尺寸和諧波模態對功率轉化效率的影響。下一個研究目標集中在無線鏈路的發射器終端，探究針對亞毫米級植入體斑點尺寸的高度定向聲束的形成，以提高傳輸效率並減少外圍曝光。

11204119.label: Realisation of objectives
11204119.value: With regards to Objective 1, we have successfully demonstrated ultrasonic power conversion at with a 1 mm device with an output in the mW range at depths of ~5 cm with source powers within the FDA limit. The results have been reported at the Transducers 2021 conference, including the power conversion efficiency of the device. Alternative topologies based on diaphragm / membrane architectures aimed at maximizing quality factor in a damped environment (such as in ultrasonic transmission in a fluid) were explored to show the effect of device orientation on performance. The results have been published in the journal Sensors and Actuators with regard to the receiver/sensor design. With regards to Objective 2, we have explored device architectures that are scalable to arrays with the aim of maximizing quality factor to boost transmission efficiency on the transmitter device design. One of the successful examples that has been reported in the Journal of Micromechanics and Microengineering is the use of higher-order modes based on the diaphragm. We have shown that this novel model scales efficiently with miniaturization to allow scaling up the number of devices to form large arrays for transmission. Not only is the quality factor boosted in this mode, but the electromechanical coupling efficiency is also excellent pursuant to boosting transmission efficiency.

11204119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204119.value: We have reported on a novel higher-order mode membrane design to boost both quality factors well maintaining excellent electromechanical coupling. We show that the merits of the device scale favorably with miniaturization compared to the other designs reported in the literature. This design is favorable for both the receiver and transmitter design in the context of ultrasonic power transmission. The results have been described in the Journal of Micromechanics and Microengineering. We were limited to Aluminum Nitride for piezoelectric and thicker membranes, as these were the only options available by foundry processes. We have exhausted the possibilities made available with foundry processes through the work in this project. Simulations show, that further improvements could be made if the stack design could be optimized more favorably. This includes the use of highly doped Scandium Aluminum Nitride that would provide substantially higher piezoelectric constants to reduce the motional resistance, which would consequently reduce the optimum loads that would lead to higher output efficiency. Voltage generated would also be increased, which also benefits the conversion efficiency.

11204119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204119.value: The findings of this research have shown that further key breakthroughs lie beyond design and await to be unlocked through materials and process innovations. Simulations from work in this project indicate that substantial gains can be made with customized processes that involve materials currently unavailable by foundry services. This includes Scandium-doped Aluminum Nitride and thinning the membrane layer such that the neutral axis lies closer to the bottom of the piezoelectric layer. The gains from this modification are at least ten times compared to what is possible with foundry processes based on Aluminum Nitride and thicker silicon.

11204119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204119.value: This proposal aims to develop a miniaturized ultrasonic power transfer (UPT) system for submillimeter biomedical implants. As healthcare costs increase, personalized healthcare management using modern technologies such as biomedical implants is a suggested solution for chronic diseases. However, conventional electromagnetic wave-based wireless power transfer (WPT) methods cannot provide sufficient power at a small scale. Ultrasound-based ultrasound energy delivery is more effective for small implants deep inside the body. Recent studies have demonstrated the feasibility of UPTs, but scaling sub-mm3 systems to chip-scale solutions requires exploring alternative receiver architectures with higher power conversion efficiencies and lead-free materials. This project explores the limits of submillimeter UPTs using aluminum nitride (AlN) based piezoelectric diaphragm structures. The goals are to examine the relationship between device geometry, size and harmonic modes, and power conversion efficiency, demonstrate highly directional beams for submillimeter implant spot sizes, and develop matching circuit networks for interfacing receivers and implant loads. The ultimate goal is to show the ultrasonic powering of μm-scale sensors co-fabricated on the same chip as UPT receivers. By achieving these goals, the project hopes to enable wireless power transfer for submillimeter biomedical devices, eliminate the need for periodic surgical battery replacements or wires passing through the skin, and increase patient adoption likelihood.

11204419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204419.value: 由於能源危機和減少溫室氣體排放的全球需求，電動汽車越來越受歡迎。鋰離子電池具有高能量/功率密度和延長的循環壽命，已被公認為電動汽車的主要儲能裝置。為了滿足大規模的電壓和功率需求，電動汽車應用的能量存儲系統必須設計成多串/並聯連接。儘管在這些能量存儲系統中使用了高安全標準，但已經發生的許多電池事件引起了大眾對可充電操作的安全性和可靠性的質疑，例如，波音787飛機鋰離子電池起火導致日本某些航班停飛，挪威增壓站特斯拉Model S電池快速充電起火事件。因此，現階段仍急需大量研究來保障和提高複雜電池管理系統（BMS）的安全性，可靠性和高效率。 該項目的主要目標是通過融合跨學科方法，使用高級數據分析持續監控動力電池關鍵的電化學和電熱參數，來確保和改善現有BMS的健康監測，預測，故障診斷和管理優化。對於典型的BMS，主要的挑戰來自能量存儲電池的複雜特性，包括它們的退化和參數耦合。在這項研究中，將基於控制工程領域的知識以及可充電電池的物理，電氣，化學和熱性能開發新的理論和方法，以確保安全，可靠和有效的動力電池系統管理。 該項目研究包括開發有效的多時間尺度模型用於表徵儲能係統的電氣，熱學和化學動力學特性; 提出系統的方法用於監測和評估系統健康狀況;用於管理電池安全的在線診斷技術;搭建先進的BMS原型用於測試和評估電池系統的可靠性和效率。我們研究團隊在可靠性分析、退化建模、機器學習、信號處理和控制工程領域知識方面擁有豐富的經驗和專業知識。我們可以與實驗室和工業合作夥伴聯繫，收集實驗和現場數據以測試和驗證我們提出的BMS系統。我們的研究成果將為動力電池BMS提供安全可靠的操作和性能，為行業提供最先進的方法以有效管理可充電電池，並通過最大限度地減少BMS事故發生和火災危險為社會創造安全可靠的環境。

11204419.label: Realisation of objectives
11204419.value: This project was implemented first under the leadership of Prof. Kwok-Leung TSUI and next under the joint effort of Prof. Zijun ZHANG and Prof. Kwok-Leung TSUI as Prof. Tsui left CityU HK and joined Virginia Tech in U.S. in 2021. The revised objectives of this project include: 1) Develop models to accurately capture battery dynamics on electrical, chemical, thermal, and degradation behaviors; 2) Develop estimation and prognostics methodologies to effectively monitor health status and accurately predict remaining useful life for storage batteries; 3) Validate developed models and algorithms with experimental and field data from our test lab, and the developed prototype BMSs. Due to the great efforts in past 3 years, the project has been completed with research outcomes going beyond its original expectation, which include 29 research articles published in top and flagship journals crossing systems engineering, power and energy, transportation, etc. as well as 6 Ph.D. students graduated with joining mainland 985/211 class universities as Assistant Professors, joining leading tech companies as OR scientist, and joining QS top 100 universities as post-doc fellows. Among published journal articles, quite a portion of them have attracted great interests from academia and received many citations (1 article has been tagged with ESI top 1% highly cited work). More importantly, the machine learning based modelling methods for battery health estimation and diagnosis have attracted interests of a Shanghai Exchange Listed company, Tongda Electric, in Knowledge Transfer. In 2022, research team at CityU HK side and Tongda Electric jointly applied a Hong Kong Technology Transfer Project Scheme funded by Guangdong Government and got funded in 2023. The total amount is 4.5 million RMB with 3.5 million RMB matched by Tongda and 1 million came from Guangdong Province funding. Among this 1 million, 40% has been directly allocated to CityU HK in April 2024 to kick off the join effort in deploying technologies invented by CityU HK team to the IoT system developed by Tongda for monitoring condition and health of batteries operating on over 8000 electric buses as well as advising the battery replacement strategies. It is foreseeable that a further profound impact will be generated by results from this research project. In this project, the team has successfully achieved and even gone beyond three objectives. For the first objective, the team has explored the development of data-driven models on top of extending classical machine learning and recent deep learning methods. For example, the gradient boosting regression model with augmented trees has been developed to leverage voltage-, capacity-, and temperature-related features to profile battery dynamics and reason battery degradation behaviours. The change-point based statistical method has also been invented for the similar task for pursuing a better modelling accuracy. Meanwhile, a special attention has been paid into understanding the machine learning mechanisms for processing the battery data as well as conducting feature engineering and model selection. A set of systematic development of machine learning methods corresponding for various data availability and charging profile completeness scenarios have been accomplished to offer advices on data-driven modelling algorithms and mechanisms for scenarios with complete data observed, partial data observed, data from complete charging-discharging cycles, or dynamic charging-discharging cycles. Results successfully fill up the knowledge gap in machine learning principles for processing data and understanding their capacities under various conditions. Publications relevant to Objective 1 please refer to publications No. 1 – No. 7 listed in Part C: Research Output. These works appeared in famous journals in systems engineering and energy storage, such as IISE Transactions, IEEE Trans. on Industrial Informatics, Journal of Power Sources, Applied Energy, Reliability Engineering and System Safety, etc. For the second objective, research efforts have been devoted into developing novel deep learning based method for more effective feature engineering based on battery data as well as for promoting the adaptiveness and generalizability of data-driven models in state-of-health estimation and remaining useful life prediction facing various batteries. Such research efforts can be categorized into two sets. The first set of efforts was devoted into studying the mechanism of better leveraging information in tabular form battery data to construct a tensor-form input naturally fuse the information from spatial, temporal, and attribute-wise dimensions. Next, a convolution and recurrent deep network architecture with attention mechanism and its variants were designed for automating effective latent feature engineering based on the high-dimensional tensor-form input. Meanwhile, we also investigated the joint consideration of classical statistical based feature selection and recent deep learning power latent feature extraction in deriving meaningful and valuable data features for the subsequent estimation and prognostics of battery health status. The second set of efforts were devoted into developing novel model learning schemes for enhancing the performance adaptiveness and robustness of modelling methods towards multiple types of batteries. We have studied learning schemes with novel regularization designs and loss designs. Methods were tested based on battery data from multiple types of re-chargeable batteries including Lithion-ion, NMC, etc. We have also extended the methods with applications into mechanical components remaining useful life prediction and fault diagnosis tasks. Similar performance advantages were also obtained. Publications regarding Objective 2 can refer to publications No. 9, 10, 12 – 14, 16-24, 27 listed in Part C: Research Output. For the third objective, which refers to the experimental verification of developed models and algorithms as well as the prototype BMSs, some of previously stated research efforts have partially addressed it. We have a test-bed located in CityU HK Shenzhen Research Institute, which is an experimental platform for the battery degradation acceleration experiments. The experimental platform can apply different temperature, humidity, and charging-discharging pattern settings to simulate the real scenarios. We have conducted our own physical experiments and collected data from batteries purchased by us. In addition, we also leverage the publicly accessible datasets published by MIT Group, U Maryland Group, NASA, etc. to further verify the effectiveness of our developed methods. On top of that, to further simulate batteries operating in EVs, we developed novel deep learning methods for first processing data with incomplete and variable charging-discharging profiles which simulate the real cases and next predicting the remaining useful life or estimating health status of batteries. To better accommodate the practical scenarios, we further studied robust deep learning methods which enable using limited charging-discharging cycle data to conduct the remaining useful life prediction task as well as further advance the method to enable online prediction. Meanwhile, we also extend the study with considering a wide application scope, e.g., incorporating the battery health consideration into a multi-energy system level operational optimization as well as on the electrical vehicle traffic time and collision predictions. Publications regarding Objective 3 can refer to publications No. 8, 11, 15, 25, 26, 28, and 29. Listed in Part C: Research Output. In summary, it is observable that original 3 objectives of the project have been successfully achieved. Moreover, the research story along this direction does not stop within the scope of 3 objectives. We have exceeded with extending the methodological development to fit more real applications as well as trigger a knowledge transfer project to root the research outcomes into realism and to generate real social impact.

11204419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204419.value: This project conducts a systematic study of AI or machine learning based methods for battery health management via leveraging nowadays growing volume and accessibility of battery data. Main findings of this project are 3-fold: 1) Battery data processing and feature engineering mechanisms. This project considered a variety of battery data including battery data collected via the research group’s experimental platform and battery datasets offered by research groups in MIT, UofMaryland, NASA, etc. in studying advanced methods for deriving meaningful data features for subsequent inference tasks based on various data availability scenarios, such as limited cycles, incomplete cycle data, noisy data, etc. A bi-branch network based system incorporating traditional LASSO based statistical feature selection and deep learning based latent feature engineering was developed to achieve a more adaptive response towards this need; 2) Data-driven model development for remaining useful life prediction and state-of-health estimation. Regarding data features engineered previously, methods ranging from traditional statistical learning (e.g., boosting regression tree, change-of-point method), classical machine learning (e.g., support vector regressor, shallow neural networks, splines-based regressors), and latest deep learning (e.g., CNN-LSVM, Attention, Transformer, etc.) have been explored in the modelling tasks for remaining useful life prediction and state-of-health estimation. A set of advanced deep network architectures have been designed for those tasks under different real charging-discharging scenarios. Moreover, novel model learning loss and regularization term designs are also explored to facilitate learning more reliable and generalizable models; 3) Application-oriented method studies. Customized modelling schemes regarding the real scenarios which might face limited battery cycle data, dynamic charging-discharging behaviours, and real-time reasoning functions have also been presented in results of this projects. Meanwhile, battery conditions targeted in the inference have also been incorporated into multi-energy system and transportation system to study a larger-scale system operations optimization.

11204419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204419.value: The machine learning and AI methods developed in this project for processing battery data, engineering advanced data features, and enabling robust performance in battery remaining useful life prediction and state of health estimation have attracted an IoT company, Tongda Electricm, in Guangzhou to work on the knowledge transfer. The methods and technologies developed will be deployed on the IoT system of Tongda for monitoring batteries of over 8000 electric buses operating in multiple cities in mainland China. This project received Guangdong government funding support of an amount 1 million RMB.

11204419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204419.value: This project studies machine learning/AI based methods for powering battery state-of-health estimation and remaining useful life predictions based on real battery data from various sources. The research development of this project can be described from three aspects, the novel battery data utilization mechanism, the novel battery data feature engineering schemes, and the novel battery modelling methods. A new mechanism of re-organizing tabular form battery data into a high dimensional tensor structure is invented to enable incorporating spatial and temporal correlated patterns across voltage-, capacity-, and temperature-related battery attributes. A comprehensive multi-branch feature engineering scheme which enables both traditional statistical attribute selection and deep learning powered latent feature engineering is developed to realize more effective and valuable feature pools for subsequent modelling. In modelling, latest famous deep network structures, such as attention mechanisms and transformers, are customized with new loss and regularization term designs to enable accurate and robust battery state-of-health estimation and remaining useful life predictions. Research outcomes have been verified via experimental data collected from the research group’s test-bed and other publicly accessible battery datasets. Meanwhile, the developed methods have been extended and applied into other applications considering remaining useful life prediction and fault diagnosis with similar advantages observed.

11204519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11204519.value: 基於混沌時間的高速光子隨機數發生器

11204519.label: Project Objectives
11204519.value: To demonstrate the extraction of randomness in the timing of rarely occurring pulses in a chaotic semiconductor laser. Through injection and feedback, the laser will be perturbed into chaos with bandwidths of over 10 GHz, which can be extended to 100 GHz through nonlinear propagation. The occurrences of rare and strong emission pulses will be used for triggering the sampling of clocks to yield random bits. To quantify the complexity of the chaotic timing for RBG. Both experimentally and numerically, the correlation dimensions of the chaotic signals will be analyzed when a laser is perturbed by continuous-wave optical injection, chaotic optical injection, conventional optical feedback, or dispersive optical feedback. This will allow for the optimization of the operating points for increasing the difficulties of state reconstruction in order to enhance security. To investigate correlated RBG by linking two identical arms of bit generation based on the randomness in timing. The two arms will be constructed as two identical fibers for nonlinear propagation of a common chaotic signal. They will also be constructed as two identical lasers subject to a common noisy injection. The consistency and synchronization of the outputs will be utilized for correlated timing RBG.

11204519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204519.value: High-speed generation of random bits is required in the areas of computation and secure communications. Compared to pseudo-random bits based on deterministic algorithms, random bit generation (RBG) based on physical devices are usually preferred because of the better randomness quality. In particular, photonic devices with wide bandwidths are useful sources of physical entropy for high-speed RBG. Photonic RBG has been investigated through various approaches based on quantum fluctuations, optical noise, and semiconductor lasers. With the capability of synchronization of fast dynamics, chaotic semiconductor lasers have attracted much attention for RBG through the endeavors of various groups, including our group, over the past years. However, the bandwidths of the intrinsic chaotic signals require fast postprocessing electronics. This is exemplified by the common use of analog-to-digital converters with a fine resolution of over 16 bits and a large bandwidth of over 10 GHz for RBG. Such a dependence on the postprocessing electronics not only increases the cost but also implies possible contamination of thermal noise during detection. In this proposal, RBG will be investigated by extracting timing randomness in chaotic dynamics of semiconductor lasers through both experiments and simulations. The approach relies on a semiconductor laser subject to perturbations of different forms into chaos and a fiber appended for subsequent nonlinear propagation, which will result in some rare occurrences of strong pulsations. Firstly, the irregular time intervals between the rarely occurring high-intensity pulses will be converted into random bits through triggered sampling of fast digital electrical clocks. Secondly, the chaotic signals will be analyzed for its complexity to ensure the randomness quality of the output, as linked to the evaluation of the correlation dimensions of the chaotic waveforms generated under different perturbations. Thirdly, correlated RBG will be investigated through linking two arms of bit generation using progressively secure ways for key distribution, where the consistency of nonlinear propagation in fibers and synchronization of chaotic lasers are utilized. Overall, the proposed approach based on the chaotic timing offers some unique advantages. It does not sensitively rely on the amplitude of the emission intensity. It avoids the possible contamination of electronic thermal noise. It does not require fast electronics for analog-to-digital conversion. By successfully utilizing the timing information of the rare pulses, the simplification of hardware and improvement in correlation will be achieved for high-speed RBG. 計算科學和保密通信需要高速隨機數發生器。相較於確定算法生成的偽隨機數，基於物理器件的隨機數發生器通常擁有更優秀的隨機特性。寬帶光子器件可作為信號源用於生成高速隨機數。光子隨機數發生器可基於量子擾動，光學噪聲或半導體激光器實現。過去幾年中在科研人員們的不懈努力之下，混沌半導體激光器因其具有快速同步的能力，引起了廣泛關注，我們課題組也致力於相關研究。然而，混沌信號的固有帶寬決定了它需要能夠快速響應的後處理電子器件。隨機數發生器通常需使用具有超過16位分辨率和超過10 GHz帶寬的模數轉換器。對後處理電子器件的依賴不僅僅增加了成本，亦可能在探測信號時引入熱噪聲污染信號。 本項目計劃通過數值仿真和實驗提取混沌半導體激光器時間信息來研究隨機數發生器。該方法需要不同擾動下的混沌半導體激光器以及用於後續非線性傳輸的光纖。該光纖可產生罕見高強度脈衝。該方法的具體步驟如下。首先，經由快速數字電子時鐘觸發採樣，罕見高強度脈衝不規則的時間間隔被轉換成隨機數。其次，為了確保其隨機性能優良，分析生成隨機信號的複雜度，如通過度量不同擾動下產生的混沌波形的關聯維數。接著，通過保密秘鑰分發鏈接兩個隨機數發生器，經由光纖非線性傳輸以及混沌激光器同步，生成相互關聯的隨機數。總而言之，本方法基於混沌的時間信息以獲得其獨特優勢。此方法幾乎不依賴激光強度的振幅，避免了電子熱噪聲的潛在影響，且不需要高速模數轉換的電子器件。利用罕見脈衝的時間信息，本項目可實現性能優良且硬件簡化的高速隨機數發生器。

11204519.label: Realisation of objectives
11204519.value: The project aims to investigate fast chaotic behaviors of semiconductor lasers in various aspects of timing properties. The temporal characteristics of the laser dynamics are considered in relation to random bit generation (RBG). Starting with a theoretical analysis on the timing behavior about regular bursts of unstable oscillations, a form of quasiperiodicity in the route-to-chaos was studied, where microwave oscillations at around 10 GHz were found to be organized in packets for a laser under optical feedback. While deterministic variations about the timing were analytically found to be inversely proportional to the feedback field strength, randomness associated with irregular bursts was extracted for generating unpredictable bits. Moreover, the complexity of the laser under a combination of feedback and injection was investigated by carefully measuring the correlation dimension D2 in the state space. Building on the conventional approaches, a refined method of measurement was adopted with a finite time-window and segmentation of the data, thereby obtaining one of the largest values of 10.6 for the dimension in experiments. Good agreements were yielded between numerical and experimental results about estimating the dimensions for complexity. Furthermore, in an attempt to generate more than one random signal, an experimental approach was developed for selecting multiple wavelengths in chaos generation, which was based on exciting some residual side modes of a single-mode laser. The effort resulted in broadband chaos generation at different wavelengths, which can be viewed as form of employing grossly detuned external gratings. Details about the research addressing the objectives as elaborated below. Objective 1 is about investigating the timing of bursts of intensity oscillations in a chaotic semiconductor laser. Using optical feedback on the laser, the repeated stable-unstable switching was first investigated, where the uncertain deviation of the timing from the simple round-trip time was analyzed. An analytical derivation was developed for the effective dwell time for the signal in the laser, which corresponds to a temporal expansion for the unstable oscillations. This dwell time was found to decrease when the linewidth enhancement factor increases. It is proportional to the photon lifetime and is inversely proportional to the feedback field strength. Generalization to the alternations between stability, period-one oscillations, and period-two oscillations was made in leading to chaos. Then, chaotic bursts were experimentally utilized for RBG by digitizing the timing signals. With a microwave oscillation frequency of about 3.6 GHz, bursts appeared erratically with a nominal time interval of 2.5 ns, resulting in an output bit rate on the order of 1 Gbps. The quality of the randomness was confirmed by the NIST Special Publication 800-22 statistical tests, where a total of 1000 streams of 1 million bits were tested at a significance level of 0.01. Additionally, by employing a 5-km long feedback loop, generation of random bits with the capability of storage across consecutive round trips was recently observed, despite some delay in conducting the experiments due to the unusual circumstance in the past few years. RBG based on such intermittent oscillations were obtained at 8 Gbps through the extraction of microwave envelopes and detecting the associated time instances. Objective 2 is about quantifying the complexity associated with the chaotic laser under various combinations of perturbations of feedback and injection. The complexity is measured through evaluating the maximal correlation dimensions D2 of the chaotic signals. By introducing a continuous-wave optical injection, a laser under optical feedback is found to exhibit enhancement of complexity, as quantified by the enhancement of D2 from 5.2 to 10.6 experimentally. The large D2 is desirable because of the linkage to the difficulty of state-space reconstruction in secure and randomness applications. To ensure correctness, D2 was carefully measured by observing a number of important criteria, which were occasionally ignored in related works. These include obeying the Takens criterion using large embedding dimensions up to 35, the Theiler window in relation to the relaxation resonance, an exceptionally long acquisition time span for ensuring statistical significance beyond the free-running laser coherence time, and short temporal segments for enabling computation using a relatively large data size of 20 million. Principal component analysis for re-embedding was considered for verifying the values too. As a result, although injecting a solitary laser is known to be low-dimensional, injecting the laser under feedback was confirmed to enhance D2 in the experiments. Numerically, the behavior of dimension enhancement was verified based on a single-mode laser model. Extensions to balanced homodyning with a delay was further considered, where the estimated dimension was found to nearly double as the baseband was strengthened. Also, the dimension enhancement was confirmed to be achieved together with the suppression of the undesirable time-delay signature. The combined perturbations with optical feedback and injection are found to effectively enhance the complexity. Objective 3 is about utilizing multiple channels of chaos on a single laser source. Perturbations with the use of dispersive fiber gratings at the main mode of the laser was proposed, but the research led to a modified approach of using grossly detuned gratings to match the residual side modes instead. Experiments on generating correlated arms were found to be quite challenging because of the influences of noise. Through an effort to suppress noise, an investigation on a form of external locking was subsequently adopted for improving frequency-modulated continuous-wave signals that reached 100 GHz. Then, the effort was steered towards generating chaos at multiple wavelengths for broadband signals with low self-correlation. This led to an experimental demonstration of broadband chaos by selectively exciting residual side modes of the single-mode laser. Although the residual side modes are often ignored in the study of chaos, the unique properties of these modes were unveiled to support broadband chaos with short coherence times. In particular, chaotic dynamics with spectral broadening was experimentally obtained by selectively feeding back light to a residual side mode via a grossly detuned grating. With the suppression of the main mode and selective excitation of the residual side mode, broadband chaotic dynamics was generated at the chosen wavelength that was tunable beyond 10 nm in a discrete manner. The resultant broad electrical bandwidth reached at least 26 GHz that corresponds to a significant broadening by over 50% when compared with the main mode. The dynamics was uniquely attributed to only one selected mode without invoking uncontrollable multimode interactions. Optically, the 30-dB optical linewidths have been enhanced to approach about 1 nm in wavelength that corresponds to 125 GHz in frequency. Electrically, the broadband chaos was measurable up to 32 GHz, as enabled by an enhanced data acquisition capability through an equipment upgrading, which was crucial for the characterization in the millimeter-wave range. The adjusted approach has hopefully opened up new opportunities for utilizing the fast photon decay rates of the residual side modes. Through the effort to address the objectives, the project enabled the development of the approaches of extracting the random timing in chaotic bursts, quantifying the complexity via careful measurements on the dimension D2, and extension to invoking residual side modes in broadened chaos generation, which are expected to enable future studies on the nonlinear dynamics at multiple wavelengths.

11204519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204519.value: The research contributed to 5 journal papers and 3 conference papers, including one currently in revision for submission. A Ph.D. student has recently received the degree through participating in the research as enabled by the project. The major findings of this project are summarized below. For extracting randomness in the bursts of intensity oscillations, a theoretical analysis on the timing of unstable oscillations resulted in a mathematical expression of the effective response time of the laser under feedback, which was found to be proportional to the photon lifetime and inversely proportional to the feedback strength. By passing the NIST Special Publication 800-22 statistical tests, bursts carried at 3.6 GHz were demonstrated for outputs at 1 Gbps. Improvements were obtained by employing a very long feedback loop of 5 km, thereby invoking intermittent oscillations with irregular timing in the envelope, which was processed for RBG at 8 Gbps. The results were documented in the derivation in journal publication [1] and conference publications [1,2], while additional recent demonstrations are to be reported in journal paper [5] in Part C. For quantifying complexity, a comprehensive effort was devoted to calculate the dimension D2 using the correlation integral. Amongst the highest experimental values in the literature, D2 of 10.6 was obtained under a number of criteria in the reconstruction of state-space based on the chaotic intensity-time series. Each estimation relied on 40 thousand segments, where each segment contained about 500 samples. Statistical significance was carefully ensured by using large data covering beyond the free-running coherence time of the laser. Relatively large embedding dimensions of around 30 were nominally adopted. The relatively meticulous procedure ensured verification of D2 enhancement via the combined perturbations. The results were documented in journal publication [2] and a recent conference publication [3] in Part C. As for utilizing multiple wavelengths of chaos, the correlation was found to be a challenge under noise that required suppression via investigations by locking, but the approach of dispersive feedback from gratings were applicable when grossly detuned. Besides leading to an investigation about external locking, the effort yielded the realization of chaos generation at multiple wavelengths by selecting the commonly ignored residual side modes of a single-mode distributed-feedback laser. Broadband signals were obtained with electrical spectra covering 32 GHz, where a conservative estimation suggests a broadening by over 50% in electrical bandwidth. The results were documented in journal publications [3,4] in Part C.

11204519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204519.value: Building on the study about the chaotic behavior under the combination of feedback and injection, further experimental and analytical investigations became possible. Firstly, about the extraction of randomness in the oscillatory envelope, it was observed that a long feedback loop can retain information across round trips. Such a generation of randomness along with storage is expected to enable future applications for which reproducibility is required. Secondly, for the careful evaluation of the dimension, the enhancement through combining injection with feedback was verified. The effort has led to identifying the criteria for determining the dimensions, while the efficiency of computation can be further improved through segmenting data. Lastly, about the observations of exciting the residual side modes, the laser was originally designed for single-mode operation with strong suppression of the other modes, where the unexpectedly broad chaotic dynamics could now be attributed to the fast cavity decay rates. Different from most approaches on wideband chaos, the use of a residual side mode avoids multimode interactions, implying the possibility of developing a model for synchronization without involving a large number of unknown parameters for multiple modes. Further development is foreseeable based on the newly observed chaos in the residual side modes.

11204519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204519.value: High-speed generation of random signals is required in the areas of computation and secure communications. Different from pseudo-random bits based on deterministic algorithms, random bits generated from physical devices are usually preferred due to the inherent entropy. Chaotic dynamics in semiconductor lasers has been known for supporting such applications, but the properties associated with the oscillatory bursts, complexity, and multiple channels required much investigation. This proposal enabled experimental and theoretical studies to investigate the above aspects. Random bits based on timing were generated at a high rate reaching 8 Gbps with only the envelope of the signals. Also, complexity was carefully shown to be much enhanced to beyond 10 dimensions based on time-windowed averaging of correlation integrals. Additionally, the residual side modes of single mode lasers are found to be of importance in broadband and wavelength-selective chaos generation at different channels. Such side modes are commonly ignored in the investigations of chaos. To continue along this line of work, researchers may be much interested in these methods of invoking and characterizing optical chaos due to the potential of direct modeling and fast responses in applications.

11204919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11204919.value: With the booming of social media services, huge amounts of images are being shared constantly, like Instagram, Flickr, Twitter, etc. These massive image resources, associated with rich semantics, are of significant value for exploration in the computer vision area. In particular, image classification has long been regarded as the foundation and the necessary preprocessing step for other computer vision tasks, from object detection to face recognition, semantic segmentation, image generation, and so on. Furthermore, the results of image classification can be integrated or utilized in multimodal learning scenarios where knowledge is mined from heterogeneous modalities including images, text, audio, etc. In recent years, deep neural network based models, owing to their excellent representation power, have achieved great success in image classification tasks. However, these models usually address image classification in the supervised setting, where the ground-truth category for each image needs to be available during the training stage. Unfortunately, date labelling can be quite expensive or even impossible to obtain for large datasets, making it difficult to learn robust deep models with good generalization performance. To overcome this obstacle, semi-supervised image classification aiming to employ a large amount of unlabeled data in conjunction with a small amount of labeled data has attracted lots of interests. Specically, semi-supervised learning improves the performance of classification models based on the cluster assumption, i.e., geometrically close data points should lie in the same classes. Existing works fall into two research lines: generative models based methods and perturbation based methods. Despite the progresses achieved, the results are far from satisfactory when trying to compete with the supervised models. To address the limitations of existing approaches for semi-supervised image classification, we propose to develop a generalized framework for semi-supervised learning by utilizing adversarial examples. An adversarial example is a slightly perturbated variant, thus human-recognizable, of an real image, designed to mislead the classification model to make totally different predictions despite their high perceptual similarity. Inspired by the recent success and popularity of adversarial networks, we will design the framework as a min-max game with two players, a generator for generating adversarial examples, and a classifier for classifying both the original samples and the adversarial examples correctly. To validate our proposed framework and its complementarity with other orthogonal works, an experimental prototype will be devised with large-scale real-world images to be collected from social media sites, thereby testing the effectiveness of the theory and techniques proposed in this project. 随着社会媒体服务的蓬勃发展，Instagram、Flickr、Twitter等海量图像不断共享，这些海量的图像资源与丰富的语义相结合，对计算机视觉领域的探索具有重要的价值。特别是，图像分类一直被视为其他计算机视觉任务的基础和必要的预处理步骤，从目标检测到人脸识别、语义分割、图像生成等。此外，图像分类的结果可以集成或应用于多模式学习场景中，这些场景中的知识是从图像、文本、音频等异构模式中挖掘出来的。近年来，基于深度神经网络的模型因其出色的表示能力而得以集成或使用，在图像分类任务中取得了很大的成功。但是，这些模型通常在监控设置中处理图像分类，在培训阶段需要提供每个图像的地面真值类别。但对于大型数据集来讲，日期标记可能非常昂贵，甚至不可能获得，这使得学习具有良好泛化性能的健壮深层模型变得困难。为了克服这一障碍，半监督图像分类试图将大量未标记的数据与少量标记的数据结合使用。从而提高了分类模型在聚类上的性能。现有的研究分为两个研究方向：基于生成模型的方法和基于扰动的方法。尽管取得了一些进展，但在试图与受监督模型竞争时，结果远不令人满意。为了解决现有的半监督图像分类方法的局限性，我们提出了一种利用对抗性实例来开发半监督学习的通用框架。一个对抗性的例子是一个稍微受干扰的变体，因此对人类识别没有困难，但却能误导分类模型作出完全不同的预测。在最近对抗性网络的成功和流行的启发下，我们将框架设计为两个参与者的最小-最大博弈，一个为生成对抗性示例的生成器，另一个为对原始示例和对抗性示例进行正确分类的分类器。为了验证我们提出的框架及与其它正交作品的互补性，我们将设计一个实验原型，从社交媒体网站上收集大规模的真实世界图像，来测试本项目中提出的理论和技术的有效性。

11204919.label: Realisation of objectives
11204919.value: For the first objective, a generalized semi-supervised image classification model is proposed [Ma et al. 2019]. More specifically, the model consists of two modules which are trained in an adversarial process: a generator mapping the original samples to adversarial examples which can fool the classifier, and a classifier that tries to classify the original samples and the adversarial examples consistently. This model can thus facilitate semi-supervised learning by Generated Adversarial examples based on Adversarial networks (GAA). This framework is applicable to unlabeled data by making the classifier minimize the distance between the output distribution on the original samples and their corresponding adversarial examples. Minimizing this distance based on unlabeled data improves the generalization performance of the classifier for semi-supervised learning. While this proposed method shows improved performance, it only focuses on the local neighborhood around the training samples while ignoring the space in-between them, leaving the model unpredictable in these regions. To overcome this problem, we further propose a novel consistency regularization technique, called Adversarial Mixup (AdvMixup) [Ma et al. 2020], by unifying the local neighborhood and the in-between neighborhood. In particular, we consider the neighborhood formed by the samples lying along the paths between the real samples and adversarial samples. For the second objective, we design an encoder-decoder architecture for the generator, allowing the model to generate adversarial examples beyond the pixel-wise perturbation and learn various types of perturbation such as local spatial transformation and color transformation. In addition, we also further studies how to generate images with higher quality. Considering that many losses in GANs heavily rely on a fixed-value function with limited expressive power in terms of robustness, we propose a parametric and robust alphabeta-loss function that can improve the performances of GAN on different data sets [Gnanha et al. 2022a]. Besides, there is a gap between the loss function of GAN used in theory and in practice. In theory, the proof of the Jensen divergence minimisation involves the min-max criterion, but in practice the non-saturating criterion is instead used to avoid gradient vanishing. We argue that the formulation of divergence minimization via GAN is biased and may yield a poor convergence of the algorithm. Thus, we propose the Residual Generator for GAN (Rg-GAN) [Gnanha et al. 2022b], which is inspired by the closed-loop control theory, to bridge the gap between theory and practice. Rg-GAN minimizes the residual between the loss of the generated data to be real and the loss of the generated data to be fake from the perspective of the discriminator. In this setting, the loss terms of the generator depend only on the generated data and therefore contribute to the optimisation of the model. We formulate the residual generator for standard GAN and least-squares GAN and show that they are equivalent to the minimisation of reverse-KL divergence and a novel instance of f-divergence, respectively. Furthermore, we prove that Rg-GAN can be reduced to Integral Probability Metrics (IPMs) GANs (e.g., Wasserstein GAN [Arjovsky et al. 2017]) and bridge the gap between IPMs and f-divergence. Additionally, we further improve on Rg-GAN by proposing a loss function for the discriminator that has a better discrimination ability. For the third objective, we develop an experimental prototype system to evaluate the proposed models for semi-supervised image classification on two benchmark datasets, i.e., the SVHN dataset and CIFAR-10 dataset. The SVHN dataset consists of 72,257 training images and 26,032 test images, and the CIFAR-10 dataset consists of 50,000 training images and 10,000 test images. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed techniques. To investigate the improvement from the proposed techniques in image generation, our experiments are based on CIFAR-10 (10 classes of colour images with 5k samples per class), the Cat dataset (containing 10k cat head images of different resolutions), and the LSUN dataset (which contains 3,033,042 bedroom images). The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed techniques can further boost model performance. References [Arjovsky et al. 2017] Arjovsky, M., Chintala, S., & Bottou, L. (2017, July). 11204919.label: Major findings and research outcome
11204919.value: Different with existing techniques building adversarial examples based on the pixel-wise perturbation, we consider that other types of adversarial examples (e.g., with spatial transformation) should also be useful for improving the robustness of the classifier. Thus, we incorporate GANs into the training of the classifier to further improve its performance. Although the proposed technique has improved model performance, it only focuses on the local neighborhood around the training samples while ignoring the space in-between them, leaving the model unpredictable in these regions. To overcome this problem, we further propose a novel consistency regularization technique. We conduct experiment on various datasets and the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed techinques. Besides, we find that many losses in GANs heavily rely on a fixed-value function with limited expressive power in terms of robustness, so we propose a new training objective to tackle this problem. Specifically, unlike standard GAN loss function it exploits the AB-divergence to weigh the likelihood ratio associated with each data point. This weighing mechanism makes the model robust to noises and yields better models in terms of FID score. Furthermore, the formulation of divergence minimization via GAN is biased and may yield a poor convergence of the algorithm, so we propose the Residual Generator for GAN to tackle this problem. Our proposed method is inspired by the closed-loop control theory, which can bridge the gap between theory and practice.

11204919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11204919.value: Although we have gained significant improvement in the research field, there are significant directions need to be further explored. The first one is how to further stabilize the training of GANs. The fragile training process of GANs may have negative influence on model performance when we adopt our method on more complicated scenarios. Another promising direction is how to adopt well-trained GANs in our proposed framework. The well-trained GANs are always trained on large scale dataset. They can generate more realistic images while the generated images may not be in the same distribution of the target dataset. If the well-trained GANs can be adjusted to generate images having same distribution as the target dataset, the performance of our proposed framework can be further improved.

11204919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11204919.value: In this project, we propose a new framework, which can boost model performance by making use of GANs to generate adversarial examples. Different with previous studies only building adversarial examples based on the pixel-wise perturbation, our proposed techniques can generate other types of adversarial examples (e.g., with spatial transformation). In addition, we further propose a novel consistency regularization technique which unify the local neighborhood and the in-between neighborhood. To improve the quality of generated images, we analyse the limitations in the existing training objectives of GANs and propose a new one. Our proposed objective weighs the likelihood ratio associated with each data point. Furthermore, we propose the Residual Generator for GAN to tackle the biased divergence minimization in existing GANs.

11205219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205219.value: Deep ultraviolet (UV) lasers are essential for enormous use ranging from medical and life science to environmental and industrial applications. Conventional deep UV lasers reliant on gas discharge and high-order harmonic generation are large in size, expensive in cost, and difficult to operate. These drawbacks largely limit applications of these technologies in many scenarios. Semiconductor lasers hold the potential for miniaturization. However, it is unlikely to achieve deep UV lasing solely based on semiconductors, because no method is available to fabricate high-quality wide-bandgap semiconductor materials. Herein, we propose to develop a class of nanostructured materials comprising high concentration of lanthanide dopants for performing photon upconversion lasing. The design combines the advantage of the sophisticated semiconductor technology and unique photon upconversion property of lanthanide ions. The heavily doped nanocrystals are expected to enhance the absorption of pumping light, and subsequently generate intense upconverted emission in shorter wavelengths. Careful optimization of hierarchical core-shell structures coupled with design of innovative excitation schemes will be utilized to alleviate concentration quenching in the nanocrystals. Once refined, we envisage that our study may deepen our understating of lanthanide luminescence and revolutionize the fabrication of cost-effective and miniaturized solid-state lasers operating at short wavelengths. 深紫外激光器在科研、国防、医疗、工业等领域都有重要的应用。传统深紫外激光器通常体积大、造价高、操作复杂，因而在很多应用场合受到限制。半导体激光器具有小型化的特点，但是受制于宽带隙半导体的制备工艺，深紫外半导体激光器目前尚未完全实现。本项目拟采用高掺杂的稀土纳米晶为增益介质，经由长波长的半导体激光器激发，通过光频上转换实现深紫外激光。我们计划通过核壳结构设计结合新型激发平台来克服稀土掺杂离子的浓度猝灭，从而在高掺纳米晶中获得高亮度的上转换发光，并籍此实现高效率的上转换激光器。本研究的实施有望加深我们对稀土发光的认识，并推进小型化深紫外激光器制备技术的革新。

11205219.label: Realisation of objectives
11205219.value: This project aims to mitigate the concentration quenching effect in lanthanide-doped luminescent materials through nanostructural engineering of the host crystals. In this way, intense upconversion luminescence with large anti-Stokes shift can be realized via heavy doping, thereby enabling UV lasing by NIR excitation. We have achieved these objectives through the following deliverables. 1. We have established novel protocols for controlled synthesis of high-quality core-shell nanocrystals of different compositions, such as NaLaF4:Nd@NaLaF4, NaYbF4@NaNdF4, NaYbF4@NaYF4, ScF3:Yb/Er@ScF3, NaGdF4@NaGdF4:Nd/Yb@NaGdF4, and NaYF4:Yb/Tm@NaErF4:Ce@NaYF4. Using these materials platforms, we have systematically examined the interaction of lanthanide dopants at the nanometer scale using steady-state and transient spectroscopy. The results reveal that localized energy exchange (e.g., cross-relaxation and phonon-assisted energy transfer) and long-distance energy migration, which are strengthened at high doping concentrations due to the shortened separation of dopant ions, are the main origins of concentration quenching. 2. We demonstrate that energy-migration-induced concentration quenching can be eliminated by doping the lanthanide ions in the core level of a core/inert-shell structure, which can prevent long-distance energy migration towards quenching centers at the nanoparticle surface. Meanwhile, local energy dissipation can be minimized by high-power excitation. On a separate note, we have found that some special dopant ions, such as Yb3+ and Tm3+, can act as trapping centers to recycle the excitation energy, which effectively mitigates concentration quenching as well. Accordingly, by appropriate doping in core-shell structured nanocrystals coupled with high-power excitation, we have achieved intense upconversion luminescence at unusually high doping concentrations. 3. We have devised a tandem upconversion scheme based on heavy doping of Yb/Tm/Er/Ce in a NaYF4:Yb/Tm@NaErF4:Ce@NaYF4 nanocrystal, realizing UV emission at 290 nm by NIR excitation at 1550 nm with an anti-Stokes shift of 1260 nm (~3.5 eV). By systematically investigating the energy cascade process, we demonstrate a domino upconversion (DU) scheme that relies on the core-shell structure design and high concentration doping of multiple lanthanide ions, including 99% Yb3+ in the core level and 70% Er3+/30% Ce3+ in the inner shell layer. These results substantiate that core-shell nanostructrual engineering is a versatile strategy for combating concentration quenching, which largely expands the scope of lanthanide-doped upconversion materials. 4. A waveguide structure is developed for effective excitation of upconversion nanocrystals at low input powers. Owing to its small dimension, the waveguide structure spatially confines the incident light and thus enhances the power density of the excitation field. The nanocrystals sitting at the top of the waveguide structure can be excited through the evanescent fields of the waveguide. Specifically, a high excitation power density of 2073 kW cm−2 can be obtained at an input power of 311 mW. As a result, a miniaturized system comprising a waveguide excitation platform and a fiber-coupled spectrometer can be easily constructed for effective excitation of upconversion nanocrystals and collection of upconverted emissions. 5. We have successfully integrated upconversion nanocrystals into a toroidal microresonator with high Q factor (200K). The toroidal microresonator acts as the laser cavity by supporting whispering gallery mode at the internal boundaries of the nanoparticle-doped microtoroidal resonator. Under free-space excitation of a 1550 nm pulse laser with 6 ns frequency duration and 10 Hz repetition rate, multiwavelength lasing at 289 nm, 346 nm, 381 nm, 410 nm, 450 nm, 475 nm, 526 nm, and 547 nm are realized. Notably, the microlasers are susceptible to the Q-factor of the cavity, which can be affected by contaminations such as small biological species. Accordingly, we demonstrate reliable single-particle detection by monitoring the emission intensity and threshold pumping power.

11205219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205219.value: We have identified the critical role of misfit strain in controlling the epitaxial habit. We also reveal that the strain effect on epitaxial growth can be mitigated by manipulating the synthetic variables, such as precursor concentration and reaction temperature. These advances have enabled us to assemble different crystal compositions into core-shell nanostructures with high conformality, which is essential for deliberately tuning upconversion luminescence without compromising the emission efficiency. Based on the newly developed nanocrystals, we have identified the equally important role of localized energy transfer and long-distance energy migration in quenching luminescence at high doping concentrations. We have also found a practical approach to mitigate concentration quenching by using active-core/inert-shell nanostructure in combination with a waveguide circuit excitation platform. Notably, the approach can effectively solve the concentration quenching between multiple types of lanthanide ions. The nanostructural engineering of host materials largely expands the designability of photon upconversion, simultaneously creating new possibilities in technological applications. Due to their small feature size and high uniformity, the core-shell nanocrystals can be easily integrated into composite microcavities to generate tunable lasing emissions. We also find that the core-shell nanocrystals are a powerful platform for drug delivery. They can serve as a vehicle to load and transport drugs, simultaneously achieving on-demand drug release through the NIR-triggered light emission. Due to our innovative and systematical works in this field, we have been invited to summarize our findings in a number of review papers, which include 1) Lanthanide-Based Luminescent Materials for Waveguide and Lasing (Chem. Asian J. 2020, 15, 21); 2) Combating concentration quenching in upconversion nanoparticles (Acc. Chem. Mater. 2020, 32, 2004142); 5) Visible-to-Ultraviolet Light Conversion: Materials and Applications (Adv. Photonics Res. 2021, 2, 2000213); 6) Recent Advances in Cellular Optogenetics for Photomedicine (Adv. Drug Deliv. 11205219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205219.value: Our study highlights that core-shell nanostructured host materials can integrate incompatible lanthanide dopants at high doping levels to achieve unprecedented luminescence processes. Given the variable host configurations and the enormous number of available activator combinations, we expect more upconversion materials to emerge and promote advanced applications. Particularly, our investigation of short-wavelength lasing through upconversion luminescence may inspire the development of miniaturized UV lasers at low costs.

11205219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205219.value: The light emission properties of lanthanide-doped luminescent materials are dominated by dopants because the host materials are typically transparent. Therefore, a high doping concentration is usually necessary to generate strong luminescence. However, an over-high doping concentration can lead to very weak luminescence due to deleterious cross-talk between dopant ions in the crowded host lattice. To solve this problem, we designed a class of nanostructured host materials to regulate the dopant-dopant interactions by spatially separating incompatible dopant ions at the nanoscale. In addition, a waveguide circuit platform is devised for efficient excitation of the dopant ions. By promoting the majority of the dopant ions to the excited state, the cross-talk due to interaction between excited dopants and unexcited (ground-state) dopants can be further minimized. During the course of our investigation, we have established advanced synthetic protocols for preparing a diversity of core-shell nanocrystals. Based on these new nanocrystal systems, we have achieved striking upconversion luminescence properties (e.g., high intensity and large anti-Stokes shift) and realized deep UV lasing by excitation in the telecommunication wavelengths. Overall, our findings provide both the theoretical basis and practical guidance to construct highly doped nanocrystals for applications in short-wavelength lasing, anti-counterfeiting, optogenetics, and beyond.

11205419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205419.value: 由于小型无人机在侦查、运输等领域可观的潜在价值，研究小型的人机友好的无人机受到了科学家和工程师们的广泛关注。这些小型机器人可能彻底改变我们对机器人的认识。然而，与传统飞行器不同的是，在小尺度上，飞行器的效率急剧下降。这限制了小型飞行器的发展。 人们的兴趣转向于探索多运动模式的飞行机器人，试图克服能量限制，并扩展其功能。小尺度机器人拥有更大的表面重量比，因此更加适合执行平面上的运动。应用合适的粘性介质，小型机器人可以倒挂或暂时停留在屋顶上以节省能量。另外，空-地混合的运动已被证明是一种可行的穿越非结构化环境的策略。然而，到目前为止，多运动模式飞行器往往需要额外的执行机构或复杂的机制来适应不同运输模式的要求。 在这项研究中，我们将展示如何利用简单的气动效应和折叠机构，创造出一种新型的具有更高效能的多功能可变形四旋翼无人机。本项目中我们通过三个步骤来提升飞行器效率。首先，为了实现表面下的飞行，我们利用了螺旋桨的天花板效应。根据我们的初步实验，当旋转螺旋桨置于一个平面以下时，其功耗可降低为三分之一。我们试图对该现象进行建模，并利用该效应，消耗极小的能量让无人机停留在表面之下。第二，我们的目标是将这些空气动力学效应与微型支架相结合，设计一种机械装置，使机器人能够在没有反馈的情况下被动的停在表面之下。最后，我们将结合“折纸技术”来制造一个强大而轻巧的可变形机身。这种被动式可折叠结构使机器人能够旋转推力矢量，以便在平坦地形上滚动。与现有设计相比，矢量化的推力可将功率耗散降低至多两倍，从而使地面运动的范围从根本上扩大。 由此可见，该项研究将通过扩展微型飞行器的续航力和工作范围，扩大了飞行器的应用范围，为微型飞行器领域的发展做出贡献。科学价值将来自：（i）开发空气动力学模型和验证螺旋桨的天花板效应；（ii）实施提供附加功能的被动转换的机械智能设计；以及（iii）实现具有空中-地面-平面移动能力的高效能机器人。

11205419.label: Realisation of objectives
11205419.value: The research project "Reconfigurable Quadrotors with Energetically Efficient Multimodal Locomotion" aimed to explore and develop strategies for enhancing the energy efficiency and operational capabilities of small-scale rotorcraft through multimodal locomotion. The project focused on three main objectives: characterizing and modeling ceiling effects, developing damping mechanisms for perching on vertical surfaces, and creating a reconfigurable MAV capable of efficient rolling motion. Throughout the project, significant progress has been made in achieving these objectives, leading to the development of novel models, mechanisms, and designs that contribute to the advancement of energy-efficient multimodal locomotion for MAVs. The first objective of characterizing and modeling the ceiling effects, including the aerodynamic interaction between multiple propellers, has been thoroughly investigated and achieved [Hsiao and Chirarattananon, 2019]. By employing the momentum theory, we have successfully developed a theoretical model that describes the relationship between the thrust and power consumption of spinning propellers in proximity to a ceiling. The proposed model introduces a dimensionless parameter, the ceiling coefficient, which quantifies the reduction in the aerodynamic power required to generate a given thrust when a propeller operates near a ceiling. Furthermore, the model has been extended to account for the nonaxisymmetric flow and the recirculation of the wake caused by the interaction between neighboring propellers in a multirotor configuration. A series of comprehensive experiments using two different propeller sizes (23-mm and 50-mm radii) in various configurations validated the proposed model, confirming the substantial power reduction of up to three times for a quadrotor with 23-mm propellers operating near a ceiling. The successful characterization and modeling of the ceiling effects provide valuable insights into the development of energy-efficient multimodal locomotion strategies for small-scale rotorcraft. The second objective, which aimed to develop and design damping mechanisms suitable for perching on vertical surfaces based on the dynamics of Micro Aerial Vehicles (MAVs), has been thoroughly completed [Hsiao et al., 2023]. We developed a 32-gram rotorcraft capable of repeatedly perching and taking off from both overhangs and walls on various wet and dry surfaces. The perching strategy combined the use of propelling thrust to support the robot against the surface and maintain balance, along with mussel-inspired wet adhesives. This approach eliminated the need for additional components typically required for attachment and detachment, which would increase power consumption due to added weight. The final rotorcraft design was only 1.09 grams heavier than the original prototype, but demonstrated a 50% and 85% reduction in power consumption when perching on ceilings and walls, respectively. This substantial reduction in power consumption led to a fourfold increase in the total mission time, successfully validating perching maneuvers as an effective energy conserving strategy for MAVs. The third objective, which aimed to adopt an origami-inspired fabrication method for creating a reconfigurable MAV and validate the rolling motion as a strategy for extending the robot's range, has been thoroughly achieved. The development of the Quadrolltor, as detailed in the IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters paper [Jia et al., 2023], exemplifies the successful realization of this objective. The Quadrolltor employs passively reconfigurable structures that enable a tightly coupled rolling and turning mechanism, significantly improving rolling efficiency and terrestrial maneuverability. By integrating four passively reconfigurable joints, the Quadrolltor can efficiently generate the necessary torque for rolling without additional actuators, thereby conserving energy. Experimental results demonstrated the robot's ability to perform precise rolling and turning maneuvers, and power measurements indicated a 15-fold extension in operational range at low speeds. This innovative design, leveraging passive morphological adaptation, validates the effectiveness of the rolling motion as a viable strategy for extending the MAV's range, meeting and even surpassing the initial project expectations. In conclusion, the project has successfully met its goals, demonstrating significant advancements in the field of MAVs. The first objective's thorough investigation into the aerodynamic ceiling effects has provided a robust theoretical model and experimental validation, contributing valuable insights into energy-efficient propeller configurations. The second objective’s completion resulted in a novel perching mechanism that dramatically reduces power consumption and extends mission duration, showcasing the practical benefits of energy conservation strategies. Finally, the third objective's realization through the development of the Quadrolltor highlights the potential of reconfigurable MAVs with rolling capabilities to significantly enhance operational range and versatility. These achievements collectively represent a substantial step forward in the design of energetically efficient multimodal locomotion for MAVs, paving the way for their wider adoption in various demanding applications.

11205419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205419.value: The research project has yielded significant advancements in the field of Micro Aerial Vehicles (MAVs), contributing to both theoretical knowledge and practical applications. The major findings and outcomes of this project are as follows: 1. Characterization and Modeling of Ceiling Effects: • Developed a theoretical model using momentum theory to describe the relationship between thrust and power consumption of spinning propellers near a ceiling. • Introduced the dimensionless ceiling coefficient to quantify power reduction. • Validated the model experimentally, demonstrating a substantial power reduction of up to three times for a quadrotor with 23-mm propellers operating near a ceiling. • These findings provide crucial insights for optimizing propeller configurations to enhance energy efficiency in MAVs. 2. Development of Perching Mechanisms: • Created a 32-gram rotorcraft capable of perching and taking off from various vertical surfaces using mussel-inspired wet adhesives. • Achieved a 50% and 85% reduction in power consumption when perching on ceilings and walls, respectively. • This innovation led to a fourfold increase in total mission duration, validating perching as an effective energy-conserving strategy for MAVs. 3. Origami-Inspired Reconfigurable MAV: • Developed the Quadrolltor, an MAV with passively reconfigurable joints enabling efficient rolling and turning maneuvers. • Demonstrated a 15-fold extension in operational range at low speeds through experimental validation. • This design showcases the potential of rolling motion as a viable strategy for extending MAV operational range and conserving energy. These findings have been disseminated through several high-impact publications and intellectual property filings, highlighting the project's contribution to the scientific community and industry: • Journal Publications: Five journal papers have been published, including three in IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics, one in IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters (IEEE RAL), and one in Communications Engineering. • Academic Contributions: The research has culminated in one PhD thesis. • Patents: One US patent has been granted, and one patent has been filed in China, protecting the innovative designs and mechanisms developed during the project.

11205419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205419.value: Moving forward, our research will continue to tackle the endurance and power challenges of small drones by leveraging multimodal locomotion. Specifically, we are shifting our focus from wheeled locomotion, which is limited to structured terrains, to exploring legged locomotion for jumping. We have initiated studies on hybrid hopping-flying locomotion, which promises to further enhance the versatility and efficiency of MAVs. This innovative approach has already garnered support, resulting in a successful GRF proposal and the commencement of a new project in 2024. Our initial findings have been promising, culminating in a publication in Science Robotics (2024). By integrating jumping capabilities with traditional aerial functions, we aim to develop MAVs that can navigate complex environments more effectively, thereby expanding their practical applications in various fields.

11205419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205419.value: Our research project focused on making small flying robots, called Micro Aerial Vehicles (MAVs), more energy-efficient and versatile. We aimed to improve their ability to fly, perch, and move on the ground by developing new technologies and methods. First, we studied how MAVs use less energy when flying close to the ceiling, discovering ways to reduce power consumption by up to three times. This helps them fly longer without needing to recharge. Second, we created a tiny, lightweight MAV that can stick to walls and ceilings using a special adhesive inspired by mussels. This allows the robot to save energy by perching instead of constantly flying, leading to a much longer operational time. Finally, we designed a reconfigurable MAV that can roll on the ground, inspired by origami. This rolling capability extends the robot's range significantly, allowing it to cover more ground with less energy. Overall, our research has led to significant improvements in the efficiency and capabilities of MAVs, making them more practical for various applications, such as search and rescue, environmental monitoring, and inspection tasks. These advancements have been shared through scientific publications and patents, showcasing their potential impact on both academia and industry.

11205619.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11205619.value: 帶預算的設施選址博弈: 從參與者到設施

11205619.label: Project Objectives
11205619.value: For the proposed budgeted facility location games where some locations are to be selected to build facilities from a given set of candidate positions with the total building cost not exceeding the government's budget, we consider the strategic behavior of agents and aim to design strategyproof mechanisms with guaranteed performance. We will start with uniform cost model where the cost of building at each given location is the same and then extend to the general model where the costs could be different. For the budgeted facility location games, we then consider the strategic behavior of facility holders, who has a private building cost or other information. We aim to design strategyproof mechanisms with good approximations with respect to certain social objectives, maximizing social utility or minimizing social cost. We also aim to prove approximation lower bounds. For the combined model where each agent itself is also a potential facility holder, we firstly study the uniform case and aim to design strategyproof mechanisms with payment which could achieve good performance guarantee and then extend to the possibility of mechanisms with partial payment where payment can only be made to the winning agent while other agents also share utilities. For the combined model, we will further study the weighted version and budget feasible version of the problem and try to design truthful mechanisms with guaranteed approximation ratios.
