11205619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11205619.value: 算法博弈論結合了博弈論和算法設計，其主要目標是在復雜的博弈環境中設計性能优异的算法。在本項目中，我們主要研究設施選址博弈問題。在最傳統的设施选址博弈问题中，通常假設政府計劃在一條街道上蓋一個設施（比如超市或者公共汽車站）。街道上住著一些擁有私有信息的住戶。他們希望距離這個設施盡可能的近。政府的目標是在收集住戶的信息之後作決策，使得住戶報虛假信息不會得到任何好處（具有這種性質的機制叫做可信機制），而同時政府的目標（比如社會代價或最大代價）可以近似優化。機制可以是確定性的，也可以是隨機的，性能的上界可以通過設計一個特定的機制得到，而性能的下界意味著任何可信機制都不能比該界做的更好。 近年来有很多关于设施选址问题的扩展，比如如果住戶希望離設施越遠越好，則問題稱為排斥型設施選址問題。 我們把兩種喜好合在一起考慮了耦合模型。並且也研究了住戶既不想太靠近設施又不想太遠離設施的雙峰喜好模型。如果有两个不同的设施，我们之前考虑了用户代价由近的设施或远的设施决定的选择喜好模型，以及当两个设施具有类似功能时的比例喜好模型，其中用户的代价为他到两个设施的加权和。 设施选址博弈问题近年来得到了广泛的研究, 但之前的研究仅考虑设施使用者的欺骗行为。本项目计划将设施本身也纳入到允许欺骗的范围内，尝试设计可以让双方都无意欺骗的机制。为此也需要将钱引入到设施选址博弈的机制设计中，从而为传统的无金钱交易的设施选址博弈注入新的血液，并尝试将两种机制设计统一起来。在本项目中我们会考虑设施有几个备选的地点以及政府有一定的预算。最后我们将设施使用者和设施的身份统一在社区的概念上，设计两个角色统一时的可信机制。在该新问题上的机制设计将有别于传统的带金钱交易的机制设计，因为一个用户即使没有拿到设施的建设权也会有效用，从而建立带金钱的机制设计和不带金钱的机制设计之间的桥梁。

11205619.label: Realisation of objectives
11205619.value: For Objective 1, we have studied the uniform cost model of budgeted facility location games. Formally, given a set of m candidate locations of facilities in a metric space, we want to select k locations to build facilities, based on the information reported by agents. Each agent reports her nearest candidate location to a mechanism, and has a cost equal to the distance to the nearest opened facility. We designed mechanisms with guaranteed performance. Precisely, for the objective of minimizing the total cost of agents, we designed a deterministic mechanism with approximation ratio of 3, which is best possible for all deterministic mechanisms. When k=m-1, we improved this ratio to 3-2/m by randomization, which is also best possible. Moreover, we studied the objective of maximizing the total utility of agents, and derived upper and lower bounds on the approximation ratio of all mechanisms. This work is published in AAAI 2020. We also considered the general model where the building costs of candidate locations could be different and the total building cost of the selected candidates cannot exceed the given budget. When the building cost of every candidate is more than half the budget, the problem is equivalent to the uniform cost model with k=1, and there is a 3-approximation deterministic strategyproof mechanism for minimizing the maximum cost: choose the candidate that is nearest to the leftmost client. For the settings with more general costs, while no deterministic strategyproof mechanism can have an approximation ratio better than 3 for the social cost, there is no positive result yet because this problem is at least as hard as the mechanism design version for knapsack problems. This part of results are not sufficient for publication. For Objective 2, we have studied the model in which facility holders act strategically to report their own costs for building facilities. Formally, customers (i.e., agents) and facilities holders are located at publicly known locations on a line. Each facility holder has an opening-cost as her private information, and may strategically report it. Upon receiving the reports, the government uses a mechanism to select some facilities to open and pay to them. The cost/utility of each customer depends on the distance to the nearest opened facility. Under a given budget B, which constrains the total payment, we derived upper and lower bounds on the approximation ratios. Precisely, for minimizing the social cost, we shown that no deterministic (randomized universally) truthful budget feasible mechanism can achieve bounded approximation ratio; for maximizing the social utility, we proposed a deterministic truthful budget feasible mechanism with approximation ratio 2, which is best possible. Moreover, we studied the case when augmented budget is allowed. This work is published in IJCAI 2020. In the journal version JAAMAS 2022, we further considered a more general setting where the customers can also strategically report their locations (as in the classic setting), while facilities still bid the opening costs. We presented a truthful budget-feasible mechanism that is 3-approximation for the social utility. Moreover, we discussed the online setting in which facilities arrive online one after another in a random order, and we derived a mechanism with 2e competitive ratio. For Objective 3, we have studied the combined model where each agent itself is also a potential facility holder. Formally, each agent is located on a publicly known location in a metric space, and can allow a facility to be opened at her place. But the opening cost is private information and she may strategically report it. Besides, each agent also bears a service cost equal to the distance to her nearest opened facility. Given agents’ reports, a mechanism outputs a set of agents whose facilities could be opened, and a payment to each of these agents who opens a facility. We first characterized the truthful mechanisms, and then designed truthful mechanisms with payments. For the social cost objective, we gave an optimal exponential-time truthful mechanism; for the minmax cost objective, we provided an optimal polynomial-time truthful mechanism. When agents have uniform weight and the total weight selected cannot exceed a budget, the above results still hold. This result is published in AAMAS 2019. For Objective 4, we have studied the combined model for designing budget feasible and truthful mechanisms with guaranteed approximation ratios. Assume that the government has a total financial budget B, and a mechanism is called budget feasible if the total payment does not exceed the budget. For the social cost objective, every truthful and budget-feasible mechanism has a linear approximation ratio in terms of the number of participants n. For the minmax cost objective, we find a lower bound 1.5 for the approximation ratio of any truthful and budget feasible mechanisms. For both objectives, if at most one facility is allowed to open, there is an optimal truthful and budget feasible mechanism, running in polynomial time. Augmented budget scenario is also studied where budget can be violated to a certain multiplicative factor. This result is published in Theoretical Computer Science.

11205619.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205619.value: We considered budgeted facility location problems where the government plans to build some public facilities to serve self-interested agents or residents in the city, and the decision-making is based on the preferences of these agents. We designed strategyproof mechanisms for building facilities that can elicit truthful information from the agents, and these mechanisms have good performance guarantee (measured by the approximation ratio) in terms of the social cost or maximum cost objectives. For the budgeted facility location games with strategic clients (Objective 1), in the uniform-cost model, we presented a deterministic strategyproof mechanism with best possible approximation ratio of 3 for social cost, and improved this ratio to 3-2/m by randomization when selecting m-1 candidate locations for building facilities. In the general model, no deterministic strategyproof mechanism can have an approximation ratio better than 3. This result is published in AAAI 2020 in Part C. For the budgeted facility location games with strategic facilities (Objective 2), we shown that no truthful budget feasible mechanism has bounded approximation ratio for social cost, and we proposed a deterministic truthful budget feasible mechanism with approximation ratio 2 for maximizing the social utility. In the online setting where facilities arrive online one after another in a random order as in a secretary problem, we derived a 2e-competitive mechanism. This result is published in IJCAI 2020 in Part C. For the more general setting where the customers can also strategically report their locations while facilities still bid the opening costs, we presented a truthful budget-feasible mechanism that is 3-approximation for the social utility. This result is published in JAAMAS 2022 in Part C. For the combined model with both strategic clients and facilities (Objective 3&4), we provided a characterization of all truthful mechanisms, and presented truthful mechanisms for social cost and maximum cost. Further, when there is a budget constraint, we shown that every truthful and budget-feasible mechanism has approximation ratio at least O(n) for social cost and at least 1.5 for maximum cost. If at most one facility is allowed to open, we found an optimal truthful and budget feasible polynomial-time mechanism. If at most k facilities can open for any constant k ≥2, we exclude the possibility of acceptable approximation for both objectives. These results are published in AAMAS 2019 and Theoretical Computer Science 2022 in Part C.

11205619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205619.value: The horizon for mechanism design in facility location research is expansive, with potential strides in algorithmic game theory and computational social choice. Future developments could see the design of mechanisms that incorporate predictive analytics to anticipate agents' behaviors and preferences, thereby enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of facility placement. The exploration of multi-agent systems where facilities impact each other could lead to more nuanced solutions. Advancements may also involve robust mechanisms that can withstand strategic manipulation and ensure social welfare even when agents have incomplete or asymmetric information. The integration of ethical considerations and fairness constraints into mechanism design is another promising avenue, ensuring that the outcomes are not only efficient but also equitable. To achieve these advancements, a multidisciplinary approach is essential, combining insights from economics, computer science, and urban planning. This collaborative effort would involve both theoretical research to refine the models and empirical studies to test their real-world applicability. The ultimate goal is to develop mechanisms that are not only theoretically sound but also practically implementable, leading to improved societal outcomes in the allocation of resources and services.

11205619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205619.value: The research project studies the decision-making process of the government for building facilities (e.g., libraries, parks, schools) to service the residents of the city, based on the preferences of the residents over the facility locations and the social welfare. We designed mechanisms that determine (approximately) optimal facility locations and elicit truthful information from the residents who may have incentives to misreport their own private information like their locations. The specific scenarios studied in the project is building facilities within certain budget and allowing the agents (communities) to build public facilities that can be used by all communities. One of the significances of the project is the extension to the auction theory where even those who do not win in the auction also have utility. This field has seen significant progress with various methodologies developed to handle different problem variants. The research topic is not just about placing physical facilities; the principles extend to other decision-making scenarios, such as political representation and temporal decision making. This study of mechanism design for facility location is therefore not only academically rich but also practically invaluable, providing solutions that are both strategically sound and socially optimal.

11205819.value: 2017年，3D列印（也稱為增材製造）的全球收入達到73億美元，是1995年的25倍。預計其市場將繼續增長，從2017年到2023年其預計複合年增長率為25.76％，在2023年其市場將達到327.8億美元。這項顛覆性技術將改變建築、生物組織工程、航空航太等行業。例如，在迪拜、上海和阿姆斯特丹等地已經出現了整個房屋都使用3D列印來建造。其他例子還包括培養的皮膚細胞可以直接印製在燒傷的傷口上；宇航員可以在國際空間站上列印替換部件。 將3D列印用於天線加工的目標不僅僅在於提高其性能，而且還通過利用其提供的卓越的幾何靈活度來實現天線設計的範式轉移。 在5G無線通訊時代初期，對更高無線傳輸速率不斷增長的需求要求將載波頻率提高到太赫茲頻帶以獲得更多通道容量。我們專案的目標是推動當前3D印表機的性能以實現工作在太頻段的新型透鏡天線，包括圓極化透鏡，雙圓極化透鏡，圓極化聚焦透鏡，二維線極化焦點掃描透鏡和軸向線極化焦點掃描透鏡。這些透鏡都採用商用的太赫茲線極化喇叭饋電。利用旋轉和平移設備，結合最後兩個透鏡便可組成太赫茲三維成像系統的硬體平臺。由此項目獲得的知識以及不斷提高和進步的3D列印解析度和材料使我們能夠為將來的幾百Gbps的無線通訊以及太赫茲三維成像的天線設計提供指導。 由於所提出的用於太赫茲三維成像系統的透鏡天線具有複雜的結構和形狀，其成功實現將大大提升香港和珠江三角洲地區的加工製造業水準。

11205819.label: Realisation of objectives
11205819.value: We investigated the use of Form2 printers from FormLabs using the approach outlined in the original proposal. It has a minimum thickness of 25 microns and a laser spot size of 140 microns, which prints objects upside down without filling material. Therefore, supporting struts with 2mm in length and 0.2mm in diameter are used when the base of the printing structure is not flat or cannot be easily detached from the printer’s raft. This printing method differs from that FormLabs recommended, fulfilling Objective 1. To generate circular polarization (CP), we made use of a dielectric grating. When the electric field direction of a normally incident wave is oriented 45° from the axis along the length of the grating, the two orthogonal components of the electric field will propagate at different speeds, leading to a CP wave when the grating is properly designed. The conference paper (C1) in Part C presented a CP Bessel beam launcher fed by a standard linearly-polarized (LP) pyramidal horn operating at 300 GHz. The launcher is a dielectric lens of 30×30 pixels. Each pixel has two sections. The lower section has a fixed length for the polarizer, which converts LP to CP. The upper section has a variable length for phase adjustment. The launcher's upper section transforms a quasi-Gaussian beam radiating from the horn to a well-confined, collimated pseudo-Bessel beam. In designing the lens, the phase distribution at the lens aperture plays a much more vital role than the amplitude of the wave. Once the aperture phase is determined, the lens is realized by choosing the pixel height. This work addressed Objectives 1 and 2. One of the appealing properties of Bessel beam is its nondiffractive characteristic, meaning that the radiating wave maintains confined and does not suffer from diffractive spreading as it propagates. However, the beam exhibits nondiffractive properties in practice and maintains a high-intensity focus over a considerable distance. As given in the original proposal, we provided the design methodology for a dual orthogonal CP with two designated radiation directions. The phase common and phase difference as well as CP properties were implemented in a single 3D-printed pixel. The whole dual-CP lens was fabricated using Form2 printer. Unfortunately, the pixel elements operating at 0.3 THz resulted in residues trapped in the air voids, adversely affecting the lens performance. We attempted the use of Form3 printer that has a smaller laser spot size of 85 microns but still failed. As the Mid-Term Progress Report stated, we resorted to lowering the operating frequency to 60 GHz. The journal paper (J4) presented a high-gain dual-circular-polarized (dual-CP) filtering antenna for 60 GH millimeter-wave applications. The dual-CP was achieved by designing a ±45° dual-polarized filtering antenna to illuminate the CP-polarizer-integrated lens. For the Bessel beam launcher in C1, the beam propagates in the axial direction and maintains non-diffractive for a certain distance. To equip the Bessel beam launcher with 2D beam scanning capability, we modified the design in C1 such that the new launcher consists of two identical in-plane rotatable discrete dielectric lenses (DDLs) fed by a pyramid horn operating at 0.3 THz as presented in J1 in Part C. As the total required aperture phase is now equally split between the two thin DDLs. To allow for scanning in the x-direction, we need to add an additional term that has a linear dependence on x in the total aperture phase, which is again equally divided by the two thin DDLs. Through mathematical manipulation, we demonstrated in J1 that the Bessel beam can be scanned in zenith and azimuth angles which depend only on the difference and sum of the physical rotation angles of the two identical DDLs. In other words, one can independently rotate the two DDLs to realize 2-D Bessel beam scanning. When the rotation angle of the top and bottom DDLs is 180°, the additional linear dependence terms in x of the two DDLs cancel each other, and the total aperture phase reduces to that of C1, and the Bessel beam propagates in the axial direction in z. In J1, the beam scanning in both E- and H-planes are demonstrated with the designated in-plane orientations of the two DDLs. A large field of view (FoV) of 86.2° is achieved. This work addressed Objectives 3 and 4. For J2, we reported the design, fabrication, and measurement of a DDL doublet with 3D focus-tunable capability. The in-plane synchronous counter rotation and co-rotation of the DDL doublet can scan its focus radially and azimuthally, respectively, while the linear translation of the upper DDL can move the focus longitudinally. The lower DDL (DDL #1) is capable of transforming the spherical phase front from the feed source into a tilted plane wave phase front. The upper DDL #2 can concentrate the incident plane waves from DDL #1 into a specific focal point. The phase requirement of the upper metalens is optimized using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) scheme at four focus points along the radial direction. This PSO optimization reduces the sidelobe of the beam furthest away from the axial direction by 5 dB. The final measured results demonstrate that the metalens doublet can scan its focus at any position in a cylindrical 3D space with a diameter of about 29mm and length of 8mm at 0.3 THz. The FoV of 72°. This work addressed Objectives 3 and 4. The resolution of our low-cost 3D printer (Form2) is sufficient only for the designs depicted in C1, J1, and J2 operating at 300 GHz. We resorted to a micromachining fabrication process to demonstrate Bessel beam scanning at 1 THz by exploiting the dispersion effect of the pixel element. A multiresonance structure is utilized as the metasurface element to offer additional design freedom, resulting in various phase slope variations. Its broad phase range at all frequencies can facilitate the phase-matching process to improve direction control accuracy and the generated beams' nondiffractive performance. The designed metasurface, composed of 79×79 half-wavelength elements, was illuminated by an LP wave from 0.8 to 1.1 THz. Bessel beams were generated and scanned from 6.4° to 15.2° off normal. We have demonstrated millimeter-wave imaging in which a metasurface antenna can provide focal point scanning in one dimension. A receiver can measure the scattered field from an object under test (OUT). The raw measured electric fields resulted from the superposition of the scattering from the OUT and the ambient environment and the mutual coupling between the transmitting and receiving antennas. A calibration procedure was carried out to eliminate the effects of scattering from the surroundings and mutual coupling for imaging enhancement by substracting the reference data without the OUT from the raw measured data. To further improve the image quality, a compensation model was applied to the collected S21 data. The calculated compensation factors were applied to the collected data in conjunction with the calibration process to enhance the imaging quality. The 2D image is obtained by moving the antenna vertically in the y-direction with a translational stage. Our DDL doublet can perform 2D focus scanning via the counter- and co-rotation of the DDL and since no suitable rotary motors that could hold the two thin DDLs in close proximity were found, we did not demonstrate the 2-D imaging at 300 GHz.

11205819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11205819.value: A beam-steering Bessel beam launcher consisting of two identical thin and lightweight discrete dielectric lenses DDLs is reported in journal paper J1. The quasi-Gaussian beam with a spherical phase front from the feed horn is transformed into a well-collimated and confined pseudo-Bessel beam. The Bessel beam is a nondiffractive and self-healing beam that maintains a relatively stable intensity in the longitudinal direction without wavefront distortion in the transverse direction. It can extend the depth of view and enhance imaging quality. We demonstrated that simultaneous in-plane rotation of the two DDLs in the same (co-rotation) and opposite (counter-rotation) directions can steer the generated Bessel beam in the azimuth and elevation, respectively. The measured results reveal that the launcher can generate 2-D scanning nondiffractive Bessel beam with a large field of view (FoV) of 86.2° and full azimuth coverage. In conference paper C1, we demonstrated the generation of CP Bessel beam by integrating a dielectric grating polarizer with the DDL. In journal paper J2, we modified the DDLs so that the in-plane synchronous counter-rotation and co-rotation could scan its focus radially and azimuthally. We found that the shape of the focused spot was distorted when it moved away from the center. A multi-focus synthesis method that compensates the required transmission phases at multi-focus points has been developed to improve near-field focus performance. The DDL-based antenna can realize 3D focus-scanning using a combination of rotation and linear translation mechanisms. For the latter, the second DDL of the doublet is moving away from the first DDL. The designed 15 mm-diameter antenna prototype can scan its focus in a 3-D cylindrical space with a diameter of 29 mm and a length of 8 mm at 300 GHz. The proposed 3D focus-scanning antenna with a large field of view (FoV) of 72°. We used a micromachining process to fabricate metasurface for Bessel beam steering operating at 1 THz in J3. Illuminated by an LP wave, the metasurface can produce Bessel beams with controllable directions by adjusting frequencies. As a proof-of-concept, a metasurface prototype operating from 0.8 to 1.1 THz achieved beam scanning from 6.4° to 15.2° off normal. Due to the limited resolution of the low-cost 3D printer, we demonstrated dual-CP operation at 60 GHz only. In J4, we demonstrated dual-CP radiation using a single DDL integrated with a dielectric grating polarizer under the illumination of the ±45° dual-polarized antenna source.

11205819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11205819.value: We have perfected our printing method using the low-cost 3D printer from FormLab, allowing us to print lenses for operating at 300 GHz. The 3D printing technology was adopted in a recent paper published in Science Advances in January 2023, “A 6G meta-device for 3D varifocal,” collaborating with Professor Ding Ping Tsai’s research group (doi:10.1126/sciadv.adf8478). Two devices were reported. One is a DDL doublet that generates 2D scanning focus Airy beam on a plane. The other is a DDL triplet that produces a 3D focus Gaussian beam in a cylindrical volume. In J2, we varied the focus plane by increasing the separation between the lenses of the DDL doublet. In the Science Advances paper, a third DDL was added to form a DDL triplet and 3D focusing was achieved by rotation of the DDLs only. As beam scanning is achieved only through rotation of the DDLs without any expensive phase shifters in conventional phased arrays, the research output would have excellent potential for radar applications and satellite communications on the move (SOTM). The key factor is to reduce the antenna profile, namely, the distance between the DDL doublet and the feed horn and the folded transmitarray approach would be most suitable.

11205819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11205819.value: We have demonstrated a focus beam steering approaches operating at 300 GHz or 0.3 THz (terahertz). It can deliver the energy to a pin-pointed location to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio to enhance the quality of service for imaging and communicaitons for future 6th-generation (6G) wireless communications. We first determine the phase distributions required to manipulate the beam radiation mechanism. The phase distributions are realized using the discrete dielectric lens (DDL) approach, in which the height of the dielectric post of each lens pixel determines the phase. To generate a circularly-polarized beam, a dielectric grating is integrated into the DDL and then fabricated using an inexpensive 3D printer through a printing process that we have devised. In addition to the focus beam steering, we have also demonstrated Bessel beam steering. A Bessel beams is nondiffractive and self-healing that it maintains a relatively stable intensity in the beam direction, enhancing imaging quality and depth of view. The elevation and azimuth steering can be achieved by in-plane rotation of two DDLs. For 3D focus beam steering, the focal plane can be controlled by varying the separation of the two DDLs. The field-of-views are 72° and 86.2° for the focus and Bessel beams, respectively.

11206219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206219.value: 隨著環境意識的增強，位於利用單個結構或微電網的一部分的分佈式發電（DG）系統的普及率正在增長，該微電網與主電網並聯或獨立地運行。例如，香港於2018年正式啟動光伏系統和可再生能源證書的上網電價政策計劃。與傳統的集中供電系統相比，DG系統具有許多潛在優勢 - 提供清潔電力，減少碳排放，提高效率，優化資產利用率，提高系統安全性，穩定性，容量，靈活性和可靠性。 典型的DG系統首先將由微源產生的電能轉換成處於調節電壓的DC形式。然後，通過並網逆變器將DC電力轉換為用於電網的AC形式。並網逆變器的功率轉換級包括開關網絡和輸出濾波器。隨著微電子和封裝技術的進步繼續使開關網絡小型化，輸出濾波器的體積成為限制逆變器功率密度的關鍵因素。 通常，輸出濾波器的體積隨著其階數的增加而減小。然而，高階濾波器包含多個電抗元件，因此表現出多個諧振頻率。然後可能出現電抗元件之間的電路諧振。在過去的十年中，已經進行了大量的研究來解決這種共振現象並提高系統性能，但所開發的技術在處理未知的，不可忽視的電網阻抗和系統的非線性負載時仍面臨一些共同的挑戰。不同電網條件下的穩定性此外，有限空間內的熱管理，聲學噪聲和組件之間的電磁耦合對電路設計者提出了挑戰。 該項目旨在研究用功率半導體濾波器（PSF）替換輸出濾波器以控制逆變器輸出電流的新視角。除了消除濾波器諧振之外，還可以減小濾波器部分的物理尺寸。 PSF技術首先用於控制開關轉換器的輸入電流。因此，除了能夠更全面和準確地了解PSF在不同類型的轉換器中的使用之外，該項目還將有助於實現小型化過濾器部分的體積和提高其性能特徵的長期目標。用於DG系統的新型逆變器，由多並聯逆變器組成。

11206219.label: Realisation of objectives
11206219.value: Objective 1: The project was started from applying the concept of power semiconductor filter in a power factor corrector for AC/DC conversion. The power factor corrector is extended from a boost-type structure with power semiconductor filter (PSF). The concept of the PSF is based on using a series pass device (SPD) to profile the input current and regulate the output voltage, and an input capacitor to circulate the ripple current generated by the boost converter. However, the input capacitor is charged up slowly with small input current around the zero crossings, causing high voltage stress on the SPD. Then, a high-voltage device for the SPD is needed. However, high voltage devices have large channel length modulation effect, high leakage current, large voltage drop, and slow response. To accelerate the capacitor charging and thus reduce the voltage stress, this article proposes to replace the output diode with a controllable switch. The converter is temporarily operated as a buck converter during the zero crossings with the input capacitor charged up swiftly by the output capacitor. The voltage across the SPD can be kept low over the line cycle, resulting in improved input current waveform and reduced power dissipation. A series pass module constructed by multiple parallel-connected low-voltage devices is used to increase current rating. The devices are regulated to operate around the knee point of the output characteristics to reduce power loss. A 1 kW, 85–265 Vac/400 Vdc prototype has been built and evaluated. With further extension, the stability issue is studied. In order to avoid input current oscillation, a fixed-frequency dynamic ramp modulator has been proposed. It is based on operating the converter at a fixed switching frequency and setting the switching frequency away from the grid-side resonant frequency. Regardless of the input variation, the voltage across the SPD is also maintained at a low level by a dynamic ramp, resulting in low power dissipation in the SPD. An optimized fast-current regulation circuit is designed to achieve high conducted electromagnetic interference (EMI) suppression. A method to predict the EMI suppression performance of the PSF has been proposed in this article. Furthermore, the ground loop inductance in the fast-current regulation circuit has been analyzed, and PCB layout guidelines have been given to mitigate the performance degradation of the PSF caused by this inductance. A 100-W, 90–264 Vac/200 Vdc buck–boost PFC prototype has been built and evaluated; the prototype with the PSF satisfies EMC standard EE55015 class B in the whole range of 150kHz to 30MHz. A general structure of active bridge rectifier has been studied. It cannot only perform bidirectional power flow, but also EMI suppression. A new linear control scheme for operating power MOSFETs in the third quadrant (i.e., synchronous rectifier (SR) operation) is proposed and applied to electromagnetic interference (EMI) mitigation of switching converters. MOSFETs operating in the third quadrant exhibit electrical characteristics equivalent to a voltage-controlled voltage source between the gate-source and the drain-source voltages. Such operation is an alternative to typical SR mode, allowing fast control of the ac drain-source voltage. It is applied to active bridge rectifiers (ABRs) that can produce the necessary high-frequency voltage compensation signal to reduce differential-mode EMI. The ABR can then play the role of ac line rectification and EMI reduction at the same time. Its characteristics are modeled, and experimental verifications are carried out on a boost-type power factor corrector (PFC). The EMI performance of the PFC is improved with the proposed technique. The proposed technique facilitates the reduction of passive filter size and gives the potential of integrating active filtering function into the ABR as a solid-state front-end module. The idea can, thus, help increase the power density of power converters. Objective 2: The technology has been applied to three-phase systems. The stepwise common-mode (CM) voltage at the output of inverters causes electromagnetic interference (EMI) and damage to motor bearings. This project proposed a new output active CM filter (ACF) to compensate for the steep rising/falling edges of CM voltage for EMI reduction and bearing protection. An input ACF is also necessary to attenuate the CM noise injected into the grid. Hence, a holistic assessment of input and output ACFs for three-phase inverter-fed motor drive systems has been demonstrated. The motor drive system satisfies the CM EMI standard with this new active CM filtering architecture. Ferrite materials and winding configurations of the CM transformer used in the output ACF have been investigated. Moreover, the relationship between the input and output ACFs has been discussed. New perspectives and implementation guidelines for the ACFs in three-phase motor drive systems have been explored.

11206219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206219.value: The project focuses on various aspects of power electronics and proposes innovative solutions to enhance performance and address challenges in different applications. One area of investigation involves the use of power semiconductor filters (PSFs) in power factor correctors (PFCs) to improve efficiency and reduce voltage stress on components. By replacing the output diode with a controllable switch, the capacitor charging process is accelerated, resulting in improved input current waveform and reduced power dissipation. [J1], [P1], [P2]. The stability issue is also addressed by employing a fixed-frequency dynamic ramp modulator and a fast-current regulation circuit, which enhances EMI suppression and mitigates performance degradation caused by ground loop inductance [J2]. Another area of research focuses on active bridge rectifiers (ABRs) that enable bidirectional power flow and EMI suppression. A linear control scheme is proposed for synchronous rectifier (SR) operation, allowing fast control of the AC drain-source voltage and reducing differential-mode EMI. The ABR serves as both an AC line rectifier and an EMI reduction component, leading to potential integration of active filtering functions and increased power density in power converters [J3], [P3], [C1]. Furthermore, the project explores the use of active common-mode filters (ACFs) in inverter-fed motor drive systems to compensate for CM voltage edges, reduce EMI, and protect motor bearings. The investigation includes the selection of ferrite materials, winding configurations, and the relationship between input and output ACFs [J4], [P4]. The project's findings have been disseminated in academic journals and patents have been granted for certain innovations. Overall, the research contributes to the advancement of power electronics, improving efficiency, EMI suppression, and system performance in various applications. References: [J1] C. Tung, J. Fan, J. 11206219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206219.value: The power semiconductor filtering technology, proposed in the project, combines the advantages of switching-mode and linear-mode power conversion techniques. Switching-mode operation is known for its high efficiency, while linear-mode operation offers improved dynamic response, harmonic and electromagnetic performance. Building upon this concept, further research can be done on exploring and investigating different types of power conversion for DC/DC and AC/DC applications. This includes enhancing the conversion efficiency and reducing harmonic distortions and reactive power. These advancements will have a significant impact on applications such as grid-connected systems, industrial power supplies, and consumer electronics. Moreover, as shown in the project results, the power density of the power conversion systems can be enhanced by reducing the size of the passive elements.

11206219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206219.value: As environmental awareness increases, there is growth in the penetration of distributed generation (DG) systems located at the point of utilization for a single structure or a part of a microgrid operating in parallel with, or independently from, the main power grid. Compared to traditional centralized power systems, DG systems have many potential advantages - providing clean power, reducing carbon emissions, improving efficiency, optimizing asset utilization, and improving system safety, stability, capacity, flexibility and reliability. Typical DG systems firstly convert electric energy generated by micro-sources into a DC form at a regulated voltage. Then, the DC power is converted into an AC form for the power grid by a grid-connected inverter. The power conversion stage of the grid-connected inverter consists of a switching network and an output filter. As advances in microelectronics and packaging technology continue to miniaturize the switching network, the volume of the output filter becomes a key factor limiting the power density of the inverter. The project aims to investigate a new perspective of replacing the output filter with a power semiconductor filter (PSF) to control the inverter output current. In addition to eliminating filter resonance, the physical size of the filter section can also be reduced.

11206819.label: Project Objectives
11206819.value: Create an optimized marker gene set in order to maximize the sensitivity of species-level virus composition analysis. Modern sequencing technologies have contributed a large number of strains, especially for fast-mutating viruses. It is not clear to users how to take advantage of this large number of strains to maximize reference-based composition analysis. Most users choose to use commonly seen strains as references, which will lead to biased species-level analysis because viruses of different genotypes/subtypes can differ significantly. We thus proposal to construct the smallest marker gene set possible that fully represents all viral strains, which could not be achieved by using existing marker gene sets such as MetaPhlan [8]. We will develop a novel algorithm that models the marker gene set derivation problem as the vertex cover problem in a gene similarity graph. Develop a read classification method to identify reads of novel viruses or strains. Read mapping against reference sequences is the state-of-the-art strategy for virus identification. However, when a novel virus or strain does not share high identity with the marker genes or reference genomes, read mapping will fail to classify targeted reads. We propose an iterative read classification method by carefully identifying sequence features that distinguish different species. Design new approaches for genome-scale haplotype reconstruction using metagenomic data. Each strain is defined by its haplotype sequence. Knowing all mutations in all genes is important to the phenotype prediction of RNA viruses because of their abundant epistatic interactions. Despite numerous efforts, existing assembly tools still tend to produce fragmented haplotypes. We plan to construct genome-scale haplotypes by incorporating key features of viral quasispecies into a novel expectation-maximization algorithm.

11206819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11206819.value: Pathogenic RNA viruses, such as HIV and HCV, still claim millions of lives each year despite intensive research. It is estimated that billions of viral particles of fast replicating viruses can be generated each day in chronically infected patients. Due to the high mutation rate of RNA viruses, these viral particles can contain an unknown number of different strains. If some of the strains possess resistance to anti-viral drugs, the treatment will fail. Therefore, inferring all different strains within a viral population can provide indispensable knowledge for preventing and treating viral diseases. In contrast to the methods that sequence only targeted viruses, metagenomic sequencing is able to sequence all viruses in a sample, including novel ones. The focus of this research plan is to develop much-needed approaches for deriving all strains in viral populations of both known and novel viruses using metagenomic data. To our best knowledge, there lack such high-resolution metagenomic analysis tools optimized for RNA viruses. Toward this goal, we must tackle the following challenges. First, novel viruses or divergent strains of a known virus family may only share low conservation with reference sequences, making widely used reference-based virus detection tools miss a large number of reads from novel viruses or strains. Second, despite promising results on gene-wise or local strain recovery, genome-scale reconstruction of viral strains is still difficult because of the high sequence identity between strains within the population. Based on our 10+ years of experience in sequence analysis and our deep understanding of the viral population properties through our preliminary work on viral strain assembly, we propose three objectives to address these challenges. 1) Build the smallest possible marker gene set for RNA viruses in order to maximize the sensitivity of species-level virus composition analysis. We propose a novel formulation that models marker gene derivation as the vertex cover problem in a gene similarity graph. 2) Develop highly scalable read classification methods to identify reads from novel viruses or strains. 3) Infer the number of strains, their relative abundance, and genomes inside each viral population by developing a novel EM algorithm that integrates strains’ global similarity and different abundance. The tools are expected to reveal new strains and viruses that could not be identified by existing tools. As novel viruses usually emerge in densely populated regions with high biodiversity such as Hong Kong, our research outcome is needed to better prepare us for future viral outbreaks.

11206819.label: Realisation of objectives
11206819.value: The research project has three objectives, which are summarized below. We have achieved the targeted performance for the three objectives. Obj. 1: construct optimized marker gene sets for RNA viruses Obj. 2: classifying reads from novel viruses or strains Obj. 3: Genome-scale haplotype reconstruction In Obj. 1, we have constructed a marker gene set based on RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) genes, which are responsible for replicating the genome and performing transcription in RNA viruses. RdRp gene exists in almost all RNA viruses, except retroviruses, such as human immunodeficiency viruses (HIV). Besides the marker gene, we also constructed other gene sets that can be used to distinguish viruses from other organisms. We created 1384 gene sets that can be used to identify RNA viruses. By using our own gene sets, we can confidently identify all RNA viruses. In addition, we conducted a very comprehensive comparison of available RNA viral gene sets for RNA virus identification. To decide the best usage of these gene sets, we align them to RNA viruses and other organisms. If a gene set can incur better scores in RNA viruses than other species, we will record the lowest match score against an RNA virus as “pos”. Similarly, the highest score against a non-RNA virus is recorded as “neg”. Then, we design the adaptive cutoff as [neg + (pos − neg) ∗ h], where h is a default value of 0.1. We conducted multiple experiments to test the utility of these gene sets. Exp 1: Simulated metagenomic data. We first evaluated the marker sets on two semi-synthetic marine metagenomic samples (NCBI SRA ID: ERR1992810 and ERR2185279) constructed from 82 eukaryotes, 365 prokaryotes and DNA/RNA viruses (Mitchell et al., 2019). They showed the highest precision and F1 scores in these samples. Exp 2: Real metagenomic data. We tested the marker sets on 21 human clinical samples for pathogen detection. They successfully retrieved all the reported RNA viral pathogens and achieved an average recall of 99.3% and precision of 99.2% among different groups. Obj. 2. To recruit reads from novel viruses or strains, we used iterative search method to identify reads with decreasing similarity with the reference. Using the identified RdRp marker genes from Obj. 1 as the reference, we can recruit reads from remotely related viruses. Our expectation is that this method can achieve higher recall than available tools, such as Bowtie. To test this method, we used three types of data. First, we evaluated Obj.2 on simulated RNA viral sequencing data, which contains reads sampled from viruses in different orders. For the simulated data with known ground truth, we focus on testing three main factors that can affect the performance of read classification. They are the similarity between the marker genes and the test set, the size ratio of the markers to the test set, and the sequencing coverage of samples in test set. Then, we tested the method on a simulated viral marine metagenomic dataset that contains eukaryote, prokaryote, RNA viruses, and DNA viruses from the marine ecosystem. Although there are publicly available mock metagenomic datasets, they mainly contain bacteria and thus cannot be conveniently applied to our test. We thus constructed the simulated metagenomic data by including many non-RNA virus reads from a comprehensive marine genome survey Finally, we tested the method on a real metagenomic data. For all the experiments, we benchmarked our method against several popular and extensively tested read-level taxonomic classification tools that can be applied to RNA viruses, including DIAMOND, MMseqs2, Kaiju, and Kraken2. The results show that similarity plays an important role on the classification performance. The tools that rely on exact match, including Kaiju and Kraken2, have the average F-score reduction of 72.7% and 80.1%, respectively, when the similarity decreases from 0.6 to 0.4. In contrast, when the similarity is 0.4, our method still has a high F-score. In addition, its average F-score is 12.8% higher than that of the second-best tool DIAMOND BLASTX. To focus on the difficult case where the test set has diverged from the reference sequences, we removed the reference viruses that have similarity with the test set above 40%. We aligned marker genes from 16 RNA viruses to the dataset by DIAMOND BLASTP and removed all reference sequences with similarity greater than 0.4. Finally, the number of reference genes under Bunyavirales, Mononegavirales, and Picornavirales are 34, 40, and 60, respectively. The performance of Kaiju and Kraken is not good under the default parameters. Although the precision of Kaiju is 1, its recall is only about 0.007. And Kraken2 doesn't identify any reads in the test set. DIAMOND BLASTX and MMseqs2 are both alignment-based tools. Although MMseqs2 has lower precision, it has a higher recall (0.251) than DIAMOND BLASTX (0.218), leading to a slightly better F-score. Using PRC can increase the recall to 0.464 while keeping the precision at 0.997, compared with BLASTX. Our method can further improve the recall to 0.849. Obj. 3. In this objective, our goal is to develop a more accurate haplotype reconstruction tool than the state-of-the-art tools. To evaluate this, we tested our method on both simulated and real viral sequencing datasets. In experiments on the simulated data, we focused on testing the tool on reconstructing multiple haplotypes with different similarity and abundance distributions. First, we conducted (I) multiple-haplotype experiments using simulated sequencing data for HIV. Then, we tested the tool on (II) simulated data containing 5 HIV haplotypes. Following that, we evaluated the performance of the tool on (III) simulated datasets with different sequencing error rates. Then, we investigated (IV) the limits of our method on minimum diversity and abundance of haplotypes. In addition, we evaluated the (V) influence of using different reference genomes on its performance. For experiments on real viral sequencing datasets, we tested our tool on viral population sequencing data with known haplotype compositions, including a 5-haplotype HIV dataset and a 2-haplotype HBV dataset. We evaluated different tools using seven metrics following previous publications, which quantify the completeness of the reconstructed haplotypes, their quality, and their abundance distributions. Each contig is aligned to a reference genome based on the best alignment from samtools. First, we will report the number of contigs and N50. In order to measure the completeness, we compute the “target genome coverage”, which is the average percentage of reference genomes that have the same bases as the aligned contigs. To evaluate the quality of contigs, we compute the average error rate (the sum of indel rate and mismatch rate) of alignments between the contigs and their closest target genomes/haplotypes. Besides, we compute Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), a commonly used metric to measure the similarity between the estimated haplotypes’ abundance distribution and the ground truth. Our method achieved the best overall performance on these metrics. For example, when we tested the method on HIV quasispecies dataset that contains 5 haplotypes, it returns 6 contigs, which is the closest to the known haplotypes. In addition, it achieved the highest genome coverage (over 80%), the lowest error rate, and the highest completeness. On the 2-haplotype HBV dataset, it correctly recovered two haplotypes with near 100% genome coverage.

Develop a read classification method to identify reads of novel viruses or strains. Read mapping against reference sequences is the state-of-the-art strategy for virus identification. However, when a novel virus or strain does not share high identity with the marker genes or reference genomes, read mapping will fail to classify targeted reads. We propose an iterative read classification method by carefully identifying sequence features that distinguish different species.

Design new approaches for genome-scale haplotype reconstruction using metagenomic data. Each strain is defined by its haplotype sequence. Knowing all mutations in all genes is important to the phenotype prediction of RNA viruses because of their abundant epistatic interactions. Despite numerous efforts, existing assembly tools still tend to produce fragmented haplotypes. We plan to construct genome-scale haplotypes by incorporating key features of viral quasispecies into a novel expectation-maximization algorithm.

11206819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11206819.value: RNA viruses have high diversity. We constructed multiple marker gene sets to improve the tradeoff between recall and precision of virus read classification. With the carefully designed marker gene sets and the adaptive score cutoff, we can identify novel viruses (with F-score above 0.8) that share low similarity with known viruses (such as 0.4). The maker gene sets and the read classification method description can be found in the following publications. 1. VirBot: an RNA viral contig detector for metagenomic data. Bioinformatics, 39(3):btad093, Mar 1 2023. (IF: 5.8. Rank: 8/77 in Biochemical Research Methods) 2. "RdRp-based sensitive taxonomic classification of RNA viruses for metagenomic data", Briefings in Bioinformatics, 23(2):bbac011, Feb. 7th, 2022 (IF: 13.994. Rank: 2/58 in Mathematical & Computational Biology) 3. "CHEER: HierarCHical taxonomic classification for viral mEtagEnomic data via deep leaRning", Methods, 189: 95-103, May, 2021. (IF: 3.608. Rank: 27/77 in Biochemical Research Methods) 4. “Utilizing profile HMM databases for discovering viruses from metagenomic data: a comprehensive review”, accepted by Briefings in Bioinformatics In paper [4], we compared viral genes in available databases and provides some insights that are helpful to the community of virology. First, users should take great caution in using the current public viral marker gene databases. Although these databases are built using viral proteins, this does not guarantee that they won't be aligned to non-viral proteins. Our analysis shows that many of these hallmark genes can incur statistically significant alignments against non-viral proteins. Thus, using model-specific cutoff can help reduce FP. Second, it is worth noting that the marker gene sets can change with the continuous identification of new viruses. These new viruses can enlarge the viral gene catalogue and the boundary between viral proteins and non-viral proteins. Our marker gene set identification method in Obj. 1 can be conveniently extended to include new viral proteins. In addition, the tool in Obj. 2 can be used to identify new viruses and thus leads to identification of new viral proteins. The haplotype reconstruction performance heavily depends on the virus type, the mutation rate, and the number of haplotypes in the quasispecies. Overall, if the haplotypes in quasispecies only differ by a handful of mutations, it becomes difficult to reconstruct all the haplotypes. Our haplotype reconstruction tool still outperforms other benchmarked tools. Specifically, our method can recover the largest number of correct haplotypes with high completeness. The outcome is listed in Part C.

11206819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11206819.value: With the fast development of AI models, especially various foundation models that are built on Transformer, further development of new virus identification and quasispecies identification can benefit from using these foundation models. An increasing number of foundation models that are built on DNAs or proteins of various organisms have been developed by various groups who have access to large computing resources. These models can be finetuned for viruses so that novel viruses can be recognized from sequencing data. As these foundation models are trained on a large number of organisms including some viruses, they are expected to learn better features that can distinguish viruses from others. The finetune step needs virus-related data as the training set. The marker gene sets developed in Obj. 1 can be used as training data. An alternative method is to use all viral genomes as training set. Then we can formulate this as a binary classification problem where the viruses and non-viruses are the positive and negative sets, respectively.

11206819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11206819.value: RNA viruses, such as HIV and HCV, continue to pose significant health challenges worldwide. These viruses can rapidly mutate, giving rise to numerous strains within a single patient, some of which may be resistant to treatment. To effectively combat these viruses, it is crucial to identify and understand all the strains present in a viral population. Our research aims to develop cutting-edge tools that can analyze metagenomic data to uncover both known and novel viral strains. By creating a minimal set of marker genes specific to RNA viruses, we can improve the sensitivity of virus detection. Additionally, we will develop highly efficient methods to classify reads from novel viruses or strains and reconstruct their genomes. Through this research, we expect to uncover previously unidentified strains and viruses, providing valuable insights into viral diversity. As Hong Kong is a hotspot for novel virus emergence, our findings will contribute to better preparedness against future viral outbreaks.

11207419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207419.value: Effective stimulation strategies are key to achieving successful neural implants for the treatment of neurological disorders, such as Parkinson’s disease, dystonia, chronic pain, and loss of vision and hearing. In recent decades, bionic vision systems have been developed for use as a substitute for natural vision in blind patients suffered from the loss of photoreceptors. Electrical pulses are applied to the retina or the cerebral cortex to restore partial vision to implant recipients. The current stimulation strategy used in visual implant is a regular, periodic pulse train, which is far from natural frequency dynamics. Studies have shown enhanced responses to temporal irregularity across tactile, auditory and visual modalities, in both animals and humans. Natural spiking patterns in the retina and cortex are highly irregular and characterized by their temporal variations. Introducing irregularities in the patterns that are used to activate retinal or cortical neurons may well enhance the efficacy of electrically-evoked cortical responses. However this approach has thus far been investigated only sparsely. We already investigated the effect of regular retinal stimulation on the spatial interactions of neurons in the visual cortex. This research received support allocated from the General Research fund for 2011/12 (CityU123412). Our results indicate that it will be essential to study the efficacy of irregular electrical stimulation in vivo, an approach which has not been pursued so far. Therefore we propose an investigation of the cortical activity at threshold currents, the spatially activated areas and the retino-cortical information transmission in live rats in response to irregular retinal stimulation. Retinal prosthesis currently uses regular, periodic pulse trains, which is far from any natural frequency dynamics. To date, no systematic study of primary visual cortical responses to irregular, aperiodic electrical stimuli in normal sighted rats or rats with retinal degeneration has been reported. This study will elucidate the efficacy of visual cortical responses to irregular temporal stimulus patterns in both normal sighted rats and rats with retinal degeneration. We will also examine the effects of spike train irregularity on excitatory and inhibitory neurons in both healthy and unhealthy rat visual cortices. Studying the interactions between irregular stimuli and excitatory as well as inhibitory networks in the visual cortex will help decipher the mechanisms underpinning brain plasticity in response to electrical stimulation. By addressing key challenges in human visual prosthetics, particularly desensitization to repetitive stimulation, this stimulation strategy could pave the way to high-resolution retinal prosthesis for long-term implantation. 有效的刺激策略是成功实现神经植入物治疗神经系统疾病的关键，例如帕金森病，肌张力障碍，慢性疼痛以及视力和听力丧失等神经系统疾病。近几十年来，业界相继研发出仿生视觉系统用于替代因为光感受细胞损失致盲患者的自然视力。其神经植入体工作的大致原理为将规则的周期性电脉冲序列施加到视网膜或大脑皮层以恢复植入受体的部分视力。研究表明，在动物和人类的触觉，听觉和视觉模式中，对不规则时序的反应有所增强。视网膜和皮层中的自然尖峰模式是高度不规则的并且以其时间变化为特征。在用于激活视网膜或皮质神经元的模式中引入不规则性可以很好地增强皮层电诱发反应的响应。然而，到目前为止这种方法未能被深入的研究。我们的团队已经研究了常规视网膜刺激对视皮层神经元空间相互作用的影响。该研究得到了2011/12年度综合研究基金的支持（CityU123412）。我们的结果表明，研究在体不规则电刺激的功效至关重要，而这种研究迄今尚未深入开展。因此，我们提议探索活体大鼠皮层对于不规则视网膜刺激活动的阈值电流，空间激活区域和视网膜皮质信息传递等响应情况。当前视网膜假体使用的是规则的周期性脉冲序列，其远离任何固有的频率动态。迄今为止，尚未有对正常视力大鼠或视网膜变性大鼠的不规则非周期性电刺激的初级视觉皮层响应的系统研究。本研究将揭示对正常视力大鼠和视网膜变性大鼠施加不规则时间刺激模式其初级视觉皮层的反应。我们还将研究不规则尖峰序列对健康和非健康大鼠视觉皮层中兴奋性和抑制性神经元的影响。研究不规则刺激与视觉皮层中的兴奋性和抑制性网络之间的相互作用将有助于破译支持大脑可塑性的机制以响应电刺激。通过解决人类视觉修复术中的关键挑战，尤其是针对重复刺激的脱敏现象这一重大挑战。得到的相应刺激策略可以为高分辨率视网膜假体长期植入铺平道路。

11207419.label: Realisation of objectives
11207419.value: Summary – The two objectives have been achieved successfully. In the following sections, methodologies and results will be reported. We characterized the temporal precision of the cortical neuronal response to the repeated electrical retinal stimulation with periodic and aperiodic temporal structures. We investigated stimulation frequencies and different irregular stimulation patterns for the stimulation types. Methodology Animals This work used six SD rats (age: P80-P100) and seven retinal degenerated S334ter-line-3 (F1) rats (age: P80-P120). The F1 rats were obtained from the Rat Resource & Research Center. The rats were fed and watered ad libitum under 12 h light-dark cycle conditions. All experimental procedures were approved by the Animal Subjects Ethics Sub-Committees of the City University of Hong Kong and the Health Department of the Hong Kong SAR (Ref No.: (22-129) in DH/HT&A/8/2/5 Pt.9). The Ketamine-Xylazine (K-X) mixture (Ketamine: 30 mg/kg, and Xylazine: 15 mg/kg; Alfasan International B.V., Holland) was used for rat anesthetization with intraperitoneal injection; the maintenance of anesthetization was kept by intramuscular injection with 0.1 mL K-X combination hourly during the whole experiment. The animals' body temperature was monitored during the entire experiment and maintained at around 37.5°C by a heating pad (Model # TP702; Gamry Industries, Inc., NY, USA). Epiretinal Electrode Insertion After anesthesia, the rat’s eye was proptosed using a rubber membrane with a small hole. Two drops of tropicamide (1.0%, Alcon, Switzerland) and proparacaine hydrochloride (0.5%, Alcon-Couvreur, Belgium) were applied to the right eye for pupil dilation and local anesthesia, respectively. The stimulating bipolar concentric electrode (FHC Inc., Bowdoin, ME, USA) was inserted through the incision site behind the limbus made by a needle. The electrode was finally positioned close to the ventral-temporal retina near the optic nerve using the articulating arm holder (Noga, Noga Engineering Ltd., Israel) with calipers. Aperiodic Electrical Stimulation A stimulus generator (STG 4004, Multichannel Systems MCS GmBH, Germany) generated the cathodic-first, symmetric, biphasic current pulse with 200 μA amplitude and 1 ms phase duration without inter-phase interval. The stimulation frequency applied to the retina was 5, 10, and 20 Hz. This study applied two forms of stimulation train: (1) the periodic train and (2) the aperiodic train, cataloged by inter-pulse interval (IPI) sequence. The definition of IPI was the interval between the initiation time of two consecutive pulses. The periodic train was composed of pulses with a uniform IPI. Give 5 Hz as an instance, all the ten IPIs in the train were 200 ms equally. Differently, the IPIs in the irregular train were mixed. Furthermore, aperiodic stimulation contained two patterns: noise pattern and Poisson pattern. In the noise pattern, the train contained several specific percentages (called noise level) of shorter and longer IPIs than the mean IPI. The IPIs in the Poisson patterns’ train followed the Poisson distribution. Recording Electrode Implantation A craniotomy was conducted at the occipital lobe, approximately 2-5 mm lateral to the midline and 4.5-7.5 mm posterior to the bregma, to access the visual cortex on the side opposite the stimulated eye. After the removal of the skull piece, the dura was gently removed using a bent 30-gauge needle. A 6-channel electrode array (Clunbury Scientific LLC., Bloomfield Hills, USA) with 400 μm inter-electrode space following 2×3 distribution was inserted into V1 at around 1000 μm depth contralateral to the stimulated eye with a microdrive inserter (Micropositioner, David Kopf Instruments, Tujunga, USA). Electrophysiology The neuronal responses in V1 were recorded using a data acquisition system (Micro1401, CED, United Kingdom) at a 5 kHz sampling frequency. Spike2 (CED, United Kingdom) was used to record signal at 0.3-3 kHz band-passed filter with a gain of 1k. MATLAB was used for offline data processing and analysis. The threshold for spike detection was set as 3.5× to 50× of the noise's root mean square (RMS). The most activated channel was used for further analysis, which was selected by determining the channel with the maximum spike counts among all six channels. Two-way ANOVA and post hoc tests were used for statistical analysis. Descriptive statistics (mean±S.E.M) were provided. Results 1. Characterize the responses of visual cortical neurons of rats to trains of repeated events (electrical stimulation) with a periodic temporal structure and a non-periodic temporal The study applied aperiodic stimulation with 'repeated' noise conditions to examine the time precision of cortical responses across trials. The spikes in response to each stimulus pulse were counted in a time window of 30 ms post-stimulus and then averaged over 10 trials. Consequently, larger spike counts evoked by each stimulus pulse implied a high temporal consistency. At 5 Hz and 10 Hz, the response to aperiodic stimulation was generally higher than the periodic stimulation in both SD and F1 rats. As the frequency increased to 20 Hz, the time precision of the response elicited by irregular stimulation with 50% noise was pronouncedly higher than that evoked by periodic stimulation in normal rats and retina-degenerated rats. Additionally, in SD rats, the Poisson stimulation also increased the time precision of the spike activity compared to the periodic stimulation at 20 Hz. Specifically, the spike elicited by the first pulse was greater than that elicited by the following pulses, implying that regular stimulation reduced the temporal precision of response with repeated stimulation. The introduction of the aperiodic pattern improved the temporal precision. 2. Examine the effect of irregular stimuli on visual cortical responses, assessed through the amount of information transferred To explore the effect of irregular stimulation on visual cortical responses, the power spectrum of local field potential (LFP) was calculated to assess the amount of information transferred. The spectrum of responses elicited by periodic stimulation decreased sharply with the frequency band increased compared to that evoked by irregular stimulation at all frequencies. Additionally, the response to aperiodic stimulation following Poisson distribution generally showed the highest spectrum, except for the 20 Hz stimulation in the SD group. Specifically, the mean spectrum of the response to 50% noise stimulation was higher than that evoked by Poisson stimulation at 20 Hz in the SD group, which also showed a large standard error mean. Besides, a noticeable negative peak at 50 Hz resulted from the power-line noise filter. These results indicated that aperiodic stimulation could increase the efficacy of the information transferred regarding the LFP band in both the SD and F1 groups. The Poisson stimulation was the most efficient in information transfer.

11207419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207419.value: In the presented study, S334ter-line-3 (F1) rats were used as the retinal degenerated animal models for human retina degeneration diseases. Pt/Ir bipolar concentric electrode of inner diameter 75 μm and impedance around 8 kΩ in vivo was used as the stimulating electrode to stimulate the epiretinal surface. Subsequently, a 2×3 electrode array was employed to record electrical evoked neural signals from the primary visual cortex (V1) regions in the left hemispheres of the brain, which is contralateral to the stimulated eye. In summary, the following conclusions are suggested from all the results reported in the aforementioned experiments of the present study. Firstly, the irregular stimulation pattern can improve the desensitization of the visual cortical neurons in response to repeated retinal stimulation. Secondly, the irregular stimulation showed higher efficacy in information transferred regarding the LFP signal band than the regular stimulation. These findings suggest a possible stimulation strategy to improve the performance of the retinal prosthesis. Overall, we have completed all objectives of this study and published in one journal paper (IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering), one international conference (the 43rd Annual International Conferences of the IEEE Eng Med Biol Soc), and orally presented in one conference meeting (the 12th The Eye and the Chip World Research Congress), as listed in Part C.

11207419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207419.value: There are some limitations in the present study, so we suggested some possible directions for future work below. To investigate the effect of the aperiodic stimulation on the cortical responses, this study explored the temporal features of the neuronal responses in V1. At the same time, the spatial characteristics in V1 are also important in improving the performance of the retina implants. To further understand the efficacy of aperiodic stimulation, we plan to explore the spatial feature of the responses elicited by the aperiodic stimulation. Furthermore, it will be interesting to explore the spatial distribution using a recording array with more channels instead of the 2×3 array used in this work, which offers a larger area and higher spatial resolution of the recorded signal. An alternative to the single stimulating electrode used in this work, a flexible microelectrode array (MEA) can also provide multi-channel stimulation. In this regard, the cortical activation map could be studied by applying current stimuli via different channels or activating several channels simultaneously.

11207419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207419.value: The bionic vision systems aim to restore partial vision in blind patients using electrical pulses on the retina or cerebral cortex. However, the current stimulation strategy used in visual implants is a regular, periodic pulse train, which is unnatural. Studies have shown that irregular stimulation patterns can more effectively activate neurons in the retina and cortex. These irregular patterns mimic the natural spiking patterns found in these areas and can potentially enhance the efficacy of electrically evoked responses. However, this approach has not been extensively studied. In this study, researchers used rats with retinal degeneration as models for human retinal diseases. They used a specific electrode to stimulate the retina and recorded neural signals from the primary visual cortex. The results showed that the irregular stimulation pattern improved the response of visual cortical neurons to repeated retinal stimulation and was more effective in transmitting information than regular stimulation. These findings suggest that using irregular stimulation patterns could be a promising strategy to improve the performance of retinal prostheses, providing hope for better vision restoration in blind patients.

11207519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11207519.value: 熱帶氣旋風特性以及極端風對香港超高層建築風效應研究

11207519.label: Co - Investigator(s)
11207519.value: Prof Duan, Zhongdong Dr He, Yuncheng Prof Li, Shuaicheng

11207519.label: Project Objectives
11207519.value: Observational study of TC structures and wind characteristics To date, most studies of TC winds have merely focused on a shallow range of TC depth, so investigations of TC wind characteristics and structural features within the entire depth of TCs are therefore required. In particular, reliable observations of TCs over land with respect to the design of high-rise structures are still lacking. The Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) has established over 50 weather stations to provide systematic monitoring of the climate. A wide range of measurement instruments are used, including GPS dropsonde, radiosonde balloons, Lidar, Sodar, and Doppler wind profilers, and numerous anemometers on meteorological masts and buoys, which can provide a full range of observations of various weather elements during TCs. Based on long-term (20 years) observation records of TCs in Hong Kong from various types of meteorological instruments, extensive studies of TC structures and wind fields in a vertical scope covering the entire TC depth will be conducted through both case study and composite analysis. The dependency of TC structural characteristics on terrain condition, radial distance, TC intensity, and environmental factors will be identified. The vertical variability of atmospheric temperature and pressure, relative humidity, and horizontal wind will be quantified. Vertical TC wind profiles will be investigated as a function of TC intensity, wind strength, terrain condition, and storm-relative position. The low-level jet (LLJ) feature in TC wind profiles will be quantitatively defined. In addition, the derived typical TC wind profiles will be compared with those obtained from monsoons and thunderstorms, to identify the special features of TCs. Modeling of TC spatial pressure/wind fields There are lack of reliable 3-D wind field models in wind engineering. A height-resolving model will thus be developed based on the long-term observation records, to describe the spatial pressure fields of TCs below the outflow layer. This model will take into account the dependency of the TC pressure field on both radial and vertical positions. The proposed TC pressure field model will be further applied in conjunction with a wind field model, to establish a refined height-resolving TC wind field model (3-D). The outward tilting feature of the radius of maximum wind (RMW) will be integrated, and different models of turbulence viscosity will be used and their effects on TC spatial wind field modeling assessed. Establishing vertical profiles of TC-dominated design wind speeds Except the Australian loading code, which incorporates special provisions for wind profiles for TC regions, there is no other code or standard involving such items. Statistical analysis will be conducted to establish the statistical models of TC activities in the western North Pacific Basin, based on over 60 years of records. Monte Carlo simulation techniques will then be utilized in conjunction with the statistical models to simulate the thousands of TCs that affect the southeast coast of China. The wind field of each of these simulated TCs above Hong Kong and other selected coastal cities will be generated via the proposed height-resolving TC wind field model. The TC-dominated design wind speeds with respect to different return periods will be determined and demonstrated in the form of vertical profiles. Assessment of TC-induced effects on super-tall buildings Evaluation of structural performance of super-tall buildings excited by extreme winds will provide valuable information for the design of future skyscrapers with increasing height. TC-induced wind effects on two super-tall buildings will be investigated through field measurements and wind tunnel tests. Comprehensive structural health monitoring systems will monitor the wind effects on the skyscrapers during TCs. Realistic wind fields with typical features of TCs (e.g., LLJ, veering wind, and profiles of TC winds) will be simulated in the wind tunnel tests. Field measurements of cladding pressures and structural responses will be compared with those from the model tests, to evaluate the applicability and accuracy of different experimental techniques in estimating the wind effects on high-rise buildings during TCs.

11207519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11207519.value: 熱帶氣旋可能導致極具破壞性的自然災害，而有效預防和減少熱帶氣旋引發的災害需要深入而廣泛的熱帶氣旋相關知識。然而，前人對熱帶氣旋風場的觀測主要是在較低的高度範圍內進行的，目前高層建築設計所需的陸地上熱帶氣旋的可靠觀測數據非常有限，並且仍缺乏可用於災害風險評估的高度分辨熱帶氣旋壓力場和風場模型。因此，有必要對熱帶氣旋整個高度範圍內的風特性和結構特徵進行探索，並以此為基礎改進當前的熱帶氣旋風場模型。香港位於熱帶氣旋多發地區，境內已建立了50多個氣象站來進行各種氣象參數的長期觀測。觀測的儀器包括飛機投擲的下投式探空儀，無線電探空氣球，多普勒雷達，聲雷達，激光雷達，氣象桅杆、海上氣象平台和浮標上配備的風速計等。這些儀器的長期觀測記錄為研究不同地形條件下熱帶氣旋的風特性提供了一個獨特而寶貴的數據平台。 本項目旨在對熱帶氣旋的風特性以及熱帶氣旋極端風對香港超高層建築的風效應進行全面的研究調查，研究主要包括四個任務：（1）對熱帶氣旋整個高度範圍內的風特性和結構特徵進行觀察研究； （2）建立熱帶氣旋流出層以下壓力和風場的空間分佈模型; （3）建立熱帶氣旋設計風速的垂直風剖面; （4）評估熱帶氣旋對超高層建築的風效應。任務1將基於香港境內超過20年的多種類實測數據進行。通過個例研究和復合分析，研究熱帶氣旋整個高度範圍內的風場特性及熱力學和動力學特徵，建立熱帶氣旋風速、風向、大氣壓力、溫度和相對濕度的垂直剖面關於氣旋相對位置、強度、地形條件和其他環境影響參數的函數。任務2首先將實測總結的熱帶氣旋垂直剖面與徑向模型耦合，構建高度分辨熱帶氣旋壓力場模型。然後，將該模型與熱帶氣旋風場模型耦合，構建新的三維熱帶氣旋風場模型。該模型將考慮最大風速半徑的向外傾斜特徵和水平渦粘度的垂直變化，並能夠重現熱帶氣旋風廓線的低空急流特徵及其與徑向位置的相關性。任務3和4將側重於風工程實踐中的兩個關鍵問題。首先，將使用蒙特卡羅方法和新提出的三維熱帶氣旋風場模型，建立香港不同回歸期下熱帶氣旋設計風速的垂直剖面。然後，在熱帶氣旋期間對兩棟超高層建築的風效應進行實測，以評估熱帶氣旋對超高層建築的風效應。並對這兩棟建築物的剛性模型和氣動彈性模型分別進行風洞試驗，試驗將模擬真實的熱帶氣旋風場特徵，包括低空急流，轉向風，風剖面等。試驗結果將進一步與實測結果進行比較，以評估不同模型試驗技術在評估熱帶氣旋對高層建築的風效應方面的適用性和準確性。 該項目的目的是對熱帶氣旋的風特性和結構特徵進行探究，從而建立新的三維熱帶氣旋風場模型，為熱帶氣旋多發地區超高層建築的抗風設計提供參考，並驗證風洞試驗技術。

11207519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11207519.value: Based on long-term (20-years) observation records of tropical cyclones (TCs) in Hong Kong from various types of meteorological instruments, extensive studies of TC structures and wind fields in a vertical scope covering the entire TC depth were conducted through both case study and composite analysis. The dependency of TC structural characteristics on terrain condition, radial distance, TC intensity, and environmental factors was identified. The vertical variability of atmospheric temperature and pressure, relative humidity, and horizontal wind were quantified. Vertical TC wind profiles were investigated as a function of TC intensity, wind strength, terrain condition, and storm-relative position. The low-level jet (LLJ) feature in TC wind profiles was quantitatively defined. In addition, the derived typical TC wind profiles were compared with those obtained from monsoons and thunderstorms, to identify the special features of TCs. A height-resolving model was developed based on the long-term observation records, to describe the spatial pressure fields of TCs below the outflow layer. This model was applied in conjunction with a wind field model, to establish a refined height-resolving TC wind field model (3-D). The outward tilting feature of the radius of maximum wind (RMW) was integrated, and different models of turbulence viscosity were used and their effects on TC spatial wind field modeling were assessed. Statistical analysis was conducted to establish the statistical models of TC activities in the western North Pacific Basin, based on over 60 years of records. Monte Carlo simulation techniques were then utilized in conjunction with the statistical models to simulate the thousands of TCs that affect the southeast coast of China. Based on the model, the TC-dominated design wind speeds with respect to different return periods were determined and demonstrated in the form of vertical profiles. TC-induced wind effects on two super-tall buildings were investigated through field measurements and wind tunnel tests. Comprehensive structural health monitoring systems monitored the wind effects on the skyscrapers during TCs. Realistic wind fields with typical features of TCs (e.g., LLJ, veering wind, and profiles of TC winds) were simulated in the wind tunnel tests. Field measurements of cladding pressures and structural responses were compared with those from the model tests.

11207519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11207519.value: In the future, artificial intelligence can be utilized for the investigation of tropical cyclone wind characteristics and the effects of extreme winds on super-tall buildings, aiding in the development of more accurate wind field models and the assessment of wind effects on high-rise structures. Moreover, new data measurement techniques can be developed, and additional observation stations can be established to support subsequent research.

11207519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11207519.value: This project focuses on understanding the wind characteristics of tropical cyclones and how extreme winds impact super-tall buildings. By observing these extreme windstorms and subsequent analysis of the records, this project aims to develop accurate models to predict wind structure and characteristics, which is crucial for the design and safety of high-rise structures. The significance of this work lies in its potential to enhance building resilience against extreme weather conditions, thereby protecting lives and reducing economic losses.

11208119.value: 建立相对竞争与合作的动态疏散行为模型
