11208119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11208119.value: In performance-based study of fire engineering, the determination of the required-safe-egress-time (RSET) is critical to the safety of a fire scenario. Numerical modelling of evacuees’ movements provides an estimate of the required movement time, which is a major component of the RSET. Researchers have reported that the detailed interactions between evacuees are critical and greatly affect the overall evacuation pattern and time. Therefore, in-depth investigation of human behaviours and the interactions between evacuees during evacuation is necessary. In the pioneering studies of evacuation modelling, the behaviours of the evacuees (either competitive or cooperative) were predefined prior to the simulation. Heuristic interaction rules were applied based on their predefined behaviours. However, psychologists have reported that evacuations in practice can never be purely competitive or cooperative. Also, the behaviour of an evacuee can dynamically change according to his/her situation (e.g. near a fire source or exit) and his/her relationship to neighbouring evacuees (e.g. family, friends or strangers), etc. Psychologists have also found that evacuees’ behaviour is relative in nature. Evacuee A may be cooperative towards B because they are members of the same group, but competitive towards C because they are members of different groups. Also, we can envisage that these relative behaviours between two evacuees are not necessarily the same in the opposite direction. For example, evacuee A may behave cooperatively towards B because they are members of the same group. However, evacuee B may behave less cooperatively or even competitively towards A because B is exposed to hazard (e.g. excessive heat radiation from fire). This relative competitive-cooperative (c-c) behaviour was not addressed in previous models but has been found to exist in actual situations and is in fact among the major components governing the interactions between the evacuees. This proposed study will develop a c-c behavioural model according to the relevant psychological theories. A c-c matrix will be developed to represent the c-c behaviours between any two evacuees within their influence radii. The matrix will be translated to virtual forces between the evacuees. The forces will be imposed on the traditional social force model based on the near- and far-zone concept developed by psychologists to simulate the interactions between evacuees and also the overall evacuation process. The model will be verified using the results of group evacuation experiments to be conducted in this project. The performance of the model will also be benchmarked with other commercial packages. 在性能化消防工程研究中，确定所需安全逃生时间（RSET）对于火灾场景的安全至关重要。當中人员疏散运动的数值模拟能提供所需的逃生时间估计，这正是RSET的主要组成部分。不同的研究人员报告在疏散中人员之间的微细相互作用是至关重要的，并且极大地影响整體撤离的模式和时间。因此有必要深入研究當中的人类行为以及疏散人员在疏散过程中的相互作用。在初期疏散建模研究中，撤离者的竞争或合作行为往往在模拟之前已预先定义了。基于其预定义的行为而發展出人员间的启发式交互规则。然而，心理学家們报告在实際情况中的疏散绝不是纯粹的竞争或合作。此外，撤离人员的行为可以根据他/她的情况（例如靠近火源或出口）和他/她与邻近疏散人员（例如家人，朋友或陌生人）等的关系而産生动态变化。心理学家也发现疏散人员的行为本质上是相对的。撤离者A可能与B合作，因为他们是同一群体的成员，但对C有竞争，因为他们是不同群体的成员。此外，我们可以设想两个撤离者之间的这些相对行为在相反的方向上不一定相同。例如，撤离者A可能与B合作，因为他们是同一组的成员。然而，撤离者B可能对A的协同作用或甚至竞争性较小，因为B正暴露于危险情境中（例如来自火的过度热辐射）。这种相对竞争-合作（c-c）行为是在先前的模型中没有考慮到的，但確實存在于实际情况中，并且实际上是撤离者之间相互作用的主要组成部分。该拟议研究将根据相关心理学理论开发c-c行为模型。我們将开发一个c-c矩阵来表示其影响半径内任何两个撤离者之间的c-c行为。矩阵将被转换为撤离者之间的虚拟力。这些力将强加于传统的社会力量模型，该模型建基于心理学家开发的近区和远区概念，以模拟撤离者之间的相互作用以及整个疏散过程。该模型将使用現有的群体疏散數據进行验证。该模型的性能也将与其他商业软件包进行基准测试。

11208119.label: Realisation of objectives
11208119.value: Objective 1 A cumulative prospect theory (CPT) implemented cellular automata (CA) model has been developed to determine the natural human decision making, which could be competitive or cooperative, during the evacuation process. However, people are not always rational in real-life risk emergencies. Addressing this inconsistency, cumulative prospect theory (CPT) was developed to make the most prospective decision under risk or uncertainty by applying weighting functions to transform the outcomes and probabilities of the available options and combine them into prospects. This approach has been reported to realistically model human decision-making behaviour. At each time step of the evacuation, each evacuee is involved in the decision-making of the moving path, which critically affects the evacuation process and efficiency. Thus, CPT can be applied to model the movement direction. In our study, CPT was integrated with the CA model (CPT-CA) to mimic exit choices and route choice behaviours [3,4]. Objective 2 We further developed a model to simulate an undeclared leader and follower behaviours during evacuation by use of transfer entropy [2]. Social force model is adopted as the platform for implementation. Due to the attractive forces between leader and followers, the followers cooperate with the leader as group as a group during evacuation. Similarly, due to the repulsive force between leaders, the leaders compete with each other during the evacuation. This new idea was successfully implemented into the social force model. Objective 3 and 4 We did literature survey and found the video records which can be downloaded from the the literature: P. Geoerg, J. Schumann, S. Holl, M. Boltes, and A. Hofmann, “The influence of individual impairments in crowd dynamics,” Fire Mater., vol. 45, no. 4, pp. 529–542, Feb. 2020 and its website: http://ped.fz-juelich.de/da/2017sime. The video shows the target area within which 15 participants are distributed. They were required to exit through a 0.9-m-wide door on the right side of the area. The trajectories of these people during the moving process were extracted from the website for validating the simulation results. By use of the experimental results, the model parameters were calibrated to achieve the best performance. Objective 5 Our developed evacuation model was compared with the traditional social force model in [1]. Our developed model outperformed the social force model in providing more accurate trajectories. Our method is expected to serve as a novel methodological tool for recognising local interactions (either competitive or cooperative) between evacuees. [1] Xie W, Gao D, Lee EWM (2022) Detecting Undeclared-Leader-Follower Structure in Pedestrian Evacuation Using Transfer Entropy, IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems 23(10), 17644-17653. [2] Xie W, Lee EWM, Lee YY (2022) Simulation of spontaneous leader–follower behaviour in crowd evacuation, Automation in Construction 134, 104100. [3] Gao DL, Lee EWM, Lee YY (2022) Integration of cumulative prospect theory in cellular automata model for building evacuation, International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction 74, 102904. [4] Gao DL, Xie W, Cao RF, Weng JW, Lee EWM, Lee YY (2023) The performance of cumulative prospect theory's functional forms in decision-making behavior during building evacuation, International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction 99, 104132.

11208119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11208119.value: As the competitive and cooperative behaviours in the movements of the evacuees and their interaction can greatly affect the overall evacuation patterns and times, in-depth investigations of evacuees’ behaviours and interactions are warranted. In this research, the cellular automata (CA) model, widely used to simulate building evacuations, determines the moving direction of evacuees (i.e., they either remain stationary or move to a neighbouring cell) and provides agents in the model with rational competitive or cooperative choices. However, people are not always rational in real-life risk emergencies. Addressing this inconsistency, cumulative prospect theory (CPT) was developed to make the most prospective decision under risk or uncertainty by applying weighting functions to transform the outcomes and probabilities of the available options and combine them into prospects. This approach has been reported to realistically model human decision-making behaviour. At each time step of the evacuation, each evacuee is involved in the decision-making of the moving path which involves competition and cooperation among evacuees, which critically affects the evacuation process and efficiency. Thus, CPT can be applied to model the movement direction. In our study, CPT was integrated with the CA model (CPT-CA) to mimic exit choices and route choice behaviours. Simulation results showed that the CPT-CA model can provide near realistic evacuation patterns and evacuation times even when the sensitivity parameters are not adjusted. The proposed CPT-CA model can be helpful for logistical planning in evacuation design and emergency risk management. It was also found that the undeclared leader-follower relation between evacuees happens during evacuation. After implementation of this leader-follower behaviour in the social force model, it was found that the followers cooperate with their leaders while the leaders compete with each other during the evacuation process. In this research, we adopted transfer entropy to determine roles of leaders and followers of the evacuees and simulate their movements during the evacuation process. The existing experimental results extracted from previous research demonstrate that our model predict a more close-realistic trajectories of evacuees' movement than the traditional social force model.

11208119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11208119.value: In future, this developed model will be merged with other psychology-based models to establish a psychology implemented building evacuation simulation model. Literatures stated that the actual behaviour of human is a mix of different social behaviours (e.g. competitive, cooperative, impatient, stress, etc.). Combining the behaviours is the next challenges of this research. However, the movement of an evacuee in every moment depends on his current route choice which is a decision making process. This decision making can be simplified as a process converting the visual context of the evacuee to the speed and direction of his movement in next time step. We believe this conversion is very complicated. Instead of developing mathematical models for this conversion, it is proposed to be simulated by use of machine learning approach. Therefore, we will develop a project to capture the movements of pedestrians by video recording, extract the movement data from the video clips, use the data to train an artificial neural network model. The trained model will be validated by the collected pedestrian movement data.

11208119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11208119.value: The competitive and cooperative behaviors do exist in the course of building evacuation. Our developed models for movement decision making are able to simulate the two behaviours of the evacuees. The results show that our model outperformed the traditional model to provide a close realistic simulation of building evacuation. Therefore, the building designer, building manager and crowd-control planner can develop their plans according to the simulation results so that over-crowded condition or even stampede can be avoided. The implementation of psychological theories in building evacuation modelling is a novel idea. This research confirmed the feasibility of this approach and explore this new research arena to the researchers to further improve the pedestrian movement or building evacuation modelling.

11209219.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11209219.value: 面向复杂环境的迁移学习方法及其应用研究

11209219.label: Project Objectives
11209219.value: Develop a noise module for addressing noisy data in transfer learning. Develop an imbalance module for addressing the issue of imbalanced label data. Develop an online module for handling incremental data. Apply the developed TL framework to real-world applications.
rows: Develop a noise module for addressing noisy data in transfer learning.
Develop an imbalance module for addressing the issue of imbalanced label data.
Develop an online module for handling incremental data.
Apply the developed TL framework to real-world applications.

11209219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209219.value: To date, due to the fast development of digital technologies, huge volumes of data with complex properties which come from various sources, such as mobile devices and internet applications, are involved in many machine learning (ML) tasks. As problems seldom exist in isolation, transfer learning (TL) has been proposed in the literature as a paradigm to leverage the rich labeled data from the source domain to improve the learning performance in the target domain where only few (or no) labeled data are available. TL is a revolutionary breakthrough that makes it possible to reuse prior work and democratize ML models (https://tdwi.org/articles/2018/08/24/adv-all-secret-behind-new-ai-spring-transfer-learning.aspx). Recently, TL has been used as one of the core techniques in Google’s Cloud AutoML which was announced in January 2018 (http://www.fast.ai/2018/07/23/auto-ml-3/). However, despite the great success TL has enjoyed so far, there is a lack of TL models designed to pursue the positive transfer performance in today’s applications with data in complex environments, such as intelligent robot training and logistic systems, where the data available for training are often noisy, imbalanced, and received incrementally. Keeping the above in mind, we aim to design and develop a new TL framework for resolving real-world applications featuring noisy, imbalanced, and incremental data, where most existing TL methods may fail to enable positive knowledge transfer and thus cannot achieve the desirable performance. In particular, by leveraging techniques such as importance sampling and Bayesian estimation, which have been successfully applied in deep learning, imbalanced learning and online learning, the research proposed in this project will be carried out in four different aspects including 1) Develop a noise module for addressing noisy data in transfer learning; 2) Develop an imbalance module for addressing the issue of imbalanced label data; 3) Develop an online module for handling incremental data; 4) Apply the developed TL framework to real-world applications, i.e., optimal motion generation for robots in complex environments and fast route planning in logistic systems. 机器学习面临的重大挑战是如何处理具有复杂属性的海量数据。迁移学习作为一种利用源域标记信息来改善目标域学习性能的方法，已经被证明在解决此类问题上的有效性。然而，当利用现有的方法来解决现实世界的问题时，仍然性能不彰，例如使用迁移学习来使得机器人具备更强的智能和处理复杂工况下的物流调度系统，都有较大的改进空间。而主要的原因之一是因为此类的数据常含有噪声，并且类别不均衡同时会随着时间而不断变化。在本项目中，我们提出了一个新的迁移学习框架，并利用它来处理动态环境下的带噪的类别不均衡的数据。具体的说，我们将使用深度学习、不平衡学习以及在线学习的技术，从以下四个方面展开研究：1）设计一个处理的噪声数据的迁移学习方法；2）开发一个能够应对样本不均衡的迁移学习方法；3）设计在线算法以来动态变化的数据；4）将设计开发的迁移学习框架应用到实际复杂应用中，例如复杂环境中机器人的最优动作生成和物流系统里的快速车辆路径规划。

11209219.label: Realisation of objectives
11209219.value: Overall, the project team has successfully completed the project and achieved all the project objectives. All the research findings have been published in top-tier international journals and conferences. The developed techniques and algorithms in this project have been comprehensively evaluated on both benchmark datasets and real-world applications, which demonstrates the practical value and applicability of the research conducted in this project. In particular, for the first objective, i.e., develop a noise module for addressing noisy data in transfer learning, we have conducted comprehensive literature review on knowledge transfer in both learning and optimization, and completed a survey on evolutionary transfer optimization (ETO) based on the type of problems being solved by existing ETO methods, which are ETO for optimization in uncertain environment, ETO for multitask optimization, ETO for complex optimization, ETO for multi/many-objective optimization, and ETO for machine learning applications. This work also highlighted some of the challenges faced in this emerging research field of computational intelligence and discussed some promising future research directions in ETO. Based on these investigations, we have developed a deep reinforcement learning based approach to learn the useful policy from evolutionary optimization data which include both useful and noise data, to predict the proper search operator while the optimization progresses online. Moreover, we defined the concept of transfer rank, and developed a transfer rank and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) based knowledge transfer approach to identify the useful data to be transferred across optimization tasks towards efficient and effective evolutionary multi-task optimization. Furthermore, we developed a multilayer perceptron with only one hidden layer, in which the number of neurons in the input and output layers is equal to the dimension of the decision space of a given problem, to learn from the obtained search data (where noise data may exist) for predicting further promising search direction in solving large-scale multi-objective optimization problems (LMOPs). Comprehensive experimental studies against state-of-the-art evolutionary optimization methods validated the effectiveness of the proposed approach when handling the search space of LMOPs with dimensionality ranging from 1,000 to 10,000. Therefore, we have 100% achieved the first objective for handling noise data in transfer learning as planned. For the second objective, i.e., develop an imbalance module for addressing the issue of imbalanced label data, we have developed several approaches for address the knowledge transfer in imbalanced data environment. Particularly, taking the large-scale multi-objective optimization problem (LMOP) domain as the case study, we have developed a discriminative reconstruction network (DRN) model (containing an encoder, a decoder, and a classifier) for knowledge transfer across different LMOPs. Considering there are only limited nondominated solutions (label data) and much dominated solutions, in the proposed approach, the DRN is trained by the currently obtained nondominated solutions for all LMOPs via backpropagation with gradient descent. With this well-trained DRN model, the proposed algorithm can transfer the solutions of source LMOPs directly to the target LMOP for assisting its optimization, can evaluate the correlation between the source and target LMOPs to control the transfer of solutions, and can learn a dimensional-reduced Pareto-optimal subspace of the target LMOP to improve the efficiency of transfer optimization in the large-scale search space. Moreover, in the case of having no labelled source data, we have developed a random embedding-based evolutionary multitasking paradigm for multi-objective optimization. In this work, the target problem is firstly embedded into multiple low-dimensional subspaces by using different random embeddings, aiming to build up a multi-task environment for identifying the underlying effective subspace. Then the implicit multi-objective evolutionary multitasking is performed with seamless knowledge transfer to enhance the optimization process. Besides random embedding, we have also developed a multi-variation multifactorial evolutionary algorithm for solving LMOPs. In this work, we conduct an evolutionary search on both the original space of the LSMOP and multiple simplified spaces constructed in a multi-variation manner concurrently. To improve the usefulness of each created simplified space, dynamic task replacement is also developed based on the evaluation of the transferred knowledge across tasks. Comprehensive empirical studies were carried out on a set of LSMOPs with 2-3 objectives and 500-5000 variables. The experiment results highlighted the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed method compared to the state-of-the-art methods for solving LSMOPs. Therefore, we have 100% achieved this objective successfully. For the third objective, i.e., develop an online module for handling incremental data, we have also developed several approaches for handling the knowledge learning and transfer in an online data environment. Particularly, taking dynamic optimization where the problem to be addressed may change over time, as the case study, we have developed an inverse Gaussian process-based prediction approach for solving dynamic multi-objective optimization problems (DMOPs), which exploits the inverse Gaussian process to construct a predictor that learns and transfer the historical optimal solutions from the objective space to the decision space. A sampling mechanism was developed for generating sample points in the objective space. Then, the inverse Gaussian process-based predictor is employed to generate an effective initial population by using these sample points. Moreover, we have developed a clustering-based transfer learning method to solve DMOPs. When the environment changes, two novel operations (clustering-based selection and clustering-based transfer) are used to guide knowledge transfer. Specifically, clustering-based selection aims to find a population with nondominated solutions and dominated solutions as the training data for the new environment. Then, clustering-based transfer further collects the previous Pareto optimal solutions and some noise solutions as the training data for the previous environment. In addition, we have also developed an evolutionary search with multi-view prediction for solving DMOP, which conducts knowledge learning and transfer from the views of both decision and objective spaces. To estimate dynamic changes in DMOP, a kernelized autoencoding model is derived to perform the multi-view prediction in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), which holds a closed-form solution. The performance of this method has been comprehensively investigated on the commonly used DMOP benchmarks, as well as a real-world case study on the movie recommendation problem. The obtained experimental results verified the efficacy of the proposed method for solving both benchmark and real-world DMOPs. Therefore, we have successfully achieved the third objective in 100%. For the forth objective, i.e., apply the developed TL framework to real-world applications, we have applied the developed transfer learning approaches to several real-world applications, such as dynamic flexible job shop scheduling, movie recommendation problem, and real-world LMOP test suite (termed RMTF). Moreover, to meet today’s requirement of learning and optimization services on the cloud for many real-world applications, where hundreds or thousands of requests are often received at the same time, we have developed an evolutionary multi-task optimization paradigm based on the graphics processing unit (GPU), and realized the GPU-based implicit and explicit knowledge transfer mechanisms for conducting transfer across optimization tasks. Therefore, we have also 100% achieved the forth objective as planned.

11209219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209219.value: The research project has been successfully completed, and all the research findings have been published in top-tier international journals and conferences. The project's objectives have been achieved, and the developed techniques and algorithms have been evaluated on benchmark datasets and real-world applications, demonstrating the practical value and applicability of the research. The project team focused on three modules: noise, imbalance, and online, to address the problems of noisy data in transfer learning, imbalanced label data, and incremental data, respectively. For the noise module, the team conducted a comprehensive literature review of knowledge transfer in learning and optimization and completed a survey on evolutionary transfer optimization (ETO). Based on the investigation, the team developed a deep reinforcement learning-based approach to learn the useful policy from evolutionary optimization data that includes both useful and noise data. Additionally, they developed a transfer rank and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) based knowledge transfer approach to identify useful data for efficient and effective evolutionary multi-task optimization. For the imbalance module, the team developed several approaches for knowledge transfer in imbalanced data environments. They developed a discriminative reconstruction network (DRN) model for knowledge transfer across different large-scale multi-objective optimization problems (LMOPs). They also developed a random embedding-based evolutionary multitasking paradigm for multi-objective optimization, which builds a multi-task environment for identifying the underlying effective subspace. Moreover, they developed a multi-variation multifactorial evolutionary algorithm for solving LMOPs. For the online module, the team developed several approaches for handling knowledge learning and transfer in an online data environment. They developed an inverse Gaussian process-based prediction approach for solving dynamic multi-objective optimization problems (DMOPs), a clustering-based transfer learning method, and an evolutionary search with multi-view prediction for solving DMOP. These approaches exploit the inverse Gaussian process to construct a predictor that learns and transfers historical optimal solutions from the objective space to the decision space and conduct knowledge learning and transfer from the views of both decision and objective spaces. Comprehensive experimental studies were carried out on a set of problems with various dimensions and objectives. The results highlighted the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed methods compared to state-of-the-art methods for solving problems in different domains. Overall, the project team's research outcomes have practical implications and offer promising directions for future research in the field of computational intelligence.

11209219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209219.value: Transfer learning has shown great potential in many different applications, allowing the transfer of knowledge learned in one domain to improve performance in a related but different domain. However, transfer learning in complex environments with multiple related tasks and varying levels of similarity between them is still a challenging and active area of research. There is significant potential for further development in this field, as transfer learning can lead to significant improvements in performance and efficiency when applied to complex environments. One potential avenue for further development is the investigation of more advanced techniques for selecting and adapting source domains to target domains, such as active learning or reinforcement learning. These techniques could enable more efficient and effective transfer of knowledge in complex environments. Another promising direction for research is the development of multi-task learning approaches that can simultaneously learn multiple related tasks and transfer knowledge between them. This approach could be especially useful in complex environments where multiple tasks must be performed simultaneously or sequentially. In terms of proposed course of action, it may be beneficial to start by identifying key challenges and limitations in current transfer learning methods for complex environments. Then, a plan for developing and testing new techniques to address these challenges can be formulated. This plan should include the development of benchmark datasets and evaluation metrics that can be used to compare and measure the effectiveness of different transfer learning techniques in complex environments. Overall, there is great potential for further development of transfer learning in complex environments, and with continued research and experimentation, this field could lead to significant improvements in a wide range of applications.

11209219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209219.value: Transfer learning is a machine learning technique where knowledge learned from one task is utilized to improve the performance of another related task. The proposed research project aims to advance transfer learning techniques in complex environments, where the data is noisy, imbalanced, or incremental. A noisy data environment means that the data used to train the machine learning model contains errors, which can lead to incorrect predictions. An imbalanced data environment means that there are more examples of one class than the other in the dataset. In incremental data environments, new data is continuously added, and the model needs to learn from the new data without forgetting what it learned before. This research project is significant because it will develop new transfer learning techniques that can handle these complex environments. These techniques will improve the accuracy and reliability of machine learning models, especially in real-world scenarios where the data is often noisy, imbalanced, or incremental. The value of this research project lies in its potential impact on various applications of machine learning and optimization, such as healthcare, finance, and transportation. For example, in healthcare, the proposed techniques can help to diagnose diseases accurately, especially in cases where the data is noisy or imbalanced. In finance, these techniques can assist in optimizing the investment strategy dynamically over time. In transportation, the proposed techniques can aid in developing self-driving cars that can learn from new data without forgetting what they learned before. Overall, the proposed research project has the potential to advance the field of transfer learning by developing new techniques that can handle complex environments, improve the accuracy and reliability of machine learning and optimization models, and have a positive impact on various real-world applications.

11209519.value: 采用低精度模拟/数字转换器的大规模MIMO系统

11209519.label: Project Objectives
11209519.value: We will study treatments of quantization distortion in massive MIMO systems with LR-ADC. We will investigate a decorrelation principle. We will study its applications in systems involving channel estimation, interference cancellation and quantization compensation. The decorrelation principle provides an efficient means to suppress correlation among multiple local processors. We will derive state evolution technique to track the performance of iterative receiver for massive MIMO systems with LR-ADC. We will study optimization techniques to match multiple local processors. We conjecture that such matching can offer near-optimal performance obtained by mutual information analysis. We will rigorously verify this conjecture. We will design fast implementation algorithms to reduce complexity. The current form of the decorrelation technique requires high cost matrix inversions to achieve good performance. We will investigate low cost technique using memory terms, which can avoid matrix inversions. We will develop a solution that can offer good trade-off between performance and complexity.

11209519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209519.value: The massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system is a key technology for future wireless systems. A practical obstacle for massive MIMO is the high cost of high-resolution analogue-to-digital (AD) and digital-to-analogue (DA) conversions. In a full digital implementation, each antenna requires an individual radio frequency (RF) chain with DA/AD converters. The related cost is a serious burden when the number of antennas is large. In this project, we will study the use of low-cost, low-resolution (LR) AD converter (ADC) for the up-link systems. We will develop advanced post-conversion signal processing algorithms and devise corresponding forward error control (FEC) coding techniques. Our proposed tasks combine the recent advances in iterative statistical signal processing and iterative decoding. The so-called turbo principle is a conventional technique to avoid correlation buildup during iterative processing. This technique can deliver nearly optimal performance in binary decoding, but it is not optimal when more complicated operations, such as channel estimation, interference cancellation and quantization compensation, are involved. In this project, we will study a novel decorrelation technique that allows more effective information exchange and, in the same time, avoids the correlation problem. We will study methods to match multiple local processors. Based on preliminary numerical results, we conjecture that this matching technique can offer near-optimal performance. We will rigorously verify this conjecture in the proposed project. We will also design algorithms that can provide good performance without resorting to costly matrix inversions. In our preliminary work, we observed that the new techniques outperform the conventional turbo technique as well as the state-of-the-art AMP (approximate message passing) technique in a broad range of massive MIMO channel conditions. These observations are very encouraging since the turbo and AMP techniques are among the most powerful tools for communication and signal processing systems available. The outcomes of this project will provide new insights and solutions to massive MIMO systems. 大規模多輸入多輸出（MIMO）系統是未來無線系統的關鍵技術。大規模MIMO的一个實際障礙是高分辨率模數（AD）和數模（DA）轉換的高成本。在全數字實現中，每個天線需要具有DA / AD轉換器的一个射頻（RF）鏈路。當天線數量很大時，相關成本是一個嚴重的負擔。 在這個項目中，我們將研究在上行鏈路系統接收端使用低成本，低分辨率（LR）AD轉換器（ADC）。我們將開發先進的轉換後信號處理算法並設計相應的前向差錯控制（FEC）編碼技術。我們提出的目标結合了迭代統計信號處理和迭代解碼的最新進展。所謂的turbo原理是在迭代處理期間避免相關性的傳統技術。該技術可以在二進制解碼中提供幾乎最佳的性能，但是當涉及更複雜的操作（例如信道估計，干擾消除和量化補償）時，它不是最佳的。在這個項目中，我們將研究一種新的去相關技術，它允許更有效的信息交換，同時避免相關性的問題。我們將研究匹配多個本地處理器的方法。基於初步的數值結果，我們推測這種匹配技術可以提供接近最優的性能。我們將在此項目中嚴格驗證這一猜想。我們還將設計能夠提供良好性能的算法以避免採用昂貴的矩陣求逆。 在我們的初步工作中，我們觀察到新技術在许多大規模MIMO信道條件下優於傳統的turbo技術以及最先進的AMP（近似消息傳遞）技術。這些觀察結果非常令人鼓舞，因為turbo和AMP技術是已知的通信和信號處理系統最強大的工具。該項目的成果將為大規模MIMO系統提供新的理解和解決方案。

11209819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11209819.value: Recently, there has been an increasing demand of the ultra-high-definition (UHD) video services. The UHD video, which provides a realistic viewing experience with high volume of data, is revolutionizing the video ecosystem and driving the upgrade of the information industry. In this context, the contradiction between the exponential growth of ultra-high-definition video big data and limited storage space as well as transmission bandwidth has become increasingly prominent. In view of these challenges, the joint video experts team from ITU-T and MPEG has launched the project of next generation video coding standard-versatile video coding (VVC). In VVC, new coding structures and a set of coding tools are adopted, which significantly boost the coding performance compared to the previous HEVC standard. Along with the standardization process, it is urgent and important to study the encoder optimization algorithms, which not only facilitate the implementation and deployment of the VVC standard in the future, but also provide useful information and guidance for the standardization process. In this project, we will systematically study the VVC encoder optimization from the perspectives of high efficiency rate control and low complexity encoding by leveraging the artificial intelligence technologies. In particular, we first study the rate-distortion characteristics of UHD videos in VVC to regularize the coding bit rate. More specifically, the rate-quantization and distortion-quantization relationships are investigated with the new coding structure that incorporates both quadtree-binary tree as well as triple tree partitioning, and the intelligent rate control is achieved based on the recent development of reinforcement learning. As such, the number of coding bits for each frame and CTU is optimized to achieve high efficiency rate control. Furthermore, we extend the rate-distortion modeling to the joint rate-distortion-complexity (RDC) optimization of VVC codec, aiming to achieve a good trade-off between rate-distortion performance and encoding complexity for low complexity encoding. In particular, by modelling the relationship between them with the advanced machine learning techniques, the encoder structure can be determined in the complexity constrained scenario. Furthermore, the decision of coding modes can be further optimized with the complexity allocation strategy. By intelligently modelling the local RDC relationship, the complexity allocation is optimized for each coding unit to achieve the overall optimal coding performance. 11209819.label: Realisation of objectives
11209819.value: All four objectives are investigated, and several findings are published. In this work, we have developed a joint decision tree and visual feature optimization rate control scheme for ultrahigh-definition (UHD) versatile video coding (VVC). 1) First, we design a new rate-distortion (R-D) model for UHD videos, and we establish a decision-tree-based multiclass classification scheme to improve the prediction accuracy of the R-D model by fully considering visual features. 2) Second, based on the proposed R-D model, the globally optimal solution is obtained through convex optimization. 3) We embed our algorithm into the latest VVC reference software, VTM 10.2. According to our experimental results, compared with the latest algorithm in VTM 10.2 and other state-of-the-art algorithms, our method can achieve significant bit rate reductions while maintaining a given peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) or structural similarity index measure (SSIM) 4) We have developed a number of rate control algorithms address the optimal complexity allocation scheme of VVC at coding unit level and achieve fast coding mode selection under the limitation of constrained complexity.

11209819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11209819.value: This work comprehensively reviews the latest progress in RC for the H.265/HEVC and H.266/VVC video coding standards and discusses relevant development prospects. More specifically, this paper first introduces and compares different kinds of RC methods based on various R-D models, as well as emerging DL-based schemes. Then, the implementation schemes of RC methods in different hardware platforms are reviewed. Finally, we discuss RC methods based on ML and DL, the evolution from RC to quality control, RC methods considering human visual perception and depth perception, RC methods for 360-degree/HDR video, and RC methods for the predicted video content. A comprehensive summary of directions of future work on topics such as RC methods and RDO in depth coding, is also presented. The aim was to provide valuable guidance for improving, implementing, applying, and continuously developing the current and next generations of RC standards.

11209819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11209819.value: These works can help provide better video streaming applications, and we are working closely with a local company to launch the findings.

11209819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11209819.value: Video coding is a video compression technique that compresses the original video sequence to achieve a smaller archive file or a lower transmission bandwidth under constraints on the visual quality loss. Rate control (RC) plays a critical role in video coding. It can achieve stable stream output in practical applications, especially in real-time video applications, such as video conferencing or game live streaming. Most RC algorithms directly or indirectly characterise the relationship between the bit rate (R) and quantisation (Q) and then allocate bits for every coding unit to guarantee the global bit rate and video quality level. Our work comprehensively reviewed and investigated the classic RC technologies used in international video standards of past generations, analyses the mathematical models and implementation mechanisms of various schemes, and compares the performance of recent state-of-the-art RC algorithms. Finally, we developed a few directions and new application areas for RC methods. We hope that this review can help support the development, implementation, and application of RC for new video coding standards.

11210119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210119.value: We study the problem for finding complex proteoforms from protein databases based on top-down tandem mass spectrum data. The main difficulty to solve the problem is to handle the combinatorial explosion of various alterations on a protein. To overcome the combinatorial explosion of various alterations on a protein, the problem has been formulated as the alignment problem of a proteoform mass graph (PMG) and a spectrum mass graph (SMG). The other important issue is to handle mass errors of peaks in the input spectrum. In previous methods, an error tolerance value is used to handle the mass differences between the matched consecutive nodes/peaks in PMG and SMG. However, such a way to handle mass error can not guarantee that the mass difference between any pairs of nodes in the alignment is approximately the same for both PMG and SMG. It may lead to large error accumulation if positive (or negative) errors occur consecutively for a large number of consecutive matched node pairs. The problem is severe so that some existing software packages include a step to further refine the alignments. In this paper, we propose a new model to handle the mass errors of peaks based on the formulation of the PMG and SMG. Note that the masses of sub-paths on the PMG are theoretical and suppose to be accurate. Our method allows each peak in the input spectrum to have a predefined error range. In the alignment of PMG and SMG, we need to give a correction of the mass for each matched peak within the predefined error range. After the correction, we impose that the mass between any two (not necessarily consecutive) matched nodes in the PMG is identical to that of the corresponding two matched peaks in the SMG. Intuitively, this kind of alignment is more accurate. We design an algorithm to find a maximum number of matched node and peak pairs in the two (PMG and SMG) mass graphs under the new constraint. The obtained alignment can show matched node and peak pairs as well as the corrected positions of peaks. The algorithm works well for moderate size input instances and takes very long time as well as huge size memory for large input size instances. Therefore, we propose an algorithm to do diagonal alignment. The diagonal alignment algorithm can solve large input size instances in reasonable time. Experiments show that our new algorithms can report alignments with much larger number of matched node pairs. The software package and test data sets are available at https://github.com/Zeirdo/TopMGRefine. An improved version was given in "Fast peak error correction algorithms for proteoform identification using top-down tandem mass spectra" (bioinformatics). The new version is much faster and it is the first that that local alignment can be computed for real datasets. We also provide a method for visualization of mass spectrum data storage and retrieval to ease the work of proteoform identification. RNA sequenced data can be handled by input modification information into our computer programs.

11210119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210119.value: The methods can be used as a base for solving quantitative identification of multiple proteoforms.

11210119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210119.value: In this project, we have developed new algorithms for proteoform identification using top-down mass spectra. We propose a new computational model to handle peak error correction so that the obtained alignments/results are more reliable. We also provide a method for visualization of mass spectrum data storage and retrieval to ease the work of proteoform identification.

11210219.label: Project Objectives
11210219.value: To develop a unified model for capturing the essence of various access schemes and incorporating the key features of coexistence; To optimize the access performance of a given network under various coexistence scenarios, and characterize the effects of coexistence on the optimal access performance; To characterize the joint optimal tuning of key access parameters of coexisting networks for fair and efficient coexistence, and develop distributed algorithms to implement the optimal tuning.

11210219.label: Realisation of objectives
11210219.value: All the proposed tasks have been successfully completed. For Objective 1, a unified analytical framework was established for modeling and performance optimization of coexisting networks. The access schemes of representative coexisting networks in unlicensed bands can be categorized into 1) CSMA-based and 2) Aloha-based, where the former requires sensing before transmissions, and the latter is sensing-free. Examples include the DCF of WiFi networks and the LBT schemes of 5G/LTE cellular networks in the unlicensed spectrum, both of which are CSMA-based, and the duty-cycle-based schemes of 5G/LTE unlicensed, LoRaWANs, and WPANs, where sensing is not required. Typical coexistence scenarios can usually be modelled either as multi-group CSMA or Aloha-plus-CSMA. A multi-group CSMA model was proposed in [1] and extended to a mixed Aloha-plus-CSMA model in [4]. For modeling of coexisting networks with distinct access mechanisms, the key lies in the modeling of Head-of-Line (HOL) packets of nodes in different networks, and the characterization of steady-state probability of successful transmissions of HOL packets of each network. In the proposed multi-group CSMA model, a Markov renewal process was established to model the HOL packets of each group. The service rate of each node was then derived as a function of the steady-state probability of successful transmissions of HOL packets of each group. For the proposed mixed Aloha-plus-CSMA model, two different Markov renewal processes were proposed to model the HOL packets of the Aloha-based and CSMA-based groups, respectively. Different from the multi-group CSMA model where transmission failures only occur in the beginning of each packet transmission, a packet transmission from CSMA nodes could be interrupted by an Aloha node which does not sense. The characterization of steady-state probability of successful transmissions of HOL packets of each network thus becomes more involved. In the above models, one AP is assumed for each coexisting network, which receives signals from multiple users. The effect of multiple APs’ locations on the network performance was further considered in [2]-[3]. Moreover, within each network, nodes are assumed to have identical traffic characteristics and parameter setting. Such symmetric setting was further relaxed to a general asymmetric scenario in [5] for sensing-free Aloha and [11] for sensing-based CSMA, respectively. By unifying different access mechanisms within the same analytical framework, performance optimization under various constraints become feasible. The proposed analytical framework lays a solid foundation for the successful accomplishment of Objectives 2 and 3. For Objective 2, the performances of two representative coexisting scenarios, i.e., multiple CSMA-based networks, and coexisting Aloha-based and CSMA-based networks, were analyzed and optimized. In both cases, it was demonstrated that if each network optimizes its own performance without coordinating with others, it may suffer from significant performance degradation or bring severe damage to its coexisting counterpart. Specifically, for the coexistence of a WiFi network and an LTE network with LBT schemes [1], it is found that even with its own access parameter optimally tuned, the WiFi throughput significantly degrades compared to its stand-alone version if the access parameters of the LTE network are not properly set. The throughput of the coexisting LTE network may drop close to zero when it adopts the Category 4 LBT mechanism. For coexisting Aloha and CSMA networks, on the other hand, it was shown in [4] that Aloha would significantly outperform CSMA if each network optimizes its own throughput performance without cooperation, leading to poor throughput performance for CSMA and severe unfairness. Therefore, for the coexistence of a WiFi network and a duty-cycle-based LTE-U network, if LTE-U and WiFi choose to optimize its own throughput in a non-cooperative manner, the LTE-U eNB would fully occupy the channel, and WiFi nodes would be unable to transmit as they always sense a busy channel. Both suggest that access parameters of coexisting networks need to be jointly tuned for achieving fair and efficient coexistence. For Objective 3, joint optimization of coexisting networks was performed, and distributed algorithms were develop to implement the optimal tuning. In [1], to optimize the coexistence performance of WiFi and LTE networks, the total throughput was maximized under two fairness constraints, including 1) throughput fairness, which is achieved when the throughput ratio between WiFi and LTE reaches a target value, and 2) 3GPP fairness, which is achieved when the WiFi throughput in the coexisting scenario is no less than that of a stand-alone WiFi network. The corresponding optimal initial backoff window sizes of both the LTE and WiFi networks were derived as explicit expressions of system parameters. To facilitate implementation in practice, distributed schemes were further proposed, with which WiFi and LTE can optimally adjust the backoff window sizes based on their own observation and estimation without the need of coordination between the two networks. In [4], the optimal transmission probabilities of Aloha and CSMA for maximizing the total network throughput under a given throughput ratio were also derived, and applied to coexisting duty-cycle-based LTE-U and WiFi networks to optimize their coexistence performance. Simulation results corroborate that with the proposed optimal setting, not only is throughput fairness between LTE-U and WiFi achieved, but the total network throughput is significantly improved compared to that with the standard setting. In [1] and [4], the throughput performance has been the primary concern. To maximize the throughput, the network needs to operate at the saturated condition, i.e., all the nodes’ buffers are always non-empty, in which case the network becomes unstable as the queueing delay of packets would increase with time unboundedly. In practice, stabilizing the network and optimizing the delay performance could be of more interest than pushing the network to saturation. For random-access networks, both stability and delay optimization have been long-standing open issues. The stability issue was recently addressed in [5] and further extended to incorporate multi-cell in [6] and sensing in [11]. Delay optimization was considered in [7], [8], [10] and [12] in various scenarios. How to stabilize coexisting networks and optimize their delay performance is a more pressing challenge, to tackle which the above techniques developed in this project would be useful.

11210219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210219.value: In this project, a unified analytical framework was established, within which different access mechanisms of coexisting networks in the unlicensed spectrum can be analyzed and optimized. It was successfully applied to various coexistence scenarios to maximize the network throughput with fairness constraints by jointly tuning the access parameters. The major findings can be summarized in three parts: 1. Coexistence of representative wireless networks in the unlicensed bands can be modelled either as multi-group CSMA or Aloha-plus-CSMA. For both cases, the key to performance analysis lies in the modeling of Head-of-Line (HOL) packets of nodes in different networks, and the characterization of steady-state probability of successful transmissions of HOL packets of each network. By unifying different access mechanisms within the same analytical framework, performance optimization of coexisting networks under various constraints become feasible. 2. Based on the proposed unified analytical framework, the coexistence performance of various scenarios can be analyzed and optimized. It was shown that if each network optimizes its own performance without coordinating with others, it may suffer from significant performance degradation or bring severe damage to others. For the coexistence of WiFi and LBT-based LTE networks, for instance, the WiFi throughput significantly degrades compared to its stand-alone version even with its own access parameter optimally tuned. When a WiFi network coexists with a duty-cycle-based LTE-U network, if they optimize their own throughput in a non-cooperative manner, the LTE-U eNB would fully occupy the channel, and WiFi nodes would be unable to transmit, leading to serious unfairness. 3. For achieving fair and efficient coexistence, access parameters of coexisting networks need to be jointly tuned. To maximize the total throughput with a certain fairness constraint, the initial backoff window sizes of coexisting networks need to be optimally chosen. Simulation results corroborate that with the proposed optimal setting, not only is throughput fairness achieved, but the total network throughput is significantly improved compared to that with the standard setting. Distributed schemes were also proposed, with which coexisting networks can optimally adjust their backoff window sizes based on their own observation and estimation without inter-network coordination.

11210219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210219.value: The findings of this project have stimulated a number of interesting topics for future research. From the theoretical perspective, in this project, the throughput performance has been the primary concern. While for low-latency applications, which have become increasingly prevalent due to the rising popularity of Machine-to-Machine (M2M) communications, the delay optimization is of more interest, which is nevertheless much more challenging. It is important to further study how to stabilize the coexisting networks and optimize their delay performance by jointly and adaptively tuning the access parameters. From the practical perspective, to offer useful insights for access design, new features introduced into WiFi networks, cellular networks, and other representative and emerging wireless networks in the unlicensed bands should continue to be incorporated into the analysis. The modeling and optimization approaches developed in this project may find wide applications in various coexistence scenarios, and provide important guidance for the optimal access design of M2M communications in the future.

11210219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210219.value: Thanks to its free-to-use nature, the unlicensed spectrum has accommodated a large number of wireless communication systems, which may strongly interfere with each other if not properly designed. For a massive number of wireless devices transmitting over unlicensed bands using various standards, ensuring their fair and efficient coexistence has become an increasingly pressing issue, which is especially critical in the uplink access as the deluge of access requests may easily paralyze the whole network and cause strong inter-network interference. To address this grave challenge, in this project, a unified analytical framework was established, within which different access mechanisms of coexisting networks in the unlicensed spectrum can all be analyzed and optimized. It was successfully applied to various coexistence scenarios to optimize the throughput performance with fairness constraints. Optimal access strategies for achieving fair and efficient coexistence were further developed by characterizing the joint optimal tuning of access parameters of coexisting networks as well as developing distributed algorithms to implement the optimal tuning. The results demonstrate significant performance gains and provide important guidance on the optimal access design of current and future wireless networks.

11210419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210419.value: The behaviour of unsaturated soils in the presence of wetting/drying cycles, which alter the saturation and stress states of the ground, has attracted significant amount of research by geotechnical engineers. In Hong Kong and many other regions with tropical/subtropical climate, heavy rainfalls and seasonal changes of the groundwater level have resulted in landslide failures and the instability of buildings/infrastructures, which, combined with the presence of variously weathered soil profiles, has triggered the interest by the geomechanics community to look into the problem of soil-environment interaction because of the uncountable losses of life and social/economic problems encountered. It is also well accepted today that soil behaviour may be significantly influenced by oxidation and development of iron-oxide coating in natural deposits. Iron-oxide coating has also triggered the interest by engineers/scientists not only on the point of view of a natural-environmental process, but it has also been used in recent years to prevent ground pollution/soil contamination. Soil coating, water-soil interaction and, in a broader sense, fluid-soil interaction have been topics of major interest as well by soil scientists and petroleum engineers since, for example, hydraulic fracturing in petroleum extraction encounters soil-rock interactions in the presence of fluids/lubricants of various viscosities. Despite the realisation by the scientific community that understanding of the complex problems involving soil-environment interaction and the improvement of our predictive tools in the safe and sustainable design of infrastructures and utilisation of resources necessitate a better understanding of the behaviour at the grain-scale and the interactions of soil grain and grain-rock contacts, there has been relatively limited amount of work investigating these problems at the fundamental level of grain interfaces in the laboratory. This project will look into the problem of soil-environment interaction at the grain scale/grain interfaces by performing an original research with cutting-edge laboratory facilities and methods, and provide new insights into various problems of major interests in Hong Kong and internationally. The major points of focus of this project are: (i) The micromechanical behaviour of variously weathered soils/rocks in the presence of wetting/drying cycles and changes in the saturation state (ii) The behaviour of iron-oxide coated grains and (iii) The interactions of soil grains and grain-rock interfaces in the presence of fluids/lubricants of various viscosities. The outcomes of the project will put an important innovative contribution to the state-of-the-art research associated with environment-soil interaction and the development of cutting-edge experimentation at the scale of grain interfaces. 岩土工程师对非饱和土在干湿循环中土体的饱和度和应力状态开展了大量研究。在包括香港在内的许多热带、亚热带地区，由于环境因素，这些区域的土壤常有不同程度的风化，再加上季节性的强降雨导致地下水位时常大幅变化，滑坡或建筑地基失稳等灾害时有发生。故此，众多专家与学者致力于研究土壤与环境相互作用下土体的力学性质以避免类似的灾害发生。许多研究表明土壤中的铁氧化物或铁氧化物对土颗粒的包覆会改变其力学性质，且研究发现铁氧化物包覆的石英沙颗粒可用于吸附过滤土、水中的污染物质。此外，在石油工程、水压致裂技术中，土颗粒表面与多种液体或其他物质的相互作用的研究也有广泛应用。虽然学界普遍意识到开展多种复杂环境下的土壤性质的研究对于基础设施的建设及可持续发展有着重要意义，但是在此方面的实验或基础理论研究却很缺乏。 本研究计划基于一系列细观到微观尺度的实验研究，从根本层面探索多种环境作用下土壤颗粒间的相互作用，并以此为宏观尺度下土体力学性质提供新的思路和依据。本研究项目的主要重点主要分为：（1）测量在干湿循环过程中，不同饱和程度下多种风化程度的土壤及岩石的力学行为变化；（2）研究铁氧化物的包覆对于沙颗粒力学性质的改变；（3）探索在不同种类，不同粘度的液体中沙土颗粒之间及沙颗粒与岩石间的相互作用。此项研究的结果将会拓展加深环境对于土壤作用的认知和理解，并创新、改进颗粒材料微观力学性质的实验研究方法。

11210419.label: Realisation of objectives
11210419.value: The project aimed to provide a new contribution to the state-of-the-art knowledge in the field of micromechanics with emphasis on the Influence of environment-soil and fluid-soil interactions at the grain contact interfaces. Throughout the project, cutting-edge laboratory facilities and experimental methods were developed, and main outcomes of the project were delivered in the form of journal publications addressing all the objectives of the project. This also gave the opportunity for two PhD students to be trained on the project and the PI to develop local and international collaborations. Preliminary and main outcomes of the projects were also presented in one Keynote Lecture and one invited seminar by PI Senetakis. Each of the project objectives was fulfilled 100%. Specific descriptions of the way each objective was achieved are given below with a summary of some of the key works appeared in international journals which contributed to the delivery of project’s objectives. Objective 1: A systematic investigation into the influence of weathering degree on the frictional behavior of particles was performed in the study by Sandeep et al. (2022, appeared in Engineering Geology). In that study, highly and completely decomposed granitic particles were examined in monotonic and cyclic modes of behavior with grain-scale experiments and an in-depth analysis on the influence of weathering degree was conducted on friction, contact stiffness and energy dissipation. Insights into the collision behavior of sand particles and the role of weathering degree were examined by Luo and Senetakis (2022, appeared in Transportation Geotechnics), in which work a novel laboratory approach was developed to coat particles with powder to reproduce analogous surfaces to that of weathered grains. These studies highlighted the substantial influence on the constitutive behavior of particles when weathering is encountered. Most importantly, based on analog wetting-drying cycles simulations by Sandeep et al. (2022), it was revealed that the environmental influences in terms of wetting-drying and saturation conditions may have a significant influence on the frictional behavior of weathered particles; however, this will also depend on the magnitude of normal load. Insights into this problem were also obtained by the study conducted by Ren, Wang He and Senetakis (2022, appeared in Tribology International), on the frictional behavior of interfaces subjected to wetting-drying cycles, in which work a novel approach in developing miniature samples of analogue sedimentary rock was introduced. PI Senetakis developed inter-disciplinary research with an academic from the Department of Chemistry, City University of Hong Kong, in which a novel laboratory method in developing controlled amount of iron oxide coating on the surface of sand particles was developed (Ren et al., 2022, appeared in Acta Geotechnica). In that study, the role of iron oxides (and their amount) on friction, constitutive behavior and elastic characteristics of sand grains was quantified. Objective 2: A novel laboratory method in the reproduction of micro-scale particles in the presence of various viscous fluids was presented by Ren et al. (2021, appeared in Granular Matter). In that study, PI’s group examined the monotonic and cyclic behavior of tailing particles under the influence of different fluids analyzing the relationship of friction – number of shearing cycles – viscosity of fluid as well as the energy dissipation and normal contact response of interfaces. One of the key findings was that the viscosity of the fluid may have a key role on the way abrasion develops due to repeating loading, however the subsequent study by Ren, Li and Senetakis (2022, appeared in Tribology International) showed that the influence of the viscous fluid on the interparticle friction is also controlled by the loading rate (which represented the speed of shearing in their experiments); in specific, these influences were more prominent in the regime of slower loading rates. The effect of fluid presence in various forms was further examined in grain-rock type impact tests by Luo et al. (2021, appeared in International Methods for Numerical & Analytical Methods in Geomechanics, 2022, appeared in Computers and Geotechnics). Objective 3: Throughout the project, novel experimental methods were developed including the coating of sand particles with iron oxides (a key study was presented by Ren et al., 2022, appeared in Acta Geotechnica) and the simulation of wetting-drying cycles (key studies were presented by Sandeep et al., 2022, appeared in Engineering Geology, Ren, Wang, He and Senetakis, 2022, appeared in Tribology International). Scale-effects in terms of particle size effects were discussed in the study by Sandeep, Li and Senetakis (2021, appeared in Tribology International), in which work it was revealed that the size of particles might have a relatively smaller influence on the interparticle friction for dry surfaces, however it has a significant effect on the microslip displacement, thereby controlling the constitutive force-displacement relationship of interfaces. An experimental method was developed by Kasyap and Senetakis (2022, appeared in the Journal of Structural Geology) which study examined scale-effects on the interface behavior of analog rock interfaces in the presence of filling/gauge material. Finally, soil-lubrication effects were presented in the key studies by PI’s group in Ren, Wang, He and Senetakis (2022, appeared in Tribology International) and Ren et al. (2021, appeared in Granular Matter), while novel experimental approaches in the study of the collision behavior of geological materials were presented by Luo et al. (2021, appeared in International Methods for Numerical & Analytical Methods in Geomechanics, 2022, appeared in Computers and Geotechnics). Objective 4: PI Senetakis developed collaborative works which proposed new modeling methods in micromechanical research with emphasis on the grain-scale contact behavior of sand particles. In one of these key studies, PI Senetakis in collaboration with Professor Yu Wang from City University of Hong Kong, developed a machine learning approach in the contact mechanics modeling of soil particles considering different types of geological materials (presented by Reddy, Senetakis and Wang, 2022, appeared in Granular Matter). This work focused particularly on the tangential load – displacement contact response and opened new directions in the integration of machine learning tools with micromechanical-based experiments. The constitutive stress-strain response of rock interfaces in conjunction with scale-effects was examined and modeled by Kasyap and Senetakis (2022, appeared in the Journal of Structural Geology), while Reddy, He and Senetakis (2023, appeared in International Journal for Numerical and Analytical Methods in Geomechanics), introduced new contact models, based on analysis of experimental micromechanical data, into a computer software to examine integrally the mechanical behavior of cemented sands and soft sedimentary rocks. That work followed the earlier study by PI Senetakis in collaboration with scholars from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Professor J. Zhao) and UCL London (Professor M.R. Coop) which aimed at developing new experimental methods in the analysis of soil-environment interactions by representing different types of cemented compounds at particle contacts (Kasyap et al., 2021, appeared in Acta Geotechnica). Analytical studies utilizing grain-scale experimental data from collision experiments, with emphasis in understanding the involved micromechanisms in the load transfer and energy dissipation were presented by Luo et al. (2021, 2022); these works introduced a new approach in modeling the interface mechanical behavior of grain-block systems based on experimental data, simulating in this way indirectly the influence of environment (saturation condition) and the characteristics of the interfaces in the vicinity of the contact.

11210419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210419.value: Major outcomes of the project were delivered in the form of international journal publications which included a total of 32 articles appeared in a number of journals covering broader fields of engineering. This included mainstream and reputable journals of Geotechnical/Geological Engineering (e.g., Engineering Geology, Bulletin of Engineering Geology and the Environment, Computers & Geotechnics, Int. J. for Numerical & Analytical Methods in Geomechanics, Acta Geotechnica, among others) to journals such as Tribology International, Pure and Applied Geophysics, Journal of Structural Geology, Journal of Petroleum Science and Engineering, Granular Matter, Powder Technology, Construction & Building Materials, among others. This also demonstrated the inter-disciplinary nature of the project and the value of its outcomes in different areas of science and engineering, apart from main contributions to Geomechanics and Geotechnical Engineering. This was contributed by the fact that a wide range of topic in soil-environment-fluid interactions were covered throughout the project. More specifically, the influence of weathering degree on the micromechanical behavior of particles and particle-block systems was studies in the journal items no. 5, 24 and 27 including both naturally weathered particles and particles artificially made in the laboratory to simulate analogue degradation. The influence of wetting-drying cycles was examined in journal items no. 23, 24, 29-30, while the collision mechanics were studied in items no. 14, 27-28. Novel experimental methods in the development and examination of the effect of iron oxide coating was presented in the journal item no. 20, which also led to inter-disciplinary research involving academics from civil/geotechnical engineering and chemistry backgrounds. An in-depth understanding of the interactions of particle-fluid and rock-fluid was achieved through the works in journal items no. 2, 23-24, 29-30-32 and scale effects on the mechanics of particle and rock systems were examined in items no. 1, 22. Original contributions with analytical studies and constitutive modeling were presented in the journal items no. 4, 14, 16, 18, 25, 28, 31, including the application of machine learning tools (items no. 11, 13, 28). Finally, a number of studies provided multi-scale insights which are very promising in understanding the behavior of granular systems not only on the point of view of grain-scale analysis, but also as a bulk (items no. 3, 8-10, 14, 17, 19, 21, 26, 31). The project provided also the opportunity for the PI to develop collaborations with institutes from Hong Kong and overseas including Europe, Middle-East Asia and Mainland China.

11210419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210419.value: Given that the project opened new directions in inter-disciplinary research, such as the collaboration of PI Senetakis with academics from Chemistry background, a promising direction will comprise the preparation, in the near future, of a larger-scale application for research fund (such as CRF or TRS) bringing together academics from different areas of Science and Engineering. A proposal of this type could investigate broader aspects of ground-environment interactions including geo-chemistry and biological processes and how these factors influence ground or rock mechanical behavior, thereby providing an in-depth understanding of soil-environment interaction with multi-disciplinary outcomes. Future research could also focus particularly on the integration of machine learning tools with micromechanical-based data to provide multi-scale insights on the behavior of large-scale geo-systems. This can be particularly beneficial to assess geo-hazards such as landslides. Future studies can also provide a stronger link between micro- and macroscopic behavior of geological systems by utilizing physical model tests and in-situ monitoring; these aspects comprise promising directions for the PI in future GRF proposal and/or larger-scale projects.

11210419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210419.value: The understanding of soil-environment-fluid interactions is critical to design safely geo-systems, and particularly, studies at the grain-scale offer invaluable tools for enhanced modeling and fundamental insights to be obtained to understand physical and mechanical processes that contribute to soil and rock behavior and failure. The present project provided an in-depth study of these phenomena covering a broader range of topics in soil-environment-fluid interactions and by developing cutting-edge experimental methods including the development of iron oxides and other types of coatings, the way wetting-drying cycles develop in an actively loaded geo-system, the way particles interact with rocks under impact loads, among other areas. The project not only looked at these problems experimentally, but also analytically by developing constitutive models as well as multi-scale studies which offered insights on the bulk behavior of the material. This was achieved through contact mechanics models, modification of traditional geomechanics models to be used in micromechanical-based research, as well as the application of artificial intelligent tools. The project also provided the opportunity to establish local and international collaborations with researchers/academics from different backgrounds highlighting the interdisciplinary nature of this broader area of research and practice.

11210719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210719.value: 该项目旨在开发基于并行模型的电池系统的热异常检测及定位方法，并可以融入到现有的电池管理系统中。该项目的主要工作可简要总结如下。 • 首先，将针对电池热系统开发一种新颖的时空建模方法，从中提取了用于异常检测的独立时间和空间分量，通过深度学习优化传感器数目及布防位置，通过增量自适应模式实现在线操作。 • 方法的基本原则是在操作中采用两个模型：一个用于正常条件的参考模型（无故障）和一个用于实时性能的在线模型。当系统处于正常状态时，这两个模型的差异应接近零；如果出现任何异常，该模型在统计意义上的性能将偏离参考模型；由此，偏差的残余信号可以在时域和空间域中做进一步处理来做有效检测。 • 最后，设计概率识别方法来实现可靠的异常检测及空间定位。

11210719.label: Realisation of objectives
11210719.value: Objective 1 To overcome the drawback of the traditional KL method, following efforts have been conducted in two different directions. 1) A novel space/time separation framework based on canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) [3] is designed to construct dimension embedded basis functions (DE-BFs) for modeling the nonlinear DPS. The mapping relationship between DE-BF and spatial sensor array is well preserved. The coupling across temporal and different spatial dimensions can be efficiently captured and modelled. • For a high dimensional DPS, a deep learning based space/time separation modeling method [8] is proposed through a high-order singular value decomposition (HOSVD). The spatially distributed nature of high dimensional DPS can be well preserved with minimal information loss, including orthogonality and uniqueness. • Further work has been spent on information completion and learning under sparse sensing [4]. This is the first work to consider DPS modeling in a sparse sensing environment. Based on incremental learning [1], all data can be effectively used from scratch without increasing the computational burden. The work can help optimal placement of sensors in the real application for the battery system. 2) Spatial construction approach [11] is studied to integrate merits of both KL and spectral method. The spatial basis function will be first designed and modelled using B-spline function, and then the temporal coefficients will be learned using data. This novel approach can significantly improve modeling performance in complex situation, and applied in the later modeling of battery system. For the modeling of battery system, a surrogate model-based scheme [6] has been designed to figure out optimal parameters of an electrochemical battery model. The method has integrated a surrogate model with an evolutionary algorithm. The method has been successfully applied to the time-consuming simulations of the P2D model with the significantly improved computational efficiency. Objective 2 An inverse spatio-temporal model based abnormal detection method [2] is designed for parabolic distributed parameter systems based on the adaptive state observer. One major advantage of the proposed model is that only the system output is utilized, without any state measurement. Theoretic analysis guarantees the convergence of the estimation error. The performance of the designed method has been evaluated in the experiment. For the industrial application, a real-time fault detection filter (FDF) [7] has been designed for abnormal detection for distributed parameter processes. A time-varying threshold is designed such that the false alarm in the transient stage can be avoided. It can be used for boundary and in-domain measurement cases without a large amount of data collection and offline training procedures. Rigorous theoretic analysis and experiment validation on a hot strip mill cooling system demonstrate the effectiveness for fault detection of industrial processes. This is a residual based fault detection approach. To accurately locate the abnormality, the continuous spatial basis functions (SBFs) are derived by the above spatial construction method from empirical data. Two new statistics are constructed based on the derived continuous SBFs and the improved independent component analysis algorithm. The abnormality can be timely detected according to the reference signals derived by the central limit theorem and hypothesis testing. With the continuous SBFs, the probability distribution of statistic contribution can be constructed to reveal the actual position of the abnormality. The proposed method [12] can timely detect and locate the abnormality under fewer sensors without the knowledge of PDE and boundary conditions. Objective 3 In application to the battery thermal management, all the above theoretical development need further modification and re-designed. Extensive efforts have been spent with following achievements, each of them is to deal with a unique problem encountered in the applicaton. • Dual separations based space/time separation has been designed for real-time modeling of the battery thermal process [9]. The proposed method integrates the non-homogeneity separation and the time-space (T/S) separation. According to the Rademacher complexity, the generalization bound of the developed model is deduced, thereby ensuring the modeling performance. • Most of modeling methods consume large computation time, and may not be suitable for online operation due to the high requirement of fast response. The approximation techniques are designed to simplify the modeling algorithm, and make the fast modeling technique available for real-time operation of the battery system [10]. • A knowledge based inference system is designed for abnormal detection of the battery system under large uncertainties [14]. This knowledge based system can work in the environment with fewer sensors and lesser mathematical information of the process.
