11210719.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210719.value: 1) Novel outcome in spatiotemporal modeling A novel space/time separation framework based on canonical polyadic decomposition (CPD) [3] is designed to construct dimension embedded basis functions (DE-BFs) for modeling the nonlinear DPS. The mapping relationship between DE-BF and spatial sensor array is well preserved, and thus, the optimal placement of sensors can be easily achieved for battery thermal modeling [13]. • Unique result has been further achieved on sparse sensing based modeling [4]. Based on incremental learning [1], all data can be effectively used from scratch without increasing the computational burden. • For a high dimensional DPS, a deep learning based space/time separation modeling method [8] is proposed through a high-order singular value decomposition. The spatially distributed nature of high dimensional DPS can be well preserved with minimal information loss, including orthogonality and uniqueness. • A surrogate model-based scheme [6] has been designed to figure out optimal parameters of the DPS model. Novel spatial construction based modeling approach is developed for integrating the traditional KL and spectral method [11], and also applied for the spatial detection [12]. 2) Novel outcome in abnormal detection in DPS An inverse spatio-temporal model based abnormal detection method [2] is designed for parabolic distributed parameter systems based on the adaptive state observer. One major advantage of the proposed model is that only the system output is utilized, without any state measurement. • For the industrial application, a real-time fault detection filter (FDF) [7] has been designed for abnormal detection for distributed parameter processes. A time-varying threshold is designed such that the false alarm in the transient stage can be avoided. • The novel spatial construction based modeling can be directly applied to detect and localize any spatial abnormality in DPS [12]. 3) Novel application in battery thermal management Based on the above theoretical progress, many new techniques are developed to deal with different difficulties encountered in the real application of thermal management. • Dual separations based spatiotemporal modeling has been designed to handle complex boundary conditions of the battery thermal process [9]. • Fast modeling technique is developed for real-time operation of the battery system [10]. • A knowledge based inference system is designed for abnormal detection of the battery system under large uncertainties [14].

11210719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210719.value: In real industrial field, multiple physical fields may be coupled which generate a very complex DPS with dynamics change sharply and strongly nonlinear. This requires multiple models integrated and parameter tuned at both spatial and temporal scale. Under such environment, the abnormal detection and spatial localization will be much difficult. Furthermore, it becomes nearly impossible to diagnose when multiple abnormalities appear in the operation. All these require extensive investigation in future study.

11210719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210719.value: DPS is a high-dimensional process that is described in partial differential equations. Modeling of such a system is very difficult because this system has spatial and temporal dynamics strongly coupled, let alone the detection and localization of abnormalities occur in the system. Traditional modeling method either relies on more sensors, known as data-based, or completely known equation of the process, known as analytical. Novel approaches, such as, structure embedded approach is designed to improve data-based approach, and the spatial construction approach is developed to integrate both data-based and analytical methods. Based on the modeling methods developed, the effective method can be developed to detect the spatial abnormality occurred and localize it in the system. Application of these development have been successfully demonstrated in the battery thermal system.

11210819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11210819.value: 可穿戴式傳感器由於其在工業機器人技術中的潛在應用而引起了極大的關注，他們會讓智能機器或機器人像人類一樣有觸覺。然而，大多數報導的皮膚傳感器，主要是基於矽的MEMS，需要復雜且昂貴的製造程序，並且不可弯曲而不能适合穿戴。在這個項目中，我們將開發一種可穿戴式皮膚傳感器，使用簡單、可擴展且經濟高效的方法制备类似人类皮肤的电子传感器，用于工业機器人电子皮膚，像人类皮肤一样感知外界壓力。我們提出了一種新穎的分層結構薄膜壓阻式皮膚傳感器，它可以直接適應于機器人的指尖皮肤，以感知物体表面紋理。所提出的分層結構的壓阻層比傳統的扁平薄膜結構更好，因為它具有更大的表面積和高密度的分佈式受體，這對於感測表面紋理是必不可少的。此外，通過器件的优化設計和材料的選擇，可以優化分層結構的壓阻層的機械性能（即柔韌性）和穩定性，從而使得傳感器可以在粘附不同形狀的表面。我們的最終目標是開發一種模擬人類指尖感覺的可穿戴傳感器，通过測試传感器在与接触物體表面滑動時產生的摩擦力来測量表面粗糙度來感測紋理。所提出的傳感器將檢測由傳感器的外微結構與傳感材料表面之間的相互移动作用引起的摩擦力的變化。由於不同的表面紋理將與傳感器产生不同的相互作用，所以產生的不同信號圖案可用於“識別”紋理粗糙度。具體而言，我們的方法包括（i）開髮用於柔性，可穿戴和穩定的壓阻式傳感器層的複合材料，該傳感器層由石墨/聚二甲基矽氧烷複合物（GPC）和模擬指尖皮膚微觀圖案的聚二甲基矽氧烷（PDMS）基材，（ii）簡單和高產量地將GPC電阻層印刷成傳感器陣列（iii）制备GPC電阻層的分级微結構，以獲得大的表面積以提高靈敏度;（iv）理解皮膚傳感器對感知各種紋理的工作機制，即所謂的“機器人感知”現象。成功完成這些目標可以实现通過一種技术簡單，生产效率高和低成本用于“皮膚傳感器” 的複合材料製造新工藝。為了成功實現這些目標，我們將在三年內解決以下關鍵技术难题：（i）技术參數优化，印刷法制备GPC微观薄膜阵列，优化（石墨/ PDMS複合材料）電阻層陣列的穩定性，機械靈活性和耐久性，用於产品質量控制; （ii）对器件的靈敏度，檢測限（LOD），響應時間，操作穩定性和動態頻率響應进行系统表征; （iii）在不同溫度，濕度下的器件性能，以及不同弯曲、扭曲度下的傳感器的机械性能; （iv）基於GPC的傳感器的溫度响应，进行理論和實驗分析，以校正傳感器的不同温度下的检测准确度; （v）闡明微結構傳感器在感測表面紋理中的基本機制，以拓展指尖皮膚傳感器的應用潜能。我們堅信，该项目中我們所提出的機器人指尖传感器，可用於感測壓力和紋理粗糙度等领域。中國香港和中國大陸有幾家小型工業企業正在尋求通过使機器人實現自動化的新技术，其中皮膚傳感器可以讓機器人感受到外界刺激，这也是該研究項目主要的研究范畴。

11210819.label: Realisation of objectives
11210819.value: 1. To develop mechanically flexible GPC (Graphite/PDMS Composite) materials as highly stable and durable resistive layers. First, the as prepared G/PDMS/NaCl composite ink was coated on the sandpaper template by blading method, followed by covering another piece of sandpaper on the top. Second, composite film with double-sided microstructures was obtained after thermal treatment and removal of sandpaper templates. Dipping the composite film into hot water under an ultrasonic bath for 2 h, NaCl sacrificial templates were removed and the G/PDMS composite film with porous structures inside the film and hierarchical microstructures on the surface (denoted as porous@microstructured) was obtained. The porous composite films with different porosities were prepared by adjusting the mass ratio between NaCl and PDMS. Meanwhile, the composite film with only porous structures (denoted as porous@planar) and composite film with only microstructures on the surface (denoted as microstructured only) were prepared for the reference devices. The fabrication procedures for these two kinds of films are similar with that of porous@microstructured composite film by using different template combinations, and more detailed fabrication procedures are illustrated in the experimental part. Third, PDMS prepolymer was coated on the sandpaper template. 2. To develop microstructured PDMS (Polydimethylsiloxanesubstrate) as the base substrate to mimic the micro-patterns of human fingertip skin. Fabrication of Microstructured PDMS substrate: First, the PDMS base mixed thoroughly with the curing agent at a base to curing agent weight ratio of 5:1 and placed in a gentle vacuum condition at room temperature to remove the air bubbles generated during the agitation process of mixture. The prepolymer was then coated on the sandpaper template (#120) with a blading method followed by covering ITO/PET film on top. After that, the prepolymer was thermal annealed at 100 °C for 1 h in a vacuum oven and the one side microstructured PDMS on ITO/PET (denoted as ITO/PET/PDMS) substrate was obtained after removal of the template. 3. To completely characterize the fingertip skin sensors, including their sensitivity, LOD (Limit of Detection), response time, stability, and dynamic frequency response. Compared to that of the porous@planar skin sensor, the device based on the sandpaper-templated without porous microstructures exhibits an improved pressure sensitivity, 46 kPa−1 in the pressure range of 0–120 kPa and 21 kPa−1 in the pressure range of 120–150 kPa, indicating that the hierarchical microstructures on the surface of the composite film play a significant role in boosting up pressure sensitivity of the skin sensor. To investigate the minimum detectable pressure of the skin sensors, the current responses to pressure were measured by loading/unloading a small grain of ormosia (≈50 mg). Furthermore, to investigate the response speed, the response and relaxation time of the skin sensor were estimated in the process of loading/unloading the small grain of ormosia. The frequency-dependent performance of the skin sensor under an applied force of 10 N (≈100 kPa) with three different loading frequencies (0.12, 0.20, and 1.10 Hz) has been further investigated. Notably, the current responsive signals closely follow the loaded force, and no obvious frequency dependence or delay is observed within the studied frequency range. Additionally, the skin sensor exhibits a robust durability in the process of loading/unloading a huge pressure of 100 kPa up to 25 000 cycles. 4. Demonstrate microsensor in mimicking the function of human fingertip skin for “texture feeling”. There are very few connections between the microhumps and ITO electrodes at the standby state; the friction force from the sliding process increased the conductive pathways, and the resistance of the device decreased simultaneously. To confirm this effectiveness, printing paper and sandpapers with different roughness (#800, #120) are chosen for the test. In the experiments, the skin sensor was affixed onto the index finger, and the finger was brought to the surface of the papers and moved from one side to the other. In this process, a gentle press force was applied on the sensor and the whole touch-move action takes 10 s from start to end. Due to the different friction forces generated in the sliding process with three different roughness, distinct patterns were obtained when the skin sensor slides across these three different surfaces. It is notable that, during the sliding process, the smooth printing paper gives the smallest current fluctuation of 52%, the sandpaper (#800) with the medium roughness gives an increased fluctuation of 240%, and the highest current fluctuation of 500% is observed for the sandpaper (#120), which has the largest roughness, indicating our skin sensor has the potential application for texture roughness recognition.

11210819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11210819.value: To obtain the stable and durable power supply, a self-powered piezoresistive pressure sensor is designed based on the redox reaction-induced electricity between the Al electrode and graphite/PDMS composite (GPC) electrode with the electrolyte participating. Meanwhile, inspired by the microstructures underlying the epidermis, the microstructured graphite/PDMS sensing films are laminated face-to-face mimicking the receptors under the epidermis to sense the external pressures which can deform the microstructures of the composite films and thereby changing the current output of the pressure sensors. This strategy endows the novel self-powered pressure sensor with the ability to detect not only the dynamic forces but also the static. Based on the redox-induced electricity and the double-layer structured composite geometry, the self-powered pressure sensors show remarkable device properties including an ultrahigh sensitivity (~103 kPa‒1) and a wide detection range (0.02‒30 kPa). Noteworthily, to our best of knowledge, redox-induced electricity based self-powered pressure/tactile sensors for simultaneous detection of both dynamic and static pressure is rare. Additionally, the device exhibits fast response/relaxation speed, outstanding durability, and excellent detection resolution as well. Benefiting from the excellent pressure-sensing performance, the pressure sensors are not only applicable to healthcare monitoring, human motion detection, communications, and e-skin, but also presenting a new insight into the development of high-performance self-powered flexible electronics as well (Part C, ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces, 12 (33), 37239–37247). In addition, we presented a large-scale facile and compatable bar-assisted printing method to achieve hierarchically microstructured polymer composite triboelectric film with good hydrophobicity to improve the electrical output performance and achieve the robustness of TENG. The electrical outputs of the TENG devices are tuned by imparting the graphite fillers into polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) with optimal concentration. The achieved microstructured graphite/PDMS composite based TENG supplies high and stable short-circuit current of 42 µA, open-circuit voltage of 410 V, and transferred charges of 160 nC under an applied force of 1.2 N, which are sufficient enough to power wearable sensors or charge the energy storage devices. The TENG devices can charge a 2.2 µf capacitor to 1.5 volts within 2 seconds, lighten 30 commercial green LEDs, and drive an electronic watch as well. Self-powered tactile sensing has also been demonstrated by attaching the TENG devices onto a rubber glove to monitor the process in grasping objects. Furthermore, a large-scale self-powered sensor array is fabricated and utilized to map the spatial pressure distributions. This work not only demonstrates a scalable fabrication of the hierarchically microstructured polymer composite films for high-performance TENGs with high electrical outputs, excellent durability and ambient stability, but also brings insight into the development of future cost-effective and self-powered electronics (Part C, Nano Energy, 80, 105521).

11210819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11210819.value: The proposed course of action will be using this devices for continuous monitoring of human pulse waveform for Chinese medicine practitioners, e-skin, and soft robotics call for large-area and robust energy-harvesting strategy to powering their embedded sensors and peripheral electronics. Triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) can be potentially used as an optimum option to energizing self-powered sensors and self-charging systems with proper electronics in place.

11210819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11210819.value: Flexible piezoresisitve pressure sensors obtain global research interest owing to their potential applications in healthcare, human-robotic interaction, and artificial nerves. However, an additional power supply is usually required to drive the sensors, which results in increased complexity of the pressure sensing system. With the help of redox-induced electricity, a bio-inspired graphite/polydimethylsiloxane piezoresistive composite film acting both as the cathode and pressure sensing layer, a neoteric electronic skin sensor is presented here to detect not only the dynamic forces but also the static forces without external power supply. On the other hand, we also demonstrate a large-scale facile and compatible bar-assisted printing method to achieve hierarchically microstructured polymer composite triboelectric film with good hydrophobicity to improve the electrical output performance and achieve the robustness of Triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG).

11211019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211019.value: Perhaps the most important challenge for high performance structural materials is the simultaneous achievement of high strength (withstanding large loads) and ductility (undergoing large deformation without fracture). Successes in this area lead to improvements in diverse applications, including transportation systems (energy efficiency/ energy absorption) and biomedical implants. Increasing strength normally implies decreasing ductility; making a material more difficult to plastically deform strengthens it but makes it easier to fracture. While there has been an explosion of interest in making ultra-high strength materials, most of these are brittle. An important strategy to overcome this is to open new pathways for the materials to deform at high stress. Two interesting experimental observations in the past few years suggest a novel path forward. That is, polycrystalline materials, where the grain size is of order 10 nanometers, have been seen to undergo diffusionless phase transformations and/or twinning at extremely high stresses (neither is seen in the corresponding bulk materials). Since these phase transformations change the shape of the material, they can relax stress and impart considerable ductility. This project is particularly current given these experimental observations and because, now, achievable ultra-high strengths mean that materials may be subject to stresses never before possible. This proposal addresses the fundamental mechanisms that control the ability of the material to access these ductilization routes, in order to harness them for the design of future structural metallic alloys. Our approach is multidisciplinary, combining ab initio methods for quantum mechanical accuracy, crystal symmetry, statistical mechanics, and continuum mechanics methods to determine phase stability and transition state methods to predict the competition between different diffusionless transition paths/rates as a function of both stress and temperature. Our own preliminary results demonstrate that the nature of these transformations may be manipulated at high stress. In many metals, the nature of the transformations (martensitic vs. twinning vs. dislocation plasticity) is controlled by the energetics of planar defects. Since our overriding focus is developing alloying strategies for ultra-high strength, transformation-ductilized alloys, we next predict how alloying affects phase transformations. We apply what we learn about the underlying transformation mechanisms and use this understanding to guide material development. Alloying provides the knob that allows us to tune the energetics and barriers that control which mechanisms dominate and thereby manipulate the stress where such mechanisms become important.

11211019.label: Realisation of objectives
11211019.value: 1. To develop a theory of and quantitative data for the relative stability of fcc and hcp phases for normally fcc metals as a function of the general (tensor) strain and temperature We developed a multi-scale theory based on non-linear elasticity and density functional theory to quantify the relative thermodynamic stability of phases under the effect of the entire stress tensor. The developed method is very general and can be applied to any material phases, any set of orientation relationship between the phases and any thermodynamic variables such as stress and temperature. The developed method is applied to Nickel to explain the fcc to hcp phase transformation under the application of stress that has been recently observed in experiments. The method is also applied to the bcc to hcp phase transformation in Iron and to explain the influence of non-hydrostaticity of stress on the transformation pressure and reconcile the scatter of transformation pressure in experimental observations. 2. To determine competitive fcc/hcp transformation and twinning paths, activation energies and strains and the critical planar fault energies as a function of the general strain and temperature. As mentioned earlier, our methodology is used to study the fcc to hcp phase transformations for basal and prismatic orientation relationships (not a limitation) typically observed in experiments. While the stresses required to stabilize a phase under the influence of stress in thermodynamic limits are studies, the activation energies and critical planar-fault energies are not studies owing to computational complexity. Reason: Completion of this scientific objective turned out to be much more complex than originally expected. This is simply because part of the work required was unprecedented, the scientific challenge exceed expectation, and the computational budget was beyond expectation when the budget was proposed. Note that we still intend to complete this science, but were unable to complete it within the time-frame of the proposal. 3. To develop quantitative data for alloying to control phase stability/transformation paths and build a theory for stress-driven, diffusion-less, phase transformation alloy design. As mentioned earlier the developed methodology is quite general and is applicable to study the influence of stress on phase transformations in any alloy system. This method thus paves way to the design of ductile alloys that can exhibit transformation induced plasticity and twinning due to the applied stress.

11211019.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211019.value: The primary objective in developing high-performance structural materials is to achieve both high strength (ability to withstand large loads) and ductility (capacity to undergo significant deformation without breaking). This can enhance various applications in, e.g., transportation systems (for improved energy efficiency and absorption) and biomedical implants. However, increasing a material's strength often results in reduced ductility, making it more prone to fractures. Despite significant interest in creating ultra-high strength materials, many remain brittle. To tackle this challenge, many researchers in the field have been investigating new ways for materials to deform under high stress. Recent experiments have shown that polycrystalline materials with grain sizes of around 10 nanometers can undergo diffusionless phase transformations and/or twinning at extremely high stress levels, unlike their bulk counterparts. These phase transformations change the material's shape, relieving stress and increasing ductility. This research is particularly relevant as advancements in ultra-high strength materials may subject them to unprecedented stress levels. In this project, the fundamental mechanisms governing a material's ability to utilize these ductility-enhancing pathways were examined, applying this knowledge to the design of future structural metallic alloys. A multidisciplinary approach was employed, incorporating ab initio methods for quantum mechanical accuracy, crystal symmetry, statistical mechanics, and continuum mechanics methods to determine phase stability. Allotropic phase transformations can be driven by the application of stresses in many materials, particularly in pressure-driven transformations. Recent advances in strengthening materials have enabled the application of very large shear stresses, expanding the stress space to six dimensions and making phase transformations dependent on crystal/grain orientation. A novel, multiscale approach based on density functional theory and guided by nonlinear elasticity was proposed for predicting the role of the entire stress tensor on phase transformations in grains of all orientations in any material. This approach focused on stress tensor-dependent allotropic phase transformations in iron at high pressure and ultra-fine grained nickel and titanium. The results were consistent with various experimental observations in these systems. In summary, a multiscale approach for exploring the effect of the entire stress tensor on phase stability, applicable to all materials systems, was proposed. This approach is density functional theory-based and guided by nonlinear elasticity calculations. As the strength of materials continues to rise through innovations in microstructure and alloy development, the role of shear stresses in inducing phase transformations becomes increasingly significant. This approach is validated by comparison with experiments for different allotropic phase transformations in iron, nickel, and titanium. In most practical situations, this approach can be applied through nonlinear elasticity calculations, with density functional theory calculations required only to determine higher-order elastic constants. This means the approach is efficient enough for application in material design and exploration, including balancing microstructure/alloying-based strengthening with phase transformation-based strategies for achieving high strength and high toughness.

11211019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211019.value: The proposed methodology and numerical framework can be extended via molecular dynamics methods using machine interatomic potentials for alloys, instead of computationally expensive density functional theory. This will enable us to explore systems of large size and compositional complexity and better incorporate the effects of temperature along with the stress tensor on phase transformations.

11211019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211019.value: We developed a multi-scale framework to compute the role of the entire stress tenor on the phase transformations in metals and alloys. The method is based on multiple scales starting from the atomic scale (quantum mechanical) to the continuum scale (non-linear elasticity). This work demonstrated how stress can drive phase transformations and twinning in materials, opening up novel pathways to understanding and engineer alloys with transformation and twinning induced plasticity. This is of high scientific impact both to academia as well as industry.

11211519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11211519.value: 邊緣計算中安全編碼的任務分配及編碼設計

11211519.label: Project Objectives
11211519.value: To study the optimal task allocation and coding design solution against untrusted and uncolluding edge devices without stragglers. We first study the case when edge devices can return the computation results in a timely manner. We take the resource constraints on edge devices into consideration and study task allocation and coding design to minimize the resource consumption while achieving information-theoretic security, i.e., none of edge devices can obtain the information on input matrices or result matrix. To study the optimal task allocation and coding design solution against untrusted and uncolluding edge devices with stragglers. In this task, we will study the impact of different options that a straggler may take to return results on decoding. We then study how to model the relationship between redundancy and computation time variance at edge devices in order to complete the task before its deadline. At last, we will study task allocation and coding design to minimize the resource consumption while ensuring task deadline and achieving information-theoretic security. To study the optimal task allocation and coding design solution against untrusted and colluding edge devices with stragglers. In this task, we will study a more general case where edge devices may collude, which imposes higher requirement on random information inserted to the computation task. When all devices in the network may collude, it becomes necessary that the user node needs to keep a small portion of computation to itself, which adds more decision dimensions to the problem. We will tackle such challenges and study how to achieve information-theoretic security and meet the task deadline under the general case.

11211519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11211519.value: Edge computing utilizes distributed computing resources close to data instead of moving data to centralized computing powerhouses as that in cloud computing. Edge computing is the pain relief for a lot of applications requiring low response time. It, unfortunately, also opens a door to additional security headaches. In edge computing, computing resources may come from users' computers, IoT devices, and edge servers owned by different service providers. The heterogeneous nature of computing devices in edge computing imposes two challenges in adopting edge computing for computation. Firstly, edge computing devices may not be trustable, thus, protecting data confidentiality becomes a critical requirement in distributing tasks to edge computing devices. Secondly, some devices may not return the results in a timely manner as edge computing devices are often less powerful than servers in datacenters. In this project, we aim to tackle these two challenges with linear coding. Linear coding can achieve data confidentiality by adding random information to the original data before it is distributed to edge devices. Linear coding can tolerate some stragglers, i.e., the devices that return results much later than expected, by adding redundant information to the original data. To this end, it is important to carefully design code such that the user can successfully decode the final result once sufficient, instead of all, intermediate results are received from the edge devices. Meanwhile, task allocation, which selects a set of edge devices to participate in a computation task, affects not only the total resource consumption, including computation, storage, and communication, but also coding design. In this project, we study task allocation and coding design, two highly-coupled problems in secure coded edge computing, in a unified framework. In particular, we take matrix multiplication, a fundamental building block of many distributed machine learning algorithms, as the representative computation task. We study optimal task allocation and coding design to minimize resource consumption while achieving information-theoretic security and meeting the task deadline. Tackling fundamental problems in edge computing systems that have a broad range of real-world applications, this project will create a set of algorithms and carefully-designed linear codes that have theoretically provable optimality and practically verifiable performance for task allocation in different system settings. With the above research outcome, this project will make significant contributions in scientific research and tangible impact in industrial practice. 邊緣計算有別於傳統的雲計算，其利用分佈式的計算資源，使得數據可以就近被處理， 因此適用於很多實時性要求高的應用。邊緣計算同時也帶來了很多安全問題。在邊緣計算中，計算資源可能來自用戶的計算機，物聯網設備，以及不同運營商的邊緣服務器。這些構成邊緣計算的設備的異構性帶來了兩個新的挑戰。首先，邊緣計算設備可能不可信，因此保護數據的安全變得非常必要。其次，邊緣計算中的計算節點的計算能力參差不齊，有些節點未必能及時返回計算結果。本項目擬通過線性編碼來解決這兩方面的挑戰。 線性編碼在數據分發給邊緣設備之前可以通過加入一定的隨機信息達到數據安全的目的。線性編碼也可以通過加入冗餘信息來容忍一定的返回計算結果慢的節點。為了實現上述兩個目標，一是要設計編碼使得用戶一旦收到足夠的中間結果就可以正確解碼， 二是要進行任務分配，即決定選擇哪些邊緣設備參與計算。任務分配不僅影響計算、存儲、及傳輸資源的消耗，也影響編碼的設計。本項目中， 我們將在統一的框架下研究安全邊緣計算中任務分配及編碼設計這兩個互相影響的問題。具體來說，我們以許多分佈式機器學習的基本模塊，矩陣運算， 為例，研究能達到數據安全且滿足任務所指定的完成時間需求的最優的任務分配及編碼設計。 研究邊緣計算中的這些基本問題不僅具有理論價值，也將對安全並可靠地使用邊緣計算提供應用上的建議。

11211519.label: Realisation of objectives
11211519.value: The first objective is to study the optimal task allocation and coding design solution against untrusted and uncolluding edge devices without stragglers. It aims to take the resource constraints on edge devices into consideration and study task allocation and coding design to minimize the resource consumption while achieving information-theoretic security, i.e., none of edge devices can obtain the information on input matrices or result matrix. This objective is achieved through papers in Part C 8(1), Part C 9(1), and Part C 9(5). In Paper (Part C 8(1)), to minimize resource consumption while achieving information-theoretic security, we investigate two highly-coupled problems: (1) task allocation that assigns data blocks in a computing task to edge devices and (2) linear code design that generates data blocks by encoding the original data with random information. Specifically, we first theoretically analyze the necessary conditions for the optimal solution. Based on the theoretical analysis, we develop an efficient task allocation algorithm to obtain a set of selected edge devices and the number of coded vectors allocated to them. Using the task allocation results, we then design secure coded computing schemes, for two cases, (1) with redundant computation and (2) without redundant computation, all of which satisfy the availability and security conditions. Moreover, we also theoretically analyze the optimization of the proposed scheme. In paper (Part C 9(1)), we use communication cost instead of communication load and take matrix multiplication as the computing tasks to study the problem of secure matrix multiplication in edge computing with minimum communication cost (SMC). Specifically, we first theoretically analyze the security and decodability conditions of SMC to get the maximum number of matrix multiplication tasks stored on each edge device. Then we propose a scheme, i.e., Minimum Communication cost Secure coded Edge Computing (MCSEC), which adopts dynamic allocation and linear coding methods to allocate the matrix multiplication tasks to multiple edge devices and complete the coding design to satisfy the requirement of information-theoretic security (ITS), respectively. Moreover, we prove that the MCSEC achieves minimum communication cost by using constructive and logical analysis methods. Furthermore, in Part C 9(5), we consider the storage resource limitation of heterogeneous edge devices and propose PCHEC, a Private Coded computation scheme for Heterogeneous Edge Computing, to protect the user’s privacy and minimize the communication load. Specifically, PCHEC first gives a storage allocation scheme to minimize the communication load in edge computing where the heterogeneous edge devices have different storage limits. Secondly, PCHEC utilizes linear coding to mix the target data with other information for the protection of the user’s privacy. To evaluate the efficiency of PCHEC, we make theoretical analysis and conduct extensive simulations. The experiments show that PCHEC effectively reduces the communication load by up to 70% compared with other schemes. The second objective is to study the optimal task allocation and coding design solution against untrusted and uncolluding edge devices with stragglers. This objective is achieved through papers in Part C 9(4) and 9(6). In paper Part C 9(4), we investigate the problem of matrix factorization in distributed computing systems with stragglers, those computing nodes that are slow to return computation results. A computation procedure, called coded Alternative Least Square (ALS), is proposed for mitigating the effect of stragglers in such systems. The coded ALS algorithm iteratively computes two low-dimensional latent matrices by solving various linear equations, with the Entangled Polynomial Code (EPC) as a building block. We theoretically characterize the maximum number of stragglers that the algorithm can tolerate (or the recovery threshold) in relation to the redundancy of coding (or the code rate). In addition, we theoretically show the computation complexity for the coded ALS algorithm and conduct numerical experiments to validate our design. In paper (Part C 9(6)), we propose DALS-MC (Distributed ALS Matrix Completion), a coding-assisted algorithm for distributed matrix completion. We analyze the trade-off between the maximum tolerable number of stragglers (recovery threshold) and coding redundancy (code rate), along with computational costs. Moreover, we prove that incomplete matrices satisfying the Restricted Isometry Property (R.I.P.) condition can recover original values. Objective 3 is to study the optimal task allocation and coding design solution against untrusted and colluding edge devices with stragglers. This objective is achieved through papers, part C 9(2), 9(3), and 8(2). In paper C 9(2), we design an efficient scheme to ensure the information-theory security (ITS) of user’s data and further reduce the total cost of edge systems against cooperative attacks. Specifically, we take matrix multiplication as an example. We theoretically analyze the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of feasible scheme and prove the security and decodeability of the proposed scheme. We also prove the effectiveness of the proposed scheme through considerable simulation experiments. Compared with the existing schemes, the proposed scheme further reduces the total cost of the edge system. The experiments also show a trade-off between storage and communication. To reactively cope with collusion attacks, we also develop schemes to verify the correctness of results and identify attackers. Specifically, in Part C 9(3) and Part C 8(2), we propose an efficient verification scheme, namely Decode-and-Compare (DC), by leveraging both the coding redundancy of edge devices and the properties of linear coding itself. To design the DC scheme, we conduct a solid theoretical analysis to show the required coding redundancy, the expected number of decoding operations, and the tradeoff between them. To evaluate the performance of DC, we conduct extensive simulation experiments and the results confirm that the DC scheme can outperform existing solutions, such as homomorphic encryption and computing locally at the user device.

11211519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211519.value: This project thoroughly studied task allocation and coding design for secured coded edge computing under different settings. In particular, we have considered various constraints in resources in terms of storage, computation, and communication. For attack models, we have considered the cases where each edge device can be a passive attacker or compromised by a passive attacker independently or collusively. We have considered the tasks for matrix multiplication, matrix factorization, and matrix completion, which are widely used in machine learning applications. Last but not least, we have considered the straggler cases where edge devices may not return computation results on time. In different settings, besides designing algorithms for task allocation and code design, we have theoretically analyzed security, decodability, and computational complexity of the proposed algorithms. Comprehensive simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed solutions. This project provides a holistic view of the tradeoff among code redundancy, the number of stragglers, and security, which is essential for adopting edge computing securely. The research outcome has been published in top journals such as IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing and top conferences in information theory such as IEEE International Conference on Information Theory. One Ph.D. student is supported and trained by this project.

11211519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211519.value: With the potential stragglers and collusion attacks, verifying the correctness of both intermediate and final results is crucial. However, the existing works on verification in coded edge computing always verify and directly discard all incorrect intermediate results. One potential direction for further development will be to develop effective partial decode and compare verification schemes, which can fully utilize the correct part in the incorrect intermediate results to reduce the complexity and tolerate more abnormal edge devices. We are currently investigating this issue.

11211519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211519.value: In edge computing, computing resources may come from users' computers, IoT devices, and edge servers owned by different service providers. The heterogeneous nature of computing devices in edge computing imposes two challenges in adopting edge computing for computation. Firstly, edge computing devices may not be trustable. Thus, protecting data confidentiality becomes a critical requirement in distributing tasks to edge computing devices. Secondly, some devices may not return the results in a timely manner. In this project, we study task allocation and coding design, two highly-coupled problems in secure coded edge computing, in a unified framework. We study optimal task allocation and coding design to minimize resource consumption in terms of storage, computation, and communication while achieving information-theoretic security and meeting the task deadline. Tackling fundamental problems in edge computing systems that have a broad range of real-world applications, this project has developed a set of algorithms and carefully designed linear codes that have theoretically provable optimality and practically verifiable performance for task allocation in different system settings. With the above research outcome, this project will make significant contributions to scientific research and have a tangible impact on industrial practice.

Long-term ground measurement is the most effective way of establishing databases for solar radiation and daylighting. Many places offer no measured solar irradiance and daylight illuminance data. Through sensitivity analysis, it was found that diffuse fraction, clearness index, turbidity, sunshine duration, visibility, cloud cover and solar altitude are important parameters for classifying the standard skies [Conference Paper 4, Journal Paper 6]. One of such sustainable energy-efficient measures is bioclimatic architecture which elaborates the investigation of the climate as it adopts to architecture for enhancing the health and comfort of building users via the use of low passive energy technologies, appropriate design components and techniques to monitor the thermal transfer process. Building energy use is largely for creating a thermally and visually comfortable built environment via air-conditioning and electric lighting. Solar energy is regarded as the most important resource for generating power. For assessing passive energy-efficient designs and active energy production, solar radiation on building facades and building integrated solar panels and daylight illuminance penetrated to building interiors are crucial. The study of bioclimatic architecture depicts useful information to lower building energy use and support to develop appropriate meteorological databases for various climates [Journal Paper 2]. The building energy-efficiency and photovoltaic applications have been studied [Conference Paper 3].

11211719.label: Major findings and research outcome
11211719.value: Luminous efficacy can generate daylight illuminance data from the corresponding solar irradiance. A systematical review of this approach was conducted. Information on model evaluation metrics, comparative models and modeling techniques were identified [Journal paper 1]. The direct normal irradiance (DNI) and vertical global irradiance (VGI) data are important to active solar energy facilities and passive energy-efficient building designs. Simple empirical and DNI is relevant in estimating vertical global irradiance needed in BIPV output analysis [Conference Paper 3]. For VGI, two models namely sunlit and shaded surfaces were modeled. To estimate VGI for sunlit surface, correlations of vertical direct irradiance (VDI) over VGI and reflected global irradiance (RGI) over VGI with solar altitude and incidence angle, and clearness index (Kt) were carried. RGI/VGI was correlated with incidence angle and Kt for shaded surface and good predictions were obtained. [Conference paper 2]. Studies presented findings from measured horizontal global, direct and diffuse luminous efficacies under Representative Skies 1, 8 and 13 and 15 CIE standard skies [Conference Paper 1, Journal Paper 5]. By using the developed vertical luminous efficacy model and solar irradiance data, VDI for the four principal orientations were estimated. The approach can provide means of deriving illuminance data, particularly for places within the subtropical climate. ML techniques were adopted to estimate vertical luminous efficacy model which was used to predict the VDI. The findings showed that scattering angle and diffuse fraction had the most influence on the model’s performance. The findings showed that acceptable daylight predictions can be obtained from all proposed models [Journal Paper 3]. An approach for modeling diffuse and global luminous efficacies using accessible measured climatic data was developed. The methodology explored ML, sensitivity analysis and empirical modeling approaches covering all-sky, overcast and non-overcast sky conditions. The ML models gave better predictions of daylight illuminance but the results of the empirical models are quite promising [Journal paper 4]. Through sensitivity analysis, it was observed that diffuse fraction, clearness index, turbidity, solar altitude, sunshine duration, visibility and cloudy cover are important variables for classifying the standard skies. [Conference Paper 4, Journal Paper 6]. Bioclimatic design can reduce building energy use and the best form of practice should be adopted in the Architecture, Engineering and Construction sector to get optimum results. The overall trend in bioclimatic architecture and mapping out areas for future studies was achieved [Journal Paper 2].

11211719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11211719.value: The requisite solar radiation and daylight illuminance data on variously oriented horizontal, inclined and vertical planes can be determined under different sky conditions. The next step would be the generation of appropriate solar radiation and daylight illuminance datasets such as the typical weather year with classified standard skies for further building façade design study and evaluation. Apart from Hong Kong, the models can be applied worldwide for various climates. Building integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) panels such as opaque and semi-transparent can provide electricity and apt to daylighting schemes that enhance visual comfort, reduce peak electrical and cooling demands, and conserve building energy expenditures and are appropriate building facades for high-rise office buildings. The building energy, thermal and visual performance will be computed via building energy simulation software and numerical approaches using the comprehensive weather database. Parametric studies will be conducted to identify the appropriate approaches to achieve net zero energy and net zero carbon buildings while maintaining occupant comfort and environmental sustainability. The energy payback period will be determined to know the time taken for the recovery of the investment. An optimal building façade design in terms of such energy, environmental, comfort and financial aspects will be conducted.

11211719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11211719.value: Solar irradiance data are a prerequisite for designing solar electric and solar thermal facilities. Data about daylight illuminance and solar irradiance on vertical surfaces are in great demand, particularly for high-rise curtain wall buildings. Long-term data measurement is the most effective and accurate way of setting up such databases, whereas short time-interval data would be more appropriate for examining dynamic variations. However, most places do not measure solar data, or offer only daily global components covering limited periods. Necessary components are commonly estimated from latitude–related data and climate-related parameters. Regression techniques are usually adopted to form the empirical models, but these underperform for modelling nonlinear correlations. To overcome some of these difficulties, the International Commission on Illumination (CIE) has adopted a list of 15 standard skies. The well-defined sky radiance and luminance pattern mathematical equations can be used to compute solar irradiance and daylight illuminance on inclined surfaces and variously oriented vertical planes. Machine learning ML algorithms have been used to obtain more accurate output results. This project used ML techniques for analysing active solar energy applications and passive building designs to improve upon solar irradiance and daylight illuminance prediction models and the categorisation of standard skies.

11212119.value: 由於手繪草圖的易用性和豐富表達性，它們被廣泛使用於檢索或構建三維模型。另一方面，已有的三維模型也可以被用來幫助做有語義的草圖理解。然而這些任務是極具挑戰性的，主要是因為手繪草圖和三維模型有著顯著不同的形狀表示，並且存在於不同維度的空間。為了解決這些問題，比較常用的方法是用一些特定的非真實渲染算法把三維模型渲染成二維線條畫。然而這些渲染出來的線條畫同手繪草圖在抽象程度和藝術表現手法方面是很不一樣的，而且後者還有經常發生的形狀或尺度上的形變。 這個項目致力於建立手繪草圖和三維模型的聯繫，主要是通過去觀察和分析一般用戶（非藝術家）怎麼樣針對一個三維物體創作手繪草圖。我們的目標與一個已有工作[Cole et al. 2009]比較類似，但是他們的重點是研究專業畫家的素描結果。儘管他們的工作得到了一些有意思的研究發現，但是由於他們聚焦於專業畫家，而且他們最後收集的素描數目較少，他們的工作不能直接用於基於一般用戶所畫草圖的應用。我們計劃通過眾包的形式去構建第一個較大規模的手繪草圖庫，其中每個草圖都有對應的三維模型。由於經費上的限制，要求我們需要更加小心地挑選需要被包含的三維模型以及其視角，使得最終的數據集可以包含盡可能多的信息，能用於許多應用中。為了更好地理解手繪草圖和三維模型之間的關係，我們會對收集來的草圖從時空以及不同尺度進行分析。 我們的研究預計會對非真實渲染以及依賴手繪草圖的應用發展帶來幫助以及新的研究角度。科學地理解手繪草圖和三維模型之間的關係使得我們可以通過基於實例的方法來針對三維模型合成類似手繪草圖的效果，這個是極具挑戰的、還欠缺探索的課題。基於實例的草圖合成不僅讓我們更好地抽象表達已有的三維模型，而且提供了一個有效的數據增強的方法，可以用於需要大量數據做訓練的基於深度學習的相關應用中。我們計劃研究多個實用的應用，包括細粒度基於草圖的三維形狀檢索、有語義的草圖分割、草圖美化、草圖到三維模型的合成、三維模型到草圖的合成等。我們最後會開放我們的數據集以及相關的工具，希望讓更多人受益於此研究項目。

11212119.label: Realisation of objectives
11212119.value: We have fully achieved all the objectives. We started to explore the proposed ideas based on an existing dataset (i.e., OpenSketch) and our own datasets for additional categories like animal-like heads and 3D hair models. Then, we collected our own large-scale and more general-purpose sketch-model dataset. [Multi-view Sketch Analysis.] In [Deng et al. TCSVT 2021], we addressed the gap between sketches depicting the same objects from different viewpoints and proposed a deep learning solution to learn a novel local descriptor from data (Objective 4). Our novel training dataset (Objective 1) contains multi-view line drawings synthesized from 3D models (Objective 3) with pixel-level correspondence. The effectiveness of our method has been evaluated on OpenSketch and our own set of multi-view freehand sketches (Objectives 1 and 5). [3D Modeling from 2D Sketches.] To bridge the 2D and 3D domain gap between 2D sketches and 3D models, we explored deep learning-based solutions for generating 3D models from 2D sketches (Objective 4). In [Du et al. TVCG 2022], we focused on 3D modeling of animal-like character heads, enabled by a novel approach based on Graph CNNs, trained on a novel dataset of sketch-3D model pairs (Objective 1). To model diverse facial shapes and rich geometric details, we presented SketchMetaFace [Luo et al. TVCG 2023], a sketching system targeting amateur users to model free-style and high-fidelity 3D faces in minutes. In [Shen et al. TVCG 2021], we focused on modeling 3D hair from 2D freehand sketches (Objective 4) by contributing to a large-scale dataset of 3D strand-level hair models with corresponding multi-view sketch maps (Objective 1). Extensive evaluations showed our method’s robustness against input sketches and view changes and the advantages of our multi-view sketch-based modeling method over state-of-the-art single-view sketch-based or image-based hair modeling methods (Objective 5). We extended this idea to support 3D modeling of a wider range of objects through iterative multi-view sketching [Zhou et al. CGF 2023]. To facilitate structural analysis at the early sketching phase, we introduced Sketch2Stress [Yu et al. TVCG 2023-J17] to allow users to easily examine the stress sustained everywhere and thus identify potential problematic regions of their sketched objects. Knowing that our models are category-specific, we explored vector sketch recognition based on an RNN-Rasterization-CNN architecture [Li et al. TVCG 2021]. This method allows the automatic identification of sketched object categories, thus potentially enabling a unified system for handling different object categories. [Sketch Refinement.] To address the gap between rough sketches and perfect line drawings, we proposed to synthesize refined sketches given rough sketches based on the shape space learned from line drawings (Objective 3). This idea was experimented with to synthesize realistic face images from rough and/or incomplete sketches [Chen et al. TOG 2020]. This approach allows the use of sketch inputs as soft constraints and outperforms the existing approaches (Objective 4), which require quality sketches as input (similar to line drawings). Later, we extended this idea to beautifying sketches of man-made objects [Yu et al. TVCG 2023-J16]. [Sketch-based Face Generation and Editing.] Following the success of DeepFaceDrawing [Chen et al. TOG 2020], we developed a series of sketch-based systems (Objective 4) for face generation and editing with disentangled geometry/appearance control [Chen et al. TOG 2021] and precise geometry control [Su et al. TVCG 2023], face editing in portrait videos [Liu et al. TOG 2022], hairstyle synthesis [Xiao et al. TOG 2021] (Objective 4). To handle complex geometry and structure in various hairstyles, we constructed a novel dataset of 4,000 pairs of hair images and sketches (Objectives 1 and 2). Various experiments were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed techniques (Objective 5). Although these systems could generate photo-realistic face images or videos, they can only produce 2D face results. Inspired by the recent advances in neural radiance fields (NeRFs), we explored disentangled 3D-aware face generation and editing in NeRFs. We proposed SketchFaceNeRF [Gao et al. SIGGRAPH 2023], a novel sketch-based 3D facial NeRF generation and editing method to produce free-view photo-realistic images. Our NeRFFaceEditing system [Jiang et al. SIGGRAPH Asia 2022] allows users to utilize a reference image and a semantic mask in certain views to edit appearance and geometry, respectively, while maintaining 3D consistency. [3D Sketching in AR and VR.] To bridge the gap between 3D sketches and 3D models, we also performed studies on how people with little drawing skills sketch 3D objects (Objective 2) by tracing real-world objects in mobile AR [Ye et al. TVCG 2022]. We performed elicitation studies to understand how users use AR-enabled mobile phones as 3D pens. We also conducted quantitative studies to understand tracking errors under different combinations of input point and grip types. We performed a formative study to compare two-handed interactions with tablet-pen interaction for VR sketching. Based on the findings of this study, we designed HandPainter [Jiang et al. CHI 2021], a VR sketching system that focused on using two hands for 3D sketching. [3D Modeling and Animation from 3D Sketches.] We showed that such 3D sketches could benefit various applications, including 3D curve creation, 3D measuring, and 3D animation. Observing that 3D sketches are effective in depicting 3D coarse shapes while 2D sketches are more suitable for controlling geometric surface details, we developed SimpModeling [Luo et al. UIST 2021], a novel two-stage sketch-based 3D modeling system focusing on 3D animalmorphic head design (Objective 4). Our solution relied on recent deep learning techniques. To train our model, we proposed 3DAnimalHead, the largest animalmorphic head dataset, containing 1,955 high-quality animalmorphic head models (manually created by artists), each with carefully annotated 3D contour curves (Objective 1). The usability and effectiveness of our system were supported by several user studies, including a usability study, a comparison study, and a perceptive evaluation study (Objective 5). We also introduced the first mobile AR system for creating 3D character animation using a single mobile phone [Ye et al. TOG 2020], which provides an easy way to specify a 3D motion path and motion gestures. [A More General-Purpose Sketch-Model Dataset.] In the above activities, we mainly focused on bridging the gap between sketches and 3D models for specific object categories, including animal heads, hairstyles, human faces. To better understand the domain gap between sketches and 3D models from a wider range of categories, we constructed DifferSketching [Xiao et al. TOG 2022] (Objective 1), a new dataset of freehand sketches to understand how differently professional and novice users sketch 3D objects. We invited 70 novice users (with limited drawing training/experience) and 38 expert users (with multiple years of professional drawing training/experience) to sketch 136 3D objects from 9 categories, rendered 2 or 3 representative viewpoints. This led to a new dataset of 3,620 freehand multi-view sketches, registered with their corresponding 3D objects under certain views. This dataset is an order of magnitude larger than the existing datasets. We analyzed the collected data at three levels (Objective 2), i.e., sketch-level, stroke-level, and pixel-level, under both spatial and temporal characteristics, and with and across groups of creators. The extensive analysis led to some interesting observations, which might inspire future research. To demonstrate the usefulness of our dataset (Objective 5), we explored two applications, namely, freehand-style sketch synthesis (Objective 3) and a potential benchmark for sketch-based 3D reconstruction (Objective 4).

11212119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212119.value: Compared to 3D models or their line drawing renderings, freehand sketches often exhibit drawing errors and depict objects from a single view or a limited number of views. We explored multi-view sketch analysis and sketch refinement by exploiting the knowledge in the collected sketch datasets. We showed that data-driven approaches can greatly benefit challenging tasks, including 3D modeling from 2D sketches and sketch-based generation and editing of face images and videos. We also examined the gap between 3D sketches and 3D models by developing novel interfaces that enable novice users to create 3D sketches in mobile AR or VR and showed the application of 3D sketches to data-driven 3D modeling and 3D character animations. The key enablers of the above techniques are our collected sketch datasets, which are released to the research community to inspire further research. In total, this project led to 17 journal publications and 3 peer-reviewed conference papers have been produced by PI’s own team and collaborators. The Co-I of this project made significant contributions to two of these papers [Yu et al. TCSVT 2021 and Xiao et al. TOG 2022]. Among them, 7 were published in ACM Transactions on Graphics (the best graphics journal), and 8 in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics (the second-best graphics journal). 8 papers were presented at SIGGRAPH or SIGGRAPH Asia (the best graphics conference), and 2 papers were presented at the top HCI conferences (CHI and UIST). Our research received the Silver Medal at Special Edition 2022 Inventions Geneva Evaluation Days (based on [Chen et al. TOG 2020]) and the 2021 Open-source Graphics Software Award (based on [Chen al. TOG 2020] and [Chen et al. TOG 2021]).

11212119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212119.value: This project has led to multiple sketch datasets, among which DifferSketching [Xiao et al. TOG 2022] is the most important dataset. To avoid wasting money on collecting useless or not very useful datasets, in the first half of the project period, we focused on exploring various applications by using existing datasets or creating datasets but for specific model categories. With the accumulated knowledge and experience, we constructed the main dataset (i.e., DifferSketching) in the project's second phase. We explored two applications, i.e., freehand-like sketch synthesis and a preliminary benchmark for sketch-based 3D modeling. While DifferSketching is an important dataset, its potential still needs more time to explore. We will enhance the currently collected sketches with additional data, e.g., segmentation map, depth map, stress map, normal map, etc. Such additional information will greatly help other researchers to explore various applications based on our collected sketches.

11212119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212119.value: Freehand sketches are often used to depict the shape and form of objects. While human viewers can easily perceive the underlying objects depicted by sketches, it is difficult to design algorithms to achieve similar tasks due to the domain gap between sketches and objects, resulting in ill-posed problems. Freehand sketches, particularly those by users with little drawing skills, often exhibit drawing errors, making it more difficult to infer 3D models from sketches. This project aims to investigate techniques to bridge the gap between freehand sketches and 3D models. We explored multi-view sketch analysis and sketch refinement by exploiting the knowledge in the collected sketch datasets. We showed that data-driven approaches can greatly benefit challenging tasks, including 3D modeling from 2D sketches and sketch-based generation and editing of face images and videos. We also examined the gap between 3D sketches and 3D models by developing novel interfaces that enable novice users to create 3D sketches in mobile AR or VR. We also showed the application of 3D sketches to data-driven 3D modeling and 3D character animations. The key enablers of the above techniques are our collected sketch datasets, which are released to the research community to inspire further research.

11212219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212219.value: Boiling, a common phenomenon in our daily life, is extensively employed in industry due to its excellent heat transfer performance. The classic pool boiling curves mainly consist of three distinct regimes: nucleate, transition, and film boiling. Among them, nucleate boiling is the most effective heat transfer method and has been widely applied in high-techs such as computer chips, electronic devices, and energy systems. As the technology advances, more efficient heat transfer over smaller surface areas, i.e. higher surface heat flux, is often required. However, the surface heat flux should be carefully controlled below the critical heat flux (CHF). Beyond that, boiling crisis will be triggered which sharply increase the wall temperature and would cause damages to the devices or systems. Therefore, it is essential to enhance the CHF in order to augment the limit of boiling heat transfer. It has been verified that the surface intrinsic wettability and surface structures have significant impact on the CHF and boiling heat transfer. Extensive researches have been conducted by different research groups around the world to improve the CHF through surface modifications. However, for those modified surfaces with hydrophilic nano/micro structures, the impact of surface wettability and structures on CHF are usually coupled together. To distinguish their individual impacts in order to better understand the underlying mechanism, it is worth conducting researches in decoupling them. In this research, surfaces coated with nanograss under different cover density will be used to compare with various hydrophilic surfaces through extensive experiments in order to identify the underlying mechanism of CHF enhancement for individual factor. In addition, some researches show that the surface orientation has very significant impact on the CHF. However, the research is still very limited on this topic and most of the research so far used smooth surface and the range of orientation angles is narrow. In this research, both bare substrates and the nanograss coated surface will be experimentally investigated and the orientation will change from 0° to 180° with an interval of 30°. A widely applicable correlation for CHF prediction of nanostructured surface under different orientation will be derived. Finally, to comprehensively understand the underlying mechanism of CHF, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations that study the boiling process from the nanoscale point of view will be carried out. It is strongly believed that with this technique, some atomic level information about CHF enhancement mechanism, which are unavailable using conventional method, could be obtained. 沸騰是我們日常生活中的一種普遍現象，由於其優異的傳熱性能，在工業中得到廣泛應用。經典的池沸騰曲線主要由三種不同的區域組成：泡核，過渡區和膜態沸騰。其中，泡核沸騰是最有效的傳熱方法，並已廣泛應用於計算機芯片，電子設備和能源系統等高科技領域。隨著技術的進步，通常需要在較小表面區域上進行更有效的熱傳遞，即更高的表面熱流密度。但是，表面熱流應小心控制在臨界熱流密度（CHF）以下以避免觸發沸騰危機，這會嚴重增加壁溫並對設備或系統造成損害。因此，必須增強CHF以增加沸騰傳熱的極限。 已經證實，表面固有潤濕性和表面結構對CHF和沸騰傳熱具有顯著影響。世界各地的不同研究小組已經進行了廣泛的研究，以通過表面改性來改善CHF。然而，對於具有親水性納米/微米結構的那些改性表面，表面潤濕性和結構對CHF的影響通常耦合在一起。為了更好地理解其潛在的機制來區分它們各自的影響，有必要進行解耦它們的研究。在這項研究中，通過大量實驗，將不同覆蓋密度下塗有納米顆粒的表面用於與各種親水錶面進行比較，以確定CHF增強個體因子的潛在機制。此外，一些研究表明，表面取向對CHF有非常顯著的影響。然而，該研究仍然非常有限，迄今為止大多數研究都使用了光滑的表面，並且取向角的範圍很窄。在這項研究中，裸基板和納米塗層表面將進行實驗研究，方向將從0°變為180°，間隔為30°。將推導出廣泛適用於在不同取向下對納米結構表面進行CHF預測的關聯式。最後，為了全面了解CHF的潛在機制，將進行從納米級角度研究沸騰過程的分子動力學（MD）模擬。利用這種技術，可以獲得一些關於CHF增強機制的原子級信息，這些信息是使用傳統方法無法獲得的。

11212219.label: Realisation of objectives
11212219.value: Experiments and numerical simulations are extensively conducted on the research objectives. All the three research objectives are fully achieved. 1. The research activities to achieve objectives 1 and 2 are summarized as below: i) Experiments An experimental setup for pool boiling is built in our lab. It mainly contains a rectangular water tank, copper heater block, immersed heaters, data acquisition system, high speed camera equipment, temperature control device, cooling system, heat insulation assemblies and supporters. The nanostructures on the surface are fabricated though the hydrothermal process. Dual-layer structures containing the nanograss as substructure and the nanoflower as the superstructures on the surface are tested. The intrinsic surface wettability can be adjusted though different fabrication process. The nanograss grown on the surface at room temperature is superhydrophilic. Exposing the surface to the vapor of a mixed solution, trichloro(1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluoroocty) silane: n-hexane=1:1000 (v/v), makes it superhydrophobic. With the same surface wettability (superhydrophilic or superhydrophobic), the effect of the nanostructures with different cover density on critical heat flux enhancement is investigated and analysed. Besides, for the surfaces with the same nanostructure, the effect of the surface wettability on the critical heat flux has been studied. The present study decouples the contributions of the intrinsic surface wettability from the hierarchical (dual-layer) structure on the boiling enhancement by growing nanograss as the substructure and the micro flowers with different cover density as the superstructure. The structured surfaces show maximum critical heat flux (CHF) enhancement by 68%. While for the multi-orientated (from 0° to 180°) substrates, the surface orientation will influence the boiling performance through different physical mechanisms. It discloses that the departure time and the thickness of the fully developed vapor film of the inclined surfaces increase with increasing surface orientation, resulting in impeded boiling performance of the downward-facing surface. Moreover, enhanced critical heat flux and heat transfer coefficient can be observed for the nanograss surface with the downward-facing orientations. In addition, new correlations regarding the downward-facing CHF prediction based on the horizontal CHF are proposed for the future multi-oriented surface design in advanced heat-transfer applications. ii) Numerical simulations In this work, the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) is employed to simulate the effect of surface orientation, wettability, geometric size, and subcooling of the downward-facing lower head on the CHF enhancement. It was found that for the downward-facing surface, the CHF increases with increasing surface orientation, while a vertical surface gives a slightly lower CHF compared to a near-vertical surface. Besides, the CHF for a downward facing surface increases with increasing wettability. The CHF performance of the near-vertical and vertical surfaces exhibits the largest improvement with decreasing surface contact angle. Moreover, it reveals that with an increased radius of the lower head, the CHF decreases for all curved surfaces, especially obvious for the inclination angle smaller than 90°. For a vertical surface, increasing the length of the heated surface has no obvious improvement on the CHF. This study also provides a discussion regarding the effect of subcooling on the CHF enhancement. It was found that the CHF increases with the increase of subcooling and the simulation results agree with the Elkassabgi-Lienhard and Zuber correlations. 2. The research activities to achieve objectives 3 are summarized as below: The boiling heat transfer enhancement using nanoengineered surfaces has been widely acknowledged but its performance and mechanism at the nanoscale remains to be elucidated. In this study, the effects of nanostructures on nanoscale water boiling heat transfer are investigated using nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations. The nanostructured substrates show great superiority over the perfect smooth surface. The bubble nucleation time is advanced and the heat transfer efficiency is enhanced on structured surfaces. Besides, the heat transfer enhancement differs on surfaces with different nanostructures with the same nanostructure volume. Through calculation, it is found that the solid-liquid interfacial area varies with the surface structure configuration and the square nanogroove case which achieves the best heat transfer performance among the nanostructured systems has the largest solid-liquid contact area. To prove the hypothesis that the heat transfer efficiency increases with the interfacial surface area, a solid-liquid-solid system is developed to measure the interfacial thermal resistance between the different solid surfaces and water molecules. The interaction energy per unit area is also calculated to explain the heat transfer variations. Results show that with the increment of surface area which adsorbs more water molecules at the interface could increase the interaction energy per unit area, thereby decreasing the interfacial thermal resistance. The results in this study could provide some insight into the nanostructure design to enhance the heat transfer involving boiling. A molecular dynamics study was adopted to investigate six biphilic surfaces with different hydrophilic/hydrophobic patterns. To the best of our knowledge, individual bubble behavior on biphilic surface was observed for the first time via molecular dynamics method. It was found that the bubble dynamics behaved differently when the wall temperature is 150 K and 200 K, respectively. In addition, the shape and volume of bubble could be controlled by designing the hydrophilic/hydrophobic patterns, and simulation results indicated that these patterns had significant effects on bubble inception temperature, film boiling temperature and evaporation rate. Also, an ever-present temperature and density difference were observed above biphilic surfaces, results shown that this difference helped to create a fluctuation and promoted horizontal heat and mass transfer, which in turn was considered to be favorable to bubble nucleation. In the end, different pattern designs were compared, results demonstrated that hydrophilic/hydrophobic pattern designing was important because heat transfer performance could be different even with the same hydrophilic to hydrophobic area ratio. A molecular dynamics study was carried out to deepen the understanding of boiling heat transfer over wettability thermo-responsive surface at the atomic level. In addition to the existing wettability switch mode, we also simulated a reverse mode whose wettability was hydrophilic at low superheat and hydrophobic at high superheat. The simulation results showed that wettability thermo-responsive surfaces under both switch modes were superior to wettability non-responsive ones especially the hydrophilic surface despite that it was thought to have a higher heat transfer efficiency, and the two switch modes themselves also had different heat transfer performance and characteristics. Moreover, three different thermo-responsive ranges were studied, results indicated that the switch range of temperature had an important impact on boiling, and an optimal switch range existed for the wettability thermo-responsive surface. In the end, the potential distribution, phase diagram and interfacial thermal conductance were discussed to further reveal the boiling mechanisms behind wettability thermo-responsive surfaces.

11212219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212219.value: A new understanding of the pool boiling mechanisms regarding the horizontal surface wettability and the hierarchical structure was achieved. Besides, a thorough investigation of the effect of the surface orientation on the pool boiling performance was carried out. New correlations were proposed for the benefit of the future predictions in terms of multi-oriented surfaces in advanced heat-transfer applications. The main conclusions obtained in this study are as below: 1. For horizontal substrate, the structured surfaces show better pool boiling performances than the plain surface. The superhydrophilic surfaces yield higher CHF as well as HTC than the superhydrophobic surfaces. While for the surfaces with different superstructure cover density but the same wettability, they show limited difference in the CHF enhancement. 2. The CHFs decrease with the increase of the downward-facing orientations for both the plain and the nanograss structured surfaces. However, the nanograss enhances the CHF of all the multi-orientated surfaces when compared with the plain multi-orientated surfaces. 3. For both the plain and nanograss structured surfaces near the CHF, the departure time and the thickness of the fully developed vapor film increase with the increase of the downward-facing orientation. 4. New correlations to predict the downward-facing CHF based on the horizontal CHF are proposed for the future multi-oriented surface design in advanced heat-transfer applications. 5. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are conducted for both nanostructure and plain surfaces. It is found that the heat transfer enhancement differs on surfaces with different nanostructures with the same nanostructure volume. The solid-liquid interfacial area, which plays a significant role for boiling heat transfer, varies with the surface structure configuration. The increases of the solid-liquid interfacial area will significantly improve the boiling heat transfer. 6. A molecular dynamics study was adopted to investigate six biphilic surfaces with different hydrophilic/hydrophobic patterns. It is found that hydrophilic/hydrophobic pattern designing was important because heat transfer performance could be different even with the same hydrophilic to hydrophobic area ratio. 7. A molecular dynamics investigation of boiling heat transfer over wettability thermo-responsive surface is conducted. It verified that he wettability thermo-responsive surface could harvest the advantages of both hydrophilicity and hydrophobicity, and the switch range of temperature had an important impact on boiling, and an optimal switch range existed for the wettability thermo-responsive surface.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212219.value: Boiling, a common phenomenon in our daily life, is extensively employed in industry due to its excellent heat transfer performance. The classic pool boiling curves mainly consist of three distinct regimes: nucleate, transition, and film boiling. Among them, nucleate boiling is the most effective heat transfer method and has been widely applied in high-techs such as computer chips, electronic devices, and energy systems. As the technology advances, more efficient heat transfer over smaller surface areas, i.e. higher surface heat flux, is often required. However, the surface heat flux should be carefully controlled below the critical heat flux (CHF). Beyond that, boiling crisis will be triggered which sharply increase the wall temperature and would cause damages to the devices or systems. Therefore, it is essential to enhance the CHF in order to augment the limit of boiling heat transfer. In this research, multi-orientated hierarchical structured surfaces coated with nanograss and microflowers are investigated extensively through experiments in order to identify the underlying mechanism of CHF enhancement. And, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations that study the boiling process from the nanoscale point of view are carried out. Some atomic level information about CHF enhancement mechanism, which are unavailable using conventional method, is obtained.
