11212519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212519.value: 癌症是導致死亡的第二大原因。在2018年，全球有近一千八百萬新症及一千萬人死於癌症。在香港，三成的死亡是由於癌症而造成的。而由於癌症發病率會隨著年齡的增長而迅速增加; 隨著香港人口老齡化，癌症的死亡率相應增加。百分之九十的死亡率是由於轉移性腫瘤擴散到新的非相鄰部位。當細胞轉移時，它們經常重塑腫瘤細胞周圍的細胞外基質(ECM)，然後通過血流遷移。緊密連接相鄰內皮細胞之間的間隙，並且調節通過血管內皮細胞進出血管的物質。侵襲性癌細胞只能通過改變緊密連接的結構和擠壓來進入血流。 由於腫瘤部位通常包含多種細胞類型，將癌細胞與正常細胞分離將會有助研究和靶向對腫瘤的治療。我們建議開發微工程，仿生三維（3D）平台，用於根據癌細胞的遷移特徵將癌細胞與正常細胞分離，並控制細胞如何通過小開口遷移。分離和研究癌細胞如何擠過小開口將導致更準確的癌症靶向治療，並且可能更好地控制腫瘤的入侵性。 支架中的微結構在研究體外癌細胞遷移和入侵中有著重要的作用，因為它們模擬體內的3D ECM和血管。開發不同尺寸，形貌和硬度的多層支架平台，用以研究不同類型的細胞從一層到另一層的遷移。在研究中將使用兩種細胞系，包括永生化的鼻咽上皮NP460細胞和惡性上皮細胞腫瘤NPC43細胞。鼻咽癌（NPC）起源於喉嚨最上面的區域，是一種高度入侵性和轉移性的癌症，分佈於東南亞和中國南方，並有著很強的種族遺傳性。由於鼻咽癌在早期的並無明確症狀，大多數患者在晚期才被診斷，難以治療。這些3D仿生平台提供精確控制的微環境，以分選出NPC細胞，用於早期檢測和治療。儘管其他報導的結果主要集中在2D培養皿或3D纖維基質上，我們建議開發預設好尺寸，佈局，硬度和蛋白質塗層的多層支架平台，以選擇性地將鼻咽癌NPC43細胞與上皮NP460細胞分離。能夠將癌細胞與正常上皮細胞分離將可能幫助藥物更有效地遞送至靶向位置，並幫助NPC和其他癌症的早期治療。 有著小開口模仿表皮的多空結構，和多孔膜下仿血管的溝槽的平台在研發當中。我們計劃使用一個三層仿生模型來模擬ECM結構，上皮多孔界面和皮下血管作為癌症轉移的微環境。通過跟踪穿過多孔膜並在溝槽中遷移的細胞，我們將能夠研究不同細胞的遷移和入侵行為。除此之外，我們也將研究孔徑，孔的形狀，引導結構設計和定向，以及化學塗層這些可能會影響細胞穿過概率的控制因素。這種仿生三維血管網絡也許和理解和控制腫瘤轉移中的細胞入侵有直接相關，將為未來治療鼻咽癌或其他癌症提供參考。

11212519.label: Realisation of objectives
11212519.value: Cell migration involves the movement of a single cell or collective cells in response to mechanical or chemical signals. Previous studies reported cell migration behaviors on two-dimensional (2D) platforms with various engineered topographies. However, 2D models do not accurately represent the microenvironment of tumors in vivo. With the additional vertical dimension, three-dimensional (3D) models can better reflect the microenvironment of living tissue in size, structure, and cell polarity. While cell migration is important in maintaining tissue health and homeostasis, unwanted migratory events are undesirable and can lead to metastatic cancer and inflammatory disease. Therefore, understanding cell migration is an important step in developing disease treatment. It is difficult to observe cell separation, invasion behaviors, and viability at the same time based on existing cell screening methods. For example, microfluidic devices have been used for high throughput cell screening. Although microfluidic devices provide a controlled physical and chemical environment, the work mostly focuses on the lateral migration of cells. In this project, with our proposed platforms, NPC cell separation efficiency could be monitored through tracking the traversing behaviors of NPC cells into narrow trenches from the top layer, which could be observed using bright field microscopy without additional complex immunofluorescence staining. In addition, tracking of single cell movement could be achieved, which provides a rapid and convenient way to analyze cell migration behaviors. The extracellular matrix (ECM) serves as a scaffold structure for cells in tissues. It consists of a 3D network of fiber-forming proteins, such as collagen, laminin, and fibronectin. The geometry and dimensions of the scaffold have big impacts on cell adhesion and migration. Based on these findings, a two-layer scaffold platform with three tunable factors was established, including overlay angles between the top and bottom layers, the trench depth of the top layer, and the topography on the bottom layer ridges, for cell separation. Herein, a two-layer scaffold platform was developed to mimic the ECM in the tissue. Using the microfabrication technologies, three designed elements were precisely controlled to form different surface contact areas for studying cell migration. In this project, platforms were developed to mimic the physical properties of ECM and to influence cell adhesion and migration. Nasopharyngeal epithelial (NP460) and carcinoma (NPC43) cells were used, and their movements were observed in real-time. The discrepancies of NP460 and NPC43 cells in cell motility, morphology, and traversing behaviors were examined. The scaffold platform was optimized to effectively separate NPC43 cells from NP460 cells. This result could potentially be used as a basis to develop early diagnosis and treatment methods for NPC tumors.

11212519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212519.value: A two-layer scaffold platform in PDMS with different control elements was designed to investigate whether different surface contact areas could influence cell migration behaviors in this project. The double-layer scaffold platforms consisted of two 15 μm thick overlying gratings with 40 μm wide ridges and 10 μm wide trenches. NP460 and NPC43 cells were cultured on the patterned platforms for 24 h, and their movements were captured for studying their migration behaviors. The two cell lines migrated differently on the scaffold platforms. NPC43 cells reacted more strongly to the different scaffold platforms designs compared to NP460 cells. When the overlay angle between the top and bottom layers increased, the cell traversing probability increased, as well as the cell separation efficiency. Cells could stay in the top layer trenches when the top layer was 15 μm thick. Introducing shallow grating structures on the bottom layer ridges attracted more NP460 and NPC43 cells to move into the 10 μm wide top trenches. The highest efficiency of separating NPC43 cells from NP460 cells was 92.3%, achieved with the top grating layer being perpendicular to the bottom layer, a 15 μm thick top layer, and 1 μm deep gratings on the bottom layer ridges. These results showed that NPC43 cells could be effectively separated from NP460 cells on the proposed platforms. If NPC43 cells are isolated, high throughput drug screening could potentially be implemented for early diagnosis and treatment of NPC. As indicated in Part C of this report, this project has resulted in 5 journal papers in top international journals, 3 presentations in top international conferences, 2 PhD students, and 4 awards from research conferences.

11212519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212519.value: Early cancer diagnosis and improved cancer therapy using technological innovations are important and helpful for cancer patients. Overall, the separation of cancer cells from normal cells helps improve the characterization of cell phenotype, diagnostic accuracy, and therapeutic efficacy. Existing cell separation technologies have low specificity and scale-up issues. Our development using microfluidic systems for cell separation have the advantages of low sample volume, high sensitivity, and higher portability. Such microsystems can be used for early disease diagnosis or treatment.

11212519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212519.value: We have designed and developed an in vitro two-layer scaffold platform to mimic the extracellular matrix of the tissue. Such platform will be useful to separate invasive nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC43) cells from epithelial (NP460) cells, which can provide early diagnosis or treatment of diseases. Three precisely controlled factors were designed to investigate how topographic cues affected migration of NP460 and NPC43 cells, including overlay angles between the top and bottom layers, various top layer thicknesses, and surface topography of the bottom layer ridges. As NP460 and NPC43 cells respond differently to the surrounding microenvironments, most NPC43 cells could move into the 10 µm wide trenches while NP460 cells stayed on the 40 µm wide top layer ridges. 11212919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11212919.value: 輻射冷卻空調具有熱舒適性高、能耗低、運行噪音小和空間需求小的優點。 但是，在炎熱和潮濕的亞熱帶氣候下，輻射冷卻面臨兩個重要問題: 製冷能力不足和易結露。 因為輻射冷卻板的空氣接觸表面與輻射表面為同一表面，所以這兩問題嚴重耦合：如果要增加製冷能力，就要降低輻射表面溫溫；但降低輻射溫度又會增加結露風險。反之亦然。 目前，輻射冷卻空調可實現的最大製冷能力一般小於100 W/m2，不能滿足在炎熱和潮濕氣候下150 W/m2的典型製冷需求。 為解決上述問題,，我們擬研發一類新的輻射冷卻機制，即解耦輻射冷卻。 核心技術是在輻射表面添加一層紅外高透、高熱阻膜，將輻射表面與空氣接觸表面進行物理分離，以削弱輻射表面的溫度控制與空氣接觸表面之間的聯繫。 這樣，可以將輻射表面溫度調節得足夠低,以提高製冷能力，又不會犧牲防結露風險。主要研究內容包括解耦輻射冷卻的傳熱過程，建立傳熱模型，評估低辐射环境下的熱舒適性。 本研究的最終目標是開發一種適用於炎熱和潮濕的亞熱帶氣候下的解耦輻射冷卻空調。

11212919.label: Realisation of objectives
11212919.value: Obj. 1: the DRC test rig was constructed. The test rig consists of a temperature control chamber with a dimension of 200×200×50 mm, a water-cooling unit and a data recording system. The chamber is made of an upper cooling surface, a lower heating surface and four inner wall surfaces. The external sides of the six surfaces are insulated using polyurethane foam to be adiabatic to the external environment. The upper cooling and the lower heating surfaces are coated by paint with an emissivity of 0.95 (close to the black body). The wall surfaces are coated by a thin nickel layer to have a low emissivity with approximately 0.05. The upper heating surface and the lower cooling surface can be regulated in the range of 5~75℃(±0.03℃) based on two Peltier cooling and heating elements, connected with a 57~75L/h water cooling unit. The heat flux through the heating and cooling surface is determined by multiplying a calibration factor with the electric voltage from the Peltier transducers. The air temperature (T_a) and humidity are measured with an SHT75 temperature and relative humidity sensor (±0.3℃,±1.8%RH). These four inner wall temperatures (T_wi, i=1~4) and the air-contact surface temperature (T_0) are measured with Omega Precision Surface Temperature Thermistors (±0.1℃). Obj. 2: We reviewed a number of materials according to their reported infrared transmittance and selected POF, PVC, BOPP, PET, and LDPE for infrared transmittance test. FTIR was used to test their transmittance and found that 20-micrometer POF, PVC, BOPP, and LDPE had the infrared transmittance over 80%. We chose LDPE membrane in our experimental studies. Obj. 3: We developed a heat transfer model for the decoupled radiant cooling unit using a two-flux method, which describes the relationship between the radiant cooling temperature and cooling power as well as air-contact surface temperature (indicating the capability of condensation prevention). We established the basic formulas and developed an efficient algorithm to solve the model. We coded the algorithm in MATLAB and validated it using the test data from the test rig. Results demonstrated that the model we developed could accurately describle the heat transfer process of the DRC. Obj. 4: The thermal environment built by the DRC was accessed using a thermal environmental model, which was developed based on the developed heat transfer model. The air temperature, mean radiant cooling temperature and the operative temperatrue were estimated using the environment model, based on which PMV was used to evalute the thermal comfort of the thermal environment. Results showed that the DRC can efficiently create comfortable thermal environment under different climate conditions even if the radiant asymmetry was slightly higher than that conditioned by a conventional radiant cooling system. Obj.4: A technical report was prepared to describe and explain the developed radiant cooling mechanism. The mechanism was also detailed in two PhD thesises together with four journal papers and two conference papers.

11212919.label: Major findings and research outcome
11212919.value: Through this research, we understand the principle of the AIRCU and investigate its application issues, including membrane material selection, membrane temperature estimation, the feasible radiant cooling surface temperature in different thermal environments, and the cooling capacity and thermal comfort under different humidity conditions. The main findings are summarized as follows: (1) The average infrared transmittances of the 20-μm-thick LDPE, POF and BOPP membranes are higher than 0.79 within the range 2–22μm, and they were suitable for the AIRCU to seal the dry air layer. (2) The developed two-flux heat transfer model can accurately estimate the membrane surface temperature and the cooling power of the AIRCU. Experiental studies showed that the overal error between the experimental measurement and model prediction was less than 5%. (3) In a typical office thermal environment with AUST= 26℃ and RH= 60%, the feasible cooling panel temperature range should be 5–16℃. The maximum cooling capacity improvement could reach 18%–159% when compared with conventional RCUs. (4) For the thermal environment created by the AIRCU with the cooling panel temperature inside [5, 20] ℃ and the RH inside [50%, 70%], the comfort zone has been identified when PMV is inside the range [-0.5,0.5]. The results showed that the operative temperature could be used as a thermal comfort index of the AIRCU, which should be maintained at approximately 25℃ for thermal comfort in the application. Overall, our experimental studies and numerical analysis show that the proposed air-layer integrated radiant cooling technique can significantly increase the cooling power while efficiently avoid condensation.

11212919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11212919.value: From the perspective of the HVAC system, both conventional RCU and AIRCU can only deal with the sensible load. The conventional RCU must be used together with an auxiliary cooling system, and the latter should deal with all latent load and partial sensible load. However, the enhanced cooling capacity of the AIRCU makes it possible to work together with a dedicated outdoor air system (DOAS) dealing with the latent load only. Therefore, the AIRCU decouples the control of the sensible and latent load, simplifying the operation of cooling systems and ventilation systems. Out future work will focus on the cooperation of the AIRCU with a DOAS and study its thermal environmental charateristics and energy performance.

11212919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11212919.value: This research develops a new type of radiant cooling technique with the core idea that the radiant cooling surface is decoupled from the air-contact surface, and thus increase the radiant cooling capacity without sacrificing the reliability of condensation prevention. The heat transfer model of the proposed radiant cooling panel has been estabilished and suitable membrane materials have been identified. Based on the heat transfer model, the thermal environment built by the proposed radiant cooling panel has been analysised and demonstrated to be suitable for application in hot and humid climates. Ultimately, this research identfies a new radiant cooling mechanism, which can solve the current problems of radiant cooling when applied in hot and humid climates. As radiant cooling can provide a better thermal environment and be more energy efficient than air-cooling, this research identifies a technique that can improve the thermal comfort and energy efficiency of buildings in such climates, thus enhancing building sustainability.

11213119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213119.value: Site investigation is indispensable to geotechnical practice. Interpretation of site investigation data leads to the expected ground conditions (e.g., spatial distribution of different soil/rock types) and geotechnical property design profiles that can then be used in geotechnical analyses and designs. Without proper site investigation or data analytics to produce reliable input parameters, the subsequent geotechnical analyses and designs are much less meaningful, and the construction projects might be subjected to significant risk, such as project delay and over-budget caused by an “unexpected site condition” (i.e., the actual ground conditions encountered during construction differ significantly and adversely from the site investigation results). For example, the “unexpected site condition” in the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong Express Rail Link project commissioned in 2018 caused a project delay of more than 2 years and an over-budget of HK$20 billion. Although the importance of site investigation is well-recognized, NO scientific or quantitative method currently exists for site investigation planning, including determination of the optimal locations and necessary number of investigation points (e.g., boreholes or cone penetration tests (CPTs)), number of specimens to be tested, and the locations and depths at which specimens shall be taken. Existing design codes around the world provide only conceptual principles for such planning. This project aims to develop machine learning methods that leverage on the multi-stage nature of site investigation and use innovative data analytic methods (e.g., compressive sensing (CS)) to analyze data obtained from previous stages (e.g., desk study or preliminary stage) and automatically make recommendations on planning of the current investigation stage (e.g., the optimal locations and necessary number of investigation points or specimens to be tested). The PI has performed preliminary studies for one-dimensional cases and obtained promising results. Major research components of the project include: (1) development of entropy-based methods to determine the optimal sampling locations, (2) development of CS-based methods to determine the necessary sample number, (3) calibration of the proposed methods using simulated and real data, and (4) development of computer software to facilitate application of the proposed methods. For the first time ever in geotechnical engineering, this project will provide quantitative and data-driven machine learning methods to facilitate informed decision-making in site investigation planning. It will also offer computer software to facilitate application of the proposed methods in engineering practices. The research outcomes will be beneficial to geotechnical practice worldwide and in Hong Kong specifically, where many large-scale infrastructure projects are currently in progress. 雖然地質勘探在岩土工程實踐中是必不可少的，但是目前還沒有科學或定量的方法來規劃地質勘探，例如如何科學地確定地勘鑽孔的數目和位置等。地質勘探不足是岩土工程項目的一個重大風險，常常導致項目的延誤和預算的超支。以香港高鐵為例：2014年香港高鐵超支200億港元，項目延誤2年。本項目將基於信息熵和貝葉斯壓縮感知，對稀疏地勘數據進行高效分析，開創性地開發一系列機器學習的方法，科學地確定地勘鑽孔的數目和位置。

11213119.label: Realisation of objectives
11213119.value: All project objectives have been successfully achieved. Smart sampling strategy has been developed for determining the optimal sampling locations and necessary sample number in geotechnical site investigation using Information entropy and Bayesian compressive sensing/sampling (BCS). The developed methods have been tested by simulated data and real field data and observations. They have also been applied to site investigation for different geotechnical problems (e.g., slope stability and soil liquefaction assessment). A computer software has been developed to facilitate application of the proposed methods. The project has resulted in publications of 25 papers in top journals, 6 conference papers (e.g., ASCE Geo-Congress 2020, 8ISGSR, ASCE Geo-Risk 2023), and training of four PhD students (see sections 7, 8, and 9, respectively). Some details on the developed smart sampling strategy are given in the following paragraphs. A smart sampling strategy based on information entropy has been proposed for delineation of slope subsurface stratigraphy and planning of geotechnical boreholes (Shi and Wang 2021, see Paper 1 in section 7). The developed method is data-driven, and it not only provides evolution of the most probable interpolation from sparse measurements and the associated interpolation uncertainties, but also adaptively determines the optimal locations of boreholes. Effectiveness of the proposed method was illustrated and validated through both a simulation example and a real case. It showed that the data-driven framework can automatically identify location of largest interpolation uncertainty within a multi-layered slope conditional on its outcrops, and that the associated stratigraphic uncertainty gradually reduces as borehole number increases. More importantly, the optimal number and locations of boreholes required for slope stability analysis is adaptively determined by the proposed method. The smart sampling method has been integrated with Voronoi diagram to determine the optimal sampling locations when there is no pre-existing data in geotechnical site investigation (Wang and Li 2021, see Paper 2 in section 7), and it has been applied to geotechnical investigation of subsurface shallow gas pressure (Guan et al. 2020, see Paper 3 in section 7). Comprehensive parametric studies have been carried out to investigate the influence of spatial variability in subsurface conditions on the minimum CPT or SPT number needed for satisfying an accuracy requirement of site investigation (Guan and Wang 2021a&b, see Paper 4&5 in section 7). In addition, a novel method is developed for determination of the efficient locations for a given number of CPT soundings in a 2D vertical cross-section during site investigation (Zhao et al. 2022, see Paper 13 in section 7). With the efficient CPT locations determined, spatial variability of soil properties can be efficiently and effectively characterized within a multilayer soil profile. This improves characterization of the spatial variability of soil properties and hence facilitates planning and execution of geotechnical site investigation and subsequent design of geo-structures. When there are no available pre-existing CPT data (i.e., the preliminary site investigation stage), the efficient locations for a given number of CPT soundings are shown to be those that are uniformly distributed along with the horizontal direction of the study area with an equal interval. Quantitative evidence is provided for the engineering practice of locating CPT soundings uniformly along with the study area. The smart sampling strategy developed has been applied to characterize spatial distribution of soil liquefaction potential in a vertical cross-section using SPTs (Guan and Wang 2022a, see Paper 19 in section 7) or CPTs (Guan and Wang 2022b, see Paper 20 in section 7). A high-resolution CPT data cross-section is interpolated from limited measurements using 2D BCS, while the location for an additional CPT is optimized using the information entropy-based method (Guan et al. 2022, see Paper 24 in section 7). When reliability level of the interpreted liquefaction assessment results does not meet the target and requires improvement, a self-adaptive process is triggered to perform additional CPT soundings at optimal locations (i.e. the locations with the maximum entropy reduction). Once the target reliability level is reached, the self-adaptive process stops. Using the proposed smart sampling method, the minimum number and optimal locations of CPT soundings are automatically determined for achieving a target reliability level of the liquefaction assessment results. The sampling strategy for liquefaction assessment have tested and validated using both simulated and field CPT data. The results show that the proposed sampling strategy is able to provide the optimal locations and minimum number of required CPT soundings.

11213319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213319.value: 電力以及航空航天工業的發展亟需提高能源的使用效率，這使得先進金屬間化合物合金的開發處在了材料科學研究的最前沿。L12型金屬間化合物具有很多獨特的高溫性能，如高熔點，低密度，高屈服強度以及良好的抗氧化能力，使其在高溫應用方面顯示出了巨大的優越性。除此以外 L12型金屬間化合物相也是構成目前商用高溫超合金的最為重要的組成相，顯著提高了超合金的高溫強度和抗蠕變能力。然而，之前的研究主要集中在Ni3Al二元合金，很少涉及到第三組元的添加。儘管這種“素”的Ni3Al合金可以進一步合金化處理，但是這往往造成了合金顯著的脆化。相比之下，我們最新的研究中發現了一種多主元(Ni,Co,Fe)3(Ti,Al,Fe)復合高熵納米相，這種納米相的加入可以同時提高材料的強度和塑性。更為重要的是，我們最近的研究發現這種塊體的復合高熵金屬間化合物 (HEIAs) 擁有了比傳統Ni3Al合金更為優越的室溫力學性能。儘管如此，我們仍然需要進行大量深入的研究對許多關鍵的問題與機制進行解釋，比如HEIAs的高溫相變行為，熱力學穩定性和高溫力學性能與機理等。因此，我們當前的研究計劃主要目的在于系統地研究HEIAs的高溫相變與微觀變形機制，同時建立起其與反常屈服行為和高溫蠕變行為之間的關係。我們將通過先進的實驗表征手段並結合理論計算與模擬，闡明合金化添加對HEIAs的高溫組織穩定性、反常屈服行為、氧化以及蠕變行為的影響。除此之外，濕度或氧氣誘導的室溫以及中溫脆性一直被認為是阻礙金屬間化合物高溫應用的另一個重要的因素。為此，我們將對合金化添加和加工工藝對HEIAs拉伸塑性的影響進行細緻的研究。該項目的成功實施將對HEIAs的成分-組織-性能之間的關係提供一個定量化的認識。該項目的成果對於加快新型HEIAs高溫結構材料的研發具有重要的意義，也將顯著提高先進飛機發動機及其渦輪葉片的能源轉化率和工程可靠性。

11213819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11213819.value: 新型低表面能材料的研發和荷葉表面結構的啟發共同促進了膜蒸餾（MD）應用中，膜抗潤濕性和超疏水性的研究發展。蓮花葉片通過表面塗層和分層微/納米雙內嵌式結構的共同作用實現了高接觸角，由此，膜表面改性的探索應運而生。初始階段，長鏈碳氟化合物模擬荷葉抗潤濕性廣泛應用於膜的化學改性過程。然而，長鏈碳氟化合物很難自降價，使用過程中容易造成生物體內積累和毒性傳播等潛在危險，近年來逐漸成為人們關注的焦點，同時，強調了開發對環境無害的更安全的替代材料的必要性。因此，非氟化分層微/納米結構改性膜和支化短鏈碳氟表面改性膜可以為當前的環境安全問題提供有效的解決方案。 在過去幾年中，我們一直在研究使用表面塗層，微/納米雙層結構，和單內嵌式結構製備應用於膜蒸餾的具有抗濕潤性的功能膜。最近，我們開始研發短鏈氟塗層和廣受材料科學領域關注的微圖案化技術，以製備新一代應用膜蒸餾的先進膜。在此，本課題組提出了從三個科學方面來進行研究改進抗濕膜及探討其對膜蒸餾運行影響的研究方案。 首先，我們建議在應用膜蒸餾的膜表面改性中使用高度支化的短鏈全氟烴基矽烷作為長鏈氟化基團的替代物，即全氟叔丁氧基的含氟矽烷。我們將應用紅外光譜分析（IR），掃描電子顯微鏡結合能譜分析（SEM-EDX）和X射線光電子能譜分析 (XPS)技術，以確定在膜蒸餾測試之前的耦合產物的產出率。同時，我們將使用表面微圖案化技術在膜表面來構建所需的微/納米圖形，以實現雙內嵌式結構，最終製備疏水疏油雙疏全能膜。其次，我們還將建立一個先進膜潤濕檢測系統，對潤濕機理進行系統性的研究。最後，將測試膜修復技術在長期膜蒸餾運行中的實用性。 膜潤濕是阻礙膜蒸餾順利長期運行和工業應用的主要問題之一，然而，膜潤濕和膜修復過程中的關鍵檢測技術依然不成熟。因此，該提案的成功實施將為應用膜蒸餾領域的先進膜研發及表面潤濕探索提供有價值的系統性研究，在此方向上進一步發展，將使極大的推動膜蒸餾商業化進程。

11213819.label: Realisation of objectives
11213819.value: During this reporting period, the PI and her research team have successfully addressed the problem of bioaccumulation of perfluoroalkyl acids and membrane fabrication/modification using non-toxic material, developed different advanced membranes that were tested in different feed scenarios, and achieved prosperous results towards membrane wetting control, thus successfully completed 1) advancing environmentally-benign membrane modification technology (objective 1) and 2) better understanding of the impact of membrane wetting on the physicochemical properties of the advanced membrane with different surface tension feeds and foulants (objective 2). Additionally, the PI and her research team is successfully develop advanced in-situ wetting and fouling detection system coupled with optical coherence tomography and air drop (objective 3) as well as towards prolonging membrane lifecycle by preventing wetting under optimum operational conditions and promoting membrane regeneration (objective 4). The details are as follows: 1. Objective 1 Research highlights under this point are summarized as follows: • We reported on the fabrication of superhydrophobic membrane surfaces by incorporating fluorous silica aerogels with branched short chain perfluoroalkyl groups, which can be safer and more environmentally benign alternatives than long PFASs. The membrane coated with fluorous SiO2 aerogel 1-(nonafluoro-tert-butoxy)-4- butyl-ethoxysilane (F1- SiG) with high fluorine content (62.4%) exhibited low surface free energy (1 mN m−1 ) and superhydrophobicity (water contact angle, CA: 151.4° ± 1.2°). The superhydrophobic membrane can maintain its stability even after 30 cycles of water abrasion, and when tested in MD, the F1-SiG100 membrane demonstrated a robust performance with a relatively stable flux and a high salt rejection of >99.99% throughout the whole experiment with 0.5 mM SDS and 3.5% NaCl feed. We anticipate that our superhydrophobic fluorous short chain branched perfluoroalkyl membranes will be environmentally benign alternatives for wastewater treatment. Green Chem., 2020, 22, 3283. 2. Objective 2 We have extensively studied the different membrane surfaces including hydrophobic membrane, Janus membrane with hydrophobic substrate and a polydopamine/ polyethylenimine hydrophilic skin layer, omniphobic membrane, and a Janus membrane with omniphobic substrate and a PDA/PEI hydrophilic skin layer to better understand the impact of membrane wetting of the advanced membrane with different surface tension feeds and foulants. Research highlights under this point are summarized as follows: • We reported the use of a two-nozzle mode to simultaneously electrospin PH (polyvinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) fibers and electrospray PS (polystyrene) beads to prepare a PH-PS composite membrane. Upon using the optimized PS solvent and PS content, the optimal PH-PS membrane exhibited superhydrophobicity (water contact angle of 157.6°) and good structural integrity, benefiting from the combination of the tough PH network and the interspersed porous irregular PS beads, as well as their homogeneous blending and good adhesion during this advantageous hybrid electrospin-electrospray process. In addition to superhydrophobicity, the PH-PS composite membrane was also endowed with a uniform pore distribution and high porosity, leading to a greatly enhanced liquid entry pressure of water (LEPw). Once applied in the direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) process, it showed high desalination robustness and excellent anti-wetting performance with stable flux and high salt rejection (~99%), tolerance for SDS concentrations of 0.2 mM with no pore wetting observed under harsh feed conditions, providing great potential in practical desalination applications. Journal of membrane science, 2020, 611, 118360. • We systematically evaluate, under the same conditions, how the wettability of Janus membranes and other special membranes can affect their wetting and fouling performance when tested with different complex feeds during MD. We measure their in-air water, in-air oil, and under-water oil contact angles to produce a comprehensive understanding of why they behave differently. his work reported the wetting and fouling mechanisms in MD do not depend solely on the membrane or the feed composition, but rather on the combination of both. Surfactant-containing oily feeds are treated efficiently by omniphobic membranes while those without surfactants result in severe fouling. We concluded that Janus membranes are still susceptible to wetting by surfactants-containing feeds if their substrate is hydrophobic, while only a Janus membrane with hydrophilic surface coating layer and an omniphobic substrate will be able to simultaneously resist both fouling and wetting during MD operation with complex feeds containing organics and low surface tension components. This study offers a roadmap for researchers in the membrane community for proper selection of omniphobic and Janus membranes based on feed composition and substrate wettability. Journal of Membrane Science, 2022, 641, 119873 3. Objective 3 We have conducted an extensive study on the application of Optical Coherence Tomography and potentiostat to develop an advanced real-time wetting and fouling detection system. The successful development of these techniques has enabled in-situ membrane characterization in Membrane Distillation (MD), greatly enhancing our understanding and ability to devise maintenance strategies in scenarios involving membrane wetting and fouling. Furthermore, the implementation of these innovative techniques has provided new insights into the mechanisms underlying fouling and wetting processes. Research highlights under this point are summarized as follows: • We have successfully developed an advanced 3D Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) imaging analysis technique that utilizes intensity range filters to quantify fouling layer formation during Membrane Distillation (MD) through a single 3D data. This innovative approach not only reduces computational power requirements but also effectively separates the fouling layer from the membrane at the microscale. Consequently, real-time evaluation of the fouling layer's thickness, fouling index, and coverage is now possible. To validate this technique, we utilized Polyvinylidene fluoride (C-PVDF) and polytetrafluoroethylene (C-PTFE) membranes to treat industrial textile wastewater as the feed. The 3D imaging analysis revealed thin and disperse foulants on the C-PTFE membrane, with a 22 µm thick fouling layer that remained undetected when using 2D images even after 24 hours. Notably, the C-PTFE membrane demonstrated superior antifouling ability compared to the C-PVDF, as evidenced by its lower fouling index. This observation was further supported by surface energy characterization, which revealed the C-PTFE's relatively low surface energy when compared to the C-PVDF. Both the membrane surface energy analysis and the data from 3D OCT explained the strong antifouling performance observed in the C-PTFE membrane, highlighting the importance of hydrophilic/hydrophobic interactions between dye molecules and the membrane surface, influencing the growth of the fouling layer. Water Research, 2021, 205, 1117668 4. Objectives 4 We have conducted extensive research and developed various strategies to prolong membrane lifecycles by preventing wetting under optimum operational conditions and promoting membrane regeneration. These strategies encompass advanced membrane cleaning and membrane fabrication technologies. One of our key approaches involves utilizing ultrasonic membrane fouling cleaning to effectively remove fouling and maintain optimal membrane performance. Additionally, we have successfully fabricated a thin conductive hydrophobic polyaniline (PANI) layer, which acts as a barrier to prevent permeate contamination and further enhances the membrane's resistance to fouling. Our research showcases the potential of these strategies to mitigate fouling, maintain membrane integrity, and prolong their useful lifespans significantly.

11213819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11213819.value: This research has resulted in 15 papers published in top journals while contributing to 2 book chapters, being presented at four international conferences, and being well received by peer engineers and academics. The success of this project has created a new direction to tackle the fouling and wetting issue in coping with the future challenges in MD application. 1. We have successfully designed a novel environmentally-benign membrane utilizing different fabrication processes, resulting in remarkable superhydrophobic and Janus properties. Our superhydrophobic membrane surfaces are achieved by incorporating fluorous silica aerogels with branched short-chain perfluoroalkyl groups. These groups serve as safer and more environmentally benign alternatives to long-chain PFASs (Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances), showcasing low surface energy and robust performance. The incorporation of environmentally-friendly materials and photothermal properties not only enhances performance but also aligns with sustainable practices, making our membranes promising candidates for various water treatment applications. Green Chem., 2020, 22, 3283. ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 2021, 13 (3), 3805-3815. 2. We have conducted comprehensive investigations into the impact of membrane surface characteristics on membrane wetting and fouling behavior across various surface tension feeds and foulants. A key highlight of our research lies in the systematic study of several unique membrane types, including electrospun PH-PS composite membrane, two-layer patterned superhydrophobic PVDF membrane, dual-layer superhydrophobic omniphobic electrospun nanofiber membrane, and Janus membrane. Our study focused on understanding their respective effects on flux performance and elucidating the potential wetting and fouling mechanisms in Membrane Distillation (MD). These findings contribute valuable insights into optimizing membrane performance and hold great promise for enhancing MD processes. Journal of membrane science, 2020, 611, 118360. 11213819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11213819.value: The current MD membrane fabrication and fouling/wetting monitoring approach still presents some challenges. Firstly, scaling up the complex membrane structure remains challenging. Secondly, our understanding of membrane wetting and fouling is still insufficient. Thirdly, the CFD and OCT results indicate that the local flow velocity on the apex of patterns contributes to anti-fouling performance, leading to questions about the optimal design of membrane surface patterns. Based on the valuable insights gained from this GRF research, we are determined to continue our MD research to address these challenges. Our environmentally-benign membrane, incorporating fluorous silica aerogels with branched short-chain perfluoroalkyl groups, still offers potential for flux improvement and a simplified fabrication process. Significantly, we recognize the urgency of developing a predictive model of membrane wetting based on impedance monitoring. Such a model would assist plant operators in determining the optimal maintenance strategy, enhancing the overall performance and lifespan of the membranes. Moreover, this technique will enable us to compare better the anti-wetting performance, a crucial factor in membrane development. Looking ahead, our focus for further development of this GRF research will be on these specific areas, striving to create greener membranes and extend their lifetime, thereby bringing MD commercialization closer to industrialization.

11213819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11213819.value: Wastewater reclamation has become a promising solution to augment water supply and recover valuable resources. However, the discharge of hypersaline brine from reverse osmosis processes poses environmental challenges. In response to this, membrane distillation (MD) has emerged as a promising thermal technology that overcomes these limitations. It can efficiently treat hypersaline wastewaters and brine generated from zero liquid discharge processes. This research aims to address two significant challenges in MD: wetting and fouling. We have designed and fabricated advanced membranes, including superhydrophobic, omniphobic, and Janus membranes, to provide superior resistance to wetting and fouling. By using cutting-edge technologies like optical coherence tomography and impedance monitoring, we gained a deeper understanding of how these membranes interact with different fouling and wetting agents based on their physicochemical properties. Utilizing these findings, we developed advanced membrane cleaning and fabrication technologies to prolong membrane lifecycles. These technologies prevent wetting and fouling under optimum operational conditions and promote membrane regeneration, thereby improving the efficiency and durability of MD systems. Overall, this research contributes valuable insights and innovative solutions to enhance the application of MD in addressing water scarcity and advancing sustainable water treatment technologies.

11214019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11214019.value: 建築消耗了全球40%以上的一次能源，這一比例在香港要高很多。空調系統占香港建築能耗的一半左右。為了節能，最近開發了非均勻的集中式氣流組織（如置換通風、層式通風等）。這些集中式的氣流組織關注房間的工作區，以儘量減少用於調節非工作區的能量。然而，由於建築管理系統通常只監測送風和排風的情況，而很少有關於房間內不均勻性的資訊，因此集中式氣流組織的不均勻性具有挑戰性。另一方面，政府和節能標準建議提高室內溫度。為了熱舒適性，必須同時提高房間空氣速度，但建築管理系統不提供有關房間空氣速度的資訊。這些缺陷可能導致室內空氣品質差、熱不舒適和在集中式氣流組織運行中的能量浪費。基於物理模型和數學/統計模型可以預測房間的不均勻性。然而，基於物理的模型需要很大的計算量。所有這些模型都需要輸入壁面溫度/熱流量，因此需要更多的感測器，從而增加感測器網路的複雜性和成本。此外，由於感測器位置的不均勻性，對房間環境調節的品質會產生顯著影響。 室內環境由送風條件和室內外條件決定。與目前用作輸入的壁溫/熱流量類似，出口空氣條件也由上述條件決定。送、排風條件均由建築管理系統隨時監控或控制。因此，本文提出了以送、排風條件為輸入的非均勻室內環境模型的理念，以調節集中式氣流組織。這種方法是可行的，因為在建築管理系統中很容易獲得必要的資料。數學/統計建模技術加上低計算負荷的優點均用於運行控制。由於一個理想的室內環境所需的能量可以在很大的範圍內變化，因此空調系統的能效將與理想的室內環境相耦合進行優化。通過這種耦合的運行優化，在不改造传感器網路的情況下，可以通過現有的建築管理系統顯示、可靠地調節集中式氣流組織的室內環境。由於各處與送、排風條件的相關性取決於在房間中的位置，因此它們可以滿足個性化的環境偏好。所以，對於具有集中式氣流組織的空調系統的實際運行，可以預期具有顯著節能效果、理想室內空氣品質和熱舒適性。探索性試驗已發現這種新方法很有前景。 建議的研究將在我們獨特的環境室中進行，該環境室能方便地改換不同氣流組織和房間用途（辦公室和教室）並進行測試。層式通風為典型的非均勻室內環境提供了較高的室內溫度、速度和能效。因此，將首先對其進行測試。將進行客觀測量、主觀調查和經驗證的CFD模擬，以收集資料，從而開發和驗證數學/統計模型。利用這些模型，將開發一種動態控制演算法用於運行控制。並證明耦合優化演算法在即時操作中的有效性。最後，將編制一套指南，用於在集中式氣流組織條件下對室內環境進行優化，並優化空調系統的能效。

11214019.label: Major findings and research outcome
11214019.value: Non-uniform collective air distributions focus on the occupied zone in rooms to minimize the energy used to condition the upper zone. However, non-uniformity is challenging because building management systems usually only monitor the conditions of supply and exit air, with little information on the non-uniformity in rooms. On the other hand, elevated room temperatures are recommended by governments and standards for energy saving. Room air velocities have to be elevated simultaneously for thermal comfort, but building management systems do not provide information on room air velocity. Physics-based models and mathematical/statistical models can predict the non-uniformity in rooms. Nevertheless, the physics-based models require high computational power. All these models need inputs of wall temperatures/heat fluxes and, thereby, more sensors, increasing the sensor network’s complexity and cost. The supply air condition and internal and ambient conditions determine the indoor environment. The exit air condition also results from these conditions. Both supply and exit air conditions are readily monitored and controlled by the building management systems. Therefore, this project originated the idea of modelling non-uniform indoor environments with supply and exit air conditions as inputs for the modulation of collective air distributions. All necessary data are readily available in building management systems. Mathematical/statistical modelling techniques were employed with the merits of a low computational load for operation control. The energy performance of the air conditioning system was optimized to couple with the desired indoor environment. The indoor environment of the collective air distributions was modulated explicitly and reliably by the current building management systems without retrofitting the sensor network. Because the correlations depended on the positions in a room, they satisfied individual occupants’ preferences in the environment. Therefore, the desired indoor air quality and thermal comfort with substantial energy saving were possible for practical operations of air conditioning systems with collective air distributions. Experiments found this new approach applicable. The study was carried out in our unique environmental chamber, which conveniently allowed for configurations of offices and classrooms with different ventilation strategies to be tested. Stratum ventilation provides typical non-uniform indoor environments with elevated room temperatures, velocities, and energy efficiency. Hence, it was tested first. Objective measurements, subjective surveys, and validated CFD simulations were conducted to collect data and develop and validate the mathematical/statistical models. With these models, a dynamic control algorithm was developed for operation control. The effectiveness of the coupled operation optimization for real-time operation was demonstrated.

11214019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11214019.value: Vertically non-uniform air distribution methods (e.g., stratum ventilation) have been proposed to reduce energy use. However, two issues limit their performances in thermal comfort and energy efficiency in a shared room: (1) the horizontal non-uniformity of the thermal conditions and (2) the different thermal preferences of occupants. However, occupants are conventionally regarded as typical persons and their thermal preferences are assumed to be identical. Hence, conventional methods fail to effectively track the actual demand for thermal comfort. Therefore, it is hoped that coupling thermal condition profiles and thermal preferences will improve thermal comfort. The coupled operation strategy innovatively takes advantage of both the horizontal non-uniformity of thermal conditions and the active role of occupants in thermal comfort management to improve thermal comfort. With improved thermal comfort, energy efficiency can also be improved by reducing unnecessary cooling. There are two core tasks in developing the coupled operation strategy: (1) developing a control algorithm that couples thermal condition profiles and thermal preferences and (2) characterizing robustly thermal conditions under different operation conditions. The coupled operation strategy may be validated in our unique environmental chamber, which conveniently allows for experiments under different air distributions (e.g., stratum ventilation).

11214019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11214019.value: Buildings consume over 40% of end-use energy worldwide, much higher in Hong Kong. Air conditioning systems account for around half of the energy use in Hong Kong buildings. The supply air condition and the internal and ambient conditions determine the indoor environment. The exit air condition also results from these conditions. Both supply and exit air conditions are readily monitored and/or controlled by the building management systems. Therefore, this project originates the idea of modelling non-uniform indoor environments with supply and exit air conditions as inputs for the modulation of collective air distributions. The indoor environment of the collective air distributions could be modulated explicitly and reliably by the current building management systems. The desired indoor air quality and thermal comfort with substantial energy savings could be expected. A dynamic control algorithm was developed for operation control. The effectiveness of the coupled operation optimization for real-time operation was demonstrated.

11214519.label: Realisation of objectives
11214519.value: 1. To quantify the resuspension of bacteria based on a real-time high-resolution laser induced fluorescence technique; parameters like resuspension fraction will be determined; The objective has been fully achieved. The Principal Investigator (PI) has conducted a series of resuspension tests in a controlled environment to accurately quantify the bacterial resuspension that occurs when a human steps on flooring seeded with bacteria. The study tested three common flooring materials: carpet, vinyl tile, and hardwood. Three different types of bacteria were tested: Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas alcaligenes, and Staphylococcus epidermidis. The resuspension process was quantified by some commonly used terms such as bacterial resuspension factor, resuspension emission factor, and resuspension fraction. The reported resuspension data was compared with the particle resuspension results documented in the existing literature. The resuspension emission factor (equivalent to the resuspension fraction) of tested bacteria ranged from 3.4 × 10^−5 to 2.1 × 10^−4. Gram-positive bacteria, S. epidermidis, gave higher resuspension than that of the other two Gram-negative bacteria for all floorings. Detailed conclusions can be referred to the publication which was published in a respectful journal Building and Environment in 2023 and also attached to this report. 2. To study factors such as temperature, relative humidity, and exposure of sunlight on viability of settled bacteria; Different factors affect the viability and the resuspension of bacteria from the flooring during human walking. The PI evaluated the resuspension of settled bacteria from human steppings on flooring under different conditions. Factors included microbial surface-attached durations (0, 1, 2 and 3 days), the absence or presence of nutrients on flooring surfaces, and changes in relative humidity (RH) (35%, 65%, and 85%). A manuscript has been submitted to Environmental Science & Technology (Oct 2023). The results showed that, in the absence of nutrients, the highest resuspension emission factor (ER) values for E. coli and S. enterica were 3.8×10-^5±5.2×10^-6 and 5.3×10^-5±6.0×10^-6, respectively, associated with microbial age of 0 days and 35% RH. As the microbial age increased from 0 to 3 days, ER values decreased by 92% and 84% for E. coli and S. enterica, respectively. ER values increased significantly with the presence of nutrients on flooring surfaces for days 1 and 2. The ER value decreased by 87% when RH increased from 35±5% to 85±5%. 3. To measure the electrostatic charges of resuspended bacteria and the charges on shoe soles/flooring; The measurements of electrostatic charges of resuspended aerosol and the charges of shoe soles were conducted for different floorings. The results showed that when humans stepped on different flooring materials, the carpet gave the highest (negative) aerosol charges, while the tile exhibited the lowest (negative) aerosol charges. The charges of shoe soles also varied. The net surface charges on shoe sole after stepping on seeded PVC, tile, and aluminum flooring were much lower than that on seeded carpet, glass, and Teflon flooring. It was found that the polarity of the airborne particle charge was opposite to the net charge of the shoe sole. The results have been published in a respectful journal Building and Environment in 2023 and also attached to this report. 4. To measure the adhesion force with the electrostatic detachment method; The adhesion forces between the particle and flooring materials were measured using the electrostatic detachment method. It was observed that the particle adhesion force varied among different types of flooring. The results showed that, under the same particle-flooring contact time, tile flooring exhibited a higher adhesion force compared to aluminum and PVC flooring. Teflon and glass flooring followed closely behind in terms of adhesion force. This trend in adhesion forces among different flooring materials is consistent with the resuspension results obtained from the resuspension experiments of the project. The PI conducted experiments on human walking-induced particle resuspension under various conditions in a full-scale chamber. Six flooring materials (aluminum with and without pattern, carpet, glass, polyvinyl chloride, Teflon, and tile) and three shoe sole materials (EVA, nylon, and rubber) were used for resuspension tests. Two relative humidity (RH) levels (normal RH: 60 ± 5% and high RH: 85 ± 5%) were investigated. The resuspension results showed that different floorings gave different resuspension results. The results also indicated a positive correlation between the charge of resuspended particles and the resuspension rate. The adhesion forces between the particles and flooring surfaces mainly include van der Waals forces, electrostatic force, and capillary force. The PI has discussed and analyzed these three components in the publication of Building and Environment (Effects of triboelectric charging, flooring materials, relative humidity, and shoe sole materials on human walking-induced particle resuspension). 5. To propose solution for reducing indoor bioaerosol exposure through building design and planning. Several feasible engineering solutions for reducing indoor bioaerosol exposure were proposed. Firstly, this study found the carpet had the highest resuspension of bacteria, compared with hard floorings such as vinyl tile, and hardwood. As a result, carpet flooring is not recommended due to its potential to cause increased microbial resuspension during human walking. Besides, effective and regular floor cleaning or disinfection can be implemented to decrease or eliminate microbial contamination on the floor and other environmental surfaces, particularly in hospital settings. It is expected that the more flooring disinfection the less bioaerosol in the air. Moreover, the dry condition (low air relative humidity) had a higher resuspension rate of bacteria from the flooring than the high humidity condition. Thus, a humidifier is suggested to increase the room humidity when the RH is very low, which also helps reduce the bioaerosol emitted from the resuspension process during human walking. PI is currently evaluating the performance of a surface disinfection method using far UVC of wavelength 222 nm, which is a safe and emerging approach to disinfection. He is investigating an effective way for disinfection soft materials including carpets. A journal manuscript is under preparation.

11214519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11214519.value: Upon completion of this project, some salient findings are observed: (1) The bacterial resuspension emission factors for different floorings ranged from 3.4 × 10−5 to 2.1 × 10−4. Different bacteria and different floorings have different resuspension results. In addition, a positive correlation between the charge of resuspended particles and the resuspension rate was observed. The measured surface static charges of different shoe sole materials before and after human stepping generally agreed with the material’s tendency to gain or lose electrons in the triboelectric series. The results suggest that triboelectric charging can generate and accumulate charges, varying the electrostatic force and further influencing particle resuspension during human walking. (2) Apart from varying the adhesion forces between the particles and the flooring, the nutrition level and RH can affect the bacterial surface loading, which further varies the bacterial resuspension during walking. It was observed that the presence of nutrition can increase the bacterial surface loading. The bacterial resuspension emission factors consistently decreased with the increasing RH, consistent with particle adhesion theory. The reported microbial resuspension data not only provides an important database to fill the research gap but also provides very useful and necessary information for estimating the bioaerosol human exposure risks. (3) Based on our results, culturable bacteria can be detected in resuspended air from human stepping on flooring surfaces even after the bacteria has deposited on the floor for three days. Effective surface cleaning is a feasible way to reduce the number of pathogens on flooring materials. Research outcome. The results have been published in two archival journals. 1. Yang, S. 11214519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11214519.value: Potential for Further Development The project has been completed with great success, and all objectives of this study have been satisfactorily achieved. We understand more fundamental knowledge about the effects of nutrients, abiotic materials and cell agglomeration on bacterial growth, adhesion and resuspension on the flooring materials. An expanded spectrum of microorganisms of different types, shapes and sizes should be included in further studies of microbial resuspension. Furthermore, additional testing can be conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of potential engineering solutions in reducing or eliminating the resuspension of settled pathogens in indoor environments. One effective method is to reduce the pathogen load on surfaces, which serves as a source control measure. The Principal Investigator (PI) is currently evaluating the performance of a surface disinfection method using far UVC, which is a safe and emerging approach to disinfection. A journal manuscript is under preparation. The normalized bacterial resuspension results obtained from this project can also serve as valuable input data for developing a model to estimate human daily exposure to indoor bioaerosols.

11214519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11214519.value: Walking is a common activity among humans. Previous studies have shown that the resuspension of particles from flooring caused by human walking is an important source of indoor aerosols and has been associated with health effects such as allergies and asthma. However, it remains unclear whether the inhalation of resuspended bioaerosols is an important pathway for airborne infections. Quantification of the resuspension process is crucial for understanding the exposure pathway of bioaerosols and estimating the dose of exposure and the associated risks of infection through inhalation. The project involved a series of experiments aimed at quantifying the bacterial resuspension from various types of flooring. Besides, the resuspension of culturable microorganisms during walking under different surface-attached times and environmental conditions was investigated for the first time. Inferring from the results, carpet flooring gave higher resuspension than other floorings such as vinyl tile, and hardwood. The settled bacteria can be resuspended from the flooring during human walking activities, even after the bacteria has deposited on the floor for three days. The findings of this study not only contribute to filling the research gap but also provide valuable and necessary information for estimating the risks associated with human exposure to bioaerosols.

11215119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215119.value: The airline industry has been striving to improve fuel efficiency. The incentives are not only economic - fuel cost accounts for a third of the operational cost for most airlines – but also environmental, since the industry is under growing pressure to reduce carbon emission and to promote sustainable growth. Existing approaches on fuel efficiency focused on aircraft or engine designs, flight operations, e.g. optimal altitude and speed, and maintenance procedures. Flight fuel planning emerged as a new area for additional fuel savings. Each aircraft carries extra fuel in order to prevent deplete given the uncertainties of fuel consumptions. Beyond the reserve fuel mandated by regulations, airlines load Contingency Fuel at their discretion. The amount of Contingency Fuel is determined by the single highest fuel consumption record in the past. As a result, most flights are carrying much more fuel than needed, and the cost of carrying these “dead weight” is significant. If fuel consumption can be more accurately predicted, the need for Contingency Fuel can be reduced for the benefit of fuel savings across all flights. With the rapid development of data intelligence and the large amount of operational data accumulated at airlines, a data-driven approach will change how uncertainties are managed for fuel planning. In this research, we propose a data-driven approach to better manage uncertainties in flight fuel consumption for airlines. The aim is to build a predictive model that can better estimate each flight’s fuel consumption by combining multiple data sources (e.g. traffic conditions, Flight Data Recorder data, etc.) which are not typically included in the current practice. Three research tasks are scheduled to achieve the aim: 1) analyze discrepancies between planned and actual fuel consumptions and identifying key contributing factors; 2) develop a data-driven model to predict flight fuel consumption; 3) optimize flight fuel loading towards a data-driven fuel planning strategy. The project is in line with the PI and Co-I’s research experiences in air transportation systems, data analytics, and optimization. A pilot study was conducted in collaboration with a major airline company based off Hong Kong. We take encouragement from preliminary results which suggest promising agreement between actual fuel consumption and prediction using our data-driven approach. A successful completion of this project will contribute to academic literature in data intelligence and aviation fuel efficiency. The collaborative nature of this project between academia and industry may impact flight fuel planning practice and further promote fuel efficiency. 航空業一直在努力提高燃油效率。不僅是經濟原因， 燃料成本佔大多數航空公司運營成本的三分之一，而且還包括環境因素，因為該行業正面臨著減少碳排放和促進可持續增長的壓力。關於燃料效率的現有方法集中在飛機或發動機設計，飛行操作，例如，最佳高度和速度，以及維護程序。 飛行燃料計劃成為節省額外燃料的新領域。鑑於燃料消耗的不確定性，每架飛機都攜帶額外的燃料以防止耗盡。除了法規規定的儲備燃料外，航空公司還可自行決定加載應急燃料。應急燃料的數量由過去的單一最高燃料消耗記錄確定。結果，大多數航班攜帶的燃料比所需的燃料多得多，攜帶這些“自重”的成本也很高。如果可以更準確地預測燃料消耗，則可以減少對應急燃料的需求，以便在所有航班上節省燃料。隨著數據智能的快速發展和航空公司積累的大量運營數據，數據驅動方法將改變燃料計劃的不確定性管理方式。 在本研究中，我們提出了一種數據驅動方法，以更好地管理航空公司飛行燃料消耗的不確定性。目的是建立一種預測模型，該模型可以通過組合多個數據源（例如交通狀況，飛行數據記錄器數據等）來更好地估計每個航班的燃料消耗，這些數據源通常不包括在當前實踐中。計劃實現三項研究任務：1）分析計劃和實際燃料消耗之間的差異，並確定關鍵因素; 2）開發數據驅動模型來預測飛行燃料消耗; 3）優化飛行燃料負荷，以實現數據驅動的燃料計劃策略。 該項目符合PI在航空運輸系統和數據分析方面的研究經驗。與香港一家航空公司國泰航空公司合作進行了一項試點研究。我們從初步結果中得到鼓勵，這些結果表明使用我們的數據驅動方法在實際燃料消耗和預測之間達成了一致。該項目的成功完成將有助於數據智能和航空燃油效率的學術文獻。學術界和工業界之間該項目的協作性質可能會影響航班燃料規劃實踐並進一步提高燃油效率。

11215119.label: Realisation of objectives
11215119.value: Objective 1: Analyze discrepancies between planned and actual fuel consumptions and identifying key contributing factors. To achieve this objective, we have collected flight data (including planned fuel consumptions, actual fuel consumptions, delay amount and reasons (if any), flight records, etc.) of a whole year of operations from our airline collaborator. One of the PhD students working on this project worked at the collaborator airline for one month to understand the flight planning process and collect the all needed data for this research. Loading Variable Fuel is a way to handle the limited capability of current FPS procedures to predict actual flight time, reflecting the dispatchers’ or pilots’ re-adjustment of FPS-calculated quantities of fuel loads. Most flights carry much more fuel than necessary because of a few records of high fuel consumption associated with significant flight time delays in the past. Thus, better predictions for flight times, especially those with significant delays, could help to reduce the need for Variable Fuel and aid in the development of better fuel loading strategies. We found that among many factors that contribute to the discrepancies between planned and actual fuel consumption, flight delay is the most important one. Objective 2: Develop a data-driven model to predict flight fuel consumption, taking in data input available at the time of flight planning. We have developed a data-driven model and a supporting method to achieve Objective 2. Given the nascent status of the field, research directly addressing excessive fuel loading in flight fuel planning is very rare. Ryerson et al., based on data from major U.S. airlines, estimated that 0.70% -1.04% of aircraft fuel consumption is attributed to carrying unnecessary contingency and alternate fuel (Ryerson et al., 2015). Kang et al. proposed to use flight gate-in fuel to measure aviation system predictability and estimated the cost to carry such gate-in fuel for six major U.S. airlines in 2012, which is $59 million to $667 million (Kang et al., 2018). Following this, they have also proposed a method based on quantile regression to recommend Contingency Fuel amount in the fuel planning stage (Kang & Hansen, 2017). Although there are many factors contributing to fuel consumption uncertainties, flight time has a strong correlation with the fuel consumption. Thus, this paper focuses on predicting flight time accurately. The flight time prediction problem, as well as a related topic: flight delay prediction, have been studied for years (Mueller & Chatterji, 2002; Sternberg, Soares, Carvalho, & Ogasawara, 2017). Many prior works employ statistical methods or probabilistic approaches. Pathomsiri et al. assessed the efficiency of US airports using a non-parametric function to model joint production of on-time and delay performance (Pathomsiri, Haghani, Dresner, & Windle, 2008). Tu et al. studied major factors that influenced flight departure delays and estimated departure delay distributions at Denver International Airport for United Airlines using a probabilistic approach (Tu, Ball, & Jank, 2008). These works attempted to separate and analyze factors contributing to flight delays, but they mainly focused on one single airport, and not considered network effects. In other works, operational research, including optimization, simulations, and queue theory, has been carried out to model and simulate flight delays and help policy makers to optimize at a system level. These classic methods are valuable for understanding root causes and interactions among the elements of delay occurrence. However, the accuracy of these models is not sufficient for the individual flight predictions (Yu, Guo, Asian, Wang, & Chen, 2019). With the vast volume of commercial aviation system data being collected and the development of artificial intelligence algorithms, machine learning has become popular in the field of flight time prediction. The commonly used data-driven methods include k-Nearest-Neighbors, neural networks, support vector machine, fuzzy logic, and tree-based methods (Sternberg et al., 2017). Rebollo et al. adopted random forest algorithms to predict departure delays with air traffic network characteristics as input features, which had an error of approximately 21 min when predicting departure delays for a two-hour forecast horizon (Rebollo & Balakrishnan, 2014). Choi et al. combined flight schedules and weather forecasts to predict whether a scheduled flight will be delayed or on-time using several machine learning algorithms (Choi, Kim, Briceno, & Mavris, 2016). Perez-Rodriguez et al. presented an asymmetric logit probability model to estimate and predict the daily probabilities of delays in aircraft arrivals (Pérez–Rodríguez, Pérez–Sánchez, & Gómez–Déniz, 2017). More recent, studies have used deep learning algorithms to improve the accuracy of flight delay prediction. Kim et al. proposed a recurrent neural network (RNN) to predict the flight departure and arrival delays of an individual airport with day-to-day sequences (Kim, Choi, Briceno, & Mavris, 2016). The results of this study show that the accuracy of RNN improved with deeper architectures. However, this model can only perform two-class predictions of flight delay rather than time prediction. In (Chen & Li, 2019; Rebollo & Balakrishnan, 2014), the authors adopted random forest methods for its low sensitivity to outliers. This “optimizing for the average” technique does not serve the purpose of the problem addressed in this paper – accurately predicting flight times of individual flights in a national network, especially flights with significant delays, to reduce the need for Variable Fuel in fuel planning stage. Objective 3: Optimize flight fuel loading towards a data-driven fuel planning strategy. Optimization models will be developed to support airline managers and dispatchers to plan flights under uncertainties. We have developed a decision support model to realize Objective 3. The core of this task is to formulate a data-driven optimization model to provide recommended values for Contingency Fuel loading for a given flight. Due to the operational uncertainties associated with every flight, the fuel planning model has to capture the tradeoff between fuel consumption savings from reducing Contingency Fuel loading and the risk of using Reserve Fuel that is required to carry by regulation. Nevertheless, the key challenge in the data-driven fuel planning problem is how to quantify the operational uncertainties and incorporate the prediction results in the optimization model. We addressed this issue by discussing with our airline partner. The solutions have been compared with the recommended values based on the Performance Based Compliance (PBC) or Statistical Contingency Fuel (SCF), which are currently used at airlines. We conducted scenario analysis & case studies with real-world data to evaluate the potential fuel savings and safety risks using different strategies developed from the optimization model.

11215119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11215119.value: The current practice on fuel loading, which has a significant impact on aircraft weight and fuel consumption, has yet to be thoroughly addressed by existing studies. Excess fuel is loaded by dispatchers and (or) pilots to handle fuel consumption uncertainties, primarily caused by flight time uncertainties, which cannot be predicted by current Flight Planning Systems (FPS). In this project, we developed a series of data-driven models and decision support tools that can provide a much more accurate prediction of fuel consumption by capturing air traffic information at a national scale based on multiple data sources. Out of the 9 journal/scholarly publications generated from this project, 4 journal papers directly address the fuel planning problems as proposed in this project, 4 journal papers focus on the underlying methods and models development, and 1 book chapter summarizes the common methodologies for spatial-temporal modeling and forecasting. Two PhD students (one fully sponsored by this project, and one partially sponsored by this project) have been trained. The research outcomes include

11215119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11215119.value: These data-driven machine-learning models and decision-support tools have technology transfer potential. Several airlines are approaching us to discuss ways to utilize the technologies developed in this project for their flight planning operations.

11215119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11215119.value: Airlines often add extra fuel than what's strictly necessary to account for uncertainties in how long the flight will take. The issue is that the current systems airlines use to plan flights don't do a great job at predicting these flight times, which can change due to a variety of factors, like air traffic and weather. To address this problem, we created a set of computer models that uses a type of AI called deep learning. This model looks at large amounts of data, including real-time air traffic updates, weather reports, and historical flight information, to better predict flight times. When we tested their model using data from an entire year of an airline's flights, we found that it could predict flight times more accurately than older methods, particularly for flights that experienced significant delays. The key takeaway is that with more accurate flight time predictions, airlines can load just the right amount of fuel — not too much, not too little — which could save fuel consumption by a small but significant percentage. This efficiency gain could reduce costs and be better for the environment, without increasing the risk of planes running out of fuel.

11215619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11215619.value: Immune diseases involve disruption to immune cell behaviors and cause fatal health problems. Leukocytes are important in both innate and adaptive immune responses, yet promising prognosis and diagnosis on the immune responses are very challenging, mainly hindered by the multiplex, heterogeneous and dynamic responses and cell-cell communications (e.g. cytokine secretion) among different immune cell subtypes in blood. Characterization of different immune subtypes on their cytokine secretion during a systematic immune response can provide important insights on mechanisms of immune diseases as well as effective treatment strategies. In particular, cell isolation from blood is a key step for diagnosing immune diseases. Despite demands on efficiency and purity of cell isolation, placement of the isolated cells at defined positions in a co-cultured environment is equally critical. Cell-cell communication should be maintained among the isolated cells such that the in vitro stimulated cytokine secretions from those isolated cells are more representative to in vivo immune responses. Additionally, it is technically very challenging to quantitatively measure the cytokine secretions from different isolated single-cells, which should belong to different immune cell types with distinct behaviors, while they are being co-cultured in the same microchamber. Considering also involvement of multiple cytokine types in an immune response, it is necessary to establish a multiplex cytokine quantification technique for different local sites over the co-culturing microchamber. This proposed research aims at developing a novel microfluidic ‘immunophenotyping’ device for determining cytokine secretions from different leukocyte subtypes during immune responses of an immune cell mixture. For the single-cell isolation, we plan to apply arrays of microstructures (micropillars and micro-sieves) to displace and trap the cells at defined positions in a co-culture region. Dimensions of the microstructures should match the immune cells; and arrangement of these microstructures is configured for the maximal cell capture rate. Further, the spatial cytokine concentration profile is measured by an array of detection microbeads for different cytokine molecules pre-captured over the co-culture region. The cell subtypes can be subsequently identified based on their surface protein expressions. Hence, we can convert the measured spatial profiles of cytokines and cell types to the cytokine secretion of different leukocyte subtypes during a target immune response. Altogether, the cell subtype-specific multiplex cytokine secretions quantified by the proposed microfluidic device are a unique signature that characterizes patients’ immunophenotypes more precisely. This can lead to better prognosis and diagnosis of immune diseases and disorders, allowing for personalized medications and effective early-stage treatment. 免疫疾病涉及破壞免疫細胞行為並導致致命的健康問題。白細胞在先天性和適應性免疫應答中都很重要有希望的預後和對免疫反應的診斷非常具有挑戰性，主要受多重，異質和動態響應以及細胞的阻礙血液中不同免疫細胞亞型之間的通訊（例如細胞因子分泌）。不同免疫亞型對細胞因子分泌的影響系統性免疫反應可以提供免疫機制的重要見解疾病以及有效的治療策略。特別是從血液中分離細胞是診斷免疫疾病的關鍵步驟。儘管要求效率和純度細胞分離，將分離的細胞置於共培養的確定位置環境同樣重要。應保持細胞間通信分離的細胞使體外刺激的細胞因子從分離的細胞中分泌出來細胞更能代表體內免疫反應。此外，它在技術上定量測量不同細胞因子分泌物非常具有挑戰性分離的單細胞，應該屬於不同的免疫細胞類型行為，而他們在同一個微室中共同培養。考慮也多種細胞因子類型參與免疫反應，有必要建立多重細胞因子定量技術，用於不同的地方站點共培養微室。 這項擬議的研究旨在開發一種新型微流體『免疫表型』用於測定不同白細胞亞型中細胞因子分泌的裝置免疫細胞混合物的免疫反應。對於單細胞分離，我們計劃應用微結構陣列（微柱和微篩）來移位和捕獲共培養區域中限定位置的細胞。微結構的尺寸應與免疫細胞相匹配;並且配置這些微結構的佈置對於最大細胞捕獲率。此外，空間細胞因子濃度曲線是通過一系列檢測微珠測量在共培養區域上預捕獲的不同細胞因子分子。隨後可以鑑定細胞亞型基於它們的表面蛋白質表達。因此，我們可以轉換測量的空間細胞因子和細胞類型對不同白細胞的細胞因子分泌的描述目標免疫反應期間的亞型。總而言之，細胞亞型特異性由提出的微流體裝置量化的多重細胞因子分泌是獨特的簽名，更準確地表徵患者的免疫表型。這可能導致為了更好的預後和診斷免疫疾病和疾病，允許個性化藥物和有效的早期治療。

11216119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216119.value: 氣體污染物會造成人類各種不適、疾病甚至死亡，嚴重威脅著人類的健康和安全，尤其是對嬰兒、老人以及一些有呼吸和心血管問題的敏感人群。為了避免氣體污染物的威脅，人們對便攜式、低成本、低能耗且適合對周圍環境進行持續監測的氣體監測系統的需求與日俱增。集成氣體傳感器就是解決此類問題的有效途徑，它能夠在單個微電子芯片中封裝先進氣體傳感器及模擬前端讀出電路，有望製備出精準、高效、緊湊的監測工具，使其更適於便攜式應用。 近十年來，關於各種各樣的集成氣體傳感器的報導不斷湧現，包括懸臂、熱電、聲波共振、生物發光和聚合物基化學氣體傳感器。然而，現在的傳感器技術還存在很多固有缺陷，如工作溫度高、需要外加熱源或光源（非單片）、穩定性差、生產工序複雜。金屬氧化物基氣體傳感器則不存在這些問題，不僅靈敏度高，而且與互補金屬氧化物半導體（CMOS）電路最為兼容（例如電壓要求和製備工藝）。 本項目擬設計、製備且實驗驗證一種集成氣體傳感微系統。此微系統將包括一個由納米結構化金屬氧化物組成的化學電阻型氣體傳感陣列。此設計及製備工藝將使氣體傳感器實現精確、低功耗和小型化。這一進展將有望實現經濟可靠的環境監測，直接解決香港及世界其他城市化地區所面臨的緊迫挑戰。
