11216219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216219.value: 在結構金屬材料研究中，物料的高強度和高可塑性都是科學家追求的目標。 現今的策略大多增加了材料的強度，但卻要犧牲其塑性。在這十年中，一些方法如：納米孿晶，梯度納米結構，位錯工程和納米粒子析出法，都能同時提供高強度和不錯的可塑性。 然而，所增強度仍有所限制：當材料達到或超出金屬玻璃E/50 (E是材料的楊氏模量)的規範時，要同時擁有強度和維護相當的可塑性便變得非常困難。 我們最近開發了一種以鎂為基體的超強材料，此材料擁有原位形成的非晶﹣納米晶納米結構，在室温中也能展示出沒有尺寸效應的理論強：3.3 GPa 。 這工作已在“Nature”期刋中刋登。然而，這高可塑性僅發生在直徑小於700納米的樣品中。 在最近的研究中，我們發現了一種新的超強納米雙相﹣玻璃晶體（NDP-GC）納米結構，它既沒有尺寸效應並擁有很大的可塑性。 對其塑性變形機制作進一步研究將會為設計擁有史無前例機械性能的材料奠下基礎。其成果將會是一個新穎和有效的方法來產生高強高韌的NDP-GC合金。 此外，最近我們開發了一個方法去打印高強三維陶瓷，此工作被出版在“Science Advances”。所以，我們有望能製造作高強高韌的三維打印的NDP-GC材料。我們的努力將可用在工業應用上，如：高強度MEMS設備、高耐磨性和熱穩定性的表面塗層、和三維打印的微結構，這會對材料工程上的基礎研究和整體社會上有莫大益處。 要改進對NDP-GC納米材料的塑料變形機制的理解，這研究將由四項任務組成： (1)研究由應用了不同沉積參數的物理氣相沉積法製備的鋁基體的NDP-GC微結構，和比較其NDP-GC的機械行為; (2)研究NDP-GC在塑性變形過程中兩相（結晶相和非晶相）各自的微結構演變和兩相（結晶相和非晶相）之間的相互作用; 和(3)研究NDP-GC的熱穩定性。

11216219.label: Realisation of objectives
11216219.value: In this project, the microstructure generation of Al-based nano-dual-phase glass-crystal (NDP-GC) produced by physical vapor deposition (PVD) with different deposition parameters has been studied and their mechanical behaviors of the NDP-GC have been obtained. The respective microstructure evolution in the two phases (crystalline phase and amorphous phase) during plastic deformation and the interaction of crystalline phase and amorphous phase in the NDP-GC during plastic deformation have also been examined. In addition, heat treatment has been applied on the metallic glass obtained by NDP and its behavior has been observed. And the applications of the NDP-GC on catalyst have been explored. In this study, we have fabricated the NDP-GC and the details as follow: For the study of microstructure generation and evolution, the hierarchical nanostructured Al95Ni2Y3 (at.%) with the thickness of 17–50 μm were fabricated by magnetron sputtering and were deposited on the Si (0 0 1) substrate. In the sputtering process, the Ar pressure was 0.2 Pa; the deposition rate was 12.5 nm per minute; the substrate bias voltage was −50 V. In order to carry out the mechanical characterization, nanoindentation was performed by Hysitron TI950 nanoindenter. The structure of the hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy was studied by TEM. A JEM 2100F FEG transmission electron microscope (from JEOL), operated at 200 kV, was used for TEM analysis to reveal the microstructure evolution in the two phases during plastic deformation. Objectives achieved All the Objectives have been achieved. High strength and high ductility are often mutually exclusive properties for structural metallic materials. A hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy with a structure of Al nanograins surrounded by nano-sized metallic glass (MG) shells in introduced in this study. It achieves an ultrahigh yield strength of 1.2 GPa in tension (1.7 GPa in compression) along with 15% plasticity in tension (over 70% in compression). The nano-sized MG phase facilitates such ultrahigh strength by impeding dislocation gliding from one nanograin to another, while continuous generation-movement-annihilation of dislocations in the Al nanograins and the flow behavior of the nano-sized MG phase result in increased plasticity. This plastic deformation mechanism is also an efficient way to decrease grain size to sub-10 nm size for low melting temperature metals like Al, making this structural design one solution to the strength-plasticity trade-off. The cross-sectional TEM image of the hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy, showing Al nanograins surrounded with light–dark contrasted grain–grain interfaces and the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern denotes the polycrystalline structure. The HRTEM images of the hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy, showing a crystalline Al nanograin is surrounded by amorphous phase with the fcc structure with zone axis of [0 1 1], and the defect-free fcc structure and a nano-sized amorphous phase forms between the two grains. The hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy’s mechanical properties were analyzed by scanning electron microscope (SEM) in situ compression and tension tests under identical conditions (sample size and loading rate) for the hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy, Al-based MG and nanocrystalline Al. Compressive engineering stress-strain curves show that nanocrystalline Al has a yield strength of only 0.2 GPa with discontinuous plastic flow while Al-based MG has a yield strength of 1.0 GPa without any plasticity. The hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy displays an ultrahigh yield strength of 1.7 GPa, and a homogeneous large plastic deformation with a strain of over 70%. The Plastic deformation mechanism of the hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy has been examined as well. To understand the deformation mechanism, the microstructure of the compressed pillar with a true strain of 150% (engineering strain of 76%) was investigated by TEM. The overall compressed pillar shows a flat-barrel shape without any shear plane/offset, which indicates homogeneous plastic deformation. In the larger magnification TEM image of the compressed pillar, the nanograins show the lamellar structure, and the vertical width of the nanograins decreases from ~40 to ~ 8 nm after compression. Nano-lamellar grains orientated with crystallographically lowindex planes is helpful to reveal the extremely thin MG layer between them. It shows that the width of the nano-sized MG phase decrease from ~4 to ~1 nm after plastic deformation. This confirms the existence of fully homogeneous plastic flow of the nano-sized MG phase without any shear band. It is clearly shown in the HRTEM images that the dark regions contain high-density dislocations, which are regarded as dislocations piled up inside nanograins. This mechanism contributes to the strain hardening of the nanograins. Furthermore, the homogeneous plastic flow in the nano-sized MG phase is notable, because bulk MGs usually exhibit limited plasticity due to shearband instability. This phenomenon may be attributed to MGs’ intrinsic plastic deformation ability in extremely small size. The flow stress of the nano-sized MG phase may reach to theoretical strength during plastic flow. This indicates that the nano-sized MG phase is still strong during plastic deformation and is able to prevent the softening mechanism of the nanograins, such as GB migration in the conventional nanocrystalline materials. Moreover, its homogeneous flow behavior accommodates the large plastic deformation of the nanograins, which prevents shear deformation mechanism, such as stress localization. The interface usually plays a key role for crack deflection, thus enhancing toughness. In this hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy, the MG phase on the interface has plastic deformation and no void or crack is seen in the highly deformed sample, which may indicate a high toughness of the alloy. This part of study has been published in Nature Communication. We have also studied the structural evolution of the Mg-based NDP-GC during compression in a MD simulation, and demonstrated an alloy design strategy that the strong-yet-brittle phases can be ductilized by wrapped with nano-sized amorphous phase. This NDP-GC alloy design strategy thus provided potential interesting applications, for instance in nano-electromechanical systems (NEMS) and flexible wearable devices that should sustain high load and deformation. This part of work has been published in Scripta Materialia. Besides studying the microstructure generation, evolution and mechanism of the Al-based NDP-GC, we also investigated the thermal stability of the NDP-GC and its feasible applications. To investigate the thermal stability of our crystal-glass high-entropy nanocomposite, the nanocrystalline CrCoNi-Fe-Si-B reference alloy (Cr29.2Fe10.2Co30.1Ni27.7B1.1C0.1O0.4Si1.2, at.%) and the crystalglass CrCoNi-Fe-Si-B high-entropy nanocomposite (Cr23.1Fe20.7Co24.8Ni26.7B1.7C0.3O0.6Si2.1, at.%) were annealed in a vacuum chamber at 350 °C and 500 °C for 1 hour, respectively. Cross-sectional TEM lamellae were prepared from the annealed samples using FIB. The microstructures of the annealed samples were investigated using TEM and HRTEM. The results show that the width of the columnar grains in the crystal-glass CrCoNi-Fe-Si-B high-entropy nanocomposite does not change after 350 °C or 500 °C annealing, i.e. the material’s columnar grain size of ~8 nm prevailed. The crystalline structure of the nanograins remains – also after these heat treatments - fcc, according to the SAED analysis. Therefore, these results show the good thermal stability of our crystal-glass high-entropy nanocomposite in terms of grain size. This piece of work has been published in Scripta Materialia. In this study, we have preliminarily explored the feasible application of NDP-GC as a potential low-cost active catalyst to replace noble metal–based HER catalysts. 11216219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216219.value: In this study, we investigated the plastic deformation mechanism and thermal stability of ultra-strong /ductile nano-dual-phase alloys. Some major important findings can be summarized: - A hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy with a structure of Al nanograins surrounded by nano-sized metallic glass (MG) shells in introduced. An ultrahigh yield strength of 1.2 GPa in tension (1.7 GPa in compression) along with 15% plasticity in tension (over 70% in compression). The nano-sized MG phase facilitates such ultrahigh strength by impeding dislocation gliding from one nanograin to another, while continuous generation-movement-annihilation of dislocations in the Al nanograins and the flow behavior of the nano-sized MG phase result in increased plasticity. This plastic deformation mechanism is also an efficient way to decrease grain size to sub-10 nm size for low melting temperature metals like Al, making this structural design one solution to the strength-plasticity trade-off. - The plastic deformation mechanism of the hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy has been examined. the existence of fully homogeneous plastic flow of the nano-sized MG phase without any shear band has been confirmed. - It is found that in this hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy, the MG phase on the interface has plastic deformation and no void or crack is seen in the highly deformed sample, which may indicate a high toughness of the alloy. - By means of annealing on a prepared Ti-based thin film metallic glasses (TFMG), the sample became partially crystallized, forming a supra-nano amorphous-nanocrystalline alloy. This nanocomposite structural material exhibited a nearly ideal strength, and a large elastic strain, which was far superior to the common amorphous alloys and nanocrystalline counterparts. - It is found that the thermal stability of high-order twins can be guaranteed because of the pinning effect of partial dislocations onto the low-order twins, even at a temperature of ~0.65 Tm. The strengthening of pinning effect occurs with the accumulation of partial dislocations onto low-order twins along with the evolution from stacking faults (SFs) to nanotwins. And it can be explained by the phenomenon of a strong partitioning of compressive and tensile stress concentration after emission of new partial dislocations across low-order twins. However, the intersectional SFs is unstable at elevated temperature while can be stabilized by large plastic deformation. Because the propagation of partials along low-order twins can effectively release the stress concentration induced during the formation of SFs. - The feasibility of nano-dual-phase alloys on catalyst has been demonstrated.

11216219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216219.value: During the reporting period, despite of the objectives achieved, we further discovered the employment of Al-based nano-dual-phase glass-crystal as catalyst for hydrogen evolution reaction. Platinum-based catalysts are widely used in hydrogen evolution reactions; however, their applications are restricted because of the cost-efficiency trade-off. Recently, we presented a thermodynamics-based design strategy for synthesizing an Al73Mn7Ru20 (atomic %) metal catalyst via combinatorial magnetron co-sputtering. The new electrocatalyst with special composition exhibits exceptional performance, similar to that of single-atom catalysts and better than that of nanocluster-based catalysts. Aluminum is used rather than a noble metal as the principal element of the catalyst and ruthenium, which is cheaper than platinum, as the noble metal component. The design strategy provides an efficient route for the development of electrocatalysts for use in large-scale hydrogen production. Moreover, the superior hydrogen reaction evolution created by the synergistic effect of the nano-dual- phase structure is expected to guide the development of high-performance catalysts in other alloy systems. In the future, we will continue to study the high-performance catalysts in other alloy systems and explore the feasibility of large-scale production of such low cost catalysts for hydrogen production.

11216219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216219.value: In the study of structural metallic materials, high strength and large plasticity are always pursuit of the goal. Plenty of strategies were developed to increase the strength of the materials, yet substantially by scarifying the plasticity. In the recent decades, some approaches such as nanotwinning, gradient nanostructuring, dislocation engineering, and nanoparticals precipitation, were able to provide high strength and good plasticity simultaneously. However, the strength increase still has limitations, i.e., it is very difficult to reach to or exceed the metallic glass (MG) regime of E/50 (E is the Young’s modulus of a material) while maintain the plasticity. In this project, a hierarchical nanostructured Al alloy with a structure of Al nanograins surrounded by nano-sized metallic glass (MG) shells is introduced in this study. It achieves an ultrahigh yield strength of 1.2 GPa in tension (1.7 GPa in compression) along with 15% plasticity in tension (over 70% in compression). The nano-sized MG phase facilitates such ultrahigh strength by impeding dislocation gliding from one nanograin to another, while continuous generation-movement-annihilation of dislocations in the Al nanograins and the flow behavior of the nano-sized MG phase result in increased plasticity. This plastic deformation mechanism is also an efficient way to decrease grain size to sub-10 nm size for low melting temperature metals like Al, making this structural design one solution to the strength-plasticity trade-off. With the excellent mechanical performance, especially the superior anti-wear behavior (proved in another project, CityU 11209918), NDP-GC is a potential candidate for biomaterials; and combining with 3/4D printing technology developed for fabricating a complex shape, NDP-GC is believed to be a promising material for the application of bioimplant.

11216619.label: Realisation of objectives
11216619.value: Due to unforeseen challenges, the project had to make adjustments from the original proposal. The COVID-19 pandemic forced the closure of our lab for a whole semester, causing some delays. Additionally, a graduate student raised concerns about the toxicity of ionic liquids, leading to the discontinuation of their use in experiments. Consequently, we only obtained preliminary data on ionic liquids (Conference paper [C1]) and focused on using the other candidate additive suggested in the proposal, stearic acid (Paper [2]). The goal of this project, as stated in the original proposal, aimed to enhance lubrication in limited lubricant supply (LLS) bearing contacts by exploiting liquid-solid interfacial forces to enrich lubricant replenishment on the lubrication track. Our research not only explored the use of additives to create oleophobic layers on the bearing tracks, but also investigated the application of anti-fingerprint coatings to generate unidirectional interfacial forces to enhance replenishment (Paper [3]). The specific achievements of all objectives are detailed below. Obj.1) To update the existing optical slider bearing test rig to enable online measurement of lubricant distribution on the lubrication track by incorporation of fluorescent technique. (*Refer to the intermediate progress report and Paper [2] in Part C.) A fluorescence system (NAVITAR ZFL Fluorescence Imaging System) was successfully integrated into the test rig, mainly for spatial measurements of oil distribution on the lubrication track. Examples of fluorescence images taken during the experiments can be found in Paper [2]. High-quality pictures allow quantitative measurements of droplet size, growth rate and spatial density. Obj.2) To perform a parametric study to identify and optimize parameters, e.g., pressure and flow fields in bearing contact, which affect the IL adsorption to realize oil dewetting on the lubrication track. (*Details can be found in Conference paper [C2] in Part C.) This objective was to investigate factors affecting oil dewetting and adsorption layer formation to enhance our understanding of the mechanism and its applications for improving lubrication in LLS conditions. We utilized an optical slider bearing setup with a steel slider and glass disc to capture dewetting in LLS tests. Advanced analytical and experimental tools, including image processing techniques, were developed to quantify and analyze the data. These tools allowed for the automatic determination of the number and lateral dimensions (diameter) of dewetting oil beads. A significant finding was the similarity between the contact angle of the dewetting oil beads and the measured receding contact angle (RCA) of the surface. This allowed us to estimate the volume size of oil beads based on the RCA and the lateral diameter, assuming the oil beads resembled perfect spherical caps. However, obtaining reliable data for analysis was limited due to the need for a very thin lubricating film for dewetting to occur. Achieving an evenly distributed oil film requires stable bearing operation with low measurement error. Unfortunately, the accuracy and stability of the existing test rig did not meet these requirements. Overcoming this limitation would be essential for further advancements in this area of research. Obj.3) To model and experimentally study lubricant replenishment with oil dewetting on the lubrication track. (*Details can be found in Papers [1, 2, 3] in Part C.) To address this objective, we focused on three dewetting patterns and their impact on lubricant replenishment. Firstly, we investigated an oleophobic track bounded by oleophilic domains (Papers [1] and [2]). Secondly, we examined an oleophilic track bounded by oleophobic domains, known as the stripe wettability pattern, (Paper [3]). Lastly, we explored an interlaced wettability pattern with alternating oleophilic and oleophobic lateral domains on the lubrication track (Paper [3]). We found that for LLS, using dewetting oil beads performed better than the conventional uniform oil layer. The oil beads generated film pressure earlier upon contact with the bearing, resulting in a larger load-carrying capacity. The stripe wettability pattern demonstrated the ability to enhance lubricant replenishment through unidirectional interfacial forces. This finding highlights the importance of tailored surface wettability in improving lubrication, allowing for efficient oil replenishment and increased load-carrying capacity. Furthermore, we explored the potential of the interlaced wettability pattern to improve oil supply on the lubrication track. This pattern led to a redistribution of lubricant in the form of droplets, primarily on the hydrophilic patches. This phenomenon was attributed to the unbalanced interfacial forces between the hydrophilic and hydrophobic patches. The results indicated that the interlaced wettability pattern outperformed the stripe wettability pattern in terms of oil replenishment. Obj.4) To experimentally characterize the influence of dewetting on lubricating film building and friction under LLS. (*Details can be found in Paper [2] in Part C.) A series of experiments involving interferometry measurements, fluorescence observations, and stearic acid adsorption were conducted to achieve the objective. The findings reveal that the adsorption of stearic acid weakens the wettability of the lubricated track, leading to the occurrence of ‘dewetting’ in the lubricating oil. This dewetting process results in the formation of discrete oil distribution, accumulating oil at the bearing entrance to create oil reservoirs. These reservoirs generate additional inlet pressure due to surface tension, thereby increasing the capacity for oil film formation. Consequently, the resulting oil film thickness is even higher compared to fully flooded conditions. However, regarding friction measurements, the test rig did not yield the desired results. It lacked the necessary sensitivity to confirm the reduction in friction caused by dewetting. This limitation indicates an area for further work. Nevertheless, it is worth noting that the lack of friction data does not affect the conclusions drawn from optical measurements of lubricant film thickness. The study also found that the morphologies of the adsorbed stearic acid layers on the glass and steel blocks showed nanoscale granular bulges and brush-like structures, respectively. Surface materials can affect the adsorption of stearic acid, thereby affecting the dewetting phenomenon and lubrication performance. Obj.5) To build a lubrication model with lubricant supply by oil droplets and develop an efficient numerical procedure to theoretically explain the experimental findings. (*Details can be found in Paper [1] in Part C.) The objective was successfully achieved, providing valuable insights into the lubrication process that challenged conventional concepts. Traditionally, it is believed that strong surface wettability promotes the formation of lubricating films. However, this study shows that providing a limited lubricant supply in the form of oil droplets can enhance lubrication performance. This surprising finding is supported by the developed models and numerical analyses, which show that oil droplets can initiate oil film pressure earlier upon contact with the bearing. Early initiation of pressure results in a greater load-carrying capacity and thus improved lubricating performance. Moreover, the study explored the effects of various factors on lubrication performance, including the specific number of droplets, the quantity of lubricant supplied, and the shape of the droplets. By considering all these variables, the study provided a more nuanced understanding of the lubrication process. The ultimate load-carrying capacity is not solely determined by a single factor, but rather by the synergistic effect of all these variables. The achievement of this objective not only contributes to the theoretical understanding of the lubrication process, but also holds practical significance for improving lubrication. The developed models and numerical procedures have proven to be efficient tools for exploring these possibilities, paving the way for further research and innovation in this field.

11216619.label: Major findings and research outcome
11216619.value: 1. Advantage of dewetting oil bead lubrication. Our experimental and modeling results proved that under limited lubricant supply (LLS), supplying oil in the form of droplets yields superior lubrication performance compared to a uniform oil supply layer. This is attributed to the early generation of film pressure by the droplets upon contact with the bearing surfaces, resulting in a higher load-carrying capacity. The quantity of droplets significantly influences lubrication. Additionally, selecting the appropriate height-to-radius ratio of the droplets can achieve good lubrication performance. Understanding the benefits of film formation by oil droplets requires considering factors like film pressure generation position, load-carrying area at the contact entrance, amount of oil dragged, and droplet size. The resultant load-carrying capacity arises from a synergistic effect of all these factors. (Papers [1]and [3]) 2. Resolving the puzzling experimental result that LLS can generate higher oil film thickness than fully flooding oil supply. Years ago, we made a perplexing observation during an experiment where, under certain bearing starvation conditions, the oil film thickness exceeded the theoretical fully flooded film thickness. This study revealed that adding a small amount of stearic acid to the oil created an adsorption layer on the bearing surface. This layer weakens the wettability of the lubricated track, leading to the ‘dewetting’ phenomenon. This dewetting caused discrete oil distribution, accumulating as oil reservoirs at the bearing entrance. These reservoirs create additional inlet pressure due to surface tension, enhancing oil film formation capacity. Thus, this study clarifies the enigma, explaining how LLS can achieve higher film thickness than fully flooded oil supply. (Paper [2]) 3. An efficient interlaced wettability pattern devised We successfully devised an interlaced wettability pattern on the lubrication track that facilitates the formation of dewetting oil beads in distinct rows. This pattern comprises alternating oleophobic and oleophilic parallel domains. The interlaced oil bead pattern outperforms randomly formed oil beads on the track. (Paper [3]) 4. Contact angle of dewetting oil droplet matched receding contact angle of the surface. The study revealed that the contact angle of dewetting oil beads closely matched the receding contact angle (RCA) of the surface. This finding allows us to make a reasonable estimation of the contact angle of the dewetting oil beads, which would otherwise be challenging or even impossible to determine in-situ. (Conference paper [C2])

11216619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216619.value: This project has identified several promising aspects of dewetting oil droplet lubrication in comparison to conventional methods. However, there are still areas that require further investigation. First, the interplay between surface wettability, original oil film thickness, and final size or height of the dewetting oil droplets needs to be explored. Second, to optimize the method, it is important to explore the optimal droplet size and distribution that will yield the most effective lubrication performance for bearings. Third, while this study addressed the impact of surface wettability on droplet formation, other essential lubricant properties such as viscosity, surface tension, and chemical composition need to be considered to achieve a comprehensive understanding. Lastly, the research primarily examined short-term lubrication performance, leaving a vacuum in the knowledge regarding the long-term durability and wear patterns of bearings under oil droplet lubrication. Addressing this gap will contribute to a more thorough and practical understanding of oil droplet lubrication, potentially enhancing machinery performance and extending the lifespan of mechanical systems across various industries.

11216619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216619.value: This project aimed to find a better way to supply lubricant to bearings, which helps reduce energy waste. The researchers wanted to make sure bearings to be well lubricated even with only limited amounts of lubricant available. Traditionally, it was believed that having a smooth, even layer of oil on the surface of the bearings was the best approach. However, the study discovered something surprising. Instead of using a smooth even oil layer, using small oil droplets on the surface actually worked better to keep the bearings well-lubricated. These droplets naturally form on surfaces that do not attract oil very well. The researchers used computer models and experiments to understand how this process works. They also looked at different ways the oil droplets can form and how they affect the lubrication. These findings are important for improving how we lubricate machines in engineering. This new knowledge about how surfaces interact with oil and how the lubricant moves can lead to better lubrication technologies. This can make machines more efficient, reduce damage, and make them last longer in different industries.

11216819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11216819.value: Hong Kong has one of the busiest road networks in the world which carries 70% of local daily trips despite its highly developed metro system. With the limited road space, sustainable development relies on enhancing and maintaining the attractiveness of high-capacity buses over private and low-capacity vehicles. This calls for transforming the traditional road management philosophy from minimising delay for general traffic to maximising service level of high-capacity buses. For service monitoring and management, many buses nowadays are tracked with GPS (Global Positioning System) in real-time. With this real-time tracking, conventional bus-oriented traffic control systems primarily aim to reduce buses’ running times through providing them signal priority. It is however noted that the effectiveness of bus signal priority is highly dependent on prevailing traffic conditions. Without reliable estimates of its traffic impact, bus signal priority could also induce significant and unnecessary general traffic delays which would deteriorate the bus services in return due to onset of congestion. An effective bus service management system should consider and adopt different control objective settings according to prevailing traffic conditions. It should also be able to capture dynamics of both general traffic and buses with all relevant data sources. This project aims to develop a multi-objective signal optimisation framework for urban bus services. The objectives considered herein include buses’ running times, headway deviations, and delays of general traffic. The framework operates on a hybrid model which consists of interacting macroscopic and microscopic components. The macroscopic component models dynamic network traffic flow with the fundamental diagram. This allows the model to capture traffic characteristics ranging from free-flow to oversaturated conditions. The microscopic component models trajectories of individual buses and their interaction with surrounding traffic flow. Its hybrid nature allows the model to incorporate both flow-based data of general traffic and trajectory-based GPS data of buses. Recognising that different buses would request for timing plan changes at different intersections at different times, the optimisation framework will be solved by a decentralised algorithm which allows it to accommodate effectively the asynchronous timing plan change requests from different buses. The optimisation framework will be tested through a selected real-world scenario. The effect of different decomposition schemes and algorithmic designs in the decentralised solution procedure on global performance will be investigated over different traffic conditions. The project contributes to network-wide public transport management by introducing hybrid traffic modelling and decentralised optimisation techniques with use of GPS data. 儘管其高度發達的地鐵系統，香港仍擁有世界其中一個最繁忙的道路網。城市可持續發展依賴於保持和增強大容量公交車的吸引力。時下許多公交車都裝有GPS （全球定位）系統以用於服務監控和管理。通過這種實時跟踪，傳統的交通控制系統主要旨在通過提供信號優先級來減少公交車的運行時間。然而，系統的有效性高度依賴於實時交通狀況。如沒有其對交通影響的可靠估計，公交信號也可能引起顯著且不必要的交通延遲。有效的公交信號管理系統應根據實時的交通狀況採用不同的控制目標設置。它應該也能夠捕捉到的動態都一般交通和公共汽車的所有相關數據源。這項目旨在開發一種多目標城市公交信號優化框架。目標函數包括公交汽車的運行時間，進展偏差，一般交通延遲。所述框架包括宏觀和微觀模型部件。宏觀模型計量從自由流動到超飽和條件的一般交通特徵。微觀組件模擬各公交車的軌跡以及與周圍交通流的紅外交互。此項目通過引入混合交通建模和利用GPS數據的分散優化技術，為全網公共交通管理做出貢獻。

11216819.label: Realisation of objectives
11216819.value: The goal of the proposed project is to develop a multi-objective network signal optimisation framework that maximises bus service performance driven by both flow-based and GPS traffic data in congested networks. The project includes three specific objectives, aiming to: 1) develop a hybrid network model that can take both macroscopic flow-based and microscopic trajectory-based data and state variables with consideration of oversaturated conditions; 2) develop a multi-objective network-wide bus service modelling and optimisation framework that can be driven by both flow-based traffic volume and trajectory-based GPS data; 3) develop an effective decentralised solution algorithm that can accommodate asynchronous requests from buses for timing plan re-optimisation. The three objectives have all been successfully completed and our research work has led to output of three publications in top-tier journals: 1) Su, Z.C., Chow, A.H.F.*, Zhong, R.X. (2021) Adaptive network traffic control with an integrated model-based and data-driven approach and a decentralised solution method. Transportation Research Part C, 128, 103154. 2) Chow, A.H.F.*, Su, Z.C., Liang, E., Zhong, R.X. (2021) Adaptive signal control for bus service reliability with connected vehicle technology via reinforcement learning. Transportation Research Part C, 129, 103264. 3) Su, Z.C., Chow, A.H.F.*, Fang, C.L., Liang, E.M., Zhong, R.X. (2023) Hierarchical control for stochastic network traffic with reinforcement learning. Transportation Research Part B, 167, 196-216. Specifically, Su et al. (2021) reported our work on development of the hybrid network model (Objective 1) and a decentralised computational approach (Objective 3) for deriving real time signal timing adjustments over different traffic conditions. The solution procedure is implemented via a gradient search approach with use of an approximate dynamic programming approach in which the state space of the optimisation problem was approximated by using linear kernel functions for reducing computational complexity. Chow et al. (2021) extended the framework developed in Su et al. (2021) to incorporate bus trajectory data and operations (Objective 2), in which the signal timing plans were derived through a reinforcement learning approach with artificial neural network surrogates were applied to approximate the state and decision spaces of the optimisation problem for reducing computational complexity. The optimization framework was implemented and tested on a case study built by using actual scenario data collected in London (UK). Su et al. (2023) further built a hierarchical control framework that integrated work done in Su et al. (2021) and Chow et al. (2021) to large-scale network-wide operations with use of macroscopic network dynamic approximation function. The above work has led to a PhD degree awarded to Su in 2022, see: 4) Su, Z.C. (2022) Adaptive Network Traffic Control with Reinforcement Learning. PhD thesis, City University of Hong Kong.

11216819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11216819.value: The project contributes to the design of adaptive urban traffic control with consideration of bus service reliability with use of connected vehicle and advanced optimisation techniques. This offers potential for inclusion of advanced technology into urban traffic management framework. The computational efficiency developed via use of approximate dynamic programming and reinforcement learning techniques also allows us to expand the scale of applications in future studies. This includes incorporation of decision variables associated with provision of individual travel guidance and individual bus speed control via the connected vehicle technology. In fact, the project has lead to an award of a Smart Traffic Fund by the Hong Kong Transport Department, with which we are researching the application of the methodology developed herein to real world applications with use of machine learning and internet-of-things technologies.

11216819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11216819.value: This project developed a traffic signal control framework for enhancing performance of urban bus services. The objectives of the control framework include reducing buses’ running times, variability, and delays of general traffic. The control framework copes with data collected from different sources ranging from traditional loop detectors to GPS devices attached to individual bus vehicles. Considering the large amount of information and control decisions encountered in real time, the project developed a computational framework using reinforcement learning techniques for reducing the computational time and complexity. Recognising that different buses would request for timing plan changes at different intersections at different times, the control framework is designed such that it can be solved by a decentralised algorithm which allows it to accommodate effectively the asynchronous timing plan change requests from different buses. The optimisation framework has been tested by real-world scenarios. The effect of different decomposition schemes and algorithmic designs in the decentralised solution procedure on global performance was investigated over different traffic conditions. The project contributes to network-wide public transport management by introducing reinforcement learning and decentralised optimisation techniques with use of advanced traffic models.

11217019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217019.value: Zebrafish is one of the most important model organisms in biology. Zebrafish behavioral studies, such as the profiling of the Light-Induced Locomotor Response (LLR), have been applied in drug discovery and neurological analyses. Multiple zebrafish larvae can be tracked concurrently. The short experiment cycle is suitable to large-scale study. The lack of mathematical models describing LLR, however, limits interpretation of the screening results. Variance in visual-motor system development can be high, whereas traditional measures to identify behavioral difference may be insufficient to experiments with diverse factors. Therefore, we propose the development of computational methods to investigate zebrafish LLR, which will be useful to the study of environmental factors, such as millimeter wave (mmWave), and drug screening applications. The human body exposes to electromagnetic field (EMF) of different frequency ranges in daily life. With the increasing prolonged use of mobile devices, the safety of related EMF on the nervous system is a public concern. The World Health Organization has recommended large-scale long-term study on mobile phone users. The majority of existing studies are unable to establish a link between EMF in wireless communications and health issues. Few studies showed that thermal effects of mmWave exposure affected the neuron excitability and the metabolism of a neurotransmitter. Despite decades of research, mmWave effects remain controversial due to technical challenges such as the limited sample size in experiments that involve animal models. In this project, we will expand the high-throughput platform to investigate mmWave influence on the neural system of zebrafish larvae using significantly reduced experimental preparation and analysis time. We will develop a transverse electromagnetic cell for generating a millimeter band electric field with plane waves that reach the zebrafish larvae in shallow water tank at controlled power, and LLR of zebrafish exposed to mmWave can be tracked. By using machine learning techniques, we will investigate if there will be change(s) in LLR induced within power level of mmWave in the current communications standards. If LLRs of the controls and mmWave exposed zebrafish larvae are indistinguishable, mmWave radiation level tested has no observable effect to the zebrafish visual-motor system. Separately, the LLR of zebrafish mutants lacking various genes for cognitive behaviors, with or without the treatment of a chemical library including neuronal signaling molecules, will be tracked. This will help elucidate the possible biological basis of mmWave interaction if there is an observable change in LLR similar to known genetic mutations and/or drug treatment. 斑馬魚是生物學中最重要的生物模型之一。斑馬魚行為研究已應用於藥物和神經學分析。然而，神經系統發育的差異可能很大，而傳統識別行為差異的方法可能不足以進行各種因素的實驗。因此，我們提出開發新型計算方法來研究斑馬魚的行為，這將有助於研究環境因素，如毫米波和藥物篩選應用。 人體暴露於日常生活中不同頻率範圍的電磁場。隨著移動設備的長期使用的增加，相關電磁場對神經系統的安全性成為公眾關注的問題。世界衛生組織曾建議對手機用戶進行大規模的長期研究。現有大多數研究認為無線通信中的電磁場不會導致健康問題。另有少數研究毫米波暴露的熱效應會否影響神經元和神經遞質的代謝。儘管進行了數十年的研究，但由於技術方面的挑戰，毫米波效應仍然存在爭議。在這個項目中，我們將發展新型高通量平台，研究毫米波會否對斑馬魚神經系統的影響。 我們將開發一種橫向電磁池，用於產生毫米波段電場，其平面波可以受控功率到達淺水槽中的斑馬魚。同時系統可以跟踪暴露於毫米波的斑馬魚的行為。通過使用機器學習技術，我們將研究在當前通信標準中是否會在毫米波的功率水平內引起的行為發生變化。如果對照和在毫米波長期暴露的斑馬魚的行為難以區分，則測試的毫米波水平對斑馬魚神經系統沒有可觀察到的影響。

11217019.label: Realisation of objectives
11217019.value: The primary objective of this project was to investigate potential changes in zebrafish behavior resulting from exposure to millimeter-wave radiation. This key objective was fully achieved through the successful completion of experiments exposing zebrafish embryos to millimeter waves and quantitatively analyzing the locomotor patterns of zebrafish larvae in response to light/dark stimuli. The results demonstrated a transient increase in alternating dark-induced locomotor activity after exposure, indicating potential effects on neurodevelopmental factors regulating locomotion. These findings provide valuable insights into the biological impacts of millimeter waves and lay the groundwork for future research on mechanisms and safety limits. Therefore, the project fulfilled its central aim of studying behavioral effects in an important model organism. This project was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic, posing unforeseen challenges from the very beginning. Campus closures and social distancing restrictions significantly impacted research efficiency. The team faced difficulties accessing lab equipment needed for designing the exposure setup and performing simulations. Collaboration was also hampered by the inability to meet in person, slowing iterative improvements to the methodology. Procuring equipment and supplies was delayed by shipment issues during lockdowns. Furthermore, the original co-investigator, Prof. Michael Lam, unexpectedly resigned from his faculty position midway through the project. This sudden loss of our zebrafish biology expert was a major setback. We had to restart all zebrafish experiments with a new collaborator, Prof. Cheng Shuk Han. Fortunately, with Prof. Cheng's generous support, we successfully completed the zebrafish experiments, overcoming this significant hurdle. In addition to the core objective of analyzing zebrafish locomotor activity after millimeter wave exposure, we pursued supplementary aims to strengthen the study. We performed extensive simulations to characterize the millimeter wave exposure under water and assessed the temperature within zebrafish larvae during exposure to rule out thermal effects. Furthermore, we tested a range of exposure durations and post-exposure timepoints to provide a more comprehensive perspective. Our collaborator took rigorous precautions to minimize confounding factors. Beyond just locomotor activity, we also performed morphological assessments of the zebrafish eye and brain to identify potential anatomical changes resulting from millimeter wave exposure. Using fluorescence microscopy, Cheng’s team imaged the eyes and distinct brain regions including the forebrain, midbrain, and hindbrain. We then quantified and compared the dimensions of these structures between the exposed and control groups. This morphological analysis enabled us to determine if the radiation exposure impacted the size and development of key neural structures involved in visual processing and locomotor control. We conducted the measurements at multiple time points post-exposure to assess whether any effects were temporary or persistent. Analysis revealed temporary enlargements of the eye and whole brain/midbrain at 5 days post-fertilization in the exposed groups, but these differences disappeared by 8 days development. This anatomical dimension complemented the behavioral findings. During pandemic restrictions that prevented laboratory experiments, our team pursued computational studies to advance the project's goals. we developed machine learning tools to automatically classify behavior into categories like freezing and erratic movement from video footage, which will enable more rapid, quantitative evaluation of locomotor patterns in future experiments. The classifier was tested on feeding experiments in mice which contributed to a paper in Neuron. Additionally, some lab members had developed a deep learning technique called Community Channel-Net (CC-Net) that could potentially be applied to analyze interactions between neuroanatomical features or behavioral metrics extracted from the zebrafish data. The algorithm was published in Pattern Recognition. However, given the ambitious timeline and scope of re-establishing the experimental platform and conducting the comprehensive analyses, the research team prioritized robust statistical methods and data visualization to directly extract insights from the experimental observations. This allowed us to focus on the primary objectives of characterizing the biological impacts of millimeter-wave exposure using the innovative zebrafish platform. As a summary, this project successfully achieved its central goal of investigating millimeter-wave effects on zebrafish behavior, producing valuable findings that lay the foundation for future research in this important area. Despite the significant challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic and the loss of a key collaborator, the research team overcame these obstacles to deliver a comprehensive study that combines behavioral, anatomical, and computational analyses. This research lays the foundation for future large-scale studies on the environmental safety of ubiquitous cell phone and WiFi radiation. In this initial study, no persistent change was observed, and long-term ecological effects of chronic exposure remain unknown. Overall, this pioneering work enhances our ability to rigorously evaluate ecological impacts of the growing wireless radiation introduced from future technologies.

11217019.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217019.value: This project aimed to investigate the effects of radio frequency electromagnetic radiation exposure, mimicking real-world conditions, on neuroanatomy and behavior in developing zebrafish embryos. We developed an adjustable platform with a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) cell system to replicate exposure at 900 MHz frequency and 1.6-2 W/kg specific absorption rates matching upper safety limit of wireless radiation level in the immediate vicinity of cell phone. The TEM cell allowed precise control and measurement of the uniform radio wave exposure experienced by the zebrafish embryos submerged in water. Zebrafish embryos were exposed to these radio waves for prolonged period post-fertilization. The embryos’ brains and eyes were then checked for any changes in size and structure. Their swimming behaviors in response to light were also tracked to detect effects on the nervous system. Analysis of the embryos' brain and eye dimensions revealed temporary enlargements at 5 days post-fertilization in the groups exposed to cell phone radiation, including increased eye size and whole brain/midbrain dimensions compared to controls. However, these size differences disappeared by 8 days development, meaning the effects were transient and not permanent. Behavioral assessments utilizing a light-induced swimming test showed potential short-term subtle impacts to activities of larvae from embryos exposed to cell phone radiation. However, their startle responses to sudden light changes appeared normal, indicating no vision impairment. By 8 days post-fertilization, swimming behaviors were comparable between radiation-exposed and control groups, suggesting the behavioral effects were also not permanent. As a summary, this pioneering study provides valuable insights into biological effects of exposure to the radiofrequency radiation. The innovative zebrafish model allows rapid, scalable analysis of morphological and behavioral alterations. While no persistent adverse outcomes were observed with short-term exposure, long-term impacts remain unknown. Major results are accepted for publication in IEEE Open Journal of Engineering in Medicine and Biology for public access of these findings.

11217019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217019.value: This initial study established a novel platform to evaluate biological impacts of wireless radiation exposure. As no persistent effects were observed with short-term highest-level exposure, the next phase could probe long-term low-level exposures mimicking real-world conditions. Extending the exposure over the full zebrafish lifespan could reveal long-term impacts not detectable in early development. While valuable insights were gained with this pioneering methodology, considerable work remains to investigate the ecological consequences of our growing wireless footprint. Overall, this initial study delivered an efficient tool to probe an important question and established a strong foundation for targeted future investigation.

11217019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217019.value: This research explores how the radiofrequency radiation affects the development of zebrafish, which represent many biological similarities with aquatic life. The study developed a first-of-its-kind high-throughput, low-cost test platform to efficiently expose fish embryos to maximal wireless radiation levels for prolonged period in the immediate vicinity of cell phone. This allows us to rapidly screen for potential impacts on ecosystems. The results showed temporary increases in eye and brain size along with slight behavior changes in zebrafish embryos exposed to highest cell phone radiation levels for a prolonged duration during development. These differences disappeared by 8 days of development, meaning the effects were not permanent even at the highest intensities. The high-throughput platform created can rapidly screen for biological impacts from wireless radiation exposure at levels above typical environmental level. This research lays the foundation for future large-scale studies on the environmental safety of ubiquitous cell phone and WiFi radiation. In this initial study, no persistent change was observed, and long-term ecological effects of chronic exposure remain unknown. Overall, this pioneering work enhances our ability to rigorously evaluate ecological impacts of the growing wireless radiation introduced from future technologies.

11217319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217319.value: In the past decades, many super high-rise buildings have been built in the Asia-pacific region. There at least 5 over 500m tall buildings are under construction in China namely, Suzhou Zhongnan Center (729m), Shenzhen Pingan IFC (660m), Wuhan Greenland Center (636m), Shanghai Tower (632m) and Tianjin Goldin Finance Center (597m) and it is likely that 1km tall buildings will be constructed in the near future. One of the prime concerns on the design of these buildings will be the safety issue. Means of protection again various hazards, such as fire, earthquake and wind effect have been extensively studied. As zero risk situation may not be achieved and absolute assurance of safe building conditions is impossible, mitigation strategies should be considered at design stage. To mitigate the ill-effect on people, evacuating them from the hazardous environment is one of the mitigation strategies. However, requiring occupants to escape from a super tall building by their own effort within a short period of time is difficult. Using mechanical means, such as elevators, to assist people to escape in supertall buildings is therefore considered by researchers, building designers as well as the governments. However, it is conventionally not to allow using elevators for evacuation because of evacuees’ safety in the elevators, capacity of elevators to transport people, firemen’s usage of elevators for firefighting operation. Some firefighting operators may believe that occupants, if they have not been directly affected by fire, should remain in the premises and await for the firemen to extinguish the fire. After the 9/11 event, engineers and researchers have re-considered the use of elevators to assist total evacuation as people have noticed the collapse of buildings. The International Building Codes of the US has subsequently included this consideration, yet the effectiveness of using elevators for escape has not been fully explored. On the basis of the emerging ICT, smart elevator evacuation system can be established under the smart building regime. The purpose of this project is to identify the issues of using elevators for evacuation in super tall buildings, to establish an elevator evacuation algorithm which integrates with smart control system on the basis of smart sensors, to review the building legislations for elevator evacuation and to arrange a forum for disseminate research findings and soliciting views for compiling guidelines for implementing elevator evacuation system. 在过去的几十年里，超高层建筑在亚太地区兴起。在设计这些高楼的时候，其中一个最关心的问题就是安全问题。超高层建筑中针对火灾、地震以及风力等各种危害的保护措施已经有广泛的研究，但零风险和绝对安全的状态是无法实现，因此应该在设计阶段考虑缓解策略。其中，及时将处于危险环境中的人们安全疏散是有效的缓解策略之一，但要求他们在短时间内依靠自己撤离超高层建筑物是很困难的。因此，研究人员、建筑设计师以及政府都在考虑利用电梯等机械手段来帮助人们安全撤离超高层建筑。可按照现有的法律法规来说是不允许利用电梯来进行紧急疏散的，因为人员在电梯中的安全性无法保证、并且电梯运输人员的能力有限，消防员会使用电梯进行消防操作。911事件后，工程师和研究人员重新考虑使用电梯来帮助所有人来完成疏散。随后，美国建筑规范也将其纳入考虑范围，但使用电梯来辅助逃生的有效性尚未被探索完全。基于新兴的信息通信技术，我们可以将智能电梯疏散系统纳入智能建筑体系中。这研究目标是探讨在超高层建筑中使用电梯进行疏散时存在的关键问题，并基于智能传感器来建立一种结合智能控制系统的电梯疏散算法，调研有关利用电梯进行疏散的建筑法规等。

11217319.label: Realisation of objectives
11217319.value: (1) The current research works, engineering practice and legislation on the use of elevators for evacuation and the corresponding legislation relating to the use of elevators in fire was thoroughly reviewed. It was discovered that using elevators for fire evacuation is currently prohibited by regulations in various countries and regions. While the International Building Code (IBC) acknowledges that elevators may be utilized for self-evacuation during a fire, provided specific safety requirements are met, and some evacuation drills in ultra-high-rise buildings have demonstrated the effectiveness of elevator evacuation, very few authorities actually implement elevators as a means of a fire evacuation. The output of this work aims to address this concern and provide a more effective approach for utilizing elevators in the fire evacuation of high-rise buildings. (2) The various issues of using elevators for evacuation were identified. The concerns come from two major parts. The first concern pertains to safety, as there is a potential for elevator call button malfunctions or power failures during the evacuation process. These factors could hinder the effectiveness of elevator evacuation during a fire emergency. The second concern relates to the overall efficiency of evacuation. Enabling all occupants to utilize elevators for evacuation may lead to increased wait times, reducing the efficiency of the evacuation process. This can pose additional risks and hinder the overall effectiveness of a complete evacuation. The proposed smart elevator-aided building fire evacuation scheme was improved from these two major concerns. (3) The research team conducted a comprehensive review of the information needs, means of data transmission, and potential services and applications in smart building fire evacuation. Moreover, an IoT-based system architecture for smart fire evacuation in high-rise buildings was developed. Information needs for smart fire evacuation encompassed fire hazard monitoring, people counting, and evacuation guidance. Accordingly, their information-sensing devices and means of data transmission were carefully designed. Furthermore, several potential services and applications for building fire evacuation were analyzed. These included an in-depth understanding of fire ground information, predicting fire-influenced hazardous areas, and implementing a smart elevator-aided building fire evacuation scheme. By using specific models and algorithms to enable these functional modules, the team proposed an effective architecture of a smart elevator-assisted fire evacuation system. (4) In this research, a bi-level elevator-aided evacuation strategy optimization model was developed. The optimization model considers both dynamic information of occupants and fire hazards. The upper-level strategy of the model focuses on prospective emergency elevator dispatch strategies that prioritize the safety of elevator evacuation operations by adhering to prescribed dispatch logic. The lower-level evacuation strategy determines the appropriate proportion of occupants utilizing staircases and elevators for evacuation. This optimization ensures a balance between using elevators for efficiency and promoting safe evacuation practices. By employing this strategy optimization model, it becomes possible to conduct fire evacuation assisted by elevators in a safe and efficient manner. (5) The practicability of smart elevator-assisted evacuation was demonstrated. A simplified prototype for planning the optimal evacuation strategy based on the on-site fire and occupant count information was developed. The development of the system follows the general architecture of an IoT system. In the perception layer, fire detectors and visual-based occupant counters were installed to measure environmental temperatures and occupant counts. Hereafter, the network layer was established. The collected sensor data was transmitted through a wire connection to input into an IoT gateway, which directly connects with a local computer. With the collected sensor data successfully stored in a local database, we were able to recall the data and analyze the optimal vertical evacuation strategy based on a series of self-developed program modules. The evacuation strategy planning program was developed based on Python 3.8 and Qt C++. Ultimately, a GUI platform based on LabVIEW was established to visualize the monitoring data and output the suggested evacuation strategy. (6) While the research outputs have demonstrated the effectiveness and efficiency of smart elevator evacuation systems, there are practical challenges that need to be addressed. One major challenge is the need for upgrades to the existing elevator systems in order to implement elevator evacuation effectively. Qualified occupant evacuation elevators must comply with multiple requirements, such as enhanced monitoring, electrical power backup, hoistway enclosure protection, and integration with fire alarm systems. These upgrades increase the costs and time required by contractors. However, since fires may not occur during the lifetime of elevators in most cases, implementing occupant evacuation elevators may not provide satisfactory returns for contractors. Another concern is the reliability of elevator operations during fire emergencies, as there may be unacceptable scenarios where elevator evacuation is affected. These concerns should be carefully addressed to ensure the safety and effectiveness of elevator evacuation systems. However, considering the increasing global aging population and the construction of high-rise apartment buildings in elderly community estates in recent years, there is a growing concern about the ability of elderly individuals to evacuate through stairs during high-rise building fires. Therefore, suggestions should be made to the authorities to address these practical challenges and concerns. They should consider the specific needs of vulnerable populations, such as the elderly, and explore the potential of elevator evacuation as a viable solution. Additionally, comprehensive testing and validation procedures should be established to ensure the reliability and safety of elevator operations during fire emergencies.

11217319.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217319.value: To facilitate effectiveness and efficient elevator evacuation in fire emergencies, research on smart fire risk situational awareness and planning of elevator assisted evacuation strategies was undertaken. In this project, a machine learning (ML)-based fire situational awareness model was developed. The model utilized on-site temperature sensor measurements to identify the fire source and stages of fire development. This model provided intelligent situational awareness of fire risks, enabling informed decision-making for elevator operation control to ensure safety. The research findings were published in reputable fire safety and building engineering journals [Part C 8.1, 8.2 refer]. In addition, an IoT-based system architecture for smart fire evacuation in high-rise buildings was devised to enable comprehensive on-site information collection and facilitate scientific and appropriate decision-making for elevator evacuation strategies. The outcomes of this research work were published in an open-access SCI journal, obtaining significant attention with over 4000 reads and 28 citations [Part C 8.3 refers]. Moreover, the concept of situational awareness-based planning and decision-making was expanded to explore pedestrians' walking behaviors on a larger scale area. This research, published in an SCI journal [Part C 8.4 refers], delved into the utilization of IoT and other sensing technologies to capture human behavior in broader urban or regional contexts, paving the way for future research on human control in these areas. To improve the safety and efficiency of occupant evacuation on building floors before entering elevators, a machine learning model was proposed for short-term prediction of fire-hazardous areas. This model assisted occupants in finding optimal escape routes to reach elevator lobbies. The research work on this model has been submitted to a top-ranked computer SCI journal [Part C 8.5 refers]. Furthermore, a PhD student (graduated in October 2023), under the supervision of the PI, has been trained. The research title of the PhD student is “System Architecture for Smart Fire Evacuation in High-Rise Buildings” [Part C 10.1 refers]. The student’s thesis included the proposed algorithm for elevator evacuation strategy planning, along with a small demonstration of the prototype generated from this research project.

11217319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217319.value: Currently, stair evacuation still remains the primary method for evacuating high-rise buildings. However, considering the increasing global aging population and the construction of high-rise apartment buildings in elderly community estates in recent years, there is a growing concern about the ability of elderly individuals to evacuate through stairs during high-rise building fires. This research project proposes a smart elevator-assisted evacuation scheme that combines IoT, smart sensors, and model algorithms. The outcomes of this project explore the utilization of elevators for high-rise building evacuation while addressing the concerns of relevant authorities and stakeholders. In the future, substantial research efforts can be dedicated to extending and modifying the model to apply it to more dynamic situations. Furthermore, comprehensive testing and validation procedures need to be established to ensure the reliability and safety of elevator operations during fire emergencies, encompassing both hardware and software aspects. It is also crucial to conduct experimental studies to assess the performance of smart elevator evacuation systems. Additionally, surveys and field studies can be conducted to gather insights into occupants' attitudes and suggestions regarding the use of elevator evacuation systems.

11217319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217319.value: Staircase evacuation is the major means of fire evacuation for current high-rise residential buildings. However, with the growing number of senior citizens living in these buildings, the feasibility of relying solely on staircases for evacuation may be questioned. The physical limitations and mobility impairments of elderly individuals can hinder successful staircase evacuation. Therefore, it is reasonable to consider using elevators as part of the overall evacuation strategy. In this study, a smart elevator-aided building fire evacuation scheme was proposed. This solution supports the use of elevators for evacuation by determining a safe and efficient strategy based on in-depth information about the fire and the number of occupants present. A simulated case study was conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme in a typical high-rise residential building. Apart from keeping the elevator evacuation safe, the planned elevator-aided evacuation strategy could save 38.0% of the time compared with the strategy using only staircases in the scene. The findings and outcomes of this study provide valuable insights into the potential of using elevators for evacuation in high-rise buildings. In addition, it encourages further studies and practical implementations of elevator evacuation strategies.

11217619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11217619.value: Systems of networked robotic vehicles have been widely applied for various tasks in recent years. Examples include large area surveillance, emergency building survey, and ocean trash collection. Such systems belong to the so-called multi-agent systems (MASs), and each robotic vehicle in the system is usually referred to as an agent. To achieve coordinated maneuvering, the cooperative control of MASs has been extensively studied in the robotics and control community since the early 2000s. Numerous researchers, including the PI, have recently been working on the cooperative control of heterogeneous MASs with time-varying network topologies. This research has been motivated by real-world missions where agents often have different dynamics or are subject to uncertainties, with communication network topologies among agents being time-varying due to environment change or vehicle failure. It has been proved that a reference internal model is necessary and sufficient for the output consensus/tracking of heterogeneous linear MASs, which is the most fundamental problem concerning this topic. Furthermore, most approaches to this problem often require that certain state information of the local controllers can be exchanged through a communication network. However, this is not feasible in many practical scenarios for the following reasons: 1) communication resources are too limited to exchange such large amounts of information; 2) communication between agents is not available or reliable due to environmental constraints; or 3) agents are not equipped with communication units. To address this issue, it is desirable to develop distributed control strategies based on pure output feedback in the sense that: 1) only the output information of individual agents is used by the controller, and 2) only the output information of neighboring agents is exchanged through the communication network. In this project, we aim to investigate tracking control problems of heterogeneous MASs with time-varying network topologies based on pure output feedback. In particular, several types of heterogeneous uncertain MASs will be studied, including general linear, second-order nonlinear, and a typical class of higher order nonlinear MASs. New stabilization techniques will be proposed. The developed control approaches will be validated via their application to tracking control of a group of mobile robots. The anticipated results of this research project will not only provide an alternative way to solve fundamental problems in robotic vehicles networks but also facilitate applications of coordinated maneuvering in real mission scenarios. This project is thus of both significant academic interest and practical importance. 為實現環境監測、屋宇測量和海洋垃圾收集等，需要應用網絡化機器人系統。這類系統屬於多智能體系統，每個機器人運載器被稱為智能體。自21世紀初以來，多智能體系統協同控制在機器人和控制領域被廣泛研究。在現實任務中，智能體通常具有不同的動態或具有不確定性，且智能體之間的通信網絡拓撲是時變的。為求解異質線性多智能體系統的輸出一致/跟蹤問題，文獻中的大部分方法需要通過通信網絡交換控制器的狀態信息。然而，由於通信資源受限，或者智能體之間通信不可靠，或者智能體未安裝通信單元，交換控制器的狀態信息在眾多實際情形中是不可行的。為此，需要構建基於純輸出反饋的分佈式控制策略，即控制器只能利用輸出信息且通信網絡只交換相鄰智能體的輸出信息。本項目的目標是基於純輸出反饋研究具有時變網絡拓撲的異質多智能體系統的跟蹤控制問題。具體來講，本項目將研究具有一般線性、二階非線性或高階非線性動態的異質不確定多智能體系統。本項目的成果將不僅提供網絡機器人系統中基本問題的解決方法，而且促進協同控制在現實任務中的應用。

11217619.label: Major findings and research outcome
11217619.value: All project objectives have been accomplished. First, we have addressed the output consensus problem for heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems by a pure output-based feedback method. In particular, we develop a class of new reference generators to generate the consensus signal for each agent, which depends on the relative output of heterogeneous multi-agent systems. However, the coupling of the reference generators and the heterogeneous multi-agent systems causes challenges to the stability analysis of the closed-loop system. To overcome the challenges, we establish a stability result for a class of switched systems based on a low-gain design approach. By constructing multiple Lyapunov functions and designing the low gain parameter delicately, the output consensus problem of heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems is solved by the proposed pure output-based feedback control law (Lu, M. and Liu, L. 2021). Then we have investigated the consensus problem of heterogeneous second-order nonlinear uncertain multi-agent systems under switching networks by a distributed control approach. To better address the practical constraints in real-life scenarios, we consider communication delays among agents. We first introduce a distributed internal model and a distributed dynamic compensator to tackle the system uncertainties, disturbances, and unreliable network communication. Then, by some coordinate transformation and establishing a technical lemma, we show that there exists some virtual control law such that the subsystem of the closed-loop system satisfies certain input-to-state stability property. Finally, by resorting to the changing supply function technique and adopting the backstepping approach and the high gain feedback control approach, we propose a stabilization controller and obtain the solution to the consensus problem (Lu, M. and Liu, L. 2020). Moreover, we have investigated the cooperative output regulation problem for unity relative degree nonlinear multi-agent systems with dynamic edges. We design a steady-state generator for them. By only using the relative outputs of neighboring agents, we design suitable dynamic couplings between the agents and construct a pure output-feedback controller for each agent, which achieves the cooperative control objective (Wu, Y. and Liu, L. 2022). Finally, we have investigated the coordinated maneuvering control of mobile vehicles. For example, we have considered the coordinated maneuvering control problem of forming a circle with a predefined radius and specific agent distribution. To minimize information exchange among agents, we develop a distributed controller based on a cyclic pursuit strategy, where each agent only needs its leading neighbor’s position. To handle the heterogeneous communication ranges and delays simultaneously, we propose a set of new potential functions. A new Lyapunov analysis method, based on the admissible upper bound of the formation error, is established to analyze both connectivity maintenance and order preservation using the proposed potential functions. It is proved that the proposed control law can achieve the predefined formation based on the agents' output (Dou, L., Yu, X., Liu, L., Wang, X. and Feng, G. 2021; Zheng, B., Song, C. and Liu, L. 2023).

11217619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11217619.value: Several results have been obtained and published on the cooperative control of multi-agent systems based on the agents' pure output. We have also explored the impact of various communication constraints, including limited communication ranges and communication delays. At the same time, our research has identified several intriguing challenges in the cooperative control of multi-agent systems. For example, during our investigation into the data transmission mechanisms of multi-agent systems, we found a significant gap in the study of asynchronous sampling methods. This issue, particularly when agents operate at different sampling rates and experience delays, requires further investigation. These concerns are important and prevalent across various applications. Consequently, these research topics have become our recent interests and could be future research focuses.

11217619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11217619.value: Several cooperative control problems for multiple dynamic systems under various practical constraints have been addressed using distributed pure output-based control protocols. These protocols apply to numerous practical scenarios where inter-system communication is limited or even unavailable, as the output information of the systems can be directly measured. The proposed approach can be applied to typical applications such as cooperative target enclosing tasks, where a group of mobile robots are deployed to encircle a moving target. In real-world scenarios, several challenging constraints, including uncertainties in robotic dynamics, potential collisions, and limited measurement ranges, are often unavoidable and must be considered. In this project, we have taken these practical constraints into account when designing the distributed pure output-based control protocols. The techniques and approaches developed will benefit both academic research and practical engineering applications in the cooperative control of multiple dynamical systems. The expected outcomes of this project will advance the current state of cooperative control research and broaden the scope of applications for coordinating multiple mobile robots under more practical conditions.
