11219919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11219919.value: Photonic Crystals (PhC) attract great interest for a number of applications ranging from micro to nano pattering and lithography, sensors and light emission enhancement, amongst others. This is because they are easy to prepare, are cost-effective and can provide great versatility for their modification and functionalization. Coupling PhC with metals results in the hybrid plasmonic-photonic crystals (PlC) with a much enhanced optical response and functionality. Responsive photonic crystals (RPCs) are an important sub-class of PhC / PlC whose properties can be tuned externally, based on a stimulus-response mechanism that must be coupled with the photonic crystal structure. We propose to investigate the use of magnetic-core nanospheres as versatile multifunctional model devices capable to dynamically couple photonic, plasmonic and magnetic effects to create multi-functional RPCs. Superparamagnetic, ~5 nm, Fe3O4, cores are embedded in larger, ~200-300 nm in diameter, dielectrics (PMMA, SiO2, TiO2, and others) spheres labeled magnetic-core dielectric nanospheres (mc-DNS) prepared on a metallic surface. In the proposed architecture, the temperature, and thus the size and refractive index of the mc-DNS can be controlled with a variable magnetic field. We will demonstrate the ability to follow these changes in real time using our group’s original strategy, namely use of spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) and Finite Difference Tine-Domain method (SE-FDTD), which is well suited to correlate the expected changes with the effective refractive index changes in the device which will then be correlated to surface plasmon resonance (SPR) investigations. Finally, this approach will provide superb opportunities when applied to advanced SPR designs including bimetallic waveguide coupled surface plasmon resonance (Bi-WCSPR) and Fano-resonances (FR-SPR) because of additional effects such as multiple resonances and electromagnetic induced transparency provide enhanced sensitivity and additional reference points that can be used for sensing as a function of analyte concentration and applied magnetic field. In summary, this will take advantage of i) well-known strategies to assemble PhC to develop RPC based on magnetically induced thermal heating; ii) advanced SE-FDTD strategy developed by our group for quantitative optical characterization of the proposed devices; iii) sensing strategies based on advanced SPR designs; and ii) synergetic RPC capabilities and proposed SPR designs, to develop a novel two-scale reading sensor, akin to the use of a Vernier scale, to replace a single-measured value. This strategy will bring the use of PhC / PlC for point-of-care optical sensing in consumer products closer and will also find long-term applications for camouflage, security, antifraud devices and others. 光子晶體（PhC）在應用上引發研究者很大的興趣，其中包括微納米圖案和光刻，傳感器和發光增強等眾多方面的應用。這是因為它們易於製備，具有成本效益，並且可以為其修改和功能化提供極大的多功能性。將PhC與金屬偶聯導致的混合等離子體 - 光子晶體（PlC）更可大大增強光學響應和功能。響應光子晶體（RPC）是PhC / PlC的重要子類，基於必須與光子晶體結構耦合的刺激-響應機制，其性質可以在外部調整。 我們建議研究使用磁芯納米球作為靈活的多功能模型設備。此設備能夠動態耦合光子、等離子體和磁性效應，以創建多功能RPC。約5 nm的超順磁性Fe3O4核心被嵌入於較大的、直徑約200-300nm的電介質（PMMA，SiO2，TiO2等）球體。此磁芯電介質納米球（mc-DNS）將製備在金屬表面上。在此建議的架構中，mc-DNS的溫度、連同其尺寸和折射率，可以用可變磁場加以控制。使用我們小組研發的的原創策略，即使用光譜橢偏儀（SE）時域有限差分法（SE-FDTD），我們將展示實時跟踪這些變化的能力。此策略非常適用於將預期變化與器件中的有效折射率變化相關聯，並隨後將與表面等離子體共振（SPR）研究聯繋起來。最後，這種方法在應用於先進的SPR設計時將提供極好的機會，此中包括雙金屬波導耦合表面等離子共振（Bi-WCSPR）和Fano共振（FR-SPR）。因為多重共振和電磁感應透明度等附加效應提供了增強的靈敏度，以及可用於感測的附加參考點，作為分析物濃度和施加的磁場的函數。 綜上所述，此提案將利用i）眾所周知的策略來組裝PhC以開發基於磁感應加熱的RPC; ii）由我們小組開發的先進的SE-FDTD策略，對所提出的器件進行定量光學表徵; iii）基於先進SPR設計的傳感策略;和iv）協同RPC功能和提出的SPR設計，以開發一種新型的雙尺度讀數傳感器，類似於使用游標刻度，來取代單一測量值。該策略將使PhC / PlC應用於消費產品中的即時光學傳感更接近實現，並且還將可長期應用於發現偽裝，安全，防欺詐等設備上。

11219919.label: Realisation of objectives
11219919.value: We achieved all the objectives proposed for the project. We successfully prepared Fe3O4 @ SiO2 @ Au nanoparticles (NPs), (Objective 1) with a core–shell structure composed of a magnetic core diameter of tens of nm and a silica shell with thickness ranging from 260 to 350 nm. Afterwards, the Au NPs are formed on the surface of the silica shell and are demonstrated to have excellent performance as SERS substrates. We have also show that it is possible to use a permanent magnet to promote preferential alignment of these NPs (Objective 2) that are confirmed to have high stability for up to 1 year stored in powder or in solution without noticeable deterioration. The optical properties of these NPs have been studies in detail using standard effective medium approximation (EMA) strategies and Fresnel equations, as well as fully-vectorial FDTD simulations (Objectives 2 and 3). We have demonstrated the ability to disperse the three types of NPs, that is i) Fe3O4 NPs; ii) Fe3O4@SiO2 NPs; and iii) Fe3O4@SiO2@Au NPs, and to then collect them using a permanent magnet with vast applications for sensing (Objective 4). We also demonstrated that excitation of the assembled Fe3O4@SiO2 at relatively low MNPs concentrations, 5 mg/ml solution in deionized (DI) water, can result in moderate temperature increase with respect to same amount of DI only. Such temperature increase was attributed to residual convective heat transfer in the measurement configuration. The dual sensing operation (Objective 5) was successfully demonstrated using two different modes of operation. In the first mode a SPR setup was designed to operate at a Raman spectrometer in order to simultaneously collect i) the shift in the absorption of the total internal reflectance (TIR) from SPR and ii) the SERS signal from the analyte. In the second mode of operation the functionalized Fe3O4@SiO2@Au NPs and analyte where both dispersed, and allowed to interact, in solution for a given period of time after which a permanent magnet was use to concentrate the MNPs in preparation for sensing. Such sensing was done using a SERS strategy facilitated by the enhanced analyte concentration (from the MNPs enhanced concentration) and the large density of hot spots from the interaction of multiple MNPs. The use of SPR-like sensing using all-dielectric Bloch Surface Wave (BSW) 1D photonic crystals as sensor, was reported in the mid-term report. However, compared to the mid-term preliminary results, we now demonstrate much better sensing performance that required increased details of FDTD modelling to explain. A second study relates to the use of coupled plasmonic and photonic resonances. In this case, our experimental results where much better than anticipated and we have been able to demonstrate unprecedented sensitivity, second best limit of detection (LOD) for refractive index unit (RIU) sensors published including SPR, LRSPR, interferometric, and metamaterial-based RIU sensors. Such results form the basis for a follow-up proposal which was submitted for the GRF 2024-25 round of applications. Only recently we elucidate the full mechanism for the very successful synergic use of BSW and AuNPs for the use of the dual channel SERS-BSW sensing that enables chemical identification (from the fingerprint of chemical bonds associated with their Raman spectra) with analytical quantification, from the BSW sensing based on the shift of the zero-reflection BSW reflection spectra (which is akin to the SPR sensing mechanism) with the highly significant difference that the SPR zero-reflection results from Ohmic losses while the BSW zero-reflection point results from strong coupling into the BSW mode with no significant transfer of energy into the substrate. This line of research is in collaboration with the Institute Fresnel at Aix Marseille University, and we are currently setting up the framework for additional collaboration which is needed to proceed to publication and patent applications. Our studies of photonic, plasmonic, and magnetically coupled responsive crystals coupled plasmonic and photonic resonances on metal/dielectric multilayers was able to demonstrate the second-best limit of detection (LOD) for refractive index unit (RIU) sensors reported to date. These results form the basis for a follow-up proposal which was submitted for the GRF 2024-25 round of applications. Additional optimization will make this strategy suitable for commercialization. We would like to emphasize that while some experimental results were obtained relatively early on in the project, see for example the results of BSW-SERS that were reported in the first midterm report (also PhD Thesis of Mr. Adesina E. Ayotunde), the publication of these results has not proceeded as expeditiously as we wanted because of a series of circumstances that included first and foremost the decision to hold these publication until we developed a quantitatively correct theory of the mechanisms for the observed SERS effect for a non-collimated laser illumination. We appeal to the reviewer to consider that, by themselves, these results are remarkable and worth of the extra effort we underwent to arrive to such quantitative theory. We further explain this as follows: for reference, the use of a microscope objective (u-objective) for SERS data collection takes the laser beam diameter from ~1 mm to ~1 um; this represents an area reduction of 6 orders of magnitude and, as the Raman intensity scales as the square of the electric field, it also represents a 10 to 12 orders of magnitude enhancement in the SERS intensity. The fact that the proposed strategy, namely BSW+LSP, was able to produce similar SERS intensities as the u-objective is remarkable (see Part C, second publication under preparation, Title: “Origin of the Ultrahigh Near- Field Enhancement in Bloch Surface Waves supporting Quantitative Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy”. We recollect that as per the past midterm report, our FDTD enhancement calculations at the time amounted to two orders of magnitude and far below what the experiment suggested. It took the efforts of a second PhD student (see PhD Thesis of May Thawda Phoo) to explain and clarify this effect. In short, it results from the very high-quality factor of the BSW resonance that has a decay time ~ 50 ps. While the LSP confines and indeed enhances its local electric field, such plasmonic resonance is expected to be short lived and to have small Q factor. However, we have been able to demonstrate that the BSW acts as an energy reservoir while the AuNPs acts as a optical antenna drawing little energy form the reservoir. In this case the energy stored, in the relatively large volume of the BSW resonance, acts as an “optical battery” that energizes the LSP for a long time (50 ps) instead of decaying, due to Ohmic losses, within few fs. Additional delays in coordinating such collaboration with relatively little actual overlap between both students, were particularly difficult during the pandemic. These are also the reason for the delay in the publication of the other two manuscripts that have been submitted for consideration. We trust the work in the manuscripts under preparation is presented sufficiently clear; these represents all original results with limited prior-art as counterparts. We are confident to be able to publish soon in journals that will allow us to reach a large audience. Further details are presented in attachment Part C for data that not been published but whose manuscripts are in preparation.

11219919.label: Major findings and research outcome
11219919.value: We demonstrated the fabrication of magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs), namely Fe3O4@SiO2@Au NPs, that present a versatile and useful combination of magnetic, optical, and plasmonic properties for sensing. First, the magnetic properties of the prepared MNPs are strong enough to enable concentration from a disperse liquid solution using the permanent magnetic field of a small magnet. Second, the resulting ensemble of MNPs enable dual-channel sensor strategies based on the synergic benefits of their optical and plasmonic properties. In particular, two modes of operation have been demonstrated that result particularly successful. In the first mode of operation, Fe3O4 @ SiO2 @ Au NPs were used as a soluble-substrate for SERS detection of ampicillin based on anti-ampicillin aptamer conjugation of the Fe3O4 @ SiO2 @ Au NPs. The functionalized MNPs can then be diluted in the analyte (ampicillin solution) where they interact in a large volume to increase the opportunities for conjugation. Thereafter, the fast manipulation of the responsive photonic crystals is activated, using a permanent magnet to effectively increase the MNP’s concentration in a dense, magnetic-slurry, of aggregated MNPs. Because the analyte is locked in the functionalized surfaces of the MNPs, due to the conjugation mechanism, the analyte concentration inside the MNPs magnetic slurry also increases. However, while the analyte remains locked inside such slurry, it is nevertheless suitable to be detected by SERS strategy because i) the SiO2 shell makes the magnetic slurry transparent, and ii) the AuNPs create multiple “hotspots” in the adjacent gaps between MNPs that enhance the SERS signal. Therefore, sensing of the ampicillin is possible for a large concentration range down to a fraction of ug/ml. In the second highly successful mode of operation, a 1D all-dielectric multilayer supporting a large electric field enhancement factor was successfully coupled with AuNPs to demonstrate one of the best RIU sensors to date. The fabricated sensor presents the second best LOD for RIU as most published results using SPR, LSPR, interferometric, ellipsometric, and metamaterial-based RIU sensor. More importantly it also presents a very large dynamic range due to the combined operation of two p-polarization resonances that enable independent track of the total RIU changes while the angle of incidence (AoI) is adjusted to overcome the expected, and observed, sensitivity saturation with increasing analyte concentration. In this way, we successfully demonstrate top performance, 10^-8 RIU LOD, over ~ 6 orders of magnitude in analyte concentration.

11219919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11219919.value: Our research is highly applied and can be developed further. In particular, the use of the MNPs to assemble a soluble SERS substrate has not been published but we are preparing both a manuscript and a patent application that is expected to be submitted around October 2024. While the results obtained so far are highly promising, with LOD of a fraction of mg/ml and up to 6 orders of magnitude dynamic range, we are confident that they can be improved further. The soluble SERS substrate approach is of great interest to overcome limitations imposed by the local nature of functionalized static surfaces whose performance is conditional to the availability of the analyte to be localized in the proximity of the functionalized surface. Variables that we anticipate need further optimization include: i) MNPs’ dilution ratio and total amount; ii) SiO2 shell thickness; and iii) magnetic slurry attachment conditions including hyper substrate surface roughness, index matching, and attachment rate.

11219919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11219919.value: We have assembled core-shell-texture hierarchical nanomaterials based on Fe3O4 cores of few tens of nm in diameter covered with SiO2 shells of 100 to 200 nm in diameter further decorated with a rich texture of Au NPs on their surface. The resulting Fe3O4@SiO2@Au NPs (or MNPs to be concise) possess synergic magnetic, photonic and plasmonic properties that have been demonstrated to be of use for sensing applications that take advantage of SPR, BSW, and SERS strategies. These results demonstrate the ability to implement dual sensing strategies that can enable advance functionality including for example, chemical identification from SERS chemical fingerprint with analytical quantification from BSW sensing, or the hybridization of photonic and plasmonic resonance modes that resulted in the second best limit of detection (LOD) for a refractive index unit (RIU) sensor outperforming many SPR, LRSPR, interferometric and metamaterial- based sensors. Our results are thoroughly supported by experimental and in-depth model calculations that use both conventional effective medium approximation (EMA) and Fresnel equations as well as fully vectorial numerical computations using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method. These results are being prepared for patent application and further optimization are expected to bring them closer to commercialisation addressing real life sensors with biomedical and environmental protection sensing applications.

11300019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300019.value: 本項目旨在開發無機和有機金屬過渡金屬絡合物作為新的磷光生物正交探針，以用於生物成像試劑和光功能治療劑。生物正交標記已成為一種在天然生物環境中可視化生物分子的有效方法。標記過程涉及兩步修飾方案：1）把被化學報告基團修飾的生物分子摻入活細胞和生物體中，2）修飾的生物分子與攜帶互補功能的生物正交探針的特異性反應。迄今為止，大多數生物正交探針都是熒光染料。由於未反應的探針會造成強烈的背景熒光干擾，這些熒光染料的一個缺點是需要嚴格的洗滌。因此，開發具有熒光開關特性的生物正交標記探針已成為一種替代策略。這類探針是極具吸引性的，因為無需洗滌步驟即可獲得高質量的圖像。由於已報導的所有熒光生物正交探針幾乎都來自有機染料，因此它們的發光局限於熒光，並且它們僅被應用於生物成像。近年來，發光過渡金屬絡合物因其有趣的光物理和光化學特性，膜滲透性和可控的細胞攝取性質，引起了人們對其在生物成像和治療中的應用的濃厚興趣。在本項目中，我們將基於這些有趣的特徵研發出在生物正交標記反應中具有磷光開關性質的過渡金屬絡合物。重要的是，我們的目標探針不僅在生物正交標記後會顯示出有利的光物理性質，而且還能有效地光誘導產生單線態氧（1O2）。這種有趣的生物正交反應引發的光敏化能力將有助於1O2量子產率的調節和可控光細胞毒性試劑的開發。此外，通過使用細胞穿透肽，腫瘤靶向分子和蛋白質標籤，我們能夠設計出可分別應用於具細胞器靶向和癌細胞選擇性的光動力治療及發色團輔助蛋白質光滅活的新試劑。對磷光無機和有機金屬探針的探索將大大拓寬生物正交標記的研究範圍，這將受到化學生物學，生物化學和細胞生物學界的歡迎。本項目的研究成果將突出發光過渡金屬絡合物在治療診斷試劑的研發中的作用，這將有助於對生命系統中生物過程的基本理解，並為一系列診斷和治療應用提供令人興奮的機會。

11300019.label: Realisation of objectives
11300019.value: The four project objectives have been achieved as illustrated by the following results. In the first study, we designed rhenium(I) polypyridine complexes containing a sydnone moiety [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-syd-Ph)](CF3SO3) as bioorthogonal probes for cellular imaging of specific organelles. The complexes were weakly emissive in fluid solutions due to the highly polar local environment of the metal core provided by the polar sydnone moiety. However, upon their strain-promoted sydnone-alkyne cycloaddition (SPSAC) reaction with a hydrophobic strained alkyne BCN-OH, the complexes displayed moderate emission enhancement (I/Io = 8.8 – 17.3). When they reacted with BCN-modified bovine serum albumin (BCN-BSA), more pronounced emission enhancement (up to 38.9) and longer emission lifetimes (1.80 – 4.71 us) were observed. Confocal microscopy images showed that the ligation of the BCN-modified morpholine by one of the complexes induced specific lysosomal labeling in live human cervical carcinoma HeLa cells. In another study, we designed a new class of iridium(III) nitrone complexes [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-nitrone)](PF6) as phosphorogenic bioorthogonal probes for BCN-BG, which is a specific substrate for SNAP-tag protein. Due to the C=N photoisomerization of the nitrone unit, these complexes remained non-emissive with negligible singlet oxygen (1O2) photosensitization. Upon strain-promoted alkyne-nitrone cycloaddition (SPANC) reaction with BCN-OH, they displayed significant emission enhancement (I/Io = 7.2 – 47.1) and 1O2 generation efficiencies (QY = 0.42 – 0.91). Confocal microscopy images suggested that only Chinese hamster ovarian CHO-K1 cells expressing SNAP-tag protein and pretreated with BCN-BG exhibited luminescence signals upon incubation with the complexes. Additionally, the presence of SNAP-tag and BCN-BG enhanced the 1O2 photosensitization of the complexes and hence their photocytotoxicity in cells. The labeling strategy in this study allows the simultaneous modulation of phosphorescence and 1O2 photosensitization of bioorthogonal probes with great adaptability for multiplex applications of other protein tags and bioorthogonal handles. In a related study, we developed a series of iridium(III) polypyridine complexes appended with a tetrazine moiety [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-Tz-Ph)](PF6). The complexes exhibited very weak emission due to the efficient quenching by the tetrazine unit. Upon inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA) reaction with BCN-OH, these complexes exhibited significant emission enhancement (I/Io = 51.7 – 105.3). However, when they reacted with the strained alkene TCO-OH, only negligible emission changes (I/Io = 1.8 – 13.5) were observed because of the formation of the quenching dihydropyridazine unit. One of the complexes was utilized to label the lysosomes and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) of HeLa cells pretreated with corresponding organelle-specific BCN-modified derivatives. When cells expressing HaloTag protein were pretreated with its strained alkyne substrate, the complexes showed strong emission and photocytotoxicity. However, no similar observation was found in cells pretreated with its strained alkene substrate. These results illustrate the potential of iridium(III) tetrazine complexes for the specific labeling of strained alkynes over other commonly used bioorthogonal handles such as strained alkenes. In a recent study, we developed monochromophoric iridium(III) complexes containing two tetrazines derivatives as the cyclometalating ligands [Ir(dptz)2(N^N)](Cl). The direct coordination of the two tetrazine units to the metal core resulted in significant phosphorogenic properties of the complexes (I/Io up to 3885.7) and enhanced reactivity of the coordinated tetrazine (k2 up to 14713.6 M-1 s-1) toward bis-cyclooctynylated derivatives, such as bis-BCN. Interestingly, these complexes exhibited selectivity toward bis-BCN over the mono-substrate BCN-OH in a cross-labeling study, which is ascribed to the elevated reactivity of the complexes toward bis-BCN. The complexes were exploited for peptide stapling and cross-labeling of BCN-modified peptides. They were also utilized in the live cell imaging of bis-BCN, confirming their lysosomal labeling properties. Additionally, the complexes showed high 1O2 generation quantum yields and hence photocytotoxicity after their reaction with bis-BCN. These complexes were utilized for the construction of luminescent nanosized hydrogels as platforms for cargo delivery and cell imaging. The novel design of this class of complexes demonstrates the unique role of the metal core in tuning the emission properties and bioorthogonal reactivity of tetrazine-based complexes, expanding the synthetic toolbox of bioorthogonal probes for bioimaging and photodynamic therapy (PDT). The exciting results from these studies have prompted us to further investigate other specific labeling reactions for biomolecules. Chemoselective reactions enable the specific modification of biomolecules with different functional entities. We studied the utilization of iridium(III) complexes incorporated with a perfluorobiphenyl (PFBP) moiety [Ir(N^C)2(bpy-PFBP)](PF6) for pi-clamp-mediated cysteine labeling. The complexes reacted with the cysteine residue of pi-clamp-containing peptide sequences in a rapid and selective manner, affording luminescent peptide conjugates with high 1O2 photosensitization efficiency. Organelle-targeting sequences were shown to direct the resulting conjugates to various intracellular localization, where they exhibited potent photocytotoxic activity. We also developed a series of rhenium(I) PFBP complexes [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-PFBP)](CF3SO3) for the labeling of pi-clamp. The complexes reacted rapidly and selectively with peptides containing the pi-clamp sequence. One of the complexes reacted with organelle-targeting sequences to prepare peptide conjugates that were localized in the lysosomes and mitochondria of the cells. The mitochondria-targeting conjugates exhibited significant cytotoxicity upon photoirradiation, highlighting the mitochondria as a potent target for efficient PDT. Interestingly, the incorporation of a caspase-3/7-cleavable sequence at the C-terminus of pi-clamp and an emission quencher QSY-7 afforded a phosphorogenic conjugate to examine the activity of caspase-3/7 during apoptosis. The results of these two works offer a new strategy to the development of photofunctional peptide and protein conjugates of luminescent transition metal complexes as new theranostic agents. We reported rhenium(I) polypyridine complexes featuring a 2,4-dinitrophenylsulfonamide (DNPS) unit [Re(N^N)(CO)3(py-DNPS)](CF3SO3) as biothiol-selective imaging reagents and photocytotoxic agents. The complexes exhibited weak emission due to photoinduced electron transfer from the excited rhenium(I) diimine moiety to the DNPS unit. Upon reaction with glutathione (GSH), the DNPS moiety was removed, resulting in the emission turn-on of the complexes (I/Io = 12.6 – 22.2). When HeLa cells were incubated with the complexes, both intense intracellular emission and potent photocytotoxicity were observed. Additionally, the incorporation of a tosylamide unit directed the complex to the ER of the cells, which can be exploited for organelle-selective bioimaging and photocytotoxic applications. We further designed near-infrared (NIR)-emitting iridium(III) complexes bearing a heteroaromatic methylsulfone moiety for the specific labeling of sulfhydryl-containing peptides and proteins. Upon photoirradiation, all the complexes exhibited intense and long-lived NIR emission with strong 1O2 generation efficiency. One of the complexes reacted with cysteine rapidly and selectively over other amino acids, such as lysine, histidine, and serine. The fast reaction between the complex and cysteine allows the preparation of peptide and protein conjugates for the labeling of various organelles, including lysosomes, mitochondria, and plasma membrane. All the conjugates showed minimal dark cytotoxicity in both cancer and normal cells. However, more significant photocytotoxicity was observed in cancer cells upon photoexcitation due to the higher cellular uptake of the conjugates by the cancer cells. In summary, there were no significant difficulties encountered in this project. Our earlier work based on sydnone and nitrone derivatives showed moderate reaction kinetics and emission enhancement. We also designed tetrazine complexes that displayed excellent bioorthogonal reactivity and phosphorogenic responses. The reported transition metal complexes showed not only emission enhancement for bioimaging, but also the activation of 1O2 photosensitization for PDT. We extended our system to explore other specific labeling reactions, affording novel photofunctional peptide and protein conjugates. Overall, a number of transition metal complexes were exploited as bioorthogonal probes and photosensitizers for theranostic applications.

11300019.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300019.value: We designed rhenium(I) sydnone complexes as bioorthogonal probes for organelle-specific labeling. The complexes were weakly emissive due to the highly polar local environment provided by the sydnone moiety. However, their specific reaction with strained alkyne derivatives resulted in moderate emission enhancement. The ligation of BCN-modified morpholine with the complexes induced specific lysosomal labeling in live cells. A two-step labeling strategy was exploited to modulate the emission and singlet oxygen (1O2) photosensitization of transition metal complexes by protein tag technologies. A new class of iridium(III) nitrone complexes was designed for labeling BCN-BG, a substrate for SNAP-tag protein. They showed strong emission and 1O2 generation only after reaction with BCN-BG. When cells expressing SNAP-tag were treated with BCN-BG and the complexes, significant luminescence signals and photocytotoxicity were observed. We reported iridium(III) tetrazine complexes as bioorthogonal probes to selectively label strained alkyne derivatives. These complexes were non-emissive due to efficient quenching by the tetrazine unit. While their significant emission was resumed by reacting with strained alkyne substrates, only negligible changes were observed in their reaction with strained alkene derivatives. This study showed that the emission of tetrazine complexes can be modulated by a specific type of reaction partners. Monochromophoric iridium(III) tetrazine complexes were explored as bioorthogonal probes for bis-cyclooctynylated derivatives. Direct coordination of tetrazine units to the metal center affords complexes with unusually high phosphorogenic properties and reactivity toward bis-cyclooctynylated derivatives, which is ascribed to their selectivity over the mono-substrates. This enabled the stapling of BCN-modified peptides and the construction of nanosized hydrogels for cargo delivery and cell imaging. This work expands the synthetic toolbox of bioorthogonal probes with fast reaction kinetics and high selectivity. These exciting results inspire us to extended our system to chemoselective reactions for modifying biomolecules including: 1) perfluorobiphenyl complexes for labeling the cysteine residue of the pi-clamp sequence to afford organelle-targeting peptide conjugates and phosphorogenic enzyme substrates; 2) dinitrophenylsulfonamide complexes for intracellular sensing of glutathione; 3) NIR-emissive methylsulfone complexes for labeling cysteine-containing peptides and proteins to prepare their photofunctional conjugates. We demonstrated that bioorthogonal probes based on transition metal complexes can realize specific bioimaging capabilities and controlled photocytotoxicity. The modification of bioorthogonal handles with transition metal complexes will enhance their reaction kinetics. Notably, the phosphorogenic properties and 1O2 photosensitization of the complexes can be modulated by bioorthogonal reactions. Our findings highlight the potential of transition metal complexes in the design of bioorthogonal probes and photosensitizers for theranostic applications.

11300019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300019.value: The incorporation of bioorthogonal handles into transition metal complexes has realized specific cellular imaging and controllable photocytotoxicity in live cells. We demonstrated that the metal center can enhance the reactivity of the bioorthogonal handles, as in the case of monochromophoric iridium(III) tetrazine complexes. In combination with other functionalities, these complexes can be utilized for other applications, including bioimaging of cancerous tissues, prodrug activation at tumor sites, and hydrogel formation for drug delivery. Bioorthogonal handles impose different quenching mechanisms that determine the phosphorogenic properties and 1O2 photosensitization of the complexes. With a judicious choice of their reaction partners, novel photosensitizers that are activatable selectively in cancerous tissues can be designed. For instance, we developed a two-step labeling strategy that utilizes protein tags and their specific substrates to modulate the phosphorescence and 1O2 photosensitization of the complexes. This strategy may be extended to target overexpressed enzymes in cancer cells, allowing the selective activation of complexes in malignant tissues to enhance the precision of PDT. This project primarily focused on bioorthogonal handles undergoing ligation reactions. Other reactions such as photoclick and cleavage reactions remain unexplored. The design of bioorthogonal probes for these reactions is expected to further expand the toolbox for biological applications.

11300019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300019.value: The aim of this project is the development of transition metal complexes as novel phosphorogenic bioorthogonal probes for bioimaging and phototherapeutic applications. Bioorthogonal labeling enables the visualization of biomolecules in their native biological environments by a two-step modification scheme: 1) the internalization of a biomolecule modified with a chemical reporter into live cells and organisms, 2) specific reaction of the modified biomolecule with a bioorthogonal probe carrying the complementary functionality. Although fluorogenic probes with turn-on emission properties upon bioorthogonal labeling have been developed, the emission is limited to fluorescence and the utilization of the probes is confined to bioimaging. In this project, we have developed transition metal complexes that exhibit phosphorogenic properties, i.e., phosphorescence turn-on upon bioorthogonal labeling reactions, and efficient photoinduced singlet oxygen (1O2) generation. This interesting bioorthogonally controlled photosensitization capability allows the modulation of 1O2 generation. Through the use of organelle-targeting molecules and protein tags, we have designed new reagents for organelle-specific and cancer cell-selective photodynamic therapy. Our results have highlighted the role of luminescent transition metal complexes in the development of theranostic reagents, contributing to the basic understanding of biological processes in living systems and providing exciting opportunities for a broad range of diagnostic and therapeutic applications.

11300319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300319.value: Organic light-emitting diodes (OLED) are already widely used in the display industry and are also promising for solid state lighting. Their advantages include high power efficiencies and great color tunability, and showing excellent versatility to yield flexible devices in all kind of sizes and shapes. Importantly, to attain both the full color monitor and white OLEDs, highly efficient emitters exhibiting all three elementary colors of the visible spectrum, i.e., red, green and blue (RGB), are required. The launch of high-end iPhone with OLED panel serve as the landmark, not to mention that similar OLED has already been installed in various 3C products and TVs. This means that the corresponding RGB emitters have already passed the stringent industrial assessments for commercial applications. In addition, there is a growing interest in developing near infrared (NIR) emitting OLEDs, i.e., devices emitting in the 700 - 1400 nm spectral region. Since NIR light cannot be seen by the human eye, this irradiation can be utilized as an invisible light source for communication and night vision devices. Moreover, it can also exert better penetration into human body such as head, arms and legs than visible light with wavelengths between 400 - 700 nm. This is due to the fact that scattering has weak dependence on wavelength; hence, the NIR has large usage window that is limited by the absorption of both blood and water at short and long wavelengths. As a result, NIR-emitting OLED are preferred technology over visible OLED to produce illumination for medical and therapeutic applications. In this proposal, we intend to design and synthesize several Pt(II) metal complexes that are capable to display bright NIR emission upon excitation. 有機發光二極管已廣泛使用在顯示器工業、並在固態照明領域展現可觀發展潛力。其長處在於：高效率、可調整的色彩、與能用以製作不同尺寸的柔性顯示器件。目前在市場販售的智能手機、與其他小型電器產品與高價位電視、即可當成有機發光二極管屏幕的使用範例、顯現出優越的技術普及性暨市場佔有率。現今、有機發光二極管亦逐漸由可見光區、推展至近紅外光區、也就是坐落在 700 - 1400 nm間的輻射光波。這項光波無法被肉眼接收、故可以用在無線通訊使用、以及做為夜間隱形光源。且由於這類光波對於生物體有較佳的穿透力、故具有多項醫療暨相關生物與安全檢測的使用潛力。在這項研究計畫、我們擬開發新型的鉑基配合物、利用這類型配合物的分子間、高強度鉑鉑原子鍵結能力、紅移發射光譜至近紅外光區、並減少非輻射焠息效應、以達成高效能、近紅外發光材料暨相關有機發光二極管器件的開發。

11300319.label: Realisation of objectives
11300319.value: This research proposal contained four main objectives, namely: (1) To design and synthesize saturated-red and near infrared (NIR) emitting Pt(II) metal phosphors that are capable to display strong inter-molecular interaction in the solid state, as well as emission in saturated-red and NIR regions. (2) To design and synthesize Pt(II) based phosphors that are capable to display strong emission in NIR region at ca. 800 nm, and with PLQY of ca. 20%. (3) To analyse the structure-property relationships of the studied Pt(II) complexes and to delineate the red-shifting in emission wavelengths. (4) Fabrication and optimization of various OLED devices using the above mentioned Pt(II) based phosphors, achieving EL emission with peak max. of approx. 800 nm, and with external quantum efficiency (EQE) of over 5 % and significantly reduced efficiency roll-off. PS: Figure will be provided if needed. Figure 1. Structures of representative Pt(II) complexes proposed and synthesized during our investigation. Efficient near-infrared (NIR) emitters has drawn much attention due to their important applications ranging from biological imaging, medical therapy, optical communication and night-vision devices. However, all organic and organometallic molecules with energy gaps closed to deep red and NIR regime are subject to dominant non-radiative internal conversion (IC) processes, which drastically reduces the emission intensity and exciton diffusion length of organic materials and hence hampers the optoelectronic performances. Scientifically, to suppress non-radiative IC rates, we suggested two complementary approaches to solve these issues: exciton delocalization and molecular deuteration. First, exciton delocalization efficiently suppresses the molecular reorganization energy through partitioning to all aggregated molecules. According to the theory on internal conversion together with the effect of exciton delocalization, the simulated non-radiative rates with the energy gap ΔE = 104 cm-1 decrease by around 104 folds when the exciton delocalization length equals 5 (promoting vibronic frequency ωl = 1500 cm-1). Second, molecular deuteration reduces Franck-Condon vibrational overlaps and vibrational frequencies of promoting modes, which decreases IC rates by one order of magnitude comparing to the rates of non-deuterated molecules under ΔE 104 cm-1. Although deuteration has long been attempted to increase emission intensity, the results have been mixing. Hence, during execution of this research proposal, we have to demonstrate its validity, especially to emission occurred in the NIR region. The concepts are next verified by the strategic design and synthesis of relevant square-planar Pt(II) complexes (c.f. Figure 1), which form crystalline aggregates in vapor deposited thin films. The packing geometries are well characterized by the grazing angle X-ray diffraction (GIXD), showing domino-like packing arrangements with the short ππ separation of 3.4–3.7 Å. Upon photoexcitation, such closely packed assemblies exhibit intense NIR emission maximized at 740–970 nm region through metal‒metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MMLCT) transition with unprecedented photoluminescent quantum yield (PLQY) of 8–82%. To validate the existence of exciton delocalization, we applied the time-resolved step-scan Fourier transform UV–Vis spectroscopy to probe the exciton delocalization length of Pt(II) aggregates, which is 5–9 molecules (2.1–4.5 nm) assuming that excitons mainly delocalized along the direction of ππ stacking. According to the dependence of delocalization length vs. simulated IC rates, we verify that the observed delocalization lengths contribute to the high NIR PLQY of the aggregated Pt(II) complexes. Moreover, for probing the isotope effect, both partially and completely deuterated Pt(II) complexes were synthesized. For the case of the 970 nm Pt(II) emitter, the vapor deposited films of per-deuterated Pt(II) complexes exhibit the same emission peak as that of the non-deuterated one, whereas PLQY increases by 50%. This result unambiguously confirmed the influence of deuteration. To put the fundamental studies into practice, organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) were fabricated with these NIR Pt(II) complexes as the emitting layer, showing the outstanding external quantum efficiencies (EQE) of 2–25% and the remarkable radiances 10–40 W·sr-1·m-2 at 740–1002 nm. The prominent device performances not only successfully prove our designed concept, but also reach a new milestone for highly efficient NIR OLED devices. Hence, our experimental procedures executed during the past three years have successfully provided workable methodologies on how to boost the efficiency of NIR emission of organic molecules from in-depth fundamental basis, i.e., molecular design, photophysical characterization and device fabrication. Most important, we have also achieved all four project objectives that proposed at the beginning of this research proposal.

11300319.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300319.value: For NIR emitters and OLED devices, the most important direction remains as the design and preparation of new and better emitters and fabrication of NIR OLED devices. As demonstrated in this project report, we have successfully made a series of Pt(II) emitters and NIR OLED devices showing peak max. reaching 1000 nm and max. EQE of over 4%. These devices have never been reported in literature and, hence, they are our major findings obtained during the past three years. Moreover, the next goal is to prepare very efficient NIR emitters with peak max. at 800 nm, such that the emitters can be tested for future industrial applications. Emission with peak wavelengths located in this region will be totally invisible to human and possessing the best efficiency based on the energy gap law. Particularly, the devices with peak max. at 850 nm (also at 1310 and 1550 nm) may be also of useful for application involving optical communications. If these emitters are accessible, OLED devices can then be fabricated using the existed fabrication technologies. They shall be good for other applications such as bio-imaging and sensing applications, making great impact to the future development of NIR OLED devices.

11300319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300319.value: Efficient near-infrared (NIR) emitters has drawn much attention due to their important applications ranging from biological imaging, medical therapy, optical communication and night-vision devices. Hence, our next goal is to prepare NIR emitters with peak max. at 800 nm. Emission with these peak wavelengths will be totally invisible to human and the devices with peak max. at 850 nm may be of useful for healthcare applications and applications involving optical communications. Moreover, our NIR OLED devices are currently fabricated using thermal vacuum deposition, as these processes will induce self-assembly in forming the closely stacked (or aligned) Pt(II) molecules for the non-doped EML. Theoretically, this structure-property relationship can be circumvented using Pt(II) based dimers or even trimers with inherently connected Pt···Pt interaction. These new molecular designs should also be our future research objectives.

11300319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300319.value: This project is a part of our combined research effect in finding the most efficient near infrared emitters. For building up the demanded emitters with suitable emission wavelength and operational lifetime, we need to control the chelate designs so that it can control the intermolecular stacking interaction between individual Pt(II) metal molecules in forming the aggregates. This linearly arranged aggregate would exert strong metal‒metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MMLCT). The resulting MMLCT transition process is much red shifted with respect to the “isolated” monomers that exist in the co-deposited thin film. Hence, the monomeric Pt(II) complexes with sky-blue and green emission may become NIR emitters when self-assembled, thus opening the gateway to efficient NIR OLEDs. In fact, the lesson learnt from this proposal, have helped us to publish two articles on Nature Photonics, c.f., https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-020-0653-6 and https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-022-01079-8. These successes confirmed the bright future of our research works.

11300419.label: Project Objectives
11300419.value: To investigate the valence energy profiles and electronic interactions in different CTC systems before, under and after photoexcitation. - Selected CTC systems (e.g. [RuCp∗Mes]2/POPy2, m-MTDATA/Alq3, TPD/Alq3, rubrene/ BP2T, etc.) with observable properties change upon and after photoexcitation would be studied. Energy profiles, excited charge distributions and electronic interactions would be carefully examined in dark, upon and after photoexcitation. Results obtained would not only provide direct information on the electronic couplings at the D/A interfaces, but also a basic reference for selection of CTC systems for AFM studies. To examine the interfacial topographies, charge polarizations, electrical conducting properties at the CTC interfaces before, under and after photoexcitation, and their correlations with electronic properties. - Local surface properties such as contact topographies, surface potential differences, photo-induced electrical signals, etc., before, under and after photoexcitation would be examined using a multifunction AFM system with different modes (e.g. KPFM, EFM, pico-current mapping image). By combining the UPS and the AFM results, we target to correlate the surface electronic interaction and local electrical properties at the D/A interfaces in dark, under and after photoexcitation. To develop strategic approaches for tuning the CTC properties for device applications. - With the developed understanding on the CTC properties from the above works, a target of this project is to develop strategies for engineering of CTC properties for device applications. Organic optoelectronic devices (e.g. OLEDs, OPVs etc) with improved performance will be realized by incorporating CTCs with custom-tuned properties.

11300419.label: Realisation of objectives
11300419.value: In this reporting period, we have 1) studied the charge transport properties of co-evaporated charge-transfer complexes (CTCs) formed at organic/inorganic interfaces; (2) explored the photocurrent generation process at interfacial CTCs of a ternary system and (3) investigated the relationship of open-circuit voltage (VOC) loss and CTC hybridization. 1) Study the charge transport properties of co-evaporated CTCs CTCs show distinguished charge transport properties from their parental materials. In this project, the electron and hole transport properties of co-evaporated MoO3:6T CTC thin film were studied. Using a simple rubbing process, we found that the intermolecular interaction of the CTC material can be tuned such that changes in optical properties, vibrational modes, chemical states and electronic structures are observed. These changes in properties and charge transport behaviors enable us to understand the influences of CTC frontier molecular orbitals and their degree of coupling on the charge transport properties. It also provides insight into the understanding of the intermolecular interactions and their influence on the charge transport properties of thin film CTCs. The above work has been published in “J. Mater. Chem. C, 2020, 8, 16725-16729” (Ref. 1) 2) Explore the photocurrent generation process at CTCs of a ternary system With the understanding of charge transport properties of single kind of CTC, we further broaden the scope to double CTCs in a ternary system. A ternary structure of SubPc/C60/MoO3 was fabricated and its charge-transfer processes were studied. We found that SubPc/C60 is a charge-transfer interface and C60/MoO3 is a Schottky junction. This leads to significant decrease of photocurrent at forward biases, while the conventional binary system shows high photocurrent at forward bias. This novel electric character is applied to design an organic photodetector (OPD), which can overcome the “color blind” of conventional photodetectrors. The combination of a high or low photocurrent under reverse and forward biases determines the colors of the received light, and that forms the heart of ‘‘non-color blind’’ ability to recognize light colors in the OPD. The energy structure and charge collection pathways in the OPD are investigated with biased external quantum efficiency (EQE), ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and current density–voltage (J–V) studies. The OPD with the ability of color and wavelength determination demonstrates its potential to recognize colors without using additional components and the dual mode operation enables it to work under different conditions via switching its detection ranges with bias voltages. This design principle can be utilized to fabricate multifunctional devices by simply selecting different donor–acceptor materials according to the desired detection ranges. This work reveals the charge generation mechanism in ternary organic heterojunction systems. The above work has been published in “J. Mater. Chem. C, 2021, 9, 3814–3819” (Ref. 2) 3) Investigated the relationship of VOC loss and CTC hybridization The VOC of organic photovoltaics has a close relationship with CTC properties. It is reported that hybridization between the CTC of a donor–acceptor pair and lowest exciton state of the donor or the acceptor can effectively reduce recombination loss in OPV devices. Although this approach shows great success in maximizing VOC, other parameters typically exhibit poor values. In this project, “complete boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine devices” with strong hybridization resulting in lower recombination loss (0.47 eV) while not penalizing charge separation dynamics (internal quantum efficiency (IQE) > 80% and fill factor (FF) > 70%) are observed. Interestingly, when boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine is paired with any other active material used in this study (“partial boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine device”), recombination losses are still consistently maintained at lower levels (<0.53 eV). These observations denote the capability of boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine to result in lower recombination loss devices while pairing with other materials. Special intrinsic characteristics of these materials (high dielectric constant, sharp absorption edge, unusually high absorption coefficient) and hybridization collectively result in reduced recombination loss and efficient charge generation in these systems. This work enlightens that how CTC influences the device parameters in OPVs. The above work has been published in “Sol. RRL 2020, 4, 2000245” (Ref 3) Other related work: Knowledge and insight from the above works have been further applied to perovskite LEDs, OLEDs and antibacterial therapy. For perovskite LED, we found that white perovskite LED with tunable color temperature can be achieved by designing a charge confinement effect at the interface of perovskite/electron transport layer. Photoluminescence quantum yield of perovskite can be improved via reducing trap-induced recombination and exciton–excitons annihilation. Suppressing non-radiative energy loss and humidity treatment can enhance the perovskite LED performance. The interfacial charge injection of inverted OLEDs can be improved using a zinc ion chelated polyethylenimine (PEI) interfacial layer. For OLED, we found that ionization process reduces carrier accumulation in PEDOT:PSS, thus enhancing the performance of OLEDs. A large centimeter-scale hole diffusion can be achieved with interfacial engineering in OLED, leading to a high efficiency and better stability. Radiative rates of the TADF emitters with vertical orientation can be substantial increased in weakly coupled organic microcavity, significantly enhancing external quantum efficiencies, reducing efficiency roll-off, and improving color-purities of TADF OLEDs. A “two-reverse intersystem crossing (RISC)-channel” design can be a novel approach for enhancing performance of TADF emitters, in particular at high excitation densities. Specifically, our CTC knowledge was successfully applied on photothermal therapy by designing high-performance organic near-infrared (NIR) photothermal agents (PTAs), especially over NIR-II bio-window (1000–1350 nm). These works have been published in “ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 13(37), 44991-45000” (Ref. 5), “Advanced Functional Materials, 32(40), 2203962” (Ref. 6), “Chemistry of Materials, 33(11), 4154-4162” (Ref. 7), “ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 14(17), 19774-19784” (Ref. 8), “Next Nanotechnology, 1, 100003” (Ref. 9), “Nano-Micro Letters, 14, 1-11” (Ref. 10), “Chemistry of Materials, 35(9), 3484-3493” (Ref. 11), “Science Advances, 8(17), eabm1999” (Ref. 12), “Light: Science & Applications, 10(1), 116.” (Ref. 13), “ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces, 13(41), 49066-4907.” (Ref. 14) and “Angewandte Chemie, 133(21), 11864-11868” (Ref. 15)

11300419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300419.value: In this project, the charge transport properties of co-evaporated CTCs were firstly studied. we found that the intermolecular interaction of the CTC material can be tuned, leading to changes of optical properties, vibrational modes, chemical states and electronic structures. These changes enable us to deeply understand the influences of CTC frontier molecular orbitals and their degree of coupling on the charge transport properties. It also provides insight into the understanding of the intermolecular interactions and their influence on the charge transport properties of thin film CTCs. (Ref. 1: J. Mater. Chem. C, 2020, 8, 16725-16729) With the understanding of charge transport properties of single kind of CTC, we further broaden the scope to double CTCs in a ternary system. In a ternary structure of SubPc/C60/MoO3, we found that SubPc/C60 is a charge-transfer interface and C60/MoO3 is a Schottky junction. This leads to significant decrease of photocurrent at forward biases, while the conventional binary system shows high photocurrent at forward bias. This novel electric character is applied to design an organic photodetector (OPD), which can overcome the “color blind” of conventional photodetectrors. The OPD with the ability of color and wavelength determination demonstrates its potential to recognize colors without using additional components and the dual mode operation enables it to work under different conditions via switching its detection ranges with bias voltages. This design principle can be utilized to fabricate multifunctional devices by simply selecting different donor–acceptor materials according to the desired detection ranges. This work reveals the charge generation mechanism in ternary organic heterojunction systems. (Ref. 2: J. Mater. Chem. C, 2021, 9, 3814–3819) We next investigated the relationship of VOC loss and CTC hybridization in OPVs. We found that “complete boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine devices” with strong hybridization resulting in lower recombination loss (0.47 eV) of VOC while not penalizing charge separation dynamics. This low recombination loss can consistently maintain when boron sub-(na)phthalocyanine is paired with any other active material. Our work enlightens that how CTC influences the device parameters in OPVs. (Ref. 3: Sol. RRL 2020, 4, 2000245) The obtained knowledge is further applied to perovskite LEDs, OLEDs and antibacterial therapy for improving performance of different optoelectronic devices and biomaterials. 11300419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300419.value: The proposed methodology has been proved to successfully investigate the chemical and electrical properties of CTCs. It also inspires the application of CTCs on novel “non-color blind” OPDs and explains the VOC loss for OPVs. However, the understanding on CTCs is still limited since the interfacial conditions are quite different for different combinations. Studies on CTCs in perovskite-based devices are also urgently required due to the fast development of this novel material. In the future, the proposed method will be applied on other systems, especially on the perovskite materials and devices. This investigation on broader configurations is expected to enrich the understanding on novel opto-electronic devices and provide guidance for future device engineering.

11300419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300419.value: Charge transfer complexes (CTCs) have drawn much attention in recent years due to its critical role on organic opto-electronic devices. The electronic, physical and chemical properties of CTCs directly determine the device performance of OPVs and OLEDs. Despite the importance, understanding on CTCs is not adequate. In this project, the charge transport properties, photocurrent generation mechanism and hybridization process of CTCs are deeply explored. Knowledge obtained is further applied to design novel organic photodetectors, which can overcome the “color blind” in conventional photodetectors. In addition, the voltage loss in solar cell is also found to be related to hybridization process. The research methodology is also extended to perovskite LED and OLEDs for improving device performance.

11300519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11300519.value: 低秩張量方法在複雜模型中的降維作用

11300519.label: Project Objectives
11300519.value: In multivariate additive models, when the functions to be estimated are approximated using polynomial splines, the coefficients naturally organize into a third order tensor. We study how the low-rank assumption of tensors can be used in high-dimensional multivariate additive models to reduce dimensionality. We will establish the theoretical results to clearly demonstrate the improved efficiency of the new estimator. We will further combine tensor approach with sparsity assumptions to deal with the case the dimension is ever larger than the sample size. Efficient algorithms will be developed to implement the approach. For linear regression models with interactions, with either univariate or multivariate responses, we treat the coefficients as tensors in fitting the model. The tensor has an interesting symmetric structure which calls for new theory. We plan to investigate the possibility of using ADMM algorithm to deal with the computational challenges. Vector autoregression is the most commonly used multivariate time series model. Due to its complexity, practitioners often adopt the lag-1 model for simplicity. For higher lag order, the number of parameters is dramatically larger. We propose to treat the parameters as a tensor and use dimension reduction strategy for tensors to solve this issue. For time series data, the theoretical issues in high dimensions are much more complicated and we will establish a suitable theoretical framework for our model. We also expect there will be significant gains in prediction accuracy using our approach and will use empirical financial data to verify this.

11300519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300519.value: In recent years there has been an increasing research interest on dealing with structured data sets. We are herein interested in the case tensors are involved in the modelling stage. Typically this means the predictors, the responses and/or the parameters are tensors. Tensors are natural generalizations of matrices. In the literature there have already been a lot of works on statistical estimation involving matrices. For multivariate (multi-response) linear model, one can apply reduced-rank regression assuming that the coefficient matrix has a low rank. Such an assumption reduced the effective number of parameters to be estimated and thus when the assumption is (at least approximately) true, the efficiency gain leads to a better estimate. Works on tensors are relatively more recent. Regression models with tensor predictors and/or tensor responses have been investigated in recent years. In this proposal, we consider several families of regression problems where the observations are scalars or vectors as in classical situations and these problems were all previously studied by non-tensor approaches. In the concrete problems we examine here, we make the key observation that the model parameters naturally organize themselves into tensors. Although tensors can be reshaped as matrices or vectors, this destroys the tensor structure. There have been a lot of works in the statistical literature that demonstrated that when parameters are matrices, one can often design models to take into account the matrix structure which performs better than using methods designed for vectors after vectorization. We expect the same phenomenon would be true for tensors. By treating parameters as tensors, more efficient and flexible dimension reduction schemes can be constructed, which is particularly useful when the number of parameters is large while the sample size is limited. In this proposal, we investigate three specific models and rely on the concept of low-rankness of tensor to reduce dimension. 近年來，對處理結構化數據集的研究興趣日增。我們在本項目研究含有張量的建模。通常，這意味著預測變量，響應和/或參數是張量。 張量是矩陣的高維拓展。在統計文獻中已經有很多關於矩陣的估計的研究。對於多變量（多響應）線性模型，假設係數矩陣具有低秩，則可以應用降秩回歸。這種假設減少了需要估計的參數的數量，因此當假設為真時，我們能得到更有效的估計。 有關張量的研究相對較新。近年來已經研究了具有張量自變量和/或張量響應的回歸模型。在這個項目中，我們考慮了幾個回歸問題，其中自變量和相應變量都是經典情境中的標量或向量，而這些問題之前都是通過非張量方法建模的。在我們研究的具體問題中，我們注意到模型參數能自然地組織成張量。通過將參數作為張量處理，可以構建更有效和靈活的降維方案，這在參數數量大而樣本有限時特別有用。在這個項目中，我們研究了三個特定的模型，並依靠張量的低秩概念來降低維度。

11300519.label: Realisation of objectives
11300519.value: The current project proposes to study the use of tensor in various complicated statistical models where only non-tensor methods were routinely applied previously. Tensors are natural generalizations of matrices. For example, the popular reduced-rank regression model for multivariate responses, researches assume the coefficient matrix has a low rank, which leads to a reduced number of effective number of parameters and improves statistical efficiency. The natural structure of the parametric matrix makes it possible to achieve dimension reduction in such a setting, and one certainly expects more extensive dimension reduction can be obtained for tensors by extending the current methodology for matrices. Study of tensors has attracted significant interest recently. However, this literature has focused mainly on the case that the observed data are tensors. On the other hand, we focus on more traditional statistical models but apply tensor methods in novel ways to reduce the effective number of parameters, leading to better estimates compared to traditional methods. Our first objective is to consider efficient estimation of multivariate additive models, containing a vectorial response and high-dimensional predictors. This problem was previously fitted by considering one response at a time, or by explicitly taking into account the similarities between the responses using regularization. Using spline expansions for each additive components, we rewrite the problem in the form of tensor regression, where the spline coefficients are organized into a 3-dimensional tensor. This makes it possible to apply dimension reduction approach for tensor to the multivariate additive model which originally does not contain tensors. Thus we discover a new approach using tensor although the original statistical model does not contain a tensor. This kind of approach is interesting, transferring tensor estimation approach onto non-tensor problems. Theoretically, we derive statistical convergence rates, which shows clearly that, by using low-rank assumption, the estimation rates improves upon the standard estimation method. Since our approach is an alternative to the traditional method based on sparsity assumption, the method is further combined with the sparsity-based regularization method, which can be better than either one method alone. Numerically, we demonstrate through a biological application that the improved efficiency in estimation leads to improved prediction performance in practice. Our second object is to use matrix or tensor approach to quadratic regression problem using interactions between two or more predictors in regression models. Although regression models using iterations have been studied frequently in the existing literature, when the dimension is high, the current approach is always based on sparsity assumptions, to select important predictors as well as important interactions. With interactions based on two predictors, obviously the interaction together with the original predictors can be arranged as a matrix, with the number of row and columns equal to the number of predictors. Thus a matrix estimation approach based on low-rank assumption can be used to fit the model. Again, this approach is new and an alternative to the sparsity-based fitting procedure, and thus can also be combined with sparsity assumption to improve the performance further. We show, both theoretically and empirically, using the low-rank assumption significantly improve model estimation and prediction performance, using simulated and real data sets. Originally we want to consider higher-order interactions (for example interaction among 3 predictors). However, due to the extremely high dimension when considering higher-order interactions, we find that the resulting estimator still does not perform well. On retrospect, this is not very surprising since no existing methods seems to work reasonably well in such an extremely high-dimensional setting and for such a complex regression problem. Our third aim is to consider vector autoregression problems using a tensor approach. In some sense, this is related to our first object, since here we also have a multivariate response. Traditionally, no one has applied tensor estimation approach to vector autoregression which does not seem to be related to tensors. We think we are basically the first to notice that the coefficients are naturally organized as tensors and low-rank assumption would play an important role here. The technical challenge is partially due to the non-i.i.d. setting in time series analysis. We successfully established the optimal rate of convergence for estimation, and propose a method to determine the ranks in a consistent way. Numerically, we illustrate using some economic data that the new estimation approach leads to improved prediction for both 1-step and multi-step prediction. In summary, all research objectives as originally proposed are satisfactorily completed.

11300519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300519.value: With the support of GRF funding, we have published several papers. More specifically, we have made the following progress on the project: 1. In the paper “High-dimensional vector autoregressive time series modeling via tensor decomposition” which is published in Journal of the American Statistical Association, we consider the classical vector autoregressive model which is a fundamental tool for multivariate time series analysis. However, it involves too many parameters when the number of time series and lag order are even moderately large. We propose to rearrange the transition matrices of the model into a tensor form such that the parameter space can be restricted along three directions simultaneously via tensor decomposition. In contrast, the reduced-rank regression method can restrict the parameter space in only one direction. Besides achieving substantial dimension reduction, the proposed model is interpretable from the factor modeling perspective. Moreover, to handle high-dimensional time series, we consider imposing sparsity on factor matrices to improve the model interpretability and estimation efficiency, which leads to a sparsity-inducing estimator. 2. In the paper “More Efficient Estimation of Multivariate Additive Models Based on Tensor Decomposition and Penalization”, which is published in the Journal of Machine Learning Research, we consider parsimonious modeling of high-dimensional multivariate additive models using regression splines, with or without sparsity assumptions. The approach is based on treating the coefficients in the spline expansions as a third-order tensor. A Tucker decomposition is used to reduce the number of parameters in the tensor. We also combined the Tucker decomposition with penalization to enable variable selection. The proposed method can avoid the statistical inefficiency caused by estimating a large number of nonparametric functions. 3. In the paper “Sparse and low-rank matrix quantile estimation with application to quadratic regression”, which is published in Statistica Sinica, we studied low-rank matrix regression problems where the predictor is a matrix and the response is a scalar. We propose an efficient algorithm based on ADMM to fit the model. At the same time, to further reduce the dimensionality, we assume the coefficient matrix is also sparse. In this setting of double dimension reduction using both sparsity and low-rankness, we established the statistical rate convergence of the estimator. As in the proposal, this serves as a working model that can be applied to quadratic regression problems, where the predictors and the interactions among predictors can be organized into a matrix format. In the numerical studies, we show the advantage of this re-organization in prediction performance.

11300519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300519.value: This project considered three concrete statistical models, all of which apply dimension reduction techniques based on low-rank assumption to some traditional estimation methods. There are additional problems one can study based on this general approach. For example, one can consider low-rank nonparametric regression where a bivariate function, after using basis expansion, can be estimated by estimating the coefficients which naturally has a matrix form. For a trivariate function, the same strategy will lead to the problem of estimation for an order-3 tensor. Traditionally, it is well-known that nonparametric regression for functions beyond the 1-d case suffers from so-called ``curse of dimensionality”. Thus efficient method, for example based on low-rank assumption, provide a novel route in this traditional statistical problem. Furthermore, estimation of multivariate function has important applications in reinforcement learning. For example, the estimation of the state-action function, also called the Q function, is a multivariate function, to be estimated based on observed sequence of states and rewards. We have submitted some grant proposals related to such extensions and some have been funded.

11300519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300519.value: The current project considers a simple and effective strategy for dealing with high-dimensional estimation problems, in which the parameters can be re-organized into a matrix or tensor form. Traditionally, high-dimensional data analysis often suffer from statistical inefficiency or stringent assumptions that may be hard to be satisfied, due to the limited sample size typically seen in real situations. Dimension reduction is thus a viable route to at least partially solve the problem of high dimensionality. For several concrete models that are traditionally fitted without using matrix/tensor methods, we shrewdly observe that, by rewriting the problems in various ways, the resulting models contain parameters that are re-organized into multi-dimensional arrays. Based on these observations, we propose new methods that incorporate low-rank assumptions to more efficiently fit the model and reduce the effective number of parameters. These results will provide users with new statistical tools for fitting old statistical problems, and also can be extended to more complex data analytic tasks.
