11300719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300719.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) is a clinically approved treatment modality for a range of cancers. It requires a photosensitive drug, light of appropriate wavelength, and oxygen to induce a chain of photochemical reactions, resulting in the generation of cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS). The therapeutic outcome depends largely on the tumor selectivity of the photosensitizers, their efficiency in generating ROS, and the oxygen concentration around the tumor. To address the first issue, activatable photosensitizers have been actively explored. Generally, these therapeutic agents are deactivated in the native form, but upon interactions with tumor-associated stimuli, such as certain proteases and the acidic and reducing tumor microenvironments, the fluorescence emission and ROS generation are restored. This approach can minimize the photodamage to normal cells and tissues. However, the oxygen-dependent nature of PDT still limits its clinical application against cancer, especially the hypoxic cancer. Recently, different approaches have been investigated to combat tumor hypoxia, including direct delivery of oxygen by oxygen carriers and in-situ oxygen generation through catalytic transformation of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen. In most of these systems, nanocarriers based on polymers, gold nanoparticles, mesoporous silica nanoparticles, or metal-organic frameworks are required, which usually involve tedious synthetic and fabrication protocols and have limited drug loading and potential toxicity to healthy tissues. As a potentially improved alternative, carrier-free self-assembled nanomedicines are of much current interest. In this proposal, we aim to develop such nanophotosensitizing systems for photodynamic eradication of hypoxic tumor. The proposed work includes the preparation of a series of glutathione-responsive phthalocyanine-based photosensitizers with a tumor-targeting ligand, followed by co-assembly with fluorenylmethyloxycarbonyl-protected amino acids and iron(III) chloride to form multicomponent nanoparticles. Upon activation by the relatively abundant glutathione in tumor, the photosensitizing properties of the photosensitizers will be restored to generate ROS upon light irradiation. As cancer cells usually have high concentration of hydrogen peroxide, it is expected that the encapsulated iron(III) ions will undergo catalase-like reaction with hydrogen peroxide to generate oxygen that can assist the photodynamic action at hypoxic cancer cells. To introduce an additional therapeutic action against hypoxic tumor, the hypoxia-inducible factor 1 inhibitor acriflavine will also be co-assembled into the nanodrugs which can block the pathways promoting the growth of tumor. It is believed that these self-assembled oxygen-replenishing nanophotosensitizing systems with tumor-targeting and activatable properties, as well as diverse cell-killing mechanisms can exhibit enhanced therapeutic efficacy against hypoxic tumor and overcome the current limitations of PDT. 光動力治療（PDT）是一種臨床批准用於多種癌症的治療手段。它主要通過光敏劑，光和氧氣來誘發一系列光化學反應從而產生具有生物毒性的氧活性物種 (ROS)。因此，光動力治療效果大大依賴於光敏劑的腫瘤選擇性，ROS的產生效率以及腫瘤微環境的氧濃度。目前基於可啟動的光敏劑的研究備受矚目，通常這類光敏劑是失活的，但一經與腫瘤相關刺激物，例如某些蛋白酶，低pH和還原性腫瘤微環境相互作用後，螢光強度和ROS的產生得以恢復，所以這種光敏劑大大降低了對正常細胞和組織的光損傷。再者，PDT的需氧的性質使得它在臨床抗腫瘤應用中仍然具有極大的限制。近年來，針對腫瘤低氧微環境的研究被廣泛地探索，包括利用氧載體直接遞送氧氣或通過催化過氧化氫原位產氧，然而目前大多數體系是基於有機聚合物，無機納米顆粒或是金屬有機框架的納米載體，但是它們往往製備繁瑣，裝載率極低以及對人體具有潛在的毒性。因此，具有生物相容性的自組裝納米藥物的開發備受關注。在本提案中，我們將發展這樣一種光敏納米藥物來對抗低氧腫瘤微環境，工作主要包括一系列具有谷胱甘肽回應性和靶向功能的光敏劑-酞菁的製備以及基於Fmoc-氨基酸和Fe3+的共組裝的多組分光敏納米藥物的製備。這些納米藥物一但進入腫瘤就會被廣泛分佈的谷胱甘肽啟動，光敏劑的光敏特性得以恢復進而在光照條件下產生ROS。同時腫瘤微環境分佈著高濃度的過氧化氫，作為納米顆粒構建單元的Fe3+將會發揮其催化劑的角色轉化過氧化氫為氧氣從而克服腫瘤乏氧問題，而且為進一步增強光動力治療效果，腫瘤低氧誘導因數抑製劑也被引入納米藥物體系中從而進一步阻斷腫瘤的生長。可以預見，這些具有腫瘤靶向和可啟動特性的自供氧型自組裝納米光敏化系統及其多種細胞殺傷機制能夠針對缺氧腫瘤微環境展現出極強的光動力治療效果並在很大程度上克服目前PDT的局限性。

11300719.label: Realisation of objectives
11300719.value: The first objective of this project is to design, synthesize, and characterize a series of activatable zinc(II) phthalocyanines, which will be co-assembled with Fmoc-amino acids and iron(III) chloride to form multicomponent nanoparticles and introduce an additional cytotoxic component to enhance the antitumor efficacy. In our initial efforts, we synthesized two zinc(II) phthalocyanines (ZnPcs) substituted with a short peptide featuring either a carboxyl or a carbamoyl group at the C-terminus and an appended biotin moiety (ACS Appl. Bio. Mater. 2020, 3, 5463-5473). They self-assembled into spherical nanoparticles through noncovalent interactions. These nanoparticles were further coassembled with chemotherapeutic doxorubicin to enhance therapeutic efficacy. Based on these findings, we have gained valuable insights into how to optimize and streamline the self-assembly process of ZnPcs and anticancer drugs. We then expanded our study by creating catalase-like photosensitizing nanozymes with a self-oxygen-supplying ability. This involved Fe3+-driven self-assembly of fluorenylmethyloxycarbonyl (Fmoc)-protected amino acids and encapsulation of ZnPc and the hypoxia-inducible factor 1 inhibitor acriflavine (ACF) (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 23228). By mixing Fmoc-Cys and ZnPc in DMSO with or without ACF, followed by the addition of FeCl3 and distilled water, the co-assembled Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc and Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc/ACF were formed. These nanovesicles could be disassembled intracellularly and the released Fe3+ ions could catalyze the transformation of hydrogen peroxide enriched in cancer cells to oxygen efficiently, thereby ameliorating the hypoxic condition and promoting the photosensitizing activity of the released ZnPc. Similarly, we also developed Cu2+-coordinated self-assembled nanoparticles by mixing a glutathione-responsive carboxy ZnPc (ZnPc∗) and CuSO4·5H2O in water with or without the presence of the anticancer drug SN38 to afford ZnPc∗/Cu/SN38@NP and ZnPc∗/Cu@NP, respectively (Acta Biomater. 2023, 162, 57-71). The Cu2+ ions not only facilitated the self-assembly of the carboxy phthalocyanine through metal complexation, but also catalyzed the conversion of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen via a catalase-like reaction, rendering an oxygen-replenishing property. In addition to using Fe3+ and Cu2+ ions, we employed the biomineralization process of calcium phosphate with manganese doping, followed by loading with ZnPc to afford CaMnP@ZnPc. Upon exposure to acidic environment, these nanoparticles released the payloads, including Ca2+ and Mn2+ ions, and ZnPc. The released Ca2+ ions could trigger mitochondrial dysfunction and suppress cellular respiration, conserving endogenous oxygen. Simultaneously, the released Mn2+ ions could engage in a catalase-like reaction, producing oxygen to enhance the PDT's efficacy (Manuscript in preparation). After preparing all these nanosystems, their size and morphology were examined, showing that they were spherical in shape with a diameter of 100-200 nm. The loadings of different components were investigated by different spectroscopic methods. The nanoparticles in organic solvents exhibited the characteristic peaks of the free form of ZnPc and other therapeutic units because organic solvents disrupt the noncovalent interactions among the components, resulting in disassembly of the nanoparticles. However, the absorption of these nanosystems became significantly weakened and broadened in water, due to the self-aggregation of the ZnPc units in the nanoparticles. Upon excitation at 610 nm where ZnPc absorbs, the nanosystems exhibited a strong fluorescence emission at 690-700 nm in DMSO ascribable to the free ZnPc units, while their fluorescence intensity was significantly diminished in water, indicating that the ZnPc units were strongly aggregated in the nanoparticles. These nanoparticles also generated singlet oxygen efficiently in DMSO or upon disassembly in water. The stability of these self-assembled nanoparticles was examined under different pH, in the presence of glutathione (GSH), and in a culture medium with 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS). We found that the nanoparticles underwent disassembly in the presence of GSH or under acidic pH in PBS, subsequently releasing the Fe3+, Cu2+, or Mn2+ ions, and other therapeutic components. However, the nanoparticles remained stable in water for 7 days and in a culture medium with 10% FBS for 48 h. We also investigated the conversion of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen catalyzed by the encapsulated Fe3+, Cu2+, or Mn2+ ions. All the nanosystems containing Fe3+, Cu2+, or Mn2+ ions effectively generated oxygen within 20 min, demonstrating their self-oxygen-supplying ability in hydrogen peroxide-enriched environments. To achieve the fourth objective, we evaluated the in vitro activities of these nanoparticles against a range of cancer cells. Their dark- and photocytotoxities were examined against HT29 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells, HepG2 human hepatocarcinoma cells, U-87 human glioblastoma cells, or 4T1 mammary carcinoma cells under both normoxic and hypoxic conditions. Without light irradiation, we observed a certain percentage of cell death due to the therapeutic effect of ACF or SN38 in Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc/ACF and ZnPc∗/Cu/SN38@NP, respectively. However, the low concentration of encapsulated Fe3+, Cu2+, or Mn2+ ions did not induce any cytotoxicity. The free ZnPc displayed a dose-dependent photocytotoxicity on HT29, U-87, and 4T1 cells under normoxia, but remained essentially non-photocytotoxic under hypoxia. However, Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc, ZnPc∗/Cu@NP, and CaMnP@ZnPc exhibited high photocytotoxicity under both conditions and the potency was not significantly affected by oxygen level. The results could be attributed to the Fe3+, Cu2+, and Mn2+-promoted conversion of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen by Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc, ZnPc∗/Cu@NP, and CaMnP@ZnPc, respectively, hence facilitating the photodynamic action on hypoxic cancer cells. With an additional therapeutic component, Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc/ACF and ZnPc∗/Cu/SN38@NP exhibited higher potency, demonstrating the synergistic effect of ZnPc and ACF or SN38, respectively. The cellular uptake, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, and hypoxia-attenuating ability of these nanoparticles were investigated against HT29 cells under normoxia and hypoxia. After incubating these nanoparticles with the cells, fluorescence of ZnPc was observed in the cytoplasm of the cells upon excitation of ZnPc, suggesting that these nanoparticles were internalized into the cells and subsequently disassembled, causing intracellular fluorescence. Moreover, these nanoparticles generated ROS under both normoxia and hypoxia, demonstrating that the released Fe3+, Cu2+, and Mn2+ ions could undergo a catalase-like reaction to elevate the oxygen concentration, thereby promoting ROS production in hypoxic cancer cells. The degree of hypoxia was also assessed based on the HIF-1α level. It was found that the hydrogen peroxide-treated HT29 cells exhibited a high level of HIF-1α under hypoxia, while the HIF-1α content was significantly reduced upon treatment with Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc, ZnPc∗/Cu@NP, and CaMnP@ZnPc, or for the PBS-treated cells under normoxia. These results were further confirmed by Western blot analysis. To address the last objective, we investigated the in vivo biodistribution and antitumor efficacy of these nanoparticles in HT29-tumor-bearing nude mice. After administration of these nanoparticles, their biodistribution was examined with whole-body fluorescence imaging and continuously monitored for 2 days. The fluorescence intensity was not visible over the first few hours, and then increased gradually at the tumor region and reached the maximum at 24 h post-injection. The fluorescence could still be observed after injection for 48 h. It suggested that ZnPc was still encapsulated and self-quenched during the first few hours after injection, and then the nanoparticles were disassembled to release ZnPc gradually. Finally, the therapeutic effect of these nanoparticles was investigated and compared with the appropriate controls. We found that Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc, Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc/ACF, ZnPc∗/Cu/SN38@NP, ZnPc∗/Cu@NP, and CaMnP@ZnPc could significantly suppress tumor growth upon light irradiation. The degree of tumor inhibition was slightly higher for those nanoparticles containing ACF or SN38, demonstrating their enhanced therapeutic potential. All the above results show that the five objectives set for this project have been fully achieved.

11300719.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300719.value: We developed a facile method to prepare a series of Fe(III) ion-driven catalase-like supramolecular photosensitizing nanozymes for photodynamic eradiation of hypoxic tumor (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 23228-23238). Fe3+ ions could effectively control the assembly of Fmoc-protected amino acids into hollow nanovesicles, which further encapsulated ZnPc and ACF. The resulting nanosystems exhibited robust stability under physiological conditions and a GSH-responsive disassembled property. They down-regulated the HIF-1α level and relieved hypoxia in HT29 cells via the Fe3+-promoted conversion of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen. These nanosystems also exhibited high PDT potency against HT29 cells under both normoxic and hypoxic conditions, and their photocytotoxicity were not affected by the surrounding oxygen level. With an additional therapeutic component, Fmoc-Cys/Fe@Pc/ACF further enhanced the cytotoxicity on HT29 cells, demonstrating the synergistic effect of ZnPc and ACF. These nanosystems could accumulate at the tumor region of the nude mice through the enhanced permeability and retention effect, attenuate the tumor hypoxia, and induce photocytotoxicity to suppress the tumor growth. A related oxygen-supplying nanotherapeutics containing Cu2+ ions was also prepared (Acta Biomater. 2023, 162, 57-71). We utilized Cu2+ ions to promote the self-assembly of a GSH-responsive carboxy ZnPc, both in the absence and presence of SN38, to form the nanosystems. These nanoparticles were stable in various aqueous media, while they disassembled in an acidic or GSH-enriched environment and released free ZnPc* and SN38. The former was also activated in terms of photosensitizing properties upon the action of GSH. The encapsulated Cu2+ ions could effectively promote the conversion of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen via a catalase-like reaction, rendering an oxygen-replenishing property. The disassembly process, GSH-responsive properties, and oxygen-replenishing ability of these nanotherapeutics were demonstrated in vitro using HT29 cells through a series of experiments under both normoxia and hypoxia. Furthermore, these nanoparticles exhibited significant antitumor efficacy and hypoxia-relieving ability in tumor-bearing nude mice. Finally, we utilized oxygen-supplying and oxygen-economized strategies to overcome tumor hypoxia for enhanced PDT (Manuscript in preparation). Ca2+ and Mn2+ ions were incorporated into the nanoparticles, in which Ca2+ ions could suppress cellular respiration to conserve endogenous oxygen and simultaneously Mn2+ ions could catalyze hydrogen peroxide to oxygen to self-supplying oxygen. These nanoparticles exhibited high ROS generation and photocytotoxicity against HT29 cells under both normoxia and hypoxia. Moreover, they caused mitochondrial dysfunction, reduced ATP production and HIF-1α expression. In vivo studies also demonstrated that these nanoparticles could retard tumor growth and relieve tumor hypoxia.

11300719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300719.value: The promising results open up several avenues for further research. We demonstrated the potential of oxygen-replenishing nanophotosensitizing systems in suppressing tumor growth, especially when combined with other therapeutic agents. The results suggest opportunities for further optimization and testing across various cancer types. Future research could refine the nanoparticle composition to enhance therapeutic efficacy and minimize side effects. A unique feature of these nanophotosensitizing systems is their self-oxygen-supplying ability, which could address tumor hypoxia, a common challenge in cancer treatment. Further studies could explore their applications for other therapeutic modalities. One of our newly-developed nanoparticles can inhibit cellular respiration while simultaneously supplying oxygen, potentially enhancing PDT effectiveness. Future research could optimize this dual action to maximize oxygen availability for PDT, improving its therapeutic efficacy. This could involve adjusting the nanoparticle composition or investigating the optimal dosage for the dual action. The proposed course of action includes comprehensive in vivo studies to assess the long-term safety and efficacy of these nanophotosensitizing systems. Exploring their potential in combination with other treatment modalities, such as immunotherapy, could also be beneficial. Finally, scaling up the synthesis of these nanosystems for potential clinical trials is a crucial step towards their eventual application in cancer treatment.

11300719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300719.value: This study presents a novel approach to overcoming the limitation of photodynamic therapy (PDT), a clinically approved treatment modality for various cancers. PDT’s effectiveness is often hindered by the oxygen-dependent nature of the process, particularly in hypoxic cancers. In this study, we designed and synthesized a series of oxygen-evolving self-assembled nanophotosensitizing systems for photodynamic eradication of hypoxic tumors. We utilized iron(III) and copper(II) ions to promote the self-assembly of photosensitizers and anticancer drugs, with or without Fmoc-protected amino acids. Moreover, these metal ions could catalyze the conversion of hydrogen peroxide to oxygen via a catalase-like reaction, providing additional oxygen for PDT. Besides, we also developed dual-functional nanoparticles using calcium phosphate with manganese doping. These nanoparticles could inhibit cellular respiration to conserve endogenous oxygen, and simultaneously supply more oxygen via a catalase-like reaction, thereby further increasing the intracellular oxygen level. This self-assembled strategy provides a facile and environmental-friendly approach to encapsulate photosensitizers and different therapeutic components into nanoparticles, which facilitates the accumulation of nanoparticles at tumor region through the enhanced permeability and retention effect. The results showed that all these nanoparticles could successfully eradicate hypoxic tumors, overcoming the limitation of traditional PDT.

11300819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300819.value: In two dimensions, gapped quantum many-body systems can host exotic quasiparticles, named anyons, that are neither fermions nor bosons. Anyons obey fractional braiding statistics. A system that hosts anyons is said to carry a topological order. Associated with the so-called non-Abelian anyons is a topologically protected low-energy degenerate state space, into which one can store quantum information and perform quantum computation — namely topological quantum computation. One of the advantages is that the information is stored in a non-local way and thereby robust against any local disturbances. It is highly demanded to find physical systems to host anyons, and to find novel detection methods to confirm their existence and probe their properties. Symmetry is one of the most powerful theoretical concepts and tools for predicting, analyzing, and identifying many physical phenomena. In this proposal, we study theoretically the deep interplay between symmetry and topological order in quantum many-body systems, aiming to uncover fundamental properties of anyons in the presence of symmetries. A topological order may exhibit different symmetry properties, dubbed different Symmetry-Enriched Topological (SET) phases. Generally speaking, there exist two kinds of interplay between symmetry and topological order: (1) symmetries can permute anyon types, i.e., under a symmetry action, a quasiparticle may change its anyon type; (2) symmetries can be fractionalized on anyons, e.g., an anyon may carry fractional charge of a symmetry. Most of the previous studies focus the second kind only. The mutual effect of the two kinds of interplay is rarely studied so far. For SETs of fermionic systems, it is suspected that many interesting physical phenomena, such as certain new kinds of quantum anomalies, require supports from both nontrivial permutations and symmetry fractionalization. The purpose of this proposed project is to carry out an in-depth theoretical study on symmetry fractionalization in the presence of nontrivial anyon permutations. We will emphasize on physical approaches, instead of more mathematical methods, to study both bosonic and fermionic SETs. This study is of fundamental importance to the general principles of topological phases of strongly corrected quantum matter. As most materials are fermionic (electronic), our results on fermionic SETs can be useful for predicting or eliminating topological order in certain materials. 二維有能隙的量子多體系統中，可以存在既不是費米子也不是玻色子的奇異的準粒子， 稱之為任意子。任意子遵從分數編織統計， 而承載任意子的系統則被稱之為具有拓撲序。如果一個系統中有所謂的非阿貝爾任意子，那麼跟它們並存的是一些受拓撲保護的低能簡併態。人們可以在這些簡併態中存儲量子信息，並進行量子計算 -- 即所謂的拓撲量子計算。拓撲量子計算的優點是信息以非局域的方式存儲，從而使得信息可以抵抗任何局域的擾動。 近年來人們迫切的尋找能承載任意子的物理系統，並摸索新的檢測方法來確認任意子的存在及探索它們的物理性質。在物理學中，對稱性是預測、分析和探測許多物理現象的強大的理論概念和工具之一。在本項目中，我們會從理論上研究量子多體系統中對稱性和拓撲序之間的深刻的相互作用，並揭示任意子的基本對稱性性質。 同一拓撲序可以展現出不同的對稱性性質，被稱之為不同的對稱富化拓撲相。一般來說，對稱性和拓撲序之間存在兩種相互作用：（1）對稱性可以置換任意子類型，即在對稱性作用下，任意子可以改變其類型; （2）任意子可以攜帶分數化的量子數，例如任意子可以攜帶分數電荷。大多數以前的研究只關注第二種相互作用，並且兩種相互作用之間的互相影響也很少被研究。另外，對於費米子系統的對稱富化拓撲相，有證據表明許多有趣的物理現象，例如某些特定的量子反常，必須有非平凡的任意子置換和對稱性分數化的支持。 該項目的研究目的是在存在非平凡的任意子置換下，對對稱性分數化進行深入的理論研究。我們會採用強調物理的而非數學的方法，來研究玻色子和費米子系統中的對稱富化相。本研究對強關聯量子物質拓撲相的基礎原理會起到重要作用 。由於大多數材料是費米子（電子），我們對費米子拓撲序的研究可能幫助預測某些材料中是否存在拓撲序。

11300819.label: Realisation of objectives
11300819.value: This project aims to study the interplay between symmetry and topology in quantum many-body systems. The focus of the project shifted from the original plan of studying bulk properties to boundary properties: we studied roles of anomalous symmetry on edge theory of 2D topological phases, via quantum field theory and lattice model. Overall, the objectives are achieved with satisfactory results. 1. For objective 1, we studied a class of edge theories of symmetry-protected topological phases using field theoretical approach. By partially gauging the symmetry group, the edge theories can be mapped to those of symmetry-enriched topological phases with nontrivial permutation of gauging fluxes that are non-Abelian anyons. We performed the study in the framework of K-matrix Luttinger liquid theory. The results are included in Paper 2 of Part C. In addition, we constructed lattice models and performed numerical studies for the edge of Abelian topological phases, published in Paper 3 in Part C. The lattice models also exhibit Luttinger liquid behavior. 2. For objective 2, we extended the K-matrix field theoretical study to fermionic topological phases. We were able to obtained the edge theory of those fermionic topological phases whose gauge fluxes carry Majorana zero modes. The quantum anomaly of symmetries were identified using techniques from conformal field theory. The results are included in Paper 2 of Part C. 3. For the edge of general symmetry-enriched topological phases, we focused more on lattice models and constructed anomalous symmetry by making use of category theory. We obtained a family of one-dimensional quantum lattice models based on G-graded unitary fusion category. The corresponding bulk of these boundary models can be of any non-chiral topological order with general symmetry properties (with or without anyon permutation). Interesting phase diagrams exhibiting quantum critical phases are numerically obtained. These results are included in the preprint 4 in Part C.

11300819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300819.value: 1. We obtained edge field theories for various bosonic and fermionic symmetry-protected topological phases, published in Phys. Rev. B 104, 075151 (2021). These edge theories are conformal field theories (Luttinger liquid) that preserve certain anomalous global symmetries. The Abelian Chern-Simons theory and K-matrix theory are used to obtain the results. In particular, we obtained the edge theory for fermionic topological phases whose symmetry fluxes host Majorana zero modes. 2. We constructed a family of 1D quantum lattice models that can be viewed as the edge of 2D symmetry-protected or symmetry-enriched topological phases, published in Phys. Rev. B 104, 075151 (2021) and arXiv:2301.06416 (2023), respectively. The models of symmetry-protected topological phases are obtained by starting with 2D models and projecting out the bulk. Numerical simulations were carried out by our collaborators. It turned out to host a gapless Luttinger liquid phase. More generally, we used category theory to directly constructed edge models of 2D symmetry-enriched topological states. The models display a set of unconventional anomalous symmetries that are characterized by the input category. They often exhibit a quantum critical phase, which can be a general conformal field theory, as supported by our numerical calculations.

11300819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300819.value: Many questions remain open in the study of the interplay between symmetry and topology. As this project was carried out, we gradually shifted from studying bulk symmetry properties to edge symmetry properties of 2D topological phases. However, some bulk properties remain elusive such as those fermionic symmetry-enriched topological orders hosting the so-called H^2 cohomology quantum anomaly. In addition, the one-dimensional lattice models that we construct can in principle describe the edge of fermionic symmetry-enriched topological phases, enabled by gauging the fermion parity. The explicit connection to the fermionic edges, however, still needs to be worked out. For further study, I would like to follow these questions and hopefully obtain explicit answers.

11300819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11300819.value: Symmetry and topology can show intriguing interplay in quantum many-body systems for both bosons and fermions. Such an interplay has recently led to the discovery of novel quantum matter such as topological insulators and topological superconductors. One of the key features is that the boundary of these topological phases display anomalous symmetry properties. In this regard, we studied anomalous symmetry properties and their consequences via the approaches of quantum field theory and lattice models. We obtained field theoretical descriptions and constructed lattice models for the edges of various two-dimensional topological phases, and identified the nontrivial roles of symmetries in these theories. As a consequence of the anomalous symmetry properties, the lattice models we constructed often show an extended quantum critical regime. Our work may be important for further study of quantum critical phenomena.

11300919.label: Project Objectives
11300919.value: A flexible latent factor framework will be developed. The developed framework is expected to effectively incorporate information across nodes in large-scale directed networks, to allow for efficient computation, and to attain desirable theoretical properties. A bi-directional community detection method will be developed under the latent factor framework. The developed method is expected to accurately identify users with similar interests and thus have similar following patterns, and users with similar profiles and thus have similar followers. A covariate-assisted link prediction method will be developed. The developed method is expected to appropriately incorporate the adapted homophily phenomenon of directed networks to improve the link prediction accuracy. A time-evolving directed network model will be developed. The developed method is expected to effectively integrate a network autoregression model into the latent factor framework, which shall accurately forecast newly evolving and diminishing edges for future time points.

11300919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11300919.value: 本研究項目將發展一個關於帶協變量和結構的大規模有向圖的靈活的隱因子模型。該隱因子模型引入兩組不同的隱因子來對有向圖中的出結點（Out-node）和入結點（In-node）分別建模。在此基礎上，我們將提出一個雙向的社區發現（Community Detection）方法來發現關於同一組結點的兩種不同可能的社區：一個出結點社區和一個入結點社區。我們也將通過局部平滑的方法在隱因子模型中引入協變量，以處理有向圖中的可適應同質化（Homophily）現象，從而提高鏈接預測的準確性。我們也會將利用網絡自回歸的思想來推廣該隱因子模型，並對時變的有向圖進行建模。我們將考察本項目提出的方法的理論性質，建立它們的大樣本及有限樣本的概率上界。我們也將利用並行計算平台的優勢針對本項目中遇到的大規模優化問題發展一些有效的算法。最後，我們將運用本項目中提出的方法對實際生活中擁有超過百萬用戶的社交網絡進行建模。

11300919.label: Realisation of objectives
11300919.value: In this project, the PI and his collaborators develop a novel method to conduct network embedding and community detection simultaneously in a large-scale directed network. The network embedding model introduces two sets of vectors to represent the out- and in-nodes separately, and thus allows the same nodes belong to different out- and in-communities. The community detection formulation equips the negative log-likelihood with a novel regularization term to encourage community structure among the nodes representations, and thus achieves better performance by jointly estimating the nodes embeddings and their community structures. The asymptotic properties of the proposed method are established in terms of both network embedding and community detection, which are also supported by numerical experiments on various simulated and real-life networks. The proposed network embedding method is also generalized to detecting communities in overlapped directed networks, particularly stochastic co-block model (ScBM). We extended the ScBM model so that each node may belong to multiple out- or in-communities. Particularly, we formulate the ScBM model as a generative model, where the unknown community assignment is modeled based on the exclusive or overlapped community. We also establish the corresponding identifiability of the generative ScBM model, and estimate its parameters via an efficient variational EM algorithm. Furthermore, we propose a regularized network embedding model to simultaneously estimate the community structure and the number of communities. The proposed model equips network embedding with a novel composite regularization term, which pushes the embedding vector toward its center and pushes similar community centers collapsed with each other. A rigorous theoretical analysis is conducted, establishing asymptotic consistency in terms of community detection and estimation of the number of communities. The superior performance of the proposed method is demonstrated via extensive numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-life brain functional connectivity network. The PI and his collaborators further extend the embedding idea to modelling text data. We proposed a embedding learning framework to deliver a higher learning accuracy while identifying an optimal learning-adaptive embedding. In particular, we propose a concept of U-minimal sufficient learning-adaptive embeddings, based on which we seek an optimal one to maximize the learning accuracy subject to an embedding constraint. Moreover, when specializing the general framework to classification, we derive a graph embedding classifier based on a hyperlink tensor representing multiple hypergraphs, directed or undirected, characterizing multi-way relations of unstructured data. We also design algorithms based on blockwise coordinate descent and projected gradient descent to implement linear and feed-forward neural network classifiers, respectively. Theoretically, we establish a learning theory to quantify the generalization error of the proposed method. Empirically, we demonstrate the utility of the classifiers on two benchmarks in grammatical classification and sentiment analysis. All proposed methods are implemented in Python, and available upon request. The PI is also closely working with one of the collaborators to wrap up all the implementations in both Python and R packages for dissemination in the coming year.

11300919.label: Major findings and research outcome
11300919.value: The major findings of this project are three-folds. First, the PI and his collaborator develop a novel method to conduct network embedding and community detection simultaneously in a large-scale directed network (Part C Output 1). The key advantages of the proposed method are that it allows each node to contribute differently to out- and in-communities and that it allows community detection is super-sparse networks, which are commonly encountered in real-life social networks. Second, the proposed embedding method is extended to detecting communities in overlapped directed networks, and to simultaneously estimate community structure and community number (Part C Outputs 3, 4 & 5). Thanks to the explicit embedding formulation, we cast the network embedding model in a generative framework or a regularization framework to attain various modelling purposes. The asymptotic consistency of the proposed methods is established even when the network sparsity is only of logarithm order of the number of nodes. Extensive numerical experiments also illustrate the superior performance of the proposed methods against some state-of-the-art competitors. Third, this project also develops tools to bridge classical text mining framework to modern unstructured data modelling techniques (Part C Output 2). Particularly, the embedding model developed for network data can be well adapted to various text mining tasks, leading to interpretable text mining models, efficient computational schemes, and superior numerical performance.

11300919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11300919.value: One potential development is to extend the proposed network embedding method to community detection in multi-layer networks and hypergraph networks. Such networks have been commonly encountered in real life, particularly when there are time stamps on the collected networks. In contrast to network data, the computational challenge becomes a major bottle network as the number of edges increases in a polynomial order of the number of nodes. The PI and his PhD student are now working on this extension, by fully utilizing the desirable properties of the network embedding method. The preliminary numerical experiments are very promising, and the required computational cost can be substantially reduced without any sacrifice of the estimation accuracy. The PI plans to admit another PhD student or a Postdoc to join the research team and complete the theoretical guarantees of these extensions.

11300919.value: This proposed research project develops novel network embedding methods large-scele networks. All the objectives are achieved, and an efficient statistical machine learning framework is developed, which is in sharp contrast to most existing methods in literature. The research findings have a wide spectrum of applications in practice, ranging from biomedicine, economics and finance, and information technology. The proposed research not only develop a novel perspective of network modeling, but also provide rich opportunities for postgraduate students to participate in cutting-edge researches. With the support of this project, the PI and his collaborators published 6 research articles on leading statistics and machine learning journals, and trained one Ph.D. student, Dr. Jingnan Zhang. Dr. Zhang is currently Assistant Professor at University of Science and Technology in China, one of the best universities in Mainland China. More importantly, this project also opens up a few potential directions for future research on learning complex structure in large-scale unstructured data.

11301419.label: Project Objectives
11301419.value: Framelets on Graphs for Deep Convolution Neural Networks. Our first objective is to investigate framelets for graph convolution neural networks (graph CNNs). We shall focus on: Objective 1.1: Discrete Fourier transforms (DFTs) on graph domains and their fast implementations. Objective 1.2: Convolution and pooling on graph CNNs. Objective 1.3: Framelets for graph CNNs. We start from the nowadays standard and classical architectures of deep CNNs. Adaptation of such standard CNN architectures to applications for data defined on graph domains requires our investigations on the two basic layers of CNNs: The convolution layer and the pooling layer. We first focus on the development of fast Fourier transforms based on either the spectral approaches (graph Laplacians) or non-spectral approaches. Convolution of graph data with filters can then be defined in the spectral domain using such Fourier transforms. The pooling layer is closely related to the graph coarsening, which plays an crucial role in the efficient realizations of the graph CNNs. Framelets or framelet filters having a multiscale structure can be defined as (structured) parameterized filters on graph CNNs. Theoretical analysis could be done from the perspective of approximation theory. Deep Convolution Neural Networks for Graph Data Processing. Our second objective is to investigate the deep learning applications using our developed framelets on graph CNNs. Regular data on Euclidian domains can be regarded as graph data through a k-NN (k nearest neighborhood) transform. We can test our systems for regular data analysis and applications such as signal/image/video processing. On the other hand, typical graph data processing shall be considered. For examples, we can consider applications of our systems in community detection, ranking, citation network, or recommender systems.

11301419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11301419.value: Artificial Intelligence known as AI enters the horizon of every people's eyes never as frequently as in today's modern society. The power of AI in terms of machine and deep learning reaches almost every branch of people's daily life. For example, smartphones' personal assistants based on natural language processing, autopilot cars based on object and pattern recognition, entertainment or e-shopping experiences based on recommender systems, and so on. Many concepts or inventions that only happened in scientific movies or novels before are now commonly appeared and used across the whole world. In short, "the future is now'' is indeed happening. Behind the great success of AI is of course the rapid advancement of computer hardware as well as software achievements that are driven by scientific research. The deep learning techniques together with data science are nowadays two of the powerful "engines'' for the AI development. Since data are not only defined on regular Euclidean domains but also on irregular domains such graphs, in this project, we focus on analysis and processing of data defined on graphs using framelets and consider its applications in deep learning. Framelets specifically designed for graphs will provide new and efficient graph data processing based on deep convolution neural networks (CNNs). The results of this project will contribute to the further development of AI. 被稱為“AI”的人工智能從未像今天的現代社會一樣如此廣闊頻繁地進入人們的視野中。人工智能以機器學習與深度學習為前沿幾乎涉及人們日常生活的每個部分。例如，智能手機中基於自然語言處理的個人助理，基於對象及模式識別的自動駕駛汽車，基於推薦系統的娛樂或電子購物體驗等。許多只發生在以前科學電影或小說的概念或發明，現在卻經常出現並在全世界中應用。簡而言之,“未來就是現在”確實正在發生。 人工智能能夠取得如此巨大成功的背後當然是計算機硬件的快速發展以及由科學研究驅動的軟件成就。深度學習技術與數據科學是當今人工智能篷勃發展後面的兩個強大的 “引擎”。由於數據不僅定義在常規歐幾裡得區域，也在不規則區域，如“圖”上的數據，在這個項目中，我們專注於分析和使用框架小波處理在圖上定義的數據並考慮其在深度學習中的應用。專為圖(Graph)設計的框架小波將提供新的和基於深度卷積神經網絡（CNN）的高效圖數據處理。該項目的成果將有助於人工智能的進一步發展。

11301419.label: Realisation of objectives
11301419.value: Objectives as per Section 5.1 above. Objective 1: Framelets on Graphs for Deep Convolution Neural Networks. Objective 2: Deep Convolution Neural Networks for Graph Data Processing. To achieve these two objectives, the PI and his collaborators focused on two main aspects: one is the characterization and construction of framelets on graphs, and the other is the applications of framelets on graphs. For the part of characterizations and construction, the PI and his collaborators mainly investigated two approaches for the construction of framelets on graphs. One approach is based on the spectral method, and the other is based on the spatial method. Both approaches are crucial in the analysis and applications of data defined on either the simple classical Euclidean domain, e.g., the squares or cubes, or the graph-structured domain we mainly investigated in the project. Based on a sequence of orthonormal bases from a hierarchical coarse-grained chain of graphs, we provided a full characterization of a sequence of decimated/undecimated G-framelet systems on graphs. Such a general characterization facilitates the construction of framelets on graphs through either the graph Laplacian (spectral-based method) or the Haar tree orthonormal basis (spatial-based method). More generally, based on hierarchical partitions, we provided the complete characterization and construction of Haar-type tight framelets/wavelets on any compact set. In particular, on the d-dimensional hypercube, such tight framelets can be built with adaptivity and directionality. We show that the adaptive directional Haar tight framelet systems can be used for digraph signal representations. For the part of applications, based on the developed framelets, the PI and his collaborators investigated their applications in both Euclidean-structured data and graph-structured data processing. For the Haar-type wavelet systems on graphs (spatial-based), we applied them in the definition of graph convolution. We used it in the design of the graph neural networks (GNNs), which demonstrate state-of-the-art results on graph-based regression and node classification tasks. Moreover, we applied such Haar graph systems for the critical operation of neural network pooling, which is crucial for the graph classification task. Such Haar systems play a vital role in the regularization model for image restoration (Euclidian data) as well. For the decimated framelet systems on graphs (spectral-based), we applied them in the design of general graph framelet neural networks (GFNNs), which demonstrate superior performance in the graph classification task for many benchmark datasets. In summary, the Objectives 1 and 2 have been achieved completely. For major findings and research outcomes, we refer to Section 6.1 of this report.

11301419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11301419.value: We introduced a Haar basis for a coarse-grained chain on the graph for the design of graph convolution in graph neural networks (GNNs). The graph convolution under the Haar basis can be defined accordingly for GNNs. The sparsity and locality of the Haar basis allow Fast Haar Transforms (FHTs) on the graph. Based on GNNs equipped with Haar convolution, we demonstrated state-of-the-art results on graph-based regression and node classification tasks. See Part C Sec. 8, the paper in “Neural Networks,” 2020, 128:188-198. For the design of graph pooling in GNNs, we proposed a new graph pooling operation based on Haar transforms: HaarPooling. A HaarPooling layer transforms an input graph into an output graph with a smaller node number and the same feature dimension. Such transforms provide a sparse characterization and preserve the structure information. GNNs with standard graph convolution and HaarPooling layers achieve state-of-the-art performance on diverse graph classification and regression problems. See Part C Sec. 8, the paper in “International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML2020),” 119: 9952-9962. Based on hierarchical partitions, we constructed Haar-type tight framelets on any compact set. In particular, on the d-dimensional hypercube, such tight framelets can be built with adaptivity and directionality. We showed that the adaptive directional Haar tight framelet systems can be used for digraph signal representations. See Part C Sec. 8, the paper in “Journal of Fourier Analysis and Applications”, 2021, 27:7. We proposed a novel multiscale representation system, called decimated framelets, which allow graph data representation on a coarse-grained chain. We established fast decimated G-framelet transforms (FGT) for the decomposition and reconstruction of the graph data. The FGT has linear computational complexity O(N) for a graph of size N. The effectiveness of our decimated framelets is demonstrated by simulated examples of random graphs and traffic networks, as well as the applications in GNNs for graph classification tasks. See Part C, the paper in “Journal of Machine Learning Research,” 2022, 23(18): 1-68. Our Haar-type framelets can be used in image restoration as a by-product of this project. We proposed a two-level non-stationary tight framelet regularization model and developed an algorithm to solve the proposed model. The numerical experiments show that the model is eﬀective and eﬃcient in image restoration. See Part C, the paper in “Applied and Computational Harmonic Analysis”, 2021, 53: 332-348. Also, see the paper in “Pattern Recognition,” 2021, 112:107705.

11301419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11301419.value: Potential for further development of the research would be the consideration of framelets on graphs in connection to deep learning applications. One can consider the design of framelets on graphs with special properties such as permutation equivariance property for the tasks in graph and node classification.

11301419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11301419.value: In this project, we focus on the construction, characterizations, and applications of framelets on graphs. Graph representation learning has many real-world applications, from self-driving LiDAR, and 3D computer vision to drug repurposing, protein classification, and social network analysis. An adequate representation of graph data is vital to the learning performance of a statistical or machine-learning model for graph-structured data. This project proposes novel multiscale representation systems, i.e., graph framelets, for graph-structured data processing. The graph framelet systems allow the graph data representation on coarse-grained graph chains. Fast graph framelet transforms for the decomposition and reconstruction of the graph-structured data via a constructive data-driven filter bank can be built. The efficiency and effectiveness of graph framelet systems together with graph neural networks are demonstrated by numerical examples for graph classification tasks with state-of-the-art performances.

11302219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302219.value: 非散度形式的二阶线性椭圆算子是一个重要的原型问题。它出现在随机最优控制中经常存在的一个基本问题 - 椭圆 Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman方程。由于线性化技术，它也出现在完全非线性椭圆问题的研究中。在许多应用中，非散度形式的椭圆算子的系数张量为 A 是如此粗糙，甚至不连续。例如，张量为 A 由Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman方程组成的方程式基本上只是有界的。因此，需要开发和分析有效数值方法来逼近使用可能很粗糙的系数张量为 A 的非散度形式二阶线性椭圆算子。 与对散度形式的椭圆方程的大量研究相比，现有的研究并不多 适用于非散度形式的椭圆算子。这是因为当系数张量是非光滑的，则通常很难定义适当变分形式的弱解。大多数存在 非散度形式的椭圆算子的数值近似基于假设: 源项的L2 - 范数可以控制相应解的 H2 - 范数。实际上，上面的假设很强，甚至L形域中的Poisson算子也不满足。 P.I.的长期目标是从理论上和计算上发展和研究非散度形式的二阶线性椭圆算子的有效，鲁棒数值逼近，以避免上述大多数现有数值方法的缺点。我们的工作可能会为Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman带来高效，易于实施，强大的数值方法方程和其他完全非线性椭圆问题。在这个提案中，P.I。将专注于研究并开发了一种新的，新兴的数值方案 - 可杂交的不连续Galerkin（HDG）方法。 我们为非散度形式的椭圆运算符提出的HDG方法可以不使用 以上关于椭圆算子的正则性估计的假设。即使粗糙系数张量 A, 我们可以保证收敛。这些属性是我们的数值方法适用于近似具有非散度形式的椭圆算子的偏微分方程。 P.I.有兴趣研究和开发高效，易于实施的HDG方法 对于随机最优控制中出现的各种方程，鲁棒性， 它涉及非散度形式的二阶椭圆算子。

11302519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11302519.value: 关于若干强耦合非线性方程组的有效和精确的有限元方法及最优误差分析

11302519.label: Project Objectives
11302519.value: First we shall study the incompressible miscible flow in porous media. The problem is governed by a nonlinear coupled system consisting of a parabolic concentration equation and an elliptic pressure equation through the nonlinear diffusion-dispersion tensor and the concentration-dependent viscosity. We will start from simple linearized Galerkin-Galerkin and Galerkin-mixed FEMs. In the former, Galerkin FE approximations are used for both the concentration and pressure and in the latter, a Galerkin approximation is used for the concentration and a mixed approximation in the classical Raviart-Thomas (or other type) finite element space is used for the velocity/pressure. Previous error estimates for Galerkin-Galerkin are not optimal for the concentration which is more important in applications. Existing analysis for the lowest-order Galerkin-mixed method is limited to two dimensional models under certain restrictive condition on both time step and spatial mesh size. Numerical approximations based on these non-optimal error estimates may not be a best choice. In this project, we shall present optimal $L^2$-norm error estimates for both Galerkin-Galerkin FEMs and Galerkin-mixed FEMs for all computational components involved. Unconditional analysis (without conditions on time-step and mesh size) for linearized schemes will be emphasised. From the established optimal error estimates, we intend to propose efficient numerical algorithms with the best choice of finite element space for each component. Also we will study certain post-process to improve further the accuracy of numerical velocity. We believe that numerical algorithms based on such a combination of finite element spaces are more accurate and efficient. Secondly, we shall extend our analysis to other popular approximations in both time direction and spatial direction with emphasises on those methods of strong physical (energy) conservation. Since the molecular diffusion of incompressible miscible flows in some applications is small, the problem is often considered to be convection-dominant. In this case, the characteristics type scheme may allow one to take a large time step and make the algorithm more efficient for numerical simulations in a long period. Also the methods with upwinding type approximations to the concentration in the spatial direction will be investigated in this project. Optimal analysis of methods for all computational components are incomplete, particularly for those low order methods. Finally, we extend our analysis and methods to several other coupled physical models, such as time-dependent viscoelastic fluid flow, compressible miscible displacement equations in porous media and Ginzburg-Landau equations with the temporal gauge. In these applications, a higher-order approximation was used for one component in systems, which may not be efficient in practical computation. More interested are those coupled systems in which one equation is degenerate. Clearly the accuracy of classical FEMs for degenerate equations is usually (one-order) lower than for regular equations. It is unknown how the inaccuracy of numerical solution for a degenerate equation influences the accuracy for other (regular) equations in the coupled system.

11302519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302519.value: Multiphysics phenomena can be found in many areas of science and engineering and often described mathematically by coupled systems. Numerical solution for such coupled systems plays an important role in these areas. The accuracy and efficiency of numerical methods for a strongly coupled system usually depend upon the approximation to each component involved. In this project, we will present a rigorous analysis of linearized Galerkin type methods for several coupled systems and develop efficient numerical methods with the best combination of approximations. 在许多科学和工程领域， 问题常常涉及多个物理场. 数学上，人们需要研究耦合的方程组。耦合的方程的数值计算一直在这些领域中扮演着重要角色。数值方法的精度和有效性常取决于对每一单个物理场的逼近和有效的组合。 在该项研究计划中， 我们将研究若干强耦合非线性物理方程， 发展更有效的组合逼近方法和严格的理论分析。

11302519.value: in this project, we present a family of linearly implicit and high-order energy-conserving schemes for solving nonlinear wave equations. The construction of schemes is based on recently-developed scalar auxiliary variable technique with a combination of classical high-order Gauss methods and extrapolation approximation. We prove that the proposed schemes are unconditionally energy-conserved for a general nonlinear wave equation. Numerical results are given to show the energy- conserving and the effectiveness of schemes. In this project designs and analyzes a new and stable Petrov–Galerkin (PG) immersed finite element method (IFEM) for the second-order elliptic interface problems by introducing stabilization terms based on the classical PG-IFEM, which lacks the local positivity. The Petrov–Galerkin immersed finite element method uses the immersed finite element functions for the trial space and the standard finite element functions for the test space. Both the a priori and a posteriori error estimates of the method are analyzed in this paper. We prove the continuity and inf-sup condition and the a priori error estimate of the energy norm. The proposed a posteriori error estimator is proved to be both reliable and efficient, with both reliability and efficiency constants independent of the location of the interface. Extensive numerical results confirm the numerical scheme’s optimal convergence and indicate the robustness concerning the interface-mesh intersection and the coefficient contrast, although the robustness of the inf-sup constant with respect to the interface-mesh intersection has yet been theoretically proved. In this project, we study least-squares finite element methods (LSFEM) for general second- order elliptic equations with nonconforming finite element approximations. The equation may be indefinite. For the two-field potential-flux div LSFEM with Crouzeix–Raviart (CR) element approximation, we present three proofs of the discrete solvability under the condition that mesh size is small enough. One of the proof is based on the coerciveness of the original bilinear form. The other two are based on the minimal assumption of the uniqueness of the solution of the second-order elliptic equation. A counterexample shows that div least- squares functional does not have norm equivalence in the sum space of H1 and CR finite element spaces. Thus, it cannot be used as an a posteriori error estimator. Several versions of reliable and efficient error estimators are proposed for the method.

11302519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302519.value: In the future, we will extend our analysis and methods to several other coupled physical models, such as time-dependent viscoelastic fluid flow, compressible miscible displacement equations in porous media and Ginzburg-Landau equations with the temporal gauge. We will also study efficient numerical methods related to interface problems, least-squares finite element methods, and other important topics in computational methods.

11302519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302519.value: The research aims to yield new insights and advancements in numerical methods for partial differential equations. Specifically, it will focus on efficient and accurate FEMs and optimal error analysis for several nonlinear and strongly coupled systems, shedding light on its principles and techniques. The outcomes of this research will yield powerful mathematical and computational tools that can be applied to a wide range of mathematical problems with both theoretical and practical implications. A rigorous numerical analysis of these method will lay the foundations of the method itself and help us to develop new methods. All these methods can potentially apply to important problems in science and engineering. The proposed research results will provide powerful computational tools for industrial and engineering computation. This project will positively impact the computing mathematics program at City University of Hong Kong by strengthening several courses offered on computational mathematics, as well as through the support of a graduate student. Moreover, this project provides many good research topics for graduate students.

11302819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302819.value: 近年来，生长引起的变形一直是一个活跃的研究课题。一个目的是了解软生物组织中的形状形成。尽管形成的形态发生可能由通用和化学因素引起，但机械效应可能引起不稳定性，导致特定的模式。在这个项目中，我们打算开发一种壳理论，用于研究由于生长引起的机械效应导致的壳状结构的不稳定性和变形。许多生物物体可以被视为壳，例如树叶，皮肤，粘膜，心脏瓣膜和动脉等。壳的一个特征是厚度远小于平面内长度尺度和曲率半径。对于建模，如果它们被视为三维对象，则对于小的纵横比，计算是非常昂贵的。一种方法是进行尺寸减小以获得二维壳模型，然后将其用于研究机械行为。对于生长诱导的板块变形，其他研究人员提出了基于特殊假设的小应变板理论，最近我们建立了一致的有限应变板理论。然而，似乎仍然没有一致的结合了拉伸和弯曲效应壳生长理论，尽管它非常需要。在这个项目中，我们将通过一个新的程序推导出一致的有限应变壳生长理论。壳和板之间的主要区别在于前者必须考虑曲率效应，因此需要对微分几何进行一些了解。为了模拟生长，变形梯度将分解为生长部分和弹性部分。假设壳由一般的不可压缩的超弹性材料组成。我们技术的出发点是关于底面的系列扩展。虽然问题是高度非线性的约束，但关键的观察是应力，拉格朗日乘数和位移/位置扩展系数之间存在某些线性关系。然后，可以从三维控制系统建立位移系数的递归关系。结果，可以仅获得第一位移膨胀系数的三个分量的三个方程，其是2D壳方程。还将考虑壳边界条件以及相关的弱形式。我们将使用派生壳理论来研究几个问题。一个是环空中生长引起的变形的后分叉分析。线性分岔分析已在文献中完成，这里重点是振幅方程的推导，它可以更多地阐明模式的形成。另一个是关于在圆管中生长引起的轴对称变形的后分叉分析。特别是，将研究各种生长场对振幅的影响。第三个是关于壳理论及其应用的半逆解析解。还将考虑通过解决逆问题进行形状编程。希望得到的有限应变壳生长理论可以为研究软材料壳状结构中生长引起的变形提供坚实的理论框架。

11302919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11302919.value: Unstable interfacial mixing occurs in many natural phenomena and in many industrial processes. Understanding unstable interfacial mixing is extremely important for both scientific development and industrial needs. Spikes and bubbles are the most important structures at an unstable material interface. Spikes are the portions of the heavy material penetrating into the light material. Developing theories for spikes is much more difficult than developing theories for bubbles which are the portions of the light material penetrating into the heavy material. This is due to the fact that spikes are more unstable than bubbles. As one changes the values of physical quantities, such as the density ratio of the two fluids across the material interface, the behavior of bubbles only changes quantitatively. However, the changes in the dynamic behavior of spikes can be dramatic. For example, for the shock-driven interfacial instability, the growth rates of bubbles always tend to zero for systems with any density ratio, including systems with an infinite density ratio. However, for spikes, the growth rates tend to zero only for systems with a finite density ratio, and tend to an initial-condition-dependent nonzero constant for systems with an infinite density ratio. For these reasons, most of the theoretical studies have been focusing on bubbles. So far, no accurate theory is available in the literature for spikes in systems with arbitrary density ratios of fluids across the material interface and for the entire time domain from early to late times. In this proposal, we plan to undertake the challenging task of developing theories for spikes at an unstable material interface. We will develop theories for spikes valid in a general setting: for systems with arbitrary density ratios, with arbitrary incident shock strengths, and over the entire time domain from early to late times. 在許多自然現象和許多工業過程中出現不穩定的界面混合。了解這類不穩定的混合界面對於科學發展和工業需求都非常重要。混合界面上重的流體擠壓輕的流體的部分稱為尖釘。輕的流體擠壓重的流體的部分稱為氣泡。尖釘和氣泡是不穩定界面上最重要的結構。建立關於尖釘的理論比建立關於氣泡的理論要困難得多。這是因為尖釘比氣泡更不穩定。當人們改變界面兩邊流體的質量密度比時，氣泡的行為只會有定量地改變,而尖釘的行為的變化可能是劇烈的。例如，在由衝擊波驅動的不穩定界面上，對於任何密度比的系統（包括無窮大密度比的系統),氣泡的增長速率總是趨向於零。然而，尖釘的增長率僅在有限密度比的系統中趨向於零。在無限大密度比的系統中其增長率趨向於一個和初始條件相關的非零常數。由於這些原因，大多數理論研究都集中在氣泡上。到目前為止，文獻中沒有對任意流體密度比的系統以及從早期到晚期的整個時域都有效的尖釘理論。在本研究項目中，我們將開展關於在不穩定的界面上尖釘理論的研究。這是一項具有挑戰性的工作。我們將建立一個在一般情況下都有效的尖釘理論。它將包括任意的密度比，任意的衝擊波強度，以及從早期到晚期的整個時域。

11302919.label: Realisation of objectives
11302919.value: All objectives of this project have been fully achieved. The following are the details of how and to what extent each objective has been achieved: 1. The dynamics of spikes plays an important role in the evolution of a Richtmyer-Meshkov unstable interface. The only nonlinear theory for spikes at arbitrary density ratios available in the literature was the work of Goncharov published twenty years ago [Phys Rev Lett 88, 134502 (2002)]. However, the theory gives quantitatively incorrect or even qualitatively wrong predictions for the growth of spikes. This is because that approach treats the spikes and bubbles (the two nonlinear structures at the unstable fluid interface) uncoupled, and leads to the same density-ratio-independent asymptotic finger curvature for both spikes and bubbles. In reality, spikes and bubbles are strongly coupled, and the spikes are narrower than the bubbles. We analyzed the intrinsic relation between spikes and bubbles and identified a generalized symmetry among them. This allowed us to construct an approach to solve the behavior of spikes and that of bubbles simultaneously and derive a governing equation that describes the dynamics of both spikes and bubbles in two dimensions during the entire evolution process, including the pre-asymptotic regime. 2. To determine the closed-form solutions for both spikes and bubble in the Richtmyer-Meshkov instability, we applied the Layzer approach, which approximates the shape of the material interface near the finger tip by a parabola. Then we conducted the Taylor expansion on the kinematic equation and the Bernoulli equation at the material interface. Combining the resulting equations and the pre-asymptotic governing equation for the curvature of fingers (spikes and bubbles), we obtained the dynamic equations for the growth of the finger tip, and solved the analytical expressions for the growth rate and amplitude of spikes and bubbles in the entire time domain, including the pre-asymptotic regime. 3. Since the pioneering work of Richtymer, people have been searching for the analytical solutions for the growth rate and amplitude of spikes and bubbles. The solutions for the early-time dynamics of fingers and those for the asymptotically late-time dynamics are available in the literature [Physics of Fluids 9, 1106 (1997); Journal of Fluid Mechanics 786, 47-61 (2016).]. However, there were no solutions applicable for both spikes and bubbles, for arbitrary density ratios and for the entire time domain from early to late times. The achievement of Objectives 1 and 2 explained above allow us to apply the asymptotic matching technique to spikes and bubbles. The matched solution not only agrees with the behavior of spikes and that of bubbles at early and late times, but also provides theoretical predictions for the behavior of spikes and that of bubbles in the entire time domain. We incorporated the effects of the incident shock into our theoretical derivation, and obtained the analytical solutions for the growth rate and amplitude of both spikes and bubbles in systems with compressible fluids, with arbitrary density ratios and for the entire time domain from early to late times. 4. To validate our newly derived theory, we derived a numerical scheme based on the vortex sheet method. This method formulates the dynamics of the entire fluid system by the evolution of vorticity confined to the material interface between the heavy and light fluids, and we determine the evolution of the material interface by solving a boundary integral equation at the material interface. We compared the results from numerical simulations and also the data from experiments with our theoretical predictions. The theoretical predictions are in good agreement with the numerical results and experimental data. These results were published in [Physical Review Fluids 7, 093904 (2022)]. 5. We extended our theoretical method from the two-dimensional systems to the three-dimensional systems. More specifically: (a) We introduced the signed Atwood number to describe the density ratio between the two fluids and used the same functional form for the solution of spikes and that of bubbles to maintain the generalized symmetry between these two types of fingers. (b) By introducing a quadratic ordinary differential equation for the evolution of the curvature of the finger tip, we determined the dynamics of the fingers (both spikes and bubbles) in the pre-asymptotic regime in three dimensions. Based on these results, we derived the governing equations for the dynamics of spikes as well as bubbles in three dimensions during the entire evolution process, including the pre-asymptotic regime. 6. Similar to the systems in two-dimensions, we approximated the shape of the material interface in three dimensions by a paraboloid of revolution. By solving the leading-order terms in the Taylor expansion of the governing equations, we obtained the analytical solutions for the growth rate and amplitude of spikes and bubbles in three dimensions for the entire time domain. We compared the theoretical predictions from our theory with all numerical results and experimental data for Richtmyer-Meshkov spikes and bubbles in the literature, and they were in good agreement. These results were published in [Physics of Fluids 34, 072115 (2022)].

11302919.label: Major findings and research outcome
11302919.value: Richtmyer-Meshkov instability, a shock-induced interfacial instability, is an extremely important topic in fluid mechanics. Spikes and bubbles are the most important features at unstable Richtmyer-Meshkov interfaces. We have derived theoretical formulas that provide accurate predictions for both spikes and bubbles, for systems with arbitrary density ratios, and for the entire time domain from early to late times in both two and three dimensions. These formulas are what researchers in this field have been actively searching for since the pioneering work of Richtmyer 60 years ago. Therefore, we have solved a long-standing problem in the field of interfacial mixing. The good agreement between our theoretical predictions and the results from numerical simulations and experiments confirms that the dynamics of spikes and that of bubbles are strongly coupled. One has to identify the intrinsic relationship between spikes and bubbles and to solved both of them simultaneously. Conducting theoretical studies of Richtmyer-Meshkov instability in three dimensions are even more difficult than that in two dimensions. This is due to the facts that conducting experiments in three dimensions require complicated apparatuses and techniques and performing numerical simulations in three dimensions requires sophisticated algorithms, very high computing power, and very long time. Therefore, the theoretical formulas will be very helpful for predicting the behavior of fingers in a wide range of physical parameters and for providing guidelines for future experiments and numerical simulations. We have derived the such formulas in this project. How to precisely control the instability at a material interface is an important and difficult task in many industrial applications. In this project we also studied how to control the gravity-induced interfacial instability, known as Rayleigh-Taylor instability, between dielectric fluids by applying a horizontal external electric field. We have developed a nonlinear theory for such a system and shown that the nonlinear effects play a critical in explaining the dynamics of the interface. We have also examined the stability of a viscoelastic thread surrounded by another viscoelastic fluid, obtained a closed-form expression for the dispersion relation and thereby assessed the stability characteristics. An energy analysis confirmed that the elasticity always increases the growth rate. 1. Zhang Q. & Guo W.; Physical Review Fluids 7, 093904 (2022). 2. 11302919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11302919.value: This project focuses on the dynamics of the spikes and bubbles at the Richtmyer-Meshkov unstable interface initially perturbed by a single-mode sinusoidal disturbance. In industrial applications, the perturbation at the initial interface usually contains multiple modes, and these modes are random. The dynamics of the randomly perturbed interface consists of the growth of each individual mode of bubble and spike and the interactions among the bubbles and spikes. Such interactions are in the form of bubble merger which forms complicated random structures at the material interface and leads to a chaotic mixing between the two fluids at late times. The behavior of each individual mode of spikes and bubbles plays a critical role in the process of bubble merger and the evolution of the chaotic mixing layer. Therefore, the analytical formulas for the growth rate and amplitude of spikes and bubbles in a single-mode Richtmyer-Meshkov system, derived in this project, will be very helpful for conducting studies on the dynamics of bubble merger and that of chaotic mixing caused by random perturbations. Since spikes in these interfacial mixing problems share many common features with other interfacial mixing problems, our approach provides guidance to developing accurate nonlinear theories for these problems.

11302919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11302919.value: When a shock wave collides with a material interface between two fluids of different densities, the interface becomes unstable. The evolution of the unstable interface leads to interfacial mixing between the two fluids. A fundamental question is how the mixing layer grows with time, which is characterized by the penetration of heavy fluid into light fluid, known as spikes, and the penetration of light fluid into heavy fluid, known as bubbles. Since the pioneer work of Richtmyer in 1960, researchers have been actively searching for analytical formulas which can predict the growth rate and amplitude of the spikes and those of bubbles. However due to the facts that it involves the compressibility of fluids, the instability of the material interface, and the nonlinearity of the dynamics of the spikes and bubbles, it remains as an extremely difficulty task. In this project we have achieved this goal. We derived analytical formulas which are applicable for the entire evolution process from early to late times. We have further extended our theoretical analysis from systems in two dimensions to systems in three dimensions. We have shown that the predictions from our theories are in good agreements with the numerical results and experimental data.

11303119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303119.value: The prevalence of metabolic syndrome is rising globally. Data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey have demonstrated that the overall prevalence of metabolic syndrome in the United States increased from 32.9% to 34.7% in the past 10 years. The International Diabetes Federation also reported that the number of people suffering from diabetes is projected to increase to over half a billion by 2030. The major risk factors that contribute to the development of these metabolic diseases include genetic background, overnutrition, and physical inactivity. However, these factors alone cannot explain the high prevalence of metabolic syndrome observed in recent years. Cumulating epidemiological and animal studies have demonstrated that exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals contributes to the development of the metabolic diseases. Among these chemicals, bisphenol A (BPA) is considered as an “obesogen” and has been reported to be associated with the incidence of metabolic syndrome. However, the mechanisms through which BPA influences these processes, leading to metabolic syndrome, remain largely unknown. Gut microbiota produce extremely diverse metabolites and play important physiological roles in the host. Epidemiological and laboratory studies have reported that gut microbiota-dependent metabolites, such as short chain fatty acids, are closely associated with the development of metabolic syndrome through their role in energy harvesting. Therefore, gut metabolites are major components that link the gut microbiota to metabolic syndrome. In our previous study in mice, we demonstrated that daily BPA uptake caused a similar profile change in the microbial community in mice fed a high-fat diet. In addition, BPA uptake promoted the growth of Proteobacteria, a microbial marker of dysbiosis. More importantly, growth inhibition of the phylum Tenericutes, which is associated with the levels of acetate and saturated fatty acids in patients with metabolic syndrome, was found in BPA-fed mice. These data suggested that alterations in the gut microbiota and microbial metabolites may account for BPA-mediated metabolic syndrome. In this proposal, we aim to use omics analyses, i.e., metagenomics and metabolomics approaches, together with physiological analysis to explore the effects of BPA on the gut microbiota and microbial metabolites, which could contribute to BPA-mediated metabolic syndrome. The structural and functional characterization of key metabolic signatures from BPA exposure can help us identify BPA-altered metabolites affecting the host’s metabolic environment. The data obtained from this study are expected to serve as valuable tools for environmental pollutant-to-disease analyses, thus integrating our understanding of environmental risk factors into human diseases. 11303319.value: All four objectives have been achieved. The finding have been published in four articles published in international journals, each article corresponding to one objective (Objective 1 in Article 1, Objective 2 in Article 2, etc., the numerotation of the articles being that used in Part C of this report). First Objective: We were able to achieve this objective by extending the approach followed in the linear case to the case where the quadratic nonlinear term involving the transverse displacement is added to the components of the linear strain tensor field. The most difficult part has been to recast the Dirichlet boundary conditions satisfied by the displacement field in terms of the new unknowns of the intrinsic theory, which involves some delicate computations based on the theory of planar curves. Then we showed that the new intrinsic equations are in fact equivalent with the classical equations in the sense that the solution of the classical equations can be deduced from solution of the intrinsic equations, and viceversa, the solution of the intrinsic equations can be deduced from solution of the classical equations. These findings have been published in Article 1 mentioned in Part C. Second Objective: We were able to recast in terms of the nonlinear strain tensor field as one of the new unknowns the classical approach the equations of a nonlinearly elastic shallow shell modeled by the nonlinear Kirchhoff-Love theory. To this end, interesting new compatibility conditions "of Saint-Venant type" had to be established, which was not an easy task, since they are of course nonlinear. Then we showed that it is possible to compute the internal stresses in the deformed shallow shell by means of an intrinsic formulation, the main feature of which is to entirely eliminate the need of computing the displacement field. This has been done by introducing a new boundary value problem whose sole unknowns are the two-dimensional stresses, or equivalently the strains, of the middle surface of the shell and by proving that the two-dimensional stresses found in this way coincide with those found by solving the classical boundary value problem of Kirchhoff-Love. These findings have been published in Article 2 mentioned in Part C. Third Objective: We were able to show that the von Kármán equations for a nonlinearly elastic plate, which classically allow to compute the vertical component of the displacement field and the Airy function of a nonlinearly elastic plate, are equivalent to another set of equations, which we call the intrinsic von Kármán equations, which have the advantage of being defined solely in terms of the bending moments and stress resultants of the middle surface of the plate. This is of importance in applications where lower-dimensional models for thin elastic bodies are most of the time used to predict the stresses that may appear in them. Furthermore, we define the notion of weak solution to the intrinsic von Kármán equations and then justify this definition by showing that a classical solution is a weak solution that is sufficiently smooth. Finally, we prove that the intrinsic von Kármán equations possess a weak solution. These findings have been published in Article 3 mentioned in Part C. Fourth Objective: We were able to recast the Marguerre–von Kármán equations in an intrinsic form, that is, in terms of new equations whose sole unknowns are the bending moments and the stress resultants of the middle surface of the shell. The advantage of this intrinsic formulation is that it allows to compute the stresses inside the shell without having to compute first the displacement field, a well-known source of numerical instabilities. Then, we prove that these new equations are equivalent with the classical Marguerre–von Kármán equations, thus justifying calling them the intrinsic Marguerre–von Kármán equations. Finally, we were able to establsih an existence theorem for the weak formulation of the intrinsic Marguerre–von Kármán equations. These findings have been published in Article 4 mentioned in Part C.
