11303319.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303319.value: The major findings of this research project are the formulation of an intrinsic theory of nonlinearly elastic plates and shallow shells, which includes modelisation and existence theory. We were able to provide such intrinsic equations and existence theorems for all four main models of nonlinear plate and shallow shells, that is, the Kirchhoff-Love equations and the von Kármán for nonlinearly elastic plates, and the Kirchhoff-Love equations and the Marguerre-von Kármán equations for nonlinearly elastic shallow shells. The importance of these findings is that they allow to compute directly the stress resultants and the bending moments of the middle surface of such a plate or shallow shell, that is, without having to compute first the displacement field of this surface, which is a well-known source of numerical instabilities. The research outcome of this research project are four articles published in international journals: these articles are listed in Part C of this report.

11303319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303319.value: The results obtained in this project will be used in a new research project about the "data-driven nonlinear plate theory". In this new theory, the “constitutive law” of the elastic material used in classical elasticity is replaced by a set of empirical and observational data (kept in a separate set of “big data”, which can be updated whenever new observational data become available). The findings of this research project will be used to integrate the classical nonlinear plate theory into this new data-driven nonlinear plate theory, which is naturally defined in terms of the same unknowns as the intrinsic theory developed in this research project.

11303319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303319.value: When an elastic structure such as a bridge or a roof of a building is subjected to external forces such as gravity, rain or wind, it will deform in such a way that these external forces are compensated by the internal forces created by this deformation. The deformation is computed mathematically from the components of the displacement field (which are the unknowns in the classical theory of nonlinearly elastic plates and shallow shells), while the internal forces are computed mathematically from the components of the stress resultants and bending moments of the middle surface of the shell or plate (which are the unknowns in the theory of nonlinearly elastic plates and shallow shells found in this project). The significance of this research project is that it provides a way to compute the internal forces arising inside a plate or shell without the need to compute first the components of the displacement field, a well-known source of numerical instabilities (and thus errors). This is important since the internal forces, not the displacement field, are the relevant unknowns in practice (for instance for engineers).

11303519.label: Project Objectives
11303519.value: Synthesize a class of shape-persistent aromatic carboxylic linker molecules equipped with electron-rich alkyne units in the side chains. The electron-rich alkyne side chains (e.g., as effected by dimethylamino groups) are meant to react with electron-deficient alkenes (namely the [2+2] cycloaddition-retroelectrocyclization (CA-RE) reaction), in order to form nonplanar conjugated systems of strong push-pull units, and to afford intense redox activities. Framework syntheses. Crystallization with chemically hard metal ions, e.g., Zr(IV), to construct the targeted porous metal-organic frameworks. The standard and highly effectively solvothermal synthesis and diffusion techniques will be employed. Post-synthetic installation of strong push-pull units. We will diffuse electron-deficient alkene guests (e.g., TCNE, tetracyanoethene) into pores of the MOF host, and to react with the electron-rich alkyne side chains to afford strong push-pull units with intense electro-active properties. We will also synthesize substrates containing multiple electron-poor alkene units, in order to cross-link the alkyne side chains into a conjugated network system, to impart better stability and to electronically integrate the MOF linkers throughout the solid state. Doping and metalation for electronic property studies. We will diffuse electron donor molecules (e.g., tetrathiafulvalene) into the electron-deficient porous framework, in order to enhance the electronic conductivity in the solid state. Further improvement of charge carrier transport and electroactivity properties will also be achieved by entering transition metal ions, e.g., Co(III), Ni(II), to link up the –CN groups in the porous matrix. We will conduct preliminary measurements/studies with regard to porosity (e.g., pore volume/surface area measurement), supercapacitor properties (e.g., cyclic voltammetry and charge/discharge behaviors) and charge/energy storage properties for potential battery applications (e.g., by collaborating with Dr. Jingdong Luo at City University of Hong Kong).

11303519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303519.value: Bridging the gap is an umbrella term describing the nature of innovative activities, but the phrase itself tends to be vague and of little value for guidance. We intend this proposal to be a real-life illustration of our gritty efforts to close the gaps in the topical research of metal-organic framework (MOFs) materials, in order to pave the way for their application in next-generation electronic and energy materials. The technologically important gaps to be addressed include the insulating gap and the stability gap, both arising from the labile metal-ligand links in these extended structures. Such labile links form reversibly and allow the building blocks to attain highly ordered, crystalline arrays: the well-defined character, together with the structural diversity of various metal ions and organic molecules, render this class of porous solids a key frontier in materials science. The functional gaps (regarding electroactivity and stability) caused by the labile bonds, however, remain distinct, and further advances crucially depend on closer integration of the divided fields of solid state materials and organic chemistry. It is by strategically bridging such a gap between solid state chemistry and organic chemistry that we constantly strive for new exciting approaches to the development of framework materials. On the organic front, we here draw on an efficient reaction between electron-deficient alkenes and electron-rich alkynes, which produces donor-acceptor units of intense electronic interaction and electroactivity (e.g., for charge storage in supercapacitors and batteries). To integrate this electroactive function into the porous medium, we resort to a synergy of network engineering and molecular design. Namely, we will design carboxylic linker molecules equipped with electron-rich alkyne side chains, such that the carboxylate moiety will selectively bind metal ions to construct the host net, all the while with the alkyne units remaining intact and non-interfering. Electron-deficient alkene guests can then be readily entered to access the alkyne units and forge the desired donor-acceptor units. As a functional tour de force, we will simultaneously bridge the stability gap and the electronic gap--by using alkene guests with multiple reaction sites for crosslinking the alkyne pendants. On the one hand, these crosslinks are covalent (e.g., like the C-C bonds in diamond), serving to strengthen and stabilize the metal-organic links of the host; on the other, they are conjugate with multiple carbonitrile units (i.e., accept electron and allow electrons to migrate), serving to enhance electroactivity and charge transport throughout the cross-linked network. 我们拟通过此研究提高金属-有机框架(MOF)固态材料的性能，缩小与实际应用的差距，为新一代电子和能源材料打下物质基础。目前，亟需解决的重要性能差距包括导电性和稳定性。MOF材料是由金属离子与配体通过配位键形成的无限网络结构，具有多孔性、高结晶度、长程有序和结构多样化等优点，这使得MOF成为前沿研究材料。但由于配位键欠稳定，导致电活性和导电性差，而这一问题的解决主要取决于固态材料和有机化学的有效整合。 通过弥合固态化学和有机化学的差距，我们探索出合成框架材料的新方法。有机合成方面，利用缺电子烯烃和富电子炔烃反应，得到具有强电子相互作用的供体-受体的电活性单元，有望作为电荷储存材料应用于超级电容器和电池。为了将电活性功能整合到多孔材料中，我们先利用设计的含炔基侧链的羧基配体与金属离子构筑MOF，再加入烯烃与未配位的炔基合成供体-受体单元。通过这一后合成功能化策略，利用含多个反应位点的烯烃与悬挂的炔基交联可大大地提高材料的稳定性和电活性：一方面，这些交联是共价的（类似金刚石中的C-C键），有效增强和稳定金属-配体的配位键；另一方面，它们与多个氰基单元共轭（利于电子迁移），可提高电活性和电荷传输效率。

11303519.label: Realisation of objectives
11303519.value: The realization of the objectives, regarding the synthesis of linker molecules and the construction of porous metal-organic frameworks, as well as the post-synthetic installation of strong push-pull units and property studies, was highlighted by all the five papers attached. Therein, we report breakthrough in the synthesis of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) extensively equipped with crosslinkable, electroactive side arms of diverse functions, ranging from electron-deficient alkene guests (e.g., for reacting with TCNE, tetracyanoethene guests; paper 1), pendant thiol units (for porphyrin grafting; paper 2), and thioether/thiophene groups (papers 3-4). Specifically, Paper 1 illustrates the fruitful linker design invoking alkyne side arm functionalization for MOF chemistry: specifically, intensely light-absorbing push–pull functions are postsynthetically installed by reacting the electrophilic TCNE (tetracyanoethylene) guests and the electron-rich alkyne side arms on a microporous Zr–organic framework, generating black microporous crystallites with a band gap smaller than 1.0 eV. The reaction proceeds in the known [2 + 2] cycloaddition–retroelectrocyclization mechanism and extensively establishes conjugated (polyene) bridges across the linker molecules. In line with the stated objectives of this project for energy related properties, Paper 2 utilizes porphyrin guests that also serve the purpose of versatile postsynthetic functionalization. For this, a tritopic linker with three trident-like thiol-flanked carboxyl units are reacted with ZrOCl2·8H2O to afford a two-dimensional (3,6-connected) net. The wide aperture of the porous framework solid, together with its stability in both air and boiling water, facilitates the entry of bulky metalloporphyrin guests and the subsequent property studies. On the porphyrin side, four pentafluorophenyl (C6F5−) groups offer multiple fluoro groups to facilitate their replacement by the thiol groups from the host net. The inserted metalloporphyrin bridges impart to the metal–organic framework (MOF) host stable and recyclable activities for photocatalytic hydrogen production. Paper 4 targets the objective of imparting better stability and to electronically integrate the MOF linkers throughout the solid state. Specifically, a linker molecule with four pendant thiophene functions was crystallized with Zr(IV) ions to form a semiconductive porous coordination solid (1.1 × 10−5 S cm−1). Oxidative treatment with FeCl3 guests then coupled the thiophene units to form conjugated bridges as covalent crosslinks. The resulting hybrid of a metal–organic framework and conjugated polymer featured robust crystalline order that withstood long-term air exposure and broad pH (from 0 to 12) conditions. Moreover, the homocoupled thiophene units, conjugated through sulfide links (–S–) with the linker backbone, afforded higher electronic conductivity (e.g., >2.2 × 10−3 S cm−1), which is characteristic of conductive polymer prototypes of polythiophene and polyphenylene sulfide. Paper 3 is an ongoing work (under review) targeting the objectives of further donor-acceptor design (i.e., based on the 1,4-dithiin units), and the resultant energy-related applications. The strong, stable radical signal is forged from two levels of structural design. On the molecular level, we fused terephthalic acid with two 1,4-dithiin (-S-CH=CH-S-) units to afford a polycyclic (3-ring), sulfur-rich linker (TTA) with versatile reactivity—e.g., for generating stable radicals. On the solid-state level, the linker was crystallized with Eu(III) to form EuTTA as a 3D metal-organic framework (MOF) featuring stacks of TTA molecules along the Eu-carboxyl rod domain. As revealed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, the slightly loosened packing of the TTA molecules allows wiggle room for uniquely selective thermal reactions: among the repeat of three TTA molecules along the stack, one first transforms into benzodithiophene (by extruding one S atom from each of the dithiin wings) at 230°C, while the other two TTA molecules only react at higher temperatures (e.g., 300-350 °C)—to form bis(dithiole) and other sulfur-stabilized radicals, as well as covalent crosslinks thereof. As a result, EuTTA-350 achieves highest efficiencies in both photothermal conversion and solar-driven water evaporation among MOF materials, holding promise in solar steam generation. Paper 5 is an invited highlight review from the Chemical Society of Japan. The summary therein speaks to the international recognition of our works supported by this grant, and also serve to the successful execution of the research plans of this project.

11303519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303519.value: The major discoveries are illustrated below. We discovered an efficient approach to converting a coordination network into a covalent solid covalent MOF system with a highest thermal stability among similar systems (paper 1), while maintaining the crystallinity and greatly enhancing the framework rigidity and redox-active and photochemical properties, as proposed in the objective of this proposal. Anohter key aspect of discovery: the donor (4-methoxyphenyl) and acceptor (dicyanovinyl) couples of the polyene bridges also act as an efficient fluorescent quencher and can be selectively installed in a thin outer layer of the host crystallite to form a core–shell assembly for turn-on fluorescent sensing of small amine molecules in water solutions. Paper 2 pioneered an aromatic nucleophilic substitution between the mercapto (−SH) and arylfluoro (Ar–F) porphyrin groups to achieve extensive and robust cross-linking for energy related applications. We also disclose an improvement in synthetic methodology, in which BBr3 is used to simultaneously cleave the ester and benzyl thioether groups to more efficiently access thiol-equipped carboxylic acid building block. Paper 4 disclosed a novel hybrid of a metal–organic framework and conjugated polymer featured robust crystalline order that withstood long-term air exposure and broad pH (from 0 to 12) conditions. The hybrid systems also serve to bridge the two field of covalent and coordination porous solids. The crosslinked solid also exhibited proton conductivity that could be increased broadly upon H2SO4 treatment (e.g., from 5.0 × 10−7 to 1.6 × 10−3 S cm−1). Paper 3 pioneered the use of 1,4-dithiin as donor units that can be polymerized for higher stability and for generating intense radical-based EPR signals. Aside from the highest thermal stability observed of its radicals (above 300°C), the black MOF product (i.e., EuTTA-350; obtained from heating at 350 °C) remain crystalline, and water/air-stable, and features strong broad absorption in the visible and near IR region.

11303519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303519.value: In pursuing the synthesis and properties of these MOF materials, we have extensively tackled the issue of highly polarizable functionalities of extended pi-system. But even larger more electroactive functions within the MOF solids can be explored, and proposed course of action the formation of robust metal-organic frameworks featuring radicals sites tunable by metal guest; and greener approach to MOF synthesis using water or without solvents (by mechanical grinding, for example). Advances in these topical direction shall paves the way for broader application of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as a growing class of tunable opto-electronic and magneto-electronic materials.

11303619.label: Project Objectives
11303619.value: Demonstrate a Valley current device sensitive to both current direction and magnitude. Demonstrate multiplexing of Valley current.
rows: Demonstrate a Valley current device sensitive to both current direction and magnitude.

11303619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303619.value: The issue of power (heat) dissipation is a major bottleneck in the design and improvement of modern digital electronics. Several new technological directions towards low dissipation and dissipation-less computation are being explored. One such direction is to move away from charge based computing (Electronics) to using other material degrees of freedom: most famously spin (Spintronics). However, recently with the investigation into graphene and graphene-like systems opened up the possibility of utilizing another degree of freedom: the valley degree of freedom (Valleytronics). Valley is a quantum number defined in an electronic system where the energy dispersion contains energetically degenerate but non-equivalent local minima due to a certain crystal structure. Here specifically, two-dimensional honeycomb lattice systems such as graphene. Breaking spatial inversion symmetry of these systems introduces a Berry curvature and enables electrical control of the valley degree of freedom. In a dual-gated bilayer graphene device inversion symmetry can be broken in a controllable manner by an application of a perpendicular electric field via the top and bottom gates. Berry curvature acts as an out of plane pseudo-magnetic field in momentum space and has opposite sign for the K and K’ valleys of graphene. Previously, in such a device, pure valley current has been demonstrated in the insulating regime. Valley Current is a dissipationless current. These results were an initial step in a new potential field known as Valleytronics. Here, we propose a valley current-based multiplexer as a follow-up device. Unlike the case of real magnetic field, where charged particles are expected to move in circular trajectories, the effect of Berry curvature is to add a transverse element to the particle velocity known as anomalous velocity. This specific effect is yet to be experimentally observed. Therefore in a ballistic device with a single injection terminal and several collection terminals located at different angles, changing the Berry curvature (and parallel Electric field) would enable one to select which output terminal will receive the flow of current, giving one access to anomalous velocity. Manipulation of the Valley degree of freedom is still in it’s infant stages such a device would be a first step towards a Valleytronics based framework, with the ultimate goal being a demonstration of a valley transistor. 功率（熱量）耗散問題是現代數字電子設計和改進的主要瓶頸。 正在探索幾種朝向低耗散和無耗散計算的新技術方向。 一個這樣的方向是從基於電荷的計算（電子）轉向使用其他材料的自由度：最著名的是自旋（自旋電子學）。 然而，最近通過對石墨烯和類石墨烯系統的研究，它開闢了利用另一個自由度的可能性：山谷自由度（Valleytronics）。 谷是在電子系統中定義的量子數，其中能量分散包含由於某種晶體結構導致的能量退化但非等效的局部最小值。 具體地，這裡是二維蜂窩狀晶格系統，例如石墨烯。 破壞這些系統的空間反演對稱性引入了Berry曲率並且能夠實現谷自由度的電控制。 在雙柵雙層石墨烯器件中，通過經由頂部和底部柵極施加垂直電場，可以以可控的方式破壞反轉對稱性。 漿果曲率在動量空間中充當平面外的偽磁場，並且對於石墨烯的K和K'谷具有相反的符號。 以前在這種裝置中，已經在絕緣狀態下證明了純谷電流。 谷電流是無耗電流。 這些結果是一個名為Valleytronics的新潛在領域的第一步。 在這裡，我們提出基於谷電流的多路復用器作為後續器件。 與實際磁場的情況不同，其中帶電粒子預期在圓形軌跡中移動，Berry曲率的效果是向粒子速度添加橫向元素，稱為異常速度。 這種特定效果尚未通過實驗觀察到。 因此，在具有單個注入端子和多個位於不同角度的收集端子的彈道裝置中，改變漿果曲率（和平行電場）將使人們能夠選擇哪個輸出端子將接收電流，從而可以獲得異常速度 。 對山谷自由度的操縱仍處於嬰兒階段。 這樣的設備將是邁向Valleytronics框架的第一步，最終目標是演示谷晶體管。

11303919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11303919.value: 隨著計算機技術的進步，許多氣象中心已能夠進行短期至中期的數值天氣預報，而結果相當準確，包括預報熱帶氣旋（TC）的路徑。然而，我們對這些預報模式在什麼情況下可以預報TC的形成仍然不大清楚。 TC形成的可預測性很重要，因為一些TC形成可能出現在離岸很近的地方，並且知道TC是否會在相對較短的時間內形成，對發布早期預警很重要。此外，雖然我們對TC形成的背景環流以比較清楚，但所涉及的實際物理過程仍未完全理解。 過去在評估這些數值模式在預測TC形成的表現的研究，一般側重於這種表現的統計數據，只有兩項涉及其中的物理過程，更沒有人研究這些模式在不同的背景下是否具有不同的可預測性。 因此，本項目的目標如下： 1.研究數值模式在預測北太平洋西部TC成因的能力 2.研究TC形成的物理過程。

11303919.label: Realisation of objectives
11303919.value: Both objectives have been achieved. The performance of a numerical weather prediction model (the ECMWF model) in predicting TC genesis has been thoroughly examined. Based on the results, we extracted the good forecasts and used them to identify the dynamical and thermodynamic processes and their sequence in generating a TC in the model.

11303919.label: Major findings and research outcome
11303919.value: The project first did a comprehensive statistical assessment of the performance of the high-resolution European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) deterministic forecast in predicting tropical cyclone (TC) genesis over the western North Pacific (WNP) between 2007 and 2018 using The International Grand Global Ensemble (TIGGE) data. Each genesis forecast at each lead time is classified into one of these categories: well predicted, early formation, late formation, or failed prediction. Based on the synoptic patterns at the actual genesis time, the genesis of a particular TC is grouped into various flow patterns. Overall, the prediction skill of the shear-line cases is the highest. No significant improvement in the model performance is found during the 12 years, probably partly because of the low percentage of cases with the shear-line pattern in the later years. Based on the first part of the study, the large-scale dynamic and thermodynamic variables associated with TC genesis occurring in the shear-line synoptic pattern are examined to identify the physical processes likely responsible for TC genesis. Moist convection appears to be one of the first important factors. Deep convection at the initial time (Day −5) is concentrated near the inner core of the pre-genesis vortex. In the lower troposphere, the northeasterly flow to the north and southwesterly flow to the south of the pre-genesis vortex begin to strengthen at Day −4 and Day −3 respectively, and then the maximum wind centres move close to the genesis position (GP) from Day −3 to Day 0. Strong low-level radial wind and the associated absolute angular momentum (AAM) import develop on Day −4, which effectively forces a transverse circulation and spins up a surface vortex near the GP. The vertical gradients of latent heat release and the decrease in mean-sea-level pressure by Day −3 further support the import of low-level AAM and the development of the low-level vortex. At the upper levels, an anticyclone moves close to the GP, reducing the vertical wind shear at Day −2, fully establishing the secondary circulation system. The positive feedback between the environmental flow and the internal thermal forcing conditions from Day−2 to the genesis time are also important to genesis.

11303919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11303919.value: This project only examined the ability of the ECMWF model in predicting TC genesis in the shear-line pattern. Other patterns should be examined in the future. In addition, we only studied the well-predicted cases. False alarm cases should also be investigated as they can help forecasters appreciate for real-time prediction as to whether a model forecast of genesis is likely to be real.

11303919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11303919.value: Prediction of when a tropical cyclone (TC) will form has large implications on disaster preparedness. Nowadays, computer models are used to make such predictions. However, these predictions are not necessarily correct. This project, therefore, attempts to identify conditions under which the predictions can lead to the actual formation of TCs. We also identify the reasons why some of the predictions are successful. These information will be useful to the forecasters.

11304319.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11304319.value: 超越奇點：對三維軸對稱歐拉方程奇異解長期行為的研究

11304319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304319.value: Whether an initially smooth, incompressible ideal flow field can develop singular behaviors (such as a perfect storm) in finite time is one of the most fundamental questions in fluid dynamics. It is closely related to the Clay Millennium Prize Problem on Navier-Stokes equations, and has remained open for more than two and a half centuries. In a recent numerical study, a class of rotationally symmetric, incompressible ideal flows that experiences tremendous growth in local spin rate (vorticity) is proposed and carefully examined. With strong supporting evidence, the study suggests the existence of a finite-time singularity, but the nature of the flow field after the singularity time remains unclear. The purpose of this study is to investigate the large-time behavior of the potentially singular flow field by extending the previously reported computation beyond the singularity time. If successfully worked out, this study would yield important insights in not only the nature of the singularity, but also the potential connection between the singularity and the onset of turbulence. 在流體力學中，一個初始光滑、不可壓的理想流場是否能在有限時間內形成類似於完美風暴那樣的奇點一直是一個最核心和基礎的問題。這個問題和克萊數學研究所的七個千禧年問題之一 —— 關於 Navier-Stokes 方程的正則性猜想 —— 密切相關，並且在超過兩個半世紀的時間裡一直懸而未決。在最近的一個數值計算中，一類具有軸對稱性質的不可壓理想流場被發現其渦度展示出極端的高速增長特性，而隨後進行的一系列深入研究也證實這一類軸對稱流場極有可能在有限時間內形成奇點。一個隨之而來的問題是，流場在形成奇點之後會如何演化？其特性能給予研究者何種啟示？針對這些問題，本研究擬由數值角度入手，將之前的奇異解計算設法延拓到奇點形成之後。如若成功，本研究將對奇異解的特性、乃至這些特性與湍流形成之間的關係提供寶貴的一手資料。

11304419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304419.value: 關於從數學上嚴格證明流體力學方程組的高雷諾數極限這一問題的研究具有很長的歷史。即便如此，雖然對經典的Navier-Stokes方程組已經取得了許多很好的研究結果，依然存在許多具有挑戰性的問題，特別是對帶物理邊界的情形。 本項目擬研究在某些物理條件下帶邊界的電導流體當邊界行為具有一定的正則性，即在邊界分離和湍流發生之前，時的動力學行為。在這種情形下，從數學上嚴格證明高雷諾數極限問題與邊界層和多尺度分析等問題的研究密切相關。處理這個問題的一個途徑是研究由Prandtl在1904年引入的Prandtl型邊界層的性態。事實上，除了Sammartino-Caflisch在解析框架下的經典工作外，對二維帶無滑移邊界條件的不可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程組Prandtl ansatz的嚴格數學證實一直是一個活躍的研究課題，只在滿足一些結構條件下有一些研究進展。 電導流體和磁流體（MHD）方程組是描述流體運動規律的基本方程組。當雷諾數和磁場雷諾數趨於無窮但是保持Hartmann數有限時，通過利用磁場對流體的穩定性效應，當邊界上切向磁場不等於零時，我們最近成功地在Sobolev空間中嚴格證實了二維Prandtl ansatz的有效性。注意到相應的結論對不可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程組而言還是沒有證實的，當然在更具有物理意義的三維情形，許多基本的問題都還是未知的。 在Prandtl型方程的適定性和MHD方程組Prandtl ansatz有效性的嚴格證實等問題研究所取得進展的基礎上，本項目擬研究在不同的物理條件下，例如Prandtl-Hartmann regime和Prandtl-Shercliff regime情形下的高雷諾數極限問題。例如，當邊界磁場和邊界垂直時，Hartmann邊界層是Hatmann1937年在研究電磁泵時觀測到的一個典型邊界層profile。對該問題，文【11】中的形式分析表明當雷諾數、磁場雷諾數和Hartmann數滿足一些尺度條件時，可以推導出一個混合的Prandtl-Hartmann邊界層方程。如何嚴格證實這一ansatz的有效性是本項目擬研究的問題之一。

11304419.label: Realisation of objectives
11304419.value: All the three objectives have been fully addressed and the research results were written in six papers that have been published or published online. Some details of the results are given as follows. In the first paper of the list, we consider the initial boundary value problem for the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with cylindrical symmetry. The existence of boundary layers is well-known when the shear viscosity vanishes. In this paper, we derive explicit Prandtl type boundary layer equations and prove the global in time stability of the boundary layer profile together with the optimal convergence rate of the vanishing shear viscosity limit without any smallness assumption on the initial and boundary data. In the third paper of the list, we establish the well-posedness of the MHD boundary layer system in Gevrey function space without any structural assumption. Compared to the classical Prandtl equation, the loss of tangential derivative comes from both the velocity and magnetic fields that are coupled with each other. By observing a new type of cancellation mechanism in the system for overcoming the loss derivative degeneracy, we show that the MHD boundary layer system is well-posed with Gevrey index up to 3/2 in both two and three dimensional spaces. The fifth paper in the list is concerned with the vanishing viscosity limit for the incompressible MHD system without magnetic diffusion effect in the half space under the influence of a transverse magnetic field on the boundary. We prove that the solution to the incompressible MHD system is uniformly bounded in both conformal Sobolev norm and L1 norm in a fixed time interval independent of the viscosity coefficient. As a direct consequence, the inviscid limit from the viscous MHD system to the ideal MHD system is established in L1-norm. In addition, the analysis shows that the boundary layer effect is weak because of the transverse magnetic field. In the last paper of the list, we consider a Prandtl model derived from MHD in the Prandtl-Hartmann regime that has a damping term due to the effect of the Hartmann boundary layer. A global-in-time well-posedness is obtained in the Gevrey function space with the optimal index 2. The proof is based on a cancellation mechanism through some auxiliary functions from the study of the Prandtl equation and the observation on the structure of the loss of one order tangential derivatives through twice operations of the Prandtl operator. To further investigate some related research topics, in the second paper, we investigate the numerical approximation of the Boltzmann equation that has the difficulty coming from its high-dimensional, nonlocal, and nonlinear collision integral. Over the past decade, the Fourier-Galerkin spectral method introduced by Pareschi-Russo has become a popular deterministic method for solving the Boltzmann equation, manifested by its high accuracy and potential of being further accelerated by the fast Fourier transform. Despite its practical success, the stability of the method was only recently proved by Filbet-Mouhot by utilizing the ``spreading"" property of the collision operator. In this work, we provide a new proof based on a careful L2 estimate of the negative part of the solution. We also discuss the applicability of the result to various initial data, including both continuous and discontinuous functions. In fourth paper, we consider the Vlasov--Nordstrom--Fokker--Planck system in the whole space. The kinetic model is a relativistic generalisation of the classical Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck system in the gravitational case and it describes the ensemble motion of collision particles interacting by means of a self-consistent scalar gravitational field satisfying a nonlinear wave equation. We construct the global-in-time classical solutions to the corresponding Cauchy problem with small perturbation of equilibrium states. Furthermore, we obtain the polynomial rate of convergence of solutions to the Maxwell--Juttner distribution function with a constant scalar gravitational field. The proof is based on the dissipative structure analysis of the linearized system together with the nonlinear energy method. In particular, we make use of the Klein--Gordon dissipation feature induced by the coupling and also overcome difficulties due to degenerate dissipation of momentum derivatives.

11304419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304419.value: The major findings and research outcome were written in the six published papers. The justification of high Reynolds number limits for MHD was studied in several different situations by using multiple scaling analysis, in particular through the investigation of Prandtl type equations. To be more precise, we first consider the initial boundary value problem for the isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with cylindrical symmetry. The existence of boundary layers is well-known when the shear viscosity vanishes. For this problem, we derive explicit Prandtl type boundary layer equations and prove the global in time stability of the boundary layer profile together with the optimal convergence rate of the vanishing shear viscosity limit without any smallness assumption on the initial and boundary data. We also establish the well-posedness of the MHD boundary layer system in Gevrey function space without any structural assumption. Compared to the classical Prandtl equation, the loss of tangential derivative comes from both the velocity and magnetic fields that are coupled with each other. By observing a new type of cancellation mechanism in the system for overcoming the loss derivative degeneracy, we show that the MHD boundary layer system is well-posed with Gevrey index up to 3/2 in both two- and three-dimensional spaces. Then we investigate the vanishing viscosity limit for the incompressible MHD system without magnetic diffusion effect in the half space under the influence of a transverse magnetic field on the boundary. We prove that the solution to the incompressible MHD system is uniformly bounded in both conformal Sobolev norm and L1 norm in a fixed time interval independent of the viscosity coefficient. As a direct consequence, the inviscid limit from the viscous MHD system to the ideal MHD system is established in L1-norm. In addition, the analysis shows that the boundary layer effect is weak because of the transverse magnetic field. Finally, we consider a Prandtl model derived from MHD in the Prandtl-Hartmann regime that has a damping term due to the effect of the Hartmann boundary layer. A global-in-time well-posedness is obtained in the Gevrey function space with the optimal index 2. The proof is based on a cancellation mechanism through some auxiliary functions from the study of the Prandtl equation and the observation on the structure of the loss of one order tangential derivatives through twice operations of the Prandtl operator.

11304419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304419.value: Even though there has been extensive studies on the boundary layer theory for fluid dynamics and boundary effect for kinetic models, the understanding on the boundary layer effects governed by kinetic models is much less in particular for the case when electro-magnetic fields are taken into account. We hope some ideas and analytic techniques obtained in this project about the boundary layers for MHD system can be applied to the study of some kinetic models such as Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system. Furthermore, there are still other cases about the boundary layer phenomena for MHD system have not be considered in this project and the existing literatures. Therefore, it is also interesting to continue the investigation on the boundary effects in various physical regimes to reveal their similarity and difference.

11304419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304419.value: This project aims to study the dynamics of electrically conducting fluid in some physical regimes with boundary when the boundary behaviour has suitable regularity, that is, before the boundary separation or turbulence occurs. In this case, to justify the high Reynolds number limit in rigorous mathematics is related to the study on boundary layer and multi-scale analysis. One approach to study this problem is to investigate the behaviour of the Prandtl-type boundary layer introduced by Prandtl in 1904 that sets the foundation of boundary layer theory. With the recent development on the Prandtl equations and the justification on the Prandtl ansatz on the MHD system, the project focuses on the high Reynolds number limit in several physical regimes.

11304519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304519.value: Electron transfer (ET) is a fundamental chemical process that happens in nature and has many chemical, biological, environmental and industrial applications. Therefore, research on the molecular principles of the ET processes are of significant importance to a wider scientific community. Improving our understanding of the mechanism of ET processes will provide invaluable insights into many scientific aspects: for examples, developing novel compounds and reaction conditions for chemical synthesis and catalysis, and engineering better materials for sustainable energy storage and designing effective drugs to cure diseases. In this proposal, the dissociative electron transfer (DET) of disulfide linkage (S-S), an important sulfur-containing functional group to maintain the shape and perform enzymatic activities of many proteins, will be investigated. Their DET reactions can be induced by excess electrons with different chemical natures, such as, hydrated electron and carbon dioxide radical anion that are strong reducing agents commonly yielded in photo- and electro-chemical methods and pulse radiolysis. These DET processes are relevant to many redox reactions and radiation damages of proteins. Their mechanisms in solution phases are believed to involve the formation of transient radical-anion pairs and are strongly influenced by solvation. Studies of ion-hydration clusters in the gas phase also suggested that each water molecule may play specific roles in the ET processes. Interestingly, the solution- and gas-phase ET reactions may undergo different selective bond cleavages, which may be attributed to the finite-size effects in hydration clusters. We are planning to model the ET reactions of the prototypical dimethyl disulfide and its derivatives with a hydrated electron and a carbon dioxide radical anion in both gas-phase water clusters and bulk aqueous solution quantum chemically at the molecular level by means of density functional theory-based molecular dynamics methods. Progression of their thermodynamics, kinetics and mechanisms from the gas phase to bulk solution will be examined, hence, to provide fundamental insights into the solvent effects and vicinal environments on the DET reactions in aqueous media. We anticipate that this proposal will improve our understanding of ion solvation and DET processes in both the gas phase and aqueous solution and also the connection between them. 電子轉移是一種在自然界中發生的基本化學過程和有許多化學，生物，環境和工業應用。因此，研究電子轉移過程的分子原理具有對科學界重要意義。提高我們對電子轉移機制的理解過程將為許多科學方面提供寶貴的見解：例如，開發新化合物和化學合成的催化反應條件，並為可持續能源儲存和設計更好治療疾病的有效藥物。二硫鍵是一種重要的含硫官能團維持許多蛋白質的形狀和進行酶活性。二硫鍵的解離電子轉移反應可以由具有不同化學性質的過量電子誘導（例如，水合電子和二氧化碳自由基陰離子）。水合電子和二氧化碳自由基陰離子是強還原劑，通常在光電化學方法和脈衝輻射分解中產生。這些解離電子轉移過程與許多氧化還原反應和蛋白質的輻射損傷有關。它們在溶液相中的機制被認為涉及瞬態陰離子並受溶劑影響。離子水合團簇的氣相研究也表明每個水分子可能發揮特定電子轉移的作用。有趣的是，溶液和氣相電子轉移反應可能經歷不同鍵斷裂的選擇性，這可能歸因於有限大小水合作用中。我們計劃通過密度泛函理論分子動力學方法模擬原型二甲基二硫醚及其衍生物在水合電子和二氧化物自由基陰離子的電子轉移反應。我們預計此提案將改善我們了解離子溶劑化和解離電子轉移之間的聯繫。

11304519.label: Realisation of objectives
11304519.value: Dissociate electron transfer of dimethyl disulfide (DMDS) with hydrated electron were assessed by mean of density functional theory based molecular dynamics (DFT-MD) simulations. In each DFT-MD simulation, a DMDS molecule was firstly equilibrated on a cluster of hydrated electron at a constant temperature of 100 K in a simulation box to observe and monitor the time evolution of the electron transfer process (Objective 1 and Objective 3). This process was initially examined with a small cluster of six water molecules, and then the cluster size was gradually increased, aiming to examine the effects of progressively incorporation of hydration about different electron donors as approaching to aqueous solution on the detailed electron transfer process (Objective 3 and Objective 4). The solvation structure and dynamics about the DMDS center and its vicinal environment, for instance, the hydrogen bond network of water clusters and the solvent cavity accommodating the excess electron were simulated and their reactivity as influence by these detailed solvation environments was systematically examined also with varied cluster sizes (Objective 2, Objective 3, and Objective 4). All these tasks were performed by two research supporting staff and postgraduate students (PhD/MSc). Technical details of our results obtained addressing these achieved objectives are highlighted as follow. Among the DFT-MD simulations, anionic water clusters of six water molecules were found to be largely reactive toward DMDS within 5 ps but the electron transfer was inefficient in larger anionic water clusters within 10 ps simulation time. The inefficient electron transfer process was because the formation of disulfide radical anion that was poorly solvated by water molecules was hindered by the Frank Condon effect. The overall reaction enthalpy have been evaluated to be -166 kJ mol−1, which was in qualitative agreement with the experimental value estimated based on the nanocalorimetric approach performed in a mass spectrometer. The entire electron transfer process could be divided into three major stages. (i) The formation of precursor complex between DMDS and the anionic water cluster. (ii) The electron transfer step is initiated by the formation of a hydrogen bond at a sulfur atom of the disulfide bond, followed by a rapid inner reorganization of DMDS (i.e. S-S elongation) and solvent reorganization (i.e. recovering a frustrated solvent cavity where the excess electron was originally located). (iii) Further solvation reorganization was able to better solvent the resulting two-center-three-electron S-S anionic species. To better understand the cluster-size effects on the electron transfer, we performed constraint MD simulations by taking SS bond distance as the reaction coordinate to enable the reaction to also be simulated for larger anionic water clusters. Comparing among all studied systems, the reaction enthalpies were independent on the cluster size. However, the reaction free energy was significantly increased from -100 kJ mol−1 to 60 kJ mol−1 for clusters with six and fifteen water molecules, respectively. Our theoretical results had demonstrated that the reaction free energy was strongly correlated to the entropy of our studied system, which was attributed from the inner and solvent reorganization as mentioned above. Therefore, these results enabled us to conclude that the previous studies solely on the enthalpy change as typically done in gas-phase mass spectrometric experiments were likely insufficient to explain the detailed thermodynamics of electron transfer disulfides. Spin evolution along the reaction coordinates had also been monitored, which showed that the electron transfer resulted in the formation of an early-stage intermediate, featuring a mixture of C‒S σ* and S‒S σ* characters, rather than the 2-center-3-electron disulfide radical anionic bond. Further S‒S bond elongation of this unexpected intermediate state led to the spin re-distribution into S‒S σ*, reaching the more typical disulfide radical anion. Radial distribution function of the oxygen atoms relative to both sulfur atoms showed that one of the sulfhur atom was preferably solvated by water molecule rather than equally solvated. This solvated sulfur atom would then accommodate the unpaired electron, resulting in the mixture of C‒S σ* and S‒S σ* bonds as discussed above. Furthermore, we performed cumulative summation of the radial oxygen distance at 4.25 Å with respect to the mid-point of two sulfur atoms to obtain the average number of water molecules at first solvation shell of disulfides. Interestingly, the formation of intermediate resulted in the water contraction in the first solvation of disulfide bond where significant amount of water molecules were drew closer to the anionic DMDS. The water molecules then further relaxed concomitant with the spin redistribution to produce the commonly observed disulfide radical anion. These results were also in agreement with our simulated solvent reorganization. We attempted to investigate the effects of neighboring functional about the disulfide bond, including CH3SSCH2CH3, CH3SSCH2OH, CH3SSCH2CH2NH2 and CH3SSCH3CH2COOH to understand the formation of intermediate feature C‒S σ* and S‒S σ* under the peptide environment. All these subtle chemical modifications resulted in much faster electron transfer process, which were happened almost spontaneously for all cluster sizes originally planned to study in this work. Such rapid reaction was not completely unexpected though, as the chemical systems were modified with polar groups that was presumably able to facilitate electron transfer process. However, considering the intrinsically stable excess electron solvated in isolated water clusters without environmental interference, these results implied that a subtle change of chemical structure was able to alter the reactivity significantly.

11304519.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304519.value: As proposed in this research that aims to examine and improve our understanding of the dissociative electron transfer process in aqueous media using finite size hydrated clusters as model systems, the size-dependence of solvation structures and reactivity of hydration cluster ions were investigated in detail using theoretical quantum chemical calculations with supports from experimental mass spectrometric measurements. Various electron sources, including excess electron stabilized in hydration clusters and valence electrons with different spin states localized at electron-rich metal ions, were all found to be playing important reducing roles in our studies systems. The primary electron transfer process from these electron sources toward substrate molecules and/or functional groups, including the sulfide bond, nitrous oxide (isoelectronic as CO2), and water solvent molecules, were remarkably dependent on the details solvation structures of not only the anionic electron but also the cationic species generated during the electron transfer process. These cations were also found to be a major candidates participating in many subsequent secondary reactions as revealed in the course of our computation studies. These chemical concepts found had been published as four original research articles and two review articles in prestige international journals. They had also been publicized as either oral or poster presentations in several recognized international conferences. In short, while hydrated electron in small water clusters was mainly located on the cluster surface, it gradually shifted to internally solvated in clusters with more than ~50 water molecules as well as with size further approaching bulk (4). This gradual change of solvation motif was similar to clusters of hydrated electron-rich metal cations in which the valence electrons were resided largely at the surface of small cluster sizes (1,2,4-6). When the cluster size was increasing, water molecules, in a hydrogen bond network enclosing the valence electrons of ionic species, could be an electron transfer acceptor to form various species (2,5,6). Electron transfer to substrate molecules resulted in reduced, anionic species, which could be largely stabilized by water molecules on the cluster surface (1,6).

11304519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304519.value: This project aimed to improve our understanding of the detailed mechanism of electron transfer processes in aqueous media theoretically by means of quantum chemical calculations. Studying this process in bulk solution experimentally was challenging because of its ultrafast nature in a timescale of few hundred femtoseconds. Hydration clusters were ideal, well-defined models, allowing detailed gas-phase experiments and computational studies. We had identified a several crucial factors governing the process. One of the factors were the entropic effects resulting from the subtle inner and solvent reorganizations. Another one was the hydration effects on the stabilization of the electron sources, such as the hydrated electron and the electron-rich metal ions. Both effects disfavored the reaction in larger water clusters. On the other hand, the reaction was largely facilitated by the presence of neighboring polar groups. These two competitive factors would presumably influence the reactivity of these electron sources and hence alter the reaction thermodynamics. As every water molecule counts in our finite-sized models, which would provide invaluable insights into the roles of solvent molecules in the electron transfer process. More computational studies on larger cluster sizes would be beneficial for further understanding this ultrafast electron transfer process, which is experimentally challenging.

11304519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304519.value: This research has made significant strides in understanding how electrons transfer in water, a process that is crucial in many areas of science, including medicine and energy production, by means of advanced quantum chemical calculations. Through computer simulations with hydration clusters as model systems, interaction between water molecules, hydrated electrons, and reactant molecules of environmental and biological importance were examined. Our theoretical results suggested that the size of hydration clusters, the organization of water molecules, and the presence of other polar functional groups could significantly affect these interactions. The findings have been published in several prestigious international journals and presented at recognized international conferences. We plan to continue this work, using larger water clusters in our simulations, to gain a deeper understanding of this complex process. This could lead to new insights into electron transfer processes in aqueous media, which have potential applications in a wide range of scientific fields.

11304619.value: To analyze the limitations of existing design and modeling techniques for metasurfaces. We will develop techniques based on smoothed near fields and larger-period periodic models, and analyze their accuracies. We plan to study optimal design problems related to the subwavelength scatterers, and analyze their intrinsic limitations.

11304619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304619.value: A metasurface is an engineered structure with numerous tiny scatterers placed on the surface of a material. In the last a few years, many interesting optical metasurfaces have been designed and fabricated to control and manipulate light, and they exhibit new functionalities that are not available before and have many advantages over existing optical devices. The tiny scatterers of a metasurface may have different shapes, different sizes and different orientations, and they may be placed on a flat surface without any periodicity. These scatterers and the distances between them are typically smaller than the wavelength of light, but a typical metasurface is many orders of magnitude larger than the wavelength. Due to the huge difference between the size of the overall structure and the wavelength of light, rigorous analysis based on solving the Maxwell's equations is impractical. Some simple modeling techniques are currently being used by engineers to analyze and design metasurfaces, but these techniques have many limitations. In this project, we carry out a mathematical study to understand quantitatively the limitations of existing modeling techniques, develop new modeling techniques to improve the accuracy, and study some key design problems for metasurfaces including the sizes and shapes of the tiny scatterers and their layout on the surface. The completion of this project will help engineers to design better metasurfaces and realize more exciting applications. 超表面是通过在一个材料的表面放置大量的小散射体形成的。近年设计和制造的光学超表面可以用来控制其操作光波。它们相对现有的光学器件具有很多优势，有些功能更是前所未有的。超表面上的小散射体可以有不同的形状，不同的大小，不同的方向，它们放置在材料表面上时可以没有周期性。这些小散射体以及它们之间的距离比光的波长还要小，但是一个超表面的总尺寸比光的波长要大好几个数量级。由于这个尺度上的巨大差异，通过求解 Maxwell 方程组来严格分析超表面是不切实际的。现在用于分析及设计超表面的是一些近似的模拟方法。这些方法有很多局限性。在本研究计划中，我们将严格分析现有模拟方法的各种局限性，提出新的更好的模拟方法，并对超表面设计中的关键元素提出新的设计方案。本计划的成果可以用了帮助工程师设计更好的超表面，实现超表面更广泛的应用。

11304619.label: Realisation of objectives
11304619.value: The first objective is to analyze the limitations of existing design and modeling techniques for metasurfaces. The objective is fully achieved. Practical 3D nonperiodic metasurfaces are very large compared with the wavelength. Direct numerical simulation by solving the full Maxwell's equations is too demanding even for modern super-computers. It is therefore necessary to assume "local periodicity", and perform numerical simulations for a finite number of different periodic structures, and use various schemes to approximate the far-field scattering solution of the metasurface by the solutions to the periodic structures. For 2D metasurfaces that are translationally invariant in one spatial direction, direct numerical simulations that take advantage of the special geometric properties are still possible, and they can be used to understand the limitations of local periodic approximation. We observe that the error decreases very slowly as the metasurface becomes more locally periodic. For metasurfaces which are not really locally periodic, the error is of order 1. A very difficult problem is to develop efficient method for simulating metasurfaces that are not locally periodic. The second objective is to develop new techniques for modeling metasurfaces. The objective is achieved when the local periodic approximation is considered valid or when the metasurface is two-dimensional. A typical metasurfacce consists of numerous scatterers on a flat surface and these scatterers are typically cylindrical structures with 1D index profile. We have previously developed the so-called vertical mode matching method with a pseudospectral method for discretising the vertical variable (perpendicular to the flat surface). In Paper [6] of Part C, we developed a Special Galerkin Mode Matching Method which can be used to study various photonic structures. The method has much better condition number compared with other numerical mode matching method based on piecewise polynomial approximations. As a result, the method remains accurate when modeling large structures. Metasurfaces have been used in many applications. When local periodicity is used, the key is to understand resonances and diffraction anomalies for the assumed periodic structure. In paper [2] of Part C, we developed a new theory for approximating the transmission/reflection spectra near an isolated and nondegenerate resonance. Our theory is systematically derived, while the popular existing theory, the so-called temporal coupled mode theory (TCMT), is proposed without using the governing equations. It turns out that our theory and TCMT differ by a phase for the scattering matrix, but are exactly the same for the transmission/reflection spectra. In paper [3] of Part C, we derive approximate formulas for transmission and reflection zeros, namely, frequencies at which the transmission or reflection coefficient is zero. In particular, we identify precious conditions for which real transmission and reflection zeros can be realized. Notice that transmission/reflection zeros are special (and important) diffraction anomalies. In paper [4] of Part C, we developed an efficient and robust numerical method for computing different type of diffraction anomalies. A diffraction anomaly is a special condition satisfied by the solutions of a boundary value problem (BVP), i.e., the scattering of a plane wave by a structure. In principle, we can determine an anomaly by repeatedly solving the BVP as parameters, such as frequency, are varied. However, this approach is highly inefficient. We reformulate diffraction anomaly as nonlinear eigenvalue problems, and solve the nonlinear eigenvalue problem by a contour integral method. The method avoids scanning parameters and does not need initial guesses, and is efficient and robust.

11304619.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304619.value: The outcome of this research project is presented in six papers in journals of American Physical Society (APS) and Optical (formally, The Optical Society of America, or Optical Society). In paper [1] of Part C, we studied "complex modes" in open lossless optical waveguides, including optical fibres and silicon waveguides. At a given frequency, the usual eigenvalue problem considers the propagation constant beta as the eigenvalue. This eigenvalue problem is not self-adjoint, even when there is no material loss and no radiation loss (so that the field decays to zero at infinity laterally). Therefore, the eigenvalue beta can be complex, leading to the so-called complex modes. We present a systematic study on complex modes for optical fibres and silicon waveguides. In paper [2] of Part C, we derived approximate formulas for the scattering matrix, as well as transmission/reflection spectra, for frequencies near an isolated and nondegenerate resonance. Unlike the popular temporal coupled mode theory (TCMT), our theory is derived from the basic governing equations. We know exactly what approximations are involved and when the result is valid. In paper [3] of Part C, we derived approximate formulas for transmission/reflection zeros, which are the frequencies at which transmission or reflection coefficients vanish. The transmission/reflection zeros are the most important diffraction anomalies. They correspond to important physical phenomena and have practical applications. In paper [4] of Part C, we developed a robust and efficient numerical method for computing various kind of diffraction anomalies. A diffraction anomaly, such as a transmission or reflection zero, is actually the solution of a boundary value problem (BVP) satisfying a special condition. We reformulate diffraction anomalies as nonlinear eigenvalue problems and solve the nonlinear eigenvalue problem by a contour integral method. The method is more efficient than existing methods for diffraction anomalies. It is also robust due to the use of contour integral method. Unlike other methods for solving nonlinear eigenvalue problems, the contour integral method does not require initial guessed. In paper [5] of Part C, we analysed bound states in the continuum (BICs) in rotationally symmetric periodic waveguides. A finer grating and a periodic array of spheres are typical examples of rotationally symmetric periodic waveguides. A guided mode in such a waveguide has a Bloch wavenumber beta, an azimuthal index m, and a frequency omega. A regular guided mode exists in the frequency range so that waves in the surrounding medium with the same beta and m can only decay exponentially. A BIC is also a guided mode, but the waves in the surrounding medium with the same omega, beta and m, can still propagate to or from infinity. Although many numerical examples have been reported in the literature, we developed a theory and show when the BICs are robust. Here a BIC is robust, if when perturbed by an arbitrary perturbation with the required symmetry, the perturbed waveguide still has a BIC (near the original one in the unperturbed structure). The BIC is related to resonances which are useful for designing the basic scattering elements of metasurfaces. In paper [6] of Part C, we developed a spectral Galerkin mode matching method, which can be used for simulating some 2D metasurfaces and periodic structures related to 3D metasurfaces.

11304619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11304619.value: Metasurfaces for which the local periodic approximation is not valid are very challenging for numerical simulation, since the diameter of a typical metasurface may be on the order of 1000 wavelengths. Since actual metasurfaces do not seem to have local periodicity, it is important to find practical, probably approximate, simulation method and modeling approaches.

11304619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304619.value: In recent years, metasurfaces are designed and fabricated to realise many applications in optics and photonics. A typical metasurfaces involves numerous scatterers (small dielectric or metallic objects with a size from a few tens of nanometers to a few hundred nanometers) placed on a flat surface (or a flat thin film). Some metasurfaces are periodic, some are locally periodic, and some are totally non-periodic. The local periodic approximation is widely used for simulating and designing metasurfaces. We have developed numerical methods and analytic models that can be used to analyze and design metasurfaces.

11304719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304719.value: This is a chemistry proposal focusing on the design, assembly and operation of photon-responsive DNA-based systems which imitate function of signal communication. Due to the limitation of top-down approach to fabricate smaller silicon chips for conventional computers, bottom-up approach becomes a promising alternative means to construct nanoscale molecular devices which can be operated by external stimuli (input) and generate some signals (outputs). We propose to build a simple and universal DNA-based platform consisting of two photolabile molecules, namely (2,7-bis-{4-nitro-8-[3-(2-propyl)-styryl]}-9,9-bis-[1-(3,6-dioxaheptyl)]-fluorene and 1-(2-nitrophenyl)-ethyl molecules, FRET fluorophore pairs and G-rich sequences as construction elements. Two different wavelengths of light (e.g. ultraviolet at 320 nm, and near infrared-red at 800 nm) are used as the two inputs to trigger photocleavage of photolabile molecules. The resulting FRET fluorescence changes accompanied by the dissociation/association of cleavable DNA oligonucleotides and the formation/deformation of G-quadruplex are used as output of 1 or 0. By adjusting the position of photocleavable molecules and number of nucleotides between them, a series of Boolean logic gates (YES, NOT, AND, OR, NAND, NOR gates) at molecular level is created. Combinational logic gates such as INHIBIT gate can also be fabricated by interconnecting basic logic elements including OR and NOT gates. The novelty is to use lights as inputs to trigger the logic operation of DNA devices. This would create a new paradigm of inputs that allows for temporal and spatial control with high specificity and overcoming the drawback of chemical inputs including waste accumulation and delivery kinetics. As light wave can be instantaneously converted into electrical outputs and vice versa, the use of photochemical inputs can shorten the gap between silicon-based computing circuity and DNA computation. This interrelation is significant for further thriving on the interface of electronic devices and DNA-based logic gates. As compared to other logic gates, this system gives real-time response while the final readout gate can be easily reset to its original state. This potentially enables devices to be used repeatedly. Although they may not yet able to rival semiconductor-based computing devices, they still emulate the digital logic circuits and serves as alternative computational media to certain extent. A successful outcome of this proposed work could lead to a step towards employing photon-responsive DNA devices as versatile tools in DNA computing, display device, optical communication and data storage. This technique brings forward with its capability to locally and spatially control logic gates at a resolution in the nm range. 這是一個化學提案，側重於光子響應基於DNA的系統的設計，組裝和操作，模仿信號通信的功能。由於自上而下方法製造用於傳統計算機的較小矽芯片的限制，自下而上方法成為構建納米級分子裝置的有前途的替代手段，其可以通過外部刺激（輸入）操作並產生一些信號（輸出）。我們建議建立一個簡單和通用的基於DNA的平台，由兩個光不穩定的分子組成，即（(2,7-bis-{4-nitro-8-[3-(2-propyl)-styryl]}-9,9-bis-[1-(3,6-dioxaheptyl)]-fluorene} 和1-(2-nitrophenyl)-ethyl分子，FRET熒光團對和富含G的序列作為構建元素。兩種不同波長的光（例如365nm處的紫外線和800nm處的近紅外紅色）用作觸發光不穩定分子的光裂解的兩個輸入。得到的FRET熒光變化伴隨著可切割的DNA寡核苷酸的解離/締合，並且G-四鏈體的形成/變形被用作1或0的輸出。通過調節光可分離分子的位置和它們之間的核苷酸數，一系列創建分子級的布爾邏輯門（YES，NOT，AND，OR，NAND，NOR門）。諸如INHIBIT門之類的組合邏輯門也可以通過互連包括OR和NOT門的基本邏輯元件來製造。新穎性是使用燈作為輸入來觸發DNA設備的邏輯操作。這將創建一種新的輸入範例，允許具有高度特異性的時間和空間控制，並克服化學輸入的缺點，包括廢物積累和遞送動力學。由於光波可以瞬時轉換為電輸出，反之亦然，光化學輸入的使用可以縮短矽基計算電路和DNA計算之間的差距。這種相互關係對於在電子設備和基於DNA的邏輯門的界面上進一步繁榮具有重要意義。與其他邏輯門相比，該系統提供實時響應，而最終讀出門可以輕鬆地重置為其原始狀態。這可能使設備重複使用。雖然它們可能還不能與基於半導體的計算設備相媲美，但它們仍然模擬數字邏輯電路並在一定程度上充當替代計算介質。這項擬議工作的成功結果可能導致採用光子響應DNA設備作為DNA計算，顯示設備，光通信和數據存儲的多功能工具。該技術提出了在nm範圍內以分辨率對局部和空間控制邏輯門的能力。

11304719.label: Realisation of objectives
11304719.value: Design, Synthesis and Characterization of Photocleavable DNA Oligonucleotides: We designed and synthesized two new phosphoramidites, based on BNSF and BNSMB motifs, for DNA conjugation. The detailed synthetic procedures and schemes can be found in Scheme S1–S3 of our peer-reviewed publication (Part C 8, No. 2). The synthesis of BNSF- and BNSMB-phosphoramidites 12 and 20 was completed through phosphitylation. The intermediates and final products underwent thorough characterization. Two DNA oligonucleotides of different lengths, d15 (sequence: 5’-CTGAGACTTTAATAA-3’) and d19 (sequence: 5’-TTGAAATTCACCTGGTAGC-3’), were synthesized by conjugating them with cyanine 5 and 6-Carboxyfluorescein (FAM) fluorophores at the 5’ and 3’ ends, respectively. The successful synthesis of the DNA oligonucleotides (Cy5-d15-BNSF-d19-FAM and Cy5-d15-BNSMB-d19-FAM) was confirmed through various analyses, including MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, denaturing polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE), and UV-Vis absorption analysis. The stability of the photocleavable linker was demonstrated under acidic, alkaline, high salt content, and high-temperature conditions. Qualitative and Quantitative Analysis on the Photolysis Efficiency: One-photon induced photolysis of d15-BNSF-d19 and d15-BNSMB-d19 oligonucleotides was examined by irradiating them at 430 nm in 1X PBS (pH 7.2). The UV-Vis absorption and mass spectra provided strong evidence of successful fragmentations of the BNSF- or BNSMB-conjugated DNA oligonucleotides under LED light irradiation. Moreover, d15-BNSF-d19 demonstrated two-photon uncaging activity at 800 nm. Comparing the HPLC peak areas of uncaged products from Cy5-d15-BNSF-d19-FAM and Cy5-d15-BNSMB-d19-FAM, the one-photon uncaging efficiencies of BNSF- and BNSMB-conjugated DNA oligonucleotides were found to be 97 ± 1% and 90 ± 3%, respectively. Rational design, assembly and operations of DNA-based logic gate systems: In our design, the logic devices consist of two DNA oligonucleotides: P-DNA and P-DNA'. These oligonucleotides are functionalized with the fluorophore Cy3, a quencher, and two photocleavable molecules (PC and BNSMB) positioned differently. The OR gate was designed as an 18 bp duplex by hybridizing BHQ-labeled P-DNA-OR with its Cy3-labeled complementary strands (P-DNA-OR'). Photocleavable molecules, PC and BNSMB, were inserted at every 6-base position on P-DNA-OR. In the initial state of the OR gate, the fluorescence emission of Cy3 on P-DNA-OR' was quenched due to its proximity to BHQ. This quenched state represented a false output signal (0), while the fluorescent state triggered by two light inputs was considered a true output signal (1). When UV irradiation was applied, the DNA band of the designed OR gate disappeared, and a new DNA band with higher mobility corresponding to the 18-mer P-DNA-OR' was observed. Notably, the PC spacer on P-DNA-OR underwent photolysis, producing a 6-base DNA fragment containing BHQ and a 12-base DNA fragment consisting of BNSMB. These shorter DNA fragments were unstable and dissociated from the Cy3-labeled P-DNA-OR', resulting in restored fluorescence as an output signal. Conversely, when visible light was applied, a new DNA band corresponding to P-DNA-OR' with higher mobility was observed, and the fluorescence emission of Cy3 was restored. These observations were attributed to the selective photocleavage of BNSMB, generating a 6-base DNA fragment and a 12-base DNA fragment containing PC and BHQ. Furthermore, inputting both UV and visible light radiations resulted in the complete fragmentation of P-DNA-OR into three 6-base DNA fragments as both PC and BNSMB were cleaved. The Cy3-labeled P-DNA-OR' was completely free from BHQ molecules, leading to restored fluorescence emission of Cy3. The NOR gate was designed as an 18 bp duplex, consisting of P-DNA-NOR strand hybridized with its complementary strand (P-DNA-NOR'), which was functionalized with Cy3 and BHQ at the 3'- and 5'-ends, respectively. In the initial state without any input (0,0), the fluorescence emission of Cy3 was at its highest level, as Cy3 and BHQ were far apart due to the duplex formation. Upon application of either UV or visible light, a new DNA band with higher mobility corresponding to the formation of an MB structure was observed, accompanied by a significant reduction in Cy3 fluorescence emission. Photocleavage of the PC spacer or BNSMB resulted in the generation of 6-mer and 12-mer DNA fragments, which dissociated from P-DNA-NOR'. Similar results were obtained when the reaction system was irradiated with both light inputs, leading to the formation of the MB structure and dissociation of the DNA fragments Using a similar strategy, a 24-mer P-DNA-AND was designed with PC and BNSMB modifications at every 8-base position, and BHQ molecules at both ends. Its complementary strand, P-DNA-AND', was labeled with fluorophores at both ends and hybridized with P-DNA-AND to form a 24-mer duplex, creating an AND gate. In the initial state without light input, the fluorescence signal of the fluorophores was completely quenched by the BHQ molecules. Upon application of either UV or visible light, the PC spacer or BNSMB was selectively photocleaved, generating an 8-mer BHQ-labeled DNA fragment dissociated from the P-DNA-AND' strand. The resulting partially hybridized DNA complex remained stable, maintaining the quenching effect and resulting in low fluorescence intensity of the fluorophores. In contrast, when both light inputs were applied, both the PC spacer and BNSMB were completely cleaved, releasing three 8-mer DNA fragments. Meanwhile, the fluorophores on P-DNA-AND' were free from BHQ molecules, allowing for fluorescence emission. The NAND gate construction consists of components from the AND gate and NOR gate. The duplex length was maintained at 24 bp, using the same DNA sequences as the AND gate to ensure hybridization between fragments while maintaining the complementary strand with a single input. PC spacer and BNSMB molecules were functionalized every 8 bases on the P-DNA-NAND strand, while Cy3 and BHQ were attached to the 3'- and 5'-ends of its complementary strand, P-DNA-NAND', respectively. In the initial state of the NAND gate without inputs, a strong fluorescence signal was detected, indicating a true output. Upon irradiation with either UV or visible light, PC spacer or BNSMB was selectively photocleaved, generating a short 8-mer DNA fragment that could not stably hybridize with P-DNA-NAND'. However, the resulting 16-mer DNA fragment could still hybridize with the 24-mer P-DNA-NAND' to prevent the formation of the MB structure of P-DNA-NAND'. As a result, the fluorescence intensities of Cy3 detected as the output of the NAND gate for inputs (1,0) and (0,1) remained high, showing no significant difference compared to the initial state (p > 0.5). In contrast, both UV and visible light irradiations led to the formation of a new DNA band with higher mobility, accompanied by a significant reduction in Cy3 fluorescence emission. This was attributed to the simultaneous photocleavage of PC spacer and BNSMB molecules, generating three dissociated 8-mer DNA fragments from P-DNA-NAND'. This promoted the self-hybridization of P-DNA-NAND' into an MB structure, bringing Cy3 and BHQ into close proximity. Consequently, the output signal for input (1,1) became false. Consequently, no such DNA cleavage and/or no variation of fluorescence signal were observed in all control duplex upon light irradiation at two different wavelengths. In our logic gate design, we employed various approaches to design DNA building blocks that can be utilized repeatedly in different types of logic gate systems. This has resulted in a high degree of reversibility in our designs. We strongly believe that we have successfully addressed the objectives 1, 2, 3 and 4 in this funded project.

11304719.label: Major findings and research outcome
11304719.value: We successfully synthesized two 400 nm light-activated phosphoramidites based on the BNSF and BNSMB structures as photocleavable linkers for oligonucleotide conjugation. The BNSF- and BNSMB- functionalized DNAs oligonucleotides showed fast and efficient one-photon uncaging properties by cleavage of photolabile bonds of NPPOC PPGs, resulting in short pieces of DNA fragments. BNSF-functionalized DNAs have also shown two-photon sensibility at 800 nm. Together with UV-cleavable molecules, photoregulated DNA devices were further designed and constructed as duplex structures which are functionalized with fluorophores, quencher, and two photocleavable molecules including PC and BNSMB molecules. Selective cleavage of PC and BNSMB is achieved in response to UV and visible light irradiations respectively as two inputs. This results in controllable dissociation of pieces of DNA fragments and then followed by changes of fluorescence emission as signal outputs in the reaction systems. By tuning the number and position of the photocleavable molecules, fluorophores and quenchers, various DNA devices were developed in which they mimic functions of Boolean logic gates and achieve logic operations in AND, OR, NOR and NAND gates in response to two different wavelengths of light inputs. By sequence design, the oligonucleotides with antisense or aptamer sequences can be precisely programmed in DNA devices and triggered release in a selective or sequential manner by irradiation of certain wavelengths of lights. Therefore, this DNA device shows potentials as a wavelength dependent drug delivery system for selective control over the release of multiple individual therapeutic oligonucleotide-based drugs such as aptamers, microRNA mimics, antagomirs, DNAzymes, DNA decoys, and synthetic guide strands for CRISPR/Cas. We strongly believe that our work enriches the library of photocleavable phosphoramidite available for bio-conjugation and pave the way of constructing wavelength-selective, orthogonal regulated DNA-based logic devices for applications in materials science, polymer, chemistry and biology. The research findings have been published in three articles: "ACS AMI 2023, 15, 1, 1944-1957" , "ACS AMI, 2021, 13, 9329–9358", and “Bioconjugate Chem. 2024, In press. DOI: 10.1021/acs.bioconjchem.4c00087”. Additionally, a US patent titled "Methods And Compositions for Synthesis of Two-photon Cleavable Phosphoramidite Molecules for Oligonucleotide Conjugation" was filed in June 2021 (Priority No. 17/344,920) and is ready for granting. Furthermore, the PI presented the findings titled "Design, Synthesis and Applications of Photoactivatable Nucleic Acids in DNA Nanotechnology" at the 30th CANADA International Conference on Research in Chemical, Biological & Environmental Sciences held in Montreal, Canada, in July 2023.

11304719.value: This study introduces a ground-breaking method for designing self-assembled DNA devices that respond to various wavelengths of light, resulting in remarkable advancements in the field. By harnessing the sensitivity of these systems, it becomes possible to develop DNA-based nanotechnology systems that can be excited by multiple wavelengths simultaneously. This breakthrough opens up exciting possibilities for applications in diverse fields, including display devices, optical information storage, and camouflage technology. Additionally, the development of light-activated logic systems holds great potential for remote interrogation and lock-in type detection. Our group has been collaborating closely with Profs. 11304719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11304719.value: We synthesized two phosphoramidites, BNSF and BNSMB, as visible light-cleavable linkers for oligonucleotide conjugation. The BNSMB linker, in addition to a commercial UV photocleavable linker, was used to construct photoregulated DNA devices in the form of functionalized duplex structures with fluorophores and quenchers. Selective cleavage of PC and BNSMB was achieved in response to UV and visible light irradiations, serving as inputs. This resulted in controlled dissociation of DNA fragments and subsequent changes in fluorescence emission, acting as signal outputs. By varying the number and position of photocleavable molecules, fluorophores, and quenchers, we developed diverse DNA devices that functioned as Boolean logic gates, performing logic operations such as AND, OR, NOR, and NAND gates in response to two different wavelengths of light. This photoregulated DNA device holds great potential as a drug delivery system that responds to specific wavelengths, allowing for selective control over the release of multiple therapeutic oligonucleotide-based drugs. Our work not only expands the library of photocleavable phosphoramidites for bio-conjugation but also paves the way for the development of spatiotemporal-controlled, orthogonal-regulated DNA-based logic devices. These advancements have broad applications in materials science, polymers, chemistry, and biology.

11304819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11304819.value: Molecular machines refer to those specially designed molecular systems that can mimic movements of mechanical machineries in the macroscopic world. In 2016, the Nobel Prize in Chemistry was given to the three pioneers, Prof. Jean-Pierre Sauage, Prof. Sir J. Fraser Stoddart and Prof. Bernard L. Feringa, who have initiated this very important field that is essential for the development of nano-/micro-scaled devices and robots for advanced nanotechnological applications. In order to generate macroscopic actuation, molecular-level motions of a large number of molecular machines have to be aligned and coordinated. One way to achieve this is to assemble molecular machines into polymers so that their concerted motions can be harnessed to create useful work-done. Yet, up to now, there are only few attempts on this approach. Our research group has developed a series of interesting binuclear platinum(II) complexes containing two subunits that can move, under the control of acid-base conditions of the media, in a manner similar to a pivot-hinge joint. We found that these “molecular pivot-hinge” machines can be convenient assembled into polymer chains or even 3-dimensional networks. Their acid-base controlled motions may produce large-amplitude alterations to the dimensions of their resultant polymers leading to macroscopic actuations. In this project, we will explore different designs of new binuclear platinum(II) molecular pivot-hinge systems and the polymers that they can form. We will also put the polymer chains of molecular pivot-hinge machines onto the surface of planar and microparticle materials. Changes to the surface properties of those modified materials due to the motions of the molecular machines will be examined.
