11305119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305119.value: 氧化鋅（Zinc Oxide ，ZnO）作為一種寬禁帶半導體材料，由於其原材料豐富、無毒和性能穩定等特性，在光電領域受到了高度關注。尤其廣泛應用於藍光/紫外光譜範圍內的光電器件，如發光二極體，鐳射二極體和光電探測器等。然而與大多數過渡族金屬氧化物類似，ZnO半導體絕大多數是n型。這主要是由於氧化物半導體的電子結構致。在大多數金屬氧化物中，價帶（VB）來自O 2p軌道，因此其價帶位置非常低，故令淺受主的有效p型摻雜非常困難。經過多年在該領域的深入研究，研究人員已經確定了實現p型ZnO的幾個主要難點，例如，受主摻雜劑的低溶解度，受主的高電離能與及補償本征施主缺陷的有利形成。在過去的二十年中，研究者已經提出了很多可能的方法來克服這些困難。迄今為止，雖然報導中有一些成功的嘗試，但尚未建立實現低電阻率的p型ZnO的可靠方法，因此限制了ZnO材料在電子和光電子領域的發展。 在此提案中，我們利用以往我們在半導體電子能帶工程工作所積累的知識來改變ZnO的價帶，通過摻雜已確定具有高溶解度和低自動補償特性的Ib族元素作為受主，以降低受主電離能來獲得可靠和有效的p型ZnO。具體而言，我們提出通過與小摩爾分數的ZnTe（形成ZnOTe高度不匹配合金）、CdO（形成纖鋅礦相ZnCdO合金）、NiO（形成ZnNiO合金）合金化來改變ZnO的電子能帶結構。之前的研究已經證明這些合金的價帶有顯著的改變。在合成和優化這些合金之後，我們將摻雜不同濃度的Cu和Ag受主，對摻雜合金的電學、電子學和光學性質進行系統地表征，並將結果與相應合金的電子特性進行關聯。最後，在優化p型ZnO之後，我們將製備並測試ZnO基p-n結的結構。 這項工作的成功將使氧化物電子、高功率電子、透明電子、顯示器和光伏等領域產生重要變化。它對於認知氧化物半導體中的缺陷也具有根本性的重要影響。

11305119.label: Realisation of objectives
11305119.value: -Systematically evaluate the electrical and optical properties of ZnO doped with group Ib elements (Cu and Ag). This objective is fully accomplished. Specifically, we sputter deposited ZnO thin films undoped and doped with various possible acceptor dopant, including Cu, Ag and Sb. Some of the samples were also grown in an O-rich environment by introducing small amount of O (~1-5%) in the sputtering Ar gas. We found that while undoped ZnO films were slightly n-type with high resistivity (>103 ohm-cm), ZnO films doped with other acceptors were very insulating. This suggested that these dopants introduced deep acceptor states in ZnO, compensating the native donors. We then conclude that none of these acceptors are able to make ZnO p-type conducting. -Synthesis of ZnO-based alloys with modified valence band position and determine their suitability for p-type doping Three different ZnO-based alloys were synthesized in this study, namely ZnO-CdO, ZnO-NiO, and dilute ZnOTe alloys. The wurtzite (WZ) phase CdZnO alloys have been reported to have a higher valence band maximum (VBM) than that of ZnO. Pure phase WZ-ZnCdO was achieved with Cd content as high as 65% when the alloys were grown in an O-rich environment. These results were further correlated with density functional theory calculations which showed that the incorporation of O as interstitial defects stabilizes the wurtzite phase of ZnCdO. XPS measurements showed that the VB of WZ-ZnCdO was lifted up by as much as ~1 eV with ~60% CdO. Such modification of the VB in these WZ-ZnCdO is expected to favor the formation as well as the ionization of acceptors. However, as-grown nominally undoped WZ-ZnCdO alloys were n-type with high electron concentration (>e19cm-3). When grown in an O-rich environment when native acceptor defects (e.g. Cd/Zn vacancies) were energetically favorable to form, electron concentration decreased by close to 2 orders of magnitude. Recent calculations suggested that rock salt (RS) structure ZnO had a high VB and can be p-type. However, RS-ZnO is a metastable phase and cannot be synthesized under normal growth conditions. In order to stabilize RS-ZnO, we alloyed ZnO with NiO which has a RS structure. A systematic investigation on the synthesis of ZnO-NiO (Zn1-xNixO) alloy thin films in the entire composition range was carried out and we found that the Zn1-xNixO alloy thin films undergo a phase transition from wurtzite (WZ) to RS structure as the Ni content x increases to x~0.27. Drastic differences in the electronic band structure of the WZ and RS Zn1-xNixO alloys were observed. In particular, at the WZ to RS transition composition of x~0.27, the VBM of the RS phase was found to be >1 eV above that of the WZ phase, making the RS alloys energetically more favorable for the formation of native acceptor defects. Indeed, nominally undoped O-rich RS-Zn1-xNixO thin films with relatively high x (e.g., x~0.5) exhibited good p-type conductivity at room temperature. The much higher VB position of RS alloys is expected to favor their extrinsic p-type doping efficiency. Another ZnO-based alloy with higher VB is the ZnO1-xTex highly mismatched alloy (HMA) thin films in which small amount (<10%) of Te substitutes the O and formed a new VB ~1 eV above the ZnO VB. We sputter-deposited ZnO1-xTex HMAs and found a drastic increase in the absorption coefficient from e4 cm-1 is observed at 2.5 eV with x in range of 0 to 0.04, consistent with the modification of the valence band due to the band anticrossing interaction between the valence band states of the ZnO and the Te localized states. While nominally undoped ZnO showed n-type conductivity, these ZnO1-xTex HMAs were highly resistive. This is consistent with their higher VB which favored the formation of native acceptor defects. -Systematically investigate the doping of ZnO-based alloys with modified valence band structure with group Ib elements. In collaboration with a computational physics group in the National Sun Yat Sen University, Taiwan, we systematically investigated the formation energetics of various native defects and acceptor dopants in ZnO and WZ-CdZnO. We found that Ag is a relatively deep acceptor (~1 eV) in ZnO and the formation energy of substitutional Ag in Zn (AgZn) is low in an O-rich environment compared to other defects. Hence, although Ag acceptors can be readily formed in ZnO, p-type ZnO cannot be easily achieved due to the high ionization energy of the AgZn acceptors. In WZ-CdZnO (with ~38% Cd) alloys, although the calculated ionization energy of AgZn acceptor is lower (by ~0.1-0.2 eV), the formation energy of Ag interstitial donors also becomes comparable to that of AgZn acceptor when the Fermi level is close to the valence band. These results are consistent with our experimental investigation of Ag doping in WZ-CdZnO which showed a much reduced free electron concentration but no p-type conductivity. We also explored the electrical and optical properties of RS-NixZn1-xO (0.3≤x≤1.0) alloys with Li doping synthesized by magnetron sputtering under different growth conditions. Our results showed that Li doping in O-rich RS alloys (NixZn1-xO1+d) can lead to reliable p-type conductivity. In the Zn-rich NixZn1-xO1+d (0.3≤x≤0.5) region, with Li doping the p-type resistivity, ρ decreased from 397 Ω-cm (x = 0.3) to 108 Ω-cm (x = 0.5), and the hole concentration increased over an order of magnitude from 1.1e17cm-3 to 3.8e18cm-3. Electrical properties of these alloys further improved as the Ni content x increased, and this can be attributed to the higher Li doping and upward lifting of the of the valence band maximum (VBM), making the Li acceptor level shallower. Finally, electrical properties of the ZnO-rich ZnO1-xTex HMAs doped with Al, H and Sb were investigated. Electrically, we found that Al and H doping in ZnO1-xTex alloys resulted in n-type materials, with both their electron density and mobility decreased with increasing x. This can be understood as the effect of upward shift of the valence band which favors the formation of native acceptors compensating the donors. Interestingly, while Sb substituting O in ZnO is expected to be a deep acceptor, Sb doped ZnO-rich ZnO1-xTex alloys also exhibited n-type conductivity. This is attributed to the formation substitutional Sb in Zn (SbZn) which are donor species. The presence of SbZn defects were confirmed by our x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy measurements. In addition, other Sb related acceptors were also present in the materials and at elevated temperature these acceptors dominated the conductivity and the alloy became p-type. The activation energy of these acceptors was estimated to be ~300 meV.

11305119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305119.value: ZnO is a wide gap oxide with intriguing properties suitable for many optoelectronic applications. However, like most transition metal oxides, it can only exhibit n-type behavior, primarily due to its dispersive conduction band minimum (CBM) positioned at energy positions more than 4 eV below the vacuum level (Evac). Conversely, the valence band maximum (VBM) of ZnO is relatively flat and located at very low energy positions, which make it challenging for achieving efficient p-type doping. Consequently, the progress in transparent electronics utilizing ZnO is hindered by the limited availability of p-type ZnO. This study explored the approach to achieve p-type ZnO-based oxides by modifying the VBM of ZnO through alloying. While undoped wurtzite (WZ) ZnO exhibits n-type behavior, recent computation studies showed that the metastable phase of RS ZnO is a promising transparent p-type oxide. Our experimental study shows that RS-ZnO can be stabilized by alloying with RS-NiO, resulting in the formation of Zn-rich RS-NixZn1-xO alloys (x≳0.27) that exhibit p-type conductivity. At the composition of the WZ to RS phase transition around x~0.27, the VBM of the RS phase is positioned at >1 eV above that of the WZ phase, thus making the formation of native acceptor defects energetically more favorable. The higher VBM of RS-NixZn1-xO also makes acceptors shallower, and indeed, we find that the p-type conductivity of RS-NixZn1-xO alloys can be further improved with Li doping. This study demonstrated that by manipulating the band structures via alloying, the unipolar limitations associated with many TM oxides can be overcome. These findings present exciting opportunities for the advancement of transparent based devices that require oxide materials with p-type or ambipolar conductivity.

11305119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305119.value: The ultimate goal of this project was to develop highly conducting, reliable p-type ZnO-based thin films for optoelectronic device applications. We have studied effects of alloying and growth environments on properties of ZnO which were affected by defects in the material. We have demonstrated that the modification of the valence band structure as an effective route to achieve p-type conductivity in ZnO-based and in general many transition metal oxide materials. Our next step is to further optimize the doping of Li and other possible dopants in ZnNiO and ZnOTe thin films to achieve high conductivity as well as optical transparency. Furthermore, we will fabricate a ZnO-based p-n junction and study the rectification behavior as a function of alloy composition and doping. This will be a crucial step towards the practical device applications of these p-type ZnO-based alloys.

11305119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305119.value: Zinc Oxide (ZnO) is a semiconductor that has great potential for use in optoelectronic devices like LEDs, laser diodes, and photodetectors that operate in the blue and ultraviolet (UV) range. It is abundant, non-toxic, and stable, making it an attractive material for various applications. However, ZnO is primarily n-type or electron conducting, which limits its use in certain electronic devices. Researchers have been trying to achieve p-type ZnO with excess of positively charged carriers. However, this has proven to be challenging due to the low position of the valence band of ZnO. In this work, we demonstrated that the electronic band structure of ZnO can be modified by alloying with ZnTe and NiO, and these alloys can exhibit p-type conductivity. The electrical, electronic, and optical properties of these alloys were investigated and we found that with the addition of appropriate impurities, the conductivity of these alloys can be optimized for device applications. These results enhance our understanding of defects in oxide semiconductors, It also provides a new direction for achieving p-type wide bandgap oxides which can open up new opportunities in oxide electronics.

11305219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305219.value: Polymer coatings harnessing optical transparency, tunable mechanical strength, reliable damage self-repairing, broad liquid-repellency, and high bonding capability to diverse surfaces would have great technical implications from buildings and architecture to flexible electronics, soft robotics, and medical devices. Supramolecular chemistry has been widely accepted and implemented in the development of advanced materials. Particularly, silicone based supramolecular materials have been recognized as promising candidates for various emerging coating applications. However, their performance on damage healing, interfacial bonding, surface and mechanical properties cannot fulfil all the requirements without compromising other functionalities. The PI’s group recently made a couple of achievements on the chemistry synthesis and molecular engineering of polydimethylsiloxane-based materials and coatings. We demonstrated hydrogen-bond crosslinked supramolecular silicones in coating applications. Particularly, comparing to silicone polymers with high molecular weight, our results revealed that multiphase assembly of siloxane oligomers may help better engineer materials mechanics and interfacial bonding. In this project, we propose to develop a series of telechelic siloxane oligomers capable of non-covalent bonding and self-assembly to form large scale networks and thus a coating, which could harvest a combination of features that are urgently required by emerging and developed fields. With the careful design on the molecular configuration and non-covalent bonding motifs, we would synthesize a family of new siloxane oligomers for innovative coating applications. Through systematical and parametric studies, we will correlate the molecular structure and chemical composition of the synthesized siloxane oligomers with targeted properties and function of the as-prepared coating, such as liquid-repellency, mechanical strength, interfacial toughness/adhesion, and damage healing efficiency. New insights on the effect of hydrogen bonding motifs on the surface and mechanical properties could be revealed. The implementation of this project will not only advance our fundamental understanding on self-assembly and molecular engineering of siloxane oligomers, but also provide new insights into the design of multifunctional silicone materials which will benefit their potential applications in flexible electronics, soft robotics, and biomedical applications. 具有光学透明度、可调节的机械强度、可靠的自修复、液体排斥性以及对不同表面的高粘合能力的聚合物涂料，在建筑、柔性电子、软机器人和医疗设备等领域都具有很大的应用潜力。超分子化学在先进材料的开发中已被广泛接受和实施。特别是，基于有机硅的超分子材料已被认为是各种新兴涂料应用的有希望的候选者。但是它们在损伤愈合、接口粘合、表面和机械性质调控等方面的调控尚有不足。 项目负责人的团队最近在聚二甲基硅氧烷基材料和涂料的化学合成和分子工程方面取得了一系列进展。我们展示了氢键交联的超分子有机硅材料在涂层领域的应用。与具有高分子量的硅氧烷聚合物相比，我们的结果表明硅氧烷的齐聚物的多相组装可以帮助更好地调节材料力学和接口粘合。 在这个项目中，我们建议开发一系列硅氧烷低聚物，通过调节非共价键合和自组装，形成大规模网络，进而得到满足一定应用需求的先进涂层材料涂层。通过对分子结构和非共价键组装的精心设计，我们将合成一系列新的硅氧烷低聚物，用于创新的涂层应用。通过系统的参数调节，我们会将合成的硅氧烷低聚物的分子结构和化学组成与所制备的涂层的目标性质和功能相关联，进而揭示氢键合图案对表面和机械性能影响的新见解。该项目的实施不仅将提升我们对硅氧烷低聚物自组装和分子工程的基本认识，也将为多功能有机硅材料的设计提供新的见解，这将有利于探索它们在柔性电子，软机器人和生物医学中的潜在应用。

11305219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305219.value: We have synthesized siloxane oligomers with poly(dimethylsiloxane) as backbone and hydrogen bonding or ion chelating motifs as terminals. The molecular weight of the poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) backbone is controlled at 870-5000, and co-polymers could also be synthesized through condensation reactions. Different terminal motifs such as catechol (Cat) and ureidopyrimidone (UPy) have been integrated to assist assembly and coating development. The PDMS-Cat oligomers can assemble into coatings with damage-healing properties due to the dynamic crosslinking. The coating also shows high substrate binding abilities. The change of metal ions will result in different colors of the coating. By blending the PDMS-Cat oligomers with different nanoparticles, for example, fumed silica nanoparticles (SiNP) or metal organic framework (MOF) nanoparticles, coatings with specific functions could be developed. The ureidopyrimidinone (UPy) terminated siloxane oligomers were also synthesized for coating development. For example, UPy-PDMS molecules are synthesized and grafted onto gold nanorod (GND), and assemble together with UPy-PDMS-UPy oligomers for the development of nanocomposites with enhanced photothermal properties. We also demonstrated the rapid and high-efficient disinfection of surface attached bacteria. Using similar methodologies, we tether UPy-PDMS onto UiO-66 MOF nanoparticles to assist assembly onto porous substrate for catalytic applications. The hydrophobic MOF coating can preserve the porosity of the substrates and enable rapid liquid superwetting and confinement within the porous substrates. Gram-scale production of chromene, a pharmaceutical which is typically synthesized via expensive catalysis, was successfully demonstrated on the MOF coating with high yielding rates, demonstrating the great potential of the MOF coating in pharmaceutical synthesis. Eight papers have been published under this project which the PI serves as corresponding author. 11305219.value: With accumulative knowledge gained in this project, we have successfully developed a series of siloxane oligomers that could assemble into bulk films by themselves or with functional nanoparticles. We also studied the role of different non-covalent bonding motifs in the oligomer assembly as well as the function of the coating, for example, damage-healing, substrate binding, recyclability, ion or nanoparticle binding. The multifunctionality and damage-healing abilities make them excellent candidates for coating related applications. Further research focused on multifunctional polymer coatings and nanocomposite materials is ongoing. Moreover, with the financial support of the project, we are able to develop protocols on oligomer synthesis and characterization, evaluation of catalytic reactions, methodologies on chemical modification of nanoparticles, as well as the nanocomposite development. Students are trained to master skills on advanced characterization methods such as the AFM mapping, nanoindentation, and rheological tests, all of which would form a solid and fundamental basis for the PI’s lab on the material innovation as well as on the exploration of polymer-centred research projects.

11305219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305219.value: We have synthesized siloxane oligomers with poly(dimethylsiloxane) as backbone, and different terminal motifs have been integrated to assist assembly and coating development. The oligomers can assemble into coatings with damage-healing properties due to the dynamic crosslinking. The coating also shows high substrate binding abilities. By co-assembling the oligomers with different nanoparticles, nanocomposite coatings with specific functions could be developed. For example, we demonstrated the nanocomposite coatings with photothermal properties for antibacterial applications, and we also demonstrated the beneficial of hydrophobic nanocomposites in catalytic applications. With our accumulative progress in the development of siloxane oligomers and the efforts on coating-related applications, we were invited to publish a review paper on the design and application of dynamic siloxane materials at the Chemical Engineering Journal in 2021.

11305319.label: Project Objectives
11305319.value: We plan to develop first-order system least-squares variational principle based reduced basis methods (LS-RBM) for linear problems. The LS formulation will be used for both the FEM and RBM solvers. The exact-residual error is certified in parameter-dependent functionals. Double adaptivity (the RB tolerance and the underlying mesh ) algorithm is used to generate an optimal RB set. We will test the methods on Stokes equations (as an example of automatic stability), transport equations (as an example of separating continuity requirements), and other challenging problems. We plan to develop first-order system LS-RBMs for nonlinear problems. Compared to the algebraic LS RBM currently used, the variational LS-RBM is automatically stable and has a natural a posteriori error estimate. We propose a new efficient artificial neuron network method to generate matrices and vectors appeared in the nonlinear RB iterations. We will test the methods on semi-linear problems, Navier-Stokes equations, and other challenging nonlinear and non-affine problems. We plan to develop non-intrusive LS-RBMs for a wide range of problems. The method is based on a least-squares RB solver and a user's own discrete truth solver. One of the non-intrusive approach is based on the auxiliary variable recovery and the first-order system least-squares method, the other approach uses the non first-order system least-squares method to do the error estimation and reduced basis mapping. We will test them on elliptic equations, Stokes equation, transport equations, nonlinear problems like the Navier-Stokes problems, and other challenging problems.

11305319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305319.value: Many chemical, physical, and engineering problems can be modeled by PDEs. It is only possible to solve these PDEs numerically most of time. Thus, it is a central research challenge to design efficient and accurate numerical methods. Solving PDEs numerically often leads to very high-dimensional problems requiring a high computational power. These high demanding tasks pose a serious problem for multi-query or real-time scenarios. Such scenarios appear in inverse problems, optimization, design, parameter studies, and statistical analysis. The reduced basis method (RBM) is a modern model reduction method for parametric PDEs, which is very efficient for these scenarios. For many challenging problems, due to the lack of the variational structure and a rigorous error estimator, a more expensive POD approach other than the greedy algorithm has to be used. For those problems which do have a variational structure, often special cares need to paid to ensure the stability of the RB formulation. Besides these, a classic RBM uses the residual error estimator. The error is estimated in some parameter independent genetic norm and an estimation of the stability constant is also needed. This type of error estimator measures only the difference between the RB solution and an unrealistic "truth" discrete solution. The choice of the RB error tolerance is often heuristic and will cause under or over-computing. To overcome these shortcomings, we will develop an exact-residual certified reduced basis method for a wide range of problems. We use the least-squares (LS) variational principle as the brute-force general energy-type minimization principle to define the variational problem and the Galerkin projection. The natural exact residual in the least-squares formulation is used as the true-error a posteriori estimator of the RBM and the related underlying finite element method. The LS formulation is automatically stable, and can separate the continuity requirements and impose boundary conditions easily. We propose two approaches in the project: one is that the LS principle is used for both the FEM and RBM, and the other is a non-intrusive approach with the LS method only used for the RBM while the discrete truth solver being user-defined. Furthermore, for the LS-RBM for nonlinear equations, we propose a new artificial neuron network method to generate matrices and vectors appeared in the nonlinear RB iterations. We will test the methods developed in the project on the second order elliptic equations, Stokes equation, transport problems, time-dependent problems, and nonlinear problems including Navier-Stokes problems. 許多化學，物理和工程問題都由偏微分方程来模拟。大部分時候, 這些方程都只能以數值的方法求解。因此，設計高效和精確數值方法的是一個核心的研究挑戰。以數值方式求解PDE經常導致需要計算的非常高維度的問題, 這需要大量的計算能力。這些高要求的任務對於多查詢或實時場景來說是一個嚴重的問題。這些情景出現在反問題，優化，設計，參數研究和統計分析中。簡化基法（RBM）是用於參數偏微分方程的現代模型簡化方法，對於這些場景非常有效。 經典RB方法的成功基於以下方面: 基於RB的Galerkin投影，貪婪程序，離線在線計算策略以及RB錯誤估計和基選擇的嚴格後驗誤差估計。 對於許多具有挑戰性的問題，由於沒有變分結構和嚴格的誤差估計子, 更昂貴的POD方法經常被使用。對於那些具有變分結構的問題，通常需要確保RB方法的穩定性。除此之外，經典RBM使用殘差估計子。在一些與參數無關的範數中估計誤差，並且還需要估計穩定常數。這種類型的誤差估計子估計RB解和不切實際的“真實”離散解之間的差異。 RB容許誤差的選擇經常是基於經驗的, 容易導致過度或者不夠計算。 為了克服這些缺點，在這個項目中，我們計劃針對各種問題開發一種精確殘留的方法。我們使用最小二乘（LS）變分原理作為一般能量型最小化原理來定義變分問題和Galerkin投影。最小二乘方法中的自然精確殘差被用作RBM的後驗估計和相關的有限元方法。 LS配方自動穩定，能分離連續要求和加載邊界條件. 我們在項目中提出了兩種方法：一種是原理用於FEM和RBM，另一種是LS方法的非侵入式方法，LS方法僅用於RBM，而離散真值求解器是用戶定義的。此外，對於非線性方程的LS-RBM，我們提出了一種新的人工神經網絡方法來生成非線性RB迭代中出現的矩陣和向量。 我們會對Stokes方程，運輸問題，時間依賴性問題和非線性問題.Navier-Stokes問題來測試我們的方法。 我們期望我們的研究能夠對很多困難的問題提出更好的計算方法。我們所提出的研究結果將為許多數學興趣和實際應用問題提供強大的計算工具。

11305319.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305319.value: The a posteriori error estimate and greedy algorithms are central in the reduced basis method (RBM). With the parametric symmetric coercive elliptic boundary value problem as an example of the primal-dual variational problems satisfying the strong duality, we develop primal-dual RBMs (PD-RBM) with robust true error certifications and discuss three versions of greedy algorithms to balance the finite element error, the exact RB error, and the adaptive mesh refinements. For a class of convex minimization variational problems that have corresponding dual problems satisfying the strong duality, the primal-dual gap between the primal and dual functionals can be used as an a posteriori error estimator. This primal-dual gap error estimator is robust with respect to the parameters of the problem, and it can be used for both mesh refinements of finite element methods and the true RB error certification. With the help of integration by parts formula, the primal-dual variational theory is developed for the symmetric coercive elliptic boundary value problems with nonhomogeneous boundary conditions by both the conjugate function and Lagrangian theories. A generalized Prager-Synge identity, which is the primal-dual gap error representation for this specific problem, is developed. RBMs for both the primal and dual problems with robust error estimates are developed. The dual variational problem can often be viewed as a constraint optimization problem. In the paper, different from the standard saddle-point finite element approximation, the dual RBM is treated as a Galerkin projection by constructing RB spaces satisfying the homogeneous constraint. Adaptive balanced greedy algorithms with primal-dual finite element and RB error estimators are discussed.

11305419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305419.value: Photoactive semiconductors are promising candidates for harnessing solar energy. A number of potentially impactful photoactive materials are currently suffering from photo-dissolution, thus hindering their practical applications. In addition to the design of novel photoactive materials, this project aims to develop innovative materials engineering methods to suppress the intrinsic instability of such materials, especially through the surface/interface engineering of the photocatalysts and its reactive media. Attaining fundamental knowledge on charge interaction at electrolyte-semiconductor interfaces will be crucial in developing the next generation of highly efficient photochemical systems in solar fuels applications. The ultimate goal in converting and storing solar energy is achievable through careful design of photoactive semiconductor with promising robustness and efficiency. Given the strategic solar-geographical position of Hong Kong, utilisation of sunlight is a promising option in renewable energy resources to tackle the issue of energy insecurity. 具有光催化活性的半導體材料有希望實現太陽能的高效轉化與利用。目前，具有潛在研究與開發價值的光活性材料普遍遭受光腐蝕分解失活的難題，從而阻礙它們的廣泛應用。在設計新型光催化活性材料之餘，本項目旨在利用創新性的材料工程學方法來抑制這些材料的內在不穩定性，尤其是通過對光催化劑的表面/界面及其反應介質的有效調控。此外，基於電荷在電解質 -半導體界面相互作用的基礎研究，將對研發下一代高效光化學轉化系統以生產化學燃料有著至關重要的作用。本項目的最終目標是通過謹慎、科學的方法，設計具有高效率的光催化活性材料，實現以可再生化學燃料的形式轉化和儲存太陽能。鑑於太陽能在香港的戰略地位，利用太陽光是可再生能源資源化的主要選擇，以解決能源安全問題。

11305419.label: Realisation of objectives
11305419.value: In this Completion Report, the PI and his research team have investigated comprehensively the elements covered in all four project objectives with measurable success. The details are as follows: 1. Objective 1: To understand the relationships between efficiency of inter-particulate charge transfer and photoinduced self-oxidation/reduction in oxide photocatalyst. We have reported carrier dynamics within a faceted semiconductor to govern the photoactivity of photocatalytic H2 generation and photoelectrochemical photocurrent measurement. In this study, rhombic dodecahedral Cu2O (RD-Cu2O)(i.e. dominant {110} exposed facets) is shown to have better performances when compared to cubic Cu2O (CB-Cu2O) with all {100} exposed facets, attributed to the higher carrier mobility determined from the contactless TRMC measurement and better charge separation efficiency demonstrated by PL and SPV measurements. Although the surface atomic arrangement and the surface electronic band structure are commonly identified as the main factors that boost the photocatalytic performance of faceted Cu2O, the inevitable evolution of defects during the synthesis and the presence of secondary facets are shown to affect the carrier dynamics of the samples. The higher defect concentrations formed within CB-Cu2O increases its conductivity and carrier density. However, our results show that the higher defect density presents a detrimental effect on carrier mobility and separation, thus hinders the photoactivity of CB-Cu2O. On the other hand, the superior carrier mobility, lifetime and diffusion length of the RD-Cu2O sample are the dominant factors that enhance the performance in PC and PEC systems. Moreover, despite the stronger SPV signals of CB-Cu2O, the homogeneous depletion layer induces an opposite electric field on CB-Cu2O and increases the charge recombination rate, while RD-Cu2O with the presence of secondary facets allows efficiency charge separation towards different directions of the surfaces. In this work, all the possible facet-dependent properties involved in crystal facet engineering were carefully interpreted. Apart from surface absorption abilities and surface energies, these findings demonstrate that surface defect density (formed during the fabrication of faceted Cu2O) and exposure of more than one facets are important factors that influence the photoactivity and should not be neglected. This work is published in Materials Advances 2022, 3 (4), 2200-2212. This paper has been selected to receive the inaugural Materials Advances Paper Prize. 2. Objective 2: To overcome the dissolution of oxide photocatalysts upon bandgap-excitation through surface chemical engineering (including facet engineering and polymeric functionalisation). We have investigated and concluded that a higher tungsten (W) concentration used to fabricate a plate-like bismuth tungstate (Bi2WO6) as an effective photoanode for PEC water splitting. Studies were carried out to investigate the differences of PEC performance of more W in Bi2WO6 in terms of electrical conductivity, charge mobility, charge recombination rate, interfacial resistance, and the charge carrier concentration. Morphology engineering to achieve smaller particle size, and higher exposure of {010} crystal facet lead to an improved PEC performance, which owes to the enhanced charge transportation (as the charge migration pathway is reduced) and higher surface electron density to participate in the water oxidation reaction. It also confirmed that the “self-doping” of W in Bi2WO6 promotes a higher charge carrier concentration and shorter W-O bond length, prevent the dissolution of photocatalysts. Based on this paper, an insight on the changes in physicochemical properties with respect to the increase in W concentration during fabrication would help toward the photoanode designs for water oxidation in the future. This work is published in SMALL 2021, 17 (35), 2102023. This paper has been selected as the journal Front Cover. 3. Objective 3: To achieve nearly complete utilisation of photogenerated charges from the photocatalytic composites that exhibit low charge recombination losses. We have attempted to fundamentally understand the multiple roles of substitutional phosphorus incorporation in mediating charge transport of the nanoporous BiVO4 samples to utilise the charge in near 100% consumption. The synergistic effects have allowed the phosphorus-doped BiVO4 to exhibit record high photon-to-current conversion efficiencies with absorbed photon-to-current conversion efficiency (APCE) of 87% and ηsep of 80% at 0.6 VRHE. NiFeOx water oxidation catalyst was coated to facilitate charge injection at the phosphorus-doped BiVO4 surface, demonstrating a high applied bias photon-to-current efficiency (ABPE) of 2.21%. This study extends the understanding of the doping effect of metal oxide photoelectrodes beyond the increased carrier density to now include charge transport dynamics, particularly with mediating trap states and polaron hopping. This work is published in Nature Communications 2022, 13, 6231. 4. Objective 4: To design highly stable photocatalytic inorganic-organic hybrid composites for hydrogen generation. We have investigated inorganic-organic hybrid composite of Cu-based metal organic frameworks (Cu-MOF), namely Cu-MOF-74, with good gas adsorption ability and was topotactically formed on Cu2O nanowires. The effect of the amount of H2dhtp (MOF precursor) on the heterostructures formed were systematically studied. The Cu2O@Cu-MOF-74 composite is an efficient photocatalyst thin film for photocatalytic reaction using water vapor as the electron donor. The resulting Cu2O@Cu-MOF-74 heterostructure demonstrated an enhanced activity and improved stability compared to the bare Cu2O thin film. The charge-transfer efficiency of the photogenerated charge carriers in Cu2O was increased by the presence of the Cu-MOF-74 shell. This study provides a prospect to develop efficient photocatalytic systems for the production of solar fuels. This paper is published in ChemPhysMater as an invited paper by the journal (ChemPhysMater 2023, 2 (2), 126-133).

11305419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305419.value: Throughout this project, we have published a total of 32 peer-reviewed papers (among them, six of them were reported in the Mid-term report in 2021). All these papers were focused on the photocharge investigation of non-TiO2 based photocatalysts. Typically, cuprous oxide (simple oxide) and bismuth-based ternary oxide such as bismuth vanadate and bismuth tungstate were investigated thoroughly. (a) Noticeable outcome of these 32 peer-reviewed research output are: - Six papers were recognised as Highly Cited Papers (by Clarivate); - Five papers were selected as the journal covers, in which the journal are all top tier journals in the field (including SMALL and ACS Energy Letters); - One paper award (by Royal Society of Chemistry, UK) (b) Additionally, the PI and his research team have presented the findings in international conference. After the mid-term report in 2021 (two conference speech), PI-Ng has delivered another six talks in Hong Kong and other international platforms: - PI-Ng was invited to deliver an Award Presentation at the Annual Meeting of the Japanese Photochemistry Association (JPA) held in Niigata Japan in September of 2021. PI-Ng gave an Award Talk on the topic “Charge Transportation in Photoactive Semiconductors for Solar Fuels Generation”. - PI-Ng invited to deliver a Keynote speech in Energy Future Conference (EF4) in October 2021, in Sydney Australia, with the title “Solar Fules from Photocatalysis”. - Another six talks were in Hong Kong (by HKIE), USA (by Electrochemical Society Meetings) and Australia (by International Society of Electrochemistry). All talks are about solar fuels from photoactive semiconductor. (c) The findings in photocatalysis studied in this project also appeared in Hong Kong Media (RTHK) and a number of international outlets (e.g. Eurekalert). - https://podcast.rthk.hk/podcast/item.php?pid=42&eid=231574&lang=en-US (香港家書) - https://phys.org/news/2023-01-method-efficient-hydrogen-production-voltage.html (New method to introduce efficient water splitting for hydrogen production at low voltage) Overall, this GRF project has enabled the promotion of photocatalytic technology and helped in expanding fundamental and applied science boundary.

11305419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305419.value: The successful execution of this research project has served as the solid foundation for more rapid development of photocatalytic science and technology. It has enabled the PI-Ng and CityU to attract attentions from governmental department (including EMSD and EPD) and industrial sectors on the potential usefulness of photocatalysis. Sparkled by this project, PI-Ng is now actively involved in the development of solar fuels project in Hong Kong (both fundamental research and applied-driven application) via multiple funded platforms.

11305419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305419.value: Photoactive semiconductors are promising candidates for harnessing solar energy. A number of potentially impactful photoactive materials are currently suffering from photo-dissolution, thus hindering their practical applications. This research project has enabled the design of novel photoactive materials through innovative materials engineering methods to suppress the intrinsic instability of such materials, especially through the surface/interface engineering of the photocatalysts and its reactive media. Fundamental knowledge attained on charge interaction at electrolyte-semiconductor interfaces has helped to expand the existing boundaries of understanding and is crucial for further development of solar fuels in Hong Kong. The project has brought the community to approaching the ultimate goal in converting and storing solar energy with promising robustness and efficiency. Given the strategic solar-geographical position of Hong Kong, utilisation of sunlight is a promising option in renewable energy resources to assist us marching towards carbon neutrality.

11305919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11305919.value: The rapid development of two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials has triggered promising biomedical applications such as nano-sensing, nano-imaging, and drug delivery. However, the clinical realization of these emerging applications is challenged by the cytotoxicity of nanomaterials. Experimental studies have revealed the complexity of nanotoxicity, which depends on properties of nanomaterials (e.g., size, dosage, surface characteristic, etc.) and surrounding conditions, such as temperature. To thoroughly understand the cytotoxicity of 2D nanomaterials, molecular and thermodynamic insights into the bio-nano interaction between biological systems and 2D nanomaterials are necessary. However, this information is difficult to access using experimental techniques. In the proposed work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, which is taken as a computational microscope, will be used to investigate the coupling of 2D nanomaterials and lipid membranes. Lipid membranes are simplified models of the plasma cell membranes, which protect a biological cell from its environment and play key roles in a huge number of cellular activities. The sharp edges of 2D nanomaterials can penetrate cell membranes, which could lead to leakage and ultimate cell death. Nanosheets may also affect cell membrane functions and alter crucial properties in a way that reduces cell viability. The goal of the proposed work is to gain molecular insights into the physical interaction between nanosheets and lipid membranes, potential side effects of nanosheets on lipid membranes, and thermodynamic driving forces that dominate behaviors of nanosheets and lipids. First, we will perform simulations to explore the atomistic interaction morphology of lipid membranes with nanosheets of varying sizes, orientations, and hydrophobicity. Then, we will evaluate the modeled cytotoxicity of different interaction states by analyzing the effects of nanosheets on membrane properties including: membrane integrity, lipid diffusivity, membrane rigidity, and lipid flip-flop rate. Next, the evolution of interaction morphologies will be decomposed, molecular motions and dynamic pathways will be identified. Furthermore, thermodynamics that dominate different molecular motions and dynamic pathways will be investigated. The proposed studies will reveal a variety of atomistic interaction morphologies, characteristics associated with them are expected to provide a necessary connection to experimentally visualized morphologies. The effects of different interaction states on membrane properties could facilitate molecular-level understanding of the cytotoxic effects of nanomaterials. The dynamic and thermodynamic results could uncover molecular mechanisms for coupling behaviors of nanosheets and lipid membranes, and provide biological implications for the mitigation of nanotoxicity. 二維（2D）納米材料的快速發展已經引發了有希望的生物醫學應用，例如納米傳感，納米成像和藥物遞送。然而，這些新興應用的臨床實現受到納米材料的細胞毒性的挑戰。實驗研究揭示了納米毒性的複雜性，其取決於納米材料的性質（例如，尺寸，劑量，表面特徵等）和周圍條件，例如溫度。為了徹底了解2D納米材料的細胞毒性，必須對生物系統和2D納米材料之間的生物納米相互作用進行分子的和熱力學的分析。但是使用實驗技術卻很難獲得這些信息。 在擬議的工作中，分子動力學（MD）模擬，作為計算顯微鏡，將用於研究2D納米材料和脂質膜的耦合。脂質膜是漿細胞膜的簡化模型，其保護生物細胞免受其環境影響並在大量細胞活動中起關鍵作用。 2D納米材料的鋒利邊緣可以穿透細胞膜，這可能導致滲漏和最終細胞死亡。納米片還可以以降低細胞活力的方式影響細胞膜功能並改變關鍵性質。 擬議工作的目標是獲得納米片和脂質膜之間的物理相互作用的分子水平的見解，以及主導納米片和脂質相互作用的熱力學驅動力。首先，我們將進行模擬，以探索具有不同大小，方向和疏水性的納米片的脂質膜的原子相互作用形態。接下來，將分解相互作用形態的演變，識別分子運動和動態路徑。此外，將研究主導不同分子運動和動態通路的熱力學。 擬議的研究將揭示各種原子相互作用形態，與它們相關的特徵有望提供與實驗可視化形態的必要聯繫。不同相互作用狀態對膜性質的影響可以促進分子水平理解納米材料的細胞毒性作用。動態和熱力學結果可以揭示納米片和脂質膜偶聯行為的分子機制，並為減輕納米毒性提供生物學意義。

11305919.label: Realisation of objectives
11305919.value: We have studied the lipid and nanosheet interactions systematically. Specifically, we have identified 5 interaction states between liposome and nano sheets, which agreed with experimental observations. We quantified the free energy for nanosheet rotation inside the lipid bilayer and found there were two states and the corresponding energy barrier between them. Furthermore, we quantified the flip-flop rate of lipids under the present of graphene and graphene oxide nanosheets. Interestingly, we found the flip-flop rate were significantly increased with graphene oxide while decreased with graphene. There is a water fore form when graphene oxide inserted into the lipid bilayer. We observed lipid flipped from one layer to another. With respect to nanosheet insertion, the sharp corners is much easier to insert into the membrane than the nanosheet edge. Moreover, we found black phosphorus is more biocompatible to lipid membrane and protein.

11305919.label: Major findings and research outcome
11305919.value: The free energy between the insertion and sandwich structure for nanosheet was quantified and found both are local minimal. When the nanosheet is small, insertion is preferred. When the nanosheet is large, the energy barrier from sandwich structure to insertion is higher to overcome. The flip-flop rate with the perpendicular insertion of graphene oxide would increase, while other configurations will decrease. The rate will also decrease with graphene. A water pore forms when the graphene oxide inserts into the membrane, thus lipid can flip from one layer to another within the simulation time scale. Black phosphorus has higher biocompatibility than graphene, as the membrane properties (diffusion constant, bending rigidity) do not change as much as that induced by graphene. Lipid could not be extracted by black phosphorus either. Nanosheet can insert into the membrane through either the sharp corner or edges. The sharp corner has a lower energy barrier. Five manuscripts and a few conferences have been reported these findings.

11305919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11305919.value: During this project, we investigate the interaction between lipid membrane and various nano sheet. As the binding affinity between lipids and nanosheet differ by nanosheet type and curvature, thus we plan to design particular nano-device for directional drug delivery (DNA, RNA and small drug molecular). We have obtained interesting results and delivered a few talks at conferences. We need more time to investigate the drug release process and device insertion process. Another potential direction is the black phosphorus as we have found the biocompatibility of it is much better than that of graphene and hexagonal BN. It is worth to investigate the replacement of black phosphorus to graphene.

11305919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11305919.value: In the past 3-4 years, our group investigated the interaction between lipid membrane and various nanosheet. The membrane properties will be siginificantly altered by graphene and hexagonal BN insertion. The insertion of nanosheet to membrane is easier for the sharp corner of the nanosheet than the edges. The insertion of graphene oxide will increase the flip-flop rate of lipids and decrease by graphene. A water pore will form in this system, thus there will be leakage of materials through the membrane. We found the black phosphorus has a higher biocompatibility than other nanosheets (graphene, hexagonal BN).

11306019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306019.value: Light carries both spin and orbital angular momentum (OAM). Spin is associated with light’s polarization; OAM is associated with light’s spatial field distribution. Their interplay and mutual conversions, i.e. spin-orbit interactions (SOIs), can give rise to numerous novel phenomena and applications such as photonic spin Hall effect, unidirectional transport of signals, and optical micromanipulation of particles. Due to their intrinsic vector nature, SOIs strongly depend on the structural properties of photonic systems. One fundamentally important property is topology, i.e., geometric properties that are preserved under continuous deformations. Therefore, understanding how topology affects SOIs is crucial to the study of light-matter interactions involving angular momentum. In this proposed project, we will carry out a theoretical study to understand how the topology of metallic scatterers affects photonic SOIs. The topology are characterized by the genus (i.e. number of “holes”), which can give rise to current singularities on the scatterers’ surface under the excitation of incident light. Such singularities could modify photonic SOIs. We will explore the photonic SOIs in two regions. In the farfield region, we will investigate the spin/OAM distribution and the mechanical effects of SOIs, i.e. optical forces/torques induced on the scatterers. In the nearfield region, we will investigate how SOIs change the emission properties of a chiral emitter and the scattering/absorption of a chiral particle. The results of this project could uncover the effects of geometric topology on photonic SOIs and bring about novel mechanisms to manipulate angular momentum in chiral light-matter interactions. It will not only deepen our understanding of spin dynamics and singular phenomena of light, but also nourish the field of photonics with new insights and perspectives. In addition, the proposed project could generate distinct approaches to control the propagation and polarization of light for communications and give rise to practical applications in micromanipulation of particles, light emission of nanoantenna, and sensing of chiral molecules. 光攜帶自旋和軌道角動量, 自旋與光的偏振有關，軌道角動量與光場的空間分布有關， 它們的相互影響和轉化，即自旋-軌道相互作用，可以產生許多新穎的現象和應用，例如光的自旋霍爾效應、光信號的單向傳輸和粒子的光學微操縱。由於其固有的矢量特征，自旋-軌道相互作用強烈依賴於光學系統的結構特性。一項根本的結構特性便是拓撲，即系統在連續變換下的幾何不變性。 因此，理解拓撲如何影響光自旋-軌道相互作用對於研究與角動量有關的光-物質相互作用至關重要。 在本項目中，我們將開展理論研究，理解金屬散射體的拓撲結構如何影響光自旋-軌道相互作用。拓撲結構的特徵取決於虧格（即“孔”的數目）。在入射光的激發下，拓撲虧格會導致散射體表面上產生電流奇點， 這種奇點可以影響光自旋-軌道相互作用。我們將在兩個區域研究光自旋-軌道相互作用。在遠場區域，我們將研究自旋/軌道角動量的分佈。 在近場區域，我們將研究自旋-軌道相互作用如何改變手性發光體的發光特性以及手性粒子的散射/吸收。 該項目的成果可以闡明幾何拓撲結構對光自旋-軌道相互作用的影響，揭示新的機制應用於手性光-物質相互作用中角動量的操縱，不僅有助於加深我們對自旋動力學和奇點光學的理解，還可以產生新的見解和觀點，從而促進光學領域的發展。此外，此項目可以促生新方法用於控制光的傳播和偏振，並且在納米天線的光發射以及手性分子的感測方面產生實際應用。

11306019.label: Realisation of objectives
11306019.value: Objective 1 The first objective is “To investigate light scattering by metallic scatterers of different topologies (i.e. genus) to uncover the effects of geometric topology on photonic SOIs.” To achieve this objective, we considered scatterers made of perfect electric conductor (PEC) and scatterers made of gold. These scatterers have different topology that is characterized by the genus g, including sphere (g=0), torus (g=1) and double torus (g=2). We conducted full-wave simulations of the scatterers under various excitations including plane waves and vector Bessel beams. The photonic SOIs mediated by the scatterers give rise to C lines (polarization singularities at which light is circularly polarized) in both the near field and far field carrying spin angular momentum. These C lines manifest intriguing configurations such as “rings” and “handles”, and they emerge in both the scattering electric field and scattering magnetic field. We investigated the effects of geometric topology of scatterers on the scattering electric field and magnetic field separately. For the electric field, we found that the polarization index of the C lines satisfies the Poincare-Hopf theorem in the far field, i.e., the summation of the indices of all C lines is equal to 2 because the electric field is tangent to the far-field momentum sphere. This property can be well explained with multipole expansions. The emergence of C lines is attributed to the interference of the electromagnetic multipoles. In the subwavelength regime, the interference of electric and magnetic dipoles gives rise to four C lines in the far field. In the near field, the electric C lines are sensitive to the geometric details of the scatterers, and there is no explicit relation between their indices with the geometric topology of the scatterers, and the properties of the C lines cannot be captured by multipole expansions. This work uncovers the important relationship between scatterers’ geometric topology and photonic SOI associated with electric field, in particular the polarization singularities of the scattering electric field. The results can be applied to manipulate optical polarizations in nanophotonic systems and find novel applications in optical sensing. The results are published Physical Review A 103, 023520 (2021). For the magnetic field, we discover a very interesting and fundamental connection between the geometric topology of scatterers and the topological properties of magnetic near field. We find that the nontrivial topology of a metal structure ensures the birth of polarization singularities in the near fields, and bounds their spatial morphologies (i.e., C lines) characterized by topological indexes. The total topological index of these singularities is always equal to the Euler characteristic of the metal structure. For example, a torus and a sphere will induce different polarization singularities with different total indices. This is decided by their different genus, i.e., torus has one “hole” while sphere has no “hole”. Remarkably, this property is unrelated to the excitation or frequency and is robust against continuous deformation of the scatterers’ geometry. In addition, introducing extra spatial symmetries can give rise to higher-order polarization singularities with intriguing polarization configurations inaccessible with conventional optical structures, including mirror-symmetric Mobius strips. By mapping the polarization singularities to non-Hermitian exceptional points, we provide a complete framework to understand their invariant properties in spatial evolutions (merging, bifurcation, and topological transitions). This work has essentially connected polarization singularities, the topology and symmetry of structures, as well as non-Hermitian physics, opening extra opportunities for fundamental conceptual explorations and many related practical applications in chiral discrimination and sensing, chiral quantum optics, and topological photonics. The results are published in Science Advances 8, eabq0910 (2022). Objectives 2 & 3 The second and third objectives are closely related to each other and were achieved in the same configuration: chiral particles coupled to the topological scatterers. The objectives aim to study the radiation, scattering, and absorption of chiral particles and their dependence on the effects of photonic SOIs. The chiral particles are deep subwavelength and thus can be treated as dipoles (i.e., chiral emitters). The photonic SOIs of the topological scatterers induce C lines in the near field, which carries strong optical chirality that can be used for chiral discriminations. We first consider the C lines of a sphere with genus g = 0. We numerically evaluated the optical chirality on the C lines and compared it to that of ordinal circularly polarized plane wave. It is found that the optical chirality of C lines can be much larger. We then considered a chiral particle locating on the C lines and studied its scattering and absorption properties. Using full-wave numerical simulations, we determined the absorption dissymmetry of the chiral particles with opposite handedness at different positions on the C lines. We find that the absorption dissymmetry can be much larger than that induced by circularly polarized plane-wave excitation. By applying analytical dipole approximations, we treat the chiral dipole as electric and magnetic dipoles and determine the dipole moments. We find that the dipole moments are different for the opposite chiral particles due to the difference in their radiation and coupling with the topological scatterers. In addition, the different dipole moments can explain the differential absorption of the chiral particles. We also find that the absorption dissymmetry strongly depends on the anisotropy of the chiral particles. The results may find applications in optical manipulations, optical sensing, and chiral quantum optics. These results are published in Physical Review A 105, 033513 (2022). In addition to a single topological scatterer, we also considered the coupling between chiral particles with an array of topological scatterers (metallic disks with genus g =0 same as the sphere). Such a structure corresponds to the so-called metasurface. Similar to the case in Ref. [Physical Review A 105, 033513 (2022)], the metasurface can also induce C lines in the near field. In contrast to the C lines of single sphere which has localized optical chirality, these C lines generated by the disk array can give rise to large-area (covering the whole unit cell) optical chirality of the same sign for the wavelength ranging from 1.2 um to 1.5 um, which is achieved by tuning the incidence angle and polarization of the incident plane wave. The average magnitude of the chirality is comparable to that of circularly polarized plane waves, with the maximum value appearing in the vicinity of the C lines. Then, we put small chiral particles in the near fields and numerically calculate their absorption. It is found that the left-handed and right-handed chiral particles manifest different absorptions due to their different coupling with the fields of the disks. Using analytical dipole approximations, we determine the dipole moments of the particles as well as the relationship between the optical chirality and the absorption dissymmetry. The analytical results quantitatively agree with the full-wave simulation results and confirm our understanding of the absorption properties of the chiral particles. The SOI induced C lines in such metasurface structures provide a convenient mechanism for broadband chiral discrimination without using chiral excitations or chiral structures. The structure is very simple and can be easily integrated into on-chip optical devices for large-area detection of chiral molecules. The results are published in Physical Review A 108, 053504 (2023).

11306019.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306019.value: This GRF project has generated 9 journal publications, including one paper in Science Advances, 6 papers in Physical Review A/B, one paper in Advanced Optical Materials, and one paper in Optics Express. The major findings are summarized as follows. 1. We find that simple metallic scatterers can generate intriguing chiral fields due to the SOIs in the light scattering by the scatterers [Physical Review A 103, 023520 (2021)]. These chiral fields correspond to the polarization singularity C lines emerging in both the electric field and magnetic field. In the far-field region, the total indices of the electric C lines satisfy the Poincare-Hopf theorem associated with line field because the field polarization is everywhere tangent to the k-sphere. In the near-field region, the electric C lines can manifest complex configurations and their total indices in general do not satisfy the Poincare-Hopf theorem due to the longitudinal component of the near fields. 2. We discover a fundamental and interesting relation between the topological properties of the scattering magnetic near fields and the topology (genus) of metallic scatterers [Science Advances 8, eabq0910 (2022)]. For metallic scatterers with smooth surfaces and small skin depth, under the incidence of arbitrary light, magnetic polarization singularities must emerge on the scatterers’ surfaces, which are characterized by polarization topological indices. Importantly, we find that the total index of the surface polarization singularities is always equal to the Euler characteristic of the scatterers and thus is decided only by the number of holes in the scatterers. This property is robust against continuous deformation of the scatterers’ geometry and is irrelevant to the material loss and excitation properties. 3. We demonstrate that the scattering near fields of the topological scatterers can be applied for chiral discriminations [Physical Review A 105, 033513 (2022); Physical Review A 108, 053504 (2023)]. The photonic SOIs mediated by the topological scatterers can give rise to chiral near fields with strong optical chirality. When small chiral particles are immersed in the chiral fields, differential absorption can be achieved for left-handed and right-handed particles, corresponding to circular dichroism phenomena. We show that this can be achieved with either a single scatterer or a periodic array of scatterers. The mechanism can be attributed to the different dipoles induced in the chiral particles in the presence of the coupling with the scattering fields of the topological scatterers.

11306019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306019.value: There are several interesting directions we can explore further for new physics. First, the spin-orbit interactions are closely related to the geometric phase of optical fields. Since the topological properties of surface polarization singularities are decided by the genus of the scatterers, there may be a connection between the topology of scatterers and the geometric phase of near fields. This geometric phase can be directly evaluated via full-wave simulations, and we then can investigate this possible connection. Second, while we have demonstrated two types of applications of the chiral near fields (C lines) induced by the SOIs mediated by topological scatterers, it is interesting to explore further applications in chiral light-matter interactions, in particular in chiral quantum optics. Last but not least, the results of this project may be extended to other classical wave systems such as acoustic systems. It is well known that sound is a longitudinal wave without spin. Interestingly, recent studies show that the velocity field of sound waves can manifest nonzero local spin density. Thus, it may be possible to explore similar SOI phenomena in acoustic topological structures.

11306019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306019.value: This GRF project investigates the interesting properties and phenomena associated with photonic spin-orbit interactions mediated by topological scatterers. Under the incidence of external light, the scattering fields of the scatterers generally carry local spin and orbital angular momentum. We find that polarization singularities can emerge in the scattering electric and magnetic fields. Remarkably, the topological indices of the magnetic near-field singularities are only decided by the genus of the scatterers, as long as the scatterers are made of metal with smooth surfaces and small skin depth. The significance of this finding is that the topological properties of optical fields are connected to the topological properties of scatterers, which provides a new degree of freedom for light manipulation. In addition, we explored the effects of photonic spin-orbit interactions on the radiation, scattering, and absorption of chiral particles coupled to the topological scatterers. We find that the chiral near fields associated with the polarization singularities can be applied to achieve chiral discriminations. The results of the project open new possibilities for light manipulation by using topological scatterers and can find broad applications in optical sensing, optical metrology, and optical manipulations of small particles.

11306219.label: Project Objectives
11306219.value: To build reasonable calculation models of disordered black TiO2 surface with O vacancies and gradient dopings of H, B, C, N, S, or P atoms. According to these models, the doping effect of nonmetal dopants on the electronic structure of black TiO2 will be shown and compared with experiments for checking their consistencies. To reveal the mechanism of passivation and transfer doping caused by effective dopings. Based on such a mechanism, special attentions will be paid to charge populations on key atoms or bonds to understand the direction and intensity of charge transfer as the gradient doping perpendicular with the surface slab. To reveal the spatial separation and time evolution of electron-hole pairs on the black TiO2 surface with different dopants. 11306219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306219.value: Black TiO2 is a promising photocatalyst that can be used in photoelectrochemcial (PEC) applications such as H2 and O2 production (ideal carriers of clean chemical energy) by water splitting. In our recent work, we have successfully obtained a surface nitrogen-doped rutile TiO2 with good photo-induced charge separation performance. It is realized that certain doping could not only improve the conductivity of charge carriers but also significantly improve the optical absorption properties. Although doping can directly enhance the conductivity, there is still much room for improvement. Complicated experimental results are by far so poorly understood that convincing doping mechanisms are urgently demanded. Systematic theoretical calculations would be benefitial for understanding the intrinsic mechanism so as to guide the doping strategy and optimize PEC conditions in green energy applications. We believe that the surface passivation mechanism accompanied by charge transfer plays an important role in the surface doping of black TiO2. Therefore, we propose in this project to conduct computational research in accordance with such a mechanism to find optimal doping design and to complement previous explorations based on substitutional and interstitial doping mechanisms. We will model the doping systems by placing nonmetal dopants such as H, B, C, N, S and P atoms into the surface nanostructures of black TiO2. We will simulate the gradient doping of these atoms in the surface regions as well as the adsorption and desorption of water molecules and other possible species such as H+/OH- and O2/H2O involved in PEC. The calculation will include geometry optimizations and molecular dynamics simulations at ground states and/or excited states, transition state searches of possible chemical reactions involved, and charge populations as well as band structures and density of states, at the level of accurate density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT functionals. We expect that our work would deliver useful information about doping types and configurations as determined by charge transfers, which provide the carriers for the conduction due to the dopant accumulation at interface and surface of the black TiO2 as well as the adsorptions and desorptions of species from the electrolyte. We will also reveal the interfacial chemical reactions involving dopants in PEC applications and identify the reactions with products on stable surfaces from photoinduced reconstruction of the black TiO2 material. 黑色TiO2是一種很有前途的光催化劑，可用於水分解制H2和O2(清潔化學能的理想載體)等光電化學領域。我們最近成功地獲得了表面摻氮金紅石TiO2，該材料具有良好的光致電荷分離性能。結果表明，一定的摻雜不僅能提高載流子的導電性，而且能顯著地改善光學吸收性能。雖然摻雜可以直接提高電導率，但仍有很大的改進空間。迄今為止，人們對復雜的實驗結果知之甚少，迫切需要令人信服的摻雜機制。系統的理論計算將有助於了解其內在機理，從而指導綠色能源應用中的摻雜策略和優化摻雜條件。 我們認為，伴隨電荷轉移的表面鈍化機制在黑色TiO2表面摻雜中起著重要的作用。因此，在本課題中，我們提出根據這種機制進行計算研究，以尋找最佳的摻雜設計，並補充以往基於替代和間隙摻雜機制的探索。我們將通過將H，B，C，N，S和P等非金屬摻雜物加入到黑TiO2的表面納米結構中來模擬摻雜體系。我們將模擬這些原子在表面區域的梯度摻雜，以及水分子和其它可能的物種如H+/OH-和O2/H2O的吸附和解吸。計算將包括基態和(或)激發態的幾何優化和分子動力學模擬；在精確密度泛函(DFT)和時間相關的DFT泛函水平上，對可能發生的化學反應進行過渡態搜索，並計算電荷布居、能帶結構和態密度。我們期望我們的工作能提供關於由電荷轉移決定的摻雜類型和構型的有用信息，這些電荷轉為由於摻雜在黑TiO2界面和表面的摻雜積累以及電解質中物種的吸附和解吸而導電提供載流子。我們還將揭示摻雜物在納米TiO2應用中的界面化學反應，並通過光誘導TiO2材料的光致重構，確定在穩定的表面與產物的反應。

11306219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306219.value: To understand the effects of oxygen vacancy (OV) and hydrogen (H) atoms, we modelled their diffusions in the A-TiO2 (101) surface employing Density Functional Theory (DFT) methods, revealing the formation mechanism of black TiO2. We found that OV transitions in the vertical direction are notably faster than in the horizontal transitions, showing deep OV transfer within the surface layer and establishing the existence of an OV channel. The smooth transition of H atoms between OV sites enables the formation of an H channel, guiding the synthesis of black TiO2. The presence of the H channel reduces the energy gap, enhancing the light adsorption efficiency of black TiO2. The well separated photoinduced holes and electrons would enhance photocatalytic activity in water-splitting reactions. These findings offer valuable insights for tailoring the properties of black TiO2, opening avenues for advanced photocatalytic applications (see more details in the paper 1 of Part C [C8-1]). Non-metal doping is usually used to narrow the band gap of TiO2 and thus improve its light absorption. It also helps create internal electric field which facilitates electron-hole separation. Our DFT calculations for N doped anatase-TiO2 revealed that the lager electronegativity of O atom significantly pulls electrons to deeper layers leading to charge redistribution. Negative charges steadily increase with the depth in N8 doped anatase-TiO2(101). A remarkable electric field throughout four surface layers is created [C8-2]. NH3 adsorptions with different coverage and different cell sizes on the anatase (001) surface by DFT calculations reveals that the structure differences for a given coverage of 0.25 at 1/4 and 4/16 ML are significant dependent on the cell size. Similar structure relaxation was also found with H2O and H2S adsorption induced by reactivity of the anatase surface and hydrogen bond effects of adsorbates [C8-3]. Our research outputs in which the funding is acknowledged also include adenine ultrafast photorelaxation via electron-driven proton transfer [C8-4] and roles of carbon dopants in photoinduced water−splitting on carbon modified g-CN [C8-5] studied using excited state dynamics simulations, As-Li electrides under high pressure [C8-6], optimization of chemical synthesis with heuristic algorithms [C8-7], developments of g-CN photoanodes with enhanced photoelectrochemical activity by bandgap state modulation [C8-8], by two-step surface boron decoration [C8-9] and by horizontal loading of SnS2 nanosheets to form 2D/2D heterojunctions [C8-10], developments of ZnSe nanorods with enhanced photoelectrochemical performance [C8-11 and C8-12], as well as the development of large and good-quality single crystals of orthochromates [C8-13].

11306219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306219.value: Black TiO2 is a promising photocatalyst that can be used in photoelectrochemcial (PEC) applications such as H2 and O2 production (ideal carriers of clean chemical energy) by water splitting. Built on our successful synthesis of a surface nitrogen-doped rutile TiO2 and the design of nonmetal surface doping with excellent carrier transportation in black TiO2 development in this project, further research would be directed to screen out optimal dopants and realize efficient sunlight conversion by fabricating photoanodes based on black TiO2 materials. The so-developed doped black TiO2 could provide optimal PEC properties and charge carrier transport, thus enabling the photocurrent in PEC cells to produce H2 efficiently.

11306219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306219.value: Black TiO2 is a promising photocatalyst that can be used in photoelectrochemcial (PEC) applications such as H2 and O2 production (ideal carriers of clean chemical energy) by water splitting. To promote the practical application of black TiO2 materials in the field of clean energy, we performed in this project systematic theoretical calculations and revealed the possibility of surface passivation and transfer dopings, so as to complement previous studies based on substitutional and interstitial doping mechanisms. We modelled the doping systems by placing nonmetal dopants at various possible sites on the surface nanostructures of black TiO2. We simulated the doping of these atoms in the surface regions as well as the adsorption and desorption of possible molecules and species involved in PEC. We have further done calculations in possible excited states to simulate the photon excitation in PEC applications. Our work would be beneficial for understanding the involved intrinsic mechanism so as to guide the doping strategy and optimize PEC conditions in green energy applications.
