11306619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306619.value: Fluorescent carbon nanomaterials are ideal for bio-imaging because they are non-toxic, and stable in biological environments. Unfortunately, the application of carbon dots, the most prevalent form of carbon nanomaterials so far, in bioimaging is still limited by their need for blue/UV excitation which leads to autofluorescence from the surrounding cellular material, resulting in high background image noise. One attractive avenue for bio-imaging probe nanoparticles is to move from spherical carbon dots into anisotropic shapes of fluorescent carbon nanoparticles, such as carbon nanorods (CNRs). The use of such anisotropic probes can offer multiple benefits. The initial stage of this proposal will focus on developing anisotropic carbon nanorods based on our encouraging preliminary experiments. We will focus on the elucidation and control of the CNR formation mechanism, and the development of the synthesis of CNRs with controllable size and strong fluorescence over the whole visible range. This will be achieved through the use of different precursors, which take a role in templating the shape of the final nanoparticles, as well as modifying the reaction parameters to manipulate the size and also the surface modification of the CNRs. Surface modification is an important factor in controlling both the fluorescence brightness and also the biocompatibility of the CNRs. The project will furthermore focus on understanding the mechanism of the polarised emission from nanorods, where the particles are undergoing both translational and rotational diffusion (Brownian motions) in various types of fluid environments and also within biological structures. Fully understanding the emission processes from dynamic, moving anisotropic fluorescent probes where the emission and probe rotation rates overlap, will allow a detailed picture to be constructed of the biological environment in which the CNRs are embedded or the motion of moieties to which they are attached. An additional bonus of moving to anisotropic carbon particles is the fact that they may possess high two-photon absorption cross-sections, which is to be confirmed in a series of related experiments. In high contrast bio-imaging applications they can be excited by long wavelength light, even into the near IR where there is a transparency range allowing deeper penetration into biological tissues. Non-blue/UV excitation resulting in two-photon fluorescence would drastically reduce unwanted autofluorescence, providing a major benefit for bioimaging with CNRs. 碳基熒光納米材料是生物成像應用中的理想選擇材料，因為它們具有無毒，在生物環境中保持穩定的良好特性。碳點作為壹種迄今為止最為常見的碳基納米材料，其在生物成像應用中的仍然受到很大限制。這是因為碳點主要是被紫外光或者藍光所激發，由此會導致來自周圍細胞的自發熒光，造成高噪聲背景圖像。基於這個原因，壹種解決方法是設計具有各向異性形狀的碳基熒光納米材料，例如碳納米棒（CNRs, 使用這種各向異性熒光探針可以提供多種益處. 本項目將基於我們實驗室的初步研究成果，探索和制備具有具有各向異性的碳納米棒。我們將重點關註CNRs形成機制的闡明和理解，以獲得尺寸可控和在整個可見光範圍內有強熒光發射的CNRs。探索使用不同的前驅體，由於在自組裝過程中不同前驅體起到的作用不同，從而操縱CCNRs的尺寸和表面性質。改變反應參數和對CNRs表面改性是控制它的熒光強度和生物相容性的重要手段。此外，該項目還將側重於通過分析測試粒子在各種類型的流體環境中同時經歷平移和旋轉擴散（布朗運動，理解CNRs極化發射的機理。對於動態移動的各向異性熒光探針在發射和探針旋轉速率重疊的情況下的發射原理的充分了解，對於CNRs發光性能的全面理解和將其應用於生物環境有重要的意義。根據壹系列文獻報道，合成各向異性碳顆粒還有另壹個好處，它們很大概率具有高雙光子吸收截面。在高對比度生物成像的應用中，它們能被長波長（紅光到近紅外光）所激發。紅光範圍的激發光能更深入地穿透生物組織，減少由於藍/紫激發引起的自發熒光，從而為生物成像提供更好的條件。

11306619.label: Realisation of objectives
11306619.value: In the work on this project, not only carbon nanorods but also several other morphologies of light-emitting colloidal carbon nanostructures such as carbon dots (CDs), carbon nanorolls (CNRs) and carbon nanobelts (CNBs) have been developed. All these different morphologies were worth to be explored in terms of objectives of this project. All 4 objectives of this project have been successfully – 100% - achieved. Objective 1 “Development of rational fabrication routes using wet-chemical approaches”: Two most commonly used synthetic approaches, namely solvothermal and microwave-assisted thermal treatments have been used for CDs’ fabrication from phloroglucinol using three different nitrogen containing solvents: ethylenediamine, dimethylformamide, and formamide. We demonstrated tenability of the CD appearance from amorphous or well-carbonized spherical particles to onion-like ones, which is controlled by solvent polarity; whereas the thermal treatment conditions mostly influence the degree of the N-doping and the nature of emissive centers of CDs formed. We achieved a successful extension of the family of light-emitting colloidal carbon nanostructures to a number of different shapes and morphologies, namely carbon nanorolls (CNRs) and carbon nanobelts (CNBs). Near infrared (NIR)-emissive CNRs were synthesized via a solvothermal fusion of carbon dots (CDs) triggered by a dehydration process of their surface functional groups. In ethanol solution, CNRs have a maximum absorption peak at 665 nm and a NIR emission band extending from 650 to 800 nm. Rolled structure of CNRs can be un-coiled under 655 nm laser irradiation (power density 1 W·cm-2) of their solution in ethanol, forming carbon nanobelts (CNBs) with the width of 7-20 nm and lengths reaching several hundreds of nanometers, which was accompanied by a considerably decreased absorption band at 665 nm. We developed a template-assisted method using porous silica microspheres for the formation of CDs with optical transitions in the near-infrared. Two organic dyes – Rhodamine 6G and IR1061 with emission in the yellow and near infrared spectral regions, respectively, were used as precursors. The template-assisted method allows us to synthesize CDs with an emission peaked at 1085 nm and photoluminescence quantum yield of 0.2%, which is the highest value reported so far for CDs emitting at wavelengths longer than 1050 nm. Objective 2 “Surface functionalization to realize strong, tunable emission”: CDs with efficient excitation and emission in deep-red/near-infrared (NIR) spectral range are important for bioimaging applications. We developed a method to significantly enhance both the absorption and emission of CDs in deep-red/NIR by suppressing nonradiative charge recombination via deprotonation of the CD surface. As compared to aqueous solutions at room temperature, NIR emission of CDs in N, N-dimethylformamide and glycerol have experienced a 50- and 70-fold increase at -20 ℃, respectively, due to enhanced deprotonation ability and viscosity. Optically active chiral compounds are important for applications in the fields of biology, pharmacology and medicine. With this in mind, we produced chiral CDs via two synthetic approaches using a chiral amino acid precursor L/D-cysteine: (i) surface modification treatment of achiral CDs at room temperature and (ii) one-pot carbonization in the presence of chiral precursor. The chiral signal in the absorption spectra of synthesized CDs originates not only from the chiral precursor but from the optical transitions attributed to the core and surface states of CDs. The synthesized CDs showed two-photon absorption which is an attractive feature for their potential bioimaging and sensing applications. In a related study, we developed a chemical protocol of colloidal complex formation via covalent bonding between carbon dots and plasmonic metal nanoparticles in order to influence and improve their fluorescence. For the most optimized architecture, emission enhancement reaching up to 5.4- and 4.9-fold for complexes with silver and gold nanoparticles has been achieved, respectively. Objective 3 “Spectroscopic studies”: We revealed the nature of optical activity in carbon dots produced from different chiral precursor molecules. In particular, it results in the formation of carboxyl/imide/carbonyl groups at the CD surface, leading to the appearance of additional blue/gren/yellow-emissive optical centers. From the analysis of the optical data together with DFT calculations, we assigned the green/ yellow emission to conjugated sp2-domains (core state) similar to organic dye derivatives stacked within disk-shaped CDs; and the broad red emission – to oxygen containing groups bound to sp2-domains (surface state), whereas energy transfer from the core to the surface state happens. In another related study, using DFT, we comprehensively analyzed how the changes in the structure of molecular centers during the synthesis of blue-emissive CDots affect their optical properties. Calculations predicted a red shift of the PL peak and a decrease in the PL intensity of CDots when the monomer-like molecular centers are replaced by the covalent or noncovalent dimers. The predicted redshift of the PL peak can be significantly reduced by shortening the length of the conjugated π-system. Objective 4 “Exploration of eventual use of as luminescent probes for fluorescence bio-imaging”: CDs exhibit robust, reproducible and environment-sensitive PL signals, enabling to monitor selected chemical phenomena including phase transitions or detection of ultra-low concentrations of molecular species in solution. We reported the PL turn-off/on behavior of aqueous CDs allowing the reversible monitoring of the water-ice phase transition. The bright PL attributable to molecular fluorophores present on the CD surface was quenched by changing the liquid aqueous environment to solid phase (ice). Based on light-induced electron paramagnetic resonance measurements and DFT calculations, the proposed kinetic model assuming the presence of charge-separated trap states rationalized the observed sensitivity of PL lifetimes to the environment. Importantly, the PL quenching induced by freezing could be suppressed by adding a small amount of alcohols. Based on this behavior, a fluorescence “turn-on” alcohol sensor for exhaled breath condensate (EBC) analysis has been developed. This provided an easy method to detect alcohols among other common interferents in EBC with a low detection limit (100 ppm), which has a potential to become an inexpensive and non-invasive clinically useful diagnostic tool for early stage lung cancer detection. A disadvantage of carbon dots used for optical sensing is their broad emission profile, leading to unspecific sensing and a potential overlap of their luminescence with autofluorescence of the samples. Machine learning approaches can address these shortcomings and greatly enhance sensing accuracy. In this study, carbon dots were employed as optical probes, while machine learning methods were applied to optimize ethanol content determination in ethanol/water mixtures, as well as in alcohol-containing beverages. A simple neural network was used to understand the importance of different optical parameters on sensing, while a modular deep learning model was developed for increased generalizability towards samples with strong autofluorescence. Drawing from multiple input channels, the deep learning model was able to predict ethanol concentrations with a mean absolute error of 0.4 vol.% in pure solvents and 6.7 vol.% in beverages (beers, wines, spirits). Apart from the original research studies conducted above, we have also published 5 review articles on the photophysics and optical processes occurring in carbon nanocolloids; on the use of carbon nanoparticles as versatile auxiliary components of perovskite-based optoelectronic devices; on the use of carbon dots in optoelectronics, in general; on the fabrication of supra-carbon dots with versatile morphologies and promising optical properties; and on the synthesis, optical properties, and emerging applications of chiral carbon dots.

11306619.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306619.value: This project provided a solid advancement of the field of light-emitting colloidal carbon materials of different shapes and morphologies. While initially formulated for elongated carbon dots, we extended our activities to several other morphologies such as carbon dots, carbon nanorolls and carbon nanobelts. In terms of synthesis of these materials, we have focused not only on shape control but also on the improvement of their photoluminescence quantum yields, and, importantly, on achieving the versatility of the surface capping and functionalization. This allowed us to demonstrate several important characteristics of those materials, such as chiral carbon dots, and to significantly shift their emission toward near-infrared spectral region. This region of the so-called biological window will allow the use of the synthesized materials for biomedical sensing and labeling. We conducted advanced spectroscopic studies of the produced carbon nanomaterials, and complemented them by density functional theory (DFT) calculations which allowed us to offer important insights into the nature of optical centres and recombination pathways. In terms of anticipated applications, we have focused on sensing in aqueous/ethanol environment, and demonstrated a fluorescence “turn-on” alcohol sensor for exhaled breath condensate (EBC) analysis. This provided an easy method to detect alcohols among other common interferents in EBC with a low detection limit (100 ppm), which has a potential to become an inexpensive and non-invasive clinically useful diagnostic tool for early stage lung cancer detection. Machine learning methods were applied to optimize ethanol content determination in ethanol/water mixtures, as well as in alcohol-containing beverages. A simple neural network was used to understand the importance of different optical parameters on sensing, while a modular deep learning model was developed for increased generalizability towards samples with strong autofluorescence. As an outcome of this project, 13 original research papers and 5 review articles have been published, as summarized in Part C of this report. One PhD student and one master student have been trained.

11306619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306619.value: This research will definitely be developed further. There are several important directions of research on luminescent carbon nanoparticles. One is devoted to the use of near-infrared emitting carbon dots for biological labeling. Another one is to produce chiral carbon dots; here a lot of fundamental optical studies are required, and machine learning can be used to further optimize their optical properties. Finally, carbon dots can be used as coatings and thin films which may offer radiative cooling. All these directions are under attention of our team. On the first two topic, we continued our very fruitful collaboration with Czech scientists from the universities of Olomouc and Ostrava. For the radiative cooling, we teamed-up with another group at CityU led by prof. Edwin Tso, and have obtained a GRF grant (CityU 11200923) in 2023/24, entitled "Coral-inspired and colored daytime passive radiative coolers using photoluminescent carbon dots for cooling power recovery in building applications".

11306719.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11306719.value: 臨界時間後的“森林大火”

11306719.label: Project Objectives
11306719.value: Analyze the near-critical “avalanches” for forest fire processes, i.e. the successive fires occurring around a given vertex after the critical time (the time when an infinite connected component of trees would arise if the ignitions were not present). For the related model of diameter-frozen percolation, where the growth of a connected component is stopped when it reaches a diameter N, study further the effect of “boundary rules”. Such rules are known to perturb significantly the macroscopic behavior of the process. Study the effect of boundary rules for volume-frozen percolation, and for forest fire processes, with or without recovery. Understanding this issue, while also interesting in itself, should be an important step toward a good description of forest fires after the critical time.

11306719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306719.value: 在統計物理中，自組織臨界性是壹個十分有趣的現象，可以被用來解釋自然界中出現的復雜性。由Drossel和Schwabl在1992年引入的“森林大火過程”就是這種現象的壹個典型。在這壹過程中，新樹在格點上以1的強度出現（即普通滲流過程），同時閃電以極小的強度zeta出現：當壹棵樹被劈中，此樹及與之相連的所有樹都會被大火燒掉。 雖然森林大火過程引起了許多關註，但人們對這壹過程的長期行為所知甚少。研究這類問題極其困難，因為有兩種相對立的效果互相競爭：假如有很多樹，導致出現了大的連通簇，它被燒掉時就會留出大片空地。由於這種非單調性，統計物理中用來研究格點模型的常規方法不能用來研究這類問題，人們需要引入新的技術和想法。這個研究計劃的目的正是在數學層面上增進對於這類模型的理解，而研究方法來源於近年來在“近臨界性滲流”以及於之相關的其它過程中發展出來的壹些突破性想法。最近，我們得出了壹些新的結果，是關於壹個有限盒裏的森林大火過程，其盒子的邊長是強度zeta的壹個合適的函數。證明過程中，我們精確地理解了臨界時間t之前出現的大火的累積效應 （t為普通滲流過程的臨界時間）。 在這份計劃中，我們特別地想研究近臨界滲流過程中，在某個格點附近的“雪崩”現象，即，在臨界時間t後的壹個極小時間段裏（時間段長度以zeta的壹個小的指數的速度趨於零），許多大火接連發生（我們期待有log log (1/zeta)數量級的大火）。我們也希望理解森林大火過程以及與之相關的凍結滲流過程的“邊界效應”。我們已經發現，在某些例子裏，即使這種“邊界效應”乍看之下並不重要，但其實會顯著地幹擾這些過程的宏觀表現。理解這種邊界效應不僅有其本身的意義，而且對於理解森林大火過程的近臨界行為有重要作用。

11306719.label: Realisation of objectives
11306719.value: Objective 1 was fully addressed in the work “Near-critical avalanches in 2D frozen percolation and forest fires”, joint with Wai-Kit Lam (NTU, Taipei). This is a rather long work (72 pages), which was made available on Arxiv in June 2021 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.10183). It has been submitted for publication later in 2021 to a top Mathematics journal, and it is still under review. In that paper, we study forest fire processes, as well the related model of volume-frozen percolation (which happens to display a similar behavior, but described by a different set of exponents). We believe that is constitutes an important contribution toward understanding the self-organized critical (SOC) nature of these processes. We analyze the whole near-critical avalanches, starting from the natural characteristic scale of each model. For the forest fire process with rate z>0, we show that the number of burnt clusters around a given vertex grows like C log log (1/z) as z tends to 0, for some constant that we were able to determine explicitly (and that a similar result holds true for frozen percolation). In addition, many properties of these clusters can be extracted from our proofs. Several unexpected difficulties arose in our work, in particular we had to extend results from my earlier article "Near-critical 2D percolation with heavy-tailed impurities, forest fires and frozen percolation", joint with Jacob van den Berg (CWI and VU University, Amsterdam), which appeared in Probability Theory and Related Fields (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00440-020-01022-4). More specifically, we used a percolation process introduced in that paper, with "heavy-tailed impurities" accounting for the effect of fires, and we have improved some of the properties established there. This amounts to analyzing the connectivity of a forest where a small, positive (bounded away from 0), fraction of it has been destroyed by fires. If the density of burnt trees is not too large, then the near-critical regime of percolation is still relevant, approximately. -- As for Objective 2, I have addressed it to a large extent, together with my collaborator W.K. Lam. In particular, we now understand quite well the perturbations created by modified boundary rules, and how to control them. Geometrically, some macroscopic "bubbles" arise. However, we are still in the process of writing the technical details, which may still take us a significant amount of time. We have obtained a convincing description of this process, based on the earlier work "Frozen percolation in two dimensions" by Demeter Kiss, published in Probability Theory and Related Fields (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00440-014-0603-7). This work was a key starting point for us, since it provides a quite complete description for some particular boundary rules, similar to those considered by David Aldous ("The percolation process on a tree where infinite clusters are frozen"). Our strategy is then to compare more general boundary rules to this reference process, by keeping track of the successive perturbations produced by the modified boundary rules. As we had emphasized in the project proposal, our earlier joint work together with Jacob van den Berg "Boundary rules and breaking of self-organized criticality in 2D frozen percolation" (https://projecteuclid.org/journals/electronic-communications-in-probability/volume-22/issue-none/Boundary-rules-and-breaking-of-self-organized-criticality-in-2D/10.1214/17-ECP98.full) had pointed out that "macroscopic" perturbations do arise: the probability for a vertex to freeze, instead of vanishing, now remains bounded away from 0. -- Objective 3 is partially addressed in the above-mentioned preprint "Near-critical 2D percolation with heavy-tailed impurities, forest fires and frozen percolation". On the one hand, we show that such boundary rules do not perturb much the avalanches well below the characteristic scale. On the other hand, we also point out in the preprint that analyzing the role of boundary rules around the characteristic scale requires more care, and we explain how to do it. For this purpose, we make some important observations, we develop geometric considerations which should be useful for addressing further this objective, and we establish some intermediate properties. We are still in the process of addressing this objective. In particular, we want to better describe the burnt clusters with a diameter larger than the characteristic scale, which we do not fully understand at the moment. We have made significant progress by combining the insights obtained when addressing Objectives 1 and 2.

11306719.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306719.value: In this project, we have improved significantly our understanding of the near-critical behavior of two classes of planar stochastic processes, namely frozen percolation and forest fires. In particular, we emphasized why these two processes are related. We discovered and established that they both display a very peculiar phenomenon, that we called near-critical avalanches. This phenomenon had not been predicted earlier, and we have understood well why it arises in these two situations, even though the microscopic rules are not the same. It is produced by the particular freezing/burning mechanism, but the technical details are quite different in both cases, and distinct sets of exponents come into play. In particular for forest fires, a key step was to improve results obtained earlier for a percolation model with "heavy-tailed impurities", which is used as a stochastic lower bound for the connectivity of the forest. We obtained the somewhat surprising result that a positive density of trees may burn, and still the near-critical regime of percolation remains relevant. We have also identified clearly the role played by boundary rules in such processes, which had remained quite mysterious so far. We showed that they create perturbations that we are able to control, despite the fact that they are macroscopic. Finally, our work on this project, as well as on related questions in percolation theory, also led us to several collaborations on arm events for critical percolation and the geometric structure of random walks.

11306719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306719.value: We hope to extend the results obtained in this project to understand the effect of boundary rules at various scales, in particular throughout the whole near-critical avalanches. We also plan to look for further applications to other real-world processes, e.g. studied in condensed matter physics, ecology (patterns in vegetation), or epidemiology (the spread of epidemics).

11306719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306719.value: In this project, we obtained novel results for two families of models introduced in physics, known as frozen percolation and forest fires. These models appear naturally, but they are still poorly understood. We were able to rigorously establish the emergence of a very surprising phenomenon, that we called near-critical avalanches, in both cases. This is quite peculiar, and it had not been observed nor predicted earlier (neither in the mathematics nor in the physics literature). This provides a better understanding of real-world complex systems with analogous freezing/burning mechanisms.

11306819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11306819.value: Mechanochemical processes and their corresponding changes of the macroscopic properties remain less fully understood. The underlying mechanism is fundamentally interesting and important for the molecular design of many advanced smart materials including mechanical responsive, shape-memory, self-healing and ultrahigh-strength materials. Due to the lack of understanding of mechanochemical changes, design of mechanoresponsive compounds or materials with tailored properties remains challenging. Because of this, research efforts on luminescent mechanochromic compounds have received growing attention in recent years; however, systematic modification of the luminescent mechanochromic characteristics is hard to achieve. In this project, we will develop luminescent mechanochromic transition metal complexes with their mechanochromism derived from simple and readily modifiable ligands. Apart from changing the framework of the ligands, it is anticipated that the tuning of the luminescent mechanochromic properties can also be achieved by coordination to different transition metal complex systems. This project will open up new strategy for designing transition metal-based luminescent mechanochromic materials. Their potential applications will also be studied. 迄今，我們對機械力化學及其相應的物質上的性質變化仍未有充分了解。這方面的研究不但提供科學上的基本知識，這些知識更可應用於許多先進的智能材料如形狀記憶材料、自我修復材料和超高強度材料的分子設計。由於現時對機械力化學及其變化的理解不足，設計機械力敏的化合物或材料仍然有很大的挑戰。因此，近年來力致發光變色化合物的研究工作受到越來越多的關注。雖然如此，系統性修改力致發光變色特性還是十分困難。 在這個項目中，我們將開發力致發光變色的過渡金屬配合物，這些配合物的力致發光變色特性將可以從配體上修飾或調節。除了改變配體外，我們預計它們的力致發光變色特性也可通過調節過渡金屬配合物的體系而改變。該項目將開闢設計力致發光變色過渡金屬配合物的新方向。並研究它們的應用潛力。

11306819.label: Realisation of objectives
11306819.value: All objectives have been achieved. The details findings are summarized as follows: Objective 1: New luminescent Ir(III), Cu(II), Zn(II), Re(I) and Ru(II) complexes with bidentate acyclic carbene ligands have been designed, synthesized and characterized. As planned in the proposal, these bidentate acyclic carbene ligands CAAC ligands can be formed by the newly developed coordination reactions of nucleophile-substituted ligands to metal isocyanide precursors complexes. To gain an understanding of the reactions leading to the acyclic carbene ligand formation, the reactivity of a wide range of metal isocyanide complex precursors and various types of nucleophile-containing ligands have been studied. All the newly synthesized transition metal complexes (both isocyanide precursors and the targeted acyclic carbene complexes) have been characterized by various spectroscopic techniques such as NMR spectroscopy, IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and elemental analysis. The structures of some of these complexes have also been determined by X-ray crystallography. Many of these transition metal complexes exhibit luminescent mechanochromism. Some of the results have been reported in journal articles, Chemical Science 2021 and Journal of Organometallic Chemistry 2023, and the book chapter entitled "Carbonyl and Isocyanide Complexes of Rhenium" in Comprehensive Organometallic Chemistry IV, , listed in the research output. The results have also been presented at international conferences, the 7th Asian Spectroscopy Conference 2020. Objective 2: As many of the newly developed complexes described above display intriguing phosphorescent properties, we have systematically examined their photophysical properties, including the nature of the emissive excited state as well as the excited state dynamics. With the open structure of the acyclic carbene ligands, we anticipated that their properties would show strong dependences on the microenvironments and external stimuli. The stimuli-responsive behaviour, as well as the effects of solvents, vapour, and host-guest interactions on their photophysical properties, have been systematically studied. As some of the complexes show drastic changes in the luminescent properties, their applications as humidity, amine sensors, mechanoresponsive materials, and dual emissive materials have been revealed. Some of these results are reported in CCS Chem 2022 and Chemical Science 2021, listed in the research output. Objective 3: Based on the detailed study of the photophysical and mechanochromic properties of these complexes described above, we have established the structure-properties relationships, which provide important insights into the future molecular design of luminescent mechanochromic transition metal complexes. The mechanism and electronic effects have also been elucidated using Raman spectroscopy, X-ray crystallography and computational study. Interestingly, in the study of the excited state properties, we discover a photocatalytic application of some of the Ir(III) complexes, which could be used for chemical surface modification. Some of the results have been published in CCS Chem 2022, Langmuir 2021 and the book chapter entitled "Carbonyl and Isocyanide Complexes of Rhenium" in Comprehensive Organometallic Chemistry IV Organic and Biomolecular Chemistry 2020, listed in the research output and presented at Singapore International Chemical Conference (SICC)-11, 2022.

11306819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11306819.value: The research was conducted following the proposed research plan and methodology outlined in the proposal. Our research led to the successful design, synthesis, and characterization of novel luminescent complexes involving Ir(III), Cu(II), Zn(II), Re(I), and Ru(II) with bidentate acyclic carbene ligands. These complexes were synthesized through new coordination reactions involving nucleophile-substituted ligands and metal isocyanide precursors. Many of these complexes displayed unique luminescent mechanochromism. We rigorously characterized these complexes using NMR, IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, elemental analysis, and X-ray crystallography. Further exploration of their photophysical properties revealed that these complexes exhibit significant responsiveness to environmental stimuli such as changes in humidity, vapors, and host-guest interactions. Importantly, their high environmental sensitivity and responsiveness highlight their potential applications as sensors and in mechanoresponsive materials. Studies show that the open structure of the bidentate acyclic carbene ligands contributed to the strong dependence of their photophysical properties on the microenvironments. The elucidation of structure-property relationships provided key insights into the electronic effects and mechanistic aspects of emissive excited states, excited state dynamics, phosphorescence and mechanochemistry, which are critical for future molecular designs. Our study also led to the discovery of the photocatalytic activity of some of the Ir(III) complexes, which demonstrated potential for applications in chemical surface modification and the development of new materials. Some of these results have been published in internationally refereed journals listed in the research output, including Chemical Science (2021), Langmuir (2021), CCS Chem (2022) and Journal of Organometallic Chemistry (2023), as well as a book chapter in Comprehensive Organometallic Chemistry IV. Apart from publications in journal articles and book, the results have also been presented as invited lectures at international conferences including the 7th Asian Spectroscopy Conference (2020) and the Singapore International Chemical Conference (SICC)-11 (2022). In short, the results of this project contribute to the development of new classes of luminescent mechanochromic transition metal complexes with bidentate acyclic carbene complexes. Many of these complexes display interesting luminescence, mechanochemistry, mechanochromism, and excited-state properties. Detailed study shows that these complexes can be used as mechanoresponsive materials, photocatalysts, and chemosensors.

11306819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11306819.value: As mentioned in 6.1, the results of this project have led to new classes of transition metal complexes with bidentate carbene ligands. These complexes exhibit novel mechanoresponsive properties and found applications as phosphorescent materials, photocatalysts, and chemosensors. On the basis of these results, we have initiated new directions to develop new mechanoresponsive polymers and soft materials using the acyclic carbene ligands as the building blocks. A research proposal on the development of metal-based mechanochromic polymer and soft materials using the results of this work has been supported by RGC. On the other hand, we have also developed a new class of luminescent chemosensors based on the host-guest chemistry of the acyclic carbene ligands revealed in this work.

11306819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11306819.value: To meet the increasing demands for new advanced materials that can change their properties by mechanical stimulation and luminescent materials, new families of metal-based materials made from unique organic structures (bidentate acyclic carbene ligands) have been developed and studied. These molecules are special and important because they can change their glow (light emission) in response to different environmental conditions, such as changes in humidity or the presence of various gases. This characteristic makes them promising as smart sensors for environmental monitoring and safety applications. We examined these molecules using advanced instrumental techniques like NMR and IR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and X-ray crystallography, providing a new understanding of their molecular structure and behaviour in detail. During our study, we discovered new photocatalysts, speeding up chemical reactions when exposed to light, which could lead to more efficient and cleaner processes. Based on these transition metal complexes, new photocatalysts, luminescent materials, mechanically responsive materials, and chemical sensors have been designed. The scientific results have been published in internationally refereed journals and presented in invited lectures at international conferences. In summary, new classes of luminescent transition metal complexes with properties suitable for developing new photofunctional materials have been developed in this project.

11307319.label: Project Objectives
11307319.value: Functional analysis of deep structured neural networks. We aim at a complete approximation theory for deep convolutional neural networks with the rectified linear unit. By showing that the output function of a fully connected multi-layer neural network equals to that of a downsampled deep convolutional neural network, we can verify the strong approximation ability of such deep structured networks. We propose to demonstrate advantages of these structured networks by studying the problem of deconvolution for regression with convoluted inputs. The effect of filter length for approximation and some other deep structured neural networks will also be studied. Capacity of deep structured neural networks and convergence of deep learning algorithms. Error bounds and learning rates of deep learning algorithms generated by deep structured neural networks are expected. This can be carried out by estimating the sample error through analyzing the capacity of the hypothesis space for batch learning algorithms and step sizes for stochastic gradient descent type online learning algorithms. Some research problems from applications with deep learning algorithms and some related approximation theory problems may also be considered.

11307319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307319.value: Deep learning algorithms using deep neural networks have brought us technological breakthroughs in many practical domains including speech recognition and computer vision. This has raised a strong demand of learning theory of deep neural networks, especially those with special structures, as a theoretical foundation of deep learning. In this project we plan to conduct rigorous mathematical analysis and establish a learning theory for some deep structured neural networks. First we propose to express the output function of a fully connected multi-layer neural network as that of a downsampled deep convolutional neural network, which would show that such deep structured neural networks have at least as good approximation abilities as the classical fully connected networks. Here the operation of downsampling in wavelet analysis plays a key role. Next we plan to show some advantages of deep structured neural networks by analyzing the problem of deconvolution for regression with convoluted inputs. The effect of filter length for approximation by deep convolutional neural networks and some other related approximation theory problems will also be studied. Then we aim at deriving error bounds and learning rates of learning with deep structured neural networks in terms of the capacity of the hypothesis space for batch learning algorithms and step sizes for stochastic gradient descent type online learning algorithms. For this complexity analysis part, some approaches from multivariate approximation theory and wavelets are essential. 使用深度神經網絡的深度學習算法為我們帶來了許多實際領域的技術突破，包括語音識別和計算機視覺。這提出了對作為深度學習的理論基礎, 深度神經網絡學習理論的強烈需求，尤其是對那些具有特殊結構的神經網絡。在這個項目中，我們計劃對有結構的神經網絡進行嚴格的數學分析並為其建立學習理論。首先，我們打算將全連接多層神經網絡的輸出函數表示為下採樣深度卷積神經網絡的輸出函數，用來表明這種有結構的神經網絡至少具有與經典的全連接網絡一樣好的逼近能力。這裡小波分析中的下採樣算子起著關鍵作用。接下來，我們計劃通過分析回歸中的反捲積問題展示深度有結構神經網絡的一些優勢。還將研究濾波器長度對深度卷積神經網絡逼近和一些其他相關的逼近論問題的影響。然後我們將為深度有結構神經網絡導出的學習算法作出誤差界和學習率的分析, 對批量學習算法結果由假設空間的容量標述, 對隨機梯度下降型在線學習算法則由步長標述。對這些問題的複雜性分析，一些來自多元逼近論和小波理論的方法是必不可少的。

11307319.label: Major findings and research outcome
11307319.value: Spectral bias arises in training neural networks and can explain generalization ability of induced deep learning algorithms. In [1] we give a comprehensive and rigorous explanation for spectral bias and relate it with the neural tangent kernel function. We prove by spherical harmonic analysis that the training process of neural networks can be decomposed along different directions defined by the eigenfunctions of the neural tangent kernel, where each direction has its own convergence rate and the rate is determined by the corresponding eigenvalue. In the invited chapter [2] for Wiley Encyclopedia of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, we give a survey on recent developments of deep convolutional neural networks including results of functional analysis and generalization analysis of structured deep neural networks. In [3] we consider a family of structured deep neural networks consisting of two groups of convolutional layers, a downsampling operator, and a fully connected layer. We establish an approximation theory with explicit approximation rates when the approximated function is a composite one with a feature polynomial and a univariate function. In particular, we prove that such a network can outperform fully connected shallow networks in approximating radial functions when the dimension of data is large. This gives the first rigorous proof of the superiority of deep convolutional neural networks in approximating functions with special structures. Then we carry out generalization analysis for empirical risk minimization with such a deep network in a regression framework. In [4], we develop an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for deep neural network training with sigmoid-type activation functions. We prove that the approximation capability of deep sigmoid nets is not worse than that of deep ReLU nets. We also establish the global convergence of the proposed ADMM. In [5] we study regularized distribution regression involving two stages of sampling and present a novel robust scheme by introducing a robust loss function. The loss is not necessarily convex and enlarges the least squares in the literature of distribution regression. Generalization analysis is carried out with robustness and learning rates provided for the scheme. In [6] we study the augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) and consider the linearly constrained problem with a nonconvex and nonsmooth objective. We introduce a Moreau envelope of the augmented Lagrangian method, MEAL, and study its iteration complexity. We establish its whole sequence convergence and a rate when a Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property is assumed. We also propose two practical variants of MEAL, one with an approximate proximal update, and the other with a composite objective. Their convergence is also established.

11307319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11307319.value: The methods developed in this project for functional analysis and generalization of structured neural networks can be used for studying problems in operator learning and learning functions with composite structures other than ridge functions and radial function. We plan to apply these methods in our further research of operator learning by deep neural networks.

11307319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11307319.value: Deep learning algorithms using deep neural networks have brought us technological breakthroughs in many practical domains including speech recognition and computer vision. This has raised a strong demand of learning theory of deep neural networks, especially those with special structures, as a theoretical foundation of deep learning. In this project we have conducted rigorous mathematical analysis and establish a learning theory for some deep structured neural networks. We have studied some structured deep neural networks consisting of convolutional layers, downsampling operators, and fully connected layers and establish functional analysis and generalization analysis of the induced deep learning algorithms when the approximated functions have composite structures. A novel robust scheme has been proposed for distribution regression with robustness and generalization analysis carried out. For training the deep neural networks, we develop some optimization methods and establish rates of convergence. These include an alternating direction method of multipliers, a Moreau envelope augmented Lagrangian method and spectral bias related to neural tangent kernels.

11307419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307419.value: The issues of toxicity and drug resistance associated with platinum-based antineoplastic agents such as cisplatin and oxaliplatin have encouraged researchers to seek novel metal-based complexes, and platinum(IV) anticancer prodrugs have shown great promise in chemotherapeutic applications. Although platinum drugs are DNA-damaging agents, only a small fraction of the drug finally reaches the nuclear area to damage DNA. A new generation of platinum(IV) complexes with a targeting property and improved anticancer activity would be highly desirable. On the other hand, although oxaliplatin’s mechanism of action has been studied, the details have not been fully revealed, which limits the further development of oxaliplatin-based platinum complexes. The proposed study will contribute to these research directions based on our unique design and approaches. We plan to obtain nucleus-targeting platinum(IV) anticancer prodrugs that can be controllably activated after they reach the desired target. Several prodrugs will be designed, synthesized, and characterized. Their stability and activation properties will be studied, and their nuclear accumulation properties will be evaluated. The cytotoxicity of the complexes against various human cancer cells, including platinum-resistant cells, will be tested. We will also conduct a detailed study on the mechanism of the nucleus-targeting platinum(IV) prodrugs. The proposed study will grant nucleus-targeting properties to platinum-based anticancer agents in an attempt to shift their subcellular distribution, with the promise that the new complexes will bear increased antitumor activity and reduced systematic toxicity, and it may also shed light on the detailed mechanism of oxaliplatin and oxaliplatin(IV) prodrugs. This information will guide the rational design and synthesis of the next generation of platinum-based prodrugs. 順鉑和奧沙利鉑等鉑類抗腫瘤藥有耐藥性和副作用兩大常見問題。因此，科研工作者一直致力於研發新型的金屬抗癌藥。其中，四價鉑前藥具有廣泛的應用前景。鉑類抗腫瘤藥以破壞細胞DNA為作用機制；然而，只有一小部分藥物最終進入細胞核導致DNA損傷，因此迫切需要研發下一代靶向細胞核的、抗腫瘤活性更高的四價鉑前藥。另一方面，雖然奧沙利鉑大量使用於臨床，其具體作用機制尚未完全闡明，這限制了基於奧沙利鉑的抗腫瘤配合物的研發。本項目採用獨特的設計方案和研究方法，將會在一定程度上解決這些問題。我們計劃設計並合成一系列可以富集在細胞核並在細胞核裡激活的四價鉑抗腫瘤前藥。將測試它們的穩定性、還原性、細胞核靶向性、以及對各種腫瘤細胞包括腫瘤耐藥細胞的毒性。還將仔細研究這些靶向細胞核的四價鉑前藥的作用機制。本研究旨在賦予鉑類抗腫瘤藥細胞核靶向性，從而改變它們在細胞內的分佈，提高抗腫瘤活性，減少副作用。這將有助於進一步闡明奧沙利鉑及其四價鉑前藥的作用機制，為設計和合成下一代鉑類抗腫瘤前藥提供借鑒。

11307419.label: Realisation of objectives
11307419.value: Objective 1: To design, synthesize, and characterize nucleus-targeting Pt(IV) prodrugs We used a clinical anticancer drug, oxaliplatin-based Pt(IV) complex {[Pt(DACH)(OH)2(ox)], DACH = (1R,2R)-1,2-diaminocyclohexane, ox = oxalate} as the scaffold. A coumarin derivative was used as the photo-caging group to conjugate with the axial ligand of the Pt(IV) complex to give a photocaged Pt(IV) complex, named complex 3, which can be reduced to oxaliplatin by 450 nm blue light irradiation. Subsequently, we employed a nucleus-targeting peptide, R8K, to conjugate with another axial ligand of the photocaged Pt(IV) complex, resulting in the formation of coumaplatin. This complex was fully characterized by ESI-MS, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, 195Pt NMR, and HPLC. The nucleus-targeting ability of coumaplatin was examined in cell-based models, revealing that coumaplatin could effectively accumulate in the nucleus of cancer cells. This result was also confirmed by a fluorescent co-staining assay, where the fluorescence of coumaplatin was well co-located with fibrillarin, a marker of the nucleolus, further confirming its nucleus-targeting ability. Objective 2: To test the stability and photoactivation property of the complexes The stability and photoactivation efficiency of coumaplatin in PBS buffer (pH = 7.4) containing sodium ascorbate and in cancer cells were studied using HPLC, LC-MS, UV-Vis, and fluorescence spectroscopy. Coumaplatin is quite stable in the dark condition, with more than 85% remaining even after 24 hours of incubation. Upon 450 nm blue light irradiation, more than 95% of coumaplatin was reduced to oxaliplatin within 60 minutes, indicating that coumaplatin is stable enough in the physiological environment in the dark but can be effectively activated through visible light irradiation. Objective 3: To evaluate the biological activity and to investigate the action mechanism of the complexes We first used the MTT assay to evaluate the anticancer activity of coumaplatin against various cancer cell lines, oxaliplatin, coumarin ligand, and complex 3 were used as controls. A lung fibroblast cell line, MRC5, was used as the normal cells to investigate the dark toxicity of coumaplatin. Coumaplatin is generally non-toxic in the dark, whereas upon blue light irradiation, the cytotoxicity of coumaplatin is greatly increased, presenting up to 62-fold enhancement. Compared with oxaliplatin, the photoactivated coumaplatin showed up to 96-fold increased cytotoxicity in the tested cancer cell lines. Importantly, the photoactivated coumaplatin successfully overcame the resistance of cancer cells towards platinum drugs: the resistance factor (RF) value of oxaliplatin is 5.1 and 2.8, respectively in A2780cisR and A549cisR cell lines; however, the RF values of photoactivated coumaplatin in these two cell lines are 1.3 and 0.6, respectively, indicating the nucleus-targeting strategy indeed dramatically improve the anticancer performance of platinum drug and could overcome drug resistance. The action mechanism of coumaplatin is investigated. Compared with oxaliplatin, coumaplatin presented more than 12-fold increased Pt level on the nuclear DNA, but unexpectedly, unlike oxaliplatin, which mainly induced apoptosis to kill the cancer cells, coumaplatin induced senescence to eliminate cancer cells. Further study indicated that oxaliplatin only slightly induced DNA damage and activated p53-mediated pathway to trigger apoptosis and cell cycle arrest. For coumaplatin, it induced both intense DNA damage and ribosome biogenesis stress to activate p53- and E2F1-mediated pathway to upregulate p16 and p21 to initiate senescence. Interestingly, the ability of oxaliplatin to induce immunogenic cell death (ICD) has been well approved, coumaplatin, however, presented an even higher ability to trigger ICD, as a consequence, cancer cells treated with photoactivated coumaplatin, could successfully trigger T cell proliferation to further enhance it anticancer performance. In conclusion, we successfully developed a photocaged and nucleus-targeted Pt(IV) prodrug, coumaplatin, which dramatically improved the anticancer efficiency of clinical Pt(II) drugs and overcame drug resistance. A thorough investigation of coumaplatin's mechanism not only provided a novel strategy to enhance the anticancer performance of platinum drugs but also advanced our understanding of platinum anticancer drugs.

11307419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11307419.value: Targeted anticancer prodrugs that can be controllably activated are highly desired for personalized precision medicine in cancer therapy. Such prodrugs with unique action modes are also promising to overcome drug resistance. Here, we report coumaplatin, an oxaliplatin-based and photocaged Pt(IV) prodrug, designed for nuclear accumulation and "on-demand" activation. This prodrug is based on a Pt(IV) complex that can be efficiently photoactivated via water oxidation without the need for a reducing agent. Coumaplatin accumulates very efficiently in the nucleoli, and upon photoactivation, exhibits a level of photocytotoxicity up to 2 orders of magnitude higher than that of oxaliplatin. Unexpectedly, this prodrug presents strikingly enhanced tumor penetration ability and utilizes a distinct action mode to overcome drug resistance. Coumaplatin induces cell senescence, p53-independent cell death, and immunogenic cell death along with T cell activation, unlike oxaliplatin. This project not only provides a novel strategy for the rational design of controllably activated and nucleolus-targeted Pt(IV) anticancer prodrugs but also demonstrates that accumulating conventional platinum drugs in the nucleus is a practical way to change its canonical mechanism of action and achieve reduced resistance.

11307419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11307419.value: In this project, we have confirmed that developing photocaged and nucleus-targeted Pt(IV) prodrugs is a promising strategy to improve the anticancer activity of platinum drugs and overcome platinum resistance in cancer cells. However, coumaplatin is activated by blue light, which has a relatively short wavelength and low tissue penetration ability, making it unsuitable for in vivo application. In the next step, we plan to develop nucleus-targeted Pt(IV) prodrugs that can be activated by NIR light irradiation and thoroughly investigate their in vivo anticancer performance, pharmaceutical properties, and safety. Subsequently, we will select Pt(IV) prodrugs that could potentially be used for pre-clinical study and further development.

11307419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11307419.value: Platinum drugs are some of the most widely used anticancer drugs in the clinic; the therapeutic outcome of platinum drugs is limited by serious side effects and resistance from cancer cells. Although nuclear DNA has been considered the major target, less than 10% of platinum drugs can bind to it, allowing cancer cells to easily repair damaged DNA and become resistant. To address these challenges, we developed coumaplatin, a clinical platinum drug-based, photocaged, nucleus-targeted Pt(IV) prodrug. Coumaplatin effectively accumulates in the nuclear region of cancer cells and remains non-toxic in the dark, but upon visible light irradiation, it can be reduced to oxaliplatin in the nucleus to effectively bind nuclear DNA to kill cancer cells and overcome drug resistance. Coumaplatin is the first nucleus-targeted Pt(IV) complex, and accumulating oxaliplatin in the nuclear region could shift the mechanism of platinum drugs from inducing apoptosis to senescence, enhancing our understanding of platinum drugs.

11307619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11307619.value: Synthesis of ammonia through electrochemical reduction of nitrogen by using electrocatalysts under ambient conditions has been proposed as a dramatic alternative to the conventional Haber–Bosch process that requires high temperature and pressure. However, the ammonia yield rate and Faradic efficiency of the current electrochemical nitrogen reduction processes are unsatisfactorily enslaved by the weak nitrogen adsorption on the active sites of an electrocatalyst and the difficulty in N≡N cleavage there. Thus, developing an electrocatalyst with high-efficiency active sites for promoting nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) has important scientific and application values. Basically, an ideal NRR electrocatalyst should possess the features such as high intrinsic catalytic reactivity and selectivity toward NRR, large active surface, and outstanding mechanical and chemical stabilities. Due to the fact that transition metals have commonly higher activity for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) which competes with NRR and leads to a poor NRR selectivity, metal-free electrocatalysts have attracted broad interest as a promising candidate for NRR. Diamond has a series of inherent properties favorable for electrocatalytic NRR; and more importantly, it has a large electrochemical potential window, which enables to suppress the competitive HER and thus to achieve a high NRR selectivity. Nevertheless, the research on utilizing diamond as an electrocatalyst for NRR is still in its infancy. In this project, we propose to develop new high-efficiency electrocatalysts for ammonia synthesis based on nanostructured diamond films. The basic idea is to endow diamond with balanced electrical conductivity and NRR efficiency (activity and selectivity) through doping, and as well to increase the active area and improve the NRR performance based on field-induced enhancement effects through surface nanostructuring of diamond films. To accomplish the targets of this project, we will prepare boron-doped and boron/nitrogen co-doped diamond nanostructure arrays by microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition and subsequent in situ reactive ion etching. The effects of the factors such as the doping concentration of heteroatoms, and the geometry, aspect ratio, and distribution density of diamond nanostructure arrays on the NRR performance will be elucidated. Through comprehensive characterization and theoretical simulation, the origin of NRR activity and reaction paths on doped diamond will be revealed, and the catalytic enhancement mechanism associated with the surface nanostructuring will be demonstrated. Implementation of this project will provide further understanding for the design and development of new metal-free carbon-based electrocatalysts for high-efficiency nitrogen fixation and promote the advance of ammonia synthesis technology.

11307619.label: Realisation of objectives
11307619.value: Object 1: To synthesize nanostructured diamond films doped with boron on current collectors by combining chemical vapor deposition and subsequent reactive ion etching. To demonstrate the dependence of microstructure of different diamond films on concentration of dopants and etching parameters. We have deposited boron-doped nanodiamond (BND) films with different boron doping levels on the current collectors (Ti meshes) by microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition. The deposition was performed in CH4, H2, and Ar gas mixture with trimethylborane (TMB, diluted by H2 to 1000 ppm) as the boron source. The boron-carbon (B/C) ratio in the feed gas mixture was adjusted from 1000 to 4000 ppm to control the boron content in diamond films. It is revealed that the boron doping levels affect the locally distorted lattice structure; however, there is no obvious effect on the morphologies of BND films. We further prepared the nanostructured BND films by bias-assisted reactive ion etching (RIE) using electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) enhanced microwave plasma. The effects of RIE conditions, e.g., substrate bias, microwave power, gas composition, and duration, on the configuration of surface nanostructures are demonstrated. Various nanostructures, such as nanocone, nanowhiskers, and nanoneedle arrays, are achieved on BND surfaces. Object 2. To evaluate the catalytic performance of doped diamond films with/without nanostructured surfaces as electrodes for nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR), and to reveal the effect of doping and surface nanostructuring on the NRR performance (e.g., yield rate and the Faraday efficiency of ammonia) of diamond nanostructures. We measured the electrochemical NRR activity of the as-prepared BND/Ti electrodes without nanostructured surfaces. It is revealed that all BND samples exhibit obvious NRR activities, indicating that B doping in nanodiamonds can indeed initiate the NRR activity. Moreover, with the increase of B doping level, the NRR activity of the samples increases first, and then decreases due to the competitive hydrogen evolution reaction. BND/Ti with a B/C ratio of 1800 ppm electrode achieves the optimal NRR activity with an NH3 yield rate of 4.1 µg h−1 cm−2 and an FE of 2.5 % at an applied potential of −0.7 V vs. reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). In addition, further studies demonstrate that the overpotential for hydrogen evolution decreases with the increase of boron content. As a result, to improve the overall NRR efficiency and selectivity, it is critical to achieve a balance between the NRR and HER activities by adjusting the B doping level. We further tested the electrochemical NRR activity of BND/Ti electrodes with nanostructured surfaces. The surface nanostructure of BND is revealed to be able to enhance the NRR activity significantly. BND-nanocones/Ti electrode with sharp tips delivers the highest NH3 yield rate (19.1 μg h−1 cm−2) and FE (21.2 %) at a potential of −0.70 V (vs. RHE), surpassing the performance of the corresponding electrode without the nanostructured surface. Moreover, the BND-nanocones/Ti electrode also shows outstanding stability in long-term electrolysis. Object 3. To understand the origin of NRR activity and reaction paths on doped diamond, and to explore the synergetic catalytic enhancement mechanism associated with the nanostructured diamond surfaces. Quantum mechanical computations based on density functional theory (DFT) were carried out to elucidate the origin of electrocatalytic NRR activity on an atomic level. NRR activities of three typical diamond surfaces, (111), (110), and (100) were analyzed. In the e-NRR condition, diamond surfaces are negatively charged, and the excess electrons will accumulate on the surface to match its Fermi level with the applied electrode potential. It is revealed that the sharp diamond tips with a small radius of curvature may enhance the local electric field, which induces extra electrons near the tips. To clarify the effect of surface charge on NRR, we calculated the evolution of reaction free energy of each unit step on (111), (110), and (100) surfaces of B-doped diamond. Interestingly, it is noted that the reaction free energies associated with the intermediate electron transfer steps are significantly influenced by the amount of surface charges. In contrast, the free energy for the step not involved in electron transfer is almost insensitive to the surface charge. Fundamentally, this phenomenon is demonstrated to be associated with the change in the density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level on the diamond surface during each unit step. For the diamond electrode without surface nanostructuring, the surface charge density could be calculated to be 3.1 x 10−3 C m−2 under a potential of −0.7 V based on the result of double-layer capacitance measurement (0.45 μF cm−2). Therefore, the rate-determining step (RDS), which is the most endothermic step among the seven elemental reaction steps, for these surfaces are different, i.e., N2 dissociation (N2 + (H+ + e−) → *NNH) on (111) and (110) surfaces, and desorption of NH3 on (100) surface. When the surface charges increase (e.g., accumulation of electrons on the nanotips), the free energy for RDS will decrease on (111) and (110) surfaces, facilitating the NRR process. In contrast, the RDS on (100) surface will not be promoted by the increase of surface charge because the desorption of NH3 is insensitive to the surface charge. However, because the diamond nanocones are polycrystalline with the surfaces of nanocrystals randomly exposed, the accumulation of charges induced by the surface nanostructuring (e.g., formation of nanotips) will definitely accelerate the reaction kinetics of NRR.

11307619.label: Major findings and research outcome
11307619.value: In this project, boron-doped diamond films with nanostructured surfaces were successfully prepared on Ti mesh substrates by microwave plasma chemical vapor deposition and subsequent in situ reactive ion etching. The effects of factors such as the boron doping concentration and the geometry of diamond nanostructure arrays on the NRR performance were systematically elucidated. The studies demonstrate that the nanostructured diamond electrodes with appropriate boron doping levels and sharp diamond tips could deliver a high NH3 yield rate of 19.1 μg h−1 cm−2, a Faradaic efficiency as high as 21.2%, and a stable operation of at least eight days under ambient conditions. Through comprehensive characterization and theoretical simulation, the origin of NRR activity and the catalytic enhancement mechanism associated with the surface nanostructuring were demonstrated. Substitutional boron atoms are illustrated to be the active centers for the NRR, and charge accumulation on the tips of the nanostructured diamond enables further enhancement of catalytic activity through reducing the reaction free energy for the rate-determining step of the NRR.

11307619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11307619.value: Integrated electrodes based on boron-doped nanodiamond films with nanostructured surface/Ti meshes for nitrogen fixation are developed in this project. It has been illustrated that substitutional boron impurities serve as active centers for nitrogen reduction, and surface nanostructure-induced charge accumulation could enhance their activity. Based on these results, some further development of the research are proposed as below. 1. Optimization of the electrode material and performance: For practical applications, the NRR performance, including ammonia yield rate and FE of diamond-based electrodes fabricated in this project, should be further improved, e.g., through adjusting the type of doping elements (e.g., nitrogen doping and/or boron and nitrogen co-doping) and doping levels, and controlling the geometry (e.g., aspect ratio) and density of diamond surface nanostructure. 2. Scalability: The scalability of the fabrication process of diamond-based electrodes using microwave plasma CVD is limited by factors including equipment cost and the limitation in sample sizes. Other more cost-effective methods for diamond deposition (e.g., hot filament CVD) and reactive ion etching (e.g., RF plasmas) could be potential candidates. 3. Application studies: The other applications of diamond-based electrodes, particularly those with special surface nanostructures, can be explored, e.g., nitrate electroreduction, oxygen electroreduction, and organic electrosynthesis.

11307619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11307619.value: Ammonia is one of the most widely produced chemicals worldwide, with a key role in the growth of the global economy. Traditional ammonia synthesis by the Haber-Bosch process runs at high temperatures and pressures with low hydrogen conversion, high energy consumption, and severe environmental pollution. Electrocatalytic reduction of nitrogen to ammonia under ambient conditions has been considered a promising alternative to Haber–Bosch process. However, the advancement in the synthesis of ammonia through nitrogen electroreduction (NRR) is seriously impeded by the lack of an efficient electrocatalyst that can facilitate multiple proton-coupled electron-transfer processes and suppress the competitive hydrogen evolution reaction required for a high NRR selectivity. In this project, we synthesized nanostructured and boron-doped diamond electrodes by combining chemical vapor deposition and subsequent reactive ion etching. It is revealed that the nanostructured diamond electrodes with appropriate boron doping levels and diamond sharp tips deliver a promising NRR performance, including a high NH3 yield rate of 19.1 μg h−1 cm−2, a Faradaic efficiency as high as 21.2%, and a stable operation of at least eight days. Further, the origin of NRR activity and the catalytic enhancement mechanism associated with the surface nanostructuring are demonstrated through comprehensive characterization and theoretical simulation.

11500019.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500019.value: 贸易动机，消费平滑与资产价格泡沫的实验研究

11500019.label: Project Objectives
11500019.value: Induced motive to trade and mispricing: Are prices closer to fundamental values when investors have an induced motive to trade due to the presence of idiosyncratic income shocks, compared to the environment where no such induced motive is present? Theoretically, in both scenarios, prices should be close to the fundamental values. Aggregate risk, market incompleteness and mispricing: In the presence of traders with well-defined motive to trade, do prices deviate more from the fundamental values when markets are incomplete and there is aggregate risk? The small literature so far has focused either on an environment with no aggregate risk or aggregate risk with dynamically complete markets. Role of asset market in facilitating welfare improving trades: While efficiency of prices is an obvious measure of the performance of the market, we intend to investigate the role of the asset market in being able to allow for welfare improving exchanges among the investors. Is it possible to achieve consumption levels closer to the first-best values even though the absolute level of prices may be far off from the fundamental values? Are traders able to use the asset to offset inter-temporal income shocks and share idiosyncratic risks? Integrate the element of consumption-based general equilibrium asset pricing into experimental asset markets and contribute to this nascent literature.

11500019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11500019.value: The study of asset price bubbles is a central topic in economics. There are many examples where speculative trade in some commodity or asset generates a phase of sustained rise in price, often followed by a sudden collapse. Whether such pricing developments can be justified in terms of market fundamentals, or are they indicative of persistent deviations from intrinsic values, has been an important topic of discussion. Given that fundamental values are usually not observable, several researchers have used the methodology of laboratory experiments in order to understand the causes of systematic deviations from fundamentals and identify what features of the market or institution can help prevent such bubbles from occurring. It is now well established that although theory predicts that no trade should occur or if trade happens at all, it should take place at the fundamental value of the asset, evidence suggests that far too many trades take place and prices deviate substantially from the fundamentals. This deviation is often attributed to strategic uncertainty that arises due to investors being unsure whether other traders are rational or not. Notice that there happens to be no exogenous reason to engage in trade for the subjects participating in these experiments. If subjects have a well-defined rational need to participate in the asset market, do they trade at the fundamental values? We ask this question in our proposed research where the motive to trade is induced through consumption smoothing incentive for traders facing idiosyncratic income shocks each period. The principal goal of our study is to explore the relationship between the presence of an induced motive to trade and mis-pricing, with and without aggregate risk. At a more fundamental level, we intend to integrate the element of consumption-based general equilibrium asset pricing into experimental asset markets. We also wish to understand that if the asset is indeed priced incorrectly in the sense that the absolute level of price is too high than the fundamental value, does it prevent the ability of market participants to reduce their idiosyncratic risk via trading. That is, do “wrong” prices impede the functioning of asset market in facilitating welfare improving trades? If the answer comes out to be “no”, then the broad implication would be that one need not focus too much on the absolute level of prices but rather on the ability of the asset market to provide opportunities for Pareto-improving exchanges. 资产价格泡沫研究是经济学的核心话题。有许多一些商品或资产的投机交易产生阶段的例子 价格持续上涨，往往是突然崩盘。是否这样定价 从市场基本面来看，发展是合理的，或者它们是指示性的 持续偏离内在价值，一直是一个重要的讨论话题。 鉴于通常无法观察到基本值，一些研究人员已经使用过 实验室实验的方法，以了解其原因 系统偏离基本面并确定市场或市场的特征 机构可以帮助防止这种泡沫的发生。现在已经很成熟了 虽然理论预测不会发生交易或者交易发生，但它应该 发生在资产的基本价值，证据表明，太多了 交易发生，价格与基本面大幅偏离。这种偏差 通常归因于投资者不确定而产生的战略不确定性 其他交易者是否理性。 请注意，恰好没有外生理由参与交易 参与这些实验。如果受试者有明确的理性需求 参与资产市场，他们是否以基本价值进行交易？我们问这个 在我们提出的研究中提出的问题，即贸易的动机是通过 对于面临特殊收入冲击的交易者而言，消费平滑激励 期。我们研究的主要目标是探索之间的关系 存在诱导的交易动机和错误定价，有或没有汇总 风险。在更基础的层面上，我们打算将基于消费的一般均衡资产定价元素整合到实验资产市场中。 我们还希望了解，如果资产在某种意义上的确定价不正确 价格的绝对水平太高于基本价值，它是否会阻止 市场参与者通过交易降低其特殊风险的能力。那是， “错误”的价格阻碍了资产市场在促进福利方面的运作 改善交易？如果答案是“不”，那么广泛的含义就会出现 是的，不必过分关注价格的绝对水平，而是关注价格 资产市场为帕累托改善交易提供机会的能力。

11500019.label: Realisation of objectives
11500019.value: The project's primary aim was to study how the induced motive to trade affects asset prices using the methodology of experimental economics. We implemented markets with different proportions of traders having induced motives to trade due to exogenous shocks to their income in a dynamic multi-period setup. We first analyzed the impact of traders' consumption smoothing incentives on mispricing, thereby addressing objective 1. Next, we created treatments and implemented markets with and without aggregate risk, in addition to varying the proportion of participants having idiosyncratic risk. This allowed us to address our second objective. The further analysis of experimental data allowed us to answer the question raised in objective 3. By implementing markets with individuals experiencing idiosyncratic income shocks, we have addressed the fourth objective. Therefore, all the four objectives have been completely addressed using the experimental economics methodology.

11500019.label: Major findings and research outcome
11500019.value: We find that the presence of investors having an exogenous reason to trade is not sufficient to eliminate asset price bubbles. However, the asset prices are more closely linked to the underlying fundamentals when markets are populated with traders all of whom have an induced motive to participate in the asset market. Secondly, our results strongly suggest that even though the asset is consistently overpriced (relative to the equilibrium price) regardless of the composition of traders in the market having an induced motive to trade, participants are able to use the asset market to share their idiosyncratic risk. We also find that the co-existence of traders with and without induced motive to trade does not prevent improvements in welfare. The investors having no exogenous reason to trade are comparable to “noise traders”, and we find that the presence of such traders is not necessarily detrimental to others who have a rational need to participate in the asset market. The latter ones are able to offset their income variation by buying securities when income is high and selling when income is low, thereby reducing their consumption fluctuations significantly when compared to autarky. Furthermore, extending our line of research to implement markets where the motive to trade is induced by information heterogeneity, we find that investors with stronger signals use the lit exchange relatively more, and uninformed traders are better off when they trade more in a dark pool. Moreover, when information is concentrated in the hands of a few investors, possibly due to sparse investor connectedness or low media coverage, dark trading primarily impacts market efficiency by deteriorating the quality of asset prices. When information is diffused, dark trading no longer harms price discovery, but the unobserved liquidity entails welfare loss. Dark trading does not widen the earnings gap between informed and uninformed traders. The research has been written in the form of three articles, one of which is already published in the Journal of Economic Theory. The other two papers are available as working papers and will be submitted soon to economics/finance journals.

11500019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11500019.value: Given its vast popularity in the macro-finance literature, it was natural to start with the consumption smoothing incentive as a rational motivation to engage in trade. Future research could explore other motives to trade and their implications for mispricing of the asset. For example, trading could be motivated through liquidity need by introducing a penalty in the event of failing to achieve an assigned trading target.

11500019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11500019.value: The study of asset price bubbles is a central topic in economics. It is now well established that although theory predicts that no trade should occur or if trade happens at all, it should take place at the fundamental value of the asset, evidence suggests that far too many trades take place and prices deviate substantially from the fundamentals. If subjects have a well-defined rational need to participate in the asset market, do they trade at the fundamental values? We find that prices continue to exceed values that can be justified by the underlying fundamentals in our markets regardless of the composition of traders in terms of having an exogenous reason to engage in trade. Despite overpricing, investors faced with consumption risk are able to share their risk through trading. Thus, “wrong” prices do not necessarily impede the functioning of the asset market in facilitating welfare improving exchanges. The broad implication of our study is that one need not focus too much on the absolute level of prices but rather on the ability of the asset market to provide opportunities for Pareto-improving exchanges.

11500119.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11500119.value: 适用于金融大数据的机器学习方法及其在资产组合中的应用

11500119.label: Project Objectives
11500119.value: This proposal intends to provide a novel machine learning approach to achieve a positive definite, bias-adjusted and consistent large covariance estimate on high-dimensional and high-frequency data. This method will enable the investigation of vast portfolios with constituent stocks from concentrated industries and with unobserved connections. We will re-study vast portfolio selection and allocation issues. This proposal will bridge machine learning techniques with financial practices and help verify the promising role machine learning methodologies can play in modern financial applications. After we obtain our theoretical results and empirical findings, we will submit them to top tier finance and economic journals.
