11505119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505119.value: 研究論文的質量為學術界及其相關持份者最爲關心的問題之一。然而，如何測量研究質量卻一向缺乏共識。最常見的方法是基於著作引用率的“影響因子”。影響因子雖然容易獲得和分析，但只反映原文的流行度而非其質量。另外有些學者則曾嘗試通過專家意見來繞過質量真實内核。因此，研究質量至今仍爲一個學術黑箱。 我們在本研究中另闢蹊徑，主張用新近湧現的知識譜圖方法來測量研究貢獻（而非研究質量本身）。我們的總體思路是將每篇論文提供的“新知識“與已有“舊知識”相比較、從而確定該論文的貢獻程度。爲此，我們計劃通過證据、方法和理論等三個維度來測量知識。該三維框架使得我們有可能比較文獻中的新舊知識。如，某論文報告了一個已知的現象，那麽其生成的知識僅爲複製的“舊酒“。相反，如果該論文為一個已有的假設提供了新的證據、或為一個已知的現象提供了新的解釋，那麽其生成的知識則為新舊兼有的”半新酒“。如果該論文發現了一個新現象並提供了新解釋，那麽其生成對知識就是”全新酒“。簡言之，這一基於知識的測量方法有望解決在研究質量（無法直接測量的隱含概念）與影響因子（容易但不准）之間長而未決的兩難問題。 方法上，我們將設計和構建一個”社會媒體知識圖譜“（簡稱SMKG）以測量和評估社交媒體的知識貢獻。我們首先會從WOS數據庫中采集有關社交媒體的相關實證案例，然後從中用有監督和無監督相結合的機器學習方法提取“知識要素”（如理論概念、方法或實證特徵、假設及驗證的關係等等），並通過共引求證、概念去疑等手段净化上述知識要素，以整合成一個多層及動態的知識庫，其中理論概念將按各抽象層面和原著時序而連接起來。該知識庫最終生成前述SMKG的本體論。 我們可以用SMKG來評估文獻中社交媒體論文所產生的知識有多少是複製性的陳酒、多少是為舊假設配新證據或為舊現象配新解釋的半新酒、多少是新現象加新解釋的全新酒。本項目完成之後，SMK可以被不斷更新，使其成爲一個追蹤社交媒體研究進展的實時評估系統。我們還計劃將本研究所構建的基本方法擴展到對其它商業或社會科學研究領域的評估之中。

11505119.label: Realisation of objectives
11505119.value: All the objectives have been completed through three key components: I. data model, II. data source, and III. extraction framework. We outline the components below, with detailed information available in item #15 of Part C Research Output (“#15” hereafter). I. Data Model Reviewing the core concepts and relations in social media publications requires modeling complex features such as the meaning of the concepts and the test results of the relations, which requires a data model that considers the semantic meaning of the core concepts and relations. Knowledge graph language provides computable syntax and expressive semantics for the needed data model. In particular, our data model rests on the following principles: 1) Triple design for organizing the data. 2) Entity class for concept label. 3) Ontology for synthesizing the concept and relation information. We aim to build an ontology for the core concepts and relations in social media publications. The knowledge graph language, including the triple design, entity class, and ontology, has provided computable syntax and expressive semantics for a data model that organizes the core concepts and relations in publications. Leveraging the knowledge graph language, we model the six kinds of information on core concepts and relations as an ontology consisting of different triples and build a knowledge graph—concept and relation graph—based on the ontology. A variable term is represented as vti. That two variable terms vti and vtj have a relation is represented as a triple (vti, has a relation with, vtj). That a relation r’s property is a value is also represented as a triple. That a relation r’s test result in the study is value v1 is denoted as a triple (v1, is the test result of, r). That a relation r’s hypothesized polarity is value v2 and empirically supported polarity is v3 are denoted as triples (v2, is the hypothesized polarity of, r) and (v3, is the empirically supported polarity of, r), respectively. Figure 1 illustrates the relation information in the ontology (see #15). We constructed the concept tree based on the classic 5W model of communication (Lasswell, 1948), i.e., “Who?”, “Says what?”, “In which channel?”, “To whom?”, and “With what effect?” This model is employed as the first (most generic) level of the concept tree. The classification at the second level aims to distinguish user characteristics, perceptions, behaviors, and benefits. We added more concepts to the initial concept tree when the concept labels are assigned to variable terms in a sample of publications. The extended concept structure is shown in Figures A1–A6 of #15. Therefore, the concept tree is generated through both a top-down approach based on the 5W model and a bottom-up approach based on a publication sample. The appendix of #15 provides more detailed explanations and descriptions of the concept tree. II. Data Source We focused on research hypothesis statements (sentences in a publication that present the hypothetical relations between concepts) as the main data source. First, many publications of quantitative empirical studies on social media that investigate relations among concepts present all focal relations as hypothesis statements. Therefore, if we extract relations mentioned in all hypothesis statements, we can guarantee the recall of the relation extraction. Second, hypothesis statements are specially written to describe the investigated relations of a study, and these sentences contain little redundant information. The precision of the relation information is high, thus enabling automatic extraction. Identifications (IDs) often appear in hypothesis statements. In terms of data collection, this ID is a vital sign that the sentence is a hypothesis statement. Using only regular expressions based on the ID, we can identify most hypothesis statements. Importantly, the IDs also enable the detection of the test results of the hypothesis statements. Therefore, the ID is an important identifier that connects a hypothesis statement and its test result. In a hypothesis statement, a variable term is described using a span of words, which is usually a phrase with variable lengths. Information sharing motive has a positive impact on employees’ usage of enterprise social media” are “information sharing motive” and “employees’ usage of enterprise social media.” This phrase can communicate the meaning of the variable in the study and the conceptual meaning under the 5W model, which we aim to obtain. Formally, three steps are necessary to obtain the 5W conceptual meaning from a variable term in a hypothesis statement. First, we identify which span of words is a variable term. Second, we determine the meaning of the variable term in the study. Third, we ascertain the conceptual meaning of the variable term using the 5W model. In a hypothesis statement, the main relation between two variables is described using typical terms, such as “affect,” “have an effect on,” and “influence.” In addition to the basic relation terms, terms indicating the properties of the relation exist. For instance, “increase” and “positive” indicate whether the relation is positive or negative. The test results of relations cannot be detected from hypothesis statements. This information is rather provided in result statements in the results section of a publication. Most result statements contain an ID. By matching the ID, we can link the result statement with its corresponding hypothesis statement. A result statement such as “H2a is hence supported” does not typically contain variable and relation information. Therefore, it is more effective to link hypothesis and result statements through the ID than through variable terms. The most important information in the test result is whether the hypothesis statement is supported. Typically, this information is indicated by terms such as “is rejected,” “is supported,” and “not significant” in the result sentence. The relation can also be partially supported, that is, more than one group of data is tested for the relation, and mixed results are obtained. The result sentence also provides the confirmed polarity of the relation, such as whether the relation is positive or negative, using relevant terms. III. Extraction Framework How to extract the information included in the data model from unstructured publications and statements is a challenging problem. To the best of our knowledge, no method of domain knowledge graph construction from scientific publications can be directly applied to our problem of synthesizing the core concepts and relations in social media publications. Therefore, we devised a new extraction framework consisting of seven extraction steps to extract the six kinds of information with NLP techniques. First, we extracted variable terms, relations, and concepts from the hypothesis statements (steps 1-4): 1. Extract hypothesis statements from each research publication. 2. Extract two phrases that represent the variable terms and the relation between the two variable terms from a hypothesis statement. 3. Extract the ID and polarity of the relation from a hypothesis statement. 4. Extract the concept label of each variable term. Build a hierarchy of the concepts. Second, we extracted result information for the hypothesis statements (steps 5-7): 5. Extract result sentences from each research publication. 6. Extract the IDs to match corresponding hypothesis statements and results—whether the hypothesis statement is supported, partially supported, or not supported—from result statements. 7. Extract the polarity of the relation from each supported hypothesis statement. We finally matched the hypothesis statements and their results according to the IDs (#15).

11505119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505119.value: Synthesizing concepts and relations is a fundamental task to enhance the understanding of the concept and relation knowledge in a research area. Accomplishing this task can help us detect hidden relations between concepts and evaluate publications’ contributions to the overall knowledge in an area. In this study, we employed a knowledge graph approach to synthesize and evaluate the concepts and relation knowledge on social media in social science publications. In particular, we extracted concepts and relations studied in more than 2,000 social science publications on the topic of social media (#15). Many new insights have been detected from the extracted results. (1) The extracted results indicate “whom/user” is the one of 5Ws has been studied the most times in publications. Besides, the most hypothesized relations are between “whom/user” and “whom/user” instead of other pairs of Ws in the 5W model. (2) The extracted results indicate that the number of hypotheses on the relations between concepts proposed each year increases. However, the number of new concepts proposed each year decreases most times. The number of new relations (both hypothesized and confirmed) firstly increases, then remains unchanged, and finally decreases. (3) The extracted results indicate that the average number of new concepts proposed by each publication decreases from 0.65 to 0.04 concepts and the average number of new relations decreases from 2.06 to 0.61 relations. This indicates that the contribution of each publication decreases in terms of the proposed new concepts and relations. We further applied the methods and algorithms developed and tested in the project to all aspects of the 5W model for social media, including Who-communicator (e.g., #7, #9), Whom-user (#1, #8, #13, #14), What-content (#3, #4), Which-channel (#2, #6, #11), and What-effects (#5, #10, #12).

11505119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505119.value: The current knowledge-graph based approach to literature review can be generalized to other domains of marketing communication research, such as advertising research, health communication research, and political communication. We integrate data model (knowledge graph), data source (information on hypothesis statements in publications), and extraction models (NLP). The information our approach aims to extract is the concepts and their relations, which is also core information in other domains of communication research. The data sources of our approach, the hypothesis statements and corresponding test results, also exist in publications in other marketing/communication domains. The information extraction steps are also generalizable and our extraction models are applicable. An adaptation should be made to build a new concept tree for a new domain in Step 4. Besides, a publication typically provides explications of concepts and theoretical explanations of proposed relations among concepts. However, these explanations and arguments are hidden in the unstructured text. Extracting the explanation and argument structure to enrich the theoretical background of the extracted relation is an important and interesting problem for future work. We plan to identify the argument structure in the theoretical explanations in publications and employ NLP reasoning models to learn and extract the arguments.

11505119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505119.value: How to synthesize existing research, identify new insights, and evaluate research quality are core challenges for marketing communication. Manual review methods allow detailed analysis but are confined to small sets of documents. Computational methods such as topic modeling can review large numbers of publications, but the results are superficial. Complex but essential information, such as the concept meaning and the relations among concepts, cannot be synthesized. Hence, we develop a novel literature review method, which leverages recent advances in knowledge graph construction and information extraction to synthesize the concept and their relations studied in a large number of publications in a research area. The approach consists of a knowledge graph data model to represent the concepts and relations, a data source of hypothesis statements in publications to provide them, and an extraction framework of seven deep learning models to extract them. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by extracting concepts and relations studied in more than 2,000 social science publications on the topic of social media. New insights, such as which relations between concepts are hypothesized or confirmed the most times in publications and how the relations accumulate with time, can be detected from the extracted results.

11505219.label: Project Objectives
11505219.value: Given the historical data containing both sales and ordering decisions, we will investigate the convergence and structural properties of a myopic policy based on the Kaplan-Meier Estimator and propose a stochastic gradient descent and its variants on bootstrapped data to learn the optimal solution for ordering decisions. We will develop algorithms for estimating the primary demands of multiple partially substitutable products from point-of-sale data. 11505219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505219.value: Motivated by consulting experience in a supermarket, we propose to tackle the repeated newsvendor problem with stockout-based substitution or multiple partially substitutable products. A retailer orders, receives and sells an assortment of product category daily and disposes of any leftover stock at store closing. The firm is challenged by the inaccurate demand information of each product, as stockout of one product would cause substitution with one or more other products. As a result, the demand for a product may not only be censored but also possibly be inflated by other products that have run out of stock during the day. Likewise, the stockout of one product can not only cause censoring of its own demand but also distort demands for its substitutable products. Hence, observed sales are not true demand. Although stockout-caused substitution has been well documented, only a few procedures have been proposed for demand estimation and optimal ordering decisions. This project aims to contribute to both the literature and practice by developing a set of computational methods to achieve demand estimation and optimal ordering decisions. 1) Aggregating the sales transaction data into daily sales data, we will consider a repeated newsvendor problem with a data-driven approach. More specifically, given the historical data containing both sales and ordering decisions, we will adopt a myopic policy based on the Kaplan-Meier Estimator. We then propose to run a stochastic gradient descent with multiple starting points on bootstrapped data to ``learn" the optimal (or near-optimal) solution for ordering decisions. Bounds will be developed and convergency rates will be derived. 2) We will develop algorithms for estimating the primary demands of multiple partially substitutable products from sales transaction (point-of-sale, POS) data. This part of the research serves two purposes: to assess how each of the existing and proposed estimation algorithms perform, and to evaluate existing and to derive new heuristic/optimal algorithms for ordering decisions. Departing from the models in the literature, we allow for an arriving customer to purchase a set of products in one or more units for each, based on which an efficient procedure will be developed for solving the order quantities of multiple partially substitutable products. These models and methods will be calibrated using simulated and sales data, and insights and computational procedures will be developed toward actual implementation. 通過超市的諮詢經驗，我們建議基於缺貨的替代或多個部分可替代產品來解決可重複的報童問題。具體來說，零售商每天訂購，接收和銷售多種產品，然後在收工時處理任何剩餘庫存。由於一種產品的缺貨會導致一種或多種其他產品的替代， 公司面臨需求信息不准確的挑戰：每種產品的需求可能被其他在同日缺貨的產品所誇大；同樣，其缺貨不僅會導致對其自身需求的數據刪失，還會導致其可替代產品的需求扭曲。因此，觀察到的銷售並非真正的需求。儘管我們可以看到很多研究缺貨導致替代的成果，但甚少研究成果可以作為需求估算和最佳訂貨決策的解決方案。 該項目旨在通過開發一套需求模型和計算方法來實現需求估算和最優訂貨決策，從而為文獻和實踐做出貢獻。具體來說，1）將銷售交易數據匯總到每日銷售數據中，我們將研究運用數據驅動方法來解決重可複報童問題。更具體的說，利用包含銷售和訂購決策的歷史數據，我們將採用基於Kaplan-Meier Estimator的“近視策略”和啟發式解決方案來選擇訂購決策。然後，我們建議在“自舉”（bootstrapped）數據上運行具有多個起點的隨機梯度下降，以“學習”最優解。且將開發上限並獲得收斂率。 2）我們將開髮用於從銷售交易（銷售點，POS）數據，估計多個部分可替代產品的基本需求的算法。該部分實現兩個目的：第一個是利用數據評估現有和將提出的估算算法。第二個目的是評估現有的和推導出用於訂貨決策的新啟發式算法。 這些模型和方法將通過銷售數據進行核實，並且取得有益的管理領悟及實際實施的計算方案。

11505219.label: Realisation of objectives
11505219.value: 1. Given the historical data containing both sales and ordering decisions, we are able to estimate the base demand and substitution probabilities. Moreover, the structural properties of a myopic policy based on the Kaplan-Meier Estimator and the convergence of the estimator have been developed. We also proposed a search method to obtain the optimal solution for ordering decisions from the data. In particular, we consider the case where unsatisfied demands due to stockout translate into a request for the other product at a probability. Besides the already complex multi-product inventory management problem involving substitutions, we face further challenges in the absence of knowledge regarding demand distributions and substitution probabilities. In their stead, all we can rely on are the historical sales data that are compromised by censoring and substitution effects. We develop a method that carefully screens the data and subjects the useful portion to a Kaplan--Meier type of estimation. Notably, a very effective estimation of the substitution probabilities is also developed. Using large deviation tools, we establish guaranteed convergence rates of our estimates on top of consistency. The precision in parameter estimates also translates into accuracy in replenishment decisions. For inventory management, we take advantage of a submodularity property to obtain an exact algorithm for the two-product case and a good heuristic for the general multi-product problem. 2. We have developed two algorithms for estimating the base demands of multiple partially substitutable products from point-of-sale data. The work belongs to the area of offline learning. 3. Based on simulated and real data, we assessed existing and proposed algorithms for demand estimation and ordering decisions and gained several insights into their relative strengths and applicability of our method. Computational studies based on simulated and actual data confirm the merits of our approach.

11505219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505219.value: Motivated by our experience from consulting with a European grocery chain, we investigate a retailer's multi-product inventory system where customers randomly seek acceptable substitutes if their initial requests are not satisfied. If the substitute is also unavailable, the sales request is lost. Besides the already complex multi-product inventory management problem involving substitutions, we face further challenges in the absence of knowledge regarding base demand distributions and substitution probabilities. In their stead, all we can rely on are historical sales data that are compromised by censoring and substitution effects. We develop a method that carefully screens the data and subjects the useful portion to a Kaplan--Meier type of estimation. Notably, a very effective estimation of the substitution probabilities is also developed. Using large deviation tools, we establish guaranteed convergence rates of our estimates on top of consistency. The precision in parameter estimates also translates into accuracy in replenishment decisions. For inventory management, we take advantage of a submodularity property to obtain an exact algorithm for the two-product case and a good heuristic for the general multi-product problem. Computational studies based on simulated and actual data confirm the merits of our approach. The algorithm can easily be implemented.

11505219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505219.value: Further investigations may attempt the extension of results such as finding a more promising optimization algorithm for the multi-product problem and applying our KM-based estimation methods relying on only weak censoring indicators to other inventory problems with complex structures. The data-driven research approach in this project also inspired me to explore other related problems under a data-driven framework; as a result, in fact, two new GRF projects adopting data-driven methodologies were further funded in 2020-21 and 2022-23 GRF exercises.

11505219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505219.value: The project was motivated by our experience from consulting with a European grocery chain. The retailer has several hundred stores, supplied with breads by a supplier with ten bakeries. Each store in the supermarket chain places and receives orders for about 30 different types of fresh bread before the store opens, and scraps any remaining stock at the end of the day. The management of the supermarket believes the loss of profit due to lost sales and leftovers to be substantial. The firm faces inaccurate demand information for each stock-keeping unit (SKU), as the stockout of one SKU induces its own demand censoring and substitution demand to one or more other SKUs. Some of the sales for a SKU might originate from other products that have run out of stock. In other words, observed sales are not true demand. In this project, the team investigate a multi-product system where customers randomly seek acceptable substitutes if their initial requests are not satisfied. We develop a method that carefully screens the data and effectively estimates the substitution probabilities. Based on such demand estimation, we have developed a good algorithm. Computational studies based on simulated and actual data confirm the merits of our approach.

11505319.label: Project Title(Chinese)
11505319.value: 異質性和商品與股票的相關性，波動性：理論與估計

11505319.label: Project Objectives
11505319.value: One of the main objectives of this project is to develop a tractable, equilibrium asset pricing model with three asset classes: equity, commodity, and bonds. The model has potentials to explain the joint dynamics of all three asset classes. We build our model in a continuous-time framework in which many powerful techniques to solve and estimate dynamic models are well-developed in the literature of term structure models. Based on the theoretical model developed, rigorous estimation and empirical analyses will be conducted. The full-fledged estimation enables us to assess the model's performance in explaining empirical data fully. This, in turn, enables us to investigate and interpret historical price dynamics through the lens of our model such that we can gain a deeper understanding of the economic forces that drive price dynamics. Our empirical exercises also yield the model-implied realization of the state variables, investors beliefs. Thus, we can investigate the characteristics of the dynamics of the beliefs, e.g., whether and to what extent macroeconomic variables can explain them. The equilibrium commodity futures prices have stochastic convenience yield curves that depend on the dynamics of investor beliefs and wealth distribution. We will study the implications of heterogeneity on the convenience yield and compare our results with the ones in the traditional approach, such as Casassus and Colin-Dufresne (2005).

11505319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505319.value: The stability of commodities prices has profound economic and political implications. The dramatic boom/bust of commodity prices in the past decade has fostered a belief among policymakers and market observers that excessive speculation in commodity futures is a major cause for the dramatic changes in commodity prices. With the rise of commodity prices, we observe a huge inflow of funds invested in commodity futures by the institutional investors. Several influential empirical studies, such as Singleton (2014) and Tang and Xiong (2012), support this hypothesis. Other empirical studies, such as Hamilton and Wu (2015) and Janzen, Smith and Carter (2018), have found that this hypothesis has little support in the data. This highlights the difficulty in addressing this question in a purely empirical exercise or a partial equilibrium framework. On the other hand, a deeper question would be what are the determinant factors that drive the dynamics of commodity and commodity futures prices. We intend to address this question in a full equilibrium model. Households in our model are both investors and speculators due to their different beliefs or models to interpret public information. Also, they also have different time discount rates. Thus, the dynamics of asset prices, including commodity and commodity futures prices, are driven by beliefs and wealth distribution of households. Our model yields closed-form solutions for prices, including stock, commodities and commodity futures, and bonds, and their dynamics. This enables us to take the model to the data with full cross-sectional asset prices of all the three asset classes. This should yield deeper economic insights into the behavior of asset prices. Specifically, our model prices and their return variance-covariance are directly linked to preference parameters and beliefs and hence enable us to study and understand the time-varying comovements among equity, commodity prices. The excess comovement among commodities is a long-standing puzzle in the literature, as documented in Pindyck and Rotemberg (1990). The equity-commodity and commodity-commodity correlations increase dramatically and are time-varying as documented in Tang and Xiong (2012). Our project will shed light on the driving forces behind these time-varying comovements and volatilities. 商品價格的穩定具有深遠的經濟和政治影響。過去十年商品價格的急劇上漲/下跌已經促使政策制定者和市場觀察人士相信商品期貨的過度投機是商品價格劇烈變化的主要原因。隨著商品價格的上漲，我們觀察到機構投資者投入商品期貨的資金大量流入。一些有影響力的實證研究，如Singleton（2014）和Tang and Xiong（2012），支持這一假設。其他實證研究，如Hamilton和Wu（2015）以及Janzen，Smith和Carter（2018），已經發現這一假設在數據中幾乎沒有支持。這突出了在純粹的經驗練習或部分均衡框架中解決這個問題的困難。另一方面，更深層次的問題是什麼是推動商品和商品期貨價格動態的決定性因素。 我們打算在完全均衡模型中解決這個問題。我們模型中的家庭既是投資者又是投機者，因為他們對公共信息的解釋信念或模式不同。此外，他們也有不同的時間折扣率。因此，資產價格的動態，包括商品和商品期貨價格，是由家庭的信念和財富分配驅動的。我們的模型為價格提供封閉形式的解決方案，包括股票，商品和商品期貨，債券及其動態。這使我們能夠使用所有三種資產類別的完整橫截面資產價格將模型轉換為數據。這應該會對資產價格的行為產生更深刻的經濟洞察力。

11505319.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505319.value: This project adopts a pure-exchange equilibrium model with a commodity, crude oil, and a generic consumption good. Households are heterogeneous in preferences (time, crude oil, and consumption goods) and beliefs about the growth rates of crude oil and the consumption good supplies. All households observe the supplies with incomplete but symmetric information; they learn different expected growth rates of the supplies based on their own beliefs about how the expected growth rates evolve. When the households’ models of the expected growth rates are different enough, they will never agree. Such households’ estimated growth rates of the fundamentals are generally different. Households have both time and good additive logarithm utilities. Taking the generic consumption good as the numeraire, the prices of stock, the claim to the stream of the consumption good, crude oil, and bonds are the consumption-weighted households’ evaluations. Household heterogeneity in beliefs makes the consumption distributions among households stochastic. Thus, our equilibrium model generates stochastic volatilities and correlation of stock and crude oil, which are functions of the differences in households’ estimated growth rates of the fundamentals, together with the consumption distributions. To estimate, we try to fit asset prices, volatilities, and correlations with data in stock, bond, and oil futures markets over time. In detail, the time-series data include the dividend yield of the S&P 500 index, volatilities and correlation between the prices of 1-month oil futures and the S&P 500 index, the term structures of Treasury yields, convenience yields of oil futures,2 and volatilities of oil futures, all covering six maturities, through 3 and 6 months, 1, 2, 3, 5 years. Compared with methods to match the moments between data and model, our estimation provides estimated state variables that generate the time-varying prices, volatilities, and correlation over time. The model performs very well in fitting the data. It captures the key time-series features of its empirical counterparts. Among the time series that the model tries to match, most of the R2s are well above 90%, with an average of 97%. In addition to capturing the time-series properties of asset prices, volatilities, and correlations, our model also sheds light on the term structures of interest rates, oil convenience yields, and their volatilities, and the relationship between oil volatility and the slopes of the oil futures curve.

11505319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505319.value: In this project, we estimate the model with Treasury bonds, the S&P 500 stock index, crude oil futures, the correlation between the latter two, and the volatilities of the S&P 500 index and crude oil futures prices. The model fits these time series very well with one set of parameters. Thus, it offers explanations and rationales for the observed empirical phenomena, including the time-varying price volatilities, the correlation between stock and crude futures, and the term structure of the convenience yields of the crude futures. Furthermore, the estimated model also generates other empirical regularities regarding the convenience yields of the crude oil futures and relations between the slope of the term structure and the volatilities of the crude oil futures prices. Even though we focus on the stock and crude oil markets in this paper, the model can be easily extended to include other commodities. The correlation dynamics among multiple commodities and between stock and commodities can be studied and understood in an equilibrium framework.

11505319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505319.value: This project explores the effects of households’ heterogeneity on the crude oil, stock, and bond markets in an equilibrium model. The asset prices, volatilities, and correlations admit closed-form solutions. The key parts of all the asset yields can be explained by different weighted averages of the expected growth rates of goods or consumption portions among households, and the time-varying movements of all these volatilities and correlations can be well captured by differences between two certain sorts of weight averages, and all these weights depend on households’ heterogeneous beliefs and preferences. The model estimation shows excellent performance in fitting three markets, including term structures of interest rates and crude oil futures, volatilities, and the correlation between crude oil futures and stock. Our model can explain many empirical regularities, including the time-varying correlation-volatility of oil and stock, decreasing and convex volatility term structure of crude oil futures, and the V-shaped relationship between the futures volatility and the slope of the futures curve.

11505419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11505419.value: Consider a principal who have multiple objects to allocate among a finite number of agents. Each agent values receiving an object and has private information regarding the payoff to the principal of selecting him. The principal can verify an agent' private information at a cost and punish the agent who receives an object by destroying a certain fraction of his surplus. There are no monetary transfers. There are several important economic environments roughly corresponding to this model. The head of personnel for an organization may need to choose several applicants from many applicants to fill multiple jobs with predetermined salaries, and each applicant has private information about his/her ability. A development aid agency may need to allocate multiple grants among several local organizations to serve some beneficiary groups, and each local organization privately knows its management ability. A funding agency may have multiple grants to allocate among several researchers, and each researcher privately knows the intellectual merit of his/her project. In many of these situations, monetary transfers are not practical or not used. In these settings, the principal can verify the agents' private information, but the verification process is often costly. The principal can also punish an agent who makes a false statement, but punishment is severely limited. The head of personnel can monitor an employee's performance and fire him after the probationary period, but cannot ask him to pay back the salary or other employment benefits. The development aid agency can evaluate a recipient's management ability by reviewing its expenditure report and disbar it from future grant application, but cannot recover the funds allocated to the organization. The funding agency can first provide support of a project for an initial specified period of time, then review the project and provide additional support only if the accomplishments achieved warrant further support. In this project, I study the design of optimal mechanisms in the environments described above and the properties of optimal mechanisms. Three earlier papers including one of the PI’s have studied this problem when there is a single object. In this project, instead of considering the allocation of a single object, I would consider a more general environment allowing for multiple and heterogeneous objects. These theoretical exercises would help us understand how some important parameters (e.g., verification cost, sustainability/complementarity between different agents) affect the characteristics of optimal mechanisms and provide guidance for the use of different mechanisms in practice. 一個有多個物品的委託人需要將物品在多個代理人中分配。每個代理人最多需要一個物品。將某一物品分配給一個代理人時委託人獲得的收益是該代理人的私有信息。委託人可以驗證代理人的私有信息，但驗證過程是有成本的。委託人可以通過銷毀一部分的剩餘價值來懲罰一位獲得了物品的代理人。沒有貨幣轉移。 有幾個重要的經濟環境大致對應於這個模型。一個組織可能需要從許多應聘者中選出幾位來填補幾個工資固定的空缺職位，而每個應聘者都有關於他/她的能力的私有信息。一個發展援助機構可能需要在一些當地的機構中分配幾個援助項目，而每個機構都有其管理能力的私有信息。一個研究資助機構可能需要選出幾位研究人員進行資助，而每位研究人員擁有關於他/她的項目的研究價值的私有信息。在許多類似的情況下，貨幣轉移不實用或不被使用。在這些例子中，委託人可以驗證代理的私有信息，但是驗證過程通常成本高昂。委託人也可以懲罰一個對自己的私有信息做出虛假陳述的代理人，但懲罰嚴是有限的。比如，人力資源部可以監控一個員工的表現並在試用期後解僱他，但不能要他歸還試用期間的工資或其他福利。發展援助機構可以通過審查其支出報告來評估一個當地機構的管理能力，並禁止其參與未來的項目申請，但無法收回已分配給該機構的資金。研究資助機構可以對獲得資助的項目進行中期審查，然後根據審查結果決定是否提供進一步的支持。 在這個項目中，我計劃研究上述環境中的最佳分配機制的設計和最佳分配機制的特征。現有的文獻已經研究過類似環境中的單物品分配，在這個項目中我會考慮多物品分配。這些理論研究會幫助我們了解一些重要參數（例如驗證信息的成本，不同代理人之間的替代性/互補性）影響最優機制並為在實踐中使用不同機制提供指導。

11505419.label: Realisation of objectives
11505419.value: The first objective of this project is to study the properties of optimal allocation mechanisms for homogeneous objects. To accomplish this objective, we first characterize the optimal mechanism when distributing r homogeneous objects. The implementation of the optimal mechanism hinges on two thresholds: vl and vu, with vl set lower than vu. Consider a scenario where j agents report values exceeding vl, and j is less than or equal to r-1. In this case, the top j agents, according to their reported values, are chosen and subject to inspection with a certain probability. The remaining r−j items are then allocated at random among the other agents without further inspection. Should the number of agents reporting values above vl exceed r but less than r report values above vu, the r highest agents are selected. These selected agents are then inspected with a specified likelihood. In the event that more than r agents report values higher than vu, r agents from this group are randomly selected, with each being inspected with certainty. The mechanism adapts to the number of participating agents: When the number of agents is small, vu is set to the upper bound of the support of the value distribution. When the number of agents is large, vl = vu. We further investigate the impact of several critical factors on the optimal mechanism, such as the cost of verification, the number of agents participating, and the total number of objects to be allocated. This project's second and third objectives are to design and analyze the properties of optimal mechanisms within a matroid framework, with a particular emphasis on a critical real-world application. To achieve these goals, our study concentrated on a particularly relevant matroid context: the planner is constrained by diversity or equity considerations, giving rise to a trade-off between efficiency and diversity. Specifically, we study the allocation of limited ``slots'' (e.g., college spots) by a planner among agents who each desire one slot. Each agent privately knows the value to the planner of assigning one slot to him, which is revealed through their reports. The planner can verify these reports, albeit at a cost. The agents are divided into ``regular'' and ``target'' groups. Two scenarios are examined: ``no investment,'' where the target group's values follow an inferior distribution, and ``investment,'' where they incur higher costs for a similar distribution. The planner aims to allocate slots to the highest-value agents, respecting a distributional constraint that requires a certain fraction of the slots to be allocated to the target group. The constrained efficient mechanism adds a (potentially type-dependent) ``subsidy'' to the values of the target group and sets a threshold. Slots are initially allocated to agents with adjusted values above this threshold. Any unallocated slots are then randomly assigned. Under a stringent distributional constraint, this randomization process favors the target group, creating a ``quota.''

11505419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11505419.value: The project produced two research papers. In the first paper, “Multi-item mechanism design with costly verification and limited punishments” we characterize the optimal mechanism when distributing r homogeneous objects. The mechanism adapts to the number of participating agents. The study also examines how verification costs, agent numbers, and object quantities influence the mechanism. In the second paper, “Optimal allocation with costly verification and distributional constraint,” we study the allocation of limited ``slots'' (e.g., college spots) by a planner among agents who each desire one slot. Each agent privately knows the value to the planner of assigning one slot to him, which is revealed through their reports. The planner can verify these reports, albeit at a cost. The agents are divided into ``regular'' and ``target'' groups. Two scenarios are examined: ``no investment,'' where the target group's values follow an inferior distribution, and ``investment,'' where they incur higher costs for a similar distribution. The planner aims to allocate slots to the highest-value agents, respecting a distributional constraint that requires a certain fraction of the slots to be allocated to the target group. The constrained efficient mechanism adds a (potentially type-dependent) ``subsidy'' to the values of the target group and sets a threshold. Slots are initially allocated to agents with adjusted values above this threshold. Any unallocated slots are then randomly assigned. Under a stringent distributional constraint, this randomization process favors the target group, creating a ``quota.'' These papers were presented at three international conferences (please see part C for details) and seminars at Hong Kong Baptist University and NYU Shanghai. Subsequent journal submissions are planned for refined versions of these studies. The project also supports the doctoral research of LI Tianxiang, who commenced his studies in 2021 and is projected to complete in 2025.

11505419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11505419.value: In the second paper, "Optimal allocation with costly verification and distributional constraint," we address the issue of the enrollment gap by implementing a distributional constraint. In reality, an individual's skills or 'human capital' are shaped by their own investment and effort. However, some groups may opt for lower investment due to higher associated costs, leading to a poorer distribution of skills or abilities. A critical inquiry stemming from our research is identifying ways to close this investment gap, which could, in turn, help narrow the enrollment gap as well.

11505419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11505419.value: This project led to two papers that tackle the challenge of how to give out resources, like college spots, fairly and efficiently. The first paper lays out the best way to distribute multiple homogenous items when everyone's claims can be checked, which costs time and money. The second paper looked at how to hand out limited spots when we also want to make sure that certain groups, who usually have fewer opportunities, get a fair share. We show that adding a subsidy to these groups helps ensure that spots go to those who'll benefit the most while still meeting goals for diversity. This paper is particularly valuable for understanding and improving policies aimed at providing equal opportunities to everyone, regardless of their backgrounds or circumstances.

11506819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11506819.value: Behavioral research suggests that consumers’ valuation for a product in a choice set may change with the configuration of the choice set within which the product is embedded. Their preference between options is often dependent of the presence or absence of other available options in the choice set and/or other reference context. When consumers think in context with choice-set dependent preferences, how should a firm position a product line to segment and discriminate consumers who have heterogeneous valuations for quality? Should all of the available options be introduced simultaneously or sequentially? Given that simultaneous and sequential introductions have distinct implied choice-set configurations for each time period, how does context-dependent choice affect the inefficiency caused by the cannibalization problem associated with selling multiple quality-differentiated products? Based on the traditional analysis of optimal product line design problem, the proposed study aims to develop a context-dependent model to address the above questions. In particular, by combining the intrinsic consumption utility (absolute valuation) and the gain-loss utility (comparative valuation) into the overall utility, the new preference structure of the proposed model is better grounded in psychological facts. This new structure will allow us to investigate a broader range of scenarios which are more consistent with empirically supported explanations of consumer choice. Hence, the results and findings of the proposed research will provide a more accurate guidance and comprehensive insights which are valuable for efficient management of product lines. 行為學研究顯示，消費者對產品的估值可能會隨著產品嵌入的選擇集的配置而改變。他們在選項之間的偏好通常取決於選擇集中所存在的其他選項。當消費者存在對比選項引發得失感的情況下，企業該如何定位產品線下的產品質量以區隔具有不同質量評估的消費者？所有產品該被同時還是依序地推出市場？價格該如何制定？根據最優產品線設計的傳統問題，我們計畫提出一個經濟模型來分析和回答上述問題。由於所提出的模型將內在消費效用（絕對估值）和得失效用（比較估值）結合到整體效用中，所得出的偏好結構將比傳統方法更能實際的描述消費心理。這種新結構將使我們能夠研究更廣泛的情境。因此，擬議研究的結果和發現將提供更準確的決策指南，幫助企業更有效的管理産品競食問題。

11506819.label: Realisation of objectives
11506819.value: To achieve Objective 1, a parsimonious analytical model that incorporates pertinent behavioral parameters into the traditional utility functions was developed to capture consumers' choice-set dependent behavior and the cannibalization problem. The model assumes that consumers differ in their quality preferences and self-select among the quality-differentiated products of the same generic type introduced by the firm. To center our analysis on the effects of choice-set dependent preferences on cannibalization, we abstracted away the role of other factors (e.g., competition, channel intermediacy structure, and production economy scale). Similarly, to focus on the role of choice-set dependent behavior on the optimal timing of product introduction, the effects of entry timing, network externality, expanding market installed base, and technology improvements were ignored. As such, the theoretical framework of our model incorporates the fundamental forces that shape the cannibalization problem of a product line, making it possible to generate relevant managerial implications for business practitioners. To achieve Objective 2, the developed analytical model was applied to explore the impact of consumers' context-dependent preferences on the cannibalization problem. As consumers’ sensations towards gains and losses with respect to a reference point may vary across different product types or consumer segments, we defined certain scenarios which are more consistent with empirically supported explanations of consumer choice. For each scenario, we explored how product cannibalization, discrimination profits, and social welfare are influenced by consumers’ context-dependent choice behavior. In addition, we defined the concept of discrimination inefficiency to explore how such inefficiency is affected by context-dependent preferences. To achieve Objective 3, the most effective quality and pricing strategies which alleviate the cannibalization problem associated with selling a product line were derived by solving the multiproduct firm’s profit-optimization problem under each possible choice behavior in the presence of context-dependent preferences. To achieve Objective 4, we investigated whether firms should introduce the differentiated products simultaneously or sequentially by modeling the problem where the firm must balance the tradeoff between the undiscounted profits with inefficient quality and the discounted profits with efficient quality. This tradeoff hinges on how consumers make their decisions based on their consumption and context-dependent utilities. Under the scenario where the products are introduced sequentially, we analyzed both the case where the firm’s commitment to future product quality and price is possible and the case where the commitment is impossible. For each case, consumers’ gain-seeking and loss-aversion behaviors were respectively considered and examined. Objective 4 is underachieved mainly because that for the case where the firm’s pre-commitment to future product quality and price is possible, the corresponding mathematical model is more intricate than expected, especially when consumers are strategic instead of reactive. Accordingly, the analytical results are too sophisticated to be desirable in terms of exposition. To overcome the issue, attempts to come up with a creative way to more succinctly present the results or to simplify the analysis are being made.

11506819.label: Major findings and research outcome
11506819.value: The notable findings of this study are summarized below: • Depending on whether consumers are gain seeking or loss averse, their context-dependent preferences have distinct impacts on the cannibalization problem. In general, gain-seeking psychology alleviates the cannibalization problem, whereas loss-aversion psychology typically makes worse the problem. • Gain-seeking psychology facilitates the firm's ability to discriminate among heterogeneous consumers. The firm can benefit from introducing a low-quality product, which is otherwise unprofitable in the absence of context-dependent preferences. This leads to a socially beneficial outcome where both the firm and consumers are better off. On the other hand, loss-aversion psychology inhibits the firm's ability to discriminate, upsetting its profitability. • It is always optimal for the firm to introduce the differentiated products sequentially in the absence of context-dependent preferences. However, when consumers are strategic and are sufficiently sensitive toward losses, sequential product introduction is undesirable. • When consumers are reactive with a weak loss sensitivity, it is optimal to release the differentiated products sequentially regardless of the firm's commitment ability.

11506819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11506819.value: This study only considers the case where the multiproduct firm is a monopolist. The theoretical framework of our model can be extended to explore additional insights for the cases where competition enters the picture. Also, it would be valuable to conduct empirical studies to verify the major results of this study regarding the effects of context-dependent choice behavior on the product cannibalization problem and the optimal timing of product introduction.

11506819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11506819.value: This research contributes to the growing body of research that adopts a behavioral economic paradigm to explore implications for marketing phenomenon. Specifically, behavioral research suggests that consumers’ preference between product options is often dependent of the presence or absence of other available options in the choice set and other reference context. This study investigates the impact of such a context-dependent choice behavior on the cannibalization problem associated with selling differentiated products in a product line. Briefly, the cannibalization problem occurs when a low-end product takes away the demand of a high-end product. It hampers a multiproduct firm’s ability to discriminate heterogeneous consumers, hurting its profitability. To remedy the challenging problem, the literature has established guidance on how quality-differentiated products should be designed and priced. However, the traditional models often ignore behavioral factors; the corresponding suggestions are thus incomplete at best and misleading at worst. Incorporating the results from the pertinent behavioral research into the traditional analysis of optimal product line design problem, the context-dependent model developed in this study is better grounded in psychological facts. It allows us to provide a more comprehensive insights and implications, which are valuable for efficient management of product lines.

11507219.value: 香港證券及期貨事務監察委員會（證監會）於二零一八年三月二十八日公佈有關證監會有關提供自動機器人顧問建議的指引，因為有越來越多的機器人顧問被派往香港各個金融機構。例如，在香港證券交易所上市的雲峰金融集團在2017年推出了第一個名為“優玉”的機器人顧問，他可以幫助個人投資者以更低的成本更有效地管理他們的全球資產。此外，Magnum Research推出了名為AQUMON的機器人顧問，在香港市場管理200只交易所交易基金（ETF）。而8-Securities部署其名為Chole的機器人顧問以支持其電子交易平台。 在國內，到2020年，機器人管理的資產預計將達到6萬億元。而螞蟻金融，招商銀行，工商銀行等積極參與者都已開發了他們的機器人顧問。 雖然機器人顧問是金融科技（Fintech）領域的熱門話題之一，但機器人顧問的設計仍處於嬰兒階段。現有機器人顧問的功能相對有限。例如，這些機器人顧問無法檢測並響應用戶的情緒反饋，而人類顧問則會這樣做。對於真正聰明的機器人顧問而言，必須對其用戶的情緒敏感，以便提供“合適的”建議。例如，如果沒有經驗的客戶表現出強烈的“恐懼”水平，並要求她的機器人顧問出售大量股票，真正聰明的機器人顧問應該認識到這種情緒並在客戶做出突然的投資決定之前提醒其客戶冷靜下來。事實上，根據香港證監會於2017年5月發布的提供網上分銷及諮詢平台的建議指引，機器人顧問應考慮客戶的具體個人情況，提出“適當”的建議。 到目前為止很少有關於智能機器人顧問的文章發表，而關於情緒敏感的機器人顧問的文章更少。 雖然深度學習是核心人工智能（AI）方法之一，有望用於開發機器人顧問的多模態情感檢測模塊，但它需要大量手動標記的示例來訓練深度神經網絡以進行多模態情感檢測。 而且，訓練深度神經網絡非常耗時。 對於實際情感敏感的機器人顧問的設計，我們必須解決這些基本問題。 在設計科學研究方法的指導下，擬議的GRF項目能夠通過開發一種新的生成性深度學習框架來填補上述研究空白，以便開發更有效的半監督深度網絡培訓，以促進開發多模式情緒敏感機器人顧問的情緒檢測模塊。 在香港行政長官2018年施政報告的前言中，我們的香港行政長官明確表示，“從提升我們作為金融中心的地位，包括上市規則的修訂和金融技術的應用（金融科技），以促進發展 創新和技術（I＆T），如人工智能和機器人技術的建立，......“。 擬議的研究項目在戰略上與香港政府利用人工智能，金融科技和機器人技術以增強香港作為國際金融中心的吸引力保持一致。 為了確保帶來商業和社會影響，我們計劃通過我們的工業合作夥伴進行技術轉讓。

11507219.label: Realisation of objectives
11507219.value: Objective 1: We have developed a novel generative adversarial network for unsupervised multimodal feature extraction and semi-supervised labeled training example generation to enhance multimodal emotion detection in robo-advisors (chatbots). In particular, we leverage transfer learning in the proposed generative adversarial network. The refined generative adversarial network (GLS-DCGAN) is separated into shared generator/discriminator, and domain-specific generator/discriminator. The generic emotion features that are learnt from source domains can be transferred to the domain-specific generator/discriminator via improved transfer learning. The original project objective-1 is completely achieved. Objective 2: We have developed a novel deep topical neural network (DTNN) for semi-supervised emotion feature extraction from texts to enhance the text-based interface of robo-advisors (chatbots). As it is computationally expensive to incorporate semantics (e.g., topical representations) in deep neural networks, we also enhance the novel parallel Gibbs sampling method to alleviate such a computational bottleneck by using an approximate generation process. Through a data augmentation process, semi-supervised training process for the proposed topical network is enhanced. The original project objective-2 is completely achieved. Objective 3: Since it is computationally expensive to train deep neural networks for multimodal emotion feature learning and classification, we improve the parallel Gibbs sampling algorithm to improve both the effectiveness and efficiency in network training of robo-advisors (chatbots). In particular, the proposed Gibbs sampling algorithm consists of a parallel stochastic gradient descent mechanism (PSGD) that can speed up the search of near optimal model parameters in deep neural networks. The original project objective-3 is completely achieved. Objective 4: We have developed a prototype of generative deep neural network enhanced by parallel Gibbs sampling algorithm for multimodal feature extraction and detection in robo-advisors (chatbots). 11507219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507219.value: The main research findings and outcomes of this GRF project are shown as follows: (1) A generative adversarial network for unsupervised multimodal feature extraction and semi-supervised labeled training example generation to enhance multimodal emotion detection in robo-advisors (chatbots) is developed. (2) A novel deep topical neural network (DTNN) for semi-supervised emotion feature extraction from texts to enhance the text-based interface of robo-advisors (chatbots) is developed. (3) Since it is computationally expensive to train deep neural networks for multimodal emotion feature learning and classification, a novel parallel Gibbs sampling algorithm underpinned by a parallel stochastic gradient descent (PSGD) mechanism is developed to improve both the effectiveness and efficiency in network training of robo-advisors (chatbots). (4) A prototype of generative deep neural network enhanced by parallel Gibbs sampling algorithm for multimodal feature extraction and detection in robo-advisors (chatbots) is implemented. Both the efficiency and the effectiveness of the prototype system have been evaluated through a series of controlled experiments and a field test involving real-world users. The results of our controlled experiments and field test confirm the merits of the propsoed model.

11507219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507219.value: Although the proposed models has been implemented in our prototype system, and evaluated via controlled experiments and a field test, further software engineering work is required to upgrade the prototype system so that it matches the reliability and the efficacy standard of the industry. In other words, some more fine-tuning work is required to complete the technology transfer part of this project.

11507219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507219.value: There have been very few published articles about the design of intelligent robo-advisors (chatbots), not to say emotion-sensitive robo-advisors. Though deep learning, one of the core artificial intelligence (AI) methods, is promising for developing the multimodal emotion detection modules of robo-advisors, it requires a large number of manually labeled examples to train deep neural networks for multimodal emotion detection. Moreover, it is extremely time-consuming to train deep neural networks. For the design of practical emotion-sensitive robo-advisors, we must address these fundamental problems. Guided by the Design Science research methodology, this GRF project has filled the aforementioned research gaps by developing a novel generative deep learning framework for a more efficient and more effective semi-supervised deep network training to facilitate the practical development of the multimodal emotion detection module of emotion-sensitive robo-advisors.

11507419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11507419.value: Virtual teams have been increasingly employed by organizations [39][30] for their potential to generate creative ideas (i.e., team creativity), instrumental for organizations to survive and innovate in a competitive world [41]. Team creativity essentially entails that a team connects and synthesizes different elements of knowledge that the team members have [36]. Thus, the process that synthesizes multiple members’ contributing inputs [36] [41], which we refer to as convergence process in our study, is also critical for team creativity development. Unfortunately, we still lack a complete understanding of the nature of the corresponding convergence process in virtual teams [30] and how such convergence can be enhanced. Thus, the first aim of this research is to better understand the convergence processes for creativity development and how it affects team creativity in virtual teams. In distributed teams, members rely heavily or even exclusively on various collaboration technologies (CTs) to perform tasks [29]. Ideally, the CTs are supposed to address the aforementioned challenges, which has been the aim of CT designers [25][92]. Whether various CTs are indeed functional at addressing these challenges and thus beneficial in facilitating the convergence process is an important question to answer for both CT designers and users. However, while CTs have been extensively examined in the team literature [5][23][92], some with focus on creativity-related behaviors such as brainstorming [46] , we know little about how CTs can be used to improve the convergence process. Thus, the third research question is how CT can influence the convergence processes for team creativity development in workplace. To address these research questions, we first leverage the most recent theoretical development in team creativity research, namely the creative synthesis perspective [36], as the theoretical lens to understand the critical convergence process in virtual teams. Then, building on this perspective, we incorporate team knowledge diversity to examine how diversity will influence the relationships between creative synthesis and team creativity. Finally, we identify how CT use could affect the creative synthesis processes by consolidating the existing IS literature on CT. This research intends to contribute to the literature, particularly virtual team creativity, by extending the creative synthesis perspective to examine how creative synthesis affects team creativity in virtual teams under different levels of knowledge diversity. It also intends to contribute by examining how team collective use of collaboration technology features can influence the creative synthesis process underlying team creativity development. 組織越來越多地使用虛擬團隊，因為他們有潛力創造創意（即團隊創造力），有助於組織在競爭激烈的世界中生存和創新。團隊創造力本質上要求團隊連接並綜合團隊成員擁有的不同知識要素。因此，綜合多個成員的知識貢獻的過程，我們在研究中稱之為融合過程，對團隊創造力發展也至關重要。遺憾的是，我們仍然缺乏對虛擬團隊中相應融合過程本質以及如何增強這種融合的完整理解。因此，本研究的目標之一是致力於更好地理解創造力發展的融合過程以及這種過程如何影響虛擬團隊中的團隊創造力。 在分佈式團隊中，成員嚴重依賴或甚至專門依賴各種協作技術（CT）來執行任務[29]。理想情況下，CT應該解決上述挑戰，這是CT設計者的目標。各種CT是否確實能夠解決這些挑戰並因此有利於促進收斂過程是CT設計者和用戶的一個重要問題。然而，雖然CT已在團隊文獻中進行了廣泛的研究，包括側重於與頭腦風暴相關的創造力相關行為，但我們對CT如何用於改善收斂性知之甚少。因此，我們的另一個研究問題是CT如何影響工作場所團隊創造力發展的收斂過程。 為了解決這些研究問題，我們首先利用團隊創造力研究中最新的理論發展，即創造性綜合視角，作為理解虛擬團隊中關鍵收斂過程的理論依據。然後，在此視角的基礎上，我們整合團隊知識多樣性，以研究多樣性如何影響創意綜合與團隊創造力之間的關係。最後，我們通過整合CT現有的IS文獻，確定CT的使用如何影響創造性綜合過程。 本研究旨在通過擴展創意綜合視角來研究虛擬團隊創造力，以研究創造性綜合如何影響不同知識多樣性水平下虛擬團隊中的團隊創造力。同時還計劃通過研究團隊如何集體使用協作技術功能來影響團隊創造力發展的創造性綜合過程。

11507419.label: Realisation of objectives
11507419.value: The first objective is to provide a better understanding of team creativity development in workplace from the creative synthesis perspective. In this project, this objective is fully achieved by conceptualizing team creativity development process as a creative synthesis process in virtual teams. The creative synthesis perspective proposes three crucial aspects to afford a nuanced comprehension of team creativity development – collective attention, similarity building, and enacting ideas. In taking this approach, we formalize creative synthesis process facilitation as a second-order construct reflected by three first-order sub-constructs based on the original theory as developed by Harvey (2014), and offer a contextualized understanding of its impact on team creativity in the specific virtual IT project team context. Through its dimensions of collective attention, similarity building, and enacting ideas, the creative synthesis process offers more insights to the collective creativity development process than other similar concepts, such as expertise integration or elaboration which has been criticized for not being clear about how the process actually unfolds and might manifest (Zahra, Neubaum & Hayton, 2020). The second objective is to develop and empirically test a research model that explains how creative synthesis and knowledge diversity jointly affect team creativity. This objective is fully achieved through the building and testing of an integrated research model that explains how collaboration technology use influences team creativity through the mechanism of creative synthesis process, conditioned at different levels of team knowledge disparity, which is a typical type of team knowledge diversity. The theoretical model was empirically tested using data collected from a leading information and communication technology (ICT) solutions provider in China. The participating corporation offers a wide range of services, including consulting, design, software development, as well as testing and maintaining services for its customers in various industries such as telecommunication, digital finance, intelligent manufacturing, and the Internet. The company has a core value of technology innovation and thus greatly emphasizes creativity and originality in their work. In data collecting, we also developed measurement for the new variables of collective attention, similarity building and enacting ideas. The final sample were 62 virtual IT project teams, consisting of 566 individual team members with 62 team leaders. Empirical analysis using multiple methods largely support the proposed research model. The third objective is to investigate the role of collaboration technology use in affecting the creative synthesis processes. This objective is fully achieved by identifying three sets of collaboration technology features based on team knowledge framework and relating them to the creative synthesis process. Specifically, we extended the team knowledge framework with two dimensions, including awarenss knowledge and long-term knowledge, originally in the context of team coordination to three dimensions by incorporating a new dimension of transitional knowledge after elaborating the context of team creativity. Then, based on the extended team knowedege framework, collaboration technology features are categorized into classes, namely features supporting awareness knowledge, features supporting long-term knowledge and features supporting transitional knowledge. Finally, the three sets of collaboration technology features are proposed to be associated with the creative synthesis process. This proposition is empirically verified with the same dataset in the second objective. The completion of this objective complements the existing literature that has paid little attention to understanding how collaboration technology can promote team creativity by focusing on the use of collaboration technology at the feature level.

11507419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11507419.value: The major findings and research outcome are as follows. First, the creative synthesis process – consisting of collective attention, similarity building, and enacting ideas – significantly and positively affect team creativity in virtual teams. Previous studies have remained silence on the nature of the process for team creativity. We develop and operationalize the novel construct of creative synthesis process as a second-order reflective construct with three sub-constructs of collective attention, similarity building, and enacting ideas, and contextualize the impact of creativity synthesis in the virtual IT project team context, thereby providing subtle insights on team creativity development process at a micro level (Chen & Adamson, 2015). Further, by subjecting the creative synthesis perspective to empirical investigation, this study also makes a novel empirical contribution by developing and validating survey measures on the creative synthesis process, thereby providing future empirical research with useful instruments. Second, the use of the three set features of collaboration technologies, including features supporting awareness knowledge, features supporting long-term knowledge and features supporting transitional knowledge, enhances the team creative synthesis process and ultimately team creativity. Previous studies has merely examined the drivers of creative synthesis, likely due to the novelty of the topic and complexity of the theory. Drawing on the team knowledge literature and our contextualized analysis of team knowledge related to team creativity, this study identifies three sets of collaboration technology features, theorizes their relationships to the creative synthesis process and team creativity, and provides empirical verification. As such, it is among the first to systematically identify the antecedents of the creative synthesis process, specifically from the angle of collaboration technologies. In addition, by identifying collaboration technology feature sets that are theoretically relevant to team creativity, we also opened up the black box of how technologies can exert effect on team processes and outcomes. Third, team knowledge disparity plays a positive moderating role in the relationship between the creative syntheses process and team creativity for virtual IT project teams. Although knowledge disparity is argued to be dysfunctional to team creativity (Harrison and Klein, 2007), we find its value by investigating how it catalyzes the effect of creative synthesis on team creativity, particularly in the virtual IT project team context. In addition, we also find its positive direct effect on team creativity in the same context. This finding adds to our understanding toward the boundary by which knowledge disparity exerts its effect on creativity.

11507419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11507419.value: There are a few directions for future research. The first one is to investigate the dynamic development of creative synthesis and its impact on team creativity over time. In the MIS Quarterly paper, the construct of “creative synthesis process facilitation” is conceptualized as a singular construct, that is reflected by the three sub-constructs of collective attention, similarity building, and enacting ideas. There are underlying mutual influences among the three process facilitation, which is an interesting point that deserves more effort. Future research can more formally examine the underlying iterative nature among the three sub-constructs. Second, the creative synthesis is a comparatively fresh perspective to understand team creativity development. More research can be executed to understand the mechanisms to induce creative synthesis process, such as team composition, leadership and human resource practices. We have conducted a follow-up survey to collect data from teams that are performing tasks related to business analytics and machine learning, aiming to address the aforementioned research opportunities, and are currently at the stage of data analyzing. Based on the data collected, we will analyze 1) the creative synthesis process development over time, and 2) the mechanisms contributing to the enhancement of creative synthesis process.

11507419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11507419.value: Contemporary organizations are increasingly leverage geographically dispersed “virtual” teams to perform innovative tasks as members have access to diversified expertise despite of spatial and temporal limits. Dispersed team members rely heavily, often exclusively, on various collaboration technologies for communication and coordination. However, unfruitful investments in collaboration technologies to support efficient innovative problem-solving has been reported as one of the major reasons for team failure. Therefore, the aim of the project is to understand how collaboration technologies can be used to support the creative collaboration, or team creativity, in virtual teams. To achieve our aim, we first disentangle how collective creativity develops in virtual teams. Then, we categorize the features of collaboration technology in the context of team creativity and relate these features to the team creativity development process, and ultimately to team creativity. The research outcome of this project work will help us to understand in more detail how virtual teams can leverage collaboration technologies to support the creativity development in virtual teams. We anticipate that this will provide guidance on the design and use of collaboration technologies and bring additional values for organizations that have made investments in these technologies treatments.
