11609119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11609119.value: 「偷拍」是一種以隱蔽攝錄器材在公共或私人地點，在當事人不知情，並未得同意下，拍攝女性裙底或胸部的行為。雖然，這種行為是否屬精神病類或犯罪行為尚在討論，有待進一步界定，但其增長情況，不論在香港或世界各地的法律及社會層面均備受關注。與其他性犯罪行為不同，例如：強姦、亂倫或兒童性侵犯等，一般情況下，「偷拍」往往沒有直接身體接觸，對受害人的入侵程度較低，這正為侵犯者帶來不容易被逮捕的假象，忽略行為對受害人帶來的傷害。雖然，這種行為在世界各地開始備受關注，但相關的文獻及實證研究仍然十分缺乏，令社會對這種行為的認知亦非常有限。以往的研究往往把性犯罪行為的成因歸咎於童年的依附關係、社會疏離、孤獨感以及欠缺親密關係等。面對現代社會個人孤獨感日益顯著的情況下，及早就整體性犯罪以及「偷拍」行為與個人孤獨感的關係作深入研究，相信有助預防問題更趨嚴重。 在這背景下，是次研究旨在探討18至34歲男性成年性犯罪者的刻板生活規律，以及個人孤獨感與其「偷拍」行為的關係。研究亦同時比較其他沉溺性犯罪者、非性犯罪者，以及一般社區控制組群的情況，分辨其犯罪的危險及保護因素，並探索性犯罪者開始相關行為、發展、持續、停止以至復康的道路。整個研究包括：量化問卷調查及質化深入訪談。量化問卷調查包括4組男性成年組群，合共600份成功收回的問卷，組群包括：100位「偷拍」行為犯罪者、100位其他沉溺性犯罪者、200位非性犯罪者及200位沒有犯罪紀錄的社區人士。而質化深入訪談則以半結構性個別深入訪談方式，訪問合共80位來自4組男性成年組群，每組20位。是次關於「偷拍」行為的實證研究在華人社區以至全球均屬先鋒，研究結果期望補充相關行為的認知及概念空隙，有助專業人士及早界定、教育及預防，並協助相關人士改過，以及在復康方面提供實證及可行的啟示。

11609119.label: Realisation of objectives
11609119.value: This project lasted for three years from January 2020 to end of December 2022. Coincidently, this period was the critical COVID-19 pandemic outburst worldwide. As the focus of this research project was highly sensitive, data collection no matter for quantitative questionnaire survey or qualitative individual indepth interviews was expected to be extremely difficult even under a usual research environment, let alone with the critical COVID-19 pandemic outburst. As a result, the data collection process and the progress of this research project had also been substantially influenced. To meet the samples of the study, the research team started using online mechanisms as means of data collection both for the quantitative questionnaire survey and the qualitative individual indepth interviews after the prolonged period of pandemic influence. Despite the difficulties encountered, this was an original, pioneering and highly valuable study. According to the NGOs, number of offenders (both sexual and non-sexual) referred by the Probation Officers of the Social Welfare Department or sought help voluntarily were dropped significantly during the pandemic. Therefore, the research team continued the data collection until mid-2023 when all the control measures were released in March 2023. Eventually, except for sexual offenders with clandestine upskirt photography, the number of quantitative and qualitative respondents collected in different target groups were fully met. Qualitatively, expected 20 interviewees from each group of (1) sexual offenders with indecent assault, (2) non-sexual offenders, and (3) non-offending community control group were successfully collected. Only 12 out of 20 expected interviewees could be collected from sexual offenders with clandestine upskirt photography. Quantitatively, 96 out of 100 expected survey respondents were collected from sexual offenders with indecent assault. 200 expected respondents from each group of (1) non-sexual offenders and (2) non-offending community control group could also be met. Only 31 out of 100 expected respondents could be collected from sexual offenders with clandestine upskirt photography. Until this final report, all qualitative and quantitative data collected had also been analyzed intensively for manuscripts preparation. As assessed, the first research objective in examining the relationships of young male adults’ everyday life routinization and sense of loneliness with their offending (sexual – clandestine upskirt photography and other paraphilic sexual offences, and non-sexual) and non-offending behaviours in contemporary Hong Kong society was largely achieved. With between-group bivariate analyses, everyday life routinization and sense of loneliness of all types of offenders (both sexual and non-sexual) were significantly higher and different from the non-offending community control group. When structural equation modelling analyses were carried out using the software IBM SPSS AMOS 29.0, it was interesting to find that sexual offenders’ (both clandestine upskirt photography and other paraphilic sexual offences) life routinization had direct and significant relationship with their sense of loneliness. Sense of loneliness also had direct and significant relationship with their sexual compulsivity. This relationship was significantly mediated by their mental wellness (including anxiety, stress and depression) and sense of self-esteem, and moderated by their meaning in life, while social support had no significant effect in this model. The difference among offenders with clandestine upskirt photography and other paraphilic sexual offences was their sexual compulsivity scores. Other paraphilic sexual offenders had significantly higher sexual compulsivity than those offenders with clandestine upskirt photography. For the community control group, meaning in life had direct and significant relationship with loneliness. This relationship was significantly mediated by their life routinization and moderated by the social support from their parents. Furthermore, loneliness also had direct and significant relationship with their sexual compulsivity. This relationship was significantly mediated by peer influence and moderated by their mental wellness (including anxiety, stress and depression). This was a double mediation and moderation model. The model developed for the non-sexual offenders (such as drug addiction, shop-lifting, fighting, etc.) was similar with the non-offending community control group. The most important difference was that social support from parents of the non-sexual offenders and their mental wellness could not play a part to moderate/buffer the influence of meaning in life and loneliness on their sexual compulsivity. The sexual compulsivity scores of the community control group and those non-sexual offenders were significantly lower than the sexual offenders. The research team was working hard to write up such meaningful quantitative findings and models into manuscripts for publication and sharing in the academic circle. The second and third objectives in investigating young male adults’ pathways onto the offence of clandestine upskirt photography from onset to rehabilitation and the risk and protective factors of the offence were also largely achieved. With the qualitative individual indepth interviews with the pilot and first few cases, the research team had successfully published a journal article in a SSCI journal discussing the risk and protective factors influencing young male adults’ onset and pathway onto the offence of clandestine upskirt photography. The interviewees evaluated that their clandestine upskirt photo-taking behaviour might not only be sexually driven as society expected, but also an emotional reaction to eliminate their sense of loneliness and break through the routinization of their everyday lifestyle. Living in a fast-paced and highly demanding metropolitan city, they felt lost and were unaware of their purpose in life. In contrast, clandestine upskirt photo-taking allowed them to have a sense of control and excitement just like peeling off the secret of a “magic egg”. Although they had strong sense of guilt and self-doubt of their behaviour, the more boring and repetitive their everyday routine was, the stronger was their sense of sexual depression and inner drive to seek life excitement. The qualitative findings were quite consistent with the quantitative results that the sexual compulsivity score of this kind of offenders was not high in comparison with other sexual offenders. The qualitative data collected in this research project for different groups of young male adults were rich and intensive. The findings of this study had widened the existing models of understanding clandestine upskirt photo-taking behaviour and provided new insights to treatment and intervention to the behaviour. Not all people engaged in the behaviour were merely for sexual purposes. It could be an emotional reaction to retrieve their sense of control and life satisfaction to fight against strong sense of loneliness and routinization in their everyday lives. Therefore, treatments that focus on eliminating or redirecting their sex drives might be not enough. Tightening legal sanctions or social control of their behaviour might also not be helpful solving the core problems of their behaviour. Given the experience of the participants and the results of this study, it is important to help them establish meaningful purposes in life amidst their busy and stressful everyday lives. Therefore, meaning-centered approach is suggested for future practice. To have early identification and prevention of the behaviour, curricular-based sexuality education and sexuality counselling services are also suggested by the participants. These meaningful suggestions had also been mentioned in the newspaper article which was published in a local newspaper in end of 2021. Hopefully, the dissemination of this newspaper article could help enhance the general public’s understanding to the behaviour and their care and concern for the needs of these sexual offenders with upskirt photo-taking behaviour. With the new insights developed and the recommendations made, the fourth objective of this study was also largely achieved.

11609119.label: Major findings and research outcome
11609119.value: Quantitatively, young male sexual offenders’ life routinization significantly influenced their sense of loneliness. Their sense of loneliness also significantly influenced their sexual compulsivity. This relationship was significantly mediated by their mental wellness and sense of self-esteem, and moderated by their meaning in life. It means that life routinization and sense of loneliness played important role to influence their sexual compulsivity, while meaning in life could help buffer the influence. The sexual compulsivity score of those offenders with clandestine upskirt photo-taking was lower than other paraphilic sexual offences. These quantitative findings were consistent with the qualitative results obtained through individual indepth interviews. Qualitatively, young male adults’ clandestine upskirt photo-taking behaviour was not merely for the purpose of sexual release as society expected. Living in a fast-paced and highly demanding metropolitan city, their everyday lives were highly routinized with strong sense of loneliness. They felt lost and lack of clear purpose in life. Clandestine upskirt photo-taking allowed them to have a sense of control and excitement to break through their loneliness and everyday life routine. Therefore, treatments that focus on eliminating or redirecting their sex drives were not enough. Tightening legal sanctions or social control as expected might also not be helpful solving the core problems of their behaviour. In contrast, understanding and support from their parents and society and enhancing their purpose in life might be helpful in reducing their chance of engagement in sexual offending behaviour. To have early identification and prevention of the behaviour, curricular-based sexuality education and sexuality counselling services were suggested. The factors influencing non-sexual offenders and the community control group’s sexual behaviour were different from those sexual offenders. The community control group’s meaning in life significantly influenced their sense of loneliness and then influenced their sexual compulsivity. Double mediation and moderation relationships were found among these factors. The relationship between meaning in life and loneliness was mediated by their life routinization and moderated by social support from parents. The relationship between their loneliness and sexual compulsivity was mediated by peer influence and moderated by their mental wellness. Although the influencing factors for those non-sexual offenders were similar, social support from parents and their mental wellness could not buffer the relationships. These results further reviewed the importance of early intervention and early prevention of the problems. It is not easy to get rid of the problems when they started engaging in any sexual or non-sexual offending activities.

11609119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11609119.value: As suggested, to alleviate the sense of emptiness and young male adults’ urge to look for an immediate breakthrough of their everyday life routinization, it is important to help them realize their meaning in life and life direction. Therefore, a meaning-centered approach is suggested as a way of intervention to know themselves and acquire positive and effective means of coping to face with life adversities. Another potential area of research is sexuality education in Hong Kong. Some participants of this study realized that enhanced sexuality education could raise their awareness and prevent them from using sexual offences as coping methods for their sense of loneliness and life routinization. Due to the exam-focused approach, sexuality education is usually insufficient in Hong Kong. Teachers also lack of proper training on sexuality education. Along with this research project, the PI and the research team had worked collaboratively with the two NGOs, which provide professional services for sexual offenders and sexual violence, offering sexuality education progamme for secondary school teachers. In view of information explosion over social media and internet, it is worth offering comprehensive sexuality education in Hong Kong and examining its impact on students’ sexuality knowledge, attitudes and values.

11609119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11609119.value: Clandestine upskirt photography was not a merely sexual offence to fulfill young male adults’ sex drives. It could be an emotional reaction to their strong sense of loneliness and routinization in their everyday lives. Living in a fast-paced and highly demanding metropolitan city, they felt lost and lack of direction and meaning in life. Clandestine upskirt photography could fill this gap of emptiness and allow them to have a sense of control and excitement to break through the everyday routinization. Therefore, more than eliminating or redirecting their sex drives or tightening legal sanctions and social control of their behavior, it is important to help them make sense of their purpose and meaning in life amidst their busy and stressful everyday lives. Social support from parents and mental wellness could buffer the effects of lack of meaning in life and sense of loneliness on young male adults’ sexual compulsivity in the community control group only. This result further reviewed the importance of early intervention and early prevention of the problem. It is not easy to get rid of the problem when they started engaging in offending activities. Curricular-based sexuality education and sexuality counselling services can play a part in the process.

11609219.label: Project Objectives
11609219.value: To survey and portrait the landscape of the second wave of Administrative Litigation under the Opening Government Information Regulations in China (2008-2018). To classify the patterns of administrative litigation, examine the trends in the Opening-Government-Information (OGI) lawsuits and investigate the factors that shape the results of such litigation at the level of individual the case. Who is suing the government? What are the plaintiffs’ chances? What are the key factors that shape the results of such litigation? Which branches of the government and which levels of the government are more likely to be sued? To what extent is suing the state like throwing an egg against a stone? To examine the regional variation of OGI litigation at the provincial level. What are the structural forces that shape the quantity of OGI litigation in each province? How do economic, political and social conditions lead to regional variation in administrative litigation? To scrutinize the court decision processes on the administrative litigation under OGI. We will further articulate the above empirical findings with the reasoning shown in DAD files and the interviews we will conduct on legal, journalistic and academic professionals. To discuss the impact of OGI on Chinese society and to determine how such administrative litigation affects the authoritarian accountability and the evolving state-society relations in China. To disseminate research results through conferences, lectures, academic journal articles and newspaper articles.

11609219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11609219.value: 中國的行政訴訟數十年來引發了激烈的爭論，鑑於此類訴訟的變化反映了不斷發展的國家 - 社會關係和專制治理中不斷變化的意識形態。中國於2007年通過了“政府信息公開條例”（中文版的“信息自由法”）之後，一股新的行政訴訟浪潮發生，政府因信息公開問題一度被起訴。 此類行政訴訟的數量從2008年的308起躍升至2017年的17,174起。該規定現已成為中國法院最常被引用的法律之一。 學界對於政府信息公開法案的評價不一。有人認為該立法是關於行政公開法制建設的里程碑，是中國透明度改革的重要一步。然而，也有學者認為，這種看似民主的措施並不減少國家權力，反而更有可能成為中央政府用來控制地方政府並控制其人民和維持權力的戰略。 這樣的矛盾解釋需要進一步的實證研究。 政府信息公開訴訟數量激增並不意味著起訴國很容易。國家具有控制信息的能力和歷史，行政訴訟法的執行不力，原告難以說服法院接受行政案件。即便訴諸法庭，告贏國家的可能性仍然很低。由於人們普遍認為“官官相護”，大多數人認為起訴中國政府仍就像“以卵擊石”。如此而言，什麼原因激勵個體公民和組織起訴政府呢？他們在法庭的贏率是多少呢？為什麼原告的贏率在不同省份各有不同？這些訴訟案件對於中國信息制度有何影響？ 又揭示了什麼樣的國家 - 社會關係的演變動態和威權主義的本質？ 隨著最近的法律透明度改革，許多法院已經開始向公眾發布他們的判決文書。這些文件形成了一個系統的數據源，揭示了法院判決背後的邏輯，並提供了一個中立的鏡頭，通過它可以觀察社會和政治力量對法院的影響。因此，該研究將採用“大數據”方法收集和分析2008年至2018年行政訴訟案件的判決文書，來回答以上問題。我們首先利用機器學習來分析這些法律文本，以探索每個案例的法律理由。然後，我們將個案與社會結構因素聯繫起來，研究中國公民和組織起訴政府的原因和方式，並研究這種訴訟的地區差異。然後，我們通過深入訪談和案例研究加深我們對信息公開訴訟模式的理解。我們進一步審視國家，法院和媒體之間的互動，並討論此類訴訟對信息制度以及威權主義問責制的影響。

11609219.label: Realisation of objectives
11609219.value: The above six objectives have been achieved, even though encountering several obstacles during the process. The following statements detail the process of achieving these objectives. Objective 1: We collected the OGI-related administrative litigation cases (2008-2018), developed a coding scheme to code the litigation cases, conducted the polit study on the validity and reliability of such coding scheme, and performed both quantitative and qualitative analysis on the data. During this process, we countered an unexcepted challenge: the courts in very levels became more conservative in publicizing their cases due to the change of political atmosphere in China. We had to work around the clock to download all related cases and also cross-checked our data with different sources. Even though there is still a censorship issue, we believe the data we collected are the most comprehensive one on this topic. Objective 2: We first applied machine learning technique to code and collect two sets of measurements, one set on court decisions on the remedies and compensation; and the other on the details of each case. Specific variables for analysis include 1) Court decisions on winning and losing. 2) Characteristics of plaintiffs. 3) Characteristics of defendants. 4) Characteristics of courts. 5) Jurisdiction. 6) Characteristics of the case: the content of the information which is demanded to be disclosed, the length of litigation, the legal reasoning of the cases. 7) Logic of legal reasoning. In addition, we were also able to collect information on the networks of lawyers and judges, which to our knowledge, is the first dataset that contains such rich information on this topic. We then applied a two-level logit model to investigate what factors shaped the individual winning chance when suing the state. Objective 3: To analyse the impacts of structural factors on OGI litigation and the regional variation, we further collected two sets of data from a variety of sources. 1) we aggregated and calculated the OGI litigation rates across provinces (2008 – 2018), based on the data we collected for Objective 1 and 2. 2) Thus we then extracted information on the structural factors – social, economic and political indicators in each province – from Annual Reports on Opening Government Information Works in all 31 Provinces (2008-2018), China Statistical Yearbooks (2008-2018), and related official archives. Each of these independent variables will be selected on the basis of existing literatures as elaborated in the above section. Key variables included - GDP per capita. We collected GDP per capital of 31 provinces from The China Statistical Yearbooks provided annual GDP from 2008 to 2018. - Foreign Direct Investment. We collected each province’s foreign direct investment from The China Statistical Yearbooks and provincial yearbooks from 2008 to 2018. - Characteristics of regional leaders. We collected the personnel information for the three influential political and court leaders in each province – governor, party secretary, and high court leader, from the government and court official websites. Following the existing research on political elites and the authoritarian cadre evaluation system, we will narrow our focus down to four factors: age, education, working experience and their career paths. - Urbanization. The level of urbanization is the percentage of urban residents relative to the total population in each province, as reported in China Statistical Yearbooks. Thus we used this indicator as a proxy to test the impacts of an urban environment on the OGI litigation. In addition, we also included education level, Internet and mobile penetration rate, and age structure of the population in each province as control variables. Objective 4: We further incorporated our big-data analytical approach with the sociological questions on legal documents by proposing an integrated method to scrutinize the court decision processes. We first conducted discourse analysis on some representative cases. We then matched the court reasoning with the legal regulation and then incorporated such reasoning into the supervised machine-learning process to do the text-mining on the court documents. Objective 5: After collecting the quantitative data on OGI litigation cases, we continued to investigate in-depth interviews on the court decision-making process on OGI cases as well as the influence of such cases. We conducted structured interviews with lawyers, journalists, and government officials. Due to the pandemic, we have modified in-person interviews to online meetings and phone conversations. And we also had to reduce the number of interviews. This component of the qualitative analysis has been incorporated into the analysis to explain the patterns we identified through the above quantitative analysis. Objective 6: We published papers and attended conferences. There are more papers to come by the time we submitted this report.

11609219.label: Major findings and research outcome
11609219.value: 1) China went through four stages of Opening Government Information (OGI). In the phase of “experiment” in the late 1980s (the late 1980s – 2000), China piloted openness in government affairs (OGA) in villages. It was not until 2000, when the central government officially endorsed and standardized the “experiment” OGA at the township level, that China established its institutional foundation for opening up government information. The second stage in China’s journey was pushed by the global community (2000 – 2008). When China entered its third phase (2008 – 2019), a top-down diffusion period, those late-comer provinces began to develop their local versions of OGI regulations. China entered the fourth stage (2019 – present) when revising the OGI Regulation in 2019. 2) The project examined 19,076 first-instance OGI cases from 2008 to 2018 and identified four features of China’s OGI litigation cases. First, the total amount of first-instances of OGI-related administrative lawsuits has increased from 26 in 2008 to 4,189 in 2018, with 2013 being the turning point. Second, there was a significant regional variation. Most OGI lawsuits occurred either in more-urbanized provinces or provinces with large populations like Henan and Shandong; while regions in Western China had fewer OGI cases. Third, OGI lawsuits were mainly about housing demolition disputes (30.3%) and land acquisition disputes (36.0%). In other words, more than 60% of OGI lawsuits were directly linked with urbanization. Fourth, however, the winning rate of OGI litigation shows a different pattern. The provinces with more OGI lawsuits had relatively lower winning rates. The average winning rates of OGI litigation in urban areas (29.4%) were much lower than those in rural areas (50.7%). 3) By investigating both individual and structural factors, the project reveals whether and how information transparency can transfer into authoritarian accountability in China. First, information transparency encourages the number of litigation and increases the plaintiffs’ chance to win. However, the authoritarian accountability is more procedural than substantive. Second, urbanization stimulates OGI litigation but decreases the plaintiffs’ winning chance. In addition, for urbanization-related disputes such as house demolishing and land acquisition, urbanization amplifies the positive impacts of transparency on accountability. 4) Our project compiles the first comprehensive dataset on China’s OGI legislation and litigation; and our findings not only offer a nuanced discussion on authoritarian information governance and accountability, which can be applied to other contexts.

11609219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11609219.value: There are several potential developments to nurture future research projects. 1) The theoretical reflection on information transparency and accountability can be further extended into many relevant contexts. For example, some of the outputs have been addressing privacy protection in authoritarian information governance in the context of the public health crisis. Such discussion can be further developed to explore the big-data governance in post-pandemic societies. We continue working on this line and there are two more papers in the pipeline. 2) The proposed big-data analytical approach can be applied to investigate legal documents and media texts in different scenarios. We are polishing this method and trying to apply the method to analyze privacy-related litigation and media reports. 3)The rich data that has been collected for this project, such as the lawyer-judge network, and the law-firm-court network, are novel. To our knowledge, no existing analysis of these two networks on the OGI in China. We are developing a new proposal around the data on these two networks. 4) To include international and comparative analysis. One working-in-progress paper in Part C is to analyze OECD countries' FOI legislation. We are planing to conduct related comparative studies on FOI litigation.

11609219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11609219.value: China’s 2008 national regulation on open government information (OGI) has triggered a new wave of administrative litigation against governments for releasing classified information. Such litigation has invited heated debates, given that the changes in OGI litigation reflect the evolving state-society relations and the changing ideology in authoritarian information governance. This study examined the 19,076 first-instance OGI cases from 2008 to 2018 to explore whether and how information transparency can transfer into authoritarian accountability in China. The project traced the four stages in the trajectory of China’s information transparency, identified the tempo and regional variation of OGI litigation, and examined the factors that shaped the outcomes of the OGI litigation. This project makes at least three contributions. First, we compiled one of the most comprehensive datasets on China’s OGI legislation and litigation, which offers scholars on similar topics valuable data. Second, we proposed a novel approach to integrate sociological thinking into big-data analytics to design a better methodological flow to study legal documents. This method can be applied to many other types of texts and contexts. Third, empirical findings suggest a nuanced theoretical discussion on economic development, information transparency, and government accountability.

11609619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11609619.value: This project examines the role of the US intelligence community (IC) in establishing and perpetuating allied, conservative regimes in Japan and South Korea during the Cold War. It is commonly held that the US played an important role in nurturing key regional allies, Japan and South Korea, through overt support mechanisms centring on security protection and market access in return for cooperating with Washington’s regional geostrategic policies. However, scholars have paid relatively little attention to the contribution of US covert action to nurturing friendly, conservative regimes in both countries. The study compares and contrasts the modalities of the US IC’s involvement in the Japanese and South Korean political processes and evaluates the effectiveness and consequences of this intervention. The timing of the most intense phase of the US intelligence intervention in the Japanese and South Korean political processes is important, occurring during the tumultuous first two decades of the Cold War when conservative dominance was uncertain. The project’s central argument is that, when considered in connection with domestic political actors, among other endogenous factors, the US IC contributed to establishing and stabilising conservative rule. It is therefore necessary to explore the role of conservative elites who actively and eagerly engaged with the US IC in pursuit of their own political and economic interests. The clandestine relationships between the US IC and Japanese and South Korean conservatives helped reinforce both countries’ status as friendly, junior allies of Washington. 暗中培育保守派：美國秘密行動在日本與南韓建立友好政權中擔當的角色 撮要 本研究課題探討冷戰期間美國情報體系在建立及維繫日本和南韓的保守、結盟體制中所擔當的角色。一般的觀點認為，美國極力與日韓發展區域盟友的關係，公開地為日韓提供安全保護和市場准入的支援，籍此換取日韓在華府區域地緣戰略政策上的合作。然而，學者們鮮有關注美國在推動日韓建立友好但保守體制方面的隱蔽行動。本研究比較美國情報體系在參與日韓政治進程時模式的異同，並評估其干預的有效性及影響。美國情報體系對日韓政治進程最密集的干預，正值冷戰期間局勢最動盪的首二十年，這個時間節點非常重要，因為當時兩國的保守政權尚未穩固。本研究的核心論點是，通過考量美國情報體系與日韓政治人物及其他內在因素的關係，該情報體系的確造就了兩國保守主義政權的建立和穩定。因此，我們需要瞭解日韓那些保守派領袖是如何積極懇切地跟美國情報體系打交道，以追求其政治經濟利益。美國情報體系與日韓保守派之間的秘密關係鞏固了華府與兩國之間新建立的盟友關係。 Cultivating Conservatives, Clandestinely: The Role of US Covert Action in Building Friendly Regimes in Japan and South Korea Abstract This project examines the role of the US intelligence community (IC) in establishing and perpetuating allied, conservative regimes in Japan and South Korea during the Cold War. It is commonly held that the US played an important role in nurturing key regional allies, Japan and South Korea, through overt support mechanisms centring on security protection and market access in return for cooperating with Washington’s regional geostrategic policies. However, scholars have paid relatively little attention to the contribution of US covert action to nurturing friendly, conservative regimes in both countries. The study compares and contrasts the modalities of the US IC’s involvement in the Japanese and South Korean political processes and evaluates the effectiveness and consequences of this intervention. The timing of the most intense phase of the US intelligence intervention in the Japanese and South Korean political processes is important, occurring during the tumultuous first two decades of the Cold War when conservative dominance was uncertain. The project’s central argument is that, when considered in connection with domestic political actors, among other endogenous factors, the US IC contributed to establishing and stabilising conservative rule. It is therefore necessary to explore the role of conservative elites who actively and eagerly engaged with the US IC in pursuit of their own political and economic interests. The clandestine relationships between the US IC and Japanese and South Korean conservatives helped reinforce both countries’ status as friendly, junior allies of Washington.

11609619.label: Realisation of objectives
11609619.value: As foreshadowed in the mid-term progress report, we were unfortunately unable to achieve the project's objectives. The Japanese government's highly restrictive border security policies during the Covid-19 pandemic made it impossible to conduct the fieldwork crucial to achieving the project's objectives. While we were generously given extensions because of these challenges, the Japanese government's refusal to change its border security policy meant that we were unable to take advantage of the RGC's magnanimity. Unfortunately, the Japanese government's belated decision to open the country's borders came after the end of the period of the second extension. As a result, we were only able to conduct basic background research for the project and only spent a negligible portion of the budget on secondary data. Needless to say, this whole experience has proven to be extremely frustrating.

11610419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11610419.value: 合成現實(SR)，不論是虛擬現實或增強現實，都結合了真實和虛擬的元素，為用家提供了第一身親臨其境的體驗。合成現實越來越表現成一種藝術媒體，它能創造一種誘發身歷其境的沉浸體驗，能通過增強媒體體驗和增加遊戲真實來促進知識的獲取及轉移。SR以視覺豐富及互動的形式將數字信息溶入現實世界中，讓學習者沈浸其中，並直觀地獲取知識，例如Kilmon等人在2010研究中指出，在醫學培訓領域，SR能幫助用家藉沈浸在互動藝術作品中來創造真實及刺激的體驗，讓學習者理解空間關係概念，從而顯著地提高知識的保存及學習表現。儘管SR在許多領域中被採用，唯其缺乏美學設計規劃，以致SR應用的結果不能被肯定，其時好時差的表現，表示SR的使用可能達致不可靠的學習成果。故此，理解如何提升利用技術創造的SR能力來改善知識轉移，仍然是一個對該領域理論及實踐的挑戰。 這項研究旨在提供對以下各點的一個全面理解: 1)對SR誘發沉浸的理論;(2)SR誘發沉浸的概念關係網絡及(3)SR在解決實用問題方面的有效應用(例如，SR誘發沉浸如何影響知識轉移)。簡而言之，本研究旨在研究如何利用SR來實現一系列藝術沉浸，從而引發沉浸體驗及認知反思，最終達致促進知識的獲取及轉移。 知識的獲取及轉移，意即吸收知識和在新的情況下應用所獲知識的能力，對學習者來說是十分重要但具有挑戰性，然而，通過精心設計的技術，是可以提高學習者將在一種情境中所獲得的知識和技能應用在其他情境的可能性，因此，這研究計劃旨在了解如何設計SR以加強知識獲取及轉移。我們將SR誘發沉浸理論推展至一個多維概念，並通過感官，戰術，戰略，敘事，空間和社交沉浸這個六個屬性展現出來。本研究將建立這些維度的操作量度，並加以驗證。我們假設SR誘發沉浸為知識獲取及轉移的前因，而享樂及反思將調節其中關係。本實證研究旨在驗證SR誘發沉浸的概念關係網絡理論，並期望具有重要的實踐相關性，和對利用SR以加強知識轉移提出設計及實施指示。

11610419.label: Realisation of objectives
11610419.value: Overview This final report summarizes project activities and outcomes over the entire reporting period. It thereby adds to the findings from the interim report. It also reports on two additional research outputs (journal articles) emanating from project activities. Project Activities and findings The research project was initiated to address the following three objectives: 1. Develop an enhanced model of immersion based on existing theory 2. Empirically validate different dimensions of immersion 3. Theorize and test the impact of immersion on knowledge transfer (learning) Objective 1: Immersion Model To address the first objective, the project began with the definition and capture of biological level indicators for immersion, through the visualization of two general types of human emotions and the human absorptive state via an LED array depicting multidimensional display patterns. Whereas immersion and flow are often described abstractly, e.g., being oblivious to the flow of time, the project set out to visualize immersion along the time, frequency, and space domain via EEG data converted into low-resolution LED output. To do so, a hardware and software implementation was created. The general view of the entire system is shown above. The EEG data reading and processing employed the Emotiv head-set and its embedded application. EEG data communication to the computer occurred via a WebSockets solution. The connection and sending of functional instructions to the LED array relied on Particle Cloud Console application program interfaces (APIs). The system was prototyped and tried in relation to an immersive synthetic reality task, namely car racing. While users engaged with a car racing simulator, their EEG data was captured and visualized. Car Racing Simulator Arousal level was captured through the change in LED movement. Faster change rate, indicated higher arousal levels. The maximum size of the illuminated LED shell represents the absorption of the individual. Different sizes of the shell (below) imply different levels of an individual’s absorption (i.e., focus level). LED Shells Representing Levels of Arousal and Absorption This prototype visualization system for immersion was submitted and accepted as a conference paper (Ke and Wagner, 2020a) to the HCII Conference. Further experimental follow-up (to address Objective 2) was intended, but stopped due to COVID-related inability to carry out an on-site experiment. Unfortunately, the experimental work could not be completed within the scope of the project. Instead, further survey work was carried out, as described below. Objective 2: Validation of Immersion Dimensions Validation of the immersion dimension is now planned for the second project year. Experimental subjects, as per prior plan, will use several racing simulators, thereby varying the application verisimilitude and expected levels of immersion. Impacts of immersion will be captured using biological data, performance data, and feedback from subjects in form of questionnaires. Following the completion of this prototype work (and not reported in the progress report), further research was undertaken to extend the immersion model. The research took advantage of the recent developments in VR software and “metaverse” platforms (e.g., VRChat) and thus explored drivers of immersion. Findings suggest that users perceive both the immersive environment (i.e., special characteristics) and the embodied experience (i.e., their own representation and the ability to carry out activities through their avatar), as drivers of immersion. The embodiment dimension was not envisioned in the original proposal and thus represents a new insight. The data collection for this research was only completed at the very end of the project (Metaverse platforms are still very new) and a corresponding manuscript is being written up, but is not yet ready for submission. The RGC will be acknowledged at that time. Objective 3: Impact on Knowledge Transfer The pilot implementation, although not yet formally tested, indicates that the system as an emotion and absorption visualization platform can help coaches and the eSports players monitor emotional changes and focus level of users. It can also serve as a monitor with real-time feedback which can help professional players to adjust their emotional state and improve their concentration during gaming. The contextual aim of the system in the training is to help eSports players understand and adjust their emotional state to an optimal level. As such, the system can serve as a tool for knowledge transfer.

11610419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11610419.value: Emotional States in Virtual Reality Immersion The training of individuals engaging professionally with virtual reality is important to improve their performance. Within the training, emotion management is also the major concern, especially in stressful situations. Numerous studies on sports science and sports psychology indicates that inappropriate emotional states usually negatively influence athletes’ in-game performance. For example, athletes may considerably decrease in skill execution and performance when self-expected standards are normally achievable, which is the result of increased anxiety under perceived pressure”. Visualising and thus recognizing positive and negative emotional states is of importance to improve virtual reality engagement. Synthetic Realities and Esports—Importance of Professionalism Esports, as a professionalized form of video game play places gamers in a synthetic reality of high realism. Esports is defined by four criteria, most importantly among them professionalism. Professionalism, at the macro level (i.e., structural professionalism), centers on the principles that organize professions and the institutional conditions that lead to efforts to professionalize an activity. Esports players’ professional commitment to excellence and their professionalized pursuits distinguish esports from purely casual and fun gameplay. While professionalism sometimes implies financial rewards, the interpretation here is the pursuit of the activity according to the standards of a professional actor. When gamers take on a professional approach to game play, it enhances their immersion, learning, and their interest in repletion through repeat participation in competitions. Impact on Learning Immersive virtual reality impacts learning outcomes via two paths, affective and cognitive. In the affective path, immersive virtual reality features influence learning outcomes through the mediation of immersion and enjoyment. In the cognitive path, immersive VR features impact learning outcomes through the mediation of usefulness, control and active learning, and cognitive benefits. By investigating how immersive virtual reality features influence learning processes and outcomes, the research provides explanations for the equivocal findings. Research subjects drawn from online crowdsourcing platforms Increasingly, research relies on subjects drawn from online venues, such as crowdsourcing platforms. With relatively low compensation, and no direct monitoring of the participants, concerns arise about the result quality. Surprisingly, crowd workers are motivated by multiple criteria of the crowd work. While money is frequently the most important, other factors, such as task learning, or use of fragmented time also factor into the crowd workers decision making.

11610419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11610419.value: Additional applications are possible. Specifically, the system is also a useful tool for people who have difficulty in recognizing the emotions of others through common expression approaches (say, facial expressions or other non-verbal expressions). The LED visualization can serve these individuals as an explicit expression assistance to help understand emotions expressed by others. For artistic or hedonic use, this system is also a potential tool in media art or emotional game development. For example, well-known media artist Maurice Benayoun has pioneered an acclaimed media art project named “The Brain Factory” which is based on EEG data. Given COVID related difficulties to address objectives empirically, the research explored the the issue of immersive game play conceptually through an analysis of eSports (the use of synthetic environments for professionalized gaming), as explained in Ke and Wagner (2020b). The project similarly explored engagement and knowledge transfer in gamified platforms in conceptually focused article that nevertheless also tested a model of engagement and its impact on participation in a gamified environment (Du, Ke, and Wagner, 2020). This work was later extended and documented in Ke, Wagner, and Du (2022), further highlighting the impact of COVID on immersive gaming as a new wave in the development of eSports. Additional Output As this study involved Amazon Mechanical Turk task workers as research subjects, the project also explored the reliability of these task workers and thus investigated their motivations to participate in the Mechanical Turk. A resulting study was published in Jiang, L., Wagner, C., and Chen, X. (2021). Further research should (and will) explore the role of compensation amounts for crowd workers who serve as research subjects.

11610419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11610419.value: Synthetic Realities (SRs), either in the form of virtual or augmented reality, combine real and virtual elements to provide users with a first-person form of immersive experience. They increasingly serve as an artistic medium to create an immersive environment inducing flow experience, which promotes knowledge acquisition and transfer through enhancing media experiences and increasing the realism of games. SR interposes digital information in the real world in visually rich and interactive ways, to immerse learners and give them intuitive access to knowledge. For example, in the field of medical training, SR helps to create authentic, stimulating experiences via immersion into interactive artworks and allows trainees to understand the spatial relationships and concepts, resulting in significantly increased knowledge retention and performance. Despite SR having been adopted in a number of areas, rules for aesthetic design are lacking, and outcomes of SR applications are equivocal. Understanding how to harness the power of technology-created SR to improve knowledge transfer thus remains a challenge theoretically and practically. This research sought to provide a comprehensive understanding of how to utilize SR to induce flow experiences and cognitive reflections and facilitate knowledge acquisition and transfer.

11612619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11612619.value: 發展的私營化？ 國際金融公司對亞洲發展的影響 本研究以世界銀行的私營成員國際金融公司（IFC）為主要的批判性研究物件，探討IFC在塑造亞洲主流的發展議程方面尚未得到充分認可的重要性。之所以選擇亞洲做具體案例研究，原因之一是，該地區一向採用以國家為主導的社會經濟發展模式，這種非正統的政策選擇與IFC 提倡及實施的關鍵發展模式截然不同，這兩者之間的衝突讓亞洲成為一個很好的例子，以檢視對政策的採納或抵制是如何發生的。其次，透過組織多邊機構如亞洲基礎設施投資銀行﹙亞投行﹚及中國的一帶一路，亞洲地區現已成為全球價值生產鏈和重塑社會經濟發展實踐的核心。透過亞洲這個例子，我們可以考察IFC的議程對新型借貸工具及增長模式的影響。再者，IFC 的投資組合中，亞洲是重要的一環，亞洲所獲得的撥款資金比其它區域都多。最後，本研究的首席研究員已經深入探究亞洲超過15年，已累積了廣泛的知識並建立了相關網絡。其研究成果包括一本由劍橋大學出版社出版的專著、四本論文書集、四次期刊上的專輯，以及諸多在權威學術期刊上發表的文章；這些研究成果被引用多達共532 次。這些研究的影響力不僅限於學術屆，在政策與實踐方面，也多次被區內的非政府組織採用，例如，“印尼國際發展聯盟”便翻譯﹑發布並傳閱了四篇關鍵的研究結果。作者資歷可以佐證此研究項目的可行性。 IFC在資金和影響力方面都是舉足輕重的，但迄今為止，卻沒有多少研究去精確勾勒IFC的發展方案，或解釋這些方案迅速得到重視的背後的原因 。此外，分析IFC工作的影響及其背後的政治鬥爭，則更是少之又少。有見及此，本研究會從形式、崛起及影響這三方面來闡釋IFC的工作，籍此為諸多重要的學術及政策討論做出貢獻。此項目以社會衝突理論為基礎，以批判性政治經濟理論為框架，集中探討全球化下的物質與理念衝突、以及相關的政策和議題。本研究包括五個涵蓋IFC不同管轄地區的具體個案研究。本項目將有助於評價和理解當代發展政策，包括如中國的一帶一路這樣的重要發展議程，對學術和政策方面都將帶來重要影響。 Privatising Development? The International Finance Corporation's impact upon development in Asia The primary objective of the proposed research objective is a critical study (see Cox 1981: 129-30; 2004) of the World Bank’s private sector arm, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and its underappreciated role in reshaping mainstream development agendas in Asia. The regional focus is firstly justified on the basis that Asia is a region that traditionally pursued dirigiste (heterodox) policy sets, in stark contrast to the key modalities deployed and developed by the IFC. Given the significant tension between past policy choices in the region and those of the IFC, the region makes a good case for testing issues of resistance and or adoption of policy agendas. Secondly, the region is now at the very centre of both global value chains and the reconfiguration of development practice through institutions such as the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). This allows observation of the impact and influence of IFC’s agenda on novel lending instruments and globally-important patterns of growth. Third, the region is also a significant component within the IFC’s portfolio, receiving by far the largest disbursed investments of all regions. Finally, the PI has done extensive research in and on the region over the last fifteen years, which has allowed the accrual of extensive knowledge and networks to build off. This research has been published in myriad outputs, including with Cambridge University Press and in leading journals such as Globalizations, Antipode, Development and Change, Journal of Contemporary Asia and Asian Studies Review. This earlier research has had an important impact in both academic and policy spheres, leading to one sole-authored book, four edited volumes, four special issues of journals, many citations (532 to date) and being used by non-governmental organisations within the region, such as the Indonesian Forum on International Development (which translated, published and circulated four key outputs). Despite the importance of the IFC in terms of funding and influence, very little work to date has mapped out the Corporation’s precise modalities and the reasons behind the rapid ascendancy of these. Moreover, even less work has been done to analyse the impacts of the IFC’s work and the politics of this. Given the above, the proposed project seeks to explain the form, rise and impact (ideational, normative, political and material) of the Corporation’s work in order to make a contribution towards various important scholarly and policy debates. The project deploys a critical political economy framework grounded in social conflict theory, concentrating on the battles between material and ideational interests under globalisation and the policy and other imperatives attached to this. The proposed study includes five thematically and sectorally-selected case studies to cover the breadth of the Corporation’s work across different jurisdictions. The project has both scholarly and policy implications for how contemporary development policy should be appraised and understood, including in relation to important development agendas such as China’s BRI.

11614419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11614419.value: When one speaks, one needs to retrieve the phonological content of the utterance prior to articulation and this process has been termed phonological encoding. There is sizable evidence showing that the primary (or first retrievable) planning unit for phonological encoding is different across languages. Dissimilar to many Indo-European languages such as Dutch and English where phonemes have been found to be the primary phonological encoding units, the primary planning units are syllables in Cantonese and Mandarin. This marked contrast between Indo-European and non-Indo-European languages has posed an interesting and important question regarding how bilinguals possessing these two types of language plan for their speech. Bilingual studies have repeatedly shown that one’s first language (L1) would affect one’s acquisition of a second language (L2) (i.e., forward transfer). Likewise, one’s L2 would in turn affect one’s L1 processing (i.e., backward transfer). However, very little is known about how language transfers are realized in the mechanism of phonological encoding. Specifically, when the two languages a bilingual possesses rely on different phonological planning units (e.g., phoneme vs. syllable), how the encoding system adapts to the different demands of L1 and L2 is an issue largely open. Therefore, two picture naming experiments using the form-preparation paradigm are proposed to investigate the role of phoneme and syllable in English (Experiment 1) and Cantonese (Experiment 2) speech production among Cantonese-English bilinguals with various L2 (English) background. Meanwhile, the participants’ event related brain potentials (ERPs) will be recorded during the production task. If forward transfer exists in bilingual phonological encoding, one would expect to see a robust effect of syllable in L2 (phoneme-based English) production at least among the bilinguals with a lesser degree of L2 exposure, a pattern similar to their L1 (syllable-based Cantonese) production. If not, a robust effect of phoneme in L2 production would be expected irrespective of the bilinguals’ L2 background. Experiment 2 investigates the possibility of backward transfer in bilingual phonological encoding. If backward transfer exists, one would expect to see a robust effect of phoneme even in L1 (syllable-based Cantonese) production at least among the bilinguals with a higher degree of L2 (phoneme-based English) exposure. Otherwise, one would expect to see a robust effect of syllable only in L1 production irrespective of the bilinguals’ L2 background. Furthermore, a number of factors regarding the bilinguals’ L2 background will be measured to investigate the possible causes for language transfer in speech production. 在說話過程中，人需要在發聲之前把語音信息先行提取，此過程名為語音加工過程。已有不少證據顯示，語音加工過程中的基本加工單位會因語言不同而有所差異。在荷蘭語和英語等印歐語中最基本的語音加工單位為音素，但在廣東話及普通話中最基本的語音加工單位卻是整個音節。這裡出現一個很有趣及重要的問題，就是能操這兩種式截然不同的語言的雙語者會如何處理語音加工的過程。 過去的雙語研究發現一個人的第一語言會影響第二語言的學習 (此為前向式轉移)。同樣，一個人的第二語言亦會對第一語言的加工產生影響 (此為後向式轉移)。然而，我們至今對此類語言轉移如何體現在語音加工的過程所知仍然非常有限。具體的說，當雙語使用者所操的兩種語言牽涉到不同的語音加工單位 (如音素和音節)，其加工系統會如何處理不同語言的要求仍是一大問號。因此，此研究將採用兩個圖片命名實驗，對具備不同英語背景程度的廣東話—英語雙語者在說英語時音素和音節的角色 (實驗一) 以及在說廣東話時音素和音節的角色 (實驗二) 進行研究。在實驗過程中被試的事件相關腦電數據會被記錄。倘若前向式轉移存在於語音加工過程中，我們會預期廣東話—英語雙語者在說英語時 (實驗一) 會出現很強的音節效應，與說廣東話時的情況相仿。倘若不然，不管雙語被試的英語程度或高或低都應該會出現很明顯的音素效應。實驗二研究後向式轉移出現在雙語者語音加工的可能性。倘若後向式轉移存在，我們會預期廣東話—英語雙語者 (至少對於那些英語程度較高的被試而言) 在說廣東話時 (實驗二) 也會出現很強的音素效應。不然，不管雙語被試的英語程度或高或低都應該只會出現很明顯的音節效應。此外，一系列與雙語者第二語言相關的背景因素都會被量度，以探討語言轉移在言語產生中各種可能的成因。

11614419.label: Realisation of objectives
11614419.value: The six project objectives listed above have been achieved using the funding support received and within the time frame proposed. One behavioural pilot study and two event-related brain potential (ERP) experiments were conducted successfully to investigate how phoneme and syllable units are processed in Cantonese-English bilingual speech production. A conventional overt speech production task (i.e., form-preparation task) was used together with concurrent electroencephalograph (EEG) signal recording. In this task, the participants were asked to name aloud sets of repeatedly presented pictures, the names of the pictures in a set were either phonologically related (e.g., sharing the same word-initial syllable or phoneme) or unrelated. The typical finding of this paradigm in the past was that participants’ picture naming response would be faster in the phonologically related condition than in the unrelated control condition. The phonological priming effect observed using this paradigm has been used to infer the nature of phonological units and the mechanism of phonological planning in spoken word production. The above project objectives have been addressed using this paradigm with concurrent EEG recording among Cantonese-English bilinguals. Details are discussed in the following. Objective 1: Participants were invited to go through the form-preparation task once in their first language (L1) Cantonese and another time in their second language (L2) English. Null effect of phoneme sharing but a significant effect of syllable sharing were found in Cantonese, similar to the findings of previous studies (Wong and Chen, 2008, 2009; Wong et al., 2012). Consistent with the notion that the type of the primary phonological planning unit is probably language-specific (O’Seaghdha et al., 2010; Wong et al., 2019). The primary phonological unit has been found to be individual phonemes in languages such as Dutch and English, whereas it has been shown to be the syllable unit in Mandarin and Cantonese Chinese (Chen et al., 2003; Wong & Chen, 2008). The present findings showed that the syllable unit has a more salient role to play than the phoneme unit in Cantonese speech production. Interestingly, in the English experiment of the present project, a similarly robust syllable-related priming effect and a null effect of phoneme sharing were observed among the same group of Cantonese-English bilingual participants. This pattern of result was in contrast to the findings from native English speakers where a significant effect of single phoneme was typically found. These results suggest that among the Cantonese-English bilinguals that we have tested, the role of syllable is more salient than the phoneme unit even in L2 English speech production, similar to the pattern of their L1 Cantonese speech production. Objective 2: In the present project, concurrent scalp EEG recording was conducted together with the form-preparation paradigm described above to track the time course of phonemic and syllabic processing in overt Cantonese (L1) and English (L2) speech production. For the EEG data, both stimulus-locked (i.e., the EEG data being analysed were time locked to the onset of picture presentation to examine the 500-ms post-stimulus EEG signals) and response-locked (i.e., the EEG data being analysed were time locked to the onset of the vocal naming response to investigate the 300-ms pre-response EEG signals) analyses were conducted to investigate the relatively “early” and “late” phonological planning processes respectively. Significant ERP effects were observed in the syllable-related condition relative to the unrelated control condition. The significant ERP effect observed in the Cantonese syllable-related condition was found in the stimulus-locked analysis as early as the 250-350 ms time window following the picture onset. Similarly, a significant ERP effect was also observed in the English syllable-related condition in the 350-450 ms time window post-stimulus onset. Interestingly, significant ERP effects were also found in the phoneme related conditions in both L1 Cantonese and L2 English speech production, but these effects were found only in the response-locked analysis within the -300 to -150 ms pre-response onset (but not in the stimulus-locked analysis). Taken together, these results suggest that ERP is a sensitive measurement tool that can be used to reveal the fine-grained processes underlying phonological planning which might otherwise be difficult to be shown using the conventional behavioural methods. More importantly, regarding the time course of phonemic and syllabic processes in bilingual speech production, the present ERP results show that syllabic encoding precedes phonemic encoding, and this pattern holds true for both L1 and L2 speech production in Cantonese-English bilinguals. Objective 3: In this project, the Cantonese-English bilingual participants showed robust syllable-related priming and a null effect of phoneme-related effect not only in their L1 Cantonese speech production but also in their L2 English speech production. In the past literature, the typical finding in English phonological planning using a similar form-preparation task with native English speakers was that a robust phoneme-related priming was usually found. The contrast between this and the previous English studies suggest that there is a forward transfer in phonological planning among Cantonese-English bilinguals. In other words, participants in the present study transferred the mechanism of their L1 Cantonese phonological planning (where syllable is the primary phonological unit) to their L2 English phonological planning, as evident by the similarly robust effect of syllable priming in their L2 English production. Objective 4: In this project, we have observed evidence showing that the degree of forward transfer (as mentioned above) would be modulated by one’s L2 experience. Specifically, we found that the size of syllable-related priming observed in the English form-preparation task was associated with the Cantonese-English bilinguals’ L2 vocabulary size. The larger the L2 vocabulary size, the smaller the syllable-related priming in L2 speech production. This is an interesting finding, suggesting that the nature of the primary phonological unit in L2 may subject to the influence of multiple factors including one’s script experiences in L2. In other words, the property of one’s L1 is not the sole factor determining the nature of phonological planning units in L2. Objective 5: Our ERP data provided evidence showing the possibility of backward transfer in Cantonese-English bilingual phonological planning. Robust and early ERP effects were found in the syllable-related condition in both L1 and L2 speech production. Nevertheless, significant ERP effects were also found in the phoneme-related conditions in both language conditions (including the Cantonese speech production condition) though the effects tended to be less robust and relatively late. These results suggest the possibility that individual phonemes also have a role to play in L1 Cantonese phonological planning possibly due to the bilinguals’ experience in an alphabetic English L2. Objective 6: Closely related to the objective 5 in the above, we have also examined the relationship between one’s L2 experience and the degree of backward transfer. We found that when all other factors were held constant, the degree of backward transfer among Cantonese-English bilinguals was influenced by the speaker’s prior experience of residing in an immersive English-speaking environment. Relative to those bilingual participants without prior foreign living experiences, our Cantonese-English bilingual participants who had previously resided in an English-speaking country (for more than 1 month) showed relatively more robust phoneme-related ERP effects in both L1 Cantonese and L2 English speech production. These results suggest that the degree of backward transfer would be affected by one’s L2 experience such as the prior experience of residing in an immersive L2 environment.

11614419.label: Major findings and research outcome
11614419.value: One behavioural pilot study and two event-related brain potential (ERP) experiments were conducted successfully to investigate how phoneme and syllable units are processed in Cantonese-English bilingual speech production. A conventional overt speech production task (i.e., form-preparation task) was used together with concurrent electroencephalograph (EEG) signal recording in this project. Our results showed a clear pattern of forward transfer, that is, the nature of the primary phonological unit used in L2 phonological planning is influenced by one’s L1. However, the degree of such forward transfer has been found to be modulated by one’s L2 vocabulary size and L2 proficiency (see Wong et al., accepted upon revision, as listed in Part C). In addition, we have also observed evidence for backward transfer, where Cantonese-English bilinguals who had prior living experiences in an English-speaking country showed a more robust phoneme-related ERP effect (in both L1 Cantonese and L2 English speech production) than those bilingual participants without a similar prior foreign country living experience (results were presented in an international conference as listed in Part C). These results indicate that the degree of backward transfer would be modulated by one’s L2 experience. Taken together, the results of this project show that the phonological planning system of the bilingual speakers is a highly dynamic system with both forward and backward transfers co-existing which are subjected to the influence of different language experience factors.

11614419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
11614419.value: This project has demonstrated that the EEG/ERP technique (with its considerably high temporal resolution) is a useful tool to uncover the temporal dynamics underlying phonological planning. In addition, findings from this project have also shown the complicated and dynamic nature of the phonological planning system in bilingual speech production. Yet, our current understanding is limited to the “bilingual” populations with a syllable-based L1 and a phoneme-based L2 (but not the other way around). Further research can be conducted to extend to a different group of bilingual population with a phoneme-based L1 and a syllable-based L2 (e.g., international students from an English-speaking country coming to HK to learn Cantonese or Mandarin). In addition, future studies in this line can be extended to the tri-lingual populations (e.g., Cantonese-, Mandarin-English tri-lingual speakers) to investigate how phonological planning is operated among the three languages, as well as the role of language similarity (given Cantonese is more similar to Mandarin than English in terms of their phonological property) in tri-lingual speech production.

11614419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
11614419.value: The purpose of this research project was to investigate how Cantonese-English bilingual speakers mentally retrieve the phonological content of the spoken word in L1 (Cantonese) and L2 (English) speech production. A conventional behavioural task, the form-preparation task, was used together with concurrent recording of the scalp electroencephalograph (EEG) signals to track the temporal brain activities during the planning for speech before articulation. This study was the first using the EEG technique to uncover the underlying processes in bilingual phonological planning where the two languages possessed by the bilinguals were phonologically distinct from each other (i.e., syllable-based Cantonese vs. phoneme-based English). Findings of this project provided evidence showing the role and relative time course of syllable and phoneme processing in Cantonese (L1) and English (L2) speech production. In addition, the present results showed clearly the inter-dependence between L1 and L2 in bilingual phonological planning and the role of different L2 experiences. This research project provided empirical evidence which is important for our better understanding of how bilingual speakers handle two phonologically distinctive languages in one mind.

11614519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
11614519.value: The economic and cultural importance of creative software companies cannot be overstated. Forbes listed two creative software companies among the 15 most innovative companies for 2018: Autodesk, which produces software to create 3D graphics, and Adobe. Adobe provides software for creative professionals in the sectors of design, photography, film industry, animation. Over the past 35 years, it has grown into an iconic company, defining and redefining a certain social understanding of what digital creativity is. In 2013, Adobe pioneered a move from a software-based model, where the software is bought by the user, to a cloud-centric model involving a monthly subscription. Recently, it has launched Adobe Sensei to empower its AI and Machine Learning (ML) in all of its clouds. The technology relies on infinite data partially provided by the users’ creative practices, paving the way for new forms of automation of the creative act. These evolutions potentially bear a radical transformation of the ways in which professionals use this software in several important sectors of the creative economy and may radically alter the current definitions of digital creativity. Current research on software stresses how algorithms have impacted on individual and social life. A significant trend in software studies embraces a transformative agenda by suggesting alternative ways to circumvent limitations imposed by software. To date, however, no research has extensively documented how creative software companies are increasingly governing creative practices. This project aims to fill this gap in knowledge with a Foucauldian perspective which emphasizes the interwoven institutional, economic, social and political ‘dispositifs’ supporting the ‘governmentality’ of creative acts. We will use a poststructuralist theoretical framework to underline the historical, cultural, negotiated construction of the meanings of creative acts through discourses on creative software. We will perform a Foucauldian discourse analysis over an extensive corpus of documents in relation to Adobe from the creation of Illustrator to Adobe Sensei. This analysis aim to study discursive mechanisms through which conceptions of creative act come to be accepted, internalized and performed or modified. This project builds on the PI’s past work on the datafication of the creative act, on videogame engines as tools of metacreation, as well as on his recent research ‘The development of new media expertise in the creative economy of Hong Kong’, studying the use of creative software by Hong Kong creative professionals, which resulted in a public policy report for the government of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. 奧多比、雲端運算及人工智能：創意軟件和創意行為的治理法 摘要 創意軟件公司對經濟及文化的重要性是不容忽視的。報福斯將2018年度15間最創新公司的其中兩間創意軟件公司上市：分別是生產製造三維圖像的Autodesk(歐德克股份有限公司)和Adobe (奧多比公司)。 Adobe為設計界、攝影界、電影業界和動畫界的創意專業人士提供軟件。在過去的35年，它定義了亦重新界定了數碼創造力的一些社會認知，成為了一間標誌性的公司。於2013年，奧多比公司首創由原本以用家購買軟件的以軟件為基礎經營模式，改變成為月供訂閱以雲端為中心的模型。最近，它推出了Adobe Sensei 去加強它所有雲端的人工智能和機器學習。此技術有賴部份提供自用家創意慣例的無限數據，為新模式的自主創意行為創造條件。這些演化潛在地包含了專業人士在不同的創意經濟重要領域中使用這些軟件的徹底變化，以及可能根本地改變現時對數碼創造力的定義。 現時對軟件的研究着重於演算法如何影響個人和社交生活。軟件研究的一個重要趨勢包括規避軟件所提供限制的變革理念。然而至今，沒有研究廣泛地記錄創意軟件公司如何增加管理創意慣例。是次研究旨在利用強調制度交織、經濟、社會以及政治部署來支持創意行為管理的傅柯觀點(Foucauldian perspective) 來填充這知識溝。 我們將會利用後結構主義理論去研究軟件創造的論述如何引致一個獨特的在於創造的文化和歷史的定義。我們亦會對關於Adobe 由建立Illustrator至Adobe Sensei的廣泛語料庫進行研究，利用傅柯論述去進行分析。這個分析目的在於由創意行為達致被接受、使內化、被施行或被更改的概念來研究論證機制。 這個研究建基於主研究者以往對創意行為的數據化、以遊戲開發引擎用作科技及超創作媒介，以及近期對名為「新媒體專業在香港創意經濟的發展」，研究香港創意專業人士使用的創意軟件，題材為香港特別行政區政府其中一個公共政策報告。

11614519.label: Realisation of objectives
11614519.value: Objective 1: To document the evolution of Adobe’s discourse on creativity Achieved: 100% This objective was fully achieved by constituting an archive of Adobe’s documentation, from the creation of Illustrator in the mid-1980s up until the announcement of the launch of Adobe Sensei (2016). The objective was achieved by collecting information about Adobe’s creative software and their uses on the company’s website and a variety of social media and information websites (including Github, Youtube tutorials, and so on). As mentioned in our mid-term report, these included: “1) company documents available online, including company structures, marketing strategies, production information, research documents, as well community forums; 2) documents of other actors involved in the direct creation of the software (individual and institutional collaborations); 3) social coding repositories (Github), Subreddits and online tutorials (including YouTube); 4) specialized news sources on creative software; 5) news sources on digital software sector; 6) applicable legal frameworks; 7) creative software and their use in art schools” They were then classified to identify the mechanisms through which Adobe became indispensable household names and how they evolved over time. What were the major themes? How was a specific discourse on creativity produced? How were products being accessed? What uses were being prescribed? How where they used, notably in art schools? How was value being captured? Challenges and strategies: Even though the documents collected may not be fully exhaustive, the data collected is sufficiently expansive and redundant to be considered representative of the major themes during that period. Objective 2: To document supporting and opposing discourses on Adobe’s creative software Achieved: 100% To address this objective, the PI relied on websites where Adobe products were discussed by different groups: specialized news sources (technical, business articles, art magazines), subreddits and other social media. Dominant discourses, practices, and products provoke resistance (in words or practices). The research team documented reviews and comments on Adobe’s products and their evolutions, to highlight how different groups of users may perceive the company, its products or the themes that were being imposed through the sources listed in Objective 1. Obstacles and strategies: The diversity of data and data sources proved to be a challenge. This was addressed by distinguishing between discourses about products, on the one hand, and discourses about the effects of their practices, on the other hand (for instance when a creative practice is deemed to result in a social issue such as the role of Photoshop on body image). This helped distinguish between a prescribed use (and the supporting and opposing discourses it generates) and its effects (perceived or real), as these tend to reinforce or weaken the apparatus of governmentality. This strategy proved quite effective. Objective 3: To describe the network of discourse production related to Adobe’s creative software Achieved: 100% How does the discourse about Adobe’s creative software expand and become inscribed in other practices? The research focused particularly on the role of training institutions and job offers as mechanisms of transfer of discourses on creativity, creative practices, and artists/creatives/creative professionals. Training institutions have been highlighted by Foucault and his followers as important mechanisms of transmission and internalisation of ways of being and doing. Therefore, they are instrumental in the network of discourse production and transfer of discourse and practices of creativity. Strategies and discourses of resistance may be marginalized by homogenizing forces. The research also attempted to identify ambivalent cases, discourses and trajectories which may show attempts to evade a clearcut identification with the dominant discourses embodied by companies such as Adobe; these cases may result in a continued use of mainstream creative software in addition to alternative strategies and identities (e.g., attempts by artists to separate their art practice from their jobs as creative professionals). The research further describes tensions and heated debates, notably during the launch of Adobe Sensei, a data-intensive tool Challenges and strategies: The material gathered for Objective 1 proved to be valuable in addressing the risk of data saturation. Forums, subreddits dedicated to Adobe products or to digital creative practices in general have been used by creative professionals to share thoughts and experiences, knowledge, and so on. Such information provides valuable illustration of lived experiences and modes of incorporating Adobe-related discourse and practices. They also highlight ways of identifying mechanisms of internalization of those discourses in the daily lives of the forum participants. Furthermore, the challenge presented by the number of local specificities was addressed by focusing on a few insightful contexts. The PI was able to rely on his previous research on the training and creative practices of Hong Kong-based media artists on his own role in a training institution. Additionally, the PI was able to contrast his findings with his previous research conducted on music scenes in a context where the transmission of the discourse on creativity operates differently (Los Angeles). Objective 4: To describe the discursive mechanisms underlying the governmentality of the creative act Achieved: 100% This objective was achieved by developing a theoretical framework to account for the research findings. It was also achieved by participating in theoretical conversations (conferences, papers) on the datafication of creative practices and the evolution of discourses on digital creative practices. The PI and co-Is followed closely the literature inspired by Foucauldian approaches in software studies, media arts, methodologies of media archaeology. In this regard, the literature reviewed by the co-investigators focused on the performative mythologies associated with technology and the implications of qualifying algorithms as ‘intelligent’. The co-investigators’ contribution focused on the mechanisms through which technologies evolved from being “dreams” (their original intent) to their realization as rationalized myths under the effect of capitalization. On the other end, the literature reviewed by the PI centered around a conception of power as productive force, a force that produces “reality” and “domains of objects and rituals of truth” (Foucault 1975, p.149), and the different mechanisms and discourses of governmentality (for example, subscription models and patents). This objective did not pose any significant challenge. Objective 5: To document the strategies of prescription and framing of the creative act Achieved: 100% Objective 5 consists in gathering documents associated with Adobe’s modes of governing creative practices and defining “creatives”. The database includes documents such as algorithms, subscription models, and terms of use. The database will be maintained and updated. Informed by theory (Task A), it contributed to the publication of academic papers (Task E). This objective did not pose any significant challenge.
