12103219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12103219.value: Despite significant progress since the First Green Revolution, the yield of rice has almost plateaued in recent years. Unless revolutionary innovations are found, it will be impossible to meet the demands of a global population of almost 10 billion by 2050. The incorporation of C4 photosynthetic pathway in rice and the modification of panicle/spikelet architecture have been considered two promising strategies to increase rice yield. However, these strategies simply cannot guarantee success, because both merely increase either the source or sink size/activity, whereas yield is a very complex outcome of source-sink relationship. Notably, despite a decades-long effort of the New Plant Type (NPT) initiatives of the International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) turned out to be unsuccessful due to the poor biomass and poor grain-filling of NPT lines. Similarly, poor grain-filling of inferior spikelets also remains a problem of super-rice varieties. Therefore, a quantitative understanding of source-sink relationships during grain-filling is very critical for future increments in rice productivity. Otherwise “NPT history” will repeat itself. We have isolated a novel rice double-grain mutant with triple distinct phenotypes: a single spikelet possessing (i) two awns, (ii) two lemmas, (iii) two grains. Moreover, both grains are almost fully filled. Therefore, the double-grained spikelet is significantly heavier than the wild type. We named the mutant double-grain-filled (dgf1), since grain-filling of the dgf1 mutant is not limited by the hull size, thus the mutant spikelet shows the open hull phenotype. The primary objective of this proposal is to identify the genetic basis of the double-grain-filled (dgf1) mutant phenotype via a BSA-seq approach instead of conventional map-based cloning and subsequent characterization of the regulation and/or evolution of the respective gene using routine molecular techniques. Grain-filling depends on three major factors: the source, sink and flow. Recently, a rice ADP-glucose pyrophosphorylase (AGPase) double mutant (agpl1agpl3) was reported where the flow factor (temporary carbon storage and its remobilization in culm) was almost absent without implications for grain-filling. Therefore, development of a triple mutant (dgf1agpl1agpl3) and comparisons of grain-filling patterns, differential gene expressions, and hormonal contents among these mutants (dgf1, agpl1agpl3, dgf1agpl1agpl3) will generate valuable information on grain-filling regulations and help to quantify the contributions of the source, sink and flow. Consequently, the outcome of this research will not only improve our understanding of the genetic control of double-grain formation, but will also provide opportunity to identify the bottlenecks of the grain-filling process. 水稻產量自第一次綠色革命以來取得了顯著進展，但近年來幾乎達到瓶頸。除非找到革命性的創新，否則糧食產量到2050年將無法滿足全球近100億人口的需求。將C4光合途徑納入水稻和加大穗型結構(新植物類型，NPT)曾被認為是提高水稻產量的兩大有希望的策略，然而，這些策略並不能保證成功，因為兩者都只是增加源或庫的大小/活力，而產量是源-庫之間一個非常複雜的關係。例如，儘管國際水稻研究所(IRRI)的對NPT進行了幾十年的努力和倡議，但由於NPT株系的生物量低和籽粒灌漿不足，結果以失敗告終。 我們分離出了一種具有三種不同表型的新型水稻雙粒突變體:具有(i)雙芒, (ii)雙外稃, (三)雙籽粒。兩顆籽粒的灌漿都可以十分充足。因此，雙粒突變體的稻穗比野生型要重得多。我們命名為雙粒灌漿突變體(dgf1)，因為dgf1突變體的籽粒灌漿不受穎殼大小的限制，表現為穎殼開放的表型。本課題的首要目標是通過BSA-seq方法,而不是傳統的圖位克隆的方法，進行基因定位，隨後使用進化生物學與常規分子生物學技術研究其基因功能。 水稻灌漿取決於三個主要因素:簡稱為源、庫和流。最近有研究報導了水稻ADP-葡萄糖焦磷酸酶(AGPase)雙突變體(agpl1agpl3)的碳流量因數中的再運轉(即在莖杆中的臨時碳儲的再運轉)幾乎不存在,但此突變體對水稻灌漿卻沒有影響。因此,開發三重突變體(dgf1agpl1agpl3)和比較這些突變體(dgf1, agpl1agpl3, dgf1agpl1agpl3)之間的灌漿模式、差異基因表達和激素含量將產生有價值的資訊，並準確量化源、庫和流在水稻灌漿中的貢獻。因此,這項研究的結果不僅將增進我們對雙粒形成基因作用機制的認識,而且將為突破灌漿過程中的瓶頸提供機會。

12103219.label: Realisation of objectives
12103219.value: Rice (Oryza sativa) yield is primarily determined by three key components: the number of panicles per unit area, the grain weight, and the number of grains or spikelets per panicle. Among these, grain number per panicle, largely influenced by spikelet number, is a major target for yield improvement. However, traditional rice breeding has primarily focused on the increase of spikelet number per panicle, without attention to the number of florets within each spikelet. This is because a typical rice spikelet produces one fertile floret, resulting in a single grain. In rice, which has determinate spikelets, the spikelet meristems produce a fixed number of floral meristems, leading to the development of a single floret. In contrast, indeterminate spikelets in crops like wheat (Triticum aestivum) generate variable numbers of floral meristems, resulting in multiple florets. To further enhance rice yield, increasing the number of florets within a spikelet could provide a novel strategy for higher productivity. We have characterized one interesting mutant, double-grain-filled (dgf1), which produce two filled grains per spikelet. To explore the regulating mechanism of floret number in rice, we have performed the following studies. We found that in the dgf1 mutant, over 80% of spikelets displayed open hulls, double lemmas or awns and dual pistils, with both ovaries developing into grains. In addition, dgf1 spikelets, along with their dual grains, were significantly heavier than their wild-type counterparts. To identify the mutant gene, GWS-sequencing was employed to locate the insertion position of the T-DNA, which showed that insertion position located at 23240016 on Chr11 according to the IVG imaging results. Gene searching results shown that the insertion position belongs to a circRNA gene, one of the non-coding RNA which has not been reported to be involved in grain development. Then we performed transcriptome sequencing of young panicles at the fifth stage of differentiation in both the dgf1 mutant and wild-type plants and a total 871 (573 up and 298 down -regulated) differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified between the wild type and the dgf1 mutant. GO analysis revealed that many DEGs were significantly enriched in categories related to “binding” and “catalytic activity”. Meanwhile, KEGG pathway analysis showed that most DEGs were associated with pathways involved in “Carbohydrate metabolism” and “Amino acid metabolism”. 32 DEGs belonging to 14 distinct TF families were identified, including MADS, bHLH, bZIP, WRKY, NAC, and ERF, which may play important roles in regulating the dgf1 mutant phenotype. Among the transcription factors identified, OsMADS1 emerged as a key regulator, with significantly increased expression in the dgf1 mutant. OsMADS1 plays a critical role in rice floret development, coordinating transcriptional and hormonal pathways (Chen et al., 2024). Further analysis on the relationship between circRNA and OsMADS1 genes were performed by using the knockout and overexpression lines of both genes to reveal the regulating mechanism of double-grain-filled phenotype. Non-structural carbohydrate transportation from source to sink is usually regulated by nitrogen application, which might be significant in revealing the source-sink relationship in dgf1 mutant. Hence, we studied physiological and molecular mechanism in inferior grains of rice under different nitrogen applications. We found that excessive application of nitrogen reduced the starch biosynthesis and grain weight of inferior spikelets but not superior spikelets. Plant hormone detection revealed that both cytokinin (CTK) and 3-Indoleacetic acid (IAA) were reduced by excessive nitrogen at the early stage of grain filling in inferior spiekelts. Quantitative real-time PCR results showed that inhibition of biosynthesis genes led to a decrease in IAA content, while elevation of CTK oxidase genes resulted in a lower level of CTK under excessive nitrogen treatment. Application of exogenous IAA or CTK significantly impaired the inhibitory effect of excessive nitrogen on starch accumulation and grain weight of inferior spikelets. Further enzyme assays revealed that excessive nitrogen application significantly suppressed the enzyme activities of sucrose synthase (SuS), adenosine diphosphate glucose pyrophosphorylase (AGP) and starch synthase (StS) in inferior spikelets. Application of exogenous IAA or CTK to the panicle under excessive nitrogen treatment significantly increased the enzyme activities of SuS, AGP and StS. Taken together, our results revealed that excessive nitrogen application in field-grown rice suppressed grain filling of inferior spikelets by reducing the accumulation of cytokinin and auxin (Chen et al., 2022). Inferior spkikelets are those grains with weaker sink activity compared to the superior spikelets. The grain filling of inferior spikelets resembles that of dgf1 mutant. Here, transcriptomic analysis of the most active grain filling stage revealed that both starch metabolism and phytohormone signaling were significantly promoted by moderate soil-drying (MD) treatment, accompanied by increased enzyme activities of starch synthesis and elevated abscisic acid (ABA) and indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) content in the inferior spikelet. Moreover, the IAA biosynthesis genes OsYUC11 and OsTAR2 were upregulated, while OsIAA29 and OsIAA24, which encode two repressors of auxin signaling, were downregulated by MD, implying a regulation of both IAA biosynthesis and auxin signal transduction in the inferior spikelet by MD. A notable improvement in grain filling of the inferior spikelet was found in the aba8ox2 mutant, which is mutated in an ABA catabolism gene. In contrast, overexpression of OsABA8ox2 significantly reduced grain filling. Interestingly, not only the IAA content, but also the expression of IAA biosynthesis and auxin responsive genes displayed a similar trend to that in the inferior spikelet under MD. In addition, several OsTPP genes were downregulated in the inferior spikelets of both MD/ABA-treated wild-type plants and the aba8ox2 mutant, resulting in lower trehalose content and higher levels of -6-phosphate (T6P), thereby increasing the expression of OsTAR2, a target of T6P. Taken together, our results suggest that the synergistic interaction of ABA-mediated accumulation of IAA promotes grain filling of inferior spikelets under MD (Teng et al., 2022ab).

12103219.label: Major findings and research outcome
12103219.value: Clustered-spikelet rice has been reported for a long time, however, its underlying mechanism has not been revealed until the BRD3-GSK2-MADS1 pathway was identified. Here we have identified another gene that controls floret number in one spikelet, which encoded a non-coding RNA, a circRNA. Further transcriptome analysis revealed that this mutant gene might also target OsMADS1 by regulating its expression level (Chen et al., 2024). Poor gain filling efficiency of inferior spikelets might be a good system for source-sink relationship study. Both nitrogen and moderate drought will affect the source-sink relationship. We first used RNA-seq and small RNA-seq to examine the expression profile of inferior spikelet under moderate drought condition. Results showed that several phytohormone pathways have been regulated by microRNA that respond to moderate drought (Teng et al., 2022a). By using mutant of ABA biosynthesis in grains, we further found that ABA and IAA synergistically interact with each other to promote grain filling of inferior spikelets under moderate drought condition, suggesting that plant hormones are involved in regulating sink activity of grains (Teng et al., 2022b). To further explore the source-sink relationship, the source activity was regulated by nitrogen application, we found that reduced source activity by excess nitrogen will inhibit the biosynthesis of IAA and CTK in inferior spikelets of rice, which thereby suppresses the sink activity by inhibiting enzyme activities for starch biosynthesis and eventually reduces grain weight (Chen et al., 2022). Together, we found that promoting sink capacity by regulating floret number and increasing source activity works synergistically to break the barriers of grain filling.

12103219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12103219.value: The mutant gene of dgf1 has been identified to be a circRNA, which is very new in plant and has not been reported in regulating grain development. In addition, the mechanism that circRNA regulating expression of target genes is a mystery, thus, further studies will be focusing on the regulating relationship between circRNA and OsMADS1 gene and their function in controlling multiple florets in a spikelet. For the downstream regulating mechanism of source-sink relationship on grain filling, the up-regulation and down-regulation lines of above genes will significantly facilitate our studies on increasing source activity and sink capacity simultaneously. Eventually, the outcome of this study will not just provide breeding materials and gene resources, but also the theoretical support of cultivation management for breaking the grain filling barriers.

12103219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12103219.value: Rice yield has reached its ceiling for years due to earlier outstanding works of rice breeders. Increasing grain number in a panicle and promoting carbohydrate transportation from source to grains are keyways to promote yield of rice. We have found a new rice with double-grain-filled which might be owning to the out of function of circRNA that targets a floret regulating gene, the OsMADS1. Enhancing the transportation of carbohydrate from sheath and stem by moderate drought application after anthesis or suppressing this transportation by excess nitrogen application will promote grain filling of inferior grains by the synergistic interaction between abscisic acid and auxin or inhibit grain filling by simultaneously reducing content of auxin and cytokinin, respectively. Our results have provided new insights in floret and grain development and new resources for higher yield rice breeding.

12103519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12103519.value: 骨關節炎的治療是世界性的醫療難題。該病目前尚無治癒方案，治療策略仍停留在緩解症狀或通過外科手術進行人工關節置換。造成這一窘境的主要原因是該病的治病因素複雜，病理生理機制尚未清晰，臨床上亦缺乏早期診斷該病之方法。骨關節炎病變累及關節的軟骨、骨及滑膜組織，其病理學主要特徵為持續的軟骨退變、軟骨下骨異常骨重塑、滑膜腫脹及骨刺增生。目前，醫學界對於軟骨及軟骨下骨異常對骨關節炎發生發展的貢獻仍充滿爭議。而且大量基礎及臨床研究證實：不管是抑制軟骨降解或是抑制軟骨下骨異常骨重塑的藥物均無法逆轉或延緩骨關節炎的疾病進程。事實上，軟骨及軟骨下骨是緊密關聯的組織，兩者之間潛在的骨-軟骨物質交換和細胞通訊已被先前研究證實。但骨-軟骨通訊在骨關節炎中的病理生理作用並不清楚。 微小核酸（miRNA）是細胞內調控蛋白質翻譯的重要調節分子。新進的研究亦表明細胞可通過分泌包裹微小核酸的外泌體與鄰近細胞進行通訊並對接收細胞的蛋白質翻譯進行調控。申請人既往的研究報導了破骨細胞可借助自身分泌的外泌體微小核酸調控成骨細胞的骨形成功能。考慮到破骨細胞在骨關節炎早期軟骨下骨異常骨重塑時大量出現並可侵犯骨軟骨交界部位，其分泌的外泌體微小核酸極有可能對骨關節炎的軟骨產生影響。申請人在前期研究了切除前十字韌帶誘導的小鼠骨關節炎模型後發現：在骨關節炎的早期，軟骨下骨特別是骨-軟骨交界處有大量的破骨細胞骨生。同時在這些成熟破骨細胞內，我們檢測到了一系列微小核酸的表達顯著上調（包括miR-214-3p, miR-30a-5p和miR-30b-5p等）。以上微小核酸的水平在這些小鼠的血清外泌體中亦顯著升高。更有趣的是，我們利用基因敲除技術下調破骨細胞中微小核酸的表達後發現，小鼠的骨關節炎病變（包括軟骨退變及血管神經侵入）大大減輕。我們進一步的體外研究顯示，破骨細胞分泌的外泌體可被軟骨細胞攝入，其中包裹的微小核酸可抑制軟骨細胞內源性的2型組織特異性金屬蛋白酶抑制劑（TIMP2）的蛋白表達，進而促進軟骨基質降解並削弱其對血管神經入侵的抵抗能力。綜合上述發現，我們形成如下研究假設：破骨細胞分泌的外泌體微小核酸可抑制軟骨細胞TIMP2進而促進骨關節炎早期的軟骨基質降解及血管神經侵入。 申請人擬在本項目中通過分別補充和阻斷破骨細胞外泌體分泌的研究策略來進一步證實該研究假說。本項研究將有助於首次揭示骨-軟骨細胞通訊機制在骨關節炎疾病早期的病理生理學功能，可望為骨關節炎的早期診斷和藥物開發提供新線索。

12103519.label: Realisation of objectives
12103519.value: In the study for aim 1, we harvested the osteoclasts-derived miRNA-Knockout exosomes (OCmiR-KO Exo) or osteoclasts-derived miRNA-intact exosomes (OCmiR-Intact Exo) from the OCmiR-KO mice and OCmiR-Intact mice, respectively. We then performed anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT) for establishing the surgery-induced osteoarthritis (OA) model on the OCmiR-KO mice, which were subsequently replenished with four doses of OCmiR-KO exosomes or OCmiR-Intact exosomes after ACLT in a 5-day interval. Burrowing assessment showed that the OCmiR-Intact exosomes-treated mice had significantly lower food pellet weight burrowed than the OCmiR-KD exosomes-treated mice at 2w and 4w after ACLT. Safranin O staining analysis revealed that the cartilage degeneration was markedly advanced in the mice administered with OCmiR-Intact exosomes as compared to those treated with OCmiR-KD exosomes at 4w after ACLT. Immunofluorescent (IF) staining analysis showed that both the number of H-type vessels and CGRP+ sensory axon around the osteochondral junctions were remarkably increased in mice administered with OCmiR-Intact exosomes as compared to those administered with OCmiR-KD exosomes at 4w after ACLT. We then assessed the effect of adeno associated virus (AAV)-mediated intraarticular overexpression of TIMP-2 on ACLT-induced OA development in the aforementioned OCmiR-KO mice administered with OCmiR-Intact Exos. Consistently, we found that the burrowing performance was improved, while the cartilage degeneration as well as the angiogenesis and sensory axon innervation around the osteochondral junctions were all remarkably attenuated, in the mice with intraarticular overexpression of TIMP-2. All these data suggest that osteoclast-derived exosomal miRNAs could suppress the chondrocyte-derived resistant factors, i.e., TIMP-2, by which deprive the resistance of articular cartilage to matrix degeneration, osteochondral angiogenesis and innervation in OA. In the study for aim 2, we blocked the exosome release from osteoclasts in Dicerfl/fl mice (OCExo-BLK) after ACLT by treating the mice with Rab27a siRNAs (7.5 mg/kg) delivered within the OCTDS. The knockdown of Rab27a mRNA specifically in osteoclasts was confirmed by QPCR. MiRNA QPCR array analysis of the serum exosomal miRNA expression showed that 16 miRNAs, were significantly downregulated in OCExo-BLK mice, whereas 8 miRNAs were significantly upregulated in OCExo-BLK mice. QPCR analysis showed that the expression of miR-214-3p, miR-21a-5p, miR-30a-5p and miR-30d-5p in BM OC were not affected in OCExo-BLK mice, whereas their levels in serum OC-exosomes were significantly lower in OCExo-BLK mice than in mice treated with nonsense control RNA (ncRNA, hereafter OCExo-Intact mice) at 2w after ACLT. Data of the burrowing assessment showed that OCExo-BLK mice had significantly higher food pellet weight burrowed than the OCExo-Intact mice at 2w and 4w after ACLT. Interestingly, TRAP staining analysis showed no significant difference in the number of SCB osteoclasts between the OCExo-BLK mice and OCExo-Intact mice at 4w after ACLT. However, Safranin O staining and OARSI scores revealed that the proteoglycan was mostly preserved, while the cartilage degeneration was retarded, in OCExo-BLK mice when compared to OCExo-Intact mice at 4w after ACLT. IF analysis showed that the number of H-type vessels around the osteochondral junctions were remarkably lower in OCExo-BLK mice when compared to OCExo-Intact mice at 4w after ACLT surgery. In addition, the number of CGRP+ sensory axon around the osteochondral junctions were also remarkably lower in OCExo-BLK mice when compared to OCExo-Intact mice at 4w after ACLT surgery. Collectively, these findings suggest that blockage of exosomes secretion from osteoclasts could notably dampen the OA progression in mice after ACLT. Taken together, the two aims of this project were realized. All the findings of this study demonstrated that the osteoclast-derived exosomal miRNAs could inhibit TIMP2 in chondrocytes to promote cartilage degradation, osteochondral angiogenesis and innervation in early OA development.

12103519.label: Major findings and research outcome
12103519.value: Through a combination of genetic and pharmacological approaches, our study demonstrated that osteoclast-derived exosomal miRNAs could inhibit TIMP2 in chondrocytes to promote cartilage degradation, osteochondral angiogenesis and innervation in early OA development. This is the first study to unravel the unique contribution of osteoclast-derived exosomal miRNAs to the early OA development, it also shed light to the development of novel therapeutic strategy for OA. Accordingly, we further developed an osteoclast-targeted exosome inhibitor and performed a proof-of-concept study to show that specifically blockade of exosome release from osteoclasts could attenuate OA development in mice with surgery-induced OA. Our study was published in Nature Aging (Liu et al., Nature Aging 2021, https://doi.org/10.1038/s43587-021-00050-6), which was highlighted by the journal (https://www.nature.com/articles/s43587-021-00052-4). Basing on this study, we also published a protocol to share our lab experience in rapid isolation of osteoclast lineage cell from mouse bone marrow for molecular study of osteoclast biology (Dang et al. Bio-protocol 2022, https://doi.org/10.21769/BioProtoc.4338). In addition, partially supported by this project, we published two review articles that reviewed the action of Cathepsin K in and beyond bone and research progress on liver-bone crosstalk, respectively. Moreover, we presented our research on the development of exosome inhibitor and the preliminary findings on the impact of skeletal muscle microRNA on bone mass that relevant to this project in the International Society for Extracellular Vesicles (ISEV) 2023 annual meeting and the 2023 World Congress on Osteoporosis, Osteoarthritis and Musculoskeletal Diseases (WCO), respectively. Our team member, the PhD student Miss LI Nanxi, also won the Young Investigator Award in the 2023 WCO.

12103519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12103519.value: The current study identified the osteoclast-secreted exosome as a potential therapeutic target for early OA intervention. Hence, it could pave a new avenue toward the drug discovery of exosome inhibitor and the tests of other osteoclast-targeted therapy for OA treatment. Moreover, we have also extended our research to the area of muscle-bone crosstalk, in which we are employing the genetic mouse models and pharmacological tools used in this study to study the contribution of skeletal muscle-derived exosomes in regulating bone.

12103519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12103519.value: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common joint diseases worldwide. However, there are currently no effective interventions for preventing or delaying OA progression due to the limited understanding of the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying this joint disease. In this project, we demonstrated that the bone resorbing osteoclast in subchondral bone could secrete exosomes, a group of extracellular vesicles encapsulating microRNA, to promote cartilage degradation, osteochondral angiogenesis, and innervation in early OA development. Our study unraveled the unique pathophysiological contribution of osteoclast-derived exosome to OA, which warrants the development of osteoclast-targeted exosome inhibitor for OA treatment.

12103919.label: Realisation of objectives
12103919.value: Objective 1: This objective was fully achieved as follows: Raw heshouwu (HSW) were collected from three major production areas in Guizhou Province, Hubei Province and Guangzhou Province. Each batch was divided into three parts; one part was labelled as raw material, and the other two parts were processed using ancient and modern processing methods. Raw samples were softened by wrapping with water-soaked non-cellulose paper, then cut into two botanical parts, i.e. bark (peel) and the rest (flesh). In vitro hepatotoxicity evaluation of HSW and its two botanical parts was performed on the typical human liver cells (L-02). Cell lines were treated with 0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1 and 2 mg/mL of the extractives of raw, peel and flesh of HSW for 24 h at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5 % CO2. The MTT assay was used to assess HSW-induced liver injury in vitro. In vivo hepatotoxicity evaluation of raw HSW and its two botanical parts was performed on SD rats (male, 180-220 g). The rats in the first group (control group) were fed with water only. The rest of the groups were intragastrically administrated with the extracts of HSW, bark part (peel) and the rest part (flesh) from raw HSW at a daily dose of 20 g/kg of the body weight (calculated on the quantity of crude material) for 5 weeks. The general behavior, body weight changes, hazardous symptoms, and mortality of rats were monitored. After treatment, the rats were dissected to collect serum samples for the following biochemical testing. Aspartate aminotransferase (AST), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), total and direct bilirubin (TBIL), total cholesterol (TC), and triglycerides (TG) were quantified on the automatic biochemical analyzer (Hitachi 7060). After treatment with the HSW, peel, and flesh, the corresponding serum, liver, urine, and cecal contents samples in rats of each group were collected and further prepared for metabolomics analysis. The chemical profiles of these serum, liver, urine, and cecal contents samples were characterized by the optimized ultra-performance liquid chromatography coupled with quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS) method. The qualitative and quantitative results were then processed by multivariate statistical analysis (chemometrics), including principal component analysis (PCA) and supervised orthogonal partial least squared discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) to map the distribution patterns and accumulation features of major secondary metabolites in the cork and cortex. The major secondary metabolites in the bark (peel) and the rest (flesh) of HSW were determined by using UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS. The qualitative and quantitative results were then processed by multivariate statistical analysis (chemometrics), including PCA and OPLS-DA, to map the distribution patterns and accumulation features of major secondary metabolites in the cork and cortex. Objective 2: This objective was fully achieved as follows: In vitro hepatotoxicity evaluations of raw and processed HSW from each processing cycle were performed on the typical human liver cells (HepG2). Cell lines were treated with 0, 0.03125, 0.0625, 0.125, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 mg/mL of the extractives of raw and processed HSW from 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 processing cycles for 24 h at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere containing 5 % CO2. The cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8) assay was used to assess HSW-induced liver injury in vitro. In vivo hepatotoxicity evaluations of raw and processed HSW from each processing cycle were performed on SD rats (male, 180-220 g). The rats in the control group were fed with water only. The rest of the groups were intragastrically administrated with the extracts of raw and processed HSW from 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 processing cycles at a daily dose of 20 g/kg of the body weight (calculated on the quantity of crude material) for 5 weeks. After treatment, hepatotoxicity evaluation of raw and processed henhouse from different processing cycles was performed using the methods described in the realisation of objective 1. The processing-induced chemical variation of HSW from different processing cycles was determined by using UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS. The major secondary metabolites in the raw and processed HSW from 1-9 processing cycles were qualitatively and quantitatively determined by using UPLC-QTOF-MS/MS. The qualitative and quantitative results were then processed by multivariate statistical analysis (chemometrics) to characterize the processing-induced chemical variation of HSW. Objective 3: This objective was fully achieved as follows: we conducted an integrated analysis of the chemical profiles and hepatotoxicity in steps 1-2. This analysis aimed to identify potential chemical components that exhibit a significant correlation with the hepatotoxicity of HSW (HSW). By thoroughly examining the chemical composition and its impact on liver health, we were able to pinpoint specific components that may contribute to the hepatotoxicity of HSW. Furthermore, we conducted an extensive literature review to explore the existing knowledge on the hepatotoxicity of the chemical components found in HSW. This additional research provided valuable insights and further substantiated our findings. By combining the results from both the integrated analysis of chemical profiles and hepatotoxicity, as well as the literature research, we were able to identify and establish a set of chemical components that met the necessary criteria. These components were deemed as potential markers responsible for the hepatotoxicity of HSW. Objective 4: This objective was fully achieved as follows: Through the integrated analysis of steps 1-3, we were able to uncover the scientific rationale behind the ancient processing method of HSW. This involved investigating and understanding two key factors, namely peeling or steaming and drying. The comprehensive analysis and evaluation of these factors provided robust evidence to support the notion that the reported liver toxicity associated with HSW in recent years could be attributed to the existing processing method. These finding sheds light on the potential impact of the processing technique on the hepatotoxicity of HSW, highlighting the importance of reevaluating and potentially modifying the current processing approach to ensure the safety and efficacy of this traditional Chinese medicine. Objective 5: This objective was fully achieved as follows: In this project, we utilized the impact of processing on the hepatotoxicity of HSW as a case study. We integrated findings from chemical composition analysis, in vitro and in vivo hepatotoxicity assessments, and in vivo metabolome analysis. These results provide a solid foundation for understanding the processing principles of HSW scientifically. Additionally, this research serves as a model for investigating other traditional Chinese medicines.

12103919.label: Major findings and research outcome
12103919.value: Firstly, our investigation revealed distinct chemical profiles between raw HSW and its two botanical parts, namely the peel and flesh (paper in preparation, publication No.1 in Part C). Additionally, we observed that steaming and drying with different cycles, also resulted in chemical variations in HSW. These findings strongly suggest that the processing techniques, including peeling, steaming and drying, significantly impact the chemical composition of HSW. Secondly, our in vitro hepatotoxicity experiments demonstrated that both HSW and the peel of HSW exhibited higher toxicity compared to the peeled flesh. Furthermore, in the in vivo hepatotoxicity assay, administration of HSW or peel extracts induced abnormalities of liver metabolism, which suggests that HSW and the peel have potential hepatotoxicity (paper in preparation, publication No.1 in Part C). Interestingly, we did not observe any significant differences in the levels of in vitro and in vivo hepatotoxicity between raw and processed HSW with different processing cycles. Based on these findings, we hypothesize that peeling may reduce the hepatotoxicity of HSW, whereas steaming and drying do not significantly affect its hepatotoxicity. Thirdly, among the chemical components analyzed in HSW, peel, and flesh samples, we found that 2,3,5,4'-tetrahydroxylstilbene-2-O-beta-D-glucoside (TSG) and Di-THSG were present in higher levels in HSW, while 2-hydroxyemodin was more abundant in the peel. These metabolites showed a positive correlation with in vitro hepatotoxicity (paper in preparation, publication No.1 in Part C). Moreover, previous studies have reported that TSG and Di-THSG enhance the hepatotoxicity of emodin in HSW, and 2-hydroxyemodin has been shown to be hepatotoxic to human liver cells. Therefore, we propose that these three compounds could serve as potential chemical markers for HSW's hepatotoxicity. Combining the above analyses, we observed that the traditional processing method of peeling significantly alters the chemical profiles of raw HSW, resulting in a reduced degree of hepatotoxicity. In contrast, the current processing method, which excludes peeling off the cork and cortex, may contribute to the hepatotoxicity reported in recent years. Lastly, this study serves as an example of how to approach the investigation of traditional Chinese medicines with unclear processing principles. By integrating chemical composition analysis, in vitro and in vivo hepatotoxicity evaluations, and in vivo metabolome analysis, we aim to provide a scientific basis for understanding the processing principles of such medicines. This methodology can also be applied to studying other traditional Chinese medicines.

12103919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12103919.value: This study has uncovered a significant correlation between processing-induced changes in hepatotoxicity and the variation of secondary metabolites in HSW (heshouwu). These findings provide a solid scientific foundation for understanding the ancient processing method of HSW and offer compelling evidence to support the standardization of its processing techniques to ensure safety. Moving forward, our future plans involve conducting further investigations into the hepatotoxicity of the identified potential chemical markers responsible for HSW's hepatotoxicity. By delving deeper into the underlying mechanisms of these components, we aim to gain a comprehensive understanding of their impact on liver health. This research will contribute to the broader field of knowledge surrounding HSW's hepatotoxicity and potentially lead to the development of safer processing methods in the future.

12103919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12103919.value: Many CMMs are processed before clinical practice, using procedures unique to Chinese medicines, with the aim of reducing the toxicity and/or enhancing the efficacy of CMMs. Clinical case reports on the hepatotoxicity of HSW, have repeatedly surfaced in recent years, attracting widespread concern. In this study, we analyzed the chemical composition, in vitro and in vivo hepatotoxicity, and in vivo metabolomics of HSW to explain the effects of different processing methods on its hepatotoxicity. We found that ancient processing methods, peeling off the cork and cortex, can change the chemical composition of HSW and reduce its liver toxicity. This work can provide information to help determine whether the liver toxicity reported in recent years is linked to the processing method and find out the potential markers responsible for HSW’s hepatotoxicity, so as to ensure its safety and effectiveness in production and use. This project can also provide a scientific basis behind the ancient processing method of HSW, thereby offering evidence to standardize the processing method of HSW to ensure its safety.

12200119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12200119.value: Organic or hyrid organic-inorganic semiconductors are now finding widespread applications in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) and organic photovoltaic (OPV) cells.[1-2] Because of these inspiring developments, numerous efforts have been devoted to understanding the optoelectronic properties of these materials, with particular emphasis on their photophysical and charge transport properties. Much less efforts, however, are focused on the fundamental thermal properties which are closely related to heat dissipation and management in organic-based devices. In OLEDs, electrical energies can be wasted in form of heat rather than light. In an OPV cell, solar energy is wasted as heat, too, rather than extracted charge carriers. How fast heat energy can escape out of an organic device will be determined by the thermal conductivity (or diffusivity) of the organic material. This proposal outlines a contactless photothermal technique for thermal diffusivity measurements. The technique is based on the mirage effect realized by the photothermal deflection measurement (PDM) of a probe beam. We will primarily focus on using PDM to study the thermal diffusivities of organic semiconductors because of their technological relevance and the need to build a data base for their thermal properties which are lacking far behind their optoelectronic properties. The outcome of this proposal should lead to a direct means for quantifying the thermal properties of organic semiconductors or novel electronic materials and better understanding in thermal diffusion in these materials. The thermal properties will be correlated to molecular structures, morphological changes (e.g. arising from additives), and charge carrier transport properties. 有機半導體材料與有機-無機混合半導體材料在發光二極管與光伏領域有著廣泛的應用。由於這些鼓舞人心的發展，人們對該類半導體材料的光電特性，尤其是光物理及載流子傳輸特性的認識逐步加深。然而，卻鮮有關於這類物料的基礎熱學性質的研究。有機物料的熱學性質與器件熱耗散/熱調控過程密切相關。例如，在有機發光二極管中，熱耗散嚴重影響著其電致發光效率。類似地，熱耗散過程同樣嚴重影響著有機光伏器件中的光電轉換效率。熱傳導率（或擴散率）決定著熱能在有機器件中的溢出速度。在此，我們提出了一種用於測試熱擴散率的無觸點式光熱探測技術，該測試的基本原理是表徵由探照激光束的光熱偏轉（PDM）所導致的錯視效應，並以PDM表徵有機半導體中的熱擴散率，建立起相應的熱學數據庫。這項研究令我們進一步理解該類材料中的熱擴散過程，從而將有機半導體材料中的熱學性質與分子結構，形貌變化（添加劑作用）與電荷傳輸等特性建立起來聯繫。

12200119.label: Realisation of objectives
12200119.value: Most objectives outlined in 5.1 have been achieved. We have realized Objective 1 by establishing photothermal deflection measurement setup for studying thermal diffusivities of materials (See e.g. Ref. 1 below). The technique has been coined scanning photothermal deflection (SPD) in our subsequent publications. Realization of Objectives 2 were demonstrated in Refs 1-3 where we showed heat diffusion in semiconducting polymers are correlated to extent of pi-conjugation of the polymer backbones (Ref. 1) as well as the conformations of the molecular structures (Refs. 2-3). Furthermore, we showed that heat diffusion is related to the local morphology of an organic semiconductor or a binary blend, which can contain a mixture of crystalline and amorphous domains (Objectives 3). The amorphous region is detrimental to heat transfer, and the introduction of a small fraction of polymer can facilitate thermal transport. Such a concept has been demonstrated in Refs. 4-6. 12200119.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200119.value: 1. We developed and implemented scanning photothermal deflection (SPD) setup to measure thermal diffusivities of materials. SPD was verified to have excellent agreement with literature, ranging from inorganic to organic materials, and from conductors to semiconductors. We then applied SPD to investigate in details factors leading to low thermal diffusivities in semiconducting polymers. We found that heat transfer in these polymers is mostly phonon-assisted. In general, the thermal diffusivity for conjugated polymers ranks in the order of 2D > 1D > amorphous polymers in the range of 2 to 0.1 mm2^s^-1. Ref. 1: Nano Select 2:768–778 (2021) 2. We showed that there is a definitive relationship between the structure of a molecule and its solid-state heat transfer properties. We applied SPD and investigated heat energy transfer in the very important class of non-fullerene ladder-type acceptors, bearing a core structure of A-DA′D-A type, commonly called Y-acceptors. Effects of different side chains [Ref. 2] and core sizes [Ref. 3] were probed. Side chains affect overall planarity and conformations of the Y-molecules whereas the core size affects the intermolecular pi-pi stacking. Overall, it was found that the heat transfer, as revealed by SPD, is favourable for more planar Y-molecules or those Y-molecules with longer core length. Ref. 2: J. Mater. Chem. A 8, 8566 (2020) Ref. 3: Adv. Funct. Mater. 31, 2101627 (2021). 3. We found that heat diffusion is related to the local morphology of an organic semiconductor. The semiconductor can be a conjugated polymer (e.g. N2200) or small molecule like PCBM. These materials form solid films with amorphous regions, which possess limited heat transfer. Surprisingly, blending “insulating” polystyrene (PS) into these materials improves heat transfer.[refs. 4,6] The blended polymer, however, can also be a semiconducting polymer such as N2200.[Ref. 5] The findings were rationalized by a model in which the blended polymer acts as thermal “bridges”, providing fast thermal transport pathways. Ref. 4: ACS Appl. Mater. & Inter. 14 (26), 30174 (2022). Ref. 5: Appl. Phys. Lett. 120, 143301 (2022) Ref. 6: J. Mater. Chem. C 9, 12281 (2021).

12200119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200119.value: As revealed in Ref. 1, scanning photothermal deflection (SPD) technique is a very reliable technique to measure lateral heat diffusion of any materials. It works for any material thin film that is capable of absorbing the incident laser pump beam. This GRF project looked into organic semiconductors for photovoltaic applications. A HeNe beam (photon energy ~2eV) served as the pump beam. The setup can be easily modified to accommodate other important semiconductors, such as wide bandgap materials. It only involves replacement of the pump beam by a short near UV laser (e.g. a GaN laser).

12200119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200119.value: Heat generation is inevitable in organic electronic devices, and wasted heat often leads to undesirable consequences including thermal degradation of materials and device performance. Thus, means of estimating how fast heat energy migrates out of the organic film is highly desirable. This project developed and implemented a contactless scanning photothermal (SPD) technique for measuring thermal diffusivity of organic thin films. The technique is based on the mirage effect realized by the photothermal deflection of a probe beam. We demonstrated that SPD is broadly applicable to all thin film materials, ranging from organic semiconductors, conjugated polymers for solar cell applications, to crystalline semiconductors of high thermal diffusivities.(Ref. 1) Specifically, we showed that for organic semiconductors, heat diffusion is strongly correlated with the nanoscale molecular structures of the molecules and their relative organization. Heat diffusion is more favorable for planar or long molecular chains.(Refs. 2, 3) At the same time, polymers dispersed in organic semiconductors with low thermal diffusivities can serve as heat conduction pathways, facilitating the diffusion of heat.(Refs. 4-6) The outcomes of this project offer a tangible method for quantifying the thermal properties of organic semiconductors and lead to better understanding in heat diffusion of these materials.

12200819.value: To design gas-efficient ADSs for supporting authenticated search in hybrid-storage blockchain systems; To develop verifiable search algorithms to allow users to check the correctness of off-chain search results; To explore optimization techniques that can strike a balance between gas cost and search performance; To perform security/cost analysis of the proposed techniques and algorithms and evaluate their performance in real blockchain systems.

12200819.label: Realisation of objectives
12200819.value: The project objectives have been successfully achieved. We have investigated integrity-assured keyword searches in hybrid-storage blockchains. Our proposal introduces a new gas-efficient ADS named the Suppressed Merkle inverted (Merkle^{inv}) index, aimed at reducing smart contract maintenance costs while preserving query efficiency. The main idea involves the smart contract solely maintaining the root digest of each MB-tree in the Merkle^{inv} index. This approach is based on the observation that, for on-chain ADS, only the root digests are utilized during authenticated keyword searches. However, updating the root digests upon the arrival of new objects necessitates the service provider to send an update proof – authenticated information enabling secure computation of the new root digests – to the smart contract. Maintaining the Suppressed Merkle^{inv} index demands constant (costly) storage operations and logarithmic (inexpensive) memory operations, ultimately achieving an overall reduction in gas costs. To further diminish the ADS maintenance cost, we proposed another novel index called the Chameleon inverted (Chameleon^{inv}) index, leveraging the Chameleon Vector Commitment (CVC) to achieve constant maintenance costs. CVC allows public verification of data stored in a vector, enabling the data owner to update the vector without altering its commitment, using a secret trapdoor. This property facilitates building a Chameleon tree with an invariant root commitment. In the Chameleon^{inv} index, each keyword corresponds to a Chameleon tree, where the smart contract maintains the root commitments with auxiliary data of the Chameleon^{inv} index, while the service provider manages the complete index for efficient query processing. Additionally, for enhanced query and verification performance, we proposed an optimized Chameleon^{inv}* index, where the smart contract maintains an additional Bloom filter for each group of objects in every Chameleon tree. These Bloom filters assist in testing non-existing objects, thereby improving query and verification performance. Moreover, to safeguard data and query privacy, we developed a novel hybrid index enabling verifiable and secure conjunctive keyword searches in hybrid-storage blockchains. This hybrid index comprises three forms: (1) an inverted index named MIK-tree in the data owner, where each keyword corresponds to a Merkle BinarySort Tree indexing included file identifiers; (2) a MIK^{kv}-tree in key-value pairs encrypted by searchable symmetric encryption (SSE) for privacy-preserving searches with sub-linear query time; (3) a MIK^{sup}-tree representing a hash digest of the root node of MIK-tree in the blockchain to ensure the integrity of query results. To verify dynamic updates, we customized the forward-privacy file update and search protocols by using a carefully designed fresh search token for newly updated files and indexes, which hinders the association between the newly updated files and the previous search tokens. In addition, we leveraged the Multi-Set Hash and the immutable property of the blockchain to guarantee the correctness of the updated files. To further accelerate the performance of query and verification, we proposed a partition-based scheme, which partitions MIK^{kv}-tree into some sub-trees based on a predefined threshold to avoid invalid checks and accelerate search termination. We also proposed an obfuscated counting Bloom filter-based scheme, which improves verification performance and search efficiency when there is no matched file without sacrificing privacy. In addition, we developed a novel blockchain system ensuring query integrity by employing a verifiable query framework. Specifically, we proposed an optimized scheme, vChain+, supporting efficient verifiable Boolean range queries with additional features. Our proposal includes a sliding-window accumulator index for efficient query processing even in the worst-case scenarios. Furthermore, we designed an object registration index enabling practical public key management without compromising security guarantees. To facilitate rich verifiable queries on lightweight clients, we introduced DCert, a novel decentralized certification framework certifying authenticated indexes for various query types on an as-needed basis. Additionally, we designed a blockchain-based verifiable and auditable framework ensuring the correctness of federated learning procedures. The proposed techniques and systems have been validated through theoretical analysis and extensive experiments.

12200819.label: Major findings and research outcome
12200819.value: We have explored various innovative search techniques in hybrid-storage blockchain systems, with a focus on ensuring the integrity of search results and optimizing query processing. We have proposed novel authenticated data structures such as the Suppressed Merkle inverted index and the Chameleon inverted index, aiming to reduce smart contract maintenance costs while preserving query efficiency. Additionally, we have developed hybrid index schemes to guarantee verifiable and secure conjunctive keyword searches in hybrid-storage blockchains. Our proposed optimized solutions, like vChain+ and DCert, enable efficient verification of queries and decentralized certification for diverse query types. Furthermore, our study has examined the fairness of blockchain incentive protocols and developed a new verifiable and auditable framework to ensure the accuracy of federated learning procedures. The research findings have been published in esteemed conferences and journals, including SIGMOD '20, SIGMOD '21, ICDE '21, ICDE '22, Middleware '22, TNSE, and TKDE.

12200819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12200819.value: For further development, we will investigate methods to enhance scalability in hybrid-storage blockchain systems. This could involve exploring sharding techniques or other scaling solutions to efficiently handle larger volumes of data and queries. Additionally, it would be interesting to study privacy-preserving techniques to strengthen privacy and access control measures in verifiable query processing. Another potential area worthy of further investigation is verifiable queries in multi-chain environments. This particular aspect presents several challenges for the querying system. First, the system must be compatible with existing blockchains, without requiring any modifications to their underlying structures or protocols, which ensures smooth integration with various blockchain networks. Second, the system should support a wide range of query types to meet the diverse and evolving data analysis needs of users. Ideally, the system should be flexible enough to seamlessly integrate with a variety of existing database engines to provide comprehensive query capabilities.

12200819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12200819.value: Blockchain has recently emerged as a promising solution for providing trustworthy storage and computation for decentralized applications. While blockchain technology has many advantages such as immutability and traceability, its resource-consuming consensus mechanism limits performance and scalability. To scale blockchain systems, recent research has suggested a hybrid storage architecture, where only small metadata is stored on-chain while raw data is outsourced to off-chain storage (e.g., Amazon S3 or Google Cloud Storage). The on-chain metadata is used to authenticate the data retrieved from the off-chain storage. However, existing studies have only considered data retrieval by specific keys. In this project, we aim to investigate efficient techniques to enable integrity-assured searches in hybrid-storage blockchain systems. We have designed several authenticated data structures and verifiable search algorithms to allow users to check the correctness of search results returned by the off-chain storage. We have also developed optimization techniques to strike a balance between the blockchain cost and search performance. Both theoretical analysis and empirical experiments have been conducted to validate the proposed techniques and algorithms.

12201119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201119.value: 近年來大量的知識網絡被創建出來，例如開源知識庫（YAGO）、維基百科的結構化數據（DBpedia）、協作知識庫（Freebase）以及谷歌知識圖譜。其中本體（Ontology）信息通常通過實體（Entity）之間的定義和語義關係進行編碼，附帶在知識網絡。近年來，很多新興的應用都建立在本體信息之上。在此項目，我們提出首個利用本體語義通用的索引圖數據的模型，從而提升查詢性能。我們簡稱該模型為語義索引。 雖然語義索引旨在提出一個通用概念，但是為了更具體地說明它的潛力，本項目著重於圖數據上的關鍵詞查詢。因為關鍵詞查詢不單具有其易用的特點，也是很多知識網絡應用的基礎。 在任務一中，我們提出一個基於本體信息的索引結構創建。首先，我們展示了語義相近的一些實體可以利用這些實體的共同父類進行泛化，實體泛化可以降低所索引的實體關係的異構性。其次，我們對泛化後的圖進行概括進而得到一個較小的圖。重複迭代上述兩個步驟，直到概括圖足夠小為止。我們所提出的語義索引就是由一系列的概括圖層構成的。 在任務二中，我們將最前沿的關鍵詞查詢算法整合於語義索引當中。現有關鍵詞查詢算法的核心包含了反向搜索、實體之間的最短距離查詢以及匹配關鍵詞查詢的實體枚舉。由於語義索引結構也是一個圖，我們期望現有在圖數據上的關鍵詞查詢算法能無縫地實現在該索引上。 本體信息為關鍵詞查詢提供了新的優化的機會。在任務三中，我們面向探索性數據分析（EDA）設計了關鍵詞查詢的高效算法。在EDA中，用戶可以發出查詢請求並且檢驗查詢結果，進而幫助用戶改良查詢並且加快下一次（語義相關的）查詢的速度。例如，對於一項關鍵詞查詢，如果另外一項關鍵詞查詢僅有一個關鍵詞與之不同，所不同的關鍵詞在本體圖中是連通並且距離不超過k跳，我們便稱其為語義相關查詢。 最後，在任務四中，我們將會研究在特定領域的知識庫上的高效關鍵詞查詢，例如PubMed和基因本體圖。此外，因為用戶通常持有自己的私有知識網絡，所以我們研究存在附加語義信息的增量式查詢算法。 本項目為在圖數據上的關鍵詞搜索提供一種新的索引方法。它能進一步提高最前沿算法的效率。

12201119.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201119.value: We start the project by proposing a generic ontology-based indexing framework for keyword search, called Bisimulation of Generalized Graph Index (BiG-index) [TKDE20a], to enhance the search performance. BiG-index uses an ontology graph to summarize and index a data graph iteratively to form a hierarchical index structure. To illustrate BiG-index’s applicability and efficiency, we show popular indexing techniques for keyword search (e.g., Blinks and r-clique) can be easily implemented on top of BiG-index. Our extensive experiments show that BiG-index is efficient. We then study its support of data exploration with a new research problem of budget constrained interactive graph search for multiple targets called kBM-IGS problem [PVLDB21]. We develop a novel framework to search using the best keyword node with the largest expected gain, which provides a balanced trade-off between the likelihood of searching the targets and the gain of information. Experiments verify both the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithms. In addition, the team considers a popular scenario of multiple graphs [ICDE20], where some graphs are public while some others are private. Specifically, we study public-private keyword search (PPKWS). In PPKWS, we revisit the query algorithms and indexing. We show that three representative keyword searches can be implemented on the PPWKS model with minor modifications. In addition, the team has proposed distributed keyword search, called DKWS [TKDE24], which enables efficient search over multiple graphs (by combining them into one large graph). Finally, this project studies ways to make keyword searches more usable. We offer a way for use to explore data is to do so via a graphical user interface (GUI), and the GUI provides guidance to data exploration [TKDE20b]. Reference: [PVLDB21] X. Zhu et al. 12201119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201119.value: This project aims to make it easier and more efficient to find information using keyword searches on graph data (such as knowledge graphs and ontologies), much like how users might use Google to find websites. We have proposed a new indexing scheme, the BiG-index, to organize information so that the searches can be both faster and more accurate. This index is versatile and can work with other well-known keyword search methods and make an impact on the literature. This project also investigates how to handle searches when dealing with different types of graphs: some are public, whereas some are private. Our research proposes efficient ways to search through such graphs. Furthermore, we have developed a distributed keyword search algorithm called DKWS that lets users search large graphs efficiently. Finally, we have made it easier and more efficient for users to explore graph data. We worked on summarizing ontologies to help users formulate their keyword searches and proposed interactive keyword searches so users could explore graph data. We developed a user-friendly visual search interface, which helps make the exploration intuitive.

12201219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201219.value: Leveraging of the data from electronic health records (EHR) for predictive analytics in healthcare has received increasing attention in recent years. High-throughput phenotyping refers to the use of machine learning to derive phenotypes (sets of clinical conditions) from the EHR data to characterize patients' disease states. Most phenotyping algorithms are developed only on the basis of records of discrete clinical events such as diagnoses and medications. For better phenotyping and patient characterization, multiple data modalities (such as laboratory test results, progress notes and vital signs) should be considered. Fusing the multi-modal EHR data for analytics is not trivial because the data are of different types, contain noisy and missing information, and are related in a complex manner. In this project, we propose the use of a temporal tensor factorization framework to infer highly interpretable phenotypes and dynamic patient representations from multi-modal EHR data, and a number of underlying research challenges will be addressed. First, even though tensor factorization is useful for phenotyping, the interaction information of the clinical events is in fact missing and thus the tensor is often defined via heuristics. We propose to infer the latent temporal tensor and perform factorization under a unified framework. Second, determination of an appropriate time scale is crucial to obtain more robust phenotyping results using tensor factorization. We propose to extend the framework to a multi-scale version so that factorization of the clinical data at multiple time scales can be considered simultaneously. Also, because the nursing progress notes contain additional health related information on patients, we propose to incorporate them using a character-aware neural model to embed the progress notes into a vector space and a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model sequences of progress notes. The RNN can then be coupled with the temporal tensor framework for joint learning. In addition, we propose to link the disease state of a patient captured by the tensor framework with a physiological time series model to allow phenotype-based predictive analytics based on the patient monitoring data. The whole proposed framework will be learned end-to-end and implemented on machines with graphics processing units. For performance evaluation, we will apply the proposed methods to the MIMIC III Critical Care database which contains electronic health records with multi-modal data. The empirical results will also undergo qualitative evaluation by clinicians. 近年來，利用電子健康記錄（EHR）中的數據進行醫療保健中的預測分析已經受到越來越多的關注。高通量表型分析是指利用機器學習從EHR數據中推導出表型（臨床條件集），以表徵患者的疾病狀態。大多數表型分析算法僅基於離散臨床事件（例如診斷和藥物）的記錄而開發。為了更好地進行表型分析和患者表徵，應考慮多種數據模式（如實驗室檢測結果，進展記錄和生命體徵）。融合多模態EHR數據進行分析的難點，包括數據類型不同，同時包含噪聲和缺失信息，並且互相間的關聯複雜。 在這個項目中，我們將研究使用時間張量分解框架從多模態EHR數據中推斷高度可解釋的表型和動態患者表示，並將解決當中潛在的研究挑戰。首先，儘管張量因子分解對於表型分析是有用的，但臨床事件的相互作用信息實際上是缺失的，因此張量通常通過人為方式來定義。我們提出推斷潛在的時間張量並在統一的框架下進行因子分解。其次，確定適當的時間尺度對於使用張量分解獲得更穩健的表型分析結果至關重要。我們提出將框架擴展到多尺度版本，以便可以同時考慮多個時間尺度的臨床數據的因子分解。此外，由於護理進度記錄包含有關患者的其他健康相關信息，我們建議使用基於字母的神經模型將它們合併，以將進展記錄嵌入向量空間和循環神經網絡（RNN）以模擬進展記錄的序列。然後，RNN可以與時間張量框架耦合以用於聯合學習。此外，我們提出將由張量框架捕獲的患者的疾病狀態與生理時間序列模型聯繫起來，以學習出來的表型及患者監測數據作出預測分析。整個提議的框架將以端至端方式學習，並在具有圖形處理單元的機器上實現。對於性能評估，我們將建議的方法應用於MIMIC III重症監護數據庫，該數據庫包含具有多模態數據的電子健康記錄。實證結果也將由臨床醫生進行定性評估。

12201219.label: Realisation of objectives
12201219.value: Objective 1: To develop a temporal tensor factorization framework for joint learning of hidden interaction of clinical events, phenotypes, and dynamic patient representation from the structured data from electronic health records. We have developed a collective hidden interaction tensor factorization framework which can be applicable to the EHR data with multiple modalities. At the same time, other than quantitative evaluation, a comprehensive evaluation including evaluation by clinicians have been conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method as compared to other state-of-the-art methods. This outcome has been published in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering. Publication: Kejing Yin, William K. Cheung, Benjamin C. M. Fung, Jonathan Poon. Learning Inter-Modal Correspondence and Phenotypes from Multi-Modal Electronic Health Records. IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering, 2020. Objective 2: To develop a multi-scale temporal tensor factorization algorithm to support more robust discovery of phenotypes and the use of deep models to regularize the dynamic patient representation. When we further look into the challenge, the multiple time scale challenge exists together with the irregular time intervals between clinical events, especially for chronic diseases. We propose a new temporal tensor factorization called TedPar that can learn the temporal dependency between clinical events with their inter-event time intervals considered for some target disease. It also learns a set of target phenotypes to capture the clinical features relevant to the diseases of interest and a set of background phenotypes to capture irrelevant but frequently co-occurring clinical features. TedPar is found to be effective in modelling the EHR data and extracting more clinically meaningful phenotypes as confirmed by clinicians. Publication: Kejing Yin, William K. Cheung, Benjamin C. M. Fung, Jonathan Poon. TedPar: Temporally Dependent PARAFAC2 Factorization for Phenotype-based Disease Progression Modeling. in Proceedings of the 2021 SIAM International Conference on Data Mining, 2021. Objective 3: To integrate sequences of progress notes into the temporal tensor factorization framework via coupled recurrent neural networks for enhancement of phenotyping accuracy. While we are examining the progress notes, we notice that sometimes only the information corresponding to the key problems of the patients is reported, making the missing information in fact unavoidable in progress notes. We thus extended the popular PARAFAC2 Factorization method to impute the temporal binary data using ideas borrowed from the PU learning so as to make the factorization more robust towards missing. We have published this work in SIGKDD conferences. Publication: Kejing Yin, Ardavan Afshar, Joyce C. Ho, William K. Cheung, Chao Zhang, Jimeng Sun. “LogPar: Logistic PARAFAC2 Factorization for Temporal Binary Data with Missing Values,” In Proceedings of the 26th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining, 2020. When we further work on the problem, we noticed that missing not at random is a serious issue where existing data imputation methods assuming missing at random (like PU learning which was used adopted in KDD paper) is insufficient. The problem also goes beyond what progress notes can supplement. We then develop a propensity-adjusted temporal network (PATNet) to conduct data imputation and predictive analysis simultaneously. PATNet contains three subnetworks: 1) an imputation subnetwork that generates the initial imputation based on historical observations, 2) a propensity subnetwork that infers the patient-, feature-, and time-dependent propensity scores, and 3) a prediction subnetwork that produces the missing-informative prediction using the propensity-adjusted imputations and the missing probabilities. The proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of binary data imputation, disease progression modeling, and mortality prediction tasks. We have published that work in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering. Publication: Kejing Yin, Dong Qian, William K. Cheung. “PATNet: Propensity-Adjusted Temporal Network for Joint Imputation and Prediction using Binary EHRs with Observation Bias,” IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (published online: Oct 13, 2023) Objective 4: To integrate physiological monitoring data into the proposed framework with a deep time series model to enable phenotype-aware times series modeling for adaptive real-time predictive analytics. To explore the multi-modality idea, we have integrated the EHR time series data with the X-ray images from MIMIC-V by making use a novel logit pooling to adaptively fuse the shared and distinct representations of the time series and x-ray images via disease-aware attention with promising results obtained on disease prediction. This work has been accepted for presentation in AAAI’24. Publication: Wenfang Yao, Kejing Yin, William K. Cheung, Jia Liu, Jing Qin. “DrFuse: Learning Disentangled Representation for Clinical Multi-Modal Fusion with Missing Modality and Modal Inconsistency”, to appear in Proceedings of The 38th Annual AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI’2024)

12201219.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201219.value: We developed a set of tensor factorization algorithms which can be applicable to the EHR data for addressing fundamental challenges face when applied for high-throughput computational phenotyping and predictive analytics. They include: i) CHITF [TKDE’22] which infers hidden associations among clinical events (e.g., diseases and medication) while learning the phenotypes at the same time. We found that the inferring the hidden interactions can effectively enhance the prediction accuracy based on the phenotypes learned; ii) LogPar [KDD’20] which extends the irregular tensor factorization method PARAFAC2 to impute the temporal binary data with missing at random considered using PU learning. By carefully capturing the missingness to distinguish the situation between missing and absence, more robust version of PARAFAC2 towards missing was derived; iii) TedPar [SIAM’21] which is a novel temporal tensor factorization method that takes into consideration irregular time intervals between clinical events to learn their temporal dependency for some target disease. It also learns a set of target phenotypes to capture the clinical features relevant to the diseases of interest and a set of background phenotypes to capture irrelevant but frequently co-occurring clinical features; iv) PATNet [TKDE’23] which can handle missing not at random settings in EHR data using a model architecture with three subnetworks: 1) an imputation subnetwork that generates the initial imputation based on historical observations, 2) a propensity subnetwork that infers the patient-, feature-, and time-dependent propensity scores, and 3) a prediction subnetwork that produces the missing-informative prediction using the propensity-adjusted imputations and the missing probabilities. For all the proposed methods, we conducted extensive quantitative evaluation using the benchmark datasets (e.g., MIMIC-III and eICU) and demonstrated that they can outperform the state-of-the-art methods in terms of prediction tasks like mortality prediction, disease progression modeling, etc. We also conducted qualitative evaluation on the extracted phenotypes by consulting clinicians and found that the effort on carefully designing the model based on some prior clinical knowledge can lead to more clinically meaningful phenotypes to be identified.

12201219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201219.value: The EHR data analytics methods developed for computational phenotyping and predictive analytics have been shown promising results. This project focuses on addressing the challenges caused by diverse types of missing data in order to increase the accuracy of the predictive analytics. It forms a good foundation so that other important challenges encountered in the EHR data can be further addressed, including causality among the clinical events, the selection bias typically encountered in treatment effect estimation, etc., which can further contribute to the long-term goal of enhancing the reliability of the analytics methods. We will continue to apply for basic research funding to support future investigation. In addition, the methods developed are generic. For real-world deployment, they can be further customized for the settings of specific diseases to enhance their applicability. We will also explore related applied research funding and/or deployment opportunities.

12201219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201219.value: The EHR data is complex, and yet embedded with rich clinical knowledge. In this project, a number of EHR data analytics methods were carefully designed and developed for computational phenotyping and predictive analytics. The analytics methods were developed with special focus to address diverse types of missing data challenges typically encountered in EHR data. Therefore, their prediction effectiveness and clinical correctness can outperform the state-of-the-art methods. Also, as the methods are developed by an interdisciplinary research team with careful consideration of the problem nature and clinical knowledge, the higher prediction accuracy achieved comes together with more clinically meaningful (and thus interpretable) phenotypes to be identified. We consider this to be important for applying analytics in practice, and believe that the approaches developed and evaluated to be effective have the potential to be further investigated for real-world deployment.

12201619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12201619.value: The goal of this project is to develop and demonstrate a novel spatio-temporal learning (STL) framework to overcome the fundamental challenges of data heterogeneity, dependency, and noise in a systematic way for spatio-temporal predictive analytics. Spatio-temporal predictive analytics, which aims to analyze and model data with both spatial and temporal information for future prediction and forecasting, has long attracted extensive research interest and has assumed increasing importance as the massive increases in both data availability and data diversity make spatio-temporal data more ubiquitous than ever. The problem of modeling spatio-temporal data is interesting and important but quite challenging due to (1) substantial data heterogeneity in terms of data formats, sizes, and resolutions; (2) complex data dependency at varying spatio-temporal scales within and/or across heterogenous data sources; and (3) various types of noise in the heterogenous spatio-temporal data. To tackle these fundamental challenges, in this project, we will develop a novel STL framework that effectively integrates, models, and analyzes the spatio-temporal data for predictive analytics. Under the STL framework, we will further propose three new methods: (1) An STL method with Tensor representation (referred to as STL-T) to effectively integrate data from heterogeneous sources while preserving the intrinsic spatio-temporal structure of data from each source via tensor-based operations. (2) An STL-T method with Deep architecture (referred to as STL-TD) to quantitatively characterize, effectively learn, and faithfully interpret the complex dependency of heterogenous spatio-temporal data. (3) An STL-TD method with Regularizer (referred to as STL-TDR) to address various sources of data noise for robust spatio-temporal predictive analytics. To investigate these issues in a systematic way, we will (i) formally define and formulate the problems; (ii) theoretically analyze the developed formulations and models; (iii) computationally validate the solutions; and (iv) practically evaluate the proposed framework and methods in three real-world scenarios with domain-specific implementations. The proposed framework and methods are general in nature and will contribute to both machine learning foundations and data analytics techniques in academia. The results derived from the proposed framework and methods, especially in the era of big data, will have practical benefit in challenging application domains of spatio-temporal predictive analytics, such as epidemiology, transportation, and climate science. This project will nurture local talent in the field by creating training and research opportunities for both undergraduate and graduate students. 该项目致力于开发与展示一种新颖的时空学习（STL）框架，从而以一种系统的方式解决时空预测分析中的数据异构性，相关性，以及噪声等根本性问题。 时空预测分析旨在通过对数据中的时间与空间信息进行分析与建模，对未来的情形做出有效的预测。该项研究长期以来受到学者们的广泛关注，并随着时空数据的规模日渐增加以及其多样性而显得愈发重要。时空数据的建模问题有趣而重要，但十分具有挑战性，其原因如下：（1）多源数据在形式，规模，分辨率等多方面存在大量异构性；（2）多源异构数据在不同的时空尺度上存在复杂的相关性；以及（3）多源异构数据中存在多种类型的数据噪声。 为解决以上时空预测分析中所存在的根本性问题，我们在该项目中开发了一种新颖的STL框架，通过对时空数据进行有效的整合与建模，为预测分析服务。在此框架下，我们进而提出三种新颖的方法：（1）一种基于张量（Tensor）表示的STL方法（简称为STL-T），旨在有效的整合来自不同数据源的数据，并保持其内在的时空张量结构；（2）一种包含深度（Deep）结构的STL-T方法（简称为STL-TD），旨在量化，刻画，学习，与解释异构时空数据间的复杂相关性；（3）一种包含正则项的STL-TD方法（简称为STL-TDR），旨在解决不同类型的数据噪声以达到鲁棒的时空预测分析。 为对以上议题进行系统的研究，我们将（i）对问题进行规范的定义以及通过公式进行阐述；（ii）对提出的公式以及开发的模型进行理论分析；（iii）对得到的解进行计算验证；以及（iv）对提出的框架与方法在三个真实世界的场景中进行实际评估。 该项目所提出的框架与方法在本质上具有普适性与一般性，将对学术界的机器学习基础以及数据分析技术有所贡献。从所提出的框架和方法中产出的结果，尤其是在目前的大数据时代，将为多个时空预测分析的应用领域（如流行病学，交通运输，以及气候科学）带来实际效益。该项目将通过为本科生与研究生创造接受培训和参与研究的机会，为当地培养本领域的拔尖人才

12201619.label: Realisation of objectives
12201619.value: In this project, all set objectives have been fully realized. To fulfill the objectives outlined in Section 5.1, we designed a detailed research plan and strictly followed our plan to accomplish the specified tasks. As reported in our Mid-Term Progress Report, following the submission of our proposal in November 2018, we started our investigation immediately. To validate the feasibility of the proposed idea, we began by formally defining the problem of STL and mathematically formulating the proposed objective functions of STL (Objective 1). Subsequently, we developed a novel deep architecture for STL and an information-theoretic framework for a rigorous theoretical analysis. We conducted a series of experiments on three real-world STL tasks: infectious disease prediction, traffic flow forecasting, and climate prediction, as initially planned in our proposal. The results of this feasibility study have been published in [1]. Following this preliminary study, we conducted some preparation work for addressing the challenges of data heterogeneity and dependency in STL, which was important to confirm the viability of our proposed concepts and to set a clear analytical framework for subsequent research activities. To achieve this goal, we approached STL as a variant of multi-task learning (MTL). Here, uncovering spatio-temporal dependencies corresponds to discovering connections between different learning tasks. We introduced a metric-guided MTL method that measures the dependencies, i.e., task relationships, by integrating a metric-guided regularizer into the objective function (Objective 2). The results of this research have been published in [2]. To improve the STL framework's generalizability, we focused on two enhancements: increasing training efficiency in high spatial dimensions, and augmenting model adaptability for new covariates or target variables. Our solution, mesoscale anisotropically-connected learning, addressed both issues (Objective 2). For efficiency, it clustered data by spatial proximity at the mesoscale and made predictions within each cluster, using an information exchange mechanism to leverage insights from adjacent clusters. For adaptability, it employed a local updating strategy that incorporated new covariates and target variables. The results of this research have been published in [3]. To advance our theoretical understanding of the STL framework and models, we investigated a particularly challenging task: predicting chaotic time series, characterized by highly irregular and unpredictable dynamics. We introduced a new information tracking mechanism to capture and adapt to chaotic changes over time (Objective 2). This mechanism utilized a probabilistic feedback approach, which refined the prediction for the subsequent time step based on the current forecast's error. Through rigorous theoretical analysis and comprehensive empirical evaluation (Objective 3), we demonstrated that our method effectively captured the essence of chaotic behavior, as indicated by two indexes of chaotic behavior, the Lyapunov and Hurst exponents. The results of this research have been published in [4]. To assess the STL framework's real-world efficacy, we selected infectious disease prediction as a case study, addressing the common issue of missing or noisy data (Objective 1). We developed two methods to tackle this (Objective 2). The first one, a deep transfer learning technique, leveraged patterns from data-rich regions/locations to enhance predictions in regions with limited or missing data. This method's effectiveness in capturing transmission dynamics and predicting disease risk, despite incomplete data, was confirmed in studies across seven major cities during the COVID-19 pandemic (Objective 3), as reported in [5]. The second approach, an epidemiology-regularized deep learning model, aimed at mitigating the impact of noisy data by incorporating the next-generation matrix (NGM) into its architecture as the regularizer and an additional learning objective. This integration allowed the model to account for mechanistic models and human mobility, providing a comprehensive characterization of disease transmission both within and between locations. Its effectiveness was validated using real-world data on influenza-like illnesses (Objective 3), with findings published in [6]. References: [1] Qi Tan, Yang Liu, and Jiming Liu*, Demystifying deep learning in predictive spatiotemporal analytics: An information-theoretic framework, IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, 32(8), pp. 3538-3552, 2021. [2] Jinfu Ren, Yang Liu, and Jiming Liu*, Metric-guided multi-task learning, in Proceedings of the 25th International Symposium on Methodologies for Intelligent Systems (ISMIS-2020), LNAI 12117, pp. 21–31, 2020. [3] Qi Tan, Yang Liu, and Jiming Liu*, Mesoscale anisotropically-connected learning, in Proceedings of the 25th International Symposium on Methodologies for Intelligent Systems (ISMIS-2020), LNAI 12117, pp. 171–180, 2020. [4] Jinfu Ren, Yang Liu, and Jiming Liu*, Chaotic behavior learning via information tracking, Chaos, Solitons & Fractals, 175(1): 113927, 2023. [5] Jinfu Ren, Mutong Liu, Yang Liu, and Jiming Liu*, TransCode: Uncovering COVID-19 transmission patterns via deep learning, Infectious Diseases of Poverty, 12, 14, 2023.
