12201619.label: Major findings and research outcome
12201619.value: In this project, we have developed a novel spatio-temporal learning (STL) framework and a series of STL methods to tackle the key challenges of data heterogeneity, dependency, and noise in spatio-temporal predictive analytics. Through rigorous theoretical analysis and systematic empirical validation on both synthetic and real-world datasets, we have proven that our STL framework and methods are effective in integrating heterogeneous data from various sources, extracting and representing the complex and multi-scale dependency of spatio-temporal data for predictive analytics, and managing noisy and incomplete data. Additionally, our in-depth case study on infectious disease modeling and prediction provided valuable insights for policy making and intervention strategies in disease management. This project's research findings have been published in reputable journals and conferences in the computer science, applied mathematics/physics, and public health domains. Four of the six project-related papers are in computer science, one is in applied mathematics/physics, and one is in public health. Specifically, in computer science, we have published: one paper in the IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems (2023 Journal Impact Factor: 10.4); one paper at the 32nd ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM-2023); and two papers at the 25th International Symposium on Methodologies for Intelligent Systems (ISMIS-20). In applied mathematics/physics, we have published: one paper in Chaos, Solitons & Fractals (2023 Journal Impact Factor: 7.8; CiteScore: 13.2, ranked #2/85 in Mathematical Physics). In public health, we have published: one paper in Infectious Diseases of Poverty (2023 Journal Impact Factor: 8.1; ranked in Q1 in three JCR Categories: Infectious Diseases, Tropical Medicine, and Parasitology). These interdisciplinary research outcomes, which have been peer-reviewed and recognized by experts from multiple domains, demonstrated the significance and practicality of our advancements in both the development of machine learning methodologies and their applications to real-world challenges.

12201619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12201619.value: Future work will be carried out on several aspects. Firstly, we plan to incorporate a variety of advanced deep learning architectures to enhance the framework's ability to capture complex patterns and adapt to diverse real-world scenarios. This will enhance the framework's representation capabilities, allowing it to handle a broader array of complex situations. Secondly, we will integrate specific domain knowledge into our framework, such as using compartment models for tracking infectious diseases and employing global climate models. This will not only improve the interpretability of our methods but also enhance their applicability and accuracy in practical settings. Thirdly, we will combine our existing framework with reinforcement learning techniques. This fusion aims to leverage predictive insights to inform and optimize decision-making processes. Lastly, our ongoing collaboration with the National Center for Parasitology, Entomology, and Malaria Control of Cambodia is a priority. We will continue deploying our AI methods and tools in Cambodia, with the goal of supporting and accelerating the elimination of malaria in the region. Through these efforts, we aim to deliver a further improved STL framework with real-world impact.

12201619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12201619.value: In our project, we have innovatively addressed the challenge of understanding complex patterns in data that vary across both space and time—such as the spread of diseases, traffic flows, or climate changes. We developed a framework for spatio-temporal learning (STL), capable of making sense of disparate data sources and discovering the intrinsic relationships within them, even when the data is incomplete or contains errors. Our STL framework is able to recognize and interpret the complex dependencies inherent in spatiotemporal data, which is critical for making accurate forecasts in various real-world situations. For example, it can predict the spread of infectious diseases by analyzing trends from different locations, even if some data is missing or inaccurate due to reporting discrepancies, which is invaluable for strategic planning in public health. We have validated our methods through extensive testing and have shared our findings in a range of respected scientific publications. Our work not only advances the field of artificial intelligence but also provides practical tools for tackling complex predictive problems in a world where data is vast but often imperfect.

12300019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300019.value: The main problem of commercial available molecular imaging agents such as fluorescein is high background noises during microscopy study. These noises are caused by biological samples’ autofluorescence scattering light from solid substrates, and lastly the luminescence from the optical components. For this purpose, more attention has been focused on the time-resolved fluorescent technique and using lanthanide complexes as imaging labels. Time-resolved spectroscopy can determine the excited lifetimes which provide insight of the excited dynamics and the decay pathways of the excited chromophore/materials. With this technique, it is possible, for example, to extract information based on differences in their fluorescence lifetime. The autofluoresence is happened in nano to few micro-second scales. The emission lifetime of lanthanide is in micro-milli second scale which is perfect for time-resolved imaging, especially lined up with the higher tissue penetration near-infrared II (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) emissive lanthanide ion, such as ytterbium/erbium/neodymium. However, most reported time-resolved lanthanide probes was only available in visible to NIR-I region (700-1000 nm) and non-specific in vitro. In this project, we are going to develop new lanthanide bioprobes (ytterbium/erbium) for time-resolved NIR-II imaging and targeting key functional protein for EBV associated cancer growth-BS69. The guideline for selection of NIR-II probe via its brightness and emission quantum yield will be demonstrated. The interference BS69 by EBNA2 protein is well known to initialize overexpressed of EBV associated cancer cells. However, the detailed in situ interacting mechanism between BS69 and EBNA2 is unclear due to lack of direct imaging agents. The lanthanide bioprobes proposed herein will be a dual function bioprobe - not only to monitor the presence of BS69 and is also able to inhibit the EBNA2-associated cancer growth via the physical interference of the BS69-EBNA2 complex. The interaction of BS69 and EBNA2 will be visualized by our proposed lanthanide probes and monitored with an in-house time-resolved microscope equipped with NIR-II camera. Four preliminary experiments have been performed to support our hypothesis, especially the binding of the proposed ytterbium complexes with the BS69 protein is confirmed by responsive NIR-II emission, Western blot and in vitro selective toxicity in the EBNA2-positive cell lines. We strongly believe this proposed study will be a pioneering work for the systematic synthesis of lanthanide-derived imaging agents and their development into time-resolved luminescent probes for NIR-II imaging. Thus, the results of this study will broaden the horizon for the vital stains and traditional heterocyclic/organic fluorophores that are currently available commercially. 目前商業化的分子成像劑如熒光素均有高背景噪音的缺點。這些噪音是由生物引起的樣品的自發熒光散射來自固體基質的光以及來自光學元件的發光。因此，目前更多的專注於時間分辨熒光技術和使用鑭系元素絡合物成像探針的開發。時間分辨光譜可以確定基於激發的壽命分析得到提供激發的發色團/材料的激發動力學和衰變途徑的見解。因此利用這種技術可以實現基於熒光壽命差異的信息分析。自動熒光多發生在納米到幾微秒級。鑭系元素的發射壽命為微米秒級，非常適合時間分辨成像，尤其是具有較高組織穿透的近紅外II（NIR-II，1000-1700nm）發射如鐿/鉺/釹等鑭系離子。然而，目前大多數報道的時間分辨的鑭系元素探針隻能在NIR-I區域（700-1000 nm）可見同時在體外成像也不具有特異性。在本項目中，我們將針對EBV相關癌症的關鍵功能蛋白BS69開發新的時間分辨NIR-II成像和靶向鑭系元素生物探針（鐿/鉺）。我們將通過探針亮度和量子產率變化實現近紅外II的檢測。 眾所周知，EBNA2蛋白可以在其過表達的EBV相關癌細胞中實現對BS69的初始化表達的干擾。然而目前由於缺乏直接成像劑，BS69和EBNA2之間的詳細原位相互作用機制尚不清楚。本文提出的鑭系元素生物探針將是雙功能生物探針： 不僅用於監測BS69的存在，而且還能夠通過BS69-EBNA2復合物的物理干擾抑制EBNA2相關的癌症生長。而 BS69和EBNA2的相互作用將通過我們提出的鑭系元素探針顯示，並使用配備有NIR-II相機的內部時間分辨顯微鏡進行監測。我們已經通過四個初步實驗証實了我們的假設，特別是通過在EBNA2陽性細胞系中響應的NIR-II發射，蛋白免疫印跡(Western blot)和體外選擇性毒性均証實了所提出的鐿復合物可實現與BS69蛋白的結合。我們堅信這項研究將成為系統合成鑭系元素衍生成像劑的開創性工作，以及它們在用於NIR-II成像的時間分辨發光探針中的開發。因此，這項研究的結果將有效拓寬傳統雜環/有機熒光團在活體染色上的商業化應用。

12300019.label: Realisation of objectives
12300019.value: Objective 1: To design, synthesize and modify lanthanide bioprobes with tailor-made peptides targeting BS69 for responsive time-resolved NIR-II in vitro imaging of the EBV-infected cells We developed five series of lanthanide systems in two categories (1) molecular lanthanide complexes and (2) double perovskite materials which can be ligated to peptides targeting EBV cancers. The excitation and emission ranges of two lanthanide systems are from visible to near infrared for time -resolved imaging and inhibition of EBV-associated cancers is achieved via ligation of the proposed peptides. (1) Molecular lanthanide systems: Trivalent lanthanides have been commonly used as emission centers due to their characteristic emission profiles and long emission lifetimes (μs−ms time frame). The fingerprint emission bands allow differentiation from the broad and structureless emission bands of organic chromophores and enable convincing discrimination of lanthanide emissions from short-lived biological autofluorescence (ns-based) using of time-resolved measurements. The technique of time-resolved spectroscopy makes use of a time-gated system to delay data acquisition of pulse-excited emission signals so that the detection window is only opened after the unwanted emissions have faded, and the desired longer-lived emission(s) are distinctly detected. The lanthanide probes have gained great advances for biological detection and imaging, especially the “switch-off” strategy based on the principle of photoinduced electron transfer or antenna−analyte electron transfer. Recently, lanthanide complexes incorporated with several functional groups have also been covalently linked to metabolic engineered substrates with bioorthogonal ligation to perform time-resolved imaging and labelling of cell surface glycans in order to get more information on how glycans regulate progression. However, these complexes with “always-on” luminescent signals suffer from the interference of unremoved complexes. Therefore, to obtain high signal/background ratios, the development of a luminogenic lanthanide probe that can be activated by a bioorthogonal reaction is highly desirable. Furthermore, time-resolved luminescence spectroscopy allows probing of the excited state dynamics and deactivation pathways of our designed imaging complexes, offering complementary evidence for our bioorthogonal ligation mechanism. To improve the imaging efficacy via combining bioorthogonal chemistry with lanthanide emission, herein, we report the design and synthesis of luminogenic tetrazine-based lanthanide probes. Our system was found to be activated via a bioorthogonal tetrazine ligation to exhibit dramatic enhancement of long-lived luminescence (5-fold) upon cycloaddition reaction with a strained cyclooctyne, trans-cyclooctenol (TCO). Notably, our system, upon ligation of our proposed peptides, could enable robust and sensitive detection of EBV cancer cells under no-wash conditions in vitro. (2) Lanthanide materials: Understanding the ultraviolet, green, red, near infrared and infrared emission properties of bismuth halide double perovskite (Cs2NaBiCl6) and explored the possibility to ligate the EBV-specific peptide on the surface of double perovskite for guided imaging and therapy. The emission and excitation spectra of Cs2NaBiCl6 samples prepared by different methods are generally similar. The spectra of Cs2NaBiCl6 prepared in DCl and HCl by the evaporation method both showed the absence of water coordination. Also, the spectra of samples prepared by the precipitation and evaporation methods are similar, so we mainly focus upon the latter samples. However, some major differences are observed for samples prepared by the solid-state method, and these are highlighted. The emission spectra span across the blue, green, orange-red, NIR and IR regions. Under UV excitation, the blue emissions are mostly quenched at room temperature (but we can still observe them) and grow stronger upon cooling, while the red emission is observed at RT. The broad NIR and IR emissions are observed at room temperature. The brightness of Cs2NaBiCl6 indicates potential as time-resolved imaging materials with long emission lifetime. (3) As a starting point, we aim to build upon the BS69 peptides and lanthanide complexes targeting the binding site - MYND in BS69. We studied the folding of designed peptides and conjugated complexes in buffer by molecular docking with Autodock 4.0. Six peptides with strong potential binding with BS69 were selected: P1: -MPSLEPK (-15.34 kcal/mol); P2: -CAhx-MPSLEPK-GG-RrRK (-10.99 kcal/mol); P3: -PSLEPK (-12.65 kcal/mol), P4: -CAhx-PSLEPK-GG-RrRK (-10.74 kcal/mol), P5: -cyclo(PSLEPK) (-14.14 kcal/mol) and P6: -CAhx-GG-RrRK-cyclo(PSLEPK) (-11.03 kcal/mol). Objective 2: To establish a general synthetic method for appending the highly cell-permeable peptides to lanthanide complexes for targeting BS69 using native chemical ligations Traditional fluorescent peptide chemical syntheses hinge on the use of limited fluorescent/dye-taggable unnatural amino acids and entail multiple costly purifications. In this project, we discovered a facile and efficient protocol for in situ construction of dipyrrins on the N-terminus with 20 natural and five unnatural amino acids and the lysine's side chain of selected peptides/peptide drugs through Fmoc-based solid-phase peptide synthesis. The new strategy enables the direct formation of boron–dipyrromethene (BODIPY)–peptide conjugates from simple aldehyde and pyrrole derivatives without pre-functionalization, and only requires a single-time chromatographic purification at the final stage. As a model study, synthesized EBNA1-targeting BODIPY1–Pep4 demonstrates intact selectivity in vitro, responsive fluorescence enhancement, and higher light cytotoxicity due to the photo-generation of cytotoxic singlet oxygen. This work offers a novel practical synthetic platform for fluorescent peptides for multifaceted biomedical applications. Furthermore, we used this synthetic method to conjugate proposed peptides and lanthanide systems from objective 1. We also studied the folding of designed peptides and conjugated complexes via several experiments, such as monitoring the change in temperature and chirality during binding. The ligation of lanthanide systems with P1 to P6 was done and more than 25 lanthanide complexes/materials were synthesised (100 mg each) for photophysical and in vitro studies. Objective 3: To investigate the selectivity and cytotoxicity of the proposed lanthanide bioprobes on both EBV-positive and negative cancer cells The in vitro, vivo and cytotoxicity of five series of lanthanide complexes in EBV-specific cancer cells have been done and all showed impressive selectivity towards EBV cancer cells. EBV-positive (VCaP, 22RV1, DU145, LCL2 and PC-3) and EBV-negative cell lines (WPMY-1, MRC-5, C666-1 and HeLa, including prostate normal cell line) were used for cellular studies. The proposed lanthanide bioprobes were evaluated in aqueous solution in vitro, ex vivo and in vivo in esophageal tissues, as well as their efficacy (pharmacokinetics and bio-distribution) on esophagus cancer in vivo. The brightness of the lanthanide complexes were determined and we also showed a new guideline for designing near-infrared emissive probes with high brightness and quantum yield for time-resolved NIR imaging.

12300019.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300019.value: (1) There are twenty newly synthesized lanthanide complexes/materials ligated with several EBV-targeting peptides. Their photophysical properties, such as brightness, emission quantum yield and biostability are well examined. The in vitro studies of lanthanide complexes are evaluated in several EBV positive/negative cell lines, the subcellular location of these complexes are worked out and two series of the EBV-specific lanthanide bioprobes are selected for in vivo imaging. Their uptake rates by tumours and various organs are determined, and the minimum (ED) and median (ED50) effective doses for tumour size reduction are identified for further pre-clinical study. The two series of lanthanide complexes are dual-functional conjugates as EBV-targeting theranostic agents which combines the lanthanide emission properties (NIR emission/magnetic) with EBV-targeting peptides to achieve imaging and EBV inhibition simultaneously in a single molecule. (Chemical Science, 2021, 12, 9977; ChemPlusChem, 2022, 87; Journal of Materials Chemistry C, 2022, 2950; Inorganic Chemistry Frontiers, 2022, 6379) (2) A new facile and efficient protocol for in situ dipyrrin construction on the N-terminus and the side chains of peptides through Fmoc-based solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS), where simple aldehyde and pyrrole derivatives can be directly utilized as building blocks without pre-functionalization in SPPS, is developed and only one final-stage chromatographic purification step is required. In connection to this research project to develop peptide-based protein inhibitors against EBV-associated malignancies, we constructed dipyrrin moieties from our own library of established protein-targeting peptides and synthesized complexes, which manifests no erosion of biotargeting performance in vitro but enhanced light cytotoxicity over dark cytotoxicity. This finding offers a new pragmatic SPPS methodology for fluorescent peptide production and facilitates a cornucopia of biomedical applications. (Chemical Science, 2020, 11266) (3) For the development of time-resolved lanthanide bioprobes, we reported a series of stable, biocompatible and functionalized lanthanide complex for bioorthogonal ligation with engineered cell-surface glycans for providing responsive luminescence. A luminescence resonance energy transfer (LRET) quencher with bioorthogonal properties is strategically incorporated in a tripodal lanthanide complex with low toxicity, which can undergo a click-cycloaddition reaction with a cyclooctyne to completely change the electronic structure of the quencher, resulting in much less efficient LRET and a 5-fold enhancement of the long-lived lanthanide emission intensity. This work therefore establishes a time-resolved platform that enables labelling and imaging of biomolecules of interest. (Inorganic Chemistry Frontiers, 2020, 7, 4062)

12300019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300019.value: We have developed an efficient and convenient methodology to conjugate peptides with dipyrrin moieties during SPPS that can be further derived into highly emissive bioactive BODIPY–peptide conjugates for multicolour imaging. The workload and cost for synthesizing dipyrrin/BODIPY–peptide conjugates is greatly reduced by this protocol, which therefore holds tremendous promise for expediting the screening of peptide-based fluorescent probes, as well as for the development of high-throughput fluorescence screening platforms and the creation of novel metal-peptide nano-frameworks for fluorescent peptide production that can leverage and impact multifaceted biomedical applications. The major problem for the potential cancer-specific small molecules in their translation from laboratory to clinical application is the cost of the synthetic work. This reported ligation method to conjugate the peptides with two proposed lanthanide complexes can offer large-scale production of pure complexes for pre-clinical examination, greatly benefiting the translation process. Large-scale pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic studies can be done soon, as a result; the toxic dose (TD), median toxic dose (TD50), lethal dose (LD) and median lethal dose (LD50) of the best imaging tracer will then be determined. The theranostic potential of the best candidate will be assessed.

12300019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300019.value: In this project, we developed a new green method to connect a peptide to lanthanide complexes with potential to inhibit EBV-related diseases, such as nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and visualize the inhibition process via near-infrared emissions. In this project, we synthesised more than twenty potential bioprobes with thorough characterization. Their toxicity and bio-function (such as anti-cancer effect) are evaluated. Four bioprobes are selected for further evaluation with the support of future funding. These bioprobes have shown potential as a new option for patients suffering from EBV-associated cancers, especially late-stage cancers. The green ligation method we developed can also support the synthesis of a large amount of peptide-ligated lanthanide complexes, thereby encouraging the development of lanthanide complexes with peptides for guided therapy and imaging.

12300419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300419.value: Hermitian Hamiltonians are commonly used to describe physical systems, thanks to their entirely real-valued eigenvalues and eigenvectors, which are suitable for representing steady states. However, recent theoretical developments on non-Hermitian Hamiltonians have inspired physicists to rethink the formalism and to use non-Hermitian Hamiltonians to study systems that incorporate loss and/or gain. Such systems are particularly commonplace in optics and classical waves. Unprecedented phenomena enabled by non-Hermiticity, including single-mode lasing, asymmetric absorption, etc., can lead to important applications in laser, energy transfer, and sensor technologies. Therefore, classical waves, such as light and acoustic waves, are quickly becoming the next hotspot for the research in non-Hermitian physics. An exceptional point (EP) emerges when two or more states coalesce at a certain parametric point of a non-Hermitian system. The critical behaviours of non-Hermitian systems in the vicinity of an EP have attracted tremendous academic attention. A particularly intriguing characteristic is the evolution of eigenvalues near an EP as the system is tuned. Typically, the complex eigenvalues form a self-intersecting Riemann surface in the parameter space, which gives the EP some peculiar properties such as unconventional topological structures. A variety of unconventional phenomena associated with these properties have been discovered, such as asymmetric guiding mode switching and topological energy transfer. Additionally, it has been shown that three or more interacting states can simultaneously coalesce to form a high order EP, which dwells on an even more exotic Riemann surface. However, the rich behaviours in the proximity of a high order EP remain unexplored. Here, we propose to study the geometric structure and topological characteristics of high order EPs. We will use tight-binding theory to identify the conditions for high order EPs to arise from 3×3 and 4×4 non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. We plan to realise these high order EPs in acoustic experiments, which have proven to be a versatile platform for studying non-Hermitian physics. EPs with specific geometric properties, such as an anisotropic high order EPs, will be designed and realised. Our acoustic wave systems will also enable the fine-tuning of relevant parameters, including coupling, loss, and detuning, and allow us to drive the systems around the EP to uncover the topological structures. 非厄米哈密頓量可用於表征帶有增益/耗散的物理系統，這類系統常見於光學和經典波體系。非厄米的引入，使許多新穎的物理現象成為可能，其中包括單模激光、非對稱吸收等。 非厄米系統中的本征態在參數空間中的所謂奇異點(exceptional point)會合並。奇異點附近參數空間的性質因此十分有趣。比如說，系統本征值所在的黎曼面會在奇異點交叉，因此奇異點在拓撲上具有奇特的性質。這些性質可以被利用來實現波的非對稱傳輸和能量的拓撲傳輸等新穎現象。這類現象目前只在二階奇異點中被實現和觀測到。最近，由三個或更多本征態同時合並而形成的高階奇異點已經在光學中被實現。本課題擬通過利用聲波系統，設計並實現高階奇異點，並系統研究高階奇異點的幾何結構和拓撲性質。

12300419.label: Realisation of objectives
12300419.value: 1. Design and study non-Hermitian systems that exhibit exceptional points of order >2 using a tight-binding model. Objective 1 is fully achieved. We have studied several three-level non-Hermitian tight-binding models. Therein, we have not only found order-3 exceptional points, but also rich exceptional geometric structures, such as exceptional arcs [1], exceptional curves [2], surfaces and even order-3 exceptional lines [3]. Their topological properties have been characterized by eigenvalue winding numbers, eigenvalue knots [4], and eigenstate geometric phases (Berry phases) [2]. 2. Realise these systems using acoustic wave experiments, and observe these exceptional points in the experiments. Candidates for investigation include an order-3 hybrid exceptional point. 3. Experimentally determine the phase rigidity of the high order exceptional points. And explore the potential applications of the distinctive phase rigidity associated with each coalescing eigenstates. Objectives 2 and 3 are both fully achieved. We have successfully designed acoustic and mechanical systems that realize non-Hermitian systems exhibiting order-3 exceptional points. The acoustic system is three coupled acoustic cavities, with each cavity exhibiting an identical resonant mode. Order-3 exceptional points with properties beyond the “hybrid exceptional points” have been realized and characterized. Phase rigidity of eigenvectors as well as eigenvalue winding numbers are used to characterize the properties near the order-3 exceptional points [1]. Phenomena such as non-Abelian state permutations have been observed by leveraging the geometric properties of the eigenvalue manifolds that host order-3 exceptional points [5]. The mechanical system is a spring-mass rotational oscillator with active components that realize either tunable non-reciprocity or tunable dissipative rate (gain or loss). See [6] for details. In addition to the abovementioned results, the PI has co-authored a review article on non-Hermitian topology and exceptional points [7]. 12300419.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300419.value: Singularities called “exceptional points” can emerge in the parameter space of non-Hermitian systems. The evolution of non-Hermitian systems is bounded to a unique type of topological manifold imposed by the Riemann surfaces of the complex eigenvalues. We have systematically investigated such topological properties from the perspective of both eigenvalues and eigenvectors [PRL (2021)]. This research led to the breakthrough discovery that a single higher-order exceptional points can possess hybrid winding numbers, thus expanding our understanding of exceptional-point topology. The theoretical and experimental methods for analyzing the topological properties of higher-order exceptional point have been successfully established. Based on these methods, we focused on three-level non-Hermitian systems exhibiting different order-2 exceptional points as well as order-3 (higher-order) exceptional points. We have discovered that in synthetic complex parameter space, the order-3 exceptional point can be formed as the nexus point of multiple order-2 exceptional arcs. Such an order-3 exceptional point can simultaneously possess distinct topological invariants (winding numbers) in different parametric planes. The discovery was experimentally verified using three coupled acoustic cavities. The results are published in Science 2020. In addition, we found that the state evolution on the eigenvalue manifolds of the three-level non-Hermitian systems can manifest as state permutations that map to a non-Abelian dihedral group. We observed such phenomena in acoustics. The results are published in National Science Reivew in 2022.

12300419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300419.value: The project outcomes contributed to non-Hermitian topology as a newly established research field in physics. The theoretical model and experimental systems developed for the investigations will be of great importance for the future development of this field.

12300419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300419.value: Non-Hermitian physics studies physical systems that are open, which means energy or substance exchange with the external environment is permitted for such systems. The research outcomes broaden the horizons of non-Hermitian physics by describing the topological properties of higher-order exceptional points, which are singularities of a system’s energies at which the energies of multiple states converge. Such properties are foundational to the novel ways for state transitions to occur, which is for them to move around these singularities. This is in stark contrast to traditional state transition, which must absorb or emit the precise amount the energy that fills the gap between two states. Such state transitions, or more precisely, permutations, are dependent of the order of operations. and may result in new applications in acoustics, optics, and photonics.

12300519.label: Project Objectives
12300519.value: We propose and develop new and novel preconditioning methods for inverse source problem in time fractional and time-space fractional diffusion equations. We analyze the spectral properties of the proposed preconditioned matrices by using matrix theory. We study and analyze the proposed regularization methods and algorithms for solving inverse source problem in time fractional and time-space fractional diffusion equations.

We analyze the spectral properties of the proposed preconditioned matrices by using matrix theory.

12300519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300519.value: The time fractional diffusion equation can be used to describe the anomalous diffusion phenomena instead of the classical diffusion process. The main idea is to replace the standard time derivative by the time fractional derivative (the Caputo derivative). In some applications, time-space fractional diffusion equation is employed by replacing the standard spatial derivative by the Riemann-Liouville derivative or the Riesz fractional derivative. Because of nonlocal nature of these derivatives, their discretized systems of equations involve dense coefficient matrices. Preconditioning iterative methods have been developed for solving such very large linear systems. In many practical applications, the source term in fractional diffusion equations is unknown. In this project, we are interested in solving this inverse source problem by employing additional measurement data. We study modified quasi-boundary value method and Tiknonov regularization method for solving this inverse source problem. The main challenge is to develop fast iterative solvers for such very large block linear systems arising from the modified quasi-boundary method and Tiknonov regularization method. We remark that the number of unknowns can be very large when the time and spatial discretization step-sizes are very small. The main objective of this proposal is to develop new preconditioning methods for solving such very large linear systems. Our idea is to construct Schur complement preconditioners based on block-circulant-type approximation and divide-and-conquer technique. We will investigate the spectra analysis of the proposed preconditioned matrices and demonstrate the fast convergence of the preconditioned iterative method. On the other hand, we study Tikhonov-type regularization methods for inverse source problem in fractional diffusion equations. We investigate into the invertibility and the condition numbers of the regularized discretized matrices from this inverse source problem by using block matrix technique and eigen-decomposition. In addition, the convergence rate analysis for unknown sources in spatial and temporal domains is studied by employing a suitable regularization matrix and a priori and an a posteriori choice rule for the regularization parameter. 時間分數擴散方程可用於描述異常擴散現象而不是經典的擴散過程。 主要的想法是取代時間分數導數的標準時間導數。 在一些應用中，採用時空分數階擴散方程代替Riemann-Liouville導數或Riesz分數的標準空間導數。 由於非局部性質，它們的離散化系統方程涉及密集係數矩陣。 預處理迭代方法有用於解決這種非常大的線性系統。 在許多實際應用中，分數階擴散方程中的源項是未知。在這個項目中，我們有興趣解決這個逆源問題採用額外的測量數據。我們研究修正的準邊界值方法和Tiknonov正則化方法解決這個逆源問題。該 主要的挑戰是為這種非常大的線性線性開發快速迭代求解器由修正的準邊界方法和Tiknonov正則化引起的系統方法, 當未知數的數量可能非常大空間離散步長非常小。主要目標是開發新的預處理方法來解決這種非常大的線性系統。我們的想法是構建基於塊循環型的Schur補充預處理器近似和分治技術。我們將研究光譜分析所提出的預條件矩陣並證明了快速收斂性預處理迭代方法。 另一方面，我們研究了分數階擴散方程中逆源問題的Tikhonov型正則化方法。 我們調查了可逆性和來自該逆源的正則化離散矩陣的條件數使用塊矩陣技術和特徵分解的問題。 除此之外空間和時間域中未知來源的收斂速度分析是通過採用合適的正則化矩陣和先驗和後驗來研究正則化參數的選擇規則。

12300519.label: Major findings and research outcome
12300519.value: In the research output [1,3,5], we proposed and studied fast preconditioning techniques for fractional diffusion equations and time-dependent non-local problems. In [1], circulant-based for symmetric positive definite system arising from the new discretization scheme was studied. In [3], circulant-based for nonsymmetric system was studied. In [5], sine transform-based preconditioner for nonsymmetric system was studied. The developed preconditioning techniques can be carried out efficiently as fast solvers are available and the techniques are very useful for the subproblem solvers in inverse problems. On the other hand, in order to deal with high-dimensional fractional equations, we developed and studied a deep Rtiz method in [4]. Our idea is to use the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension and formulate a minimal Ritz energy functional problem. Based on the approximation property of networks, our theoretical and numerical results were reported to demonstrate the effectiveness of the developed method for solving fractional Laplacian equations. In the research output [2], we studied preconditioning methods for inverse source problem in time fractional and time-space fractional diffusion equations. We developed and analyzed an inverse problem with quasi-boundary value regularization for recovering a source term of the time fractional diffusion equations from the final observation data. A two-by-two block linear system arising from the problem was studied. We studied fast preconditioning techniques that approximate the Schur complement in the system using a product of some factors, and showed that the eigenvalues of the preconditioned system are shown to be clustered around 1, and the fast convergence of the methods is guaranteed theoretically. We obtained the residual and regularization norms for various parameters and plotted the curve associated with the pair parametrized by the parameters so that the optimal parameter was selected to be the one at which the curve has maximum curvature (L-curve corner). Numerical experiments were carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed preconditioning method and parameter selection method.

12300519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12300519.value: Numerical discretization of a regularized inverse source problem leads to a non-symmetric saddle point linear system. Interestingly, the Schur complement of the non-symmetric saddle point system is Hermitian positive definite. Then, we plan to propose a preconditioner matching the Schur complement. Theoretically, we plan to show that the preconditioned conjugate gradient method for a linear system with the preconditioned Schur complement as coefficient has a linear convergence rate independent of the matrix size and value of the regularization parameter involved in the inverse problem. Fast implementations are proposed for the matrix-vector product of the preconditioned Schur complement so that the PCG solver requires only quasi-linear operations. This will be the first solver with guarantee of linear convergence for the inversion of Schur complement arising from the discrete inverse problem. Combining the PCG solver for inversion of the Schur complement and the fast solvers for the forward problem in the literature, the discrete inverse problem (the saddle point system) is solved within a quasi-linear complexity.

12300519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300519.value: The inverse source fractional problem has attracted much attention where the desired source term is usually assumed to have a prior form. Like many inverse problems, the fractional problem is ill-posed, the solution of which becomes unreliable when the known data is polluted by even small noise. To remedy this situation, a regularization technique is employed. In this project, we have developed a fast and robust solver for the inverse source problem of identifying space-dependent source term component. Theoretically, we have shown that the complexity of the proposed solver has a quasi optimal upper bound independent of discretization parameters and regularization parameters. Numerical results have supported our theoretical analysis.

12300819.label: Project Objectives
12300819.value: This proposal has been submitted the last year. We have produced two publications based on the ideas used for this project. The results from these earlier researches show that the algorithms are fast and robust. In this project, we need to extend these algorithms in several directions. The first direction is to design an algorithm to minimize the generalized elastica energy with a general fidelity term. We shall design and test on algorithms having the same efficiency and robustness as was proposed in the published papers which is for a special image processing problem. The success of this part of the project will offer some elementary techniques for people to treat minimization problems involving curvatures for level sets of functions. This kind of problem is becoming more and more common in the community for image processing and computer vision. Image segmentation, image inpainting and surface processing are special applications of the generalized elastica model. For these applications, we could remove some of the unknown functions from the general minimization problem and get some special algorithms for these special problems with even faster numerical speed. These special algorithms are often needed by many people for testing purposes or for applications to real industrial data. Thus, the specially designed algorithms will be valuable for these applications. It is often that we need to represent convex objects/shapes. An object in 2D is convex is equivalent to positivity of it curvature of its boundary. We can put this as a constraint for general object representation. Thus convex shape representation is related to curvature problems following this idea. One of the objectives of this project is to develop algorithms for this kind of applications. There exists some other ways for convex objects representation, but we have not seen other approaches using curvature due to difficulties with higher order derivatives and numerical difficulties to approximate the curvature. The well-known Rudin-Osher-Fatemi (ROF) model is a special case of the generalized elastica model we have studied in this project. Most fast algorithms in the literature for ROF model are first order methods of gradient decent type. We find that we can have a preconditioner for Newtow type of second order methods for the ROF model and the preconditioned system is optimal in the sense that the preconditioned system has a condition number that is independent of the smoothing parameter and the image size. This kind of preconditioner is really desirable when the size of the problem is very large. This algorithm will be a good addition for solvers for the ROF model which is a special case of the elastica minimization model.

12300819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12300819.value: Euler's elastica energy for curves and Willmore energy for surfaces are well established concepts and they have numerous applications in many branches of sciences. Their applications to image processing and computer vision are also well recognized. These energies measure the smoothness of curves and surfaces. If we use these energies for the level set of functions, they give us a measurement for smoothness of the functions. This proposal is about designing and testing of some fast and robust algorithms for minimizing these energies for functions. So far, it is still a very difficult task to minimize these energies. Existing algorithms are either too slow or too sensitive to parameters. The proposed algorithm is fast and nearly parameter free. This project is not about a specific application of these energies. The designed algorithms will have more general applications. To demonstrate and test on the proposed ideas, we will take image restoration, image segmentation, image inpainting and surface processing as examples. In this project, we will mainly work with designing and testing of algorithms. Some preliminary studies show the efficiency and advantages of the proposed ideas. Our research will produce a new class of fast algorithms for these problems and will lead to new ways to design efficient algorithms for minimization of curvature related models. Euler的曲线弹性能量和曲面的Willmore能量是经过多年发展过的比较完善的物理和数学概念。 它们在许多科学分支中有许多应用。它们在图像处理和计算机视觉方面的应用也得到了广泛认可。这些能量用来测量曲线和曲面的光滑度。如果我们将这些能量用于一般函数的水平集上，它们会为我们提供这些函数的光滑度的测量。本项目涉及设计和测试一些快速且稳健的算法，来极小化这些对应的能量。到目前为止，最小化这些能量仍然是一项非常困难的任务。现有算法要么太慢，要么对参数过于敏感。我们将提出的算法快速且几乎无参数。该项目与这些能量函数的具体应用无关。设计的算法将具有一般性。为了演示和测试所提出的想法，我们将以图像恢复，图像分割，图像修复和空间曲面的处理为例，展示设计算法的效能。在这个项目中，我们将将集中精力于算法的设计和测试。我们已作了一些初步研究，表明了提出的想法的效率和优势。我们的研究将会对所要研究的问题产生一类新的快速算法。 这里所提的思想可能会引导一大类此种有效的新算发。

12300819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12300819.value: Many objects in real world have geometrical properties. In many real physical applications, the objects will have the smallest volume, or object surface area or smallest twisting of the surface. Sometimes, the object needs to have the largest surface area or largest surface twisting. There are mathematical ways to express these situations. How to minimize or maximize these quantities is not an easy problem. This project has proposed some fast algorithms to solve some of these problems. The tests show success of our proposed algorithms.

12301019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301019.value: 人類認知行为是基於複雜的腦網絡上形成的動態模式，這些網絡是通過長期進化而發展起來的。最近的研究通過比較不同參與者群體 – 如病理狀態的與功能典型的群體相比，關注腦網絡中的結構 - 功能關係。然而，典型的個體在認知行為方面也存在顯著差異，但迄今為止，對大腦復雜的結構和功能網絡的這種個體差還異知之甚少。個體差異可能與進化穩健性及可進化性之間的權衡這一進化原理密切相關及； 進化穩健性需要發展可靠的結構和功能， 而可進化性要求足夠強的表型變異性。 幾個關鍵問題尚未得到很好的解決， 包括： 大腦個體間的結構和功能網絡的可靠性和可變性如何？網絡中的可靠性/可變性是均匀的還是異構的？腦結構和功能網絡的變異性如何與個體之間的行為差異相關？為什麼腦網絡中的某些變化導致典型行為的正常變化而其他變化導致病理狀況？典型的發育和衰老，腦障礙和疾病如何與大腦網絡的可靠性和可變性相關？解決這些問題對於理解大腦正常和異常功能以及開發工程和醫學上的調製方法至關重要。特別是，腦障礙和疾病的變異可能發生在變異譜的極端處，當被典型的個體差異掩蓋時，早期檢測變得極具挑戰性。因而，非常需要開髮用於人際間腦網絡變異的系統理論/計算框架並在大樣本中進行驗證。 該合作項目旨在將大規模多模態腦成像數據集（~2000個受試者）與計算模型相結合，在系統生物學鬆散性的新型框架中解決上述基本問題。鬆散性是指在各向異性參數空間中，系統狀態對一些“剛性”方向（參數組合）的變化高度敏感，而在許多“鬆散”方向上不太敏感。我們將用最大熵（Ising）模型研究腦網絡中可能的剛性和鬆散方向。該模型将擬合功能磁共振（fMRI）測量到的腦靜息狀態時空活動模式; 剛性和鬆散性將直接與實際的大樣本個體間腦網絡的可靠性和可變 性​​進行比較，並用於預測認知行為表現。該框架可能可以發展新方法，用於將認知表現中的個體的指紋識別為不同剛性或鬆散結構鏈接的組合。我們還將研究腦網絡如何隨著衰老而變化，以及這些變化如何被阿爾茨海默症（AD）的風險基因APOEε4 所調節。我們假設正常衰老和非典型神經退变改變的目標子網絡可能具有不同的剛度水平。該項目的潛在發現可能會為腦網絡的組織和普遍工作原理提供根本性的新亮點，並有助於解決這些原理是如何轉移到腦疾病的極端情況。因此，該項目將為未來對各種類型腦疾病的系統研究奠定基礎，以潛在地識別最關鍵的腦网络部位，在工程和臨床應用中用電或磁进行干預和預防。

12301419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301419.value: 核配置方法是無網格的方法，它享有不需要構建網格網格的優點。自亮相應用以來，無網格方法受到許多研究人員的歡迎，並成功解決大量不規則領域上的模擬問題。 本研究項目的目的是開發新的連續最小二乘核配置方法和數值技術用於求解低規則性的橢圓偏微分方程。 在的離散最小二乘核配置方法中所有邊界配置條件的固定權重是取決於數據點密集度。對於Sobolev space重現核，我們[SIAM Numer. Anal., 56(1):614-633. 2018]證明了這種離散配置方法是收斂的。 然而，當數據點非常不均勻時，我們采用的權重數值是不可以忽略數據點的局部幾何，這正是我們對任何用於求解具有非平滑係數，強制函數和/或邊界條件的自適應方法的期望。 我們建議研究離散最小二乘配置方法的漸近性，並考慮連續公式化，用為開發新的配置點。項目的第一項任務是數字識別一些搭配點的權重，允許內核搭配方法解決不連續係數的問題。下一個具有挑戰性的任務是為連續最小二乘核配置方法提出剛性收斂分析。 我們注意到橢圓問題的規律性估計自然不會產生L2範數的上限，並且在連續最小二乘公式之間留下間隙，我們揣測試驗函數的逆不等式並將在收斂證明裡使用。在最後部分，我們將開發一些邊界類型的內核搭配方法，這些新方法將是不受差分運算符限制的基本解方法的替代。我們建議將內部殘差的積分域擴展到一些更大的域，以允許分析或簡單的數值積分。前者在計算上是有效的，但受到我們對某些積分的分析解決方案的了解的限制。 後者更為通用，但帶有數值求積的開銷。 所有開發的算法都將採用快速直接矩陣分解算法，並進行全面的數值實驗，以了解它們的局限性。

12301419.label: Realisation of objectives
12301419.value: The project "On the Asymptotics of Least-squares Kernel Collocation Methods" has made substantial progress in achieving its stated objectives. Ever since the publication of our detailed framework for convergence analysis in [1], several researchers have incorporated our methodology in their convergence proofs for various kernel-based methods. At the time of the Annual Report, it appeared that one of these subsequent works had a significant overlap with our project's research path. However, upon its publication, it was revealed that the proof in [2] was incomplete. Specifically, their proof relied on a conjecture about an inverse inequality for Sobolev norms on the boundary for all kernel-based trial functions defined in the domain, which remains unproven. As a result, Objective 3 was reopened for investigation in our project. We address all remaining objectives in [3]. Given appropriate smoothness and boundedness assumptions on the domain, the elliptic differential operator L and the data f and g, we assume that the PDE L u = f in domain and u = g on boundary admits a classical solution u for some high order Sobolev space and satisfies a boundary regularity estimate. Then, our general framework for proving high-order convergence is: (1) Well-posedness of the PDE in the sense that any PDE solution can be bounded above by that of the associated data functions under some appropriate norms. The boundary regularity of elliptic PDEs serves this purpose. (2) Trial space is a finite-dimensional space from which we seek a numerical approximation to the PDE solution. This space represents the first discretization, and the assumptions made about the regularity/smoothness of the PDE solution determine the choice of the trial space. (3) Stability estimate (Objective 3) bounds all trial functions from above using a data norm (which can be easily computed and may be either continuous or discrete), usually derived from the well-posedness inequality. Its main role is to define the numerical solution via optimization. Specifically, the objective function in the definition of the variational least-squares (VLS) solution, i.e., the “asymptotics of Least-squares collocation”, is essentially the right-hand side of a continuous stability inequality. This is typically the most challenging part of designing a convergent numerical method. For instance, the desired continuous stability inequality in [2] (and also in [3, Eqn. 1.2]) uses L2-norms on the right-hand side, unlike the Sobolev norms in the boundary regularity. The authors of [2] then apply a conjectured Bernstein-type inverse inequality in continuous norms to derive the derive the stability inequality in L2-norm. (4) Consistency estimates use the approximation power of the trial space to determine the error bounds and convergence rates of the numerical method. Since the numerical solution is defined via an optimization problem, we can replace the numerical solution in the objective function with some comparison trial function in the error analysis. This comparison function could be, for instance, the interpolant of the true solution from the trial space, which provides an upper bound. The remainder of the convergence analysis (Objective 4) can be conducted using standard approximation theory. Our theoretical work presented in [3] makes use of our previously established theories on least-squares collocation solutions, as detailed in our prior work [1]. This approach allowed us to prove the target continuous stability inequality without resorting to the conjectured inverse inequality in [2]. Instead, we formally prove the continuous stability inequality by playing the asymptotic of the discrete stability we had already proven in [1]. Note that the proof for this discrete stability also incorporates a formally proven Bernstein-type inverse inequality [1, Lem. 3.2] in discrete norms. This technique effectively circumvents the need for relying on unproven conjectures, thereby confirming the truth of the continuous stability estimate in [2] and their convergence proof for VLS. This completed Objectives 3 and 4 in this project. To address Objective 6, we take one step further and develop a weighted stability estimate. After proving the continuous stability estimate from the unweighted discrete one in [1], we prove the existence of some zeroth-order quadrature rule, which is only approximative rather than convergent, and its corresponding weighted discrete stability is equivalent with the newly proven continuous stability estimate. This finding means that we can discretize VLS without using on exact quadrature rules. Given that this is an existence proof, we have turned to numerical experiments to demonstrate the ease of obtaining such a zeroth order quadrature. We tested Monte Carlo (MC) and even uniform random quadrature weight on nonuniform data points. Interestingly, with sufficient oversampling (about three times as much in our tests), both weighted LS methods perform comparably to VLS with Trapezoidal rules in terms of both accuracy and convergence rate. This is a significant finding as it lowers the computational complexity and makes VLS more efficient. Moreover, its convergence proof of the weighted LS follows from that of VLS. The numerical experiments conducted in [3] were designed with Objective 2 in mind and considered scenarios with rapidly changing forcing functions and PDE coefficients modelled by an arctan function with a large steepness parameter. Firstly, for the case of rapidly changing source functions, our experiments found that it did not pose much of a challenge. All the tested MC, Random, and Trapezoidal quadrature weights were able to converge at the predicted rate. In contrast, the situation with rapidly changing diffusion tensors required more care. When the steepness parameter exceeded a certain threshold, we need to collocate in divergence form. This approach yielded solutions that closely matched the reference solution, which was obtained using a highly refined finite element method. This result underscores the robustness of our method even in the face of challenging PDE scenarios. REFERENCES [1] K. C. Cheung, L. Ling, and R. Schaback. 12301419.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301419.value: The major findings of the project are detailed in [3]. A significant accomplishment was the successful addressing of a theoretical gap in a variational/continuous least-squares kernel collocation method. We provided a robust proof that did not depend on an unproven conjecture regarding an inverse inequality for Sobolev norms on the boundary for all kernel-based trial functions. This theoretical advancement played a crucial role in paving the way for subsequent convergence proofs. Another noteworthy outcome was the further development of a weighted discrete stability estimates using zeroth order quadrature rule. We proved the existence of such zeroth order quadrature rule, which is not convergent but only approximates. This allowed us to discretize Variational Least Squares (VLS) without the need for exact quadrature rules, a significant leap forward that can help reduce computational complexity in practice. In terms of numerical experiments, we considered scenarios with rapidly changing forcing functions and PDE coefficients. Rapidly changing source functions did not pose a significant challenge, while rapidly changing diffusion tensors required additional care. By collocating in divergence form, we obtained solutions that closely matched the reference solution obtained using a highly refined finite element method. Although not directly stated in the original objectives, the theoretical foundations developed for the kernel methods in this project have proven to be broadly applicable. They have been used in other works such as parabolic equations [4], Hamiltonian wave equations [5], and even in applications related to pattern formations. These publications were partially supported by this grant, and we would like to take this opportunity to express our gratitude for the support once again.

12301419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301419.value: With the robustness of our methods demonstrated in handling rapidly changing PDE coefficients, there is potential to extend this research into other types of differential equations and applications, such as nonlinear PDEs, stochastic PDEs, and problems in higher dimensions. Moreover, the broad applicability of our methods demonstrated in parabolic equations, Hamiltonian wave equations, and pattern formations suggests the possibility of exploring other domains.

12301419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301419.value: Our research project, "On the Asymptotics of Least-squares Kernel Collocation Methods," focuses on enhancing the mathematical techniques used to solve complex problems modelled by partial differential equations (PDEs) for simulating complex phenomena like heat transfer, fluid flow, or financial market behavior. In this project, we've made remarkable progress in advancing the theories behind the numerical methods used to solve these complex equations. These advancements not only improve our understanding of these methods but also enhance their performance. Moreover, we have discovered ways to make these numerical algorithms more efficient. Traditionally, solving such equations requires accurate numerical integration, a process which can be computationally demanding. We've developed a new technique that relaxes this requirement, thereby making the calculation process more efficient.

With treatment begins at an early stage, the chance of cure and survival is greatly heightened. In diseases such as cancers, exosomes can facilitate tumor progression by altering their vesicular content and, by supplying the tumor niche with molecules that favor the progression of oncogenic processes such as invasion, proliferation and metastasis. The packaging of their molecular content is known to be tissue specific, a fact that makes them ideal candidates for biomarkers and potential tools in clinical diagnostics and prognostics. The protein expression level is the most clinical relevant biomarkers. The expression profile of surface proteins on exosome certainly provides significant molecular information of the parent diseased cells. Moreover, the specific mRNAs and microRNA associated with diseases in circulating exosomes have also been attracting major interest as potential diagnostic biomarkers. DNA walkers are synthetic nanomotors created based on DNA and RNA. 12301519.label: Realisation of objectives
12301519.value: Objective 1. To develop a specific DNA walker for the circulating exosomes via protein biomarker detection. The project objective has been achieved. We have developed a sandwich-type surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) sensor to simultaneous and quantitative detection of multiple exosomal microRNAs (miRNAs). The Raman probes were rationally designed using polyA anchoring AuNPs (Au@aDNA) as the nanocore, followed by the coating of Raman signal molecules on the surface of Au@aDNA by Au-S bond, and formed gold shells around the nanocores. The asymmetric core-shell structured Au@Au@Ag nanoparticles were prepared by a simple and low-cost layer-by-layer self-assembly method. They were modified with different Raman molecules and recognition sequences (polyA-DNA) to obtain the surface-enhanced Raman probes. The capturing sequences (biotin-DNA) functionalized on the surface of immunomagnetic beads to get the capture probes. The Raman probes and capture probes could bind to the target miRNAs in the partial hybridization manner. Thus, the developed SERS sensor could indicate the target miRNAs levels in the buffer solution. Using breast cancer-related miRNAs as model targets, the limit of detection of this sensor can achieve 1.076 fM for synthetic miR-21, 0.068 fM for synthetic miR-126, and 4.57 fM for synthetic miR-1246, respectively. Such SERS sensors were further employed to detect the miR-21 in 20% human serum and the extraction solution of exosomes, respectively. This part of work has been published in a peer-review journal. "Simultaneous and Multiplex Detection of Exosomal MicroRNAs Based on the Asymmetric Au@Au@Ag Probes with Enhanced Raman Signal. Chin. Chem. Lett. 2022, 33 (6), 3183–3187." Objective 2. To design and develop a DNA walker for the detection of circulating miRNA for early disease diagnosis. The project objective has been achieved. By combining exquisitely designed hairpins with the catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) to form tripedal DNA walkers driven by enzyme, we constructed a 3D DNA walker with accordingly complementary hairpins attached on gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) and sensitive fluorescence sensing system for the sensitive detection of target miRNA-21 (miR-21). The presence of miR-21 triggers the CHA among three hairpins (HP1, HP2, and HP3), which lead to the formation of the tripedal DNA walkers. For the walking trajectories, FAM-labeled hairpins (HP4) were attached to the surface of AuNPs, the fluorescence of which was initially quenched due to its close proximity to AuNPs. After the binding/cleaving/moving process of tripedal DNA walkers with HP4 driven by Exonuclease III (Exo III), a number of single-stranded DNAs (ssDNAs) will be released with FAM fluorescence recovered. Benefiting from the DNA walker and CHA cascade amplification, the proposed sensing strategy showed remarkable improvement in sensitivity with the LOD of 42 aM. Owing to the precise design of the system, this method exhibited excellent specificity to distinguish miR-21 from its single-, double-mismatched sequences and non-complementary sequences, showing great versatility and potential for the biological analysis and early disease diagnosis. This part of work has been published at "Ultrasensitive miRNA Detection by AuNP-based 3D DNA Walker and Catalytic Hairpin Assembly (CHA) Cascade Amplification for Early Cancer Diagnosis", Chem Asian J, doi.org/10.1002/asia.202300367.

12301519.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301519.value: We have developed a SERS assay for the detection of disease-related multiplex exosomal miRNAs. Such a SERS sensor consisted of asymmetric Au@Au@Ag nanoparticles with enhanced Raman signal as the Raman probes and molecular beacon (MB) modified capture DNA as the capturing probes. The Raman probes can be effectively bound to the surface of MB by the sandwich hybridization in the presence of target miRNAs. Notably, three Raman probes successfully constructed by introducing the different Raman signal molecules to the asymmetric Au@Au@Ag nanoparticles. Simultaneous and multiplex analyses of three target miRNAs further performed by using different Raman probes as recognition signals. The limits of detection (LODs) of miR-21, miR-1246, and miR-126 were 1.076 fM, 4.57 fM, and 0.068 fM, respectively. Therefore, the proposed SERS sensor can simultaneously detect the multiple disease-related exosomal miRNAs with high sensitivity and excellent selectivity. All these results meet the needs of multiplex assays. Therefore, we anticipated this assay to be promising in the early diagnosis of cancer. Besides, an ultrasensitive miRNA-21 detection in a facile fashion through cascade amplification by catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) and 3D DNA walking was established. The system was initiated in the presence of miR-21, which triggered CHA thus forming tripedal DNA walkers. Afterward, the walkers recognize the trajectories attached on AuNPs, resulting in the remarkable fluorescence recovery of FAM fluorescence. This work outcompetes other conventional detection methods, boasting the advantages of easy synthesis steps and relatively short detection duration. The developed biosensor exhibited excellent selectivity and was successfully applied to detect miRNA-21 in human serum samples. In addition, this strategy possesses high extensibility by applying corresponding DNA hairpins to hybridize with the commensurate targets to form tripedal DNA walkers, manifesting its promising application for the detection of various targets (RNA, DNA and protein aptamers).

12301519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301519.value: Both the developed assays are promising and can simultaneously detect the multiple disease-related exosomal miRNAs with high sensitivity and excellent selectivity for early diagnosis of cancers and diseases. Future modification/optimization of the detection assays for clinical uses and clinical validation would be crucial for the commercialization potential of such developed assays.

12301619.label: Project Objectives
12301619.value: We introduce the weighted tubal decompositions for third-order tensors and study the effect of the weight tensor to the existence and uniqueness of these decompositions. We investigate the weighted tubal singular value decomposition when the weight tensor guarantees its well-definedness. We design algorithms for the weighted tubal SVD by extending the matrix case in the tubal sense. We apply the weighted tubal SVD to the low-rank tensor approximation and the low-rank plus sparse model. We use the weighted tubal low-rank decomposition to the low-rank tensor approximation and the low-rank plus sparse model when the weighted tubal SVD cannot be well-defined, which leads to nonconvex optimization problems. We design algorithms for this case and analyze the convergence affected by the weight tensors. We apply the low-rank approximation to color image compression and the low-rank plus sparse mode to seismic imaging. We design algorithms for selecting optimal weight tensors adaptively for different applications.

12301619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12301619.value: Low-rank related models are of extreme importance in many disciplines, such as data science, image processing, signal processing, and machine learning. An increasing number of real-world applications involve multi-dimensional data, which is often organized into a higher order tensor, i.e., an array with more than two indices. Researchers are motivated to investigate the low-rank tensor models and find tensor decompositions as fundamental tools. In the spirit of distinguishing the dimensions of different physical meanings, we suggest a tubal way to design tensor decompositions and tackle the low-rank models. Besides taken as a cube, a third-order tensor can also be regarded as a matrix whose entries are tubes, i.e., vectors along the third dimension. By introducing a multiplication of tubes, we define the corresponding tensor multiplications and decompositions in the tubal sense. We show in this proposal that any tube multiplication is determined by a weight tensor and the selection of the weight tensor is crucial in applications. Several existing tensor decompositions such as tensor train, t-SVD, and quaternion matrix decompositions can be unified into this framework. In this proposal, we apply the weighted tubal decompositions to the low-rank approximation model and the low-rank plus sparse model of tensors. When the weight tensor is chosen so that the tube space forms a ring, the weighted tubal singular value decomposition is well-defined. We would like to design efficient algorithms for the weighted tubal SVD similar to the matrix case and employ it to solve these two tensor models. When the tube space does not form a ring with the given weight tensor, we cannot define the SVD and thus we use the weighted tubal low-rank decompositions for these models, which lead to nonconvex optimization problems. We would also design and analyze efficient and reliable algorithms for this case. We also propose optimization methods to select the weight tensors adaptively for different applications to pursue the optimal approximation in a particular sense. We plan to apply the low-rank approximation model and the low-rank plus sparse model to color image compression and seismic imaging applications, respectively. 張量低秩模型在數據科學、圖像處理、信號處理、機器學習等許多領域中都非常重要。越來越多的現實應用問題中都會出現多維數據，我們通常將其建模成高階的張量，即指標數大於二的數組。研究者對這些低秩張量模型進行了研究，並且發現張量分解是處理這類問題的基本工具。鑒於張量的不同維度可能包含不同的物理意義，我們設計並考察張量的一類管式分解，以此來處理張量低秩模型。 三階張量除了可以看成一個立方體，還可以理解成一個元素都是“管”的矩陣，其中“管”指的就是沿著第三個維度的向量。通過引入管與管的乘積，我們可以在管的意義下定義相應的張量乘積和張量分解。事實上，這類乘積可以由一個權重張量所決定，並且權重張量的選擇在實際應用中至關重要。Tensor train、t-SVD、四元數矩陣分解等許多現有的張量分解都可以統一到我們提出的這個框架中來。 在這個項目中，我們將張量加權管式分解運用到張量低秩逼近模型和低秩加稀疏模型。當該權重張量選取使得這個“管”空間形成一個環，此時加權管式奇異值分解是良定義的。此時，我們可以推廣矩陣計算中的成果，設計計算加權管式奇異值分解的快速算法，並將其運用來解決上述兩類張量模型。當所選取的權重張量不能使得“管”空間形成環，那麼我們需要以其他方式定義張量的管式低秩分解，將會得到一些非凸優化問題。我們也將分析這類問題並且設計高效可靠的算法。進一步，我們還將提出數值優化的方法來自動選取該權重張量，從而對於不同問題以期得到最佳的逼近效果。我們計畫將上述兩類低秩張量相關的模型分別應用到彩色圖像壓縮以及地震成像領域中去。

12301619.label: Realisation of objectives
12301619.value: Tensor learning and functional data learning are two domains of research that center around the analysis of intricate data structures and patterns. The contributions made in completing this project can be categorized into two parts, each pertaining to one of these areas. The initial phase, led by the original PI Dr. Weiyang Ding (now at Fudan University), primarily concentrated on tensor learning, while the subsequent phase, led by the current PI, revolved around functional data learning. Throughout the course of the project, notable advancements have been made in the development of mathematical theory and computational methodologies, resulting in substantial progress towards achieving the majority of the project's objectives. Tensor learning is a field of study that focuses on analyzing and extracting meaningful information from data organized in higher-dimensional structures called tensors. Tensors can be thought of as multi-dimensional arrays that extend beyond the traditional two-dimensional matrices. Tensor learning techniques aim to uncover hidden patterns, relationships, and structures within the tensor data, enabling a deeper understanding of complex datasets. It involves the development of mathematical models, algorithms, and computational methods to effectively handle and analyze tensor data. In particular, a modified method is presented in [1] for solving convex optimization problems with constraints. This technique extends an existing approach to handle nonlinear scenarios, providing greater flexibility in problem-solving. The algorithm is proven to converge under reasonable assumptions, even when a specific property is not fulfilled. The paper also investigates an inexact version of the algorithm, which improves efficiency without sacrificing effectiveness. Numerical simulations on an image restoration problem showcase the algorithm's strong performance, highlighting its practical usefulness. The convergence guarantees, exploration of an inexact version of the algorithm, and favorable results from numerical simulations collectively demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed method. In [2], two sufficient conditions for determining strong ellipticity in fourth-order elasticity tensors are presented. The first condition extends the scope to include S-PSD tensors, which can be verified using an alternating projection method. Additionally, the paper introduces the elasticity mathscr{M}-tensor, which is defined based on the M-eigenvalues of elasticity tensors. It is proven that any non-singular elasticity mathscr{M}-tensor satisfies the strong ellipticity condition. This research enhances our understanding of strong ellipticity in fourth-order elasticity tensors by providing practical tools for assessing it. The established conditions and verification algorithm offer practical means for evaluating strong ellipticity, while the introduction of the elasticity tensor and its associated definitions enriches our comprehension of the properties of these tensors. In [3], the use of backward error analysis in generalized tensor complementarity problems is investigated. It establishes conditions for acceptable solutions in different forms of these problems, providing a theoretical framework for analysis. The introduction of backward errors specifically for tensor complementarity problems allows for evaluating algorithm stability and establishing stopping criteria. The paper also includes numerical examples that demonstrate the practical application of backward errors in assessing algorithm reliability and stability. The paper [4] focuses on finding the optimal low-rank approximation for pure quaternion matrices in color image processing. Quaternion matrices are commonly used to represent color images, but existing methods may include a real component that is not useful for this purpose. The paper introduces an algorithm that eliminates the real component and produces an optimal low-rank approximation. This is achieved through an alternating projections approach onto a low-rank quaternion matrix manifold and a quaternion matrix with zero real component. The algorithm's convergence is proven by showing that these manifolds have a nontrivial intersection point. Numerical examples using synthetic matrices and color images illustrate the algorithm's effectiveness. Functional data learning is a field that deals with the analysis and modeling of data observed over continuous domains, such as time or space. Instead of treating the data as individual data points, functional data learning considers the data as a continuous function or curve. This approach allows for a more comprehensive understanding of how the data changes and evolves over the domain, capturing the underlying dynamics and patterns. In particular, [5] explores how functional deep ReLU networks can approximate nonlinear continuous functionals in Lp space. The paper introduces a new network structure that effectively captures higher order smoothness features in the target function. It overcomes limitations in existing theoretical analyses, particularly when using the ReLU activation function. The paper provides quantitative approximation rates for two scenarios: (a) when the target function is continuous with a modulus of continuity and (b) when it has higher order Fréchet derivatives. These rates depend on the network's depth, width, and total number of weights. The paper establishes logarithmic rates of approximation when measuring the error on the unit ball of a Hölder space, indicating convergence as network parameters increase. Additionally, nearly polynomial rates of approximation are established when measuring the error on a space of analytic functions, indicating faster convergence. The paper [6] explores distributed learning methods for effectively managing large-scale data in functional data analysis. It introduces the DGDFL algorithm, designed to handle functional data across multiple machines. Operating within the reproducing kernel Hilbert space framework, it addresses challenges related to big data in functional analysis. The paper provides the first theoretical understanding of DGDFL by studying its properties using integral operator approaches. Additionally, a semi-supervised approach is introduced, relaxing the restriction on the maximum number of machines and ensuring optimal learning rates in distributed settings. This approach represents the first distributed iterative training method for functional learning. The paper [7] introduces a functional deep neural network for nonlinear functional regression in functional data analysis (FDA). The network architecture includes a kernel embedding step, a projection step, and a deep ReLU neural network for prediction. By utilizing smooth kernel integral transformations and data-dependent dimension reduction, the proposed network achieves efficient and robust FDA tasks. The paper provides theoretical analysis, including approximation and generalization error analysis, to validate the network's advantages. Numerical simulations further confirm the network's robustness, efficiency, and ability to generalize well with a low number of discrete points. In summary, this paper contributes to FDA by proposing a functional deep neural network with powerful dimension reduction. The network's architecture, incorporating smooth kernel embeddings and data-dependent projection, enables efficient and robust nonlinear functional regression. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations provide evidence of the network's performance, highlighting its benefits in terms of approximation, generalization, and practical applicability. While we have not achieved all of the project objectives to the fullest extent, Dr. Ding and I have maintained ongoing collaborations in the field of tensor learning. However, the progress has been somewhat hindered by the disruptions caused by the pandemic over the past three years. In 2023, we were fortunate to have Dr. Ding's visit for a week and his PhD student’s visit for a two-month period, during which we brainstormed and generated additional ideas for potential collaboration in Tensor learning.

12301619.label: Major findings and research outcome
12301619.value: The research papers stemming from this proposed research project have achieved noteworthy success, with the majority being published in highly prestigious international journals, which serves as a testament to the rigorous methodologies, novel insights, and impactful findings generated through the project. In [1], we propose a modified method for solving optimization problems with constraints. The method is flexible and can handle nonlinear scenarios, converging even when specific properties are not met. The paper also introduces an inexact version of the algorithm, which improves efficiency without sacrificing effectiveness. Numerical simulations demonstrate the algorithm's strong performance in image restoration. In [2], the focus is on determining strong ellipticity in fourth-order elasticity tensors. The paper presents two conditions for assessing strong ellipticity, including a verification algorithm. The introduction of the elasticity tensor enhances our understanding of these tensors' properties. This research provides practical tools for evaluating strong ellipticity and expands our knowledge in the field. In [3], the use of backward error analysis in tensor complementarity problems is explored. The paper establishes conditions for acceptable solutions and introduces backward errors for assessing algorithm stability. Numerical examples demonstrate the practical application of backward errors. This research contributes to backward error analysis by applying it to tensor complementarity problems and providing theoretical conditions and practical examples. In [4], a method is proposed for finding optimal low-rank quaternion approximations in color image processing. The algorithm eliminates unnecessary components and achieves convergence by using alternating projections. Numerical examples showcase the effectiveness of the method. This paper contributes to color image processing by providing a solution for obtaining optimal low-rank approximations without unnecessary components. In [5], the focus is on functional deep ReLU networks and their approximation capabilities. The paper introduces a new network structure that effectively captures the features of nonlinear continuous functionals. It provides quantitative approximation rates for different scenarios and establishes convergence properties. In [6], distributed learning methods for functional data learning are explored. The proposed algorithm is introduced to handle large-scale functional data across multiple machines. The paper provides theoretical understanding and a semi-supervised approach, advancing the field of distributed learning in functional data learning. In [7], a functional deep neural network is proposed for nonlinear functional regression in functional data learning. The network incorporates kernel embeddings and data-dependent dimension reduction, achieving efficient and robust regression tasks. The paper provides theoretical analysis and numerical simulations to validate the network's advantages.

12301619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12301619.value: The research papers resulting from this proposed project provide a strong foundation for further development in their respective fields. In particular, there is great potential for further development in the field of tensor learning and functional data learning by applying deep neural networks. Deep neural networks (DNNs), with their ability to learn complex patterns and representations from data, can offer valuable insights and advancements in these areas. In tensor learning, DNNs can be employed for tasks such as tensor completion, tensor decomposition, and tensor classification, among others. These models can learn hierarchical representations of tensor data, uncovering hidden features and patterns that may not be easily discernible through traditional methods. In functional data learning, DNNs can provide powerful tools for modeling and analyzing continuous functions. They can capture the complex dynamics and variability present in functional data, allowing for more accurate prediction and classification. However, it is important to note that applying DNNs to these fields also brings challenges, such as model interpretability, overfitting, and the need for large amounts of labeled data. Addressing these challenges and developing novel architectures and methodologies specific to tensor learning and functional data learning will be crucial for further advancements in these areas.

12301619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12301619.value: Tensor learning and functional data learning are two areas of study that deal with complex data structures and patterns. Tensor learning focuses on understanding and analyzing data that is organized in higher-dimensional structures called tensors, which can be thought of as multi-dimensional arrays, similar to matrices but with more dimensions. Tensor learning aims to extract meaningful information from these tensors and uncover hidden patterns or relationships. Functional data learning deals with data that is collected over continuous domains, such as time or space. Instead of individual data points, functional data learning treats the data as a continuous function, allowing for a more comprehensive understanding of how the data changes over the domain. In both tensor learning and functional data learning, we develop mathematical models, algorithms, and techniques to analyze and make sense of complex data. We aim to uncover underlying patterns, relationships, or structures that may not be easily visible in the raw data. These fields have various applications in different domains. For example, in image processing, tensor learning can help in understanding and analyzing multi-dimensional image data, while functional data learning can be used to analyze time-series data, such as stock market trends or weather patterns.
