12302019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302019.value: Convex programming problems arise in many fields of science, engineering, finance, business and management. Hong Kong, as one of the world centers of finance and logistics, has a very strong need for the cutting edge technology in convex programming. For instance, the portfolio optimization in finance and supply chain management in logistics often involve large scale data and require fast and efficient solvers for convex programming. The algorithms studied in this proposal ensure the polynomial-time complexity which is very crucial in developing efficient computational schemes for solving linearly constrained convex programming problems. In the literature, the following two groups of methods are very successful for linearly constrained convex programming. (a) Interior point methods: The success of interior point methods lies in the strong theoretical results. In particular, the polynomial-time complexity has been ensured for linear programming. But the polynomial-time complexity has been only available for certain special classes of linearly constrained convex programming problems. (b) Neural network methods: Besides the attractive hardware implementation, the success of neural network methods is also recognized by the introduction of a continuous trajectory in the form of the solution of some ordinary differential equation. However, the intermediate solution trajectory may not always stay in the interior of the feasible region, which could cause degeneracy issues in some cases. Based on the success of the interior point methods and neural network methods for linearly constrained convex programming, recently the interior point continuous trajectory approach has been introduced. Several interior point continuous trajectories with strong convergence results have been studied for linearly constrained convex programming. These new convergent continuous trajectories have provided alternative choices besides the central path, which could fail to converge for certain linearly constrained convex programming problems. Based on these new convergent interior point continuous trajectories, the main goal of this research project is to develop some interior point polynomial-time algorithms for linearly constrained convex programming. Specifically, in this research project, we will propose a class of novel interior point polynomial-time algorithms for linearly constrained convex programming. Theoretical and numerical investigations on this class of algorithms will be also addressed. In this research proposal, by completing the above tasks, we will be able to develop some new theoretically sound (polynomial-time) and numerical efficient interior point algorithms for convex programming with linear constraints. Our results will advance the state-of-the-art in both theoretical and computational aspects for convex programming.

12302219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302219.value: Inverse scattering problems are mathematical inverse problems arising from the physical phenomenon of wave—matter interaction. The mathematical problem of solving an inverse scattering problem is corresponding to the recovery of unknown/inaccessible physical objects by the measurement of the wave field scattered by the objects. Applications of these problems include sub-wavelength imaging, nondestructive testing, geophysical exploration, radar and sonar. This project is concerned with inverse scattering problems with incomplete measurement data. We consider two types of incomplete data that are of significant importance in applications, namely the limited-aperture data and the phaseless data. The data is called limited-aperture if the measured far-field pattern is not available for all incident angles and all observation angles, and is called phaseless if the measured data contains only the amplitude but not the phase information. For the case of limited-aperture data, we propose two approaches for the computational methods. The first approach is to apply the existing numerical methods on the limited-aperture data directly or a zero extension of the data to full aperture. From the previous works of the PI and preliminary new numerical experiments, we find this simple approach yields surprisingly good results worth further numerical and theoretical studies. The second approach is to first retrieve the data in the unavailable aperture, and then apply the existing numerical methods on the retrieved full-aperture data. One of the method we propose to accomplish this is to consider an approximate analytic continuation through truncated Fourier series expansion and progressive expansion of the aperture. We also consider the case of limited-aperture multi-frequency data, and propose to utilize the frequency-dependent property of the wave to facilitate the retrieval of the missing data. For the case of phaseless data, we propose to extend the PI’s previous work on the reconstruction of convex polyhedral obstacles and gesture recognition. In particular, we consider the reconstruction of non-convex polygonal obstacles and general polyhedral medium scatterers. Due to the complexity of the ray path in these new problems, we shall not consider our previous approach but resort to optimization methods. On the other hand, the key ideas about the geometrical structure of polyhedrons and the physical optics approximation will still be utilized in the set up and numerical solution of the optimization problem. 反散射问题是由波和物质中传播的物理现象生出的数学反问题。解决反散射问题的数学问题对应的实际问题是通过测量散射波重构未知或难以接触的物体。这类问题的应用包括次波长成像，无损探测，地球物理，雷达和声呐。 该项目关心的是不完全数据的反散射问题。我们考虑在应用中非常重要的两类不完全数据，即有限孔径数据和无相位数据。当我们不能得到所有入射方向和观测方向的散射数据时，测量数据被称为有限孔径数据。当我们只能测量到数据的振幅而不包含相位信息时，我们得到的是无相位数据。 针对有限孔径问题，我们提出两种计算方法。第一种方法是把现有的方法直接用于测量数据或有限孔径数据向全口径数据的零延拓。有鉴于申请人之前的工作和一些初步的数值试验，我们发现这个简单的方法可以产出意外好的结果，值得我们进一步的数值和理论研究。第二种方法是首先恢复不可得孔径处的数据，然后应用现有方法于恢复的全口径数据。对与如何恢复数据，我们提出一种基于截断傅立叶展开和渐进扩展孔径的近似解析延拓方法。另外我们还考虑多频有限孔径数据的情形，并提出利用频率相关的波的性质提升数据恢复的效果。 针对无相位数据，我们计划推广申请人之前重构凸多面体和手势识别的工作。特别地，我们考虑重构非凸多面体障碍物和一般的多面体介质物体。由于光线的传播路径变得更为复杂，我们不会考虑申请人以往的方法而转向基于优化的算法。另一方面，在优化问题的建立和数值算法的设计中我们仍将利用之前工作中关于多面体的几何结构和物理光学近似的想法。

12302219.label: Realisation of objectives
12302219.value: The grant has been used to support the research on the computational methods for inverse scattering problems with incomplete data. The project was initiated by Dr. Yuliang Wang in 2019, and the proposal was kindly accepted by RGC. In October 2020, since Dr. Wang left Hong Kong, the PI of this project was changed to current PI, Dr. Wei Wu. Up till the end of the reporting period, we have achieved satisfying progress on the objectives of this project, which can be summarized as follows. The proposed objectives are listed as follows: 1. Conduct numerical and theoretical studies on different sampling methods for inverse scattering problems with limited-aperture data by using the data directly or by the zero extension. Observe and summarize the different effect of the limit aperture on the methods. 2. Conduct numerical and theoretical studies on the retrieval of the missed aperture data by approximate continuation methods at a single frequency. 3. Conduct numerical and theoretical studies on the retrieval of the missed aperture data by approximate continuation methods at multiple frequencies. 4. Design computational methods for the reconstruction of non-convex polyhedral obstacles and general polyhedral medium scatterers with phaseless far-field data by optimization methods, exploiting the geometrical structure of polyhedrons. In the research, we focused on the study of wave propagation in metamaterial. The far-field behavior of metamaterial could be regarded as homogenized regular material, which implies that metamaterial is a meaningful generalization to the model mentioned in the project proposal. In relation to Objective 1 and 2, we carried out the following investigations. 1. We started from the case of a mono-chromatic elastic wave reflected by elastic metamaterial. The elastic metamaterial is an array of air bubbles embedded in elastic background medium. Normally the wave will be scattered by the elastic medium and air bubble, but the scattered wave will dramatically change because of Minneart resonance. From the analysis we proposed an explicit formula for the far-field behavior of the scattered field. 2. We investigated the effective coefficients (i.e. effective Lame parameters) of the elastic metamaterial from the far-field expression. 3. We carried out numerical simulations on the propagation of elastic wave to support our theoretical results. Due to the change of PI, the original objectives were not fully realized. I proposed four revised objectives in the mid-term report which are listed above, and published a few results regarding those objectives in the paper listed in Part 8.

12302219.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302219.value: In the first paper, we showed that the Maxwell transmission eigenfunctions carry both the geometrical and topological properties of the underlying domain Ω. First, we constructed sequences of eigenfunctions (E_1^((n)),E_2^((n)))，n∈N_+ associated with eigenvalues k_n→∞, whose L_2 energies localize around ∂Ω. In fact, we constructed both mono-localized and bi-localized eigenfunctions. Here, by a mono-localized eigenfunction (E_1^((n)),E_2^((n))), we meant that only one of the pair of eigenfunctions is surface-localized while the other one is not, and by bi-localization, we meant both E_1^((n)) and E_2^((n))are surface-localized. In the radial case with constant refractive index, we gave the analytical construction, whereas for the general case, we provided numerical verification. Second, we showed that the transmission eigenfunctions carry the topological structure of the underlying domain Ω when it has multiple connected components. Using the obtained geometrical and topological results, we proposed a novel and interesting application of generating the mirage imaging of a given optical object at a customized location. The main idea was to design suitable illuminating EM fields that are related to the underlying object as well as the associated EM transmission eigenfunctions. In the second paper, we significantly extended the previous Fourier methods for the Helmholtz equation to handle a much more complicated Navier equation. Here we emphasized that the extension is nontrivial and technical, which is distinguished in two aspects. Firstly, we were here concerned with the external force governed by a more complicated vectorial Navier equation. As we shall see, it will create much more difficulties in both theoretical and numerical aspects. Secondly, in this paper, we firstly divided the displacement field into the compressional part and shear part by using the Helmholtz decomposition. Next, according to the appropriate choice of the admissible frequencies, we set up the correspondence between the Fourier coefficients and the coupled-wave field of multi-frequency compressional wave and shear wave. To our best knowledge, this is the first attempt to reconstruct elastic body force by using a non-iterative approach. The salient features of our method can be summarized as follows. To begin with, the Fourier coefficients are formulated directly from linear combinations of compressional wave and shear wave. So our method is very easy to implement with less computational costs. Moreover, our method can be directly applied for very good reconstruction performance from half-plane measurements. Finally, the a priori information is not required for the elastic source and the method is stable and robust to the measured noise, then it has a certain value in practical application. In the third paper, we were aimed at presenting an accurate and higher-order tool to investigate numerical solutions of multi-dimensional unsteady time-fractional integro-partial differential equations with singular kernel. An iterative spectral scheme based on shifted Gegenbauer polynomials was presented to achieve this goal. First, an unknown function u(x, t) was approximated, using shifted Gegenbauer polynomials. Then, novel operational matrices to approximate the time-space delay, fractional/integer-order derivative and weakly singular integral terms were presented for the first time. Picard iteration scheme was incorporated for the iterative spectral method until the required accuracy level is obtained. In order to generate a system of linear equations, collocation approach was utilized. A computer program is developed in Maple software and the scheme is validated, using existing results in literature. Some more problems were also solved to show accuracy, stability, and reliability of the extended computational scheme. The obtained results exhibit that the extended scheme is very accurate, stable, and appropriate to seek the solutions of various problems. Furthermore, the proposed method can be employed for numerical solutions of other multi-dimensional and highly nonlinear problems of fractional or variable orders of physical nature in complex geometry.

12302219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302219.value: We consider the following further development of the research. Firstly, all the finished research didn’t take full elastic equation into consideration, and it is well-known that Lame system is much harder than Helmholtz system. Therefore a generalization of existing results to Lame system would be a challenging work. Secondly, we consider the reconstruction work of limiting far-field data scattered by anisotropic medium or complicated structures. This could have a close relationship with metamaterial, which is a recently heated topic in material science.

12302219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302219.value: In this study, we conducted numerical and theoretical studies on wave propagation in different medium and their resulting phenomenon. We discovered the mathematical relationship between scattered wave and the geometry of scatterers and generalized it to a more complicated fluid case. We also extended the research to the numerical methods on solving the system we’ve studied before.

12302419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302419.value: Remarkable progress has been observed over the last decade in the development of solution-processable organic solar cells (OSCs) made with different polymer donor-/fullerene-blend systems. Fullerene-based acceptors have some limitations with respect to cell performance improvement because of their weak light absorption, limited energy level tuning, and challenging purification process. Therefore, the development of nonfullerene acceptor materials has attracted increasing attention for application to OSCs because of their advantages of tunable electronic properties, high absorption characteristics, low lowest unoccupied molecular orbital and highest occupied molecular orbital energy levels, and solution-fabrication capability for large-area low-cost flexible OSCs. However, the fundamental understanding of the effects of morphology and vertical stratification of bulk heterojunction (BHJ) on charge transfer, charge recombination processes, power conversion efficiency and the stability of nonfullerene OSCs have not yet been systemically studied. We propose to unravel the origin of the efficient operation of nonfullerene OSCs by using newly developed polymer/nonfullerene blend systems. The role of the morphology and the vertical stratification of BHJ in the device design will be examined using the grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering and wide-angle X-ray scattering, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and atomic force microscopy. The effects of a buildup of space charges, charge extraction, and bimolecular recombination processes on the performance and the stability of nonfullerene OSCs will be analyzed using space charge-limited current and photo-physics measurement techniques. The accomplishment of the proposed project will have a profound impact on the development of high-performance solution-processable nonfullerene OSCs. 基於聚合物/富勒烯共混物體系製備的可溶液加工的有機太陽能電池的研發已取得了很大的進步。但富勒烯受體材料的光吸收較差和有限的能級調節，限制了富勒烯有機太陽能電池能量轉換效率的進一步提升。近年來非富勒烯受體材料的開發備受青睞，其可調控的光電特性、高吸收、低最低未佔據分子軌道和最高佔據分子軌道能級以及大面積低成本柔性電池可溶液加工等優點，對有機太陽能電池性能的提升和應用提供了廣闊的前景。然而，聚合物/非富勒烯體異質結的形貌和體相分離對電荷轉移、電池效率和穩定性的影響的系統研究报道比較有限。聚合物/非富勒烯有機太陽能電池的穩定性還面臨著不同的挑戰。 在本項目中，我們提出了通過界面修飾和器件工程的方法研究空間電荷累積，電荷提取和雙分子復合過程及提高器件內建場對有機太陽能電池的性能和穩定性的影響，結合掠入射小角X射線散射、掠入射廣角X射線散射、光電子能譜、原子力顯微鏡、空間電荷限制電流技術和光物理測量等手段來分析和探討有機太陽能電池高效穩定運作的機制，進而提供實現高效穩定非富勒烯有機太陽能電的解決方案。

12302419.label: Realisation of objectives
12302419.value: This GRF research project deals with a systematic study on stability of nonfullerene acceptor (NFA)-based bulk heterojunction (BHJ) organic solar cells (OSCs). The research work has been focused on realization of three objectives: (1) to investigate the effects of morphology and the vertical stratification of a BHJ on charge transfer and recombination in NFA-based OSCs, (2) to unravel the origin of efficient operation of NFA-based OSCs and develop approaches to suppress bimolecular recombination and enhance charge extraction probability, and (3) to identify the degradation pathways through an analysis of the charge transport properties in a BHJ and to find solutions to enhance the operational stability of NFA-based OSCs. These project tasks have been accomplished successfully. The achievements of the project are highlighted below: (1) To investigate the effects of morphology and the vertical stratification of a BHJ on charge transfer and recombination in NFA-based OSCs Operational stability of NFA-based OSCs is closely associated with the choice of materials, material processing, morphology of functional layers, stratification of donor and acceptor in BHJ, interfacial chemical reaction at the BHJ/charge-transporting layer, balanced charge mobility in BHJ and built-in potential across OSCs. The separation of NFA and polymer donor molecules in BHJ affects exciton dissociation, resulting in transporting charges through drift conduction in BHJ under an internal electric field in OSCs. To ensure effective charge transfer and minimize recombination processes, it is imperative to maintain a high built-in potential across BHJ. Different approaches, including hole-transporting layer (HTL)/BHJ and electron-transporting layer (ETL)/BHJ interfacial engineering, morphology control of BHJ, and optimization of ternary blend system, were adopted for retaining a high built-in potential across BHJ, thereby improving the stability of NFA-based OSCs. HTL/BHJ and ETL/BHJ interfacial reactions, and vertical phase separation of donor and acceptor in BHJ, were analyzed using the layer-by-layer (LBL) method in OSC fabrication. It shows that the LBL technique can realize a gradient donor/acceptor profile based BHJ, providing a preferred vertical donor/acceptor distribution in the active layer, thereby realizing an adequate donor/acceptor interface for efficient charge transport. The photoactive blend layer with a vertical structural profile of donor/BHJ/acceptor avoids the formation of undesired NFA-rich/HTL interface, thereby maintaining a high built-in potential across OSCs. (2) To unravel the origin of efficient operation of NFA-based OSCs and develop approaches to suppress bimolecular recombination and enhance charge extraction probability. The interfacial exciton dissociation, charge recombination and collection in OSCs were analyzed using a combination of theoretical simulation, photoelectron spectroscopy, transient photocurrent, and photo-induced charge extraction by linearly increasing voltage techniques. Several approaches were used to achieve a high built-in potential across BHJ, and hence to enhance the operational stability of NFA-based OSCs. The stable built-in potential in OSCs is realized through suppression of the interfacial reaction between BHJ and PEDOT:PSS HTL. It shows that MoO3-induced oxidation doping in PEDOT:PSS can effectively suppress the interfacial chemical reactions between the NFAs and PEDOT:PSS, thereby leading to a significant enhancement in power conversion efficiency (PCE) and stability of NFA-based OSCs. NFA-based ternary OSCs with a high PCE, attributed to the enhanced light absorption and improved energy level alignment at the BHJ/contact interface, was also studied. It shows that incorporation of the fullerene acceptor [6,6]-Phenyl-C71-butyric acid methyl ester (PC71BM) in a PM6:Y6-based binary BHJ system is beneficial for improving the operational stability of the ternary OSCs as compared to that of a control OSC with a conventional binary blend system. The use of the ternary BHJ with an addition of PC71BM helps to improve the performance of NFA-based OSCs by providing an electron percolation path in the PM6 matrix, while Y6 molecules in the blend layer tend to segregate towards the HTL/BHJ side in the blend layer. Hence, the use of PC71BM in the ternary blend system assists in alleviating charge recombination through efficient charge separation and electron transporting in the ternary blend system, leading to a high built-in potential, and contributing to the improvement in the operational stability of the ternary OSCs. (3) To identify the degradation pathways through an analysis of the charge transport properties in a BHJ and to find solutions to enhance the operational stability of NFA-based OSCs. This work identifies that removal of the interfacial chemical reactions between PEDOT:PSS HTL and the 2-(3-oxo-2,3-dihydroinden-1-ylidene)malononitrile (INCN) moieties in NFA-based OSCs is one of the critical factors for enhancing the operational stability of NFA-based OSCs. The use of a hybrid PEDOT:PSS-MoO3 HTL helps to eliminate the interfacial reaction between the PEDOT:PSS HTL and INCN moieties in NFA, one of the recently found major degradation mechanisms in NFA-based OSCs with a PEDOT:PSS HTL. The use of a hybrid PEDOT:PSS-MoO3 HTL also favors the stable operation of OSCs through retaining a high built-in potential. Therefore, a high and stable built-in potential in NFA-based OSCs with a hybrid PEDOT:PSS-MoO3 HTL is obtained to maintain an efficient charge transporting process, thereby achieving a high PCE. The possible interfacial reaction at the BHJ/ETL in NFA-based OSCs also was examined. It shows that the use of a hybrid ZnO:N,N'-Bis(N,N-dimethylpropan-1-amine oxide)perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic diimide (PDINO) ETL assists in retaining a stable and high built-in potential and UV stability of the PM6:Y6-based OSCs. The improvement in UV stability of NFA-based OSCs is obtained by preventing the chemical reactions at the hybrid ZnO:PDINO ETL/BHJ interface, which would otherwise occur at the BHJ/ZnO interface in a control OSC, caused by the photocatalytic effect of ZnO. The findings and solutions for achieving efficient and stable NFA-based opaque OSCs have also been adopted for developing high-performance NFA-based high-performance semitransparent OSCs. The work was also extended to study built-in potential and its impacts on operational stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). The results reveal that deterioration in the built-in potential in the PSCs is closely related to the formation of secondary phase in the perovskite active layer. The formation of the secondary phase in the active layer is related to the hydrolysis of the precursor solution. The suppression of the moisture encroachment greatly enhances the durability of the precursor solution and performance reproducibility of PSCs. The results reveal that HTL engineering can be an effective approach for enhancing the built-in potential across the perovskite photoactive layer in the PSCs. The outcomes of the work are very inspiring, providing a solution-processable and cost-effective approach for attaining high-performance solution-processable PSCs. The research findings and achievements in improved understanding of degradation pathways in NFA-OSCs and solutions developed for efficient and stable operation of OSCs were reported in 12 journal publications and 3 book chapters.

12302419.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302419.value: The outcomes of this GRF project provide an improved understanding of the organic/electrode interfacial exciton dissociation, charge recombination processes and charge collection, which underpin the optimum device design and performance. The charge transport and recombination properties in OSCs are investigated systematically using a combination of theoretical calculation, transient photocurrent measurements, morphology analyses and device optimization. It is found that the origin of unfavorable charge collection is mainly due to the trap-limited bimolecular recombination, resulting in the compensation of drifted photo-generated electrons at the organic/cathode interface. Enhancing stability of OSCs can be realized through interfacial modification for retaining a high built-in potential across BHJ. The use of an NFA-inert HTL benefits the efficient operation of NFA-based OSCs through suppression of interfacial reaction between the HTL and the INCN moieties in NFA. A high and stable built-in potential in NFA-based OSCs is essential for an efficient charge transporting process, thereby achieving a high PCE. The improvement in the performance of NFA-based OSCs can be attributed to 1) realizing a high and stable built-in potential obtained through modification of charge-transporting layers, 2) alleviating undesirable interfacial reactions at HTL/BHJ and BHJ/ETL interfaces, and 3) achieve efficient and balanced charge transporting process through mitigating non-radiative recombination process in OSCs [Part C, journal publications 3, 4-6, 8, and the book chapters]. Based on the knowledge gained through the improved understanding of NFA-based OSCs, we also carried out collaborative work with research groups from Shanghai University and University Polytechnique Hauts-de-France to develop high-performance NFA-based semitransparent OSCs over the two competing indexes of PCE and visible light transparency. The outcomes of the collaborative work are very encouraging. A combination of low/high index optical coupling layer is designed for high-performance semitransparent NFA-based OSCs. [Part C, journal publications 1, 2 and 7].

12302419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302419.value: NFA-based OSCs offer an attractive option for achieving low-cost and clean energy sources. The unique flexibility and semi-transparency feature of NFA-based OSCs also add a decorative and aesthetic dimension to the solar cells so that they can be used on curved and irregular surfaces, which cannot be done using traditional rigid silicon solar cells. Single junction NFA-based OSCs with a PCE of >19% have been reported, realized through an extended absorption in near-infrared (NIR) region. The development of semitransparent OSCs is still in the development stage, particularly the design and optimization of cell performance over the two competing indexes of PCE and average visible transmittance. Semitransparent OSC technology can be advanced through new materials development, including new low bandgap polymers and NFAs with enhanced absorption in NIR region, for applications in mobile electronics, smart sensors, automotive, power generating windows, building-integrated photovoltaic and self-powered greenhouse. It is envisaged that the accomplishments made with stable operation of NFA-based OSCs in the GRF (12302419) project will provide a strong support and solid foundation to the development of high-performance semitransparent OSCs.

12302419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302419.value: Exciting progress has been made in the development of high-performance NFA-based OSCs. Apart from PCE and cost competitiveness, operational stability is another important factor with practical implications if OSCs were to be a feasible option for a sustainable green energy source. This work identifies that a gradual decrease in built-in potential in NFA-based OSCs is one of the reasons leading to the deterioration in stability of NFA-based OSCs, caused by the interfacial reaction between charge-transporting interlayers and NFAs. Improvement in operational stability of NFA-based OSCs was realized by incorporating an NFA-inert interlayer, obtained by interfacial engineering. The results reveal that the use of NFA-inert interlayer prevents the interfacial chemical reaction, leading to an obvious increase in built-in potential across photoactive active layer in the devices. As a result, NFA-based OSCs with an NFA-inert interlayer exhibit a significant enhancement in device stability as compared to a control OSC with a commonly used PEDOT:PSS interlayer. It demonstrates the importance of interfacial control on achieving high stability of NFA-based OSCs and highlights the importance of developing interfacial modification approaches that have good process compatibility with NFA-based OSCs, prepared by solution-fabrication processes.

12302819.label: Project Objectives
12302819.value: We study kernel-based algorithms that perform simultaneously robust learning and outliers detection. Minimax optimal learning rates as well as outliers detection consistency will be derived for regression, pairwise learning and classification under the mean-shift outlier model, respectively. We study kernel-based gradient descent algorithms associated with truncated loss functions within the framework of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. The error analysis will be conducted and the impact of the scaling parameter on the convergence rates will be discussed. We study spectral regularization algorithms for regression function tests and goodness-of-fit tests with maximum mean discrepancy. Optimal testing rates will be derived by methods from learning theory and approximation theory. We carry out error analysis and derive optimal rates for distributed schemes together with the learning and testing algorithms proposed in this project.

12302819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302819.value: Modern applications arising from science, society and industry often involve large-scale data that create challenges for various learning tasks. With the advent of data science, an urgent need has been emerged to develop new mathematical theory to better understand the performance of numerous modern learning schemes such as distributed learning, online learning, deep learning, and many others. The goal of this project is to investigate theoretical properties of some kernel-based learning and testing schemes for large-scale data with the help of learning theory. We shall first present a general framework for double penalized kernel-based algorithms that perform simultaneously robust learning and outliers detection for contaminated data. We shall derive minimax optimal learning rates as well as outliers detection consistency for regression, pairwise learning and classification under the so-called mean-shift outlier model, respectively. We shall carry out error analysis for gradient descent algorithms associated with truncated loss functions and derive fast learning rates by choosing appropriate scaling parameter that balances the robustness and predictive performance. We shall study the spectral regularization algorithms for regression function tests in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. A Ward-type test statistic will be studied and optimal testing rates will be derived by employing the second order decomposition of operator differences. Regression function tests with varying Gaussian kernel will also be considered and error analysis will be conducted. Then we shall study kernel methods for goodness-of-fit tests associated with maximum mean discrepancy and spectral regularization algorithms. 12302819.label: Realisation of objectives
12302819.value: All objectives related to developing the mathematical theory of learning algorithms for managing large-scale and high-dimensional data have been successfully achieved. Specifically, we have introduced kernel methods and neural network techniques to handle infinite-dimensional functional data, enabling the creation of scalable and robust machine learning algorithms for supervised learning tasks. Functional data learning provides a versatile framework for analyzing inherently infinite-dimensional data represented by random functions or curves. The past two decades have seen a significant surge in interest surrounding the challenges of prediction and estimation in functional linear regression. This increased focus arises from the broad spectrum of applications where functional linear regression proves beneficial, spanning domains such as chemometrics, econometrics, biomedical studies, and more. In [4], we explore robust functional linear regression models involving a scalar response and a functional predictor within the reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces framework. To address the associated empirical risk minimization problem, we introduce a gradient descent algorithm with early stopping, integrating robust loss functions. We establish the algorithm's convergence under appropriate conditions and provide explicit learning rates for both estimation and prediction errors, determined by the regression function's regularity and the decay rate of eigenvalues linked to the integral operator induced by the reproducing kernel and covariance function. In [5], we tackle the challenge of functional linear regression in the presence of outliers by proposing an outlier-resistant model that enables robust regression and outlier detection concurrently. This model incorporates a subject-specific mean shift parameter to identify outliers and employs a double-penalized least squares method alongside the representer theorem within reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces to estimate the functional component and mean shift parameter. We establish the minimax convergence rate for both prediction and estimation in this model, highlighting that the estimation rate for the mean shift parameter remains unaffected by the functional component. However, the prediction rate for the functional component may be slowed down to the rate associated with outlier detection. Numerical studies are conducted to showcase the efficacy of the proposed methods. In [1], we investigate the potential of functional neural networks to approximate nonlinear continuous functionals in Lp space. Specifically focusing on functional deep neural networks utilizing the rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation function, we analyze the approximation rates for these networks under mild regularity conditions through continuous piecewise linear interpolation with a simple triangulation, contributing to the advancement of our understanding of functional data learning algorithms. Exploring the stability and generalization properties of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is crucial in the realm of machine learning, given its widespread use for training models on large-scale datasets due to its efficiency and scalability. Understanding the stability and generalization aspects of SGD offers valuable insights into the behavior and performance of learning algorithms. In [3], we concentrate on algorithmic stability in statistical learning theory, introducing pointwise uniform stability as a novel measure to evaluate an algorithm's sensitivity to perturbations in individual training examples. This alternative stability metric provides nearly optimal bounds and facilitates deriving the first high-probability bound for the generalization gap, measured in gradients. Sharper bounds for strongly convex and smooth problems are obtained, enhancing generalization bounds for stochastic gradient descent. Additionally, we develop concentration inequalities for sums of weakly-dependent vector-valued random variables, which may be of independent interest. Handling high-dimensional data in classification presents significant challenges in machine learning, as datasets with a large number of features compared to samples are common across various domains such as image recognition, genomics, text analysis, and sensor data processing. In [2], we introduce large-margin unified machines (LUMs) as a potent approach to address binary classification problems. LUMs act as a bridge between distribution-based likelihood methods and margin-based approaches, effectively resolving the data piling issue faced by support vector machines in scenarios with high-dimensional data and limited samples. We establish comparison theorems for LUM loss functions, crucial for analyzing large-margin learning algorithms, and derive learning rates for regularized LUM schemes employing Gaussian kernels, which hold independent significance. Our research results have been effectively published in prestigious journals like ACHA, JFAA, JoC, validating the excellence and importance of our academic pursuits. These publications not only showcase the quality of our research but also underscore the broader impact and relevance of our work within the academic sphere and beyond. Additionally, we are honored to have the opportunity to mentor a Ph.D. student on the topic "Communication-efficient distributed optimization and federated learning". 12302819.label: Major findings and research outcome
12302819.value: In [1], we focus on functional neural networks and their ability to approximate nonlinear continuous functionals in Lp space. We specifically investigate the approximation power of functional deep neural networks using the rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation function. By constructing a continuous piecewise linear interpolation under a simple triangulation, we explore the rates of approximation for these networks under mild regularity conditions. This study contributes to the understanding of functional data learning algorithms. In [2], we introduce large-margin unified machines (LUMs) to address binary classification problems. LUMs bridge distribution-based likelihood and margin-based approaches, mitigating the data piling issue of support vector machines in high-dimensional, low-sample size scenarios. Comparison theorems for LUM loss functions are established, aiding in the analysis of large-margin learning algorithms, along with learning rates for regularized LUM schemes with Gaussian kernels. In [3], we focus on algorithmic stability in statistical learning theory. The novel pointwise uniform stability measure examines algorithm sensitivity to individual training example perturbations, leading to nearly optimal bounds and high-probability generalization gap estimates. The study enhances generalization bounds for stochastic gradient descent through sharper bounds for strongly convex and smooth problems, with the development of concentration inequalities for weakly-dependent vector-valued random variables. In [4], we delve into robust functional linear regression models with a scalar response and functional predictor in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. We propose a gradient descent algorithm with early stopping and robust loss functions. Convergence of the algorithm is proven under specific conditions, offering learning rates for estimation and prediction errors based on regression function regularity and eigenvalue decay rate of the integral operator. In [5], we address functional linear regression in the presence of outliers by introducing an outlier-resistant model for robust regression and detection. The model includes a mean shift parameter for outlier identification, utilizing a double-penalized least squares method and the representer theorem within reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces. Minimax convergence rates are determined for prediction and estimation, revealing unaffected estimation rates for the mean shift parameter but potentially slowed prediction rates for the functional component. Numerical studies support the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

12302819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12302819.value: To advance the study on functional neural networks, it is worth exploring the effectiveness of different activation functions and network architectures, such as sigmoid or hyperbolic tangent, in the context of functional data learning. This exploration can provide valuable insights into the performance characteristics of these alternatives. Additionally, investigating the impact of network depth and width on approximation rates can help identify the most suitable architecture for handling functional tasks. By thoroughly examining these aspects, we can gain a deeper understanding of the capabilities and limitations of functional neural networks. Expanding the concept of pointwise uniform stability introduced in the research, future studies can apply this measure to a wide range of algorithms and domains. By evaluating the stability properties of popular algorithms, including but not limited to random forests and gradient boosting, we can gain valuable insights into the generalization behavior of these methods. This analysis can provide guidance on selecting appropriate algorithms for specific scenarios and shed light on the trade-offs between stability and other performance metrics. By exploring stability measures in different contexts and relating them to data characteristics, such as distribution or noise levels, we can develop more robust learning algorithms that generalize well across diverse datasets. To improve the gradient descent algorithm for robust functional linear regression models, We can consider alternative optimization techniques, such as stochastic gradient descent. Exploring these techniques can potentially enhance the convergence speed of the algorithm and overcome any existing limitations. Additionally, extending the robust loss functions to handle various types of outliers or heavy-tailed distributions can significantly enhance the model's robustness in real-world applications. By incorporating these extensions, the model can better handle challenging data instances and provide more reliable predictions.

12302819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12302819.value: This project aims to develop and analyze learning algorithms for managing large-scale and high-dimensional data. We investigated how functional neural networks learn nonlinear and continuous functionals, improving our understanding of their approximation capabilities and enhancing learning algorithms for infinite-dimensional data processing. We introduced large-margin unified machines for solving classification problems, especially in scenarios with high-dimensional data and limited samples. Additionally, we focused on the stability of machine learning algorithms by introducing pointwise uniform stability to measure sensitivity to individual training instances, refining generalization bounds for stochastic gradient descent and developing more robust learning algorithms. Our exploration of functional linear regression models with functions as predictors introduced a new algorithm, gradient descent with early stopping, and robust loss functions to handle outliers, enhancing regression accuracy and understanding robust regression methods. We also addressed outliers in functional linear regression by proposing a model that detects outliers and performs robust regression simultaneously, offering insights into managing outliers in regression problems and improving model performance. These studies advance our knowledge of neural networks, classification algorithms, stability measures, and regression models in machine learning, strengthening the precision, resilience, and reliability of machine learning algorithms for improved predictions and insights across various applications.

12302919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12302919.value: The project is mainly concerned with the mathematical and computational studies on the identification of anomalies beneath the Earth using the geomagnetic monitoring. Consider a collection of certain unknown anomalies presented in the shell of the Earth. The anomalies interrupt the geomagnetic field. Hence, one can monitor the variation of the geomagnetic field and use it to identify the underlying anomalies. We propose to investigate two scenarios that are motivated by the practical applications. In the first one, the variation of the magnetic field is caused by the presence of certain unknown anomalies, and as a practical example, this may be the presence of submarines. In the second one, the variation of the magnetic field is caused by the change of the unknown anomalies, and as practical examples, this may be the growth of a certain mineral or the expansion of an underground lake. In our study, we propose to consider two geomagnetic models, with the first one described by a Maxwell system and the other one described by a hydromagnetic dynamo system. We formulate the geomagnetic anomaly detection as nonlinear inverse problems associated with the aforementioned geomagnetic models. The unknowns in these inverse problems are the locations, shapes and material parameters of the underlying anomalies, and the measurement data for these inverse problems are the variations of the geomagnetic field due to the presence or the change of the anomalies. Furthermore, from a practical point of view, we shall not assume any a-priori knowledge on the geomagnetic configuration of the Earth's core. We aim to establish the unique recovery results for those proposed inverse problems in these challenging but practically significant scenarios. That is, we shall establish sufficient conditions under which the anomalies can be uniquely identified by the corresponding measurement data. Based on the theoretical results, we aim to further develop efficient numerical recovery schemes for the anomaly identification. The proposed theoretical study shall lay out a rigorous mathematical theory to the geomagnetic detection technology that has been used in practice. The corresponding computational study shall provide novel and efficient reconstruction methods for the detections that are of significant real values. 在此項目中，我們主要開展關於地磁探測技術的數學研究。地磁勘探主要利用監測到的地球磁場的變化，反演出導致此變化的地殼中的未知物體。此種技術已經取得了若干重要的應用，但是相關的數學理論研究還非常少。此項目的目標即為地磁勘探技術發展出系統的數學理論，並基於相應的理論結果發展中高效的反演算法。我們主要考慮兩類數學模型：第一類由一個線性的Maxwell系統描述，而第二類由一個耦合的磁流體系統描述。在上述兩類模型中，我們又主要研究兩類具有重要應用背景的情形。第一種情形下，地球磁場的變化是由未知物體的出現導致的；而在第二種情形下，地球磁場的變化是由未知物體的形狀大小改變或者位置的改變引起的。在上述不同的模型及不同的應用情形下，我們研究相關的反演問題，建立起相應的唯一可重構性及基於得到的理論結果發展高效的反演算法。

12303019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303019.value: To study the mode coupling mechanism of plasmonic hybrid device with nanocavity that has passive/active medium in the nanocavity, and the study will lead to demonstration of plasmonic hybrid device that has duo optical characteristics i.e. possessing both conventional mode coupling as well as parity time symmetry. Our recent work has shown that SPP can couple effectively with the nanocavity modes in a plasmonic hybrid nanocavity device, leading to Rabi-analogue split. When the passive medium inside the nanocavity is an active medium that can effectively couple the active medium luminescence to the SPP/nanocavity coupled mode was observed. This led to the observation of parity time symmetry–like characteristics and we attributed it to the suppression of the nanocavity loss. From our theoretical analysis, we can see that the plasmonic hybrid device with active medium could be designed with a strong parity time symmetry property (PTS). This needs further investigation to appreciate its physics. This proposal seeks to investigate theoretically and experimentally on the mode coupling mechanism of plasmonic hybrid device; how the design can be tuned so that it can have conventional mode coupling mode/PTS and finally demonstrating a device with duo optical characteristics – conventional mode coupling and PTS. 這項目研究具有增益介質微腔的等离子混合微腔的模式耦合機制。我們最近的工作表明，SPP可以有效地耦合混合微腔器件中的微腔模式，導致類似-Rabi分裂。當微腔內的被動介質被具有增益質取代時，將創建四波混合條件;觀察了具有增益質發光與SPP/微腔耦合模式的耦合有增强。這導致了增強的類似-Rabi分裂，我們將其歸因於微腔損耗的抑制。 從理論分析中可以看出，四波模式耦合機制仍有許多方面需要進一步研究，才能認識其物理特性。這項工作，對四波模式耦合機制進行理論和實驗研究。

12303019.label: Major findings and research outcome
12303019.value: We have theoretically and experimentally investigated nano-structures that can enhance breaking of PTS (Parity-Time Symmetry). We focused on metasurface and coupled nano-cavities; in metasurface, we use a quad-atom plasmonic metasurface to generate a nonlinear vectorial holography through the second harmonic (SH) generation [1]. Through making use of nonlinear geometric phase, we simultaneously manipulated the amplitude and phase of both left and right circularly polarized SH waves which are generated from the quad-atom metasurface. By superposing the two orthogonal polarization components, the metasurface then produced nonlinear holographic images with vectorial polarization distributions. For the coupled nano-cavities work, linear and non-linear optical coupling of the cavity modes were studied theoretically [2, 3]. Double Exceptional Points (EP) are obtained in the linear optical regime [2, 3] and when one of the passive dielectric medium is replaced by an optically active medium, non-linear optical effect begins to contribute strongly in the cavity mode coupling. This leads to time symmetry breaking [3] that manifest itself as optical bistability. We are currently verifying the theoretical findings experimentally. We have also explored the possibility of novel plasmonic materials and to this end, we have experimentally and theoretically investigated the plasmonic property of Ag/Yb alloy [4]; a gradual decrease in the resonant plasmonic frequency with a corresponding blue shift in the resonant peak wavelength was observed with the increase in Yb concentration. Furthermore, the transparency increases at the longer wavelength region of the optical range with the increase in Yb concentration. Our theoretical model shows that the bound charges, i.e., the trapped electrons, are responsible for the resonant peak blue shift, which is a consequence of bulk ε(Yb) << ε(Ag), whereas the lower plasmonic resonant frequency of Yb gives rise to greater transmission at the longer wavelength region. Ningbin Mao, Guanqing Zhang, Yutao Tang, Yang Li, Zixian Hu, Xuecai Zhang, Kingfai Li, Kokwai Cheah, and Guixin Li, `Nonlinear vectorial holography with quad-atom metasurfaces’, PNAS, 119, 22 (2022). 2. Jianming Mai, Yu Chen, Guixin Li and Kok Wai Cheah, `Double Exceptional Points in Grating Coupled Metal-Insulator-Metal Heterostructure’, Optics Express, 30(22), 40053-40062 (2022). 3. Jianming Mai and Kok Wai Cheah, `Nonreciprocal transmission in a nonlinear coupled heterostructure’, Optics Express, 30(26), 46357-46265 (2022). 4. Suet Ying Ching, Chak Ming Chan, Jack Ng and Kok Wai Cheah, 'Doped Ag - novel Tunable Plasmonic Material', Photonics, 8, 288-299 (2021).

12303019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
12303019.value: For the vectorial holography generated by metasurface, the major short coming is the low optical efficiency of plasmonic surface. However, this can be ameliorate through using dielectric materials with high nonlinear susceptibilities. Potential applications are high-capacity optical information storage, optical encryption and bio-imaging. For coupled nano-cvities, potential applications are high sensitivity optical sensors in low power or auto-tunable power fuse at high-power for high-power laser devices. Also in metal-dielectric-metal (MDM) plasmonic waveguides, photonic crystal (PC) waveguides and whispering-gallery microcavities (WGM). The novel Ag/Yb alloy opens up the possibility of the introduction of a new class of tunable plasmonic ‘transparent’ metal alloys.

12303019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303019.value: Through using nano-pattern or nano-device, novel optical properties can be developed. Some examples are holography and ultra-fast optical gate or optical power threshold sensor. They can be applied to for examples laser power control, optical information storage and bio-imaging. A new class of tunable plasmonic ‘transparent’ metal alloy is developed: Ag/Yb alloy.

12303319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303319.value: Triclocarban (TCC) is a widely used antimicrobial agent added to consumer and personal care products. It has been classified as an emerging contaminant of concern due to its widespread occurrence, environmental persistence, bioaccumulation, and potential toxicity. Recent studies have shown liver toxicity related to TCC exposure, but the toxicological effects and potential mechanism induced by TCC is largely unknown. After TCC enters animal or human body, the chemical can be metabolized to hydroxylated triclocarbans (OH-TCCs) that may possess higher toxicity. However, current studies largely neglected the potential toxicity related to OH-TCCs. Therefore, this proposal attempts to combine advanced mass spectrometry (MS) and related omics techniques to investigate the underlying mechanism of liver toxicity induced by TCC and OH-TCCs. Both cell and animal models will be used. Chemical synthesis has been utilized to obtain OH-TCC standards because of their commercially unavailability. The metabolomics and lipidomics will be applied to study the changes of endogenous metabolic profiles related to TCC/OH-TCC exposures. Specifically, non-targeted analysis will be conducted to identify small molecule biomarkers, metabolic pathways and networks related to liver toxicity. Targeted metabolomics/lipidomics analysis will be performed to clarify the metabolic changes of selected biomarkers and to investigate the potential target sites of TCC/OH-TCC. Moreover, matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization-mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) will be used to reveal distribution difference of endogenous metabolites in animal liver tissue. Biological verification of the proposed hypothesis will be carried out throughout the study. The proposed research will be an important step towards the understanding of mechanism of liver toxicity induced by TCC and OH-TCCs at cellular and molecular levels, providing scientific basis for human health risk assessments. The platform established in this project can help shed light on the investigation of toxicological effects of other environmental contaminants. 三氯卡班（Triclocarban，TCC）是一種常用的氯代抗菌劑，被廣泛添加於家用及個人護理品中。隨著人們對TCC的普遍應用性、環境持久性、生物富集性及潛在毒性認識的加深，TCC被確認為一種新型環境污染物。近期研究表明，TCC對生物體具有肝臟毒性，但其毒性效應和致毒機制尚不完全明確。此外，TCC進入生物體後會被代謝生成可能具有更高毒性的羥基三氯卡班（OH-TCCs），但現有研究大多忽略了OH-TCCs的毒性作用。因此，本專案以TCC和OH-TCCs為研究目標，首先採用化學合成法製備OH-TCCs的標準品，進而結合先進的質譜技術和組學手段，採用細胞和動物實驗模型，探究TCC和OH-TCCs引發內源性代謝物的變化，揭示其誘導肝毒性。具體地，將通過非靶向代謝組學手段，首先篩選與肝臟毒性相關的小分子生物標誌物及代謝通路；進而採用靶向代謝組學和脂質組學分析，明確生物標誌物的毒性回應特徵，確定TCC和OH-TCCs的毒性作用靶點。此外，本項目將採用基質輔助鐳射解吸電離-質譜成像（MALDI-MSI）技術，進一步探究動物肝臟組織中內源性代謝物的分佈差異，同時對實驗發現進行系統的生物學驗證。本項目研究以期在細胞和分子水準闡述TCC和OH-TCCs誘發肝毒性，為準確評估TCC的人體暴露健康風險提供重要的科學依據。所建立的研究平臺還將為其他環境污染物的毒理學研究提供理論和技術基礎。

12303319.label: Realisation of objectives
12303319.value: 1. Method development of the analysis of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban and their derivatives in biological samples. An analytical method for the simultaneous determination of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban by using UHPLC-MS/MS was developed and applied for biological sample analysis. Biological sample preparation procedures for the analysis of these components and its derivatives were established and validated. Mass spectrometric fragmentation pathways of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban were investigated by using electrospray ionization Orbitrap mass spectrometry in the presence of rat liver slices. The elemental compositions of the ions were calculated from the accurate mass data. The proposed fragmentation pathways of representative compounds of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban were verified from the analysis of isotope-labeled compounds. 2. Nontargeted metabolomics and lipidomics methods development and applications in investigation of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban induced toxicity in mice model An UHPLC/HR-ESI‐MS method was developed for the determination of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban induced toxicity in mice model. The chromatography peak alignment and metabolite extraction were achieved using the software R. Multivariate analysis, including principal component analysis (PCA), random forest (RF), partial least squares discriminate analysis (PLS-DA), and/or orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA), were implemented using software SIMCAP. The fold change was calculated by comparing the relative peak intensity of metabolites in different groups. A variety of dysregulated metabolites were found based on the criteria (VIP scores in PLS-DA > 1; P value < 0.05 and fold change >1.2 or < 0.8) between the control and exposure groups. These potential metabolite biomarkers were structurally identified by matching MS/MS fragments with data in the databases of METLIN and Human Metabolome Database. After that, a nontargeted lipidomics method with the utility of Orbitrap Fusion™ Tribrid™ mass spectrometer was developed and applied for investigation of lipid dysregulation in mice model. LipidSearch was utilized for identification of lipid species in samples by matching MS/MS fragments with MS library data. Meanwhile, the potential lipid biomarkers were selected based on VIP scores in PLSDA (VIP > 1), as well as P-value (P < 0.05) and FC (FC >1.2 or < 0.8) between the control and exposure groups. 3. Targeted metabolomics and lipidomics analyses and verification After the identification of the differential metabolite biomarkers and metabolic pathways, the endogenous metabolites altered by triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban exposure, including carbohydrates, amino acids, nucleic acids, and lipids have been quantified. Both UHPLC-MS/MS and GC-MS/MS were used for the quantification. For UHPLC-MS/MS analysis, multiple reaction monitoring mode was applied, the collision energy for each metabolite was optimized for the MRM transitions. GC-MS/MS method was developed for metabolites with small molecular weight and high polarity, such as short chain fatty acids and some amino acids. Particularly, the established methods allow quantification of various endogenous metabolites, such as amino acids, long chain-free fatty acids and acylcarnitine species. The developed methods will then be applied for targeted quantification of endogenous metabolites in cell samples, as well as mice liver and plasma samples from triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban exposure and control groups The methods were validated with high accuracy, precision, and reproducibility, which were accordingly used in investigation of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban induced toxicity. 4. Biological verification of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban induced toxicity Based on the differential metabolic pathway, the changes of related enzyme activities induced by triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban in hepatic cells and mice livers were measured. The liver function indicators, such as serum alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, aspartate aminotransferase, and alpha-fetoprotein will be tested. Meanwhile, RT-PCR measurement was applied for the detection of mRNA expression levels of related genes. Western blot was used to determine the expression levels of corresponding proteins. Other biological indicators, such as inflammatory factors, oxidative stress response, cell cycle and apoptosis were also investigated according to metabolomics and lipidomics experimental results. The hepatotoxicity mechanisms induced by triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban were elaborated based on the available advanced MS analytical platforms and omics strategies. The results collectively provided information for human health risk assessments of triclocarban and hydroxylated triclocarban exposure and extend our understanding of the interactions between human biomolecules and environmental pollutants.

12303319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
12303319.value: Triclocarban is a polychlorinated aromatic antimicrobial that has been extensively used in consumer and personal care products and extensively detected in human blood and urine samples. Human and animals are exposed to TCC mainly through direct contact with personal care products. After TCC enters human body, the chemical can be metabolized to hydroxylated triclocarbons (OH-TCCs) that may be covalently bound to biomolecules, posing significant threats to human health. TCC is also shown to be an endocrine disruptor that has significant reproductive and developmental impacts on organisms. Although TCC-induced liver toxicity has been reported, but there is a paucity of research on the toxicological effects and potential mechanism. More importantly, the toxicity induced by OH-TCCs, the hydroxylated metabolites of TCC, is often neglected, while being critical for the clarification of toxic mechanism. This proposal combined advanced mass spectrometry (MS) and related omics techniques to investigate the underlying mechanism of liver toxicity induced by TCC and OH-TCCs. By using targeted metabolomics and lipidomics analyses, the alerted metabolites and metabolic pathways induced by TCC and OH-TCCs were investigated, which thus provided scientific basis for human health risk assessments.

12303419.label: Project Objectives
12303419.value: For the cases with ﬁxed order q, consider spiked models including spiked population, Fisher and autocovariance models. We will propose some eigenvalue diﬀerence-based criteria. These criteria will be based on the ratios of diﬀerences. To well separate the ratio at the true order from the others, we will suggest adding a ridge value in the ratios such that the sequence of ratios has a so-called valley-cliﬀ pattern. That is, the true order is the index of a ratio that is smaller than a threshold and all subsequent ratios are greater than the threshold. This method could also handle multiple local minima problems from which all existing methods suﬀer at the sample level. Another typical issue in the setting of p/n → c is that only the order that corresponds the number of eigenvalues that are larger than some bound can be identiﬁed. We then also study the optimality of upper bounds for these models. Also for the cases with ﬁxed order q, consider principal component and canonical correlation models. We will consider the model structure that some components or pairs of linear combinations of the random vectors plays important role and the others have no contribution to explain the variation of data. We then propose a double ridge ratio criterion that is based on eigenvalues rather than their diﬀerences. The double ratio is to make the ratio at the true order much closer to zero at the sample level than the single ratio and adding ridge is again to create a valley-cliﬀ pattern. When the order q is also divergent with increasing the sample size n, we then ﬁrst investigate the limiting spectral distribution of all estimated eigenvalues of the corresponding matrices of these three models and then apply the above criteria to determine the order. Also, we need to discuss the optimality of upper bounds of the eigenvalues. The simulations and real data analysis will be conducted to examine their performance in ﬁnite sample scenarios.

12303419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303419.value: With the technical advancement, the collected data often involve many variables, which consists of a high-dimensional vector. Reducing the dimensionality for further data analysis is often in demand. In this project, we investigate the order determination for large dimensional matrices when the sample size is proportional to the number of variables. The examples include spiked population models, spiked Fisher models, principal component analysis and canonical correlation analysis. Unlike the models with ﬁxed number of variables, the asymptotic properties of the matrices behave very diﬀerent and the order determination becomes diﬃcult. Thus, we will propose some new methods to determine the number of spikes, the number of principal components, the number of factors in approximate factor models or the number of pairs of canonical variable and give a systematic study to show when the orders can be consistently estimated and when cannot. Numerical studies will be conducted to examine the ﬁnite sample performance of the methods. This research project investigates an important but longstanding problem in order determination in several models, and expect the new methodology and theory developed in the course of the project will have a lasting impact in the relevant ﬁelds. 大维数矩阵的定阶及其应用 随着技术的进步，采集到的数据往往涉及众多变量，这些变量自身就是高维向量。为了进一步的数据分析，减少维度通常是必需的步骤。在这个项目中，我们研究当样本大小与变量数量成比例时，大维数矩阵的定阶问题。其应用包括脉冲总体模型、脉冲Fisher模型、主成分分析和典则相关分析。与变量数量固定的模型不同，大维数矩阵估计的渐近性质表现出很大的不同，定阶的问题变得更加困难。因此，我们将提出一些新的方法确定脉冲的个数、主成分的个数、逼近因子模型的因子个数或典则相关的对数，并进行系统研究去证明阶数的估计何时可以相合，何时无法相合。我们也做一些数值研究以检验所提的方法在有限样本下的性能。 这个研究项目针对在多个模型中的定阶的一个重要但长期存在的问题，并期待在研究的过程中发展的新的方法和理论有持久的影响。

12303919.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12303919.value: 基於代謝組學和脂質組學探討全氟烷酸的免疫代謝調控作用

12303919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12303919.value: Perfluoroalkyl acids (PFAAs) are extremely persistent chemicals that are widely distributed in the environment and general population, due to their high chemical stability and extensive use. In Hong Kong, PFAAs contaminations have been reported in various environmental matrices, food, and human blood samples, suggesting the exposure risks of Hong Kong population to PFAAs. Evidence from numerous epidemiological and laboratory studies indicates that exposure to PFAAs may induce immunosuppression effects, affecting both cell-mediated and humoral immunity. Up to date, the underlying immunotoxicity mechanisms of PFAAs are still not clearly understood. In recent years, accumulating evidence indicates that metabolic reprogramming governs the function of immune cells. PFAAs are known to activate peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs), which have important roles in the regulation of lipid metabolism, fatty acid storage, and glucose metabolism. The possible interference of PFAAs in immune cell metabolism deserves further investigation for a better understanding of PFAAs associated immunotoxicity. Metabolomics and lipidomics techniques are particularly valuable for elucidating modes of action by determining exposure-associated metabolic/lipidomic profiles. In this proposal, mass spectrometry - based metabolomic and lipidomic profiling will be performed for the first time to characterize the metabolic perturbation in human immune cells associated with PFAAs exposure. Five PFAAs with different carbon chain length and functional groups will be selected to explore the potential relationship between structures - immunometabolic perturbation effects. Both liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC/MS) and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC/MS) will be used to enable a broad coverage of metabolites. Statistical data analysis including principal components analysis (PCA), partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) and t-test will be applied to identify differential metabolites between control and exposure group. The metabolite set enrichment analysis and pathway analysis will be conducted to elucidate the disturbed metabolic pathways, and to facilitate the data interpretation. Moreover, the dysregulated metabolic pathways will be further validated and quantified using targeted profiling approach. The potential enzymatic targets associated with PFAAs exposure will be identified by determining the expression levels and activities of key enzymes involved in the perturbed metabolic pathways, using RT-PCR, western blotting assays and commercial kits, respectively. The successful completion of this project will shed new insights into the immunotoxicity related to PFAAs and lead to the discovery of potential enzyme targets for future management. 全氟烷基酸（PFAAs）是壹類持久性有機汙染物，由於其化學性質極其穩定以及應用廣泛，因此普遍存在於環境和人群中。在香港地區，各類環境介質、食品和人體血液樣本中皆存在PFAAs的汙染，給民眾帶來了潛在的健康風險。流行病學和動物實驗研究顯示，PFAAs具有免疫抑制作用。目前，關於PFAAs的免疫毒理機制仍然不是十分明確。近年來，越來越多的研究表明，代謝重編程可調控免疫細胞的功能。PFAAs是PPARs的受體，而PPARs對於脂質、脂肪酸以及葡萄糖等代謝通路的調節皆具有重要作用。因此探討PFAAs對免疫細胞代謝的幹擾對於更好地理解PFAAs的免疫毒性具有重要的作用。代謝組學和脂質組學技術可通過檢測汙染物暴露引起的代謝譜和脂質譜的變化，從而推測汙染物的作用模式。本項目將首次采用基於質譜的代謝組學和脂質組學技術，探討PFAAs暴露於免疫細胞後所引起的代謝紊亂特征。本項目將選取五種含不同碳鏈長度和官能團的PFAAs，用以考察結構和免疫代謝調控的關系。采用LC-MS和GC-MS進行質譜分析，采用PCA, PLS-DA, t-test等統計分析方法篩選與PFAAs暴露相關的差異代謝物，並進行代謝物通路富集分析。進壹步采用靶向代謝組學方法對受幹擾的代謝通路進行驗證，並采用RT-PCR、western blotting等方法對相關的代謝酶進行確證。本項目的順利完成將有助於理解PFAAs引起的免疫毒性機理，並為其毒性幹預提供潛在的靶標。

12500219.label: Project Title(Chinese)
12500219.value: 企業負債架構和貨幣政策的一般均衡模型

12500219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12500219.value: I propose to study the extent to which monetary policy should react to financial market variables (such as asset prices and debt compositions) in a general equilibrium macroeconomic model. The model embeds a microfounded heterogeneous-debt framework developed by Luk and Zheng (2017) in which firms finance their investment with secured or unsecured debt depending on their endogenously-evolving credit history. The central bank uses a simple, implementable monetary policy rule that reacts to inflation, the output gap and financial market variables. I propose to solve for the optimal monetary policy reaction parameters to these variables and explore their implications. The proposed work injects new life into the long-lasting debate about the relationships between monetary policy and financial markets. The results coming from this exercise may also provide theoretical underpinnings for “leaning against the wind”-type monetary policy. 本建議利用一般均衡模型研究貨金融市場變量(如資產價格、債務組成)應如何影響貨幣政策。本文將擴展Luk and Zheng (2017)的債務異質性模型，其中企業可視乎其信用紀錄，以有擔保債務或無擔保債務進行融資。中央銀行使用簡明而可執行的貨幣政策法則，因應通脹、產出缺口和金融市場變量進行調節。我將求解貨幣政策最優回饋參數，並詳加探討。 上述研究為一場由來以久關於金融市場變量和貨幣政策的辯論注入新動力。其結果有可能為「逆向干預」貨幣政策提供理論基礎。

12500519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
12500519.value: Workplace deviance refers to these behaviors that violate organizational norms and harm the organization or other members. To date, evidence has demonstrated that such deviant behaviors occur at alarming rates and cost organizations billions of dollars every year. Given its prevalence and costs, management researchers and practitioners are paying increasing attention to organizational deviance. This literature focuses primarily on the causes of individual employees’ deviant behaviors. Yet, it is a commonplace that members of work groups may collectively violate organizational norms and harm the interests of the organization in a collective, coordinated fashion. For example, groups may collectively cheat the organization on members' performance, attendance or leave records; or fight with other teams for company resources without considering the interests of the other teams and/or the company. Despite the prevalence of such a phenomenon and potentially destructive effects of such collective deviance behavior, we know little about its causes and consequences. We therefore examine such kind of organizational deviance that is conducted or endorsed by the whole group and for the immediate interest of whole group, which we label as group collective organizational deviance (GCOD). In our previous work, we developed a measure of GCOD which includes a subscale for GCOD toward the organization (e.g., using up the budget at the end of the financial year intentionally, for unnecessary things) and a subscale for GCOD toward other groups in the organization (e.g., competes against other teams on unit performance using ways that are against regulations) and found preliminary evidence for its construct validity. In this proposal, we aim to further validate this construct and develop and test a theoretical model that explains its antecedents and consequences. We theorize that inter-group competition, group cohesiveness and leader's moral development are the determinants of GCOD because these conditions shape a moral disengagement climate and a perceived group identity threat within groups. Further, our model suggests although GCOD may generates some "benefits" for the focal groups and its members, it hurts the organization's climate and performance in longer term. We propose to validate the construct and test the model using working teams in Chinese and American organizations. 職場的越軌行為是指那些偏離企業的規定、傷害企業及企業內的其他成員的行為。現有的研究發現表明這一類行為的出現頻率令人吃驚，每年給企業造成數以億計的經濟損失。因此，管理人員與學者們對此類行為的關注日漸提升。目前文獻當中的主要關注點在於發現導致員工個人做出此類行為的原因，但有一種並不鮮為人知的集體偏離行為卻沒有得到應有的關注 — 企業當中的各種工作團隊內部，大家一起用合作的方式，集體違反企業的規定、傷害企業利益。這樣的行為，例如，團隊成員集體虛報業績、考勤記錄，不顧企業利益與企業內的其他團隊爭奪資源等等，很可能非常普遍且害處極大，但現有管理學研究當中對其前因後果的研究卻非常有限。因此，我們在此項研究當中清晰定義這樣的團隊集體越軌行為（即：由工作團隊內部成員為團隊謀私利而集體做出的職場越軌行為），並探討它的產生原因及可能的後果。在提出此項研究計劃之前，我們的前期研究已經透過訪談和問卷研究方法發展出量表來測量團隊集體越軌行為，並且發現這種行為有兩大類：針對企業的以及針對企業內其他團隊的。此項研究計劃的目的在於繼續檢驗這個量表在幾個方面的效度，著重發展關於團隊集體越軌行為的產生機制及後果的理論模型。在模型當中，我們提出團隊之間的競爭程度、團隊內部的凝聚程度、以及團隊領導的道德發展水平是導致團隊集體越軌行為的主要因素，因為這些因素令團隊內部產生一種集體的道德疏離感以及對團隊認同感的威脅。進一步，我們提出這類集體行為可能在短期內讓團隊“收益”，但長期卻損害企業的氛圍和業績。我們計劃在中國和美國企業收集數據來檢驗我們提出的理論模型。

12500519.label: Realisation of objectives
12500519.value: We have achieved all the major project objectives except for objectives #2 and 3 which we have achieved 80% so far. Regarding Obj.#1, “To develop the conceptualization of group collective organizational deviance (GCOD),” our study of the literature continues to support the unique contribution of the GCOD construct we proposed in the proposal. We have added more recent literature evidence to further clarify its nature and differentiation from other existing constructs in the literature (e.g. Pro-group unethical behaviors and Collective corruption). Regarding Obj.#2, “To examine the construct validity of GCOD” we conducted over 90 interviews with MBA and EMBA students who are managers in various industries, companies, and positions to (a) examine the existence and prevalence of GCOD in organizations by asking managers to provide behavioral incidents consistent with our defintion; (b) collect managers’ ideas about its reasons and consequences; and (c) develop items to measure GCOD based on evidence from (a) and (b). Our qualitative analyses show the prevalence and significance of GCOD. Specifically, all respondents suggested the existence of group collective OD as we defined, except for 2 respondents who said they couldn’t think of any incidents. We received 264 statements of incidents at the end which were viewed as consistent with our definition during the interviews, indicating the relevance of prevalence of GCOD. Based on the incidents, we developed a scale for GCOD following the scale development procedures. We collected another MBA-sample survey for scale validation. Results support a two-dimension structure—GCOD toward the organization (GCOD-O) and toward other work groups (GCOD-G). Our main survey study reached 218 team leaders and 806 of their corresponding subordinates in multiple companies in China and measured the antecedents, mediators and GCOD in two time waves. Results continue to support the validity of the two-dimension structure. Regarding Obj.#3 and 4, “To develop a theoretical model of GCOD that includes its antecedents and outcomes” and “to empirically test the model” we used the main survey data and found that the interactions between authoritarian leadership and inter-team competition, as well as between group cohesiveness and moral awareness shape group moral disengagement, thereby impacting GCOD. This supports our model development based the social cognitive theory overall. The results are largely consistent with our proposed model except that we revised the proposed interaction between authoritarian leadership and group cohesiveness to an interaction between authoritarian leadership and inter-team competition because our further theorization based on the goal interdependence theory of cooperation and competition suggests the importance of inter-team competition as an external factor interacting with the leadership factor. Data supported the hypothesized interaction. The uncompleted part of objectives 2 and 3 is about the consequences of GCOD. In our proposal we suggested organizational performance and climate as well group performance and inter-group conflict as the DVs. Due to difficulties with the participating companies, unfortunately we couldn’t collect the outcome variables in the survey as we planned. We need to find additional data collection opportunities for test the consequences part. Because the survey has specific requirements on the work groups, asks sensitive questions (such as deviance behaviors, conflicts, and moral sensitivities etc.), and needs companies’ cooperation in providing performance data, it has been challenging for us to find the right sample which we are still actively working on.
