To analyse trans masculinity in an Asian context by collecting empirical data on the formation of trans masculinities in Bangkok and Hong Kong.
To develop a method on framing research inquiries outside of key knowledge production systems.
To investigate social, cultural and historical linkages between the formation of Chinese and Thai modernities.

13604919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
13604919.value: In recent years, there has been heightened visibility of transgender persons and communities in Asian societies. Yet little is known about the lived experiences of transgender persons other than empirical data on medical transitions and mental health. Research studies often tend to place more focus on transgender women. Trans men and trans masculine individuals remain largely invisible in academic literature. There are very few studies that address the social and cultural meanings of identifying as a transgender man. This study proposes to explore the socio-cultural construction of trans masculinity through a qualitative ethnography study of 40 trans men living in Bangkok (Thailand) and Hong Kong. A transgender person is defined as a person identifying in a gender other than the one that matches the sex that was assigned at birth. A trans masculine person is an individual who does not identify as a man, but rather as non-binary while engaging in gender expression that is towards the masculine end of the gender spectrum. A minimum of 20 participants will be recruited from each research site. Apart from interviews with trans men, 30 interviews will be conducted with community workers, therapists, surgeons and psychiatrists in both cities. A total of 70 interviews will be conducted. A digital ethnography of mobile applications commonly used for transgender self-representations and transition videos will also be conducted. The proposed study adopts a transnational approach to understanding inter-Asia cultural and media flows as well as processes on building concepts of trans masculinities and bodies. As queer tourism between Hong Kong and Thailand is commonplace, the selection of research sites point to an in-depth exploration of linked histories and processes of modernization in the Asia region. We aim to improve the understanding of transgender men’s lives in two Asian world cities and contribute to the academic literature on gender and sexualities, media and cultural studies, Asian studies. We intend to examine the daily issues facing transgender men from education to employment, housing to healthcare, coming out to families and friends, and finding partners. One of our goals is to find out how transgender men have been differently marginalized and stigmatized in both Chinese and Thai societies. The proposed project will: (1) fill a gap in the scholarship of masculinity studies; (2) enrich literature in transgender studies by adding a global south voice; and (3) examine the circulation of knowledge and cultural flows within Asia in regards to trans men. 近年來，跨性別者在亞洲社會能見度越來越高，然而生活經歷卻鮮為人知。在學術研究方面，多數關注跨性別女性，跨性別男性相對受到忽略。至於跨性別性身份認同的社會與文化意義亦甚少受到重視。 本研究旨在以民族誌研究取向，探究居住於香港與曼谷的跨性別男性氣概之社會文化建構。研究者將於上述二個城市至少各招募20名參與者。除了訪談跨性別男性，亦將針對二地之社群工作者、治療師、外科與心理醫生進行至少30次訪談。此外，亦將針對跨性別男性常使用之行動電話應用程式以及其所拍攝之變性手術影片進行數位民族誌調查。

13604919.label: Realisation of objectives
13604919.value: There are three distinct stages in completing this research project on transmen and transmasculine persons in Hong Kong and Bangkok, Thailand. Stage One (January 2020 – March 2021) of the project faced immense difficulties in collecting empirical data during the pandemic. The first progress report and response to the review panel outlined the challenges in engaging with transgender persons and communities, and the strategies to overcome obstacles. During Stage Two (April 2021 – September 2021), the project finally took off with research team in both sites actively engaged in ethnographic field activities. An international online conference, The 2021 East and Southeast Asia Trans Communities Forum Trans Healthcare Forum, was organized and held on July 22 & 23, 2021 with participation of 15 local and international speakers and 131 attendees (Objectives 1, 3 & 4). For Stage Three (October 2021 – December 2022) with the 6-month extension, I was finally able to travel to Southeast Asia to meet up with the Thai-based research team in person, to conduct a second round of in-depth interviews, to liase with local community groups in both Singapore and Thailand. By the end of this funding period, a total of 61 (Hong Kong: 30, Thailand: 31) in-depth interviews have been conducted, meeting and exceeding the original target of 60 interviews (Objective 2). I presented on this GRF-funded research in 4 conferences, submitted and published one book chapter and two journal articles, finished and was awarded two fellowship applications on furthering comparative research with transmen, transmasculine and non-binary persons in an inter-Asian context and Asia-Australia nexus (Objectives 3 & 4). In the following sections, I will explain how project objectives have been met with the completion of this research activities for this project. Fieldwork in Hong Kong and Thailand (Objectives 1 & 2) For the completion of this project, I conducted 30 face-to-face and online interviews in Hong Kong and 31 interviews in Thailand. As the primary interviewer for the fieldwork in Hong Kong, I met up with interview participants in person as much as I could for interviews. As mentioned in the first progress report, fieldwork activities were hindered by the pandemic. In Hong Kong, participants were finally willing to meet up with some participants mentioning the rolling out of the vaccine as helpful to facilitating safe zones for interviews to take place. All interviews were taped and recorded with consent. A small number of participants preferred online interviews based on reasons ranging from personal safety to busy schedules. Duration of interviews range from a minimum of 60 minutes to 120 minutes. A minimum of two rounds of interviews for each participant with some participants meeting up more regularly at community events and social gatherings. These semi-structured interviews often begin with opening narrative accounts on becoming transgender men, the early signs and self-awareness of being different, reactions from family members and peers, and navigating various ways for female-to-male gender transitions. Issues on legal recognition, discrimination, violence, stigmatization, access to appropriate healthcare and mental health support were reported by participants. Preliminary themes from the Hong Kong site data collection included authenticity within trans identity formations, sense of belonging, building communities of care, dis-alignments of life pathways, problematics of language, the pathological discourse of trans persons. Part-time research assistants were hired to provide research support for fieldwork separately in Hong Kong and Thailand. Two of the research team members are well-known transgender rights advocate and community leaders in each respective site. They both assisted in recruiting participants for the interviews and provided research support in compiling literature on transgender persons in Hong Kong and Thailand. Apart from interviewing transgender men of ethnic Chinese background, I have also reached out to transmen-identified Filipino migrant workers. I contacted Filguys Association of Hong Kong for potential referrals. Filguys is a support group for lesbian, bisexual and transmen migrant workers. The group’s founder identifies as a transman and has since returned to the Philippines. I interviewed him through Zoom. I have also conducted participant observation with selected interview participants. I actively approached participants to conduct observation in places where they worked and socialized. For example, I joined a transmen-owned gym on my own expense where transmen and transmasculine persons frequented and worked out on and off during the pandemic. The gym was a critical space for analysis as gender binaries were strictly enforced in locker rooms. I was able to observe how participants navigated this issue in their daily activities. In another case, I spent time at the construction site where one of the participants was a construction worker. I was able to observe and participate in social gatherings where the participant, unknown to his colleagues as a transgender man, had professional relationships and recreation ties to his colleagues. For fieldwork in Bangkok, Thailand, I was finally able to conduct face-to-face second round interviews and to meet up with the research team in person in November & December 2022. Two Thai-based research assistants were trained and hired for this project, to assist with data collection, fieldwork translation and transcription of interviews. Prior to our in-person meeting, the Thailand fieldwork team and I have regular online research meetings to discuss issues related to participant recruitment and interviews, translation of specific terms and transcription issues. The interview guide has been revised and finetuned for data collection in Thai context. Thai language use, in particular, was discussed at length during these meetings to ensure cultural competency for interview questions. Similar to the interviews in Hong Kong, all interviews were taped and recorded with consent. Methods of recruitment include snowball sampling and purposive sampling. Different from the Hong Kong cohort, opening narrative accounts often focus on rural-urban migration and childhood experiences. Issues on violence and discrimination were more prevalent in the Thailand cohort, in particular, domestic violence was mentioned by a few interview participants. Healthcare matters also came up as testosterone injections as part of hormone therapy for transgender men have just been included in the public healthcare system. Similar themes include lack of legal recognition, stigmatization, authenticity within trans identity formations and building communities. Apart from conducting interviews, the research team in Thailand has been in contact with service providers and transgender community-based organizations to further understand medical information and social support provided for transgender men. As information for transgender women is readily available, the research team had to make extra efforts in locating transmen-specific services with the assistance of interview participants. With the 6-month extension, I was finally able to travel to Bangkok for in-person data collection. This is crucial for my research as language translation is already necessary and barriers to meeting interview subjects and establishing community networks can be minimized. Through my fieldwork with the Hong Kong cohort, I was also able to provide information on a list of medical hospitals, private clinics and service brokers that have facilitated the process for many Hong Kong transmen to travel to Thailand for surgeries prior to COVID. A few names of the hospitals and clinics overlapped on both lists. But transmen currently living in Bangkok were able to access more information from community-based transgender healthcare organization, Tangerine Community Health Clinic.

13604919.label: Major findings and research outcome
13604919.value: By the writing of this report, one book chapter and two journal articles have been published. More information on publications can be found in Part C of this report. I presented research findings at 4 international conferences and symposium including the Inter-Asia Cultural Studies Society Conference 2021, Queer Cultures in Digital Asia, British Sociological Association Virtual Annual Conference 2022 and Rethinking Sociology Theory in Asia symposium. The Inter-Asia Cultural Studies Society Virtual Conference was held on 26-30 July 2021, jointly hosted by the Cultural Research Centre, National University of Singapore. For the conference, I presented a paper titled ‘Work, Employment and Queer Resilience among Trans / Transgender Men in Hong Kong’. This presentation uses the concept of queer resilience to counter the usual understanding of marginalized groups and individuals as always at-risk and only at-risk, by reframing the discussion to explore resilient strategies of change and social transformation adopted by transgender persons in making decisions on life pathways despite structural inequalities and hostile environments. I participated in an art exhibit of testosterone needles accompanied by a book publication titled Proof of Stake: Technological Claims, for the collaborative group exhibit Proof of Stake – Technological Claims (September - November 2021) with the Centre for Digital Cultures, Leuphana University Lüneburg, Museum am Rothenbaum, Kulturen und Künste der Welt and University of Fine Arts Hamburg. My book chapter ‘The T Needle’, examines the testosterone needle as an object in relation to technology and time for transmen. The Queer Cultures in Digital Asia symposium (10 December 2021) was hosted by the Chinese University of Hong Kong and organized in collaboration with Queensland University of Technology Digital Media Research Centre. I presented and published a paper titled ‘Queering Dystopian Insta-Emotions Among Hong Kong Trans Men’ for a special issue in the International Journal of Communication. For the Rethinking Sociology Theory in Asia workshop (31 March 2022), hosted by Baptist University and co-organized with Villanova University and Wellesley College. I presented a paper on Bridging Contexts: A Study on Transmen in Hong Kong and Thailand. This presentation uses an inter-Asia approach to study the movement of transmen bodies and the cultural translation of transgenderisms. For the British Sociological Association Annual Conference 2022: Building Equality and Justice Now (20 - 22 April 2022), I presented on tracing digital media by examining DIY videos on testosterone injections to daily transition vlogs curated by transgender men, transmasculine and non-binary individuals.

13604919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
13604919.value: In order to further develop this research, I applied for the Humanities and Social Sciences Prestigious Fellowship Scheme 2022/23 as a continuation of this completed RGC-GRF project. I proposed ethnographic research to focus on issues surrounding work, employment and unemployment partly due to the pandemic. Transgender men have different work experiences than transgender women. As gender plays a key part in the organization of work, transgender men often found themselves in a different gender schema once being socially recognized as a man. A transgender man enters the workplace with assumptions of male privilege in comparison to women in the general population, yet not all occupations carry the same male privileges and social recognition of maleness differ for each transgender man and for each job. More investigation is needed to understand the differences in treatment towards transgender men and men in general, as well as differences in treatment towards transgender men in Asian societies. Current scholarship on LGBT diversity and inclusion in the workplace only emphasize on business management, human resource practices within corporate organizations. Other aspects of work such as in job precarity and unemployment do not fall into this area of inquiry. I was successfully awarded the fellowship.

14100019.value: 對FGF-FGFR和Hippo-YAP1通路在胃癌發生中協同作用的研究

14100019.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14100019.value: Prof CHENG, Alfred Sze-Lok Prof To, Ka-fai

14100019.label: Project Objectives
14100019.value: to comprehensively delineate the expression pattern of FGFR family and highlight the activation of FGFR2 in GC; to perform in-depth investigation to elucidate how FGFR2’s amplification and upregulation plays oncogenic role through activing YAP1 oncoprotein; to classify the GC samples as FGFR2-c-Jun-YAP1 activation and inactivation subgroups and utilize small molecules for targeted intervention.

to perform in-depth investigation to elucidate how FGFR2’s amplification and upregulation plays oncogenic role through activing YAP1 oncoprotein;

14100019.label: Realisation of objectives
14100019.value: Under the supporting this GRF, we completed our research work on comprehensive elucidation of the oncogenic role of FGFR activation and in-depth characterization of FGFR2 mechanisms in gastric cancer (GC). We revealed that aberrant FGFR2 activation promotes gastric tumorigenesis through activation of the Hippo-YAP1 pathway. The interplay of the FGFR2-c-Jun-YAP1 cascade was confirmed by RNA-seq, ChIP-Seq, and functional assays. The primary GC samples were subgrouped based on FGFR2-c-Jun-YAP1 expression, and its clinical significance was achieved by correlation analysis and drug susceptibility test. In the first part, we comprehensively delineated the expression pattern of FGFR family and highlighted the activation of FGFR2 in GC. By the cBioportal analysis, TCGA dataset was used to demonstrate the genetic and epigenetic alterations of FGFRs in primary GC cases. 36% of the cases have at least one alteration in FGFR members, including copy number changes, somatic mutations, and mRNA upregulation. The copy number aberrations of FGFR2 were assessed by using FGFR2 probes for CISH analysis in 264 samples of our in-house Hong Kong cohort. 87% of cases were counted to be diploid, while 6% possessed copy number gain, and the rest 7% of cases harbored gene amplification. Overexpression of FGFR2 was correlated with poor survival and lymph node metastasis, implying that FGFR2 activation might contribute to GC metastasis. To further elucidate the functional role of FGFR2, siRNA-mediated knockdown was performed. With FGFR2 knockdown, AGS, MKN28, and MGC-803 cells showed significant inhibition of cell proliferation, monolayer colony formation ability, and cell invasion ability after siFGFR2 transfection. The apoptotic marker cleaved PARP was increased in siFGFR2 transfectants compared with siScramble control. Meanwhile, cell cycle-related proteins cyclin D1 and p-Rb were also inactivated, while p21 and p27 expression were induced due to FGFR2 knockdown. Collectively, the knockdown of FGFR2 triggered an anti-neoplastic effect by inducing apoptosis, inhibiting cell cycle progression, and enhancing the sensitivity to 5-FU. In the second part, we investigated in-depth mechanisms to elucidate how FGFR2’s amplification and upregulation play an oncogenic role by activating YAP1 oncoprotein. In rhFGF18-stimulated cells, Gene Ontology (GO) analysis indicated that the dysregulated genes were mainly enriched in biological processes, including serine/threonine kinase activity, protein phosphorylation, and GTPase activity. Among the top-ranking signaling pathways, we observed that multiple genes related to Hippo-YAP1 signaling were highly altered. YAP1, MYC, CTGF, and CCND1 were upregulated, while TP73 and AMOT were decreased after rhFGF18 stimulation. With FGFR2 depletion, YAP1, CTGF, c-Myc, and Bcl2 were no longer responding to the rhFGF18 stimulation in AGS, MKN28, and MGC-803 cells, indicating that the FGF18 activated YAP1 signaling is suppressed. Apart from the YAP1 translocation, rhFGF18 also altered the arrangement of the F-actin cytoskeleton. siFGFR2 transfection abolished YAP1 nuclear translocation and ameliorated the F-actin cytoskeleton to the naïve status even with rhFGF18 stimulation. To explore whether inhibition of FGFR2 affects the potential downstream YAP1 signaling in GC, AGS and MGC-803 were treated with a pan-FGFR inhibitor AZD4547, which is highly sensitive to FGFR2. Under treatment of AZD4547, the YAP1 downstream effectors, CTGF and c-Myc, were suppressed in a dose-dependent manner. Together, targeting FGFR2 by small molecules inhibited YAP1 expression, suppressed tumor growth, and enhanced apoptosis in GC. In the third part, we classified the GC samples as FGFR2-c-Jun-YAP1 activation and inactivation subgroups and utilized small molecules for targeted intervention. The FGFR2-c-Jun-YAP1 co-activation group was positively correlated with poor disease-specific survival. We further analyzed the differential power of the subgrouping in intestinal and diffuse subtypes, respectively. The co-positive group is significantly associated with an unfavorable outcome in whatever type of GC compared with other cases. To evaluate the effect of targeting the FGFR2-YAP1 axis, we employed small molecules targeting FGFR2 and YAP1 individually or in combination. In vivo synergistic effect was evaluated in xenograft formation models. Co-administration of MGC-803-derived xenografts with VP (Verteporfin, a YAP1 inhibitor) and AZD4547 exerted a synergetic effect on tumor growth inhibition. This demonstrates that co-targeting FGFR2 and its downstream effector YAP1 might serve as a potential therapeutic strategy in GC. In summary, we demonstrated the overexpression of FGFR2 in GC as well as its promoting role in gastric carcinogenesis. FGF18-FGFR2 axis promotes gastric progression by activating ERK-MAPK signaling. c-Jun is confirmed as a transcription factor of YAP1. As a potential downstream effector of FGF18-FGFR2, YAP1 transduces the oncogenic FGFR2 signaling to the downstreams. F-actin cytoskeleton remodeling, which serves as a mechanotransduction mechanism for YAP1 nuclear translocation, is also regulated by FGF18-FGFR2. Co-activation of the FGFR2-c-Jun-YAP1 is identified in a group of GC cases and predicts unfavorable clinical outcomes. A combination blockade of FGFR2 and YAP1 may benefit more GC patients undergoing targeted therapy This study uncovered the molecular mechanisms of FGFR2 activation in gastric carcinogenesis and took targeting strategies to disrupt the oncogenic cascade. Our findings will potentially identify novel prognostic biomarkers and develop precision intervention strategies based on the elucidated regulatory network.

14100019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100019.value: Our research focuses mainly on the FGFR2-YAP1 mediated signaling crosstalk in gastric carcinogenesis. We firstly profiled the FGFR alterations and analyzed their clinical associations in TCGA and Hong Kong gastric cancer (GC) cohorts. FGFR2 was abundantly expressed in GC cell lines and primary tumors and predicted poor survival and was associated with advanced stages of GC. With FGFR2 depletion, GC growth abilities and cell cycle progression were inhibited, while apoptosis was activated. Moreover, FGFR2 knockdown inactivated ERK-MAPK signal transduction and enhanced first-line anti-cancer drug sensitivity. RNA-seq analysis revealed that YAP1 signaling serves as a significant downstream to mediate the oncogenic roles of FGFR2. Nuclear accumulation of YAP1 was observed by rhFGF18 stimulation while inhibiting FGFR2 by AZD4547 led to cytoskeleton collapse and failure of YAP1 nuclear translocation. Additionally, FGF18-FGFR2 signaling upregulated YAP1 expression through activating a transcription factor c-Jun, which serves as an effector of MAPK signaling. According to immunohistochemistry, 28.94% of cases were FGFR2, c-Jun, and YAP1 co-positive, and these cases demonstrated worse clinical outcomes. Co-targeting FGFR2 and YAP1 by AZD4547 and Verteporfin synergistically enhanced the anti-tumor efficacies in vitro and in vivo. In summary, our work not only provides a comprehensive picture of FGFR2-Yap1 signaling network in gastric carcinogenesis, but also sheds light on the prognostic significance of the biomarkers and provides translational potential. The main findings were published on Oncogene (Zhang J et al, Oncogene, 2020). Apart from FGFR2-YAP1 axis, we also working on other GC-related research projects supported by this GRF grant. The Hippo-YAP1 pathway is always our research focus. We confirmed that AMOTL1 and IGF2-IGF1R promote YAP1 translocation into the nuclei to activate the downstream expression, such as CTGF (Zhou Y et al, Oncogene, 2020; Zhang J et al, Journal of Pathology, 2022). As the direct YAP1 downstream, MCM6 promotes gastric carcinogenesis by activating Akt and focal adhesion pathways (Wang Y et al, Theranostics, 2022). We also elucidated the oncogenic role of STK3, an upstream of Hippo-YAP1 pathway, in driving gastric carcinogenesis by activating Ras-MAPK pathway (Chen B et al, Molecular Cancer, 2021). For the Notch signaling pathway, we identified that NOTCH3 promotes gastric carcinogenesis by upregulating PHLDB2 expression and activating the Akt pathway (Kang W et al, Oncogene, 2021). Meanwhile, we encouraged the postgraduate students and postdoctoral fellows to draft Review Articles on GC topic, thus summarizing the related findings and directing our future work. Supported by this GRF, we published 8 high-level Review Articles in peer-reviewed journals such as BBA-Reviews on Cancer, Oncogene, International Journal of Cancer, International Journal of Molecular Sciences, and Biomedicines.

14100019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100019.value: Dysregulation of FGFR signaling has been found to contribute to gastric cancer (GC). Although a number of early-stage clinical trials implicate therapeutical effects for the genetic alteration of FGFR, the sensitivities of drugs such as AZD4547 are highly variable. The complexity of FGFR cascade in patients and intratumor heterogeneity are also the key barriers to overcome. This study confirmed that aberrant FGFR2 activation promotes gastric tumorigenesis through activation of Hippo-YAP1 pathway. We also developed a novel therapeutic strategy that improved the anti-neoplastic efficacies, namely co-targeting YAP1 and FGFR2 by VP and AZD4547, in FGFR2-driven GCs. Our findings not only broadened our understanding of the FGFR2 mechanisms but also led to the identification of multiple prognostic biomarkers for GC. As AZD4547 and monoclonal antibodies targeting FGFR2 meet the bottleneck constraint, we need to screen novel small molecules specifically targeting FGFR2 from the compound library in future studies. We plan to screen the most potent FGFR2 inhibitors from a library, including 4511 anti-cancer drugs. The combinational administration of candidate drugs and 5-FU in controlling GC peritoneal metastasis will also be performed. Meanwhile, we also plan to generate patient-derived xenograft (PDX) or primary GC-derived orthotopic transplantation (PDO) models for the drug tests.

14100019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100019.value: Gastric cancer (GC) is one of the most lethal malignancies globally. It remains a prevalent malignancy in Eastern Asia areas, including Hong Kong. Recently, the number of GC cases has been increasing among the younger population. GC is a heterogeneous disease with multiple pathogenic mechanisms such as aberrant crosstalk of signaling pathways, including the FGF-FGFR pathway. Targeting aberrant activation of FGF-FGFR represents a novel therapeutic strategy in GC. Specific antibodies or small molecules targeting the FGF-FGFR have been developed and are undergoing clinical trials. Nevertheless, FGFR-targeted treatments are still under evaluation in Phase I/II clinical trials. It is urgent to investigate the molecular mechanism of FGF-FGFR and develop novel therapeutic strategies. Using multiple bioinformatics analyses and functional validation, we confirmed that YAP1, the key component of the Hippo-YAP1 pathway, is a potential downstream effector regulated by FGF18-FGFR2 signaling. Co-activation of the FGFR2-c-Jun-YAP1 signaling cascade was identified in a subgroup of GC patients with worse survival. Co-targeting YAP1 and FGFR2 by VP and AZD4547 significantly improved the anti-neoplastic efficacies in animal models. We hope the combinational targeting may convey a novel therapeutic strategy for GC patients in this personalized medicine era.

14100419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100419.value: Cancers of the head and neck frequently invade vital structures precluding surgical excision and so radiotherapy (RT) and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) are often the first-line of treatment. However, head and neck cancers may be resistant to standard treatment regimes. Modifications to RT/CRT regimes, the addition of new cancer target agents, or change of management to a surgical approach can improve the outcome of patients with these resistant cancers. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) using anatomical MRI sequences is one of the main clinical tools for planning treatment but anatomical sequences have limitations in predicting treatment response. The addition of new functional MRI sequences to the MRI examination protocol has improved the ability of MRI to identify resistant cancers and predict treatment response, but limitations exist even for the most advanced functional sequences such as diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). Quantitative T1rho imaging is a new non-invasive functional MRI technique that has great potential for evaluating the cancer microenvironment. Our team is pioneers in T1rho imaging which until now has been used mainly in research of non-cancerous conditions in the musculoskeletal system, brain and liver. T1rho imaging has the capability of detecting macromolecules within cancers, as well as water molecules, so providing complementary information to DWI. Our team has incorporated recent advances in T1rho technology into a head and neck MRI protocol and we plan to perform one of the first T1rho studies in head and neck cancer. In this proposal, we will evaluate T1rho imaging is nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) which is the most common head and neck cancer in Hong Kong. In this observational study we plan to document the T1rho measurements of NPC prior to treatment and correlate with clinical and biological endpoints; determine whether treatment induces detectable changes in T1rho imaging early (2weeks) after the start of CRT; determine whether the pre-treatment and early intra-treatment T1rho measurements have the capability of predicting short-term outcome and providing complementary data to DWI for use in multiparametric imaging. 頭頸部的惡性腫瘤的生長常常會侵犯一些至關重要的周圍組織結構以致于外科手術切除難以進行。所以針對頭頸惡性腫瘤的治療，首選常為放射治療（放療）和放射聯合化學治療（放化療）。然而，頭頸惡性腫瘤可能會對標準的放化療產生耐性。針對這些產生耐性的頭頸惡性腫瘤，如果能盡早更改治療方案，如使用放療/放化療聯合新的腫瘤靶向治療藥物或聯合手術外科治療，可以提高患者的預後。磁力共振中的常規結構成像序列是臨床工作中常用于制定治療計劃的主要工具，然而常規結構成像序列在預估治療效果的作用有限。新出現的功能成像序列提高了磁力共振在評斷耐性腫瘤以及預估治療效果的能力，然而這些包括了擴散加權成像在內的新的功能成像序列都會存在有它們的局限性。 定量T1rho成像是一種新的非侵入性功能性磁力共振技術，具有評估癌症微環境的巨大潛力。 我們的團隊是T1rho成像的先驅。迄今為止，T1rho成像已經用於研究肌肉骨骼系統，腦和肝臟中的非癌症狀況。T1rho成像具有檢測癌症中的大分子以及水分子的能力，因此向擴散加權成像提供輔助信息。 我們的團隊將T1rho成像的最新進展納入該頭頸部磁力共振研究提案。我們計劃進行T1rho成像在頭頸部癌症的首次研究。 在這項提案中，我們的目的是評估T1rho成像在香港最常見的頭頸腫瘤鼻咽癌的應用。在這項觀察性研究中，我們計劃在治療前，治療中記錄鼻咽癌的T1rho狀態并與腫瘤分期和短期預後相關聯，以達到以下的具體研究目的：（1）確定T1rho中的變化是否能夠檢測治療過程中的早期變化; （2）確定T1rho是否可以區分癌症和良性治療後的變化; 以及（3）確定T1rho是否可以向擴散加權成像提供補充數據以用於多參數成像。

14100419.label: Realisation of objectives
14100419.value: Objective 1. To document the T1rho measurements of nasopharyngeal carcinoma prior to treatment and correlate with T and N stage and biological processes. 1) Patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma without distant metastases were recruited according to the planned protocol and sample size. The objective was achieved. In all 50 patients (male = 34, female = 16, median age = 47 years) the pre-treatment T1rho measurements could be documented (mean value: 66.9 msec, range: 49.9 – 79.1 msec). Analysis with staging showed no correlation between mean T1rho and the T categories (T1, T2, T3 and T4 in 11, 8, 27, and 4, respectively) (p = 0.44) or N categories (N0, N1, N2, and N3 categories in 7, 19, 13, and 11, respectively) (p = 0.46). Nasopharyngeal biopsy samples obtained in all patients were analysed against biological processes using immunohistochemical biomarkers; tumour cells positive for programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1), hypoxia inducible factor- 1-alpha (HIF-1a), Ki67, CD3+, CD4+, and CD8+ tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) in the intratumoural compartment. A significant positive correlation was found between the pre-treatment mean T1rho and Ki67 (correlation coefficient = 0.302, p = 0.03) but not with the other immunohistochemical biomarkers (p = 0.13 -0.69). 2) We performed two additional analyses. In the first analysis pre-treatment plasma Epstein-Barr virus DNA (EBV DNA) was correlated with T1rho values in 44/50 patients. No correlation between EBV-DNA level with the mean T1rho was found (p = 0.57). In the second analysis we expanded our research into the underlying biological processes that may contribute to T1rho values. From research into the musculoskeletal system, it has been shown that T1rho values are influenced by collagen in the extracellular matrix. Collagen is a prominent structural protein associated with increased stromal content in cancers and high stromal content is linked to poor treatment outcome in NPC. We correlated T1rho with ratios for tumour-stroma, tumour-collagenous stroma, and collagenous stroma-lymphoid stroma. The mean T1rho values correlated with collagenous stroma-lymphoid stroma (R = -0.408, p<0.01). Objective 2. To determine whether changes in T1rho can be detected early in a course of CRT. 1) All patients recruited under objective 1 were scheduled for early intra-treatment T1rho imaging. The early intra-treatment scan was not performed in 13 patients. In normal circumstances it is expected that some patients will default on their intra-treatment scan appointment while undergoing chemotherapy, but this part of the study was especially challenging during the COVID pandemic. However, the number of patients who did undergo the early intra-treatment scan was sufficient for the analysis. Our objective was achieved. A change in the T1rho values between the pre-treatment and early intra-treatment scan was detectable in all patients. A mixed response was observed with 13/37 (35.1%) showing an increase (median: 5.3%, range: 0.1% to 5.3%) and 24/37 (64.9%) showing a decrease in mean T1rho (median: 7.9%, range: 0.2% to 19.8%). Objective 3. To determine whether T1rho measurements before and early in the course of CRT can predict short-term treatment response and provide data that is complementary to DWI. 1) The mean T1rho values and mean ADC values from DWI (a) pre-treatment, (b) early intra-treatment and (c) early intra-treatment % change were correlated with short-term response in 37 patients who underwent the planned biopsy 6 - 8 weeks after the completion of CRT, of whom 6/37 (16.2%) patients had residual cancer and 31/37 (83.8%) patients no residual cancer. Neither pre-treatment T1rho or ADC values (p = 0.95 and 0.53, respectively), or early intra-treatment T1rho values, absolute value or % change, (p = 0.92 and 0.41, respectively) predicted residual cancer after CRT. However, early intra-treatment ΔADC% and absolute ADC were associated with short-term response after treatment with those cancers without residual disease showing significantly higher intraADC and rise in ΔADC% compared to cancers with residual disease (p = 0.04 and 0.03, respectively). The ΔADC% threshold of 17.8% (lower increase in the intra-treatment scan) predicted residual cancer with a sensitivity of 83.3%, specificity of 74.2% and accuracy of 75.7%. 2) In addition to the planned objective, an additional analysis was performed in a subgroup of 25/50 patients (male = 17, female = 8, median age = 63 years, range of age = 34 – 74 years) who underwent induction chemotherapy before CRT. Patients were divided into responders 15/25 (60.0%) and non-responders 10/25 (40.0%) using RECIST criteria obtained from change in size on an MRI examination after the end of the course of induction chemotherapy. Early intra-treatment Δ T1rho% was associated with shrinkage in tumour size after induction chemotherapy; responders showing significantly lower rise in ΔT1rho% (i.e. lower percentage increase or a fall in the intra-treatment T1rho value) compared to non-responders (-7.3% vs 2.7%, p = 0.03). The Δ T1rho% threshold of  -3.9% (greater decrease in the intra-treatment scan) predicted responders with a sensitivity of 80.0%, specificity of 80.0% and accuracy of 80.0%.

14100419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100419.value: 1) Functional MRI techniques can be challenging in the head and neck because of the many artifacts associated with this region. However, this study has shown that T1rho imaging is a robust functional imaging technique that can be successfully applied to the head and neck to obtain images and quantify T1rho values (objective 1). 2) Nasopharyngeal cancers show a range of mean T1rho values (objective 1). 3) T1rho imaging is a new functional MRI technique in cancer imaging and the underlying biological processes responsible for the images are poorly understood. This study is the first in cancer imaging to show a positive correlation between the mean T1rho and Ki67, which is a marker of tumour proliferation. In a further development we expanded our research to include an analysis of the stroma which showed a further correlation with the ratio of collagenous stroma to lymphoid stroma. Both these biological processes are predictors of outcome, supporting the potential role of T1rho imaging in cancer imaging (objective 1). 4) Changes in T1rho values were detected early intra-treatment in all patients and unlike the ADC in DWI, which increased, T1rho showed a mixed response with both increasing and decreasing values (objective 2). 5) T1rho shows promise in the prediction of treatment response in head and neck cancer and is complementary to DWI. Early intra-treatment Δ T1rho% correlated with shrinkage in tumour size after induction chemotherapy. On the other hand, early intra-treatment ΔADC% and absolute ADC correlated with short-term response after completion of CRT (objective 3). The threshold rise in ADC to predict treatment outcome is consistent with our previous research in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. These results have the potential to adapt chemotherapy regimens and guide the post-treatment surveillance. 6) Pre-treatment T1rho or ADC values were not predictive of either response to induction chemotherapy or presence of residual cancer after CRT (objective 3) and no correlation was found between T1rho values and the T or N categories for cancer staging (objective 1)

14100419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100419.value: 1. We have already completed additional analyses to correlate T1rho values with plasma EBV DNA levels and correlate T1rho values with additional biological processes related to the cancer stroma. We have also performed a subgroup analysis to predict tumour shrinkage after induction chemotherapy using T1ho and DWI. 2. Performance of pre-treatment T1rho imaging in predicting long-term treatment response in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The results from this initial study showed no association between pre-treatment T1rho and short-term outcome at 6-8 weeks after treatment. However, short-term outcome may not predict long-term outcome as this time point does not consider later recurrence at the primary site or recurrence at other sites including the development of distant metastases. We have increased the recruitment of patients with nasopharyngeal for pre-treatment T1rho to evaluate with survival endpoints. We have recruited 117 patients and will perform the analysis in the near future.

14100419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100419.value: T1rho imaging is a new functional MRI sequence for cancer imaging. This is one of the first cancer T1rho studies in the body and the first in head and neck cancer. T1rho imaging was performed successfully in the head and neck, a challenging anatomical region for functional MRI. T1rho values of nasopharyngeal carcinoma correlated with tumour cell Ki67, a marker of tumour proliferation, and with the collagenous content of the matrix that surrounds cancer cells, both of which influence cancer treatment response. Changes in T1rho were detectable two weeks after starting treatment and predicted tumour shrinkage by the end of a course of induction chemotherapy but did not predict residual cancer after the end of full treatment. T1rho imaging was complementary to the more established technique of diffusion weighted imaging. Unlike T1rho, early intra-treatment changes in ADC did not predict shrinkage of tumour with induction chemotherapy but did predict residual cancer after the full course of treatment. The threshold rise in ADC of 17.8% to predict residual cancer is consistent with our previous research in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. These results have the potential to adapt chemotherapy regimens and guide the post treatment surveillance.

14100619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14100619.value: 內皮依賴性收縮（EDC）在維持和調節血管張力和血壓方面起著重要作用。在高血壓，糖尿病和高脂血症等疾病狀況下，EDC會增加. EDC的增強會引起內皮功能障礙並加重高血壓等血管疾病. EDC的早期信號包括內皮細胞內Ca2 +上升，收縮性前列腺素產生，最後導致血管收縮。然而，目前科學界關於內皮Ca2 +通道知之甚少。我們在初步研究中發現，內皮細胞中的一種Ca2 +通道TRPC5在此有重要的作用。內皮TRPC5通道能刺激健康小鼠的頸動脈中的COX-2活性，從而促進EDC。在本項目中，我們計劃將我們的研究擴展到高血壓的小鼠模型。我們的假說是高血壓會增加TRPC5表達，從而增加EDC反應，這可能進一步加重內皮功能障礙。此外，另一種Ca2 +通道TRPV4也會介入EDC。因此，在此計劃中我們會進一步估算TRPC5與TRPV4在介導EDC中的相對貢獻。此外，我們將鑑定TRPC5 / TRPV4敲除是否可以緩解高血壓誘導的內皮功能障礙。這些研究可以填補高血壓疾病中關於Ca2 +通道-EDC作用的重要知識空白，並可用於探討能否利用TRPC5 / TRPV4作為治療高血壓的靶點

14100619.label: Realisation of objectives
14100619.value: 1. Objective #1 was to determine the functional role of TRPC5 in mediating EDC in a hypertensive model of mice. In this aspect, we have successfully established two hypertension models of mice, namely L-NNA-induced model and AngII-induced model. We have shown that TRPC5 gene knockout or pharmacological inhibition of TRPC5 reduced the EDC in these hypertensive mice. 2. Objective #2 was to identify key signaling molecules downstream of TRPC5, such as COX isoforms and prostanoid types, in the EDC in the hypertensive model of mice. In this regard, we found that the immediate signaling molecule downstream of TRPC5 is COX-2 but not COX-1. The signaling molecules downstream of COX-2 include PGF2a, PGD2 and PGE2. 3. Objective #3 was to determine relative importance of TRPC5 vs. TRPV4 in EDC in the hypertensive model of mice. For this objective, we found that TRPC5 and TRPV4 each contributes to ~25% of EDC. In addition, we found a novel Ca2+-permeable channel Orai1 which also contributes to EDC in hypertensive mice. Orai1 accounts for ~40% of EDC in hypertensive mice. Combined inhibition of all three ion channels reduced the EDC by ~80%. Therefore, this objective is over-achieved. However, because of the identification of this novel channel Orai1 in EDC, we spent a lot of time to resolve the contribution of Orai1 in EDC and explored underlying mechanism. Therefore, the timeline for manuscript drafting and publications is delayed. The manuscript has been reviewed Acta Pharmacologica Sinica (impact factor 8.2) and is currently under "minor revision". We are currently performed some revision experiments. We expect the manuscript to be published soon. 4. The objective #4 was to determine whether gene knockout of TRPC5 and TRPV4, or pharmacological inhibition of TRPC5 and TRPV4, can alleviate hypertension-induced endothelial dysfunction. In this aspect, we have found that TRPC5 knockout improved the ACH-induced vascular relaxation in 12 month aging hypertensive mice. On the other hand, our collaborator's findings indicates that TRPV4 knockout did not improve the ACH-induced vascular relaxation in hypertensive mice.

14100619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100619.value: 1. We have successfully established two hypertension models of mice, namely L-NNA-induced model and AngII-induced model. With the use of these hypertensive models, we have shown that TRPC5 gene knockout or pharmacological inhibition of TRPC5 reduced the EDC. In addition, we also demonstrated that TRPV4 inhibition reduced the EDC. More importantly, we identified a novel Ca2+-permeable channel Orai1 which also contributes to EDC in hypertensive mice. Furthermore, we estimated relative contribution of these three Ca2+-permeable ion channels (TRPC5, TRPV4 and Orai1) in EDC. The signaling pathways downstream of Ca2+- have also been resolved. These results are packaged together in a major and lengthy manuscript (Li X, Lei Z, et al., Endothelial cell Orai1 is essential in endothelium-dependent contraction in mouse carotid arteries in normotensive and hypertensive mice). The manuscript is currently under minor revision in Acta Pharmacologica Sinica (impact factor 8.2) and is expected to be published soon. We also investigated the role of TRPC5 in cell death. The results are published in Guo J et al., Cells, 2020;9:547. 2. As stated, Orai1 is important in EDC as stated in point 1. Thus we also studied and found an important role of Orai1 in cardiac hypertrophy and hypertension in hypertensive mice. The mechanism involves Orai1 regulation on autophagy. The results are published in Zheng C et al., Frontiers in Pharmacology 2021;12:622774. 3. We have found an important role of another Ca2+-permeable channel TRPM2 in vascular smooth muscle dysfunction/death as well as in atherosclerotic lesion formation. These are closely related to vascular diseases similar to EDC. The results are published in Zhao Q et al., Scientific Reports 2020;10(1):20719, and Zhang Y et al., Cells 2022;11(9),1423. The role of TRPML2 in inflammation is studied and published in Yu H et al., Br J Cancer. 2021;125:1420-31. 4. We also studied the role of another Ca2+ regulatory protein TM9SF4 proteins in inflammation (Xie M et al., Cell Mol Gastroenterol Hepatol 2022;14(2):245-270), cell differentiation (Yu L et al., Stem Cell Res Ther. 2021;12:573) and cell migration (Meng Z et al., Nature Commun 2022;13(1):5728).

14100619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100619.value: Through this study, we have established critical roles of TRPC5, TRPV4 and Orai1 in EDC in mouse hypertensive models, and elucidated the downstream signaling pathways. These results provide a general scheme for EDC control by different Ca2+-permeable channels. In future, we will develop the strategies of targeting these Ca2+-permeable channels as a mean of alleviating EDC and partially restoring endothelial dysfunction.

14100619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100619.value: Endothelium-dependent contraction EDC contributes to endothelial dysfunction and exacerbated the progression of hypertension. The intracellular calcium concentration ([Ca2+]i) rise in endothelial cells is essential for EDC. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying endothelial Ca2+ entry channels that contribute to EDC are not well studied. In this study, we have established critical roles of TRPC5 and TRPV4 in EDC in mouse hypertensive models. More importantly, we identified a novel Ca2+-permeable channel Orai1 which also contributes to EDC in hypertensive mice. Furthermore, we estimated relative contribution of these three Ca2+-permeable ion channels (TRPC5, TRPV4 and Orai1) in EDC. The signaling pathways downstream of Ca2+- have also been resolved. Taken together, these results provide a general scheme for EDC control by different Ca2+-permeable channels. Targeting these Ca2+-permeable channels could be a novel strategy for alleviating EDC and restoring endothelial dysfunction. In addition, we have also found important roles of Ca2+-permeable channels Orai1 and TRPM2 in cardiac hypertrophy, vascular cell death and atherosclerosis. These data provide blueprint for novel treatment strategies against cardiovascular diseases.

14100919.value: 倍半萜類幼年激素（JH）是調節昆蟲發育和繁殖過程的主要激素。在非昆蟲節肢動物中，甲基法呢醇（MF）是主要的倍半萜類激素，在甲殼類動物（蝦，蟹，龍蝦）中起作用。在其他節肢動物中使用哪種倍半萜類化合物，例如多足動物（蜈蚣和千足蟲），鮮為人知。由於節肢動物佔世界上80％以上的動物，因此了解它們的生物學對基礎科學和實用價值都至關重要。 昆蟲和甲殼類動物中JH和MF的各自合成是在幼年激素甲基轉移酶（JHAMT）催化的最後生物合成步驟。到目前為止，我們的團隊幾年前只提供了一個已發表的千足蟲基因組。在這個項目中，我們建議定義和測試哪種倍半萜類激素在蜈蚣和千足蟲中都有功能。 該項目將為未被研究的多足類動物中的倍半萜類激素提供有價值的新見解。此外，激素操縱一直是節肢動物控制的主要目標，該項目還將為通過操縱土壤生物多樣性或防治農業害蟲來增強農業生產的未來發展提供新的基線信息。

14100919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14100919.value: Major findings - The Myriapoda, composed of millipedes and centipedes, is a fascinating but poorly understood branch of life, including species with a highly unusual body plan and a range of unique adaptations to their environment. In the PLOS Biology paper published in 2020, following our original plan in Aim 1, we provided the first two chromosomal-level genomes of the millipedes in the world for the first time. Collectively, our analyses of millipede genomes reveal that a series of unique adaptations have occurred in this major lineage of arthropod diversity, and shed new light on the conserved and lineage-specific features of millipedes and centipedes. It also sets up the backbone for further studies as planned for Aims 2 to 4. - Arthropod molting, metamorphosis, and reproduction are precisely controlled by hormones including sesquiterpenoids for post-embryonic growth and differentiation. However, their situations are poorly known in myriapods. In the following Nature Communications paper published in 2022, we obtained more centipede and millipede genomes as set in Aim 1, as well as investigated the sesquiterpenoid questions as set in Aims 2 to 4. As background information, the sesquiterpenoids farnesoic acid (FA), methyl farnesoate (MF), and juvenile hormone (JH) are produced through the conserved mevalonate (MVA) pathway in animals. Using a combination of in silico, in vitro, and in vivo analyses, we have shown that different types of myriapods use different sesquiterpenoids. - In addition to the original aims, we have also tested the established hypothesis and findings by looking into the molluscs, and sequenced the oyster genome in the BMC Genomics paper using other funding. In the Gigascience paper, by comparison of different mollusc genomes, we have found that different molluscs indeed also contain and produce different sesquiterpenoids similar to our findings in myriapods, which test and further expand the hypothesis, scope, and significance of this study. Research Outcome: - 6 publications including 2 high-quality research papers, 2 review papers, and 2 related research papers - 2 postgraduate students trained (1 PhD, 1 MPhil) - Staff trained in this project become P.I. and starts her own laboratory after this project - 2 undergraduates trained - Make presentations at international conferences - Make collaborations - Local community engagement and results also reported in media/press

14100919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14100919.value: We are very grateful to the generosity, trust and continous support of the RGC such that we can achieve what we propose. There could be multiple lines (on both basic and applied science) that can be further built on this project, including: Basic science: 1) investigation of sesquiterpenoid and other hormonal controls in myriapods; and 2) broader aspect in myriapod and arthropod evolution. Applied science: 3) enhancing agricultural production by way of either manipulation of soil biodiversity or combating agricultural pests.

14100919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14100919.value: Sesquiterpenoids juvenile hormones (JH) are major hormones that regulate the developmental and reproductive processes in insects. In non-insect arthropods, methyl farnesoate (MF) is the major sesquiterpenoid hormone that functions in crustaceans (shrimp, crab, lobster). Which sesquiterpenoid compound is utilised in the other arthropods, such as myriapods (centipede and millipede) is poorly known. As arthropods comprise of >80% of animals in the world, understanding their biology is of fundamental importance to both basic science and of practical values. The fundamental issue here was due to the paucity of experimental data available for sesquiterpenoid hormones in myriapods, whereas researchers always infer their situations from insects or crustaceans. In this project, we have defined and tested which sesquiterpenoid hormone (MF and farnesoic acid FA) is functional in both centipedes and millipedes. This project provides valuable new insights into sesquiterpenoid hormones in the understudied myriapods. In addition, hormonal manipulation has always been a major target for arthropod control, and this project also provides novel baseline information for future development in enhancing agricultural production by way of either manipulation of soil biodiversity or combating agricultural pests.

14101019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101019.value: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is the most common form of muscular dystrophy. DM1 is caused by a CTG repeat expansion in the 3’UTR of the human DMPK gene. Ribonuclear foci containing the CUG RNA repeats are formed in the nuclei, which sequesters splicing factors, such as mbl/MBNL1, causing impairment of the splicing machinery. While DM1 is generally recognized as a muscular dystrophy, DM1 is a multisystemic disease that harbours neuropathology. Unlike the muscle pathology of DM1, the neuropathological aspect of DM1 is relatively less explored. Here, we established a novel Drosophila DM1 model using the larval neuromuscular junction (NMJ). Remarkably, we observed synapse loss only when CUG repeats were expressed in both presynaptic motor neurons and postsynaptic muscles. Larvae expressing the CUG repeats had a lower density of active zones in their motor neurons, formed ribonuclear foci in the nuclei of motor neurons and muscles, and exhibited locomotor defects. Previous studies in Drosophila had demonstrated that splicing defects can result in dysregulation of isoforms of the adhersion molecule FasII (NCAM in mammals). Thus, we investigated isoform changes of FasII at the NMJ, and found that one of the isoforms of FasII, namely FasII-C, was significantly upregulated. We hypothesized that this upregulated might be the cause of neuropathologcal symptoms in our DM1 model, and found that overexpression of FasII-C was indeed sufficient to induce similar neuropathology. Furthermore, knockdown of FasII-C was able to rescue synapse loss. Moreover, mbl mutants exhibit similar neuropathological phenotypes as well, indicating that sequestration of mbl might be a cause of the upregulation of FasII-C. In Aim 1, we seek to complete our characterization of our Drosophila DM1 model of neuropathology using immunohistochemistry and live-imaging techniques, as well as to determine whether the severity of synapse loss has a CUG repeat length dependency. In Aim 2, we aim to uncover the underlying mechanism of neuropathology in this DM1 model, by manipulating FasII-C and mbl in motor neurons or muscles alone. Also to attempt rescuing the synapse loss by restoring intracellular signaling of FasII molecules by overexpressing FasII-A-PEST+ together with the CUG repeats. In Aim 3, we will determine if neuropathology in DM1 would accelerate muscle degeneration. In Aim 4, we will extend our study to mammals by investigating DMSXL mice tissues. This project will provide us with mechanistic insights on the neuropathology of DM1, and identify important molecules and pathways that contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease. N/A

14101119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101119.value: Aim The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of key type 2 cytokines, specifically interleukin-4 (IL-4) and interleukin-13 (IL-13), on neonatal heart regeneration. Background In 2017, the World Health Organization placed cardiovascular disease as the number one cause of deaths worldwide. Of the different conditions, high mortality amongst patients with myocardial infarction is due to the inability of adult cardiomyocytes to contribute to normal function after injury. However, recent studies have revealed that neonatal cardiomyocytes demonstrate a proliferative capacity and participate in regeneration in contrast to their adult counterparts. This is paralleled by a different immunological profile following injury. Importantly, neonatal immunity favors a broad type-2 T helper cell (Th2)-mediated response partially due to needs such as maintaining feto-maternal tolerance. Therefore, the Th2 response in neonates dictates a shortened pro-inflammatory response, and leaning towards an anti-inflammatory, pro-regenerative programs. Whilst neonatal immunity has been previously examined through a need to understand vaccine responses, how neonatal Th2 preference affects cardiac regeneration and cardiomyocyte biology is largely unknown. Therefore, this study aims to dissect the mechanisms by which the major drivers of Th2 immunity, specifically the type 2 signals: IL-4 and IL-13, contribute to neonatal heart regeneration following injury. Project Description We propose to initiate a series of experiments to address the following objectives: i) To Investigate the role of IL-4 and IL-13 in regulating neonatal immune populations during neonatal cardiac regeneration, and ii) To examine the molecular mechanisms IL-4 and IL-13 signaling utilizes in promoting successful regeneration of the heart. Significance of Project Existing interventional therapies to treat adult myocardial infarction (MI) serve to improve survival while there is no method to restore the functionality of damaged cardiac tissue. There is thus a pressing need to develop more effective treatment options. This is of utmost importance due to society's growing population of aging adults who are particularly vulnerable to ischemic heart diseases. Our proposed study examining the effects and mechanisms of Th2 immunity to enhance neonatal cardiac regeneration could be utilized to develop integrated therapies that might facilitate positive remodeling of the adult heart, by mimicking the neonatal heart recovery response and thus used to improve clinical outcomes. 研究目的：本研究旨在探討關鍵的Ⅱ型細胞因子白細胞介素-4（IL-4）和白細胞介素-13（IL-13）對新生兒心臟再生的影響。 研究背景：世界衛生組織2017年發佈的衛生統計報告表明，心血管疾病是全球範圍內造成死亡的首要原因。在各種心肌損傷的情況下，心肌梗死患者往往死亡率較高，這歸因於成人心臟在損傷後不能自發地修復其受損心肌。而近期研究表明，與成人相比，新生兒的心肌細胞表現出了較強的增殖能力，從而在心臟再生的過程中發揮著重要作用。而這種修復模式恰與人體損傷應激的免疫表達特徵相對應。更重要的是，出於維持母胎耐受的需要，新生兒體內的免疫應答是由Ⅱ型輔助性T（Th2）細胞主導的抗炎反應，因而縮短了炎症反應的時間，進而促進恢復周圍組織的再生作用。雖然前期出於對疫苗反應進行評估的需要，人們已對新生兒的免疫展開了一些研究，但是新生兒體內主導的Th2型免疫反應如何影響心臟再生及與其相關的心肌細胞生物學在很大程度上還是未知的。因此，本研究旨在剖析新生兒體內激發Th2免疫應答的主要驅動因素，尤其是Ⅱ型細胞因子IL-4和IL-13對新生兒受損心肌再生功能的影響。 研究內容：本項目擬開展系列實驗以實現以下目標：i）研究IL-4和IL-13在新生兒心臟再生過程中對其免疫細胞群分布的調節作用；ii）檢測IL- 4和IL-13促進心臟再生的分子信號傳導機制。 研究意義：現代社會中越來越多的老年人容易患上缺血性心臟病，而現有的介入療法雖有助於改善心肌梗死患者的心肌功能，提高其生存率，但卻無法恢復受損心臟組織的功能，因此開發更有效的臨床治療方案是迫切而又至關重要的。基於以上，本項目探討Th2型免疫應答對提高新生兒心臟再生的影響及其作用機制，通過模擬新生兒的心臟恢復反應，可應用於開發促進成人心臟重塑的綜合療法，以期改善臨床結果。

14101119.label: Realisation of objectives
14101119.value: In Objective 1, our aims were to investigate how IL-4 and IL-13 modulated neonatal immune populations in the cardiac niche during tissue regeneration. Specifically, our aims were to: 1) characterize the reparative effects of IL-4 and IL-13 by examining immune populations after treatment of either IL-4 or IL-13 cytokine in mice lacking both IL-4 and IL-13 (DKO) after cardiac ischemic injury in the neonate, and 2) to determine the effects of IL-4 and IL-13 on specific immune cell populations such as macrophages in the heart after injury by utilizing an IL-4Rα myeloid specific knockout neonatal mouse. In both cases, we were able to successful determine the temporal kinetics of immune cell populations within the neonatal heart after ischemic injury. Our work showed that loss of Th2 immune cell drivers: IL-4 and IL-13, negatively impacted cardiac regeneration after ischemic injury in neonatal mice, which was reversed with treatment of either interleukin-4 or interleukin-13. Furthermore, alternatively activated macrophage populations signaled through IL-4Ra was necessary for neonatal hearts to functionally recover after ischemic injury. Through a variety of in vivo experiments utilizing both the IL-4/IL-13 knockout mouse and the IL-4Ra-myeloid specific knockout mice, we showed the necessity of IL-4/IL-13 driven Th2 immune populations in the neonatal heart and the role of alternatively activated macrophages signaled by IL-4 and IL-13 in neonatal cardiac regeneration. We were able to successfully address and accomplish the aims set forth in Objective 1. In Objective 2, our aims were to determine how IL-4 and IL-13 promoted successful cardiac regeneration in injured neonatal hearts. While our initial hypothesis examined the role of the HuR protein, a mRNA stabilizing protein, in driving the recover of neonatal hearts, our research indicated a more significant molecular pathway, STAT6, a canonical transcription factor of IL-4 and IL-13, regulating the impact of IL-4 and IL-13 on cardiac regeneration in neonates. Through the use of a small molecule inhibitor of STAT6, we showed that loss of STAT6 signaling in the presence of IL-4 or IL-13 resulted in loss of regenerative functionality in injured neonatal hearts. While we did not specifically address the role of HuR protein in neonatal hearts, due to the inability to knockout the HuR protein without significant detriment to the animal and the fact that loss of the HuR protein is embryonically lethal (Data not shown), we moved to examine canonical downstream transcription factors regulated by both IL-4 and IL-13. From our analysis of the STAT6 signaling pathway in relation to IL-4 and IL-13 in the neonatal heart, we were able to show the molecular mechanism by which IL-4 and IL-13 regulates neonatal immune cells to maintain an anti-inflammatory profile conducive for neonatal cardiac repair.

14101119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101119.value: The major findings in our work is that neonatal immunity, specifically the neonate’s propensity to maintain a Th2 immune response, is necessary to allow for successful neonatal cardiac regeneration after ischemic injury. Moreover, that the drivers of Th2 immunity, IL-4 and IL-13, are indispensable in modulating alternatively activated macrophages through a STAT6 dependent manner to promote the regeneration of heart tissue. Finally, bulk RNA-sequencing analysis reveal that loss of alternatively activated macrophages, driven in part by the neonate’s preference for Th2 immunity through IL-4 and IL-13, increases oxidative damaging metabolites and pro-inflammatory cytokines such as type 1 interferons that negatively affect the expansion of neonatal cardiomyocytes. The work derived from funding from this grant was published in Theranostics and was presented at various conferences, winning awards such as an ATVB Travel Grant for Young Investigator Award.

14101119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101119.value: Future research will examine the role of IL-4 and/or IL-13 directly on cardiomyocytes and other peripheral cell populations such as cardiofibroblasts in the context of neonatal cardiac injury. It is understood that IL-4 will expand cardiofibroblast populations and increase overall ECM deposition in the injured adult heart, while IL-13 has been shown to moderately expand cardiomyocyte populations in the adult after injury. However, the role of how both cytokines affect other non-immune populations in the neonatal cardiac niche has not been fully explored. Moreover, our lab aims to continue to dissect the temporal kinetics of immune cell populations and how changes in immune development from neonate to perinate to adolescence impact the cardiac niche with respect to homeostatic functionality and injury repair.

14101119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101119.value: Our work shows the impact of neonatal immunity on cardiac repair. Specifically, we show that the anti-inflammatory profile of the neonate contributes to the neonate's ability to regenerate injured cardiac tissue which is no longer observed in adults. Moreover, the anti-inflammatory immune profile in neonates is driven in part by two cytokines: interleukin-4 and interleukin-13. These cytokines differentiate macrophages within the heart to an anti-inflammatory response that is conducive for cardiac repair in the neonate. Understanding how the neonatal heart changes over time, both developmentally and in its response to injury, can greatly expand on our understanding on why the adult mammalian heart does not regenerate.

14101219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14101219.value: The plant endomembrane system contains several functionally distinct membrane-bound organelles, including the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi apparatus, trans-Golgi network (TGN) or early endosome, prevacuolar compartment (PVC) or multivesicular body (MVB), and vacuole. We have recently characterized a unique plant ESCRT (endosomal sorting complex required for transport) component termed FREE1 (FYVE domain protein required for endosomal sorting 1) and demonstrated that FREE1 plays multiple functional roles in regulating membrane trafficking and MVB biogenesis in plants. Interestingly, our recent studies indicate that FREE1 may also be involved in the regulation of lipid droplet (LD) degradation in germinating seedlings. Indeed, our preliminary TEM (transmission electron microscopy) and confocal immunofluorecent studies showed that LD degradation was impaired in the Arabidopsis free1 mutant vs. the wild type (WT) plant. We thus hypothesize that FREE1 plays a role in regulating LD turnover in plants. LDs are ubiquitous dynamic organelles in all eukaryotes that store and supply lipids for energy metabolism, production of essential lipid-derived molecules, and membrane synthesis for cell growth. Triacylglycerol (TAG) is the main composition of neutral lipids stored in LDs. Two major pathways are responsible for LD turnover in eukaryotes: lipolysis involving lipase and lipophagy involving authpoagy. During lipolysis, the breakdown of LDs is initiated by the lipases, Sugar-Dependent 1 (SDP1), which catalyzes the hydrolysis of TAGs to release free fatty acids and glycerol. In Arabidopsis, SDP1 has been demonstrated to be the major TAG lipase responsible for lipid hydrolysis. Our preliminary data showed that LD degradation is impaired in free1 mutant, whereas the proper trafficking of the SDP1 to the surface of LDs is affected in the free1 mutant. Furthermore, the tubulation of SDP1-marked peroxisome was also defected in the free1 mutant. Based on these new findings, we hypothesize that FREE1 also participates in the regulation of LD degradation through modulating SDP1 trafficking and peroxisome tubulation. Therefore, the central goal of this research proposal is to illustrate the underlying mechanisms of FREE1 in regulating LDs turnover using a combination of cellular, molecular and genetic approaches. 植物內膜系統包含幾種功能不同的膜結合細胞器，包括內質網（ER），高爾基體，反式高爾基體網絡（TGN）或早期內體，液泡前體（PVC）或多泡體（MVB ）和液泡。我們最近發現了一個植物特異的ESCRT（轉運所需的內體分選複合物）組分稱為FREE1（內體分選所需的FYVE結構域蛋白1），並證明FREE1在調節植物膜運輸和多泡體（MVB）生成過程起多重作用。有趣的是，我們最近的研究表明，FREE1也可能參與種子發芽過程中脂滴（Lipid droplet, LD）降解的調節。因此，我們假設FREE1在調節植物的脂滴降解過程中起作用。該研究提案的中心目標是通過細胞，分子和遺傳方法的組合來證明FREE1在調節脂滴降解過程中的潛在機制。

14101219.label: Realisation of objectives
14101219.value: Objective 1: To perform morphological and biochemical analysis of LDs degradation in free1 mutant. A. To demonstrate that LDs degradation was impaired in free1 mutant, we performed time lapse confocal imaging and western blot analysis to examine LD mobilization profiles in germinating seedlings of the wild type (WT), dexamethasone (DEX)-induced knock-down (KD) of FREE1 lines (DEX::FREE1-RNAi), and transgenic DEX::FREE1-RNAi LDAP3-RFP line with or without DEX treatment for 1-5 days. The LDs were either stained by BODIPY or marked by the LD marker LDAP3-RFP. The results showed that LDs were gradually disappeared and lost most signals at 5 DAG (days after germination) in germinating seedlings of DEX::FREE1-RNAi and DEX::FREE1-RNAi LDAP3-RFP without DEX, which is similar to those in the WT seedlings. However, in the presence of DEX, numerous LDs were still detected at 5 DAG seedlings of DEX::FREE1-RNAi and DEX::FREE1-RNAi LDAP3-RFP. Confocal imaging analysis showed that the BODIPY-stained LDs were also accumulated in germinating seedlings of free1 T-DNA insertional mutant at 5 DAG compared to the WT, indicating that FREE1 is required for LDs degradation in germinating seedlings. B. We also performed transmission electron microscope (TEM) analysis on the accumulation of LDs in free1 mutant, showing that LDs accumulated in root epidermis cells in 7-day-old seedlings of free1 mutant, distinct from the WT. C. We have also analyzed the amount and composition of TAGs in germinating seedlings. Total lipids were extracted from the germinating DEX::FREE1-RNAi lines in the presence or absence of DEX at 1-5 days respectively for subsequent identification and quantification of TAGs using tandem mass spectrometry. The results showed that the total TAG contents and different TAG species contents in DEX::FREE1-RNAi seedlings with DEX induction were significantly higher than those without DEX treatments at 5 DAG. Taken together, these data demonstrated that LDs degradation is impaired in free1 mutants. Objective 2: To illustrate the underlying mechanisms of FREE1 regulation on SDP1 trafficking and LDs degradation. A. We performed confocal imaging analysis on the hypocotyl region of 4-day-old transgenic Arabidopsis plants expressing GFP-SDP1 or PEX11e in the background of WT and free1 mutant. The results showed that the GFP-SDP1 and mcherry-PEX11e label long tubules along with puncta and ring-like structures in the WT but do not show obvious tubular structures in the free1 mutant. B. We also performed confocal imaging analysis to observe the relationship between LDs and peroxisomes in the hypocotyl region of 4-day-old germinating seedlings of DEX::FREE1-RNAi GFP–SDP1 in the presence or absence of DEX with Nile Red staining LDs. The results showed that without DEX treatment or in the WT seedlings, many of the Nile Red-stained LDs are located inside the lumen of the GFP-SDP1 ring-like structures. In contrast, upon DEX-induced KD (knock-down) of FREE1, the Nile Red-stained LDs are found largely outside and separated from the GFP-SDP1-positive ring-like structures. Similar results were obtained from the free1 T-DNA mutant. C. We also performed EM-based analysis on the relationship between LDs and peroxisomes in 1-day-old root tip cells in the background of free1 or using DEX::FREE1-RNAi GFP–SDP1. We performed conventional two-dimensional (2D) TEM, immunogold-TEM, and electron tomography (ET) analysis with nanometer resolution. The results showed that LDs are engulfed and tightly associated with the peroxisomal tubules in the WT. However, few elongated peroxisomes or few surface areas tethering between peroxisomes and LDs were observed in free1 mutants. D. We generated transgenic lines of GFP-FREE1 mcherry-SDP1, and GFP-FREE1 mcherry-PEX11e to perform confocal imaging analysis on the hypocotyl regions of 3-day-old seedlings. Results showed that some FREE1 puncta were closely associated with PEX11e and SDP1. E. We performed a protease protection assay to analyze the SDP1 topology. Results confirmed that the SDP1 is an integral membrane protein and both the C-terminus and the N-terminus of SDP1 face the cytosol. F. PEX11e, PEX11c, and PEX11d are highly conserved among themselves, but both PEX11a and PEX11b are less similar to PEX11e, PEX11c, and PEX11d. G. We performed protein interaction analysis among FREE1, PEX11e and SDP1 by multiple experiments, including yeast two hybrid (Y2H) assay, in vitro pull-down assay, acceptor photobleaching fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET-AB) analysis, and co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP). Results showed that FREE1 interacts with both PEX11e (rather than PEX11a and PEX11b) and SDP1, and that PEX11e cannot interact directly with SDP1, suggesting that FREE1 may act as a scaffold bridging PEX11e and SDP1 during LD metabolism. Taken together, these data demonstrated that FREE1 is required for the proper trafficking of SDP1 to LD surface in germinating seedlings, and that FREE1 interacts directly with SDP1 for its proper localization. Objective 3: To investigate the underlying mechanisms of FREE1 regulation on peroxisome tubulation. A. We performed sequence alignment analysis on PEX11s in plants and other eukaryotes. We also performed the Heliquest analysis on PEX11e. Results showed that Arabidopsis PEX11e contains a putative amphipathic helix (AH) motif at its N-terminus (amino acids 44–75). B. We performed pull-down assays using synthetic peptides corresponding to different regions of PEX11e together with protein extracts isolated from transgenic Arabidopsis cells expressing Myc-FREE1 or recombinant His-Sumo-FREE1 proteins. Results showed that FREE1 specifically interacts with the putative AH motif of PEX11e. C. In Arabidopsis, the PEX11 family proteins promote peroxisomal proliferation and tubulation. And the AH motif of PEX11s, conserved in eukaryotes, has membrane remodeling capacity. Therefore, our results indicated that FREE1 may play a role in peroxisome tubulation by its interaction with the AH motif of PEX11e. Taken together, our study demonstrated that FREE1 is required for proper SDP1 targeting and peroxisome tubulation for engulfment of LDs in germinating seedlings, and FREE1 interacts with both SDP1 and PEX11e directly for proper lipolysis in Arabidopsis seedlings. All these results have been published in The Plant Cell in 2022. This article contains 7 regular figures and 17 supplemental figures. Thus, we have completed the original goals of this project completely and successfully. Other related research: With the partial support of this GRF grant, we have also performed cellular, molecular and genetic studies on the endomembrane system and autophagic pathway in plants, resulting in several important publications in Plant Physiology, The Plant Journal, Nature Plants, PNAS, Autophagy, and Molecular Plant. In conclusion, we have achieved all the original objectives in the research project successfully. This RGC-funded project sheds new light into the research about new unique regulators in regulation of LD degradation in germinating seedlings. This project has also nurtured several graduate students with first-author publications in international journals such as The Plant Cell, Nature Plants, PNAS, Autophagy, and Molecular Plant.

14101219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14101219.value: A. We have uncovered a new role of FREE1 in regulating peroxisome-mediated turnover of lipid droplets in germinating Arabidopsis seedlings. B. We demonstrated that FREE1 is required for peroxisome tubulation and proper SDP1 targeting to LDs for degradation. C. We demonstrated that FREE1 interacts directly with SDP1 and PEX11e to mediate LDs turnover in germinating Arabidopsis seedlings. D. With partial support from this project, we have also trained several excellent postgraduate students with outstanding research outputs as demonstrated by their first-author publications of their thesis research in international journals such as Plant Cell, Nature Plants, PNAS, Autophagy, and Molecular Plant.

14101219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14101219.value: Our studies have shed new lights on the functions of FREE1 and other regulators (PEX11e and SDP1) in regulating peroxisomal extension and trafficking of the lipase SDP1 to lipid droplets (LDs) to mediate LD degradation. We have thus provided the first example of a plant specific ESCRT component FREE1 functioning in a non-endosomal organelle in eukaryotes. In a new project, we will further illustrate A) the dynamic formation of peroxisome tubulation via live-cell imaging analysis; B) the molecular mechanism underlying FREE1/PEX11e-mediated peroxisome tubulation; and C) develop an in vitro reconstitution system to demonstrate peroxisome tubulation in vitro.

14101219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14101219.value: This is the first study to illustrate the role of FREE1 in regulating LDs degradation via the lipolysis pathway in germinating Arabidopsis seedlings. FREE1 interacts directly with both SDP1 and PEX11e, and FREE1 is required for proper SDP1 targeting, peroxisome tubulation, and LDs engulfment. Findings from this study will service as the basis for future study of FREE1/PEX11e-mediated LDs degradation in germinating Arabidopsis seedlings as well as crosstalk between lipolysis pathway and the plant endomembrane system.
