14102719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14102719.value: In utero exposure to either maternal overnutrition or undernutrition can result in the disturbance of neuroendocrine control, homeostasis and epigenetic programming of a developing fetus, contributing to future risks of non-communicable diseases. This revolutionary concept was derived from the Barker’s hypothesis since 1980’s. Our team has reported a few important findings through the follow-up of mother-child pairs participated in the Hyperglycemia and Adverse Pregnancy Outcome (HAPO) study at 2001-2005: (i) maternal hyperglycaemia in pregnancy independently increased children’s future risk of obesity, abnormal glucose regulation, higher insulin resistance and blood pressure (BP); (ii) both inadequate and excessive maternal gestational weight gain (GWG) increased children’s insulin resistance and BP; (iii) low umbilical cord blood vitamin D level was associated with children’s higher blood glucose levels and arterial stiffness, when the offspring were at 7 years of age (from two projects supported by General Research Fund). Our work has sparked off an international multicentre HAPO follow-up study, supported by NIH and NIDDK, when the children were 11-14 years of age. Our research team was among the 10 study centres, and this was our second HAPO follow-up study; surprisingly, out of the 736 local adolescents assessed, 18% of them were diagnosed with prediabetes/diabetes. Our findings on the association between maternal hyperglycaemia and children’s dysglycaemia and obesity was confirmed in other ethnic groups and the first paper was recently published. The HAPO offspring will reach young adulthood by 2020, so we expect to see more prevalent important outcomes, namely type 2 diabetes (DM) and hypertension. We, therefore, propose a third HAPO follow-up study to assess the trajectory of children’s cardiometabolic risks, and explore their associations with maternal hyperglycaemia, GWG, pre-pregnant BMI in adjustment of children’s environmental exposure, like dietary pattern and exercise level, in this unique cohort. Given we have systematically collected offspring’s BMI, multiple time point glucose and insulin levels, lipid profile and arterial stiffness in both follow-up studies, we can explore the predictability of children’s and adolescent’s insulin resistance, pancreatic beta cell functions and arterial stiffness contributing subsequently to the development of type 2 DM and hypertension in young adulthood. The findings will have important input to the Barker’s hypothesis in the area of in utero hyperglycaemia and overnutrition on the long-term cardiometabolic risk in offspring, and hopefully spark another international study on all HAPO offspring with different ethnic groups. 母親懷孕期的營養過剩或營養不良可能影響胎兒內分泌平衡和表觀遺傳過程的發展，從而增加日後發生慢性疾病的風險。這革命性的概念來源自Barker於八十年代提出的學說。我們的研究團隊已經從2001-2005年間母親與子女共同參與的「血糖過高與妊娠不良結果關係」(HAPO)的隨訪研究中有了一些重要的發現：（1）母親妊娠期高血糖會增加子女日後肥胖、血糖異常、胰島素抵抗和高血壓的風險；（2）母親妊娠期體重增加過多或過少均會增加子女胰島素抵抗和高血壓的風險；（3）臍帶血維生素D含量低會導致子女七歲時血糖增高以及動脈硬化指數（來自於GRF資助的兩項研究結果）。 當子女滿11-14歲時，我們發起了一項得到美國國立衛生研究院（NIH）和美國國立糖尿病、消化、腎病協會（NIDDK）支持的國際多中心隨訪研究。此次研究是我們團隊第二次的HAPO隨訪研究，我們的研究團隊是10個研究中心之一。出乎意料，736個青少年參與者中，18%已出現被診斷為糖尿病前期或糖尿病。此外，我們發現母親妊娠期高血糖和子女血糖異常以及肥胖相關並發表了第一篇文獻，其他種族的研究結果也與我們一致。 在2020年，HAPO研究中的子女即將成年，我們希望屆時能有更多的有關如二型糖尿病和高血壓等流行病的研究發現。因此，我們提出第三次HAPO隨訪研究的申請，希望用這個特別的隊列研究來評估兒童心血管代謝風險的發展軌跡，以及在調整了兒童環境暴露因素（如飲食方式、運動水平）後，它們與母親妊娠期高血糖、體重增長、妊娠前體重指數之間的關係。 鑑於我們在兩次隨訪研究中都已有系統地採集了子女的體重指數、數個時間點的血糖和胰島素水平，血脂情況和動脈硬化的信息，我們可以探索兒童和青少年胰島素抵抗、胰島β細胞功能和動脈硬化對成年後發生二型糖尿病和高血壓的預測價值。 此次研究結果將在妊娠期高血糖和營養過剩對子女遠期心血管代謝風險領域對Barker提出的學說做出貢獻。同時，對於HAPO子女，我們還希望可以開展另一個由多個種族參與的國際性多中心研究項目。

14102719.label: Realisation of objectives
14102719.value: Among 1,667 singleton pregnant women enrolled in the Hong Kong Centre between 2000 and 2006, who underwent a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) at 24-32 gestational weeks, 506 mother-child pairs followed up to 18 years between 2020-2023 and 59 mothers (11.66%) had gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). For objective 1, we have conducted several analyses to evaluate the association of maternal glycaemic levels with offspring’s risk of DM and adiposity at 18-20 years of age. Among 506 mother-child pairs followed up to 18 years, per 1-SD increase for maternal FPG in pregnancy was associated with an increase in children’s FPG by 0.05 mmol/L, while per 1-SD increase for maternal 1-hour PG was associated with an increase in children’s fasting, 30-min, and 2- hour PG by 0.04, 0.20, and 0.14 mmol/L, respectively. Per 1-SD increase for maternal 1-hour PG at OGTT was associated with a higher risk of offspring’s IFG by 235%. All maternal glycaemic levels at OGTT were associated with an increased risk of offspring adiposity, per 1-SD increase for maternal FPG, 1-hour PG, and 2-hour PG was associated with a higher risk of offspring’s adiposity by 32%, 50%, and 50%, respectively. For objective 2, association of insulin resistance and pancreatic beta cell functions at 7 and 11 years of age with the development of young-onset type 2 DM at 18-20 years of age Among 506 mother-child pairs followed up to 18 years, 407 children without abnormal glucose tolerance had a measurement of insulin resistance and pancreatic beta cell function at 7 years of age. Children’s 2-hour PG at 18 years significantly decreased with increased Matsuda index at 7 years of age. However, there is no significant difference in children’s glycaemic levels at 18 years among pancreatic beta cell function groups at 7 years of age. Due to the low proportion of abnormal glucose tolerance at 18 years of age (36, 8.85%), no significant association was observed between children’s Matsuda index and pancreatic beta cell function at 7 years and the risk of abnormal glucose tolerance at 18 years of age. Among 506 mother-child pairs followed up to 18 years, 314 children without abnormal glucose tolerance had a measurement of insulin resistance and pancreatic beta cell function at 11 years of age. No trends were observed in children’s glycaemic levels at 18 years with changes in Insulin resistance and pancreatic beta cell function at 11 years of age. Due to the low proportion of abnormal glucose tolerance at 18 years of age (21, 6.69 %), no significant association was observed between children’s Matsuda index and pancreatic beta cell function at 11 years and the risk of abnormal glucose tolerance at 18 years of age. For objective 3, we have conducted separate analyses regarding the association of children’s carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity at 7 and 11 years with their blood pressure and young-onset hypertension at 18 years of age. Among 506 mother-child pairs followed up to 18 years, 411 children had a measurement of cfPWV at 7 years of age. There is a significantly linear relationship between children’s cfPWV at 7 years and blood pressure at 18 years of age, and children’s SBP and DBP at 18 years significantly increased with increased cfPWV at 7 years of age. After adjusting for maternal sum of glucose z-score at OGTT, gestational weight gain z-score, hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, and traditional cardiovascular risk factors at 7 years of age, children’s cfPWV at 7 years was not associated with blood pressure at 18 years of age, but per 1 m/s increase for children’s cfPWV at 7 years was associated with a higher risk of hypertension at 18 years of age by 97%. Moreover, per 1 m/s increase for children’s cfPWV at 7 years was directly associated with the 11-year increase in SBP and DBP by 2.76 and 3.34 mmHg. Among 506 mother-child pairs followed up to 18 years, 324 children had a measurement of cfPWV at 11 years of age. There is a significantly linear relationship between children’s cfPWV at 11 years and blood pressure at 18 years of age, and children’s SBP and DBP at 18 years significantly increased with increased cfPWV at 11 years of age. After adjusting for maternal sum of glucose z-score at OGTT, gestational weight gain z-score, hypertensive disorders in pregnancy, and traditional cardiovascular risk factors at 11 years of age, per 1 m/s increase for children’s cfPWV at 11 years was associated with increased DBP at 18 years of age. Moreover, there is a sex difference that a significant increase in SBP by increased cfPWV at 7 years was observed among girls at 18 years of age. In addition, per 1 m/s increase for children’s cfPWV at 11 years was associated with a higher risk of stage 1/stage 2 hypertension at 18 years of age by 122%. For the 7-year longitudinal progression of children’s BP from 11 to 18 years of age, per 1 m/s increase for children’s cfPWV at 11 years was associated with increased SBP and DBP by 4.12 and 4.34 mmHg.

14102719.label: Major findings and research outcome
14102719.value: Objective 1: Maternal hyperglycaemia in pregnancy showed long-term effects on offspring metabolic health into young adulthood. The continuous associations across the full maternal glucose spectrum, rather than only above GDM diagnostic thresholds, suggest the importance of optimal glycaemic control during pregnancy for offspring metabolic health later in life. Our findings not only support the Pedersen and DOHaD hypotheses, but also highlight the potential importance of glucose measurements during pregnancy beyond traditional thresholds for GDM screening. The persistence of these associations into early adulthood, despite potential attenuation over time, emphasizes the need for optimal glycaemic control during pregnancy. The persistence of the effects of maternal hyperglycaemia to early adulthood highlights the potential intergenerational effects of maternal hyperglycaemia impact on future generations. Objective 2: Though a significant difference in children’s 2-hour PG at 18 years of age among oral disposition index groups was observed, with a lower proportion of children’s abnormal glucose tolerance at 18 years of age, no significant associations of children’s insulin resistance and pancreatic beta cell functions at 7 years with young-onset abnormal glucose tolerance at 18 years of age were observed. Objective 3: Children’s increased arterial stiffness, measured by cfPWV at 11 years, showed long-term effects on offspring blood pressure into young adulthood, and children’s increased arterial stiffness at 7 and 11 years is associated with an increased risk of young-onset hypertension at 18 years of age, regardless of in-utero exposure and traditional cardiovascular risk factors. Young-onset hypertension prevention from childhood or early adolescence may require developing novel approaches to mitigate arterial stiffness.

14102719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14102719.value: Future studies with more frequent glucose measurements throughout pregnancy may better understand the critical windows for metabolic programming and develop prevention strategies for long-term offspring metabolic health, given the important findings in Objective 1 that mothers with higher plasma glucose levels at OGTT in pregnancy, even below the diagnostic threshold for gestational diabetes mellitus, could affect their offspring’s cardiometabolic health into early adulthood. For Objective 2, further large-scale prospective cohort studies are needed to confirm the effect of longitudinal progression of children’s insulin resistance and pancreatic beta cell dysfunction from early childhood to adolescence on the development of young-onset type 2 DM at 18-20 years of age. Further large-scale prospective cohort studies might be needed to identify the risk factors related to increased arterial stiffness in children and develop new strategies to mitigate arterial stiffness in early childhood or adolescence, given the current findings in Objective 3 that children with increased arterial stiffness in early childhood or adolescence are at a higher risk of developing young-onset hypertension in early adulthood.

14102719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14102719.value: First, this research, with the current findings, highlights the long-term effects of maternal hyperglycaemia in pregnancy on offspring’s cardiometabolic risk factors in young adulthood. Mothers with higher plasma glucose levels at OGTT in pregnancy, even below the diagnostic threshold for gestational diabetes mellitus, could affect their offspring’s cardiometabolic health into early adulthood. This underscores the importance of maintaining optimal plasma glucose levels in pregnancy to reduce future cardiometabolic risks for their offspring. Second, children with increased arterial stiffness, measured by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity, at 7 and 11 years of age are more likely to have increased blood pressure or hypertension in early adulthood, regardless of traditional cardiovascular risk factors. This suggests that arterial stiffness in childhood plays a key role in young-onset hypertension in early adulthood. Preventing high blood pressure in young adults may require new strategies to address increased arterial stiffness starting in early childhood or adolescence. In short, managing maternal plasma glucose levels during pregnancy and mitigating arterial stiffness in early childhood or adolescence could help reduce their offspring’s risks of young-onset type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension later in life.

14103119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103119.value: 背景 「鼻病毒感染只是感冒」的概念已過時了。因呼吸道感染而需住院的兒童中，主要都有鼻病毒感染，而且臨床表徵多樣化. 早前的研究指出，鼻病毒可以是導致下呼吸道感染的唯一病原。也有報告指出，幼兒早期接觸鼻病毒以至日後在兒童期形成哮喘有著莫大的關聯。更有趣的是，無症狀的鼻病毒感染也很常見。如此多樣的臨牀病況，可能是因為宿主因子的差異，更有機會是因鼻病毒間不同的基因型中的不同毒性所產生的。鼻病毒屬於腸病毒屬，有三個品種：鼻病毒-A, 鼻病毒-B和鼻病毒-C，共有168個基因型。 研究人員嘗試尋找三種鼻病毒與臨牀病況的關係。而鼻病毒-C則被認為與嚴重病況和哮喘發作有著最密切的關係。事實上，鼻病毒-C有56個被確認的基因型和11個暫定基因型。除非它們全都有保守生物途徑，否則若能依據它們所引致臨牀病況的嚴重性，從而優先針對研究個別的鼻病毒，將能更有效管理和鼻病毒有關的病況。至今，流行病學家仍在基因型的層面上監控鼻病毒，可是煩多的基因型卻令基因型和臨牀病況之間的關聯統計結果不甚顯著。有見及此，我們將以不少於1,368 個對鼻病毒呈陽性反應的樣本進行深入分析。 目標與假設 我們的目標是要將鼻病毒依疾病表型歸納為功能分組，表型包括 一、上呼吸道感染； 二、急性細支氣管炎； 三、病毒性肺炎； 四、無症狀社區對照。 我們會將歸納在以上功能分組的鼻病毒進行全基因組測序，與以比較不同功能分組間的基因組測序。我們假設每個鼻病毒功能分組中的鼻病毒基因型都會有獨特的基因序列，而該基因序列則是在鼻病毒功能分組中的保守序列。而這些關鍵的保守序列，則讓在這功能分組的鼻病毒擁有其特性，從而產生其在人體中特定的病理機制以致疾病表型。 研究設計 於2015年至2016年間對鼻病毒呈陽性的住院兒童和社區對照的樣本將用作鼻病毒功能分組。成功歸納在鼻病毒功能分組中的的呼吸道樣本，將以下一代測序技術來作完整病毒基因組測序。功能分組中獨特的保守序列會被鑒定出來。最後，這些序列所引致的不同宿主反應，將在人呼吸道上皮細胞實驗中，以轉錄組高通量測序來評估。

14103119.label: Realisation of objectives
14103119.value: Objective 1: Identify the Functional Groups of Rhinovirus Genotyping of RV from nasopharyngeal aspirate or swab specimen Acquisition of nasopharyngeal aspirate samples: Nasopharyngeal aspirate (NPA) frozen archive specimens of hospitalised patients aged 1 to 17, from 2015 to 2017, were examined for genotype distributions in RV infections. Viral RNA was extracted from the NPA specimen and underwent reverse transcription. The cDNA was subjected to a nested PCR of the viral protein (VP)4 and VP2 region. PCR product with an expected band size of 550 bp was sent for Sanger sequencing (BGI Genomics). The nucleotide sequence of the amplicons in the VP4/VP2 was compared with the prototype sequence of RV in GenBank using BLAST+. The genotyping result was returned subject to our in-house BLAST+ database rules. All the available RV complete genomes or segments of the prototype RV sequences, recognised by the International Committee on Taxonomy of Virus (ICTV), were downloaded by the NCBI E-Utils tool by E-Fetch command. The classification of the RV genotypes was validated against the standard RV classification proposed by McIntyre's research team (McIntyre et al., 2013), and the updated classification from Picornaviridae group on https://www.picornaviridae.com/, up to October 2022. A qualified genotyping result requires the following: 1) The percentage of similarity is greater than or equal to 89.5% in RV-A and RV-C and 90.5% in RV-B in the VP4/2 region; 2) The e-value in the BLAST matches is greater than or equal to 0.001; and 3) The alignment length is greater than or equal to 90% of the coverage of the prototype available in the database. Sample inclusion criteria: Patients aged 1 to 17, admitted to two regional tertiary hospitals, namely PWH and ANH in New Territories East Cluster of Hong Kong. NPA specimens tested EV/RV positive as the single agent were selected for downstream analysis for functional grouping. The clinical records of these subjects were reviewed by physicians without knowing the genotype result. The symptoms in the discharge notes were reviewed and categorised into upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), bronchiolitis, pneumonia, and asthma exacerbation (AE). Global Initiative for Asthma guideline was used to examine the asthma exacerbation cases in the review ("Global Initiative for Asthma", 2022). Immunocompromised patients were excluded from the study. The statistical analysis for the association of each genotype was tested against each disease's phenotype, namely virus-genotype-to-disease-phenotype association, and the odds ratio calculation with a 95% confidence interval (CI) was done by Fisher's Exact Test using R (R Core Team, 2021) and logistic regression using IBM SPSS (IBM Corp, 2020), with the level of significance set at 0.05, unless specified. Result: RV Genotyping: Using this system, 1,898 specimens were tested with 1543 (81%) of the Enterovirus/RV-positive nasopharyngeal aspirate being genotyped. An overall distribution of 46% of RV-A, 5% of RV-B and 49% of RV-C was found. The ‘unsuccessful’ genotyped samples were coxsackievirus, enterovirus D68, echovirus and enterovirus A2. The distribution of RV was evaluated at the species level: RV-A, RV-B and RV-C, and by classification based on receptor usage: major group (ICAM-1), minor group (LDLR family), or RV-C (CDHR3). At the species level, RV-C contributed nearly half of the cases (49.3%), followed by RV-A (45.7%) and a minority of RV-B (5.1%). By classification by receptor usage, RV-C contributed nearly half of the cases (49.3%), followed by major group RV contributed 42.1%, and minor group RV of 8.6%. A total of 135 RV genotypes were identified out of the 169 documented genotypes. The most prevalent RV genotype was RV-C15 (n=76), contributing to 4.9% of all the RV genotypes identified. Followed by RV-A49 (n=67) with 4.3%, RV-C6 (n=62) with 4.0%, RV-C2 (n=39) with 2.5%, RV-C11 (n=33) with 2.1% and RV-C12 (n=32) with 2.1%. The remaining genotypes contributed less than 2% individually, which were either RV-C viruses or major group RVs (RV-A12, -A16, A101). The association of rhinovirus genotype-to-disease-phenotype: Upper respiratory tract infection was the most prevalent disease phenotype in RV-positive patients, with a mean of 22.0% ± 5.6% annually (n = 113 ± 25). Asthma exacerbation was the second most prevalent disease phenotype in RV-positive patients. The mean cases yearly were 16.1% ± 1.7% (n = 83 ± 19). The third prevalence disease was bronchiolitis, with a mean of 13.2% ± 4.7% (n = 68 ± 19) cases per year. Lastly, there were 8.9% ± 1.2% (n = 46 ± 1) reports of pneumonia yearly. Each disease outcome was tested against the 135 genotypes discovered in the cohort by Fisher's exact test. To obtain a statistical significance in comparing the association among 135 categorical comparisons (RV genotype found in this project) per each disease outcome, the statistical significance of the 135 Fisher’s exact test is denoted as p<0.05/135. It was revealed that RV-C35 was associated with asthma exacerbation (p=1.58 × 10^-7), with an odds ratio of 8.797 with a 95% CI of (3.701, 21.971). Using a logistic regression model, we found that RV-C35 again had a positive association with asthma exacerbation with a (P < 0.036, OR 6.4, 95% CI (1.12, 36.44)). On the other hand, RV-C15 (p=0.005), C12 (p=0.035), C5 (p=0.047) and A16 (p=0.050) were found to be negatively associated with pneumonia. Objective 2: Complete and compare the complete genomes of the viral strains clustered in the functional groups. From the result of objective 1, we aim to isolate the RV-C35 and perform sequencing. In total, we have identified 26 samples positive with RV-C35, in which 16 of them were associated with the clinical presentation of asthma exacerbations while 10 of them were not. For objective 1, 140uL of the specimens were used up. We attempted to perform the viral RNA extraction, synthesis of dsDNA and purification to proceed with the library preparation for the NGS sequencing. Unfortunately, the RNA yield ranged between 20ng and 150ng, which is far below the minimum requirement for RNA sequencing, i.e., 200ng. Therefore, we were not able to perform further investigation of the subsequent sequence. The final attempt we made was to pick the specimens with the highest viral gene copy as quantified in the quantitative PCR, and inoculate them into a primary human nasal epithelial cell (HNEC) culture that expresses the entry receptor (cadherin-related family member 3) required by RV-C, with the expectation that the virus would replicate into higher quantity for measurements. Objective 3: Characterize the differential host response induction by some of these functional groups in human respiratory epithelial cells Three RV-C35 specimens with a viral cycle of threshold (Ct) of 19, 20, and 25 were used to inoculate the HNEC and the supernatant was harvested 48 hours post-infection (hpi). While only one of these supernatants tested positive for RV viral gene. The supernatant sample was then used as the standard RV-C35 stock for the subsequent inoculation of HNECs in order to characterize the RV-C35-induced host response as planned. Four different HNEC donors were included in the subsequent experiment using this RV-C35 stock. One set of the HNEC from each donor underwent the IL13 treatment, while the other set was an untreated control. RV-C35 induced an obvious cytopathic effect to IL13-treated but not in control HNECs. Transcriptomic analysis of these HNECs were also performed at 48 hpi.

14103119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14103119.value: As the basis of the study, the evaluation of the respiratory virus epidemiology in children is inevitable (Part C, Research Postgraduate Thesis), and the viral interference exerted between rhinovirus and influenza at the population, individual and cellular levels were also described in Tao et al. (Part C, Publication 3). In Jan 2020, SARS-CoV-2 was first introduced in Hong Kong. With the strict social distancing and mask mandate, all the other respiratory viruses vanished except rhinovirus. We studied the diversity of the circulating rhinovirus and found a monopoly of minor group viruses in the community, namely RV-A47 in Oct 2020 and RV-A49 in April to August 2021. This finding was disseminated in Pun et al., 2022 (Part C, Publication 2). With the vast RV genotypes (168+), the EV-positive sample size was not enough to achieve a statistically significant association of individual genotypes to upper respiratory infection, acute bronchiolitis, and viral pneumonia but pinpointed the potential of RV-C35 as the trigger of asthma exacerbation (AE). The findings of the functional grouping were disseminated in Pun et al., 2020 (Publication 1, Part C). A bootstrap phylogenetic tree was done using the viral protein 4/2 junction of the 16 RV-C35 samples from cases with AE and 10 RV-C35 samples from cases without AE. A clear clustering of samples into AE and without AE groups was resulted, suggesting the possible involvement of viral determinants in clinical outcomes. To evaluate the innate immune response induced by RV-C35 in the airways, four different primary human nasal epithelial cells (HNEC) donors were included. HNECs were cultured in an air-liquid interface (ALI) platform for the full differentiation of goblet, ciliated, club and basal cells in a pseudostratified epithelium. A pre-treatment of IL-13 at the basolateral compartment ALI culture of the HNECs was used as an in vitro asthmatic model to investigate the impact of RV-C35 between ‘asthmatic’ and non-asthmatic airways. Upon RV-C35 infection, a similar viral load between IL-13 treated and non-treated cells was comparable. When comparing the DEGs at 48 hours post-infection, RV-C35 induced 874 more upregulated and 1121 downregulated genes in the IL-13 treated HNECs than the untreated cells. Moreover, we identified that RV-C35 caused cytopathic effects in IL-13-treated HNECs but not in untreated HNECs. This observation infers the interaction between the viral and host components that leads to specific biological outcomes.

14103119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14103119.value: A prospective study with specimens freshly collected from subjects will greatly improve the sample quality. Therefore, the RV of interest can be isolated using differentiated human nasopharyngeal epithelial cells to overcome the inadaptability of isolating RV in H1-HeLa cells. With RV being successfully isolated, whole genome sequencing can be used to identify the biological niches causing a particular disease. With further experiments in animal models, with integrations of the method used in this study, the molecular determinants in rhinovirus by virus-genotype to disease-phenotype can be revealed.

14103119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14103119.value: Rhinovirus (RV) is a dominant infectious cause of hospitalization in the paediatric populations, and it involves a spectrum of disease outcomes. The diverse clinical outcomes could be attributed by the host factors and very likely the differential virulence among the numerous RV genotypes. By genotyping 1543 Enterovirus/RV-positive nasopharyngeal aspirate of hospitalised children with respiratory symptoms in Hong Kong, 46%, 5% and 49% were RV-A, -B and -C, respectively. In the association study between RV genotype and clinical symptoms, RV-C35 was found to be the RV genotype associated with asthma exacerbations (AE). Although the whole genome sequencing of the RV-C35 samples was not achieved due to limited viral materials, a bootstrap phylogenetic tree of the viral protein 4/2 junction of the 26 RV-C35 samples showed a clear clustering of samples into groups with and without asthma exacerbations, suggesting the possible involvement of viral determinants in clinical outcomes. Moreover, by utilising IL-13 pre-treated primary human nasal epithelial cell (HNEC) as an in vitro asthmatic model, we identified that RV-C35 caused cell death in IL-13-treated HNECs but not in untreated HNECs. This observation infers the interaction between the viral and host components that leads to specific biological outcomes.

14103419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14103419.value: Myopia (short-sightedness) is a global health threat. By year 2025, it is predicted approximately 50% and 10% of world’s population being myopic and highly myopic respectively. Notably, high myopia is associated with excessive eyeball growth leading to many sight-threatening complications. Low-concentration atropine eye drop is one of the emerging therapies for myopia control, but its optimal concentration and long-term efficacy is poorly defined. Our study Low-concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression (LAMP) is the first placebo-controlled double-blind randomized trial on 438 Chinese children aged 4 to 12 using 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine eye drops. Phase 1 to 2 (year 1 to 2) results proved that low concentration atropine could effectively reduce myopia progression along a concentration-dependent response. In phase 3 (year 3), half of the subjects in 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% were randomized to atropine-continued group of the respective concentration, and half to washout group for one year. We demonstrated that 0.05% is the optimal concentration at three-years follow up. Our current proposal is LAMP Phase 4 study (year 4 and 5) to examine the ideal treatment regimen and long-term efficacy of low-concentration atropine for 5 years. A total of 260 subjects aged 8-16 will be recruited for follow up at 6-months interval for two years. Half of group (130 subjects), recruited from Phase 3 atropine-continued groups 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01%, will be assigned to atropine-continued treatment group (0.05% atropine daily for two years). Another half (130 subjects), recruited from Phase 3 washout groups 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01%, will be assigned to the Pro Re Nata (PRN) treatment group. (0.05% atropine eye drops daily will be restarted if myopia progresses more than 0.5 diopter in one eye during the follow up at year 4 and year 5.) The primary outcomes include 1) spherical equivalent (SE) progression of using low-concentration atropine eye drops over a 5-year period; and 2) SE progression in the atropine-continued treatment group and PRN treatment group during year 4 and year 5 follow up. The secondary outcomes include: 1) Axial length elongation; 2) Pupil size; 3) accommodation amplitude; 4) near and distance visual acuity; 5) vision-related quality of life We will provide evidence-based data on the ideal treatment regimen and long-term efficacy of low-concentration atropine for myopia control. The results will definitely shift the current paradigm in the management of childhood myopia.

14103419.label: Realisation of objectives
14103419.value: Objective 1 We have found that a high percentage of children requiring restart of treatment after cessation at year 3, but when children who experienced myopia progression during the cessation period, retreatment with 0.05% atropine demonstrated similar efficacy comparable to the continuous use of 0.05% atropine. Proportion of restart treatment Among 107 children in the PRN retreatment group, 94 (87.9%) children needed to restart the treatment during year 4 to 5, and the proportion of retreatment among the groups of initial usage of 0.05%, 0.025% and 0.01% groups were 88.6% (31/35), 84.4% (27/32) and 90.0% (36/40) with no significant differences (P=0.76). 74 (69.2%) children needed to restart the treatment at the beginning of year 4, and the proportion of retreatment among the groups of initial usage of 0.05%, 0.025% and 0.01% groups were 71.4% (25/35), 68.8% (22/32) and 67.5% (27/40) with no significant differences (P=0.93). Successful treatment cessation was associated with older age (OR=2.40, P<0.001), but not atropine concentration, sex, or baseline SE. Changes in SE Refraction and AL between Continued Treatment and PRN Retreatment Groups from Years 3 to 5 From year 3 to 5, SE progressions for the continued treatment and PRN retreatment groups were – 0.97D±0.82D, and –1.00±0.74D (P=0.55), and AL elongations were 0.51±0.34 mm, and 0.49±0.32 mm, respectively (P=0.84). There were no significant differences in both SE progression and AL elongations across concentration subgroups (P from 0.25 to 0.92, and from 0.68 to 0.98 respectively). Our study revealed a high percentage of children requiring restart of treatment after cessation at year 3. While the retreatment rate is not affected by the concentrations among 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01%, it is associated with age. With 1-year younger, 2.40-fold more chance to restart atropine treatment. Young age has also been shown as a strong risk factor with either poor treatment outcomes or more rebound. This can be related to the faster inherent physiological progression of children at younger ages. We suggest that low-concentration atropine treatment should not be stopped at young ages as the natural myopic progression rate is still fast. Children who experienced myopia progression during the cessation period, retreatment with 0.05% atropine demonstrated similar efficacy comparable to the continuous use of 0.05% atropine. While SE was more myopic in PRN retreatment than in continued treatment group at the end of year 3, reintroduction of 0.05% atropine in PRN retreatment group achieved a greater effect than in continued treatment, probably due to the hyperopic shift after retreatment. This offset the progression observed in year 3. Therefore, the overall efficacy of both groups from years 3 to 5 were similar. Our findings suggest if myopia progression is noted during a cessation period, restart of atropine therapy should be considered. Given the observed high rates of retreatment in our study, we suggest continued treatment of 0.05% atropine until the fifth year in Chinese children. Objective 2 We have determined continued 0.05% atropine treatment was effective in myopia control with good tolerance over 5 years. Changes in SE Refraction and AL over 5 Years In the continued groups, the cumulative mean SE progressions over 5 years were –1.34±1.40 D, –1.97±1.03 D, and –2.34±1.71 D (P=0.02), and the cumulative mean AL elongations 0.79±0.54 mm, 1.11±0.46 mm, and 1.24±0.72 mm (P=0.007) for in the initial 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine subgroups, respectively. In the PRN retreatment group, similar trends of the cumulative mean SE progression and AL elongation over 5 years were observed (Table 2 and Figure 2). In the switchover group, SE progression and were -1.86±1.14 D, faster than either -1.34±1.40D of 0.05% continued group (P=0.03), or 1.45±1.28 of 0.05% PRN retreatment group (P=0.006) over 5 years. Similar trends were observed in AL elongation. Side Effects and Vision-Related Quality of Life Over 5 Years Photophobia was the most common adverse event and was reported by 26 (38.2%), 17 (28.8%), 28 (35.4%) and 19 (29.7%) participants in the initial 0.05%, 0.025%, 0.01% atropine, and switchover groups in the year 5. No significant differences among groups were observed in vision-related quality of life (P>0.05, Supplement Table 6). Our results revealed concentration-dependency of low concentration atropine over 5 years, the higher concentration the better efficacy. This suggests that the trend of treatment effects for higher concentration of atropine against myopia may be different from the low-concentration atropine. Notably, direct comparisons between 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% over 5 years are not appropriate because 0.025% and 0.01% were switched to 0.05% during years 4 and 5. Nevertheless, concentration-dependent effect remained over 5 years among the studied concentrations, the higher concentration, the better effectiveness. Continued 0.05% atropine over 5 years is more efficacious than either the 0.05% atropine PRN restart treatment or switchover groups, indicating 0.05% continued treatment as an effective option for myopia control. Our results also revealed that safety of low concentration atropine over 5 years, across the continued treatment subgroups, all concentrations were well tolerated over the 5-year study period.

14104019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104019.value: Lupus nephritis (LN) is a severe, and yet the most common complication of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and it is the major cause of overall morbidity and mortality of SLE patients. LN is characterized by massive production and deposition of autoantibodies, activation of complements, and progressive renal injury mediated by both innate and adaptive immunity. However, the regulatory mechanisms of LN remain largely unclear and treatment remains unspecific and suboptimal. TGF-beta/Smad signaling has been shown to play a critical role in many autoimmune diseases. In order to explore the novel role of TGF-beta/Smad signaling in LN, we successfully deleted the Smad3 gene from NZM2410-derived B6.Sle1.Sle2.Sle3 lupus-prone mice (B6.NZMSlie1-3) with unexpected findings that Smad3KO-B6.NZMSlie1-3 mice developed much more severe LN with higher mortality rate, higher circulating dsDNA, massive renal autoantibodies deposition and complement activation, and progressive renal inflammation and functional injury. Mechanistically, we observed that lupus mice lacking Smad3 largely promoted Th1, Th2 and Th17 while suppressed Treg immune responses in the kidney. Unexpectedly, deletion of Smad3 largely promoted dsDNA-induced B cell activation and autoantibody production via the transcription factor E4BP4-mediated macrophage inducible C-type lectin receptor (Mincle)-Syk signaling. Based on these novel observations, we hypothesized that TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling may be protective in LN by rebalancing the T cell immunity and importantly, by inhibiting B cell activation and autoantibody production via the E4BP4-Mincle-Syk-dependent mechanism. We plan to test this hypothesis with three Specific Aims. Firstly, we will examine TGF-beta/Smad signaling in SLE patients and mice with LN. Secondly, we will determine the functional roles of Smad3 in the pathogenesis of LN in Smad3KO-B6.NZM Sle1-3 mice, and finally, we will investigate the regulatory mechanisms of TGF-beta/Smad3 in T and B cell activation and functions in vivo and in vitro. We expect to find: 1) TGF-beta/Smad signaling is dysregulated in LN, showing inactivation in T and B cells but overactivation in the intrinsic kidney cells. 2)TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling is protective in LN as deletion of Smad3 from lupus mice exacerbates LN. 3) Increased Th1, Th2 and Th17 while suppressed Treg immune response and enhanced E4BP4-Mincle-Syk-dependent B cell activation and autoantibody production may be key mechanisms through which deletion of Smad3 worsens LN. The identification of the regulatory roles and mechanisms of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in LN will lead to the development of novel and specific therapies for LN by modulating this pathway. Thus, outcomes from this study will be of great significance both scientifically and clinically.

14104019.label: Realisation of objectives
14104019.value: The grant has been successfully completed with all objectives obtained. 1. By collaborating with Prof ZHENG Zhihua's team at the Seventh Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University in Shenzhen and Professor Szeto at Prince of Wales Hospital, and Professor TM Chan at the University of Hong Kong, as well as Professor Yu Xueqing from the Guangdong Provincial Hospital, Guangzhou, we have successfully completed the Specific Aim 1 and found that TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling was highly dysregulated in patients and mice with SLE. We found that in patients and mice with SLE, serum and urinary levels of TGF-beta1 were highly upregulated and were correlated with the severity of SLE and LN. Similarly, Smad3 signaling was also highly activated in the kidney with LN in both patients and mice. However, further analysis showed that although TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling was highly activated in the target organ kidney with progressive LN, it was suppressed in the immune system as demonstrated by a significant decrease in TGF-beta1, TGF-beta receptor II, and phospho-Smad3 in spleen cells of SLE mice. Thus, we can conclude that TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling is highly activated in patients and mice with SLE, particularly in the target kidney with LN. However, it is inhibited in the immune system. These findings suggest that overactivation of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in the kidney may contribute to progressive LN. In contract, decreased TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in the peripheral immune system may result in overreactive autoimmunity in patients and mice with SLE. 2. We have successfully completed the Specific Aim 2 by generating the Smad3 KO-SLE mice with a clear phenotype of Smad3 KO-SLE mice identified. This is the first SMAD3 KO-SLE mouse model. There were several novel findings from this novel Smad3 KO-SLE mouse model. 1) Smad3 is protective in the pathogenesis of lupus nephritis. This was supported by the finding that lupus mice lacking Smad3 developed more severe SLE mice with a double mortality rate. 2) We also found that Smad3 KO-SLE mice developed much more severe LN as demonstrated by elevated serum creatinine, a fall of creatinine clearance, and severe necrotic renal pathology. 3) Unexpectedly, deletion of Smad3 largely promoted renal inflammation in SLE mice as demonstrated by a marked activation of NF-kB and NF-kB-dependent renal inflammation including a marked infiltration of F4/80+ macrophages, CD3+ /CD4+ T cells, and a marked upregulation of proinflammatory cytokines. Thus, results from this study uncovered a general protective mechanism of Smad3 in renal inflammation in lupus nephritis. 3. We have also completed the Specific Aim 3: To investigate the regulatory mechanisms of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in LN by focusing on T and B cell activation and functions in vivo and in vitro with several novel findings. 1) We found that Smad3 deficiency suppressed Treg while promoting Th2 immune response as demonstrated by double serum levels of total IgG, anti-dsDNA antibody, the IgG subclasses IgG1, and IgG2b, resulting in a massive anti-dsDNA antibody and IgG deposition and complement activation in the kidney. 2) A novel finding from SMAD3 KO-SLE mice was that SLE mice lacking Smad3 largely enhanced the B cell immunity. This was evidenced by increased B cell population in both spleen and the diseased kidney with massive B cell activation and proliferation systemically as determined by CFSE-labelling cells and upregulation of CD86 and MHC class II expression, 3) Mechanically, we also discovered that deletion of Smad3 from SLE mice largely enhanced B cell activation via a Mincle-dependent mechanism in vivo and in vitro as silencing Mincle from B cells largely inactivated B cell proliferation, activation, and antibody production. In summary, we have successfully completed all 3 objective studies with expected achievements as described in Part C (#29). In addition, due to the COVID-19 pandemics, we have extended this study to investigate the role of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in COVID-19 acute kidney injury and immune-mediated kidney diseases including diabetic nephropathy, while we were waiting for the pro-long-generation of Smad3 KO-SLE mice. Excitingly, we found that SARs CoV-2 N protein can bind to Smad3 directly and promotes Smad3-mediated tubular necrosis via the p21/p16 and Rip3/MLKL necroptosis pathways. We also found that overexpression of SARS-CoV-2 N can cause massive renal inflammation by activating macrophages via the Mincle-dependent mechanism. Moreover, we also found that TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling plays an important role in macrophage-mediated kidney inflammation and diabetic nephropathy. All these findings have resulted in 28 publications in high impact journals such as Signal Transduct Target Ther; Adv Sci (Weinh); Autophagy; Mol Ther et al as described in the research output (Part C, #1-28). However, the proposed study was delayed due to several reasons: 1) Deletion of Smad3 from lupus mice resulted in a high mortality rate. This unexpected finding required much longer time to generate enough mouse numbers for the studies as described in the grant application. 2) Due to the COVID-19 and social unrest in Hong Kong, two research staff who were originally engaging in this grant were unable to come to Hong Kong. Thus, it needed much longer time to recruit new staff and generate Smad3KO-lupus mice to complete the experimental studies. Fortunately, we have now just completed all the experiments and all data have been collected for analysis. A new manuscript is preparing as seen in the attachment (Part C #29). Hopefully we are able to complete it within 4 months.

14104019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14104019.value: We have completed all 3 Specific Aim studies as originally described. There were several major findings. 1. In patients and mice with SLE, plasma and urinary levels of TGF-beta1 and activation of TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling were significantly elevated and were correlated tightly with the severity of LN clinically. In contrast, TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling was suppressed in the spleen. These findings suggest that TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling was dysregulated between the target organ and the immune system. Overreactive TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling may contribute to the development of LN, whereas, impaired TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in spleen may contribute to overactive systemic immunity in SLE patients and mice. 2. We also uncovered a protective role for TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling in SLE and LN. This was supported by the findings that SLE mice lacking Smad3 developed much more severe SLE and LN with double mortality rate and renal dysfunction. Indeed, most of Smad3 KO-SLE mice died within 6 months of the age with double serum creatine and progressive renal inflammation. 3. Mechanistically, we found that Smad3 deficiency suppressed Treg while promoting Th-2 responses, resulting in dysregulation of T cell immune responses with double serum levels of total IgG, anti-dsDNA antibody, the IgG subclasses IgG1, and IgG2b, and massive anti-dsDNA antibody and IgG deposition with complement activation in the kidney. More importantly, SLE mice null for Smad3 greatly enhanced the B cell immunity by expending B cell population in both spleen and the diseased kidney and promoting massive B cell activation and proliferation systemically as determined by CFSE-labelling cells and upregulation of CD86 and MHC class II expression. Furthermore, we also discovered that deletion of Smad3 from SLE mice largely enhanced B cell activation via a Mincle-dependent mechanism in vivo and in vitro as silencing Mincle from B cells largely inactivated B cell proliferation, activation, and antibody production. In conclusion, TGF-beta/Smad3 is dysregulated in patients and mice with SLE. Overreactive TGF-beta/Smad3 in the diseased kidney may cause severe LN, whereas, impaired TGF-beta/Smad3 in the spleen may promote autoimmunity systemically in SLE. Thus, Smad3 plays a protective role in SLE. Mechanistically, Smad3 may inhibit B cell activation and functions to protect against Th2-mediated SLE and LN via a Mincle-dependent mechanism.

14104019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14104019.value: The novel finding that TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling is protective in SLE suggests that targeting TGF-beta signaling could be harmful for patients with autoimmune diseases. This also well explains the failure of clinical trails by using anti-TGF-beta antibody to treat patients with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and diabetes. Thus, findings from this study are highly significant both scientifically and clinically.

14104019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14104019.value: Although TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling is pathogenic in chronic kidney disease with progressive renal fibrosis, results from this study found that TGF-beta/Smad3 signaling is protective in autoimmune diseases such as lupus nephritis. We found that disrupted Smad3 gene in lupus mice can largely promote lupus nephritis with double mortality rate and kidney injury. Mechanistically, we uncovered that disrupted Smad3 gene from lupus mice resulted in overreactive B cell immunity, thereby promoting Th-2 type immune responses with double increase in anti-dsDNA antibody and massive anti-dsDNA antibody deposition and complement activation in the kidney. Thus, anti-TGF-beta treatment may not be benefit to patients with autoimmune diseases such as lupus nephritis clinically.

14104119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104119.value: 表觀基因組在植物發育中起重要作用。在番茄中，果實成熟需要活性DNA去甲基化。去甲基化可以進一步分為兩個單獨的階段。全基因組去甲基化首先在果實發育早期發生，而在果實發育的最後階段成熟開始後發生局部去甲基化。這些局部去甲基化區域富含轉錄因子結合位點附近的基因啟動子。有趣的是，已經表明這些局部DNA去甲基化變化並不總是與成熟基因表達相關。這表明全球去甲基化可能在已經確定的成熟過程中發揮重要作用。 植物胚乳組織也經歷全基因組去甲基化，其需要與番茄果實類似的去甲基化酶。我們的初步數據顯示玉米和水稻胚乳改變了3D染色質結構。已經報導了擬南芥DNA甲基化突變體的類似模式。我們的初步數據還表明，番茄成熟基因具有遠端增強子樣區域，其與組織特異性方式的活性組蛋白標記H3K27ac相關。因此，我們假設早期果實發育過程中的全球去甲基化可能改變了3D染色質結構，並使遠端增強子與成熟基因相互作用。我們建議使用RNA-Seq，ChIP-Seq，原位Hi-C和HiChIP來檢測和比較野生型和番茄脫甲基酶DML2 CRISPR / Cas9敲除果實中的轉錄組，表觀基因組和3D染色質結構。 作為概念驗證實驗，我們使用低深度Hi-C顯示番茄果實改變了與去甲基化胚乳組織相似的3D染色質結構。我們還進行了一項試驗性HiChIP實驗，以證明我們可以檢測增強子和近端啟動子染色質相互作用。因此，我們相信所提出的研究可以及時實現，並且它將從尚未探索的獨特染色質3D結構視角提供對果實成熟機制的寶貴見解。這將首次嘗試將表觀基因組變化與染色質3D結構聯繫起來，並將其動力學與實際生物學功能聯繫起來。

14104419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14104419.value: The aims of this 2-by-2 factorial, international, multi-center clinical trial are: (1) to determine the safety and efficacy of perioperative tranexamic acid administration to reduce surgical bleeding, and (2) to evaluate the effectiveness of a blood pressure management strategy that avoids hypotension to prevent postoperative vascular complications, in patients with, or at risk of cardiovascular disease, presenting for noncardiac surgery. Perioperative bleeding and hypotension are common adverse events that may lead to immediate death or trigger a cascade of complications. In our previous studies, postoperative bleeding accounted for 20.1-31.9% of perioperative deaths and increased the risk of sepsis and myocardial injury. Similarly, clinically important hypotension produced the largest population attributable risk for postoperative stroke and death. Therefore, proving the efficacy and safety of interventions to reduce surgical bleeding and assessing the effectiveness of strategies to avoid hypotension is a priority for research in the perioperative setting. We propose to conduct a non-inferiority trial to determine the efficacy and safety of tranexamic acid to reduce bleeding and transfusion after surgery. Using a partial factorial design, we will also carry out a superiority trial among patients in the same population taking antihypertensive medications before surgery, to compare the effect of a perioperative hypotension-avoidance strategy with standard care on postoperative vascular complications. In the standard care group, patients will continue to take their usual antihypertensive medications as per current guidelines. In the hypotension-avoidance group, we aim to avoid perioperative hypotension by limiting administration of antihypertensive medication and maintaining intraoperative mean blood pressure ≥ 80 mmHg. A total of 10,000 adult patients with known or at risk of cardiovascular disease having major noncardiac surgery will be enrolled. The primary outcomes are life-threatening, major and critical organ bleeding, and a composite of postoperative vascular complications or death within 30 days after randomization. Five hundred patients will be recruited in Hong Kong, and the requested funding is being sought to support local contribution to the trial. We anticipate the findings of this study will have considerable scientific, social and economic significance. Given that over 200 million of patients are having noncardiac surgery worldwide every year, an effective strategy to prevent postoperative bleeding and hypotension would spare 3 to 5 million of patients from devastating major vascular complications or death. As tranexamic acid is widely available, and our proposed strategy to avoid perioperative hypotension can be easily implemented, a positive finding could be readily translated into contemporary clinical practice. 是次2×2因子、國際性多中心的臨床研究旨在（1）確定於圍手術期給予患者氨甲環酸以減少手術出血的安全性和有效性，以及（2）評估一血壓管理措施對患有心血管疾病、或具有心血管疾病風險的患者進行非心臟手術時防止術後血管併發症的有效性。 圍手術期出血和低血壓為常見的不良事件，可導致患者突然死亡或引發一系列的併發症。我們的前期研究顯示，術後出血佔整體圍手術期死亡原因的20.1-31.9%，且同時會增加患敗血症和心肌損傷的風險。同樣，臨床上嚴重的低血壓是患者出現術後中風或死亡的最大原因。因此，圍手術期研究有迫切需要證明有效且安全的臨床幹預措施減少手術出血以避免患者出現低血壓。 因此，我們提出一項非劣效試驗來評估氨甲環酸對減少術後出血和輸血的有效性和安全性。我們將使用部分因子設計，於同一群患者中就術前服用降壓藥進行優勢試驗，以比較避免圍手術期低血壓的策略與標準治療對術後血管並發症的影響。在標準治療組中，患者將繼續按照現行指引服用其常用的降壓藥。在避免低血壓組中，我們的目標是通過限制降壓藥的使用，並維持術中平均血壓於 ≥80mmH，來避免圍手術期出現低血壓。 是次臨床試驗將招募10,000名將進行非心臟手術，並已知患有心血管疾病或具有心血管疾病風險的成年患者。我們的主要結局指標是在隨機分組後，出現危及生命重要器官出血、術後30天內血管併發症或死亡。我們將在香港招募500名患者，目前正在申請支持香港當地試驗所需要的經費。 我們強調是次研究成果將具有重要的科學，社會和經濟意義。鑑於全世界每年有超過2億的患者進行非心臟手術，提出有效預防術後出血和低血壓的策略將避免300萬至500萬名患者出現嚴重的血管併發症或死亡。由於氨甲環酸十分普遍，以及我們提出避免圍手術期低血壓的策略簡單易行，所以我們相信是次研究的正面成果能容易推廣並納入現行臨床工作。

14104419.label: Realisation of objectives
14104419.value: We have completed the Perioperative Ischemic Evaluation (POISE)–3 Trial. Between June 2018 to July 2021, a total of 9,535 patients having noncardiac surgery, and at risk of bleeding and vascular events, from 114 hospitals in 22 countries were recruited to the trial. This was about 95.3% of the originally planned sample size. However, given the rate of composite outcomes was higher than we previously estimated, the actual sample size provided adequate power (>90%) to evaluate our objectives: (1) Objective 1: In POISE-3, we have compared the rate of perioperative bleeding (life-threatening, major, and critical organ bleeding) in patients having tranexamic acid 1 g or saline ivi given at the start and then at end of surgery – a superiority analysis (2) Objective 2: we have compared the rate of composite vascular / safety outcomes (myocardial injury, stroke, peripheral arterial thrombosis, and symptomatic proximal deep venous thromboembolism) between tranexamic acid or saline administration – a non-inferiority analysis (3) Objective 3: we have also compared the effect of two perioperative blood pressure management strategies – hypotension-avoidance vs hypertension-avoidance on major vascular complications in a subset of 7,490 patients who were also enrolled to the factorial arm of the POISE-3 trial.

14104419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14104419.value: POISE-3 was an international, randomized, controlled trial evaluating: (1) the effects of tranexamic acid versus placebo in patients having noncardiac surgery; and (2) the effects of hypotension-avoidance versus a hypertension-avoidance strategy, among patients who were receiving ≥1 chronic antihypertensive medication, based on a partial factorial design (Trials 2022; 23: 101). The trial enrolled a total of 9,535 patients (tranexamic acid or saline). Among these patients, 7,490 were included in the factorial arm of the trial (hypotension-avoidance or a hypertension-avoidance strategy). In the main trial, we have shown that tranexamic acid reduced the risk of perioperative bleeding (9.1% vs 11.7%), absolute difference: 2.6%; 95% confidence intervals (CI): 1.4-3.8, hazard ratio (95% CI): 0.76 (0.67-0.87), two-sided p<0.0001 for superiority. Similar risk reduction was shown for bleeding associated with mortality, major bleeding or transfusion after surgery. Given that tranexamic acid may increase perioperative thrombosis due to its antifibrinolytic activity, we compared the major postoperative vascular events (including myocardial infarction, myocardial injury, stroke, pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis) in patients receiving tranexamic acid or saline. In POISE-3, vascular outcome occurred in 14.2% of patients receiving tranexamic acid and 13.9% who had saline, hazard ratio (95% CI): 1.023 (0.918-1.142). Since the upper bound of the one-sided 97.5% confidence intervals was above the prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.125. Therefore, noninferiority of major vascular outcome was not confirmed. However, the difference was small, absolute difference (95% CI): 0.3% (-1.1 to 1.7), p=0.044 for noninferiority. These data suggested that tranexamic acid reduced the risk of life-threatening, major, and critical organ bleeding in patients undergoing noncardiac surgery. Although tranexamic acid did not demonstrate noninferiority for major vascular (thrombotic) complications, tranexamic acid did not significantly increase the risk of any perioperative complication (N Engl J Med 2022; 386: 1986-1997). In patients having noncardiac surgery, who were using chronic antihypertensive therapy, a perioperative hypotension-avoidance strategy (by withholding perioperative hypertensive agents, and use of fluid, vasopressor and inotropic agents, aiming intraoperative mean arterial pressure ≥80 mmHg) did not differ from a hypertension-avoidance strategy (continuing antihypertensive agents, aiming mean arterial pressure ≥60 mmHg) regarding the effects on vascular death and nonfatal MINS, stroke, and cardiac arrest. Results also proved similar between the two strategies for other outcomes, including death, myocardial infarction, atrial fibrillation, congestive heart failure, and sepsis (Ann Intern Med 2023; 176: 605-614).

14104419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14104419.value: In addition to the hemostatic function, tranexamic acid by blocking the lysine-dependent production of plasmin, improves immune function and may reduce the risk of infection after major surgery. We are currently undertaking a prespecified planned analysis of the POISE-3 data to evaluate the effects of tranexamic acid on surgical site infection and sepsis. Similarly, we also wish to examine the effects of perioperative blood pressure control (hypotension-avoidance or a hypertension-avoidance strategy) on postoperative kidney injury (Can J Kidney Health Dis 2022; 9: 20543581211069225) and cognitive performance. We have already collected these data and the results will be reported in the near future. Our results are currently being discussed by a number of professional bodies and will be incorporated into guidelines for perioperative management.

14104419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14104419.value: Emerging research shows that bleeding and thrombosis are major contributors to postoperative outcomes. The POISE-3 trial was designed to assess whether tranexamic acid, a commonly available antifibrinolytic agent, could reduce bleeding. More than 9,500 patients were recruited to the trial from 22 countries. Compared with placebo, tranexamic acid unequivocally reduced the risk of major bleeding, postoperative transfusion or bleeding associated mortality. At the same time, there was very small risk of increase in thrombotic-related complications, such as deep vein thrombosis. In addition, we also examined whether continuing or stopping chronic antihypertensives before and after surgery, known as hypertension-avoidance strategy (aiming mean arterial pressure (MAP) ≥60 mmHg) or hypotension-avoidance strategy (aiming MAP≥80 mmHg), respectively. Overall, we found no difference between the two strategies for death, heart injury, stroke or cardiac arrest at 30 days after surgery. These data suggested that maintaining MAP≥60 mmHg is safe and that targeting higher MAP does not make a difference. Also, whether or not patients continued taking their antihypertensives did not impact on blood pressure or major cardiovascular complications. The POISE-3 trial provided a wealth of data to resolve two important perioperative management problems in how to reduce perioperative bleeding and management of blood pressure.

14105419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14105419.value: 肥胖會增加肝細胞癌（HCC）的發生，男性更容易受到肥胖的影響，引起包括脂肪變性和非酒精性脂肪肝炎（NASH）在內的非酒精性脂肪肝疾病（NAFLD）。在2016年GRF的支持下，我們的研究表明了細胞週期相關激酶（CCRK）在非酒精性脂肪肝相關肝癌中的重要作用。 CCRK是雄激素受體（AR）的直接下游癌基因，作為連接多條致癌信號通路的樞紐，驅動肝臟代謝的紊亂和肝臟抑制性免疫環境形成，從而營造一個適合HCC發生發展的肝臟微環境（ Nature Communications，2018）。從機理上來講，肥胖誘發的促炎症信號轉導及轉錄激活蛋白3（STAT3）與AR協同作用上調CCRK，從而激活哺乳動物雷帕黴素靶蛋白複合體1（mTORC1）信號通路，導致脂質代謝和糖代謝紊亂、抑制性免疫環境的形成以及腫瘤的發生。進一步了解NAFLD-HCC的肝臟環境中致癌信號通路激活、代謝紊亂以及免疫微環境相互作用的機制，將會為解決此類疾病治療的弱點開啟新的篇章。 最近，有關阻斷免疫檢查點療法的臨床I期及II期試驗的結果表明，免疫療法在HCC晚期病人中僅有17%-20%的客觀緩解率，如此低緩解率的背後原因之一就是抗腫瘤免疫防禦系統的缺失。在本項申請中，我們希望繼續探究這個新的研究領域，長遠目標是開拓免疫療法在HCC中的重要療效。我們檢測了高糖高脂飼料餵養後患有肥胖和NASH小鼠的肝臟免疫細胞群分佈，初步得到的實驗結果證實自然殺傷（NKT）細胞的減少，而且NKT細胞與CCRK-mTORC1信號通路的激活以及膽固醇的上調呈負相關。然後我們用處於臨床I／II期的mTORC1/C2激酶抑製劑vistusertib（AZD2014）處理小鼠，發現AZD2014不僅抑制了mTORC1／S6K／SREBP2信號通路，降低了膽固醇水平，而且回復了肝臟中NKT細胞的數量以及活性。然後我們使用了小鼠肝臟原位同種腫瘤移植模型，發現提前用AZD2014處理的小鼠的腫瘤生長受到顯著抑制。因此，在本項提議中，我們希望通過使用肝臟原位同種腫瘤移植模型和肝癌自發小鼠腫瘤模型進一步闡述CCRK-mTORC1信號通路如何通過調節免疫起到致癌性作用，尤其是解釋NKT細胞在其中的作用。與臨床上所觀察到的NASH病人提高的血液循環氨基酸水平一致的是，我們的數據也表明CCRK通過與氨基酸轉運載體相互作用，促使氨基酸誘導的mTORC1通路激活，同時我們也發現了膽固醇對NKT細胞的抑製作用。這項基金的繼續支持將會有助於我們進一步理解CCRK-mTORC1信號通路在NAFLD-HCC中影響免疫防禦的機制。在當今社會，肥胖作為快速增長的流行病因，導致NAFLD相關肝癌的發生率和致死率大大提升，我們的研究將為治療此類疾病所需要的有效免疫療法的發展提供理論基礎。

14105419.label: Realisation of objectives
14105419.value: For Objective 1, we have determined the effect of hepatic mTORC1/SREBP2 signaling on NKT activity in vivo, based on the experimental data that 1) inhibition of mTORC1/SREBP2 signaling by AZD2014 could reduce liver cholesterol level and enhance the anti-tumor cytolytic ability of NKT cells; 2) liver-targeting lentiviral-mediated short-hairpin (sh)RNA knockdown of SREBP2 decrease cholesterol biosynthesis on NKT cell-mediated antitumor immunosurveillance; 3) cholesterol-lowering rosuvastatin restored NKT expansion and cytotoxicity to prevent obesogenic diet-promoted HCC development. Moreover, we also confirmed the role of NKT cells on the anti-tumorigenic effect of AZD2014 in orthotopic NAFLD-associated HCC model.by showing that 1) NKT cell stimulation by αGalCer may inhibit HCC tumorigenicity in the NAFLD background; 2) NKT depletion would abolish the anti-tumorigenic effect of AZD2014 in this orthotopic NAFLD-associated HCC model. In addition, we validated the effect of AZD2014 on the pro-tumorigenic liver microenvironment in spontaneous NAFLD-associated HCC model. Collectively, all three tasks listed under Objective 1 in our proposal have been addressed. For Objective 2, we have determined the role of amino acid (AA) on the physical interaction between CCRK and SLC7A5/SLC3A2 transporters, as 1) we identified two AA transporters, solute carrier 7A5 (SLC7A5) and SLC3A2 as CCRK-associated proteins by Mass spectrometry analysis; 2) interaction between CCRK and AA transporters demonstrated by Co-IP; 3) AA stimulation relocates CCRK to plasma membrane and activates mTORC1 signaling in a CCRK-dependent manner. Moreover, we also elucidated that the underlying molecular mechanisms by which CCRK/mTORC1/SREBP2 signaling on NKT inactivation via cholesterol production, based on that 1) inducible expression of CCRK in LO2 cells increased cholesterol production, which was abolished by mTORC1/C2 inhibitor AZD2014; 2) CCRK also up-regulates SREBP2 in a mTOR-dependent manner. These data highlights CCRK/mTORC1/SREBP2/cholesterol-mediated NKT dysfunction in the tumor-promoting NAFLD liver microenvironment.

14105419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14105419.value: As obesity and diabetes reach epidemic proportions, non-alcoholic-fatty-liver-disease (NAFLD) increases as a global health problem and emerges as a major risk factor for HCC. Based on our previous findings, we hypothesize that CCRK-mTORC1 signaling inactivates NKT cells via aberrant cholesterol production, resulting in suppression of anti-tumor immune surveillance against HCC. To address this hypotheses, we utilized transgenic, orthotopic and spontaneous HCC mouse models. The major findings are described below: Using an inducible liver-specific transgenic model, we found that CCRK overexpression dramatically increased both melanoma and colorectal cancer (CRC) metastasis to the liver, which was highly infiltrated by polymorphonuclear-myeloid-derived suppressor cells (PMN-MDSCs) and lacking natural killer T (NKT) cells. Depletion of PMN-MDSCs in CCRK transgenic mice restored NKT cell levels and their interferon gamma production and reduced liver metastasis in the melanoma and CRC models, respectively. Mechanistically, CCRK activated nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-κB) signaling to increase the PMN-MDSC-trafficking chemokine C-X-C motif ligand 1 (CXCL1), which was positively correlated with liver-infiltrating PMN-MDSC levels in CCRK transgenic mice. Accordingly, CRC liver metastasis patients exhibited hyperactivation of hepatic CCRK/NF-κB/CXCL1 signaling, which was associated with accumulation of PMN-MDSCs and paucity of NKT cells compared to healthy liver transplantation donors. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that the enhanced metastatic tumor growth in CCRK-TG mice depends on PMN-MDSC accumulation, which was associated with a decreased NKT cell proportion and function in the liver (Zeng et al., Cellular & Molecular Immunology 2020). Furthermore, using high-fat high-carbohydrate diet-associated orthotopic and spontaneous NAFLD-HCC mouse models, we found that hepatic cholesterol accumulation in obesity selectively suppressed natural killer T (NKT) cell-mediated antitumor immunosurveillance. Transcriptome analysis of human liver revealed aberrant cholesterol metabolism and NKT cell dysfunction in NAFLD patients. Notably, cholesterol-lowering rosuvastatin restored NKT expansion and cytotoxicity to prevent obesogenic diet-promoted HCC development. Moreover, suppression of hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis by a mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitor vistusertib preceded tumor regression, which was abolished by NKT inactivation but not CD8+ T cell depletion. Mechanistically, sterol regulatory element-binding protein 2 (SREBP2)-driven excessive cholesterol production from hepatocytes induced lipid peroxide accumulation and deficient cytotoxicity in NKT cells, which were supported by findings in people with obesity, NAFLD and NAFLD-HCC. This study highlights mTORC1/SREBP2/cholesterol-mediated NKT dysfunction in the tumor-promoting NAFLD liver microenvironment, providing intervention strategies that invigorating NKT cells to control HCC in the obesity epidemic (Tang et al., Cellular & Molecular Immunology 2022).

14105419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14105419.value: We have uncovered a central role of mechanistic target of mTORC1, a master regulator of lipid homeostasis and growth control involved in diabetes and cancer, in mediating CCRK-dependent immune reprogramming in NAFLD-associated HCC. In particular, we found that natural killer T (NKT) cells, specialized CD1d-restricted T cells that recognize lipid antigens to activate both innate and adaptive immune cells in TME, may be specifically inactivated by the CCRK-mTOR signaling in NASH and HCC mouse models. Given the clinical use of mTOR inhibitors in the treatment of a number of different cancers, the recent developments of more potent and selective compounds and NKT cell-targeted cancer immunotherapies, the results of this project will provide insight into effective strategies to empower HCC immunotherapy in the midst of global obesity and diabetes. The continual delineation of the functions of CCRK-mTOR signaling will provide pharmacological proof-of-concept for the development of new combination immunotherapeutic strategies against NAFLD-associated HCC.

14105419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14105419.value: The major risk factors of HCC are undergoing a global transition, with the prevalence of hepatitis B and C viruses declining while obesity and diabetes increasing in many regions. Moreover, patients with non-viral HCC, in particular NAFLD-associated HCC, are less responsive to T cell-based immunotherapy targeted at PD-1 or its ligand PD-L1, possibly due to fatty acid-induced aberrant T cell activation causing tissue damage that impairs immune surveillance. Our results from obese mice and people provide a mechanistic linkage between mTORC1/SREBP2 activation, hepatic cholesterol accumulation, and impaired antitumor immunosurveillance in NAFLD. Our study also highlights the importance of manipulating mTORC1/SREBP2/cholesterol signaling cascade as an alternative strategy to prevent and treat HCC in the era of obesity epidemic.

14107719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14107719.value: Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are hepatic and carcinogenic phytochemicals widely produced by ~3% of flowering plants. Humans are exposed to PAs through the consumption of PA-producing herbs/natural products and PA-contaminated foodstuffs. Prolonged intake of low doses of PAs may cause liver cancer. However, it is a big challenge to assess the risk of human liver cancer associated with PA exposure. Hepatic metabolic activation of PAs produces pyrrole-protein or pyrrole-DNA adducts, causing hepatotoxicity, or gene mutations and liver cancer. Evidence from animal studies demonstrated that several PAs are genotoxic and tumorigenic, and induce gene mutations. However, to date, there are no epidemiological data on tumorigenesis of PAs in human, and the detailed mechanisms underlying PA tumorigenesis, such as specific genes mutated by PA exposure, remain largely unexplored. Recently, using our developed PA exposure biomarker, pyrrole-protein adducts, we found that ~32% (11/34) of liver cancer patients in Hong Kong exposed to PAs, indicating a high risk of PA exposure, which could potentially cause liver cancer. Nevertheless, this exposure biomarker alone cannot directly and definitively demonstrate PA-associated liver cancer. Moreover, we demonstrated that different PAs produced a same set of pyrrole-DNA adducts and their hepatic level correlated with liver tumor formation in animal models, suggesting that there is a common initiating mechanism for most/all carcinogenic PAs. Therefore, we believe that pyrrole-DNA adducts may initiate liver tumor through this common pyrrole-DNA adducts-mediated mechanism, and there may exist a mutational pattern specific to PA exposure. Considering the unrecognized potentially high prevalence of PA exposure in the liver cancer patients, it is significant and timely to understand mechanisms underlying PA-induced liver cancer, from PA-derived pyrrole-DNA adducts to gene mutations resulting in cancer development, identify mutational signature of PA exposure, and develop a specific method for illuminating the epidemiology of liver cancers associated with PA exposure. Therefore, in the proposed study, we aim to 1) investigate the PA-induced gene mutations and pathological processes of PA-induced liver tumor in cell and animal models; 2) identify mutational signature and recurrently mutated genes of PA exposure by gene sequencing in cell, animal and human samples; 3) evaluate PA exposure in liver cancer patients by our developed biomarkers; and 4) using the discovered PA mutational signature to assess PA-associated liver cancer in human. The results obtained will reveal the association of PA exposure with liver cancer and establish PA mutational signature for the risk assessment of PA-associated liver cancer in human. 吡咯裡西啶類生物鹼（PA）是一類存在於近3%有花植物中的肝臟毒素及致癌物質。人們常通過服用含有PA的草藥或植物和PA污染的食物而攝入PA。長期攝入低劑量的PA可致肝癌。然而，關於如何科學地評估PA暴露相關的肝癌，目前仍極富挑戰。 PA於肝臟中代謝產生吡咯-蛋白加合物和吡咯-DNA加合物，從而導致肝毒性和基因突變及肝癌。動物實驗證明，多種PA均具有基因毒性和致瘤性，可致基因突變。然而，到目前為止，仍然沒有PA致瘤的流行病學研究。具體的PA致瘤機制，如PA暴露所致的具體基因突變等，仍有待研究。近來，利用本課題組開發的PA暴露生物標識物，我們發現有近32% (11/34)的香港肝癌病人曾攝入過PA。結果提示了PA暴露的高風險及其潛在的致肝癌可能性。遺憾的是，僅靠此PA暴露生物標識物不能直接、確切地證明PA相關的肝癌發生。此外，我們證明了不同的PA均可產生一組相同的吡咯-DNA加合物，而且動物肝臟中的吡咯-DNA加合物含量與其肝臟腫瘤形成程度正相關，提示大多數或所有致癌性PA均可通過一個共同的啟動機制而致肝癌。因此，我們推測致癌性PA均可通過這種吡咯-DNA加合物介導的共同機制而引致肝腫瘤發生，並形成一個基於PA暴露的基因突變特徵譜。 考慮到肝癌病人中PA的潛在高暴露率，PA所致肝癌的相關機制研究已十分迫切，包括：從PA派生的吡咯-DNA加合物到基因突變所致的腫瘤發生、識別PA暴露的基因突變特徵譜，以及開發特異的方法用於PA暴露相關肝癌的流行病學研究。因此，本項目旨在：1）于細胞及動物水平研究PA引發的基因突變及PA所致肝癌的病理學過程；2）利用基因測序技術對所得細胞、動物及人類樣品進行測序，識別PA暴露的基因突變特徵譜及相關突變基因；3）利用本課題組開發的生物標識物，評估肝癌病人中的PA暴露風險；4）利用上述研究所得的PA暴露基因突變特徵譜，評定PA所致或相關的肝癌的發病率。預期的研究結果將揭示PA暴露與肝癌之間的關係，並建立PA暴露的基因突變特徵譜用於PA相關肝癌的風險評估。

14107719.label: Realisation of objectives
14107719.value: Liver cancer development is characterized by a complex exposure history affected by multiple environmental carcinogens. Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are a group of common phytotoxins with liver mutagenicity and tumorigenicity. Humans are frequently exposed to PAs via ingestion of PA-containing herbal remedies and PA-contaminated foods. In fact, the nontraceable PA contamination in various foods or dietary supplements makes people more often and unavoidably exposed to PAs. Therefore, due to the lack of human epidemiological data, whether PA exposure is correlated with human liver cancer is unexplored. In this project, we developed PA mutational signature as the biomarker to investigate the association of PA exposure in human liver cancer. We firstly revealed that upon metabolic activation, the reactive metabolites of PAs induced DNA damage and DNA repair in rat livers, providing the basis for mutagenesis. Next, we identified the mutational patterns associated with PA exposure in both cellular and animal models. Mice were exposed to retrorsine (RTS), a representative PA, for 14 weeks (RTS-14w) followed by a 30-week post-exposure period (a total of 10 months (RTS-10m)), to establish a mouse model of PA-induced staged liver tumorigenesis. Although the initial RTS-exposure for 14 weeks did not induce overt tumor lesions in mice, the RTS-exposed mouse livers had enriched hepatic progenitor cells (HPCs), which were demonstrated to be tumorigenic. This finding confirms that initial RTS-exposure promotes the malignant transformation of HPCs into tumor-initiating cells (i.e., cancer stem cells), which serve as the cellular niche for liver tumor development after cessation of RTS exposure. The findings were supported by the developed tumors found in RTS-10m mouse livers. To add more human relevance, we further exposed HepaRG cells (representing human hepatocytes) to RTS. To identify PA-induced mutation patterns, both mouse and human HepaRG cell samples were subjected for genomic DNA analysis. By comparing DNA sequence variations between PA-treated and control mice, we identified genetic alterations that occurred specifically due to PA exposure. Predominant G>N mutations were observed in RTS-exposed mice and HepaRG cells. Murine mutation spectra were highly comparable among premalignant RTS-14w liver samples, HPC-tumor samples, and RTS-10m tumor samples which represented key events of PA-induced liver tumor initiation and progression. The results support that PA-induced genetic alterations are the molecular basis driving oncogenic transformation of HPCs and switching on liver carcinogenesis. Additionally, RTS-exposed HepaRG cells demonstrated similar base substitutions compared with mouse samples, suggesting that RTS induced concordant mutation processes in humans and mice. Moreover, we found significant strand bias of the predominant G>T transversions on non-transcribed strands, which serves as an auxiliary indicator for PA-specific mutations. Overall, the abovementioned work provides comprehensive insights into distinctive mutation patterns underlying PA-induced hepatocarcinogenesis (Abstracts 1-2 and Papers 1-4 in Part C). With the clear understanding of cellular and molecular mode of action of PA-induced mutagenesis and tumorigenesis, we next explored the association between PA exposure and human liver cancer. Pyrrole-protein adducts (PPA), a PA exposure biomarker developed by our group, were measured in liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC) patients in Hong Kong. Utilizing our developed HPLC-MS analysis, we detected PPA in liver specimens of a limited number of HCC patients with 32% positive rate, suggesting a high and unrecognized prevalence of PA exposure in liver cancer patients. However, it should be noted that PPA detection can only indicate exposure history and is inadequate for inferring PA-related mutagenesis and tumorigenesis. At molecular level, PA-induced tumorigenic processes are believed to be initiated by the formation of pyrrole-DNA adducts (PDA) followed by DNA damage, which was observed in both RTS-exposed mouse livers and HepaRG cells. Our results confirmed that genotoxic effect of RTS laid the mechanistic basis for PA-induced genomic instability (Abstracts 1-4 and Papers 1 & 4-5 in Part C). We then compared experimental exome mutations to that from PA-related human HCC samples. Of note, the patients with detected PPA-positive HCC demonstrated mutation patterns similar to PA-exposed experimental models, whereas the mutation portraits of PPA-negative HCC samples significantly differed from PA specific mutation patterns. Consistent with the mutation spectra observations, PA-positive clinical HCCs exhibited a closer relationship with RTS-exposed HepaRG cells compared with PPA-negative HCC samples, which were unambiguously different from experimental and clinical PA-positive samples. The results indicated that PA-specific mutation spectra observed in PPA-positive human HCCs can serve as distinctive signature for identifying PA-related malignancies. Further, we developed PA mutational signature, characterized by predominant C>A, C>T, and T>C mutations, the imprint of PA-induced mutations with liver cancer relevance, by interrogating experimentally and clinically-derived PA mutation patterns. Collectively, the specificity validation of this signature in clinical PPA-positive HCCs reflects a reasonably uniform set of PA-induced mutational processes; thus, the characteristic mutation imprint is technically feasible to serve as the biomarker for screening the involvement of PAs in human liver cancers. Moreover, we successfully identified PDA in non-tumor patients poisoned by PAs, thereby enabling early tumorigenic risk management approach (Abstracts 3-6 and Papers 1-2 in Part C). Furthermore, we examined the established PA mutational signature in public database of human liver cancer genomes. A mutational signature in 193 of 398 HCCs (48%) from Mainland China, 34 of 78 HCCs (44%) from Hong Kong, 62 of 282 HCCs (22%) from Japan, 13 of 218 HCCs (6%) from South Korea, 7 of 28 HCCs (25%) from Southeast Asia including Singapore and Vietnam, 8 of 290 HCCs (3%) from North America including the United States of America (USA) and Canada, and 11 of 219 HCCs (5%) from European countries including France, Italy, and Spain. Apparently, the PA mutational signature was widely implicated in human HCC genomes in several Asian regions (especially China) but was found to be a minor component in North American and European data sets. Interestingly, our results appear to be consistent with the local PA intake characteristics. As the ingredients in herbal products, PAs have been restricted or banned in several countries including Germany, the United Kingdom, and USA. However, in China, which features the highest liver cancer burden and pervasive use of herbal medicine, no regulations are available for restricting PAs, despite the alarming number of liver injury cases related to the intake of PA-containing herbal supplements locally. Strikingly, four PA-producing plants (Symphytum officinale, Tussilago farfara, Circium japonicum, and Sculellaria barbata) are documented as medicinal herbs in China Pharmacopeia. Combined with our findings of chronic PA intoxication characteristics, patients who experience a short-term but high levels of PA exposure could potentially experience DNA damage and subsequently have a higher chance of developing PA-associated liver tumors. More importantly, as commonplace food contaminants, PAs are unregulated, less regionally specific, and likely present in various food products that are easily and widely accessible to the public. In European countries and USA, cases of PA poisoning, mostly due to inadvertent ingestions of PA-contaminated herbal teas or dietary supplements, have been reported sporadically but continuously. Thus, under common scenarios, people are frequently exposed to foodborne PAs to various extents, and the resultant chronic intoxications over prolonged periods are more prevalent instead of acute liver injuries. To address these health problems associated with untraceable PA exposure, the PA mutational signature, combined with or without PPA analysis, holds promise for regular monitoring of carcinogenic risks and diagnosis of liver tumors associated with PAs. (Abstracts 3-4 and Papers 1-2 & 4 in Part C).
