14107719.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107719.value: Chronic exposure to PA through contaminated food or herbal remedies has been linked to liver tumor in experimental settings, but the associated tumorigenicity in humans remained unclear. Mutational signature analysis is an effective tool in identifying cancer etiology. Therefore, this research project identified the mutational signature associated with PA exposure and assessing the implication of PA-induced liver cancer. Utilizing in vivo and in vitro experimental models, we conducted comprehensive investigation on PA-induced liver genotoxicity, mutagenicity, and tumorigenesis. In terms of the mode of tumorigenic action, PA exposure induced the malignant conversion of hepatic progenitor cells which serve as the cellular niche initiating liver tumorigenesis, therefore liver tumor developed long after the withdrawal of PA exposure. In addition, we revealed that PA exposure induced DNA adducts in both mouse livers and human liver cell lines, the molecular basis of PA-induced genotoxicity and tumorigenicity. We then delineated the association between PA exposure and human liver cancer by developing, validating, and applying the PA mutational signature. PPAs, the PA exposure biomarker, were measured and found in 32% of surgically resected specimens from 34 patients with liver cancer in Hong Kong. PA mutational signature, as the unique molecular fingerprint of PA-induced mutation, was derived from exome mutations in retrorsine-exposed mice and human HepaRG cells. Notably, PA mutational signature was validated in genomes of patients with PPA-positive liver cancer but not patients with PPA-negative liver cancer, confirming the specificity of this biomarker in revealing PA-associated liver cancers. Furthermore, we examined the established PA mutational signature in 1,513 liver cancer genomes and found that PA-associated liver cancers were potentially prevalent in Asia (Mainland China [48%], Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Southeast Asia) but minor in Western countries (North America and Europe). Overall, our findings provide the first evidence of PA exposure in liver cancer patients. By utilizing our newly identified PA mutational signature, we discovered an unexpectedly extensive implication of PA exposure in liver cancer patients. Therefore, this study provides a clinical implication of PA-associated liver cancer. We also discovered an unexpectedly extensive implication of PA exposure in patients with liver cancer, laying the scientific basis for precautionary approaches and prevention of PA-associated human liver cancers. Parts of the results have been published in scientific papers and/or reported in conferences (Papers 1-5, Abstracts 1-6 in Part C, Yun Long Thesis). Few more manuscripts reporting the above-mentioned findings are currently under preparation for future publication.

14107719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107719.value: The successful identification and application of PA mutational signature open several avenues for further development. These include investigating PA-induced genome-wide mutation patterns, frequently mutated genes, and broader application on pan-liver cancer genomes. Firstly, this research identified PA mutational signature based on Whole Exome Sequencing analysis, and further genome-wide sequencing can provide comprehensive information of PA-induced mutation patterns, adding more specificity and accuracy to the imprint of PA-induced mutation. Secondly, the mutated genes, particularly the activation of oncogene and the defunction of tumor suppressor genes, are the basis of tumor initiation and progression. Therefore, identification of frequently mutated genes, with special focus on oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes, and delineation of the mutated locus, can provide useful information of PA-induced tumorigenesis on a molecular basis. Thirdly, human liver carcinogenesis is reported to be associated with multiple tumor initiators and promotors, and thus, utilizing the strategy of our developed PA mutational signature can screen a diverse array of liver cancers with different etiologies. By taking these steps, further research can be advanced to not only deepen the scientific understanding of PA-induced hepatocarcinogenesis but also translate these findings into actionable strategies to reduce the burden of liver cancer associated with PA exposure.

14107719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107719.value: Natural toxins in medicinal products or foods are threats to public health, while it is challenge for the clinical identification of their resultant toxicities, particularly cancers. Pyrrolizidine alkaloids (PAs) are produced by ~6000 plant species worldwide and represent one of the most common phytotoxins to cause liver mutagenicity and tumorigenicity. Although people are readily exposed to PAs via the ingestion of PA-containing herbal remedies or widespread PA-contaminated food stuffs, it remains unknown whether PA exposure is correlated with human liver cancer. The mutational signature analyses have substantiated associations between liver cancer and environmental carcinogens such as aflatoxins and aristolochic acids. In this study, we developed PA mutational signature, which is the tell-tale imprint of PA-induced mutations, using a multisystem strategy comprising PA-induced mouse liver tumors and PA-exposed HepaRG cells (a human liver cell line). Notably, the distinct PA-induced mutations were also found in PA-related liver cancer patients, confirming the specificity of PA mutational signature for application in human samples. Moreover, by screening the public database of liver cancer genome, we found that PA exposure was widely implicated in human liver cancer, which warrants precautionary approaches for risk management of dietary exposure to carcinogenic PAs.

14107919.value: 研究背景：轉錄是RNA由DNA製成的過程。通過RNA聚合酶，細菌轉錄受到一系列因素的高度調節。“管家”轉錄起始因子sigma對於細菌生存是必需的，並且在已知細菌中有高度的同源性，同時在基因水平上不與對應的人類細胞轉錄因子同源。這使得sigma因子成為開發新型安全和有效抗菌藥物的有吸引力的目標。 知識差距填補：“超級細菌”（多重耐藥細菌）作爲重新出現的流行病病因，在全世界範圍內造成社會和經濟危機。因此，人類迫切需要具有新穎作用方式的抗菌藥物。細菌轉錄是一個有效的抗菌目標，然而它並沒有得到充分利用。目前使用的以轉錄為靶點的藥物僅有兩種（利福黴素和非達黴素）。 跟踪記錄和初步數據：本團隊首先報導了通過合理的設計，發現針對細菌轉錄的小分子抑製劑。本團隊化學合成了靶向RNA聚合酶與sigma因子之間的蛋白質 - 蛋白質相互作用的抑制劑化學衍生物庫（82個小分子），並加以評估。其中一些化合物具有針對臨床上顯著的病原體（包括金黃色葡萄球菌和肺炎鏈球菌) 的抗菌活性，其水平與一些上市的抗生素相當。這些化合物對人體細胞系具有低細胞毒性。 目的和假設：該提案的目的是針對先前開發的靶向細菌轉錄起始的抑製劑（抗SigA 化合物）的抗菌效果評估和機理研究。我們假設RNA聚合酶與sigma因子之間的蛋白質 - 蛋白質相互作用是新型抗菌藥物開發的可用靶點。 目標和方法： 1.檢查抗SigA化合物的抗微生物活性和細胞毒性特徵。 2.在分子水平上研究抗SigA化合物的機制。 3.在細胞水平上建立抗SigA化合物的機制。 預期結果：本研究將評估先前發現的抗細菌轉錄的小分子抑製劑的抗菌活性和細胞毒性，和其在分子和細胞水平上的機理研究。該提案將建立一個引領轉錄靶向抗生素發現研究領域的綜合平台。 長期結果：從該提案中獲得的信息將提供開發具有獨特新型作用方式的抗菌藥物的依據。從這項研究中獲得的抑製劑也可以作為標準試劑開發，用于探索sigma因子的功能的微生物學研究。

14107919.label: Realisation of objectives
14107919.value: Objective 1 was with excellent antimicrobial activities achieved. Based on the essential amino acid residues involved during the RNAP clamp helix (CH)-σ interaction, we previously constructed a pharmacophore model for in silico screens. The computational screen yielded a hit compound, C3 with modification potential, drug-like structure, and synthetic efficiency. In this work, we constructed a C3-series compound library consisting of over 300 candidates. Antimicrobial susceptibility tests were performed by the broth microdilution assay according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines. Some C3 analogues, especially C3-005, demonstrated drastically improved activity against S. pneumoniae from a MIC of 256 μg/mL to 8 μg/mL. Time-kill kinetic curves were constructed by administrating compounds to S. pneumoniae at various concentrations (¼, 1, 4, and 16 MIC) to evaluate in vitro antibacterial effects. C3-005 acted predominantly in a bacteriostatic manner at lower concentrations yet showed bactericidal effects at 16  MIC. ATP production assay, performed in parallel with the time-kill kinetic assay showed the reduced ATP level in the C3-005-treated S. pneumoniae cells, suggesting the arrest of cellular respiration. To evaluate cytotoxicity, human liver cancer HepG2 and A549 human lung carcinoma cell lines were cultured with C3-005 for 48 and 72 hours. MTT assay was performed to evaluate the cell viability. C3-005 showed no significant toxicity against the two human cell lines compared to the anticancer drug cisplatin. Thus, compound C3-005 was selected for structural optimisation. Most derivatives retained activity against the Gram-positive S. pneumoniae and S. aureus. Interestingly, the selected compounds demonstrated potent activity against S. epidermidis and S. saprophyticus with MICs ranging from 0.5 to 1 μg/mL, comparable to the last-resort antibiotic vancomycin. Since bacterial transcription inhibitors, rifampicin and fidaxomicin, are currently in clinical use for the management of C. difficile infections, our representative compound was also assessed for antimicrobial effects against C. difficile. Broth microdilution assay was performed by culturing bacterial cells in degassed BHI media with compounds anaerobically at 37 oC for 48 hours. The tested C. difficile type strain and clinical lineages were susceptible to our representative compounds. The shortlisted C3-005 derivatives were subjected to cytotoxicity study using the human liver and lung cancer cell lines. Compared to cisplatin, our compounds showed no significant toxicity. It suggested the structural modification improved antimicrobial activity but did not result in toxicity against human cells. Additional characterisation was performed for in vitro pharmacological evaluation via the haemolysis and Caco-2 permeability assay, respectively. Our compounds showed low haemolytic potential and good human intestinal epithelial cell permeability. These results implied the drug-like pharmacological properties of our C3 compounds. Objective 2 was completed by establishing the molecular mechanism of anti-SigA compounds, which were designed to mimic σ at its major RNAP binding site. A previously developed split luciferase-based assay was adapted for quantifying PPI inhibitions. During a specific PPI, two proteins with complementary tags are in close proximity for the reformation of a functional luciferase that catalyses light emission in the presence of substrate. PPI inhibition can be extrapolated by the decrease in luminescence signal. Purified RNAP CH fragment and σ tagged with the complementary luciferase fragments were treated with C3 compounds, and a substantial decline of luciferase activity was detected, suggesting the inhibition against RNAP CH-sigma interaction. Effects on RNA synthesis were tested under a purified transcription system in vitro. RNAP was supplied with nucleoside triphosphates (NTPs) with or without two selected C3 compounds, followed by the segregation of RNA products on a polyacrylamide gel. Compared to the untreated group, C3 compounds caused a decrease in RNA products. To verify the effects of compounds on RNAP subcellular localisation, B. subtilis strain BS1048 expressing the GFP-tagged beta subunit of RNAP was examined under a confocal microscope. While fluorescently tagged RNAP localised to the central chromosome-containing lumen of untreated cells, diffusion of fluorescent signal into the cytosol was observed at ½, 1, and 2  MIC. It reflected the delocalisation of RNAP and thus impaired RNAP functions. Most C3 compounds cannot be tested using isothermal titration calorimetry because of the insolubility under the experimental condition. Nevertheless, the inhibitory activity can be assessed by in vitro transcription assay. Objective 3 was succefully completed. S. aureus ATCC 29213 was cultured to the early log phase prior to the addition of C3 compounds or the well-characterised transcription inhibitor rifampicin at sub-MIC doses. Cells were harvested for extraction of total DNA, RNA, and proteins for quantitation. Compared to the drug-free control, both C3 compounds and rifampicin reduced the RNA level. To evaluate compound effects on the virulence of S. pneumoniae, the pneumococcal cells were grown to the early log phase supplemented with 5% CO2 in the BHI media before adding compounds or control drugs (rifampicin and ceftriaxone). After pelleting the cells, aliquots of supernatant were collected in the stationary phase for virulence protein secretory assay. Western blot was performed to detect the presence of pneumolysin by antibodies. While ceftriaxone stimulated toxin secretion, rifampicin and our compounds caused a substantial decrease in pneumolysin secretion compared to the untreated control group. The result suggested that C3 compounds were capable of attenuating the virulence of S. pneumoniae. Since a representative compound demonstrated anti-clostridial activity, the compound's impact on clostridial virulence was investigated. Following the broth microdilution assay to determine the MIC anaerobically, cells were pelleted by centrifugation, whereas their supernatants were collected for ELISA, by which clostridial cytotoxins TcdA and TcdB levels under different treatments were detected. In contrast to vancomycin which stimulated the toxin release, the transcription inhibitors C3 compound and fidaxomicin were able to suppress the production of both toxins TcdA and TcdB in the tested hypervirulent C. difficile strains. Intriguingly, at ½  MIC, the C3 compound could largely match the inhibitory effect of fidaxomicin. This suggested the therapeutic potential of C3 compounds for novel anti-clostridial agents. To enable the feasibility of further in vivo studies, the metabolic stability of C3 compounds was investigated. C3 compounds were incubated with rat liver microsomes, followed by the LC/MS/MS method to identify the remaining compounds. An average of 100% of compounds remained after incubation, whilst the control drug carbamazepine reduced to 45%. It suggested that our compounds were stable under an in vivo system with minimum metabolism.

14107919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14107919.value: The protein-protein interaction (PPI) between bacterial RNA polymerase (RNAP) and the housekeeping initiation factor sigma is essential to RNA synthesis and cell viability. It also represents a potential antibiotic target, for which we previously identified a hit compound, C3, through a pharmacophore-based computational screen. In this study, we biologically evaluated C3 and its rationally designed derivatives for new antimicrobial discovery. C3-series compounds demonstrated particular antimicrobial activities against a number of significant Gram-positive pathogens, especially pneumococci. Subsequent characterization revealed that C3 compounds suppressed bacterial growth in a bacteriostatic manner with a stronger suppression of the exotoxin pneumolysin release than the currently marketed drug tested. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated their inhibitory effects against RNAP CH-SigA PPI and transcription in vitro, as well as the disruption of RNAP localisation in cells. The result suggested the molecular mechanism of these compounds via the RNAP CH-SigA PPI disruption. No significant cytotoxicity was observed in human lung and liver cells. Following the hit-to-lead process, we assessed some rationally designed derivatives for their antimicrobial activities. A compound showed potent activity against S. epidermidis with a MIC of 0.5 μg/mL, matching that of the last resort drug vancomycin. Expanded antimicrobial spectrum were also observed. The representative compound showed antibacterial effects against Clostridioides difficile which may lead to lethal infections, and attenuated the release of clostridial cytotoxin Toxin A and B in the hypervirulent strains. It implied the potential of our C3 compounds as anti-clostridial agents. Mechanistic studies showed that those C3 derivatives retained the ability to target PPI inhibition and disruption of RNAP functions in cells without significant cytotoxicity in the two human cell lines. Additional characterization showed that our compounds exhibited very low toxicity to human blood cells, excellent human intestinal epithelial cell permeability, and high stability in rat liver microsomal metabolism assay. Data generated in this work suggested this series of compounds as promising candidates for further development towards novel antimicrobial agents with a new mode of action. Our pharmacophore model-based screening approach can also pave the way for discovering other potential drug targets, with a focus on bacterial transcription.

14107919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14107919.value: The antimicrobial compounds identified in this study have shown promising effectiveness against drug-resistant bacteria, which is a major problem in healthcare. Further development would involve conducting studies to understand the mechanism of action of these compounds and their impact on bacterial RNA synthesis, as well as optimisation of antimicrobial activities and drug-like properties. This would involve testing the compounds in different bacterial strains and assessing their effectiveness in treating infections, as well as further optimization and refinement of these compounds to enhance their efficacy and reduce toxicity and potential side effects. Further research can be conducted to evaluate the safety and efficacy of these compounds in animal models and eventually in clinical trials. Furthermore, the compounds can also be used as chemical probes to study the relationship between bacterial growth and the regulation of RNA synthesis. This can provide valuable insights into the fundamental processes of bacterial survival and potentially lead to the discovery of new targets for antimicrobial therapies. Overall, further development involves optimization, preclinical and clinical testing, and continued exploration of the compounds' mechanisms of action. This would pave the way for their potential development as new antibiotics and contribute to our understanding of bacterial biology.

14107919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14107919.value: The antimicrobial compounds created in this study have a unique target and a new way of fighting drug-resistant bacteria. This opens up possibilities for developing them into new antibiotics for medical use. The discovery of these compounds using computer-based screening also shows that this approach can be used to find other potential drug targets. In addition to their potential as treatments, these compounds can also be used to study how bacteria grow and regulate RNA synthesis, which is important for their survival. Overall, this research has significant value in the field of antibiotic development and understanding bacterial growth.

14108119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108119.value: Aim of Project: The aim of this project is to conduct research into carboxylesterase-mediated herb–drug interactions and to ascertain the impact of flavones on pro-drugs whose activation is mediated by carboxylesterase. Project Background: The number of drugs that are activated via carboxylesterase (CES) hydrolysis is significant and continues to grow with the development of new drugs whose absorption benefit from esterification modification on their structures. Although still a very nascent area of study, there is growing in vitro and in vivo evidence which suggests that CES hydrolysis is subject to many of the same issues of altered enzyme activity as the cytochrome P450 system and that it most likely represents a clinically important unrecognized reason for the variability of the therapeutic response in individual patients given CES substrate drugs. Evidence from others and ourselves indicates that alterations in hydrolytic activity by co-administered drug or herbal ingredients (especially flavones) may lead to alteration in not only the pharmacokinetics profiles of the pro-drugs but also the therapeutic efficacy or toxicity, which unfortunately lacks in-depth mechanistic investigations as well as clinical evaluations. Brief Project Description: In order to focus on exploring the clinically relevant CES-mediated herb–drug interactions, CES inhibition both on hCE1 and hCE2 substrate pro-drugs that have been reported for therapeutic monitoring in clinical practice by flavones, including baicalein, wogonin, oroxylin A and their corresponding dominant in vivo metabolites baicalin, wogonoside, and oroxylin A-7-glucuronide, will be investigated, aiming: (i) to screen for the potent inhibition of selected flavones on pro-drugs whose activation is mediated by CES, and (ii) to develop a whole body Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling based on the above identified potential herb–drug interaction in rats for further quantitative interpretation of the herb-drug interactions in-vivo. Significance of Project: Our proposed novel mechanistic-cum-PBPK modeling approaches are expected to clarify not only the role of CES hydrolysis in drug metabolism, and the factors that affect it, but also the subsequent therapeutic implications for the safe and effective use of pro-drugs that are the CES substrates. 本課題旨在研究由羧酸酯酶介導的中西藥相互作用，主要著重於研究黃酮對經羧酸酯酶激活的前體藥物的影響。 在新藥研發過程中，羧酸酯修飾的化合物常被採用來增強藥物的體內吸收。因此，此類經體內羧酸酯酶激活的前體藥物在新藥研發中越來越多。體內的羧酸酯酶和肝內CYP450酶一樣會受各類因素的影響而改變，從而導致藥物在體內的活性反映不一。我們及其他研究者均發現藥物和天然產物可以改變體內羧酸酯酶的活性，從而導致藥物代謝動力學甚至是相關前體藥物的活性及毒性的改變。然而，此類改變的機制及臨床研究仍然十分缺乏。 為了探尋臨床相關的羧酸酯酶介導的中西藥相互作用，我們選擇了一系列黃酮化合物及經羧酸酶激活的前體藥物用以以下研究1）以相關的前體藥物為底物，從黃酮中篩選出有效的羧酸酯酶的抑制劑；2）基於發現的黃酮類羧酸酯酶抑制劑和前體藥物的在大鼠體內相互作用，開發一種生理藥代動力學模型用以定量評估其體內的影響。 我們首次提出的兼顧機制及模型的研究方法不僅可以闡明羧酸酯酶在藥物代謝中的重要角色及其相關的影響因素，而且有助於我們評估其帶來的藥效的改變。該研究對於臨床中頻繁應用的前體藥物的安全及有效使用具有重大意義。

14108119.label: Realisation of objectives
14108119.value: To screen for the potent inhibition of selected flavones on pro-drugs, we have conducted a series of screening for flavone inhibition on CES-mediated hydrolysis of pro-drugs in rat plasma, intestine and liver microsomes with the following highlights:  A novel and rapid bioluminescence assay using NLMe as the selective CES1 bioluminescent sensor with sufficient sensitivity and convenience has been developed and validated for monitoring CES1 activity in various tissues of rats.  OXA and B demonstrated stronger inhibitions than the others on CES1-mediated NLMe hydrolysis and B showed the strongest inhibition among the studied six flavones on CES2-mediated NCEN hydrolysis, respectively. To further evaluate the inhibition effectiveness of OXA and B, dose-response inhibition curves of the two flavones on NLMe and NCEN hydrolysis in rat plasma, intestine and liver S9 were generated. Both B and OXA showed potential inhibitory activities toward CES1 and CES2.  Our further docking analysis suggests that OXA and B would exhibit the strongest inhibitory effect on hCE1, while the inhibitory effect for OXA, B and W on hCE2 should be similar.  Both the in-vitro incubation study and docking analyses consistently indicated that B and OXA demonstrated strongest inhibition on irinotecan among all the studied flavones and pro-drugs. To quantitatively interpret the in-vivo impact of above mentioned herb–drug interactions, a series of in-vivo animal studies and in-vitro mechanistic studies have been conducted to provide key parameters for PBPK model building with the following highlights:  Rats from eight groups (G1 to G8) were administered with the selected western drug irinotecan (IV) in absence or presence of the selected flavones of B or OXA (IV/PO) daily for 5 consecutive days. To evaluate the impact of co-administered B or OXA on plasma concentrations of irinotecan and SN-38, eighteen rats were randomly divided into six groups (G1-G6, n= 3/group) to receive irinotecan (IV), B and OXA (IV/PO). In G1-G3, two hours before the IV administration of irinotecan (0.07 μmol/kg), rats received IV pre-treatment of water (G1, vehicle), B (2.80 μmol/kg, G2) or OXA (2.80 μmol/kg, G3), respectively. In G4-G6, two hours before the irinotecan treatment (IV, 35 μmol/kg), rats received PO pre-treatment of water (G4, vehicle), B (2800 μmol/kg, G5) or OXA (2800 μmol/kg, G6), respectively. On day 4, after drug administration, jugular vein cannulation was conducted to the rats in G1-G6 followed by fasting for 12 h with free access to water. On day 5, blood samples were collected via the jugular vein at 0.083, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4 and 6 h after the last dosing and then all the rats were sacrificed. Another eighteen rats were divided into two groups (G7 and G8, n=3 for each observation time point at 0.5, 2 and 5h post dosing) for irinotecan tissue disposition evaluation. At two hours before the irinotecan administration (IV, 35 μmol/kg), rats in G7 and G8 received PO pre-treatment with water and OXA (2800 μmol/kg), respectively. On day 5, rats in G7 and G8 were sacrificed at 0.5 h, 2 h and 5 h after irinotecan administration followed by collecting of blood and tissues including liver, lung, kidney, and intestine for analyses with the following findings: - Oral pre-treatment with B significantly changed the AUC0-6h of both SN-38 and irinotecan (p<0.001 for decreased SN-38 and increased irinotecan), while OXA oral pre-treatment significantly decreased the AUC0-6h of SN-38 (p<0.001) with no significant change on that of irinotecan. Furthermore, significant decreases of the SN-38/irinotecan concentration ratios were found in oral pre-treatment groups of both B and OXA with a more significant trend in that from OXA. - Further evlautions on various tissues obtained from the above mentioned in-vivo studies identified that significant inhibitions on CES2 activities in the intestine were observed at both 0.5h and 5h post irinotecan dosing in OXA pre-treatment group, while trends of decreasing CES2 activities in liver and lung were also observed at 5h post irinotecan administration in OXA pre-treatment group. In addition, tissue distribution of irinotecan and SN-38 in major organs suggested that i) both irinotecan and SN-38 were highly accumulated in intestine after its IV administration and ii) OXA could significantly reduce such accumulation in intestine, especially for those of SN-38 possibly due to its inhibition on the CES2-mediated hydrolysis of irinotecan. - Our further analyses on CES2, PXR and CAR expression in rat intestine indicated a potential upregulation of CAR and downregulation of PXR in response to irinotecan treatment, which could be restored by the co-administered OXA.  To provide the inhibition kinetics parameters for PBPK model, metabolic kinetics of Irinotecan and CES inhibition kinetics of OXA were conducted. Briefly, the in vitro incubation studies were carried out in 200 μL mixtures containing irinotecan (2.5, 5, 10 and 20 μM), rat plasma/intestine S9/liver S9 (1mg/mL) with 15 minutes pre-incubation in the absence and presence of OXA (50 and 200 μM) at 37°C for 30 min followed by determination of the SN-38 formation. The Lineweaver–Burk plot reflected the competitive inhibition on irinotecan metabolism by OXA in rat plasma, intestine, and liver S9. OXA demonstrated the strongest inhibition on the formation of SN-38 from irinotecan in rat plasma with a Ki of 3.107 μM, suggesting a potential decrease on the plasma concentration of the active metabolite of irinotecan and the subsequent efficacy when it was co-administered with OXA.  In addition, it was noticed that the presence of OXA significantly enhanced the unbound fractions of irinotecan in rat plasma and rat intestine S9 (p <0.05).  To build the PBPK model, pharmacokinetics data of irinotecan and SN-38 from our current study and those of OXA from literature were used. Tissue distribution of irinotecan and SN-38 were used for model validation. The modeling and simulations were carried out with PK-SIM® version 11.1. Physicochemical properties (LogP, pKa, fup and solubility) of irinotecan, SN-38, SN-38 glucuronide, OXA and OAG were taken from Drugbank or SciFinder. Unbound fraction (fup) values of each analyte were predicted with fu,p Predictor if they were not available from the literature. Enzyme expression profiles of CES2, UTG1A1, P-gp and BCRP were estimated from the reported relative enzyme activities or by assuming the same levels of expression in major tissues if no supporting data was available. The kinetics of these enzymes and transporters were defined using Vmax and Km in rat liver microsomes or estimated with PK-SIM®’s parameter identification. The best methods for partition coefficients of each compound were also determined through parameter identification. Sensitivity analyses were performed for all the parameters of the PBPK model of each compound to identify critical parameters of the models. Visual predictive check interval was obtained by checking the “Calculate Sensitivity” during parameter identification. The PK-Analysis in PK-SIM® was used to calculate non-compartmental analysis PK parameters for the observed and simulated PK profiles. Our PBPK model for OXA could closely predict its plasma concentration at three dose levels with the Cmax and AUC0-t of the simulated PK profiles all within 2-fold changes in comparison to the observed data. PBPK model of irinotecan was also developed and linked with that of OXA via Ki of OXA to further illustrate their interactions.

14108119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108119.value: To screen for the potential inhibition of selected flavones on pro-drugs whose activation is mediated by CES, we first developed a novel and rapid bioluminescence assay using NLMe as the selective CES1 bioluminescent sensor with sufficient sensitivity and convenience for monitoring CES1 activity in various tissues of rats. Both the in-vitro enzyme incubation studies and docking analyses indicated that B and OXA demonstrated strongest inhibition on irinotecan in all investigated carboxylesterases containing matrix and would be selected for the follow up experiments among all the studied flavones and pro-drugs. To develop a whole body PBPK modelling based on the above identified potential herb–drug interaction in rats to quantitatively interpret its impact, a series of in-vivo animal studies and in-vitro mechanistic studies have been conducted to provide key parameters for PBPK model building. It was noticed that significant decreases of the SN-38/irinotecan concentration ratios were found in oral pre-treatment groups with both B and OXA with a quicker and bigger decreasing trend in that from OXA pre-treatment. In addition, tissue distribution of irinotecan and SN-38 in major organs suggested that i) both irinotecan and SN-38 were highly accumulated in intestine after its IV administration and ii) OXA could significantly reduce such accumulation in intestine, especially for those of SN-38 possibly due to its inhibition on the CES2-mediated hydrolysis of irinotecan. The Lineweaver–Burk plot reflected the competitive inhibition on irinotecan metabolism by OXA in rat plasma, intestine, and liver S9. Based on the Ki value, OXA demonstrated the strongest inhibition on the formation of SN-38 from irinotecan in rat plasma with a Ki of 3.107 μM, suggesting a potential plasma concentration decrease of the active metabolite of irinotecan and the subsequent decrease in efficacy when co-administered OXA with irinotecan. In addition, it was noticed that the presence of OXA significantly enhanced the unbound fractions of irinotecan in rat plasma and rat intestine S9. Our final integrated PBPK model could successfully predict not only the PK profiles of irinotecan and SN-38 after IV administration of irinotecan but also their inhibited PK profiles in presence of OXA with the observed data within the 5th-95th percentile of predicted PK profiles and the fold errors for pharmacokinetics parameters ranging from 0.99 to 1.27. With the PBPK model, we for the first time indicated that the inhibition of CES2-mediated irinotecan hydrolysis in intestinal mucosa could be the underlying mechanism for the pharmacokinetics interaction between irinotecan and OXA.

14108119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108119.value: Our developed novel and rapid bioluminescence assay using NLMe as the selective CES1 bioluminescent sensor can be further utilized to monitor the CES activities in human plasma and other tissue samples. In addition, our findings on significant inhibition on the formation of active metabolite of irinotecan by co-administered OXA could provide clinical guidance to avoid the combination use of irinotecan with herbs/supplement containing flavones of B and OXA. Moreover, our novel PBPK model for illustration of the underlying mechanism for the pharmacokinetics interaction between irinotecan and OXA could also be applicable for the other herb-drug interactions. Our current established novel mechanistic-cum-PBPK modeling approach not only clarify the role of CES inhibition in the CES-mediated herb-drug interactions but would also be applicable for other enzyme-mediated herb-drug interactions, whose pharmacokinetic properties and mechanisms of actions are well identified, and it can be verified by using well-established in-vitro screening technologies.

14108119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108119.value: As more herbs are used in daily life, the safety of co-administering herbs and Western drugs should receive greater attention. Although benefiting from improved absorption, significant numbers of drugs are being developed as pro-drugs with esterification modification on their structures that will be activated via CES hydrolysis in-vivo to release the active drug, there is growing evidence which suggests that CES hydrolysis is subject to altered enzyme activity by other co-administered drugs or herbs, which could be the unrecognized reason for the variability of the therapeutic response in patients given pro-drugs. The current project was proposed aiming to investigate mechanisms of CES inhibition by reported herbal flavones, including B, W, OXA and their corresponding dominant in vivo metabolites BG, WG, and OAG, on pro-drugs that have been reported for therapeutic monitoring in clinical practice. Our in-vitro screenings firstly identified that herbal flavones B and OXA had strongest inhibition on irinotecan. Our in-vivo studies with developed mechanistic model further demonstrated the most significant decreases in the active metabolite formation of irinotecan by orally co-administered OXA with the inhibition of CES2-mediated irinotecan hydrolysis in intestinal mucosa as the major underlying mechanism, suggesting such combination use would be recommended for clinical practice.

14108219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108219.value: 隨著對腫瘤免疫學的深入研究，以免疫檢查點抑制劑（immune checkpoint blockade，ICB)為代表的免疫治療在多種實體瘤中被證實可以起到治療，甚至治愈的效果。然而，在存在強免疫抑制微環境的肝細胞癌（Hepatocellular carcinoma，HCC)中，ICB的治療效果也就差强人意了。目前在對HCC腫瘤微環境的研究中發現，髓源性抑制細胞（myeloid derived suppressor cell，MDSC)作爲維持抑制性免疫微環境和介導腫瘤免疫逃逸的主要調控細胞之一,可以通過抑制淋巴細胞，特別是殺傷性T細胞應答和增殖，發揮强大的免疫抑制功能。MDSC是一種來源於骨髓的未成熟髓細胞組成的異質性細胞群，在 癌症病人中與其存活率以及對ICB的抗藥性成正相關。所以， MDSC的靶向藥物，特別是促進MDSC進一步分化成抗原呈遞細胞的藥物將對腫瘤的免疫逃逸其重要的抑制作用。因此，進一步揭示MDSC的增殖和分化的作用機制對研發創新性MDSC的靶向藥物有至關重要的作用。 细胞周期蛋白依赖性激酶家族（cyclin-dependent kinases，CDKs)的靶向藥物是目前癌症治療中重要的組成部分。申請人的前期研究發現，CDKs家族中最新成員細胞周期激酶20（CDK20/cell-cycle related kinase, CCRK）可以激活腫瘤細胞内的致癌信號通路，並介導白介素6的釋放，從而誘導MDSC的擴增和在腫瘤微環境中的聚集。基因敲除CCRK可以明顯減少血液、肝臟以及腫瘤微環境中的MDSC，從而增强殺傷性T細胞的數量和功能，有效抑制腫瘤的發展並顯著性增强ICB在HCC中的治療效果 (Gut 2018)。鑒於其他CDKs在免疫細胞内的信號轉導和功能中也有重要的調節作用，所以我們對CCRK的作用和功能進行了進一步的研究。前期的研究顯示HCC的小鼠模型和病人樣本中的MDSC有特異性的CCRK高表達，而基因敲除CCRK可以促進MDSC向抗原呈遞細胞的分化以及增强T細胞的增殖和殺傷功能。在HCC小鼠模型中，基因敲除CCRK可以抑制腫瘤的生長。從分子機理上來説，基因敲除CCRK可以抑制MDSC中主要的轉錄因子STAT3/E4BP4信號通路，從而控制在髓樣細胞分化中起重要作用的白介素10/12。因此，我們認爲MDSC中過表達的CCRK可以激活STAT3/E4BP4信號通路來控制MDSC的免疫抑制功能，從而介導腫瘤的生長和調節ICB在HCC中的治療效果。在本研究計劃中，我們將應用已經建立的HCC小鼠模型對靶向MDSC中CCRK信號通路的腫瘤抑制效果進行進一步的闡述。同時深入研究CCRK信號通路在MDSC的免疫抑制以及分化中的分子機理和功能。最後，在ICB耐藥的HCC小鼠模型中測試聯合CCRK抑制劑的治療效果。鑒於HCC病人MDSC中CCRK也有過表達，本項研究結果可以部分反應病人中免疫逃逸的機制，從而創新性的揭示MDSC分化和作用的分子機理。我們期望這種特異性針對MDSC的藥物能在聯合免疫治療中對HCC的臨床治療中起到指示和應用效果。

14108219.label: Realisation of objectives
14108219.value: The project objectives have been successfully completed. For objective 1, we have determined the role of CCRK signaling in MDSC-mediated tumor immunosuppression and development in vivo based on the experimental data that 1) knockdown of Ccrk by lentivirus-based shRNA in bone marrow (BM)-MDSCs induced the differentiation of these cells into antigen-presenting macrophages, representing by increased CD80/CD86 and IL-12 expressions in naïve and tumor-bearing mice in vivo; 2) intratumoral injection of BM-MDSCs with low Ccrk expression resulted in enhanced anti-tumor T cell responses indicating by increased IFN-g production and proliferation ability, leading to reduced tumor growth in vivo; 3) in reverse, over-activation of Ccrk induced by tamoxifen in human Ccrk-expressed transgenic mice lead to increased MDSC accumulation and immunosuppressive activity, which resulted in reduced anti-tumor T cell responses and increased tumor development and metastasis in vivo. For objective 2, we have confirmed that CCRK could trigger the activation of STAT3/E4BP4 signal to induce immunosuppression in myeloid cells as 1) CCRK promoted STAT3 activation by phosphorylating STAT3, in which the p-STAT3 then bound to the promoter region of E4BP4 for its upregulation; 2) knockdown of E4BP4 could abolish the CCRK/STAT3-mediated immunosuppressive features in myeloid cells; 3) the unregulated E4BP4 in CCRK over-expressed myeloid cells transcriptional controlled the expression of IL-10 and IL-12 via promoter binding. Collectively, our data demonstrated that CCRK determined MDSC phenotype and immunosuppression by controlling IL-10/IL-12 balance via STAT3-mediated E4BP4 transcriptional activity. For objective 3, we have determined the therapeutic potential of targeting myeloid CCRK and MDSCs together with anti-PD-L1 treatment in vivo as 1) lentivirus-mediated Ccrk knockdown in MDSCs resulted in reduced tumor growth compared to lentivirus control, independent of tumoral-CCRK expression; 2) we have successfully generated a transgenic mouse model bearing Ccrk indel mutation (Ccrk indel/indel), which showed inactivated CCRK pathway in myeloid cells in vivo. Compared to wild-type C57BL/6 mice, orthotopic tumor growth was significantly restricted and survival rate was remarkably prolonged in Ccrk indel/indel transgenic mice, accompanied by increased accumulation of antigen-presenting macrophages and IFN-g and TNF-a releasing T cells in the tumors; 3) clinical-in-used chemotherapy drug 5-Fu which was able to induce MDSC recruitment in the tumor microenvironment could abrogate the therapeutic efficacy of anti-PD-L1 in vivo, further confirmed the importance of MDSC in immunotherapy resistance; 4) constructed two anti-PD-L1 resistant HCC tumor cell lines through serial orthotopic implantation into C57BL/6 immunocompetent hosts for anti-PD-L1 therapy, and observed an improved survival in Ccrk indel/indel transgenic mice bearing anti-PD-L1 resistant orthotopic tumors by anti-PD-L1 treatment compared to wild type controls. Finally, we observed that the cross-talk between MDSCs and anti-tumor lymphocytes in controlling tumor growth of different cancer models showed differences. Our in vivo data showed MDSCs with low Ccrk expression led to reduced subcutaneous tumor growth accompanied by increased CD8+T cell accumulation in the tumor microenvironment. In parallel, over-activation of Ccrk induced by tamoxifen resulted in aggressive tumor growth via intrahepatic injection, which was associated with MDSC accumulation and reduced CD8+T cells. When we used the intrasplenic injection to establish liver metastasis models, although over-activation of Ccrk lead to increased metastatic tumor growth, natural killer T (NKT) cells instead of CD8+T cells were negatively correlated with tumor growth. Taken together, these data showed that CCRK may regulate different aspects of MDSC phenotype and functions. The parallel analysis of different lymphocytes was included in the initial proposal under “Alternative hypotheses and complementary approaches” to fully understand the importance of the CCRK signals in modulating different functions of MDSCs. In summary, our findings not only unravel mechanistic insights of CCRK in determining MDSC expansion, differentiation and different functions, but also offer a novel therapeutic kinase target for cancer immunotherapy.

14108219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108219.value: This project aims to identify potential therapeutic targets for cancer immunotherapy based on mechanistic insights from tumor immunosuppression. With a focus on tumor-associated MDSCs, we have uncovered the importance of CCRK in tumor immunosuppression by modulating MDSC expansion, differentiation, and immunosuppressive function. Our findings demonstrated that targeting MDSCs via inhibiting CCRK signal could potentiate anti-tumor adaptive immune responses, limit tumor progression and prolong survival. The major findings and research outcome are described as follows: 1. Using clinical-relevant orthotopic HCC mouse models, we found that the clinical-in-used chemotherapy drug 5-Fu can promote MDSC recruitment in the tumor microenvironment to abrogate the therapeutic efficacy of anti-PD-L1. Importantly, similar MDSC accumulation and impaired anti-tumor adaptive immunity were also observed in HCC patients under chemotherapy, which provides additional evidence to support our focus on MDSC in tumor immune escape and immunotherapy resistance (Kwong et al., JH Reports 2021). 2. Overexpression of CCRK induced MDSC accumulation and immunosuppression on anti-tumor NKT cells, resulting in aggressive progression of metastatic liver cancers in an inducible CCRK transgenic mice. Depletion of MDSCs in these CCRK transgenic mice could therefore restore the NKT cell levels and their IFN-g production to control liver metastasis. As the CCRK and MDSCs are concordantly upregulated in patients with liver metastasis, our findings demonstrate that immunosuppressive myeloid cell reprogramming by CCRK signaling undermines the anti-metastatic immunosurveillance (Zeng et al., CMI 2021). 3. In addition, we uncovered a myeloid-specific CCRK upregulation in mice and patients with HCC. Using the lentivirus-mediated knockdown strategy to modulate CCRK expression in MDSC, our data demonstrated that myeloid CCRK expression is essential for the maintenance of MDSC features and immunosuppressive function, in which CCRK knockdown skewed MDSC differentiation towards antigen-presenting macrophage-like phenotypes. Mechanistically, CCRK activated STAT3 to revert E4BP4-dependent transcriptional regulation on the expressions of immunosuppressive molecules. Furthermore, we constructed a new transgenic mouse strain with host-Ccrk inactivation by introducing an indel mutation into the exon 2 of the Ccrk genome. Our findings further validated that host Ccrk inactivation resulted in tumor reduction and prolonged survival in orthotopic-HCC models by reprogramming the immunosuppressive myeloid cells. Therefore, our data unravel mechanistic insights on MDSC-mediated tumor immunosuppression and offer a potential therapeutic kinase target for cancer immunotherapy (Zhou et al., manuscript under preparation). Taken together, the results from this project further highlighted the importance of MDSCs in cancer immune escape and pointed out that CCRK may serve as a potential therapeutic target (Zeng et al., Cancers 2021).

14108219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108219.value: Based on the data generated in the current project, we uncovered the essential role of His73 and Gly74 (located in the exon 2) in determining the function of myeloid Ccrk. Through the established collaboration with Oxford University, Sussex University, and Cardiff University in the Structural Genomics Consortium, we will continue working on the delineation of the 3D structure and specific inhibitors of CCRK. In addition, we showed that CCRK expression may not only regulate primary cancer development but also function in controlling liver metastasis by modulating different functions of MDSCs. Therefore, we will also further study the tumor-myeloid cell interaction that may be modulated by the CCRK signaling. Furthermore, recent clinical findings pinpointed that the presence of liver metastasis correlates with a diminished responding rate and poor survival in advanced cancer patients treated with current immunotherapy approaches. Therefore, we will explore to the potential of targeting myeloid CCRK in overcoming liver-metastasis-related immunotherapy resistance using our established orthotopic and transgenic mouse models. These results may provide proof-of-concept for the development of new combination immunotherapeutic strategies in different cancers.

14108219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108219.value: Myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) are one of the fundamental features of malignant tumors and treatment strategies that target MDSCs have shown promising outcomes in both preclinical studies and clinical trials. MDSCs undergo massive expansion during tumor progression and maintain the immature and immunosuppressive status to support tumor immune escape. In the project, we have uncovered an important role of cell cycle-related kinase (CCRK), the latest member in the cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) family, in promoting MDSC expansion, immunosuppression, and immature status maintenance. Using multiple clinical-relevant orthotopic mouse models and in-house constructed CCRK transgenic mice, our data demonstrated that inhibition of the CCRK pathway could restrict tumor progression and metastasis by regulating the phenotype and function of MDSCs in vivo. Clinical-in-used chemotherapy drugs may abrogate the clinical benefits of current immunotherapy approaches by inducing MDSCs in liver cancer patients. As we also showed the activation and upregulation of CCRK/MDSCs signatures in human cancer patients, the findings of our study not only unravel mechanistic insights into MDSC-mediated cancer immune escape, but may also offer a novel therapeutic kinase target for cancer immunotherapy in the future.

14108719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14108719.value: 多發性骨髓瘤（MM）是一種現時無法被根治的漿細胞惡性腫瘤。雖然蛋白酶體抑製劑（PI）（例如硼替佐米（BTZ）、卡非佐米（CFZ））的應用顯著改善了患者的預後，但遺憾的是，由於帶有對PI耐藥性的癌細胞克隆形成，幾乎所有病人都要經歷疾病的複發。早期有研究表明，耐藥性可能由蛋白酶體亞基的基因突變或蛋白酶體增強造成，但與此矛盾的研究結果也有被報導。因此，潛在的機制尚不明確，相關的藥物靶點仍有待深入研究。 PI通過內質網應激誘導細胞凋亡從而抑制MM細胞生長，是廣泛認可的機制。但也有研究報導BTZ也可以促進MM細胞生長，增強細胞惡性。內質網應激除了誘導凋亡，還激活“活化T細胞核因子”（NFAT）信號通路。已經有越來越多的癌症相關研究證明了NFAT信號通路在腫瘤形成和藥物耐藥方面的重要性。我們發現MM具有獨特的NFAT調控因子和信號傳導介質表達模式，而這種表達模式是會激活NFAT信號通路的，這提示了NFAT信號通路可能參與了骨髓瘤的腫瘤形成。此外，在一個接受單一BTZ治療的病人研究裡面，我們發現，預後較差的MM群組具有比較活躍的NFAT信號通路，這提示了NFAT具有影響BTZ療效的功能。 通過研究PI對NFAT信號通路的作用，我們在MM細胞中發現兩種PI類藥物都能誘導NFAT核轉移，並且BTZ可以增加NFAT的基因轉錄活性。 BTZ可上調與NFAT相關的抗凋亡基因BAG3和DDIT4的表達，這兩個基因也參與細胞自噬而應付內質網應激的。 因此，我們也發現BTZ能夠誘導MM細胞自噬。這些初步研究結果證明了抑制蛋白酶體可以激活NFAT信號通路，從而激活抗凋亡和促細胞適應的信號通路，賦予MM細胞對BTZ的耐藥性。 為了加強NFAT信號通路作為治療靶點的效果，在使用PI的同時聯合使用NFAT抑製劑/NFAT上游的鈣調磷酸酶抑製劑，可加強BTZ/CFZ引起的內質網應激誘導的細胞凋亡，最終增強BTZ/CFZ介導的抑制MM細胞生長的作用。內質網應激標誌物上調和抗凋亡基因BCL2下調可以證明這個機制的參與。 我們在此提出進行NFAT信號通路對誘導PI耐藥性的研究。我們將評價NFAT活性與接受BTZ治療的MM患者的臨床療效之間的相關性，並且研究PI如何激活MM細胞中的NFAT及其下游的其它信號通路的機制。此外，我們還會使用MM病人的原代癌細胞和動物模型來研究聯合使用BTZ/CFZ和NFAT抑製劑/鈣調磷酸酶抑製劑的治療價值。最後，我們會研究MM細胞中NFAT抑製劑/鈣調磷酸酶抑製劑對於BTZ/CFZ誘導的促生長信號通路及自噬的阻斷效應。此課題的研究成果將揭示PI耐藥性的關鍵，並且最終應用於MM臨床治療，有潛力讓MM成為可治之症。

14108719.label: Realisation of objectives
14108719.value: We completed the research work funded by this GRF. In this study, we revealed that 1) aberrant activation of NFATc1 is associated with proteasome inhibitor (PI)-resistance in MM; 2) BTZ/CFZ activates NFATc1 via Calcineurin to counteract cell death; 3) the calcineurin/NFAT inhibitors (CsA and FK506) synergizes with BTZ/CFZ to exacerbate ER stress-related apoptosis and growth inhibition in MM. In the first part, we comprehensively delineated the expression pattern of NFAT signaling and highlighted the role of NFAT activation in PI-resistance in MM. In our PWH cohort, we observed upregulations of NFATc1-c3 expression in MM samples as compared to NPC, while NFATc4 expression was barely detectable. Most of MM cell lines showed high expression of NFATc2-3, while NFATc1 expression was relatively low. However, ARH77, more resistant to BTZ than the others, exhibited robust expression of NFATc1. And BTZ could raise NFATc1 nuclear translocation by immunofluorescence staining and western blotting, but did not affect the cellular localization of NFATc2 and NFATc3 in ARH77. To further corroborate the relationship between NFAT activation and PI responsiveness, we employed IHC to examine the expression pattern of NFATc1 in trephine biopsies at diagnosis from MM patients treated with BTZ. IHC scoring for diagnostic MM samples (11 responders and 7 non-responders) indicated that BTZ-non-responders had significantly higher proportion of positive nuclear staining of NFATc1 than BTZ-responders, but had lower proportion of cells with cytoplasmic staining or negative staining than the responders. It suggests the correlation between NFATc1 nuclear accumulation and poor BTZ responsiveness in MM. Taken together, these findings indicated the escalated NFATc1 activation, particularly in the subgroup of patients with poor prognosis, potentially confers PI-resistance in MM. In the second part, we elucidated the upstream and downstream signaling of the BTZ/CFZ-induced NFATc1 activation in MM. Canonically, calcineurin (CaN) dephosphorylates and activates NFATc1-c4 upon Ca2+. Survival analysis of APEX cohort showed, for the BTZ group, patients with higher levels of PPP3CA (encoding calcineurin subunit A, CnA) had worse clinical outcomes than those with a lower level of this gene (HRhigh = 1.342), especially those patients with progressive MM (non-responders) (HRhigh = 1.822). However, the PPP3CA expression showed no specific correlation with the clinical outcome of the dexamethasone group. PPP3CA expression is a potential risk factor for MM patients exposed to BTZ. Further, PPP3CA siRNA increased BTZ-triggered cleavage of apoptotic marker PARP. BTZ treatment increased NFAT luciferase signals, which reflects CaN activation. Next, we tested whether BTZ/CFZ drives NFATc1 activation via CaN. As expected, we demonstrated by immunofluorescence staining and western blotting that NFATc1 nuclear translocation stimulated by BTZ/CFZ was impeded by calcineurin inhibitor CsA in ARH77 and MM.1S. Last, we deciphered the downstream consequences of NFATc1 activation in MM cells. Gene set enrichment analysis of APEX cohort indicated the correlation of NFATc1 expression and other oncogenic signatures. In detailed, the Oxidative Phosphorylation and the MYC Targets hallmarks were significantly enriched in cases with higher level of NFATc1. The patients with lower NFATc1 showed significant downregulation of genes related to Negative Regulation of Autophagy and Cancer Relapse, which contributes to drug resistance. The association between NFATc1 and these gene sets hints at the involvement of NFATc1 in promoting MM and thereby, inferior responses to BTZ. In ARH77, NFATc1 siRNA increased the early apoptotic marker cleaved-PARP after BTZ treatment. Flow cytometry analysis detecting Annexin V and 7-AAD showed that BTZ-induced apoptosis was promoted by NFATc1 siRNA. Similarly, in MM.1S, NFATc1 siRNA exacerbated BTZ-induced apoptosis and cell growth inhibition. These data support the role of NFATc1 activation via calcineurin participates in counteracting cell deaths in the context of BTZ resistance in MM. In the third part, we extensively evaluated the combinational effect of BTZ/CFZ and calcineurin/NFAT inhibitors (CsA, FK506, and 11R-VIVIT) on MM. Strikingly, we found the combined therapy of CsA or FK506 and BTZ was significantly more effective than BTZ as a monotherapy. However, pre-treatment with 11R-VIVIT could not synergize with BTZ. Further, we measured the effects of these drugs in apoptosis induction of MM cells. The results showed a dramatic increase in cell apoptosis in the combination therapy compared with BTZ alone. Moreover, the combination of CsA or FK506 raised the apoptotic regulators cleavage of caspase-3 and its downstream PARP to exacerbate apoptosis compared with BTZ alone. Also, both CsA and FK506 intensified BTZ-triggered ER stress, as demonstrated by upregulation of apoptotic ER stress markers (GRP78, CHOP, PPP1R15A and TRIB3) and downregulation of an anti-apoptotic signal, BCL2. Totally, cells treated with BTZ + CsA/FK506 reached a higher apoptotic stage compared with BTZ alone. To further define the molecular mechanisms underlining the synergistic effect of BTZ + CsA/FK506, we profiled the expression of NFAT-regulated anti-apoptotic genes (DDIAS, c-FLIP, BCL2A1, DDIT4 and BAG3) by real-time PCR. As a result, we demonstrated BTZ treatment up-regulated expressions of DDIT4 and BAG3, but not the others. Besides anti-apoptotic roles, both genes are involved in autophagy. In this regard, BTZ up-regulated expression of BAG3-associated aggresome partner and autophagy marker (MAP1LC3B), and increased conversion of LC3B-I into LC3B-II. Collectively, these observations indicated the induction of anti-apoptosis and autophagy by BTZ. However, BTZ-induced expression of DDIT4, BAG3, and MAP1LC3B increased further upon pre-treatment with CsA or FK506. This discrepancy suggested the synergistic effect of BTZ + CsA/FK506 on MM cells may involve other mechanisms. Nevertheless, our findings implicate that adjuvant therapy with CsA or FK506 may be exploited to circumvent BTZ resistance. Finally, we evaluated whether this synergistic effect is also relevant to MM patients. To this end, we collected bone marrow samples from MM patients and sorted CD138+ population by CD138-conjugated magnetic beads. We used CD138+ cells to evaluate the patient’s ex vivo response to BTZ and BTZ + CsA, which is determined by Annexin V apoptosis assay. In these primary MM cells, the combination of BTZ and CsA significantly decreased 11.99% cell viability compared to BTZ alone (p = 0.0003, n = 20). In conclusion, we find that calcineurin/NFATc1 activation contributes to PI resistance in MM. Genetic and pharmacal perturbation of calcineurinNFATc1 signaling promotes BTZ-induced ER stress-mediated apoptosis and growth inhibition, and thus sensitizes MM cells to BTZ treatment. This study provides novel mechanistic and therapeutic insights into the PI-based chemotherapy in MM. Explanations for 90% percentage achieved in Objective 1 and 3 are following: For IHC staining analysis of NFATc1 in MM patients mentioned in Objective 1, the expression of NFATc1 in many trephine biopsies were barely detectable using anti-NFATc1 antibody (sc-7294) from Santa Cruz. We also tried NFATc1 (NB100-56732) antibody from Novus. But its specificity is not good enough to show the cellular localization of NFATc1. Many precious specimens were wasted. In addition, it is difficult to get commercial antibodies immediately due to covid-19 pandemic. We will try more antibodies and recruit more MM patients to further confirm the correlations of NFAT activity with BTZ responsiveness and clinical outcomes. For in vivo study mentioned in Objective 3, MM1S and ARH77 were injected subcutaneously into NSG mice. Unfortunately, in our study, both of them were failed to grow xenograft tumors. We have developed various methods to establish MM xenograft model. However, covid-19 pandemic and HBV contamination in Animal Centre frequently interrupted our study. In further development of the research, we plan to generate Matrigel xenograft and SCID-Rab MM models for the drug tests.

14108719.label: Major findings and research outcome
14108719.value: Our research focuses mainly on the role of NFAT signaling in PI-resistance in MM. We firstly profiled NFAT alterations and analyzed their clinical associations in PWH MM cohort. Upregulation of NFATc1-c3 in MM samples was observed compared with NPC, while NFATc4 expression was barely detectable. In ARH77, BTZ triggered the nuclear translocation of NFATc1 but not NFATc2-c3. And nuclear activation of NFATc1 is associated with lower BTZ sensitivity in our MM patients. NFATc1 siRNA promotes BTZ-induced apoptosis. Moreover, BTZ activated NFAT signaling through induction of ER stress-calcineurin. The calcineurin inhibitors (CsA and FK506) blocked the BTZ/CFZ-triggered NFATc1 nuclear translocation and NFAT signals from the luciferase reporters. Also, they showed synergistic effect with BTZ/CFZ in MM cell lines. We also studied the combinatorial treatment of BTZ and CsA in primary myeloma cells and observed further reduction of cell viability in the co-treated cells as compared to those with BTZ alone. Mechanistically, the exaggerated cytotoxicity was due to intensification of BTZ/CFZ-triggered ER stress-induced apoptosis. Unexpectedly, we found that CsA and FK506 exacerbated BTZ-induced autophagy and upregulation of anti-apoptotic BAG3 and DDIT4, downstream of NFAT signaling. There may be other players underling the synergistic killing of MM cells by calcineurin/NFATc1 inhibitors and PIs. In summary, we find that calcineurin/NFATc1 is directly involved in PI resistance, and that CsA and FK506 synergizes with PI to overcome resistance of MM. The main findings have been drafted in manuscript (Jinglin Zhang et al, Targeting calcineurin/NFATc1 promotes proteasome inhibition treatment in multiple myeloma). Apart from NFAT signaling in MM, we also working on other blood cancer-related research supported by this GRF grant. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is the most common leukemia and can be diagnosed at any age. For pediatric AML, the leading cause of childhood leukemic mortality, we unveil complex mutational patterns of biological relevance and disease mechanisms including MYC deregulation and highlight TP53 alterations as strong adverse prognostic markers (Chi-Keung Cheng et al, Communications Biology, 2023). Also, we report a novel NUP98-JADE2 fusion in a 15-month-old AML patient. Mechanistically, we showed that NUP98-JADE2 perturbs wild-type JADE2 and retinoic acid signaling thereby contributing to an APL-like phenotype (Chi-Keung Cheng et al, Blood Advances, 2022). For prefibrotic primary myelofibrosis (Pre-PMF), a rare blood cancer classified by the WHO in 2016, we have revealed the mutational spectrum and its clinicopathological significance in Chinese pre-PMF patients and suggested a specific prognostic model for this entity (Chi-Keung Cheng et al, eJHaem, 2021).

14108719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14108719.value: This study confirmed that aberrant calcineurin-NFATc1 activation confers intrinsic proteasome inhibitor (PI)-resistance in multiple myeloma MM. We also developed a novel therapeutic strategy that CsA or FK506 synergizes with PI to overcome resistance of MM. However, 11R-VIVIT, a cell-permeable NFAT inhibitor, was failed to enhance the anti-tumour effect of BTZ in ARH77 and MM.1S. Thus, it is necessary to develop a more specific and effective NFATc1 inhibitor to benefit MM patients with refractoriness to BTZ. The combinational administration of candidate drugs and BTZ/CFZ in controlling MM cell growth and apoptosis will be performed. Meanwhile, we also plan to generate Matrigel xenograft and SCID-Rab MM models for the drug tests. In addition, the role of NFAT activation and its functions in mediating the PI resistance remains to be deeply investigated. We plan to perform RNA sequencing to dig out the downstream consequences of NFAT activation in MM cells. There will be 3 treatment groups including BTZ alone, BTZ + CsA and untreated control. Insights thus gained will provide opportunities to overcome the MM treatment refractoriness and improve long-term clinical outcomes of patients.

14108719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14108719.value: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a cancer of plasma cells. Healthy plasma cells manage antibody production to fight infection. However, cancerous plasma cells produce abnormal proteins, accumulate in the bone marrow, and then crowd out healthy blood cells. According to Hong Kong’s Hospital Authority, there were 320 new cases of MM in 2019, an increase of about 40% compared with a decade ago. Up to date, the disease can be initially controlled by proteasome inhibitors (PI). But the issue of inevitable relapse and drug resistance remains. It is urgent to investigate the underlying mechanisms of PI resistance and develop novel therapeutic strategies. In this study, we confirmed that aberrant NFATc1 activation confers intrinsic PI-resistance in MM. We also developed a novel therapeutic strategy that CsA or FK506 synergizes with PI. Mechanically, co-treatment-induced exaggerated cytotoxicity was mediated through intensification of PI-triggered ER stress-induced apoptosis. Besides, proteasome inhibition could induce stress related heart failure in mice via NFAT activation and an increased risk of morbid cardiac events was reported in the recent trial of CFZ in MM patients. Therefore, the administration of NFAT inhibitors also could improve the safety profiles of PIs.

14109519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14109519.value: Background: Atherosclerosis is the inflammation of vascular wall triggered by initial dysfunction of the luminal endothelial cells potentiated by high cholesterol which leads to immune cell accumulation underneath the endothelium, forming atherosclerotic plaques. Atherosclerotic plaque causes narrowing, blockage of arteries often followed by plaque rupture and thrombosis, leading to serious consequences and it is the major cause of cardiovascular diseases (CVD) such as coronary artery disease and stroke. CVD remains among the top three causes of death with a mortality rate >13% and also one of the top causes of in-patient discharges in Hong Kong. Sirtuin 3 (SIRT3) is a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) -dependent deacetylase, mainly functioning in the mitochondria to regulate protein acetylation. A beneficial role of SIRT3 was implicated in aging- and oxidative stress- related diseases, due to the hyper-acetylation and inhibition of protein function. Although previous studies showed the correlation between enhanced metabolic inflammation and Sirt3 deletion in mice, there lacks mechanistic evidence on whether Sirt3 deletion accelerates endothelial inflammation and atherosclerosis through hyperacetylation of mitochondrial proteins. Although NAD+ is believed to be protective in vascular cells, the detailed mechanism and involvement of SIRT3 is poorly defined. Hypothesis: We hypothesize that the deletion of Sirt3 in endothelial cells exacerbates vascular dysfunction and inflammation, leading to increased atherosclerotic plaque formation, due to inhibition of argininosuccinate lyase (ASL) which reduces L-arginine bioavailability and nitric oxide production. Supplement of NAD+ precursor nicotinamide riboside can reduce atherosclerosis through SIRT3 activation and subsequent activation of ASL. Project Description: To test the hypothesis, atherosclerosis will be induced by feeding endothelial-specific Sirt3 knockout and wild type mice after PCSK9 overexpression, or Apoe knockout mice, with high cholesterol diet. We will first examine whether targeted deletion of Sirt3 in endothelial cells exacerbates vascular inflammation and plaque formation during the development of atherosclerosis. NAD+ precursor nicotinamide riboside will be given orally to mice aiming to examine whether NAD+-SIRT3 activation mitigates atherosclerosis. We will then analyze the acetylated mitochondrial protein due to Sirt3 deletion to identify SIRT3 target proteins aided by proteomics approach. In addition, we will examine whether ASL is a downstream effector to mediate the effect of SIRT3 by regulating the L-arginine and nitric oxide production in endothelial cells. Significance: This study shall provide insight into endothelial mitochondrial dynamics regulated by post-translational modification in vascular inflammation of atherosclerosis. Results from this study will also explore the potential of targeting NAD and SIRT3 in treating CVDs. 動脈粥樣硬化是高膽固醇誘發的從內皮細胞功能障礙發展到血管壁內免疫細胞浸潤形成斑塊的血管炎症反應。斑塊變大使血管狹窄、阻塞、甚至發生斑塊破裂和血栓，導致更嚴重的心血管事件如冠心病心肌梗塞或中風。在香港，心血管疾病是主要的致死因素，也是導致病人住院的首要原因。去乙酰化酶Sirtuin家族的SIRT3是一個腺嘌呤二核苷酸NAD+依賴性的去乙酰化酶，主要作用在線粒體。以往的研究顯示SIRT3在衰老或氧化應激相關的疾病中通過引起抑制蛋白高乙酰化改善蛋白功能，具有保護作用。Sirt3敲除在小鼠中加劇代謝綜合征和代謝性炎症反應，但是SIRT3在內皮細胞中對炎症的抑制和其作用機制尚未明確有待進一步研究。在本課題中，我們假設Sirt3敲除加劇內皮細胞功能障礙和內皮炎症，導致更多的動脈粥樣硬化斑塊，而且這個作用主要是通過高乙酰化抑制ASL的功能，減少精氨酸的生物有效性，抑制一氧化氮生成的機制。為了驗證此假設，我們會建立內皮特異性Sirt3敲除的小鼠模型，用高表達PCSK9引起高脂血症和動脈粥樣硬化，檢測在體抑制SIRT3的作用，我們會使用NAD+前體煙酰胺核糖餵養Apoe敲除小鼠檢測利用促進SIRT3激活是否能抑制斑塊生成。我們會用蛋白組學檢測Sirt3敲除對線粒體蛋白乙酰化的影響，從中找出下游的作用分子。我們也會進一步研究在內皮細胞中ASL乙酰化對其功能的影響和對精氨酸和一氧化氮生成的調控。這些實驗希望能幫助揭示蛋白翻譯后修飾在內皮細胞炎症反應和功能障礙中的作用和在心血管疾病中的意義。

14109519.label: Realisation of objectives
14109519.value: For Objective 1 (To investigate the protective role of endothelial SIRT3 against endothelial dysfunction and inflammation in mouse model of atherosclerosis.) There are two sub-aims. The realizations of each sub-aim are described under 5.3.1 and 5.3.2. 5.3.1. To examine whether vascular dysfunction and inflammation during atherosclerosis is aggravated in endothelial specific Sirt3 knockout mice: We have used the endothelial specific Sirt3 knockout (Sirt3EC-KO) and their wild type control littermates (Sirt3EC-WT) mice generated by crossbreeding the Sirt3 floxed mice and Cdh5-Cre mice to induce experimental atherosclerosis after the injection of AAV to overexpress PCSK9 followed by high cholesterol diet feeding to induce hypercholesterolemia. We showed that the plaque formation was further increased with Sirt3 deletion in the Sirt3EC-KO mice. The atherosclerotic plaque in the Sirt3EC-KO mice was more unstable, with more lipid deposition, macrophage accumulation, and higher expression of inflamed endothelial cell (EC) markers such as ICAM-1 and E-selectin. These results are included in the Figure 1 of the manuscript under revision (Advanced Science advs.202307256R1). 5.3.2. To examine whether SIRT3 mediates the effect of NR treatment on atherosclerosis: We have used the NR (Nicotinamide Riboside) to treat the ApoE knockout mice fed with high cholesterol diet in vivo. NR reduced plaque formation, vascular inflammation, and improved endothelium-dependent vasodilatation in the ApoE knockout mice (Figure 5-6. DOI: 10.3390/antiox11040706). The effect of NAD was also examined on isolated aorta from Sirt3EC-KO and Sirt3EC-WT mice. The results showed that the superoxide production induced by oxLDL or IL-1β was further increased with Sirt3 deletion, which could be rescued by NAD treatment (Figure 3, DOI: 10.3390/antiox11040706), whereas the impaired endothelium-dependent vasodilatation in the Sirt3EC-KO mice could not be rescued by NAD treatment (Figure 4, DOI: 10.3390/antiox11040706). For Objective 2 (To investigate whether SIRT3-dependent deacetylation of ASL contributes to the protective effect of SIRT3 activation in endothelium against atherosclerosis) There are two sub-aims. The realizations of each sub-aim are described under 5.3.3 and 5.3.4. 5.3.3. To examine whether Sirt3 deletion worsens endothelial cells in response to inflammatory stimuli. First, we showed that in both primary human endothelial cells (HUVECs) and mouse endothelial cell line (mBMECs), silencing or knockdown SIRT3 further enhanced EC inflammation markers such as E-selectin, VCAM-1, ICAM-1, and CCL2 (Figure 1, DOI: 10.3390/antiox11040706). In isolated aorta from Sirt3EC-KO and Sirt3EC-WT mice, the superoxide production measured at mitochondrial level by mitoSOX both showed more increase in the Sirt3EC-KO mice (Figure 3, DOI: 10.3390/antiox11040706). In the HUVECs, silencing of SIRT3 showed similar change (Figure 4, Advanced Science advs.202307256R1, under revision). Nitric oxide (NO) production measured by DAF-FM fluorescent probe showed that IL-1β diminished NO production in both control and SIRT3 silenced HUVECs, and similar results was also observed with isolated aorta (Figure 3, Advanced Science advs.202307256R1, under revision). Mitochondrial respiration, especially the ATP-linked respiration was further decreased by IL-1β in the SIRT3 silenced HUVECs, which was rescued by NAD treatment (Figure 2, DOI: 10.3390/antiox11040706). 5.3.4. To identify whether SIRT3 mediated deacetylation of ASL is critical for endothelial function through enhancing NO production. We examined the lysine acetylation in both liver ECs isolated from Sirt3EC-KO and Sirt3EC-WT mice, and also the cell line mBMECs with lentiviral knckdown of Sirt3, which showed similar hyperacetylation with Sirt3 inhibition. After a careful and rigorous repeating of the experiments on protein lysine acetylation, we found that the acetylation level of ASS1 was more affected by SIRT3 rather than that of ASL. Both the ASS1 (Argininosuccinate synthase 1) and ASL (Argininosuccinate lyase) are enzymes in the urea cycle involved in L-arginine recycling from L-citrulline. The lysine acetylation of ASS1 was more consistent with SIRT3 inhibition. We therefore further examined the lysine residue of ASS1 and identified two sites (K165 and K176) on ASS1 regulated by SIRT3 (Figure 2, Advanced Science advs.202307256R1, under revision). Furthermore, we measured arginine concentration together with other amino acids by metabolomics. The results showed that only arginine concentration in the blood decreased in the Sirt3EC-KO mice, suggesting the involvement of ASS1 and SIRT3 in arginine biosynthesis. Next, we examined the effect of NO and L-arginine. In vitro L-arginine treatment rescued the vascular inflammation, NO production, mitochondrial function, and overproduction of mitochondrial superoxide in the HUVECs with SIRT3 silencing. In vivo L-arginine treatment but not L-citrulline attenuated the increased plaque formation and vascular inflammation in the Sirt3EC-KO mice (Figure 3-6, Advanced Science advs.202307256R1, under revision). Because ASS1 and ASL have similar location and function in the cell, we consider that the results still align well with the objective.

14109519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14109519.value: We found that the selective deletion of SIRT3 in endothelial cells further impaired endothelium-dependent vasodilatation in the aorta treated with IL-1β, which was accompanied by upregulation of vascular inflammation markers and mitochondrial superoxide overproduction. Excepting the dysfunction of endothelium-dependent vasodilatation, such effects could be attenuated by treatment with NAD+. In human umbilical vein endothelial cells, SIRT3 silencing potentiated the induction of inflammatory factors by IL-1β, including VCAM-1, ICAM-1, and MCP1, and the impairment of mitochondrial respiration, both of which were alleviated by NAD+ treatment. In ApoE-deficient mice fed with a high-cholesterol diet, supplementation with nicotinamide riboside, the NAD+ precursor, reduced plaque formation, improved vascular function, and diminished vascular inflammation. Our results support the SIRT3-dependent and -independent of NAD+ to improve endothelial function in atherosclerosis. These results are included in Cao et al., Antioxidants (Basel). 2022 Apr; 11(4): 706 (doi: 10.3390/antiox11040706). We also highlighted the intrinsic L-arginine biosynthesis mediated by ASS1 in endothelial cells plays an important role in vascular homeostasis. ASS1 activity is largely controlled by SIRT3-dependent deacetylation. Without SIRT3, impaired ASS1 activity and L-arginine deficiency is a critical factor contributing to mitochondrial dysfunction, disturbance of NO and redox status, endothelial inflammation, and enhanced atherosclerosis induced by SIRT3 deletion in mice. our study has provided new insights into the role of endothelial SIRT3 in maintaining vascular homeostasis and preventing atherosclerosis through SIRT3-mediated deacetylation of ASS1, which is responsible for de novo arginine biosynthesis. This highlights the importance of arginine biosynthesis and urea cycle enzymes in endothelial function, particularly in the context of cardiovascular disease. These results are included in a manuscript under revision at Advanced Science (advs.202307256R1).

14109519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14109519.value: Our researching finding showed the significance of vascular SIRT3 in vascular homeostasis and its athero-protective role, adding important information supporting the use of pharmaceutical or nutraceutical agents which works through activation of SIRT3, such as the those supplements replenishing NR, NMN, and NAD+. Our study is also the first to report an indispensable role of endothelium selectrive SIRT3 in this vascular protective effect, rather than SIRT3 in other vascular cell types. Future clinical or epidemiological studies to investigate whether SIRT3 activation would be beneficial to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease is needed. In addition, our study also highlighted the importance of endogenous L-arginine synthesis for its vascular protective effect. Although L-arginine as the substrate to produce nitric oxide has been known for quite a long time. We provided new information to show that the importance of L-arginine recycling and L-arginine deficiency due to endothelial cell dysfunction, which is a causative factor for vascular dysfunction and atherosclerosis. Because of the side effect of directing supplement L-arginine, modulating the urea cycle enzymes such as ASS1 and ASL may be an alternative to increase L-arginine biosynthesis, and improve nitric oxide bioavailability, could be a more feasible future clinical approach.

14109519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14109519.value: Sirtuin 3 (SIRT3) is a protein in the mitochondria responsible for post-translational modification of mitochondrial protein. It can be activated by increasing NAD level. There are many nutriceuticals on the market which can boost NAD level, such as NMN and NR (nicotinamide riboside. The health benefit of increasing NAD or activating SIRT3, particularly about their beneficial effect against cardiovascular disease is not well characterized. In this research project, we showed that NR treatment reduces atherosclerosis in mice. NR can increase vasodilator nitric oxide production in the endothelial cells, and reduce inflammation, contributing to its beneficial effect. NR can also improve mitochondrial function. We also find that SIRT3, which is known to function as a protein deacetylase as one form of post-translational modification in the vascular endothelial cells, which is important to maintain normal protein function and activity. Without SIRT3, many mitochondrial proteins are functionally impaired. Among these mitochondrial proteins are some enzymes responsible for arginine synthesis, such as ASS1. Arginine is the substrate for producing nitric oxide. Without SIRT3, endothelial cell cannot produce enough arginine to generate nitric oxide, causing endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerosis. Therefore, this research also indicate that arginine supplementation may provide benefit for cardiovascular disease.
