14113219.label: Realisation of objectives
14113219.value: The project was commenced at the time at the time when the COVID-19 pandemic evolved in Feb 2020. As the subject recruitment was in the respiratory clinics of the hospital, the study implementation was strictly prohibited by the infectious control policy. We would like to thank the RGC for the support in the 6-month project extension. We also continued the data collection in the gap year for result dissemination. Eventually, the subject recruitment took place from Jan 2022 to March 2023 (last data collection point took place at March 2024). Of 6361 patients who consecutively attended the respiratory clinics in the two regional hospitals, 124 patients (mean [SD] age, 70.1 [8.0] years; 57 men [46.0%] were recruited (Part C, No 2, Table 1). A total of 31 (25.0%) and 64 (51.6%) suffered from chronic obstructive airway disease and sleep apnea, respectively. About 37 (29.8%) patients had admitted to hospital for one or more time in the past year. Comorbidity was prevalent and the Charlson’s comorbidity index was >4 for both groups. No between-group differences were found in the baseline characteristics. A total of 111 patients completed the 12-month posttest assessment, with 56 (90.3%) from the IMB-NIV group and 55 (88.7%) from the usual care group (Part C, No 2, Figure 1). No attrition bias was detected. The GEE analysis controlled the effect of clinical-demographic characteristics which were different between the study groups at p<0.25. The Information-Motivation-Behavioral-based Model (IMB-NIV Program). The 6-week IMB-NIV Program adopted a hybrid approach including home visit, tele-care and clinic visit to increase the accessibility to the chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure (CHRF) patients who are more likely to have compromised activity tolerance. [Part C, No1. Supplementary Figure 1]. The program was delivered by a registered nurse who had received training in advanced respiratory care. Central to the IMB-NIV program was to use a person-centered approach to enhance the knowledge and skills in the CHRF disease management and to cultivate positive attitude and social motivation for long-term domiciliary NIV adherence. The Program was commenced with a home visit during which the nurse assessed the participant’s self-care on CHRF and NIV. Health education on these areas by the nurse was given in a way so that the participants’ misconception and ineffective illness behaviors, together with the concomitant health consequences, were highlighted. This arrangement was very effective to motivate the participants to enhance the NOV adherence. They were very concerned about how to resolve the challenges in using the NIV. The major concerns included i) sleep disturbance due to air leakage, ii) discomfort with the mask, iii) unawareness of the health consequence of hypoventilation during sleep, iv) local skin irritation, v) motivational issues and vi) disturbed self-image. By using a nurse-patient partnership approach, the nurse addressed the concern and worked with the participants to set self-directed goals and action plan to increase the NIV update. Skill training on proper NIV handling and complication prevention were provided with emphasis on how to optimize the related self-care in the home environment. The visit was closed with a brainstorming on anticipated barriers for goal attainment, and the corresponding resolving methods were discussed. Two tele-visits scheduled at 2nd and 4th week were timely to monitor the goal-attainment process during which explicit methods were advised to tackle the encountered barriers and motivational messages are given to highlight the positive changes. The IMB-NIV program was well received by the participants and there was no attrition during the intervention. The goal setting process provided a clear direction and explicit method to encourage behavioral changes. By optimizing their choice in actions, they had higher acceptance to the recommended actions. The partnership approach by working with a nurse was also highly appreciated. We conclude this 6-week program experience was important to empower the participants to make adjustment to their used NIV-related self-care and increase the uptake. Realization of objective 1-6 The longitudinal outcome evaluation went smoothly. The NIV machine data was obtained to avoid recall bias in measuring adherence. Blood taking for HCO3- was well facilitated by the clinical collaborators. The patient-reported data collection using the Chinese Pittsburg Sleep Quality Index and Chinese Severe Respiratory Insufficiency Questionnaire (CSRI) for sleep quality and health-related quality of life was highly feasible and well accepted. In summary, the six objectives aimed to examine the impact of the IMB-NIV program on adherent behaviors, venous bicarbonate, sleep quality, health-related quality of life, hospital admission and mortality were well achieved as follows. Effect of the IMB-NIV program on NIV adherence (Objective 1) NIV adherence is the primary outcomes which captured by the criterion of night-time use of >4 hour for >70% of days. Referring to (Part C, No. 2, Table 2), there were significantly more participants in the IMB-NIV group became adheres (51.6-61.3%) than the usual care group (16.1 – 27.4%) across the 12-month evaluation period, with the IMB-NIV group has significantly greater increase in mean daily use than the usual care group. Such positive change was sustainable to the 12-month evaluation endpoint [Group*Time effect: B(95% CI) = 2.37 (1.44 – 3.31), p<0.001), Cohen’s d = 0.724 -0.997]. Effects of IMB-NIV program on (Objective 2 and 4) The IMB-NIV group reported greater improvement than the usual care group in sleep quality and HRQoL (Part C, No2, Table 2). For PSQI, the IMB-NIV group reported significantly greater improvement in the overall score and the seven domain scores since the 3rd month post-test, and such effects (time x group interaction) was sustained for 12 months, with effect size for overall sleep quality (Cohen’s d) ranges from 0.59 – 0.92. The greater improvement in the CSRI summary score and domain scores among the IMB-NIV group was detected even earlier upon the completion of the IMB-NIV program, and such between-group difference lasted until the 12-month endpoints, with effect size (Cohen’s d) for the summary score ranges from 0.53-0.93. Nevertheless, there is no significant difference between the study groups on serum HCo3-. Effects of IMB-NIV program on hospital admission and mortality (Objective 5-6) The IMB-NIV program also significantly improved the unplanned ER attendance at the 12-month evaluative period. Negative binary regression indicated that the incidence rate ratio (IRR) of the IMB-NIV (ER admission = 27) versus usual care (ER admission = 66) was 0.467 (95% CI = 0.26 – 0.84, p = 0.013). However, the IMB-NIV did not significantly reduce the risk of hospital admission, though there is a non-significant trend of lower admission rate in the 12-month evaluation period (number of admission (IMB-NIV vs control = 44 vs 65; IRR = 0.689 (0.398 – 1.190), p=0.181). The time to events for respiratory-related ER attendance and hospital admission were shown by the survival curves (Part C, No 2, Fig 2-3). Cox regression indicated that the IMB-NIV program significantly delayed the time for respiratory-related ER attendance with hazard ratio as [0.511(95% CI = 0.276-0.947)] but not for hospital admission [Hazard ratio (95% CI) = 0.690(0.384-1.241)]. As for mortality, there were three events from each of the IMB-NIV program and usual care group (Part C, No 2, Figure 1). In view of the small number of events and even distribution, no survival analysis was conducted.

14113219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113219.value: This study identified the positive effect of a behavioral strategy based on the IMB model to improve the NIV adherence among patients with CHRF. The extended benefits of the IMB-NIV program on sleep quality, HRQL and ER service use, together with the high fidelity, imply high translation potential. Following actions will be taken to support knowledge translation: 1) The study findings were communicated to the respiratory medical and nursing team in the two collaborating hospitals, and support has been solicited for the upcoming science implementation. 2) A knowledge translation fund will be sought from HKU to use a co-design approach to incorporate users' perspective to the IMB-NIV program. Based on the intervention materials being developed, toolkit will be developed to facilitate the process (including video, health education booklets, goal-oriented care plan, tele-care health record, etc). 3) The absence of treatment effects on HCO3-, hospital admission and mortality may be related to the recruitment of more stable out-patients. Future research may test the therapeutic value of the IMB-NIV program among the newly diagnosed patients or those with disease worsening. 4) With the positive findings, the IMB-based model will be extended to improve the adherence to boarder self-care among this clinical cohort.

14113219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113219.value: Chronic hypercapnia respiratory failure (CHRF) is the complication of various respiratory, cardiovascular and neuromuscular disorder, associated with distressing symptoms and poor quality of life. Domiciliary non-invasive ventilation (NIV) has high therapeutic value among this clinical cohort, but the treatment benefits are compromised by patient non-adherence. This study integrated a behavioral strategy called Information-Motivation-Behavioral model (IMB-NIV program) to address the intricate determinants of NIV non-adherence in CHRF patients. This 6-week program was delivered by a nurse who used person-centered assessment, motivational counseling and goal-setting to enhance NIV adherence. The results showed that the more patients in the IMB-NIV group became adheres (51.6-61.3%) than the usual care group (16.1–27.4%) across the 12-month evaluation. The IMB-NIV group reported better sleep quality, symptom control, physical function and psychosocial wellness. Although there were no effects on serum bicarbonate and hospital admission, the IMB-NIV program significantly reduced the emergence room (ER) admission. There is chance that the breathing pattern of IMB-NIV group improved with better NIV adherence, as perceived breathlessness is a common trigger for ER admission among this clinical cohort. Together with the high feasibility of the program, this paper provides important insights how to enhance the NIV support to patients with CHRF.

14113419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113419.value: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration (EUS-FNA) is an indispensable tool for tissue acquisition for pancreatic lesions. However, FNA alone has several limitations including inadequate acquisition of cells, and unable to provide core tissue for further histological analysis. The use of rapid on-site evaluation (ROSE) by cytopathologist has the biggest impact on improving diagnostic accuracy and is regarded as the gold standard for EUS-FNA. Unfortunately, it is not widely available due to limited resources.(1-3) In order to overcome these limitations, new fine needle biopsy (FNB) needles have been recently developed to collect not only cells but also the entire core tissue for histological analysis. Having core biopsy with preserved tissue provides additional advantages of allowing molecular analysis, which are of emerging importance in cancer management. Early results comparing FNB with FNA showed the superiority of FNB over FNA in the absence of ROSE. (4) Data comparing FNB and FNA with ROSE are limited. In order to study to true merits of FNB over FNA, comparison with the most optimal method is necessary. To improve the diagnostic yield of EUS-FNB, we have recently demonstrated, in a multicentered prospective randomized controlled trial, that EUS-FNB combined with a new technique called macroscopic on-site evaluation (MOSE) by endoscopists provided comparable diagnostic accuracy and better quality of tissue with fewer number of passes when compared with FNB alone. A total of 12 international centres participated in this study which implied that MOSE technique is easy to master with high generalizability. We hypothesized that EUS-FNB with MOSE have comparable diagnostic yield as EUS-FNA with ROSE, and hence can replace ROSE as the gold standard for EUS guided tissue acquisition for solid pancreatic masses. Moreover, data on feasibility of molecular analysis on FNA samples are scarce. In this study, we aim to compare (1) the diagnostic yield of EUS-FNB with MOSE vs EUS-FNA with ROSE; and (2) the feasibility of FNB and FNA samples for further molecular analysis. If our study can show that the FNB with MOSE is comparable to FNA with ROSE, then FNB with MOSE could replace FNA with ROSE and be implemented across hospitals worldwide in an easier and less expensive fashion. Patients will be benefited from reduced need for repeated procedures and earlier diagnosis and treatment. Results of this study can also provide important information on the best method to obtain tissue for molecular analysis, which is essential for cancer management. 內鏡超聲引導細針穿刺（EUS-FNA）是胰腺病變組織獲取的必不可少的工具。然而，FNA具有若干限制，包括細胞的不充分獲取，以及不能提供用於進一步組織學分析的核心組織。細胞病理學家使用快速現場評估（ROSE）對提高診斷準確性具有最大影響，並被視為EUS-FNA的黃金標準。不幸的是，由於資源有限，它沒有廣泛使用。為了克服這些限制，最近新開發了細針穿刺活檢（FNB）針，它不僅收集細胞，還收集整個核心組織進行組織學分析。 具有保存組織的核心活組織檢查提供了允許分子分析的額外優點，這在癌症管理中具有新的重要性。比較FNB和FNA的早期結果顯示，在沒有ROSE的情況下，FNB優於FNA。 將FNB和FNA與ROSE進行比較的數據是有限的。為了研究FNB相對於FNA的真實優點，需要與最優方法進行比較。為了提高EUS-FNB的診斷率，我們最近在一項多中心前瞻性隨機對照試驗中證明，EUS-FNB結合了一種被內鏡醫師稱為宏觀現場評估（MOSE）的新技術，可提供相約的診斷準確性和更好的質量與單獨的FNB，但只需要較少通過次數 。這項研究一共有12個國際中心參與，這意味著MOSE技術很容易掌握，具有很高的普遍性。我們假設具有MOSE的EUS-FNB與具有ROSE 的EUS-FNA 的診斷產率相約，因此可以取代ROSE作為EUS引導的固體胰腺腫塊組織獲取的黃金標準。此外，關於FNA樣品的分子分析可行性的數據很少。在本研究中，我們的目的是比較（1）EUS-FNB與MOSE和EUS-FNA與ROSE的診斷率; （2）FNB和FNA樣品用於進一步分子分析的可行性。如果我們的研究能夠證明有MOSE的FNB與有ROSE的FNA相當，那麼有MOSE的FNB可以取代有ROSE 的FNA，並且可以更方便，更便宜的方式在全球各地的醫院實施。患者將從減少重複手術和早期診斷和治療的需求中受益。該研究的結果還可以提供關於獲得用於分子分析的組織的最佳方法的重要信息，這對於癌症管理是必不可少的。

14113419.label: Realisation of objectives
14113419.value: An international, multicentred randomized controlled trial was carried out. Patients with solid pancreatic lesions >1cm requiring EUS-guided tissue acquisition from 12 international centres were recruited. From February 2019 to April 2023, a total of 340 patients were recruited and 170 patients were allocated to each treatment arm (Fine needle biopsy with macroscopic on-site evaluation FNB-MOSE vs. fine needle aspiration with rapid on-site evaluation FNA-ROSE). FNB-MOSE showed superior diagnostic accuracy over FNA-ROSE (97.6% vs 92.9%, p = 0.04). It was also associated with a lower number of passes (2 vs 3, p < 0.001), and shorter procedure time (25.5min +/-13.4min vs 29.5min +/-19min, p = 0.024) than FNA-ROSE. The sensitivity, specificity, and complication profiles were comparable between groups. FNB-MOSE also demonstrated a higher feasibility rate for next-generation sequencing (NGS) than FNA-ROSE. (86% vs 59%, p = 0.005). In conclusion, FNB with MOSE was associated with higher diagnostic accuracy, shorter procedure time, a lower number of passes, and a higher feasibility rate for NGS than FNA with ROSE.

14113519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113519.value: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a form of malignant brain tumor in which the underlying pathogenesis most likely involved defective astrocyte differentiation. The incidence of glioblastoma in Hong Kong is 1 to 2 per 100,000. Although concomitant temozolamide-based chemoradiotherapy provides some objective survival benefits, the 5-year survival rate remains poor. Characterization of the genetic landscape of GBM revealed mutations in the phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3-K) pathway in over 50% of tumor specimens suggesting that uncontrolled activation of this growth/survival pathway is the main driver of tumor initiation and/or progression. PTEN is a negative regulator of the PI3-K pathway that is mutationally inactivated in over 30% of GBM. Transcriptomic profiling of primary astrocytes derived from Pten knockout mice revealed that an enrichment of mitotic regulators is upregulated in human GBM. Coincidentally, PTEN has been shown to assemble mitotic spindle poles by interacting with the kinesin-related motor protein, EG5, at the centrosomes. The proposed study will aim to define the mitotic machinery that is vulnerable to therapeutic targeting of GBM with the activated PI3-K pathway. Specifically, we found that the upregulation of the PI3-K pathway is associated with the Regulator of Chromosome Condensation 1 (RCC1), a component of the chromatin that stimulates mitotic spindle formation by inducing local nucleation of the microtubules. RCC1 is expressed at different levels in the GBM cell lines. Overexpression of RCC1 promotes cell proliferation while its silencing has a repressive effect. Mammalian mitosis is characterized by highly coordinated signaling events that are monitored by a host of checkpoint regulators to ensure proper attachment of the spindle to kinetochore and the subsequent separation of the sister chromatids into two daughter cells. Therefore, the major hypothesis of the proposed study will be that the loss of PTEN in human GBM causes a global upregulation of the mitotic regulators that play a critical role in sustaining the rapid proliferation of tumor cells. We believe that GBM with a hyperactivated PI3-K pathway is particularly vulnerable to the selective inhibition of mitotic spindle formation and/or destruction. However, the efficacy of temozolomide is limited by both intrinsic and acquired drug resistance. Various PI3K chemical inhibitors are being tested in clinical trials but eventually toxicity and drug resistance impose great challenges. We expect that our findings will identify new therapeutics targeting the mitotic machinery that have greater efficacy and reduced toxicity. 多形性膠質母細胞瘤（GBM）是惡性腦腫瘤的一種，其中潛在的發病機制最可能涉及有缺陷的星形膠質細胞分化。香港膠質母細胞瘤的發病率為每10萬人1至2人。雖然伴隨的基於替莫唑胺的放化療提供了一些客觀的生存益處，但5年生存率仍然很差。 GBM遺傳景觀的表徵揭示了超過50％的腫瘤標本中磷酸肌醇3-激酶（PI3-K）途徑的突變，表明該生長/存活途徑的不受控制的激活是腫瘤起始和/或進展的主要驅動因素。 PTEN是PI3-K途徑的負調節物，其在超過30％的GBM中突變失活。源自Pten敲除小鼠的原代星形膠質細胞的轉錄組學分析顯示，有絲分裂調節因子的富集在人GBM中被上調。巧合的是，已經證明PTEN通過與中心體上的驅動蛋白相關的運動蛋白EG5相互作用來組裝有絲分裂紡錘體極。擬議的研究旨在確定易受GBM治療靶向激活的PI3-K途徑的有絲分裂機制。具體而言，我們發現PI3-K途徑的上調與染色體凝聚1調節劑（RCC1）相關，染色體凝集調節劑是染色質的一種成分，其通過誘導微管的局部成核來刺激有絲分裂紡錘體形成。 RCC1在GBM細胞系中以不同水平表達。 RCC1的過表達促進細胞增殖，而其沉默具有抑製作用。哺乳動物有絲分裂的特徵在於高度協調的信號傳導事件，其由許多檢查點調節器監測以確保紡錘體與動粒的正確附著以及隨後將姐妹染色單體分離成兩個子細胞。因此，所提出的研究的主要假設是人GBM中PTEN的喪失導致有絲分裂調節因子的全面上調，其在維持腫瘤細胞的快速增殖中起關鍵作用。我們認為具有過度活化的PI3-K途徑的GBM特別容易受到選擇性抑制有絲分裂紡錘體形成和/或破壞的影響。然而，替莫唑胺的療效受內在和獲得性耐藥性的限制。各種PI3-K化學抑製劑正在臨床試驗中進行測試，但最終毒性和耐藥性面臨巨大挑戰。我們希望我們的研究結果將確定針對有絲分裂機制的新療法，這些機制具有更高的療效和更低的毒性。

14113519.label: Realisation of objectives
14113519.value: Objective 1. Establish a regulatory link between the PTEN/PI3-K pathway and mitotic regulators We have completed this objective. Please refer to Section C for figures. We have conducted an expression analysis of 14 members of the PI3-K pathway and mitotic regulators (PTEN, AKT, FOXO1, EG5, ATM, Aurora B, CENPC, CHK2, Exportin 5, Importin 11, NEK2, RAN, RCC1, and RCC2) in 13 human GBM cell lines. When cells were cultured at 0% serum, the activation states of the PI3-K pathway (based on p-AKT levels) showed concordance with CHK2, NEK2, and RCC2 (Fig. S7). RCC1 showed less concordance. In a separate attempt to link PI3-K pathway and mitotic regulators, we utilized bioinformatic approach of Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) of TCGA cohort to search for PTEN regulated genes (Fig.1A). To identify those PTEN-regulated genes that may be involved in glioma, we utilized a Pten-null astrocyte model. By RT-qPCR, only RCC1 and RCC2 have been confirmed significantly upregulated in Pten-null astrocytes (Fig.1F). However, Western blotting analysis confirmed a significant increase in RCC2 but not RCC1 protein levels in Pten-null lysates (Fig.1G). To determine whether PTEN regulates RCC2 expression via PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, glioma cells were treated with various inhibitors PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. We utilized different combinations of inhibitors to get a full inhibition of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway. As shown in Fig. S2A, the combination treatments displayed variable inhibition on RCC2 levels. In A1172, any two combinations or the triple combination resulted in a ~4-fold decrease in RCC2 expression levels. In U87 cells, combinations of rapamycin and MK2206 or PX866, or the triple combination, resulted in greater than 3-fold suppression of RCC2 expression levels (Fig. S2A). Collectively, these results imply that RCC2 is a downstream transcriptional target of the PTEN/PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, and it was the main focus of this study. Objective 2. Delineate how PTEN and the mitotic regulators modulate the GBM phenotypes We have completed this objective. Please refer to Section C for figures. RCC2 mRNA levels were positively associated with the histological grade and poor prognosis of gliomas (Fig. 2B&C). RCC2 silencing significantly suppressed cell proliferation (Fig. 2D and S2C), and impaired wound-healing ability by ~30% (Fig. S2D). Using CRISPR-Cas9 to knockout RCC2 in glioma cell lines, resulted in a ~30% decrease in the number of Ki67+ cells (Fig. S2E), and reduced colony-formation (Fig. S3A). In addition, RCC2 silencing resulted in a 30-60% reduction in the number of M-phase cells (Fig. S3C&D). By RNA-seq analysis, we have identified hexose kinase 2 (HK2) as a transcriptional target of RCC2 (Fig. 2D-G, 3A-E). HK2 is a member of the hexokinase family and has been reported to catalyze the crucial first step of glycolysis. Indeed, RCC2-knockout in glioma cells showed downregulated HK2 levels (Fig. 3F and S4F), and overexpression of RCC2 upregulated HK2 levels by ~2-fold, suggesting the positive regulation of HK2 by RCC2 (Fig. 3G). For glucose metabolism, RCC2 knockout resulted in a significant downregulation of glucose uptake (Fig. 3H), lowered energy demand, decreased basal respiration rate and baseline extracellular acidification rate (Fig. 3I). These results suggest that RCC2 may positively regulate both glycolytic and oxidative metabolism. To identify the metabolites involved, targeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis of selected metabolites was conducted in RCC2-knockout A1235 and A1172 cells. Overall, 22 metabolites in glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) were enriched (Fig. 4A). Notably, we observed decreases in the levels of ribose-5-phosphate (R5P), an intermediate of the PPP, upon RCC2 knockout in both cell lines (Fig. 4B). R5P has been reported to be involved in the biosynthesis of both DNA and RNA. These results imply that RCC2 may upregulate R5P levels to sustain glioma cell proliferation. Thus, RCC2 may exert its oncogenic effect on glioma by regulating glycolysis and the non-oxidative PPP (Fig.4E). To identify the transcriptional factor (TF) for HK2, Metascape, GeneHancer, and CSan bioinformatics tools, were used and BACH1 was the top-ranked TF (Fig. 5A & S6B). RCC2-knockout glioma cell lines showed downregulated BACH1 levels (Fig. 5D) and RCC2 overexpression upregulated BACH1 protein level (Fig. 5E). Unexpectedly, BACH1 mRNA levels were not altered, suggesting that RCC2 may regulate the stability of the BACH1 protein (Fig. 5B). Indeed, the half-life of endogenous BACH1 reduced from ~10 hrs to ~5 hrs in RCC2-knockdown cells (Fig. 5H-I & S6D-E). We further showed that BACH1 binds the promoter region of the HK2 gene by chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)-qPCR analysis (Fig. 5G). We also delineated how RCC2 affects the stability of BACH1. First, RCC2 suppressed the ubiquitination and thus the degradation of BACH1 (Fig. 6A&B). Next, we localized the region of ubiquitination to the C-terminal of BACH1 by using a C-terminal truncated mutant, BACH1 (L630*) (Fig. 6C). We further mapped the residues involved to 4 lysine residues, K640R, K655R, K657R, and K731R by using a compound mutant BACH14R:K640/655/657/731R (Fig. 6C&D). As expected, the half-life of BACH14R protein was prolonged compared with BACH1 wild type protein (Fig. 6G). Objective 3. Test whether mice lacking PTEN PDZ-BD can modulate gliomagenesis. We have completed this objective. Please refer to Section C for figures. We established a GBM model as proposed by injecting Cre-inducible pTomo lentiviral vectors carrying H-Ras V12 and RCC2 into either Pten Pdz+/+ or Pten Pdz-/- mice carrying a GFAP-Cre transgene for astrocytic-specific gene expression. To examine the expression levels of the lentiviral constructs, expression plasmids were transfected either alone or together with Cre recombinase (Cre-GFP) in 293T cells. Robust expression of 4- and 20-fold over background was observed for RCC2 and H-Ras Val12, respectively, only in cells co-transfected with GFP-Cre plasmid (Fig. S8). Following co-injection of H-Ras V12+RCC2 lentiviruses into the hippocampal region, mice were monitored by pre-determined pathological criteria for 7 months. Mice were sacrificed when humane endpoints have been reached. As shown in Fig. S9, by the 7-month timepoint, 30% of the Pten Pdz+/+ mice displayed neurological symptoms while 75% of the Pten Pdz-/- mice have phenotypes. This implies the PDZ domain of PTEN may be involved in suppressing gliomagenesis induced by Ras+RCC2 in this mouse model. Objective 4. Examining the anti-tumor effects of targeting the PTEN-regulated mitotic regulators We have completed this objective. Please refer to Section C for figures. To explore the oncogenic role of RCC2 in vivo, A1235 control or RCC2-knockout cells were injected subcutaneously in nude mice. The average tumor weight was 90% less in the A1235 RCC2-knockout group than in the control group, suggesting that RCC2 is essential for tumorigenicity in vivo (Fig. 2E). In parallel, U87 RCC2-knockout cells were used to establish intracranial xenograft model. The RCC2 knockout prolonged survival of intracranial tumor-bearing mice when compared with control (Fig.2F). By using the same GBM mouse model in Objective 3, we tested the ability of RCC2 in promoting Ras+Pten+/fl induced gliomagenesis. As shown in Fig. S10A-B, Ras alone or in combination with RCC2 only induced modest neurological deficits in Pten+/+ (WT) mice. On the contrary, neurological manifests were observed with greater frequency in astrocyte-specific Pten heterozygous mice (Fig. S10C-D). More importantly, RCC2 augmented the effect of Ras significantly. This implies the RCC2 plays a promoting role in gliomagenesis induced by Ras and Pten hemizygosity.

14113519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113519.value: There are 4 major findings from this project. First, we have evaluated the interplay between the PI3-K pathway and a broad array of mitotic regulators in a panel of GBM cell lines. Together with bioinformatic tools, we identified the mitotic regulator, RCC2, as being most correlated with PTEN/PI3-K pathway status in human gliomas. Second, by focusing on RCC2, we delineated a novel signaling axis involving RCC2 in glucose metabolism through the transcriptional upregulation of hexokinase 2 (HK2). We further identified the transcription factor, BACH1, being involved in upregulating HK2 expression through binding to its promoter region. On the other hand, RCC2 regulates BACH1 through stabilizing its protein by binding to the C-terminal tail region of BACH1 and thereby suppressing its ubiquitination and subsequent degradation. Higher RCC2 expression is associated with high-grade gliomas and silencing RCC2 in multiple glioma cell lines resulted in growth suppression, reduced motility, M-phase depletion and attenuated tumorigenicity. Thirdly, using a Pten Pdz-/- knockout mouse model, we have shown that the PDZ-binding motif (PDZ-BM) of PTEN is involved in supressing glioma formation driven by the co-expression of Ras and RCC2. However, since we failed to detect any physical interaction between PTEN and RCC2, we did not further pursue the role of PTEN PDZ-BM in terms of identify the interacting partner(s). Finally, by using a Pten+/- animal, we observed the ability of RCC2 to augment the ability of H-Ras V12 in inducing glioma in this mouse model. In term of the novelty of our finding, RCC2 has previously been implicated in kinetochore-microtubule interaction during prometaphase. Separately, RCC2 has also been known to be regulated by p53 and play a role in suppressing metastasis in colon cancer. Our finding assign a novel biological function to RCC2 as a promotor of glucose metabolism, and especially pentose phosphate pathway.

14113519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113519.value: Based on our findings, RCC2 is the latest PTEN regulated genes uncovered in human gliomas. There are three major unanswered questions to be addressed. First, which structural domain(s) within RCC2 are responsible for its three biological activities - mitosis, motility and metabolism. RCC2 is composed of 7 RCC1-like repeats interspersed with a switchback loop, a disordered region loop, and a -hairpin loop. For that, we will generate a series of RCC2 mutants to delete or domain swapping with those from RCC1. These mutants will be tested for any altered M-phase progression, migration and glucose metabolism. They will also be tested for their abilities in regulating the following downstream effectors – RalA (mitosis), Rac1 (migration), and HK2 (metabolism). Second, the link between PTEN PDZ-BM and RCC2 will be studied. PTEN PD-BM regulates mitotic spindle assembly through binding to DLG1/EG5. For this , we will examine the glioma induced in objective for evidence of M phase defects. Finally, we would like to investigate how the loss of PTEN can lead to gliomagenesis through RCC2. For that, we will utilize the animal model in objective 4 to delineate defects in M phase, cell migration and metabolism at different stages of gliomagenesis.

14113519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113519.value: This research project studied the underlying mechanism of how an aggressive form of human brain cancer can acquire the ability to proliferate uncontrollably, spread to other brain regions, and survive in a hostile nutrient poor environment. By studying the network of genes frequently mutated in high-grade brain cancers, a new player has been identified. This molecule, RCC2, plays a multifaceted role in brain cancer formation. It has been known that RCC2 can regulate cell division and cell migration. This project further assigns a new function to RCC2 and that is cell metabolism. In particular, RCC2 promotes brain cancer cells to take up glucose and turn them into building blocks of cellular machinery. We further delineated the detailed steps involved through biochemical and bioinformatics approaches. In addition, we have established two new brain cancer models in mice to firmly establish a critical role of RCC2 in brain tumor formation. The multifaceted role of RCC2 in brain cancer formation renders this molecule a potential target for drug development. The knowledge gained and the animal models established in this project will be invaluable for pursuing this goal.

14113819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14113819.value: Parkinson’s disease is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder that affects up to 3% of people over 65 years of age, in particular incapacitating their locomotive function and other motor abilities. Dopamine deficiency in the striatum as a result of neuronal loss in midbrain substantia nigra is the immediate cause of Parkinson’s disease. As there are still no practical ways to prevent or decelerate the death of dopamine neurons, effective means to suppress the symptoms via different approaches would still be the most important strategy to manage this disorder in the years to come. Significant knowledge has been accumulated in the past in understanding the pathogenesis of Parkinson’s disease and the neurophysiological mechanisms and perturbations underlying the disease and its symptoms. In the cortex-basal ganglia-cortex feedback loop, while aberrant neuronal and network activities in various basal ganglia nuclei have been well documented, the pathological changes in the motor cortex, which directly controls movement, are appreciated only relatively recently. There is emerging evidence that motor cortex output neurons may directly contribute to parkinsonian motor symptoms, but the relationship between their abnormal activities and motor ability is still largely unknown. In this study, based on our previous published findings and recently obtained preliminary results in the mouse model, we propose that the subthreshold, synaptic activities of deep output neurons in the primary motor cortex are directly correlated to different locomotive states, namely quiescence, movement and specific limb actions. Also, in parkinsonism, as a result of basal ganglia circuit malfunctions, network-driven aberration in synaptic inputs via the motor thalamus directly causes pathological activities of motor cortical neurons, leading to impaired locomotive ability of the subjects. To test these hypotheses directly, we will apply in vivo whole-cell patch-clamp recordings from the motor cortex of awake behaving normal and parkinsonian mice, to record the firing activities, membrane dynamics and synaptic input events to the neurons. Optogenetic manipulation of motor thalamic activities combined with in vivo recordings will be used to determine the role of anomalous synaptic inputs from the thalamic feedback pathway. The results of this project would not only provide a wealth of critical information in understanding how movement and movement-related parameters are encoded or represented in the output neurons of the motor cortex, but could also provide insights into the pathogenic process of motor deficits in Parkinson’s disease, and the exploration of evidence-based therapeutic strategy directly targeting the motor cortex. 帕金森病是第二種最常見的神經退行性疾病，其影響多達3％的65歲以上的人，特別是使他們的運動能力喪失能力。 中腦黑質神經元丟失導致紋狀體多巴胺缺乏是帕金森病的直接原因。 由於仍然沒有實際的方法來預防或減緩多巴胺神經元的死亡，通過不同方法抑制症狀的有效方法仍然是未來幾年治療這種疾病的最重要策略。 過去在了解帕金森病的發病機理以及該疾病及其症狀的神經生理機制和干擾方面積累了大量知識。 在皮質 - 基底神經節 - 皮質反饋環中，雖然已經發現了各種基底神經節核中的異常神經元和網絡活動，但是直接控制運動的運動皮層的病理變化僅在最近才被認識到。 有證據表明運動皮質輸出神經元可能直接導致帕金森病運動症狀，但其異常活動與運動能力之間的關係仍然很大程度上還未知。 在這項研究中，基於我們先前發表的研究結果和最近在小鼠模型中獲得的初步結果，我們提出初級運動皮層中輸出神經元的突觸活動與不同的運動狀態直接相關，即靜止，運動和特定的肢體動作。此外，在帕金森病中，由於基底神經節神經迴路故障，通過丘腦運動的突觸輸入的網絡驅動的異常直接引起運動皮層神經元的病理活動，導致受試者的運動能力受損。為了直接測試這些假設，我們將應用來自清醒行為正常和帕金森病小鼠的運動皮質的體內全細胞膜片鉗記錄，以記錄神經元的活動和突觸輸入。結合體內記錄的運動丘腦活動的光遺傳學操作將用於確定來自丘腦反饋途徑的異常突觸的作用。 這項目的結果不僅提供了大量關鍵信息，了解運動和運動相關參數如何在運動皮層的輸出神經元中編碼，還可以提供對帕金森氏症運動缺陷致病過程的了解, 以及直接針對運動皮層的治療策略的探索。

14113819.label: Realisation of objectives
14113819.value: We have conducted experiments largely according to the proposal plan, as described below. Objective 1: To investigate whether there are changes in intrinsic properties of motor cortex output neurons contributing to altered firing activities in parkinsonian mice To address this question, in vivo whole-cell patch-clamp technique was applied to record the intrinsic properties, membrane potential dynamics and synaptic activities from M1 layer 5b neurons in head-fixed anaesthetized and awake normal and MPTP (1-methyl-4-phenyl- 1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine)-treated mice. MPTP mice exhibited reduced locomotive activity and dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra pars compacta. In these animals, M1 output neurons showed increased firing rate, especially during movement. The firing activity was behavioral state-dependent changes bidirectionally. Intriguingly, no neurons showed suppressed firing rate during movement in the MPTP mice. More importantly, burst firing activity increased in moving and anesthetized MPTP mice. The changed firing activity was not induced by changes in intrinsic properties of the neurons, including input resistance and membrane time constant, since these parameters remain unchanged. Objective 2: To decipher how locomotive status are represented by motor cortex output neurons at the neuronal and synaptic levels, and how they are altered in parkinsonism Quantitative analysis of EPSCs revealed that the properties of EPSCs, including amplitude, rise time and decay time of EPSC were unchanged during different movement states. The results indicated that the averaged EPSC rate during quiet status kept a relatively steady level in 2 s window. Around 0.3 s before movement initiation, the EPSC rate significantly increased and continued increasing till at 0.3 s after motion initiation to reach the maximum rate. Statistic analysis indicated that the EPSC rate was significantly increased after motion start compared to those before the start, suggesting dense excitatory synaptic inputs to the M1 neurons to initiate and accelerate movement speed. The EPSC rate gradually reduced during motion and stopped states to a lower level than those in quiescence, which was consistent with the previous findings of the reduced firing rates during movement in M1. In parallel, EPSCs occurring in bursts followed a similar pattern. The EPSC burst rate was significantly increased after motion started and then reduced during and after motion, which suggested the enhanced bursty excitatory synaptic inputs during initial motion acceleration, and then gradually reduced bursty inputs after reaching the maximum speed. Together, these results indicated that the excitatory synaptic inputs showed a clearly pattern change in different motion states, and the increased bursty inputs contributed to the motion initiation and acceleration. A parallel analysis in MPTP (PD) animals indicated that excitatory synaptic inputs were diminished, and the input source might be changed during movement in MPTP mice. Furthermore, when we analysed the frequency bands of membrane currents, we found that MPTP mice exhibited abnormally changes, especially the increased beta frequency bands during movement, which might be explained by the changes in EPSCs. Overall, we detected aberration in EPSCs that could account for motor deficit under Parkinsonism. Objective 3: To determine the contributions of motor thalamic inputs to the activities of motor cortex neurons and their aberrations in parkinsonian mice Results from retrograde beads and anterograde virus indicated that multiple brain areas send projections to M1 layer 5 output neurons, among which the ventral anterior and lateral thalamus provide dense excitatory synaptic input. By means of optogenetics, we functionally inhibit these thalamic neurons when the MPTP mice were under whole-cell in vivo recording at the same time. We found that the increased firing rate was significantly reduced by inhibition and quickly recovered to abnormal levels after inhibition. Importantly, corresponding changes in motion was observed. The difference in neuronal firing between normal and parkinsonian animals was reversibly diminished by the intermittent photoinhibition. Moreover, the increased burst activity (burst rate and burst duration) was suppressed during photoinhibition in MPTP mice M1 neurons. Unfortunately, because of the pandemic, the results had not been reported via scientific conferences. Also, because of the departure of the PhD student undertaking this project and the time required to analyse the large volume of data via computational/statistical approaches, the manuscript for disseminating is still in progress but is expected to be completed in the second half of this year.

14113819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14113819.value: The primary motor cortex (M1) is responsible for voluntary movement. Although decoding of M1 neuronal spiking represented motion has been well established, how the synaptic activity of M1 characterized movement has not been explored. To record the synaptic inputs of M1 neurons during voluntary movement, we applied in vivo whole-cell patch-clamp technique in awake head-fixed mice. Excitatory synaptic currents of M1 layer 5 neurons were recorded and analyzed as phasic inputs under different motion states. Based on input frequency, EPSCs were separated to burst EPSCs and sporadic EPSCs. Our data revealed that burst EPSCs help start and accelerate motion speed in control mice. However, the EPSC inputs maintain a relatively lower level during and after motion than those under quiescence. In parkinsonian mice, the overall excitatory synaptic inputs were reduced, but robustly increased to the similar level as healthy mice during locomotion, due to the increased sporadic EPSCs inputs. Time-frequency analysis indicated the increased sporadic EPSCs in MPTP mice were at the beta frequency band. Furthermore, EPSC rate were better correlated to speed and would improve the relationship after MPTP administration. Taken together, these findings revealed the representation of voluntary movement, especially initiation and maintenance, by the excitatory synaptic activity of M1 neurons in physiological and pathological conditions. Results from retrograde beads and anterograde virus indicated that multiple brain areas send projections to M1 layer 5 output neurons, among which the ventral anterior and lateral thalamus provide dense excitatory synaptic input. By means of optogenetics, we inhibited these thalamic neurons when the MPTP mice were under whole-cell in vivo recording at the same time. We found that the increased firing rate was significantly reduced by inhibition and quickly recovered to abnormal levels after inhibition. Importantly, corresponding changes in motion was observed. The increased burst activity (burst rate and burst duration) was suppressed during photoinhibition in MPTP mice M1 neurons.

14113819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14113819.value: Our in vivo whole-cell patch study of the correlation of excitatory synaptic inputs and movements in normal animals and aberrant changes in M1 of MPTP-treated mice provide unprecedented details of the potential contributions of anomaly in Parkinsonism. This findings corroborate with previous publications highlighting the role of M1 in Parkinson's disease and thus as a therapeutic target. Future grant proposals could target this line of research.

14113819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14113819.value: In this study, we explored the functional changes and role of excitatory synaptic activity of primary motor cortex layer 5 neurons under different locomotion states in both healthy and parkinsonian mice. Different parameters of excitatory synaptic inputs were analyzed and played distinct roles under various motion states. In healthy mice, burst excitatory post-synaptic currents (EPSCs) assisted in initiating and accelerating motion, but the EPSCs inputs were gradually decreased during motion till the motion terminated. In Parkinsonian mice, the excitatory synaptic inputs were reduced and became more sporadic. More importantly, EPSCs encoded motion speed and direction and better-predicted motion states in Parkinsonian mice. The source of inputs to M1 neurons were also traced to the motor thalamus, which is subject to neural intervention. Our findings corroborate with previous publications highlighting the role of M1 in Parkinson's disease and thus as a therapeutic target.

14115019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115019.value: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) as the most lethal type of breast cancer highly occurring in younger population, is more likely to metastasize to distant sites during the early stage. Although therapeutic strategies are effective in treating early breast cancer, most TNBC patients present with late stage tumors with metastasis or relapse. Thus, more mechanistic studies are urgently needed to develop better biomarkers and more specific therapeutic strategy for TNBC. Proteasome dysfunction and abnormal accumulation of oncoproteins contribute to cancer pathogenesis. ‘RING’ motif proteins are the largest group of E3 ubiquitin ligases. Ubiquitin- proteasome pathway (UPP) has been well-documented as therapeutic targets in breast tumorigenesis. The agents targeting specific proteins for proteasomal degradation has entered Phase II clinical trial in metastatic breast cancer patients. Thus, identifying and characterizing RING finger ubiquitin ligases is important for further understanding the molecular pathogenesis of TNBC. Through our previous studies of integrative genome studies in breast cancer, we identified a novel RING finger gene (RINES), located at frequent loss region 5q. In our pilot studies, we found that RINES was frequently downregulated in TNBC tumors, which is associated with poor survival of breast cancer patients. Promoter CpG methylation mediates RINES silencing. RINES methylation was detected in breast tumors but rarely in normal breast tissues, suggesting a tumor-specific methylation. Ectopic expression of RINES inhibited tumor cell growth and induced apoptosis, indicating its role as a tumor suppressor. RINES contains RING finger domain, coiled-coil domain and transmembrane domain, thus may potentially modulate protein ubiquitination. We found that RINES downregulated STAT3 protein levels. In this study, we will study the roles and mechanisms of RINES as an E3 ubiquitin ligase in TNBC pathogenesis. We will assess: 1) RINES suppresses metastatic potential of TNBC tumor cells; 2) STAT3 as a substrate of RINES for ubiquitination and degradation; 3) Inhibition of tumor sphere formation by RINES requires the RING domain; 4) RINES deregulates actin networks in TNBC cells via STAT3 signaling; 5) RINES re-sensitizes resistance of TNBC cells to drug targeting ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. My study will provide not only deep insight into the roles of RING finger proteins as tumor suppressors in breast tumorigenesis, but also a new paradigm linking epigenetic modifications and protein ubiquitination, and further elucidate the signaling network of RINES-STAT3 in breast cancer cells, which helps to develop targeted therapy. 三陰性乳腺癌（TNBC）作為在年輕人群中高度發生的最致命類型的乳腺癌，在早期階段更可能轉移到遠處。儘管目前的治療策略在治療早期乳腺癌方面是有效的，但是大多數TNBC患者惡變為轉移或複發的晚期腫瘤。因此，迫切需要更多的機制研究來研發更好的生物標誌物和TNBC治療策略。 蛋白酶體功能障礙和癌蛋白的異常積累有助於癌症的發生和惡性演進。 'RING'基序蛋白是E3泛素連接酶中最大的一組。泛素 - 蛋白酶體途徑（UPP）已被充分認為乳腺腫瘤發生中的治療靶標。靶向特定蛋白質用於蛋白酶體降解的藥劑已進入轉移性乳腺癌患者的II期臨床試驗。因此，鑑定和闡明RING泛素連接酶對於進一步理解TNBC的分子發病機理是重要的。 通過我們前期對乳腺癌整合基因組的研究，我們發現了一種新的RING基因（RINES），位於染色體頻繁丟失區域5q。在我們的試驗研究中，我們發現RINES在TNBC腫瘤中下調，這與乳腺癌患者的生存率低有關。啟動子CpG甲基化介導RINES沉默，在乳腺腫瘤中檢測到RINES甲基化，但在正常乳腺組織中很少檢測到甲基化，這表明RINES的腫瘤特異性甲基化。 RINES的異位表達可抑制腫瘤細胞生長並誘導細胞凋亡，表明其作為腫瘤抑製因子的作用。 RINES含有RING指結構域，捲曲螺旋結構域和跨膜結構域，因此可能潛在地調節蛋白質泛素化。我們發現RINES下調STAT3蛋白水平。在本研究中，我們將研究RINES作為E3泛素連接酶在TNBC發病機制中的作用和機制。我們將評估：1）RINES抑制TNBC腫瘤細胞的轉移潛能; 2）STAT3作為RINES泛素化降解的底物; 3）RINES抑制腫瘤球形成需要RING結構域; 4）RINES通過STAT3信號傳導調節TNBC細胞中的肌動蛋白網絡; 5）RINES使TNBC細胞對靶向泛素 - 蛋白酶體途徑的藥物抗性再敏感。我的研究不僅深入了解RING指蛋白作為腫瘤抑制因子在乳腺腫瘤發生中的作用，而且提供了一種將表觀遺傳修飾與蛋白質泛素化聯繫起來的新範式，並進一步闡明了乳腺癌細胞中RINES-STAT3的信號傳導網絡，有助於開發靶向治療。

14115019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14115019.value: Major findings Aberrantly activated RAS signaling is frequently observed in ESC. However, Ras mutations are rarely detected in ESCC tumors, highlighting the importance of epigenetic disruption of Ras signaling balance in ESCC pathogenesis. This study identifies a novel RasGAP gene, RASAL3, frequently silenced by promoter CpG methylation in ESCC, which contributes to the aberrant activation of RAS signaling in ESCC. RASAL3 antagonizes Ras signaling and inhibits ESCC cell metastasis. Low RASAL3 expression is inversely correlated with cancer patient survival. RASAL3 promoter methylation in ESCC is tumor-specific, which could be used as a potential biomarker for ESCC diagnosis. Research outcome We published one paper in Clinical Epigenetics and submitted one revision in Cell Death Differentiation, one in submission. We attended 1 related international/local conference. Due to the impact of COVID-19 during the project implementation, the progress of the project was partially delayed, but the task of the project was completed finally. The research results of this project " RING finger protein RINES suppresses breast cancer metastasis by targeting STAT3 for proteasomal degradation" has been shown in the attachment, but further polishing and modification of this manuscript is needed before the final submission. I attended an expert panel discussion for a conference. 14115019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14115019.value: Breast cancer is one of the leading causes of death among women in Hong Kong, thus molecular study of its pathogenesis helps to develop biomarkers and target therapy for this tumor, including Hong Kong, with metastasis and recurrence as the major cause of patient death. Molecular mechanistic studies (including epigenetics) on its metastasis pathogenesis are urgently needed. Our study will provide deep molecular insight into the functions and mechanisms of RINES, a 5q12 RING finger protein, acting as an E3 ubiquitin ligase by targeting STAT3 for degradation in breast cancer. Moreover, the tumor-specific methylation of the RINES promoter could serve as an epigenetic biomarker for breast cancer diagnosis and prognosis prediction, benefiting patients in China including Hong Kong and the world.

14115319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14115319.value: Skeletal muscle allows voluntary movement and plays a key role in regulating metabolism and homeostasis in the organism. Meanwhile it has a remarkable ability to regenerate after injury thus provides an excellent model to study tissue regeneration. Muscle regeneration relies on its resident muscle stem cells (also called satellite cells, SCs) which normally lie quiescently beneath muscle fiber. SCs can quickly activate and proliferate following injury, then differentiate and fuse into myofiber; meanwhile a subset of SCs undergoes self-renewal and returns to quiescent state to replenish the adult stem cell pool. Each state of the myogenic lineage progression is orchestrated by complex regulatory networks of intrinsic and extrinsic factors/mechanisms. Disruption of the regulations may render their loss of ability to regenerate, contributing to muscle wasting conditions such as muscular dystrophy, cachexia, and sarcopenia that are prevalent in our society. Post-transcriptional regulation of mRNA by RNA binding proteins (RBPs) exerts critical functions in many biological processes but its importance in SCs remains largely elusive. Here we propose to investigate the functional roles of a RBP and helicase, Dhx36 in regulating SC activities and muscle regeneration process. In the pilot study, we found inducible deletion of Dhx36 in SCs hampered myoblast proliferation thus delayed muscle regeneration after acute muscle injury. To elucidate the underlying mechanisms, by combined Dhx36 CLIP-seq, rG4-seq and Polysomal profiling, we provide the binding landscape of endogenous Dhx36 and transcriptome wide rG4 formation in myoblast cells. We demonstrated Dhx36 can bind to diversified regions of a wide range of mRNAs, among which Gnai2 encodes a protein known to promote SC proliferation and its binding at 5’UTR rG4 site may facilitate Gnai2 translation. These preliminary results lead us to hypothesize that Dhx36 is a critical regulator of SC proliferation through its diversified binding ability and versatile functions in orchestrating post-transcriptional processing of RNAs. Three aims are thus proposed (1) to further characterize Dhx36 function in skeletal muscle satellite cells and muscle regeneration. (2) to investigate Dhx36/rG4 mediated translational regulation of Gnai2 in muscle satellite cells. (3) to explore other aspects of Dhx36 regulation of mRNA metabolism. Once completed, this study will for the first time uncover Dhx36 as a novel RBP regulator of SC function and muscle regeneration; it will thus enhance our knowledge foundation in the post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle regeneration for future therapeutic development of treating muscle damages and diseases. 骨骼肌不僅是人體的重要運動器官並調節生物體內的新陳代謝和機體平衡，同時它具有非凡的再生能力從而成為研究組織再生的模型體系。骨骼肌再生依賴於肌纖維中的成體幹細胞（也稱為衛星細胞，SCs）。它們通常處於靜息狀態，但在肌肉受損時可以快速激活並增殖，然後分化並融合成肌纖維;同時一部分SC返回靜止狀態以補充幹細胞群。這個過程中的每一步都由內在和外在因素/機制精細調控，如有差錯可能會影響再生能力，從而促進肌肉萎縮症，惡病質和肌肉減少症等疾病的形成。RNA結合蛋白（RBPs）對mRNA的轉錄后調節在許多生物過程中發揮關鍵作用，但其重要性在SC中仍然未知。在這個研究中，我們將解析一個RBP,Dhx36對SC活動和肌肉再生過程的調節。在初步研究中，我們發現SC中Dhx36的誘導性缺失阻礙了成肌細胞的增殖從而延遲了急性肌肉損傷后的再生。通過結合Dhx36 CLIP-seq，rG4-seq和Polysomal Profiling數據，我們發現 Dhx36可以結合上千種mRNA的多種區域。其中一個靶點Gnai2 mRNA的5'UTR rG4有很強的Dhx36結合，該結合可促進rG4解旋從而增強Gnai2翻譯。這些初步結果使我們假設Dhx36是通過其多樣化的結合能力和多樣性調節功能促進SC增殖和肌肉再生。我們因此提出三個研究目標（1）進一步鑑定Dhx36缺失對骨骼肌衛星細胞和肌肉再生的影響。 （2）進一步研究Dhx36 / rG4介導的對Gnails的翻譯調控。 （3）繼續探討Dhx36對mRNA代謝的其他方面的調控。一旦完成這項研究， 我們將首次揭開Dhx36在肌肉再生中的調節機制, 增強我們對轉錄后調控的認識，從而為肌肉相關疾病的未來治療提供理論基礎。

14115319.label: Realisation of objectives
14115319.value: Objective 1: To further characterize Dhx36 function in SC and muscle regeneration. To further test Dhx36 cell-autonomous functions in SCs during muscle regeneration, we crossed Dhx36fl/fl mice with Pax7CreER/ROSAEYFP mice to specifically induce Dhx36 deletion in adult SCs. Genetic inactivation of Dhx36 in SCs was induced by intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection of tamoxifen (Tmx) in adult (8-12 weeks old) mice for five consecutive days followed by five days of chase. We next examined whether loss of Dhx36 in SCs impacts adult muscle regeneration, by intramuscular injection of BaCl2, which induced acute damage followed by regeneration to an extent similar to CTX injection, in control and iKO mice. At 5 dpi, regenerating fibers with centrally localized nuclei were readily observed in control damaged muscles while they were rare in iKO damaged muscles, which still presented abundant immune cell infiltrates. At 7 dpi, regeneration in iKO muscles was still significantly compromised, with newly formed myofibers much smaller than those in control mice. eMyHC staining confirmed delayed muscle regeneration in iKO mice: at 5 dpi, both control and iKO injured muscles presented eMyHC+ fibers, which were larger in control mice, as shown by myofiber cross-sectional area (CSA) measurement; at 7 dpi, however, eMyHC+ fibers were no longer present in control muscles but persisted in iKO muscles, consistent with the larger size of newly-formed myofibers in control muscles as compared to iKO muscles. At 28 dpi, regeneration of TA muscles had advanced in both control and iKO mice; however, this process was still severely compromised in iKO mice, which had significantly smaller new fibers as compared to control mouse muscles, consistent with their 22%-reduced muscle weight. Thus, deletion of Dhx36 in SCs markedly blunts adult muscle regeneration, indicating its requirement for this process. Objective 2: To investigate Dhx36/rG4 mediated translational regulation of Gnai2 in SC. To validate the rG4 formation in the identified site of Gnai2 5’UTR, we found that the G-rich region is very conserved among multiple species, and that it is predicted to form a canonical rG4 structure. ThT probing showed that the 5’-UTR of WT Gnai2 exhibited an enhanced emission at 490-nm wavelength in K+ conditions as compared to Li+ conditions which was largely lost upon G4 mutation. Probing with the additional G4 ligand NMM confirmed that the WT but not mutated 5’-UTR formed an rG4 in K+ conditions. Next, to validate the interaction between the above identified rG4 site and DHX36, we performed RNA pull-down assays and found that the WT 5’-UTR sequence retrieved a significant amount of DHX36 protein, which was completely lost in the GGG-to-GAG mutated sequence. Consistently, RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP) experiment showed that the Dhx36 antibody effectively retrieved Gnai2 mRNA but not control RNAs. Moreover, when myoblast cells were treated with carboxyPDS (cPDS, a derivative of PDS which stabilizes rG4), the interaction between DHX36 and Gnai2 mRNA was significantly enhanced. Altogether, these results strengthened the finding that DHX36 interacts with the 5-UTR of Gnai2 through its rG4 site. To further investigate the translational control exerted by DHX36 in myoblasts, we found that the GNAI2 protein, but not Gnai2 mRNA, was significantly reduced in both activated SCs from Dhx36-iKO mice compared with those from control mice as well as in proliferating Dhx36-KO C2C12 myoblasts as compared to control myoblasts. Moreover, we found that GNAI2 protein expression was significantly downregulated after cPDS treatment of SCs or C2C12 myoblasts while the mRNA level increased or were unaltered, suggesting that GNAI2 protein levels were indeed regulated by the G4 structure. Interestingly, we also found that SC proliferation was significantly decreased after cPDS treatment. To further study whether DHX36 modulation of Gnai2 mRNA translation is mediated by resolving the rG4 formation, we generated a EGFP reporter by inserting the WT or mutated full-length 5’-UTR of Gnai2 to the upstream of the EGFP ORF in a pEGFP-N1 plasmid. When transfected into C2C12 myoblasts, the protein levels of EGFP of all three WT reporters were drastically decreased as compared with the corresponding mutated reporters as measured by Western blot of the EGFP protein levels. Lastly, to test the functional connection of DHX36 and GNAI2 in SC proliferation, we tested SCs transfected with siRNAs against Gnai2, a modest but significantly decreased level of EdU incorporation was observed. Conversely, when SCs were transduced with Gnai2-expressing lentivirus, cell proliferation was promoted with a 26.9% increase in EdU+ SCs. These results thus suggested that DHX36 and GNAI2 conform a regulatory axis for SC proliferation. In fact, transduction of SCs from Dhx36 iKO with a Gnai2-expressing virus led to a 28.5% increase in EdU+ cells as compared to SCs infected with control virus. Moreover, overexpression of the Dhx36 plasmid also increased the GNAI2 protein level and rescued SC proliferation, with a 30.8% increase. Altogether, the above results demonstrate that GNAI2 is indeed a downstream effector of DHX36 in promoting SC proliferation. Objective 3: To explore other aspects of post-transcriptional regulation by Dhx36. Through CLiP-seq of DHX36, we identified the majority of the DHX36 binding peaks (3032; 82.7%) were mapped to protein-coding mRNAs, with a small portion of binding to non-coding RNA (ncRNA) (422), small nucleolar RNA (snoRNA) (142), or other RNA species (66). Thus, DHX36 appears to have a predominant function in regulating mRNA processing. Close examination of mRNA binding revealed a large number of binding sites resided in coding sequence (CDS) (2040) and introns (1345); however, the 5’-UTRs possessed the highest binding density, followed by CDS, 3’-UTR and introns, suggesting that DHX36 carries out its dominant functions through binding and regulating 5’-UTRs. Notably, 216 transcripts had DHX36 binding sites in multiple regions (e.g., in their 5-UTR, 3-UTR and CDS). Gene ontology (GO) analysis of the 1262 genes associated with DHX36 binding, showed enrichment in “regulation of gene expression, epigenetic”, “gene silencing”, and “DNA conformation change”, suggesting that DHX36 has diversified gene regulatory functions. In addition to the G-rich sequences, one type of AREs (often defined as adjacent repeated AUUUA repeats) was also found to be highly enriched (ranking no. 3) in the DHX36-binding regions in 3’-UTR but not in 5’-UTRs or CDS. Previously, DHX36 was shown to bind to ARE motifs and to regulate urokinase plasminogen activator (uPA) mRNA degradation; our finding thus indicated that ARE binding may be a transcriptome-wide event that endows DHX36 with key regulatory functions. Indeed, a total of 292 AREs (within 154 genes) were bound by DHX36, with most in the 3-UTRs; GO analysis revealed that the genes with ARE–DHX36 binding sites in their 3-UTR ARE were enriched for “mesenchyme development”, “cell migration” and “cell morphogenesis involved in differentiation” processes, among others. In addition to the above rG4 and ARE motifs, we noticed that C/U- rich motifs were highly ranked in both 5’-UTRs and 3’-UTRs, although no specific sequences could be identified. Nevertheless, these sequences were predicted to form very similar secondary structure, defined by continuous hairpins with flanking stems, suggesting that DHX36 recognizes other specific secondary structures besides G4 and ARE.

14115319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14115319.value: In this study we show that DHX36, a helicase that unwinds RNA G-quadruplex (rG4) structures, is essential for muscle regeneration by regulating SC expansion. DHX36 (initially named RHAU) is barely expressed at quiescence but is highly induced during SC activation and proliferation. Inducible deletion of Dhx36 in adult SCs causes defective proliferation and muscle regeneration after damage. System-wide mapping in proliferating SCs reveals DHX36 binding predominantly to rG4 structures at various regions of mRNAs, while integrated polysome profiling shows that DHX36 promotes mRNA translation via 5′-untranslated region (UTR) rG4 binding. Furthermore, we demonstrate that DHX36 specifically regulates the translation of Gnai2 mRNA by unwinding its 5′ UTR rG4 structures and identify GNAI2 as a downstream effector of DHX36 for SC expansion. Altogether, our findings uncover DHX36 as an indispensable post-transcriptional regulator of SC function and muscle regeneration acting through binding and unwinding rG4 structures at 5′ UTR of target mRNAs. Our findings were published on Nature Communications, Cell Reports and other Journals with high impact. Our work was also presented in international meetings to increase exposure to peer researchers. Moreover, four PhD students obtained their PhD degree with the support of this project.

14115319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14115319.value: We characterized the functional role of G4 helicase DHX36 in regulating SC activity and muscle regeneration in this study. We demonstrate that DHX36 is induced in activated SCs and functions to promote the proliferative expansion of myoblasts in vitro and in vivo during the regeneration process. Further mechanistic investigation using the CLIP-seq, polysome profiling and Mass spec data of Dhx36 binding proteins in myoblast cells reveals that DHX36 promotes mRNA translation via 5′-untranslated region (UTR) rG4 binding. Specifically we demonstrate that DHX36 regulates the translation of Gnai2 mRNA by unwinding its 5′ UTR rG4 structures and identify GNAI2 as a downstream effector of DHX36 for SC expansion. Since the regenerative capacity of SC declines with aging, which is correlated with muscle aging related disease, e.g. sarcopenia, we could further investigate the functional role of Dhx36 regulation of mRNA translation in SC aging process. Moreover, as DHX36 can bind both RNA and DNA G4 structures, we can also explore other mechanism of DHX36 functions in SCs.

14115319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14115319.value: Adult muscle stem cells, also known as satellite cells (SCs) play pivotal roles in muscle regeneration and the post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression in SCs remains largely unknown. In this study we identify a G4 helicase, DHX36 which is induced in activated SCs upon acute muscle injury. We demonstrate that DHX36 is essential for SC proliferation and mouse muscles regeneration. Mechanistically, we uncover that DHX36 promotes mRNA translation via binding to and resolving the rG4 formed at 5′-untranslated region (UTR) of target mRNAs. Altogether, our findings identify DHX36 as a novel post-transcriptional regulator in SCs to promotes myoblast proliferation and acute injury induced muscle regeneration, which increases the knowledge of regenerative biology for skeletal muscle.

14116119.label: Realisation of objectives
14116119.value: The current project was supported by the study grant from 1 Oct 2019 to 31 Mar 2022. Until then, a total of 243 subjects were recruited, including 25 early drug-naïve PD patients, 115 iRBD patients, 43 iRBD-FDRs, and 60 controls. However, according to our plan, we aimed to recruit 60 controls, 60 iRBD patients, 60 first-degree relatives (iRBD-FDRs), and 30 drug-naïve PD patients. The completion rates for RBD-FDRs and drug-naïve PD patients were only 71.7% and 83.3%, respectively. Therefore, in order to achieve the planned sample size, the recruitment of subjects was continued until 09 Jan 2023. A total of 333 subjects were finally recruited in this study, including 28 early drug-naïve PD patients, 157 iRBD patients, 66 iRBD-FDRs, and 82 controls. Our actual recruitment has reached our planned target sample size except for drug-naïve PD patients (Completion rate: 93.3%, 28/30) and exceeded in both iRBD and control subjects. All subjects have undergone a series of clinical, neurological assessments and a battery of impulsivity measures. The impulse control behaviors were measured by the Questionnaire for Impulsive-Compulsive Disorders in Parkinson’s Disease-Rating Scale. The trait impulsivity was measured by Barratt Impulsiveness Scale 11 (BIS-11). The motor and decisional impulsivity were assessed by a panel of computerized neuropsychological tests, including go/no-go task, four-choice serial reaction time task (4CSRTT), balloon analogue risk task (BART), beads task, and delay/effort discounting task. In brief, the trait impulsivity and impulse control behaviors were not altered among the subjects at early and prodromal stages of α-synucleinopathy. However, reflection impulsivity was increased in drug-naïve PD, iRBD, and probably in high risk iRBD-FDRs, while response inhibition and risk taking were decreased in these subjects. Altered impulsivity was associated with the putative neurodegenerative risk of prodromal PD. These novel findings indicated that a complex construct of altered impulsivity has already occurred at the prodromal stage of α-synucleinopathy (especially at iRBD), which will have implication for underlying pathophysiology and clinical management of α-synucleinopathy.

14116119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116119.value: We have recruited a total of 333 subjects, including 28 early drug-naïve PD patients (mean age ± SD: 70.2 ± 5.8 years, 82.1% man), 157 iRBD patients (67.1 ± 6.7 years, 76.4% man), 66 iRBD-FDRs (63.2 ± 6.5 years, 50.0% man), and 82 controls (67.5 ± 8.0 years, 63.4% man). There were no significant differences in BIS-11 total score and the percentages of impulse control behaviors among the four groups. In terms of decisional impulsivity, the drug-naïve PD and iRBD patients had fewer numbers of extracted beads in beads task 1 (median [IQR]: drug-naive PD vs. iRBD vs. iRBD-FDRs vs. controls: 5.0 [7.0] vs. 6.0 [12.0] vs. 12.0 [13.0] vs. 10.5 [14.0], P<0.001) and task 2 (8.0 [8.0] vs. 10.0 [9.0] vs. 15.0 [9.0] vs. 14.5 [10.0], P<0.001) before making their decisions. In addition, drug-naïve PD and iRBD patients had fewer numbers of pumps of unexploded blue balloons (median [IQR]: drug-naive PD vs. iRBD vs. iRBD-FDRs vs. controls: 8.3 [11.7] vs. 7.7 [7.8] vs. 9.9 [15.6] vs. 11.0 [14.1], P=0.003) in BART than controls. Taken together, these two findings indicated a higher level of reflection impulsivity but a lower level of risk taking in both iRBD and drug-naive PD patients. In addition, in terms of motor impulsivity, iRBD patients had more no-go errors in go/no-go task than controls (median [IQR]: 4.5 [4.0] vs. 4.0 [4.0], Padjusted=0.036). There were more premature responses in 4CSRTT in iRBD patients than that of iRBD-FDRs (median [IQR]: 3.0 [6.0] vs. 2.0 [4.0], Padjusted=0.036). Thus, both tests suggested a higher level of motor impulsivity in iRBD patients. In terms of delay and effort discounting indexes, the results were comparable among four groups. We further investigated the impulsivity among iRBD-FDRs subjects with or without recurrent dream-enactment behaviors (iRBD-FDRsDEBs+ vs. iRBD-FDRsDEBs-). We found that iRBD-FDRsDEBs+ had a marginally fewer numbers of extracted beads in beads task 2 (median [IQR]: 12.0 [9.0] vs. 16.5 [9.0], P=0.082) than iRBD-FDRsDEBs-, suggesting a marginally higher level of reflection impulsivity in iRBD-FDRsDEBs+. In terms of correlation of impulsivity measures and neurodegenerative features, premature responses in 4CSRTT were positively related to the scores of UPDRS-part III excluding action tremor (β=0.30, Padjusted=0.002) in iRBD patients. Besides, The premature responses in 4CSRTT (β = 0.16, Padjusted=0.01) and the no-go errors in go/no-go task (β = 0.13, Padjusted=0.02) were positively associated with the log-transformed total likelihood ratio of prodromal PD, whereas numbers of extracted beads in beads task (β = -0.24, Padjusted <0.001) and pumps of unexploded blue balloons in BART (β = -0.18, Padjusted=0.002) were negatively associated with the log-transformed total likelihood ratio of prodromal PD. In summary, trait impulsivity and impulse control behaviors were not changed among the subjects at early and prodromal stages of α-synucleinopathy. However, reflection impulsivity was increased in drug-naïve PD, iRBD, and probably high risk iRBD-FDRs, while response inhibition and risk taking were decreased in these subjects. Altered impulsivity was associated with the putative neurodegenerative risk of prodromal PD features. These novel findings indicated that a complex construct of altered impulsivity has already occurred at the prodromal stage of α-synucleinopathy (especially at iRBD), which will have significant implication for underlying pathophysiology and clinical management of α-synucleinopathy.

14116119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116119.value: There are several considerations for future research. At first, our study found that there was alteration of impulsivity at the early and prodromal stages of α-synucleinopathy, suggesting the involvement of pathological changes of α-synucleinopathy on the control of impulsivity. Nonetheless, the underlying mechanism remains unknown. Future neuroimaging and preclinical studies are warranted to uncover the detailed mechanisms, especially on the dopaminergic and neural circuitry related to the complex construct of altered impulsivity. Secondly, further longitudinal follow-up studies of these subjects, especially on the trajectory of impulsivity measures and its association with future phenoconversion into α-synucleinopathy are needed. Although our study suggested the association between impulsivity level and neurodegenerative risk, it needs to be further determined whether impulsivity will predict the phenoconversion in iRBD and high risk RBD-FDR subjects. In particular, from the clinical management, it is pertinent to investigate whether altered impulsivity at such early prodromal stage would predict future development of impulse control behaviors/disorders when the PD subjects would start their dopaminergic medications. Therefore, longitudinal follow up studies will help to understand the complex relationships between impulsivity and evolvement of α-synucleinopathy.

14116119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116119.value: This project indicated that iRBD and drug-naïve PD patients had a complex construct of altered impulsivity at which they have lower levels of risk taking and response inhibition but a higher level of reflection impulsivity than healthy controls. In other words, compared to healthy individuals, iRBD and drug-naïve PD patients may have a tendency to prefer lower risk choices/situations to higher risk choices/ situations in their daily life. On the other hand, iRBD and drug-naïve PD patients will deem to make quicker decisions without adequate information and consideration. Together, iRBD and drug-naïve PD patients are conservative about the value at risk, but impulsive in making decisions and motor responses. Thus, it is of importance for physicians and patients’ caregivers to pay more attention to iRBD and drug-naïve PD patients’ daily behaviors and decisions to avoid undesirable outcomes due to their premature and impulsive decisions and motor responses.
