14116719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116719.value: Definitive endoderm (DE) emerging at early embryonic stages gives rise to all endodermal tissues and organs. Wnt signaling is a key player controlling DE specification during in vivo embryogenesis as well as in vitro stem cell differentiation. However, three different Wnt pathways (the canonical Wnt/β-catenin pathway, the noncanonical Wnt/planar cell polarity and Wnt/calcium pathway) exist with extensive complexity, which hampers in-depth investigation. Hence, the regulatory roles of individual Wnt pathways during DE differentiation are still not fully understood. Recently, human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) provides an invaluable in vitro platform to study early differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells. Meanwhile the groundbreaking CRISPR technology permits targeted genome editing with high accuracy and efficiency. Together, these advances have offered new opportunities to study the dynamic and complex Wnt functions during human DE differentiation under in vitro conditions. Our preliminary analysis using chemical inhibitors revealed a previously unreported phenomenon that both canonical and noncanonical Wnt signaling are required for DE differentiation. Interestingly, by generating CTNNB1 knockout hESCs using our recently established CRISPR-based approach, we confirmed that DE differentiation was abolished due to genetic depletion of β-catenin, the central effector of canonical Wnt pathway encoded by CTNNB1 gene. Furthermore, we found that the disruption of noncanonical Wnt pathways by a truncated mediator protein also caused failure of DE differentiation. These results suggest previously unreported functions of Wnt pathways during DE differentiation. In the proposed project, we aim to dissect the functional roles of individual canonical and noncanonical Wnt pathways during DE differentiation from hESCs (Fig. 1). First, we will employ the previously established CTNNB1-/- hESCs and WNT3-/- hESCs, and introduce ectopic expression of the full-length as well as truncated β-catenin, to elucidate the role of canonical Wnt pathway during DE induction. Next, we will generate hESCs carrying knockout of noncanonical Wnt genes ROR2 or WNT5A, and introduce constitutively active downstream effectors, to address the roles of noncanonical Wnt pathways in DE differentiation. Finally yet importantly, using the hESCs carrying different knockout, we will examine the effect of altered canonical Wnt activity on noncanonical Wnt pathways, or wise versa, to probe the interaction between canonical and noncanonical Wnt pathways and to investigate mechanisms controlling DE differentiation. This research will provide novel insights into the sophisticated and dynamic regulatory functions of canonical and noncanonical Wnt pathways during DE differentiation. The knowledge obtained will shed lights on both the stem cell research and technology development.

14116719.label: Realisation of objectives
14116719.value: OBJECTIVE #1 We thoroughly studied the functional roles of β-catenin and canonical Wnt pathway during DE differentiation, by generating the CTNNB1-/- and WNT3-/- hESCs followed by ectopic expression of full-length and various truncated CTNNB1. 1) Canonical Wnt signaling β-catenin is essential to the DE induction from hESCs CTNNB1-/- hESC clones were generated using the CRISPR-NHEJ-based gene disruption approach. Among the eight single-cell clones raised based on GFP expression, we identified two clones (KO#3 and KO#7) carrying biallelic disruption of CTNNB1 gene and confirmed the depletion of full-length CTNNB1 transcripts as well as β-catenin protein in these cells. Both KO#3 and KO#7 clones maintained normal hESC morphology, stable expression of hESC markers (OCT4, NANOG and SOX2), and unchanged localization of E-cadherin and α-catenin at cell junctions. As the compensatory response to the loss of β-catenin, higher levels of JUP were detected in the CTNNB1-/- clones compared in wt H1 cells. Both KO#3 and KO#7 CTNNB1-/- hESCs failed in the DE differentiation. These cells did not adopt the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) as observed in wt hESC (H1) at day 2 post DE induction, and they were unable to activate DE markers SOX17 and FOXA2 at day 4 post DE induction. Notably, the ectopic expression of Dox-inducible full-length (FL) β-catenin via lentivirus transduction rescued the DE differentiation of both KO#3 and KO#7 clones. Significantly improved EMT and substantial activation of SOX17 and FOXA2 were robustly observed at corresponding time points. We also examined the DE differentiation in WNT3-/- hESC, which were obtained from Dr Boris Greber. Consistently, the DE differentiation was largely inhibited while ectopic expression of Dox-inducible FL β-catenin can successfully rescue the differentiation defect. These results collectively demonstrated that canonical Wnt signaling, and β-catenin are essential to the hESC commitment to DE differentiation. 2) Distinct rescue outcomes yielded with different β-catenin functional mutants Multiple β-catenin mutants were generated to carry different deletion(s)/mutation(s) that ablated distinct functional domain(s). Transactivation activities of these β-catenin mutants were examined through TOPFlash assay using CTNNB1-/- HEK293T cells to avoid the interference by endogenous β-catenin. We introduced the Dox-inducible various β-catenin mutants into the CTNNB1-/- hESC (KO#7) via lentivirus delivery. Single-cell clones maintained normal hESC morphology and pluripotency markers in the absence of Dox while could express specific β-catenin mutants upon Dox induction. Interestingly, the defects of DE differentiation in CTNNB1-/- hESCs were successfully rescued to varied extents by different β-catenin mutants. The ΔN148 and ΔN148C clones underwent rapid cell scattering upon Dox treatment and colonies dispersed even before Activin A was supplemented for DE induction, while the FL, S33Y, ΔN90 and ΔC clones still maintained intact colonies resembling the unmodified H1 hESCs under the same condition. At day 1 post DE induction (DE (d1)), dramatic cell scattering was also observed in S33Y and ΔN90 clones, while wt hESC (H1) and FL β-catenin rescue clone only showed minor morphological changes. In the ΔC clones, the cell scattering phenotype was further delayed and only became evident at day 2 post DE induction. Interestingly, after 4 days of DE induction, FL, ΔN148, ΔN148C and ΔC clones all gave rise to some epithelial-like cells resembling DE, while the S33Y and ΔN90 clones largely produced fibroblasts-like cells. Consistently, immunostaining detected high ratios of DE cells expressing FOXA2 and SOX17 among the FL, ΔN148, ΔN148C and ΔC clones, whereas ΔN90 and S33Y clones yielded few positive cells. Collectively, these results supported that the truncation mutants ΔN148, ΔN148C and ΔC rendered a true rescue of β-catenin function in mediating DE differentiation, while surprisingly, the dominant and hyperactive mutant S33Y and ΔN90 yielded the least rescue effects. OBJECTIVE #2 We generated WNT5A-/- and ROR2-/- hESC clones using our established CRISPR-NHEJ approach, characterized these cells clones and confirmed the loss of WNT5A and ROR2, and analyzed the endodermal differentiation to address the roles of noncanonical Wnt signaling in DE differentiation. WNT5A and ROR2 are the key ligand and receptor of the non-canonical WNT signaling pathway, and have been found to be upregulated during DE induction. To assess the functional role of non-canonical WNT pathway in the DE lineage induction, we have generated the WNT5A-/- and ROR2-/- hESC clones using our previously established CRISPR-induced NHEJ knock-in approach. Among the single cell clones raised, we confirmed 4 clones carrying WNT5A knock-out by genome PCR, which showed disruption of both alleles in the WNT5A gene locus. Among these 4 clones, clone #5 was further verified by qRT-PCR, where WNT5A mRNA was largely reduced compared to that in wild type hESCs. Among 7 clones examined, we identified two clones with normal morphology proper genome modification of ROR2. However, the DE differentiation from these WNT5A-/- and ROR2-/- hESC clones did not show significant defects, suggesting that the non-canonical Wnt signaling is dispensable in the early endodermal differentiation. OBJECTIVE #3 To explore the unconventional transactivation mediated by β-catenin underlying the DE differentiation, we performed RNA-seq analysis of the various rescue clones. This analysis revealed that the truncated β-catenin ΔN148C and ΔC rescued DE induction through CTD/TCF-independent transactivation of primitive streak genes. Transcriptome data were collected from various rescue clones at two time points, after Dox treatment and at DE (d1), and we examined the transcriptome profile changes in ΔN148C and ΔC clones, which both lacked the CTD and TCF-dependent activity. Notably, GO analysis of 70 genes commonly upregulated in ΔN148C and ΔC clones upon DE induction highlighted primitive streak (PS) and endoderm formation. Moreover, expression heat map revealed that several other commonly recognized mesendoderm genes were also consistently upregulated, Extended analysis of PS- and mesendoderm-related genes among all examined clones showed that their expression levels in FL, ΔN148, ΔN148C and ΔC clones were positively correlated with the DE rescue outcomes. Rather surprisingly, in S33Y and ΔN90 clones, significant and even higher activation of PS genes were observed upon DE induction, which were contradictory to the poor DE rescue observed. The activations of PS genes were further confirmed by qRT-PCR analysis. Interestingly, EOMES, GSC, and CER1 genes showed higher activation in ΔN148C clone than in S33Y and ΔN90 clones, indicating more evident CTD/TCF-independent transactivation. These results indicated that PS genes were subjected to regulations via distinct mechanisms. Further comparison of genes upregulated in ΔN148C and ΔC clones with the potential β-catenin target genes previously identified by ChIP-seq analysis in hESCs (GSEA58476, GSE64758) also highlighted PS genes, including GSC, T, EOMES and MIXL1. Next, we constructed luciferase reporters carrying the enhancers that were occupied by β-catenin in T, EOMES, and MIXL1 locus. Indeed, all three enhancers from EOMES, T and MIXL1 were significantly activated by the Dox-induced ΔN148C, yielding enhanced luciferase signals. Meanwhile, consistent with the above observations, FL β-catenin triggered much higher activation of T and MIXL1 enhancers compared to ΔN148C and ΔC. Much lower reporter activities were detected in ΔC clones, which was coherent with its weaker and delayed DE rescue compared to ΔN148C clones.

14116719.label: Major findings and research outcome
14116719.value: Major findings: Activation of Wnt/β-catenin signaling is pivotal to the formation of definitive endoderm (DE) lineage during early embryonic development, but its regulatory mechanism was not yet fully understood. In this study, we generated new CTNNB1-/- human ES cells (hESC) through CRISPR-based insertional gene disruption approach and performed systematic rescue using various truncated or mutant β-catenin to study the Wnt/β-catenin-centered cellular mechanisms underlying DE differentiation from hESC. Interestingly, while the dominant active β-catenin with S33Y mutation or N-terminal deletion (ΔN90) failed to restore β-catenin function to induce DE differentiation, a truncated β-catenin lacking both N- and C-terminal domains (ΔN148C) and showing defect in TCF-dependent transactivation could robustly rescue the DE formation from CTNNB1-/- hESC clones. Further analysis indicated that ΔN148C mutant lost β-catenin function in maintaining adherens junctions and cell-cell contacts, while showed prominent nuclear translocation upon DE induction. The nuclear accumulation of ΔN148C mutant, which depended on Dox-induced expression levels and was negatively influenced by E-cadherin overexpression and knockout, positively correlated with the DE rescue outcome. These observations suggested that ΔN148C mutant preserved a TCF-independent nuclear activity of β-catenin to mediate the DE rescue. Indeed, subsequent RNA-seq analysis on the various rescue clones upon DE induction further revealed that primitive streak genes were activated by β-catenin independent of its C-terminal transactivation domains (CTD) and TCF activity. Our study revealed an unconventional regulatory mechanism by β-catenin, supporting that β-catenin-mediated TCF-independent transactivation plays an important role in controlling the endodermal commitment of hESC. 14116719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14116719.value: Through this research work, we have further developed the CRISPR-NHEJ based knock-in technology in human pluripotent stem cells, which could be applied in both human ES and iPS cells for targeted gene insertion at specific loci as well as insertional gene disruption. The relevant technology has been filed for patent application and the US patent (US App No. 15/354,329) is expected to be granted soon. Based on this technology platform, we collaborate with a renown stem cell team from Guangzhou Institute of Biomedicine and Health (GIBH), Chinese Academy of Sciences, to introduce tumor-specific chemical antigen receptor (CAR) into established human iPS cells for the generation of CAR-NK and CAR-macrophage cells as novel therapeutics for solid tumors. Meanwhile, with the established technology, we further developed CRISPR-HDR based approach for directly engineering primary human T cells for the generation of off-the-shelf universal dual CAR-T cells to treat the refractory and relapsed paediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). We are collaborating with a clinician scientist in this project and have secured a Pediatric Oncology Research Grant from the Children’s Cancer Foundation in 2023.

14116719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14116719.value: In this study, the researchers examined how Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway influences the early endodermal development using human embryonic stem cells as a model. They used a new CRISPR technology to abolish the β-catenin protein. By introducing different forms of the β-catenin protein, they investigated how the endodermal differentiation was affected. Surprisingly, they found that a specific truncated form of the β-catenin could rescue the differentiation in the modified stem cells, although it showed defects in activating its usual target genes. Further analysis revealed that this truncated protein had nuclear activity, and its nuclear accumulation was influenced by the levels of its expression and the presence of a partner protein called E-cadherin. Moreover, this truncated protein could activate genes related to early differentiation, which explained its rescuing activity. Overall, this study uncovered an unconventional mechanism by which β-catenin controls the commitment of human embryonic stem cells to the endodermal lineage. The research also advanced the CRISPR-based gene editing technology in human pluripotent stem cells, which could have applications in targeted gene insertion and gene disruption. The relevant technology has been filed for a patent application, and the US patent is expected to be granted soon.

14116919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14116919.value: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) is associated with a variety of important complications, namely cardiovascular, neurocognitive and metabolic disturbances. The prevalence of OSA is well studied in children and adults. However, adolescence – an interface between childhood and adulthood, and a period of developmental changes known to affect sleep is largely unexplored in relation to OSA. The only published prevalence study on adolescents is limited by its small sample size, not a true representation of the general population and primarily focused on Caucasians. In this proposal, we aim to determine the prevalence of OSA, and associated clinical features in a population-based sample of adolescents aged between 12 and 16 years. The sample selection will be based on a stratified (by districts) and clustered (subjects within randomly selected schools) randomised sampling frame. We will stratify all secondary schools registered under the Education Bureau according to the four geographic regions in Hong Kong. In order to avoid sampling bias towards the region that has less population, the final number of schools to be recruited from each of the 4 geographical regions will be in proportion to the adolescent population that resides in that region. Students in each year grade from the chosen school will be randomly selected to participate. Each participant will fill in a sleep symptom questionnaire, undergo anthropometric measurements, physical examination and complete home polysomnographic recordings. They will also be invited to undergo Conners’ Continuous Performance Test and have blood samples taken to phenotype their cardiovascular and metabolic risk. The primary outcome is prevalence of OSA, assessed by the obstructive apnoea hypopnoea index. Secondary outcomes include the use of logistic regression models to assess association between different severities of OSA and various demographic, clinical and laboratory variables. The obtained result will provide the much-needed OSA prevalence in adolescents, which is essential for estimating the true burden of disease within this population. This information is also vital when considering population-based health policies and interventional strategies. Globally, the findings from currently evidence-sparse region of the world allow future international comparison of disease burden. Our study will also form a platform from which repeated measurements can be made to assess time trends and to answer the important question of whether adulthood OSA takes its origin from adolescence. 心血管疾病、神經認知障礙、代謝紊亂等，都是與阻塞性睡眠窒息症(OSA)有關的併發症。我們對於OSA的流行病學在兒童和成人這兩個年齡階層中已經有一定程度的了解。青少年時期是兒童長大成人的重要階段，當中發展上的改變已被揭示會影響睡眠，但對於OSA的影響卻幾乎未曾探討。現有文獻中，有關OSA在青少年的流行病學的研究數據都有所局限，不是沒有足夠的樣本量，就是樣本的代表性不足。此外，這些相關研究的對象主要是西方白人，研究結果可能跟亞洲人種有差別。在這項研究提案，我們會研究十二至十六歲青少年的阻塞性睡眠窒息症的發病率和有關的臨床特徵。 我們會按地區進行隨機抽樣挑選中學進行口調查。首先會將所有於香港教育局註冊的中學根據它們的所屬地區歸類到四大區域，再於各區域挑選中學。在各區域隨機挑選的學校數量會和各區域的青少年居住人數成正比，從而避免因青少年人口在各區域不平均的分布而造成的抽樣偏差。在被選中的學校中，每一個年級的學生均會被隨機地邀請參與研究。參與者需要填寫一份有關睡眠習慣的問卷，接受身體測量和檢查，以及在家中進行睡眠監測。他們亦會接受克氏注意力持續度表現測驗，及抽取血液樣本用作分析他們患心血管疾病和代謝紊亂的風險。這項研究的主要目標是探討OSA的發病率，而OSA會以阻塞性睡眠呼吸暫停低通氣指數來定義；次要的目標是評估OSA的嚴重程度與人口特徵，臨床表現和血液樣本中不同變項之間的聯繫。 研究所得的數據對於估計OSA在青少年人口中的疾病負擔是不可或缺的。這些數據對於亦有助改善青少年人口的健康政策和治療對策。在國際層面來說，我們的數據將能填補過往研究的不足，將來亦可與其他地區的數據作跨種族比較。此外，這項研究亦會創立一個平台以便日後可以作追蹤研究。得出的數據不但可以評估青少年OSA隨著時間的變化，亦可以回答一條重要的問題：成人OSA是否從青少年時期衍變而來？

14117319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14117319.value: 隨著社會老齡化加劇，骨質疏松性骨折的發病率不斷上升，已成為骨科最常見的疾病之一。因骨質疏松性骨折愈合遲緩，患者常面臨住院時間長、並發癥多、生活質量降低等困擾，亟需能有效促進骨質疏松性骨折愈合的治療方式。背根神經節電刺激是一種有效的神經調節手段，廣泛應用於慢性疼痛的臨床治療。目前，我們研究發現背根神經節電刺激能夠通過上調降鈣素基因相關肽來緩解廢用性骨質疏松及促進脊柱後外側融合。前期實驗結果進壹步證實多個節段的背根神經節電刺激能夠提高大鼠股骨缺損處降鈣素基因相關肽的濃度。與此同時，本課題組近來研究發現由鎂離子所釋放的降鈣素基因相關肽可以促進骨膜幹細胞的成骨生物學效應，從而加速骨質疏松性骨折的愈合（發表於Nature Medicine, 2016）。除此之外，先前研究證實降鈣素基因相關肽在血管修復及形成上亦發揮著重要作用。最新研究表明，在骨代謝穩態中，成骨作用和成血管作用是相互影響的。因此，我們推測背根神經節電刺激能夠上調降鈣素基因相關肽合成，促進其在外周釋放並發揮促成骨成血管雙重生物學效應，最終促進骨質疏松性骨折的愈合。為了提供更為精準的治療，我們將探索單一節段背根神經節電刺激的有效性。根據逆向神經示蹤劑的實驗結果，我們發現股骨主要由腰4背根神經節支配，因此腰4背根神經節電刺激治療骨質疏松性骨折成為可能。綜上，本研究將驗證單一節段背根神經節電刺激在骨質疏松性骨折治療中的有效性，探究電刺激在降鈣素基因相關肽合成及釋放過程中的調控機制，進壹步研究降鈣素基因相關肽的骨折修復過程中的重要作用，為神經幹預促進骨折修復提供理論基礎。

14117319.label: Realisation of objectives
14117319.value: The incidence of osteoporotic fracture is increasing significantly with global population aging. The healing of osteoporotic fractures is poor due to limited bone regeneration potential, especially in elderly individuals. Prolonged healing time results in higher morbidity, disability, and even mortality, urging us to develop effective strategies for enhancing osteoporotic fracture healing. As a well-established neuromodulator, electrical stimulation (ES) has been widely applied at dorsal root ganglions (DRGs) to relieve chronic postsurgical and neuropathic pain. Previous studies reported that ES (pulse width: 90 μs, frequency: 150 Hz, voltage: 0.25 V) at lumbar (L4, L5, and L6) DRGs could prevent unloading-induced bone loss and enhance bone regeneration in inter-transverse spinal fusion model by increasing the expression of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP). CGRP exerts promising anabolic effects in bone fracture healing by enhancing the osteogenic potential of stem cells including periosteum-derived stem cells (PDSCs). Available evidence supports that CGRP can also stimulate angiogenesis, an early event coupling with osteogenesis during bone fracture healing. Therefore, we speculated that ES at DRGs would promisingly enhance bone healing via upregulating the synthesis of CGRP in DRGs and its release to the fracture site. In this study, we first retrogradely traced the DRGs innervating rat femur and investigated the effect of ES on CGRP release at the femur. The effect of ES on the synthesis of CGRP in DRGs and underlying mechanisms were then investigated by quantitative polymerase chain reaction and immunofluorescence staining. The therapeutic effect of ES at DRGs on bone healing was investigated in rat closed osteoporotic femur fracture model by micro-CT, biomechanical test, and histological analysis. The critical role of CGRP in ES at DRGs enhanced fracture healing was validated as local administration of CGRP receptor antagonist (BIBN 4096 BS) at fracture site which could significantly abolish the effect of CGRP. In an in vitro study, bone marrow stem cells (BMSCs) were used to investigate the effect of CGRP (10 nM) on endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) production during endothelial differentiation. Our results showed that the rat femur was mainly innervated by L3 and L4 DRGs. ES at 10 Hz increased CGRP concentration at the femur by 2 folds (addressed Objective 1-2). Meanwhile, ES up-regulated CGRP synthesis in DRGs by activating the CaMKII/CREB signaling pathway. After daily stimulation for the first two weeks post-fracture, ES at L3 and L4 DRGs enhanced fracture healing, demonstrating the increased formation of bone as well as blood vessels (dual labeled with CD31 and Endomucin antibodies). Immunohistochemistry staining showed that ES at DRGs significantly increased the CGRP expression at fracture callus and DRGs (addressed Objective 3). Local application of CGRP receptor antagonist at fracture site significantly blocked the ES at DRGs enhanced bone regeneration and vessel formation in fracture healing. In vitro endothelial differentiation of BMSCs showed that CGRP increased EPCs population by activating the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway (addressed Objective 4). The induced EPCs formed tube-like structures and promoted osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Overall, this study demonstrated that ES upregulated CGRP synthesis in DRGs and triggered CGRP release to the terminal (the femur). The increased CGRP by ES at DRGs promoted bone regeneration and vessel formation in osteoporotic fracture healing.

14117319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14117319.value: We found that electrical stimulation (ES) at dorsal root ganglions (DRGs) triggered calcium influx and activated the Ca2+/CaMKII/CREB signaling cascade, resulting in the transcription of calcitonin gene‐related peptide (CGRP). After synthesized in DRGs, CGRP was transported to peripheral nerve terminals and released following depolarization by ES. The released CGRP and subsequently increased type‐H vessel formation promoted osteoporotic fracture healing. We have published the aforementioned findings in Advanced Science (Five-year impact factor 16.7). One PhD was trained. Due to the pandemic in the past few years, we have not participated in conferences.

14117319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14117319.value: This proof-of-concept study established a foundation to design non-invasive methods, such as focused ultrasound, to modulate the biological function of DRGs for treating challenging fractures with impaired regeneration potential in clinical practice, which in turn will help reduce our socioeconomic and healthcare burdens in the long run. As CGRP can directly affect osteoclastogenesis and osteoclasts play a crucial role in callus remodeling, osteoclasts may also engage in ES‐enhanced fracture healing. Although most osteoporosis occurs in postmenopausal women, the prevalence of senile osteoporosis is increasing due to the aging of the population. Thus, it is necessary for us to investigate the therapeutic effects of ES at DRGs on fracture healing enhancement in aged male rats. In addition, some other nerves, such as SP or tropomyosin receptor kinase A positive nerves, may also respond to ES stimulation, which shall be investigated in future studies.

14117319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14117319.value: The neuronal engagement of the peripheral nerve system plays a crucial role in regulating fracture healing, but how to modulate the neuronal activity to enhance fracture healing remains unexploited. Here it is shown that electrical stimulation (ES) directly promotes the biosynthesis and release of calcitonin gene‐related peptide (CGRP) by activating Ca2+/CaMKII/CREB signaling pathway and action potential, respectively. To accelerate rat femoral osteoporotic fracture healing which presents with the decline of CGRP, soft electrodes are engineered and they are implanted at L3 and L4 dorsal root ganglions (DRGs). ES delivered at DRGs for the first two weeks after fracture increases CGRP expression in both DRGs and fracture callus. It is also identified that CGRP is indispensable for type‐H vessel formation, a biological event coupling angiogenesis and osteogenesis, contributing to ES‐enhanced osteoporotic fracture healing. This proof‐of‐concept study shows for the first time that ES at lumbar DRGs can effectively promote femoral fracture healing, offering an innovative strategy using bioelectronic devices to enhance bone regeneration.

14119019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119019.value: The Emprint™ Ablation System with Thermosphere™ Technology is intended for use in percutaneous, laparoscopic, endoscopic, and intraoperative coagulation (ablation) of soft tissue, including partial or complete ablation of non-resectable tumors. In this study, the flexible Emprint™ Ablation Catheter will be deployed bronchoscopically using the superDimension™ Navigation System’s EWC in order to ablate lung nodules. This study will be the first prospective study in the world to investigate, and characterize the safety and performance of the Emprint™ Ablation Catheter Kit with Thermosphere™ Technology in clinical use for patients with small lung cancers. The technology offer a potential totally non-invasive method of treating one or multiple lung cancers in patients through the bronchoscopic route. The primary endpoint is the composite rate of adverse events related to the Emprint™ Ablation Catheter Kit with Thermosphere™ Technology through 1-month follow-up. Secondary objectives would be to investigate patient satisfaction and pain; quality of life; technical success; and technique efficacy. The study will be conducted in multicenter trial setting with St Bartholomews Hospital, London, and Radboud university medical center, The Netherlands; with anticipated contribution of 10 cases each from each centre. The study will provide the world first evidence of safety for ablation treatment of small lung cancer using microwave via the totally non-invasive endobronchial route.

14119019.label: Realisation of objectives
14119019.value: The safety of the devices tested were characterized, as we prospectively recruited the planned 30 patients into the study to undergo endobronchial lung ablation for their malignant lung nodules and followed all of them up till study end point. The study primary endpoint was the composite rate of serious or non-serious adverse events related to the transbronchial MWA device through one-month follow-up. The secondary safety endpoints were the composite rate of serious adverse events related to the transbronchial MWA device through one-month follow-up, and the composite rates of serious and overall adverse events related to the study procedure or other study devices through one-month follow-up. Secondary efficacy endpoints were technical success (target nodule reached and ablated according to the study protocol) and technique efficacy (satisfactory ablation as evidenced by the nodule being completely covered by the ablation zone based on one-month follow-up imaging). An independent medical monitor adjudicated all reported adverse events. Subject satisfaction, subject self-reported pain, and subject self-reported breathlessness were evaluated at one-month post-procedure. Quality of life was also a secondary endpoint and was evaluated at baseline and at one-month post-procedure using the EQ-5D-3L questionnaire. Analyses were performed using SAS® Version 9.4 (SAS Inc., Cary, NC) and data were summarized by descriptive statistics (for continuous variables) or frequencies and percentages (for categorical variables). A one-way repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) test was used to evaluate whether the mean of the subject-reported pain scores differed over time. The study outcomes can be seen in section Major Findings and Research Outcomes below.

14119019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119019.value: Thirty subjects with lung nodules (primary lung cancer in 66.7% and oligometastatic in 33.3%) with size 5 to 27 mm (mean 13.7 mm). Distance from nodule to pleura ranged from 6 to 44 mm. Median bronchoscopy procedure time was 123 mins. The average ablation time was 8.1 ± 2.3 minutes (range 3.5-10 minutes). Mean post-procedure average ablation margin was 9.9 ± 2.7 mm, with 90% of nodules (27/30) achieving at least a 5 mm margin on all edges. Safety: The primary endpoint rate (composite AE related to device through one-month follow-up) was 3.3%, which was a single case of mild (non-serious, CTCAE Grade 1) haemoptysis reported by the subject in a phone discussion on Day 5 post-ablation. The patient returned for a chest CT scan on Day 6 post-ablation, which showed a satisfactory ablation zone smaller than the post-procedure CT, and reported that the symptom had resolved without treatment. There were no serious adverse events related to the ablation device. Nine serious adverse events in four subjects (13.3%), all rated as CTCAE Grade 3, were considered by the medical monitor to be related to the study procedure or other study devices. A total of 51 adverse events were reported in 21 subjects (29 Grade 1 events, 13 Grade 2 events, 9 Grade 3 events); these included all events related to any aspect of the study transbronchial procedure (including anaesthesia, navigation, biopsy, and ablation). There were no CTCAE Grade 4 or 5 events, no pneumothoraces, and no deaths. Technical success was 100%. One-month follow-up CT showed technique efficacy was 100% defined as a satisfactory ablation as evidenced by the follow-up CT scan. On a 0-10 pain scale subjects’ self-reported pain and discomfort 1.5 ± 2.2 immediately after ablation, 1.4 ± 1.8 one week after the procedure, and 0.5 ± 1.1 one month after the procedure (P=0.016). On a scale of 1-5 (1 being the least), subjects rated their breathlessness at 1.8 ± 1.0, 1.6 ± 1.0, and 1.5 ± 0.9 immediately after, at one week, and at one-month post-ablation. On a scale of 1-5 (1 being “extremely unlikely” and 5 “extremely likely”), subjects rated their willingness to have another transbronchial ablation procedure, if necessary, at 4.8 ± 0.8 (range 2-5). On EQ-5D-3L scale, 15 subjects’ overall assessment of their current health state was 74.6 ± 12.8 (range 50 to 90) at baseline versus 77.4 ± 14.2 (range 47 to 100) at 1-month post-ablation (on a scale of 0-100, with 100 being the best imaginable health state), representing a change from baseline of 2.8 ± 15.9. Fifty percent of subjects noted an improvement in their overall health state, 26.7% reported a decrease, and 23.3% reported no change.

14119019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119019.value: This is a single-arm, two-centre study of 30 subjects with one-month follow-up. The inclusion of selected patients with nodules ≤30 mm in maximum diameter and ≥5 mm from the pleura may not represent the entire population of patients undergoing transbronchial MWA. The short-term measures of technical success and technique efficacy were based on standardized terminology and reporting criteria for image-guided tumour ablation;14 however, longer follow-up is required to provide a full evaluation of local control and recurrence. These results will need to be replicated in a larger study among users with varying experience levels, a broader subject population, and employing longer follow-up. In addition, due to differences in measurement units, we were unable to calculate the average radiation dose, which is an important factor in assessing the risk-to-benefit ratio of this technology. The larger scale data required and longer follow-up will be gathered in the project " Transbronchial Microwave Ablation Lung Surveillance (TAMAS) Registry" RGC Grant 2022/23 No. 14111222.

14119019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119019.value: This NAVABLATE study has shown endobronchial microwave ablation of small malignant lung tumours to be safe and feasible, with 100% technical operative success. There were no major adverse effects, no pneumothorax or mortality. Follow-up CT imaging at 1-month shows that all patients lung tumours have been completely treated without complications. The prospective multicenter international study provides evidence to further develop this non-invasive technique for treatment of malignant lung lesions, in particular for patients who are non-surgical candidates or have limited treatment options. The next stage would be the collection of larger scale data and longer follow-up from the project " Transbronchial Microwave Ablation Lung Surveillance (TAMAS) Registry" RGC Grant 2022/23 No. 14111222.

14119219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119219.value: Allergic diseases including asthma, allergic rhinitis and atopic dermatitis are common in developed countries, causing significant social and economical burden to individuals and government. Among the various causes for allergic diseases, house dust mite allergy is the most prevalent cause of allergic sensitization. However, the contribution of storage mites to allergic diseases cannot be neglected because many previous studies have shown that a significant proportion of allergic patients are sensitive to Tyrophagus (T.) putrescentiae as revealed by skin prick test. Furthermore, as a storage mite T. putrescentiae has a wider range of habitats when compare with dust mites. In this study, the reference genome and transcript dataset of T. putrescentiae will be constructed. Afterwards, novel allergen groups as well as members of known allergen groups will be identified by immunoblotting and mass spectrometry. Finally, the metabolic characteristics analysis of T. putrescentiae, Dermatophagoides farina and Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus will unlock the mystery behind the significant different habitats of these two types of mites. In summary, the first complete and accurately annotated storage mite genome and new allergens will be delivered in this project and such data will provide new and valuable insights into allergen genes in storage mites and opportunities to identify new allergens for future therapeutics development. The comparison of metabolic characteristics in T. putrescentiae and dust mites will also broaden our understanding on the relationship between mite biology and human allergic diseases. 過敏性疾病包括哮喘，過敏性鼻炎和特應性皮炎在發達國家很常見，給個人和政府帶來了沉重的社會和經濟負擔。在過敏性疾病的各種原因中，塵蟎過敏是致敏的最普遍原因。然而，倉儲蟎對過敏性疾病的貢獻不容忽視，因為許多先前的研究已經表明，通過皮膚點刺試驗顯示，相當大比例的過敏患者對腐食酪蟎敏感。此外，與塵蟎相比，腐食酪蟎作為倉儲蟎具有更廣泛的棲息地。本研究將構建腐食酪蟎的參考基因組和轉錄組數據庫。然後，通過免疫印跡和質譜鑑定新的過敏原組以及已知過敏原組的成員。最後，腐食酪蟎，粉塵蟎和屋塵蟎的代謝特徵分析將揭開這兩種不同類型的蟎的顯著不同棲息地背後的神秘面紗。總而言之，此項目將首次提供完整且準確基因標示的倉儲蟎基因組和新過敏原，這些數據將為倉儲蟎中的過敏原基因提供新的及有價值的見解，並為未來開發新的過敏原識別方法和過敏性疾病治療提供機會。 最後，腐食酪蟎和塵蟎的代謝特徵比較也將拓寬我們對蟎生物學與人類過敏性疾病之間關係的理解。

14119219.label: Realisation of objectives
14119219.value: Objective 1: We employed a hybrid assembly approach using a combination of two sequencing technologies: Single Molecule Real-Time (SMRT) sequencing (PacBio Sequel) and sequencing by synthesis (Illumina HiSeq 4000). Based on the genome size estimation by KAT, T. putrescentiae’s genome size was determined to be 83 Mb. The size of the final polished genome assembly is 97.4 Mb, which consists of 176 scaffolds with N50 scaffold size of 2,914 kb and the longest scaffold size is 6,764 kb. Compared to the previously published relative species D. farinae and D. pteronyssinus, the T. putrescentiae’ genome reported in this study represents an approximately 16-fold improvement in scaffold N50. Blobplot showed that 92.16% reads were mapped to the assembly, in which 92.06% of the mapped reads belongs to Arthropoda reads. Alignment of three sets of RNA-Seq reads to the de novo genome assembly using HISAT2 yielded an overall mapping rate between 33 – 84%. We have annotated a total of 24,656 transcripts, with 22,974 (93.2%) being supported by RNA-Seq data, showing that a good and accurate annotation was achieved. Functional annotation for GO and the KEGG pathway database using the Blast2GO program mapped 13,360 protein-coding genes to GO project categories. Objective 2: Based on the genome assembly and annotation of T. putrescentiae, a genome-wide analysis was performed to explore the allergen groups. Using the reported mite allergens in the WHO/IUIS allergen nomenclature database as reference genes, thirty-seven allergen groups were identified and covered a comprehensive allergen profile of T. putrescentiae. A wide range of gene expansion was observed in the allergen gene families, such as the five homologues of the cysteine protease Tyr p 1. To evaluate the allergenicity of the newly identified allergens, recombinant proteins were cloned and expressed, and the IgE reactivity was assessed by the enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) with the sera of T. putrescentiae sensitized patients. For the two serine protease allergens, the recombinant proteins rTyr p 6.0101 and rTyr p 9.0101 presented low allergenicities of 11.1% and 22.2%, respectively. Similarly, the chitinase rTyr p 18.0101 was tested as positive in only two samples (11.1%). For the arginine kinase and the myosin light-chain, rTyr p 20.0101 and rTyr p 26.0101 exhibited higher allergenicities, 44.4% and 50.0%, respectively. Although all the patients were diagnosed as T. putrescentiae sensitized, only 11/18 (61.1%) of the serum samples showed positive responses to the crude protein extract. Despite of low allergenicities, all the five proteins, Tyr p 6.0101, Tyr p 9.0101, Tyr p 18.0101, Tyr p 20.0101 and Tyr p 26.0101, were verified as novel allergens of T. putrescentiae. Besides the in silico analysis, proteomic identification was performed using the pooled sera of allergy patients to identify T. putrescentiae allergens. Totally thirty-one protein spots of T. putrescentiae bound by IgE in the serum samples underwent de novo peptide sequencing by MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, then the sequenced peptides were searched against the annotated protein sequences of T. putrescentiae genome. A range of our identified allergens could be found in the spots, including members of Tyr p 1, 2, 3, 8, 10, 13, 20, 21, 25, 28 and 39 (Table 2). As expected, the best matched homologues were in the spots, including Tyr p 2.0101, Tyr p 10.0101, Tyr p 20.0101, Tyr p 21.0101, Tyr p 25.0101, Tyr p 28.0101 and Tyr p 39.0101. Especially, Tyr p 21.0101 were matched by four spots, while Tyr p 10.0101, Tyr p 20.0101 and Tyr p 25.0101 were found in two spots, respectively. However, in Tyr p 2, Tyr p 2.0101/Tyr p 2.0201, Tyr p 2.0601 and an ungrouped Tyr p 2 (gene locus: TP_020235.01) were matched by the sequenced peptides (Table 2). As for Tyr p 28, Tyr p 28.0101, Tyr p 28.0201 and an ungrouped Tyr p 28 (gene locus: TP_006940.01) were identified in the spots. Objective 3: In addition to D. farinae, D. pteronyssinus, B. tropicalis and T. putrescentiae, which are known as free-living allergic mites, two parasitic mites, P. ovis and S. scabiei, are also human allergy related. A phylogenomic analysis was performed with the genome assemblies of these six species and other publicly available genomes. When a gene gain/loss analysis was performed, higher numbers of expanding and contracting gene families were found in T. putrescentiae and S. scabiei. GO enrichment analysis of critical orthogroups involved in the evolution of the four psoroptid mites (D. farinae, D. pteronyssinus, P. ovis, S. scabiei) and the two canonical storage mites (B. tropicalis and T. putrescentiae) suggested divergent evolution of serine protease, ionotropic glutamate receptor and various detoxification gene families including ABC transporter (ABC) and cytochrome P450 (CYP). A wide range of rapidly expanding gene families were identified in T. putrescentiae, including several glycoside hydrolases, serine protease, heat shock protein 70 (HSP70), and detoxification gene families including UDP glucuronosyltransferase (UGT), CYP and ABC. Notably, T. putrescentiae has a much larger number of species-specific orthogroups, including many proteases, glycoside hydrolases, CYP, and ionotropic glutamate receptors, suggesting that this storage mite underwent more sophisticated adaptation during evolution. As a canonical storage mite, T. putrescentiae possessed more alpha glucosidases (21 genes) than the other five astigmatic mites, and gene expansion and diversification observed in the phylogenetic analysis are consistent with its preference for a high-carbohydrate diet, as a canonical storage mite. Unexpectedly, alpha amylase was duplicated in D. farinae, D. pteronyssinus, P. ovis, and B. tropicalis but not the storage mite T. putrescentiae. According to our metagenomic analysis, Neurospora crassa (a starch utilizer with highly stable amylase) was identified as the most abundant microorganism in T. putrescentiae (5.26% in abundance) but was not found in the other five astigmatic mites, implying that the alpha amylase of Neurospora crassa is an alternative to the alpha amylase gene duplication in T. putrescentiae. More genes of triacylglycerol lipase were identified in T. putrescentiae (58 genes), which was consistent with the fact that T. putrescentiae is referred to as a cheese mite and prefers food with high fat content. The phylogenetic tree of all triacylglycerol lipases of the six astigmatic mites confirmed the gene expansion in T. putrescentiae. Of the five major gene families responsible for detoxification, T. putrescentiae had the largest number of genes, while S. scabiei had the smallest. The huge increase in the number of detoxification genes in the storage mite T. putrescentiae indicates its higher probability of encountering xenobiotics in living environments. The variation in gene numbers was particularly apparent in the UGT family. There were only 5 UGT genes identified in S. scabiei, but 73 UGT genes in T. putrescentiae.

14119219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119219.value: Tyrophagus (T.) putrescentiae, also known commonly as a storage mite or mold mite, is an important mite species that infests a wide variety of stored foods, especially those with high protein and fat contents. T. putrescentiae is found to be associated with allergic disorders including asthma and allergic rhinitis similar to other domestic mites. In this study, we were able to assemble a high-quality T. putrescentiae draft genome with relatively small scaffold number and extremely long scaffold N50 and contig N50. The genome was highly complete which pave the way for studying the genes in T. putrescentiae and investigating the differences between storage mites and house dust mites (HDM) by comparative genomics. Comparison of the metabolism and allergens in T. putrescentiae, B. tropicalis, D. farinae, and D. pteronyssinus was performed to uncover the differences in their habitats and allergenicity. The comparative genomics results had been published in the prestigious journal Molecular Biology and Evolution, which has a 5-year impact factor of 20 (Reference 1). Novel allergen groups, as well as members of known allergen groups, were identified in T. putrescentiae by in silico prediction, which were then confirmed by immunoblotting and mass spectrometry. Interested novel allergens were cloned in order to confirm their allergenicity by ELISA experiments. The results about novel allergens will be submitted to the Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology in October 2022. Moreveor, our finidngs were highlighted in the press conference of The Chinese University of Hong Kong titled “CUHK unveils the evolutionary history of medically important mites, laying the genomics groundwork for diagnosis of and intervention in mite allergy” on 16 June 2022. In summary, here we report the first complete and accurately-annotated storage mite genome which provided an effective means to reveal its encoded allergens. Such data shall provide novel insights for allergen genes in storage mites and valuable opportunities to characterize unknown allergens for future therapeutics development. References 1. 14119219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119219.value: In this study, a substantial advancement in the scientific knowledge of genomics, transcriptomics, allergen profiles and miRNA profiles for HDMs and storage mites has been presented. In particular, the first complete and annotated genome of T. putrescentiae will help to understand the biology and allergy-driving potential of mites in human allergic diseases. The results provide insights for allergen genes in storage mites and hints for characterization of unknown allergic agents for therapeutics development in future studies. The method employed can serve as an effective means to reveal a complete allergen profile in other species. In addition, the genomes we constructed had facilitated comparison in metabolic characteristics between T. putrescentiae and HDM which bridged the knowledge gap in mite biology and human allergic diseases. We can anticipate that novel diagnosis and treatment of storage mite allergy could be derived from the deliverables of this study.

14119219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119219.value: Allergic diseases are immune-system disorders characterized by IgE-mediated immunological reactions, including asthma, allergic rhinitis, and atopic dermatitis; and especially prevalent and dangerous among children, such as asthma even causes death. In Hong Kong, over 50% population have at least one form of allergic disease and especially the number of children keep soaring in past decades. In this study, the first complete genome of T. putrescentiae was constructed using the state-of-the-art genomics and bioinformatics tools. The deliverables of this project will help understand the biology and allergy-driving potential of storage mites in human allergic diseases. Moreover, they could provide insights for allergen genes in storage mites and hints for characterization of unknown allergic agents for therapeutics development in future studies. The method we employed can also serve as an effective means to reveal a complete allergen profile in other species. In addition, the genomes we constructed had facilitated comparison in metabolic characteristics between T. putrescentiae and house dust mites, which bridged the knowledge gap in mite biology and human allergic diseases. We can anticipate that novel diagnosis and treatment of storage mite allergy could be derived from the findings of this study.

14119419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14119419.value: Our understanding of the drivers of speciation that generate observed biodiversity has been revolutionized in light of recent findings how microsymbionts have significantly contributed to the evolutionary fitness and success of their hosts. The acquisition of symbionts allows rapid adaptation and exploitation of novel ecological niches at a pace faster than the evolution on new metabolic pathways in the host genome. This “innovation through symbiosis” has promoted speciation in many groups, notably in terrestrial herbivorous insects. Our understanding of the evolution of key adaptive host innovations, however, cannot be complete without elucidating the roles of gut microbial community and how such important symbiotic relationships got established. Furthermore, it is hypothesized that core microsymbionts linked to fundamental functions of hosts are favorably inherited from ancestor to progenitor species, and therefore exhibit a tight host-symbiont co-evolution. Research, however, has been strongly biased towards mammal and insect taxa with patterns in other taxa in the tree of life largely unknown. In addition, processes inducing phylosymbiosis - whether through active filtering by host genetic factors or passive inheritance from the ancestor (or both) - are seldom studied. Crabs of the family Sesarmidae (Crustacea: Brachyura) dominate mangroves and are an excellent model to fill in our knowledge gap in the host/gut symbiont evolution in aquatic ecosystems. They underwent rapid diversification after acquisition of a plant-feeding lifestyle, which is believed to be largely facilitated by gut microbes, followed by successful colonization to intertidal and terrestrial environments. To elucidate the patterns and mechanisms underlying phylosymbiosis, and how these gut microbes prompted the evolution of herbivory and diversification of Sesarmidae, this study will adopt an integrative approach by combining the latest 16S rRNA gene amplicon metabarcoding characterization of gut microbial community, host/symbiont co-speciation phylogenetic analyses and microbiota transplant experiments. Findings will not only shed new light on how the gut microbiome contributes to herbivory in aquatic invertebrates and promote speciation, but also yield valuable information on the prevalence of and mechanisms underpinning phylosymbiosis and host/microbial symbiont co-evolution across the tree of life. The results will provide a better understanding on the forces promoting and generating biodiversity in nature.

14119419.label: Realisation of objectives
14119419.value: In the first part of the research project, we attempted to reconstruct the phylogenetic history of the Sesarmidae and related crab families in the Thoractotremata to determine the origin of terrestrialization and test the hypothesis that terrestrialization will promote speciation rate in crabs. The Thoracotremata is a large and successful group of “true” crabs (Decapoda, Brachyura, Eubrachyura) with a great diversity of lifestyles and well-known intertidal representatives. The group represents the largest brachyuran radiation into terrestrial and semi-terrestrial environments and comprises multiple lineages of obligate symbiotic species. In consequence, they exhibit very diverse physiological and morphological adaptations. Our understanding of their evolution is, however, largely obscured by their confused classification. Here, we resolve interfamilial relationships of Thoracotremata, using 10 molecular markers and exemplars from all nominal families in order to reconstruct the pathways of lifestyle transition and to propose a new taxonomy corresponding to phylogenetic relationships. The results confirm the polyphyly of three superfamilies as currently defined (Grapsoidea, Ocypodoidea and Pinnotheroidea). At the family level, Dotillidae, Macrophthalmidae, and Varunidae are not monophyletic. Ancestral state reconstruction analyses and divergent time estimations indicate that the common ancestor of thoracotremes already thrived in intertidal environments in the Late Cretaceous and terrestrialization became a major driver of thoracotreme diversification. Multiple semi-terrestrial and terrestrial lineages originated and radiated in the Early Eocene, coinciding with the global warming event at the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM). Secondary invasions into subtidal regions and colonizations of freshwater habitats occurred independently through multiple semi-terrestrial and terrestrial lineages. Obligate symbiosis between thoracotremes and other marine macro-invertebrates evolved at least twice. On the basis of the current molecular phylogenetic hypothesis, it will be necessary in the future to revise and recognize seven monophyletic superfamilies and revisit the morphological character states which define them. Furthermore, we found that the speciation rate was only enhanced in Sesarmidae, but not in the other families also successfully invaded the terrestrial and/or semi-terrestrial habitats (e.g. Grapsidae, Ocypodidae). Therefore, this suggests that engagement into herbivorous lifestyle, instead of colonization onto the terrestrial habitat is the major driver of rapid speciation in crabs. Subsequently, we attempt to investigate the patterns and mechanisms that facilitate the adaptation to the herbivorous lifestyle in Seasarmidae crabs. Although endogenous cellulases expressions were reported in crab species, it remains unknown if the endogenous enzymes alone can complete the whole lignocellulolytic pathway, or they also depend on the contribution from their intestinal microbiome. Therefore, we characterized and compared the gut microbiome composition across 43 species of Sesarmidae and other mangrove crab species using 16S metabarcoding to explore how these gut microbes prompted the evolution of terrestrialization. We found that the gut microbiome assemblage in crabs is largely determined by host identity, and to a lesser extent influenced by environmental factors, including microhabitat and sampling locations. Patterns of phylosymbiosis were observed in different crab families but the levels of strength were varying, suggesting the importance of host filtering in shaping the bacterial assemblage. The Sesarmidae further displayed cophylogeny with its core gut bacterial genera, of which were predicted to be functionally important to their hosts by providing lignocellulolytic enzymes, essential amino acids and fatty acids supplementation. Our results support the hypothesis of microbial contribution to herbivory, and hence terrestrialization, in mangrove crabs and the tight association and codiversification of the crab holobiont. Finally, in order to confirm the function and contribution of microbiome in lignocellulose degradation in crabs, shortgun metagenomics analyses on 43 crab gut samples from 23 species of mangrove crabs were conducted. The results revealed a wide coverage of 127 CAZy families and nine KOs targeting lignocellulose and their derivatives in all species analyzed, including predominantly carnivorous species, suggesting the crab species gut microbiome have lignocellulolytic capacity regardless of dietary preference. Microbial cellulase, hemicellulase and pectinase genes in herbivorous and detritivorous crabs were differentially more abundant when compared to omnivorous and carnivorous crabs, indicating the importance of gut symbionts in lignocellulose degradation in mangrove crabs and the enrichment of lignocellulolytic microbes in response to diet with higher lignocellulose content. The herbivorous and detritivorous crabs showed highly similar CAZyme composition compared to dissimilarities observed in taxonomic profiles observed in both groups, suggesting a stronger selection force to gut microbiota by its functional capacity than by taxonomy. The gut microbiota in herbivorous sesarmid crabs were also enriched with nitrogen reduction and fixation genes, implying possible roles of the gut microbiota in supplementing nitrogen that is deficient in plant diet. In conclusion, we found that endosymbiotic cellulolytic microbes play an important role in lignocellulose degradation in most crab species but their abundance is strongly correlated with dietary preference, and they are highly enriched in herbivorous sesarmids, thus enhancing their capacity for digestion of mangrove leaves. Dietary preference is a stronger driver in determining the microbial CAZyme composition and taxonomic profile in mangrove crab microbiome, resulting in functional redundancy of endosymbiotic microbes. Our results showed that crabs implement a mixed mode of digestion utilizing both endogenous and microbial enzymes in lignocellulose degradation, as observed in most of the more advanced herbivorous invertebrate species.

14119419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14119419.value: Based on integrated profiling of both host transcriptome and gut microbial metagenome, we can conclude that crabs implement a mixed mode of digestion utilizing both endogenous and microbial enzymes in lignocellulose degradation, as observed in most of the more advance herbivorous invertebrate species. Furthermore, most crab species exhibit certain capacity of lignocellulose degradation attributed to their opportunistic and highly plastic dietary composition., but the mangrove herbivorous sesarmid crabs showed the highest level of endogenous expression lignocellulolytic gene as well as CAZyme gene abundance in gut microbiome when compared to other crab species, reflecting their enhanced capacity to digest and utilize mangrove leaf litter as major food source. We showed here that the microbiome could contribute to the lignocellulose degradation and supplement nutrients to adaptation to the new niche, which in turn promotes terrestrialization and speciation in mangrove Sesarmidae crabs. The functional importance of the microbial symbionts results in tight co-diversification of both parties, resulting in the observed phylosymbiosis and cophylogeny in core bacteria groups. The evolutionary innovations through symbiosis, whereby organisms develop novel traits and adapt to new ecological niche by the acquisition of symbionts, are important speciation drivers in nature. The holobiont perspective also has major implication for the ecosystem functioning. Herbivorous crabs in the mangal systems process a significant amount of plant materials daily. Their feeding activities do not only shred leaf litter to fine-sized particles, the digestive processes along the digestive tract also significantly promote the bacterial density in the digesta and egesta. The functions of microbial partners in crabs are indeed not limited to their hosts, but also extend into the community and ecosystem levels, by contribution to the carbon and nitrogen cycling of mangrove ecosystems in additional to providing a trophic link, accentuating the importance of considering the crab holobiont functions in a nested ecosystem.

14119419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14119419.value: In the future, we will attempt to further dissect the mechanism of lignocellulose degradation in mangrove crab species based on a multi-omics approach consisting of three major components: metagenome of gut microbiome, transcriptomic analyses on endogenous CAZyme expression profile, and proteomic analyses and enzyme activity assay on host/microbial digestive enzymes, and to elucidate its evolution among crabs with different dietary preference and phylogenetic position. We aim to test TWO major hypotheses: 1/ the holobionts, consisting of endosymbiotic gut microbiome and host encoded CAZymes, work complementarily to effect lignocellulose degradation in mangrove herbivorous sesarmid crabs; and 2/ there is an evolutionary trend of key CAZyme gene family expansion with higher expression level and enrichment of cellulolytic endosymbiotic microbes in mangrove herbivorous sesarmid species to better adapt to lignocellulose degradation compared to omnivorous or carnivorous species in related families. The project will therefore reveal the mechanism(s) facilitating the utilization of plant materials as food source and hence promote terrestrialization as well as rapid adaptive radiation of sesarmid crabs. We can also illuminate the uncertainties on how the dependence on microbial and host encoded enzymes on lignocellulose degradation may vary according to the phylogenetic and environmental drivers to overcome evolutionary constraints.

14119419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14119419.value: Crabs of the family Sesarmidae (Crustacea: Brachyura) dominate mangrove forests and underwent rapid diversification after acquisition of a plant-feeding lifestyle, which is believed to be largely facilitated by gut microbes, followed by successful colonization to intertidal and terrestrial environments. The acquisition of microbial symbionts allows rapid adaptation and exploitation of novel ecological niches have significantly contributed to the evolutionary fitness and success of their hosts. The microbe-host interactions and their evolution remain largely understudied in marine invertebrates. We studied the composition and functional capacity of the gut microbes for mangrove species and found that the gut microbiome assemblage in crabs is largely determined by host identity, and to a lesser extent influenced by environmental factors. Patterns of phylosymbiosis and cophylogeny were observed in different crab families with different levels of significance, with the gut microbiome of Sesarmidae showing signals of both. Metagenome analyses suggested that the microbiome in Sesarmidae is functionally important to their hosts in sustaining under a low-quality diet by providing digestive enzymes, essential amino acids and fatty acids supplementation, thus supporting their host to fulfill their ecological roles. With our discovery, we put forward the application of the holobiont concept on the studies of crustaceans.

14120419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120419.value: Our aim is to identify and characterize metastasis-associated genes that play critical roles in the progression of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Metastasis is the major cause of PDAC high mortality. However, genes that regulated PDAC metastasis are largely unknown. To prompt the development of novel therapeutics, it is necessary to identify genes and pathways critical in PDAC metastasis. In our preliminary study, we conducted a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screening in PDAC orthotopic mouse model to identify genes that associated with PDAC metastasis. We established mutated PDAC cell pool by lentivirus of CRISPR/Cas9 genome-wide sgRNA library. The cells were then implanted into the pancreas of nude mice. The distal metastatic tissues were obtained for sequencing sgRNA motifs to identify the genes which promote metastasis. We identified a gene POU4F3 which was not previously reported to be associated with cancer metastasis. POU4F3 expression was downregulated in PDAC cell lines and tissues from our own cohort and public clinical datasets (GEO, TCGA). More importantly, our data demonstrated that POU4F3 expression was dramatically reduced in metastatic tumors as compared to primary tumors, suggesting important roles in PDAC metastasis. We manipulated POU4F3 expression in PDAC cells by knocking out, or rescued for assays including soft agar assay, chamber assays and orthotopic implantation to study its functions in PDAC. We demonstrated that POU4F3 exhibited anti-metastatic role in PDAC. Knockout of POU4F3 promoted PDAC cell transformation, migration and invasion in vitro and metastasis in vivo. We next explored the mechanism leading to POU4F3 silencing. Our results demonstrated that DNA hypermethylation of CpG island frequently occurred within the POU4F3 promoter, leading to the reduced expression in PDAC tissues. We further showed that POU4F3 negatively regulated ARHGDIB, CEBPD, BCYRN1 and ETV4 that play important roles in the metastatic phenotypes of cancer cells. Our exciting preliminary results prompted us to believe that POU4F3 is a novel metastasis-associated gene with critical roles in PDAC progression. In this proposal, we intend to 1) further characterize the function and delineate the pathways of POU4F3 and its target genes; 2) characterize the transcriptional regulation of POU4F3 on its target genes; 3) unravel the epigenetic mechanisms in the silencing of POU4F3; and 4) study the clinical implication of POU4F3 and its targets gene in PDAC. Knowledge gained from this project will unveil a critical pathway in regulating PDAC metastasis, and provide novel therapeutic targets against metastasis. 本研究的目的是發現胰腺癌發展過程中與轉移相關的重要基因。 腫瘤轉移是胰腺癌高死亡率的主要原因，而目前與胰腺癌轉移相關的基因，很大程度上是未知的。 因此尋找與胰腺癌轉移相關的關鍵基因和信號通路，能夠極大的促進用於胰腺癌的臨床創新療法發展。 在前期的初步研究中，通過胰腺癌原位接種小鼠模型進行全基因組CRISPR / Cas9篩查，以鑒定與胰腺癌轉移相關的基因。 使用包含CRISPR / Cas9全基因組sgRNA文庫的慢病毒建立了一系列突變的胰腺癌細胞，將突變細胞植入裸鼠的胰腺，借此獲得遠端轉移組織。 並將轉移組織用於sgRNA motif測序，以發現相關的促轉移基因。 基於此，我們發現一種轉移相關的基因POU4F3，該基因之前無相關報導。 對實驗室已有細胞系和組織樣本以及一些公共臨床資料庫（GEO,TCGA）進行分析，結果均證實在胰腺癌中POU4F3表達下調。 同時，我們的結果也發現，與原發性腫瘤相比，POU4F3在轉移性腫瘤中表達量更低，這也進一步證明POU4F3在胰腺癌轉移中具有重要作用。 通過基因敲除或者高表達實驗調控POU4F3的表達水準，並運用軟瓊脂實驗，小室實驗以及原位移植動物實驗研究POU4F3在胰腺癌中的功能。 體外實驗結果證實敲除POU4F3能夠增強胰腺癌細胞轉化，遷移和傾襲能力，體內實驗證實敲除該分子可以促進腫瘤發生轉移。 我們對導致POU4F3沉默的機制也進行了研究探討，結果表明POU4F3啟動子內CpG島DNA超甲基化，是導致胰腺癌組織中POU4F3表達降低的主要原因。 進一步的實驗表明，POU4F3對ARHGDIB，CEBPD，BCYRN1和ETV4基因有負調控作用，而這些基因在癌細胞的轉移表型中均起著重要作用。 基於以上這些結果，我們認為POU4F3是一個新穎的腫瘤轉移相關基因，其在胰腺癌發展過程中具有重要作用。 接下來的研究計畫主要包括：1，進一步發現並闡明該分子的功能和涉及的信號通路，以及相關的靶分子; 2，闡明POU4F3對靶基因的轉錄調控作用; 3，揭示POU4F3沉默相關的表觀遺傳機制; 4，研究POU4F3及其靶基因在胰腺癌中的臨床意義。 該專案的成果不僅將揭示調節胰腺癌轉移的關鍵信號通路，更為抗胰腺癌轉移提供新的移治療靶點。

14120419.label: Realisation of objectives
14120419.value: The clinical relevance of POU4F3 in PDAC POU4F3 was lower in pancreatic cancer tissues than their matched adjacent normal tissues. Furthermore, the expression of POU4F3 was lower in metastatic pancreatic cancer tumors than primary ones. The decreased expression of POU4F3 in malignant pancreatic tissues was further observed in public pancreatic cancer datasets. In the GDS4102 and GDS4103, the expression of POU4F3 in the pancreatic cancer samples were significantly lower than non-malignant tissues (P < 0.01 and P < 0.0001, respectively). POU4F3 functions as a metastasis suppressor in pancreatic cancer Knocking out POU4F3 did not significantly change cell proliferation in vitro. Consistently, rescuing POU4F3 in POU KO cells showed similar results. POU KO PANC1 cells formed a higher number of colonies than control cells by soft agar assay (P < .05). Furthermore, the number of migrated and invaded cells was higher in sgPOUs group than in sgNTCs group in BxPC3, Capan2 and PANC1 (P < .0001, P < .01 and P < .05, respectively), whereas rescuing POU4F3 in POU KO PANC1 cells reversed the migration and invasion trend. Consistent with in vitro proliferation assays, the tumor growth of POU KO group and control group showed no significant difference in the subcutaneous transplant model. In the orthotopic implantation model, the metastases on six organs/tissues were examined, including the diaphragm, mesenteric lymph node, liver, lung, peritoneum, and spleen. These mice of the sgPOUs group developed severe metastatic tumors than these of sgNTCs group (P < .01). Firstly, comparing metastases on each organ/tissue, the sgPOUs group derived more metastatic tumors than the sgNTC group. Secondly, the sgPOUs group showed multi-organ metastases, while most mice of the sgNTCs group only developed metastases in one or two organs. EZH2 regulates POU4F3 expression in pancreatic cancer We reported previously that Enhancer of Zeste Homolog 2 (EZH2) plays an important role in the progression of pancreatic cancer and hepatocellular cancer by epigenetic gene silencin. Thus, we hypothesized that EZH2 may also regulate the expression of POU4F3 through epigenetic modification in pancreatic cancer. By analyzing GDS4103, POU4F3 expression level was associated reversely with EZH2 expression level. We knocked down EZH2 in PANC-1 and SW1990 by shRNA or siRNA, and found that the expression of POU4F3 was significantly increased in these cells. On the contrary, ectopic overexpression of EZH2 in HPDE led to a significant decrease of POU4F3 level. As EZH2 is the catalytic subunit of polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2) which inhibits target genes expression by trimethylation of Lys-27 of histone 3 (H3K27me3), we examined the role of histone modification on POU4F3 expression. By ChIP assays, more EZH2 and H3K27me3 but less RNA polymerase II was recruited to the promoter of POU4F3 in PANC-1 and SW1990, comparing to those in HPDE. After knocking down EZH2 in PANC-1 by shRNA, we detected a decrease of EZH2, EED, SUZ12 and H3K27me3 enrichment at the POU4F3 promoter. In contrast, HPDE cells overexpressing EZH2 showed an enhancement of the occupancy of EZH2, EED, SUZ12 and H3K27me3 at the promoter. DNA methylation regulates POU4F3 expression in pancreatic cancer DNA hypermethylation in POU4F3 gene was reported in cervical cancer, glioma, and colon cancer. Hence, DNA methylation might also regulate POU4F3 expression in pancreatic cancer. Firstly, we analyzed the feature of the POU4F3 promoter and found this region harbors two CpG islands which may be the target for methylation. Then, we analyzed DNA methylation of pancreatic adenocarcinoma in TCGA dataset and found the methylation level in POU4F3 promoter was significantly higher in cancer samples than the paired normal samples (n = 9, P < .01). Furthermore, we validated this result with pancreatic cell lines and clinical samples by qMSP. All tested pancreatic cancer cell lines displayed an increased methylation level in POU4F3 promoter compared to HPDE cells (P < .05 to .001). Pancreatic cancer samples also exhibited enhanced methylation level in the promoter compared to the paired adjacent normal tissue samples (n = 42, P < .0001). To reveal the methylation map of the POU4F3 promoter in pancreatic cells, we performed the bisulfite sequencing. The fragment (357 bp) within the POU4F3 promoter, which spanned the qMSP detected region and adjacent to transcript start site, was amplified from bisulfite-treated genomic DNA of HPDE and SW1990 cells, respectively, and sequenced. The sequencing results confirmed the results of qMSP. The whole region was hypermethylated in SW1990 cells, but not in HPED cells. Next, we treated PANC1 cells and SW1990 cells with 5-azacytidine (5AZA), a DNA methyltransferases (DNMTs) inhibitor, or DZnep, an inhibitor of all PRC2 complex, and found that POU4F3 expression increased significantly. We previously reported that EZH2 can regulate DNA methylation indirectly. So we investigated the role of EZH2 in regulating the DNA methylation of POU4F3 promoter. We found that knocking-down EZH2 with shRNA resulted in less DNMT3B binding to and decreased DNA methylation in the promoter of POU4F3, and increased POU4F3 expression in PANC1 cells, while overexpressing EZH2 in HPDE led to increased occupancy of DNMT3B and DNA methylation level in the promoter of POU4F3, and decreased POU4F3 expression. POU4F3 inhibits directly the expression of ARHGDIB in pancreatic cancer Next, we decided to reveal the downstream target of POU4F3 in pancreatic cancer. Considering POU4F3 as a metastatic suppressor gene, we focused on detecting genes related to tumor metastasis, such as EMT-related molecules, MMPs, tumor stem cell-related molecules, and perineural invasion (PNI) associated genes. We found that the perineural invasion (PNI) related gene ARHGDIB may be a direct target of POU4F3 in cells with knocked-out or upregulated of POU4F3. Knocked out of POU4F3 in PANC-1 led to an increase of ARHGDIB expression, while overexpression of POU4F3 in PANC-1 cells resulted in a reduction of ARHGDIB level. Then, we analyzed the public dataset and found that ARHGDIB expression was negatively correlated with the expression of POU4F3 in clinical samples. Further analysis showed that it displayed a significant increase of expression in pancreatic cancer compared to non-cancerous tissue, and significantly upregulated ARHGIB expression in circulating tumor cells (CTCs) compared to the primary pancreatic cancer. In addition, by analyzing survival data for pancreatic cancer patients, we could observe that patients with high expression ARHGDIB exhibited shorter overall survival than those with low expression ARHGDIB. Therefore, we chose this gene with significant clinical relevance as a candidate target gene of POU4F3 for follow-up research, and hypothesized that POU4F3 directly regulated the expression of ARHGDIB. Firstly, we used the analysis tool to predict the binding site of POU4F3 in ARHGDIB, and then we carried out the ChIP-PCR experiment,. We showed that there was a significant enrichment of POU4F3 at this site. In turn, we performed the double fluorescent enzyme reporting test and found that only ectopic intact POU4F3, but not its mutants with truncated DNA binding domain, could repress the ARHGDIB-Luc reporter activity in transfected PANC-1. The above experiments demonstrated that POU4F3 directly negatively regulated the expression of ARHGDIB.

14120419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120419.value: This study highlights the discovery of a novel pancreatic cancer metastatic suppressor POU4F3, which is regulated by EZH2 that can be targeted. Revealing the pathways regulated by POU4F3 will allow deeper understanding of the cancer metastatic network in PDAC, and provide novel therapeutic targets for the effective and specific treatments for advanced PDAC. This study will provide more evidence for the therapeutics targeting epigenetic aberrancy for treating advanced stage cancers with distal metastasis. The association of the metastasis suppressor gene POU4F3 and its regulating targets with the clinicopathological parameters will prompt the development of prognostic markers predicting the chance of developing distal metastasis. Lastly, our study will provoke the investigation of POU4F3 and its target genes in various cancers.

14120419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120419.value: The metastatic nature of pancreatic cancer is the major cause of its high mortality. However, little is known about genes that regulate the metastasis of pancreatic cancer. Here, we employed a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screening system in an orthotopic implantation mouse model to identify genes that might modulate pancreatic cancer metastasis. We identified a novel metastasis regulator POU4F3 and confirmed its functions with in vitro and in vivo assays. Expression of POU4F3 decreased gradually from pancreatic primary to metastatic tumor compared to normal tissue. It's expression positively associated with patient survival. Knocking out POU4F3 promoted transformation, migration and invasion of pancreatic cancer cells without changing its growth, and increased the incidence of metastasis in the orthotopic implantation model without changing the growth of tumor in the subcutaneous model. These indicated that POU4F3 acted as a metastasis suppressor in pancreatic cancer. Furthermore, we demonstrated that POU4F3 was suppressed in pancreatic cancer by upregulated EZH2 which bound to the promoter of POU4F3 and established repressive histone modification and DNA methylation. Overall, our work suggested that EZH2-POU4F3 pathway might serve as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in pancreatic cancer.
