14120619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14120619.value: Initially discovered as transcripts out of “junk DNA” regions of our genome, long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are emerging as key regulators of major biological processes impacting development, differentiation, and diseases. Characterization of lncRNA functions has been the focus of many research groups in the past decade. It is well known that functional modes of lncRNAs are intimately associated with their cellular localization; relative nuclear enrichment of lncRNAs compared to mRNAs is a prevalent phenomenon but the underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. Considering the crucial roles of RNA binding proteins (RBPs) in determining RNA fate, we reasoned that a system wide screen for RBPs associated with nuclear enriched lncRNAs (nuc-lncRNAs) will reveal novel mechanisms of how lncRNA nuclear localization is determined and shed light into lncRNA functionality. To test the notion, we have harnessed a recently released large cohort of RBP eCLIPseq data from K562 and HepG2 cells and analyzed their binding profiles on nuc-lncRNAs. The pilot study leads to the discovery of an array of RBPs that bind with nuc-lncRNAs, among which HNRNPU and SAFB2 display the highest affinity. We thus hypothesize that lncRNA-RBP interactions is prevalently present in transcriptome and HNRNPU/SAFB2 binding may play active role in directly lncRNA nuclear enrichments. To test this hypothesis, three aims are proposed (1) to further characterize RBP and nuc-lncRNA interactions; (2) to further elucidate HNRNPU/SAFB2 association with nuc-lncRNAs; (3) to experimentally test the active role of HNRNPU/ SAFB2 in lncRNA nuclear localization. Once completed, our findings will for the first time map RBP-lncRNA interactome and identify novel mechanisms regulating lncRNA nuclear enrichment, thus will significantly advance our understanding of lncRNA fate and function in cells. 最初被發現作為我們基因組的“垃圾DNA”區域的長非編碼RNA（lncRNA）正在成為影響發育，分化和疾病的主要生物過程的關鍵調節因子。在過去的十年中，lncRNA功能的表徵一直是許多研究小組關注的焦點。眾所周知，lncRNA的功能模式與其細胞核中的位置密切相關;與mRNA相比，lncRNA的相對富集於細胞核中是一種普遍現象，但潛在的機制仍然未知。考慮到RNA結合蛋白（RBPs）在RNA調控中的關鍵作用，我們推斷，與對在細胞核中富集的lncRNA（nuc-lncRNA）相關的RBP種類的系統研究將揭示如何確定lncRNA在細胞核中的定位機制並揭示lncRNA的功能。 為了驗證這一假設，我們利用了最近發布的來自K562和HepG2細胞的RBP eCLIP-seq數據，並分析了它們對nuc-lncRNAs的結合譜。通過該試驗研究， 還發現一系列與nuc-lncRNA結合的RBP，其中HNRNPU和SAFB2顯示出最高的親和力。因此，我們假設lncRNA-RBP相互作用普遍存在於轉錄組中，並且HNRNPU / SAFB2結合可能在直接lncRNA核富集中起積極作用。為了進一步驗證這一假設，我們提出了三個目標（1）進一步研究RBP和nuc-lncRNA相互作用; （2）進一步闡明HNRNPU / SAFB2與nuc-lncRNA的相關性; （3）實驗測試HNRNPU / SAFB2在lncRNA核定位中的作用。一旦完成，我們的研究結果將首次揭示RBP-lncRNA相互作用組，並鑑定調節lncRNA核富集的新機制，從而將顯著提高我們對細胞中lncRNA命運和功能的理解。

14120619.label: Realisation of objectives
14120619.value: For Objective 1, we leveraged several publicly available datasets from ENCODE which were generated from both K562 and HepG2 cells; these include RNA-seq, performed on nuclear (nuc) and cytosolic (cyto) fractions of the cells, eCLIP performed for 90 RBPs(RNA-binding proteins) in K562 and 78 in HepG2 cells. The results revealed HNRNPU, SAFB2 in K562 cells, HNRNPL and HNRNPC in HepG2 cells are associated with nuc-lincRNAs(large intergenic non-coding RNAs) and may function to regulate lincRNA nuclear retention. The objective has been completely achieved. For Objective 2, we further elucidated HNRNPU/SAFB2 association with nuc-lncRNAs through binding distinct core motifs, flanking sequence compositions, or secondary structures of nuc-lincRNAs, by analyzing the nuc-lincRNA sequence specificities near the RBP binding sites. The Objective has been compeletly achieved. For Objective 3, we knocked down HNRNPU in K562 cells and selected 7 nuc-lincRNAs to examine their nuclear distribution. The results confirmed that HNRNPU promotes nuc-lincRNA nuclear retention. We further conducted a λN peptide-BoxB system and demonstrated that HNRNPU indeed actively drives RNA nuclear enrichment. Moreover, by CoIP experiments, we confirmed that HNRNPU shares overlapping binding sites with SAFB2 and physically interacts with SAFB2, indicating they work synergistically to co-regulate lincRNA nuclear localization. The Objective has been completely achieved.

14120619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14120619.value: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) are key regulators of major biological processes and their functional modes are dictated by their subcellular localization. Relative nuclear enrichment of lncRNAs compared to mRNAs is a prevalent phenomenon but the molecular mechanisms governing their nuclear retention in cells remain largely unknown. Here in this study, we harness the recently released eCLIP data for a large number of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) in K562 and HepG2 cells and utilize multiple bioinformatics methods to comprehensively survey the roles of RBPs in lncRNA nuclear retention. We identify an array of splicing RBPs that bind to nuclear-enriched lincRNAs (large intergenic non-coding RNAs) thus may act as trans-factors regulating their nuclear retention. Further analyses reveal that these RBPs may bind with distinct core motifs, flanking sequence compositions, or secondary structures to drive lincRNA nuclear retention. Moreover, network analyses uncover potential co-regulatory RBP clusters, and the physical interaction between HNRNPU and SAFB2 proteins in K562 cells is further experimentally verified. Altogether, our analyses reveal previously unknown factors and mechanisms that govern lincRNA nuclear localization in cells.

14120619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14120619.value: We find that RNA binding protein HNRNPU promotes lincRNA retention in the nucleus but the mechanism is unknown. In the future, more efforts can be directed to further investigate the underlying mechanism of how HNRNPU actively drives lncRNA nuclear retention or indirectly through preventing lncRNA export to the cytoplasm. Moreover, we find that RBP bind distinct core motifs, flanking sequence compositions, or secondary structures to drive lincRNA nuclear retention. It would be interesting to assess the contribution of each of these binding specificities to the lincRNA nuclear retention. Finally, since our study is limited to the RBPs with available eCLIP data from ENCODE; with the rapid release of more protein-RNA binding profiles, we envision a more comprehensive view of nuc-lncRNA/protein interactomes and mechanisms will be uncovered; multiple independent pathways are likely to be responsible for nuclear enrichment of lncRNAs, recognizing specific RNA sequences and/or other features of the ribonucleoprotein.

14120619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14120619.value: LncRNA represent a relatively novel family of RNAs and important functional molecules in cells. Unlike mRNAs that are exported from the nucleus and translated in the cytoplasm, some long noncoding RNAs remain in the nucleus and have various functions such as regulating DNA methylation, modulating enhancer activity, and promoting the formation of biomolecular condensates. However, the mechanism of how some lncRNAs remain in the nucleus is unknown. In our research project, we used the high-throughput sequencing data detecting RNA-binding protein(RBP) binding sites on RNAs, and RNA-seq data of RNAs from nuclear and cytoplasm fractions to address whether some RNA-binding proteins may function to retain lncRNAs in the nucleus and whether there are sequence-specificities of nuclear-lncRNAs that dictate their nuclear location. In conclusion, our research finds that some RBPs such as HNRNPU and SAFB2 bind and promote nuclear retention of lncRNAs. We also find that the RNA sequence of core motifs, flanking sequence compositions, or secondary structures of lncRNAs drive their nuclear retention. Altogether, our analyses reveal previously unknown factors and mechanisms that govern lincRNA nuclear localization in cells.

14121019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14121019.value: The plant Golgi is a carbohydrate factory that produces non-cellulosic polysaccharides necessary for maintenance of the cell wall. The biosynthetic machinery is arranged along the cis-to-trans axis of the Golgi. The plant cell wall is a dynamic structure that is restructured as the plant cell differentiates. Polysaccharide synthesis and vesicular trafficking are modulated to support these changes. The root cap is a thimble-like structure that protects the root meristem as the root grows into the soil. Border cells are secretory cells that deposit mucilage into the soil. The cells that constitute the skin of the root cap are continuously sloughed off and replenished by underlying precursor cells. Border cell detachment coincides with an increase in levels of the pectic polysaccharide xylogalacturonan (XGA) secretion. We recently showed that XGA is sorted into large vesicles derived from the trans-Golgi, which we termed XGA-LVs. Interestingly, XGA-LVs accumulate in border cell precursors, but they do not fuse with the plasma membrane until the precursor cells mature into border cells. The cargo molecules of XGA-LVs are distinct from regular secretory vesicles derived from the trans-Golgi network. Our data suggest that XGA-LV secretion is regulated to ensure that the contents localize to the interface between the root cap and the soil. However, the cargoes of XGA-LVs have not been characterized, and how the trafficking is controlled is not known. We propose to identify protein cargos of the XGA-LV and investigate how they are sorted. Our preliminary data indicate that XGA-LVs carry a polysaccharide-degrading enzyme. We will determine the amino acid sequences required for sorting of this protein into XGA-LVs. To identify other XGA-LV cargo proteins, we will isolate vesicle fractions associated with XGA epitopes from the root cap samples and carry out proteomic analyses. Arabidopsis mutant lines in which border-like cell release is defective are available, and we demonstrated that some of them do not produce XGA-LVs. Combined use of microscopy and molecular biology approaches in wild-type and mutant Arabidopsis are expected to reveal the molecular mechanisms involved in regulation of XGA-LV trafficking. Our research will identify factors involved in the secretory pathway that play roles in exocytosis amplification in a cell type-specific manner. Furthermore, our deliverables will contribute to design of efficient phytotechnologies for engineering plant roots to produce commercial proteins or to secret polypeptides that protect plants from soil contaminants.

14121019.label: Realisation of objectives
14121019.value: We successfully achieved most of the research goals we outlined in our initial objectives. These findings have been compiled into a manuscript for publication in the Plant Cell, titled "Bearskin2 (BRN2) mediates the coordinated secretion of xylogalacturonan and root cap polygalacturonase in Arabidopsis border-like cells." However, the editor suggested further experiments to enhance the impact of our work in relation to plant development. During subsequent studies, we discovered that root cap-mediated secretion and root cap cell detachment play a protective role against abiotic stresses. Since the root cap lacks a cuticle layer, continuous cell turnover and mucilage deposition at the root cap surface appear to provide both chemical defense and a rhizobium-conducive environment for root growth. We will soon submit a revised manuscript, supplemented with additional data about stress protection, to a respected journal. The new title of the manuscript is "Bearskin2-mediates secretion of mucilage from the Arabidopsis root cap to facilitate border-like cell turnover and protection from salt stresses” to underscore the safeguarding function of the root cap. Our transcriptomic analysis of the root cap, conducted as part of Objective 3, identified genes involved in auxin synthesis, transport, and response, associated with mucilage secretion and root cap cell separation. This finding was unexpected and shifted our research direction toward local auxin gradient for root cap morphogenesis. We are currently preparing two additional manuscripts based on our new findings: one on Golgi stack remodeling and xylogalacturonan secretion regulated by auxin gradient, and the other on cell differentiation kinetics in the root cap controlled by auxin distribution. Objective 1. To determine motifs in root cap polygalacturonase for its sorting into XGL-LVs Root cap polygalacturonase (RCPG) is a protein cargo found in a distinct type of secretory vesicle that transports xylogalacturonan (XGA). Unlike conventional secretory vesicles derived from the trans-Golgi network, these vesicles are produced from the trans-Golgi. We discovered that RCPG, a putative pectin-digesting enzyme, accumulates in these vesicles. This study aims to identify the regions in RCPG that are essential for its sorting. Transgenic lines were generated expressing truncated RCPGs lacking either the catalytic domain or the linker between the signal peptide and the catalytic domain. The RCPG lacking the catalytic domain failed to reach the trans-Golgi, where XGA is packaged into vesicles. Instead, the truncated RCPG was retained in the cis-Golgi, indicating that the catalytic domain is required for proper sorting. Conversely, RCPG lacking the linker region remained in the endoplasmic reticulum. These results were confirmed using confocal laser scanning microscopy and immunogold labeling. Interestingly, full-length RCPG was detected only in root cap cells despite being driven by a constitutive promoter. However, the modified RCPGs lacking either the linker or catalytic domain accumulated in all root cells, suggesting that RCPG secretion is regulated by cell type-specific expression that overrides the constitutive promoter. Objective 2. To identify cargo proteins of XGA-LVs by mass spectrometric analyses Despite our efforts, we have encountered significant challenges in isolating XGA-LVs from root cap samples of Arabidopsis, alfalfa, and maize roots. We have employed various purification strategies, including sucrose density gradient centrifugation, pull-down purification using our RCPG antibody, and pull-down purification using an RFP antibody. However, these methods have failed to yield XGA-LV fractions that are free of contamination from cell wall polysaccharides, including xyloglucan, homogalacturonan, rhamnogalacturonan that are characteristic of regular secretory vesicles when we examined via immunoblot analysis (dot blot). In light of these difficulties, we are pursuing alternative strategies for identifying XGA-LV cargo proteins, which is proximity labeling, where RCPG is tagged with a biotin ligase and search for proteins associated with RCPG with mass spectrometry. This approach has provided clues to identify proteins that are physically associated with XGA-LVs without the need for extensive purification. Objective 3: Identifying Genes Involved in XGA-LV Production via Comparative Transcriptomic Analysis To achieve this objective, we developed a dissection method for isolating root cap-specific RNA samples suitable for transcriptomic analysis. This method enabled us to identify 3235 and 746 genes that were differentially expressed in smbbrn1brn2 and brn1brn2 mutants, respectively, compared to the wild type. Gene Ontology (GO) term analysis of these differentially expressed genes (DEGs) revealed an enrichment of genes involved in auxin signaling, auxin transport, and auxin biosynthesis pathways. Notably, these auxin-related pathway genes were altered in the smbbrn1brn2 mutant, but not in the brn1brn2 mutant, where XGA-LV production is inhibited. Our initial investigation focused on genes encoding auxin response factors (e.g., ARF10 and ARF16) and their regulators (e.g., IAA33 and miR160). These studies revealed that XGA-LV production is downstream of a broader cell differentiation program that begins in meristematic cells and progresses towards border-like cells (BLCs). This finding was somewhat unexpected, suggesting that studying XGA-LV in isolation from the root cap developmental program might pose a significant challenge. Objective 4: Characterizing XGA-LV Trafficking in Arabidopsis Mutants with Defective BLC Detachment To address this objective, we conducted detailed electron microscopy and tomography analyses, along with correlative light and electron microscopy (CLEM), of BLCs from smb, brn1, and brn2 mutants. As mentioned in the mid-term report, syp41/42, ala3, and Atkinesin-13a mutants were not suitable for comparison due to their respective issues. Our investigations revealed that BRN2 is the gene responsible for XGA synthesis, and mucilage secretion is indeed inhibited in brn2 BLCs. Interestingly, RCPG secretion still occurred via TGN-derived vesicles in brn2, indicating that its export is not significantly affected by the absence of XGA-LVs. We demonstrated that RCPG is essential for normal BLC detachment, but BRN2 is not. In addition to BRN2, we also examined the effects of auxin transport and synthesis inhibition on XGA-LV production. BLC detachment and XGA secretion are also defective in the smb root cap. But we found that auxin distribution is altered in smb, which caused not only impaired XGA-LV production but also aberrant in root cap architecture and remodeling of organelles, including Golgi stacks, vacuoles, and plastids associated with root cap differentiation. These findings suggest that auxin is a fundamental regulator of the root cap morphogenesis and BLC turnover. Using electrophoretic mobility shift assay, we were able to demonstrate that SMB binds to promoter regions of genes encoding auxin signaling, auxin synthesis, and auxin transport, indicating that SMB plays key roles in the establishment of auxin gradient in the root cap.

14121019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14121019.value: 1. BEARSKIN2 (BRN2) Mediates Mucilage Secretion and Protects the Root Cap from Abiotic Stresses BRN2 is a BLC-specific NAC family transcription factor essential for XGA-LV production. XGA synthesis and mucilage secretion were significantly impaired in brn2 BLCs. This disrupted mucilage secretion rendered the brn2 root cap more susceptible to salt or osmotic stresses, leading to stunted root growth in the mutant. These findings demonstrate that BRN2-mediated mucilage secretion acts as a chemical barrier, shielding the root cap from abiotic stresses. 2. SOMBRERO (SMB) Regulates Auxin Distribution and Root Cap Morphogenesis SMB is a root cap-specific NAC family transcription factor crucial for XGA-LV production. Gene expression analysis revealed alterations in auxin signaling, auxin synthesis, and auxin transport pathways in the smb mutant root cap. Additionally, cell organization and auxin gradient were disrupted in the smb root cap, indicating that auxin plays critical roles in root cap morphogenesis and BLC turnover. Collectively, these findings establish SMB as a central regulator of local auxin distribution in the root cap, essential for maintaining the root cap architecture and its developmental gradient. 3. RCPG is a protein cargo of XGA vesicles and its overexpression accelerates BLC turnover RCPG is a BLC-specific polygalacturonase secreted via XGA-LV, and its secretion is essential for BLC detachment. Truncated RCPGs failed to reach the cell wall due to impaired sorting into XGA-LVs. Overexpression of RCPG accelerated BLC turnover without altering root cap cell organization, suggesting that cell loss at the root cap surface is coordinated with cell division in the root cap meristem. Our research has advanced our understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying root cap development and its role in plant stress tolerance. The absence of a cuticle layer and Casparian strips renders root caps vulnerable to the diffusion of potentially toxic water-soluble molecules. We demonstrated that BLCs and the mucilage they secrete form a protective barrier against these challenges and that BRN2 plays a central role in the protection mechanism. The identification of SMB as key regulators of auxin distribution adds valuable insights into the intricate processes that govern root cap development. Our findings underscore the importance of auxin metabolism and transport in organ development in plants. Furthermore, we provide evidence for novel functions of rhizo-secretion in protecting the root cap from abiotic stresses. These results offer promising strategies for designing crop plants that can thrive under unfavorable soil conditions by manipulating mucilage secretion and border cell shedding.

14121019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14121019.value: 1. Identification of genes regulated by BRN2 BRN2 inactivation leads to a reduction in mucilage secretion. Genes contributing to mucilage secretion could be identified by searching promoter regions where BRN2 binds. We will employ chromatin immunoprecipitation to search for candidate genes controlled by BRN2. Given the critical role of rhizosecretion in root protection and growth, uncovering novel genes involved in this process would have significant implications for agrobiotechnology. 2. Coupling of BLC loss and cell division in the root cap The overexpression of RCPG accelerated BLC turnover without disrupting the root cap structure. This suggests that the loss of BLCs at the root cap surface triggers the supply of new root cap cells. We hypothesize that calcium signaling and mechanosensors play crucial roles in the coupling. We are preparing calcium sensor lines for monitoring calcium concentrations using time-lapse microscopy and isolating mechanosensor mutant lines. 3. Functional characterization of SMB in root cap morphogenesis The root cap architecture is disrupted in smb. We are creating SMB inducible mutant lines to observe the progressive loss of root cap structure and changes in auxin distribution with time-lapse imaging to elucidate the precise roles of SMB in maintaining root cap integrity and auxin regulation.

14121019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14121019.value: The root cap is a timble-like structure covering the root apical meristem. The root cap secrets mucilage that lubricates the root growth through the soil and molecules that control soil microbiome in the root’s vicinity. Mucilage and cells derived from the root cap form an extracellular trap surrounding the root to shield it from microbial pathogens. Our research identified a gene essential for mucilage secretion and demonstrated that mucilage also acts as a chemical barrier, protecting root cells from salt and osmotic stress. This finding holds promise for engineering crop plants that can better withstand unfavorable soil conditions. The outer cells of the root cap, known as border cells, shed from the root cap. We discovered that root cap mucilage contains a cell wall-digesting enzyme essential for border cell detachment. Interestingly, excessive secretion of this enzyme accelerated border cell loss without disrupting the root cap's organization, implying that lost cells are replenished through cell division. This compensatory mechanism suggests a novel signaling pathway within the root cap that links cell detachment in the outer cortex to cell division in the center, providing a valuable research system for investigating local cell-cell communication in plants.

14121619.value: 幽門螺旋菌是胃癌的主要因素，也是主要的致癌因子。幽門螺旋菌具有一系列的毒力因子幫助其宿主定植和感染。其中，細胞毒素VacA是一個重要的關鍵，這因子與胃病的風險有密切相關。然而，VacA如何與細胞膜結合並形成膜通道的機制是未知的。最近，我們的團隊應用冷凍電鏡技術獲得了3.3Å VacA六聚體的結構，首次揭示了其原子細節並其聚合組裝的基礎。我們的結果表明，VacA六聚體相互作用涉及p33和p55域。值得一提的是負責膜插入的VacA N端區域被埋在原體界面中，這表明膜通道形成需要明顯的結構變化。我們建議應用冷凍電鏡技術和X射線晶體學方法確定VacA的膜通道結構及其遺傳同種型。此外，我們將研究VacA膜通道形成之機制。這研究工作將讓我們更了解如何利用VacA來中斷宿主細胞和病機。我們的研究結果也將為設計治療新型治療藥物提供新的途徑。

14122019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14122019.value: The life expectancy at birth of males and females in Hong Kong increased from 67.8 and 75.3 years in 1971 to 81.7 and 87.7 in 2017, respectively. Approximately 17% of the Hong Kong population was 65 or older in mid-2018. These alarming statistical data and others collected from different regions of the globe indicate that chronic and old age-related diseases will have a huge impact on Hong Kong, China and the world in the future. With recent advances in genomic medicine, an increasing number of patients have been diagnosed with rare forms of hereditary neurodegenerative diseases which many of them are adult-onset, old age-related disorders. From 2015 to 2016, the general prevalence of rare diseases in Hong Kong was 1 in 67. In addition to DNA, which stores genetic materials inside the cell nucleus, RNA and proteins are two major biomolecules responsible for maintaining the proper functioning of cells, including neurons. In patients who suffer from hereditary rare neurodegenerative disorders, genetic mutations at the DNA level trigger neurological damage in the nervous system via toxic RNA and/or proteins. Polyglutamine (polyQ) diseases, including Huntington’s disease and several types of spinocerebellar ataxia, are caused by the genomic expansion of existing glutamine-coding trinucleotide cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat sequences. Contributions to the neurotoxicity of polyQ diseases are made by 1) RNA toxicity from expanded CAG repeat-containing mRNA and 2) protein toxicity from the corresponding elongated polyQ protein. Our group identified a set of genes that are dysregulated in cell and animal polyQ disease models. Intriguingly, we found that CAG RNA per se downregulated cellular gene expression, induced DNA damage and subsequently triggered apoptosis. We identified a hit inhibitory compound with the ability to rescue behavioural defects in a mouse model of polyQ disease. Importantly, CAG RNA-induced DNA damage could be restored upon treatment with our hit compound. We further found this compound to be capable of penetrating the blood-brain barrier in rodents. In the proposed work, we will aim to 1) further elucidate how CAG RNA mediates gene silencing, which leads to DNA damage, and 2) dissect the mechanism by which the hit compound mediates its suppression of DNA damage in patient neuronal cells and animal models. This work will enrich our current understanding of CAG RNA pathogenic mechanisms, and provide a mechanistic explanation to the inhibitory effect of a hit compound counteracting RNA toxicity in polyQ diseases. 除了細胞核內儲存遺傳信息的脫氧核糖核苷酸（DNA）分子外，核糖核苷酸（RNA）和蛋白質（protein）也是兩大類維持細胞正常功能的重要生物分子。深受罕見遺傳性神經系統退行性疾病折磨的患者，其DNA分子突變的遺傳信息便是通過毒性RNA和protein分子觸發神經系統的損傷。多聚穀氨醯胺疾病（Polyglutamine diseases，polyQ diseases），包括亨廷頓舞蹈症（Huntington's diseases，HD)和多種亞型的脊髓小腦運動失調症（Spinocerebellar ataxia，SCA），便是一大類遲發性顯性遺傳中樞神經系統退行性疾病。該疾病是由致病基因中編碼穀氨醯胺的CAG三核苷酸重複序列拷貝數異常擴增導致其編碼的多聚穀氨醯胺蛋白鏈（polyQ）異常延長所致。研究表明，包括異常延長的CAG三核苷酸重複RNA分子和polyQ蛋白鏈都會引起polyQ疾病病理。本實驗室的前期研究發現，在多聚穀氨醯胺疾病的細胞和動物模型中，一系列的基因表達水平會出現紊亂。更有趣的是，我們還發現異常延長的CAG三核苷酸重複RNA分子本身就會下調這些基因的表達，進而引起DNA損傷和触發細胞凋亡。本實驗室前期的小分子抑製劑篩選結果還發現了一個能有效提高多聚穀氨醯胺疾病老鼠模型的運動能力的小分子藥物。更重要的是，通過該藥物的治療，CAG三核苷酸重複RNA分子引起的DNA損傷也會被修復。而且，該藥物具有較強的滲透動物血腦屏障的特性。之後，我們計劃在病人神經元細胞和小鼠動物模型中繼續深入研究探索以下兩個方向：（1）進一步闡明CAG三核苷酸重複RNA分子如何介導基因沉默，從而引起DNA的損傷；（2）解析我們的小分子抑製藥物修復DNA損傷的分子機制。這項研究有助於我們更好地了解polyQ致病機制中CAG三核苷酸重複RNA的分子毒性，以及小分子抑製藥物的作用機理，為針對該毒性的下游藥物研發提供依據。

14122019.label: Realisation of objectives
14122019.value: Objective 1 Elucidate how sCAG RNA targets NUDT16 transcript to mediate gene silencing We identified several naturally occurring CTG repeats in the NUDT16 gene sequence, among which each of six such regions consist of at least six nucleotides of CTG repeats and are located within the transcribed region. Besides, we also detected distinct CTG-rich regions in the mouse Nudt16 gene. When transcribed, these CUG sequences could be targets of sCAG RNAs generated from expanded mutant CAG transcripts, which subsequently lead to NUDT16 gene silencing. As expected, the NUDT16 transcript level was reduced in cells transfected with synthetic sCAG RNA, and the silencing effect was positively correlated with the amount of sCAG RNA used in the transfection as well as proportional to the extent of caspase 3 activation. No such effects were observed in cells transfected with noncontinuous sCAG RNA rG-(CAACAG)3-C. Our findings thus indicated that synthetic sCAG RNA transfection per se is capable of inducing a specific down-regulation of NUDT16 and caspase activation. In addition to NUDT16, we performed quantitative real-time PCR on the remaining 16 down-regulated DEGs to determine whether they also demonstrated similar down-regulation in sCAG RNA-transfected SK-N-MC cells. Our results showed that the expression level of LTBP1, MOGS, NDUFV1, and QARS1 was reduced. We further found that these four genes all harbor CUG-rich regions in their transcripts, and each of these regions constitutes at least six nucleotides of continuous CUG sequences. The above observations suggested that sCAG RNA forms a heteroduplex with CUG sequences in general. Objective 2 Determine the involvement of single-strand and double-strand DNA breaks in sCAG RNA-induced DNA damage We determined whether the cellular DNA damage triggered by CAG RNA would lead to the activation of DDR pathways and found that expanded CAG RNA induced the phosphorylation of all ATR, ATM, and checkpoint kinases (CHKs) 1 and 2. The total level of these proteins remained unaltered. These protein kinases are involved in both single-strand (ATR and CHK1) and double-strand (ATM and CHK2) DDR pathways. We further detected the phosphorylation of p53 and an enhanced level of caspase 3 cleavage in cells transfected with expanded EGFP-CAG78 RNA. We observed enhanced cell death, using the lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) assay, in EGFP-CAG78-expressing SK-N-MC cells when compared with the unexpanded EGFPCAG27-expressing cells and the untransfected control. Our data indicate that both single- and double-strand DNA breaks are involved in sCAG RNA-induced DNA damage. Objective 3 Examine how the identified hit inhibitory compound counteracts sCAG RNA-induced NUDT16 gene silencing We investigated whether the stabilization of sCAG by our hit compound DB213 could inhibit the undesired hybridizations between the sCAG and CUG-containing NUDT16 mRNA and therefore impact NUDT16 gene silencing. Using 1H NMR spectroscopy, we observed that the addition of DB213 clearly reduced the guanine imino signals from C-G Watson–Crick base pairs in the sCAG-CUG heteroduplex. A corresponding increase in the intensity of the G7 signal from the sCAG homoduplex was observed, suggesting that DB213 has the ability to reduce the sCAG-CUG RNA heteroduplex by stabilizing the sCAG homoduplex. In line with this finding, our isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) results showed that DB213 had a higher binding affinity to rGG-(CAG)6-CC (Kd = 3.8 µM) than rGG-(CAG)4-(CUG)2-CC (Kd = 19.2 µM), suggesting that DB213 formed a stronger complex with the rCAG homoduplex over the rCAG/CUG heteroduplex. In synthetic sCAG RNA-transfected SK-N-MC cells, DB213 treatment restored cellular NUDT16 expression, an effect that was observed to be DB213 dose-dependent. In addition, both cell death and caspase 3 cleavage were suppressed in the DB213-treated cells. We further showed that DB213 treatment is capable of restoring the phosphorylation status of DNA damage kinases and cellular DNA damage. The total protein level of DNA damage kinases and p53 remained unchanged upon the treatment of DB213. In summary, our data show that DB213 counteracts sCAG RNA-induced NUDT16 gene silencing by preferentially stabilizing rCAG homoduplex RNA formation. This spares CUG-containing NUDT16 RNA transcripts in cells, and in turns maintains NUDT16 expression. Objective 4 Determine the roles of the hit compound in suppressing sCAG RNA-mediated NUDT16 DNA damage in mouse model Consistent with our cell-based data, activation of ATR and ATM DNA damage kinases as well as caspase 3 were observed in the brains of the R6/2 Huntington’s Disease (HD) transgenic disease model. Our data thus confirmed NUDT16 perturbation and DNA damage in HD mice in vivo. We previously demonstrated that in situ thermosensitive gel-assisted intranasal administration is an effective delivery route for brain-targeted delivery of DB213 in mice. The tolerance dose of DB213 was determined empirically. In open-field and rotarod tests, a 4-wk daily treatment of 25 mg/kg DB213 in in situ thermosensitive gel formulation significantly rescued the locomotor defects of the R6/2 mice by week 11. At the molecular level, down-regulated NUDT16 protein expression was restored, and the downstream DNA damage-induced apoptotic pathway was suppressed after DB213 treatment. Our findings provide in vivo evidence that DB213 has a positive effect on molecular and motor phenotypes in an HD mouse model.

14122019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122019.value: In this study, we showed that the expression of untranslatable expanded CAG RNA per se induced the cellular DNA damage response pathway. We found that expression of the Nudix hydrolase 16 (NUDT16) gene was down-regulated in mutant CAG RNA-expressing cells. The loss of NUDT16 function results in a misincorporation of damaging nucleotides into DNAs and leads to DNA damage. we identified a bisamidinium compound, DB213, that interacts specifically with the major groove of the CAG RNA homoduplex and disfavors the CAG-CUG heteroduplex formation. This action subsequently mitigated RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC)-dependent NUDT16 silencing in both in vitro cell and in vivo mouse disease models. After DB213 treatment, DNA damage, apoptosis, and locomotor defects were rescued in HD mice. This work establishes NUDT16 deficiency by CAG repeat RNAs as a pathogenic mechanism of polyQ diseases and as a potential therapeutic direction for HD and other polyQ diseases.

14122019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14122019.value: Finding a blood–brain barrier–penetrable hit compound for modulating the DNA damage repair pathway would be ideal for counteracting DNA damages in polyQ diseases in general. Our previous findings showed that the DB213 compound can pass blood brain barrier (Q. Wanget al., Efficient brain uptake and distribution of an expanded CAG RNA inhibitor DB213 via intranasal administration. Eur. J. Pharm. Sci.127, 240–251 (2019).). In the current study, we showed that DB213 is a strong binder to the major groove of sCAG duplex RNA and intranasal administration of the compound resulted in rescue of locomotor defects in disease mice. All the above findings indicate that DNA damage repair modulation is a feasible therapeutic approach for polyQ, including Huntington's, diseases, and DB213 can further be developed into a hit compound for treatment.

14122019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14122019.value: More than 40 human diseases are caused by simple repeat expansion in the human genome. Huntington's Disease (HD), a neurodegenerative disorder, is one example. This study established the role of toxic RNA in inducing DNA damage in HD. This basic science finding led us to identify a compound that has the ability to neutralize the toxic RNA. As a result, DNA damage is alleviated. In the long run, this study opens up a new direction for drug development on HD and other repeat expansion diseases.

14122319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14122319.value: Serine-arginine rich proteins (SR proteins) are a family of non-snRNP splicing factors that are essential for both constitutive and alternative splicing. They are extensively phosphorylated at multiple serine residues at their C-terminal arginine-serine (RS) domain, which are crucial to the regulation of spliceosome assembly, splice site selection, mRNA export, and translation. SR protein kinases (SRPKs) have been established as the major kinase family that phosphorylates SR proteins and regulate pre-mRNA splicing. Given their key roles in splicing regulation, abnormal expression or misregulation of SRPKs have been implicated in many diseases including multiple forms of cancer, Alzheimer’s disease, and the infection of viruses like HIV-1, HBV and HCV, suggesting that SRPKs represent new candidates for targeted therapeutics. Indeed, a number of studies have shown that knockdown or inhibition of SRPK1, the prototypic member of the family, has anti-tumoral effects. Several inhibitors of SRPK1, which all belong to the ATP-competitive class, have been reported thus far. However, ATP-competitive inhibitors must contend with the intracellular levels of ATP and more importantly may suffer from drug resistance caused by the development of resistance mutations at the ATP-bind clefts of the target kinases. Such mutations, which hinder drug binding but preserve the kinase catalytic activity, have been observed in many kinases targeted by clinically-approved ATP-competitive small molecule inhibitors. Therefore new strategy is required to develop novel SRPK1 inhibitor(s) that can overcome these caveats. We have recently developed a peptide inhibitor that targets a critical substrate docking groove in SRPK1. This inhibitor competes with the binding and phosphorylation of the prototypic SR protein SRSF1, which subsequently alters VEGF splicing and inhibits angiogenesis. Our work demonstrates that peptide inhibitor targeting the protein-protein interaction site between SRPK1 and its substrate is a feasible strategy. In addition, this inhibitor could be used together with ATP-competitive inhibitors to achieve synergistic inhibitory effect. In this proposal, through structure-based rational design and peptide engineering, we aim to optimize our peptide inhibitor into a novel lysine-specific covalent peptide inhibitor of SRPK1 that targets its substrate docking groove. This new inhibitor will feature target-specificity, site specificity, covalent tethering and possibly self cell-penetrating. Its activity against angiogenesis and tumor metastasis will be investigated. In addition, using this inhibitor, we will attempt to identify the SRPK1-regulated pre-mRNA splicing event(s) that contribute to tumor metastasis. Therefore our proposed works not only will provide a new specific inhibitor against SRPK1 but will also reveal new mechanism(s) to combat cancers. 絲氨酸/精氨酸富含蛋白（SR蛋白）是一類必需的剪接因子蛋白，屬於非核內小分子核糖核蛋白（snRNP）剪接因子家族，參與調節真核細胞mRNA的特定以及選擇性剪接。SR蛋白富含絲氨酸/精氨酸的C端結構域中的多個絲氨酸殘基都能被磷酸化，其不同的磷酸化狀態與SR蛋白細胞內功能，如剪接體聚集的調節，剪接位點的選擇，mRNA的運輸以及翻譯等都緊密相關。SR蛋白激酶（SRPKs）是目前被發現的主要負責SR蛋白磷酸化修飾以及pre-mRNA剪接的家族。鑒於它們在剪接調節中的重要作用，SRPKs 在細胞內的不正常表達或者調節已經被證明與多種疾病有關，其中包含一些類型的癌症，阿茲海默症以及艾滋病毒1型（HIV-1）、乙肝病毒（HBV）和丙肝病毒（HCV）感染等，這表明SRPKs可以作為一個靶向治療的潛在靶點。實際上，很多的研究已經表明敲除或者抑制SRPKs家族中典型的一種SRPK1后，已經出現了抗腫瘤效果。目前為止，已經有一些SRPK1的抑制劑被研究和報道出來，它們全都屬於与ATP 競爭的抑制剂。然而，作為潛在藥物，ATP競爭的抑制劑不僅要與細胞內高濃度的ATP競爭，更重要的是容易因目標激酶ATP結合域耐藥突變的產生而失效。 這種ATP結合域的耐藥突變會阻止藥物的結合但不影響激酶的催化活性，並且目前已經在多種臨床批准的以蛋白激酶為靶向目標的ATP競爭的小分子抑制劑中被發現。 因此需要新的策略來研究新型的 SRPK1抑制劑來克服上述提到的這些缺陷。近期我們已經發現了一個靶向SRPK1上一個重要的底物對接槽的多肽抑制劑，它可以競爭性抑制典型的SR蛋白SRSF1的結合以及磷酸化，隨後改變血管內皮生長因子（VEGF）pre-mRNA的剪接從而抑制血管生成。我們的研究表明，選擇多肽抑制劑靶向SRPK1及它的底物之間的蛋白-蛋白相互作用位點是一種可行的方案。此外，這個多肽抑制劑還可以與和ATP競爭的小分子抑制劑共同使用起到協同抑制的效果。 在此項研究計劃中，通過基於結構的理性設計輔助多肽工程，我們致力於優化我們現有的多肽抑制劑，使其成為一個新型的靶向底物對接槽并與賴氨酸特異性共價結合的SRPK1的多肽類抑制劑。這個新型的抑制劑將呈現出目標特異、位點特異、共價約束以及潛在的自主滲透細胞的特點。它的抗血管生成以及抑制腫瘤轉移的能力將被評估。此外，通過使用這個抑制劑，我們也將嘗試研究并鑒定由SRPK1對pre-mRNA的剪接調節而產生的對腫瘤新陳代謝的系列影響。 因此我們的研究計劃不僅能提供一種新型的SRPK1抑制劑的設計思路也能揭開抗癌的新機制。

14122319.label: Realisation of objectives
14122319.value: Objective 1 i) We have screened a panel of lysine-reactive modifications to identify the one with best conjugation efficiency and specificity. The chosen reactive groups were aryl-sulfonyl fluoride (X1), 4-nitrophenyl (X2), 1-fluoro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (FDNB) (X3), 4-fluorophenyl (X4), and phenyl (X5) groups. Among these, aryl-sulfonyl fluoride was found to conjugate to SRPK1 most effectively and was chosen for the rest of the study. ii) In addition to E9, we have installed our reactive groups near the N-terminal region of DBS1 at E2 and near the C-terminal region at E15, respectively, to test which position will allow more effective conjugation. Our results revealed that the conjugation efficiency did not change no matter where the reactive group was installed, therefore we continued to install it at E9 for the rest of the study. iii) Since the installation of an aryl-sulfonyl fluoride has already significantly improved the IC50 value of DBS1 from 11 micromolar to 640 nanomolar, we did not perform the SPOT array and one-bead-one-compound library to further optimize the sequence of DBS1 as proposed. Instead, we tested if changing the length of the modified side chain at position 9 would affect the conjugation efficiency and inhibitory activity. We replaced the lysine side chain at position 9 with lysine analogs diaminobutyric acid (Dab) and diaminopropionic acid (Dap), respectively. We found that the latter modification improved the IC50 of the DBS1 derivative to 142 nM, a 75-fold improvement over that of DBS-1, and an apparent Kd of 402nM prior to the covalent interaction. Given the significant improvement, this derivative was selected for the rest of the study and hereafter refer to as covalent docking blocker of SRPK (C-DBS). iv) We have performed MALDI-TOF/TOF analysis to identify that K604 is the site of conjugation. Site-mutagenesis followed by conjugation assays were performed to confirm the finding. In addition, we have shown that C-DBS specifically conjugated to recombinant SRPK1 in the presence of HeLa cell lysate, or endogenous SRPK1 in MDA-MB-231 lysate. v) We have also investigated the cell penetrating ability of C-DBS and proved that it was readily internalized by human non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) A549 cells and it was not trapped in endolysosomal compartments after internalization. vi) C-DBS was stabilized by N-acetylation and C-amidation modifications and because it showed potent inhibitory activity in cell culture (see results in Objective 2), we speculated that it remained stable at least under our experimental conditions. Its stability is being improved further and studied in our follow-up RGC project. vii) As stated in the mid-term report, soaking experiments using SRPK1deltaNS1 crystals with DBS1 or C-DBS failed to yield complex crystals. Extensive attempts to co-crystallize the kinase in complex with the inhibitor also failed to yield diffractable crystals. To gain insights into the molecular mechanism of interaction between the kinase and inhibitor, we have performed structure prediction using AlphaFold 3 using SRPK1deltaNS1 structure (PDB ID: 1WAK) and the sequence of DBS1. The prediction result showed that DBS1 may adopt a partial helical structure and dock into the docking groove of SRPK1. Detailed analysis of the model will be performed to further optimize the inhibitor in our follow-up RGC project. Objective 2. i) We have performed fluorescence polarization (FP) assay to determine the apparent dissociation constant Kd of C-DBS and SRPK1 to be 402nM. ii) We have performed MTT assays to assess the cytotoxic effects of C-DBS on A549, MDA-MB-231, HeLa, and HEK-293 cells. Our results showed that C-DBS is non-cytotoxic to these cell lines up to 100 micromolar. iii) We showed that C-DBS could inhibit the phosphorylation of SR proteins in A549 and MDA-MB-231 cells. C-DBS also inhibited angiogenesis in our tube formation assays using culture medium collected from C-DBS-treated A549 and MDA-MB-231 cells. Objective 3. i) We have shown that C-DBS inhibited the migration and invasion of A549 and MDA-MB-231 cells using transwell assays with or without Matrigel. ii) We have shown that C-DBS altered the expression of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) markers in A549 and MDA-MB-231 cells after treatment, indicating that C-DBS has potential to inhibit metastasis. iii) Roles of the splicing of Ron and MAP4K during SRPK1 inhibition have been studied. Preliminary results showed that treatment of A549 cells resulted in lower expression of both Ron and deltaRon, albeit a higher Ron:deltaRon ratio. This suggested that inhibition of SRPK1 might not only alter the splicing of Ron but its overall expression. The mechanism behind the observation is being investigated. On the other hand, we did not observe any changes of MAP4K4 splicing in A549 cells. We speculated that the lack of changes might be caused by the difference in cell lines being used in our studies and the previously published work. Such cell line/tissue type-dependent effects of SRPK inhibition have been observed in our other studies where knockout or knockdown of SRPK2 could lead to opposite effects on cancer cell invasion when different cancer cell types were used. These results will be reported elsewhere. Nonetheless, we have successfully confirmed that C-DBS can inhibit metastasis in the NSCLC A549 cells and triple-negative breast cancer MDA-MB-231 cells.

14122319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14122319.value: Serine–arginine (SR) proteins are splicing factors that play essential roles in both constitutive and alternative pre-mRNA splicing. Phosphorylation of their C-terminal RS domains by SR protein kinases (SRPKs) regulates their localization and diverse cellular activities. Dysregulation of phosphorylation has been implicated in many human diseases, including cancers. In this project, we report the development of a covalent protein–protein interaction inhibitor, C-DBS, that targets a lysine residue within the SRPK-specific docking groove to block the interaction and phosphorylation of the prototypic SR protein SRSF1. We show that C-DBS exhibited high specificity and conjugation efficiency both in vitro and in cellulo. It possesses self-cell-penetrating ability and it attenuates the phosphorylation of endogenous SR proteins and subsequently inhibits the angiogenesis, migration, and invasion of cells from two different cancer cell lines. These findings provide a new foundation for the development of covalent SRPK inhibitors for combatting diseases such as cancer and viral infections and overcoming the resistance encountered by ATP-competitive inhibitors. Both the original inhibitor DBS1, which requires optimization, and the newly developed covalent inhibitor C-DBS have been reported in two manuscripts that are published in the journals iScience and Communications Chemistry, respectively. In addition, a US provisional patent application on the development of C-DBS has been filed.

14122319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14122319.value: We have recently received another GRF grant to continue our investigation of the effects of C-DBS on cancer cell growth and proliferation, apoptosis, cancer stem cell-like phenotype, as well as its effects on the drug responsiveness of cancer cells toward chemotherapeutics like cisplatin. In addition, we will investigate how inhibition of SRPKs by C-DBS affect global pre-mRNA splicing in cancer cells. Finally, we will investigate the effects of C-DBS in vivo using mouse tumor model. We are confident that C-DBS could be further developed into a drug-like inhibitor for testing under clinical settings.

14122319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14122319.value: SRPKs are one of the major kinase families that regulate pre-mRNA splicing, an important cellular event that governs cell fate. Dysregulated expression of the SRPKs has been implicated in various diseases including cancer, making them promising therapeutical targets. To combat diseases caused by dysregulation of SRPKs, our lab has designed a protein-protein interaction peptide inhibitor DBS1, which specifically blocks a substrate-binding site in SRPK1 or SRPK2 to inhibit their functions in splicing. We have also shown that DBS1 inhibits angiogenesis, a blood vessels forming event that promote cancers. However, the inhibitory activity of DBS1 is only moderate and warrant further optimization and development. In this project, we successfully performed the structure-based modification of DBS1 into a covalent inhibitor C-DBS by the installation of a chemical warhead. We provided evidence that C-DBS was covalently bound to SRPK1. We also showed that C-DBS could enter cells without any aids and effectively inhibited the angiogenesis, migration, and invasion of lung and breast cancer cells. Our work demonstrates that SRPK1 is a druggable target and our new inhibitor has great potential to be further developed into a lead and eventually a drug to combat cancers.

14200319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200319.value: While the research on robotic manipulation of rigid objects has been well established, the robot's ability of manipulating deformable objects is less explored. Most deformable objects, especially the deformable linear objects (DLOs, e.g. wires, cables, ropes), are very common in manufacturing, food industry, and household service, and the progress on robotic manipulation of DLOs can benefit those application domains. However, it is very challenging for the robot to manipulate DLOs, because i) the DLO exhibits high degrees of freedom (DOFs), ii) the deformation model of DLO is usually unknown, and iii) unforeseen changes (e.g. falling) may arise during the manipulation. This project aims to systematically address the aforementioned open issues and lay a theoretical foundation for understanding the problems of robotic manipulation of DLOs. In particular, this project is devoted to controlling the overall shape of the DLO and planning the movement/task of its end tip. The need of shape control and task planning is reflected in many specific scenarios involving DLOs. For example, in interior renovation, the electric cables are installed along the edge of walls (shape control) then inserted into a designated socket (task planning). In 3C manufacturing, the USB wires are sorted such that the alignment follows the color code (task planning). The shape controller is proposed to manipulate multiple feature points along the DLO and keep them inside a series of dynamic regions, and the regions are scaled down sequentially to drive the features to the reference positions of a desired shape. The task planner is proposed to generate the desired trajectory for the robot end effector which grasps the end tip of DLO, and the trajectory is optimized offline according to the initial status of DLO and also adjusted online subject to the real-time changes. The proposed methods guarantee the feasibility of shape control and resolve the problems associated with the high DOFs of DLO (e.g. conflicts between multiple features). It also eliminates the requirement of prior calibration or identification by estimating the unknown deformation model of DLO with adaptive techniques. Moreover, it allows the robot to assess both the initial and the real-time status of DLO then act intelligently to deal with both existing issues (e.g. entanglement) and unforeseen changes (e.g. falling). Hence, the research output in this project can significantly improve the autonomous capability of robots handling DLOs and provides a general solution to the manipulation of various DLOs in different scenarios. 14200719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14200719.value: Automatic answering natural language queries or questions issued by users can facilitate the development of a wide range of intelligent applications. This demand drives a great deal of research effort in the area of question answering (QA). We intend to investigate a practical setting in which there exists a large collection of text documents. The aim is to infer and find the answer from the document collection given a question issued by the user. One related area is factoid question answering where answers are assumed to be simple facts or entities. One previous approach is to employ information retrieval techniques treating the question as a query for searching passages and extracting answers. Another family of methods extract shallow knowledge from texts and consider aggregate statistics of answer candidates. However the above approaches cannot handle effectively complex questions or non-factoid questions. A popular related task known as Reading Comprehension (RC) has drawn a lot of research attention recently. However, RC methods focus on factoid questions with entity-type answers. Also, they have limitations when dealing with complex questions. This problem becomes more serious when there is vocabulary mismatch. Some QA tasks focus on chatbots and community QA setting (CQA). Both tasks mainly utilize a large collection of question answer pairs as the information source. Consequently most of the existing chatbots and CQA methods ignore or cannot effectively analyze a collection of text documents, if available, and conduct reasoning on text passages for answer finding. We propose a new framework for answering complex natural language queries and questions capable of conducting reasoning and integrating evidence derived across multiple text snippets or passages from different documents. We intend to employ and extend the latest semantic representation and understanding technique for handling texts in questions and sentences in the document collection. Our framework conducts question semantic analysis which understands and decomposes the question into smaller appropriate units of sub-questions and semantic units. Then question-relevant text snippets or passages from multiple documents are retrieved from which a set of semantic graphs are constructed for capturing the semantic content of sentences in snippets. A new approach is proposed for reasoning and graph matching considering evidence derived across multiple sources with the aim of inferring the appropriate intermediate and final answers. Furthermore, we intend to apply our proposed framework to e-commerce. We consider some characteristics of e-commerce and refine our framework for building an intelligent e-commerce product QA system. 自動回答用戶發出的自然語言査詢或問題，可以促進各種智能應用的發展。這一需求推動了問答領域的大量研究工作。我們打算研究一個實際場景，其中存在大量的文檔集合。目的是根據用戶提出的問題，從文檔集合中推斷並找到答案。一個相關的研究領域是事實型問答，其中答案被假定為簡單的事實或實體，一類現有的方法是使用信息檢索技術，將問題視為檢索段落和選取答案的査詢，而另一類方法是從文本中提取淺層的知識，並考慮候選答案的整體統計信息。然而，上述方法不能有效地處理複雜問題或非事實型問題。閱讀理解（Reading Comprehension）是近年來備受關注的一項相關課題。然而，閱讀理解方法關注的是具有實體類型答案的事實問題。另外，這類方法在處理複雜問題時也有局限性，並且當詞彙不匹配時，這個問題會變得更加嚴重。一些問答任務側重於聊天機器人和社區問答（Community Question Answering），這兩項任務主要利用大量的問答對作為信息源。因此，大多數現有的聊天機器人和社區問答方法在存在大量文檔集合的情況下不能有效地對文檔進行分析，並對文本段落進行推理以找到答案。 我們提出了一個新的框架，用於回答複雜的自然語言査詢和問題，並能够綜合從不同文檔的多個文字片段或段落中獲得的證據進行推理。我們打算採用和擴展最新的語義表示和理解技術來處理問題與文檔中的文本。我們的框架先對問題進行語義分析，將問題理解並分解為更細緻且恰當的子問題和語義單元。然後，從多個文檔中檢索與問題相關的文字片段或段落，從中構建語義圖，用於捕獲片段中句子的語義內容。並提出一種新的推理和圖匹配方法，考慮了從多個來源獲得的證據，從而推斷出合適的中間答案和最終答案。另外，我們打算將我們提出的框架應用於電子商務。我們考慮了電子商務的一些特點，針對構建智能電子商務問答系統完善了我們的框架。

14200719.label: Realisation of objectives
14200719.value: We have successfully achieved all project objectives. The details are given below. For the first objective, we have developed a new framework for answering complex natural language questions capable of conducting reasoning. Our framework is able to integrate multiple evidence across documents. It attempts to conduct reasoning on text snippets retrieved from different text sources and documents. Question semantic analysis is conducted for understanding and decomposing the question content into smaller semantic units. We consider the heterogeneous nature of the collection of text information. It includes natural language text in the source documents, natural language feedback texts from the user, as well as text-based domain attribute information. We select fashion domain as a sample context. Fashion product attributes are exploited. We also investigate the sequential nature of text information commonly found in conversational information seeking agents, which exhibits multiple turns of information exchange between the user and the system. This capability is suitable in the setting of e-commerce product question answering (QA). For the second objectives, we investigate question semantic analysis and the modeling of reasoning chain. We develop a new approach for performing explainable reasoning without the need of corpus-specific annotations such as human-annotated entity mentions. Our approach also supports reasoning based on evidence derived across multiple text passages. Our proposed framework first generates reasoning chains from a semantic graph constructed by Abstract Meaning Representation of retrieved evidence facts. A chain-aware loss concerning both local and global chain information is also designed to enable the generated chains to serve as distant supervision signals for training the retriever. Extensive experiments have been conducted on some benchmark datasets. We extend our framework to tackling the problem of aspect-based sentiment analysis for question answering (QA) forums. We attempt to jointly detect the discussed aspects and their sentiment polarities for a given QA pair. Unlike review sentences, a QA pair is composed of two parallel sentences, which requires interaction modeling to align the aspect mentioned in the question and the associated opinion clues in the answer. To this end, we propose a model with a specific design of cross-sentence aspect-opinion interaction modeling to address this task. The proposed method is evaluated on three real-world datasets and the results show that our model outperforms several strong baselines adopted from related state-of-the-art models. Furthermore, we investigate pre-trained language models for natural language understanding. Question answering and named entity recognition are some tasks under natural language understanding and these tasks are useful for conducting reasoning spanning multiple text passages. For the last objective of this funding, namely, building an intelligent e-commerce product QA considering characteristics of e-commerce settings. One characteristic of QAs in e-commerce settings is that there are many non-factoid questions. Document summarization methods have been adopted as an effective way to summarize salient information, which can then be adopted to provide a concise answer for the given question. Based on this idea, we investigate non-factoid QA problem as a query-focused summarization problem. Our framework leverages graph-enhanced reasoning techniques to tackle multihop inference. If the text content involves spatial information, we investigate a new method for spatial reasoning using graph neural networks. We design a novel node memory scheme and aggregate information over the depth dimension. This enables handling long dependencies.

14200719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14200719.value: Automatic answering natural language queries or questions issued by users can facilitate the development of a wide range of intelligent applications. This demand drives a great deal of research effort in the area of question answering (QA). We intend to investigate a practical setting in which there exists a large collection of text documents in a particular vertical professional domain. The aim is to infer and find the answer from the document collection given a question issued by the user. Existing approaches cannot handle effectively complex questions or non-factoid questions. We propose a new framework for answering complex natural language queries and questions capable of conducting reasoning and integrating evidence derived across multiple text snippets or passages from different documents. We intend to employ and extend the latest semantic representation and understanding technique for handling texts in questions and sentences in the document collection. A new approach is proposed for reasoning and graph matching considering evidence derived across multiple sources with the aim of inferring the appropriate intermediate and final answers. Furthermore, we apply our proposed framework to building an intelligent e-commerce application.

14201819.label: Project Objectives
14201819.value: Generalization of flow availabilities estimation via importance sampling and online learning techniques. In particular, we will extend our current preliminary result of estimating a single flow availability to a more practical scenario of estimating many flow availabilities. This research will provide a new simulation paradigm which can help network operators to quickly and efficiently carrying out capacity/sales planning. Generalization For the ``partial state information'' so that network operators do not need to have full information about the set of links which may cause the flows unavailabilities. This will further expand the usefulness of our methodology to practical network scenarios. We propose to use multi-armed bandit (MAB) framework or distributed weighting adjust algorithm to dynamically explore the solution space. The long term impact of this research endeavor is not only in providing the fundamental understanding on how to quickly and accurately estimate flow availabilities, but we also aim to apply our mathematical results, algorithms and parallel simulator to some the multimedia Internet services. We refer reviewers to the attachment of the supporting letters from our research partners.

14201819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14201819.value: 這研究提案側重於通過回答以下問題幫助網絡提供商執行網絡和銷售計劃：給定網絡配置，它能滿足當前的流量需求嗎？ 特別是，我們定義了“流量可用性”的概念，它是底層網絡滿足流量服務質量（QoS）要求的概率。 我們制定了流量可用性估計（Flow-AE）問題，並表明Flow-AE實際上是一些傳統網絡問題的“概括”，如網絡連接估計問題或網絡最大流量可靠性問題。 對於大型和現實的網絡，流量可用性估計通常無法通過分析進行評估，因此通常使用模擬。然而，諸如基於蒙特卡羅（MC）的模擬技術或甚至標準重要性採樣（IS）技術的傳統方法花費了過多的時間。在這項研究中，我們提出了一種系統的方法來解決上述挑戰。我們首先建議使用增強版的重要性抽樣技術來快速準確地估算流量可用性。我們提出的方法可以實現幾個有吸引力的特性，特別是它可以實現有界甚至消失的相對誤差（即，可用性估計器的方差將接近零）並且同時它具有線性計算複雜度。使用我們的方法，網絡運營商可以以更低的仿真成本快速估算流量可用性。其次，在應用我們的增強型重要性抽樣技術時，如何動態調整反映不同網絡拓撲重要性的權重是一個基本問題。最佳地設置這些權重並且我們建議使用在線學習技術（例如，多臂強盜方法）來有效地選擇加權值以使得我們的結果與最優離線算法相比具有近似常數是非常重要的。 本研究考慮了新型和新型仿真範例的數學分析和算法設計，以便快速估算大型網絡的流量可用性，最終結果是網絡運營商可以快速準確地執行容量和銷售計劃。

14201819.label: Realisation of objectives
14201819.value: We believe we have completed this project with our stated objectives. That is: - We provide a generalization of flow availabilities estimation, in particular, using our new methodology proposed of using "importance sampling" and "online learning" techniques. This is particularly important when there are many flows available in a large scale network. This will help network operators to efficient perform capacity planning and sales planning. To this end, the flow estimation, which was a computationally expensive procedure, can now be down with computationally efficient algorithms and more importantly, can be carried out in real-time. This significant improve the network operating cost and network capacity planning operation. That is the main reason why our proposed method is so valuable to network operators. - We also extended and generalized our methodology to allow operators to only need "partial state information". This is particularly importantly since it expands the scalability of our methodology, and allows practical implementation and operation for network management. In particular, we used this multi-armed bandit techniques to allow "partial information feedbacks" so as to make sure one can apply our methodology in practical scenarios. Previous, network operators had to collect a lot of information so as to carry out capacity planning, but using our approach, one only needs to collect partial information, this reduces the data collection costs and computational cost, and this is the main reason why using our approach, the network operators can carry out network capacity more often. - The proposed methodology is being cited and used in some networking companies, and some companies are enhancing their network planning software using our methodology. We believe that by introducing this new method and that the method is being applied to real life is an important societal contribution.

14201819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14201819.value: The major findings of this research project is that to estimate flows in a large scale networks, one can use "importance sampling" techniques to handle the large amount of traffic so that one can carry out accurate statistical estimations of traffics. This will allow operators to perform future network planning and capacity planning of the network. We also introduced the concept of using multi-armed bandits to carry out online and computationally efficient method to calculate the "weights" on different flows so as to estimate whether a given network topology can provide the promised quality of service guarantees.

14201819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14201819.value: The mathematical theory developed in this project is really elegant. It is important to understand the mathematics and algorithms develop in this project, and then translate them into running software so that operators can use the capacity planning tools. Currently, some companies are in the process of "porting" our algorithms and theories into their network management tools. One interest idea is whether one should apply, say ITF, to carry out this software development and do software licensing.

14201819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14201819.value: The main objective of this project is to develop a new theory and the associated algorithms to carry out network capacity planning and network management. Networking capacity planning is a tedious and computationally expensive task because one needs to have accurate estimate of all traffic flows in the network. However, due to the large volume of traffic, this is computationally expensive. In this project, we first proposed using "importance sampling technique" to reduce the traffic estimate cost. To map the traffic estimate and how to do network capacity planning, we propose to use an online learning framework so to have a computationally efficient approach to check whether the current network topology can provide the promised quality of service guarantees. In association of this projects, we also develop various online learning algorithms for various network and higher layer applications.

14202219.value: 用於加強零件機械性能的多軸3D打印路徑規劃

14202219.label: Project Objectives
14202219.value: Investigation of anisotropy in filament-based AM: Computational analysis will be conducted to analyze the distribution of principal stresses and how anisotropy influences the corresponding strain distribution. Specimens with simple shapes will be fabricated by planar-layer based FDM, and the anisotropy will be studied on these specimens to derive the criteria for tool-path generation. Field-governed working surface generation: A field-governed algorithm will be developed to decompose a solid model into working surfaces that can be collision-freely accessed by a multi-axis AM system. The decomposition of working surfaces should be optimized according to the stress distribution inside a model. Tool-path generation on surface: A scalar-field will be computed on each working surface according to the criteria for seeking an optimized alignment of filaments. Optimized tool-paths, which can be applied to strengthen 3D printed models, are then generated from the scalar-field.

14202219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202219.value: 3D printing is a process of joining materials to make objects directly from 3D digital models. Filament-based fuse deposition modeling (FDM) is the most widely adopted 3D printing process as it can fabricate much more types of materials than other 3D printing technologies. In the current practice of 3D printing, materials are usually accumulated layer upon layer in planes along a fixed direction so that is also called layered manufacturing. Converting 3D problem into 2D tool-path planning in sliced planes significantly simplifies the algorithms for process planning. When applying this simplification to FDM, the weak adhesion between neighboring planar-layers of filaments always leads to an easy-to-delaminate problem. The anisotropy of mechanical property – strong along the axial directions of filaments but weak in other directions – can be observed on all models fabricated by FDM. Different from planar-layer based fabrication, the anisotropy of mechanical property on a 3D printed model can be controlled in a multi-axis 3D printing system as materials can be accumulated along dynamically varied directions. The purpose of this research is to investigate a new computational framework to generate specially designed tool-paths of multi-axis 3D printing for strengthening a model by aligning filaments along the directions with large tension. Computing multi-axis tool-paths for strengthening 3D printed models is challenging. Although existing techniques are conceptually able to perform multi-axis 3D printing on a given surface, the tool-path generation problem to be solved in this project is in a larger design space – i.e., the volume of an input model. While increasing the dimension from surface to volume, the complexity of computation increases and therefore innovative planning algorithms with better efficiency and scalability need to be invented. Specifically, we will generate multi-axis FDM tool-paths along the directions with large tension so that the anisotropy of fused filaments can be well used to strengthen 3D printed models. This challenge will be tackled by 1) studying the principle to optimize the directions of filaments for strengthening, 2) investigating the methodology to effectively decompose a solid into a sequence of strength-aware and collision-free working surfaces, and 3) investigating the methodology to generate continuous and direction-enforced tool-paths for covering a working surface. Field-based new algorithms will be developed to tackle these problems. A hardware platform with multi-axis motion will be employed to conduct physical fabrication for verifying the effectiveness of tool-paths generated by these new algorithms. 3D打印是一種通過堆積材料以直接從3D數字模型制作物體的過程。基於打印絲的熔絲沉積建模（FDM）是目前最廣泛採用的3D打印工藝，因爲它可以製造比其他3D打印技術更多類型的材料。在目前的3D打印實踐中，材料通常沿著固定方向逐層平面堆積，因此也稱爲分層制造。在切片平面中將3D問題轉換爲2D工具路徑規劃可顯著簡化工藝規劃的算法。當將這種簡化應用於FDM時，相鄰的長絲平面層之間的弱粘附性總是導致層與層之間易於撕裂的問題。在FDM制造的所有模型上都可以觀察到機械性能的各向異性 - 沿著熔絲的軸向強但在其他方向上很弱。 與基於平面層的制造不同，3D打印模型上的機械性能各向異性可以在多軸3D打印系統中控制，因爲材料可以沿動態變化的方向堆積。這項研究的目的是研究一種新的計算框架，以生成專門設計的多軸3D打印工具路徑，通過沿著大應力方向擺放打印熔絲來加強模型的機械強度。 計算用於加強3D打印模型的多軸加工路徑具有挑戰性。儘管現有技術在概念上能夠在給定表面上執行多軸3D打印，但是在該項目中要解決的工具路徑生成問題存在於更大的設計空間 - 即輸入模型的體積。在從表面到體積增加幾何維度的同時，計算的複雜性也顯著增加，因此需要發明具有更高效率和可擴展性的新型路徑規劃算法。具體來說，我們將沿著具有大應力方向來生成多軸FDM加工路徑，以便熔絲的各向異性可以很好地用於加強3D打印模型。這一挑戰將通過以下方法解決：1）研究優化熔絲加強方向的原理，2）研究將固體有效分解爲強化機械性能和無碰撞工作表面序列的方法，以及3）研究生成用於覆蓋工作表面的連續且方向控制加工路徑生成方法。我們將開發基於場計算的新算法來解決這些問題。將採用具有多軸運動的硬件平台來進行3D打印製造，以驗證由這些新算法産生的多軸加工路徑的有效性。

14202219.label: Realisation of objectives
14202219.value: 1. Investigation of anisotropy in filament-based AM Computational analysis has been conducted to analyse the anisotropy of 3D printed models by both empirical tests and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) based simulation. Specifically, the Conjecture 1.1 and the Conjecture 1.2 discussed in the proposal have been verified to be correct through these studies. We further verified that delamination caused by the weak adhesion of materials between neighbouring filaments is the major source of fracture on 3D printed models. The results were published in a book chapter [J1 in Part C8] and a paper in ACM Transactions on Graphics (SIGGRAPH Asia 2020) [J3 in Part C8 and #2 in Part C9]. 2. Field-governed working surface generation A field-governed algorithm has been developed to decompose a solid model into working surfaces that can collision-freely accessed by a multi-axis AM system. Specifically, we introduced a field-based optimization framework to generate curved layers so that the anisotropy of fused filaments can be well controlled in multi-axis 3D printing to reinforce the mechanical strength of 3D printed models. When optimizing the field for layer decomposition, we enabled the collision-free printing by 1) selecting a ‘best’ setup orientation and 2) updating the field in the regions with collision. Moreover, we extrapolated the optimized field to generate curved layers of supporting structures for enabling the fabrication of large overhang in multi-axis 3D printing. This new algorithm has been published in the paper of ACM Transactions on Graphics (the paper was also presented in SIGGRAPH Asia 2020 conference). 3. Tool-path generation on surface With the help a vector-field as the intermedia of computation, a scalar-field can be computed on each working surface according to the criteria for seeking an optimized alignment of filaments. Optimized tool-paths, which can be applied to strengthen 3D printed models, were then generated from the scalar-field as isocurves, which were later merged with the isocurves generated from a boundary distance field. As a result, the hybrid tool-path can be generated on each curved working surface. The toolpath generation for continuous fibre reinforced thermoplastic composites and distortion reduction in laser power bed fusion process were published in the papers published in the journal Additive Manufacturing [J6 and J8 in Part C8].

14202219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202219.value: We presented a method [J1 in Part C8] for effectively planning the motion trajectory of robots in manufacturing tasks, the tool paths of which were usually complex and have a large number of discrete time constraints as waypoints. The jerk of motion was optimized in our trajectory planning method at the meanwhile of fabrication process to improve the quality of fabrication. Multi-directional 3D printing has the capability of decreasing or eliminating the need for support structures. To obtain optimized decomposition, a large beam width was used in the search algorithm, leading to a very time-consuming computation. We proposed [J2] a learning framework that can accelerate the beam-guided search by using a smaller number of the original beam width to obtain results with similar quality. The anisotropy of mechanical strength on a 3D printed model can be controlled in a multi-axis 3D printing system as materials can be accumulated along dynamically varied directions. We presented a new computational framework [J3] to generate specially designed layers and toolpaths of multi-axis 3D printing for strengthening a model by aligning filaments along the directions with large stresses. Additive manufacturing has been adopted to process nickel‑titanium shape memory alloys due to its advantages of flexibility and minimal defects. The spatial characterization of nickel‑titanium shape memory alloy fabricated by continuous directed energy deposition was investigated [J4]. We presented a field-based method of toolpath generation for 3D printing continuous fibre reinforced thermoplastic composites [J6]. Our method employed the strong anisotropic material property of continuous fibres by generating toolpaths along the directions of tensile stresses in the critical regions. The performance of our method has been verified on a variety of models in different loading conditions. Direct metal deposition (DMD) process has been regarded as a promising additive manufacturing technology. The multi-axis DMD process with an improved regrouping strategy was developed [J7]. A novel sequence planning algorithm was proposed by minimizing the cost function to avoid excessively accumulated temperature fields. Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) is one of the most commonly used metal additive manufacturing technologies. We proposed novel adaptive toolpath generation algorithms [J8] based on minimizing thermal gradients so that can reduce the part distortion. The objective function of temperature fields was determined by numerical simulation both considering time and distance. Two constraints including collision-free and smoothing constraints were also incorporated during the toolpath patterns generation process. Experiments were conducted to validate the proposed algorithms.

14202219.value: Significant results (8 journal papers, 1 book chapter, and 3 conference papers) have been obtained from this completed project. Two PhD students were trained with their theses: Shiming Gao, “Fabrication of NiTi Shape Memory Alloy Using Directed Energy Deposition with Assistant Strategies,” Ph.D. Thesis, July 2021. (Co-Supervised with Prof. P. Guo, Northwestern University, USA); Mian Qin, “Toolpath Generation and Optimization for Metal Additive Manufacturing,” Ph.D. Thesis, July 2022. For the further development, it would be beneficial to develop adaptive 3D printing technology, aim at enabling the adaptive structure design, manufacturing with adaptive toolpath patterns, data-drive modeling and AI-based toolpath optimization for 3D printing, which further extends the functionality of 3D printed objects by providing extra dimensions - the functionally graded adaptive structure design, novel toolpath generation framework, computationally feasible modeling and optimization methods, and applications with smart functions.

14202219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202219.value: The effectiveness of toolpaths generated by this project has been verified on the multi-axis AM (additive manufacturing, or 3D printing) hardware realized by a robotic arm. Moreover, we have also physically tested the effectiveness of toolpaths on a multi-axis AM machine that was modified from a 5-axis CNC table tilting machine. The results have been published as the supplementary video of the ACM Transactions on Graphics paper, which was also publicly accessible from YouTube at: https://youtu.be/X2o2-SJFv2M. When using the same material, models fabricated by using our multi-axis 3D printing method can withstand up to 6.35x loads in experimental tests. A motion planning method for optimizing the kinematic realization has been developed to execute the multi-axis tool-paths for material accumulation. As a by-product, we have developed a machine-learning based method to find an optimized sequence of plane-clipping, which gave volume decomposition of a given 3D model. Different printing directions were employed in different regions to fabricate a model with tremendously less support (or even no support in many cases).
