14202619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202619.value: The cooperative output regulation problem aims to design a distributed control law to make the outputs of all followers asymptotically track a class of reference signals generated by a so-called leader system in the presence of a class of disturbances. The problem is a generalization of the classical output regulation problem from a single plant to a multi-agent system, and it contains the leader-following consensus problem and / or the synchronization problem as special cases because it can not only achieve state consensus but also output consensus, it allows all subsystems of the multi-agent system to have different dynamics, and it handles both tracking and disturbance rejection. The cooperative output regulation problem for multi-agent systems was first formulated in 2012 by PI and his student, and was solved first by a so-called distributed observer approach and later by adaptive distributed observer approach in 2016. It turns out that this problem is very effective in dealing with many practical cooperative control problems such as the coordination of multiple mobile robots, attitude synchronization of multiple rigid-body systems, position formation of multiple quadrotor helicopters. Moreover, the techniques of the cooperative output regulation problem also apply to some other cooperative control problems such as formation, rendezvous, and flocking. However, the communication networks of most complex multi-agents systems only permit intermittent information transmission, and most continuous-time control laws have to be implemented in digital platforms. The most common method for digitally implementing a continuous-time control law is by periodically sampling continuous-time signals and zero-order holding the sampled signals within each period. Nevertheless, since the action of the sampling and zero-order hold incurs time delay, which in turn causes performance degradation or even instability of the closed-loop system, it is important to study how to select the appropriate sample period to guarantee the stability and the performance of the closed-loop system. In this project, we will establish a framework for solving the cooperative output regulation problem for multi-agent systems by a sampled-data distributed control law. We will first develop a sampled-data distributed observer for a leader system, then solve the problem by a sampled-data decentralized control law, and, finally, synthesize a sampled-data distributed control law based on the sampled-data distributed observer and the sampled-data decentralized control law. Additionally, we will apply our result to such problems as the formation of multiple mobile robots, attitude synchronization of multiple rigid-body systems, and position formation of multiple quadrotor helicopters. 協同控制問題的目的在於設計分佈式控制律使所有的跟隨者的輸出信號在一類擾動存在的情況下漸進地跟踪由所謂領導者生成的一類參考信號。此問題可视之为經典單一系統的輸出調節問題到多智能體系統的推廣。由於該問題不僅要實現狀態一致，而且要實現輸出一致，允許多智能體系統的所有子系統具有不同的動力學模型，並且能夠同时處理跟踪和擾動抑制， 因此該問題包括了領導者-跟隨者的一致性問題和/或同步問題作為特殊情況。 多智能體協作式輸出調節問題最初是由PI和他的學生於2012年構思而出，並且通過所謂分佈式觀測器方法解決，之後在2016年 通過自適應分佈式觀測器方法解決的。事實證明這個問題能夠有效地解決如多個移動機器人的協作、多剛體系統的姿態同步、多個四旋翼直升機的位置編隊等諸多實 際的協作式控制問題。此外，協作式輸出調節問題的技術也適用於其他一些協同控制問題，如編隊、交會對接和集群。然而，大多數的複雜多智能體系統的通信網絡 只允許間歇性的信息傳輸，並且大多數的連續時間控制律必須要在數字平台實現。數字化地實現連續時間控制律最常用的方法是通過週期性地對連續時間信號進行採 樣，並在每個週期內對採樣信號進行零階保持。然而，由於採樣和零階保持會產生時間延遲，從而導致閉環系統的性能下降甚至不穩定，因此研究如何選擇適當的採 樣週期以確保閉環系統的穩定性和性能是至关重要的。本項目將建立一個通過採樣數據分佈式控制律來解決多智能體系統協作式輸出調節問題的框架。 我們將首先為領導者係統設計一個採樣數據分佈式觀測器，然後通過採樣數據分散式控制律解決問題，最後根據採樣數據分佈式觀測器和採樣數據分散式控制律來合 成採樣數據分佈式控制律。此外，我們將把我們的結果應用於诸如多個移動機器人編隊、多剛體系統的姿態同步及多個四旋翼直升機的位置編隊等問題中。

14202619.label: Realisation of objectives
14202619.value: This project aims to achieve the following three objectives: 1. Develop a sampled-data distributed observer for a leader system. 2. Study the output regulation problem for a multi-agent system by a sampled-data decentralized control law that guarantees the stability and performance of the closed-loop system. 3. Synthesize a sampled-data distributed control law based on the certainty equivalence principle. All three objectives are fully accomplished. The research has led to 6 journal papers and two conference papers. The six journal papers include two papers in Automatica and one paper in IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics, both journals are among the top journals of the control field. Details of the research outcomes can be found in Section 6.1. Two Phd students Changran He and Xiongnan He have been trained through conducting this project. The project has led to collaboration with Prof. Wei Liu of South China University of Technology. Prof. Liu and PI have jointly published two journal papers and one conference paper supported by this project. The PI has been invited to deliver plenary speeches in three conferences under the support of this project.

14202619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202619.value: We have fully achieved all three objectives and the main findings are summarized as follows: 1. We have considered the cooperative output regulation problem for heterogeneous linear multiagent systems by the distributed sampled-data control approach. We classify the problem into two cases. The first case is that the state of the leader system is constant. For this case, we have shown that the cooperative output regulation problem is solvable exactly by a distributed sampled-data output feedback control law. The second case is that the state of the leader system is time-varying with bounded derivative. For this case, we have further shown that the problem is solvable practically by a distributed aperiodic asynchronous sampled data output feedback control law. These findings are reported in Journal Paper 1. 2. We have further extended our approach to solve sampled-data semi-global robust output regulation for a class of nonlinear systems. The main findings are summarized in Journal Paper 2. 3. We have further consolidated and validated the results by applying our approach to the leader-following consensus of multiple rigid body systems by a sampled-data distributed observer. The main findings are reported in Journal Paper 3. 4. We have further considered the event-triggered control. Like the sampled-data control, the event-triggered control is another way for implementing continuous-time control laws in digital platforms. However, unlike the sample-data control where the samplings and the control actions take place periodically, the event-triggered control generates the samplings and the control actions only when the system state or output deviates away from a prescribed set and thus it is more efficient in reducing the control execution times and saving energy resources while maintaining the desired. By establishing some new technical lemmas, and integrating the distributed internal model approach and the distributed hybrid observer approach, we recursively construct a distributed output-based event-triggered control law and a distributed output-based Zeno free event-triggered mechanism to solve our problem. The main findings are summarized in Conference Paper 1. 5. We have enlarged the scope of the objectives of this project from several directions as follows: a) Leader-following formation tracking for multiple quadrotor helicopters in Journal Paper 4. b) Distributed Nash equilibrium seeking in Journal Paper 5 and Conference Paper 2. c) Exponential estimation of the unknown frequencies of discrete-time multi-tone sinusoidal signals in Journal Paper 6.

14202619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202619.value: Two potential expansions of the project are summarized as follows: 1. In this project, we have established a sampled-data observer for a known leader system. It is more interesting and more practical to establish a sampled-data distributed observer for an unknown leader system. This generalization is under way. 2. This project has focused on establishing the sampled-data distributed observer. There is another way to deal with the cooperative output regulation problem called distributed internal model approach, which has the advantage of being able to deal with uncertain multi-agent systems. The extension of this project to sampled-data distributed internal model is on-going.

This problem applies to many practical cooperative control problems such as the coordination of multiple mobile robots, attitude synchronization of multiple rigid-body systems, formation of multiple quadrotor helicopters. By the beginning of this project, this problem had been thoroughly studied by the continuous-time distributed observer approach. 14202919.label: Project Objectives

14202919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14202919.value: In the big data era, machine learning techniques have been extensively studied to learn new things from a huge amount of data, instead of find new things by programming. Given the goal of machine learning is to learn from data, it becomes a natural question how machine learning and database system can be integrated tightly in the same platforms, instead of simply extracting massive data from a database system to conduct machine learning tasks every time when there is such a need, which is with high cost. We concentrate ourselves on supporting machine learning in the kernel of a database system. As observed by many researchers, there is a mismatch between machine learning and database system, regarding data handling. From the viewpoint of machine learning, a machine learning algorithm will take a matrix (or its relation representation) as an input to learn, which implies that it will be easier to keep everything in a single relation in a database. From the viewpoint of database system, data needs to be maintained in several relations in a database instead of managing everything in a single relation for the purpose of reducing information redundancy. Reducing information redundancy is an important issue in dealing with consistency since data will be updated from time to time. In addition, to maintain data in several relations will help to improve performance in general. When data is stored in several relations, it needs to join the relations to form a single relation for a machine learning algorithm to use, which incurs high computational cost. The key issue to be studied is how to reduce such cost. In this project, we focus on query processing techniques, and aim at enhancing query processing to efficiently support machine learning algorithms in a standalone/distributed database system. The academic significance of the project is of two folds. In addition to publications reporting the project finding, the methodology and techniques developed will be implemented to demonstrate the strength of our approach. 在大數據時代，機器學習技術已被廣泛研究用於從海量數據中學習新事物，而不是通過編寫程序找到新事物。鑒於機器學習的目標是從數據中學習，如何將機器學習技術和數據庫系統緊密集成在同壹平臺中是當下壹個自然的問題。這種集成區別於壹旦有執行機器學習任務的需求，就簡單地從數據庫系統中提取海量數據來執行， 而這壹過程會帶來較高計算開銷。我們專註於在數據庫系統的內核中支持機器學習。正如許多研究者的觀察，機器學習和數據庫系統之間在數據處理方面存在壹種不匹配。從機器學習的角度來看，機器學習算法將采用矩陣（或其關系表示）作為學習模型的輸入，這意味著將所有數據保存在數據庫中的單個關系中會更容易執行機器學習任務。從數據庫系統的角度來看，為了減少信息的冗余，在數據庫中，數據以若幹關系維護，而不是用單壹關系來管理所有內容。這是因為數據會不斷更新，而減少信息冗余是處理數據壹致性的壹個重要問題。此外，在幾個關系中維護數據將有助於提高整體性能。當數據存儲在幾個關系中時，它需要連接關系以形成單個關系供機器學習算法使用，這將導致高計算開銷。我們要研究的關鍵問題是如何降低這種開銷。在這個項目中，我們旨在以先進的查詢處理技術，在獨立/分布式數據庫系統中高效地支持機器學習算法。該項目的學術意義有兩個方面。除了發表展示項目成果的刊物，我們還將實現所研究的方法和技術，以驗證我們方法的優勢

14202919.label: Realisation of objectives
14202919.value: The two objectives of this project on support machine learning by query processing techniques are: to investigate new ways to support machine learning in the kernel of database systems, in order to make it possible to handle large datasets that need to be updated or used for general purposes, and to explore new ways to support machine learning with new query processing techniques. Machine learning (ML) plays a leading role in predictive and estimation tasks. It needs to fully explore how to build, utilize and manage ML models in RDBMSs for the following reasons. First, data are stored in a database system. It is time-consuming of exporting the data from the database system and then feeding it into models, as well as importing the prediction and estimation results back to the database system. Second, users need to build a model as to query data in RDBMSs, and query their data by exploiting the analysis result of the models trained as a part of a query seamlessly in RDBMSs. A flexible way is needed to train/query an ML model together with data querying by a high-level query language (e.g., SQL). Third, the data maintained in RDBMSs are supposed to change dynamically. The analysis result of the ML models trained may be outdated, which requires repeating the process of exporting data from RDBMSs followed by importing the model trained into RDBMSs. It needs to support ML model update automatically in RDBMSs. We study how to support ML by SQL. As an example, we focus on how to support Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithms which is a general technique for finding maximum likelihood estimators. We discuss how to represent data in RDBMSs, how to compute E-step and M-step of EM using relational algebra operations, how to update parameters using relational algebra operations, and how to support its while-loop using SQL recursive queries. Note that mutual recursion is needed for both E/M-step in EM, where the E-step is to compute the conditional posterior probability by Bayesian inference, which is a monotonic operation, whereas the M-step is to compute and update the parameters of the model given a closed-form updating formula, which can be non-monotonic. This fact suggests that SQL’99 recursion cannot be used to support EM, since SQL’99 recursion (e.g., recursive with) only supports stratified negation, and therefore cannot support non-monotonic operations. We adopt the enhanced SQL recursion (e.g., with+) we proposed/developed based on XY-stratified, to handle non-monotonic operations. We have implemented our approach on top of PostgreSQL and Spark SQL. We show how to train a batch of classical statistical models, including Gaussian Mixture model, Bernoulli Mixture model, the mixture of linear regression, Hidden Markov model, Mixtures of Experts. Given a model trained by EM, we further design an automatic in-database model maintenance mechanism to maintain the model when the underlying training data changes. Inspired by the online and incremental EM algorithms, we show how to obtain the sufficient statistics of the models to achieve the incremental even decremental model updating, rather than re-training the model by all data. Our setting is different from the incremental EM algorithms which are designed to accelerate the convergence of EM. We maintain the model dynamically by the sufficient statistics of partial original data in addition to the delta part. ML often require processing complex join queries in parallel in distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark, and Flink. The previous works consider that the main bottleneck of processing complex join queries is the communication cost incurred by shuffling of intermediate results, and propose a way to cut down such shuffling cost to zero by a one-round multi-way join algorithm. The one-round multi-way join algorithm is built on a one-round communication optimal algorithm for data shuffling over servers and a worst-case optimal computation algorithm for sequential join evaluation on each server. The previous works focus on optimizing the communication bottleneck, while neglecting the fact that the query could be computationally intensive. With the communication cost being well optimized, the computation cost may become a bottleneck. To reduce the computation bottleneck, a way is to trade computation with communication via pre-computing some partial results, but it can make communication or pre-computing becomes the bottleneck. With one of the three costs being considered at a time, the combined lowest cost may not be achieved. Thus the question left unanswered is how much should be traded such that the combined cost of computation, communication, and pre-computing is minimal. We study the problem of co-optimize communication, pre-computing, and computation cost in one-round multi-way join evaluation. We propose a multi-way join approach ADJ (Adaptive Distributed Join) for complex join which finds one optimal query plan to process by exploring cost-effective partial results in terms of the trade-off between pre-computing, communication, and computation. We analyze the input relations for a given join query and find one optimal over a set of query plans in some specific form, with high-quality cost estimation by sampling. Our extensive experiments confirm that ADJ outperforms the existing multi-way join methods by up to orders of magnitude. In addition, we study parallel query processing at the relational algebra level, instead of multi-way join algorithms which cannot be used with other relational algebra operators (e.g., projection, aggregation). We study parallel query processing with a focus on reducing the communication cost, which is the dominating factor in parallel query processing. The communication cost becomes large if the intermediate results between operators are large in intra-operator parallelism. To reduce communication cost, we separate communication from computation using several new operators. We have developed a distributed system named Secco by revamping SparkSQL on Spark, and confirmed the efficiency of our approach in our performance studies using real datasets.

The second objective is to explore new ways to support machine learning with new query processing techniques.

14202919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14202919.value: First, we study how to support ML by SQL. We study how to support Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithms which is a general technique for finding maximum likelihood estimators. SQL’99 recursion cannot be used to support EM, since SQL’99 recursion only supports stratified negation, and cannot support non-monotonic operations. We have implemented our approach on PostgreSQL and Spark SQL. We show how to train a batch of classical statistical models, including Gaussian Mixture model, Bernoulli Mixture model, the mixture of linear regression, Hidden Markov model, Mixtures of Experts. Given a model trained by EM, we design an automatic in-database model maintenance mechanism to maintain the model when the underlying training data changes. We report it in DASFAA’21. Second, as ML often require processing complex queries, we have developed two distributed systems on Spark. (i) To support complex join queries, we co-optimize three costs: communication, pre-computing, and computation in one-round multi-way join evaluation. We report it ICDE’21. (ii) To support SQL in parallel, we study parallel query processing at the relational algebra level, instead of multi-way join algorithms which cannot be used with other relational algebra operators. We reduce the dominating communication cost by separating communication from computation using new operators. We have developed a distributed system Secco on Spark. We report it in SIGMOD’22. Third, we study how learning can help complex cyclic join and report it in ICDE’22. Fourth, we study how to accurately estimate cardinality in query processing by Neural Network Gaussian Process, which is a lightweight approach that can learn very fast. The work is reported in SIGMOD’22. Fifth, we study how to learn a sketch for subgraph isomorphism counting which is NP-hard. We report it in SIGMOD’21 and VLDB Journal 2023. We study how to provide a DL solution when there is no efficient training data to learn initially. We report it DASFAA’23 and Data Science and Engineering 2023. We study local subgraph counting to find the number of all different topological patterns for every node in a large graph, which helps GNN. We report it in PVLDB’20. Sixth, we study efficient algorithms for budgeted influence maximization on massive social networks in PVLDB’20, efficient parallel shortest path counting on large-scaled graphs in ICDE’23, and hub labeling for shortest path counting in SIGMOD’20.

14202919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14202919.value: With machine learning being widely used, the needs to support machine learning by query processing techniques are high. There are common techniques used in machine learning training and database systems. We will continue our effort to explore a unified way to support both.

14202919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14202919.value: Machine learning techniques have been extensively studied to learn from large datasets. There is a question how machine learning and database system can be integrated tightly in the same platforms, to avoid extracting massive data from a database system to conduct machine learning tasks every time when there is such a need, which is with high cost. We concentrate ourselves on supporting machine learning in a database system. As observed, there is a mismatch between machine learning and database system, regarding data handling. From the machine learning, a machine learning algorithm will take a matrix (or its relation) as an input to learn, which implies that it is to keep everything in a single relation in a database. From the database system, data needs to be maintained in several relations for reducing information redundancy and improving query performance. When data is stored in several relations, it needs to join the relations to form a single relation to learn, which incurs high computational cost. We show that SQL can be used to support machine learning. We study approaches to efficiently support SQL queries, and developed two distributed systems on Spark. All works are reported in major international conferences and journals.

14203019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203019.value: 該項目旨在研究軟體裝置的磁氣混合控制並開發軟連接磁氣混合驅動內窺鏡系統（STEM-Endo）。該系統可用於微創手術，特別是單孔胸腔鏡手術。 肺癌是世界上最常見的癌症[1]，它佔新癌症的13％。在香港，肺癌發病率排名第二，死亡率排名第一[2]。手術切除是肺癌治療的常用方法。以往這些手術是通過開胸手術，這涉及打開胸腔。現代方法是使用胸腔鏡，尤其是單孔胸腔鏡。在單孔胸腔鏡手術中，所有手術器械和內窺鏡都通過一個小切口進入胸腔。外科醫生在胸腔鏡引導下執行手術操作，無需打開胸腔。這顯著減少了創傷，失血量，住院時間，術後疼痛等。因此，自2010年推出以來，胸外科醫生一直倡導單孔胸腔鏡手術。該手術的主要挑戰在於胸腔鏡的視野有限並經常乾涉其它手術器械操作。這會延長手術時間並可能導致轉換到開胸手術。替代方案包括磁錨定和引導系統（MAGS）。在MAGS中，無軸內窺鏡被輸送到胸腔內，然後通過體外的永磁鐵或電磁線圈驅動。這可以大大降低器械干涉的機會並提供更寬廣的視野。然而，儘管有這些優點，但目前臨床上還沒有使用MAGS。這是因為：1）由於運動耦合，MAGS內窺鏡的可控性差; 2）無法放大/縮小視野; 3）術中不能清潔鏡頭。 在這個項目中，我們提出STEM-Endo的方案。它包含一個錨定模塊，一個轉向模塊，一個沖洗模塊和一個機模塊。這些模塊集成在軟體結構中提供天然的安全性。另外，採用直觀的人機交互以便輕鬆控制STEM-Endo。該研究團隊在MAGS方面擁有超過四年的經驗。之前的工作得到業內認可。我們希望這項研究能夠解決MAGS在臨床化方向的挑戰，促進單口胸腔鏡手術的推廣從而讓患者受益。

14203019.label: Realisation of objectives
14203019.value: The aim of this project is to investigate the magnetic-pneumatic hybrid control of soft-bodied devices and develop a soft-tethered magnetic-pneumatic steered endoscope system (STEM-Endo) for minimally invasive surgery. The project has two main objectives, both we have fully achieved. The first objective is the development of a soft-tethered magnetic-pneumatic steered endoscope (STEM-Endo), which includes: design and prototyping of the device (STEM-Endo); kinematic modelling of the system; studying the magnetic-pneumatic hybrid control of soft-bodied structures to understand the control such devices; and using the device to realize autonomous instrument tracking with visual servoing. The second objective is the evaluation of the STEM-Endo system. This includes lab evaluation of the key functions in STEM-Endo system, including anchoring distance adaptation, base position adjustment, viewing angle steering and soft structure elongation; mock up single-port surgery to evaluate the clinical feasibility of the device (STEM-Endo). To explore the capability of hybrid actuation strategy using magnetic-pneumatic controls, we developed a number of prototypes. One example uses a pneumatic actuator on a soft tethered magnetic endoscope. Upon expansion, the pneumatic actuator anchors the endoscope position within a lumen, allowing an electromagnet array to directly control the bending orientation of a soft tethered endoscope. The electromagnetic array generates a magnetic field in desired orientation and strength, depending on the current input into each coil within the array. A magnetic field model is developed, and accurately estimate the force and torque applied to control the soft tethered magnetic endoscope. Testing in a range of applied force from 0 N to 0.6 N (0.1N steps), the model is accurate with an average absolute error of only 0.018N. For magnetic field applied torque ranging from 0 to 30 N·mm, average absolute error is only 0.599 N·mm. Using this model, the soft tethered endoscope can be guided by electromagnet array to follow desired trajectories: e.g. square path with 30mm edge, and circular path with a diameter of 30 mm. Another example is a soft tethered magnetic endoscope developed for uniport video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS) applications. Using permanent magnets embedded inside a small camera capsule, the device can pair with an external magnet located outside patient’s chest wall, and anchor under the internal surface of chest wall. With the external magnet position and orientation controlled by a robot arm, the soft tethered endoscope can be guided to various locations within the chest cavity. Magnetic rolling of the capsule allows the camera to sweep a range of viewing perspectives, whereas additional pneumatic actuator attached to the camera base allows change of perspective in an orthogonal direction, increasing the dexterity of system and expanding the view coverage. Based on the magnetic rolling actuation principle, and base position adjustment, we completed kinematic modelling of the system. The model maps from the image space target coordinates of tracked instrument, to the joint space of the robot system controlling STEM-Endo. Thus, upon specified target coordinates are defined in the camera view (i.e. an instrument to be tracked), the STEM-Endo system can calculate the robot joint motions to guide the target towards desired coordinates within camera view (e.g. centre of view). Initially an eye-gaze control scheme was developed to allow surgeon to operate the endoscope system intuitively. However, upon first hand observation of surgical procedures, and taking test feedbacks from clinicians who have operated the system, it is determined a voice command pairing with visual servoing scheme would be more intuitive. This is because it better mimics the interaction between surgeon and human assistants operating conventional laparoscopes. To realize this, a multi-modal AI strategy is developed to first detect and classify surgical instruments present within camera view, then allow surgeon to vocally specify an instrument type as target for tracking, and finally control the STEM-Endo to track target near centre of view. This function is demonstrated in a realistic human chest simulator. (details of workflow and logic in part C). This work received best paper award in ROBIO 2022. Targeting the objective of anchoring distance adaptation as a key function, a custom permanent magnet array is developed to optimize long range magnetic anchoring force. Specifically, a magnetic capsule weighing 23g, is paired with an array consisting two radially magnetized cylindrical EPMs (φ 50 mm×l30 mm) at both left and right ends, and one axially magnetized semi-cylindrical magnet (r25 mm×l16 mm) in the middle. Using a unified evaluation index called attractive force per unit volume (FPV), the custom array is shown to increase attractive force by 96.76%, and FPV up by 55.82% as compared to un-optimized magnets. This translates to stable anchoring and rotation control of magnetic capsule at 95mm distance from external magnet. Going one step further, we also invited expert surgeons specialized in VATS to test the STEM-Endo system in a human cadaver. The test covers the key functions including base position adjustment, viewing angle steering and soft structure elongation. In summary, surgeons commended the ease of control and dexterity of the STEM-Endo system, and deemed the design feasible in human body.

14203019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203019.value: This project aims to investigate the magnetic-pneumatic hybrid control of soft-bodied devices and develop a soft-tethered magnetic-pneumatic steered endoscope system (STEM-Endo) for minimally invasive surgery. Particularly, a soft-tethered magnetic endoscope has been developed for video-assisted thoracic surgery (VATS), with pneumatic actuator for additional camera dexterity. The magnetic capsule is anchored under the chest wall, pairing with an external magnet placed near human’s chest. A robot system controls the external magnet, guiding the STEM-Endo device to various spots within the chest cavity, expanding surgeon’s view of the surgical scene. A kinematic model is developed for the system. The model maps target coordinates in camera view to joint space of robot system, allowing tracking of instruments using visual servoing control scheme. Paired with a multi-modal AI, the STEM-Endo system can take vocal commands from surgeon, classify instrument types within camera view, and follow instrument class specified by surgeon. This closely mimics the interaction between surgeon and human assistant operating conventional laparoscopic systems. The function was tested in a realistic human chest simulator. This part of the work was award “best paper in robotics" in IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Biomimetics (ROBIO 2022). Human cadaver test was also used to prove the feasibility of the STEM-Endo system in human anatomy. Surgeon specialized in VATS operations was invited to evaluate the STEM-Endo system. Key functions such as base position adjustment, viewing angle steering and soft structure elongation were all demonstrated inside cadaver. To optimize the magnetic anchoring for long range operation, a custom magnetic array with three permanent magnets is developed and tested. Compared to un-optimized design, the custom array showed 55.82% increase in anchoring force per volume, and 96.76% increase in anchoring force. It can securely anchor a 23 g magnetic capsule at 95mm distance, and guide its position as well as orientation. In addition to the soft tethered magnetic endoscope designed for VATS, we also explored magnetic-pneumatic hybrid control in a soft tethered colonoscope. A pneumatic actuator can expand and anchor the endoscope within a lumen. An electromagnet array is used to generate magnetic field with desired strength and orientation, which allows fine adjustment of the force and torque acting on the endoscope tip. The device can follow specified trajectory, demonstrating accuracy of control scheme. These results are published in top peer-reviewed journals and leading international robotics conferences as shown in part C.

14203019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203019.value: In the current study, we demonstrated the feasibility of magnetic-pneumatic hybrid endoscope for minimally invasive surgery. Compared to conventional laparoscopic tools, the novel device can limit risk of collision with other instruments, while liberating the device from constraints of access port, expanding the reachable area. There are various instruments that can adopt similar control scheme and its benefits. For example, retractors for pull target tissue from various direction; illumination device magnetically anchored under chest wall, with pneumatic joint to direct lighting at area of interest. On the other hand, there are still a number of challenges such devices must address. First, the operable distance and anchoring force is directly proportional to the size of magnetic elements. This is partially mitigated by optimizing the magnets array, allowing low weight device like camera to operate at over 90mm. For high load devices like retractor, alternative strategy using electromagnets or multiple magnets on a deployable frame may be needed. Second, rare earth magnets offer high coupling force per volume, but always introduce rigid components to soft structures. High performance soft-ferromagnetic material could improve compliance and safety. Third, pneumatic actuation usually requires tether. Soft material with programmed magnetic region could remove need of tether.

14203019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203019.value: Lung cancer is one of the most common cancer types, and leading cause of cancer death. Thoracic surgery is an effective direct intervention for removing malignant tissues. Modern minimally invasive approach for treating lung cancer is limited by slender laparoscopic instruments design. The use of magnets, combined with pneumatic soft actuator for fine control, creates a new type of device that can operate inside human chest without the shaft of conventional tools. A magnet located outside human patient can attract a capsule endoscope inside the chest cavity, placing it under the chest wall internal surface, while guiding its location. A soft actuation driven by air/water pressure is attached to the magnetic capsule, located behind the camera. This allows fine adjustments to the camera viewing direction, improving the perspectives provided to surgeon. This can lower the risk of collision with other instruments, and expand the area covered by freeing the device from the entry point. A control scheme is developed to mimic the interaction between surgeon and human endoscope operator. The key functions of the device are tested in lab settings and human cadaver. Surgeons with expertise in thoracic operations tested the device, and approved its feasibility in human.

14203119.value: 邁向對細胞類型中基因調控的完整建模

14203119.label: Project Objectives
14203119.value: Developing a computational framework for integrating many types of gene regulatory mechanisms for the purpose of understanding how they work together in regulating gene expression. This framework will take into account specific properties of each type of data, such as false positives, false negative, data sparsity and clustering structures. Applying the framework to study gene regulation in several human cell lines from which the largest amount of experimental data are available for reconstructing the regulatory mechanisms. The relative contribution of each mechanism to the overall gene regulation system and inter-mechanism relationships will be studied. Developing an algorithm that can automatically search for a set of metapaths that are most useful for learning an embedding of biological objects and inferring gene expression. The metapaths will provide additional information of how the different gene regulatory mechanisms are related. Systematically evaluating the effects of different types of perturbations to individual nodes, edges and sub-networks on the overall gene regulatory system by inferring the changes in gene expression before and after the perturbations.

14203119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203119.value: 基因調控是一個複雜的過程，涉及轉錄，轉錄後，翻譯和翻譯後層面的許多不同機制。近年來，由於高通量方法的出現可以探測許多類型的分子活動，基因調控的研究已經從定性轉變為定量。例如，長期以來已知啟動子處的DNA甲基化與基因抑制有關，但是在先前的研究中，我們進一步演示如何可以從啟動子和基因體的甲基化定量估計確切的基因表達的變化量。 我們和其他人的研究也探討了其他調節機制與基因表達之間的定量關係，但每項研究只考慮了一種或幾種機制。這是不充分的，因為不同的機制相互作用並相互影響。 利用一些從特定人類細胞系產生的多種類型實驗數據，我們在這個研究項目中將構建能夠整合所有這些數據的模型，以研究各個調節機制對基因表達的貢獻，並破譯它們之間的關係，如緩沖和協同作用。 為了同時對多種類型的數據建模，我們將擴展metapath2vec方法。該方法提供了一個統一的框架，用於從不同類型的數據中學習。該框架使用根據領域知識定義的元路徑通過隨機遊走來識別網絡鄰域，並使用skip-gram模型來學習在潛在特徵空間中嵌入生物對象。由於metapath2vec框架是無監督(unsupervised)的，所學習的特徵向量可能與我們的基因表達推理任務無關。因此，我們將其擴展到半監督(semi-supervised)環境，以便利用訓練基因的表達信息。我們整合蛋白質相互作用，DNA可及性和染色體構象的初步研究表明，我們的半監督方法確實可以改善基因表達的建模。 我們還將開發能夠自動搜索有用的元路徑的算法，以發現基因調控的新知識。 這些方法將進一步用於研究擾動的影響，例如人類疾病中的基因突變。將對我們的主要發現進行實驗驗證，例如基於CRISPR-Cas9的基因組編輯，然後進行表達譜分析。 在概念層面，我們的項目將基於已知的調節機制和產生的實驗數據評估我們與細胞類型中基因調控的完整建模的距離。

14203119.label: Realisation of objectives
14203119.value: We have successfully carried out the project and realized all the objectives. Objective 1: We have developed the Gene Expression Embedding framework (GEEK). It is a framework for integrating various types of biological data for the joint study of multiple gene regulatory mechanisms. GEEK first uses a generic graph formation to represent various types of data, allowing for directed and undirected interactions, heterogeneous node and edge types, and node and edge attributes. It then performs random walks on the graph according to pre-defined metapaths to learn an embedding of the nodes using a semisupervised extension of the metapah2vec method, which is based on the word2vec method originally developed in the natural language processing (NLP) field for word embedding. The embedding of the nodes produced by GEEK, which are biological objects, can then be used for various downstream tasks such as modeling gene expression levels. Objective 2: We have used GEEK to integrate information about protein-protein interactions, broad chromatin domains, local genomic neighborhoods and three-dimensional genome structures for modeling gene expression, using data from five ENCODE cell lines. By using each metapath individually or in combination, we were able to evaluate their relative ability in producing embedding that is indicative of gene expression levels. In particular, we found that three-dimensional genome structures are very informative about gene expression levels when the corresponding experimental data (Hi-C) are of high quality, and in order for protein-protein interactions to explain gene expression levels accurately, those involving proteins encoded by genes on different chromosomes have to be included. Interestingly, the best modeling performance was always obtained by integrating all metapaths, showing that they contained complementary information. We have also shown that the embedding is useful for other tasks such as inferring replication timing, protein complexes, and frequently interacting regions (FIREs) in the genome architecture. Objective 3: We have developed a new computational framework for this objective. In contrast to the GEEK framework developed for Objective 1, which requires manually defined metapaths as input, this new framework automatically discovers the most informative metapaths from the input heterogeneous network directly. This allows discover of novel knowledge about gene regulation. We have applied this framework to 10 ENCODE cell lines, which have various types of chromatin interaction, transcriptomic, and epigenomic data produced. In addition to the biological networks we considered in Objective 1, we have also included additional networks when testing this new framework, including protein-RNA interactions, miRNA-target interactions, protein co-localization, and gene functional relationships. Objective 4: We have designed methods to perform in silico perturbation and estimate their effects on expression level of different genes. The main idea is to propagate the effects through the computational model that we have learned, by removing network nodes (in the case of gene deletion) or modifying node features (in the case of epigenetic modulation). Perturbations can be applied to one gene at a time, or a group of genes at the same time. We are now using the methods we have developed to systematically study effects of different types of perturbations in different cell lines."

14203119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203119.value: The major findings are summarized in Section 5.3 above. The main output of Objectives 1 and 2 is a journal publication in Nature Machine Intelligence (Cao, Zhang et al., 2020). We investigated an application of the graph-based machine learning method in studying cancer genes, which led to a second journal publication in Nature Machine Intelligence (Hong, Cao et al., 2022). Some of the modeling techniques were also used to study other diseases, including Hirschsprung disease, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and type II diabetes, which led to three other journal publications (Fu, Lui et al., Genome Research 2020; Lee et al., BMC Genomics 2022; Li et al., Nature Communications 2023). We are now preparing a new manuscript that summarizes our work in Objectives 3 and 4. We plan to submit it for journal publication in early 2024."

14203119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203119.value: There are two potential further developments. First, with the emergence of single-cell multi-modal assays, it is now possible to profile multiple modalities (e.g., histone modifications and gene expression) in the same cell. Performing the same type of modeling at the single-cell level will provide information about cell-to-cell variability in terms of the relative importance of different gene regulatory mechanisms. Second, instead of modeling transcript levels, which was the main focus of this project, it would be instructive to model protein abundance levels. It is well-known that transcript levels and protein levels do not correlate strongly, and that there are various translational and post-translational regulatory mechanisms that affect protein abundance, modifications, and turnover. Modeling protein levels would require incorporation of additional types of biological networks and features related to these mechanisms."

14203119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203119.value: Genes are DNA segments that produce functional products required for various activities in the cell. The production of these functional products is governed by multiple mechanisms. Why there should be multiple mechanisms, which of them is more important, and how they work together with each other are all fundamental questions in biology. This project uses advanced artificial intelligence methods to study many of these mechanisms at the same time, which was previously not doable. We have found that some mechanisms are particularly informative about gene activities, and that different mechanisms are not redundant but rather provide complementary information about gene activities. A practical application of our work is estimating effects of gene aberrations in diseases, by computationally mimicking such aberrations and using our models to infer the resulting gene activity changes.

14203619.value: 利用基於深度學習的智能語音技術對認知障礙進行早期檢測

14203619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203619.value: With the global trend of population aging, high prevalence of dementia and related cognitive disorders has become a critically emerging challenge to public health and societal well-being. Effective means of early detection and intervention are highly desired to mitigating the disease’s impact. Language impairment is one of the observable symptoms at a relatively early stage of dementia. An overarching goal of the proposed project is to develop automated systems and methods for quantifying and detecting language impairment that may mark early-stage cognitive decline. To address the need of local population in Hong Kong, our investigation is focused primarily on Cantonese. A large-scale database of Cantonese elderly speech will be developed. The database also includes clinical assessment results for individual subjects. Signal processing and machine learning methods are applied extensively to the analysis, modeling and classification of normal and impaired elderly speech. A deep neural network based automatic speech recognition system is developed to facilitate multi-scale acoustic and linguistic analysis. Word embedding methods are used to achieve robust representation and classification of natural language. Taking a non-blackbox approach, we aim to maximally incorporate clinical and linguistic knowledge into engineering system design, and to provide useful clinical interpretations on machine learning based speech analytics. The project team comprises experienced researchers and clinicians with inter-disciplinary knowledge background in spoken language technology, machine learning, speech and language pathology, clinical psychology and neurology. We seek for a funding of 1,527,276 to support this project for 36 months. 在全球人口老齡化的趨勢下，認知障礙症已經成為大眾健康和社會福利面對的最大挑戰。有效的早期檢測和干預對減低疾病的影響至關重要。過去的研究顯示，語言能力的下降為認知障礙及相關疾病的主要早期症狀之一。本項目旨在研究及開發新的口語語言自動評估技術，用於偵測和評估早期認知能力下降。本研究特別針對香港本地居民日常使用的主要語言──粵語，開發一個大規模的老齡人粵語語音數據庫。該數據庫除了包含語音聲學信號，亦將附有每個說話人的神經心理學臨床診斷結果。本研究將廣泛使用信號處理和機器學習技術，對正常和病理語音進行分析，建模和分類。重點包括，開發一個基於深度神經網絡的粵語語音識別系統實現多尺度的語音語言特徵提取，利用詞向量的方法實現自然語言的表達和分類。本研究採用非黑盒子的角度進行系統和算法設計，強調對語言學和臨床醫學知識的理解，運用和總結。研究團隊成員來自語音技術，機器學習，言語病理，臨床心理學及神經內科等多個領域，獲批研究經費港幣673,470元，項目為期36個月。

14203719.label: Realisation of objectives
14203719.value: Bioaerosols are airborne particles of biological origin, such as bacteria, fungi, pollen, and other organic matter. The components of bioaerosols include microorganisms and their byproducts. Exposure to bioaerosols is associated with a wide range of health effects, such as allergies, toxic reactions, and infectious diseases. Previous studies mainly investigated indoor or outdoor air pollutant exposure scenarios only. However, there is limited information about outdoor and individual exposure to bioaerosols, and the comparison of exposure concentrations between personal exposure and measurements from outdoor sampling station in Hong Kong. This study aimed to investigate the associations between outdoor and personal bioaerosol exposures, as well as their toxicity to humans, while also conducting in vitro experiments to explore molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in allergic airway inflammation. A population-based sampling strategy was used to recruit non-smoking subjects for non-occupational personal air exposure measurement in Hong Kong. All potential subjects were recruited through advertisement and convenience sampling. Eligibility criteria included permanent Hong Kong residency and/or residence in Hong Kong for the past twelve months, non-smoker status, aged 18 or above, with no symptoms of respiratory illnesses, no current allergies, cardiovascular diseases, or other chronic diseases. To achieve the objectives, personal and outdoor bioaerosol monitoring was conducted using portable air samplers. Two personal monitors for sample collection were provided in a backpack assigned to each participant. Throughout each sampling session, the temperature and relative humidity were collected using a temperature sensor. Sampler inlets were fastened to the backpack's shoulder strap. Participants needed to wear personal backpacks during all activities, except for bathing, sleeping, and changing clothing, during which they should keep the backpack around their breathing height. Duplicates and field blank filter samples were treated in the same manner for quality control purposes. Two portable samplers set with a flow rate of 10 L/min were used to conduct outdoor PM sampling concurrently with personal sampling. During the personal air sampling period, each subject was required to keep a fifteen-minute resolution time-activity diary, reporting the time spent in each primary microenvironment (residential indoor/outdoor environment and workplace), exposure to environmental tobacco smoking (frequency and duration), and other potential exposures (e.g., cooking activity duration, cleaning type, and frequency). Additionally, subjects were asked to report any symptoms of respiratory-related diseases and daily medication in the given diary. After sampling, gravimetric analysis and quantification of biological PM were applied to pre-treatment of samples. Before and after each sampling, all filters were weighed in a temperature-controlled weighing room (25 °C, 30–40% relative humidity). With an electronic microbalance, the mass of PM particles (μg) collected on the Teflon filters was calculated gravimetrically. After that, the exposed sample filters were kept in a refrigerator at -20°C. In a pyrogen-free centrifuge tube, the Teflon-filter PM sample was deposited into 2 ml of pyrogen-free water with Tween-20 (0.05%). The tube was then transferred into a vortex shaker set to 600 rpm for 120 minutes at room temperature. This procedure allowed for the extraction of water-soluble components, including endotoxins and soluble metals. Following extraction, each eluate was centrifuged for 10 minutes at 3500 rpm to remove insoluble particles and filter fragments that might interfere with subsequent analyses. Subsequently, 300 µL of the supernatant was transferred to pyrogen-free tubes for endotoxin testing and cell experiments. The remaining samples were re-suspended, and particles were concentrated on a 0.22 µm pore size cellulose membrane for DNA extraction. Blank Teflon filters, which were taken to the site without sampling, served as negative controls. Endotoxin levels in all samples were measured using the chromogenic LAL Endotoxin Assay Kit (Beyotime Biotechnology) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Briefly, samples were diluted and combined with the provided reagents. Following incubation at 37°C, a chromogenic substrate was added to initiate color development. The optical density of each sample was measured using a microplate reader, and endotoxin concentrations were reported in units (EU) relative to a standard endotoxin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from E. coli. Total genomic DNA from the samples was extracted using the CTAB/SDS method (CTAB, Nobleryder, China). The concentration and purity of the DNA were assessed using 1% agarose gels. The DNA was then diluted to a concentration of 1 ng/µL with sterile water based on the initial measurements. Distinct regions of the 16S rRNA/18S rRNA/ITS genes (e.g., 16SV4, 16SV3, 16SV3-V4, 16SV4-V5, 18SV4, 18SV9, ITS1, ITS2, ArcV4) were amplified using specific primers (e.g., 16SV4: 515F-806R; 18SV4: 528F-706R; 18SV9: 1380F-1510R, etc.) with barcodes. Each PCR reaction consisted of 15 µL of Phusion® High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix (New England Biolabs), 0.2 µM of forward and reverse primers, and approximately 10 ng of template DNA. The thermal cycling conditions were as follows: initial denaturation at 98°C for 1 minute, followed by 30 cycles of denaturation at 98°C for 10 seconds, annealing at 50°C for 30 seconds, and elongation at 72°C for 30 seconds, with a final extension at 72°C for 5 minutes. After purification, ligation, and transformation, positive clones were selected for sequencing using the Illumina NovaSeq platform. Paired-end reads from the original DNA fragments were merged using FLASH (Magoč and Salzberg, 2011) and assigned to each sample based on unique barcodes. Vector sequences and chimeras were excluded, and bacterial 16S rRNA sequences were denoised with the DADA2 or deblur module in the QIIME2 software (version QIIME2-202202) to obtain initial ASVs (Amplicon Sequence Variants). Species annotation was performed using QIIME2 software based on the Silva Database. Cell Experiments Human A549 lung alveolar epithelial cells, obtained from the American Type Culture Collection (ATCC, Manassas, VA, USA), were cultured in an incubator at 37°C with 95% humidity and 5% CO2. The cells were maintained in RPMI medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum, penicillin, and streptomycin. Cells were exposed to 25 µL of extracted particles at a density of 10^4 cells/mL for 24 hours. The extracted supernatants (200 µL) were freeze-dried and re-suspended in 200 µL RPMI medium. Each PM exposure experiment was conducted in triplicate. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) and malondialdehyde (MDA) production were assessed using colorimetric assay kits from Nanjing Jiancheng Technology Co., Ltd. The concentrations of interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kits, according to the manufacturer’s instructions. All assays were performed in triplicate. Oxidative stress and inflammation were found after exposure to PM samples, and the characterization of microbial components was identified. According to our pilot study on personal exposure to PM2.5 in Hong Kong, we drafted a manuscript titled "Health Risks of Adults in Hong Kong Related to Inhalation of Particle-Bound Heavy Metal(loid)s," which has been accepted for publication in "Air Quality, Atmosphere & Health." However, the recruitment of subjects and sampling activities faced significant delays due to the protests and the COVID-19 pandemic, which extended our entire sampling and analytical schedule. Despite these challenges, we conducted two extra studies on the effectiveness of intervention measures during the COVID-19 pandemic, resulting in the acceptance of two additional papers. Overall, we successfully achieved our proposed aims as planned. Additionally, one outcome has been published in peer-reviewed journal. More results are anticipated and expected for further articles.

14203719.value: • Personal exposure to PM2.5 ranged from 1.98 to 55.59 μg/m³, averaging 16.78±9.16 μg/m³ in summer and 18.57±8.06 μg/m³ in winter. Outdoor PM2.5 levels ranged from 6.35 to 42.82 μg/m³, with averages of 18.78±8.53 μg/m³ in summer and 23.05±10.47 μg/m³ in winter. Generally, personal exposure to PM2.5 was lower than outdoor levels in both seasons. Endotoxin levels, a key component of airborne bioaerosols, were higher in personal samples, particularly in summer (1.086 to 1.912 EU/m³), underscoring the significance of individual or indoor exposure. • A549 cell responses to air samples showed increased oxidative stress and inflammation. Summer personal samples led to higher MDA levels, indicating more lipid peroxidation (oxidative stress) compared to outdoor samples, while winter personal samples had lower MDA levels. Summer personal samples resulted in higher IL-6 and IL-1β levels than outdoor samples, while winter personal samples induced lower IL-6 and IL-1β levels than outdoor samples. • High-throughput sequencing revealed that the dominant bacterial phyla in air samples were Proteobacteria, Bacteroidota, and Firmicutes, with variations at the genus level. In summer, personal samples were dominated by Chryseobacterium, Ralstonia, and Stenotrophomonas, while outdoor samples had Chryseobacterium, Ralstonia, and Proteus. In winter, dominant genera in both sample types were Chryseobacterium, Stenotrophomonas, and Delftia. Summer personal samples contained more Vibrio, while winter outdoor samples had more Escherichia-shigella. The common OTUs (Operational Taxonomic Units) shared between personal and outdoor samples were 10.81% in summer and 18.81% in winter, indicating a greater difference between personal and outdoor samples in summer compared to winter. • MetaGenomeSeq analysis identified significant bacterial genera differences between personal and outdoor air samples. In summer, personal samples had higher levels of Vibrio, Pseudoalteromonas, and Methyloversatilis, all potential pathogens contributing to higher endotoxin levels. In winter, only Qipengyuania was significantly higher in personal samples, but its low abundance minimally impacted endotoxin levels. • Correlation analysis revealed positive associations between endotoxin concentrations and both chromium (Cr) and nickel (Ni), suggesting their potential roles in nutrient transport via fine inorganic particles. A mixed-effects model showed that Tumor Necrosis Factor-α (TNF-α) production was positively associated with endotoxin concentration and Cr as a combined exposure factor.

14203719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203719.value: The present study focused on the biological and toxicological characterization of outdoor and personal exposure to bioaerosols in PM2.5, as well as their corresponding toxicity. Cytotoxicity caused by bioaerosols was investigated and compared. Future studies should further explore microbial components from bioaerosols and their mechanisms of inducing allergic airway inflammation. Additionally, it is crucial to compare the health effects triggered by different types of bioaerosols. This study identified only a portion of bioaerosol components, leaving many microbial fractions, such as pollen and mold spores, unresolved in detail. Epidemiological evidence linking outdoor air pollution exposure to new-onset asthma and COPD suggests a potential similar link between outdoor bioaerosol exposure and allergic airway inflammation. Further in vitro and in vivo studies could investigate the specific mechanisms by which bioaerosols trigger inflammatory responses in the airways. Additionally, future research should consider how environmental factors like temperature and humidity may modulate the relationship between bioaerosols and airway inflammation.

14203719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203719.value: This research investigates how exposure to bioaerosols—airborne particles like bacteria and endotoxins—affects human health, particularly in Hong Kong. Bioaerosols can cause allergies, toxic reactions, and infections, but little is known about the differences between personal and outdoor exposure. This study compared personal exposure to bioaerosols with outdoor levels and examined their toxic effects on humans. Participants carried portable air samplers to measure personal exposure, while outdoor samples were collected simultaneously. The study found that personal exposure to PM2.5 was generally lower than outdoor levels, but endotoxin levels—a component of bioaerosols—were higher in personal samples, especially in summer. Laboratory tests on lung cells exposed to these samples revealed increased oxidative stress and inflammation. Key bacterial groups, including some that can cause infections, were identified in the air samples, providing insight into potential health risks. High-throughput sequencing identified common bacteria in air samples, with significant seasonal variations. The findings highlight the importance of assessing individual bioaerosol exposure to better understand its health impacts. This research provides valuable insights for future studies on how bioaerosols contribute to respiratory issues and suggests a need for further investigation into specific microbial components and their inflammatory mechanisms.

14203919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14203919.value: Aim of the Project The aim of the project is to develop an integrated microfluidic system for the loading of enzyme payloads into erythrocytes based on modulated membrane deformation, and to subsequently investigate how the deformability of erythrocytes may affect the loading efficiency. Project Background Enzyme-mediated arginine depletion has shown significant promise for the treatment of cancers, but the low circulatory life-time and significant cytotoxicity of these recombinant enzymes in either their native or modified forms still present challenges. The erythrocytes, colloquially known as red blood cells, have been extensively explored as a natural enzyme carrier for sustained intravascular delivery. Although strategies relying on the passive delivery of enzyme payloads through hypotonic treatment have shown initial promise, the treated erythrocytes may be damaged by the hypotonic shock and thus lose their biocompatibility. Furthermore, maintaining enzyme functionality for enzyme-mediated therapies is of equal importance, so the search for optimal methods of balancing the erythrocytes’ integrity, enzyme functionality and loading efficiency continues. Brief Project Description To address the above-mentioned challenges, a microfluidic platform will be established incorporating the following features: (1) active and controllable membrane deformation of erythrocytes and the subsequent encouragement of enzyme loading; (2) gentle and effective separation of excess enzymes from loaded erythrocytes; and (3) on-chip monitoring of erythrocyte deformability. Planned technological developments will enable the intrinsic heterogeneity of erythrocytes in their deformability to be examined, along with an exploration of how deformability may affect the loading efficiency of enzyme payloads, which has not been previously investigated. Significance of the Proposed Project The conceptually innovative membrane deformation mediated enzyme loading into erythrocytes is expected to bridge the gap between enzyme- and erythrocyte-mediated therapies, and to ultimately generate health benefits in cancer treatments by offering a controllable loading technique to internalise enzyme payloads, as per the mechanical properties of erythrocytes. The success of this proposal represents an important opportunity for us to gain ground in the competitive landscape of personalised anticancer therapies. 本項目的目的是開發一個集成的微流體系統，基於可調控的膜形變將酶加載至紅細胞中，並研究紅細胞的可變形性如何影響加載效率。 酶介導的精氨酸耗盡有望用於癌症治療，但是這些以天然或修飾形式存在的重組酶所具有的循環壽命短、細胞毒性顯著等問題依舊是一項挑戰。紅細胞近來已被廣泛用於天然酶在血管內持續遞送的載體。儘管通過低滲處理被動遞送酶的策略已初步顯示成效，但低滲處理過的紅細胞可能產生低滲休克損壞並喪失其生物相容性。此外，對於酶介導治療，維持酶功能同樣重要，因此尋求平衡紅細胞完整性、酶功能和加載效率的最佳策略仍是重要的課題。 為了克服上述挑戰，本項目將建立一個微流體平台，其具有以下特徵：(1)通過主動且可控的膜變形將酶加載至紅細胞中; (2)溫和且有效地分離負載酶的紅細胞與過量的酶; (3)紅細胞可變形性的芯片上監測。本項目提出的技術將可檢驗紅細胞在可變形性上的內在異質性，並同時探索細胞膜的可變形性如何影響酶的加載效率。此一概念上創新的膜變形介導酶加載方法，依據紅細胞的力學性能提供可控的酶內化技術，有望彌合酶和紅細胞介導療法目前存在的缺口，並最終作為個性化抗癌療法的基礎用於癌症治療。

14203919.label: Realisation of objectives
14203919.value: The aim of the project is to develop an integrated microfluidic system for the loading of enzyme payloads into red blood cells (RBCs) based on modulated membrane deformation, and to subsequently investigate how the deformability of RBCs may affect the loading efficiency. We have realized the proposed objectives as the following: Objective 1. Design and fabricate the microfluidic device for the membrane deformation of erythrocytes and the subsequent loading of arginine degrading enzymes: We have developed a microfluidic system capable of introducing different levels of stress and varied duration of stress exposure, collectively modulated by the channel geometry and the flow rates. The microfluidic device is fabricated by soft lithography techniques, casting polydimethylsiloxane prepolymer on a SU-8 master for micro-molding. A simulation based on coarse-grained molecular dynamics analysis predicted the stable formation of pores at around 6 nm in diameter on RBC membranes. The poration was indirectly assessed by the outflux of hemoglobin, when the areal deformation reached around 10% under a shear stress of ~ 40 Pa (shear rate ~40,000 1/s). Previous findings also showed that the deformation of RBCs occurred upon shearing by a stress between 20-60 Pa (corresponding to a shear rate of 20,000-60,000 1/s), and RBCs may be lysed at a shear stress greater than approximately 100 Pa (shear rate of 100,000 1/s). Therefore, a microchannel was introduced to initiate transient membrane poration, referred as “transient deformation” hereafter, with a mean shear stress in a range of 46-102 Pa (shear rate 46,350-101,979 1/s). Different from the previous microfluidics-based delivery strategies, a cross-junction was designed to situate RBCs in a stagnation point, where both laminar and extensional shear stresses were employed, presumably capable of generating profound deformation compared to those under laminar shear solely in a straight channel. The membrane tension was maintained at ~10 mN/m, lower than the rupture tension of mouse RBC’s membrane (90 mN/m). Empirically, the membrane poration was quantified by the outflux of hemoglobin molecules, whereas the membrane damage was assessed by the phosphatidylserine (PS) exposure from the inner to the outer leaflet of RBC membrane. The optimal shear stress at around 64.9 Pa (shear rate of 64,900 1/s) was empirically determined for sufficient pore formation on mouse RBCs, while the membrane integrity was preserved at around 80%, a typical threshold to maintain the in vivo lifespan of RBCs without causing hemolysis. To systematically investigate the effect of shear duration on membrane poration, the transiently deformed RBCs were further guided through a constricted serpentine microchannel to induce an “extended deformation” for a duration between 0.21 ms to 1.44 ms at a constant level of shear in a range of 55-75 Pa (modulated by the volumetric flow rate of 60-80 µL/min). Under the mean shear stress of 64.9 Pa (optimized from the transient deformation), the percentage of hemoglobin release increased monotonically with the duration of shear exposure for mouse RBCs. The shear duration was optimized for extended deformation at around 0.82 ms by setting the threshold of preserved membrane integrity at 80%. Given the typical size of protein payloads in the range of 1-6 nm, enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP, Stokes radius 2 nm) was used to optimize the experimental conditions and allow for quantification of loading. At a constant concentration of RBCs, the transient deformation and extended deformation yielded approximately 2.5- and 4-fold increase in EGFP-loading compared to osmotic entrapment, respectively. Subsequently, human arginase (hArgI, Stokes radius 3.1 nm), an arginine degrading enzyme commonly employed in anticancer therapies, was introduced to evaluate whether the shear-mediated membrane deformation may also load functional protein. hArgI labelled with fluorescent dye was employed to quantify that the loading efficiency was indeed enhanced by the transient and extended deformation. The functional activity of hArgI encapsulated into RBCs by the transient and extended deformation were approximately 5- and 13-fold higher than that of osmotic entrapment’s, respectively. The potential therapeutic efficacy of delivered hArgI was evaluated in vitro by incubating the model cell line human liver cancer (HepG2) cells with RBC-encapsulated-hArgI. The RBC-encapsulated-hArgI by transient and extended deformation exhibited comparable level of growth suppression as those loaded by osmotic entrapment. Objective 2. Develop a microfluidic platform to gently and effectively separate loaded erythrocytes and excess enzymes: The percentage of EGFP-positive RBCs increased with the rising concentration of EGFP used for both osmotic entrapment and transient deformation, implying that the transport of EGFP into RBCs was mainly through diffusion. Notably, the delivery via transient deformation was consistently more efficient compared to osmotic entrapment. Given that the effect of osmotic entrapment was not involved in the shear-mediated deformation, the enhanced loading efficiency was attributed to the combinatorial effect of passive diffusion and an “active” delivery, plausibly mediated by the membrane poration caused by both laminar and extensional shear stress. It is of note that the loading efficiency reached a plateau at a protein concentration of 4-8 µM in both cases. Therefore, subsequent experiments were conducted with a fixed protein and RBC concentrations of 4 µM and 4 × 10^6 cells/mL, respectively. To rule out the confounding effect of excess enzymes and to avoid the damage of RBCs by centrifugation, we propose to separate the excess enzymes and loaded RBCs by inertial microfluidics. The inertial lift and the so-called Dean drag forces collectively determine the transversal migration of particles of different mass along the channel width. Thus, the equilibrium position of particulates is determined by the mass of the particulates and the Dean vortices generated by the flow. We have designed a chip to separate the loaded RBC (6-8 µm) from the excess hArg. Objective 3. Systematically analyse the deformability of erythrocytes using mice erythrocytes as a model and investigate whether the loading efficiency may be modulated based on the deformability: The deformation index (DI) is a widely employed in vitro characterization of the deformability of RBCs. Previous studies have shown that the in vitro measured DI of RBCs may serve as an adequate indication of the sustainability of RBCs in the in vivo environment. In line with a previous report, RBCs treated with osmotic entrapment showed significantly lower DI due to the osmotic shock, potentially leading to their shorter in vivo lifetime. On the other hand, RBCs treated by transient and extended deformation showed insignificant difference in DI compared to the untreated RBCs, implying that RBCs treated with the shear-mediated deformation may retain similar in vivo lifetimes as that of untreated RBCs. Aside from the deformability of RBCs, membrane lesions play an important role in in vivo circulation as reported previously. The RBCs treated with shear-mediated deformation were able to better preserve membrane integrity and to recover from potential PS exposure compared to the osmotic entrapment’s. Taken together, this project has presented a novel method to encapsulate protein payloads into RBCs by controlling membrane deformation either transiently or extendedly in a microfluidic channel. Significantly, mouse RBCs loaded with hArg exhibit higher enzymatic activity and membrane integrity compared to the counterparts loaded by osmotic entrapment. These features together with the fact that this shear-mediated encapsulation strategy allows loading under physiological buffers highlight the key advantages of this approach compared to traditional osmotic entrapment.

14203919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14203919.value: The proposed shear-mediated membrane poration modulated by the presented microfluidic device was shown promising for loading functional payloads into RBCs through a delicate control of transient and/or extended deformation. The potential of this loading strategy was validated by delivering EGFP and hArgI to mouse RBCs. Under the empirically optimized conditions of transient and extended deformation, the shear-mediated loading yielded 5- and 13-fold increase enzymatic activity from the loaded hArgI compared to the osmotic entrapment, respectively. Notably, the proposed shear-mediated loading relied solely on the physical deformation of RBCs to generate membrane pores, which allowed loading in a physiological buffer that is better suited for proteins instead of a hypotonic buffer, and presumably in the preservation of membrane integrity of the treated RBCs as well. This study presented the investigation to deliver functional and therapeutic proteins into RBCs mediated by membrane deformation, which is expected to bridge the gap between enzyme- and erythrocyte-mediated therapies, and to ultimately generate health benefits in cancer treatments by offering a modulable loading technique to internalize therapeutic biomolecules into the erythrocytes with minimal membrane damage. We have published the developed platform and findings in an article published in Lab on a Chip (Impact Factor: 6.1, top 10% in the field of Biochemical Research Methods, Peer-Reviewed Publications #1), and in four conference papers particularly the two presented in the flagship conference series of microfluids (The International Conference on Miniaturized Systems for Chemistry and Life Sciences (MicroTAS), Recognized international conference #3-4 (presented). The technology has been patented (M. H. Rahman, M. K. Chan, M. M. M. Lee, C. H. N. Wong, and Y. P. Ho, "Systems and Methods for Controlled Membrane Disruption Field," 2018 (US Provisional Patent, Application No. 62/832,638; PCT/CN2020/084117; US Patent No. WO 2020/207456 @ June 2, 2022, Other Impact #1). As part of our collaborative effort with Prof. Michael Chan at the School of Life Sciences in CUHK, we have further the study to in vivo validation by the scale-up production and successfully acquired funding from the Innovation Technology Fund (ITF) in Hong Kong (Project No: ITS/133/20). From the education’s perspective, the PI has contributed a book chapter in collaboration with Prof. An-Chi Wei in the National Taiwan University. The shear produced in the microfluidic device is used to extract mitochondria (Other Impact #2).

14203919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14203919.value: Beyond this project, we have extended the scope to study the mechanical properties of mesenchymal stem cells as a label-free biomarker, in collaboration with Prof. Renjie Zhou (Biomedical Engineering) and Prof. Hon Fai Chan (Institute for Tissue Engineering and Regenerative Medicine) in the Chinese University of Hong Kong, as well as Prof. Wayne Yuk-wai Lee (Orthopaedics and Traumatology) in the Prince of Wales Hospital and Prof. Youhua Tan (Biomedical Engineering, Hong Kong Polytechnic University). Moreover, a start-up company situated in the Hong Kong Science Park, EggLogics, has expressed the interest of employing the developed technique to investigate the quality of eggs by measuring the deformation index prior to the in vitro fertilization. The collaborative activities were supported by the CUHK Technology Start-up Support Scheme for Universities (TSSSU), Project No: TSU21MED15.

14203919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14203919.value: This project is aimed to develop a platform based on a microfluidic chip for the loading of enzyme payloads into red blood cells (RBCs) via membrane deformation, termed "micro shear-porator". Enzyme-mediated amino acid depletion has shown significant promise for the treatment of cancers, however, the low circulatory lifetime and significant cytotoxicity of the recombinant enzymes in either their native or modified forms are holding the back of enzyme-based therapies. Strategies that rely on the passive delivery of enzyme payloads into RBCs by hypotonic treatment may extend the stability of enzymes, but the treated RBCs may be damaged by the hypotonic shock and thus lose their biocompatibility. We have developed and patented the technique of micro shear-porator to deliver the enzyme payloads into RBCs through active and controllable membrane deformation without compromising the membrane integrity. We will further the studies by prototyping the micro shear-porator, scaling up the processing speed, testing the scale-up loading with functional enzyme payloads and evaluating the activities of enzymes loaded RBCs in mice. The developed micro shear-porator is expected to bridge the gap between enzyme- and RBC-mediated therapies, and to ultimately generate health benefits in cancer treatments by offering a controllable loading technique to internalize payloads.

14204019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14204019.value: Optical scattering effects like Brillouin scattering, Rayleigh scattering etc in optical fibers have been used to build up distributed fiber senor systems, e.g. Brillouin optical time domain analyzer (BOTDA) and Phase-sensitive Optical Time Domain Reflectometer (Phase-OTDR), which have attracted much interest in the past three decades due to their capability of distributed temperature, strain, vibration etc monitoring. Those sensors employ the conventional fiber as the sensing medium and allow all locations along the long fiber to be measured simultaneously, which provide an efficient and cost-effective way of simultaneously achieving multi-points sensing. However, despite years of intensive research, the performance of distributed fiber sensors is still limited by the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) degradation of sensing signals, leading to tradeoffs among key parameters, e.g. spatial resolution, sensing distance, sensing accuracy, measurement time etc. To resolve as many sensing points as possible with ultimate sensing performance still remains to be the most challenging for distributed fiber sensors. Current state-of-the-art techniques addressing the limitations benefit from mature electrical and optical devices to build up advanced hardware configurations from the optical side, which improve the system performance but with increased system complexity and cost. In contrast, post signal processing of sensing signals using Digital Signal Processing (DSP) techniques can be implemented in conventional setup to improve the system performance without adding system complexity and cost. Over the recent two years, some advanced image/video denoising techniques and machine learning techniques have been brought to distributed fiber sensing by a few research groups including us for post processing of sensing signals to improve the system performance, and they have shown very encouraging results. Thus it is expected that more advanced DSP techniques from DSP area and computer science should be introduced and well explored to further improve the system performance without adding any system complexity and cost. The purpose of the proposed research is to investigate the use of novel advanced DSP techniques to address the limitations existing in distributed fiber sensors from the side of post signal processing, and hence improve the system performance in terms of the key parameters. The advanced DSP techniques developed in this proposal will serve as complementary methods to state-of-the-art optical techniques and can be combined together with them to potentially achieve ultimate sensing performance for a wide types of fiber sensors.
