14205419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205419.value: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability. It is commonly associated with abnormal muscle coordination and loss of dexterity, particularly in the hand. Although non-invasive current stimulation can modulate cortical excitability transiently, it only stimulates limited target regions. For example, standard high-definition transcranial direct current stimulation(HD-tDCS) only has an anodal/cathodal electrode surrounded by four return electrodes. Rather than operating in isolation, brain regions interact with other regions through networks. Therefore, to stimulate multiple brain regions and reinforce the connections between them, researchers have proposed multisite transcranial direct current stimulation(tDCS). The stimulation of multiple connected regions related to motor function may further enhance cortical excitability for stroke rehabilitation. Multisite tDCS, a recent advanced technology, can deliver various currents with up to eight electrodes with 2mA. A study showed the primary motor cortex excitability following multisite tDCS was more than doubled the increase following traditional tDCS in healthy subjects. The main challenge in applying multisite tDCS lies in finding the dose and areas of the brain to stimulate. To solve this problem, one study proposed mapping the finite element model(FEM) current distribution map, which is determined by the derived dose and location of electrodes from the computational optimization method, with a resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging(fMRI) map and minimizing the difference between the two maps. Previous studies have placed electrodes on the unimpaired brain, whereas we will emphasize motor related brain networks of the paretic hemisphere to facilitate motor recovery. Therefore, this proposal will adopt hand function task-based fMRI to find “activation foci” (i.e., shifted primary motor cortex after stroke) in combination other motor related brain regions and then investigate optimization method for the electrode location and dose. The multisite tDCS electrodes are similar in size to 128-channel electroencephalography(EEG) electrodes and can be integrated with a standard EEG cap, offering higher flexibility in exploring the dynamic neural responses immediately after the stimulation. A randomized controlled trial will be conducted in three groups of stroke survivors: personalized multisite tDCS, in which the dose and electrode location will be determined by the above FEM-fMRI method; standard HD-tDCS; and sham multisite tDCS. A 10-session stimulation will be provided to evaluate the effectiveness of the transient modulation of cortical excitability through tDCS with clinical assessment scores, fMRI, TMS and EEG. These assessments will be conducted before and after training and at the 3-month follow-up, to track tDCS-induced cortical excitability and the effects on hand motor function recovery. 中風是導致長期殘疾的主要原因。它通常與異常的肌肉協調和靈活性有關，特別是在手部。儘管非侵入性電流刺激可以調節皮質興奮性，但它僅刺激有限的區域。例如，標準的高清經顱直流電刺激（HD-tDCS）僅具有由四個返回電極圍繞的陽極/陰極電極。大腦區域不是孤立地運作，而是通過網絡與其他區域相互作用。因此，為了刺激多個大腦區域並加強它們之間的聯繫，研究人員提出了多位點經顱直流電刺激。與運動功能相關的多個連接區域的刺激可以進一步增強中風康復的皮質興奮性。 多點經顱直流電刺激可以通過多達8個電極（2mA）提供電流。一項研究表明，在健康受試者中，傳統tDCS後，多位點tDCS後的初級運動皮層興奮性增加了一倍以上。應用多點tDCS的主要挑戰在於找到刺激大腦的劑量。為了解決這個問題，一項研究提出將有限元模型（FEM）電流分佈圖與靜止狀態功能磁共振成像（fMRI）圖進行映射，該電流分佈圖由計算優化方法的電極的導出劑量和位置確定。以前的研究已經將電極放在未受損的大腦上，而我們將強調中風大腦的運動相關腦網絡以促進運動恢復。因此，提議採用fMRI來組合其他運動相關腦區域中的“激活灶”（即，中風後移位的初級運動皮層），然後研究電極位置和劑量的優化方法。多區域tDCS電極的大小與128通道腦電圖（EEG）電極相似，可以與標準EEG帽集成，在刺激後立即探索運動神經反應。

14205419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205419.value: The research was structured into three distinct phases. The initial phase involved creating realistic Finite Element Models for 25 chronic stroke patients to simulate the electric field induced by tDCS during standard motor rehabilitation montages. The average electric field measured in the ipsilesional hand knob area was 0.24V/m, with significant variations observed across individuals. Stroke lesions near the stimulation targets altered the path of the electric field. This necessitates the customization of stimulation montages to account for the varied lesion locations. In the second phase, we aimed to confirm the precision of our simulated electric fields. The stroke patients from the initial phase were split into two groups. Twelve individuals received a 20-minute session of active conventional tDCS, while a separate group of 13 participants underwent sham stimulation. We used resting-state fMRI functional connectivity to evaluate the stimulation's impact. The findings indicated that conventional tDCS significantly improves intra-hemispheric connectivity in the ipsilesional hemisphere. Importantly, the electric field simulation models we developed successfully accounted for the individual differences in functional connectivity resulting from tDCS. These results suggest that electric field models are effective in predicting the outcomes of stimulation, which could lead to the refinement of tDCS applications. These findings were documented in Neuroscience Research in 2023. In the final staqge, we employed the FEM models developed earlier to construct personalized multisite tDCS montages. Initially, we identified individual stimulation targets using fMRI-derived ipsilesional hand-motor activation maps. Then, we optimized the process to enhance the electric field targeting these ipsilesional motor areas while reducing stimulation to non-target areas. To validate this method, we conducted a single-blinded, randomized controlled trial with two groups. Eight participants received personalized multisite tDCS before EMG-driven robot hand training, while ten participants received sham tDCS before the training. The results showed that the active tDCS group had a greater improvement in upper extremity function than the sham group. The motor activation patterns in the active group increasingly matched the target area optimized for stimulation, indicating the potential of tDCS to guide neuroplasticity and aid motor recovery. Additionally, the results showed decreased inter-hemispheric inhibition and increased intra-hemispheric premotor-motor facilitation, correlating with motor recovery. A portion of this study was published in the IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering in 2023, and another manuscript is under review by the Journal of NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation.

14205419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205419.value: Our current study exclusively focused on optimizing tDCS montages for targeting ipsilesional hand motor activation. Future investigations will explore and compare various optimization strategies, such as: Single target versus multiple targets: Assessing the relative merits of stimulating a single key target area versus simultaneously targeting multiple regions known to contribute to motor recovery; Task-based activation versus resting-state fMRI maps: Investigating whether task-specific brain activation patterns derived from functional tasks better guide montage optimization compared to resting-state fMRI maps, or vice versa; Anodal versus cathodal stimulation: Examining the differential effects of applying anodal (excitatory) and cathodal (inhibitory) stimulation within personalized multisite tDCS montages, potentially revealing optimal polarity configurations for maximizing therapeutic benefits. These follow-up studies will broaden our understanding of the factors influencing the efficacy of personalized tDCS in motor rehabilitation and contribute to the refinement of tDCS montage design for enhanced neurorehabilitation interventions.

14205419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205419.value: Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation (tDCS) is a noninvasive technique that applies mild electrical currents to the scalp to alter brain activity. It is increasingly acknowledged that repeated tDCS sessions can improve motor recovery in individuals recuperating from chronic stroke. Nonetheless, the optimal placement of stimulation electrodes remains elusive. This study introduces a novel method to ascertain electrode placements that effectively target specific brain areas for each individual. Contrary to traditional tDCS, which can produce variable effects due to personal anatomical differences, our approach utilizes simulations to accommodate these variations and personalizes stimulation according to each person's distinct brain activation patterns. The results of this research provide information on personalized tDCS treatments, potentially enhancing neurorehabilitation interventions to be more precise and effective, tailored to the unique requirements of each patient.

14205719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14205719.value: Recognition has been a core topic in computer vision. Over the past several years, the advances in deep learning have resulted in remarkable improvement on recognition performance. Yet, this is not the end of the story. Cognition is not just about recognition. Imagination is also a very important kind of cognitive process, which, however, has not been extensively explored in the context the computer vision. In the real world, it is not uncommon that people can imagine an entire story, just looking at a picture about it. This amazing capability of imagination motivate us to ask a question: can we develop a machine that can emulate this capability? This is certainly a challenging problem. Specifically, this task requires one to supplement a great amount of information, both visually and semantically. For example, seeing that a person boarding a ship, we should imagine the ship sailing towards the horizon. It is very difficult to connect these two scenes visually, but the connection can be established based on common sense at the semantic level. This project aims to explore such semantic connections for story generation and develop an algorithm to learn them from data. This key aspect distinguishes the proposed work from many conditional generation tasks, which are primarily based on visual coherence. We plan to investigate a principled framework with three key modules: (1) A visual analysis module for extracting key semantic elements from the given image, e.g. people, objects, scene, and their interaction. (2) A semantic flow module for extrapolating from a single semantic point to a story line. Particularly, we desire to generate a diverse set of story lines from a given point, while ensuring that the semantic structures are logical. The formulation of this module together with the algorithm to learn it from data constitute a key contribution. (3) A presentation module for rendering the story line into a sequence of images or a long video. The techniques developed in this project can open up a number of new applications, e.g. compiling photos into story threads, story video generation, and story editing. These applications are not only valuable in themselves, but also great demonstrations of modern computer vision techniques. 視像識別是計算機視覺領域的一個核心課題。在過去幾年，深度學習技術的進展帶來了識別性能的巨大提升。但是，視覺認知的能力並不僅限於識別，想象也是一種重要的認知過程。在計算機視覺領域，過去對這種能力尚未有充分探索。在真實世界中，人們往往看到一張照片就能想象出整個故事。這種觀察讓我們提出一個問題：我們是否可以讓計算機模擬此種能力？這顯然是一個很有挑戰性的問題。具體而言，這個任務要求我們在所看到的圖像之外補充很多信息，包括可視的以及語義層面的。比如，當看到一個人登上帆船，我們會想象揚帆遠航的情景。雖然登船和遠航的情景在視覺上差別很大，但是它們是可以在語義層面連接在一起的。此項目致力於探索這種聯繫，并由此研發出可以從圖像生成故事的算法。對於語義聯繫的運用是此項目區別于之前主要基於視覺的生成框架的重要方面。我們計劃研發一個新型框架，它包含三個主要模塊。(1) 視覺分析模塊：用於從圖像中提取重要的語義元素，比如人、物體、場景、以及它們之間的交互；(2) 語義流模塊：從單個語義節點推演出一條故事線；(3)表達模塊：從故事線生成出圖像序列或者視頻。此項目研發的技術將能帶來很多新的應用，比如把圖片排列為故事線、自動生成故事視頻、以及支持故事編輯等。這些應用不僅本身很有價值，它們也是對現代計算機視覺技術的很好的展示。

14205719.label: Realisation of objectives
14205719.value: 1. For Objective 1: Extracting key semantic information from multimedia content requires comprehensive visual understanding abilities. To achieve this goal, we developed strong perception systems for humans, objects, scenes, and high-level semantics. Specifically, (1) for person recognition, the reliance on annotated data became a major obstacle for face recognition. We desired to explore an alternative approach (Huang et al., ECCV 2020) for face recognition, using captioned images, which are widely available on the web for training. As a result, we can train a state-of-the-art face recognition model without manual annotation. Furthermore, searching for certain people in videos has seen increasing potential in real-world applications, such as video organization and editing. We proposed an online person search framework (Xia et al., ECCV 2020), which can recognize people in a video on the fly. (2) For object perception, we found that current object detection frameworks mainly rely on bounding box regression to localize objects. The precision of bounding box regression remained unsatisfactory, hence limiting performance in object detection. Therefore, we proposed Side-Aware Boundary Localization (SABL) (Wang et al., ECCV 2020), where each side of the bounding box is respectively localized with a dedicated network branch, leading to significant improvements. To detect objects from videos with 3D bounding boxes, we took advantage of the strong geometry structure provided by camera ego-motion for accurate object depth estimation and detection. We proposed Depth from Motion (DfM) (Wang et al., ECCV 2022), which can establish geometry to lift 2D image features to the 3D space and detect 3D objects thereon, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a large margin. (2) For scene understanding, we explore semi-supervised semantic segmentation aimed at training the scene parsing model with limited labeled data and a large amount of unlabeled data. We proposed a novel framework, Gentle Teaching Assistant (GTA-Seg) (Jin et al., NeurIPS 2022), to disentangle the effects of pseudo labels on the feature extractor and mask predictor of the student model, which transfers the beneficial feature representation knowledge and protects the model from negative influences. It achieves consistent gains for scene parsing benchmarks. (3) For semantic extraction, we developed video semantic understanding frameworks from large-scale databases. We introduced OmniSource (Duan et al., ECCV 2020), a novel framework for leveraging web data to train video recognition models. OmniSource overcomes the barriers between data formats, such as images, short videos, and long untrimmed videos for webly supervised learning. Moreover, we proposed a novel learning scheme (Qian et al., ECCV 2022) for self-supervised video representation learning, which first learns general visual concepts and then attends to discriminative local areas for video understanding. With the proposed works, we successfully extract key semantic information for images and videos, facilitating the exploration of story generation. 2. For Objective 2: Given a single image input, we explore generating human-centric storylines. The storyline is converted into synthesized human motion in a given image scene via our proposed frameworks. Specifically, we proposed a new framework (Wang et al., CVPR 2021) for this task with the interaction between the scene and the human motion taken into account. Considering the uncertainty of human motion, we formulate this task as a generative task, whose objective is to generate plausible human motion conditioned on both the scene and the human’s initial position. We assess the effectiveness of the proposed method on two challenging datasets for both synthetic and real-world environments. Furthermore, we attempted to generate a long-term storyline with human motion sequences. We focused on the problem of synthesizing diverse scene-aware human motions under the guidance of target action sequences (Wang et al., CVPR 2023). The experiment results show that the proposed framework remarkably outperforms previous methods regarding diversity and naturalness. Thanks to our proposed methods, we can readily generate long-term storylines with diverse and natural human motions. 3. For Objective 3: In the context of a storyline, we developed multiple approaches to generate photo sequences. The photo sequence can comprise retrieved real photos, generated contents, and rendered images from 3D models. (1) We proposed to compose a video from the images/videos gallery following a given text storyline in three steps. The first step was to segment a long video in the gallery into shots, aiming to identify the composition of scenes. We proposed a local-to-global scene segmentation framework (Rao et al., CVPR 2022), which can distill complex semantics from hierarchical temporal structures over a long movie, providing top-down guidance for scene segmentation. Secondly, the types of shots greatly influence how the underlying ideas, emotions, and messages are expressed. We proposed a learning framework, Subject Guidance Network (SGNet) (Rao et al., ECCV 2020) for shot type recognition. Finally, we presented Transcript-to-Video (Xiong et al., MM 2022), a weakly-supervised framework that uses texts as input to create video sequences from an extensive collection of shots automatically. (2) We further investigated the potential of generating sequences of images from a storyline. Specifically, we focused on a practical application that generates a speaker image sequence driven by an initial image and speech audio. We proposed a novel framework, Audio-driveN Gesture vIdeo gEneration (ANGIE) (Liu et al., NeurIPS 2022), to effectively capture the reusable co-speech gesture patterns and fine-grained rhythmic movements. The proposed framework shows a promising possibility to be generalized for more free-form scenarios. (3) We further explored creating image sequences via rendering from 3D models. We proposed BungeeNeRF (Xiangli et al., ECCV 2022), a progressive neural radiance field that achieves level-of-detail rendering across drastically varied scales. In summary, the proposed research effectively generated image sequences following a given storyline, demonstrating potential from real-world applications. 4. For Objective 4: To support the training and evaluation of proposed frameworks, we construct several datasets and benchmarks. (1) FineGym (Shao et al., CVPR 2020) and TAPOS (Shao et al., CVPR 2020) are datasets and benchmarks for fine-grained gymnastic video recognition. (2) MovieNet (Huang et al., ECCV 2020) is a holistic dataset and benchmark for movie understanding. (3) Placepedia (Huang et al., ECCV 2020) is a large-scale place dataset and benchmark for place recognition. (4) We scaled up the scene segmentation task by building a large-scale video dataset, MovieScenes (Rao et al., CVPR 2022). And we built a large-scale dataset, MovieShots (Rao et al., ECCV 2020), for shot classification. These datasets and benchmarks are the cornerstone of our research works. 5. For Objective 5: We have constructed prototype applications for photo thread compilation and video generation, which shows the strength of our methods. Overall, the works mentioned above have resulted in 20+ papers published on top conferences on computer vision.

14205719.label: Major findings and research outcome
14205719.value: Our research project takes on the challenging task of extracting key semantic information from images and translating it into coherent stories showcased through image sequences or videos. This endeavor requires a synergistic integration of multiple frameworks. 1. Comprehensive Image Understanding: Delving into computer vision area, we attempted to tackle the fundamental task of comprehending content within images. It demands a rich understanding of various elements, such as humans, objects, and scenes, and the ability to extract high-level semantic information. To achieve this, we harnessed the power of state-of-the-art models in face recognition (Huang et al., 2020) and person search (Xia et al., 2020), ensuring accurate human identification. On object detection, we achieved precise localization in both 2D (Wang et al., 2020) and 3D spaces (Wang et al., 2022). In terms of scene analysis, we employed advanced semantic segmentation techniques (Jin et al., NeurIPS 2022) and captured high-level semantics via holistic frameworks (Duan et al., 2020; Qian et al., 2022). These concerted efforts ensure a robust and comprehensive analysis of image content. 2. Storytelling through Semantic Flow and Visual Presentation: We aimed to craft stories from single images. Utilizing our Semantic Flow module, we generated storylines on a semantic level, ensuring coherence and relevance. These storylines were then translated into captivating image sequences or videos through our Visual Presentation module. We generated the storyline formulated as human motions (Wang et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2023), creating diverse and natural human movements representing stories. Additionally, we explored various avenues for visual translation, including the utilization of real photos (Xiong et al., 2022), generated content (Liu et al., 2022), and images rendered from 3D models (Xiangli et al., 2022). While our solutions have shown promising results, we acknowledge the vast potential and untapped possibilities in this domain, signaling exciting opportunities for future exploration. 3. Data: The Cornerstone of Innovation: Our progress was driven by a diverse and rich data collection. We combined meticulously annotated human data (Shao et al., 2020; Shao et al., 2020; Huang et al., 2020; Rao et al., 2022; Rao et al., 2020) with vast repositories of unlabeled (Qian et al., 2022) or weakly labeled data (Huang et al., 2020;Jin et al., 2022;Duan et al., 2020), enabling the development of next-generation algorithms. In summary, our research stands at the crossroads of image understanding and storytelling, pioneering approaches that are not only innovative but also foundational for future endeavors.

14205719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14205719.value: This project brings up several topics that are worthy of further exploration. 1. Holistic Foundation Model for Image Understanding: Current methodologies often involve multiple specialized models to comprehend different information within an image. There is a promising goal in developing a unified, holistic foundation model capable of seamlessly perceiving humans, objects, scenes, and extracting high-level semantics from images. Such a model will simplify the process, enhance efficiency, and potentially lead to more accurate image interpretations. 2. LLM for Visual Storytelling: Leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) for visual storytelling presents an comprising potential, due to their strong ability in composing text storylines. Extending capabilities of LLMs to guide the generation of image sequences may lead to more coherent and contextual results. 3. Video Generation Foundation Model: The project also reveals a emergent demand of a foundation model for video generation. This model would directly translate given stories into videos, streamlining the current multi-step process. In essence, this project not only contributes to the present landscape of image understanding and storytelling but also sets the stage for groundbreaking advancements in these domains, encouraging further investigation and innovation.

14205719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14205719.value: This research project is developing a system that understands and creates stories from a single image. Given a photo and additional information, it can not only recognize key information, e.g., people and objects in it, but also generate a story that is demonstrated in a sequence of images, e.g., videos. To achieve this goal, we made several key contributions: 1) Visual Analysis: We developed sophisticated frameworks capable of extracting semantic information from images and videos. This includes identifying people, objects, and the overall scene, which form stories. 2) Semantic Flow: We created frameworks that take the visual information and generate a coherent storyline. 3) Visual Presentation: We built a system to translate the generated storyline into a sequence of images or a video. This involves retrieving or creating visual content that matches the story, ensuring a seamless and engaging narrative. 4) Comprehensive Datasets and Benchmarks: We constructed datasets and benchmarks to train and evaluate our system. By combining these contributions, our project paves the way for more intuitive and engaging ways of storytelling through images, making it accessible and enjoyable for a broader audience. Overall, this project has resulted in 20+ papers published on top conferences on computer vision.

14206419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14206419.value: Cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) have some important unique advantages compared with traditional serial and parallel mechanisms, namely: very large potential workspace, high transportability and high payload-to-weight ratio. This allows CDPRs to be potentially used in applications such as within manufacturing of large structures such as airplanes and ships, sports stadium cameras, large motion simulators and building construction. Despite these advantages, CDPRs typically suffer from limited workspace due to lack of rotational ability and cable interference with the environment. One promising solution to address these issues is to allow the cable attachment locations to be moving (reconfigurable). This would both: 1) increase the workspace by allowing the cables to be able to avoid interferences; and 2) optimise the robot performance and characteristics, such as energy consumption and dexterity. Currently, there lacks methods to solve the online planning and control problem for the reconfiguration of cable attachment locations given required motion trajectories. Another important issue that has not been studied thus far is the design of reconfiguration, where existing works only allow the cable attachments to reconfigure linearly and in an orthogonal and symmetrical (regular) arrangement. The objectives of this project are to study the analysis, planning, control and design of continuously reconfigurable CDPRs. The study consists of four innovative components. 1) A novel new type of workspace analysis and reconfiguration planning approach that incorporates the reconfiguration DoFs (reconfiguration workspace analysis) with both feasible continuous and optimal reconfiguration. 2) Design optimisation strategy to determine optimal reconfiguration paths of cable attachments, including reconfiguration over non-linear curves and irregular placements, with the goal to minimise the number of reconfiguration DoFs and actuators. 3) An online model predictive control (MPC) strategy for both the cable forces and cable attachment locations to track end-effector trajectories when subject to disturbances through using CDPR workspace analysis to achieve a linear MPC formulation. 4) Experimental validation and realisation of the developed algorithms in this project. The proposed project will be the first to achieve the analysis, planning and design for reconfiguring CDPRs for the generalised class of CDPRs. The success of this study will contribute both to the fundamentals of reconfigurable robots, analysis of higher DoF complex systems, and control of constrained robotic systems. Furthermore, the project opens the potential in using reconfiguring CDPRs for new applications that otherwise may not have been possible, such as within large-scale manufacturing processes and building construction. 與傳統的串、並聯機械系統相比，繩並聯驅動機器人(CDPRs)具有大工作空間、高可攜性、高載荷比等獨特的優點。這使得CDPRs可應用於飛機和船舶等大型結構的製造、體育場攝像機、大型運動模擬器和建築施工等領域。即使如此，由於其有限的旋轉角度和繩索對障礙物的碰撞，CDPRs的工作空間會因此被減少或限制。以上的問題可以透過移動繩索連接的位置（重構機械的結構）來解決。重構結構可以帶來以下好處: 1) 增加工作空間，使工作空間内的碰撞減少; 2) 優化機器人的性能和特點，如能耗和靈活性。對於給定的運動軌跡，目前缺乏解決實時規劃和控制繩索連接位置的方法。另一個尚未被深入研究的問題是可重構系統的設計，目前只有有關綫性重構和正交及對稱（有規則的）重構的分析。本專案的目的是針對可連續重構繩並聯驅動機械人的分析、規劃、控制和設計。 本研究由四個創新的部分組成。1) 新型的工作空間分析與重構規劃方法，將重構 的自由度(重構后的工作空間)與可行的連續重構和最優重構相結合。2) 設計優化策略，找出重構后最優的繩索連接位置，包括非線性曲線上的重構和不規則位置上的重構，並以減少使用驅動器的自由度和數量作爲目標。3) 透過利用CDPR工作空間的分析結果得出其線性預測控制(MPC)的公式，實現繩索施展的作用力以及繩索連接位置的實時模型預測與控制(MPC)策略，以對應末端執行器受擾動時的運動軌跡。4) 透過相應開發的演算法進行實驗驗證與應用。此專案將是首個針對可重構CDPRs的分析、規劃和設計的專案。并且能應用在廣泛的CDPRs上。本研究的成功將有助於可重構機器人的基本原理、高自由度複雜系統的分析和被約束機器人系統的控制。此外，可重構機械人還可以應用在新的領域上，例如大規模的建造及建築工程。此專案為類似的應用提供了前所未有的可能性。

14206419.label: Realisation of objectives
14206419.value: Objective 1: Develop algorithms for workspace analysis and online planning of generalised reconfigurable CDPRs. In this project, two different algorithms were developed for the workspace analysis and the reconfiguration planning for R-CDPRs, respectively. Both algorithms were based on the concept of formulating the reconfiguration, and hence the resulting workspace conditions, as polynomial functions. By doing so, it was shown that the interference-free workspace could be expressed as polynomial equations and hence can be efficiently and accurately solved. Beyond R-CDPRs, it was shown that this approach could be used on the general class of CDPRs. This method formed the foundations to study the workspace that included the reconfiguration variables (in addition to the robot poses), where it was shown that the workspace conditions are also polynomial in nature. Using this knowledge, an optimisation-based reconfiguration planning method (that is, determining the optimal reconfiguration of cable attachments to satisfy workspace constraints while achieve some desired objectives) was proposed. It was shown that to satisfy the wrench-closure workspace condition, interference-free workspace condition, and achieve objectives such as maximisation of the tension factor and minimisation of the cable forces, the optimal cable reconfiguration can be determined by solving a polynomial optimisation problem (POP). By framing the problem as a POP, the Lasserre’s method can be used to determine the globally optimal solution. In both works, the methods were validated in simulation on a range of R-CDPRs, to show the generalisability of the works. Objective 2: Systematic study for the design, in both location and shape, of continuously reconfiguring cable attachments. The design problem refers to the type and placement of the reconfigurable element of the R-CDPR. In this project, several novel developments were made to this objective: 1) the study of different types of reconfigurations and its performance; and 2) the optimisation of desired placements of reconfiguring elements. To the first development, in this project three different types of reconfiguration elements were explored: a) reconfiguration through rails, whether linear or curved; b) reconfiguration through one or more mobile base(s); and c) reconfiguration of thruster elements serving as “virtual cables”. It was discovered that each mode of reconfiguration has its advantages and disadvantages relating to the system’s flexibility and complexity. Furthermore, different applications were explored for the different modes, including brick-laying and façade works. These works are currently in progress and publications relating to this is in preparation. It should also be noted that the consideration of hybrid reconfigurable thrusters and cable-driven robots is a concept in its early stages resulting from this project. Objective 3: Develop online model predictive control strategies for reconfiguring CDPRs. Using the workspace understanding developed from objective 1, a novel online model predictive control (MPC) strategy was studied in this project. By initially considering only the reference trajectory, the MPC problem becomes a model predictive planning (MPP) one. It can be shown that the MPP can be expressed as a convex quadratic program (QP) by knowing the convex region of the feasible cable attachments from the workspace. The resulting QP generates a smooth and effective reconfiguration strategy for the reference trajectory. This was then extended to a closed-loop controller through the combination of a reactive control element within the MPP, with assumptions on the control performance and hence it’s region of deviation from the reference trajectory. The proposed approach was shown to be plausible for linear rail reconfiguration, and also being extended to reconfiguring thrusters on thruster R-CDPRs. Objective 4: Experimentally validate the developed methods on hardware systems. The developed methods and understanding have led to the development of several R-CDPRs. First, a more “traditional” R-CDPR with linear rails that reconfigure were developed for the CU-Brick robot, for the purpose of brick-laying to construct complex geometrical structures. This has been realised for various scales, from a 1m x 1m, 2m x 2m robot to a 10m x 10m robot. Second, the Robo-Tapper robot, consisting of a cable robot suspended by mobile base(s) at the building rooftops, was developed for hammer tapping façade inspection. The mobility of the system allows for increased performance (due to reconfiguration) and eliminating the need to fix the robot to the building. Finally, initial concepts for reconfiguring thruster CDPRs are building explored, in order to increase the performance of the CDPR while avoiding cable interferences. In addition to the development of the R-CDPRs, the robots have provided a platform to validate the developed methods. Finally, a novel method studied during the R-CDPR hardware development is the analysis and planning of CDPRs by considering the torque-velocity profile of the cable-driven actuators. It was shown that the true workspace and potential of the robot must consider this property, a concept that was neglected in all traditional CDPR studies. Summary In summary, the objectives of this project were well achieved, as demonstrated by the fundamental and practical developments as a result of the project. Furthermore, this project resulted in 4 journal publications (two in IEEE Transactions on Robotics and two in Elsevier Mechanisms and Machine Theory), the training of 2 PhD students, and also the recipient of several awards relating to a reconfiguring CDPR developed.

14206419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14206419.value: Reconfigurable cable-driven parallel robots (R-CDPRs) are a special type of cable-driven robots where the cable attachment points, hence the force directions of the cables, can dynamically change in order to increase the performance of the robot. The typical approach to achieve the reconfiguration is through active movement of the cable attachment point(s), either through linear rails, mobile bases or other means. This project aims to deal with the fundamental aspects related to R-CDPRs, including the development of workspace analysis techniques, the design of reconfiguration and most importantly the planning and control of the reconfiguration. With respect to workspace analysis, a new extension to the ray-based workspace approach was developed to consider the interference of CDPRs (IFW), including cable-cable and cable-obstacle interference. It was shown that by considering the workspace conditions one degree-of-freedom at a time, the IFW boundaries can be determined by solving univariate polynomial equations. It was shown that the computational efficiency and accuracy of the approach was superior to existing point-wise methods. Finally, a path planning method to ensure both wrench-closure and interference-free path can be generated given desired start and end points. In addition to gaining an increased understanding of CDPRs and R-CDPRs, the proposed workspace generation method was also be used for the reconfiguration planning of R-CDPRs. Using this concept, it was then shown that by considering the reconfiguration variables as the unknowns, various objectives (maximisation of tension factor and minimisation of cable forces) and workspace conditions (wrench-closure and interference-free) can be expressed as multivariate polynomial equations. As such, the resulting reconfiguration planning problem for R-CDPRs can be expressed as a polynomial optimisation problem (POP), which can be efficiently and optimally solved. This is the first generalised reconfiguration planner for R-CDPR that considers the general family of R-CDPRs and can be solved without black-box search-based solvers. On the practical development point of view, three different types of R-CDPRs were studied and developed. First, a more traditional R-CDPR with linearly reconfiguring rails was developed. Second, the development of a mobile base R-CDPR began during this project for the purpose of building façade inspection. Third, a new type of R-CDPR that uses drone propellors was investigated during this project also. During the practical development, a first of its kind analysis method that considers the actuator torque-speed curve for CDPRs was considered. These practical developments pave the way for future novel R-CDPR research beyond this project.

14206419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14206419.value: Through this project, both fundamental and practical developments of R-CDPRs have demonstrated the large potential for future research and development on CDPRs. Fundamentally, the optimisation-based reconfiguration control and planner has inspired our further development on a new class of convex reconfiguration design optimisation techniques that differ significantly from mainstream approaches where they are solved using black-box solvers. As such, the proposed work shows great potential for future development and real-world adoption, and will be continued in future projects. Moreover, the new developments on R-CDPR types resulting from this project, particularly the mobile CDPR Robo-Tapper and reconfigurable thruster CDPR (RT-CDPR). The Robo-Tapper is a cable-driven robot that has a mobile robot base that operates at the rooftop of a building and can effectively perform inspection of high-rise buildings. The methods of this project are beneficial to the design and control for Robo-Tapper. To further develop the Robo-Tapper, there are plans to apply for the upcoming round of Research Impact Fund. The RT-CDPR is an alternative form of R-CDPR where mechanisms to orient thrusters are proposed to serve as additional cables. This is a unique and novel type of CDPR and a GRF has been submitted to continue this research.

14206419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14206419.value: Reconfigurable cable-driven parallel robots (R-CDPRs) are a special type of cable-driven robots where the cable attachment points, hence the force directions of the cables, can dynamically change in order to increase the performance of the robot. In this project, both the fundamental and practical aspects related to R-CDPRs were studied and developed. Fundamentally, an efficient ray-based workspace analysis approach to ensure that the cables do not collide with each other and with obstacles was proposed. Extending on this, a new method was proposed to solve the optimal reconfiguration for R-CDPRs based on the desired trajectory and workspace of the robot. The proposed formation was shown to be both effective and rigorous in ensuring finding a feasible solution if it existed. Practically, three different types of R-CDPRs were studied and developed. First, a more traditional R-CDPR with linearly reconfiguring rails was developed. Second, the development of a mobile base R-CDPR began during this project for the purpose of building façade inspection. Third, a new type of R-CDPR that uses drone propellors was investigated during this project also. These practical developments pave the way for future novel R-CDPR research beyond this project.

14207019.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14207019.value: 金融工程中回撤衍生產品的定價和對冲

14207019.label: Project Objectives
14207019.value: We will develop a computationally efficient and generally applicable algorithm for pricing and hedging drawdown derivatives in one-dimensional Markovian asset price models. We will prove the algorithm's convergence and obtain its convergence rate. We will find out the effectiveness of drawdown derivatives in hedging the price risk of some highly volatile assets.
rows: We will develop a computationally efficient and generally applicable algorithm for pricing and hedging drawdown derivatives in one-dimensional Markovian asset price models.
We will prove the algorithm's convergence and obtain its convergence rate.
We will find out the effectiveness of drawdown derivatives in hedging the price risk of some highly volatile assets.

14207019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207019.value: Investors demand protection against sharp price falls, which are not uncommon in financial markets. A key concept in measuring the severity of price drops is drawdown, which is defined as the decline of the current price or current log-price from the maximum price or maximum log-price to date. Maximum drawdown further marks the worst retreat from the peak. As standard financial derivatives like put options typically cannot provide investors with adequate protection against the risk of incurring large drawdowns, various types of drawdown derivatives with payoffs determined by the maximum drawdown have been proposed as insurance against drawdown risk. How to price and hedge these derivatives is undoubtedly an important question in practice, which concerns financial institutions offering these products to investors as well as those with trading positions in these derivatives. In this project, we aim to develop a computationally efficient method for pricing and hedging different types of drawdown derivatives in general one-dimensional Markovian asset price models. Our approach is based on continuous time Markov chain approximation and numerical integration. Such a general and efficient method is still lacking in the literature, and having it is essential in practice as it allows more realistic models to be employed to properly price and hedge drawdown risk in real time. We also plan to conduct an empirical study for highly volatile assets like cryptocurrencies, which have been increasingly drawing interests from investors, but at the same time have also sparked serious concerns from regulators. We will investigate how a variety of drawdown derivatives perform in protecting investors from the price risk of these assets based on real market data. We anticipate that some drawdown derivatives can serve as a potential solution to ease the concern over lack of protection in cryptocurrency investments. The general and efficient pricing and hedging tool we develop will enable financial institutions to offer these products in reality. 投資者需要針對市場突然大幅下跌的保護，而這些突然的變換在市場并非不常見。金融中用來刻畫價格下跌嚴重程度的一個關鍵概念是回撤，它定義為當前的價格或者對數價格與迄今最大價格或者最大對數價格的差值。最大回撤給出了從頂峰最大的下跌。 由於標準的金融期權例如看跌期權通常不能為投資者面臨的回撤風險提供充分的保護，多種基於回撤的衍生產品作爲針對回撤風險的保險提出，它們的收益由最大回撤決定。毫無疑問，如何定價和對冲這些衍生產品在現實中是個受到提供以及交易這些產品的金融機構關注的重要問題。 在本科研項目中，我們的目標是開發有效的計算方法來定價和對冲多種基於最大回撤的衍生產品。我們的方法基於連續時間馬氏鏈逼近和數值積分。在文獻中這樣一個廣汎使用并且計算效率高的方法還不存在。擁有這樣的方法在現實中很重要，因爲它能讓金融機構采用真實的模型實時定價和對冲這些產品。 我們也計劃針對高波動性資產例如加密貨幣開展實證研究。加密貨幣吸引了越來越多投資者的興趣，但同時也引發了監管者對其的憂慮。對這些資產，我們會基於市場數據研究各種基於最大回撤的衍生產品保護投資的效果。我們期待其中一些最大回撤的衍生產品能夠提供一個潛在的方案來降低對加密貨幣投資缺乏保護的憂慮。

14207019.label: Realisation of objectives
14207019.value: We have solved a series of drawdown related problems under general one-dimensional Markov asset price models and achieved the first objective fully. (1) The option that compensates the investor the amount of drawdown over a given time period is the classical floating-strike lookback put option. In output 3, we have developed an efficient algorithm by combining continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) approximation with effient numerical quadrature rules to price various types of lookback options. In particular, it applies to the drawdown option. (2) In output 1, we analyze the distribution of the first passage time of the drawdown process. We are able to compute its Laplace transform by CTMC approximation, based on which we have developed an efficient algorithm for pricing maximum drawdown options. (3) In output 2, we consider the pricing problem of Americal style drawdown call options and develop an efficient algorithm using CTMC approximation and numerical solvers for variational inequalities. (4) In output 4, we propose an efficient method to compute the distribution of the speed and duration of drawdown based on CTMC approximation. (This paper was submitted to the journal "Quantitative Finance" in 2022 and it took about 11 months for us to get the review reports. We have submitted the revision to the journal for the second-round review.) We have also realized the second objective fully. In each of these four problems, we have developed rigorous convergence theory of our algorithms by proving their convergence mathematically. For the convergence rate, we obtain it either theoretically (in outputs 1, 3, and 4) or numerically (in output 2). For the third objective. we have also achieved it fully. In output 1, we consider bitcoin which is a highly volatile asset and conduct an empirical study based on the real market data for bitcoin to understand the effectiveness of hedging by using three major types of drawdown derivatives. We show that some drawdown derivatives can achieve substantial risk reduction in bitcoin investment. The original proposal only considered one-dimensional Markov asset price models, but our research has gone far beyond this framework. In output 1 and 3, our algorithms can also be applied to important two-dimensional asset price models including regime-switching models and stochastic local volatility models. During the project, I trained one Ph.D. student Xiang ZHANG. The research results in output 2 form the major part of his dissertation, where he also studied some portfolio optimization problems with drawdown constraints. He is now working as a quantitative analyst in the equity derivatives group of CLSA, an investment bank in Hong Kong. To present our research results and exchange ideas with the academic community, I have attended two major international conferences in the area of financial engineering during the project period. Unfortunately, I could not go to more due to a significant reduction in conferences or workshops during the COVID-19 pandemic. I would like to explain the unspent balance for this project. The two conferences I attended were held online due to travel restrictions imposed by the pandemic. Therefore, a significant portion of the budget for conferences is not spent.

14207019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207019.value: In output 1, we develop a novel method to solve the first passage problem of the drawdown process for general one-dimensional Markov processes as well as regime-switching and stochastic volatility models. We compute its Laplace transform based on continuous-time Markov chain (CTMC) approximation and invert the Laplace transform numerically to obtain the first passage probabilities and the distribution of the maximum drawdown. We prove convergence for general Markov models and provide sharp estimate of the convergence rate for a general class of jump-diffusion models. We apply our method to price and hedge maximum drawdown options and demonstrate its accuracy and efficiency through numerical experiments. In addition, we can apply our method for investment analysis. In output 2, we consider the pricing problem of perpetual American style drawdown call options, which allow the holder to optimally choose the time to receive a call payoff written on the drawdown. We use CTMC approximation and develop two types of algorithms to solve the optimal stopping problem for the drawdown process. The first one is a transform based algorithm which is applicable to exponential Lévy models. The second approach solves the linear complementarity problem (LCP) associated with the variational inequalities for the value function and applies to general Markov models. We propose an efficient Block-LCP (BLCP) method and identify the best LCP solver through numerical experiments. We prove the convergence of our algorithms and validate their computational efficiency. We also provide an extension of the BLCP method to the finite maturity case. I apologize for not specifying this grant in the acknowledgement section of this paper due to oversight, but this work is directly related to the grant as can be seen from the content. In output 3, we propose a computationally efficient method for pricing various types of lookback options under Markov models by combining efficient numerical quadrature with CTMC approximation. In particular, our method is applicable to the drawdown option that compensates the option holder the asset price drawdown over a specified time period. In output 4, we compute the distributions of the speed and duration of drawdown for one-dimensional Markov processes based on CTMC approximation. We demonstrate the efficiency of our method, prove its convergence and obtain a sharp estimate of the convergence rate under some assumptions. As applications, we consider pricing two financial options that provide protection against drawdown risk.

14207019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207019.value: In this project, we focused on developing computational methods for the distribution of drawdown-related quantities and applied them to price various types of drawdown derivatives. In practice, drawdown constraints often appear in investment decision problems. In future research, we can consider how to solve optimal investment problems with drawdown constraints by utilizing the algorithms we have developed for drawdown analysis.

14207019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207019.value: The drawdown in the price of an asset shows how much the price falls relative to its historical maximum and drawdown risk is a major concern in financial markets. Large drawdowns in asset prices can trigger substantial losses to investors, as seen from the collapse of cryptocurrencies and the stock market meltdown during the pandemic. Thus, it is practically important to chacterize the distribution of drawdown-related quantities so that investors can accurately assess the risk in their investment. The contributions of our research are mainly twofold. On the technical side, we have developed fast and accurate algorithms to compute the distribution of drawdown-related quantities that facilitate accurate risk assessment and derivative pricing. On the empirical side, we have underscored the importance of drawdown derivatives in protecting investors from extreme price movements. We expect the outputs of this project will equip financial market participants with computationally efficient tools to price and manage their drawdown risk.

14207119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207119.value: Cleaning, inspection and repairing of exterior walls/windows are the most common but difficult maintenance tasks of high-rise buildings. Existing solutions rely on human workers who are hung from the building top directly by a rope or via a cage, and hence put them in great dangers. A number of death accidents, happened last a few years, cause strong concerns on the operational safety. A solution is to replace the workers by a robot that performs the tasks while climbing the rope. There are several technical challenges in controlling a robot resting on or climbing a rope to perform a task. First, a rope is a deformable continuum not only with complicated dynamics but also with unknown dynamic parameters. It is not trivial to develop a dynamic model of the rope-manipulator system. Second, the motion of the robot, together with various disturbances, cause vibration of the rope and the system. It is a big challenge to design a controller that controls motion of the robot stably regardless of the vibration and disturbances. In this project, we will develop 1) a dynamic model of the rope-robot manipulator system, 2) a vision-based controller for controlling position and trajectory of the end-effector without using the model parameters of the rope, 3) an energy-based approach for analyzing the stability of the system, and 4) an experimental setup for validating the modeling method and the visual servo controller. The outputs of this project will not only advance the technology in robotics and automation but also have direct applications, e.g. wall cleaning of high-rise buildings, in Hong Kong. 高層大廈外牆與窗戶的清洗，維修等工作目前主要依賴人工完成，但高空作業不僅效率低，而且對工人非常危險，經常有死亡事故發生。用爬繩機械人代替工人完成這些高空作業是一個較好的解決方案，但技術上面臨多項挑戰。首先，機械人在高空懸挂繩子爬行的運動學和動力學都很難建模，其次機械人爬行時需要克服各種干擾和不確定性控制繩子的變形和振動。因此在高空懸挂繩子上爬行機械人的運動控制是一個難題，目前還沒有解決方法。本研究將1）建立一個爬繩機械人的動力學模型，2）設計一個不需要繩子變形參數的機器人運動視覺反饋控制器，3）利用能量方法分析系統的穩定性，及4）通過使用驗証所提出的方法。研究成果不僅推進機械人技術的發展而且在香港有直接的應用前景。

14207119.label: Realisation of objectives
14207119.value: (1) To develop the dynamic model of a robot manipulator climbing a rope: We have fully achieved this objective. We developed the dynamic model of the rope-manipulator system using the Lagrange equation based on the approximation of the deformation of the rope by two-dimensional springs. The dynamics of the rope-manipulator system interacting with the environment is also developed. To facilitate the controller design, we decoupled the dynamics of the system into the free subspace and the constrained subspace so that position control and force control can be realized independently in the two subspaces, respectively. The dynamic models were simulated using Matlab and an approach was developed for identifying the dynamic parameters. The dynamic model is the foundation for designing the motion controller and conducting the stability analysis. (2) To design a visual servoing controller for controlling motion of the end-effector of the robot manipulator without using the model parameters of the rope We have fully achieved this objective. While the rope-climbing robot offers superior vertical mobility, the deformation of the rope leads to technical challenges in designing controllers for motion and force control of the rope-manipulator system. The deformable nature of the rope results in the vibration of the base and hence positioning the end effector is challenging. In this project, we developed a novel adaptive vision-based controller for controlling motion of the end-effector of the robot manipulator mounted on the rope-climbing robot under the unknown vibration from the rope. The proposed controller guarantees the stable performance of the robot for two reasons. First, the control problem is directly formulated in the image space so that the exact spatial relationship between the moving base of the manipulator, i.e. the rope-climbing robot, and the target is not required. Second, a novel adaptation law was developed to estimate the vibration from the rope online and the vibrations are cancelled out in the robot control so as to stabilize the end effector as well as the entire system. (3) To analyse stability of the rope-manipulator system under control of the developed controller We have fully achieved this objective. To investigate the stability and robustness of the developed controllers, we have constructed energy-like functions and used Lyapunov theories to analyze the stabilities of the dynamic systems. We have rigorously proved the asymptotic stability and robustness of the visual servoing controllers based on the full closed-loop system dynamics. (4) To build a rope-climbing robot and carry out experimental validation of the modelling method and the vision-based controller. We have fully achieved this objective. We have built a prototype of the rope-manipulator system, which consists of a robot manipulator and a mobile base that climbs the rope. A novel climbing mechanism was invented to ensure reliable and energy-efficient climbing of the robot along the rope. The sensing system was also developed to measure the motion of the base and the interaction force between the robot and the environment. A vision system is installed to measure the position and orientation of the environment and to construct the 3D information of the working built environment as well. Novel algorithms have been developed to construct the 3D information of the working environment. Particularly, a novel sensor for 3D imaging of transparent objects like glass window was patented. Experiments in lab and field experiments for cleaning glass windows of a building were conducted to validate the sensing and control methods. The results demonstrated good potential of the developed rope-manipulator system in wall/glass window cleaning of high-rise buildings

14207119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207119.value: The project was completed according to the proposal and the major findings and research outcomes are summarized as follows: (1) We developed the dynamic model of the rope-manipulator system by approximating the deformation of the rope by two-dimensional springs, and the dynamic model of the system interacting with walls. The models were further employed to model rope manipulation using robot manipulators. The work led to one conference paper (Part C-9-1), and one journal paper submitted to the Advanced Intelligent Systems (Part C-8-5). (2) We built a prototype of the rope-manipulator system, which consists of a robot manipulator, a mobile base that climbs the rope, and a vision system. A compact rope-climbing mechanism was invented. The prototype was used to carry out the validation experiments. The work is included in the journal paper (Part C-8-6). (3) An adaptive vision-based controller was developed for the rope-manipulator system interacting with external environments such as windows, walls, etc. New vision-based methods were proposed to estimate and suppress the vibration of the base. Novel methods were also developed to estimate the pose of the objects to be manipulated. The work led to one conference paper (Part C-9-1), and two journal papers (Part C-8-2 and C-8-4). (4) Theoretical analysis was conducted on the stability of the rope-manipulator system under the control of the proposed visual servoing controller. Simulations and experiments were carried out experiments to verify the performance. The work led to one conference paper (C-9-1) and one journal paper submitted to the Advanced Intelligent Systems (Part C-8-5). (5) Since one potential application of the rope-manipulator system is glass windows cleaning of high-rise buildings, we investigated the 3D reconstruction of the working environment using vision. First, a new method is invented for 3D imaging of transparent objects like glass windows (see the patent). Second, a qusai-optimal and near-true real-time method was developed to estimate 3D information of parallel lines (edges) in the built environments whose distinguished features are parallel lines. An efficient method was also developed for accurate registration of the 3D information. The work led to two publications at IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (Part C-8-1 and C-8-3). Third, we conducted more investigations on robotic manipulation of soft objects, which led to one journal paper submitted to IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (Part C-8-6).

14207119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207119.value: Further development of the research could be carried out on the improvement of the flexibility, complexity, and accuracy of the manipulation control, and exploring potential applications of the technologies in building maintenance and smart manufacturing. Following are possible research topics: (1) Improving the robustness to noises and disturbances of the vision-based contact controller of the robot manipulator interacting with unknown surfaces like windows or walls of high-rise buildings; (2) Improving the accuracy in both position and force control of the controller; (3) 3D construction of large working environment using vision and vision-based on-line and offline planning of the robot manipulator for cleaning tasks of high-rise buildings; and (4) Exploration of potential applications such as wall cleaning of buildings.

14207119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207119.value: This project aimed at developing a novel rope-manipulator system and its advanced visual servoing controller for carrying out challenging tasks like windows/walls cleaning, inspection, etc. of high-rise buildings. The research outputs have great potential to be applied in building maintenance. In this project, we designed and built a rope-manipulator system composed of a novel rope-climbing robot and a robot manipulator with real-time vision system. The kinematics and dynamics models of the system have been developed and the adaptive visual servoing controller have been designed for controlling positions and forces of the end-effector of the rope-manipulator system interacting with exterior walls. Novel approaches were also developed to build the 3D model of the working environment using vision systems and to estimate the pose of the objects to be manipulated during the operations. Experiments were carried out to validate the approaches and field experiments for window cleaning were also conducted. The experiments demonstrated feasibility of the developed rope-manipulator system in carrying out the challenging widow-cleaning of high-rise buildings. The work led to publications of 6 papers in journals, 3 conference presentations, and a patent on 3D imaging of transparent objects. Further investigation could be improvement of the system for practical applications.

14207219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207219.value: With the advent of Big Data, sensor networks, and Internet of things (IoT), more and more data are being collected, processed, and analyzed in a routine manner. How to handle such a large volume of data in the communication network in terms of transmission and storage has become an imminent research problem. In Big Data applications, data are collected distributively over the network at a very high rate. Due to the limited communication bandwidth within the network and the limited storage at the intermediate nodes, it is not always possible to transmit this very large volume of data back to the collector node where the data are processed. Rather, it is desirable to perform part of the data processing inside the network, with the aim to reduce the data volume along the way. In a wireless sensor network, a large number of sensors are responsible for sensing the environment and reporting to a designated receiver node. Typically, the receiver node is not interested in all the data collected but only some relevant statistics of the data. For example, the maximum temperature detected by a sensor in a sensor network deployed in a forest may indicate the outbreak of a wildfire. Therefore, it is desirable to perform certain computation at the intermediate nodes to facilitate the receiver node to obtain the statistics of interest. In certain time-critical applications, this can also reduce the delay incurred by transmitting a lot of data in the network. The above application scenarios can be formulated as a network function computation problem. In such a problem, messages are generated at a set of nodes called the source nodes. These source nodes are connected to a designated sink node through a network. At the sink node, a mathematical function of the messages, called the target function, is computed. In the above example of a sensor network deployed in a forest, a temperature reading is taken at each source node every unit time, and the sink node needs to compute the maximum of the temperature readings at every time instance. In this project, we aim to tackle the fundamental information-theoretic problem of de- termining the network function computing capacity, namely the maximum average number of times the target function can be computed per use of the network. This study will have the long-term impact of reducing the need of storing and transmitting a lot of data in the Internet. 伴隨著大數據、傳感器網絡、以及物聯網時代的到來，需要對越來越多的數據進行提取、處理和分析。由於通信網絡上傳輸和存儲的限制，如何在通信網絡中處理這些海量數據成為一個迫切的研究問題。 在大數據應用中，海量的數據在網絡上以較高的速率被分佈式地提取出來。由於網絡中信道的傳輸帶寬和結點的存儲容量的限制，將全部海量原始數據傳輸到中心結點處再統一進行數據處理往往是不可行的。因此，我們渴望在網絡內部對數據進行部分處理以減少網絡上數據的傳輸量，從而提高網絡效率。 在無線傳感器網絡中，大量部署的傳感器會用來感應所處環境的某些指標並發送給指定的接收結點。通常，接收結點所關心的並不是採集到的數據本身，而是這些數據的某些相關統計信息。例如，在森林中會部署大量傳感器用來採集環境溫度以檢測森林火災，那麼接收結點所關心的並不是所有傳感器採集到的環境溫度，而是這些溫度中的最大值從而判斷是否存在森林火情。因此，我們渴望在網絡內部結點上進行特定的計算使得接收結點能夠更加高效地獲得其所需要的統計信息。此外，在某些時間敏感的應用中，網絡函數計算亦能夠降低由傳輸大量數據所帶來的時間延遲。 上述應用場景都可以用網絡函數計算問題來描述。在這個問題中，網絡中的多個信源結點生成數據消息。這些信源結點通過網絡連接到一個指定的接收結點。該接收結點需要計算這些數據消息的一個數學函數，稱其為目標函數。在上述例子，在森林中部署一個傳感器網絡，每個信源結點在每個單位時間對溫度進行一次測量，接收結節點需要計算傳感器每次測量溫度的最大值。 在本項目中，我們旨在確定該網絡函數的計算容量這個基本信息論問題，其中網絡函數的計算容量指平均每使用一次網絡可以計算目標函數的最大次數。在互聯網中，對於減少傳輸和存儲大量數據有著重大需求，這項研究將對其產生長期的積極影響。

14207219.label: Realisation of objectives
14207219.value: Objective 1: To identify problems in network function computation that are analytically tractable. Status: Full achieved We put forward secure network function computation over a directed acyclic network. In such a network, the sink node is required to compute a target function of which the inputs are generated as source messages at multiple source nodes, while a wiretapper is not allowed to obtain any information about a security function of the source messages. The characterization of the secure computing capacity is in general overwhelmingly difficult. Thus, we consider the special case that the target function is a linear function and the security function is the identity function (i.e., the source messages need to be protected from the wiretapper). Objective 2: To design coding schemes for problems identified in Objective 1 that approach the network function computing capacity. Status: Full achieved We present a construction of linear function-computing secure network codes and obtain a lower bound on the secure computing capacity. We also give some sufficient conditions for the tightness of the lower bound in terms of the network topology. With this lower bound and the upper bound we have obtained (Objective 3), the secure computing capacity for some classes of secure models can be fully characterized. Objective 3: To obtain upper bounds on the network function computing capacity for problems identified in Objective 1 and for general problems. Status: Full achieved We have proved an upper bound on the secure computing capacity, which is applicable to arbitrary network topologies and arbitrary security levels.

14207219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207219.value: We put forward secure network function computation over a directed acyclic network. In such a network, a sink node is required to compute with zero error a target function of which the inputs are generated as source messages at multiple source nodes, while a wiretapper, who can access any one but not more than one wiretap set in a given collection of wiretap sets, is not allowed to obtain any information about a security function of the source messages. The secure computing capacity for the above model is defined as the maximum average number of times that the target function can be securely computed with zero error at the sink node with the given collection of wiretap sets and security function for one use of the network. The characterization of this capacity is in general overwhelmingly difficult. In this project, we consider securely computing linear functions with a wiretapper who can eavesdrop any subset of edges up to a certain size r, referred to as the security level, with the security function being the identity function. We first prove an upper bound on the secure computing capacity, which is applicable to arbitrary network topologies and arbitrary security levels. This upper bound depends on the network topology and security level. Furthermore, we obtain an upper bound and a lower bound on this bound, which are both in closed form. In particular, when the security level r is equal to 0, our upper bound reduces to the computing capacity without security consideration. Also, we discover the surprising fact that for some models, there is no penalty on the secure computing capacity compared with the computing capacity without security consideration. Furthermore, we obtain an equivalent expression of the upper bound by using a graph-theoretic approach, and accordingly we develop an efficient approach for computing this bound. On the other hand, we present a construction of linear function-computing secure network codes and obtain a lower bound on the secure computing capacity. By our code construction, for the linear function which is over a given finite field, we can always construct a (vector-) linear function-computing secure network code over the same field. We also give some sufficient conditions for the tightness of the lower bound in terms of the network topology.

14207219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207219.value: We have introduced a new class of network function computation problems with security considerations and obtained some results for the special case that the target function is a linear function of the source messages and the security function is the identity function. There are many other meaningful cases that can be considered. For example, in an ongoing work, instead of being the identity function, we consider the interesting case that the security function is the target function.

14207219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207219.value: Function computation is about computing the value of a function with possibly multiple inputs. In the classical setting, all the inputs are available at the location where the computation is performed. In the case that the inputs are generated at different nodes in a communication network, instead of transmitting all the inputs to the "destination node" where the value of the function is needed and performing the computation there, it is more efficient to utilize the communication network to compute the function in a distributed manner. The advantage of this approach is that it is in general not necessary to transmit all the inputs to the destination node, thus saving the communication bandwidth required for the function computation. This is referred to as network function computation. In this project, we introduced a new class of network coding function problems with security considerations. In such a problem, there are wiretappers who can wiretap certain communication links in the network. We need to design the network function computation scheme with suitable security measures. We obtained different characterizations on the maximum rate at which the function can be securely computed by the network when the function is linear.
