14207319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207319.value: The objective of this project is to develop novel cyclic generative models and novel algorithmic frameworks based on cyclic generative models to learn disentangled feature representations for different vision tasks, including image recognition and domain adaption. Learning disentangled feature representations with deep neural networks draws increasing attention in recent years. Such algorithms do not only require learning discriminative features but also aim at "distilling" key and vital feature representations from task-unrelated information in the data. For instance, for person recognition, the key disentangled features should capture the clothes appearances of different persons and be distilled from other task-unrelated features that encode person poses, camera viewing angles, and image background. For domain adaption, the feature disentanglement algorithms should encode the key features representing the image contents while separating them from other domain-specific information, such as color styles, image resolutions, and camera angles. By learning to disentangle task-related representations from task-unrelated information, more robust and dsicriminative feature representations could be obtained to achieve more accurate image recognition performance. Other vision applications, such as image manipulation and image-to-image translation, could also be improved with the disentangled visual features. Cyclic generative models, including CycleGAN and its variants, were originally proposed to tackle the image translation problem between multiple image domains. However, the forward and backward image translators could only receive partial and indirect supervisions from the cyclic generation process. To solve the problem, we propose to design novel generative models based on flow-based cyclic generative models. Unlike CycleGAN and its variants, the proposed flow-based generative models are naturally invertible, i.e., the inverse of a domain A-to-B translator is naturally a B-to-A backward translator. The commonly used image reconstruction loss (cycle-consistency loss) in existing CycleGAN-based methods would therefore no longer be needed. Such a novel cyclic generative model would be much easier to train and avoid image blurs brought by the reconstruction loss. Based on the cyclic generative models, we propose a novel denoising identity-disentangled feature learning framework for person recognition, and a novel framework to learn domain-disentangled feature representations for domain adaption. The key novelty is to integrate auxiliary identity-switching and domain-switching image generation tasks into the end-to-end learning frameworks for enforcing learning disentangled feature representations. The outcome of this research will have significant impact on cyclic generative models, disentangled feature learning, image recognition, and domain adaption. It will also provide powerful tools for related vision tasks, including image manipulation and image-to-image translation. 該項目旨在研發新穎的循環式生成模型以及新穎的基於循環式生成模型的特徵表達解耦算法框架，這類算法框架可以被應用於各類計算機視覺任務，包括圖像識別以及領域自適應問題等。近年來，基於深度神經網絡學習解構特徵表達獲得了廣泛的關注。這類算法不僅要求獲得的特徵表達是有著強辨別力的，同時也能夠從數據任務無關的信息中中解耦和獲取任務相關的特徵表達。例如，在行人衝識別的問題中，獲取的特徵表達應該能夠捕獲不同人物的衣物外觀，同時將其與任務無關信息（如人體姿態、攝像機角度、圖像背景等）解耦分離。在領域自適應問題中，特徵解耦算法應該能夠捕獲圖像內容中與圖像領域無關的信息，如顏色風格、圖像分辨率、攝像機角度等。通過學習從任務無關的信息中解耦出任務相關的特徵表達，能夠獲得更魯棒和更具有辨識力的圖像特徵表達來增強圖像識別的性能。其他的視覺應用，如圖像編輯與圖圖翻譯，也能夠受益於解耦特徵表達。循環式生成模型（包括CycleGAN及其變種）最初被提出用於解決多領域的圖像翻譯問題。但是，前向與後向的圖像翻譯器只能從循環生成的過程中獲取非直接的監督信號。為了解決這個問題，本項目提出設計基於Flow模型的循環式生成模型。不同於CycleGAN及其變種，提出的基於Flow模型的生成模型是天然可逆的。現有CycleGAN中傳統的圖像重構損失函數不再需要。這種新穎的循環式生成模型更容易訓練也能夠更好的避免圖像重構損失函數所帶來的生成圖像模糊問題。基於這種循環式生成模型，我們也提出一種針對行人衝識別問題，新穎的身份解構特徵表達學習框架，以及一種面向領域特徵解構的領域自適應算法。該項目核心的創新點是如何將輔助的身份交替和領域交替的圖像生成過程整合到端到端的學習框架中來增強解耦特徵表達的學習。該項目的成果能夠極大的促進循環式生成網絡、解耦特徵學習、圖像識別以及圖像自適應等領域，也能夠為相關的計算機視覺任務，如圖像編輯和圖圖翻譯提供強有力的算法工具。

14207319.label: Realisation of objectives
14207319.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have developed deep neural networks with cyclic generative models to learn identity-disentangled feature representations for person recognition. There were previous methods using image-to-image translation to create additional training samples for improving the training of deep learning models. However, The inter-sample relations are not well maintained. We argue that maintaining intersample relations during image-to-image translation (generation) is critical for generating informative training samples, which cannot be effectively regularized by identity-based regularization in previous methods. To tackle this challenge, we propose an end-to-end structured domain adaptation (SDA) framework with a novel online relation-consistency regularization term. It consists of a structured domain-translation network, a source-domain person image encoder and a target-domain encoder. The structured domain-translation network generates the source-to-target translated images, which can benefit the training of the target domain encoder. At the same time, two domains’ encoders are coupledly trained to model inter-sample relations on the fly, which regularizes the training of the domain-translation network. A novel relation-consistency loss is proposed to regularize the training of source-to-target domain translation for maintaining the original inter-sample relations, which are generated by the source-domain encoder on-the-fly. Our proposed method is able to effectively maintain their original inter-sample relations during translation via the proposed structured domain-translation network and relation-consistency loss. (2) We have developed deep neural networks with cyclic generative models to learn domain-disentangled feature representations for domain adaption. Previous methods on domain adaptive recognition generally follow a two-stage training scheme. In stage 2, a pseudo-label-based paradigm is used to alternate between generating pseudo classes by clustering and cyclic generation target-domain instances and training the network with generated pseudo classes. We propose a hybrid memory to encode all available information from both source and target domains for feature learning. A cyclic generative model is utilized to transform feature representations back and forth between the different domains. For the source-domain data, their ground-truth class labels can naturally provide valuable supervisions. For the target-domain data, clustering can be conducted to obtain relatively confident clusters as well as un-clustered outliers. All the source-domain class centroids, target-domain cluster centroids, and target-domain un-clustered instance features from the hybrid memory can provide supervisory signals for jointly learning discriminative feature representations across the two domains. A unified framework is developed for dynamically updating and distinguishing different entries in the proposed hybrid memory. We propose a self-paced contrastive learning strategy, which initializes the learning process by using the hybrid memory with the most reliable target-domain clusters. Trained with such reliable clusters, the discriminativeness of feature representations can be gradually improved and additional reliable clusters can be formed by incorporating more un-clustered instances into the new clusters. Such a strategy can effectively mitigate the effects of noisy pseudo labels and boost the feature learning process. Our unsupervised version without labeled source-domain data on object re-ID task significantly outperforms state-of-the-arts methods by over 10% accuracy on multiple benchmarks. (3) We have extended the developed algorithms for tackling the problem of partial point cloud completion, we propose to create a unified and structured latent space for encoding both partial and complete shapes. To apply strong supervisions for unsupervised point cloud completion via cyclic generation between partial point clouds of different occlusion levels, we make an assumption that each partial shape is created by occluding a complete one. If a complete shape is occluded to become partial in the 3D space, its code in the latent space should also be “occluded” from a complete shape code accordingly. We model the “occlusion” of a complete code in the latent space as weighting each of its feature dimensions. However, instead of manually determining the occlusion weights, we make them learned from the training data. In this way, the complete and partial shapes are strongly bounded in a unified latent space. In addition, to better regularize the relation between partial point clouds from the same complete shape, the occlusion code of a more occluded shape is required to have smaller weights than that of a less occluded shape.

IEEE Transactions on Neural Network and Learning Systems is one of the top journals in machine learning. CVPR/ECCV/NeurlPS are the top conferences on computer vision and machine learning. In this project, we proposed Structured Domain Adaptation (SDA) method (Part C.8, J1) to we proposed an end-to-end structured domain adaptation framework with an online relation-consistency regularization term. Our proposed framework is shown to achieve state-of-the-art performance on multiple Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) tasks. In (Part C.8, C7), we proposed a novel self-paced contrastive learning framework with hybrid memory for domain adaptive object re-ID. The hybrid memory dynamically generates source-domain class-level, target-domain cluster-level and un-clustered instance-level supervisory signals for learning feature representations. Our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods on multiple domain adaptation tasks of object re-ID and even boosts the performance on the source domain without any extra annotations. In StereoGAN (Part C.8, C1), we proposed an end-to-end deep learning framework consisting of domain translation and stereo matching networks to estimate stereo disparity on the target domain, using only source-domain synthetic stereo image pairs with ground-truth disparity and target-domain real stereo image pairs without any annotation. 14207319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207319.value: In this project, we found that cyclic generative neural networks can help the deep learning models to overcome the issues of domain gaps when learning from data of multiple domains. The proposed cyclic generative models and strategies can be integrated into existing networks in an end-to-end manner, which shows that it can be more widely used in other topics beyond person recognition and image classification. The technique can also be extended to solve domain gaps in NLP problems by adopting text-to-text style transfer models as the data-translation model. We will continue to work along this direction.

14207419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207419.value: Centrifugation is a common technique for material separation based on density difference. Yet for many decades, the design of a centrifuge has always been the same – a spinning rotor that drives sample holder tubes around at high speeds. Despite the recent introduction of Analytical Ultra-Centrifugation (AUC), all current centrifugation systems are “passive” devices. There is no provision to change any parameter during centrifugation, let alone the capability to perform in situ experiments. This project proposes to develop a new class of centrifugation devices based on the “lab-in-a-tube (LabTube)” concept. Optofluidic chips compatible with common sample holders serve as the workbench for conducting experiments inside commercial ultra-centrifuge systems. We specifically aim to develop several key functional blocks for the LabTube platform, namely wireless-controlled opto-mechatronics for real-time actuation and sample processing, an integrated optical microscope for capturing image responses from the sample, optofluidic microfluidics for conducting bioassays. LabTube is potentially a disruptive approach for conducting bioanalysis experiments. With the combined merits of extreme g-force centrifugation, on-chip reconfigurable microfluidics and real-time response capture, this approach offers users the freedom of varying experimental conditions fundamental to biological reactions. As demonstration application examples, we shall develop LabTube modules to (i) monitor shifting of cell elasticity, which is an essential cell physiology indicator, when exposed to different chemicals, (ii) perform on-chip fluorescent imaging that enables in situ monitoring of cell responses when internal organelles are being “stretched”, (iii) control fluidic operations during centrifugation for accurate on-demand fractionation of precipitated reaction products, (vi) perform exploration of g-force actuated nanopore DNA sequencing. For the last objective of DNA sequencing, we propose to use g-forces for driving the target ssDNA through a sampling nanopore. Currently all reported cases are based on electrical actuation. Sequencing is achieved by monitoring electrical current fluctuations as a target ssDNA passes through the nanopore. This approach is inherently single-channel. Multi-channel operation is fundamentally impossible because the electrolytes on either side of the nanopore have shunted all currents from individual channels. The proposed g-force approach completely removes the need of electrolytes. With the nanopores fabricated in 2-D materials such as graphene, one can readily measure fluctuations of electrical conductance in a transverse direction independently for each nanopore. This will deliver the goal of parallel sequencing of multiple ssDNAs simultaneously. Successful demonstration of this objective will greatly enhance sequencing capacity, hence bringing us closer to the “$1000 Genome” target, which is being pursuit intensely everywhere. 離心是基於密度差異的材料分離的常用技術。然而幾十年來，離心機的設計始終都是一個旋轉的轉子，可以高速驅動樣品架管。儘管最近引入了分析超離心（AUC），但所有目前的離心系統都是“被動”裝置。沒有規定在離心過程中改變任何參數，也沒有進行原位實驗的能力。 此項目提出基於“實驗室管（LabTube）”概念開發一種新型離心裝置。與普通樣品架兼容的光流控芯片可作為在商用超離心機系統內進行實驗的工作台。我們專門為LabTube平台開發了幾個關鍵功能模塊，即用於實時驅動和样品處理的無線控制光機電一體化，用於捕獲樣品圖像響應的集成光學顯微鏡，用於進行生物測定的光流體微流體。 憑藉極端g-force離心，片上可重構微流體和實時響應捕獲的綜合優勢，該方法為用戶提供了對生物反應基本不同的實驗條件的自由。作為示範應用實例，我們將開發LabTube模塊，以（i）監測細胞彈性的變化，這是一種必不可少的細胞生理學指標，當暴露於不同的化學物質時，（ii）進行片上熒光成像，實現細胞的原位監測當內部細胞器被“拉伸”時的響應，（iii）在離心期間控制流體操作以精確按需分級沉澱的反應產物，（vi）進行g力驅動的納米孔DNA測序的探索。 對於DNA測序的最後一個目標，我們建議使用g力通過採樣納米孔驅動目標ssDNA。目前，所有報告的病例均基於電致動。當靶標ssDNA通過納米孔時，通過監測電流波動來實現測序。這種方法本質上是單通道的。多通道操作基本上是不可能的，因為納米孔兩側的電解質分流來自各個通道的所有電流。所提出的g力方法完全消除了對電解質的需求。利用諸如石墨烯的2-D材料製造的納米孔，可以容易地針對每個納米孔測量橫向上的電導率的波動。這將實現同時對多個ssDNA進行平行測序的目標。成功證明這一目標將大大提高測序能力，從而使我們更接近“1000美元基因組”目標。

14207419.label: Realisation of objectives
14207419.value: Overall, the project has been largely successful in addressing it objectives in the context of using inertial kinetic forces to perform actuation of molecules or biological objects. The major issue, which is yet to be resolved within the limitation of hardware resources, is to get the electronics to operate for sufficiently long period of time under ultra high g-force conditions. The highest spinning speed that we have been able to achieve without causing long-term damage of the electronic components, particularly the camera module, is 33,000 rpm, which corresponds to 41,000 g-forces. Nonetheless, below this spinning speed limit, the project has produced considerable amount of experimental data to successfully demonstrate several highly innovative lab-in-a-tube instrumentation ideas. For Objective 1 and 2, this project has produced a fully functional lab-in-a-tube system, which has real-time data communication for interactive control, image transmission for in-tube microscopy, electrical data capture, change of sample orientation and sample heating for DNA amplification. The work is summarised in project output entitled “Lab-in-a-Tube: A portable imaging spectrophotometer for cost-effective, high-throughput, and label-free analysis of centrifugation processes”. For Objective 3, we have spent considerable amount of time to optimise the temperature field of a 3-zone in-tube microfluidic chip, and its simultaneous operation with an in-tube stepper motor system and a microscope camera, so that a droplet of DNA sample can undergo temperature cycling and hence amplification of target DNA. We have finally completed a prototype to perform such tasks and the system can also quantify amplification by measuring fluorescence intensity using the in-tube blue LED working simultaneously with a miniaturised fluorescence microscope. For Objective 4, the project has been able to generate a large amount of experimental data to demonstrate the operation of a novel inertial force-actuated nanopore-based single molecule detection technique. For the intellectual elements of the hardware system, which includes a new photon-inhibited anisotropic wet etching technique for the fabrication of a funnel-shaped nanopore in silicon, inertial force actuation of single molecules through the nanopore in a sequential manner, and modulation of single molecule translocation current blockade pulses using an external light source, are all previously not reported in the literature. We have used the system to differentiate different types of single molecules such as proteins, metallic nanoparticles, carbon nanotubes and organic macromolecules by monitoring the pulse shapes. The effort has generated one manuscript submitted to Nature Communication, which is currently undergoing a second review cycle (i.e. high chance of being accepted), one manuscript submitted to Advanced Materials, and one US patent. Within this project, we have also explored the use of image processing with deep learning for high-speed visual classification of droplet-based single-cell micro-reactors. The work has led to the publication of a paper entitled “Deep-qGFP: A Generalist Deep Learning Assisted Pipeline for Accurate Quantification of Green Fluorescent Protein Labeled Biological Samples in Microreactors” in Small Methods.

14207419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207419.value: Major findings include: 1) Successful demonstrate of a lab-in-a-tube system that can be readily fitted inside a common centrifuge tube with the built-in functionalities of real-time capture and transmission of image and electrical signals, simultaneous changing of sample orientation on-demand, and DNA amplification and signal monitoring through temperature cycling and sample transfer between heating zones. 2) A new photon-assisted techniques for preparing a funnel-shaped nanopore in silicon. 3) Successful demonstration of using the lab-in-a-tube system for nanopore-based single molecule analysis and characterisation through monitoring the shape of the current blockade pulses.

14207419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207419.value: The inertial force actuation approach established through this project has very high potential to be further developed into a commercial method for conducting single molecule analysis, and might eventually lead to single DNA sequencing, which is currently being researched intensely worldwide. A unique advantage of inertial force actuation is the decoupling of generation of current blockade pulses and actuation of molecules, as all existing approaches are using electrical energy to perform both operations simultaneously. The project team is currently in the process of preparing proposals to secure more funding for further improvement of the prototype in terms of gaining comprehensive understanding of the underlining physics of the translocation events and the formation of the corresponding current blockade pulses, nanopore fabrication accuracy, resolution of molecular size and the introduction of new functional features to the nanopore in light of its unique funnel shape.

14207419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207419.value: The common centrifuge is an indispensable tool in almost every biology and chemistry laboratory for separating different components in a liquid. However, currently centrifugation is entirely a passive technique. The user is confined to a "trial and error" mode of operation. This project aims to address this issue through the development of an "active" centrifugation tube. The so-called lab-in-a-tube device offers smart operational options including real-time capture of image and sample characteristics, change of centrifugation direction and heating of sample. The user will be able to perform real-time monitoring of the sample while it undergoes centrifugation. This project has also successfully demonstrated a new type of nanopore-based single molecule analysis technique with the molecules under investigation being moved around purely by centrifugal force instead of the conventional electro-kinetic energy.

14207619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207619.value: Building a task-oriented dialog system that can help human users achieve their intents/goals through natural interactions is a challenging problem. It requires accurate natural language understanding to extract semantics from the user’s input. The system must also track dialog states to follow the thread of semantic reasoning throughout multi-turn interactions. Additionally, the system must infer the user’s goal and take relevant actions to complete the intended task. Task-oriented dialog modeling is often formulated as a slot-filling problem – where a domain-specific semantic frame with information slots is filled over the course of the dialog, and the (partially) filled semantic frame at each turn characterizes the dialog state. The semantic frame encodes the user’s goal and extracted attributes for actions such as database access. However, slot-filling mostly uses supervised learning and requires sizeable, semantically annotated corpora, which is expensive to obtain. This limits the scalability of the approach. Another newly emerged approach, called sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) modeling, learns question-response mappings from unlabeled dialog corpora using neural networks. The corpora are often created from popular text-based instant messengers and online services. Seq2seq offers scalability by training on unlabeled data, but lacks explicit semantic structure for describing user goals or informational attributes. This affects the transparency and interpretability of the process of dialog evolution. We propose to develop the Convex Polytopic Model (CPM) for scalable and interpretable data-driven task-oriented dialog modeling, that can train on datasets with minimal annotations. CPM applies unsupervised learning to generate a knowledge representation from text. It projects the textual data into a latent semantic space as a point set and generates a compact convex polytope to enclose all points. The polytopic vertices represent extracted semantic concepts. We propose to transform the CPM for dialog modeling by generating a polytope to encompass the user’s task-oriented goals and dialog states. Each user input will be “understood” as a semantic representation, which is a sequence of polytopic vertices. Dialog state transitions in multi-turn dialogs will be represented by a sequence of vertex sequences. We can use semi-supervised methods to align the polytopic vertices with semantic labels from data annotations. The CPM can thus model dialog semantics, with interpretability enhanced by the polytope’s geometry. The sequence of vertex sequences representing dialog state transitions can use reinforcement learning to derive the optimal dialog policy. This will improve performance of task-oriented dialog systems in virtual assistants, chatbots, etc., that are rapidly gaining widespread use globally. 構建一個旨在通過自然交互幫助用戶實現其意圖或目標的任務導向型對話系統，是一個具有挑戰性的問題。它要求通過自然語言理解技術從用戶的輸入中提取準確的語義信息。系統還必須跟蹤對話狀態，以便在多輪對話中遵循語義推理的線索。此外,該系統必須預估用戶的目標並採取相應操作來完成預期任務。任務導向型對話模型通常被定義化為插槽填充問題，即在對話過程中填充具有信息槽的特定領域的語義框架，而在每一輪對話中，（部分）已被填充的語義框架代表著當前對話狀態。語義框對用戶的目標進行編碼，並為諸如數據庫訪問之類的操作提取屬性。然而，插槽填充主要使用監督學習並且需要價格昂貴，規模龐大，語義註釋的語料庫，從而限制了方法的可擴展性。另一種新出現的序列到序列（seq2seq）模型使用神經網絡從未標記的對話語料庫中學習問題 – 回應映射。這些語料庫通常是根據普遍流行的基於文本的即時消息平台和在線服務創建的。 Seq2seq通過訓練未標記數據來提供可擴展性，但缺乏用於描述用戶目標或信息屬性的明確語義結構，從而影響對話演變過程的透明度和可解釋性。我們提出開發凸多面體模型（CPM），其用於可擴展和可解釋的數據驅動的面向任務的對話模型，可以訓練具有最少註釋的數據集。 CPM應用無監督學習從文本生成知識表示。它將文本數據作為點集，投影到潛在的語義空間，並生成一個包含所有點的緊湊的凸多面體。多面體頂點表示提取的語義概念。我們提出通過生成包含用戶的任務導向性目標和對話狀態的多面體來轉換CPM以進行對話建模。每個用戶輸入將被“理解”為語義表示，其是多面體頂點的序列。多輪對話中的對話狀態轉換將由一系列頂點序列表示。我們可以使用半監督方法將多面體頂點與數據註釋中的語義標籤對應。因此，CPM可以對對話語義進行建模，並通過多面的幾何特性增強可解釋性。表示對話狀態轉換的頂點序列的序列可以使用強化學習來導出最優對話策略。這將提高任務導向性對話系統在虛擬助手，聊天機器人等正迅速得到全球廣泛使的設備中的性能。

14207819.value: Develop a target-oriented distributionally robust optimization framework by designing a class of target-oriented decision criteria. The proposed decision criteria should satisfy a set of normative properties and capture the impact of target. In addition, they should be easily evaluated and optimized in distributionally robust optimization problem. Develop algorithms to effectively solve the proposed target-oriented distributionally robust optimization problem over continuous decision variables. For the more challenging target-oriented distributionally robust optimization problem where the decision variables are discrete, we also explore efficient methods to find the optimal solutions. Apply the theoretical results on certain operations management problems where targets are playing a key role, and hence the applicability and effectiveness of the proposed framework can be illustrated.

14207819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207819.value: It is widely believed that meeting or missing financial targets is a key performance metric for firms. In this project, we aim to incorporate the impact of target into the distributionally robust optimization framework, which has been recently popularized for decision making under only limited information on distribution. Specifically, we extend from Value at Risk (VaR), the ubiquitous monetary risk measure. VaR is defined as a threshold loss value such that the loss from the risky position exceeding that threshold is with probability at a given level. Nevertheless, it fails to provide any performance guarantee on other probability levels, which is also a critical concern in many decision making processes. In addition, due to its property of Translation Invariance, VaR would decompose the target from the uncertain target premium and hence we cannot capture the impact of target by optimizing VaR. Nevertheless, VaR still receives extensive attention in both academic research and industrial application due to its attractive properties which include Monotonicity and Positive Homogeneity. Inspired by VaR, we plan to develop a class of decision criteria which can encompass a range of quantile values in evaluating uncertain loss with respect to a prespecified target. The proposed decision criteria are expected to 1) satisfy certain desirable normative properties such as stochastic dominance, 2) allow us to specify the probability bounds of losses exceeding thresholds at all levels, and 3) bring no significantly extra burden on distributionally robust optimization. We will then explore effective algorithms to optimize the proposed decision criteria. We plan to consider both optimization problem over continuous decision variables and that over discrete decision variables. For the former case, we show in our preliminary results that under a special case, the optimal solution can be solved from a second order cone programming problem. For the latter case, we demonstrate that the optimal solution can be found using a bisection search method. After the theoretical exploration, we also plan to apply the theoretical framework to several practical operations management problems, such as the shortest path problem and patient scheduling problem. 能否達到預期的收入/利潤目標被普遍認為是商業公司的一個關鍵運營指標。在本項目中，我們希望把此目標對運營管理之影響結合到分佈魯棒優化的框架中去。分佈魯棒優化是研究如何在僅有不完整的隨機分佈信息下做決策的方法，在過去二十年里變得日益重要。具體而言，本項目將從風險價值（Value at Risk，也就是VaR）出發。風險價值被定義為在給定置信區間內的最大潛在損失，是一個經典的風險測度。然而，風險價值並不能在其他任何的置信區間內給出損失額度的保證或者是其他刻畫，而這其實正是很多決策過程中的一個關鍵考慮因素。此外，由於其具有平移不變性，風險價值在考慮與目標相對應的風險時會簡單的把目標剝離開，從而無法通過優化風險價值以達到考慮目標之影響的目的。然而，由於其一些直觀可靠的特性（如單調性或一次齊次性等），風險價值依然在學術界及工業應用上都受到了廣泛關注。受到風險價值的啟發，我們計劃提出一組新的決策準則，使之可以概括在一系列置信區間內的所有相關於預設目標的最大損失額度。所提出的決策準則應當具有以下三個特點。首先，它滿足一系列理所當然的範式的性質，如隨機優勢；第二，它應使得我們可以在所有的置信區間內都知道預期損失額度的界限；第三，它不應該為分佈魯棒優化帶來計算上的額外負擔。基於此決策準則，我們會設計有效算法來做分佈魯棒優化。我們計劃把此框架應用到連續優化問題以及離散優化問題。對於前者，在前期研究中，我們證明了在某些特殊情況下，最優解可以通過解決一個二階錐規劃問題而得到。對於後者，我們發現了最優解可以通過二分法來查找。在以上的理論探索后，我們也計劃把所提出了理論框架應用到幾個具體的運營管理問題上，例如最短路問題以及病人排期問題等。

14207819.label: Realisation of objectives
14207819.value: All the four objectives are completed. The details are as follows. 1. We have developed a general target-oriented distributionally robust optimization making framework. Specifically, we propose a new distributionally robust optimization framework such that by using the targets, we can incorporate all probability distributions, rather than only those in a given ball as in the traditional distributionally robust optimization setting. 2. We show that with the newly proposed target-oriented distributionally robust optimization framework, those with continuous decision variables (such as linear programming problem) can be solved with a similar level of complexity. 3. For more challenging problems, such as those with discrete decision variables or two-stage optimization problem, we have also developed corresponding algorithms for the newly proposed optimization framework. 4. We apply our new framework and algorithm on a number of applications, such as portfolio optimization, network lot-sizing problem, capacity management problem in project management. The computational results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of our work.

14207819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207819.value: We introduce a new concept of distributionally robust optimization. In contrast to the conventional framework that only takes into account the impact of probability distributions within a pre-defined ambiguity set, our methodology guarantees performance across all probability distributions. Our goal is to maximize robustness relative to a set target, allowing for any possible probability distributions. Utilizing this new paradigm, we reassess a variety of traditional optimization problems, including linear programming, two-stage optimization, and discrete optimization. We devise corresponding solution techniques for all these problems, maintaining similar computational costs as the traditional optimization framework. Following this, we implement our innovative optimization framework and algorithms in various scenarios, such as portfolio optimization, network lot sizing, and project management capacity management. Our computational results validate the efficiency of our contributions.

14207819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207819.value: Going forward, we are highly interested in applying our proposed framework to a broader range of applications. A compelling example would be exploring the multi-period decision-making problem. Its practical significance and computational challenges, especially due to the "curse of dimensionality," are widely acknowledged. The presence of ambiguity in probability distributions undoubtedly adds to the complexity of the multi-period decision-making problem, resulting in limited research on its robust optimization version. However, our new paradigm opens the door to revisit this issue and implement it in numerous practical applications, such as multi-period inventory control.

14207819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207819.value: Uncertainties are pervasive across all facets of life, including operations management. The mishandling of these uncertainties can result in ineffective solutions, leading to subpar business operations. In our project, we are introducing a novel paradigm for optimization under uncertainties, with applicability across a wide range of business contexts, such as portfolio optimization, project management, logistics, and supply chain management. Our unique approach to this new paradigm involves considering a target and enhancing the robustness in relation to this target, even as the actual uncertainties may adhere to any potential distribution patterns. After theoretically establishing our paradigm, we put it to the test along with the related solution algorithms. Our findings highlight the superiority of our methods.

The application of the proposed technique to the design of practical antenna arrays;

14207919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14207919.value: Wireless communication has become an essential element of our daily lives. The current 4G technology provides ubiquitous communication with data-rate of tens of M-bit/s. In practice, this magnitude of transmission speed is usually not attainable due to interference, multi-path effect as well as polarization loss. In modern communication systems, adaptability to ever-changing environment is therefore an important feature for enhanced performance, size and cost reduction. For instance, in the field of mobile communication, antenna diversity (e.g. frequency, pattern, polarization) may be applied to combat complex radio-wave propagation issues. Moreover, it is proven that MIMO (Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) technology can create multiple channels to substantially increase system capacity and spectrum efficiency. However, in practice, the effect of mutual coupling between closely-spaced antenna elements can severely degrade the overall system performance. Besides, the deployment of MIMO technology in commercial systems is largely prohibited by design complexity and cost factors. This project aims to develop advanced MIMO antenna technology for current 4G and upcoming 5G mobile systems. To address the above issues, novel antenna system with both port isolation and pattern reconfigurable capabilities are exploited for the enhancement of channel capacity and reliability under complex and dynamic multi-path environment. This research also attempts to develop low cost solution with compact size and simple structure. In the long run, the research outcomes are expected to have a high impact on the design of mobile handsets and terminals for future wireless applications.

14207919.label: Realisation of objectives
14207919.value: This project has investigated the design of MIMO antenna with port isolation and beamforming capabilities. Six new design ideas have been proposed including the use of different radiation modes for cancellation of mutual coupling associated with closely spaced antenna elements. For example, by the proper shaping (meandering) of printed dipole pair, both parallel and collinear coupling modes (J1) can be created for the enhancement of port isolation by more than 20dB. Printed-dipole antennas are adopted here as they are easy to implement and can radiate almost in all directions (wide coverage). Besides, they can be made (by meandering) to fit the very limited space available. Since the radiating elements are fed using coaxial cables, the antennas can be placed far away from the main circuit board, if deemed necessary. Mobile terminals and wireless access points (e.g., routers) are potential applications. This new method overcomes both mutual coupling and space issues without any bulky decoupling structures (highly undesirable in terms of size constraint and design flexibility). For verification, antenna arrays operating at 2.45 GHz have been fabricated and characterized. Good agreement between the simulated and measured results has been observed. Improvement in efficiency (>80%), port isolation (>20 dB), ECC (<0.05), and impedance bandwidth (>100 MHz) has been demonstrated. Alternately, modified patch antenna has been introduced (J2) to generate two distinct radiation modes for the decoupling of a 2x2 MIMO system. Cancellation of mutual coupling is accomplished by the introduction of additional coupling paths. When compared to conventional decoupling approaches, the new coupling path is created by the novel patch design, without the need of external scattering structures. For the first time, self-generated mixed radiation modes are thoroughly demonstrated for the decoupling of high-order MIMO antennas. In this design, a suspended patch, internally loaded by two vertical branches (resonators), enables the creation of the patch and quasi-monopole radiation modes simultaneously. Subsequently, with proper control of these mixed radiation modes, cancellation of mutual coupling effect can readily be attained without any external decoupling structures which results in size miniaturization. Moreover, under certain circumstances (e.g., 2-D antenna array), these mixed radiation modes can be optimally combined for the suppression of both adjacent and non-adjacent mutual couplings. For demonstration, a compact 2 × 2 MIMO antenna prototype is designed, fabricated, and characterized. Experimental results reveal that the proposed technique can provide high port isolation (>20 dB), increased antenna efficiency (> 90%), and improved pattern diversity (ECC < 0.05) over an operating bandwidth of almost 10%, with simple and compact configuration. The proposed antenna array may find application relating to the construction of wireless access points. And for dual-band applications, a combination of printed monopoles and neutralization line has been devised (J3) to realize decoupling and impedance matching at two independent and widely separated frequency bands (f2 & f1). Decoupling condition at the upper band (f2) is established by the optimal meandering of the monopole antennas. Meanwhile, port isolation at the lower band (f1) is obtained by the introduction of an embedded T‐shaped neutralization line structure with built‐in transmission zero located at f2. Both simulated and experimental results show that the proposed design can offer substantial enhancement in port isolation, antenna efficiency, and ECC (pattern diversity). To achieve simultaneous port decoupling and pattern switching (beamforming) in MIMO systems, two new DMN circuit topologies (C1 & C2) have been proposed and verified by simulation and experiments. These designs can offer switching of radiation patterns, high port isolation and return loss performance. For validation, the proposed MIMO antenna based on slot antennas and printed monopole antennas, with small element spacing and operating frequency of around 2 GHz, has been constructed and tested. Two distinct radiation patterns are clearly observed when the proposed antenna is switched electronically, with minimal impact on the established high port isolation and return loss performance. Excellent agreement between simulated and measured results has been demonstrated. Lastly, an advanced design of reconfigurable antenna with 14 distinctive steerable radiation patterns (unidirectional and bidirectional) has been developed (C3). Dynamic pattern selection is attained by the adoption of 8 RF switches and 4 quasi-Yagi antenna elements. It features planar structure, compact size, and wide impedance bandwidth. The proposed design can offer wide impedance bandwidth (~ 10%) and simple control circuitry. For validation, the proposed antenna has been constructed and characterized, with a center frequency of 2.0 GHz. Overall efficiency of about 70% and antenna gain of ~ 3.5dBi have been measured. In conclusion, all proposed objectives have been realized with satisfactory results. Out of this research, 3 journal (including 2 IEEE transactions) and 3 international conference papers have been published/presented in 2020-2023. Finally, one PhD (Y. F. Cheng) and one MPhil (C. Y. Lau) students have been trained (graduated in 2020 & 2021) in the area of MIMO antenna technology. Dr. Cheng is currently associate professor, at the School of Electronics and Information, Hangzhou Dianzi University, Hangzhou, China. Mr. Lau is now with HKU SPACE as college lecturer.

14207919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14207919.value: The major findings of this research project are summarized as follow: 1. (J1) A new decoupling method for MIMO arrays without the need of decoupling structure has been developed. By the introduction of optimally shaped meandered dipole elements, mixed-coupling modes can be exploited for the suppression of mutual coupling and size reduction. Parametric study has also been carried out to investigate the impact of meandering and dimensioning on port isolation, resonant frequency, as well as impedance matching performances. 2. (J2) A novel design of patch antenna element (with loaded resonators) has been proposed to offer mixed radiation modes (patch and monopole) for enhancement of port isolation. Its design principle has been systematically investigated and applied to the decoupling of a 2 × 2 MIMO antenna system. The new design also features compact size, wide decoupling bandwidth, high port isolation, enhanced antenna efficiency, and pattern diversity. 3. (J3) A novel dual‐band decoupling technique for two‐element MIMO antenna design has been developed. It is based on the combination of optimally meandered printed monopole elements and a newly developed neutralization line structure. The proposed design offers size reduction, arbitrarily selection of two widely separated frequency bands (f2 & f1), as well as moderate available bandwidth. 4. (C1) A new design approach for pattern-reconfigurable MIMO antenna array (2-element) has been proposed with high port isolation and return loss performance. Unlike conventional solutions, reconfigurable DMN is employed to allow switching of radiation patterns with simple circuit structure and control scheme (4 RF switches are needed). 5. (C2) In this work, a novel switchable DMN approach has been proposed for the realization of 2-element MIMO antenna with reconfigurable radiation patterns, enhanced port isolation and return loss performance. This circuit is small in size (elimination of external matching circuitry), simple in control (only 2 RF switches are needed), and power efficient (due to reduced number of RF switches). 6. (C3) A novel design of a reconfigurable antenna with 14 pattern states has been developed. Compared to prior works, the proposed design can offer more reconfigurable and distinct radiation patterns, reduced number of RF switches and insertion loss (< 4 RF switches are being turned on at any time), compact size, planar structure, with comparable impedance bandwidth and antenna efficiency.

14207919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14207919.value: Currently, the proposed design methods are mainly focused on small array (2-4 elements) and single-band operation (e.g., J1 & J2; C1 & C2). However, they can easily be extended and applied to the construction of large antenna arrays and multi-band systems. In practice, suppression of both adjacent and non-adjacent mutual couplings is one of the major design challenges. Further enhancement in antenna gain and efficiency may be achieved by the adoption of low-loss microwave substrates and/or RF switches. For commercial exploration, the proposed techniques are mostly applicable to the upgrading of existing infrastructures, including wireless access point and mobile terminals, for size and cost reduction.

14207919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14207919.value: Current wireless technology can offer ubiquitous communication with transmission rate of hundreds of Mbit/s. In practice, adaptability to time-varying signal propagation environment is a critical feature for enhanced system performance and size/cost reduction. For instance, in the field of mobile communication, antenna diversity (e.g., space, polarization) may be applied to combat the complex multi-path issues. Moreover, it is proven that MIMO (Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) technology can substantially increase the system capacity and spectrum efficiency. However, the mutual coupling associated with closely spaced antenna elements can severely degrade the system performance. Besides, the deployment of MIMO technology in commercial systems is largely prohibited by the implementation complexity and cost factor. In this research project, a number of novel MIMO antenna design techniques, offering mutual coupling suppression and beamforming capabilities (e.g., beam steering), have been proposed and validated for improved channel capacity and reliability in a complex and dynamical multi-path environment. This work has also attempted to develop solutions with reduced cost, smaller size and lower implementation complexity, targeted for commercial electronic products. In the long run, the research outcomes (with further development) are expected to have a high impact on the construction of wireless communication infrastructures for emerging 5G and IOT applications.

14208019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208019.value: 近年來，物聯網技術飛速發展，越來越多的物聯網設備逐漸進入家庭和工業系統。由於物聯網設備能夠自動地根據預先定義的算法和規則去採集外部數據並做出相應的動作，物聯網設備的安全性對於用戶的人身安全有着重要的影響，若不加以慎重對待，可能會造成數據泄漏、財產損失甚至危及生命。 本項目以物聯網爲背景，研究物聯網中的協議安全分析與設計問題，具體包括如下幾個方面的內容： 1. 基於側信道的物聯網通信協議指紋生成，尤其是在加密流量的基礎之上。該流量指紋技術不但可以用於異常行爲檢測，也可以用於評估既有流量的用戶隱私泄漏問題。 2. 對現有物聯網協議的安全性分析。目前物聯網生態圈中並沒有一個統一的通信協議，導致安全性分析方面存在諸多困難。基於我們在藍牙協議方面的現有工作，我們將繼續研究藍牙協議方面的安全性問題，同時也將擴展到固件升級協議的安全性分析。 3. 設計新的物聯網安全協議。基於前期工作，我們將重點研究物聯網系統所面臨的關鍵安全問題，並針對這些問題研究和設計相應的安全協議。例如，我們將研究物聯網系統中的遠程多方設備綁定協議，以及與第三方進行交互時的用戶認證與授權協議等

14208019.label: Realisation of objectives
14208019.value: * Realization of Objective 1: ============================= Our first object is to implement an algorithm to generate robust fingerprint for protocols used by IoT devices based on the side-channel information extracted from encrypted network traffic. Overall, we have successfully achieved this research objective. More specifically, we have investigate the problem of automated fingerprinting over IoT traffic, and the works had led to the paper published on ASIA CCS 2020 titled: “Your Smart Home Can’t Keep a Secret: Towards Automated Fingerprinting of IoT Traffic”. The first author is the PhD student supported by this project and PI is the correspondence author. During this research work, we had explored different methods in order to generate robust fingerprints for IoT devices based on their network traffics. There are several technical challenges which we had to overcome. First of all, the traffic could be encrypted (e.g., if the connection is established with VPN or using HTTPS protocol). Normally, encrypted traffic will not provide much useful information about the connection and the IoT devices behind. To address this problem, we investigated the use of various side-channel features such as packet sizes, lengths, interval timings, etc. to generate fingerprint. The second challenge is related to the widely used technique called Network Address and Port Translation (NAPT) which allow multiple devices to share the single public IPv4 address (to mitigate the problem of limited IPv4 address space). It turns out that the IPv4 address sharing will mix traffics from different devices (including the target IoT device) together, making it extremely difficult to learn the traffic patterns of IoT devices. To overcome above challenges, we proposed a novel traffic analysis framework based on sequence-learning techniques (like LSTM) and leverage the temporal relations between packets. We built a prototype of the analysis framework and evaluated it under different environment settings (e.g., pure-IoT settings, noisy environment with multiple non-IoT devices, etc.) The results showed our framework was able to differentiate device types with a high accuracy. This result suggests that IoT network communications pose prominent challenges to users' privacy, even when they are protected by encryptions and morphed by the network gateway. As such, new privacy protection methods on IoT traffic need to be developed towards mitigating this new issue. For more technical details, please refer the relevant paper in Part C. * Realization of Objective 2 & Objective 3: ============================================ The second and the third objectives are related, with the second objective focused on the security investigations of the firmware upgrading protocols, while the third objective is about the responsible disclosure and relevant defense solutions of the identified problems in firmware upgrading protocols. To realize these two objectives, we have bought many different types of IoT devices, like smart home WiFi routers, smart speakers, smart power-plugs, etc., and perform security analysis of their firmware upgrading protocols. Since the source code of the firmware is not available, we have to perform binary code analysis and try to recover their firmware upgrading protocol through reverse engineering. That is an extremely challenging job and with lots of hard works, we were only able to recover the firmware upgrading protocol of three smart meters used in modern smart power grids (e.g, the smart meter model PAC4200 Siemens). Based on above protocol reverse engineering works, it was found that for some smart meters we had studied, their firmware upgrading processes were vulnerable and could be hacked (e.g., attackers were able to replace the firmware with a new firmware containing malicious code). This was shown in Figure 6 of paper with title "Hidden Electricity Theft by Exploiting Multiple-Pricing Scheme in Smart Grids" (listed in Part C). Actually, it was the study of firmware upgrading protocol that had motivated us to investigate the potential security implications of compromised the smart meter firmware. It is obvious that with the modified firmware, malicious users could report less usage of electricity, but that can be detected easily, so we further explored the potential threats caused by the vulnerable firmware upgrading protocol and it turned out that attackers could exploit the Multiple-Pricing scheme to pay much less money that they should but without being detected. Such a work was later published on IEEE Transaction on Information Forensics and Security, one of the top journal in security area. * Realization of Objective 4: ============================== In objective 4, we are expected to design a new three-way device binding protocol that can provide guaranteed proof about security. We have done two piece of works to realize this objective. We first performed a security analysis of existing three-way device binding protocols, because we believe that: in order to design a secure protocol, it is necessary to understand the limitation of existing protocols. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to conduct such a systematic study on authorisation management of IoT third‐party integration by: (1) presenting two attacks that leak control permissions of the IoT device in the integration of third‐party services; (2) conducting a measurement study over 19 real‐world IoT platforms and three major third‐party services. Our investigation results showed that eight of the platforms are vulnerable to the threat. To educate IoT developers, we also provided an in‐depth discussion about existing design principles and proposed several secure design principles for three-way cross‐cloud IoT binding protocols. Our second work towards this objective is applying the secure design principles we have learned to the construction of trustable electronic voting system (called SecTEV). SecTEV is a secure and trustable electronic voting system aiming to use mainstream technologies to solve the pain points of existing voting systems. It follows three secure design principles: privacy protection be strong enough to prevent coercion and vote-buying, leverage interest-conflicting parties to detect anomalies, and verify the output instead of inspecting the code. The detailed design of SecTEV were elaborated in the paper with title "SecTEV: A Secure and Trustable Electronic Voting System" (listed in Part C). A thorough security analysis is given to explain how SecTEV achieves various security goals, e.g., integrity and anti-coercion, etc. Security analysis under typical attacking scenarios is also provided to demonstrate SecTEV’s security guarantees. SecTEV aims to achieve a good trade-off between usability, security, and trustability. By mimicking the flow of the traditional voting system, voters are able to understand and verify the correctness of critical outputs, including the ballot itself and the tallying process. With such a design, SecTEV has successfully reduced the complexity of system integrity checks. The complexity is further reduced by shifting works from software to hardware whose correctness is easier to verify.

14208019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208019.value: (1) We found it is not enough to just encrypt the communication (with either VPN or HTTPS protocols) of IoT devices. Our research showed that, even with encrypted traffic, attackers can still infer the types (as well as some user behavior) of certain IoT devices. With proper features derived from encrypted traffics and carefully designed machine learning models (e.g., LSTM model), attackers can also differentiate IoT traffic from traffic of other non-IoT devices. As the output of this study, we also investigated and presented some methods to mitigate the threat of such kind of side-channel attacks to the IoT communication protocols. The work was published on ASIS CCS 2020. (2) We also found that the firmware upgrading protocols used by some existing IoT devices (e.g., smart meters) are not secure enough and can be exploited by attackers to inject malicious code into the upgraded firmware. We have confirmed these findings on three different models of smart meters, and report the problem to their vendors respectively. (3) Although a naive attack can be easily detected with above vulnerable firmware upgrading protocol, further investigations showed that: by leveraging the weakness of existing multiple-pricing scheme of electricity market, it is possible for attackers to launch more sophisticated attack (i.e., using more electricity than they paid for and without being detected at the same time). This and the previous firmware upgrading protocol work had motivated our works published for the journal paper published on IEEE Transaction on Information and Forensics, 2020 (4) We performed a systematic security analysis of existing three-way device binding protocols, and found several loop-holes inside these protocols. We reported two attacks that may leak control permissions of the IoT device in the integration of third‐party services. We also conducted a measurement study over 19 real‐world IoT platforms and three major third‐party services. We also provided an in‐depth discussion about existing design principles and proposed several secure design principles for three-way cross‐cloud IoT binding protocols. This part of work was published in the journal paper pushed on “IET Information Security” in 2022. (5) Finally, we applied the secure design principles learned from previous studies in designing an electronic voting system. This work is completed now, and the relevant paper was sent for journal review at the current stage. We hope it will be published soon in the near future.

14208019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208019.value: There are several potential further developments of the research. (1) The security of Bluetooth protocol under the scenario of IoTs. Bluetooth is a commonly used communication protocol due to its low-cost and energy efficiency. However, in recent years, people have found several security problems with the Bluetooth protocol, especially for the low-energy version (BLE). When applying Bluetooth in an IoT application, it is possible for the designers and developers to make certain assumptions in order to optimize the cost, energy consumption, etc. Unfortunately, such kinds of trade-offs and assumptions may often lead to security problems. So it is worth further investigation in this direction. (2) Another possible future research direction along the line of IoT protocol security is the interactions and inter-connections between IoT devices from different vendors. Currently there are several different IoT ecosystems, like Google, Apple, Samsung, Xiaomi, etc. and it is well known that there is no industry standard protocol that will bridge devices from different ecosystems and to make them interact or coordinate with each other smoothly and securely. How to design such a standardized protocol would be very important and may generate huge impacts.

14208019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208019.value: Internet of Things (IoTs) are smart devices that are becoming increasingly popular in people’s daily life. Common IoT devices may include smart watches, smart speakers, smart WiFi routers, etc. However, when people are using and interacting with smart IoT devices, it is inevitable for such devices to access our personal information (like your activity patterns, your special interests, etc.). It is important to ensure the security of IoT devices before people use and trust them. In this project, we have studied the security of IoT devices from the angle of protocols used by them. A protocol defines the steps and data format when an IoT device is going to do something, like communicating with servers, upgrading its functionality, and pairing with other devices, etc. More specifically, our studies have shown that: (1) it is not enough to just encrypt IoT communications, because attackers can still infer some information about device users from the encrypted traffic; (2) the firmware upgrading protocols used by some IoT devices (e.g., smart meters) are not secure enough, so that attackers can implant malicious code to attack the power grid; (3) existing IoT device binding protocols can be improved in terms of security.

14208219.label: Realisation of objectives
14208219.value: We have fully accomplished the objectives of the proposal. - We have systematically investigated the effects of expansion areas on flow instability and heat transfer coefficient (HTC) for flow boiling in microchannels. Inspired by reentrant cavities and saw-toothed structures, we introduce a new type of reentrant structures, i.e. expansion areas, to mitigate flow boiling instabilities in microchannels. Expansion areas contain both forward-facing and backward-facing steps on the sidewalls, which are expected to have the joint effects of reentrant cavities as effective nucleation sites and saw-toothed structures on the flow field. Using deionized (DI) water as the working fluid, flow boiling experiments were conducted on plain microchannels and microchannels with single and three expansion areas at different mass fluxes for comparison. Results show that expansion areas can effectively mitigate flow reversal and enhance the HTC of flow boiling in microchannels, while the increase of pressure drop is less than 3 kPa. The underlying mechanisms of the HTC enhancement were analyzed based on the flow boiling curves and visualization of flow patterns. - We have experimentally studied the effects of the pin fin height on the pressure drop and the heat transfer performance for flow boiling in microchannels with pin fins. To understand the effects of the pin fin to channel height ratio on flow boiling in microchannels, we developed a novel two-step deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) method to fabricate microchannels with pin fins lower than the channel walls. Microchannel heat sinks with the pin fin height ratio of 50%, 71%, and 100%, respectively, together with a plain microchannel heat sink without pin fins were fabricated for comparison. Flow boiling experiments were conducted at two mass fluxes, using DI water as the working fluid. The results showed that decreasing the pin fin height ratio from 100% to 50% could significantly reduce the pressure drop while only causing a slight decrease in the critical heat flux (CHF). The performance evaluation criterion (PEC) analysis also confirms that lowering the pin fin height is beneficial for flow boiling in finned microchannels. - We further explored the combined effects of pin fins and Cassie-wetting nucleation sites on the flow boiling heat transfer performance in microchannels. Based on the newly developed fabrication method of pin fins with variable heights, we have developed a novel structure containing both pin fins and nucleation sites in microchannels. Such a structure is achieved by first fabricating the mixed-height pin fins in microchannels, then removing the high pin fins and performing DRIE at those locations to form nucleation sites. Pin fins can effectively enhance both HTC and CHF, while nucleation sites are expected to promote nucleate boiling. The major concern of pin fins is the large pressure drop, while for nucleation sites, the largely enhanced bubble nucleation may lead to the elongated bubble in the channel and increase flow instability. By combining pin fins and nucleation sites in microchannels, it is expected that the pressure drop can be lower than the channel containing only pin fins, and the bubble expansion can be controlled through the enhanced flow resistance. Flow boiling experiments were conducted on plain microchannels and microchannels with only pin fins, only nucleation sites, and both of them to fully understand their effects on the flow instability and the heat transfer performance. We have demonstrated that combining both pin fins and nucleation sites in microchannels is a superior approach to enhance the flow boiling HTC with only slight increase in the pressure drop.

14208219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208219.value: - We have shown that expansion areas in microchannels can enhance the flow boiling HTC by 44.2%, compared to that of plain microchannels, without the obvious increase in pressure drop. As disclosed by the flow boiling curves and visualization of flow patterns, the improved HTC can be attributed to the early onset of nucleate boiling and the delayed dryout due to the low flow velocity near the corners of expansion areas. In addition, as the effective range of single expansion area is limited, increasing the number of expansion areas leads to the further enhancement of the HTC during the boiling process. (Publication on International Journal of Thermal Sciences) - We have demonstrated that the pressure drop for flow boiling in finned microchannels can be effectively reduced through lowering the pin fin to channel height ratio. At low to moderate heat flux, all the microchannel heat sinks with pin fins show nearly overlapping boiling curves, as pin fins elevate flow boiling heat transfer through enhanced bubble nucleation in this heat flux range, which is not affected by the height of pin fins. However, higher pin fins lead to a larger HTC in the high heat flux range and a higher CHF, which can be attributed to the enlarged surface area and the increased flow velocity. Importantly, compared to the microchannel heat sink with full-height pin fins, the pressure drop can be significantly reduced by lowering the pin fin height ratio, while the CHF is only slightly decreased. The performance evaluation criterion (PEC) analysis also confirms that lowering the pin fin height is beneficial for flow boiling in finned microchannels. Moreover, flow reversal is effectively suppressed for flow boiling in finned microchannels due to the increased flow resistance and the confinement of bubble growth by pin fins. (Manuscript under review) - Compared to plain microchannels, the HTC is enhanced by 75.1%, 66.5%, and 125.4%, respectively, for microchannels with only pin fins, only nucleation sites, and both of them. The pressure drop slightly increases from 18.1 kPa for plain microchannels to 30.6 kPa for the microchannels with the combined pin fins and nucleation sites. Visualization studies reveal the earlier onset of nucleate boiling in microchannels with the combined structures, while the flow instability is suppressed as indicated by the largely reduced fluctuation of the inlet temperature. (Manuscript under preparation)

14208219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208219.value: The success of the project shows that surface engineering such as adding expansion areas, pin fins, nucleation sites, or the combination of them in microchannels can effectively enhance the flow boiling heat transfer performance and mitigate flow instabilities. Based on these approaches, we have observed a significant enhancement on the flow boiling heat transfer coefficient, up to 125.4%. However, the continuous increase in the heat flux of electronic chips poses high demand on efficient thermal management solutions. In the future, we will further explore in two directions: (1) using active fluid to manipulate the surface wettability and bubble dynamics; (2) using 3D printed triply periodic minimal surfaces (TPMS) to mitigate flow instabilities and enhance the flow boiling heat transfer performance. It might lead to ultrahigh-performance two-phase microchannel heat sinks for electronic cooling.

14208219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208219.value: In this project, we have demonstrated several surface modification methods including expansion areas, pin fins, and nucleation sites to mitigate flow instabilities and enhance the flow boiling heat transfer performance in microchannels for electronic cooling applications. All these surface structures can effectively promote bubble nucleation and thus enhance the flow boiling HTC. Moreover, pin fins can enhance the critical heat flux (CHF) through the enlarged surface area and the increased flow velocity, while expansion areas are able to modify the flow field and thus suppress flow instabilities. Our research has shown that expansion areas can effectively mitigate flow reversal and enhance the HTC for flow boiling in microchannels, without the obvious increase in the pressure drop. For flow boiling in microchannels with pin fins, the pressure drop can be significantly reduced by lowering the pin fin to channel height ratio, while the CHF is only slightly decreased. More importantly, we have shown that the flow boiling HTC can be enhanced up to 125.4% by combining pin fins and nucleation sites in microchannels, and the flow instability is significantly suppressed. This project provides new insights on the design of high-performance two-phase microchannel heat sinks.

14208319.label: Project Objectives
14208319.value: (Research Thrust 1) The aim of the present proposal is a thorough understanding of the behavior of decoding algorithms for quantum stabilizer codes, in particular message-passing iterative algorithms like the sum-product algorithm (SPA). The SPA has become a very popular algorithm due its efficiency and parallelizability, which stem from the fact that the SPA locally combines information on a graphical model. However, this locality is also the major weakness of the SPA, because it cannot resolve certain ambiguities. For classical codes, this sub-optimality has been formalized by the PI in joint work with Ralf Koetter. The resulting approach studies so-called pseudo-codewords, which are real vectors that are projections of codewords in finite covers of the graphical model describing the code. This pseudo-codewords can be used to characterize the sub-optimality of the SPA w.r.t. maximum-likelihood decoding. A central aspect of this proposal is to use and enhance this methodology towards synthesizing and analyzing graphical models of quantum stabilizer codes. Crucially, many approaches for designing classical codes that perform well under the SPA cannot be used because the self-orthogonality constraint imposes severe constraints, and so novel techniques have to be devised. (Research Thrust 2) A key quantity of graphical models is the so-called partition sum. For large DE-NFGs this partition sum is typically intractable and so efficient approximation algorithms are highly desirable. The Bethe approximation of the partition sum, obtained by running the SPA on the DE-NFG, is a particularly interesting option. A central goal of this research thrust is to obtain a better understanding of the gap between the partition sum and its Bethe approximation. The main approach towards this goal will be to investigate how to extend, from classical NFGs to DE-NFGs, the PI's graph-cover interpretation of the Bethe approximation.

14208319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208319.value: 我們社會和經濟運作的核心要素是資訊處理，即有效地收集，評估，儲存，及分發資訊。 多年來從紙質基礎系統，到機械系統，再到電子系統，各種設備都得到了發展。通用設備 和專用設備之間一直存在著競，特別是在電子時代。儘管專用設備通常更昂貴，但是它們 的優勢在於效率更高或者有超越通用裝置的能力。 有一類特別有意義的專用設備是量子電腦和通用量子資訊處理設備。由於持續不斷的進步， 特別是最近，這些設備因其可能提供的有趣應用而受到越來越多的關注。這一進展不僅促 進了美國，歐洲和中國的量子資訊處理的研究工作力度的增加，還吸引了各公司的大量投 資。 退相干是一些量子電腦的主要問題，因此需要製定合適的策略來處理這個問題。有一種很 有前景的方法就是使用所謂的量子穩定碼，其允許通過將量子電腦的量子態進行冗餘編碼， 使得當檢測到實際行為與目標行為產生偏差時，可以採取適當的步驟來矯正量子電腦的量 子態。這種方法在精神上類似於當今許多數位電腦系統中使用的記憶體刷洗。 （記憶體刷 洗是一個檢查記憶體晶片的後臺進程，由於儲存的資訊冗餘，該進程可以檢測錯誤並適當 地糾正錯誤。 ） 圖模型已經成功地應用於通信，信號處理，和人工智慧領域。例如，許多出現在最新電信 標準中的編碼方案依賴於圖模型。基於該專案負責人對經典通道碼圖模型的重要研究和對 量子穩定碼圖模型的初步研究，本專案旨在從圖模型和在其上運行低複雜度演算法兩個方 面對量子穩定碼進行深入而有效的理解。 本專案中用於描述量子穩定碼和更通用的量子資訊處理任務的圖模型的類型與經典圖模型 相容。然而，它們之間也有足夠大的差異，需要設計新的數學分析技術來評估在其上運行 低複雜度演算法的性能。本提案旨在對這些問題進入深入調查，從而有效推動量子資訊處 理領域的發展。

14208319.label: Realisation of objectives
14208319.value: Two of my PhD students and one of my MPhil students have worked on topics related to this project: (1) July X. Li (LI Xialu) (PhD, supported by this grant January 2020 - January 2021) (2) Anthony Huang (HUANG Yuwen) (PhD, supported by this grant October 2022 - December 2022) (3) Jacky Ng (NG Kit Shing) (MPhil, January 2021 - May 2021, August 2022 - December 2022). For all of the above students, I directly supervised their research by having individual weekly meetings, giving them advice on how to proceed, telling them about relevant papers, sometimes outlining potential solutions, sometimes proving results and writing computer programs myself, and giving guidance while writing papers. Contributions toward objectives (more details below): (1) July X. Li has contributed to Objective 1. (2) Anthony Huang contributed to Objective 2. (3) Jacky Ng contributed to Objective 2. The unifying theme of this project was to gain a better understanding of graphical models (GMs) and the sum-product algorithm (SPA). Of particular interest were (Objective 1, Research Thrust 1) quantum stabilizer codes: design of GMs to represent such codes, along with the analysis of the sum-product algorithm (SPA) and its variants running on these GMs. More generally (Objective 2, Research Thrust 2), this project investigated the approximation of quantities of interest (like the partition sum) of graphical models with the help of the SPA. While Research Trust 2 initially aimed at DE-NFGs, a particular class of GMs that are useful in the context of quantum information processing, we mainly dealt with NFGs, a particular class of GMs that are useful in the context of classical information processing. We are currently working on the extension of these results from NFGs to DE-NFGs. (On the side, the PI has been elevated to IEEE Fellow (class of 2021) "for contributions to graphical models for channel coding".) Before stating some of the students' contributions, here is some background information on GMs and the SPA. Namely, consider a function with multiple arguments (known as the global function) that can be written as the product of simpler functions (known as the local functions). A GM is a visual representation of this global function in terms of a graph consisting of vertices and edges: there is a vertex for every variable, there is a vertex for every local function, and there is an edge connecting a variable vertex and a local function vertex if the former is an argument of the latter. Some key quantities of a GM are as follows. (i) The partition sum (or partition function) Z is defined to be the sum of the global function over all possible variable assignments. (Note that a mnay combinatorial problems can be formulated as finding the partition function Z of a suitable GM.) (ii) Marginals of the global function. (Note that the decoding of codes can be formulated as finding certain marginals of the global function a suitable GM.) For scenarios of interest, the partition sum and marginals are usually intractable and so one has to approximate them. A particularly interesting approach is via the SPA. The SPA is very popular because it is of relatively low complexity and allows for parallel processing. The disadvantage of the SPA is that for (the practically relevant case of) GMs with cycles, the quantities computed by the SPA are only approximations of the desired quantities. Yedidia et al. showed that the approximation of Z obtained by the SPA can also be obtained by minimizing the so-called Bethe free energy function associated with a GM. More precisely, they showed that fixed points of the SPA correspond to stationary points of the Bethe free energy function. For this reason, the approximation of Z obtained by the SPA is also known as Z_Bethe. In prior work, the PI showed a combinatorial interpretation of Z_Bethe in terms of so-called graph covers of the underlying GM. While the expression of Z_Bethe in terms of an optimization problem is useful for numerical purposes, the expression of Z_Bethe in terms of graph covers has proven beneficial for analytically relating the values of Z and Z_Bethe. In particular, the PI showed that the average partition sum of M-covers of the GM yields Z_Bethe when M goes to infinity. This graph-cover interpretation by the PI has also proven beneficial in the context of SPA decoding, as it allows to characterize unwanted fixed points of the SPA, so-called non-codeword pseudo-codewords. (1) Some of July's contributions are as follows: (a) The construction of quantum stabilizer codes is made non-trivial by the fact that these codes have to satisfy a certain self-orthogonality constraint. (This is in contrast to codes for classical communications, where no such constraint exists.) July and I devised a methodology that allows to design graphical models of large quantum stabilizer codes based on shorter quantum stabilizer codes. Various known constructions of quantum stabilizer codes were shown to be special cases of this methodology. (b) July formulated two-stage decoders of quantum stabilizer codes, where the first stage is based on the SPA. If the first stage is successful, i.e., the outcome is a valid error pattern, then the decoder terminates (and a suitable correction is applied to the quantum state stabilized by the quantum stabilizer code). If the first stage is not successful, i.e., the outcome is not a valid error pattern, then pseudo-configuration corresponding to the final state of the SPA is analyzed toward obtaining a valid error pattern. All operations are designed so that they have low complexity and scale well when increasing the codelength. (2) Some of Anthony's contributions are as follows: (a) The above-mentioned result by Yedidia et al., is based on certain assumptions about the GM and the fixed point of the SPA. While these assumptions are frequently satisfied, there are interesting cases where these assumptions are not satisfied. Anthony presented a framework for analyzing and characterizing such cases. (b) Another focus of Anthony was on the permanent for non-negative matrices, which can be written as the partition sum of a certain GM. (The permanent of a non-negative, square matrix is one of the most prototypical weighted counting problems in theoretical computer science and appears naturally in many information processing scenarios.) Using the above-mentioned results, the Bethe approximation of a permanent is given in terms of the average partition sum of M-covers when M goes to infinity. For the permanent setup, Anthony characterized the average partition function of M-covers for any finite M, not just for M to infinity, thereby resolving a conjecture in an earlier paper by the PI. (3) Some of Jacky's contributions are as follows: Jacky considered also the Bethe approximation of the permanent. While worst case upper and lower bounds on the approximation ratio Z / Z_Bethe were established earlier on by other researchers, numerical results suggest that in many cases much better guarantees on the approximation ratio Z / Z_Bethe can be given. Jacky established such results for certain families of matrices of interest. Some of the insights gained in the above research have be weaved into my postgraduate course IERG5200 (Channel Coding), typically taught in the spring of even years, and my post-graduate course IERG6120 (Quantum Information Processing), typically taught in the spring of odd years.
