14208319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208319.value: (References below are w.r.t. to Part C.) (1) July: Various graph representations for general stabilizer quantum error-correction codes and entanglement-assisted quantum error-correction codes were established. While so-called quantum-code normal factor graph representations can be used to design new codes out of known codes, prove self-orthogonality of stabilizer label codes, and find possible encoding and decoding circuits, so-called quantum-probability normal factor graph representations provide a way to compute the quantum-mechanical probabilities for the represented codes. [Section 8, No. 1] A pseudocodeword-based two-stage decoder for quantum (stabilizer) color codes was proposed. This decoder has local operations w.r.t. the underlying graphs, syndrome-weight-dependent computational complexity, and better decoding performance compared with previous approaches for quantum color codes. [Section 9, No. 1] (2) Anthony: The above-mentioned result by Yedidia et al. was proven only for GMs with local functions that take on strictly positive values. Yedidia et al. conjectured that similar results hold for factor graphs where the local functions take on non-negative values. We gave examples where the results of Yedidia et al. generalize and examples where their results do not generalize. Moreover, we presented a general framework for analyzing fixed-points of the SPA based on a suitable dualization of the Bethe free energy function. [Section 9, No. 2] In the context of permanents of square, non-negative matrices, i.e., square matrices with only non-negative entries, a degree-M-Bethe-permanent-based lower bound on the permanent of a matrix was proven, which solves a conjecture in an earlier paper by the PI. Similarly, a degree-M-Bethe-permanent-based upper bound on the permanent of a matrix was proven. In the limit M to infinity, these lower and upper bounds yield known Bethe-permanent-based lower and upper bounds on the permanent of a matrix. [Section 8, No. 2; Section 9, No. 4] (3) Jacky: In the context of permanents of square, non-negative matrices, a key observation that was obtained is that for various families of matrices of interest, the ratio Z / Z_Bethe, i.e., the ratio of the permanent to the Bethe approximation of the permanent, can, to a large extent, be understood by analyzing 2-covers of the original GM. This is of significance because 2-covers are easier to analyze than M-covers with M to infinity. The analysis of 2-covers of certain families of interest was then carried out. [Section 9, No. 3]

14208319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208319.value: Research Thrust 1. In the context of graphical models of large quantum stabilizer codes based on shorter quantum stabilizer codes, some of the properties of the large quantum stabilizer codes are well understood in terms of the properties of the shorter quantum stabilizer codes and the way they are connected. However, some properties of the large quantum stabilizer codes are not well understood yet. Moreover, in this framework, an interesting but challenging question is how to design graph-based quantum stabilizer codes that facilitate so-called degenerate decoding. Research Thrust 2. As mentioned earlier on, while this research thrust initially aimed at DE-NFGs, a particular class of GMs that are useful in the context of quantum information processing, we mainly dealt with NFGs, a particular class of GMs that are useful in the context of classical information processing. We are currently working on the extension of some of the obtained results for NFGs to DE-NFGs. In particular, we are analyzing DE-NFGs that are a natural generalization of NFGs whose partition sum equals the permanent of a matrix.

14208319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208319.value: Error-correction schemes play a critical role in data storage and data transmission in today's computer system. These computer systems are classical in the sense that they only take advantage of bulk properties of quantum systems. In contrast, quantum computers will take advantage of intricate properties of quantum systems. However, quantum computers are inherently noisy and must be made noise tolerant with the help of suitable schemes. A particularly important approach are schemes based on so-called stabilizer quantum codes (SQCs). The decoding of these codes can be done on classical computers: based on suitable measurements of the quantum system, they do some classical calculations, which then result in suitable corrections to the quantum system. An appealing approach to formulate SQCs and their decoders are so-called graphical models and the sum-product algorithm. (Note that reliable data communication in the recent 5G telecommunications standard is achieved with the help of low-density parity-check codes, which are decoded by running the sum-product algorithm on a suitably formulated graphical model.) The aim of this project was to enhance our knowledge of graphical models and the sum-product algorithm, in particular in the context of SQCs, but more generally for approximating quantities of interest of graphical models.

14208619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14208619.value: The objective of this project is to develop deep learning approaches for understanding and reconstructing 3D objects from monocular images. Learning discriminative geometry-aware feature representations is the key to achieve accurate and robust 3D object understanding and reconstruction. Understanding and reconstructing 3D objects from monocular images are fundamental problems in computer vision. In recent years, deep learning based approaches achieved great success for different vision tasks because of its capability of learning from large-scale training data. The key task is to learn discriminative feature representations that capture important appearance and shape variations of 3D objects. However, several challenges remain for accurately understanding and modeling 3D objects from 2D images. (1) The lack of large-scale training data. Deep learning approaches generally require a large amount of training data. However, 3D ground-truth shapes for general daily objects, especially non-rigid objects, are usually difficult or expensive to acquire. It cannot be guaranteed that each type of objects would have a large-scale training dataset. (2) Naive extension of 2D techniques to 3D shape modeling is computational and memory inefficient. For instance, when modeling multiple objects in an image, the most common way is to ROI-pool features from visual feature maps. However, the naive extension from 2D to 3D by many existing methods is inefficient and requires generate a large number of 3D ROI proposals. In this project, we propose novel algorithms for handling those challenges. We aims at 3D object understanding and reconstruction for different vision applications: (1) modeling and reconstruction of 3D faces in the wild by bridging the domain gap between synthetic and real images. We take advantages of the large-scale synthetic face data and an end-to-end CycleGAN sub-network to learn geometry-aware face representations for faces in the wild. (2) For understanding and reconstructing 3D human poses, we propose a weakly-supervised framework to learn robust geometry representations for human poses from multi-view information with only 2D information as supervision. (3) For 3D 6DOF object detection in autonomous driving scenes, we propose a framework that includes 3D bounding box proposal augmentation and geometry-aware multi-view feature pooling modules for learning discriminative 6DOF object representations. 14208619.label: Realisation of objectives
14208619.value: All the objectives in this project have been realized successfully. (1) We have developed deep neural network for reconstructing human face shapes and textures in the wild via learning from large-scale synthetic data. Existing methodologies often rely on a limited set of real-world data or images fitted with 3DMM parameters. Recent strides have been made to address this limitation by delving into training on diverse settings using large-scale synthetic data. However, the realism is far from satisfaction. To utilize the prior knowledge power from large-scale synthetic data, while tackling the domain gap problem at the same time, we propose an expressive two-stage framework, where a hybrid 3D generative network architecture is explored. The first stage is a geometry-aware cycleGAN, which bridges the real-synthetic domain gap by converting real-world images into synthetic-style ones. The second stage focuses on learning human head structures with reasonable geometry by our proposed HeadFormer network. It is a variant of neural radiance fields (NeRF) which is capable of reasoning 3D radiance field for human heads from a monocular image. We achieve this by introducing a novel 2D-to-3D transformer into the NeRF paradigm with several designs. Specifically, we propose a voxel-based 3D Transformer architecture, and show that when recovering the complete radiance field from partial observation, it is vital to learn long-range relations and geometry-consistency in three levels: among 2D patches, between 2D and 3D spaces, and among voxels in 3D spaces. Such a transformer design does not only conduct plausible inpainting for unseen parts, but also generalizes to unseen person identities via learning from large-scale synthetic data. Building upon the voxel-based 3D Transformer, we then integrate a multi-resolution hash encoding octree structure with CUDA implementation to reduce memory usage, and to capture high frequency and local details. (2) We have developed deep neural network that supports learning feature geometry-aware feature representations for 3D human pose estimation. To achieve the robustness, instead of directly utilizing network predicting 3D human pose, we make network predict 3D mesh, and extract 3D human pose from the mesh prediction. Prior works reconstructed 3D mesh from global image feature extracted by using convolutional neural network (CNN), where the dense correspondences between the mesh surface and the image pixels are missing, leading to suboptimal solution. This paper proposes a model-free 3D human mesh estimation framework, named DecoMR, which explicitly establishes the dense correspondence between the mesh and the local image features in the UV space (i.e. a 2D space used for texture mapping of 3D mesh). DecoMR first predicts pixel-to-surface dense correspondence map (i.e., IUV image), with which we transfer local features from the image space to the UV space. Then the transferred local image features are processed in the UV space to regress a location map, which is well aligned with transferred features. Finally, we reconstruct 3D human mesh from the regressed location map with a predefined mapping function. We also observe that the existing discontinuous UV map is unfriendly to the learning of network. Therefore, we propose a novel UV map that maintains most of the neighboring relations on the original mesh surface. (3) We have developed deep neural network that enables learning feature geometry-aware feature representations for 3D object detection in autonomous driving scenes with only monocular images as inputs. Since the location recovery in 3D space is quite difficult on account of the absence of depth information, this paper proposes a novel unified framework which decomposes the detection problem into a structured polygon prediction task and a depth recovery task. Different from the widely studied 2D bounding boxes, the proposed novel structured polygon in the 2D image consists of several projected surfaces of the target object. Compared to the widely-used 3D bounding box proposals, it is shown to be a better representation for 3D detection. In order to inversely project the predicted 2D structured polygon to a cuboid in the 3D physical world, the following depth recovery task uses the object height prior to completing the inverse projection transformation with the given camera projection matrix. Moreover, a fine-grained 3D box refinement scheme is proposed to further rectify the 3D detection results. Experiments are conducted on the challenging KITTI benchmark, in which our method achieves state-of-the-art detection accuracy. (4) We have applied the technologies to related problems, including face and body image generation, and face animation. To tailor the technologies seamlessly into the topics, we made several modifications. Specifically, to apply the technologies on body generation (such as human video inpainting), we proposed FuseFormer based on the HeadFormer, a Transformer model designed for video inpainting via fine-grained feature fusion based on novel Soft Split and Soft Composition operations. The soft split divides the feature map into many patches with given overlapping interval. On the contrary, the soft composition operates by stitching different patches into a whole feature map where pixels in overlapping regions are summed up. These two modules are first used in tokenization before Transformer layers and de-tokenization after Transformer layers, for effective mapping between tokens and features. Therefore, sub-patch level information interaction is enabled for more effective feature propagation between neighboring patches, resulting in synthesizing vivid content for hole regions in videos. Moreover, in FuseFormer, we elaborately insert the soft composition and soft split into the feed-forward network, enabling the 1D linear layers to have the capability of modeling 2D structures. And the sub-patch level feature fusion ability is further enhanced. In both quantitative and qualitative evaluations, our proposed FuseFormer surpasses state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, to apply the technologies on face generation and animation, we further proposed a conditional 3D generative radiance field, which inserts explicit prior (facial landmarks) into the framework HeadFormer, to serve as an explicit handle that supports controls over the learning of radiance field.

14208619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208619.value: As research outcomes, 8 conference papers are published. IEEE Transactions on Neural Network and Learning Systems is one of the top journals in machine learning. CVPR/ECCV/ICCV/AAAI are the top conferences on computer vision and machine learning. In this project, we propose a model-free 3D human mesh estimation framework, named DecoMR (Part C.8, C1), which achieves state-of-the-art performance on both 3D human body mesh reconstruction and 3D human body pose estimation. The key insight of this work is learning geometry-aware representation via explicitly establishing the dense correspondence between the mesh and the local image features in the UV space. In (Part C.8, C2), we propose a novel monocular-based 3D Object Detection framework, which decomposes the complicated 3D detection problem into a structured polygon prediction task and a following depth recovery task. In (Part C.8, C4), we propose the Spatially Modulated Co-Attention (SMCA) mechanism, a simple yet effective scheme for improving the Transformer paradigm in object detection scenarios. In (Part C.8, C3), we present a novel framework that recovers the 3D scene from monocular inputs via decoupling the instances from a coarsely completed scene and exploits category priors to guide the reconstruction. These technologies can be applied to other related domains to help improve performances. Specifically, in (Part C.8, C5), we present FuseFormer to show how to utilize the Transformer idea to improve human inpainting. In StereoGAN (Part C.8, C6), we extend the idea of cycle-generative model used in domain translation to help learn stereo matching in synthetic datasets. In (Part C.8, C7), we extend the idea of geometry-aware feature learning to the point cloud completion domain, where we propose a novel framework, which learns a unified and structured latent space that encodes both partial and complete point clouds. In (Part C.8, C8), we further extend this idea into 6D object pose estimation from monocular image. We integrate the geometry-aware feature learning process into a recurrent neural network (RNN) for object pose refinement, which is robust to erroneous initial poses and occlusions. The key insight is a consistency check mechanism based on the learned descriptors of the 3D model and observed 2D images, which downweights the unreliable correspondences during pose optimization.

14208619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208619.value: In this project, we found that neural radiance fields and Transformer structure can help the deep learning models to overcome the insufficient geometric information reasoning from monocular images. Besides, we also found that cycle-generative model paradigm can help ease the issues of real-syntenic domain gaps. The proposed models and strategies can be integrated into widely used in other topics beyond 3D object reconstruction. The technique can also be extended to solve the domain gap problem in robotic problems by leveraging the technique as the data-translation model. We will continue to delve into this direction.

14208619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208619.value: The objective of this project is to develop deep learning approaches for understanding and reconstructing 3D objects from monocular images. Learning discriminative geometry-aware feature representations is the key to achieve accurate and robust 3D object understanding and reconstruction. The outcome of this research have significant impact on 3D object understanding, detection, and reconstruction. The proposed algorithms could be generalized to a large scope of 3D objects. We demonstrate that the proposed technologies can also provide powerful tools for various related vision tasks, including 3D object recognition and 3D animation.

14208819.label: Realisation of objectives
14208819.value: The objectives have been satisfactorily achieved. A unified framework for a large class of constant-modulus optimization problems has been successfully developed. It covers a wide range of applications, such as MIMO detection with binary or M-ary phase shift keying constellations, sparse principal component analysis (PCA), fair PCA, the densest k-subgraph problem, graph matching, size-constrained assignment, and non-negative orthogonal matrix factorization. Extensive numerical experiments have been made, and it has been demonstrated that the proposed framework works well in the aforementioned applications. In some applications, it provides computationally much more efficient solutions than the state-of-the-arts (SOTAs). Some important theoretical breakthrough has also been made. In the beginning of this project, we used the notion of concave minimization to build the proposed framework. The error bound technique, which was rarely considered in prior related works, has been employed as a new approach to study the framework. It has led to expansion of the framework, allowing us to cover a wider scope of problems and develop improved solutions. Our fundamental research endeavor has also led to a number of other meaningful contributions, such as a new explanation of a deep learning-based MIMO detection method through the proposed framework.

14208819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14208819.value: Constant-modulus (CM) optimization has many important applications in different fields such as signal processing, communications, image processing, computer vision, data science and machine learning. In general CM problems are challenging, and methods for CM optimization were usually developed in a problem- or application-specific manner. The most significant contribution of this project lies in developing a unified framework for a large class of CM problems, with concrete applications. The main benefit of the framework is that it provides a universal systematic way to convert a CM problem to a convex-constrained optimization problem, which thereby allows us to use simple optimization algorithms to tackle the problem. Our extensive empirical study has shown that the framework is promising. For example, we have successfully applied the framework to the densest k-subgraph problem, which is a problem of subgraph discovery from a graph (say, community discovery from a social network). We performed tests on graphs as large as nearly 4,000,000, and the proposed method achieves good performance with very competitive runtimes. We have also been successful in the application of graph matching in computer vision, outperforming the SOTAs by a clear margin. At the heart of the aforementioned advances is the notions of exact penalization, the core theoretical aspects for converting CM problems properly (or with theoretical guarantees). In this part of exploration, the most important finding is that of the error bound technique. It expands the scope of the framework and opens the door for many previously unseen possibilities. Our practical success with the graph matching application is, for instance, powered by the error bound technique. The error bound technique also enables to deal with applications such as sparse PCA and fair PCA, and it gives rise to new efficient solutions for applications such as size-constrained clustering and non-negative orthogonal matrix factorization. From the theoretical perspective, the finding of the error bound technique has immense significance in enriching our fundamental understanding of the subject. The major findings have been published as a two-parts paper in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing. The support of this project has also resulted in a number of meaningful outcomes in the form of published works. A notable one is that we use the proposed framework to explain a deep learning method in the context of MIMO detection. Simply speaking, some deep neural networks for carrying out multivariate binary decisions can be regarded as optimization algorithms under the proposed framework.

14208819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14208819.value: The error bound technique used in this project has great potential for further development. The error bound technique did not receive wide attention in the context of CM optimization, and our endeavor may be seen as a concrete instantiation of the technique for the first time. But we believe that this does not end here. Rather, it could just be the beginning. The error bound technique is a flexible approach that allows researchers to leverage problem nature in different ways. So far, and after the completion date of this project, we have found that the error bound technique can be further extended in different directions. Some extensions allow us to improve computational efficiency in existing applications such as the densest k-subgraph problem, while some give new opportunities to work on new applications. Some applications even go beyond CM optimization. To be specific, we may be able to apply error bounds to the difficult problem of cardinality sparsity. We hope that the current contributions of this project would, in the future, provide the first step toward sustained research by the communities.

14208819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14208819.value: Constant-modulus (CM) optimization arises in many important applications across different fields, such as MIMO detection in signal processing and communications, community detection in social network science, sparse principal component analysis in statistics, graph matching in computer vision, capacity-constrained clustering for paper-to-session assignment in a conference, non-negative orthogonal matrix factorization in machine learning, etc. CM optimization was usually treated in a problem-specific manner. In this project we have developed a framework that provides a systematic way to treat a broad class of CM problems. The framework allows us to apply standard numerical algorithms, such as the basic projected gradient descent algorithm, to process the problem, which greatly facilitates the effort of devising algorithms. It also gives flexibility for researchers to utilize specific CM problem structures to tailor-build computationally efficient algorithms. At the heart of the framework is theoretical developments related to exact penalization in mathematical optimization. In particular, the error bound technique developed in this project is important and provides valuable new insights. Numerical experiments have shown that the framework works well in a variety of applications. For example, it has been successfully applied to a large-scale graph identification problem (up to nearly four million nodes), offering competitive runtime performance.

14209419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209419.value: Randomness is a basic resource in computation, but often only imperfect sources with unpredictable correlations are available. For the purpose of simulating repeatable computations, any high-entropy source is sufficient as its randomness can be harnessed by applying a seeded extractor. In distributed environments, however, repeating a computation is not always feasible, and in cryptography dependent repetitions can be harmful to security. Dodis, Ong, Prabhakaran, and Sahai (FOCS 2004) proved that there exist distributions of very high entropy rate, but whose randomness cannot be extracted for many useful cryptographic applications including encryption and secret sharing. One objective of this project is to classify sources of randomness with respect to their suitability for distributed and cryptographic applications. Cryptography intuitively requires random bits of "high quality", but there are no known sources of randomness with respect to which cooperative distributed algorithms are possible, but cryptography is not. In this context, we outline a candidate source of entropy that might separate these two types of applications. We propose some additional questions regarding the relation between extractability of a source and its suitability for cryptography. Several recent works have investigated blockchains as an entropy source for applications such as randomness beacons and distributed lotteries. Owing to their incentive structure, fair randomness extraction from the blockchain state is not always possible. Boneh et al. (CRYPTO 2018) have proposed the application of verifiable delay functions as a countermeasure. Current candidates, however, are either inefficient, or are insecure against quantum adversaries. We outline a new proposal for the post-quantum world and provide some evidence towards its verifiability. 隨機性是計算的基本資源，但通常隨機源並不完美－它們具有不可預測的相關性。任何高熵源都足夠用以模擬可重複的計算，因為有種子的隨機性提取器可以充分利用它們的隨機性。然而，在分佈式環境中，重複計算並不總是可行；互相關聯的重複計算更會影響密碼學安全性。Dohis, Ong, Prabhakaran 和 Sahai (FOCS 2004) 證明有些分佈縱然非常高熵，其隨機性卻不可提取並用於密碼學應用，例如加密和秘密分享。 此項目的目標是根據隨機源在分佈式和密碼學應用的適用性，對其進行分類。密碼學直觀地需要「高質素」的隨機位元，但在目前已知的隨機源中，若其適用於協作分佈式算法，它亦適用於密碼學。有鑑於此，我們概述了一個可能將這兩種應用分開的熵源。我們亦提出了一些關於隨機源可提取性及其在密碼學的適用性之間的關係的其他問題。 最近的一些研究探討了區塊鏈作為隨機信標和分佈式財票等應用的熵源。由於區塊鏈以激勵方式運作，並不總能從中提取到公平的隨機性，Boneh et al. (CRYPTO 2018) 提出可驗證延遲函數作為對策。然而，目前的候選函數不是效率低，就是不量子安全。我們概述了一個新的後量子的函數，並為其可驗證性提供一些證據。

14209419.label: Realisation of objectives
14209419.value: The works "Non-interactive composition of sigma-protocols via share-then-hash" and "Acyclicity Programming for Sigma-Protocols" studied the role of randomness in the composability of zero-knowledge sigma-protocols. These are the most common and natural types of protocols for tasks like identification and digital signatures. The main finding is that there are composition tasks motivated by certifying certain blockchain computations in which random oracles (an idealized model of perfect randomness) allow more efficient protocols. A secondary contribution is an optimization of the CDS composition method which is prevalent in this context. These works partially address objectives 1 and 2. The paper "Bounded indistinguishability for simple sources" develops a general theory of imperfect randomness sources that occur in secure distributed computation, contributing to our understanding of objective 1. The paper "Hitting sets for regular branching programs" constructs new low-entropy pseudorandom sources that are secure against space-bounded distinguishers. While these only satisfy the hitting set property which is insufficient for cryptographic applications it gives quantitative improvements in space-bounded derandomization. The long-term objective of this line of work is to understand which pseudorandom properties suffice for security against space-bounded adversaries, partially addressing objectives 1 and 2. Question 3 was addressed in an unpublished manuscript with Alon Rosen, in which we propose a new proof of sequentionality based on new hardness assumptions. The reason we did not publish this manuscript is that the same construction was discovered independently by Lai and Malavolta "Lattice-based timed cryptography" and published in CRYPTO 2023. (Our work is acklowedged in their publication.) Ongoing discussions with them and other researchers demonstrate some vulnerabilities in this proposal. This line of work fulfills objective 3.

14209419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209419.value: In the context of zero-knowledge proof composition, the major findings are that the two composition frameworks of Cramer, Damgard, and Shoenmackers and Abe, Okhubo, and Suzuki are incomparable: There exists composition predicates that are more efficiently composable in one than in the other and vice-versa. Moreover the latter method has potential advantages in certain blockchain-inspired computations. In the context of security of distributed protocols, the main conclusion is that stronger forms of security can be achieved with fewer assumptions than previously known. We also showed that pairs of distribution that are locally indistinguishable but also sampleable with low complexity have properties that are desirable for secure distributed protocol design. Regarding proofs of sequentiality from lattice assumptions, the main finding is that while a plausibly secure construction should possible in principle, there are preprocessing attacks that do not have analogues in discrete log-based constructions. Providing a construction that is provably secure under reasonable assumptions remains a challenge. The last contribution is a new and improved hitting set generators for regular branching programs, giving evidence that hitting sets may be easier to construct than fully pseudorandom sources and identifying the hardest parameter regime for this longstanding open problem.

14209419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209419.value: There is some ongoing research activity related to lattice-based proof of work. The proposed course of action is to develop models of "reasonable" preprocessing attacks that could potentially lead to a proposal that is provably secure in such models.

14209419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209419.value: Randomness is an essential resource for secure computation in distributed environments like blockchains. Improper assumptions and models about the "type" of randomness in such applications is a common source of vulnerabilities. This project furthers our rigorous understanding of the interplay between randomness and security in the settings of multi-party computations.

14209519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14209519.value: This proposal aims to experimentally investigate on-chip lasers with geometry independence based on topological valley kink state. Topology is a branch of mathematics that deals with highly robust conserved quantities that do not change when objects are continuously deformed. Since the discovery of quantum Hall effect in crystalline materials, this mathematical concept has entered the field of physics and emerged as an indispensable property of electrons, photons, and phonons. In photonics, the most important application of topology is the prediction of edge states that allow light to flow unidirectionally around large imperfections or sharp bends without back-reflection. This unique feature implies a new class of geometry-independent photonic components. The possibility to construct arbitrarily shaped cavities opens a new paradigm for integrated lasers as it enables denser packing of light sources of arbitrary form factors. To date, the study of interplay of topology with light emitters and with optical gain is one of the most active directions in topological photonics, which is expected to offer novel features in light sources, amplifiers, and laser devices. Recently, two types of topological lasers have been demonstrated experimentally, one of which relies on magneto-optical materials and the other has bulky footprints. Due to its versatile applications in communication and signal processing, a topological laser operating in the telecommunication band with magnetic-free nanophotonic structures is highly desirable. We propose to realize a magnetic-free topological laser with arbitrarily shaped cavities by using a novel degree of freedom, namely valley pseudospin. On an active semiconductor chip, we will design and fabricate two types of honeycomb photonic crystal structures with distinct topological phases induced by broken spatial-inversion symmetry. We will harness the topological kink state confined at the interface between these two regions to create geometry-independent photonic crystal cavities. Under electrical or optical pumping, lasing action will be obtained from such topological photonic crystal cavities. By exploring interesting topological phenomena in an active medium, this proposal has far-reaching significance to both fundamental research and some cutting-edge engineering applications. Fundamentally, studies of the intrinsic non-Hermitian and nonlinear Hamiltonians in lasers will extend the existing topological theories in solid-state physics, because of the intrinsically distinct behaviors between the bosonic photons and the fermionic electrons. Technology-wise, topological laser sources with geometry-independent cavities will lead to more compact, robust, and flexible optical networks on a chip. 本項目旨在研究基於拓撲谷扭結態的不依賴幾何形狀的片上激光器。 拓撲學是數學的一個分支，涉及物體連續形變時不會改變的高強健守恒量。自從在晶體材料中發現量子霍爾效應以來，此數學概念已進入物理學領域，並成為電子、光子和聲子不可或缺的特性。在光子學裏，拓撲學最重要的應用是邊緣態的預測，其允許光沿單向繞過大的瑕疵或急彎而無背向反射。這種獨特的特征預示了一類新的不依賴幾何形狀的光子元件。由於構造任意形狀的光腔成為可能，這為集成激光器開辟了新的範例，人們能夠更密集地擺放具有任意形狀因子的光源。迄今為止，對拓撲學與光發射器或光增益相互作用的研究是拓撲光子學中最活躍的方向之一，預計它將為光源、光放大器和激光器件提供新的特性。最近已有實驗展示了兩類拓撲激光器，其中一種依賴於磁光材料而另一種具有龐大的占片面積。由於其在通信和信號處理中的多種應用，人們迫切需要一種工作在通信頻段、無需外磁場的納米光學拓撲激光器。 我們提議利用一個新的自由度（即谷贗自旋）來實現具有任意形狀光腔的無需外磁場的拓撲激光器。在有源半導體芯片上，我們設計和構造兩類由於空間反演對稱破缺而導致不同拓撲相的蜂窩狀光子晶體結構。我們利用限制在這兩個區域間界處的拓撲扭結態來構造不依賴幾何形狀的光子晶體腔。在電或光泵浦下，可從這種拓撲光子晶體腔獲得激光發射。 通過探索有源介質裏有趣的拓撲現象，本項目對基礎研究和一些前沿的工程應用具有深遠意義。從根本上說，研究激光裏的本征非厄米和非線性哈密頓量將拓展固體物理學中現有的拓撲理論，這是因為具有玻色子特性的光子和具有費米子特性的電子在行為上有本質的不同。在技術方面，具有不依賴幾何形狀的光腔的拓撲激光光源將導致實現片上更緊湊、更強健且更靈活的光網絡。

14209519.label: Realisation of objectives
14209519.value: 1. (Objective 1) To study the theory of topological photonics in a gain medium. We have fully achieved this objective by exploring fundamentally new architectures supporting topological states on several photonic platforms at visible, telecom, and terahertz wavelengths. (1) Topological photonic structures are the cornerstone of topological cavity for lasing because of their topological robustness. We have theoretically proposed topologically protected photonic structures, which support bit-error-free signal transmission [J1, C1]. Topological signal transmission at terahertz wavelengths ∼270–290 GHz was consequently obtained [J2]. These theoretical results show that the topological signal transmissions are robust against local perturbations, allowing the exploration of reliable cavity for strong light–matter interactions, optical nonlinearities, and lasing. (2) We have also investigated a topological photonic crystal cavity array on an integrated photonic platform, which exhibits nontrivial topology and supports strongly localized topological edge states. By engineering the geometric parameters, we have numerically demonstrated the Hofstadter butterfly spectrum, which is one of the most important phenomena in the topological model. Such structures can be adopted for experimental investigation of topological photonics and will facilitate development of topological lasers [J3]. 2. (Objective 2) To design topological lasers with cavities of arbitrary shapes. We have fully achieved this objective by developing a standard design process for the cavity and monitoring the behavior of the lasing mode. (1) The coupling between light sources and waveguides are essential for lasing. We have designed and experimentally demonstrated a waveguide structure for coupling photoluminescence from tungsten sulfide (WS2) monolayer. With a finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, we designed a lossless waveguide structure for perfectly confined optical wave and numerically obtained coupling efficiency of ∼2.3% for an in-plane-oriented dipole at wavelength of 620 nm. This platform breaks through the limits of 2D-material integration with conventional photonic architectures and offers a new perspective for lasing [J4]. (2) Microdisk lasers are important components in photonic integrated circuits. We have designed ultrathin curved visible microdisk lasers with a thickness of ∼80 nm for single-mode lasing emission. With a three-dimensional FDTD method, we calculated the three-dimensional spatial intensity distribution of the lasing mode. We also experimentally demonstrated the designed microdisk laser with an intrinsic linewidth of ∼0.04 nm measured near the threshold, corresponding to a Q factor of ∼17,000 [J5]. (3) Halide perovskites are considered as a new material platform for lasing due to their excellent optical properties and low fabrication costs. We have also explored quasi-2D Dion–Jacobson-phase perovskites as the gain material for optically pumped lasers. The results suggest that a low lasing threshold can be obtained due to the nonradiative decay pathways and multicarrier recombination mechanisms. Distributed-feedback lasers based on the Dion–Jacobson-phase perovskites were designed and experimentally demonstrated, exhibiting a low lasing threshold of ∼5.5 μJ cm−2 and high Q factor up to 30,000 [J6]. 3. (Objective 3) To simulate the optical behaviors of topological lasers with cavities of arbitrary shapes. We have fully achieved this objective by simulating the behaviors of the topological lasing mode with cavities of several shapes. For verification, we have also fabricated some topological lasers and experimentally characterized the behaviors of the topological lasing modes. (1) We have simulated and experimentally realized ultralow-threshold continuous-wave optically pumped single-mode topological corner state nanolasers on a silicon substrate. In simulation, we obtained the topological mode based on a zero-dimensional topological corner state. From experiment, we observed the linewidth narrowing effect above the laser threshold, which verifies the lasing emission. The topological nanolasers operated under room-temperature continuous-wave optical pumping conditions, with an ultralow lasing threshold of ∼3 μW and a lasing linewidth of ∼0.66 nm [J7]. (2) We have simulated and experimentally realized topological Dirac-vortex microcavity lasers on a silicon substrate, where room-temperature continuous-wave linearly polarized vertical laser emission at a telecom wavelength was observed, with a lasing threshold ∼0.4 kW cm−2. The lasing spectra suggest that the samples with a larger cavity size exhibit a narrower lasing linewidth, which agrees well with the simulated Q factors. The simulated and experimental results confirm that the emission wavelength of the Dirac-vortex lasers is topologically robust against variations in the cavity size [J8]. (3) We have simulated and experimentally realized topological parametric phonon lasers based on nanoelectromechanical Dirac-vortex cavities. We applied an incoherent white-noise voltage centered at a frequency of 90.43 MHz with a bandwidth of 20 kHz to parametrically pump the device. We observed from the measured spectra that the linewidth reduces from 11.0 to 3.8 kHz when the pump voltages increases from 2.00 to 4.45 V, which is a distinctive evidence of phonon lasing [C2]. Our devices can not only be used as a robust coherent phonon source for topological phononic integrated circuits, but also be harnessed for investigating the interplay between topology and nonlinearities.

14209519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209519.value: (1) In [J1, C1], the theoretically proposed topological photonic architectures support bit-error-free signal transmission. In [J2], we observed topological signal transmission at terahertz wavelengths ∼270–290 GHz. These photonic architectures provide enhanced robustness against local perturbations, and thus facilitate the development of topological cavities for lasing. (2) In [J3], we investigated topological photonic crystals in the configuration of a cavity array. We found that these photonic structures support strongly localized topological edge states, which can be harnessed for constructing low-threshold, high-Q laser cavities. The topological photonic crystal structures hold great promise for making highly robust cavities for lasing. (3) In [J4], we developed a new mechanism for coupling between photon sources and waveguides. We found that the photoluminescence from tungsten sulfide (WS2) monolayer can be coupled to a waveguide with a coupling efficiency of ∼2.3%. This mechanism sets a new paradigm for on-chip 2D-material photonic integration and lasing. (4) In [J5], we demonstrated ultrathin microdisk lasers for single-mode laser emission. These microdisk lasers exhibit a linewidth of ∼0.04 nm and a Q factor up to 17,000. They can be adopted for on-chip applications such as integrated photon sources. (5) In [J6], we developed quasi-2D Dion–Jacobson-phase perovskites as a new functional material for the next-generation on-chip lasers. We found that the nonradiative decay pathways and multicarrier recombination mechanisms contribute to an ultralow lasing threshold. These Dion–Jacobson-phase perovskites pave the way for photonic and optoelectronic applications due to their processability and operational stability. (6) In [J7], we demonstrated topological corner state nanolasers on a silicon substrate, exhibiting an ultralow threshold, continuous-wave operation, and CMOS compatibility. These topological lasers represent a new route toward ultracompact, highly robust integrated on-chip light sources for silicon photonics. (7) In [J8], we demonstrated topological Dirac-vortex microcavity lasers on a silicon substrate. We observed room-temperature continuous-wave linearly polarized vertical laser emission at a telecom wavelength. We confirmed that the wavelength of the Dirac-vortex laser is topologically robust against variations in the cavity size, and its free spectral range defies the universal inverse scaling law with the cavity size. These lasers mark an important step toward integrating topological lasers on the silicon nanophotonic and microelectronic platform. (8) In [C2], we demonstrated topological parametric phonon lasers with a nanoelectromechanical system. These parametric phonon lasers can not only be used as a robust coherent phonon source, but also be harnessed for investigating the interplay between topology and nonlinearities.

14209519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209519.value: In this project, we have designed, simulated, and experimentally realized several types of on-chip topological lasers with different cavity shapes. Further development of the research can include the following aspects: (1) Exploration of topological lasers in some other physical domains. For example, by applying the principles of topological transport in nanomechanical systems, one can realize low-threshold parametric phonon oscillation, which can be used as a coherent phonon source for phononic integrated circuitry. (2) Extension of the topological lasers to other functional material platforms. For example, by exploring new semiconductor gain materials such as perovskites or 2D transition-metal dichalcogenides, one can realize new types of active photonic integrated circuits with topological robustness. (3) Investigation of advanced physical topics with topological lasers. This will open the door to many intriguing phenomena such as non-Hermiticity, bosonic nonlinearity, and quantum electrodynamics. Specifically, the topological lasers can be employed to construct a non-Hermitian system to enable chiral dynamics and high-sensitivity sensing. (4) Integration the developed topological lasers with conventional photonic integrated circuits. This may enable highly robust, high-density integrated photonic chip for next-generation applications, such as 5G/6G communications, autonomous driving, smart sensing, Internet of Things, etc.

14209519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209519.value: This project focuses on the development of topological lasers on a chip. We have fully achieved all the objectives by designing, simulating, and experimentally realizing several types of on-chip topological lasers with different cavity shapes. The demonstrated topological lasers break through the fundamental limitations of conventional photonic architectures, by enhancing the device’s robustness against structural imperfections and disorders. This project has a great impact on both topological physics and practical applications. Fundamentally, the realization of topological lasers enriches the topological theories and will inspire the exploration of topology in other physical domains to reduce dissipation loss and/or enhance system robustness. Practically, the developed topological lasers will find various applications such as transmitters in fiber-based or free-space communication networks, light sources in Lidar or face-recognition systems, and chemical or biomedical sensors. These topological lasers have paved the way for the development of on-chip light sources for next-generation photonic integrated circuits. We expect the strategies developed in this project to be adopted in other functional materials and/or on other platforms, which can offer high versatility and potential for applications in high-power photonics, nonlinear optics, and quantum photonics.

14209619.label: Project Objectives
14209619.value: We propose a novel system that employs the motion sensors (accelerometer and gyroscope) of smartwatch to capture accurate and rich respiratory information during physically inactive states including meditation, resting, and sleeping, without requiring any training effort from users. By measuring the duration and phase of inhalation/exhalation of each breath cycle, our system can help to understand breathing behavior in sleep disorders and meditation. Moreover, we will develop real-time feedback mechanisms that will connect meditators with the sensation of breathing, enabling them to make their own adjustment to achieve a more effective meditation in a unobtrusive fashion. Operating solely on a smartwatch, the system can immediately reach the growing population of smartwatch users, making it ideal for longitudinal data collection for health and physiology studies. We propose a smartphone-based system for improving respiration and locomotion coordination during rhythmic aerobic exercises including running and cycling. Our approach integrates lightweight sensing algorithms for accelerometer and microphone, and exploits the characteristics of a physiological model called Locomotor Respiratory Coupling (LRC) to achieve real-time accurate measurement of exercise rhythm. The system can improve exercise efficiency through sound-induced stabilization of exercise rhythm, such as listening to an external auditory stimulus with a proper tempo. We propose a mobile system that can automate (respiratory sinus arrhythmia) RSA-based breathing training with biofeedback, which is a common cardiorespiratory intervention that has been commonly used as a complementary treatment to diseases (e.g., asthma, COPD, generalized and post-traumatic stress disorder) by improving the autonomic control of cardiopulmonary function. 14209619.label: Realisation of objectives
14209619.value: Objective 1: We complete the design and implementation of iSleep—a practical system to monitor people’s sleep quality using off-the-shelf smartphone. iSleep uses the built-in microphone of the smartphone to detect the events that are closely related to sleep quality, and infers quantitative measures of sleep quality. iSleep adopts a lightweight decision-tree-based algorithm to classify various events. For two-user scenario, iSleep differentiates the events of two users either when two phones can collaborate with each other or when two phones cannot communicate with each other. The experimental results show that iSleep achieves consistently above 90% accuracy for event classification in a variety of different settings in one-user scenario and above 92% accuracy for distinguishing users in two-user scenario. By providing a fine-grained sleep profile that depicts details of sleep-related events, iSleep allows the user to track the sleep efficiency over time and relate irregular sleep patterns to possible causes. Objective 2: We complete the design and implementation of DeepHeart, a novel approach for HR estimation using deeplearning-based denoising and spectrum-analysis-based calibration. DeepHeart applies a deep CNN ensemble for denoising PPG signals. To obtain the labels of contaminated PPG signals, a method to generate clean PPG signals from ECG signals is designed. With the contaminated PPG signals and their labels, a DCNN is trained for denoising. As a result, most of motion artifacts can be removed from contaminated PPG signals. Then, a spectrum-analysis-based HR calibration algorithm is applied to the processed PPG signals. In this algorithm, estimation errors in successive frames are detected and the spectrum of the frame with estimation error is analyzed to find the correct HR or replace the error with a predicted HR. DeepHeart is evaluated based on the IEEE SPC training data set with 12 records collected during various physical activities. DeepHeart achieves an average absolute error of 1.74 bpm, outperforming two state-of-the-art methods, TROIKA and Deep PPG. Our experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of DeepHeart in providing accurate HR estimation and its practicality in various physical activities. Objective 3: We complete the design and implementation of BreathCoach – a smart and unobtrusive system that enables in-home RSA-BT using sensors on smartwatch and smartphone-based VR. To achieve this goal, BreathCoach adopts a suite of lightweight algorithms to continuously monitors BP, IBI and RSA using raw acceleration and PPG signals collected from the smartwatch. The system uses these real-time measurements to intelligently switch between two feedback mechanisms, IBI-based and RF-based, in order to derive the optimal BP. The recommended BP is then conveyed to users in the form of VR game to provide an intuitive training experience. We implemented BreathCoach using an off-the-shelf wrist-type wearable, a smartphone and a VR viewer, and designed two exploratory VR games. BreathCoach is evaluated in three aspects, including accuracy of physiological measurements, effectiveness of training, and user experience. Our experimental results collected from 10 subjects with each one performs both traditional and BreathCoach-based training indicate that BreathCoach is able to provide accurate physiological measurements with breathing cycle duration and IBI errors lower than 0.61s and 15ms respectively. Moreover, compared to traditional RSA-BT protocol, BreathCoach achieves significant improvement (p < 0.05) on training effectiveness and experience. Objective 4: We have validated the design of proposed systems and evaluate their performance through real-world experiments that involve 90+ families in Hong Kong. The results shown that our proposed systems outperform the existing state-of-the-art systems in various settings.

14209619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14209619.value: 1. We propose iSleep [1]—a practical system to monitor people’s sleep quality using off-the-shelf smartphone. iSleep uses the built-in microphone of the smartphone to detect the events that are closely related to sleep quality, and infers quantitative measures of sleep quality. iSleep adopts a lightweight decision-tree-based algorithm to classify various events. The experimental results show that iSleep achieves consistently above 90% accuracy for event classification in a variety of different settings in one-user scenario and above 92% accuracy for distinguishing users in two-user scenario. 2. We propose DeepHeart [2], a new HR estimation approach that features deep- learning-based denoising and spectrum-analysis-based calibration. DeepHeart generates clean PPG signals from electrocardiogram signals based on a training data set. Then a set of denoising convolutional neural networks (DCNNs) are trained with the contaminated PPG signals and their corresponding clean PPG signals. We evaluate DeepHeart on the IEEE Signal Processing Cup training data set with 12 records collected during various physical activities. DeepHeart achieves an average absolute error of 1.61 beats per minute (bpm), outperforming a state-of-the-art deep learning approach (4 bpm) and a classical signal processing approach (2.34 bpm). 3. We propose BreathCoach [3], a smart and unobtrusive system that enables effective in-home RSA-BT using sensors on a smartwatch and smartphone-based VR. Specifically, BreathCoach continuously measures key bio-signals including breathing pattern (BP), inter-beat interval (IBI), amplitude of RSA, and intelligently calculates the optimal BP based on current and historical measurements. The recommended BP is conveyed to users through a VR game to provide intuitive guidance. The experiment results suggest that BreathCoach is able to reliably measure needed bio-signals and intelligently calculate BP recommendations which result in improved performance compared with the traditional approach. 14209619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14209619.value: Objective 1: Environmental factors such as room temperature play an important role in quality of sleep. We will further integrate iSleep with tools that can monitor sleep environments. This will enable in-depth analysis of causes of interrupted sleep and irregular sleep patterns, providing important information for healthcare providers to find trends related to certain diseases. Objective 2: We note that DCNN is trained by leave-one-record-out cross-validation in this work, which allows our solution to achieve better applicability than the leave-one-window-out validation. In particular, the parameters used in the spectrum-analysis-based calibration are identical for all 12 records, rather than being optimized for each record as other signal processing solutions. Moreover, the methods of deep-learning-based denoising and spectrum-analysis-based calibration are independent, and hence improvements can be made on them separately in future work. We believe that, by training with a dataset that has more subjects and activities, longer session recording, and more realistic sample surroundings, DCNN can have a better generalization ability, leading to more accurate HR estimations from PPG signals.

14209619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14209619.value: Aerobic respiration plays a critical role in maintaining normal human body functions and sustaining life. Respiration monitoring has numerous applications, ranging from improving the efficiency and experience of aerobic exercises like running and cycling, alleviating daily stress through meditation and resting, to treating diseases like chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, which is one of the leading causes of deaths due to the population aging. However, to date, there has been no practical and convenient tools that people can use on a daily basis for respiration monitoring and feedback. This project developed new mobile and pervasive systems that leverage commodity mobile devices (smartwatch, smartphone, and Bluetooth headset) for real-time respiration monitoring and feedback without resorting to professionals or specialized equipment. Specifically, our approach empowers individuals to adapt their respiration during physical inactive states (such as meditation sleeping) for improving their health, track and improve the coordination between breathing and locomotion during running and cycling, and conduct (respiratory sinus arrhythmia) RSA-based breathing training with feedback of several critical physiological signals including interbeat interval (IBI) and the amplitude of RSA. These systems offer an unobtrusive solution for personalized, long-term respiration monitoring and training, complementary to existing professional devices that are designed for short-term use.

14210019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210019.value: Robotic exoskeletons are wearable bionic devices that are equipped with actuators at human joints, by integrating both robot power and human intelligence. The objective of this project is to develop robotic exoskeletons for elderly people with impaired mobility. With the motion assistance provided by robotic exoskeletons, the physical and mental health of these elderly people are expected to be improved, so as to improve their quality of life. Robotic exoskeletons will be developed to be light-weight, portable, and comfortable to wear through optimal structure design and use of 3D printing parts. Compliant actuators will be developed to lower down the mechanical impedance of robotic exoskeletons, filter unwanted collisions from the ground, and improve the system energy efficiency. Human gait analysis will be performed to evaluate the user’s motion performance in real-time based on the innovative gait modeling and analysis methods. Intelligent control will be developed to provide user-initiated, effective, safe and comfortable motion assistance. Prototypes of robotic exoskeletons will be fabricated and used in clinical trials for effectiveness evaluation. With these innovative robotic exoskeletons, elderly people can obtain significant benefits in both physiological and psychological aspects, and the developed technologies will greatly benefit the healthcare in Hong Kong. 外骨骼機械人是一種可穿戴仿生設備，它在人體關節處安裝了驅動器並且結合了機械人的動力和人類的智能。本項目的目標是為行動不便的老人研製外骨骼機械人。通過外骨骼機械人提供的輔助，這些行動不便的老人的身心健康將會得到改善，從而提高他們的生活品質。通過優化結構設計和使用3D列印部件，我們將研製輕重量，便攜且穿著舒適的外骨骼機械人。柔順驅動器將被研製來降低機械阻抗，過濾來自地面的碰撞，並且提高能量使用效率。基於新穎的步態建模和分析方法，我們將進行人體步態分析來即時評估使用者的運動表現。智能控制將用來為穿戴者提供用戶啟動的，有效，安全並且舒適的運動輔助。我們將製造出外骨骼機械人樣機並在臨床試驗中評估其有效性。有了這些創新的外骨骼機械人，老年人的身心健康將顯著受益，並且開發的技術將有益於香港的醫療保健。

14210019.label: Realisation of objectives
14210019.value: Due to low power consumption and fast response, magnetorheological (MR) dampers have been used as actuators. To enhance the performances, efforts have been made to increase the field dependent force with the same power consumption. However, the fluid viscous force is also increased significantly, which is undesirable in practical use. To tackle this problem, we have designed and tested an MR damper with multi-grooves (small multiple annular flow gaps) on piston for performance enhancement. The detailed design of the proposed MR damper was provided. A coupled field model to describe the characteristics of MR fluid in different regions of MR damper was derived. Parametric analysis of the number and width of multi-grooves was also performed. Experimental results of the two MR dampers without and with multi-grooves were given and compared with the simulation results. The advantages of MR damper with multi-grooves over the one without multi-grooves and the accuracy of the coupled field model were validated by experiments and simulations. Active exoskeletons hold the promise of improving the mobility of lower-limb impaired individuals. Locomotion mode identification (LMI) is essential for these devices precisely reproducing the required function in different terrains. We have proposed a terrain geometry-based LMI algorithm. The environment should be built according to the inclination grade of the ground. Given that, the locomotion mode/terrain can be classified by the inclination grade. Besides, human feet move along the surface of terrain to minimize the energy expenditure for transporting lower limbs and get the required foot clearance. Hence, the foot trajectory estimated by an IMU was used to derive the inclination grade of the terrain that we traverse to identify the locomotion mode. In addition, a novel trigger condition (an elliptical boundary) was proposed to activate the decision making of the LMI algorithm before the next foot strike thus leaving enough time for performing preparatory work in the swing phase. Most lower limb exoskeletons (LLEs) used passive ankles instead of active ones for reducing system weight. Joint angle trajectories are essential for level ground walking and other desired motions. Most LLEs measured trajectories from healthy individuals, which have not considered features of passive ankles and lack adjustability of step length and foot clearance for different patients. In this project, the joint trajectories were planned in joint space, which interpolates the joint angles of assigned via-points considering adjustable step length and foot clearance, and avoiding backward falling. Considering the swing foot with passive ankle drops down that requires larger flexion angles of knee and hip joints and consumes more energy for enough foot clearance, a mobile cable-driven ankle and a cable-spring ankle design were proposed for reducing motion ranges and energy consumption. In addition, the joint trajectory generation of LLE was investigated for stair ascent and descent. Multiple sensors and fuzzy logic inference were used for adapting to various dimensions of stairs. Besides the motion assistance for paraplegic patients, the force/torque-field assistive strategy for rehabilitation was discussed. A user-adaptive method was proposed to determine the size of virtual space online and determine adaptive assistance for the patients. Different conditions of patients were simulated on a dummy leg and user-adaptive method outperforms the fixed width of virtual tunnel. The proposed motion assistance and rehabilitation methods were verified through human trials with both healthy subjects and patients with mobility impairment.

14210019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210019.value: Locomotion mode identification (LMI) is essential for exoskeletons precisely reproducing the required function in different terrains. We proposed a terrain geometry-based LMI algorithm [J1 in Part C8]. According to the inclination grade of the ground, the locomotion mode/terrain can be classified. We also estimated the motion of the knee joint during walking using the kinematics of wearer’s thigh measured by a single Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU). A long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network model was adopted to model intra-limb synergy between the motion of thigh and the knee joint. With the trained LSTM model, the knee angle can be precisely predicted [J4]. In our further studies, LSTM showed good synergy for generating trajectories in line with the wearer’s motion for lower limb assistive devices [J8]. Due to low power consumption and fast response, magnetorheological (MR) dampers have been used as actuators. We have designed and tested an MR damper with multi-grooves on piston for performance enhancement [J2]. Shape optimization of MR damper piston based on parametric curve was performed [J5]. Progress of medical applications of MR fluid were systematically reviewed [J6], mainly focused on six categories including lower limb prosthesis, exoskeleton, orthosis, and rehabilitation device. With MR fluid, natural and stable limb motions in lower limb prostheses, exoskeletons, orthoses, and flexible muscle trainings in rehabilitation devices, can be realized. Harvesting energy from human motions is a promising solution to the power issue for wearable devices. We develop a lightweight human knee energy harvester to capture energy from the knee motion [J3]. A variable radius drum-cable mechanism with variable transmission ratio was employed to allow the generated torque to match the torque of the human knee joint. We also developed a bimorph piezoelectric bending beam-based energy harvester to scavenge energy from the human knee motion [J7]. During walking, the human knee will flex and extend to periodically deform piezoelectric macro fiber composites (MFC) bounded to the bending beam, thus generating electricity. These energy harvesters would improve the energy efficiency of the exoskeletons. A proxy-based torque controller (PTC) was designed for safe and performant interaction torque control of motor-driven exoskeletons under different scenarios [J9]. We also proposed a feedforward-feedback hybrid control strategy of sliding mode impulsive control with gravity and friction compensation, based on the event-triggered mechanism of Lyapunov function [J10], to achieve complete gait tracking with bounded error and has excellent dynamic performance under constraints.

14210019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210019.value: Significant results (10 journal papers and 3 conference papers, one Best Conference Paper Award, one granted US Patent, and another patent application) have been obtained from this completed project. Three PhD students were trained with their theses: F. Y. Liang, “Human Locomotion Synergy for Robotic Assistive Devices,” Ph.D. Thesis, September 2021; G. Y. Liu, “Structural Design and Optimization of Magnetorheological Dampers for Prosthetic Knees,” Ph.D. Thesis, May 2022; X. Guan, “Trajectory Tracking and Motion Control of the Lower Limb Exoskeleton for Locomotion Assistance,” Ph.D. Thesis, December 2022 (co-supervised with Prof. J. Huang). For the further development, an intelligent motion recognition-based framework for motion analysis should be developed to detect the motion of wearers for gait assessment with the developed motion capture system and assistive devices. It would be desired to advance a wearable motion capture system, which consists of (1) multiple sensors such as IMU, force sensors, and EMG sensors; (2) motion capture algorithms; (3) motion identification algorithms. It would be beneficial to provide user-initiated, intelligent and safe motion assistance. More clinical trials on subjects with impaired mobility wearing robotic exoskeletons should also be conducted.

14210019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210019.value: Robotic exoskeletons are wearable bionic devices that are equipped with actuators at human joints, by integrating both human intelligence and robot power. The objective of this project was to develop robotic exoskeletons for people with impaired mobility. With the motion assistance provided by robotic exoskeletons, the physical and mental health of these mobility impaired people are expected to be improved, so as to improve their quality of life. Robotic exoskeletons were developed to be light-weight, portable, and comfortable to wear through optimal structure design and use of 3D printing parts. Compliant actuators were developed to lower down the mechanical impedance of robotic exoskeletons, filter unwanted collisions from the ground, and improve the system energy efficiency. Human gait analysis was performed to evaluate the user’s motion performance in real-time based on the innovative gait modeling and analysis methods. Intelligent control was developed to provide effective motion assistance. Prototypes of robotic exoskeletons were fabricated and used in clinical trials for effectiveness evaluation. With these innovative robotic exoskeletons, mobility impaired people can obtain significant benefits in both physiological and psychological aspects, and the developed technologies would greatly benefit the healthcare in Hong Kong.

14210219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210219.value: The adversaries have recently switched their focus onto attacking the availability of target systems, because completely taking control over a remote server has become much more difficult with the deployment of advanced memory corruption protection mechanisms. Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks are a class of attacks that threaten the availability of a computing system. DoS attackers can make a system unavailable by sending requests that can make a vulnerable application crash. Alternatively, they can degrade a victim server's performance by exhausting its available computing resources, including but not limited to CPU cycles, memory, disk spaces, network bandwidth and connections. Traditionally, attackers exhaust the network resources of a victim server by flooding it with numerous amount of requests, which are usually crafted from thousands of bots. More recently, attacks that exhaust a server's CPU cycles have emerged. These attacks usually require only moderate amount of requests to cause significant CPU consumption. For example, an attacker can send a request that can trigger the worst-case execution of an application. These kinds of attacks are often very difficult to prevent and detect, because they exploit the design flaws in an application's logic rather than the traditional memory vulnerabilities. In this project, we aim to develop a set of security mechanisms that help detect the CPU-exhaustion DoS vulnerabilities in web applications. In particular, we focus on applications that are developed in PHP, which is the most popular server-side programming language. First, we aim to develop new static program analysis algorithms to detect and fix CPU-exhaustion DoS vulnerabilities in web applications before they are deployed. Second, we will also develop algorithms that detect CPU-exhaustion DoS vulnerabilities in a web application dynamically. The outcomes of this project can help detect potentially previously unknown DoS vulnerabilities and protect web servers running vulnerable applications from CPU-exhaustion DoS attacks. 隨著先進的內存保護機制的部署，完全地控制一個遠程服務器已經變得更加困難。攻擊者們最近將註意力轉移到了攻擊目標系統的可用性上。拒絕服務（DoS）攻擊是一種可以威脅一個計算機系統的可用性的攻擊。DoS攻擊者可以通過發送可以令一個存在漏洞的應用程式崩潰的請求來使一個系統不可用。他們也可以通過耗竭一個受害服務器可用的計算資源來降低其性能。這樣的資源包括但不限於CPU周期，內存，硬盤存儲空間，網絡帶寬及連接。 傳統上，攻擊者通過從數千個僵屍機器發送大量的請求來耗竭一個受害服務器的網絡資源。近期，耗竭一個服務器的CPU周期的攻擊已經出現了。這樣的攻擊通常只需要少量的請求就可以引起大量CPU消耗。例如，一個攻擊者可以發送一個能觸發一個應用程式最壞執行情況的請求。這樣的攻擊利用的是一個應用程式邏輯上的設計缺陷而不是傳統的內存漏洞，防止和檢測它們是非常困難的。 在這項研究課題中，我們旨在開發一些可以幫助檢測網絡應用程式中的CPU耗竭拒絕服務漏洞的安全機制。我們特別關註用PHP這一最流行的服務端編程語言所開發的應用程式。首先，我們開發新的靜態程序分析算法來在網絡應用程式部署前檢測並修復他們中的CPU耗竭DoS漏洞。其次，我們開發動態檢測這類漏洞的算法。這項研究項目的成果可以幫助發現潛在的未知DoS漏洞和保護運行存在漏洞的應用程式的網絡服務器。

14210219.label: Realisation of objectives
14210219.value: We have realized all the major project objectives and achieved additional results beyond what were originally proposed. We discuss next in detail how and to what extent each objective has been achieved. 5.3.1 Develop a static taint analysis tool for finding potentially user-controlled computation-expensive code blocks in PHP applications. We have developed several new static program analysis tools for analyzing and finding vulnera- bilities in PHP programs. First, we developed a static analysis system—LChecker—for PHP and targeted a class of logic bugs—loose comparison bugs. PHP loosely compare two operands by implicitly converting their types and values. Such a feature can cause unexpected results, leading to authentication bypass and other functionality problems. LChecker employs a context-sensitive inter-procedural data-flow analysis and a basic taint analysis together with several new PHP program analysis techniques. Using LChecker, we discovered 42 previously unknown bugs, including 9 new CVE IDs. Second, we worked on developing a general static program analysis tool for finding common taint-style vulnerabilities, including CPU-exhaustion DoS vulnerabilities, in PHP programs. An initial implementation was integrated with our symbolic execution tool, which to be discussed in the next objective. We further extended our prior works and finally developed TChecker— a precise static inter-procedural analysis tool for detecting taint-style vulnerabilities in PHP applications. In developing TChecker, we overcame the limitations of the existing static taint analysis approaches and advanced the state of the art. It performs a static inter-procedural data-flow analysis in a context-sensitive manner and builds a precise call graph iteratively. It tracks taints in object properties and supports several commonly used dynamic language features. These techniques enable TChecker to accurately propagate taints to the correct target functions and objects in modern complex PHP applications. Using TChecker, we found 18 previously unknown vulnerabilities which can be exploited for severe security consequences. 5.3.2 Develop a tool to estimate the reachability of potentially vulnerable PHP code blocks using symbolic execution. To determine the feasibility of an execution path and to generate attack inputs, we developed a symbolic execution tool—XSym—for PHP applications. Although symbolic execution has been widely used in finding vulnerabilities in programs developed in many programming languages, there existed no complete open-source symbolic execution tool for PHP when we started this project. A critical and important challenge in symbolic execution is to model the language-specific built-in functions. Prior works commonly translate the complex build-in functions manually into the SMT-LIB language for constraint solving, which requires an excessive amount of human effort and deep understandings of the function behaviors. We proposed a cross-language symbolic execution method to automate the built-in function modeling task for PHP symbolic execution with the observation that the PHP built-in functions are implemented in its interpreter written in C. We synthesize a C program to symbolically execute the built-in functions in C, and integrate the C symbolic execution with the symbolic execution at the PHP source code level. Our method is implemented in the tool XSym, which can successfully model 287 PHP built-in functions in an automated fashion. Given a potential vulnerability (e.g., a CPU-exhaustion DoS vulnerability) in a PHP program, XSym can symbolically analyze the PHP program and find the path and/or data constraints for reaching and triggering the potential vulnerability. It then requests a constraint solver to help generate concrete attack inputs for exploiting the potential vulnerability. XSym helped exploit 141 vulnerabilities in our evaluation dataset, including 13 vulnerabilities that cannot be exploited by the state-of-the-art manual modeling tool. 5.3.3 Develop a resource-guided fuzzer for PHP applications to find inputs that may cause significant CPU consumption. We have implemented several fuzz testing techniques for detecting vulnerabilities in PHP applications. Our initial implementation of a fuzzer employs both code coverage and resource consumption as the execution feedback for a specific input. By favoring the inputs that discover new code (e.g., basic blocks or functions) and/or consume more CPU time, it can focus on exploring program paths that are likely to cause significant CPU consumption. Although it was able to reproduce some known CPU-exhaustion DoS vulnerabilities, it cannot reach deeper program locations for quite complex applications. This is because that modern PHP applications take much more complex inputs than traditional target programs for fuzzing and the path constraints in these PHP applications are quite difficult to satisfy with simple input mutation strategies. To overcome this challenge, we have developed a directed fuzzer for PHP programs to perform targeted vulnerability validation. Instead of letting the fuzzer explore a very huge path search space, we leverage the analysis results of our static analysis tools. The statically reported potential vulnerable code locations are set as the targets, so that the directed fuzzer would prefer execution paths close to those that are reachable to the targets. This could avoid exploring a large portion of execution paths that are irrelevant to the potential vulnerabilities. Furthermore, to improve the performance, we perform backward taint analysis to find the control-dependent external parameters for more precise input mutation. This greatly reduces the input mutation space. The evaluation results show that our technique can largely outperform the state-of-the-art fuzzer for PHP applications.
