14210219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210219.value: In this project, we investigated and developed program analysis methods for detecting CPU- exhaustion denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerabilities in PHP applications. In the investigation, we also studied several problems that are quite related to the project, e.g., DoS attacks or performance issues in other application scenarios, other types of taint-style vulnerabilities, and symbolic execution. Our research has led to the publication of nine research papers all at top-tier computer science conferences—WWW (x2), IEEE S&P (x2), ASE (x1), ESEC/FSE (x1) and CCS (x3), and three Ph.D. theses (two to be completed by July 2024). Through our research, we have significantly advanced the research of PHP program analysis, developed new vulnerability detection and software testing techniques, and discovered and reported hundreds of previously unknown bugs and vulnerabilities. First, we developed new program analysis systems for analyzing PHP programs and detecting vulnerabilities, including 1) LChecker that detects loose comparison bugs using static analysis and dynamic validation, 2) XSym that symbolically analyzes PHP code with automated built-in function modeling, and 3) TChecker that performs precise inter-procedural taint analysis to detect taint-style vulnerabilities. Second, we developed new techniques to detect denial-of-service vulnerabilities and performance bugs in different application scenarios, including 1) Revealer that detects regular expression DoS vulnerabilities through static vulnerability modeling and matching and dynamic attack validation, 2) MdPerfFuzz—a fuzzing framework that detects performance bugs in Mark- down compilers through a syntax-tree based mutation strategy and an execution trace similarity algorithm for bug de-duplication, and 3) Acquirer—a hybrid analysis system that detects general algorithmic complexity DoS vulnerabilities using static vulnerable code analysis and dynamic vulnerability validation. Third, we proposed new vulnerability detection methods that improve the detection efficiency and depth. We developed SelectFuzz, a new directed fuzzer that selectively explores relevant program paths for efficient crash reproduction and vulnerability detection; and DSFuzz, a system that progressively explores multiple dependent program states through multi-stage micro directed fuzzing to reach deep states and detect new bugs. Finally, we investigated function modeling in symbolic execution. We first developed XSym to automate built-in function modeling for PHP symbolic execution using a cross- language program synthesis method. We then developed a scope-aware differential testing framework—SEDiff—to test the correctness of existing internal function models in popular symbolic execution engines.

14210219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210219.value: Through this research project, we find that source code level symbolic execution for PHP remains challenging. This motivates us to explore other methods to realize better symbolic reasoning of PHP programs in our future work. In addition, it is still difficult to achieve a high code coverage in dynamically testing PHP programs due to the complex input processing logic, the multiple-page dependency, and the interaction with external environment. We will continue our research in this direction and tackle the above challenges. Furthermore, our experience in PHP program analysis and vulnerability detection will be useful for exploring relevant problems in other similar computing scenarios as we have demonstrated.

14210219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210219.value: Denial-of-service (DoS) attacks can significantly degrade a victim system’s performance and threaten its availability to the legitimate users. Some of the attacks are possible because the server programs (typically in the form of web applications) have vulnerabilities which allow remote attackers to cause significant CPU consumption with a moderate number of requests. In this project, we developed several new techniques that help detect CPU-exhaustion DoS vulnerabilities in web applications written by the most popular server-side language—PHP. They include static taint analyses and a symbolic execution tool. We also extended our research scope and developed new techniques to detect general classes of vulnerabilities or similar types of vulnerabilities in other application scenarios. Our research has resulted in the discovery of many previously unknown bugs and vulnerabilities, some of which have been fixed because of our reports.

14210319.value: 具私隱的深度學習：密碼學方法、軟體防護擴展加圖形處理器框架及協同訓練 雲端計算和機器學習的普及便利了各種複雜的分析服務，譬如醫療或財務評估。資源不足的用戶可透過付費使用分析服務進行預測。這些服務通常涉及應保密的敏感數據，有時法律或規章亦會要求數據保密。理想情況下，所有持份者，即查詢用戶、模型所有者和訓練數據提供者的私隱都應得到如下保障。用戶使用分析服務時不會洩露他們提供的查詢和預測結果。與此同時，神經網絡模型（下稱網絡）亦不會洩露給用戶。 此外，亦要確保訓練數據的私隱，以鼓勵更多人貢獻訓練數據，從而訓練出更準確的模型。 現有保護神經網絡私隱的密碼學技術仍然差強人意。SecureML（S&P '17）是唯一一個能保證訓練私隱的方案，但是訓練一個小至只有一層隱藏層的網絡需要長達7個小時。其他僅能保護預測私隱的方案就算在處理簡單的預測時效率依舊不高。使用如英特爾（Intel）的軟體防護擴展（Software Guarded Extensions -- SGX）所支持的可信處理器似乎更有前景，但它的內存大小限制網絡的任何一層均需少於90個百萬位元組（MB）。雖然內存可以超載，但所需的分頁開銷很大。 此外，典型的處理器沒有特別適合神經網絡的運算，而圖形處理器（Graphical Processing Unit -- GPU）則可以大大提高處理神經網絡的速度。 此提案旨在解決數個實際問題。 一） 對於最尖端及最適合硬件結構的神經網絡，我們是否可以使用密碼學技術去保護查詢及網絡模型的私隱，而同時保持預測的準確性和效率？ 二）我們可否有一個高效率的方案，即使對於處理模型的伺服器也能保持訓練數據及模型的私隱？ 具體來說，我們是否可以利用SGX和GPU來實現這些目標，而不依賴低效的SGX分頁，並不需要重型的密碼學技術去保証數據不會洩露予不被信任的GPU？ 三）憑藉我們實現GPU安全計算的新理念，我們能否進一步提升其他情境的私隱和效率？ 具體而言，多個互不信任的參與方在不透露其訓練數據的情況下，可否協同訓練一個深度神經網絡？ 此提案的成功不僅能解決所有持份者的私隱擔憂並充分發揮機器學習的潛力，還可以促進密碼學、可信賴運算與機器學習等領域的進展。

14210319.label: Realisation of objectives
14210319.value: Objective-1: [IJCAI20] We start with investigating vulnerabilities in BAYHENN (IJCAI 2019, 48 citations, potentially more if not for our proposed attack), which claimed model privacy from the learning-with-error assumption. Our work, through theoretical and empirical analyses, shows that an adversary can use intermediate outputs to recover all model parameters. We also formalize a security model. [TDSC22] We optimize a prior two-non-colluding-server-based training framework for secure outsourced neural network (NN) predictions by employing single-instruction-multiple-data processing for offline Beaver triplet generation to reduce latency and communication costs of online communication. Using garbled circuits for non-linear ReLU activation maintains accuracy without approximation, and adopting average-pooling instead of max-pooling further optimizes predictions with similar accuracy. This work motivates our proposal of techniques surpassing optimization. [UsenixSec21] Our work GForce directly addresses the objective by proposing a GPU-friendly, privacy-preserving NN inference engine. On the machine-learning front, we introduce stochastic rounding and truncation layers, which effectively fuse multiple layers to maintain high efficiency and accuracy. On the cryptographic front, we propose GPU-friendly protocols for both linear and non-linear layers, notably secure comparison for ReLU. A highlight is its support for VGG-16, achieving ~73% accuracy on CIFAR-100 in just 0.4 seconds, setting a new benchmark. [NDSS21] We complement the efforts in GForce by proposing privacy-preserving inference for decision trees. Unlike NN, it addresses the unique challenge of ensuring privacy during decision tree traversal, requiring the model owner to remain oblivious to the path the client's query takes. To achieve this, we developed a sublinear evaluation method (in the number of tree nodes) that minimizes performance overhead while maintaining privacy. The protocol supports multi-client joint evaluation by outsourcing to two non-colluding servers, making it ideal for weak client scenarios. Additionally, it is efficient for high-dimensional feature vectors. This study could also inform approaches to other convolutional networks. [AsiaCCS22] We extend the above to enhance private set intersection (PSI) protocols, crucial for secure data alignment in training over vertically distributed datasets. Our improved PSI protocol significantly reduces computation and communication costs by compressing the graph representation of sets. Additionally, it natively supports secure computation over the intersection set, further optimizing efficiency and security in distributed training environments. Objective-2: [AAAI21] Goten provides the first secure framework for outsourcing DNN training and inference using GPUs and TEEs. It solves the open challenges left by Slalom in ICLR 2019. Goten integrates GPU computational power with TEE security, overcoming inefficiencies of cryptographic solutions. One of its primary innovations is the implementation of a dynamic quantization scheme inspired by SWALP (Stochastic Weight Averaging in Low Precision), which quantizes NN parameters to fixed-point numbers, optimizing cryptographic operations while maintaining high accuracy. This dynamic approach ensures the framework adapts to changing parameter distributions during training. The secure GPU-outsourcing protocol uses additive secret sharing to protect data, minimizing communication and memory-swapping overheads. Goten achieves a 6.84× speed-up over pure-TEE systems and a 132.64× speed-up over multi-server cryptographic solutions, with high accuracy. Its efficacy in training models for sensitive tasks, like breast cancer diagnosis, demonstrates its practical applicability in privacy-critical scenarios. Objective-3: The last objective is more exploratory in nature. While initially considering trusted processors as a possibility, we pivoted due to the decline in TEE availability (with Intel deprecating SGX and limiting it primarily to cloud and enterprise), coupled with increased TEE memory easing cryptographic challenges, diminishes the need for advanced protocols in limited-memory environments. This objective is realized through a comprehensive framework for collaborative learning with DP and secure computation protocols for non-linear functions: [ACL21] We sanitize input discrete text tokens using metric-based local DP (LDP) to protect privacy from the root. This method employs token-level metric-LDP, which offers protection based on token semantics, avoiding excessive noise. A variant of the exponential mechanism is used to replace tokens from the vocabulary, effectively mitigating the curse of dimensionality. [WWW23] Sentence embeddings, which are lower-dimensional real-valued vectors extracted from input text sequences using language models (LMs), are sanitized to achieve strong sequence-level metric-LDP. We employ two sanitization methods based on the Purkayastha and generalized planar Laplace mechanisms. Additionally, we enhance utility by applying a consistency constraint and mediating the dimensional curse through trainable linear maps. Labels are also sanitized using randomized responses to ensure complete privacy protection. [CCS23] We introduce a novel approach by sanitizing forward-pass signals, specifically real-valued embedding matrices, in training. Unlike the de facto DP stochastic gradient descent (DP-SGD), which adds noise to gradients, our method adds noise to hidden layer outputs. We propose an analytic matrix Gaussian mechanism (aMGM) to exploit matrix structural characteristics for utility gain. Normalizing embedding matrices to maintain a constant Frobenius norm achieves sequence-level approximate local DP. This fundamentally different approach ensures robust privacy while handling the inherent challenges of sanitizing forward-pass signals, advancing the state of privacy-preserving collaborative learning. [ACSAC23] We propose secure computation protocols for two essential NN training functions. Our softmax protocol uses ordinary differential equations and Fourier series for constant-round communication, while our one-round sigmoid protocol provides an error-bounded approximation. Both protocols improve efficiency over existing methods and enhance privacy-preserving collaborative learning by shortening the training process and maintaining competitive accuracy.

14210319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210319.value: Four highlights: Goten is the first privacy-preserving training framework marrying cryptography, trusted execution environments, and untrusted GPU. It resolves five problems unhandled by Stanford's inference-only Slalom (ICLR 2019), supporting dynamic quantization over "mismatched" cryptographic and GPU data types with good precision/efficiency by stochastically training low-bitwidth yet accurate models. It also tackles system-design challenges with reduced memory-swapping overhead and proposes a round-optimal, cryptographically-secure GPU-outsourcing protocol minimizing communication. Goten outperforms Falcon (PETS 2021, Princeton, UC Berkeley, MSR, Technion, and Algorand), a leading non-colluding-server training framework, by 132.64x using VGG-11. Goten demonstrates its real-world impacts with a showcase of training breast cancer diagnosis models over sensitive images. GForce is an interdisciplinary framework addressing latency challenges in privacy-preserving neural network inference, supporting (non-linear) machine-learning computations hindered by (linear) cryptographic techniques over finite fields. GForce drives a paradigm shift by confronting root causes of latency; eschewing approximated non-linear computations. GForce advances the frontier in low-precision machine learning by introducing stochastic rounding and truncation layers that seamlessly integrate machine-learning computations. GForce also proposes a secure linear computation protocol for non-linear comparison. GForce remains competitively performing in privacy-preserving inference despite emerging follow-ups. Harnessing GPU capabilities and marrying the latest advances in cryptography and machine learning have been followed by many works. Our systematization of knowledge (SoK) systematizes 53 privacy-preserving neural network frameworks from 2016-2022, including 16 using homomorphic encryption, 19 using secure computation for inference, and 18 using non-colluding servers (12 supporting training). It dissects their cryptographic techniques and relationships with machine learning, highlighting noteworthy developments in a comprehensive genealogy. Additionally, we re-evaluate the state of the art under WAN conditions. SoK should not be mistaken for surveys or paper catalogs. Our study offers a valuable guide connecting experts across related fields, meeting IEEE S&P's high SoK standards by providing a rigorous, foundational resource for advancing cryptographic machine learning. DP-Forward presents an innovative DP framework that sanitizes forward-pass signals, diverging from the de facto DP-SGD approach of adding noise to gradients. DP-SGD, requiring per-example gradient computation (>110M parameters), cannot scale for training large (language) models. DP-Forward focuses on real-valued embedding matrices, introducing the aMGM to add calibrated noise, ensuring model accuracy. This reduces communication and computational overhead. Tested on standard datasets like Stanford Sentiment Treebank (SST-2) and IMDb, it mitigates embedding inversion and sensitive attribute inference attacks, lowering attack success rates by up to 88pp and 41pp compared to DP-SGD, demonstrating effectiveness against recent top-tier security attacks.

14210319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14210319.value: Our attacks [IJCAI20] underscore the necessity for rigorous security analysis and highlight the need for collaboration between cryptographers and machine-learning experts to develop practical, provably secure solutions. Our SoK demonstrates GForce's state-of-the-art status in low latency, even compared with non-colluding-server frameworks, while having high throughput under non-ideal network conditions. This SoK provides a comprehensive guide that connects experts across fields, advancing the broader domain of privacy-preserving machine learning. Our [NDSS21] and [AsiaCCS22] techniques in efficient oblivious traversal could inspire the evaluation of graph convolutional networks. Our private set intersection protocol [AsiaCCS22] is directly relevant to data alignment for collaborative training over vertically partitioned datasets. Additionally, our [ICDCS21] and [ACSAC21] (not about machine learning) proposed payment systems that might financially motivate the contribution of training data. LDSP [ICDCS21] supports a dynamic and scalable setup with payer privacy, allowing low-latency, off-chain cryptocurrency transactions. Sipster [ACSAC21] enables private and efficient settlement of IOUs using smart meters, ensuring payer anonymity and efficient verification. Future development will integrate these privacy-preserving techniques into broader applications, enhancing secure data sharing and collaboration in machine learning. Emphasizing interdisciplinary efforts, we aim to refine cryptographic protocols and optimize systems for practical, real-world deployments, advancing privacy-preserving technologies across diverse domains.

14210319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210319.value: Our research focuses on making machine learning and neural networks more secure and private. We developed methods to protect sensitive data while allowing powerful computers to analyze it efficiently. In collaborative training, we created data protection techniques, ensuring each person's information remains private even when shared. One system, Goten, combines advanced encrypted data processing with special hardware to keep data safe during training. Another system, GForce, improves the speed and accuracy of private neural network predictions. We also reviewed over 50 cutting-edge privacy-preserving technologies from different research communities, spanning cryptography to machine learning, providing a valuable resource for future research. Our work contributes to secure and private machine learning by reducing data leak risks while making privacy technologies faster and more effective. This research is crucial for applications ranging from medical data analysis to financial services, ensuring sensitive information is safe while benefiting from advanced data analysis techniques. In an era of ubiquitous AI, including large language models, facial recognition, and autonomous driving, our solutions protect privacy, comply with privacy regulations, advance scientific research without mass surveillance, and address public concerns over data misuse. The results have been presented in peer-reviewed, top-tier scientific conferences with open-source code and reproducible results.

14210419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14210419.value: The growing traffic in data centers, access and metro networks necessitates effective data transmission and detection schemes. However, the conventional coherent detection scheme designed for long haul transmission is comparatively complicated, power inefficient, and expensive. By contrast, direct detection of optical signals in advanced modulation formats is promising owing to system simplicity and low cost. To achieve comparable data capacity as the coherent system, full exploitation of the degrees of freedom provided by optical carriers is necessary, which also facilitates compensation of linear transmission impairments. However, it is challenging to recover the information coded in both quadratures and polarizations by direct detection. In this proposal, we present innovative solutions to realize direct detection of optical quadrature-amplitude-modulated signals in a wavelength- and polarization-division multiplexed transmission system. The recently proposed Kramers-Kronig (KK) direct detection scheme effectively combines coherent transmission with direct detection to reconstruct the complex signal field. The scheme requires a strong carrier which unfortunately will consume power and limit the nonlinear tolerance of the transmission system. Alternatively, a local oscillator can be applied at the receiver, which however faces the issue of unlocked carrier frequency and phase. In this proposal, we investigate three different schemes to regenerate the multi-wavelength carriers after transmission, thereby locking the frequency and phase at the transmitter and receiver. In the first scheme, the central comb line is unmodulated while the remaining channels are modulated with coherent signals. After transmission, by referencing the unmodulated comb line, a locked frequency comb is regenerated for KK detection of other channels. In the second scheme, pilot tones are added at the edge of the signal spectra for all non-central channels. KK detection is realized by using strong carriers obtained from Brillouin amplifying the weak pilot tones through a shifted pump comb generated at the receiver. In the third scheme, all channels carry single sideband signals with relatively low carrier to signal power ratio (CSPR). The CSPR is enhanced when the original modulated comb is Brillouin amplified by its frequency up-converted copy before KK detection. To identify the practical challenges of KK detection system and to further improve its performance and expedite its deployment, we extend our investigation to include the following: field test of the system over a deployed fiber link, addition of optical phase conjugators to mitigate nonlinear signal distortion and increase the transmission distance, and realization of optical transmitter and receiver on integrated silicon photonic platform. 隨著數據中心、接入網和城域網數據流量的迅速增長，人們需要更為有效的數據傳輸及探測方案。然而，用於長距離傳輸的傳統相干光探測方案有著結構複雜、能效水準低、成本昂貴等缺點。相比之下，直接探測方式大大降低了系統成本和複雜度。因此，對高階調製格式的光信號使用直接探測是大有前景的。為了實現與傳統相干光通信系統相當的數據容量，直接探測必須充分利用光載波的自由度，這也有利於補償線性傳輸損傷。然而，通過直接探測方式同時恢復雙正交態和雙偏振態中的編碼信息是極具挑戰性的。在本研究中，我們提出了新的解決方案，以實現傳輸系統中對波分偏振複用正交幅度調製(QAM)信號的直接探測。 最近提出的基於Kramers-Kronig(KK)關係的單光電探測器相干接收機有效地結合了傳統相干光傳輸和直接探測，以重建覆信號，即QAM信號。此方案需要一個強連續光載波，但這個載波會限制信號的光功率，並且會限制傳輸系統對非線性效應的容限。為了解決這個問題，人們可以在接收端應用本地振盪器，然而這面臨著光載波頻率和相位的失鎖問題。在本研究中，我們探討了三種重建多波長載波的方案，用以實現發射和接收端的頻率和相位的鎖定和同步。第一種方案中，光頻梳的中心頻率分量未被調製，而其餘通道用相干方式調製信號。在接收端，我們參考未調製的光頻梳分量，重新生成了頻率鎖定的光頻梳並且用以其他通道的KK探測。第二種方案中，在發射端，所有非中心通道的信號頻譜邊緣處都添加了光功率較低的連續光載波。在接收端，頻移放大後的光頻梳作為泵浦光，通過受激布裡淵散射(SBS)放大了原光頻梳的光功率，並生成了高光功率的光頻梳，從而實現KK探測。第三種方案中，所有通道都載有低載波信號功率比(CSPR)的單邊帶信號。在接收端，原始的調製光頻梳被自身的頻移項進行了SBS放大，CSPR得到增強，從而完成KK探測。 為了鑒定KK單光電直接探測系統的實際應用可行性，進一步改善其性能，並加快其部署，我們擴展了研究範圍。擴展的研究範圍包括：光纖通信鏈路系統中信號傳輸通道的現場測試，增加光學相位共軛對減輕非線性信號失真以及增加傳輸距離的影響，集成矽光子平臺中光收發機功能的實現。

14210419.label: Realisation of objectives
14210419.value: 1. To regenerate optical frequency combs by the proposed schemes and to characterize their qualities Following our proposal, we have successfully demonstrated the regeneration of optical frequency combs for WDM systems by applying self-seeded stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) at the optical receiver [J2, C3]. The comb consists of 5 frequency tones spaced at 30 GHz. Each frequency tone carries a data signal at 10-Gbaud with 16-QAM orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) single-sideband signals. The Brillouin amplification is performed in a dispersion shifted fiber using a Brillouin pump obtained from a frequency upshifted copy of the signal comb. After the amplification, the carrier to signal power ratio (CSPR) of the optical frequency comb is improved from 5 dB to ~12.5 dB with an SBS pump power of 63 mW. A drawback of applying Brillouin amplification is that it will introduce a phase variation that is spectrally dependent, giving rise to signal distortion. To minimize this effect, we have developed an optical interferometric approach that results in a significant reduction of the phase variation by a factor of 5.54 [J3]. In addition, we have demonstrated programmable optical frequency comb generation by cross-phase modulation in a silicon photonic waveguide [C4, C5]. To improve the carrier-to-noise ratio of the frequency combs and to support their use in reconfigurable communication systems, we have applied programmable Talbot processing to tune the frequency spacing [J5, C8] and to purify the frequency combs by passive amplification [J7, C7]. With the availability of high-quality frequency combs, we have achieved wideband wavelength multicast of a single-sideband signal by applying ultrafast cross-phase modulation, supporting high-capacity KK detection links while minimizing the usage of network resources [J4]. 2. To demonstrate the proposed frequency comb based KK detection systems and to investigate the different effects of operating parameters on the system performance We have analyzed and built the comb-based KK detection system using the frequency comb regeneration technique described in the previous paragraph. Different effects of the operating parameters have been measured, and BER system performances have been obtained [J2, C3]. The BER values without and with the comb regeneration are 4.64×10^(-2) and 1.45×10^(-2), respectively. The corresponding Q factor is improved by 2.27 dB. The constellation diagrams also show the superior functionality of the proposed regeneration technique in improving the system performance. Our scheme enables low-CSPR signal transmission by enhancing the CSPR prior to the KK detection, thus minimizing the propagation-induced distortion while maintaining the minimum phase condition for the receiver link. In addition, the BER performance of all channels have been measured as a function of the optical signal-to-noise ratio (OSNR), as well as a function of the Brillouin gain applied in the frequency comb regeneration. We also extend our work to investigate learning rate decay in least mean square based channel equalization for a KK detection system, removing inter-symbol interference induced by non-flat channel response [J1]. In addition, we apply KK detection in a high-capacity wavelength multicast system enabled by optical frequency combs [J4]. More than 20 channel copies of a 40-Gb/s QPSK OFDM single-sideband signal are generated with a frequency spacing of 50 GHz. With KK detection, we observe that the difference in the required OSNR among the central 16 channels is less than 1.3 dB at the HD-FEC threshold. In addition, by applying a feed-forward fitting artificial neural network, we can precisely determine the scaling factor used in a rate-adaptive communication system [J6], supporting effective use of system bandwidth in both conventional and KK-detection based transmission links. Further improvement has been demonstrated by adopting entropy loading in our frequency comb-based communication system [J8]. 3. To identify the practical challenges of KK detection systems and to develop enabling technologies for boosting the system performances and reducing the transponder footprint In the proposal, we suggested to use optical phase conjugation to mitigate transmission impairments caused by optical dispersion and nonlinearity in a KK receiver link. We have performed both simulation and experiments to prove that this is in fact an effective approach to improve the system performance, despite that there are certain limitations in the deployment of optical phase conjugator (OPC) in transmission links. Compared to digital compensation of chromatic dispersion, OPC improves the Q factor by 0.9 dB, optimum launched optical power (LOP) by 1.0 dB and OSNR sensitivity by 1.7 dB in a 180-km SMF transmission experiment. In the simulation, the OPC also achieves higher optimum LOP compared to the case of chromatic dispersion compensation using DCF. The performance enhancement from OPC leads to an extension of the transmission distance by 135 km. Our scheme is proved to be an effective approach in enhancing SSB signal transmission systems. Also, we propose an artificial neural network based demodulation block to mitigate the effect caused by signal-signal beat noise in a KK receiver link. Experimental results show that our proposed scheme outperforms the conventional Volterra equalizer assisted scheme [C2]. Besides, we have demonstrated that the signal-signal beat noise can be mitigated by simply computing the square root (SQRT) of the detected photocurrent. Performance comparison between the original received signal, the SQRT processed signal, and the KK processed signal is experimentally conducted in a single sideband direct detection system carrying 110 Gb/s probabilistically shaped 64 QAM signal for a 100-km single mode fiber transmission. The SQRT scheme reduces the required CSPR and OSNR by 2.7 dB and 4.6 dB respectively with reference to the performance of the original signal, while induces additional penalty compared to the KK scheme that relies on the Hilbert transform. [C1]. Towards reducing the transponder footprint, we investigate the generation of optical frequency combs on the silicon photonic platform. The frequency combs can be effectively used to carry WDM based single sideband signals, as well as in facilitating high-capacity wavelength multicast. The technique can potentially be applied to the regeneration of optical frequency combs at the receiver side for multi-wavelength KK transmission links. With the use of ultrafast cross-phase modulation on the silicon waveguide [J5, C4, C5], we have generated optical frequency combs with spacings ranging from 140 to 200 GHz. We also achieve a maximum carrier-to-noise power suppression ratio (CNR) of 45 dB. Apart from silicon photonic based frequency combs, we also investigate an integrated photonic solution for performing stimulated Brillouin scattering [C6]. Our 1-cm long waveguide is designed to be supported by periodic pillars on a silica substrate. Experimentally, we observe a Brillouin resonant frequency of 8.23 GHz and an acoustic mode quality factor of 155. The findings shed light on potential use of silicon nanowire waveguide for frequency comb regeneration at the receiver, given that the interaction length can be extended to tens of cm to provide sufficient gain filtering to enhance the CNR. Lastly, we develop new methods to purify the optical frequency combs and to improve the CNR by Talbot processing, making use of coherent addition of the power in neighboring frequency tones [J7, C7, C8]. With a multiplied mode spacing of 94.5 GHz and up to 35 dB CNR, we have experimentally demonstrated 80-km transmission of complex-modulated signals on a 10-channel frequency comb, each carrying 32-Gbaud PCS-64QAM modulation [C8].

14210419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14210419.value: The primary objectives of this research were to: (1) Regenerate high-quality optical frequency combs and characterize their properties, and (2) Demonstrate comb-based Kramers-Kronig (KK) detection systems while investigating the effects of operating parameters on their performances. We have successfully demonstrated regeneration of optical frequency combs for WDM systems using self-seeded stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) to enhance the carrier-to-signal power ratio at the receiver. A 5-tone comb was generated with 30 GHz spacing, where each tone carried a 10 Gbaud 16-QAM OFDM signal [J2, C3]. With the Brillouin amplification, the carrier-to-signal power ratio was enhanced from 5 dB to 12.5 dB. However, Brillouin amplification also introduced phase distortion in the communication signals. To mitigate this distortion, we have developed an interferometric approach that reduced the phase variation by a factor of 5.54 [J3]. Meanwhile, we also demonstrated programmable comb generation in an integrated silicon photonic platform using cross-phase modulation [C4, C5], and applied Talbot processing to tune the comb spacing and improve the carrier-to-noise ratio [J5, J7, C7, C8]. Using the regenerated combs, we have built and analyzed KK detection systems. We observed BER performance improvements and Q-factor enhancement by 2.27 dB using the comb regeneration technique [J2, C3]. The regeneration capability of the comb-based KK systems enabled low carrier-to-signal power ratio transmission while maintaining the minimum phase condition. We also investigated channel equalization [J1], wavelength multicast [J4], and rate adaptation techniques [J6, J8] for communication systems supporting complex modulated signals. To address practical challenges, we demonstrated that optical phase conjugation can effectively mitigate transmission impairments, extending the reach by 135 km compared to chromatic dispersion compensation alone. Furthermore, we have proposed an artificial neural network-based demodulator to reduce signal-signal beat noise, outperforming conventional Volterra equalization [C2]. Finally, we explored integrated photonic solutions to reduce the transponder footprint. We have generated high-quality optical frequency combs on the silicon photonic platform, achieving up to 45 dB carrier-to-noise ratio [J5, C4, C5]. An integrated Brillouin waveguide was also demonstrated, offering a potential path for comb regeneration [C6]. We apply novel Talbot processing method to further purify the combs, enabling 80 km transmission of 10-channel 32 Gbaud PCS-64QAM signals [J7, C7, C8]. In summary, our research has advanced the state-of-the-art in optical frequency comb generation and regeneration, KK detection systems, and integrated photonic solutions to enable high-capacity fiber-optic communications.

14210419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14210419.value: Our research project is focused on developing advanced optical communication technologies that can significantly enhance the performance and efficiency of high-speed data networks. The key aspects of our work are in regenerating high-quality optical frequency combs and demonstrating comb-based Kramers-Kronig (KK) communication links. We have developed a new method to generate programmable optical frequency combs that can carry multiple data channels simultaneously. The frequency combs are critical for enabling more efficient use of the available optical bandwidth and associated network resources. We also explored novel signal detection techniques that leverage these regenerated combs to improve the quality and reach of data transmission, even when operating with low power signals. The significance of our research lies in its potential to address some of the fundamental challenges in optical communication systems. By improving comb regeneration and enabling more advanced detection methods, our work can lead to increased capacity, lower power consumption, and extended reach for high-speed data networks. This has immense value for modern society, as it can support the growing demand for faster, more reliable, and more energy-efficient internet connectivity - critical for applications like 5G, cloud computing, and data centers. Our innovations can ultimately enhance the overall performance and accessibility of global digital infrastructure.

14300119.label: Project Objectives
14300119.value: Study of higher-order correlation functions of sequential weak measurement on single nuclear spins via an electron spin sensor. The sequential weak measurement can be mapped to an effective pseudo-spin model. Therefore, the measurement correlations will be analyzed using the methods and concepts of statistical mechanics of spin models (such as phase transitions, correlation lengths, critical exponents, and Lee-Yang zeros). The higher order correlations will be utilized to identify and characterize the couplings and correlations in nuclear spin clusters.

14300119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300119.value: 本項目將發展用於探測多核自旋的多維關聯譜技術，該技術能在單核自旋尺度上達到亞Hz的譜分辨率。 在單分子級別上對核自旋之間的耦合以及關聯進行區分、標定以及操控不僅對於單分子核磁共振非常必要而且對於基於磁共振的可擴展量子計算也非常有用。雖然傳統多維核磁共振譜也能用於探測核自旋之間的耦合，但是其低靈敏度限制了在自旋系綜中的應用。近年來單分子核磁共振已經通過動力學解耦的辦法實現。而且，結構化的動力學解耦控制也被提出用於單核自旋尺度上的多維磁共振量子探測。然而，基於動力學解耦方法的量子探測的譜分辨率受到了探測自旋的退相干時間的限制(大概kHz)。對於探測經典信號，關聯譜方法原則上可以達到任意譜分辨率。然而，將其用於探測量子目標要解決量子測量反作用所導致的譜展寬問題。量子弱測量方法可以用來減小量子反作用。本研究組與合作者先前的研究工作表明了序列弱測量是一種有潛力的方法(在金剛石中探測C-13核的譜分辨率達到了3.4Hz)。但是迄今為止，本方法只局限於二階關聯和探測獨立單核自旋。 本項目將研究對核自旋集團進行弱測量所引起的高階關聯。我們將通過對氮空色心進行光學探測實現對核自旋的弱測量。在序列弱測量下，有效的贗自旋模型成立，因此統計力學中的有關於自旋模型的方法以及概念，比如相變、臨界指數、關聯長度、以及李楊零點，就可以用來分析弱測量的關聯信號。我們將審示高階關聯是否可以用來揭示出隱藏在二階關聯中的核自旋的信息以及鑒別與標定核自旋集團中的耦合和關聯。核自旋之間真實的相互作用與測量氮色心所誘導的有效相互作用會相互影響。我們將研究如何利用它們之間的相互影響, 從而通過弱測量來操縱核自旋集團的量子演化以及操控它們之間的關聯。 本項目將有助於促進單分子核磁共振譜技術和結構分析以及發展新的工具用於基於核自旋比特的可擴展量子計算。

14300119.label: Realisation of objectives
14300119.value: The objectives of this project have been fulfilled. I. To address the first objective, we developed the theory of higher order quantum correlations for the detection of single nuclear spins using electron spin sensors. We established the theory of quantum nonlinear spectroscopy based on the extraction of arbitrary types and orders of correlations in a target using a quantum sensor. This theory presents a shift of paradigm from classical nonlinear spectroscopy to quantum nonlinear spectroscopy. In conventional nonlinear spectroscopy, which is widely used in optics, magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and transport, a target system is perturbed by a classical force and consequently the response of the target system contains only commutators of system operators. In quantum sensing, the “force” is a quantum operator of the sensor and therefore the response of the target system contains both commutators and anti-commutators of system operators. The quantum nature of the “force” from the sensor makes it possible to select which kind of responses (commutator or anti-commutator) is detected by choosing how the sensor is initialized and is measured. Therefore, quantum nonlinear spectroscopy can measure the full set of correlation functions of a quantum system while conventional nonlinear spectroscopy can detect only one type. Furthermore, we propose that the higher-order quantum correlation can be exploited for classical-noise-free sensing. We demonstrate that quantum sensing can not only enhance existing metrological technologies (imaging, detection, spectroscopy, etc.) as shown in numerous previous works, but also enable new approaches that have no classical counterparts. The key idea is that the quantum nature (quantumness) of the sensors and the targets makes it possible to detect quantum correlations of the target that is not accessible to a classical probe and/or does not exist in a classical target. As a concrete and non-trivial example, we show that the higher order quantum correlations of a quantum target (a single spin) can be measured through a quantum sensor to detect the target fully free of classical noise background, even when the target would be undetectable using conventional correlation methods. This noise exclusion method is based on the fact that the classical quantities commute, but quantum ones do not in general. Thus, a correlation containing a commutator is fully free of the effects of classical noises. Such a general approach to suppressing noise effects in quantum sensing, unlike conventional ones (such as dynamical decoupling or quantum error correction), does not rely on the specific properties of the noise. It works for Gaussian and non-Gaussian noises, weak and strong noises, color and white noises, and so on. In collaboration with the HKUST team, we realized the detection of single nuclear spins in diamond objects free of classical noise via correlation-based quantum signal distillation’. We design a novel correlation-based quantum signal distillation method to single out the quantum signal of a remote nuclear spin from overwhelming classical noise backgrounds, which is impossible to be removed by conventional filter methods. Our work demonstrates the quantum-classical nature as a new degree of freedom in quantum signal processing. The technique demonstrated is easy to implement in a broad of physical qubit systems. II. To address the second objectives, we developed the quantum sensing theory to distinguish different types of classical and quantum noises and used the quantum nonlinear spectroscopy to detect multiple nuclear spins. We show that quantum nonlinear spectroscopy provides fingerprint features to identify different types of objects, such as Gaussian noises, random-phased AC fields, and quantum spins, which would be indistinguishable in second-order correlations. We carried out the measurement of the fourth order correlations of nuclear spins in diamond using sequential weak measurement. The measured fourth-order correlation unambiguously differentiates a single nuclear spin and a random-phased AC field. It also provides a discrete count of the number of spins (similar to the photon-count correlation for determining the number of quantum emitters). Using the quantum correlation approach, we achieved the parallel characterization of quantum states of multiple nuclear spins. Characterization of quantum states is vital for quantum computing, simulation and sensing. However, it is non-trivial for a quantum system involving dark qubits, such as nuclear spins and magnons, where no direct readout methods are available. Through measurement of different types of quantum correlations of multiple nuclear spins using an electron spin quantum sensor, the quantum state of dark qubits has been reconstructed. This method does not require strong coupling conditions, so it can characterize the quantum state of multiple dark qubits in parallel. This greatly reduces experimental overhead. Specifically, we used the second-order quantum correlations to characterize quantum states of nuclear spins in a hybrid system composed of a nitrogen-vacancy center (bright qubit) and several nuclear spins (dark qubits) and monitor the dynamics of their quantum states.

14300119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300119.value: 1. Classical noise-free detection of quantum objects using higher-order quantum correlations. We show that the higher order quantum correlations of a quantum target (a single spin) can be measured through a quantum sensor to detect the target fully free of classical noise background, even when the target would be undetectable using conventional methods. This new noise-resilient approach does not rely on the specific (statistical, spectral, etc) properties of the noise. In collaboration with the HKUST team, we realized the detection of single nuclear spins in diamond free of classical noise using correlation-based quantum sensing. These works were published in [Chinese Physics Letters 38, 010301 (2021); Physical Review Letters 130, 070802 (2023)] 2. Quantum nonlinear spectroscopy – a paradigm shift in quantum sensing We put forward a new theory of quantum nonlinear spectroscopy, which makes a shift of paradigm from classical nonlinear spectroscopy to quantum nonlinear spectroscopy. In quantum sensing, the “force” is a quantum operator of the sensor and therefore the response of the target system contains both commutators and anti-commutators of system operators. The quantum nature of the “force” from the sensor makes it possible to select which kind of responses (commutator or anti-commutator) is detected by choosing how the sensor is initialized and is measured. Therefore, quantum nonlinear spectroscopy can measure the full set of correlation functions of a quantum system while conventional nonlinear spectroscopy can detect only one type. We use a nitrogen-vacancy centre spin as the sensor to apply a quantum “force” and detect the correlations of a single nuclear spin (as well as a classical random noise for comparison) up to the fourth order. We demonstrate the usefulness of the quantum nonlinear spectroscopy by showing that a quantum spin target and a classical random noise have indistinguishable second-order correlation functions but have distinct spectral characteristics in their fourth-order correlations. This work was published in [Nature Communications 13, 5318 (2022)]. 3. We established a theory on the formation of strong projective interaction using the data of a sequence of weak measurement and applied the general theory to the case of the detection of single nuclear spins using an electron spin quantum sensor. The papers are published in [Physical Review A 107, 012217 (2023)] and [Physical Review Applied 19, 054037 (2023)].

14300119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300119.value: We established a new theory of quantum sensing, coined quantum nonlinear spectroscopy, which uses a quantum object to detect arbitrary types and orders of correlations in a quantum target, while the conventional method can only access very few of the many different types of correlations. This method enables the detection of quantum objects free of classical noise background, regardless of the specific properties of the noises. We apply this method to detect single nuclear spins in diamond and managed to characterize the states of multiple spins in parallel. These works constitute a shift of paradigm from classical nonlinear spectroscopy to quantum nonlinear spectroscopy. It also makes a transition from enhancing to enabling by quantum sensing. The capability to detect arbitrary types and orders of quantum correlations opens a window for studying quantum many-body physics, for loophole-free test of quantum foundation, and for ultrasensitive detection of quantum objects. The detection and characterization of multiple nuclear spins in parallel offers a new platform (a hybrid electron-nuclear spin system) for quantum information processing and quantum memory.

14300219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300219.value: Image recovery refers to the process of restoring sharp and clean images from degraded observations. This is a very important image processing task with various scientific, medical, engineering, and commercial applications. For example, deforestation ratio can be estimated more accurately if the image quality of forest regions is improved in SAR images, and in cryo-EM imaging biologist can understand the molecular mechanism much better if one can obtain high resolution 3D reconstructions of the molecule from noisy and blurry 2D micrographs. Since there are various types of images and they are usually degraded by different types of blurs and noises, image recovery remains a challenging task. We propose to design novel and efficient methods to recover images degraded by serious blur and heavy noise, and we propose to extend our new methods for two fields of applications: SAR imaging and cryo-EM imaging. Unlike classical recovery problems, SAR images suffer from heavy multiplicative noise and blur. The aim is to recover clean and sharp images so that people can detect objects correctly, such as tree branches, roads or rivers. Multiplicative noise is intensity dependent and is difficult to remove. It is also difficult to maintain structures of elongated objects during the recovery. In cryo-EM image processing, the aim is to reconstruct macromolecular structures from 2D images which are corrupted by heavy noise and blur. The degradation limit resolution of the 3D reconstruction. The changes of spatial orientations of the molecules when 2D images are taken make recoveries more challenging. Recovery methods which exploit statistical information of noise and spatial information of objects can improve restoration results. Our novel recovery approach is based on variational frameworks and a deep learning method proposed by us recently. Our deep learning method can learn the relationship between degraded images and soft edges of the corresponding high quality images. Based on the deep learning model, we propose an edge regularization which can better restore fine details and edges. To better suit the two fields, we also propose to add other regularization such as the Euler elastica term or the mean curvature term. Our new approach will adopt different fidelity terms suitable for various noises. We will design efficient solvers for our new models, and we will provide new theories such as convergence and speed of the solvers. Extensive numerical experiments and comparisons with other state-of-the-art methods will be provided. 圖像恢復是指從觀測到的存在污染的數據中恢復清晰圖像的過程。這是一項非常重要的圖像處理任務，具有各種科學，醫學，工程和商業應用的價值。例如，利用合成孔徑雷達來觀測森林區域，如果可以改善雷達成像的質量，則可以更準確地估計森林砍伐率。在冷凍電鏡成像中，如果可以從含有噪聲和模糊的二維顯微照片中獲得分子的高分辨率三維重建，那么生物學家將可以更好地理解分子機制。由於存在各種類型的圖像並且它們通常被不同類型的模糊和噪聲所污染，因此圖像恢復仍然是具有挑戰性的任務。我們設計新穎有效的方法來恢復被強模糊和嚴重噪聲污染的圖像，我們將擴展所提出的方法並用於兩個領域：合成孔徑雷達成像和冷凍電鏡成像。與經典恢復問題不同，合成孔徑雷達圖像受到大量乘性噪聲和模糊的污染。我們的目的是恢復乾淨和清晰的圖像，以便人們可以正確地檢測物體，例如樹幹，道路或河流。乘性噪聲與圖像信號強度有關，因此難以去除。而且在恢復圖像時維持細長物體的結構也很困難。在冷凍電鏡圖像處理中，我們的目標是從被嚴重噪聲和模糊破壞的二維圖像中重建大分子結構。因為污染的存在，三維重建的分辨率很難提高。在拍攝二維圖像時，不斷改變的分子空間方向也使得圖像恢復更具挑戰性。我們提出的方法還將分析並利用觀測對象的噪聲和空間數據的統計信息來改善圖像恢復效果。

14300219.label: Realisation of objectives
14300219.value: 1. Development of the soft-edge approach The objective was to develop the soft-edge approach systematically by utilizing various data-fitting terms with different smooth or nonsmooth regularizers and higher-order derivative operators. We successfully achieved this goal by employing a comprehensive range of mathematical techniques and algorithms. Through rigorous experimentation and analysis, we explored the effectiveness of different combinations of data-fitting terms, regularizers, and derivative operators. Our research yielded promising results, demonstrating the versatility and adaptability of the soft-edge approach. We developed a systematic framework that allows for flexible customization of the approach based on specific application requirements. This achievement significantly enhances the applicability and effectiveness of the soft-edge approach in various fields. 2. Efficient and accurate recovery models for image super-resolution in SAR Imaging The objective was to design recovery models that can efficiently and accurately enhance the resolution of images in Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imaging. We made substantial progress by developing novel and efficient algorithms tailored specifically for SAR image super-resolution. Our models leveraged advanced machine learning techniques, such as deep neural networks, and incorporated domain-specific knowledge to achieve superior performance. Through extensive evaluation and comparison with existing methods, we demonstrated that our proposed models outperformed state-of-the-art approaches in terms of both accuracy and computational efficiency. The successful realization of this objective contributes to improved image quality and enhanced interpretation capabilities in SAR imaging applications. 3. Better image recovery results from 2D Cryo-EM micrograph observations. The objective was to design models that could provide improved image recovery results from 2D cryo-EM micrograph observations. While progress was made in this area, we encountered some challenges due to the inherent complexity and noise characteristics of cryo-EM data. Despite these difficulties, we developed innovative approaches and novel algorithms to address the unique requirements of cryo-EM image recovery. Although the achieved results fell slightly short of our initial expectations, our models still exhibited notable improvements over traditional methods. We utilized advanced denoising techniques, and regularization strategies to enhance the recovery quality. Additionally, we conducted extensive simulations and comparative analyses to validate the effectiveness of our proposed models. 4. Enhanced recovery results for 3D Cryo-EM image reconstruction. The objective was to design models that could provide better recovery results for 3D cryo-EM image reconstruction. We invested substantial effort in this area and achieved significant advancements in the field of cryo-EM image reconstruction. Our research focused on developing robust algorithms that could accurately reconstruct high-resolution 3D structures from sparse and noisy cryo-EM data. By integrating advanced optimization methods, regularization techniques, and prior knowledge about the cryo-EM imaging process, we improved the accuracy and fidelity of the reconstructed 3D images. While the complexity of the problem made it challenging to achieve perfect results, our models demonstrated noteworthy improvements in the quality and resolution of the reconstructed cryo-EM images. 5. Development of efficient solvers for addressed models. The objective was to develop efficient solvers for the models addressed in our research. We dedicated significant attention to this aspect and successfully devised optimized algorithms and computational techniques. Our solvers significantly reduced the computational burden associated with the addressed models, enhancing their practicality and scalability. We employed a combination of optimization algorithms, and algorithmic optimizations to achieve efficient solvers. Through extensive benchmarking and performance evaluations, we demonstrated the effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed solvers in handling large-scale datasets and complex models. In conclusion, we have made substantial progress in realizing the objectives outlined in this project. We successfully developed the soft-edge approach systematically, designed efficient and accurate recovery models for image super-resolution in SAR imaging, and made notable advancements in image recovery from 2D and 3D cryo-EM observations. Additionally, we developed efficient solvers that contribute to the practical applicability of the addressed models. Although we faced challenges and encountered some limitations, we actively addressed these issues through innovative approaches, rigorous experimentation, and in-depth analysis. Our findings and achievements have the potential to significantly impact the fields of image processing, SAR imaging, and cryo-EM, paving the way for future advancements and applications.

14300219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300219.value: 1. An efficient and trusty denoising scheme, which combines the convolutional neural network (CNN) technique with the traditional variational model, offers interpretable and high-quality reconstructions. 2. A new three-stage segmentation framework based on a convex variant of the Mumford--Shah model and the intensity inhomogeneity information of an image. 3. A novel deep-learning-based image denoiser prior to effectively remove Cauchy noise with blur. Numerical experiments demonstrate clearly that our method has better performance than the existing image restoration methods for removing Cauchy noise in terms of the quantitative index and visual quality. 4. A multilevel edge features guided network (MLEFGN). Extensive experiments clearly illustrate that our MLEFGN achieves favorable performance against other methods and plenty of ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed Edge-Net and MLEFGN. 5. A fast directional spherical Haar framelet transform and develop a novel optimization framework based on a sparsity assumption of the framelet transform. Numerical experiments are conducted and show that the proposed algorithms can greatly recover damaged spherical images and achieve the best performance over purely using a deep learning denoiser and a plug-and-play model. 6. A new real-time scene recovery framework to restore degraded images under different weather/imaging conditions, such as underwater, sand dust, and haze. Comprehensive experiments of the scene recovery illustrate that our method outperforms competitively several state-of-the-art imaging methods in terms of efficiency and robustness. 7. A three-dimensional weighted nuclear norm minimization (3DWNNM) model for single-particle reconstruction in the cryo-EM task. Numerical experiments fully demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method. 8. A quaternion-based WNNM method (QWNNM) for color image restoration. Numerical experiments are carefully conducted with different kinds of degradation to illustrate the superior performance of our proposed QWNNM over the state-of-the-art methods, including a celebrated deep learning approach, in both visual quality and numerical results. 9. An efficient boosted difference of convex functions algorithm (BDCA) for solving the MAP-Rician model. Numerical simulations are then reported to clearly illustrate that our BDCA approach outperforms some state-of-the-art methods for both medical and natural images in terms of image recovery capability and CPU-time cost. 10. A novel quaternion-based color image recovery method that combines the advantages of dictionary learning and the total variation method for color image restoration. 11. An overlapping domain decomposition method for solving the nonconvex optimization problem in ptychographic imaging.

14300219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300219.value: Image recovery is a fundamental task in image processing, aiming to enhance the quality of images that have been affected by various factors. It involves recovering or reconstructing degraded image scenes from complex scenarios. This research project focuses on developing efficient novel image recovery models using variational approaches, with a strong emphasis on practical applications. Previous attempts at image recovery have involved complex algorithms designed for specific conditions. These algorithms are highly intricate and impose strict conditions, limiting their versatility. In contrast, this project adopts variational approaches based on the theory of image recovery, image restoration, optimization, and statistics to address the challenges of image recovery. The research primarily focuses on several crucial aspects, including the development of explainable models and efficient algorithms that consider blurring effects, different weather conditions, and noise the extension of recovery techniques to handle heavy noise. These aspects represent critical issues that require substantial research to advance the field of image recovery. The significance of this research extends beyond academia, as it is directly applicable to real-life scenarios. By improving image recovery techniques, this research has the potential to enhance image quality, enabling better analysis, understanding, and decision-making based on high-quality visual information.

14300319.label: Project Objectives
14300319.value: (LRT for monotonicity of density) Though there is a well-established estimation theory for monotonic NPMLE for density, the Grenander estimator, statistical testings for monotonicity are still rare in the literature. We first plan to resolve the long-standing problem of finding the asymptotic behavior of the likelihood ratio test (LRT) for the global monotonicity of density. To conquer this, we propose to first decompose the LRT statistic into two terms: one involving consecutive uniformly distributed spacings, and another one with monotonic structure. For the first term, a tricky use of Renyi's lemma together with the classical limit theory should deduce its asymptotic distribution. While for the second term, due to the involvement of the Grenander estimator, asymptotic properties of the latter and other shape-constrained estimation theory together with the techniques developed in our work of Chan et al. (2018) could be adopted to obtain the corresponding limiting behavior. Perhaps whenever LRT is involved, one may expect to see the asymptotic Chi-square distribution (Wilk, 1983); or one may guess about the connection of the present LRT statistic with Chernoff's distribution arisen in monotonic density estimation (Groeneboom, 1983; Groeneboom & Wellner, 2001). Instead, a preliminary investigation suggests that the targeted one should rely neither of those, but it should even be distribution-free, indeed. (LRT for log-concavity of density) In recent years, research on density estimation subject to log-concavity has become very popular in mathematical statistics; however, the testing counterpart remains barely touched except a few works. We now plan to provide a complete solution to the open problem of deriving the limiting distribution of the LRT statistic for global log-concavity of density. To this end, we believe that, by combining some other latest convergence results in the field such as those in Doss and Wellner (2016), the methodology to be developed in (1) could be modified and used to resolve all the matter. (Higher order theory and power analysis) A higher order theory will also be investigated so as to strengthen the effectiveness of the LRT statistic if the first order theory, to be constructed in (1) and (2), is truly free from the underlying density. Furthermore, power analysis concerning the consistency of the LRT statistic under the alternative hypothesis would also be explored in detail by using various tools in shape-constrained inference and our own expertise in limit theory and statistical testing. Finally, various simulation studies would be carried out.

14300319.value: 在大數據時代，若預先了解所收集的稀疏但相關的數據背後的理論機制和本質，便能夠有效地提高預測能力。當然，如果潛在的參數模型是已知的，其效率應該是最理想的，但事實並非如此。幸好，透過一些先驗的溫和拓撲結構，其相應非參數統計推斷的效率已經可以獲得顯著的改善;這也解釋了最近數理統計中備受關注的形狀約束推斷。所有形狀約束的估計量都具有共同的特徵，即保留相同的形狀結構，即原始理論所建議的形狀結構。代表例子之一是密度函數的單調性或分佈的凹性。除此以外，形狀約束推斷在社會科學，工程及生物科學上都有廣泛的應用;例如，隨著密度假設的減少，Langaas等（2005）估計 DNA微陣列數據中滿足零假設的次數比例; Jewel和Shiboski（1990）; Jewel和van der Laan（1995）基於當前的狀態數據，估計了免疫缺陷病毒（HIV）傳播可能性的分佈函數。此外，最近亦有很多的研究是關於對數 - 凹性的密度函數及受單調性比例影響的密度函數對的估計理論。然而，假設檢驗及診斷某些形狀結構的存在性，仍然幾乎沒有被觸及，以致有相當多的未解問題; 我們目前提出的研究的項目旨在提供完整方案解決一些形狀結構存在性中具代表性的未解問題。 研究項目中的其中一部分，我們研究用作測試密度函數全局單調性的似然比檢驗（LRT）統計量的極限表現。 根據我們的初步研究，根據威爾克定理，它在零假設下的漸近分佈應該與廣受認知的卡方分佈有很大的不同。我們將在基於替代假設下進行進一步的功率分析。該解決方法將巧妙地結合順序統計理論和形狀約束估計理論（Groeneboom和Jongbloed，2014），以及在我們以前的研究中開發了的各種方法：Chan等（2018）。 如上所述，受對數凹陷影響的估計最近受到了很大關注，並且它能被應用在統計和經濟學中的各種問題上，參見Walther（2009）和Bagnoli和Bergstorm（2005）。其他近期在統計領域的理論和應用上的進展，例如：Samworth（2017）摘要了回歸，聚類和分類。儘管如此，測試全局對數 - 凹性的研究仍只有很少，我們將在第二部分討論一些相關的未解決問題。當中，我們將應用在前一部分中的機制，並結合在Doss和Doss中獲得的全局收斂率，和Wellner（2016），以建立密度函數的全局對數凹性的LRT統計量的漸近理論。 我們將探討這些理論在社會科學和物理科學領域上的可能應用。我們的總體研究目標將通過以下研究課題來完成：形狀約束估計，經驗過程理論，遍歷理論和泛函分析。我們預期（1）提供一些形狀受限推斷上未解問題的完全解，以及其在生物統計學和人口學中的潛在應用; （2）統一針對測試對數似然比率序的技巧及豐富其應用，並在金融風險管理發揮持久影響力（3）建立一套有系統及通用的方法來實現全局單調結構的各種LRT統計數據的漸近表現

14300319.label: Realisation of objectives
14300319.value: For Revised Objective 1: The objective is accomplished with a number of publications and more extensions obtained as stated below. a) In the s-sample biased sampling models in [2], we first show that the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator of the decreasing density function is asymptotically the left-continuous slope of the least concave majorant of that for the distribution in the larger model, without assuming monotonicity. In particular, due to the different proof directions in showing the weak convergence of these two estimators, we require extra results so as to establish their weak convergence in a unified approach, such as the tightness of an inverse processes associated with the estimator. We demonstrate other results in connection with testing in particular via numerical simulation and a real data illustration. b) Some methodologies and ideas stemming from [2] also motivated our research in other statistical tests and estimation. For example, in [1], we study the applicability of Benford’s law and Zipf’s law, two commonly adopted laws in hypothesis testing in fraud detection, to national COVID-19 case figures, based on formal statistical analysis can be developed. In particular, Benford’s law imposes a decreasing shape constraint on the distribution of digits, that allows us to apply our proposed methodology in this work. In [8], we propose a portmanteau hypothesis test on the shape of the graph-structured network, and discuss its asymptotic distribution under the null hypothesis.. Numerical simulations are carried out to demonstrate and confirm the derived asymptotic results, and a significant increase in statistical power is also observed relative to some recently proposed permutation tests. For Revised Objective 2: The objective is accomplished, and the key results are now published with some further extensions. a) For a study with cross-sectional sampling without any follow-up in [9], we study the corresponding nonparametric estimation of the underlying survival function of a survival time now with a shape constraint, which had been absent in the literature before our work. Under a stationarity assumption on disease incidence rate in the population, the survival function S_0 is related to the observed density of the backward recurrence time, f_0, via the relationship S_0(x) = f_0(0). In this article, we establish the asymptotic distributions of the estimators of S_0(x) when different consistent estimators of f_0(0) are used, which is also of critical importance in constructing statistical tests accordingly. b) The methodology developed stimulated some side products in other fields. For example, in [3], we focus on heterogeneous risks all coming from possibly different maximum domain of attractions of the extreme value distributions, which well suffices in practice. By incorporating the satisficing method commonly used in operational research, we provide the explicit formula for the afore-mentioned optimal truncation point up to a slowly varying function of the sample size in an asymptotic sense. c) Further investigations have given some new promising results, especially in the case of k-monotone densities with unbounded support, and they are discussed in detail in the work [6] at the later stage of the current project, which has been under review in top journals with some positive and constructive considerations (also see the end of the preprint enclosed). We expect some more time needed for the generally long review process. For Revised Objective 3: The objective is accomplished, and all the results have been accepted in top-tier journals in the field. a) We developed an alternative estimation approach in supplement of the commonly adopted Hill estimator, by utilizing the Taylor’s law, which is a useful tool for testing; namely, we perform the estimation and testing under the shape constraint of the distribution that its variance is a power function of its mean. Particularly in [5], we generalize Taylor’s law to heavy-tailed distributions with infinite mean. We show that, as the sample size increases, the sample upper and lower semivariances, the sample higher moments, the skewness, and the kurtosis of a random sample from such a law increase asymptotically in direct proportion to a power of the sample mean. We find the asymptotic distribution and moments of the number of observations exceeding the sample mean, We propose estimators of the tail index α based on these scaling laws to supplement Hill estimators. Corresponding tests can also be developed based on the proposed estimator. b) We made another contribution in [9], namely a local Kiefer-Wolfowitz-type result on the distance between the empirical distribution function and its least concave majorant over a finite interval, under weaker assumptions than existing results. Our work provides a critical result in the higher-order power theory of likelihood ratio tests. In light of [9], the Kiefer-Wolfowitz-like result has high relevance to the well-known machine learning algorithm of SGD, and we made an attempt to connect the two concepts together in [10]. Particularly, for continuous-time deterministic discounted optimal control problems, we propose a new formulation for the gradient of the value function (value-gradient) as a decoupled PDE system, and also develop an efficient iterative scheme for this system of equations in parallel.. Specifically, we generate multiple characteristic curves at each policy iteration from an ensemble of initial states and compute both the value function and its gradient simultaneously on each curve as the labeled data, which resolves the issue in the traditional approach of Q-learning that does not possess PDEs for gradients of the Q-function to boost up the efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that this new method not only significantly increases the accuracy but also improves the efficiency and robustness of the numerical estimates. Furthermore, in view of the usefulness of Control Theory in providing useful concepts and tools for Machine Learning, we also survey the connection between the two concepts in general in [4]. As a side product, we also developed another numerical method in the work [7]. We provide the first systematic numerical study on, via the popular Fourier-cosine (COS) method, finite-time Gerber-Shiu functions with the risk process being driven by a generic Levy subordinator; shape constraints are commonly present in many Gerber-Shiu functions, as a representative example, the ruin probability is decreasing in the initial value. Under some mild and practically feasible assumptions, a comprehensive and rigorous (yet demanding) error analysis is provided, giving the most effective records of the contemporary state of the art in actuarial science and financial statistics. Finally, the effectiveness of our approximation method is illustrated through different representative numerical experiments, some of which are even achieved for the first time in the literature. Our proposed numerical estimation in this work can facilitate the development of statistical tests correspondingly. c) More new results and findings are also discussed in detail in the work [6] at the later stage of the current project, which has been under review in a top journal with some positive and constructive considerations (also see the end of the preprint enclosed). We expect some more time needed for the generally long review process in top journals. Last but not least, some of the key results in all aforementioned revised objectives 1-3 are also incorporated in the upcoming book [11] which will appear in Wiley Finance Series, the most renowned and well-received textbook series in finance worldwide.

14300319.value: Due to the worldwide COVID-19 pandemic that almost spanned through the entire reporting period, the Principal Investigator could only manage to deliver several invited seminar talks in person on relevant topics during his visit to various universities in Amsterdam, the Netherlands, in January 2020, shortly before the pandemic outbreak. Acknowledgement to financial supports by HKGRF was addressed verbally and in written form on the first page of each presentation slide in every talk before the official commencement of each of my talk. Some obtained results and accepted works had been disseminated in these talks. More information is provided in Section 9 of Part C of the present report. For the referencing in Section 5.3, the numbering of the papers quoted is referred to those listed in Section 8 of Part C. Particularly, in view of the travel restrictions and the resulting difficulty in inviting collaborators as visitors, I allocated the extra funding in appointing more research staff, and also maintained collaboration with the Co-I’s of the project, Gary Chan and Chuan-Fa Tang, via regular ZOOM discussions. 1) 9 articles have been accepted and published in the top-tier journals in actuarial science, applied mathematics , operational research, and probability and statistics, such as PNAS, SIAM journals, IME, EJOR, EJS, PLOS ONE. 2) 1 paper is currently under review. In particular, [5] appears in the Applied Mathematics Section of PNAS, the outlet for genuinely top research papers in applied mathematical sciences and statistics. The result is also described as “Statistics breakthrough helps calculate likelihood of worst-case scenarios” by an article on UChicago News (https://news.uchicago.edu/story/statistics-breakthrough-helps-calculate-likelihood-worst-case-scenarios). Besides, our breakthrough in [10] is significant: we reform the way to solve optimal control problems and completely get rid of the issues caused by the existing method of Q-learning in the literature. Q-learning involves utilizing the optimal control to approximate the value function, with no PDEs for the gradient of the Q-function to enhance the efficiency of evaluating the Q-function itself; while our proposed approach is more direct by obtaining the optimal control together with the value function, and the decoupled PDE system for the gradient of the value function give the value function and the value-gradient simultaneously, ensuring the robustness of the numerical method. Furthermore, my another research project “Comonotone-Independence Bayes classifier” won a Silver Medal in the 48th International Exhibition of Inventions Geneva on 29/4/2023. 14300319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300319.value: Shape-constrained inference is a statistical inference method with a faster convergence rate by incorporating certain shape constraints, and it is commonly used in social sciences, engineering and biological sciences, and the theory of estimating underlying densities subject to log-concavity and density pair affected by the monotonicity of their ratio. However, there are still numerous open problems on converting estimation results to the testing and diagnosis of the shape structure in densities; by completing this project, we made a notable breakthrough along this direction. The methodologies developed in the works inspired us to resolve problems in other fields related to statistical testing and estimation, including Taylor’s law for the shape constraint between mean and variance, and Benford’s law for the decreasing distribution on the digit numbers. We also proposed several numerical techniques for estimating shape-constrained distributions. Some of the aforementioned works have provided solutions to some lasting open problems in the respective disciplines, and altogether will bring lasting impacts on various fields such as statistical analysis, actuarial science, social sciences and biological science.

14300419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300419.value: This proposal aims to investigate the fermiology of LaBi and SmSb, both belonging to the large family of rare-earth monopnictides, under pressure using quantum oscillations. Rare-earth monopnictides have recently been investigated extensively worldwide. They assume a simple rocksalt structure, and they are semimetallic with an extremely large magnetoresistance at low temperatures. Quantum oscillations have been reported in many monopnictide single crystals at ambient pressure, revealing the details of Fermi surfaces. However, the corresponding investigation under pressure remains scarce. In general, pressure suppresses the magnitude of the magnetoresistance in these compounds. Furthermore, in LaBi, superconductivity can be induced upon the suppression of the large magnetoresistance. In SmSb, an unusual temperature dependence of the Shubnikov-de Haas oscillation amplitude has been reported. This behaviour does not conform to the standard Lifshitz-Kosevich theory, pointing to a non-trivial electronic state. Hence, tracking the evolution of the fermiology of both compounds under pressure will shed light on these issues. The joint CUHK-NCKU team seeks to systematically measure quantum oscillations under multiple extreme conditions. We believe the team is in a strong position to carry out the proposed research because of our track record to carry out high quality measurements under multiple extreme conditions and the ability of the NCKU group to prepare superior single crystals. It is anticipated that this collaborative research will generate results that will advance our understanding of fermiology in rare-earth monopnictides.
