14300819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14300819.value: Hessian equations or prescribing Weingarten curvature equations are natural generalizations of the Monge-Ampere equation. These equations appear naturally in convex geometry, calibrated geometry, conformal geometry, and complex geometry. There are many interesting and important issues related to the Hessian equations or the Curvature equations. For example, an important regularity result of the Monge-Ampere equation is that the interior second-order estimate is true in dimension two but fails to hold in dimensions greater than or equal to three. In general, the Hessian equations have similar results as the Monge-Ampere equation. The only exception is the 2-Hessian equation or the scalar curvature equation which has the interior estimate in dimension three. Understanding the interior regularity estimate for the 2-Hessian equation or the scalar curvature equation is important to the fully nonlinear partial differential equation theory. The other objective of the project is to study the Neumann boundary problem for the Curvature equation. The Dirichlet boundary problem for Hessian or Curvature equations has been extensively studied. Many geometric problems with boundary reduce to the existence of Neumann problems instead of Dirichlet problems. But there are relatively few results about the Neumann problem for these equations because of the difficulty of the boundary estimates. Moreover, finding some suitable compatible conditions to guarantee the existence of the Neumann boundary problem for the Curvature equations is an interesting problem. The aim of this project is to study the interior estimates, boundary estimates, of the Hessian and Curvature equations. These types of estimates may be helpful when one study the geometric problems for hypersurfaces with boundary or for non-compact hypersurfaces. 海森方程或預定曲率方程是蒙日--安培方程的自然推廣。這些方程自然地出現在 凸幾何，校準幾何，共形幾何和復幾何的研究中。關於海森方程和預定曲率問題有許多有趣的問題。例如，蒙日--安培方程的正則性理論中有一個重要的結果是內部二階導數估計在二維中是正確的但是三維或更高維是不對的。一般來說，海森方程具有與蒙日--安培方程類似的結果。唯一的例外是三維的2-海森方程或標量曲率方程具有內部二階導數估計。所以了解2-海森方程或標量曲率方程的內部估計對於研究完全非線性方程是很重要的。該項目的另一個對像是研究預定曲率方程的紐曼邊界問題。對應方程的狄氏邊界問題已被廣泛研究。許多帶邊的幾何問題可以約化到紐曼邊界問題而不是狄氏邊界問題的存在性。然而關於預定曲率方程的紐曼問題的結果相對較少。一個原因是邊界估計相對困難。另一個難點是如何找到一些適當的相容性條件。總之，這個項目的目標是研究海森和預定曲率方程的內部估計，邊界估計。這些類型的估計在研究帶邊或非緊的超曲面的幾何問題時可能會有所幫助。

14300819.label: Realisation of objectives
14300819.value: For the first objective, we have completely understood the case in dimension three. In higher dimensions, possible singular solutions are also constructed using convex integration method. We prove a priori interior $C^2$ estimates for 2-Hessian equations in dimension three. This was previously known only for the constant data case. The new techniques introduced are a trace Jacobi inequality and a doubling lemma which are crucial components in the resolution of the four-dimensional case by Shankar-Yuan. Combining the solvability and uniqueness of the Dirichlet problem for viscosity weak solutions, the above a priori estimates imply that viscosity solutions become smooth when $n=2,3,4$ (at least for $f=1$ when $n=4$). We also prove a priori interior curvature estimates for hypersurfaces of prescribing scalar curvature equations in dimension three. The new observation here is that we construct a Lagrangian graph which is a submanifold of bounded mean curvature if the graph function of a hypersurface satisfies a scalar curvature equation. Moreover, we apply a modified integral method of Warren-Yuan without relying on Sobolev inequality. Thus, in dimension three, we have a complete understanding of the interior regularity issues related to 2-Hessian equations and scalar curvature equations. For higher-dimensional cases, especially when $n>4$, the interior regularity of 2-Hessian equations and scalar curvature equations remains unknown to us. This is not an easy thing, because the most crucial ingredient for obtaining the interior estimate is the validity of the Jacobi inequality when $n=3$, as demonstrated in our papers. But the crucial Jacobi inequality does not hold when $n>4$. Thus one may inquire whether it is possible to construct $C^{1,alpha}$ viscosity weak solutions by combining the convex integration method with other approaches. Thus, we define very weak solutions for 2-Hessian equations in higher dimensions and construct infinitely many very weak solutions that are not $C^2$. For the second objective, we study the Neumann problem for special Lagrangian type equations with critical and supercritical phases. These equations can be viewed as a higher codimension version of prescribed mean curvature equation equations. Moreover, these equations naturally generalize the special Lagrangian equation and the k-Hessian equation. The special Lagrangian equations are high codimension minimal submanifold equations which have geometric background and are more interesting geometric PDEs. Previously, we believed that special Lagrangian-type equations were significantly more challenging than k-Hessian equations due to their nature as linear combinations of k-Hessian equations. However, after carefully studying the structure of the special Lagrangian equations, we gained insights into their geometric meaning. As a result, we adjusted our previous computations to adopt a more geometric approach, leading to a simplified proof of the boundary double normal derivative estimate. By establishing uniform a priori estimates up to the second order, we obtained existence results using the continuity method. A notable technical aspect of our work is the direct proof of the boundary double normal derivative estimates. Furthermore, we addressed the classical Neumann problem by proving the uniform gradient estimate. The ideas and techniques developed for achieving first two objectives have played important roles in the study of the free boundary problems in fluid-dynamics and transonic flows with substantial progress, such as well-posedness of interfacial waves in MHD, multi-dimensional contact discontinuities, incompressible impinging jet flows with gravity, vacuum dynamics, and transonic flows with vorticities.

14300819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300819.value: We prove a priori interior $C^2$ estimates for 2-Hessian equations and scalar curvature equations in dimension three. The new techniques introduced are a trace Jacobi inequality and a doubling lemma. The new observation is that we construct a Lagrangian graph which is a submanifold of bounded mean curvature if the graph function of a hypersurface satisfies a scalar curvature equation. In higher dimensions, possible singular solutions are also constructed using convex integration method. The papers about these were published in Frontiers of Mathematics in 2024 [1]. We have proved the Neumann problem for special Lagrangian type equations with critical and supercritical phases. The paper on this topic was in arXiv : 2403.06110v2 [11]. We have also obtained the first global in time well-posedness of plasma-vacuum and plasma-plasma interfacial waves for the incompressible inviscid resistive MHD [2], proved the local well-posedness of multi-dimensional contact discontinuities for compressible MHD [10], obtained the existence of impinging jet flows with gravities [6], showed the first existence of smooth transonic steady compressible flows with vorticities and non-trivial accelerations [3, 9]. We have also discovered several new phenomena in vacuum dynamics [5, 7], and shown the global well-posedness and regularity of weak solutions to the 2-dimensional unsteady Prandtl’s system in the theory of viscous boundary layers [8]. Some results of the effects of heat-conductive resistive compressible MHD on a bounded domain has been obtained [4]. Most of these have been published in top international research journals.

14300819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300819.value: I believe there are still some interesting topics that need to be understood. 1. Can we construct Higher dimensional viscosity solutions which may blow up interior for 2-Hessian equations and scalar curvature equations in dimensions higher than four? Our very weak solutions about 2-Hessian equations may provide evidence for singular solutions. 2. Given a manifold with the metric defined by the linearized operator of the scalar curvature equation, can we construct an isometric embedding such that the mean curvature is bounded by the scalar curvature? This is unknown for dimension four and higher. This would be helpful in understanding the regularity of the prescribed scalar curvature equation. In dimension three, we find this isometric embedding similar as the special Lagrangian submanifold. Using this observation, we can use mean value inequality on this submanifold for subharmonic quantities.

14300819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300819.value: In Riemannian geometry, scalar curvature is one of the simplest geometric invariants that describe the curvature of space. This topic is dedicated to studying whether hypersurfaces possess smoothness when locally given a scalar curvature equation. We provide a positive answer to this question in the case of three-dimensional graph case. In higher dimensions, especially in dimensions five and above, our methods and results lead us to believe that there are likely examples of curvature breakdown in the graph case of the given scalar curvature equation. Several important applications in the mathematical theory of fluid dynamics have been achieved.

14300919.label: Project Objectives
14300919.value: To synthesize functionalized octabenzo[8]circulenes and heptabenzo[7]circulenes, which are rationally designed to contain a variety of substituting groups for formation of networks. To grow crystals of the metal organic frameworks and hydrogen-bonded networks of negatively curved nanographenes, and to use X-ray crystallography to study their three-dimensional structures. To polymerize functionalized negatively curved nanographenes using different coupling reactions, and to characterize the resulting covalent networks using a variety of techniques. To study the self-assembly of alkylated octabenzo[8]circulenes in the solid state, and to explore the opportunities of the π-stacked nanosheets of alkylated octabenzo[8]circulenes as a supramolecular two-dimensional electronic material in organic field effect transistors.

14300919.label: Realisation of objectives
14300919.value: 1. We have successfully synthesized a series of functionalized octabenzo[8]circulenes and heptabenzo[7]circulenes, incorporating various functional groups such as bromine, iodine, carboxylic acid, aldehyde, ethynyl, and perylene diimide. In addition to this, we have expanded our initial synthesis objective to include the development of synthetic strategies for incorporating eight-membered rings into negatively curved nanographenes. These strategies have provided us with new building blocks for constructing networks of negatively curved nanographenes. 2. We conducted an investigation into the crystallization of metal organic frameworks and hydrogen-bonded networks using octabenzo[8]circulene tetracarboxylic acid. Unfortunately, we were unable to obtain high-quality crystals suitable for the characterization of the 3D structures using X-ray crystallography. 3. We successfully polymerized the tetrabromo derivative of octabenzo[8]circulene using the nickel-mediated Yamamoto coupling reaction. This reaction yielded a novel porous carbon-rich material called POB8C, which consists of a covalent network of negatively curved nanographenes. In collaboration with Prof. Quan Li from the Department of Physics at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, we investigated the application of POB8C as an anode material in lithium-ion batteries. Our findings revealed that POB8C exhibited a maximum capacity of 830 mAh·g−1 at a current density of 100 mA·g−1. Furthermore, in collaboration with Prof. Marina A. Petrukhina from the Department of Chemistry at the University at Albany, State University of New York, we studied the step-wise chemical reduction reactions of octabenzo[8]circulene with alkali metals. X-ray crystallography analysis revealed a unique highly-reduced hydrocarbon pentaanion, providing valuable insights into the reduction and alkali metal intercalation processes of negatively curved carbon allotropes. 4. We studied the self-assembly of tetra(t-butyl)octabenzo[8]circulene and found that the crystal structure of this compound exhibits supramolecular nanosheets as a result of interlocking the saddle-shaped molecules through both face-to-face and edge-to-face π-π interactions. We attempted to fabricate thin films of this compound using solution-based methods and vacuum deposition. Unfortunately, the solution-based methods only yielded isolated crystals that were unsuitable for the fabrication of field-effect transistors. On the other hand, vacuum deposition resulted in amorphous films that functioned as p-type organic semiconductors in field-effect transistors, with a hole mobility on the order of 10−3 cm2/Vs. Furthermore, we expanded our research objective to include the self-assembly of peryleneimide functionalized octabenzo[8]circulene. We investigated the self-assembly of this new molecule in solution-processed films and explored its application as an n-type organic semiconductor in field-effect transistors, as well as in solar cells. 5. We broadened the scope of this project by conducting a synthesis to merge a negatively curved nanographene (octabenzo[8]circulene) with a carbon nanoring. This synthesis yielded two constitutional isomers, one with D2 symmetry and the other with C2v symmetry. The successful synthesis of the C2v isomer represents a significant advancement in our bottom-up approach towards precisely synthesizing carbon schwarzites, in good alignment with the key objective of this project.

14300919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14300919.value: 1. We successfully synthesized the first covalent network of negatively curved nanographenes by polymerizing the tetrabromo derivative of octabenzo[8]circulene using the nickel-mediated Yamamoto coupling reaction. This material was utilized as an anode material in a lithium-ion battery, demonstrating a maximum capacity (830 mAh·g−1) that was more than twice that of graphite. These significant findings were published in Publication 1 in Part C, suggesting that this network has the potential to closely resemble carbon schwarzites in both structure and function. 2. We developed two new strategies for synthesizing negatively curved nanographenes. As reported by Publication 2 in Part C, we investigated naphthalene-directed Scholl reactions to successfully synthesize an unprecedented aromatic saddle consisting of 80 sp2 carbon atoms. This work demonstrates that the challenges of incomplete cyclization or skeletal rearrangement during the Scholl reaction can be overcome by introducing naphthalene moieties to the substrate. Additionally, as reported by Publication 3 in Part C, we introduced a synthetic approach to incorporate eight-membered rings into polycyclic aromatic frameworks through a ring expansion reaction. The resulting octagon-embedded hexabenzocoronene exhibited a saddle-shaped polycyclic framework, as confirmed by single crystal X-ray crystallography. 3. We synthesized two new molecular nanocarbons, where a negatively curved nanographene and a carbon nanoring are merged together in different geometries. These novel negatively curved molecular nanocarbons were synthesized from tetrabromooctabenzo[8]circulene through Suzuki−Miyaura coupling with C-shaped paraphenylene precursors, followed by intramolecular Yamamoto coupling and reductive aromatization reactions. The synthesis of the C2v isomer represents a further step towards the precise synthesis of carbon schwarzites through a bottom-up approach, aligning with the key objective of this project. These findings were published in Publication 4 in Part C.

14300919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14300919.value: The main discoveries of this project highlight that amorphous covalent networks of negatively curved nanographenes possess negative curvature, porosity, and three-dimensionality, resembling carbon schwarzites in their structure and functionality to some extent. These findings serve as motivation for further investigation into novel three-dimensional carbon nanomaterials with negative curvature. Our future objective is to attain periodicity within this covalent network, as it is a crucial characteristic of carbon schwarzites. To accomplish this, we propose constructing covalent organic frameworks (COFs) using negatively curved nanographenes and forming dynamic covalent bonds. This approach holds the potential to achieve long-range order in the structure. This research direction has the potential to advance our understanding of carbon nanomaterials and pave the way for the development of innovative materials with unique properties.

14300919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14300919.value: Carbon schwarzites are long-sought-after carbon allotropes that are three-dimensional structures exhibiting negative curvature. Therefore, they are distinct from the well-known carbon nanomaterials, graphene with zero curvature and fullerenes with positive curvature. Carbon schwarzites are predicted to have interesting electronic and magnetic properties, but they have not been fully realized yet. The goal of this project was to explore bottom-up approaches to carbon schwarzites from smaller building blocks called negatively curved nanographenes. In this project, we successfully synthesized the first covalent network of negatively curved nanographenes and demonstrated its application as an anode material in lithium ion batteries. We also developed two new strategies to synthesize negatively curved nanographenes. Moreover, we merged negatively curved nanographenes with carbon nanorings to create new types of molecular nanocarbons. These findings provide a preliminary experimental basis for further exploration of new three-dimensional carbon nanomaterials with negative curvature. This project has led to four peer-reviewed publications, and the results of this project were also presented at two international conferences. Our research has resulted in four published papers and has been presented at two international conferences. Furthermore, one of our PhD students received valuable training through this project.

14301019.label: Realisation of objectives
14301019.value: Objective 1: Whether the local fundamental group can determine some classes of infinitesimal covers or some classes of purely inseparable field extensions? This is 90% achieved. Yes, the local fundamental group can determine some classes purely inseparable field extensions. If K is any field over a perfect field of characteristic p, then the purely inseparable extensions of K are determined by its local fundamental group schemes. However, still not much is known for the infinitesimal covers of a general scheme. Objective 2: Whether the local fundamental group together with the étale fundamental group could recognize completely the finitely generated infinite fields (not up to their perfect closures)? This is 20% achieved. We know that the étale fundamental group can determine the finitely generated infinite fields up to their perfect closures. From here we can only use our result on local fundamental group schemes to determine the field in some specific situations. For example, we can say that if there is a common subfield K subseteq K_1 and K subseteq K_2 where the extensions are purely inseparable, and if K_1,K_2 have the same étale fundamental group and local fundamental group scheme, then K_1=K_2. The problem appears to be much more difficult than we conceived initially. Although we devoted considerable effort to analyze examples that are accessible within known techniques, and we learned quite a bit from these examples, it is difficult to obtain general theoretical results. Objective 3: What do the quotients of the local fundamental groups look like? This is 90% achieved. Let X be an affine curve over an algebraically closed field k of positive characteristic. We show that if G is a simple finite local group scheme over k, then it is a quotient of the local fundamental group of X. In addition, we have some other partial results, for example, if X is a rational variety, then every finite local group scheme G is its quotient. Reason for no spending the budget: the project started in 1/1/2020, during the pandemic. The budget for mathematical research is mainly for traveling and paying visitors / collaborators to travel, and both became impossible during the pandemic. The original PI (Lei ZHANG) had to work alone and partly work jointly with the current PI (Jiu-Kang YU). The original PI left Hong Kong in 2022 and transferred the project to the current PI, who later realized that it is difficult to continue without the presence of the original PI. Consequently the project saw little progress since the transfer and the budget remained unspent.

14301019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301019.value: The major findings and research outcome are the partially achieved objectives listed above. In addition to the aforementioned results, we also have some other interesting findings which reveal some surprising differences between the purely inseparable world and the étale world. For example in the mixed characteristic case, the Galois group of a local field is the decomposition subgroup of the Galois group of the global field (of course, after a choice of the embedding of the algebraic closures). However, for local group schemes, the situation is quite different. We can show that the local fundamental group scheme of a characteristic p local field goes surjectively to the local fundamental group of the respective global field, but it is not an isomorphism!

14301019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301019.value: We think it would be highly interesting if there could be a description of the quotients of the local fundamental group of higher dimensional varieties. But of course, there is a long way to go, even for the étale world.

14301019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301019.value: The covering space in algebraic topology is a fundamental object of study. Its incarnation in algebraic geometry is the étale covering space of a scheme. These étale covering spaces behalve very nicely: they resemble, to a great extent, the covering spaces in algebraic topology. However, in algebraic geometry, there is another extreme world of covering spaces, namely, the purely inseparable coverings (or the radical coverings, or the infinitesimal coverings) which is parallel to the world of étale covering spaces but at the opposite side of algebraic geometry. In the world of purely inseparable covering spaces the geometric intuition could fail and can be rather misleading at some point, so one needs algebraic tools to study them. The value of this research project is that it reveals the fundamental nature of purely inseparable coverings and at the same time develop some algebraic tools for studying them.

14301119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301119.value: 超冷原子已經成為了物理學中最令人興奮的研究方向之一，而將超冷物理的研究擴展到分子也成為了一個研究的熱點，特別是由於極性分子可以通過電偶極相互作用，可以用來進行很多原子無法研究的內容。然而，分子之間的相互作用比原子要複雜的多。最近的一些實驗已經表明，即便是處於絕對基態的分子，在沒有兩體化學反應的情況下，還是會有很大的損耗，從而使得後續的研究變得非常困難。 在2016年，本小組已經成功製備了基態NaRb分子並進行了一些碰撞損耗的研究。在本課題中，我們將研究如何利用電偶極相互作用抑制分子的損耗。首先，我們將研究在準二維勢阱中，排斥的電偶極相互作用對長程分子作用的影響；其次，我們還將嘗試研究處於轉動激發態的分子間的偶極相互作用對碰撞的影響。 我們的實驗研究將在已經工作的系統上開展。由於這些研究需要較大的電場，首先我們需要對系統進行升級，主要是需要把電極置於真空中。因為NaRb分子具有3.2德拜的大電偶極矩，已有的理論工作已經表明碰撞損耗抑制作用應當比較突出。如果損耗可以被抑制，則有可能得到長壽命的樣品，並對分子樣品進行蒸發冷卻已獲得更接近量子簡併的分子氣體。

14301119.label: Realisation of objectives
14301119.value: The main objective of this project is to explore ultracold collisions between polar molecules with strong dipolar interactions. A full investigation of the dipolar collisions will help us to understand and control the unexpected loss problem for ultracold polar molecules even without two-body loss channels. Suppression of the lossy inelastic collisions with dipolar interaction may be the key to overcome the loss problem for obtaining a long-lived sample. The start date of the project was January 1st, 2020. During the 1.5 years, the Covid-19 pandemic has affected the project a great deal. We have been trying our best to keep up with the schedule and at the same time be flexible in pursuing the objectives. Especially, with the implementation of microwave-induced loss suppression, we have delayed the upgrade to the new high-voltage electrodes system, which will involve a major overhaul of the UHV system. Objective 1: We designed a new high-voltage electrodes system with several different configurations. In our final design, two pairs of ring electrodes with different diameters are used. According to our design, this will allow us to generate electric fields up to 5.5 kV/cm with tunable electric field gradient. We also ordered a custom-designed metal UHV chamber to mount the electrode in order to avoid the charge accumulation problem in glass cells. In principle, this design also allows us to create a DC quadrupole trap for polar molecules. In the future, we plan to use this to investigate trapping in the absence of light. A challenge of this design is the very high requirement for mechanical precision, and the stray electric field from the leading wires. Especially, the latter problem could generate an appreciable electric field gradient. We thus designed a set of symmetrical dummy leads to make the electric field as uniform as possible. Objective 2 and 4: We have successfully implemented the 1-D optical lattices and created 2-D samples of ground-state NaRb molecules. The lattice gas of molecules is created by directly loading the ground-state molecules. The number of molecules is limited due to the loss during the loading process. We then measured the loss of the 2-D sample as a function of the electric field. In our initial result, from 0 to 1.2 kV/cm, the loss rate decreases as expected. Unfortunately, the measurement is hampered by the electric field gradient which increases with higher electric field. As the permanent electric dipole moment of the NaRb molecule is large, this gradient is enough to push the molecules away from the trap. Because of this, we have not been able to investigate collisions in higher electric fields. We then went on to load NaRb directly in a 3D optical lattice. As we are starting from thermal samples, a large portion of the molecules are not in the ground band. We then used the two-body loss as the band purification method to get rid of these higher band population. Afterwards, we obtained a long-lived (with a lifetime of about 10 s) sample of NaRb in a 3D optical lattice, albeit with a rather low filling factor. With this sample, we studied the coherence between the nuclear spin states in the J = 0 rotational level. After identifying the residual magnetic field gradient as the main source of decoherence, we extended the coherence time to several seconds, without spin echo. This long coherence time has allowed us to demonstrate a sub-Hz two-photon Rabi lineshape. The combination of long lifetime and coherence time, and the high spectroscopic resolution make our system a promising candidate for quantum information storage and quantum simulation. This work was published in PRL. Objective 3: We also investigated the dipolar collisions between molecules in the J = 0 and J = 1 rotational level. In this configuration, the molecules can interact via the so-called resonant dipole interaction. Such a sample is prepared by adding a resonant π/2 microwave pulse connecting the two rotational levels. To get rid of the coherence, we simply waited for several milliseconds. In two different rotational hyperfine mixtures prepared in this manner, we observed a significant increase in molecule losses as a result of the resonant dipolar interaction. We note that this interaction mechanism has been proposed as a way to implement quantum gates between two rotational qubits of polar molecules. This work was published in Physical Review Research. In addition, we also studied the loss suppression with a blue detuning pure circularly polarized microwave. By creating a dressed state between J = 0 and 1, this leads to a long-range potential barrier which prevents two NaRb from reaching the short range and forming the complex. With this method, we reduced the loss rate from 10^-10 cm^3s^-1 to 10^-12 cm^3s^-1. This low loss rate has allowed us to observe and measure the elastic rate in the collision between two NaRb molecules and demonstrate efficient evaporative cooling between ground-state molecule. This work was published in Phys. Rev. X. Additional investigations: For understanding the decoherence of the rotational mixture, we also studied the anisotropic polarizability of NaRb molecules in the 1064 nm trapping light. With a magic wavelength polarization, we observed the mixing among different hyperfine levels induced by the light and determined the combination of polarization angle and intensity that could maximize the rotational coherence. Additionally, in the J = 1, mJ = 0 state, we observed a very strong dependence of the rotational coherence on the polarization of the 1064 nm light. By rotating the polarization to the magic angle, we significantly extended the coherence time of the sample. We have also studied the creation of ultracold Na2Rb2 complex in the collision between two NaRb molecules. Contrary to previous results, we found that the complex lifetime must be much longer than that predicted from the most state-of-the-art calculations. This discrepancy shows that the quantum mechanical calculation of the potential energy surface for the complex formation is still a challenging problem. It also shows that our understanding of ultracold chemical reaction is still incomplete. This work was published in PRL. Conclusion: We have made significant progress in understanding and controlling dipolar collisions between ultracold polar molecules. We believe that the results obtained in the project will help us to improve the loss of the ultracold polar molecule samples and will have significant impacts on the research field of ultracold polar molecules. We also believe that the techniques developed in this project will be beneficial for other research groups in this field. We expect to continue our work in this exciting field in the upcoming period.

14301119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301119.value: In our research project, we are studying polar molecules, which are a type of tiny particle with distinctive properties. However, when these molecules are cooled down to extraordinarily low temperatures of only a millionth of a degree above absolute zero, they tend to collide and vanish, making them difficult to study. The main goal of our project is to understand why this happens and find ways to mitigate it. This would enable us to observe these molecules for more extended periods. We have made some careful progress, such as developing a specific system to better control the environment of these molecules and finding ways to maintain them in a trapping potential for a longer period. This research is crucial in the world of physics since polar molecules hold great potential in quantum science and technology. By understanding how matter behaves in such extreme conditions, we are contributing to the scientific community's shared knowledge. In the long run, the insights from our work may even help further developments in areas like quantum computing. It is thus significant step in a much larger journey of scientific discovery.

14301219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301219.value: 重整化群是現代物理學中的重要觀念，尤其對於具有標度不變性的臨介系統的研究。在凝聚態物理學中，重整化群不動點給出了相變普適類這一重要觀念，可以用來刻畫和分類連續相變的普適性質。在高能物理學中，重整化流的觀念還可以預言自然界的基本相互作用在不同能標下的變化，例如著名的強相互作用漸進自由理論。最近，人們還進一步發現了實空間重整化群與深度學習的內在聯系。因此，對於重整化群的全新認識將會對基礎物理學和現代工業產生革命性影響。 不幸的是，傳統的微擾重整化方案無法對強相互作用系統作出有意義的寓言。因此，一種非微擾的重整化方案是及其需要的。最近幾年，凝聚態物理學和量子信息理論使得我們對於實空間重整化的理解有了裏程碑式的突破。長程糾纏和糾纏重整化的突破性觀念使得發展全新的普適實空間重整化理論成為可能。 在眾多可能的方案中，一種叫做張量網絡重整化的方案最為鼓舞人心。在這個研究計劃裏，我們會用一種叫做圈優化張量網絡重整化的方法來研究1+1維相互作用量子體系。這樣的實空間重整化方案可以嚴格的積掉量子系統的短程量子漲落並自動生成長波極限下的重整化流。特別的，我們打算用這種方法來計算1+1維量子臨界系統的不動點張量的代數結構並且得到精確的臨界指數。 在這個研究計劃裏，我們會1）發展基於Grassmann代數的圈優化張量重整化算法並得到1+1維費米子臨界系統的精確臨界指數。2）計算1+1維量子臨界系統的動力學性質。3）用不動點張量來刻畫1+1維量子臨界系統並得到不動點張量的完整代數結構。

14301219.label: Realisation of objectives
14301219.value: We have successfully executed our plan and achieved all the set objectives, exceeding our initial expectations in many instances. Notably, in objective 1, we extended the Grassmann loop-TRG results to 2+1D systems as a variational method, yielding significant advancements. Furthermore, in objective 3, we accomplished the explicit construction of the exact fixed-point tensor in our recent work. These outcomes showcase the progress made and highlight the fruitful results obtained throughout our research endeavor. Below we explain our achievement in full details. (a) Our research has led to the development of the Grassmann-valued loop-optimized tensor renormalization (loop-TNR) scheme, which is applicable to generic 1+1D fermionic quantum critical systems. We have successfully applied this algorithm to investigate both spinless interacting fermion models and the t-J model. Through comparisons with previous studies, we have observed consistent and systematic agreement in the critical exponents. Additionally, we have recently utilized the Grassmann loop-TNR algorithm as a variational method to explore the honeycomb lattice t-J model in 2+1D, leading to the derivation of the global phase diagram. (b) By employing the loop-TNG algorithm, we have made significant contributions to the study of gapless domain wall models spanning different topological phases. Our approach has allowed us to accurately extract various conformal data, including central charges and scaling dimensions. The obtained results showcase the remarkable precision achieved through our investigations. (c) Our novel approach involves computing dynamical correlation functions in both imaginary time and real time using the loop-TNR algorithm. In contrast to traditional methods that only handle correlations in the spatial direction with integer separations, our algorithm can handle correlations in the temporal direction with decimal values. This capability is achieved through a tensor network representation constructed from a path-integral formalism, allowing us to explore correlations comprehensively. (d) Utilizing the state-of-the-art loop-TNR algorithm, we conducted simulations to investigate the phase diagram and critical behavior of the q-state clock model on the square lattice. Our results exhibit exceptional accuracy in determining the two phase transition points for q≥5. By computing the conformal scaling dimensions at these transition points, we obtained precise values for the radius R of the compactified boson theories. Notably, we found that the radius R at the higher temperature phase transition point aligns precisely with the prediction of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition. Moreover, for sufficiently large q, we observed approximate convergence of the fixed-point tensors at the higher temperature transition point, enabling direct extraction of the operator product expansion (OPE) coefficient of the compactified boson theory from the fixed-point tensor. (e) In a recent breakthrough, we have presented an explicit analytical construction of the fixed-point (FP) tensor for two-dimensional rational conformal field theory (RCFT). We define the FP tensor as a correlation function involving "boundary-changing operators" on triangles. Our construction fully satisfies all the real-space renormalization group (RG) conditions. To illustrate its effectiveness, we provide a concrete example using the Ising model, in which we compute the scaling dimensions explicitly based on the corresponding FP tensor. This new result has been recognized as a major breakthrough in the fields of condensed matter physics, mathematical physics, and high-energy physics, showcasing its wide-ranging impact.

14301219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301219.value: We successfully extended the Grassmann-valued loop-TNR scheme into 2+1D and utilized it as a variational method to investigate the global phase diagram of the square lattice t-J model. Our analysis included a comprehensive review of the important aspects of d-wave superconductivity and pair-density wave (PDW) states at low doping levels. The detailed findings are summarized in the master thesis of our talented student, Kwok Ho Pai. Using the fermionic tensor network approach, we conducted a thorough examination of the honeycomb lattice t-J model. By exploring different unit cells within our ansatz, we made exciting discoveries of multiple stripe states with distinct periods that exhibit strong competition with uniform states. These significant results have been published in the prestigious journal Physical Review B (Phys. Rev. B 108, 035144, 2023). We proposed a physical mechanism to comprehend the gapless nature of specific domain wall models and achieved notable progress in their construction. By leveraging group cohomology theory and the classification and construction of twisted gauge theories, we successfully generalized these models into arbitrary dimensions. This advancement provides us with a systematic approach to understanding gapless domain walls and topological quantum phase transitions. Our findings have been published in the esteemed journal Physical Review Research (Phys. Rev. Research 4, 023038, 2022). In addition to studying ground state properties using the loop-TNR algorithm, we expanded our approach to simulate dynamic correlation functions, aiming to overcome the well-known entanglement barrier problem. Our work in this area has been posted as an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2311.18785) and recently submitted to Physical Review B. We utilized both the loop-TNR algorithm and analytical methods to study the structure of the FP tensor in CFT. Our focus encompassed two types of systems: those with an emergent U(1) symmetry arising from the q-state clock model and those without any continuous symmetry, known as rational CFT (RCFT). Since U(1) symmetric CFT with a central charge c=1 poses challenges for analytical methods, we employed the C4 symmetric loop-TNR algorithm to fit the leading components of the FP tensor. Relevant results have been published in the respected journal Physical Review Research (Phys. Rev. Research 4, 023159, 2022). Additionally, we have made recent progress in the exact construction of RCFT based on a holographic picture. This work has been posted as an arXiv preprint (arXiv:2311.18005) and recently submitted to Physical Review Letters.

14301219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301219.value: In the future, our research will focus on two main directions, where we aim to make significant contributions: (a) Generalization of the loop-TNR algorithm: Our primary objective is to extend the loop-TNR algorithm into 2+1D as a comprehensive space-time renormalization group scheme, going beyond its current application as a simple variational method. By doing so, we seek to enhance our understanding of quantum systems in higher dimensions and provide a more robust framework for studying their critical behavior. (b) Exploration of fixed point tensor structures for conformal field theory: We are committed to investigating the potential fixed point tensor structures associated with conformal field theory (CFT). Our goal is to develop a deeper understanding of critical quantum systems in higher dimensions by studying their tensorial properties. Furthermore, we aim to employ the holographic picture to gain new insights into these systems, enabling us to uncover hidden connections and provide novel perspectives on their behavior. By focusing on these two directions, we expect to make significant contributions to the field of quantum physics, advancing our understanding of critical phenomena and providing new tools for studying complex systems in higher dimensions.

14301219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301219.value: Our research focuses on developing real space renormalization group (RG) schemes using innovative concepts like long-range entanglement and entanglement renormalization. The tensor network renormalization (TNR) scheme stands out as a highly promising approach. Developing the Grassmann-valued TNR scheme for 1+1D fermionic quantum critical systems, enabling us to compute critical exponents with exceptional precision. Extending it to 2+1D systems will provide insights into realistic correlated electron systems. Employing the TNR scheme to study the dynamical properties of 1+1D quantum critical systems, addressing a long-standing problem in quantum simulation. Utilizing fixed point tensors to describe and understand 1+1D quantum critical systems, leading to a new understanding of conformal field theory. Our research will have a significant and lasting impact on real space RG, advancing fundamental understanding. Additionally, we will explore the application of the TNR scheme to deep learning, contributing to advancements in the machine learning industry in Hong Kong.

14301319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301319.value: This project aims at studying free boundary problems for minimal surfaces and exploring their relationship with geometry and physics. Minimal surfaces are mathematical models for soap films whose shape is governed by differential equations, which arise through variational principle as least-energy configurations. The study of minimal surfaces lies at the intersection of multiple disciplines including geometry, analysis and physics. Much of the earlier research focus on minimal surfaces with either a fixed boundary or no boundary. In a confined region with boundary, it is most natural to consider the free boundary problem for minimal surfaces. Not much is known about this problem despite its relevance to actual physical systems. The PI proposes a systematic study of the geometric and analytic aspects of this free boundary problem. Specifically, we investigate when and how singularities are formed. State-of-the- art techniques from analysis and partial differential equations will be employed to understand their boundary behaviour. The PI will explore further connections of the problem to other fields of research including phase transitions, fluid dynamics and general relativity. 本項目旨在研究極小曲面中的自由邊界問題與探索這些問題跟幾何和物理的關係。 極小曲面是肥皂膜的數學模型，其幾何形狀須滿足某個微分方程。該微分方程通過變分原理作為最小能量配置產生。極小曲面的研究位於多個學科的交叉點，包括幾何學，分析和物理學。大多數早期研究都集中在具有固定邊界或無邊界的極小曲面上。在具有邊界的有限區域中，我們最自然考慮的是極小曲面的自由邊界問題。儘管這與實際物理現象息息相關，但我們目前對這個問題所知甚少。 申請人提出對此自由邊界問題的幾何與分析方面作出系統性的研究。具體來說，我們會研究奇異點是在何時以及如何形成的。我們將使用來自分析和偏微分方程裡最先進的技巧來理解它們的邊界行為。 申請人將探討該問題與其他研究領域的進一步聯繫，包括相變，流體動力學和廣義相對論。

14301319.label: Realisation of objectives
14301319.value: Regarding Objective 1, we have successfully study the existence and regularity of minimal surfaces arising in the van der Waals-Cahn-Hilliard theory of phase transitions. More specifically, we use techniques from geometric measure theory to study the general asymptotic behaviour of general critical points, including those which are not necessarily minimizing or stable, to the Allen-Cahn energy functional in a bounded domain. Under a natural uniform bound on the energy, we proved that as the limit interface arising from a sequence of general critical points is a free boundary varifold which is integer rectifiable up to the boundary. This extends earlier work of Hutchinson and Tonegawa on the interior regularity of such limit-interface. A key novelty in our result is that no convexity assumption of the boundary is required and it is valid even when the limit-interface clusters near the boundary. Moreover, our arguments are local and thus works in the Riemannian setting. This work provides the first step towards the regularity theory for the Allen- Cahn min-max theory for free boundary minimal hypersurfaces, which was developed in the Almgren-Pitts setting by the PI and Zhou. This completes the major objective (Objective 1) in this project. Since the entire project was done during the whole period of CoViD-19, this made it very difficult to carry out international collaborations and to hire postdocs to work on some parts of the project (This is reflected in the relatively low percentage of fund being used during the project period). To overcome this difficult, the PI has decided to train some of his own graduate students to work on certain parts of the project. This is particularly the case for Objective 2. The PI has trained his PhD student Gaoming Wang to work on Objective 2 towards a better understanding of geometric variational problems that involve certain types of singularities. One particularly interesting singularity model that arise naturally in the historical study of soap films and minimal surfaces are the triple junctions, also known as Y-singularity. We successfully extend the classical Bernstein theorem to minimal surfaces possessing Y-singularities. In the process, we gave the first systematic study of the stability of such singular minimal surfaces and derived new Schoen-Simon-Yau type curvature estimates in this singular setting. On the other hand, we performed a more quantitative study of embedded geodesic networks in the two-sphere, which are natural singular objects arising in the Almgren-Pitts min-max theory. We devise a novel method to compute the Morse index and nullity of such stationary geodesic network in terms of certain Dirichlet-to-Neumann map defined on a sub-network. Our study has opened up new directions to study the geometric and analytic properties of mildly singular objectives arising in natural geometric variational problems (particularly in the context of minimal surfaces). Finally, regarding Objective 3, we have extended our methods to analyze other free boundary problems arising in the context of mathematical general relativity. The study of apparent horizons (or marginally trapped surfaces) in initial data sets for the Einstein equation is fundamental in the singularity formation due to the pioneering deep work of Penrose and Hawking. The celebrated work of Schoen and Yau used the blow-up of Jang’s equation to study the existence of apparent horizons which is an important step in their proof of spacetime positive energy theorem. In numerical relativity, it is often necessary to consider certain boundary value problems for the Einstein equation and it is hence extremely interesting to look for apparent horizons satisfying certain natural boundary conditions and relate their existence to the formation of black holes and singularities. Motivated by these, we combined techniques from quasi-linear PDE theory and geometric measure theory to study the existence and regularity of free boundary apparent horizons via a mixed boundary value problem for the Jang’s equation. By establishing new a-priori estimates and the regularity theory of almost minimizing currents, we are able to show existence based on natural barrier conditions and establish up-to-the-boundary regularity of such apparent horizon. We expect that our constructions of such apparent horizons will be useful in the positive energy theory and singularity formulation for initial data sets which possess a boundary, and hence will be relevant to the numerical study of Einstein equations on bounded domains. In summary, all the three objectives set out in this project has been successfully completed. Our work has also opened up new directions for further investigations.

14301319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301319.value: In Research Output 1, we have given the first systematic study of the stability of minimal surfaces possessing triple junctions, which requires a delicate compatibility condition for the Jacobi operators at the junction. As an important application, we proved a Bernstein theorem for such stable minimal surfaces with triple function in the 3-dimensional Euclidean space. This work has been published in the journal Calculus of Variations & PDE in 2022. In Research Output 2, we discovered a new connection of the index and nullity of embedded geodesic networks in the two-sphere with certain Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of its sub-network. Using this new tool, we gave a precise formula for the Morse index in terms of the topological complexity of the network and showed that all such geodesic networks are non-degenerate in the sense that all Jacobi fields are generated by rotations. This has been accepted by Journal of Functional Analysis. In Research Output 3, the PI has studied the boundary behaviour for limit interfaces arising in the Allen-Cahn equation. In particular, we showed that, under uniform energy bounds, any such limit interface is a free boundary minimal hypersurface in the generalised sense of varifolds. Moreover, we established the up-to-the-boundary integer rectifiability of the limit varifold. Our work extends earlier work of Hutchinson-Tonegawa for the interior regularity. We have developed novel techniques which can also handle the boundary concentration scenario. Our analysis is local and hence works in the more general Riemannian manifold setting. This work has been submitted to a highly reputed international journal - Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis - and provides the foundation for the free boundary min-max theory via the Allen-Cahn equation. In Research Output 4, the PI has studied the existence and regularity of free boundary marginally outer trapped surfaces arising in the context of Einstein’s theory of general relativity. We established the PDE framework on the mixed boundary value problem for Jang's equation and used the Perron's method of Eichmair to prove the existence of free boundary MOTS. We also proved the up-to-boundary-regularity for the free boundary MOTS using methods in geometric measure theory based on earlier work of the PI and Xin Zhou. Due to the interruption of CoViD-19, there has been some delay and we are in the process of doing some final editing before submitting the paper to a journal within the next few months.

14301319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301319.value: With our foundational work in Research Output 3, we will further develop the higher regularity theory for limit interfaces that arises from stable or finite index critical points to the Allen-Cahn functional. This will potentially lead to a new min-max theory for free boundary minimal hypersurfaces via the more PDE-based Allen-Cahn approach. We shall expect to see more interesting results along this new direction. On the other hand, it would also be interesting to study the problems in an ambient space which is mildly singular, for example, which possess edge singularities that are similar to triple junctions in minimal surfaces. Such singular spaces are important in other areas like complex geometry. We also hope to apply our geometric methods to other free boundary problems e.g. Bernoulli type problems. With the robustness of our techniques, we expect that many other geometric variational problems can be studied by our methods developed in this project.

14301319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301319.value: This project has initiated a systematic study of the geometric and analytic aspects of objects arising naturally in physical problems. These objects often demonstrate certain singularities which are difficult to study using ordinary calculus methods. Together with his students and collaborators, the PI has developed novel techniques from analysis and partial differential equations to study the fine structure of such singularities. These new techniques have opened up new directions to study problems arising in a range of research areas including phase transitions, differential geometry and general relativity.

14301519.label: Project Objectives
14301519.value: Inner/Outer bounds on rates: We aim to provide non-trivial inner and outer bounds on the rates obtainable for general adversarial communication problems, by combining our preliminary achievability/converse techniques with classical ideas from coding theory. Computational aspects: We aim to explore the computational complexity of our inner and outer bounds. For specific AVCs. Large alphabet problems: In classical coding theory, it is considerably easier to obtaining precise characterizations of capacities and design computationally efficient capacity-achieving codes in the large alphabet regime. We therefore aim to specifically examine classes of general large-alphabet problems. Semi-adversarial noise: Understanding the impact of additional random noise in the channel: Our preliminary results provide a provide characterization of adversarial communication problems for which a positive rate is possible, but only for channels in which the only source of noise is adversarial. We have intriguing examples showing new phenomena when additional random noise is possible, and aim to extend these to general semi-adversarial channels, and thereby examine the interplay between random and adversarial noise on communication problems.

14301519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301519.value: 當今信息時代的一個關鍵挑戰是數據整合性，這對我們提出了通過帶噪媒介進行可靠存儲與可靠傳輸的要求。在克勞德·香農的開拓性工作中，他以優雅的信息論語言提出了該問題，並刻畫了通過帶有隨機噪聲的的信道做可靠通信的基本極限。 然而，在當今隨處可見的網絡環境中，來自惡意對抗者的非法訪問的可能性是真實存在的。這對我們提出了如下問題：我們能否為可能被智能干擾對抗者控制的媒介給出魯棒性的傳輸率保障？ 該問題在一個信息論框架下以由布拉克維爾提出的“廣義任意變化信道”的方式得以體現。與香農的框架不同，這裡最基本的問題包含了一個全知的干擾對抗者（他預先了解整個傳輸過程），在“完全勝利”或零錯誤的判則下，最大傳輸率至今仍然是未解的。該問題與高維堆積問題密切相關——一個充滿各種公開問題的數學領域。 該提案旨在從若干基本角度研究該對抗性通信問題。 •基本極限：儘管對一個給定的（即使非常“簡單的”）對抗性干擾問題精確刻畫最大可能通信量是一個極其困難的問題，我們旨在給出非平凡的可達與不可達結果。作為非平凡的第一步，我們已經得到了在給定對抗信道上非平凡通信量可達性的精確刻畫（儘管離對最大通信量的理解仍然非常遙遠）。 •可計算上下界：許多已知的可達通信量的上下界都難以計算。在我們的工作中，我們旨在提供快速算法近似這些上下界，或提供計算困難性的結果。 •計算高效的通信方案：除了傳輸率的保障外，我們有必要提供計算高效的方案來實際實現這些保障。該領域現有的結果僅限於非常特殊的模型。我們旨在推廣其中的一些關鍵性原則並把這些結果拓展到相當廣泛的設定下。在這個過程中，我們希望進一步改進這些結果。

14301519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301519.value: The main results of this project are (1) a complete characterization of feasibility of decoding and list-decoding (for small list size) for General Omniscient Arbitrarily Varying Channels (AVC)s; (2) rate lower bounds on the rate of codes for AVCs that are in the feasibility region and (3) a formulation of a combinatorial conjecture that, if correct, would certify the optimality of the construction in (2).

14301519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301519.value: The main research directions that the results from this project suggest is an investigation of the structure of optimal codes for AVCs (towards resolving conjecture (3)). The starting point is to investigate the plausibility of the conjecture for specific simple classes of channels (e.g. binary channels with uniform marginals).

14301519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301519.value: Coding theory studies the design of schemes for reliable transmission of messages over unreliable channels. Much of the focus in the classical theory are simple error models such as bit flips and erasures. This project generalizes many of the fundamental classical results to a very general class of error models, rendering them applicable to virtually any scenario in which information is corrupted.

14301619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301619.value: The geometry of Calabi-Yau manifolds is a very rich subject and it has been studied extensively from many different perspectives, including differential geometry, algebraic geometry, symplectic geometry, as well as string theory in physics. For instance, mirror symmetry is a highly nontrivial duality between mirror Calabi-Yau manifolds. Quantization of a classical mechanical system produces a quantum mechanical system. Quantization in mathematics has many far-reaching applications in geometry and representation theory. In this proposal, the PI plans to study several important aspects of symplectic geometry of Calabi-Yau manifolds and quantization. These include examples properties and moduli of coisotropic A-branes, Gukov-Witten proposal for deformation quantization and geometric quantization, representations associated to nilpotent orbits and other related geometric problems. Calabi-Yau流形的幾何是一個非常豐富的研究科目， 並且已經進行了來自許多不同的觀點的研究，包括微分幾何， 代數幾何，辛幾何，以及物理學中的弦理論。 例如，鏡對稱性是鏡像Calabi-Yau流形之間非常重要的對偶性。 經典力學系統的量子化產生量子力學系統。 數學中量子化在幾何學和表示論中有許多深遠的應用。 在這提案中，研究員計劃研究Calabi-Yau流形的辛幾何和量子化。 這些包括A-branes的屬性，Gukov-Witten提出的變形量子化和幾何量子化， 冪零軌道的相關表示，及其他有關的幾何問題。

14301619.label: Realisation of objectives
14301619.value: For objective 1, ‘Further our understanding of symplectic geometry of Calabi-Yau manifolds and related problems’, in joint work with Kwokwai Chan and Ziming Ma, we apply techniques of asymptotic analysis developed in our previous works to tropicalize the pre-dgBV algebra which governs smoothing of a maximally degenerate Calabi-Yau log variety introduced in another of our recent work. Then a comparison between this tropicalized algebra with the dgBV algebra associated to the deformation theory of the semi-flat part allows us to extract consistent scattering diagrams from appropriate Maurer-Cartan solutions. This proved a conjecture of Fukaya. For objective 2 ‘Studies of deformation quantization and geometric quantization’, the PI had obtained many new results : (1) developing the theory of quantization for symplectic manifolds with transversal real polarization. This includes deformation quantization, geometric quantization, Toeplitz quantization. Certain polarizations with toric singularities are also investigated. (2) studying various quantization schemes for Kahler manifolds with Hamiltonian T-symmetry. We constructed a one-parameter family of Kahler polarization limiting to a mixed polarization, describing the behaviours of geometric quantizations of this family and their limiting behaviours. In particular, this gives a geometric description of the ‘quantization commutes with symmetry’ results of Guillemin and Sternberg. (3) analysing non-formal deformation quantization. Applying the Fedosov connections constructed in our previous work, we find a (dense) subsheaf of smooth functions on a Kähler manifold X which admits a non-formal deformation quantization. We prove that this subsheaf of functions can be quantized to a sheaf of twisted differential operators (TDO), which is isomorphic to that associated to the prequantum line bundle. We also show that examples of such quantizable functions are given by images of quantum moment maps.

14301619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301619.value: In the paper ‘Smoothing, scattering, and a conjecture of Fukaya’, we verify a conjecture of Fukaya, in which he proposed a remarkable explanation of mirror symmetry detailing the SYZ conjecture by introducing two correspondences: one between the theory of pseudo-holomorphic curves on a Calabi-Yau manifold Xˇ and the multi-valued Morse theory on the base Bˇ of an SYZ fibration pˇ:Xˇ→Bˇ, and the other between deformation theory of the mirror X and the same multi-valued Morse theory on Bˇ. In this paper, we prove a reformulation of the main conjecture in Fukaya's second correspondence, where multi-valued Morse theory on the base Bˇ is replaced by tropical geometry on the Legendre dual B. In the proof, we apply techniques of asymptotic analysis developed in our previous works to tropicalize the pre-dgBV algebra which governs smoothing of a maximally degenerate Calabi-Yau log variety introduced in another of our recent work. Then a comparison between this tropicalized algebra with the dgBV algebra associated to the deformation theory of the semi-flat part allows us to extract consistent scattering diagrams from appropriate Maurer-Cartan solutions. In the 2 joint papers with Tony Yau ‘ Berezin-Toeplitz Quantization in Real Polarizations with Toric Singularities’ and ‘ Deformation quantization via Toeplitz operators on geometric quantization in real polarizations’, we developed the theory of Toeplitz quantization for symplectic manifolds admitting transversal real polarisation. In the 2 joint papers with Dan Wang ‘ Geodesic rays in the space of Kähler metrics with T-symmetry’ and ‘Geometric quantizations of mixed polarizations on Kähler manifolds with T-symmetry’, we developed the theory of quantization for Kahler manifolds with Hamiltonian T-symmetry. We constructed a natural one parameter family of Kahler polarizations limiting to a naturally constructed mixed polarization. Then we analysed the behaviour of the geometric quantizations for these family of Kahler polarizations and their limiting behaviours. As a result, this gives a geometric description of the result of Guillemin and Sternberg on quantization commutes with reduction. In the paper ‘Quantizable functions on Kähler manifolds and non-formal quantization’, we apple the Fedosov connections constructed in our previous work, we find a (dense) subsheaf of smooth functions on a Kähler manifold X which admits a non-formal deformation quantization. When X is prequantizable and the Fedosov connection satisfies an integrality condition, we prove that this subsheaf of functions can be quantized to a sheaf of twisted differential operators (TDO), which is isomorphic to that associated to the prequantum line bundle. We also show that examples of such quantizable functions are given by images of quantum moment maps.

14301619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301619.value: The theories and results we developed from these outcome will provide us with new tools to uncover new and exciting hiding structures in mirror symmetry and quantization problem.

14301619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301619.value: Calabi-Yau geometry plays important roles in mirror symmetry in both geometry in mathematics and string theory in physics. We proved an important conjecture of Fukaya about SYZ mirror symmetry proposal. Quantization is originated from the studies of quantum mechanics in physics and now it played many important roles in various fields in mathematics. We have obtained many new results in this important subject, including relationships between different quantization schemes.

14301719.label: Project Objectives
14301719.value: To construct the approximation solution to the steady Boltzmann equation with diffusive reflection through the superposition of the solution to the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with slip boundary and the solution to the Knudsen layer equation. For the spatial domain, the focus is first on the one-dimensional case with slab symmetry and then on the two-dimensional case where one variable is in the bounded interval and the other one is spatially periodic. To study the same problem in the time-dependent setting. The main issues include: a) to establish the uniform estimate and global well-posedness for the IBVP on the full CNS equations with slip boundary in general bounded domains; b) to construct the approximation solution of the Boltzmann equation as in the setting of the first objective; c) to study the possibility of including initial layer.

14301719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301719.value: This project is concerned with the fluid dynamic approximation to solutions of the steady or unsteady nonlinear Boltzmann equation in bounded domains with diffusive reflection boundaries for a slightly rarefied gas flow. We mainly aim at constructing the approximation solution through solving the full compressible Navier-Stokes system with slip boundaries combined with a first-order kinetic boundary layer correction when the Knudsen number is suitably small. The Knudsen layer is necessarily introduced to derive the slip boundaries for the viscous fluid equations so that the kinetic boundary condition can be also approximated up to the first order in the Knudsen number. The obtained fluid dynamic approximation solution is realistic and useful in the numerical computations over the whole domain of the Boltzmann solution at small Knudsen numbers. The main goal in the mathematical analysis is to establish the uniform estimates on the fluid solution, the Knudsen layer solution, and the Boltzmann solution for the remainder under the corresponding boundary conditions. One challenge of such problem is due to the boundary singularity of the velocity distribution function and also the interaction of the boundary layer with the fluid solution around the boundary. The subject on the fluid dynamic limit or approximation in the Boltzmann theory has a long history, dating back to Maxwell and Boltzmann themselves, and developed by Hilbert, Chapman and Enskog, and later by many others. For the Boltzmann equation with boundaries, most of research works in the mathematical literature have been focused on investigations of the incompressible hydrodynamical limit, while there are few results studying the compressible viscous fluid approximation, particularly when the realistic slip boundary condition on the fluid equations is taken into account. We expect the current project to provide a preliminary understanding of the problem in several specific physical situations. 該項目涉及在有界域中的穩態或非穩態的非線性Boltzmann方程解的流體動力學逼近，邊界條件假定為描述稀薄氣流的擴散反射邊界。我們主要旨在通過求解具有滑移邊界的完全可壓縮Navier-Stokes系統來構造逼近解，並結合適當小Knudsen數的一階動力學邊界層修正。必須引入Knudsen層的目的是以此導出粘性流體方程的滑移邊界條件，故動力學邊界條件也能近似到一階Knudsen數。所獲得的流體動力學逼近解對於帶小Knudsen數的Boltzmann方程解在整個區域上的數值計算中具有實際意義而且有用。數學分析的主要目標是在相應的邊界條件下建立流體解、Knudsen層解和Boltzmann餘項解的一致估計。該問題的一個挑戰是由於速度分佈函數的邊界奇異性以及邊界層與邊界周圍的流體解的相互作用。 Boltzmann理論中流體動力學極限或逼近的研究歷史悠久，可追溯到Maxwell和Boltzmann本身，由Hilbert、Chapman和Enskog發展，後來由許多其他人研究。對於帶邊界的Boltzmann方程，數學文獻中的大部分研究工作都集中在不可壓縮流體動力學極限，而研究可壓縮粘性流體逼近的結果很少，特別是考慮流體方程的較現實的滑移邊界條件。我們希望本項目能夠在幾種特定的物理情況下對提出的問題有初步的理解。

14301719.label: Realisation of objectives
14301719.value: The first objective is concerned with the steady Boltzmann equation with diffusive reflection boundary condition. The main goal is to construct the fluid dynamic approximation solution through the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with slip boundary condition together with the Knudsen layer solution. Specifically, we studied the one-dimensional steady Boltzmann flow in a channel. The walls of the channel are assumed to have vanishing velocity and given temperatures at two end points. This problem was studied by Esposito et al where they showed that the solution tends to a local Maxwellian with fluid parameters satisfying the compressible Navier-Stokes equation with no-slip boundary condition. However, a lot of numerical experiments reveal that the fluid layer does not entirely stick to the boundary. In the regime where the Knudsen number is reasonably small, the slip phenomenon is significant near the boundary. Thus, we revisited this problem by taking into account the slip boundary conditions. Following the lines of Coron, we first give a formal asymptotic analysis to verify that the flow governed by the Boltzmann equation is accurately approximated by a superposition of a steady CNS equation with a temperature jump condition and two Knudsen layers located at two end points. Then we establish in a rigorous way uniform estimates on the remainder term and derive the slip boundary condition for compressible Navier-Stokes equations. The second objective of this project is concerned with the time-evolutionary problem on the Boltzmann equation with diffusive reflection boundary condition. The main goal is to still construct the fluid dynamic approximation solution via the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with suitable boundary conditions. However, the time-dependence makes the problem more subtle to treat. It is well known that the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations can be deduced via the Chapman-Enskog expansion from the Boltzmann equation as the first-order correction to the Euler equations with viscosity and heat-conductivity coefficients of order of the Knudsen number. Regarding our objective, we have carried out the rigorous mathematical analysis of the compressible Navier-Stokes approximation for the Boltzmann equation regarding the initial-boundary value problems in general bounded domains. The main goal is to measure the uniform-in-time deviation of the Boltzmann solution with diffusive reflection boundary condition from a local Maxwellian with its fluid quantities given by the solutions to the corresponding compressible Navier-Stokes equations with consistent non-slip boundary conditions whenever the Knudsen number is small enough. Specifically, it is shown that for well chosen initial data around constant equilibrium states, the deviation weighted by a velocity function turns out to be the higher order of small Knudsen number with corresponding uniform estimates global in time. The proof is based on the uniform estimates for the remainder in different functional spaces without any spatial regularity. One key step is to obtain the global-in-time existence as well as uniform-in-Knudsen estimates for regular solutions to the full compressible Navier-Stokes equations in bounded domains when the Knudsen number is involved in the analysis.

14301719.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301719.value: In paper no 1, we studied the compressible Navier-Stokes approximation for the Boltzmann equation in bounded domains. We first obtain the global existence and uniform regularity of solutions to the compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system in bounded domains. Different from the isentropic case, the appearance of temperature equation in the full system induces an extra difficulty. We made use of the Galerkin method together with the Helmholtz decomposition and also carried out our energy estimates via the conormal differentiation. In paper no 2, we studied the heat transfer problem for the Boltzmann equation in a channel with diffusive boundary condition. We first gave a formal asymptotic analysis to show that the Boltzmann flow is accurately approximated by a superposition of a steady CNS equation with a temperature jump condition and two Knudsen layers located at end points. We further established uniform estimates on the remainder and derived in a rigorous way the slip boundary condition for compressible Navier-Stokes equations. In paper no 3, we studied the compressible Euler-Maxwell limit for global smooth solutions to the Vlasov-Maxwell-Boltzmann system, and in paper no 4, we studied a half-space problem on the full Euler-Poisson system. The main goal of these two works is to understand the possibility of extending those results in papers no 1 and no 2 to the situation where an electric or magnetic field is present.

14301719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301719.value: It has been of its own interest to study the full compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system in general bounded domains with slip boundary conditions which are consistent with those derived from the Boltzmann equation via the Navier-Stokes approximation. For instance, it is interesting to develop the well-posedness theory in both the steady and unsteady cases. More importantly, we notice that the ghost effect equations are also justified through the fluid dynamic limit of the Boltzmann equation in the steady case instead of the NS approximation, and hence we need to understand the difference of such limiting solutions and NSF approximation solutions with small Knudsen number.

14301719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301719.value: This project is concerned with the fluid dynamic approximation to solutions of the steady or unsteady nonlinear Boltzmann equation in bounded domains with diffusive reflection boundaries for a slightly rarefied gas flow. We mainly aim at constructing the approximation solution through solving the full compressible Navier-Stokes system with slip boundaries combined with a first-order kinetic boundary layer correction when the Knudsen number is suitably small. The Knudsen layer is necessarily introduced to derive the slip boundaries for the viscous fluid equations so that the kinetic boundary condition can be also approximated up to the first order in the Knudsen number. The obtained fluid dynamic approximation solution is realistic and useful in the numerical computations over the whole domain of the Boltzmann solution at small Knudsen numbers.

14301819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14301819.value: This project applies combinatorial methods to study knots and other related topological objects. We will study various aspects of grid diagrams and the grid Floer homology. We will mainly focus on three parts: First, we look for combinatorial proofs of two significant properties of grid Floer homology, namely, the detection of genus and fiberness of a knot. Second, we want to study various invariant of filtered grid complex, which can be potentially used to give stronger bounds on slice genus and unknotting number of knots. Third, we plan to use a refined grid diagram to study spatial graphs. We hope to develop Legendrian grid invariant for graphs and increase our overall understanding of Legendrian graphs and contact geometry. 此課題主要使用組合方法研究紐結及相關的拓撲對象，包括網格圖和相關的網格同調群。 我們主要著眼於以下三個方向：第一，利用組合方法來證明網格同調群和紐結虧格與纖維化的關係。第二，研究率子網格群的相關不變量，並給出紐結平凡化的一個較強估計。第三，通過改良網格圖來研究空間圖，並發展Legendrian網格圖不變量用以研究Legendrian空間圖和接觸幾何。

14301819.label: Realisation of objectives
14301819.value: The project objectives were investigated and partially realized through various publications, with some shifts in research direction based on emerging opportunities and constraints. Below is a detailed assessment of each objective: 1. In the Mid-Term Progress Report, we mentioned that the investigation of combinatorial proofs for grid homologies' detection of genus and fiberness of knots (Objective 1) faced significant challenges. The planned collaboration with Prof. Margaret Doig (US) was severely impacted by COVID-19 travel restrictions, preventing crucial in-person discussions initially scheduled for summer 2020. Subsequently, Prof. Doig's research interests shifted away from this area, further complicating the collaboration. After careful consideration, we strategically redirected our efforts toward more promising directions (detailed in point 4), though this meant partial achievement of this original objective. 2. Objective 2 was successfully addressed through a collaborative paper with Dr. Jingling Yang (former Ph.D. student). While our initial approach centered on grid diagrams, we ultimately employed classical Floer homology methods to investigate slice genus in rational settings. This work has yielded significant results and has been submitted to a leading journal in the field for review. 3. We made substantial progress on Objective 3, developing a "weak" version of the Alexander polynomial for graphs using grid diagrams (detailed in Paper 9, Section 8). While this represents meaningful theoretical advancement, we are currently enhancing the manuscript with additional applications to improve its impact before submission. It's worth noting that similar ideas of the project have been undertaken by Hajime Kubota, who wrote two papers on grid homology for MOY graphs, including "Some Properties of Grid Homology for MOY Graphs" and "Concordance Invariant \Upsilon for Balanced Spatial Graphs Using Grid Homology" 4. A significant breakthrough emerged during the project's second half (from 2023), when we discovered that spatial graphs could be more effectively studied using spanning trees rather than grid diagrams. This new direction, while deviating from our original grid-diagram focus in Objective 1, has proven extremely fruitful. The results are documented in Papers 7, representing substantial contributions to the field. This unexpected development, while leading us away from our original objective, has opened promising new research avenues and compensates for the partial achievement of Objective 1. In summary, while not all objectives were achieved exactly as originally envisioned, the project has yielded significant mathematical insights and contributions
