14301819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14301819.value: The project yielded several significant breakthroughs, with the most notable emerging through our development of the spanning tree model for studying spatial graphs. This novel approach, detailed in Paper 7, makes substantial progress toward resolving Fox's conjecture - a 50-year-old open problem concerning the unimodality of Alexander polynomials of alternating knots. This work contributes to the broader understanding of log-concavity in polynomial invariants, a fundamental phenomenon in combinatorics that Fields Medalist June Huh specifically highlighted in his 2018 ICM address. Another major breakthrough came in our study of rational slice genus, conducted in collaboration with Dr. Jingling Yang. We introduced the innovative concept of middle relative Spinc structures, which provided crucial new insights into the structure of knot Floer complex. This framework enabled us to develop a more natural and conceptually elegant proof of Rasmussen's conjecture regarding minimal genus of knots. While this result was previously established through ad hoc methods by Ni and the PI (published in Advances in Mathematics), our new approach offers a more illuminating and structurally revealing perspective. The project's overall productivity is demonstrated through 9 research papers and presentations at 7 international conferences (detailed in Part C), representing significant contributions across multiple aspects of knot theory and low-dimensional topology. These works collectively advance our understanding of both classical problems and emerging directions in the field.

14301819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14301819.value: The spanning tree model shows exceptional promise for further development, particularly in addressing fundamental questions about polynomial invariants' unimodality or log-concavity. With support from a new RGC-funded project starting in 2025, we plan to: 1.Further develop techniques addressing Fox's conjecture 2. Extend the model to study broader classes of graphs 3. Investigate connections with Huh's work on combinatorial log-concavity Additionally, we will continue developing applications of middle relative Spinc structures in knot Floer homology, aiming to unlock new geometric insights and potentially find general surgery formulas in rational homology sphere.

14301819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14301819.value: This project originally aimed to study knots and graphs using a method called "grid diagrams" - a way of representing three-dimensional structures on a two-dimensional grid. While exploring this approach, we discovered an even more powerful method using "spanning trees", which led to unexpected breakthroughs. Our most significant achievement was making progress on a 50-year-old mathematical puzzle known as Fox's conjecture. This conjecture deals with a fascinating pattern in number sequences from coefficients of a knot polynomial invariant: the numbers first increase then decrease, like mountain peaks (called "unimodality"). An even stronger pattern, called "log-concavity," appears when these numbers satisfy the inequality $a_i^2>a_{i-1}a_{i+1}$. Fields Medalist June Huh showed that such patterns mysteriously appear across many areas of mathematics, making our progress particularly significant. We also made important advances in understanding knot complexity in four-dimensional space, developing new tools that give clearer insights into classical problems. Although we deviated from our original planned method, this flexibility allowed us to make more impactful discoveries. These findings contribute to our fundamental understanding of shapes and structures, with potential applications in molecular biology and network design.

14302319.label: Project Objectives
14302319.value: We shall investigate the existence of stationary solutions to the Cahn-Hilliard model with singular potentials and inpainting source terms. Then, we shall extend the result to account for the stationary problem and the time-dependent problem with more general source terms. We shall develop iterative numerical schemes based on the existence proof in Objective 1 to solve the stationary Cahn-Hilliard inpainting model with singular potentials. Then, we shall investigate how to implement the numerical schemes and conduct numerical experiments to compare with previous methods for inpainting. We shall investigate a Cahn-Hilliard model with singular potentials and tumour growth source terms. We propose to derive regularity estimates for an auxiliary variable, from which the regularity estimates for the solution variables can be obtained. Then, we shall use these new regularity estimates to establish the uniqueness of solutions to the tumour model. We shall extend the results of Objective 3 to a multiphase Cahn-Hilliard model with singular potentials and tumour growth source terms. We propose to identify suitable auxiliary variables whose regularity properties can be derived more easily. Then, following a similar strategy, we shall develop new regularity arguments for the solution to the multiphase tumour model and establish the uniqueness of solutions.

14302319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302319.value: The Cahn-Hilliard (CH) equation is a fourth order nonlinear partial differential equation (PDE) originally used to model the separation of a mixture containing two phases of matter, such as water and oil, and is now an ubiquitous component of many mathematical models in applied sciences. It is formulated with a nonconvex potential function, usually taken as a smooth polynomial, that possesses two equal minima, say -1 and 1. Through the addition of appropriate source terms, the CH equation has seen recent applications in modelling the growth of tumours and in repairing damaged black-and-white images (also known as inpainting). However, an unfortunate feature with a polynomial potential is that the solution may not stay bounded in between -1 and 1, and undesirable effects, such as negative mass densities in tumour models or new shades of colour in black-and-white images, can occur. A remedy is to employ singular potentials, such as a logarithmic-type function, to ensure that the solution to the model stays in between -1 and 1. In exchange, the mathematical analysis of these models with singular potentials become more involved compared to the polynomial potentials. For recent applications in tumour growth and inpainting, the new combination of singular potentials and source terms has not received much attention in the literature, and current analytical studies are mostly confined to establishing the existence of weak solutions. In this project, we plan to expand the scope of the analysis for these new Cahn-Hilliard models with singular potentials and source terms by investigating the issues of uniqueness and regularity of solutions, as well as addressing the existence of stationary solutions analytically and also numerically. We believe that the proposed methodologies can yield both theoretical and practical contributions towards the active research areas of tumour growth and inpainting, in the form of a novel and alternative strategy to perform inpainting with the CH equation that is built upon a rigorous analytical basis, and a mathematical foundation for practitioners to make meaningful comparisons between tumour model simulations and experimental data. 14302319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302319.value: We studied several Cahn-Hilliard models with singular potentials and source terms that have seen applications in image processing and tumour growth. Through a series of auxiliary results developed to handle the interplay between the potentials and relevant source terms, our chief contributions are the existence of weak solutions, well-posedness of strong solutions, long-time behaviour in the context of global and exponential attractors, optimal control and parameter identification for the models, as well as stable and convergent numerical schemes. In particular, our research result is the first in obtaining a direct proof of stationary solutions of these kind of systems that do not admit an obvious Lyapunov structure. These works are published in some of the best applied mathematics journals, such as SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis, Journal of Differential Equations, SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization, Advances in Nonlinear Analysis and Journal of Numerical Mathematics.

14302319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302319.value: While the main focus of the project is around the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the associated Cahn-Hilliard models, practitioners are more interested in optimisation applications. In the context of tumour modelling these involve parameter estimation, computing optimal dosage of chemotherauptic drugs and optimal treatment times. In this project we have several analytical results but did not explore the numerical aspects in part due to the lack of data. Hence, it would be very interesting to combine our analytical investigations with the clinical data available to the practitioners in developing some form of data-driven cancer treatment based on these Cahn-Hilliard models. These topics would make very good PhD research projects.

14302319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302319.value: The Cahn-Hilliard equation appears in many areas of scientific applications, ranging from fluid dynamics, material sciences, to image processing and tumour modelling, and so it is essential to develop mathematical models that can accurately capture the relevant physical phenomena. This will involve singular terms that lead to a challenging mathematical study. In this project we explored the mathematical analysis of realistic models based on the Cahn-Hilliard equation that are currently in use by practitioners for tumour growth. Our theoretical investigations demonstrate that these models are mathematically sound, leading to further studies in related optimal control problems and the development of convergent numerical schemes. Our ideas developed to tackle the challenging singular terms can also be used on similar types of equations prevalent in other areas of scientific applications, such as pattern formation and active emulsions.

14302419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302419.value: Hot fluid tends to rise and cold fluid tends to fall. When the driving force due to the temperature difference is large enough to overcome the dampening effects of fluid viscosity and thermal diffusivity, convective motion occurs. Increasing the temperature difference further, the convective motion eventually becomes turbulent. Turbulent thermal convection is ubiquitous in nature, occurring in the the atmosphere and oceans of the Earth as well as in the outer layer of the Sun, and plays an important role in many technological applications. It is often studied in the setting of Rayleigh-Benard convection in a closed container of fluid heated from below and cooled from above. There are two important problems of interest in turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection, namely the spatial structure of the boundary layers and the dependence of the turbulent heat transfer and the velocity of the large scale circulation, measured respectively by the Nusselt number (Nu) and Reynolds number (Re), on the two dimensionless control parameters, the Rayleigh number (Ra) and Prandtl number (Pr), of the system. Boundary layers are flow regions in the vicinity of solid boundaries that are characterized by comparatively large gradients of the time-averaged velocity and/or temperature fields in the direction perpendicular to the boundaries, and play a critical role in turbulent transport. In turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection, the thermal and velocity boundary layers are non-steady with fluctuations, the mean horizontal velocity vanishes far away from the plates, and the motion of the fluid arises due to buoyancy. There is not yet a boundary layer theory that takes into account all of these effects. Built on our earlier work, we have recently successfully derived boundary layer equations for both the velocity and temperature fields that take into account all of the above effects. In this project, we shall make use of these new theoretical developments to study the two important issues of interest: the spatial structure of boundary layer and the dependence of Nu and Re on Ra and Pr. 14302419.label: Realisation of objectives
14302419.value: Objective 1: We focus on the boundary layer thickness, an important spatial feature of the boundary layers, and have derived analytical results for the thickness of the velocity and thermal boundary layers in the high Rayleigh-number regime where the horizontal pressure gradient is negligible. Our results show that both the velocity and thermal boundary layer thicknesses are approximately inversely proportional to the square-root of the Reynold number. The velocity boundary layer thickness is independent of the parameter that measures the correlation between the velocity and temperature fluctuations and the thermal boundary layer thickness also does not depend on this parameter in both the high and low Prandtl number (Pr) limits. Thus, the velocity boundary layer thickness has a similar behavior as in steady state forced convection but with a faster growth rate in the horizontal coordinate x. Moreover, the velocity boundary layer thickness is independent of the Pr and the thermal boundary layer thickness has the same Pr-dependence as the inverse of the Nusselt number. Our analytical results are in excellent agreement with the numerical results obtained by solving the boundary layer equations numerically. Hence, objective 1 is fully realized. Objective 2: Using the set of boundary layer equations developed for turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection, we have derived analytical results for the dependence of the heat flux, measured by the Nusselt number (Nu), on the Reynolds (Re) and Prandtl (Pr) numbers and two parameters that measure fluctuations in the high-Rayleigh-number regime where the horizontal pressure gradient is negligible. Our theoretical results show that Nu approximately scales as the square-root of Re and scales as Pr to 1/3-power in the high-Pr limit and scales as Pr to 1/2-power in the low-Pr limit. Our theoretical predictions of Nu are in good agreement with direct numerical simulation (DNS) results. Our theoretical results further reveal a close resemblance of the scaling dependencies of Nusselt number on Reynolds and Prandtl numbers, in the low- and high-Pr limits, in turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection and steady forced convection. This result is non-trivial as velocity fluctuations are important and contribute to the scaling dependence of Nu in the low-Pr limit in our theory, but they are non-existent in steady forced convection. This finding thus solves the longstanding puzzle of the apparent applicability of the scaling results of steady forced convection in turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection. Hence, we have exceeded objective 2. Objective 3: By solving the boundary layer equations, we have obtained the mean velocity and temperature profiles at different values of the two parameters that measure the size of the fluctuations and compared these theoretical results with the numerical profiles obtained in direct numerical simulations (DNS). Specifically, we have successfully fitted the numerical profiles obtained by DNS calculation using our results obtained by solving the boundary layer equations and obtained the best-fit values of the two parameters at Ra=10^8 and Pr=0.1. Thus we have realized the major part of objective 3. This procedure, when repeated for DNS data at different Ra and Pr, enables us to study the dependence of the size of fluctuations on Ra and Pr and completely realize objective 3. While we were working on this, we became aware that it is more challenging and scientifically more worthwhile to study turbulent vertical convection in a fluid between two differentially heated vertical surfaces, another important model system of thermally driven turbulent flows, especially because the important question of how heat flux depends on the control parameters has not yet been answered (at that time) for turbulent vertical convection despite a number of theoretical attempts. As a result, we have devoted our remaining efforts in this project to derive results for heat flux in turbulent vertical convection. By studying the mean flow equations in the large aspect-ratio limit, we have successfully derived relationships between the heat flux and the wall shear stress with minimal closure approximations. Using these relationships, we have derived analytically the dependence of heat flux as well as wall shear stress on the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers, the two control parameters of the flow in the high-Ra limit. Our theoretical results are in excellent agreement with available DNS results for different Prandtl numbers.

14302419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302419.value: We have derived analytical results for the boundary layers and heat flux in turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection. Our results for the boundary layer thickness for both the velocity and thermal boundary layers provide useful and important information about the spatial structure of the boundary layers. In particular, the velocity boundary layer is found to have the similar dependence on Reynolds number as in forced convection. Our analytical results for the heat flux advance the existing knowledge obtained from a scaling theory. Moreover, our results show that the dependence of the Nusselt number on Reynolds number and Prandtl number in the limits of high and low Prandtl number resembles the scaling dependencies in forced convection. This finding thus explains the puzzling apparent applicability of scaling results of forced convection in turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection. These results have been published in "Heat flux in turbulent Rayleigh-Bénard convection: Predictions derived from a boundary layer theory" reported in Part C. We have further extended our project to study turbulent vertical convection in a fluid between two vertical walls at different temperatures, another common model system of thermal convection besides Rayleigh-Benard convection. The important question of how heat flux depends on the control parameters of the flow has not been answered for turbulent vertical convection despite earlier theoretical attempts. We have derived relationships between the heat flux and the wall shear stress in the large aspect-ratio limit with minimal closure approximations. Using these relationships, we have successfully obtained the dependence of heat flux and wall shear stress on the Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers, the two control parameters of the flow in the high-Ra limit, and thus answered the longstanding heat flux question for large aspect-ratio turbulent vertical convection. The results on turbulent vertical convection have been published in "Heat flux and wall shear stress in large-aspect-ratio turbulent vertical convection" reported in Part C.

14302419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302419.value: Our success in deriving analytical results for turbulent vertical convection in the large aspect ratio limit has motivated us to propose a theoretical study of the challenging problem of turbulent double-diffusive convection in a fluid layer between two vertical walls kept at different temperatures and salt concentrations. Turbulent double-diffusive convection plays an important role in oceanography and is crucial for ice-ocean interactions. The melting process of ice is controlled by a combination of heat and salinity transport. Results obtained in the proposed theoretical study can thus be important for the prediction of ice-melting rate due particularly to the impacts of global climate change. We have submitted a new RGC GRF application and successfully secured finding for the proposal theoretical study of turbulent double-diffusive convection.

14302419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302419.value: Turbulent thermal convection is ubiquitous in nature and in many technological processes. It occurs in the atmosphere and oceans of the Earth as well as the outer layer of the Sun. There are two important model systems used for studying turbulent thermal convection: Rayleigh-Benard convection in a fluid confined between two horizontal plates, heated from below and cooled from above and vertical convection in a fluid between two vertical walls at different temperatures. In this project, using the boundary layer equations developed by us for turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection, we have derived analytical results on the velocity and thermal boundary layers thickness and heat flux in turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection. Analytical results for turbulent flows are rare and our results advance the existing knowledge in the field and explain a puzzle. We have further extended our project to study large aspect-ratio turbulent vertical convection and obtained analytical results that answer the challenging question of how heat flux depends on the control parameters of the flow.

To develop efficient computer programs for producing accurate results and to post these programs onto freely available websites for general use. 14302519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302519.value: Zero-inflated data arise frequently in medical, social, behavioral, and financial studies and typically take non-negative values but have a substantial proportion at zero. A common way to manage a zero-inflated variable is to first split it into two random variables, a binary indicator to determine the occurrence of excess zeros, and a continuous/discrete random variable to determine the actual level of the response. Second, a two-part/zero-inflated model is proposed to simultaneously model the two random variables. Traditional two-part/zero-inflated models have mainly focused on zero inflation in continuous, count, ordinal, and nominal data and assumed that predictors can be fully observed. However, partially ordered data, which are neither completely ordered nor completely unordered, are commonly encountered but under-recognized in practical applications. Moreover, latent factors, which are characterized through multiple observed variables from different perspectives, may exist and influence the probability of excess zeros and the actual level of the response in various ways. Despite considerable literature on modeling zero-inflated data, available approaches have neither addressed zero inflation in partially ordered data nor accommodated the latent factors in the two-part/zero-inflated model framework. This study aims to develop a novel modeling approach to jointly address the aforementioned data structures. The proposed model consists of three parts: the first is an exploratory factor analysis (EFA) model that summarizes latent factors through multiple observed variables while leaving the number of latent factors and the associations between latent and observed variables to be unspecified and allowing them to be fully determined by the data; the second is a logistic regression model that predicts the probability of excess zeros; and the third is a class of partitioned conditional models that examines potential predictors for a partially ordered response without excess zeros. Several interesting extensions include the following: (i) allowing mixed-mode and/or highly non-normal variables in the EFA model; (ii) modeling longitudinal/clustered zero-inflated and partially ordered data; and (iii) managing missing data in responses and covariates. This study also aims to develop a full Bayesian approach coupled with advanced MCMC methods to simultaneously determine latent factors based on observed variables, select relevant predictors for each part of the model, and perform parameter estimation. To the best of our knowledge, no existing method is available for simultaneously accomplishing these multiple tasks. Computer programs/packages for statistical analysis are also developed and are available to practitioners. The developed methodologies are applied to real problems in Hong Kong and in other settings.

14302519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302519.value: Zero-inflated and partially ordered data arise frequently in medical, social, behavioral, and financial studies. The presence of latent variables is also prevalent in various research settings. This study proposed novel modeling approaches to model the multiple data structures jointly. The newly proposed models have several unique features, such as accommodating latent responses or predictors, addressing zero-inflated data, and proposing a hierarchical structure to formulate partially ordered data. The proposed models and developed methodologies are original and applicable to various problems in medical, behavioral, social, and psychological sciences. The novel methods developed in this project have addressed challenging issues in regression with multi-mode data and thus fill the gap in regression analysis with complex data structures. The applications of the developed methodologies have produced essential findings and new insights into vital problems in different research areas. A total of 19 papers in international journals, such as Biometrics, Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics, Statistics in Medicine, Journal of Multivariate Analysis, Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, Science China Mathematics, Sociological Methods and Research, Multivariate Behavioral Research, and Structural Equation Modeling, represent the primary outputs. Some extensions of the proposed methods beyond the project objectives have also been considered.

14302619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302619.value: In this proposal, we aim to design and validate hydrogel-based artificial cells capable of communicating with neighboring artificial or natural cells. We will first construct the plasmids that enable the artificial cells to sense and response to the signaling molecules released by P. aeruginosa, a bacterium that causes severe acute and chronic infections. The plasmid contains two part, the regulator part and the reporter part. The regulator part of the plasmid allows the signaling molecules diffusing into the artificial cells to activate the reporter part of the plasmid, which will produce a protein product. The protein product can be a fluorescent protein, an antibacterial toxin or a protein factor disrupting biofilm. Secondly, we will demonstrate the communication between two groups of artificial cells co-cultured in a microchamber. The first group of artificial cells will produce the signaling molecules. The second group of artificial cells will receive the signaling molecules and start the production of an enzyme capable of breaking down the signaling molecules. With proper experimental design and conditions, we expect to achieve a synchronized oscillation of the protein expression in both groups of artificial cells. Finally, we will investigate the communication of the artificial cells with P. aeruginosa cells. Upon the diffusing of the signaling molecules from nearby P. aeruginosa cells into the artificial cells, the artificial cells will express an antibacterial toxin and a biofilm dispersion factor. In this way, the artificial cells can sense and kill the P. aeruginosa cells and disrupt the formation of biofilm. Comparing to the previous research on lipid vesicle-based artificial cells capable of communication, the proposed hydrogel-based artificial cells are robust against rupture by osmotic pressure, have significantly extended lifetime and support the mass exchange between the cells and the surroundings. 14302719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302719.value: 本計劃的目標是製定第一個統計程序，試圖預測未來時間序列的變點。 隨著數據收集技術的進步，在工程，環境，金融計量經濟學和遺傳學等的各種科學領域中經常遇到很長的時間序列數據。在分析這些時間序列時，越來越多的例子揭示了數據中存在結構變化。為了檢測這些結構變化， 變點檢測和估算程序已在文獻中廣泛開發。 但是，變點分析中常用的方法只是側重於 檢測整個時間序列內的變點（離線方法），和 最快地檢測數據中的變化點（在線方法）。這兩類方法都牽涉已經發生的變點。 遺憾的是，未來的變點何時發生這一顯然更為重要的問題仍被探索。 為了填補文獻中的這一重要空白，本計劃的目標是 開發一種描述變點發生機制的新型統計模型。特別的是， 這個模型假設一個由非負噪聲驅動的潛在隨機漫步過程，衍生出觀察到的時間序列。 根據模型構造, 當潛在的過程屬於不同的區間,，時間序列便有不同的相關結構. 因此, 變點的發生等同於潛在過程達到不同區間的門檻。所以，通過預測潛在過程何時達到下一個門檻，我們便可以檢測未來的變點。 此項目計劃研究模型的概率性質，如平穩性和遍歷性，開發基於似然的參數估計方法，模型選擇程序，模型的變點檢測算法，並構建未來變點的估計和預測區間。 成功執行此項目將產生一個完整程序, 可以估計時間序列未來的變點和構造未來變點的預測區間。 隨著變點分析問題的需求不斷增加，本研究 將產生一個能夠預測未來變點的有效程序。這將促進廣泛科學研究領域的進展，如計量經濟學，電氣和環境工程，金融和遺傳學。

14302719.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302719.value: This project has developed the first statistical model for predicting future change-points in time series. By introducing a mechanism which governs the occurrence of change-points in the model, the location of future change-points can be predicted once the model parameters are estimated. We developed a composite likelihood based method for parameter estimation and inference. An information criterion is designed for selecting the number of states and the time series model at each state of the change-point model. Moreover, prediction intervals are derived based on stopping time theory.

14302719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302719.value: The current model is on univariate time series. Extensions to multivariate time series, integer valued time series, functional time series, and spatial temporal data are interesting and important topics for further investigation.

14302719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302719.value: Although change-point analysis has received considerable attention, it mainly concerns detection of changes that have already occurred. This project develops the first statistical model, the threshold autoregressive state space (TASS) model, for predicting future change-points in time series. The model has a latent process which governs occurrence of abrupt changes, and the data follows different time series models according to the location of the latent process. By predicting when the latent process hit a threshold, the location of a future change-point can be predicted.

14302819.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14302819.value: 完全可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程組的真空動力學行為

14302819.label: Project Objectives
14302819.value: Well-posedness of regular entropy-bounded solutions to the Cauchy problem for the multi-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes systems with constant viscosities and heat conductivity in the presence of far field vacuum only. Both local and global (in time) solutions in suitable inhomogeneous Sobolev spaces will be investigated. Note that known studies give either information on unbounded entropy. However, for the classical theory of non-vacuum solutions, the entropy can be bounded uniformly. Thus it is reasonable to expect that when the initial density approaches to vacuum state with a slow rate at far field, than the boundedness of the entropy can be maintained at least locally in time, and global estimates may also be possible under some suitable smallness assumption. However, in the case that the initial density decays to vacuum very fast at the far field, we conjecture that the entropy becomes unbounded immediately after the initial time. As observed by Boltzmann [2], in physical gas dynamics, the viscosity and heat conductivity coefficients depend the temperature (in the form of power laws). Then the requirement of bounded entropy implies that these viscosities and heat conductivity coefficients become degenerate at vacuum. In this case, there are no general existing results on the well-posedness theory for the full compressible Navier-Stokes system. We aim to study the well-posedness of regular solutions in suitable inhomogeneous Sobolev spaces for the initial density which contains vacuum only at far field. We will start with a barotropic model. To understand the vacuum dynamics of the viscous compressible fluids in the presence of magnetic field. In particular, we will investigate the well-posedness of regular solutions and long time dynamics for the viscous compressible magneto-hydrodynamics (MHD).

14302819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14302819.value: The vacuum dynamics is an unavoidable and challenging problem in the study of the full compressible Navier-Stokes system, which leads to many important but difficult problems, especially for multi-dimensional compressible fluids in whole space and with finite mass and total energy. Despite many recent interesting progress in this direction, in particular for isentropic fluids, many important issues, such as the well-posed of regular solutions with bounded entropy, and existence of regular solutions in inhomogeneous spaces when the viscosity and heat conductivity coefficients may be degenerate at vacuum, remain open for the full compressible Navier-Stokes system. In the presence of vacuum, some of the major difficulties in analyzing the solutions are that besides the strong degeneracy of the momentum equations near vacuum, the physical entropy solves a highly singular equation near vacuum and the regularity has nothing to do with that of the density and the temperature, furthermore, in the case that the viscosity and heat conductivities coefficients depend on the absolute temperature, the Lame operator becomes degenerate near vacuum region due to the requirement of bounded entropy. This project aims to understand some of these key issues on entropy bounded solutions (both locally or globally) at the case that the vacuum appear only at the far fields. In particular, we propose to study the local and global regular solutions with finite entropy and far field vacuum to the Cauchy problem for the full compressible Navier-Stokes with either constant or variable viscosities and heat conductivity in inhomogeneous spaces. The related problems such as vacuum dynamics of viscous compressible fluids in the presence of magnetic field will also be investigated. 真空的動力學行為是完全可壓縮Navier-Stokes方程組理論研究中一個不可避免的挑戰性難題之一，它導致了許多重要而且困難的問題，特別是對高維在全空間具有有限質量和能量的粘性可壓縮流體具有重大意義。儘管過去在這方面已取得了一些重要進展﹙如對等熵流體﹚，但許多重要挑戰都等待解決：如有界熵的正則解的適定性，當粘性和熱傳導系數在真空蛻化時正則解的存在性等。當真空出現時，分析解的主要困難不只在於動量方程是高度蛻化的，而且物理熵滿足的方程具有高度奇性，更困難的是物理熵的正則性和密度和絕對溫度無關。而當粘性和熱傳導系數依賴於溫度時，在真空附近，Lame算子也嚴重蛻化。這個項目的主要目的是探索當真空出現在無窮遠時，物理熵有界的解的短時間或長時間的適定性及解的性態，特別我們將研究一般完全Navier-Stokes方程組在全空間的初值問題的具有有界物理熵和無窮遠真空的正則解在非齊次空間的局部或全局適定性，也將研究相關的磁場對真空動力學行為的影響。

14302819.label: Realisation of objectives
14302819.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved fully. Indeed, for the first objective to study the bounded entropy solutions to the full Navier-Stokes equations with positive constant heat conductive and viscous coefficients, the PI and his collaborator have established the local and global well-posedness of entropy bounded and velocity in some inhomogeneous Sobolev spaces in the one-dimensional case for initial density containing vacuum at far fields only and decaying slowly to the vacuum (which has been published in a top research journal CPAM, see publication No. 1), and then we have generalized such results to the multi-dimensional case (see publication No. 11). These have been achieved by overcoming the major difficulties such as high degeneracies and singularities of the governing equation for the entropy in the presence of the vacuum by developing a framework based on some elaborately singular weighted energy estimates and a modified De Giorgi type iteration techniques for degenerated parabolic equations. For the multi-dimensional case, further techniques have been developed for the estimates of the vorticity fields in the Eulerian coordinates. The ideas and techniques developed here will be important for studies of strongly degenerate nonlinear parabolic-hyperbolic systems. These are reported in published papers, see publications No. 1 and No. 11. The PI has achieved the second objective of this project. Jointly with his collaborators, the PI has successfully established the local well-posedness of the entropy bounded solutions to the Cauchy problem for the 3-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes equations with temperature-dependent viscosity coefficients which degenerate near vacuum and zero-heat-conductivity for a class of initial data containing far fields vacuum. Jointly with his collaborators, the PI first has identified a class of initial data for the case of zero-heat conductivity, so that the Cauchy problem possesses a local in time strong solution with far field vacuum, and within the life span of such solution, the velocity stays in an inhomogeneous Sobolev space, the entropy remains bounded, and the total mass, momentum and energy are conserved in time. These have been achieved by exploring the underlying structure of the system which are coupled parabolic-hyperbolic system with strong degeneracies and singularities near vacuum and an elaborate design of an enlarged system which couples a symmetric hyperbolic equation with some singular parabolic system and is equivalent to the full compressible Navier-Stokes system in terms of the density, velocity and entropy. These results have been published at a top research journal ARMA, see publication No. 8. The third objective of this project has also been fully achieved. Indeed, the PI and his collaborator Yanjin Wang have successfully investigated the effects of the magnetic field for the vacuum interface problems. Indeed, we have established the global well-posedness of the plasma-vacuum interface motion in a horizontally periodic slab impressed by a uniform non-horizontal magnetic field where the plasma is governed by the inviscid and resistive MHD and while the vacuum is governed by the pre-Maxwell equations with initial configuration close to an equilibrium. The solution is shown to decay to the equilibrium almost exponentially. Our results reveal for the first time the strong stabilizing effects of the transversal magnetic field and resistivity. Similar results hold for plasma-plasma interfaces. These have been achieved by the key discovery of the induced damping structure of the plasma vorticity due to the transversal magnetic field and resistivity. These results are the first ones for interfacial problems without irrotationality and viscosity, and have been published in a top journal CMP, see publication No. 2. Furthermore, the PI has also obtained some other significant results on important wave motions for the compressible Euler equations, MHD systems and viscous models, which are closely related to the main objectives of this project. In particular, the PI and his collaborators have obtained several significant results on the structural stability of transonic shocks in various geometries such as 3D axisymmetric nozzles and annulus, etc., and proved the first existence results on subsonic steady flows past an airfoil with a vortex line at the training edge; and gave the existence of 2-dimensional incompressible impinging jet flows with gravity. These have been published in a series of papers, see publications No. 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. Second, the PI and his collaborators have also obtained some results on the effects of the magnetic fields in the presence of physical boundaries. These results have been published, see publications No. 9, 10. Finally, the PI and his collaborators have also made progress on the dynamic motions of vacuum free boundaries for some important viscous fluid models such as the compressible primitive equations and the viscous Saint-Venant systems for shallow waters. These results are reported in two preprints, see publications No. 12, 13.

14302819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14302819.value: With the major support of this project, the PI and his collaborators have achieved the following main results: First, for both the one-dimensional and multi-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes system with positive heat conductive and viscous coefficients, the local and global (in time) well-posedness of entropy bounded and velocity in some inhomogeneous Sobolev spaces have been established for a class of initial density which contains vacuum only at far fields and decays to the vacuum state slowly. Furthermore, the critical rate of decay of the initial density is also found and justified. This is achieved by establishing a new framework based on singular weighted energy estimates and a modified De Giorgi type iterations for degenerate parabolic equations. Several new techniques for treating singular and degenerate parabolic systems have been found. These results have been published (see publications No. 1 and 11). Next, for the more physically relevant case that the viscous coefficients depend on the temperature and degenerate at vacuum, the local well-posedness of strong solutions have been also established for the full Navier-Stokes system with zero-heat-conductivity for a class of initial data containing vacuum only at far fields. It has been shown further that within the life-span of the strong solution, the velocity stays in an inhomogeneous Sobolev space, the entropy remains bounded and smooth, and the total mass, momentum and energy are all conserved in time. These have been achieved by discovering the key underlying structure of the full Navier-Stokes system which are coupled parabolic-hyperbolic systems with strong degeneracy and singularities, but hyperbolic dominant in a new reformulation. These have been published, see publication No. 8. Finally, it is shown that the transversal magnetic fields have strong stabilizing effects on the inviscid interfacial motions. Indeed, it has been established the global (in time) well-posedness of the plasma-vacuum interface motion in a horizontally periodic slab impressed by a uniform transversal resistive magnetic field. This is the first result on the stabilizing effects on interfacial motion of the transversal resistive magnetic field, which is based on our new discovery of the damping structure of plasma vorticity due to the resistive transversal magnetic field. These results have been published, see publication No. 8.

14302819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14302819.value: The studies in this project lead to many new interest and challenging problems to investigate further such as the necessity of the slow decay of the initial density to far field vacuum for local well-posedness; the effects of non-zero heat conductivity in the case of temperature dependent viscous and heat-conductive coefficients degenerating at vacuum; the relationship between bounded (or smooth) entropy and the physical vacuum, and the vacuum dynamics in the presence of both physical boundaries or free boundaries. The ideas and techniques developed in this project should shed light on these interesting problems.

14302819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14302819.value: The theory established in this project yields for the first time of the local or global well-posedness of regular solutions with vacuum at far which possess bounded entropy and velocity field in some suitable inhomogeneous space for the multi-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes systems. This will be of great significance both physically and mathematically. Indeed, since the entropy is one of the fundamental physical states for a viscous compressible fluid, thus these solutions with bounded entropy are physically more preferred than those obtained previously. Furthermore, this theory identifies a class of initial data, in particular, the rate of decay of the initial density at far fields and compatibility conditions for the initial velocity and temperature, so that the corresponding bounded entropy solutions lie in suitable inhomogeneous space, possess bounded total mass and energy. These lead to the resolution of several open problems in this area give several new phenomena.

14303019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303019.value: This project is a continuation of the PI's investigation on how perturbative quantum field theories (QFTs) can be applied to understand mirror symmetry (mainly from the SYZ perspective) and solve other geometric problems. The recent pioneering work of Kevin Costello and his school on a mathematically rigorous formulation of perturbative QFTs gives us a golden opportunity to understand string dualities from a mathematical viewpoint and possibly opens up ways to obtain further and deeper applications in mathematics. One spectacular and highly nontrivial application of Costello’s theory is the joint work by Costello himself and Si Li in which they gave the first mathematically rigorous definition of the higher genus B-model for Calabi-Yau manifolds, building on the famous BCOV theory. Related to this, the foremost goal of this project is to pave the way for developing a higher genus version of SYZ mirror symmetry, or in other words, a quantization of SYZ mirror symmetry. To achieve this, a thorough understanding of the classical field theory, namely, genus 0 SYZ mirror symmetry, is indispensable. We plan to build on our recently obtained knowledge of the classical master equation (or Maurer-Cartan equation) and some preliminary ideas on using BV structures to obtain such an understanding. This in turn leads us to a new local-to-global approach to proving genus 0 mirror symmetry, at the level of isomorphisms between Frobenius manifolds. Such an approach is closely related and supported by the ingenious ideas of Seidel and Kontsevich that, up to deformations, the A-model objects can also be localized and obtained by gluing local models. From here we would like to develop a Dolbeault version of the classical theory which is one possible way to construct the quantization. Another way is to apply the configuration space method of regularization due to Kontsevich and Axelrod-Singer. These two approaches have their own advantages and difficulties which we plan to address in this project. We also plan to explore at least two applications of the techniques to be developed in this project (especially the technique of asymptotic analysis on Maurer-Cartan equations): one is to relate geometric quantization with deformation quantization in the Kähler setting; the other is to gain new understanding of some newly discovered and very important objects called spectral networks. 本項目將繼續PI對如何應用微擾量子場論來理解SYZ鏡對稱的研究。 最近Kevin Costello和他的合作者在數學微擾量子場論的開創性工作為我們提供了一個從數學角度理解弦論對偶的黃金機會，並可能為在數學中獲得更深入的應用開闢了新方向。 Costello理論的一個引人注目且非常重要的應用是Costello本人和李思的工作，他們在著名的BCOV理論的基礎上，給出了卡拉比 - 丘流形的高虧格B模型的第一個數學上嚴格的定義。與此相關，本項目的最重要目標是為SYZ鏡對稱的量子化鋪路。 要做到這一點，徹底了解經典場論，即虧格0 的SYZ鏡對稱，是不可或缺的。我們計劃建立在我們最近獲得的經典主方程（或Maurer-Cartan方程）的知識以及使用BV結構來獲得這種理解的一些初步想法的基礎上。 這反過來引導我們採用新的『局部到整體』方法來證明虧格0 的鏡對稱(作為Frobenius流形之間的同構)。這種方法與Seidel和Kontsevich的巧妙想法密切相關，即在變形之前，A模型也可以通過粘合局部模型獲得。 從這裡開始，我們想要開發經典理論的Dolbeault版本，這是構建量子化的一種可能方式。另一種方法是應用Kontsevich和Axelrod-Singer的正規化配置空間方法。這兩種方法各有其優點和困難，我們計劃在本項目中解決。 我們還計劃探索本項目中要開發的技術的至少兩個應用（尤其是Maurer-Cartan方程的漸近分析技術）：一個是將幾何量子化與Kähler流形的變形量子化聯繫起來; 另一個則是理解一類新發現的非常重要的物體 - 光譜網絡。

14303019.label: Realisation of objectives
14303019.value: The first objective of this project was to develop a local-to-global approach to proving mirror symmetry. In the previous project (RGC Ref No 14302015), the PI and collaborators successfully applied asymptotic analysis to the Maurer-Cartan equation of the Kodaira-Spencer DGLA and proved that consistent scattering diagrams arose from semi-classical limits of the Fourier modes of a specific class of Maurer-Cartan elements in a natural way. Scattering diagrams are tropical combinatorial objects which encode quantum corrections coming from holomorphic disks with boundary on Lagrangian torus fibers. They have played a crucial role in the important works of Kontsevich-Soibelman and Gross-Siebert on the reconstruction problem in mirror symmetry. Our theorem gives the proof of a local version of Fukaya’s conjecture in 2002 which was the main inspiration behind the above works of Kontsevich-Soibelman and Gross-Siebert. We applied the same method to study the extended deformation theory of the Landau-Ginzburg (LG) model mirror to a compact toric surface and proved that semi-classical limits of Fourier modes of a specific class of Maurer-Cartan elements naturally give rise to counting of tropical disks with Maslov indices 0 and 2, the latter of which produces a universal unfolding of the superpotential of the Hori-Vafa LG mirror. In a joint work with Leung and Ma, we worked out an algebraic framework for smoothing singular Calabi-Yau varieties equipped with good local smoothing models. The novel discovery is that our algebraic framework can produce a pre-DGLA, instead of an honest DGLA, which governs the smoothing. Indeed, one cannot get an honest DGLA because there is nontrivial topology change in a smoothing and hence the trivial deformation should not give a Maurer-Cartan solution. Assuming Hodge-to-de Rham degeneracy and freeness of the Hodge bundle, we were able to prove a logarithmic version of the important Bogomolov-Tian-Todorov unobstructedness theorem. This gives a substantial generalization and a unified proof of the previous smoothing results of Friedman, Kawamata-Namikawa, Kontsevich-Soibelman and Gross-Siebert. Combining and applying the techniques developed in the above works, we have very recently proven the global version of Fukaya’s conjecture for any compact Calabi-Yau manifolds which admit toric degenerations. Besides proving Fukaya’s conjecture, our approach is expected to lead to a new local-to-global proof of genus 0 mirror symmetry as an isomorphism between Frobenius manifolds. Such an approach is along the line of thought in Seidel’s program spelled out in his 2002 ICM talk, which suggests that mirror symmetry can be proven by first identifying both sides at the large volume/complex structure limits, and then deforming. On the A-side, Kontsevich conjectured that the Fukaya category of the Weinstein manifold at the large volume limit can be localized to its Lagrangian skeleton; our new work showed that the same is true for the closed-string theory on the mirror B-side. The second objective of this project was to apply Costello’s construction of perturbative QFT to mirror symmetry at higher genera. All the aforementioned works have laid part of the foundation for formulating the Gross-Siebert program, or genus 0 SYZ mirror symmetry, as a classical field theory under Costello’s framework. The next step, which would require completely new techniques and ideas, would be constructing a propagator of the theory. After this, the ultimate goal is to prove that the resulting classical field theory can be quantized and apply the quantization to investigate higher genus mirror symmetry. Log Calabi-Yau surfaces should be a very feasible testing ground for such a quantization approach to higher genus mirror symmetry. In future projects, we plan make use of recent works of Bousseau and his collaborators on higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of log Calabi-Yau surfaces as well as the local-relative correspondence to explore related problems. We hope this can shed new light on higher genus mirror symmetry as a quantization of genus 0 mirror symmetry. The third objective of this project was to explore further geometric applications of asymptotic analysis on Maurer-Cartan equations and perturbative QFTs. In a joint work with Suen and Ma, we initiated the study of the reconstruction problem for higher rank vector bundles over Calabi-Yau manifolds. More precisely, we restrict ourselves to the two-dimensional setting. We introduced the notion of tropical Lagrangian multi-sections over a two-dimensional integral affine manifold with singularities, and used them to study the reconstruction problem for higher rank locally free sheaves over Calabi-Yau surfaces. This study was based on the algebraic framework for smoothing degenerate Calabi-Yau varieties and pairs developed in earlier joint works of the PI with Leung and Ma. We were still able to find some easily checkable combinatorial conditions which can guarantee smoothability of a pair consisting of a locally free sheaf over a maximally degenerate Calabi-Yau surface coming from some tropical Lagrangian multi-sections. Under the same conditions, we believe that these tropical Lagrangian multi-sections should arise as certain “tropical limits” of genuine Lagrangian multi-sections on the mirror side. Also, there should be more concrete correspondence between the geometric properties/structures on the two sides. Recent works of Suen and Oh have addressed some of these problems. In a series of works with Leung and Li, we constructed a new quantization scheme for Kähler manifolds, from which we were able to deduce several new novel relationships among the various known quantization schemes. Our construction, which is geometric in nature, came from modifications and generalizations of Fedosov’s famous construction of deformation quantization on a symplectic manifold. It is also motivated by Costello’s pioneering rigorous construction of perturbative quantum field theories. More precisely, we showed that Fedosov’s construction can be made compatible with the complex structure of a Kähler manifold, yielding a class of very natural Wick-type star products which contain the Berezin-Toeplitz star products as examples. We also generalized Fedosov’s construction to construct sheaves of modules, called Bargmann-Fock sheaves, over the sheaf of Berezin-Toeplitz deformation quantization algebras. This implies that there is indeed an action of deformation quantization on geometric quantization after an appropriate localization (using so-called peak sections), and the action is by local formal Toeplitz operators. At the same time, we discover that the Fedosov connections we obtained are quantizations of Kapranov’s L-infinity structure of a Kähler manifold, and they give rise to BV quantizations which are one-loop exact. These nice features of our construction indicate that it is indeed very natural. We expect that there are many more applications of our construction. Also, it should be related and can be applied to Gukov-Witten’s brane quantization scheme, which is still far from being understood, but is expected to yield applications even in representation theory.

14303019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303019.value: The first major finding in this project is the discovery that a combination of techniques developed in our asymptotic-analytic approach to scattering diagrams and tropical geometry and our algebraic framework for smoothing degenerate Calabi-Yau varieties can lead to a new local-to-global proof of genus 0 mirror symmetry. Although such an approach has been anticipated by Seidel and Kontsevich in their earlies works, it is still highly nontrivial to work out the detailed picture. Works done in this project made this possible, and we are now closer than ever to realizing mirror symmetry as a T-duality via the SYZ conjecture. The second major finding is the incorporation of the algebraic framework for smoothing degenerate Calabi-Yau varieties developed earlier by the PI with Leung and Ma with the geometry of SYZ transforms. In this project, we showed how such a framework can be applied to construct smoothable locally free sheaves over maximally degenerate Calabi-Yau surfaces from tropical Lagrangian multi-sections over two-dimensional integral affine manifolds with singularities. The latter has also recently been shown to arise as tropical limits of genuine Lagrangian multi-sections on the mirror side. A very important message is that now we can establish geometric correspondences in mirror symmetry even when SYZ fibrations admit singular fibers. The third major finding is a new novel quantization scheme for Kähler manifolds. This came from delicate modifications and generalizations of Fedosov’s famous construction of deformation quantization on a symplectic manifold. The key is to make the constructions compatible with the complex structure of a Kähler manifold. This turns out to a class of very natural Wick-type star products which enjoy very nice properties. Applications we obtained so far include new relations among various known quantization schemes as well as a relation to Kapranov’s famous L-infinity structures which were originally motivated by Rozansky-Witten theory. We expect to see a lot more new applications in the near future.

14303019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303019.value: This project has led to many future research directions. We would first like to further investigate the relation between mirror symmetry and quantization. Recently, the PI and his collaborators discovered new applications of the mirror symmetry framework and quantization framework developed in this project. We wish to study these applications in details in future projects. Another direction is to continue our study of the smoothing problem for degenerate pairs. One question is the relation between our smoothing criterion and spectral networks, in particular in the two-dimensional case. Such an investigation is expected to yield further relations between mirror symmetry, Hitchin systems, D-module theory and even holomorphic Floer theory. On the other hand, the PI also plans to use log Calabi-Yau surfaces (and perhaps higher dimensional examples) as a testing ground for studying higher genus mirror symmetry as a quantization of genus 0 mirror symmetry. We will make full use of recent works of Bousseau and his collaborators on higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants of log Calabi-Yau surfaces as well as the local-relative correspondence.

14303019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303019.value: Mirror symmetry is a highly nontrivial and mysterious duality between the symplectic geometry of a space and the complex geometry of a completely different space. It was discovered by string theorists in the early 1990s. It has led to numerous surprising and deep mathematical conjectures. Since its discovery, mathematicians have been working very hard to try to understand the mechanism of mirror symmetry. A breakthrough came in 1996 when Strominger, Yau and Zaslow proposed that mirror symmetry should be understood as a geometric Fourier-type transform. Lying at the heart of the SYZ conjecture is the role played by quantum corrections, which is the key to explain the miraculous power of mirror symmetry. This research project studied mirror symmetry using techniques from quantum field theory. Outstanding results include a new framework for smoothing Calabi-Yau varieties and a new local-to-global approach to genus 0 mirror symmetry. These have deepened our understanding of the geometry of mirror symmetry. We have also demonstrated how our new techniques can be applied to other problems in mirror symmetry and quantization.

14303119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303119.value: The aim of this project is to map thermokarst landforms on the Tibetan Plateau by applying deep-learning algorithms to high-resolution satellite imagery. Permafrost occurs over large areas on the Tibetan Plateau and has been undergoing strong warming in recent decades. Thawing of ice-rich permafrost causes abrupt degradation, forming thermokarst landforms which strongly affect local ecosystem, hydrology, permafrost carbon decay, and infrastructure stability. However, thermokarst landforms on the Tibetan Plateau are not being mapped systematically or comprehensively. A lack of knowledge of their location and spatial extent limits our understanding of permafrost degradation and the associated impacts. We propose the DeepThaw project that will develop a novel, deep-learning-based mapping method and apply it to high-resolution images acquired by the Planet CubeSat constellation to automatically map thermokarst landforms on the Tibetan Plateau. In particular, we will focus on two types of non-lake thermokarst landforms, i.e., retrogressive thaw slumps and active layer detachments, along the disturbance-prone Qinghai-Tibet engineering corridor. We will obtain a comprehensive inventory of these thermokarst landforms and subsequently conduct a statistic analysis of their spatial distribution and assess the controlling topo-climatic factors. We will also quantify their temporal changes from multi-temporal images taken by the Planet CubeSat constellation from 2017 to 2021, supplemented by the Landsat spectral trends from 1999 to 2014. This study will fill the gap between local and regional studies of non-lake thermokarst landforms on the Tibetan Plateau. The results will provide a regional distribution of thermokarst landforms, and thereby advance the understanding of permafrost degradation on the Tibetan Plateau. The method developed, including the trained deep-learning network, will provide the first step to assess permafrost stability on the entire Tibetan Plateau. 本項目的總體目標是使用深度學習技術從高空間分辨率遙感影像上自動提取位於青藏高原的熱喀斯特地貌。 多年凍土廣泛分布於青藏高原，並且近幾十年來呈現變暖的趨勢。富冰多年凍土消融可能會導致其急劇退化，形成熱喀斯特地貌，進而影響當地的生態、水文、碳循環、以及威脅基礎設施的安全。 然後目前針對青藏高原熱喀斯特地貌，系統且全面性的研究十分缺乏，也限制了人們對多年凍土退化以及相關影響的認識。 本項目將創新性地提出一種基於深度學習的熱喀斯特地貌提取方法。以青藏高原工程走廊為研究區域，使用Planet微衛星高分辨率影像，自動提取兩種典型的非湖泊類型熱喀斯特地貌，即後退型熱融滑塌和活動層邊坡坍塌。在自動提取的基礎上，獲取研究區域內這些地貌的空間分布以及詳細的統計信息，同時評估地形氣候因子對這些地貌形成的影響。本項目還會以2017到2021年Planet影像為主要數據，1999年至2014年的Landsat數據為輔助定量地調查這些地貌的時間變化。 本項目將會填補了青藏高原上非湖泊類型熱喀斯特地貌區域性研究的空白。項目完成後，將會提供熱喀斯特地貌空間分布數據，進而促進對青藏高原多年凍土退化的認識。對深度學習技術的應用研究，包括相應的神經網絡結構、參數，以及在此基礎上形成的自動提取算法，將會為調查整個青藏高原多年凍土的穩定性提供基礎。

14303119.label: Realisation of objectives
14303119.value: I have completed all the proposed research tasks and realized all the objectives. "Objective 1: To develop a deep-learning-based method for mapping thermokarst landforms from Planet CubeSat images" We have developed five innovative methods for mapping retrogressive thaw slumps from optical imagery. (1) The first is a deep-learning-based method for automatically delineating thaw slump boundaries. This method builds on a semantic segmentation model called DeepLabv3+ and uses training data carefully obtained for the thermokarst landforms in the Beiluhe region in central Tibet. (2) The second method uses an object detection algorithm called YOLO to detect retrogressive thaw slumps. Trained iteratively using the accumulated labels from Beiluhe and other regions, this method enables fast detections and has been applied to very large permafrost regions. (3) The third method integrates deep learning, change detection, and medial axis transform for automatically quantifying the temporal changes and development of thaw slumps on multi-temporal images. (4) The fourth is a change detection algorithm based on the Siamese neural network, aiming to automatically detect temporal changes of thaw slumps from multi-temporal images. (5) The fifth uses deep-learning-based heatmap regression for estimating thaw slump areas from moderate-resolution images. Through multiple case-studies, we have proven that these deep learning methods are reliable, robust, and transferable in mapping thermokarst and other landforms such as rock glaciers and glacial fronts in various settings and large regions. "Objective 2: To obtain the spatial distribution of retrogressive thaw slumps and active layer detachments along the Qinghai-Tibet engineering corridor" We have applied our developed deep learning methods to high-resolution PlanetScope CubeSat images, firstly to the engineering corridor area (~54,000 km2) and then to the entire permafrost region on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1 million km2). We have compiled an inventory of thaw slumps for the engineering corridor area with the reference year of 2019. We have also compiled annualized inventories of thaw slumps over the entire Plateau from 2016 to 2022. Based on these inventories, we conducted detailed documentation and analysis on their spatial distribution, geomorphic and geometric attributes, as well as climatic, topographic, and vegetation settings. "Objective 3: To quantify the temporal variations of the mapped thermokarst landforms from multi-temporal images" Applying our developed deep learning methods to multi-temporal images taken by PlanetScope CubeSat from 2016 to 2022, we have quantified the areal change, headwall retreating rate and direction, and initialization years of each inventoried thaw slump. We have also investigated the environmental factors behind the observed thaw slump activities, revealed high summer temperature and strong precipitation as triggering factors, and evaluated the possible impacts of thaw slump activities to infrastructure, water and ecosystem carbon.

14303119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303119.value: The project has produced six journal papers, four associated datasets, two software packages, and two conference papers. Please refer to Part C for detailed citation information and the full papers. Below I summarize our major findings as reported in the three retrogressive thaw slump papers. Huang et al. (2021) proposed a method that integrates deep learning, change detection, and medial axis transform, aiming to automatically quantify the thaw slump development on multi-temporal images in the Beiluhe region. Our method reveals that among 342 thaw slumps in Beiluhe, 83% and 76% of them expanded from 2017 to 2018 and 2018 to 2019, respectively. Within one year from 2018 to 2019, the average and maximum expanding areas were 0.22 ha and 1.47 ha, while the average and maximum retreat distances were 25 m and 212 m. This study provided the very first quantitative report on thaw slump development on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Codes are available on GitHub (https://github.com/yghlc/ChangeDet_DL). Xia et al. (2022) presented the first inventory of retrogressive thaw slumps along the Qinghai-Tibet Engineering Corridor, compiled using deep learning methods. The inventory includes 875 thaw slumps, of which 474 are clustered in the Beiluhe region, and 38 are near roads or railway lines. Through statistical analysis, we found that (1) the thaw slumps tend to develop on north-facing and gentle slopes and tend to appear at medium elevations or areas receiving less solar radiation; (2) a large portion of the thaw slumps are located on the ground covered with alpine meadows and by loam soil. The dataset is publicly accessible at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6397029, with the Chinese version at https://doi.org/10.11888/Cryos.tpdc.272672. Xia et al. (2024) created a spatially comprehensive thaw slump inventory with annual intervals across the entire Qinghai-Tibet Plateau from 2016 to 2022. We found significantly enhanced thaw slump activities during these seven years: their number increased by 1.4 times from 1592 to 3805, and their total area increased by 2.8 times from 1714 ha to 6507 ha. We also revealed that thaw slumps tend to be clustered and show distinct spatial and temporal heterogeneity characterized by (1) various responses towards high temperatures and precipitation and (2) different inclinations on topography and vegetation types. It is the first annual inventory of thermokarst landforms in cold regions.

14303119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303119.value: 1. Method improvement: More advanced deep learning methods such as transformers-based neural networks are expected to outperform our exiting methods built on DeepLabv3+. Together with much more training labels accumulated in the past few years and over many permafrost regions, deep learning still bears great potentials of automating the detection and delineation of various thermokarst landforms with better accuracy and efficiency. 2. Integration with multi-sensor remote sensing, field observations, and models: Optical remote sensing, as advanced through this work, can be combined with radar (interferometric synthetic aperture radar, in particular) and aerial photogrammetry towards four-dimensional quantifications of thermokarst landform evolution, expressed as area and volumetric changes over one decade or longer. These can be further combined with field observations, physics-based and statistical models to gain a better understanding of thermokarst processes. 3. Assessing and projecting socio-economic impacts: Our thermokarst inventories and observed changes serve as fundamental datasets to identify permafrost areas that are susceptible to abrupt thaw, to evaluate carbon emissions from these landforms and the threats posed to nearby infrastructure, and to inform policymakers on future mitigations to climate impacts resulting from mountain permafrost degradation.

14303119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303119.value: Permafrost on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, characterized by shallow thickness and relatively high temperature, is sensitive to climate warming and human disturbances and is undergoing accelerating degradation. As a consequence of the abrupt permafrost thaw, thermokarst landforms are widely distributed on the plateau, but their spatial distribution or temporal evolution has not been quantitatively studied. This project develops deep-learning-based methods to automatedly map retrogressive thaw slumps from high-resolution satellite images. We compiled thaw slump inventories and quantified their changes from 2016 and 2022 over the entire plateau. Our results reveal enhanced thaw slump activities as indicated by 1.4 times increase in number and 2.8 times area enlargement. The new knowledge obtained through this project as a crucial step toward evaluating how abrupt permafrost degradation is accelerated by climate change and can serve the policymakers and stakeholders to pursue sustainable socio-economic development on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.

14303219.label: Project Objectives
14303219.value: Specific Aim 1: Characterization of PML entrapped in Cry3Aa* crystals. We plan to characterize the temperature stability, solvent tolerance, and recyclability of a new genetically-encoded biodiesel catalyst generated by the in vivo entrapment of Proteus mirabilis lipase (PML) within Cry3Aa crystals. We will also work to cocrystallize of Cry3Aa and PML in vitro, with the hope that we can get suitable crystals for an X-ray crystallographic analysis. The hope is that an in vitro structure of PML bound within Cry3Aa crystals will provide insights into their mode of interaction. Specific Aim 2: Improving the activity of PML entrapped in Cry3Aa* crystals. We will perform directed evolution studies of PML entrapped in Cry3Aa crystals by introducing random mutations in both the pml and cry3Aa genes and then selecting for crystals with increased stability and activity. Our hypothesis is that in addition to identifying mutations in PML that enhance PML activity, we will also find Cry3Aa mutations of residues that line the channels of the Cry3Aa crystal. If successful, this would illustrate a novel feature of our system - the ability to evolve both the framework as well as the enzyme itself to impact function.

14303219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303219.value: Cry3Aa is one member of a family of protein toxins that naturally form crystals when expressed in the bacteria Bacillus thuringiensis. Previously, we discovered that when a reporter gene is fused to the C-terminus of Cry3Aa, expression of the resulting Cry3Aa-reporter fusion protein still forms crystals in the bacteria. We subsequently showed that this Cry3Aa-fusion platform can be employed to produce a genetically-encoded immobilized lipase in B. thuringiensis that can be isolated in a single centrifugation step, and directly used for the conversion of coconut oil to biodiesel over multiple reaction cycles. This demonstration was significant, since it was the first reported example of a genetically-encoded immobilized biocatalyst with both high activity and recyclability. The current proposal seeks to build on this work by generating improved Cry3Aa-lipase catalysts with enhanced reactivity towards waste cooking oils. This will involve exploring the use of other lipase enzymes, as well as utilizing directed evolution approaches to identify lipase mutants with enhanced catalytic efficiency and stability. We will also investigate the ability of the Cry3Aa-fusion platform to immobilize other relevant enzymes. 14303219.label: Realisation of objectives
14303219.value: Specific Aim 1 was fully realized and a paper on this work was published in JACS. We demonstrated the successful production of Cry3Aa crystals containing entrapped PML molecules, and performed the characterization of its temperature stability, catalytic properties, and recyclability. We also prepared in vitro crystals grown from a solution of Cry3Aa and dye-tagged PML and demonstrated that the resulting Cry3Aa crystals contained entrapped PML based on the color. While the resulting crystals retained the structure of the Cry3Aa framework, density for the PML molecules could not be observed in the X-ray structure presumably because their position is disordered within the channels. Specific Aim 2 was also completed, though we were unable to identify significantly improved mutants of PML entrapped within Cry3Aa crystals by directed evolution. Since we had shown that more negatively charged Cry3Aa mutant (Neg3Aa) crystals binds more PML, we also tested the activity of Neg3Aa[PML] crystals, but found that the overall activity was reduced - presumably because the higher loading of PML resulted in poorer accessibility of the triacylglycerol substrate to the PML enzyme sites within the crystal.

We plan to characterize the temperature stability, solvent tolerance, and recyclability of a new genetically-encoded biodiesel catalyst generated by the in vivo entrapment of Proteus mirabilis lipase (PML) within Cry3Aa crystals. We will also work to cocrystallize of Cry3Aa and PML in vitro, with the hope that we can get suitable crystals for an X-ray crystallographic analysis. The hope is that an in vitro structure of PML bound within Cry3Aa crystals will provide insights into their mode of interaction.

Specific Aim 2: Improving the activity of PML entrapped in Cry3Aa* crystals. We will perform directed evolution studies of PML entrapped in Cry3Aa crystals by introducing random mutations in both the pml and cry3Aa genes and then selecting for crystals with increased stability and activity. Our hypothesis is that in addition to identifying mutations in PML that enhance PML activity, we will also find Cry3Aa mutations of residues that line the channels of the Cry3Aa crystal. If successful, this would illustrate a novel feature of our system - the ability to evolve both the framework as well as the enzyme itself to impact function.

14303219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303219.value: The major demonstration of this project was the ability to entrap the Proteus mirabilis lipase (PML) within in vivo generated Cry3Aa crystals by coexpression of PML and Cry3Aa within the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis. This provided a new approach to produce in vivo immobilized enzymes that was distinct from other known approaches. The entrapped PML showed improved thermostability, and could be used for the recyclable conversion of waste cooking oil to FAME biodiesel. This work was published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society. Towards the development of a general strategy to co-immobilize multiple enzymes on Cry3Aa crystals, we produced crystals of a fusion of Cry3Aa to SpyCatcher, a domain that can catalyze its coupling to a SpyTag sequence. Reaction of the Cry3Aa-SpyCatcher crystals with a set of enzyme-SpyTag fusion allows for the co-immobilize of this set of enzymes onto and within the crystal. We demonstrate that the resulting co-immobilized enzyme Cry3Aa-SpyCatcher crystals exhibit good activity, and can be used for multiple reaction cycles. This work was published in the journal Bioconjugate Chemistry.

14303219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303219.value: There are several different directions that can be taken for the further development of this project. For practical use as a catalyst, it will be important to optimize the catalytic activity and enhance the overall stability of the crystal, as well as work out the scale up of the catalyst production and the waste cooking oil to FAME biodiesel reaction. Another direction to explore could be the coupling of the biodiesel reaction with other enzyme processes to maximize the value added and extend this methodology to the production of higher value commodity chemicals.

14303219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303219.value: Normally in order to produce an enzyme catalyst, one needs to produce the target enzyme in cells, purify it, and then immobilize it on a support so that it can be used for multiple reaction cycles. In this study, we demonstrate a new way to immobilize enzymes directly as they are being generated within the cell, greatly simplifying the production process. Our technology is based on the ability of a protein called Cry3Aa to form crystals directly in the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis. The crystals formed from Cry3A a protein have large pores that target proteins can fit into and get trapped. Here we show that when the Cry3Aa crystals are formed in the presence of a target enzyme Proteus mirabilis lipase (PML), PML gets trapped in the crystals in an active form. The resulting PML-entrapped Cry3Aa crystals could be used as a recyclable catalyst for the conversion of waste cooking oil to FAME biodiesel - a biofuel that can be used to power diesel trucks.
