14303519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303519.value: This project aims to understand the growth mechanism of an organic photovoltaic active layer from a precursor solution to a thin film. Our goal is to establish the structural correlation between solution and film, which will in turn guide the development of feasible methods to achieve favorable three-dimensional film morphology for high-efficiency organic solar cells. The bulk morphology of an organic photovoltaic active layer, in terms of molecular packing and nanophase separation, is known to be crucial to solar cell device performance. However, the importance of solution morphology is often overlooked. Most treatments on solution thus far have been empirical and oriented by the resultant film morphology. In fact, how organic molecules disperse and aggregate in the solution is the starting point of film growth, thereby directly influencing the film morphology. Furthermore, the layered device structure breaks the symmetry into the in-plane and out-of-plane directions with respect to the substrate, leading to intrinsic anisotropy in morphology. However, the characterization of out-of-plane nanophase separation remains technically challenging. Therefore, in this proposal, we intend to investigate two key aspects of morphology: “solution” and “three-dimensional film”. Various X-ray scattering methods will be employed and developed. The solution morphology will be characterized by small-angle X-ray scattering in the transmission mode (SAXS). In contrast, the three-dimensional film morphology will be measured by X-ray scattering in the grazing incidence mode. The probing length scale can be tuned with the sample-to-detector distance to collect wide-angle scattering for molecular level information and small-angle scattering for nanoscale information. Particular effort will be devoted to applying an alternative new method to probe the out-of-plane nanomorphology: grazing-incident transmission small-angle X-ray scattering (GTSAXS), which exploits a unique experimental geometry that eliminates data distortion. Our preliminary data have confirmed the temperature sensitivity on solution morphology. The effects of additives, solvents, material concentrations, processing conditions, and other factors will be carefully studied. In addition, we carried out preliminary GTSAXS measurements at BL19U2, the Shanghai Synchrotron Radiation Facility. The results have demonstrated the capability of acquiring three-dimensional nanomorphology via this new technique. The successful execution of this project will allow a thorough comprehension of the organic photovoltaic film formation mechanism, which will provide rationales for developing efficient morphology tuning methods from the solution stage. 該項目旨在理解有機光伏活性層從前驅體溶液到薄膜的生長機理。我們的目標是建立溶液和薄膜之間的結構相關性，指導發展可行的方法來調控薄膜的三維形貌，以實現高效有機太陽能電池。 有機光伏活性層的體異質結的形貌，例如分子堆積和納米尺度相分離，對於太陽能電池器件性能是至關重要的。然而，前驅體溶液的形貌的重要性經常被忽視。到目前為止，大多數溶液處理手段都是經驗性的，取決於所得到的薄膜形貌。事實上，有機分子如何在溶液中分散和聚集是薄膜生長的起點，從而直接影響薄膜形貌。此外，層狀薄膜的器件結構將各向同性的形貌改變為相對於襯底的面內和面外方向的形貌的各向異性。然而，表徵面外納米尺度相分離在技術上仍具有挑戰性。 因此，在本項目中，我們打算研究形貌的兩個關鍵方面：“溶液”和“三維薄膜”。各種X射線散射方法將被採用和開發。溶液形貌將通過透射模式的小角X射線散射（SAXS）來表徵。相反，三維薄膜形貌將通過掠入射模式的X射線散射來測量。探測長度尺度可以通過樣品到探測器距離進行調整，以收集分子水平信息的廣角散射信號和納米級信息的小角散射信號。我們將致力於應用新方法來探測面外方向的納米尺度形貌：掠入射透射小角X射線散射（GTSAXS），利用它獨特的實驗方法來消除數據失真。 我們的初步數據已經證實了溶液形貌具有溫度敏感性。我們將仔細研究添加劑，溶劑，材料濃度，加工條件和其他因素的影響。此外，我們在上海同步輻射裝置BL19U2進行了初步的GTSAXS測量。結果證明了通過這種新技術可以獲得三維納米尺度相分離的薄膜形貌信息。 該項目的成功實施將有助於從根本上理解有機光伏薄膜形成機制，將為從溶液階段開發有效的形貌調控方法提供理論依據。

14303519.label: Realisation of objectives
14303519.value: To study the solution morphology of active layers, we conducted small angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) measurements and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for the precursor solutions under various conditions (objective 1). The solution morphology of PBDB-T and ITIC in chlorobenzene solvent was investigated with SAXS, revealing that the sizes of aggregates in solution changed with storage time and temperature. In-depth interaction mechanisms between common solvent additives and state-of-the-art Y6-series nonfullerene acceptors (NFAs) in the solution state were successfully revealed, indicating the presence of π-π interactions between naphthalene derivatives and IC terminals of Y6 analogues, contributing to improved long-range ordering (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2023, 11, 21895-21907). Furthermore, the terminal-symmetry of Y6-series NFAs was found to play a critical role in their interactions with conjugated solvent additives. Unlike terminal-symmetric NFAs, terminal-asymmetric NFAs showed remarkable insensitivity to various additives (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2023, 11, 21895-21907). To interpret the three-dimensional (3D) molecular packing structures of organic photovoltaic (OPV) materials (objective 2), we systematically measured thin film GIWAXS for Y6 and its analogues processed under various conditions with the aid of MD simulations. The study found that thermal annealing at high temperatures (over 200 ℃) enhanced crystal growth and reorientation of Y6 in thin films, resulting in square and rectangular lattices for pure and blend films, respectively (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2021, 9, 17030-17038). Incorporating CN additive enabled the revelation of the crystalline packing structure of Y6 in device active layers for the first time (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2023, 11, 21895-21907). Terminal-asymmetric NFAs exhibited insensitivity to solvent additives and robust crystalline packing structures even under high temperatures (250 ℃), characterized by TT packing motifs consisting of hetero-terminals. To acquire both in-plane (IP) and out-of-plane (OOP) nanomorphology of OPV bulk heterojunction (BHJ) (objective 3), we developed the formalism of grazing-incidence transmission small-angle X-ray scattering (GTSAXS) within the framework of Born Approximation. The 3D phase separation structures of typical OPV BHJ systems (P3HT:PC71BM, PBDB-T:ITIC, PM6:Y6) were determined successfully for the first time (Nature Communications, 2021, 12: 6226-6235). The study found that OOP domain sizes were much smaller than IP domain sizes for P3HT:PC71BM and PBDB-T:ITIC blend films, whereas PM6:Y6 system showed similar OOP and IP domain sizes. Additionally, 3D domain sizes of NFAs-based systems tended to shrink with additive incorporation and expand after thermal annealing. In light of GIWAXS crystal analysis results, GTSAXS characterizations, and theoretical calculations (objective 4), an in-depth understanding of the correlation between solution morphology, film morphology at molecular and nanometer scales, and device performances was obtained. π-π interactions between naphthalene additives and IC terminals of Y6 analogues were identified as crucial for long-range ordering in BHJ films, contributing to improved Voc, Jsc, and FF of corresponding devices (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2023, 11, 21895-21907). Terminal-asymmetric NFAs exhibited excellent additive-insensitive and thermally stable crystalline structures, contributing to additive-free devices with high PCE of 18.4% and excellent intrinsic stability. The impact of vertical morphology tuning on the open-circuit voltage of OPV devices was demonstrated, achieving an impressive Voc of 0.922 V with a PCE of 18.7% (Advanced Science, 2022, 9, 2200578). Throughout the project, the understanding of morphology was applied to achieve high-performance all-small molecule systems (Adv. Func. Mater. 2023, 33, 2303307), and collaborations with several research groups in the field of OPV were established (i.e., Adv. Mater. 2020, 32, 2001160; Adv. Mater. 2020, 32, 2001621; Adv. Mater. 2021, 33, 2007231).

14303519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303519.value: Throughout this project, we've published 10 articles in respected journals and shared our findings at four local and international conferences. Our collective results offer valuable insights into the intricate relationships between the chemical structure, physical morphology, and device performance of organic photovoltaic materials. This knowledge contributes to the on-going quest for high-efficiency and stable organic solar cells. Major Finding 1: We introduced the use of GTSAXS on OPV BHJ systems (P3HT:PC71BM, PBDB-T:ITIC, and PM6:Y6) for the first time. This groundbreaking technique revealed a strong link between the 3D nanomorphology, particularly the out-of-plane (OOP) domain sizes, and the performance of organic solar cells. This discovery opens up a fresh perspective on understanding the phase morphology of BHJ, offering a promising avenue for future device optimization. Major Finding 2: By studying Y6 in thin films after thermal annealing at high temperatures, we uncovered the crystallization enhancement and reorientation effect. This finding provides a direct and straightforward method, using GIWAXS, to explore the crystalline structure of Y6 in thin films, advancing our understanding of its characteristics. Major Finding 3: For the first time, we revealed the intrinsic crystalline structure of Y6 in its device active layer. The CN additive was identified as a key player in the formation of crystalline Y6. This discovery sheds light on the crystalline structure of Y6 in the active layer of organic solar cells and its crystallization mechanism in the presence of solvent additives. Major Finding 4: Through our work, we achieved significant improvements in vertical morphology, resulting in enhanced crystalline packing and reduced phase separation domain sizes. This optimization led to an impressive efficiency of 18.7%, featuring the highest-reported open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.922 V among organic solar cells with efficiencies over 17%.

14303519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303519.value: 1. Designing and synthesis of new materials based on the relationships between chemical structure and physical morphology that we have revealed. Novel photovoltaic materials with ideal BHJ morphology will enable optimized device performance. 2. Interpreting the basic optoelectronic properties of Y-series NFAs for novel device applications. The characteristic aggregation structure of newly-emerged Y-series NFAs has a direct impact on their photo-physical process, therefore allowing potential application for other optoelectronic devices.

14303519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303519.value: Organic solar cells, with efficiency nearing 20%, hold great promise for future clean energy solutions. Attaining exceptional efficiency relies on innovative materials and optimal bulk heterojunction (BHJ) morphology. This project employs advanced X-ray scattering techniques to explore the intrinsic physical morphology of cutting-edge OPV BHJ systems under diverse treatments. It reveals the intrinsic crystalline structure of Y6 in the device's active layer and its crystallization mechanism with solvent additives. The study highlights the crucial role of non-fullerene acceptor (NFA) molecular symmetry in crystalline packing and device characteristics, while also investigating the 3D phase structure at the nanoscale for typical OPV BHJ blends. These findings provide valuable guidelines for understanding and manipulating BHJ morphology, essential for the development of high-efficiency and enduringly stable organic solar cells.

14303619.label: Project Objectives
14303619.value: To synthesize and characterize ß-galactosidase activatable BODIPY photosensitizer. The photophysical properties and the enzymatic activation of the novel compound will be characterized by extensive solution studies. To develop cancer-targeting cyclic peptide-ß-galactosidase conjugates. The linear peptides will be cyclized and conjugated onto the ß-galactosidase via the novel one-pot peptide cyclization-bioconjugation reaction. The novel cyclic-peptide-ß-galactosidase will be extensively characterized by RP-HPLC, MALDI-TOF, and SDS-PAGE. 14303619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303619.value: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has emerged as an alternative anti-cancer treatment. It has been welcomed by the general public because of the straightforward and non-invasive procedure that can be done on an outpatient basis. Selective killing of tumor cells without affecting others is one of the major challenges in PDT. Non-specific administration of photosensitizer causes undesired phototoxicity and lowering of the effective dose. Installation of tumor targeting groups against overexpressed receptor or proteins as well as designing tumor microenvironment-specific activatable photosensitizers have been explored. Nevertheless, the similarity between tumor and healthy tissue has lowered the tumor targeting specificity and photosensitizer activation, which result in the high background to tumor ratio and low therapeutic index. In this proposal, a novel approach called extrinsic enzyme activation strategy will be explored to address the former challenges. This strategy involves the development of two components including the tumor targeting extrinsic enzyme and the corresponding enzyme activatable photosensitizer. We envisage the sequential administration of the two components will result in more precise activation of photosensitizers and tumor targeting effect. Here, ß-galactosidase will be used as the extrinsic enzyme that does not normally appear in healthy tissue and circulation; and a quenched galactose-BODIPY photosensitizer that only can be activated by the ß-galactosidase. To offer tumor targeting ability to the ß-galactosidase, tumor targeting cyclic peptide will be conjugated to the enzyme surface. Cyclic peptides combine a number of favorable properties including enhanced binding affinity, target selectivity and low toxicity that make cyclic peptide an attractive modality for the development of therapeutics. However, conventional methods to cyclize and conjugate the peptide on protein remain a challenging and tedious. Thus, we will be developing a novel efficient one-pot peptide cyclization-bioconjugation reaction by designing bifunctional linker for this purpose. The bifunctional linker contains a dibromo methylbenzene (DBMB) and a phthalaldehyde linked by a linear chain of PEG. The DBMB will be used to cyclize peptides that contains two cysteines, while the phthalaldehyde will react with amino groups of protein spontaneously via our recent developed phthalaldehyde-amine capture reaction. The PEG could extend the serum stability, enhance the targeting effect, increase the molecular size, and lowering immunogenicity. With the two components in hand, the orthogonal pair of ß-galactosidase conjugate and ß-galactose-BODIPY will be characterized by solution studies, in vitro, and in vivo experiments to accomplish the advanced targeted, activatable PDT that goes beyond the state-of-the-art. 光動力療法（PDT）已成為另一種新抗癌治療方法。 因為它可以在門診病人的基礎上進行直接和非侵入性的手術，所以受到了公眾的歡迎。 選擇性殺死腫瘤細胞而不影響其他細胞是PDT的主要挑戰之一。 光敏劑的非特異性給藥導致不希望的光毒性和有效劑量的降低。在該提案中，將探索一種稱為「外源酶激活策略」的新方法來解決前面的挑戰。該策略涉及兩種組分，包括腫瘤靶向外源酶和可被相應的酶活化的光敏劑，導致更精確的光敏劑活化和腫瘤靶向作用。

14303619.label: Realisation of objectives
14303619.value: To fulfill the stated objectives and add the dimension of in vivo validation to our work, we engaged in a comprehensive research and development process. Here’s an overview of how these objectives were addressed: 1. **Synthesis and Characterization of β-Galactosidase Activatable BODIPY Photosensitizer:** We synthesized a novel BODIPY-based photosensitizer specifically designed to be activated by β-galactosidase. This design enables the photosensitizer to remain non-toxic in its dormant state and become activated in the presence of the enzyme, which is more prevalent in cancerous tissues. Through extensive solution studies, including absorption and fluorescence spectroscopy, we characterized the photophysical properties of the compound. The enzymatic activation mechanism was thoroughly investigated, demonstrating a clear response to β-galactosidase. 2. **Development of Cancer-Targeting Cyclic Peptide-β-Galactosidase Conjugates:** Utilizing a novel one-pot peptide cyclization-bioconjugation reaction, we developed cyclic peptide conjugates of β-galactosidase. This approach allowed us to target the enzyme specifically to cancer cells. Extensive characterization of these conjugates was performed using Reverse Phase High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC), Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionization Time of Flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry, and Sodium Dodecyl Sulfate Polyacrylamide Gel Electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE). Solution studies confirmed the retained activity of β-galactosidase, and optimization experiments focused on peptide loading and linker characteristics improved targeting efficiency. 3. **In Vitro Tumor Targeting and Activity Assessment:** We conducted in vitro studies to evaluate the tumor-targeting capabilities of our system and the cellular-level activity of β-galactosidase. The Photodynamic Therapy (PDT) efficacy was quantitatively measured using the MTT assay, demonstrating significant cytotoxicity in cancer cells while sparing healthy cells. This specificity is attributed to the enzymatic activation of the photosensitizer and the targeted delivery of the enzyme. **In Vivo Experimental Validation:** Beyond in vitro assessments, we extended our research to in vivo studies to confirm the efficacy and safety of our design in a living organism. These experiments involved the application of our cyclic peptide-β-galactosidase conjugates and BODIPY photosensitizer in animal models bearing tumors. Monitoring the progression and response of tumors to our treatment provided valuable insights into the potential of our approach for clinical application. The in vivo results reinforced the targeting precision, therapeutic efficacy, and minimized side effects, showcasing the practical applicability of our design in cancer treatment. This comprehensive approach not only met the outlined objectives but also established a robust foundation for future clinical applications, potentially offering a more effective and safer alternative for cancer photodynamic therapy. Details can be found in our published article in JACS, 2022, 144, 10647. Building upon our research, we delve further into a sophisticated strategy for delivering bioactive proteins into target cells, guided by acid-responsive mechanisms for precise control. This innovative approach focuses on enhancing the selectivity and efficacy of therapeutic proteins by employing a cell-penetrating peptide (CPP) that is activated in the acidic environment typical of tumor sites. This method ensures that the therapeutic payload is released specifically within the tumor cells, minimizing effects on healthy tissues and maximizing therapeutic outcomes. For a deeper understanding of the methodology and findings related to acid-responsive protein delivery systems, the details are extensively discussed in the study available at Pharmaceutics, 2024, 16, 71. This research underscores the potential of utilizing environmental triggers, such as pH differences, to refine targeted therapy approaches, thereby offering a promising avenue for the development of next-generation cancer treatments.

14303619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303619.value: The key findings and outcomes of this research are: 1. Development of a novel bioconjugation strategy for enzyme modification and selective delivery into cancer cells. The researchers used a bifunctional linker to induce cyclization of a peptide sequence (Ac-NH-CRGDfC-CONH2) and couple it with β-galactosidase (β-Gal) via a phthalaldehyde-amine capture reaction. This enabled the facile preparation of cyclic RGD-modified β-Gal (cRGD-β-Gal) that could be selectively internalized into cancer cells overexpressing αvβ3 integrin. 2. Design of an extrinsic enzyme-activated photosensitizing system. The researchers conjugated a distyryl boron dipyrromethene (DSBDP)-based photosensitizer with a galactose moiety through a self-immolative linker (gal-DSBDP). This deactivated photosensitizer could be specifically cleaved and activated by the extrinsic cRGD-β-Gal enzyme selectively delivered into cancer cells, restoring its fluorescence and ROS generation capabilities. 3. Demonstration of high specificity and efficacy of the extrinsic enzyme-activated photosensitizing system. The activation of gal-DSBDP was found to be highly selective towards β-Gal, with no response to other common interfering species. In cancer cells overexpressing αvβ3 integrin, pre-incubation with cRGD-β-Gal led to significantly higher intracellular fluorescence and ROS production upon light irradiation compared to using the native β-Gal. 4. In vivo validation of the extrinsic enzyme-activated photodynamic therapy. Using nude mice bearing αvβ3 integrin-positive U87-MG tumors, the researchers demonstrated that the specific activation of gal-DSBDP by cRGD-β-Gal at the tumor site resulted in complete eradication of the tumor upon laser irradiation, while using native β-Gal showed largely reduced effects. In contrast to conventional activation using intrinsic enzymes, this extrinsic enzyme-activatable approach can further minimize nonspecific activation, leading to more precisive photodynamic therapy. The ability to selectively deliver functional proteins into cancer cells through direct conjugation with tumor-targeting ligands also represents a novel strategy for targeted cancer treatment. Overall, this work provides a new paradigm for developing smart photosensitizing systems with enhanced specificity and therapeutic efficacy.

14303619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14303619.value: The extrinsic enzyme-activated photosensitizing system demonstrated in this work has significant potential for further development and clinical translation. Some key areas for future research include: 1. Expanding the scope of extrinsic enzymes and cancer targets: While β-Gal and αvβ3 integrin were used in this study, other enzymes overexpressed in specific cancer types and corresponding targeting ligands could be explored to broaden the applicability of this approach. 2. Optimizing the photosensitizer design: Further modifications to the DSBDP photosensitizer, such as improving its photophysical properties, water solubility, and tumor-targeting ability, could enhance the overall therapeutic efficacy. 3. Enhancing the enzyme delivery efficiency: The current protein delivery method relies on direct conjugation with tumor-targeting peptides. Exploring alternative carrier systems like nanoparticles or cell-penetrating peptides may improve the cellular internalization and intracellular trafficking of the extrinsic enzyme. 4. Investigating the in vivo safety and pharmacokinetics: Comprehensive in vivo studies are needed to evaluate the biocompatibility, biodistribution, and long-term safety of this photosensitizing system before clinical translation. 5. Extending to other phototherapeutic modalities: The extrinsic enzyme activation strategy could potentially be applied to other phototherapy approaches, such as photodynamic diagnosis, photoimmunotherapy, and photothermal therapy, further expanding its clinical utility. Addressing these aspects through continued interdisciplinary research efforts will help realize the full potential of this novel extrinsic enzyme-activated photosensitizing platform for precise and effective cancer phototherapy.

14303619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14303619.value: This research developed a novel cancer treatment approach that uses an "extrinsic" enzyme - an enzyme not naturally found in cancer cells - to selectively activate a light-sensitive molecule (photosensitizer) within the tumor. By delivering this foreign enzyme into cancer cells using tumor-targeting molecules, the photosensitizer can be specifically activated to generate toxic chemicals that kill the cancer cells upon light exposure, while leaving healthy cells unharmed. This "extrinsic enzyme-activated photodynamic therapy" represents a significant advance over previous methods that relied on enzymes naturally present in both cancer and healthy cells, demonstrating improved specificity and efficacy in cell and animal studies. This innovative targeted activation strategy has broad applicability and could lead to more precise and effective light-based cancer treatments in the future.

14303719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303719.value: Measurement of material deformation under local load is important to reveal the mechanical properties in general. Meanwhile, the non-local sensing of surface deformation will offer a new insight into the mechanical response such as surface tension in soft materials. Currently, the non-local surface deformation is measured under conventional fluorescence microscopy. It results in low spatial resolution. Meanwhile, owing to the low sensitivity, big loading force (more than 100 nN) is required to induce such microscale surface deformation. However, the loading force in this range might not suitable to obtain the elastic mechanical response in many systems such as thin film materials and some other soft materials. The sensing of these surface deformation with nanometer resolution is essential to further reveal their mechanical properties. Previously we developed a novel method that non-locally sense the nanoscale surface deformation upon an AFM nanoindentation by a confocal-AFM correlation microscopy. However, the developed method needs to acquire the ODMR spectrum of individual NDs in a sequence, resulting in long measurement time. It thus limits the further applications, such as reveal the dynamics and mechanical response of the deformed systems. We will develop a new method which correlates the wide-field quantum sensing to an AFM system. The quantum sensors are nanodiamonds containing nitrogen vacancy centers. We will obtain many NVs’ orientations by measuring their ESR spectrum. By comparing the orientations of NDs before and during the nanoindentation, we can thus reconstruct the surface deformation upon the nanoindentation in nanoscale (~10 nm resolution in the z-axis). We will apply this technique to investigate the mechanical response of the thin film materials in nanoscale. Moreover, owing to the high sensitivity and fast measurement ratio, we will investigate the dynamics of the surface deformation upon nanoindentation. The proposed method will investigate the non-local mechanical response of the materials upon an external stimulation in nanoscale. Compared to the conventional methods, the new method will increase the spatial sensitivity one to two orders of magnitude. It indicates that such smaller loading force is required to induce material surface deformation. It will offer a new platform to study the mechanical response of the material systems with a wide range. N/A

14303819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14303819.value: Analyzing massive datasets of thousands or even millions of variables is becoming a routine task in many scientific research fields and industry applications. Variable selection is indispensable for scientific discoveries from such datasets. Penalized regression methods, such as LASSO, SCAD and the Dantzig selector, cannot handle ultra-high dimensional problems. Thus, various variable screening procedures, such as SIS and the Kolmogorov filter, are introduced to crudely reduce the dimension to a moderate size by filtering out spurious variables according to their marginal association with the response variable. The remaining variables are then inputted for further variable selection and model fitting. There are several aspects that we need to improve over existing variable screening procedures. Firstly, they can only guarantee the sure screening property instead of consistency. Secondly, they cannot explicitly control the type-I error. Instead, they usually stop at a preselect model size without knowing how many false positives have been selected. We propose a new screening method for selecting variables from ultra-high dimensional datasets where the response variable is binary. The new method enjoys consistency instead of only the sure screening property, and enables us to select screening thresholds according to the desired type-I error rate. Moreover, it is a robust model-free method, thus it can handle complex nonlinear association between the response and the covariate. It can even detect covariates which are jointly affecting the response but show no marginal effect. We achieve these by designing a new consistent test for two-sample distribution comparison, which is motivated by two key observations: (1) the low statistical power of the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test to local density differences is due to its low resolution; (2) the regular Chi-square goodness-of-fit test often performs underpowered due to suboptimal partitioning of the domain. Our preliminary studies show that this new test is consistent and its finite sample performance is better than existing methods. Thus, the superior performance of the proposed screening method is guaranteed. Both synthetic data and real data will be used to evaluate our method and compare with existing methods. An R package will be produced to facilitate applications. As to our knowledge, this will be the first consistent variable screening method for ultra-high dimensional problems. Many important problems will benefit from this new method, such as detecting genetic disease factors from thousands of genes based on microarray gene expression data or millions of CpG sites based on methylation array data. 越來越多的科研和工業應用問題需要分析包含數千甚至數百萬變量的大數據集。變量選擇是分析此類數據必不可少的一步。現有的懲罰回歸方法，如LASSO、SCAD和Dantzig selector，都無法處理超高維問題。因此，人們引入了各種變量篩選方法，例如SIS和Kolmogorov filter，以過濾掉與響應變量沒有明顯相關性的變量，從而大幅降低變量數。剩餘的變量將用於進一步的變量選擇和模型擬合。 現有的變量篩選方法有幾個需要改進的方面。首先，它們只能保證sure screening性質，而不是更好的一致性。其次，他們無法明確控制I型錯誤率；相反，它們需要用戶自選最終模型的變量數，從而無法知道輸出變量中有多少誤報。 我們針對二元響應問題提出一種新的篩選方法，用於從超高維數據集中選擇變量。該新方法享有一致性，而不僅僅是sure screening性質；而且該方法能夠根據所需的I型錯誤率選擇篩選閾值。此外，它是一種魯棒的無模型方法，因此它可以處理響應與協變量之間複雜的非線性關聯。它甚至可以檢測共同影響響應但沒有邊際效應的協變量。我們通過設計一個新的一致的雙樣本分佈比較測試來實現這些目標。該新測試是由兩個關鍵的觀察結果推動的：（1）Kolmogorov-Smirnov測試對局部密度差異的低統計功效是源自其低分辨率; （2）由於域的次優劃分，常規的卡方擬合優度檢驗通常表現不佳。我們的初步研究表明，這項新測試是一致的，它在有限樣本上的性能優於現有方法。這些優勢保證了我們所提出的篩選方法的優越性能。合成數據和實際數據都將用於評估我們的方法，並與現有方法進行比較。我們還將製作R包以便於應用。據我們所知，這將是第一個針對超高維問題的一致性變量篩選方法。許多重要問題將受益於這個新方法，例如基於微陣列基因表達數據檢測來自數千個基因的遺傳疾病因子，或基於甲基化陣列數據檢測數百萬個CpG位點。

14303819.label: Realisation of objectives
14303819.value: All five objectives are fully achieved. For the first objective, we developed the maximum adjusted chi-squared statistic (MAC) for marginal screening with binary response (https://www3.stat.sinica.edu.tw/statistica/oldpdf/A32n106.pdf) and the HHG-CIS screening procedure for continuous response (https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00949655.2020.1724291). Both screening methods are model-free and consistent for variable screening. For the second objective, we developed the MAC filter for pairwise screening, which is model-free and consistent. For the third objective, we theoretically proved the consistent screening properties of the new methods. The asymptotic distributions of the newly proposed statistics are non-standard distributions, thus pre-compiled distribution tables are suggested. For the fourth objective, we used real bioinformatics data and simulated data to compare our methods with other methods such as Kolmogorov-Smirnov test/Kolmogorov Filter, Cramer-von Mises test, Anderson-Darling test and Zhou et al. (2017). Our methods performed better for most cases. For the fifth objective, we shared our codes freely online, such as R package (https://github.com/szcf-weiya/earth.dof.patch) and Julia package (https://github.com/szcf-weiya/DegreesOfFreedom.jl) which runs faster. We not only fulfilled all the above five objectives, but also produced some byproduct methods during related research exploration. For example, when studying the variable screening and model selection along the LASSO type of approaches, we proposed a modified search degrees of freedom to directly account for the cost of searching in the original or augmented model space. Model selection with this new degree of freedom definition is shown to outperform other definitions. The application of such byproduct methods in biomedical problems produced several papers.

14303819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14303819.value: (Note: Publications listed in Part C Section 8 are cited here according to their order in the table of Section 8) As planned by the project, we developed new screening method for selecting variables from ultra-high dimensional datasets. Our main contribution is a new class of non-parametric test statistics called maximum adjusted chi-square statistics for the two-sample distribution equality test, which is used to construct a variable screening method. The new method enjoys consistency instead of only the sure screening property and enables us to select screening thresholds according to the desired type-I error rate. Moreover, it is a robust model-free method, thus it can handle complex nonlinear association between the response and the covariate. It can even detect covariates which are jointly affecting the response but show no marginal effect. Although the asymptotic distributions of the newly proposed statistics are non-standard distributions, but we can use pre-compiled distribution tables for convenience applications. During the research exploration for this project, we ran into quite some other related statistical problems and their applications, which led to multiple research outputs. For example, LASSO is a widely used variable selection method which we ought to analyse while we were proposing new methods. Model degree of freedom is a fundamental concept in model selection. We found that LASSO’s search degree of freedom is limited since it does not consider fitting procedures in augmented space such as splines and regression trees. Thus we proposed a modified search degrees of freedom to directly account for the cost of searching in the original or augmented model space, which significantly improved model fitting performance [8]. For another example, while researching joint variable screening, the correlation among high-dimensional covariates is important. To estimate such high-dimensional correlation matrix, we ended up with attractive new methods, one based on Bagging [6] and another based on Bayesian approach [1]. When the variates are structured within a tree topology, the correlation is hard to assess, but we proposed a Bayesian method to solve the problem [7]. Along the way of constructing applications, we solved some biomedical problems using various model selection and fitting methods [2-5].

14304019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304019.value: Converting nitrogen to ammonia via the nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR) is essential for human survival. This is done in industrial scales by the Haber-Bosch process. It requires a huge amount of energy input as well as a constant supply of hydrogen gas. To feed the Earth’s future population, a more sustainable alternative must be developed. A promising approach is photocatalytic NRR, in which only sunlight, air and water are needed. However, the traditional photocatalysts such as TiO2, CdS, and WO3 powders are not efficient for NRR. This proposal describes the development of two-dimensional (2D) layered photocatalysts with enhanced surface areas, shortened charge diffusion distances, and unique electronic structures. The objective is to fabricate ultrathin 2D photocatalysts with optimized surface for NRR. The photocatalysts used in the project will be based on 2D single-unit-cell PbBiO2Br nanosheets. This should result in a powerful internal electric field. Such field can promote exciton dissociation and thus drive the transfer of electrons to (PbBiO2) layers and of holes to (Br) layers. On the (PbBiO2) layers, we will create atomic vacancies by thermal treatment under vacuum or H2 atmosphere; anchor single atom catalysts of Ru, Rh, Fe, Ni, Co, Mo, Pd, or Pt by the combination of photo-deposition and thermal grafting; and introduce strain by N, S, and P doping. Through these surface engineering approaches, we would open up abundant active sites for adsorbing, splitting, and hydrogenating N2. 利用空氣中的氮氣作為原料來合成氨氣，對於人類生存和社會發展至關重要。哈伯發明的氨合成法是應用最為廣泛的人工固氮途徑，不過該方法需要在高溫和高壓下進行，每年消耗大量的電能；同時該反應需要使用化石燃料生產的氫氣，造成每年數億噸的二氧化碳排放。為了平衡社會能源和環境結構與人口快速增長所急需的氨氣衍生產品之間的矛盾，發展溫和條件合成氨的新途徑迫在眉睫。半導體光催化還原氮氣合成氨，僅需太陽能作為唯一輸入能源，利用水作為質子源，可以作為哈伯合成氨的最有希望的潛在替代者。然而，以金屬氧化物和硫化物為代表的傳統半導體光催化劑，受制於較低的電子空穴分離效率及較弱的表面催化還原氮氣動力學，在光催化合成氨領域進步甚微。 本項目致力於設計合成二維單層PbBiO2Br納米片光催化合成氨催化劑，利用其超薄特性相關的內電場來定向分離電子空穴（電子到達{PbBiO2)層，空穴到達(Br)層），通過超薄二維平面提供高密度氮還原活性位元點，進一步在其{PbBiO2)層創造原子空位缺陷、修飾過渡金屬（例如釕、銠、鐵、鎳、鈷、鉬、鈀、鉑）單原子催化劑、摻雜非金屬晶格張力調控劑來提高位點催化還原氮氣的固有活性，以期實現高效的光催化氨合成。

14304019.label: Realisation of objectives
14304019.value: All proposed objectives have been achieved, and we have established research collaboration to expand the scope of the inverstigations to other 2D electrocatalysts for environmental and energy applications. For example, we found that highly dispersed bismuth nanoparticles alone exhibited very attractive catalytic properties. We therefore developed a method to deposit Bi on a stable porous titanium dioxide substrate, and used it as a highly active electrocatalyst for reducing the greenhouse carbon dioxide gas to valuable formic acid. In an early stage of our investigation, 2D single-unit-cell PbBiO2Br nanosheets were prepared. However, we found that the addition of lead in the catalyst composition was not a good idea. This toxic metal should be avoided or replaced by other elements that are more environmentally acceptable. Therefore, we developed the following catalysts: To explore the potential of using other 2D nanosheets to catalyse nitrogen fixation processes, we designed a structure based on the more conventional ruthenium catalyst. Ru/oxygen-doped-Ru core/shell nanoclusters were fabricated for electrocatalytic nitrate reduction (NITRR) to form ammonia. Oxygen dopants expand the Ru unit cell to trigger tensile strains. The strains suppress HER but favor ·H formation by lifting the barrier of hydrogen−hydrogencoupling. The resulting ·H promotes the hydrogenation of reaction intermediates to ammonia. Benefiting from the HER prevention and NITRR promotion, our room-temperature electrocatalysis exhibits high ammonia-synthesizing rate. Moreover, the nanoclusters maintain a high selectivity across a wide range of applied potentials, and they show superior durability against strong currents because of the firm bonding of Ru with subsurface oxygen dopants. Another Bi-based catalyst, Bi2WO6 was found to be a suitable electrode material for H2O2 production through a two electron water oxidation route. The H2O2 generation rate was further optimized by Mo-doping and enlarged specific surface area. The Faraday efficiency of electrode FTO/ Bi2WO6 :Mo reached peak 79% at 3.2 V vs. RHE, and it also showed good durability at least in 6 h. As revealed by DFT calculation, the DGOH* value for both Bi2WO6 and Bi2WO6 :Mo was favorable for a two-electron water oxidation reaction, and W atoms should be the reaction center. This on-demand production approach would allow maximum utilization of H2O2 in a system. S-doped BiOBr was synthesized via a solvothermal method in the absence of water. Although this catalyst was not effective for nitrogen fixation, it could be used for visible-light driven degradation of ibuprofen. S-doping tuned the band structure of BiOBr, leading to a narrower band gap and thus higher utilization efficiency of visible light. The degradation of ibuprofen on SeBiOBr could be attributed to the generation of H2O2 and OH radicals. We also tested the use of BiOBr for other chemical concersions. A new bromide-mediated photocatalytic approach was developed for highly selective synthesis of ethylene oxide or ethylene glycol from ethylene. The bromine/hypobromous acid (Br2/HOBr) generated in photocatalytic process are effective active species for conversion of gaseous ethylene to liquid intermediates, bromoethanol and dibromoethane. These intermediates were further converted to ethylene oxide or ethylene glycol via a facile alkali treatment in different temperatures, giving rise to a high selectivity. Long-term stability (> 40 h) of BiOBr is maintained by adding KBr in the reaction system to automatically replenish Br in BiOBr. This work provides a potential alternative to current industrial method for green synthesis of ethylene-derived commodity chemicals. A similar 2D catalyst, graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4), was prepared through a facile thermal polymerization approach. The S, Kdoped/alkalized g-C3N4 product could generate singlet oxygen (1O2) efficiently. This powerful yet selective oxidant was found to be effective for the oxidation of bisphenol A (BPA). The main oxidant was found to be the super oxide anion radicals. This approach would prevent the production of undesirable toxic intermediates which may be inevitable during ⋅OH-based photocatalysis. This photocatalytic approach could preferentially oxidize pollutants in a complex matrix. In a subsequent study, we incorporated pyrophosphate into g-C3N4 to make it effective for proton shuttle and oxygen activation. This new material was prepared by facile thermal polymerization to overcome the problem of lack of protons in alkaline conditions. In another study involving g-C3N4, we doped K into it to creat N-vacancies foe efficient non-sacrificial H2O2 synthesis. We also found that adding iodide species to K-doped C3N4 would allow selective photocatalytic treatment of phenolic pollutants. A very interesting discovery in this project was the fabrication of a bimetallic layered double hydroxide for seawater oxidation. We demonstrated a homogeneous multimetallic catalyst consisting of Ni and Fe coincorporated into CuCo layered double hydroxide (denoted as NiFe-CuCo LDH) that served as an active and durable OER electrode for high performance seawater electrolysis. With abundant exposed multimetal sites and well-defined micronanostructures, the NiFe-CuCo LDH catalyst required overpotentials of only 259, 278, and 283 mV to yield current densities of 100, 300, and 500 mA cm-2, respectively, in a seawater electrolyte. Moreover, it exhibited very high OER selectivity (Faradaic efficiency of 97.4% for O2 at 500 mA cm-2) and superior durability during operation, working stably under a large current density of 500 mA cm-2 for up to 500 h in 6 M KOH seawater electrolyte. We applied our experience with 2D bimetallic catalysts and extened it to the fabrication of CoNi-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs).We found that the in situ formed metal oxyhydroxides on the catalyst surface were the real OER active species, and the incorporated Fe effectively regulated the local electronic configurations of the neighboring Co site for more favorable adsorption of the *OH intermediate to reduce the energy barrier of the rate-determining step. This ultrafast Fe incorporation method was also successfully applied to boost the OER performance of many other MOFs as well as to synthesize large-size electrodes. We took advantage of the atomic vacancies idea and designed an asymmetric coupled heteronuclear photocatalyst. The new catalyst contained single atoms of nickel and cobalt loaded on titanium dioxide. It exhibited an impressive 71% selectivity for acetic acid. The experimental data and theoretical calculations revealed that the Ni and Co single atom sites not only significantly decreased the energy barrier of electron transfer in photocatalysis but also efficiently promoted the C-C coupling toward CH3COOH. The high activity of such a heteronuclear catalyst system would shed light on the future development of effective materials for CO2RR. The approach of using bi-metallic catalysts with dual active sites for H2O2 generation was fould to be extremely useful. We fabricated a ZnGa2O4 anode with dual active sites to improve the selectivity and to avoid the decomposition of peroxides. Based on our experimental observations and theoretical calculations, the H2O2 was formed on ZnGa2O4 through both indirect and direct reaction routes. More importantly, the indirect route, mediated by the HCO3-/HCO4-, was the critical step in H2O2 production. We also designed a Bi4Ti3O12 nanosheet for photocatalytic overall water splitting. This was a spatially differentiated structure that can overcome the limitation of charge transfer occurring only across different crystal planes in a single crystal semiconductor. This photocatalyst could produce 40.3 μmol h-1 of hydrogen and 20.1 μmol h-1 of oxygen at a near stoichiometric ratio of 2:1 and a solar-to-hydrogen efficiency of 0.1% under simulated solar light.

14304019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304019.value: All of our important finings are summarized in 14 papers published in (or submitted to) high-impact journals including JACS (Part C, No. 1 & 13), Angew. Chem. (No. 2), Nature Commun. (No. 11 & 14) and PNAS (No. 6). All these are elegant solutions to energy/environmental problems. For example, ammonia can be produced electrochemically from nitrate containing wastewater. The new approach is more energy efficient and environmental-friendlier than the traditional high-temperature Haber-Bosch process. It makes perfect sense as breaking the strong N to N triple bonds requires 941 KJ/mole while disintegration of nitrate needs only 204 KJ/mole. Our extensive experience in catalytic water splitting provides the source of hydrogen. All these reactions occur efficiently on a novel catalyst consists of strained ruthenium nanoclusters. Record breaking rate of ammonia generation is achieved. We reported for the first time a system that can generate just the right amount of hydrogen peroxide for chemical conversion or pollution treatment. We discovered an efficient way to produce the green oxidant electrochemically from water on demand. The key to realizing the water to hydrogen peroxide conversion is a highly selective anode catalyst, Bi2WO6:Mo. The water oxidation reaction follows a 2e-pathway with record high selectivity. This on-demand production approach allows maximum generation and utilization of H2O2 in a single system. This is an elegant solution to energy/environmental problems. The efficiency of this system could be further improved by using a zinc gallium oxide anode with dual active sites, Based on our experimental observations and theoretical calculations, H2O2 is formed on ZnGa2O4 through both indirect and direct reaction routes. More importantly, the indirect route, mediated by the HCO3-/HCO4-, was the critical step in H2O2 production. Reaction pathways involving the major ionic and radical species were elucidated. Our new system could overcome the mass transfer limitation of the traditional approach. Finally, our findings from using a bimetallic layered double hydroxide for seawater oxidation suggest the great potential for clean energy generation from the most abundant source of water.

14304019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304019.value: Further development on the application aspect of our technology should be based on the versatility of the active sites on a 2D catalyst surface. Taking advantage of these active sites would allow the development of more effective systems for (sea)water splitting, nitrogen fixation, carbon dioxide reduction, hydrogen peroxide production, and pollutant degradation. As we found out early in our study, toxic heavy metals should be avoided as much as possible in the catalyst composition. Future studies can also be focused on optimizing the composition of electrolytes and reaction media to enhance production efficiency, and to elucidate the reaction mechanism behind it.

14304019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304019.value: This research is significant as it demonstrates how catalytic materials can be used for solving energy and environmental problems. Many new catalysts have been prepared by low-cost green technologies. These catalysts are found to be highly effective for nitrogen fixation and water splitting. Foe example, a carefully designed catalyst can produce ammonia from nitrate containing wastewater. The new approach is more energy efficient and environmental-friendlier than the traditional high-temperature Haber-Bosch process. It makes perfect sense as breaking the strong N to N triple bonds would require much more energy than the disintegration of nitrate . Our extensive experience in catalytic water splitting provides the source of hydrogen. All these reactions occur efficiently on a novel catalyst consists of strained ruthenium nanoclusters. Record breaking rate of ammonia generation is achieved.

14304119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304119.value: Bernoulli convolutions are the probability distributions of some random series and have a natural convolution structure. They are the most important examples of self-similar measures. These measures have been studied since the 1930's, revealing remarkable connections to a lot of branches of mathematics such as probability theory, harmonic analysis, fractal geometry, dynamical systems and number theory. In the 1960's, Garsia introduced a notion of entropy for Bernoulli convolutions, which nowadays is called Garsia entropy. This notion describes the arithmetic complexity of the generating iterated function systems of Bernoulli convolutions, and plays a significant role in the recent studies of their analytic and geometric properties. In this project, we plan to investigate the relation between the Garsia entropy and other dynamical invariants of the associated iterated function systems. We aim to provide efficient algorithms to compute the Garsia entropy numerically. As applications, we plan to use them to analyze the dimensional and smoothness properties of Bernoulli convolutions. Bernoulli卷積是一些隨機級數的概率分佈，其具備自然的捲積結構。它們是最為重要的一類自相似測度。這些測度的研究源於上世紀30年代，它們與諸如概率論，調和分析，分形幾何，動力系統及數論等數學分支之間有著極為深刻的聯繫。在上世紀60年代，Garsia引入了關於Bernoulli卷積的熵這一概念，目前它已被稱為Garsia熵。這一概念定量描述了Bernoulli卷積所對應的生成迭代函數係統的算術複雜性，並在當前關於Bernoulli卷積分析及幾何性質的研究中起到了至關重要的作用。在該項目中，我們將研究Garsia熵與迭代函數係統所對應的動力系統不變量之間的聯繫，並希望提供關於Garsia熵的數值計算的有效算法。作為應用，我們計劃用它們來研究Bernoulli卷積的維數及光滑性質。

14304119.label: Realisation of objectives
14304119.value: One of the fundamental questions in fractal geometry is to determine the Hausdorff dimension of Bernoulli convolutions. Recall that Bernoulli convolutions are the most interesting and important examples of overlapping self-similar measures, and each of them is parametrized by a number beta in (1,2). According to the recent breaking results of Hochman (2014) and Varju (2019), it is known that for each transcendental parameter beta, the corresponding Bernoulli convolution has dimension 1, whilst for each algebraic parameter beta, the dimension of the corresponding Bernoulli convolution is determined by its Garsia entropy H(beta). Hence it is important to estimate the magnitude of the Garsia entropy. In this project, we associate the Garsia entropy to the projection entropy, a notion introduced by the PI and Hu in 2009. Hence to estimate the Garsia entropy, one can estimate the projection entropy. We successfully develop an algorithm to estimate the projection entropy from below, so that we can estimate the Garsia entropy and the dimension of Bernoulli convolutions from Below. As an application, we show that for any parameter beta in (1,2), the dimension of the Bernoulli convolution associated with beta is bounded below by 0.98040856, which improves a previous uniform lower bound 0.82 obtained by Hare and Sidorov in 2018. This new uniform lower bound is very close to the known numerical approximation 0.98040931953 (with error less than 10^{-11}) for the dimension of the Bernoulli convolution associated with the tribonacci number (which is the the largest root of the polynomial x^3-x^2-x-1. Moreover, the infimum of the dimension of the Bernoulli convolution is attained at a parameter in a small interval of length 10^{-8} containing the tribonacci number. Moreover when beta is a Pisot number, we express H(beta) in terms of the measure-theoretic entropy of the equilibrium measure for certain matrix pressure function. This enables us to present an algorithm to estimate the Garsia entropy and dimension from above as well. Besides the above main findings, in the project we have also obtained a complete result regarding the L^q dimension of overlapping self-similar measures (satisfying the exponential separation condition) on the line for each q in (0,1), and some sufficient conditions for a typical self-similar, or more generally, a typical self-affine set to have non-empty interior. Our approach combines different techniques from multifractal analysis and Fourier analysis.

14304119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304119.value: In [1], we study the L^q dimension and the multifractal structure of overlapping self-similar sets and measures. Under the assumption of exponential separation condition, we give a precise formula for the L^q dimension of an overlapping self-similar measure for each q in (0,1), which completes a previous result of Shmerkin (2019) who determines the formula of the L^q dimension for those q greater or equal to 1. Under the same condition, we also give a necessary and sufficient condition for an IFS to satisfy the so-called asymptotically weak separation condition (AWSC). Moreover for a class of homogeneous IFSs with algebraic contraction ratios and algebraic translations, we investigate when they satisfy AWSC, and also give a formula for the dimension of the attractors. In [2], we provide an algorithm to estimate from below the dimension of self-similar measures with overlaps. This work is based on a previous result of Feng and Hu (2009) stating that the dimension of an overlapping self-similar measure can be expressed in terms of the so called projection entropy. In this paper, we develop an algorithm to estimate the projection entropy from below, so as to estimate from below the dimension of self-similar measures. As an application, we show that for any parameter beta in (1,2), the dimension of the Bernoulli convolution associated with beta is bounded below by 0.98040856, which improves a previous uniform lower bound 0.82 obtained by Hare and Sidorov in 2018. This new uniform lower bound is very close to the known numerical approximation 0.98040931953 (with error less than 10^{-11}) for the dimension of the Bernoulli convolution associated with the tribonacci number (which is the the largest root of the polynomial x^3-x^2-x-1. Moreover, the infimum of the dimension of the Bernoulli convolution is attained at a parameter in a small interval of length 10^{-8} containing the tribonacci number. Moreover when beta is a Pisot number, we express the dimension of the corresponding Bernoulli convolution in terms of the measure-theoretic entropy of the equilibrium measure for certain matrix pressure function, and present an algorithm to estimate the dimension from above as well. In [3] we provide some sufficient conditions for a typical self-affine set to have non-empty interior. Our approach is based on some transversality arguments and Fourier transform.

14304119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304119.value: In this project, we investigate the relationship between the Garsia entropy of Bernoulli convolutions and other dynamical invariants of the associated iterated function systems. We provide an efficient algorithm to estimate the lower bound of the Garsia entropy for Bernoulli convolutions. Based on this algorithm, we obtain a very sharp uniform lower bound for the dimensions of Bernoulli convolutions with parameters in the interval (1,2). Meanwhile, for a specific class of algebraic parameters known as Pisot numbers, we can express the Garsia entropy in terms of the measure-theoretic entropy of the equilibrium measure for certain matrix pressure functions. This allows us to also estimate the Garsia entropy (and consequently the dimension of the corresponding Bernoulli convolution) from above.

14304219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304219.value: 這項提議的工作的目的,是開發基於雙硫屬元素鈷鹽的高效有機路易斯酸催化劑，並且應用於各種化學轉化。 在有機路易斯酸催化中，結合 sigma-holes（由原子電子密度的各向異性分佈引起的缺電子區域）的概念引起了越來越多的關注，因為他們在一些化學轉化中有特別的反應性和選擇性。有機路易斯酸也被認為是金屬催化劑的更環保的替代品。 含軟硫屬元素（包括硫，硒和碲的第16族元素）的有機化合物具有sigma-holes，並可與孤對電子相互作用（相互作用也稱為硫屬元素鍵）。一個新興的研究領域涉及使用軟硫屬元素作為路易斯酸有機催化劑。硫屬鍵表現出高方向性和疏水性。通過改變取代基，硫屬元素鍵系統的路易斯酸性和空間需求很容易調節。因此，含軟硫屬元素的有機化合物是具吸引力的路易斯酸有機催化劑開發平台。在文獻中，已經有使用二取代的硫屬元素化物作為有機路易斯酸催化劑的實例。然而，由於它們的路易斯酸度相對較弱，高催化劑負載量是難以避免的。 我們的研究小組多年來一直致力於開發基於軟硫屬元素的有機催化劑（例如，Yeung, Y.-Y. J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2013, 135, 1232; J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2014, 136, 5627）。最近，我們成功發現三取代的陽離子單硫屬元素鹽是有效的有機路易斯酸，並且應用於一些反應（Yeung, Y.-Y. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 12869）。然而，它們的催化性能尚未提高到實用水平。此外，它們的不對稱催化方案還沒有被開發。 最近，在一項未發表的研究中，我們發現雙硫屬元素鈷鹽系統，可以通過兩種硫屬元素陽離子的協同作用，並有效地催化相關的化學轉化。我們也發現雙硫屬元素鈷鹽有機催化劑，比相應的單硫屬元素系統更有效。此外，我們成功製備了具有手性陰離子的硫屬元素鈷鹽，並且發現它們可以催化一些對映選擇性的不對稱轉化。基於這些試驗結果，在這項擬議的工作中，我們計劃進一步開發和探索雙硫屬元素鈷鹽作為有機路易斯酸，並且應用於各種轉化的應用。我們預計新的催化方案將成為有機合成的有力工具。

14304219.label: Realisation of objectives
14304219.value: 1. Prepare a series of bis-chalcogenium salt organocatalysts. At the initial stage of the project, we prepared a series of bis-chalcogenium salt catalysts based on a modified literature procedure. For examples, two equivalents of diphenyl selenide were reacted with dihaloalkane (e.g. 1,4-diiodobutane) followed by in situ ion-exchange of the iodide anion with triflate using the silver triflate. Thus, a series of bis-selenonium triflate catalysts with different spacers between the two selenonium cations were prepared successfully. By using the same strategy but with the use of silver tetrafluoroborate in the ion-exchange process, the corresponding bis-selenonium tetrafluoroborate catalysts were furnished. In addition, we have prepared the mono-selenonium catalysts bearing similar alkyl substituents for comparison. A single crystal of bis-selenonium tetrafluoroborate catalyst was analyzed by X-ray crystallography. The distances between the Se atoms and the fluorine of tetrafluoroborate anions (2.89 Å and 2.94 Å) were found to be considerably shorter than the sum of van der Waals’ radii of Se and F (3.37 Å). Both selenonium centres in the bis-selenonium catalyst were found to adapt trigonal bipyramidal geometry with a phenyl and a BF4- groups occupying the apical positions. These factors suggest that the two Se cations in the catalyst might interact with fluoride via chalcogen bond, electrostatic interaction and/or dispersion force. 2. Examine the performance of the bis-chalcogenium salt organocatalysts in various transformations that involve the activation of carbonyls and imines. Aza-Diels Alder reaction between Danishefsky diene and N-phenylbenzaldimine was examined under ambient conditions. To our delight, the bis-selenonium catalyst (2 mol%) catalyzed the reaction to give the desired cyclized product in quantitative yield. The performance of mono-selenonium catalyst analogue was significantly lower than that of the bis-selenonium catalyst even when the catalyst loading was doubled, revealing that a synergistic activation of the substrate by the bis-selenonium cation should be involved. The cationic Se centre appears to be crucial in which the neutral divalent selenide catalyst was unable to promote the reaction. We are also delighted to realize that the performance of the bis-selenonium catalyst was superior to the strong (and moisture sensitive) Lewis acid BF3. The catalytic performance of bis-selenonium was intriguing because Lewis acids that have good catalytic performance typically suffers from poor hydrolytic stability. However, the reaction with the bis-selenonium executed smoothly under ambient conditions. Pyridine (1:1 to the Lewis acidic centre) was added to the reactions to examine the inhibition effect of Lewis base on the catalysts. The BF3-catalyzed reaction was severely suppressed while the bis-selenonium catalyzed reaction was only slowed down gently. Substrate bearing a pyridinyl substituent was also examined and the catalytic performance of bis-selenium catalyst was superior to that of other catalysts including BF3, AgOTf, Schreiner’s thiourea, a divalent chalcogen bond catalyst and a halogen bond catalyst. The reaction progresses with the bis-selenonium catalyst and BF3 were probed using 1H NMR. The catalytic efficiency of bis-selenonium catalyst was steady throughout the reaction. In contrast, the reaction with the strong Lewis acid BF3 was fast at the beginning but slowed down dramatically later on, which is a typical phenomenon of competitive inhibition in catalysis. NMR studies on a mixture of substrate and the catalysts were performed. The substrate complexed with BF3 readily but it unexpectedly interacted weakly with the bis-selenonium. Bis-selenonium was mixture with water in CD3CN for 24 h and no decomposition nor strong binding was observed based on the NMR studies. It is intriguing to realize that the bis-selenonium did not bind to the substrate strongly but its catalytic performance was superior to the strong Lewis acid BF3. So, we believe that although the bis-selenonium might be a weaker Lewis acid than BF3 in the substrate activation, bis-selenonium was less deactivated by the amine residues (in the substrates and products) and so overall a higher turnover frequency could be achieved. We then turned our attention to other substrates with various substituents and they were compatible with the catalytic protocol. Diels-Alder reaction between cyclohexa-1,3-diene and methyl vinyl ketone was also examined. The reaction was sluggish (<5% yield) with 5 mol% of mono-selenonium salt and a much higher catalyst loading (40 mol%) was necessary to produce small amount of product (18%). However, the endo/exo (1:1) selectivity was negligible. In sharp contrast, the endo/exo selectivity (20:1) was enhanced dramatically when 5 mol% of bis-selenonium catalyst was used. The high selectivity could be attributed to the interaction between the dienophile and the bis-selenonium, which might offer a rigid s-trans conformation of the enone for a better endo/exo selectivity. Diels-Alder reactions with other substrates were also examined and satisfactory yields were obtained. The catalytic protocol was then applied to the electrophilic bromination reactions. N-Bromosuccinimide (NBS) was used as the halogen source, and we believe that the bis-selenonium catalyst could activate NBS via bidentate coordination to the succinimide’s carbonyl group. Electrophilic bromination of anisole and anisole-type substrates with substituents at the para, ortho, and/or meta-position could be promoted by catalytic amount of bis-selenonium catalyst, giving the corresponding product in excellent yield. The mono-bromination of 1,3-benzodioxole also worked well and gave the desired product in 80% yield. Naphthyl substrates reacted smoothly in the presence of 0.5 mol % catalyst. The cyclopropane-containing substrates underwent the reaction smoothly under the mild catalytic condition with the cyclopropane ring, which is known to undergo halogen-mediated ring-opening process readily, remaining intact. The same protocol could be applied to the bromolactonization and bromocycloetherification reactions. We sought to understand the interaction mode between bis-selenonium and electron donors via computational analysis. Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations were carried out. In the optimized structure, it was found that the oxygen’s lone pairs of electrons in ketone interact with the two selenonium cations of the bis-selenonium catalyst in a bidentate manner with the two O-Se-C bond angles (~170o) almost linear. In addition, the Se-O distance is shorter than the sum of van der Waals’ radii of Se and O (3.42 Å), suggesting that there is considerable interaction between the two atoms. The vinyl ketone appears to be forced at s-trans conformation potentially due to the steric effect associated with the rigid bidentate interaction, which could explain the high endo/exo selectivity in the reaction. The superior catalytic performance of the bis-selenonium catalysts and the minimum catalyst inhibition effect as compared to those typically strong Lewis acids could be attributed to the unique feature of catalysis originated from the donor-to-sigma* interaction, which is non-covalent and weakly enthalpic. We also attempted to use the selenonium salt to catalyze the Ritter-type reaction of allyl bromide using acetonitrile and water. However, the reaction was sluggish and only trace amount of desired product was detected. Nonetheless, during the research avenue it was realized that silver salt can promote the reaction in yield. In addition, during the development of catalytic protocol, we also realized that bifunctional phosphonium salts and oxaselenolium cations are potent organic Lewis acid catalysts and their utilities in the functionalization of unsaturated compounds were briefly explored. 3. Publish the results in world-class peer-reviewed international journals Under this project, four high-impact publications were produced. The detail appears in Part C. Overall, all objectives have been fully realized and a summary of the major research outcomes is shown below.

14304219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304219.value: 1. Lewis acids are frequently employed in catalysis but they often suffer from high moisture sensitivity. In many reactions, catalysts are deactivated because of the problem that strong Lewis acids also bond to the products. In this research, hydrolytically stable bidentate Lewis acid catalysts derived from selenonium dicationic centers have been developed. The bis-selenonium catalysts are employed in the activation of imine and carbonyl groups in various transformations with good yields and selectivity. Lewis acidity of the bis-selenonium salts was found to be stronger than that of the mono-selenonium systems, attributed to the synergistic effect of the two cationic selenonium centers. In addition, the bis-selenonium catalysts are not inhibited by strong bases or moisture. 2. Intermolecular haloesterification is an important class of transformations. The resulting products are valuable building blocks. However, it is often necessary to use super-stoichiometric amount of acid in order to compensate the low reactivity. In this work, we developed a zwitterion-catalyzed intermolecular bromoesterification using acid and olefin in an equimolar ratio. Mechanistic study revealed that the charge pair in the zwitterion works synergistically in activating both NBS and carboxylic acid. 3. A facile, efficient, and chemoselective synthesis of allylic amides has been developed. Allyl bromides were used as the precursors activated by silver triflate. A Ritter-type reaction readily proceeded to give various allyl amides under mild conditions. The reaction protocol was also applicable to different nucleophilic partners to give a wide range of allyl-substituted products in the absence of a base. 4. A proof-of-concept study of hypervalent chalcogenonium···π bonding catalysis was performed. A new catalytic strategy using 1,2-oxaselenolium salts as chalcogen bond donors and alkenes as chalcogen bond acceptors is described. The feasibility of this concept is demonstrated by the use of trisubstituted selenonium salts in the metal-free catalytic hydrofunctionalization and polymerization of alkenes via unconventional seleniranium ion-like intermediates. The results indicate that counter anions have a significant effect on the catalysis based on hypervalent chalcogenonium···π bonding interactions.

14304219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304219.value: Lewis acid catalysts are very useful in various chemical transformations. While Lewis acid catalysis is well established, many of Lewis acid catalysts involve toxic metals. In addition, many Lewis acids are moisture sensitive and tedious reaction setup is needed. In some other cases, substrates with acid-sensitive functional groups or Lewis basic substituents are incompatible. In this research project, bis-selenonium catalysts are used to activate electron-donor substrates such as carbonyl and imine compounds. The two selenonium cations in the catalyst activate the substrates synergistically and the catalytic performance is superior to many other organocatalysts. The steric and electronic demands of the catalysts can be altered easily by changing the substituents. In addition, the bis-selenonium catalysts are not sensitive to moisture and the catalytic protocol can be operated under ambient conditions. Moreover, the reactions can still proceed smoothly even in the presence of Lewis bases. In future, we will further explore the applications of bis-chalcogenium catalysts in other chemo and/or stereoselective reactions that can be operated under ambient conditions and has high functional group compatibility.

14304219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304219.value: Many chemical manufacturing processes are energy- and atom-inefficient, leading to the generation of significant amounts of wastes and emissions. To meet the growing demand on energy for the global economy, it becomes more important than ever to look for green alternatives of energy-efficient processes. However, the current state of technology lags behind the schedule to meet the international targets. Small molecule catalysts are considered as nanoscale molecular machines that can provide control in various transformations at molecular level. Catalysis underpins many industries as over 90% of chemicals produced rely on the use of a catalyst to certain extent. It is obvious that catalytic processes play a key role in improving air and water quality, reduce energy consumption and emission, and offer solutions to long-term sustainable energy and environmental protection. In the current project, we have developed a number of useful catalytic protocols using bis-chalcogenium catalysts. Our work on the novel catalysis provides a very useful tool for various transformations. In addition, organocatalysis is mild and metal-free, which are attractive features to the manufacturing sectors. The research endeavor results in the synthesis of a wide range of useful building blocks for various medicinal and chemical applications.

14304419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304419.value: High-pressure offers a clean and systematic route to control strongly correlated system. The physical process and mechanism are strongly dependent on the carrier density and the interaction strength. By changing the pressure applied on the materials, we can tune these parameters continuously while keeping other parameters intact. However, due to restriction in accessibility introduced by the high pressure devices, many conventional sensing methods cannot be easily applied. In this proposal, we will break this barrier by developing a powerful quantum sensors made from nanodiamonds for studying pressure-driven superconductivity. NV centers is a versatile quantum sensor with high sensitivity for DC/AC magnetic signals, electrical signals, mechanical strains and temperature. With their small size, nanodiamonds can provide nanometer-scale spatial resolution and can withstand pressure much stronger than other sensors. In this proposal, we will use the NV centers as a magnetic field sensor to probe the change of magnetic field distribution in the sample during the superconducting transitions via Meissner effect, which was not possible to measure in this extreme condition before. By measuring the spatial distribution of magnetic field, the dependence on the strength of external magnetic field effect, we can get a well-informed picture of this phase transition under pressure, and determine key parameters such as London penetration depth which is ultimately related to the superconducting gap function. The comparison between experimental results and theory will lead to new understanding of the system. This project will provide a new tool for solid state quantum physics research and give new insights to quantum phase transitions. 高壓提供了一個幹凈和系統的調控強關聯體系的方法。這個物理過程強烈依賴載流子濃度和相互作用的強度。通過改變加在樣品上的壓力，我們可以在不改變其他參數的情況下連續調控這兩個參數。但是由於高壓實驗本身的各種局限，常規的探測手段沒法使用。 在這個項目中，我們提出用納米鑽石做量子傳感去研究相變引起的超導。鑽石裏的色心缺陷可以探測磁場，電場，應力和溫度。由於尺寸很小，可以提供納米尺度的空間分辨率，同時又可以在很高的壓強下工作。在這個工作中，我們用色心去探測磁場在超導相變中的變化。通過測定磁場的空間分布，對於外界磁場的依賴，我們可以得到倫敦穿透深度，進一步的得到超導帶隙的大小。通過跟理論比對，我們可以對這個體系有更深刻的了解。 這個項目研發了一個新的研究固體物理的方法，也對研究量子相變帶來了新的視角。

14304419.label: Realisation of objectives
14304419.value: In this project, we developed a series of quantum sensing techniques to study pressure driven transitions with quantum sensors. (1) We have realized the measuring pressure distributions inside pressure instrumentation for various pressure medium (PR Applied 13, 024041 (2020)). We demonstrated that the pressure calibration with color centers has much higher spatial resolution and pressure resolution. We also used this method to measure the solidification critical pressure for different pressure medium. Along this direction, we further developed a method to study the solidification process of polymer materials (ACS Appl. Polym. Mater. 2021, 3, 1, 162–170). We also pointed out that by using polymer solidification, one can apply high stress to materials without the need of high pressure instrumentation. These results fulfill Objective 1 and partially Objective 3. (2) We have designed a set of measuring methods based on measuring Meissner effect with color center for studying superconductivity, including measuring the critical temperature, the lower and upper critical fields, phase diagram, and the critical current density. We applied these methods to YBa2Cu4O8 and BaFe2(As0.59P0.41)2 , and mapped out the distribution of magnetic fields during the superconducting transitions (PR Applied under review, JAP 129, 241101 (2021), Functional Diamond 1, 160 (2021)). These results fulfill Objective 2 and 3. (3) We did several spectroscopy studies on quantum sensors under pressure. We measured the optical spectra, ESR spectra and NMR spectra of both implanted color centers and color centers in nanoparticle form. We studied their dependence on pressure, stress and external magnetic fields (PR Applied 18, 064042 (2022), PR Applied 19, 044091 (2023).). With these results, we compared pros and cons of quantum sensors in implanted form and in nanoparticle forms. Also we made optimized solutions for the performance of quantum sensor under pressure in various scenarios. These results fulfill Objective 1 and partially objective 3.

14304419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304419.value: Superconductivity transition driven by pressure is hard to study as the experimental conditions are harsh for near field sensing techniques. In this project, we developed a set of novel methods to solve this bottleneck. We used quantum sensors made from nitrogen vacancy center in diamond and use them to probe magnetic field, stress, pressure and temperature with high spatial resolution. Traditional transportation measurement or susceptibility method can only probe response from superconductor. And it takes the combination of several methods to probe different critical parameters. We have designed a set of measuring methods all based on measuring Meissner effect with color centers in diamond to measure the critical temperature, the lower and upper critical fields, phase diagram, and the critical current density together. This can solve the problem of sample spatial inhomogenierty. Also, as a method without the need of conducting contact, it can help to study materials which have large contact resistance under noble metal contacts. We applied these methods to YBa2Cu4O8 and BaFe2(As0.59P0.41)2 , and mapped out the distribution of magnetic fields during the superconducting transitions (PR Applied under review, JAP 129, 241101 (2021), Functional Diamond 1, 160 (2021)). Besides superconductivity itself, pressure is a key parameter for changing superconductor's property. therefore to know the exact pressure distribution is important. We measured the pressure distribution with sub-micron resolution (PR Applied 13, 024041 (2020)). It is much more accurate compared with previous methods (using Ruby). Furthermore, we developed a method to study the solidification process of polymer materials (ACS Appl. Polym. Mater. 2021, 3, 1, 162–170). From this approach, we pointed out that by using glue, one can apply high stress to materials without the need of high pressure instrumentation. Later, this method was adapted by others to apply stress to tune material properties. Furthermore, to have better sensing resolution, we have to optimize the quantum sensor's properties under strong pressure. We measured this issue by measuring various spectra including the optical spectra, ESR spectra and NMR spectra of both implanted color centers and color centers in nanoparticle form. We studied their dependence on pressure, stress and external magnetic fields (PR Applied 18, 064042 (2022), PR Applied 19, 044091 (2023).). These results help to optimize the performance of quantum sensors.

14304419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304419.value: With these measurement methods and optimized quantum sensors ready, one can use them to study novel materials emerging recently. For example, there are several controversial results on new materials which were claimed to have superconductivity under pressure. Transportation measurements have the problem of limited resolution and background deduction. Measuring Meissner effect can be the key evidence. One can use our method of NV center sensing for that. It can also be used to estimate the superconducting volume ratio. these information can greatly help the community to verify the true nature of these new materials and understand their properties. What we developed in this project has become an important toolset for material research.

14304419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304419.value: Like temperature, pressure is a useful parameter to change material properties. It has been discovered that under strong pressure, one can generate superconductor with high transition temperature. However, to study these materials under such high pressure is challenging. In this project, we developed a set of tools for this challenge. It is based on using color center quantum sensors to measure magnetic field, pressure, stress and temperature with sub-micron resolution. By measuring the on-set of Meissner effect, we studied the properties of superconductor under pressure. Furthermore, we optimized the quantum sensors' properties for this application. The output from this project opens a new research direction in high pressure physics. What we developed in this project has become an important toolset for material research.
