14304519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304519.value: Transition metal-catalyzed cross-coupling process has emerged as one of the most straightforward and widespread used protocols for chemists to assemble structurally varied molecules, in which they are materially attractive and pharmaceutically useful compounds. Indeed, these methods have revolutionized the way to perform complex organic synthesis. At the center of these synthetic technologies, catalyst development which allows challenging or problematic bond construction process to be proceeded smoothly would be highly attractive. Thus, catalyst exploration and development is particularly central to contemporary catalysis research for innovative organic synthesis. The new development of aromatic bond-construction methodology would advance the current coupling process and put forward of catalysis research. The purposes of this project are (1) to rationally design and explore a new family of tunable phosphine ligands via a facile approach and the establishment of new possible synthetic pathways; (2) to investigate fundamental aspect, scope and limitation of the new palladium-catalyzed aryl acetate cross-coupling process; (3) to carry out mechanistic investigation using experimental and theoretical technique and the new palladium catalyst activation pathway. This project is expected to explore a new field in cross-coupling reactions. The fundamental knowledge gained during the course of catalyst development and the rationale of proximal coordination of ligand to the cross coupling partners (i.e. aryl acetate) would be of significant value for academic interest and potential applications. The proposed study is based on our previous success in the ligand/catalyst design and synthesis, and our extensive experiences in aromatic bond-construction research. These new areas will offer us an excellent opportunity in making a substantial advancement to the frontier of catalysis research and put forward to establish a foundation for fine-chemical industry in Hong Kong. 過渡金屬催化的交叉偶聯方法已經成為化學家組裝結構多變的有機分子最直接和最廣泛使用的方案之一，而大部份的有機分子都是在藥學、材料學上有用的化合物。過渡金屬催化的交叉偶聯方法徹底改變了複雜有機合成的傳統步驟。在這些合成技術中，催化劑的開發是非常有吸引力的，它使2具有挑戰性或有難度的構造過程能順利地進行。因此，催化劑的勘探和開發對於創新有機合成的當代催化研究尤其重要。芳香鍵的構建方法新發展將推動當前的偶合過程。此項目的研究目的是：（1）通過簡便的方法設計和探索新的可調控的膦配體系列，並建立新的合成途徑; （2）研究新型鈀催化芳基乙酸酯交叉偶聯過程，偶合範圍及其局限性; （3）利用實驗理論技術對新的鈀催化劑活化途徑進行機理研究。此項目有望探索交叉偶聯反應的新領域，在催化劑開發過程中獲得的基本知識和配體與交叉偶聯配偶體（即乙酸芳基酯）的配位基本原理，此研究對於學術和潛在應用都具有重要價值。此研究基於我們以往在配體/催化劑設計和合成方面取得的成功作基礎，加上我們在芳香鍵建設研究方面的豐富經驗，此項目研究的新領域將為我們在催化研究前沿方面取得實質性進展提供絕佳機會，並為香港精細化工業奠定基礎。

14304519.label: Realisation of objectives
14304519.value: This is the completion report of project GRF14304519. This project was kick-started on 01-01-2020 and was completed on 31-12-2022. During this entire COVID-19 period, we had tried our best to accomplish the project goals, given there were a number of quarantine periods in the research laboratory. We did explore a new family of tunable phosphine ligand (with systematic structural variations) for tackling cross-coupling catalysis. The easily made benzimidazole-based phosphine ligands were successfully developed and examined in aromatic C-C and C-N bond formation. Interestingly these phosphine ligand demonstrated complementary P,N and P,O coordination modes to the palladium metal center. The P,N type coordination palladium complex realized explicit C-C bond formation even with other NH nucleophiles. This orthogonal phenomenon also existed in the P,O-type complex where it preferably promoted aromatic C-N bond formation. The relevant metal complexes were fully characterized by the X-ray crystallographic analysis. This research contribution was published in Organometallics in 2021 (Organometallics, 2021, 40, 2265). In addition to benzimidazolyl phosphine lignads, we also developed new ligand entities particularly fit for regioselective N-arylation of arylhydrazines. The -NH position was selectively arylated given with other neighboring -NH2 site. This highly regioselective palladium-catalyzed monoarylation of arylhydrazine was published in The Journal of Organic Chemistry in late 2020 (J. Org. Chem. 2020, 85, 14664). The arylation of heterocycles has been a challenging topic in transition metal catalysis as those nucleophilic heterocycles would coordinate to metal center and render the relevant metal complex coordinatively saturated. In this project, we also developed an alternative approach to reach the arylated chromenes using DMAP-catalyzed annulation of ortho-AQM. The resulting arylated products are versatile, yet difficult to be accessed from traditional cross-coupling methods. This interesting finding was published in Organic Letters in late 2020 (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 9444). Moreover, we also used a similar approach to, i.e. cascade double 1,4-addition/intramolecular annulation strategy, for assembling unsymmetrical dibenzofurans. These structures were found difficult to be reached using common cross-coupling technology. This research outcome was published in Communications Chemistry in mid 2021 (Commun. Chem. 2021, 4, 42). With regard to the investigation of phenolic electrophiles (e.g. aryl carboxylates), we made attempts to employ structurally fine-tuned ligand fit for this catalysis. Interestingly, the 5-substituted indole core-based phosphine ligand displayed superior performance in the palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling of aryl acetate. The scope and limitation were also evaluated. Moreover, we also carried out mechanistic study using computational approach (DFT calculation). Interestingly, we discovered that this catalysis does not follow traditional oxidative addition and transmetallation step-wisely. We found that this catalysis goes through a concerted reaction pathway (i.e. both oxidative addition and transmetallation occurred at the same time). This new mechanism, as well as the first examples of aryl acetate coupling in palladium catalysis are of important scientific knowledge in catalysis community. The manuscript has been prepared (as attached) and will be submitted to Nature Catalysis soon.

14304519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304519.value: Major finding and research outcome: In this project, we developed a new family of phosphine ligands which can effectively promote orthogonal C-C or C-N bond cross-coupling, given two nucleophilic partners are in the same system. Moreover, we also realized the regioselective N-arylation of arylhydrazine at the -NH position instead of more spatially available -NH2 group. These findings were published in Organometallics 2021 and J. Org. Chem. in 2020. Remarkably, we also established a collection of phosphine ligands which particularly fit of cross-coupling of aryl acetate. We successfully realized the first examples of aryl acetate coupling under palladium catalysis. Moreover, through our theoretical study, we found an interesting concerted mechanism which is not commonly appeared in traditional cross-coupling reactions. The results of this finding have been complied and the manuscript (as attached) is ready for submission to Nature Catalysis.

14304619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304619.value: 酶已經被廣泛用於衣物洗滌劑中，和表面活性劑一起起到各種清潔和去污效果。 然而，成功地將酶摻入洗滌劑配方中是非常具有挑戰性的。這是因為在普通洗滌劑配方中常見的表面活性劑和添加劑（漂白劑，助洗劑，著色劑等）的存在對酶的穩定性和活性具有顯著的影響。在粉末狀衣物洗滌劑中，可以通過物理方法將酶分離成獨立的顆粒來解決該問題。 然而，在液體製劑中，通過物理方法將酶與配方中其他成分分離尚未成功實現。 爲了增加液體洗滌劑製劑中酶的保質期，人們已經進行了許多嘗試，包括合成酶-聚合物絡合體或添加其他化學物質。然而在這個過程中，化學改性通常伴隨著酶活性的喪失，而化學添加劑會影響整個配方的設計並且價格昂貴。而另一個研究方向則專注於可用於封裝和遮罩活性酶的工程微膠囊。“膠體體”，即由膠體顆粒組裝而成的中空微膠囊，已經成為可用於封裝酶的最有前景的方法，因為由顆粒構成的殼可以有效保護酶在周圍環境中不會變性失活。然而，很少有關於膠體體作為液體洗衣產品中活性物載體的實際運用的報導。 最近，我們的課題組報導了基於二氧化矽的亞微米膠體體的製備，這種膠體體的殼結構是緻密的，並且能夠長期包封小的親水性分子。更有針對性的是，我們使用這些膠體體來包封脂肪酶，並且證實了膠體體中所封裝的酶的比活性比溶液中游離的酶的比活性高出20倍以上。目前得到的初步結果是令人振奮的，所以我們現在提出對這種新型封裝技術進一步研究的想法，即製備裝有衣物清潔相關酶的微膠囊，並探索它們在液體洗滌劑配方中的潛在應用。具體而言，我們計劃：（1）製備不同大小和殼特性的膠體體; （2）檢測標準洗滌劑配方中的酶包封效率，儲存穩定性和釋放性能; （3）測試洗滌性能。 今天，衣物洗滌劑是一個十億美元的產業，而液體衣物洗滌劑佔銷售額的75％。 該項目的成功完成不僅將提供有關衣物清潔相關酶與商用表面活性劑之間相互作用的基本理論，而且還將促進新型液體洗滌產品的開發。

14304619.label: Realisation of objectives
14304619.value: There are four objectives in this project and the details of the realization related to each objective are as follows: 1. To synthesize and characterize colloidosomes with varying structures, sizes and shell properties through a w/o inverse particle-stabilized (Pickering) emulsion template. We have prepared a series of water-in-oil (w/o) inverse Pickering emulsions stabilized by single or binary mixtures of particles with different functional groups, opposite charges, opposite wettabilities (i.e., they are hydrophilic or hydrophobic) or softness. The results showed that compared with Pickering emulsions stabilized by single colloidal particles, colloidosomes fabricated from emulsion stabilized by binary mixtures of particles have higher stability and customizable properties than thus can enable the exploration of the enzyme encapsulation and protection. 2. To investigate the encapsulation efficiency and release properties by using as-prepared colloidosomes for encapsulating laundry-relevant enzymes in a standard detergent formulation. Several strategies have been developed and used to investigate the encapsulation efficiency and catalytic activity of encapsulating enzymes. We have synthesized and used of the protein nanoparticles to anchor artificial enzymes (Au NCs), combined with glucose oxidase (GOx) of the aqueous phase, for preparing Pickering emulsion. Apart from anchoring enzymes into protein particles for carrying out the interfacial enzymatic reaction, we also use the protein-stabilized emulsion as template for the preparation of polymeric porous microspheres. In addition, we developed an approach to encapsulate laundry-relevant enzymes, whereby a w/o Pickering emulsion was stabilized by binary particles, including hydrophobic fumed silica R974 dispersed in the continuous phase and hydrophilic protein NPs dispersed in the dispersed phase. Covalent crosslinking of protein NPs could be induced by poly(hexamethylene diisocyanate) (PHDI) at the interface to generate a hybrid shell. The resultant capsules are stable, and their final structures can be preserved after drying in the air. Different protein NPs (e.g., casein and zein) were used as emulsifiers with silica R974 to illustrate the universality of this method. Finally, we have tried to transfer the protein/R974-PHDI capsules containing the enzymes to water either directly or via double emulsion system. 3. To examine the storage stability and long-term enzymatic activity of colloidosomes containing laundry-relevant enzymes in standard detergent formulations comprising different combinations of commercial detergent surfactants and additives. We attempted to encapsulate commercial lipase and investigated whether it was protected from environmental factors after encapsulation. Lipase was successfully encapsulated within the aqueous core, where the enzyme dispersed uniformly, without aggregating at the interface. In addition, different amounts of the crosslinker, PHDI, were tested to study the influence on enzyme activity. As compared with the non-crosslinked group (0% crosslinker), the encapsulated enzyme had much higher activity after undergoing crosslinking. This is because contact with the organic solvent will damage the lipase. By encapsulating lipase, the lipase has little access to the organic solvent with a robust physical barrier (the chemically crosslinked shell), and thus retained its activity. An increase in the amount of crosslinkers caused the relative activity of the enzyme to rise, which is attributable to increased crosslinking density, and thus, a stronger shell that affords better protection. However, there was an upper limit to the amount of crosslinker beyond which the relative activity of lipase decreased. We believe that the excess of crosslinker further reacted with lipase in the aqueous core, resulting in its denaturation, and thus, weakened activity. According to our results, optimized crosslinker amounts were in the range of 40-60%, with the highest relative activity of enzyme being almost 98%. 4. To test the washing performance of the liquid detergent containing the enzyme-loaded colloidosomes and evaluate the possibility of knowledge transfer with potential stakeholders. We have tried different methods to encapsulate lipase, which is one of the laundry-relevant enzymes in liquid detergent with Pickering emulsion as the template. Firstly, we tried to transfer the protein/R974-PHDI capsules prepared to liquid detergent with different approaches. However, it was found that the methods did not work because of the hydrophobic surface of the capsule and the high osmatic pressure of liquid detergent. Therefore, we have used another approach to encapsulate the lipase, in which pure silica-based capsules were templated from w/o Pickering emulsion stabilized by R974 fumed silica. After the sol-gel reaction, capsules with porous cores could be obtained, and the small pores could prevent the enzyme from surfactant in the environment. According to the result of the stimulating washing process, the encapsulated enzymes had a higher cleaning effect compared to the untreated enzyme solution, indicating that this method should be a possible method for enzyme encapsulation in liquid detergent. We believe this method is helpful to explore enzyme-contained liquid detergent with great market potentials.

14304619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304619.value: This research project has been successfully accomplished by our group. A series of engineered colloidosomes were synthesized and characterized based on Pickering emulsions stabilized by a binary mixture of particles including particles with different functional groups, opposite charges, opposite wettabilities (i.e., they are hydrophilic or hydrophobic) or softness. The as-prepared colloidosomes were then applied to the encapsulation of laundry-relevant enzymes, in which their encapsulation properties, long-term enzymatic activity and washing performance of the liquid detergent containing the enzyme-loaded colloidosomes were examined. This project has generated a total of 18 high-quality publications in the colloid, surface chemistry and material science fields. The obtained results have been presented in several international and regional conferences. This project has trained 2 PhD and 1 MPhil students.

14304619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304619.value: In this project, a series of engineered colloidosomes were synthesized and characterized based on Pickering emulsions stabilized by a binary mixture of particles. By dissolving laundry-relevant enzymes in the aqueous phase, we demonstrated that the enzymes were encapsulated in the capsules and been effectively protected from the liquid detergent environment. This method of encapsulation does not require any tedious preparation of particle stabilizers and can be extended to the entrapping and protecting of sensitive water base ingredients with high activity, such as biomolecules. We believe that the proposed method for fabrication of engineered colloidosomes can also be used effectively in food, drug, cosmetic, and personal care industries, which often require encapsulation of sensitive biomaterials. In long run, it is worth to study the feasibility of replacing the hydrophobic fume silica and protein stabilizers by biocompatible particles such as polylactic acid particles and other bio-based colloids, including polysaccharides in order to explore a wide application of the as-prepared colloidosomes.

14304619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304619.value: Enzyme-containing products account for more than 80% of the total laundry detergent market in the world. In the past two decades, consumer preference has gradually shifted from solid laundry detergent to liquid detergents because of increased convenience for the consumer and the lack of solubility issues. This is particularly true in Asian regions, where the use of low wash temperatures is popular. However, liquid laundry products impose a challenge when developing enzyme-containing detergents with satisfactory storage stability because in the liquid phase (e.g., water), enzymes are susceptible to a wide range of degradative pathways, oxidation, and proteolysis through their interactions with surfactants, bleaches, and other additives in common detergent formulations. The storage of liquid detergents comprising enzymes and surfactants, even over short periods, results in a loss of their cleaning benefits. In this project, we have developed a novel encapsulation technique to prepare engineered colloidosomes containing the most commonly used laundry-relevant enzymes, and extended their potential application in laundry detergent formulations. The outcome of this research may lead to a new formulation for making liquid laundry detergents.

14304719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14304719.value: Nonlinear problems arise in many applications. Most of these are of multiscale nature as they are typically posed in heterogeneous domains and different components of the solutions interact each other over various scales. Solving these problems directly require very large computational time and memory, as many degrees of freedoms are needed to resolve the solution. Thus, developing upscaling methods, that are robust and accurate, is an important research topic for many application areas including material sciences, membrane applications, groundwater hydrology, petroleum engineering, geothermal reservoir and so on. The purpose of upscaling methods is to construct reduced order systems so that only the essential coarse components of the solutions are computed, and the computational efficiency is therefore improved. Existing upscaling techniques are designed for linear multiscale problems. They are typically based on the solutions of some local problems and on the fact that the solution of the multiscale problem can be represented linearly by these local solutions. Extensions of these linear methods to nonlinear multiscale problems give only very limited accuracy or even impossible. In this project, our focus is to develop a general nonlinear upscaling framework for nonlinear multiscale problems. One key component of the methodology is macroscopic variable. These variables typically represent important coarse scale features that have nonlocal effects. It is well-known that one macroscopic variable per coarse region is not enough for most practical situations. We will develop a systematic approach to identify multiple local macroscopic variables, in the spirit of multicontinuum approaches. Another important component of our proposed nonlocal upscaling operator is the construction of a downscale function, which can be seen as a reconstruction of a fine scale function having a given set macroscopic values. It also satisfies a localization property, so that it can be computed only on some local oversampled regions. This downscale function provides an important bridge to connect macroscopic variables in a nonlinear and nonlocal way. Our proposed nonlinear upscaled model is then constructed using these local downscale functions. The resulting upscaled model gives a relation of macroscopic variables and gives solutions that satisfy important conservation properties. The proposed research provides a new nonlinear upscaling method for many "real-world" nonlinear multiscale problems. Our novel techniques avoid the concept of linearity, and provide reduced models using a nonlinear construction. We expect that our methodology will provide a brand new way to obtain upscaled models for nonlinear multiscale problems. 非線性問題在許多應用中出現。其中大多數具有多尺度性質，因為它們通常在異構域中構成，並且解決方案的不同組件在不同尺度上相互作用。直接解決這些問題需要非常大的計算時間和內存，因為解決該解決方案需要很多自由度。因此，開發強大而準確的升級方法是許多應用領域的重要研究課題，包括材料科學，膜應用，地下水水文學，石油工程，地熱儲層等。升級方法的目的是構造降階系統，以便僅計算解的基本粗分量，從而提高計算效率。現有的升級技術是針對線性多尺度問題而設計的。它們通常基於一些局部問題的解決方案以及多尺度問題的解決方案可以通過這些本地解決方案線性地表示的事實。這些線性方法對非線性多尺度問題的擴展僅提供非常有限的精度甚至是不可能的。 在這個項目中，我們的重點是為非線性多尺度問題開發一個通用的非線性升級框架。該方法的一個關鍵組成部分是宏觀變量。這些變量通常代表具有非局部效應的重要粗尺度特徵。眾所周知，對於大多數實際情況，每個粗糙區域的一個宏觀變量是不夠的。我們將根據多連續性方法的精神，開發一種系統的方法來識別多個局部宏觀變量。我們提出的非局部放大算子的另一個重要組成部分是構建縮減函數，它可以看作是具有給定集合宏觀值的精細尺度函數的重建。它還滿足本地化屬性，因此只能在某些本地過採樣區域上計算。這種縮減功能為以非線性和非局部方式連接宏觀變量提供了重要的橋樑。然後使用這些局部縮減函數構建我們提出的非線性放大模型。得到的放大模型給出了宏觀變量的關係，並給出了滿足重要保護特性的解決方案。 所提出的研究為許多“現實世界”非線性多尺度問題提供了一種新的非線性升尺度方法。我們的新技術避免了線性概念，並使用非線性結構提供簡化模型。我們希望我們的方法論能夠提供一種全新的方法來獲得非線性多尺度問題的升級模型。

14304819.label: Realisation of objectives
14304819.value: This is the completion report of GRF14304819. This funding support was originally secured by the PI, Prof. Xiaoshui PENG, in 2019. In mid 2020, Prof. PENG relocated to The Chinese University of Hong Kong - Shenzhen, to continue his academic career. This project was transferred to Prof. Henry N. C. WONG at that time. Prof. Henry N. C. WONG retired in mid 2021 and then transferred this project to the current PI, Prof. Fuk Yee KWONG (while Prof. Henry N. C. WONG serves as the Co-I of this project). With the support of this funding, the project team was able to achieve the first total synthesis of cryptotrione from commercially available homoveratric acid in a diastereoselective and diastereo-divergent manner. This synthetic protocol features with a novel platinum(IV) chloride-catalyzed diastereoselective cycloisomerization of 1,5-enynes to construct the bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane core, a Lewis acid-induced diastereoselective polyene cyclization, and a stereo-divergent conjugate addition to construct the tertiary carbon center of the side chain with full stereocontrol. The stereogenic tertiary carbon center in the side chain was installed in a diastereodivergent manner by conjugate addition reactions. These synthetic methodology were employed for synthesizing other entities of the structurally unprecedented cryptotrione family and its analogs for possible biological evaluation. Part of these notable results were published in Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. in 2020. (Angewandte Chemie-International Edition 2020, 59 (45), 19929-19933; DOI: 10.1002/anie.202009255). Moreover, during the COVID-19 situation, the research team members conducted relevant literature overview, and summarized the most updated enyne cycloisomerization and polyene cyclization reactions. This result was published in Synlett in 2021. (Synlett 2021, 32 (18), 1796-1815; DOI: 10.1055/a-1472-4594). In addition to intended total synthesis via a polyene strategy, the research team was able to develop iron-catalyzed cross-coupling protocols for generating the relevant polyene or -yne substrates. This finding was published in Organic Letters in 2021. (Organic Letters 2021, 23 (11), 4385-4390; DOI: 10.1021/acs.orglett.1c01318). The introduction of the -yne moiety towards the non-activated C-H bond was also found successful. This additional finding was published in Org. Chem. Front. in 2022. (Organic Chemistry Frontiers 2022, 9 (13), 3438-3445; DOI: 10.1039/d2qo00584k). Relevant review articles were also contributed by our research team. (Organic & Biomolecular Chemistry 2023, 21 (30), 6083-6095. DOI: 10.1039/d2sc05475b, and Chemical Science 2023, 14 (6), 1342-1362. DOI: 10.1039/d2sc05475b).

14304819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14304819.value: The intriguing structure and potential bioactivities of cryptotrione, a novel C35-terpene with an unprecedented skeleton possessing an abietane diterpene together with a unique spiro-bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane sesquiterpene, have attracted our attention. Since there were no total syntheses reported, we have conducted synthetic studies towards the total synthesis of cryptotrione. From commercially available homoveratric acid, the key intermediate with all cyclic backbone of cryptotrione was constructed successfully in 25 longest linear steps. The key feature of this synthetic work included: (1) The first discovery of a gold(I) catalyzed intramolecular cascade reaction of 1,5-enyne benzyl ether triggered by a 1,6-hydride transfer/cyclization. (2) A substrate controlled diastereoselective formation of bicyclo[3.1.0] moiety by platinum (IV) catalyzed 1,5-enyne isomerization was successfully disclosed; (3) The construction of the abietane-type skeleton of cryptotrione by utilizing a Lewis acid induced diastereoselective polyene cyclizaiton. It is possible for us to develop the divergent synthesis of other members of cryptotrione family employing this strategy.

14304819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14304819.value: Inspired by the hypothetical biogenetic pathway for the cryptotrione family, we proposed and validated a modified biomimetic approach involving metal-catalyzed cycloisomerization of enyne species and biomimetic transformation. This methodology may be practical for the syntheses of other members in the intriguing cryptotrione family as well as other potential lead molecules for the understanding of their relevant biological action and biogenetically synthetic protocol in nature.

14304819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14304819.value: This research demonstrated the power and potential of an our proposed protocol to render scarce biologically active natural products containing the functionalized bridged bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane units readily available for chemical and biological investigations. Moreover, structural analysis of new compounds produced in this proposal have been carrying out and leading to a greater understanding of the fundamental chemistry involved. This project would also yield invaluable information about a range of novel synthetic reactions and also a novel route for the synthesis of bioactive compounds bearing the bicyclo[3.1.0]hexane skeleton. These synthetic works herein have broadened range of bioactive derivatives beyond those related to cryptotrione. The relevant SAR studies of synthetic intermediates and their analogs Have been investigated and evaluated for their relevant discovery of lead candidates, as well as for the study of their possible biological action and biogenetically synthetic protocol in nature.

14305019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305019.value: Landau-de Gennes 理論越來越多的被物理學家和數學家所關注。大量的研究工作集中在對平衡態的研究。這些平衡態，特別的平衡態中缺陷的結構，在對於液晶材料相位的研究中起到了至關重要的作用。1988年，一個特殊的徑向解被發現。這個解是單軸的。並且具有一個零態。這個解的數學特性一直到最近才被Lamy研究。除了徑向解外，在1989年，研究者們發現 Landau-de Gennes 理論中還具有另外一個平衡解。這個解具有雙軸結構。它的指標向量有一個拓撲度為1/2的缺陷。一直到2000年，第三個平衡解才被Gartland 和Mkaddem發現。這個解的結構更加複雜。數值分析的結果顯示它具備裂核結構。以上三個結構被認為是液晶理論裡面三個基本的結構。越來越多的研究者相信，在一些適當的環境裡面，徑向解是不穩定的。它會分歧出兩個更加穩定的平衡態。一個就是具有1/2缺陷的雙軸解。另一個就是具有裂核結構的解。我們這個研究項目的目的就是希望給出一個嚴格的數學理論去解釋上述的分歧現象。

14305019.label: Realisation of objectives
14305019.value: All the objectives of the project were achieved. Here I briefly explain the process of how PI managed the project. The proposal for this project was prepared in October 2018. During the preparation of the proposal, PI read large number of articles related to the topics in the proposal. Some ideas and basic technical tools were already for solving the project's problems. Based on the numerical work of Gartland-Mkaddem (2000), PI decided to investigate the project's problems using the vector Signorini method. This idea was new at the time. To test whether the method worked, PI started solving the problems of the project as soon as the proposal was submitted. Between October 2018 and May 2019, PI worked intensively on the problems related to the fourth and fifth objectives of the project. For the spherical droplets, PI successfully found the harmonic maps with ring and split-core disclinations using the vector Signorini method. This is an important result. Without hesitation, PI submitted the article to Arxiv. You can read the manuscript at the following link: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1905.01638. Since the work of Penzenstadler-Trebin (1989), the problem of understanding the different types of disclinations in liquid crystals has been open to experts for a long time. Therefore, our work attracted the interest of mathematicians as soon as it was published on Arxiv. Soon after our work, Dipasquale-Millot-Pisante published a series of papers on related topics. In their second paper, they wrote that: "even if weakened and even if valid only in a restricted class, the conclusion of [60] remains very interesting because no rigorous result was previously known for the ball with the constant norm hedgehog on the boundary, which is by far the most interesting and representative case considered in literature." The article [60] cited above is my paper submitted to Arxiv in May 2019. It exceeds PI's expectations that the problem can be solved so smoothly and recognized quickly by experts in the field. This makes the work a great success. However, PI has decided to publish the work in May 2019, 7 months before the start of the project. Support from the current project cannot be announced in the final publication. See the publication at the link: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00205-020-01505-7 PI clarifies that the problem solved in this paper was conducted after the submission of the proposal. It was finished in April 2019. But no declaration of the work conducted was submitted to RGC during proposal update in April 2019. The main reason is that PI thought that the results in this paper are about spherical droplets and with restrictions on the symmetry of the solutions. The results in the fouth and fifth objectives should be valid for the axisymmetric solutions on general domains. More details of the solutions, even for the spherical droplets, should be investigated, e.g. the locations of split-core segment. These are the most important and challenging topics that PI plans to study in the objectives 4 and 5 in the proposal. Indeed, PI spent almost 3 years in the project to extend the results in this submitted paper from the spherical droplets to the droplets with general shape. More details will be given later. After the start of the project, PI began to investigate the limiting process from the original Landau-de Gennes theory to the theory of harmonic maps. This topic is related to the first, second, third, and sixth objectives of the project. For spherical droplets and in the low-temperature regime, PI and his PhD student Ho-Man Tai finally found solutions in the original Landau-de Gennes theory, which also has ring and split-core disclinations. See the article: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0022123623000800 In this long paper, we have systematically analyzed objectives 1, 2, 3, and 6 of the project. Our analysis illustrates the behavior of the solutions within the core regions, which was unknown in the field before our paper. The work introduced several new ideas, e.g. vector Signorini method, multiplicity-one property of zero locations, and blow-down argument for axially symmetric maps. PI would like to point out that the domain of the above work is a spherical droplet. In the remaining time of the project, PI has made great efforts to extend the results to general domains. In addition, the above work deals with the energy minimizing solutions. In general, the number and locations of singularities are not easy to determine. Inspired by the work of Brezis-Coron-Lieb and Lin, PI and his collaborators have developed a new approach to study the problem of prescribed singularities in the limiting Landau-de Gennes theory. The topics in the fourth and fifth objectives of our project are investigated on the general axisymmetric domains. This result improves the former work which was finished in April 2019 from the spherical droplet to any general axisymmetric domains. However, due to the time limit, this work cannot be published before the end of the project. At the time PI is preparing the completion report of this project, the work on the prescribed singularities is almost complete. It has taken PI and his collaborators almost 3 years to finalize the manuscript. The paper will be submitted to Arxiv as soon as it is available. Support for the current project will also be announced in the preprint and final publication, even though the paper will not be finalized until after the project is complete.

14305019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305019.value: In 1988, Schopohl-Sluckin found the radial hedgehog solutions in the Landau-de Gennes theory when the domain was a standard ball. Soon after, in 1989, Penzenstadler-Trebin showed that the radial hedgehog solutions are unstable in some parameter regimes. The core of the radial hedgehog solution can be split horizontally into a half-degree ring disclination. In around 2000, the third structure was discovered by Gartland-Mkaddem. We can also split the core of the hedgehog solution vertically to get the split-core structure of strength one. Before my work, these results were only confirmed by numerical studies. See also the work of Pingwen Zhang. Since 2018, PI started thinking about this 30-year-old open problem. In two publications, the ring and split-core disclinations are theoretically confirmed in both the limiting and non-limiting cases and for the ball-shaped droplets. A new approach is introduced. Indeed, we successfully introduced the vector Signorini method, by which two different solutions can be bifurcated from the hedgehog solution. One has a half-degree ring disclination, while the other has a split-core segment disclination on the rotating axis. Moreover, to study the non-limiting case, we need to understand the non-degeneracy of the zero of the order parameter. To achieve this goal, we prove a Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality. With this inequality, we can show the uniqueness of the zero of the order parameter in a given core region. Moreover, the multiplicity of the zero is equal to one. Similar multiplicity one problem has also been studied by Chodosh-Mantoulidis and Guaraco-Marques-Neves for the Allen-Cahn model. In the second half of the project, PI began to study the problems in this project on general axisymmetric domains. Based on the work of Brezis-Coron-Lieb, Prof. Lin investigated the prescribed singularities for axially symmetric harmonic maps into a 2-sphere. Inspired by the work of Lin, PI and his collaborators extended the relaxed energy used by Brezis-Coron-Lieb from the 2-sphere to the 4-sphere. The harmonic maps into the 4-sphere with prescribed singularities are constructed. This work is almost complete and we will publish it on Arxiv first when it is ready.

14305019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305019.value: Through this project, PI builds up several new ideas and tools to find solutions in the Landau-de Gennes theory with ring and split-core disclinations. In application, there are some similar and related models in biology and physics. The Cahn-Hilliard model is a popular model used to describe the phase separation of a binary fluid. What's more, it can also model the pores of codimension two and the micelles of codimension three. Recently, the Cahn-Hilliard model has been coupled with the Landau-de Gennes theory to describe active nematics. This is an interesting direction. Several transitions from active and passive domains are numerically investigated. The current studies on the ring and split-core disclinations can be extended to this complex model. On the other hand, the slow motion of monopoles in the Yang-Mills-Higgs theory was studied by Stuart in 1994, with the method of energy modulation. The solutions found in this project can be viewed as stationary solutions of the hydrodynamical Beris-Edward system. In the next stage, we can extend the approach of Stuart on the Yang-Mills-Higgs theory to the Beris-Edward system, and study the motion of disclinations. The motion of split-core disclinations might be a good starting point.

14305019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305019.value: This project is completed with great success. In the project, PI solved a 30-year-old open problem in the field of liquid crystal materials. The results and approaches obtained in this project have also attracted the attention of both mathematicians and physicists. Because of the results obtained in the project, PI received the Mr. and Mrs. Joseph W N Cheung Research Excellence Award in 2022. This is a recognition of PI's contribution. In recent years, more and more attention has been drawn to free boundary problems of vector-valued unknowns. See the recent survey by Figalli. PI believes that a new wave of studies on obstacle problems will revive. Physically, many properties of the disclinations of liquid crystals were only understood by experiments and numerical studies. The mechanism of how these disclinations are formulated is not quite clear. This project provides theoretical explanations to the following questions: 1. why is the radial hedgehog solution unstable; 2. how can we bifurcate more stable solutions from the radial hedgehog one; 3. how do the liquid crystals behave near their disclinations? These questions now have a new understanding from the mathematical point of view.

14305219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305219.value: The proposed project will develop new electrophilic reactions of pi-character carbon–carbon bonds with Lewis base-activated hypervalent iodine. Difunctionalized molecules are very useful building blocks in medicinal chemistry and organic synthesis. The electrophilic functionalization of unsaturated compounds/strained three- and four-membered rings is useful for affording 1,1-, 1,2-, 1,3- and 1,4-difunctionalized molecules. Hypervalent iodine reagents (HIR), due to their reduced toxicity and hypervalency, have been identified as valuable and important alternatives to transition metals in electrophilic functionalization reactions. Lewis or Brønsted acid activators are often used to achieve high reaction efficiency and selectivity in HIR-mediated electrophilic functionalization reactions. For cases using in situ-generated HIR, two key components are typically involved: 1) an oxidant such as mCPBA, oxone, sodium perborate, hydrogen peroxide, etc., and 2) an acidic reaction medium such as TFA. The downsides of these acidic, oxidizing conditions are the limited compatibility of the oxidants with specific substrates and the poor survival of acid-sensitive substrates. Thus, an efficient and practical method that is reactive and complementary to the acid-promoted electrophilic HIR difunctionalization of unsaturated compounds/strained cycloalkanes is highly desirable. Recently, our research group has developed a facile and efficient system for regio- and chemoselective electrophilic functionalization of cyclopropanes (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2018, 57, 3782–3786) using Lewis base-activated HIR. This approach can eliminate the need for strong oxidant and acidic reaction media. However, so far, the substrate scope has been limited to the intermolecular oxidative dioxygenation of cyclopropanes. In addition, the asymmetric variants using the Lewis base-activated HIR system remain unknown. We rationalize that the Lewis base catalytic protocol can also be applied to the difunctionalization of unsaturated compounds and other strained cycloalkanes. Moreover, we envision that the asymmetric versions of reactions can be achieved by using chiral Lewis bases as promoters to activate achiral HIR. In a recent unpublished preliminary study, we demonstrated that Lewis base-activated HIR can efficiently promote the difunctionalization of olefins and cyclobutanes. In addition, the asymmetric variants can be achieved by using chiral Lewis base promoters. In the proposed project, we will carry out a systematic investigation of the electrophilic difunctionalization reactions of pi-character carbon–carbon bonds with various Lewis base-activated HIR. 14305219.label: Realisation of objectives
14305219.value: 1. To design and prepare Lewis basic organocatalysts for electrophilic reactions using hypervalent iodine reagents (HIR) At the initial stage of study, a range of hard Lewis bases including amines and soft Lewis bases including sulfides and selenides were prepared. Different substituents were incorporated to these Lewis bases in order to control the steric and electronic properties. These catalysts were then mixed with hypervalent iodine reagents (HIRs) including the commonly used diacetoxyl iodobenzene (DIB) and the more reactive compound phenyliodine(III) bis(trifluoroacetate) (PIFA) to examine the complexes. The weak or bulky bases was no favorable in binding with the HIRs. On the other hand, the strong bases bind tightly with HIR, leading to diminishment of the reactivity of the HIR species. Thus, Lewis bases with moderate basicity were found to be suitable in activating HIRs and benzamide was found to be the optimal one. 2. To explore novel protocols for electrophilic reactions of pi-character carbon–carbon bonds using HIR a) Lewis base catalyzed difunctionalization of olefins After studying different Lewis bases, difunctionalization of olefins was then studied. In general, the allyl-type substrates worked well in this protocol and gave the corresponding diols with moderate-to-good yields. We extended the substrate scope to styrene type substrates and achieved satisfactory isolated yields of the diols. In particular, the relatively inert substrates bearing electron-withdrawing groups can also be converted to the corresponding diols using our protocol. Then, we tried the substrates bearing oxidant-sensitive aldehyde that was intolerant in the typical methods (e.g. in situ generated HIRs involving inorganic oxidants or peracetic acids). Apart from the monosubstituted substrates, we also extended the substrate scope to disubstituted one; trans-stilbene can be converted to the corresponding diol in a moderate isolated yield with 6:1 ratio of dl- and meso-isomer. Interestingly, it was realized that styrene derivatives could be transformed into anti-Markovnikov methyl acetal products using 4-tosylamide as the Lewis base catalyst in the solvent blend MeOH/CH2Cl2. Styrenes bearing a range of substituents including ether, ester, silyl ethers, OBoc, and NHBoc were well-tolerated under the reaction conditions and gave the corresponding methyl acetal products with good yields and excellent regioselectivity. Several experiments were conducted in order to shed light on the mechanistic picture. Based on the NMR study, it was found that PIFA exists in equilibrium with its dimer in solution phase and the dimer is an inactive species towards electrophilic reaction. Addition of the Lewis base catalyst benzamide coordinates to the iodine center of PIFA to give the amide-PIFA adduct, hence driving the equilibrium to the monomer side. The polarized hypervalent iodine center as a result of the ammonium moiety might enhance the electrophilicity of the iodine center towards electrophilic reaction. Olefin’s pi-electron might then interact with the HIR to give the iodoiranium-like species together with the elimination of the benzamide. Trifluoroacetate anion might then substitute the iodoiramium species in a Markovnikov fashion, followed by the degradation of the hypervalent iodine via substitution by another trifluoroacetate gave the desired product. b) Difunctionalization of olefinic substrates under ball-milling conditions After the successful development of the Lewis base-catalyzed difunctionalization of olefins, we further studied the reaction with ball-milling under solvent-free condition so that the reaction could proceed in a greener manner. Unexpectedly, the reaction could proceed without catalyst. In addition, 1,3-difunctionalization instead of 1,2-difunctionalization was found to happen more readily. Such reaction involves the intermolecular reaction of two molecules of olefinic substrates. The reaction system as found to be generally applicable to styrene substrates bearing electron-donating or withdrawing substituents. A study on the enantioselective deoxygenation of styrene was performed using sub-stoichiometric amount of chiral iodine compound and mCPBA as the stoichiometric oxidant in order to in situ generate the corresponding hypervalent iodine species. To our delight, the desired 1,3-diol product was obtained with good enantioselectivity. In addition, we explored the applicability of this mechanochemical PIFA reaction protocol. Thus, styrene was used as the substrate and treated with an equivalent of molecular iodine and PIFA under ball-milling conditions, after which the reaction was quenched with ammonia. This afforded a 38% yield of 1,4-iodoalcohol as a single diastereomer together with some diols. To further exemplify the synthetic utility of this approach, the natural product calyxolane A was synthesized in two steps from styrene. Typical synthesis of calyxolane A requires multiple steps and low overall yield was obtained. In contrast, the ball-milling protocol furnished calyxolane A in 2 steps with 30% overall yield. Based on the mechanistic studies, it was found that the preference of 1,3-difunctionalization could not be achieved by simply mixing the reactants under neat condition. As a result, the mechanical force played a crucial role for the selective 1,3-difunctionalization. Based on various spectroscopic studies including XRD, NMR, and IR experiments, it was found that PIFA might dimerize at solid state. Since the sigma-hole at the iodine of PIFA is occupied in the dimer, the PIFA-dimer should be inactive towards functionalization of olefin. The PIFA-dimer might slowly degrade and gave a small amount of active monomeric PIFA, which is the key for the chemoselective 1,3-difunctionalization. c) Intermolecular 1,3-difunctionalization of cyclopropanes Concurrently, we also investigated the reaction with halogen, which has a similar reaction mechanism to that of hypervalent iodine. Electrophilic halogenation of the pi-character carbon–carbon bonds in cyclopropanes gives rise to 1,3-difunctionalized compounds that are useful building blocks. While 1,3-difunctionalization of cyclopropanes via cyclization reactions have been demonstrated in literature, the difunctionalization of unactivated cyclopropanes via intermolecular electrophilic halogenation remains less exploited and has been an attractive research area. We have found that cyclopropylbenzene was converted to beta-haloformate in 55% yield and excellent regioselectivity (Markovnikov product) at room temperature. Higher reaction yields were obtained using 1,3-dibromo-5,5-dimethylhydantoin as the halogen source. The substrate scope of the bromoesterification reaction of cyclopropane was investigated. Good conversion and regioselectivity were generally observed. The reactions were also found to be compatible with substrates bearing various electron-withdrawing and electron-donating substituents. Apart from monosubstituted cyclopropanes, we also extended the substrate scope to a 1,1-disubstituted cyclopropane, (1-methylcyclopropyl)benzene. Instead of DMF, the use of N,N-dimethylbutyramide yielded the corresponding butyl ester product thought the efficiency was moderate. The 1,2-disubstituted substrate cis-1,2-diphenylcyclopropane was also converted into 3-bromo-1,3-diphenylpropyl formate with a good diastereoselectivity. Further study revealed that the methanol could be used as the reaction partner, giving the bromoether as the product. Substrates with various substituents were also compatible with the protocol. Similar to the bromoesterification, bromoethers were obtained smoothly using the corresponding disubstituted substrates. When ethylene glycol was used in place of methanol in the bromoetherification, the desired mono-functionalized product was obtained in 95% yield and no dimerized product was observed. Di- and trisubstituted cyclopropanes were well-tolerated. Spiro substrate was also found to be compatible to the reaction. Mechanistic studies indicate that the solvent DMF has multiple roles. Other than dissolving the reactants, DMF was found to also act as a Lewis base in the activation of the electrophilic halogen. After the formation of the bromiranium active intermediate, DMF could act as a nucleophile to open the bromorianium-like intermediate and give the desired 1,3-difunctionalized products. 3. To publish the results of the HIR-promoted electrophilic reactions in high-impact peer-reviewed journals Under this project, a number of high-impact publications were produced. The detail appears in Part C. Overall, all objectives have been fully realized and a summary of the major research outcomes is shown below.

14305219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305219.value: 1. 1,2-Diols are extremely useful building blocks in the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and natural products. Vicinal dioxygenation of olefins is a straightforward way to prepare 1,2-diols, and many useful methods have been developed and widely used to date. However, typical methods frequently involve toxic metallic reagents. Hypervalent iodine reagents are useful for the vicinal dihydroxylation of olefins to give 1,2-diols under metal-free conditions but strongly acidic promoters are often required. We have successfully developed a reaction protocol using PIFA as an oxidant and benzamide as a Lewis base promoter for the vicinal dioxygenation of olefins to give their respective 1,2-diols. The protocol is compatible with acid-sensitive and oxidant-sensitive substrates. Besides, a substrate scope is also given for converting styrene derivatives to terminal methyl acetals using the Lewis base activated HIR in good yields. 2. Mechanochemistry is a powerful technique for organic synthesis and has been identified by IUPAC as one of 10 emerging world-changing technologies in chemistry. In this research, a mechanochemical and solvent/catalyst-free functionalization of olefins with hypervalent iodine reagents has been developed, enabling the synthesis of 1,3-dioxygenated compounds. Under similar reaction conditions with the addition of molecular iodine, 1,4-iodoalcohols can be synthesized. These valuable products are non-trivial to achieve via standard solution phase methods. Mechanistic study reveals that the hypervalent iodine reagent might dimerize at solid state with the help of mechanical force. The active monomeric form of hypervalent iodine reagent might trigger the 1,3-and 1,4-difunctionalization reactions in an intermolecular cascade manner. In literature, ball-milling transformations with hypervalent iodine reactions are merely improved versions of known solution phase reactions. This report represents the first case of ball-milling hypervalent iodine chemistry that leads to different selectivity from that of solution phase reaction. 3. 1,3-difunctionalization of cyclopropane is an useful organic transformation. The corresponding 1,3-difunctionalized products are synthetic synthons and building blocks in many organic syntheses. Many existing ring-opening difunctionalization methodologies rely primarily on the use of donor-acceptor cyclopropanes, while the difunctionalization of unactivated cyclopropanes is less exploited. In this research, 1,3-bromoesterification and 1,3-bromoetherification of unactivated cyclopropanes were successfully achieved using N-bromosuccinimide as the brominating agent with high yields and regioselectivity. The reaction is mild, efficient, and regioselective. The methodology features advantages including broad substrate scope and products being possible 1,3-difunctionalized synthons to other biologically essential organic molecules. Mechanistic studies indicate that the solvent DMF is also a good Lewis base in activating the electrophile.

14305219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305219.value: Hypervalent iodine reagents are very useful in various organic transformations. These reactions can be operated under metal-free conditions and they have attracted much attention from synthetic chemistry. However, in many cases strong acids or metal promotors are needed. In some occasions, harsh reaction conditions are needed and problems such as poor functional group compatibility are encountered. In this study, Lewis bases are used as the promoters to activate the hypervalent iodine reagents and the reactions can be operated under mild conditions. The catalytic protocol can be applied to the synthesis of the valuable 1,2-diol building blocks. In addition, it was unexpected to realize that under ball-milling conditions, 1,3-difunctionalization occurred and it is otherwise hard to be achieved using conventional methods. Under similar reaction conditions with the addition of molecular iodine, 1,4-iodoalcohols can be synthesized. These valuable products are non-trivial to achieve via standard solution phase methods. In future, we will further explore the applications of Lewis base-promoted functionalization of unsaturated substrates using hypervalent iodine reagents. Since it is also realized that mechanochemical force has special effect on the chemistry with hypervalent iodine reagents, we will also extend the development of electrophilic reactions using mechanochemical forces.

14305219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305219.value: Many chemical manufacturing processes are energy- and atom-inefficient, leading to the generation of significant amount of wastes and emissions. To meet the growing demand on energy for the global economy, it becomes more important than ever to look for green alternatives of energy-efficient processes. However, the current state of technology lags behind the schedule to meet the international targets. Small molecule catalysts are considered as nanoscale molecular machines that can provide control in various transformations at molecular level. It is obvious that catalytic processes play a key role in improving air and water quality, reduce energy consumption and emission, and offer solutions to long-term sustainable energy and environmental protection. In the current project, we have developed a number of useful transformations using hypervalent iodine reagents and Lewis base catalysts under mild and metal-free conditions. We have also identified that the reactions can be operated using mechanical force and unique chemoselectivity has been achieved. Our works on the development of novel methodologies provide very useful tools for various transformations. The research endeavor results in the synthesis of a wide range of useful building blocks for various medicinal and chemical applications.

14305319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305319.value: The aim of this project is to develop statistical methods for joint estimation of a set of phylogenetic trees. A phylogenetic tree displays the evolutionary relationships within a group of organisms. The past three decades have witnessed extensive research into the construction of a single phylogenetic tree with DNA sequence data. In recent years, more and more clinicians have collected samples from multiple tumor sites from a single cancer patient to conduct multi-region sequencing; meanwhile, single-cell sequencing technologies allow researchers to simultaneously measure the genomic profiles of hundreds of individual cells from a single patient. As a result, a phylogenetic tree can be constructed for each patient to understand the evolutionary history of the cells within that person. Consequently, it is now of great interest to analyze the phylogenetic trees of various patients to better understand cancer mechanisms. However, statistical methods for joint estimation of multiple phylogenetic trees for multiple patients are lacking. Aligning tree topologies across patients is challenging. On the one hand, patients can share some common cell types such as white blood cells, red blood cells, and T cells. On the other hand, patients can also have distinct cell types. For example, patient A's cancer cells may originate from white blood cells, whereas those of patients B and C may have evolved from T cells. Therefore, a two-stage approach of first estimating a separate phylogenetic tree for each patient and then comparing the learned trees is not ideal. In this project, we propose a Bayesian framework to simultaneously learn multiple phylogenetic trees for a group of patients, remove the technical artifacts that arise from measuring various patients separately, assign each sample from each patient to a cell type, and identify the genomic profile for each cell type. Our proposed framework naturally aligns the tree topologies across patients despite the potential different numbers of cell types among patients. For posterior inference, we will develop efficient parallel Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms and provide them as a free software package. We will apply the developed method to publicly available datasets and to the Hong Kong Liver Cancer Genome project. This project will solve cutting-edge statistical inference problems in cancer genomics and will make profound contributions to statistical modeling, statistical computing, parallel programming, phylogenetics and cancer genomics. The scientific discoveries from this project will enhance our understandings of disease mechanisms and ultimately aid the development of personalized medicine in Hong Kong and elsewhere. 該項目旨在開發聯合估計一組進化樹的統計方法。 進化樹表示一群物種之間的進化關係。在過去三十年，人們對如何用DNA序列數據構建一棵進化樹進行了廣泛的研究。 近年來，越來越多的臨床醫生從單個癌症患者的多個腫瘤部位採集樣本進行多區域測序；同時，單細胞測序技術使研究人員能夠同時測量來自一個患者的數百個細胞的基因組譜。因此，我們現在可以為每個患者構建一顆進化樹來理解該患者體內細胞的進化歷史。為了更好地了解癌症的機制，如何同時分析不同患者的進化樹變成一個非常關鍵的問題。 然而，現在對於不同患者同時構建多個進化樹的統計方法還很匱乏。比較不同患者之間的進化樹非常困難。一方面，不同患者可以共同擁有一些常見的細胞類型，如白細胞，紅細胞和T細胞。另一方面，患者也可以擁有各自特有的細胞類型。例如，患者A的癌細胞可以源自白細胞，而患者B和C的癌細胞則由T細胞進化而來。因此，首先為每個患者估計單獨的進化樹然後再比較所得進化樹的兩階段方法並不理想。 在這個項目中，我們提出了一個貝葉斯框架來同時為一組患者學習多個進化樹。我們提出的方法能去除由於分別測量不同患者所導致的技術誤差、將每個患者的每個細胞樣本歸類到一個細胞類型，並確定每種細胞類型的基因組特徵。儘管每個患者所擁有的細胞類型可能不同，但我們提出的框架能自動把不同患者的樹的拓撲結構進行對齊。我們將開發並行馬爾可夫鏈蒙特卡羅算法進行後驗統計推斷，並將它們實現為免費的軟件包。我們將把開發的方法應用於公開數據集和香港肝癌基因組計劃。 該項目將解決癌症基因組學中的前沿統計推斷問題，並將對統計建模、統計計算、並行計算、細胞進化和癌症基因組學作出重大貢獻。該項目的科學發現將加深我們對疾病機制的認識，並最終有助於香港及其他地方個性化醫療的發展。

14305319.label: Realisation of objectives
14305319.value: We have fully achieved the objectives of the proposal. The reference number is indexed according to the references listed in Part C. The first major challenge for learning phylogenetic trees for a set of patients using their gene expression data is the severe batch effect. Because of the batch effects, we cannot directly combine expression data from different subjects together to do clustering and learn the tree structure. With the wide adoption of single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) data, another big challenge is that some cell types may be missing for some patients. If we learn a single tree separately for each patient, then it would be very difficult to compare the learned trees across patients as different trees can have different number of leaf nodes. Therefore, it was an open question when we can combine scRNA-seq data collected from multiple patients with potential missing cell types and severe batch effects to do cell type clustering and learn phylogenetic trees for the learned cell types. In addition, the analysis of scRNA-seq data suffer from large numbers of missing data due to dropout events, overdispersed read counts and cell-specific size factors. In this project, we have developed a Bayesian hierarchical model BUSseq [1], which can simultaneously correct batch effects, cluster cell types, impute missing data caused by dropout events, and detect differentially expressed genes without requiring a preliminary normalization step. Based on the learned cell-type-specific mean expression profiles, we can construct a phylogenetic tree that contains all cell types observed in the dataset, make the resulting tree as the super tree and annotate the cell type proportions for each patient to the super tree [5]. As a result, the trees for different patients can be aligned and compared even if some tree branches are missing for some patients. We have further developed an efficient parallel Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm (MCMC) for posterior inference for the proposed model and implemented both a parallel CPU version https://github.com/songfd2018/BUSseq-1.0 and a parallel GPU version https://github.com/Anguscgm/BUSseq_gpu. The parallel CPU version has been further developed into a Bioconductor R package BUSseq https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/BUSseq.html, which has already been downloaded over 1,500 times. The reason for separating the cell type clustering with batch effects correction and tree learning into two steps rather than integrating them into a single Bayesian hierarchical model is the concern of computation time. In particular, as the numbers of cells in scRNA-seq studies approach the scale of hundreds of thousands or even millions, we find the current two-step approaches is computationally more efficient. Theoretically, we have developed techniques to prove the model identifiability and shown for the first time the requirements on experimental designs under which we can distinguish cell type effects from batch effects when the data suffer from severe batch effects and have missing cell types. Building upon the work, we have also developed a deep learning method, TAPE, to deconvolute bulk RNA-seq data by integrating bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq data [2]. The techniques we developed for the model identifiability proof for BUSseq by creating a linear mapping that maps a probability distribution to a function that shares a similar spirit as a probability generating function also enable us to prove the model identifiability for a mixed membership blockmodel developed for time-to-event data collected from a social network [3]. Noteworthy, although the mixed membership blockmodel for binary outcome has been widely used for modeling social network data, the proof for its identifiability is emerging only recently, let alone the results for time-to-event data collected from social networks, so we have tackled a challenging theoretical problem. Moreover, the analysis of multi-omics data collected from multi-region sequencing for liver cancer patients that motivated this project has revealed novel insights into the disease mechanism of liver cancer [4]. In addition, we have been collaborating with colleagues from Hong Kong Eye Hospital and Chinese Academy of Science in Shanghai to apply our developed method to scRNA-seq data to study eye diseases and sleep disorders. Due to the pandemic, the planned research trips were not carried out, and the conference attendance were mainly virtual. As a result, the actual expenditure is lower than the budget.

14305319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305319.value: With the emergence of multi-region sequencing and scRNA-seq experiments, researchers can now simultaneously measure the genomic profiles of multiple bulk samples or single cells for each patient. In principle, a phylogenetic tree can be constructed for each patient, and it is of great interest to compare the trees between patients. However, as different patients may have different cell types, if we construct trees separately for each patient, it would be very difficult to align and compare the trees across patients. On the other hand, if we directly pool data from all of the patients and learn a single tree, the resulting tree will fail to cluster cells of the same cell types together due to severe batch effects. To tackle the problem of missing cell types and batch effects, we have developed a Bayesian hierarchical model BUSseq to simultaneously correct batch effects and cluster cell types [1]. BUSseq allows some cell types to be missing from some patients. We mathematically prove that as long as the batch graph, in which each node represents a batch and two batches are linked by an edge if they share at least two cell types, is a connected graph, we can distinguish cell type effects from batch effects. The preliminary results of BUSseq and the experimental design of chain-type design were declared in the initial proposal and the proposal updates in April, 2019. Nevertheless, great theoretical advances were achieved during the paper revision, and we eventually proved the more general connected batch graph condition in publication [1]. For statistical inference, we have developed an efficient parallel MCMC algorithm and provided it as a Bioconductor R package. Based on the learned cluster-mean-expression profiles, we can construct a super tree which contains all the cell types existing in the dataset and annotate the cell type proportions of each individual patient [5]. Thus, our approach automatically aligns trees across patients and facilitates the comparison. BUSseq is applicable to both bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq data. Building upon the work, we have also developed a deep learning method to integrate bulk and scRNA-seq data [2]. The proof of the identifiability of BUSseq enables us to prove the identifiability for a mixed membership blockmodel developed for time-to-event data collected from a social network [3]. Moreover, the analysis of multi-omics data collected from multi-region sequencing that motivated this project has revealed novel insights into the disease mechanism of liver cancer [4].

14305319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305319.value: The parallel MCMC algorithm of BUSseq works well for hundreds of thousands of cells. Nevertheless, with the number of cells in scRNA-seq data approaching millions or even tens of millions, it would be of great interest to explore even more computationally efficient inference approaches, such as expectation maximization algorithms with stochastic updates or Variational Bayes, which we are currently working on.

14305319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305319.value: With the advancements in single-cell sequencing technologies, we can now measure the genomic profiles for hundreds or thousands of cells for each patient. In principle, we can construct a phylogenetic tree for each patient to understand the evolution of cells within that patient. However, it is very difficult to align and compare tree structures across patients as different patients may have different cell types so that the individual trees may have different numbers of nodes and topology. Moreover, pooling data from all the patients directly to cluster cells or learn a tree is impossible due to severe technical artifacts between patients. The technical artifacts can be comparable to or even larger than the cell type effects. In this project, we develop a novel statistical method to simultaneously adjust batch effects and cluster cell types. Consequently, we can learn a super tree that contains all the cell types in the dataset and annotate the cell type proportions of each individual to the super tree to obtain the individual tree. As a result, even if some individuals lack certain cell types, their tree structures can be compared to that of others. Our developed software package has been well received by the community.

14305419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305419.value: Drawing on inspirations from physics, gauge theories have been one of the most important tools in the modern study of low-dimensional topology. A fully-developed gauge theory is supposed to assign invariants to smooth 3- and 4-manifolds that fit into the ``TQFT'' framework proposed by Atiyah [A]. Two notable variants of gauge theories are the Yang-Mills (instanton) theory and the Seiberg-Witten (monopole) theory. A relation between the closed 4-manifold invariants from the two theories is conjectured by Witten [W] for a large class of 4-manifolds (those of ``Seiberg-Witten simple type''). Following an outline sketched in [PT], Feehan and Leness proved (in a series of long papers) Witten's conjecture for a large class of simply-connected closed 4-manifolds. An outstanding (and daunting) question is whether the aforementioned conjecture/partial results may be extended to the TQFT framework. In particular, the relation between the Floer homologies in the two theories, the instanton Floer homology and the monopole Floer homology, is presently far from understood. We propose to take some initial steps towards this problem. 所謂"規範理論" 是現代低微拓撲的重要工具之一。理論上，一個完整的規範理論對三維和四維流型定義了不變量。 這些不變量應該符合 Atiyah 的 “TQFT”。 Yang-Mills (SU(2) (or SO(3)) instanton) theory 和 Seiberg-Witten (monopole) theory 是兩個重要的規範理論。 Witten 的 猜想描述了這兩規範理論的閉四維流型不變量的關係； 這個猜想目前已經由 Feehan & Leness 證明了大部分的情形。我們希望推廣這個關係到整個TQFT， 而這個計劃的目的是這個長期目標的初步。

14305419.value: As stated in the research proposal, this is a long term project which will take longer than 3 years; especially, Objective 3 would most likely be the subject of a future project. The progress of this project is also delayed by difficulty of communication/discussions among collaborators, availability of suitable postdocs due to the pandemic, and the fact that all of us were busy with other projects. As the PI and her collaborators were not able to meet each other in conferences or research visits, we tried discussing online via Skype and emails. However, these methods proved inefficient. Objective 1: We computed the Seiberg-Witten invariants and the Donaldson invariant of some 4-manifolds of the form S^1x Y, and verified the Conjecture of Marinõ and Moore relating these two invariants in such cases. We also generalized the computation to some 4-manifolds which are mapping tori. More work will be needed to establish a relation in the general case. Objective 2: The author published a paper on Seiberg-Witten moduli spaces for general 4-manifolds with cylindrical ends. This result will be useful for computing Seiberg-Witten Floer homology. We made some progress on understanding the general properties of moduli spaces of PU(2) monopoles on 4-manifolds with cylindrical ends, and are working on the draft of a long article (which might eventually be split into several articles) on these results. However, it will take more work to construct (variants) of PU(2) monopole Floer homology. Objective 3: We formulated some conjectures. As expected, further research in this direction is left to a future project.

14305419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305419.value: Both the instanton Floer homology and the Seiberg-Witten Floer homology are important tools for the study of 3-manifolds. The instanton Floer homology is closely related to the fundamental group of 3-manifolds, which essentially determines the 3-manifold. Seiberg-Witten Floer homology, on the other hand, is better developed and much more computable via its relation to the Heegaard Floer homology, a result established by the PI and her coauthors. On the other hand, the relation between Donaldson and Seiberg-Witten invariants for a large class of closed 4-manifolds have been established by Feehan and Leness by studying PU(2) monopoles on closed 4-manifolds. Studying PU(2) monopoles on 4-dimensional manifolds with cylindrical ends should likewise help understanding the relation between instanton Fler homology and Seiberg-Witten Floer homology.

14305619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305619.value: The discovery of a particle compatible with the Higgs boson marked the beginning of a large effort to study its properties, its interactions with other particles and its potential deviations from the Standard Model (SM) expectations. The discovery was announced in 2012 by the ATLAS and the CMS collaborations at CERN (the European Organization for Nuclear Research) in the analysis of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), at center-of-mass energies of 7 and 8 TeV/c^2 [Cer12]. Subsequent studies [Ata13, Atb13, Cms13, Cms14] demonstrated that this particle is compatible with being a scalar, as predicted by the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism [Eng64]. The theoretical proposal and experimental discovery were recognized, among other awards, with the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics and the 2013 High Energy and Particle Physics Prize of the European Physical Society. After a shut-down period for maintenance and upgrades, the LHC resumed operations with an energy of 13 TeV/c^2, in a data-taking period called Run 2, which will end this year; after another long-shut-down period, Run 3 will start in 2021. Data from Run 2 and Run 3 will allow further measurements of the properties of the Higgs boson; in particular, searching for its decay into muon pairs, unobserved so far, will allow us to further probe the coupling of the Higgs boson to second-generation fermions, to test its proportionality to the muon mass, and to potentially reveal a discrepancy in a process sensitive to new physics. Hong Kong institutions, building over the solid foundation provided by the success of the Daya Bay Reactor Experiment, joined efforts as the Joint Consortium for Fundamental Physics in Hong Kong, which was accepted as a member of the ATLAS Collaboration in 2014. Currently many Hong Kong researchers and students are strongly involved in the analysis of LHC data. The goal of this project is to further strengthen this participation through work on the following areas: 1. Search for the decay of the SM Higgs boson into muon pairs in pp collisions in ATLAS 2. Study and update the ATLAS muon identification algorithms that are based on calorimeter information, in preparation for the additional detector systems and the data-taking conditions expected during Run 3. These areas are designed to complement other ongoing research activities of the Hong Kong ATLAS team to build a complete and solid physics program from Hong Kong institutions, with a significant impact and a long-term contribution to LHC Physics.

14305619.label: Realisation of objectives
14305619.value: Objective 1. Search for the decay of the SM Higgs boson into muon pairs in pp collisions in ATLAS. The discovery of the Higgs boson by the ATLAS and CMS collaborations at CERN [ATL12, CMS12] prompted a rich program of precision measurements and searches related to this particle that has been on the forefront of experimental high-energy physics. The search for discrepancies between data and the predictions of the Standard Model (SM) is one of the main goals of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) research program at CERN, and there are processes that currently can only be observed at the LHC (if at all); such is the case of the decay of the Higgs boson into muon pairs, which offers the opportunity to measure the Higgs coupling to second-generation fermions. The SM prediction for the corresponding branching ratio is (2.17±0.04)×10^(-4) [LHC16], which would put it at or below the current sensitivity of LHC experiments, but this number could be significantly enhanced by physics beyond the SM [VIG09, DER13]. Both the ATLAS and CMS collaborations have published searches for H→μμ using data from run 2 at the LHC, both with partial (around 36 fb^(-1)) and full datasets (around 140 fb^(-1)) [ATL17, ATL21, CMS19, CMS21]. As the period covered by this project corresponds to the end of a long LHC shutdown and the beginning of Run 3, we focused our attention on the use of the full Run 2 dataset to explore the potential improvements to this search in Run 3. Due to the relative simplicity of the final state under consideration (two isolated, oppositely charged muons), one of the most important areas to study and improve is the overall performance of single-muon identification and reconstruction. We have participated in Higgs boson measurements since the beginning of our work at LHC, and our group has made significant contributions to the four-lepton decay studies in ATLAS, which also relies heavily on the performance of muon reconstruction and identification. Building upon that experience, we have strengthened our involvement on muon monitoring and reconstruction infrastructure in ATLAS. Besides muon performance studies (and the work described in objective 2), we have explored the use of alternative classification strategies that could take advantage of the total integrated luminosity expected in Run 3, now under way. We have also studied the effect of training independent machine-learning-based classifiers against each one of the main backgrounds in each region of phase space, to be later consolidated into a single estimator. We have used similar strategies in the search for decays of the Higgs boson into lepton-flavor-violating final states that include muons, which resulted in a significant increase in sensitivity. Objective 2. Study the ATLAS muon identification algorithms that are based on calorimeter information, in preparation for the additional detector systems and the data-taking conditions expected during Run 3 of the LHC, and explore possible improvements for future updates. Since the beginning of our work with ATLAS, our group has been involved in the implementation, study, and improvement of muon identification algorithms. Before the beginning of this project, in collaboration with the ATLAS Muon Combined Performance (MCP) group, we studied and characterized the performance of the two algorithms used in ATLAS to identify muons using only tracking and calorimeter information and, based on those studies, we were able to modify and improve both algorithms. We explored the use of multivariate analysis techniques not contained in the ATLAS software, and developed tools to interface the ATLAS Software framework with publicly available machine learning systems (specifically TensorFlow [ABA15], Keras [CHO15] and PyTorch [PAS17]), to use novel machine learning techniques with our signal extraction methods. We studied the use of boosted decision trees, deep neural networks, and refinements in the neural network activation functions, to benefit from the different detector sensitivities available in different pseudorapidity and energy regions. Also, due to the various detector upgrades to be installed during the long shutdown 3 (LS3) towards the HL-LHC (High-Luminosity LHC), ATLAS is aiming for a homogenized detector description format. While the description of the muon MDT, RPC and Micromegas chambers was partially covered, the description of the sTGC and TGC chambers was fully uncovered. Our group has implemented the description of the sTGC chambers in the GeoModelXML format, and this description has been added to the ATLAS repository; we are also contributing to the integration of the NSW GeoModelXML description into the ATLAS simulation framework. Objective 3. Train Hong Kong students and postdocs for research in the forefront of fundamental physics. One postdoctoral research associate, two PhD students (Minlin Wu and Pan Tong), and two undergraduate students (Amit Singh and Ho Ching Luk) have worked on the project. This allowed them to benefit from the close interaction with colleagues from other ATLAS institutions (located both in Hong Kong and overseas), to work with recent machine learning and multivariate analysis techniques, to learn several of the tools used for research in High Energy Physics, and to work with recent proton-proton collision and Monte Carlo simulation data from the Large Hadron Collider on searches and measurements at the energy frontier.
