14305619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305619.value: A search for the dimuon decay of the Standard Model (SM) Higgs boson is performed using data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb−1 collected with the ATLAS detector in Run 2 proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV at the Large Hadron Collider. The observed (expected) significance over the background-only hypothesis for a Higgs boson with a mass of 125.09 GeV is 2.0σ (1.7σ). The observed upper limit on the cross section times branching ratio for pp → H → μμ is 2.2 times the SM prediction at 95% confidence level, while the expected limit on a H → μμ signal assuming the absence (presence) of a SM signal is 1.1 (2.0). The best-fit value of the signal strength parameter, defined as the ratio of the observed signal yield to the one expected in the SM, is μ = 1.2 ± 0.6. Regarding the muon identification algorithms based on calorimeter information, several working points have been studied under the current detector conditions, leading to the determination of the parameters to be used so as to maintain the performance obtained under the (relatively cleaner) run 2 conditions. We have also migrated the description of the new components of the muon detectors to the format to be used in Run 3, and continue to contribute to the operations and daily monitoring of the ATLAS muon reconstruction algorithms, an important task to ensure the integrity of the incoming muon data.

14305619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305619.value: An extended use of machine learning techniques may yield a larger sensitivity, especially in the categories that have a lower ratio between the expected signal and the expected standard model backgrounds. Also, the use of different classifiers for different backgrounds, later combined into a single test statistic, has yielded promising preliminary results in other channels that can be further explored in the H to mu mu measurement. Regarding the muon identification algorithms, particle information provided by the New Small Wheel, recently installed in the ATLAS detector, should be included into the machine learning systems used to identify muon candidates.

14305619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305619.value: This research project contributes to our understanding of the fundamental processes of Nature on two fronts: (a) searching for phenomena that is not expected in our current theories, and (b) improve the particle reconstruction tools used to study high-energy particle collisions. These objectives are pursued through the analysis of proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland. There, protons travel almost at the speed of light; when they collide, they can transform into any particle allowed by the laws of Nature. Our current description of these laws (the “Standard Model”, or SM) provides very precise predictions for the possible outcomes of these collisions, but we know that the SM is incomplete, so we are making a systematic search for phenomena not contained in it. We aim specifically to (a) measure the frequency with which the Higgs boson, discovered in 2012, decays into muon-antimuon pairs, to determine any possible discrepancies with the SM prediction, and (b) improve the methods used to identify and reconstruct the muons that are produced in high-energy particle collisions at the Large Hadron Collider.

14305719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305719.value: Carboranes, carbon-boron molecular clusters, possess extraordinary characteristics including three-dimensional aromaticity conjugated by σ-bonds, icosahedral geometry and inherent robustness. These properties make carboranes very important molecular building blocks for applications ranging from structural materials to medicines. The effective functionalization of carboranes has therefore attracted enormous research interest, especially regioselective cage BH derivatization. Transition metal catalyzed vertex-specific functionalization of carboranes has recently been developed, however the established protocols all require noble transition metal catalysts and this compromises both efficiency and generality. Base metal catalysis exhibits the advantages of economy, low-toxicity, sustainability and green in comparison with that of noble metals. Recent research has highlighted the versatility of base metals in valence change and single electron transfer. Given these advantages, and on the basis of our own pioneering work in noble metal catalyzed carboranyl B-H functionalization (for concept article: Chem. Eur. J. 2018, 24, 2795), we intend in this study to investigate and develop base metal catalyzed straightforward and regioselective B-H activation for the economical, green and selective functionalization of o-carboranes. The project is expected to generate a series of new base metal catalyzed synthetic methodologies, bringing more possibilities to the effective and efficient construction of carborane-based functional molecules and the corresponding applications. Reaction mechanisms will also be systematically investigated with the aim of enhancing the fundamental understanding of base metal induced B-H activation, which would in turn shed light on chemo- and regio-selectivity control in other base metal catalyzed chemical transformations. 14305819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14305819.value: Nitrogen is essential for amino acids, DNAs and RNAs, the basic building blocks in living organisms. Although nitrogen molecules occupy 78 vol% of the atmosphere, they cannot be directly used by most organisms because of the strong triple bond. They need to be fixed into ammonia or nitrate before being taken up by organisms. Because the fixed forms of nitrogen are continuously consumed through geological sedimentation and back conversion to dinitrogen, continuous nitrogen fixation is required to form a nitrogen cycle to sustain life on the Earth. Nitrogen fixation can be realized by nitrogenase enzymes in some organisms. However, biological fixation is not enough for sustaining the entire human population. The Haber-Bosch process is a large-scale artificial technology for nitrogen fixation. At least a half of the nitrogen amount in human bodies is supplied by this technology. The process is run under high temperatures and high pressures. The required energy and hydrogen are derived from fossil fuels. The process consumes ~2% of the total energy and produces ~1% of the total amount of carbon dioxide generated on the world. On the other hand, ammonia can be liquefied easily. Besides being used in fertilizer, ammonia can be transported to power plants for electricity generation and cracked into hydrogen for fuel cell vehicles. Therefore, there exists a great potential for an “ammonia economy". Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation can operate under mild conditions and use solar energy. The challenge lies in overcoming the kinetic obstacle associated with the concerted transfer of multiple electrons and protons in the reduction of dinitrogen into ammonia. So far, the highest reported solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency is ~0.1%, which is too low for practical applications. The low efficiencies can be ascribed to the difficulties in the generation and control of nitrogen activation sites, as well as the wide bandgaps of employed semiconductors. Herein we propose to develop hybrid nanostructures out of oxides and plasmonic metal nanocrystals for efficient photocatalytic nitrogen fixation. Oxygen vacancies will be introduced to act as nitrogen activation sites and reduce the activation barrier. The plasmonic nanocrystals will function as electron sources for reduction. Similar to the case in the nitrogenase enzymes, the two components will work "in-tandem”. Systematic studies will be carried out to understand the roles of both components and their synergetic mechanism. The hybrid nanostructures will be optimized for photocatalytic nitrogen fixation with largely improved efficiencies, paving the way towards the future “ammonia economy". 氮是氨基酸、去氧核糖核酸(DNA)和核糖核酸(RNA)等生物分子的必備元素，這些生物分子是生物發育與生命機能運作的基本構件。雖然大氣中氮氣的體積佔比高達78%，但由於氮氣分子的三鍵的鍵能很强，這些儲存在氮氣中的氮元素是不能被絕大多數的生物體直接吸收利用。氮元素需要經過固氮過程，以氨或硝酸鹽的形式被生物吸收。由於這些固氮過程所產生的氮化合物會隨著地質沉積和逆反應而不斷地被消耗，因此爲了維持地球上的生命，持續地固氮來完成一個氮循環是不可或缺的。 雖然一些生物體中的固氮酶可以完成固氮過程，但僅僅依靠生物固氮是無法滿足現代人口對氮化合物的巨大需求。哈伯-博施法是一個大規模的人工固氮技術。現在，在人體中至少有一半的氮元素是由這種人工固氮技術提供的。然而在哈伯-博施法中，通過消耗化石燃料來達到的高溫和高壓是必需的反應條件，這也使得哈伯-博施法佔全球能源消耗總量的2%，並佔全球1%的二氧化碳排放量。另一方面，由於氨很容易被液化，因此除了被用作肥料之外，氨還可以運輸到發電廠用於發電，並且可以把氨分解成氫氣用在燃料電池車輛中，這使得「氨經濟」這一概念有著巨大潛力。 光催化固氮可以使用太陽能在溫和條件下操作。氮氣還原成氨的最大挑戰在於多個電子和質子的協同轉移相關的動力障礙。到目前為止，光催化固氮太陽能轉化成化學能的最高效率約為0.03%，這遠低於實際應用的需求。其低效率可歸咎於氮活化位點的產生和控制的困難，以及寬帶隙的半導體對太陽光的低吸收率。 在此，我們提出開發由氧化物和等離激元金屬納米晶體組成的雜化結構，以進行有效的光催化固氮。我們將引入氧空位以充當氮活化位點並降低反應的活化能，而等離激元納米晶體將被用作還原反應的電子源。類似於固氮酶，這兩種組分將「串聯」起作用。我們將通過系統的研究去理解兩個組成部分的作用及其協同機制。最後，我們將圍繞光催化固氮應用對雜化結構進行優化來大大提高其效率，為未來的「氨經濟」做好充分的準備。

14305819.label: Realisation of objectives
14305819.value: There are 7 objectives for this project. All of them have been completely realized. We will discuss them one by one below. Please refer Section 6.1 below for the acronyms of the output journal publications. (1) Synthesize hybrid nanostructures from metal oxides and plasmonic metal nanocrystals for photocatalytic nitrogen fixation We synthesized two types of (plasmonic metal)-semiconductor hybrid photocatalysts. The used plasmonic metal is spherical Au nanoparticles. The semiconductor in one type of the hybrid photocatalyst is graphitic carbon nitride (JMCA2020), which is a widely studied non-metal material for various photocatalytic reactions, including water splitting, CO2 reduction, and N2 reduction. The semiconductor in the other type is Ti3C2 MXene (CS2021). MXenes are a family of two-dimensional layered transition metal carbides, nitrides or carbonitrides. They have attracted much interest since the first report in 2011. Benefiting from the metallic conductivity, abundant surface terminal groups, large surface-to-volume ratio, excellent hydrophilic and ion transport properties, MXenes have been explored in diverse fields. Ti3C2, the first reported MXene, possesses several unique features for photocatalysis. It has become a research hot spot in photocatalysis. (2) Study the effects of the concentration, nitrogen adsorption strength and generation method of oxygen vacancies on photocatalytic nitrogen fixation In a previous study that was reported in 2018, we deposited Au nanoparticles on TiO2 nanosheets that were a few nanometers in thickness. Oxygen vacancies were introduced on the TiO2 nanosheets, with their number density varied by thermal annealing in air. The nitrogen fixation activity was found to decrease with decreasing densities of the oxygen vacancies. In order to study the effect of different oxygen vacancies, we prepared TiO2 spheres and doped them with Fe at extremely high concentrations by aerosol spray (ACIE2021N2). We also synthesized MoO3 and introduced oxygen vacancies through thermal treatment in a reducing atmosphere (AM2022) and doping with vanadium (ACSML2022) in this project. In order to study the effect of different types of nitrogen activation sites, we synthesized (plasmonic metal)-semiconductor hybrid nanostructures by selecting graphitic carbon nitride (JMCA2020) and Ti3C2 MXene (CS2021). The former has nitrogen vacancies, and the latter has carbon vacancies. These materials possess different optical and electronic properties. Because many factors affect the photocatalytic activity jointly, it is difficult to extract the separate effect of the activation site on the photocatalytic activity in these different materials. To pinpoint out the effects of the different factors in photocatalytic nitrogen fixation has been challenging. Enormous effort will be required to achieve this goal in the future. (3) Study the effects of the amount, size, shape, plasmon wavelength, interface and metal type of plasmonic metal nanocrystals on photocatalytic nitrogen fixation We prepared (Au nanoparticle)-C3N4 hollow nanospheres (JMCA2020) and (Au nanoparticle)-(Ti3C2 MXene) structures (CS2021) as hybrid photocatalysts for nitrogen fixation. The amount, size, plasmon wavelength, and interface were all studied in the project. Moreover, noble metals are generally very expensive, which limits their large-scale applications. To address this issue, we synthesized non-noble-metal plasmonic nanomaterials, which included titanium oxynitride (ACSAMI2022) and titanium nitride. Interestingly, we found that the surface of TiN can be easily oxidized into TiO2 when it is exposed to air. The oxidized TiO2 on the surface contains oxygen vacancies, which can adsorb and activate N2. As a result, these non-noble-metal plasmonic nanomaterials are very active for photocatalytic nitrogen fixation. We are currently working intensively on these nanomaterials for photocatalytic nitrogen fixation. The results will be reported in the near future. (4) Investigate the synergetic mechanism between the nitrogen activating component and plasmonic electron source component for photocatalytic nitrogen fixation In this project, we totally prepared 7 types of nanomaterials for photocatalytic nitrogen fixation. They are Au-C3N4 (JMCA2020), Au-Ti3C2 (CS2021), Fe-doped TiO2 (ACIE2021N2), Au-(Fe-doped TiO2) (ACIE2021N2), MoO3-x (AM2022), V-doped MoO3 (ACSML2022), and TiNO (ACSAMI2022). These materials contain different nitrogen activation sites and different plasmonic materials. The synergetic interplay between the nitrogen activating component and plasmonic electron source component for photocatalytic nitrogen fixation were investigated systematically. Significant understanding on the interplay was gained. Our understanding on how to utilize excited plasmon energy efficiently was discussed in an invited perspective article (ACSNano2021). (5) Examine the competition between photocatalytic hydrogen evolution and nitrogen fixation We examined the production of both NH3 and H2 for the Au-C3N4 (JMCA2020), Au-Ti3C2 (CS2021), and MoO3-x photocatalysts (AM2022). NH3 was found to be dominant in the products for the Au-C3N4 and MoO3-x photocatalysts, with only a small fraction of H2 produced. In comparison, no H2 was produced with the Au-Ti3C2. We reason that the different selectivities for NH3 production might be caused by the active sites on the photocatalysts. More studies will be required to gain full understanding about this point. (6) Design the oxide/metal hybrid catalysts to eliminate the hole scavenger agent during photocatalytic nitrogen fixation Whether a hole scavenger agent is required in the photocatalytic nitrogen fixation process is dependent on the position of the valance band edge of the photocatalyst relative to the redox potential of the oxidation reaction of H2O. In this project, no hole scavenger agent is required for all of the three types of photocatalysts, which are Au-C3N4 (JMCA2020), Au-Ti3C2 (CS2021), and MoO3-x (AM2022) photocatalysts. During the photocatalytic nitrogen fixation tests, the production of O2 was detected. These results indicate that the oxidation potential values of these photocatalysts are positive enough to directly oxidize H2O into O2. (7) Optimize the oxide/metal hybrid catalysts according to the achieved understanding to improve the efficiency for nitrogen photofixation We optimized the relevant parameters for each type of photocatalyst. The highest solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency for the Au-Ti3C2 photocatalyst was 0.013% (CS2021). The conversion efficiency for the Au-C3N4 photocatalyst reached 0.032% (JMCA2020). For the Schottky-barrier-free MoO3-x photocatalyst, the conversion efficiency was found to be 0.057% in our first report (AM2022). We have been optimizing the relevant parameters for this photocatalyst, including the photocatalyst concentration, reaction volume, N2 flow rate, reaction temperature, and stirring rate. The conversion efficiency has been raised to 0.25%, which is a world record. Up to date, the efficiency record reported in the literature is 0.1%. We are still working on this photocatalyst system. The conversion efficiency is expected to be pushed to a higher value.

14305819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305819.value: We published 10 papers and trained 2 PhD students on this project. The 10 papers are (1) J. Mater. Chem. A 2020, 8, 16218 (JMCA2020) (2) Chem. Sci. 2021, 12, 11213 (CS2021) (3) Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 927 (ACIE2021N2) (4) Adv. Mater. 2022, 34, 2104226 (AM2022) (5) Adv. Funct. Mater. 2021, 31, 2101255 (AFM2021) (6) ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 51855 (ACSAMI2021) (7) Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 24958 (ACIE2021motors) (8) ACS Nano 2021, 15, 10759 (ACSNano2021) (9) ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2022, 14, 28769 (ACSAMI2022) (10) ACS Mater. Lett. 2022, 4, 1584 (ACSML2022) There are 7 major findings and outcomes out of this project. First, we developed two types of (plasmonic metal)-semiconductor hybrid nanostructures that can function as photocatalysts for nitrogen fixation. One type is based on Au and graphitic carbon nitride (paper 1), and the other is based on Au and MXenes (paper 2). Graphitic carbon nitride is a widely studied, versatile photocatalyst, and MXenes are an emerging type of two-dimensional material. Second, we realized doping titania with Fe at extremely high concentrations by aerosol spray. The doped product is able to drive the disproportionate reaction of nitrogen to give nitrate and ammonia in one step (paper 3). The embedding of Au nanoparticles transforms the disproportionation reaction into the complete nitrogen fixation reaction. Third, we developed Schottky-barrier-free plasmonic photocatalysts, which enables the efficient utilization of plasmonic hot charge carriers (paper 4). We have achieved a world-record solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency with this type of photocatalyst for nitrogen fixation. Fourth, we synthesized two types of all-metal plasmonic nanostructures. One is based on Cu deposited asymmetrically on Au nanobipyramids and used for electrocatalytic CO2 reduction (paper 5), and the other is based on the asymmetric deposition of Pt and Pd on Au nanocups for photooxidation of o-phenylenediamine (paper 6). The latter is extremely sensitive to light and highly active even under room light. Fifth, we developed plasmon-enhanced Au nanocrystal-based nanomotors on Si substrates (paper 7). Sixth, based on our understanding on plasmons and plasmonic photocatalysis, we contributed an invited perspective article on how to efficiently utilize excited plasmon energy (paper 8). Seventh, we developed two types of non-noble-metal plasmonic materials for solar seawater desalination. One is titanium oxynitride spheres with broad plasmon resonance (paper 9), and the other is dielectric MoO3 that is turned black through doping (paper 10).

14305819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305819.value: Based on the results and understanding from this project, there are three aspects that are worthy of further investigation. First, complete photocatalytic nitrogen fixation involves the oxygen evolution reaction, where the photo-generated holes oxidize water into oxygen. This oxidation reaction involves four electrons. There is a large probability that the entire reaction is limited by this oxidation half reaction. We will design experiments to understand the mechanism of the water oxidation reaction. We will further deposit co-catalysts on our photocatalysts to enhance the oxygen evolution reaction and thus the entire nitrogen fixation reaction. Second, the photocatalytic nitrogen fixation is carried out in water solutions. Water absorbs sunlight at wavelengths longer than ~900 nm. Above ~1000 nm, almost all sunlight is absorbed by water. It is therefore urgent to eliminate the light-absorption problem of water. We will embed our photocatalysts into floatable polymer films, which are hydrophilic and porous. They can absorb water easily. Third, our photocatalytic nitrogen fixation is carried out in glass or quartz bottles. These vessels are typically in a round shape. They are inappropriate for the utilization of sunlight and difficult to be scaled up. We will design flatbed reactors to enhance sunlight absorption and utilization.

14305819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305819.value: Nitrogen is an indispensable element for living organisms. Although the volume percentage of nitrogen molecules in the atmosphere reaches 78 vol%, they cannot be directly used by living organisms. They have to be converted into ammonia or nitrate for use, which is known as nitrogen fixation. Natural nitrogen fixation became insufficient in the 19th century for sustaining the entire human population. The Haber-Bosch process was then invented in the early 20th century for artificial nitrogen fixation. The process consumes ~2% of the total energy and produces ~1% of the total amount of carbon dioxide on the world. Photocatalytic nitrogen fixation can operate under mild conditions and use solar energy and water. In this project, we have developed hybrid nanostructures out of oxides and plasmonic metal nanocrystals for efficient photocatalytic nitrogen fixation. Systematic studies have been carried out to understand the roles of both components and their synergetic mechanism. We have further developed a type of photocatalyst solely based on highly doped semiconductors. We have achieved world-record-high solar-to-chemical conversion efficiencies in our project. Our plasmonic photocatalysts can be further optimized for photocatalytic nitrogen fixation with largely improved efficiencies, which paves the way towards the future “ammonia economy”.

14305919.value: Design and implement data-driven mathematical algorithms for various image analysis and processing problems. This includes (i) data-driven geometric models for 2D and high-dimensional mapping problems of degraded images and (ii) data-driven geometric models for image segmentation of corrupted images. Develop a deep network that mimics the architecture of deep convolutional neural networks, in which the geometric meaning of each layers can be described. Practical applications of the algorithms to medical imaging. This includes: (i) the development of data-driven image registration tools for brain MR images and (ii) the development of data-driven image segmentation tools for segmenting a brain subcortical structure, called the hippocampus.

14305919.value: 隨著二維和三維圖像採集技術的發展，圖像數據的可用性顯著增加。數據驅動的數學模型越來越適用於各種的成像任務。傳統方法通常通過一些合適的數學模型來解決問題。雖然現有的數學模型通常可以給出不錯的結果，但是我們相信把數據信息結合到數學模型中可以進一步獲得更好的結果。在這個項目中，我們的目標是將數學模型和幾何信息結合起來，為不同的圖像分析和處理任務開發數據驅動的幾何模型。 本研究主要可分為兩部分。在研究的第一部分，我們希望通過數據轉換開發有效的數據驅動幾何模型，用於各種圖像分析和處理任務。我們將考慮幾個成像問題。首先，許多圖像分析問題可以被表述為映射問題，主要任務是要在圖像或曲面之間找到有意義的點對點對應關係。該問題對於低質素的圖像尤其具有挑戰性。在這個項目中，我們將研究開發數據驅動幾何模型，根據圖像以及訓練數據的匹配程度來查找所有映射（可能具有多種模式）的概率分佈。我們將考慮二維和高維的映射問題。其次，圖像分割是圖像分析的另一個關鍵但具有挑戰性的任務，特別是對於損壞的圖像。通過整合現有數據中的信息，我們有興趣開發用於分割低質素圖像的數據驅動幾何模型。第三，深度卷積神經網絡（DCNN）在各種成像應用中取得了巨大成功。然而，DCNN的一個缺點是缺乏解釋各種架構的理論。受此啟發，我們將開發模擬DCNN架構的深度網絡，其中可以解釋每層的幾何意義。通過對每個層的幾何理解，我們可以針對不同的數據驅動成像任務仔細設計深層網絡架構。從每個層提取的有意義的特徵也可以合併到不同的數學模型中。 接下來，在我們研究的第二部分，我們有興趣把我們的方法應用於醫學圖像分析。更具體地說，我們將會把數據驅動的幾何模型用於磁力共振圖像的配準。我們還會把數據驅動圖像分割工具應用於分割大腦中的海馬體。

14305919.label: Realisation of objectives
14305919.value: The proposed project has three main objectives. The main goal of this project is to investigate and develop various data-driven geometric models for various imaging problems. The focus is on the combination of data information and mathematical models to accurately tackle various 2D and 3D imaging tasks. The PI and his team have successfully completed the project objectives. Below we would like to report the development we have made in details. Objective 1: The first objective of this project is to design and implement data-driven mathematical algorithms for various image analysis and processing problems. The goal is to combine quasiconformal models with training data for various imaging tasks, which can be formulated in terms of mapping problems. The PI has successfully achieved this goal. There are several tasks involved in this objective. Below, we describe in detail what we have achieved for each task. 1.1 Data-driven geometric models for 2D mapping problems One task in this objective is to develop data-driven geometric models for solving the mapping problems of degraded images. The goal is to combine quasiconformal models with training data to achieve more accurate mappings of degraded images. Degraded images often possess ambiguity that hinders the computation of accurate mappings between them using conventional mathematical models. However, as the availability of image data increases, incorporating information from the training data into the mathematical model can help overcome this problem. The PI has successfully developed and implemented a data-driven geometric framework to solve the 2D mapping problems. The main idea is to combine quasiconformal models (mathematical models) with the available training data (data-driven) to improve the mapping accuracy. A deep neural network is utilized to integrate the quasiconformal model with the available training data. This special deep neural network incorporates quasiconformality into the network structure. By training the deep neural network with the data, the information can be integrated, and a data-driven geometric model to solve the mapping problem is developed. Experimental results demonstrate outstanding performance for mapping degraded images. Furthermore, we have developed a novel energy term that incorporates correspondence information from training data, based on the truncated CNN features. The addition of this term into the registration model can significantly improve the registration accuracy. In some scenarios, there may be more than one possible solution given the incomplete information of the degraded images. To handle this, we have successfully developed a deep neural network framework to compute multi-modal uncertainty estimation and estimate the probability distribution of multiple plausible solutions. This framework has been successfully applied for joint image registration and segmentation with multiple possible solutions, accurately generating multiple plausible outcomes and estimating the probability associated with each suggested solution based on the data information. 1.2 Data-driven geometric models for high-dimensional mapping problems Conventional quasiconformal imaging models have primarily focused on 2D images. Another task in this objective is to extend the 2D data-driven geometric models to develop data-driven geometric models for high-dimensional mapping problems. The PI has successfully developed a mathematical framework to accomplish this task. More specifically, we have developed a deep neural network framework for solving high-dimensional mapping problems. The deep neural network is integrated with an n-dimensional mapping optimization model, which mimics the 2D quasiconformal model. The energy functional in the optimization model is used as a loss function to control the properties of the output mapping by the deep neural network. Under this deep learning-based framework, data information can be easily incorporated to enhance the accuracy of the solution. Additionally, the high-dimensional mapping can be parameterized by the parameters of the deep neural networks. In this setting, the number of network parameters is commonly much less than the number of variables under conventional high-resolution discretization schemes. Thus, the framework can enhance the efficiency and capability to handle large-scale problems. 1.3. Data-driven geometric models for image segmentation Another task in this project is to develop data-driven geometric models for image segmentation of corrupted images. The PI has successfully developed various mathematical algorithms to tackle this problem. More specifically, we have developed a deep neural network-based data-driven model to learn the probability distribution of segmentation results, given a training dataset of images. Given a dataset of images, we are able to obtain all possible segmentation results with an estimation of the probability associated to each segmentation. The proposed model can also successfully estimate the probability distribution of segmentation results with multiple modes. Mathematical models for topology- and/or convexity-preserving segmentation have been developed to enhance the accuracy of segmenting degraded or corrupted images, which is also necessary for processing the training dataset. Besides, we have incorporated deep neural networks with the developed geometric image segmentation models to obtain deep learning-based segmentation models. The deep neural network-based models facilitate the integration of data information, enabling the development of data-driven geometric models to solve the image segmentation problem for corrupted images. Objective 2: One of the objectives in this project is to develop a deep network that mimics the architecture of CNNs, in which the geometric meaning can be explained. The PI has successfully developed such a framework. More specifically, we have developed a novel network structure, which replaces the CNN layer by a quasiconformal transformer network. Intuitively, the input data is transformed by a quasiconformal mapping into another meaningful feature space before feeding into a downstream network for a specific imaging task. The transformed data lies within a distribution of features, with which the data structure can be easily analyzed. Under this setting, the geometric meaning of the network can be interpreted. A key challenge in implementing this idea is how to incorporate quasiconformal mappings into the deep network. Quasiconformal mappings are related to their associated geometric quantities, called the Beltrami coefficients. It involves solving a partial differential equation, called the Beltrami's equation. Therefore, a deep neural network that can reconstruct the quasiconformal mapping from its Beltrami coefficient is needed. For this purpose, we have successfully developed and implemented the Beltrami Solver Network, which can accurately solve the Beltrami equation to reconstruct the quasiconformal mapping. Experimental results show that the newly proposed deep neural network is able to not only enhance the interpretability of the deep network, but also significantly improve the accuracy of imaging results, especially for degraded or corrupted images. Objective 3: Our third objective is to apply the developed algorithms to medical imaging. The PI has successfully accomplished this task. More specifically, the developed data-driven image registration model has been successfully applied to registering brain MRI scans with high accuracy. The proposed data-driven geometric models for image segmentation can also be applied to segmentation of various medical images, including lung segmentation of chest radiographs with pulmonary opacities, segmentation of lesions, and segmentation of brain anatomical structures. The proposed models can obtain good imaging results with high accuracy and efficiency, even when working with degraded or corrupted medical images.

14305919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14305919.value: In this project, we have developed various data-driven mathematical models for different imaging tasks, resulting in 7 published papers and 3 submitted papers (under revision). The major findings and research outcomes are as follows: - Data-Driven Geometric Models for 2D Image Registration: Various data-driven geometric models for 2D image registration have been developed [1,2,3]. In [2,3], we have developed a deep learning based geometric model for data-driven registration of 2d images and 2D brain geometric images. Furthermore, we have developed a novel energy term that incorporates correspondence information from training data, based on the truncated CNN features [1]. The addition of this term into the registration model can significantly improve the registration accuracy. - Data-Driven Geometric Models for nD Image Registration: Building upon the 2D data-driven geometric registration models, we have also developed a deep learning-based data-driven geometric model for extending the registration capabilities to higher-dimensional (nD) imaging data [5]. A specialized loss function is utitlized to train the model [4]. - Multi-Modal Uncertainty Estimation: Medical imaging often involves working with incomplete or degraded data, leading to multiple possible solutions for a given task. To address this challenge, we have developed a deep neural network framework capable of computing multi-modal uncertainty estimates [6,7]. This innovative approach allows us to generate a set of plausible imaging solutions and provide probabilistic estimates for each plausible outcome. - Data-Driven Geometric Models for Image Segmentation of degraded images: We have developed data-driven geometric models for image segmentation of corrupted images using deep neural network frameworks [6,7]. Additionally, we have derived mathematical models for topology- and/or convexity-preserving segmentation to enhance the accuracy of segmenting degraded or corrupted images [8,9], which is also necessary for processing training dataset. - Quasiconformal Transformer Network: In [10], we have introduced a novel network structure, which incorporate a quasiconformal transformer network. With this framework, the geometric meaning can be better interpreted. This new architecture not only enhances the interpretability of the deep network but also significantly improves the accuracy of imaging results, especially for degraded or corrupted images.

14305919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14305919.value: The research conducted has laid a strong foundation, but there are several areas that warrant further exploration and development. 1. One key direction is to incorporate shape information learned from training data into the data-driven geometric models used for image registration and segmentation. Rather than relying solely on the image data itself, a neural network could be trained to learn the shape distributions of important objects, which could then be integrated as a shape prior to improve the accuracy of the geometric models. 2. Another promising avenue is to extend the data-driven geometric registration techniques to handle the registration of Riemann surfaces, particularly those with high genus, such as the vestibular system. Adapting the methods to handle these more complex geometric structures could significantly expand the applicability of the research. 3. Finally, the current model for generating multiple plausible solutions with associated probabilities may still be susceptible to modal collapse when dealing with complicated data distributions. Developing more robust techniques to tackle this challenge would be valuable, as generating diverse, probabilistic outputs is an important capability for many real-world applications.

14305919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14305919.value: The main goal of this research is to develop advanced data-driven geometric models to tackle various imaging challenges. We have explored two key directions: designing effective data-driven geometric models for solving imaging problems, and applying these algorithms to real-world practical applications. For the first direction, we have developed new mathematical models that combine powerful quasiconformal techniques with data-driven information. This allows us to address image registration and segmentation problems, even with degraded or corrupted images. We have also developed a deep network that mimics the architecture of CNNs, in which the geometric meaning can be explained. This framework allows us to not only enhance the interpretability of the deep network, but also significantly improve the accuracy of imaging results, especially for degraded or corrupted images. As for the second part of the project, we have explored the applications of proposed algorithms for practical uses. We have applied the data-driven registration model to aligs brain MRI scans with high accuracy. We have also applied the data-driven geometric segmentation models on diverse medical images, including the segmentation of lungs, lesions, and brain structures. Our developed models perform well, even with degraded or corrupted data.

14306119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306119.value: Earthquakes have caused significant damage and casualty in human history and accordingly there is a critical need to advance our understanding of earthquake physics. The largest earthquakes occur on the shallow megathrust interface in subduction zones, sometimes accompanied by devastating tsunami. Megathrust rupture extents play critical roles in ground shaking and tsunami generation but are difficult to estimate before earthquakes occur. Interseismic locking distributions derived from geodetic measurements are often used to qualitatively evaluate future earthquake potential and rupture extents. However, considering uncertainties in the locking models and the non-linear dynamic rupture process, it is extremely challenging to accurately estimate future earthquake sizes, although it is of critical significance to mitigate seismic hazard. We propose to derive earthquake rupture scenarios from interseismic locking distributions along the Cascadia subduction zone, where a series of earthquakes with magnitudes of ~9 occurred in the past 10,000 years with an estimated recurrence interval of ~500 years. Despite the unknown occurrence time, a great earthquake (magnitude>8) has been anticipated because geodetic measurements show that the Cascadia megathrust has been locked. But the locking degree is controversial, especially in central Oregon where potential rupture segmentation was implied in paleo-earthquakes. Whether the next earthquake will break the entire Cascadia or is segmented to a smaller magnitude event remains elusive, yet is important for hazard evaluation. Furthermore, the locking uncertainties become worse at the near-trench portion because of no constraint from inland observations. As such, it is mysterious whether the shallow portion may break so as to generate tsunami even in a relatively small earthquake. We will conduct numerical simulations to derive rupture scenarios by incorporating three-dimensional fault geometry, with initial stress estimated from the locking models. For the non-constrained locking degree on the shallow megathrust, we will investigate the potential for ruptures to break the trench by assuming a series of ad-hoc models with locking degrees ranging from 0 to 1. We will also investigate the hypocentral dependent rupture scenarios, which are important for earthquake and near-field tsunami early warning. The estimated economic loss in next Cascadia magnitude 9 earthquake may exceed 500 billion US$ according to insurance company. Therefore, the anticipated results of rupture scenarios will not only fill in a critical knowledge gap in Cascadia, but also have high societal impact on better evaluating earthquake and tsunami hazard along subduction zones. One graduate student will be supported in the project.

14306119.label: Realisation of objectives
14306119.value: To tackle the above scientific objectives, we have conducted a variety of investigations, including successful construction of a finite element mesh for the Cascadia subduction zone, computation of stress changes due to the scenario slip derived from interseismic locking distributions, and simulation of dynamic ruptures on the mesh. In addition, we have conducted extensive research of constraining frictional parameters on seismogenic faults that are crucial for dynamic rupture simulations, in regions such as Nicoya Peninsula and Mexico because we have observational data. Two graduate students are trained to perform numerical simulations of earthquake rupture propagation. One postdoc is partially involved in this project as well. We first use Cubit to generate the 3D mesh of the Cascadia subduction zone. By building a spline surface from depth contours that were derived in McCrory et al., 2004, we construct the slab geometry. Then we estimate the stress field from interseismic locking models along the Cascadia megathrust. Three typical locking models (Burgette et al., 2009, Schmalzle et al., 2014, Li et al., 2018) are used during the study to investigate the potential along-strike rupture segmentation in Cascadia. Assuming that the slip deficit is linear and continuously accumulated, the total slip deficit of each node on the slab surface, from the last earthquake until the present, is calculated by multiplying the slip rate with its locking fraction and 320 years since last megathrust earthquake. After obtaining the slip distributions, we interpolate the unevenly distributed slip to a fine uniform distribution for reasonable projection on mesh nodes. Frictional properties are crucial for earthquake generation and rupture propagation, but remain the least constrained parameters on seismogenic faults. Here we adopt a linear slip-weakening law on faults. To reasonably estimate the parameters, a well-monitored earthquake with near-field observations is desired. Therefore, we resolve the dynamic rupture process of the 2012 Mw 7.6 Nicoya earthquake and constrain the frictional strength to be < 7.5 MPa in average prior to the earthquake (Yao and Yang, 2020, Geophys. Res. Lett.). Such low strength indicates the existence of compacted fluids with a high pore pressure on the megathrust. The critical weakening distance Dc is estimated to be ~0.3 m in average. The estimated frictional parameters on the Nicoya megathrust served as a reference for parameter prescriptions in numerical simulations for the Cascadia subduction zone. When conducting rupture simulation, we test a suit of nucleation sizes and locations, because different hypocenters may lead to different rupture extent, attributed to the heterogeneous stress distribution (Yang et al., 2019). Our dynamic rupture scenarios show that the southern Cascadia can generate both segmented ruptures (>Mw 7.3–8.4) and margin-wide ruptures (>Mw8.6) depending on the hypocenter location (Chan et a., 2023, JGR). The along-strike rupture length appears to coincide with rupture lengths hypothesized from paleoseismology. Our results also indicate that earthquakes with magnitudes smaller than 8.0 will unlikely break the trench, according to the present locking models we’ve tested. Such hypocenter-dependent rupture scenarios are not only limited to Cascadia, but also hold true for continental fault (Yao and Yang, 2022 EPSL). Furthermore, we computed ground motions and validate such locking-based ground motion predictions with observational data, as well as the ground motion prediction equation (Yao and Yang, 2023 EPSL). The results demonstrate the feasibility of our physics-based approach to improve near-field predictions for future hazard assessment. As such, we’ve realized all objectives. We have extended a bit from the original objectives to investigate factors that affect estimation of frictional parameters and rupture propagation. It has been pointed out that seismogenic width plays critical roles in rupture extent from dynamic rupture simulations (Weng and Yang, 2017). We test such a hypothesis in the 2020 Mw 7.4 La Crucecita, Mexico, earthquake and find a narrow rupture zone during this earthquake (Guo et al., 2021, Seismo. Res. Lett.). We also considered the effect of plate bending in subduction zones and computed the stress distribution among the incoming and overriding plates (Zhang et al., 2022 GRL), which hold implications for megathrust rupture propagation.

14306119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306119.value: The Cascadia subduction zone has well-documented geological records of megathrust earthquakes with the latest ∼Mw 9 rupture occurring in CE 1700. The paleoseismic observations suggest that southern Cascadia is mature for future earthquakes since the last event. Consequently, it is crucial to investigate the potential rupture scenarios. Although existing interseismic locking models share similar moment deficits, whether future earthquakes would be margin-wide or segmented remains unknown. We first set up a framework of linking interseismic locking models with stress distributions on the seismogenic faults, and then conduct numerical simulations to derive rupture scenarios and ground motions during future earthquakes (Chan et al., 2023, JGR). Our dynamic rupture scenarios show that the south can generate both segmented ruptures (>Mw 7.3–8.4) and margin-wide ruptures (>Mw 8.6) depending on the hypocenter location. Furthermore, we utilize near-field observations to constrain frictional parameters on seismogenic faults (Yao and Yang, 2020 GRL), which are crucial for estimating future earthquake scenarios. We also extended such physics-based rupture and ground motion into other regions (Yao and Yang, 2022 EPSL; Yao and Yang, 2023 EPSL), with results shedding lights on future seismic hazard assessment. Two graduate students (Bowie Chan and Suli Yao) worked for this project; their theses have received IEEE GRSS Hong Kong Chapter Excellent Dissertation Award and Chinese Geophysical Society Excellent Dissertation Award, respectively.

14306119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306119.value: To extend our numerical simulations of ground motions during future potential earthquakes into the tsunami scenarios, the work can be extended into tsunami modeling with consideration of more realistic earthquake source models. Furthermore, more interseismic locking models can be included as they become available, so that physics-based ground motion prediction can be obtained in near field.

14306119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306119.value: The Cascadia subduction zone is a region off the coast of North America where one tectonic plate (Juan de Fuca) slowly slides beneath another (North America). Although there have been no significant earthquakes in Cascadia recently, geological records indicate that the last earthquake, estimated as a magnitude 9, occurred in CE 1700. In between earthquake occurrences, stress is accumulated and manifested in strain build-up measurable by instruments. Existing models infer stress accumulation from these measurements but are variable along the length of the earthquake fault. Based on stress distributions suggested by the models, we design potential future earthquake scenarios using three-dimensional computer simulations. Our results show how the final earthquake size and expected ground-shaking change depending on where it is allowed to initiate, shedding lights on understanding the earthquake and tsunami hazard on the Cascadia and other subduction zones.

14306219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306219.value: 罕見病患者需要更多的支持，這是毋庸置疑的。全世界超過6000種罕見疾病及其症狀因地而異因人而異 ，正是因為罕見病的稀有性和多樣性，現代生物醫學技術的研究應確保國際的專家，研究人員和臨床醫生進行聯網並且共同努力提供更好的治療方案。在統計學家的眼中，我們用回歸模型分析和研究數據的內在關係。邏輯回歸是非常受歡迎的統計模型，它經常被用於生物統計學和生物醫學科學建模兩類或多類數據，例如：活著/死亡，生病/健康等。在大數據時代，邏輯回歸模型在分析各種應用更加普及，例如文獻分類，模式識別等等。病例對照方法是研究跟罕見疾病發病有關的因素的主要工具，與前瞻性研究方法相比， 它具有顯著的優勢。現有的基於邏輯回歸模型分析病例對照數據的方法是很有效的， 但模型中的截距項卻是不可識別不可估計的。隨著數據規模的快速增長，人們急需有新的方法用以分析罕見病數據。 這項研究課題將集中於建立一個新的統計回歸模型框架用以分析從不同國家/地區收集的分佈式病例對照數據，並且找出新的統計方法來估計和推斷模型中的回歸參數。 該項目將會用到的主要工具是邏輯回歸模型，曲線的估計和 穩定的數值算法。隨著統計科學的最新發展和快速增長的計算能力，解決相關的技術問題和發展新方法對推進研究邏輯回歸模型分析病例對照數據是迫切的。該研究項目的目標是基本統計模型中的基本問題，它具有重要的科研意義和深遠的的影響

14306219.label: Realisation of objectives
14306219.value: The PI and her coauthors have delivered a number of research outputs to achieve the objectives in this research. 1. The PI and her co-authors studied an efficient estimation for the intercepts and slope parameters of the logistic regression models under distributed case-control studies. With K case-control studies of different purposes from the same population or collected from K heterogeneous subpopulations, the data can be pooled together for integrative analysis. By combining K case-control studies, surprisingly, the intercepts become identifiable under mild conditions. The resulting estimates of the slope parameters are proved to be semiparametric efficient, with asymptotic variance smaller than the counterparts in single case-control study. The resulting estimates for the intercepts and slope parameters are shown to be consistent, asymptotically normal and asymptotically efficient. An iterative algorithm is employed to compute the maximum likelihood estimates numerically. Simulation studies are conducted to confirm our theoretical findings. We demonstrate the performance of the proposed method with an analysis of Hepatitis C infection dataset. This research output currently under review has successfully addressed objectives 1-5. 2. During the project period, we focus most of our research efforts on statistical modelling and analysis of distributed datasets and semi-supervised data, and have a number of findings: (2a) We consider the problem of estimating the nonparametric function in nonparametric logistic regression under semi-supervised framework, where a relatively small size labeled data set collected by case-control sampling and a relatively large size of unlabeled data containing only observations of predictors are available. A two-stage nonparametric semi-supervised estimator based on spline method is proposed to estimate the target regression function by maximizing the likelihood function of the labeled case-control data. The unlabeled data are used in the first stage for estimating the density function that involves in the likelihood function. The consistency and functional asymptotic normality of the semi-supervised two-stage estimator are established under mild conditions. The proposed method, by making use of the unlabeled data, produces more efficient estimation of the target function than the traditional supervised counterpart. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated through extensive simulation studies. An application is illustrated with an analysis of a skin segmentation data. This research output has successfully addressed Objectives 1, 3-6. Detailed results can be found in the publication entitled Semi-supervised inference for nonparametric logistic regression, which has been published in Statistics in Medicine. (2b) Due to privacy concern and other technical limitations, imbalanced data distributed across locations/machines cannot be simply combined and stored in a single central location. We propose a fused estimation for logistic regression in analyzing distributed imbalanced data by combining all the cases available on all machines, which is stable and efficient. The consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimator are established under regularity conditions. Asymptotic efficiency compared with the oracle estimator based on the entire imbalanced data is also studied. An application is illustrated with a credit card data for default payment. This research output has successfully addressed Objectives 1-5. Detailed results can be found in the publication titled Efficient fused learning for distributed imbalanced data in Communications in statistics-Theory and Methods. (2c) We consider a semi-supervised setting wherein the data are typically a combination of a relatively small labeled dataset and large amounts of unlabeled data. A new class of M-estimator, which efficiently uses the useful information contained in the unlabeled data, is proposed via a projection technique. We prove consistency and asymptotic normality, and provide an inference procedure based on K-fold cross-validation. It is shown that the proposed method, by taking advantage of the unlabeled data, produces asymptotically more efficient estimation of the target parameters than the supervised counterpart. Supportive numerical evidence is shown in simulation studies. Applications are illustrated in analysis of the homeless data in Los Angeles. This research output has successfully addressed Objectives 1, 2, 5, 6. Detailed results can be found in the publication entitled A General M-estimation Theory in Semi-Supervised Framework" in Journal of the American Statistical Association. (2d) To accommodate more complicated distributed data, we consider statistical inference for single or low-dimensional parameters in a high-dimensional linear model under a semi-supervised setting. Our proposed method utilises both labelled and unlabelled data without any imputation or removal of the missing observations. The asymptotic properties of the estimator are established under regularity conditions. Hypothesis testing for low-dimensional coefficients are also studied. Extensive simulations are conducted to examine the theoretical results. The method is evaluated on the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative data. This research output has successfully addressed Objectives 1, 2, 5, 6. Details can be found in the publication entitled Semi-supervised inference for block-wise missing data without imputation, which has been published in Journal of Machine Learning Research. 3. The PI and her coauthors have got some new insights and findings during the exploration for possible extension to higher dimensional data, so as to achieve objective 3 and Objective 6. Under case–control study, we consider the confidence intervals and statistical tests for single or low-dimensional parameters in high-dimensional logistic regression model. The asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators are established under mild conditions. We also study statistical tests for testing more general and complex hypotheses of the high-dimensional parameters. The general testing procedures are proved to be asymptotically exact and have satisfactory power. This paper titled Post-selection inference of high-dimensional logistic regression under case–control design has been published in Journal of Business and Economic Statistics. 4. Last but not least, in the pursuit of the main objectives in this project, the PI has published several papers in high dimensional data analysis and semiparametric inference. (4a) The PI and her coauthors concerned with identifying important features in high-dimensional data analysis. Without any specification of an actual model, we introduce a multiple testing procedure based on the quantile correlation to select important predictors in high dimensionality. The quantile-correlation statistic is able to capture a wide range of dependence. A stepwise procedure is studied for further identifying important variables. This work has been published in Journal of Business and Economic Statistics. (4b) Moreover, we propose a cross-validation metric learning approach to learn a distance metric for dimension reduction in the multiple-index model. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to reduce the dimensionality of multiple-index models in a framework of metric learning. This work has been published in Statistica Sinica. (4c) The PI and CI had numerous discussions focusing on how to estimate the density function with an explicit form for high-dimensional data such as medical imaging data, it is a pity that we still don't have a satisfactory solution yet. The CI provided several ideas to solve this challenging problem including GANs, diffusion models, etc. We will continue to work along this direction for a finer solution.

14306219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306219.value: To summarize, the main findings of this research are several new and efficient statistical technologies to model and analyze distributed datasets under different settings, including 1. A statistical procedure to combine distributed case-control studies for efficiency improvement. 2. Semi-supervised inference of nonparametric logistic regression. 3. A general M-estimation under semi-supervised framework. 4. A semi-supervised inference procedure for blockwise missing data. 4. An efficient fused learning for distributed imbalanced data. They have been shown to enjoy favorable theoretical properties. Though it is not easy to directly extend some of our methods to high dimensional setting, the PI and her coauthors have new findings in analyzing high dimensional data associated with this project: 1. A quantile correlation-based variable selection. 2. A post-inference procedure for high dimensional case-control studies. 3. Metric-learning via cross validation. We believe the outcome of this research is significant and is of theoretical and practical values.

14306219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306219.value: The methodologies in the main outputs of this projects, both semiparametric logistic regression or nonparametric logistic regression, work well for low-dimensional case. One interesting direction for future work is to extend the univariate nonparametric logistic model to an additive model to handle the multi-dimensional predictors. Another area that deserves further exploration is to consider deep neural networks in approximating the target function, since deep neural networks have been shown to be powerful in approximating multivariate or high dimensional functions. Thus, the exploration of promising methods in analyzing distributed or semi-supervised datasets with higher dimension will be a future research direction for further development.

14306219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306219.value: Overall, we think the outputs of this project are sufficient and all objectives have been addressed and achieved, which might provide better ways for practitioners and researchers to integrate datasets from multiple sources and identify significant important variables. We are fortune to have the timely support from RGC, without which everything would not have been possible.

14306419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306419.value: The aim of this project is to study core-collapse supernovae through gravitational-wave measurements and simulation. We propose to construct analysis tools for the detection and reconstruction of core-collapse supernovae in data from ground-based gravitational-wave detectors and perform numerical simulations of core-collapse supernovae with different input physics, such as alternative theories of gravity. Massive stars are expected to undergo core collapse once they burn all their thermonuclear fuel. If the resulting iron core becomes too massive, it will undergo a collapse which often forms a neutron star or a black hole. During this collapse, a rebound is expected to produce a shock wave that interacts with other infalling matter. Whether the shock is successful in shedding the outer layer of the star determines whether an explosion in the form of a supernova occurs. The exact mechanism of such explosions remains unclear, because of the complex interaction amongst various branches of physics. Understanding this process means making major advances in understanding the interaction of fundamental forces of nature, but also important astrophysical processes such as the formation of neutron stars and black holes, and the production of heavy elements that have important applications to our daily lives. Observing core-collapse supernovae may provide us with direct input into the relevant physics. Gravitational-wave measurements, in particular, can provide novel insight into the explosion mechanism. However, problems such as the lack of robust models, and the existence of loud noise sources mean that significant work remains to be done. Conversely, simulating the physics inside these collapsing stars provides part of the insight into the problem of core-collapse supernovae. Various codes focus on different aspects of this problem, such as stellar structure and evolution, nuclear and neutrino physics, hydrodynamics, kinetic theory and general relativity. We propose a research effort that contributes to both methods of investigating core-collapse supernovae. In particular, we propose to develop model-specific and model-agnostic analysis techniques to capture different parts of the gravitational-wave signal emitted by core-collapse supernovae. Moreover, we propose to study core-collapse supernovae through numerical simulations with different input physics, including alternative theories of gravity. 該項目的目的是通過重力波測量和模擬研究核心坍縮超新星。我們提出構建分析工具，用於檢測和重建來自地基重力波探測器的核心坍縮超新星訊號，並加入不同的物理計算（如廣義相對論的替代理論）對核心坍縮超新星進行數值模擬。 一旦燃燒了所有的熱核燃料，巨大的恆星預計會發生核心崩塌。如果所得的鐵芯變得太大，它將經歷坍塌，並形成中子星或黑洞。在這些坍塌期間，反彈將產生與其他物質相互作用的衝擊波。衝擊波是否成功地脫離恆星的外層決定了是否發生了超新星形式的爆炸。 然而，這種爆炸的確切機制仍不清楚。各種物理分支之間複雜的相互作用決定了爆炸。如果理解這一過程，我們將在理解自然基本作用力的相互作用方面取得重大進展，同時也將重要的天體形成過程，如中子星和黑洞的形成，以及重要元素的產生，這些重要元素對我們的日常生活有重要意義。 對這些坍縮恆星內部的物理進行數值模擬，可以深入了解核心坍縮超新星的問題。各種程式集中在這個問題的不同方面，如恆星結構和演化，核物理和微中子物理，流體動力學，動力學理論和廣義相對論。 反過來，觀察核心坍縮超新星可能會為我們理解相關的物理，特別是重力波測量可以提供對爆炸機制的新見解。然而，諸如缺乏可靠的模型以及存在大量噪聲源之類的問題意味著仍有大量研究工作要做。 我們提出的研究工作有助於研究核心坍縮超新星的兩種方法。特別是，我們建議在重力的替代理論中擴展我們現有的模擬，以研究重力在這個過程中的影響。此外，我們還希望研究從中微子和電磁觀測中獲得的信息。最後，我們將開發模型化和未模型化的分析技術，以捕獲核心坍縮超新星發射的重力波信號的不同部分。

14306419.label: Realisation of objectives
14306419.value: 1. Explore the use of a model-agnostic analysis to search for and reconstruct gravitational waves emitted by core-collapse supernovae The project objective of exploring the use of a model-agnostic analysis to search for and reconstruct gravitational waves emitted by core-collapse supernovae has been achieved based on the provided publication abstracts. Our studies demonstrate methods to infer the presence of alternative polarizations alongside tensor polarizations in gravitational wave signals. Remarkably, fixing the polarizations to those from General Relativity, we can construct a model-agnostic analysis to search for and reconstruct gravitational waves emitted by core-collapse supernovae. 2. Explore the use of template-based techniques to search for deterministic portions of the gravitational-wave signals from core-collapse supernovae The project objectives of exploring template-based techniques to search for deterministic portions of gravitational-wave signals from core-collapse supernovae have been achieved to a significant extent based on the provided publication abstracts. The Summed Parallel Infinite Impulse Response (SPIIR) pipeline successfully utilizes template-based techniques, such as infinite impulse response (IIR) filters and singular-value-decomposition (SVD) technique, to detect gravitational-wave signals with extreme low-latency matched filtering. Additionally, the aligned-spin template bank constructed by the Gstreamer and Ligo Algorithm Library (GstLAL) covers a wide parameter space, including systems relevant to core-collapse supernovae, demonstrating a comprehensive approach to template-based gravitational-wave signal analysis. Finally, we have proposed a novel method to compare gravitational-wave data to simulations, a cornerstone for template-based searches. 3. Improve understanding of core-collapse supernovae by numerical simulation The project objectives of improving understanding of core-collapse supernovae through numerical simulation have been partially achieved based on the provided publication abstracts (see Part C). The research has made progress in linking gravitational-wave signals from binary neutron stars (possible end products of supernovae) to fundamental oscillation modes and mass ratios, potentially advancing gravitational-wave asteroseismology. Additionally, advancements in the General-relativistic multigrid numerical (Gmunu) code have been made, enhancing its capabilities in solving complex equations related to general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics and radiation transport. Further research and development are needed to fully achieve the project objectives.

14306419.label: Major findings and research outcome
14306419.value: GRAVITATIONAL-WAVE SIGNALS FROM BINARY NEUTRON STARS: * Investigated the relationship between neutron star oscillation frequencies and gravitational-wave frequencies. * Found a 1% difference between the two frequencies across various binary neutron star systems. * Showed tidal resonance conditions are met near merger, explaining universal relations between tidal deformability. * Established a link between gravitational-wave signals, oscillation modes, and mass ratio in binary neutron star systems. GENERAL-RELATIVISTIC MULTIGRID NUMERICAL CODE (GMUNU): * Developed a code for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics with efficient multigrid elliptic solvers. * Implemented methods to handle magnetic monopoles and ensure divergence-free conditions. * Showed robust performance in solving relativistic magnetohydrodynamics problems. GENERAL-RELATIVISTIC RESISTIVE MAGNETOHYDRODYNAMICS: * Implemented solvers and divergence-free handling methods in Gmunu code. * Demonstrated robust recovery from ideal to highly resistive magnetohydrodynamics limits. * Applied in modeling magnetized neutron stars, showing the impact of different handling methods on star evolution. PULSATIONS OF HIGHLY MAGNETIZED NEUTRON STARS: * Investigated pulsation modes of highly magnetized neutron stars with strong magnetic fields. * Showed how extreme magnetic fields affect pulsation mode frequencies and stellar compactness. GENERAL-RELATIVISTIC MULTIGROUP RADIATION TRANSPORT MODULE: * Implemented a radiation transport module in Gmunu code for neutron star and supernovae modeling. * Demonstrated the handling of radiation-matter interactions and stiff terms in optically thick regions. POLARIZATION CONTENT OF GRAVITATIONAL WAVES: * Explored methods to infer the presence of alternative polarizations in gravitational wave signals. * Developed techniques based on null stream for sources with electromagnetic counterparts. * Applied methods to analyze binary neutron star signal GW170817, showing consistency with tensor-only hypothesis. SPIIR PIPELINE FOR GRAVITATIONAL WAVE ALERTS: * Introduced the SPIIR pipeline for low-latency matched filtering in gravitational wave detection. * Accelerated with GPUs, achieving median latency of less than 9 seconds. * Demonstrated the potential for joint time-domain observations and early public alerts for binary coalescence systems. GRAVITATIONAL-WAVE DATA ANALYSIS WITH PSI4 TEMPLATES: * Developed a framework to analyze gravitational-wave data directly using ψ4 templates. * Addressed integration artifacts in strain templates, improving the analysis of gravitational wave signals. ALIGNED-SPIN TEMPLATE BANK FOR GRAVITATIONAL WAVEFORMS: * Constructed an aligned-spin template bank for gravitational wave analysis in Advanced LIGO and Virgo data. * Expanded parameter space coverage for merging compact binary systems, including neutron star-neutron star and black hole-black hole binaries. These research outcomes contribute to advancing our understanding of gravitational wave astronomy, outcomes of supernovae, and numerical methods in relativistic simulations.

14306419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14306419.value: The research project on gravitational-wave signals from supernovae shows promise in further development by exploring the link between the frequency of quadrupolar oscillations of neutron stars (the remnants of supernovae) and gravitational-wave frequencies. The proposed course of action involves investigating the relationship between fundamental oscillation modes, mass ratio, and gravitational-wave signals. Additionally, the development of the General-relativistic multigrid numerical (Gmunu) code for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics presents opportunities for more stable and accurate simulations. Further research could focus on applying these advancements to study the role of magnetic fields on core-collapse suprernovae, as well as improving the detection and parameter inference of gravitational-wave signals from these sources.

14306419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14306419.value: This research project has delved into understanding how exploding stars behave, how the vibrations of their end products relate to gravitational waves, and how extreme conditions like strong magnetic fields affect their pulsations. We have also developed advanced computer codes to simulate these phenomena accurately. By studying these aspects, scientists can better grasp gravitational wave astronomy, supernova outcomes, and improve the accuracy of simulations in extreme conditions. The research helps us learn more about the universe and how these cosmic events shape the world around us.

14306519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14306519.value: Icosahedral carboranes are carbon-boron molecular clusters with many features such as σ-aromaticity, spherical geometry, high thermal and chemical stability. These unique characteristics make them attractive building blocks for boron neuron capture therapy agents in medicine, functional units in supramolecular design/materials, and versatile ligands in organometallic/coordination chemistry. Generally, the preparation of cage C-substituted carboranes is realized via the deprotonation of weakly acidic cage C-H proton by strong bases, followed by reaction with electrophiles. This general method is, however, limited to sp3-carbon electrophiles only and also suffers from strong basic conditions. Hence, it is highly desirable to develop new synthetic methodologies for selective and facile synthesis of cage C-substituted carboranes. In recent years, photocatalysis has emerged as an increasingly viable tool to realize cross coupling reactions. One of the most important features of these reactions is the achieved reactivity via the open shell reactive species, which is otherwise difficult or impossible by other means of chemical process. Our recent preliminary results show that photoarylation of iodocarboranes with arenes serves as a clean and facile method for the synthesis of cage C-arylated o-carboranes (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2017, 56, 712). Inspired by this proof-of-concept study, we plan in this proposal to utilize photochemical process for the generation of carbon-centered carboranyl radicals, aiming at the development of new methodologies for the synthesis of a variety of cage C-substituted carboranes. The elucidation of reaction mechanism is also an important subject of this proposal. It is anticipated that this research will result in a new toolbox for the preparation of a new class of cage C-substituted carborane derivatives and enhance our fundamental understanding of photochemical reactions of carboranes. It will also be fascinating to discover what lies beyond. 碳硼烷是一類由碳、氫、硼組成的二十面體簇合物。它們擁有σ芳香性，球形結構，熱及化學穩定性等諸多特性。這些特性使得碳硼烷作為非常重要的結構单元出現在硼中子捕獲化療試劑，超分子材料及配體中。碳硼烷籠碳的衍生化通常利用籠碳氫的酸性，其被強鹼去質子化後與親電試劑反應得到籠碳衍生物。然而，此方法僅適用於sp3雜化的及強鹼耐受的親電試劑。因此，發展簡便、溫和並具有選擇性的碳硼烷衍生化方法意義重大。近年來，光反應已逐漸成為一種重要的合成手段以實現偶聯反應，這類反應的特性就是反應過程中形成用其它化學過程不易獲得的活潑單電子自由基中間體。基於這些工作，我們以碘代碳硼烷為自由基前體，初步實現了光誘導的碳硼烷籠碳的芳基化(Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2017, 56, 712)。根據這個結果，我們計畫利用光化學的過程來形成碳硼烷的籠碳自由基，以發展出一系列碳硼烷籠碳官能團化的新方法。反應機理的研究闡釋也是這項研究計畫中非常重要的一部分。我們預計此研究將為碳硼烷籠碳取代物的合成提供一類新方法，並且，它將提高我們對碳硼烷參與的光反應的認知。同時，我們也期待意外的發現。

14306519.label: Realisation of objectives
14306519.value: Carboranes are finding a broad range of applications encompassing materials, polymers, catalysis, organometallic/coordination chemistry and more. As a result, increasing efforts have been directed toward the area of carborane functionalization. In this project, we have developed new methodologies for selective cage carbon functionalization of o-carboranes via cage carbon-centered carboranyl radicals with or without light irradiation. Our proof-of-concept study has shown that the cage C-I bond in 1-iodo-o-carboranes can undergo homoleptic cleavage upon ultraviolet light irradiation to generate efficiently carbon-centered carboranyl radicals. We speculate that these carboranyl radicals can react with radical acceptors, leading to the formation of a new class of cage C-substituted carboranes. Accordingly, a transition-metal-free coupling protocol between iodocarboranes and terminal alkynes enabled by light at room temperature has been developed, leading to the synthesis of a variety of 1-alkynyl-o-carboranes. Moreover, following this strategy, the introduction of 1-I-3-aryl-o-carboranes or 1-I-2-aryl-o-carboranes results in the formation of o-carborane-fused cyclics. Interestingly, when 1-I-3-(p-R-C6H4)-o-carboranes are chosen as coupling partners, unexpected R-group migration products are also isolated. Based on the results of control experiments and isolation of the key intermediates, a possible reaction mechanism is then proposed, involving the formation of spiro radical species. Following the same strategy, a synthetic method to alkenylated-o-carboranes via photoalkenylation of iodocarboranes with unactivated alkenes has been achieved. This reaction features a transition-metal-free protocol, light-promoted reaction with mild reaction conditions, broad substrate scope and good functional group tolerance. Control experiments suggest that the reaction may involve the cage C-centered radical species. The aforementioned two methods require iodocarboranes as starting materials. We wondered if non-prefunctionalized carboranes could serve as the starting materials. By merging photochemistry with base metal catalysis, a light-promoted Cu catalyzed cage C-arylation of o-carboranes with a variety of aryl iodides at room temperature has been developed, leading to the preparation of a variety of 1-aryl-o-carboranes and o-carborane-fused cyclics. Employment of earth abundant copper as catalyst, this method also demonstrates the advantages of using simple o-carboranes as starting material, not prefunctionalized iodocarboranes, and mild reaction condition under room temperature. Further control experiments suggest that the reaction undergoes a radical pathway facilitated by Cu catalyst. Our previous work shows that o-carborynes exhibit biradical properties upon UV light irradiation. We thought that o-carborynes could serve as synthons for cage C functionalization. Subsequently, using 1-Li-2-OTf-o-C2B10H10 as precursor, o-carboryne undergoes an efficient [2 + 2] cycloaddition with a large variety of vinyl ethers at room temperature to give a series of carborane-fused cyclobutanes in very good to high isolated yields. This reaction is compatible with many functional groups and has a very broad substrate scope ranging from alkyl, aryl to silyl substituted vinyl ethers. In addition, o-carboryne undergoes an efficient [4 + 2] cycloaddition with various conjugated enynes, followed by a subsequent [2 + 2] cycloaddition at room temperature, generating a series of carborane-fused tricyclo[6.4.0.02,7]dodeca-2,12-dienes in moderate to high isolated yields. This reaction is compatible with many functional groups and has a broad substrate scope. A reactive carborane-fused 1,2-cyclohexadiene intermediate is involved, which is supported by experimental results and DFT calculations. Furthermore, o-carboryne undergoes at room temperature an efficient ene reaction with a large variety of alkynes and alkenes possessing α-CH proton to give a series of o-carboranyl allenes and alkenes in good to high isolated yields. This reaction has a broad substrate scope from alkyl, aryl to silyl substituents. This protocol provides a facile synthetic method to access cage C-substituted carboranyl allenes and alkenes. In summary, we have developed several new methods on the basis of carbon-centered carboranyl radicals for the preparation of a wide range of functionalized carborane molecules, which might find valuable applications in many realms. The associated reaction mechanisms have also been investigated via the combination of control experiments and DFT calculations. The results offer a better fundamental understanding of hypervalent carbon radical reaction in o-carboranes, which in turn would shed light on how to control the selectivity for the effective synthesis of target products. This project has been very successfully carried out and all objectives have been achieved.
