14307819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307819.value: This project aims to systematically explore the fabrication methods and formation mechanisms of structured organometal halide perovskite (OHP) thin films and their applications in light-emitting devices. The core tasks include (1) development of the fabrication strategies for size controllable OHP structures; (2) improvement of the OHP properties with additive-assisted growth and hybrid passivation; and (3) investigation of the structure formation and structure-property correlations in OHP devices with new optical microscopy and microspectroscopy methods. Recently OHP materials have emerged as a promising class of light-emitting semiconductor with high photoluminescence efficiency, great color tunability and low-temperature processability. OHP based optically-pumped lasers and light-emitting diodes (LEDs) have been demonstrated, and the external quantum efficiency of OHP LEDs has just exceeded the benchmark 20% in some spectral regimes. A critical factor that leads to the efficiency breakthrough is improvement of light-extraction in the device, achieved by introducing submicron structures in the OHP layer. (A planar OHP layer tends to trap a large portion of light due to its high refractive index as compared to the neighboring layers.) However, despite the reported observation of the phenomenon, it remains unclear how the formation process and final dimension of the OHP structures can be controlled. Furthermore, suitable crystal growth and defect passivation methods for these structures are yet to be systematically explored. This project is devised to address the aforementioned issues through material and structure design, processing development and application of new characterization tools. Firstly, we will focus on the fabrication methods to create micro- or submicro-structures of OHPs to allow for manipulation of light out-coupling in the devices. Both spontaneous formation and template-guided formation (on physically structured surface or via mold confinement) processes will be explored. Secondly, to ensure high crystal quality and low defect density of the OHP structures, we will explore the use of molecular additives in controlling the crystal growth and substrate modification and develop a hybrid passivation approach to combine the additives with post-deposition metal halide-treatment for surface defect passivation. Thirdly, we will systematically characterize and optimize the OHP structures and devices. In particular, quantitative phase microscopy will be applied to in-situ study the OHP formation processes and electroabsorption microspectroscopy will be developed to study the device physics and degradation mechanisms in the new structured OHP devices. The fundamental findings and technological know-hows generated from this project will contribute to the performance enhancement and commercialization of OHP based LED and laser technologies. 該項目旨在系統地探索結構化有機金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦（OHP）薄膜的製備方法和形成機理及其在發光器件中的應用。核心任務包括（1）開發尺寸可控的OHP結構的製備方法; （2）通過添加輔助生長和混合鈍化改善OHP性質; （3）用新的光學顯微鏡和顯微光譜法研究OHP薄膜的微觀結構形成和結構- 性質相關性。 最近，OHP材料已經成為一種極具應用前景的發光半導體，具有高光致發光效率，高顏色可調性和低溫加工性。基於OHP的光泵浦激光器和發光二極管（LED）已被實現，並且OHP LED在一些光譜波段中的外部量子效率超過20％。導致LED效率飛躍的關鍵因素之一是通過在OHP層中引入亞微米結構來實現器件中光提取的改進。 （與相鄰層相比，平面OHP層具有高折射率，因而其發光無法被導出器件。）然而，該種結構如何形成、如何對其尺寸進行控制仍是為解決的問題。此外，結構化薄膜的晶體生長和缺陷鈍化方法仍需探索。 該項目旨在通過設計材料和薄膜結構、研發薄膜製備方法、以及應用新的表徵工具來解決上述問題。首先，我們將專注於製造微觀或亞微結構的製造方法以製備可以優化光耦合的OHP結構。將探索自發形成和模板引導形成的薄膜結構化過程。其次，為了確保OHP結構的高晶體質量和低缺陷密度，我們將探索分子添加劑在控制晶體生長和基板改性中的應用，並開發一種混合鈍化方法，將添加劑與後沉積金屬鹵化物處理相結合用於表面缺陷鈍化。第三，我們將系統地優化OHP結構和裝置。應用定量相顯微鏡原位研究OHP薄膜形成過程，並將開發電吸收顯微光譜法來研究新結構化OHP器件中的器件物理和降解機制。 通過該項目發現的新機理和技術方法將有助於提高基於OHP的LED和激光器件的性能、促進該技術的商業化。

14307819.label: Realisation of objectives
14307819.value: We have achieved all the project objectives and developed several patterning strategies to realize structured perovskite films for LED and laser applications. Below please find the research achievements corresponding to each objective: Object 1: We realized OHP micro- and submicro-structures with both spontaneous formation (via the use of excess organic ammonium halide precursors or molecular additives) and template-guided formation. In particular, for the template-guided formation strategy, explored three post-deposition patterning methods, namely e-beam lithography, thermal imprinting and holographic parallel femtosecond-laser processing. We found that the quality of the patterned structures is highly dependent on the morphology and stability of the flat films before processing; accordingly, we developed a two-step treatment, which combines self-assembled monolayer to enhance the perovskite-substrate interactions and thermal pressing to confine and direct perovskite crystallization, to obtain ultrasmooth (e.g., rms roughness of 0.3 nm) and compact perovskite films. Combining the two-step method with the use of Dion–Jacobson (D–J) phase perovskites, we obtained thin films that exhibit excellent stability during various types of processing, including electron-beam lithography, thermal pressing, laser cutting, solvent development and rinse. As a result, high quality submicron structures leading to record high laser quality factor (i.e., Q factor of 30,000) for thin-film perovskites have been achieved. Objective 2: To understand how molecular additives, or more specifically, the molecular spacers in large-n D-J phase perovskites, affect the structure-property relations in the OHP structures, we investigated a series of molecular spacers, ranging from linear alkyldiammonium to phenyl and piperidinium derivatives and analogous. A comprehensive comparative study on two representative D–J perovskites based on 4-(aminomethyl)piperidinium (4AMP) and 1,4-diaminobutane (BDA) spacers was carried out. The results suggest that the lasing threshold is primarily determined by the nonradiative decay pathways and multicarrier recombination mechanisms, which together govern the carrier build-up in the 3D perovskite phase component; on the other hand, the quality factor (Q factor) of the lasers is extremely sensitive to the surface roughening of the film during nanofabrication. All these factors are affected by the structure of the molecular spacers. Objectives 3 & 5: We explored surface treatment of the FAPbI3 perovskite films with phenylalkylammonium iodide molecules of varying alkyl chain lengths. Combining experimental characterization and theoretical modelling, we show that these molecules stabilize the perovskite through suppression of iodide ion migration. The stabilization effect is enhanced with increasing chain length due to the stronger binding of the molecules with the perovskite surface, as well as the increased steric hindrance to reconfiguration for accommodating ion migration. The passivation also reduces the surface defects, resulting in a high radiance and delayed EQE roll-off. Using the optimized passivation molecule, phenylpropylammonium iodide, we achieved a high radiance of 1282.8 W/(sr × m^2) and a record T50 half-lifetime of 130 hrs under a high stress current density of 100 mA/cm^2 (based on the empirical stress luminance/current - T50 relation, this corresponds to a T50 of more than 1000 hours under 20 mA/cm^2 stress). Furthermore, by introducing an ultrathin PMMA interlayer in the PeLEDs to modulate charge injection balance, we obtained an external quantum efficiency of 21.2%. Objective 4: We have applied both quantitative phase microscopy and electroabsorption (EA) microspectroscopy to study the OHP films and devices. While the microscopy systems can monitor the overall film optical transition during crystallization and degradation, the spatial resolution is still limited to several microns. Nevertheless, we found the EA spectroscopy a powerful tool to study the degradation process of PeLEDs during operation as it can directly evaluate the stability of each functional layer (i.e., charge transporting layers and light-emitting layer) by monitoring their unique optical signatures. The EA measurements unambiguously reveal that the degradation of the PeLEDs occurs predominantly in the perovskite layer. With finite element method-based device modeling, we further point out that the degradation is likely to initiate from the interface between the perovskite and hole-transporting layers and that the interface defects could further accelerate the degradation.

14307819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307819.value: 1. By combining self-assembled monolayer assisted film growth with thermal pressing, we obtain a series of compact and extremely smooth D–J phase perovskite thin films that exhibit excellent stability during electron-beam lithography, solvent development and rinse. Combining spectroscopic and morphological characterizations, we further demonstrate how organic spacers can be used to fine tune the photophysical properties and processability of the perovskite films. The distributed-feedback lasers based on the D–J phase perovskites exhibit low lasing threshold, record high Q factor (up to 30,000) and stability. The manuscript based on this work has recently been accepted by Science Advances (Publication #4). 2. Applying extensively excess ammonium halides in forming perovskite microstructures is a widely used approach to achieve high-performance perovskite LEDs. In this study we pointed out that the electric-field driven diffusion of excess iodide ions, originated from the use of excess ammonium halide, is the dominant factor for performance degradation at high voltage/current and demonstrated a simple wash-off treatment to address this issue. We also achieved an external quantum efficiency of 21.2% by introducing an ultrathin PMMA interlayer in the PeLEDs to modulate charge injection balance. The work has been published on ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces (Publication #3). 3.We explored surface treatment of the FAPbI3 perovskite films with phenylalkylammonium iodide molecules of varying alkyl chain lengths. Combining experimental characterization and theoretical modelling, we show that these molecules stabilize the perovskite through suppression of iodide ion migration. The stabilization effect is enhanced with increasing chain length due to the stronger binding of the molecules with the perovskite surface, as well as the increased steric hindrance to reconfiguration for accommodating ion migration. Using the optimized passivation molecule, we achieved a high radiance of 1282.8 W/(sr × m2) and a record T50 half-lifetime of 130 hrs under a high stress current density of 100 mA/cm2. The work has been published on Nature Communications (Publication #1). 4. We introduced electroabsorption spectroscopy (EA) to study the degradation process of PeLEDs during operation and directly evaluate the stability of each functional layer (i.e., charge transporting layers and light-emitting layer) by monitoring their unique optical signatures. The EA measurements and device modelling unambiguously reveal that the degradation of the PeLEDs occurs predominantly in the perovskite layer and in particular, the interface between the perovskite and hole-transporting layers. The study has been published on Advanced Functional Materials (Publication #2).

14307819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307819.value: The patterning methods and perovskite materials developed in this project can be used to realize perovskite micro-LEDs as well as photonic devices such as lasers, metasurfaces for structural coloring or chiral photoluminescence, as well as polarization-sensitive photodetectors.

14307819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307819.value: Optoelectronic and photonic devices based on inorganic materials have been widely used and will continue to dominate the market in the foreseeable future. On the other hand, organic/inorganic hybrid perovskite materials, which combine excellent color tunability and high absorption/photoluminescence efficiency with low-temperature processability and mechanical flexibility, have shown great promise in enabling novel optoelectronic/photonic devices with lower cost and new functions. Through this project, we have developed a variety of techniques to create structured perovskites in a controllable fashion and provided recipes for providing effective defect passivation of these structures. Such know-hows will be valuable to create high quality perovskite photonic structures and devices. Furthermore, the fundamental findings on the relations among the material composition, structure formation process and ultimate optical and electronic properties of the perovskite structures shed light on design and optimization of next-generation low-cost and high-performance perovskite based electronics.

14307919.label: Project Objectives
14307919.value: We will systematically investigate the structure-property-performance relationship of electrolyte solvent on the O2/KO2 reaction potential, electrode kinetics and reversibility via well-defined electrode and analytical platforms. We aim to understand how each solvent property including donor number, acceptor number, dielectric constant, and viscosity affects the K-O2 reaction potential, electrode kinetics, and reversibility. Since the morphology of the discharge product potassium superoxide (KO2) directly affects the achievable capacity, we aim to develop quantitative understanding on factors dictating KO2 morphology including (i) facet-dependent solvent adsorption and (ii) the competition between O2 reduction (consumption) and O2 supplement, from which to develop strategies to achieve desire non-passivating KO2 morphology. In order to address the critical issue of low capacity and pre-mature cell termination (KO2 blocking at the O2-entrance) in the conventional flooded K-O2 electrode, we will develop two types of non-flooded cathode structure: (i) partially wetted electrodes with surface tension-controlled thin films and/or non-wetting binders to prevent pore-flooding; (ii) immobilized electrolyte film analogous to proton-exchange membrane fuel cell. We will investigate the influence of air impurities including H2O and CO2 on the reaction kinetics, electrochemical and chemical reversibility and (side)reaction mechanisms of K-O2 reactions and apply redox mediator to decompose potassium carbonates (K2CO3) and other by-products. We will exploit comprehensive characterization techniques coupling with isotope labelling to study the reaction and degradation mechanisms of the K-O2 reactions electrodes including time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), online electrochemical mass spectrometry (OEMS), ambient pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), Raman spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction (XRD).

14307919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14307919.value: 該項目旨在開發高效可逆以及高容量的鉀氧電極，揭示電極和電解質的結構 - 性質- 性能之間的關係，以及研究電池工作過程中的衰減機理。 可充電鉀氧電池擁有極具吸引力的理論能量密度（935 Wh/kg），與其他鹼金屬氧氣電池相比具有低成本以及因其快速且可逆的單電子反應而顯著提高的能量效率和使用壽命。鉀氧系統的這些獨特優勢使其成為低成本和大規模儲能有希望的候選者。 然而，鉀氧電池的發展仍處於研究的初期階段。開發可實用鉀氧電極所面臨的關鍵挑戰包括（1）因快速電極鈍化和低電極利用率而導致的低容量; （2）對電解質如何影響反應動力學和可達到的放電容量缺乏基本的了解; （3）使用純氧氣而非空氣顯著增加了系統複雜性和成本。 在此項目中，我們採用系統的方法揭露電解質和電極結構的結構 - 性質 - 性能關之間的關係對鉀氧正極的功率能力，能量和化學/電化學可逆性的影響。具體來說，我們將（1）通過完善的分析工具，包括循環伏安法（CV），旋轉圓盤電極以及電化學阻抗譜，研究電解質溶劑結構 - 性質 - 性能之間的關係對氧氣 /超氧化鉀反應電位，電極動力學，形貌和可逆性的影響；（2）開發兩種非完全浸潤正極結構，包括部分浸潤電極和非流動性薄膜聚合物電解質。非完全浸潤正極的設計對於在高電流密度下在形成固態超氧化鉀從而實現高電極利用率是非常必要的; （3）研究包括水和二氧化碳在內的空氣雜質對反應動力學，電化學/化學可逆性的影響，並製定緩解策略; （4）採用全方位的表征技術結合同位素標記的手段研究鉀氧反應（正極，負極和界面）的反應和衰減機理，包括飛行時間二次離子質譜，原位電化學質譜，近室壓X射線光電子能譜，傅裏葉變換紅外光譜，拉曼光譜和X射線衍射。 通過此項目的研究，我們將指出發展適用於低成本和大規模儲能應用的具有實用能量和功率能力的高效鉀氧電極所需的基本理解和設計策略。

14307919.label: Realisation of objectives
14307919.value: All the project objectives are achieved providing fundamental insights into electrode-electrolyte design and degradation mechanism of potassium-oxygen Batteries. We investigated the role of different electrolyte including diglyme (DG) and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) on the O2/KO2 reaction potential, electrode kinetics and reversibility and discharge product morphologies. Comprehensive spectroscopic techniques were employed to study the stability of the O2/KO2 reactions. We investigated the key factors that dictate the KO2 morphologies and achieved capacities including (i) the desolvation energy of KO2 in different electrolytes; (ii) the competition between O2 reduction (consumption) and O2 supplement, from which to correlate the achieved capacities and morphologies of discharge products; (iii) electrode wetting degree, i.e. the ratio of electrolyte amount to the total void volume of cathode. We investigated the influence of air impurities (e.g. carbon dioxide and water) on the electrochemical and chemical stability of K−O2 reactions including (i) quantitative understanding of how water and CO2 affect the chemical and electrochemical reversibility of the cathode reactions; (ii) exploring the role of water and CO2 under true ambient air conditions on K−O2 reactions. We investigated the effect of air impurities (e.g. CO2, H2O) on the cycle performance of K−based air batteries. Various operation environments including pure oxygen, 21.8% O2 in N2 and true ambient air were examined. Comprehensive characterization techniques were employed to reveal the side products accumulated during cycle. We exploited comprehensive characterization techniques to study the reaction and degradation mechanisms of the K-O2 reactions. We designed an in situ ambient pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) cell to probe potassium–oxygen chemistry at the solid/liquid interface via APXPS to unravel the reaction and degradation mechanism of K−air batteries. In addition, we extended the solvent beyond DMSO and DG with a wider range of donor/acceptor number, dielectric constant, and viscosity and evaluate their influence on the K-O2 reaction potential, electrode kinetics, and reversibility. We studied the reaction and degradation mechanisms of the K-O2 reactions using online electrochemical mass spectroscopy (OEMS) coupling with isotope labelling to study the reaction interface of the K−O2 batteries.

14307919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14307919.value: We exploited a strong donating solvent, e.g. dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), to stabilize the discharge product in K−O2 system. Extensive electrochemical and chemical characterizations results indicate that K−O2 redox has fast kinetics and superior reversibility in the strong-donating solvent DMSO than in the weak-donating solvent diglyme. Direct probing of metal–oxygen chemistry at the solid/liquid interface is essential to unravel the reaction mechanism of metal–air batteries. Ambient pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) is an effective tool to study metal–oxygen reactions but has been limited to solid-state environments. In this project, for the first time, we demonstrate in situ probing of potassium oxygen reduction/evolution reaction (ORR/OER) via APXPS in ionic liquid-based air batteries. We reveal the formation and oxidation of K2O/K2O2 in K–O2 batteries, highlighting new reaction pathways in addition to the widely established one-electron process in K–O2 batteries. Importantly, we show that the formation and subsequent oxidation of K2O2 trigger irreversible cell chemistry, which could be responsible for capacity decay in K–O2 batteries. We further show that common impurities in air such as H2O/CO2 reduce chemical reversibility of ORR and OER. This study reveals root causes of irreversible cell chemistry in K–air batteries via direct probing of ionic liquid-based air batteries via APXPS, which can be widely applied to study the chemistry of solid/liquid interfaces of metal–air batteries (Part C-1). Singlet oxygen was reported a major root cause for the electrolyte/electrode degradation of metal-oxygen batteries (Part C-3). We demonstrate an effective strategy to suppress 1O2 using redox mediators. Using operando spectroscopy techniques, we show that 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-1-piperidinyloxy (TEMPO), as a model redox mediator, drastically reduces 1O2 formation and reduces the by-product generation. The 1O2 suppression effect is attributed to an increased intersystem crossing rate induced by redox mediators, with which the relaxation of a singlet-state intermediate to a triplet-state one is accelerated. We further show that this 1O2 suppression effect applies universally across six common redox mediators with up to three orders of magnitude higher 1O2 suppression efficiency compared to the most efficient quencher used in metal–O2 batteries to date. We discuss the plausible governing principle dictating redox mediators’ effectiveness in suppressing 1O2. Our study achieves effective 1O2 suppression and provides guidelines for designing redox mediators for efficient and reversible metal–oxygen batteries (Part C-2).

14307919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14307919.value: The following directions are important aspects for future development. (1) Close system. The superoxide−peroxide conversion has been proven feasible with the assistant of the catalyst RuO2. We believe that developing economical catalytic cathode matrix and/or redox mediators could facilitate the reversibility of KO2/K2O2 without evolving O2. In addition, fundamental studies on KO2/K2O2 redox kinetics and the effect of electrolyte on KO2/K2O2 reversibility will provide critical insights into this novel system. (2) Solid−state K−O2/air battery. Safety challenges including flammability of nonaqueous electrolyte and K dendrite formation upon cycling could be addressed by the design of solid−state K−O2/air batteries. Solid−state oxygen battery allows fast oxygen transport but requires designs of highly conductive solid electrolyte membrane assembly to maximize the capacity and rate capability. Although solid−state K−O2 batteries have yet to be realized, it can be an important direction to achieve safe and efficient K−O2/air battery.

14307919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14307919.value: Energy storage system is the key bottleneck of the widespread of renewable energy and the development of electric vehicles (EVs). Metal–oxygen batteries are identified one of the promising next-generation energy storage systems owing to their potential to provide higher gravimetric energy density (3500 – 935 Wh kg−1) than conventional lithium−ion batteries (100 – 265 Wh kg−1). Rechargeable K−O2 batteries offer an attractive theoretical energy density (935 Wh kg−1) with a significantly improved energy efficiency and life time compared to other alkali metal−O2 batteries owing to its fast and reversible single−electron reaction. However, the development of K−O2 batteries is still in its early stage and its round-trip efficiency is still lower than lithium–ion batteries. This project systematically investigates the structure-property-performance relationship of electrolyte solvent on the O2/KO2 reaction potential, electrode kinetics and reversibility via well-defined electrode and analytical platforms. We reveal critical insights into electrode-electrolyte interface design and degradation mechanism and developed strategies to significantly improve the energy efficiency and cycle life of the K−O2 and K–air batteries.

14308019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14308019.value: High precision measurement and estimation is one of the main driving forces in scientific and technological advances. Compared to classical metrology, quantum metrology, which makes use of quantum mechanical effects such as coherence and entanglement, can achieve higher precision limits and has found wide applications in many areas, including atomic clocks, spectroscopy, magnetometry, and gravitational-wave detection. The aim of this project is to develop new schemes for quantum metrology that can lead to an even higher precision limit than the present schemes. In the standard scheme of quantum metrology, the parameter is usually assumed to be encoded in one component of the dynamics (typically in the Hamiltonian). By allowing a probe state to evolve under the dynamics, the unknown parameter can be encoded in the probe state and then estimated through measurements on the probe state. In the standard scheme, the noises during the evolution, such as dephasing and decay, are typically detrimental to the precision limit. Various strategies, including quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, have thus been exploited to suppress the noises in order to obtain higher precision limits. Instead of trying to suppress the noises, this project proposes to explore the interactive effects between the noises and the control field to improve the precision limit. Through the cooperative interplays between the noises and controls, both the Hamiltonian and the noisy operator can contribute to the parametrization of the probe state, which can lead to higher precision limits. Our preliminary calculations show that in certain regimes the cooperative scheme can even outperform the ideal unitary dynamics. The cooperative interplay between the noises and controls thus offers many new possibilities for realizing higher precision limits. The proposed project aims to identify the highest precision limits that can be achieved under this kind of cooperative schemes and to design protocols to achieve them. The project's findings will broaden the horizon of quantum metrology research and are expected to have wide implications for various applications in quantum metrology, including quantum sensing, quantum gyroscope, and quantum imaging. 高精度測量和估計是科學和技術的主要驅動力之一。與經典計量學相比，量子計量學可以達到更高的精度並已在許多領域得到廣泛應用，包括原子鐘，光譜學，磁力測定和引力波檢測等。本項目的目標是發展量子計量的新方案來達到更高的精度。 在量子計量的標準方案中，通常假設參數只被編碼在動力學的一個組成部分（通常在哈密頓量中）。在標準方案中，噪聲，例如消相干和衰減，通常對測量精度有害。各種策略，包括量子糾錯和動態去耦，都被用來抑制噪聲以獲得更高的精度。本項目則試圖探索在噪聲和控制場之間的互動效果提高精度。通過噪聲和控制之間的相互作用，哈密頓算子和噪聲的算子都可以幫助提高精度。我們的初步結果表明，在某些情況下，這種互動甚至可以勝過理想的無噪聲系統。因此，噪聲和控制之間的協作相互作用提供了實現更高精度的許多新的可能性。擬議的項目旨在確定在這種合作方案下可以達到的最高精度並設計實現它們的協議。該項目的研究結果將拓寬量子計量學的研究視野，預計將對各種應用產生廣泛的影響,如量子傳感，量子陀螺和量子成像等。

14308019.label: Realisation of objectives
14308019.value: We developed systematic methods to design the optimal cooperative scheme for quantum parameter estimation of spin systems. These developed methods were able to obtain optimal schemes to achieve high precision for parameter estimation, fully addressing the first objective related to optimal cooperative scheme for single-spin systems. We also developed the methods to address the optimal cooperative scheme for multi-spin systems, allowing them to identify the best precision limit and scaling for multi-spin systems. This second objective has also been fully realized. For the third objective on applying the cooperative scheme to different applications of quantum metrology, we successfully used the cooperative scheme to estimate parameters such as frequencies, rotating speed/axis, and orientations. Regarding the extension and experimental implementations, we studied practical physical systems, like Nuclear Magnetic Resonance, and were able to experimentally implement the cooperative schemes. Several experiments were successfully conducted and published in high-impact journals.

14308019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14308019.value: We have conducted an in-depth investigation into cooperative schemes for the estimation of Hamiltonian parameters in both single and multiple spin systems. Our findings, which include the design of optimal control strategies to enhance the precision of magnetic field estimation, have been published in Physical Review Research, volume 2, issue 033396 (2020). This has been further extended to incorporate reinforcement learning for devising optimal cooperative schemes, with the results published in Physical Review A, volume 103, issue 042615 (2021). One of the co-authors of this work, Wang Lingna, is a Ph.D. student at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK). By collaborating with the experimental group, we have successfully translated these theoretical frameworks into experimental practice. Our collaborative work led to the successful execution of an experiment aimed at the simultaneous estimation of We demonstrated that the application of optimally controlled cooperative schemes can yield the highest precision for these parameters. This work is published in Physical Review Letters, volume 126, issue 070503 (2021). Another experiment focusing on the simultaneous estimation of the magnitude and the orientation of a magnetic field was completed, with the outcomes published in Science Advances, volume 7, eabd2986 (2021). Hongzhen Chen, a Ph.D. student in our group at the time and a co-author of both experimental works, graduated in 2020. Another experiment has also been conducted on spin systems, utilizing the adiabatic evolution of critical quantum systems to further refine the precision of magnetic field estimation. This has been published in npj Quantum Information, volume 7, 170 (2021). Yu Chen, a co-author on this publication, was a Ph.D. student in our research group and is now at Tencent.

14308019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14308019.value: The methods developed in the current research could be applicable to a wide range of physical systems, including different types of quantum systems such as photonic, atomic, solid-state, and superconducting platforms. The course of actions include performing theoretical and small-scale experimental studies to assess the feasibility and potential benefits of applying the methods to the identified platforms and engaging with experts in the fields related to the target platforms to gain insights and advice on how to best adapt the methods then creating strategies for adapting the methods to the specific characteristics and constraints of the new platforms.

14308019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14308019.value: Within our project, we have successfully developed a suite of systematic methodologies designed to delineate the fundamental limits of parameter estimation within cooperative frameworks. These methods are not only theoretical but are also highly applicable, offering a pathway to the derivation of optimal schemes tailored to a spectrum of practical applications. Our optimized schemes have been instrumental in enhancing the precision of magnetic field measurements, specifically in the estimation of both its magnitude and frequency components, as well as the magnitude and orientation of the field. This level of precision is a substantial advancement for applications such as quantum magnetometry, where high-accuracy measurements are paramount. The implications of our work extend beyond the laboratory, offering transformative potential for fields that rely on precise magnetic field sensing. By pushing the boundaries of what is measurable, we are enabling new possibilities in quantum sensing technology, which could lead to breakthroughs in areas such as medical imaging, mineral exploration, and fundamental physics research.

14500019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500019.value: An increasing number of trade-in programs for electronics products, e.g., smart phones, have emerged recently due to both economical (the market has become large enough and profitable) and environmental (government regulations and incentives on waste reduction and product reuse) considerations. These programs could be operated by original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), e.g., Apple, or by third-party platforms, e.g., Huishoubao, and they target at customers who seek to salvage or upgrade their old devices. There are two widely adopted trade-in schemes: trade-in-for-upgrade and trade-in-for-cash. For the former, a customer exchanges its old device with the firm for a new or refurbished device at a price lower than directly buying the device; for the latter, a customer just sells its old device to the firm. In this project, we consider a firm who offers both trade-in schemes (i.e., a hybrid trade-in program) to acquire different types of old products which are then refurbished and put on sale. Customers with old devices choose which scheme to trade in their products; and if choosing trade-in-for-upgrade, whether buying a new product or some type of refurbished product. New customers who have no used device decide which refurbished product to buy or buy a new product. The firm dynamically sets the trade-in prices for different products and the resale prices of refurbished products so as to maximize its expected total profit over a finite selling season. We formulate the problem using stochastic dynamic programming and derive the optimal pricing decisions and their structural properties. Furthermore, as the problem is inherently high dimensional, its optimal solutions are expected to be complicated and difficult to compute and implement. We further employ techniques in approximate dynamic programming (ADP) to derive bounds and simple heuristic solutions. Finally, we collect data from some representative companies in the region to fit our model and design numerical experiments in order to demonstrate the effectiveness of our solutions. 近年來， 由於人們對經濟因素（回收市場的龐大規模與潛在利潤）以及環境因素（政府對於減少廢物和增加產品再利用出臺的法規與獎勵機制）的考慮，越來越多的電子設備（如智慧手機）“以舊換新”計畫湧現出來。這些計畫的運營者一般是原始設備製造商（如蘋果）或者第三方回收平臺（如回收寶），並將目標客戶定位在想要出售或升級自己舊設備的顧客。被廣泛採用的“以舊換新”形式有兩種，一種是以舊設備換取設備升級，另一種是以舊設備換取現金。前者指顧客將自己的舊設備交予公司並以低於直接購買的價格換獲取一部新設備或翻新設備，後者指顧客直接將自己的舊設備賣給公司獲取現金。在本項目中，我們考慮一家公司提供以上兩種“以舊換新”形式（稱爲混合“以舊換新”形式）以回收不同類型的舊設備，並將這些舊設備翻新後進行再次出售。持有舊設備的顧客會在不同的“以舊換新”形式中做出選擇。如果選擇換取設備升級，顧客還將決定換取某一種翻新設備或者新設備。沒有持有舊設備的新顧客則會直接從不同種類的翻新設備或是新設備中進行選擇購買。為了最大化有限長度銷售季裡的期望利潤，公司將動態地調整不同種產品的以舊換新價格以及翻新產品的再售賣價格。我們采用隨機動態規劃對這個問題進行建模，並推導出最優的定價策略以及其結構特性。此外，由於這個問題的高維度性，最優解十分複雜，在實際中難以計算和直接利用。為此，我們進一步運用近似動態規劃的方法來推導出邊界和簡單的近似解。最後，我們收集到該行業中幾個代表性的企業的資料來擬合我們模型，並設計數值實驗以驗證我們得到解決方案的有效性。

14500019.label: Realisation of objectives
14500019.value: All five objectives of the project have been successfully achieved. In the working paper titled “Dynamic Pricing for Multi-Product Consumer Electronics Trade-in Program,” we study the pricing problem for electronics trade-in programs. We develop a dynamic model, in which a profit-maximizing firm sets prices for both trade-in-for-cash and trade-in-for-upgrade options to acquired used products; meanwhile, it also sets prices to sell the refurbished products. Pricing is a core operational problem for electronics trade-in programs as it needs to decide the prices for thousands if not millions of different SKUs (stock keeping unit) in real time to match supply and demand effectively. Facing the challenges of solving the optimal prices using dynamic programming due to high dimensional state space, we develop simple and provably effective heuristic policies. We first propose a policy termed Static Control (SC) policy that computes prices before the start of the selling horizon. We show that its profit loss (relative to the optimal profit) is in the order of O(T^{1/2}) which matches that of the best possible stationary policy, where T is the number of selling periods. We then design a dynamic policy called the Batched-Adjustment Control (BAC) policy. Under BAC, the selling horizon is divided into different consecutive and disjoint batches for different products and the prices in one batch are updated based on the realized uncertainties in the previous batch. The profit loss of BAC is in the order of O(T^{1/3}). We numerically show that both policies perform well and BAC has superior performance over SC. We also numerically discussed several insights including the benefit of offering a hybrid trade-in program versus one with single option (either trade-in-for-cash only or trade-in-for-upgrade-only) and the value of joint optimization of both trade-in and resale prices because some firms have separate units of trade-in and resale. Finally, we study three extensions of our model: Initial stocking of new products (for upgrade purposes), additional features of trade-in programs, and vertically differentiated products. We extend the dynamic policy and its theoretical performance analysis to all three extensions. Both policies we proposed can be easily computed and scaled up for practical implementation. We submitted the paper to Operations Research (OR) and received positive feedback from the review team who recommended a “Major Revision.” We have recently completed the revision and submitted it to OR for the second-round review.

14500019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500019.value: The PI has two working papers closely related to this project. The first one is “Dynamic Pricing for Multi-Product Consumer Electronics Trade-in Program,” which is currently under second-round review at Operations Research. This paper develops a dynamic pricing model for multi-product electronics trade-in programs. We develop two simple heuristics: SC and BAC, and show both of them are asymptotic optimal when the length of the planning horizon increases. In particular, the BAC policy has a superior performance over the SC policy both analytically and numerically. Some of the numerical study is build on the real dataset from a trade-in program in China. The second paper is “Innovative Business Models in Ocean-Bound Plastic Recycling,” which is currently under major revision for M&SOM. This paper develops and analyzes several emerging business models in ocean-bound plastic (OBP) recycling. In particular, some companies, enabled by the technologies such as Blockchain, sell plastic offsets to individuals or companies and use the income to support OBP recycling in developing countries; other companies, acting as a distributor, buy and sell OBP (following certain requirements or quality standard) to large companies that use plastic in their products. Under a triple-bottom line objective (TBL), i.e., a weighted sum of profit, environmental, and social impacts, we show that selling offset or OBP generates positive environmental and social impacts. Selling OBP gives a larger share of the local supply chain surplus to the collectors than offset. Furthermore, when the firm sells both OBP and offset, it attains the highest TBL value but could perform worse than selling OBP only in the collectors' share of local supply chain surplus and worse than selling offset only in terms of its social or environmental impacts. We also perform a numerical study calibrated with real data. We find that firms that employ a TBL objective can generate much larger environmental and social impacts with a slight reduction in profits than profit-maximizing firms. For the special case where the firm aims to maximize its profit, it is easier to generate social and environmental impacts if the local price of recycled plastic is low or the number of collectors is not large. Our model and results provide theoretical support and insights into new initiatives for tackling ocean plastic pollution.

14500019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500019.value: There are several future research directions worth pursuing. For product trade-in, we have assumed the firm knows about the choice probabilities of different customers. In practice, the firm needs to learn the information from the data it has. Hence, developing data-driven algorithms for pricing decisions has both practical and theoretical values. Meanwhile, it is also important to develop a framework to measure the environmental impact of electronics trade-in programs. For OBP recycling, our paper has been focusing on firms that act as intermediate and aims to increase the recycling of OBP. We can expand the scope by including the manufacturers who use OBP in their products in the supply chains and study their interactions.

14500019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500019.value: Circular economy is playing an increasingly critical role in tackling climate change and ensuring sustainable development. In circular economy, products and materials are kept in circulation through reuse, refurbishment, and recycling. As part of circular economy, trade-in programs for electronics products, e.g., smart phones, have emerged recently due to both economic and environmental considerations. For the trade-in programs, one core operational decision is how to set the prices to acquire thousands of different used products and sell the refurbished products to match supply and demand and generate profits to the program. We develop simple and implementable algorithms for firms to set these prices and analyze their theoretical performance. Moreover, we demonstrate their performance via numerical study with real data. Another essential part of circular economy is recycling of material. We study business models that aim to alleviate ocean plastic pollution while being financially sustainable at the same time. We analyze and compare the financial, environmental, and social impacts of these business models.

14500119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500119.value: Which company is the largest customer of Hewlett-Packard and FedEx? Most people would guess it is a large international conglomerate firm, such as General Electric or WalMart. Surprisingly, the biggest buyer of these companies in recent years has been Blackstone, a private equity firm that has more than 90 portfolio companies, 460,000 employees, and USD$430 billion assets under management. More surprisingly, private equity firms like Blackstone save input cost and create value by using aggregated purchase from their portfolio companies to extract surplus from the suppliers of portfolio companies. While value creation has been an important theme of the private equity literature, existing studies suggest that private equity firms add value to portfolio companies through the following two channels. In the first channel, private equity firms discipline slack managers, mitigate agency problems, and improve operating efficiency (i.e., the “corporate governance” channel); in the second channel, private equity firms save taxes and reduce cost of capital by adopting an extremely high level of leverage (i.e., the “financial engineering” channel). To the best of our knowledge, no study has shown that private equity firms create value through supply chain channels by exercising their bargaining power based on aggregated purchases from all portfolio firms. This is a surprising “synergy” while portfolio companies of private equity firms are organized as separate legal identities. In this proposed research, we will fill this gap between business practice and academic research. Specifically, we aim to investigate 1) how acquisitions of a private equity firm would affect operating and stock performance of its portfolio companies’ major supply chain partners; 2) whether the impacts are determined by the supply-chain relationships of other portfolio companies controlled by the same private equity firm; 3) whether the impacts are conditional on the required relationship-specific investment in these relationships; 4) how supply-chain relationships affect the likelihood of a firm being targeted by private equity firms, and 5) do private equity firms that bring changes to supplier-customer relationships of their portfolio companies outperform private equity firms that do not. Ultimately, we are going to examine the wealth transfer from major supply-chain partners of portfolio companies to private equity firms and show whether the added value to portfolio companies is at a higher or lower cost of their supply chain partners. The research outputs from this proposal will generate important policy implications, e.g., how should regulators apply anti-trust laws on PE-driven acquisitions? 哪個公司是惠普(HP)和聯邦快遞(Fedex)最大的客戶？大多數回答會是類如通用電氣或者沃爾瑪這樣的跨國公司。令人意外的是，惠普(HP)和聯邦快遞(Fedex)最大的客戶是黑石公司(Blackstone)，一個擁有90個下屬公司，46萬名員工，4300億美金轄下管理資產的私募基金。更加令人吃驚的是，類似黑石一樣的私募基金公司，正在協調下屬公司的購買行為，以巨大的加總購買力向上游供應商施壓，從而在供應鏈中獲得最好的採購價格。 在研究私募基金的文獻中，如何創造價值一直是一個核心問題。現有文獻指出，私募基金主要通過兩種方式創造價值。第一，私募基金公司通過收購企業，辭退或者紀律懶散的經理人，減少委託人代理問題，從而改善企業經營效率；第二，私募企業通過運用非常高的金融槓桿，減少稅收支付，降低資產成本。就我們所知，目前還沒有任何關於私募企業通過構建下屬企業供應鏈的協調來創造價值的相關文獻。在下屬公司是以單獨法律個體構建的前提下，私募基金公司以這種供應鏈協調方式來創造價值是令人吃驚的。 本研究致力於填補文獻上的這個空白。我們的研究將會關注以下幾個問題1）私募基金公司的收購行為如何影響被收購公司上下游企業的經營和股市表現？ 2）私募公司對被收購企業供應鏈的作用是否由私募公司其他下屬企業的供應鏈組成決定？ 3）私募公司對被收購企業供應鏈的作用是否由供應鏈關係特定投資決定？ 4）供應鏈關係和供應鏈管理如何影響被私募公司收購的可能性？ 5）私募公司是否能夠通過整合下屬企業的供應鏈關係創造新的價值？最終，我們將會檢驗私募基金供應鏈管理是否產生一種從供應鏈上下游公司向私募基金的財富轉移。我們的研究將對政府如何管理私募基金產生深遠的政策效應。

14500119.label: Realisation of objectives
14500119.value: In the mid-term report, I have reported that the progress of the original project was not smooth and we cannot find meaningful results for many predictions. Here are a summary of what we have achieved: a) We have cleaned all data from Pitchbook. This task requires three steps. In step one, we retrieved all portfolio companies held by private equity firms and we constructed panel data for PE holdings; in step two, private equity firms typically buy private companies or privatize public companies, we need to manually classify portfolio companies into industry groups; in step three, lacking of commonly-used firm identifier in PE dataset, we need to manually merge this company with disclosed principal customers from Compustat Segment Customer File manually. b) In our first set of empirical tests reported in appended tables, we examine the capital market and operating performance of the suppliers of acquired company (i.e., the Suppliers of Company 3 in the highlighted cell where Portfolio Company 3 is the target of PE firm. We construct three sets of control variables: D_SameInd is a dummy variable equals one if the acquired principal customer is in the same industry as other portfolio firms of the PE (e.g., in the table above, Portfolio Company 3 is in the same industry as Portfolio Companies 1 & 2), and zero otherwise. D_SameSupInd is a dummy variable equals one if the supplier is in the same industry as the suppliers of the other portfolio firms of the PE (e.g., in the table above, Suppliers of Company 3 are in the same industry as Suppliers of Companies 1 or 2), and zero otherwise. D_SameSupPrtf is a dummy variable equals one if the supplier is in the same industry as the other portfolio firms of the PE (e.g., in the table above, Suppliers of Company 3 are in the same industry as Portfolio Companies 1 & 2), and zero otherwise. We do find two sets of interesting results under this research design. First, when the acquired customer firm is in the same industry as some existing portfolio firms held by the acquiring PE firm, investors interpret this as a bad news for the suppliers for acquired firms, as shown in the negative announcement effects. For example, the investors might believe that the bargaining power of the acquired customer firm may increase and, therefore, generate negative impact on the profit margin on the supplier firms. However, while we examine its impact on operating performance of these supplier firms, we find that, under this situation, the total sales of the supplier increase and the profit margin does not go down, leading to an increase in profitability (as captured by ROA). For the second layer, we find that, when the supplier is of the same industry as the suppliers of the other portfolio firms of the PE, its performance will be significantly affected once the customer is acquired by the PE firm, e.g., its sales and profit margin will go down and the relationship with acquired customers are likely to be discontinued in the following three years. This suggests that the supplier is likely to face internal competitions from suppliers of existing portfolio companies. While we find a significant impact on operating performance, the announcement effect associated with this layer is not as significant as the first layer, suggesting an overall investor underreaction to this supply-chain information. However, we do not find any effect on the announcement effect or operating performance for the third layer, i.e., when suppliers are in the same industry with existing portfolio companies. For the announcement effect, we find no results for the first two layers. However, the third layer, when suppliers are in the same industry with existing segments of acquirers, is associated with a positive announcement effect. Theoretically, we have a difficulty to explain that. We find no operating performance changes associated with three layers under strategic acquisitions. Although no results are also good (and honest) results, it is difficult to write papers with no results. After discussing with my collaborators, we decide to try again when we accumulate more data around/after COVID period. On the other hand, the related paper (which has already been reported in the mid-term report) arising from data collected for this project went out well. This paper has been presented in many conferences (will be reported separately) and obtained the Best Paper Award from the Asian Finance Association Annual Meeting 2022. What Do Questions Reveal? Skill Acquisition, Detection, and Recognition in the Capital Markets (https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3730815) Abstract: We construct an ex ante topic-specific skill measure based on the frequency of topic-specific questions that analysts raised in past earnings conference calls. In a supply chain information setting, we show that analysts with supply-chain-specific skill achieve a greater improvement in forecast accuracy relative to their peers when the firms experience firm-specific or market-wide supply-chain shocks. Analysts acquire skills through cross-brokerage learning and within-brokerage coaching. While brokerage firms do not assign tasks according to topic-specific skills, evidence based on the market reactions to recommendation updates and the information diffusion speed along the supply chain suggests that investors do recognize these skills. Overall, we provide a generalizable method that penetrates the black box of information processing and study the skill acquisition, detection, and diffusion in the capital market. This project starts with a technique to detect supply-chain-specific skill. This is something that private equities care a lot. However, this is more interesting if we ask this question in the capital market setting, where firms, investors, and regulators all care about supply-chain-specific skill. After finishing the first draft of this paper, we realize that this methodology is not restricted to supply-chain-specific skill. It can be applied to detect any type of skills. We realize that this project can really go beyond the original plan and provide an important contribution to the literature.

14500119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500119.value: The paper "What Do Questions Reveal? Skill Acquisition, Detection, and Recognition in the Capital Markets" has the following main findings: 1. We propose an approach that successfully identifies topic-specific skills of financial analysts by analyzing their self-revealed interest and skill based on the frequency of topic-relevant questions they raise in previous earnings conference calls. 2. Analysts with high frequency (top 10 percentile) of raising supply chain-related questions in earnings conference calls are identified as experts with supply chain-specific skills. 3. Supply chain expert analysts demonstrate lower forecast errors compared to non-expert analysts when a firm discloses important supply chain relationships with public principal customers. This effect is economically significant. 4. Past forecast accuracy has unconditional predictability for future forecast accuracy, but it does not generate incremental effects when firms experience supply chain shocks. Supply chain-specific skill is more effective in predicting future forecast accuracy for firms disclosing important supply chain relationships. 5. The information advantage generated by supply chain-specific skill is more pronounced for supplier firms with higher information asymmetry and customer-switching risk. 6. Supply chain-specific skills identified in the study are mainly related to analysts' ability to interpret public information rather than uncovering private information. 7. Supply chain-specific skill diffuses among analysts, with cross-brokerage learning observed after relationship disclosures. Rookie analysts are more likely to become supply chain experts if they cover customer and supplier firms simultaneously or have more co-workers who are supply chain experts. 8. Brokerage firms do not consider analyst supply chain expertise when making dual coverage assignments, but investors recognize supply chain-specific skills and react more aggressively to recommendation downgrades by expert analysts after relationship disclosures. 9. The number of supply chain expert analysts covering a supplier firm is positively correlated with the speed of information diffusion from customers to suppliers around earnings announcements of customer firms.

14500119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500119.value: Most ideas fail. We haven't completely given up on the original project yet. While the existing findings are interesting, they lack significant real economic outcomes, making it challenging to draw policy implications. However, if we analyze data from the COVID period, which could potentially provide us with more substantial economic outcomes, the project holds promise. Most successful research comes from surprises. The derived project has the potential to make a significant impact on the existing literature. The methodology we developed can be applied to any skill, not just limited to analysts. It has broad applicability to various individuals, such as managers, politicians, and researchers. Furthermore, it is not confined to earnings conference calls but can be employed in any context involving repeated public talks and speeches. In essence, this methodology offers a versatile and widely applicable approach for detecting topic-specific skills.

14500119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500119.value: We created a way to measure the specific skills of financial analysts based on the types of questions they ask during company meetings. In the context of supply chain information, we found that analysts with expertise in supply chain matters are better at making accurate predictions when companies face supply chain challenges. These analysts learn from each other, both across different brokerage firms and within the same firm. Interestingly, brokerage firms don't assign tasks based on these specific skills, but investors do pay attention to analysts with supply chain expertise and react strongly to their recommendations. We believe our approach can be applied more broadly to understand how analysts acquire and spread their skills in the financial market.

14500519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14500519.value: 關於有限記憶和合約過度選擇的理論和實驗研究

14500519.label: Project Objectives
14500519.value: First, we develop a new theory to explain contract overchoice and analyze the implications for firm optimal behavior and welfare. Second, we use lab experiments to test unique predictions of the proposed theory.
rows: First, we develop a new theory to explain contract overchoice and analyze the implications for firm optimal behavior and welfare.
Second, we use lab experiments to test unique predictions of the proposed theory.

14500519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500519.value: Many economic models assume that preferences are present-biased and can be misestimated. These assumptions imply that future consumptions would be overestimated for investment goods that involve immediate costs and delayed benefits, and underestimated for leisure goods with immediate rewards and delayed costs. Previous studies test these predictions by comparing ex ante contract choice with ex post usage behavior. Observed contract overchoice has been typically interpreted as evidence for the naivety hypothesis. However, one notable caveat is that the flat-rate bias is documented for both investment and leisure goods, which is inconsistent with the hypothesis. We address two sets of research issues in this proposed project. First, we will develop a new theory to provide an alternative perspective on contract overchoice. We will present a general framework to reconcile several puzzling empirical findings, even without assuming any nonstandard preference or belief. Our proposed explanation hinges on the potential loss of information due to limited memory, as time elapses from contract choice to subsequent consumption decisions. When consumers are aware of their memory constraints, they may intentionally change their contract choices to deal with this issue. In particular, if they can make inference about the lost memory from the chosen contract, they will tend to choose contracts with higher fixed payments and lower marginal prices. However, if this becomes infeasible, they will favor contracts with higher marginal prices such that they will not consume too much. In addition, we will examine the implications of limited memory with respect to optimal contract design and welfare. Under what conditions would limited memory lead to higher or lower prices charged by a firm? Relatedly, would social welfare and consumer surplus become higher or lower when consumers have limited memory? Second, we plan to test experimentally the unique predictions that are generated from the the proposed theory. In particular, we predict that limited memory can lead consumers to overchoose contracts that seem ex post suboptimal. In addition, the consumption level will be lower when a consumer is assigned (rather than choose) a flat-rate contract. Nevertheless, we expect the flat-rate bias to become stronger as the fixed payment in the flat-rate contract increases. Moreover, it is predicted that the flat-rate bias would emerge for both investment and leisure goods. Finally, we predict that consumers will display the flat-rate bias when they choose from multiple two-part tariffs, but exhibit the steep-rate bias when only one of the tariffs is available. 許多經濟學模型都假設偏好是現時偏向性的（present- biased），並且人們會錯誤估計將來偏好的現時偏向性。這些假設意味著，關於投資型商品(及時成本和延遲回報)的將來消費會被高估，而享受型商品(及時回報和延遲成本)的消費會被低估。以前的研究通過比較合約的選擇以及事後的消費行為來檢驗這些預測。對某類型合約的過度選擇，通常被解讀為證據，來支援錯誤估計現時偏向性偏好的假設。然而，值得注意的一點是，扁平價格合約偏向性（flat-rate bias）的現象對於投資型和享受型商品都會出現，而這和錯誤估計現時偏向性偏好的假設是不一致的。 在本計畫中我們研究兩組問題。第一，我們會構建一個新理論，對合約的過渡選擇行為提供不同的解讀。我們會提供一個一般性的框架，即便在沒有依賴于任何非典型假設的前提下，對之前的幾個令人費解的實證研究結果進行解釋。我們的解釋的基本出發點在於，當時間從合約選擇推移到之後的消費決策的時候，資訊可能會因為記憶的有限而流逝。當消費者意識到這個問題時，他們可能會有意的選擇不同的合約來應對他們記憶上的局限。具體而言，如果他們可以從所選的合約來推斷已經忘記的資訊，那他們會傾向于選擇那些有著更高的固定支付價格和更低邊際價格的合約。反之，他們偏向選擇的合約是有更高的邊際價格的，以此來降低將來的過度消費。 另外，我們會研究有限記憶對公司的最優合約設計以及福利的影響。在什麼情況下，有限記憶會促使公司在合約中要求更高或者更低的價格？相關的問題是，當消費者的記憶是有限的時候，社會福利和消費者剩餘會增加還是減少？ 第二，我們計畫用實驗方法對我們提出理論的預測進行檢驗。具體而言，我們預測有限記憶會使消費者過度選擇在事後看起來並不是最優的合約。另外，當扁平價格型合約是分配（而不是自主選擇）給消費者的時候，消費會下降。然而，我們預計，當扁平價格型合約的固定支付價格上升的時候，扁平價格合約偏向性會變得更強。另外一個預測是，對於投資型和享受型商品都會出現扁平價格合約偏向性。最後，我們預測，當消費者從多個合約中進行選擇時會表現出扁平價格合約偏向性，但是只有單一合約時會表現出上升價格合約偏向性。

14500519.label: Realisation of objectives
14500519.value: First, “to explain contract overchoice and analyze the implications for firm optimal behavior and welfare,” we develop a new theory of contractual screening that generates substantial insights. The theory captures the equilibrium interaction between a seller and a buyer whose prior information can be losable, forgettable, or unattended. We examine the implications of limited memory with respect to optimal contract design and welfare. The theoretical model allows to address questions such as: under what conditions can limited memory lead to higher or lower prices charged by a firm, and would social welfare and consumer surplus become higher or lower when consumers have limited memory? We finish all the analysis and report the results in a paper titled “The Mnemonomics of Contractual Screening,” which is published at Management Science. Therefore, the first project objective has been fully achieved. Regarding the second objective on “test unique predictions of the proposed theory,” we have generated the predictions to be experimentally tested, by developing a general theoretical framework to characterize how individuals with limited memory may choose between alternative contracts and how the contract choice may influence subsequent consumptions. That is, we have identified theory-based factors, which can be experimentally manipulated to moderate the choice of seemingly suboptimal contracts as well as the influence of the chosen contract on consumptions. However, unfortunately, because of the covid-19 pandemic, the normal operation of the university has been severely interrupted during past years of the project period. As a result, we were severely short of basic research facilities and support. In addition, it has been infeasible to recruit human subjects to participate in lab experiments. Therefore, we have been focusing on the theoretical work, and addressing the reviewer requests (which involve many unplanned efforts and work such as model extensions). As mentioned above, the paper titled “The Mnemonomics of Contractual Screening” has been published at Management Science. Overall, the second projective is partially achieved.

14500519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500519.value: We build a game-theoretical model to investigate how limited memory may influence the optimal design of contracts for sequential screening. We build on the standard problem of how a principal (e.g., a seller) can offer a menu of contracts to induce sequential revelation of private information from an agent (e.g., an industrial or individual buyer), who nonetheless may forget prior information in our setting. We show that, despite memory loss, the buyer can make ex post inference about her initially informed type from the chosen contract, which would yield an endogenous demand for separation in ex ante contract choice. In response, limited memory can either attenuate or strengthen the upward distortion of the marginal price in the optimal contract design, leading to improved or undermined social welfare, respectively. As a result of attenuated distortion in the contract, the equilibrium buyer surplus can be higher than that under perfect memory. We also show that the buyer can exhibit the so-called flat-rate bias, even though her preference is time consistent and perfectly predicted. In addition, we find that, as memory can be perfectly recovered from the equilibrium contract choice, investing on any other memory-improving instrument is redundant. Moreover, the buyer’s demand for screening can induce her to choose dominated refund contract. Nevertheless, we show that, when dominance must be obeyed, the seller may offer a menu of refund contracts with two-way distortions.

14500519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500519.value: There are several directions to further develop the research. The most related one is to run controlled experiments to test the predictions we have derived from our theory. Would the consumption level be lower when a consumer is assigned (rather than choose) a flat-rate contract? Would the flat-rate bias become stronger as the fixed payment in the flat-rate contract increases? Would the flat-rate bias emerge for both investment and leisure goods? Would consumers display the flat-rate bias when they choose from multiple two-part tariffs, but exhibit the steep-rate bias when only one of the tariffs is available? Another direction would be to extent our theory of memory management to potentially explain other well-documented behavioral or cognitive biases. For example, we can extend our theory to address the puzzle that some people seem to procrastinate excessively and persistently, even when simple remedy is available and not costly. Similarly, seemingly overconfident behaviors (e.g., CEO overinvestment) may reflect a conscious strategy to deal with (individual or organizational) memory constraints. It would also be interesting to study how costly recall may influence equilibrium market behavior in other settings. For instance, how would limited memory influence consumer search and price competition?

14500519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500519.value: It is common in many markets that buyers sign advance contracts before actual decisions on transactions or consumptions are made and, as time moves on, forget about the prior information that has justified their choice of a particular advance contract. In this research we investigate how limited memory may influence the optimal design of contracts, and what are the welfare implications of sellers taking into account consumers’ limited memory in their contract design. Our analysis and results can yield profound managerial implications to guide sellers on optimal contract design. For example, we provide conditions under which a seller should mitigate or intensify the upward distortion of the marginal price in the menu of contracts they offer. In addition, our research can lead to important policy implications. We suggest that the mere observation of some buyers choosing some seemingly suboptimal contract does not necessarily imply the need or the direction for government intervention. Our theoretical analysis would suggest that optimal firm response to consumer memory management may result in beneficial outcomes for social welfare and consumer well being. That is, seller exploitation of buyer memory constraint can yield beneficial welfare outcome.

14500719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500719.value: This research aims to study the determinants of assortative mating and its effect on the gender gap and income inequality. The project applies the theory of marriage matching to data primarily from the Chinese mainland. Gender difference in education attainment has been closing all over the world. Prominent economists and social scientists have devoted extensive efforts to uncover forces behind the "closing gender gap" in education and income. While the vast amount of existing research focuses on changing gender differences in the labor market, a growing strand of literature starts to note a driving force behind the closing gender gap, that is, the "marital return to education." However, most existing studies on the marital education premium are grounded on observations from the developed world. I intend to exploit multiple policy changes in China to identify key determinants of assortative mating and their links with the closing gender gap and rising income inequality across households. China, like other parts of world, has experienced a closing gender gap. Meanwhile, income inequality is on the rise. After 1979, China has undergone dramatic social economic changes, offering researchers an unprecedented rich pool of natural experiments, such as the one-child policy and the lift of labor mobility restrictions. Equipped with the recent advances in the theory of stochastic marriage matching, I am able to examine and quantify the effects of multiple policy changes on assortative mating, gender gap, and income inequality. The proposed project should offer important implications on education, distribution, and immigration policies. Gauging the marital return to education, beyond the earning return to education, contributes to the picture of the effect of education on human welfare. I can estimate the contribution of assortative mating to income inequality, offering guides for redistribution policies. I also intend to examine the impact of marriage migration on different part of the population, which can be the basis for immigration policies. In summary, this research aims to exploit Chinese data to carry out theory-based empirical studies on assortative mating and its distributional consequences. 本研究項目旨在研究相稱匹配的決定因素，以及其對性別鴻溝與收入分配的影響。本項目將運用婚姻匹配理論，并主要使用來自中國大陸的數據。 教育上的性別差異正在日益縮小。經濟學家與社會科學家在研究教育與收入的性別鴻溝的縮小上做了很多努力。儘管大量的現有研究分析了勞動力市場上的性別鴻溝變動，最近才有一支文獻注意到婚姻市場在性別鴻溝的變動上所起的作用，而且這些研究都是基於發達國家的數據。 我意圖運用中國的多重政策衝擊來識別婚姻匹配的決定因素，并研究婚姻匹配對性別鴻溝和收入分配的影響。中國和世界上其他國家和地區一樣，也在經歷性別鴻溝的收窄。同時，中國的收入分配日漸變得不平等。中國經歷了巨大的社會經濟變遷，為研究者提供了諸如一孩政策和人口遷移政策放鬆的自然實驗。我將檢驗多重政策變動對相稱匹配，性別鴻溝和收入分配的影響。 本項目對教育，分配和移民政策的制定有重要含義。測量教育對婚姻的貢獻，而不是僅僅對收入的貢獻，將豐富教育對人類福祉影響的研究。我將估算相稱匹配對收入分配的貢獻，指導再分配政策的制定。我也意圖研究“婚姻移民”對不同人群的影響，為移民政策的制定提供參考。總的來說，本研究意圖用中國數據，就相稱匹配及其後果，進行有理論依據的經驗研究

14500819.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14500819.value: M/M/n+GI系統的穩態分析：泰勒展式方法

14500819.label: Project Objectives
14500819.value: To identify a one-dimensional Markov process to represent the status of an M/M/n+GI queueing system. To establish universal tightness for a sequence of M/M/n+GI queueing systems. To establish universal approximations for M/M/n+GI queueing systems.
rows: To identify a one-dimensional Markov process to represent the status of an M/M/n+GI queueing system.
To establish universal tightness for a sequence of M/M/n+GI queueing systems.
To establish universal approximations for M/M/n+GI queueing systems.

14500819.label: Realisation of objectives
14500819.value: All three objectives of the project have been successfully achieved (though there is 210,128.45HKD underspending due to the difficulty in hiring research assistants during the COVID-19). One noteworthy achievement is the development of a Taylor expansion technique for analyzing queueing systems. Objective 1 was accomplished through the construction of Markovian and one-dimensional martingale representations for complex queueing systems. In paper #1 (see Section 8), a high-dimensional Markov process was used to model a queueing system. We then use the Markov process to construct a one-dimensional martingale. We connect the martingale to a one-dimensional diffusion process via using the Ito's formula and Taylor expansion. The one-dimensional diffusion process served as an approximation for the discrete-state stochastic queueing systems. The same approach was used in paper #2 to represent the system state of a different queueing system with a non-Markovian representation objective. Objective 2 was achieved by establishing tightness for a sequence of the steady states of queueing systems. In paper #1, appropriate Lyapunov functions were constructed to establish the tightness of the steady states in two different state regions. The same framework was used in paper #2 to analyze another queueing system. Objective 3 was accomplished by establishing convergence results for the steady states. In paper #1, the existence of the steady states was first established, followed by the establishment of a steady-state version of state-space collapse. The steady-state analysis and the Taylor expansion approach provided a comprehensive analysis for the complex stochastic systems. The same framework was used in paper #2 to conduct a steady-state analysis for another queueing system. In summary, the successful use of a Taylor expansion, along with a one-dimensional representation and tightness results, led to the establishment of diffusion approximations for the steady state of queueing systems.

14500819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500819.value: Our project has made significant contributions to both theoretical and practical aspects. We created a framework that integrates Taylor expansion, tightness arguments, and a steady-state version of state-space collapse to analyze complex queueing systems. To analyze a highly complex queueing system, we first represent the system state using a multi-dimensional Markov process and construct a one-dimensional martingale based on it. The use of the one-dimensional martingale representation enables us to make use of Ito's formula. We then demonstrate the existence of the steady state of the Markov process by carefully constructing a Lyapunov function and applying the Foster-Lyapunov criteria. Our Lyapunov function is tailored to explore the specifics of the queueing system structure. We also establish the tightness of a sequence of steady states by constructing two different Lyapunov functions for different state regions and obtaining tail bounds for stationary distributions. We then prove a steady-state version of the state space collapse. We analyze the steady-state of queueing systems by adopting a lower bound approach and combining it with the steady-state state space collapse. Our paper is the first to combine the Taylor expansion approach with the steady-state state space collapse to analyze complex queueing systems. The framework has been outlined in our paper published in Mathematics of Operations Research (paper #1). We also applied this framework to analyze another queueing system which has a non-Markovian representation objective. To utilize the framework, we established a heavy traffic version of the generalized version of Little’s law, and our results are summarized in a paper published in Operations Research (paper #2).

14500819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500819.value: Our project involves creating a framework that combines the Taylor expansion approach and the steady-state state space collapse technique to analyze complex queueing systems. We can further apply this framework to investigate other queueing systems, such as those which does not have a clear Markovian representation objective, as suggested by paper #2. However, studying such a queueing systems will require linking a non-Markovian objective to one which involves a Markov process. Additionally, we can explore moderate or large deviations, building on the findings of our project.

14500819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500819.value: Our project introduces a framework that combines the Taylor expansion approach with the steady-state state space collapse to analyze complex queueing systems. We begin by constructing a one-dimensional martingale and applying Ito's formula to it. We prove the existence of the steady state and establish the tightness of a sequence of steady states by constructing different Lyapunov functions. Additionally, we establish a steady-state state space collapse. Our paper is the first to use this combination of approaches to analyze complex queueing systems. We have successfully applied this framework to analyze complex queueing systems, including one without a Markovian representation objective. To ensure the applicability of our framework, we established a heavy traffic version of the generalized version of Little's law. Our project has made significant contributions to both theoretical and practical aspects of queueing system analysis.
