14500919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14500919.value: The study explores the impact of new text-based measures of perceived volatility on the cross-section of equity option returns. The ever-increasing contents in digital text encode rich yet complex cues about the firms and provide an ideal source for understanding market participants’ perceptions about stock volatility, the key input for option pricing. We use textual analysis to extract new information regarding future stock volatility from various resources and examine its impact on equity option pricing. Forecasting volatility is difficult and the error can lead to inaccuracy in option pricing (Figlewski (1989); Figlewski and Green (1999)). While statistical models like GARCH captures a good deal of the volatility dynamics, it ignores the rich information content available to the market participants (such as firm disclosures, management discussions, reports from analysts, opinions from investors forum) that could help shape their volatility forecasts in real time. However, it is unclear whether such qualitative information affects investors trading behavior and asset prices. Particularly, to what extent it is incorporated in the equity options market and whether the answer depends on the sources. Managers’ and financial analysts’ perceived uncertainty is more likely to be associated with potential fundamental change in volatility. Such information, once incorporated into option price, leads to a change in the premium of option price relative to the underlying stock price. The opinions from the social networks, however, could be different. On one hand, literature documents crowd wisdom from the non-experts (Chen et al. (2014)). On the other hand, sentiment can add noise to volatility information. This study applies textual analysis to obtain measures of perceived volatility from various resources including financial reports, analyst forecasts, press releases, news media, and investors social networks. We examine the impacts of the perceived volatility by different participants on the cross-section of delta-hedged equity option returns to understand the nature of the information. We also use machine learning techniques to better categorize the volatility information from various unstructured data sources. The contribution of the study is two-fold. First, we extend the literature on textual analysis in finance, accounting and economic literature. Previous studies largely focus on directional information about stock price movement. We focus on the volatility information, which is equally important given the difficulty of forecasting volatility. Second, the study sheds light on the option pricing practices and on the cross-sectional option return predictability. Our study demonstrates the sources of information used by option market participants. 本研究探討了一种全新的基於文本的感知波動性對股票期權收益的影響。數字化的文本中日益剧增的內容包含着公司豐富而復雜的線索，這為我們理解市場參與者對股票波動率（期權定價的關鍵輸入）的看法提供了理想的資料。我們使用文本分析從各種資源中汲取有關未來股票波動率的新信息，並研究其對股票期權定價的影響。 學術界一直致力於波動性的預測，然而並非易事，並且錯誤的預測可能導致期權定價的不准確（Figlewski（1989）; Figlewski和Green（1999））。雖然像GARCH這樣的統計模型能夠很好的擬合波動率，但它忽略了市場參與者可獲得的其他豐富的信息內容（例如公司披露，管理層討論，分析師報告，投資者論壇的觀點等等），這些內容可能有助於預測更加實時的波動率。但是，目前還不清楚這種定性信息是否會影響投資者的交易行為和資產價格，特別是，它在多大程度上會被納入股票期權市場的定價，而且是否取決於信息來源。管理者與金融分析師認知的不確定性可能與波動性的潛在基本變化更相關。這些信息一旦被納入期權價格，就會導致期權之相對於標股票價格的溢價發生變化。然而，來自社交網絡的意見可能會有所不同并產生其他影響。一方面，文獻記載了來自非專家群體的集體智慧（Chen et al.（2014））。另一方面，市場中的投資者情緒可能會增加波動信息的噪音。本研究採用文本分析從各種資源中獲取感知波動率的度量，包括財務報告，分析師預測，新聞稿，新聞媒體和投資者社交網絡。我們研究了不同參與者對波動性的感知，對橫截面上delta中性期權收益的影響，進而能了解信息背後的本質。我們還使用機器學習技術更好地分類來自各種非結構化數據源的波動率信息。該研究的貢獻是雙重的。首先，我們擴展了金融學，會計學和經濟學中文本分析的研究。以前的研究主要注重文本中關於股票價格的信息。而我們關注文本中的波動率信息，鑑於預測波動率的難度，這同樣重要。其次，該研究揭示了期權橫截面收益率的可預測性，對期權定價的實踐有重要啟示作用。同時我們的研究展示了期權市場參與者使用的信息來源。

14500919.label: Realisation of objectives
14500919.value: We have explored all our proposed objectives in the working paper “Forecasting Option Returns with News”, which has been presented at several high-quality conferences such as The China International Conference in Finance (CICF), and accepted for presentation at the 2025 American Finance Association (AFA) Annual Conference. Moreover, our related working paper “Do Insurance Companies Listen to Earnings Conference Calls? Evidence From Corporate Bond Market” was presented at the 2024 AFA Conference and is ready for submission. Objective 1 & 2. We have collected news articles from the most popular newspapers in the U.S., e.g., the Wall Street Journal, New York Times, etc. The data are available at the daily level and are collected from ProQuest and complemented with Factiva. With a clean and concise representation of the text, we analyze tasks as outlined by objectives in our proposal. Our textual data do not have firm identifier, so we match each article with the corresponding firms by first conducting a textual fuzzy matching between company names in the text and the list of all company names from the Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP). To ensure the quality of our matching, we exclude those firms that are difficult to identify by company names and remove articles matched with more than seven different companies. By the matching process, we establish links between the news (text) and the public firm. We next turn to link text data with options data to understand whether news contains useful information, such as volatility and sentiment that could predict option returns. We obtain equity option data from the Option-Metrics database. We collect variables on underlying stocks from CRSP database. Each month, we keep equity options with more than one month until expiration and standard expiration dates. After applying standard filtering, we choose options that are closest to being at the money. We require that the information is available at the portfolio formation to avoid look-ahead bias. The holding period is from the beginning to the end of each month. After merging the newspaper database and the option data, our final sample consists of 1,061,737 article-month observations and 872,405 unique articles. The final sample contains 89,895 option-month observations for both call and put options on individual stocks over a 323-month sample period from January 1996 to November 2022. Since we require a firm to be both media-covered and have valid options, our sample consists of mostly large firms. We measure the return of equity calls and puts by constructing daily-rebalanced delta-hedged long option positions. We hold the delta-hedge positions for a month. We follow Kelly et al. (2021) to merge all the news articles covering a firm during a given month into a single document and construct a simple counting matrix for each month using the term frequency-inverse document frequency method. Thus, we have all the ingredients available to apply machine learning and word-counting methods and explore the relation between rich text data and options return patterns. We use the Support Vector Regression (SVR) approach to establish the predictability from text data to option returns. The results reveal that textual information generates significant return spreads economically and statistically, which holds after controlling for the risk exposure to factors in the stock and options market. The results are robust to different machine-learning methods, large language models (LLM), and word-counting approaches. Thus, we have completed our Objective 2. To understand the nature of the text information that could be used to predict option returns, we first create a dictionary that captures key features from option returns data. This dictionary serves as an intuitive means to visually represent textual information pertinent to option returns. We sort word features in the SVR model into positive and negative groups based on the sign of coefficients during each training iteration. From each group, we select top 2000 words with the largest absolute value of the coefficients magnitudes as the important words. Subsequently, we compile and count these words’ occurrences, noting their positive or negative impact on option returns. For both call and put options, we form two distinct dictionaries related to the delta-hedged option returns: a positive and a negative dictionary. By exploring the overlapped and non-overlapped subsets of the dictionary, we have an intuitive explanation for our findings. We find that the overlap between important words that are positive (negative) in the call option dictionary and the put option dictionary is 58.6% (56.5%). This suggests that the majority of word features convey information affecting both call and put options similarly. If underlying stock returns or sentiment drives option return predictability, we would find the overlap to be small. The evidence points to that volatility information is likely to drive the results. Consistent with the findings in our related publication, Cao, Chordia, and Zhan (2021), anomalies (IVOL puzzle) in the stock market could be partially driven by options’ expiration, but not vice versa. In another related publication, Cao, Han, Song, and Zhan (2023) corroborate the information flow argument by extending the analysis to REITs markets. Next, we analyze the overlap between the words that significantly forecast option returns in SVR and words related to various option return determinants including changes in future implied volatility (∆IV), idiosyncratic volatility (IVOL), volatility deviation (HV–IV), and so on. Zhan, Han, Cao, and Tong (2022) find these variables to significantly predict future option returns. Among various return determinants, the highest average overlap score is observed for ∆IV, which has an average overlap score of 21.8% (21%) for the call (put) option dictionary. This suggests that the information set related to ∆IV is a key source of textual information for option return predictability. Another publication, Cao, Vasquez, Xiao, and Zhan (2023) confirms that change in volatility is an important source of option return predictability. Thus, Objective 1 is achieved. Objective 3. We explore Objective 3 in two ways. First, we apply the model that we obtain from news text to conference call information. We find similar results indicating that our machine learning model could be generalized to capture volatility information from alternative text data. Second, in a separate working paper “Do insurance companies listen to earnings conference calls? Evidence from the corporate bond market”, we find that the sentiment information in earnings conference calls affects insurance companies trading in the corporate bond market. We further show that the sentiment information is largely driven by the sentiment related to default/ credit risks. Thus, Objective 3 is fully achieved. Objective 4. We construct abnormal trading volume for retail and institutional traders in the options market. Utilizing signed option volume data from the International Stock Exchange and the Chicago Board Options Exchange, we obtain options trading volume data from various investor types. Institutional investors are classified as ‘professional customers’, who place an average of over 390 orders per day in each month. Retail investors are defined as customers who trade on their own accounts and do not fall under the ‘professional customer’ category. We find that textual predictors are significantly and positively related to future abnormal trading volume from both retail investors and institutional investors. Thus, Objective 4 is fully achieved.

14500919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14500919.value: Cao, Han, Li, Yang, and Zhan (2024) examine the information content of news media for the cross-section of expected equity option returns.Applying various machine learning methods, we derive text-based signals from news articles on publicly traded companies that strongly forecast delta-hedged equity option returns. The option return predictability is robust to variations in methodology and remains significant after controlling for existing predictors. The return predictability shows that text data contains rich information relevant to option returns. Cao, Han, Li, Yang, and Zhan (2024) further develop text-based method to understand the underlying sources of the textual predictors. Among the multiple underlying economic mechanisms, the most important source is the ability of text-based signals to predict future change in stock volatility. As a further attempt, Cao, Vasquez, Xiao, and Zhan (2023) investigate whether volatility change and its uncertainty could robustly predict option returns and document corroborating evidence. Cao, Han, Li, Yang, and Zhan (2024) rule out that stock return patterns drive the predictability by text. Specifically, the text has little significant value in predicting stock returns, highlighting the drastic difference between option and stock markets. In two related publications, the PI and co-authors show the predictability in option and stock returns differ significantly. Cao, Chordia, and Zhan (2021) explain IVOL puzzle by equity option expiration. Zhan, Han, Cao, and Tong (2022) document that a set of stock characteristics could predict option returns, but not underlying stock returns. In Cao, Han, Song, and Zhan (2023), the PI further applies option-implied information to REIT return predictability. These papers together show that options contain unique information, especially volatility information, that could have non-negligible impacts on both options market and underlying stock market. The PI and coauthors make further attempt to understand how text information affects financial markets by examining whether corporate bond market participants react to earnings conference calls. Cao, Li, Wermers, Zhan, and Zhou (2024) document that insurance companies react to information, especially default-related information, embedded in earnings conference calls. These results confirm the value of text information in a different financial market.

14500919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14500919.value: 1. We plan to extend our study to other derivatives. Important derivatives of a firm include options and CDS. Firms might also use interest rate swaps and currency swaps to hedge certain risks. Our empirical framework could be applied to extract information that is particularly important for a certain derivative. Moreover, by aggregating firm-level information, we could study the pricing of market or industry derivatives. 2. We plan to study the role of AI (artificial intelligence) in textual information incorporation in asset prices. The fast development and wide use of AI have greatly reduced information processing costs. Thus, the application of AI could facilitate price discovery in the financial markets. We expect the efficiency of models generated by traditional approaches to dimmish in the era of AI.

14500919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14500919.value: Textual analysis is crucial for financial markets because it transforms unstructured data into actionable insights, enhancing predictive power and comprehensive analysis. Despite the rich application of text information in the stock market, little is known about the role of text information in the options market. Equity options are important risk management tools and highly sensitive to volatility. Thus, linking text with equity options opens a window to investors, regulators, and researchers to see the volatility and other information embedded in text. This study collects comprehensive news data for US companies and allows machines to learn the deep link between text information and option pricing. Our analysis shows that news articles can help predict the returns of stock options. The predictability is different from those documented in previous studies, including firm performances, stock market movements, etc. By examining the words that carry important predictions for option returns, we find that the words could also be used to predict future changes in volatility. Therefore, news contains firm-specific risk information, which further affects option prices.

14501019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501019.value: As the research of the former Chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve suggests, banking panics are key forces behind the major economic downturns such as the Great Depression in the 1930s and the recent Great Recession. In the modern banking system where the traditional banking sector is typically backed by regulatory authorities, it is those non-bank financial firms that are subject to the risk of market-wide runs. Most of these non-bank financial firms operate outside of the radar of regulatory authorities and thus they are often referred to as shadow banks. The main goal of this research proposal is to build a framework that we can use for assessing the magnitude and likelihood of banking panics in a modern banking system with both traditional and shadow banks. With this framework, we can improve our understanding of how risks originated from the shadow banking sector is amplified and spreads to the entire banking system. This framework is also a laboratory for bank regulators to examine the macroeconomic consequences of different regulatory changes. Since the framework captures both the traditional banking sector and the shadow one, we can use the framework to evaluate the impact of regulation on both or either of the two sectors. In the proposed project, I will also apply the systemic risk assessing framework to China's case. The recent concern over China's debt problem is largely due to the rapid expansion of its shadow banking sector. By estimating the framework based on the data of China's macroeconomic and financial data, I expect the framework to provide the quantitative assessment of the systemic risk faced by China's economy. Ideally, such a framework would also be helpful for policy prescription for regulation regarding both commercial banks and shadow banks. To complete the empirical exercise with respect to China's economy, I will compile a comprehensive data set that covers key segments of China's shadow banking sector. Key components include wealth management products issued by banks and other financial firms, trust products, and peer-to-peer lending platforms. With this data set, I can provide a big picture of the entire shadow banking system in China. 正如前美聯儲主席伯南克的研究所示, 銀行恐慌是引起如1930年大蕭條和2008年大衰退這類大規模經濟下行的主要原因. 在當代銀行體系中, 傳統銀行部門可以得到來自於監管部門的支持, 然而非銀行金融企業則常受困於市場擠兌的風險. 同時多數非銀行金融機並不受制於金融監管部門, 這些企業則是我們所說的影子銀行. 本研究計劃之主旨爲構建一個評估金融恐慌風險的框架並使之適用於傳統銀行與影子銀行並存的當代銀行體系. 於此框架之下, 我們可以深入理解源自影子銀行的風險是如何在整個金融體系放大及傳播. 並且此框架可以幫助政策制定者評估監管制度改革的宏觀經濟影響. 因爲此框架同時涵蓋了傳統和影子銀行部門, 我們可以利用此模型考察各項銀行制度同時對兩個部門的影響. 在此研究計劃中, 我將會應用所提出的系統性風險評估框架於中國. 近來關於中國的債務問題擔憂主要來自於其影子銀行體系的高速鼓脹. 通過基於中國宏觀和金融數據的模型估計, 我預期此框架可以對中國經濟所面臨的系統性風險進行定量的評估. 理想的情況下, 此框架可以幫助政策制定者規劃對商業銀行和影子銀行的合理管制. 爲完成關於中國經濟的實證分析, 我需要收集並整理中國影子銀行體系各板塊的數據. 主要板塊包括銀行及其他金融機構發行的理財產品, 信託產品, 點對點(P2P)借貸平臺. 藉助這些數據, 我可以就中國影子銀行體系進行一個全面的刻畫.

14501019.label: Realisation of objectives
14501019.value: Objective 1: Dynamics of Banking Panics We commenced with a thorough theoretical examination of the macroeconomic influences leading to banking panics. Utilizing sophisticated continuous-time macro-finance models, we established a robust characterization of the system-wide panic threshold within regular banking systems. Through this analytical autopsy of banking panics, we extrapolated critical economic indicators that presage such events. Our revelations have effectively discerned panic-inducing conditions across diverse economic states, setting a foundational analytical platform for regulatory forewarning systems. Objective 2: Analyzing Implicit Guarantees and Systemic Runs Our exploration turned to the shadow banking sector, where we assessed the consequential role of implicit guarantees in systemic runs. A key finding is that implicit guarantees, while serving as a linchpin of temporary stability, unwittingly embolden risk-taking behaviors that can engulf the entire financial spectrum in crises. We furnished a nuanced dissection of this phenomenon, dissecting the circumstances in which these guarantees mitigate or amplify systemic runs within shadow banking. Objective 3: Systemic Risk Framework A centerpiece of our project was the construction of a unified framework for assessing systemic risk encompassing both regular and shadow banking sectors. This comprehensive framework includes inter-bank exposure assessments and liquidity risk spill-over, offering a powerful analytical toolset crafted to decode the intricacies of systemic risk in a dual-banking ecosystem. Objective 4: Quantitative Assessment of Systemic Risk The project then ventured into a quantitative realm, applying the developed framework to appraise the extent of systemic risk within China's banking system. Through incisive data analytics and quantitative analyses, we unveiled a systemic risk index sensitive to China's unique economic levers and banking practices. This assessment empowers regulatory bodies with actionable metrics that echo the subtle shifts in the systemic risk landscape. Objective 5: Comprehensive Data Compilation Enhancing future research and policy discussions, I have compiled a dataset on China's shadow banking sector. This dataset, unrivaled in scale and detail, encapsulates transactional data, credit instruments, and regulatory changes spanning the shadow banking domain. It is poised to be a useful resource for subsequent investigations and regulatory oversight.

14501019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501019.value: Our theoretical models revealed that non-linear dynamics are at play within traditional banks, with specific economic thresholds where panic becomes more probable. The role of implicit guarantees was found to be nuanced, providing temporary stability yet potentially instigating risk-taking behaviors that exacerbate systemic risk. The proposed framework underscored the need for integrated regulatory oversight, as risks within the shadow banking sector have the potential to quickly spill over into the traditional banking space. Our quantitative assessment suggested that while China's banking system is robust against minor perturbations, it remains vulnerable to large-scale economic downturns, given the current interdependencies between regular and shadow banking institutions. Our dataset provides an unprecedented level of detail and scope that will prove invaluable for policymakers, regulators, and future research. While developing the systemic risk-assessing framework, I also developed a deep learning-based methodology that could solve high-dimensional nonlinear models.

14501019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501019.value: The research lays a foundation for advanced exploration into systemic risks affecting global financial stability. Further development should include real-time application of the systemic risk framework, incorporating evolving economic indicators and regulatory changes. Future action will involve continuous data accumulation, extending the dataset to incorporate real-time banking transactions, and monitoring fintech's influence on financial stability. Collaboration with international regulatory bodies will refine the framework’s applicability across various banking systems, ensuring its relevance in diverse regulatory landscapes. Additionally, applying deep learning-based probabilistic techniques to build nonlinear models and predict systemic risks can significantly amplify the framework's predictive power, guiding preemptive policymaking and fortifying financial systems against potential crises.

14501019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501019.value: This project has made significant strides in understanding how risky situations in banks can affect China's entire economy, especially considering both traditional and less regulated "shadow" banks. We've created models to predict when a banking crisis might happen, examined the hidden promises that could trigger a bank run, and developed a tool that helps see where the financial danger points are. I've also gathered a large amount of data on China's shadow banking system for further study. Moving forward, we plan to keep updating our risk detection tools with the latest information and explore how new technology can help us predict problems before they happen, making banks safer for everyone.

14501919.value: To collect a cross-sectional experimental dataset of youth in Hong Kong, which measures several key behavioral economics parameters in an incentivized manner, including risk attitudes, time preference, self-control, attention span, self-confidence, probabilistic inference, and social preferences. To additionally collect detailed survey information on the same individuals, including information on living quarters, lifestyle, time use, leisure activity, life ambitions, academic and other outcome variables. To cleanly identify the short-term causal impact of small space and crowding on the behavioral parameters of interest, using a randomized experimental approach. To combine macroeconomic data on Hong Kong’s housing market and related policy changes with the experimental and survey data, in order to assist with the challenge of identifying the long-run effects of living space size on behavioral parameters, adaptive behaviors, and outcomes. To econometrically analyze the impact of reduced living quarters on life attitude and outcome variables, using information gathered on adaptive habits and behavioral primitives as potential explanatory pathways. To draw policy and lifestyle recommendations broadly applicable across societies, for individuals seeking to reduce the negative impacts of small living spaces.

14501919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14501919.value: In urban areas around the world and especially in Asia, high population density and an active market economy lead to high house prices and often consequently, shrinking living spaces. While much of the economic literature and policy discussion centers around real estate prices, the behavioral consequences of shrinking residence space is seldom discussed by economists. The idea that confined and crowded living quarters could be detrimental to human psychology has long been discussed as a potential social hazard of mass urbanization (Evans, Wells and Moch, 2003). While the debate on this issue continues, studies seldom focus specifically on the effects of small living quarters on economically relevant psychological parameters. Could small living space be responsible for cultivating risk aversion, patience, attention span, and regard for other individuals, thus affecting some of the important life decisions of young people? This project aims to answer this question by utilizing an experimental economics approach combined with real-world economic data and econometric analyses. In addition to the possibility that living space may generally affect behavioral primitives, a second-order effect of living space size may exist, which is that individuals adapt their lifestyles to accommodate the limited comforts of home. Some of these adaptations could be beneficial, while others could be harmful. What are the marginal impacts of these adaptations? To address this question, we incorporate a detailed participant survey into the experimental design, asking subjects about their time use, physical activities, and leisure choices. An econometric analysis combined with the experimental data can shed light on the best adaptive behaviors for the situation of small living spaces. As one of the most crowded cities in the world, the effects of small living on economic behavior are important for the economy and quality of life in Hong Kong. In addition to the policy relevance for Hong Kong itself, the research also holds potentially important lessons for other cities in Asia and in high population density locations around the world. 在世界各國尤其是亞洲的城市地區，稠密的人口與活躍的市場經濟往往導致高昂的房價，從而造成人們的生活空間不斷縮小。儘管有大量的經濟學文獻與政策討論聚焦於房地產價格，但少有經濟學家關注狹窄的居住空間對個體可能帶來的行為影響。在不同大小的空間生活的個體是否會培養出不同的風險態度、耐心程度、注意力集中度、及利他偏好，從而影響到這些個體尤其是年輕一代的某些重要人生決定？本研究項目旨在通過綜合利用實驗經濟學手段、現實經濟資料和計量分析方法來回答上述問題。生活空間的大小除了會直接影響個體偏好與行為決策，還可能造成這樣一種二階效應：個體會通過調整自己的生活方式來適應其所面臨的居住空間。為了研究這一問題，我們將在實驗設計中引入詳細的參與者問卷調查，收集被試在時間分配、物理活動、閒暇選擇等方面的資料。基於問卷資料與實驗資料的計量分析將有助於發現個體在狹窄生活空間下的最優適應性行為。本研究不僅對香港具有重要的政策意義，對亞洲以及世界上其他人口密度較高的地區也有著潛在的借鑒價值。

14501919.label: Realisation of objectives
14501919.value: With permission from the RGC in an earlier progress report, we revised our research plan in order to accommodate the COVID-19 pandemic situation. We did not apply to revise the project objectives out of hope that an improvement in the overall pandemic situation would eventually allow us to complete the original project objectives. However, even by the time of the project's completion, the pandemic was still in a cautious and transitory situation in both the location of PI and co-Is, where the proposed laboratory experiments were intended to be implemented. We instead went forward with the revised research plan, under the acknowledgement that some of the earlier objectives may not be able to be fully completed. Our original research plan involved running laboratory experiments under different physical space and crowding conditions in order to mimic and test the influence of limited residence spaces on economic preferences in the short-term, while conducting a survey to assess the relationship between residence space and preferences in the longer-term. During the COVID-19 pandemic however, this plan was initially infeasible and later highly impractical due to the social distancing needed to prevent the spread of COVID in close quarters such as in a laboratory setting. Instead, we revised our project plan to focus on the survey-based approach, while at the same time, expanding the project to address how living spaces affected well-being and lifestyles during the COVID pandemic. Our reasoning was that during the COVID pandemic, people tended to spend more time than previously in their residences, which made our original topic actually more pertinent than before. However, the limitation of the survey-based approach is that we could no longer focus on the short-term causal relationship between activity space and preferences. Nevertheless, we have collected 3 significant original datasets for this project using professional survey collection methods, and have found results which we hope will lend useful and publishable knowledge about the relationship between pandemic conditions, behavioral traits and living conditions. Our successfully completed objectives of the project are as follows, while the original objectives and their percentage achieved are listed in Section 5.4 : 1. To collect and analyze a representative sample of Hong Kong residents, obtaining survey responses about their daily lifestyles before and during the pandemic, as well as under a worsening pandemic scenario. (100%) 2. To understand and test the relationship between living space and adaptability to pandemic conditions, including meal preparation, time spent in and out of their residences, as well as social activities. (100%) 3. To examine the extent to which survey-based behavioral measurements and demographic variables account for differences in lifestyle choices. (100%) 4. To collect and analyze representative samples of individuals in the United States and mainland China to assess how their experiences during the COVID pandemic, combined with their living conditions, affected their economic and psychological status. (100%) 5. To assess the factors that determine US and China residents' beliefs about the COVID-19 pandemic, such as length of the pandemic, origins of COVID, and the pandemic's influence on their home country in the world. (100%) The main part of the original objective which has not been achieved is implementing the randomized laboratory experiments, which require imitating highly crowded urban density as the key treatment, since it was impractical during the pandemic due to COVID contagion concerns. The lack of fulfillment of this objective affected the degree to which we could complete the other interrelated objectives as well. However those objectives which could be addressed with survey work have been largely fulfilled. We implemented a representative telephone-based survey with the assistance of the Centre for Communication and Public Opinion Survey, Chinese University of Hong Kong between January to March 2022, which corresponded to the crucial time for Hong Kong transitioning from zero-COVID to living with COVID. A total of 1471 responses were collected, and were analyzed to assess the relationship between living space per person, household composition, demographic and behavioral factors and pandemic relevant behaviors such as eating out, socializing and time spent at home. We also implemented a representative online survey of Shanghai residents with the assistance of professional survey company Dynata in December of 2022. A total of 3005 responses were collected against the backdrop of the Shanghai lockdown period earlier that year, and analyzed to assess how demographics, experiences, and behavioral characteristics affected residents’economic and psychological conditions, their life plans, and their outlook on the future. We implemented a nearly identical survey as the Shanghai survey on a representative sample of residents in the United States. We collected 1297 responses online with the assistance of professional survey company Dynata in early December of 2022, and 660 responses using the CloudResearch Panel of Mechanical Turk, for a total of 1957 responses from the United States. We conduct similar analyses as we did for the Shanghai sample, and make comparisons between the two samples to shed light on how different pandemic management and media environments influenced residents' well-being and outlook on the future.

14501919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14501919.value: We utilized the above collected datasets to thus far put together two working papers. In the first paper, which focuses on the Hong Kong sample, “Hong Kong in the Pandemic, Survey Evidence on Lifestyles under Limited Residence Space", we examine the factors which influence residents' changes in outside the home meal consumption choices, time spent outside of their home, and socializing activities, before the pandemic, during the survey period, and under the hypothetical scenario of worsening pandemic conditions. We found that residents substantially curbed their activities in these three domains under the pandemic and planned to curb their activities even more drastically under worsening conditions. Demographic variables such as gender, household composition, age, and in some cases residing in public housing were significant explanatory variables, but we did not find that living space was a consistent significant factor in activity changes under the pandemic. One interpretation is that Hong Kong residents across the living space distribution that our survey successfully reached, were either resilient or perhaps unable to adjust their living habits as a function of pandemic conditions. We do find some statistical relationships between behavioral characteristics, living space size, length of residence in Hong Kong, and activity choices. In the second paper, “Attitudes on COVID Late in the Pandemic: Survey Evidence from Shanghai and the United States", we focus on the comparison between Shanghai and US residents' reported extent to which their lives have been influenced by the pandemic. Substantial fractions of residents from both regions reported being still affected by the pandemic as of December 2022. Overall, US residents as a whole reported being more severely affected by the pandemic compared to the Shanghai residents. Among Shanghai residents, other factors held constant, party members and residents who left their apartments more often during the lockdown reported being more adversely affected by the pandemic. The US data often exhibited opposite experiences, attitudes and views between residents affiliated with the two major political parties in the US system. Respondents from the two regions also showed substantial differences in beliefs about the pandemic's origins, conclusion, and the effect on their home country. In the aggregate, US respondents generally expressed more pessimism towards the future in relation to these factors. The drafts of these papers which contain additional detailed findings, are attached to the completion report for reference, and will later be refined and submitted for publication.

14501919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14501919.value: We will refine the existing drafts and submit them for publication in reputable academic journals. In addition, we plan to pursue at least one additional related research topic on gender differences in attitudes towards COVID. We will also try to further consider about additional socially valuable questions that can be addressed with the collected responses.

14501919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14501919.value: We implemented original representative surveys in three regions (Hong Kong, Shanghai and the United States) to assess how demographic factors, living conditions, pandemic experiences, and behavioral characteristics affected life during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. Although we found that living space played a relatively minimal role in statistically accounting for Hong Kong residents' lifestyle choices as compared to other observable factors such as demographics, we believe further work is needed to better understand this issue. We also implemented a separate survey on US and Shanghai residents, seeking to understand their different experiences and views related to the pandemic, including the relationship between their living space and degree of being affected by the pandemic. Larger living spaces in the US and Shanghai did correspond to significantly lower levels of reported negative influence of the pandemic. While the Hong Kong survey focused on daily lifestyle changes, the Shanghai and US surveys focused on more general assessments by respondents. Thus, additional research may be needed to more fully understand the pandemic's effect on Hong Kong residents as it relates to their living space conditions.

14502519.label: Project Objectives
14502519.value: Characterize the distribution of consumers’ privacy preferences and their association with creditworthiness. 1) How much do people really care about privacy; i.e., what is their willingness to pay? 2) How do privacy preferences vary across individuals? Characterize the selection effect of the privacy-based screening mechanism. Understand the managerial effect of the current data provision promotion offer and identify the “optimal” promotion offer. Provide empirical evidence for policy makers on topics related to consumer privacy preferences.

14502519.label: Realisation of objectives
14502519.value: The project successfully characterized the distribution of consumers' privacy preferences and their association with creditworthiness (Objective 1). The findings revealed that a significant proportion of consumers are willing to pay a premium in exchange for data protection. This highlights the importance of privacy as a key concern for consumers. Additionally, a positive correlation was observed between higher privacy preferences and higher creditworthiness, indicating that individuals with stronger privacy preferences tend to exhibit better creditworthiness. The project effectively characterized the selection effect of the privacy-based screening mechanism (Objective 2). The analysis revealed that consumers who opt for enhanced privacy measures tend to exhibit higher creditworthiness. They are more likely to pay back their micro-loan. This selection effect suggests that privacy-conscious individuals are more likely to be financially responsible. These findings provide valuable insights for understanding the relationship between privacy preferences and creditworthiness. The project successfully examined the managerial effect of the current data provision promotion offer (Objective 3). The analysis indicated that the promotion offer had a positive impact on micro-loan company. However, further analysis is needed to identify the "optimal" promotion offer that minimizes consumer default rate while maintaining a balance between data provision and privacy concerns. These findings provide valuable insights for managers and policymakers in designing effective data provision promotion strategies. Policy Implications The realizations of the project objectives have important policy implications. The findings highlight the significance of privacy protection for consumers. Policymakers can utilize these insights to develop policies that prioritize privacy concerns while ensuring the responsible utilization of consumer data. Conclusion In conclusion, the successfully realized its objectives of characterizing consumers' privacy preferences, understanding the selection effect of privacy-based screening mechanisms, analyzing the managerial effect of the current data provision promotion offer, and providing empirical evidence for policymakers. The project's realizations contribute to the understanding of consumer privacy preferences and offer valuable insights for policymakers and businesses to make informed decisions.

14502519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14502519.value: In this paper, we estimate consumers valuation for privacy by examining their data sharing decisions under a wide range of incentives, for customers of a microloan provider in Hong Kong. During the application process, the loan provider uses interest rate discounts to incentivize applicants to provide additional personal data. This percentage discount translates to dollar gains from 4,643 to 9,285 Hong Kong dollars (amount to 30 to 50 percent of their monthly salaries) for applicants who request different loan terms and expect different repayment behaviors. Using a structural model, we calculate the dollar price for personal data as a function of applicant risk type and the characteristics of the loan that they apply for. Despite the substantial benefits of sharing data, only 19 percent of applicants choose to share any optional personal data requested. In the counterfactual, we show how the incentive scheme can balance its role in collecting personal data to improve loan offering decisions and its role in screening applicants who accept the loan. Our research has two main contributions. First, we quantify the willingness to pay for the personal data. Second, we estimated joint distribution of privacy preference and consumer risk type, which will help microloan companies develop risk-type screening mechanisms for applicants to mitigate adverse selection. To our knowledge, we are among the first empirical studies to monetize consumers’ revealed privacy preference while at the same time estimating its relationship with consumer risk type.

14502519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14502519.value: The research has laid a foundation for understanding consumers' valuation of privacy and its relationship with their risk types in the context of microloan providers. There are several potential avenues for further development of the research: 1. Develop personalized privacy-based screening mechanisms: Building on the estimated joint distribution of privacy preferences and consumer risk types, further research can focus on developing personalized risk-type screening mechanisms. These mechanisms can assist microloan providers in making more accurate loan offering decisions while considering individual privacy preferences. 2. Explore policy implications: Extend the research to explore the policy implications of consumers' privacy preferences in the microloan industry and beyond. This may involve analyzing the effectiveness of existing privacy regulations, identifying gaps in privacy protection, and proposing policy recommendations to balance privacy concerns and data utilization.

14502519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14502519.value: This research project aimed to understand how much people value their privacy when applying for a microloan in Hong Kong. The study looked at whether customers were willing to share personal information in exchange for lower interest rates on their loans. This research is important because it helps us understand how people make decisions about their privacy and the value they place on it. By quantifying the willingness to pay for personal data, the study provides insights into the economic value that individuals assign to their privacy. Additionally, by estimating the joint distribution of privacy preferences and consumer risk types, the research can help microloan companies develop better ways to assess the risk of their applicants and make more informed loan decisions. The significance of this research goes beyond microloans. It sheds light on the broader issue of privacy and its importance in our digital world. Understanding how people make decisions about sharing personal information can help policymakers create better regulations and companies design more effective privacy protection measures. In summary, this research project provides valuable insights for microloan companies, policymakers, and society as a whole in managing privacy concerns and developing strategies to protect individuals' personal data.

14503219.label: Project Objectives
14503219.value: To compile a new data-set on outdoor advertising markets in major Chinese cities for the recent decade and present a set of stylized facts that summarize key points of the evolution of this industry; to match this data-set to monthly data on air pollution in the selected cities. To empirically examine the causal effects of air pollution on market outcomes, such as ad revenue and per-unit ad price - in China’s outdoor advertising industry; in order to address the potential endogeneity issues, to use an instrumental variable (IV) approach by exploiting exogenous variations in weather or meteorological factors. To study the specific mechanisms through which air pollution affects outdoor advertising, and the test the “attention economy” hypothesis by taking the following steps: (i) to compare the pollution effects on outdoor and indoor ads (e.g., in subway stations); and (ii) to separately look at the effects of air pollution versus visibility on outdoor ads. To deploy a model-based strategy to shed lights on the pollution effect on the underlying advertising technology and to provide estimates on the economic costs of pollution on this industry.

14503219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503219.value: Pollution problems have tremendous impacts on almost every aspect of daily life and the society. In the context of both developed and developing countries, previous literatures have focused on the adverse effects of pollution on numerous socio-economic variables, ranging from morbidity and mortality to consumption and productivity. This project proposes a novel angle to assess the impact of pollution on economic activities in China. In particular, we attempt to study how air pollution affects the commercial value of consumer attention, based on empirical evidence from China’s outdoor advertising industry. Because air pollution can reduce both outdoor activities and visibility of outdoor advertising – as we hypothesize – it should have negative impacts on how much advertisers are willing to spend on outdoor ads. We strive to provide convincing evidence on such causal effects of air pollution. In order to achieve the objectives, this project will compile a new data-set on China’s outdoor advertising industry for a decade (2008 to 2017). The data-set will cover monthly information on total advertising expenditure in more than 30 major Chinese cities, and will contain further data on price and quantity of outdoor ads that are specific to a geographic location. Matching the data-set on advertising to China’s air pollution data, we will conduct a series of econometric analysis to establish causal relationship between air pollution and outdoor advertising activities. To address the potential endogeneity problem, we will both exploit the panel structure of the data and use instrumental variables, such as air pollution in nearby cities or measures of “thermal inversion,” that are commonly used in literature. In support to our hypothesis, we will further investigate on the mechanisms through which air pollution may effect on ad expenditure. Specifically, we will look separately at how visibility itself affects ad revenue, controlling for air pollution, and whether there are differential effects of pollution on ads that are displayed in different locations. By providing a first look at the impact of pollution on a service sector in China, our research should not only add one more interesting observation to the long, existing list of economic variables affected by pollution, but also it sheds lights on our understanding of the “attention economy” – a subject that has become increasingly important in an era of information explosion and digital innovation.

14503219.label: Realisation of objectives
14503219.value: This project has achieved all proposed objectives. In the working paper of Shi and Zhang (2022), first, we have compiled a unique dataset that covers monthly city-level outdoor advertising spending for 24 major Chinese cities from 2008 to 2017. We have accessed the advertising data through a research partner, which resulted in a surplus of funding in this particular category. In particular, the advertising information is broken down by location: functional area (e.g., shopping or industrial districts) and type of road (e.g., branch or main roads). We have linked the advertising information with external meteorological and environmental data. Second, to overcome the empirical hurdle of endogeneity, we have exploited the meteorological phenomenon of thermal inversions. As a high-atmosphere phenomenon, the occurrence of a thermal inversion is generally independent of economic activity, which makes it a valid instrument for air pollution. Deploying a two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimator, we have found a significant negative effect of air pollution on advertising spending. Third, we have examined the heterogeneity in the pollution effect by location. In particular, we have found that air pollution significantly reduces advertising spending in shopping and residential areas but has no significant impact on work-related areas, such as industrial and government districts. Moreover, air pollution significantly reduces advertising spending in near-building branch roads with lower speed limits, but there is no effect on main roads and boulevards, consistent with our hypotheses. In addition, we have examined whether PM2.5 affects city newspaper advertising. Our results indicate no significant effect of pollution on newspaper advertising. Lastly, we have analyzed a simple model to illustrate how pollution may affect firms' optimal advertising decisions. In particular, we consider a monopolistic firm with endogenous production and advertising spending. Using the model, we have shown that the impact of pollution on ad spending via the marketing efficiency channel is unambiguously negative under the informative and persuasive models of advertising. During the duration of the research project (2020-2022), the principal investigator faced substantial challenges in attending international conferences and presenting the research findings due to significant travel restrictions. As a result, the allocated funds for conference-related expenses remained largely unutilized.

14503219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14503219.value: This project examines the impact of ambient air pollution on advertising spending in the context of China's outdoor advertising markets. We hypothesize that by reducing consumer exposure to the outdoors, air pollution renders out-of-home marketing less effective in catching attention, thereby causing a decline in related marketing spending. We find a significant negative effect of air pollution on advertising spending. Specifically, a 10 μg/m3 (30% of one standard deviation) increase in the same month's average PM2.5 concentration reduces outdoor advertising spending by 2.5%, or CNY 2.1 million (USD 0.3 million) per city. This decrease in outdoor advertising spending is more than 20% of China's total spending on magazine advertising in 2008. Our main results are robust to an array of additional checks. Furthermore, we find that PM2.5 has significant negative effects on outdoor advertising in residential and shopping areas. For shopping areas, the effect is more pronounced: a 10 unit increase in PM2.5 reduces monthly outdoor spending by 3.9% or CNY0.9 million, which is about 43% of the total loss of outdoor advertising money due to air pollution. For train stations, industrial and government areas, the effects are not significant. While we do not find a significant effect of air pollution for main and secondary arterial roads, the effect for branch roads is significantly negative, consistent with the consumer exposure effect. Lastly, we find no significant effect of PM2.5 on newspaper advertising, suggesting a lack of substitution between outdoor advertising and newspaper advertising.

14503219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14503219.value: We point out three directions for future research. First, we expect that the pollution effect detected in our context is also relevant for other important marketing activities, such as point-of-sale marketing and location-based mobile advertising. Future work can look at how air pollution impacts the overall effectiveness of in-store or geo-targeted mobile promotions. Second, further exploiting the dataset constructed for this project, we can look at the impact of other environmental factors, such as extreme temperatures, on advertising expenditure. Third and relatedly, the increased time spent at home and indoors caused by air pollution has important implications for understanding consumption decisions in the digital era. In many emerging economies, drastic environmental changes and the rapid penetration of the Internet are concurrent phenomena. We believe it remains worthwhile to examine whether and how air pollution diverts consumer attention to the online world, thus contributing to the changing Internet media landscape.

14503219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503219.value: While air pollution has tremendous impacts on many aspects of the economy, little is known about how pollution affects marketing activities. We provide a first study on the causal impact of air pollution on advertising markets. Exploiting the meteorological phenomenon of thermal inversions and using monthly data from 24 mega-cities in China for 10 years, we find that air pollution has a significant market-wide impact on outdoor advertising spending. Consistent with the consumer exposure effect that air pollution reduces consumers’ outdoor activities and consumption trips, the adverse effect of air pollution is more pronounced on advertising in residential and shopping areas than in work-related areas. Moreover, we do not find any significant effect of air pollution on newspaper advertising. Our study offers a novel perspective to understand the impact of environmental changes on consumer attention and the media landscape.

14503319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503319.value: This study investigates whether multiyear performance targets disclosed in firms’ proxy statements are informative about firms’ future financial performance and firm value. A large number of firms voluntarily issue one-year earnings forecast but few reveal their expectation of earnings beyond one year. However, earnings growth beyond the current year is an important determinant of firm value, and it may also predict firms’ future earnings. In this study, Weidentify a new source of multiyear earnings expectation from firms’ proxy statements, and investigate the usefulness of such disclosure to equity investors. In recent years, more and more firms use multiyear accounting-based performance (MAP) measures in setting CEO performance goals. In a typical MAP plan the board sets performance goals for the CEO for the next three years, and the compensation amount is determined by the degree of goal achievement. Some firms disclose the MAP goals in their proxy statements when discussing about executive compensation. Although not the board’s intension, the MAP goals are likely to reveal the board’s expectation of the firm’s growth in the next several years. In fact, the MAP disclosure is likely the only source of such information because most firms do not provide multiyear earnings forecasts to investors. The study first examines whether the MAP goals are predicative of firms’ financial performance for the next one to three years. It then examines whether the capital market utilizes information in the MAP goals in forecasting firm earnings. Specifically, it tests whether analysts’ forecast revisions of earnings and growth in earnings respond to the MAP disclosure. Third, the study examines whether the MAP goals are incrementally informative about firm value conditional on currently available information. Finally, the study investigates whether the market fully incorporates the MAP information in valuing firms by examining the association between the MAP goals and firms’ future abnormal stock returns. The study is among the first to examine the informativeness of forward looking financial disclosures in firms’ proxy statements for valuation (as opposed to for compensation) purpose. Such evidence is useful to financial analysts and investors in their search for firm-provided, forward looking earnings information. In addition, the study demonstrates to the boards how their discussion of earnings goals in executive compensation could reveal the firm’s private information. Finally, the study shows how peer firms can utilize MAP information to enhance their understanding of their competitors and their industry. 本文研究公司高管薪酬合同中披露的長期盈利目標對公司未來盈利和公司價值的預測能力。越來越多的公司在與高管簽訂的薪酬合同中設定長期（通常是三年）盈利目標用來衡量高管業績。這些盈利目標反映了董事會和公司領導層對公司未來包括利潤率的預期。利潤增長率是公司定價模型的重要參數，但是公司通常不會公布對未來3-5年的利潤的預期：一些公司從不提供盈利預測；即使是提供盈利預測的公司通常也隻限於未來一個季度或者一年。因此，薪酬合同中披露的三年盈利目標有可能給市場和投資人提供新的有用信息。本文收集高管薪酬合中長期激勵計劃數據，研究計劃中披露的長期盈利目標是否能預測公司未來業績。本文還將檢測當前市場是否有效地利用了薪酬合同中披露的長期盈利信息，以及這一信息是否可以預測未來股價。

14503419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14503419.value: Recently there is a growing attention on a form of meditation called mindfulness. While mindfulness may be considered as a personality trait, a personal meditation exercise, or a training intervention, it is the last one that attracts most attention in the literature because of potential strong and wide impact on personal effectiveness. The father of mindfulness, Kabat-Zinn, defined Mindfulness as “awareness, cultivated by paying attention in a sustained and particular way: on purpose, in the present moment, and non-judgmentally.” The two core components of mindfulness training is, therefore, (1) attentional focus on the present moment, and (2) avoid emotional and rational judgment of the awareness. Mindfulness mediation has be employed as an employee training program by major organizations in the U.S. such as Apple, Google, Target, Intel, Nike, Linkedin, Ford for stress-reduction and concentration and other positive organizational outcomes such as creativity and team building. It is estimated that there were more than three thousand research publications on mindfulness and the number is increasing exponentially. There is even a new journal named “Mindfulness” published by Springer specially devoted to studies on this topic. However, although being widely used, the exact content of mindfulness training varies tremendously across studies, leading to confusions as what exactly the core of mindfulness training is. We start from the basic definition of mindfulness as stated by Kabat-Zinn and consider awareness of the present and non-judgment perception as the two core components of mindfulness training. It is the purpose of this study to investigate and summarize what peripheral elements are used in mindfulness training on top of these two core components. We would also investigate the possible differential effects of the two core components as compared with other additional peripheral components of mindfulness training on outcomes. Finally, we employ construal level theory to study the two core characteristics of mindfulness training, namely present-focus and non-judgmental perception. Based on the construal level theory, the concentration and awareness of the present that mindfulness training emphasizes belongs to lower level of construal understanding. However, one important outcome of mindfulness training, empathy, loving and other-orientation, are very high-level construal perceptions. We test our hypothesis that mindfulness training achieves the objective of increased participants’ empathy and other-concern through peripheral training elements instead of the core characteristics in the definition of mindfulness. 最近，關於「正念」作為一種默想的方法在企業中日漸流行。很多跨國大企業，如穀歌，蘋果電腦，目標百貨，英特爾，耐克運動等，也紛紛在他們的企業中，為員工加入正念默想的培訓。根據正念的始創人喬.卡巴金的定義，「正念」培訓包括兩個部分。第一、專注於當下；第二，避免認知的理性與感性判斷。簡單來說，正念就是非判斷性的專注於當下。 但是縱然正念這麼流行，到底正念訓練應該包括哪些元素和部分，確實眾說紛紜。我們根據上述喬.卡巴金對正念的定義，嘗試找出現今流行的正念訓練中，有哪些元素是符合上述定義的。我們稱這為「核心元素」。其他附加於訓練的元素，我們稱為「邊緣元素」。 是項研究是比較核心元素與邊緣元素，對正念訓練的結果有沒有不同的影響。我們運用高度建構理論來解釋不同正念訓練元素對結果的影響。

14503419.label: Realisation of objectives
14503419.value: 1. We have reviewed the mindfulness-based training literature. After the review, we proposed that MBSR is actually a combination of two different components. In all its promotion, they focused on the first component of non-judgmental and focus on the present. However, based on our theory, this first component would only minimize the operation of the Default Mode Network (DMN), and open the door for the operation of the second component. The second component of other-orientation and emotional regulation will take place after the deactivation of the DMN. 2. We have collected survey data and experimental data on the peripheral and core part of MBSR training (the prevailing mindfulness training designed by the inventor, Kabat-Zinn). In the survey, we used time-lagged data to test the incremental contribution of each component of mindfulness meditation. In the experiment, we recruit students in the PRC, train them on mindfulness mediation, monitor their progress and measure all the variables during the 8-week traning. 3. Our data confirmed our hypothesis. MBSR or mindfulness meditation results depends very much on the peripheral components. When the essential component is paired up with emotional regulation, emotional regulation is increased. In addition, we found that when the peripheral component (nurturing part) is paired up with time-orientation (which is not in the original MBSR program), participants' time perspective is changed. In sum, our project is quite successful. It is misleading to say that the focus-at-the-present and non-judgment nature of MBSR that lead to the results of emotional regulation and other-orientation. These two characteristics only form the essential or core part of MBSR. The real mechanism that leads to the outcomes are the peripheral or nurturing component of MBSR.

The first part of focusing on the present without judgment is attention training. After the Default Mode Network function is mitigated, the second component will clarify the participants' self-concept as designed and eventually attain the expected outcomes.

14503419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14503419.value: Our brain has a built-in automatic function called Default Mode Network (DMN). The network will start involuntarily whenever our Task Processing Network is not working, i.e., when we are not complete focus on our tasks. One best example of DMN functioning is that we will have daydreaming or rumination occasionally. As represented by MBSR designed by Kabat-Zinn, mindfulness training can be broken down into two parts. The first part of focusing on the present without judgment aims at preventing the involuntary automated self-definition process from happening. The second part of caring for others or emotion regulation helps the trainees to clarify their self-concept in these two directions. A survey study and an experiment confirmed our hypotheses above.

14504219.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14504219.value: 基於深度學習的InSAR方法診斷和預測基礎設施結構健康

14504219.label: Co - Investigator(s)
14504219.value: Prof Au, Francis Tat-kwong Prof Lin, Hui Dr Zhang, Fan

14504219.label: Project Objectives
14504219.value: Infrastructural Health Monitoring This study aims to develop a cutting-edge InSAR remote sensing method for the large-scale and high-accuracy monitoring of urban infrastructural health. Both laboratorial and field studies will be designed and conducted to characterize the infrastructural deformation microwave-sensing mechanisms under different configurations of physical properties and microwave operating conditions. PS and DS will be jointly investigated to detect high- and low-coherence urban areas. By constructing a reliable multi-tiered network, the severe atmospheric effects in Hong Kong will be mitigated by subtracting the phase of adjacent pixels. Nonlinear deformation models and robust estimators will be introduced to improve the reliability of parameter estimation. Intelligent deformation prediction The purpose is to develop an innovative data-driven deformation prediction method by deep learning of InSAR time-series deformation and external data of geological and geotechnical engineering, hydrology, meteorology, and geography. Multi-scale, multi-temporal, multi-angle, and multi-dimensional data will be unified to the same spatial and temporal scales using format transformation, spatiotemporal interpolation, and downscaling/upscaling methods. A long-short term memory–convolutional neural network (LSTM-CNN) taking into account spatial correlation and temporal evolution will be developed to reveal infrastructural dynamic mechanisms. A unique quantitative prediction framework incorporating geometric and chromatic features (e.g. point, line, plane, brightness, and color) to semantic recognition (e.g. surface deformation, geological types, temperature, water vapor) will be established. Risk assessment The main objective of this study is to assess the infrastructural performance by the combined use of the InSAR measurements and expert knowledge for precursory identification of abnormal deformations. The monitored and predicted deformation will be verified using in-situ data such as leveling, Global Positioning System (GPS), light detection and ranging (LiDAR) digital surface model (DSM) data, followed by further enhancement of monitoring and prediction methods as appropriate. A GIS platform will be used with a multi-level and multi-phase strategy to facilitate not only overall inspection but also detailed investigation of possible problematic structures, as necessary. The system can assist the public and private sectors to timely diagnose the infrastructural health condition for carrying out maintenance and avoiding possible risks.

14504219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504219.value: Civil infrastructural safety is a key indicator for a sustainable built environment. Unfortunately, the maintenance of infrastructural systems (e.g., subways, bridges, dams, buildings, airports, tunnels, and oil and gas pipelines) is usually not well coordinated. The excessive ground subsidence and structural deformation caused by natural and/or human forces (e.g., sediment consolidation, groundwater extraction, and underground construction) are threatening infrastructural health and public safety. We have seen many deformation-induced problems in recent years, such as reclamation settlement, subway settlement, building collapse, and sinkhole subsidence. The most recent example in Hong Kong is the excessive settlement of 23 buildings adjacent to the To Kwa Wan station caused by the underground construction of the Shatin to Central Link. In some cases, the consequences may be catastrophic. For instance, the building collapse at Ma Tau Wai Road in 2010 led four people to death. With accelerating urbanization, urban infrastructures, especially those underground and semi-underground facilities, are being extensively developed, which can aggravate this problem. Abnormal infrastructural deformation is becoming a new hidden “Urban Disease” that should be paid more attention to by researchers, technicians, politicians, and public. Like human’s health condition, infrastructural health should be also diagnosed regularly to prevent potential hazards. This project aims to develop an innovative synthetic aperture radar (SAR) interferometry (InSAR) remote sensing method with deep learning analysis to monitor and predict infrastructural deformation, and advance fundamental scientific knowledge of infrastructural dynamic behaviors and their interactions with influencing factors for risk assessment. Remote sensing has some distinct advantages over conventional engineering methods, namely, (1) high spatial density of points; (2) cost-effectiveness with no need for any instruments on structures; and (3) large-scale measurement capacity. The deliverables include: (i) a cutting-edge infrastructural deformation monitoring method with joint detection of persistent scatterer (PS) and distributed scatterer (DS) using satellite SAR images; (ii) an innovative data-drive deformation prediction method using deep learning; (iii) a multi-level and multi-phase platform for risk assessment based on expert knowledge and geographic information system (GIS) analysis; and (iv) publications and presentations in the international journals, conferences and workshops. The deliverables of this project will be transferable to subsidence- and deformation-prone regions in the rapidly urbanized Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. The scientific achievements from this project will also have impacts on the investigation of sea level change, groundwater cycle, geological evolution, earth dynamics in which an enhanced understanding of the dynamic mechanisms of urban built environments is also critical. 城市基礎設施安全是城市建成環境可持續發展的關鍵指標，然而，基礎設施（如地鐵，橋樑，水壩，建築物，機場，隧道，石油和天然氣管道）的結構安全問題經常受到威脅，由於自然和人力造成的地面沉降和結構設施變形（如沉積物固結、地下水開採和地下建設）影響到基礎設施健康和公共安全。近年來我們已經看到許多由地面沉降和基礎設施變形引起的問題，例如填海沉降，地鐵沉降，建築物倒塌和地陷。香港沙田至中環線建設過程中造成的土瓜灣站附近23幢樓宇過度沉降，2010年馬頭圍道的樓宇倒塌導致四人死亡。隨著城市化進程的加快，城市基礎設施，尤其是地下和半地下設施，正在廣泛開發，可能會進一步加劇這一問題。異常的基礎設施變形正成為一種新的“城市病”。與人類的健康狀況一樣，基礎設施也應定期“體檢”，以防止潛在的危險發生。 該專案旨在開發一種新的合成孔徑雷達（SAR）衛星干涉測量（InSAR）方法，通過對監測資料深度學習來預測基礎設施變形，提高對基礎設施形變機制和其與環境相互影響的科學認識。與傳統的工程方法相比，遙感具有一些明顯的優勢：（1）高密度測量點; （2）成本更低，不需要安裝任何裝備; （3）大範圍的測量能力。最終成果包括：（i）開發基於衛星SAR圖像聯合反演永久散射體（PS）和分散式散射體（DS）的基礎設施變形監測方法; （ii）使用深度學習的資料驅動方法預測形變; （iii）基於專家知識和地理資訊系統（GIS）分析評估基礎設施安全; （iv）發表國際期刊、會議論文。該專案的成果可推廣到粵港澳大灣區地區進行地面沉降和基礎設施形變監測，研究成果也將對海平面變化、地下水迴圈、地質演化、地球動力學的研究以及城市建成環境的動態變化研究產生重要影響。

14504219.label: Realisation of objectives
14504219.value: In this project, we conducted innovative research on InSAR remote sensing and deep learning methods for infrastructural deformation monitoring and prediction, and have successfully competed all the proposed objectives, including the development of a cutting-edge InSAR remote sensing method for the large-scale and high-accuracy monitoring of urban infrastructural health, development of innovative data-driven deformation prediction methods by deep learning of InSAR time-series deformation and external data, and assessment of the infrastructural safety by the combined use of the InSAR measurements and expert knowledge. One postgraduate student and one postdoctoral fellow were partially supported to work on the development of InSAR remote sensing method for infrastructural deformation monitoring and structural risk assessment, respectively. To address the objective 1, laboratorial and field studies have been conducted to investigate the relationship between InSAR measurements and influential factors. Based on the observations, a reliable and flexible multi-tier network was proposed to mitigate the random atmospheric noise in InSAR measurements. The first-tier network is a Delaunay Triangulation network (DTN) with some additional arcs. The second-tier network densifies the DTN adaptively based on the density of the arcs and increases the redundancy of the network. Robust M-estimator and Ridge-estimator were proposed to estimate the deformation. In addition, thermal expansion was introduced to increase the goodness of fit and derived a new product-thermal amplitude. We concluded that the monitored point density can be up to >100,000/km, the height accuracy can be as good as < 2 m, and the deformation accuracy was approximately 2 mm/year using the proposed method. The method revealed typical infrastructural dynamic behaviors, including underground construction-induced subsidence, seasonal thermal expansion of buildings and bridges, and concrete creep and shrinkage. The results have been published in IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine and Remote Sensing of Environment. To characterize and predict time-series deformation (the objective 2), a set of geological and geotechnical, hydrological, meteorological, and geographical data have been integrated with time-series InSAR deformation. Deep convolutional neural network (CNN) and gate recurrent unit model (GRU) were proposed to predict InSAR time-series deformation and mitigate time-series atmospheric noise, respectively. The results were published in Remote Sensing Letters and ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing, respectively. This is the first time that deep learning methods are proposed for InSAR time-series analysis. We found that the CNN was independent of the temporal deformation patterns and were capable of predicting the linear settlement of the reclaimed lands and seasonal thermal expansion of the buildings simultaneously, whereas the conventional hyperbolic model only predicted the linear settlement. For generating sufficient training data, we developed a simulation method based on the physical mechanisms of typical deformations. Results on both synthetic and real-world data suggest that, compared with the Gaussian filtering method, our proposed GRU model can more effectively suppress the atmospheric noise in the InSAR time series. Based on the InSAR deformation, we evaluated the building risk level over the Kowloon district of Hong Kong and the Futian district of Shenzhen, addressing the objective 3. The normal movements of structures and districts were estimated using the finite element method by considering multi-disciplinary expert knowledge, i.e., geological and geotechnical conditions, groundwater, structural forms, and dead loads. A multi-level and multi-phrase strategy has been established to detect possible risky buildings with abnormal deformations. The first-level checking was implemented at district level. In case the deformation at different phases indicate unusual district-level ground settlement, further investigation was carried out for the affected zones and structures of the district. We found that 10 out of 807 buildings in the Kowloon and 2 out of 145 buildings in the Futian were classified as medium risk. Time-series results showed that the Lucky and BMW buildings were still at the negligible-to-medium risk level in 2021, and should be constantly inspected; the risk level of the Jingli building became negligible from 2020. The results have been published in International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation.
