14504219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14504219.value: We developed a cutting-edge InSAR remote sensing method with a reliable and flexible multi-tier network, robust estimation and nonlinear deformation models to estimate infrastructural deformation. By properly removing random atmospheric delay and thermal expansion, our method can achieve the point density of >100,000/km, the height accuracy of < 2 m, and the deformation accuracy of about 2 mm/year (Shi et al., 2021 RSE; Ma et al., 2022 GRSM). Based on the monitored deformation, deep convolutional neural network and gate recurrent unit model were proposed to characterize and predict time-series deformation (Ma et al., 2020 RSL; Zhao et al., 2021 ISPRS). This is the first time that deep learning methods are proposed for InSAR time-series analysis. For generating sufficient training data, we developed a simulation method based on the physical mechanisms of typical deformations. Compared with conventional model-based methods, deep learning networks are independent of the temporal deformation patterns in the prediction and can adaptively mine the temporal patterns. Building risk levels were identified using the integrated InSAR and finite element method by considering multi-disciplinary expert knowledge of geology, lithology, and hydrology. Results showed that 10 out of 807 buildings in the Kowloon and 2 out of 145 buildings in the Futian were classified as medium risk. Time-series results showed that the Lucky and BMW buildings were still at the negligible-to-medium risk level in 2021, and should be constantly inspected; the risk level of the Jingli building became negligible from 2020 deformation (Ma et al., 2022 JAG).

14504219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14504219.value: The current study focuses on the major infrastructural deformation monitoring at local scales, and there is limited elevation-related atmospheric noise. However, when monitoring large areas such as the entire river delta, regional-scale noise (e.g., elevation-related atmospheric noise and soil moisture) will bias the parameter estimation and challenges the millimeter deformation monitoring accuracy. For deep learning of InSAR measurements, training on synthetic data while testing on real-world data is a transfer learning problem. Without a possible fine-tuning or other domain adaption strategies, achieving a good testing performance requires that the distribution of the training dataset can well cover the distribution of the real-world dataset. There always exists a domain gap between the real and synthetic data, which may lead to a systematic bias. In addition, the risk level assessment highly depends on the standards used, and there are no universal engineering standards for different infrastructures. In the future research, more accurate and universal standards will be investigated.

14504219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14504219.value: Civil infrastructural safety is a key indicator for a sustainable built environment. Unfortunately, the maintenance of infrastructural systems (e.g., subways, bridges, dams, buildings, airports, tunnels, and oil and gas pipelines) is usually not well coordinated. The excessive ground subsidence and structural deformation caused by natural and/or human forces (e.g., sediment consolidation, groundwater extraction, and underground construction) are threatening infrastructural health and public safety. This project aims to develop an innovative synthetic aperture radar (SAR) interferometry (InSAR) remote sensing method with deep learning analysis to monitor and predict infrastructural deformation. The deliverables can help constantly monitor urban structural deformation and assess infrastructural safety over large areas for timely early warning of potential risks.

14504319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14504319.value: This project aims to uncover the mystery of China’s fast-growing private sector that defies severe market imperfections and limited private property rights protection. The novelty comes from two edges: (i) our access to confidential administrative data on firm-to-firm ownership and production networks covering more than 10 million Chinese firms; (ii) using the state-of-the-art quantitative tools for analysing large networks. We want to achieve three specific goals. The first is to deepen our understanding of how firm networks may serve as informal institutions to overcome formal institutional deficiencies. Then, we will back out the unobserved “political capital” attached to each firm that helps to forge China’s firm networks and conduct external validity check for the reliability of our measures. Finally, we will quantify the welfare implications of political capital. Our contributions will be on both theoretical and empirical fronts. The existing study often focuses on the network characteristics that connect private firms to the state sector and ignores the other potentially important features. This project takes a more general approach by identifying firm-specific “political capital”, which is defined as a fundamental force to deal with institutional deficiencies through firm network formation. Empirically, political capital cannot be directly observed and, hence, will have to be inferred from firm networks. Our approach is to structurally estimate a network formation model where political capital is a latent variable. Such estimation has never been done on networks with millions of vertexes. More sophisticated statistical tools will have to be adopted. This project will also deliver rich policy implications. We will characterize the dynamics of China’s firm networks and, then, infer the evolution of political capital. We will also connect the network formation model to the firm dynamics and production network literature to quantify the welfare implications of network formation (i.e., the extent to which it affects private firm entry and subsequent growth). 本項研究旨在利用企業所有制數據分析和估計中國企業的關系網絡、形成機制及其經濟影響。

14504319.label: Realisation of objectives
14504319.value: Objective 1: Construct a conceptual framework to deepen our understanding of how firm networks may serve as informal institutions to overcome formal institutional deficiencies. The main output of this project is "The Rise of State-Connected Private Owners in China" (Working Paper, No. w28170. National Bureau of Economic Research, 2020). This paper further develops the idea that firm investment networks serving as informal institutions by penetrating firms' complex ownership structure, focusing on the ultimate owners of firms and studying how the equity connections (owning joint ventures) between state and private owners serve as informal institutions given weak formal institutions. A paper in Chinese which summarized the major findings of this project was also published on Comparative Studies (Pinyin: Bi Jiao; https://bijiao.caixin.com/m/2021-03-02/101669308.html) in 2021, which is a journal mainly focusing on important topics related to China's policies and reforms. Inspired by cases in which Chinese private entrepreneurs usually circumvent discriminating restrictions by setting up joint ventures (equity connections) with state-owned enterprises. We investigate China's administrative registration records, which include more than 40 million firms and 60 million owners (state or private), and construct an owner network, showing all firms' ultimate owners, number and size of firms they owned, and how they are linked through equity connections. For the first time, we document a hierarchy of private owners: the largest ones usually are directly connected with state owners, the next largest private owners are not connected with state owners but they are more likely to be indirectly connected with state owners through the directly connected private owners, while the smallest private owners do not have any ties with state owners. We also find that the directly and indirectly state-connected private sector has expanded significantly in last two decades, accounting for almost all the increase of private sector in China. We then construct a network formation model to understand the mechanism of the hierarchy structure, in which (i) all private owners bear an output tax due to "bad institutions"; (ii) a private owner can choose to connect with a state owner which lowers her output tax by paying a price; and (iii) once a private owner becomes connected, she can also provide downward connections to other private owners and charge a price for each connection. Several key facts observed in the data can be well explained by this model. For example, larger owners (owners with higher TFP in the model) are connected closer with the state owners; the span of an owner (number of downward connections provided by the owner) is decreasing in owner's distance from the state owners; larger benefit (reduction of output tax caused by bad institutions) will increase the share of connected private owners. Objective 2: Back out the unobserved "political capital" attached to each firm by estimating the formation of firm network. On the basis of the owner network formation model, we structurally estimate the by-distance-to-the-state-owner benefit of connections for year 2000, 2010, and 2019. In the cross-section, the benefit from becoming connected is generally decreasing in distance to the state, which is consistent with the model implications. In the time series, the benefit for each distance gets larger in the past 20 years, which explains the growth of connected private sector in the same period. We do not know for sure what the institutional reasons exactly are. Two possibilities are growing financial resources controlled by the state and the large expansion of local government budgets from the emergence of local government financial vehicles and increasingly lucrative land sales. Our results suggest that these financial resources may not have been kept in the state sector but instead were allocated to connected private owners and firms through various channels. Objective 3: Conduct external validity checks for the reliability of our measures. We take advantage of Xi's anti-corruption campaign initiated in 2013 as an exogenous shock to test the existence of benefit of connections with the state owners. The general idea is that if a private owner get benefit by connecting to some state owner, she will loss when the state owner is targeted in the anti-corruption campaign. What's more, private owners directly connected with the state owner will loss more than those indirectly connected ones. We prepare a list of anti-corruption campaign involved state owners by reading announcements made by China's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and identify affected directly and indirectly connected private owners. Tax survey data are used to provide the financial indicators, while propensity score matching method is adopted to make sure that we are comparing similar private owners. We find evidences that affected directly connected private owners significantly reduced their investment after the campaign, while the effect for indirectly connected private owners is smaller. Objective 4: Quantify the welfare implications of political capital. We also conduct counter-factual analyses in which we raise the benefit of connections from the level of 2000 to the level of 2019, holding other conditions unchanged. Our results show that this may increase aggregate output of the private sector by 2.5% per year between 2000 and 2019, which explains 23.1% of the growth of the private sector in the same period.

14504319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14504319.value: We delivered two major research papers from this project (Bai et al., 2020; 2021). We use administrative registration records with information on the owners of all Chinese firms to document their equity connections (owning joint venture). We find a hierarchy of private owners: the largest private owners have direct equity connections with state owners, the next largest private owners have equity connections with private owners that themselves have equity ties with state owners, and the smallest private owners do not have any equity connections with state owners. The network of "state-connected" private owners has expanded over the last two decades. The share of registered capital of state-connected private owners increased by almost 20 percentage points between 2010 and 2019, driven by two trends. First, state owners have increased their investments in joint ventures with private owners. Second, private owners with equity connections to state owners also increasingly invest in joint ventures with other smaller private owners. The expansion in the state-connected private sector may have increased aggregate output of the private sector by 2.5% a year in this period. 14504319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14504319.value: The impact of this study is twofold. First, it sheds light on further researches on state-owned enterprises (SOE), in which SOEs should not be treated as isolated economic entities, instead their effects on connected private firms through equity connections and other channels (e.g., production networks) need to get more attention. Second, institutions may generate both good and bad consequences in different economic and policy environments. Although this paper shows some evidences that this informal institution (equity connection) may contribute to the growth of private sector of China, the conclusion could be challenged by the development state-owned sector in recent years. Further researches need to be done to keep updating knowledge about the role SOEs play in the Chinese economy.

14504319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14504319.value: A puzzling question about Chinese economy is why China has a thriving private sector, given its weak economic institutions. This research proposes an explanation that equity connections between private and state owners may serve as an informal institution which help private owners circumvent discriminating restrictions. We investigate China's administrative registration records and construct an owner network, showing all firms' ultimate owners and how they are linked through equity connections. For the first time, we document a hierarchy of private owners: the largest ones usually are directly connected with state owners, the next largest private owners are not connected with state owners but they are more likely to be indirectly connected with state owners through the directly connected private owners, while the smallest private owners do not have any ties with state owners. We also find that the state-connected private sector has expanded significantly in last two decades. We also construct a theoretical framework to understand the formation mechanism of the hierarchy structure, in which private owners are allowed to build connections with state owner to reduce wedges caused by bad institutions, and what's more, they can also provide connections to other private owners once being connected.

14505519.label: Project Objectives
14505519.value: Construct a long-term contracting model to analyze how information feedback during the contract affect incentives. Show that when the length of the contract is sufficiently long, a contract that rewards the agent for the part of his performance that exceeds a minimum performance standard is near optimal. Investigate how the performance standard is affected by the information feedback the agent receives during the contract. Compare the performance of this near-optimal contract to that of a fully optimal contract in an example where the optimal contract can be derived explicitly. Apply the results of this model to study repeated games with private monitoring.

14505519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505519.value: Many long-term principal-agent contracts involve a lump-sum component that depends on the agent's overall performance over a number of periods. For example, an assistant professor may need to publish six papers or more in six years for tenure, but it does not matter whether she publishes one every year or six in one year. As time passes, her incentive may change as she receives feedback about her output. If she believes she is likely to meet the standard, she may continue to exert effort; otherwise, she may give up and start seeking another career. This project uses a T-period contracting model to study how information feedback during a contract affects contract design. In our model, the agent chooses a private action in each of T periods. The chosen action generates two signals, one privately observed by the agent and one privately observed by the principal, according to some action-dependent signal distribution. At the end of period T, the agent reports her signals to the principal. A contract is a function that maps the principal's signals and the agent's report about her signals to a payment. The agent is liquidity constrained so that the contract payment must be non-negative. The objective of the principal is to design a contract to implement a constant action in all T periods at a minimum cost. One feasible contract is to enforce the desired action in each period independently through T identical one-period contracts. But such a "linear" contract is usually not cost effective. By linking incentives over periods the principal can reduce the expected payment to the agent. Yet, the form of the optimal linking contract is sensitive to what information the agent may observe on and off the equilibrium path during the contract. The main objective of this project is to show that despite this apparent complexity a properly designed simple contract that rewards the agent linearly when her performance exceed a minimum performance standard is near optimal when T is large. We aims to understand how the performance standard depends on what feedback the agent receives on and off the equilibrium path. 許多長期委託 -代理（ principal-agent ）合約涉及一次總付的部分，這取決於代理者在多個時期的整體表現。 例如，助理教授可能需要在六年內發表六篇或更多論文以獲得終身教職，但無論她是每年發表一篇還是一年發表六篇論文都無關緊要。 隨著時間的推移，她的激勵可能隨著收到有關她的輸出的回饋而改變。 如果她認為自己可能符合標準，她可能會繼續努力：否則，她可能會放棄並開始尋求其他職業。 該專案使用 T 期合約模型來研究合約中的資訊回饋如何影響合同設計。 在我們的模型中，代理者（agent）在每個T期選擇一個私人的行為。 根據一些依賴于動作的信號分佈，所選擇的行為產生兩個信號，一個由代理者本人（agent）才可以觀察，另一個由委託人本人（principal ）才可以觀察。 在週期T結束時，代理者（agent）向委託人（principal ）報告她的信號。 合約是一種將委託人的信號和代理者所報告的信號映射到付款的函數。 代理者受流動性限制，因此合約付款必須是非負的。 委託人的目標是設計一個合約，以最低的成本在所有T期內實施持續的行動。 一個可行的合約是通過 T 個 相同的一期合約，獨立地在每個時期強制執行所期望的行動。 但這種「線性」合約通常不符合成本效益。 通過將激勵與時期聯繫起來，委託人可以減少對代理者的預期付款。 然而，最優連接契約的形式對於代理者在契約過程中，其在均衡路徑上和非均衡路徑上可能觀察到的資訊非常敏感。 該專案的主要目的是表明儘管存在這種明顯的複雜性，一個正確設計的簡單合約，當代理者表現超過最低表現標準時，線性地獎勵代理者，當T很大時是接近最優的。 我們的目標是瞭解績效標準如何取決於代理者在平衡路徑和非平衡路徑上獲得的回饋。

14505819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505819.value: Facing underdeveloped credit reporting systems and banking systems, many small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in developing countries such as China have great difficulty obtaining sufficient financing to compete in their markets. As a result, some SMEs often have to rely on inventory-based financing (IBF), a form of asset-based financing that uses inventory as collateral to secure loans, to fill their needs for working capital. Motivated by real-world practices, we propose to study a firm (retailer) who faces a stochastic demand of his product in a future period. Anticipating higher future price for a key raw material for his product, the firm is willing to purchase the raw material ahead of the scheduled manufacturing of the product in order to "lock up" a potentially cheaper price. However, doing so will incur early commitment of working capital and risk the price volatility of the raw material. The cash-strapped retailer in our study can secure additional loans under an IBF scheme by pledging his raw material inventory as collateral. We propose to study the retailer's optimal raw material purchasing, financing, and inventory decisions using a multi-period stochastic modeling approach. We will characterize the optimal inventory and financing decisions, provide managerial insights on the firm’s inventory decisions with and without the option of securing additional capitals through IBF, and identify business environments in which a firm will significantly improve its profitability with the availability of the IBF. We will also collect real world data and use it to conduct a numerical study to validate the theoretical results and to potentially develop further managerial insights. Our proposed study will significantly contribute to the supply chain financing literature by studying a new multi-period inventory management problem with IBF. A unique feature of our proposed problem is that the retailer could be forced to liquidate his inventory pre-maturely when the value of the collateralized inventory, which is stochastic, falls below a certain pre-specified threshold under the IBF covenant. Our study is motivated by real-world practices, and therefore it has the potential to help practitioners better understand their operational and financial risks and improve the effectiveness of their inventory and financial decisions. 面對不完善的銀行與融資系統許多發展中國家（比如中國） 的中小企業面臨極大的融資困難，因而影響到他們的競爭力。 許多中小企業經常要用庫存融資的方式，來滿足他們資金 的需要。本研究項目將使用多期動態優化決策模型， 來研究一個企業用庫存融資的方式購買一批原材料， 以滿足將來某個時期的需要的庫存與融資決策。 研究模型的一個獨特之處是企業用來融資的抵押庫存的 價值波動，可能造成融資的企業的庫存被強制平倉。 本研究項目將對供應鏈金融的理論和實踐帶來重要的貢獻。

14505819.label: Realisation of objectives
14505819.value: The PI has achieved the three objectives for this project. Specifically, the PI was able to complete a paper based on the proposed research. In the paper, a single season (period) model, with stochastic inventory value and uncertain demand, is developed to study the impacts of various inventory-based financing (IBF) structures on a supply chain's performance. Thus, Objective 1 is completely achieved. Furthermore, the paper characterizes the optimal production, inventory and financing decisions for the borrower under various IBF schemes. Thus, Objective 2 is also achieved. Finally, the paper provide in-depth analysis of the interdependencies between inventory flow and financial flow in a supply chain under various business settings, and offer new managerial insights on how the structure of an IBF can affect supply chain decisions. Thus, Objective 3 is completely achieved.

14505819.label: Major findings and research outcome
14505819.value: The major findings of the completed research project focus on how the structure of an inventory-based financing (IBF) contract can impact the production, inventory and financing decisions in a supply chain. Specifically, in the completed paper that is supported by the research project, the PI and his co-authors study the impacts of a contract structure called borrowing-based covenant (BBC) in IBF by considering a supply chain in which a supplier sells a key material to a cash-strapped retailer, and offers an IBF facility to the retailer using purchased inventory as collateral. They found that the deployment of a strictly enforced BBC in IBF could be a double-edge sword to the supply chain. On the one hand, when the supply chain profit margin is low, a restrictive BBC can help the supplier to mitigate the retailer’s default risk induced by dramatic decrease in the collateralized inventory value; and it can even bring benefit to the entire supply chain by discouraging the retailer from taking on excessive inventory risk. On the other hand, when the supply chain profit margin is high, a partial or full liquidation of pledged inventory triggered by the breach of the BBC could undermine the retailer’s ability to fulfill future demand and therefore potentially magnifies the risk of default. The presence of such risk could also cause the retailer to become conservative in borrowing through IBF to carry more material inventory, and ultimately hurt the entire supply chain’s profitability. The study further proposes a so-called flexible BBC (FBBC) with flexibility in inventory liquidation when BBC violation occurs. The study shows that the FBBC with its liquidation decision based on supply chain profit maximization is more effective than the traditional BBC commonly observed in practice.

14505819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14505819.value: There are several potential future research directions based on the research supported by the project. First, the completed study uses a styled two-period model to investigate the impacts of BBC in IBF with stochastic inventory salvage value. It would be valuable to develop a multi-period inventory management model to study the retailer’s inventory decisions under an IBF scheme with BBC, but this extension is expected to be much harder technically. Second, the current completed study assumes that the retailer will not proactively sell his collateralized inventory. It would be interesting to study the setting in which the retailer can strategically buy and sell his inventory in a multi-period environment.

14505819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14505819.value: Borrowing base covenant (BBC) is commonly used in inventory-based financing (IBF) in practice to protect a lender against the potential market value erosion in collateralized inventory. The research study conducted under this project finds that this practice, though very popular in real-world practice, can potentially cause pre-mature inventory liquidation and lead to higher supply chain disruption risk which may eventually make both lender and borrower worse-off. Our study proposes an improved contract structure called flexible BBC and show that it is a more effective contract structure to achieve better supply chain performance.

14505919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14505919.value: Severance pay for executives is one of the most controversial features of executive compensation. There was widespread outrage in the United States when executives who had apparently run their companies to the brink of bankruptcy following the 2008-2009 financial crisis were allowed to leave their companies with severance pay in tens of millions of dollars. For example, Leo Apotheker left Hewlett Packard in 2011 after only 11 months as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) with a severance package of 13.2 million. Many have labelled such payments as “pay for failure” and seen such practices as another instance of “board capture” by powerful CEOs. However, others have argued that severance pay can actually be in shareholder interest. Arguments include enabling CEOs to take on more risk which can be in shareholder interest, honoring implicit contracts, and making it easier to remove CEOs when this would be beneficial to the firm. In this research, we will build on the PI’s earlier published work (Dasgupta et al. (2018)) and examine how severance pay and retention policies are affected when firms in an industry are exposed to greater foreign (import) competition. Specifically, we will examine the effect of major import tariff cuts in US industries on severance pay practices. The PI’s previous research shows that tariff cut-induced competitive pressure increases the rate at which CEOs exit the company. Both turnovers that can be classified as “voluntary” and “forced” increase following major tariff cuts. Thus, it is expected that such turnovers will trigger more severance payments. Incentive pay provisions may also have to be changed. This study will examine, using a hand-collected sample of executive severance contracts, how pay practices change following tariff cuts, with a particular focus on severance pay and incentive pay. We will examine both ex ante or contractual severance pay and ex post or ad hoc severance pay, and the relationship between the two. Our analysis is expected to enhance our understanding of why severance pay features in executive compensation.

14506119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14506119.value: Stocks of companies involved in alcohol, tobacco, and gaming are “sin stocks,” which are avoided by some investors, particularly institutions subject to social norms. Hong and Kacperczyk (2009) show that these stocks earn higher expected returns as they are neglected by norm-constrained investors. In this project, we will examine whether stocks of high-emission firms represent a new class of sin stocks. As people become more aware of climate change, the pressure on financial institutions to avoid these stocks increases. As a result, some existing shareholders need to sell their holdings. We plan to identify the types of institutional investors that sell and divest and the time when they do so, which will help us examine closer the mechanism of how sin stocks earn higher future returns. There is plenty of evidence that large investors divest from stocks of climate-unfriendly companies: Norway’s sovereign wealth fund, the world’s largest with close to US$1 trillion in assets, began to divest from coal companies in 2015. A report by Arabella Advisors shows that a total of almost 1,000 institutions around the world, including faith-based organizations, philanthropic foundations, government institutions, university endowments, and pension funds, have committed to divest from the fossil fuel industry. While current stock prices would fall when large investors sell their holdings, if future cashflows of these companies do not decrease, the future returns of these stocks would be higher because they are neglected by some socially responsible investors. It is possible that some divestments are based on negative information about future cashflows. We will focus on cases in which this is less unlikely to be the motive. For example, if the public awareness of climate change in a country is higher, institutions in the country tend to face more pressure from their clients and sell accordingly. Passive institutions such as pension funds do not actively gather information on firms’ cashflows. Future returns of high-emission firms are more likely to be higher after these divestments. Our earlier work, Choi, Gao, and Jiang (2018), shows that retail investors revise their beliefs about climate change upwards when the local weather is unusually warm. This complementary project focuses on institutional investors and the long-term pricing of stocks of high-emission firms. Climate finance is a relatively new research area. We attempt to understand the effect of heightened climate risk and public awareness on investment decisions and asset prices. 涉及酒類，煙草和遊戲的公司的股票是「罪孽股票」。一些投資者，特別是受社會規範約束的機構，會避免持有這些股票。 過往研究發現，因為受到規範約束的投資者的忽視，這些股票獲得更高的預期回報。在這個項目中，我們將研究高碳排放公司的股票是否代表一類新的罪孽股。隨著人們越來越意識到氣候變化，金融機構避免持有這些股票的壓力越來越大。因此，一些現有股東需要出售其持股。 我們計劃確定出售和撤資的機構投資者的類型以及他們這樣做的時間，這將有助於我們更仔細地研究罪孽股如何獲得更高的未來回報。有大量證據表明，大型投資者對氣候不友好的公司撤資：挪威的主權基金是世界上最大的及擁有近1萬億美元資產的基金，於2015年開始從煤炭公司撤資。一份報告顯示，全世界近1000家機構，包括信仰組織，慈善基金會，政府機構，大學捐贈基金和養老基金，都承諾對化石燃料行業撤資。雖然當大型投資者出售其持有的股票時當前股價會下跌，但如果這些公司的未來現金流量沒有減少，因為他們被一些對社會負責的投資者所忽視，這些股票的未來回報將會更高。 有些撤資可能基於有關未來現金流量的負面信息。我們將重點關注不太可能成為動機的案例。例如，如果一個國家的公眾對氣候變化的認識較高，那麼該國的機構往往會面臨來自客戶的更多壓力並相應地進行出售。養老基金等被動機構不積極收集有關公司現金流量的信息。在這些撤資之後，高排放公司的未來回報更可能更高。 我們早期的作品表明，當當地天氣異常溫暖時，散戶投資者會對氣候變化的信念進行調整。這個補充項目側重於機構投資者和高排放公司股票的長期定價。氣候融資是一個相對較新的研究領域。我們試圖了解氣候風險提高和公眾意識對投資決策和資產價格的影響。

14506119.label: Realisation of objectives
14506119.value: All the objectives are achieved. For objectives 2 and 3, we focus on price valuation ratios (price-to-book, price-to-earnings, price-to-sales, and price-to-cashflow) rather than returns for the following reasons: most of the literature focuses on returns, but as Pastor, Stambaugh, and Taylor (Journal of Financial Economics 2021, 2022) show both theoretically and empirically, green stocks' returns are higher when socially responsible investors buy these stocks in recent years, but green stocks' future expected returns should be lower. We think price-to-book ratios map more closely to Pastor, Stambaugh, and Taylor's (2021) model, where firm managers care about the stock price. A few other studies have shown that brown stocks and sin stocks have lower market-to-book ratios (e.g., Bolton and Kacperczyk (JF forthcoming) and Hong and Kacperczyk (JFE 2009)). In the working paper, we also look at the follow-up question that how lower price valuation ratios faced by brown firms push them to become cleaner. This shows the real impact of stock prices.

14506119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14506119.value: There are two papers. The first one, titled "Measuring the Carbon Exposure of Institutional Investors," was published in the Journal of Alternative Investments in 2020. It introduces a simple definition of carbon-intensive firms to measure institutional investors’ exposure to the emission intensities of portfolio companies. We show that 13F institutions, on average, gradually reduce their carbon exposure relative to the US value-weighted market portfolio, from overweighting stocks of high-emission firms by 0.5% in 2001 to underweighting by 0.2%–0.7% since 2015, consistent with the view that investors have become more concerned about the financial implications of climate change. The second paper, titled "Carbon Stock Devaluation," (previous title: "Global Carbon Divestment and Firms' Actions") is a working paper and has been submitted to top finance journals. The paper won the CICF Best Paper Award at China International Conference in Finance in 2021. We show that high-emission firms have lower price valuation and they take actions to become greener.

14506119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14506119.value: We will continue to work on the working paper and submit it to top finance journals for publication. The most recent presentation is in May 2023 and we have received a lot of valuable comments. In particular, we would like to use natural disasters, which increase climate awareness, as an instrumental variable to further establish the link between stock prices and firms' actions. We believe that our work can contribute to the climate finance literature and stimulate more future research. Firms' green actions are important to help lower carbon emissions and achieve carbon neutrality targets.

14506119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14506119.value: Using global evidence, we show that high-emission firms tend to have lower price valuation ratios than low-emission firms in the same country, especially in recent years. The price gap coincides with heightened climate awareness following local natural disasters, as well as with the divestment from high-emission stocks by financial institutions and retail investors. In the presence of equity price pressure in the country, high-emission firms reduce carbon emission intensities, increase green innovation activities, and downsize their operations. The changes we identify are unlikely a consequence of tighter environmental regulations, as private high-emission firms do not show the same results.

14600019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600019.value: 此項目的研究目的是建立一個標準化、25,281個雙字詞的唸名反應時間和準確率的數據庫，並探討字符和詞彙變量如何影響大學生對這些雙字詞的唸名反應時間和準確率。 項目背景 透過香港研究資助局的支持，我們創立了一個關於雙字詞的標準化詞匯判斷（即，決定兩個字符是否構成中文雙字詞）反應時間和準確率的數據庫。此數據庫提供雙字詞的詞彙變量和其描述性統計（Tse et al.，2017）。與詞匯判斷任務相似，在唸名任務（即，朗讀出雙字詞）中的表現，也常用於過往中文詞語識別過程的研究。 項目設計 我們計劃創立一個唸名反應時間和準確率的數據庫來擴展漢語詞匯方案。我們將收集大學生對由Tse等人編制的25,281個雙字詞的唸名反應時間和準確度數據。同時，我們會添加與字符和詞彙音韻相關的其他變量。我們將透過項目級多元回歸模型分析平均唸名反應時間和準確率。 項目意義 透過詞彙變量的資料和標準化雙字詞的唸名反應時間和準確率，我們計劃解決以下問題。首先，我們將探討詞彙變量的主要影響及其潛在的相互作用，以測試字形變量（例如，筆劃數），語音變量（例如，同音密度）和語義變量（例如，語義透明度）對唸名反應時間和準確率的預測能力。其次，我們將比較詞彙變量對詞匯判斷和唸名表現的影響，以確定很多詞語識別過程的結果是任務特定的（例如，僅在唸名任務中發生，而不在詞匯判斷中發生）還是任務不特定的現象。第三，對一些先前在因子設計實驗中證據不太穩固但理論上很重要的詞彙效應（例如，同音密度×字符頻率相互作用），我們會透過對標準化雙字詞的唸名反應時間和準確率的項目級多元回歸模型分析來驗證這些效應能否在超過二萬個詞語的數據庫中出現。 總體而言，此項研究將為學術界提供一個重要的數據庫，以提高我們對中文詞語識別過程的認識，及為心理語言學研究作出重要貢獻。

14600019.label: Realisation of objectives
14600019.value: We successfully recruited participants and collected data as planned in our proposal. We collected norms for speeded naming reaction times and accuracy rates, and compiled lexical variables (e.g., phonological consistency and semantic neighborhood size) for 25,281 two-character Chinese words. We published our work (i.e., Tse, Chan, Yap, & Tsang, in press) in Behavior Research Methods, which is a top journal in the field (impact factor = 5.953 and 5-year impact factor = 7.867) and ranked 6th out of 91 in Psychology, Experimental Category, and 1st out of 13 in Psychology, Mathematical Category in the most updated version of Social Science Citation Index. In Tse, Chan, Yap, and Tsang (in press), we reported this database and using the megastudy approach we conducted item-level regression analyses to test the relative predictive power of orthographic variables (e.g., stroke count), phonological variables (e.g., phonological consistency), and semantic variables (e.g., semantic transparency) in speeded naming performance. This fulfills our Objective 1. We also compared the effects of lexical variables on naming performance and Tse et al.’s (2017, Behavior Research Methods) lexical decision performance to examine the extent to which those effects are task-specific or task-general. This fulfills our Objective 2. We make this dataset freely accessible to the research community (see https://osf.io/vwnps) as this resource provides a valuable addition to other influential mega-databases, such as Balota et al. (2004) and furthers our understanding of Chinese word recognition processes. The large-scale corpus data of various lexical variables and normed lexical decision and speeded naming performance with more than 25,000 Chinese words provide important benchmarking data for Chinese word processing, which will facilitate the informing and constraining of computational models. Freely accessible to the research community, this resource provides a valuable addition to other influential Lexicon Projects (e.g., English, Dutch, French, and Malay) being rapidly developed across the world and in line with the current research zeitgeist. This fulfills our Objective 3. In Tse, Yap, and Chan (2023), a poster titled, “Are Chinese words accessed as a whole or via characters in lexical decision and speeded naming task?”, that is under review for the 33rd International Congress of Psychology, we performed linear mixed-effect analyses on Tse et al.’s (2017) lexical decision data and Tse et al.’s (in press) speeded naming data. We first controlled for the effects of orthographic (e.g., stroke count), phonological (e.g., consistency), and semantic (e.g., number of meanings) character-variables and word-variables. Next, we tested interactive effects among semantic transparency (ST, whether the characters are semantically related to the word), word frequency (WF), and character frequency (CF). In lexical decision, we obtained ST x CF and WF x CF interactions, but not a ST x WF interaction. The effect of CF was stronger for transparent words than for opaque words and was stronger for low-frequency words than for high-frequency words. In speeded naming, we found ST x CF and WF x CF interactions, resembling the patterns seen in lexical decision. Importantly, there was also a ST x WF interaction: the effect of ST was positive (faster recognition for transparent, compared to opaque, words) for high-frequency words but negative for low-frequency words. These results suggest that word-level processing is involved in Chinese word processing, as demonstrated by the influence of WF and ST variables, and character-level processing is also involved, as indicated by the modulation of the CF variable. These results shed light on the interactions between character-level and word-level properties. These empirical benchmarks will help inform and constrain models of Chinese word processing. This also fulfills our Objective 1. Furthermore, we completed data analyses to investigate the main effects of neighborhood size, neighbor frequency, homophone density, and phonological frequency, as well as the interaction effects associated with neighborhood size in lexical decision and speeded naming performance, as motivated by previous research (e.g., Li et al., 2015; Tse & Yap, 2018; Wu et al., 2013). A manuscript based on these analyses is submitted to Journal of Memory and Language, which is attached with this report.

14600019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14600019.value: In Tse, Chan, Yap, and Tsang (in press, Behavior Research Methods), we reported a database of norms for speeded naming reaction times and accuracy rates, as well as the compilation of lexical variables (e.g., consistency and neighborhood size) for 25,281 two-character Chinese words. In item-level regression analyses, we tested the relative predictive power of orthographic variables (e.g., stroke count), phonological variables (e.g., regularity), and semantic variables (e.g., semantic transparency) in speeded naming performance. We replicated most of the benchmark findings in speeded naming, such as the effects of phonological consistency, neighborhood size, and phonological regularity. Moreover, we compared the influence of the words and/or the first and second characters on speeded naming and found that the first character had a stronger influence than the second character in most of the lexical variables (e.g., character frequency and semantic transparency). This suggests that the pronunciation of Chinese words is likely activated through the combination of the characters, rather than via holistic representation of the word. Furthermore, we compared the predictive power of phonological versus semantic variables in speeded naming versus lexical decision by comparing the current speeded naming dataset with the lexical decision dataset that we established in our previous work (Tse et al., 2017, Behavior Research Methods). Importantly, we observed that task demands influence relative contribution of phonological and semantic variables in speeded naming and lexical decision performance: orthographic variables accounted for more variance than semantic and phonological variables in both lexical decision and speeded naming performance, but semantic variables accounted for more variance than phonological variables in lexical decision while phonological variables accounted for more variance than semantic variables in speeded naming. In Tse, Yap, and Chan (2023), we performed linear mixed-effect analyses on Tse et al.’s (2017, in press) data to test interactive effects among semantic transparency, word frequency, and character frequency. These findings suggest that both word-level and character-level processing are at play in Chinese word recognition, whether participants make lexical decision or read aloud the words. Similar to our previous work (Tse et al., 2017), we have made speeded naming dataset freely available to researchers across various disciplines. They can use it to select word stimuli matched on extraneous lexical variables across conditions when designing factorial-design experiments, run virtual replication experiments to test whether previous findings can be replicated with different stimuli that share similar lexical characteristics, and compile more lexical variables to address future research questions.

14600019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14600019.value: Using the current speeded naming dataset and Tse et al.’s lexical decision dataset, we are now investigating the interaction effects among lexical variables in lexical decision and speeded naming performance. This research is motivated by previous studies, e.g., word frequency x neighborhood size interaction (Li et al., 2015). Those interaction effects were previously obtained in factorial design experiments that may not necessarily generalize when more extraneous variables are controlled for (as was the case in our megastudy approach). This work is submitted for publication and attached with this report. In the next step, we plan to apply for General Research Fund to norm auditory lexical decision performance. In this task, participants listen to a sound clip of a two-character Chinese word or a recombined-character Chinese nonword and decide whether it is a correct Chinese word by keypress. By comparing this dataset with Tse et al.'s (2017) visual lexical decision dataset, we will examine relative importance of lexical variables influencing performance in different modalities (visual and auditory). Similar projects were reported in English (Goh, Yap, & Chee, 2020; Tucker et al., 2019) and French (Ferrand et al., 2018). To our knowledge, no such project has been reported for Chinese two-character words.

14600019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14600019.value: In this project, we have created a large-scale repository of lexical variables and speeded naming responses for more than 25,000 traditional Chinese two-character words. Using this dataset and the one we previously developed for lexical decision responses, we identified how continuously varying lexical characteristics, such as the number of strokes and character/word frequency, individually and jointly modulate word recognition performance. We also tested whether this modulation depends on the task demands, such as judging the lexicality of the word or reading aloud the word. This repository of lexical characteristics and behavioral measures is a valuable resource for researchers. It allows them to select word stimuli matched on lexical variables across conditions when designing factorial-design experiments, run virtual replication experiments to test whether previous findings can be replicated with different stimuli that share similar lexical characteristics, and compile new lexical variables to address research questions of their interest. This resource is freely accessible to the research community and provides a valuable addition to other influential Lexicon Projects, such as those for English, Dutch, French, and Malay, that are being rapidly developed across the world and are in line with the current research zeitgeist.

14600319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600319.value: 目標 本項目旨在確定 (i)認知控制如何影響患有妄想的病人重新評估和形成妄想，以及(ii)接收到與妄想有關的內容如何影響病人的認知控制。 項目背景 70%的精神病性障礙患者都有妄想症狀。前人研究已經證明，並非所有的妄想都是固定不變的。大約有25-50%的病人承認，他們的妄想有可能出錯，並且能夠接受其他解釋。這一被稱作“信念靈活性” 的現象具有臨床上的重要性，因為能夠靈活地重新評估其妄想的病人，治療效果更佳。然而，信念靈活性的測量主要使用聚焦妄想的臨床訪談。由於妄想的內容和相應情緒的潛在影響，該方法可能難以純粹地測量到受訪者對於信念的認知評估。因此，解析信念靈活性所包含的認知過程，可以促進該研究領域的發展。雖然已有研究指出，認知控制對於一般的信念評估有重要作用，其與妄想評估的關係卻尚未得到檢驗。因此，我們提出下列適時且重要的問題：(i) 認知控制對個體評估妄想的影響有多大？(ii) 接收到妄想或情緒的信息會在多大程度上干擾認知控制能力？ 項目簡述 本項目以行為範式為主要的研究方法，將模擬認知控制過程（抑制控制，工作記憶更新，和定式轉換）與信念靈活性及妄想之間橫向和縱向的關係。96名患有首發非情感性精神病性障礙的成年病人將在項目開始（基線時間），和六個月之後，接受兩次臨床訪談和認知控制測試。我們提出以下假設：(i) 在基線時間，認知控制將通過信念靈活性影響妄想，並且(ii)認知控制能力將預測妄想經過六個月後的變化。在兩次測量中，每名被試將在三中實驗情境中完成認知控制任務——當聽到妄想詞彙時，當聽到情緒詞彙時，及聽到中性詞彙時；(iii)與其他兩種實驗情境相比，在聽到妄想詞彙的實驗情境中，認知控制的表現將受到更為顯著的影響。 項目重要性 本項目的成果將有助於形成關於認知控制和妄想維持之間，動態相互作用的理論解釋，並且可能啟發針對妄想的心理干預。

14600919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14600919.value: Meta-analyses of dyslexia intervention studies in alphabetic languages have shown that children benefit from meta-linguistic training, such as phonological processing and grapheme-phoneme conversion. It remains to be shown, whether meta-linguistic training is also effective for dyslexia in Chinese, where traditional learning methods emphasize memorization. Moreover, evaluation studies have typically focused on short-term rather than long-term effects, even though the presence or absence of long-term effects have important practical implications. Finally, neural measures of underlying mechanisms have the potential to complement intervention evaluation and to predict intervention outcome based on pre-intervention measures. The present proposal aims to take advantage of a unique opportunity by following up children who are currently participating in a dyslexia training study with pre- and post-intervention measures, funded by other sources. In that study 60 children with dyslexia are randomly assigned to one of two intervention types (meta-linguistic vs. working memory training) and trained in both Chinese and English. In addition, 60 children without reading impairment are tested and 24 children with dyslexia are included as a waiting control group. Following up these 144 children as part of the present application and testing 30 new children with dyslexia who did not receive intervention will allow a comprehensive long-term evaluation of the intervention methods by pursuing three Aims: In Aims 1 and 2, the long-term outcomes of the two intervention methods shall be tested at the behavioral and neural levels, respectively. In Aim 3, training outcome shall be predicted based on neural measurements taken before intervention. The study is expected to provide evidence whether meta-linguistic training is effective in the long-term to improve reading skills in Chinese children with dyslexia. The study is also expected to show whether improvements in reading skills are due to remediation of deficits at the neural level or due to compensatory activity. Finally, the study is expected to show whether neural measures are feasible to predict the outcome of dyslexia intervention before the start of training. The research is significant, because it can clarify whether success of meta-linguistic intervention extends from alphabetic languages to Chinese. It is also significant, because it will show how neural measures can complement behavioral measures for evaluation and prediction of training success. The study is therefore expected to have an impact on dyslexia treatment in Chinese due to its evidence-based approach and due to its potential for personalized treatment. 在字母語言的讀寫障礙干預研究的元分析(meta-analyses)表明，兒童受益於元語言(meta-linguistic)訓練，如語音處理(phonological processing)和字素音素轉換(grapheme-phoneme conversion)。因學習中文的傳統方法注重記憶，元語言訓練對於中國的讀寫障礙患者是否也有效，尚有待證明。此外，即使長期影響的存在與否具有重要的實際意義，評估研究通常側重於短期而非長期影響。最後，潛在機制的神經測量有可能補充干預評估，並可基於干預前的神經數據預測干預結果。本提案將跟進目前正在參與由其他來源資助的讀寫障礙訓練研究的兒童，而該研究含有干預前和干預後的測試。在該研究中，60名患有讀寫障礙的兒童被隨機分配到兩種干預類型之一（元語言或工作記憶(working memory)訓練），並接受中英文訓練。此外，60名沒有讀寫障礙的兒童也進行了測試，而另外24名患有讀寫障礙的兒童則被分入等待對照組。對這144名兒童進行跟進是本申請的一部分，而另一部分為30名沒有接受干預的新的讀寫障礙兒童將接受測試，這兩部分將透過三個目標對干預方法進行全面的長期評估：在目標一和目標二中，兩種干預方法的長期結果將分別在行為和神經方面被測試。在目標三中，干預前的神經測量會被用作預測訓練結果。我們預計此研究將提供證據，證明元語言訓練在長期是否能有效提高中國讀寫障礙兒童的閱讀能力。我們還預計此研究將顯示讀寫能力的提高是否歸因於神經方面缺陷的補救(remediation of deficits)或是因為補償性活動(compensatory activity)。最後，我們預計此研究將顯示神經測量在訓練開始前預測讀寫障礙干預的結果方面是否可行。這項研究具有重要意義，因為它可以澄清元語言干預的成功是否能從字母語言延伸到中文。此研究也很重要，因為它將顯示神經測量如何補充行為測量，以作評估和預測訓練成功的用途。由於循證方法(evidence-based approach)的使用以及將來被用作個性化治療(personalized treatment)的潛在可能，我們預計此研究將對中文的讀寫障礙治療產生影響。

14600919.label: Realisation of objectives
14600919.value: Given the difficult circumstances of the project (social unrest, pandemic; see mid-term report), the data collection is described in more detail. The difficult circumstances also contributed to a delay in publication. Summary of data collection: After initial delays due to the social unrest and school closure early in the pandemic, we started collecting behavioral data online, and could complete EEG recordings later, when schools were open again. Still, the large refusal rate (32-40% depending on the group) is likely due to the stressful situation of families during the pandemic. That means overall that we could only collect data from 85 of the 129 children. For this reason we collected data from new typically developing children and from a larger group of adults than originally planned (40 instead of 24), so that overall we collected EEG data from 130 participants (instead of 183, as planned initially). Taken together, although the number of tested participants is only 71% of the original targeted sample, the sample size is still considerable and allows us to address the aims of the project. Objective 1: Long-term intervention effects at behavioral level The project application was submitted, while the original intervention study was ongoing with the last 1/5 of the sample still being trained. The results of the intervention study were not known yet at that time. Although the intervention methods were previously shown to be effective in typically developing readers (Siu et al., 2018), the intervention methods did not significantly improve reading skills in the children with dyslexia (Wang et al., 2021). The reason is probably that children with dyslexia need more intensive intervention to overcome their learning difficulties. This also meant that the likelihood of finding long-term intervention effects in the current study was decreased to start with. Indeed, a longitudinal analysis including the follow-up data after 2.4 years after intervention indicated that, although the children with dyslexia increased in their literacy skills (p<0.001 for character recognition accuracy; p<0.01 for reading fluency), their reading was still poorer than the typically developing children despite the intervention that they had received (p<0.001 for character recognition accuracy; p<0.001 for reading fluency). Moreover, the type of intervention did not affect the reading gain between pre-test and follow up (main effect of time: p<0.001 for both reading tests, and interaction between time and intervention group not significant). That means, while the objective of evaluating the intervention effects was achieved, the evaluation itself came out with a negative result. Objective 2: Long-term intervention effects at neural level (EEG) While previous studies in alphabetic languages reported N1 tuning deficits in dyslexia (Maurer et al., 2007), we could not replicate this finding in Chinese despite a robust N1 print tuning effect. As with the behavioral results, the likelihood of finding significant longterm effects in the absence of short-term effects was reduced to start with. An analysis comparing the N1 component between children with and without dyslexia revealed a larger N1 for familiar Chinese than unfamiliar Korean characters (F(1,64)=23.6, p<0.001) that got smaller from pre-test to follow-up test (F(1,64)=5.6, p<0.05). In addition, the N1 component decreased in general, presumably reflecting maturation (F(1,64)=29.1, p<0.001). Similar to objective 1, the objective itself was achieved, but the outcome of the result was negative. Objective 3: Predicting individual intervention gain based on EEG After a first PhD student had started in 2018 on developing machine learning techniques for classifying dyslexia, the student unfortunately did not pass her qualifying exam in 2019. This led to a delay of the machine learning research in the lab and objective 3 of this grant. This line of research could only picked up in 2021, when a new student with interest and skills in this area joined the lab. In the 2.5 years, the student made good progress and has been developing machine learning analyses based on convolutional neural networks (CNN) to predict dyslexia status in the participating children. The manuscript is in an advanced stage of preparation and has been presented at a conference recently (Yang et al., in preparation; Yang et al., 2024). Importantly, while classification accuracy is higher than 90% in several measures using classical five-fold validation methods, classification remains significant with close to 70% accuracy with new independent data. After having established the feasibility of the machine learning approach, as demonstrated in the first analysis, she will calculate predictive analyses of intervention gain based on pretraining EEG in study 3 of her PhD thesis. Other work: Although pursuing the original aims was possible, it was made more difficult by the delay and restrictions posed on the project by the social unrest and the pandemic. And the likelihood of finding long-term effects was reduced by the absence of short-term effects at both the behavioral and neural levels. Still, despite the pandemic, we were able to collect a relatively large sample that allowed us to investigate other topics that are summarized in “Major findings and research outcome” below.

14600919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14600919.value: Resting state and task-based EEG was used to train a convolutional neural network (CNN) model to classify participants’ dyslexia status. Functional connectivity measures were calculated for different frequency bands. The training with five-fold validation resulted in models with maximally 97% accuracy of classification in the case of the RHO connectivity index in both eye-closed and eye-open data. The model of the eye-open data with the RHO index was able to classify 69.95% of the participants in an independent sample accurately demonstrating the feasibility of this model for general application (Yang et al., in preparation). Although significant, an accuracy of 70% suggests that the model should still be improved before clinical application is feasible. Brian Wong, an MPhil student who was writing his thesis as part of this project, added an EEG experiment to the study that investigated predictive processing in dyslexia by using an experiment to tease apart N1 adaptation from mismatch negativity effects. His analysis of the data from adults showed that the classical MMN is composed of two different types of adaptation effects, an N1 adaptation effect that occurs after the first stimulus repetition, and a continuous increase with repetition in the subsequent P2 component (Wong et al., under revision). He also presented the results of the children with a and without dyslexia at a conference, although the results suggest only subtle group differences in correlations between the late MMN and N250 adaptation, which requires further investigation (Wong et al., 2023). While contributing to project during his MPhil thesis, Brian Wong secured some additional funding from the Faculty of Social Science, to test the participants with dyslexia in the follow-up assessment regarding their view of their dyslexia using a metaphor elicitation technique. The results suggest that the method is valid, as the attitudes assessed with the technique correlated with behavioral measures of reading skills (Wong et al., 2023). Lucas Chan, the RA in the project who replaced Anita Lam in October 2021, conducted analyses on pen tablet experiments that we had continued in the follow-up study from the original intervention study in collaboration with Prof. Dillenbourg at EPFL in Switzerland. The analyses showed that children with dyslexia paused longer between characters, but not within characters compared to typically developing children, suggesting slowing down during the planning stage of writing rather than the writing execution itself (Chan et al., 2024).

14600919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14600919.value: The classification results suggest the feasibility to predict dyslexia based on EEG data. Classification accuracy with independent data, however, was not high enough for clinical application. One possibility to increase accuracy is to combine resting state and task-based EEG. Another possibility is to collect both temporally-and spatially sensitive data by combining EEG and fMRI. We have submitted an HMRF application with this purpose. Moreover, the lack of training effects in the previous intervention (previous HMRF) and the current follow-up studies – though disappointing – may indicate that the intensity of the intervention was not large enough to help children with learning disabilities with their literacy acquisition. The intervention method seems suitable, as training effects were found previously in typically developing children. Therefore, we are seeking funding for an intervention study that provides intervention for children with dyslexia with more intensity. Finally, the findings of the pen tablet study point to the feasibility of this method to study cognitive processes that are involved in writing and that might be impaired in children with dyslexia. We plan to combine writing tablet and EEG techniques in the future to look at neural processes that are involved in skilled and impaired writing in children.

14600919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14600919.value: Although 5-10% of children have severe difficulties learning to read and are considered to be dyslexic, few intervention programs have been evaluated in Chinese, and little is known whether training effects can be retained. We applied intervention programs in the current study that were previously shown to be effective in typically developing children. However, we could not find any significant intervention effect in children with dyslexia, neither in the short-term nor in the long-term, and neither at behavioral or neural levels. This suggests that the intensity of the intervention may need to be larger to improve reading in children with dyslexia. In addition, machine learning algorithms were developed based on EEG data in the current study that were able to accurately classify the children with up to 97% accuracy. Importantly, the model’s ability to identify dyslexia generalized to new children with up to 70% were classification accuracy. These results suggest that further improvements in classification accuracy will be necessary before clinical application becomes feasible. After establishing the basic feasibility of the algorithm, it will be used to predict individual training success based on EEG data as part of an ongoing PhD thesis.

14601819.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14601819.value: 西南攬勝：抗戰時期旅遊、山水畫與國家的想像

14601819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14601819.value: Using site-specific landscape paintings as material points of focus on southwest China during the Sino-Japanese War (1937–1945), this project explores correlations between scenic landscapes, travel, guohua國畫, nationalism and political propaganda in wartime China. Throughout the Nanjing decade (1927–1937), the Nationalist government promoted tourism and encouraged the public to visit scenic sites, particularly in the southeast, to boost the economy and enhance nationalism. Using a top-down model, the state embedded traditional landscape aesthetics and guohua in the official discourse of travel. These policies were disrupted in 1937 with the onset of the Sino-Japanese War, which had a devastating effect on travel and artistic activities, particularly in south-eastern coastal cities. Once the war began, the Nationalist government relocated people and resources on an unprecedented scale to the southwest, in effect turning this previously marginalised region into the political and cultural centre of China, and thus causing dynamic collisions between different art forms and between art and politics. Thanks to the rapid development of transportation infrastructure in the southwest, hitherto inaccessible scenic sites were developed by the government and began to be explored by cultural figures, including artists keen to document their wartime experiences in paintings. Whereas some of these artists depicted the devastating effects of the war in their work, turning ruins and refugees into artistic subjects, others embraced traditional landscape aesthetics in their idealised portrayals of natural scenes, in effect expressing nationalistic sentiments metaphorically. Drawing extensively on primary sources such as archival documents, diaries, paintings, photographs, guidebooks and newspaper articles, the project comprises of three parts: 1) tracing the discourse of wartime tourism, 2) reconstructing the discourse of guohua and the institutional organisation of the art world in the ‘rear areas’大後方and 3) contextualising site-specific paintings whose subjects were taken from southwestern landscapes. The project takes an interdisciplinary approach to unravelling the symbolic meanings attached to site-specific paintings and aims to shed light on the relationship between travel culture, art and the process of nation-building in wartime China. 本計劃以抗戰期間（1937-1945）西南風景為主題的實景山水為切入點，探討山水畫、旅遊、國畫、民族主義和政治宣傳之間的緊密關係。南京時期（1927-1937）國民政府推廣旅遊事業並鼓勵國民遊覽國內名勝，又將傳統山水美學注入旅遊的宣傳中，使國畫成為官方推廣旅遊的藝術門類。1937年中日戰爭爆發，為東南的旅遊和藝術發展帶來影響。國民政府退至西南，並將資源西遷，為一直在文化發展進程中處於外圍的西南帶來前所未有的生機。交通道路的建設為西南未開發的名勝帶來機遇，吸引了大量遊客，當中包括了隨著政府西遷的藝術家。藝術家以繪畫記錄他們在戰爭中的經驗，以理想山水表達他們對西南名勝和戰爭的印象。本計劃建基於大量的文獻，其中包括檔案、日記、繪畫、攝影、旅遊指南及報刊，期望能重構抗戰時期的旅遊論述；重組國畫論述以及藝術界的機制；以及分析以西南名勝為主題的山水畫，用跨學科的角度探索抗戰時期旅遊、藝術和國家建構的緊密關係。

14601919.label: Realisation of objectives
14601919.value: A total of 120 survivors of sarcoma were recruited from the long-term follow-up (LTFU) clinics of the Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology and the Department of Paediatrics of the Prince of Wales Hospital in Hong Kong. After excluding survivors with incomplete treatment records or ambiguous cancer diagnosis, data from 116 survivors were analyzed. Half of the survivors were male (51.7%), and their mean age at follow-up was 28.2 (standard deviation [SD] = 8.2) years. They were diagnosed with osteosarcoma (49.1%) or soft-tissue sarcoma (50.9%) at a mean age of 13.3 (SD=7.2) years. Most of the survivors were treated with surgery (94.8%) and chemotherapy (81.9%). One third (31.0%) received radiation. The research procedure included a prospective neurocognitive assessment and survey, and a retrospective review of the participants’ previous cancer treatment/clinical data from the Clinical Management System (CMS), an in-house electronic health record. In summary, all of the 3 research objectives have been met during the study period. Problems encountered and deviations from the original plan: 1. Change in neurocognitive tools (stated in progress report in March 2020) Our original intention is to use the NIH Toolbox to assess survivors’ neurocognitive outcomes. Certain tests within NIH Toolbox are not language dependent. Hence, we need permission from the developers to translate the instructions into Chinese. We have contacted NIH Toolbox (Washington DC, USA) to request for their permission. However, we faced problems with receiving timely responses from them (Our earlier correspondences with them in late 2018 took almost 4 months). The developers mentioned that there is another group in mainland China who is translating the instructions, therefore we are not allowed to embark on another set of Chinese instructions. Deviation: We changed the NIH Toolbox to a traditional battery of neurocognitive tests. - Attention: Conners’ Continuous Performance Test (CPT) - Executive function: Trail Making Test A and B - Visual-motor processing speed: Grooved Pegboard - Memory: Modified Taylor Complex Figure (MTCF) - Behavioral function: Achenbach System of Empirically Based Assessment (ASEBA) Adult Self-report Behavior Checklist List These tests have been previously used for research in the Chinese population, particularly in our previous cognitive research in survivors of childhood leukemia (GRF Ref: 24614818). We reckoned that it is reasonable to replace the NIH Toolbox with these tests. 2. Recruitment Recruitment was not badly affected by the COVID pandemic as survivors of cancer typically still return to the hospital for follow-up consultations. However, we do acknowledge that the recruitment rate is slower than expected. Despite the COVID situation, we still managed to recruit on average 1 survivor per week when we submitted the progress report in Dec 2020. We expanded recruitment to the clinics of the Department of Orthopaedics and Traumatology from December 2020 onwards. Our Co-investigator (Dr. Wong Kwok Chuen) facilitated the recruitment of survivors from his clinics. 3. Recalculated sample size We analyzed preliminary data from 74 survivors when we submitted the progress report in Dec 2020, and increased the targeted sample size to 120 (from 100) to ensure that the sample is sufficiently powered to address Objective 1. We completed recruitment of 120 survivors by Aug 2022. On hindsight, it was a wise decision to increase the sample size as it allowed us to conduct subgroup and interaction analyses to enrich the results for Objective 3.

14601919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14601919.value: Objective 1: (Pls refer to Publication 1) At an average of 14.9 years post-cancer diagnosis, a minority of the survivor population demonstrated impairment in attentiveness (4.3–13.0%), immediate recall (16.4%), visual memory (delayed recall) (19.0%), motor processing speed (34.5%) and cognitive flexibility (18.1%). Compared with published norms, the survivors reported significantly worse behavioral functioning in depressive problems (13.8%), anxiety problems (4.3%), somatic problems (6.0%), and avoidant personality problems (6.9%). Objective 2: 2.1 (Pls refer to Publication 1) Factors associated with neurocognitive outcomes: After adjusting for clinically relevant variables, we found that physical inactivity was associated with inattentiveness. Survivors who consumed alcohol had a worse performance on multiple measures of attention outcomes. Compared with survivors who reported working ≤ 9 h per day, survivors with longer working hours demonstrated more inattentiveness and lower cognitive flexibility. 2.2 (Pls refer to Publication 2) Factors associated with behavioral outcomes: Based on the published cutoffs for the Body Image Scale (BIS), the prevalence of body image dissatisfaction was 35.3%. After adjusting for cancer and treatment variables, we found that a higher BIS total score was associated with depressive problems, anxiety problems and avoidant personality problems. Objective 3 (Exploratory): (Pls refer to Publication 1) 3. There was significant interaction for chronic health conditions*physical activity for cognitive flexibility and attention. This suggests that survivors who developed chronic health conditions and reported low physical activity (<150 min of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity per week) demonstrated the worst cognitive flexibility and attention outcomes, than survivors in other subgroups. Summary: 1. At >10 years after cancer diagnosis, up to 35% of AYA survivors of sarcoma in Hong Kong demonstrated significant neurocognitive impairment and behavioral problems. 2. Our results show a novel finding on the interactions between physical inactivity and chronic health conditions and their effects on attention and executive function. 3. Negative perception of body image was associated with internalizing behavioral problems.

14601919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14601919.value: 1. While it may not be possible to fully eliminate the neurotoxic effects of cancer treatment, our results suggest that survivors may benefit from appropriate interventions to address modifiable risk factors. - We have obtained a grant from the Food and Health Bureau - Chinese Medicine Development Fund. Our collaborative project (Ref: 21B1-2/014A_R1) aims to promote the safe use of dietary recommendations and lifestyle modifications to address fatigue, stress, cognitive problems, and body image issues in AYAs with cancer. 2. Future work includes examining the profile patterns or distinct trajectory of functional outcomes. - We have obtained a HMRF grant (Ref: 09202846) to initiate an AYA cancer cohort in Hong Kong. This study has been completed. We have recruited 409 AYA patients with cancer. - We have obtained another GRF grant (Ref: 14604022) to investigate the trajectory of behavioral outcomes in AYA patients with cancer throughout the cancer care continuum. We aim to develop a prognostic framework and algorithm predicting functional outcomes using machine learning techniques.

14601919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14601919.value: Young survivors of bone tumors and soft-tissue sarcoma are at risk of cognitive impairment and behavioral problems due to the cancer experience and the development of cancer-/treatment-related chronic health conditions as they age. Up to 30% of the survivors of sarcoma demonstrated impairment in attention, processing speed and executive function (higher order thinking ability). Our study found that a compromised health status, coupled with the continued engagement in an unhealthy lifestyle during survivorship, may further exacerbate cognitive impairment among survivors. These unhealthy lifestyles include physical inactivity, smoking, and long working hours. In terms of behavioral outcomes, a minority (6 to 13%) reported significant depressive problems, anxiety, and avoidant personality problems. Female survivors and those who had received radical surgeries might have a negative body image perception, which is associated with symptoms of depressive and avoidance personality. Our findings support continual efforts to investigate intervention targets and leverage health behaviors as modifiable risk factors to prevent cognitive dysfunction and psychological distress in this population.

14602319.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14602319.value: 全球/地方對中國穆斯林起源敘事和廣州伊斯蘭遺產的看法

14602319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602319.value: 回族穆斯林的長期傳統將伊斯蘭教在中國的到來歸咎於由先知穆罕默德（570-632）的親戚Sa'dibnabīWaqqā（約595-ca.574）領導的使命。雖然這個故事的歷史性被質疑到令人懷疑的程度，但是 Sa'd ibn abī Waqqāṣ與廣州的兩個重要地點 - 懷聖清真寺和據說被埋葬的墳墓有關。廣州是唐朝（618-906）最初的穆斯林商業和移民中心之一，近幾十年來，回族國內移民以及國際穆斯林都開始營業。懷聖清真寺和 Waqqāṣ 墓已成為兩群穆斯林新人的焦點，成為廣州古代伊斯蘭傳統的象徵。這座墳墓特別吸引了來自世界各地的穆斯林，他們將其視為一個神聖的地方，並將那個人作為聖人埋葬在那裡。 Waqqāṣ 敘事的神話力量不僅在回族穆斯林中持續存在，他們將其作為身份的來源，而且還遠遠超越了中國，擴展到世界各地的穆斯林社區，他們將墳墓視為 mazār 或朝聖地。這些重疊的趨勢使廣州成為貿易和宗教旅遊中心，建立了中國，回族穆斯林人口和全球穆斯林民族之間的聯繫。擬議的項目將以清真寺和墳墓為參考點，追溯廣州伊斯蘭遺產和穆斯林生活的歷史和發展。具體而言，它將探討這些網站如何幫助回族穆斯林創造一種原始敘事，將他們束縛在伊斯蘭教起源於阿拉伯半島的神聖記憶中，從而有助於建立一個充滿合法性和宗教信仰的社區身份。該研究還將包括廣州伊斯蘭遺產在中國境內的外國穆斯林商人和其他旅居者中的作用，以及最近吸引國際宗教旅遊的作用。最後，該項目將研究伊斯蘭遺產的聲望如何為中國的穆斯林和中國政府當局帶來互惠互利，他們合作使廣州成為地帶，國家和地區融合的一帶一路。全球利益。

14602619.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14602619.value: 遠距離親密關係：以錄像研究方法研究中國打工父母與留守兒童的視頻聊天

14602619.label: Project Objectives
14602619.value: To conduct an innovative video-based study of video calls between migrant parents and their left-behind children, which will allow a move from accounts ‘about’ the importance of video calls to a study ‘of’ the interactional practices during those video calls. To contribute to studies of video-mediated communication, by investigating how seamless video-mediated parent-child interaction is not a purely two-party interaction, but requires an active caregiver to facilitate that communication (e.g., to be submitted to ‘Research on Language and Social Interaction’). To bring the perspective of conversation analysis to the field of migration and new media, which will allow to re-conceptualize intimacy from a psychological to an interactional phenomenon; in the same way that sociologists have explored ‘family practices’ (Morgan, 1996; Wajcman et al., 2008) we explore ‘practices of intimacy (at a distance)’ (e.g., for ‘New Media & Society’). To draw out the practical implications for both social services and technological design for supporting multi-local families. On the one hand, to collaborate with NGOs which support such families to make use of new technologies to facilitate family relationships (see attached letter of support from International Social Services, Hong Kong branch). On the other hand, to consider the consequences for design of mobile phones and video apps such as WeChat (see attached letter from Tencent Research Institute).
