14602619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14602619.value: Loving one’s children may necessitate going away. Across the world, parents leave their children with caregivers to seek out better paying jobs in distant cities and countries. In China this desire for economic security has led to the emergence of the phenomenon of ‘left-behind children’. It has been reported that 61 million children, roughly a third of all children in rural China, have parents who work far from home and who often only see their children once a year. But what happens to parent-child relationships when parents are not at home? How do devoted parents, who work far away to provide for their children’s future, try to build ‘intimacy at a distance’ with their children? This project explores the role of video calls on mobile phones in facilitating intimacy in multi-local families, in this case between Chinese rural-urban migrant parents and their young children. Previous interview-based research has shown the value that migrant parents see in video calls for forging relationships with their children, in particular, helping them to overcome the fear of their child not recognizing them upon their visits home. However, such studies do not explore what actually happens during those video calls, in particular, how participants employ various practices to ‘do’ intimacy. This project uses the innovative methodology of qualitative video analysis in pioneering research on how video technologies both facilitate and limit parent-child interaction. It aims to record and analyse 60 video calls in twenty families in China. It will focus on children under three years of age, since the advantages of video calls are frequently associated with very young children. In order to capture the parent-child interaction, we will combine recordings from an external camera in the room with a screen capture of the video chat on the mobile phone. This research will contribute to both interactional studies of video-mediated communication and the field of new media and migration. Our preliminary research suggests that seamless video-mediated parent-child interaction is not a pure two-party interaction, but requires an active caregiver to facilitate that communication (something that is missed by most existing research). It also highlights that it is important to re-conceptualize the very notion of intimacy from a psychological to an interactional phenomenon, where participants are actively involved in ‘practices of intimacy’. Finally, it points to practical implications for both social services and smartphone design to make use of new technologies to facilitate intimate family relationships. 對父母來說，疼愛孩子反而可能促使需要與孩子離別。在世界各地，父母將孩子留給其他看護者，以便在遙遠的城市和國家尋找薪水更高的工作。在中國，渴望經濟保障導致了出現「留守兒童」現象。據報導，中國有6100萬兒童（約佔中國農村兒童總數的三分之一）的父母遠離家鄉在異地工作。這些父母往往每年只見到他們的孩子一次。但是當父母不在家時，親子關係會發生什麼變化？這群獻身於孩子未來而努力在外工作的家長，如何努力與孩子建立「遠距離的親密關係」的？ 該項目探討移動手機中視頻通話功能如何促進異地家庭的親密關係，並以中國打工家長與在農村的子女作為個案。以往基於訪談的研究發現移民父母普遍認為能夠在視頻見到自己孩子本身非常重要，因為「見到」孩子能夠讓助他們克服孩子在回家時不認識他們的恐懼。然而，這類研究並沒有探究在視頻通話中實際了甚麼，特別是參與者如何採用各種方法來「營做」 親密關係。 該項目利用質性錄像分析所帶來創新方法論，開拓有關研究視頻技術如何促進和限制了親子互動的研究。它旨在記錄和分析20個中國家庭的60則視頻通話。計劃重點放在三歲以下的兒童，原因在於與幼童的視頻通話似乎更反映到視頻通話本身的優點。為了記錄親子互動，我們將在房間裏的外部攝錄機記錄房間情況，並結合手機錄頻軟件錄製研究對象的手機屏幕上的視頻。 這個項目將對新媒體與移民領域的互動研究均有貢獻。我們的初步研究表明，視頻通話中介下的親子互動不是純粹的雙方互動，而是需要同時存在熱心的看護者來促進這種溝通（大多數現有研究都忽略了這一點）。這個項目還強調，我們需要重新概念化「親密關係」，由以往心理現象轉變為互動現象，因為不同人等均積極參與「親密實作」之中。 最後，本項目致力於探討項目對於社會服務和智能手機設計的應用意義，以利用新技術促進親密的家庭關係。

14603019.label: Project Title(Chinese)
14603019.value: 體育鍛煉與空氣污染暴露的聯合效應： 縱向性隊列研究

14603019.label: Project Objectives
14603019.value: To investigate the joint mortality/morbidity effects of habitual PA and long-term exposure to ambient PM2.5 air pollution in a large longitudinal Chinese cohort.
rows: To investigate the joint mortality/morbidity effects of habitual PA and long-term exposure to ambient PM2.5 air pollution in a large longitudinal Chinese cohort.

14603019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603019.value: 目標： 應用大型縱向性隊列研究體育鍛煉與PM2.5空氣污染暴露的聯合效應 背景： 眾所周知，體育鍛煉可以促進健康，包括減低非傳染性疾病死亡和促進精神健康。但體育鍛煉會提高肺部對空氣污染物的吸入，潛在地加重空氣污染對人體健康危害。因此，體育鍛煉與空氣污染暴露的聯合效應成為一個重要而迫切的公共衛生問題。世界上大約92%的人群居住在空氣品質未達世衛標準的地方，人們無法回避空氣污染，急切需要政府制定相關指引，清楚告知人民關於體育鍛煉與空氣污染的關係。然而，這方面的資訊非常少，因為世界上普遍缺乏大型的醫學佇列和先進的空氣污染評估技術。 項目： 我們提出應用一個現存的大型醫學隊列來研究這個重要的公共衛生問題。這個大型佇列包括1996至2014年間的59萬名參與者合併136萬筆醫學檢查記錄。隊列也收集了其它相關資訊如生存狀態、體育鍛煉和各種混雜因素。我們應用衛星遙感技術評估每個參加者的 PM2.5暴露濃度。我們將分別用time-varying Cox model分析分類健康結局（如死亡和疾病等）和 generalised linear mixed model分析連續變數健康結局（如血壓、血糖和血脂等）。 意義： 體育鍛煉與空氣污染都是全球重要的公共衛生問題。獲得體育鍛煉與空氣污染聯合效應的相關知識將具有重大的政策指導作用。本研究項目將會提供實證，辨明在不同的空氣污染水準下體育鍛煉是否有益或損害健康。

14603019.label: Realisation of objectives
14603019.value: Background: The objective of this project was to investigate the combined mortality and morbidity effects of habitual physical activity (PA) and long-term exposure to ambient PM2.5 air pollution within a large longitudinal Chinese cohort. Achievement of Research Objective: The research team successfully met this objective through extensive data analyses utilizing a robust mega database. These analyses explored the concurrent impact of habitual PA and prolonged PM2.5 exposure on a variety of health outcomes. For dichotomous health outcomes, a time-varying Cox model was employed, whereas a generalized linear mixed model was utilized for continuous health outcomes. Publication of Findings: The team's comprehensive research culminated in ten publications in prestigious journals, focusing on outcomes such as total natural cause mortality, cardiovascular and cancer-related mortality, pneumonia, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, renal function and chronic kidney disease, C-reactive protein levels, and lung function. Recognition and Dissemination: Significantly, three of these publications were highlighted in news releases by the American Heart Association, Canadian Medical Association Journals, and Diabetologia. Additionally, the team presented four abstracts at international academic conferences. Key Findings: A pivotal discovery was that regular physical activity reduces the risk of numerous adverse health outcomes, a benefit that generally surpasses the risks associated with air pollution exposure. This finding underscores the importance of habitual exercise as a health improvement strategy, even in moderate polluted environments. Pioneering Research: This project represents a pioneering foray into systematically examining the risk-benefit relationship between outdoor exercise and air pollution exposure. As the largest and most extensive study of its kind, it offers reliable evidence for future policy formulation in physical exercise promotion and air pollution control. Impact and Media Attention: The findings garnered significant media attention, reported globally in various languages. This widespread coverage has heightened public awareness about the dual importance of promoting physical exercise and improving air quality for public health. Conclusion: In conclusion, the research team meticulously analyzed the interplay between physical activity and PM air pollution, affirming that the health benefits of regular exercise generally outweigh the risks of air pollution exposure. However, it's crucial to recognize that both physical inactivity and pollution detrimentally impact health. A balanced approach that encourages active lifestyles without compromising health due to pollution is essential. Adopting synergistic, upstream, system-level strategies to address these public health challenges can yield long-term benefits for both human health and the environment.

14603019.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603019.value: • Joint effects on hypertension: A high-PA and low PM2.5 exposure were associated with a lower risk of hypertension. The negative association between PA and hypertension remained stable in people exposed to various levels of PM2.5, and the positive association between PM2.5 and hypertension was not modified by PA. • Joint effects on lung function: We found significant negative interaction effects between long-term exposure to PM2.5 and habitual PA, suggesting that the increased intake of PM2.5 due to PA may attenuate the benefits of habitual PA on lung function. However, the PA benefits generally remained stable at different stratum of PM2.5 in the stratified analyses. • Joint effects on diabetes: Higher physical activity and lower PM2.5 exposure are associated with lower risk of type 2 diabetes. Habitual physical activity can reduce the risk of diabetes regardless of the levels of PM2.5 exposure. • Joint effects on death: Increased levels of exercise and reduced PM2.5 exposure are associated with a lower risk of death from natural causes. Habitual exercise can reduce risk regardless of the levels of PM2.5 exposure. • Joint effect on lipids: Increased levels of exercise and reduced levels of PM2.5 exposures were associated with a lower incidence of dyslipidemia. Although an increase in habitual exercise slightly increased the risk of dyslipidemia associated with PM2.5 exposure, the benefits of the increased habitual exercise outweighed the risks. • Joint effects on C-reactive protein: Increased levels of exercise and reduced exposure levels of PM2.5 are associated with a lower CRP level. Habitual exercise reduces CRP level regardless of the levels of chronic PM2.5 exposure. • Joint effects on kidney function and disease: Increased habitual exercise and reduced PM2.5 exposures are associated with lower risks of renal function decline and CKD development. Habitual exercise reduces risks of renal function decline and CKD development regardless of the levels of chronic PM2.5 exposure. • Joint effects on mortality due to cardiovascular disease: High level of habitual exercise combined with low exposure level of ambient particulate matter 2.5 is associated with the lowest risk of cardiovascular death. A higher level of habitual exercise is associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular death at all levels of particulate matter2.5 exposure. • Joint effect on pneumonia mortality: Lower risk of pneumonia mortality was associated with both higher exercise and lower PM2.5 air pollution levels. For adults exposed to different levels of PM2.5, exercise benefits remained. • Joint effects on cancer mortality: Increased levels of exercise and reduced exposure levels of PM2.5 are associated with a lower risk of death from cancer. Habitual exercise reduces the risk of death from cancer regardless of the levels of chronic PM2.5 exposure.

14603019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603019.value: Contextualizing Our Research: Our initial research was centered in Taiwan, characterized by its moderately polluted air. This raises an intriguing question: Are the health benefits of regular physical activity equally significant in regions with higher levels of air pollution? Expanding the Research Scope: To address this, our next step is to broaden the geographical scope of our study. We aim to create a large-scale cohort platform that encompasses diverse countries and regions, each experiencing varying degrees of air pollution. This expansion will enable a more comprehensive investigation of the health impacts of physical activity in different pollution scenarios. Future Research Focus: The focus will be on examining the joint effects of habitual physical activity and varying levels of air pollution on health outcomes. By comparing regions with differing air quality, we can gain deeper insights into how air pollution levels might modulate the health benefits of regular exercise. A Global Perspective: This extended research will not only provide valuable insights specific to each region but also contribute to a broader understanding of the global interplay between air pollution and physical activity. Intended Outcomes: Through this research, we anticipate uncovering vital information that could inform public health guidelines and policies, particularly in areas grappling with high pollution levels. This approach aligns with our commitment to enhancing global health strategies and environmental policies.

14603019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603019.value: The Dilemma: Exercise vs. Air Pollution In our quest for good health, we often turn to physical exercise, which is known for its numerous benefits. However, when we exercise, especially outdoors, we might breathe in more air pollutants. This raises a critical question: Does the harm from increased exposure to pollution during exercise outweigh its health benefits? This issue is especially pressing considering that most of the world's population lives in areas where air quality is below the World Health Organization's recommended standards. Our Research: Balancing the Scales Funded by the GRF, our project delved into this complex relationship between regular outdoor exercise and air pollution. We wanted to understand whether it's healthier to stay active outdoors despite the pollution, or if the risks of air pollution negate the benefits of exercise. What We Found: Exercise Triumphs Our research brings good news. We found that for most health measures, the advantages of regular physical activity generally exceed the risks posed by air pollution. This means that regular exercise is a beneficial health strategy, even for those living in areas with relatively high pollution levels. The Caveat: A Balanced Approach However, it's important to note that both lack of exercise and exposure to air pollution are harmful. Therefore, we should not ignore the risks of pollution in our pursuit of an active lifestyle. It's not about choosing one over the other; rather, it's about finding a balance. Our Recommendation: A Dual Approach We advocate addressing both these significant public health issues simultaneously. By developing strategies that promote physical activity and reduce air pollution at the same time, we can achieve lasting health benefits for people and the planet.

14603519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14603519.value: The mental wellbeing of teachers and students has attracted much attention from the public and media in Hong Kong recently. Although academic pressure, particularly in secondary schools, has been cited as a key contributor of poor wellbeing, there may be other ways in which teacher and student mental health are related. One possibility is that compromised wellbeing affects teachers’ ability to notice and care for students in need. Another possibility is teachers’ attitude. Could teachers’ negative attitude toward help seeking be associated with the reluctance to refer students in need for mental health support? In particular, reasons for referral studied thus far often focus on perceived problem severity and teachers’ self-efficacy, but rarely on teachers’ psychological health and personal attitudes about help seeking. Given the extensive interaction that frontline teachers have with students, a comprehensive understanding of factors that affect timely referral of students to mental health services is needed. This proposal has three parts. First, a new measure on attitude toward referring students for mental health support will be developed and evaluated on 150 secondary school teachers. Second, another 250 secondary school teachers will be recruited to validate this new measure and to complete other questionnaires. In particular, teacher factors, such as gender, teaching experience, and counselling training will be examined in relation to teachers’ attitude about help seeking. Teachers will also be asked to rate how likely they are going to refer students on standardized vignettes for mental health support. The likelihood of referral will be examined in relation to teachers’ wellbeing, self-efficacy, perceived problem severity, attitude about help seeking, and attitude about referral. Structural equation modelling will be used to test a novel theoretical framework on referral decision in education settings. Finally, to uncover unique contextual factors that influence teachers’ referral decisions in Hong Kong, 12 teachers will be invited to participate in a phone or in-person interview. For comparison, six who score high on the referral questions in Study 2 will be selected along with six who score low (match on demographics if possible) to discuss their decisions to refer or not to refer. Data will be analyzed using Consensual Qualitative Research (Hill, 2012). Results from these studies will help identify teacher and system factors so that professional development activities may be developed to improve teachers’ attitudes toward help seeking and referrals, with the goal of enhancing mental health for both teachers and students. 教師和學生的心理健康一直廣受關注。雖然學業壓力被認為是導致心理失衡的主因，但教師個人因素與學生的心理健康可能有着緊密的關係。 其中一種可能的關係是，教師的心理失衡會影響教師在留意和照顧有需要的學生的能力。另一種可能性是教師的態度; 教師若對自身求助持有負面態度，這會否阻礙他們轉介有需要心理健康服務的學生？ 到目前為止，研究教師轉介的原因大多集中在學生問題的嚴重程度和教師的自我效能上，但甚少關注教師的心理健康和個人對求助態度與轉介學生的影響。有見於前線教師與學生之間的頻繁互動，我們更需要全面了解有關影響教師及時轉介學生接受心理健康服務的因素。 此研究建議書有三部分。首先，為了探討影響香港教師轉介決定的獨特背景因素，我們將邀請教師參與電話訪問或面談，討論他們如何作出轉介與否的決定。討論內容將使用Consensual Qualitative Research（Hill，2012）作分析。 其次，從第一部分獲得的質性研究結果會被用來制定一個新量表去評估教師對轉介學生接受心理健康服務的態度。 最後，本研究將招募教師來驗證這新量表，並完成其他問卷調查，包括性別，教學經驗，輔導培訓和對個人求助的態度。除了制定新量表之外，本研究亦透過模擬學生情況的情境題，收集教師如何評估他們轉介學生接受心理健康服務的可能性。結構方程分析將用於測試教師心理健康、自我效能、學生問題嚴重程度、個人求助態度以及轉介態度之間的關係並以驗證新理論框架。 研究的結果將有助於掌握教師和環境制度因素，開發專業發展活動，以改善教師對求助和轉介的態度及增強教師和學生的心理健康。

14603519.label: Realisation of objectives
14603519.value: The five objectives were achieved in two studies, as described below. Objective 4 In Study 1, 12 secondary school teachers in Hong Kong were interviewed about their experiences referring students in need of support to mental health professionals (MHPs). This study addresses Objective 4 by revealing the context specific factors, such as student factors, parent/guardian factors, and MHP factors that influence teachers’ referral decisions. The findings were organized and presented as a comprehensive model of factors influencing teachers’ referral decisions in a paper published in one of the top journals in educational psychology. Objective 2 Based on the findings in Study 1 and the adaptation of items in related scales, we developed an initial pool of 47 items of the Thoughts About Referral Scale (TARS) as part of Study 2. These items were then evaluated by 22 in-service teachers and 12 pre-service teachers. Two items were eliminated because they either lacked clarity or overlapped with other items. A sample of 292 teachers from 24 secondary schools in Hong Kong were then recruited to complete the resultant 45-item TARS. Standard item reduction procedure using exploratory factor analysis led to the final 26-item, 4-factor TARS, which can be used to examine the relationship between teachers’ attitude toward referring students and its correlates. The development of TARS achieves Objective 2. Objectives 1 and 3 Besides completing the TARS, the 292 teachers completed measures of wellbeing and attitude toward seeking professional psychological help, and provided information about their teaching experience, experience providing support to students, and experience receiving counseling themselves. In addition, to determine teachers’ self-efficacy in handling student concerns and their inclination to refer students, eight vignettes depicting students with varying degree of mental illness were created. The development of vignettes is crucial in this project as it allows us to assess teachers’ self-efficacy and inclination to refer students based on the same set of student scenarios, rather than relying on their real-life school environment (such as the number of referrals made in the previous year), which can differ significantly across school settings. To evaluate the context validity of the vignettes, ten experienced teachers were recruited to provide comments on whether the vignettes reflect students’ presentations seen in Hong Kong classrooms. Furthermore, nine mental health professionals, including two educational psychologists, a clinical psychologist, a psychiatrist, a social worker, and four educational psychology trainees were recruited to evaluate whether the vignettes depict adolescents in need of referral and mental health support. Comments from teachers and mental health professionals were incorporated to produce the final version of the vignettes. Structural equation modeling was conducted on the scores on completed measures to look at factors that are associated with teachers’ attitude toward seeking professional psychological help (Objective 1) and the relationships between teachers’ attitude toward help-seeking, attitude toward referring students, and their tendency to refer students as depicted in standardized scenarios (Objective 3). Objective 5 Using the findings and materials from Study 1 and 2, we developed the booklet <<中學生精神健康與教師轉介研習小册子>> for teacher training. In this booklet, readers are introduced to the model of factors influencing teachers' referral decisions from Study 1. The eight vignettes from Study 2 are also included in the booklet to raise awareness of the common mental health issues that students face in Hong Kong schools. In addition, readers learn about the local mental health resources available, as well as possible ways to address students' and parents' concerns about referrals (examples derived from the qualitative interviews in Study 1). In terms of dissemination, we have conducted a public seminar (other impact #1) to discuss project findings and how to use the booklet for teacher training. The seminar was attended by 100 participants from the education sector, and each participant received two hard copies of the booklet and a soft copy sent via email. The booklet has also been introduced and distributed in classes and workshops designed for mental health professionals and trainees, such as educational psychologists, SENCO, and counsellors. (other impact #4)

14603519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14603519.value: Based on the interviews with teachers in Study 1, several factors were found to affect teachers’ decision to refer students to mental health professionals (MHPs). These include student factors (e.g., problem severity and persistence, willingness to be referred, familiarity with professional support), parent/guardian factors (e.g., beliefs about the usefulness of referral, trust and collaboration with teachers), MHP factors (e.g., perceived effectiveness, frequency in meeting students, quality of interaction with teachers), and teacher factors (e.g., self-efficacy in handling student issue). Although these factors have been investigated previously in separate studies, our work offers a comprehensive framework to understand the interconnection among different factors. The findings from this qualitative study had been published in one of the top journals in educational psychology, Journal of School Psychology (SSCI Q1; 5-year IF: 6.4; see publication #1). They were also presented in a panel in Denver, Colorado, USA, in June 2022 (conference #1). Using the qualitative findings from Chui et al. (2023) and adaptation of items from related measures, we developed the Thoughts About Referral Scale (TARS) in Study 2. This scale contains 26 items and assesses teachers’ attitude toward referring students for professional psychological help. Using exploratory factor analysis, the TARS was found to have four dimensions: Projected Stigma of Help-Seeking (PS), Valuing Independent Problem-Solving (VI), Dedicated Action to Facilitate Referral (DA), and Perceived Helpfulness of MHPs (PH). When the TARS was administered along with other teacher self-report measures, it was found that teachers who reported higher self-stigma of seeking help also reported higher PS and VI, but lower DA and PH. In addition, DA fully mediated the relationship between teachers’ help-seeking stigma and referral of students, suggesting that those with favorable attitude toward seeking help themselves are more likely to dedicate efforts to facilitate student referrals, which predicts a higher tendency to refer students. Moreover, compared to teachers who had not sought counselling, those who had been to counselling perceived greater helpfulness among MHPs, have lower self-stigma toward help-seeking, valued independent problem-solving to a lesser extent, and are more likely to refer students. The development of the TARS in Study 2 has thus offered a valuable tool that can be used to investigate the correlates of teachers’ attitude toward referring students. Study 2 had been presented in Dublin, Ireland, in June 2023 (conference #2), and the manuscript is currently under preparation.

14603519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14603519.value: The results from Study 1 highlighted that the quality of interactions between teachers and MHPs may affect teachers’ decisions to refer students for help. It is therefore important that the discussion around referral does not only involve teachers but also MHPs. When MHPs are more intentional about working collaboratively with teachers, teachers will become more familiar and confident with MHPs and refer more students. To this end, we have disseminated project findings to MHPs by publishing in an international journal read by psychotherapists (other impact #2) and giving a keynote on this topic at a professional meeting for counseling psychologists in Taiwan (other impact # 3). We also have plans to extend outreach to other stakeholders at school (e.g., special education needs coordinators). Based on the findings of Study 2, we proposed in the GRF 2024/25 exercise to use an experimental design to investigate the effect of incorporating personal counseling in teacher continuing education on teachers’ self-stigma toward help-seeking, thoughts about referring students for professional psychological help, intention to refer and actual referrals made, and self-efficacy in managing student problems. The GRF proposal (Ref No. 14602424) is under review at the time of the submission of this report.

14603519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14603519.value: Mental health challenges often emerge during adolescence. Frequent interaction between secondary school teachers and their students enables teachers to notice students’ difficulties and refer students to MHPs to receive support. In Hong Kong, where academic pressure is high and teachers have significant involvement in guidance and counselling, teachers’ ability make timely referrals is crucial. This project aimed to identify factors affecting teachers’ referral decisions to facilitate the development of targeted training to improve student referrals and enhance mental health outcomes. Based on Study 1’s findings, we developed a model of factors influencing teachers’ referral decisions. One such factor is the quality of interaction with MHPs. This motivated us to expand outreach beyond schools to MHPs and emphasize the importance of collaboration with teachers. In Study 2, we developed a measure to assess teachers’ attitude towards referrals. Results showed that teachers with prior counseling experience had lower stigma toward seeking help, took more proactive actions when facilitating referrals, and were more inclined to refer students. This demonstrates the need to complement knowledge and skill training of teachers with experiential learning and attitude change. New approaches to teacher training are thus proposed for further investigation.

14604219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14604219.value: Anglo-American translators played a crucial role in intercultural communication between China and the West in the nineteenth century. This tumultuous period saw the creation and solidification of enduring stereotypes of both the Chinese to Westerners and Westerners to Chinese that are still with us; understanding who these translators were will help us better to understand where we are today in Chinese-Western interactions. Several scholars, including myself, have already conducted in-depth research on key texts and individual translators, for example Sir George Staunton and Sir John Francis Davis. Although a few scholars have also attempted a more syncretic overview of translation activity in this period, no one has yet attempted to link details of the translators’ background and personal lives with their translation practice on a large scale. We thus lack a sense of the broader picture of why these translators chose certain texts and particular translation strategies during this crucial period in Chinese-Western interaction, which the Chinese still look back upon as the “century of humiliation.” This study will employ methods based on firmly established sociological analyses (Bourdieu, Latour, and Collins) and data-driven, computational social network methods to collect detailed biographical information that will then be encoded in a database. Using these to build a detailed social network map will allow us to identify hitherto unnoticed correlations between various factors including birthplace, social background, religious beliefs, profession, and societies; it will also allow us to link those trends to their choice of what to translate, how to translate it (translation strategies), and where to publish. The study will be original in two ways. First, it will yield new insights into the behavior of this crucial group of intercultural communicators, and establish links between broader historical and social trends with particular translation choices. Second, it will introduce new Digital Humanities methods into translation studies, which in the area of digital methods to date has mainly focused on parallel and comparable corpus-based studies. In particular, synchronic and diachronic data visualization techniques and GIS mapping will be among those techniques which it will pioneer for translation studies. Finally, the database thus created can be used for future studies to answer other research questions, and will be made publicly available. Since it is modular, it can also be expanded to include other time periods and/or other language combinations in collaboration with an international team of scholars. 英美翻譯家於十九世紀中西跨文化溝通上扮演著重要角色。在這段動盪時期，中國人與西方人開始產生並加深對彼此的刻板印象，至今這些印象依然植於人心。因此，理解十九世紀的英美翻譯家將有助於我們理解中西交流互動的現況。 本人及另幾位學者已對若干重要文本及士丹頓爵士 (Sir George Staunton) 、戴維斯爵士 (Sir John Francis Davis)及其他翻譯家進行了深入研究。目前有些學者已嘗試為當時的翻譯活動提出更統合的概述，然而迄今尚未有學者嘗試把當時的翻譯家背景﹑個人生活及其翻譯實踐的具體細節進行大規模的連結。十九世紀實乃中西交流互動的關鍵時期，今日不少華人仍視之為「百年國恥」，但在研究上，我們仍欠缺更宏觀的視野來瞭解當時這些翻譯家為何選擇特定的翻譯文本，而其特定的翻譯策略為何。 本研究將採用布迪厄 (Pierre Bourdieu)﹑拉圖爾 (Bruno Latour)和柯林斯 (Randall Collins)等理論家所確立的社會學分析方法，以及數據驅動與計算社交網絡的方法收集翻譯家的詳細生平資料，並將其編入數據庫，據此建立一個詳盡的社交網絡地圖。透過這張新建的資料圖，我們將能在諸多不同因素間取得目前尚未建立的關聯性，包括翻譯家的出生地﹑社會背景﹑宗教信仰﹑專業及所屬社群。這張資料圖亦能使我們將上述趨勢連結到翻譯家對文本的選擇﹑翻譯方式 (翻譯策略)﹑由何處出版等其他重要的訊息面。 本研究將有兩項創新。首先，這項研究會為這群跨文化溝通者的行為提出新的創見，亦能夠在特定翻譯選擇與更廣袤的歷史與社會趨勢間建立新的連結。其次，目前數位方法領域中的翻譯研究主要仍聚焦於平行語料庫和可比語料庫的研究模式，本研究將新的數位人文研究方法引入翻譯研究中，特別是在運用共時和歷時的數據視像化技術及地理資訊系統數據映射 (Geographic Information System [GIS] mapping) 技術方面，本研究將為翻譯研究方法開創先例。 最後，研究依據上述方法所建的數據庫能供未來的研究使用，以解答其他的研究問題，此數據庫亦會開放予大眾使用。這是一個模塊化數據庫，因而將來可以透過與其他國際學者團隊合作，納入其他時間階段及/或其他語言組合而擴建此數據庫。

14604219.label: Realisation of objectives
14604219.value: Objective 1: To my knowledge, this is the first major historical study to employ the digital humanities tool of network analysis to a large body of translators. The project has shown that this method is effective, if time-consuming. I will showcase the results in two conference presentations this coming December, one emphasizing methodology, the other emphasizing a case study derived from the project revolving around the figure of Robert Morrison (1782–1834), who had an extensive social network that he drew upon to accomplish a variety of intercultural knowledge transfers, including translation, dictionary compilation, and the establishment of educational institutes. Objective 2: With the assistance of my research assistant and an IT specialist, I have been able to create two types of mappings of Chinese-English translators in the nineteenth century. First, on our website we have an historical map that displays the location of the various translators throughout their lives; with this tool, we can see which translators were working where (Hong Kong, Macau, Singapore, Penang, Shanghai, London, et cetera) and when. This allows us to analyze translation ‘hot spots’ and to verify Mary Louise Pratt’s work on contact zones. In other words, Pratt assumes in her work that places where people from different parts of the world mingle are also the places where cultural information is exchanged on a large scale; her belief was that these are usually either the capital of an empire (London, Paris) or major cities in colonies or semi-colonized areas. My network analysis documents this in detail, providing information about where exactly translators lived while they worked on translations, the location of major publishing houses (or private printing presses), and periods of higher activity. Interestingly, the network shows two hotspots that are not identified by Pratt: Oxford and Cambridge. As major seats of learning but not metropolises, these two locations did in fact serve as loci for translation activity between Chinese and English in the nineteenth century, partly because some missionaries and foreign service personnel ‘retired’ from their first career to take up a career in education, and partly because these sites of learning attracted students from colonial and semi-colonial areas. Second, we created a translators’ social network visualization tool, with information about the social connections of over fifty translators. This includes the names of all individuals we could identify who were in some way related to the translators. These ties are separated into 50 categories, including kinship ties (including various in-law relations), professional ties, educational, and personal. The relationship visualization tool allows data to be sorted and displayed in various ways, including all ties for a single translator, all direct ties between translators (first degree; Translator A knows Translator B), and all second degree ties (Translator A knows person X [not a translator], person X knows Translator B). This tool allowed me to identify central and peripheral translators at a glance, while the data behind it allows for statistical analysis relating to things such as averages and network density. Objective 3. This objective turned out to be a bit trickier than I expected. To date I have been able to identify certain broad connections between biographical information and translation practice, but these trends were largely anticipated. For example, translators who were linked with religious organizations translated large amounts of religious material, while translators associated with commercial ventures or government affairs translated material relating to politics, current affairs, and the legal system. This is really no surprise, although it is nice to be able to document it. However, what was perhaps more surprising was the amount of material that translators in all categories translated that was not obviously related to their biographical information. In other words, translation decisions were often not motivated by personal predilection. Traditionally in translation studies, there has been a tendency to view translators as free agents, but my data shows the extent to which even these people who overwhelmingly translated ‘on the side’ (i.e., few of the translators in the nineteenth century identified themselves as professional translators) seem to have made decisions based on happenstance. I must confess that I have not yet finished analyzing this aspect of the data, but I can see the broad outlines of a paper on translation choices in relation to social networks. Objective 4. The project has enabled me to document thoroughly the role of Anglo-American translators in Chinese-English intercultural communication in the nineteenth century. Concentrating as I have been on translations into English, the data clearly shows that, while Chinese actors played an important role in the translation process, virtually all C-E translation projects in this century were initiated by Anglo-American actors. The first translation of a novel by a Chinese translator, for example, was given the task by an English translator James Legge, who saw it as a way of his convert gaining experience in English. The first independent translation by a Chinese translator was in the 1890s, by Ku Hung-ming. My paper on Robert Morrison, to be presented in December 2023, will highlight his role in intercultural communication in the nineteenth century between on the one hand British and Americans and on the other the Chinese. Objective 5. Based on the geographical mapping and the network visualization tools, I have been able to identify various trends in intercultural translation in the nineteenth century between Chinese and English. One of the two papers to be presented in December 2024 concerns an unusual case, Robert Morrison, whose extensive network of religious and professional ties enabled him to carry out extensive intercultural transfers, including several translation projects, the first substantial Chinese-English dictionary, and the founding of the Anglo-Chinese College in Malacca, where several generations of translators, traders, and Chinese converts studied together (this institution was ultimately moved to Hong Kong). Morrison was able to draw upon his vast network of colleagues, friends, and religious figures to carry out extensive fund-raising campaigns in order to finance these endeavours. For example, his close contacts and friendship with many of the men working in the East India Company in Macau and Guangzhou enabled him to persuade the directors of that Company to underwrite his Chinese-English dictionary project, a massive undertaking that included the acquisition of a Chinese character set of types, the hiring of various assistants, and the cost of printing. He was also able to raise substantial funds from individual members of the East India Company for the establishment of the Anglo-Chinese College, and in a tour of the United Kingdom on a visit back home, he raised funds through a speaking tour at local churches in England, Ireland, and Scotland for missionary work in China.

14604219.label: Major findings and research outcome
14604219.value: This project demonstrates the usefulness of network theory in historical studies of translators. Through careful documentation of the total social network of fifty-three individual translators to date, we can see larger patterns, such as the high density of the network, which clearly demonstrates the degree to which Chinese-English translators in the nineteenth-century were interconnected, both directly and indirectly (through a shared common contact). Indeed, many of the translators shared multiple connections with each other, often through both professional and kinship networks, suggesting that professional ties often led to kinship ties through marriage. While there are some outliers with relatively little connection or mostly negative connections, this density of the network speaks to the relatively small size and homogeneity of the translators. Although we do find particularly dense clustering within two large groups – missionaries and civil servants – ties also cut across these and other groups, showing a tight-knit community of sinological experts in this period. The network is also useful in examining the life and work of individual translators as well. A case study of Robert Morrison uncovered the role of social and economic power in nineteenth century translation practice. Having input information about Morrison’s social network gleaned from various online and print resources, an extensive social network emerges (over 500 people), revealing that Morrison actively sought and maintained contact with hundreds of individuals from various social strata. These individuals ranged from highly-placed figures such as Sir George Staunton to itinerant preachers in Tahiti, and was maintained both through direct contact and a vast and voluminous correspondence. This extensive network is one of the key factors in Morrison’s success as a translator and cross-cultural communicator, opening up doors for him in terms of job opportunities; it also enabled him to be one of the most successful fundraisers among the early missionary translators. He was able to solicit funds from the East India Company, members of the aristocracy and the professional classes, and from church-goers throughout England, Scotland and Ireland. These funds provided the necessary foundation for his dictionary project, his translation activities, and the Anglo-Chinese College. The network analysis highlights these aspects of his career. Two conference presentations in December 2023 are currently being written up, one on methodological obstacles and general trends of the data, and one on the case study of Robert Morrison. These will be further refined for subsequent publication as journal articles in 2024.

14604219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14604219.value: There are several possible avenues for further development. First, the database can be expanded forward in time to include early twentieth century translators, which would allow for more longitudinal and comparative studies of translator networks in the lead-up to the collapse of the Qing Dynasty and the early Republican Era. Second, there is still quite a bit of information in the database that could be analyzed. Third, the website interface could be improved to allow for more different ways of sorting and displaying information; the present configuration is based on the needs of the project to date. Third, there are at least two topics that are tangential to the original project which have been explored in my website blog but should be expanded and submitted as journal articles: one on the life of translators at sea (most translators in this period spent years living on ships voyaging back and forth between Britain or America and China), and one on the development of different typographical layouts for bilingual editions of works.

14605119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14605119.value: 本研究旨在建構神經預測模型來預測學習粵語的聽力受損的兒童在耳蝸植入後的語言發展。同時也基於本研究團隊正在進行的另一個關於學習英語的耳蝸植入兒童的研究，本研究可用以評估這個神經預測模型是否僅適用於特定語言還是多種不同的語言。人工耳蝸植入已是重度至嚴重聽力受損的治療標準，整體而言能顯著提升聽力受損兒童的語言發展。然而，就這些個體兒童而言，術後的語言發展水平仍然存在相當大的差異，令手術前諮詢評估和制定手術後的語言治療變得更為複雜。因此我們需要更好的預後指標，以便制定更有效的術後復康方案。通過神經影像和機器學習技術，我們將會為香港的學習粵語的人工耳蝸植入兒童構建語言發展的神經預測模型。我們會收集所有接受研究的對象手術前詳細的神經解剖磁力共振影像和基線聽力水平，同時會追踪記錄人工耳蝸啟動後的12和24個月的語言發展水平。通過支持向量機和回歸算法，我們將以這些數據來構建預測模型。這些模型會被用於評估聽覺剝奪後神經重組的競爭性神經再生和神經保留假設。此外，用學習粵語的數據構建的模型將會更廣泛地用於測試耳蝸植入後語言發展的神經預測模型的語言特定性。由於我們在另一個相關項目中，正在構建類似的適用於學習英語的耳蝸植入兒童的預測模型，我們可以用學習粵語兒童的數據去驗證這些模型，反之亦然。這種跨語言驗證的方式使我們能夠檢驗前文提到的語言特定和語言普遍的假設。我們的研究結果將會對聽障兒童的護理具有很重要的理論和實踐意義，這個預測模型可以提高香港和其他地方耳蝸植入的現行護理標準。手術前更精確的預測結果能夠幫助照顧者和臨床醫生更加謹慎和有效地制定術後語言治療方案，以便優化耳蝸植入的潛能和每個兒童的語言學習能力。這個項目的結果首先能使在香港學習粵語的兒童受益，其後更可以推廣到全世界3200萬學習任何語言的聽障兒童。

14605119.label: Realisation of objectives
14605119.value: Objective 1 aims to examine whether pre-surgical neural measures can predict post-surgical spoken language outcome in children diagnosed with hearing loss who would eventually receive a cochlear implant (CI). We conducted two studies in conjunction with this objective. First, we investigated the extent to which hearing loss would lead to changes in neuroanatomy and whether hearing aid (HA) as an interim intervention measure (while the child is waiting for CI surgery) would assist with preventing further changes in the brain. Twenty-one children with bilateral congenital sensorineural hearing loss who were candidates for CI were recruited. As standard practice, these children were provided with hearing aids before CI surgery. Neuroanatomical MRI were available from all of these children. Voxel-based morphometry analysis was conducted to assess the gray matter (GM) volume in the auditory cortex. Children’s residual hearing was measured by pure-tone audiometry at different frequencies. Multiple linear regression models were conducted to examine the effects of residual hearing and the use of HAs on GM volume in the auditory cortex with the control of age and gender. We found that children with more residual hearing at high frequencies had larger GM volume ratio (corrected by total intracranial volume) in the left Heschl’s gyrus. An interaction effect between residual hearing and the use of HAs suggested that the effect of residual hearing on GM ratio was moderated by the use of HA. Specifically, compared with children with less residual hearing, children who had more residual hearing benefited more from longer use of HAs in terms of a larger GM ratio. These findings highlight the impact of residual hearing on the neuroanatomy of the auditory cortex in children with hearing loss. Moreover, our results call for more auditory input via HAs for children with more residual hearing to preserve the auditory cortex before cochlear implantation. For children with less residual hearing who might receive limited benefit from HAs, an early cochlear implant would be necessary. This study was published in the American Journal of Audiology (Yuan et al., 2023). While the first study establishes that the impact of hearing loss on neuroanatomy is associated with auditory input supported by HAs, the second study follows these patients to investigate whether the patient’s neuroanatomical characteristics would predict spoken language outcome. MRI and outcome data were available from 17 patients. Voxel-based morphometry was applied to examine the children’s whole-brain structure. Machine learning was conducted using neuroanatomical features to predict children’s post-CI outcome up to 24 months after CI. The whole-brain neural model was compared with a non-neural model (with factors such as age of CI activation, residual hearing and gender), an auditory cortex neural model and a visual cortex neural model. Model performance was quantified using the mean squared error (MSE) between predicted values and observations. We found that the preoperative neuroanatomical features outperformed the non-neural features in predicting auditory skills in children with CIs. Specifically, the auditory-related area played a more important role in predicting post-CI outcomes. Similar to our previous study that examined English-learning CI candidates (Feng et al., 2018), the present study also found that spoken language outcome could be predicted by pre-CI MRI data in Chinese-learning children. This study is under review (Yuan et al., under review, see full submission attached). Objective 2 aims to examine whether neural predictive models constructed for one language can be generalized to data obtained from children who are learning another language. To address this aim, additional data were obtained from English-learning children from Lurie Children’s Hospital in Chicago using a grant supported by the National Institutes of Health in the US (no RGC funds were used to support the project in the US, and no NIH funds were used to support the project in Hong Kong). We constructed neural predictive models using data from 143 English-learning children. Because of the relatively large sample size, we were able divide data from Lurie into training and testing sets (the testing set was not used in training). The AUC of the model exceeds .80 for English-learning children. We then test the same model using data from Chinese-learning children collected in Hong Kong as discussed above (Yuen et al., under review). The performance of the model dropped to close to chance level. These results seem to suggest that neural predictive models for CI outcome must be constructed with language-specific data. However, our results could also be explained by the fact that different scanners were used for the patients at Lurie and in Hong Kong. At Lurie, we were also able to obtain data from 37 Spanish-learning children who were scanned using the same scanner as the English-learning patients. We tested the English model with these data from Spanish-learning children; poor model performance was also found. Thus, it seems to be the case that no matter whether the data are collected from the same site or from similar languages (Spanish and English are arguably closer than Chinese and English), as long as the languages in question are different, model generalizability would be poor. The ability for neural predictive model for CI outcomes to generalize could be quite narrow. These findings are clinically significant because they speak to the limitation of this approach in predict outcome. However, because the sample sizes are small in general, the results may only speak to the need for multi-site and multi-language studies with much larger sample sizes. We reported these findings in another study that is currently under review (Wang et al., under review, see full submission attached). COVID-19 has significantly disrupted our project. In our approved revised research plan, we have set an enrollment target of 25 patients. In actuality, we were only able to enroll 21, 17 of whom with follow-up data to address Objective 2. For a long period of time, virtually no patients were enrolled. Even for those who have enrolled, it was not possible to conduct follow-up assessments. Many families were unwilling to participate in research or unwilling to attend any follow-up appointments because their lives were completely disrupted by the pandemic. They did not wish to receive our phone calls or attend any online assessments even if they were possible or available. Nevertheless, were able to complete the project and address the two objectives of the proposal. Our output dissemination plan targets two conference presentations and one journal publication. In actuality, we made 3 conference presentations and have published one journal paper so far. We have two additional journal publications under review.

14605119.label: Major findings and research outcome
14605119.value: Objective 1. We investigated the extent to which auditory input may affect brain structures of Chinese-learning children with hearing loss who were waiting to undergo cochlear implant (CI) surgery. We also examined whether these children’s spoken language outcomes can be predicted by their pre-CI neuroanatomical features. In Yuan et al. (2023), we found that not only the extent of hearing loss could impact the auditory region of the brain, the use of hearing aid as an interim intervention (before CI surgery) could help preserve some of these brain structures that may otherwise be affected by the reduced auditory input resulting from hearing loss. In Yuan et al. (under review), we then examined whether pre-CI neuroanatomical features could predict post-CI spoken language outcomes. Several predictive models were constructed using machine learning, with neural and non-neural (e.g., age of implant, residual hearing, age) features as predictors. Neural predictive models outperformed models without neural features. The results suggest that using pre-CI MRI scans and machine learning could predict the child’s post-CI outcomes. However, it is not whether predictive models are only accurate if they are constructed with data collected from the same site or the same language. Objective 2. Our studies conducted in this project (Yuan et al., 2023; Yuan et al., under review) as well as before this project (Feng et al., 2018) indicated that post-CI outcomes can be predicted by using pre-CI MRI scans and machine learning analytics. However, these studies considered children from one site who were learning one language (English or Chinese). How useful are models constructed with data only from one site when it comes to informing the outcomes of children implanted in another site? To answer this question, we constructed a neural predictive model using data collected from English-learning children and tested this model with data collected from Chinese-learning children (as explained in Objective 1). For our limited sample sizes, we did not find the English-learning model to be able to generalize to the data collected from Chinese-learning children in Hong Kong (Wang et al., under review). As far as the current clinical practice is concerned, it is not possible to rely on predictive models with data from other sites to forecast outcomes of children from out site. In addition to research outputs, the current project contributed to training PhD student Di Yuan.

14605119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14605119.value: The findings associated with Objective 1 are very encouraging. Detailed MRI brain scans obtained before CI surgery are in fact useful for predicting post-CI outcomes in Chinese-learning children in Hong Kong. The findings call for clinicians to adopt our MRI protocol as part of their routine pre-CI planning more widely, in Hong Kong and elsewhere. Findings associated with Objective 2 speak to the need for further research. Although the findings may suggest that neural predictive models are only valid if they are constructed with patient data from the same site who are learning the same language, with a much larger dataset encompassing more sites and language groups, it might be the case that one model would be sufficient for making prediction of any children who are about to undergo CI surgery anywhere. Data outside of the English-speaking regions including those from China would certainly be needed for this considerable effort.

14605119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14605119.value: Cochlear Implantation (CI) has become the standard of care for severe-to-profound hearing loss for children who are learning different spoken languages. Although spoken language has significantly improved for these children as group, the benefit from CI that each child receives remains variable, which complicates planning for post-CI intervention. In this project, we found that MRI brain scans obtained before CI surgery, along with machine learning methods, can be used to construct predictive models to forecast a Chinese-learning child’s post-CI outcomes. These predictive models outperformed models that rely only on non-neural measures such as age of implantation. Similar encouraging results were obtained in a study separate from this project that examined English-learning children. With data from English-learning children, we were then able to address the question of whether CI predictive models must be language- and site-specific. We tested English neural predictive models with the Chinese data collected in this project. With the relatively small sample sizes of these studies, it did not seem to be the case that cross-language generalization could be achieved. Currently, neural predictive models for CI outcomes must be constructed using data from the same language and same site in order to be useful.

14606319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606319.value: This project studies the impacts of the Umbrella Movement on the participants and the social movement in Hong Kong. It assesses the impacts of the Umbrella Movement on the values, worldviews, goals and participation practices of its participants. It also explores how post-Umbrella social movements and political participation is changed because of changed values of the participants, and as responses to a changed and unfavourable political environment. Through interviewing participants of the Umbrella Movement who now take up different positions in the movement community, this study hopes to uncover the factors that affect their post-movement participation. It includes what factors determine if they would continue to participate in social and political movements, and the forms of participation they chose. It also ascertains the changes to the social movement practices, including the formation of new networks, new identities, and new social capital. It will see how the post-Umbrella movements adapt their practices to the changing political environment after the movement. The interviews will focus on three levels: (1) the electoral level: post-Umbrella groups or candidates that ran or would run in Legislative Council and District Council elections; (2) community-level and civil society organizations that undertake movement action at the grassroots level; (3) cultural and artistic groups and individuals that use artistic creations, documentary-making and other presentations as forms of resistance. We will also include a group of interviewees who took part in the Umbrella Movement, but now has no regular movement participation, as a control group for the study. The study hopes to assess the biographical and cultural impacts of the Umbrella Movement, largely through transformation of the movement participants. This will have significant implications for the theory of social movement outcomes, and also in understanding the future development of social and political development in Hong Kong. 本研究審視雨傘運動對參與者及香港社會運動的影響，包括對參與者的價值觀、世界觀、目標和參與模式的改變，以至這些價值和行為改變，如何因應轉變的政治環境，而重塑了香港雨傘後社會運動的軌跡。 本研究透過訪問雨傘運動的參與者，發掘影響其是否繼續參與各種運動之因素，以及如何構建新的身份、網絡和社會資本。焦點會集中在三個層面：選舉層面、社區層面和文化藝術層面，亦會訪問傘後不再參與社運的人的改變以作比較。

14606319.label: Realisation of objectives
14606319.value: When the GRF research proposal was first written and submitted in September 2018, the assumption was that the social and political movements of Hong Kong was in a stage of abeyance after the Umbrella Movement (the project title and reviewed literature refers). By the time the project started in October 2019, Hong Kong was embroiled in an unprecedentedly highly mobilized movement, the Anti-Extradition Bill Movement (Anti-ELAB Movement). Some of the research questions asked became not directly relevant. I have amended some of the research procedures and contents, with the focus on how the Umbrella Movement (UM) had impacted the Anti-Extradition Movement. Through interviews with activists, electoral politicians, and activists with arts or culture background, and other documentary research, the study assessed how the Umbrella Movement (UM) had affected the trajectory of participation of these people, and how the UM affected their values and views, choice of movement repertoires, and adaptations to the new political and movement environments (namely the Anti-ELAB Movement). In particular, in studying various protest activities in the 2019 Anti-ELAB Movement, we examined how the 2014 UM affected the 2019 movement, in terms of choice of strategies, attitude to the movement, and networks and practices inherited from the past movement(s). We examined how the abeyance period (2015-18) had affected the evolution and process of the 2019 movement. In this light, the research objectives were realized as the project examined the legacy of UM, especially in terms of how it impacted the participants in terms of their values, worldviews, networks, movement resource and capital, and choice and actions in future social movements, in particular in the 2019 Anti-ELAB movement. Our research output from this project were mostly on three fronts, derived from major research finding/directions of this research. The first was about how participants in different professions used their professional resource or status to participate in the movement, and how the “traces” of the 2014 movement impacted the 2019 practices in this regard. The most significant output was a published article in the journal Social Movement Studies. The UM’s impact on various professionals was also written in two other book chapters published in 2020 and 2021. (Remark: in the funding acknowledgement, we have given a wrong project code for the journal. We are contacting the journal for correction). Secondly, we followed up on the impacts of the UM to see how different movement activists, if they did, participated in the 2019 District Council elections. We also examined how the landslide victory of the democrats brought about political changes at the local level, as an experiment of grassroot democracy reform or continuation of the social movement. The PI had written this into a new GRF project (project code: 14606321), which was funded in 2021 and is on-going. The PI already had one article from this project accepted in Journal of Contemporary Asia. Unfortunately most of the interviewees related to this project were not able to participate in the changed Legislative Council elections thereafter, and it is unlikely for the PI to continue research on this front. Thirdly, we examined the overall impacts of the UM on the Anti-ELAB movement. The UM left significant footprints on a lot of people, in terms of their views towards the movement, towards the government, and the possible choice of repertoires and strategies in future movements. There were quite a number of publications that discussed to what extent the UM affected the Anti-ELAB Movement. The movement learning effect on the Anti-ELAB Movement has been an important finding for the voluminous publications on the Anti-ELAB Movement. For example, the PI has written a comprehensive book (in Chinese) on the 2019 Anti-ELAB Movement. The co-I has published numerous articles on the Anti-ELAB Movement. His forthcoming book, to be published by the Cambridge University Press, would have a chapter on the evolution of the movement trajectory of Hong Kong. Our study of the impacts of the UM informed many of our subsequent research and publication on the 2019 Anti-ELAB Movement. It was however difficult to pinpoint how this project financed the 2019 movement researches, thus funding was usually not acknowledged in our later publications.

14606319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14606319.value: Different groups and movement activists moved into abeyance in the period 2014-18. Some of them had a rethink of what they are going to do in the future. Some of them changed track and some of them accumulated new networks and capital in the movement community. The most important finding was about how the experience of the 2014 Umbrella Movement affected their thinking, network and capital, and choice of strategies and repertoires in later movements (i.e. the 2019 Anti-Extradition Bill Movement). Through interviews with participants of the 2019 movement, our research findings were mostly about two groups of participants: professionals and District Council members or candidates. A lot of professionals were mobilized since the 2014 Umbrella Movement, and had increased their connection and activity in the years 2014-18. This affected how they participated in the events and the 2019 Anti-ELAB movement. The results of these findings were published in the items listed in the “research output”, including one journal article and two book chapters. Quite a number of movement participants chose the electoral path, and some of them ran in the 2019 District Council elections. Some of the movement activists ran and won in the 2019 election, and tried to experiment with grassroot democracy reforms with their institutional positions and resources of the District Council. The study of this trajectory was continued in another GRF project, which has brought new publications as stated in the research output section.

14606319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14606319.value: The 2019 Anti-ELAB Movement brought a sea change to the political environment of Hong Kong, and fundamentally changed the movement trajectory of many a movement activist and electoral politician. So a lot of the political changes after 2019 could be seen as indirectly “traces” of the Umbrella Movement. As far as the PI is concerned, the study on how movement activists learned from the UM and participated in the District Councils was developed into a new research. It was written into a GRF project proposal “Local Councils as Centers of Resistance” (Ref. 14606321), which was funded in 2021 and is on-going. With the political change after the imposition of the National Security Law in 2021, it was unlikely that there would be much potential for research on movement activists and public mobilization in the near future.

14606319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14606319.value: This project studied how the Umbrella Movement in 2014 affected and changed the worldviews, pattern of participation, values and attitudes to the movement, and choice of movement strategies of movement participants, and how this affected future movements. By the time this project started in October 2019, Hong Kong was already embroiled in an unprecedentedly highly mobilizational movement, the Anti-Extradition Bill Movement. The project studied how the 2014 Umbrella Movement affected the 2019 Movement. It studied how different participants of the 2014 movement learnt from their past experience and adopted new movement strategies and brought different results. The major research findings and outcomes were on two aspects. The first is what different groups and individuals did from 2014 to 2018, including developing new networks and resources, and how this impacted the 2019 movement. In particular, we studied how professional groups enhanced their resource and network and played more active roles in the 2019 movement. The other was the participation of many movement activists in the 2019 District Council election, how the movement drove them to run in the 2019 DC election and brought about more political changes.

14606519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606519.value: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is a decline of cognitive function, and individuals may have problems with memory, language, thinking and judgment that are greater than normal age-related changes. Although the decline is not serious enough to interfere with the daily life of the individuals, older adults with MCI are more likely to develop Alzheimer’s disease or other dementias than people without MCI in the future. On the other hand, many studies reported a high level of MCI symptoms among the elderly and the trend is increasing in Hong Kong. To our knowledge, there is still a lack of effective treatment or therapy for MCI, it is important to investigate effective intervention that can efficiently improve the cognitive ability of MCI patients. The objective of the present study is to study the effect of Photoneuromodulation (PNM) for improving the cognitive function of individuals with MCI. Forty middle-aged and older adults will be recruited, and the subjects will be divided randomly and equally into an experimental group, as well as the control group. Neuropsychological assessment of memory, language, and frontal function will be administered before and after the PNM. In addition, the hemodynamic changes associated with the PNM will be measured by the near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). It is hypothesized that compared to participants without PNM, those with PNM will show improvement in cognitive function as measured by the neuropsychological assessment. The results of the present study will provide evidence on the possibility of PNM in treating individuals with mild cognitive problems, as well as those with other mental disorders. 輕度認知障礙（MCI）就是一種認知功能倒退的現象。患者可能記憶，語言，思維和判斷的倒退程度比正常因年長而退化的程度更大。雖然倒退程度不足以干擾患者之日常生活運作，但患有輕度認知障礙的長者比起沒有患此病的長者，較容易發展阿爾茨海默病或其他癡呆症。在另一方面，許多研究報告指出本港越來越多長者呈現輕度認知障礙的徵狀。據我們所知，至目前為止仍未有有效治療輕度認知障礙的方法，所以探索能有效改善這類患者的認知功能的介入方法甚為重要。此研究的目的是探討生物光調節對改善輕度認知障礙患者的認知功能的效用。我們將招募四十名中老年人， 然後將受試者隨機分配到實驗組和對照組，並透過腦神經心理學評估來評定參加者的記憶，語言和執行功能。評估會於治療之前和之後分別進行。除此之外，我們會利用近紅外線光譜測量儀（NIRS）來量度參加者的相關大腦血流量。我們推測接受生物光調節的參加者與沒有接受生物光調節的參加者相比，會呈現認知功能的改善。本研究的結果將對生物光調節以治療輕度認知障礙患者及其他大腦疾病患者的可行性提供了證據。

14606519.label: Realisation of objectives
14606519.value: This research project aimed to evaluate the effect of photoneuromodulation (PNM) on older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). To achieve this goal, older adults were recruited through advertisements. Initially, around 63 adults (aged 40 years or above) with subjective memory complaints signed up to participate in this experiment. All of them completed the pre-assessment, assessing their cognitive functions with standardized neuropsychological assessments. Eight participants dropped out, and 55 remained. However, due to the pandemic of COVID-19, the intervention part of the research was suspended, given that the PNM intervention required participants to participate in 18 PNM sessions in nine consecutive weeks. Since COVID-19 has lasted for three years, conducting a longitudinal study was almost impossible. We then invited the applicants for a PNM experiment, which evaluated the effect of a single PNM trial on cognitive function with the use of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measuring the prefrontal cortex hemodynamics when the participants were performing a visual working memory task. This experiment could address the objective of this research project by understanding whether PNM could be applied with improved cognitive ability and frontal activation. The above experiment focused on a single PNM trial, and we also wanted to determine the effect of PNM if multiple PNM sessions were applied to MCI patients. Therefore, the 9-week PNM intervention study was resumed, and the participants were recruited again. Finally, nine participants who had been recruited previously returned, and their cognitive function was reassessed. They were classified as amnestic MCI and non-amnestic MCI based on their memory test performance. In addition to cognitive function, we also evaluate the improvement of their depressive and anxiety symptoms after PNM. This study provided us with information on the effect of multiple PNM sessions on MCI patients with different subtypes. The two experiments could give us a holistic understanding of the effect of PNM on improving various cognitive functions and mood symptoms in different MCI subtypes. Furthermore, functional neuroimaging (i.e., fNIRS) results could provide us with insights in brain functional changes induced by PNM. Therefore, it is believed that the objective of the present project was achieved to a large extent.

14606519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14606519.value: We first evaluated the effect of single-trial photoneuromodulation (PNM) on older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). We found that participants who received real PNM demonstrated significant improvements in a visual working memory task compared to those who received sham PNM (Chan, Lee, Hamblin et al., 2021). Additionally, the real PNM group exhibited lower prefrontal hemodynamic responses as measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). These findings suggest that PNM may reduce cognitive effort and enhance cognitive performance in individuals with MCI. Building upon these results, we conducted further research to investigate the effects of multiple sessions of PNM on individuals with MCI (Chan, Lee, Sze et al., 2021; Cheung et al., 2023). In a case study involving three amnestic MCI participants who received 18 PNM sessions over 9 weeks, significant improvements in memory within the normal range were observed after PNM (Chan, Lee, Sze et al., 2021). Specifically, one participant showed improved verbal memory from the 1st to the 67th percentile, another improved from the 4th to the 26th percentile, and the third improved from the 11th to the 54th percentile. In contrast, amnestic MCI participants who did not receive PNM either experienced deterioration or remained at a moderately impaired level. Consistently, improvements in frontal lobe cognitive functions were observed in all three non-amnestic MCI participants after 18 PNM sessions (Cheung et al., 2023). These improvements were characterized by reduced intrusion and perseveration errors. One participant improved her intrusion and perseveration errors from the <1st – 2nd percentile to the 41st – 69th percentile, another older adult also improved her intrusion error from the 11th to the 83rd percentile, and the third from the 5th to the 56th percentile. In addition, they also showed improvements in anxiety and/or depressive symptoms. One participant’s anxiety and depressive symptoms improved from the severe range at baseline to the mild range after PNM. The other two improved their depressive symptoms from the mild range at baseline to the normal range after PNM. Therefore, these case studies suggest that PNM may enhance the memory of amnestic MCI participants and improve frontal lobe cognitive function and mood symptoms of non-amnestic MCI participants.

14606519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14606519.value: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, some of the participants had dropped out when we resumed the 18 PNM intervention sessions, which resulted in a small sample size. Despite this, the results of the present project still provided us with important preliminary support that photoneuromodulation (PNM) may effectively improve the cognitive functions of older adults with mild cognitive improvement (MCI), regardless of its subtypes (i.e., amnestic MCI or non-amnestic MCI). Therefore, the present study encouraged future large-scale studies to replicate the positive results. Besides, the encouraging results found in this project suggested that PNM has the potential to improve the cognitive function of older adults with MCI. This suggests that this novel brain stimulation technique may also be applicable to older adults with other clinical conditions, such as traumatic brain injury, or stroke. Future studies may consider applying PNM to different clinical populations. Finally, given that the present project focused on frontal lobe cognitive function, only the prefrontal hemodynamics was investigated using fNIRS. In order to have a more in-depth understanding of the effect of PNM on different regions of the brain, a whole-head functional imaging system could be employed in the future.

14606519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14606519.value: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) refers to a decline in cognitive function that exceeds normal age-related changes. Older adults with MCI have a higher risk of developing dementia compared to those without MCI. Recent studies have observed an increasing prevalence of MCI symptoms among older adults in Hong Kong. However, effective treatments for MCI are currently lacking. Therefore, it is crucial to explore interventions that can effectively enhance the cognitive abilities of MCI patients. This research project focused on investigating the effect of photoneuromodulation (PNM), a form of near-infrared light stimulation targeting the brain, on cognitive function in MCI patients. The findings revealed that MCI patients exhibited significant improvements in cognitive functions, including memory, frontal lobe functions, and symptoms of depression and anxiety, following PNM intervention. Furthermore, functional brain imaging results indicated that PNM may enhance the cognitive efficiency of the prefrontal cortex. This suggests that MCI patients could utilize their brain resources more efficiently after PNM. In contrast, MCI patients who did not receive PNM did not show these changes. These results provide support for the use of PNM as a means to enhance cognitive function in MCI patients.
