14606919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14606919.value: Introduction Evidence has consistently shown the high efficacy of human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines in preventing cervical cancers. However, the rate of HPV vaccine uptake was very low in Hong Kong. We plan to develop an innovative, theory-based multidisciplinary team-led school-based HPV vaccination health-promotion programme (MDL-SHPVP) and will engage female adolescents, their parents/guardians and secondary school personnel in multicomponent educational strategies and interactive discussions. Age-appropriate and user-centred resource materials and video games will be provided. Aim To develop and evaluate the effects of the MDL-SHPVP and to examine whether the effect of the MDL-SHPVP on the rate of HPV vaccine uptake 1 year after intervention is mediated by parents’/guardians’ and female adolescents’ HPV knowledge, attitudes and beliefs, adolescents’ intention to receive HPV vaccination and vaccine acceptance among their parents/guardians. Methods A cluster randomised controlled trial is proposed. We will recruit 2520 adolescents and their parents or guardians from 18 local secondary day schools. The MDL-SHPVP is underpinned by the Health Belief Model and the Precaution Adoption Process Model. Multicomponent interventions will be offered to the intervention schools including education sessions with small group dialogues with a registered nurse and trained healthcare and lay volunteers and educational computer games. To build and strengthen the community capacity in health promotion, a team of volunteers will be established to raise awareness of HPV, cervical cancer and HPV vaccine. Primary outcomes include the female adolescents’ uptake of the HPV vaccine 1 year after the intervention. Secondary outcomes include the female adolescents’ intention to receive HPV vaccination, vaccine acceptance among their parents/guardians, and the parents’/guardians’ and female adolescents’ HPV knowledge, attitudes and beliefs. Data will be collected at baseline, 1 month and 1 year after intervention. The mixed-effects model will be used to compare the differential changes for each of the primary and secondary outcomes across time between the two groups. Path analysis will be conducted to examine whether the vaccine uptake rate is mediated by psychosocial variables including HPV knowledge, attitudes and beliefs, intention to receive HPV vaccine and vaccine acceptance. Discussion and significance The project is expected to instil a more accurate understanding of HPV and HPV vaccination and support the decision to undergo vaccination. This project will play a pioneering role in gathering concerted cross-sectoral efforts to enhance the uptake of HPV vaccination among female adolescents, and it will be the first of its kind to build this capacity among the Chinese community. 有證據顯示子宮頸癌疫苗在預防子宮頸癌方面具有很好的療效。然而，香港子宮頸癌疫苗的接種率一直偏低。我們將會評估子宮頸癌疫苗注射健康促進計劃（MDL-SHPVP），並鼓勵青少年及其家長∕監護人參與有關的多元教學策略和互動討論。計劃將提供適齡和以用者為中心的資源及影像遊戲。 目的 計劃旨在開發MDL-SHPVP和評估其效用，並評估MDL-SHPVP對1年後子宮頸癌疫苗接種率的影響。計劃包括調節父母/監護人和青少年女性對子宮頸癌的知識，態度和信仰；青少年女性接受疫苗注射的意向；及其父母/監護人對子宮頸癌疫苗的接受程度。 方法 研究將採用集群隨機對照試驗方式。我們會邀請共2,520位來自18所本港中學的青少年女性及其家長或監護人參與是次研究。MDL-SHPVP以健康信念模式（Health Belief Model）和預防採用歷程（Precaution Adoption Process Model）為基礎。計劃將向實驗組學校提供多元介入措施，包括由註冊護士及已受培訓的義工進行的教育課程，內容包括小組對話及教育類電子遊戲等。為了建立和加強社區健康推廣，計劃將成立一個提高對子宮頸癌認識的義工團隊。研究主要指標為介入後一年的青少年女性子宮頸癌疫苗的接種率。次要指標包括青少年女性接受疫苗注射的意向，父母/監護人對子宮頸癌疫苗的接受程度，以及父母/監護人和青少年女性對子宮頸癌的知識，態度和信仰。計劃將在介入後，介入後1個月和1年後收集數據。混合效應模型將用於比較兩組之間主要和次要指標的差異。因徑分析將分析疫苗接種率是否由心理社會後果影響，包括子宮頸癌的知識，態度和信念，接受疫苗注射的意向和對疫苗的接受程度。 討論及含義 計劃旨在灌輸更準確的子宮頸癌及其疫苗的資訊，以提高青少年女性子宮頸癌疫苗的接種率。該計劃將在收集及協調跨界力量作為先鋒角色，並為華人社區中首創。

14606919.label: Realisation of objectives
14606919.value: The objectives of the project were achieved. We recruited a total of 1,340 female students from 18 secondary schools in Hong Kong at baseline. Among the students, 306 (22.8%) of them had received human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, 18 (1.3%) provided blank/invalid information on the questionnaires, and 14 (1.0%) declined to participate. After excluding these students, a total of 1,002 (74.8%) students were included in the analysis. In addition, a total of 848 (84.6%) and 638 (63.7%) students completed the questionnaires at one month (T1) and one year (T2) after completion of the intervention respectively. The number of students recruited were lower than the targeted sample size of 2,520. The low rate of recruitment could be attributed to two major factors. First, the study was commenced on 1 January 2020 and majority of the secondary schools declined to participate during the coronavirus pandemic because classes were frequently cancelled, and all on-campus extracurricular activities were suspended. In the aftermath of the coronavirus pandemic, secondary schools prioritised academic activities over other types of learning and extracurricular activities amid the busy schedules of their students. In spite of our best efforts to coordinate activities and interventions with school schedules, many schools declined to participate. In addition, some schools only permitted us to reach a limited number of students so the majority could attend make-up classes to prepare for the Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination. Consequently, recruiting, collecting data, and implementing interventions took longer time than expected. Second, there was an increase in the number of students who left the secondary schools between 2020 and 2023 due to emigration, further decreasing the pool of students for recruitment. This also explained why fewer students were available to complete the follow-up assessments, with other reasons for the decrease included having left the school after graduation or declined to continue to participate in the study. We have collected 853 copies of the parent/guardian-version questionnaires from the 18 participating secondary schools. Among the questionnaires, 187 (21.9%) were excluded for indicating that their daughters (students) had previously received HPV vaccination. A total of 18 (2.1%) declined to participate, while 4 (0.5%) provided blank or invalid information on the questionnaires, leaving a total of 644 copies. At T1 and T2, a total of 445 (69.1%) and 277 (43.0%) copies of the parent/guardian-version questionnaires respectively were collected from the 18 participating schools. A variety of strategies were used to maximise parents’/guardians’ participation, including providing options for completing the questionnaire on paper or electronically via a designated link created by the research team, sending reminders to parents to complete the questionnaires, and extending the deadline for completing them by a week to two weeks. Nevertheless, the number of parents who participated was still much lower than anticipated. The low response rate could be due to the parents’/guardians’ busy work schedule for completing the questionnaires and/or attending the intervention sessions amid the coronavirus pandemic. Besides, the total number of questionnaires received from the schools in the intervention group was nearly double the total number of parents/guardians who attended the intervention sessions. There was also around one-third of all the parent/guardian-version questionnaires had the student's age incorrectly filled in by the parents/guardians. Since the questionnaires were collected by the schoolteachers who invited students to ask their parents/guardians to fill them out, which was either requested by or discussed with the schools to maintain respect for the parents’/guardians’ privacy, verification of the parents’/guardians’ completion of the questionnaires could not be made. To avoid generating potentially misleading results, we therefore analysed the responses of the students only. Among the 18 secondary schools recruited, nine schools were randomly allocated to the intervention group and the students (n=485) of the nine schools received the intervention as planned, which is the multidisciplinary team-led school-based HPV vaccination health-promotion programme consisting of health information delivery, animated video games, and interactive dialogues with the expert healthcare team. On the other hand, students (n=517) of the remaining nine schools, which were randomly allocated to the control group, received online educational videos introducing HPV and HPV vaccination as planned. A total of 128 lay volunteers (mostly undergraduate students) and 30 healthcare professionals were trained to conduct the health-promotion programme according to the study protocol. Very positive feedback was received from the lay volunteers. They particularly appreciated for the opportunities to interact with the health experts of the research team and other healthcare professionals, and learned the latest research evidence about efficacy of the HPV vaccine as well as clarified common misconceptions about HPV vaccination. Both the lay volunteers and the healthcare professionals found the health-promotion programme meaningful and were pleased to be a member of the team to support the programme. Considering the potential design effect of the randomisation conducted at the school level instead of by individual participant, the outcome analyses were performed on the basis of a mixed-effects model with up to three levels to account for inter-correlation among individuals within the same school and for intra-correlation over time within an individual and variations between individuals. More specifically, a (two-level) random intercept mixed-effects model was used to compare the HPV uptake rate at T1 and T2 between the intervention and control groups accounting for the clustering design, while a (three-level) random intercept mixed-effects model was used to compare the differential change for each of the repeated measures outcomes at T1 with respect to T0 accounting for the intra-correlated clustered and repeated-measures data. The restricted maximum likelihood method was used in the mixed-effects models to handle the missing data which could produce unbiased estimates even in the presence of missing data, provided that the data are missing at random. Regarding the second objective of the study, as there was no significant interventional effect found for the HPV vaccine uptake, the proposed mediation analysis was therefore not conducted.

14606919.label: Major findings and research outcome
14606919.value: A total of 1,340 female students from 18 secondary schools were recruited. Among the students, 338 students were excluded because they received HPV vaccination prior to enrolment (n=306), provided invalid information on the questionnaires (n=18), or declined to participate in the study (n=14). Therefore, a total of 1,002 female students (mean age=15.3 years, standard deviation=1.1, range=12-18 years) were included in the analysis. There were 12.5% (n=125) of the students whose family members had received HPV vaccination and 13.1% (n=131) had previously attended an educational talk related to HPV vaccination. Only 3.1% (n=31) had prior discussions with healthcare professionals about HPV vaccination in the preceding 12 months. A total of 848 (84.6%) and 638 (63.7%) students completed the questionnaires at one month (T1) and one year (T2) after the intervention respectively. Uptake Consistently more students in the intervention group reported receiving HPV vaccination at one month and one year after the intervention respectively than that of the control group, with 19 (4.9%) versus 6 (1.3%) students at T1, and 32 (11.9%) versus 29 (7.9%) students at T2, though the differences between the two groups were not statistically significant. Intention to receive vaccination Students in the intervention group reported a greater increment in likelihood of having HPV vaccination than students in the control group after the intervention (Group-by-time interaction B=0.23, 95% Confidence Interval (CI), [-0.06 , 0.53], p=0.123). Attitudes Measured by the modified Carolina HPV Immunisation Attitudes and Beliefs Scale, significantly greater changes were found in the subscales of Barriers (B=-2.20, 95% CI, [-3.46 , -0.94], p=0.001), Risk Denial (B=-0.82, 95% CI, [-1.60 , -0.05], p=0.038), and Uncertainty (B=0.72, 95% CI, [0.16 , 1.27], p=0.011) among the intervention group students than the control group students after the intervention, indicating that the intervention group students had more positive attitudes towards HPV vaccination particularly reduced perception of harms and denial of risk of HPV related infections. The increase in perceived uncertainty about HPV vaccination among the intervention group students may be contributed by their increased informational need after the intervention. Knowledge The intervention group students consistently showed improvement in their knowledge about HPV, with greater increase in the total scores of the HPV Knowledge Scale (B=0.94, 95% CI, [0.16 , 1.72], p=0.018) and the Vaccination Knowledge Scale (B=0.32, 95% CI, [-0.06 , 0.70], p=0.095) than that of the control group students after the intervention.

14606919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14606919.value: The study results supported that the MDL-SHPVP was beneficial in improving the adolescent female students’ knowledge and positive attitudes towards HPV vaccination, and their uptake of HPV vaccine, with 11.9% of the students reported receiving HPV vaccination within one year after the intervention. With the introduction of the government-subsidised HPV vaccination scheme for female students in Primary Five or Six since 2019/20, the intervention still plays an important role in strengthening the knowledge and positive attitudes of students towards HPV vaccination and hence enabling an informed choice, particularly given the extremely low percentage (13.1%) of students who have attended HPV vaccination talks previously. Further directions of research may include longer follow-up longitudinal quantitative evaluation to assess the effects on HPV vaccination coverage among students and qualitative exploration of the perceptions of key stakeholders including schoolteachers and parents/guardians on usefulness of the intervention and further health information needs. For parents/guardians to be able to participate fully and provide feedback, tailored recruitment strategies for parents/guardians should be developed with school personnel. The educational materials can also be adapted to the health needs of adolescent boys and evaluated in randomised controlled trials for its impact on HPV vaccine uptake, knowledge, and attitudes.

14606919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14606919.value: A multidisciplinary team-led school-based human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination health-promotion programme was evaluated in this cluster randomised controlled trial. A total of 1,340 female adolescents from 18 secondary schools in Hong Kong were recruited. Following the health-promotion programme, students' knowledge and attitudes toward HPV vaccination were significantly improved, with 11.9% reporting that they had been vaccinated against HPV during the 1-year follow-up. The vaccination rate was higher than that of the students who only received online educational videos on HPV vaccination (7.9%). The government-subsidised HPV vaccination scheme for girls in Primary Five or Six has been in place since 2019/20, yet the health-promotion programme developed in this study has the potential to play a crucial role in empowering adolescent girls to make informed decisions about HPV vaccination by strengthening their knowledge and positive attitudes. A future focus of the research will be to evaluate the longer-term impact of the programme on HPV uptake and explore the perceptions of key stakeholders including schoolteachers and parents on usefulness of the programme and further health information needs. The educational materials can be adapted to meet the needs of adolescent boys and evaluated to determine its impact on HPV vaccine uptake, knowledge, and attitudes.

14607219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14607219.value: The 2014 Umbrella Movement and recent conflicts to do with the advocacy of Hong Kong independence have brought to the fore the question of what Hong Kong is, as constituted by social and political imagination. Evidently, what is being urgently contested is the very notion of the Hong Kong nation as an "imagined community", to use Benedict Anderson's concept. The prevailing methodology and language used to examine Hong Kong's contemporary situation often stem from historical (Ortmann 2015), social (Hui and Lau 2015), and legal-political (Yuen 2015) frameworks. Such frameworks, to some extent, predetermine what is being examined. As such, scholarship have yet to directly address the central issue of what Hong Kong is, as viscerally thought and felt by the person on the street. As has been argued, “[w]hat is real … about cities is as much emotional as physical” (Pile 2005). Scholarship that endorses historical, social, political and legal frameworks often leave out the individual's qualitative experience of the environment. Such experience can turn out to be transformative, allowing for the emergence of new configurations of affect in relation to the experience of institutional and social change. This project maps the affective terrain of Hong Kong, through the intertwined disciplines of street photography, autoethnography and psychogeography. Street photography engages with "the literal and the figurative, the given and the possible, the seen and the hallucinated", negotiating between the actual-empirical and the actively-experienced in Hong Kong's urban space (Scott 2007). Autoethnography allows the researcher to attend to "lives, identities, and feelings ... connected to the sociocultural contexts in which we live" and hence is able to foreground the practice of art-making in relation to the sociocultural environment (Leon Anderson 2006). Psychogeography, the practitioners of which include Iain Sinclair and Peter Ackroyd, attends to the influence of external environment on the thoughts, feelings and behaviour of individuals, is a discipline this project also draws on. This is an art-making project. It is a literary, visual and creative exploration, seeking to produce a "thick description" of Hong Kong at present, tracing its "webs of significance", thus bringing to bear an interpretive approach to the understanding of what Hong Kong is alongside its condition of possibilities (Geertz 1973). It is about "thinking in, through and with art", offering a reminder of "unfinished thinking" amidst ideas and affect that form polar oppositions, such that Hong Kong begins to speak (Borgdorff 2011). 在2014年的雨傘運動，以及最近因提倡香港獨立而起的衝突的氛圍下，香港的本質，及其在社會與政治想像下構成的形象引起了強烈且廣泛的討論和關注。顯然地，目前逼切的爭論重點在於香港民族如何作為一個如Benedict Anderson提出的「想像的共同體」。當今的香港近況研究普遍使用的方法及語體大部分以歷史（Ortmann 2015）、社會（Hui，Lau 2015）與法律政治（Yuen 2015）的範疇出發。在相當的程度上，這等範疇也為了研究的範圍定了前設。因此，現有的理論仍未能直接地從最切身處地的角度，如香港人的思想感受，去探討何謂香港的中心議題。如學者之前所提出，「關於城市的情感與實體一樣真確。」（Pile 2005）那些使用歷史、社會、政治，以及法律觀點的的研究往往遺漏了個人對環境的定性的經歷。這些經歷卻對議題有著改革性的作用，因為這因制度與社會的改變而引發出的種種的感受為現有的論述提供了全新的角度。本次研究分別透過這兩種不同形式，又相互聯繫的街頭攝影 – 自我民族誌及地理心理學，去刻畫香港的情感地帶。街頭攝影探索「字面的淺意與比喻的深度，現存的狀況與潛在的可能，可見的事實與理想的幻像」，把身處在香港的城市空間的經驗及體驗連結(Scott 2007)。在自我民族誌的框架下，研究者著眼於「生活，關係與情感...以及它們跟我們身處的社會文化景況的關係」，因而為創造與社會文化環境息息相關的藝術設立了前景(Leon Anderson 2006)。另一方面，本研究也會運用地理心理學（著名學者包括Iain Sinclair與Peter Ackroyd），探究外在環境對個人思想，感情及行為的影響。本研究是一個創造藝術的計畫。這是個文學、視覺，與創意的探索，通過追溯「意義的網羅」，為現今的香港繪製一個有質感的描述，以及為香港的本質及其可能性提供一個互動性的理解方向(Geertz 1973)。本研究旨在「於藝術思想，從藝術探索，與藝術共覓」，在當今兩極化的意見與情感下提出「未完的思考」的方向，好讓社會聆聽到香港最真實的聲音(Borgdorff 2011)。

14607219.label: Realisation of objectives
14607219.value: All objectives have been realised via the publication of the academic monograph Hong Kong as Creative Practice. The book maps the affective terrain of places like Tsim Sha Tsui and Sham Shui Po, among others. It is a blend of scholarship (via autoethnography) and art-making (via street photography) that uses creative expression for creative documentary writing to give meaning to Hong Kong's city spaces. It explores feelings, affects, and states of mind as probes into the city and its social life. Two conference papers were presented and they were subsequently revised for publication, one as a journal article, the other as part of the above-mentioned book.

14607319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14607319.value: Introduction The emerging health problem of adolescent Internet gaming disorder (IGD) is prevalent globally. It causes severe physical, psychological, and social harms. IGD is included in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) in 2013, and the 11th edition of the International Classification of Disease (ICD-11), together with video gaming disorder, as a mental health disorder in 2018 (WHO, 2018). Pharmaceutical treatment of IGD has inadequate evidence and may cause significant side effects among adolescents. Despite the urgency, there is few evidence-based treatments for IGD. Systematic reviews showed that maladaptive beliefs and coping accounted for IGD. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is potentially useful as it is effective in treating mental/behavioral disorders, restructuring cognitions and cultivating positive coping. A gap exists as the only two existing clinic-based small randomized controlled trials (RCT) yielded mixed findings on CBT’s treatment effect for adolescent IGD. Objectives This RCT study develops a brief group-based CBT intervention. The primary objective is to evaluate the efficacy of the CBT in reducing IGD, compare to a wait-list control group. We also test the hypothesis that the treatment effect would be mediated by improvements in maladaptive cognitions and adaptive coping. Subjects and methods The study design is two-armed RCT. The participants are Secondary 1-4 students (n=226) with IGD (DSM-5 classification) identified in a school-based screening. Evaluation involves surveys at baseline, end of CBT intervention, and 6 months afterwards. In addition to information received by the wait-list control group, the intervention group receives a carefully designed brief 8-week group-based CBT. The control group will receive CBT after the 6-month follow-up. Trained social workers of a collaborating NGO that serves secondary school students will conduct the CBT. Outcomes and measures The primary outcome is IGD (a validated DSM-5 IGD classification tool). Secondary outcomes include time spent on Internet/Internet games and the intention to reduce IGD. Measures of potential mediators (maladaptive beliefs and coping) include: Internet Gaming Cognition Scale, Generalized Problematic Internet Use Scale, Emotion Regulation Questionnaire, and Coping Scale for Children and Youth. Data analysis Intention-to-treat analysis is performed. The primary outcome is assessed by absolute and relative risk reduction. Generalized Linear Mixed Models and Structural Equation Models are used to test secondary outcomes and mediation effects. Implications The findings may lead to an evidence-based treatment for adolescent IGD, a newly defined disease, which has been rarely reported in literature. Understanding its mechanism contributes to theoretical development of IGD and related treatment. 青少年網路遊戲障礙（IGD）的健康問題在全球普遍存在。它能導致嚴重的身體、心理和社會傷害。IGD 與視頻遊戲障礙被作為心理健康障礙被包含在2013年第五版精神障礙診斷和統計手冊（DSM-5）和第11版《國際疾病分類》（ICD-11）（WHO，2018）。藥物治療對IGD的療效證據不足，且可能對青少年產生顯著的副作用。對IGD的循證治療方法很少。系統的文獻回顧表明，不適當的信念和應對方法是導致IGD的原因。認知行為療法 （CBT）能有效治療精神/行為障礙，重新整合認知和培養積極應對方法。因此，它可能對治療IGD 有顯著效果。僅有的兩個基於臨床的小型隨機對照試驗（RCT）對CBT對青少年IGD的治療效果發現了不一致的結果。該領域的研究依然存在空白。 此 RCT 研究旨在發展一個基於小組的 CBT 短期干預。主要目標是評估 CBT 與控制組相比是否能有效降低 IGD 。另外，我們檢測適當認知和積極應對方法對治療效果的中介作用。 研究設計為包括對照組和控制組的RCT。參加者為中學1-4年級學生（n=226）。他們經過以學校為單位的篩查并被確認為有IGD（DSM-5分類）。 評估包括基線調查、CBT 干預結束調查和 6 個月之後調查。對照組和控制組都會收到關於IGD的資訊。除此之外，干預組亦收到一個為期8周的基於小組的CBT。控制組將在6個月的隨訪後接受CBT干預。受過培訓的社會工作者將開展CBT。 主要結果變量是IGD。次要結果變量包括互聯網/網路遊戲上的使用時間和減少 IGD的意願。潛在中介變量包括不適當的信念和應對方法。 數據分析包括執行意圖處理分析，絕對和相對風險率降低，廣義線性混合模型和結構方程模型。 IGD是一種新界定的疾病，相關文獻也較少。本研究會為青少年IGD的治療提供實證依據。對療效機制的探索有助於IGD及相關治療的理論發展。

14607319.label: Realisation of objectives
14607319.value: Three major steps to achieve the project objectives including design, implementation, and evaluation of the intervention: 1. Designing a cognitive behavioral therapy for internet gaming disorder of adolescents in Hong Kong A multi-session intervention was developed. First, themes and respective subtopics that captured different aspects of behavioral promotion for internet gaming disorder of adolescents in Hong Kong were identified based on both well-documented manual of cognitive behavioral therapy as well as quantitative and qualitative evidence. A review of significant predictors of internet gaming disorder were first conducted to inform the selection of topics and cognitive and behavioral factors. Focus group discussions with six local youth and three social workers of the collaborating NGO (the Hong Kong Family Welfare Society) providing service for youth mental health were then conducted to collect knowledge, views and information needs on specific topics, motives, coping styles, and preferred activities under each theme/modules, and to seek their suggestions on the development of intervention materials. The revision to session themes, subtopics, focuses, strategies and activities was also made based on feedbacks from the collaborating NGO (the Hong Kong Family Welfare Society) staff and specialists in this field. Second, the materials for cognitive behavioral therapy and education control were developed and finalized. For cognitive behavioral therapy, materials for eight sessions/modules were developed, including rapport building, emotional regulation, cognitive restructuring, time management, problem solving, and progress review and addiction relapse prevention. Cartoon characters, metaphors, daily examples, lively narrative stories, and interactive games were designed to facilitate participants to learn and practice the skills and techniques of cognitive behavioral therapy. For education control, materials for the topics of internet gaming disorder, its definition and consequence, and help seeking resources were developed. Third, a 3-day training was conducted among social workers of the collaborating NGO (the Hong Kong Family Welfare Society). Three social workers with degree and at least 2-year experience in social work of the collaborating NGO, the Hong Kong Family Welfare Society, finished the training and delivered the cognitive behavioral therapy. They delivered cognitive behavioral therapy for mental health in previous work; they are familiar with students’ problems as the NGO is serving >40 local secondary schools; and they are experienced in offering internet addiction programs and psychosocial programs to students. The 3-day sessions were conducted by a health psychologist and a clinical psychologist. Training contents include concepts about internet gaming disorder, cognitive behavioral therapy techniques and theories, with the means of role-play, supervised practices, questions/answers, and feedbacks. A 4-week pilot run were conducted for some sessions to six students with internet gaming disorder in the presence of trainers; feedbacks were provided to the facilitators, who needed to obtain satisfactory assessment from the trainers before starting the actual sessions. Continual and timely support was available to the facilitators throughout the intervention period. The PI and clinical psychologists met regularly with the social workers and randomly sat in some sessions. 2. Implementing a randomized controlled trial to test for the intervention efficacy First, with the help of the collaborating NGO (the Hong Kong Family Welfare Society), secondary schools were invited to join the study. The significance and logistics were explained in a leaflet for schools. Parents received an information sheet and invitation letter. Both the students and parents were informed about voluntary participation, and that refusal has no impact of any kind on the students. Written informed concern was obtained from parents and students. The school-based screening survey in secondary school students (n=4553) was conducted in classroom settings in the absence of teachers. The research team worked on data analyses and identified eligible students who were at high-risk of internet gaming disorder (>=5 criteria of IGD in the DSM-5). Assisted by teachers and social workers, the eligible students were invited to join the following interventions. Eligible participants were evenly randomized into the intervention and control groups, based on computer-generated random number and block randomization (size of four). The randomization was clearly explained in the information sheet and explained to the students and parents. Second, the enrolled participants (n=230) were randomly allocated by the computerized system to either the intervention group or the education control group and finished the 6-month follow-up. For both groups, the entire intervention lasted for 8 weeks and there were 8 sessions in total. Each session was delivered by well-trained social workers of the collaborating NGO (the Hong Kong Family Welfare Society). The intervention was implemented at a group-level (5-11 persons/group). The control group received the educational information of well-being only. The documents were not allowed to share outside the study, so as to avoid the potential contamination between conditions. Third, a post-intervention survey was conducted among the intervention participants in classroom settings after the intervention. A long-term follow-up survey was conducted after six months. Both follow-up surveys were administered to the total enrolled sample regardless of the retention status during the treatment. Notwithstanding, variables related to the treatment (e.g. engagement with messages) were not measured among treatment dropouts. 3. Evaluating the comparative efficacy of the intervention condition As indicators of the intervention efficacy, outcomes of behaviors and cognitions with respect to internet gaming disorder (IGD) were repeatedly measured before and after the intervention. Primary outcome: The 9-item IGD checklist is a short, user-friendly, self-report measure for assessing the DSM-5 classification of IGD. Secondary outcomes: (1) Number of hours used on Internet gaming and (2) Internet during a typical week in the last three months will be recorded. (3) Motivation/intention to reduce IGD is assessed by the question ‘How much do you want to correct your IGD problem in the next three months’ (5-point scale). Potential mediators: (1) Maladaptive beliefs will be assessed by the 24-item Internet Gaming Cognition Scale (0=do not agree to 2=strongly agree). It has adequate to excellent internal reliability; it assesses the four key previously mentioned types of maladaptive beliefs of IGD, and was developed by the same researcher who developed the framework of the maladaptive beliefs on IGD. (2) Adaptive coping: a. Self-regulation to be measured by the adapted subscales (the Compulsive Use Subscale and Cognitive Preoccupation Subscale of 6 items) of the Generalized Problematic Internet Use Scale. b. Emotion regulation will be assessed by the 10-item Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (1=strongly disagree to 7=strongly agree). c. Problem solving skills to be assessed by the Coping Scale for Children and Youth (0=never to 3=very often). Background variables and potential confounders: grade, gender, age, school, residency, living arrangement, facilitator, timing (first or second term), perceived parental/peers’ Internet gaming behaviors, and parental education levels. Finally, a total of 194 and 158 participants completed the post-intervention and 6-month follow-up assessment, respectively, and were included for the analyses. Baseline characteristics were first compared between conditions. Significant group imbalance, if found, was further controlled for as the potential confounder of intervention effects. Within-group comparisons between baseline and follow-up levels of efficacy outcomes were conducted for each condition. Between-group comparisons in efficacy outcomes were then conducted for each follow-up wave. Next, structural equation modeling was followed to test for the mediation effect of mechanism-related variables. The effect of intervention condition on efficacy outcomes and potential mediators was first examined. The indirect effect of intervention condition on efficacy outcomes through the potential mediator was further examined.

14607319.label: Major findings and research outcome
14607319.value: 1. Background variables In the CBT group, 73.7% were male; 94.9% were born in Hong Kong, and the majority were 13 years old, accounting for 33.3%. Most participants lived with both parents (73.7%), followed by those living with their mother (17.2%), father (4%), and neither parent (5.1%). The majority of fathers (41.4%) and mothers (47.5%) completed secondary high school education level. In the control group, 77.7% of participants were male, with 90.4% born in Hong Kong. The largest age groups were 13 and 14 years old, each making up 31.9%. Most participants lived with both parents (84%), followed by those living with their mother (8.5%), father (3.2%), and neither parent (4.3%). Most common parental education level was secondary school, with 43.6% of fathers and 41.5% of mothers. 2. Group comparison According to ANCOVA, after controlling for pre-scores, there was a significant relationship between group and maladaptive beliefs at post-test, F(1, 192)= 6.387, p=0.012, with significance also found in the follow-up self-regulation (p = 0.011). However, no significant difference was found between group and IGD, regardless of post-test or follow-up period. Regarding the secondary outcome of the number of hours spent on internet gaming, after adjusting for age and gender, the results indicated a significant main effect in time, F(2) = 19.451, p < 0.001. However, no significant difference was found between the time and the number of hours spent on internet (p=0.343). Regarding Motivation/intention to reduce IGD, results indicated a significant main effect in time, F(2)=4.067, p=0.018 but not in group, F(1)=2.889, p=.090. 3. Identify the significant mediators Both SEM models showed good model fit indices (with maladaptive beliefs): TLI = 0.934, CFI = 0.960, SRMR = 0.038; the model with adaptive coping: TLI = 0.914, CFI = 0.957, SRMR = 0.033). In the adaptive coping model, there was a significant negative relationship with the group (B = -0.195, p = 0.01), and a significant positive relationship with IGD (B = 0.596, p < 0.001). Additionally, the indirect path from the group to Adaptive Coping to IGD showed a significant negative relationship (B = -0.116, p = 0.015). There was a significant negative relationship between maladaptive beliefs and the group (B = -0.175, p = 0.02), and a positive relationship between IGD and maladaptive beliefs (B = 0.56, p < 0.001). Furthermore, maladaptive beliefs mediated the effect of the group on IGD (B = -0.098, p = 0.028).

14607319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14607319.value: Future research on the most optimal construction of cognitive behavioral therapy for IGD is warranted. A more complex study design (e.g. factorial design) needs to be applied to manipulate specific cognitive behavioral techniques and sequence of themes/modules, and understand their potential interplays. The most effective combination of cognitive behavioral therapy needs further exploration to maximize the synergistic effect on promoting behavioral change and addiction reduction. Also, implementation science study of cognitive behavioral therapy in secondary schools and by social workers is needed to better understand the facilitators and barriers of the project implementation. In terms of the practical applications, the present study could inform the future incorporation of cognitive behavioral therapy as part of the comprehensive prevention and intervention services for IGD. Given the rigorous development procedures, the intervention can be efficiently replicated and adapted to other regions and high-risk populations, though its efficacy needs to be further tested in other settings. Moreover, this social worker-delivered intervention has the potential to be scaled-up and integrated into regular prevention and intervention services in schools and NGOs when its cost-effectiveness being further demonstrated. The key actions are enhancing adolescents’ health literacy about IGD as well as exploiting usable and sustainable healthcare service.

14607319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14607319.value: The study is the first evidence-based RCT study investigating the efficacy of an adolescent IGD treatment in Hong Kong, and one of the few globally. Cognitive behavioral therapy is evidence-based and effective in improving adolescent mental health and substance-use disorders. The findings demonstrated its efficacy and extended its application to IGD and non-substance-use disorders/behavioral addiction. The mediation analysis would allow researchers, as one of the very few attempts to understand the mechanism of cognitive behavioral therapy for treating adolescent IGD (specific maladaptive beliefs and coping such as problem solving and time management). It can lead researchers to refine adolescent CBT for non-substance-use disorders/behavioral addiction.

14607519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14607519.value: Scoliosis is characterised by uneven shoulders, curvature of the spine and uneven hips. Around 15-20% of adolescents in the community suffer from mild scoliosis (that is, spinal curvature angle between 10° and 20°) due to poor posture and/or spinal deformity. Mild scoliosis adversely affects their quality of life, and they may suffer from lower self-image and poor daily function. At present, adolescents with mild scoliosis are only observed every 6 to 12 months, with no active interventions. Although the majority of cases (around 80-90%) are non-progressive, the remaining adolescents are at risk for curve progression during puberty (age 10-16) if they are skeletally immature. Thus, the adverse influence of poor posture and/or spinal deformity on adolescents’ health and well-being can be prominent and enduring. Paraspinal muscle imbalance is found in adolescents with deviation of the spine from normal curvature. Asymmetry in paraspinal muscle activities is also a prominent risk factor for curve progression in scoliosis. Thus, posture training to improve symmetry in paraspinal muscle activities in adolescents with mild scoliosis is essential to enhance their quality of life and to reduce their risk of curve progression. The improvement of their spinal posture will result in better physical health and psychological wellbeing. This study is an inter-disciplinary collaboration that includes expertise in social work, textile technology and orthopaedics (spine surgeon) using a single-blind, randomised controlled trial. A mixed methods approach will involve quantitative (standardised survey, female adolescents, age between 11 and 13 years old, n ≥ 600, and training paradigm, n = 60) and qualitative (in-depth interviews, n = 24) research designs. This innovative joint effort will investigate quality of life issues due to poor posture and/or spinal deformity and their associated risk factors in daily activities, and will evaluate the effectiveness of non-invasive, user-friendly and evidence-based surface electromyographic (sEMG) biofeedback posture training for female adolescents with mild scoliosis. The development of sEMG biofeedback posture training will facilitate the proactive involvement of adolescents, improving their spinal posture, enhancing their quality of life and decreasing the likelihood of further curve progression. The findings from this study will increase public awareness on the influence of adolescents’ spinal posture on their mental health and wellbeing, provide further evidence for the need for better spinal posture, and substantiate evidence-based sEMG biofeedback posture training as an effective intervention in AIS, especially for individuals who have mild scoliosis and who are at high risk for curve progression.

14607519.label: Realisation of objectives
14607519.value: Throughout the course of the project, four major stages of research activities were conducted in realizing the project objectives, namely (i) a school screening programme to identify adolescents with trunk asymmetry, their health-related quality of life, and pattern of daily activities; (ii) a pilot study to examine the use of a surface electromyography (sEMG) biofeedback posture training programme in adolescents with mild scoliosis; (iii) an extended study to evaluate the benefits of the training programme with a larger sample size of both sexes; and (iv) in-depth interviews with adolescents to understand their subjective experience regarding the influence of the training programme. The school screening programme recruited a total of 1165 community-dwelling early adolescents with age between 10 to 14 years (at least 600 early adolescents stated in the proposal). Their trunk asymmetry was screened by our research team, and the result showed that 938 adolescents were normal while 227 adolescents were potential candidates for mild scoliosis. A total of 60 early adolescents having mild scoliosis as stated in the proposal were recruited to be randomly assigned to either the training group receiving 30-session biofeedback posture training or the control group without such training. Ten early adolescents dropped out during the whole project. To characterise the influence of poor spinal posture on health-related quality of life in community-dwelling early adolescents in Hong Kong (Objective 1), 200 early adolescents (52 male and 148 female) aged 10 to 14 recruited from the school screening programme were selected for comparison. Among them, 100 adolescents were considered to have trunk asymmetry with the angle of trunk rotation ≥ 5° and one or more physical signs on visual inspection. All early adolescents recruited from the school screen programme were invited to complete the Hong Kong version of the 36-item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36), which assessed their health-related quality of life. The results revealed that adolescents with trunk asymmetry had a lower health-related quality of life, compared with those without. In particular, except for physical functioning and role limitation due to physical health problems, statistically significant differences were found in all other scales, including bodily pain, general health, vitality (energy/fatigue), social functioning, role limitation due to emotional problems and mental health (Cheung et al., 2021). To investigate the risk factors in daily activities associated with poor spinal posture in community-dwelling early adolescents in Hong Kong (Objective 2), we have conducted three studies (Cheung et al., 2021; Cheung, Lai, & Yip, 2022; Cheung, Yip, & Cheung 2022) to investigate how daily activities affected the health-related quality of life of early adolescents and compared its effects between early adolescents with and without trunk asymmetry. The results showed that the average daily time spent using smartphones was significantly negatively associated with two scales in the physical domain and four scales in the mental domain of health-related quality of life of early adolescents, whereas the average daily time spent using computers was significantly negatively associated with two scales in the mental domain (p < 0.05). Moreover, a statistically significant association has been found between trunk asymmetry and the average daily duration of computer use. Specifically, early adolescents who used a computer for an average daily duration of less than 1 hour to over 4 hours were found to be 1.63 times more likely to have trunk asymmetry than those who did not use a computer. Moreover, computer use for more than four hours was only found among early adolescents with trunk asymmetry, accounting for around 16% of this group. To further identify abnormalities in paraspinal muscle activities in early adolescents with mild scoliosis and their association with risk factors in daily activities (Objective 3), a pilot study (Cheung, Yip, & Lai, 2022) was conducted with seven early adolescents from the school screening programme. The adolescents underwent a baseline sEMG measurement, during which the sEMG electrodes were placed onto their paraspinal muscles, namely, the trapezius, latissimus dorsi, thoracic erector spinae, and lumbar erector spinae, in pairs to determine the muscle activities along the spine in habitual sitting postures in terms of sEMG signals. The RMS sEMG ratio of each tested muscle pair of each adolescent was then calculated. While a ratio of 1 indicates that the tested muscle pair has relative symmetry in sEMG activity between the concave and convex sides, the results showed that the RMS sEMG ratios during baseline were significantly deviated from the ratio of 1 over the muscle pairs of the trapezius and lumbar erector spinae, suggesting a relative asymmetry of the paraspinal muscle activities in these two muscle pairs of the seven adolescents. The effectiveness of the 30-session sEMG biofeedback posture training programme on quality of life and posture parameters, symmetry of paraspinal muscle activities and curve progression among adolescents with mild scoliosis was then systematically evaluated (Objective 4). Following the baseline measurement, these seven adolescents received a 30-session sEMG biofeedback posture training programme developed by our research team, which was delivered in one to two sessions per week for approximately 6 months. During posture training, they were instructed to sit in an ideal recommended posture, maintain this posture, and relax the captioned four pairs of paraspinal muscles for 5 minutes. This posture training programme was administered five times in each session, with a 2-minute resting period between each time. The training was considered to be beneficial if the RMS sEMG ratio of the tested muscle pair was closer to 1 and significantly different from that at baseline. After receiving 30 tailor-made sessions of the training, they demonstrated more symmetrical paraspinal muscle activity over the trapezius and lumbar erector spinae muscle pairs. In two adolescents, the spinal curvature decreased by 5.7° and 5.6° respectively, while the remaining five adolescents exhibited a minimal curve progression over the thoracic and/or lumbar regions of under 5°. The findings from the quantitative study provided preliminary empirical evidence to support that sEMG biofeedback posture training can be used to attenuate asymmetry in paraspinal muscle activities among adolescents with mild scoliosis. As an extension, we conducted another study by recruiting more early adolescents of both sexes to evaluate the benefits of the 30-session sEMG biofeedback posture training in reducing spinal deformity or controlling curve progression and improving health-related quality of life. Twenty-six adolescents who received biofeedback posture training have maintained or improved their Cobb angle as assessed by X-ray. Six of them have great improvement: reduction in Cobb angle for > 5°. The improvement was maintained in the 6-month follow-up (Objective 5). The improvement was not shown in the control group. A qualitative study was also carried out to conduct in-depth interviews with 24 early adolescents as stated in the proposal (Cheung et al., 2023). Early adolescents aged between 11 and 13 years with mild scoliosis, who completed 30 sessions of training, acknowledged that the programme improved the physical and mental domains of their health-related quality of life, resulting in (a) posture correction, (b) an improvement in body appearance, (c) the restoration of muscle relaxation, (d) a reduction in bodily pain and fatigue, (e) the enhancement of self-confidence/self-image, and (f) an improvement in social functioning. Given its positive effects, the sEMG biofeedback posture training programme has the potential to be an alternative early intervention for early adolescents with mild scoliosis.

14607519.label: Major findings and research outcome
14607519.value: Our findings from the school screening programme (Cheung, Lai, & Yip, 2022; Cheung, Yip, & Cheung 2022) demonstrated that the average daily time spent using smartphones/computers was significantly negatively associated with health-related quality of life of early adolescents. Those with trunk asymmetry had a lower health-related quality of life than that of early adolescents without. Moreover, a statistically significant association has been found between trunk asymmetry and the average daily duration of computer use. Specifically, early adolescents who used a computer for an average daily duration of less than 1 hour to over 4 hours were found to be 1.63 times more likely to have trunk asymmetry than those who did not use a computer. Computer use for more than four hours was only found among early adolescents with trunk asymmetry, accounting for around 16% of the studied group (Cheung et al., 2021). Asymmetry in paraspinal muscle activities is observed in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), the most common type of poor posture. Therefore, posture training to improve the symmetry of paraspinal muscle activities may reduce the risk of curve progression of AIS. With this research hypothesis, our research team developed a 30-session surface electromyography (sEMG) biofeedback posture training programme as another line of early intervention for early adolescents with mild scoliosis. Results from quantitative (Cheung, Yip, & Lai, 2022) and qualitative (Cheung et al., 2023) studies demonstrated that the training programme reduced or controlled the Cobb angle of early adolescents with mild scoliosis over time, that is, a reduction in spinal curvature Cobb angle by at least 5°, or a minimal curve progression with changes in the Cobb angle controlled under 5°. In addition, the adolescents acknowledged that the sEMG biofeedback posture training programme improved their health-related quality of life, resulting in (a) posture correction, (b) an improvement in body appearance, (c) the restoration of muscle relaxation, (d) a reduction in bodily pain and fatigue, (e) the enhancement of self-confidence/self-image, and (f) an improvement in social functioning. According to the International Scientific Society on Scoliosis Orthopaedic and Rehabilitation Treatment 2005 consensus paper, quality of life, psychological well-being, back pain, and Cobb angle are included in the list of the most general goals of the conservative treatment of AIS. Our findings suggest that sEMG biofeedback posture training has the potential to achieve these goals for early adolescents with mild scoliosis, and to be an alternative early intervention for them.

14607519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14607519.value: To determine the training as an evidence-based clinical practice, further empirical studies are needed in exploring the predictors for positive training outcomes, substantiating its effectiveness, and evaluating the sustainability of its benefits over time. We hypothesize that using demographic and clinical data of the adolescents, such as age, height, weight, BMI, curve type, Cobb angle, as well as sEMG measures assessed at baseline in machine learning (ML) algorithms will provide effective and valid differentiation of responders from non-responders to the training. A quantitative research design will be implemented. A total of 60 adolescents with mild scoliosis will be recruited (n=50), for developing the trained model using ML approaches to provide outcome prediction of the training, and the validation group (n=10), to provide an unbiased evaluation of the trained model, respectively. With the development of a trained model that provides outcomes predictions for separating responders from non-responders to sEMG biofeedback posture training, medical/health professionals would be more capable to refer adolescents with mild scoliosis to the most appropriate intervention, enabling the latter to seize the prime time of puberty to improve their health and well-being.

14607519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14607519.value: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is characterized by uneven shoulders, back hump, and unlevel pelvis, with a prevalence of around 2% to 3%. Although most mild cases are non-progressive, the remaining adolescents are at risk of curve progression. These adolescents are suggested to have a significantly lower self-image and poorer daily function than their counterparts. Nevertheless, their choice of early intervention is relatively limited. Asymmetry in paraspinal muscle activities is observed in AIS and may be of value for predicting curve progression. With this hypothesis, our study developed a 30-session surface electromyography (sEMG) biofeedback posture training programme for early adolescents with mild scoliosis, and systemically evaluated its effectiveness. The results of our research project demonstrated that the training attenuated the asymmetry of paraspinal muscle activities, and reduced or controlled the Cobb angle of early adolescents with mild scoliosis over time. In addition, the adolescents acknowledged that it improved their health-related quality of life, resulting in posture correction, improvement in body appearance, restoration of muscle relaxation, reduction in bodily pain and fatigue, enhancement of self-confidence/self-image, and improvement in social functioning. Our findings suggest that the training programme has the potential to be an alternative early intervention for early adolescents with mild scoliosis.

14607619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14607619.value: Wu (吳語) is of great interest for phonological and phonetic investigations because it preserves an ancient feature of Middle Chinese that has already vanished in other Chinese languages – the voicing contrast of initial consonants. It also has a complex tonal inventory. The coexistence of voicing and tonal contrasts indicates that Wu is in a transitional stage of tonogenesis (voicing contrast being replaced by tonal difference). Investigating voicing and tone contrasts in Wu allows us to address historical sound change issues using contemporary data. The phonetic nature of the phonologically defined “voiced consonants” in Wu remains elusive since there are different realizations: as voiceless but breathy sounds in some Northern Wu varieties (e.g. Suzhou), but as truly voiced sounds in Southern Wu varieties (e.g. Wenzhou). The picture becomes even more complex when the voicing contrast is considered together with tonal registers since there is a consistent mapping between the two features. Interestingly, some tone pairs appear to be merging in Wenzhou Wu. Furthermore, the perceptual cues for the voicing and tonal register contrasts still remain largely unexplored. The present study aims to investigate the phonetic nature of voicing contrast and tonal registers of Wu comprehensively by examining the Southern (Wenzhou) and Northern (Suzhou) Wu varieties using both acoustic and articulatory measures. Second, it will explore the interaction between the voicing of initial consonants and tonal register in perception. Third, it will explore the on-going changes of the voicing contrast and related tonal changes by surveying different age groups. Fieldwork on-site with electroglottography (EGG) and acoustic recordings will be obtained at Wenzhou and Suzhou to investigate the articulatory and acoustic features of the voicing and tonal register contrasts and their interactions. Perceptual experiments with controlled acoustic parameters will be conducted to assess the perceptual cues that distinguish the two types of contrasts. This project not only will be the most comprehensive phonetic investigation of the voicing contrast and tonal register contrasts in Wu to date, documenting the unique linguistic features of Wu before they vanish like in other Chinese languages, but will also provide critical data to investigate the on-going sound change processes that can shed light on historical changes in voicing and tonogenesis in general. Finally, many young speakers can no long speak Wu with native proficiency due to strong Mandarin influence in recent years. This project can help document the Wu language for future generations. 吳語有别於其他漢語的典型特徵，在於它保留了中古漢語的清濁對立，此特徵對語音學及音系學的研究均具特殊價值。清濁對立及相應聲調陰陽對立並存之現狀，表明吳語可能正處於聲調起源的最終過渡階段，即輔音清濁對立正漸被聲調對立取代。因此，對吳語聲調及清濁對立的研究，可為我們提供以共時數據反映歷時音變之角度。吳語「濁輔音」之語音學性質十分複雜：在北部吳語例如蘇州話中，這些輔音實際上並不帶音，而是後接氣聲化元音；而在南部吳語例如溫州話中，它們則是帶音的真濁音。此外，吳語輔音的清濁對立，亦與聲調陰陽有對應關係：清輔音配陰調，濁輔音配陽調，但在溫州話中某些陰陽調類亦存在聲調合併的跡象。就語音感知而言，何者爲吳語聲調及清濁對立之感知提示特徵仍待研究。 本計劃首先旨在以聲學及發聲方法對吳語北部（蘇州）及南部（溫州）方言進行研究，以期實現對吳語聲調及清濁對立之語音學性質的全面考察。其次，本計劃將探究輔音清濁及聲調陰陽在語音感知中的互動關係。第三，本計劃將調查不同年齡段的母語者，以考察清濁對立及相應聲調中音變的關係。於溫州及蘇州進行的田野調查，將通過聲學方法及電子聲門儀，考察吳語此兩種方言的聲調及清濁對立之特徵及其互動關係。其後，通過以控制相關聲學參數設計的感知實驗，本計劃會研究此項音系對立的感知特徵。本計劃不僅是迄今關於吳語聲調及清濁對立最全面的語音學研究，以記錄吳語此一已不見於其他漢語的獨特特徵，還將為清濁對立的演變及聲調起源的一般性歷時音變提供重要的共時例證。最後，由於近年來普通話推廣的强大影響，不少年輕群體的吳語能力已無法達至母語水平，本研究可爲保育吳語盡一份力。

14607619.label: Realisation of objectives
14607619.value: The project started in a very challenging time, coinciding with the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic. Travel restrictions and social distancing measurements had made data collection extremely difficult. Despite these difficulties, great efforts were made to achieve the proposal objectives, and the project was extended to Kunshan Wu beyond the two Wu varieties mentioned in the original proposal. For the Suzhou part, the Co-I Prof Wentao Gu in Nanjing provided invaluable help in collecting the Suzhou production data. We also recruited one MA graduate (a native speaker of Suzhou Wu) from our department to assist in running the perception experiment online remotely in Suzhou. For the Kunshan and Wenzhou parts, the research assistant and PhD student working on the project went back to collect data braving rounds of quarantine. Despite the multiple challenges, we managed to achieve the objectives satisfactorily with good research outputs. For the first objective, although the voicing contrast with breathy voice in Wu Chinese is well-known, studies have concentrated on the prominent variety, Shanghainese. This project investigated three Wu varieties, including both Northern (Suzhou, Kunshan) and Southern Wu (Wenzhou). The scope of this project is beyond previous studies. Recent developments in the acoustic (VoiceSauce) and articulatory (Electroglottographic, EGG) measurements of voice quality enable us to describe the voicing contrast quantitatively and in more dimensions. For the three varieties investigated, both acoustic and articulatory (EGG) data were collected and meticulously analyzed. The descriptions have revealed important patterns which have not been reported before. In Suzhou Wu, both the acoustic data and articulatory measurements showed that low register tones are pronounced with breathy voice with greater spectral tilt measurements and stronger noise, which could be due to the larger glottal opening and slacker vocal folds. The older speakers also exhibited a gender difference, in that male speakers produced clearer breathy voice than female speakers (Ge et al. 2022). Moreover, it was found that T2 (yangping) is creaky voiced, especially for the younger female speakers, which is unexpected, since it has voiced initial consonants. This, however, is due to a recent ongoing sound change in Suzhou Wu (see discussion of the third objective below). The investigation of Suzhou disyllabic words showed that the intervocalic voiced initial consonants are not always truly voiced with negative VOT, but are realized with voicing extending from the previous vowel for most of the time (Ge & Mok 2023). For Kunshan Wu, it is found that the time course of breathy voice in low register tones can be preserved well beyond the later part of the target syllable, contrary to what was assumed (i.e., only the first half of the syllable) in earlier studies. Moreover, in disyllabic words, the domain of breathy voice can even appear in the second syllable in a prosodic word (Xu & Mok 2023). The investigation of Kunshan Wu also showed that children can still produce breathy voice related to low register tones (Xu et al. 2022). In Wenzhou Wu, a Southern variety, it is found that voiced initial consonants are still realized as truly voiced in isolation, in contrast to the Northern varieties. Moreover, the negative VOT does not seem to diminish for younger speakers. Data from both native Wenzhou words and English-lettered words in Wenzhou show that the distribution of true voicing seems to be mainly an effect of the phonetic environment, regardless of the existence of prosodic boundaries, and the realisation of vowel phonation contrast is dependent on the syllable’s position in the prosodic hierarchy (Zhang 2023; Zhang & Mok 2023). Taken together, the meticulous descriptions of the three Wu varieties have documented different stages of tones split, and also uncovered novel patterns which can only be found in a comprehensive and quantitative study. Because the perception-production link is closely related to the ongoing sound change in Wu Chinese, the realisation of the third objective will be presented before the second objective. To investigate any potential sound change in contemporary Wu, data from different age groups were collected for all the three varieties. For Kunshan, child data were also collected. With cross-sectional data, ongoing sound changes were indeed found in Suzhou and Wenzhou Wu. In Suzhou Wu, breathy voice is gradually disappearing in the younger speakers' production (Ge et al. 2023). This disappearance is influenced by another sound change in tone. T2 is changing from a rising tone to a falling-rising tone and the younger speakers produce T2 with strong creaky voice in the middle of the syllable. It accelerates the disappearance of breathy voice in T2. Therefore, Suzhou Wu is in the completion stage of tone split and breathy voice is going to disappear. These findings also suggest that after the transphonologization of the voicing contrast, the cues can change independently and also influence each other on a physiological basis. Another ongoing sound change is also found in Wenzhou Wu. In Wenzhou Wu, breathy voice is more prominent in the younger speaker's production and perception than the older speakers (Zhang 2023). Therefore, Wenzhou Wu is more likely to be in an earlier stage of tone split than Suzhou Wu. Taken together, this project also accomplished the goal of documenting potential sound changes in contemporary Wu Chinese. The thorough description using acoustic and articulatory measurements also shed light on the likely process and the mechanism of these sound changes, contribute to better understanding of the theory of sound change (see Ge et al. 2023, and Ge & Mok (revised)). Based on the documentation of the ongoing sound changes, the perceptual aspect of the voicing contrast (the second objective) was also investigated. The focus was on the sound change in Suzhou Wu, the disappearance of breathy voice in the production of the younger speakers. It is logical to ask whether the younger speakers can still employ the phonation cue in their perception, given that they do not produce it themselves. A comprehensive perception study was conducted to investigate the role of breathy voice in tone identification of the younger speakers as compared to the older and middle-aged speakers. The results showed that the younger speakers are still sensitive to breathy voice, yet the sensitivity is smaller than those of the older and middle-aged speakers. An interesting and novel finding is that the voice of the stimuli can also influence how listeners respond to the stimuli with breathy voice. The older voice can induce a larger effect in tone identification than the middle-aged voice. The findings have implications in how sound change is transmitted in the speech community and across generations. In Wenzhou Wu, the change on cue weighting between age groups found in the perception data was not completely synchronous with the change in production. The voicing/tone register contrast with various phonetic realisations in production between syllables with different types of onsets and between different age groups of speakers may also have various perceptual cues in these conditions. The perception pattern can be the source of change in production, and the change in specific features in production can possibly influence the perceptual cue weighting of some other unchanged features as well. The introduction of an additional contrasting feature in production may also accelerate the loss of perceptual importance of the merging feature in perception.

14607619.label: Major findings and research outcome
14607619.value: The project investigated three Wu Chinese varieties, Suzhou and Kunshan (Northern) and Wenzhou (Southern). The main findings are twofold. Synchronically, the phonetic realizations of the voicing contrast in Wu Chinese have been comprehensively described and several significant characteristics were reported. Suzhou Wu is at the completion stage of tone split and even the intervocalic voiced initial consonants are rarely realised with negative VOT (Ge & Mok 2023), while true voicing is still found in Wenzhou Wu, even in the production of younger speakers (Zhang & Mok 2023). Breathy voice is found in all three varieties yet with some variations. In Suzhou Wu, breathy voice is gradually disappearing in the younger speaker's production, and in Wenzhou Wu, breathy voice is produced more clearly by the younger speakers. Kunshan Wu seems to be in an intermediate stage between the two, in which children can still produce breathy voice. Moreover, breathy voice is found to persist to the second syllable of disyllabic words in Kunshan Wu (Xu & Mok 2023), demonstrating that the domain of breathiness can be the prosodic word instead of just the initial syllable. Diachronically, ongoing sound changes in Wu Chinese were also documented and investigated in both production and perception. Using data from three different age groups, it is discovered that breathy voice in Suzhou Wu is gradually disappearing in the younger speakers' production. There are further tone changes in T2 and T8, both of which are changing from rising to falling-rising in pitch contour. Furthermore, the tone change in T2 also influences the disappearance of breathy voice (Ge et al. 2023). However, the younger listeners are still able to make use of the phonation cue in identifying the low register tones, while the effect of breathy voice is decreasing for the younger listeners as compared to the older and middle-aged listeners (Ge & Mok revised). Sound change has also been found in Wenzhou Wu, in which the younger speakers rely more on breathy voice than older speakers in both production and perception. The comparison between the seemingly contradictory patterns between Suzhou Wu and Wenzhou Wu illustrates the two varieties are at different stages after tone split in tonogenesis. Our findings can shed new light on the theories of tonogenesis and sound change in general. These findings were disseminated in a prominent international journal (Journal of Phonetics) and conferences (Speech Prosody, International Congress of Phonetic Sciences, etc).

14607619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
14607619.value: This project has revealed some ongoing changes regarding tone and phonation in Wu Chinese. Further studies can be conducted along two lines. Firstly, sound change is transimitted from generation to generation. Given the presence of ongoing sound changes in the speech community, how do children acquire the sound system (preliminarily investigated in our Kunshan part)? Do they increment the sound change towards the direction in their parents’ patterns? An acquisition study can be conducted to answer these questions. It can reveal the actual progress of the transmission of sound change across generations and also corroborate the predictions based on some theories of sound change. The second question concerns the universality of the findings of this project. Tonogenesis and tone split are prevalantly found in East and Southeast Asian languages. Does an intermediate stage of phonation always appear in these sound changes? In those languages where voiced obstruents do induce breathy voice, would breathy voice eventually disappear? A large-scale typological study can be conducted to answer these questions and it will further our understandings of both the phonetic motivation and the phonological constraints of tonogenesis.

14607619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
14607619.value: Language is an ever-changing system, and the change in one sub-system can be closely related to another sub-system. This project looked into the inter-connections between three such sub-systems, voicing in onset consonants, phonation type on the following vowel, and tone in three Wu Chinese varieties given their unique contemporary retention of the voicing contrast in Middle Chinese. Previous studies have shown that onset consonants and vowel phonation type can have profound influence on the evolution of tone in Chinese and other languages, and this project showed that the development of tone can also have critical influence on vowel phonation type and onset consonants, a perspective not shown in previous studies. Moreover, speaking and hearing, as two fundamental activities in speech communication, both play fundamental roles in the changes investigated in this project. The patterns in the three Wu varieties demonstrate different stages of the same sound change. This project revealed subtle details of sound changes in Wu Chinese, which can contribute greatly to our understanding of the mechanisms of language change in general.

14607819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
14607819.value: Hong Kong, as one of the most-developed economies in the world, is facing one of the greatest income inequality. The link between poverty and poor health has been well-established in previous studies. However, most of these studies were cross-sectional, which may overestimate the association due to failure to control for potential confounders and possibility of reverse causality. Research is especially lacking on the long-term, longitudinal association of deprivation, in addition to income poverty, with general health. Accumulating evidence has shown that deprivation is a better measure of poverty, and that changes in deprivation level may be more strongly associated with health in long-term than changes in income level. However, no studies have ever investigated this longitudinal relationship in the context of Hong Kong. This proposed study will be a continuation of the previously funded project “Trends and Implications of Poverty and Social Disadvantages in Hong Kong: A Multi-disciplinary and Longitudinal Study,” from which we aim to extend the data collection process and conduct an additional survey as the third time point of the study. In addition to cross-sectional associations between poverty and health, the analysis will focus on the longitudinal association between changes in poverty and health. We will apply the multidimensional concept of poverty to our study, and use deprivation, in addition to income poverty, to measure poverty. We would examine if changes in deprivation will be a stronger predictor of health outcomes than changes in income poverty. This study will be the first prospective study in Hong Kong to be able to assess the temporal association between deprivation and health over a long period of time, which may help generate evidence for designing policies and interventions to improve health of socially-deprived groups and tackle health inequality in Hong Kong. 香港作為世界上最發達的經濟體之一，正面對著最嚴峻的收入不平等問題。過往已有充分的研究確認貧窮與健康狀況欠佳的聯繫。不過，這些研究大部分都屬橫斷面研究，或會因沒有調整干擾因素和反向因果關係，而高估了關係的強度。現時除了欠缺入息貧窮和健康關係的長期及縱向性研究，還缺乏針對匱乏和健康關係的長期及縱向性研究。有越來越多的證據顯示，匱乏更能反映貧窮情況，而相比起收入水平的變化，匱乏程度的變化與長期的健康狀況有更強的關係。可是，暫時還未有以香港作背景的研究去探討這個縱向性關係。 這項擬議的研究是之前獲資助名為《香港貧窮與社會弱勢的趨勢-跨學科及縱向研究》的延伸，我們將會延長數據收集過程，額外收集多一次問卷調查，作為研究的第三個時間點。今次的研究除了探討貧窮與健康的橫向聯繫外，還會著重分析貧窮情況的變化與健康狀況的縱向聯繫。我們的研究將應用多維度的貧窮概念，以入息貧窮和匱乏衡量貧窮情況。 我們亦會測試匱乏程度的變化是否一個比入息貧窮的變化更強對應健康狀況的預測因子。 這將會是香港第一個評估匱乏與健康狀況之間的時間性關聯的前瞻性縱向研究，研究結果可協助設計改善社會貧困群體健康狀況的政策和干預措施，並有助解決香港的健康不平等問題。
