15102219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15102219.value: Abdominal cancers are a major cause of cancer-related deaths in Hong Kong and worldwide. For example, liver and pancreatic cancers are the third and fourth leading causes of cancer-related deaths, respectively, in Hong Kong. The role of radiotherapy in the treatment of abdominal cancers is limited because of radiation toxicity to the surrounding healthy tissues. Current radiotherapy treatment planning (TP) technique is based on computed tomography (CT). However, soft-tissue contrast in CT images is often very limited for visualizing tumour/organs, particularly in the abdomen. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides excellent soft-tissue contrast and allows better visualisation and direct tracking of tumour/organs. Therefore, it is highly desirable to develop MRI-based TP (MRI-TP) techniques to improve dose conformity for abdominal cancers. Despite many advances, the clinical routine use of MRI-TP is still in its infancy due to unsolved problems. In this proposed project, we will address a fundamental problem in current MRI-TP techniques: lack of a systematic and efficient methodology to performing various MRI-TP tasks, including organ/tumour segmentation, synthetic CT generation, and four-dimensional MRI (4D-MRI). As a result, current MRI-TP techniques based on isolated uses of MR images are inefficient and ineffective, potentially leading to inconsistent and suboptimal outcomes. Magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is a recent breakthrough in MRI technology. Unlike conventional MRI, MRF allows for the simultaneous quantification of multiple tissue properties (T1, T2, proton-density, etc.) in a single, time-efficient acquisition. MRF has great potential to significantly improve the accuracy and work efficiency of TP for abdominal cancers, as compared to CT and conventional MRI. Our long-term goal is to develop and clinically implement a MRF-based TP (MRF-TP) technology to improve the radiotherapeutic management of cancers. The objective of the project outlined in this application is to develop a preliminary MRF-TP framework for radiotherapy for abdominal cancers. The proposed research will be innovative on several levels. It will develop multiple novel MRF-based techniques for radiotherapy applications (MRF-based segmentation, MRF-based synthetic CT, and 4D-MRF) by synergising a collection of novel MR imaging and data analytics techniques. The MRF-TP technique can increase dose conformity by reducing uncertainties in imaging and human interpretation and improve work efficiency by using a single MRF acquisition to perform multiple TP tasks, ultimately improving the local control and increasing the survival rate of abdominal cancer patients. 腹部癌症是香港和全世界癌症相關死亡的主要原因。例如，肝癌和胰腺癌分別是香港癌症相關死亡的第三和第四大原因。由於對周圍健康組織的輻射毒性，放射療法在治療腹部癌症中的作用是有限的。目前的放射治療計劃（TP）技術基於計算機斷層掃描（CT）。然而，CT圖像中的軟組織對比度通常非常有限，特別是在腹部。磁共振成像（MRI）提供出色的軟組織對比度，允許更好的可視化和腫瘤/器官跟踪。因此，開發基於MRI的TP（MRI-TP）技術以改善腹部癌症放射治療 是非常需要的。儘管取得了許多進展，MRI-TP的臨床常規使用仍處於初期階段。在這個項目中，我們將解決當前MRI-TP技術的一個基本問題：缺乏系統和有效的方法來執行各種MRI-TP任務，包括器官/腫瘤分割，合成CT生成和四維MRI（4D-MRI）。當前MRI-TP技術效率低且無效，可能導致不一致和次優結果。磁共振指紋（MRF）是MRI技術的最新突破。與傳統MRI不同，MRF允許在單次採集中同時高效獲得多種組織特性（T1，T2，質子密度，等）。與CT和常規MRI相比，MRF具有顯著提高TP對腹部癌症的準確性和工作效率的巨大潛力。我們的長期目標是開發和臨床實施基於MRF的TP（MRF-TP）技術，以改善癌症的放射治療。本項目的目標是開髮用於腹部癌症的放射治療的MRF-TP初步框架。擬議的研究將在幾個層面上進行創新。它將通過協同一系列新的MR成像和數據分析技術，開發多種基於MRF的新技術，用於放射治療應用（基於MRF的分割，基於MRF的合成CT和4D-MRF）。 MRF-TP技術可以通過減少成像和人工解釋的不確定性來提高劑量一致性，並通過使用單個MRF採集來執行多個TP任務來提高工作效率，最終改善局部控制並提高腹部癌症患者的存活率。

15102219.label: Realisation of objectives
15102219.value: We have largely achieved all objectives without major hurdles. As MRF is a very new technique, especially in the area of radiotherapy in terms of application, our developments of multiple MRF-based techniques are all considered novel and world-leading. In particular, the 4D-MRF technique is the first and best, as demonstrated by journal publications and recognitions. One key limitation so far is the limited number of patients enrolled in the study, which is probably already the largest patient cohort of abdominal MRF in the world, is insufficient for deep learning model development which typically requires a very large sample size. To address this issue, we have investigated the transfer learning strategy for deep learning training with a small sample size. Another issue that we identified as the project evolves in the past a few years is that some techniques as proposed in this application, such as synthetic CT and segmentation, have advanced significantly due to the enormous interest in these topics by researchers as AI emerged as a super powerful tool for medical image applications. Consequently, in the later stage of this project we have focused more on true MRF developments (such as 4D-MRF) than the AI-focused developments (such as segmentation and synthetic CT).

15102219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15102219.value: We developed a coarse-to-refinement architecture for abdominal segmentation. It contains: (1) an automatic deep fusion learning network as a coarse segmentation strategy; (2) a modified automatic searching polygon tracking method; (3) an explainable mathematical map function. We first trained the model on a large dataset (>100) of trans-abdominal ultrasound patients and then on the small dataset of MRF through transfer learning. Our proposed method achieved DSC of 93.5%. We demonstrated a novel time-resolved MRF (TR-MRF) technique capable of imaging respiratory motions and investigated the TR-MRF technique using three different acquisition methods: (1) continuous acquisition without delay between MRF repetitions; (2) continuous acquisition with 5s delay between MRF repetitions; and (3) triggered acquisition with variable delay between MRF repetitions to allow the next acquisition to start at different respiration phase. We found that the triggered method showed better performance than the other two methods. We further improved TR-MRF by developing a respiratory-correlated (RC) 4D-MRF (RC-4DMRF). RC-4DMRF has a high agreement with Cine-MRI in tumor motion measurement, achieving an average Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.96 ± 0.05 and 0.91 ± 0.09 in the superior-inferior (SI) direction and anterior-posterior (AP) direction. The average amplitude motion difference between RC-4DMRF and Cine-MRI is 1.27±0.94 mm (SI) and 0.78±0.62 mm (AP). RC-4DMRF achieved high accuracy in tissue properties quantification (T1, T2, proton density), with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 8.8%, 9.6%, and 5.0%. We built a deep learning model based on a multi-channel multi-path generative adversarial network for generating synthetic-CT (sCT) from MRF using digital phantoms and real patient. An adapted model using transfer learning were trained to finetune the model from patient data. The fine-tuned model showed excellent results with mean MAE of 36.40±7.93 HU, RMSE of 82.83±19.39 HU, PSNR of 27.80±2.00 and SSIM of 0.80 ± 0.046. We conducted a dosimetry study to investigate the sCT for RT treatment planning on tumour patients. Original RT plan calculated on planning CT were recalculated on resampled sCT using Eclipse. Dosimetric agreements were assessed in terms of dose-volume-histogram (DVH) for target and organ-at-risk (OAR), and 3D gamma analysis. In target coverage, 0.33% deviation were observed in V100% isodose level (p=0.02), while no significant different were identified in other DVH metrics in all sample. Most OAR did not have significant differences after recalculation. Gamma passing rates were all > 96.5%. This study validated the sCT for clinical use with promising dosimetric agreement with planning CT.

15102219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15102219.value: There are future developments to improve the performance of RC-4DMRF. First, the current inter-phase motion calculation is time-consuming and susceptible to the image quality of the motion reference images. Though the pyramid motion compensation could mitigate the under-sampling artifact of the motion reference images, some inherent artifacts caused by the under-sampling trajectory may not be fully eliminated. Considering that MRF follows the consistent k-space trajectory readout, deep learning-based contrast-invariant registration may potentially to improve the accuracy of motion compensation. Second, a slight contrast variation could still be observed in the coronal and transverse planes of PD maps (shown as dark lines), which could be explained by the slice-wise normalization variation induced in the PD calculation. An efficient 3D MRF acquisition sequence could solve this problem in the future. Third, a more comprehensive clinical evaluation of RC-4DMRF is warranted. For example, the internal target volume (ITV) determination is a key step in motion management and treatment planning. The ITVs generated from RC-4DMRF need to be evaluated for its accuracy and with comparison to those generated from 4DCT and 4DMRI. In addition, dosimetric study is desired for evaluating the clinical benefits of RC-4DMRF in tumor control and normal liver tissues sparing.

15102219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15102219.value: Abdominal cancers are a major cause of cancer-related deaths in Hong Kong and worldwide. For example, liver and pancreatic cancers are the third and fourth leading causes of cancer-related deaths, respectively, in Hong Kong. The role of radiotherapy in the treatment of abdominal cancers is limited because of radiation toxicity to the surrounding healthy tissues. Current radiotherapy technique is based on computed tomography (CT) imaging. However, soft-tissue contrast in CT images is often very limited for visualizing tumour/organs, particularly in the abdomen. In this research, we developed multiple novel techniques for abdominal cancer radiotherapy based on a magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) which has excellent image quality in the abdomen. Our technique can improve the accuracy of radiotherapy delivery to the tumour by reducing errors in imaging and treatment planning, and improve clinical work efficiency by using a single MRF acquisition to perform multiple radiotherapy treatment planning tasks. Ultimately, our techniques can improve the management and increase the survival rate of abdominal cancer patients.

15103819.label: Project Objectives
15103819.value: Biochemical and structural characterization of the Rubicon-UVRAG interaction mediated by the Rubicon central coiled coil domain The Rubicon-UVRAG interaction is mediated by the Rubicon central coiled coil domain but the UVRAG regions involved are not known. We will carry out in vitro ITC and in vivo Co-IP studies to map Rubicon-binding regions in UVRAG. Our preliminary data has confirmed that the very C-terminal end of UVRAG termed the Uniq-C region, but not its coiled coil domain, is essential for Rubicon binding. Structure determination of the Rubicon-UVRAG complex involving the key domains will be carried out as well. Biochemical and structural characterization of the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction mediated by the Rubicon C-terminal RH domain The Rubicon Homology (RH) domain is responsible for specific interaction with GTP-bound Rab7. It contains a helix coils (HC) portion with unknown function followed by a cysteine-rich (CR) region with putative lipid binding activity. We plan to investigate the individual roles of HC and CR in Rab7 interaction by in vitro ITC and in vivo Co-IP. Our initial study shows that HC-derived peptides bind to Rab7 but CR region binds neither lipid nor Rab7. Structural characterization of Rab7 in complex with either HC-derived peptide or the whole RH domain will be tried by both NMR and x-ray crystallography. Structure-based functional characterization to elucidate how the Rubicon-UVRAG interaction promotes LC3-associated phagocytosis Using the biochemical and structural findings of Objective 1 as guidance, we will generate Rubicon mutants with weakened or abolished interaction with UVRAG. The impact of these mutations on Rubicon-mediated LC3-associated phagocytosis will be investigated by transfecting the mutants into RAW macrophage cells and then tracking zymosan-induced LC3-associated phagocytosis by standard assays. Structure-based mutational studies to delineate how the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction inhibits autophagy and endocytic trafficking Biochemical and structural characterization of the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction in Objective 2 have confirmed direct physical interaction between Rab7 and HC-derived peptides. Based on such information, we will generate a series of Rubicon mutants with key hydrophobic residues in HC region perturbed to reduce the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction. The effect of these mutations on relieving the Rubicon-mediated inhibitory effect on autophagy and endocytic trafficking will be investigated by cell-based standard assays.

15103819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15103819.value: 细胞自噬是一种分解代谢过程，通过将胞浆内容物包装到被称为自噬体的双膜囊泡内，再将自噬体转运至溶酶体进行降解和再循环。近期研究已显示自噬在多个重要细胞过程扮演关键角色，而自噬的功能缺失与糖尿病、癌症、神经退化性病变和衰老等多种疾病紧密相关。 LC3相关的吞噬过程（LAP）是一种新发现的特殊形式的吞噬过程。其独特之处在于所形成的单膜结构的吞噬体上富含LC3-II蛋白，而LC3-II一直以来被认为是双膜自噬体的特征标记。 LAP是吞噬和清除入侵微生物和垂死细胞的关键机制，因此与宿主免疫功能紧密相关。 自噬和LAP是两种截然不同但广泛交叉的细胞内膜转运途径。两个在自噬过程中扮演关键角色的分子机器，包括负责生产PI3P的Beclin1-Vps34复合物和用于LC3脂化的Atg5-Atg7-Atg12系统，已被证实对LAP也是必需的。 Rubicon是针对含有UVRAG的Beclin1-Vps34复合物的二级调控因子。它是一个超过1000个残基的大分子蛋白，可以与多个蛋白相互作用，如UVRAG，Rab7和NOX2模块中的p22phox。有趣的是，Rubicon在自噬和LAP中发挥着不同的作用。对自噬过程而言，Rubicon极大可能是一个非必需的负向调节因子。但是在LAP过程中，Rubicon对于LC3相关的吞噬体（LAPosomes）的生成和产生活性氧物质的NOX2模块的稳定化，却起着不可或缺的作用。 我们的假设是Rubicon通过与UVRAG和Rab7结合，形成两个生化和结构上可分离的Rubicon-UVRAG和Rubicon-Rab7相互作用，从而协调Rubicon在自噬和LAP过程中的不同作用。具体而言，我们推测Rubicon-UVRAG的相互作用通过在LAPosomes上维持含UVRAG的Beclin1-Vps34复合物II，从而促进PI3P的持续产生，对LAP发挥正面调控作用。另一方面，Rubicon-Rab7的相互作用通过锁定Rab7而阻止其参与内膜体成熟和内膜体-溶酶体融合过程，从而对自噬和内膜转运过程产生负面影响。 我们将对Rubicon-UVRAG和Rubicon-Rab7这两个蛋白相互作用进行全面的生化和结构研究，以证实我们的假设。首先我们将以生化手段界定UVRAG和Rubicon涉及其相互作用的关键功能域。然后通过一系列实验手段解析两个复合物结构，包括由Rubicon中心卷曲螺旋结构域介导的Rubicon-UVRAG结构和由Rubicon的HC片段介导的Rubicon-Rab7结构。我们还将进行基于细胞的功能研究，以确认我们的结构发现。本项目的研究结果不仅能扩展我们对自噬的认识，还将提供对LC3相关的吞噬过程的新见解，有助于我们深入了解宿主免疫这个至关重要的过程。

15103819.label: Realisation of objectives
15103819.value: Objective 1: Rubicon specifically associates with PI3KC3-C2 to exert inhibitory effect on autophagy. However, the molecular mechanism of how Rubicon selectively binds to PI3KC3-C2 but not the PI3KC3-C1 is not known. We first hypothesized that Rubicon might interact with UVRAG, the unique member of PI3KC3-C2, through their respective coiled coil (CC) domains. However, our Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC) data shows that CC domains of Rubicon and UVRAG only had weak endothermic interaction that is unlikely to be detected in vivo. We then proceeded to characterize whether the N-terminal RUN domain of Rubicon would play a role in mediating the Rubicon-UVRAG interaction. The RUN domain is an evolutionarily conserved structural module that commonly binds to small Ras-like GTPases like Rab and Rap. A recent study by Tremel et. al. (Nat. Comm. 2021) showed that Rab5 specifically recruited PI3KC3-C2 to membranes and activated its lipid kinase activity. Inspired by this study, we developed our second hypothesis that the RUN domain of Rubicon might bind to Rab5. This Rubicon-Rab5 interaction may compete against the interaction between Rab5 and PI3KC3-C2, thus causing inhibitory effect on the autophagy process mediated by PI3KC3-C2. We purify the Rubicon RUN domain and tested its binding to Rab5 by in vitro pull-down assay and NMR titration studies. Our data shows that the Rubicon RUN domain readily pulled down Rab5, including both wild-type form as well as mutant forms that are constitutively active (Rab5-CA) or dominantly negative (Rab5-DN). The binding interface between the Rubicon RUN domain and Rab5 were mapped out by mutational studies in vitro and validated by co-IP experiments in vivo. Furthermore, we did similar studies for Rab7, another GTPase intimately involved in PI3KC3-mediated processes including endolysosomal trafficking. Our results revealed that Rubicon RUN domain could bind to Rab7 in similar manner as Rab5. In summary, Objective 1 is 100% accomplished with our initial hypothesis of direct Rubicon-UVRAG interaction mediated by their respective CC domains ruled out. Instead, our study reveals that the N-terminal RUN domain of Rubicon binds to both Rab5 and Rab7, two GTPases prominently involved in endolysosomal trafficking process. Notably, Rab5 has been reported to specifically associate with PI3KC3-C2 to activate its lipid kinase activity. Our study suggests that Rubicon may be tethered to PI3KC3-C2 through Rab5. Additionally, Rubicon may exert inhibitory effect by competitively sequestering Rab5 away from PI3KC3-C2. Objective 2: The C-terminal Rubicon Homology (RH) domain contains an N-terminal portion with predicted helix coils (HC) and a C-terminal cysteine-rich (CR) part. Previous studies have reported that the RH domain in Rubicon binds to Rab7 but the exact binding site is not known. To delineate the molecular determinants of the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction, we first focused on the CR part within the RH domain because this region belongs to the RING/ FYVE/PHD zinc finger superfamily that is known to bind to PI3Ps, the type of lipids particularly enriched on autophagosomes and early endosomes. However, our data from in vitro liposome-binding assay suggested that this CR region had little or no lipid binding activity. Additionally, our NMR study of 15N-labeled CR construct showed that this region was poorly folded by itself. To overcome this problem, we expressed and purified the entire RH domain and confirmed that it is well folded by NMR study. We also conducted in vitro pull-down assay and in vivo co-IP experiments to confirm that the RH domain binds to Rab7 specifically but not Rab5. Using mutational scanning coupled with NMR titration studies, we also mapped residues within the RH domain of Rubicon and the switch II region of Rab7 that are critical for their interaction. In summary, Objective 2 is 100% accomplished. We have conducted biochemical and structural studies of the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction by focusing on the entire RH domain. Our data shows that the FYVE-like CR region within the RH domain has no obvious lipid binding activity and does not interact with Rab7 directly. Instead, the whole RH domain, especially the HC region, is required for effective Rab7 binding. Notably, our biochemical and structural study of the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction is validated by the crystal structure of this complex reported during our study. Objective 3: Rubicon has been reported to be a positive regulator of LC3-associated phagocytosis (LAP) both in terms of recruiting the UVRAG-containing PI3KC3-C2 to early-stage LC3-associated phagosomes (LAPosomes) for sustained PI3P production and in facilitating the downstream translocation of LC3-II to mature LAPosomes. However, the molecular mechanism of how Rubicon mediates the LAP process through its binding partners is not known. Our biochemical and structural studies in Objectives 1 and 2 have shown that while Rubicon does not have direct binding to as initially hypothesized, Rubicon does bind to both Rab5 and Rab7, two GTPases that are enriched in early- and late-stage endosomes respectively. Specifically, the N-terminal RUN domain of Rubicon binds to both Rab5 and Rab7 while the C-terminal RH domain binds selectively to Rab7 but not Rab5. Guided by these findings, we carried out cell-based functional studies to investigate whether the Rubicon-Rab5/7 interaction would affect the LAP process. The standard assay to measure LAP activity is to track the rapid phagocytosis of fluorophore-labeled zymosan beads in RAW264.7 macrophage cells. Our studies reveal that mutations in the C-terminal RH domain that weaken or abolish Rab7 binding significantly reduced LAP in RAW264.7 cells. We also tracked the co-localization of zymosan beads with LC3-II and ROS production and observed similar effect. In summary, Objective 3 is 100% accomplished. We have confirmed that the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction mediated through the C-terminal RH domain plays a critical role in promoting LAP, probably by acting as a Rab7 effector to promote eventual fusion with lysosomes. Objective 4: Rubicon has been reported to exert inhibitory effect on both autophagy and endocytic trafficking through its selective association with PI3KC3-C2. While previous studies suggested that Rubicon may interact with UVRAG, the unique member of PI3KC3-C2, to exert selective inhibitory effect on PI3KC3-C2, our biochemical and structural studies in Objective 1 have ruled out this possibility. Instead, our studies in Objectives 1 and 2 have shown that Rubicon binds to both Rab5 and Rab7 as mediated by the N-terminal RUN domain and the C-terminal RH domain. Additionally, our study in Objective 3 confirmed that the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction mediated by the C-terminal RH domain is most critical for the LAP process by promoting the recruitment of LC3 and ROS to LAPosomes. Building upon these findings, we proceed to investigate how the Rubicon-Rab5/7 interaction would affect autophagy and endocytic trafficking. Cellular autophagy was monitored by standard autophagy assays including imaging studies of autophagosome puncta in HeLa cells and western blot of autophagy markers LC3 and p62 in HEK293 cells. The endocytic trafficking process was monitored by tracking the degradation of EGFR in HEK293 cells. Our studies reveal that, while transient over-expression of wild-type Rubicon in HEK293 cells led to reduced autophagy and slower EGFR degradation, over-expression of Rubicon RUN domain mutants that lost Rab5/7 binding failed to exert such inhibitory effect. In summary, Objective 4 is 100% accomplished. We have confirmed that the Rubicon-Rab5 interaction mediated through the N-terminal RUN domain exerts inhibitory effect on autophagy, possibly by sequestering Rab5 from PI3KC3-C2.

15103819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15103819.value: Our biochemical and structural studies have uncovered novel insight on how Rubicon associates with Rab5 and Rab7, two GTPases prominently involved in the endomembrane network and how the Rubicon-Rab5/Rab7 interactions regulate PI3KC3-mediated processes including autophagy, endocytic trafficking and LC3-associated phagocytosis. Firstly, our study showed that the selective binding of Rubicon to PI3KC3-C2 is not mediated by UVRAG, the unique member of PI3KC3-C2. Instead, the N-terminal RUN domain of Rubicon binds to Rab5, which also specifically associates with PI3KC3-C2. Thus, Rubicon may be tethered to PI3KC3-C2 through Rab5. Additionally, Rubicon may sequester Rab5 from PI3KC3-C2 to inhibit autophagy. Secondly, our study also showed that the C-terminal RH domain of Rubicon selectively binds to Rab7 but not Rab5. This Rubicon-Rab7 interaction is important for LC3-mediated phagocytosis by allowing Rubicon to serve as Rab7 effector to promote downstream events including LC3 recruitment and ROS production. Manuscripts reporting these findings are under preparation and will be submitted to relevant journals shortly. Additionally, our team also continued with our exploration to design Beclin 1-targeting stapled peptides as novel autophagy modulators. In our previous studies, we developed stapled peptides that specifically bind to the coiled coil domain of Beclin 1 to induce autophagy and inhibit proliferation of cancer cells. During this project, we carried out cell-based studies to confirm that our designed peptides exerted potent anti-proliferative effect by inducing autosis, an autophagy-dependent necrotic cell death program (Part C, journal papers #1-5). Additionally, our designed peptides also showed promising anti-tumor effect in animal models and synergized with existing cancer therapeutics to overcome drug resistance (Part C, journal papers #1-5). We also obtained patents for our designed peptides in US and China (Part C, other impact #1-2). Our work of these designed peptides was also awarded Gold Medal at the 49th International Exhibition of Inventions Geneva, 2024 (Part C, other impact #3). Furthermore, our lab also carried out structural studies of Beclin 2, a mammalian homolog of Beclin 1 and demonstrated that the potent Beclin 2-Atg14L interaction mediated by their respective coiled coil domains regulates the endolysosomal degradation of GASP1-associated GPCRs (Part C, journal paper #6). Overall, this project has been successfully completed with output including journal papers, patents and awards.

15103819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15103819.value: Autophagy, endocytic trafficking and LC3-associated phagocytosis are endomembrane-mediated trafficking processes that share the same destination of lysosomes. Additionally, they also share certain molecular machineries such as the PI3KC3 complex for PI3P production, the HOPS complex for endocytic trafficking and SNARE proteins for lysosomal fusion. While our studies of the Rubicon-Rab5/Rab7 interactions have delineated the molecular mechanism of how Rubicon exerts dual-natured role in autophagy and LAP through its Rab5-binding RUN domain and the Rab7-binding RH domain respectively, it does lead us to wonder how these distinct interactions are integrated within Rubicon. For future studies to investigate such integration, we would need to generate Rubicon mutants that functionally separate the Rubicon-Rab5 and Rubicon-Rab7 interactions. Specifically, we hope to identify mutations in the RUN domain only would only abolish the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction. We also hope to identify residues in the RUN domain and the RH domain that, when mutated together, would abolish the Rubicon-Rab7 interaction entirely without affecting Rab5 binding. These separation-of-function mutants would allow us to assess how Rubicon exerts distinct roles in coordinated manner for PI3KC3-mediated processes including autophagy, endocytic trafficking and LC3-associated phagocytosis.

15103819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15103819.value: The mammalian Class III phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase Complex (PI3KC3) is an essential molecular machinery for multiple endomembrane-mediated cellular processes including autophagy, endolysosomal trafficking and LC3-mediated phagocytosis. PI3KC3 exists in two biochemically and functionally distinct subcomplexes as defined by the invariable core unit of Vps34-Vp15- Beclin 1 in association with two mutually exclusive primary modulators Atg14L and UVRAG to form the Atg14L-containing Complex I (PI3KC3-C1) and the UVRAG-containing Complex II (PI3KC3-C2). Rubicon (RUN domain Beclin-1-interacting cysteine-rich-containing) is a secondary modulator of PI3KC3 and specifically associate with PI3KC3-C2 but not PI3KC3-C1. Our studies reveal that the N-terminal RUN domain of Rubicon binds to both Rab5 and Rab7. This Rubicon-Rab5 interaction permits Rubicon to inhibit autophagy and endocytic trafficking by sequestering Rab5 from PI3KC3-C2. Our studies also reveal that the C-terminal RH domain of Rubicon specifically binds to Rab7 but not Rab5. This Rubicon-Rab7 interaction promotes LC3-associated phagocytosis AP process by recruiting LC3 and machineries for ROS production. Overall, this project has delineated the molecular mechanism of how Rubicon exerts dual-natured regulatory role in PI3KC3-mediated processes including autophagy, endocytic trafficking and LC3-associated phagocytosis. Our findings offer novel insights on how to target Rubicon to tackle PI3KC3-implicated diseases such as cancer and bacterial infection.

15104019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104019.value: Depressive disorders are the first leading cause of disability worldwide. There remain significant limitations of current antidepressant treatment, including delayed therapeutic effect, drug-resistance and high remission rates. Non-pharmacological strategies such as exercise interventions that can enhance stress resilience and may critically reduce the incidence rate of depression. Moreover, clinical studies indicate that maternal exercise during pregnancy has beneficial effects on the developing infant’s brain. Animal studies have shown that the offspring of exercised mothers during pregnancy (maternal exercise) display improved learning and memory and decreased anxiety/depressive behaviours. This may be due to increases in adult neurogenesis, brain derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and neuronal activity in the hippocampus of the offspring, although the role of these potential mechanisms has yet to be evaluated. Our previous studies have shown that an enhancement in hippocampal neuroplasticity contributes to the antidepressant and pro-cognitive effects of physical exercise in animal models. Our pilot data have demonstrated that maternal exercise promotes learning and memory, reduces depression-like behaviour and enhances adult hippocampal neurogenesis in offspring. Impaired hippocampal neuroplasticity depending on epigenetic regulation of brain enriched microRNA-124 in the hippocampus has been implicated in the susceptibility to stress. This led us to hypothesize that maternal exercise induces persistent stress resilience of the offspring via enhancing epigenetic regulation of BDNF signalling in the hippocampus, which in turn promotes hippocampal neuroplasticity, and consequently protects against stress-induced depressive phenotypes. Here we aim to further evaluate these mechanisms by: (1) testing whether maternal exercise reduces depressive phenotypes and enhances hippocampal neuroplasticity (adult neurogenesis, dendritic complexity and synaptic plasticity) of adult female and male offspring; (2) determining if maternal exercise protects offspring from chronic stress-induced depressive-like behaviours and hippocampal atrophy; and (3) determining the role of microRNA-124 and its target BDNF signalling in maternal exercise-enhanced stress resilience in the offspring. We will employ adult C57/6J mice with voluntary wheel running during pregnancy and adopt chronic unpredictable stress to examine the effects of maternal exercise on hippocampal plasticity and depressive phenotypes in both female and male adult offspring. We anticipate that maternal exercise can protect the offspring from chronic stress-induced depressive phenotypes via the epigenetic regulation of BDNF signalling, hence promoting hippocampal neuroplasticity. The study findings will translate to the clinic with exercise interventions for pregnant moms and identify biomarker of stress resilience in clinical research. The results will also pave the way for discovering new therapeutic targets and mechanisms for enhancing stress resilience. 抑鬱症是全球殘疾的第二大原因。目前抗抑鬱藥物治療仍存在顯著局限，包括延遲治療效果，耐藥性和高緩解率。非藥物策略，如運動干預，可以增強壓力恢復能力，並可能降低抑鬱症的發生率。此外，臨床研究表明，懷孕期間的母親運動對發育中的嬰兒的大腦有益。動物研究表明，懷孕期間運動的媽媽（母親運動）的後代表現出改善的學習和記憶，並減少焦慮/抑鬱行為。這可能是由於成年神經發生，腦源性神經營養因子（BDNF）和後代海馬神經元活動的增加。我們之前的研究表明，有助於動物模型中, 體育鍛煉的抗抑作用與海馬神經可塑性的增強有關。我們的試驗數據表明，母體運動促進學習和記憶，減少抑鬱樣行為，並增強後代成人海馬神經發生。受壓的易感性與海馬神經可塑性取決於海馬中的microRNA-124的表觀遺傳調節有關。因此,我們假設母體運動通過增強海馬中BDNF信號傳導的表觀遺傳調節來誘導後代的持久應激反應，這反過來促進海馬神經可塑性，並因此保護免受應激誘導的抑鬱表型。在這裡，我們的目標是通過以下方式進一步評估這些機制：（1）測試母體運動是否減少抑鬱表型並增強成年雌性和雄性後代的海馬神經可塑性（成人神經發生，樹突複雜性和突觸可塑性）; （2）確定母親的運動是否能保護後代免受慢性壓力引起的抑鬱樣行為和海馬萎縮; （3）確定microRNA-124及其靶BDNF信號在母體運動中的作用 - 增強後代的應激反應。我們將採用成年C57 / 6J小鼠，在懷孕期間自願轉動輪胎並採用慢性壓力來檢查母體運動對雌性和雄性成年後代的海馬可塑性和抑鬱表型的影響。我們預計，通過BDNF信號傳導的表觀遺傳調節，母體運動可以保護後代免受慢性應激誘導的抑鬱表型，從而促進海馬神經可塑性。該研究結果將轉化為臨床，為孕婦提供運動干預，並在臨床研究中確定應激反應的生物標誌物（microRNA-124）。該結果還將為發現新的治療目標和增強壓力恢復的機制鋪路。

15104019.label: Realisation of objectives
15104019.value: Objective 1: To determine if maternal exercise during pregnancy enhances hippocampal neuroplasticity in both female and male offspring Results achieved: We have completed this aim with experiments using electrophysiology for measuring synaptic plasticity, Golgi staining for dendritic spine changes, Western blotting for checking synaptic proteins in synaptoneurosome extraction and behavioral tests for antidepressant response in both female and males. Our data demonstrated significant effects of maternal running on improving synaptic plasticity as indicated by enhancement in long-term potentiation in the hippocampal dentate gyrus in both young adult male and female offspring at the age of 5 week old, though there was no significant effect in paired pulse ratio, suggesting synaptic enhancing effects of maternal exercise on offspring hippocampal synaptic plasticity is mainly present in the post-synaptic side, but no effect on pre-synaptic changes in acute hippocampal slice recording. Western blot analysis revealed that maternal exercise significantly enhanced synaptic protein synaptophysin in both male and female offspring, but only male offspring showed significant increase in PSD-95 levels, but not effects on female offspring. Analysis of Golgi staining shows that maternal exercise has gender specific effect on enhancing dendritic spine density in the hippocampal dentate granule neurons from the female offspring but no effect on male offspring. Female offspring showed significant enhancement in spine density of mature granule neurons (morphologically with multiple primary dendritic branch and located in the outer layer of the granule cell layer) and younger neurons (morphologically with single primary dendritic branch and located in the inner layer of granule cell layer) in the hippocampal dentate gyrus. The data indicated that maternal exercise only benefit female offspring on enhancing spine density in the dentate subregion. Overall, our results clearly indicated that maternal exercise can effectively enhance hippocampal synaptic plasticity with more profound effects on female offspring, and this enhanced hippocampal synaptic plasticity was observed in addition to enhanced hippocampal adult neurogenesis (Yau et al. 2019), suggesting that maternal exercise can effectively enhance hippocampal structural and functional plasticity in both male and female offspring, though there is gender specific effect in modulating molecular and cellular changes in the hippocampus. Objective 2: To determine if maternal exercise increases stress resilience by protecting female and male offspring from chronic stress-induced depressive phenotypes and hippocampal atrophy To demonstrate that enhanced hippocampal neuroplasticity in the offspring could enhance stress resilience by protecting offspring from stress-induced depression-like behavior and hippocampal impairment, male and female offspring at the 5-week old age were subjected to 4-weeek chronic unpredictable stress. Behavioral analysis revealed that both male and female offspring from exercised dam showed significant reduction in immobility time in forced swim test and increased grooming time in sucrose splash test, suggesting maternal exercise protects both male and female offspring from chronic stress-induced depression-like behavior and anhedonia-like behavior. Only male offspring showed significant increase in time spent in the center of the open field test, suggesting maternal exercise showed gender specific effect in lowering anxiety-like behavior in male offspring, but not female offspring. Since maternal exercise enhances synaptic plasticity in both male and female offspring, we therefore measured changes of synaptic protein in the hippocampus of offspring with chronic stress exposure as indicator for changes in synaptic plasticity. Both stressed male and female offspring from exercised dams show decrease in synaptic protein levels including PSD-95 and synaptophysin levels in the hippocampus. The results showed that maternal exercise confer stress resilience to chronic stress-induced depression-like behavior in both male and female offspring with enhanced hippocampal synaptic plasticity. Objective 3: To examine whether maternal exercise-enhanced stress resilience in the offspring is mediated by epigenetic regulation of BDNF signaling in the hippocampus. To investigate the underlying mechanisms of the transgenerational effects of maternal exercise, we examined changes of synaptic plasticity-related to molecular changes that could be contributed by epigenetic up-regulation of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). BDNF is an important downstream neurotrophic factor for enhancement in synaptic plasticity. Since hippocampal long-term potentiation formation depends on activation of NMDA receptor, we measure synaptic fraction of NMDA receptor subunits. Results showed that maternal exercise has main effect in enhancing synaptic expression of phosphorylated AMPA receptor subunit GluA1, and with gender specific effect on enhancing NMDA receptor GluN2A subunits, but not GluN2B subunits in female offspring, suggesting that female offspring benefits more from maternal exercise in terms of enhanced hippocampal NMDA receptor function. There are significant main effects of maternal exercise in up-regulating BDNF protein levels in the hippocampus, both male and female mice show higher hippocampal BDNF levels, indicating maternal exercise has transgenerational effects on promoting BDNF levels which play a critical role in enhancement of synaptic plasticity. Overall, we observed a stronger effect of maternal exercise on promoting hippocampal plasticity in female offspring, suggesting a potential gender effects of maternal exercise on offspring brain health. We further investigated if enhancement of BDNF by maternal exercise is linked to alternation in non-coding miRNA-124 which could contribute to enhanced stress resilience. Animal study has suggested that inhibiting miRNA-124 in the hippocampus increases CREB and BDNF levels and reduces depression-like behavior. Our data showed a higher miRNA-124 mRNA expression levels in the hippocampus of female offspring, while there was no effects on miRNA-124 levels in the male offspring. The higher miRNA-124 in association stress resilience to chronic stress is consistent to another findings that increasing miRNA-124 in the hippocampus confers stress resilience to chronic stress. Our results have demonstrated that maternal exercise confers offspring to stress resilience to chronic stress-induced depression-like behavior in association with higher expression levels of BDNF in the hippocampus of both male and female offspring. An association with higher miRNA-124 levels in the hippocampus was found in female offspring, but no effects on male offspring. This data may suggest that miRNA-124 may not be the key epigenetic player for up-regulating hippocampal synaptic plasticity by maternal exercise since the positive influence of maternal exercise on up-regulating miRNA-124 was only observed in female offspring, but not male offspring, however, both female and female offspring demonstrated enhanced hippocampal synaptic plasticity and enhanced stress resilience. Difficulties: The project progress was affected during COVID pandemic with shortage of mouse supply and delayed delivery of chemicals, reagents and antibodies for conducting experiments. The expected waiting time did have some negative impact on the project progress. The miRNA-124 blocking experiment was not conducted owing to unexpected result that no significant up-regulation of miRNA-124 mRNA levels in the hippocampus were not observed in male mice displaying enhanced hippocampal synaptic plasticity and stress resilience. The result indicated that there could be other epigenetic regulation for up-regulated hippocampal BDNF levels.

15104019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104019.value: The study has provided scientific evidence that maternal exercise has long-lasting effect on improving hippocampal synaptic plasticity in both male and female offspring, which may in turn confer offspring to stress resilience against chronic stress insult, and thus prevents chronic stress-induced depression-like behavior. This effect could be contributed by increased BDNF levels in the hippocampus of offspring. The beneficial effects on hippocampal plasticity are more pronounced in female offspring, suggesting a gender difference of maternal exercise’s influence on offspring. Major research outcome: The results have been presented in different international conferences including Society of Neuroscience Meeting 2023, Washington DC. were presented in virtual platform for World Congress of International Neuropsychopharmacology 2019, Taiwan, and Neural Regeneration Research Symposium 2021, and a local symposium related to healthy ageing during covid pandemic. The abstract submitted to SFN 2023 was selected for press conference showing its impact to general public in promoting maternal exercise a potential and feasible strategy to enhance stress resilience and lower incident rate of stress-related mental disorders. There are three manuscripts derived from this funded project: (1) systemic review and meta-analysis (to be submitted) Title: Neuroprotective effect of maternal exercise on offspring and its mechanisms: a systemic review and meta-analysis (2) Comprehensive review (to be submitted) Title: Beneficial effects of maternal exercise on offspring’s cardiovascular, metabolic, and neurodevelopmental health: a comprehensive review (3) Research article (in preparation) Title: Maternal exercise during pregnancy enhances hippocampal synaptic plasticity to confer stress resilience in adult male and female offspring

15104019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104019.value: The current data have suggested that maternal physical exercise increases stress resilience of both male and female offspring with this transgenerational effect on promoting hippocampal synaptic plasticity. We hypothesized that enhanced miRNA-124 as the underlying mechanistic action to mediate the epigenetic changes, however, the data from the results indicated that miRNA-124 may not play a critical role in epigenetic up-regulation of BDNF in the hippocampus. Further direction will be performing miRNA sequencing or transcriptomic or metabolomic analysis to identify potential key miRNA or protein or signaling pathway that linked to up-related BDNF in the hippocampus of the offspring, and study factors for example 3’ Sialyllactose in breastmilk (Harris et al., 2020 Nature Metabolism) or adiponectin (Yau et al., 2019 PNAS) in the blood that pass through placenta from the pregnant dams to offspring to mediate the effects of maternal exercise on offspring’s brain plasticity.

15104019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104019.value: Our animal study suggested that maternal physical exercise during pregnancy could have a long-lasting effect in promoting brain plasticity in adult offspring, which is linked to enhanced stress resilience of adult offspring. Maternal exercise can effectively confer stress resilience to offspring against stress. This effect could be contributed by enhanced brain neurotrophic factor which can in turn enhances neural function in the hippocampus, a brain regions critically involved in mood regulation. The current results imply that maternal exercise during pregnancy should be recommended for pregnant mothers throughout pregnancy, especially who have reported to be suffered from stress. Maternal exercise could be a manageable way to enhance brain function to achieve stress resilience for preventing onset of depression in offspring.

15104119.label: Realisation of objectives
15104119.value: 1. To functionally characterize the role of SREBP2 in the regulation of liver T-IC (100%) i. To study the effects of SREBP2 modulation on T-IC phenotypes. Using RNA sequencing analysis, we compared the expression profiles of sorafenib- and lenvatinib-resistant PDTXs and the corresponding mock controls and found that cholesterol biosynthesis was most significantly and commonly upregulated in these two drug-resistant PDTXs, according to ingenuity pathway analysis (IPA), while upstream regulator analysis identified many genes controlled by SREBP2 in PDTX#1 and PY003 were activated. Based on filipin staining, an increase in filipin-labeled free cholesterol was consistently observed in both drug-resistant PDTXs. Based on these findings, we found that sorafenib/lenvatinib-resistant HCC cells exhibited increased cholesterol biosynthesis. To examine whether SREBP2-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis functionally drives self-renewal and tumor formation, we performed SREBP2-knockdown and overexpression experiments using a lentiviral-based approach. PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L cells were chosen for the knockdown experiment, while Hep3B cells were chosen for the overexpression experiment. Upon alteration of SREBP2 expression, as described above, we observed corresponding changes in the intracellular cholesterol levels and genes responsible for cholesterol biosynthesis in Hep3B, PLC/PRF/5, and MHCC-97L cells, further confirming the role of SREBP2 in the regulation of cholesterol biosynthesis in HCC. Using a limiting dilution assay, SREBP2 knockdown significantly reduced the stem cell frequencies of PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L cells. In an in vivo tumorigenicity assay, knockdown of SREBP2 dramatically reduced the size and number of tumors formed. We found that shSREBP2-transfected cells exhibited decreased percentages of CD133 and CD47. Opposite effects were observed in SREBP2-overexpressed Hep3B cells. ii. To study the effects of SREBP2 modulation on HCC metastasis and drug resistance. Transwell and matrigel-coated assays showed that both PLC/PRF/5 and MHCC-97L shSREBP2 cells had significantly lower migration and invasion efficiencies. In addition, suppression of SREBP2 resulted in sensitization of HCC cells to molecularly targeted drugs, including sorafenib and lenvatinib. We demonstrated the maximal growth-suppressive effect of simvastatin in combination with sorafenib and lenvatinib in organotypic ex vivo human HCC clinical samples and HCC PDTX models. iii. Characterization of SREBP2 in the regulation of the liver T-IC phenotype by a cell sorting approach Given the molecular similarities between liver T-ICs and normal liver stem cells, we examined whether cholesterol biosynthesis was preferentially activated in liver T-ICs. First, we sorted CD133+ cells and CD133- cells from a 0.1% DDC (3,5-diethoxycarbonyl-1,4 dihydrocollidine)-induced liver regeneration mouse model and two HCC mouse models, including 1) a mouse model with hydrodynamic injection of activated forms of NRAS/AKT and 2) a model with diethylnitrosamine (DEN)/carbon tetrachloride (CCl4)-induced fibrosis-related HCC. Next, we analyzed the enriched signaling pathways in CD133+ cells using CD133- cells as the corresponding baselines in these three mouse models by RNA sequencing analysis. When compared to that of regenerating liver, cholesterol homeostasis was found to be the most commonly upregulated pathway in CD133+ HCC cells from two HCC mouse models. 2. Elucidation of the molecular mechanism by which SREBP2 functionally contributes to tumor initiation, self-renewal, and drug resistance i. To study the effects of SREBP2-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis on liver T-ICs To further confirm the role of cholesterol biosynthesis as a downstream effector of SREBP2 in mediating CSC function, we treated SREBP2 knockdown HCC cells with 5 μM cholesterol solubilized in methyl-β-cyclodextrin (MβCD) to investigate whether the effects of SREBP2 suppression can be eliminated by exogenous cholesterol. We found that addition of exogenous cholesterol restored the inhibitory effects of SREBP2 knockdown on stem cell frequency, CSC marker expression, and invasiveness of MHCC-97L cells. In addition, the addition of exogenous cholesterol recovered the inhibitory effects of SREBP2 knockdown on drug resistance in MHCC-97L cells. ii. To study the effects of SREBP2-mediated SMO activity by cholesterol metabolite To determine the major downstream effector of SREBP2, we performed RNA sequencing analysis to compare the gene expression profiles of shSREBP2 and non-target control cells derived from MHCC-97L cells. GSEA showed enrichment of the sonic hedgehog (SHH) pathway. By western blot analysis, we found that the expression of GLI-1, SUFU, SHH, PTCH1, and PTCH2 was consistently altered in SREBP2 knockdown and overexpressing HCC cells. Using ELISA, we found that Cholesterol-25-hydroxylase (CH25H), an enzyme responsible for the production of 25-hydroxycholesterol (25-OHC), was downregulated in shSREBP2 cells. Finally, administration of 25-OHC at 15 µM in MHCC-97L cells rescued the suppression of the SHH pathway in shSREBP2 HCC cells. iii. To study the effects of SMO activation on SREBP2-mediated T-IC phenotypes To further confirm the role of SHH as a downstream effector of CASP3/SREBP2 in mediating cancer stemness and drug resistance, we treated SREBP2-overexpressing Hep3B cells with GANT61, a GLI-1 inhibitor, to investigate whether the effects of SREBP2 overexpression could be eliminated by the suppression of GLI-1. We found that the addition of GANT61 offset the enhancing effect of SREBP2 overexpression on self-renewal ability, as well as resistance to sorafenib and lenvatinib treatment. 3.To evaluate the correlation of SREBP2 expression with prognostic and clinicopathological significance and liver T-ICs in human HCC Analysis of the publicly available dataset, GSE14520, and the Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset revealed that SREBP2 mRNA was significantly upregulated in HCC tumor tissues compared to non-tumor liver tissues. In a tissue microarray consisting of 50 HCC samples and corresponding matched non-tumor liver tissue samples, patients with high SREBP2 expression had shorter disease-free survival (p=0.0002; log-rank test). In addition, we found that patients with high SREBP2 expression had a higher chance of HCC recurrence (p=0.0006). IHC analysis revealed that cleaved CASP3 was coexpressed with SREBP2 and GLI-1. 15104119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104119.value: Resistance to molecularly targeted drugs, such as tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), develops in most cancer patients and limits their long-term survival, which is a great hurdle for efficient cancer therapy. Cancer stem cell (CSCs) are now regarded as the source of therapeutic resistance. However, how tumors expand CSC populations in response to drug treatment remains largely unknown. In this study, we have provided a new mechanistic insight of how tumor cells expand CSC populations in response to TKI treatment using hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) as a cancer model. In this study, we established two sorafenib- or lenvatinib- resistant patient-derived tumor xenografts that mimicked the clinical situation of the development of acquired resistance to sorafenib or lenvatinib treatment in HCC patients. By RNA sequencing coupled with pathway analysis, we found that cholesterol biosynthesis was most commonly activated in these two xenografts. Consistently, we found that this process was activated in enriched CSC populations in both mouse and human origins, but not in the normal liver stem cells. Functional analysis shows that SREBP2-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis is crucial in the regulation of acquired drug resistance in HCC via augmentation of liver CSCs. Similarly, exogenous cholesterol-treated and high cholesterol-utilizing HCC cells exerted the similar effects. We idetified a distinct function of caspase-3, which cleaves SREBP2 from the endoplasmic reticulum in response to TKI treatment and consequently render resistance to sorafenib/lenvatinib treatment by driving activation of the cholesterol biosynthesis-driven sonic hedgehog signaling pathway via 25-OHC regulation. Lastly, we demonstrated that Simvastatin, an FDA-approved cholesterol-lowering drug complemented the effects of sorafenib/lenvatinib in HCC cells. In this study, we have identified the relationship of caspase-3 (CASP3) and SREBP2 as the driving event that initiates CSC expansion through the promotion of the cholesterol biosynthesis-driven SHH signaling pathway. Targeting the cholesterol biosynthesis pathway may be a promising strategy to combat TKI treatments in HCC. Our findings are scientifically important and clinically relevant and will definitely appeal to the readership of stem cell and cancer research. Our finding will convey several important messages to the readers: (1) cholesterol biosynthesis is activated in tumor cells in response to TKI treatment; (2) We first found that cholesterol biosynthesis was preferentially activated in liver CSCs when compared to their normal counterparts; (3) SREBP2-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis plays a crucial role in regulation of cancer stemness and drug resistance; (4) The role of cholesterol in cancers is controversial; we found that exogenous cholesterol-treated and high cholesterol-utilizing HCC cells is crucial for regulation of liver CSCs, and bears clinical significance; (5) we first identified the non-apoptotic role of CASP3 in HCC, which acts a switch from apoptotic signaling to survival signal via activation of SREBP2-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis and hence targeting CASP3 may not be a good option for cancer therapy; (6) we have provided a previously unanswered question of how liver CSCs expand in response to TKI, which is mediated via CASP3-dependent, SREBP2-mediated cholesterol biosynthesis-driven sonic hedgehog signaling pathway; (7) Targeting cholesterol biosynthesis by FDA approved drug, Simvastatin, synergized the effect of TKIs in HCC.

15104119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104119.value: Researchers ave found that cancer stem cells (CSCs) can result in drug resistance in cancer by repopulating tumors, although the underlying mechanism is not well understood. In this study, we discovered that cholesterol biosynthesis is a crucial process in CSC repopulation, leading to acquired drug resistance. Our findings also revealed that HCC cells treated with exogenous cholesterol exhibited enhanced CSC abilities and drug resistance. We identified caspase-3 (CASP3), a protein known to play a role in apoptosis, as the factor that induced cholesterol biosynthesis by cleaving SREBP2 from the endoplasmic reticulum, resulting in the activation of the sonic hedgehog signaling pathway, promoting resistance to sorafenib/lenvatinib treatment. This data let the researchers to rethink the new role of CASP3 in expansion of CSCs. Our study suggests that combining sorafenib/lenvatinib with cholesterol-lowering drugs like simvastatin may be a new potential strategy for HCC treatment. However, further clinical testing is necessary to verify these findings. Additionally, there are several new cholesterol-lowering drugs, including Inclisran, which have demonstrated superior potency in reducing cholesterol levels with fewer side effects. In the future, it would be worthwhile to investigate the combination effect of these new cholesterol lowering drugs with sorafenib/lenvatinib in both in vitro HCC organoid models.

15104119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104119.value: Targeted drug therapies, such as sorafenib and lenvatinib, represent the primary therapeutic option for patients with advanced-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, the survival benefits are limited due to the development of acquired drug resistance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the underlying mechanism leading to treatment failure. Our study reveals that HCC cells initiate the production of cholesterol, which leads to the expansion of cancer stem cell (CSC) populations, considered the root cause of tumor relapse and drug resistance. Furthermore, we have identified a signaling pathway driving this cholesterol-induced CSC expansion and resistance to treatment. In conclusion, our findings suggest a new therapeutic approach for improving the survival of HCC patients.

15104419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104419.value: Obesity is a major risk factor for many non-communicable diseases such as diabetes, cardiovascular diseases and cancers. The prevalence of such diseases is growing rapidly to epidemic proportions globally. Many pharmacological therapies are proposed but none of them can cure these costly non-communicable diseases. Understanding the pathophysiological mechanisms behind them is a prerequisite for the development of new therapies. We analysed the phenotypes of knockout mice and expression profiles from various genes in obese subjects from various databases and found a novel gene named CYSTM1 that is a potential mediator of obesity-related metabolic complications. The evidence include (1) cystm1 knockout mouse that had obvious metabolic phenotypes, including decreased lean body mass, respiratory quotient, food intake and dysregulated lipid and glucose homeostasis; (2) CYSTM1 is a potential secretory protein produced from the stomach and its expression is associated with nutritional status; and (3) CYSTM1 binds to glucagon-like peptide-1 receptors (GLP-1R) and inhibits GLP-1-induced cAMP accumulation in CHO cells. We hypothesise that CYSTM1 is a novel gastric factor that regulates energy metabolism via the brain and various GLP-1R-expressing metabolic organs such as the liver and adipose tissue. In this study, we will fully elucidate the physiological functions of CYSTM1 in metabolism by using a diet-induced obese mouse model, decipher its underlying molecular mechanisms by both in vitro and in vivo experiments, and investigate the therapeutic potential of targeting CYSTM1. 肥胖是非傳染性疾病的一種主要致病源，其能導致糖尿病、心血管疾病和癌症。此類疾病的致病率在全球範圍內迅速上升，並達到成為流行病的程度。目前藥物並不能治癒這些非傳染性疾病，因此瞭解其病理生理機制能有助於開發新療法。 我們觀察並分析了基因敲除小鼠的表型，同時檢測不同資料庫中肥胖受試者的不同基因表達譜後，發現了一種名為CYSTM1的新基因。研究結果顯示，新基因CYSTM1是肥胖相關代謝併發症的潛在介質。（1）CYSTM1基因敲除小鼠顯著地表現出與代謝相關的表型，如淨體重下降、呼吸熵降低、食物攝入減少、脂肪與葡萄糖穩態失調；（2）CYSTM1是一種潛在的胃分泌蛋白，其表達與機體營養狀況有關；（3）CYSTM1與胰高血糖素樣肽-1受體（GLP-1R）結合，從而抑制CHO細胞中GLP-1誘導的cAMP累積。 我們假設，CYSTM1是一種可以通過大腦和各個表達GLP-1R的代謝器官（如肝臟和脂肪組織）作用來調節能量代謝的新胃因子。在此研究中，我們將利用飲食誘導的肥胖老鼠模型來瞭解CYSTM1在代謝中的生理作用，進一步通過體內和體外實驗來闡明其作用的分子機制，從而探究靶向CYSTM1治療的可能性。

15104819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15104819.value: Myopia is the most common refractive disorder, affecting over 2.3 billion people globally. High myopia predisposes to many sight-threatening complications. Local instillation of atropine, primarily used to induce mydriasis and cycloplegia in ophthalmological examination, is also widely used off-label for myopia control. Atropine is a well-known muscarinic receptor antagonist but its site(s) of action and therapeutic mechanism(s) in myopia remain unclear. Recent studies suggest it activates the release of dopamine, another established retinal neurotransmitter for myopia control. In myopia development, optical signals are first received in the retina, integrated, to regulate scleral remodeling. Conventional laboratory research usually targets a single or a few candidates at a time which has limited capacity to elucidate the global interplay between the commonly believed, multiple pathways orchestrating myopic eye growth and in therapeutic interventions. We were the first group to apply proteomics to myopia research and demonstrated the dynamic and complex changes of the retinal proteome during eye growth in a chick model. Since then, we have identified several novel proteins and pathways potentially involved in the development of myopia. Among them, apoprotein A-1 (ApoA1), a key protein in lipid metabolism, was found to be a ‘stop’ signal. Interestingly, our pilot data using topical instillation of 0.01% atropine in chick myopia modulation also showed that lipid/cholesterol metabolism and GABAergic pathway (a well-known retinal regulator in eye growth) are two major potential mediating mechanisms in myopia control. Due to the differences in scleral composition between avian and mammalian eyes, we recently adopted the guinea pig as a more relevant mammalian model for myopia research. In a pilot study, we identified a significant up-regulation of ApoA1 and a protein related to GABA receptors in the sclera of guinea pigs recovering from experimental myopia. These latest findings in chick and guinea pig proteomes demonstrated the feasibility of this proposal: aiming to comprehensively characterize temporal changes in protein expression and of signal cascades from the retina to the sclera upon atropine treatment at the highest sensitivity and dynamic range currently feasible. Observations from our pilot studies, though preliminary, are exciting in that they demonstrate an unexplored connection of atropine-specific myopia control with dual regulatory cascades in both the retina and sclera. To narrow the focus in this initial proposal, we hypothesize that there are novel molecular machineries related to lipid/cholesterol metabolism and GABAergic system in the posterior eye that are responsive to atropine treatment. 近视又称短视眼，是全球发生率最高的屈光不正。据近期的流行病学研究表明，全世界有超过23亿人患有近视。其中，高度近视所引发的并发症严重威胁到人类视力健康。阿托品作为一种典型的非选择性胆碱能M型受体 (毒蕈碱受体) 拮抗剂, 在眼科临床上多用于解除调节痉挛和散瞳。近年来，阿托品滴眼液较为普遍地用于减缓近视进展, 但其属于超说明书用药，大都属于临床试验。虽然其临床效果已在循证医学方法中得到肯定，但其具体作用部位和控制近视的根本作用机制尚不明确。先前的动物实验近视研究表明来自视网膜神经递质在近视的形成和发展过程中会有上调或下调，多巴胺 (dopamine, DA) 在其中正扮演着重要角色。最新的研究亦表明，阿托品可能通过激活多巴胺的释放，进而发挥控制近视作用。 视网膜作为眼部结构的组成部分，对于视觉信号的传递，发挥着重要的作用，它处于视觉系统的最前端。在近视的发展过程中，异常的视觉信息首先作用于视网膜, 经视网膜色素上皮层-脉络膜信号转导, 最终作用于巩膜, 最终引发巩膜重塑。传统的实验研究通常一次只能研究一个或几个候选蛋白或基因，因此限制其无法全面阐明与近视相关的多条信号通路之间的交互作用，也无法揭示与近视治疗、干预相关的多条信号通路之间的相互作用。在以往的研究中，我们是第一个将蛋白质组学应用于近视研究的团队，在雏鸡近视眼模型中，通过蛋白质组学手段，成功阐述了视网膜蛋白质变化的多样性和复杂性。从那以后，我们陆续发现了几个可能与近视发展相关的全新的候选蛋白和生物信号通路。这里列举其中较为典型之一，脂蛋白A-1（ApoA1）作为脂质代谢相关的关键蛋白之一，在我们先前的研究中发现其是一种与近视相关的“停止”信号。同时，以往研究表明,抑制性氨基酸神经递质γ-氨基丁酸（GABA）在近视的发生和发展过程中发挥关键作用。 我们最新的阿托品研究亦发现，当给予近视小鸡眼以0.01％浓度的阿托品眼局部滴注后，其对近视的影响潜在与脂质/胆固醇代谢和γ-氨基丁酸（GABA）信号通路有密切的关系。 由于禽类和哺乳动物之间眼部巩膜组织结构的不同，我们在近视实验性动物方面，逐渐从小鸡转向了与人类更接近的哺乳动物模型-豚鼠。在最新的研究中，我们从实验性近视恢复中的豚鼠巩膜发现，脂蛋白A-1（ApoA1）和与GABA受体相关的蛋白质显著上调。正式基于上述近视小鸡眼和近视豚鼠眼模型的发现，为该课题立项提供了可靠依据，该课题旨在应用现行最高灵敏度和最大动态范围的蛋白质组学技术手段，从视网膜到巩膜，全面探索分析与阿托品控制近视进展密切相关的差异性表达的蛋白质及所涉及的生物信号通路调控。虽然我们的预实验是初步的，但令人兴奋的是，它证明了阿托品对近视进展的调控作用在视网膜和巩膜上体现出相关的双重联系。为了缩小该课题中的研究重点，我们将重点在眼后极部揭示一些与脂质/胆固醇代谢和γ-氨基丁酸（GABA）信号通路相关的全新信号蛋白，这也将是我们阐释阿托品调控近视进展的根本分子机制及相关信号通路的重要途径。

15104819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15104819.value: Supported by the grant, we successfully developed and refined advanced proteomics protocols to identify and quantify ocular proteomics using the state-of-the-art Zeno-SWATH MS platform. By employing integrated labeled and unlabeled strategies, we uncovered novel mechanisms of myopia and identified specific protein targets influenced by both high and low doses of atropine. This project has culminated in the publication of seven high-quality SCI research papers (the majority in Q1 journals) and two conference presentations, one of which received a prestigious conference award. Key findings and novelty of each manuscript: 1. We developed the largest data-dependent acquisition (DDA) spectral library for the mouse retina, identifying 5,950 proteins at a 1% FDR, thereby enhancing research into retinal diseases significantly. 2. We further achieved the identification and quantification of 9,401 protein groups in the retinas using AI-enabled DIA-NN platform, significantly advancing the understanding of retinal proteomes, especially in the context of myopia research, showcasing the effectiveness of a library-free method for proteomic analysis in drug discovery 3. We achieved significant insights into lipid metabolism alterations in the retinas of guinea pigs during early lens-induced myopia, identifying 58 differentially expressed proteins and some novel pathways. The integrated SWATH and MRM approaches provided a comprehensive view of the molecular changes occurring in myopic development. 4. Using transcriptomics, we highlight the down-regulation of the genes VIP and UTS2B and the consistent up-regulation of FOXG1 in lens-induced myopia, demonstrating their potential roles in early myopia development. 5. We demonstrated that low-dose atropine does not significantly alter the spike frequency or morphology of ON and OFF αRGCs but may unmask GABAergic inhibition, impacting retinal signal processing in about 25% of OFF αRGCs. This suggests that while low-dose atropine is effective in controlling myopia, it could have unintended consequences on retinal information transmission to the brain 6. We explored retinal protein changes in myopic guinea pigs receiving 1% atropine treatment. It highlighted modifications in EIF2 signaling, glycolysis, and dopamine secretion pathways, identifying alpha-synuclein as a crucial regulated protein for the first time. 7. The sclera proteomics analysis identified 2,863 unique proteins and revealed 63 differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) between atropine-treated and untreated groups, Key pathways affected by atropine included oxidative phosphorylation and reactive oxygen species, suggesting its role in modulating mitochondrial function, which is the common pathways regulated by atropine in both the retina and sclera.

15104819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15104819.value: Following confirmation from our study that atropine can directly regulate proteins in posterior ocular tissues, we have initiated follow-up research focusing on spatial proteomics. This involves profiling proteins isolated from distinct layers of retinal tissues, such as photoreceptors and retinal ganglion cells (RGCs), which previously posed significant technical challenges. Furthermore, with the identification of novel protein targets in response to atropine treatment, we have discovered a biologic known to modulate the expression of these targeted proteins and regulate pathways of interest. Our objective is to evaluate its effects on myopia control using the same animal model.

15104819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15104819.value: This project utilized advanced molecular techniques and the latest next-generation technologies to investigate the mechanisms of atropine eyedrop in myopia control, which remains unknown. Our team was the first to identify and quantify novel protein targets associated with atropine treatments at varying concentrations from highthrougput protein profiling at the posterior eyes using a mammalian guinea pig model. Our study suggests that myopia entails a synchronized set of molecular changes in both the retina and sclera, and atropine's therapeutic effects may involve modulation of mitochondrial activity and reduction of oxidative stress across ocular tissues. These findings could pave the way for new and effective therapies aimed at preventing or slowing down myopia progression in humans, highlighting the interconnected role of different eye tissues in this condition.

15105119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15105119.value: Ageing is the underlying cause of multiple chronic diseases including type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. Adipose tissue plays a central role in maintaining health span and metabolic homeostasis, but its function deteriorates during ageing. NLRP3 inflammasome activation occurs in adipose tissue with ageing in humans and rodents. Global knockout of NLRP3 alleviates ageing-induced adipose tissue dysfunction and glucose dysregulation in mouse model. However, the understanding of pathogenesis of ageing-related adipose tissue dysfunction, including inflammasome activation, and its contribution to chronic metabolic disorders remains enigmatic. The xenobiotic enzyme flavin containing monooxygenase 3 (FMO3) is known to convert gut microbiota-derived trimethylamine (TMA) into trimethylamine-N-oxide (TMAO) in the liver. Hepatic FMO3 mRNA level and circulating TMAO level are positively correlated with type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular diseases. Inhibition of hepatic FMO3 or blocking TMAO production protects against atherosclerosis, obesity and insulin resistance in mouse models. However, little is known about the role of FMO3 and TMAO in adipose tissue functions and ageing. In our pilot study, we demonstrated that adipose tissues also abundantly express FMO3. Expression of FMO3 and its metabolic product TMAO in adipose tissue but not in the liver increases with ageing. FMO3 expression is dramatically induced in mature adipocytes by the activation of p53, a key contributor to adipose tissue ageing. Treatment with the pathophysiological concentration of TMAO markedly induces secretion of interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18, the surrogate markers of inflammasome activation, in bone-marrow derived macrophages. Consistently, circulating TMAO levels are positively correlated with IL-18. Based on these information, we hypothesize that ageing causes the upregulation of FMO3 expression in adipocytes, which in turn enhances TMAO production in adipose tissues, leading to inflammasome activation in adipose tissue macrophage (ATM) and subsequent systemic metabolic disorders. In this project, we will use adipocyte-specific FMO3 knockout mouse model (1) to examine whether adipocyte FMO3-derived TMAO is the major source of TMAO in ageing and (2) to investigate whether adipocyte FMO3 contributes ageing-induced adipose tissue dysfunction, if so, whether this FMO3 action is mediated by TMAO. Furthermore, we will elucidate how aged adipocytes, via FMO3-derived TMAO, causes inflammasome activation in ATM. The findings from this study will reveal how a gut microbiota-derived metabolite mediates the cross-talk between adipocyte and ATM and regulates host metabolism, and provide scientific evidence to target FMO3-TMAO axis in adipose tissue for alleviation of ageing-related chronic diseases and/or extension of healthy life span. 衰老是多種慢性疾病的根本原因，當中包括2型糖尿病和心血管疾病。 脂肪組織在維持健康和代謝穩態中起著重要作用，但其功能在衰老過程中逐漸損失。在人和齧齒動物的老化過程中，脂肪組織中會發生NLRP3炎症小體的啟動。動物實驗表明了 NLRP3的敲除減輕了衰老誘導的脂肪組織功能障礙和葡萄糖失調。 然而，對衰老相關的脂肪組織功能障礙及其在慢性代謝紊亂中發病機制的研究仍然不是很清楚。 異生素酶黃素單加氧酶3（FMO3）在肝臟中可以將腸道菌群產生的三甲胺（TMA）轉化為氧化三甲胺（TMAO）。肝臟FMO3 mRNA水準和血液中TMAO水準與2型糖尿病和心血管疾病呈正相關。抑制肝臟FMO3或阻斷TMAO的產生可抵禦小鼠模型中的動脈粥樣硬化，肥胖和胰島素抵抗。然而，關於FMO3和TMAO在脂肪組織功能和衰老中的作用知之甚少。我們的初步研究證明了脂肪組織也大量表達FMO3。 FMO3的表達及其代謝產物TMAO的含量在脂肪組織中隨著衰老而增加。脂肪組織衰老的關鍵因素p53的上升可以顯著誘導成熟脂肪細胞中FMO3表達。用病理生理學濃度的TMAO處理骨髓來源的巨噬細胞顯著誘導白細胞介素（IL）-1β和IL-18的分泌，IL-1β和IL-18是炎症小體啟動的替代標誌物。同樣地，血液中TMAO水準與IL-18呈正向相關。基於以上研究結果，我們假設衰老導致脂肪細胞中FMO3表達的上調，增強脂肪組織中TMAO的產生，導致脂肪組織巨噬細胞中炎症小體的啟動和隨後的全身代謝紊亂。 在這個研究課題中，我們將使用脂肪細胞特異性敲除FMO3的小鼠模型（1）來檢查脂肪細胞FMO3產生的TMAO是否是衰老中TMAO的主要來源;（2）研究脂肪細胞FMO3是否促進衰老誘導的脂肪組織功能障礙及FMO3的這個作用是否是由TMAO介導。 此外，我們將闡明衰老的脂肪細胞如何通過FMO3產生的TMAO在脂肪組織巨噬細胞中引起炎症小體啟動。 這項研究的結果將揭示腸道菌群產生的代謝物如何介導脂肪細胞和脂肪組織巨噬細胞之間的串擾並調節宿主代謝，並提供科學證據來靶向脂肪組織中的FMO3-TMAO軸，以減輕與衰老相關的慢性疾病和 /或延長健康壽命 。

15105119.label: Realisation of objectives
15105119.value: Objective 1. To investigate whether adipose tissue is the main site for TMAO production via the p53-FMO3 axis in ageing. 1. Expression of FMO3 and its derived TMAO were reduced in both white and brown adipose tissues of Adipo-FMO3-KO mice when compared to their WT littermates. 2. A significant reduction of circulating TMAO level was observed in aged Adipo-FMO3-KO mice when compared to their wild-type littermates. 3. Two different p53 activators, namely doxorubicin and nutlin-3a increased mRNA and protein level of FMO3, accompanied with induction of the senescent markers including p53 and Cdkn1a. Treatment with doxorubicin also upregulated d9-TMAO production in mature adipocytes. Genetic deletion of FMO3 abolished doxorubicin-induced TMAO production in adipocytes. 4. Doxorubicin induced p53 and FMO3 expression and TMAO abundance in WAT of 12-week-old C57BL/6J mice, which were accompanied with increased circulating TMAO level. 5. To examine whether p53 directly controls FMO3 activity, we cloned the FMO3 promoter and intron 1 region consisting of p53 binding sites into a luciferase vector. We transfected 3T3-L1 pre-adipocytes or HEK293 cells with the pGL3 luciferase vectors with the intron 1 and promoter of human FMO3 containing p53 responsive element, followed by treatment with the nutlin-3a (the MDM2 inhibitor upregulates p53 expression) and plasmid-mediated overexpression of p53. The luciferase assay showed that overexpression of p53 or treatment with nutlin-3a enhanced luciferase expression controlled by the promoter but not the intron 1 of Fmo3. Objective 2. To examine whether adipocyte-specific FMO3 deletion alleviates ageing-induced adipose tissue dysfunction and its related metabolic disorders. 1. Glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity were improved in Adipo-FMO3-KO mice when compared to WT controls during ageing. Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion during glucose tolerance test was decreased in the aged-Adipo-FMO3 KO mice, suggesting a better insulin sensitivity. 2. Adipo-FMO3-KO mice are more resistant to fasting-induced hypothermia. 3. Adipo-FMO3 KO mice displayed similar levels in oxygen consumption, carbon dioxide production, energy expenditure, locomoter activity and respiratory exchange ratio, when theywere at 3-month and 6-month-old. However, increased energy expenditure and locomoter activity was observed in Adipo-FMO3 KO mice at the age of 20- to 22-month-old. 4. Adipo-FMO3 KO mice displayed improved triglyceride clearance and lower levels of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) relative to WT controls. 5. We found an increase of muscle mass in Adipo-FMO3 KO mice at age of 2-year-old compared to their respective WT control groups. 6. Transcriptomic analysis demonstrated that the pathways related to p53-related senescence, interferon-α/γ, inflammatory responses and NF-κB were downregulated, whereas those related to adipogenesis, and cholesterol homeostasis were upregulated by adipocyte-specific deletion of FMO3. 7. QPCR analysis confirmed reduction of the gene related to inflammatory cytokines and chemokine, fibrotic genes, and senescent genes, as identified by the RNAseq. 8. Histological analysis showed a decrease of immune cell infiltration, pro-inflammatory M1 macrophages, and lower collagen deposition in eWAT of Adipo-FMO3 KO mice. A reduction in adipocyte hypertrophy were observed in the eWAT of Adipo-FMO3 KO mice. 9. We confirmed that the senescent markers such DNA damage and p53 and p21 expression are reduced in eWAT of Adipo-FMO3 KO mice than that in WT controls. 10. Inflammatory macrophage markers including F4/80, iNOS and Il-1β and inflammasome protein NLRP3 were reduced in sWAT of Adipo-FMO3 KO mice. Adipocyte deletion of FMO3 also modestly improved fibrosis in sWAT. Adipo-FMO3 KO mice displayed less lipid accumulation and higher gene expression of Prmd16 and a lower level of p53 in sWAT. In addition, brown adipocytes of Adipo-FMO3 KO mice were less hypertrophic and had less lipid accumulation compared to those in WT controls. 11. Doxorubicin triggered a similar degree of senescence between both FMO3 deficiency and WT adipocytes, which was reflected by β-gal staining and gene expression of p53, Cdkn1a and Cdkn2a as well as the IL-1β. However, incubation with TMA potentiated the doxorubicin-induced senescent responses in WT adipocytes, but such potentiating effect was completely abrogated by FMO3 deletion. In addition, replenishment of TMAO reversed the anti-senescence effect of FMO3 deletion in mature adipocytes. 12. LPS induced pro-inflammatory cytokine and chemokine expression, and such effect was further enhanced by TMA treatment in WT adipocytes. Whereas FMO3 deletion abrogated the potentiating effects of TMA on LPS-induced inflammatory response in adipocytes. On the other hand, replenishment of TMAO neutralized the anti-inflammatory effect of FMO3 deletion in mature adipocytes. 13. To further confirm whether FMO3-TMAO induces inflammation in mature adipocytes, we established three stable 3T3-L1 cell lines overexpressing (1) GFP as control, (2) wild-type (WT) FMO3 and (3) a FMO3-P153L mutant with defective catalytic activity for TMAO production34. As expected, overexpression of WT-FMO3 but not FMO3-P153L increased conversion of d9-TMA into d9-TMAO. Consistently, overexpression of WT-FMO3 but not FMO-P153L augmented LPS-induced IL-1β and MCP1 secretion in 3T3-L1 mature adipocytes These above findings suggested that adipocyte-specific deletion of FMO3 alleviates ageing-induced adipose tissue dysfunction via a TMAO-dependent manner. Objective 3. To determine whether and how upregulation of FMO3-TMAO in adipocytes triggers inflammasome activation in adipose tissue macrophages. 1. Mature IL-1β, active form of caspase 1 and NLRP3 proteins were downregulated in eWAT of Adipo-FMO3 KO mice. Circulating levels of inflammasome cytokines including IL-1β and IL-18 were diminished in Adipo-FMO3 KO mice, whereas MCP1 and adiponectin remained unchanged. In addition, immunofluorescent staining revealed that cleavage form of caspase-1 was increased on F4/80+ macrophages with visceral WAT was decreased in aged-Adipo-FMO3 KO mice when compared to WT controls. 2. Treatment with TMAO modestly enhanced p65 and IKB-α phosphorylation as well as well as inflammasome genes including NLRP3, caspase-1, Il-1β and Il-18 in the BMDM. However, caspase-1 activity was dramatically markedly induced by TMAO in LPS-primed BMDM. Treatment with caspase 1 or NLRP3 inhibitor attenuated TMAO-induced IL-1β production in BMDM. Likewise, LPS+TMAO significantly increased IL-1β production and cleavage of capase-1 but had minimal effect on inflammasome gene expression in human THP1 macrophages compared to those treated with LPS alone. 3. Apart from macrophages, we found that FMO3 overexpression and its derived TMAO also triggered inflammasome activation and IL-1β production in mature adipocytes. 4. PERK has been identified as the receptor for mediating detrimental effects of TMAO on metabolism. But we showed that TMAO has no effect on PERK in macrophages. We also found that calcium signalling and potassium efflux did not mediate the effect of TMAO on inflammasome activation in macrophages. 5. By using proteomics, we identified revealed that 379 and 194 TMAO-binding proteins in BMDM and adipocytes, respectively. Pathway analysis revealed that those potential TMAO-binding proteins involved in inflammatory pathways such NF-κB, interleukins in both adipocytes and macrophages. 6. There were 18 TMAO-binding proteins in common between mature adipocyte and macrophages. Among them, Pycard is an essential component of the NLRP3 inflammasome. 7. By using DARTS, we showed that TMAO protected proteinase-induced Pycard protein degradation in a dose-dependent manner. siRNA-mediated silencing of Pycard completely abrogated TMAO-induced IL-1β production and capase-1 activation in THP1 macrophages and BMDM primed with LPS. The above findings suggest that adipocyte FMO3-derived TMAO acts as an autocrine and paracrine factor to induce inflammasome activation via binding with Pycard.
