15105119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15105119.value: We showed that WAT-expressed FMO3 and its derived TMAO contribute to the systemic elevation of TMAO, WAT dysfunction, and metabolic diseases in aging. FMO3 expression and TMAO levels are upregulated in WAT of naturally aging animals and human subjects. This upregulation is due to p53 activation in mice and could be mitigated by calorie restriction in humans. Adipocyte-specific ablation of FMO3 attenuates TMAO accumulation in WAT and circulation, leading to enhanced glucose metabolism, energy homeostasis, and lipid regulation in aged and obese mice. These metabolic improvements to reduced senescence, fibrosis, and inflammation in WAT. Mechanistically, TMAO facilitates inflammasome activation by binding to the inflammasome adaptor protein Pycard, thereby inducing caspase-1 activation, and subsequent IL-1β production. We uncover a pivotal role for adipocyte FMO3 in modulating TMAO production and WAT dysfunction by promoting inflammasome activation in ageing via an autocrine and paracrine manner. Research outcomes: (1) Presentation in the international and local conferences: a) Australasian Diabetes Congress Conference, August 2023, Poster presentation (International) b) Postgraduate Symposium (organized by Department of Health Technology and Informatics [HTI], PolyU), June 2024, Oral presentation. Award obtained: 3rd place in Oral presentation c) PolyU Research Students Conferences, May 2023, Oral presentation d) 3rd ABCT Research Postgraduate Symposium, PolyU, August 2022, Poster presentation. Award obtained: Best poster presenter award e) 2nd ABCT Research Postgraduate Symposium, PolyU, August 2021, Oral presentation (2) Training of one Ph.D. student (HTI, PolyU; student name: Thashma Ganapathy) and one undergraduate students (BSc of Medical Laboratory Science; student name: Kwok Wing Yee). (3) We have submitted a manuscript entitled " Adipocyte FMO3-derived TMAO induces WAT dysfunction and metabolic disorders by promoting inflammasome activation in ageing " to Nature Metabolism in June 2024. Apart from the macrophages as originally proposed, we also found that TMAO acts as an autocrine factor to induce inflammasome activation in mature adipocytes. Unexpectedly, calcium and potassium signalling are not involved in TMAO as we originally hypothesized. Instead, we identified numerous TMAO-binding proteins involved in inflammation. In particular, we demonstrated that TMAO bind with Pycard to trigger inflammasome activation in mature adipocyte and macrophages. We originally planned to submit and publish our manuscript in late 2023. However, the progress has been delayed due to the outbreak of COVID19 (2020-2023). Of note, the project duration is from Jan 2020 to Jun 2023. Nevertheless, we will inform RGC once the manuscript is accepted for publication.

15105119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15105119.value: 1. We proved a concept that genetic deletion of FMO3 alleviates ageing-induced adipose tissue dysfunction and metabolic diseases. To further translate our finding in human, we need to examine whether treatment with the FMO3 inhibitor methimazole also prevents ageing-induced metabolic disorders. Of note, methimazole is currently used for hyperthyroidism and approved by FDA. Once the beneficial effects of methimazole are validated in rodents, we can examine its effects in human subjects in the future. 2. We found that TMAO binds with Pycard in macrophages and adipocytes. Inhibition of Pycard also blocked the potentiating effect of TMAO on IL-1β secretion. However, the exact binding site between TMAO and Pycard and how TMAO modify Pycard activity is currently unknown. Further investigation of the above questions is required. 3. We observed that adipocyte specific deletion of FMO3 improves inflammation, fibrosis and senescence in WAT. However, whether the improvement of fibrosis and senescence is secondary to reduced inflammation or a direct action of FMO3-TMAO required further studied.

15105119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15105119.value: White adipose tissue (WAT; also known as fat) dysfunction contributes to metabolic disorders such as type 2 diabetes in ageing, however, the underlying pathogenesis remains poorly understood. Our current study uncovers that the metabolic enzyme flavin-containing monooxygenase 3 (FMO3) is active in adipocytes, particularly in the context of ageing. We demonstrated that adipocyte FMO3-derived trimethylamine oxide (TMAO) serves as a harmful factor to induce inflammation in adipocytes and WAT-resident macrophages, thereby leading to WAT dysfunction and metabolic disorders. Our study suggests that inhibition of FMO3 might be a feasible approach to alleviates ageing-related WAT dysfunction and metabolic diseases. Key findings: 1. FMO3 protein and TMAO are abundantly expressed in mature adipocytes, induced by natural ageing and ageing inducer p53, alongside increased circulating TMAO levels. 2. Genetic deletion of adipocyte FMO3 diminishes adipose tissue and circulating TMAO levels in ageing mouse models, which mitigates inflammation, senescence, and fibrosis in WAT, thereby improving metabolic homeostasis in ageing context. 3. In humans, high FMO3 expression correlates with inflammation pathways and adipogenesis in subcutaneous WAT. Whereas calorie restriction reduces FMO3 expression and inflammatory genes in WAT of human subjects. Significance: Inhibition of adipose FMO3-TMAO might be a feasible approach for treating ageing-related diseaees.

15105919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15105919.value: Stroke is the leading cause of physical disability. Facilitating the process of motor relearning would greatly accelerate the rehabilitation of motor functions and elicit positive neuroplasticity of the damaged brain area [1]. Previous research have already explored the feasibility of motor priming techniques embedded in stroke rehabilitation programs using strategies such as non-invasive brain stimulation (NIBS) and mirror therapy (MT). These treatments are usually implemented along with the standardized rehabilitation, sequentially or simultaneously, and have been demonstrated to be more effective than the standardized rehabilitation programs alone [2-4]. Mirror neuron, as indicated traditionally by the decrease in the amplitude of Mu rhythm, i.e. a suppression over central electrodes of electroencephalography (EEG), reflects the “seeing” of movement after “perception”. Such oscillations are based on neural substrates that are discharged during the observation and execution of a motor act, which is also associated with other human functions, such as imitation, language. etc. [5-7]. The core mirror neuron system (MNS) is thought to be located in the premotor and the primary sensorimotor cortices, indicating that motor learning could be enhanced during action observation and overt movement. Preliminary research has shown that repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (rTMS) can enhance the corticomotor excitability in mirror neurons during both observation of movement (by others) or imagined movement in healthy subjects; in particular as measured by enhanced motor evoked potentials (MEP) [8, 9]. Increases in MEP has also been induced by short-term action observation and mirror visual feedback in stroke survivors [8, 10]. However, it is not yet known if MNS can be activated by TMS in MT following stroke, and the relationship between mirror neuron activation and clinical improvements in stroke remains unclear. Our research study team has already published preliminary findings in patients with hemiplegic upper extremity, rTMS, and MT. Here, we propose to test the hypothesis that rTMS in the form of theta burst stimulation (TBS) over the ipsilateral and contralateral motor cortices can modulate mirror illusion-induced rhythm suppression while observing unilateral arm movement in stroke individuals. We further hypothesize that this intervention will lead to the revision of interhemispheric asymmetry. Finally, this study will also explore the longitudinal relationship between rhythm suppression and motor recovery as indicated by motor excitability in the form of MEP. The results of this study will provide significant new information regarding neurophysiological motor relearning mechanisms which could inform the development and evaluation of innovative treatments for individuals with stroke. 運動功能尤其是上肢功能障礙是中風病人常見的現象，儘管目前已有多種上肢康復訓練,部分嚴重偏癱病患的康復進展仍然十分緩慢。鏡像療法是一種簡單、方便又經濟的治療方法，針對中風後偏癱上肢的康復治療。此技術是以患者從鏡中觀看健側上肢做治療師指定的動作，同時及同步使用患側上肢模仿此鏡像動作的治療方法，是促進嚴重腦中風病人運動學習的康復訓練方法之一，通過健側肢體運動的鏡像回饋，腦中風病患能在患側肢體運動的同時，接受同步的鏡像視覺回饋。研究證明，神經系統中存在一部分在運動觀察及運動執行均能活化的神經細胞群，稱為鏡像神經系統(MNS)，而此系統的啟動被認為與人類的運動理解，運動學習及模仿肢體功能均有密切的關係，而鏡子治療被認為是啟動鏡像神經元的方式之一。並且，通過鏡像幻覺誘發的腦電波節律抑制(ERD) - 通常在Mu頻率發生，被認為是人類鏡像神經元活動的主要神經標誌物之一。並且，提高腦電波Mu節律抑制可能與腦中風病人運動功能的恢復直接相關。 重複性經顱磁刺 (rTMS) 是一種無創治療方法，由“8”字形線圈產生的磁信號通過影響腦電活動從而選擇性調控大腦功能。重複性短高頻刺激是重複性經顱磁刺激的一種新型的刺激模式。研究人員已經證明短時間，高頻但低強度的重複性短高頻刺激 (TBS) 具有與傳統重複性經顱磁刺激相當的治療效果，目前此療法已經被大量臨床研究證實有效並廣泛用於治療多種神經系統疾病。本研究的主要目的是重複性短高頻刺激的使用能否影響腦中風病人的腦電波節律抑制(ERD)以初步探索重複性短高頻刺激對於鏡像神經系統(MNS)的調製作用及對偏癱上肢康復的臨床效用。

15105919.label: Realisation of objectives
15105919.value: Objective 1: To investigate the short-term and long-term modulatory effects of intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) on mirror illusion-induced event-related desynchronization (ERD) for hemiplegic upper extremity recovery in subacute stroke patients, compared with iTBS plus Sham mirror therapy and Sham iTBS plus mirror therapy, in a randomized controlled study. Deliverable: We investigated the modulatory effects of intermittent TBS (iTBS) with MVF in mirror therapy (MT) on hemiplegic upper extremity motor recovery and neurophysiological outcomes in patients with stroke. In our randomized controlled trial, 36 patients with chronic stroke were enrolled and randomly assigned to one of three groups: iTBS with MT, sham iTBS with MT, and iTBS with bilateral arm training (BAT). The number of participants enrolled was (iTBS + MT: n = 12; sham iTBS + MT: n = 12; and iTBS + BAT: n = 12). No between-group difference in demographical characteristics and clinical scores at baseline was found. Outcomes included Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE), the Action Research Arm Test (ARAT), and sensorimotor beta event-related desynchronization (ERD) using EEG induced by MVF. Because there were only very few patients referred from Queen Mary Hospital, University of Hong Kong, the PI has changed to recruit patients with chronic stroke from the community self-help organizations. According to our previous sample size prediction in the proposal considering the effect of iTBS, the implementation of four repeated measurements and an estimated 10% attrition rate, a sample of 36 participants would be necessary, with 12 participants in each group for a three-group design to achieve 80% in power and Type I errors set at the 0.05 significance level. Therefore, we have achieved the proposed target. Our results show that there was a significant time-by-group interaction effect in the FMA-UE hand sub-scores (F = 2.49, P = 0.042). Post hoc analyses showed that patients who received iTBS with MT or BAT demonstrated greater improvements in the FMA-UE hand sub-scores at the one-month follow-up, in contrast to those who received sham iTBS with MT (P = 0.043 and 0.012, respectively). Among patients with lower upper limb functioning, iTBS with MT yielded a greater improvement in the FMA-UE total scores than the sham iTBS with MT after the first session (P = 0.014), the 10th session (P = 0.025), and at one-month follow-up (P = 0.005). Objective 2: To investigate TBS will reduce the interhemispheric asymmetry as indicated by an assimilation of mirror illusion-induced ERD in both hemispheres which will lead to motor recovery. Deliverable 2: A subset of patients who were eligible in the randomized controlled trial were further invited to participate in the EEG experiment before randomization. Fifteen out of the included 36 cases participated in the EEG (iTBS + MT: n = 5; sham iTBS + MT: n = 5; and iTBS + BAT: n = 5). During the MVF condition, our results revealed a significant time-by-group interaction (F = 5.06, P = 0.025) in MVF-induced ERD in the beta-2 band over channel 2RA (located within the ipsilesional SMC) during the movement stage, and post hoc comparisons using paired t-tests showed that iTBS with MT induced a significantly greater enhancement in ERD (i.e., more negative) after 10 sessions, compared with the baseline (P = 0.008). No significant interaction effect was noted in the beta-1 and beta-3 bands. Explanatory paired t-tests showed that, over the beta-1 band, iTBS with MT enhanced the magnitude of ERD in channel 2RA (located within the ipsilesional SMC) after 10 sessions, compared with the baseline (P = 0.040), while iTBS with BAT enhanced the magnitude of ERD in channel 2LA (located within the contralesional SMC) over the beta-1 after 10 sessions, compared with the baseline (P = 0.037). Over the beta-3 band, iTBS with MT enhanced the magnitude of ERD in channel 5R (located within the ipsilesional SMC) after 10 sessions, compared with the baseline (P = 0.019). Overall, EEG findings showed that iTBS with MT, but not the other two protocols, enhanced the beta ERD over the ipsilesional sensorimotor area. The neurophysiological findings of this study support the notion that combining iTBS and MT primes the brain to be more receptive to MVF, thereby facilitating the lateralization of brain activation toward the ipsilesional SMC when patients observe the MVF. On the other hand, we also observed that iTBS combined with BAT may enhance sensorimotor ERD over the contralesional SMC during the mirror view condition, indicating that pairing iTBS with different training protocols may promote post-stroke motor recovery via differential neurophysiological mechanisms. However, our correlation analysis did not reflect any causality between the improvement in FMA-UE and the increase in MVF-induced ERD over the ipsilesional SMC. Therefore, we have addressed the objective but we suggest that neurophysiological mechanisms of post-stroke recovery in response to different forms of training can be further studied with hemispheric ERD neural substrates. Objective 3: To examine the longitudinal relationship between mirror illusion-induced ERD in core and adjacent movement-related regions and motor evoked potentials (MEP) in the primary motor cortex for the upper extremity at various time points after stroke, and explore their potential as biomarkers for the trajectory of patients’ motor recovery. Deliverable 3: During the direct visual feedback (DVF) condition, no significant time-by-group interaction effect was noted in the sensorimotor beta ERD. Explanatory paired t-tests showed that, over the beta-2 and beta-3 bands, iTBS with MT induced a significantly greater enhancement in ERD over channel 2LA (located within the contralesional SMC) after 10 sessions, compared with the baseline (P = 0.032 and 0.034, respectively). No significant difference across time was observed in the other two groups. Since significant interaction effects were only found in the FMA-UE total scores and its hand sub-scores, we further used these two outcomes in the correlation analyses. During the MVF condition, a significant correlation was found between the improvement in the FMA-UE total scores after 10 sessions and the change from baseline in ERD in the beta-3 band over channel 5R (over the ipsilesional SMC; r = -0.56, p = 0.031). A significant correlation between the change from baseline in MVF-induced ERD in beta-2 and beta-3 bands over channel 5R and the improvement in FMA-UE hand sub-scores was also noted (r = -0.56, p = 0.029; r = -0.57, P = 0.027). No significant correlation pair was found in the DVF condition. According to our ERD results, we conclude that iTBS combined with MT appears to prime the ipsilesional motor cortex to be more receptive to MVF, achieving interhemispheric symmetry for motor recovery. The majority of our sample consisted of chronic subcortical stroke patients without evocable MEP found during the ipsilesional M1 stimulation. Our EEG analyses were conducted in a small subset of participants, only 15 out of the included 36 cases agreed and participated in the EEG, the EEG results should be deemed preliminary, due to the sample size. We have partially addressed the objective that movement-related ERD could be potential biomarker for motor recovery but that further investigation for the potential use of MEP as biomarker is needed because of its limited application in patients with lower functioning.

15105919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15105919.value: In this study, 36 patients with chronic stroke were enrolled and randomly assigned to one of three groups: iTBS with MT, sham iTBS with MT, and iTBS with bilateral arm training (BAT). Outcomes included Fugl-Meyer Assessment-Upper Extremity (FMA-UE), the Action Research Arm Test (ARAT), and sensorimotor beta event-related desynchronization (ERD) induced by MVF. There was a significant time-by-group interaction effect in the FMA-UE hand sub-scores (F = 2.49, P = 0.042). Post hoc analyses showed that patients who received iTBS with MT or BAT demonstrated greater improvements in the FMA-UE hand sub-scores at the one-month follow-up, in contrast to those who received sham iTBS with MT (P = 0.043 and 0.012, respectively). Among patients with lower upper limb functioning, iTBS with MT yielded a greater improvement in the FMA-UE total scores than the sham iTBS with MT after the first session (P = 0.014), the 10th session (P = 0.025), and at one-month follow-up (P = 0.005). EEG findings showed that iTBS with MT, but not the other two protocols, enhanced the beta ERD over the ipsilesional sensorimotor area. The results support the notion that prior priming using iTBS to the hand representative area of the M1 over the affected hemisphere can facilitate the efficacy of motor learning during MT and, hence, achieve a more superior clinical outcome. In this study, the significant clinical effect was noted in the hand scores of the FMA-UE postintervention and the persisting observed superiority effect of the combined intervention using iTBS and MT, which was also dominant at one-month follow-up. Our findings substantiated the hypothesis that iTBS combined with MT appears to prime the ipsilesional SMC to be more receptive to MVF, achieving a better interhemispheric symmetry, which further reduces susceptibility to interhemispheric interference, and strengthens long-term retention in motor learning. However, no significant difference between iTBS with MT and iTBS with BAT was observed in clinical outcomes. Subgroup analyses of the meta-analysis showed that MT was more effective in improving upper limb motor outcomes when compared to control training using a covered mirror, but the effect was comparable to control training with an unrestricted view. Our exploratory subgroup analyses demonstrated that a superior effect of the combined intervention was found in participants with lower upper limb functioning (i.e., levels 3–4 in the FTUHE), but not those with higher functioning (i.e., levels 5–7 in the FTUHE).

15105919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15105919.value: iTBS combined with MT or BAT is superior to sham iTBS combined with MT in regard to improving the distal function of the hemiplegic upper extremity in patients with stroke. In addition, superiority is evident at one-month follow-up. iTBS combined with MT appears to prime the ipsilesional motor cortex to be more receptive to MVF and achieve interhemispheric symmetry for motor recovery. Regarding ERD, we found similar effects of combining iTBS and MT can enhance the ERD responses over the SMC contralateral to the MVF (i.e., the ipsilesional SMC) in stroke patients. The neurophysiological findings of this study support the notion that combining iTBS and MT primes the brain to be more receptive to MVF, thereby facilitating the lateralization of brain activation toward the ipsilesional SMC when patients observe the MVF. However, our correlation analysis did not reflect any causality between the improvement in FMA-UE and the increase in MVF-induced ERD over the ipsilesional SMC. Therefore, we suggest that neurophysiological mechanisms of post-stroke recovery in response to different forms of training can be further studied with hemispheric ERD neural substrates.

15105919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15105919.value: Theta burst stimulation (TBS) and mirror visual feedback (MVF) have been used to reduce interhemispheric asymmetry in both hemispheres, which leads to motor recovery. We investigated the modulatory effects of intermittent TBS (iTBS) with MVF in mirror therapy (MT) on hemiplegic upper extremity motor recovery and neurophysiological outcomes in patients with stroke. In this randomized controlled trial, 36 patients with chronic stroke were enrolled and randomly assigned to one of three groups: iTBS with MT, sham iTBS with MT, and iTBS with bilateral arm training (BAT). We found that patients who received iTBS with MT or BAT demonstrated greater improvements in the hand performance at the one-month follow-up, in contrast to those who received sham iTBS with MT, particularly patients with lower upper limb functioning. EEG findings showed that iTBS with MT, but not the other two protocols, enhanced the sensorimotor beta event-related desynchronization over the ipsilesional sensorimotor area. We conclude that iTBS combined with MT or BAT is superior to sham iTBS combined with MT in improving the distal functions of hemiplegic upper extremity after stroke. iTBS combined with MT appears to prime the ipsilesional motor cortex to be more receptive to MVF, achieving interhemispheric symmetry for motor recovery.

15106619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15106619.value: Colorectal cancer is the third most common cancer worldwide. Post-operative recurrence and metastasis are the major causes of cancer-related death. Since early treatment of recurrence and metastasis is critical for patient survival, identifying patients at high risk of these complications would be useful for guiding therapy. Hence, biomarkers that allow an accurate prediction of the risk of recurrence, metastasis and treatment response are urgently needed. In recent years, circulating tumor cells detection has provided a new non-invasive strategy in cancer diagnosis, prognosis and treatment monitoring. Circulating tumor cells are found in many cancers such as breast, colorectal and lung cancers. However, the main drawbacks to translate this technology into patient care are the low sensitivity and specificity. Recent studies have showed that cadherin 17 overexpression is associated with worse prognosis in liver and gastric cancers. Besides, cadherin 17 is also an attractive therapeutic target for liver cancer. Pathologically, cadherin 17 protein is proposed to be a diagnostic marker for metastatic colorectal cancer. These findings provide evidence that cadherin 17 is involved in multiple cancer signaling pathways which open up important gateways for cancer detection, monitoring and therapeutic treatment. In this proposal, we have developed a novel technology to detect cadherin 17-positive circulating tumor cells, using a custom-made anti-cadherin 17 antibody of a patented peptide sequence, in patients with colorectal cancer. This novel technology attributes to the successful simultaneous detection of cadherin 17 and nuclear beta-catenin proteins in the same circulating tumor cell. Thus, the surge in the detection sensitivity is balanced by the significant improvement in specificity because nuclear beta-catenin expression is an adjunct biomarker for colorectal cancer. In this proposal, the diagnostic significance of cadherin 17- positive circulating tumor cells with nuclear beta-catenin will be examined using this novel technological platform. Preliminary results show that cadherin 17-positive circulating tumor cells with nuclear beta-catenin were detected in 82% colorectal cancer patients, 0% colorectal adenoma patients and 0% colonoscopy confirmed normal subjects. As our latest research has shown that this custom-made anti-cadherin 17 antibody can reduce the growth and suppress metastasis in liver cancer, we will investigate the curative potential of this antibody in colorectal cancer cells using xenograft nude mouse model. This study represents the first investigation of utilising cadherin 17-positive circulating tumor cells as a non-invasive approach to detect colorectal cancer and may shed insights into targeting cadherin 17 expression as potential therapeutic intervention for treatment of colorectal cancer.

15200119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200119.value: Ultra-precision freeform surfaces(UPFSs) are widely used in various fields such as precision moulds,optics,photonics,biomedical,etc. Fluid jet polishing(FJP) is one of the most promising polishing methods for fabricating UPFSs. However,the low polishing efficiency of FJP adversely affects its application in polishing large-sized components or components made of difficult-to-machine materials. Hence, a multi-jet polishing(MJP) process was developed by the research team led by the PI which has proven to be effective to largely boost the polishing efficiency, while maintaining good surface quality. However, there still exist some challenges when polishing UPFS,such as effect of the surface shape on the material removal characteristics and surface generation in MJP of UPFSs. This project aims to develop a novel shape-adaptive multi-jet polishing(SAMJP) system for catering for the effect of the variation of materials removal characteristics due to the surface shape in polishing the UPFS. Theoretical modeling and analysis of the material removal characteristics and surface generation will be investigated systematically to provide a deeper understanding of the SAMJP method. The fluid flow field during MJP will be analyzed to study the effect of the fluid jet interference. Optimal design of the MJP nozzle will be undertaken to generate the fluid jets with high stability, including the optimization of the orifice shape and nozzle distribution principle. Hence, the multi-scale material removal characteristics of MJP will be investigated by analyzing the micro-scale and macro-scale material removal mechanisms. The micro-scale material removal mechanism refers to the single particle erosion mechanism under low fluid pressure(<20bar), which will be modelled by molecular dynamic simulation. The macro-scale material removal mechanism refers to the modelling of the tool influence function in MJP considering the curvature and shape effect. A pressure-dependent shape-adaptive(PDSA) control method and hence a SAMJP system will be developed for real-time pressure control of each jet to compensate for the variation of material removal characteristics due to the effect of the surface shape of the UPFS. The surface generation of SAMJP of the UPFS will be modelled by taking into consideration tool path planning, uniform and corrective polishing. Experiments will be conducted to validate the performance of the SAMJP methods and systems. The success of the project will provide a novel polishing technology for machining UPFSs and gain scientific understanding of the fundamental science and mechanism of material removal in SAMJP. The proposed SAMJP system will provide an innovative turnkey solution for highly efficient and highly accurate polishing of UPFS.

15200119.label: Realisation of objectives
15200119.value: Basically, all the project objectives of the project were successfully achieved. For objective 1, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation was conducted to optimize the design of the multi-jet nozzle. To avoid interference between adjacent jets and achieve highly accurate material removal, the nozzle was designed by adjusting the interval of the jets and the distribution of positions. CFD simulation was conducted to model the fluid flow field and optimize the design of the nozzle. The tool influence functions (TIF) of different nozzles were obtained via experiments to validate the CFD simulation model. On the other hand, to restrain the middle-spatial frequency error in the polishing process, the nozzle was also optimized by adjusting the nozzle orientation based on the surface generation model. After optimization, the ripple errors were greatly reduced, improving the performance of optical components. The results provide an important means for implementing shape-adaptive functionality for the shape-adaptive multi-jet polishing SAMJP process. In order to investigate the multi-scale material removal and surface generation mechanisms in the SAMJP process (Objective 2), a physical model was developed to predict the surface morphology and surface roughness after fluid jet polishing (FJP), by integrating the CFD simulation and kinetic analysis of the abrasives. The single abrasive erosion process at the microscale including indentation action, plowing action, and cutting action was analyzed using kinetic analysis. In addition, the overlap of single abrasive erosion pits was modeled to simulate the surface morphology evolution in FJP and determine the surface roughness after polishing. Different parameters were considered in the model including jet pressure, jet angle, and abrasive size. A series of polishing experiments were conducted to validate this model and the effect of different polishing parameters on surface quality was elucidated from the impact velocity distribution and erosion morphologies. It was found that the simulation results agreed well with the experimental results. These results not only provide a deeper understanding of the microscale material removal in FJP but also an effective method for the prediction of surface roughness in FJP. To improve the form accuracy in the SAMJP of ultra-precision freeform surfaces (UPFSs), the tool influence function (TIF) variation at the macroscale in the freeform surface polishing was modeled via CFD simulation, considering the effect of surface shape. A series of spot polishing experiments were subsequently conducted on the surfaces with different curvature radii and slope angles. The experimentally measured data including cross-section profiles of polishing spots, Peak-to-valley (PV) value, and material removal rate were found to agree well with the simulation results, which verified the effectiveness of the CFD model. The effect of surface curvature and slope angle on the material erosion distribution was investigated and revealed by the fluid flow field distribution, abrasive impact, and abrasive trajectories. This part not only provides a deep scientific understanding of the material erosion characteristics in the FJP of UPFSs but also offers a simple and cost-effective solution to build the database of TIFs on UPFSs under various shape conditions, which provides a solid foundation for gaining a better understanding of the multi-scale material removal and surface generation for form control during the SAMJP of UPFSs. To develop a pressure-dependent shape-adaptive control method for the precision real-time pressure control of each jet and hence establish a prototype SAMJP system (Objective 3), a mathematical model of the material removal rate was formulated through force analysis and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation. The study revealed that the material removal rate is directly proportional to both the jet pressure and a constant, denoted as 'k'. The value of 'k' is determined by the properties of the workpiece and the abrasives used. To validate this theoretical model, a series of experiments were conducted, taking into account the effect of the jet impinging angle and the types of abrasives used. This study deepens our understanding of the impact of jet pressure on material removal, thereby facilitating the optimization of the polishing parameters and eliminating the need for numerous preliminary experiments. Moreover, deterministic material removal at a constant feed rate can be achieved by controlling the jet pressure, rather than the dwell time. This approach effectively eliminates the instability of the motion system caused by high acceleration speeds. A real-time pressure control system was established through the integration of a reducing valve, a proportional valve, and an NI I/O system. This pressure control system can independently adjust the jet pressure of each jet. The jet pressures for different jets were determined and input into the computer prior to the polishing process. To validate the effectiveness of the shape-adaptive polishing method, the jet pressure response was measured using a force sensor. The results indicated that the jet pressure response was sufficiently rapid (significantly less than 0.1 seconds), which is advantageous for accurately deterministic material removal in freeform surface polishing. To model the surface generation in the SAMJP (Objective 4), the surface curvature and slope angle distribution of the freeform surface were determined before polishing. The material removal capacity at different positions can be determined by the fitting map of the material removal rate under various surface conditions, and is obtained via the validated CFD simulation. Combined with the established mathematical model of the effect of jet pressure on the material removal rate, the material removal amount at different positions can be determined. Hence, the surface form after polishing can be obtained by the initial surface form and the material removal distribution. To achieve the synergistic polishing of different jets in SAMJP, the workpiece surface is divided into several subregions and each subregion corresponds to one jet. The toolpath was optimized by using the square spiral path instead of the raster path to avoid nonuniform material removal at the edges of subregions. The interval of the adjacent subregion edge equals the polishing path spacing. The polishing performance was validated by the polishing experiments. To validate the effectiveness of the SAMJP, uniform polishing of different UPFSs was conducted including F-theta surfaces and sinusoidal surfaces. The surface forms were measured before and after polishing by traditional jet polishing and SAMJP. SAMJP can achieve a more uniform material removal due to the consideration of surface shape, contributing to the maintenance of form accuracy. A surface quality comparable to traditional single-jet polishing can be obtained by multi-jet polishing. Additionally, due to the increasing number of jets, the polishing efficiency was greatly enhanced. In addition, the project team has also extended the application of multi-jet polishing to structured array surfaces and post-process finishing 3D-printed surfaces. Machine learning methods were also adopted for the prediction of the surface roughness after polishing. Up to present, the research results of all objectives have been disseminated in 10 refereed journal papers and presented at 5 refereed international conferences. One PhD student has been trained and a best paper award was received.

15200119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200119.value: The theoretical modeling and characterization of surface generation in the shape-adaptive multi-jet polishing (SAMJP) of ultra-precision freeform surfaces (UPFSs) were conducted. The research attempted to gain a better scientific understanding of the material removal characteristic and surface generation mechanisms to improve surface quality and form accuracy in SAMJP. In this project, the micro-scale material removal mechanism was physically modeled to predict surface roughness and surface morphology evolution in fluid jet polishing (Journal paper 8), providing guidance for the optimization of polishing parameters (Journal paper 6). Hence, the tool influence function regarding the macro-scale material removal mechanism was investigated and analyzed via computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation to consider the effect of surface shape on material removal characteristics, including the material removal rate and distribution (Conference papers 1 and 3, Journal papers 4 and 9). This work offers a cost-effective solution to design the multi-jet nozzle and establish a database of material removal rates at various positions of freeform surfaces under the same jet pressure in order to implement shape-adaptive functionality in the SAMJP process. The numerical relationship between jet pressure and material removal rate was elucidated via kinetic analysis and validated by polishing different materials (Conference paper 2 and Journal paper 2). Based on the theoretical models, a surface generation model for freeform surface polishing was developed (Journal paper 5). A pressure-dependent multi-jet polishing system was established to compensate for the material removal characteristic difference resulting from surface shape changes such as curvature and slope angle in the polishing of UPFSs (Journal paper 9). In the SAMJP, the workpiece surface was divided into several subregions, each corresponding to one jet. To avoid non-uniform material removal at the edges of the subregion, the tool path was optimized and validated by experiments (Journal paper 2). To restrain the middle-spatial frequency (MSF) error in the polishing of optical components, the nozzle design was optimized, and a low MSF error could be achieved along with high polishing efficiency (Journal paper 3). Different UPFSs, including the F-theta surface and the sinusoidal surface, were polished to validate the effectiveness of the shape-adaptive ability (Conference papers 4 and 5, Journal papers 1, 3, 5, 7 and 10). On the whole, all project objectives were successfully achieved and one PhD student has been trained. The research outcomes were disseminated in 10 refereed journal papers and presented at 5 refereed conferences. One best paper award was received.

15200119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200119.value: More in-depth analysis will be conducted to study the material removal and surface generation mechanisms in the shape-adaptive multi-jet polishing (SAMJP) of different types of materials such as hard and brittle materials. Further development work will be undertaken on the established SAMJP system which will be integrated with a smart manufacturing system to further enhance the polishing efficiency and accuracy. On the one hand, in-situ surface measurement equipment will be installed on the machine. The tool path and jet pressure information will be generated automatically based on the surface generation model of SAMJP and measured surface profile. In the polishing process, it is unnecessary to unload the workpiece. On the other hand, the polishing parameters will be optimized by combining the proposed physical models and artificial intelligence algorithms so that the SAMJP system can achieve the smart polishing of ultra-precision freeform surfaces (UPFSs). Besides, cooperation with high-tech companies in different fields will be strengthened such as precision molds and optical components, especially for the polishing of surfaces with optical functional structures. It is necessary to transfer the SAMJP technology to the industry and achieve the mass production of high-end components, benefiting different sectors of industries such as biomedical and optics.

15200119.value: Ultra-precision freeform surfaces (UPFSs) are widely used in various fields such as precision molds, optics, biomedical, etc. Although a multi-jet polishing (MJP) process was developed which has proven to be effective to largely boost the polishing efficiency of traditional fluid jet polishing (FJP), while maintaining good surface quality, there still exist some challenges when polishing UPFSs, such as the effect of the surface shape on the material removal characteristics and surface generation in the MJP of UPFSs. In this project, a novel shape-adaptive multi-jet polishing (SAMJP) method and hence a SAMJP system have been successfully developed for real-time pressure control of each jet to compensate for the effect of the variation of material removal characteristics due to the surface shape when polishing UPFSs. 15200619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200619.value: 由於神經系統疾病患者的神經肌肉信號不能有效地從大腦傳遞到四肢，他們的活動能力和日常生活因此受到的影響。為了促進神經康復，可以利用腦機接口系統（BCI）設計康復鍛煉，直接從患者的大腦無創地獲取腦電（EEG）信號，並識別其運動意圖，從而給患者產生外部反饋以促進大腦的可塑性。這種方法目前主要用於上肢康復。然而開發用於下肢康復的BCI較具挑戰性，因爲下肢運動信號是從較深層的大腦區產生的，使獲取的腦電信號較弱，增加了準確識別及分類的難度。本項目的重點正是針對下肢的神經康復，旨在開發先進的機器學習技術來處理較深層腦區的EEG信號及準確地識別運動意圖。其中，具有卓越可解釋性和分類性能的 Takagi-Sugeno-Kang（TSK）模糊系統（FS）將會被用於系統開發。首先，本項目將通過開發多視角算法以集合各種特徵提取方法的優勢，從EEG信號獲得更有效的特徵。此外，本項目亦會開發多任務算法以準確地識別患者移動左或右髖關節、以及左或右膝的意圖。該算法是通過對個別運動意圖進行識別任務和考慮任務之間的相關性來實現意圖分類，同時也利用深度學習來進一步提高準確性。本項目將參考鏡像治療法，建造虛擬環境以給予患者提供基於EEG信號的交互式視覺提示和引導，以及通過由外骨骼機器人和振動器件產生的交互式觸覺反饋。本項目將進行實驗以評估所提出的智能運動意圖識別算法的性能。

15200619.label: Realisation of objectives
15200619.value: The three of objectives have been realized. Novel machine learning algorithms were developed based on various theories and principles, including fuzzy systems (FS) and support matrix machines (SMM), multi-view, multi-task, transfer learning and deep learning techniques, to detect and classify movement intentions from EEG signals with outstanding performance. The project produced 10 journal papers and 2 conference papers, which are listed at the end of this sub-section, numbered from 1 to 12, and are referenced in the report. For FS, we developed algorithms based on Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) FS which can be used for EEG classification. Since EEG signals contain features of different domains (views) and that the availability of labeled data is usually limited due to the time and labor cost incurred, multi-view TSK-FS algorithm with transductive learning were developed for effective feature extraction [1]. Furthermore, in Motor Imagery (MI) Brain Computer Interface (BCI) systems which involve the tasks of imagining movement of different body parts, e.g. hands and feet, EEG recognition performance can be enhanced by leveraging the information obtained from recognizing each individual MI task. In the regard, we investigated multi-task FS where the pseudo label matrix was decomposed by non-negative matrix factorization, and collaborative learning between multiple tasks and view weighting mechanism were adopted in the fuzzy modeling [2]. By representing EEG data in matrix form, we employed SMM to exploit high level representation of EEG features, i.e., structural information, and achieved effective model optimization [3, 4, 6, 10]. Deep learning was applied to stack matrix classifiers to yield deep stacked SMM to improve MI-BCI performance [3]. In addition, transferring learning was used to enable model training for a specific subject with limited labeled data by leveraging the EEG data of other subjects with sufficient labeled data [4]. The idea was further extended to develop an adaptive multi-layer model knowledge transfer learning scheme to improve the generalizability and thus reducing the calibration time of BCI systems [6]. Other than using pre-extracted EEG features as input, we proposed deep stacked architecture running on raw EEG data to capture more fully the neural information at the input, in which SMM and common spatial pattern of EEG signals were included [10]. On the other hand, the issue of overfitting caused by the deficiency of MI EEG data was tackled. In this approach, a novel objective function (i.e., loss function) was created for convolutional neural network models by combining categorical cross-entropy and center loss to suppress overfitting, while the ability of deep features in discriminating different movement intentions was also enhanced [9]. Presence of noise, particularly non-Gaussian noise, and outliers is a well-known issue against accurate detection of MI tasks. Following a similar strategy, we developed another novel objective function based on the correntropy induced distance (CID) between features and the corresponding class center. The function, so called correntropy based center loss, was used to learn the class centers while penalizing the CID to get rid of noisy samples and outliers [5]. To ensure the practicality of MI-BCI, we conducted further research to improve the generalizability of MI-BCI so that different users can use the model with minor adaptations only, and model re-training for a specific user can be avoided. For the former, we made use of the EEG data from multiple subjects preforming the same MI tasks to develop a shallow inception domain adaptation network, where marginal and conditional discrepancies of deep features were reduced to achieve good MI task classification performance [8]. For the latter, relation learning was exploited by learning the encoded episodic temporal patterns between trials to avoid the need for model re-training even for a new user [7]. All these models had been evaluated using public domain datasets or EEG data collected by the researchers of the project, i.e., the benchmarking public datasets from the BCI Competitions which are widely adopted in the BCI research community, and the dataset obtained by recording the EEG signals of ten BCI users when they were performing MI of lower limb movements. The performance of the proposed algorithms is competitive with the state-of-the-art algorithms and outperforming them in many cases. The concept of virtual mirror therapy was realized using virtual reality (VR). A virtual environment was built in which limb movement of the avatar (male or female, selectable) was controlled online based on the movement intentions identified using the EEG signals acquired when a user was performing MI tasks [12]. In addition to visual feedback that was provided graphically through the avatar, the virtual environment also provided vibrotactile feedback. A study was conducted to understand the suitable settings for producing vibrotactile stimulation [11]. The findings were then applied during the VR-assisted MI such that user could feel vibrations at their limbs as feedback when the corresponding MI tasks were detected. 15200619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200619.value: The studies in the project demonstrated that deep learning is a promising approach for recognizing movement intentions with EEG signals generated from MI-BCI [3-10]. To boost the performance, we proposed a number of sophisticated approaches to tackle the challenges that existing MI-BCIs are facing. Transfer learning was exploited to leverage the data available from source subjects to model target subjects with limited labeled data [4]. Novel objective functions based on smoothed cross-entropy, correntropy and center loss were proposed to improve the discriminability of deep features and tackle the problem of overfitting caused by limited training data [5, 9]. SMM was used to extract high-level representation of EEG patterns [3, 10]. Adaptive multi-layer transfer mechanism was developed to improve model generalizability so that the major calibration can be avoided for different MI-BCI users [6]. In addition, domain adaption and inception architecture in deep learning were combined to extract distinctive features of MI tasks performed by different individuals [8]. Furthermore, relation learning was adopted to identify the relations between temporal patterns between trials in each episode so that re-training is not required for new users [7]. These models were evaluated with public benchmark MI EEG datasets and data collected experimentally from subject performing lower-limb MI tasks. On the other hand, inheriting the good interpretability of fuzzy systems, multi-view and multi-task TSK FSs were also built to enhance classification accuracy by integrating EEG features from different domains and from different MI tasks [1, 2]. These models were found to outperform many state-of-the-art methods. A VR-based prototype system was built to realize the concept of virtual mirror therapy based on MI-BCI [12], in which vibrotactile stimulation was incorporated based on the settings concluded from a comprehensive review conducted on the relevant studies reported in literatures [11].

15200619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200619.value: In the project, a number of advanced algorithms have been developed successfully for MI tasks involving lower-limb movements, where the detection accuracy and generalizability are enhanced to facilitate practical use of MI-BCI. Further research is needed to demonstrate the feasibility by incorporating the developed algorithms into the VR-based mirror therapy system to investigate more comprehensively the practical performance. Given the variety of the algorithms developed, it is necessary to study the best combination(s), and under what situation(s) that they could give rise to a usable and practical EEG-based BCI. Such studies can be conducted in phase through an ablation analysis by first investigating the BCI performance of each algorithm, followed by different combinations of them. With the optimal algorithm suite identified, the VR-based mirror therapy system has to be further evaluated on people with stroke or paralyzed. The clinical trials are important to assess whether the project can achieve the ultimate goal of providing a practical rehabilitation tool. Controlled trails comparing with the proposed MI-BCI based approach and the conventional treatment methods can be conducted in terms of rehabilitation progress and system usability.

15200619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200619.value: People with neurological diseases may suffer from movement impairment due to inability to transfer muscle-controlling brain signals to the limbs. Brain computer interface (BCI) provides an alternative channel so that brain signals can be acquired directly from scalp, classified by computer algorithms, and then used to control external devices. However, the signals are noisy, and that it is time and labor consuming to acquire the signals. To tackle these issues, the project has developed a number of novel algorithms using fuzzy systems and deep learning respectively as the major framework. The algorithms are evaluated with public benchmark datasets and experimentally acquired data from human subjects, and the performance is found to be competitive with state-of-the-art methods. A virtual reality based rehabilitation system is developed by which users can control avatar movement using their brain signals, while visual and vibrotactile feedback are provided in return. The rehabilitation training process has the potential to promote reorganization of brain structure of people with neurological diseases, thereby assisting them to regain motor ability through repeated practice.

15200719.label: Project Objectives
15200719.value: to understand and identify the fundamental mechanisms of the interactions between transient waves and different pipe anomalies. Four common pipe anomalies of leakage, blockage, unknown junction and cross-sectional deformation are investigated by 1D transfer-matrix analysis and laboratory experiment data analysis; to characterize and distinguish the influences of different anomaly configurations (types and numbers) on transient wave behavior, so as to gain the missing physics and unexpressed knowledge in current transient-based method (e.g., frictional linearization). Laboratory experimental data are analyzed and compared with 1D analysis results to achieve this objective; to incorporate the results and findings from (1) and (2) into existing transient theory, with aim to develop a holistic transient-based method for pipe diagnosis. Systematic and parametric analysis is conducted for this objective; to validate and evaluate the developed method for the detection of different pipe anomalies under various system operations, through extensive numerical simulations and available experimental data.

15200719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15200719.value: In urban water supply systems (UWSS), pipelines usually encounter many different problems that may affect the function and operation of UWSS, such as leakage, corrosion, biofilm and deformation, which are termed as pipe anomalies in this project. The formation and existence of pipe anomalies may result in serious problems, including (but not limited to) the reduction of flow capacity, increase of energy loss and deterioration of water quality. For example, in Hong Kong (HK), the annual cost for water and energy losses of its dual pipeline systems (fresh-water and sea-water) was estimated at over HK$1.5 billion (~US$200 million/year). Therefore, it is urgent to develop effective technologies to diagnose these pipe anomalies in a timely manner, so as to minimize the resultant problems and wastage. Existing methods for pipeline condition assessment have played important roles in resolving such anomalous issues in UWSS, but current critical state of water and energy losses (e.g., over 30% in UWSS worldwide) has evidenced the inadequacy and inefficiency of these methods in improving further the situation. Recently, transient wave-based method, which is thought to be non-intrusive, efficient, and economic, has been developed for pipeline anomaly diagnosis (e.g., leakage and blockage). However, this new method is so far developed only for relatively simple anomalous situations, such as single anomaly, multiple anomalies with known/single type and simplified 1D configuration, which has greatly limited its superiority for practical applications. Consequently, it is important to develop and extend further this promising method to more realistic situations in UWSS. This project is aimed at exploring and characterizing transient wave responses of different pipe anomalies in water pipelines, based on which a holistic transient-based method is developed for tackling more realistic pipeline diagnosis in UWSS, with objectives to: (1) understand and characterize the interaction mechanisms between transient waves and four common types of pipe anomalies (leakage, blockage, unknown junction and cross-sectional deformation); (2) develop a holistic transient-based method for the diagnosis of different pipe anomalies with mixed types and more realistic configurations; and (3) evaluate the validity and accuracy of the developed method for pipe diagnosis in UWSS. The combined methodology of theoretical analysis, numerical simulations and experimental tests (laboratory program and field test-bed) is used in this project. The achievements and deliverables of this project are useful to bridge the gap between transient-based methods and practical applications for pipeline diagnosis in UWSS, which can make advancement of smart UWSS development. 在城市供水系統中，管道經常出現諸多影響其正常運行和操作的異常問題，例如洩漏、腐蝕、生物膜和變形，在本項目中稱之為管道缺陷。這些管道缺陷可能給城市供水系統帶來嚴重的後果，包括（但不限於）降低管道輸水能力、增加系統能量損耗以及引起水質惡化。在香港，這些缺陷普遍存在於其特有的雙管（淡水和海水）供水系統之中，造成大量的水和能量損耗，每年的直接經濟損失逾15億港幣（約2億美元）。因此，急需開發一種快速高效的管道缺陷檢測技術，以緩解產生的問題並降低水和能量的損耗。 現有的管道缺陷檢測技術在城市供水系統中扮演著重要的角色。但是，目前的水和能量損耗狀況越發嚴重（全球平均逾30％），這表明現有的檢測技術存在嚴重不足並且效率低下，以至於無法進一步改善城市供水系統的現狀。最近，一種基於瞬變流壓力波的技術已被用於管道缺陷檢測（例如洩漏和堵塞），該方法具有非侵入、高效和經濟等優點。然而，迄今為止，這種新型方法只能檢測相對簡單的管道缺陷，例如管道中存在單個缺陷或已知類型的多個缺陷，並且，這些缺陷往往被簡化為一維結構，這極大地限制了該方法的實際應用。因此，將這種有應用前景的方法進一步開發並拓展到實際的城市供水管道之中至關重要。 本項目旨在探究和表徵水管中不同管道缺陷的瞬態響應，在此基礎之上，開發一種基於瞬變流的整體方法，用於檢測城市供水系統中更實際的管道缺陷。具體內容為：（1）理解和表徵瞬變流壓力波與四種常見的管道缺陷（洩漏、堵塞、未知連接和管道變形）之間的相互作用機理;（2）開發一種基於瞬變流的整體方法，用於檢測混合類型和具有實際結構的不同管道缺陷;（3）評估所提出的管道缺陷檢測方法在城市供水系統中的有效性和準確性。本項目將採用理論分析、數值模擬和實驗測試（實驗室和現場測試）相結合的研究方法。 本項目取得的研究成果將能夠進一步填補瞬變流理論方法與城市供水系統中實際缺陷檢測之間的技術空白，并將有助於推動智慧型城市供水系統的發展。

15200719.label: Realisation of objectives
15200719.value: All the objectives listed in section 5.2 have been well achieved during this project period. Meanwhile, the research outputs and findings from this project will be useful to provide insights to future research direction of this topic, as well as to the practical applications of the transient flow modeling and analysis in water supply pipe networks. The realization of these objectives can be summarized as below: (1) the numerical models were established by coupling the 1D water hammer models with steady and unsteady friction elements which were then applied to simulate transient flows in water supply pipes under various conditions. Meanwhile, the analytical derivations were performed for different flow conditions in water pipes based on 1D transfer matrix analysis method. The results obtained are reasonable and useful to this application field, which have been published in top journals in this field, such as Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing (MSSP), ASCE Journal of Hydraulic Engineering and so on (which can refer to the outputs in Part C). (2) the derived analytical expressions in (1) were used to characterize the transient-induced patterns of different types of pipe defects. Furthermore, a laboratory experimental test system was designed and set up by the Co-I (Prof. Pedro LEE) for transient pipe flows in different flow and pipe configuration conditions. The pressure data have been secured by the high-resolution transducers (with a sampling frequency of 1kHz), which were used for validating and verifying the established numerical models, as well as for analytical results for this project. (3) based on the validated numerical models and established experimental system, various application cases were carried out for data integration and analysis, so as to provide the fundamental understanding and practical application of transient based detection for different anomalies/defects in water pipes (leakage, blockage, etc.). Meanwhile, the developed analytical expressions and experimental test data from this project have been well packaged for future use. (4) all the key results and findings from this project have been published on the important journals in this field as well as presented in the professional conferences in the community. The details refer to the outputs in Part C of this report. With these research activities and outputs/achievements, the objectives of this project have been well achieved (100%) during the project period.

15200719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200719.value: This project has been achieved to develop a holistic transient-based approach for different pipe defects detection in water supply pipe systems, with aims to: (a) understand the characteristics and the influences of different types of pipe defects on transient wave propagation and evolution in water pipes; (b) explore a holistic method for the detection of different pipe defects/anomalies through the transient wave analysis. The developed model is then calibrated and validated by experimental data obtained in this project; and (c) examine the key factors affecting the transient-defects interactions under different system and flow conditions (including pipe scales, initial flows, different defects and initial transient generations). With achieving these objectives, the main findings mainly include: (1) development of analytical expressions for pipe defects-wave interactions by coupling the 1D transient/waterhammer model and 1D transfer matrix analysis method under different pipe and flow conditions; (2) establishment of a laboratory experimental system for extensive tests, under close collaboration with the Co-I (Prof. Pedro Lee in New Zealand), for calibrating and validating the effectiveness and accuracy of the developed numerical model under different test flow scenarios and system configuration conditions; (3) applications of the validated analytical expressions and holistic pipe defects detection model for various pipe systems and flow conditions, so as to examine the key influence factors affecting the accuracy and validity of the developed method. Based on these results and findings, the main outcomes of this research can be summarized as follows: (i) in total 8 journal papers have been published in key/top journals directly from this project through broad collaborations with local and overseas research groups (see details in Part C), which have provided substantial progress on this topic in this community. (ii) the results and findings have also been presented in front of peers and experts in this field in the international conferences and workshops, so as to gain essential feedback and connections with other research groups. In this regard, 3 conference papers were generated and included in the conference proceedings (details given in Part C). (iii) 1 PhD student and 2 Research Assistants have been successfully trained/graduated (or going to graduate soon) during the project period, and four undergraduate students (2 part-time student assistants and 2 final year project students) have been educated through participating this research project, which is also one of key objectives and outcomes for this project (i.e., young generation education and training purpose). (iv) various external collaborations have been carried out through the research plans of this project, which has led to both international and national connections on this research topic. More details on the publication outputs, young research students training and external collaborations can be found in the Part C of this report.

15200719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200719.value: As stated in the objectives in Section 5 and achievements in Section 6.1, all the key objectives and planned tasks of this project have been well achieved. Through the implementation process of this project, it has been also found that further development of this research can be performed for future work, including (but not limited to): (1) more complex pipeline systems such as pipe networks can be tested and applied for the validity and accuracy of the developed holistic transient-based method for the detection of different pipe defects; (2) more complex surrounding conditions in urban water supply systems can be considered and included in the modeling and testing process of this project, such as buried conditions (soil and water), surface loading and traffic influences, as well as elevation variations of pipelines. To extend such research work, it will involve more practical factors and urban conditions, which requires more collaboration with local government department and authorities so as to gain enough geographical and hydrological/hydraulic information. To this end, an engineering R&D project and/or technology transfer project may be more suitable to continue and extend the results and findings of current project to more realistic and practical systems.

15200719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200719.value: In urban water supply pipeline systems, different types of pipe defects and/or anomalies are commonly existent, which may greatly affect the system function and operation performance. In this context, understanding and investigating an innovative method of different pipe defects detection become urgent and may have great benefits to the industries and cities in both social and economic aspects. To this end, this project develops a holist method that can be used for detection simultaneously different types of defects by using transient flow analysis. This project has been well achieved for the planned objectives and tasks, under the close collaborations with the PI and Co-I, as well as the research student and staff involved in this project. Specifically, effective numerical models, analytical derivations and rigorous experiment tests are developed applied for this investigation. The results and findings obtained from this project are helpful to further development of transient theory and pipe diagnosis method and thus will be useful to effective management of urban water supply pipeline system in Hong Kong and other cities in the world.

15200819.label: Realisation of objectives
15200819.value: This project utilized acoustic waves as an active and pre-filtering technique for acoustic agglomeration. Furthermore, we investigated the thermo-acoustic (TA) effect using various carbon nanotube (CNT) and graphene materials, representing an advancement in sound transducer technology capable of producing sound without the need for a moving surface. It has the potential for scalability, offering a flat-band frequency range and high-intensity sound pressure. To achieve this TA-based approach, the focus was on conducting experimental investigations and exploring the theoretical principles behind different agglomeration mechanisms. The TA effect can be efficiently controlled by an adaptive system that responds to changes in particle interactions. The proposed three objectives of this project have been fully addressed. The major achievements of this research include: • An in-depth analysis of TA sound-generating devices using CNT, 2D planar graphene thin films (2DGTF), and 3D graphene foam (3DGF) materials on a substrate with a 50-µm gap separation was studied [Objective 1]. Experimental studies were carried out to verify the gap separation effect and identify the acoustic performance of both 2DGTF- and 3DGF-based TA devices. The 3DGF materials demonstrated favorable mechanical properties, low resistance, stable sound performance, and robust sound generation. In comparison to the 2DGTF-based TA devices, the 3DGF-based TA devices required a lower driving voltage, similar to that of a conventional magnet-based speaker. Conversely, a high-voltage amplifier was necessary for electrical excitation in 2DGTF due to its high resistance. However, these devices exhibited broadband and stable frequency responses, which cannot be achieved by conventional piezo-type acoustic speakers. • A novel U-shaped acoustic-manipulated design to enhance the working performance of low-efficiency filters for sub-micron particles (0.25-1.0 µm) in mechanically ventilated systems was proposed [Objectives 2 and 3]. Experimental studies were conducted to verify the present design, showing an overall filtration efficiency of up to 89% for 1.0-μm airborne particles when the acoustic-driven device was coupled with a low-grade coarse filter (e.g., MERV-6 filter). As a standalone device, the acoustic effect worked well for the submicron particles with a filtration efficiency of up to 61% under a lower sound pressure level (116 dB), which was not achieved in previous literature. The analysis examined the impact of different aerodynamic effects and acoustic radiation force on sub-micron particles. It also investigated the device’s performance through parametric studies on acoustic frequency, sound pressure level, and flow speed. This investigation offered valuable insights into enhancing the design of a non-invasive pre-filtering approach for air-conditioning ventilation systems, as the design demonstrates a high degree of adaptability to work with various filter types. • The mechanical, thermal, and buckling characteristics of graphene-platelet reinforced materials in thin-walled structures (e.g., plate and arch structures) under various boundary conditions and external loads were investigated [Objective 1]. In addition, an investigation was conducted on a plate with line defect patterns, known as a locally resonant phononic crystal, which consisted of elastic-wrapped core scatterers periodically embedded in epoxy resin, to study energy localization and harvesting. • Computational analysis using an advanced time-marching physics-informed neural network (AT-PINN) approach for the dynamic behaviour of thin-walled structures was introduced [Objective 1]. This study focused on the development of an efficient PINN approach for structural vibration analysis in "long-duration" simulation, which is a technical but unresolved issue of PINN approaches. Using the new approach, the dynamic analysis of a thin plate structure under multi-physics loads (i.e., thermal and acoustic loads) was investigated under a long-duration simulation. On the other hand, transient heat conduction of materials is a dynamic problem that can be classified as an initial value problem. Unlike steady-state heat conduction, it includes the temperature derivative over time, leading to more complex calculations. We incorporated the matched interface and boundary (MIB) method into time integration computation, a new MIB-based time integration (MIBTI) approach was proposed for solving transient heat conduction problems. In contrast to traditional recursive methods for time integration, this is a truly time-domain approach that can solve transformed boundary-value problems to determine all unknown variables. The proposed method was examined using discrete and continuous systems with and without internal heat sources, under various boundary conditions, to evaluate its performance. The project involved theoretical, computational, and experimental studies, and the outcomes exceeded the scope of the objectives. Additionally, there are some relevant research studies supported by this project.

15200819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15200819.value: The significant results of this project have been documented in ten research publications [Journal Papers 1-10]. In this research, we proposed a novel acoustic-driven device [Journal Paper 1]. Previous studies have shown significant progress in dealing with high sound pressure levels (SPLs) of 130-140 dB. However, the issue of high SPLs poses a potential obstacle to the practical application of acoustic-driven techniques in real building environments. Hence, it is needed to achieve breakthroughs in enhancing the removal efficiency of airborne fine particles, particularly sub-micron particles, at lower SPLs. To address this, we developed a simple U-shaped device, known as double resonant acoustic chambers, which can operate at lower SPLs (116 dB) to enhance the filtration efficiency of sub-micron particles using low-grade filters. This technique is based on a unique airflow configuration in a ventilation duct, where fluid flows in parallel but sound waves move in opposite directions. Our study included both numerical analysis and experimental research, with the numerical analysis providing design guidelines for the experimental work, such as the working conditions of loudspeakers and the dimensions of the U-shaped device. In the experimental part, a testing prototype was assembled to verify the filtration efficiency of submicron particles in the presence of acoustic waves. Additionally, we demonstrated that a high filtration efficiency can be achieved when the acoustic-driven technique is used in conjunction with a commercial MERV-grade filter. We delved into the details of how particulate matter filtration can be achieved by the acoustic-based pre-filter. Furthermore, we investigated innovative TA devices designed using graphene-based materials (i.e., 2D planar graphene thin films (2DGTF) and 3D graphene foam (3DGF)) [Journal Paper 7], with the 3DGF-based devices showing favorable mechanical properties compared to the 2DGTF-based devices. The 3DGF-based TA devices required a lower driving voltage, similar to that of a traditional magnet-based speaker. Conversely, a high-voltage amplifier was necessary for electrical excitation in 2DGTF due to its high resistance. However, TA devices based on both 2DGTF and 3DGF exhibited stable and broadband frequency acoustic responses, a capability that piezo-type speakers cannot achieve. All studies involved proof-of-concept, prototype design, theoretical analysis, and experimental work. Under the support of this project, it has also resulted in additional outcomes in the investigation of mechanical and thermal properties of graphene-based materials [Journal Papers 2-6] and the computational analysis of thin-walled structures under thermal and acoustic effects [Journal Papers 8-10], further contributing to advancements in this research.

15200819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15200819.value: The potential for advancing the research using a novel acoustic-driven manipulation technique as a pre-treatment, active, and non-invasive engineering control filtration strategy is substantial. This method has the potential to provide a more effective and environmentally friendly approach to managing the movement and separation of sub-micron particles. One potential area for further development involves exploring the utilization of different acoustic frequencies and amplitudes to enhance the manipulation of particles in diverse filtration systems. This may entail conducting experiments to identify the most efficient acoustic parameters for various particle types and filtration media. Additionally, research efforts can focus on creating advanced control systems to precisely adjust the acoustic manipulation for specific filtration applications. Another potential avenue for development is the integration of acoustic-driven manipulation with other filtration technologies, such as membrane filtration or electrostatic precipitation. By combining these methods, it might be possible to achieve even higher levels of filtration efficiency and particle separation. Furthermore, collaboration with industry partners and stakeholders would be crucial to ensure that the technology is developed in a manner that aligns with the requirements of real-world potential applications.

15200819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15200819.value: Studies have demonstrated that in indoor settings with insufficient ventilation, the short-range airborne transmission of viruses can extend to long-range, leading to individuals becoming infected and a decline in air quality. Airborne viruses can be transmitted through dust, fibers, and other microscopic particles, as air serves as the main transporter of contaminants and airborne particulates. In commercial and office buildings, where there is a high risk of infection among individuals in close proximity, central air-conditioning mechanical ventilation systems are essential in removing viral particles from the air and ensuring proper ventilation. While the use of filtration methods in ventilation air ducts is an effective strategy for reducing virus transmission and cross-infection, the practical implementation of such techniques presents technological challenges, including filtration efficiency and energy consumption. To address these challenges, advancements in material technology offer new opportunities for significant progress in acoustic engineering fields. This project has developed a novel acoustic-driven manipulation technique as a pre-treatment, active, and non-invasive engineering control filtration strategy to improve indoor environmental health.

15201419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201419.value: Fiber-based wearable thermoelectric (TE) energy conversion systems comprise a new type of flexible solid-state generator devices that convert between thermal and electric energy by Seebeck and Peltier effects. They have great potentials in applications such as waste heat recovery, power source for wearable microelectronic systems as well as active microclimate control by personalized smart apparel systems. In order to realize these novel generator devices, we must overcome the shortage of suitable TE materials, one of the great difficulties. These TE materials should possess high thermoelectric performance working in a range close to room or body temperature, flexible, stable, capable of being processed with polymer fibers materials at low temperature, and preferably fabricated by solution routes. We have recently demonstrated that thermoelectric performance of homogeneous particle-polymer composites can reach or even surpass that of the pure constituent thermoelectric material. However, the mechanisms of this interaction in the composite systems remain elusive. Up to date, existing theoretical treatments, often not verified by experiments, have had conflicting conclusions regarding to the effective properties of thermoelectric composites. Solid scientific understanding and quantitative analysis are necessary to address several key fundamental issues. What are the ideal composite structures for high effective thermoelectric performance as well as flexibility? What are the influences of constituent materials, connectivity, volume fraction, orientations of TE particle and interface in the order of importance? In this proposed project, we will attempt to probe these questions. Theoretical models of homogeneous, layered and modular TE composites made from two constituent materials will be developed, in order to predict the effective properties of the composites in terms of TE properties of the constituent materials, connectivity, volume fraction, orientations of TE particle and interface condition. The project will deliver a series of high-performance thermoelectric composites and their precursors that are suitable to be applied for fiber assemblies such as textile fabrics via room- or low-temperature processes. The results from numeric simulation based on the theoretical models will be compared with measurement results of the TE composites thus verifying the theoretical work. Finally, a fiber-based thermoelectric generator prototype will be designed, made from the optimized TE composites and evaluated for wearable thermal energy harvesting applications. The research is most likely to generate new fundamental knowledge in TE materials, innovative technologies for high performance TE composites and wearable products with fiber-based TE generators. Publications in top-tier scientific journals and patents will be the anticipated deliverables. 基於塞貝克和珀耳帖物理效應所構建的織物基可穿戴熱電能量轉換器件可有效的實現熱能和電能之間的相互轉換。作為一種新型的柔性固態能源轉換裝置，其在廢熱回收、可穿戴微電子系統的電源供給、以及個性化智慧服裝系統的主動微氣候控制等方面具有巨大的應用潛力。然而在目前，尋找適用於可穿戴能量轉換應用的熱電材料依然存在很多困難。首先，適用於可穿戴器件的熱電材料需要在接近室溫或體溫的範圍內具有很高熱電轉換性能，其次，材料本身應具有良好的柔性及穩定性，加工工藝應簡單易行，且能夠在較低的溫度下通過溶液法與聚合物纖維進行同時加工。 在我們近期的研究中發現，通過採用納米熱電材料與聚合物進行複合可得到具有均相結構的高性能柔性熱電複合材料，其性能甚至能達到以及超過純組分熱電材料的熱電性能。稍顯不足的是，複合材料體系中組分之間的相互作用機制尚不清楚。迄今為止，現有的理論處理（通常未經實驗驗證）對熱電複合材料的有效性能有相互矛盾的結論。我們必須有扎實的科學理解和定量分析來解決幾個關鍵的基本問題。例如，高效熱電性能和靈活性的理想複合結構是哪些組成材料，連線性，體積分數，TE顆粒的取向和介面的對性能有何影響？ 針對上述問題，我們在該專案中擬通過建立基於均相複合體系熱電材料的理論模型，對熱電材料在聚合物基體中的分散、層與層之間的排列、連線性，體積分數，取向性以及介面相互關係進行詳細研究。並將開發一系列可在室溫或者低溫條件下應用於紡織品表面的高性能柔性熱電材料。通過對熱電複合材料的理論模型與實際測試結果進行相互比較，進一步驗證以及優化理論模型。最後，將設計一種基於優化後的熱電材料所製備的織物基可穿戴熱電能量轉換器件，並針對該器件的熱電轉換性能進行應用評估。 這項研究有望拓寬業內對熱電材料領域的基本理解，開發高性能熱電複合材料的創新技術以及製備可穿戴纖維基熱電轉換產品。我們預期將把研究成果發表於在頂級期刊，並將申請專利。
