15201419.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201419.value: We have designed, fabricated and characterized a series of TE composites and their precursors comprising two phases of constituents, that is, p-type and p-type TE particles with electrically conductive polymers for 3D printing by controlling the volume fraction, interface and layer/module dimensional parameters of the TE composites. We developed a high performance flexible thermoelectric generator made of the polymeric thermoelectric composites and heat sink fabrics. The thermoelectric composites comprise n- and p-type Bi2Te3 particles and poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate, exhibiting a synergic effect that results in Seebeck coefficients higher than those of the constituent alloys and conductive polymer. The flexible and light thermoelectric generator produces an output power of 9.0 mW, a specific output power of 2.3 mW/g, and an areal power density of 6.5 W/m2 at ΔT = 45 K. By using the heat sink fabrics to maintain a large and uniform distribution of temperature difference across the generator, a three-fold increment of the output power is obtained. We discovered a universal phenomenon of giant Seebeck coefficient during the phase transtion of polymer TE materials. We further studied the mechanism and proposed a model that deals with the whole process. Six factors influencing the huge variation of the thermopower during the phase-transition were probed.

15201419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15201419.value: Further development of the work has been collaboratively carried out with former team members. Proposals have been submitted for industrial applications of the results.

15201419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201419.value: In this project, we successfully developed high performance thermoelectric polymer composites that can be used for printing by controlling the material and structural parameters of the TE composites. We further developed a high performance flexible thermoelectric generator made of the polymeric thermoelectric composites and heat sink fabrics. The flexible and light thermoelectric generator produced an output power of 9.0 mW at ΔT = 45 K. By using the heat sink fabrics to maintain a large and uniform distribution of temperature difference across the generator, a three-fold increment of the output power was obtained. Furthermore, we discovered a universal phenomenon of giant Seebeck coefficient during the phase transition of polymer TE materials. We further studied the mechanism and proposed a model that deals with the whole process with six factors influencing the huge variation of the thermopower during the phase-transition and shed new light on the possible gigantic changes of thermopower during the phase transition. Hence, a possible route was uncovered to design and control the desired thermoelectric performances of materials, which can lead to a new sight in tunable TE devices for low-heat energy harvesting applications.

15201719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15201719.value: 蜘蛛牽引絲（SDS）因其同時具有高強度、高模量、高延展性以及高韌性，使得它們在製造航太服、防彈背心、降落傘、醫療設備和特種繩索等高性能應用中成為最理想的材料。然而，儘管全球的科學家們已經做出了巨大的努力，特別是在蜘蛛絲蛋白（蛛絲蛋白）的基因工程領域，到目前為止，人工SDS的大規模生產仍然是一個夢想。從可規模化生產和成本的角度來看，化學合成途徑是製造人造蜘蛛絲模型（SSM）聚合物（即人造蛛絲蛋白）的理想方法。目前有限的人造蜘蛛絲蛋白化學合成方法的主要問題是：（1）合成過程效率低; （2）人造蛛絲蛋白的分子量低; （3）所得纖維/聚合物的機械性能極不令人滿意。基於我們最近在聚多肽-聚氨酯/脲中取得的成就，即一種具有10倍普通聚氨酯強度的可拉伸的含有氨基酸的聚合物，以及受到蜘蛛絲多級結構的啟發，我們提出了一種簡單有效的化學合成方法構建全氨基酸（AAA）、高分子量蜘蛛絲模型（SSM）聚合物的方法，並以期通過仿生紡絲工藝製備具有SDS性能的人造纖維。 為了達到上述目的，我們將首先使用氨基酸的開環聚合（ROP）製備必需的具有蜘蛛絲蛋白結構的聚多肽片段：β-折疊和α-螺旋多肽，然後通過賴氨酸二異氰酸酯形成的微小的脲鍵（橋鍵）來連接它們，從而合成出全氨基酸聚合物/共聚肽，即人造蜘蛛絲蛋白。橋鍵與蛋白質主鏈中的肽鍵相似，並且合成效率高，從而可實現聚合物的高分子量和可規模化的生產。之後將使用諸如傅立葉轉移紅外，透射和掃描顯微鏡以及原子解析度斷層掃描等先進技術研究人造蛛絲蛋白的分子自組裝形成的一級至四級結構。仿生幹法紡絲將確保纖維形成過程中的原纖多級結構的形成。不同因素包括化學成分，紡絲條件，β-晶體，α-螺旋和非晶區等對纖維強度，模量和伸長率等力學性能的影響將被系統地研究。本專案的提出將直接提供SSM材料的有效製備方法，並為理解蛋白質材料的組成 - 結構 - 性質關係和多級結構提供研究依據。更重要的是，這項工作將為加快商業化進程奠定堅實的基礎，從而實現人造蜘蛛絲材料的夢想。

15201719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15201719.value: The research project on artificial spidroin-based hierarchical structural formation yielded several major findings and outcomes, including: 1. Successful Fabrication of SSM Polymers: The researchers were able to design and fabricate synthetic polymers with the capability to form hierarchical structures similar to spider dragline silks. This achievement marked a significant step forward in biomimicry and advanced materials science. (No. 1, 4, 6, Part. C) 2. Insights into Molecular Assembly Mechanisms: Through advanced characterization techniques, the project shed light on the molecular assembly mechanisms of artificial spidroins. Understanding the bonding energy, α-helices, β-sheet, β-turn, random coils, and higher-order building blocks contributed to a deeper comprehension of these innovative materials. (No. 2, 9, Part. C) 3. Development of Hierarchical SSM Fibers: The project's bionic spinning process successfully induced hierarchical structural formation in SSM spidroins, resulting in the creation of artificial spidroin fibers. These fibers exhibited properties reminiscent of natural spider dragline silk, including strength and flexibility. (No. 1, 5, Part C) 4. Performance Evaluation of SSM Silks: The performance investigation demonstrated that the SSM silks achieved a balanced fineness, high strength, Young's modulus, and extensibility, comparable to natural spider dragline silk. This outcome has promising implications for various industries seeking stronger and more flexible materials. (No. 1,2, 4, 5, 9, Part. C) Overall, the research project significantly advanced the field of artificial spidroin-based materials, offering a foundation for further developments in biomimicry, advanced textiles, biomedical applications, and other industries where strong, flexible, and sustainable materials are in demand. These findings have the potential to drive innovation, inspire new technologies, and contribute to a greener, more sustainable future.

Optimization of Artificial Spidroin Properties: Further research can focus on refining the design and fabrication process of SSM polymers to enhance their mechanical properties, such as tensile strength, elasticity, and biocompatibility. This will be crucial in tailoring the materials for specific applications in industries like textiles, medicine, and beyond. 2. Scaling up Production: The project's success in creating artificial spidroin fibers through a bionic spinning process lays the foundation for scaling up production. Exploring methods for large-scale manufacturing can make these innovative materials more accessible and commercially viable. 3. Exploring New Applications: Investigating novel applications for artificial spidroin-based materials in fields like aerospace, construction, and environmental protection can unlock additional value and impact. 5. Eco-friendly and Sustainable Alternatives: Emphasizing the development of environmentally friendly processes and biodegradable materials aligns with the growing global demand for sustainable solutions.

15201719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15201719.value: The research project aimed to create synthetic materials that mimic the structure and properties of spider silk, which is known for its remarkable strength and flexibility. This involved designing and fabricating artificial spider silk-like polymers and understanding how they are assembled at the molecular level. By using advanced techniques, the researchers were able to produce fibers with hierarchical structures, similar to those found in natural spider silk. This research is significant because it opens up exciting possibilities in various fields. Artificial spider silk materials could be used to make stronger and more flexible textiles, medical implants, and even eco-friendly alternatives to plastic. These materials have the potential to revolutionize industries, leading to more durable and sustainable products. Moreover, studying the molecular assembly of these materials helps us understand nature's remarkable design and inspires us to develop innovative solutions to real-world problems. In summary, this research project's value lies in creating advanced materials that imitate nature's design, offering numerous applications and promoting a greener, more sustainable future.

15202019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15202019.value: Shipping is the most cost-effective way to move goods around the world, and annually, over 80% of worldwide trade volume is carried by sea. However, the shipping industry is mainly powered by diesel oil, which creates a heavy environmental footprint due to the emission of polluting substances, such as sulfur oxides (SOx), nitrogen oxides (NOx) and particulate matter (PM). Concerned with the issues of environmental pollution, the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and governments have instituted increasingly stringent regulatory measures for the shipping industry to control and reduce adverse impacts on the environment. As a cost-competitive and clean marine fuel, liquefied natural gas (LNG) is currently the most promising solution to achieve environmentally friendly shipping. LNG technology, which complies with existing and upcoming air emission requirements, significantly reduces pollutant emissions in comparison with diesel oil. To adopt LNG as a marine fuel on a global scale, several issues should be addressed. A fundamental and inherent issue is the limited number of ports with LNG bunkering infrastructure (LNGBI). Ships with LNG-fueled engines have to deviate from their planned routes to refuel LNG at a long distance, which significantly increases the sailing time and operating cost that discourage shipping lines from investing in or utilizing LNG-fueled ships. Accordingly, many national governments seek to accelerate the uptake of LNG as a marine fuel by establishing LNG bunkering infrastructures at ports (LNGBIs). Hence, it is vital to formulate a long-term deployment plan of setting up LNGBIs at different ports to achieve eco-friendliness. Another major issue is the limited budget: an LNGBI costs over 100 million euros and funds that governments can invest in LNGBIs are limited. Therefore, the deployment plan to establish LNGBIs in a country/region should take into account the best use of limited funds stage by stage. The aim of this project is to develop an LNGBI deployment plan for government that could promote wide adoption of LNG and ultimately attain a significant reduction in shipping emissions. A multistage optimization framework will be developed to capture the effects of the deployment of LNGBIs by government on the uptake of LNG by shipping lines. A case study of ports in China (including the Port of Hong Kong) will be conducted to formulate policy measures. This project will contribute to an environmentally friendly maritime industry by reducing air pollution. 海運業每年承擔全球貿易額80%的貨運量。然而，船舶排放了大量的硫氧化物、氮氧化物和顆粒物。國際海事組織和各國政府制定了越來越嚴格的船舶尾氣排放管制措施。液化天然氣作為一種性價比高而清潔的船舶燃料引起了廣泛關注。在全球範圍內大規模使用液化天然氣作為船舶燃料尚需克服幾個困難。一個根本性的問題是能夠為船舶提供液化天然氣加注服務的港口數量有限。因此，船舶可能需要繞路進行液化天然氣加注，增加了運營成本。港口液化天然氣加注設施的建設成本非常高昂。因此很多國家政府補貼港口建設液化天然氣加注設施。如何有效利用有限的資金進行最優的液化天然氣加注設施佈局規劃以減少海運排放是一個亟待解決的問題。本課題將提出一個多階段優化模型進行液化天然氣加注設施佈局規劃，促進船舶減排。將針對中國港口（包括香港港）做一個案例分析，以提供政策建議。本課題對清潔航運具有推動作用。

15202019.label: Realisation of objectives
15202019.value: To achieve Objective 1, a thorough literature review on data analytics for fuel consumption management in maritime transportation was conducted to help sketch the fuel consumption scenarios of different marine fuels, which is critical to liquefied natural gas (LNG) usage in shipping. Fuel consumption prediction models were reviewed in three groups, namely white-box models, black-box models, and grey-box models, according to the prediction basis. Ship operation optimization models based on fuel consumption prediction results were also presented and discussed. After analyzing and comparing these models, we identified the current research challenges, potential research questions on ship performance monitoring and operational optimizations. With the knowledge about consumption rates of marine fuels, we further evaluated adopting LNG as marine fuel for propulsion from the shipping company’s perspective. Based on the evolutionary game theory, a mathematical model for transport service pricing problem considering market competition, LNG investment, and price elasticity was proposed. The preference of shippers for LNG powered ships was also considered. Two liner shipping companies, which aim to maximize their own profit, compete in the shipping market while making LNG investment decisions. It was revealed that with stringent emission regulations, LNG strategy is more beneficial and will be chosen by the majority of liner companies. Given the profit evaluation, we found that the high initial investments are the main barrier to the extensive application of LNG-fueled ships. In practice, for the environmental benefits, governments tend to provide subsidies to cover the high initial investments. Therefore, we investigated the subsidy design optimization problem of LNG bunkering for maritime transportation from the government’s perspective, identifying the subsidy amount and recipients. Based on the characteristics of LNG bunkering, two-stage mixed subsidy plans were proposed with optimization models that aims to minimize the total subsidy amount while achieving the LNG promotion target. Analytical solutions, which provide more details of the relationship between parameters and optimal solutions than numerical ones, were obtained under various scenarios, including cases with homogeneous and heterogeneous ships. Compared to the homogeneous case, flexible subsidy plan that customizes subsidy amount for each recipient further reduces the total subsidy amount. Besides, we also explored the LNG bunkering price optimization and figured out the impacts of LNG purchasing price and traditional marine fuel bunkering price on the optimal LNG bunkering price. Conclusions gained from analytical solutions in our study and the logical judgement, as we predicted, corroborated each other. In Objective 2, we determined the LNG bunkering infrastructure (LNGBI) deployment plan. In practice, LNG bunkering amount and environmental benefits achieved depend on the deployment of LNG-fueled vessels, and therefore we investigated the joint planning of fleet deployment of dual-fueled ships considering methane slip from the shipping company’s perspective. A nonlinear mixed-integer programming model was developed to describe the joint problem. While making multiple management decisions, the shipping company takes both main and auxiliary engines, ship carbon emissions, and availability of LNG at different ports of call in to account. A tailored linearization method containing multiple techniques was proposed to convert the original model into a linear one that can be solved by off-the-shelf solvers. Abundant numerical experiments were performed to validate the model and solution method proposed. Focusing on price difference between low sulfur fuel oil (LSFO) and LNG, carbon tax, and methane slip amount, sensitivity analyses were conducted to investigate the influences of critical parameter values on operation decisions and the optimal solution. Results indicated that the economic advantage of LNG from the lower density and higher calorific value becomes more obvious with a higher price of LSFO. It was revealed that methane slip is still a critical issue in the deployment of LNG-fueled ships, which may setoff the economic profit of using LNG as marine fuel and discourage shipping companies. However, no close relationship between carbon tax and LNG adoption was found, by reason of the small gap of carbon emissions between LNG and LSFO. Based on the obtained knowledge about ship deployment, we investigated the LNGBI deployment problem by figuring out the governmental subsidy plan modeling and optimization for LNG as fuel for maritime transportation from the government’s perspective. Taking the operation decisions of different stakeholders into consideration, a tri-level model consisting of the government level, the port level, and the ship level was proposed to describe the subsidy plan optimization problem, which aims to maximize the social benefit. In each level, the stakeholders act on behalf of their own interest, based on which a tailored solution method was proposed to solve the problem. Having port group that manages all ports as the leader and ship operators that operating independently as the followers, we converted the bilevel-structured problem between these two parties into an equivalent single level one and then enumerated all possible subsidy plans to identify the optimal subsidy rates for ports and shipping lines. Abundant numerical experiments were performed to validate our model and solution method. The comparison between cases with and without government subsidies showed the huge benefit of using LNG as marine fuel and demonstrated the necessity and efficiency of a well-thought-out government subsidy plan. Results also showed that a higher subsidy rate for ports or shipping lines do not necessarily lead to higher social benefit. The government must balance environmental revenue and subsidy expenditure to obtain the optimal government subsidy plan. Besides, it is important to determine the subsidy amount wisely, and subsidizing at both the port and ship levels is more efficient than focusing on just one of them. Afterall, the consumption of LNG will soar with both complete bunkering system and large demand. The influence of other critical parameters on the optimal solution were investigated, too. In the last phase, to validate the models, algorithms, and analyses obtained in our studies, a case study of the LNGBI deployment problem on the real Chinese container shipping network was performed. Standing at the point of the government, we tried to identify the locations of LNGBIs that can minimize the annual emission costs from the shipping lines considered in the case of China. In this case study, the government aims to build an LNG bunkering system that can promote LNG usage efficiently. Given the availability of LNG bunkering service, shipping lines decide the type and number of ships to be deployed and their sailing speeds. Based on the shipping lines operated by the biggest shipping company in China, the China COSCO Shipping (Group) Company, we built the Chinese container shipping network, whose scale obviously exceeds those of previous studies. To be specific, 43 container ports (including the Port of Hong Kong) and 44 sailing routes that cover China’s coastline and the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area were considered. Results showed that with 14 ports providing LNG bunkering service, including the port of Hong Kong, 38 shipping routes will switch from traditional ships to dual-fueled ships. The deployment plan turned to be cost-effective when the durability of the LNGBIs was considered. Besides, it was also revealed that lowering the LNG bunkering price and the station construction costs help to promote the adoption of LNG as well as allocating a large budget.

15202019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202019.value: First, we adopted the evolutionary game theory to evaluate LNG as marine fuel. A mathematical model for transport service pricing problem was proposed, considering market competition, LNG investment, price elasticity. We proved that LNG strategy is beneficial for shipping companies facing stringent emission regulations, and the high initial investments were identified as the main barrier to the promotion of LNG-fueled ships. We investigated the subsidy design optimization problem of LNG bunkering for maritime transportation from the government’s perspective. Two-stage mixed subsidy plans with optimization models determining the subsidy amount and the recipients were proposed. Analytical solutions obtained show the superiority of flexible subsidy plans and the impacts of LNG purchasing price and traditional marine fuel bunkering price on the optimal LNG bunkering price. From the shipping company’s perspective, we investigated the joint planning problem of fleet deployment of dual-fueled ships considering methane slip. A nonlinear mixed-integer programming model was developed. We proposed a tailored linearization method containing multiple techniques to convert the original model into a linear one that can be solved by off-the-shelf solvers. Numerical experiments were performed to validate the model and solution method proposed. Results indicated that the economic advantage of LNG is closely related to the price of LSFO and methane slip rate. We investigated the LNGBI deployment problem by figuring out the governmental subsidy plan modeling and optimization from the government’s perspective. A tri-level model consisting of the government level, the port level, and the ship level was proposed to maximize the social benefit. A tailored solution method was developed to convert the multilevel-structured problem into an equivalent single level one. Abundant numerical experiments were performed, and the results show the huge benefit of using LNG as marine fuel. Besides, the government must balance environmental revenue and subsidy expenditure to obtain the optimal subsidy plan. In addition, subsidizing both the ports and ships is more efficient than focusing on just one of them. We performed a case study of the LNGBI deployment problem on the real Chinese container shipping network, based on the shipping lines operated by the biggest shipping company in China, China COSCO Shipping. Specifically, 43 container ports and 44 sailing routes were considered. With 14 ports providing LNG bunkering service, including the port of Hong Kong, 38 shipping routes will turn to dual-fueled ships. The deployment plan was also cost-effective when the durability of the LNGBIs was considered.

15202019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202019.value: Uncertainty in fuel prices can be incorporated into the joint planning of fleet deployment, ship refueling, and speed optimization for dual-fuel ships. In addition, other alternative marine fuels, such as hydrogen and biofuels, can be considered. Other emission regulations like maritime emission trading system, can be integrated into the model. To investigate the integrated stochastic problem, optimization model considering the uncertain fuel prices will be developed. Prediction methods will be adopted to capture the possible scenarios of fuel prices. A tailored algorithm based on the problem structure will be proposed. Competitions in the port level and ship level can be integrated into the subsidy optimization problem. The competition between ports in the LNG and traditional marine fuel bunkering market and the shipping companies’ competition for cargoes in the freight market will bring new challenges. Besides, more in-depth research on subsidy plan with more complicated priorities can be investigated in the future. Regarding the competitions in different layers, game theory models will be developed in future research. Meanwhile, with the more complicated priorities, the problem complexity will increase. More efficient solution methods will be required to handle the interrelationships between different stakeholders.

15202019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202019.value: As the most cost-effective transportation method, the shipping industry covers over 80% of worldwide trade volume. However, ships are mainly powered by diesel oil with high emission level of polluting substances. Therefore, as one of the cleanest fossil energy sources for ship, LNG becomes the most promising alternative marine fuel to alleviate the pollutant problem. Currently, the lack of adequate LNG bunkering infrastructures (LNGBIs) is hindering the promotion of LNG. Hence, this project investigated the deployment problem of LNGBIs to accelerate the process, taking government subsidy as a promising way to reduce the financial burden caused by the high construction costs. We have evaluated LNG as marine fuel from the shipping company’s perspective. Investing in LNG-fueled ships was proved to be beneficial for shipping companies under stringent emission regulations. Studying the joint planning problem of fleet deployment of dual-fueled ships, we identified the external factors that affect LNG’s economic advantages. We also investigated the subsidy design and deployment plan optimization problems of LNGBIs from the government’s perspective to give constructive managerial insights. A case study of a Chinese container shipping network, including Hong Kong, was conducted to validate the models and algorithms proposed in this project and yield practical suggestions.

15202119.label: Project Objectives
15202119.value: Synthesize GTP-loaded, multi-responsive MCH NPs. The NPs will be modified with (a) cathepsin B/MMP-9-cleavable anti-bacterial poly-β-peptides, (b) targeting ligand CycloRGD and (c) MMP-9-detachable PEG-PCL corona. The resultant NPs are expected to have dual-targeting (anti-bacteria and anti-tumor), bioresponsive and programmed site-specific drug release properties. Characterize and optimize the chemical, drug release and biological properties of the synthesized MCH NPs in vitro. We will first investigate the effects of various parameters (e.g., size and porosity of the MCH NPs, chain lengvth of PEG-PCL and grafting density of different functional groups) on the drug release profile. We will then fine-tune these parameters to achieve optimal drug loading capacity and drug release rates. We will further assess the cellular uptake, cytotoxicity and anti-bacterial activity against Mycoplasma hyorhinis of the synthesized MCH NPs. The established correlation between the drug release and the biological responses will help with the NP design and ultimately achieve the dual (anti-bacteria and anti-tumor) functions.

15202119.label: Realisation of objectives
15202119.value: In this project, we proposed to fabricate a dual-targeting (anti-bacteria and anti-cancer) and programmed site-specific mesoporous nanoparticle (NPs)-based drug delivery system for treatment of pancreatic cancer. Due to the high cost of anti-bacterial poly-B-peptides, we used nano-silver with broad-spectrum antibacterial properties to kill y-proteobacteria in pancreatic cancer instead. We prepared mesoporous hydroxyapatite (HA) -based NPs doped with silver ions (Ca10-xAg2x(PO4)6(OH)2, x=0, 0.5, 1,1.5), denoted as AgHA, for combating the bacteria in pancreatic cancer environment. Next, we synthesized gemcitabine (Gem)-loaded silver doped mesoporous HA NPs by incorporating Ag and GEM during the HA synthesis process, denoted as Gem-AgHA. Then we modified the GEM-AgHA with a polydopamine (PDA) thin layer (P@Gem-AgHA) followed by conjugation with CycloRGD peptide (RP@Gem-AgHA) and with matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9)-cleavable NH2-polyethylene glycol (MMP-PEG) (Mn = 1500 - 2000) chain to enhance the targeted GEM delivery and prolong its circulation time, respectively. Hence, GEM-loaded, multi-responsive NRs grafted with Ag and Cyclo(RGD) ligands surrounded by an MMP-PEG were obtained (MRP@Gem-AgHA). Upon injection, the MMP-PEG shell protects the nanoparticles from leakage or degradation in circulation. As they reach the MMP-rich tumor site, the shell will be broken down to expose the RGD peptides, which selectively bind to integrins over-expressed on pancreatic cancer cells to facilitate cellular uptake. The engulfed NPs will gradually be degraded by lysosomal cathepsin B enzymes, releasing Ag ions to exert bacterial inhibition against intracellular Gammaproteobacteria. The disabled bacteria will no longer be able to inactivate the loaded gemcitabine released in high capacity from the mesopores of HA NPs. The unimpeded gemcitabine would then be able to promote apoptosis in actively dividing cells by inhibiting DNA synthesis and blocking DNA strand elongation in the nucleus, successfully suppressing tumor growth (Figure 1). XRD was used to characterize the crystalline structure of all the HA groups (Figure 2), showing a strong peak at around 31.9 degrees corresponding to the 211 plane of HA crystalline structure with good accordance with the XRD pattern of the HA and Ag standards available from the Joint Committee on Powder Diffraction Standards (JCPDS; standard number 84-1998, 04-0783). Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS) was performed to characterize the elements present in HA NPs (Figure 3, 4). Ag was absent in base HA NPs but were significantly expressed in AgHA, showing that the doping was successful. FTIR was used to characterize the functional groups on the surface of HA NPs (Figure 5A). The phosphate peaks at 1050 cm-1 in all groups verified the integral chemical composition of HA while Raman Spectroscopy was used to further characterize the functional groups of HA NPs showing C=C and O-H stretches (Figure 5B). XPS was used to verify the chemical structures of HA groups, showing that the Ca : Ag and Ca + Ag : P ratios were within expected values (Figure 5C). The peak of Ag3d binding energy demonstrated Ag ion chelation with HA, while the peak of F1s binding energy showed gemcitabine adhesion with AgHA. Dynamic light scattering (DLS) was used to characterize the size properties and zeta potential of all HA groups. Results demonstrated that particle size were approximately 184.7 nm-252.0 nm, and the surface modifications on the NPs did not alter the size properties, showing that there was no additional aggregation induced in NPs (Figure 5D, 6). Next, Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analysis was performed to quantify the surface properties of different HA groups (Figure 5E-F, 7). The overall specific surface area and pore volume of the mesoporous HA reduced with each loading and surface functionalization step, suggesting that the modifications were successful. Finally, gemcitabine and Ag+ release profile was conducted to find the release kinematics of different HA groups in different pH conditions (pH 7, 6, 4) (Figure 5G-L). Gem-AgHA exhibited substantial burst release on the first 3 days while P@Gem-AgHA, RP@Gem-AgHA, MRP@Gem-AgHA exhibited sustained release over 14 days, showing that surface modification of HA NPs greatly reduced leakage and burst release properties. Meanwhile Ag+ exhibited sustained release for all HA groups under all pH conditions over 14 days. After verifying the physical and chemical properties of our HA groups, we assessed their biological characteristics (Figure 8). HA showed no cytotoxicity when incubated with PANC-1 cells, indicating its suitability for drug delivery. Additionally, AgHA displayed effective anti-bacterial activity against C. freundii and P. putida(Figure 9). The 20% Ag group exhibited the highest anti-tumor efficacy (Figure 9). To assess the anti-tumor activity of AgHA, different concentrations of AgHA were synthesized and incubated with PANC-1 cells, where the 20% Ag group showed the highest anti-tumor activity (Figure 10). Gem-HA formulations demonstrated superior anti-tumor effects compared to free gemcitabine (Figure 11). Next, we assessed the anti-tumor activity of both agents combined in HA NPs (Figure 12). Combining both agents in HA NPs enhanced tumor suppression, with MRP@Gem-AgHA showing the most significant effect by improving intracellular uptake and inducing cell death (Figure 13). To visualize the anti-tumor effects of our delivery system against pancreatic cancer cells, HA groups were co-cultured with PANC-1 cells over 3 days (Figure 14, 15). We found that MRP@Gem-AgHA exhibited the highest tumor suppression through both increased intracellular uptake of HA NPs and death expression in cell population, thereby verifying that our system was highly effective at facilitating gemcitabine delivery to tumor cells. To validate our delivery system in a living system, we initially used a pancreatic cancer model in female nude mice, replacing Gem with DiD during NP synthesis (Figure 16). By administering free DiD and various HA groups to the mice via the tail vein, we tracked the distribution of NPs using in vivo fluorescence imaging over 24 hours (Figure 17). Mice treated with PR@DiD-AgHA, PM@DiD-AgHA, and PRM@DiD-AgHA displayed specific fluorescence in the abdominal area near the pancreas. Upon organ examination, the PC-targeting ligand CycloRGD (RP@DiD-AgHA and MRP@DiD-AgHA) exhibited significant DiD signals in the tumors. Adding the sustained release ligand MMP-PEG2000 to MRP@DiD-AgHA enhanced drug confinement to the tumor, reducing dispersion to non-target sites(Figure 18, 19). Histological study using proliferative activity marker Ki-67 antibody staining assay showed similar findings, with substantial inhibition of tumor cell proliferative activity found in the integration of MP@Gem-AgHA, RP@Gem-AgHA or MRP@Gem-AgHA when compared to those treated with saline, GEM, or MRP@AgHA alone (Figure 17B, 20). Tumor cell necrosis/apoptosis was also found significantly increased in mice treated with MRP@Gem-AgHA using the terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase uridine triphosphate nick end labeling (TUNEL) staining when compared to the other five groups (Saline, Free Gem, MRP@AgHA, MP@Gem-AgHA, RP@Gem-AgHA). Further histological study of other internal organs showed no obvious biological toxicity in mice treated with MRP@Gem-AgHA (Figure 21, 22). The above in vivo findings suggest MRP@Gem-AgHA shows both excellent PC-cell targeting ability and superior anti-tumor effect when compared with Gem treatment alone, with minimal off-site damage to other vital organs.

15202119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15202119.value: We have demonstrated that the synergistic action of Ag and Gem can effectively suppress PC cell proliferation. While Gem was reported to be inactivated by intracellular bacteria, the introduction of Ag+ ions via a mesoporous doped AgHA NPs can effectively eliminate the bacteria activity, thereby enabling the full functionality of Gem within a tumor setting. Additionally, the use of cycloRGD as PC cell targeting and homing ligand greatly improved both the NP localization and penetration at the tumor site, while the MMP-9 sensitive PEG shell acted as selective barrier to be only released at MMP-9 rich tumor sites, greatly enhancing the circulation and targeted release of Ag and Gem within PC cells. These properties were proven within both an in vitro and in vivo setting by the use of PANC-1 cells and pancreatic cancer xenograft model of athymic, female nude mouse model. This grants great insight to the design of future drug delivery systems for targeted therapy and deep penetration. Through the combination of MMP-degradable protective shell for inactivation of NPs and peptide homing, this will greatly reduce the undesirable leakage of free drug molecules within the circulatory system and the side effects that many chemotherapy drugs exhibit. The enhanced activity of Gem and improved localized release means the systematic dosage could be reduced drastically compared with the original amount used for clinical injection, while the synergistic effects of Ag+ ions to both eliminate bacteria and supplement Gem anti-tumor effects grants an excellent alternative to increased drug dosage when traditional treatment protocols prove less effective. The related findings have been published in 7 SCI papers such as: P. N. A.S. 119.8 (2022): e2117221119; Biomater. Sci. 10.13 (2022): 3493-3502; Biomater. Sci., 8.24 (2020), 6814-6824; ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 14.7 (2022): 8793-8803; Nanoscale 13.6 (2021): 3594-3601; J. Mater. Chem. B 12.38 (2024): 9686-9694; Polym. Test. 94 (2021): 107042.

15202119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15202119.value: To further consolidate our findings, in vitro experiments involving bacterial infected PANC-1 cells may be performed with live cell imaging to track the intracellular uptake and subsequent actions of our HA NPs and fluorescent-marked Gem. This would allow for visualization of the NP uptake, bacterial elimination, transport of Gem to the nucleus, and finally the apoptosis of the PANC-1 cells. For similar effects, an PC animal model with intact immune systems will need to be performed to observe the effects of our delivery system within the clinical setting and assess if our delivery system would induce immune responses such as inflammation. Additionally, tumors induced with bacterial growth should be used to further validate our system viability against PC tumors.

15202119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15202119.value: Pancreatic cancer is difficult to treat owing to its irreplaceable role in the human body, causing surgical excision of tumors to be extremely risky and improbable. Use of traditional chemotherapy also proves to be ineffective owing to the dispersion of drug molecules once injected, and the inactivation of drugs by intracellular bacteria within the tumor. Hence, we designed a drug delivery system using Ag-doped HA NPs to combat bacterial activity within tumor cells. The silver ions can effectively suppress bacterial growth and prevent chemotherapy drugs from being inactivated. Peptides were further modified onto the surface of the NPs to improve their targeting and uptake by cells which overexpress in membrane proteins specifically programmed to bind to these peptides. And a protective polymer shell that only opens up at tumor regions was used to shield the NPs from degradation while they travel in blood. We validated our findings through observing tumor cell response and uptake in cell culture, and tumor size and NP penetration into tumor surface using a nude mouse model transplanted with pancreatic cancer cells. This system will allow for more effective usage of chemotherapy drugs and a safer treatment option for cancer patients, improving their quality-of-life.

15203119.value: To update the existing spectrally tuneable lighting system and control systems in a full-size space by developing customized spectrally tuneable LED luminaires and control systems to provide a wide range of lighting conditions, in terms of light levels and colour rendition. To investigate preferred colour rendition, as characterized using colour fidelity, colour gamut, and gamut shape, for three different applications (e.g., museum/gallery, restaurant, and typical interior) across a wide range of light levels. To investigate change of object colour appearance across a wide range of light levels by collecting corresponding colour datasets through short-term memory colour matching experiments. An enhanced colour appearance model that considers the effect of light level in calculating the post-adaptation cone responses will be developed using the datasets.

15203119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203119.value: Real life experience suggests that object colours appear faded and dull in dimly lit spaces, especially compared to the colourful appearance under daylight, which is critical to some applications. For example, artefacts (e.g., artworks, silk textiles, and painted pottery) in museums and galleries are displayed at dimmed light levels (≈ 50 lx) for conservation purposes, though some of them (i.e., artworks) are commonly created at very high light levels under daylight (as high as 50,000 lx). In recent years, the wider adoption of LEDs in general illumination motivated very active research on light source colour rendition and colour appearance models for characterizing the effect of light source spectrum and viewing condition on object colour appearance. Nevertheless, these studies mainly focused on common interior applications (e.g., retail displays) with the light levels being limited within a small range (e.g., 200 to 500 lx) and the light levels were seldom varied in individual studies. Therefore, the effect of light level is not considered in developing and specifying lighting products. The PI’s recent works, however, suggested that the effect of light level cannot be ignored in characterizing light source colour rendition and object colour appearance and it is possible to achieve good color rendition at various light levels, which attracted great interests from the lighting community. This project aims to comprehensively investigate the effect of light level on light source colour rendition and object colour appearance characterizations. Customized tuneable LED luminaires will be used to produce light levels from 20 to 24,000 lx (~ 6 to 8,000 cd/m2). To investigate colour rendition, observers will complete colour preference evaluations under various carefully designed light stimuli in a full-size space with three different setups. To investigate colour appearance, short-term memory colour matching experiments will be carried out under different light stimuli. Guidelines for specifying light source colour rendition across a wide range of light levels will be developed; an enhanced colour appearance model will be developed to better characterize the effect of light level. Given the easier spectrum adjustment for LED products, this project is timely and will make great contributions to the lighting community. Manufacturers and designers can develop and specify high-quality LED products to enhance viewing experience and object colour appearance for different lighting applications at different light levels. Standardization bodies can revise LED colour rendition specifications for different lighting applications. This project can also further our knowledge on human perception to light and colour stimuli. 生活经验告诉我们，物体的颜色在昏暗的灯光下会比在阳光下暗淡许多，这样的现象对于许多照明应用而言是非常重要的。例如，博物馆为了保护文物会把灯光调的非常暗，虽然有些文物（特别是书画）是在户外自然光充足的情况下创作的。随着LED照明在通用照明中不断被广泛应用，针对照明光源的显色能力和表征物体在不同照明情况下的研究越来越多。但是，这些研究大多仅针对常见的室内应用场景（例如商业照明）去研究在200-500lx下的情况，并且不会去研究照明水平对于物体颜色和照明显色能力的影响。因而，照明水平的影响在光源的研发与使用中往往都被完全忽略了。项目申请人最近的研究明确揭示了在评价光源显色能力和物体色貌时照明水平不可忽视的作用。本项目将全面研究照明水平对于光源显色能力和物体色貌的影响。我们将定制高亮度LED灯具来提供大范围的照明水平（从20-24000lx)。观察者将在实验空间和灯箱内完成颜色偏好评估、颜色匹配等实验。基于实验结果，我们将总结在不同照明水平下光源显色能力评价的指引，并将提升现有色貌模型对于不同照明水平下物体色貌的评价能力。本项目将对于照明领域和色度学利用提供重要的理论基础。照明厂商和设计师可以基于本项研究来研发选择高品质LED照明产品，政府部门和相关行业可以基于本项研究修订针对不同照明应用的标准与指引。此外，本项目可以帮助我们更深入地了解人眼视觉对于颜色和光刺激的反应。

15203619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15203619.value: 該項目的目的是開發嚴格而強大的數學工具，通過關注以下三個主題，解決量子有限能級系統的結構分析、反饋控制和濾波器設計中的一些問題。 主題1：為量子二能級系統開發規範分解理論。更具體地說，基于研究人員最近開發的量子線性系統的卡爾曼分解，建立量子二能級系統的規範分解理論，以簡單的形式呈現量子二能級系統，以便進行分析和控制器設計。 主題2：為光子態工程開發相干反饋網絡理論。更具體地說，我們研究如何在相干反饋網絡上控制光子 - 光子相互作用，該反饋網絡由兩個兩能級系統，或兩個腔，或甚至兩個腔量子電動力學（腔QED）系統組成。這一基礎研究具有物理意義，將有助於量子信息處理集成量子網絡的理論基礎。 主題3：開發量子有限能级系統濾波器設計的新方法。更具體地說，我們的目標是通過Stratonovich隨機泰勒展開和量子信息幾何技術開發一種新型的量子投影濾波器。由於所提出的濾波器將在較低維度的子流形上定義，因此它在計算上比通常遭受“維度詛咒”的原始量子濾波器更有效。因此，所提出的濾波器可以在基於測量的量子反饋控制中找到應用。

15203619.label: Realisation of objectives
15203619.value: We have achieved all the three objectives in the proposal. In the following we give an in-depth descriptions. 1. We systematically studied the dynamics of a quantum coherent feedback network composed of two two-level systems (qubits) driven by two counter-propagating photons, one in each input channel. The coherent feedback network enhances the nonlinear photon-photon interaction inside the feedback loop. By means of quantum stochastic calculus and the input-output framework, the analytic form of the steady-state output two-photon state is derived. Based on the analytic form, the applications on the Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interferometer and marginally stable single-photon devices using this coherent feedback structure have been demonstrated. The difference between continuous-mode and single-mode few-photon states is demonstrated. 2. The control of flying quantum bits (qubits) carried by traveling quantum fields is crucial for coherent information transmission in quantum networks. We developed a general framework for modelling the control processes of flying qubits, which is based on. The framework is based on the quantum stochastic differential equation (QSDE) that describes the flying qubit input-output relations actuated by a standing quantum system. Under the continuous time-ordered photon-number basis, the infinite-dimensional QSDE is reduced to a low-dimensional deterministic differential equation for the non-unitary state evolution of the standing quantum system, and the outgoing flying qubit states can be calculated in the form of randomly occuring quantum jumps. This makes it possible, as demonstrated by examples of flying-qubit generation and transformation, to analyze general cases when the number of excitations is not reserved. The proposed framework lays the foundation for the design of flying-qubit control systems from a control theoretic point of view, within which advanced control techniques can be incorporated for practical applications. 3. We conducted a comprehensive study of a coherent feedback network where the main component consists of two distant double quantum dot (DQD) qubits which are directly coupled to a cavity. This main component has recently been physically realized (Microwave photon-mediated interactions between semiconductor qubits, Physical Review X, 8(4):041018, 2018). The feedback loop is closed by cascading this main component with a beamsplitter. The dynamics of this coherent feedback network is studied from three perspectives. First, an analytic form of the output single-photon state of the network driven by a single-photon state is derived. In contrast to the experimental observations made in the above paper where a laser is used as input, new interesting physical phenomena are revealed by means of single-photon input. Second, excitation probabilities of DQD qubits are computed when the network is driven by a single-photon input state. Finally, if the input is vacuum but one of the two DQD qubits is initialized in its excited state, the explicit expression of the steady-state joint system-field state is derived, which shows that the output single-photon field and the two DQD qubits can form an entangled state if the transition frequencies of two DQD qubits are equal. This analytical expression can be used to interpret experimental results in the existing literature. 4. We studied the attraction domain analysis for steady states in Markovian open quantum systems, which are mathematically described by Lindblad master equations. The central question is proposed as: given a steady state, which part of the state space of density operators does it attract and which part does it not attract? We answer this question by presenting necessary and sufficient conditions that determine, for any steady state and initial state, whether the latter belongs to the attraction domain of the former. Furthermore, it is found that the attraction domain of a steady state is the intersection between the set of density operators and an affine space which contains that steady state. Moreover, we show that steady states without uniqueness in the set of density operators have attraction domains with measure zero under some translation invariant and locally finite measures. Finally, an example regarding an open Heisenberg XXZ spin chain is presented. We pick two of the system's steady states with different magnetization profiles and analyse their attraction domains. 5. We studied study two-photon dynamics induced by the coherent feedback control of a cavity quantum electrodynamics (cavity-QED) system coupled to a waveguide. In this set-up, the two-level system in the cavity can work as a photon source, and the photon emitted into the waveguide can re-interact with the cavity-QED system many times after the transmission and reflection in the waveguide, during which the feedback can tune the number of the photons in and out of the cavity. We analyze the dynamics of two-photon processes in this coherent feedback network in two scenarios: the continuous mode coupling scheme and the discrete periodic mode coupling scheme between the waveguide and cavity. The difference of these coupling schemes is due to their relative scales and the number of semi-transparent mirrors for coupling. Specifically, in the continuous mode coupling scheme, the generation of two-photon states is influenced by the length of the feedback loop by the waveguide and the coupling strength between the waveguide and the cavity-QED system. By tuning the length of the waveguide and the coupling strength, we are able to generate two-photon states efficiently. In the discrete periodic mode coupling scheme, the Rabi oscillation in the cavity can be stabilized and there are no notable two-photon states in the waveguide. 6. We proposed and analyzed a scheme to generate large-size Schr"{o}dinger cat states based on linear operations of Fock states, squeezed vacuum states and conditional measurements. By conducting conditional measurements via photon number detectors, two unbalanced small-amplitude Schr"{o}dinger kitten states combined by a beam splitter can be amplified to a large-size cat state with the same parity. According to simulation results, two Schr"{o}dinger odd kitten states with amplitudes of $|eta|=1.06$ and $|eta|=1.11$ generated from one-photon-subtracted 3 dB squeezed vacuum states, are amplified to an odd cat state of $|eta|=1.73$ with a fidelity of $F=99\%$. A large-size Schr"{o}dinger odd cat state with $|eta|=2.51$ and $F=97.30\%$ is predicted when 5.91 dB squeezed vacuum states are employed. According to the analysis on the impacts of experimental imperfections in practice, Schr"{o}dinger odd cat states of $|eta|>2$ are available. A feasible configuration based on a quantum frequency comb is developed to realize the large-size cat state generation scheme we proposed.

15203619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15203619.value: Partially supported by this project, our research team has focused on investigating the analysis and control of quantum finite-level systems. Specifically, we have conducted the following studies: 1. Explored the dynamics of two photons interacting with a two-qubit coherent feedback network. 2. Investigated the control of flying qubits. 3. Examined the dynamics of the Tavis-Cummings model. 4. Analyzed the dynamics of a quantum coherent feedback network consisting of cavity-mediated double quantum dot qubits. 5. Conducted attraction domain analysis for steady states of Markovian open quantum systems. 6. Explored quantum coherent feedback control with photons. 7. Developed an implementation protocol based on a frequency comb for the amplification of optical Schrödinger cat states. Furthermore, with the support of this project, we have expanded our research into quantum machine learning and pursued the following studies: 1. Utilized unsupervised learning techniques for the detection of quantum entanglement. 2. Proposed efficient depth selection methods for the implementation of the noisy quantum approximate optimization algorithm. 3. Explored efficient quantum feature extraction for CNN-based learning. 4. Developed quantum context-aware recommendation systems based on tensor singular value decomposition. We have published 13 journal papers in esteemed publications such as IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, Automatica, Physical Review A, Physical Review B, and Quantum Science and Technology. As a result of our significant contributions to this field, we have received several notable invitations: 1. We were invited by the Annual Reviews in Control to write a tutorial paper aimed at promoting quantum control within the broader control community. 2. The PI was invited to deliver two keynote speeches. 3. The PI was invited to serve as the Principal Lecturer for two summer school courses.

15203619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15203619.value: Based on the existing research results, we plan to carry out the following research. 1. Multi-Qubit Systems and Entanglement: Extend the investigation to larger quantum systems and explore the dynamics and control of multi-qubit interactions. 2. Adaptive Control Of Quantum Systems: Explore adaptive control methods for quantum systems, where the control parameters are adjusted in real-time based on the system's response. Investigate adaptive feedback control techniques that can adapt to changing environmental conditions or system parameters, thereby enhancing robustness and performance. Develop adaptive control algorithms tailored for specific experimental setups or applications, such as adaptive control of flying qubits in quantum information processing. 3. Experimental Implementations and Protocols: Collaborate with experimentalists to implement and validate the proposed control strategies in real-world quantum systems. Design experimental protocols for realizing the studied dynamics and control schemes. Work closely with experimental teams to address practical challenges, optimize control parameters, and assess the scalability of the proposed techniques.

15203619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15203619.value: The project aims to develop mathematical tools and techniques to better understand and manipulate quantum finite-level systems. By harnessing the unique properties of quantum mechanics, such as superposition and entanglement, this research project hopes to unlock the potential for advanced technologies. The research is divided into three main topics: 1. It aims to develop a method called "canonical decomposition" for quantum two-level systems. By breaking down these systems into simpler forms, this research projectcan gain a deeper understanding of their behavior and design more effective control strategies. 2. By studying how photons interact with each other in a feedback network, it can gain insights into the fundamental principles of quantum information processing. 3. it aims to develop a new type of filter called a "quantum projection filter." This filter will help estimate and track the state of a quantum system more efficiently, even when the system has a large number of dimensions. Overall, this research project is driven by the goal of advancing our understanding of quantum systems and developing practical tools for their control and manipulation. The findings can contribute to the development of quantum technologies such as quantum computing, quantum communication, and high-precision sensing.

15204419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204419.value: 三維超聲成像在工業領域已發展較為成熟，並得到廣泛的應用。傳統方法通常是將傳感器陣列在被檢查試樣的表面進行二維檢測，或沿球形路徑進行三維檢測，從而構造出一系列二維切面圖，並通過合成這些二維切面圖以得到損傷的三維構造。然而，（i）精確地描繪嵌入式散射體的下表面往往具有極大的挑戰性，實現對其三維特徵的詳細描述更為困難；（ii）目前大多數方法表徵小尺度嵌入式散射體的能力有限；（iii）並且這些方法需要移動體積龐大的傳感器陣列，此舉明顯對於三維成像從無損評估到連續結構健康監測的延伸有所限制。 基於此，該項研究提出了一種新的三維非綫性超聲成像方法，以克服前述不足。該項研究的特點突出表現在以下幾個方面：（i）使用一種增強逆時偏移算法可以精確的描繪具有三維特徵的嵌入式散射體，包括其下表面，而並非簡單合成二維切面圖；（ii）通過原位傳感器網絡（不需要移動傳感器）產生和捕獲彌散波，並利用彌散波的非綫性去測量小尺度的損傷；（iii）快速、簡單和有效地形成一種薄膜型二維陣列，這種陣列具有拓撲設計的模式和優化的陣列參數，可以永久地沉積在樣品表面上；通過這種方式可以最大化增強逆時偏移算法的效率。將上述這些特點組合到一起可以實現原位連續監測材料退化或損傷擴展，從微觀裂紋到宏觀損傷。 結合基礎理論發展，專項建模和強化實驗，該項研究將致力突破現今三維超聲成像的一些瓶頸，並強化一種可行的方法將三維超聲成像從離綫無損評估擴展到連續的、自主的、原位結構健康監測。

15204419.label: Realisation of objectives
15204419.value: 3-D ultrasonic imaging has gained prominence and widespread use over the past decades since it was first demonstrated successfully in the 1970s. By taking advantage of the appealing merits of ultrasound including superior penetration ability and high sensitivity to multi-scale abnormalities, 3-D ultrasonic imaging has now become an almighty, proven non-intrusive inspection tool across industrial sectors, as typified by computerized tomography in clinic, non-destructive evaluation (NDE) in machine maintenance, and contouring in industrial design, to name a few. Conventionally, 3-D imaging refers specifically to the volume rendering of ultrasonic data, in which 2-D ultrasonography or tomography is employed to obtain a series of 2-D images (e.g., 2-D slices in B-mode scanning or pyramidal-shaped images in clinical nuclear magnetic resonance imaging); subsequent combination of these 2-D images leads to a 3-D anatomy of the inspected sample. In practical implementations, ultrasonic data can be acquired via diverse modalities of measurement using tools such as freehand or matrix transducer arrays. To obtain a 2-D slice image, transducer arrays must be manipulated either by moving on a flat surface of the inspected sample two-dimensionally or by scanning the whole sample in its three dimensions (e.g., along a spherical track). Despite that 3-D ultrasonic imaging has gained maturity and popularity across industrial sectors, this technique has encountered some deficiencies including the failure to precisely delineate the lower surface of an embedded scatterer in the inspected sample, the limited capability to characterize small-scale embedded scatterers, and the mandatory movement of bulky arrayed transducers. All these deficiencies have clearly restricted the extension of 3-D imaging from NDE to continuous structural health monitoring (SHM). In recognition of this, a new 3-D nonlinear ultrasonic imaging approach has been developed in this GRF project, to circumvent, partially if not fully, the foregoing deficiencies. To this end, three key objectives were proposed and all of them have been successfully accomplished by the end of this project. This completed GRF project included mainly the following four aspects: (1) achieved, from theoretical development to experimental validation, a new 3-D ultrasonic imaging approach, in conjunction with the use of diffuse waves, by expanding conventional 3-D ultrasonic imaging from offline NDE to continuous, in-situ SHM; (2) develop an enhanced reverse-time-migration (ERTM)-based imaging algorithm, via which 3-D features of embedded scatterers (including their lower surfaces) can be depicted precisely and cost-effectively (NOT a simple combination of 2-D slices); and (3) aided by ERTM, to exploit the nonlinearity of diffuse ultrasonic waves that are generated and captured by an in-situ 2-D transducer network with a topologically designed pattern (No transducer movement required), thereby facilitating continuous monitoring and imaging of the progress of embedded flaws from their embryonic stage to the formation of macroscopic damage (4) experimentally validated the developed approach. This project embraced fundamental theory development, dedicated modeling and intensive experiment. Fundamental investigations were first carried out. From fundamental research to application-oriented implementation, this research has reached its expectation, ending up with an innovative yet practical 3-D ultrasonic imaging approach, to troubleshoot a real engineering problem, and extend 3-D ultrasonic imaging from offline NDE to in-situ SHM.

15204419.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204419.value: A new 3-D nonlinear ultrasonic imaging approach has been developed by completing this GRF project. The developed technique has been proven capable of circumventing, partially if not fully, the deficiencies of prevailing ultrasonic imaging. The research features highlights including (i) an enhanced reverse-time-migration (ERTM) algorithm, allowing precise depiction of an embedded scatterer with 3-D features including its lower surface (not a simple combination of 2-D slices); (ii) use of the nonlinearity of diffuse waves that are generated and captured with an in-situ transducer network (no transducer movement required), for gauging small-scale damage; (iii) quick, simple and efficient formation of a film-type, 2-D array with a topologically designed pattern and optimized array parameters, to be permanently deposited on the sample surface, via which ERTM efficiency can be maximized. Together, these features allow in-situ, continuous monitoring of material deterioration or damage progressing from microscopic cracks to macroscopic impairment. Benefiting from in-depth fundamental interrogation and intensive experiment, this research has reached some very important conclusions and achieved important findings and outcomes which can benefit relevant students in future. For scientific research, it breaks through some limitations in the theoretical cornerstones of 3-D ultrasonic imaging that limit this technique from accurately accessing 3-D features of an embedded scatterer; for real-world engineering, it can continuously monitor material deterioration and damage progressing from the presence of embryonic cracks, through the formation of undersized defects, to the growth of macroscopic impairment. Outcomes of this GRF project are expected to troubleshoot a real engineering problem, and extend 3-D ultrasonic imaging from offline NDE to in-situ SHM. A number of high-level publications have been arising from this research project, including 25 papers in top-tier SCI journals, along with another 1 paper in the international conference proceedings. In addition, two PhD students were systematically trained via this GRF project.

15204419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204419.value: All the proposed objectives have been adequately achieved, and in the meantime the team has also identified some potential directions along which deeper and broader research could be expanded. All work has been done in the laboratory, with mock-up structures. The team is now proactively coordinating with industrial partners, to seek opportunity to validate this technique in real engineering applications in railway industry and aerospace industry, via the team’s industrial partners.

15204419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204419.value: Despite that 3-D ultrasonic imaging has gained maturity and popularity across industrial sectors, this technique has some deficiencies including the failure to precisely delineate the lower surface of an embedded scatterer in the inspected sample, the limited capability to characterize small-scale embedded scatterers, and the mandatory movement of bulky arrayed transducers. All these deficiencies have clearly restricted the extension of 3-D imaging from NDE to continuous structural health monitoring (SHM). A new approach has been developed by completing this RGC-funded research project. This framework retrofits conventional 3-D ultrasonic imaging, to break through some bottlenecks of today’s 3-D ultrasonic imaging, and to cement a feasible way to expand 3-D ultrasonic imaging from offline NDE to continuous, autonomous, in-situ SHM. It breaks through some technical bottlenecks of conventional 3-D ultrasonic imaging techniques. Research outcomes are expected to enhance safety, drive down exorbitant maintenance costs, and extend residual service life of ageing assets in service.

15204719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204719.value: 尋找合適的工俱全球建築行業的健康和安全記錄都很糟糕。一個主要原因是建築任務具有高度的物理性和要求性。很多時候，施工任務是：（1）持續時間較長而沒有足夠的休息時間，（2）在惡劣的氣候條件下和/或（3）在有限的工作空間內。這種情況使建築工人面臨身體疲勞的風險。如果工人在疲勞時繼續工作，可能會：（1）導致與工作相關的肌肉骨骼疾病（MSD）的發展，（2）使工人更容易出錯，（3）降低工藝，（4）降低生產率， （5）危害身體和認知功能，（6）在建築工地引發事故，特別是“跌倒”事故。特別是，對於因體力勞動能力，肌肉量和心輸出量減少而更容易出現疲勞發展的老年工人而言，疲勞是一個更為關鍵的問題。由於56％的勞動力在香港等國家/地區超過50歲，因此迫切需要緊急關注和採取行動來識別和預防與疲勞有關的不良影響。因此，主動疲勞監測和疲勞管理已成為最重要的問題。 不幸的是，沒有適合於建築工人實時疲勞監測的易於部署的工具。傳統上，建築行業的疲勞監測依賴於使用問卷調查和自我報告收集的主觀信息。儘管有一些優點，但它們本質上是侵入性的，耗時且不可行作為連續監測的手段。最近，已經進行了使用生理數據，工人個人特徵，任務特徵和環境變量來評估疲勞的研究。雖然這些方法可以提供連續的疲勞評估，但它們的缺點包括精度低或僅在陽光直射下使用傳感器（用於WetBulb Globe溫度測量或WBGT）以及工人位置數據。為克服這些局限性，該項目將評估三種新型連續疲勞監測技術的準確性和感知工人舒適度。這些新技術包括：（1）心肺呼吸和熱調節措施（侵入性）的組合使用，（2）肌肉氧合測量的體積描記術（中度侵入性）和（3）計算機視覺和可穿戴鞋墊技術的融合（非侵入性的）。 將進行實驗室和現場實驗，以比較三種技術與血液乳酸測量，這被認為是疲勞評估的黃金標準（Tanner等人，2010），以及參與建築工人佩戴傳感器的舒適感。技術。值得注意的是，除了使用生理測量進行疲勞評估（前兩項技術）之外，該項目還首次旨在驗證計算機視覺和可穿戴鞋墊技術的無創融合的有效性。 該項目將有助於確定一種可行的技術，用於建築工人的連續疲勞監測。新技術將引入乾預的能力;從而大大降低了疲勞造成的傷害/死亡的可能性，並大大提高了工人的健康和安全。

15204719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204719.value: By comparing three technologies for fatigue measurement of construction workers against the blood lactate measurement (which is considered the gold standard for fatigue assessment) and the comfort perceptions of participating workers, the most accurate, yet the least invasive, tool for proactive fatigue monitoring has been identified for future use in the construction industry. This tool enables the provision of immediate rest-breaks for workers involved in prolonged periods of work suffering higher fatigue levels. It helps identify those individual workers with relatively low endurance levels who could be referred for detailed medical/physical examinations or placed on training programme. In addition, it assists in the increased monitoring of those trades or workers at higher risk of fatigue development. Moreover, it helps in designing work-rest schedules appropriate for different construction trades. Finally yet importantly, the results arising from the project helps mitigate fatigue levels for others at high-risk, such as mineworkers and firefighters.

15204719.value: We are working with the Construction Industry Council in order to develop relevant policies for implementing the developed technologies from the project.

15204719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204719.value: Fatigue is a critical issue for older workers who are more prone to fatigue development because of decreases in physical work capacity, muscle mass and cardiac output. Since 56% of the workforce are over the age of 50 years in countries/regions like Hong Kong, there is a dire need of urgent attention and action to identify and prevent fatigue-related ill effects. As such, proactive fatigue monitoring and fatigue management have become an issue of utmost importance. This project helps identify a feasible technology for the continuous fatigue monitoring of construction workers. The new technology introduces the ability to intervene; hence significantly reduce the possibility of fatigue-incurred injuries/fatalities and greatly improve workers health and safety.

15204819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15204819.value: Polymer-modified asphalt (PMA) binders are often used in the most challenging locations of road and airport pavements. The higher cost of PMA compared with neat asphalt is believed to be well justified because of its superior performance. There are, however, a variety of polymers available for asphalt modification. Even for the same type and dosage of polymer, its effects on PMA vary greatly. Recent studies in Hong Kong found that the desired properties of some PMA samples dropped significantly after mixture production. Moreover, as Hong Kong is embracing a long-life pavement strategy that aims to achieve more than 40 years of pavement life, the durability of PMA remains a question to be investigated. This research proposes an in-depth investigation of the following issues: 1) What occurs inside PMA binders of different types at the fundamental physicochemical levels during their lifecycles, including storage, mixture production, construction, and long-term road use, 2) how the physicochemical evolution affects performance-related properties, 3) what characteristics of PMA lead to better lifecycle performance. Asphalt derived from different crude oil sources and commonly used polymers of different types and varying dosage will be used to create PMA samples, some of which will be jointly modified with non-organic modifiers. The prepared samples will be subjected to four treatment stages: Stage I to simulate storage conditions, Stage II to simulate mixture production and transportation, Stage III to simulate construction, and Stage IV to simulate road use. The physicochemical properties of PMA samples before and after each treatment stage will be systematically characterized from the sub-nano scale to the microscale. In addition to existing characterization methods, a new method developed by the research team will be used, involving a solvent-free procedure to create an ultrathin asphalt film for the examination of its internal structures. This method is of high-resolution (<1 nano-meter), solvent-free and non-destructive. Consequently, it enables examination of the evolution of polymers and other PMA components, helping to reveal the working and deterioration mechanisms of PMA created by different modification schemes. Systematic engineering tests will also be performed on PMA binders and mixtures. Statistical and mechanistic-based models will be developed to identify relationships between the physicochemical properties of PMA and performance-related engineering properties. The anticipated research outcomes include: 1) scientific insights into the working and deterioration mechanisms of PMA, 2) new approaches to PMA quality management, 3) optimized pavement structure design and material selection, 4) improvements in PMA binder and mixture production. 聚合物改性瀝青（PMA）通常被用於道路和機場鋪面中最具挑戰性的位置。與非改性瀝青相比，PMA具有優異的性能， 也對應於比較高的成本。然而，有多種聚合物可用於瀝青改性。即使對於相同類型和劑量的聚合物，其對PMA的影響也差異很大。最近在香港的研究發現，使用聚合物改性瀝青混合料在生產施工後，其性能有顯著地下降。由於香港正在採用長壽路面設計規範，旨在實現超過40年的路面使用壽命，因此，PMA的耐久性非常需要深入研究。 該研究項目擬對以下問題做深入的研究：1）在聚合物改性瀝青的生命週期中， 包括其儲存、混合料生產、施工和長期道路使用中，聚合物改性瀝青到底發生了什麼樣的根本的物理化學的變化？ ，2）這些根本的物理化學演化對使用性能有哪些影響？ 3）PMA的哪些特性可以在其生命週期中帶來更好的使用性能？ 本研究擬將來自不同原油產地的瀝青和不同類型的、不同劑量的常用聚合物用於製備PMA樣品。準備好的樣品將經歷四個處理階段：階段I模擬儲存條件，階段II模擬混合料生產和運輸，階段III模擬施工過程，階段IV模擬道路使用。 在每個處理階段之前和之後，PMA樣品的物理化學性質將從亞納米級到微米級被進行系統地表徵。除了現有的表徵方法之外，本研究還將使用研究團隊開發的一種新方法研究無溶劑產生的超薄瀝青薄膜的內部結構。該方法具有高分辨率（<1納米），無溶劑且無破壞性的特點。因此，它能夠幫助識別聚合物和其他PMA組分的演變，有助於揭示由不同改性方案產生的PMA的工作和劣化機制。 本研究還將對PMA改性瀝青和混合料進行系統地工程測試，並開發基於統計學和力學的模型，以確定PMA的物理化學性質與性能相關的工程性質之間的關係。預期的研究成果包括：1）對PMA工作和劣化機制的科學見解，2）PMA質量管理的新方法，3）優化的路面結構設計和材料選擇方法，4）PMA改性瀝青和混合料的生產改進工藝。

15204819.label: Realisation of objectives
15204819.value: Realisation of Objective 1 The Objective 1 was fully achieved in this study. In this study, we received generous supports from a major (asphalt-use) polymer producer—the Kraton Corporation. The company not only provided us with the industry-grade polymers, but also instructed us how to prepare samples following the industrial standard. In preparing SBS polymer-modified asphalt binders, we used a base asphalt binder with a penetration grade of 60/70 and three types of SBS polymers (D0246, D1101, and D1184) produced by Kraton Corporation. D0246 is a high diblock SBS, while D1101 and D1184 are linear triblock and radial SBS, respectively. We prepared modified asphalt with two polymer contents, 3 and 6 % by the mass of the base binder, which are frequently used for conventional polymer-modified asphalt (PMA) and highly-modified asphalt (HiMA), respectively. To investigate the effects of polymer structure and polymer content on the compatibility between SBS polymer and base binder, we examined the storage stability of all the SBS-modified asphalt binders as per the ASTM D7173. To investigate the evolution in mixture production, we treated the samples by using rolling-thin film oven (RTFO), and then systematically tested the specimens, including tests at the microstructural level and molecular levels by using confocal fluorescence microscopy (FM) and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), respectively. The engineering properties of the asphalt binders were evaluated for modulus and phase angle at small amplitude oscillatory shear, changes in modulus and phase angle at shear strain amplitude sweep, and multiple stress creep recovery (MSCR). To investigate the evolution in road use stage, we developed a new aging method to simulate asphalt aging in simulated natural conditions. We used 15.4 g RTFO-treated binder to create a 1 mm binder film. Eight pans of samples were prepared for each binder. Then, all the pans were stored in a dark and ventilated environmental chamber at 60 ℃ with a maximum aging duration of 70 days. The pans were removed from the chamber with different sampling intervals, 5 days in the first 20 days, 10 days in the 20-50 days, and 20 days in the 50-70 days. The aged samples were comprehensively investigated using physicochemical methods. Realisation of Objective 2 The Objective 2 was fully achieved in this study, too. To identify the co-evolutions of polymers, asphaltenes and other components in asphalt under the conditions in objective, we used a patented method to examine such microstructures in transmission electron microscopy (TEM). We also used confocal fluorescence microscopy (FM) and image analysis to evaluate the changes. The equipment of FM was a Leica TCS SP8 MP multiphoton/confocal microscope with the laser emission wavelength of 488 nm, the detector reception wavelength ranging from 535 to 625 nm, and the reference wavelength for the Airy calculation of 580 nm. Realisation of Objective 3 The Objective 3 was also fully achieved in this study. Tests on asphalt binder are typically performed in its linear viscoelastic (LVE) range. In this research, the rheological properties of polymer-modified asphalt binders were examined over a wide range of shear strain amplitude, and focus was placed on their non-linear viscoelastic (NLVE) behaviours. The shear strain amplitude was set to range from a very small value (0.01 %) to a very large one (1000 %). This helped reveal experimental variations and binder property changes in small amplitude oscillatory shear (SAOS), medium amplitude oscillatory shear (MAOS), and large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS). Besides strain amplitude, the effects of polymer content, short-term ageing and test frequency were also evaluated. The Lissajous-Bowditch (LB) curves, Fourier transform analysis, and stress decomposition approach were used to analyse the test results. We also tested the fatigue properties of the asphalt binder and the permanent deformation of the asphalt mixture samples. Realisation of Objective 4 The Objective 4 was also fully achieved in this study. Based on all the tests on physicochemical properties of the asphalt and the performance-related property tests, we systematically evaluated their connections. We used a full factorial experimental design to evaluate the effects of polymer structure (3 types of structures), polymer content (3 and 6 %), aging condition (4 combinations), and the interaction of these factors. The main effects and the interaction effects of polymer structure (s), polymer content (c), and aging condition (a) on the physicochemical and performance-related properties of SBS-modified asphalt binders were systematically assessed.
