15204819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15204819.value: The PI would like to thank RGC for providing the opportunity to conduct this meaningful research. Polymer-modified asphalt (PMA) is an important material in the field of pavement engineering. This study systematically investigated the short-term and long-term durability of PMA. The major findings and research outcomes are summarized as follows. (1) The interactive effects of polymer structure, polymer content, and aging Currently, engineering use of PMA typically does not consider the effects of polymer structure and aging conditions. In this study, we found that the morphologies of polymers in asphalt and storage stability are highly affected by polymer structure, the elastic recovery is highly affected by polymer content, and the stiffness/viscosity are highly affected by aging conditions. Such interactive effects need to be considered in material production and quality management. (2) New findings from experiments in the non-linear viscoelastic (NLVE) range Tests on asphalt binder are typically performed in its linear viscoelastic (LVE) range. In this research, we also systematically evaluated the behaviours of PMA in the non-linear viscoelastic (NLVE) range. Besides strain amplitude, we also analysed the effects of polymer content, short-term ageing and test frequency on NLVE behaviours. The NLVE behaviours were found to be affected by shear strain amplitude, polymer content, shear frequency, and the interactions of such factors, but to a less extent by short-term ageing. Besides polymer content, the size and morphology of polymer phase affect the property variations of modified asphalt binders. Large amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS) test and morphology analysis help identify the threshold polymer content in producing high-quality polymer-modified asphalt binders. (3) Innovations and findings in in test methods In this study, we developed and used innovative test methods to study polymers in asphalt, including the use of confocal fluorescence microscopy and transmission electron microscopy. Such characterization methods offer new insights in the states of polymers in PMA. In addition, we developed a new method to accelerate the long-term aging simulation of PMA in natural conditions. This new method enables us to better evaluate the performance of PMA. (4) Durability of PMA and long-life road In this study, we identified factors that affect the long-term durability of PMA from material production to road use stages. Such findings help pavement engineers to take proper actions to build durable road using PMA. This will result in a reduction in life-cycle cost and green-house gas emissions from the road transportation industry.

15204819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15204819.value: This study has high potentials for further meaningful research. One promising area is the applications of non-traditional polymers in asphalt, including liquid polymers (epoxy, polyurethane, etc.) and waste polymers such as plastics. Such non-traditional polymers help improve the “greening” of asphalt materials. The test, analysis, and evaluation methods developed in this study will assist the evaluation and optimal use of these non-traditional polymers. Another area is the application of PMA in the structural layer of road pavements. PMA can significantly improve the fatigue resistance of asphalt material, but it is more expensive than neat asphalt. Research is needed to evaluate the cost/effectiveness of using PMA in the structural layer of pavements. This research will also help improve the quality control/quality assurance (QC/QA) procedure and PMA assessment method. For example, it is recommended that the PMA should be evaluated in the non-linear viscoelastic (NLVE) range, using the parameters recommended in this study. The new method developed in this study is recommended to treat PMA to assess its long-term durability. The QC/QA of PMA should consider the interactive effects of polymer structure, polymer content, and aging conditions. Production conditions should be carefully chosen to prevent the excessive degradation of PMA.

15204819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15204819.value: Polymer-modified asphalt (PMA) is a commonly used material in asphalt pavements, which are used to build roads, ports, and airport runways. PMA is more expensive than non-modified asphalt (neat asphalt), hence, it is often used in the most challenging locations of pavements. The higher cost of PMA compared with neat asphalt is believed to be well justified because of its superior performance. There are, however, a variety of polymers available for asphalt modification. Even for the same type and dosage of polymer, its effects on PMA vary greatly. Material production process significantly affects the long-term durability of PMA. In this research, we conducted in-depth investigation of the following issues regarding PMA: 1) What occurs inside PMA binders of different types at the fundamental physicochemical levels during their lifecycles, including storage, mixture production, construction, and long-term road use, 2) how the physicochemical evolution affects performance-related properties, 3) what characteristics of PMA lead to better lifecycle performance. The research findings and outcomes help pavement industry choose proper polymers for modification, produce PMA mixtures in a proper way to conserve its durability, and improve the procedures for quality control and quality assurance.

15205019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205019.value: In recent years, analytic databases have been increasingly used in various enterprises to facilitate decision making in business intelligence applications. Traditional online analytical processing (OLAP) tools were built to aggregate data by simple functions (e.g., SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX), whereas analytic databases support a much wider range of data analytic functions (e.g., regression, density estimation, clustering, classification and outlier detection). New challenges arise from the need for performing these data analytic functions interactively in analytic databases. First, data analysts expect rapid response time (e.g., 1 second) even on massive data size. Second, many data analytic functions are data intensive and require scanning a dataset. Third, certain types of visualizations would trigger an expensive data analytic function many times as the number of pixels in display resolution. To achieve practical response time, a promising direction is to compute fast approximate results that are sufficiently accurate. Extensive research have been done on computing approximate results but for simple aggregation functions (e.g., SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX), which were mainly used for data aggregation in OLAP tools. Only few works have studied how to compute approximate results for the aforementioned data analytic functions. Three important issues remain unsolved: (i) hard to control the accuracy of approximate data analytic results, (ii) lack of efficient means to refine the accuracy of approximate results interactively, (iii) hard to automate the discovery of relevant data analytic results based on analysts' preferences. In this project, we aim at developing techniques to enable fast approximate data analytics for analytic databases. To tackle the above issues, we formulate the following research objectives. First, we will develop techniques to compute approximate results with accuracy guarantees, in order to deliver reliable results to data analysts. Second, we will design efficient techniques to refine the accuracy of approximate results interactively. Third, we study how to utilize an analyst's preference to automate the discovery of relevant data analytic results. Fourth, we will build a prototype system based on our proposed techniques, and release it to the public as open-source software. This project will bring advancement to the data analytics area and also benefit enterprises in metropolitan cities like in Hong Kong. 近年來，分析型數據庫在各種企業中廣泛使用，以幫助商業智能應用部署決策。傳統聯機分析處理（OLAP）工具的聚集函數（例如SUM求和, AVG平均, MIN最小數, MAX最大數）可實現數據聚集操作，然而分析型數據庫可實現更廣泛的數據分析功能（例如遞歸，密度估測，聚類，分類和異常值檢測）。 分析型數據庫的交互性要求成為新挑戰。首先，即使是在大量數據情境下，數據分析專家對數據操作反應時間有要求（例如1秒之內）；其次，大量數據分析功能屬數據密集型操作，需掃描數據集；再次，某些數據可視化根據分辨率展示不同數量的像素值，需多次調用代價較高的數據分析功能。為了達到具有實用性的響應時間，一個實用方案是迅速給出足夠準確的近似結果。 在簡單聚集函數（例如 SUM求和, AVG平均, MIN最小數, MAX最大數）方面，大量研究可以使其計算出近似結果，這些研究成果已經在OLAP工具聚集分析中使用。但對於在前文提到的數據分析功能，幾乎沒有相應的研究。主要有三方面的問題尚待解決：（i）近似結果的準確性難以控制；（ii）在迭代提高近似結果準確度方面，缺少高效的方法；（iii）很難實現基於分析者偏好的自動數據分析。 在此項目中，我們意在研發分析型數據庫實現快速近似分析數據果的技術。我們規劃以下研究目的以解決以上問題。首先，我們的技術提供的近似結果具有準確性保證，為數據分析師提供可信賴性；其次，我們將設計高效技術來不斷完善、迭代提高近似結果的準確性；再次，我們將研究如何使用分析者偏好來實現相關數據分析結果的自動呈現；最後，基於我們所研究的各方面技術，我們將構造實現原型系統並將其發布成為公開的開源軟件。該項目將促進數據分析領域進步，幫助香港等大城市的企業。

15205019.label: Realisation of objectives
15205019.value: We have carried out research activities for all project objectives. Two PhD students have been recruited to investigate those issues. One PhD student has graduated and the other PhD student is still on-going. We have developed approximate computation techniques (objective 1) and refinement techniques (objective 2) for distance distribution and kernel aggregation, and then published our results in two IEEE TKDE papers in 2022. We have studied query processing in the continuous preference space (objective 3) and then published a SIGMOD paper in 2022. Regarding objective 4, we have developed a prototype tool for progressive kernel density visualization and then published a SIGMOD paper in 2020. We have also conducted performance evaluation of indexing methods on approximate range aggregate queries and then published a EDBT paper in 2021.

15205119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205119.value: China has the second highest annual incidence of tuberculosis in the world. Despite the success of their Tuberculosis (TB) Control Plan, TB remains one of the biggest threat to public health in Shandong Province, China. Meanwhile, multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB) has become the biggest hurdle for further TB prevention. We propose to study the confirmations of TB at the city-level from 2006 to 2017 and that of MDR-TB from 2004 to 2017 in Shandong, during which time there were evident changes in both TB and MDR-TB confirmations. Furthermore, the role of external factors including ambient air pollution on the spreading of TB and MDR-TB remains poorly understood. Our innovative approach makes use of powerful state-of-the-art statistical modeling, that is natural for studying these datasets. We obtained population data from Census and Statistical Yearbooks in Shandong, laboratory-confirmed notifications for TB from 2006 to 2017 from the Tuberculosis Surveillance System across seven cities and MDR-TB from 2004 to 2017 across 38 TB medical units in Shandong, daily meteorological data and air pollutant data for the seven cities over the same study period. We plan to apply four approaches to analyze these data: (1) use generalized linear regression models to explore the intrinsic information of TB and MDR-TB notifications; (2) apply age-period-cohort (APC) models to further investigate the heterogeneities of age groups and period (historical trend) on TB confirmation between cities, as well as forecast the future trend of TB confirmations and MDR-TB confirmations; (3) apply boosted regression trees (BRT) to investigate the impact of external factors on the spread of the TB and MDR-TB. Our preliminary results on six out of the seven cities indicate that (1) farmers contribute most TB confirmations, especially in Jining, Linyi and Dezhou, where rural population has a large proportion of the total population, while college students are the second main source of TB confirmations in Jinan, Yantai, and Weifang; (2) much higher TB infected risk of male, and of elderly people who are around 60 years old. We forecast continuous decreasing TB confirmations in the coming 5 years, but gradual increasing MDR-TB confirmation in the next 6 years. 15205119.label: Realisation of objectives
15205119.value: Regarding Objective 1. Tuberculosis (TB) incidence has been in steady decline in China over the last few decades. However, ongoing demographic transition, fueled by aging, and massive internal migration could have important implications for TB control in the future. We collated data on TB notification, demography, and drug resistance between 2004 and 2017 across seven cities in Shandong, the second most populous province in China. Using these data, and age-period-cohort models, we (i) quantified heterogeneities in TB incidence across cities, by age, sex, resident status, and occupation and (ii) projected future trends in TB incidence, including drug-resistant TB (DR-TB). Between 2006 and 2017, we observed (i) substantial variability in the rates of annual change in TB incidence across cities, from -4.84 to 1.52%; (ii) heterogeneities in the increments in the proportion of patients over 60 among reported TB cases differs from 2 to 13%, and from 0 to 17% for women; (iii) huge differences across cities in the annual growths in TB notification rates among migrant population between 2007 and 2017, from 2.81 cases per 100K migrants per year in Jinan to 22.11 cases per 100K migrants per year in Liaocheng, with drastically increasing burden of TB cases from farmers; and (iv) moderate and stable increase in the notification rates of DR-TB in the province. All of these trends were projected to continue over the next decade, increasing heterogeneities in TB incidence across cities and between populations. To sustain declines in TB incidence and to prevent an increase in Multiple DR-TB (MDR-TB) in the future in China, future TB control strategies may (i) need to be tailored to local demography, (ii) prioritize key populations, such as elderly and internal migrants, and (iii) enhance DR-TB surveillance. Regarding Objective 2. Few studies conducted in China have assessed the effects of ambient air pollution exposure on tuberculosis (TB) risk and mortality, especially with a multicity setting. We evaluated the effect of short- and long-term ambient sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), ozone (O3), and particulate matter≤2.5 μm in aerodynamic diameter (PM2.5) exposures on development and mortality of active TB in 7 Chinese cities in Shandong province from January 1, 2013, to December 31, 2017. We estimated the pollution-associated risk to new infection TB, recurrent TB, and mortality in relation to 1-μg/m3 increases in air pollutants using the penalized multivariate Poisson regression models. A total of 83,555 new infective TB and 3060 recurrent TB including 997 deaths were recorded. Short- and long-term exposures to outdoor air pollutants (SO2, NO2, CO, O3, and PM2.5) were significantly associated with new infection TB, recurrent TB risk, and mortality. The dominant positive effects of SO2, NO2, CO, and PM2.5 for new infection and recurrent TB risk were observed at long-term (>30 days) exposure, whereas the dominant effects of SO2, CO, and PM2.5 for mortality were observed at short-term (≤30 days) exposures. Of the 5 air pollutants we assessed, SO2 and PM2.5 exhibited more consistent and strong associations with TB-related outcomes. We estimated an increase of 1.33% (95% CI 1.29%, 1.37%) and 3.04% (95% CI 2.98%, 3.11%) in new infection TB count for each 1-μg/m3 increase of SO2 at lag 0–180 days and PM2.5 at lag 0–365 days, respectively. This epidemiologic study in China shows that air pollution exposure is associated with increased risk of active TB development and mortality. The control of ambient air pollution may benefit the control and decrease the mortality of TB disease. Tuberculosis (TB) is still an important public health issue in Jiangsu province, China. In this study, based on the TB transmission routes and the statistical data of TB cases, we formulate a novel TB epidemic model accounting for the effects of the contaminated environments on TB transmission dynamics. The value of this study lies in two aspects. Mathematically, we define the basic reproduction number, R0, and prove that R0 can be used to govern the threshold dynamics of the model. Epidemiologically, we find that the annual average R0 is 1.13,>1 and TB in Jiangsu is an endemic disease. Therefore, in order to control the TB in Jiangsu efficiently, we must decrease the virus shedding rate or increase the recovery rates, and increase the environmental clearance rate.

15205119.value: Our results highlight the heterogeneities among sex, age groups, regions, and occupations for TB notifications, as well as a continuing increase in MDR-TB notifications in the future. Based on criteria such as rural population size, occupation, and sex, we suggest varied focuses for the future control of TB: (i) raising awareness among college students in urban cities, such as Jinan, while improving medical facilities in rural regions, such as Linyi and Liaocheng; (ii) regular surveillance of the senior population, especially senior females; and (iii) strengthening detection techniques for reactivated TB over the next decade. Our study shows a possible link between ex-posure to ambient air pollution and increased risk of active TBdevelopment and mortality in 7 Chinese cities. Short- and long-term exposures to SO2, NO2, O3, CO, and PM2.5 were positively and significantly associated with TB development and mortality. SO2 and PM2.5 exhibited more strong associations with TB risks among the 5 air pollutants. These findings support the Chinese government efforts in reducing high levels of air pollution, in order to reduce TB incidence and mortality. A tuberculosis model incorporating contaminated environments is developed. A threshold theorem of the model is established. The annual average of the basic reproduction number is obtained. TB in Jiangsu is an endemic disease and will persist for a long time.

15205219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205219.value: The past decade has witnessed many great achievements in terms of metamaterial and metasurface-enabled unique acoustic wave manipulations, within or beyond the diffraction limit. However, those demonstrations dominantly targeted airborne acoustic waves. Compared to air who has extremely low acoustic impedance, most natural and synthetic materials can be treated as being rigid. The design of artificial structure and the realization of preferred refractive index are rather simple and straightforward. Underwater acoustics, on the other hand, studies acoustic wave phenomena in water and the related instrumentation. In contrast to the highly attenuated electromagnetic waves, acoustic waves can travel long distances in water. For this reason, underwater environment is where acoustic waves really shine with great potential in practical applications, as they are among the few that can be utilized to sense and communicate in water. However, for underwater metamaterial design, the large acoustic impedance of water complicates the matter. Most media can no longer be treated as rigid. Shear modes and modes conversion associated with solids come into play. Analytical model derivation is almost impossible. The extraordinary challenge of designing metamaterials for underwater acoustic wave manipulation remains unsolved. To deal with the above-mentioned challenges, this proposed study aims at developing a genetic algorithm-based methodology to guide the inverse design of underwater acoustic metamaterials and devices, by combining the ability of genetic algorithm to solve both constrained and unconstrained optimization problems with the powerful finite element method numerical simulation. The unique capability of genetic algorithm to find the best optimized values for each crucial parameter within the limit will play a critical role in complex underwater acoustic metamaterials development. This proposed study shall ultimately result in an effective and accurate inverse design methodology for different acoustic meta-devices such as cloak, field concentrator, noise absorber, beam shifter et al. The proposed research will be implemented in three phases including: (1) Investigating the evolution of the genetic algorithm with finite element method to design metamaterials for acoustic wave manipulation in water, adjusting the natural selection process and model parameters accordingly. (2) Experimental verification of acoustic wave manipulation capabilities in water. (3) Design, fabrication and experimental measurement of multiple acoustic meta-devices in water, designed based on the verified genetic algorithm-based methodology. It is expected that this project can achieve two accomplishments. First, a reliable genetic algorithm-based design methodology for underwater acoustic metamaterials development. Secondly, the realization and experimental demonstration of multiple acoustic meta-devices for underwater applications. 過去十年來，基於超構材料和超構表面的聲學材料設計基礎研究獲得了豐碩的成果，並推動了在應用領域的進展。但是這些成就決大多數針對的是空氣聲學。由於空氣的聲阻抗非常低，大多數自然和人工合成的材料在空氣中可以被看作是絕對堅固的。因此人工結構的設計和等效參數的實現都相對簡單直接。 水聲，作為聲學的另外壹個分支，研究水下的聲學現象以及相關儀器設備。相對於電磁波在水中的高衰減，聲波在水環境中可以傳播非常遠的距離，是為數極少的可以用於水中環境探測和通信的手段之壹。然而，由於水較大的聲阻抗值，在水中大多數材料不能再被作為堅固材料對待，固體材料中存在的聲波的橫波模式必須被認真考慮分析。在水環境中，獲得聲波傳播的解析解往往是不現實的。 這也阻礙了水聲超構材料和超構表面的實現。 為了解決這個挑戰，本項目提出，結合遺傳算法的優化能力和有限元算法的計算能力，研究復雜水聲環境中超構材料和器件的設計方法問題。遺傳算法獨特的快速搜尋優化參數設計能力將在項目中發揮重要作用。 本項目旨在達到壹種有效和準確的聲學超構材料和設備的設計方法並展示不同的設計結果，預計將分三個階段的研究來實現：第壹個階段將主要研究如何在水下聲波傳輸的研究中融合遺傳算法以及有限元方法。第二階段將主要是設計方法的實驗驗證。最後壹個階段將是多種聲超構設備的制備和性能測試。 本項目預期將實現首先壹種基於遺傳算法的水聲超構材料設計方法。其次，若幹種不同功能的水聲超構器件。

15205219.label: Realisation of objectives
15205219.value: This project aimed to achieve five objectives, all of which have been successfully accomplished. The design of underwater acoustic metamaterials presents a complex challenge due to the significantly higher acoustic impedance of water compared to air. As a result, deriving an analytical effective medium model becomes nearly impossible. Consequently, the design of acoustic metamaterials, metasurfaces, and devices for underwater applications remains an outstanding and unsolved challenge. Motivated by this, our research sought to establish a comprehensive research program focused on developing a new methodology for inverse acoustic metamaterials design and realizing acoustic meta-devices capable of various acoustic wave modulation functions in water. This research encompassed in-depth analytical investigations, dedicated simulations, and rigorous experimental studies, spanning from fundamental research to engineering applications. This completed GRF project included mainly the following aspects: (1) developed a new in verse underwater acoustic metamaterials design methodology, by combining the genetic algorithm with the finite element method numerical simulation. (2) experimentally verified the acoustic wave manipulation capabilities offered by underwater acoustic metamaterials designed from the genetic algorithm-based methodology, in water tank. (3) compared the design objectives with the experimental measurement outputs to further optimize the methodology. (4) developed multiple underwater acoustic meta-devices utilising the genetic algorithm-based in verse design methodology. (5) fabricated underwater acoustic meta-device samples and experimentally demonstrate the performance in water tank. The project began with fundamental investigations, progressing towards application-oriented implementation. Through a combination of fundamental research and practical approaches, this proposed research has successfully met its objectives, culminating in the development of innovative and practical underwater metamaterial devices using an inverse optimization methodology. In conclusion, all the proposed research objectives have been successfully and fully accomplished.

15205219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205219.value: Acoustic waves are a crucial tool for sensing the environment and communication in water due to their ability to travel long distances. Over the past decade, there has been significant research on acoustic metamaterials and metasurfaces, which are artificial structured materials capable of modulating acoustic waves in unique and unexpected ways. However, the significantly higher acoustic impedance of water compared to air introduces complications, as natural or artificial media can no longer be treated as rigid. Shear modes and mode conversion in solid media become relevant and cannot be neglected. As a result, deriving an analytical effective medium model becomes nearly impossible. Motivated by these challenges, this GRF project has developed a new research framework that incorporates the concept and design philosophy of inverse optimization in the development of acoustic metamaterials and metasurfaces for manipulating acoustic waves in water. The optimization method combines genetic algorithms with finite element methods to design underwater acoustic metamaterials while considering the properties of solid materials. The optimized samples are then fabricated and experimentally verified. This research has contributed to the development of multiple underwater acoustic meta-devices, bridging the gap between fundamental research and real-world application-oriented implementation. Through in-depth fundamental investigations and intensive experiments, this research has yielded important conclusions and significant findings that will benefit future researchers in the field. The outcomes of this research serve as a pilot study for a new long-term direction in underwater acoustics research, enhancing our understanding of how to manipulate acoustic waves in water and providing valuable guidance for materials and device design. Moreover, the developed framework shows promising application prospects in various fields such as signal communication, noise control, medical imaging, and disease treatment. This research project has resulted in a number of high-level publications, including 16 papers published in top-tier SCI journals1-16 (see Part C).

15205219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15205219.value: All of the proposed objectives have been successfully accomplished, and the research team has also identified potential directions for further exploration and expansion. The entirety of the work has been carried out in the laboratory, with structures fabricated using 3D printing and precision CNC machining techniques. Currently, the team is actively collaborating with industrial partners to explore opportunities for validating this technique in real-world engineering applications.

15205219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15205219.value: Metamaterials are artificial materials engineered with unique properties derived from their precisely designed and periodically arranged unit cell structures. The field of metamaterials research is relatively new but has garnered significant scientific attention over the past two decades. In the case of underwater acoustic metamaterials, the coupling and interaction between acoustic waves in water and the complex wave modes within solid materials pose challenges in deriving objective functions, making the realization of underwater metamaterials highly challenging. To tackle this issue, a novel approach combining genetic algorithms with finite element methods has been developed through this RGC-funded research project. This framework enables a "design by specification" philosophy, where users can simply specify the desired functionality and boundary conditions, and the program searches the entire design space to find the optimal solution that meets the requirements. This methodology facilitates the achievement of a proper balance between performance and design requirements, making it possible to design materials and structures for complex environments.

15205619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205619.value: The visual system of human beings and animals can efficiently recognize, identify and classify the objects from a complicated world, exhibiting strong cognitive recognition capability than the conventional computing system based on von Neumann computation architecture and Si CMOS technologies. It is a both fundamental interest and practical usage for us to emulate the neuromorphic visual system through hardware implementation. State-of-the-art image sensor can collect visual information in a real time, but is required to pass the information to next-level computing system for further signal processing. Recently, researchers employ static random access memory (SRAM) and emerging non-volatile resistive memory as on-chip synaptic device for neuro-inspired computing. However, they cannot directly response to optical stimuli and require complicated peripheral circuits to convert the optical signal to electronic spike, and digitalize the collected information. In this proposed work, we will prepare an optoelectronic synaptic transistor to response both electronic and optical stimuli, and mimic the basic characteristics of neuromorphic visual system. Two-dimensional (2D) layer materials possess ultrathin body thickness and excellent electronic characteristics. Electrically, their large surface-to-volume ratio allows them to efficiently response to external stimuli; mechanically, their atomic-level thickness gives rise to excellent flexibility, which offers a broad field of view, more uniform illumination and few aberrations for image detection. Organometal halide perovskites show excellent light absorption, unusual defect physics, and tunable band gap. These characteristics enables them to respond optical stimuli effectively, form volatile and non-volatile memory states, and detect the signals with different wavelengths. By constructing the hybrid 2D/perovskite synaptic transistor, we can modulate the resistance states of the device by electrical and optical stimuli and mimic the visual cortex in human brains. In this project, we will first fabricate the 2D/perovskite synaptic transistor, where the conductance of 2D materials channel can be modulated by electrical stimuli, and the perovskite can effectively respond to optical illumination. Second, we will characterize the basic synaptic characteristics of the optoelectronic synaptic transistor under electrical and optical stimuli, respectively. Third, we will construct the optoelectronic synaptic transistor at array level to mimic the neuromorphic visual system. 人類和動物的視覺系統可以有效地從復雜的世界中識別和分類對象，相對於基於馮諾依曼計算架構和矽基的傳統計算系統，人類的認知識別能力更強。這驅使我們通過硬件來模擬人類的視覺系統。圖像傳感器可以實時地收集視覺信息，但需要將信息傳遞給下壹級計算系統以進壹步的信號處理；靜態隨機存取存儲器可以作為神經芯片上的突觸器件，但不能直接響應光學刺激。在本項目中，我們將制備光電子突觸晶體管，可以響應電與光的刺激，並模仿神經形態視覺系統的基本特征。 二維層狀材料具有超薄的厚度和優異的物理性能。它們的比表面積很大，允許它們有效地響應外部刺激。而且它們的原子級厚度使得它們具有很高的柔性。有機金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦有著出色的光吸收特性，缺陷以及可調帶隙。這些特點使得它們能夠有效地響應光學刺激，形成易失性和非易失性記憶狀態，並檢測不同波長的信號。通過構建二維材料與鈣鈦礦異質的突觸晶體管，我們可以通過電和光刺激調制器件的電阻狀態，並模仿人腦中視覺皮層的功能。 在這個項目中，我們將首先制備出二維材料與鈣鈦礦異質突觸晶體管，其中二維材料通道的電導可以通過電刺激來調制，鈣鈦礦可以有效地響應光學刺激。其次，我們將測試光電子突觸晶體管在電和光分別刺激下的基本突觸特征。第三，我們將構建光電子突觸晶體管陣列來模仿神經形態視覺系統。

15205619.label: Realisation of objectives
15205619.value: 1. To fabricate hybrid optoelectronic synaptic transistor based on two-dimensional semiconductor and photosensitive perovskite materials We design and demonstrate a monolithic vision enhancement chip with light-sensing, memory, digital-to-analog conversion, and processing functions by implementing a 619-pixel with 8582 transistors and physical dimensions of 10 mm by 10 mm based on a wafer-scale two-dimensional (2D) monolayer molybdenum disulfide (MoS2). The light-sensing function with analog MoS2 transistor circuits offers low noise and high photosensitivity. Furthermore, we adopt a MoS2 analog processing circuit to dynamically adjust the photocurrent of individual imaging sensor, which yields a high dynamic light-sensing range greater than 90 decibels. The vision chip allows the applications for contrast enhancement and noise reduction of image processing. This large-scale monolithic chip based on 2D semiconductors shows multiple functions with light sensing, memory, and processing for artificial machine vision applications, exhibiting the potentials of 2D semiconductors for future electronics. 2. To characterize the electronic and optical synaptic transistor at single device level with different excitation protocol. We report bioinspired vision sensors that are based on molybdenum disulfide phototransistors and exhibit time-varying activation and inhibition characteristics. Charge trap states are intentionally introduced into the surface of molybdenum disulfide, enabling the dynamic modulation of the photosensitivity of the devices under different lighting conditions. The light-intensity-dependent characteristics of the sensors match Weber’s law in which the perceived change in stimuli is proportional to the light stimuli. The approach offers visual adaptation with highly localized and dynamic modulation of photosensitivity under different lighting conditions at the pixel level, creating an effective perception range of up to 199 dB. The phototransistor arrays exhibit image contrast enhancement for both scotopic and photopic adaptation.

15205619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15205619.value: To overcome the computational efficiency issue at sensory terminals, we made a disruptive proposal of in-sensor computing paradigm and revolutionize AI computations at sensor level (Nature, 2020, 579, 32-33; Nature Electronics, 2020, 3, 664-671). We extended this computing paradigm to vision sensors, resulting in increased efficiency and enriched functionalities, including improved image recognition (Nature Nanotechnology, 2019, 14, 776-782), visual adaptation in extremely dim/bright lighting (Nature Electronics, 2022, 5, 84-91; Nature, 2022, 602, 364), agile perception of dynamic motion (Nature Nanotechnology, 2023, 18, 882-888), and event-driven in-sensor spiking neural network (Nature Electronics, 2023, accepted). We also write review articles in this area (Advanced Materials, 2022, 2203830; Science China Information Science, 2022, 65(4), 1-14.). We has been invited to express views on the development of in-sensor computing in Nature Podcast. These research findings are also highlighted in academic and public media. One of the research works has been highlighted in Nature and recognized as one of the top 10 Innovation and Technology News in Hong Kong in 2022. We also demonstrated the latest results to Chief Executive during her visit at PolyU in 2021.

15205719.value: 變頻空氣源熱泵室外機組在大於0度的室外環境作無霜運行的冷凝結霜性能圖譜

15205719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205719.value: Air source heat pump units (ASHPs) have found increasingly wide applications worldwide because they are highly energy efficient. Frosting on the outdoor coil in a space heating ASHP can, however, negatively impact its operational efficiency, and the thermal environment inside a heated indoor space. Therefore, there have been extensive research efforts in developing various frost suppression measures, without, however, much successful practical application. With the increasingly wide uses of variable speed (VS) technology, VS ASHPs are increasingly being used. According to the previous related studies by the Investigators on the performance maps of VS direct expansion (DX) air conditioning (A/C) systems, simultaneously varying both speeds in a VS ASHP can result in varied evaporating temperatures in its outdoor coil and be thus used to enable frost free operation at above 0 ℃ ambience. In this project, condensing - frosting performance maps for the outdoor coil in an experimental VS ASHP system will be developed by both experiments and mathematical modelling. The performance maps will clearly show the status of the outdoor coil surface, dry, wet or frosted, when the experimental ASHP system is operated at different combinations of compressor and fan speeds and hence different output heating capacities, under different ambient conditions and varied outdoor coil surface areas. Such performance maps can be directly used as essential guidelines in the design and control of VS ASHPs, to enable their frost-free operation at above 0 ℃ ambience, subject to providing the required output heating capacity by using appropriate speed combinations. In addition, to showcase the practical applications of the performance maps developed, a follow-up modelling study will be carried out on developing a control strategy for a three- indoor coil VS ASHP providing frost-free operation at above 0 ℃ ambiences when only two of the three indoor coils are used. The successful carrying out of the proposed project will help enable frost free operation for a space heating VS ASHP at above 0 ℃ ambience, thereby achieving at least 20% improvement in energy efficiency, better occupant thermal comfort and improved operational reliability, as a result of frost free operation. This would in turn encourage wider use of ASHP technology, contributing significantly to energy conservation and sustainable development worldwide, and to the advance of ASHP technology by including these performance maps as part of ASHPs product inventory. 空氣源熱泵（ASHP）具有能效高的特性，因此在全球範圍應用越來越廣泛。然而室外機盤管的結霜問題，會對機組的運行效率，以及室內熱環境產生負面的影響。因此，大量的研究精力被用於開發各種各樣的抑霜措施，但是目前並沒有產生成熟的應用。隨著變頻技術的發展，變頻空氣源熱泵的應用得到持續性的增長。根據已有對直膨變頻空調系統性能圖譜的相關研究可以發現，同時改變變頻空氣源熱泵中的風機轉速和壓縮機轉速，能夠改變其室外機盤管中的蒸發溫度，從而可使其在0℃以上的環境中實現無霜運行。 在本課題中，針對所實驗的變頻空氣源熱泵機組，其室外機盤管的冷凝-結霜性能圖譜將通過實驗和數值類比的方式進行研究。當所實驗的變頻空氣源熱泵機組在不同的環境條件、室外盤管面積以及壓縮機轉速和風機轉速的組合運行時，其性能圖譜能直觀地顯示出室外機環路表面的狀態為乾燥，潮濕或是結霜。研究所得的性能圖譜可以直接的為變頻空氣源熱泵機組的設計和控制提供必要的指導，使其能夠在0℃以上的環境下進行無霜運行，並通過使用適當的轉速組合提供所需的制熱量。此外，為了進一步推廣性能圖譜的實際應用，後續將進行相關的數值模擬的研究，以制定具有三室內盤管的變頻空氣源熱泵多連線的控制策略，特別是在0℃以上的環境中進行無霜運行時，僅使用其中的兩個室內盤管。 本課題的成功實施將有助於在0℃以上的環境中，實現變頻空氣源熱泵機組的無霜運行，從而使其能效提高至少20％，並在提高用戶熱舒適度的同時提高機組運行的可靠性。該技術方案反過來可進一步促進空氣源熱泵技術得到更廣泛地應用，為全球的節能和可持續發展的戰略目標繼續做出重大的貢獻，並且性能圖的引入可推動空氣源熱泵技術得到進一步發展。

15205919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15205919.value: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common and clinically significant arrhythmic disorder that results in increased risk of morbidity and mortality. Compelling evidence has demonstrated that the left atrial appendage (LAA), a finger-like structure originating from the left atrium, is the most common site for thrombus formation in association with AF. In recent years, many studies have suggested that occluding LAA and isolating it from the left atrium is an effective treatment for preventing patients with AF from the stroke. However, nowadays it is challenging for surgeons to perform a successful LAA occlusion procedure due to (1) the large variation in the anatomical characteristics of LAA among patients, (2) the complicated surgical anatomy and environment, and (3) the inconveniences of current intraoperative guidance settings. In this project, we aim at developing a novel system with a set of effective and enabling technologies to meet these challenges to facilitate patient-specific planning and intraoperative guidance of LAA occlusion. The proposed system is composed of two modules: a planning software and a toolkit for intraoperative guidance. To construct the planning software, we shall first propose a novel weakly-supervised deep learning model to automatically segment the LAA and relevant tissues from 3D TEE images with limited manual annotations. We shall then propose a perception-aware visualization approach to clearly exhibit the surgical environment with lucid morphological information of LAA for precise planning. To construct the toolkit for intraoperative guidance, we shall propose a new 2D X-ray and 3D TEE registration algorithm based on domain adaptation and adversarial learning. Then, a novel occlusion-manageable and lightness-consistent visualization algorithm will be developed to clearly display the fused data obtained based on the registration. Furthermore, we shall propose a novel context-driven touchless interaction framework allowing the surgeons to interact with the fused guidance image naturally, intuitively and effectively. We shall extensively evaluate these proposal algorithms and the system based on widely used metrics and clinical requirements. This is a joint project with a strong interdisciplinary team including experts in both technical and clinical fields. The proposed computer-assisted system, so far as we know, is the first one to comprehensively address the challenges in the LAA occlusion procedure and hence has great potential to improve its outcome and efficiency. We believe the proposed novel techniques can also to be used to develop planning and intraoperative guidance systems for other complicated structure heart interventions, especially the ones taking TEE as guidance. 心房顫動是一種常見且臨床上顯著的心律失常症, 該症狀會導致心臟病發病率和死亡率風險增加。 臨床證據證實了左心耳---一個起源于左心房的手指狀結構---是最常見的與心房顫動相關的血栓形成部位。近年來, 許多研究表明封堵左心耳並將其與左心房隔離是預防房顫患者中風的有效治療方法。然而, 迄今為止, 外科醫生要成功完成一個左心耳封堵手術仍是極具挑戰的工作, 主要由於: (1)患者之間左心耳解剖特徵的變化很大, (2)複雜的手術解剖環境, 以及(3)目前術中指導設置的不便之處仍需改進。 在本專案中,我們的目標是基於一系列有效的新技術開發一個新系統, 來應對這些挑戰並推動患者特異性精准左心耳封堵手術計畫和術中引導系統的發展。 我們提出的系統由兩個模組組成: 一個手術計畫系統和一個構建術中引導系統的軟體工具組。為構建手術規劃系統, 我們首先提出一個新型的弱監督深度學習模型用於自動化分割經食道三維超聲圖像中的相關組織, 該模型根據有限的標注資料就能完成自動化分割。接下來我們會的提出一種基於知覺感知的視覺化方法, 以清晰地展示左心耳封堵手術的解剖環境, 用於精准規劃。為了構建術中引導系統, 我們將提出一個新的基於領域適應和對抗學習的2D X-Ray圖像和3D 超聲圖像的配准演算法。然後, 我們會實現一種新穎的管理遮擋和處理亮度的視覺化演算法, 以清晰地顯示基於配准獲得的融合資料。此外, 我們還將提出一種新穎的內容驅動非接觸式交互框架允許外科醫生自然、直觀、有效地與融合引導圖像進行交互。我們將依據廣泛使用的指標和臨床要求評估我們的演算法和系統。 這是一個由跨學科團隊組成的聯合專案組, 包括技術專家和臨床專家。據我們所知, 我們提出的電腦輔助手術系統, 是第一個綜合性解決左心耳封堵手術各項挑戰的系統, 因此極具潛力改善該手術的結果和效率。我們相信本專案提出的新技術也可用於構建其他複雜結構心臟介入手術的手術規劃和手中引導系統, 特別是用經食道三維超聲做引導的手術。

15206019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206019.value: Assembly of different materials with disparate properties into one continuous fiber can lead to a novel kind of 1D fiber materials/devices with advanced functionality (such as sensing, communicating, actuating, energy harvesting and storage) for a broad range of high-tech applications in wearable technology, smart home and healthcare, but it often results in a kind of fiber-like materials/devices with compromised performance caused by the formation of solid layers and/or poor integrity caused by mechanical mismatch and interfacial incompatibility. To address these challenges, integration of functional components using a continuous fiber surface-engineered with conformal porous microstructures would be an effective and attractive strategy to obtain a kind of advanced functional fibers (AFFs) with enhanced structural and functional integrity and performance. A survey of the literature, however, has shown that no systematic study is conducted in this area. Therefore, this project aims to develop a brand-new kind of continuous fibers surface-engineered with Honeycomb Porous Microstructures (F@HPMs) based on a novel, simple and efficient 1D confined Breath Figure (1D-cBF) approach with easily-scalable and non-destructive characteristics to integrate desired functional components for customizable fabrication of AFFs. In this project, the dynamic behaviors of nucleation, growth and self-assembly of BFs confined on a 1D substrate with different sizes will be studied systematically, for the first time, under different environmental conditions. They are expected to act as soft nonsolvent templates for induced assembly of polymers and lead to form F@HPMs after spontaneous evaporation of solvent and water successively. The influential variables including polymeric bricks, solvent types, solution concentration and fiber substrates will also be investigated systematically for F@HPMs with controllable microarchitectures (i.e. pore size, pore shape, pore layers, spacing distance and pore array regularity). Such kind of F@HPMs will also be studied and developed as a kind of AFFs by direct incorporation of functional/reactive additives during the 1D-cBF process, leading to a new kind of Hybrid F@HPMs (HF@HPMs). Both F@HPMs and HF@HPMs will be further used as a smart 1D substrate to accommodate the properties of functional components and integrate them for customizable fabrication of new AFFs with enhanced structural and functional integrity. As a demonstration of application, AFFs devices with rational design of porous microstructures and electroactive components will be developed as high-performed AFF energy storage devices for flexible and wearable energy storage. 將具有不同特性的材料組裝成一根連續纖維，可以制備一種新穎的一維先進纖維材料/器件（例如傳感，通信，驅動，能量收集和存儲），以廣泛用於可穿戴技術，智能家居和醫療保健等高科技領域。但這種纖維材料常常會由於固體層的形成或物理性能不匹配和界面不相容性導致性能受損。為了應對這些挑戰，通過在連續纖維的表面制備多孔結構來集成功能性材料，是一種制備具有結構增強和功能性完整的先進功能纖維（AFF）的一種有效且有吸引力的策略。然而，文獻調查表明，在這一領域目前還沒有相關的系統研究。因此，該項目旨在採用一種新穎，簡單且高效的一維限制呼吸圖（1D-cBF）的方法， 來開發一種全新的具有蜂蝸狀多孔微結構（F @ HPMs）的連續纖維。該方法可以在易擴展和非破壞性的條件下集成所需的功能材料，來定制AFF。本項目將首次在不同環境條件下，系統研究在一維纖維基質上BF的成核，生長和自組裝的動態行為。它們將作為非溶劑模板用於誘導聚合物的組裝，並且在溶劑和水自蒸發之後連續形成F @ HPM。對於具有可控微結構（即孔徑，孔形，孔層，孔間距和均勻性）的F @ HPM，還將系統地研究包括聚合物，溶劑，溶液濃度和纖維基質的影響。通過在1D-cBF過程中直接摻入功能性/活性物質，這類F @ HPM也將作為一種AFF進行研究和開發，從而形成一種新型的混合F @ HPM（HF @ HPMs）。 F @ HPM和HF @ HPM都將進一步用作一維智能器件，用以承載和支持功能組件，並將它們集成到具有結構增強和功能性完整性AFF的制備中。作為應用的示範，具有合理設計的多孔微結構和電活性部件的AFF將被開發為用於柔性和可穿戴能量存儲的高性能AFF能量存儲設備。

15206019.label: Realisation of objectives
15206019.value: All the objectives of this project have been fully achieved. For the first research objective, a novel one-dimensional confined breath figure (1D-cBF) approach for efficient preparation of a brand-new kind of 1D continuous fibers surface-engineered with conformal honeycomb porous microstructures (F@HPMs) and a novel kind of Hybrid F@HPMs (HF@HPMs) with functional nanomaterials incorporated in porous microstructures has been designed and developed [1-3]. Various functional additives (such as TiO2 NPs, Cu NPs, ZnO NWs, and Ag NWs) were incorporated for developing HF@HPMs for customized functionalities. Moreover, the loaded additives can be well dispersed in the porous platforms with an alleviative embedded phenomenon and enlarged exposing areas. As a demonstration, TiO2/HF@HPMs that incorporate with TiO2 nanoparticles were fabricated for enhanced photodegradation of organic pollutants [2]. For the second research objective, a facile approach to investigate the thermodynamic behavior of the HPMs formation process on 1D fiber substrates under different environmental conditions such as relative humidity and temperature has been developed [3]. By terminating the condensation process at different intervals of time, three main stages of BF process (i.e., nucleation, growth and self-assembly) can be readily and systematically studied, thus providing new and deeper insight into the formation mechanism of HPMs on 1D fiber substrates. Specifically, a high relative (RH) humidity environment is the key factor in forming uniform and conformal HPMs during the BF process. A higher RH means higher condensation efficiency, so water nuclei would form more easily at the nucleation stage. As the evaporation-condensation process proceeds, the high RH environment would also facilitate the growth and self-assembly of water droplets, resulting in conformal HPMs on fiber surfaces after the removal of both water and solvent. As for the temperature, results indicate that both too high or too low temperature will prevent the forming of conformal HPMs on fiber surfaces, and the ideal temperature to conduct the BF process is 25°C [3, 6]. For the third research objective, fabricating and regulating HPMs on 1D fiber surfaces has been developed through systematically investigating the main influential factors such as the solvents, concentration, and polymer bricks that affect the formation of HPMs [1-6]. Specifically, solvents that have different water solubility, vapor pressure, and interfacial tension with water can significantly change the shape of porous microstructure as well as the spacing distance between these porous structures. Besides, a polymer solution with insufficient concentration cannot uniformly cover the whole surface of a fiber, resulting in an irregular surface microstructure, while an excessive concentration of the solution would introduce some surface defects on the obtained F@HPMs due to its high viscosity. Furthermore, the concentration would also affect the pore size and regularity of the HPMs, which implies that the F@HPMs with adjustable and controllable surface microstructures can be achieved by adjusting these experiment parameters. For the last research objective, a novel strategy to fabricate hydrothermally grew electroactive NiCo layered double hydroxide (LDH) on conductive porous microstructured stainless steel yarn (SSY@CPMs) electrode with hierarchical structures and mechanical stability has been developed [4]. The introduced porous microstructures with controllable diameter not only provided more active sites and larger exposing areas of the NiCo-LDH, but also acted as ideal platforms by establishing the mechanical interlock and firmly held the loaded materials on the substrates. The capacitive properties of the NiCo-SSY@CPMs showed a significant improvement owing to the high porosity and enhanced dispersive adhesion. The advanced all-solid-state asymmetric supercapacitor (ASC) device with great electrochemical performance and excellent mechanical reliability based on the NiCo-SSY@CPMs electrode was further assembled. The ASC device can deliver a high energy density and power density as compared to other ASC devices with similar electroactive material and configuration. More importantly, given the outstanding flexibility and robustness of this 1D fiber-shaped ASC devices, it can directly sew onto common fabrics for energy storage and power the commercial electronics [4]. 15206019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206019.value: In this project, a unique 1D confined breath figure (1D-cBF) strategy for direct fabrication of a brand-new kind of continuous fibers surface-engineered with honeycomb porous microstructures (F@HPMs) as well as a new kind of hybrid F@HPMs (HF@HPMs) that were incorporated with desired functional components were designed and developed for fabrication of advanced functional fibers (AFFs). The approach was facile and versatile for customizable preparation of AFFs based on different fibers (e.g., PET fibers, nylon fibers, and stainless-steel yarns) with different polymer bricks (e.g., SBS, PMMA, and PDMS-g-PAs). The thermodynamic study showed that, with the synergistic effect of the substrates, environmental conditions (relative humidity and temperature) and other influential variables (e.g., diameters of substrates, solvent types, concentrations, and polymer bricks), the surface morphology of the micropatterns was controllable and adjustable with the variation of these preparation parameters. Solvent with low boiling point and high immiscibility with water are ideal candidates for the 1D-cBF process. Besides, the optimal solution concentration in the 1D-cBF process to form ideal F@HPMs is between 150 and 200 mg/ml. In addition, high relative humidity (e.g. >99%) and room temperature (e.g. 25oC) is preferred for forming uniform and conformal HPMs. Moreover, this strategy allowed various functional nanocomponents (such as TiO2 NPs, Cu NPs, ZnO NWs, and Ag NWs) to be directly incorporated on the fibers for developing HF@HPMs with customized functionalities. This novel kind of AFFs have demonstrated promising application in various fields including photocatalytic degradation, biomechanical energy harvesting, human motion sensing, and energy storage. Experimental results showed that photocatalytic efficiency of TiO2-incorporated HF@HPMs sample shows 30% enhancement as compared to that of control sample without porous microstructures. For biomechanical energy harvesting, the AFFs based SNF@HPMs-TENG with optimal surface microporous structures showed high electrical outputs with a high power density of 390.8 mW/m2. For human motion sensing, the AFFs based SNF@HPMs-Fabric sensor possesses great sensing capacity that can detect the bending, tactile and frictional variations. For wearable energy storage, the AFFs based conductive NiCo-SSY@CPMs electrode with hierarchical structures showed significantly promoted electrochemical performance. The assembled supercapacitor device also showed a high voltage window, great electrochemical performance and excellent mechanical stability. It can deliver a maximum energy density of 22.52 μWh·cm-2 and the maximum power density of 7.43 mW·cm-2. Based on the research work of this project, we have published 4 SCI journal articles (among which 3 articles were published in journals with impact factor over 10.0) and they have been cited for 45 times in the reporting period. In addition, we also presented our research outcomes in 2 international conferences. One PhD student has also been successfully trained. Two awards, including one conference presentation award and one RPg outstanding research achievement award, were obtained.

15206019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206019.value: In this project, the novel AFFs-based materials/devices have been developed and fabricated through 1D-cBF surface microstructural engineering. Through investigating the formation mechanism of the BF-induced HPMs on fiber substrates followed by developing the AFFs with customized functions, this research project may create a new route for AFFs to fulfill specific requirements of advanced applications. Results showed that their customizable functionalities and improved performance have promising potentials in various applications such as photocatalysis, sensing, and energy harvest/storage applications. A possible direction for future work is to explore how this novel approach and the resulting AFFs can be used for high-impact and meaningful applications. This may require identifying and choosing a suitable application domain, conducting a thorough analysis and comparison of other alternatives with similar functionalities, improving the proposed method, optimizing the composite materials and structures, obtaining quality certification, and developing prototypes, etc. Potential partnerships with interested companies may also be sought to support these future endeavors.

15206019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15206019.value: Assembly of different materials with disparate properties into fiber can lead to a novel kind of 1D advanced functional fibers (AFFs) materials/devices with desired functionality for a broad range of applications. However, the poor integrity of the functional additives with the solid fiber surface often results in compromised performance. To address these challenges, developing a fiber that is surface-engineered with conformal porous microstructures is an effective and attractive strategy. A survey of the literature has shown that no systematic study is conducted in this area. Therefore, this project aims to develop a kind of continuous fibers surface-engineered with honeycomb porous microstructures (F@HPMs) and hybrid F@HPMs (HF@HPMs) based on a novel 1D confined breath figure (1D-cBF) approach for customizable fabrication of AFFs. More specifically, the project addresses fundamental issues of the design, fabrication, structure, performance and application of the 1D AFFs based materials/devices. Studies were also carried out to analyze various influential factors of materials and processing parameters. The significance of this project is to provide a feasible way for direct creation of conformal porous microstructures on nonplanar and flexible fiber surface and shed light on the rational design of AFFs as efficient materials/devices through manipulation of surface microstructures.

15206419.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15206419.value: 太陽能光伏發電與能量存儲智能協調控制

15206419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206419.value: Now, it is time to start thinking beyond the conventional proportional–integral–derivative (PID) methods. For decades, the cascaded linear control with PID regulators has been dominating the power converter control techniques. This control approach can achieve satisfactory performance in applications like electric drives. In distributed generation systems with fluctuating output from renewable energy sources and variable power demand, power quality issues such as voltage rise or drop have become critical concerns. Traditional cascaded control featuring relatively slow dynamic response is not effective to tackle this fluctuation. The objective of this project is to develop innovative control strategies to facilitate renewable energy grid integration for reliable and high quality power supply. As the electronic interface between the renewable energy sources and the power grid, power converters play a vital role to accommodate the additional variability of renewables. Unfortunately, existing power converters still lack sufficient control flexibility and intelligence that enable smart operation. Despite research efforts that have been committed previously on distributed generations and the so-called microgrids, further development of grid integration is still under investigation. By jumping out of the box of traditional cascaded linear control that has been widely used for decades, this proposal aims to develop a holistic approach to integrate large-scale solar photovoltaics (PVs) into the distribution network. At the converter level, for the first time, an innovative strategy using model predictive control for energy storage DC-DC converters and parallel PV inverters will be developed for reliable grid integration and high quality power. Then, a decentralized power control method will be developed for improving the stability of grid voltage, through which both the bidirectional active and reactive power flows can be coordinated by controlling the grid-connected inverters. The Hong Kong government is urgently looking for solutions for high PV penetration under the context of its own environment featuring high population density and large power demand within limited space. The Hong Kong Polytechnic University will collaborate with Aalborg University on such an important topic. The proposed methods will be verified by both numerical simulation and experimental testing. The theoretical findings and results will be disseminated in top journals and summarized into technical reports. With our years of experience in power electronics and renewable power generations, together with the support from industry, we believe that the project is feasible and will have a positive impact in global academic and industry communities. 盡管傳統的級聯式PID線性控制技術已經廣泛應用於電氣驅動等領域，其相對緩慢的動態響應特性卻不能有效處理能源系統中的能量波動。雖然研究人員對分布式發電和微網有一定的研究，但現有的功率變換器仍缺乏足夠的控制靈活性和智能程度。在這個背景下，這個項目致力於研究新穎的控制技術以實現大規模的太陽能光伏並網發電。首先，我們將會開發一種全新的預測控制技術來調度光伏系統中的能量存儲單元。然後，通過並網逆變器來實現微電網的能量優化流動，以提高電壓質量。基於在電力電子和可再生能源發電方面的經驗，以及來自業界的支持，我們相信本項目將會對學術和業界帶來積極影響。

15206519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15206519.value: In recent years, there has been growing interest in the development of the aviation and aerospace industries in Hong Kong and China. Hong Kong has set aside HK$100 million budgets to establish a training fund for aviation transport to attract young talents to enroll in the aero-industry. In China, huge resources have been devoted to aerospace engineering, which is expected to continue in the foreseeable future. Hong Kong academia shall seize this golden opportunity and play an active role in her motherland’s endeavor. In this project, thermochemical nonequilibrium phenomena occurring in flowfields over hypersonic vehicles will be investigated via numerical and experimental techniques. During hypersonic flights, the properties of air deviate from ideal behaviors due to the extremely high temperature (up to 30,000 K depending on the velocity). Under these conditions, excitation of molecular internal energy modes and chemical reactions among reactive species would occur, which could have a significant impact on the aerothermodynamic characteristics of hypersonic vehicles, for example, the anomalous flap angles observed in the maiden flight of Space Shuttle Columbia. Given that there have been only a limited number of experiments, understanding the so-called real gas effects heavily relies on computations. There are many examples of hypersonic flows of contemporary interest that state-of-the-art computational fluid dynamics (CFD) solvers using conventional vibration–dissociation coupling models fail to simulate accurately. An illustrative example is shock-induced separated flows with real gas effects. In this project, numerical simulations based on the high-fidelity state-specific method and high-enthalpy wind tunnel experiments will be conducted to further understand the processes of vibrational excitation and dissociation, as well as their coupling. The numerical data will be analyzed in detail to gain insight into the flow physics and provide a guideline to establish a more accurate reduced-order model for CFD simulations. The experimental measurements will serve as a supplement to the existing experimental studies and a benchmark for CFD validations. The outcomes of this project are expected to finally explain the large discrepancies between numerical simulations and experiments for high-enthalpy shock-induced separated flows that have troubled the aerospace community for more than two decades. Also, to the applicants’ knowledge, this proposed study will be the first comprehensive experimental and numerical study on the thermochemical nonequilibrium modelling in China. It is envisaged that the knowledge gained from this project will provide an academic foundation for the development of next-generation hypersonic transportation systems.

15206519.label: Realisation of objectives
15206519.value: The project has been completed successfully. All the project objectives have been achieved. For objective 1, state-specific kinetic data for vibrational excitation and dissociation of air species have been collected from recent quantum chemistry calculations including the vibration‒translation (V–T) and vibration‒dissociation (V–D) transition rate constants for N2‒N, O2‒O, N2‒O, and O2‒N interactions. We have also calculated a complete dataset of vibration–vibration–translation (V–V–T) transition rate constants for N2‒N2, O2‒O2, N2‒O2, and NO‒NO interactions using forced harmonic oscillator models over a wide range of temperature. Using these data, state-specific simulations were performed in different scenarios including post normal shock flow, nozzle flow, expansion flow, etc. For objective 2, numerical simulations have been performed to further understand hypersonic double-cone flows prior to the wind tunnel experiments. Specifically, the effect of nose bluntness and the global stability were examined. Experiments were conducted in the JF-12 hypersonic wind tunnel at different flow conditions. Surface pressure and heat transfer were measured. For objective 3, based on the high-fidelity state-specific data, we established an improved two-temperature model to compare with the existing two-temperature models. Different models were used to simulate the high-enthalpy double-cone flow. For objective 4, a non-Boltzmann two-temperature model was established and used to revisit the double-cone flow. Non-Boltzmann effects were also examined in high-enthalpy flow in expansion tunnel nozzles. The project has successfully developed many theoretical and numerical tools and generated valuable experimental data for the study of high-enthalpy flow. The outcomes have advanced the understanding of the underlying physical mechanisms.

15206519.label: Major findings and research outcome
15206519.value: The major findings are listed below: 1. For post normal shock flow, comparisons were made with existing NO emission measurements in the ultraviolet and mid-infrared spectrum. At velocities of 3–4 km/s, some of the current O2 dissociation rates may be inaccurate. At a higher velocity of 6.81 km/s, the NO mole fraction predicted by the state-specific model is around an order of magnitude greater than that predicted by the two-temperature model. 2. For thermochemical nonequilibrium flow in expansion tunnel nozzles, different thermochemical excitations in the freestream at the test section can lead to different postshock radiation emissions by more than 50%. However, the non-Boltzmann distributions in the freestream have no influence. 3. For the first time in the literature, we found a critical nose radius, beyond which the separation bubble grows suddenly. An estimation of the critical radius was also established, which agreed well with the numerical results and existing experimental data. 4. We also revealed that the double-cone flow can be globally unstable to three-dimensional perturbations. The criterion of the onset of global instability was established in terms of a scaled deflection angle. Direct numerical simulations confirmed that the supercritical double-cone flow is intrinsically three-dimensional, unsteady and exhibits strong azimuthal variations in the peak heating. 5. Double-cone experiments were conducted at 3 MJ/kg. The effects of vibrational excitation were found to be weak. However, flow transition was detected, which merits further investigations.

15206519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15206519.value: In future study, more experiments will be conducted over different configurations, such as double cones at higher enthalpies, compression corners, Prandtl-Meyer expansion, etc. Modeling of thermochemical nonequilibrium at higher enthalpies will also be considered to include electronic excitation, ionization, and radiation.

Under these conditions, excitation of molecular internal energy modes and chemical reactions among reactive species would occur, which would have a significant impact on the aerothermodynamic characteristics of hypersonic vehicles. 15207519.value: The project has yielded significant findings and research outcomes, leading to the publication of 13 papers in top journals and supporting the work of several PhD students and postdoc research. Here is a summary of the major findings and research outcomes based on the objectives outlined: (1) Analyzed systematically the mechanisms and identify the applicable regions for different operation modes when using the “adaptive full-range decoupled ventilation strategy”, over the full range of internal load and outdoor climate conditions; (2) Developed an uncertainty-based method for the robust optimal design of air-conditioning systems by introducing a proposed uncertainty factor to handle the uncertainties effectively for the convenient and full implementation of the proposed adaptive ventilation strategy; (3) Developed a risk-based online robust optimal control strategy, which determines the optimal control mode and settings in order to minimize energy use and make online control optimization decisions based on qualified risk and benefits when taking measurement uncertainties and component degradation into account. (5) Comprehensively investigated the commonly-used air-conditioning systems for high-tech cleanrooms, and systematically assessed energy and economic performance, and applicable situations in the full range of climatic conditions during the total life span. (6) Identified the most influential design parameters of buildings in different climate zone by sensitivity analysis and systematically compared the impacts of climate and building height on the key building design focus. (7) Developed a generic air-conditioning system design optimization framework for air-conditioning systems by integrating heat recovery and free cooling techniques at air-side and water-side, respectively. (8) Developed a novel outdoor air ventilation strategy that enables maximum air-side free cooling potential and optimized energy-efficient operation for air-conditioning systems under full ranges of weather conditions and application scenarios.

15208019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15208019.value: Nowadays, electronic and electrical equipment continues to proliferate in buildings to meet the ever-increasing demand of businesses. Some of the engineering equipment in buildings is connected via wiring systems to outdoor overhead or underground lines. Such wires may not be struck by lightning directly, but are frequently subject to induced transients in indirect lightning strikes. These transients propagate along the lines to the buildings, and can be reinforced by short-wire structures in the buildings. They will cause damage to or the malfunctioning of sensitive devices if protection is not provided appropriately. In recent decades, lightning transients in line systems have been studied significantly using different methods, including the transmission line method and the equivalent circuit method. However, there has been no systematic discussion on transients in a grounded system consisting of both short wires and long transmission lines in indirect lightning strikes. Two major challenges are encountered when applying these methods, including (a) the instability in evaluating transient currents in wire loops and (b) the inconsistency of voltage definition used in these two methods. This project aims to develop a novel electromagnetic model of a grounded wire structure connecting transmission lines in indirect lightning strikes. This model will be built by integrating field-to-line equations for long lines and partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) equations for shot wires with the full electric and magnetic coupling method. A generalized field-to-line model will be developed by including the influence of the grounding grid or ground potential rise. An enhanced PEEC model will be developed to tackle the instability problem. In this project a comprehensive modelling and simulation procedure will be developed to evaluate the lightning transients in a grounded structure during indirect lightning strikes. The structure with a combination of short and long wires is commonly used in electric power systems, electrified railway systems and telecommunication systems. This procedure will help to evaluate lightning stress on the connected equipment of practical systems, the risk of equipment failure as well as the losses resulting from failure. The results obtained from the procedure will further enhance our knowledge of lightning-induced effects and enable updating of design principles and the production of guidelines for effective lightning protection. 为满足日益增长的社会发展需求, 用电设备在建筑物中不断增加。建筑物中存在大量的用电设备，这些设备的供电系统会通过电缆连接到室外架空线或地下线路。此类导线在间接雷击中会产生暫态过电压电流。如果没有提供有效地保护,将会导致设备的损坏或出现故障。 近几十年来,供电系统在雷电暂态过程受到的影响得到了大量的研究,研究方法包括分析“传输线路法”和“等效电路方法”。然而目前还没有对由长短线组成的接地系统在间接雷暂态影响下的研究。目前研究这个问题会遇到两个主要的挑战, (a) 不稳定的暂态环路电流(b) 这种长短线组成的接地系统中，电压定义与通常传输线系统不一致。 此项目旨在开发一种新型的接地线结构电磁模型。 该模型将采用全电磁耦合方法,同时建立一个修正后的PEEC模型来解决不稳定问题。此项目将提供一个完整的建模和仿真程序,以评估间接雷击期间接地结构中的雷电暂态过程。我们知道短线和长线组合的线路结构常用于电力系统、电气化铁路系统和电信系统。此过程将有助于评估实际系统连接设备的雷电影响、设备雷害故障风险以及故障造成的损失。从该程序获得的结果将进一步增强我们对雷电感应效果的了解,并且能够优化防雷设计准则和制定完善的防雷指南。

15208019.label: Realisation of objectives
15208019.value: This project targeted the development of an integrated model for short wires and long wires in electric power grids for lightning transient analysis under lightning and its application to different energy systems. The objectives set in this project have been achieved. Under indirect lightning strikes, the general field-to-line-coupling equation can be obtained by using either Jeffimenko’s equations or Uman’s equations. However, an instability problem was observed. After conducting both analytical and numerical studies extensively, an improved algorithm was provided to solve this instability problem and was tested for both near- and far-field cases. It was validated by the finite-difference time-domain method. The issue of time step and segment length was addressed. Green’s functions for the generalized PEEC formulation in the air and lossy-ground space were developed. Both the source and field points can be located in any layer of the air-ground. As a robust and easy-implemented approach, the direct real-axis integration is presented with the techniques for removing the singularity and accelerating the convergence. Closed-form expressions were derived for the quasi-static and asymptotic approximation of SIs, and an image model was developed for quasi-static SIs. The Greens’ functions then were contributed by the source and/or its image. This model was used to derive the frequency-invariant PEEC model for fast transient simulation in the time domain. These results helped to develop PEEC models for lightning transient analysis. Under direct lightning strikes, the lightning channel can be directly integrated into a PEEC model. This issue has been thoroughly investigated in this project. Two options were exploited, i.e., a full-scale retarded PEEC model and a hybrid distributed circuit (DC)/PEEC model. The DC model has a great advantage in modeling the lightning channel, by including the dynamic physical behavior of the lightning flash. A lumped voltage source was introduced to ensure an “undisturbed” current waveform at the attachment point. A procedure was provided to determine this voltage source in a nonlinear circuit. The proposed model was verified with the experimental data collected under lightning. In this project a novel Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC)- multi-conductor-transmission-line (MTL) hybrid numerical method was first proposed. This method retains both computational efficiency and accuracy when dealing with lightning surges in a mixed system with long wires and short wires, which is difficult to tackle with traditional computation methods. In this framework, overhead line wires are represented by the MTL model, poles, grounding electrodes, and others with the PEEC model. A model for mutual coupling among different parts including a lightning channel is proposed to integrate sub-systems. The mutual coupling between the long and short wires is considered by matrices of mutual inductance and potential coefficient, as well as the time-retarded effect. The code for building the hybrid model has been implemented on the MATLAB platform. The transient surge calculations of the hybrid method have been verified by both the 3D-FDTD model and experimental measurements. With a high computing performance and convenient integration of the nonlinear devices, such as surge arresters, insulators, and transformers in electrical systems, the hybrid method has been used to investigate the lightning transient issues focusing on the lightning protection of high-voltage towers and medium-voltage distribution networks. With the proposed method, this project investigated a systematic parametric investigation into lightning protection on MV distribution lines, including a shield wire (SW), surge arresters (SAs), line insulation, and grounding configurations, from the design point of view. Furthermore, a novel comprehensive assessment of lightning protection schemes was introduced for the distribution OHLs from two aspects: lightning performance and economic cost. Traditional protection assessments tended to focus on the flashover rate but ignored the failure rate of protection equipment itself, e.g., surge arresters. This led to a situation in which the economy of a lightning protection scheme could not be addressed appropriately. This project introduced differentiated protection for distribution systems and developed a novel procedure for the design of differentiated SA configurations, i.e., identifying appropriate positions for limited SAs to achieve desired lightning performance. In addressing differentiated SA protection, a multi-objective optimization problem was formulated by minimizing both the flashover number and SA damage rate. An artificial neural network and an energy-distribution surrogate model were developed for efficiently evaluating these two parameters in the optimization. When addressing the flashover rate, a simplified probability-based approach was proposed A theoretical time-domain analysis of lightning surge propagation on a multistage and multi-conductor tower was performed. An extended traveling wave theory using electric scalar potential was introduced. The non-TEM wave propagation in the tower is characterized by time/position-variant transient impedance. The analytical formulas of the transient impedance are presented for any position/time in the tower, as well as those of the reflection coefficient at a discontinuity. The concept of primary and secondary waves is introduced to depict the multiple reflections in the tower. Using the traditional transmission line theory could lead to a significant error of the current in the tower. The proposed method was also applied to studying the lightning transients on PV systems. With the rapid growth of solar energy generation, lightning hazards to photovoltaic (PV) plants have received increasing attention. Many PV plants were built in the transmission corridor, leading to an increased occurrence of lightning damage. These damages were caused by lightning strikes to the transmission line nearby, which had not been well addressed in the literature. This project investigated the transient behaviors of a practical PV plant when a nearby transmission line was struck by lightning. Three types of lightning damages were investigated, namely failure of PV inverters, breakdown of bypass diodes, and arcing between metallic parts. Both bypass diode breakdown and arcing-related incidents in the PV systems have not been analyzed systemically in the literature.
