15208019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15208019.value: 14 journal papers and 2 conference papers were published. In this project, the PEEC model of wires in the air-ground space was developed using the scalar and dyadic Green’s functions. The ground effect on the wires in the air or ground soil was reported. Numerical evaluation procedures of Green’s functions and circuit parameters of the wires were provided. The quasi-static and asymptotic models of the lossy ground were derived. An image theory of the ground was proposed. This model facilitates the fast transient simulation in the time domain [9]. Two different integrated models for short wires and long wires have been proposed. In these models, short wires were represented with the PEEC model, and long wires were represented with transmission line equations which were discretized either by the central difference method or backward Euler method. When the back Euler method was employed, a large matrix equation using the modified nodal analysis technique was employed to solve the problem. While the central difference method was employed, the big matrix was broken down into several small standalone matrices. This greatly improves the computational efficiency in solving a nonlinear circuit [1-2]. A traveling wave theory for a vertical structure such as a tower in the transmission line system was developed. The non-TEM wave propagation in the tower was characterized by time/position-variant transient impedance. Similar to the traditional wave propagation theory, the transient impedance varying with position/time was introduced, and its analytical formulas were derived, as well as those of the reflection coefficient at a discontinuity [3]. The proposed method has been applied to analyze lightning transients as well as their impacts on equipment and devices in PV power stations and distribution systems. The mechanism of component failures was investigated in the PV power systems, and mitigation measures were proposed [6]. The lightning transients on insulators, lightning arresters, and transformers were analyzed, and insulator flashover and lightning arrester failures in the distribution systems were characterized against the design parameters [1,5,7]. A concept of differentiated protection with lightning arresters was proposed, and optimization techniques to design effective protection schemes [10-13]. Lightning performance of a distribution line using the Monte Carlo method was also performed with special acceleration techniques [11,14]. A special strategy was proposed to select lateral distance for the assessment area in the Monte Carlo simulation procedure, which helped to relieve the computational burden while the assessment accuracy was preserved.

15208019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15208019.value: We will target the full-wave electromagnetic transient analysis on the overhead lines in the time domain when the TEM-mode assumption does not hold. The overhead lines are subjected to direct or indirect lightning or other intense electromagnetic pulses. The PEEC method will be fully developed by resolving the issues arising from the connection of lumped circuit components, large-size power equipment, and traditional transmission line models; the issue of ground return current; the issue of PEEC formulation selection; and the issues of improving computation efficiency in the PEEC applications.

15208019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15208019.value: Nowadays, electronic and electrical equipment continues to proliferate to meet the ever-increasing demand of businesses. It is connected via a wiring system to outdoor overhead or underground lines. Such wires may not be struck by lightning directly, but are frequently subject to induced transients in indirect lightning strikes. These transients propagate along the lines to the connected equipment and can be reinforced by short-wire structures in the buildings. This project developed a novel electromagnetic model of a grounded wire structure connecting distribution lines for transient analysis under indirect lightning strikes. This model was built by integrating field-to-line equations for long lines and partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) equations for shot wires with the full electric and magnetic coupling method. A generalized field-to-line model was developed by including the influence of the grounding grid or ground potential rise. An enhanced PEEC model was developed to tackle the instability problem. A comprehensive modeling and simulation procedure has been developed to evaluate the lightning transients in a grounded structure during indirect lightning strikes. This procedure can help to evaluate lightning stress on the connected equipment of practical systems, the risk of equipment failure as well as the losses resulting from failure.

15209119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209119.value: Geo-hazards, including landslides, debris flows, collapse of dikes/levees, ground subsidence, sinkholes/cavities, have caused great annual death toll and/or property/infrastructure damage in Hong Kong and around the world. Hazard mitigation and prevention have been a long-standing challenge. Hong Kong is particularly vulnerable to landslide and debris flow due to frequent heavy rainfall and dense population living close to steep terrains. One major mechanism accounting for the initiation of landslide and debris flow is the mitigation of fine particles through broadly graded or gap-graded soils during rainfall infiltration, as evidenced by data from many disaster sites. Eroded fines may on one hand lead to loosened soil structure with degraded soil strength, and meanwhile they may cause clogging in soil, reduce soil permeability and result in buildup of excess pore pressure and drop of effective stress towards instability. The concurrent mechanisms of internal erosion with fines clogging (or self-filtration) are broadly termed as suffusion in engineering practice, but have not been thoroughly investigated towards deeper understanding of the phenomenon. Indeed, it is widely known that suffusion has attributed to the collapse of dams/dikes/levees, ground subsidence and sinkholes/cavities. There is indeed an urgent need to advance our understanding on suffusion for better hazard mitigation. An advanced predictive model reflective of key grain-scale physics during the suffusion process is highly desirable but unavailable in current practice. This project aims at developing an integrated computational and theoretical model to elevate our predictive capability of soil suffusion and enhance our understanding of the mechanics of suffusion in gap-graded cohesionless soils. A coupled CFD-DEM approach will be developed to understand the governing mechanisms from grain scale of soils. Primary focus will be placed on the interplaying mechanisms of internal erosion and clogging with their influence on the overall hydro-mechanical responses. The influences of soil fabric and grain shape will be accounted for realistic modeling. Based on that, a novel suffusion rule and a micromechanics-based constitutive model will be developed and further integrated into a finite element code for simulation of engineering scale problems where suffusion may be important. The project will constitute a first-ever systematic multiscale and multiphysics study on suffusion. It will offer a novel and reliable coupled hydro-mechanical modeling tool with rigorous microstructural characterizations, and provide a theoretical basis to understand rainfall-induced suffusions accounting for major geo-hazards. It will contribute significantly to geo-hazard mitigation and prevention for Hong Kong and many other regions/countries around the world. 地質災害，包括山體滑坡、泥石流、堤壩倒塌、地面沉降、天坑或洞穴等，在香港和世界各地造成了巨大的人員傷亡和財產或基礎設施破壞。減輕此類災害和預防是一項長期挑戰。由於頻繁的強降雨和陡峭的地形，居住人口密集的香港特別容易受到山體滑坡和泥石流的影響。導致滑坡和泥石流發生的一個主要機制是在降雨入滲在間斷性級配土中細顆粒發生遷移，如許多災害現場的數據所示。細粒沖刷一方面可能導致土結構鬆散、土強度降低，同時可能導致土堵塞而誘發土滲透性降低，導致孔隙壓力過大，有效應力下降，最終導致土體不穩定。這種內部沖刷與細粒堵塞的並發機制在工程實踐中被廣泛稱為滲流侵蝕，但目前尚未深入研究以更深入地理解該現象。事實上，人們普遍知道，滲流侵蝕會導致大壩/堤壩垮塌、地面沉降的發生和天坑或洞穴的形成乃至崩塌。因此。確實迫切需要提高我們對此現象的深入理解以期達到更好的減災效果。為此，一個基於顆粒物理的能描述滲流侵蝕的高級預測模型是非常期待的，然而在當前工程實踐中尚缺乏此類模擬方法。 該項目旨在開發一個綜合的計算和理論模型，以提高我們對土滲流侵蝕過程的預測能力，並增強我們對間斷性級配無粘性土中滲流侵蝕現象的理解。本項目將從顆粒角度出發開發一種耦合水動力-離散元方法來理解土中滲流侵蝕的控制機制。主要重點為內部侵蝕和堵塞的相互作用機制及其對整體水力響應的影響。土體組構和顆粒形狀的影響將被考慮到模擬中來。在此基礎上，將提出一種新的滲流侵蝕法則和基於微觀力學的本構模型，並進一步導入到有限元代碼中，用於模擬滲流侵蝕較為突出的工程問題。 該項目首次針對滲流侵蝕作非常系統的多尺度和多物理場耦合研究。項目最終將提供一個考慮微觀結構特徵的創新可靠的水力耦合模擬工具，為理解降雨誘發主要地質災害的成因提供理論依據，對香港和世界上許多其他地區/國家的減災和防災很有實踐意義。

15209119.label: Realisation of objectives
15209119.value: All of the objectives have been achieved through the following activities along with the original plan. (1) Unresolved CFD-DEM modelling approach was developed for spherical particles and suffusion simulations were carried out for different influencing factors and mechanical conditions. In addition, fully resolved CFD-DEM modelling approach was also developed for irregular particles and suffusion investigation. In the un-resolved CFD-DEM method, the fluid is solved by the locally averaged Navier-Stokes (N-S) equations, which account for the presence of solid particles based on the Eulerian formulation. The obtained flow field is a weighted average over the fluid grid in the Eulerian formulation, while the particle motion is described by the Lagrangian formulation. Therefore, a key issue in calculating the fluid-solid interaction forces is to perform the Lagrangian-Eulerian mapping, i.e., to determine the volume fraction of the fluid and the solid within each fluid mesh. The fluid–solid interaction forces consist mainly of the drag force, the pressure gradient force, the lift force, and the virtual mass force. For dense particle flow, the main factors are the pressure gradient force and the drag force. The CFD-DEM coupling involves several steps for the initialization and transfer of information between the fluid and solid phases. The un-resolved CFD-DEM method has high computational efficiency, thanks to the use of the averaging theory, which permits the use of a coarse fluid mesh. However, this approach results in fluid pressure and velocity being averaged within the grid, which lowers the computational accuracy, particularly when dealing with bypassing fluids around complex boundaries, such as shaped particles. The fully-resolved CFD-DEM method differs from the un-resolved approach in that it employs the classical Navier-Stokes equations, which consider only the fluid phase to determine the flow velocity and pressure. Interaction forces between solid and liquid are directly obtained via the integration of the equations along the particle boundary, rather than relying on empirical drag force models, which significantly enhances the computational accuracy. The fluid phase fulfils the two equations, mass and momentum balance. The fully-resolved CFD-DEM provides an accurate solution of the bypass flow field around the particles through the above N-S equations, where the particle surface is regarded as a no-slip boundary in the pore fluid flow region. The particle surface boundary in the CFD fluid calculation region is always changing because the particles are subject to translation and rotation. The key problem of the fully-resolved coupling is to deal with this fluid boundary motion due to particle motion. The commonly used method is the Fiction Domain Method (FDM). In order to consider the influence of particle motion on the fluid field and satisfy the rigid body constraint, the velocity of the fluid needs to be corrected through the mapped particle velocity and fluid cell velocity. Through this correction of velocity, the rigid body constraint is enforced in the particle domain and the no-slip boundary condition in FDM is ensured. The hydraulic force exerted on the particles by the fluid is calculated by integrating the fluid stress over the particle surface. The fully-resolved CFD-DEM method provides an accurate solution for the fluid, making it a valuable tool for an accurate calculation of the fluid flow in cases such as the coupling between fluid and non-spherical particles. A fine grid in the fully-resolved approach allows taking into account the particle morphology, including angularity and roughness, with high accuracy. However, the use of a fine grid increases significantly the computational cost, limiting therefore the fully-resolved method to situations involving only a small number of particles and fluid domains. (2) The micromechanics-based multiscale model was developed with considering suffusion-induced anisotropy using the computer language FORTRAN. The recently developed micromechanics-based elasto-plastic sand-silt mixture model by the PI was adopted. The novelty of this model is the introduction of the equivalent mean size and the evolution of the position of the critical state line in terms of average coordination number with fines content for various sand-silt mixtures, which was validated by many experimental results including drained triaxial tests on HK-CDG samples before and after internal erosion conducted. The model was developed under static hypothesis, in which the micro–macro relationship can be derived by linking the inter-particle forces to the stress increments. The force-displacement relations defined at inter-particle contacts are displacement driven contact laws. Using the orientation distribution function for contacts, the soil anisotropy is physically characterized in a direct way. The key point of this phase should be to capture the initial and suffusion-induced anisotropy in terms of soil fabric for different particle shapes and different initial deposition angles. This was described by proposing the evolution rules representing the induced anisotropy or evolution of soil fabric according to CFD-DEM simulations. (3) The multiphysics and multiscale continuum modeling approach was developed based on mixture theory using ABAQUS-UEL function (user defined element for hydro-mechanical coupling analysis, computer language FORTRAN). All models were validated using the measured or CFD-DEM results. A four-constituent based two-dimensional finite element model has been developed by PI for only internal erosion, in which the saturated soil is considered as a mixture of four interacting constituents. In this task, the new suffusion rule (developed in Task 1) describing the detachment, transport and clogging of the fine particles induced by suffusion was implemented into the mass exchange model between the solid and the fluid phases. Then, the solid skeleton behavior was described by the micromechanics-based model accounting for effects of fines content and anisotropy. Based on the mass balance, the momentum balance equations, and the mechanical model, the coupled suffusion-mechanical process with the finite element approach was proposed, with governing equations can be obtained by combining the balance and constitutive equations in order to formulate the Initial Boundary Value Problem (IBVP) of suffusion. Since this is a non-linear transient problem, weak forms of the governing equation system was implemented into a finite element solver ABAQUS. A new isoparametric 20-node quadrilateral 3D cubic brick element, so-called UEL (user defined element) technique, was developed for this purpose. The soil skeleton displacement discretization is based on a quadratic Serendipity element with a 20 nodes element, whereas the other 4 variables (pw, fi, c and qw) are discretized using a linear interpolation (8 nodes located at the corners).

15209119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209119.value: For Objective 1: The research team has developed coupled CFD-DEM modelling approach (both unresolved for spherical particles and fully resolved for shaped particles) and well validated it through particle settling tests (settling of particles with different shapes into water) compared to analytical solutions. Then it has been served as numerical tests for investigating suffusion with different factors, including the seepage direction compared to gravity, fines content, particle roughness, concentration of fines in fluid, particle morphology, fabric anisotropy, and so on. The role of all these factors has been identified under different hydraulic and mechanical loading conditions, including torsional shear condition, simple shear condition, an engineering condition-tunnel with leakage, and so on. The coupling process of erosion and clogging with these factors has been investigated and clarified. Novel suffusion rules have been proposed with introducing some important factors. For Objective 2: The initial and suffusion-induced anisotropy relating to soil fabric and grain shape for different kinds of soil samples and mechanical & seepage conditions has been investigated and clarified through coupled CFD-DEM simulations. The micromechanics-based anisotropic constitutive model has been enhanced considering effects of fines with initial and suffusion-induced anisotropy. The framework has been established based on static approach with volume averaging from particle contact level to macro stress-strain relationship. The evolution of fabric anisotropy for different variables has been carefully examined in terms of modeling performance as well as the numerical convergence. The modeling performance and numerical convergence have been examined. For Objective 3: In this approach, the mechanical models for granular soil, the unified modeling approaches for fines content-dependency of granular soils and the hydraulic modeling of suffusion are necessary. The hydro-mechanical model considering both suffusion and mechanical loading has been developed by combining the three components. For each component of the model, alternative choices were provided. Then, a multiphysics and multiscale (micromechanics-based) continuum modeling approach has been established based on mixture theory using ABAQUS-UEL function (user defined element for hydro-mechanical coupling analysis) and validated with good model accuracy. The proposed computational framework was solved using an enhanced stabilized finite element method. Simulations of laboratory tests, an example of a dike-on-foundation problem, as well as an example of seepage-induced granular slope failure, demonstrated the reliability and applicability of this coupled numerical approach for suffusion problems. Parameters identification using optimization method has been proposed and validated.

15209119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209119.value: The research carried out and the outcomes achieved provide us a good potential for further development of some interesting aspects, which has been preliminarily investigated and can be further investigated in the future: (1) The process of triggering, initiation and sliding/collapse for slopes and hydraulic works features typically large deformation. In treating large deformation, we developed the Stabilized Node-based Strain-smoothing Particle Finite Element Method (SNS-PFEM) that inheriting both the ﬂexibility of mesh-free particle methods on the arbitrary changes in geometry and the solid mathematical foundation of the traditional FEM. For hydro-mechanical modeling, a two-phase two-layer model has been developed based mixture theory and can be adopted for suffusion-related large deformation problem. (2) Using the developed large deformation approach SNS-PFEM, more disasters such as collapse of dams/dikes/levees, land subsidence and sinkholes/cavities induced by suffusion will be systematically investigated. There is an urgent need to improve the fundamental understanding of such kind of suffusion-induced geo-hazards. One PhD student trained in this project plans to work on these problems as a postdoctoral fellow.

15209119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209119.value: Hong Kong is particularly vulnerable to landslide and debris flow due to frequent heavy rainfall and dense population living close to steep terrains. One major mechanism accounting for the initiation of landslide and debris flow is the mitigation of fine particles through broadly graded or gap-graded soils during rainfall infiltration. The concurrent mechanisms of internal erosion with fines clogging are termed as suffusion in engineering practice. There is indeed an urgent need to advance our understanding on suffusion for better hazard mitigation. This project aims at developing an integrated computational and theoretical model to elevate our predictive capability of soil suffusion and enhance our understanding of the mechanics of suffusion in gap-graded cohesionless soils: (1) A coupled CFD-DEM approach has been developed to understand the governing mechanisms from grain scale of soils. (2) The influences of soil fabric and grain shape has been accounted for realistic modeling. (3) A novel suffusion rule and a micromechanics-based model has been developed and integrated into a finite element code for simulating engineering problems. The project offers a novel and reliable coupled hydro-mechanical modeling tool with rigorous microstructural characterizations, and provides a theoretical basis to understand rainfall-induced suffusions accounting for major geo-hazards.

15209619.label: Project Objectives
15209619.value: The primary objective of this study is to investigate the structural responses of the proposed beam-to-beam SMA-SCF connections when subject to cyclic loading for seismic applications in the energy dissipation bays (EDBs) of a steel MRF. In particular, the self-centring behaviour and the energy absorption capability of the proposed connection will be examined experimentally and numerically. Another major objective of the study is to develop a preliminary design model for the proposed SMA-SCF connection. All tests will be conducted at a controlled room temperature to ensure the superelastic property of the SMA. A numerical investigation of the SMA-SCF connection will be conducted using a finite element model validated by the test data. The model will be used to study the structural behaviour of the novel connection in detail. Task I-Experimental investigation. Tests of the SMA components (SMA plates and SMA Belleville spring washers) and the proposed beam-to-beam SMA-SCF connections will be conducted. The SMA component tests include tension coupon tests of the SMA plates to determine their superelastic material properties and cyclic tests in compression of the SMA-BVS washers to determine the cyclic responses of the washers. Tests of the connection, which will include 1) the thickness of the SMA plates and 2) the clear length (c) of the SMA plates (Fig. 5) as the main parameters, will be conducted to investigate the connection self-centring behaviour, its energy absorption capability, and its strength and stiffness. Task II-Numerical investigation. The numerical study of the connection specimens, which includes both material and geometric nonlinearity, will be conducted using the commercial finite element (FE) analysis programme ABAQUS. The SMA material model (Auricchio’s model) in ABAQUS will be employed to simulate the superelastic effect of the material. The validated FE model of the connection specimens will then be used to study the strength and cyclic behaviour of the proposed connection. A simplified FE model of the connection, which is able to simulate the structural behaviour of the connection and needs much less computation time, will be developed to examine numerically the seismic responses of MRFs equipped with the proposed SMA-SCF connections in the EDBs. Task III-Development of a preliminary design model for the proposed connection. A preliminary design model of the proposed SMA self-centring fuse connection will be developed based on the test and the numerical study results. The design model will ensure that the connection moment is resisted by the SMA plates and the applied shear force is resisted by the HS bearing bolts. The proposed design model will enable optimisation of the use of the SMA materials and to produce a SMA self-centring fuse connection with good self-centring behaviour and enhanced energy absorption capability.

15209619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209619.value: ABSTRACT A steel moment resisting frame (MRF) subjected to earthquake loading usually develops plastic hinges in the beams and columns to resist the applied forces and dissipate the seismic energy. The permanent deformation of the plastic hinges in the beams and columns generally leads to costly repair, or may even result in a complete demolition of the structure. To alleviate this drawback, researchers have been applying self-centring technology in steel MRFs to minimise the residual deformations of the frame developed after a seismic event. Innovative materials such as Shape Memory Alloy (SMA), in particular, Nitinol, are often employed in material-based self-centring technology. SMA is a class of metal which can sustain large deformation with the ability to recover the undeformed shape either by unloading (i.e. the superelastic effect) or heating (i.e. the shape memory effect), and dissipates energy during the loading and unloading processes. This study proposes to develop an innovative beam-to-beam SMA self-centring “fuse” (SMA-SCF) connection to be used in the energy dissipation bay (EDB) of a steel MRF. The plastic hinges formed in the beams of an EDB subject to seismic loading are expected to develop at the proposed connection. The SMA-SCF moment connection uses superelastic SMA plates connected to the steel flanges by high strength friction grip bolts to resist the connection moment. End-plates are welded to the web at the beam ends and are connected by high-strength (HS) bearing bolts with superelastic SMA-Belleville spring (BVS) washers to resist the connection shear force. The SMA-BVS washers are used to absorb the possible axial deformation of the HS bearing bolts caused by the connection moment and to contribute to the energy absorption capability of the connection. Therefore, the proposed connection is equipped with good self-centring and moderate energy absorption capabilities. The former helps provide the self-centring ability of MRFs subject to seismic loading. The primary objective of this proposed study is to investigate experimentally and numerically the structural responses of the proposed beam-to-beam SMA-SCF connections subject to cyclic loading for seismic applications in energy dissipation bays of steel MRFs. Numerical models of the connection will be developed and validated by the test results enabling a parametric study to be then made. A simplified but realistic FE model of the connection, which needs much less computation time, will be developed to examine the seismic responses of MRFs equipped with the proposed SMA-SCF connections in the EDBs using a numerical study. 在地震作用下，抗彎鋼框架通常在樑柱節點處形成塑性鉸，以抵抗外力並耗散地震能量。梁與柱上塑性鉸的永久變形會產生高昂的維修代價，甚至需要對結構進行完全拆除。為了克服這個缺點，研究人員已在抗彎鋼框架中應用自復位技術，以儘量減少震後所形成的框架殘餘變形。基於材料的自復位特性，形狀記憶合金等新材料已被使用。形狀記憶合金，是一種能夠承受較大變形的金屬材料，通過卸載（即超彈性效應）或加熱（即形狀記憶效應）可恢復初始狀態，並在載入和卸載過程中消耗能量。 本研究提出一種配置形狀記憶合金“保險絲”的自復位梁-梁新型節點，該節點使用在抗彎鋼框架中的耗能跨，地震作用下塑性鉸預計出現在耗能跨的節點連接處。形狀記憶合金“保險絲”的自復位節點是通過摩擦型高強螺栓連接超彈性形狀記憶合金板與鋼樑翼緣板。端板焊接在梁端的腹板上，並通過承壓型高強螺栓與超彈性形狀記憶合金-碟形彈簧墊圈連接，以達到節點抗剪的目的。承壓型高強螺栓的軸向變形被形狀記憶合金-碟形彈簧墊圈吸收，且有助於節點的耗散能量。所以，研究中提出的節點具有良好自重定性能和一定的耗能能力，該節點有利於增強抗彎鋼框架在地震荷載作用下的自復位能力。 本研究的主要目的是通過試驗和數值分析研究抗彎鋼框架中配置形狀記憶合金“保險絲”的自復位梁-梁新型節點的耗能跨在受迴圈荷載作用下的結構回應。本研究通過建立節點的數值模型，並對試驗結果進行驗證，以便運用該結果進行參數化分析。擬提出具有高效計算效率的節點簡化力學模型，並用於分析配置新型自重定耗能跨的抗彎鋼框架的地震回應。

15209619.label: Realisation of objectives
15209619.value: In general, all the objectives of the study have been achieved according to the planned research activities. A full-scale experimental investigation on the thermo-mechanical properties of shape memory alloy (SMA) plates and the hysteretic performance of beam-to-beam SMA self-centring fuse (SMA-SCF) connections was conducted. A series of nonlinear finite element (FE) analyses and a parametric study were performed. A practical design model for the proposed SMA-SCF connections was established and validated. The experimental programme consisted of 34 tests of the SMA plates and 10 tests of the beam-to-beam SMA self-centring fuse connections. For the SMA plate specimens, the effect of different geometries and varied loading protocols on the thermo-mechanical properties were primarily examined. The Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) method was used to determine the austenite start and finish temperatures and the martensite start and finish temperatures of the SMA plate materials. SMA plate coupons were fabricated to study the load deformation characteristics of the material under the cyclic tension-release loading protocol. In general, all the SMA plate specimens showed good superelasticity accompanied by moderate energy dissipation capability. The plates were tensioned to a maxiumn tensile strain of 4% under the first loading protocol and a residual strain varied from about 1% to 1.5% was observed. The corresponding equivalent viscous damping of the plate specimens increased with increasing number of loading cycles due to the development of a fuller hysteretic loop. Nevertheless, the SMA plates with large dimensions were found to exhibit less satisfactory superelasticity compared to that of the smaller SMA plates. The SMA coupons extracted from the edge areas of the SMA plates with large dimensions were susceptible to brittle fracture at low strain levels. It was also observed that the proposed training protocols could effectively reduce and stabilise the residual stain of the SMA plates, accompanied by decreased martensitic transformation stress, reduced energy dissipation and increased post-yielding stiffness. The hybrid self-centring beam-to-beam fuse connection (SMA-SCF) was proposed to connect the two beam segments at the flanges using the SMA plates and at the beam web endplates using SMA Belleville spring washers with high strength bolts. The SMA-SCF connection specimens developed the expected deformation mode of “V-gap” opening between the adjacent beams causing tension force on the SMA plates and compression force on the SMA Belleville spring washers. The inelastic deformation of the SMA-SCF connection was concentrated on the SMA components, and the other components such as the beams, endplate and column maintained an elastic state. During the loading cycles, the SMA plates in the SMA-SCF connection experienced tension-release action, and the SMA Belleville spring washers deformed in compression-release action. In general, all the ten SMA connection specimens exhibited good re-centring behaviour and energy dissipation capability. The strength and stiffness of the SMA-SCF connection could be adjusted by varying the dimension or the number of the SMA plates to suit practical engineering applications. However, the results also highlighted that the fabrication and installation quality could significantly influence the performance of the SMA-SCF connection. A slight separation between the adjacent beams would change the rotation centre of the SMA-SCF connection, leading to buckling of the SMA plates when there was no buckling-restraining mechanism. The buckling behaviour of the SMA plates compromised the stiffness, self-centring ability and energy dissipation capacity of the SMA-SCF connection. Therefore, buckling restraints were introduced to the connection, and the effectiveness was validated. Nonlinear finite element (FE) analyses of the coupon test specimens and the connection test specimens were conducted. A hybrid modelling technique, combining self-centring layers with energy-dissipation layers, was developed to capture the development of residual deformations in the SMA plates. In general, the FE predictions using the hybrid modelling technique agreed well with the test results of both the SMA plates and the SMA-SCF fuse connections. Utilising the validated hybrid modelling technique, a parametric study was conducted, examining the effect of the material properties of the SMA plates and the gap between the adjacent beams on the SMA-SCF connection. The results indicated that the material characteristics of the SMA plates obviously influenced the hysteresis of the SMA-SCF connection. Increasing residual deformation of the SMA plates would noticeably weaken the re-centring ability of the SMA-SCF connection, which had a limited impact on the nonlinear dynamic response of a structure equipped with SMA-SCF connections. Nonlinear spectral analyses of structures equipped with the SMA-SCF connections were also conducted based on a single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) system. The results showed that the variance of the strength reduction factor under different earthquakes was reduced owing to the enhanced post-yielding stiffness ratio of the trained SMA plates. However, the decrease in energy dissipation resulting from the training protocols could increase the seismic demand. Based on the test results and numerical studies results, a design model according to the component-based method for determining the yield moment capacity and the initial stiffness of the SMA-SCF fuse connection was developed. The model was able to produce good agreement to the connection test results and the corresponding finite element analysis results of the connection.

15209619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15209619.value: A total of 34 SMA plate specimens and 10 beam-to-beam SMA self-centring fuse connection specimens were tested. For the SMA plate specimens, it is observed that the SMA plates exhibited promising recentring behaviour while dissipating energy subjected to cyclic tension-release loadings. The geometric dimensions and training protocols had significant effects on the thermo-mechanical properties of the SMA plates. The small size SMA plates showed more favourable self-centring ability compared to those with a larger size. The SMA coupons extracted from the edge area of the large SMA plates exhibited brittle rupture at low strain levels. The training protocols could effectively reduce and stabilise the residual deformation of the SMA plates, accompanied by increasing post-yielding stiffness and decreasing energy dissipation. For the SMA connection specimens, the good self-centring behaviour, moderate energy dissipation capacity and ductility demonstrated the feasibility and applicability of the proof-of-concept connections. The supelastic deformation of the connection can be concentrated on SMA plates and the SMA Belleville spring washers through the expected deformation pattern. By increasing the dimension or the number of the SMA plates in the SMA-SCF connection, the strength and stiffness appropriate for practical engineering applications can be achieved. The hybrid modelling technique, combining self-centring layers with the energy-dissipation layer, can accurately capture the hysteretic performance of the SMA plates and SMA-SCF connections considering residual deformation development. The proposed design equations based on the component method can be utilised to determine the yield moment resistance and initial stiffness of the SMA-SCF connection. The research findings have resulted in three journal papers. Two journal papers were published in “Thin-Walled Structures” and the third one was published in “Journal of Constructional Steel Research”. In addition, two conference papers were also published.

15209619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15209619.value: Although this study has shed considerable light on the feasibility and design philosophy of SMA-SCF fuse connections, there are still several important unsolved issues. Firstly, considering that the maximum thickness of the SMA plates is 7 mm in this study, it may be beneficial to explore SMA plates with larger thicknesses, as they are more suitable for practical engineering applications. Secondly, conducting further tests to assess the influence of heat-treatment temperatures on the thermo-mechanical properties of SMA plates is recommended. SMAs are sensitive to temperature changes, and investigating heat-treatment details may further enhance the superelastic effect and lower the austenitic finish temperature, thereby expanding the working temperature. Thirdly, the proposed design model of the SMA-SCF connection only considered the yield moment resistance and initial stiffness, and could not capture the full hysteretic behaviour. A new design model including the post-yield stiffness can be further explored. Lastly, tt would be beneficial to conduct additional tests to consider the effect of preload of the HS bolts and the energy-dissipation capacities of SMA plates and SMA Belleville spring washers. The test data can be then used to develop and validate detailed design equations.

15209619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15209619.value: Conventional steel moment-resisting frames (MRFs) normally develop plastic hinges in each bay to dissipate seismic energy, which results in significant structural damage and unrecoverable residual deformations of the structureal members after a major earthquake. To enhance seismic resilience and mitigate post-earthquake damages, energy dissipation bays (EDBs) were introduced to MRFs, which aims to concentrate plastic deformations on EDBs and hence protect the main bays of MRFs. The incorporation of self-centring technologies into EDBs is expected to further minimise post-earthquake residual deformations and seismic losses. The study investigated the thermo-mechanical properties of shape memory alloy (SMA) plates and validated the seismic application of SMA plates experimentally and numerically. The test results indicate that the SMA plates have superelastic effect and energy dissipation capability in a large strain range. The proposed beam-to-beam self-centring connections with SMA plates also exhibited promising self-centring behaviour with moderate energy dissipation ability. An effective hybrid modelling technique, combining the self-centring layers and the energy-dissipation layer was developed in the numerical analyses. The predicted results of the numerical analyses agreed well with the test results. Preliminary design considerations of the beam-to-beam self-centring connection with SMA plates were also recommended, and the design predictions reasonably matched the test results

15209919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15209919.value: Optical fibre communication is already an important part of our everyday life and our economy. It not only provides the high speed internet connectivity through fixed broadband network such as fibre to the home systems(FTTH), but is also the enabler of broadband wireless systems such as current 4G and future 5G mobile communication systems. Since the amount of data carried by an optical fibre is huge, any disruption of the services will have a significant impact on our everyday life and the economy. Ability to provide sensing of disturbance to deployed fibre such as unauthorized digging will certainly be important to the reliable operation of the high capacity optical communication systems. In addition, since there is a large amount of deployed optical fibre in both terrestrial and submarine networks, if we can use these fibre to provide additional sensing services, many additional functions can be incorporated, these include temperature sensing for fire prevention, earthquake early warning and traffic monitoring and monitoring of transportation systems. When we use the sensing information provided by the massive amount of deployed fibre and process the information obtained using machine learning techniques, we may then have a very large intelligent sensing network. Although it is attractive, the integration of communication and sensing functions into a single fibre can be a challenging task and at the same time an interesting research problem. In the proposed project, we will investigate techniques that may enable the integration of communication and sensing systems. Key challenges will be identified and potential solutions will be investigated. In particular, we will investigate three possible approaches: using additional supervisory channel for distributed sensing while using digital coherent detection for event identification; using subcarriers in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) based optical communication systems for distributed sensing; Using multicore fibre for enhanced optical communication system performance while providing additional sensing functionalities. If carried out successfully, the proposed study shall certainly help to further advance the development of high capacity optical communication systems and networks and at the same time expand the functions of current optical communication networks. 光纤通信已经是我们是我们日常生活和经济活动的重要组成部分。它不仅通过光纤到户为我们提供宽带接入，也是实现4G，5G宽带无线系统的重要技术。由于在光纤系统里传输的数据量巨大，任何光纤服务的中断将对我们的日常生活及经济活动产生很大影响。因此对光纤系统的监测对光纤通信系统的正常运行将有重大的意义。同时由于在陆地及海洋中已布有大量的光纤，如果能用这些光纤提供传感服务，例如温度监测，地震预警，交通监测， 将给我们提供一个巨大的智能传感网络。 如何融合通信及传感功能在同一根光纤里是一个很有挑战性的研究问题。在本研究项目中，我们将研究光纤传感及通信系统的融合技术。我们将考虑如何利用光纤中的监测信道及光纤通信中的前向信号相干检测，以实现分布式震动传感， 如何利用多芯光纤实现通信及传感集成系统。此项目的成功完成不仅对未来光网络的正常运行有重大意义，也对扩大光网络的功能有很大的影响。

15210019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210019.value: Hearing Loss is a growing global health issue impacting both young and old alike. An estimated 360 million people around the world have some form of hearing loss. World Health Organization estimates that by 2050, 1 in 10 people will have disabling hearing deficiencies. The ratio increases to one third in those over the age of 65 years. Cochlear implantation surgery is the current standard of care to treat profound sensorineural hearing loss. A cochlear implant (CI) generally consists of an electrode array (EA) which is implanted into the inner ear (cochlea) bypassing the missing or defective sensory receptors by directly stimulating the auditory nerve and thereby, restoring hearing in deaf patients. This extremely delicate surgical procedure which involves high precision and complex navigation, but the absence of any feedback makes insertion of the CI challenging and depends entirely on human tactile perception. The quality of hearing restored to a deaf patient depends on accurate positioning of the EA while preserving the cochlear membranes. Furthermore, new bone formation occurred inside the cochlea as a result of electrode insertion trauma, which not only negatively impact the hearing performance but also make future explantation and re-implantation of CIs difficult. The typical lifetime of CIs is just over 20 years, so replacement of old implanted CI will be required several times over a young person's life. Furthermore, with current technology electrodes end up at an undesirable (traumatic) intracochlear location up to 50% of the time. Various techniques for reducing trauma during CI surgery were reported. These involve providing feedback to the surgeon or a robot during the implant procedure, so that the surgery can be modified accordingly. Examples include an automated CI insertion tool with integrated force sensors, or use of a fibre sensor embedded in a CI to measure tip force between the tip of the electrode array and inside wall of cochlea. The former technique does not measure contact force between the implant and the inside of cochlea, and the latter technique stiffened the CI rendering this approach unsuitable. In this project, we propose the application of low-bending loss, four-core fibres inscribed with fibre Bragg grating sensor arrays which can be integrated inside a CI's EA, to provide real-time measurements to aid surgeons to navigate EAs in cochlear implantation surgery, and minimise insertion trauma. Ultimately, such Smart Cochlear Implants could be used with automated insertion tools to pave the way towards robotic surgery. 聽力損失是一個日益嚴重的全球性健康問題，影響著年輕及老年的人群。 據估計，全世界有3.6億人患有某種程度的聽力損失。 據世界衛生組織估計，到2050年，十分之一的人存在聽力損失，該比例在65歲以上的人群中則增加到有三分之一。 人工耳蝸植入手術是目前治療嚴重感音神經性聽力損失的標準方案。耳蝸植入器（CI）通常由電極陣列（EA）組成，可植入內耳（耳蝸）中以繞過缺失或有缺陷的聽覺神經部位，進而通過直接刺激聽覺神經而恢復耳聾患者的聽力。 這種極其微型的外科手術涉及高精度和復雜定位，但卻沒有任何的反饋，使得耳蝸植入器的插入極具挑戰性，且處於人類觸覺所能感知的極限。 恢復耳聾患者聽力的質量取決於電極陣列的準確定位，同時不損傷耳蝸內膜。 此外，由於電極插入引起的創傷部位在耳蝸內部易形成新骨，這不僅會降低助聽的性能，而且使得將來耳蝸植入器的移植和再植入變得困難。通常，耳蝸植入器的使用期限僅為20多年，因此在一個年輕人的生命中可能需要多次更換舊的耳蝸植入器。此外，以當前的技術，在內耳植入的電極處於不理想的（創傷性）位置的概率仍可達50%。 在耳蝸植入器手術期間，在減少創傷方面已有多種技術報道，包括在植入過程中向外科醫生或機器人提供反饋，從而可以相應地調整手術操作。已有的案例包括集成有力傳感器的人工耳蝸自動插入工具，及在耳蝸植入器中嵌入光纖傳感器用於測量電極陣列尖端和耳蝸內壁之間的接觸力。 但是前一種技術並不測量植入器和耳蝸內部之間的接觸力，而後一種技術則增加了耳蝸植入器的硬度，從而也不適用。 在這個項目中，我們提出應用低彎曲損耗的四芯光纖，刻寫光纖布拉格光柵傳感器陣列，可以集成在耳蝸植入器內，提供實時的測量，幫助外科醫生在人工耳蝸植入手術中定位電極陣列 ，並盡量減少插入創傷。 最終，這種智能人工耳蝸植入器可以與自動插入器械集成，從而實現機器人手術。

15210119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210119.value: Recent advances of deep learning have improved the accuracy of video analytics to a level that becomes realistic to support a wide range of applications, e.g., self-driving cars, augmented reality, surveillance, etc. To support user experiences, video analytics requires a very short response time. In these applications, videos are generated in the edge; and there are debates on the topic of *edge-cloud video analytics*, i.e., whether video analytics should be executed in the edge or in the cloud, so that the delay requirement can be satisfied, and the video analytics accuracy is high. In this project, we study one important question in this debate: *how the network-induced delays affect the edge-cloud video analytics latency*. Existing research usually studies the network delays among a variety of objectives; and none of them investigates the *sources* of the network delays that can be experienced by an edge device in-depth. In this project, we aim to systematically answer *where* the network delays come from (by measurement and modeling), and *to what extent* we can manage the network delays (by proposing viable solutions) for edge-cloud video analytics. Our research methodology is to first study three fundamental sources of network-induced delays: 1) the nodal delay, 2) the transmission delay, and 3) the propagation delay; and then develop a video analytics framework that can manage various network delays and support diverse video analytics applications. More specifically, 1) we observe that the network interface card (NIC) of an edge device are often idle in video analytics applications. We propose an approach that can leverage the large idle computation resources of the NIC to video analytics acceleration; 2) network transmission delay (bandwidth) varies significantly. We model the computation of video analytics into fine-grained units of a stream of deep neural network (DNN) layers; and propose an approach to automatically partition the stream of DNN layers to adapt to bandwidth variation; 3) significant (propagation) delay occurs during the handoffs in mobile scenarios. We propose an application layer multi-path approach to leverage the asymmetric handoffs of different underlying paths to mask the propagation delay. The expected outcomes of this project include in-depth understanding of the impact of network-induced delays on the video analytics latency; and the implementation of a video analytics framework where it becomes an add-on module to existing platforms, e.g., TensorFlow, thus readily deployable to support a wide range of edge devices and video analytic applications. 深度學習的進展已將視頻分析的準確性提高到可以支持廣泛應用的水平，例如自動駕駛，增強現實，視頻監控等。為了支持用戶體驗，視頻分析需要極短的響應時間。在這些應用中，視頻在邊緣生成的；因此存在關於邊緣-雲視頻分析為主題的爭議，即視頻分析是應該在邊緣還是在雲中執行，以便可以滿足延遲要求，並提高視頻分析的準確性。 在這個項目中，我們研究這場辯論中的一個重要問題：網絡引發的延遲如何影響邊緣雲視頻分析延遲。在現有研究中網絡延遲只是優化各種目標之一；並且現有工作沒有深入研究網絡延遲的*來源*。在這個項目中，我們系統地回答網絡延遲來自哪裡（通過測量和建模），以及我們可以在多大程度上改善邊緣雲視頻分析的網絡延遲（通過提出可行的解決方案）。 我們的研究方法首先研究網絡誘導延遲的三個基本來源：1）節點延遲，2）傳輸延遲，以及3）傳播延遲；然後開發一個可以管理各種網絡延遲的視頻分析框架。具體來說，1）我們觀察到邊緣設備的網卡（NIC）在視頻分析應用中通常是空閑的。我們提出了一種可以利用空閑NIC的資源的計算的方法提供視頻分析加速; 2）網絡傳輸延遲（帶寬）變化很大。我們將視頻分析的深度神經網絡（DNN）分解成細粒度單元;並提出一種自動劃分DNN層流以適應帶寬變化的方法; 3）在移動場景中的切換會發生顯著的傳播延遲。我們提出了一種應用層多路徑方法，以利用不同底層路徑的非對稱切換來掩蓋傳播延遲。 該項目的預期成果包括深入了解網絡引發的延遲對視頻分析延遲的影響；以及視頻分析框架的設計，使它成為現有平臺如TensorFlow的附加模塊，以部署支持各種邊緣設備和視頻分析應用。

15210119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210119.value: With the emergence of artificial intelligence, video analytics (i.e., to extract useful events, such as vehicle counting, object detection, etc., from video streams) has shown great practical value. Video analytics applications have a time constraint to complete the video analytics tasks. This asks for research on an understanding of where the delays come from and how we can address the delay problem. This project provides understanding from the perspective of networking delays. This project specifically studies three typical types of networking delays, i.e., nodal delay, transmission delay, and propagation delay. We try to answer the questions, i.e., in what scenarios these delays will have impact on video analytics applications, and to what limit we can maximize the video analytics accuracy under these delays. We first did an analysis on the network traffic characteristics [4][5], we then presented a framework of networked video analytics [1], and finally we studied the impact of networking delays to the performance of video analytics [2][3][6][7]. We have graduated a Ph.D. student and several undergraduate students. Part of our research results have been adopted in industry, with one patent granted. SEC is a peer-reviewed first-tier conference on edge computing. • Five journal papers, IEEE Transactions on Computer, IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing, IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing, IEEE Network, IEEE Internet of Things Journal Education: • One Ph.D. graduated and one Ph.D. on-going • Three undergraduate students, two went on to their graduate studies, one in CMU, USA and one in CityU, Hong Kong Broader Impact: • The FPGA research stimulates industry adoption with a follow-up ITF project • One patent granted • One video demo

15210119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210119.value: There are many future works for video analytics acceleration. On the resource side, there are not only communication (networking) constraints, but also computation constraints. On the privacy side, video data from the edge are subject to privacy concerns, yet privacy removal/protection are also resource consuming; thus, it is again challenging to protect privacy while conducting video analytics. On the application side, there are killer applications such as High Definition (HD) Map, and how to effectively support such applications is an interesting research problem. We have successfully developed a new project, GRF, Federated Analytics for Real-time Environment Construction: Framework, Algorithm and Application in 2022 to study these research challenges.

15210119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210119.value: With the emergence of artificial intelligence, video analytics (i.e., to extract useful events, such as vehicle counting, object detection, etc., from video streams) has shown great practical value. Video analytics applications have a time constraint to complete the video analytics tasks. This asks for research on an understanding of where the delays come from and how we can address the delay problem. This project provides understanding from the perspective of networking delays. This project specifically studies three typical types of networking delays, i.e., nodal delay, transmission delay, and propagation delay. We try to answer the questions, i.e., in what scenarios these delays will have impact on video analytics applications, and to what limit we can maximize the video analytics accuracy under these delays. We first did an analysis on the network traffic characteristics, we then presented a framework of networked video analytics, and finally we studied the impact of networking delays to the performance of video analytics. We observe various opportunities where we can better utilize resources. As a result, we can substantially improve the accuracy given delay constraints.

15210219.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15210219.value: 豎向荷載對鋼筋混凝土樑柱節點的影響

15210219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210219.value: Beam-column joints (“BCJs”) are key structural members in reinforced concrete buildings. Under seismic action, failure of BCJs is prevented by joint shear reinforcements. Hong Kong has no seismic provisions and BCJs are provided with joint shear reinforcements following New Zealand’s approach that caters for strong seismicity. As Hong Kong is in a moderate seismic region, joint shear reinforcements are over-prescribed. This has caused construction difficulties due to over-congestion of reinforcements in BCJs, not to mention cost and time. Over the years, there are repeated complaints from the trade urging a comprehensive study on this matter. In Hong Kong, BCJs are used in low-rise buildings/structures and are gravity-load-dominated. With small-size heavily reinforced columns and long span beams, depth of beams is large than width of columns. This class of BCJs are uncommon in strong seismicity regions and neglected by international seismic codes. Based on recent studies by PI, seismic effect acting on gravity-load-dominated BCJs decreases with increasing gravity load. Their performance is still unclear, despite its importance in areas with moderate seismic risk like Hong Kong. In the proposed study, gravity-load-dominated BCJs commonly found in Hong Kong will be extensively studied to address the influence of gravity load on BCJs and to recommend rational design rules. Representable low-rise facilities and podium structures will be selected from our building stock. These structures will be analyzed to categorize and define one commonest class of gravity-load-dominated BCJs. Based on the above, 4 BJCs will be designed in accordance with local design code and 4 international seismic codes (Chinese code, American Code, New Zealand Code and European Code). A series of experiments will be conducted on 12 BCJs specimens with gravity load simulated through prestressing. Numerical analysis using non-linear strut-and-tie models will be implemented to predict the performance of BJCs. Finally, rational design rules for this class of BCJs will be recommended. The proposed study will assist the development on earthquake resistant design. It is the first time ever that experiments will be conducted on BCJ specimens with effect of gravity load truly incorporated into BCJs specimens. Combined with non-linear strut-and-tie models, we will have better understanding of the structural performance of gravity-load-dominated BCJs. Lastly, the rational design rules will be equally applicable internationally. 樑柱節點(“節點”)是鋼筋混凝土結構中的重要構件。節點應加上箍筋，以抵禦地震作用。現時香港沒有針對抗震的構造規定，節點中的箍筋配置參照新西蘭對抗強震的方案。然而香港是中震區，若按抗強震要求設計，會過度配置節點中的箍筋。這樣不僅增加了施工的難度，也增加工期和成本。故這些年來，業界不斷要求對此課題進行全面研究。 在香港，節點主要以豎向荷載為設計的標準. 並用於低層建築物。在柱子截面小，配筋量高及樑跨度大的情況下，樑的高度較柱子的寬度為大。這一類型的節點在強震區並不常見，也被國際抗震規範所忽略。根據本項目研究員的近期研究所得，地震作用對節點的影響，會因豎向荷載的增大而減小。在中震區如香港，儘管節點是很重要的構件，其結構性能，依然需要進一步了解。本項目將廣泛研究香港以豎向荷載為設計標準的節點，以了解豎向荷載對節點性能的影響，及提出合理的設計準則。 本項目會從香港現有建築物中，選擇具有代表性的低層建築物和平台結構進行分析及分類，希望找出一種最有代表性的節點。並以此為基礎，根據香港設計規範和四個國際抗震規範（中國規範，美國規範，新西蘭規範和歐洲規範）設計四種樑柱節點。研究將在十二個節點上，進行以預應力的方法模擬豎向荷載的實驗，並採用非線性拉壓桿模型，對模擬節點的性能進行分析。最後根據實驗及分析的結果，建議這一類型節點的設計準則。 是次研究將會首次對節點進行實驗，以分析豎向荷載對節點的影響，研究將有助抗震設計的發展。此外，透過結合非線性拉壓桿模型，可對受豎向荷載主導的節點有更深入的了解。最後，本項目建議的設計準則，對國際抗震規範也同樣適用。

15210319.value: 基於二維/三維複合鈣鈦礦的高性能柔性太陽能電池的製備

15210319.label: Project Objectives
15210319.value: To prepare high-efficiency and stable flexible perovskite solar cells based on 2D/3D perovskite composites. To realize flexible perovskite solar cells with high bending durability and efficiency using novel flexible transparent electrodes. To investigate the mechanical flexibility of 2D perovskites and 2D/3D perovskite composites and make clear the underline mechanism.

To realize flexible perovskite solar cells with high bending durability and efficiency using novel flexible transparent electrodes.
To investigate the mechanical flexibility of 2D perovskites and 2D/3D perovskite composites and make clear the underline mechanism.

15210319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210319.value: 鈣鈦礦太陽能電池作為代表性的新一代光伏技術，因其高能量轉換效率，低成本和便利的器件製造而備受矚目。由於鈣鈦礦薄膜的溶液加工性，柔性鈣鈦礦太陽能電池（FPSC）可以在塑料薄膜上通過捲對卷溶液工藝製造，預計這種薄膜比剛性基板上的傳統太陽能電池便宜得多。更重要的是，FPSC將在許多新興領域具有廣闊的應用前景，包括便攜式和輕型光伏系統，可穿戴電子設備，建築一體化光伏發電等。然而，由於一些困難，獲得高性能FPSC是具有挑戰性的。具體地讲，常規的有機 - 無機金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦易碎且在空氣中不穩定。在柔性器件中，機械應變在沿鈣鈦礦晶界容易引起裂紋，導致光伏性能嚴重下降。因此，應為FPSC開發本徵上柔韌且穩定的鈣鈦礦材料。 我們的初步工作清楚地表明，二維/三維（2D / 3D）複合鈣鈦礦本徵上是柔性的。根據我們在透射電子顯微鏡下的觀察，2D鈣鈦礦可以有效地釋放鈣鈦礦薄膜中的應變，因為它們具有低楊氏模量和獨特的2D晶體結構。具有功能性有機陽離子的2D組分也可以改善鈣鈦礦膜的空氣穩定性。因此，我們計劃在柔性太陽能電池中使用2D / 3D複合鈣鈦礦來克服傳統3D鈣鈦礦的缺點。將進行2D / 3D鈣鈦礦的組成工程以進一步改善器件的彎曲耐久性，效率和空氣穩定性。此外，我們將使用高摻雜石墨烯和導電聚合物薄膜作為器件中的柔性透明電極。基於這些新方法，預計將在該項目中實現高性能的FPSC。 該研究的成功將帶來以下成果：（i）用於製造具有本徵柔性鈣鈦礦材料的高性能FPSC的最先進技術。 （ii）對2D / 3D鈣鈦礦的獨特機械和光電性質的深入了解。 （iii）通過使用石墨烯和導電聚合物電極來改善FPSC的彎曲穩定性的有效方法。 （iv）該研究將為FPSC的大規模生產鋪平道路。這是一項涉及材料科學，綠色能源技術，電子工程，物理和化學的多學科研究項目，將為培訓香港學生和研究人員提供許多機會。

15210319.label: Realisation of objectives
15210319.value: 1. To prepare high-efficiency and stable flexible perovskite solar cells based on 2D/3D perovskite composites. A 2-dimensional (2D) perovskite (PEA2PbI4) with low Young’s modulus has been introduced at the boundaries of 3-dimensional perovskite (Cs0.05(FA0.95MA0.05)0.95Pb(I0.95Br0.05)3) grains as a lubricant to release internal stress, which is revealed under in-situ transmission electron microscopy (TEM), leading to enhanced mechanical flexibility of perovskite films. With the addition of 0.5 mol% PEA2PbI4, the device power conversion efficiency (PCE) can be significantly improved from 19.58% to 22.90%, with Voc increased from 1.03 to 1.16 V, Jsc from 24.45 to 24.50 mA/cm2, and FF from 77.75 to 80.58%. 2. To realize flexible perovskite solar cells with high bending durability and efficiency using novel flexible transparent electrodes. PEDOT:PSS is a conductive material popularly used in flexible electronics due to its intrinsically flexible and conductive nature. However, normal PEDOT:PSS cannot meet the requirement of high conductivity for transparent electrodes in f-PSCs. To improve its conductivity, PEDOT:PSS (PH1000) was doped by D-sorbitol with different amounts. Notably, the addition of D-sorbitol leads to negligible change on the transparency of PEDOT:PSS film, which is higher than 90% in the visible region. The sheet resistance of PEDOT:PSS films based on different doping amounts of D-sorbitol was characterized. The sheet resistance of PEDOT:PSS film can be significantly decreased from about 1200 to 50 Ω sq-1 when the addition concentration of D-sorbitol is increased to 50 mg/mL. The improved conductivity is due to the phase segregation between PSSH and PEDOT chains after the addition of D-sorbitol. Then, the PEDOT:PSS thin films were spin coated on the PDMS substrates to measure their electrical stability during stretching processes. The PEDOT:PSS films can sustain higher strain at higher D-sorbitol concentrations. PEDOT:PSS films with additions of 50 or 70mg/mL of D-sorbitol can maintain their high conductivity at a strain up to 40%. PEDOT:PSS thin films have been observed under optical microscopy with 0 % and 40% strain. Many cracks appeared in the pristine PEDOT:PSS thin film under 40% tensile strain. In comparison, several wrinkles, instead of cracks, can be observed in the film with D-sorbitol under the same tensile strain. The increased mechanical stretchability is attributed to the plasticization of D-sorbitol to PEDOT:PSS where D-sorbitol can form hydrogen bonds with PSSH and thus breaking the hydrogen bond interactions among the PSSH chains of PEDOT:PSS. Then, PEDOT:PSS thin films doped with D-sorbitol were used as the bottom electrodes in f-PSCs. The device based on pristine PEDOT:PSS and MAPbI3 perovskite can only achieve a low PCE of 11.23% with a Voc of 1.04 V, a Jsc of 19.46 mA/cm2, and an FF of 55.49%. With the addition of 50 mg/mL D-sorbitol in PEDOT:PSS, the device PCE can be significantly increased to 20.07% with a Voc of 1.13V, a Jsc of 23.24 mA/cm2 and an FF of 76.42%. To further improve the device performance, mixed perovskites Cs0.05(FA0.95MA0.05)0.95Pb(I0.95Br0.05)3 have been introduced in the f-PSCs. The PCE of the f-PSC was increased from 12.67% to 22.43% after the addition of 50 mg/mL D-sorbitol in the PEDOT:PSS electrode. The optimized device shows a Voc of 1.16 V, a Jsc of 23.99 mA/cm2 and an FF of 80.6 %. Finally, an ultrathin PET substrate with a thickness of 1.4 µm was employed to shift the neutral plane close to the perovskite film which further improves the bending durability of the device. Consequently, an ultrathin f-PSC was successfully fabricated with a power conversion efficiency of 21.44% and a record power-per-weight value of 47.8 W/g. The bending stability is also measured under a bending radius of 0.5 mm. The ultrathin f-PSC can keep the initial PCE after 1000 bending cycles. 3. To investigate the mechanical flexibility of 2D perovskites and 2D/3D perovskite composites and make clear the underline mechanism. The distribution of 2D perovskite in the MAPbI3 films can be observed under a transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of grain boundaries of PEA2PbI4 -added MAPbI3 film shows that the lattice structures in grains and grain boundaries are obviously different, suggesting the different kinds of perovskite phases in the two regions. Selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern was characterized on grain and grain boundary regions to find the corresponding lattice structures. The diffraction spot in grain region can be referred to (220) plane of MAPbI3 due to the matched interplane distance of 0.31 nm, while the diffraction spot in grain boundary region can be indexed as (002) plane of PEA2PbI4 with the interplane spacing of 0.75 nm, demonstrating that the material at the grain boundary is 2D perovskite PEA2PbI4. The TEM images of the MAPbI3 perovskite films demonstrate that 2D perovskite mainly locates at the grain boundaries of 3D perovskite. It is expected that the 2D phase between perovskite grains can release strain by the reversible sliding and rotation between neighboring layers. For the pristine MAPbI3 film, it can be observed that there are some holes or amorphous structure at the grain boundaries, which is unfavorable for device performance. Hence, the 2D perovskite can fill the holes and replace the amorphous phase at grain boundaries of 3D perovskites. To investigate how a 2D perovskites can release strain at grain boundaries, in-situ strain was applied on a perovskite film via tearing the underlying carbon film with electron beam under TEM. This method is usually used to study the lattice change of nanomaterials under strain. It can be found that cracks are formed along the grain boundaries, which suggests that strain in the perovskite film tends to be released by forming cracks along the grain boundaries. Since the crack tip is the stress concentrating area, HRTEM observation is conducted on this area. The raw and filtered HRTEM image of a local area close to the crack tip shows deformed 2D crystal lattice close to the crack tip. The geometric phase analysis (GPA) displayed the factor that the elastic modulus (shear modulus e12 and normal modulus e33) of the 2D perovskite is much smaller than 3D perovskite. Notably, the weak van der Waals (vdW) interactions between 2D perovskite layers can allow lattice deformation and even slippage on the 2D plane. The strain-concentrated zones can reach a local ultrahigh shear strain level of about 10%, indicating a high flexibility of the 2D perovskite phase. Therefore, the flexible 2D perovskite located at the grain boundaries provides abundant pathways for strain release in the 2D/3D mixed perovskites.

15210319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15210319.value: 1. High-performance PSCs with a maximum PCE of 21.47% and high stability by employing a controllable amorphous 5-SSA/PbI2 passivation layer in MAPbI3 films. The technology has been also successfully used in flexible PSCs that exhibit high efficiencies over 21%. (J. Mater. Chem. A, 2021, 9, 21708–21715) 2. Graded vertical heterojunctions are constructed in the perovskite films with a compositional gradient, which can enhance photocarrier separation and suppress carrier recombination in the resultant PSCs. Under optimal fabrication conditions, the Sn–Pb mixed PSCs show power conversion efficiency up to 22% along with excellent stability during light soaking. (Adv. Mater. 2022, 34, 2107729) 3. We introduce a small amount of KBF4 as an additive to elevate the quality of triple-cation mixed perovskite thin films. Under optimum fabrication conditions, triple-cation mixed perovskite solar cells with an inverted structure show power conversion efficiency over 23% as well as excellent stability under different conditions. (Adv. Funct. Mater. 2022, 32, 2204880) 4. The ultrasmooth surface of the Cu3(HHTT)2 film can facilitate perovskite growth and enable defect passivation on the perovskite surface. The selfassembly approach is suitable for preparing large-area films conformally on a substrate, promising the application of the film in large-area devices. Encouragingly, an efficiency over 22% is obtained from ideal-bandgap PSCs. (ACS Energy Lett. 2022, 7, 3362−3369) 5. A high-performance flexible PD is presented by gating an organic electrochemical transistor (OECT) with a flexible perovskite solar cell. Due to the ultrahigh transconductance of the OECT, the device demonstrates a high gain of ≈10^6, a fast response time of 67 μs and an ultrahigh detectivity of 6.7 × 10^17 Jones to light signals under a low working voltage (Adv. Mater. 2023, 35, 2207763) 6. 2D WS2 flakes with defect-free surfaces are introduced as a template for van der Waals epitaxial growth of mixed perovskite films for the first time and the devices show improved PCEs up to 21.1%. (Adv. Funct. Mater. 2020, 30, 2002358) 7. An ultrathin f-PSC with a thickness of 1.4 µm was successfully fabricated with a power conversion efficiency of 21.44% and a record power-per-weight value of 47.8 W/g. A stretchable device was realized by laminating the ultrathin f-PSC on a pre-strained substrate, which shows stable performance when it is stretched for up to 40%. In addition, the stretchable PSC shows a high efficiency of 36.25% under room light intensity. (To be submitted)

15210319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15210319.value: Excellent mechanical flexibility and robustness have been achieved. The ultrathin devices show a record power-per-weight value. A stretchable PSC with the stretching ratio of up to 40% has been realized. Moreover, the stretchable PSC demonstrates excellent indoor photovoltaic performance under room light intensity. The high-performance, lightweight, stretchable, and ultrathin f-PSCs are expected to find many niche applications, such as wearable electronics, internet of things and building integrated photovoltaics, in the future. For the further development of the research, we will focus on large-area fabrication of the devices, the device encapsulation and the integration of the devices with different systems like wearable devices, sensors and printable fabrication approaches for practical applications. To further improve the device performance, novel 2D perovskites with different organic ligands will be developed to improve carrier transport and optimize perovskite morphology in the 2D/3D perovskite composites.

15210319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15210319.value: In summary, ultrathin and low-coast flexible perovskite solar cells (PSCs) with high mechanical flexibility and power conversion efficiencies have been fabricated with three strategies for material and device optimization. First, the introduction of a 2D perovskite in 3D perovskite phases can significantly improve the mechanical flexibility and carrier lifetime of the perovskite active layer. Second, intrinsically flexible PEDOT:PSS film shows dramatically improved flexibility and conductivity after the addition of D-sorbitol, which acts as the transparent electrode of the device. Third, ultrathin PET substrate is used in the devices to shift the neutral plane within or close to perovskite film, further improving the mechanical robustness of the device. The ultrathin flexible PSCs have achieved a high efficiency over 21% and a record power-per-weight of 47.8 Wg-1 for f-PSCs. A stretchable device based on the ultrathin flexible PSC shows excellent device stability under tensile strain for up to 40%. In addition, the device can achieve a high PCE of 36.25% under 1000 lux light, showing a great potential in indoor photovoltaic applications. It is expected that the ultra-flexible PSCs will find niche applications in wearable electronics, internet of things (IOT) and building integrated photovoltaics.

15210919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15210919.value: Automatically generating a well-organized answer summary in response to a user question has wide applications. It is an important yet not fully solved problem. This proposal is targeted at research problems in question-focused summarization. While the traditional approaches mainly focus on sentence ranking and extraction, we believe the next technological breakthrough is to equip a summarization machine with the necessary language understanding and generation abilities. Only in this way can it be expected to create a truly concise and coherent summary like a human. To this end, we explore neural network techniques in consideration of their demonstrated initial successes and recognized future potentials in machine reading comprehension and generation. Current state-of-the-art neural summarization models are sequence-to-sequence models based on the encoder-decoder architecture. They are, however, inadequate to question-focused summarization. First of all, since an answer summary must be generated with reference to question and relevant documents, understanding interactions among question and documents is critical. This requires complicate interactive text modeling and even gradual adjustment. More importantly, when the answer information to be summarized is dispersed in multiple documents, the sequence-to-sequence summarization models, which work well at the sentence level, are entirely incapable. It is desirable to endow a summarization model with the information fusion mechanism. Fusing information is more challenging than paraphrasing information. It depends on the effective organization of the available information. To address the above-mentioned problems, we focus on the following research issues. To achieve a thorough understanding of the text, we explore the mutual dependence of question and answer to ensure they are derivable from each other. We design the iterative and collaborate reasoning process to step-by-step locate and update answer span regions. To facilitate fusion-based summary generation, we innovatively propose to build an answer graph to connect the related information and to develop graph-to-sequence models to fuse the structurally organized information into a sequence of coherent summary sentences. Due to its complexity, we explore multi-pass refined writing strategies using the answer graph as guidance. In short, we argue that question-focused summarization cannot be achieved by a single model. It demands a more capable and strategic reinforced document/question reading, answer reasoning and summary writing process. The research problems we attempt to tackle in this proposal are not only crucial to the success of neural network based question-focused summarization machines. They are also fundamental to the development of advanced language understanding and generation technologies. 自動生成組織良好的答案摘要以響應用戶問題是一個重要但尚未完全解決的問題，且具有廣泛的應用價值。傳統方法主要關注句子排序和抽取，但我們認為下一個技術突破是為摘要系統配備必要的語言理解和生成能力。只有這樣才能期望機器能夠像人一樣“書寫”出真正簡潔和連貫的摘要內容。為此，該研究課題將重點探索神經網絡技術，考慮到它們在機器閱讀理解和生成方面所展示的初步成功和公認的未來潛力。 當前最先進的神經概括模型是基於編碼器-解碼器架構的序列到序列模型。然而，它們不足以生成以問題為中心的摘要。首先，由於必須參考問題和相關文檔生成答案摘要，因此理解問題和文檔之間的相互作用至關重要。這需要復雜的交互式文本建模甚至逐步調整。更重要的是，當要匯總的答案信息分散在多個文檔中時，在句子級別上運行序列到序列模型完全無法實現。我們期望賦予摘要模型信息融合機制。融合信息比解釋信息更具挑戰性，這取決於可用信息的有效組織。 為解決上述問題，我們關注以下研究問題。為了更深刻理解文本內容，我們探索問與答的相互依賴，以確保它們是相互衍生的。我們設計迭代和協作推理過程，逐步定位和更新答案範圍區域。為了促進基於融合的摘要生成，我們建議首先構建一個答案圖，以連接相關信息並開發圖形到序列模型，以將結構組織的信息融合成一系列連貫的摘要句子。由於其複雜性，我們使用答案圖作為指導探索多遍精煉寫作策略。簡而言之，我們認為單一模型無法實現以問題為中心的摘要生成，它需要一個更有能力和戰略性的強化文檔/問題閱讀、回答推理和總結寫作過程。 該研究課題解決的研究問題不僅對基於神經網絡以問題為中心的摘要系統的成功至關重要，它們也為更先進的語言理解和生成技術的發展奠定了相關基礎。

15211219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211219.value: Humans have the ability to make complex assessments of different clothing types from a fashion photo, including the aesthetic and design details, by simply looking briefly at the image. Such information provides many clues about the clothing preferences of the subject. Finding similar fashion-product images for a given image query is a classical problem in computer vision. However, the problem itself is still challenging due to the absence of a well-accepted definition of similarity among arbitrary fashion products. Over the past half-decade, deep learning technology has realised great success in many computer vision tasks, such as efficient feature representation, classification, and segmentation. However, the focus of the computer vision community in tasks such as object recognition and feature learning may be different from humans’ perceptions and assessments. Moreover, computer vision algorithms only work in similar product retrieval. Fashion product recommendations are not only for similar items, but also for mix-and-match coordination. In this project, we will develop a computer software system with a similar ability as humans for clothing recognition/assessment. Building on the previous work in the area of somatotype recognition from still images, we propose in this project to recognise clothing types, as well as fine-grained attributes using cutting-edge deep learning technology, taking into account domain specific knowledge in the fashion industry. With the known clothing preferences and the users’ own body-shape characteristics, we will formulate personalised fashion recommendations for individual users, including figure-flattering styles and effective mix-and-match fashion coordination. 人類能透過單單地看一幅時尚圖像，就從照片中對不同的服裝類型進行評估，包括美觀性和設計細節等等。這些信息提供了關於穿衣者服裝偏好的不少線索。 通過特定圖像進行查詢相似的時尚產品，是計算機視覺中的常見問題。由於缺乏時尚產品之間相似性的廣泛定義，問題本身具有相當的挑戰性。在過去的五年中，深度學習技術在許多計算機視覺領域中取得了巨大成功，例如高效的特徵展示，分類和分割。然而，在如對象識別和特徵學習等任務計算機視覺與人類的感知和評估有不同的焦點。另外，至今為止計算機視覺算法僅適用於類似的產品檢索；其實時尚產品推薦不僅適用於類似產品，也包含搭配款式的推薦。 在這個項目中，我們將開發一個具有與人類相似能力的計算機軟件系統，用於服裝識別/評估。基於靜態圖像識別和體型識別的前期工作，我們在此項目中使用創新的深度學習技術識別服裝類型以及細微屬性，同時考慮到時尚行業中的領域特定知識。憑藉已知的服裝偏好和用戶自身的體形特徵，我們將為用戶制定個性化的時尚推薦，包括塑造風格和有效的款式搭配的推薦。

15211219.label: Realisation of objectives
15211219.value: This project encompasses five research objectives, which include reviewing recent advancements in deep network models for image vision, developing a fashion classification system, developing clothing parsing and segmentation models, analyzing image features, and learning/establishing mix-and-match association rules for personalized fashion recommendation. These objectives have been successfully achieved through: - Completion of a comprehensive review of fashion recommendation systems. - Development of a robust fashion classification system. - Creation of new deep-learning models for human and clothing parsing, as well as personalized 3D human avatar generation. - Analysis and utilization of image facial and texture features for tasks such as repeated pattern extraction and face reconstruction. - Innovation in fashion clothing recommendation by integrating cross-media information. 9 journal publications/submissions have been generated from this project, most of these are published except one. In addition, 5 conference publications are generated from this research. One PhD student is trained.
