15211219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211219.value: This project research on machine learning and deep learning methods for personalized fashion recommendations based on heterogeneous information mining. In relation to research objective 1, the recent research works on fashion recommendation have been reviewed comprehensively from technology perspective, resulting in a survey journal publication (corresponding to Part C, item 3 of section 8). In relation to research objectives 2 and 3 on heterogeneous information extraction from images, two new deep learning-based methods were developed for human and clothing parsing and a fashion classification system was developed to automatically detect and recognize clothing category and attributes from fashion images. There are also new findings to address current issue in 2D pose estimation, which mining useful information from human fashion photos. This results in 3 journal publications (corresponding to Part C, items 1-2 and 9 of section 8). In relation to research objectives 4 and 5 on image feature analysis and heterogeneous information mining for personalized fashion recommendation, new methods and applications were also developed. For example, a new method based on deep learning is developed for automatic extraction of repeat patterns. The results are reported in journal submission and conference publication (corresponding to Part C, item 8 of section 8 and item 2 of section 9). Additionally, two new realistic 3D facial reconstruction methods were developed for personalizing human avatars. Furthermore, a fashion clothing recommendation method was developed using cross-media information, which includes automatic extraction of textual and image features of products through human parsing and fashion classification models. From a large number of full-body fashion images, mix-and-match rules were also mined for recommendation. These results are reported in journal publications (items 4-7 of section 8 in part C) as well as conference publications (items 1, 3-5 of section 9 of part C).

15211219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211219.value: These proposed methods have advanced the technology in image processing and personalized recommendation, which have a wide range of applications in various domains including fashion. The proposed development has vast potential for commercial applications, in particularly in mobile shopping. With the developed personalized fashion recommendation, consumers can discover trendy fashion items tailored to their individual preferences. This system also facilitates up-selling and cross-selling by suggesting complementary items once a selection is made. Moreover, it offers brands and retailers a valuable tool to capitalize on the expanding m-commerce market and enhance customer service. Additionally, our research has led to new applications for personalizing human avatars, enhancing convenience, confidence, and satisfaction for online shoppers across web and mobile platforms.

15211219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211219.value: Despite achieving significant success in various computer vision tasks, deep learning technology still faces challenges in understanding fashion images and developing accurate fashion recommendation systems due to the lack of domain specific knowledge in the fashion industry. This project investigates the related technology of human/clothing parsing, clothing recognition and 3D image reconstruction, supporting the human and clothing information extraction from fashion images for personalized recommendations. Based on the analysis of mined information, this project formulates personalised fashion recommendations for individual users, including figure-flattering styles and effective mix-and-match fashion coordination. The research findings in this project can be applied in e-commerce sector, enabling brands and retailers to capitalize on the growing m-commerce market and enhancing the convenience, confidence, and satisfaction of online shoppers.

15211619.label: Project Objectives
15211619.value: OPM is vital for optical network management to achieve fault diagnosis and location. Among various OPM parameters, OSNR is the key indicator for quality of signal. Therefore, we will propose and experimentally demonstrate the OSNR monitoring method based on delay tap plot, which is obtained after a low-bandwidth cost-effective receiver. Neural network is a powerful tool to achieve complex mapping from input to output. The OSNR information hidden in the delay tap plot is hard to extract through traditional signal analysis. In the previous research work, we proposed the method to extract the OSNR through the mean and variance at diagonal of delay tap plot, which is affected by the number of sampling point, the bandwidth of receiver and so on. Therefore, we will combine neural network and delay tap plot to achieve automatic OSNR extraction to improve the robustness of the OSNR monitoring system. In the dynamic optical communication system, the modulation format, bit rate and optical power of signal are adjustable to meet the demands of transmission. At receiver end, the information of signal modulation format can help to adopt appropriate algorithm for incoming signal. Therefore, we will explore the neural network trained by delay tap plot to achieve modulation format recognition. Other optical signal impairments, such as CD, PMD and nonlinear noise are also important for optical performance monitoring, since the corresponding compensation is operated at receiver end but not at the intermediate nodes in general. We will explore the features of delay tap plot to achieve the multiple impairments monitoring. The performance of OPM will also be affected by the parameters of neural networks, such as the type of neural network (deep neural network or convolution neural network), the structure of neural network (number of hidden layers, the number of neurons in each layer), the type of activation function and so on. Therefore, we will investigate and optimize the parameters of neural networks to improve the performance and robustness of monitoring system. The features of delay tap plot are decided by the delay time between two branches, modulation format, bit rate and the bandwidth of receiver. We will also investigate the effects of these parameters on the accuracy of OPM.

The performance of OPM will also be affected by the parameters of neural networks, such as the type of neural network (deep neural network or convolution neural network), the structure of neural network (number of hidden layers, the number of neurons in each layer), the type of activation function and so on. Therefore, we will investigate and optimize the parameters of neural networks to improve the performance and robustness of monitoring system.

The features of delay tap plot are decided by the delay time between two branches, modulation format, bit rate and the bandwidth of receiver. We will also investigate the effects of these parameters on the accuracy of OPM.

15211619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15211619.value: With the development of cloud computing, multimedia communication and intelligent devices, the network traffic grows at an exponential rate in recent decades. To achieve intelligent management of high-capacity complex optical networks, optical performance monitoring (OPM) is critical at the nodes of network to obtain the information of signal quality. The heterogeneous optical networks impose new requirements on OPM modules: 1. The massive demand requires cost-effective OPM devices; 2. The various transmission signals in optical networks require OPM should be compatible with different modulation formats and different bit rates; 3. OPM must monitor multiple parameters, such as optical signal to noise ratio (OSNR), chromatic dispersion (CD), polarization mode dispersion (PMD) and nonlinear noise at the intermediate nodes of networks. OSNR is the key parameter for monitoring, since channel power relative to the Erbium-doped-fiber-amplifier (EDFA) generated amplified-spontaneous-emission (ASE) noise must be maintained at a fairly high level throughout the transmission link to ensure error-free data recovery. Any simple change can dramatically impact the OSNR, and these changes include: laser power decrease, connector degradation, mux/demux wavelength drift, and EDFA pump power decrease. Monitors can help to isolate and diagnose such problems. Thus, the main purpose of OPM is measuring OSNR with relatively high accuracy under various distortions. OSNR monitoring has attracted much attention from both academia and industry. The method based on delay tap sampling is cost effective and the components of setup are commercially available. However, the mapping relation between the OSNR and delay tap sampling is hard to quantify through traditional signal analysis. Fortunately, machine learning such as the neural network technique provides a powerful tool to achieve complex mapping between inputs and outputs. Therefore, the method combining neural network and delay tap sampling is promising to achieve OSNR monitoring with low cost and high accuracy. In this project, we propose jointly employ the neural networks and delay tap plots with cost-effective low-bandwidth receiver to achieve multi-parameter monitoring. we will employ the neural network technique on the delay tap plot to measure OSNR. The information of modulation format, bit rate, CD and PMD can also be extracted at the same time. We will study the details of our proposed techniques by both simulations and experiments. The research has both academic impacts and practical applications. 隨著雲計算、多媒體通信和智能設備的發展，近幾十年來網絡流量以指數速度增長。為了實現大容量複雜光網絡的智能管理，光性能監測（OPM）在網絡節點獲取信號質量信息至關重要。異構光網絡對OPM模塊提出了新的要求：具有成本效益的OPM設備; 光網絡中的各種傳輸信號要求OPM應兼容不同的調製格式和不同的比特率; OPM必須監測多個參數，例如光信噪比（OSNR），色散（CD），偏振模色散（PMD）和網絡中間節點的非線性噪聲。 OSNR是監測的關鍵參數，因為相對於摻鉺光纖放大器（EDFA）產生的放大自發輻射射（ASE）噪聲，信道功率必須在整個傳輸鏈路中保持在相當高的水平，以確保數據恢復。任何簡單的更改都會對OSNR產生巨大影響，這些變化包括：激光功率降低，連接器性能下降，復用器/解復用器波長漂移，以及EDFA泵功率降低。光性能監測器可以幫助隔離和診斷此類問題。因此，OPM的主要目的是在各種失真下，以相對高的精度測量OSNR。 OSNR監測已引起學術界和工業界的廣泛關注。基於延遲抽頭採樣的方法的優點是使用商用器件、成本較低。然而，OSNR和延遲抽頭採樣之間的映射關係很難通過傳統的信號分析來量化。幸運的是，諸如神經網絡技術的機器學習提供了一種強大的工具來實現輸入和輸出之間的複雜映射。因此，結合神經網絡和延遲抽頭採樣的方法有望實現低成本，高精度的OSNR監測。 在這個項目中，我們將使用經濟有效的低帶寬接收器實現多參數監測。我們將在接收到的延遲抽頭圖上採用神經網絡技術來測量OSNR。調製格式、比特率、CD和PMD等信息也可同時提取。我們將通過模擬和實驗研究我們提出的技術細節。該研究兼具理論意義和實際應用價值。

15211619.label: Realisation of objectives
15211619.value: We have successfully achieved the goals of this project, and both the experiment and simulation works have been conducted to obtain significant results and achieve the corresponding objectives. The project until now is completed in accordance with the schedule and arrangements, and we believe that the completion of this project can promote advancements in the optical performance monitoring (OPM) method, especially for achieving intelligent management of high-capacity complex optical networks. For objectives 1 and 2, we start conceptually with the idea of building the OSNR-dependent delay tap plot based on the difference of time domain waveform between signal and ASE noise. To save one sampler cost and simplify the monitoring system, we obtain the delay tap plot by single channel sampling in place of two channel sampling. After obtaining the OSNR-dependent delay tap plot, we need to extract the OSNR information which is hard to extract through artificial analysis. The neural network is a powerful tool to achieve complex mapping between input and output. Therefore, we employ a neural network to achieve the mapping between the delay tap plot and OSNR. The neural network contains deep neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and convolutional neural networks. In this proposal, we employ the feedforward neural network to realize the mapping. In feedforward neural networks, convolutional neural networks and artificial neural networks are promising to deal with the problem. For the method based on convolutional neural networks, we build a delay tap plot image library with different OSNR values for training the convolutional neural network, which can avoid the complex preprocessing of images and achieve automatic feature extraction. Through convolution layers and pooling layers, the convolutional neural network can achieve automatic extraction of image features. Then through fully connected layers, the convolutional neural network can realize the different OSNR classifications. Besides, considering the difficulty of training a completely new neural network, transfer learning will also be investigated in this proposal. To investigate the performance of the proposed OSNR monitoring method, we carry out the experimental consists of an arbitrary waveform generator (AWG) to generate optical signals with different modulation formats and baud rates, an erbium-doped fiber amplifier (EDFA) to introduce amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) noise, variable optical attenuators (VOAs) to adjust the OSNR, and different lengths of fibers (0, 50.5, and 88.7 km) to introduce chromatic dispersion. The received optical signals are then converted to electrical signals using a photodetector (PD) and sampled by a digital signal analyzer (DSA) to generate AADTPs and AAHs for the neural network. We set up a neural network to realize the complex mapping from DTP to OSNR, aiming to improve the robustness of OSNR monitoring. Compared to traditional OSNR extraction methods based on the mean and variance of the DTP diagonal, using a neural network enables automatic extraction of all OSNR-related statistical features hidden in the DTP, making it more robust against factors such as the number of sampling points and receiver bandwidth. Experimental results show that the method achieves excellent performance with strong robustness, having a mean absolute error of only 0.2867 dB for OSNR estimation under various conditions, including two modulation formats (QPSK and 16QAM), two baud rates (14 Gbaud and 28 Gbaud), three dispersion values (0, 858.5, and 1507.9 ps/nm), and an OSNR range of 10-29 dB. For objectives 3 and 4, we try to realize modulation format recognition and multiple impairments monitoring in intermediate nodes of optical networks. The generation of AADTP only depends on the sampling rate without requiring prior knowledge of the symbol rate. Inputting both AADTP and AAH into the multi-task learning neural network can extract more features compared to a single input, thereby improving the recognition and monitoring performance. The designed neural network consists of three parts: The first part is used to extract features from AADTP, including four convolutional layers, four max-pooling layers, and one flatten layer; the second part extracts features from AAH, containing only one fully connected layer; the third part consists of four parallel task outputs, namely modulation format identification (MFI), baud rate identification (BRI), chromatic dispersion identification (CDI), and OSNR estimation. Each task includes three hidden fully connected layers and one output layer. The first three tasks are classification problems using the cross-entropy loss function, while OSNR estimation is a regression problem using the mean absolute error loss function. The loss function of the entire network is a weighted sum of the loss functions of the four tasks, achieving multi-task learning through this approach. To investigate the performance of the proposed multi-task learning neural network, we carried out experiments using optical signals with two modulation formats (QPSK and 16QAM), two baud rates (14Gbaud and 28Gbaud), three dispersion values (0ps/nm, 858.5ps/nm, 1507.9ps/nm), and varying OSNR (10-24dB for QPSK, 15-29dB for 16QAM). The experimental results show that the recognition accuracies of MFI, BRI, and CDI tasks reach 100%, 99.81%, and 99.83%, respectively, fully demonstrating the high-accuracy recognition capability of the proposed method for modulation format, baud rate, and dispersion. Additionally, the analysis revealed that when the receiver bandwidth exceeds 5GHz, the accuracy of the proposed method approaches the optimal value. Furthermore, a comparison with single-input and single-output network structures highlights the advantages of using a 2D matrix to enhance model performance and effectively handle different tasks by sharing common features, thereby improving overall performance. Finally, the results indicate that the model's performance can be further improved by optimizing parameters such as the delay factor and bin number in the generation process of AADTP and AAH. Moving forward, we will continue to optimize the model in these areas. For objectives 5 and 6, we automatically update the hyperparameters of the NN model. For classification tasks, the loss function is called cross-entropy (CE). The corresponding loss function is mean absolute error (MAE). Here we use MAE but not root mean square error (RMSE). Because MAE outperforms RMSE as the metric to evaluate the average error of the model. We investigate the impact of the delay factor in AADTP generation and the bin number in AAH generation on the neural network. By training the neural network models using datasets generated with different delay factors and bin numbers, they evaluate the OPM performance. The results show that the OPM performance fluctuates with different delay factors and bin numbers without significant impact, indicating that AADTP and AAH have sufficient features for OPM regardless of the specific parameters used. However, by selecting the best combination of parameters through pre-training, the model achieves the highest overall prediction accuracy. To validate the robustness of the proposed method against sampling jitter, we simulate three degrees of sampling errors based on the 8 GSa/s sampling rate and compare the OPM performance with the case of no sampling error. The results demonstrate that sampling errors within a specific range (e.g., jitter RMS values of 0.0125, 0.025, and 0.05) have almost no effect on the three classification tasks (MFI, BRI, and CDI), with accuracies maintained above 98%. In conclusion, we propose novel optical performance monitoring methods based on adaptive asynchronous delay tap plot, asynchronous amplitude histogram, and multi-task deep learning, enabling accurate and robust monitoring of multiple parameters using a low-bandwidth, cost-effective receiver. The proposed methods contributes significantly to the advancement of intelligent optical networks.

15211619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211619.value: 1. A novel method for OSNR estimation based on the relationship between OSNR and DTP is proposed. This approach utilizes the AADTP and AAH as input features, enabling accurate OSNR estimation using a low-bandwidth, cost-effective receiver. The proposed method addresses the challenge of OSNR monitoring in resource-constrained scenarios and demonstrates the feasibility of using DTP for OSNR estimation. By leveraging the statistical features hidden in the DTP, the proposed approach achieves high accuracy and robustness in OSNR estimation, outperforming traditional methods based on the mean and variance of the DTP diagonal. The AADTP adapts the signal baud rate and optimizes the delay tap resolution, while the AAH captures the amplitude distribution information. The combination of these two features provides a comprehensive representation of the signal characteristics, contributing to the improved performance in OSNR estimation. (This work was published in No. 1 journal paper) 2. A multi-task deep learning neural network architecture for simultaneous estimation of multiple OPM parameters is proposed. The network is designed to jointly monitor OSNR, MF, baud rate, and chromatic dispersion, leveraging the shared information among these parameters. The multi-task learning framework enables the sharing of hidden layer representations, allowing the network to learn more generalized and robust features. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed multi-task architecture over single-task counterparts, achieving state-of-the-art performance in parameter estimation and identification. The joint estimation of multiple parameters not only reduces the computational complexity but also enables a more comprehensive understanding of the signal quality and impairments. (This work was published in No. 1 journal paper) 3. An automatic modulation format identify method based on amplifier features is proposed. The approach utilizes a convolutional neural network to extract discriminative features from the signal quality, enabling accurate classification of different modulation formats. The proposed MFI method eliminates the need for manual feature engineering and demonstrates robustness against various impairments, such as chromatic dispersion and sampling jitter, making it suitable for practical deployment in optical networks. The convolutional layers in the network are designed to capture the spatial dependencies and hierarchical features, leading to improved classification accuracy. The proposed MFI method is extensively evaluated on a diverse dataset encompassing a wide range of modulation formats, signal qualities, and impairments, demonstrating its generalization capability and practicality. (This work was published in No. 2 journal paper) 4. A comprehensive investigation of the impact of various factors on OPM performance is conducted. We analyze the effects of receiver bandwidth, delay factor, bin number, and sampling jitter on the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method. The findings demonstrate that the method maintains high performance under different conditions, highlighting its adaptability to practical scenarios. Furthermore, it is shown that optimizing the input data parameters through pre-training can further enhance the OPM performance. The pre-training process involves fine-tuning the delay factor and bin number to maximize the information captured by these features. The results provide valuable insights into the design and deployment of robust and efficient OPM systems in real-world optical networks. (This work was published in No. 2 journal paper) Besides the main research objectives, we also apply the similar fiber system for sensing application. We also trained PhD students LUO Huaijian, YUAN Weihao, LIU Yifan, WANG Zhuo and CHEN Shuyang. Among them, LUO Huaijian has got his PhD degree based on the research of this project.

15211619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211619.value: Based on the successful completion of the objectives outlined in the research, there is significant potential for further development on intelligent and efficient OPM systems. One potential avenue for further development is the integration of additional OPM parameters, such as polarization mode dispersion (PMD) and nonlinear impairments (NLI), into the multi-task learning framework. This expansion would enable a more comprehensive understanding of signal quality and facilitate more informed decision-making in optical network management. Additionally, further research could focus on the investigation of transfer learning techniques. By leveraging pre-trained models from related domains or larger datasets, the proposed method could be adapted to new modulation formats or network architectures with minimal retraining. Another potential area for development is the incorporation of domain adaptation techniques. This could enhance the robustness of the proposed method against variations in network conditions and hardware configurations. To fully realize the potential of the proposed OPM system, future work should also consider the development of efficient hardware implementations. Designing specialized accelerators or optimizing the neural network architecture for edge computing could enable real-time, low-latency OPM in practical deployments. Moreover, integrating the proposed method with software-defined networking (SDN) and network function virtualization (NFV) paradigms could pave the way for autonomous and dynamic optical network management. By pursuing these avenues, researchers can unlock the full potential of intelligent and adaptive OPM systems, leading to significant advancements in the field of optical networking.

15211619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211619.value: This research project introduces a groundbreaking approach to optical performance monitoring (OPM) by leveraging machine learning and advanced signal processing techniques. By establishing a link between signal quality and deep learning neural networks, our method can accurately and simultaneously estimate multiple key performance parameters. This innovation holds the potential to transform OPM, making it smarter, more efficient, and cost-effective. The proposed solution outperforms traditional methods in terms of accuracy and robustness, and it adapts well to different network conditions and hardware setups. By enabling real-time, comprehensive monitoring of optical signal quality and impairments, this technology supports proactive maintenance, dynamic resource allocation, and autonomous network management. Our research advances the field of intelligent optical networking and sets the stage for future innovations. Ultimately, our OPM method can improve the reliability, efficiency, and scalability of optical communication systems, meeting the growing demand for high-speed, high-capacity data transmission in applications like data centers, and beyond.

15211919.label: Project Objectives
15211919.value: The goal of this research is to investigate the assimilation of densely distributed, ground- and space-based multi-sensor WV data into a localized NWP model to improve the performance of weather forecasting and GNSS positioning performance. The aim is to develop WV assimilation strategies to enhance the performance of weather forecasting and GNSS positioning under various weather conditions. More specifically, this project will achieve the following objectives: (1) Investigating the impact of assimilating densely distributed, multi-sensor 3D / 2D water vapor data into a localized WRF 4D-Var model on improving the performance of weather forecasting under different weather conditions, particularly under extreme weather events. Examining the impact of water vapor data from each type of sensors on 3D tomographic PWV modeling, WRF 4D-Var assimilation results, and consequently the performance of weather forecasting under different weather conditions, particularly under extreme weather events. Understanding how the GNSS positioning performance in terms of positioning accuracy, success rate and convergence time of GNSS carrier phase ambiguity resolution, in both real-time-kinematic and precise point positioning modes, is impacted by WRF 4D-Var water vapor assimilation strategies under different weather conditions, particularly under extreme weather events.

15211919.label: Realisation of objectives
15211919.value: This project’s researchers have innovatively developed a series of novel, machine-learning-based algorithms to calibrate PWV data from remote sensing satellites, before they are officially assimilated into Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models. These algorithms have significantly improved the PWV data accuracy. For instance, we developed a Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN)-based algorithm to retrieve PWV data from near-infrared (NIR) bands of MODIS sensor, on board both Aqua and Terra satellites. The RMSE of PWV data retrieved from BPNN machine learning algorithm has reduced by 57.26% from 10.95 mm of MODIS original data to 4.68 mm of our new algorithm data under all-sky (including clear sky and cloudy sky) conditions; and reduced by 47.49% from 5.58 mm to 2.93 mm under confident-clear conditions. Similarly, we have developed an algorithm for the NIR channels of the OLCI sensor on board the European Sentinel-3A satellite. The RMSE of operational OLCI PWV products was reduced by 12.91% from 3.114 mm to 2.712 mm at the OLCI O19 channel, and by 10.69% to 2.781 mm at the OLCI O20 channel, and by 11.75% to 2.748 mm for the weighted mean PWV, when compared with GPS PWV reference data. We also developed a Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT) based correction model to enhance the accuracy of PWV products from infrared bands of Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS) sensor, on board the Aqua satellite. Under clear-sky condition, the PWV RMSE is reduced by 26.16% from 3.02 mm to 2.23 mm, when using GNSS PWV as reference; and by 17.00% from 2.47 mm to 2.05 mm, when using radiosonde PWV as reference. In the presence of clouds, the GBDT-based algorithm reduces the RMSE of AIRS PWV by 21.08% from 4.27 mm to 3.37 mm when evaluated by GNSS PWV, and by 17.03% from 3.64 mm to 3.02 mm when evaluated by radiosonde PWV. In all-sky conditions, the RMSE of AIRS PWV after the calibration by the GBDT-based algorithm is reduced by 21.43% from 4.17 mm to 3.28 mm when evaluated by GNSS PWV, and by 17.28% from 3.53 mm to 2.92 mm when evaluated by radiosonde PWV. Both remote sensing satellite and GNSS PWV data have been successfully assimilated into NWP modeling (based on WRF model) for South China region (including Hong Kong). Different schemes have been experimented and improved NWP results have been obtained. PWV data collected from the Sentinel-3 satellite have been assimilated into WRF model in two schemes: Sentinel-3 only clear-sky PWV and Sentinel-3 all-sky PWV. For each scheme, 14 days of WRF Data Assimilation (DA) experiments in March 2020 with moderate humidity conditions and 14 days of WRF DA experiments in June 2020 with high humidity (severe weather) conditions were conducted. Results showed that assimilation of all-sky PWV outperforms that of clear-sky PWV. This implicitly indicates that PWV data (in all-sky conditions) is important for weather forecasting. All-sky PWV data have a larger amount of PWV data compared to that in clear-sky condition. For June 2020, assimilating Sentinel-3 all-sky PWV improves rainfall forecast skill score by 2.4%, while the score is improved by only 1.0% after assimilating clear-sky PWV. In June 2020, the comparison results with radiosonde profiles show that assimilating Sentinel-3 PWV appreciably corrects the bias of WRF water vapor mixing ratio forecasting results. For the March 2020 DA, the contribution of assimilating PWV is not as significant as June 2020. This implies that assimilating PWV under wetter, high humidity condition (such as June 2020) is more important than relatively dry condition (such as March 2020). We have also experimented the PWV DA from GNSS and radiosonde sensors into WRF mode. The South China region during the period April 01, 2020 to May 31, 2020 were selected with the following different WRF schemes: WRF scheme 0: no data assimilation (DA); WRF scheme 1: assimilating PWV from 76 GNSS stations; WRF scheme 2: assimilating PWV from 213 GNSS stations; WRF scheme 3: assimilating PWV from 23 radiosonde stations; WRF scheme 4: assimilating both PWV from 213 GNSS stations and 23 radiosonde stations. The results indicate that all the DA schemes (WRF schemes 1 to 4) improve the WRF forecasting performance in terms of PWV and rainfall, compared to the control scheme (WRF scheme 0). For the first 6 hours after DA, WRF schemes 1 to 4 improve the PWV forecasting accuracy by 11.6%, 14.5%, 2.9%, and 14.8%, respectively. For the forecasting of rainfall within the first 6 hours after DA, the WRF scheme 4 is the best one among all five schemes. WRF scheme 4 improves the rainfall forecast probability of detection (POD) and equitable threat score (ETS) by 0.085 and 0.057, respectively. This is equivalent to an improvement of POD and ETS values by 8.5% and 5.7%, respectively, as theoretically possible maximum value for both POD and ETS is 1.0. In our understanding, such a magnitude of improvement (5.7% to 8.5%) represents a significant advancement. This indicates that assimilating more water vapor data has a positive contribution to weather forecasting performance. WRF scheme 2 has a performance similar to WRF scheme 4 and outperforms other DA schemes. It should be noted that to the best of our knowledge, the UK Meteorological Office (UKMO) is the world’s first agency to assimilate NIR PWV data into NWP model. UKMO published first research paper in September 2021 and started to routinely do DA since May 2022. Our first research paper was published in March 2023 and we claimed ourselves to be the 2nd one in the world to conduct NIR PWV DA. Traditionally, NIR radiance data (PWV information is implicitly embedded) are assimilated into NWP models and this is still being so in almost all other national agencies. In addition, to the best of our knowledge, GNSS PWV DA still have not been conducted in many agencies, such as Hong Kong Observatory (HKO), China Meteorological Administration (CMA), and many other national agencies. Our results have clearly shown the merits of assimilating different types of PWV into NWP models. This work is anticipated to bring significant benefits to the Hong Kong as the PI Prof. Liu is actively working with HKO in attempt to transfer the DA algorithms, developed in this project, to the HKO’s daily routine NWP system. In addition, PWV data from NWP model can be used to improve the accuracy of GNSS positioning. We have conducted extensive GNSS positioning tests under different schemes, such as, kinematic and static positioning; under moderate and high humidity conditions. We find that NWP-derived PWV can significantly improve GNSS positioning accuracy, particularly in the vertical component. In GNSS static positioning mode, the accuracy can be improved by 14.6% under moderate humidity condition; and the improvement can be 33.7% under high humidity condition. In GNSS kinematic positioning mode, the GNSS positioning accuracy is slightly lower but it is still 13.8% under moderate humidity condition and 19.0% for users under high humidity condition. In addition to accuracy improvement, the needed time is also significantly shortened. Our results show that in static mode, the GNSS positioning time can be shortened by 41.8% and 25.0% under moderate humidity and high humidity, respectively. For kinematic positioning, the positioning time in moderate humidity level is reduced by up to 8.2%.

15211919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15211919.value: This project has made significant progress in the Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) modeling and has advanced the data assimilation technique in the meteorological community. More specifically, we have developed a series of novel, machine-learning-based algorithms to calibrate PWV data collected from different remote sensing channels and from different satellite platforms. After the calibration, the accuracies of satellite-based water vapor data have been significantly enhanced. The improvements range from approximately 10% to more than 50%, depending on the water vapor remote sensing channels and the specific sensors used. We are confident to claim that this project’s research team has clearly demonstrated a leadership in this research area and the research papers have been cited by multiple research groups. This project has developed novel data assimilation methods to assimilate various sources of water vapor data, including remote sensing satellite, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) water vapor data, and radiosonde. Extensive test results showed that after the water vapor data assimilation, that rainfall forecasting scores can be improved. The probability of detection (POD) score and equitable threat score (ETS) can be improved by up to 8.5% and 5.7%, when GNSS water vapor data and radiosonde data are assimilated. With the assimilation of remote sensing water vapor data, forecasting scores can be improved by 2.4% even during South China’s most humid season (in the month of June). To the best of our knowledge, the UK Meteorological Office (UKMO) is the world’s first agency to assimilate Near-Infrared water vapor data into NWP model and they started this routine work since May 2022. We claim that we are the 2nd institution to do this work independently, just after the UKMO. Actually, this research team has done a little more work than the UKMO. We have assimilated all-sky (including cloudy-sky and clear-sky) remote sensing water vapor data while UKMO assimilated clear-sky data only. This project’s results have a significant demonstrative value for the meteorological agencies in Hong Kong, Great Bay Area, Mainland China, and other regions/nations. This is because many agencies have not assimilated GNSS water vapor data into their models, not to mention the remote sensing water vapor data. In addition, we have demonstrated that GNSS water vapor from NWP model (the Weather Research & Forecasting (WRF) model in this project) can significantly benefit the GNSS precise positioning. Our results showed that the PWV error can be reduced by up to 14.8%. Water vapor with reduced error can help improve the accuracy of GNSS positioning in both static and kinematic mode, with an improvement up to 33.7%, depending on the weather conditions. In addition, the GNSS time can be shortened significantly by 8.2% to 41.8%.

15211919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15211919.value: This project has explored and developed new approaches to assimilate precipitable water vapor (PWV) data into Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models, which have shown from extensive experiment analyses to be able to improve the forecasting scores. Moreover, multiple machine-learning based algorithms can be used to enhance the accuracy of the satellite PWV data, before they are assimilated into NWP models. The work has a great potential to benefit Hong Kong, the Greater Bay Area (GBA), and other coastal regions if it is adopted by the meteorological agencies. Hong Kong as a coastal city has a high level of humidity and annual mean rainfall is over 3,000 mm in some areas of Hong Kong. Improving the rainfall forecasting scores, particularly for the extreme rainfall, has long been a challenge in Hong Kong and other coastal regions. A record-breaking rainfall event occurred in Hong Kong on September 7-8, 2023. It exemplifies a urgent need to develop better NWP methods. The PI Prof. Liu is actively working with the scientists in Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) and institutions in the GBA in an attempt to transfer the data assimilation methods to their daily routine forecasting system. We are collaborating to conduct more case studies with more data support from HKO and GBA agencies.

15211919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15211919.value: We have developed algorithms to assimilate atmospheric precipitable water vapor (PWV) data into a localized Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) model. The PWV data are collected from multiple sources, such as Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), radiosonde, and remote sensing satellites. Our extensive experiments under different weather conditions have shown that assimilating different sources of PWV data can significantly improve the forecasting scores. To the best of our knowledge, many meteorological agencies have not conducted this type of work, including Hong Kong, Mainland China, and many others. This project proves that the direct data assimilation of Near-Infrared PWV data can be successfully done and satisfactory results can be achieved. To the best of our knowledge, we are the 2nd institution to assimilate Near-Infrared PWV data into NWP model, just after the UK Meteorological Office which started to routinely do so in May 2022. The outcomes of this project exemplify the significant benefits of using these datasets into NWP models. In addition, we have developed multiple innovative machine-learning methods to improve the accuracy of PWV data from remote sensing satellite data. We also showed that using the PWV data from NWP model can significantly improve the performance of GNSS positioning in different modes.

15212319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212319.value: Biorefinery technique associated with anaerobic digestion (AD) process has become an environmentally attractive approach to support sustainable waste and management. In this process, heterotrophic bacteria carry out a series of biochemical reactions to hydrolyze and convert organic pollutants into useful products and/or energy. Mixing lignocellulosic biomass or other plant based bio-wastes into the AD for co-digestion has been considered a feasible approach for organic waste treatment in Hong Kong, but this application has impacted the performance of the original AD process treating sewer sludge. This is mostly due to slow hydrolysis rate of the substrates (before methanogensis is in concern). Plant cell wall is a complex 3-dimension structure evolved to protect plant cells from physical and biological attacks. The specific “biomass recalcitrant” is created by the unique arrangements of three building block chemicals, i.e., cellulose, hemicelluloses, and lignin. Since the structure is plant-specific, different biomass has various digestibilities during biodegradation. To reduce biomass recalcitrant, a few pretreatment processes (such as hydrothermal or microwave treatment) have been developed to improve the digestibility of the substrate in the ADs. Due to costs concern and simplicity of the basic feedstocks most of the introduced pretreatment approaches have applied only water and heat for those AD-oriented thermal pretreatment processes, and no chemicals have been considered. The pretreatment severity in those processes is chemically limited and hence those techniques can only apply on low recalcitrant biomass. The power consumption is also very high for the proposed strategies. In fact, AD can generate many metabolites (i.e., organic acids, ammonia, and other compounds) that may be applicable in the pretreatment. With improved thermos-chemical pretreatment, a conventional AD may be used to treat high recalcitrant feedstock, such as yard or woody product wastes. Finally, cellulase and cellulosomes are two representative hydrolyzing systems to convert cellulose into glucose. The state-of-the-art biorefinery processes have been recently developed based on comprehensive understanding of cellulase, while the related interaction between cellulosome, lignin, and substrates has not been widely investigated. In our recent works, we investigated the key mechanisms affecting enzymatic hydrolysis from cellulase, such as the hydrophobic hydrophilicity, electrostatic interaction, and H-bonding from small molecular weight components. Similar interactions may or may not apply in AD. By clarifying this fundamental question it is our hope that a new biorefinery approach can be developed to improve the exiting AD before introducing new feedstock in waste based biorefinery in Hong Kong and the world. 生物煉製技術結合厭氧生物處理已逐漸形成一個環境友好且可持續的有機廢棄物處理趨勢。在適當的反應條件下，異營菌可藉由一連串的生化反應將熱化學預處理後的底物轉化為有價產物或能源。香港在近年嘗試混合木質生物質或其他植物類生物質廢棄物與廢水處理汙泥進行厭氧共消化，但由於二級汙泥與木質生物質的水解速率有顯著不同，共消化的效率因此受到影響。植物細胞壁是一種極為嚴謹的三維結構，經由不斷地演化成為可以有效抵抗物理或生物降解的複合材料。此類的“生物頑抗性”主要來自三種基礎化合物(即纖維素、半纖維素與木質素)在特殊的比例下的結合，由於這些結合的條件在不同物種間不盡相同，不同植物種與組織間的生物降解效果也各異。預處理(如水熱與微波)是打破木質生物質生物頑抗性的關鍵流程。由於成本考量，近年為厭氧消化處理設計的預處理流程多以非化學為主的水熱反應為主。然而，這些缺少反應劑的低強度預處理方式通常只適於處理低頑抗的生物質；能源的損耗也大，因此未能被廣泛地應用。事實上，厭氧消化可以產生許多適合用來進行預處理的代謝產物(例如有機酸、氨、與其他有機物)。如能結合這些化合物的特性來進行熱化學預處理，一般傳統的厭氧消化流程或許也有機會升級成可以處理高頑固生物質(如園林與木質廢棄物)的新反應系統。再者，纖維素酶與纖維小體代表好厭氧兩種截然不同的生物水解系統，用以將纖維素轉化為可發酵的葡萄糖。近年絕大多數新式預處理流程的設計理念皆以較為熟知的纖維素酶為目標，這類理論基礎如蛋白-木質素-底物的交互作用在厭氧生物流程中的纖維小體水解系統中多未被詳細研究。例如，我們在最近的研究中曾對纖維酶水解的主要機理如親疏水、電磁屬性、與氫鍵在充滿各類小分子化合物的水解系統中的影響進行探討；但同樣的研究基礎在厭氧系統中不見得適用。藉由深入探討這些基礎問題，本研究希望能進一步提升厭氧處理效率、增加可用的生物質底物、並為本港與全球生物煉製技術研究開發新方向。

15212319.label: Realisation of objectives
15212319.value: [Pretreatment] Our study discovered an unique reactive lignin stream with great solvent solubility and preserved alpha-O-4 linkages from eucalypts, after a modified organosolv pretreatment using 1,4-butanediol (1,4-BDO). Unlike conventional pretreatment using ethanol or dilute acid solution, lignin deposition was not formed in 1,4-BDO pretreatment. 2D HSQC NMR analysis revealed that the residual lignin obtained from 1,4-BDO pretreated eucalypts contained a relatively higher amount of alpha-O-4 interunit linkages, indicating higher integrity than other lignin. This result agreed with the lower content of phenolic hydroxyl groups in dissolved lignin via 31P NMR analysis. With increasing pretreatment severity, the amount of aliphatic hydroxyl groups decreased in conventional lignin while it remained at a higher level in 1,4-BDO pretreated lignin. 1,4-BDO could quench the benzyl carbocation intermediate and formed ether linkages with a hydroxyl tail at the alpha position of the lignin. Solubility tests revealed that grafting aliphatic hydroxyl groups on 1,4-BDO lignin increased its dissolution. This phenomenon was further demonstrated for four different diols with similar structures. More than 90% cellulose conversion was obtained for all the diol pretreated eucalyptus after 48 h of enzymatic hydrolysis with cellulase at a loading of 7.5 FPU per grams of glucan. Diols offer a promising reaction pathway to coincide with three pillars of biorefinery for lignin fractionation, lignin structural integrity, and cellulose hydrolysis and therefore has become the key metabolite to be produced for biorefinery pretreatment. [Set-up bioreactor] The study was initiated by treating the chemical enhanced primary treated (CEPT) sewage sludge with AD. The CEPT sludge was collected from the Stonecutters Island Sewage Treatment Works, Hong Kong. The sludge is a slurry type of biomass containing approximately 70% water; and the dry content of CEPT sludge is composed of 30-33% of cellulose and 5% hemicellulose. Cellulose and hemicelluloses are major potential carbon source of fermentation in biorefineries, but cellulolysis is still a rate-limiting factor in the system. A semi-continuous mesophilic AD (2-L) was constructed and operated in five stages for over 180 days. The digester was controlled at a temperature of 37°C, 150 rpm mechanic stirring and pH 7. The inoculum sludge was collected from a full-scale digester in Sha Tin Sewage Treatment Works, Hong Kong. To control the SRT, a constant volume of digested sludge was decanted during each cycle, and the fed sludge was supplemented (133 mL for 15 d SRT and 200 mL for 20 d SRT). The produced biogas was collected by 5-L gas bags and analyzed by using a commercial gas sensor for determining methane (CH4), carbon dioxide (CO2), and hydrogen sulphide (H2S) contents. Sludge samples were collected from the AD periodically. The volatile fatty acids (VFAs) of the solid samples were determined using a high-performance liquid chromatography system (Shimadzu LC-20AD, Prominence, Kyoto, Japan). The sludge samples were clipped and oven-dried at 105°C; and the cellulose and hemicellulose contents were determined using the two-step acid hydrolysis method. [DNA sequencing] Total DNA of the sludge samples was extracted using the PowerSoil DNA Isolation Kit. The library construction of 16S rRNA genes and next-generation sequencing on the Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform by Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI) Genomics (Shenzhen, China). The primers used for polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of 16S rRNA genes for bacterial were 515F (5′GTG CCA GCMGCC GCG GTA A 3′) / 806R (5′ GGA CTA CHV GGG TWT CTA AT 3′), which targets the V4 variable region. The raw reads were processed and analysed using the Mothur software. The sequences were sorted into operational taxonomic units. Taxonomy was assigned with the SILVA-based 16S rRNA database with 97% similarity. A neighbour-joining phylogenetic tree was generated using software ARB, with SILVA database SSU NR99 as a reference database. The distance matrix was used in hierarchical clustering by unweighted pair group method. [Metagenomics analysis] For metagenomics analysis, the library construction and sequencing were conducted by BGI Genomics (Shenzhen, China). The raw reads were first trimmed with a minimum quality cut-off at 3 and further screened to be at least 78 bp in length, having an average quality score above 30 and containing less than three ambiguous nucleotides (N's) using trimmomatic. The trimmed clean paired-end reads were further de novo assembled into long sequence contigs using SPAdes version 3.9.0 based on the de Bruijn graph. Contigs were clustered into taxonomic bins with MetaWRAP. The qualities of draft genome bins were evaluated by CheckM. The recovered genome bins were compared against the reference phylogenetic tree with PhyloPhlAn. Protein coding genes were annotated with Prokka version 1.11. BLAST with RefSeq non-redundant database was used to further characterize individual gene functions. Cellulosome-relative genes were identified by aligning amino acid sequence with known cellulosome subunits sequence.

15212319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212319.value: The gas productions/compositions, solid/cellulose contents, and volatile fatty acids are demonstrated. At Days 0-20, the reactor was operated under batch mode with an initial feed of 30 g/L VSS CEPT sludge. Low amounts of biogas (lower than 500 mL/d) were produced during this initiation stage. At Days 20-90, the reactor operation was then modified to continuous mode with 15 d SRT. The biogas production started to increase from 500 mL/d to approximately 1,200-2,000 mL/d at 30 g/L VSS continuous feeding. CH4 and CO2 were approximately 41% and 28% in the biogas, respectively, and high H2S concentration (approximately 35,000 ppm) was recorded, mostly owing to the high sulfate content in the substrate. At Days 90-135 and Days 135-155, with the increase of SRT (from 15 d to 20 d) the daily biogas production increased slightly from 1,500 mL/d to 2,000-2,800 mL/d, and CH4 content increased gradually to approximately 70%. The CH4 yield was 0.42 L/kg VSSin, which was much higher than that recorded from the AD treating excess secondary sludge (0.2-0.35 L/kg VSSin). Hydrogen gas was not detected in the tested gas samples throughout the experiments, implying that hydrolysis was still the rate limiting factor affecting the reaction kinetics in comparison with hydrogenotrophic methanogenesis. The gene content of the reconstructed draft genome bins was annotated, thereby illuminating the potential functional properties of the microbial species. The microbial association networks with respect to the operational factors were constructed based on relatively abundant OTUs by CoNet for investigating the correlation of the microbial population shifts with cellulose concentration in the effluent of the reactor. For the bacterial community, the most abundant class in the system is Bacteroidia (35%-58%), followed by Clostridia (15%-32%). They are the anaerobic bacteria that often observed in the anaerobic fermentation system. The genera DMER64 (CSA36), Proteiniphilum (CSA19) and Bacteroides_unclassified (CSA17, CSA21), Dysgonomonadaceae unclassified belong to the order of Bacteroidales. The genus DMER64, which belongs to the Rikenellaceae family, was the most abundant genus in the system. The relative abundance of Saccharofermentans (CSA20) from Clostridiales was 5-10% during experiment. CSA20 and chiristensenellaceae classified to Clostridia showed positive correlations with cellulose in the association network, which means these bacteria may play a relatively direct role in cellulose degradation. Sphaerochaeta (CSA1, CSA31) observed from Day 9 is a strictly fermentative and anaerobic bacterial, which reportedly ferment complex sugar, monosaccharides, and disaccharides to ethanol, acetate, and formate.

15212319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212319.value: An unexpected result of this study is that cellulosome genes were identified from two highly abundant species of Methanosarcina (CSA5, CSA9) recovered through metagenome sequencing. This implies its potential of cellulose degradation which has never been identified in previous genome sequence studies of Methanosarcina, which may worthwhile in future study.

15212319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212319.value: The project aims to investigate the key factors affecting cellulolysis efficiency in Anaerobic digestion (AD) treating cellulosic or lignocellulosic substrate. AD is a widely applied technology for the treatment of organic wastes, but the biogas production rate and yield are both low and need to be improved, due to the slow hydrolysis rate of the lignocellulosic biomass. Biorefinery techniques are developed to overcome those rate limiting factors by utilizing metabolic products produced from the bioreactor in the pretreatment processes. The chosen metabolites are easily accessible in biological processes; and may show potential to loosen the lignocellulosic structure of different types of biomass. During the pretreatment process, the metabolites could act as organic solvent, catalysts, or reagents for delignification. By clarifying the mechanisms of delignification and cellulolysis, more biomass feedstock can therefore be converted into biogas, which support sustainable waste management. The finding of this project has resulted in 15 journal publications, 4 conference presentations, and 1 PhD student in training in the related research area.

15212419.label: Project Objectives
15212419.value: To propose new efficient mining attacks in the blockchain. By adopting our new mining attacks, an attacker can be more profitable than honest mining and current attacks, e.g., BWH and FAW. To successfully launch selective mining attacks in both public/private blockchains and achieve DoS to transaction confirmation. To identify network vulnerabilities and propose new network attacks to private blockchains, e.g., delay attacks and eclipse attacks, aiming at double-spending and DoS consequence to normal users. To propose practical mitigation solutions against the novel attacks. We expect to identify more than 95% attacking nodes under mining attacks and minimize the effect of network attacks (no intentional forks). Double-spending can be avoided in the whole system and DoS can be remedied once detected. To carry out simulations and real experiments in a test bed to evaluate the performance of proposed attacks and countermeasures. We will build our test bed in a programmable system for the public blockchain and in Hyperledger for the private blockchain.

15212419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15212419.value: 區塊鏈技術已廣泛應用於從加密貨幣到供應鍊等領域的商業交易。然而，根據腾讯的報告，區塊鏈應用程序中的漏洞导致2018年上半年损失超過27億美元。由於設計問題，以太坊在2016年7月遭受了DAO攻擊。攻擊者獲得了超過3500萬的ETH，並將以太坊分成兩部分ETH和ETC。中國交易所币安於2018年3月7日遭遇分佈式攻擊。攻擊者通過VIA（一種加密貨幣）獲取了大量賬戶並獲得了巨額利潤。兩種類型的攻擊，挖掘攻擊和網絡攻擊，可以破坏區塊鏈系统，例如拒絕向客戶提供交易確認服務，創造分叉並導致雙重支出，破壞同行之間的信任。因此，這個項目將研究對今天的區塊链網絡存在的威脅，識別採礦程序和區塊鏈中的新攻擊網絡，並提出有效的解決方案來抵制它們。 我們將首先採用一個新的角度來分析對區塊鏈系統的挖掘攻擊。現有採礦攻擊與誠實的採礦相比，攻擊者獲得相對較小的額外獎勵。額外的獎勵對攻擊者沒有吸引力，因為它們會冒被發現的風險。不同與當前的採礦攻擊方法，我們將提出PAW，賄賂採礦和選擇性採礦攻擊。PAW和選擇性挖掘攻擊是全新的攻击模式。選擇性挖掘攻擊可以推遲甚至否認共識節點的交易（例如，在使用DPoS的公共區塊鏈中 - 委託的證明，或私人區塊鏈）。賄賂採礦攻擊可以大大增加攻擊者的可能性分支被選為主鏈，故意創建另一個分支。我們的採礦攻擊可以獎勵攻擊者利潤高於當前的採礦攻擊，從而使它們適合發起。 我們還將解決區塊鏈中的網絡攻擊問題，即延遲攻擊和日食攻擊。以前的研究工作只關注對公共區塊鏈系統的攻擊。我們擴展研究聯盟（或私人）區塊鏈系統，攻擊可以利用私有區塊鏈功能並造成嚴重後果。雖然聯盟（或私人）區塊鏈可以強制執行嚴格的用戶授權和認證機制，他們無法避免網絡攻擊，因為區塊鍊是部署並連接到分佈式网络。通過延遲一些交易或孤立一些區塊鏈系統中的節點，我們的新方法可以觸發雙重攻擊，拒絕服務（DoS）攻擊，在區塊鏈系統中分叉，或浪費受害礦工的採礦工作量。最後，該項目將針對研究的攻擊提出有效的對策，實現安全和可信賴區塊鏈系統。

15212419.label: Realisation of objectives
15212419.value: We have fully achieved the above-listed five objectives in this project. 1. Objective 1: To propose new efficient mining attacks in the blockchain. By adopting our new mining attacks, an attacker can be more profitable than honest mining and current attacks, e.g., BWH and FAW. We analyze the efficacy of mining attacks in our paper GLOBECOM-2023. We study the new efficient mining attacks in the blockchain and present the selfish mining strategy under the checkpoint mechanism in the paper GLOBECOM-2023. We develop a rigorous analysis method to study the behavior of selfish mining in various scenarios. Our method can be extended to analyze more sophisticated selfish mining strategies under the checkpoint mechanism. We conclude that the checkpoint mechanism can effectively restrict selfish mining, by reducing the profit of selfish mining and raising the threshold of computational power that makes selfish mining profitable. We further show the bottlenecks in the UTXO-based blockchain systems, which can affect the launch of mining attacks in the paper IPDPS-2022. In the paper IPDPS-2022, we propose EBV, an efficient block validation mechanism for UTXO-based blockchains, which mainly changes the representation method of status data, from the UTXO set to a bit-vector set. EBV can support various checking of inputs, including EV, UV, and SV, which ensures system security. 2. Objective 2: To successfully launch selective mining attacks in both public/private blockchains and achieve DoS to transaction confirmation. First, we analyze the architecture and consensus protocols in both public/private blockchains in the paper ACM-CSUR-2020. In particular, we give an architecture overview of popular IoT-blockchain systems by analyzing their network structures and protocols. We show that selective mining attacks can undermine the consensus protocols in a blockchain system. Furthermore, we have proposed a novel consensus protocol: G?PBFT in the IPDPS-2020 paper. G?PBFT is a lightweight and scalable private blockchain consensus protocol, which mines new blocks on selective nodes. As a result, G?PBFT achieves high consensus efficiency and low traffic intensity. Then, we analyze the DoS attacks to blockchain networks in the TNET-2020 paper. SDN-aimed DoS attacks can cause long packet delay and high packet loss rate by using massive table-miss packets to jam links between the two planes. To detect and mitigate SDN-aimed DoS attacks, this paper presents FloodDefender, an efficient and protocol-independent defense framework for SDN/OpenFlow networks. The results from the TNET-2020 paper can successfully defend against selective mining attacks by mitigating DoS to transaction confirmations. 3. Objective 3: To identify network vulnerabilities and propose new network attacks to private blockchains, e.g., delay attacks and eclipse attacks, aiming at double-spending and DoS consequence to normal users. First, we developed a blockchain network simulator to analyze the traffic pattern in blockchain system, which can help us identify blockchain network vulnerabilities in the papers ICC-2021 and ACM-CSUR-2020. The developed blockchain network simulator is pluggable so that we can test different blockchain consensus protocols on it. We have evaluated the PoW protocol on permissioned blockchain in the ICC-2021 paper. Our experiment results show that the network can carry hundreds of devices with a low error rate. Then, new attacks are given and analyzed in the paper ACSAC-2021 and those attacks can lead to double-spending and DoS consequence to normal users. For example, we show in the paper ACSAC-2021 that the infamous reentrancy bug in the DAO contract allows attackers to arbitrarily withdraw ethers, which caused millions of dollars loss. Currently, the main countermeasure against contract bugs is to thoroughly detect and verify contracts before deployment, which, however, cannot defend against unknown bugs. Moreover, we identify the cache poisoning attack and DDoS attack to DNS systems in the paper TNSE-2021. In this paper, we propose B-DNS, a blockchain-based domain name system, which can provide a secure and efficient DNS service. B-DNS fills up two shortcomings of current blockchain-based DNS, namely computation-heavy Proof-of-Work (PoW) protocol and inefficient query, by building a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus protocol and an index of domains. 4. Objective 4: To propose practical mitigation solutions against the novel attacks. We expect to identify more than 95% attacking nodes under mining attacks and minimize the effect of network attacks (no intentional forks). Double-spending can be avoided in the whole system and DoS can be remedied once detected. First, we propose the checkpoint mechanism against novel attacks in the paper GC2023. In this paper, we analyze the profitability of selfish mining under the checkpoint mechanism. We develop a rigorous analysis method and conduct quantitative evaluations in various scenarios to explore the mechanism's suppression effect on selfish mining. The results illustrate that the checkpoint mechanism can restrict the profit of selfish mining and increase the threshold of computational power that makes selfish mining profitable, suggesting that it is a practical defense mechanism against selfish mining. Second, we propose SolSaviour, a framework for repairing and recovering deployed defective smart contracts for a blockchain system in the paper ACSAC-2021. Our defense can redeploy patched contracts and migrate old contracts' internal states to the new ones. Our experiment results show that SolSaviour can successfully repair vulnerabilities, reduce asset losses, and recover all defective contracts for blockchain systems. Furthermore, we proposed FloodDefender in the paper TNET-2020, which can detect and mitigate the DoS attacks. FloodDefender can capture the frequency features of DoS attack traffic and then filter them out. Cache poisoning attacks severely affect the security of DNS, the fundamental of Internet. We proposed a blockchain-based DNS in the paper TNSE-2021, which can significantly improve the security of DNS. We also quantitatively demonstrated that the attack cost against our proposed DNS is thousands of times higher than the attack cost against legacy DNS. 5. Objective 5: To carry out simulations and real experiments in a test bed to evaluate the performance of proposed attacks and countermeasures. We will build our test bed in a programmable system for the public blockchain and in Hyperledger for the private blockchain. Simulations and real blockchain systems are constructed in the project. For example, we conduct quantitative evaluations using our theoretical results in the paper GC2023. We find that the checkpoint mechanism can restrict the profit of selfish mining and increase the threshold of computational power that makes selfish mining profitable. In the paper IPDPS2022, we implement a prototype on top of Bitcoin to evaluate EBV, whose experimental results demonstrate its low memory requirement and acceleration of block validation. In the paper ACSAC2021, we build a TEE cluster based on Intel SGX to take charge of asset escrow and contract state migration. Experiment results show that SolSaviour can effectively mitigate the loss caused by smart contract vulnerabilities with little overhead. In the paper TNSE2021, we design two sets of experiments to evaluate the security and performance of B-DNS. In the security evaluation, we compare the security properties between legacy DNS and BDNS from three dimensions. Experiments show that B-DNS is much more secure than legacy DNS. In the paper IPDPS2020, we conduct extensive experiments to compare the performance of G-PBFT against existing consensus protocol with over 200 participating nodes in a blockchain system. Experimental results demonstrate that G-PBFT significantly reduces consensus time, network overhead, and is scalable for IoT applications.

15212419.label: Major findings and research outcome
15212419.value: The major findings from the project include new attacks and defense mechanisms for the blockchain systems. First, we develop a rigorous analysis method to study the behavior of selfish mining in various scenarios. We present a realistic model of PoW-based blockchains in the paper GC2023, which is consistent with the models in previous analyses of mining attacks. We present a 3-dimensional Markov process that models the selfish mining strategy under the checkpoint mechanism. Then, we derive the stationary distribution of the Markov process and further calculate the selfish miner’s long-term revenue. We also identify various attacks on different blockchain systems, e.g., smart contracts, DNS systems, and consensus protocols. Then, we propose practical defense solutions to current blockchain systems when facing potential attacks. The proposed checkpoint mechanism can make selfish mining attacks unprofitable. The proposed SolSaviour framework in the paper ACSAC-2021 can repair and recover deployed defective smart contracts for a blockchain system securely. We proposed a blockchain‐based DNS in the paper TNSE-2021, which can significantly improve the security of DNS against DoS attacks. This project has fruitful research outcomes. The research outcomes of the project have been shown in top journal and top conference papers. Top journal papers include IEEE TNSE-2021 (A Secure and Efficient DNS Based on the Blockchain Technology), ACM-CSUR-2020 (Blockchain Systems: Architecture, Consensus, and Traffic Modeling), IEEE TNET2020 (Detection and Mitigation of DoS Attacks). Top conference papers include IEEE GC2023 (Selfish Mining Attack under the Checkpoint Mechanism), IEEE IPDPS2022 (Block Validation Mechanism for UTXO-based Blockchains), ACSAC2021 (A Defending Framework for Deployed Defective Smart Contracts), and IEEE IPDPS2020 (A Location-based and Scalable Consensus Protocol for IoT-Blockchain Applications), and IEEE ICC2021 (Communication Traffic Model for Permissioned Blockchain). With the support of this project, one Ph.D. student, Mr. Zecheng Li, has been enrolled, trained, and graduated in 2022.

15212419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15212419.value: The project research can be further extended to more complex scenarios, e.g., layer2 structure, cross-chain environments, and sharding-based blockchains. New attacks can be found in these complex blockchain systems, due to the multiple chain systems. However, the layer2 structure may provide the checkpoint mechanism that can reduce the attack possibility, which needs more investigation. Some privacy-preserving methods, e.g., zero-knowledge based information posting, may cause some new attacks on the mining, which is being conducted in our research group. Providing both security and privacy could be challenging in a blockchain system, e.g., in Web3, which will be posted to the blockchain security community, to arouse more attention.

15212419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15212419.value: Blockchain technology has been broadly applied in areas from cryptocurrency to supply chain and other business transactions. However, blockchain systems (public, private, or cryptocurrency exchange platforms) are constantly under various attacks, e.g., mining attacks and network attacks. The attack problems should be well addressed to prevent losses of normal users (e.g., due to double spending) and blockchain platform developers (e.g., due to DoS, trust undermining). Thus, this project is valuable for analyzing new threats to blockchain systems and giving effective countermeasures. The project outcome includes new selfish mining attacks analyzed, new defending mechanisms proposed for different blockchain systems. Our defending mechanisms are practical and efficient to be applied to various blockchain systems. For instance, the proposed checkpoint mechanism can effectively throttle against selfish mining attacks and double spending attacks. Our proposed SolSaviour framework can repair and recover deployed defective smart contracts securely and timely, which has not been done previously. Our proposed B-DNS system fills up two shortcomings of current blockchain-based DNS with efficient DNS query services. The project research results are published in top journal/conference papers, including IEEE IPDPS 2022, 2020, ACSAC 2021, IEEE ICC 2021, IEEE Globecom 2023, IEEE TNSE 2021, IEEE TNET 2020, and ACM CSUR 2020.

15213019.value: To design and build a large-size physical model with comprehensive instrumentation and to conduct a series of tests on fast consolidation of bentonite slurry installed with PVDs subjected to vacuum preloading and heating and to use the data to access the effectiveness of the thermo-vacuum-PVDs. To propose a new T-EVP model for clays which will be verified using CRS test data on the bentonite slurry. To develop a 2D FE model with T-EVP model incorporated for fully coupled consolidation analysis of clays subjected to temperature changes, which will be verified using data from physical model tests and will be used for a parametric study. To have a better understanding of the influences of temperature on stress-strain behaviour of the bentonite and the effectiveness of the thermo-vacuum-PVDs for fast consolidation of the bentonite slurry and to make recommendations on how to apply the T-EVP constitutive model, the 2D FE model, and the thermo-vacuum-PVD method for fast consolidation of clayey soils in real projects.

15213019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213019.value: 许多天然粘土，例如中国沿海城市天津的海洋粘土，许多国家和地区的膨胀粘土，含有蒙脱粘土成份，其渗透性很低。在香港，使用泥浆隧道掘进机方法，建造隧道，会产生大量的膨润土（蒙脱粘土）泥浆作为建筑垃圾储存在一些地方。在这些有膨润土（蒙脱粘土）的土地可用于支撑任何结构之前，必须改进所有这些粘土（或浆料）。前人已经提出了许多不同的方法用于加速粘土的固结，包括使用具有真空预压垂直排水（PVD），电动力学和加热方法。在软土地面上的结构（例如地基，机场跑道）的沉降是一个大问题，甚至比剪切破坏更重要。一些研究人员已经对用于分析软土的方法或模型进行了广泛的工作，所研究的软土或有垂直排水板或真空预压。一些研究人员研究了温度对土壤应力 - 应变行为的影响，但忽略了时间和速率效应。另一方面，一些研究工作考虑了温度和应变率的影响，但尚未将其本构模型应用于通过加热和真空预压改善软粘土的完全耦合固结模型。研究温度和应变率对极低渗透性粘土（如蒙脱石/膨润土）的应力 - 应变行为的影响及其在固结建模中的应用都很少见。 基于上述综述，我们需要考虑到时间（蠕变），应变率和温度的影响，进一步改进软粘土的快速固结方法，本构模型和完全耦合固结模型存在很大研究空间。 该项目的主要工作是对单元体的力学行为进行实验室测试，并在高温下使用热真空PVD对膨润土浆料进行物理模型试验，以研发新的温度依赖的弹性粘塑料（T-EVP）本构模型和新的二维轴对称有限元（2D FE）模型与T-EVP模型相结合，用于完全耦合的固结模拟。该项目的具体目标是：（a）设计和建造一个带有综合仪器的大型物理模型，并对安装有PVD的膨润土浆料进行真空预压和加热的快速固结进行一系列试验，并使用数据，以获得热真空PVD的有效性; （b）在高温下进行一系列多阶段固结仪测试和Rowe Cell测试以及一系列恒定应变率（CRS），以研究时间/应变率和温度相关的应力 - 应变行为。膨润土浆料; （c）为粘土提出新的T-EVP模型，该模型将使用膨润土浆料的CRS测试数据进行验证; （d）开发具有T-EVP模型的二维有限元模型，该模型用于温度变化的粘土的完全耦合固结分析，将使用物理模型试验的数据进行验证，并将用于参数研究; （e）更好地了解温度对膨润土的应力 - 应变行为的影响以及热真空PVD对膨润土浆料快速固结的有效性，并就如何应用T-EVP提出建议本构模型，二维有限元模型，以及真空项目中粘性土快速固结的热真空-PVD处理方法。如果我们的物理模型试验和二维有限元模型模拟已经证明热真空-PVD处理方法能够有效地快速固结非常低渗透的膨润土浆料，那么，这种处理方法可以用来快速巩固所有其他天然粘性土壤，如天津的疏浚海洋粘土和香港的海洋粘土。 该项目将在本构模型，有限元全耦合固结模拟，热真空PVD的物理模拟以及低渗透粘土的快速固结以及更好地理解温度，时间和应变率的影响方面取得重大进展。该项目的研究成果将产生积极影响，不仅可以通过沿海城市使用热真空PVD快速整合疏浚海洋土壤进行快速海洋填海造地，还可以解决香港土地短缺问题。

15213019.label: Realisation of objectives
15213019.value: 1. Three sets of laboratory physical model tests were carried out on a dredged waste slurry containing montmorillonite with ultra-high water content using the PVD and grid-PHDs vacuum preloading at different temperatures to study the influence of temperature on the vacuum preloading consolidation and the improvement of slurries. The heating can enhance the efficiency of PVD- and PHD-vacuum preloading consolidation and make the consolidation more uniform. The undrained shear strength has significantly increased and the compressibility extremely decreases for the soils after heating treatment as temperature increases owing to the higher effective stress applied on soil at higher temperature. The use of PHDs has advantages over PVDs for soft slurry due to the less bending, clogging and vacuum loss. Therefore, the study has been leveraged toward on PHD consolidations in the later stages. 2. A series of temperature-controlled oedometer tests have been performed on the binary bentonite-sand mixtures with different bentonite contents under various temperature conditions. The test results were used to investigate the coupled effects of temperature and clay content on the hydro-mechanical behaviours, consolidation, and time-dependent behaviour of bentonite-sand mixtures. The results of oedometer test indicate that the hydraulic conductivity significantly increases with increasing temperature and decreasing fine content. The compression and swelling indices of bentonite-sand mixtures are temperature dependent. Microscopic techniques, such as X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP) tests, were adopted to study the mineral composition, evolution of microstructure and change in micro pores with temperature. The contact manner between particles converted from edge-to-face to the edge-to-edge association and some intra-aggregate pores merged to form inter-aggregate pores as temperature increases. 3. A new thermal elastic visco-plastic (TEVP) constitutive model has been developed and validated. The 1D TEVP model was first proposed (Chen and Yin 2023, ,JGGE) based on the oedometer test findings. The concept of virgin heating line and thermal elastic line were proposed following the Yin and Graham’s 1D EVP model with equivalent time concept. Later, a 3D TEVP model (Chen et al. 2023 CGJ) was developed based on the 1D model and the critical state framework, the overstress theory, with consideration of structured soils and anisotropic plasticity. The 1D and 3D TEVP model have been validated with a number of test data, including CRS tests and triaxial tests with various temperature and stress paths for both different clayey soils. 4. We developed a series of large-strain thermal consolidation models based on Gibson’s consolidation theory, considering the thermal elastoplastic constitutive model or thermal elastic visco-plastic constitutive model, self-weight of soil, nonlinear hydraulic conductivity, and compressibility during the consolidation process, heat conduction, and heat convection process. These models include one-dimensional, two-dimensional, three-dimensional, and radial models. To facilitate the use of these established and verified models, an automatic calculation platform was programmed to include all of the above-mentioned models into a .exe file for direct use purposes. We also propose a radial consolidation model considering smear effects under free strain conditions. This study points out the issue of solving the consolidation model in the previous research and gives a numerical solution to this problem followed by analysing the effect of smear effects on consolidation behaviour. Last but not least, we have proposed the theory of unified drainage boundary for saturated and unsaturated soil and program a graphical user interface for potential users to conduct consolidation analysis. The above-mentioned numerical models have been used to simulate physical model tests conducted in Objective 1. The computation results are well in line with the measurement. Parametric studies were then carried out to investigate the thermal consolidation of slurries under different conditions. 5. Through the physical and numerical modelling in this study, a better understanding on the consolidation of bentonite slurry with prefabricated drains and heating is achieved. It is suggested to use PHDs for the soft slurry during the filling or construction, followed with PVDs which can avoid significant bending. Besides, it is suggested that using a moderate temperature around forty degree is helpful and efficient for real applications. The influence of temperature is significant, especially on the vacuum pressure conduction and the non-uniform consolidation of the slurry, apart from the change of permeability. All these aspects should be considered in the real application of thermo-vacuum preloading of bentonite slurry.

15213019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213019.value: We successfully conducted a pilot multi-scale investigations on the bentonite clay slurry under effects of heating and vacuum preloading. The micro- and macro-characteristics of smectite clays have been revealed through the experiments, from SEM, MIP, oedometer, triaxial, to physical model tests. The influence and mechanisms of different temperature on the vacuum preloading of bentonite slurry has been studied. A new constitutive model (T-EVP) has been developed and verified for considering thermal and creep effects of clays. Fully coupled and simple methods that integrate the T-EVP model in 1D and 2D consolidation analysis have been developed and applied for a series of cases. More than 10 research articles have been published in reputable journals under the research topic and financial support of this project. Although affected by the COVID pandemic, we still present our research findings in several impactful local and international conferences.

15213019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213019.value: Future studies may focus on: 1) field-scale tests and applications for thermo-vacuum preloading of bentonite/dredged marine deposits slurries; 2) more energy-efficient heating schemes and technologies for the PVDs and PHDs; 3) micro-scale quantification on the thermal effects on clay behaviour, such as molecular dynamics and coarse-grain molecular dynamics simulations; 4) constitutive and numerical models considering the fine particle migration under vacuum pressure and the locally unsaturated zones at the surface and under high temperature.

15213019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213019.value: In this study, we proposed and developed a technology for fast treatment of bentonite slurry with vacuum preloading and heating using prefabricated band drains. It is found that under higher temperature, the consolidation is faster and the soil is denser in a shorter time of treatment, and the proposed technology is effective and promising in treating the soft bentonite slurries. The work has been widely recognized by academia and attracted researchers worldwide. With the success of this method, the waste slurry or dredged marine deposits can be treated efficiently and turned into construction materials to save cost and time for infrastructure development and environmental conservation of our cities.

15213219.value: To propose a novel IEC with suitable hydrophilic coating, hydrophobic coating and a condensate drainage system to improve its energy recovery performance in hot and humid regions. An analytical heat and mass transfer model will be developed first for describing the actual heat and mass transfer with and without condensation and sprayed water films on both sides of the IEC channels. To develop experiment-based semi-empirical models for predicting the wettability ratios in the secondary air channels with and without the hydrophilic coatings and to develop experiment-based semi-empirical models for predicting the thickness of condensate water film in the primary air channels with and without the hydrophobic coating of the proposed IEC. Based on the above analytical and experimental models, a comprehensive heat and mass transfer model of the novel IEC will be developed by incorporating wettability ratio and thickness of condensate water film parameters. The simulation results will be validated by lab experiments. A final report will be completed from the above findings. The optimum design parameters, design guidelines and operational guidelines enabling the use of the IEC energy recovery technology will be summarized.
