15213219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213219.value: The indirect evaporative cooler (IEC) is a sustainable cooling device consisting of alternative primary air and secondary air channels. Water sprayed into the secondary channels to cool the channel separating walls with the aid of water evaporation and reversed secondary air flow. The adjacent primary air is then sensibly cooled. The IEC can be used as a high-efficient energy recovery device which pre-cools fresh air using exhaust air from air-conditioned spaces in buildings. Based on our previous studies, energy saving by an IEC is promising, especially in hot and humid subtropical regions. Because of the high humidity of fresh air, condensation is very likely to occur in the primary channels of an IEC. The condensation improves the total heat transfer rate. However, some problems have been identified. Firstly, poor wetting in the secondary air channels was found in lab tests, resulting in much lower operating cooling efficiency than expected. More seriously, condensate water accumulated in the primary air channels degrades the overall heat transfer process. Lastly, although some performance correlations based on experimental regressions were developed in our previous studies, some other key operational parameters, such as surface wettability and thickness of the condensate water film, were not taken into account, resulting in relatively large discrepancies with the real cases. To solve the problems, a novel IEC with hydrophilic coating, hydrophobic coating and a condensate drainage system is proposed for investigations in this project. The secondary air channel wall surfaces will be coated with hydrophilic coatings to improve the surface wettability and the primary air channel wall surfaces with hydrophobic coatings for better condensate drainage. A drainage channel removes the condensate water to avoid water accumulation. The project team will investigate the enhanced performance of this novel IEC, in which condensate from the primary air may take place. Experiment-based semi-empirical models for predicting the wettability ratio and thickness of condensate water films in both non-coated and coated IECs will be deduced and a complete simulation model for the heat and mass transfer processes of the novel IEC will be developed and validated by experiments. Comparative studies will be conducted to quantitatively evaluate the benefits of the new features. The outcomes of the research work will help promote the IEC energy recovery technology in hot and humid regions by overcoming the weakness of traditional IECs and a reliable simulation model will be developed for IECs' performance prediction, system evaluation and optimization. 間接蒸發冷卻器（IEC）是一種可持續型空氣冷卻裝置，由間隔佈置的一次空氣通道和二次空氣通道組成。其工作原理是將水噴淋到二次空氣通道中，在逆流的二次空氣下蒸發，通過蒸發過程吸收並帶走來自通道壁面的熱量，從而冷卻相鄰通道中的一次空氣。 IEC可作為高效能量回收裝置應用於建築物的空調系統中，通過回收空調房間回風中的能量來預冷新風。研究表明，IEC具有顯著的節能潛力，並在炎熱和潮濕的亞熱帶地區效果更佳。在這些地區，室外新風具有較高的濕度，在IEC的一次空氣通道中會發生冷凝。冷凝現象提高了IEC的總熱交換量，但是卻存在一些新的問題。第一，實驗測試結果表明二次空氣通道的潤濕性差，IEC實際運行時的冷卻效率比預期低。第二，由於冷凝水累積在一次空氣通道中，大大降低了相鄰通道之間的傳熱效率。第三，大量研究通過實驗驗證了IEC性能變化及影響因素，但是沒有考慮到一些關鍵的運行參數，例如板表面潤濕度、冷凝水膜的厚度等，與實際情況存在較大差異。為了解決這些問題，本項目提出了一種具有親水塗層、疏水塗層和冷凝水排水系統的新型IEC。在二次空氣通道壁面使用親水塗層，以改善表面潤濕性；在一次空氣通道壁面使用疏水塗層，以促進冷凝水的劃落、避免增加熱阻。另外，在IEC中設置了排水通道，以快速排出冷凝水、避免積水。本項目團隊將對這種新型IEC的性能進行研究，並考慮發生在一次空氣中的冷凝過程。包括：基於實驗結果推導半經驗模型，用於預測在非塗層和塗層的IEC通道中壁面潤濕度和冷凝水膜厚度的變化；開發並通過實驗驗證新的完整的傳熱和傳質過程模型。並通過對比研究，對新型IEC的性能進行定量評價。本研究工作的成果克服了傳統IEC的弱點，將有助於在炎熱和潮濕地區推廣IEC能量回收技術，並將為IEC性能預測、系統評估和優化，開發可靠的模擬模型。

15213219.label: Realisation of objectives
15213219.value: The five objectives have been successfully accomplished, and the specific details can be elaborated upon through the following five points respectively. 1) To address the issue of condensation occurring in the dry channels of IEC operating in hot and humid regions, where the primary air comes into contact with surfaces below its dew point temperature, application of hydrophobic coatings on the surface of dry channels has been tested. The hydrophobic coatings, in conjunction with a condensate drainage system, help reduce the accumulation of condensate on the surface, thereby enhancing convective heat transfer in the IEC. Furthermore, the addition of hydrophilic coatings to the wet channel of the IEC optimizes the distribution of water film on the surface, alleviates shrinkage issues, and increases the evaporative heat transfer area, thus improving the energy performance of the IEC. 2) In order to enhance the energy recovery performance of IEC in hot and humid regions, a comprehensive research effort was conducted. Initially, a 2D simulation model was developed to accurately depict the heat and mass transfer phenomena within an IEC, accounting for potential condensation and water film formation on both sides of the IEC channels. Additionally, to reduce computational time associated with iterative processes in the indirect evaporative cooling energy recovery system (ERIEC), which typically rely on numerical approaches, a novel statistical modelling approach was established. This approach allows for the evaluation of the ERIEC performance in hot and humid regions, incorporating a decision tree model that determines the occurrence of condensation based on inlet air temperature and relative humidity conditions. Subsequently, a 2-level factorial design was implemented to establish correlations between ERIEC performance indicators under non-condensing and condensing states, respectively. The developed models can be seamlessly integrated into existing simulation tools, providing a reliable means for predicting the performance of ERIEC auxiliary air-conditioning systems for building energy assessments. 3) To optimize the distribution of the water film in the wet channel and further enhance the heat recovery performance of IEC, a 3D CFD model was developed. This model describes the motion of spray droplets and the formation and flow behaviour of the water film on the surface of the plates, taking into account the actual wetting factor of the wet channel surface. To validate the simulation model, a visualization experimental setup of an IEC wet channel was established to observe and record the distribution of the water film on the heat exchanger plates. Subsequently, based on the validated model, an analysis was conducted on whether hydrophilic coatings should be applied to the secondary air channel of the IEC. It was found that adding hydrophilic coatings to the wet channel surface of the IEC can improve the uniformity of droplet distribution by reducing the contact angle between the droplets and the heat exchange surface, thereby optimizing the distribution of the water film. The results showed that the contact angle on the wet channel walls with the hydrophilic coating decreased by 20° compared to using traditional epoxy resin coatings, and the coverage of the water film increased by 14.5%. Therefore, the improvement mechanism of hydrophilic coatings in an IEC is based on optimizing the contact state between water droplets and the heat exchanger walls, thereby expanding the contact area and mass transfer area between the water film and the secondary airflow. This leads to an increased contact area between water and the plate surface, effectively increasing the available surface area for evaporation. In addition, by employing a visualization technique to observe the evolution process of condensation droplets on the heat exchanger plate surface within the dry channel, the dynamic behaviour of primary air condensation and its impact on the convection and overall heat transfer rate of the IEC system are experimentally investigated. This approach integrates the analysis methods of contact angle and droplet volume to explore the dynamic behaviour of primary air condensation, a topic that has been rarely explored in existing studies. Subsequently, by analysing the effect of condensate accumulation on convective heat flux, the surface characteristics of the heat exchanger are examined. The findings demonstrate that enhancing convective heat transfer in IEC can be achieved by modifying the surface materials to minimize the accumulation of condensate mass on the plate surface. This provides a foundation for the application of hydrophobic coatings on the plate surface of the primary air channel, thereby improving the condensate drainage performance. Moreover, utilizing visual observation and measurement data, an analytical model and experimental investigation of condensation heat transfer in IEC under varying dehumidification conditions are proposed. An image processing technique is developed to quantify the area ratio of dropwise condensation (DWC) and filmwise condensation (FWC) on the plate surface. It is concluded that the relative humidity of the primary air significantly impacts the overall heat flux on the plate surface, as the increase in FWC under high relative humidity leads to a reduction in the growth rate of the heat transfer coefficient. This finding serves as a valuable reference for enhancing heat transfer in air-conditioning systems through the promotion of dropwise condensation. 4) The influence of surface wettability on the cooling potential of IEC has been a key focus of numerical studies. However, in practical wetting conditions, it is rare to represent them with a single, constant value of surface wettability. Therefore, based on the aforementioned analysis and experimental models, the ANSYS ICEM program was used to construct a numerical mesh model. Considering temperature, humidity, heat transfer, and mass transfer, a comprehensive heat and mass transfer model for the novel IEC with the integrated spray system was developed. This model simulated the dynamic processes of droplet generation from the nozzles and the accompanying water film along the surface, while predicting the operational performance of the IEC. To validate the model, a complete IEC test rig comprising primary air channel, secondary air channel, and spray system was established. The developed numerical model was successfully validated through experimental results, enabling further parameter analysis and optimization of IEC performance. The results demonstrate that the optimization of the contact state between water droplets and the heat exchanger walls in the IEC effectively mitigates the shrinkage effect of the water film. This optimization leads to an expanded contact area and mass transfer area between the water film and the secondary air, consequently increasing the available surface area for evaporation. As a result, the wet-bulb efficiency of the IEC is enhanced, and the overall heat exchange capacity is significantly improved. 5) Based on the aforementioned research findings, all the proposed objectives have been achieved successfully. The optimal design strategy for energy recovery of IEC applications in humid and hot regions can be summarized as the optimal design targeting two aspects: the primary air channels and the secondary air channels. The hydrophobic coating in the primary channels' plate surface can help facilitate the condensation of water droplets and enhance the discharge capability of condensate in the IEC. Utilizing hydrophilic coating in the secondary channels can optimize the contact state between liquid droplets and the heat exchanger walls, which can significantly improve the wet-bulb efficiency of the IEC system.

15213219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213219.value: The major findings and research outcome are as follows: 1) A simulation model has been developed to describe the actual heat and mass transfer conditions in the IEC channels, considering the presence or absence of condensation and water film from spray. Additionally, a predictive model for the wetting ratio in wet channels has been established. The models are integrated with wetting ratio and condensate film thickness to create a comprehensive heat and mass transfer model for the novel IEC. 2) It has been observed that the relative humidity of the primary air significantly affects the overall heat flux on the plate surface, as an increase in relative humidity leads to a decrease in the growth rate of heat transfer coefficient due to the increased FWC. This finding provides valuable insights for enhancing heat transfer in air conditioning systems by promoting DWC. 3) Then, the surface characteristics of the heat exchanger have been studied by analysing the impact of condensate accumulation on convective heat flux. The results indicate that the convective heat transfer of the IEC can be enhanced by reducing the amount of condensate trapped on the plate surface through changes in surface materials. This provides a basis for applying hydrophobic coatings on the plate surface in the primary air channel to improve condensate drainage performance. 4) Moreover, it has been clearly demonstrated that IEC with hydrophobic coatings exhibits better sensible cooling and dehumidification performance when handling fresh air due to its enhanced condensate drainage capabilities. The coated IEC shows an improvement of 11.8% in wet-bulb efficiency and an average dehumidification enhancement of 13.1% compared to uncoated IEC. The thermal resistance performance of the coated IEC for energy recovery increases by 8.5-17.2% under different inlet conditions. 5) The study further demonstrates that the distribution of moisture in the wet channel has a significant impact on the wetted area, film thickness, and heat/mass transfer efficiency of the IEC. Moreover, the improvement in surface wetting properties of the IEC primarily relies on the effective moisture diffusion rate of the plate material. 6) Last, it has been discovered that the addition of hydrophilic coatings on the plate surface in the wet channel reduces the contact angle between water droplets and the plate surface, weakening the film contraction effect and increasing the water film coverage. Compared to traditional aluminium plate IECs, the water film coverage and COP have increased by 14.5% and 7.4%, respectively.

15213219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213219.value: Based on current research, it has been observed that the adoption of hydrophilic materials in the secondary air channel can significantly improve the wetting factor and enhance the performance of the IEC. Additionally, porous materials, with their high porosity and excellent water storage characteristics, are increasingly being utilized in heat exchangers. Therefore, leveraging the comprehensive heat and mass transfer model of the novel IEC, which incorporates parameters such as wetting ratio and condensate film thickness, further analysis can be conducted to investigate the improvement of the wetting factor in the secondary air channel by employing porous materials for optimizing the overall performance of the IEC. Moreover, by combining the water storage capabilities of porous materials in the IEC and optimizing the spray strategy, it is possible to achieve lower energy consumption and higher efficiency to a greater extent. In addition, optimization of the water spray system of an IEC system is also important for optimizing the total energy efficiency of the IEC. We will focus on these two aspects for future studies in this area.

15213219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213219.value: An analytical heat and mass transfer model has been developed from this project for describing the actual heat and mass transfer with and without condensation and sprayed water films on both sides of IEC channels. Application of hydrophobic and hydrophilic coatings on IEC channel surfaces to optimize the performance of the IEC has been tested for a hot and humid weather condition and for the operating characteristics of the dry and wet channels, respectively. Firstly, a simulation model is developed to describe the condensation effect in the dry channel of the IEC, and a CFD model is developed to simulate the spraying and water film distribution in the wet channel. Then experimental benches were built separately to validate the simulation results of the models and to confirm the usability of the developed models. Finally, the validated models were used to analyse the heat and mass transfer with and without hydrophobic and hydrophilic coatings and the performance improvement of the IEC. The results are very good and the nanocoating can significantly improve the heat and mass transfer in the IEC. These findings provide optimized references and guidance for future academic research and engineering applications in the field.

15213319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213319.value: The building sector represents over 40% of global energy consumption and is a major consumer of grid electrical power. Accurate characterization and modeling of building energy dynamics is a key fundamental problem of improving building energy efficiency and grid reliability. With the dramatic increase in the scales and complexity of modern buildings, it has become increasingly challenging. Building dynamic behavior is the result of the joint effect of all interactions between building envelope, energy systems, controls, occupants and climate conditions. Big building operation data are stored in building automation systems (BASs), which represent the real building dynamic behavior under various disturbances and interactions. This research adopts the data-driven/inverse approach to learn building energy dynamics from building operation data. Different from the forward approach, which models building dynamics based on physical principles and needs elaborate details of building, occupancy and systems, the data-driven approach requires little a priori knowledge of system configurations and interactions and is computationally efficient owing to the advances in data analytics and high-performance computing. It is promising for online control optimization applications in large complex buildings in this respect. This research aims to develop a generalizable big data-driven methodology based on temporal data mining and machine learning for characterizing and modeling the energy dynamics of large complex buildings using big multivariate time series BAS data. The methodology comprises actionable procedures, customized data analytic methods and software tools. The project will make the following new contributions to the R&D of data-driven approach and building dynamics: i) make the best use of the big building operation data; ii) enhance the applicability of data-driven models in wider/full range of building operating conditions; iii) properly handle numerical and categorical data and seasonality in long time series; iv) define new representations of dynamics for characterizing energy dynamics of large complex buildings; and v) develop novel model evaluation metrics and model interpretation methods for data-driven approach. The data used to develop and test the methodology will be real data from large buildings. The project will bring a new paradigm for the data-driven approach, i.e. big data-driven approach, which is a valuable supplementary to existing methodologies to characterize and model building dynamics. The methodology provides methods and tools for online control optimization in BAS to improve building energy efficiency and grid response capability. In the long term, this project represents an important step on the road to smart and sustainable buildings and cities. 建築行業消耗了全球40%的能源，而且是電網的主要用戶。準確的表徵和模擬建築能源的動態特性是提升建築節能和電網穩定性的關鍵基礎問題。這個問題隨著現代建築的規模和複雜性不斷增加而變得更具挑戰性。 建築的動態反應是建築圍護結構、能源系統、控制系統、居住者和氣候環境共同作用的結果。存儲在建築物自動化系統（BAS）中的海量建築系統運行數據，是在各種幹擾和交互作用下的真實建築動態反應。本研究擬採用數據驅動/逆向方法從建築運行數據中學習建築能源的動態特性。數據驅動方法幾乎不需要系統和設備的信息及各種交互作用的先驗知識，並且計算效率高。由於數據分析和高性能計算技術的進步，數據驅動方法在大型複雜建築物中的在線控制優化應用中具有很大的潛力。 為利用BAS上的海量時序數據来表徵和模擬大型複雜建築及其能源系統的動態特性，本項目將基於數據挖掘和機器學習技術开发一种普适的大数据驱动的時序數據分析方法。這個方法包括可行的數據分析步驟和定制的數據分析方法。本項目將為數據驅動方法和建築動態特性的研究做出如下新貢獻：1）有效利用建築運行大數據；2）提高數據驅動模型在更廣的運行工況下的適用性；3）有效的處理長時序數據包含的數值數據和分類數據以及季節性；4）為大型複雜建築定義新的能源動態特性表徵參數；5）為數據驅動模型開發新的評價指標。本項目將採用實際大型建築的數據來開發和驗證研究成果。 本項目將為表徵和模擬建築動態特性帶來一種新的數據驅動方法，即大數據驅動方法，為以提升建築節能和電網穩定性為目的的建築能源系統在線優化控制提供大數據分析方法。長遠來說，本項目有助於推動智慧和可持續建築和城市的發展。

15213319.label: Realisation of objectives
15213319.value: All objectives have been fully achieved. Objective 1: Select and customize data analytics algorithms and procedures for analyzing big multivariate time-series BAS data by conducting case studies on real building operation data Critical and comprehensive investigation of state-of-the-art data analytics algorithms and procedures were conducted on the multivariate time series BAS data retrieved from International Commerce Center (ICC) which is the tallest building in Hong Kong, education buildings in the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, education buildings in Politecnico di Torino in Italy, and open-source building datasets (e.g., Building data genome project, Chicago Energy Benchmarking). The data analytics algorithms investigated included pattern recognition, clustering analysis (e.g., “Follow the Leader” clustering, K-means clustering), and machine learning-based predictive modeling (e.g., artificial neural network, classification and regression tree). BAS data are usually saved in two-dimensional data table with x-axis representing different variables at the same time instant and y-axis representing samples at different time instants. The BAS data were analyzed as cross-sectional data (along x-axis), multivariate time series (along y-axis), and multi-relational data (multiple tables) using different data analytics algorithms. The typical challenges of analyzing big multivariate time-series BAS data include high dimensionality, multivariate time series, multiple scales, different types (numerical vs. categorical), large volume and poor quality due to sensor faults and unreliable data transmission. Data analytics procedures and methods aiming at each problem were developed to enhance the quality and reliability of data analysis results. Detecting and replacing punctual inconsistencies (e.g., missing values, global and local outliers) were accomplished by a data preprocessing module. Data transformation methods based on one-hot encoding, Symbolic Aggregate approximate (SAX) and frequency analysis were developed to prepare appropriate data format for subsequent tasks, and transform numerical time series into series symbols based on its statistical properties therefore reducing the data dimensionality and allowing for efficient analysis. Objective 2: Develop temporal data mining-based methods for identifying new representations of building energy dynamics, such as frequent sequential patterns, temporal associations and time lags between the operations of major equipment and indoor and outdoor disturbances for large complex buildings Based on the analysis of multivariate time series BAS data, temporal data mining-based methods were developed to extract typical and infrequent sequential building energy consumption patterns considering a daily time scale. A robust framework was proposed based on effective transformation of whole building energy consumption time series and pattern recognition techniques to handle inconsistent, infrequent, abnormal energy use in buildings/systems. Data reduction, transformation and machine learning methods (e.g., decision trees, symbolic aggregate approximation) were coupled and applied to discover unexpected patterns in electrical energy consumption data. A multi-step clustering process was implemented for different portions of each daily load profile in order to perform an advanced temporal abstraction of the time series and to enable an effective identification of infrequent patterns. The extracted sequential patterns were representative of the relation between different indoor and outdoor disturbances and energy demand, and valuable for automatic detection and identification of operation strategies and faults in building systems. Objective 3: Develop and compare a diversity of data-driven models for building energy dynamics using machine learning algorithms, and develop model evaluation metrics Data-driven building energy dynamic modeling has attracted increasing interest in recent years as it requires little a priori knowledge of buildings and building energy systems which cannot be easily obtained in large modern buildings. While machine learning is becoming more powerful, the models developed, especially artificial neural networks like Recurrent Neural networks (RNN), are becoming more complex, resulting in “darker models” with lower model interpretability. This research project developed and compared a diversity of data-driven models for 24-hour ahead building cooling load prediction in terms of both model accuracy and model interpretability, including attention-based seq2seq recurrent neural network, multi-layer perceptron, and Long short-term memory (LSTM). The attention-based seq2seq recurrent neural network showed improved accuracy and interpretability compared with other models. The obtained attention vectors explained the model inference process and revealed crucial temporal information for understating the building dynamics. Objective 4: Test and implement the methodology in two important operation strategies in real buildings, i.e., the optimal chiller start-up/stop control to improve energy efficiency and building peak power limiting for grid reliability The proposed methodology was deployed and tested in the campus building of Hong Kong Polytechnic University via cloud platform for AI-enabled online building management. A building cooling load prediction model was developed and updated using real-time BAS data. The real-time data transmission (collection of building operation data and dispatch of control recommendations) was fulfilled by Influxdb database and BACnet protocol. A robust chiller sequencing control strategy was developed based on the building energy dynamic model to improve energy efficiency and avoid frequent switch (startups and shutdowns) of chillers. A daily demand limiting control strategy (using building thermal mass) was also tested on a chiller plant, where the peak demand limiting threshold was determined based on 5-days ahead building cooling load prediction and the building limiting capacity. The proposed methodology demonstrated effective and reliable performance in real applications.

15213319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213319.value: This project investigated and compared a number of data analytics and machine learning algorithms and procedures for analyzing big multivariate time-series BAS data. Specifically, this project developed a transfer learning-based model pre-train method to address the data scarcity issue and enhance the performance of data-driven models deployed in information-poor buildings. The method was evaluated using a large open-source building benchmark dataset. The major research findings include: 1) transfer learning method can significantly reduce the amount of training data required for most buildings and improve the model prediction performance; 2) the source buildings with similar building usage and industry as target buildings are recommended. This project developed an attention-based interpretable neural network for 24-hour ahead building cooling load prediction. The model was tested using real measurement data from a high-rise commercial building in Hong Kong. The major research findings include: 1) the attention-based model achieves improved accuracy and interpretability, which can be implemented in developing optimal operation control strategies and improving demand and supply management; 2) the obtained attention vectors can depict the influence of different model inputs on the prediction result and provide interesting temporal information for understanding building thermal dynamics, which helps the users to understand why predictions are made by the model. Accurate building cooling load and energy consumption prediction is fundamental for reducing building energy consumption and improving the reliability of the building-grid eco-system. This project developed a temporal data mining-based methods for the detection and diagnosis of anomalous building daily energy patterns, including anomalies and rare events. The proposed tool was evaluated on a university campus in Italy. The major research findings include: 1) the detection tool can support building managers to early recognize abnormal evens avoiding their protraction over a long time, and lead to a significant reduction of energy waste; 2) by hyperparameter finetuning, the achieved detection rate of anomalous daily load profiles is high, and the false alarm rate is low enough to consider the procedure and procedure robust and reliable if implemented on real building energy management systems. This project developed a machine learning-based building performance benchmarking framework with improved generalization and interpretability. The major research outcomes include: 1) a reliable and convenient data augmentation approach is established to overcome the data imbalance problem while avoiding the overfitting problem; 2) a complete rating framework is proposed, with proper explanations of results at sample level.

15213319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213319.value: Future works on transfer learning will be aimed at proper similarity measurement between source and target buildings to contour the range of application of transfer learning. A standardized evaluation framework of transfer learning techniques in different building engineering tasks will be developed for performance benchmarking. Future works on the data analytics-based FDD tool will be aimed at extending the tool capabilities and testing the process on other data sets for benchmarking purposes. The capability of this tool will be enhanced in terms of recognizing new kinds of anomalies or rare events and optimally scheduling the re-training of the prediction models. A visualization will be conceived and developed for supporting different actors (e.g., energy manager, users) in enhancing their awareness of building operation saving energy and costs. Future works on the attention-based building cooling load prediction model will be aimed at more complex model architecture, such as implementing attention mechanism on temporal and spatial dimensions via multi-layer multi-head attention. Besides soft attention adopted in this project, the effectiveness of other categories of attention mechanism (including hard attention and local attention) will also be investigated.

15213319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213319.value: This research project aimed to improve building energy performance by making full use of large-volume building operation data based on advanced data analytics and machine learning techniques to model the energy dynamics of large complex buildings. Accurate and robust models and tools were developed for modeling energy dynamics of building operations, identifying anomalous building energy patterns, and enhancing building control. Additionally, the explainable building energy performance benchmarking framework developed can reflect details in individual buildings and assist the policymakers in identifying the improvement potential for retrofit measures. This research project also addressed the data scarcity issue (lack of sufficient representative training data), real-time processing of high-dimensional data streams, and low model interpretability issue of complex machine learning models in modeling building energy dynamics. The developed models and tools are scalable, configurable and interpretable, which can continuously assist building engineers and maintainers in evidence-based decision-making. The research outcomes can contribute to reduction of energy consumption and carbon emission, and improvement of building control performance and reliability of the building-grid eco-system.

15213619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213619.value: Digital thermal imaging based on the integration of Infrared (IR) lenses and a focal-plane array of microbolometers has many potential applications in modern society but remains expensive. This is mainly due to the high cost of the lens materials required (e.g., monocrystalline germanium) and the manufacturing process associated (e.g., single-point diamond turning). Since the beginning of this century, Chalcogenide glasses (ChGs) have been used as replacements for crystalline IR materials for lens fabrication owing to their low cost of synthesis and excellent IR transmittance. More importantly, these amorphous materials have a low glass transition point (Tg), which facilitates mass production based on Precision Lens Molding (PLM) technology. However, ChGs are more difficult to mold than oxide glasses because of their low strength and toughness that arises from their weak and directional covalent bonds. To avoid fracture, molding must therefore be conducted at a much higher temperature than Tg, which causes adhesion, evaporation, oxidation, and high-level residual stresses, which significantly impairs the surface quality and the optical performance of the resulting molded lens. Additionally, the need for a large aperture to achieve sufficient IR intensity means that IR lenses are generally aspherical with large curvatures, and sometimes have surface steps to reduce thickness, which results in additional difficulty in implementing PLM technology. In a comparative study on the vibration responses of ChGs and oxide glasses, we noted that the amplitude decay rate of the former was much larger than that of the latter at the same viscosity level, indicating a pronounced frequency-dependence of the relaxation rate of ChGs. In addition, it was found that ultrasonic loading could assist the nucleation of nanocrystals, which can improve the toughness of ChGs without degrading their IR transmittance. These findings inspired us to introduce ultrasonic oscillation into the PLM process to reduce the molding temperature and thus improve the quality of molded ChG lenses. In addition, we shall also explore the minimum surface feature size that can be achieved using ultrasound-assisted PLM (UAPLM), which may allow molded flat IR lenses with wavelength-scale surface structures to focus light. To realize a dedicated UAPLM technology for ChGs, we propose to start with the physics-based models describing nontrivial relaxation and crystallization behaviors of ChGs, then to validate and parameterize theoretical models based on controlled experiments, and finally to design and validate several UAPLM processes based on numerical simulation and actual molding experiments, respectively. 由紅外鏡頭和焦平面微熱輻射儀陣列整合而成的數位熱像儀有著廣泛的應用。然而其紅外鏡頭須由單點金剛石車削晶體材料（例如單晶鍺）製成，因此成本十分高昂，且難以通過大規模生產降低。本世紀初，熱輻射穿透性更好的硫系玻璃開始取代晶態紅外材料用於生產紅外鏡頭。硫系玻璃的成本低廉，且由於較低的玻璃轉變溫度而適合精密模壓製造。模壓製造技術適宜大規模生產，因此有望大幅降低熱像儀的成本。但是，相較於氧化物玻璃，硫系玻璃的硬度和韌性都比較差，容易在模壓過程中開裂。為此，模壓過程通常要在具有較低粘度的高溫度範圍進行，又造成了材料的汽化、氧化，和磨具的粘合，以及鏡頭中較高的殘餘應力。此外，紅外透鏡通常具有較大的曲率，甚至階梯狀表面，這也提高硫系玻璃透鏡模壓製造的難度。 在一項硫系玻璃與氧化物玻璃對比的研究中，我們發現硫系玻璃的應力鬆弛有極強的頻率依賴性：即外加的頻率越高，應力鬆弛得越快。這意味著高頻振盪可以降低模壓壓力，提高硫系玻璃的可塑性。同時，高頻的振盪載荷有利於玻璃中納米晶的析出；這些納米晶可以在不損失透光性的情況下提高玻璃的強度和韌性。這些發現啟發我們在模壓過程中引入超聲振盪以提高硫系玻璃的模壓品質，甚至可以通過超聲精密模壓製造小於紅外波長的表面微結構，以改善成像品質。因此，我們將發展硫系玻璃複雜鬆弛和結晶過程的物理模型，並通過實驗驗證和參數化這一模型，最終實現硫系玻璃超聲模壓的模擬，設計，和初步應用。

15213619.label: Realisation of objectives
15213619.value: The research progress as planned in the proposal was significantly influenced by the pandemic of Covid-19 because the project period (2020.1 - 2023.6) overlapped with the pandemic. Hence, we used the funding to support more theoretical developments and achieved some interesting findings and several publications (cf. Part C). These findings are elaborated hereunder according to the objectives. (i) To establish a physics-based model describing the non-linear viscoelastic behavior of chalcogenide glasses The establishment of the theoretical model of chalcogenide glass (ChG) has been completed. It is found that the concerned ChGs (As2Se3, Ge28Se60Sb12 and Ge25Se60Sb15) have a relatively simple relaxation behaviour because the time-dependent decay of their Young’s modulus can be described by a simple exponential decay function (cf. publications [2, 3] in part C). Hence, the viscoelastic model of ChG can be simplified to be a Maxwell model describing its stress relation. We have also developed a model based on a Monte Carlo (approximate) solution of master equations describing the variation of occupancy of the minima of a potential energy landscape (PEL) for a chalcogenide glass (ChG). As the model provides a way to connect the atomistic picture of ChG, i.e., the mechanically stable arrangements of a covalent network, and the variations of macroscopic properties, e.g., specific volume, Young’s modulus, and enthalpy, it has excellent extensionality to describe non-linear viscoelastic behavior. That is, the stress-dependent viscous behavior, the main target to be unveiled by this proposed research, can be described to be a stress-induced decay in the height of a hopping barrier between two minima because a stressed network structure must have higher potential energy than a stress-free network. In this case, stress causes a higher relaxation rate and thus a smaller apparent viscosity, or correspondingly, the viscosity becomes rate-dependent at a temperature. While this project focuses on chalcogenide glasses, we also developed theoretical models for other brittle materials with the financial support (partially) of this project. Oxidation and corrosion happen in ChG at elevated temperatures; therefore, the mechanochemical modeling is related. In particular, we developed mechano-electrochemical phase-field models to describe the process of cracking under both electrochemical and mechanical forces. These efforts led to the journal publications [1, 4, 5] listed in Part C. The PI also organized a symposium in MRS annual meeting to lead the discussion on this topic. (ii) To validate and parameterize the theoretical model The simple relaxation of ChG in terms of the variation of its Young’s modulus leads to the discovery that glass transition is likely a transition on the convergence of the relaxation time. We found that there existed a critical temperature Tp. Above Tp, the relaxation time was history-independent, and below Tp, the relaxation time became dependent on thermal history. This interesting finding leads to the publication [2] in Part C. With our model, this unusual experimental result can be well described, which, simply put, is caused by the difficulty to jump out of a deep basin in the PEL. Other than that, the structural relaxation based on the time-and-temperature-dependent results of Young’s modulus can be employed to parameterize the model. For a non-linear (or non-Newtonian) stress relaxation behavior, further experiments based on dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) were conducted. However, we encountered difficulty in the experiments as the ChG is very fragile. ChG samples were easily broken during the test or even when a sample was loaded. This is probably the reason that the literature DMA data of ChG is very rare; we cannot obtain any results of frequency sweep at elevated temperatures for a ChG. Hence, we conducted direct molding experiments using a self-developed glass molding device. This device cost most of the efforts in the reporting period. Fortunately, the comparison between the experimental and numerical results indicated consistency. Hence, the proposed viscoelastic model can be adaptable. (iii) To explore the feasibility of ultrasound-assisted nucleation of nanocrystals We determined the crystallization temperature and the kinetics of crystallization by observing the increase of Young’s modulus when a ChG sample was heated. For this study, we have chosen (purchased) Ge28Se60Sb12 which is more easily crystallized than As2Se3. We developed a theoretical model to estimate the temperature-dependent crystallization rate of the glass based on the increase in Young’s modulus. In addition, the observations using a transmission electron microscope (TEM) confirmed the formation of nanocrystals in heated glass. Furthermore, we found that the nanocrystals did not impair the infrared transparency of the glass, instead, the transparency of the glass with nanocrystals was improved in comparison with the original glass. Unfortunately, we did not find that ultrasound can assist crystallization. This is partially caused by the unavailability of ultrasound-assisted molding device to us during the pandemic period. We strived to develop our own ultrasound-assisted molding device in the reporting period, but it is still under development. A related side product of this project is that we also studied a peculiar crystal-amorphous-crystal two-step phase transition in a metastable alloy and developed and parameterized a theoretical model to describe such a solid-state phase transformation. This work led to the journal publication [6] in Part C. (iv) To establish a computational model to assist the design of ultrasound-assisted precision lens molding The computational model has been established as it only involves the effort to code the proposed model of ChG to be a subroutine of a commercial finite element package (e.g., ABAQUS). This subroutine is essentially identical to the code we have developed for Objective 1 to study heterogeneous relaxation. The difficulty lies in experiments to verify the model. Owing to the travel restriction, we could not go to the CI’s laboratory in Beijing, China to conduct experiments on ultrasound-assisted lens molding and we were later informed their ultrasound-assisted molding system was broken. Therefore, we focused on developing an in-house ultrasound-assisted hot embossing system on our own. Other than the development of the device, we have also conducted the following related developments. We developed molds for hot embossing by using glassy carbon. The reason is that glassy carbon has excellent stability and chemical inertness at high temperatures, which could be the ultimate mold material for precision glass molding. In addition, glassy carbon is obtained through the pyrolysis of a polymeric precursor, which can be thermoformed to have various surface features. After pyrolysis, these features are downscaled. This opens a low-cost avenue to fabricate molds with microscopic surface features. We also studied possible coatings for glass molding and proposed Ru-Cr coatings. It is found that when the top Ru layer is thicker than 600 nm, a very thin and dense chromium oxide layer can form on the coating surface to prevent further oxidation or reaction with glass. This study led to the publication [6] in Part C.

15213619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213619.value: The efforts in this project led to the following findings: 1. Chalcogenide glass (As2Se3, Ge28Se60Sb12 and Ge25Se60Sb15) exhibits a simple exponential decay during relaxation. This allows an accurate determination of the temperature-dependent relaxation time and the finding that the relaxation kinetics can diverge when temperatures are lower than a critical temperature (c.f., journal publication [2]). 2. Crystallization in chalcogenide glass can occur at temperatures much lower than those determined through calorimetry. We suggest using the impulse excitation technique (IET) to problem the variation of Young’s modulus with temperature, which can lead to the knowledge of crystallization kinetics. In addition, it is found that the nanocrystals formed in the glass do not impair the infrared transparency but improve the hardness of the glass. (c.f., journal publication [3]) 3. Based on the phase-field approach, the fracture of brittle material can be modelled. This method was developed in this project and led to several publications (c.f., journal publications [1, 4, 5]). For example, we employed the model to simulate corrosion cracking in metals [1] and fracture caused by lithium-ion transport in solid electrolytes [4, 5]. These simulations allow researchers to look into the details of the failure process in mechano-electrochemical systems and thus develop strategies to reduce the probability of failure. 4. A crystalline-amorphous-crystalline two-step phase transformation was revealed using various experimental techniques (IET, TEM, and neutron diffraction) and theoretically modelled based on the master equations. This finding demonstrates that solid-state phase transformation can pass through a lattice collapse and recrystallization process in a material, which in the past was only revealed using model systems (e.g., colloidal systems). This finding leads to the publication [6].

15213619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213619.value: The objectives of this project were not all achieved due to the restrictions in experiments especially in the three years of the pandemic. We suggest and are also working on the following developments. (i) The experimental system for ultrasound-assisted molding/embossing Chalcogenide glasses have very broad applications in infrared optics (e.g., thermal imaging, optical switches, etc.). This project achieved theoretical models and simulations indicating that ultrasonic vibration could improve molding or embossing results. Hence, continuous efforts are needed to realize such an effect. (ii) Optical designs based on the hot embossing method In this project, we have conducted hot-embossing experiments to confirm the viability and the range feature height that can be achieved through hot embossing. However, we have not achieved any optical design using this manufacturing method. It is suggested that further research can combine optical designs and hot-embossing methods to achieve flat optical components for infrared/thermal imaging.

15213619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213619.value: Glass can be thermoformed to achieve precision geometry because heating leads to a transition from a solid to a liquid-like material. This principle also works for chalcogenide glasses which are compounds composed of the chalcogenide elements such as S, Se, and Te and their neighboring elements. This type of glass is transparent to far-infrared radiations and thus can be used to fabricate thermal imaging lenses. In this project, the researchers investigate the glass transition and crystallization phenomena of chalcogenide glass and found that crystallization can happen at temperatures much lower than those determined based on the measurement of latent-heat release. This finding indicates that in a thermoforming process with chalcogenide glass, crystals can nucleate in glass. Fortunately, the crystals are very small, with size of several nanometers. They do not impair infrared transparency but improve the hardness of the glass. With these results, it is possible to fabricate thermal imaging lenses through precision thermoforming and to strengthen the glass at the same time by inducing nanocrystals. This project also explored the effect of ultrasonic vibration on the forming quality. Researchers found that applying ultrasonic vibration can improve the glass-filling ratio into the holes in a mold surface.

15213719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15213719.value: Due to high payload to weight ratio, high speed and large workspace, cable-driven parallel mechanisms (CDPMs) are widely applied in the area of crane technology and camera positioning. Although intensive researches on CDPMs were carried out in recent years, no integrated method for topology and kinematic modeling and analysis has been proposed. Additionally, unlike under-constrained ones, limited topology structures of fully constrained CDPMs have been focused on. Besides the spatial CDPMs with six degree-of-freedoms (DoFs) and the planar ones with three DoFs, few sub-spatial and sub-planar lower-mobility fully constrained CDPMs have been reported till now. Aimed at providing a systematic framework for the design of CDPMs and inventing novel lower-mobility fully constrained CDPMs, a manifold based method for topology synthesis and kinematic analysis will be studied in this project. Firstly, the underlying relationships between CDPMs and conventional parallel mechanisms (PMs) with rigid limbs will be investigated, and the kinematic equivalences between them will be revealed. Based upon this, five-DoF constraint cables with fixed lengths will be introduced as the limbs of lower-mobility CDPMs, leading to the principles to construct non-overconstrained and non-redundant CDPMs. Secondly, by employing manifolds in finite screw form to model the finite motions generated by constraint cables and drive cables, general topology model of CDPM containing all its topological information will be formulated. On one hand, the obtained topology model can be used for type synthesis of CDPMs to invent new mechanisms; On the other hand, by regarding the model as displacement model, forward and inverse kinematics, as well as dimensional synthesis of CDPMs can be conducted. In the end, the topology model will be closely related to velocity and acceleration models for kinematic and dynamic analysis of CDPMs. The differential mappings among these models will be revealed, which unifies synthesis and analysis of CDPMs under a consistent mathematical framework of finite and instantaneous screw theory. Several new CDPMs will be invented during the implementation of this project. Among them, a four-DoF CDPM will be designed as a novel end-effector of a crane. Virtual prototype will be built using the SolidWorks® and ADAMS® software for performance and control simulation. Then, a physical prototype will be fabricated in cooperation with a Hong Kong crane company. Some experiments will be conducted on the prototype to further verify the theoretical and simulation results. This project has very important theoretical significance and application values for the innovative design of CDPMs. 由於有效載荷與自重比高、高速及大工作空間等優勢，繩驅動並聯機構被廣泛用於起重技術和相機定位等領域。近些年，儘管繩驅動並聯機構被大量研究，但現有研究尚未提出關於該類機構的拓撲與運動學建模和分析的集成方法。此外，僅有較少的完全約束繩驅動並聯機構的拓撲構型被發明和關注。與空間六自由度和平面三自由度繩驅動並聯機構不同，空間與平面少自由度完全約束繩驅動並聯機構很少被研究和報導。本項目以微分流形為數學工具，研究少自由度完全約束繩驅動並聯機構的拓撲與運動學建模和分析方法，旨在提出適用於該類機構創新設計的系統理論框架。首先，本項目研究繩驅動並聯機構與傳統剛性並聯機構之間的本質關聯，兩者間的運動學等效關係將被揭示。在此基礎上，通過引入繩長固定的五自由度約束纜繩作為少自由度繩驅動並聯機構的支鏈，給出非過約束、非冗餘驅動型機構的設計、構造準則。其次，以有限旋量格式的微分流形為數學工具，解析描述約束繩與驅動繩的有限運動，進而建立包含繩驅動並聯機構全部拓撲信息的通用拓撲模型。一方面，所建立的拓撲模型可直接用於開展該類機構的構型綜合研究，發明新的機構構型；另一方面，該模型可視為機構的位姿模型，據此開展其正、逆運動學分析，尺度綜合等研究。最後，繩驅動並聯機構拓撲模型、速度模型、加速度模型之間的微分映射關係將被揭示，由此將該類機構的綜合與分析研究統一在有限與瞬時旋量理論框架下。在本項目執行期內，將發明很多新的繩驅動並聯機構。其中，一種四自由度機構將被設計成起重機的新型末端執行器。本項目將利用SolidWorks®與ADAMS®軟件，建立該機構的虛擬樣機，開展其性能與控制仿真。在仿真基礎上，本項目研究團隊擬與香港起重機公司合作，建造該機構的微型物理樣機，將在樣機上開展相關實驗來進一步驗證理論與仿真結果。本項目在繩驅動並聯機構的創新設計方面具有重要的理論研究意義與實際應用價值。

15213719.label: Realisation of objectives
15213719.value: 1. We have derived the kinematic equivalences between cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) and conventional parallel robots by assigning virtual kinematic joints. The driving cables of CDPRs can be considered as an SPS kinematic chain connecting the base and the moving platform, where S indicates the spherical joint, and P indicates the prismatic joint. In this way, a spatial CDPR with six cables can be regarded to be a kinematic equivalence of a 6-SPS parallel robot. The kinematic and dynamic modeling and analysis techniques corresponding to conventional parallel robots are extended to the synthesis and analysis of CDPRs. 2. We have investigated two methods to introduce constraint cables for constituting lower-mobility CDPRs. The first method is to use cable-and-pulley differentials, which are mechanisms that couple and transmit the output of a single actuator to several cables. They can be used on CDPRs to introduce constraint cables and reduce the number of actuators. A novel type of cable-and-pulley differentials is designed by adding an extra pulley to eliminate the modeling inaccuracies due to the pulley radius and obviate the need of solving the complex model which considers the pulley kinematics. The second method is to construct cable parallelograms, which are composed of parallel cables driven by the same motor. When the parallel cables are in tension, the rotational motion of the moving platform about the normal direction of the parallelogram plane is constrained. The cable parallelograms are suitable for constructing lower-mobility CDPRs with constrained rotational motions. 3. We have proposed an integrated method for topology and kinematic synthesis and analysis of CDPRs and applied this method to develop novel CDPRs. The proposed method first conducts geometric synthesis, deriving all the robot geometries that can generate the desired sub-planar or sub-spatial motions. Then the kinematic and dynamic models of the feasible CDPRs are derived, and the singularity conditions are analyzed. Based on the derived models, the dimensional synthesis of CDPRs is conducted by optimizing multiple performance indices. Two new performance indices, static tension factor and interference number, are proposed to facilitate the dimensional synthesis. Finally, the performance of the obtained CDPRs is evaluated, and the former procedures are repeated until the desired performance is achieved. 4. By adopting the proposed synthesis and analysis method, we have developed two novel CDPRs. The first one is a planar CDPR driven by four cable-and-pulley differentials. The design parameters of the proposed CDPR are determined through multi-objective optimal design for the largest total orientation wrench closure workspace and the highest global stiffness magnitude index. The proposed differentially driven CDPR is evaluated by comparing various performance indices with a fully actuated CDPR, and the results show that the proposed CDPR has better performance in most of the aspects. The second one is a spatial CDPR constrained by cable parallelograms to generate Schönflies motions. The dimensional parameters of the proposed CDPR are determined through multi-objective optimal design. A numerical approach is adopted to calculate the large interference-free static workspace of the proposed robot. A prototype of the proposed robot is fabricated, and experimental tests are performed to evaluate the performance of the proposed robot. 5. We have explored the application of the proposed CDPRs to perform fast container handling tasks in automated ports. For CDPRs to manipulate heavy payloads such as large containers, the effects of cable weight and elasticity cannot be neglected. Thus, the elastic catenary cable model is integrated into the kinematic and dynamic models of the proposed CDPRs. Meantime, a time-optimal motion planning approach is investigated to calculate the fastest motions for the container handling tasks by exerting the maximum motion capability of CDPRs. Simulation results indicate that the proposed CDPRs are capable of performing fast container handling tasks in automated ports.

15213719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15213719.value: 1. An integrated method for topology and kinematic synthesis and analysis of CDPRs is proposed. The proposed method first conducts geometric synthesis, deriving all the robot geometries that can generate the desired sub-planar or sub-spatial motions. Then the kinematic and dynamic models of the feasible CDPRs are derived, and the singularity conditions are analyzed. Based on the derived models, the dimensional synthesis of CDPRs is conducted by optimizing multiple performance indices. 2. Two novel lower-mobility CDPRs are designed. The first one is a planar CDPR driven by four cable-and-pulley differentials. The proposed differentially driven CDPR is evaluated by comparing various performance indices with a fully actuated CDPR, and the results show that the proposed CDPR has better performance in most of the aspects. The second one is a spatial CDPR constrained by cable parallelograms to generate Schönflies motions. A prototype of the proposed robot is fabricated, and experimental tests are performed to evaluate the performance of the proposed robot. 3. A time-optimal motion planning approach is investigated to calculate the fastest motions of CDPRs for specified tasks subject to third-order constraints. The proposed method formulates the third-order time-optimal motion planning as a four-stage optimization involving only linear programming by exploiting the special structure of the problem. Simulation and experiment results indicate that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art approaches in terms of solution quality and computation time.

15213719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15213719.value: The proposed research has developed several lower-mobility CDPRs, while the topological structure of the developed CDPRs strongly depends on the way to introduce constraint cables. In future works, we will try to find more novel methods to introduce constraint cables. Since the kinematic chains of CDPRs are simplex, we need to couple the motions of multiple driving cables in order to introduce constraints. The novel combinations of constraint cables will derive new topologies of lower-mobility CDPRs. Moreover, the special structure of lower-mobility CDPRs also complicates the robot control system. To further improve the motion tracking performance, we will develop a robust control framework for the proposed CDPRs. A hierarchical robust control framework that consists of a high-level pose controller for the moving platform and a low-level torque controller for the actuators will be designed to resist model uncertainties and external disturbances. For the high-level control loop, we will adopt model predictive control to regulate the pose of the moving platform. For the low-level torque control of actuators, we will propose to use adaptive terminal sliding mode control to handle model uncertainties and external disturbances.

15213719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15213719.value: This project proposes an integrated method to design and analyze lower-mobility cable-driven parallel robots (CDPRs) by synthesizing the kinematic equivalences between CDPRs and conventional parallel robots. Two novel approaches to adding constraint cables into CDPRs are developed, and several novel robot structures are investigated to complement the field of lower-mobility CDPRs with sub-planar and sub-spatial motions. A prototype of the proposed novel CDPR is fabricated, and experimental tests indicate that the proposed robot has good performance. The motion planning approach is also investigated to generate the fastest motions of the robot by exerting the maximum motion capability. This project has both theoretical and practical benefits for improving the performance and expanding the application of CDPRs.

15214019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214019.value: The use of sustainable energy sources, such as solar energy, to generate hydrogen from water splitting is always a dream of humankind to produce a clean energy source. In this project, we propose to generate hydrogen through water splitting by making use of the pyro-catalytic effect. Lead-free BaTiO3-based ferroelectric nanoparticles will act as the pyro-catalysts. When the temperature is changed, the spontaneous polarization of the ferroelectric nanoparticle will change, which results in uncompensated surface charges and a pyroelectric voltage across the two oppositely polarized surface of the nanoparticle. Those pyroelectric charges with suitable pyroelectric voltage will trigger the catalytic water splitting reaction. To enable a rapid temperature change, we propose to use plasmonic nanoparticles to induce local heating of the ferroelectric nanoparticles under the illumination of sunlight. The material composition and the amount of plasmonic nanoparticles loaded will be optimized in this project. It is estimated that the hydrogen generation through the pyro-catalytic water splitting will be much faster that the photocatalytic water splitting. The hydrogen generation rate will be further increased by using concentrated sunlight, where light induced plasmonic hot electrons will play a synergistic role with the pyro-catalyst in the catalytic water splitting. This research project opens a new avenue in solar water splitting and has attractive potential for practical applications in clean energy. 利用可再生能源，如太陽能，來分解水制氫一直是人類夢寐以求的產生清潔能源的方式。我們在本項目中提出利用熱釋電催化來分解水制氫。鈦酸鋇是一種無鉛鐵電材料，其納米顆粒將被用作熱釋電催化劑。當溫度改變時，其鐵電自發極化將發生改變，從而在顆粒表面產生剩余電荷和熱釋電電壓。在合適的熱釋電電壓下這些電荷將參與到水分解的催化反應中。我們利用金屬納米顆粒在光照下的表面等離子效應產生的局域發熱來快速地改變鐵電納米顆粒的溫度，從而實現高的產氫量。我們將對材料的組分和金屬納米顆粒的負載量進行優化，以達到最佳效果。預計這種熱釋電水分解催化產氫將遠遠快於單一的光催化水分解產氫。另外，通過聚焦太陽光產生的等離子體熱電子將有可能與熱釋電催化產生協同效應，從而進一步提高產氫效率。本研究項目開辟了光致水分解的一個新的鄰域，將為清潔能源的利用帶來誘人的前景。

15214019.label: Realisation of objectives
15214019.value: All objectives are 100% achieved. Objective 1: To synthesize ferroelectric BaTiO3 nanoparticles with/without Sr-doping and load the synthesized nanoparticles with plasmonic nanoparticles. BaTiO3 nanoparticles (NPs) were synthesized through a hydrothermal method. Typically, 1.25 g of titanium dioxide (TiO2) and 24.08 g of sodium hydroxide (NaOH) were dissolved into 60 mL of deionized water. After stirring for 30 min, the mixed solution was transferred into a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, heated at 180 °C for 24 h, and then cooled down to room temperature naturally to get sodium titanate (Na2Ti3O7). The obtained material was then dispersed into HCl solution (pH = 1) for 4 h to obtain hydrogen titanate (H2Ti3O7). After repeated wash with deionized (DI) water, H2Ti3O7 was washed to pH = 7 and dried at 60 °C for 12 h. After that, 0.1288 g of H2Ti3O7 and 0.95 g of barium hydroxide (Ba(OH)2·8H2O) were dissolved in 60 mL of deionized water. The mixed solution was set in a 100-mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave at 210 °C for 85 min and cooled down to room temperature naturally. Then, barium titanate (BaTiO3) was collected by centrifugation and washed with DI water and ethanol several times until pH = 7. Finally, BaTiO3 catalyst was obtained after dying at 60 °C for 12 h. The Au/BaTiO3 NPs were synthesized in situ via a citrate reduction method. In the synthesis of the Au/BaTiO3 NPs, 16.5 mg of BaTiO3 NPs, 750 µL of sodium citrate (40 mmol L−1) and 500 µL HAuCl4 (10 mmol L−1) were added into 19 mL water. After 30 s ultrasonication, the solution was heated to reach boiling point for several minutes (around 10–12 min) under vigorous stirring to obtain the Au/BaTiO3 NPs (until the color the solution turns to be purplish red). For hydrogen production experiment, 3 mL of Au/BaTiO3 NPs solution were collected by centrifugation at 6000 rpm and dispersed in 12 mL water. After 10 s ultrasonication, the obtained catalyst was added into the reactor for H2 production. All reagents used as starting materials were of analytical grades. Objective 2: To fully characterize the ferroelectric properties of the synthesized ferroelectric nanoparticles. The phase formation and structure of the as-prepared materials were characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD). Rietveld structure refinement was conducted to calculate c/a ratio, which is an important parameter to tell that the synthesized material is in a ferroelectric state. Raman spectroscopy provides additional support to the ferroelectric state. The synthesized BaTiO3 nanoparticles was spread on a Si substrate and piezoresponse force microscope (PFM) was used to probe the local piezoelectric response of the BaTiO3 nanoparticles. The morphology and particle size of the BaTiO3 nanoparticles were studied by field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area analysis was conducted via surface area and porosity analyzer. UV-Vis diffuse reflectance spectra was tested by Shimadzu UV-2550 UV-vis spectrophotometer. The UPS was measured by thermo Fisher Nexsa X-ray photoemission spectroscopy, where the catalyst was dispersed on Pt coated silicon sheet (photon energy of 21.22 eV and bias voltage of −10 V). The dielectric properties were measured by impedance analyzer and broadband frequency analyzer on compacted pellet samples after slight sintering of the nanoparticles. The P-E hysteresis loop was measured on the same pellet samples by a ferroelectric tester using the modified Sawyer-Tower circuit. The pyroelectric coefficient was estimated from the temperature dependence of the saturated polarization. Objective 3: To study the pyro-catalytic water splitting behavior and its pyro-catalytic mechanism of the synthesized Au-loaded ferroelectric nanoparticles. The pyro-catalytic hydrogen production of the Au decorated BaTiO3 NPs was evaluated offline. In pyro-catalytic experiment, around 2.62 mg Au decorated BaTiO3 NPs were dispersed in 12 mL deionized water. The aqueous suspension was put into a 30 mL pear-shaped quartz reactor and sealed using septa in advance, which was then evacuated and purged by N2 for about 20 min to completely remove air. The distance between light irradiation source and reactor is 10 cm. To detect the amount of hydrogen production, 300 µL gas component within the reactor was intermittently extracted and injected into a gas chromatograph with a thermal conductivity detector. 300 µL N2 gas is refilled into reactor after sampling, which was taken into consideration in the calculation. The amount of hydrogen gas produced was calculated using a calibration curve (y = 137.78x + 18.95, R2 = 0.99962) of hydrogen concentration versus peak area (working range: 300–15,000 ppm; limit of detection: 50 ppm; limit of quantification: 150 ppm). All the hydrogen production experiments were performed three times per experimental parameter set. The optical modelling of the plasmonic local heating effect was carried out to study the underlying mechanism. A two-step simulation was conducted by using the commercial full-wave Finite Element Method software (COMSOL RF and Multiphysics 5.5). A circularly polarized plane wave was used as the background field to interact with the faceted gold nanospheres with different radii, i.e., 6, 9, and 12 nm suspended over a BaTiO3 cylinder. BaTiO3 nanowire is placed 1 nm below the faceted gold nanospheres. The absorption cross section was thus obtained as the absorbed energy normalized to the incident optical intensity. PML condition was applied to the outer surface of water domain. The plasmonic local heating effect was studied by using the COMSOL Multiphysics 5.5 Heat Transfer module. The geometries and the relative position of the faceted gold nanospheres and BaTiO3 cylinder are all set the same as the optical modelling except that they are surrounded by a water sphere with 20 μm in diameter, which is large enough to render the average temperature rise negligible during the one-pulse excitation, complying with the experimental observation. The gold nanospheres are modeled as heat sources whose heating power equals to the time dependent laser power density times their absorption cross sections obtained from the optical modelling. The heat transfer coefficient 1000 W m−2 K−1 of the convective heat flux was assigned to the outer surface of the water sphere, a commonly used value describing the stirring process. Objective 4: To optimize the water splitting performance by composition modification and the use of concentrated solar light. To optimize the water splitting performance, it is very important to generate large enough temperature change and as many as possible thermal cycling within a unit time. Three different types of light sources were compared, those were, a 500 mW 532 nm nanosecond pulsed laser with repetition rate of 10 Hz and pulse width of around 12.7 ns, a 1 W 532 nm continuous laser, and a 300 W high-pressure Xenon lamp. Although the nanosecond pulsed laser has the smallest power, it was much better than the other two light sources. It has a very high energy density, which brings about a high temperature change in the BaTiO3 nanoparticles. Moreover, its repetition rate is 10 Hz, which brings about 10 thermal cycling per second. As a result, a very high hydrogen production rate was achieved under the irradiation of the nanosecond laser.

15214019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214019.value: The greatest challenge that limits the application of pyro-catalytic materials is the lack of highly frequent thermal cycling due to enormous heat capacity of ambient environment, resulting in low pyro-catalytic efficiency. We introduce localized plasmonic heat sources to rapidly yet efficiently heat up pyro-catalytic material itself without wasting energy to raise the surrounding temperature, triggering a significantly expedited pyro-catalytic reaction and enabling multiple pyro-catalytic cycling per unit time. In our work, plasmonic metal/pyro-catalyst composite is fabricated by in-situ grown gold nanoparticles on three-dimensional structured coral-like BaTiO3 nanoparticles, which achieves a high hydrogen production rate of 133.1 ± 4.4 μmol/g/h under pulsed laser irradiation. The synergy between plasmonic local heating and pyro-catalysis will bring new opportunities in pyro-catalysis for pollutant treatment, clean energy production, and biological applications. (Nat.Commun., 2022). By using DFT simulations we theoretically disclose that hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activity on TiO2-terminated ferroelectric BaTiO3 (BTO) is tunable by manipulating its polarization state. Overall, among the out-of-plane and in-plane polarization states, the latter is demonstrated to be the most favourable toward the HER. The interplay between surface rumpling and surface polarization exists and greatly affects the surface reactivity. The correlation of the surface oxygen 2p band center and hydrogen adsorption free energy change can be well established to satisfactorily characterize the HER activity trend, and the in-plane polarized BTO exhibits the optimal band center and adsorption strength. Moreover, the in-plane surface dipole–dipole interaction strongly affects the surface adsorption strength due to the depolarization effect. In addition, the HER catalytic cycle based on ferroelectric catalytic behaviour and functional design of the switchable ferroelectric polarization state by applying periodic mechanic strain are proposed and hold great promise to conquer the Sabatier limit. This work may shed light on the understanding of the performance of ferroelectric catalysts by applying controllable ferroelectric polarization state. (J.Mater.Chem.A, 2023). We successfully construct a highly efficient oxygen-deficient Bi5Ti3FeO15 piezocatalysts using a simple self-modified strategy. It is evident that too few or excessive oxygen vacancies suppress the piezocatalytic activities of the catalyst. As a result, the enhanced synergistic effect between moderate carrier concentration and piezoelectric property promotes the piezocatalytic performance of the catalyst, and its superior piezocatalytic activities for single and multiple dye degradations are demonstrated. The environmental adaptability evaluations demonstrate that the Bi5Ti3FeO15 catalyst possesses superior adaptability for pH value changes, common inorganic anions addition and water sources. 15214019.value: During the pyro-catalytic water splitting experiment, we detected the generation of many hydroxyl radicals, which can be used for medical therapy. In the future, we will try plasmonic materials with longer absorption wavelength (longer penetration depth into the skin) so that pyro-catalytic hydroxyl radical generation can be triggered under the skin of animals.

15214019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214019.value: The use of sustainable energy sources, such as solar energy, to generate hydrogen from water splitting is always a dream of humankind to produce a clean energy source. In this project, we propose to generate hydrogen through water splitting by making use of the pyro-catalytic effect of lead-free BaTiO3-based ferroelectric nanoparticles. When the temperature of BaTiO3 is changed, uncompensated surface charges are generated, which results in a pyroelectric voltage across the two oppositely polarized surfaces of the nanoparticle. Those pyroelectric charges with suitable pyroelectric voltage will trigger the catalytic water splitting reaction. To enable a rapid and efficient temperature change, we in-situ grow Au nanoparticles onto BaTiO3 nanoparticles. Under intense light illumination, the plasmonic effect of Au locally heat up the ferroelectric nanoparticles and hydrogen is generated through the pyro-catalytic water splitting. This local heating method efficiently changes the temperature of pyro-catalyst and reduces the amount of heat loss by shortening the heat transfer pathway. The synergy between plasmonic local heating and pyro-catalysis will bring new opportunities in pyro-catalysis for pollutant treatment, clean energy production, and biological applications.

15214619.label: Project Title(Chinese)

15214619.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15214619.value: Dr JIANG, Ding Prof PAN, Feng

15214619.label: Project Objectives
15214619.value: Aim 1: Synthesis and characterization of hybrid ZnIn2S4/GQD submicrosphere. Multi-color GQDs will be synthesized with hydrothermal/solvothermal synthesis methods with various co-reacting reagents to modulate absorption spectra. Hybrid ZnIn2S4/GQD submicrospheres will be synthesized by a one-pot solvothermal approach. The synthesis conditions will be optimized to achieve controllable size, stable structure and high porosity. The photoelectronic properties such as photo-current conversion efficiency and colour sensitivity under light irradiation with different wavelengths will be explored. Aim 2: Synthesis and characterization of hybrid ZnIn2S4/GQD-polymeric substrate based interface. Polymeric substrate based interface will be prepared by transferring a ZnIn2S4/GQD submicrosphere monolayer to a flexible and transparent PDMS substrate using a mechanical-force pressing approach. The temporal and spatial properties of local photocurrents under light illumination with various spot sizes and wavelengths will be tested. Aim 3: Testing of the photoelectronic interfaces for stimulation of primary neurons in vitro. Both dispersible and substrate-based interfaces will be tested for photo-stimulation of primary neurons in vitro. The cell-material interface will be evaluated with super-resolution microscopy and TEM. The stimulation efficiency with various light wavelengths, light spot sizes and power intensities will be evaluated for various types of artificial photoreceptors. Aim 4: Testing of the photoelectronic interfaces for stimulation of degenerative mice retina explants. Both dispersible and substrate-based interfaces will be tested for photo-stimulation of degenerative mice retina explants. Colour sensitivity and spatial resolution will be evaluated by measuring the retina output signals. The results will be compared with those of normal retinas and degenerative retinas without hybrid interfaces.
