15214619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214619.value: 與光感受器神經元死亡相關的視網膜變性是人類失明的主要原因之一。但是，沒有可治癒的治療方法。視網膜刺激已顯示出基於通過外部刺激（例如電刺激和光遺傳學刺激）刺激殘餘視網膜神經元來恢復視網膜變性疾病的視力的前景。然而，電刺激需要用於外部連接的侵入性跨眼電纜。光遺傳學刺激還具有病毒載體的安全性問題和光敏性蛋白質的低光敏性的挑戰。最近，光電刺激作為一種有吸引力的選擇正在出現，因為它能夠將光轉換成電信號，這消除了對侵入性跨眼電纜的需要和病毒載體轉染的風險。然而，目前的光電刺激方法由於空間分辨率低而無法實現局部單神經元刺激，並且沒有人類視網膜樣顏色敏感性。因此，開發具有類人類感光度和光刺激的高空間分辨率的新型光電子材料人工感光器具有重要意義。 在該項目中，我們提出開發基於混合ZnIn2S4 /石墨烯量子點（GQD）亞微球的光電子人工感光器，用於恢復退行性小鼠視網膜的光敏感性，具有人類視網膜樣色分辨性，高空間分辨率和增強的與視網膜神經元的接口效率。 。這將是用於恢復退行性視網膜色彩敏感性的光電人工感光細胞的首次試驗。混合ZnIn2S4 / GQD亞微球將使用單罐溶劑熱方法建立，其中多孔ZnIn2S4亞微球作為可見光驅動的光電平台和用於GQD耦合的多孔基板，以及用於光采集和顏色靈敏度調製的多色GQD。將合成各種ZnIn2S4 / GQD亞微球以模擬人感光體的藍色，綠色和紅色敏感性。將測試可分散的亞微球體界面和柔性聚合物/亞微球基質基界面對體外原代神經元和退行性小鼠視網膜外植體的光刺激。分散的亞微球界面有利於局部單神經元刺激，並且柔性基底界面適合於與大組織表面接合以進行長期刺激。在光照射下，光信號被轉換成電刺激，以激活具有顏色靈敏度和高空間分辨率的簡併視網膜中的殘餘神經元電路。所提出的混合光電納米界面可以是良好的光電刺激平台，以恢復具有高空間分辨率的退行性視網膜的色光敏感性和增強的細胞 - 材料界面連接效率，作為視網膜再生疾病的有效治療方法。

15214619.label: Realisation of objectives
15214619.value: During the whole project period, all the 4 objectives have been realized. 1) The hybrid cell-like ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs were synthesized using a one-pot hydrothermal approach with a mixture of Zn(NO3)2, In(NO3)3, and NGQDs, in which nucleation occurred first, followed by aggregation and re-crystallization. The as-prepared NGQDs exhibited an average diameter of 2–5 nm with a crystalline structure when analyzed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging. The shape of ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs, analyzed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), showed a flower-like structure with an average size of 2–5 μm, which is close to the natural diameter of rods (≈2 μm) and cones (0.5–4 μm). In these “flowers” numerous thin nanosheets form the 2D nanopetals, giving them a larger surface area to achieve higher charge transfer capability and more efficient interaction with retinal tissues. The photoconversion properties of the ZnIn2S4 and ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs were demonstrated by photocurrent measurements under green light irradiation (520 nm). The typical substrate size was 1 cm2 with a deposition concentration of 4 mg mL-1. Compared with the dark state without light, when the ZnIn2S4 and ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs were illuminated by green light, a significant increase in photocurrent was observed immediately, whereas the photocurrent decreased to the original dark state as the light irradiation was turned off. The photogenerated currents of the ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs under green light irradiation were about 2 times that of ZnIn2S4 MFs. Under full visible light irradiation, the photogenerated currents of the ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs were approximately 3.75 times that of the ZnIn2S4 MFs. 2) Polymeric substrate-based interface was prepared by transferring a ZnIn2S4/GQD submicrosphere monolayer to a flexible and transparent PDMS substrate using a mechanical-force pressing approach. The solution with ZnIn2S4/GQD submicrospheres is firstly spin-coated on cleaned glass substrate surface to form a self-assembled submicrosphere monolayer. An incomplete thermal curing process of a PDMS elastomer substrate is firstly performed from a PDMS mixture with pre-polymer solution and curing agent at a 10:1 weight ratio in an oven at 800C for 40 minutes. Various spin-coating speeds and initial concentrations of ZnIn2S4/GQD submicrospheres will be explored to find optimal parameters to achieve high packing density of submicrospheres on PDMS substrate. The local photo-response properties of the substrate-based interface is essential for efficient local photo-stimulation. The temporal and spatial properties of local photocurrents under light illumination with various spot sizes and wavelengths were measured using a patch pipette positioned close to the centre of light stimulation. A circular illumination spot can be generated by passing light through a pin hole and focusing the light with a water immersion ×40 objective. The photocurrent intensity profile surrounding the centre of light stimulation was measured by positioning the patch pipette at different distances away from the centre in both horizontal plane and vertical planes. The temporal and spatial properties of local photocurrents under light illumination with various spot sizes and wavelengths were tested. 3) The photoelectronic interfaces has been tested for stimulation of primary neurons in vitro. Both dispersible and substrate-based interfaces were tested for photo-stimulation of primary neurons in vitro. Whether ZnIn2S4/NGQD MF implantation could induce responses in single RGCs level was explored using patch clamp approach. The ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs were implanted and formed a biointerface with the remaining bipolar cells. Both the loose and whole-cell patches were applied. The light response of ON RGC was successfully recorded with light stimulation (525 nm). The peri-stimulus time histogram of the ON RGC responses with spike frequency was calculated. 4) The photoelectronic interfaces were used for stimulation of degenerative mice retina explants. Both dispersible and substrate-based interfaces were tested for photo-stimulation of degenerative mice retina explants. Spatial resolution were evaluated by measuring the retina output signals. The formation of a ZnIn2S4/NGQD based MF biointerface and its capability to induce light-dependent neuronal activation in the RGCs of degenerative retinas from P66 rd10 mouse were systematically tested. ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs and glass microspheres (MSs) were microinjected into the subretinal space of degenerative retinas. Retinas from wild-type (WT) mouse were used as normal controls. Five days after microinjection, the ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs were closely attached to the retinal layer to form an MF–retina biointerface. SEM revealed that ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs formed close contact with the retina along the surface of the retinal layer. Some ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs were partially immersed in the retinal layer, and some wrinkles were generated on the boundary between the MFs and the retinal layer, which greatly increased the contact area of the MFs and the retinal layer, providing a good foundation for subsequent photoelectric stimulation. In contrast, smooth glass MSs were also attached to the retinal layer; however, partial immersion of the glass MSs and wrinkle generation on the boundary were not observed. The flower-like structures of the ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs promoted cell attachment and the formation of a close interface between the ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs and retinal layer. The cell-material interface was evaluated with super-resolution microscopy and TEM. The stimulation efficiency with various light wavelengths, light spot sizes and power intensities were evaluated for various types of artificial photoreceptors. The biophysical properties of RGCs in degenerative retinas photostimulated with ZnIn2S4/NGQD MFs were studied. Both patch-clamp and microelectrode array approaches are used for evaluation. Our findings demonstrate that implanted hybrid cell-like ZnIn2S4/NGQD microflowers in degenerative retinas can transfer light signals to electrical activity at the biointerface, acting as artificial photoreceptors and restoring light responses in seven major types of RGCs in P66 rd10 mice retinas. In these degenerative retinas, the number and distribution of the seven types of RGCs activated by ZnIn2S4/NGQD showed a pattern similar to that of the normal mice retina. Compared with wild-type retinas, the latency of the spikes in RGCs induced by ZnIn2S4/NGQD microflowers was 500 ms longer. As a proof-of-concept, the implanted MF biointerface indicates the desirability of bionic technology in visual rehabilitation. The further clinical application of ZnIn2S4/NGQD microflowers could be realized by designing of biofunctional modifications and the precise integration between retina and the MF biointerface. One key point of design is the surface biofunctionalization of the microflower by incorporating cell adhesion molecules to promote cell attachment/proliferation/differentiation, and reduce the host immune responses. Besides, basing on the 3D physical structure of the MF biointerface, loading bioactive factors or neurotrophic factors, may further augment the promotion of neural cell attachment and growth. Besides, loading of therapeutic drug molecules onto MFs holds could promise for sustained retinal therapy.

15214619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214619.value: We firstly explored the synthesis methods for new photoelectrochemical nanomaterials. A new facile and environment-friendly hydrothermal synthesis process was developed to synthesize nitrogen-doped graphene quantum dots-dedicated tungsten oxide nanosheets (dWO3•H2O@N-GQDs) (Biosensors & Bioelectronics, 2021, 183, 113214 in Part C, impact factor: 10.7) The synthesized dWO3•H2O@N-GQDs provided a much-enhanced photoelectric response due to the efficient charge transfer. We also synthesized TiO2–Ag/nitrogen-doped graphene composites, which could amplify the photocurrent outputs. These composites perform a photocurrent-switchable operation, where photocurrents can be switched between anodic and cathodic directions by simply regulating the irradiation wavelength (Biosensors & Bioelectronics, 2022, 202, 113999 in Part C, impact factor: 10.7). We then developed quantum dot-doped ZnIn2S4 microflowers (MF) to construct a biomimetic photoelectric interface with a 0D/3D heterostructure, aiming to restore the light responses in dysfunctional photoreceptors (PR)-degenerative mice (Small, 2024 10.1002/smll.202400300 in Part C, impact factor: 13) The MF biointerface has dimensions similar to those of natural PRs and can be distributed within the curved spatial region of the retina, mimicking cellular dispersion. The soft 2D nanopetals of the MF provided large specific surface area for photoelectric activation and simulated the flexibility interfacing between cells. This biointerface could selectively restore the light responses of seven types of retina ganglion cells that encode brightness. The distribution of responsive cells forms a pattern similar to that of normal mice, which may reflect the generation of the initial “neural code” in degenerative retina. Patch-clamp recordings indicated that the biointerface could induce spiking and postsynaptic currents at the single-neuron level. The results showed that the implanted MF biointerface possess the potentials of bionic technology for visual rehabilitation and RP treatment. Furthermore, we also developed NIR-light responsive nanoprobe for detecting intracellular pH and unravelling metabolic variations in cells (ACS Nano, 2024, 18(24), 15935–15949 in Part C, impact factor: 15.8). This technique can be used for monitoring pH value in retina cells in the future. Retinal cells, particularly photoreceptors, have high metabolic demands, and disruptions in energy production can lead to cell dysfunction and death. Monitoring pHi in retinal cells can help unravel the metabolic disturbances associated with degenerative diseases such as age-related macular degeneration (AMD) or retinitis pigmentosa.

15214619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214619.value: The further development of artificial photoreceptor-based vision recovery will be focused on soft polymeric photoelectronic materials which may provide higher biocompatibility, good mechanical property and color sensitivity. Moreover, the complex visual signal transduction mechanism of artificial photoreceptors for vision recovery will be studied.

15214619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214619.value: Retinitis pigmentosa is a genetic condition that often leads to blindness because it damages the cells in the eye that respond to light (photoreceptors). Traditional treatments try to fix or replace these cells, but they can harm the eye's structure and genetic makeup. Scientists are now looking at a new method called optoelectronic stimulation, which is less damaging but still has some challenges, especially in controlling the stimulation precisely. Researchers have created tiny, flower-like structures made of a material called quantum dot-doped ZnIn2S4 to act like artificial photoreceptors. These tiny "microflowers" are similar in size to natural photoreceptors and can fit nicely in the eye's curved shape. They have soft, petal-like parts that can catch light and turn it into electrical signals, just like real cells do. When tested in mice with a disease like retinitis pigmentosa, these microflowers helped restore the ability to detect light in several types of cells in the back of the eye. The pattern of these active cells looked a lot like that in healthy mice, suggesting that the artificial cells might be starting to recreate the way the eye sends visual information to the brain. Experiments showed that these microflowers could even work at the level of individual neurons. This exciting research suggests that these microflower structures could one day help people with retinitis pigmentosa regain some of their vision.

15214719.label: Project Objectives
15214719.value: Identification of optical and electric measurements of lightning attachment process: Lightning attachment refers to the transition from leader process to return stroke process. It usually involves a downward negative leader (DNL) and an upward positive leader (UPL), characterized with short duration, lower luminosity, small currents and weak electric field change but may be accompanied with detectable VHF radiations. So far, observations of lightning attachment are primarily based on optical records. Therefore, we would like to extend the observation by close measurements of the currents, electric and magnetic field change, VHF radiation and high-speed image of the lightning attachment. For this, the first must-to- do thing is to define the dynamic range, sensitivity, space-time resolution etc. for each of the measurements based on literature review and analysis of the phenomenon concerned. Experiment setup and field observation of lightning attachment: In collaboration with Meteorological Bureau of Shenzhen, China, a 356m high meteorological tower was built up in suburban area of Shenzhen in 2016, which is good for the study of lightning strike to tall structures. Based on the pre-defined specifications for each measurement, adequate instruments including Rogowski coils and current shunts, electric field mills, slow and fast antennas, cross-loop magnetic antennas, broadband VHF interferometers and high-speed cameras will be calibrated and installed to observe the lightning attaching to the tower during summers. Development of a macroscopic model for lightning attachment process: Besides the observation, numerical modelling is another helpful way for lightning research, particularly for understanding of the observation result. A typical attachment process usually includes a downward negative leader (DNL) and upward positive leader from the prospective strike object. A model that can simulate the behavior of a DNL-induced UPL – the attachment process will be developed and tested. Mutual interpretation of the observation and modelling results: For a specific lightning attaching to the tower, VHF interferometer and high-speed camera can detect the spatial development of the DNL and UPL. The shunt and Rogowski coil can record the current of the UPL. Slow and fast antennas sense the electric field changes produced by the process, and the electric field mill provides the information of the average ambient electric field at the moment the lightning occurring. These can be compared with the model results for mutual validation of the model and the observation. Generalization of the condition of upward leaders initiated from tall structures: Moreover, based on timely analysis of the observation and modelling results, the conditions of upward leaders initiated from high-rise structures will be discussed and generalized, based on which new technologies for forecasting and protection of lightning discharge to high-rise structures may be proposed.

15214719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15214719.value: 自然閃電可能發生在雲層內部或者雲地之間。大多數雲地閃電包含一個起始於雲內的下行負極性先導，隨後緊接著一次回擊過程。當下行負先導向地面傳播時，在地表建築物上會引發一個上行正極性先導。當下行負先導和上行正先導連接時，在連接處會產生一個巨大的電流脈衝（即回擊過程）。從上行正先導起始到和下行負先導相連接的整個過程被定義為閃電的連接過程。這一過程決定了閃電在地面上的閃擊點。 目前有關閃電連接過程的研究大多集中在用高速攝像機或高時間解析度的數位光學成像系統對人工引雷或自然閃電進行觀測。亦有一些結合高速攝像資料和電場觀測資料對連接過程的研究。然而，由於這一過程持續時間很短以及發光強度很弱，閃電連接過程仍是瞭解最少的閃電過程之一。 因此，該課題旨在拓展對位於中國深圳的356米高氣象觀測塔上針對閃電連接過程進行多參數觀測的研究。該高塔上除了風速計、溫度計和濕度計等常規氣象觀測設備之外，還在塔的不同高度上安裝了大氣電場儀以及塔頂安裝了一套閃電電流測量系統。在距離高塔440米處設有主觀測站，站內安裝了快慢電場天線、磁場天線、寬頻甚高頻干涉儀系統以及高速攝像機。另一台高速攝像機將被安裝在另一個觀測網站，用來重建閃電通道的三維圖像。同時，建立一個下行負先導—上行正先導耦合物理模型用來解釋塔上有關閃電連接過程的觀測結果。該課題所獲取的觀測和模擬結果可以使人們更好地瞭解從高層建築物上起始的上行先導的條件和前提特徵，進而開發用於短時預報和對高層建築物進行有效雷電防護的新技術。

15214719.label: Realisation of objectives
15214719.value: This project aims to get insights of the lightning attachment process by carrying out multi-parameter observations of the lightning attachment process to a 356-m-high meteorological tower in Shenzhen, China. Besides, a physical model is to be developed and applied to interpret the observation results. There were 5 specific objectives: 1) Identification of optical and electric measurements of lightning attachment process; 2) Experiment setup and field observation of lightning attachment; 3) Development of a macroscopic model for lightning attachment process; 4) Mutual interpretation of the observation and modelling results; and 5) Generalization of the condition of upward leaders initiated from tall structures. Through the period from the summer of 2019 (when the project was funded) to October of 2023 (when the project was completed), we have been carried our continuously field observations and huge lightning data has been collected and analyzed. Specifically, a)Experiments: for execution of the project, starting from the summer of 2019 (when the project was funded), the Shenzhen meteorological tower, besides the conventional meteorological instruments, was also equipped with several atmospheric electric field mills at different heights of the tower and a lightning current measuring system at the tower top. A main observation site was setup at 440 m away from the tower, where a fast and a slow electric field antenna, a magnetic field antenna, a broadband VHF interferometer system and a high-speed camera were deployed and were put into the observations. Besides, in 2021, a low-noise shock-tolerated preamplifier was designed and installed on the Shenzhen Meteorological Gradient Tower with a 0.25-mΩ coaxial shunt for current measurement. With this device, we have succeeded in measuring milli-ampere-level corona discharges, which provided us the firsthand information of the transition of a corona discharge to a leader discharge [Ref.: https://doi.org/10.1109/APL57308.2023.10182038.] With these works, 100% of objective 1) and 50% of Objective 2) have been achieved. b) Lightning observations: from 2019-2020, two initial upward positive leaders (UPLs) in upward negative flashes initiated from the Shenzhen tower were observed with the high-speed camera, the electric field and magnetic field sensors. Both camera images and magnetic fields showed that the two UPLs had obvious stepwise characteristics in their upward moving stage. The magnetic fields associated with the UPLs were characterized by a series of fast-changing bipolar impulses superimposed on a slowly increasing continuous component as the leaders moved upward, which were well corresponding to the light intensity changes of their high-speed camera images. Besides the 2D step length and step extension speed, the radius of the leader luminous channel as a function of time and height was also estimated. The channel radius showed first a stable increasing trend in the leader upward moving stage and then 4 - 5 times of shrinking and expanding processes after the leader connected the cloud. Particularly, the channel radius showed an obvious increasing trend with the increase of the height all the time, which is in good agreement with the concept of leader corona sheath in literature. [Ref.: https://doi.org/10.1029/2019JD031508.]. With these works, 100 % of Objective 2) and 50% of Objective 3) have been achieved. c) Lightning modellings: also in 2020, an approach for retrieving the leader channel charge density, leader current, ambient electric field, and space charge along a leader channel path from ground observations with a complicated ground condition was proposed. With this approach, properties of two downward positive leaders (DPL1 and DPL2) struck at high-rise buildings were studied based on electric and optical measurements made on the roof of a high building. The channel line charge density for both leaders showed firstly a sharp increasing trend and then a decreasing trend as the leader going down, while both the ambient electric field and the space charge for them showed an alternating polarity along the leader path, which may reflect the in-loud electric structure and the corona charge distribution between the cloud and ground. [Ref.: https://doi.org/10.1029/2020JD032818]. with these works, 100% of Objective 3) and 50% of Objective 4) have been achieved. d) Lightning evolutions: Lightning mapping with radio frequency location systems plays more and more important roles in understanding the mechanism of lightning discharges during thunderstorms. In 2021, a comprehensive analysis on the LF electromagnetic field measurements and 3D mapping of two coincident lightning flash were conducted, which consists of an upward positive flash (+CG) triggered by a nearby downward negative flash. The LF 3D maps showed clearly that the in-cloud (IC) activity relating to the –CG moved probably with negative charges away from overhead position of the upward negative leader (UNL) relating to the +CG, which did a favor for the UNL initiation. The UNL developed firstly upward and then extended horizontally. The total positive charge transferred from the cloud to ground by the +CG flash was estimated to be about 5.8 C. From the 3D maps, we inferred that the IC activity relating to the –CG flash which moved negative charge away from overhead region of the UNL could be responsible for the UNL initiation. And the existence of extensive lower positive charges further favored the long horizontal propagation of the UNL inside the cloud. [Ref.: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2020.105408]. With these works, 100% of Objective 4) and 50% of Objective 5) have been achieved. e) Lightning attachments interpretation: In 2023, Two downward negative flashes (F1612 & F1613) with multiple return strokes struck to the 356-m Shenzhen Tower were observed and analyzed in detail. The high-speed camera captured upward positive connecting leaders (UCL) for the first strokes of both flashes and two subsequent strokes of F1612. The observations also show that none of the downward negative leader (DNL) completely propagated to the tower tip before the occurrence of the return stroke (RS), so that we inferred that the UCL initiated from the tower tip might exist for each RS of the two flashes. The possible height of the UCL and DNL connecting point above the tower tip for each RS was estimated, which showed a positive correlation to the speed of corresponding DNL. The striking distances estimated for 8 subsequent RSs in F1612 were in a range from 14.6 m to 85.4 m and that for 3 subsequent RSs in F1613 were from 24.2 m to 66.2 m. There was a weak positive linear relationship between the DNL speed and striking distance for subsequent RSs in the two flashes. The DNL speed showed a positive correlation to the peak current of corresponding RS. [Ref.: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2024.107661]. With these works, 100% of Objective 5), therefore, all the 5 objectives have been achieved.

15214719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15214719.value: Firstly, we succeeded in measuring milli- to kilo-ampere currents of upward leaders for the first time. With a 100V-shock-tolerated preamplifier installed on the Shenzhen tower, we have successfully observed the corona discharges of several hundred milli-amperes just before the formation of upward lightning leaders, which provided us the firsthand information of the transition of corona discharge to a leader discharge [Ref.: conference paper No. 1: https://doi.org/10.1109/APL57308.2023.10182038.] Secondly, we succeeded in identifications of the lateral and longitudinal evolution of upward positive stepped leaders initiated from the Shenzhen tower for the first time. Two initial upward positive leaders (UPLs) in upward negative flashes initiated from the Shenzhen tower were observed with the high-speed camera, the electric field and magnetic field sensors. Both camera images and magnetic fields showed that the two UPLs had obvious stepwise characteristics in their upward moving stage. Besides the conventional 2D step length and step extension speed, the radius of the leader luminous channel as a function of time and height was also estimated. Particularly, the channel radius showed an obvious increasing trend with the increase of the height all the time, which is in good agreement with the concept of leader corona sheath. [Ref.: journal paper No.1: https://doi.org/10.1029/2019JD031508]. Thirdly, we proposed a new approach for retrieving the leader channel charge density, leader current, ambient electric field, and space charge along a leader channel path from ground observations with a complicated ground condition was proposed. With this approach, for two downward positive leaders struck a high-rise building, It was found that their line charge densities showed firstly a sharp increasing trend and then a decreasing trend as the leader going down, while both the ambient electric fields and space charges showed an alternating polarity along the leader path. [Ref.: journal paper No.2 and 3: https://doi.org/10.1029/2020JD032818; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2020.105408]. Lastly, we succeeded in observations of upward connecting leaders in subsequent leader-returns stroke processes during two downward negative flashes with multiple return strokes struck to the Shenzhen tower. The high-speed camera captured upward positive connecting leaders for the first strokes of both flashes and two subsequent strokes of one flash. There was a weak positive linear relationship between the downward leader speed and striking distance for subsequent return strokes RSs of the two flashes. The downward leader speed showed a positive correlation to the peak current of corresponding return stroke. [Ref.: journal paper No.4: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.atmosres.2024.107661].

15214719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15214719.value: Due to its short duration and faint luminosity, the lightning attachment process is poorly understood. By this project, we have extended the study by carrying out multi-parameter observations of the lightning attachment process to the Shenzhen meteorological tower in China. Besides conventional meteorological instruments (Anemometer, Thermometer and Hygrometer), the tower was also equipped with atmospheric electric field mills along the tower body and a lightning current measuring system at the tower top. Besides, at 440 m away from the tower, a fast and a slow electric field antenna, a magnetic field antenna, a broadband VHF interferometer system and a high-speed camera were also deployed. With these instrumentations, we have obtained huge amount of data of lightning attached to the tower. Further analyses of these data may lead to a good understanding of the conditions and pre-characteristics of upward leader initiations from high-rise structures, and hence may lead to the development of new techniques for effective protection of lightning discharges to high-rise structures.

15214719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15214719.value: A cloud-to-ground lightning flash usually involves a downward negative leader originated inside the cloud and an upward positive connecting leader from a grounded object. The process that the two leaders get contact is referred as the lightning attachment. Due to its short duration and faint luminosity, this attachment process is poorly understood. By this project, we have extended the study by carrying out multi-parameter observations of the lightning attachment to a 356-m-high meteorological tower in China. The tower, besides conventional meteorological instruments, was also equipped with atmospheric electric field mills along the tower body and a lightning current measuring system at the tower top. Besides, at a main site 440 m away from the tower, a fast and a slow electric field antenna, a magnetic field antenna, a broadband VHF interferometer system and a high-speed camera were also deployed. With these instruments, we have obtained huge amount of data of lightning attached to the tower. A physical model was proposed to explain these observations. These observations have deepened our understanding of the conditions and pre-characteristics of upward leader initiations from high-rise structures, which may help us to develop new techniques for forecasting and protection of lightning to high-rise structures.

15215019.value: 智能電網級聯故障分析

15215019.label: Project Objectives
15215019.value: Modeling: We aim to construct a model that allows topological structure and cyber-coupling pattern to be conveniently examined and incorporates the deterministic power flow processes to generate realistic loading data. The model is expected to use stochastic processes to describe the uncertain time to failure for each occurrence of component failure so that a complete cascade propagation can be generated in time scale. The model therefore permits simulation of cascading failure versus time to be produced, thus providing information on the failure propagation pattern. In addition, we will consider cyber-coupling as an important extension of the model to describe the interactive processes that exist in coupled networks, which would intensify the rapidity and extent of power blackouts. Analysis: The second objective is to derive effective analytical procedure to identify crucial parameters and structural properties of a cyber-coupled power network that influence the way in which failure cascade will proceed in time. Robustness parameters, failure rates of power system components, structural parameters of network and operational parameters will form a multi-dimensional parameter space in which analysis will be conducted to identify the relationship between parameters and propagation patterns. The information generated is expected to expose how rapidly a failure cascade will occur, and how soon and to what extent a blackout may occur after an initial failure occurs, for certain ranges of structural, operational and network parameters. In addition, we expect to derive important information on how coupling strategies affect power network robustness. Data Verification and Applications: The propagation profiles generated by the model will first be compared with historical data. At this stage we have partially re-constructed historical data of 1996 and 2003 power blackouts in North America, based on data publicly available but embedded in formal reports. In the proposed work, we will perform mining of the available 2016 data aiming to put the failure cascade profiles in a format that facilitates comparison and verification of our models. We will also apply our prediction methods to real power grids in China.

15215019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215019.value: This proposal is a resubmission of last year's unfunded proposal, incorporating the key reviewers' comments as described in detail in Part-II-3. Existing power delivery networks consist of complex interconnection of generators, loads and substations, with sophisticated control incorporated to ensure their safe and robust operation. Conventional power flow models have been used for studying these networks, but complex interactions of causes leading to failure of power components are often not readily analyzed. Cascading failure has been a topic receiving much attention; however, there is no effective tool for analysis and prediction of propagation of the failure cascade due to the lack of adequate models that can incorporate the complex interactions of the connected system. In 2015, we reported a novel approach for robustness study of power networks using a complex network perspective, and our work was immediately put in the IEEEXplore Innovation Spotlight. Following this success, we published in 2017 a contribution demonstrating the use of this model to generate and explain the propagation profiles as typified in the 1996 and 2003 North-American blackouts. In this proposal, we aim to conduct a research study, combining deterministic power flow models with essential stochastic processes, as well as extensive simulations and collection of real data, to identify the topological properties and operational parameters that are crucial in determining the safe and robust operation of power networks. Our research will consist of the following components. First, we develop a model for describing the failure processes in power networks with cyber coupling. While some network theorists had applied complex network models for power network systems, the main shortcoming was the lack of proper description for the physical power flow processes. The key novelty is the combined use of physical power flow equations and complex network models allowing crucial parameters and coupling patterns to be readily examined. This model will also incorporate stochastic processes to allow failure timings to be included, and hence propagation profiles generated in time scale. Extensive simulation study will be conducted, in comparison with historical blackout data, aiming to recover the relationship between the failure propagation profiles, network structure, network parameters, and cyber coupling patterns. Robustness metrics will be developed for indication of the extent and onset time for large-scale blackout upon an initial element failure. Our findings are expected to generate ground-breaking contributions for development of future power grids by providing prediction of the likely failure propagation and extent of damages. 現有的電力輸送網絡，包括緊密互連的發電機、負載和變電站，結合了複雜的控制以確保其安全和穩健的運行。傳統的功率流模型不容易分析導致功率部件故障的複雜原因及其相互作用。級聯故障一直是一個備受關注的課題；然而，由於缺乏可以結合連接系統的複雜相互作用的適當模型，至今沒有有效的工具來分析和預測故障級聯的傳播。 2015年，我們報告了一種使用複雜網絡角度進行電網魯棒性研究的新方法，我們的工作立即被納入了 IEEEXplore 2017年11月的創新聚焦。基於這個新方法，我們在2017年發布了一份文章，展示了使用該模型生成和解釋1996年和2003年北美洲停電時的傳播概況。在這項目中，我們的目標是進行一項嶄新的研究，將確定性潮流模型與基本隨機過程相結合，叫入廣泛的模擬和真實數據的收集，從而找出在確定安全和穩健性方面至關重要的拓撲屬性和操作參數，是電力網絡的運作更安全可靠。

15215019.label: Realisation of objectives
15215019.value: The project had progressed smoothly in accordance with the proposed plan, and has completed all objectives as set out in the original proposal. The project's main tasks were to "model", "analyze" and "verify", as detailed in our original proposed plan corresponding to the three key aims, respectively. The first task has resulted in models that allowed topological structure and cyber-coupling patterns to be conveniently examined and incorporated the deterministic power flow processes to generate realistic loading data. Specifically we adopted stochastic processes to describe the uncertain time to failure for each occurrence of component failure, resulting in cascade propagation to be generated in time scale. This has followed our main methodology proposed for this task and the detailed procedures have been developed and reported in our journal publications. In addition, we had also considered cyber-coupling as an extension of the model so as to describe the interactive processes that are specific in coupled networks, providing a practical means to assess the robustness of cyber-coupled power networks. Then, the second task aimed toward finding an effective analytical procedure to identify crucial parameters and structural properties of a cyber-coupled power networks, and the results allowed convenient analysis to be conducted to identify the relationship between parameters and propagation patterns. In particular, the information generated can expose how rapid a failure cascade may proceed and to what extent a blackout may occur after an initial failure. We particularly focused on the ranges of structural, operational and network parameters. Again, our results have been indicated highly satisfactory simulation processes that can quickly identify blackout extents and how cyber-coupling may intensify it. Our final task, as planned in our proposal, was aimed at verification and applications. We compared statistical results with historical data, and verified the proposed simulation processes that involved rather key practical steps in real-world power systems during a cascading failure process. We have completed 100% of all objectives within the proposed timeframe, and in fact we had gone beyond the three stated objectives and extended the project to investigate the impact of grid-connected power electronics, which paved the way for a next GRF project (which was funded two years later).

15215019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215019.value: As outlined in Section 5.3, this project has performed "modeling", "analysis" and "verification" in accordance with the set objectives, plans and methodologies, Our focus was cyber-coupled systems, and our major findings have contributed directly to the identification of the impact of cyber-coupling on the robustness of power systems, pinpointing the key system (and control) parameters, types of network structures and coupling patterns (i.e., connection styles) that significantly affected robust operation. The key findings include: 1. A model that simulates the behavior of power grids during failure events: This model accurately captures the complex interactions and connections within the grid. The simulations generated realistic scenarios of cascading failures by incorporating both predictable power flow processes and uncertain component failure times. 2. Identifying influential factors: We analyzed various factors that influence the spread of failures in power grids, including the robustness of the grid, the failure rates of different components, the structure of the network, and operational parameters. By studying these factors, we gained insights into how quickly failures can spread and how soon and to what extent a blackout can happen after an initial failure. 3. Validating with historical data: To ensure the relevance and accuracy of the simulations, the project compared the model's predictions with historical data and verified that simulations aligned well with real-world events. 4. Practical applications: The insights gained from this research can inform decision-making processes related to grid design, maintenance, and operational strategies. Additionally, the prediction methods developed can be applied to real power grids to assess their vulnerability to failure cascades and implement appropriate measures for grid resilience. The project generated SEVEN journal papers. Among these outputs, one full IEEE journal paper represents original contributions to modeling, reporting novel approaches to achieving a computationally feasible and analytically convenient model for subsequent studies. Another one describes the general modeling framework, and was written in the form of a tutorial published in an IEEE Transactions. Furthermore, detailed analytical methods and applications are reported in two journal papers, as well as an invited review paper that appeared in an IEEE Open Journal. The results reported there had included verifications with real-world data. The extension of the project, which went beyond the original objectives, had paved the way for continuous research efforts into the study of the evolving power grid, as summarized in another two IEEE Transactions papers that acknowledged the support of this funding.

15215019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215019.value: As mentioned in Section 6.1, the project had attempted to extend beyond the original objectives and to pave the way for continuous efforts into the research of the evolving power grid. Indeed, two years later, another GRF project was funded that focused on power electronics penetration which has been a key trend in the development of power grid, apart from the cyber-coupling development. This extension project is ongoing and is expected to generate impactful results for understanding the various factors affecting the robustness of power systems. We further expect to engage industrial partners (including local power companies and China's State Grid) to extend collaborative efforts and will be seeking RGC further support for a larger scale project.

15215019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215019.value: This research project successfully contributed to our understanding of power grid failures and their cascading effects. By creating realistic simulations, identifying influential factors, validating with historical data, and exploring practical applications, the project has provided valuable insights for enhancing power grid resilience and minimizing the occurrence and impact of blackouts. These achievements have important implications for maintaining a reliable and robust power supply for communities and industries. Specifically, the project investigated the causes and patterns of cascading failures in power grids, developed models to simulate these failures, and provided valuable insights for enhancing grid resilience and preventing widespread power outages. The findings have practical applications for improving power grid reliability. By understanding the causes and patterns of cascading failures, stakeholders in the energy sector can develop strategies to prevent or mitigate blackouts.

15215319.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15215319.value: 带約束的時間不一致隨機控制及若干金融應用

15215319.label: Project Objectives
15215319.value: While the field of time-inconsistent stochastic control has been well explored, little has been done to address problems with state-control constraints under random coefficients. This research project aims to fill this gap and study issues with practical relevance rooted in financial models. The first problem is a general time-inconsistent control problem with state-control constraints where the cost functional involves the conditional expected states. We shall apply Ekeland's variational principle to derive a Pontryagin type stochastic maximum principle for this problem. The second problem is a time-inconsistent linear-quadratic control problem where the dynamic system is linear, the cost functional is quadratic and state-control constraints follow linear inequalities. We plan to study this problem using coupled backward stochastic differential Riccati-like equations as well as the general results obtained in objective (2). The third problem is a dynamic time-inconsistent portfolio selection problem involving a piecewise linear state-dependent function in the cost functional with no-shorting and borrowing constraints based on a behavioral risk aversion criteria. We plan to extend the findings obtained in objectives (2) and (3) to address this research question.

15215319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15215319.value: 带約束的時間不一致隨機控制問題在科學，工程，經濟學和金融投資的各個領域中非常重要。最近，人們越來越關注研究這種類型的時間不一致的隨機控制問題以及解決其應用問題。與標準隨機控制問題相比，在一些最近時間不一致的線性二次控制問題和均值 - 方差投資組合選擇問題中，動力系統，代价泛函或兩者中都不僅涉及狀態而且涉及它的期望值。這一關鍵特徵使得這些問題不能滿足Bellman的最優性原則，因此导致通常的动态规划方法失败。然而，在現實生活中，當人們期望在財富与投資組合（即狀態与控制）約束和隨機係數下更好地管理風險時，情況就更加複雜。本項目旨在解決隨機係數下的狀態与控制約束這一難題，不僅考慮其理論意義，而且考慮其實際重要性。在這個擬議的研究項目中，我們計劃開發一些新的方法，這些方法應該與現有文獻中沒有約束的時間不一致的隨機控制問題顯著不同，以應對上述特徵自然產生的困難。此外，我們將把我們的理論結果應用於具有挑戰性但又具有實際意義且重要的決策模型，比如在金融投資中不可卖空和借貸約束問題。該模型將幫助投資者更好地理解和有效控制風險，以便在有限的投資範圍內實現更高的回報。

15215319.label: Realisation of objectives
15215319.value: This project mainly investigated a class of time-inconsistent problems featuring both stochastic control and stochastic systems with constraints over a finite/infinite time horizon. We developed new methodologies, which are significantly different from those in the existing literature's standard control theory. In our models, the inclusion of constraints introduces significant technical difficulties, including random coefficients, which lead to its theoretical significance and its practical importance. We considered a class of time-inconsistent investment problems such as no-shorting rules, borrowing constraints and consumption constraint, further developed the theory and presented the numerical examples (papers 3, 4, 6 and 12 in Part C). We showed that the value function is strictly increasing yet strictly concave in the wealth variable. In particular, comparing with the existing literature, the utility measures the difference between the control and its running maximum, and a nonnegativity constraint on consumption is imposed. Also, we studied indefinite time-inconsistent stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ, for short) control problems, which allow the weighting matrices for state and control in the cost functional to be indefinite (papers 8 and 9 in Part C), including mean-field terms. We developed two-person mean-field LQ non-zero sum stochastic differential games in an infinite horizon. The existence of an open-loop Nash equilibrium is characterized by the solvability of a system of mean-field forward-backward stochastic differential equations in an infinite horizon and the convexity of the cost functionals, and the closed-loop representation of an open-loop Nash equilibrium is given through the solution to a system of two coupled non-symmetric algebraic Riccati equations. The existence of a closed-loop Nash equilibrium is characterized by the solvability of a system of two coupled symmetric algebraic Riccati equations (paper 9 in Part C). Besides the above works, we studied a reinforcement learning (RL) method to solve infinite horizon continuous-time stochastic LQ problems, where the drift and diffusion terms in the dynamics may depend on both the state and control. Based on the Bellman’s dynamic programming principle, we presented an online RL algorithm to attain optimal control with partial system information (paper 5 in Part C). We further developed this theoretical result to tackle a class of time-inconsistent control problems featuring delayed terms (papers 8, 11 and 13 in Part C). During this project period, we also investigated open-loop and closed-loop solvabilities of stochastic LQ optimal control problems with random coefficients and Markovian regime-switching system (papers 1, 10 and 12 in Part C). We provided an alternative characterization of the open-loop solvability of the LQ problem using a perturbation approach. Then we studied the closed-loop solvability of the LQ problem of the Markovian regime-switching system. In particular, we established the equivalence between the open-loop (closed-loop, resp.) solvability and the existence of an adapted solution to the corresponding forward-backward stochastic differential equation with constraint, and applied the theoretical results established in this project to treat a continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem with random coefficients and Markovian regime-switching system (paper 1 in Part C). The results obtained from our work are expected to help readers have a better understanding of stochastic LQ control based on the Markov chain model. In paper 8 in Part C, we analyzed time-inconsistent control and stabilization problems for continuous-time mean-field systems with input delay, which are the fundamental development of control and stabilization problems for mean-field systems. We established the necessary and sufficient solvability condition for this kind of time-inconsistent control problem with input delay, and derived the analytical form of an optimal controller through overcoming the obstacle that separation principle no longer holds for multiplicative-noise systems. In paper 13 in Part C, we studied partially-observed time-inconsistent control problems for the state governed by stochastic differential equation with delay. We developed a stochastic maximum principle for this kind of control problems using a variational method and a filtering technique. Also, we established a sufficient condition without assumption of the concavity. Besides these, we also introduced the above methods to study continuous-time and discrete-time portfolio selection problems in financial investment (papers 4, 6, 7 and 12 in Part C). In addition to contributing to the academic literature, our research has important and practical significance. With the alarm bell's sounding and the ongoing financial crisis, risk hedging has attracted more attention than ever before. Among various hedging methods and managing risks, institutional investors prefer consumption cost, non-smooth utility, and mean-variance portfolio selections under stochastic systems. We performed a sensitivity analysis of the value function, the optimal consumption and portfolio on some model parameters, namely the reference degree parameter, the mean return and the volatility of the risky asset, and discussed some quantitative properties and their financial implications. Moreover, our approach is easily implementable with a standard numerical technique, and therefore it provides managers with a usable way to make decisions.

15215319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15215319.value: This project is to deal with time-inconsistent control problems with constraints in many fields such as science, engineering, economics, management, and especially financial investment. We mainly revisited some challenging, yet practically important wealth management models over a finite/infinite time investment horizon, reformulated them as time-inconsistent control problems with constraints, and derived their equilibrium analytical strategies. Also, we analyzed stochastic differential games over an infinite time horizon using coupled Riccati equations within a game-theoretic framework during this project period. Besides these, we developed a reinforcement learning (RL) method to solve infinite horizon continuous-time stochastic LQ problems, and also tackled a class of time-inconsistent control problems including delayed terms. Although we did not project expenses for graduate student training in the original GRF proposal submitted to RGC in October 2018, our university appointed Mr. Si Kehan as a Research Assistant to work with us on this GRF-sponsored project in the period of 7 August 2020 – 7 February 2021. On or before 31 December 2020, he was a PhD student of Shandong University. Our university appointed Mr. Zeng Yijie as a Research Assistant in this GRF project during the period from 11 July to September 30 2022 and then I provided PhD supervision to Mr. Zeng after his completing service for this project. He will graduate at the end of 2027 from our university. In the future, I will pay more attention to the training of research postgraduate students. During this project period, I attended at the 10th International Congress on Industrial and Applied Mathematics from 20 to 25 August 2023 in Tokyo. I presented an invited talk at Recent Advances on Quantitative Finance from 27 to 30 August 2023 in Hong Kong. I participated in SIAM Conference on Financial Mathematics and Engineering and introduced our research works in Phildelphia, USA from 6 to 9 June 2023. I attended the 9th International Colloquium on BSDEs and Mean Field in Annecy, France from 26 June to 1 July 2022. This conference invited specialists from various universities, including those from Princeton University, University of California at Berkeley, University of Edinburgh, Imperial College, ETH Zurich, etc. Also, I served on the organizing committee of the 11th World Congress of Bachelier Finance Society and gave a talk in Hong Kong from 13 to 17 June 2022. In addition, we obtained Award in Natural Science for the Chinese Association of Automation (First Prize) on November 24, 2022.

15215319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15215319.value: Although the research in this direction has been well developed for constrained control problems under mean-field stochastic differential equations, it lacks progress in both theoretical investigation and applications for standard and non-standard time-inconsistent problems within the more general stochastic system framework, such as path-dependent, delayed, and partially-observed stochastic differential equations. We will further study these potential research works in the future. [1] Our methodologies and techniques on portfolio selection can be adopted to analyze behavioral portfolio selection, while one encounters investment problem with reference to the historical consumption maximum over his/her investment time horizon. We will further develop those results established in papers 4 and 6 of Part C in the future. [2] Our methods developed in this project can be applied to two-person mean-field LQ non-zero sum stochastic differential games with random coefficients and Markovian regime switching system over a finite/infinite time horizon. We will further study the corresponding techniques in papers 1, 3, 9, 10 and 12 of Part C so that we solve the above problems. [3] Reinforcement learning method proposed in this project (paper 5 in Part C) can be further employed to study more general stochastic control problems over a finite/infinite time horizon.

15215319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15215319.value: As for the theoretical contributions, this study will contribute to the literature on various topics. Specific to the literature on portfolio theory and investment, we expect the results to help shed light on the investment strategies (papers 1, 3, 6, 7 and 12 in Part C). In addition, the methods adopted in the current research program will also improve the optimal control studied and the implementations developed in the field of stochastic control constraints (papers 3, 4, 6 and 12 in Part C) and under the regime-switching system (papers 1, 10 and 12 in Part C). In particular, one of our findings provides a fundamental tool (papers 6 and 13 in Part C) to study the delayed problems with random coefficients in the future. We studied two-person mean-field LQ non-zero sum stochastic differential games over an infinite horizon using open-loop and closed-loop Nash equilibria (paper 9 in Part C). Besides these, introducing reinforcement learning method paves the avenue for analyzing a class of optimal stochastic control problems (paper 5 in Part C). Therefore, this project is believed to be of value and of practical importance with long-term significance, and it helps provide risk-management advice for policy makers and institutional investors.

15216519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216519.value: 物聯網將促進政府公共服務、智慧城市和工業製造業等領域的創新及應用。然而，重要科學問題有待解決。首先，當前的低功耗廣域網採用集中式網絡模型，其中所有數據包都需要通過回程網絡中繼到中央服務器。隨著低功耗廣域網的迅速擴展，回程網絡可能成為瓶頸並限製網絡可擴展性。其次，物聯網設備的並發傳輸將導致網關衝突。此外，因為低功耗物聯網設備容易受到許多主動攻擊，物聯網設備的安全性也引起了公眾的關注。當前的低功耗廣域網在網絡層及以上採用傳統的安全機制（例如，端到端加密，認證），而物理層並未受到足夠保護。 本項目提出一種用於低功耗廣域網的邊緣計算協作框架，以提高低功耗廣域網的可擴展性並增強其安全性。1）為提高網關的可擴展性，我們開發了物理層衝突恢復技術，以解決網關衝突並支持更多物聯網設備的並發傳輸。 2）為減輕網絡服務器的工作量，我們將工作負載從網絡服務器轉移到分佈在網絡邊緣的大量網關。在協作框架中，網關使用概率數據結構壓縮數據，檢測重複數據包，並避免不必要的傳輸以降低網絡負擔。 3）為檢測隱蔽通道並保護物聯網設備，我們開發了一種基於機器學習的物理層隱蔽通道檢測技術。

Study the feasibility of applying the established procedures, inverse models and validated lab results for in-situ mapping of material damages.

15216619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15216619.value: Various shallow subsurface surface damages deteriorate infrastructures, like horizontal delamination and water seepage in concrete and road structures. Visual inspection is very limited. Alternative nondestructive testing and imaging method, such as ground penetrating radar (GPR), is popular for locating buried objects within infrastructure in last two decades. However, extension from object location to imaging and diagnosis in GPR is still relatively uncommon. Part of the reasons is the usual fixed distance between one transmitter (Tx) and one receiver (Rx) restraining the only wave mode called 'reflection'. In this proposed work with partnership with scientists from Germany and Canada, refraction wave mode will be attempted by separating the Tx and Rx antennas via wide angle reflection and refraction (WARR). WARR shall be suitable to measure horizontal delamination and localized patch water seepage in concrete and pavement which leading to formation of GPR’s waveguide paths. Most GPR works with one transmitter sending pulses into the material and the reflections from interfaces are collected by another receiver, or known as reflection mode. However, wave in materials can be characterized into different wave modes, such as the ground wave and critically refracted wave, and its dispersions studied in this work. Such dispersion is similar to white light dispersed into rainbow colors after passing through a prism, and to multi-channel analysis of surface wave (MASW) in seismology. Such methodology has two advantages. Firstly, the broadband wave is dispersed in different frequency bandwidths, resulting in velocity dispersion which can be measured by WARR’s dispersion analysis, in addition to traditional common offset profiling (COP) with fixed distance between transmitter and receiver. Secondly, material damages such as horizontal delamination and localized patch water seepage become waveguides causing different velocity dispersions realized after inversion. In this work, these shallow subsurface damages will be generated experimentally to validate the measurement methods and algorithms, then characterized by electromagnetic wave’s inversion with the Jonscher 4p-variant model. Data collection will be in two GPR bandwidths, one centered at 500/1000MHz for pavement structures and another at 2000MHz for concrete structures. Preliminary findings have proven to be convincing in the PI’s previous works with the German Co-I, and a work by the Canadian Co-I’s team. The deliverables will have long term impacts on both theory and practice. The theoretical side refers to development of inversion procedures for frequency-dependent phase velocity mapping. The practical aspects refer to spatial mapping of GPR waveguide in damaged materials in infrastructures. 各種淺層地下表面的破損會破壞基礎設施，如混凝土和道路結構中的水平分層和滲水。目視檢查非常有限，替代的無損檢測和成像方法，例如探地雷達（GPR），在過去二十年中非常適用於在基礎設施內定位埋藏的物體。然而， GPR的成像和診斷仍然相對不常見。部分原因是一個發射器（Tx）和一個接收器（Rx）之間的通常固定距離限制了唯一稱為“反射”的波傳遞模式。在與德國和加拿大科學家合作的這項擬議工作中，將通過廣角反射和折射（WARR）分離Tx和Rx天線來嘗試折射波模式。 WARR適用於測量混凝土和路面中的水平分層和局部水滲漏，導致GPR波導路徑的形成。 大多數發射器一邊發射脈衝進入材料，接口的反射由另一邊的接收器收集，稱為反射模式。然而，材料中的波可以被表徵為不同的波傳遞模式，例如地表波和臨界折射波，並且在這項目中研究它的色散特性。這種色散類似於通過棱鏡後分散成彩虹色的白光，以及地震學中表面波（MASW）的多通道分析。這種方法有兩個優點。首先，寬帶波分散在不同的頻率帶寬中，除了傳統的固定較短距離切面分析（COP）和可調但仍固定的距離分析之外，還可以通過WARR的色散分析來測量不同頻率波的速度。其次，水平分層和局部補片水滲漏等材料損傷成為波導媒介和色散的原因。在這項工作中，這些淺的次表面損傷將通過實驗，以驗證測量方法和算法，然後用Jonscher 4p變量模型的電磁波反演進行表徵診斷。數據採集將採用兩個GPR帶寬，一個以500 / 1000MHz為中心用於路面結構，另一個用於2000MHz用於混凝土結構。事實證明，初步調查結果在PI先前與德國Co-I的合作以及加拿大Co-I團隊的工作中具說服力。 可交付成果將對理論和實踐產生長期影響。理論方面指的是頻率相關速度的色散反演程序。實際方面是以GPR導波診斷基礎設施中材料淺層受損的程度。

15216619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15216619.value: This work studies the dispersion of GPR wave’s phase velocity at different wide-band frequencies in plywood and concrete with varying moisture content, using wide angle reflection and refraction (WARR). In homogeneous materials, spectral analysis of the surface wave (SASW) was done (Lai et al. 2021) and In waveguide layered material structures, full waveform inversion based on fundamental equation of modal theory was adopted (He et al. 2023). For homogeneous material (Lai et al., 2021), the computation of phase velocities is based on the acquisition of the cross-power spectrum and phase unwrap of two distorted ground waves at positions closer to and farther away from the transmitting antenna. The velocities of the ground waves are found to experience greater dispersion in low frequency regimes within the effective frequency bandwidths deter mined and thresholded by time–frequency analysis (TFA) and coherence plotting of the ground waves. This study validates the optimal distance between the first (Rx1) and second (Rx2) receivers as k/2, based on a fixed transmitter (Tx) minus the first receiver (Rx1) distance. It serves as an indication of changeable separation distance when other lower frequency GPR is used because the distances of Tx-Rx1 and Rx1-Rx2 are wavelength- and frequency-dependent. Effects of moisture contents and chloride contamination in concrete were also characterized according to the dispersion plots . that wave travelling in lower frequencies in GPR wave is much decelerated than that in higher frequencies. For waveguide in layered material structures (He et al. 2023), detection of layered materials, e.g. delamination in asphalt pavement by GPR is useful for effective maintenance and repair. However, limitations of GPR survey resolution and multiple wave interferences have made thin delamination layer characterization a challenging task in conventional common offset profiling (COP) mode. A new method is proposed for characterizing delamination layers in asphalt pavement using the GPR waveguide dispersion model in a WARR configuration. The approach was validated through synthetic experiments and laboratory experiments using an asphalt pavement model. Our results show that the cutoff frequencies of all modes are sensitive to air-filled delamination, while water-filled delamination leads to a significant decrease in the phase velocity of GPR waves. By observing these trends, we are able to detect delamination layers with 1 cm thickness and identify delamination layers with different properties. This new method can aid in the detection and identification of delamination layers in asphalt pavement structures.

This research also contributes to the realization of the effects of wave dispersion on phase velocity and the inverse modelling to characterize variations in the material properties of infrastructure as a means of detecting surface damage, such as road delaminations filled with or without water.

15217019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217019.value: The phylogenetic tree is a 150-year-old data structure used by scientists and scholars to describe evolutionary history. Given a set of objects created by an evolutionary process (such as biological species, different types of tumor cells in a patient, natural languages, or hand-copied medieval manuscripts), a phylogenetic tree represents the objects by leaves and their common ancestors by internal nodes so that the branching structure reflects the evolutionary relationships. Such trees can help scientists to understand the mechanisms of evolution, to organize information, and to deduce knowledge about the past. Despite their success and popularity, three serious limitations of the currently existing mainstream algorithms for building phylogenetic trees are: 1. Their running times are too high to handle big data. 2. They are sensitive to errors in the input. 3. The phylogenetic tree model is not powerful enough to express non-treelike evolutionary events such as lateral gene transfer or hybridization in biology. The goal of this project is to deal with these shortcomings. Our approach is to develop and analyze efficient algorithms for a number of well-defined computational problems related to limitations 1, 2, and 3 above. In particular, for 1, we will investigate how to approximate a huge phylogenetic tree by a simplified one (containing much fewer internal nodes) without destroying too much branching information, in order to obtain fast algorithms that are scalable to big data. For 2, we will define a new type of consensus tree to deal with noise and errors in the input data. For 3, we will focus on the more general phylogenetic network model and study the combinatorics of phylogenetic networks in order to find some combinatorial structure that can be exploited to obtain fast algorithms for building and comparing such networks. 系統發育樹是一個有150年曆史的數據結構，由科學家和學者用來描述進化史。給定由進化過程創建的一組對象（例如生物物種，患者中不同類型的腫瘤細胞，自然語言或手工複製的中世紀手稿），系統發育樹通過葉子及其共同祖先通過內部表示對象節點使分支結構反映了進化關係。這些樹可以幫助科學家理解進化的機制，組織信息，並推斷出有關過去的知識。 儘管它們的成功和普及，但是目前存在的用於構建系統發育樹的主流算法存在兩個嚴重的局限性是： 1.他們的運行時間太長，無法處理大數據。 2.他們對輸入中的錯誤很敏感。 該項目的目標是解決這些缺點。 我們的方法是針對與上述限制1和2相關的許多明確定義的計算問題開發和分析有效算法。 特別地，對於1，我們將研究如何通過簡化的系統發生樹（包含更少的內部節點）來近似一個巨大的系統發育樹而不破壞太多的分支信息，以便獲得可擴展到大數據的快速算法。 對於2，我們將定義一種新類型的共識樹來處理輸入數據中的噪聲和錯誤。

15217019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217019.value: In publication 2 in Part C, we combined two fundamental, previously studied optimization problems related to the construction of phylogenetic trees called maximum rooted triplets consistency (MAXRTC) and minimally resolved supertree (MINRS) into a new problem, which we call q-maximum rooted triplets consistency (q-MAXRTC). The input to our new problem is a set R of resolved triplets (rooted, binary phylogenetic trees with three leaves each) and the objective is to find a phylogenetic tree with exactly q internal nodes that contains the largest possible number of triplets from R. Our first new result was that that q-MAXRTC is NP-hard even to approximate within a constant ratio for every fixed q >= 2. For this reason, we then developed various polynomial-time approximation algorithms for different values of q. Next, we showed experimentally that representing a phylogenetic tree by one having much fewer nodes typically does not destroy too much triplet branching information. As an extreme example, we showed that allowing only nine internal nodes is still sufficient to capture on average 80% of the rooted triplets from some recently published trees, each having between 760 and 3081 internal nodes. Finally, to demonstrate the algorithmic advantage of using trees with few internal nodes, we proposed a new algorithm for computing the rooted triplet distance between two phylogenetic trees over a leaf label set of size n that runs in O(q n) time, where q is the number of internal nodes in the smaller tree. This is faster than the currently best algorithms for the problem (with O(n log n) time complexity [SODA 2013, ESA 2017]} whenever q = o(log n). We have also shown that the rooted triplet distance can be computed in O(n sqrt(log n)) time in the special case of two input caterpillars with n leaves each [see publication 1 in Part C].

15217019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217019.value: It would be interesting to further investigate how quickly the rooted triplet distance between two phylogenetic trees with n leaf labels can be computed. As mentioned in point 6.1, the problem is known to be solvable in O(n log n) time [SODA 2013, ESA 2017]. However, the only known lower bound on the time complexity is the trivial one of Omega(n). Thus, there is a gap between the known upper and lower bounds, and to close this gap is a major open problem. In publications 1 and 2 in Part C, we have presented algorithms that go below the O(n log n)-time upper bound for certain special classes of inputs. Although this doesn't solve the open problem, it makes some partial progress. Whether or not the techniques developed here can be extended to more general inputs remains to be seen, but we believe our findings open up an interesting new research direction and that they show there is hope for an o(n log n)-time (i.e., faster than O(n log n) time) algorithm for the general case.

15217119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217119.value: This project aims to investigate the local and global buckling resistance of fabricated high strength steel regular and irregular octagonal tubular section structures subject to monotonic concentric compression. The structures are formed using high strength steel plates in the grades of S460 and S690 which are the most commonly used high strength steel in structural applications. Octagonal tubular structures are fabricated by cold-forming steel plates into half-sections with different geometries and dimensions and subsequently welding half-sections together to form the target shapes. Such structures provide the flexibility for the architects and engineers to employ different geometries to suit a variety of design and engineering purposes. The octagonal tubular sections allow to obtain better local buckling resistance than square and rectangular tubular cross-sections while the flat surfaces of the sections enable the easier formation of connections with any in-coming members comparing with the circular tubular sections. In addition, the potential to be applied to form concrete-filled tubular members will also enhance the structural load-carrying capacity and bring the further benefit of fast-track construction since the octagonal tubular members are used as the formwork to eliminate the need of temporary formwork for concrete-casting. However, no design rules are available to predict the cross-sectional and member behaviour of the structures subject to critical loads. Therefore, this project aims firstly to characterise the local buckling behaviour of the structures subject to concentric compression in order to develop the design approaches at cross-section level and, secondly, to examine the global buckling behaviour of the structures subject to concentric compression in order to develop the design approaches for predicting the global buckling resistance of the structures. Both experimental and numerical investigations will be carried out to obtain a clear understanding on the local and global buckling behaviour of the high strength steel regular and irregular octagonal tubular members subject to concentric compression. The research output of this project will add values to the research area of high strength steel structures and contribute to facilitating the applications of high strength steel in construction. 此項目主要目標為研究高强鋼冷彎正八邊形及非正八邊形鋼管柱結構受軸向靜壓力條件下的局部及整體失穩强度。所研究的結構使用S460及S690高强鋼加工而成，此兩類鋼材為工業中應用較廣汎的高强鋼材料。八邊形鋼管結構加工過程為先由高强鋼板冷彎成半個八邊形截面，再將兩個冷彎半截面通過焊接製成每個八邊形鋼管結構。此類正八邊形及非正八邊形鋼管結構可以根據建築及結構工程師設計要求靈活製成、以滿足多種工程應用的要求。與正方形、長方形鋼管結構相比，八邊形鋼管結構有更高的局部失穩强度。與圓形鋼管結構相較，八邊形結構的八個平面板亦使其更易與其他結構連接，使節點加工及建設更方便。此外，八邊形鋼管結構亦可用與建造鋼管混凝土結構、實現更高的承載力、并且鋼管作爲混凝土澆築外模可實現快速施工。然而，目前尚未有設計槼範可用於計算高强鋼八邊形鋼管結構在不同受力情況下的截面及整體結構强度。因此，本項目首先研究高强鋼八邊形鋼管短柱結構在軸壓下的局部失穩受力特性、並提出設計結構强度公式。其次，本項目亦研究高强鋼八邊形鋼管柱受壓下的整體失穩受力特性、並提出設計結構强度公式。為研究以上具體問題，實驗及數值分析研究將展開、以得到充分的關於正八邊形及非正八邊形鋼管柱結構受軸向靜壓力條件下的局部及整體失穩受力特性數據。以上所得結果將為高强鋼結構研究領域增加研究成果並為推廣高强鋼結構應用做出貢獻。

15217119.label: Realisation of objectives
15217119.value: Objective 1 has been achieved through the following comprehensive investigations: Understanding the complicated relationship between the manufacturing process, mechanical performance, and structural integrity of the cold-formed steel octagonal hollow section (OctHS) columns, is crucial for both designers and engineers to achieve proper structural design. During the manufacturing process of cold-formed OctHSs, the cold-forming process generates permanent plastic deformation in shaping the cross-sections, and leads to two significant characteristics: residual stresses and changes in material properties within the cold-formed corner regions. These characteristics are interconnected and tend to compensate each other within the cross-section. In this project, an experimental programme was conducted to analyse the variation in material properties and the distribution of residual stresses within high strength irregular OctHSs. New material constitutive models were proposed to characterise the stress-strain responses of high strength irregular OctHS materials with and without yield plateau. Additionally, measurements of residual stresses were performed on four high strength irregular OctHSs. Based on the obtained measurement results, a residual stress pattern predictive model was proposed for high strength irregular OctHSs. In addition, extensive experimental investigations to analyse the effects of cold-forming were conducted. Normal and high strength steel plates were employed in the material tests. A total of 93 flat tensile coupons extracted from the parent steel plates and 212 corner tensile coupons machined from the cold-formed corners were tested. The test results reveal that the mechanism behind changes in material properties due to cold-forming does not differ significantly across steel grades, indicating a lack of distinct boundaries between normal and high strength steel. In conjunction with the experimental results, a substantial database was compiled, consisting of test results on 341 flat tensile coupons and 613 corner tensile coupons. Semi-empirical models were subsequently developed using this extensive database to predict the changes in material properties of cold-formed steel. Objective 2 and 3 has been achieved through the following comprehensive investigations: The global buckling behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel regular and irregular OctHS long columns under concentric compression was first studied through experimental investigation. A total of 22 regular and irregular OctHS long column specimens were fabricated through four types of high strength steel plates, Q460 3mm, Q460 6mm, Q690 3mm, and Q690 6mm. To fabricate the regular and irregular OctHSs with different aspect ratios, two half sections were first formed by press-braking, and were then welded together to assemble the whole OctHS. Under proper control of welding parameters, it is believed that there is almost no reduction in the mechanical properties of high strength welded sections. The measured yield strengths of flat coupons ranged from 541 to 753 MPa, while those of cold-formed corner coupons ranged from 669 to 900 MPa. Pin-ended long column tests were conducted on 22 regular and irregular OctHS columns. The axial load versus mid-height lateral deflection curve, axial load versus axial strain curve, maximum capacity, and failure mode of each specimen were reported. Additionally, numerical investigations into cold-formed high strength steel regular and irregular OctHS long columns were conducted. Finite element models for both regular and irregular OctHS long columns were validated against the experimental test results, including the axial load versus mid-height lateral deflection curves, maximum capacity, and failure modes. Validation results indicate that the developed finite element model can accurately capture the global buckling behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel regular and irregular OctHS long columns. After FEM validation, extensive parametric studies were conducted on OctHS long columns. The analysis of the parametric studies explored the effects of steel grades, cross-sections, aspect ratios, and member slenderness on the structural behaviour of cold-formed steel regular and irregular OctHS long columns. Furthermore, the test results combined with the numerical results were used to evaluate the applicability of current steel design codes, such as the European code EN 1993-1-1:2022, the Chinese standard GB 50017-2017, the American specifications ANSI/AISC 360-22 and ASCE/SEI 48-19, and the Australian standard AS 4100:2020, on the column buckling strength design of cold-formed steel regular and irregular OctHS long columns. Based on the evaluation results, it can be summarised that the modified Eurocode 3 method can greatly improve the prediction accuracy and consistency as compared with the original method which adopts column curve “b”, but a larger partial factor γM* of 1.10 should be incorporated to achieve the required safety level. Moreover, it was observed that utilizing curve ‘a’ in GB 50017–2017 achieves the highest prediction accuracy. ANSI/AISC 360–22 and AS 4100:2020 also provide reasonably accurate prediction results for OctHS column design. However, the ASCE/SEI 48–19 design method tends to overestimate the column strength for a majority of OctHS columns. A design recommendation is proposed to address this overestimation issue by adopting the same design expressions from ANSI/AISC 360–22 within the ASCE/SEI 48–19 method. In conclusion, the codified design methodologies from Eurocode 3 (curve ‘b’), GB 50017–2017 (curve ‘a’), ANSI/AISC 360–22, and AS 4100:2020 are recommended for the flexural buckling design of OctHS columns due to their accuracy and reliability in prediction results.
