15217119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217119.value: Residual stress distributions of cold-formed high strength steel irregular OctHSs and changes in material properties of cold-formed steels were investigated in this project. A predictive model for residual stresses in cold-formed high strength irregular OctHSs was proposed. Corresponding material constitutive models were developed to construct the stress-strain responses of high strength irregular OctHS materials with and without yield plateau. A series of predictive models were proposed to predict the changes in material properties of corner material after cold-forming. Detailed findings are summarised in Liu, Fang and Chan (2022), Liu, Chen and Chan (2023), and Liu, Chen and Chan (accepted). The research also involves comprehensive experimental and numerical investigations focused on the global buckling behaviour of cold-formed high strength steel regular and irregular OctHS long columns. Various parameters including cross-sectional slenderness, aspect ratios, steel grades, and specimen lengths were deliberately chosen to study their influence on the global buckling behaviour. Experimental and numerical data, including axial load versus mid-height lateral deflection curves, axial load versus axial strain curves, maximum capacities, and failure modes, were reported. Existing design codes from European code, Chinese standard, American specifications, and Australian code were discussed and evaluated based on the collected experimental and numerical data. Subsequently, design recommendations on the column buckling strength design of cold-formed steel regular and irregular OctHS columns under concentric compression were proposed. Comprehensive details and findings of this research are summarised in publications by Liu et al. (2021), Liu, Zhu and Chan (under review), and Liu, Zhu and Chan (2023).

15217119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217119.value: This research investigates the residual stress pattern, cold-forming effect, and global buckling behaviour of cold-formed high strength regular and irregular OctHS columns. To implement the reported research, the structural behaviour of cold-formed steel regular and irregular OctHS beam-columns (under the combination of compression and bending) is worth investigating. This further investigation is to complete the design rules of regular and irregular OctHS column under different loading scenarios, and to promote the use of OctHS columns in practical engineering applications. Furthermore, the incorporation of concrete infill within OctHS long columns and beam-columns has the potential to greatly increase the load-carrying capacity. This hybrid structure offers the additional advantage of accelerating construction processes, particularly as the outer OctHS steel tube can act as the temporary formwork during concrete casting. Further development of corresponding design provisions can be conducted through a comprehensive investigation including experimental and numerical investigations. These investigations can effectively contribute to refining and enhancing the design guidelines for such composite OctHS column structures, optimising their structural efficiency and performance.

15217119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217119.value: This project proposes to investigate the fabrication induced-residual stresses, cross-section capacity, and member buckling strength of cold-formed high strength steel regular and irregular octagonal hollow section columns under concentric compression. This unique type of structural steel member, composed of eight equal or unequal sides, can be easily manufactured by cold-forming and subsequent welding, without the need for a large-scale production machine. Compared to the most used circular hollow section columns, the multiple flat surfaces feature of octagonal hollow section columns can provide a construction platform for performing beam-column joint connections or meet some specific construction and design purposes. To facilitate the practical use of regular and irregular octagonal hollow section columns in the field of civil engineering, a comprehensive investigation programme including experimental and numerical studies, was performed. Through the investigations, the structural behaviours of octagonal hollow sections from the cross-section and member levels have been well understood. Moreover, corresponding design rules and recommendations have been proposed based on the investigation results.

15217219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217219.value: This proposed study concerns with the overall performance enhancement of plenum windows, which are potential ventilation-enabling sound insulation devices for application in congested high-rise cities. Traffic noise pollution control and sustainable ventilation have long been a challenging task for all stakeholders. The situation is expected to get worse as more and more people will live in cities. In the urban areas, conventional mitigation measures, such as noise barriers, have been proven not to be solutions. Neither are balconies, as the reflections at their ceilings and city reverberation significantly offset their barrier effects. The soundscape approach is also not working for high traffic noise levels. Closing windows, multi-glazing windows and similar mitigating measures are not acceptable as they adversely affect natural ventilation inside residential units. Mechanical ventilation can help, but the required electrical energy consumption is not welcome for sustainability considerations. Urban redevelopment usually takes place in areas which were regarded as noise tolerant in the past and thus are all noisy places. This adds to the challenge of noise protection and high quality natural ventilation. Plenum windows are partially opened double-glazing windows. The two openings and the space between the two glass panes form a passageway, allowing air movement between the openings. Plenum windows can offer reasonable sound insulation levels while also meeting minimum local statutory natural ventilation requirement. They provide a potential solution and have been adopted in several residential building projects. However, owing to the shortage of buildable land and because less noisy sites are increasingly hard to find, one has to cope with increasingly noisy sites. Under the current plenum window design, higher sound insulation levels do tend to jeopardize air movement. This study seeks to provide solutions which enhance both the sound insulation of and the air movement across plenum windows using sonic crystals (sound scatterer arrays) and aerodynamically designed louvres. It is proposed to carry out an in-depth parametric analysis to provide a fundamental understanding of how sonic crystals interact/couple with various acoustic modes inside confined spaces and on the subsequent improvement of plenum window performance in terms of sound insulation and air movement when they are assisted by aerodynamically designed louvres. Numerical simulations, theoretical analyses, experimental investigations and field tests will be carried out. Combined the sonic crystals and Venturi effect of the louvre structures will enable significantly better air movement and high sound insulations. 這項擬議的研究涉及隔音通風窗的整體性能增強。隔音通風窗是一種極具潛力又適用於擁擠的高層城市的通風隔音裝置。 交通噪聲污染控制和持續通風長期以來一直是所有持份者面對的挑戰。隨著越來越多的人居住在城市，情況預計會變得更糟。在城市地區，傳統的緩解噪聲措施，如隔音屏障，已被證明不是解決方案。也不是陽台，因為它們的天花板的反射和城市混響大大抵消了它們的隔音屏障效應。音景方法也不適用於高交通噪音水平的情況。關閉窗戶，多層玻璃窗和類似的緩解措施是不可接受的，因為它們會對住宅單元內的自然通風產生不利影響。機械通風可以提供幫助，但出於可持續性考慮，不歡迎所需的電能消耗。城市重建通常發生在過去被視為噪音容忍的地區，因此都是嘈雜的地方。這增加了噪音保護和高品質自然通風的挑戰。 隔音通風窗是部分打開的雙層玻璃窗。兩個開口和兩個玻璃板之間的空間造成通道，允許空氣在開口之間移動。隔音通風窗可以提供合理的隔音水平，同時還滿足當地法定的自然通風要求。它們提供了一種解決隔音通風的方案，並已被多個住宅建築項目採用。然而，由於可建造土地的短缺，並且由於越來越難以找到較低嘈雜場地，因此我們必須應對越來越多的嘈雜場地。在目前的隔音通風窗設計下，達致較高的隔音水平確實會危及空氣流動。本研究旨在提供解決方案，使用聲波晶體（聲音散射體陣列）和空氣動力學設計的百葉窗，增強隔風通風窗的隔音能力和空氣運動。 建議進行深入的參數分析，以便基本了解聲波晶體如何與受限空間內的各種聲學模式相互作用/耦合，以及隨後在聲音絕緣和空氣運動方面，由空氣動力學設計的百葉窗輔助下改善隔風通風窗的整體性能。也將進行數值模擬，理論分析，實驗研究和現場試驗。結合了百葉窗結構的聲音晶體和文丘里效應，可以顯著改善空氣流動和高隔音效果。

15217219.label: Realisation of objectives
15217219.value: The first and the fourth objective are 100% completed. Our research progress has involved exploring various configurations of plenum windows (PW) and sonic crystals (SC) arrays installed within the PW. Through designed numerical simulations and experiments, we have analyzed the noise insulation performance and aerodynamic effects of each configuration. The results have shown the positive impact of SC in creating a 'bandgap' (a frequency range where noise propagation is blocked) in reducing noise within the PW. We have also studied the natural acoustic modes within the PW cavity and investigated their influence, such as their coupling with the SC bandgap, on the overall performance of the PW. However, we have discovered a limitation in the ability of PW with SC to mitigate low-frequency noise, which we have detailed in our publication. We replace the non-resonating SC currently used with a slit resonator, known for generating lower-frequency bandgaps, and the sound transmission losses are improved. We add in louvers at the entrance section of the PW before the SC, the louvers, under appropriate configurations, they increase the air velocity within the PW, and give rise to improved indoor ventilation. The second objective is also fully accomplished. We have conducted numerical simulations and experiments to comprehensively study the impact of lattice constant, scatterer sizes, and lattice orientation of SC on the noise reduction performance of PW. Our study encompasses two choices of lattice constant, three types of scatterer sizes, 12 kinds of lattice orientations, and three different sizes of PW. Section 6 will provide a comprehensive explanation of these effects. The third objective is 100% completed. As discussed before, the louvres can help increase the air flow speed between the SC and within the PW. The stronger and more directional air movement results in stronger shear within the received room, which enhanced pollutant transport out of the receiver room. This is obtained under some louver configurations.

15217219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217219.value: With an integrative review about acoustic environment, noise pollution is a pervasive issue that significantly impacts human well-being, affecting physical health, mental health, and daily life. Continuous exposure to high noise levels can lead to hearing loss, increased stress, elevated blood pressure, sleep disturbances, and cognitive impairment. To address this problem, researchers conducted an investigation into the performance of plenum windows (PW) in noise mitigation, with a focus on incorporating sonic crystals (SC), a type of acoustic metamaterial, into the PW cavity. The study involved numerical simulations and physical experiments using scaled-down models of different PW sizes (98 mm, 158 mm, and 218 mm widths) and SC diameters (10 mm, 19 mm, and 32 mm). Twelve different arrangements of SCs, including rectangular, square, and rhombic lattice configurations, were examined. The results showed that the installation of SCs in PWs generally improved their performance, particularly at higher frequencies (starting from 1000 Hz), where a significant portion of daily noise originates. The most notable improvement was observed with a PW width of 158 mm and SCs with a diameter of 32 mm arranged in a square lattice configuration, which resulted in a nearly 4 dB(A) increase in transmission loss (TL). The frequency bandgaps created by the SC arrays were found to be the key factor in this performance enhancement, as they restricted the propagation of acoustic waves. Rectangular and rhombic lattice arrangements were more effective in creating low-frequency bandgaps, making them preferable for PW installations where low-frequency noise is the primary concern. Despite the positive outcomes, the performance of PWs in the low-frequency range (below 800 Hz) remained unsatisfactory due to limitations on the number of SCs that can be installed inside the PW cavity. To address this issue, future research will explore the use of slit SCs with low-frequency resonating behavior, which have proven to be highly effective in mitigating low-frequency noise. Additionally, the formation of cavity acoustic modes was observed to have adverse effects on the performance of PWs, weakening the bandgap property. The comprehensive coupling effect between acoustic bandgaps and cavity modes is still under investigation. By fine-tuning the geometries of PWs and SCs, it is possible to achieve better noise reduction within the targeted frequency range, ultimately creating a more comfortable and quieter living environment.

15217219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217219.value: The researchers have made significant progress in developing an accurate analytical model to predict the performance of porous windows (PW) with sound-absorbing screens (SC) installed. They have initially focused on a simpler case of a straight waveguide, which has been published in a conference paper. The dedicated PhD student, Mr. Lam, is currently working on extending this analytical approach to the more complex case of PW. To address the unsatisfactory low-frequency performance of non-resonating SC, the researchers are investigating the replacement of SC arrays with slit resonators, which have the capability to create wider and lower bandgaps. They have modified the analytical approach to accommodate this modification, and the corresponding results have been published in another conference paper. Furthermore, the researchers are exploring the use of specific materials, such as elastic and porous materials, within PW to further enhance its acoustical performance. They are also investigating the impact of the incident angle of acoustic waves on PW's performance and considering alternative designs for the SC, such as nested slit resonators and slit resonators with porous materials. The researchers are confident that the combination of these approaches will significantly enhance PW's overall performance and provide a more pleasant living environment.

15217219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217219.value: The incessant noise pollution originating from sources like vehicular traffic and construction sites poses significant risks to the mental and psychological well-being of residents and workers, potentially leading to debilitating conditions such as insomnia and anxiety disorders. Therefore, the imperative of devising effective noise mitigation strategies, particularly within building structures like windows, is paramount. Moreover, it is essential to ensure that these strategies maintain a satisfactory level of natural ventilation, thereby minimizing the reliance on electronic ventilation devices and fostering sustainability practices. In this context, we propose a novel design incorporating distinctive acoustic structure and louvers into the plenum window cavity. Through a combination of experimental validation and numerical simulation, our proposed structure demonstrates notable efficacy in reducing noise transmission and improving insulation capabilities. Furthermore, our simulations confirm that the structure facilitates a sufficient airflow rate, thereby ensuring adequate natural ventilation. As a result, the proposed structure offers a promising solution for addressing noise pollution in residential and industrial buildings, particularly in densely populated urban environments like Hong Kong. By shielding residents and workers from the detrimental effects of excessive noise, our structure contributes to fostering a harmonious and conducive living and working environment within society as a whole.

15217719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217719.value: Research on facial expressions has been conducted extensively for several decades, mainly for classifying the basic expressions. This has a wide range of applications, including digital entertainment, human-computer interaction, etc. In this project, we propose to study the facial expressions of comprehension, which are the kinds of expressions related to learning. We aim to investigate the multidimensionality of comprehension exhibited by facial expressions. Therefore, we can identify whether a person or a student, who is reading or learning, understands or comprehends the sentences or the new knowledge. In this project, we investigate the facial expressions of comprehension, while people are at different stages of reading sentences in the form of true-false questions. Their facial expressions are recorded and then analyzed, when they are reading the statements, responding to the statements as true or false, and seeing the answers. The experiment is designed to be a self-paced reading task, where participants are asked questions with true or false answers. After participants read a question, their facial expressions should reflect whether they know the answer or not. Then, the participants will be given the feedback to their answers. In this project, we will study and investigate participants’ facial dynamic behaviors when they are reading the sentences and when feedback is provided, so that we can identify (1) whether they know the answer to the question of interest or simply guess, i.e. knowing facial expression and guessing facial expression will be classified, and (2) the veracity of the statements through the dynamics of their facial expressions. Furthermore, new expressions related to learning will also be explored. This is a new research area for affective computing. Currently, we have created a small database for this research. Through this project, we aim to increase the number of participants to more than 200, and further enhance the questions used in our behavior experiments. The data collected includes RGB and depth streams. Based on the RGB videos, we have conducted some preliminary research on recognizing the facial expressions of comprehension. Currently, based on the video clips, a handcrafted feature and different classifiers have been employed to analyze and recognize the facial expressions. In this project, in addition to the facial appearance from the RGB videos, we will also consider using the facial animation units in the analysis, as well as the head motion. Through this project, we can have a better understanding of the comprehension level of students in lectures. 在這幾十年來，面部表情的研究已經廣泛展開，主要是對基本表情進行分類。這具有廣泛的應用，包括數位娛樂、人機交互等。在本項目中，我們將提出研究面部理解的表情，即是與學習相關的表情。我們的目標是研究面部表情對學習理解的表現。因此，我們可以確定學生在閱讀或學習時，其理解程度有多少。 在這項目中，我們研究當人們閱讀不同階段的真假問題時，他們面部顯示的理解表情。當他們閱讀陳述時，回應問題真或假，並看到答案時，我們記錄他們的面部表情，然後進行分析，這實驗設計成一個自定進度的閱讀過程，參與者被問到正確或錯誤的答案的問題。參與者讀完問題後，他們的面部表情應該反映他們是否知道答案。然後，參與者會知道其真正答案。在本項目中，我們將研究參與者在閱讀句子時和提供答案時的面部動態行為，以便我們確定 (1) 他們是否知道問題的答案，還是只是猜測，即知道面部表情和猜測面部表情可被分類，及(2)通過面部表情的動態表達陳述的真實性。此外，我們還將探討與學習有關的新表清。這是情感計算的一個新研究領域。 目前，我們已經為這項研究創建了一個小型資料庫。通過這個項目，我們的目標是將參與者人數增加到200人以上，並進一步增強我們在實驗中使用的問題。收集的資料包括 RGB 和深度資料。基於RGB視頻，我們進行了一些初步的研究，識別面部表情的理解。目前，基於視訊短片，已使用人工製的特徵和不同的分類器來分析和識別面部表情。在這個專案中，除了從RGB視頻的面部外觀，我們還將考慮使用面部單元和頭部運動的分析。通過這個項目，我們可以更加瞭解學生在課堂中的學習理解程度。

15217719.label: Realisation of objectives
15217719.value: Objective 1: Study and represent the multimodal data collected for recognizing Facial Expression of Comprehension In our study, based on the database for facial expressions of comprehension (FEC), we consider the dynamics of the facial animation units and the RGB frames of video clips for the recognition of FEC. To analyze the dynamic changes in facial configuration, we proposed Event-Related Intensities (ERIs). ERIs are time-dependent measures of intensity changes caused by a stimulus. ERIs differ from previous approaches that exploit the intensity of facial expressions, such as the Facial Action Coding System (FACS), in that intensity within ERIs is stimulus-dependent and continuous per Animation or Action units rather than categorical. They provide a new approach to the study of facial expressions in that they can be rigorously controlled within experimental designs, while simultaneously providing for the production of natural responses. A critical feature of ERIs within the FEC database is that they allow for the ability to not only analyze facial behavior during both successful and unsuccessful recall of target information but also expressions during guessing. The presented findings can later be used to design a classification system to predict participants’ learning outcomes. The other modality used in our study is the video clips. The faces in the videos are aligned based on the eye positions and are then cropped. Then, the eye and the mouth regions are located, and local features are extracted and concatenated. In our study, the local features are based on a descriptor called “Local Phase Quantization Three Orthogonal Planes” (LPQ-TOP). LPQ-TOP, which is a spatiotemporal extension of LPQ into three orthogonal planes (TOP). These two modalities are combined to recognize the expressions of comprehension. This work has formed a journal paper, which has been published in the IEEE Trans. on Affective Computing. Objective 2: Devise efficient algorithms to recognize the Facial Expressions of Comprehension We studied different efficient algorithms for facial expression recognition, which can be used for recognizing the expressions of comprehension. We reviewed the state-of-the-art subspace-learning methods, and then proposed a novel manifold-learning method, named soft locality preserving map (SLPM), for expression recognition. SLPM aims to control the level of spread of the different expression classes, which is closely connected to the generalizability of the learned subspace. Then, we extended manifold learning methods to deep learning by formulating the loss functions for training, and further reformulated SLPM into a soft locality preserving (SLP) loss. These loss functions are applied as an additional regularization to the learning of deep neural networks. We have evaluated these subspace-learning methods, as well as their deep-learning extensions, on facial expression recognition. This work has been published as a journal paper in the APSIPA Trans. on Signal and Information Processing. To further improve the performance of facial expression recognition based on deep neural networks, we have proposed a deep multi-task learning method for both facial expression recognition and synthesis. Most of the existing multi-task learning methods take into limited consideration the feature selection, when transferring information between different tasks, which may lead to task interference when training the multi-task networks. To address this problem, we proposed a novel selective feature-sharing method and established a multi-task network for facial expression recognition and facial expression synthesis. The proposed method can effectively transfer beneficial features between different tasks, while filtering out useless and harmful information. Moreover, we employ the facial expression synthesis task to enlarge and balance the training dataset to further enhance the generalization ability of the proposed method. This work has formed a conference paper, published in the Proceedings of IEEE Conference on Pattern Recognition 2020 (IEEE ICPR 2020). To recognize facial expressions accurately, it is important to learn discriminative representations with good robustness from facial observations. To achieve this objective, we will study a novel geometry-aware facial expression recognition (FER) framework to boost the FER performance based on both geometric and appearance knowledge. Specifically, we have investigated an encoding strategy for facial landmarks, and adopted a graph convolutional network (GCN) to fully explore the structural information of the facial components behind different expressions. Deep models are then further applied to the whole facial observation to learn the global characteristics of different expressions. We have proposed effective methods to fuse the features from these two networks to form a comprehensive high-semantic representation, which promotes the FER reasoning from both visual and structural perspectives. Moreover, to facilitate the networks to concentrate on the most informative facial regions and components, we have applied multi-level attention mechanisms into the proposed framework. In addition to recognizing the facial expression from an image, we also extended our deep neural network to recognize facial expressions from a video. We applied attention mechanisms in the spatial dimension and the temporal dimension, as well as a vision transformer, to achieve state-of-the-art performance. This work has formed two journal papers, which have been published in the IEEE Trans. on Affective Computing. Objective 3: Develop a database for Facial Expressions of Comprehension We have created a multimodal spontaneous facial expression database, namely ‘Facial Expressions of Comprehension (FEC)’. The FEC database was created using data obtained in a behavioral experiment in which participants were asked to first read knowledge-based statements; second, provide a ‘true’ or ‘false’ answer; and finally, receive feedback as either ‘correct’ or ‘false’. During the experiment, the Kinect v2 device was used to record multiple streams of data. The collected data is divided into segments, and each segment has the facial animation units and the frames belonging to only one trial answered by one participant, i.e. per trial and per participant. Each participant has up to 100 RGB video shots, 100 depth video shots, etc. corresponding to 100 stimuli. The Kinect v2 device provides a high resolution of RGB videos, depth and infrared data, as well as facial landmarks and animation units. In order to spare computational power while saving a huge amount of data, only a subregion of RGB frames (300  500 pixels) was saved. The trials in which the participants were out of the frame were deleted from the database. While watching and annotating each video, we also realized that sometimes the participants got distracted and looked at somewhere other than the screen, for example at the door. We did not include this kind of video segment in the database or include them in the experiments to follow. Post exclusion of out-of-frame or distracted trials, the database consists of 3,576 unique segments from 44 participants and 100 stimuli. Each unique segment has the RGB, depth and infrared video shots, as well as 17 animation units per frame provided by the Kinect 2.0 device. The average length of the videos is 9.2 seconds (STD: 3.7 seconds). Each video clip is labelled according to (1) Category, which reflects the difficulty of the statement (Baseline/Range), (2) Value, which is the veracity of the statement (True/False), and 3) PA, which is the participants’ accuracy (Correct/Incorrect). Further information includes whether the video had occlusion, and whether the participant in the corresponding video was talking. In addition, participant metadata includes the subject’s age, gender, total years of education, and self-rated English proficiency.

15217719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217719.value: In this research, we found that recognizing the facial expression of comprehension (FEC) is a challenging task. In order to conduct this research, a FEC database must be constructed. From our experiment results, the feature, namely Event Related Intensities (ERI), can be used to not only analyze facial behavior during both successful and unsuccessful recall of target information but also expressions during guessing. The presented findings can later be used to design a classification system to predict participants’ learning outcomes. To improve the recognition performance, we found that the loss functions used for training and the network structures are of utmost importance. Our proposed loss function, namely soft locality preserving (SLP), can achieve the best performance compared to other loss functions. Furthermore, encoding the structure of a face image, graph representation is an effective means. We found that by integrating facial geometry with facial observation, with the application of attention mechanisms, the best performance can be achieved.

15217719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217719.value: In this project, a database for FEC has been constructed. However, the number of samples is still limited. More people can be invited to generate more videos for the database. Furthermore, we will try to use deepfake methods to augment the database. We have also developed several efficient algorithms for facial expression recognition. We are currently studying a better graph model for representing facial geometry and more advanced transformer models to enhance facial expression recognition performance.

15217719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217719.value: In this project, we have studied the dynamics of face images for understanding the expression of comprehension. This research can help us understand the comprehension of people, in particular, students in a classroom. To achieve this task, we have constructed a database for this research and have developed efficient algorithms for recognizing expressions. In our research, we have investigated effective ways to train deep neural networks by using efficient loss functions and developed effective algorithms based on deep networks, with attention mechanisms, for expression recognition. This research will be useful for the development of real-world facial expression recognition systems.

15217919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15217919.value: 物聯網中設備和數據的激增推動了邊緣計算在未來工廠，智能電網和自動駕駛等新興應用中的應用。這些應用程式需要分佈在不同地理區域中的組件之間相互協作完成。協作邊緣計算已經成為一種新的計算模式以支持該類型應用程式。該計算模式下，多個服務提供者相互連接以促進邊緣節點之間的數據交換和協作。 在本項目中，我們專注於如何在協作式邊緣設備上處理應用程式的計算任務，以在執行時間和可靠性方面實現高性能。協作邊緣系統具有分層結構，包括邊緣節點網路和底層的大量移動終端設備。任務由終端設備釋放，然後由終端設備和邊緣節點協同處理。 此外，在任務執行期間，當終端設備移動和/或邊緣節點發生故障時，任務可以在邊緣節點之間遷移。我們將研究終端設備和邊緣節點之間的協同任務劃分問題，以及邊緣節點網路內的任務遷移問題。 據我們所知，本專案擬研究的任務劃分和遷移問題尚未進行充分研究。在傳統移動雲計算任務劃分問題中，雲上計算資源不受限制，並且終端到雲上的資料傳輸成本較高。然而，在協作式邊緣計算中，終端設備和邊緣節點之間的連接頻寬相對充足，但與雲相比，邊緣節點具有的計算能力有著較大限制。系統資源的差異需要新的解決方案。另一個相關領域是並行任務調度和分散式運算，已有研究考慮如何將具有確定工作負載的一組任務分配到處理器上。在此專案中，需要調度的任務的工作負載不是預先確定的。此外，我們考慮由終端設備的移動性引起的多個任務的遷移。已有資料中心中任務遷移問題幾乎幾乎為考慮如何在多個線上遷移任務之間分配網路頻寬資源。 我們將開發一組演算法來對終端設備和邊緣節點之間的任務進行分區，分配和調度，旨在最小化任務的平均完成時間。此外，我們將設計底層系統機制以支援邊緣節點之間的任務線上遷移，並且基於這些機制，開發併發任務線上遷移場景下具有QoS感知特性的頻寬資源配置演算法。我們將在Edge Mesh框架下實現和驗證所提出的演算法和機制，該框架為我們之前針對邊緣計算中可擴展連接和分散式智慧研究而開發。該專案研究重要且具有挑戰性的問題，有助於推進邊緣計算相關技術和應用，既有較大學術價值和實際影響。

15217919.label: Realisation of objectives
15217919.value: We have finished the main objectives listed in the proposal. The first objective is to investigate the requirements and identify the challenges of task partition and migration in collaborative edge computing. We have systematically surveyed different problems, solutions, and challenges for resource scheduling in an edge computing environment [J2022e]. We have also identified different challenging issues for the task partition and migration problem in collaborative edge computing environments under different application models, including independent tasks, dependent tasks, and stateful tasks. We have also investigated the challenging issues and published a new framework, E-tree learning, for model learning in a collaborative edge computing environment [J2021b]. The second objective is to develop algorithms and mechanisms for the identified task partition and migration problems in collaborative edge computing and conduct theoretical analysis and simulations to evaluate the proposed solutions. We have studied four specific problems. The first problem is the task partitioning problem of stateful data stream applications [J2021a] in a dynamic edge cloud environment. The second problem is the multi-hop task offloading problem, considering joint task and network flow scheduling in collaborative edge computing [J2020b] [J2020c]. The third problem is the bandwidth allocation during live task migration in the edge cloud environment [J2020a]. The fourth problem is incorporating reliability for service chain scheduling in the 5G edge computing environment [C2021][J2022c]. First, we study the problem of task partitioning for stateful data stream applications in dynamic environments [J2021a]. The problem is given the dynamic network channels and computation partitioning decision; the objective is to update the computation partitioning decision and migrate state for alleviating network congestion to minimize the make-span. Existing works on computation partitioning usually consider applications with stateless function modules that lead to high state migration overhead while partitioning stateful applications. Since the problem is formulated as an NP-hard problem, we design a novel heuristic algorithm, namely Score Matrix-based Heuristic (SM-H), which updates the partitioning of the current arriving data frame. Based on the one-shot SM-H algorithm, we further extend to solve the partitioning problem with multiple steps look-ahead. The evaluation using simulation experiments shows that proposed algorithms not only could selectively migrate state but also outperform the benchmark algorithms in terms of the make-span. Second, we study the multi-hop offloading problem in collaborative edge computing for directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks [J2020b] and independent tasks [J2020c]. This offloading problem for directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks considers jointly deciding the task scheduling and network flow scheduling decisions to minimize the application completion time. While few existing works have studied the scheduling of DAG tasks, these works have not jointly considered network flows, leading to network congestion and poor performance. Since the formulated problem is NP-hard, we have proposed a joint-dependent task offloading and flow scheduling heuristic (JDOFH) leveraging the knowledge of parallelism and dependencies within each DAG task to make a joint scheduling decision. Performance comparisons show JDOFH leads to up to 85% improvement in average completion time compared to benchmark solutions, which do not make a joint decision. We have also studied the multi-hop offloading problem for independent tasks in collaborative edge computing while considering the partitioning of tasks into local and remote subtasks [J2020c]. Compared to the multi-hop offloading problem with DAG tasks, there is an additional decision variable of partial offloading ratio for each task, along with the offloading and network flow scheduling decisions. This problem is challenging due to the complex dependency among variables. A heuristic algorithm, joint partial offloading and flow scheduling heuristic (JPOFH), has been proposed that decides the partial offloading ratio by considering the waiting time for task and network flows. The performance comparison of the proposed solution, JPOFH, using simulation experiments shows up to 32% improvement in average completion time compared to benchmark solutions that do not make a joint decision. Third, we study the resource allocation problem for multiple live VM migrations across the edge clouds [J2020a]. The problem is to allocate the bandwidth and determine the service rate for the VM migration tasks to maximize the average QoS of the migration tasks while meeting the deadline. Compared to existing works for single VM migration, this problem considers concurrent multiple VM migrations caused by user mobility in edge clouds. We propose a solution by transforming the formulated non-linear programming problem into a linear one. The initial feasible solution is iteratively adjusted to maximize the average QoS. Furthermore, several evolutionary algorithms, including the genetic algorithm (GA) and particle swarm optimization (PSO), have also been proposed to find a good initial solution. Evaluation conducted using extensive simulations experiments shows one of the proposed genetic algorithms has a slightly better performance than the others, while all the proposed algorithms have fast convergence speed. Fourth, we study the reliable service chain scheduling in dynamic 5G networks [C2021][J2022c]. This problem considers the deployment of the virtual network functions (VNFs) and schedule arriving requests to maximize the number of requests satisfying the latency and reliability constraints. Compared to existing works that assume a static network and a priori knowledge of SFC requests that is not practical, this work assumes a dynamic 5G network. Additionally, this work considers the redeployment of all types of VNF at computing nodes, which comes with an extra time cost. The problem is formulated to be NP-hard and solved by an efficient approach that separates the redundancy determining from SFC scheduling. The redundancy subproblem is solved using a heuristic approach, while the SFC scheduling subproblem is solved by proposing a reinforcement learning-based approach. The evaluation results using simulation show that our proposed method can increase the success rate by 18.7% compared to the benchmark algorithms. We also conducted another study to address the problem of collaborative caching for multi-bitrate videos in an edge-computing environment [J2022d]. This problem considers caching and video transcoding decisions to minimize long-term costs. The long-term cost minimization problem requires making coupled caching decisions for adjacent time slots. We have addressed this problem by proposing a polynomial-time online orchestration framework that decomposes the problem into individual time slots. A theoretical analysis has been conducted to analyze the competitive ratio of our proposed algorithm. Simulation results show that our proposed algorithm outperforms benchmark solutions with a 13.6% improvement on average in terms of total cost. The third objective is to build a prototype for collaborative edge computing and validate the effectiveness and performance of our proposed algorithms and mechanisms. We have developed a prototype to evaluate the efficacy of the proposed solutions for distributed machine learning in collaborative edge computing environments. We have developed EdgeTB, a hybrid emulation testbed that can be used to generate a large number of emulated edge nodes and network-flexible test environments while incorporating real physical nodes to guarantee fidelity [J2022b]. We have conducted extensive case studies and experiments to demonstrate the usability of EdgeTB for high-fidelity evaluation of distributed machine learning solutions. We have also proposed novel solutions to optimize the aggregation frequency for hierarchical model training in collaborative edge computing and evaluated them using the developed EdgeTB prototype [J2022a]. Our proposed EdgeTB prototype can be further leveraged for large-scale evaluation of different types of task and resource scheduling solutions in collaborative edge computing environments.

15217919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15217919.value: Our findings include four main aspects. First, we have developed a set of novel algorithms to update the task partitioning based on the changing network bandwidth while considering the state migration overhead [J2021a]. We have developed mathematical models to formulate the stateful data stream application computation partitioning problem (SCPP). We have proposed a heuristic solution, SM-H, for one-shot SCPP that can alleviate the network congestion and minimize the make-span by selectively migrating state. We have also proposed an online algorithm, RSM-H, for the multiple-step look-ahead SCPP. Extensive simulation experiments show the superior performance of our proposed solutions. Second, we have designed the mathematical models and a set of heuristic algorithms for the multi-hop offloading in collaborative edge computing, considering directed acyclic graph (DAG) tasks [J2020b] and independent tasks [J2020c]. We proposed the JDOFH heuristic that leverages knowledge of parallelism and dependencies to determine the offloading of multiple DAG tasks generated at different release times. On the other hand, the JPOFH heuristic proposed for multi-hop offloading of independent tasks additionally decides the partial offloading ratio of independent tasks by leveraging knowledge from Nash equilibrium. Simulation experiments show our proposed heuristics can achieve significant improvement of up to 85% and 32% for JDOFH and JPOFH, respectively, compared to benchmark solutions. Third, we have developed a heuristic solution to solve the bandwidth allocation problem for multiple live VM migrations in an edge cloud environment [J2020a]. Our proposed solution first transforms the formulated problem to obtain an initial solution and then leverages the adjustment heuristic to improve the average QoS. The main principle of the adjustment heuristic is to exchange the bandwidth between migration tasks while satisfying the constraints. We have further proposed a set of evolutionary algorithms to get a better initial solution. Performance comparison conducted using simulations shows that the proposed solutions can achieve good QoS and also have a fast convergence speed. Fourth, we have developed a novel reliability-aware dynamic service function chain scheduling (SFC) approach to decide the virtual network function (VNF) deployment in a dynamic 5G network [C2021][J2022c]. Our proposed approach decomposes the overall problem into the redundancy determination that satisfies reliability constraints while minimizing delay and SFC scheduling to maximize the success rate for SFC requests. We propose an optimal algorithm to determine the redundancy of VNFs and a reinforcement learning-based solution for dynamic SFC scheduling. The efficacy of our proposed solutions is comprehensively evaluated using simulation experiments.

15217919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15217919.value: The task partition and migration problem in collaborative edge computing can be extended in the future by considering the uncertainty in the available resources and the application workload. The edge computing environment is dynamic and uncertain due to the mobility of devices, intermittent arrival of heterogeneous workloads, and failures in devices due to dynamic wireless networks. Future work on task partition and migration can incorporate these dynamics and uncertainties to propose solutions that are more suitable for practical environments. Another dimension for future work is to propose distributed solutions for task partition and migration that require making scheduling decisions at devices with incomplete and inaccurate information. Current problems studied in this project have proposed centralized solutions that assume global knowledge and are not scalable in large-scale networks. Thus, more work is required to propose distributed solutions for the different problems studied in the project. We will also extend our developed solutions for the distributed machine learning problems in a collaborative edge computing environment. More specifically, we will study different optimization problems to improve the collaborative model training and inference at resource-constraint edge devices. The study of these topics would help in advancing the state-of-the-art for edge computing and intelligence.

15217919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15217919.value: This research makes a significant contribution to the scheduling theory for different types of tasks in collaborative edge computing. In particular, this research addresses the key problems of task partition and migrations under different contexts in edge computing environments. Several novel problems, including stateful computation partitioning, multi-hop offloading, resource allocation for live VM migration, and reliable service function chain scheduling, have been investigated in this project. The proposed system models and solutions in these works can empower many emerging applications and enable better performance for end users. The research problems in this project have been studied for different application domains, including edge cloud environment, collaborative edge computing environment with a mesh network of edge devices, and dynamic 5G networks. We have also demonstrated the efficacy of our proposed solutions by developing a prototype that enables large-scale testing for distributed machine learning solutions in a collaborative edge computing environment. This research does not only lead to advances in the task scheduling theory in edge computing but also provides significant impact by enabling emerging advanced applications, including autonomous vehicles, video analytics, and smart cities.

15218019.label: Realisation of objectives
15218019.value: A general screening method of multi-permanent-magnet-excited reluctance-coupled electric motors has been developed to search for possible structures by a computer program for applications in low-speed direct drive. A proposed optimization method has also been implemented in the program to achieve full automation. Various structures are represented by general topology models (GTMs). The developed program automatically converts the data of GTMs to the finite-element method (FEM) input data. The performances of the effective GTMs verified by the analytical method are further analyzed and optimized computed using FEM. A self-learning database has been established and automatically updated by running the developed program. GTMs have been proposed to describe the geometric structures of possible typologies, which make it easy to implement different machines in computer programs. Not only the geometric structures but also the magnetomotive force (MMF) and magnetic reluctance of each object have been expressed. A series of classes in c++ computer programs have been developed to express the GTMs. The design indicators are adopted in GTMs. With different design indicators and design parameters in GTMs, the different structures of the machines are produced. A multi-stage optimization strategy has been developed. A harmonic analysis method is first applied to check whether the design can output effective torque with combinatorial optimization to select sample points. The effective designs are further optimized based on the multi-objective functions computed using FEM. Local topologies are further explored using our proposed topology optimization method. A database of existing structures with their performances has been established, and novel structures are automatically added to the database. A low-speed motor for the direct drive of industrial robots has been proposed based on the screening method. The performance, including torque density, losses, and efficiency of the proposed motor, has been well analyzed by FEM analysis. The prototype is manufactured and tested to validate the results. An experiment has been conducted to validate the performance of the proposed motor and compare it to the FEA results.

15218019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218019.value: A general screening method of multi-permanent-magnet-excited reluctance-coupled electric motors is developed to search for possible structures by a computer program. In this program, different structures are presented by the GTMs. The proposed optimization method is implemented in the program as well. The analytical harmonic analysis is employed to verify the effectiveness of GTMs. The effective GTMs are analyzed and further optimized based on the optimization method by using FEA. The advantages of this proposed method are summarized as follows: (1) GTMs provide general expressions of machine structures which simplifies the implementation of the structure in the computer program. (2) The computation efficiency is improved due to the multi-stage optimization strategy. (3) The program can automatically offer possible designs, and more unexpected novel structures are proposed. (4) The database is smart and effective since the system is dynamically updated and has a self-learning ability. Several novel multi-PM-excited reluctance-coupled motors for a low-speed direct drive in industrial robots have been screened out and proposed [1-6]. On the one hand, more PMs inside electric machines are properly applied with the assistance of the proposed program, which is an effective way to improve the performance of the machines [1, 2]. Three sets of PMs are applied in the proposed motor. The output torque improves by 100.3% compared to the conventional machine while the volume of the motor keeps the same. In addition, efficiency is also improved, which achieves as high as 94.5%[1]. On the other hand, the energy conversion efficiency of the proposed motor also improved due to the stronger magnetic field with higher alternating frequency [6]. The reluctance coupling method is well employed in machine structure so that the frequency increase of the coupled magnetic field for power generation does not lead to the increase of pole pairs of the windings. As a result, the electromagnetic performance of the machines utilizing this design principle can be significantly improved. All the proposed machines well validate the effectiveness of our proposed screening method. The topology optimization is also well investigated [3-5]. The optimization algorithm is coupled directly to the FEM analysis to achieve a completely automatic process. Various topologies can be obtained by changing the parameters. With the aid of the optimization program, asymmetric rotor structures with better performance are obtained [3,4]. A unique PM arrangement that utilizes an asymmetric Halbach array is also obtained [5]. The results show that with the utilization of topology optimization, the performance of the machines has notable improvement.

15218019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218019.value: Firstly, for the general screening method program, the computational efficiency can be further improved by using surrogate models. The multi-stage optimization strategy is a key part of the currently proposed method, which involves numerous FEM analyses to analyze motor performance. The computing time is highly affected by the mesh quality in the FEM analysis. On the one hand, good mesh quality can produce a more accurate result. However, the whole process is time-consuming. On the other hand, if the mesh quality is reduced, the computing time can be shortened. Nonetheless, the accuracy of the result will be influenced. The surrogate model can improve the computing time and keep the accuracy simultaneously. The well-trained surrogate model can produce accurate results in a short time. Secondly, the scope of the general screening method program can be extended. Nowadays, the demand for electric machines with high rotation speeds is huge. Similar to the employment of the proposed method in low-speed direct drive applications, the topologies, and design parameters are also required a comprehensive investigation in high-speed machines. Thus, the proposed method can be applied to high-speed machines and other motors with different operation statuses.

15218019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218019.value: A general screening method of multi-permanent-magnet-excited reluctance-coupled electric motors has been developed to search for possible structures by a computer program for applications in low-speed direct drive. The proposed computer program highly improves the diversity and efficiency of different typologies designs. The full automatic program is realized by combining the screening and design method and the proposed topology optimization method. Additionally, the FEM is embedded in this program to calculate electromagnetic performance. Several novel structures have been proposed to showcase the effectiveness of this method. The performance of the proposed structure based on the screening method is investigated by simulation and validated by the prototype experiments. The torque density, ripple, losses, and efficiency are computed using the magnetic field computation of FEM. The results show that the proposed motor has an enhanced performance compared to the conventional designs, which further validates the practicability of the proposed method. The application of this research is not only limited to low-speed direct drive machines, but it can also be extended to high-speed electric machines or other types of electromagnetic devices with minor modifications of the general screening method. In the future, the proposed method can be further developed by continuously updating the database to include more application situations.

15218219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218219.value: Generalized equations in optimization include linear and nonlinear inequality systems and linear and nonlinear variational inequality problems. In practical application problems, basic data in the models such as demand, prices, resources, technical parameters etc. are often not estimated accurately. Stability analysis of generalized equations is to determine intuitively verifiable conditions to guarantee that the accuracy of the solutions obtained increase with the degree of approximation of the initial data. The literature on the subject is vast. However existing results of generalized equations are mainly concentrated on canonical perturbation of linear and nonlinear inequality systems and linear and nonlinear variational inequality problems. This project will study stability of generalized equations with an explicit set constraint and the matrix perturbation of a linear constraint system. These considerations are motivated by the facts that the explicit treatment of the set constraint allows one to use its special structure when calculating its normal cone and that the projection on the intersection of two simple polyhedral sets may be easily computed by alternating projection onto each simple polyhedral set. Moreover it is worth noting that the matrix perturbation of a linear constraint system arises in some linear portfolio selection optimization problems. Our approach relies on the Mordukhovich criterion, a remarkable variational analysis tool in the study of stability. We will study the Lipschitz-like continuity of the set of solutions of a fully perturbed linear constraint system with a set constraint and apply the obtained results to sparse linear complementarity problems. We will investigate the Lipschitz-like property of the stationary set of linear and nonlinear variational inequality problems with a matrix perturbation in the linear constraint system by virtue of a unconstrained minimization approach and a set constraint approach respectively. We will apply the obtained results to linear portfolio optimization problems. 优化中的广义方程包括线性和非线性不等式系统以及线性和非线性变分不等式问题。 在实际应用中，模型中的基本数据，如需求、价格、资源、技术参数等，往往难以准确估计。因而，广义方程的稳定性分析是建立直观可验证的条件，以保证所获得的解的准确性随着初始数据的近似程度增加而提高。目前为止关于该主题的文献非常广泛。 然而，现有广义方程的结果主要集中在线性和非线性不等式系统和线性和非线性变分不等式问题的典范扰动上。 本项目将研究带有显式集合约束和线性系统约束带矩阵扰动的广义方程的稳定性。这主要基于以下两点考虑：一是显式集合约束的特殊结构能让我们计算它的法锥；二是到两个多面体交集的投影能够更简单地通过交替计算到每个多面体的投影而得到。除此之外，线性约束系统的矩阵扰动在一些投资组合模型的线性优化问题上有应用。我们的研究方法主要基于莫尔杜霍维奇准则：一个在稳定性研究中具有重要意义的变分分析工具。 我们将研究带有集合约束或者带全扰动线性约束系统的广义方程的解集的类利普希茨连续性（或者奥滨性质），并将结果应用于带有稀疏约束的线性互补问题。同时，通过分别运用无约束优化方法和集合约束方法，我们将讨论当线性和非线性变分不等式问题中的带矩阵扰动的线性约束系统的稳定点集的类利普希茨性质。我们并将得到的结果应用于线性投资组合优化问题。

15218219.label: Realisation of objectives
15218219.value: For objective 1, the stability of the solution of an underdetermined linear system with noise was considered. Motivated by small scale examples that the iterates of proximal gradient algorithm with continuation and truncation were able to move away from local solutions, the approximate global solution of the underdetermined linear system was described by a general nonconvex regularization problem. The calmness type estimate of the approximate true sparse solution of the regularization problem was obtained in related to the given sparest solution of the undetermined linear system. For this purpose, the approximate true sparse solution was achieved by introducing two types of iterative thresholding algorithms with the continuation technique and the truncation technique respectively. To establish the estimate, a notion of limited shrinkage thresholding operator was introduced and applied, together with a restricted isometry property, to show that the proposed algorithms converge to an approximate true sparse solution within a tolerance relevant to the noise level and the limited shrinkage magnitude. The obtained results of the general scheme was applied to several structured nonconvex regularization problems including smoothly clipped absolute deviation, minimax concave penalty and l_p penalty (0 ≤ p ≤ 1). Further utilizing the recovery bound theory established in the literature, the calmness type estimate of the iterates of the related proximal gradient algorithms in related to a global solution of nonconvex regularization problems was established. The established results included the existing convergence theory for l_1 or l_0 regularization problems for finding a true sparse solution as special cases. Numerical results with some simulated data with noise showed that our proposed algorithms can find approximate true sparse solutions that were much better than stationary solutions that were found by using the standard proximal gradient algorithm. The comparison with the branch-and-bound method in the literature showed that our methods are 100 times faster. For objective 2, the Lipschitz-like property of set-valued mappings relative to a set was studied. Some neighbourhood necessary conditions and sufficient conditions were derived respectively for a set-valued mapping to have the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed set. To do this, the tangent cone of the relative set and the regular coderivative of the restricted set-valued mapping were used for the necessary condition, while the coderivative of the restricted set-valued mapping was instead employed for the sufficient condition. By combining necessary condition and sufficient condition, a complete neighbourhood characterization for a set-valued mapping to have the Lipschitz-property relative to a closed and convex set was obtained by virtue of the projection of the coderivative of the restricted set-valued mapping onto a tangent cone. Moreover the corresponding Lipschitz-like modulus was expressed by the corresponding projections. To obtain a verifiable complete characterization of Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed and convex set at the given candidate point, a projectional coderivative of set-valued mappings was introduced by virture of outer limit of the projection of the normal cone of the restricted set-valued mapping onto the tangent cone of the relative set. Therefore, a verifiable generalized Mordukhovich criterion for the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed and convex set was established. This was a generalization of the existing Mordukhovich criterion in the literature, which has found many applications in studying the stability of various optimization problems. Moreover the representation of the graphical modulus of a set-valued mapping relative to a closed and convex set was also obtained by using the outer norm of the corresponding projectional coderivative value. Some formulae for the projectional coderivative of a smooth mapping were given for the cases when the relative set is an affine set or a half-space. Comparison with other type of sufficient condition showed that our sufficient condition is more close to the necessary condition. As applications of generalized Mordukhovich criterion, the local Lipschitz continuity of an extended real-valued function relative to a closed and convex set was shown to be equivalent to that a newly-defined projectional subdifferential is locally bounded. For the Lipschitz-like property of a level-set mapping relative to a half line was characterized by a relative outer limiting subdifferential set. Stability property was also applied in convergence analysis. The relaxed CQ algorithm was one of the most important algorithms for solving the split feasibility problem. The strong convergence of the relaxed CQ algorithm in Hilbert spaces was obtained together with estimates on the convergence rate. Under a kind of Hölderian type bounded error bound property, strong convergence of the relaxed CQ algorithm was established. Furthermore, qualitative estimates on the convergence rate was presented. In particular, for the case when the involved exponent is equal to 1, the linear convergence of the relaxed CQ algorithm was established. Finally, numerical experiments were performed to show the convergence property of the relaxed CQ algorithm for the compressed sensing problem. For objective 3, the minimization of a sum of a twice continuously differentiable function f and a nonsmooth convex function was investigated. An inexact regularized proximal Newton algorithm was proposed by an approximation to the Hessian of f involving the rho-th power of the Karuch-Kuhn-Tucker residual. For rho = 0, the global convergence of the iterate sequence for the KL objective function and its R-linear convergence rate for the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz objective function of exponent ½ were justified. For rho ∈ (0, 1), by assuming that cluster points satisfy a locally Hölderian error bound of order q on a second-order stationary point set and a local error bound of order q > 1+ rho on the common stationary point set, respectively, the global convergence of the iterate sequence and its superlinear convergence rate with order depending on q were established. A dual semismooth Newton augmented Lagrangian method was also developed for seeking an inexact minimizer of subproblems. The efficiency of the proposed method was confirmed by numerical comparisons with two state-of-the-art methods on 1-regularized Student’s t-regressions, group penalized Student’s t-regressions, and nonconvex image restoration. A power penalty approach to a finite-dimensional double obstacle problem was developed. This problem was first approximated by a system of nonlinear equations containing two penalty terms. It was shown that the solution to this penalized equation converges to that of the original obstacle problem at an exponential rate when the coefficient matrices are M-matrices. Numerical examples were presented to confirm the theoretical findings and illustrate the efficiency and effectiveness of the new method. A power penalty-based method was also proposed for numerically solving a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) complementarity problem in R^N arising in optimal control as well as financial engineering. By penalizing one of the complementarity constraints, the HJB complementarity problem was transformed into a nonlinear equation. It was shown that the solution to this nonlinear system converges to that of the HJB complementarity problem exponentially when the appropriate coefficient matrix is an M-matrix. A modified Newton-type iterative method was proposed to solve the resulting nonlinear system. Numerical examples were presented to test the sensitivity of the magnitude of the power and it was confirmed that smaller magnitude of the power the more stable the option value.

Neighbourhood necessary conditions and sufficient conditions were derived respectively for a set-valued mapping to have the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed set. A verifiable generalized Mordukhovich criterion for the Lipschitz-like property relative to a closed and convex set was established. The strong convergence of a relaxed CQ algorithm was obtained together with estimates on the convergence rate. The global convergence of the iterate sequence produced by an inexact regularized proximal Newton algorithm for solving the minimization of a sum of a twice continuously differentiable function and a nonsmooth convex function and its either linear or superlinear convergence rate were established. The difference between the solution to the penalized equation of a double obstacle problem or a constrained Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation and that of the original problems was estimated as an exponential rate.

15218819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218819.value: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS, such as GPS) are nowadays used in almost any industry that requires information about the position. In surveying, mapping, and geographic information system (GIS) applications, GNSS are used to determine accurately 3-D coordinates. In Hong Kong, GNSS measurements are realized in the International Terrestrial Reference Frame 1996 (ITRF1996). The network of continuously operating GNSS stations is used to determine horizontal coordinates with an accuracy of about ±1 cm. A determination of the vertical position by GNSS in the official height datum is, however, more challenging. GNSS measure ellipsoidal heights (above the WGS84 ellipsoid) in ITRF1996 that have to be converted to orthometric heights (typically taken with respect to mean sea level) in the official height datum that is realized by Hong Kong Principal Datum (HKPD). In most countries, official height datums are practically realized by a network of levelling benchmarks. For a practical conversion of heights measured by GNSS to HKPD, the levelling network is not convenient. For this reason, a simple transformation model was provided by the Survey and Mapping Office, Lands Department of Hong Kong for the height conversion. The accuracy of this transformation model (±10-15 cm), however, does not meet current requirements for most surveying and engineering purposes. Aim of this project is to modernize the height datum in Hong Kong by introducing the geoid model instead of a traditional levelling network. Since the geoid determination requires information on topographic density, digital rock density model will be prepared. The geoid model will primarily serve for the height conversion of GNSS measurements in ITRF1996 to HKPD with the accuracy ±1 cm (or better) that meets all practical needs. The use of the geoid model will also reduce the cost of maintaining levelling benchmarks. Special emphasis will be given to promote the implementation of the geoid model into surveying practice in Hong Kong. To achieve a high accuracy of the geoid and rock density models, the state-of-the-art techniques will be applied through international partnerships with world-leading scientists in the research field. Professional surveyors and surveying agencies will be major beneficiaries of this project as the use of new geoid model will significantly reduce the cost of surveying logistics and maintaining levelling benchmarks. The rock density model with the global coverage will help users from other countries. This is particularly relevant to developing countries, where a significant effort is underway to modernize their national height datums. 全球导航卫星系统（GNSS，如GPS）现在几乎被使用 任何需要有关该职位信息的行业。在测量，绘图和 地理信息系统（GIS）应用，GNSS用于确定 精确的三维坐标。在香港，全球导航卫星系统的测量实现了 1996年国际地球参考框架（ITRF1996）。网络 连续运行的GNSS站用于确定水平坐标 精度约±1厘米。 GNSS确定垂直位置 然而，官方身高数据更具挑战性。 GNSS测量椭球高度 （ITRF1996中的WGS84椭圆体上方）必须转换为正交 在官方身高数据中的高度（通常取决于平均海平面） 由香港校长基准（HKPD）实现。在大多数国家，官方身高 通过平整基准网络实际上实现了基准。实用 通过GNSS测量的高度转换为HKPD，平整网络不是 方便。因此，调查提供了一个简单的转换模型 香港地政总署及测绘处进行高度转换。该 然而，这种转换模型的准确度（±10-15厘米）不符合当前的要求 大多数测量和工程目的的要求。 该项目的目标是通过引入现代化香港的高度数据 大地水准面模型而不是传统的水准网络。自大地水准面确定 需要有关地形密度的信息，将准备数字岩石密度模型。 大地水准面模型将主要用于GNSS测量的高度转换 在ITRF1996到HKPD，精度为±1厘米（或更好），满足所有实际需要。 大地水准面模型的使用还将降低维持水准基准的成本。 将特别强调促进大地水准面模型的实施 香港的测量实践。实现大地水准面和岩石的高精度 密度模型，最先进的技术将通过国际应用 与研究领域的世界领先科学家建立伙伴关系。专业测量师 和测量机构将成为该项目的主要受益者，因为使用新的大地水准面 模型将显着降低测量物流和维持平整的成本 基准。具有全球覆盖范围的岩石密度模型将帮助其他用户 国家。这对于需要付出巨大努力的发展中国家尤为重要 正在进行国家高度基准的现代化改造。

15218819.label: Realisation of objectives
15218819.value: Summary Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS, such as GPS) are nowadays used in almost any industry that requires information about the position. In surveying, mapping and geographic information system (GIS) applications, GNSS are primarily used to determine 3-D coordinates with a high accuracy. In Hong Kong, GNSS measurements are realized in the International Terrestrial Reference Frame 1996 (ITRF1996). The network of continuously operating GNSS stations is used to determine horizontal coordinates with an accuracy of about ±1 cm. A determination of the vertical position by GNSS in the official height datum is, however, more challenging. GNSS measure ellipsoidal heights in ITRF1996 that have to be converted to orthometric heights in the official height datum realized by Hong Kong Principal Datum (HKPD). In most countries, the official height datum is practically realized by a network of levelling benchmarks. For a practical conversion of ellipsoidal heights in ITRF1996 to orthometric heights in HKPD, the levelling network is not convenient. For this reason, a simple transformation model was provided by the Survey and Mapping Office, Lands Department of Hong Kong for the height conversion between ITRF1996 and HKPD. The accuracy of this transformation model (±10-15 cm), however, does not meet current requirements for most surveying and engineering purposes. Delivery of Objectives The initial objectives of the project involved the modernization of the height datum in Hong Kong by introducing the geoid model instead of a traditional levelling network. Since the geoid determination requires information on topographic density, the second objective involved the preparation of the digital rock density model. The third objective was related to a promotion of the implementation of a new geoid model to surveying practice. We anticipated that the geoid model for the Hong Kong will be prepared together with Co-Is Dr Slobbe and Prof. Klees at the TU Delft in the Netherlands. It was planned that PI (Dr. Tenzer) will visit the TU Delft in order to use their state-of-the-art software and high-performance computing facilities to determine the geoid model by using the SRBF approach developed at the TU Delft by Prof. Klees research group. Due to the COVID related restrictions, however, PI could not visit TU Delft. The geoid model was therefore computed by applying the KTH method. This alternative method provides results with the accuracy similar to that expected from the TU Delft method. The analysis of the new geoid model revealed that the expected accuracy of ±1-2 cm (in terms of a standard deviation of residuals) was achieved even without applying the TU Delft method. The new geoid model was published in Nsiah Ababio and Tenzer (2022a). To check the accuracy of the geoid model, we determined the orthometric heights of Hong Kong levelling benchmarks. The reason is that heights of levelling benchmarks were determined from levelling measurements but without using the gravity information. The officially used HKPD heights are thus not compatible with the geoid model. The results were published in Nsiah Ababio and Tenzer (2022b). Since the global digital rock density model was prepared by the research group at the University of New Brunswick, we use it to investigate globally the effect of rock density variations on the geoid. The numerical findings were published in Tenzer et al. (2020). We have prepared the first digital rock density model for the Hong Kong territories and published the result in Nsiah Ababio and Tenzer (2024). 15218819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218819.value: We have prepared a new geoid model for the Hong Kong territories. We have achieved the expected accuracy of the geoid model at the level of 1-2 cm in terms of a standard deviation of residuals between the gravimetric and geometric geoid heights at GNSS-levelling points. We also improved the accuracy of HKPD heights by taking into consideration the gravity data that was interpolated along levelling lines from gravity measurements. According to our error analysis, the accuracy of physical heights improved by about 2 cm by taking into consideration the gravity information. We have used the global digital rock density to estimate the effect of anomalous topographic density variations on the geoid globally. According to our results, the errors due to disregarding the topographic density variations are typically less than 5 cm but could reach several decimeters in regions with elevated topography and a complex geological structure. We also estimated that the effect of density variations on the geoid and orthometric heights in Kong Kong could reach up to 2 cm. We have compiled the first digital rock density model for the Hong Kong territories. We have promoted the geoid model and established collaboration with the Lands Department of the Government of the HKSAR. We are now actively participate on a modernization of the geodetic vertical datum in Hong Kong.

15218819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15218819.value: Since the HKPD heights are shifted about 1.23 m below the mean sea level and the mean sea level changes are not taken into consideration, the determination of orthometric heights and the geoid model should be realized so that both coincide with the current mean sea level. To address this objective, we estimated the current mean sea level and its changes and presented the finding in Zou et al. (2021). The results from this study will be used to fit the new geoid model and orthometric heights with the current mean sea level and apply the correction for annual sea level change. The geoid model should be compatible with the orthometric heights. For this purpose we determined orthometric heights at levelling benchmarks in Hong Kong by applying an approximate method. To improve the accuracy, advanced numerical methods will be applied for a geoid and orthometric height determination that take into consideration also rock density variations. To address this issue we compiled the first digital rock density model and published it in Nsiah Ababio and Tenzer (2024) Zou F , Tenzer R, Fok HS, Meng G, Zhao Q (2021) The sea level changes in Hong Kong from tide-gauge records and remote sensing observations over the last seven decades. 15218819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218819.value: The project delivered the new geoid model for the Hong Kong territories that was computed from gravity data and then fitted with the newly determined orthometric heights at levelling benchmarks. The accuracy of the geoid and orthometric heights is about 2 cm. This accuracy is significantly better than the accuracy of the 7-parameter transformation model (about 10-15 cm) that is currently used to convert the GNSS measured heights into the HKPD heights that are used to define the official geodetic height system in Hong Kong. We have conducted the most comprehensive global analysis of the effect of rock density variations on the accuracy of geoid and heights that are currently determined (in all countries around the world) by considering only the average rock density. According to our results presented in Tenzer et al. (2020), the rock density variations could improve the accuracy of geoid and heights significantly already in regions with a moderately elevated topography and a relatively homogenous geological structure.
