15218919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15218919.value: 雲計算和人工智能的蓬勃發展催生了機器學習即服務(MLaaS)這一新興領域，從而能解決機器學習中計算資源和數據科學家的稀缺性問題。在MLaaS中，用戶只需提供訓練樣本，機器學習即服務商即可根據樣本數據類型和應用場景決定合適的機器學習模型及訓練算法、進行訓練並提供新樣本的在線推斷服務。目前主流雲計算商均提供機器學習即服務產品，如亞馬遜ML、微軟Azure ML Studio、谷歌Prediction API和IBM Watson ML。 由於機器學習即服務搭建於軟件即服務(SaaS)和數據庫即服務(DBaaS)之上，受後兩者的影響無法避免產生可靠性和完整性問題。傳統的完整性驗證機制如數字簽名和消息認證碼由於機器學習即服務的模型和訓練樣本來源的複雜性原因並不可行。本項目提出了全新的完整性驗證機制，涵蓋MLaaS的整個服務週期，包括訓練完整性、樣本完整性和在線推斷服務完整性，為蓬勃發展的機器學習即服務提供了基礎安全保障。

15218919.label: Realisation of objectives
15218919.value: After 42 months of research endeavors, most objectives set out in the original proposal have been thoroughly studied and resolved. As for the detailed progress, we have achieved objectives 1-2 by the end of year 2021, and objectives 3 and 4 by the end of year 2022, and mid 2023, respectively. First, we study the problem that is presented in the first task of the original proposal (objectives 1 and 2) of integrity assurance scheme against training fraud. As existing MLaaS training heavily relies on the edge computing paradigm, to start with, we investigate the most fundamental problem of data aggregation in the centralized sink of an edge computing setting. The main objective is to ensure all sources, intermediate, and sink nodes faithfully execute the aggregation protocol. The challenge, however, lies in the insecure communciation channel as well as the colluding or compromise of some nodes, which lead to the compromise of encryption and MAC keys. We propose a group-based hierchical achitecture for data and MAC aggregation, namely, Onion Homomorphic Encryptionbased Aggregation (OHEA), where sources form groups with their dedicated encryption and MAC keys. The result is published in 29th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM '20). For privacy preservtion on the verified contents, Prefix Verifiable Message Authentication Code has been proposed. But it only works if the portion to be authenticated is a prefix of the message. We propose a more general scheme called Scalable Prefix Verifiable Message Authentication Code (SPMAC). It inherits the advantage of PMAC while overcoming the drawbacks. The result has been published in IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management. For the emerging edge computing and fog computing paradigm, the devices have low computation capability, so they cannot verify the integrity of all incoming messages using traditional message authentication code (MAC), especially when the messages are in large volume and high frequency. As such, we propose a novel MAC scheme, namely, Partial Verification Message Authentication Code (PV-MAC), to partially offload the verification tasks to a device with more processing power, (e.g., a fog node). The result has been published in Computers & Security. To overcome the limitation of computation ability in one edge node, recently collaborative edge computing is proposed. Each edge node only needs to verify a subset of the message integrity, which is beneficial when incoming messages are large. So we propose an Elliptic Curve Based Multi-hop Sanitizable Signature (ECMSS), which can provide both signature aggregation and subset verification. The result is published in Journal of Computer Security. Last but not the least, Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) is a classic transmission protocol in IoT, and it is essential to ensure its security in the temporal domain. On one hand, some messages are time-sensitive, so their integrity should only be valid in a determined time interval. On the other hand, when the subscriber is out of the service, his key should not be able to verify the message, which is known as subscriber validity. We study the time-specific integrity service in the MQTT protocol and propose Time-specific Signcryption (TSSC) and the Dynamic Time-specific Signature (DTSS). The result is published in 23rd ACM/IEEE International Conference on Information Processing in Sensor Networks (IPSN). Second, we investigate the problem in the second task of the original proposal (objective 3) of integrity assurance scheme against training sample poisoning fraud. To start with, we have studied local differential privacybased training sample collection and aggregation techniques for social network, time-series data, and high-dimensional sensor data with correlation. These works have been published in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (TKDE), Proc. of IEEE International Conference on Computer Communications (INFOCOM’21), and Proc. of 18th IEEE International Conference on Sensing, Communication and Networking (SECON) 2021, IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE '22), INFOCOM’23, Proceedings of the VLDB Volume 16 (PVLDB ’23) , respectively. To assure integrity, we have been studying on a local-differential-privacy-based mechanism to attack existing sample poisoning detection method. Our main idea is to obfuscate the target label class of the poison so that the detection will fail to recognize its true target. This work is publised with title "3DFed: Adaptive and Extensible Framework for Covert Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning" in IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P) 2023. Although there are a few works have proposed some countermeasures to address training sample poisoning attacks, they all require prior knowledge of either the attacking pattern or the poison value distribution. We thus adopt a general opportunistic-and-colluding threat model and propose a multi-group Differential Aggregation Protocol (DAP) to improve the accuracy of mean estimation under LDP. Different from all existing works that detect sample poison values on individual basis, DAP mitigates the overall impact of poison values on the estimated mean. It relies on a new probing mechanism EMF (i.e., Expectation-Maximization Filter) to estimate features of the attackers, two EMF post-processing procedures, and a group-wise mean aggregation scheme to optimize the final estimated mean. This work is publised in IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE '23). Alternatively, we also designed Byzantine LDP amplified gain attacks (BLAGA) as an enhanced version of the most popular and classic Maximal gain attack (MGA), which is precisely derived from the randomness of an LDP protocol. Based on this, we propose a defense framework that makes use of a data-driven approach to automatically identify the target items via multi-round data collection. This work is publised in 28th International Conference on Database Systems for Advanced Applications (DASFAA). For graph data, GNN, and the link prediction task, we propose centroid-guided graph poisoning (CGP). Without participating in the training process of the target model, CGP operates on links between malicious nodes to make the target model more vulnerable to graph link inference attacks. This work is publised in IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData) 2023. Third, we also study objective 4 in the proposal of integrity assurance scheme against model extraction fraud by clients. We have attempted model extraction attacks on various machine learning models and application domains. For image recoginition, we have used a combination of Variational Autoencoder (VAE) and kd-tree to achieve satisfactory extraction ratio. The paper has been pulished in Proc. of SPIE 11766, International Workshop on Advanced Imaging Technology (IWAIT) 2021 and receives Best Paper Award. For general AI models, we have developed an active learning based modele extraction framework that integrates model inference to boost the fidelity of extracted copy model. In this paper, we show that ME and MI can reinforce each other through a chained and iterative reaction, which can significantly boost ME attack accuracy and improve MI by saving the query cost. As such, we build a framework MExMI for pool-based active model extraction (PAME) to exploit MI through three modules: “MI Pre-Filter”, “MI Post-Filter”, and “semi-supervised boosting”. The paper is publised in 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022). As for counter measures, we have developed a local differential privacy-based boundary protection scheme called BDPL that allows MLaaS to perturb the output labels in order to guard against model extration adversary. This work is published in IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing (TDSC).

15218919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15218919.value: Our major research findings and outcome are listed as below. Due to space limitation, more technical details are presented in Section 5.3 as above. 1. A secure aggregation mechanism which support group-based integrity assurance in edge computing and wireless sensor network. This paper has been published as a full research paper in ACM CIKM 2020. 2. A Scalable Prefix Verifiable Message Authentication Code (SPMAC) scheme for integrity assurance in machine learning and IoT systems. This work has been published in IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management (TNSM), 2022. 3. An active video integrity authentication system for high-resolution video camera data in AI-based surveillance systems. This work has been published in IEEE Internet of Things Journal, 2022. 4. A time-specific integrity service in MQTT protocol that addresses the time-sensitive contents in edge intelligence. This work has been published in 23rd ACM/IEEE International Conference on Information Processing in Sensor Networks (IPSN). 5. A novel MAC scheme, namely, Partial Verification Message Authentication Code (PV-MAC), to partially offload the verification tasks in fog computing to a device with more processing power, (e.g., a fog node). The work is published in Computers & Security. 6. An Elliptic Curve Based Multi-hop Sanitizable Signature (ECMSS), which can provide both signature aggregation and subset verification. This work has been published in Journal of Computer Security. 7. An adaptive, extensible, and multi-layered framework to launch covert federated learning backdoor attacks in a black-box setting. This work has been published in IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy (S&P), 2023. 8. A general opportunistic-and-colluding threat model and a multi-group Differential Aggregation Protocol (DAP) to improve the accuracy of mean estimation or more general statistics under LDP. The work is published in IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering (ICDE '23). 9. A defense framework that makes use of a data-driven approach to automatically identify the target items via multi-round data collection. 15218919.value: As for further development, we plan to further build and enhance our existing schemes to make it suitable for commercial demonstration and knowledge transfer. 15218919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15218919.value: Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) provides an inexpensive solution to two scarce resources in machine learning — high computational power and experienced data scientists. However, MLaaS cannot be fully trusted. In practice, adversarial machine learning literatures already demonstrate various attacks such as model extraction, training data poisoning, and adversarial example (model evasion) attacks. Unfortunately, traditional auditing and integrity assurance techniques such as Merkel Hash Tree no longer work in MLaaS. In this project, we have proposed several mechanisms to audit MLaaS throughout the entire machine learning cycle. We focus on the integrity of MLaaS (against training fraud), training samples (against sample poisoning), and clients who request MLaaS inference service (against model extraction). With the emerging importance of integrity assurance and machine learning, we believe the outcomes of this project will contribute to the security foundation for the booming MLaaS industry. We also expect this project to spark off similar endeavor in other sectors such as internet of things, where integrity is also essential. The outcomes will benefit the research community, the industry, and the city of Hong Kong, “one of the world's smart cities”, a vision quoted from the Chief Executive.

15219319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219319.value: The supporting of smart contracts is the landmark of blockchain 2.0, which allows running various applications on the blockchain other than cryptocurrency. A smart contract is a piece of autonomous program that can execute automatically and mandatorily according to the program logic defined beforehand. Due to many unique advantages, smart contracts have the power to reshape a number of industries, such as banking, insurance, financial exchange, etc. Therefore, many blockchain systems support smart contracts, among which Ethereum is the largest one with more than 21 billion USD market capitalization, 7 million smart contracts, and 340 million transactions. Moreover, Ethereum supports the majority of cryptocurrency tokens through smart contracts. The top 100 tokens have more than $15 billion USD market capitalization. Unfortunately, smart contracts have been exploited unintentionally or intentionally to cause financial damage to users. For instance, vulnerable smart contracts, especially token contracts, have led to losses amounting to millions of dollars in the past few years. As another example, more and more Ponzi scheme smart contracts appear and swindle users out of lots of money. Moreover, problematic token contracts will also cause financial damage to users. We name all such behaviors as undesirable behaviors. Although there are some recent studies on such undesirable behaviors in smart contracts, there lack of systematic approaches and tools for analyzing smart contracts. First, most of existing studies conduct static analysis on smart contracts and suffer from the inherent limitations. Second, although a few studies employ dynamic analysis (e.g., fuzzing) to detect vulnerabilities, none of them takes into account the context information on which smart contracts rely and thus may miss many paths. In this project, we take the first step towards designing a systematic approach and developing practical tools for automatically exposing the undesirable behaviors in smart contracts. In particular, by exploiting the unique features of blockchain, we will propose a hybrid analysis framework that synthesizes transaction-oriented analysis, static and dynamic analysis to effectively and efficiently identify two kinds of undesirable behaviors in smart contracts, including inconsistent tokens and Ponzi scheme smart contracts. This project will provide theoretical foundations and practical systems for analyzing smart contracts and discovering two kinds of undesirable behaviors in them. This research will lead to a deep understanding of the security issues in smart contracts. It will also result in new methodologies for discovering undesirable behaviors in smart contracts as well as new practical tools and valuable data sets. 支持智能合约是区块链 2.0的显著特征。部署在区块链上的智能合约将会自动执行预定的程序逻辑并具备其他优点，因此将会对许多行业产生深远影响。当前很多区块链系统支持智能合约，其中以太坊是最大的支持智能合约的区块链平台（市值210亿美元），包括超过700万智能合约和3亿4000万交易。同时，以太坊通过智能合约支持绝大部分的加密货币，例如排序最前的100个加密货币市值150亿美元。但是不少智能合约被有意或者无意利用导致用户的经济损失。例如，有漏洞的智能合约在过去几年导致数百万美元丢失。另外，旁氏合约欺骗了用户很多金钱。有问题的加密货币合约也会导致用户经济损失。我们统称这些为智能合约的不良行为。虽然最近有工作分析智能合约，但缺乏系统性的对智能合约的研究以及分析工具。同时绝大部分现在的工具都是基于静态分析，而动态分析工具没有考虑智能合约所依赖的上下文信息。 在这个项目中，我们将设计一个系统性的方法并研发工具来自动发现智能合约中的不良行为。利用区块链的独特性质，我们将研发基于混合分析的框架来研究智能合约并分析两类不良行为，包括不一致的加密货币以及旁氏合约。本研究将从理论和实践两方面对智能合约进行系统性的分析，将加深对智能合约安全问题的认识。

15219319.label: Realisation of objectives
15219319.value: We have realized the three objectives. 1. Detecting abnormal behaviors involving smart contracts. We developed new data acquisition systems for three major blockchain platforms: Ethereum, EOSIO, and Bitcoin. Our systems fetch raw blockchain data during synchronization, extracting information on blocks, transactions, and smart contracts along with their execution traces. Since Bitcoin does not support Turing-complete programming languages for smart contract development, we only collect smart contracts and execution traces from Ethereum and EOSIO. We instrument all interpretation handlers in the smart contract runtimes to gather details on every executed operation, including the program counter, opcode, operand, and the stack/memory/storage items read or written. We organize the collected data hierarchically. At the top level, we record the causal relationships between different accounts and their interactions. At the account level, we document each smart contract involved in a causal relationship, detailing external and public functions invoked and the states modified by these functions. Additionally, we include an instruction level to record major instructions that access or modify states. We developed new approaches to detect anomalies for various applications. For instance, we identified 73 short address attack transactions on Ethereum, involving 25 smart contracts. These findings are detailed in our TSE 2022 paper. From the data collected on EOSIO, we discovered several notable (mis)behaviors, including bot-like accounts for malicious purposes, unchecked input attacks, and predictable state attacks. These results are published in our SIGMETRICS’20 paper. By analyzing the Bitcoin transactions in our dataset, we conducted the first investigation into Bitcoin mixing services, which enhance anonymity without altering the Bitcoin protocol. Our approach identifies most mixing transactions, aiding applications like profit calculation and money laundering investigation. These insights are reported in our WWW’21 paper. Additionally, through transaction analysis, we identified and measured the impact of counterfeit cryptocurrencies on Ethereum, presented in our SIGMETRICS’21 paper. We also used transaction analysis to detect and characterize scam tokens on Uniswap, with findings published in our SIGMETRICS’22 paper. 2. Conducting static and dynamic analysis on smart contracts. We have designed new approaches for conducting static and dynamic analysis on smart contracts. First, we identified the needs of smart contract developers to design better tools, as detailed in our ICSE’21 paper. We collected numerous smart contract bugs from multiple sources, categorizing them into nine groups by extending the IEEE Standard Classification for Software Anomalies. We also designed criteria for detecting each type of bug and constructed a dataset covering all categories. Our framework and dataset assist developers in learning about smart contract bugs and developing new tools for bug detection and localization. These results are detailed in our ICSME’20 paper. To invoke functions in Ethereum smart contracts, a caller must know the function signature of the callee, which includes its function ID and parameter types. Recovering these signatures from contract bytecode is challenging due to the lack of debug and type information. We proposed SigRec, a novel solution leveraging EVM to automatically recover function signatures. SigRec outperforms existing tools, achieving 98.7% accuracy in 0.074 seconds. Recovered function signatures are useful for attack detection, fuzzing, and reverse engineering of EVM bytecode. The corresponding paper was published in IEEE TSE 2020. We developed DEFECTCHECKER, which conducts static analysis of Ethereum smart contract bytecode to automatically reveal defects causing unwanted behaviors. DEFECTCHECKER has a high F-score (88.8%) and analyzes a contract in 0.15 seconds on average. Applied to 165,621 distinct smart contracts, we found that 25,815 contained at least one defect. The corresponding paper appeared in IEEE TSE 2022. We also proposed EOSAFE, the first static analysis framework for automatically detecting vulnerabilities in EOSIO smart contracts at the bytecode level. EOSAFE features a symbolic execution engine for Wasm, a library emulator for EOSIO smart contracts, and four heuristic-driven detectors for the most common vulnerabilities. EOSAFE achieves an F1-measure of 98% and identified vulnerabilities in over 25% of the 53,666 smart contracts analyzed, with 48 confirmed in-the-wild attacks causing at least $1.7 million in financial losses. These results are reported in our USENIX SEC’21 paper. For dynamic analysis, we conducted a systematic investigation of smart contract fuzzing techniques, providing new insights and directions for future research, published in our ICSE’24 paper. We also developed RLF, a vulnerability-guided fuzzer using reinforcement learning to generate transaction sequences that detect sophisticated vulnerabilities. RLF models fuzzing as a Markov decision process and uses a reward system considering both vulnerability and code coverage. Experimental results show RLF outperforms state-of-the-art tools, detecting 8%-69% more vulnerabilities within 30 minutes. The corresponding paper appeared in ASE’22. 3. Characterizing undesirable behaviors in smart contracts. We conducted extensive research on cryptocurrency tokens, starting with an analysis of over 190,000 ERC-20 tokens on Ethereum. We identified 2,117 counterfeit tokens targeting 94 of the 100 most popular cryptocurrencies. Our study characterized the counterfeit token ecosystem, including their popularity, creators, holders, fraudulent behaviors, and advertising channels. We discovered that over 7,104 victims lost at least $17 million in these scams. The findings were published in SIGMETRICS'21. Next, we developed SADPonzi, a semantic-aware detection approach for identifying Ponzi schemes in Ethereum smart contracts. By strictly adhering to the definition of Ponzi schemes, we used a heuristic-guided symbolic execution technique to generate semantic information for each feasible path in smart contracts, identifying investor-related transfer behaviors and distribution strategies. SADPonzi achieved 100% precision and recall, outperforming all existing machine-learning-based techniques. Applied to 3.4 million smart contracts, we identified 835 Ponzi schemes with over $17 million invested by victims. This work was also published in SIGMETRICS'21. To address challenges in recognizing token transfer behaviors accurately, we developed TokenAware. This tool infers token transfer behaviors from modifications in the internal bookkeeping of token smart contracts, recording information about tokens. TokenAware overcomes the lack of type information in smart contract bytecode by learning the instruction sequences for locating basic types and then deriving sequences for sophisticated types. Our experiments showed that TokenAware can automatically identify new types of bookkeeping and recognize 107,202 tokens with 98.7% precision, incurring only 4% overhead. The corresponding paper appeared in ACM TOSEM 2023. We also took significant steps to detect and characterize scam tokens on Uniswap, a prominent decentralized exchange (DEX). By analyzing transactions related to Uniswap V2, we proposed an accurate approach for flagging scam tokens using a guilt-by-association heuristic and machine-learning techniques. We identified over 10,000 scam tokens, suggesting that roughly 50% of the tokens listed on Uniswap are scams. These scams, often involving "rug pull" schemes with embedded tricks and backdoors in smart contracts, resulted in at least $16 million in profits from 39,762 potential victims. This work was published in SIGMETRICS'22. Additionally, we systematically analyzed three types of defects in NFT contracts: fragile NFT binding, non-compliant implementation, and implanted backdoors. We proposed Emerium, the first extensible detection framework for capturing these defects by inspecting smart contract bytecode. Applied to 87,839 ERC-721 and 9,808 ERC-1155 NFT contracts, Emerium uncovered 34,510,279 defects of fragile NFT binding, 1,412 defects of non-compliant implementation, and 65 backdoors, including a new CVE. This paper has been submitted to IEEE TDSC.

15219319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219319.value: We proposed and developed a hybrid analysis framework combining transaction-oriented, static, and dynamic analysis to identify undesirable behaviors in smart contracts, such as inconsistent tokens and Ponzi schemes. We created data acquisition systems for Ethereum, EOSIO, and Bitcoin, extracting information on blocks, transactions, and smart contracts along with their execution traces. We instrumented interpretation handlers in smart contract runtimes to gather detailed execution information. Through novel transaction analysis, we identified various undesirable behaviors in smart contracts. For example, we detected 73 short address attack transactions on Ethereum involving 25 smart contracts. On EOSIO, we found several misbehaviors, including bot-like accounts and unchecked input attacks. Our analysis of Bitcoin transactions led to the first investigation into Bitcoin mixing services, aiding applications like profit calculation and money laundering detection. Additionally, we identified and measured the impact of counterfeit cryptocurrencies on Ethereum and detected scam tokens on Uniswap. We designed new approaches for static and dynamic analysis of smart contracts. We identified developers' needs and provided a comprehensive categorization of smart contract bugs. We developed a framework and dataset to assist in bug detection and localization. We proposed SigRec for recovering function signatures in Ethereum smart contracts, achieving 98.7% accuracy in 0.074 seconds. DEFECTCHECKER, our static analysis tool, revealed defects in 25,815 out of 165,621 smart contracts, with a high F-score of 88.8%. EOSAFE, our framework for detecting vulnerabilities in EOSIO smart contracts, identified vulnerabilities in over 25% of the 53,666 contracts analyzed, uncovering 48 confirmed attacks. For dynamic analysis, we investigated smart contract fuzzing techniques and developed RLF, a reinforcement learning-based fuzzer that outperforms state-of-the-art tools, detecting 8%-69% more vulnerabilities within 30 minutes. We conducted extensive studies on cryptocurrency tokens. We analyzed over 190,000 ERC-20 tokens on Ethereum, identifying 2,117 counterfeit tokens targeting popular cryptocurrencies, resulting in $17 million in losses for 7,104 victims. We developed SADPonzi to detect Ponzi schemes in Ethereum smart contracts, identifying 835 schemes involving $17 million in investments. To address token transfer recognition challenges, we proposed TokenAware, which identifies token behaviors with 98.7% precision and low overhead. Finally, we detected and characterized scam tokens on Uniswap, finding over 10,000 scam tokens and revealing $16 million in profits from 39,762 victims. We published three journal papers and ten conference papers and submitted one to TDSC. We trained one Ph.D. student, one M.Sc. student, and several undergraduate students. Additionally, we collaborated with researchers from multiple universities on this research.

15219319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219319.value: Our research has laid a strong foundation for identifying undesirable behaviors in smart contracts and cryptocurrency transactions. Moving forward, we propose three key areas of development to enhance and expand our framework's capabilities. First, leveraging LLMs can significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of transaction analysis. By integrating LLMs, we can better understand and classify complex transaction patterns and behaviors, enhancing our ability to detect fraudulent activities and other anomalies in real-time. Second, to accelerate the analysis process, we propose utilizing GPUs to handle the computationally intensive tasks involved in static and dynamic analysis. GPUs can process parallel tasks much faster than traditional CPUs, enabling quicker identification of bugs and vulnerabilities. This speedup will allow for real-time or near-real-time analysis of smart contracts, making our system more responsive and scalable, especially as the volume of blockchain data continues to grow. Third, as blockchain technology evolves, so do the techniques used by malicious actors. New methods and tools are needed to detect and mitigate emerging threats. This includes developing advanced algorithms and heuristics to handle novel attack vectors and integrating machine learning models that adapt to new attack patterns.

15219319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219319.value: Our research enhances the security of smart contracts, which are blockchain programs enabling applications beyond cryptocurrency but can be exploited, causing financial losses. Our goal is to identify and prevent these harmful behaviors. To achieve this purpose, we developed a systematic approach combining transaction, static, and dynamic code analysis to automatically detect undesirable behaviors in smart contracts. For example, we revealed the impact of fake cryptocurrencies on Ethereum and detected scam tokens on Uniswap, a popular decentralized exchange. We also uncovered short address attack transactions on Ethereum and identified problematic behaviors on the EOSIO platform. We developed many innovative approaches and tools to facilitate the analysis, including SigRec, which recovers function signatures with 98.7% accuracy in 0.074 seconds; DEFECTCHECKER, which found defects in 25,815 out of 165,621 smart contracts; EOSAFE, which detects vulnerabilities in over 25% of analyzed EOSIO contracts; SADPonzi, which discovers 835 Ponzi schemes involving $17 million in investments; TokenAware, which accurately identifies token behaviors with low overhead, and others. This research improves our understanding of smart contract security, introduces new methods for detecting harmful behaviors, and provides valuable tools and data. It will also be used to train students in developing secure and reliable smart contracts.

15219619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219619.value: Due to massive proliferation of various uncertainties including fluctuating renewable generations and unpredictable consumer-driven loads, traditional deterministic planning approach to seek and assess the ‘worst scenario’ often results in either non-economical or non-robust solutions. It can be certainly expected that probabilistic planning approach will play a vital role in future operational planning to compensate the noticeable disadvantages of deterministic approach. On the other hand, with the development of active distribution network (ADN), the network nature changes significantly, and system operational planning becomes indispensable for distribution network owner (DNO), who starts devoting more resources to distribution system operator (DSO) role. However, quite many operational planning tools cannot be directly borrowed from transmission system operator (TSO) owing to different characteristics of distribution network (e.g., unbalancing phase and radial topology). There are many probabilistic approaches for transmission network security assessment but not many for distribution network, where however most distributed renewables and EVs are actually connected. Considering the above-mentioned points, there is an urgent need to develop an effective probabilistic planning approach for both TSO and DSO. Probabilistic analysis has been used in power system stability assessment such as probabilistic oscillatory stability analysis and so far most research efforts including PI have been devoted to investigating low frequency oscillation (LFO) in transmission network. However, various emerging oscillation problems brought by the integration of power electronic converter-interfaced equipment (e.g., sub-synchronous oscillation/resonance between wind farm and weak grid) have posed a severe threat and enormous challenge to both TSO and DSO, which are essentially different from LFO. Those complicated oscillations and their probabilistic assessment approaches have not been systematically examined. Therefore, the project aims to develop an integrated probabilistic analysis methodology to assess oscillatory instability risk in both transmission and distribution networks. A holomorphic embedding-based intelligent technique will be proposed to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the established methodology. Two major scientific questions will be essentially tackled: 1. What is the general methodology to quantify the probabilistic stability margin of multiple oscillations to provide a critical guidance&indicator to system operators for decision-making? (extension from analysis of pure LFO to multiple oscillations across frequency spectrum) 2. How to accommodate the requirement of ADN? (extension from TSO planning to coexistent TSO&DSO planning) The methodology will be validated in real large-scale power systems and the project will undoubtedly bring significant benefits to future operational planning worldwide especially for Hong Kong CLP, National Grid UK and Southern California grid. 由於大量不確定性源的出現（如波動的可再生能源發電和不可預測的消費者行為驅動型負荷等），旨在尋找和評估“最壞情況場景”的傳統確定性規劃方法很可能會帶來不經濟或者不魯棒的解決方案。可以預見概率性規劃方法將在未來的電網運行規劃中發揮重要作用，以彌補確定性方法的顯著缺陷。另一方面，隨著主動配電網的發展，電網的網絡性質發生了重大變化，配電公司需要進行電網的運行規劃工作，因此配電公司開始將更多的資源投入到配電網運行規劃中。然而，由於配電網的特性不同（如三相不平衡運行和輻射狀拓撲結構），不能直接借用輸電網的運行規劃方法。目前用於輸電網安全評估的概率性方法很多，但用於配電網的概率性方法卻不多見，大多數分布式可再生能源和電動汽車實際上卻是通過配電網接入的。考慮到上述幾點，迫切需要開發一種同時適用於輸配電網運行的有效的概率性規劃方法。概率性分析在電力系統穩定性評估中得到了廣泛的應用（如概率振蕩穩定性的分析），迄今為止包括項目負責人在內的大多數研究者都致力於研究輸電網中的低頻振蕩問題。然而，電力電子變流器連接的設備並網所帶來的各種新型振蕩問題（如風電場與弱電網之間的次同步振蕩或諧振）與低頻振蕩有著本質上的區別，對輸配電網運行都構成了嚴重的威脅和巨大的挑戰。這些覆雜的振蕩及其概率性評估方法尚未得到系統性的研究。因此，本項目旨在研發一套完整的概率性分析方法來評估輸電網和配電網的振蕩不穩定風險。將會提出一種基於holomorphic embedding的智能技術來提高所提出方法的準確性和效率。本項目主要解決兩個科學問題：1、能否找到量化多類型振蕩的概率穩定性裕度的通用性方法（即從單一的低頻振蕩分析擴展到多類型的各種頻率振蕩分析）從而為系統運行規劃人員的決策提供重要的指導？2、如何滿足主動配電網的需求（即從單一的輸電網規劃擴展到同時適用於輸配電網的規劃）？本項目提出的方法理論將在實際的大型電網中進行驗證，項目成果無疑將為包括中華電力、英國國家電網和南加州電網在內的電網未來運行規劃帶來顯著的效益。

15219619.label: Realisation of objectives
15219619.value: The original project objective 4 has been revised after the project is granted based on the actual given funding and resources as well as the comments from the reviewers. To date, all the objectives of the project have been achieved. Some cut part of the original objective 4 has also been achieved. The details are provided as follows. Objective 1: Impact characterization and quantification of various uncertainty sources and derivation of their probabilistic models suitable for planning studies. The practicability of power system uncertainty characterisation of existing probabilistic modeling by considering various technical details in both breadth and depth has been enhanced in order to meet the operational requirements and standards. The improvement on probabilistic modeling diversity (breadth) mainly includes the consideration of the uncertainty of converter control effects due to varying wind speed or solar radiation, the uncertainty of different grid interactive loads and the uncertainty of measurement error. The improvement on probabilistic modeling details (depth) mainly includes the consideration of detailed individual wind generator model to replace the aggregated wind farm model. Both the internal and external wake effects and correlations among different wind farms and wind generators have been properly modeled and thus taken into account. The detailed probabilistic modeling has been compared with the aggregate probabilistic modeling and proved to be more accurate and practical. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 13 and 15, and Conference Paper 4 in Part C. Objective 2: Development of spectral impedance margin index-based universal probabilistic analysis of multiple oscillatory stability in electricity networks covering both transmission and distribution systems In order to develop the capable spectral impedance margin index for multiple oscillatory stability, mechanism analysis of wideband oscillation in the power electronics-dominated cyber-physical transmission and distribution systems has been conducted to provide in-depth physical insights and understanding. Then the difference and connection of different criteria of small-signal stability have been systematically reviewed and the limitations of existing criteria in dealing with the wideband oscillations in power electronics-dominated power systems have also been revealed. On this basis, a novel frequency response gradient-enabled impedance-based stability criterion has been proposed to effectively explain and address the zero-zero interference, pole-pole interference and zero-pole interference, and efficiently determine the frequencies, stability and margins of potential wideband oscillations. The proposed criterion has been employed in the form of spectral and sequence impedance respectively for the probabilistic analysis of multiple oscillatory stability in transmission and distribution systems. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 4, 6, 7, 10-12 and 14, and Conference Paper 1 in Part C. Objective 3: Intelligent technique to improve accuracy and efficiency of probabilistic analysis methodology Multiple intelligent techniques have been developed to improve the accuracy and efficiency of probabilistic analysis methodology including the efficient sampling algorithm, partitioning around medoids (PAM)-convex hall (CH) and density-based spatial clustering of application with noises (DBSCAN)-PAM ensemble methods, holomorphic embedding algorithm, physics-informed dynamic mode decomposition method, generalized polynomial chaos expansion method and domain-adversarial graph neural network. The interlinked frequency and voltage stability issues have been also studied and the intelligent techniques to accelerate the probabilistic analysis can be easily extended and applied in oscillatory stability. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 1, 3, 5 and 8, and Conference Paper 2-5 in Part C. Revised objective 4: Implementation and demonstration of developed methodology for oscillatory risk assessment and visualization of large-scale power systems with multiple uncertain sources The developed frequency response gradient-enabled impedance-based stability criterion and spectral/sequence impedance margin index-based universal probabilistic analysis have been implemented and demonstrated in multiple large-scale power systems with different uncertain sources including IEEE 68-bus transmission benchmark test power system, IEEE 33-bus distribution benchmark test system, provincial power grid in East China, and Great Britain power grid. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 9 and 14, Conference Paper 3 and 5 in Part C. Cut part of original objective 4: Design of optimal and robust control strategies to tackle various probabilistic oscillatory instabilities in transmission and distribution networks. Based on the results of probabilistic analysis, different risk mitigation strategies regarding the optimal allocation of control resources have been proposed and compared. The real-time robust control and dispatch of massive distributed energy resources have also been designed for damping the oscillations in the interconnected transmission and distribution systems to achieve the TSO and DSO coordination. For more details, please refer to Journal Paper 2 and 9 in Part C.

15219619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219619.value: The major findings and research outcome are summarized associated with the selected research outputs of the project. By carefully reviewing and studying emerging security issues in both transmission and distribution grids, it is revealed that many security issues are in the form of oscillations in different frequency range (associated with Journal Paper 4, 6, 7 and 10 in Part C). Hence, more efforts should be made in the risk assessment of wideband oscillations. By systematically reviewing and comparing the existing small-signal stability criteria, it is discovered that there are some major restrictions of existing criteria in dealing with the wideband oscillation problems (associated with Journal Paper 11 and Conference Paper 1 in Part C). They cannot accurately indicate the stability margin like eigenvalue does and they can easily miss the poles and zeros due to the so called zero-zero interference, pole-pole interference and zero-pole interference. There is a pressing need to develop a new small-signal stability criterion for the project purpose. Therefore, the frequency response gradient-enabled impedance-based stability criterion has been developed to tackle the restrictions of existing criteria (associated with Journal Paper 12 in Part C) and then employed for the probabilistic small-signal stability analysis for multiple oscillations in both transmission and distribution systems (associated with Journal Paper 14 in Part C). The advantages of the developed method include: there is no need to know the exact frequency of the oscillation mode but can focus on a concerned oscillation frequency range; By using the spectral impedance, it is straightforward to visualise the oscillatory instability risk for the benefit of system operator; The method can deal with various uncertainty sources (associated with Journal Paper 13 and 15, and Conference Paper 4 in Part C.) and can be accelerated by using multiple intelligent techniques (associated with Journal Paper 1, 3, 5 and 8, and Conference Paper 2-5 in Part C). The developed integrated probabilistic analysis method has been extensively validated in multiple large-scale real power grids to be effective and efficient, and some trials have been conducted to mitigate the risk of oscillatory instability in both transmission and distribution systems (associated with Journal Paper 2, 9 and 14, and Conference Paper 3 and 5 in Part C).

15219619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219619.value: Based on the current achievements of the project, further development of the research can be planned and conducted in the following aspects: 1. To tackle the impacts of measurement errors on measured impedance and analysis results and consider the uncertainty induced by measurement errors during the determination of the proposed spectral/sequence impedance-based stability index; 2. To measure the impedance of different system components or regions at the same time; 3. To utilise multiple-point-based linearization method to improve the accuracy of the method and obtain the sensitivity at different operating points for the proposed spectral/sequence impedance-based stability index; 4. To determine the relationship between the proposed positive/negative sequence impedance and the oscillations in three-phase active distribution networks; 5. To consider the impact of topology uncertainties on oscillatory stability. Besides, we have almost completed a paper titled ‘Sequence Impedance-based Oscillatory Instability Risk Analysis in Unbalanced Active Distribution Networks’ to assess the risk associated with oscillatory instability of distribution networks by using proposed impedance-based stability index. This paper is not included in Part C: Research Output of the Completion Report but will be ready for submission soon.

15219619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219619.value: To limit global warming to 1.5 degrees compared to pre-industrial levels, the Carbon Neutrality target by 2050 has become a consensus among many countries and regions worldwide. Renewable energy and electric vehicle (EV) will be expected to have a large market share and their integration into both transmission and distribution system sides will introduce massive uncertainties, thus posing critical risks to power system secure operation, particularly on the oscillatory stability. Moreover, the large-scale integration of renewables and EVs have significantly increased the modeling complexity and computational burden of system risk assessment in the operational planning. Therefore, there is a pressing need to provide an effective and economical solution to both transmission and distribution system operators to facilitate their decision-making in the operational planning. This project aims to develop an integrated probabilistic analysis tool to efficiently assess and visualise the oscillatory instability risk for both grids and tackle the technical bottleneck of the existing operational planning tools. The project outcomes have been very fruitful and of both substantial theoretical and practical values. The project has provided theoretical guidance and technical support to both transmission and distribution system operators for the secure operation of future power grids.

15219819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219819.value: The condition of civil infrastructure around the world is rapidly degrading due to a variety of deteriorating processes. Fatigue is a primary example of this; the cyclical loading due to traffic, winds, etc., can induce fatigue damage and lead to fracture and failure of steel bridges. Currently, structural health monitoring (SHM) techniques have been implemented in structural condition assessment and diagnosis process. Although civil engineering practice has been largely impacted by advances in SHM, there is still an outstanding question of how to convert data into useful information for infrastructure owners to make optimal decision over service lives of infrastructure. Therefore, further research is needed to harness the powerful information embedded in SHM data by systematically integrating it into reliability-informed life-cycle maintenance planning of infrastructure and related decision-making. In order to incorporate SHM within decision-making processes for management of deteriorating structures, performance should be assessed and predicted forward in a way that accounts for uncertainties of structural resistance, operating conditions, and loading, among others. In this research project, time-dependent reliability and life-cycle costs, with and without monitoring, will be computed. The proposed study will investigate the propagation of uncertainties through the life-cycle analysis. Subsequently, by Bayesian inference, time-dependent performance will be updated by incorporating data from SHM. In this way, the remaining service life of infrastructure can be determined and updated by coupling SHM data with physical models and probabilistic methods. Given the updated performance, decision of maintenance can be made. In practice, maintenance decisions are usually made based on the decision maker’s experience or intuition, and may not account for information ascertained from SHM. Alternatively, data from monitoring can be integrated with decision theory to support optimal infrastructure management. Value of Information (VoI) can be used to represent the difference between expected benefits evaluated with and without a certain piece of information, i.e., SHM data. This research will integrate the VoI of SHM data into decision theory to support the optimal life-cycle management of structures. Overall, the proposed project aims to develop a comprehensive framework for utility-informed decision-making for management of bridges through the efficient integration of SHM data, time-dependent reliability theory, life-cycle analysis, Bayesian approaches, and VoI. This project will advance both the state-of-the-art and state-of-practice in equipping bridges with a near real-time optimum decision-making system. Tsing Ma Bridge and Stonecutters Bridge, equipped with advanced SHM systems, provide a unique platform for implementation and demonstration of the proposed framework. 受環境、汽車荷載以及自然災害等作用的影響，世界各地的基礎設施的狀況正日益惡化、甚至破壞（例如靜力破壞和疲勞破壞）。目前，結構健康監測（SHM）系統已在結構狀態評估和診斷過程中得以廣泛的應用。儘管SHM推動了土木工程的發展，但仍然存在一個突出的問題：如何將監測的數據轉換為有用的信息，從而支持決策者做出能夠延長基礎設施的壽命的最佳決策。為此，需要進一步探究SHM數據中的信息，並將其係統性地集成到基礎設施全壽命週期維護管養的體系中。 為了更系統、全面地管理日益惡化的基礎設施，應該綜合考慮結構抗力、運營條件以及結構荷載的不確定性，對結構的全壽命性能進行更可靠的評估和預測。在此研究項目將計算基礎設施全壽命內的時變可靠度和全壽命成本，同時研究各種不確定性在全壽命週期內的傳播規律。隨後，通過貝葉斯框架，利用SHM的數據來更新結構的性能指標。通過此方式，可以將SHM數據、物理模型以及概率方法等理論體系加以耦合，從而確定和更新基礎設施的性能指標和殘餘壽命。基於更新後的結構性能，可以做出可靠和魯棒的維修決策。在實際工程中，維護決策往往基於決策者的經驗或直覺，尚未系統的考慮SHM中的信息。對此，需要把監控的數據與決策理論結合，以建立系統全面的基建管理體系。信息價值（VoI）可用於計算使用和不使用某信息（即SHM數據）帶來的預期收益之間的差異。該研究將SHM數據的VoI整合到決策理論中，從而建立最佳的結構全壽命管理體系。 總之，此項目旨在建立一個基礎設施全壽命週期的運營管理框架：通過有效整合SHM數據，根據時變可靠性理論、全壽命週期分析、貝葉斯方法和VoI來管理橋樑的管養和運營決策。青馬大橋和昂船洲大橋配備先進的SHM系統，為擬建框架的實施和演示提供了獨特的平台。

15219819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219819.value: The funded project has introduced a comprehensive framework for decision-making aimed at optimizing the life-cycle management of bridges. This optimization is achieved through the efficient integration of Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) data, time-dependent reliability theory, life-cycle analysis, Bayesian approaches, and Value of Information (VoI) considerations. The overarching goal of this project is to significantly advance both the state-of-the-art and state-of-practice in equipping bridges with a near real-time optimal decision-making system. The developed techniques and technologies from this project have yielded an integrative monitoring platform and decision-making tool. These tools are poised to play a crucial role in the future design and maintenance of a broad spectrum of infrastructure. The incorporation of SHM data, time-dependent reliability theory, life-cycle analysis, Bayesian approaches, and VoI considerations ensures a holistic and efficient approach to decision-making throughout the life cycle of bridges. As a testament to the project's success, the research team has published six journal papers based on their findings. Additionally, they have actively participated in international conferences, disseminating the project's key insights and contributing to the broader scientific community. These efforts not only underscore the project's impact but also position it as a notable and influential contribution to the field of bridge engineering and infrastructure management.

15219819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219819.value: The project has successfully achieved all its objectives and stands ready to be embraced as a user-friendly, comprehensive infrastructure management framework that spans multiple infrastructure systems, accommodating various deterioration scenarios. While the project has primarily emphasized fatigue, it provides a flexible foundation for further development to include other deterioration mechanisms within the established unified framework for further development. Specifically, the research team has delved into the corrosion-fatigue effect, laying the groundwork for subsequent phases of development. Moving forward, the team is poised to concentrate on life-cycle maintenance planning, utilizing the algorithm developed in this project. This extension of focus beyond fatigue to include corrosion and other potential deterioration mechanisms reflects the adaptability and versatility of the project's framework. As such, it positions the framework as a robust solution for holistic infrastructure management, ensuring resilience across diverse deterioration scenarios and contributing to the long-term sustainability of infrastructure systems.

15219819.value: The condition of civil infrastructure around the world is rapidly degrading due to a variety of deteriorating processes. Fatigue is a primary example and can lead to fracture and failure of steel bridges. Although civil engineering practice has been largely impacted by advances in SHM, there is still an outstanding question of how to convert data into useful information for infrastructure owners to make optimal decisions over the service lives of infrastructure. This research project has provided a novel direction for the evolution of infrastructure management by innovatively bridging the gap between the current infrastructure decision-making and monitoring research and practice. The project has combined emerging health-monitoring techniques, time-dependent structural reliability theory, life-cycle analysis, Bayesian inference, utility theory, VoI, and decision-making. 15219919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15219919.value: Use of externally bonded (EB) fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) reinforcement to strengthen existing reinforced concrete (RC) structures has become very popular. However, due to the poor fire performance of polymer matrix, the fire safety has become a major issue that impedes the wider adoption of the EB-FRP techniques in building applications particularly in Hong Kong. Substantial efforts have been devoted to the development of a rational fire design approach for the EB-FRP strengthening system to maintain sufficient fire safety while minimizing the need for insulation. Recently, the focus shifts to the development of fabric-reinforced cementitious matrix (FRCM) strengthening systems as an alternative, which are expected to possess better fire performance due to the inflammable nature of the cementitious matrix. However, little has been understood about the fire behavior of FRCM-strengthened systems and most of cementitious matrices may exhibit significant mechanical performance deterioration during a fire. This project aims to develop an innovative FRCM system for strengthening of RC members to offer a new avenue for fire protection. The system is based on a sodium hexametaphosphate (SHMP)–modified calcium aluminate cementitious matrix recently developed in the PI’s group, which could maintain most of its ambient temperature strength even after exposure to 1000°C for 2 h. Besides, the cement matrix will be entitled with ultra-high ductility and multiple crack characteristics by addition of short fibers, to prevent/delay the debonding failure between the strengthening layer and the concrete substrate. To fully understand the performance of the above FRCM strengthening system under fire and facilitate its wider practical application, the following specific topics will be covered: (1) Thermal and mechanical properties of the proposed FRCM at elevated temperatures; (2) Bond deterioration mechanisms of the proposed FRCM system with substrate concrete at elevated temperatures; (3) Time-dependent structural performance of RC beams strengthened with the proposed FRCM systems under standard fire exposure; and (4) Simplified fire-resistant design approach for the strengthened RC beams. The project meets an urgent socioeconomic need to upgrade aging building structures in Hong Kong and the rest of the world. It provides an innovative but cost-effective solution to the critical fire problem that hinders the wider adoption of the FRP strengthening technology in Hong Kong. Upon the completion of the project, a significant body of knowledge will also be created on the fire-resistant cementitious materials and their scientific implication on the structural safety of RC members strengthened with them. 15219919.label: Realisation of objectives
15219919.value: All the objectives set out for the project have been completely achieved. 1. Objective 1 has been realized through experimental programs on the mechanical performance of different FRCMs after different temperature exposures and theoretical modeling of their tension-stiffening behavior. 2. Objective 2 has been achieved by investigating the bond deterioration mechanisms of a series of FRCM-to-concrete bonded joints after different temperature exposures. 3. Objective 3 has been achieved by investigating the temperature elevation in RC beams strengthened with FRCM systems subjected to a sustained service load and exposed to the ISO standard fire and associated deflection increase of the beams. Finite element modeling was conducted to simulate the time-dependent temperature field changes and deflection evolution. 4. Objective 4 has been achieved by theoretically predicting the time-dependent load-carrying capacity of FRCM-strengthened RC beams after different periods of elevated temperature exposure. The modeling was carried out based on sectional analyses considering the degradation of different material components.

15219919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15219919.value: The project has involved a significant amount of experimental tests, theoretical analyses, and finite element modeling work, which led to the major findings and research outcomes as follows: (1) A new FRCM system has been developed, which utilizes basalt FRP grids as the reinforcing fabrics and geopolymer as the inorganic cementitious binder. The use of inorganic mineral basalt fabrics in combination with a cementitious matrix presents a promising solution for creating high-performance FRCM composites. These composites demonstrate superior high-temperature resistance and good bond performance with concrete substrate. (Refer to journal papers 1,2,5, and 11 in Part 3); (2) An extensive experimental study was carried out to compare the residual bond performance of epoxy and cement-bonded carbon/basalt fiber-reinforced polymer reinforcement to concrete interfaces exposed to varying levels of elevated temperatures ranging from 20 °C to 600 °C. Different types of cementitious matrices were used as the cement binder for comparison. The study aimed to elucidate the change in failure modes and associated failure mechanisms at different temperatures. It revealed a decrease in interfacial fracture energy and bond-slip relationship of FRCM-to-concrete interfaces at elevated temperatures, along with an examination of microstructural degradation. (Refer to journal papers 3, 4, 7, and 8 in Part 3); (3) A systematic investigation has been conducted to reveal the different debonding mechanisms (plate-end debonding and intermediate crack-induced debonding) in FRCM-strengthened RC members considering the coupled mechanical and temperature effects, through experimental tests, analytical modeling, and finite element modeling. Based on the precise understanding of the debonding mechanisms that are associated with the degradation of interfacial bond properties and material degradations, the load-carrying capacity of the strengthened beams at elevated temperatures could be accurately predicted. (Referred to journal papers 6, 9, 10, 13, and 14 in Part 3); (4) A hybrid-bonding technique was developed to provide additional mechanical fastening through a steel cover plate for the strengthening layer of RC beams. The friction between the steel cover plate and the strengthening layer and the reacted normal stress at the interface could enhance the concrete aggregates' interlocking and the interface bond strength. Additionally, the normal stresses can be also activated through pre-tightening the anchors. (Refer to Journal paper 12 in Part 3). In summary, these above findings have led to a promising alternative to externally bonded FRP systems in fire-critical applications for significant improvement of fire resistance as well as superior structural strengthening efficiency.

15219919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15219919.value: The completed research project focused on the flexural performance of FRCM-strengthened RC members subjected to elevated temperatures. The PI’s team plans to further investigate the shear performance of FRCM-strengthened RC members as well as the structural performance of FRCM-confined RC members subjected to elevated temperature. Eventually, a unified theoretical approach will be formed to predict the structural performance of FRP and FRCM-strengthened RC structures under elevated temperature exposures. In the future, the PI will attempt to reflect all the research outcomes into the code of practice development for FRCM-strengthened RC structures, which will promote the adoption of FRCM-strengthening technology in practical applications.

15219919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15219919.value: Using externally bonded fiber-reinforced cementitious matrix (FRCM) to replace externally bonded (EB) fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) reinforcement to strengthen existing reinforced concrete (RC) structures has become very popular. FRCM is believed to possess better performance than FRP at elevated temperatures due to the inorganic and inflammable nature of the cementitious matrix. However, little has been understood about the fire behavior of FRCM-strengthened systems, although most cementitious matrices may exhibit mechanical performance deterioration during a fire. This project provides an innovative but cost-effective FRCM solution to the critical fire problem that hinders the broader adoption of the FRP strengthening technology for indoor applications and investigates systematically the structural performance of such FRCM-strengthened RC members subjected to elevated temperature at material, interface, and structural levels. Upon the completion of the project, a significant body of knowledge was created on the fire-resistant properties of the FRCM system, and the scientific implication on the structural safety of RC members strengthened with the FRCM system and led to a simplified design approach. 15220119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220119.value: This project is to study a novel optical fibre-based hybrid mid-infrared (MIR) – near-infrared (NIR) photothermal interferometry (PTI) technique for gas detection with high sensitivity and large dynamic range. Previously, we demonstrated compact hollow-core photonic-crystal-fibre (HC-PCF) PTI sensors for detecting absorptive gases. A HC-PCF confines simultaneously a pump and a probe beam as well as gas-phase materials in its hollow-core. Pump absorption of gas molecules produces heat and modulates the phase of the probe beam via photothermal (PT) effect, which is detected by fibre-optic interferometry. The HC-PCF PTI sensors have achieved remarkable detection sensitivity and dynamic range, about three orders of magnitude better than the direct absorption sensors with the same HC-PCF. However, HC-PCFs have a limited transmission window (e.g., 1.4 to 1.7 micrometers for NKT’s HC-1550-02 fibre), making it difficult to access to the stronger absorption lines in the MIR to develop higher sensitivity sensors. Recently, nodeless hollow-core negative-curvature-fibres (HC-NCFs) with transmission windows covering both NIR (e.g., 1.5 to 1.8 micrometers) and MIR (e.g., 2 to 4.5 micrometers) have been reported. This provides the opportunity to assess the potential offered by these fibres for PTI gas sensors with a MIR pump and a NIR probe. The use of a MIR pump enables access to the much stronger absorption lines to produce larger PT phase modulation, while a NIR fibre-optic interferometer provides a cost-effective means to detect the phase modulation with high sensitivity and large dynamic range, avoiding the use of bulky and costly MIR components and cooled photodetectors. Here we propose to investigate such hybrid MIR-NIR PTI sensors with HC-NCFs. We will focus on ethane detection here, but the technique can be used to detect many other gases that have strong absorption in the MIR. Ethane is an important bio-marker in breath test but has no strong absorption line in the NIR. We plan to use a 3.35-micrometer-laser to pump the gas-filled HC-NCF and an all-fiber interferometer at 1.62 micrometer to detect the PT phase modulation. Our preliminary analysis shows that, with 1-meter-long HC-NCF and a pump power of 5 mW, the hybrid PTI sensors could achieve a bandwidth-normalized noise-equivalent limit-of-detection of ~25 ppb/(Hz)1/2 ethane and a dynamic range of six orders of magnitude. To our knowledge, such a high performance cannot be achieved with compact optical sensors. We will study the phase modulation dynamics and performance-limiting factors, and optimize the detection system to achieve the envisioned record-breaking performance. 本課題旨在研究一種新型的基於光纖的混合中紅外(MIR)–近紅外(NIR)光熱干涉測量(PTI)技術,用於高靈敏度和大動態範圍的氣體檢測。 此前, 我們曾演示了用於檢測吸收性氣體的緊湊型空芯光子晶體光纖 (HC-PCF) PTI 感應器。HC-PCF 可以同時限制泵浦光和探测光以及氣相材料在空芯中。氣體分子吸收泵浦光產生熱量, 通過光熱(PT)效應調製探测光的相位,通过干涉測量可以檢測到氣體濃度。HC-PCF PTI 檢測技術使感應器的檢測靈敏度和動態範圍的得到了顯著提升,比利用同樣 HC-PCF 的直接吸收感應器高出約三個數量級。 但是, HC-PCF 的傳輸視窗有限(例如, NKT 的 HC-1550-02 光纖的傳輸視窗為 1.4 至 1.7 微米), 因此難以利用 MIR 區域更強的氣體吸收線以開發更高靈敏度的感應器。 最近出現了無節點空心-諧振型負曲率光纖(HC-NCFs), 其傳輸視窗同時覆蓋NIR (例如,1.5至1.8微米)和MIR(例如,2至4.5微米)。 這使得在同一光纖中傳輸MIR泵浦光和和NIR探測光成為可能。 使用 MIR 泵浦可以利用更強的吸收線,從而產生更大的 PT 相調製,而NIR光纖干涉儀提供了一種經濟高效的方法來實現高靈敏度和大動態範圍的相位解調, 避免了使用笨重且昂貴的MIR元件和冷卻光電探測器。 在這裡, 我們提出研究這種基於HC-NCF的混合型MIR-NIR PTI氣體感應器。 我們將專注于對乙烷的檢測, 但該技術可用於檢測在MIR中具有強吸收的許多種其他氣體。 乙烷是呼吸測試中的重要生物標記物,但在NIR沒有很強的吸收線。 我們計畫使用 3.35 微米鐳射器泵浦送充滿氣體的 HC-NCF 和 1.62 微米的全光纖干涉儀來檢測 PT 相位調製。 初步分析表明,應用有1米長的HC-NCF和5 mW的泵浦功率,可實現的頻寬雜訊等效乙烷檢測極限為±25ppb/(Hz)1/2, 動態範圍為6個數量級。 我們將研究相位調製動力學和性能限制因素, 並優化檢測系統, 以實現設想的優良性能。

15220119.label: Realisation of objectives
15220119.value: Objective 1 HC-NCFs (they are now called AR-HCF in most of the literatures), which are capable of transmitting both NIR (1 - 2 micrometers) and MIR (2 to 5 micrometers), are designed and fabricated. AR-HCF gas cells optimized for different applications are designed and fabricated. The three typical configurations of gas cells are: a. Single mode Fabry-Perot gas cell for gas measurement with MIR absorption lines. A piece of AR-HCF is spliced to a NIR silica single mode fiber (SMF) at one end while the opposite end of the AR-HCF is spliced to an MIR InF3 SMF. The AR-HCF has a hollow-core of ~65 micrometers in diameter. Microchannels are fabricated along the AR-HCF, by using femtosecond laser drilling, to speed up the gas exchange. The MIR fiber guides and couples the MIR pump beam into the AR-HCF while the NIR fiber couples the probe beam (1550 nm) into the AR-HCF. The reflected probe beams at the AR-HCF/SMF joints, which interference with each other, are also collected by the NIR fiber and guided to photodetector for further processing. b. Single mode Fabry-Perot gas cell for multi-component gas measurement using both NIR and MIR absorption lines. The basic design is like that described in (a) with the following modifications: the NIR pump beams are combined with the NIR probe beam using WDM and launched into AR-HCF from the NIR fiber from one end. The MIR pump beams are combined and launched into the AR-HCF from the opposite end using the MIR fiber. c. Gas cell based on mode-phase-difference detection. An AR-HCF that can guide two modes, i.e. LP01 and LP11 modes, with approximately equal loss is used as the sensing fiber. The probe beam is coupled into the dual-mode AR-HCF with offset alignment at one end to excite the two modes; at the opposite end of the AR-HCF, both modes are reflected by a dichroic mirror (i.e., reflect the probe and transmit the pump) and reflected beams are coupled back into the NIR SMF to form a reflective dual-mode interferometer to detect the gas-absorption-induced photothermal phase modulation. The pump beams are launched into the AR-HCF via the dichroic mirror from the opposite end. Objective 2 Based on the gas cell design in (1), we conducted theoretical modelling and analysis on the photothermal phase modulation dynamics for the detection of ethane (C2H6) using the absorption line at 3348 nm, methane (CH4) at 3270 nm, carbon dioxide (CO2) at 2004 nm, carbon monoxide (CO) at 4602 nm, and water vapor (H2O) at 1393 nm. With an AR-HCF of hollow-core diameter of ~65 micrometers, for ethane, methane, and water vapor, the dominating factor that affects the frequency response of the photothermal phase modulation is the thermal conduction process of the gas-filled fiber. A smooth response curve with a 3-dB frequency of ~20 kHz is observed. However, for CO and CO2, the frequency response is significantly affected by its long relaxation time. The water molecules work as a relaxation promoter, which lead to different frequency response for different water concentrations. The frequency response of CO at low humidity shows a two-step declining trend, which is dominated by the relaxation time at low frequencies and the thermal conduction time at higher frequencies. With a higher humidity level, the relaxation time reduces significantly, and the frequency response becomes a one-step declining function dominated by the thermal conduction process. For CO2, the frequency response declines a little faster with increasing modulation frequency for lower humidity than for higher humidity. For the Fabry-Perot gas cells used in our investigations, the detection noise is fundamentally limited by the phase noise of the probe laser at low gas concentrations, since the Fabry-Perot is intrinsically an unbalanced interferometer. For the gas cells based on mode-phase-difference detection, the effect of the probe phase noise is minimized, and the probe intensity noise dominates at low gas concentration. At higher gas concentrations, the pump intensity fluctuation and modulation instability start to affect the measurement precisions, for both the Fabry-Perot gas cells and the gas cells based on mode-phase-difference detection. Objective 3 Experimental systems for the detection of CH4, C2H6, CO, CO2 and water vapor using the AR-HCF gas cells were constructed and experimental tested. Experiments were conducted to test the system performance for different gas cell configurations and phase detection approaches as well as different modulation parameters. The experimental results agree with the theoretical modelling and analysis. The performances of the systems for different gases are: Methane detection at 3270.42 nm with a 1.8-m-long gas cell based on mode-phase-difference detection. LOD: 410 ppt with 1 s time constant, 129 ppt with 100 s averaging and 44 ppt with 800 s averaging. Stability: 1.8% over 1 hour. Ethane detection at 3348.15 nm with a 14-cm-long Fabry-Perot gas cell. LOD: 13 ppb with 1 s time constant, 2.6 ppb with 410 s averaging. Stability: 2.2% over 8 hours. Ethane detection at 3348.15 nm with a 10-cm-long Fabry-Perot gas cell with reflected double pass pump. LOD: 3.6 ppb with 1 s time constant, 140 ppt with 1400 s averaging. Stability: 1.7 % over 2 hours. Multi-component (CO at 2004 nm, CO2 at 4602 nm, H2O at 1392 nm) gas detection with a 13-cm-long Fabry-Perot gas cell. LOD: 9 ppb (CO), 25 ppb (CO2), and 2.7 ppm (H2O) for 1 s time constant; 0.6 ppb (CO), 1.5 ppb (CO2) and 222 ppb (H2O) for 1000 s averaging. Stability: 1.7% over 2 hours. The dynamic ranges for CH4, C2H6, CO and CO2 are approximately six orders of magnitude. It was found that the humidity level affects the measurement of carbon monoxide significantly but in a predictable manner, which can be compensated for once the humidity level is measured simultaneously.

15220119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220119.value: Three types of compact AR-HCF gas cells for photothermal interferometry (PTI) spectroscopy with MIR pump and NIR probe are designed, constructed and tested. They are (i) single mode Fabry-Perot gas cell for gas measurement with MIR absorption lines [Optics Express 28(25), 38115-38126 2020], (ii) single mode Fabry-Perot gas cell for multi-component gas measurement using both NIR and MIR absorption lines [Analytical Chemistry 94, 143473-13480, 2021], and (iii) gas cell based on mode-phase-difference detection [9/2022/Alexandria, Virginia, OFS27]. With these gas cells, we have demonstrated all-fiber detection of multiple gases with different pump sources, i.e., CH4 at 3270.42 nm [9/2022/Alexandria, Virginia, OFS27], C2H6 at 3348.15 nm [Optics Express 28(25), 38115-38126, 2020 and 7/2021/Hong Kong, OECC26], and CO at 2004 nm, CO2 at 4602 nm, H2O at 1392 nm [Analytical Chemistry 94, 143473-13480, 2021], and achieved ppb or sub ppb level detection of CH4, C2H6, CO, and CO2 with dynamic range of six orders of magnitude and good stability of a few percent over two hours. These results represent the state-of-the-art optical fiber gas sensors and comparable with the performance of the complex free-space optical gas spectrometers based on multi-pass or resonant cavity gas cells. Simultaneous detection of multiple gas species has been demonstrated with a single AR-HCF gas cell with spectral coverage of all the absorption lines of the gases as well as the probe wavelength [Analytical Chemistry 94, 143473-13480, 2021]. The signal separation was achieved by using frequency division multiplexing. For carbon monoxide detection with PTI spectroscopy, the frequency response is significantly affected by its long relaxation time. The water molecules work as a relaxation promoter, which lead to different frequency response for different humidity levels. This phenomenon may be exploited favorably to improve the sensitivity of CO detection. On the other hand, the varying humidity level may affect the accuracy for carbon monoxide measurement; however, the effect is predictable and can be compensated for if the humidity level is measured simultaneously [Analytical Chemistry 94, 143473-13480, 2021].

15220119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220119.value: HCF based PTI spectroscopy is a novel technique for high precision gas detection. This project has developed AR-HCF gas cells with broadband spectral coverage, which enables the use of multiple MIR pumps to access the strongest absorption lines in the MIR region for enhanced photothermal phase modulation and at the same time a NIR probe for cost-effective and high precision detection of the phase modulation. The technique can achieve similar or better performance as compared with free-space laser gas spectrometers but with smaller instrument size, lighter weight and lower cost. We will seek further funding to develop products for high sensitivity gas sensing.

15220119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220119.value: This project studies a novel hollow-core fiber-based hybrid mid-infrared (MIR) – near infrared (NIR) photothermal interferometry (PTI) spectroscopy technique for gas detection with high sensitivity and large dynamic range. An anti-resonant hollow-core fiber with transmission windows covering both NIR (e.g., 1 to 2 micrometers) and MIR (2 to 5 micrometers) is used as the gas cell, which enables the implementation of PTI gas sensors with a MIR pump and a NIR probe. The use of a MIR pump enables access to the much stronger absorption lines to produce larger photothermal phase modulation, while a NIR fiber-optic interferometer provides a cost-effective means to detect the phase modulation with high sensitivity and large dynamic range, avoiding the use of bulky and costly MIR components and cooled MIR photodetectors. With this technique, we have demonstrated the detection of multiple gas species (i.e., methane, ethane, carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide) with detection limit down to ppb and ppt levels and dynamic range of six orders of magnitude.
