15220519.label: Project Objectives
15220519.value: Analysis of Influencing Factors to Forklift Operator’s Situation Awareness • Approach: Mobile equipment-related accident cases at construction sites will be collected from construction accident investigation reports from different countries, including Hong Kong, the United States and South Korea (e.g., OSHA incident reports). Useful information will be extracted from aggregated data using named entity recognition and relationship extraction methods based on natural language processing techniques. The methods will 1) classify accident cases that are associated with mobile equipment operator SA failures, 2) distinguish types of accidents, and 3) find influencing factors that account for such failures. Design of a Realistic IVR Simulator by Customizing Existing Simulation Software • Approach: A realistic IVR simulator will be designed for assessing forklift operator SA in a complex construction environment. To create convincing IVR, specific requirements for three realism criteria (i.e., behavioral realism, presence, and visual realism) will be analyzed based on the extensive review on literature and accident cases along with construction site observational data. A simulator that meets the realism requirements will be designed, assessed by field experts, and revised until a sufficient level of realism in IVR is achieved. Measurement of Forklift Operator SA to Understand the Impact of SA Influencing Factors through Multifactorial IVR Experiments • Approach: We will recruit more than 20 experienced forklift operators for forklift operation simulations in an IVR simulator. While simulating forklift tasks under different SA factor settings, operator SA levels will be assessed by comparing their knowledge to the SA requirements during simulation freezes. This direct measurement using queries will help understand the impacts of each factor on SA failures.
rows: Analysis of Influencing Factors to Forklift Operator’s Situation Awareness • Approach: Mobile equipment-related accident cases at construction sites will be collected from construction accident investigation reports from different countries, including Hong Kong, the United States and South Korea (e.g., OSHA incident reports). Useful information will be extracted from aggregated data using named entity recognition and relationship extraction methods based on natural language processing techniques. The methods will 1) classify accident cases that are associated with mobile equipment operator SA failures, 2) distinguish types of accidents, and 3) find influencing factors that account for such failures.

Design of a Realistic IVR Simulator by Customizing Existing Simulation Software • Approach: A realistic IVR simulator will be designed for assessing forklift operator SA in a complex construction environment. To create convincing IVR, specific requirements for three realism criteria (i.e., behavioral realism, presence, and visual realism) will be analyzed based on the extensive review on literature and accident cases along with construction site observational data. A simulator that meets the realism requirements will be designed, assessed by field experts, and revised until a sufficient level of realism in IVR is achieved.

Measurement of Forklift Operator SA to Understand the Impact of SA Influencing Factors through Multifactorial IVR Experiments • Approach: We will recruit more than 20 experienced forklift operators for forklift operation simulations in an IVR simulator. While simulating forklift tasks under different SA factor settings, operator SA levels will be assessed by comparing their knowledge to the SA requirements during simulation freezes. This direct measurement using queries will help understand the impacts of each factor on SA failures.

15220519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15220519.value: Fatal accidents on construction sites are highly associated with human errors, including errors made by mobile equipment operators. Often these errors are caused by operators’ poor situation awareness. In order to understand the root causes of such errors, it is essential to understand what operator ‘situation awareness (SA)’ actually is, and thence, how it might be enhanced. This research study will investigate mobile equipment operator SA at construction sites using immersive virtual reality (IVR) presented through a head-mounted display, especially focusing on forklift operations. The specific aims of the research are 1) to analyze influencing factors to forklift operator SA; 2) to design a realistic IVR simulator for forklift operations; and 3) to measure forklift operator SA to understand the impact of SA influencing factors through multifactorial IVR experiments. Specifically, the use of simulated mobile equipment operations in a fully controllable immersive virtual environment will allow us to investigate 1) the operator’s responses to SA influencing factors that are similar to reactions in real-world situations, and 2) the impact of these factors within scenarios that mimic realistic construction equipment operations in risk-free settings. The success of this research will open a new door to revealing the causes of equipment accidents from a cognitive perspective, which has not been fully investigated in the construction domain. In addition, assessing the effects on operator SA by varying the influencing factors could help to identify effective workplace and equipment design interventions, or better operator training strategies that can enhance safety on construction sites. 建築工地上的致命事故與包括移動設備操作員失誤在內的人為錯誤密切相關。通常情況下，操作員薄弱的環境感知意識是由造成人為錯誤主要原因。為了理解此類錯誤的根本發生原因，深刻理解操作員的情景感知意識（SA）的意義，並且如何增強該意識顯得極其重要。這項研究將使用頭戴式顯示器，配合沉浸式虛擬現實（IVR）技術，調查移動設備操作員在建築工地，尤其是操作員在專注操作叉車時的情景感知意識（SA）。具體研究目的包括1）分析叉車操作員SA的影響因子; 2）為叉車操作設計一個實用的IVR模擬器; 3）測量叉車操作員的SA，並且通過多控制變量的IVR實驗理解SA影響因子的影響。具體來說，在完全可控的沉浸式虛擬環境下使用模擬移動設備操作將允許我們調查1）操作員對SA影響因子的反應與現實世界中的反應是否相似，2）在無風險環境中模擬真實建築設備操作的情景中影響因子的變化。此項研究的成果將為從認知角度揭示設備事故的原因打開一扇新的大門，這在建築領域尚未得到充分研究。此外，評估改變影響因子的情況下操作員SA的影響有助於識別有效的工作場所和設備設計干預措施，以及改善操作員培訓策略，以提高施工現場的安全性。

15220519.label: Realisation of objectives
15220519.value: This research project’s objectives include 1) Analysis of Influencing Factors to Forklift Operator’s Situation Awareness, 2) Design of a Realistic IVR Simulator by Customizing Existing Simulation Software, and 3) Measurement of Forklift Operator SA to Understand the Impact of SA Influencing Factors through Multifactorial IVR Experiments. These objectives have been successfully achieved during the project period (100%) as below. 1. Analysis of Influencing Factors to Forklift Operator’s Situation Awareness (SA) In SA research, creating a breakdown structure of tasks and subtasks is essential so that the specific context of SA (e.g., what specific things the operator needs to be aware of in performing a specific task) can be developed for each task. In this regard, a Goal-Directed Task Analysis (GDTA), which is a cognitive task analysis for listing the requirements of operator SA in a breakdown structure, is often used as the first step of SA study. The main focus of a GDTA is identifying an operator’s comprehensive goals that need to be accomplished, the decisions that need to be made to achieve the goals, and information required to make appropriate decisions. In this research, a GDTA was developed based on forklift operation safety guidelines, such as High-Risk Work – A Guide to Forklift Safety, as well as forklift accident reports extracted from the US OSHA accident database (i.e., OSHA Fatality and Catastrophe Investigation Summaries, https://www.osha.gov/pls/imis/accidentsearch.html). Forklift safety guideline documents and the accident case reports provided detailed information regarding the goals and tasks to be achieved by a forklift operator. Among the subgoals identified, the second subgoal, ‘handling loads without any accident’, was focused in this research. This subgoal (i.e., the safe operation of a forklift) is related to three decisions, each of which is related to an accident type, such as hitting, tip-over, and having someone caught in moving parts of the equipment, respectively. This categorization of different types of forklift accidents is based on accident case reports included in the OSHA’s accident database. The authors identified 158 forklift operation-related accident cases by analyzing frequencies of word usage of the term “forklift” in the database. A further investigation on the identified cases revealed that 41 cases (25.94%) among them were directly associated with a SA error by the operator, and the majority of them was of the type that someone was hit by a forklift in motion (63.41%). Further categorization of these accident cases revealed that such collision accidents occurred while the operator was driving straight without any load (36.58%), backing up (31.70%), making a turn (14.63%), driving with load (9.75%), or loading (7.31%). 2. Design of a Realistic IVR Simulator by Customizing Existing Simulation Software When designing simulation-based training such as IVR training, simulator fidelity is one of the most critical design features, as it not only affects learning outcomes but is also associated with the cost effectiveness of the systems. While the definition of fidelity could vary depending on the application, one of the traditional definitions is the extent to which the simulator replicates the actual environment. For the higher transferability of training from a simulated environment to complicated real-world situations, high-fidelity simulators featuring realistic 3D views and interfaces have been preferred. However, the trade-off between realism and abstraction in the context of safety training has not been fully understood, as higher fidelity means an increased cost for developing the IVR system and using more sophisticated IVR devices, which may lower the economic viability of IVR training in practice. From a practical point of view, the goal of the IVR training system design is to identify an appropriate balance between the fidelity of simulation and learning outcomes and find an economically feasible solution to achieve that balance. This study investigated the impact of scenario and interaction fidelity on IVR-based forklift safety training, focusing on presence and usability. Scenario fidelity varied the Level of Development (LOD) in IVR model (high LOD vs. low LOD), while interaction fidelity varied the control interface (steering wheel and pedals vs. keyboard). A 2-by-2 experiment with 120 participants examined high/low scenario and interaction fidelity. Results showed scenario fidelity enhanced presence and usability significantly, while interaction fidelity had no effect. The realism of training scenarios is more influential for presence and immersion than control interface realism. These findings would provide a valuable insight on how to balance IVR simulation fidelity and learning outcomes and help guide the development of cost-efficient IVR-based safety training. 3. Measurement of Forklift Operator SA to Understand the Impact of SA Influencing Factors through Multifactorial IVR Experiments As a next step, a simulation scenario of forklift operation was developed. Based on an interview with a licensed forklift operator, the accident reports and the forklift operation guidelines, four main subtasks of forklift operation for material handling were included in the final scenario: 1) driving forward without a load, 2) driving reverse with a load, 3) making a turn, and 4) lifting a load. Notably, these four subtasks possess different characteristics in terms of task complexity (e.g., driving straight/curved path, forward/backward, and with/without load) and require different levels of mental workload for maintaining a good SA. As mentioned above, the scope was determined to be the forklift operation for material handling, and other types of use of forklifts, such as using a forklift as a lift, were excluded in this research. Using the developed IVR simulation module, this study conducted experimental studies to measure SA using SAGAT during various forklift operational scenarios. The results demonstrate that a forklift operator’s SA is significantly influenced by what task the operator is carrying out at the moment. Specifically, the analysis tells us that a forklift operator will have a reduced SA regarding the workers around when he/she is performing a loading or unloading task. This implies that the operators’ attention may be narrowed when he/she performs a loading or unloading. In the RTA session, those subjects who failed to maintain a good SA during these tasks reported that they did not see a worker approaching the forklift because they were focusing on carrying out the task accurately. In other words, the subjects were experiencing a higher mental workload due to the complexity of the task. This kind of attention narrowing when performing a complex task and the resulting reduction of situation awareness has been reported in the various contexts of high-risk machine operation. However measuring SA is challenging due to the limitation of existing SA measurement methods such as SAGAT as it relies on subjective surveys while randomly freezing the VR scene. To overcome this issue, this study additionally investigated the potential of using physiological data including eye tracking as a means of objective SA measurement. The experimental study has found that eye tracking data is significantly associated with SA, and in particular, it can be used to differentiate Level 1 and Level 2/3 SA.

15220519.label: Major findings and research outcome
15220519.value: The major findings from this study is that 1) VR-based investigation is feasible to understand the influencing factors on situational awareness during forklift operations (Choi et al., 2020), 2) Fidelify and usability are significant factors that can facilitate behavioral change through VR-based safety training (Abbas et al. 2023), 3) Scenario fidelity of VR simulation is one of the most important variables to improve the effectiveness of VR-based forklift safety training (Luo et al. 2023), and 4) Eye tracking data (e.g., purple diameters, fixations etc.) has great potential as indicators of situational awareness (Luo et al. 2024). 15220519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15220519.value: Although eye movement data provide rich information about the subject’s attention and cognitive workloads, the information is still only an indirect indication of such brain activities. Distinguishing Levels 2 and 3 SA possibly requires the integration of supplementary physiological data associated with cognitive activity in addition to eye movement data. Brain imaging technology such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) might be considered in future research to help distinguish Level 2 and 3 SA. Also, the VR environment used in this study was static, unlike actual construction work environments. Such a static VR environment would not be an ideal reflection of reality because a construction site is always dynamic and complex, and future research should consider how to capture eye movement characteristics in a more dynamic VR environment and how to use such data for understanding SA characteristics in the context of hazard identification.

15220519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15220519.value: As many accidents involved with forklifts can be attributed to a low situation awareness (SA), it is essential to understand the factors that can influence forklift operators’ SA for reducing forklift accidents, especially, collision accidents. This research aims to investigate how forklift operators’ SA can be influenced by the type of subtasks they are carrying out at the moment. In this research, a virtual reality (VR) environment is used as the experiment environment, in which a subject performs a series of subtasks, such as driving, turning, reversing, loading and unloading, with a VR forklift simulation model. A SAGAT is used as the main method to collect data about forklift operators’ SA in various situations. The results show a forklift operator is likely to have a reduced SA regarding the workers around when he/she is performing a loading or unloading task due to attention narrowing, which can easily occur when the person concentrates on a cognitively demanding task. The findings provide insights into how forklift operator SA may be improved through SA-oriented safety training programs or how sensing technologies may assist forklift operators to maintain good SA.

15221119.label: Project Objectives
15221119.value: To design and theoretically investigate submillimeter-scale fiber-top optomechanical resonators for PAS sensors. We will theoretically investigate the light-heat-mechanics multiphysical interactions and unveil dynamic behaviors of submillimeter-scale fiber-top optomechanical resonators for PAS sensors. Complex folded-beam structures will be devised to overcome the stringent size limitation (on deflection amplitude and operation frequency) imposed by the small area of fiber end-faces. Numerical simulations will be carried out to solve the Helmhotz wave equation with boundary conditions to reveal the joint influence of the induced thermal and acoustic waves on the excitation and resonance operation of resonators. The geometry of optomechanical resonators as well as the modulation frequency and the relative position of the excitation laser beam will be optimized to achieve both highest Q-factor and minimal noise level and thereby enhance the detection limit under low-power excitation. To develop in situ 3D μ-printing technology for fabrication of complex and robust fiber-top stereostructures. We will further develop the in-house 3D μ-printing platform to pursue higher resolution and more complex 3D geometry so as to enable in situ printing of sophisticated optical fiber-top optomechanical microsystem. Spatial light modulator and projection optics will be upgraded to enhance the optical resolution of the optical engine. Micro-heating components will be renovated with a dual-light-source optical engine to improve the in-situ processing capability. Moreover, computation lithography algorithms will be incorporated to correct proximity effects. Silica nanoparticles/SU-8 epoxy nanocomposite will be used to directly print 3D fiber-top microstructures. Effects of nanoparticle size and content as well as fabrication conditions will be comprehensively optimized to improve the elasticity and fatigue strength of SU-8 nanocomposite so as to fabricate robust fiber-top microstructures and devices. To develop ultracompact low-power PAS gas sensor system and demonstrate for acetylene detection. With the improved optical 3D μ-printing platform, we will fabricate optical fiber-tip PAS gas sensors and demonstrate their application on acetylene gas detection. Upon the end-face of a multicore optical fiber, a high-transparency polymer-based micro-prism reflector and an on-plane folded micro-beam resonator will be directly printed to fabricate a PAS microsystem. A photoacoustic spectrometer system based on wavelength modulation spectroscopy will be established to demodulate the signal at a specific second-harmonic frequency. Experimental results will be compared with theoretical analysis to reveal the correlation between the laser’s excitation wavelength and modulation frequency, resonator’s resonance frequency and Q-factor, and sensor’s detection sensitivity. Both of the geometric parameter and signal demodulation scheme will be optimized to reduce operation power and enhance operation stability and detection limit. The ultimate goal of this project is to create a new pathway to rapidly in situ print robust 3D optomechanical resonators on optical fiber end-faces and thereby develop ultracompact high-sensitivity low-power PAS gas sensors, whose detection limit can reach around 100 part-per-billion of C2H2 at the excitation power of less than 10 mW (Class 1 for infrared lasers).

15221119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221119.value: This project aims to investigate the light-heat-mechanics multiphysical interactions of submillimeter-scale photoacoustically excited optomechanical resonators on optical fiber end-faces and thereby develop miniaturized photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) sensors for trace-gas detection in space-constrained circumstances. Because of its high sensitivity, good selectivity and quick responsivity, PAS technology has been widely used for gas detection in biomedical diagnostics, production control and pollution monitoring. In conventional PAS sensors, the acoustic signal induced by the absorption of modulated light was intensified by a gas cell-based acoustic resonator before detected by microphone. Thereafter, an improved version, called quartz-enhanced PAS (QEPAS), using a quartz tuning fork as the resonant acoustic transducer for accumulation of acoustic energy, was gradually developed to the most representative PAS technology. QEPAS sensors exhibit excellent performance on detection of various gases. However, their inherent drawbacks, such as bulky size (~10 mm) and inapplicability for long-distance monitoring, restrict wider application. Those obstacles may be overcome by optical fiber technologies, which have merits of small size, electromagnetic interference immunity and long-distance signal-transmission ability. However, the tiny size and large aspect-ratio of optical fibers make it challenging to fabricate subtle microstructures on fiber end-faces to develop small PAS sensors. Recently, we developed an optical 3D μ-printing technology for direct printing of optical fiber-top microstructures and sensors, e.g. fiber-tip air-cavity pressure sensors and gas-adsorption polymer-based CO2 gas sensors. Although these sensors are not very complicated in term of geometry, the printing technology exhibited great promise for fabrication of complex innovative fiber-top microdevices. In this project, we aim to develop ultracompact high-sensitivity low-power PAS gas sensors through the design and fabrication of fiber-top optomechanical resonators together with the further development of optical 3D μ-printing technology towards higher resolution and more flexible processing ability. Complex folded-beam resonators will be devised to overcome the small-size imposed limitations on deflection amplitude and resonance frequency for performance enhancement. Thanks to the resonance amplification mechanism as well as low weight and high operation frequency, such PAS gas sensors may have not only reduced operation power but also lower detection limit, in virtue of lower ambient acoustic noise at higher frequency. The successful implementation of the project will create a new generation of PAS gas sensors evolving from millimeter/centimeter to submillimeter scale for various gas-sensing-based intelligent applications. Moreover, the advancement of the proposed optical fiber-top microengineering technologies and devices may drive revolutions in many scientific areas such as cavity optomechanics and “lab-on-fiber”. 本項目旨在研究亞毫米尺度光聲激勵光纖端面光機諧振器及其光-熱-機械多物理機制相互作用，從而發展可用於微小空間裡進行痕量氣體檢測的微型光聲光譜(PAS)傳感器。 由於其靈敏度高、選擇性好及響應速度快等優點，PAS技術已廣泛用於生物醫學診斷、生產過程控制和污染監測等領域進行氣體檢測。在傳統的PAS傳感器中，由於吸收特定頻率調製光而產生的聲信號，在被傳聲器檢測之前通常用基於氣室的聲諧振器進行增強。 後來，使用石英音叉作為聲能積累諧振聲換能器的改進版本，即石英增強型PAS(QEPAS)，逐漸發展成最具代表性的PAS技術。 QEPAS傳感器在檢測許多氣體中表現出了優異的性能。然而，它具有一些固有的缺點，比如尺寸較大(約10毫米)、不適用於長距離監測等，從而限制了其更廣泛的應用。因為具有體積小、抗電磁干擾能力強、遠距離信號傳輸能力強等優點，光纖技術有望克服這些缺點。然而，光纖的小尺寸和大縱橫比使得光纖端面上精巧微結構的製備變得困難，從而使得小型光纖PAS傳感器的發展極具挑戰性。 最近，我們研究小組開發了一種光學3D微打印技術，可用於直接打印光纖端面微結構和傳感器，如光纖端面氣腔壓力傳感器、基於氣體吸附聚合物的CO2氣體傳感器等。 儘管這些傳感器的幾何形狀並不算非常複雜，但該獨特的光學微打印技術在製造創新光纖端面微器件方面表現出了很大的潛力。 在本項目中，我們擬進一步發展光學3D微打印技術，實現更高的分辨率和更靈活的加工能力，從而進行光纖端面光機諧振器的設計和製造，研製超緊湊的高靈敏度低功率PAS氣體傳感器。我們將設計複雜折疊梁結構諧振器，克服小尺寸對撓曲幅度和諧振頻率的限制，從而提高其性能。鑒於其共振放大機制、低重量與高工作頻率，以及較高頻率下環境噪聲較低，該PAS氣體傳感器不僅可降低操作功率還有望降低檢測限。 本項目的成功實施將研製出尺寸從毫米/釐米減小至亞毫米級的新一代PAS氣體傳感器，推動各種基於氣體傳感的智慧應用。此外，項目所發展的光纖端面微納工程化技術與器件，有望推動許多科學技術的革新與發展，例如諧振腔光機械系統和「光纖實驗室」等。

15221119.label: Realisation of objectives
15221119.value: This project proposed to investigate submillimeter-scale optomechanical resonators and develop optical 3D micro-printing technology to fabricate optical fiber photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) sensors for trace-gas detection. In the past several years, many remarkable research results in line with the project objects have been achieved: 1. To design and theoretically investigate submillimeter-scale fiber-top optomechanical resonators for PAS sensors. We have systematically investigated submillimeter optomechanical resonators (OMRs) and developed a fiber-top spirally-suspended OMRs for PAS gas sensors. Spiral microbeams are devised to overcome the small deflection amplitude imposed by the small size of OMRs via increasing the effective length of microbeams supporting microdisk that forms a Fabry-Perot cavity with the end-face of optical fiber. It can enhance the sensitivity of the acoustic sensor typically restricted by the short supporting microbeam (or cantilever) in miniaturized sensors. Moreover, we have demonstrated that the design can enable tailoring the vibration resonances of an OMR to make its resonance frequency matching with the frequency of acoustic wave generated by the absorption of pump laser for resonance-enhanced signal amplification. Finite element analysis using commercial software (COMSOL Multiphysics) has been conducted to simulate the multiphysical interactions of OMRs. With the geometric and mechanical properties (that was selected to fabricate the designed OMRs, i.e., SU-8 epoxy), the dynamic responses of the designed fiber-top OMRs have been systematically studied. Simulation results revealed that a fiber-top OMR with 198-μm long microbeams has a resonance frequency at 126 KHz and the quality factor of the resonance peak is 20.7. Compared with the sensitivity of the OMR working at a frequency far away from the resonant frequency, the OMR’s sensitivity to acoustic pressure can be greatly enhanced by 40.1 times when the frequency of acoustic wave matches with the OMR’s resonance frequency. To further increase the OMR’s design flexibility and signal enhancement ability, we have designed an optical fiber ferrule-top OMR for PAS sensors. The use of fiber-optic ferrule can provide a relatively larger area to tailor the vibration modes of OMRs. Particularly, we demonstrated an optical fiber ferrule-top OMR whose outer diameter is 400 μm. Numerical simulations revealed that such a ferrule-top OMR can increase the resonance-based signal amplification by over two orders of magnitude. 2. To develop in situ 3D μ-printing technology for fabrication of complex and robust fiber-top stereostructures. We have independently developed an in-situ 3D micro-printing platform to fabricate complex and robust fiber-top stereostructures. With a digital micromirror device (DMD), the system can manipulate about a million light pixels to generate dynamic optical patterns of UV light for optical microfabrication. Micro-heating element has been integrated to improve the in-situ printing ability, and computational algorithms have been developed to pretreat image data to correct proximity effects for high-resolution printing. In the experiments, SU-8 epoxy was diluted by cyclopentanone with the concentration of 15 ~20 % in weight ratio. Tributylamine was mixed into the SU-8 solution as an inhibitor. 2-(2H-Benzotriazol-2-yl)-4,6-bis (1-methyl-1-phenylethyl)phenol, also known as Tinuvin 234, was added into the solutions as an UV absorption agent to enhance the vertical discernibility of the optical 3D μ-printing process. Uniform thin layers of SU-8 were deposited upon the cleaved end face of a single-mode optical fiber (SMOF) by using either spray coating or dip coating processes. After coating each layer of SU-8, the solvent was evaporated by a pre-bake process. Thereafter, with the assistance of the digital camera-based machine vision technology, the sample was automatically moved to the pre-aligned position for optical exposure process. The image data sliced from the 3D model of the designed structure was used to dynamically generate UV patterns to optically pattern the SU-8 film on the end-faces of optical fiber or fiber-optic ferrule. Such a fully own-developed optical 3D micro-printing system provides a foundation for systematical experimental study of complex and robust OMRs for PAS gas sensors. Moreover, our research demonstrated that such an optical 3D micro-printing system can also be used to fabricate many kinds of photonic sensors and devices, such as suspended-disk whispering-gallery mode resonators and polymer optical waveguide devices. 3. To develop ultracompact low-power PAS gas sensor system and demonstrate their application in acetylene detection. With the improved optical 3D micro-printing platform, we have successfully fabricated optical fiber optomechanical resonant PAS (OMR-PAS) gas sensors to detect the concentration of acetylene (C2H2) gas. Using the optimized optical fiber OMR sensors, we have built PAS gas sensor system based on wavelength modulation spectroscopy to test the performance of the optical fiber OMR-PAS gas sensor. A non-resonant PA cell was used to minimize gas sample consumption and confine the generated acoustic signal. The detection limit of the gas system is tested by filling N2-balanced 1001-ppm C2H2 into the gas chamber. The pump wavelength was scanned across the P(13) line of C2H2 at different input pump power levels. With a lock-in-amplifier, the peak-to-peak value of the 2f signal (PA signal) against the input pump power level was measured. The minimum NEC of the fabricated ferrule-top FPI microresonator for C2H2 gas detection was assessed by using an Allan-Werle deviation analysis. When the integration time is 68 s, the NEC goes down to 179 ppb C2H2, which corresponds to a NEA of 1.88×10^-7 cm^-1. The NEC is 357 ppb C2H2 for 10-s integration time. Remarkably, the optical fiber OMR-PAS gas sensor revealed a very fast response in the detection of C2H2 gas. In the experiments, pure N2, 1001 ppm C2H2 in N2, and then pure N2 were sequentially filled into the gas chamber with at a flow rate of 250 standard cm³/min (SCCM) while the pump wavelength is fixed to the center of P(13) absorption line of C2H2. The measured response time, specifically the time required for the response reaching 90% (i.e., rise time) and descending to 10% (i.e., fall time) of the maximum 2f signal, is around 0.1 seconds. Moreover, we have developed another kind of miniature optical fiber sensor, i.e., optical fiber-tip 3D-microprinted photothermal interferometric sensor, for detection of C2H2 gas. Our experimental results revealed that it can detect C2H2 gas at a noise equivalent concentration of 160 ppb leven and its response time is about 0.5 seconds. 4. To create a new pathway to rapidly in situ print robust 3D optomechanical resonators on optical fiber end-faces and thereby develop ultracompact high-sensitivity low-power PAS gas sensors. We have successfully developed an in-situ 3D micro-printing platform to fabricate complex and robust optomechanical resonators on the end-faces of optical fiber or fiber-optic ferrule for PAS gas sensors. Our study has demonstrated that such optomechanical resonators can provide a new pathway to develop ultracompact high-sensitivity PAS sensors. The fabricated optical fiber OMR-PAS gas sensors can detect C2H2 at a noise equivalent concentration of 179 ppb, and its response time is extremely fast at 100-ms level. Such a small-size fast-response optical fiber gas sensor provides a new trace-gas detection technology for various applications such as environmental monitoring, industrial process control, and medical diagnostics.

15221119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221119.value: This project proposed to investigate submillimeter-scale optomechanical resonators and develop optical 3D micro-printing technology to fabricate miniature optical fiber photoacoustic spectroscopy (PAS) sensors for trace-gas detection. Major findings and research outcomes of the project include: i. A new type of optomechanical resonator, called optical fiber-top spirally-suspended optomechanical microresonator, has been developed for acoustic sensing. It can tackle the trade-off between small size and high sensitivity to develop small-size high-sensitivity optical fiber-tip acoustic sensors. It has not only a miniaturization-induced broad bandwidth but also a resonance-enhanced ultrahigh sensitivity and thus is very promising in various acoustic wave-based sensing, imaging, and testing applications (See the paper published in Optics Letters, 2020). ii. An optical 3D micro-printing system has been independently developed. It provides a technological foundation for experimental study of optomechanical micro-resonators-based optical fiber gas sensors. It has also been extended to fabricate many kinds of photonic sensors and devices, such as high-Q optical whispering-gallery-mode microresonators and polymer optical waveguide devices (see the papers published in Lab on a Chip, 2022, and Journal of Lightwave Technology 2022). iii. Using our own-developed 3D micro-printing technology, we have developed a miniature 3D micro-printed optical fiber optomechanical acoustic sensor for PAS gas sensing. A spirally suspended micromirror is directly 3D micro-printed on the end-face of a fiber-optic ferrule to form a miniature Fabry-Pérot interferometric (FPI) acoustic sensor. It can be utilized as an optomechanical resonant PAS gas sensor to detect the concentration of C2H2 gas at 179-ppb level and its response to gas concentration change can be very fast at 100-ms level. It provides a new trace-gas detection technology for a variety of emerging applications ranging from biomedical diagnostics to in-reactor process monitoring. (See the attached paper on review, 2024). iv. Using our own-developed 3D micro-printing technology, we have also developed an ultraminiature optical fiber-tip photothermal gas sensor for C2H2 gas detection. A low-finesse FP microcavity with the length of 66 μm, which not only acts as an open gas micro-chamber but also enables interferometric interrogation of gas sensing signal, was directly 3D micro-printed on the optical fiber end-face. The optical fiber-tip sensor can detect C2H2 gas at the concentration down to 160 ppb level and its response time is about 0.5 s. (See the paper published in Laser & Photonics Reviews, 2024). In short, we have developed a 3D micro-printing technology and then systematically investigated submillimeter-scale optomechanical resonators for development of small-size high-performance optical fiber sensors for trace-gas detection. It provides new technology for various applications such as environmental monitoring, industrial process control, and medical diagnostics.

15221119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221119.value: We will continue to develop high-precision optical 3D micro-printing technology to pursue higher resolution and fast processing speed. It might be used to fabricate many kinds of photonic sensors and devices, such as high-Q WGM microcavities and optical waveguide devices. The research on optical fiber gas sensors will also be continued to further improve their performances for practical applications in e.g., environmental monitoring, industrial process control, and medical diagnostics. Moreover, we will design and investigate different optomechanical resonators to develop new kinds of optical fiber sensors for different applications, such as optical fiber resonant accelerometers that have potential to overcome the shortages of electronic accelerometers to meet the demands of high-requirement applications.

15221119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221119.value: This project aims to investigate submillimeter-scale optomechanical resonators and develop optical 3D micro-printing technology to fabricate miniature optical fiber photoacoustic spectroscopy sensors for trace-gas detection. In the project, we have successfully developed an optical 3D micro-printing technology to microengineer optomechanical resonators at submillimeter scale. A new optomechanical resonator, i.e., spirally-suspended optomechanical microresonator, has been developed and demonstrated in experiments. It can tackle the trade-off between small size and high sensitivity to develop ultraminiature high-performance optical fiber-tip acoustic/photoacoustic sensors. One of the promising applications of such optomechanical resonators is to develop miniature optical fiber gas sensors. In the project, we have developed a miniature 3D micro-printed optical fiber optomechanical acoustic sensor based on such a spirally-suspended optomechanical resonator. It has been demonstrated to detect the concentration of acetylene gas at 179-ppb level, and its response to gas concentration change can be as fast as 0.1-seconds level. By innovation of optical 3D micro-printing technology, optical fiber may be able to unleash its full potential on the development of gas sensors. Such small-size fast-response optical fiber gas sensors provide a new technology to remotely detect trace gases for a myriad of applications such as environmental monitoring, industrial process control, and medical diagnostics.

15221619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221619.value: One of the key logistics activities for many companies is to reposition valuable items, called “assets”, by picking them up from locations having a surplus, and delivering them to locations with a deficit. For example, for companies that operate shared bike systems, bikes are assets that need to be transported by trucks for rebalancing among various city locations. In asset repositioning, therefore, companies face very challenging problems of how to transport assets by vehicles from pickup points to delivery points with the total travel cost minimized. Due to limited capacities, vehicles often have to visit pickup and delivery points multiple times, and loads for transport also have to be split. These problems are known as pickup and delivery vehicle routing problems with split loads. Compared to classic vehicle routing problems, where each pickup or delivery point can only be visited once, and loads for transport cannot be split, pickup and delivery vehicle routing problems with split loads are much more challenging. Their existing algorithms are restricted, and can only produce optimal solutions for certain small-sized instances, thus lagging far behind the algorithms for classic vehicle routing problems. Their existing lower bounds on costs of the optimal solutions are mainly based on relaxations with a large number of decision variables, which can hardly be used for algorithm design and evaluations when solving median and large-sized instances. In this research, we aim to develop new solution methods for pickup and delivery vehicle routing problems with split loads. We plan to derive new relaxations that can not only provide lower bounds near the optimal solutions but are also easy to compute, as well as to develop algorithms that can efficiently generate optimal solutions for small and median-sized instances, and near-optimal solutions for large-sized instances. The best algorithms will be translated into a computer tool that can be validated by our industrial partners to identify how asset repositioning practices can be further improved. The outcome of the project is promising, as our new idea has already been proved feasible in a preliminary study, from which we have obtained a much improved lower bound based on a novel large-scale integer programming model. The project’s success will significantly enrich the literature on vehicle routing problems, as well as enhance the theory and applications of integer programming, leading to further related interesting topics and useful results.

15221619.label: Realisation of objectives
15221619.value: In this project, we have investigated the following three pickup and delivery vehicle routing problems (PDVRP), resulting in three papers [1,2,3], with two published in INFORMS Journal on Computing, and one under minor revision for Operations Research. - Multiple Depot Split Delivery Vehicle Routing Problem (MDSDVRP) [1]: which is a PDVRP with one commodity type and is widely faced in applications of inventory repositioning; - Multi-trip Pickup and Delivery Vehicle Routing Problem with Split Loads (SPDVRP) [2]: which is a general PDVRP with vehicles allowed to travel multiple trips from depots, and is widely faced by service providers of courier express; - Liner Shipping Network Design Problem (LSNDP) [3]: which is a PDVRP with addition decisions on vehicle (vessel) deployments and constraints on frequency requirements, and is widely faced in applications of liner shipping. As illustrated below, ALL the four objectives of this project have been achieved for these three problems. Objective 1: For various pickup and delivery vehicle routing problems with split loads, derive new relaxations that can imply lower bounds close to the optimum and easy to compute About Achievements: - Problem MDSDVRP: For this problem, we derive a new relaxation, named k-depot constrained cycle sequence problem. To this relaxation, a feasible solution is only a cycle sequence not necessarily consisting of exact m cycles (where m is the number of vehicles), but containing all the customers, with each cycle having one and only one depot. It satisfies a constraint imposed on the connected components of the graph defined by vertices and edges of the cycle sequence. - Problem SPDVRP: For this problem, we present a new set-partitioning-like formulation, which is a pattern-based formulation. Here, a pattern represents the total amount of the product picked up from or delivered to a customer on a given route. This formulation leads to a new linear programming relaxation of the problem. - Problem LSNDP: For this problem, we present a new set-partitioning-like formulation, featuring an exponential number of variables and constraints. The formulation considers decisions on general rotation configurations of various service components, including but not limited to the ship type, sailing speed, and service frequency. This formulation leads to a new linear programming relaxation of the problem. As explained in our achievements for Objectives 2 and 4, all these new relaxations can be solved efficiently and provide close-to-optimal lower bounds. Objective 2: For various pickup and delivery vehicle routing problems with split loads, develop efficient algorithms to compute the new lower bounds About Achievements: - Problem MDSDVRP: For the new relaxation of this problem, i.e., k-depot constrained cycle sequence problem, we develop a polynomial time approximation algorithm. It first computes a minimum constrained spanning forest of the given graph, and then iteratively generates a new spanning forest by replacing one existing edge with a new one. For each spanning forest obtained, the algorithm transforms it to a feasible solution to the relaxation problem. Among all the relaxation solutions, the one with the smallest total cost is returned. We have proved that this approximation algorithm for the relaxation problem achieves an approximation ratio of 5/2. - Problem SPDVRP: To solve the new relaxation of this problem, which is a linear program with an exponential number of columns (or variables), we develop a column-generation algorithm. The critical step of this algorithm is to solve the pricing problem, for which we develop an efficient bi-directional label-setting algorithm. The novelty of this label-setting algorithm is to propose and apply a set-based dominance rule. Compared with the classic point-based dominance rule, such a set-based dominance rule is significantly more effective in reducing the number of labels generated, improving the efficiency of the label-setting algorithm significantly. - Problem LSNDP: To address transshipment costs of the problem correctly, the proposed new formulation is associated with exponentially many rotation-dependent variables and constraints, with the result that even solving the linear programming relaxation is a big challenge. To solve this linear programming relaxation, we propose a new simultaneous column-and-row generation solution method together with some novel speed-up techniques. Objective 3: For various pickup and delivery vehicle routing problems with split loads, develop efficient exact and heuristic algorithms based on the new lower bounds About Achievements: - Problem MDSDVRP: Based on the new relaxation, we develop a new approximation algorithm for the MDSDVRP. For each feasible relaxation solution, the algorithm applies a cycle splitting procedure and a vehicle assignment procedure to transform it to a feasible solution to the MDSDVRP. We prove that this algorithm ensures an approximation ratio of 6. - Problem SPDVRP: For the SPDVRP, we develop a new a branch-price-and-cut exact algorithm based on the new pattern-based mathematical formulation and its linear programming relaxation. The exact algorithm involves four types of branching rules adapted for the SPDVRP, together with a best-first strategy to decide the node-selection rule. - Problem LSNDP: We embed the newly proposed simultaneous column-and-row generation solution method within a branch-and-price algorithm to develop a new exact method for the LSND. To further speed up the computation at each node of the enumeration tree of the exact algorithm, we occasionally allow a premature termination for solving the relaxation problem and based on the relaxation solution obtained at the premature termination, we can compute a valid upper bound for the problem. Objective 4: Evaluate the quality and performance of the new lower bounds and algorithms using theoretical and computational analyses About Achievements: - Problem MDSDVRP: We have conducted extensive experiments to compare the computational experiments of our newly proposed approximation algorithm for problem MDSDVRP and three other benchmark algorithms, including two exact methods and one standard heuristic. The results demonstrate that our approximation algorithm significantly outperforms these benchmark algorithms, achieving improvements in objective values by more than 10\% on average. - Problem SPDVRP: We have extensive computational experiments on different classes of benchmark instances of problem SPDVRP. The results illustrate that the newly proposed exact algorithm solves several open SPDVRP instances and significantly improves the running times of state-of-the-art algorithms. - Problem LSNDP: We test our newly developed exact algorithm for the LSNDP on two main problem variants based on different rotation configurations. Results from computational experiments based on benchmark instances validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the newly proposed solution method. This exact method solves to optimality, for the first time, some difficult benchmark instances with transshipment costs (of up to 12 ports), and significantly improves the solutions provided by existing exact and heuristic methods for some other benchmark instances (of up to 20 ports). Luo, R. Baldacci, H. Qin, and Z. Xu. A new exact algorithm for single-commodity vehicle routing with split pickups and deliveries. INFORMS Journal on Computing, 35(1):31–49, 2023. [3] J. Xia, Z. 15221619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221619.value: In this project we have investigated three pick-up and delivery vehicle routing problems with split loads. (1) The first study is on the multiple-depot split delivery problem (MDSDP). It aims to serve customers’ demands using a fleet of capacitated vehicles located in multiple depots, such that the total travel cost of the vehicles is minimized. This is a challenging problem with broad applications in the logistics industry, for which no constant ratio approximation algorithm is known. In our study, we find the first polynomial time approximation algorithm that can ensure a constant approximation ratio for the MDSDP. To achieve this, we propose a novel solution framework based on a new relaxation of the problem, a cycle splitting procedure, and a vehicle assignment procedure. The new algorithm has demonstrated a significantly better computational performance than some benchmark solution algorithms. (2) The second study is on the Multi-trip Pickup and Delivery Vehicle Routing Problem with Split Loads (SPDVRP). In the SPDVRP, any amount of a product collected from a pickup customer can be supplied to any delivery customer, and the demand of each customer can be collected or delivered multiple times by the same or different vehicles. This problem arises regularly in inventory and routing rebalancing applications, such as in bike sharing systems. In this study, we develop a new branch-price-and-cut algorithm based on a novel pattern-based mathematical formulation and its linear programming relaxation. The new exact algorithm significantly solves several open SPDVRP instances and significantly improves the running times of state-of-the-art algorithms. (3) The third study is on a liner service network design problem (LSNDP), which is a vehicle routing problem in ocean shipping. It aims at creating a set of regular services or rotations of oceangoing ships (vehicles) to transport containerized cargo among seaports. Existing literature has shown that finding an optimal solution for the LSNDP is particularly challenging, even for small-scale problems, because of the complex rotation structure and the joint decision-making on rotation design, fleet deployment, cargo routing, etc. In this study, we develop a new branch-and-price exact algorithm for the LSNDP. It is based on a novel simultaneous column-and-row generation method for solving a relaxation of the problem. Results from computational experiments validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the newly proposed solution method. Our work not only enriches the solution methods for the LSND but also enhances the SCRG and vehicle routing solution method in general.

15221619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221619.value: The project has laid a solid foundation for future research towards several promising directions as explained below: (1) For the study on MDSDP, our newly proposed solution framework can be applied to developing approximation algorithms for several other variants of the problem. It is also of great interest to develop exact and heuristic algorithms to achieve better efficiency and solution qualities for the MDSDP based on our new approximation algorithms. (2) For the study on SPDVRP, the optimization techniques proposed, such as the set-based dominance rules, can be applied to enhance exact algorithms for other vehicle routing problems. Furthermore, the relaxation model of the pattern-based formulation of the problem can further be improved by introducing some valid inequalities. (3) For the study on LSNDP, we can further improve the SCRG-based method by enhancing the approaches to solving the pricing problem. The proposed SCRG-based solution method can also be adapted to incorporate additional rotation constraints arising in real-world situations. Moreover, our newly developed optimization techniques, such as the post-pricing method, can also be adapted to solving other optimization problems.

15221619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221619.value: One of the key logistics activities is to reposition valuable items, called “assets”, by picking them up from locations having a surplus, and delivering them to locations with a deficit. For example, for companies that operate shared bike systems, bikes are assets that need to be transported by trucks for rebalancing among various city locations. In asset repositioning, companies face very challenging problems of how to transport assets by vehicles from pickup points to delivery points with the total travel cost minimized. These problems are known as pickup and delivery vehicle routing problems with split loads, which, compared to classic vehicle routing problems, are much more challenging. In this project, we develop new solution methods for variants of the pickup and delivery vehicle routing problem with split loads arising in three applications. For each variant, we derive new relaxations that can not only provide lower bounds near the optimal solutions but are easy to compute. Based on these relaxations, we develop new exact or approximation algorithms that can efficiently generate optimal or near-optimal solutions. The success of the project has significantly enriched the vehicle routing literature, as well as enhance the theory and applications of integer programming.

15221719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221719.value: Sustainable energy utilization needs the effective energy storage system. The electrification of transportation also demands batteries with high energy density, long service life and good safety. For one material to fulfill the three requests is almost impossible. However, composite materials may hold the answers for such questions. For example, nickel-rich layered metal oxide cathode materials show the potential of high energy density. Its service life is relatively short and it is not yet safe. Coating a thin layer of polymer was shown to enhance the performance of such cathode materials. Conformal coating of conductive polymers was confirmed in the researchers' lab to improve the performance of service life, safety and also power delivery. In this project, the investigators propose to coat a thin conformal layer of elastomeric conductive polymer with good ionic conductivity. This could be done using chemical vapor deposition method which is a green in nature and easy in operation. The conductive polymers will be PEDOT, PANi. The polymer with good ionic conductivity would be PEG. The elasticity will be provided by PB, the synthetic rubber. PVI may be able to provide elasticity and ion conductivity judged from its similar structure to that of PEG. The coated cathode materials will be tested for their physical, chemical and electrochemical properties. Their morphology, surface composition, electron/ion conductivity, elasticity on the performance of battery cells will be investigated in-depth. State-of-the-art instruments such as, In-situ HEXRD, HRTEM, SEM, XPS, FTIR, TGA/DSC, ICP-MS, DMA, would be employed to reveal the information behind the expected significant improvement of the performance of the cathodes by conformal coating of elastomeric conducting polymers with ionic conductivity. The success of the project will make a significant impact on the battery communities in Hong Kong, China and the world. 可持續能源的利用需要有效的能源儲存系統。 交通的電氣化也要求動力電池具有高能量密度、長使用壽命以及良好的安全性。 期望一種材料來滿足這三項要求幾乎是不可能的。 然而,複合材料可能具有解決這些問題的答案。 例如,富鎳層狀金屬氧化物具有高能量密度的潛質,雖然它的使用壽命相對短,同時使用該材料尚未安全。 包覆一薄層聚合物業已證明可以提高此類正極材料的特性。 本專案研究者們的實驗室已經確認保形包覆導電聚合物可以改善正極材料的使用壽命,安全性和動力傳送。 本專案的研究者們提議包覆一薄層擁有較好的離子傳輸功能的彈性導電聚合物。 包覆過程將採用容易操作且本證綠色的化學蒸氣沉降法。 導電聚合物為PEDOT, PANi. 具有較好的離子傳輸能力的聚合物為PEG. 彈性性能將由合成橡膠PB提供。 從它與PEG的相似結構判斷,PVI有可能同時具有彈性以及離子傳輸能力。 我們會研究包覆的正極材料之物理、化學、電化學特性。 我們將深入研究它們的形貌、表面化學成分、電子/離子導率、彈性對電池表現的影響。 預計包覆過的正極材料之表現會有重要改善。 我們會利用現代化設備諸如 線上 HEXRD, HRTEM, SEM, XPS, FTIR, TGA/DSC, ICP-MS, DMA, 來揭示其機理。 本專案的成功將會對香港、中國甚至世界的電池領域產生重要影響。

15221719.label: Realisation of objectives
15221719.value: All four objectives have been successfully achieved, as evidenced partially in the attached publication and other findings presented in the paper draft. 1. A significant accomplishment is the successful preparation of conformal coatings of elastomeric conducting polymers with high ionic conductivity, namely PV4D4-PPy and PV4D4-PBA. Our results demonstrate that the combination of elasticity from PBA and PV4D4, along with the conductivity of PPY, synergistically enhances the stability of the cathode material. This objective's realization is supported by Output No. 1-4 (No.4 paper under preparation). 2. The cathode material has undergone thorough characterization using a range of comprehensive techniques. The structural analysis was carried out through FTIR, Synchrotron XRD, and XAF, while surface characterization employed XPS, TOF-SIMS, and AFM. Notably, advanced characterization techniques such as X-ray spectroscopy imaging, FIB-SEM, and FIB-TEM were employed to reveal the structural and surface evolution during cycling. These achievements are reflected in research outputs No. 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. 3. Various polymers, including PEDOT as an electronic conductive polymer, PV4D4 as an ionic conductive polymer, and PBA as an elastomer, were compared in this study. Our systematic research revealed that electronic conductive polymers lack mechanical flexibility, thus failing to stabilize the mechanical properties of cathode particles (output No. 1 & 2). In contrast, the electrochemical performance of ionic polymers is strongly influenced by their thickness (output No. 1 & 4). Elastic polymers were found to significantly improve the mechanical fatigue toughness of particles, enabling NCMs to achieve superior stability when combined with ionic conductive polymers (output No. 4 and conference No. 2). 4. Advanced characterization techniques such as TXM, XAENs, in-situ XRD, FIB-SEM, and TOF-SIMS were employed to understand the enhancing mechanism of the polymer coating. Our findings indicate that key aspects of the polymer coating include elasticity, ionic conductivity, electronic conductivity, and chemical stability. For polycrystalline NCM with high Ni content, which is prone to intergranular cracks, mechanical stability plays a dominant role in achieving stability. Elastic polymers with ionic conductivity provide an ideal solution to mitigate capacity decay. On the other hand, for mechanically robust cathodes such as single-crystal Ni-rich NCM, conductive polymers are effective due to the importance of SOC homogeneity. These findings are reflected in research outputs No. 1-6 and conference presentations No. 1-2.

15221719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221719.value: During the studies, several elastomers with good ionic conductivity were successfully prepared using the newly developed iCVD system. These included adhesive PV4D4, crosslinked PEGMA, and soft PBA. Moreover, these elastomers were combined with electronic conductive polymers such as PEDOT and PPy to create composite coating layers with both electric and ionic conductivity. The use of iCVD and oCVD as integrated platforms, along with a diverse polymer pool, facilitated systematic investigations, leading to the following main findings: Polymer coating with high ionic conductivity is crucial for maintaining high-rate performance and providing surface protection to NCMs (standard cathode materials tested). The research revealed that polymers with limited ionic conductivity, such as PEDOT and PPy, negatively impact on rate performance and high-rate cycling stability. In contrast, the ionic conductive PV4D4 combined with PEDOT and PPy outperforms PEDOT and PPy in achieving high-rate capability and stability during cycling. This finding highlights the importance of ionic and electric conduction in the coating and expands the range of useful polymers for effective coatings. Soft polymer grain boundary coating plays a key role in mitigating NCM microcracks and enhancing cycling and storage stability. Unlike rigid PEDOT and PPy, soft polymers like PBA have the advantage of suppressing microcracks in NCM due to their ability to accommodate volume variations. Detailed mechanical analysis uncovered the elastomer buffering effect, which inhibits crack propagation and enhances stability. This discovery provides new insights and perspectives for addressing the challenge of microcracks. Composite surface coatings with both electric and ionic conductivity exhibit a synergistic effect in enhancing stability, particularly at high-rate conditions. By combining electric and ionic conductivity on the surface layer of NCM cathodes, the charge-transfer kinetics is significantly improved, enabling high-rate cycling. As a result, the PV4D4-PPy coated NCM demonstrates superior cycling performance compared to coatings of PPy or PV4D4 alone, surpassing many recent publications. This finding opens up new possibilities for designing polymer surface coatings to achieve super-performance in lithium-ion battery materials. Overall, the systematic investigations using iCVD and oCVD platforms, along with a diverse polymer pool, have yielded important insights into the role of ionic conductivity, the benefits of soft polymers in mitigating microcracks, and the synergistic effects of composite coatings. These findings contribute to the advancement of polymer surface coating design for high-performance materials of lithium-ion batteries.

15221719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221719.value: We developed a versatile polymer coating technique with the ability to design the electric, ionic conductivity, and mechanical properties of the coatings based on a diverse selection of polymers. Here are the potential areas where further research can be extended: 1. Extension to Anode Materials: The technique can be extended to address the challenges faced by anode materials such as Si and Si/C, where elasticity is crucial as a protective layer. For instance, the use of highly elastic polymers like poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) (elongation over 1200%) holds promise for accommodating the size changes in Si/C anodes. 2. Application in New Battery Chemistries: By applying polymer coatings with tailored properties, including conductivity, adhesion and strechability, the interfacial stability and overall performance of these can be enhanced, including Na+ and K+ -ion batteries. 3. Surface Modification for Solid-State Lithium Metal Batteries (SSLBs): The chemical stability and mechanical capabilities of polymers make them ideal candidates for surface modifications in SSLBs. By applying polymer coatings on the cathode and Li anode, it is possible to facilitate fast lithium ion (Li+) diffusion and create a soft contact surface, thereby addressing the challenges associated with chemo-mechanical deterioration. In summary, the newly developed method can be extended to future research on materials surface engineering in batteries field and beyond.

15221719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221719.value: In this project, we developed a new vapor-phase method to grow elastomers with ionic conductivity on lithium-ion battery cathode materials to improve the service life of batteries. We found that using a polymer with good ionic conductivity helps the battery charge and discharge quickly without any issues. Additionally, the flexible polymer can absorb the changes in size of the cathode materials, which is a major problem causing battery deterioration. When we combine different types of polymers, they work together to enhance the battery's overall performance, including its stability and ability to charge and discharge at a high rate. Our research has uncovered new principles for designing materials and introduced a new method to boost battery performance. As a result, we have published six impactful research papers in respected international journals, which has helped raise Hong Kong's reputation in the global research community and fostered collaborations with other outstanding researchers worldwide. Furthermore, this project has made significant contributions to education in Hong Kong by training three research students (two PhD students and one MPhil student). The knowledge gained from this work can be further developed and expanded in the future to improve other areas of battery technology, contributing to sustainable research advancements. The technology can also be translated to industry for commercial benefits in this important field.

15221819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221819.value: The conventional power distribution is based on 50/60Hz AC or pure DC distribution. Optical distribution has been discussed and it is used for communication rather than power distribution and its research in power distribution using optical fiber is not promising. However, the magnetic distribution could be an alternative method for power distribution besides the above 3 methods. One of the key advantages is the magnetic distribution does not have an electrical connection and it is electrical safer. The concept is based on a long magnetic core for magnetic power distribution and a new technique has been examined initially to tap the energy from the magnetic path without using physical contact or metal conduction. Concerning the safety of power transfer, magnetic power distribution is a promising method to replace the present-day solid-wire-based power distribution and provide a socket-less living and working environment for mankind. It is expected to be applied in the smart living where electricity is free to tap from anywhere of the smart house, say the ground, walls, and even the ceilings, which facilitate installations of electrical appliances, such as air conditioning and TV set, and increases the flexibility of modern house development. In high-speed train constructions, by embedding the long magnetic core under the rails, power is transferred contactlessly to the train for motor driving and lighting purposes. The proposed methodology can also be used in stand-alone systems. For example, in smart vessel systems, batteries or other energies sources are compactly installed under the deck, while energy is still transferred wirelessly via near-field coupling for onboard usage. Hence, the perfect protection of energy sources greatly reduces chances of hazards brought by electricity leakage in humid, mine or wet location. The proposed work is not a single point wireless power transfer, but a long-distance wireless power transfer with many tapings for power output. High-frequency magnetic design and distributed magnetic design is the core research components. It is envisaged that the success of the proposed project will bring a new concept of high-efficiency power distributed instead of only electric and optical. Power output is distributed and without metal contacts. It is applicable to domestic and industrial users. The expected power from several watts to several of Kilowatts can be transferred through such magnetic distribution plus near-field coupling. Thus, the new technology will provide an alternative method for power distribution. Such research also contributes to smart-living and safe-industrial development. 傳統的功率分配給基於50 / 60Hz交流電或純直流電分配，光能常用於通信而不是功率分配，並且其在使用光纖的功率分配方面的研究是不可取的。然而，除了上述3種方法之外，磁分佈可以是用於配電的替代方法。其中一個關鍵優勢是磁性分配沒有電氣連接，分電氣更安全。該概念基於用於磁力分配的長磁芯，並且已經初步研究了一種新技術，以在不使用物理接觸或金屬傳導的情況下從磁路中獲取能量。關於電力傳輸的安全性，磁力配電是一種很有前途的方法，可以取代現今的固體電線配電，為人類提供無插座的生活和工作環境。它預計將應用於智能生活，智能住宅的任何地方都可以免費供電，比如地面，牆壁，甚至是天花板，這些都可以方便地安裝電器，如空調和電視機，以及增加現代住宅開發的靈活性。在高速列車結構中，通過將長磁芯嵌入軌道下方，電力無接觸地傳遞到列車以用於電動機驅動和照明目的。建議的方法也可用於獨立系統。例如，在智能船舶系統中，電池或其他能源緊湊地安裝在甲板下方，而能量仍然通過近場耦合無線傳輸以用於船上使用。因此，對能源的完美保護大大降低了潮濕，礦井或有水位置漏電帶來的危險。擬議的工作不是單點無線功率傳輸，而是具有許多點功率輸出的長距離無線功率傳輸。高頻磁設計和分佈式磁設計是核心研究的組成部分。設想該項目的成功將帶來一個新的高效率電力概念，而不僅僅是電力和光學。功率輸出是分佈式的，沒有金屬觸點。適用於家庭和工業用戶。從幾瓦到幾千瓦的預期功率可以通過這種磁分配加上近場耦合來傳遞。因此，新技術將提供另一種配電方法，此類研究還有助於智能生活和安全工業發展。

15221819.label: Realisation of objectives
15221819.value: In recent years, Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) has gained attention for its flexible, safe, and user-friendly characteristics. It enables power transfer through magnetic coupling without direct electrical contact. Research in this field focuses on achieving higher power levels and improved efficiency. Multiple transmitters in a WPT system have been found to enhance power transfer and efficiency. This paper introduces a novel WPT cell for multiple transmitters and receivers, providing a simple and flexible wireless magnetic power distribution method. These cells can be easily installed in walls or the ground, reducing the need for cables and electrical shock risks. Power electronics circuits are recommended to convert the AC output of the WPT system to DC for target devices. The proposed system incorporates high-permeability magnetic cores for solid coupling. The research addresses four key objectives and are fulfilled as below: Objective 1: Examination of Long-Distance Magnetic Power Distribution using Combined High and Low Permeability Magnetic Cores The magnetic distribution for long-distance power transmission necessitates the utilization of magnetic resonance and the examination of associated resonant properties for wireless power transfer. Firstly, we conducted a comprehensive study on the magnetic stability of coupled coils. This involved examining the associated emissions and coupling disturbances. Different coil configurations and models were employed to investigate emissions on the receiving side for the reduction of the fluctuation of ripple output. To achieve efficient power transfer over long distances, a study was conducted on a long magnetic ferrite-based core spanning over 1 meter, focusing on the mechanism of joining magnetic cores. The reduction of leakage was a key aspect of the investigation. Various core shapes, including E, I, and U shapes, were examined on the secondary coupling side to optimize the magnetic core structure for magnetic power distribution. Equivalent circuit models were developed for the different shapes. The power transfer process involved magnetic distribution to the load and utilized resonant excitation to enhance power efficiency. Different permeabilities were explored to achieve optimized power transfer, and corresponding models were established. The proposed new core structure, along with its examination of leakage fields for emission minimization, represents a significant advancement in magnetic power distribution. The study considered both ferrite cores and coreless configurations, analyzing factors such as geometry, cost, and weight. Through the implementation of the new core structure approach, losses were successfully reduced. For driving the secondary side coupled coils, the multilevel technique proved to be a valuable approach for the driving circuit. Additionally, a staircase method with the potential to configure the output voltage in the form of AC current is prospoed. The soft-switching and modular concepts introduced in this study offer practical techniques for magnetic power distribution. Objective 2. Examine the magnetic emission of the magnetic distribution To address the parallel and series coil configurations generate leakage fields, various methods have been explored, including the utilization of magnetic topologies, optimized coil arrangements, soft-switching techniques, and compensation mechanisms. Several studies have investigated these approaches, employing associated models and finite element analysis to compare their effectiveness in reducing leakage and interference. In the field of dynamic magnetic distribution wireless power transfer systems, attention has been given to the fluctuations in mutual inductance. The study primarily focuses on electric vehicle (EV) or battery loads. A small-signal model is developed, taking into account coupling vibrations, and emphasizes the significance of employing a feedforward loop. Experimental results demonstrate a considerable reduction in battery charging current ripple during constant speed driving, along with enhanced stability and faster system response in step-change cases. The study achieves faster settling time, mitigates overshoot problems, and eliminates the need for communication between transmitters and receivers, thereby improving reliability and reducing costs. Furthermore, extensive research has been conducted on various magnetic components and their associated circuits. To minimize leakage, a control method utilizing a simple proportional-integral (PI) controller is employed. The stability of the system is analyzed using Bode diagrams, and it is observed that the stability performance is significantly improved with this approach. These findings have been published, highlighting the importance of considering leakage reduction techniques and stability analysis in magnetic power distribution systems. The research contributes to the development of more efficient and reliable systems, paving the way for advancements in magnetic component design and control methodologies. Objective 3: Control of Parallel and Series Power Magnetic Paths in Alignment and Leakage Path In this study, the field of magmatic path management is explored, with a focus on parallel and series magnetic configurations. A novel approach involving tapped inductors is introduced, enabling diverse connections of magnetic cores. By utilizing a tapping technique, the inductors can be connected in parallel and series configurations, providing increased flexibility in the magnetic power distribution system. To enhance power conversion, a power converter based on the boost topology is implemented, operating in the current source mode. This departure from the conventional voltage mode is a notable feature. The performance of the system is rigorously analyzed through extensive simulation and experimentation, considering ripple, conversion, and efficiency. Furthermore, the challenge of developing circuits for multiple output magnetic power distribution systems is addressed. The utilization of the current source mode for parallel and series paths is examined, along with the investigation of the hybrid pulse width modulation (PWM) technique to facilitate efficient multiple output connections. The study also incorporates switched-capacitor technology to further enhance efficiency. These techniques collectively contribute to improved performance in the magnetic power distribution system. The research findings underscore the achieved enhancement in efficiency and are documented accordingly. Objective 4. Develop the best magnetic topology for high efficiency power distribution. Parallel and series coils provide an alternative approach to guide magnetic flux in power transfer topologies, allowing a single input to achieve multiple outputs with high efficiency. However, the inclusion of magnetic topologies becomes crucial to address leakage and magnetic interference. Techniques like zero-voltage switching and leakage compensation using various inductances and capacitors are employed. Furthermore, the secondary side of coupled coils significantly influences power conversion performance. Implementing switched-capacitor technology and current source mode proves beneficial in reducing unnecessary ripple caused by electromagnetic emission from mutually coupled coils. Various coil designs are explored to alleviate fluctuations and enhance overall performance. In addition, other topologies involving DD (double-D) and DQ (double-Q) coils have been explored. The mutual inductance between various inductors on the distribution line has been extensively studied, resulting in an efficiency exceeding 80%. The efficiency of the magnetic power distribution system is also impacted by the ferrite structure. The study involves examining leakage fields for emission minimization, considering both ferrite core and coreless configurations. Factors such as geometry, cost, and weight have been carefully analyzed. Furthermore, the optimal topology is closely related to the circuit connections of the coils. A novel parallel compensation technique, utilizing external inductance on the primary side, has been proposed, demonstrating significant efficiency improvements. This compensation method is applied in the LLC (inductor-inductor-capacitor) and series-series configurations. The research conducted in these studies contributes to the advancement of magnetic power distribution systems, providing valuable insights into various coil configurations, compensation techniques, ferrite structures, and circuit connections. These findings pave the way for enhanced efficiency and improved performance in power transfer applications.

The study focused on magnetic stability, emissions, and coupling disturbance. Different coils and models were utilized to analyze received side emissions and reduce ripple output fluctuation. Techniques such as magnetic topology, coil arrangement, soft-switching, and compensation were explored to reduce emissions. Finite element analysis and experimental comparisons were conducted to evaluate leakage and interference. The study also examined mutual inductance fluctuations in dynamic magnetic power distribution for wireless power transfer systems. The use of a feedforward loop and control methods like simple PI and Bode diagram analysis improved stability performance.
