15221819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221819.value: To advance this research further, several areas can be explored. Advanced Magnetic Topologies: Develop and optimize advanced magnetic topologies with novel core materials, innovative coil designs, and advanced magnetic structures. Research new materials with enhanced magnetic properties to improve power transfer efficiency and reduce emissions. Wireless Power Transfer Integration: Explore techniques like resonant inductive coupling and magnetic resonance coupling to integrate wireless power transfer technologies into magnetic power distribution. Optimize resonant properties and mitigate interference and losses for efficient wireless power transfer over longer distances. Control and Conversion Techniques: Develop advanced control methods such as model predictive control or adaptive control algorithms to enhance system performance, stability, and efficiency. Explore new power conversion topologies and circuit designs for improved power quality, reduced losses, and increased overall efficiency. Integration with Renewable Energy Sources: Investigate integrating magnetic power distribution with renewable energy systems like solar or wind power. This can lead to more efficient and reliable power distribution systems with reduced environmental impact. For longer-distance power distribution, propose new methods to extend the distance beyond the current limit of 1 meter. This requires the development of new materials and magnetic topologies capable of supporting power transfer over longer distances.

15221819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221819.value: The research conducted in this study aimed to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of long-distance magnetic power distribution. The researchers investigated various aspects of the technology, including how to reduce magnetic emissions, optimize magnetic topologies, and enhance power conversion. The study focused on developing new methods and materials to extend the distance over which power can be efficiently transferred using magnetic fields. The major achievement of this project was the development of novel magnetic topologies and materials that enabled more efficient and reliable power distribution over longer distances. The use of new arrangement of materials allowed for more efficient power transfer. Another important achievement was the reduction of magnetic emissions and interference. The researchers investigated techniques to minimize leakage fields and electromagnetic interference, which can affect the performance of the power distribution system. Additionally, the study explored the integration of wireless power transfer technologies into the magnetic power distribution system. 15221919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15221919.value: 該項目旨在利用微液滴芯片來簡化光捕獲和級聯式酶反應，以尺寸一致的微液滴作為微反應器來產生葡萄糖，集中研究納米材料的合成、微反應器的開發和酶反應的機制。 眾所周知，綠色植物依靠自然光合作用（NPS）來捕捉陽光和CO2來產生碳水化合物。NPS過程的一個關鍵步驟是通過酶催化光反應來產生輔酶NADH，使水分子分裂成氧和氫。氧氣直接釋放到大氣中，而氫立即與CO2結合，形成糖和其他有機分子。即使經過數十億年的進化，NPS的能源效率仍然很低（通常為<1%），遠低於其理論極限的30%。另一方面，光流體技術能夠在對微結構中對光和液體同時進行精準控制。受此激發，我們提出本項目，將光流體技術用於葡萄糖的人工光合作用（APS），研製出簡單高效的集成光流體晶片。主要工作包括：（一）納米材料的合成；（二）開發集成光流體晶片，利用RuBP從CO2生產NPS的中間產物（即G3P）；（三）嘗試從G3P再生RuBP，以完成整個卡爾文循環；（四）開發大型反應器以擴大葡萄糖生產。 已有的APS系統多數用於水裂解和生物質生產，與其相比，該項目的獨特之處在於利用微流體芯片來復現鏈接光合反應的各個步驟，同時提供在NPS裡面不存在但是對光合作用至關重要的新功能，比如消除NPS中CO2擴散限制、克服O2抑制作用、實現葡萄糖的連續生產等。 在本項目的準備期間，我們開展了一些預研性工作，並演示了NADH再生、微液滴的生成和葡萄糖轉化等功能，證實了本項目技術方案的可行性。據我們所知，這是第一次嘗試使用光流體芯片來實現整個光合過程。本項目如果成功，有望於開發出一條新的技術路徑，用工業生產的方式來製作糖和澱粉等基本食品材料，從根本上解決人類社會的食品短缺危機，為未來的太空殖民做好技術儲備。

15221919.label: Realisation of objectives
15221919.value: In relation to Objective 1, we have successfully synthesized following key materials: (i) g-C3N4 nanopowders for the highly-efficient photo-enzymatic reduction of NAD+ to NADH; (ii) new dual-defect-abundant g-C3N4 nanopatches for enhanced photocatalytic regeneration of NADH; (iii) new self-assembled naphthalimide nanoribbons for high efficient photoreduction reaction; (iv) electron mediator [Cp*Rh(bpy)H2O]2+ (Cp* = pentamethylcyclopentadienyl and bpy = 2,2′-dipyridyl) for selective transfer of electrons and protons to NAD+ to regenerate the targeted cofactor 1,4-NADH; (v) new template-assisted EWOD method for rapid, batch generation of a large number (10^6) of droplets whose size can vary from a few hundred nanometers to a few millimeters. In relation to Objective 2, we have immobilized RuBisCO to the sidewall of PDMS microchannels using chemical and physical adsorption methods and have successfully converted RuBP and CO2 into 3-PGA. In relation to Objective 3, we have investigated different strategies to improve production rate, such as scaling up, scaling out, layer-by-layer stacking, and have tested the scaling laws of these strategies. For large reactors, we have developed a new spray coating method to fabricate large solar photocatalytic panels (1 m x 0.5 m). Unfortunately, the experimental tests have shown that the photocatalyst layers are not durable enough and the energy efficiency is low. Further studies of immobilization processes should be conducted.

15221919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15221919.value: Major findings: (1) We have developed dual-defect g-C3N4 (DDCN) with controllable defects of nitrogen vacancies and cyano groups for efficient photocatalytic cofactor regeneration via a KOH-assisted thermal polymerization by using urea as a precursor to introduce nitrogen vacancies and cyano groups into C3N4 crystalline structures. The DDCN samples assisted with 0.1-g KOH produce 3 times more NADH than the pristine g-C3N4. We have found the dual defects vary the energy levels and trap states and result in stronger light absorption and faster charge separation, both are beneficial to the photoregeneration of NADH. This work provides a green, energy-saving, and promising strategy for nicotinamide cofactor regeneration and would promote its application in biosynthesis and drug manufacturing. This finding was published in ACS Sustainable Chemistry & Engineering in 2023 (reported as an output of this project). (2) We have developed a physical immobilization method which can easily, reversibly immobilize RuBisCO (i.e., the first enzyme of Calvin cycle) onto PDMS surfaces via hydrophobic interaction. Using this method, we have fabricated biomimetic reusable microfluidic reactors for continuous production of glucose precursor 3-phosphoglycereate at 0.145 ± 0.008 nmol/min. The reactors are also scaled out to 2 and 6 parallel reactors as a proof-of-concept of large-scale synthesis. This finding was published in Catalysis Science & Technology as the cover page in 2022 (reported as an output of this project). (3) We have developed a layer-by-layer strategy to immobilize more RuBisCO into the microreactors, and have obtained a continuous conversion of CO2 into glucose precursor at 1.9 nmol min-1 with enhanced activity (1.5 times), stability (~8 times) and reusability (96% after 10 reuses) relative to the free RuBisCO. The microreactors are further scaled out from one to six in parallel and achieve the production at 15.8 nmol/min, obtaining an energy conversion efficiency 3.3 times of rice. This is the first demonstration that artificial photosynthesis can have a better performance than natural photosynthesis in terms of energy conversion efficiency. This part of work is still under intensive study and will be published in future. Research outcome: (1) Published 5 journal articles and 4 conference papers. (2) Obtained 1 Best Poster Award. (3) Established close research collaborations with other institutions, for example, with Abdel El Abed of Université Paris-Saclay (France) on droplet generation, Prof. Jia Yanwei of University of Macau on bio-microreactors, Prof. Liu Detao of South China University of Technology on photoenzymatic reactions, and Prof. Shui Lingling of South China Normal University on droplets’ electrical manipulation. The PI is collaborating with Prof. Abdel El Abed to apply for the ANR/RGC joint project, and in the process of setting up a Mainland/GBA Joint Research Centre for Advanced Microfluidics with Prof. Jia Yanwei, Prof. Liu Detao and Prof. Shui Lingling.

15221919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15221919.value: Further studies will be conducted in 3 main aspects: (1) other enzyme immobilization methods such as hydrogel encapsulation to improve enzyme content, stability and activity; (2) conversion of glucose precursor G3P to glucose to complete the reaction path from CO2 to glucose; (3) regeneration of RUBP from G3P to complete the Calvin cycle in a self-sustainable manner.

15221919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15221919.value: Green crops use sunlight and CO2 to make food through a process called photosynthesis. But even after billions of years, this process is not very efficient, using less than 1% of the energy it could. This project tried to improve this by using tiny droplets to capture light and speed up the reactions that make glucose, a type of sugar. We focused on creating new materials, developing tiny reactors, and figuring out how to make bigger ones. We made a new material that increased the speed of a key reaction by three times. We also made tiny reactors that could be used over and over again, and they made glucose faster and more efficiently than rice plants do. We also looked at different ways to make our reactors bigger, and found some promising methods. This project is a step towards making basic food ingredients like sugar and starch using only sunlight and CO2, like a factory. This could help solve big problems like food shortages and reducing carbon emissions.

15222119.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15222119.value: 大规模边缘计算中的主动性和合作式资源管理技术

15222119.label: Project Objectives
15222119.value: Propose an edge resource allocation framework including three components of service demand predication, resource allocation and performance evaluation. Develop edge service predication algorithm based on pattern mining on incomplete historical information, and conduct the pattern based resource allocation via the steps of a priori resource allocation and on-demand evacuation under both single and multiple stakeholder situations. Develop a prototype to deploy example applications and evaluate the performance of the proposed framework.

15222119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15222119.value: 随着大数据时代的到来和万物互联的新纪元开启，基于传统云计算服务的应用面临响应时延长，网络通信代价高等问题，从而导致用户服务质量下降。为应对以上挑战，本项目着眼于大规模边缘计算，通过将用户服务部署在分布于大规模广空域范围内且邻近终端用户的边缘设备上来有效提升响应速度，并降低网络带宽消耗，从而显著提升用户服务质量。 现有的边缘计算模式缺乏对边缘设备资源受限问题的充分考虑，且忽略了通过大规模边缘节点间的合作机制进行有效资源调度和负载管理。本项目设计主动性和合作式的资源管理方法，通过挖掘用户服务需求大数据，预测用户长期需求变化和短期波动，并在大规模边缘设备间进行协同合作。初步研究结果显示相比传统边缘计算模式，本项目所研究的数据驱动的资源管理方法能显著提高用户服务质量。本项目所研究的在大规模边缘计算中部署大数据驱动的资源管理方法面临以下挑战： 1. 分布在广时空域范围的用户需求预测需要通过历史数据挖掘潜在的影响因子，而用户需求记录往往存在不完备和数据异构等问题； 2. 数据预测往往存在误差，如何通过协同合作、资源预留等手段克服预测误差，维持算法健壮性，即保证响应速度，同时降低带宽消耗具有很强挑战性； 3. 协调服务提供商、边缘设备运营方、用户以及其他利益相关者之间的合作和管理存在困难。 本项目系统研究了基于大规模边缘计算的数据驱动资源管理方法，并提出适用于城域规模的边缘计算解决方案。拟设计一种基于双记忆预测模型的编解码架构，从异构的用户历史大数据中挖掘负载变化规律并预测用户需求；在此基础上，研究以资源预分配和实时调度为导向的边缘共享机制。在资源预分配步骤中，设计一种基于用户需求预测的博弈算法，平衡用户、边缘、运营商等利益需求；在实时调度步骤，设计基于强化学习的任务调度和资源分配算法，达到降低响应时延和均衡负载的目的。 本项目研究的算法和机制将基于实际系统验证性能，拟基于电信用户需求数据进行数据挖掘，并在实际边缘设备系统上运行资源分配算法，提供算法性能衡量标准和验证体系。

15222119.label: Realisation of objectives
15222119.value: This project conducts a systematic investigation on the data-driven resource allocation among cooperative edges and proposes feasible solutions enabling its deployment in public city-scale edges. In the first half of this 3-year project, we devised a game mechanism to coordinate the edges and service providers belonging to different stakeholders. We also developed deep learning models that make the best execution action via capturing features of historical user demands and resource allocation actions. In the second half of this project, we integrate emerging and promising technologies, such as federated learning, digital twin, zero-shot learning and so on, to develop novel paradigms. For these paradigms, we also develop a lot of advanced algorithms to improve system performance, such as learning efficiency, service delay and information freshness, etc. The improvement of our proposed paradigms and algorithms has also been fully evaluated by extensive experiments with real-world datasets.

15222119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15222119.value: We investigated two novel digital twin assisted, SFC-enabled reliable service provisioning problems in MEC, through exploring reliability dynamics in VNF instance placements, and showed the NP-hardness of both problems. We also devised an approximation algorithm with a constant approximation ratio for it when the problem size is large. We then considered the dynamic service provisioning by formulating a dynamic service admission maximization problem, for which we formulated an ILP solution for its offline version, followed by devising a performance guaranteed online algorithm. Multi-label zero-shot learning extends conventional single-label zero-shot learning to a more realistic scenario that aims at recognizing multiple unseen labels of classes for each input sample. Existing works usually exploit attention mechanism to generate the correlation among different labels. However, most of them are usually biased on several major classes while neglect most of the minor classes with the same importance in input samples, and may thus result in overly diffused attention maps that cannot sufficiently cover minor classes. We argue that disregarding the connection between major and minor classes, i.e., correspond to the global and local information, respectively, is the cause of the problem. In this paper, we propose a novel framework of unbiased multi-label zero-shot learning, by considering various class-specific regions to calibrate the training process of the classifier. Federated Learning (FL) is susceptible to gradient leakage attacks, as recent studies show the feasibility of obtaining private training data on clients from publicly shared gradients. Existing work solves this problem by incorporating a series of privacy protection mechanisms, such as homomorphic encryption and local differential privacy to prevent data leakage. However, these solutions either incur significant communication and computation costs, or significant training accuracy loss. In this paper, we show that the sensitivity of gradient changes w.r.t. training data is an essential measure of information leakage risk. Based on this observation, we present a novel defense, whose intuition is perturbing gradients to match information leakage risk such that the defense overhead is lightweight while privacy protection is adequate.

15222119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15222119.value: Most existing personalized federated learning (pFL) methods rely on model parameters aggregation at the server side, which require all models to have the same structure and size. Such constraints would prevent status quo pFL methods from further application in practical scenarios, where clients are often willing to own unique models, i.e., with customized neural architectures to adapt to heterogeneous capacities in computation, communication and storage space, etc. We seek to develop a novel training framework that can accommodate heterogeneous model structures for each client and achieve personalized knowledge transfer in each FL training round. Federated Semi-supervised Learning (FedSSL) has emerged as a new paradigm for allowing distributed clients to collaboratively train a machine learning model over scarce labeled data and abundant unlabeled data. However, existing works for FedSSL rely on a closed-world assumption that all local training data and global testing data are from seen classes observed in the labeled dataset. It is crucial to go one step further: adapting FL models to an open-world setting, where unseen classes exist in the unlabeled data.

15222119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15222119.value: This project aims to develop advanced paradigms and algorithms for proactive and cooperative resource allocation in wide-scale edges. We focus on emerging and promising technologies, such as federated learning, digital twin, zero-shot learning and so on, and make edge users access the profits of these technologies with limited resources and privacy concerns. For example, we design a novel pFL training framework dubbed Layer-wised Personalized Federated learning (pFedLA) that can discern the importance of each layer from different clients, and thus is able to optimize the personalized model aggregation for clients with heterogeneous data. We focus on the software and hardware synergy of on-device learning techniques, covering the scope of model-level neural network design, algorithm-level training optimization and hardware-level arithmetic acceleration. We also propose Chiron, an incentive-driven long-term mechanism for edge learning based on hierarchical deep reinforcement learning. These advanced paradigms and algorithms can be alternative solutions for future AI applications based on edge intelligent technologies, which can empower construction, public health, environment, transportation and other industries, and promote the upgrading of urban intelligence.

15223319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223319.value: 該專案將側重于地基雷達的關鍵技術問題，將地基雷達發展成一種能夠準確、高效地監測大面積快速地面變形（如香港機場第三跑道的填海區的沉降）的技術。目前顯然缺乏這種技術。 由於凝固、地下建築和採礦活動、地下水抽取和地殼運動等原因造成的地面變形，可能導致沉降漏斗、地震和對基礎設施的破壞。 地面變形率通常從每年亞毫米到每天幾釐米，甚至更大，具體取決於變形的原因。 通常需要密切監測地面變形，以確定變形的時空模式，以便更好地描述變形並降低其危險。 已開發出各種監測地面變形的技術。 差分水準是測量垂直地面變形的傳統但非常準確可靠的方法。 但是，當需要詳細監測很大面積時，該方法變得非常低效和勞動密集。 舉例來說，如果需要監測香港國際機場的第三條跑道的650公頃填海土地的沉降情況，需要很多測量隊晝夜工作。 空間干涉合成孔徑雷達（InSAR）是測量大面積變形的理想的技術選擇。 在良好的觀測條件下，該技術提供非常高的空間解析度（高達約 1 米）和精度（使用多時態 InSAR 處理時每年可達 1 mm 或更高）。 但是，空載 InSAR 可以測量的變形梯度有限，超過此限時，作為 InSAR 測量基礎的干涉圖將變得不相干，不能用於計算變形資訊。 事實上，地面變形往往可以超過這樣的極限。 原位感應器，如鑽孔引長計、傾斜計、基於 GNSS 的監控感應器也可用於監測地面變形。 然而，感應器通常價格昂貴，因此不能大量使用。 某些感應器也容易因過度變形而損壞。 顯然，需要開發新的先進技術，以便更有效地監測第三跑道施工場地等地區的快速地面變形。 我們將開發和測試地面雷達技術，以填補這一技術空白。 這項研究將解決此類技術中的一些關鍵技術問題，包括大氣對雷達觀測的影響，這些影響往往是雷達觀測最重要的誤差源，以及處理大量雷達資料的挑戰。該專案的創新點是觀測方案的設計以及新的資料處理模型和演算法。 該專案將一方面推進雷達遙感研究，另一方面產生一項具有重大實際影響的新技術。 這項技術將有潛力在香港及海外得到廣泛應用。 香港已規劃了一些未來重大的發展計畫。 例如，香港政府行政長官林鄭月娥女士在最近的第二份施政報告中，提出了"明日大嶼"的願景，其中包括一個占地1700公頃的填海工程，為26萬至40萬戶家庭的70萬至110萬居民提供住房。因此，未來對精確、高效的變形監測技術的需求將更高。 因此，該專案被認為具有重要科學價值和實際意義。

15223319.label: Realisation of objectives
15223319.value: All the three objectives have been fully achieved. A new approach has been developed for more accurate mitigating the atmospheric effects on ground-based radar observations. The approach consists of new field measurement techniques and data processing algorithms. We in particular proposed a concept of using selected ground control points to model the spatiotemporal variation of the atmospheric conditions within an area of measurements. We also used key atmospheric parameters measured in the field at selected locations to constrain the atmospheric models to enhance their accuracies. Test results have shown that the new approach is effective in reducing the impacts of the varying atmospheric conditions on ground-based radar observations especially when the measurement ranges are long. It has also been discovered in the research that the setting up procedure of the radar equipment could also bring significant measurement errors as it is difficult to centre the equipment at exactly the same location each time when the equipment is reset up and it is also not possible to level radar equipment perfectively. We have carried out extensive tests to determine the magnitudes of the errors due to equipment setting up. A model has been developed to estimate the setting up errors. The errors are parameterized and mitigated effectively in processing radar data and estimating the deformation based on a least squares model. We have validated the proposed method with a series of experiments. The volume of radar observations can be huge and it is always a challenging task to process the data especially when repeat observations are acquired in a multi-temporal (time series) radar measurement mode. It is therefore important to develop techniques that can process the large volume of radar observation data efficiently and in the same time extract all the important information in the observations such as the information on ground deformation. We have in the project developed and tested both sequential data processing and AI-based approaches. The approach allows radar observations obtained in a multi-temporal mode to be processed sequentially. For example, if the radar observations have been carried out for 5 times (5 surveys at the same time but at different dates) and the data have been processed to determine the deformation of the site based on the observations. When a new set of radar observations (6th survey) becomes available, the standard approach is to process all the raw data from the 6 sets of observations again to determine the time series of deformations. In this case the large volume of data needs to be put together to form a time series and reprocessed. According to the new approach developed in the project, the results from processing the observations from the first 5 surveys can be combined directly with the observations from the 6th survey to produce a time series of deformation measurements. In this case, the volume of the data that needs to be processed is much reduced and the computational resources required are significantly lower while the results from the new approach are almost the same. The ViT model is also very efficient in extracting the deformation information compared to the traditional models. The new approaches are therefore much more advantageous technically. Although satellite-based radar remote sensing can cover a large ground area very efficiently to measure the ground deformation in the area, the method will however not work when the ground deforms very fast due to the decorrelation effect. The main reason for the phenomenon is that the orbital satellite radar platforms have their fixed repeat cycles. When the deformation between two satellite measurements exceeds half the wavelength of the radar, in principle the deformation cannot be exactly determined as the phase measurements cannot be correctly unwrapped. However, many practical applications require effective technologies for measuring fast ground deformation. For example, in land reclamation, the land can often subside very fast at the initial stage. Satellite radar remote sensing often does not work in such a case in measuring ground subsidence. We have developed and tested a new technology for monitoring fast ground deformation. Test results have indicated that the technology works well except that when the incidence angles of the radar measurements are too small.

15223319.value: A new approach has been developed for more accurate mitigating the atmospheric effects on ground-based radar observations (e.g., Wu et al., 2022; 2023; Xie et al., 2022; Abdallah et al., 2024). The approach consists of new field measurement techniques and data processing algorithms. We in particular proposed a concept of using selected ground control points to model the spatiotemporal variation of the atmospheric conditions within an area of measurements. We also used key atmospheric parameters measured in the field at selected locations to constrain the atmospheric models to enhance their accuracies. It has also been discovered in the research that the setting up procedure of the radar equipment could also bring significant measurement errors as it is difficult to centre the equipment at exactly the same location each time when the equipment is reset up and it is also not possible to level radar equipment perfectively. The errors are parameterized and mitigated effectively in processing radar data and estimating the deformation based on a least squares model. It is therefore important to develop techniques that can process the large volume of radar observation data efficiently and in the same time extract all the important information in the observations such as the information on ground deformation. We have in the project developed and tested both sequential data processing and AI-based approaches (e.g., Wu et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2021 [3]; Zhu et al., 2023; Abdallah et al., 2024). The ViT model is also very efficient in extracting the deformation information compared to the traditional models. The new approaches are therefore much more advantageous technically. When the deformation between two satellite measurements exceeds half the wavelength of the radar, in principle the deformation cannot be exactly determined as the phase measurements cannot be correctly unwrapped. However, many practical applications require effective technologies for measuring fast ground deformation. For example, in land reclamation, the land can often subside very fast at the initial stage. Satellite radar remote sensing often does not work in such a case in measuring ground subsidence. We have developed and tested a new technology for monitoring fast ground deformation (e.g., Xie et al., 2022 [8]; Wu et al., 2023 [10]; Wu et al., 2023 [12]). Test results have indicated that the technology works well except that when the incidence angles of the radar measurements are too small.

15223319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223319.value: We plan to develop some of the concepts further to make them more useful for practical applications.

15223319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223319.value: Radar remote sensing is one of the most powerful technologies for studying deformation of the ground and structures. The technology has had significant impacts on fields such as earthquake studies, geohazard investigation, land subsidence, and monitoring of stability of infrastructures. The technology has however still some significant limitations. For example, the measurement results are often affected by various error sources. The technology is often unable to monitor fast deformation (the rate of deformation is high). The data processing process is often slow and requires significant computing resources. This project focused on some of the key issues in current radar remote sensing technology and has developed various new models and methods to overcome some of the key limitations. We have developed a new approach for more accurate mitigating the atmospheric effects on radar observations. We have also developed a model to estimate the radar equipment setting up errors. We have developed and tested both sequential data processing and AI-based approaches to enhance the efficiency of radar data processing. We have developed and tested a new technology for monitoring fast ground deformation.

15223419.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15223419.value: 隨機脈衝系統的最優控制及其應用

15223419.label: Project Objectives
15223419.value: In order to model stochastic impulse control problems, we will study various kinds of stochastic process. In addition to Wiener processes and Poisson jump processes, we will study extensively the use of mean reverting processes to model novel problems. The application domain include inventory control and financial portfolio optimization. The developed model will include a nonlinear feedback mechanism to adjust the state variable level. For systematic jumps following certain exogenous conditions, we will investigate the use of Markov switching between different states to account for a change in the regime. In general, we will study the optimality of solutions and study the set of quasi-variational inequality (QVI) for possible solutions. In order to solve for the optimal impulse control under the developed stochastic models, we will first study the limiting cases with perpetual time and ergodic control. For general situations with finite terminal time, we will investigate numerical techniques for solving the resulting set of quasi-variational inequalities. Specifically we will investigate the use of a penalty function approach to discretize and optimize on the optimal control. The control parameterization enhancing technique is employed to handle the impulse jumps in the control variables. For certain problems in finance with utility and habit functions, trial function approach will also be attempted. In general, software will be developed to enable visualization of the general solutions to the problem. In this objective, we will extend the developed models and investigate probabilistic constraints imposed on the impulse control problem. Following previous approaches, the constraints are first converted into certain algebraic constraints on the control variables, which can easily be embedded into existing solvers and the developed software. In particular, we will look at quantile probability with applications in finance, which is known as the value-at-risk constraint. We will developed a general framework to handle these kinds of constraints. Furthermore, we will also study suitable partial information models to infer the real state and hence the optimal control policy.

15223419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15223419.value: The impulsive systems are basically defined by continuous dynamical systems, but with jumps occurring at various time points along the solution trajectory. These jumps may be due to the application of impulsive control actions at various discrete time points. The impulsive systems arise naturally from a wide variety of applications in science and engineering, and are also important for solving finance and supply chain problems. At the same time, there are many different stochastic processes in modelling practical problems which account for real phenomena occurring in empirical data. In practice, development of solutions for different developed models remain to be an important issues in this area. Many practical models are often simplified in order to trade off solvability of the optimization problems. In this research project, our objective is to study stochastic models, solution methods, and novel applications of various kinds of impulsive systems. More specifically, our objective include: (i) to develop practical stochastic models with nonlinear feedback mechanism for impulsive control systems; (ii) to develop efficient computational algorithms for the construction of optimal controls for optimal impulsive control systems; and (iii) to apply the obtained methods to real world problems such as investment in portfolios, exchange rate dynamics, optimal dividends, and inventory control in supply chains. 脈衝系統基本上是連續動力系統，並沿著軌跡在不同時間點發生跳躍。這些跳躍可能是由於在各個離散時間點的脈衝控制動作而產生。脈衝系統在科學和技術工程上有著很多的應用，對解決財務和供應鏈問題也很重要。在同時，因應真實數據中出現的現象，建模實踐中存在許多不同的隨機過程。在實踐中，為不同的模型尋找解決方案仍然是重要的硏究方向。為了權衡優化問題的可解性，通常會簡化許多實用模型。 在這個研究項目中，我們的目標是研究隨機模型，解決方法，和各種脈衝系統的新穎應用。更具體地說，我們的目標包括：（i）開發具有非線性反饋的隨機脈衝控制系統的機制; （ii）開發有效的計算方法用於構造最優脈衝控制系統的解; （iii）將所獲得的方法應用於現實世界的問題，例如投資組合，匯率動態，最佳股息和庫存控制供應鏈。

15223419.label: Realisation of objectives
15223419.value: In this project, our main objectives are to investigate different optimal control problems with switches following certain exogenous conditions. Following the objectives of the proposal, we have published 12 journal papers, 1 paper under major revision and 1 under review. To summarize, we have achieved the following. The stochastic control problems involving regime switching jumps are of interest and of practical importance in financial management and economics. More recently, there has been dramatically increasing interest in studying this family of stochastic control problems as well as their financial applications. We have formulated the general stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problem with a mean-field state together with random coefficients governed by a Markov regime switching system [1]. We show that the convexity of the cost functional is necessary for the finiteness of the problem, whereas uniform convexity of the cost functional is sufficient for the open-loop solvability of the problem. We develop the sufficient and necessary condition for the open-loop solution and derive the minimizing sequence that can converge to the solution of the problem. We demonstrate with a few examples and tackle the mean-variance portfolio selection problem by constructing the optimal solution. We have studied another continuous-time mean-variance problem with a random investment horizon [2]. Both deterministic and stochastic functions of the exit time (in particular, the default time) are studied. We developed a switching regime model to describe the stochastic density process of the exit time. An interesting finding is that even in the deterministic case, the variance is no longer minimal with the risk-free investment only and the minimal variance is positive. Moreover, the efficient frontier is an upper part of a hyperbolic curve. When real data is employed, we studied and proposed a new volatility model called buffered threshold stochastic volatility (BARSV) model which does not only mitigate the side-effect of the estimation error of the threshold variable but also captures the hysteretic regime switching on both mean and volatility equations [3]. In portfolio optimization, we have developed a solver based on the branch-and-bound method in solving the cardinality constrained portfolio optimization with a new precise lower bound to speed up the calculations [4]. To handle such discrete cardinality constraint, we construct a smaller diagonal matrix derived from the covariance matrix with some special matrix processing techniques to formulate a lower bound problem. For stochastic optimization problems, the optimized solutions are related by the sampling process. We have studied the optimal solutions of an optimization problem based on sample average approximations (SAA) in the moderate deviation region, including moderate deviation principles and laws of iterated logarithm [5]. We studied the asymptotic behaviours of the stochastic process limit theorems for the optimal value and established the Donsker invariance principle (functional central limit theorem), the functional moderate deviation principle, and the Strassen invariance principle (functional law of iterated logarithm). These results show that the SAA has very good asymptotic behaviours in moderate deviation region. We extend the method to stochastic variational inequalities [6] to study the convergences in regimes of moderate deviations for the SAA solution which is an asymptotically consistent point estimator for the true solution to a stochastic variational inequality. Some central limit results and large deviation estimates for the SAA solution have been obtained. We have also studied a few optimal control problems for engineering applications. The first one is an optimal switching problem of switched systems in continuous time, which consists of a family of linear subsystems and a quadratic cost functional [7]. Our purpose is to find the optimal switching strategy so that the cost functional reaches its minimum value. We have derived a precise expression of lower bound such that a branch and bound method can be developed to find the global solution for the optimal switching sequence. The second type belongs to cyber-physical systems and multi-agent systems, and in particular their security issues when they are under attacks. Model predictive control (MPC), a widely accepted control method, can solve optimization control problems with constraints. The major challenge of this study is to design a dynamic event-triggered model predictive controller, that can guarantee the stochastic stability of a system subject to combined network attacks. In [8], we have developed a dynamic event-triggered MPC strategy to obtain the desired control objective. A novel online-solved MPC optimization problem is proposed to guarantee the stochastic stability of a system subject to randomly occurring deception attacks and packet dropouts simultaneously. In [9], we have studied the multi-agent systems (MASs) with time-varying switching subject to deception attacks. The nonidentical double event-triggering mechanisms (ETMs) are adopted for only a fraction of agents, and each agent transmits the data according to its own necessity. Semi-Markov process modeling with time-varying switching probability is adopted for switching topology and deception attacks occurring in transmission channel are considered. By using the cumulative distribution function (CDF) and the linear matrix inequality (LMI) technology, sufficient conditions for MASs to achieve consensus in mean square are obtained. An effective algorithm is presented to obtain the event-based control gains. In [10] we have studied state estimation of multi-agent systems under homologous attacks. We developed a sufficient and necessary condition on agents’ dynamics and proposed a fully distributed discrete-time estimation algorithm. This algorithm allows each agent to estimate its state and the attack signal through local information sharing. Unlike existing discrete-time estimation methods, agents need not to access global information of networks and agent dynamics by the proposed algorithm. In [11], we have developed an exact penalty function based tuning method for PID controller for the two-link manipulator. The PID tuning problem is described as a state constrained optimal parameters selection problem by formulating the control specifications into state constraints. In [12], we have proposed a sliding mode controller for the attitude control of spacecraft reorientation with attitude constraints. With the structure of the proposed sliding function, uniqueness of the equilibrium and fixed-time convergence are rigorously proven. Another advantage of the proposed controller is that the feasibility of attitude constraints can be proven not only on the sliding surface but also outside it. Another progress is to study the consumption-portfolio optimization problem with habit formation in a regime-switching jump-diffusion market [13]. The living standard, as a habit level that involves regime switching and jump diffusion, reflects the endogenous impact of past consumption. To solve the problem with general utility functions and non-Markovian random parameters, we complete the market by introducing some additional jump assets. After reducing the problem to solving a stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, we derive an optimal control by jointly adopting the envelope theorem and a backward stochastic partial differential equation. We have also extended the traditional portfolio theory is to include higher moment in a continuous time framework [14]. We have investigated a class of time-inconsistent stochastic control problems, where the objective function includes the mean and several higher-order central moments of the terminal value of state. We establish a partial differential equation (PDE) system for deriving a closed-loop Nash equilibrium control, which does not include the equilibrium value function. We show that our PDE system is equivalent to the extended HJB equations.

15223419.label: Major findings and research outcome
15223419.value: In this project, we have studied a number of optimal control problems with financial and engineering applications and developed some novel formulations and models. This includes stochastic linear-quadratic optimal control problems with a mean-field state together with random coefficients governed by a Markov regime switching system. Another important problem is continuous-time mean-variance problem with a random investment horizon. We developed a switching regime model to describe the stochastic density process of the exit time. Due to the timing risk, two mutual funds are needed to replicate the portfolio, which refutes the conventional wisdom that optimal portfolio strategy is not affected by the presence of an uncertain time horizon. Another new formulation is the consumption-portfolio optimization problem with habit formation in a regime-switching jump-diffusion market. We have also extended the traditional portfolio theory is to include higher moment in a continuous time framework. For parameter estimation, we proposed a new buffered threshold stochastic volatility (BARSV) model which does not only mitigate the side-effect of the estimation error of the threshold variable but also captures the hysteretic regime switching on both mean and volatility equations. In portfolio optimization, we have developed a solver based on the branch-and-bound method with a new precise lower bound in solving the cardinality constrained portfolio optimization, and is much faster than CPlex and SCIP solvers. The stochastic nature of the optimal solutions is addressed and the functional central limit theorem, the functional moderate deviation principle, and the functional law of iterated logarithm are established. For engineering applications, we have studied several cyber-physical and multi-agent systems when they are under attacks. We have developed a dynamic event-triggered MPC strategy to obtain the desired control objective. For multi-agent systems (MASs), sufficient conditions to achieve consensus in mean square are obtained subject to deception attacks. Moreover, we studied state estimation of multi-agent systems under homologous attacks and developed a sufficient and necessary condition on agents’ dynamics and proposed a fully distributed discrete-time estimation algorithm. Finally, we have developed an optimization method for PID controller for the two-link manipulator, and proposed a sliding mode controller for the attitude control of spacecraft reorientation with attitude constraints with several advantages. A method to find the optimal switching strategy for an optimal switching problem of switched systems in continuous time is proposed.

15223419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15223419.value: In the present project, we have studied a number of optimal control problems with financial and engineering applications. There are a number of extensions that could be considered. For portfolio problems, it is possible to add risks including interest rate and inflation. Their influences will likely affect the conclusion of the two-fund separation theorem. In the stochastic model, it would be of interest to add the effect of health investment of investors which will affect the consumption pattern. For parameter estimation problems, it would be of interest to develop Bayesian approaches in order to employ enough real data in the process. For engineering applications, we have developed a few event-triggered controls and estimation methods. Future extension can consider to include more cyber-attacks in the models and how to maintain estimation integrity in case of attacks.

15223419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15223419.value: In this project, we consider several practical problems in which unknowns are modelled by continuous dynamical systems, and the purpose is to optimize on the control variables in order to achieve certain objectives. In particular, it would be difficult to tackle when the control variables contain jumps and switches, as they appear to be discontinuous at certain points in time. This kind of problems arise naturally from a wide variety of applications in science and engineering, and are also important for solving finance and supply chain problems. The jumps and switches correspond to a change in decision making following the time varying objective. At the same time, there are many different stochastic processes in modelling practical problems which account for real phenomena occurring in empirical data. Derivation of solutions for different developed models remains to be an important issue in this area. Here, we study and develop several optimal control problems with switches following certain exogenous conditions, and we propose some solution techniques in solving the problems which have better performances and properties. The research outcomes can benefit both academia and industry.

15300019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300019.value: Gold catalysis has emerged as a powerful synthetic strategy for novel organic transformation reactions with exceptional selectivity and reactivity, broad functional group tolerance, and excellent compatibility to air/moisture reaction conditions. Particularly, gold(I) complexes are able to activate alkenes, alkynes, as well as allenes through π‐bond coordination to achieve a diversity of useful organic transformation reactions. Note that efforts on asymmetric gold(I) catalysis have been producing encouraging results. However, a major challenge for asymmetric catalysis using chiral gold(I) complexes comes from their linear geometry with only two coordination sites. During the chiral induction step in asymmetric catalysis, the chiral ligands are far away from the substrates resulting in poor stereochemical communications and hence leading to low enantioselectivity. To achieve high enantioselectivity, the use of chiral counter anions and specially designed dinuclear gold species would be needed. However, these strategies may not be generally applicable. In this proposal, we plan to rationally design and synthesize novel chiral oxazoline gold(III) complexes in a modular approach to function as efficient catalysts for asymmetric organic transformation reactions. We aim to synthesize novel gold(III) complexes featuring chiral oxazoline ligands bearing sterically bulky substituents that would extend the chiral environment around the catalytically active gold(III) center for better asymmetric induction. To enhance the stability of the gold(III) catalysts, we propose to employ chiral cysteine-based ligands by taking advantages of the strong Au-S bonding. In addition, the high modularity of the cysteine-based ligands provides an easy access to diverse chiral environment. We intend to develop mercaptophenyl oxazoline ligands for the construction of novel cyclometallated gold(III) complexes in which the sterically bulky substituents would be in a closer proximity to the catalytic gold(III) center resulting in higher enantioselectivity in asymmetric catalysis. We plan to develop novel chiral gold(III) complexes with distinct pseudo-C2 symmetric chiral cavity that would fully accommodate the substrates in a well-defined chiral cavity facilitating stereochemical communication in organic transformation reactions. With the newly developed chiral gold(III) complexes, we will conduct detailed application studies on catalytic asymmetric carboalkoxylation and 1,6-enyne cyclization reactions. Finally, we propose to study the novel axial-central-axial chirality transfer of chiral C,O-chelated BINOL/cyclometallated gold(III) complexes by a stereoselective complex formation and protodeauration reaction sequence aiming to achieve chiral resolution of racemic BINOL ligands.

15300019.label: Realisation of objectives
15300019.value: [1] Rationally Design and Synthesis of Novel Chiral Oxazoline Gold(III) Complexes by a Modular Approach (a) Efficient Synthesis of Chiral C,O-Chelated BINOL/Gold(III) Complexes for Asymmetric Catalysis Gold catalysis has significantly contributed to organic synthesis with high reactivity and selectivity. Asymmetric gold(I) catalysis has been demonstrated as an efficient strategy for synthesizing chiral compounds. However, the linear geometry of chiral gold(I) complexes consisting of two coordination sites in opposite direction remains a significant challenge for chiral induction. To achieve high enantioselectivity, specially designed chiral ligands with extended chiral cavities and bifunctional ligands for better substrate recognition have been developed. In contrast, asymmetric gold(III) catalysis remains less explored. Chiral gold(III) complexes have a square-planar geometry with four coordination sites. Notably, by rational ligand design, the chiral substituents of the chiral gold(III) catalysts can be placed in proximity to the substrates for efficient asymmetric induction leading to high enantioselectivity. In this work, we have developed a novel approach for efficient synthesis of chiral C,O-chelated BINOL/gold(III) complexes 3 by diastereomeric resolution using enantiopure BINOL as chiral resolving agent. The BINOL/gold(III) diastereomers with different solubility were separated by simple filtration, providing optically pure BINOL/gold(III) complexes with up to >99:1 dr. Combining with the efficient BINOL decoupling process, a simple and column-free method for chiral resolution of racemic gold(III) dichloride complexes in gram scale was established, giving their enantiopure forms in good yields (overall 70%). Conversely, the resolved enantiopure gold(III) dichloride complexes could serve as chiral resolving agent to resolve disubstituted BINOL derivatives, achieving both BINOLs and gold(III) complexes in good to excellent yields (overall 77 – 96% and 76 – 95%, respectively) with high optical purity up to 99% ee. Through a consecutive chirality transfer process, the chiral information from an inexpensive chiral source was transferred to highly valuable gold(III) complexes followed by the sterically bulky BINOL derivatives. This work would open a new synthetic strategy facilitating the development of structurally diverse chiral gold(III) complexes and gold(III)-mediated chiral resolution of BINOL derivatives. This work together with the study reported in [2] has been summarized as a manuscript under review. (b) Controlled Supramolecular Assemblies of Chiral Cyclometalated Gold (III) Amphiphiles in Aqueous Media Supramolecular assemblies in nature are serving vital roles in various biological proper functions. Advanced synthetic methodologies enable fabrications of artificial supramolecular assemblies, featured with high structural versatility and responsiveness to external stimulations, including light, pH, ion strength, organic molecules, and organic solvents. Amphiphilic molecular design is commonly combining both hydrophilic and hydrophobic moieties to exert good aqueous solubility and function turnability. Chiral organic amphiphiles are ready for assembling non-covalently into supramolecular chiral hierarchical structures, enabling additional stimulation responsiveness than that of natural counterparts. During our studies on chiral gold(III) complexes, we found that chiral gold(III) cyclometalated based amphiphiles in aqueous media achieved excellent supramolecular transformations to external stimuli to open new pathways for soft functional material fabrications. Notably, we have developed a new chiral cyclometalated gold (III) amphiphile (GA) assembling into lamellar nanostructures in aqueous media confirmed with transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Counterion exchange with D-, L-, or racemic-camphorsulfonates features the significant supramolecular helicity enhancements, enabling transformations of GA from lamellar structure to vesicles and to nanotubes with multi-equivalents of counterion. The limited cytotoxicity of GA in aqueous media exhibits good biocompatibility. This work has been published in ChemPlusChem 2023, e202300316. [2] Exploration on the Use of the Newly Developed Chiral Oxazoline Gold(III) Complexes for Asymmetric Catalysis With the new chiral oxazoline gold(III) complexes developed in the section [1a], we studied their catalytic activity in asymmetric carboalkoxylation of ortho-alkynylbenzaldehydes. Given that the chiral gold(III) complex (R,R)-3a could be easily prepared and purified by simple filtration, it was used as the catalyst for optimizing the reaction conditions. 2-Ethynylbenzaldehyde 4a was selected as the model substrate for the reaction. Without addition of activator, the catalyst was inactive in the reaction. We commenced the initial optimization studies with catalyst (5 mol%) and variation of acid (2.5 mol%). The desired product 5a was obtained with 22 – 54% yield and 75 – 89% ee. D-camphorsulfonic acid (D-CSA) was found to be the most efficient acid giving 5a with 89% ee and was selected for further studies. With the optimized reaction conditions, we investigated the ligand configuration effect on the product enantioselectivity. We first used 5 mol% of the four enantiomers/diastereomers (R,R)-3a, (R,S)-3a, (S,R)-3a and (S,S)-3a with 2.5 mol% D-CSA to catalyze the reactions at room temperature. The desired products were obtained with high enantioselectivity (89% ee, -88% ee, 80% ee and -89% ee, respectively). Notably, the gold(III) complexes (R,R)-3a and (R,S)-3a with opposite configuration on oxazoline moiety gave similar but opposite ee value (89% ee and -88% ee, respectively). Similarly, this opposite chiral induction was also observed by (S,R)-3a and (S,S)-3a which afforded 80% ee and -89% ee, respectively. These results indicated that the chiral induction of the reaction was dominant by the chiral oxazoline ligand of the gold(III) catalysts, while the configuration of BINOL ligand showed little effect on the enantioselectivity. Substrate 4a was all consumed after stirring for 16 h, as observed by TLC, giving 47% and 37% yield, respectively. Then, we screened the substrates using chiral (R,R)-3g as catalyst for further improving the enantioselectivity. As (R,R)-3g was less active in the carboalkoxylation reaction, we only selected substrates 4a, 4c, 4g, 4h and 4j for the reaction to examine its catalytic performance. We first conducted the reaction using substrate 4a with 5 mol% of (R,R)-3g and 2.5 mol% of D-CSA at -20 °C, but the desired product was not determined. Surprisingly, product 5a was obtained with excellent enantioselectivity of 99% ee when the acid loading was increased to 5 mol%. Under the same reaction conditions, chiral products 5c, 5g and 5h were obtained in low to moderate yields and excellent enantioselectivities (16 – 52% yield, 92 – 99% ee) while product 5j bearing electron withdrawing group was not determined. We performed the reaction at room temperature for substrate 4j and obtained the product with low yield but excellent enantioselectivities (17% yield and 92% ee). These results suggested that the oxazoline ligand of the gold(III) catalyst with more bulky isopropyl substituent on the aryl ring possibly reduced the product yield but improve the enantioselectivity. This study in asymmetric gold catalysis together with the study reported in [1a] has been summarized as a manuscript under review. [3] A Minireview on Asymmetric Gold Catalysis Asymmetric gold catalysis has been rapidly developed in the past ten years. Breakthroughs have been made by rational design and meticulous selection of chiral ligands. We have published a minireview summarizing the newly developed gold-catalyzed enantioselective organic transformations and the recent progress in ligand design (since 2016), including bisphosphine ligands, monophosphine ligands, phosphite-derived ligands, and N heterocyclic carbene ligands for asymmetric gold(I) catalysis as well as heterocyclic carbene ligands and oxazoline ligands for asymmetric gold(III) catalysis. This minireview has been published in Chem Asian J. 2021, 16, 364 –377.

15300019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300019.value: We have developed a novel approach for the synthesis of optically pure C,O-chelated BINOL/gold(III) complexes by diastereomeric resolution. Assisting with the successful BINOL decoupling process, we have established the simple, efficient and column-free method for chiral resolution of racemic oxazoline-based gold(III) dichloride complexes in gram scale. Meanwhile, the resolved enantiopure gold(III) dichloride complexes were capable of acting as chiral resolving agent to resolve disubstituted BINOL derivatives. These results open new avenues in the development of chiral gold(III) complexes and gold(III)-mediated chiral resolution of BINOL derivatives. The outstanding performance of a consecutive chirality transfer process was demonstrated, in which the chiral information was transferred initially from the inexpensive chiral source BINOL to the highly valuable gold(III) complexes, and finally to BINOL derivatives. We envision that this work would greatly facilitate the synthesis of a diversity of novel chiral gold(III) complexes and chiral BINOL ligands and enrich the applications of chiral gold(III) chemistry in different research fields such as the use of chiral gold(III) complexes for selective bioconjugation and materials science research. We have developed sterically hindered C,O-chelated cyclometalated gold(III) complexes by modifying the substituents of the aryl group attached on the chiral oxazoline moiety. The enantioselectivity was increased from 9% to 92% by changing the steric size and position of the substituents on the aryl group, revealing that the enantioselectivity was highly sensitive to the structural change of the chiral ligands. The enantioselectivity was further improved by decreasing the reaction temperature, providing the excellent enantioselectivity up to 99% ee. Our research findings demonstrated the great potential of chiral gold(III) complexes in asymmetric catalysis for organic synthesis. We have firstly designed and synthesized chiral gold(III) amphiphile (GA) to show enhanced supramolecular helicities in aqueous media. The lamellar nanostructures of GA were confirmed with TEM. Upon addition of D-, L-, or racemic-camphorsulfonates, the counterion exchanges enable supramolecular assembly transformations from lamellar structure to vesicles, and to nanotubes with significant supramolecular helicity enhancements, though multi-equivalents of counterion is needed. The reversibility of supramolecular transformation was partially possible in the current gold(III) amphiphilic design with good cytocompatibility.

15300019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300019.value: We have developed a novel consecutive chirality transfer strategy for efficient synthesis of new classes of structurally diverse optically pure C,O-chelated BINOL/gold(III) complexes by diastereomeric resolution. In addition, the resolved enantiopure gold(III) dichloride complexes were capable of acting as chiral resolving agent to resolve disubstituted BINOL derivatives. We will further explore the use of this novel consecutive chirality transfer strategy to construct structurally complicated chiral gold(III) complexes and chiral substituted BINOL ligands contributing to the research area of asymmetric catalysis. We have developed sterically hindered C,O-chelated cyclometalated gold(III) complexes by modifying the substituents of the aryl group attached on the chiral oxazoline moiety to achieve excellent enantioselectivity up to 99% ee in asymmetric carboalkoxylation of ortho-alkynylbenzaldehydes. We will investigate the application of the chiral gold(III) complexes as efficient catalysts for asymmetric catalysis of other organic transformation reactions. We have first demonstrated chiral gold(III) amphiphile (GA) to show enhanced supramolecular helicities in aqueous media. This new discovery is serving as the foundation to our next works on controls of supramolecular P-, M-helicities of chiral gold (III) amphiphiles with chiral counterions.

15300019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300019.value: Gold catalysis has become as a powerful synthetic tool for organic synthesis. Although great advancement in asymmetric gold(I) catalysis has been made, a great challenge in using chiral gold(I) complexes for asymmetric catalysis arises from their linear geometry causing a long distance between the chiral ligands the substrates resulting in poor chiral induction and low enantioselectivity. To achieve high enantioselectivity, chiral counter anions and specially designed chiral ligands are needed. However, these strategies may not be generally applicable. In this project, we have developed a novel consecutive chirality transfer strategy for efficient synthesis of structurally diverse optically pure C,O-chelated BINOL/gold(III) complexes by diastereomeric resolution. The resolved enantiopure gold(III) dichloride complexes can act as chiral resolving agents to resolve disubstituted BINOL derivatives. By modifying the substituents of the oxazoline unit of the chiral gold(III) catalysts, excellent enantioselectivity up to 99% ee in asymmetric catalysis has been achieved. Furthermore, we have expanded the scope of chiral gold(III) complexes to materials science by synthesizing chiral gold(III) amphiphile (GA) to show enhanced supramolecular helicities in aqueous media. Through counterion exchanges, supramolecular assembly transformations from lamellar structure to vesicles and nanotubes with significant supramolecular helicity enhancements have been demonstrated.

15300219.label: Project Objectives
15300219.value: We will develop efficient group coordinate algorithms for solving nonsmooth optimization problems with non-overlapping groups, by using special group structure of practical applications. We will establish comprehensive theoretical results on convergence rate and complexity bounds for regularization methods to solve nonsmooth optimization problems with group sparsity penalties. We will derive innovative first order and second order necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for local minimizers of nonsmooth optimization problems with group sparsity penalties. We will explore more theoretical properties of smoothing approximation functions for nonsmooth objective functions, such as the gradient consistency and Hessian consistency regarding first order and second order directional derivatives. We will extensively test the proposed regularization methods and compare them with the existing methods in terms of speed, accuracy, robustness and complexity. Real data from biology, imaging and signal processing will be used to test the efficiency of the new theory and algorithms.

15300219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300219.value: Numerous practical models arising from medical image analysis, statistical learning, signal processing, compressed sensing, gene selection, bioinformatics, share the feature of seeking a solution with group sparsity of a nonsmooth optimization problem. The solution is said to have group sparsity structure if its components are grouped together into several distinguishable index sets, and the components within some groups are all zero. The group structure is imperative in many statistical and machine learning cases in which the explanatory variables demonstrate high correlation that can be used to classify them into groups. In the setting of compressed sensing, group sparsity is referred to as block sparsity. In the last decade, many nonsmooth optimization models with group sparsity penalties appeared widely in the literature. Mathematically, these models have the difficulty of nondifferentiability and nonconvexity. Moreover, in the era with big data where the dimensionality of models increases rapidly, these group sparse optimization models usually have another common difficulty of high dimensionality. All these difficulties urge us to develop efficient optimization algorithms with affirmative theoretical supports. This project aims to systematically investigate the special structure of these problems and develop efficient optimization algorithms for some group sparse optimization models with strong application backgrounds, such as nonsmooth regression with group sparsity penalties. We will establish corresponding theoretical properties such as the convergence of these algorithms to first order stationary points, second order stationary points, local minimizers and global minimizers. Simulation studies will be conducted to evaluate developed algorithms and compare them with existing algorithms in terms of speed, accuracy and robustness. Real data from medical image processing and genomic research will be used to demonstrate the applications of the new theory and methods. The outcomes of this project will have a long-term and significant impact, because nonsmooth optimization problems with group sparsity penalties arise naturally from many applications in data science and urgently need efficient algorithms for implementation. 15300319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300319.value: In this proposal, the PI and his coworkers will study efficient algorithms for large-scale optimization problems that induce simultaneous structures in the solution. These models arise in various applications such as system realization and network structure identification, and induce structures in solutions by incorporating suitable regularizers. The regularizer involved is typically the sum of so-called "basic regularizers": these are convex or nonconvex functions whose proximal mappings are easy to compute. When the problem is convex, various splitting methods have been developed for solving these optimization problems, where each iteration only makes use of the proximal mappings of the basic regularizers involved. However, these methods are not guaranteed to converge in the presence of nonconvex basic regularizers. In this project, the PI and the two co-I's will develop efficient algorithms for these optimization problems, especially when nonconvex basic regularizers are involved. First, based on the recent work of the PI and one of the co-I's on the successive difference-of-convex approximation method, we plan to develop and study similar approximation methods for better efficiency and wider applicability. An improvement of these kind of algorithms may encourage the proposal of new models involving sums of nonconvex basic regularizers in applications. Second, based on the recent work of the PI and another co-I on the convergence analysis of the Douglas-Rachford splitting method in some nonconvex settings, we will analyze the convergence of some splitting methods for problems involving the sum of nonconvex basic regularizers. The techniques developed may help build a convergence analysis framework for general splitting methods in some nonconvex settings. 本項目將研究大規模帶並行結構優化問題的有效解法。此類問題常見於系統及網絡結構識別，並利用適當的正則函數辨識各類結構。正則函數一般為基礎正則函數的和：基礎正則函數的近似算子較易計算。目前常用的解法如分裂算法善用近似算子的運算，但只針對凸優化問題。本項目將循兩方面進行，並著重針對非凸帶並行結構優化問題提出有效算法。首先，我們將研究並改良已知有收歛性保証的逐步凸差逼近法，同時發展類似算法。另外，我們亦會分析分裂算法作用在非凸模型的收斂性。成果有望促進非凸帶並行結構優化模型的研究與發展。

15300319.label: Realisation of objectives
15300319.value: One of the goals of this project is to develop approximation techniques for solving a wide class of optimization problems for inducing simultaneous structures. In this regard, in the paper “Error bounds, facial residual functions and applications to the exponential cone”, we developed a general framework for deriving error bounds for conic feasibility problems (i.e., finding a point in the intersection of a cone and a given affine set) and apply that to obtaining error bounds for the exponential cone feasibility problem. We derived the desired error bound based on the facial structure of closed convex cone and a new object called 1-step facial residual function. The resulting error bound characterizes how well the intersection of cone and the affine set can be approximated by getting close to each of the two individual sets. Such error bounds lay a solid foundation for the evaluation of the performances of algorithms that attempt to obtain points lying simultaneously in the closed convex cone and any affine set that intersects the cone. We then specialized our findings to the exponential cone feasibility problems. In addition, in the recent paper “Doubly majorized algorithm for sparsity-inducing optimization problems with regularizer-compatible constraints” joint with one of the co-I’s, we studied an optimization model that requires both sparsity and order structure in the solution. Such models arise naturally in applications such as compressed sensing with order constraints and sparse time-lagged regression problems with block order constraints: the latter problems arise in estimation involving time-series-type data such as ozone concentration over a period. We applied the standard proximal gradient (PG) algorithm with a twist. Specifically, while the PG subproblems do not seem easy to solve, we exploit the absolute value symmetry in the constraint and the regularizer and further transform these problems into a form to which the PG algorithm can again be applied. However, for computational efficiency, we only apply one step of the PG algorithm to these transformed subproblems and immediately move on to the next iteration, yielding a variant of PG with highly inaccurately solved subproblems. Convergence to a new notion of stationary point was established, despite the crude approximation used when solving the subproblems. In summary, we have investigated some approximation techniques for optimization problems involving simultaneous structures. The other goal of the project is to extend splitting methods for inducing simultaneous structures in some nonconvex settings. In this regard, we studied in “Analysis and algorithms for some compressed sensing models based on L1/L2 minimization” an efficient optimization algorithm for compressed sensing problems with “hard” noise constraint: in other words, this problem requires the solution to be simultaneously sparse and respect the noise tolerance. Our development was based on an approximation technique known as moving-balls-approximation (MBA) technique, which was first introduced in 2010 and was then extensively studied in the literature. MBA can be viewed as a variant of the PG algorithm (also known as forward-backward splitting) applied to the constraint function. In addition, as mentioned above, the recent paper “Doubly majorized algorithm for sparsity-inducing optimization problems with regularizer-compatible constraints” joint with one of the co-I’s studied an inexact variant of the PG for solving a class of nonconvex problems. In summary, we have studied some new variants of splitting methods in some nonconvex setting for inducing simultaneous structures.

15300319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300319.value: Three papers were submitted and all of them have already been published (with one of them being published only online at the time of submission of this report). The first paper is “Error bounds, facial residual functions and applications to the exponential cone”, which was reported in the midterm progress report as a preprint and is now published in Mathematical Programming. This paper studies error bounds that characterize how well the intersection can be approximated by getting close to each of the constituent sets. The second paper is “Analysis and algorithms for some compressed sensing models based on L1/L2 minimization”. It was also reported in the midterm progress report as a preprint and is now published in SIAM Journal on Optimization. This paper studied an algorithm based on moving-balls-approximation techniques for finding sparse signals that respect the noise tolerance as a “hard” constraint. Finally, towards the end of the project period, a third paper “Doubly majorized algorithm for sparsity-inducing optimization problems with regularizer-compatible constraints”, joint with one of the co-I’s, was submitted. This paper is now published (online) in Computational Optimization and Applications. It studied a variant of PG which involves highly inexactly solved subproblems for finding sparse solutions that respect an order structure.

15300319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300319.value: There are several avenues for further development. First, other than the order constraint for each entry, it may be interesting to consider order constraints on the norm of subvectors, in the same spirit as Group Lasso penalty. In addition, additional structures such as sign constraints may be incorporated into compressed sensing problems and it will be interesting to see how the moving-balls-approximation based method can be extended to deal with these additional constraints. These are possible avenues for future research.

15300319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300319.value: In this project, the PI and his coworkers studied algorithms for handling some optimization problems that involve simultaneous structures. In details, we developed optimization methods based on techniques such as moving-balls-approximation and double majorization for handling simultaneous structures in some nonconvex settings. The techniques developed may lead to further splitting methods for optimization problems involving various structure inducing regularizers / constraints, and encourage the proposal of new models involving regularizers / constraints for inducing simultaneous structures in applications.

15300519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15300519.value: 相变层很薄的Allen-Cahn和Cahn-Hilliard方程的数值方法与分析

15300519.label: Project Objectives
15300519.value: We shall approximate the Cauchy problem of the Allen-Cahn equation in the whole space by an initial-boundary value problem in a convex polyhedral domain with the Dirichlet boundary condition. Then, we approximate the initial-boundary value problem by the BDF methods in time and finite element method in space, and establish an optimal-order error estimate for the numerical solution with explicit dependence on a small parameter ε describing the thickness of the phase transition layer. The reduction from whole space to a bounded domain generates an error in the boundary condition. The influence of boundary errors on numerical solutions will be studied in Objectives 2 and 3. We shall prove the weak maximum principle of finite element methods for elliptic equations with respect to boundary values, and the maximum-norm stability of finite element solutions in convex polyhedral domains. These results will be used to estimate the influence of the boundary error on the numerical solution for the Allen-Cahn equation studied in Objective 1. We shall prove the weak maximum principle of BDF time discretization methods for parabolic equations, and maximum-norm stability of fully discrete finite element methods for parabolic equations. These results will be used to estimate the influence of the boundary error on the numerical solution for the Allen-Cahn equation studied in Objective 1. We shall further develop arbitrarily high-order energy decaying time discretization methods for the Allen-Cahn equation based on the scalar auxiliary variable formulation. Rigorous proof will be presented for a discrete version of energy decay and high-order convergence of numerical solutions. Numerical experiments will be provided to illustrate the discrete energy decay and accuracy of the proposed methods.

15300519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300519.value: We shall develop high-order numerical methods for the initial-boundary value problems and Cauchy problems of Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations with a very thin phase transition zone, with backward difference formulae (BDF) in time and finite element methods in space. We shall establish optimal-order error estimates for the numerical solution with explicit dependence on the thickness of the phase transition layer, and investigate the rate of convergence of the numerical solution to an equilibrium state as time increases to infinity. The analysis of BDF methods for the Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard equations will utilize the Nevanlinna-Odeh multiplier technique combined with a time-dependent inner product constructed based on a spectrum estimate of the linearized Allen-Cahn operator. The reduction of the Cauchy problem from the whole space to a bounded domain will generate an error in the boundary condition. To estimate the influence of the boundary error on the numerical solution, we shall establish the maximum-norm stability of BDF methods with respect to the boundary value. 我们将用时间上的倒向差分公式（BDF）和空间上的有限元方法，对相变区域很薄的Allen-Cahn方程和Cahn-Hilliard方程的初边值问题和Cauchy问题发展高阶数值方法，建立显式依赖于相变层厚度的最优阶误差估计。对Allen-Cahn方程的BDF方法的分析将利用Nevanlinna-Odeh乘数技术，结合基于线性化Allen-Cahn算子的谱估计构造的时间相关内积。将柯西问题从整个空间简化为有界域，会在边界条件下产生误差。为了估计边界误差对数值解的影响，我们将建立边界值的BDF方法的最大范数稳定性。

15300619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300619.value: 十多年來，HfO2作為高k柵極電介質在集成電路（IC）工業中的場效應晶體管（FET）器件中取代SiO2取得了巨大成功。最近，還發現​​HfO2是鐵電的並且在FET結構中表現出負電容效應。這使得HfO2更具吸引力，因為負電容效應導致FET的較低工作電壓，因此有利於邏輯和存儲器IC器件的較低功耗。 HfO2對於擴展到鐵電隨機存取存儲器（FeRAM）應用也是非常有吸引力的，其中HfO2柵極介電層中的上下極化產生1和0個存儲狀態。然而，HfO2鐵電性的起源仍然是一個令人費解的問題，因為其鐵電性質不同於傳統的鈣鈦礦氧化物如BaTiO3的鐵電體，並且喚醒效應（僅在多次操作循環後出現大鐵電性）仍然是一個大問題。要解決。因此，HfO2鐵電性的研究是半導體工業中一個迫切需要解決的問題。 另一方面，當考慮將HfO2應用於柔性電子設備中時，利用其在柔性和可穿戴基板中的FET和FeRAM應用的高k特性和鐵電特性，還有更多需要解決的問題和豐富的物理學習。雲母正在成為柔性器件的良好候選者，並且通過在雲母上外延生長的合適氧化物電極，可以生長高質量的HfO2膜（甚至外延）。除了透明性和柔韌性的優點之外，由於原子層之間的范德瓦爾斯連接，雲母的彎曲僅引起非常小的應變量。這將使HfO2在雲母上的電子特性相對穩定，防止彎曲過程中的參數漂移，但可以在該平台上研究HfO2鐵電性的彎曲依賴性及其鐵電性的起源。 在這個項目中，我們將進行以下研究： （1）摻雜的HfO2（如La和Zr摻雜）在雲母基底上的沉積。通過控制退火條件和摻雜，可以實現優化的鐵電性。將表徵HfO2薄膜的微觀結構及其晶體結構，並研究鐵電性的起源。 （2）HfO2膜的介電性能將基於金屬氧化物半導體（MOS）結構表徵，其中底部電極用作半導體層。沉積在雲母上的半導體氧化物層將用作底部電極。 （3）研究了HfO2鐵電性的彎曲誘導應變依賴性。該研究將為HfO2鐵電的起源提供進一步的證據。

15300619.label: Realisation of objectives
15300619.value: using the combination of X-ray diffraction (XRD) associate with Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM), we reveal the epitaxial growth of Al-doped HfO2 possessing various phase structures on different oriented SrTiO3 substrates. The well-oriented films show different ferroelectricity indicated by piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM). The film grown on the (111) SrTiO3 substrate shows the largest electromechanical effect. These results, with the analyses of structural characterizations, demonstrate the orientation control of phase transitions and ferroelectricity in Al-doped HfO2 thin films. This work demonstrates the substrate orientation driven phase transitions and tuned ferroelectric properties in Al-doped HfO2 thin films, providing an alternative approach to manipulate the crystal structure and ferroelectric performance of HfO2-based ferroelectrics. Ferroelectricity in dopant-free HfO2 thin films deposited by PLD has been observed. Without subsequent annealing and confined layer, by only adjusting the deposited temperature, oxygen pressure and thickness, the growth window of ferroelectric HfO2 is mapped and the ferroelectric phase and properties can be tailored. It is revealed that the ferroelectricity of dopant-free HfO2 thin films is determined by the fraction of orthorhombic phase. The HfO2 film with 7.4 nm thickness has the optimal remanent polarization of 14.7 μC/cm2. In the deposited process of HfO2 thin films by PLD, the concentration of defects and grain size strongly influence the formation of metastable ferroelectric phase and the polarization value. Our work provides a route for the preparation of high-quality ferroelectric HfO2 thin films, promising for the application of HfO2 thin films in nonvolatile memory devices. HfO2 thin films have been successfully deposited on mica substrate with top electrode and the ferroelectricity including wave-up effect were studied.
