15300619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300619.value: We fabricated Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) FE thin films on various high-κ dielectric SLs, including ZrO2, HfO2, (HfO2)0.75(Al2O3)0.25 (HAO), and Al2O3, and investigated their microstructures, ferroelectricity, and memory characteristics in the MFIS devices. The results show that the nucleation and growth of the FE orthorhombic phase in HZO films are affected not only by the surface energy but also by the microstructure of the high-κ SL. Additionally, we clarified the role of the high-κ SL on the memory characteristics of the MFIS devices, which were reasonably explained by the accurately calculated interface electric field. Finally, we realized a good tradeoff between the FE polarization and interface charge injection in the MFIS device with HAO high-κ SL, demonstrating a large FE window (> 1.0 V), excellent retention (> 1.6×10^4 s), and endurance cycles (> 10^5). The results will provide valuable ideas to overcome the challenge of endurance in the Fe-HfO2-based FeFET and contribute to developing other high-performance electron devices with Fe-HfO2 films grown on a dielectric SL.

15300619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300619.value: With the results we achieved and understanding we reached, this HfO2 thin film materials may be applied to microwave devices for 5G/6G communications.

15300619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300619.value: These project demonstrated our ability to grow high-quality HfO2 ferroelectric thin films. We have studied the deposition of HfO2 on Mica substrate with different strain states and found out that, the bending of Mica as a flexible substrate does not change the ferroelectricity; this property enables the application of HfO2 ferroelectric thin films in flexible devices. With the results we achieved and understanding we reached, this HfO2 thin film materials may be applied to microwave devices for 5G/6G communications.

15300819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300819.value: 在多相催化化學中，過渡金屬納米團簇（NCs）扮演著非常重要的角色。它們具有高原子經濟性和獨特的量子尺寸效應。除了使用傳統的配位方法之外，它們也能以沸石之類的多孔材料為基得到商業應用。最近的文獻指出，多核NCs能解決許多長期的催化問題。例如，二核和三核銅氧NCs能將甲烷催化成甲醇。然而，製備由過渡金屬製成的NCs仍然具有巨大操作上的挑戰性。這項目的目的是開發一種精確合成中後期3d過渡金屬多核NC的方法，以廣泛應用於催化系統。 申請人團隊在設計沸石催化劑方面擁有專業知識。在前期工作中，我們成功製備了以ZSM-5沸石為基中的三核Cu3 NCs（Cu3 / ZSM-5）。此合成方法具創新性，以順序方式在沸石中成長NCs。 基於我們前期工三核Cu3 / ZSM-5，我們將在ZSM-5和MOR沸石中製備單金屬和雜化NCs （如鐵鈷鎳銅鋅等）。通過定制NC的結構，我們將研究其催化性能，比如甲烷轉換為甲醇。通過巧妙地設計金屬絡合物前體，我們將製備具有可精細調節的局部結構的NCs。同時，本項目將使用專門設計的毛細管反應器，通過原位同步輻射X射線粉末衍射以闡明其構效關係。 本項目有十分重要的科學意義，從原子層面合理設計NCs，其電子和結構特性更可根據其尺寸，粘合和協調進行微調。此順序製備方式不僅能應用於沸石，而且還可以對其他多孔材料進行精細內腔設計，更有助開發更優越的催化系統。

15300819.label: Realisation of objectives
15300819.value: Scope of Investigation Undertaken The scope of investigation undertaken in this study involves the precise synthesis, characterization, and catalytic applications of 3d transition metal multinuclear nanoclusters encapsulated in ZSM-5 zeolites. The investigation aims to address the following key aspects: 1. Methodology Development: - Develop a methodology for the precise synthesis of mid-to-late monometallic 3d transition metal multinuclear nanoclusters in ZSM-5 zeolites and related structures such as metal-organic frameworks. - Investigate the effects of various synthesis parameters, such as temperature, reaction time, precursor concentrations, and zeolite framework modifications, on the formation and stability of the nanoclusters. 2. Preparation of Hybrid Nanoclusters: - Prepare related hybrid nanoclusters by introducing additional components, such as promoters or dopants, to modify the catalytic properties of the multinuclear nanoclusters. - Explore the influence of these hybrid structures on the catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability of the resulting materials. 3. Characterization of Nanoclusters: - Utilize advanced characterization techniques, including powder X-ray diffraction, and spectroscopic methods (e.g., EXAFS, XPS, FTIR, XANES), to reveal the atomic and structural information of the multinuclear nanoclusters within the zeolite frameworks. - Investigate the distribution, size, composition, and coordination environment of the nanoclusters to gain insights into their formation mechanisms and interactions with the zeolite host. 4. Design of Catalytic Systems: - Rationally design the local nanocluster structure to optimize catalytic performance for selected reactions. - Investigate the structure-activity relationship by correlating the atomic and structural information of the nanoclusters with their catalytic properties. - Explore the influence of factors such as cluster size, metal composition, and coordination environment on catalytic activity, selectivity, and stability. 5. Catalytic Applications: - Assess the catalytic performance of the synthesized 3d transition metal multinuclear nanoclusters in relevant reactions - Evaluate the activity, selectivity, and stability of the nanocluster catalysts and compare them with conventional catalysts or benchmark systems. - Investigate the underlying mechanisms and reaction pathways involved in the catalytic processes facilitated by the nanocluster catalysts. Results achieved The project objectives have been fully achieved by the following 8 example publications. 1. A rational study on the geometric and electronic properties of single-atom catalysts for enhanced catalytic performance (Nanoscale, 2020, 12(45): 23206-23212.) 2. Guest-anion-induced rotation-restricted emission in UiO-66-NH2 and advanced structure elucidation (Chemistry of Materials, 2021, 33(13): 5422-5429.) 5. Designing the electronic and geometric structures of single-atom and nanocluster catalysts (Journal of Materials Chemistry A, 2021, 9(35): 18773-18784.) 6. Copper dual-atom catalyst mediated C3–H amination of indoles at room temperature (Catalysis Science & Technology, 2022, 12(17): 5390-5396.) 7. Atomically dispersed 3d metal bimetallic dual-atom catalysts and classification of the structural descriptors. (Chem Catalysis, 2022, 2(9): 2346-2363.) 8. 15300819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300819.value: The objectives of the research have been fully realized through the following achievements: 1. Development of a methodology for the precise synthesis of mid-to-late monometallic 3d transition metal multinuclear nanoclusters encapsulated in ZSM-5 zeolites: A stepwise assembly strategy was developed, utilizing the principles of solid-state chemistry and coordination chemistry. By using 2-methylimidazole as an assembly agent, multiple mid-to-late 3d transition metal ions were assembled in a stepwise manner, resulting in the synthesis of monometallic nanoclusters with controllable metal nuclearity (e.g., Cu2 and Cu3) supported on zeolites. 2. Preparation of related hybrid nanoclusters: The approach was expanded to study heterometallic nanoclusters. A successful example is the Cu-Zn nanocluster supported on ZSM-5 bimetallic sample, which exhibits structural features similar to those of native Cu,Zn-containing superoxide dismutase (Cu,Zn-SOD). The zeolitic framework provides a rigid support for the immobilization of foreign metal species and an isolated cavity for effective catalysis. The stepwise synthetic approach allows the preparation of different nanocluster combinations based on mid-to-late 3d transition metals. 3. Revelation of atomic and structural information of the nanoclusters with respect to the zeolite frameworks: Various techniques, including synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), resonant X-ray diffraction (RXRD), and extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS), were employed to determine the atomic and structural information of the supported nanoclusters. RXRD, unique to synchrotron facilities, was used to determine the crystal structures of heterometallic samples, such as Cu-Zn supported on ZSM-5, which contains atoms with low electronic contrast. Rietveld refinement and control procedures were employed to ensure the accuracy and sensitivity of the resonant SXRD refinement. 4. Rational design of the local nanocluster structure for selected catalytic reactions and revelation of the structure-activity relationship: The nuclearity of Cu atoms at the active sites was investigated through model reactions, such as the photocatalytic reforming of formic acid over related nanoclusters supported on UiO-66 (Zr-based metal-organic framework). The different metal nuclearities resulted in substantial differences in the adsorption modes and catalytic reactivity. The fine control of structural descriptors allowed for sophisticated control of product selectivity. A rational structure-reactivity interplay was discerned, considering surface chemistry, geometric structure, reaction energetics, and catalytic properties. These achievements demonstrate the successful realization of the research objectives and provide valuable insights into the synthesis, characterization, and catalytic properties of nanoclusters encapsulated in zeolite frameworks.

15300819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300819.value: From the extensive collection of studies, it is evident that the catalytic properties of nanoclusters are strongly influenced by their electronic and geometric structures. The electronic structures of NCs are particularly affected by four key parameters: elemental variation, nuclearity control, metal-support interaction, and ligand coordination. It is anticipated that the precise synthesis of multi-metallic multinuclear nanoclusters with tunable electronic and geometric structures will be a crucial focus of future research. This direction aligns closely with the concept of single-atom catalysis systems. By harnessing the synergistic effects between neighboring metal nuclei, many long-standing challenges that require the use of multiple catalytic centers can be addressed. For example, multinuclear nanoclusters can serve as highly effective catalysts in cross-coupling reactions due to the presence of multiple adjacent metal nuclei, facilitating co-adsorption of reaction substrates for subsequent co-activation. Effectively, we have achieved high reactivity and selectivity in a series of catalytic reactions, including (but not limited to): Huisgen azide-alkyne ‘click’ cycloaddition Superoxide dismutation Selective amination of indoles Direct amination of phenols Ethane/propane dehydrogenation Methanol steam reforming to release hydrogen Thanks to the promising progress, we are motivated to further exploration the applications of this interesting class of atomic materials.

15300819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300819.value: The development of a creative approach enables the genome engineering of atomically precise metal nanoclusters. By utilizing the underlying principles of solid-state chemistry (via microporous confinement) and coordination chemistry (using a di-basic linker to connect two different metal cations), multiple mid-to-late 3d/4d/5d transition metals within various porous materials can be modularly assembled. The di-basic linker can be subsequently removed, yielding metal nanoclusters with different chemical properties. This creative assembly approach has been specifically highlighted by Chem and Chem Catalysis, where precise control of the distribution and local environment of each active site can be achieved. This project has enabled surface, solid-state and coordination chemists to develop more extensive, more cohesive and more appropriate frameworks to rationalise the electronic and geometric structures of these atomically synthesised entities, which further provides the necessary details for the identification of chemical trends and benchmark quantum sciences.

15300919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15300919.value: Numerous kinds of metal-DOTA complexes are known to show excellent stability under physiological conditions, hence making them preeminent for use in biomedical applications. Notable examples are the use of [GdDOTA]− as a contrast agent in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), with diverse literature studies showing use of DOTA and its derivatives in radiopharmaceuticals as well as fluorescence microscopy for diagnosis and therapy. Our proposal focus on a broad design based on chiral DOTA derivatives and utilization of their Gd(III) complexes as contrast agents for MRI as well as for use with radionuclides. In contrast to previous works the derivatization are oriented on the cyclen skeleton and a few more chiral DOTA-like ligands are developed for more specific functional imaging purpose, such as a hepatobiliary MRI contrast agent. From our prior ground work, the conformation of the Gd(III) complexes caused by the chiral derivatization leads to exceptional stability of the complexes as well as higher abundance of TSAP isomer when compared to the parent GdDOTA, and subsequently improves the MRI properties. The conserved formation of the cyclen geometry also promotes fast complexation for radionuclides and our latest designs with conjugatable functions also affords the possibility to produce a class of targeting radiotherapeutic chelators. To date, there is still no perfect contrast agents even after decades of extensive work in the area. With the evolution of more advance technology there is an ever increasing demand of more multifunctional contrast agents to match the technology. Hence, the field of biomedical imaging agents are forever expanding and in demand, either for safety reasons or for better sensitivity and targeted selectivity. Our key goals here are to develop a probe that can be a better hepatobiliary imaging agent with improved stability for MRI as well as develop better chelators for radio-metals which can be used in PET imaging or in radio-therapeutics. In our compound designs we have considered synthetic methodology and conjugation routes to make our probes to be biocompatible, as well as have high stability and have conjugatable functional groups for necessary vector targeting specificity. 15300919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15300919.value: The major outcome of this project is that we further developed lanthanide chelators with different chiral substituents on the cyclen backbone to explore the coordination chemistry to enable them to be more biocompatible for imaging applications. Simultaneously, we also optimised our designs to generate compounds with a conjugatable handle for targeting vectors. In our studies with the many newly developed chelators, we shown improved imaging functions as well as retained good kinetics and thermodynamic stability of our compounds which are crucial in terms of safety considerations as a diagnostic agent. In our developed chiral platform design, we show that we can utilise the chiral substituents on the macrocyclic backbone to enhance biocompatibility without the need of modifying the pendant arms which often compromises the stability. We also shown that the chiral substituents on the backbone, offers a more rigid macrocyclic cavity for metal chelation as well as a better control of the coordination isomers formed during the complexation especially when compared to the parent DOTA macrocyclic ligand. In one study we showed that by fine tuning the structural modification on the peripheral, we also can improve the overall relaxivity property which is important for a T1 MRI contrast agent. In this work, we show that besides consideration of just the inner coordination sphere, the second-sphere and outer-sphere relaxation (often neglected), can play an important role in improving the overall relativity of an MRI contrast agent. In this project, we delivered several publications in high impact journals -showcasing the potential use of our lanthanide complexes in various imaging applcations such as PET, MRI and CPL. The papers are titled as below- “Design and synthesis of chiral DOTA-based MRI contrast agents with remarkable relaxivities” “Design of Functional Chiral Cyclen-Based Radiometal Chelators for Theranostics “Unusual Magnetic Field Responsive Circularly Polarized Luminescence Probes with Highly Emissive Chiral Europium(III) Complexes” “Multimodal Visualization of Bioorthogonal Systems by Off–On Luminescence and Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging”

15300919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15300919.value: Based on these chiral metal chelators, further development will be focus on more precise targeting by developing a universal strategy for ease of appending antibodies or specific targeting vectors to these developed platforms to enable them to be used in theranostics or for radioopharmaceuticals. More proof of concept work will be done by appending these lanthanide complexing agents to known targets such as PSMA and Somatostatin. The benefits of these chiral metal chelators are its versatility to form complexes with a wide range of metals that are commonly employed in diagnostics such as Lu and Ga used in PET and Gd in MRI. Taking in account of this advantage, future work will also be directed in further optimising these chelators to develop designs for use in multimodal imaging – such as PET/MRI. Simultaneously work will also be directed to explore the radiolabeling chemistry of these chelators.

15300919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15300919.value: Our research work paves the way for further development of the use of lanthanide compounds for clinical translation. From our studies, we shown the potential use of our chelating agents with lanthanides for applications in both PET, MRI and optical imaging. In terms of comparing to the currently commercial agents,e.g MRI – where most compounds are Gd based, we show that there are still scope for further improvement in terms of both performance (imaging capabilities) as well as specificity – being disease orientated (or in personalised medicine). With the development of these stable chelators, we show that lanthanide compounds can serve as a platform for exploring further in the direction of therapeutics such as in radio-medicine, as the chelators are suitable for various types of radioisotopes.

15301119.value: 线性二次鲁棒协同优化问题: 软约束方法

15301119.label: Project Objectives
15301119.value: To formulate uncertainty (disturbance) of team optimization (TO). To calibrate appropriate disturbance characteristics (in particular, common noise, soft-constraint and its attenuation level) of formulation (1). Considering (2), to study robust team optimization (ROTO) by deriving related decentralized team optimal strategies. Based on (3), to verify the asymptotic team (social) optima of ROTO strategy derived. Given (1)-(4), to apply theoretical ROTO results to some real applications. For example, inter-banking robust operations.

15301119.label: Realisation of objectives
15301119.value: All objective have been effectively realized in this project. Specifically, we formally introduce and formulate some interesting drift dynamics uncertainty, that is called disturbance, into the recently well investigated mean-field team setting. We also present various real applications as solid motivation to our uncertain ROTO formulation. We also carefully examine the suitable characters in our robust team ROTO formulation along with the uncertainty, in particular, the soft-constraint attenuation parameter is well calibrated with some real backgrounds and selection criteria. The decentralized mean-field team with disturbance is derived using maximum principle method. Some forward-backward mean-field system is formulated to characterize the consistency condition in presence of uncertainty. The wellposedness of such consistency condition system has also been well investigated. We also verify the asymptotic optimality of derived decentralized mean-field team strategies suing the perturbation analysis. The convergence rate is also verified to calibrate the performance of derived near optimal robust team controls. Last but not least, some real applications are well investigated using our theoretical outcomes. Our research also open some new application potential frontier to cooperative team and other decision making in real world.

15301119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301119.value: We published a verity of journal papers based on investigation of this project. All objectives are fulfilled within project's investigation period. We have realized the robust ROTO decentralized strategy and its sensitivity analysis based on various underlying parameters turns to be interesting. Keep this in mind, we consider the related new optimality in team coordination and its consequence to the related social optima. We also find some new types of forward-backward consistency condition system, and it follows that their wellposedness is new and has its own interest. We examine the relevant topics in details. Some by-product includes some new discounting, and monotonicity conditions under which the existence and uniqueness of forward-backward stochastic system. Based on this project, it is also found that the robust team policy differs substantially to the policy in case of model certainty. In particular, some new backward component should be introduced into the final optimal system to respond the possible adversarial nature. Also, the soft constraint attenuation parameter also plays some crucial role in the decentralized robust team strategy design.

15301119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301119.value: Future developments from the research of this project include more sensitivity analysis of the soft constraint parameter to resulting optimal policy performance. Also, the possible to introduce more realistic constraint bound into the disturbance, and confine its energy into a more practical range. this has some interesting real application potential in case of the big data and learning scheme under which we may gain more insightful and reasonable knowledge to the underlying disturbance or uncertainty.

15301119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301119.value: We investigate the robust decision design in case the underlying dynamic system is subject to possible modeling variations. As a result, we derive and verify some robust team decision under such model uncertainty. The real world has more or less uncertainty especially in the evolution of the dynamic system. One typical example is the disturbance into the drift evolution that appears quite often in financial, economic and engineering systems. one example is the uncertain growth rate in production and revenue planning. In this case, it is really necessary to introduce and analyze the related worst-case strategy. On other hand, today's world has many large-population system in which numerous team decision makers may apply some cooperative decisions, but are subject to the same underlying disturbance or model uncertainty. In this case, it becomes interesting to examine the robust decision in team formation, that is ROTO in current project. We successfully derive some reasonable robust team decision design using soft-constraint method. This robustness design may help to solve many real decision problem in which the model uncertainty is given.

15301519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15301519.value: 复杂数据结构的函数型回归及其在ADNI疾病人群的应用

15301519.label: Project Objectives
15301519.value: For the general high-dimensional functional additive regression (FAR) model with heteroscedasticity, we will develop a penalized functional sparse asymmetric least square regression so as to implement variable selection and estimation simultaneously. We plan to give the rigorous theoretical derivation for linear and nonlinear FAR models along the line of functional principal component and projection, respectively. We will make inference for a series of problems including the potential strong oracle or oracle properties, the convergence rates, the bounds for the estimation error for the corresponding number of selected predictors, and so on. We aim to develop a quantile-based functional classifier. Practically, a fast algorithm will be developed for selecting a large number of tuning parameters efficiently. Theoretically, the consistency and optimality of the proposed classifier will be studied. For the nonparametric random effect model, we plan to design new Bayesian methodologies for functional clustering and estimation simultaneously. Starting from the Pólya Urn and stick-breaking representations, respectively, we will develop new nested Dirichlet-Beta process prior. Gibbs sampling algorithms will also be formulated. To maximize the utility of the models and methodologies in Objectives 1-3, user-friendly computer programs or libraries will be developed for the researchers and practitioners from neuroimaging and neurological disease fields. Clearly, the objectives only reflect part of the possible developments to analyze date from the ADNI study. During the course of this project, we expect to address additional and important issues as they arise.

15301519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15301519.value: 腦部影像與神經系統的疾病的診斷的最新進展產生了龐大，複雜，及高維度的函數型數據。相應的，揭示諸如神經疾病的發展狀態之類的臨床與神經心理學的基因表現型與諸如影像測量這樣的函數型生物標記的關係，變得非常重要。作為一個主要的數據來源，發起於2004年的阿茨海默症神經影像學倡議(ADNI),在集結多站點數據，致力於研究阿茨海默症（AD）的進化和提高AD的預防與治療上，具有全球性的影響。在ADNI研究中，異質態數據及復雜性數據結構對統計學家們提出了新的挑戰，尤其在函數型回歸這個領域裡去建立新模型和發展新方法。本項目旨在解決那些挑戰。 首先，在對AD進展的評分時，人們需要從大量的函數型生物標記中選出重要的標記和評估這些標記是如何影響到AD的進展。與此同時，來自於多站點的數據可能會有異質性分佈。我們提出一個相當廣義的能包容異質性的高維函數型可加回歸模型。我們將發展一套帶懲罰項的函數型稀疏非對稱最小二乘回歸來同步選變量和估計，並在理論上推導出模型選擇的強oracle性質。這任務既重要又艱難。 其次 臨床醫生需要對AD的狀態進行正確分類，基於從大量的函數型生物標記提取的信息，來判斷認知正常，輕微受損（MCI），或者患有AD。已有的函數型數據方法或者需要較強的假設條件，或者對厚尾分佈敏感。我們意在通過分位數函數來發展穩健的函數型分類器。這個新方法預期，在相對溫和的理論假設下，以低的錯分率對一個新的函數型生物標記進行分類標籤。 最後，ADNI疾病人群研究借助多中心的交叉信息，因而也產生了數據聚類的需要。發展穩健的新模型和方法去刻畫與評估數值型與函數型生物標記如何联合影響從MCI態發展成AD的失效時間是挺有裨益的。我們提出一類新的能包含聚類結構的非參數隨機影響模型，其中心思想是發展有效的貝葉斯技術用於減輕分層結構造成的繁重計算負擔。為了解決推斷中的難點，我們提出一個新的以Beta過程做先驗的嵌套Dirichlet過程和相關的MCMC算法。這樣的嵌套Bayesian過程計算有效，在實用上可行。

15301519.label: Realisation of objectives
15301519.value: Objective 1: Objective 1 is a HEAVY project objective. We have proposed a series of high-dimensional functional additive heteroscedastic regression models (FAHM) that both consider the continuous image representation and the heterogeneity among functional data, and have resolved the inferential theories based on the nonlinear coupled sparse asymmetric least squares with LASSO or nonconvex algorithms, which include the linear and homogeneous scenarios as special cases. This objective has been classified into eight scenarios in detail. We have completed the theoretical proofs of all scenarios. Thanks to the support of the GRF, we have set up a high-performance workstation so that numerical computing efficiency has been greatly improved. By far, we have completed the numerical experiments of the other seven scenarios, aside from the complicated scenario of the nonlinearity of the functions of single indices and heteroscedasticity. For the nonlinear optimal algorithm, the computational costs and times increase rapidly as the sample size and number of covariates increase. As a result, we may need more time to complete the numerical analysis part. The PI and her team (Co-I: Prof. Yehua Li co-leading the progress, two postdoc fellows successively: Dr. Haiqiang Ma focusing on the theory, and Dr. Xu Zhang focusing on computing) have regular and irregular online discussions to carry on the project toward completion and submission of the manuscript. The target journal is AOS. After the manuscript is published, we will still acknowledge the strong support of this specific GRF project for our work. The workstation offered by GRF not only serves this project but also contributes to my ongoing GRF project. During the processing of image data in Objective 1, we have extended this objective to two new works: Extension I: Motivated by the ADNI fMRI dataset (4D image) in the original objective, which mathematically is recorded as a 4D tensor. we extend the objective to statistical learning of tensor-variate. We have completed this extension. We have developed two sets of tensor PCA variants to estimate the components in the low-rank signal under the Tucker tensor factor model. We have established the inferential theory of the proposed estimators and illustrated how the proposed estimations can work in tensor reconstruction, and clustering for independent video and dependent economic datasets, respectively. This work has been published in SCIENCE CHINA Mathematics. Extension II: We have proposed a new nonlinear regression that relates multiple responses (multi-label) to ultra-widefield (UWF) fundus images of both eyes (OU) through convolutional neural network (CNN). Myopia screening using cutting-edge UWF fundus imaging is potentially significant for ophthalmic outcomes. To tackle such 3D medicinal images, we have developed a statistical method to extract information to harness AI model by proposing a framework of copula-enhanced adapter CNN, which learns with OU UWF fundus images (OUCopula) for joint prediction of multiple clinical scores. We have shown that OUCopula can far exceed the performance of models constructed for single-eye inputs. This work has been published in the Proceedings of the Thirty-Third International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence. Objective 2: We have successfully completed the objective 2. It is included in the thesis of the graduated PhD student (Dr. Sheng Xu) under my supervision. We have first finished the quantile-based classifier for univariate functional classification tasks and extended the proposed classifier to high-dimensional cases to be a state-of-the-art technique. We have developed an enhanced iterative hard-thresholding algorithm by adapting the non-monotone proximal gradient method under the Cox model. We have given a rigorous theory proof. The advantages of our proposed work have been demonstrated by numerical studies and illustrated by the diffuse large B-cell lymphoma data example. This work has been published in Computational Statistics. Objective 3: We have completed the objective 3. We proposed a generalized share frailty model that includes both parametric and nonparametric frailty random effects and models the dependency among functional random effects through the dependent Dirichlet process. We have developed a survival-function version of the ANOVA dependent Dirichlet process to model the dependency among the baseline survival functions. The posterior sampling is implemented by the No-U-Turn sampler in Stan, a contemporary Bayesian computing tool, automatically. We have validated the proposed model by analysis of the bladder cancer recurrence data. My graduated PhD student (Dr. Chong Zhong) accomplished the part of this work and is the lead author. All works have been invited to publish two book chapters at IntechOpen with the book name Computational Statistics and Applications. From the viewpoint of Bayesian analysis, we have extended this original objective to other works. Extension III: Motivated by the stumbling block that the multi-modal posterior under unidentified nonparametric models yields poor mixing of Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), we have conceptualized a prior informativeness threshold that is essentially the variance of posterior modes and expressed by the uncertainty hyperparameters of nonparametric priors. The threshold plays the role of a lower bound of the within-chain MCMC variance to ensure MCMC mixing, and engines prior modification through hyperparameter tuning to descend the mode variance. Our proposed method achieved MCMC mixing and outperformed existing approaches in survival predictions. This work has been done by my graduated PhD student (Dr. Chong Zhong) and the work has been submitted and is under review in JASA. Objective 4: For Objective 1, the numerical simulations are in progress, we have completed the R programs for 8 algorithms. The procedure for Objectives 2 and 3 is pretty fast, and an R package is ready. Objective 5: During the course of this project, COVID-19 spreads around the world. This motivated us to study some statistical research on COVID-19. We have formulated a new infectious dynamic model for forecasting the COVID-19 pandemic within the human mobility network, named the SaucIR-model. We have employed dynamic modeling of population flow in the model in order that spatial effects can be incorporated effectively. We forecasted the spread of accumulated confirmed cases in some provinces of mainland China and other countries that experienced severe infection during the period from late February to early May 2020. This work has been published in Statistics and its Interface. In addition, motivated by diagnosing the COVID-19 disease using two-dimensional (2D) image biomarkers from computed tomography (CT) scans, we have proposed a novel latent matrix-factor regression model to predict responses that may come from an exponential distribution family. The proposed approach can be implemented conveniently. Through the application to a real COVID-19 dataset, the proposed approach has been shown to predict efficiently the COVID-19. This work has been published in Statistics in Medicine. Besides the academic journal, the PI has organized three discussions on three special issues in Statistics and It Interface, Computational Statistics and Data Analysis, and Frontiers in Big Data.

15301519.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301519.value: The completed project has led to fruitful research outcomes, including six peer-reviewed papers, three book chapters, one paper under review, three editorials for the special issue, two M.Phil. students trained to have obtained M.Phil. in statistics, and one Ph.D. student trained to have obtained Ph.D. in statistics. The major findings are the realization and extensions of the objectives, which demonstrate the potential of advanced statistical tools for complicated structural data analysis in biomedical research. These findings pave the way for future innovations in handling high-dimensional and complicated datasets across various scientific fields.

15301519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301519.value: The research conducted in this project lays a robust foundation for further development in several key areas. For example, we have conducted some research on medical image data. The medical image data become more and more widespread in the statistical community. Since the medical image data can be represented by a matrix-variate observation, further investigation into medical image data can consider statistical modeling and inference for high-dimensional matrix-variate observations. A potential development involves extending the statistical model related to the matrix to accommodate more complex image data structures, such as those found in multi-modal imaging studies. By integrating statistical methods with artificial intelligence (AI), we can extract more complex information from medical image data to identify and validate biomarkers that are crucial for early diagnosis. Through this research, we will prove to all that statistics can harness AI and provide a more valuable view of disease.

15301519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301519.value: The project aims to develop some novel statistical regression and extensions for complicated data, especially in health and medicine, to conduct analysis and prediction. For disease gene data, we proposed a functional ANOVA test procedure to screen out new variant genes related to Alzheimer's disease and detected the KAZN gene significantly at GWAS level (10e-7). For UWF imaging (3D) data, we employed CNN (nonlinear multilevel function) to relate multi-labels to UWF images of both eyes (OU) to improve the myopia screening prediction significantly. For COVID-19 data, by diagnosing the COVID-19 disease using image (2D) biomarkers from CT scans, we proposed a latent generalized matrix regression to predict and discriminate efficiently. In addition, we established an infectious dynamic model for forecasting confirmed cases of COVID-19 pandemic and early involved asymptomatic into compartment. The fANOVA test is the first nonparametric test for functional data. The OUCoupla is the first to use OU fundus images jointly in AI modeling in ophthalmology. In the analysis of COVID-19, the LaGMaR is fast and efficient due to being tuning-free. Our project involves many images, which also pave the path toward a future where image data leads to the field of AI and achieves statistics harness AI.

15301719.label: Project Objectives
15301719.value: To develop ligand sets for chemo- and enantioselective intramolecular ruthenium-nitrene C-H amination: We will prepare some defined arene-ruthenium complexes coordinating with ligands bearing electron-donating and -withdrawing substituents. Their reactivity toward nitrene C-H amination will be examined, and their chemo-, regio- and enantioselectivites will be analyzed and correlated with various electronic and steric parameters. To design new chiral arene-ruthenium complexes for broadly applicable enantioselective intramolecular nitrene C-H amination: Based on the structure-reactivity model developed in this study, we would design new chiral ligands with desirable steric and electronic properties for highly enantioselective nitrene C-H amination. It is hoped that a catalytic system of predictable chemo- and regioselectivity would be developed. To develop chemo- and regioselective intermolecular metal-nitrene C-H amination at distal secondary C-H bonds: Having developed a working model for intramolecular asymmetric C-H amination, we would pursue a more challenging intermolecular amination problem. Non-covalent interaction will be examined as a means to stabilize the transition state for intermolecular reactions. The reactivity of arene-ruthenium complexes bearing motifs for non-covalent interactions that bind to the polar functional groups on the hydrocarbon substrates will be examined for intermolecular C-H amination.

15301719.value: 手性γ-内酰胺普遍存在于生物活性分子中（例如：乳胞素）以及具有治疗作用的药物分子中（例如：维加巴丁）。传统的方法可以通过不对称氢化和共轭加成α，β-不饱和内酰胺构建β-取代的γ-内酰胺。但是对化学家来说，能否寻找到一种更高效、更直接方法（例如：直接着修饰γ-内脂周边的不活泼的C(sp3)-H）来构建手性γ-内酰胺显得尤为迫切。近期我们的研究发现频哪醇类的-钌络合物能有效地活化C(sp3)-H键，并且能得到理想的98% ee值。在这里我们的计划是设计一系列的具有手性中心的钌络合物。然后通过钌-氮卡宾直接插入不活泼的C(sp3)-H来实现更高效，更经济的手性γ-内酰胺合成。

15301719.label: Realisation of objectives
15301719.value: [1] Further to our development of the (arene)ruthenium-catalyzed intramolecular gamma-selective aliphatic C–H bond amidation for enantioselective gamma-lactams synthesis, we turned our attention to exploring the analogous regioselective arene C–H bond amidations. With a dioxazolone bearing a phenyl substituent as substrate, we found that the Ru catalysts effective for the aliphatic C–H bond amidation were all unsuccessful catalysts for the desired intramolecular arene C–H amidation. After screening a library of bidentate ligands that include L-type diimines and diamines, LX-type amino acids and amides, we found that the LX-type bidentate ligands are more effective to bring about the desired arene amidation to form dihydroquinolinones. Further studies led to the finding that (L)-proline was the best ligand for the intramolecular arene C–H amidation. The desymmetrization of the prochiral symmetric dioxazolones has been examined for enantioselective arene C–H amidation. Several bidendate LX-type ligands have been studied, and the highest enantioselectivity of 30% ee was accomplished with (L)-proline. Several attempts to improve the enantioselectivity failed to yield better results. Assuming the reactive Ru-nitrene intermediate, the amidation occurred by ipso-selective electrophilic nitrene addition to the arene group, followed by 1,2-alkyl migration to form skeletal rearranged dihydroquinolinone products. With dioxazolones bearing phenolic moiety as probe substrates, the spirolactams intermediates have been isolated and structurally characterized. The Ru-catalyzed arene amidation reaction has been applied for synthesis of anticancer compounds and Alk-2 inhibitors. This work has been published in Organic Letters, 2021, 23, 3310. [2] Prompted by the success of the (arene)Ru catalysis for direct C–H amidation, we hypothesized that the analogous iron catalysis would be plausible. Indeed, the prevailing challenge for developing oxidative iron catalysis is the lability of the iron complexes due to high spin configuration. In this project, we found that ferrocenium complex can effect direct arene C–H amidation with dioxazolones as substrates. Based on computational study (in collaboration with Prof. Zhenyang Lin of HKUST), reactive Fe(IV)-amidyl species is the plausible intermediate for the amidation reaction. The ferrocenium-catalyzed reactions proceeded by ipso-selective electrophilic amidyl radical addition to the arene moiety to afford a spirocyclohexadienyl radical intermediate. Subsequent radical-polar crossover and 1,2-alkyl migration furnished the skeletal rearranged dihydroquinolinones in excellent yields. Computational study revealed that the ipso-selective nitrene radical attack is directed by electron-releasing substituents such as MeO group. Dioxazolones bearing weaker releasing groups would react to afford a mixture of ortho- and ipso addition products. The robustness of the ferrocenium catalysts has been tested by immobilizing the ferrocenium complex onto commercial silica gel. Under the standard reaction conditions, the immobilized ferrocenium catalysts can be used repeatedly (over five consecutive runs) after recycling by simple filtration. A cumulative turnover of 333 has been attained. This work has been published in ACS Catalysis, 2023, 13, 11389. [3] Apart from intramolecular C–H amidation of C–H bonds, the NiH-mediated intermolecular amidation of methylene C–H bonds of alkenes. With Ni(II) salt as catalyst and 2,9-dibutylphenanthroline as ligand, treating the thioether-tethered unactivated alkene with pinacolborane and dioxazolones produced the gamma-methylene C–H amidation products. It should be noted that electronic and steric control for targeting methylene C–H bonds functionalization is often ineffective because they form the uniform hydrocarbon skeleton of the substrates with similar bond strengths and steric environment. Therefore, intermolecular direct C–H amidation targeting regioselective methylene C–H bonds are highly challenging. In this work, we installed an alkyl-Ni moiety onto the hydrocarbon substrate by hydrometallation of the C=C bond. The spontaneous alkyl-Ni chain-walking isomerization occurred by reversible hydride elimination-hydride migratory insertion. Here, the thioether group effectively captured the alkyl-Ni group and terminated the chain-walking isomerization at the gamma position through five-membered metallacycle formation. The metallacycle reacts with the dioxazolones to forge the amide bond at the gamma-position. This protocol applies to a broad substrate scope (> 40 examples) with excellent yields and selectivity. This work has been published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2021, 143, 14962.

15301719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15301719.value: [1] We report the [Ru(p-cymene)(L-proline)Cl] ([Ru1])-catalyzed cyclization of 1,4,2-dioxazol-5-ones to form dihydroquinoline-2-ones in excellent yields with excellent regioselectivity via a formal intramolecular arene C(sp2)−H amidation. The reactions of the 2- and 4-substituted aryl dioxazolones proceeds initially through spirolactamization via electrophilic amidation at the arene site, which is para or ortho to the substituent. A Hammett correlation study showed that the spirolactamization is likely to occur by electrophilic nitrenoid attack at the arene, which is characterized by a negative ρ value of −0.73. This work has been published in Organic Letters, 2021, 23, 3310. [2] Taking the advantage of the strong Cp−Fe linkages, here we developed the 17-electron ferrocenium complexes as effective catalysts for facile intramolecular aryl C−H amidation with 1,4,2-dioxazol-5-one as amidyl radical precursors. The ferrocenium-catalyzed reaction affords 3,4-dihydroquinolin-2(1H)-ones in excellent yields and selectivity. Our experimental and computational studies revealed that the intramolecular arene amidation is brought about by electrophilic arene addition by reactive Fe(IV)-amidyl radical species. Consistent with the experimental findings, the regioselectivity (ipso- versus ortho-amidyl radical addition) is influenced by electronic factors. The ipso amidyl radical addition should form an azaspirocyclohexadienyl radical intermediate. Subsequent radical-polar crossover and 1,2-alkyl migration followed by rearomatization afforded the skeletal rearranged dihydroquinolinone lactams. A recyclable heterogeneous amidation catalyst has been prepared by grafting ferrocene onto commercially available silica, and comparable catalytic activities with the homogeneous system were observed. This work has been published in ACS Catalysis, 2023, 13, 11389. [3] A NiH-catalyzed thioether-directed cyclometalation strategy is developed to enable remote methylene C−H bond amidation of unactivated alkenes. Due to the preference for five-membered nickelacycle formation, the chain-walking isomerization initiated by the NiH insertion to an alkene can be terminated at the γ-methylene site remote from the alkene moiety. By employing 2,9-dibutyl-1,10-phenanthroline (L4) as the ligand and dioxazolones as the reagent, the amidation occurs at the γ-C(sp3)−H bonds to afford the amide products in up to 90% yield (>40 examples) with remarkable regioselectivity (up to 24:1 rr). This work has been published in the Journal of the American Chemical Society, 2021, 143, 14962.

15301719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15301719.value: This project successfully tackled the challenging issues of regiocontrolled C–H amidation. With Ru, Fe and Ni as catalysts, effective ligand-enabled reactivity and regioselectivity have been achieved. Based on the results obtained in this project, we can forsee the following potential development: [1] Development of chiral amide synthesis: Both inner- and outer-sphere metal nitrene pathways are successfully exploited for regioselective C–N bond coupling reactions. Yet, limited examples are there in the literature concerns the enantioselective C–H amidation. We surmised that the use of chiral ligand would effect enantioselective C–N bond formation. [2] While regiocontrolled C–H bond amidation has been realized, the position control remains limited to five-membered ring formation. Other positions would be highly challenging. Possible targets for position selectivity include beta- and delta-positions. [3] We found that ferrocene moieties can be utilized for catalytic nitrene transfer reactions. Further study on ligand structure development would be of interest to bring about position and enantiocontrolled C–H amidation., Carbene transfer reactions mediated by ferrocenium complexes are also feasible topics for further investigation.

15301719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15301719.value: With dioxazolones as substrates, effective gamma-selective C–H bond amidation has been realized by exploiting inner- and outer-sphere metal-nitrene reaction pathways. With a suitable metal-ligand combination, a high degree of chemo- and regioselectivity has been accomplished. The remarkable position selectivity stems from the favorable formation of five-membered cyclic transition states or metal-organic intermediates. This approach was widely applicable to the broad scope of substrates and systems. This should constitute a guiding principle for designing regiocontrolled amidation reactions. Our approach would be of practical value for application to synthesis of valuable medicinal products and intermediates for total synthesis.

15302019.value: 对纳米级电化学技术的操作的原子描述

15302019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302019.value: Resistance random access memories (ReRAM) represent an emerging class of non-volatile memory devices based on the change of the resistance state of the memory element to store information. The operation of ReRAM involves Redox reactions, ionic diffusion and nucleation as well as electronic transport. Because of the complex physics involved, currently there is no atomistic model to capture accurately ReRAM operation. For example, the description of Redox processes from first principle calculations is challenging and extremely computer intensive limiting the size of the system studied to few hundred of atoms. To address this problem, we propose an atomistic model based on a semiclassical treatment of electrons and accurate electrostatics. Our method is based on reactive molecular dynamic simulations with explicit electrons interacting with the background ions via electrostatics. Charges are computed from the split-charge equilibration method including the effect of long-range Coulomb. The external electrochemical potential is modelled from grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations. We propose to apply the model to describe the operation of resistive memories in a view to optimize retention and switching speed. 电阻随机存取存储器（ReRAM）表示基于存储元件的电阻状态的变化来存储信息的新兴类非易失性存储器件。 ReRAM的操作涉及氧化还原反应，离子扩散和成核以及电子传输。由于涉及复杂的物理，目前没有原子模型可以准确捕获ReRAM操作。例如，来自第一原理计算的氧化还原过程的描述是具有挑战性的并且极其计算机密集地将所研究的系统的大小限制为几百个原子。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了一种基于电子和精确静电的半经典处理的原子模型。我们的方法基于反应性分子动力学模拟，显式电子通过静电与背景离子相互作用。电荷由分裂电荷平衡方法计算，包括远程库仑的影响。外部电化学势是通过大规范蒙特卡罗模拟建模的。我们建议应用该模型来描述电阻存储器的操作，以优化保持和切换速度

15302319.label: Project Objectives
15302319.value: We propose to develop a general experimental protocol that we plan to couple the steady- state with our ultrafast broadband TRF and TA to enable a direct and comprehensive probe of temporal evolution of the electronic spectra of the varied selected DAPI-DNA systems. The protocol is proposed also to examine change as time of the fluorescence anisotropy and influence of e.g. solvent kinetic isotopic effect on the excited state dynamics. Such procedure will allow acquisition of direct information for extracting the hydration dynamics probed by DAPI for the various chosen ds- and ts-DNAs. We propose to use the procedure in (1) to perform a comparative and system study on non-bound DAPI and DAPI bound to dsDNAs from Dickerson-Drew dodecamer and its analogues in controlled condition for quantitative binding. The study is planned to provide the hitherto unknown spectral and dynamic characterization for the minor groove binding and to unveil the origin of the “light switch” effect; it is also planned to examine influence of binding strength and variation in binding base or size of the minor groove on the photo-physical property of DAPI. We propose to conduct parallel spectroscopic study on DAPI with GC dsDNAs. The result will allow observation of transient species and spectral dynamics for understanding difference in mode of DAPI binding to GC vs AT DNAs. The data will also provide insight for clarifying role of excimer formation, charge transfer, and variation in dsDNA micro-hydration condition induced by the site and base specific binding to DAPI. We propose to conduct study for DAPI interacting to GQs with varied molecularity and different folding topology formed from e.g. human telomeric G-rich sequences under controlled condition. The finding of this work will provide spectral and dynamics that will enable to assess capacity of DAPI in stabilising the GQs; it will also allow acquiring concrete evidence for illustrating affinity and the site and mode of DAPI binding to the diverse structures of the GQs involved. We propose to study the spectra and dynamics of DAPI interacting with various structure of iMs formed from e.g. C-rich human telomeric sequences. The work is planned to examine proclivity and character of DAPI in binding to iMs, the tsDNA featuring the unique inter-digitised architecture and structure and binding site distinctive from dsDNA and tsGQ. This study is timely in view of the surge of interest and the rapidly growing attention in iM and its role in human genome. 15302319.value: 核酸與小分子間的相互作用在核酸結構識別，生物納米技術和抗腫瘤藥物設計等眾多領域具有重要的應用。這些應用源自於小分子與核酸分子間的特異性相互作用。4'，6-二脒基-2-苯基吲哚（DAPI）是目前已知的一種重要核酸熒光標記試劑，被廣泛應用於核酸生物化學研究。過往的研究發現，該分子可與雙鏈核酸中的腺嘌呤和胸腺嘧啶序列鍵合，進而增強DAPI的熒光發射，即誘發所謂的“光開關”效應。然而目前人們對在分子水平上導致這種DAPI與雙鏈核酸相互作用序列特異的根源，所知甚少。除雙鏈核酸外，了解目前尚屬未知的DAPI與非常規四鏈核酸結構，如鳥嘌呤四鏈核酸（GQ）和胞嘧啶四鏈核酸（iM）間的相互作用，亦是目前核酸生物、物理、化學研究中的重要前沿和熱點課題。這些四鏈核酸可存在於體外和體內人類細胞中，在基因調控和靶向抗癌藥物研發等方面發揮重要作用。為了探索這些未知領域，本項目建議將常規的穩態光譜與尖端的組合寬帶飛秒超快時間分辨光譜方法相結合，深入、系統地研究DAPI與一系列雙鏈核酸及若干四鏈核酸，包括人類端粒GQ及iM四鏈核酸間的相互作用。通過實現對所選體系激發態光譜和動力學的首次實時探測與跟踪，項目的研究結果將為闡明和識別DAPI與雙鏈核酸不同序列及與四鏈核酸GQ及iM構型間相互作用的鍵合模式與動力學，提供直接的實驗證據及光譜與動力學信息。本項目研究對揭示小分子與核酸二級結構相互作用的構效關係，促進靶向抗癌藥物設計及核酸結構熒光探針研發等方面，皆具重要意義。

15302319.label: Realisation of objectives
15302319.value: For objective 1: 100% achieved We have developed a general experimental protocol that couples the steady-state with our femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence (fs-TRF) and femtosecond transient absorption (fs-TA) experiments to probe the temporal evolution of the electronic spectra of the varied selected 4’,6-Diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI)-DNA systems after excitation. The protocol helps to determine the lifetime and efficiency of transient species as well as to examine change as time of the fluorescence anisotropy and influence of solvent kinetic isotopic effect (KIE) on the excited state dynamics, thereby to establish a comprehensive picture for deactivation pathways in the selected systems. For objective 2: 90% achieved We have performed an integrated spectroscopic investigation where we combined steady-state absorption and fluorescence, fs-TRF and fs-TA experiments on non-bound DAPI and DAPI bound to selected Dickerson-Drew dodecamers. The DAPI-d(GCGAATTCGC)2 (DAPI-DDS) shows the highest fluorescence quantum yield and longest excited-state dynamics, further analysis is ongoing. These results have been used to examine the dynamic characterization for the minor groove binding and to unveil the origin of the “light switch” effect. For objective 3: 85% achieved We have performed an integrated spectroscopic investigation where we combined fs time-resolved and steady-state spectroscopy experiments on DAPI interacting to GC dsDNAs. We found no DAPI fluorescence enhance with the presence of GC dsDNAs, implying no interaction between them. The results in the objective 2 have also been used to direct comparison between the excited-state behaviors of the various GQs. This work has provided evidence for understanding difference of DAPI binding to GC vs AT DNAs. For objective 4: 95% achieved We have performed an integrated spectroscopic investigation where we combined fs time-resolved and steady-state spectroscopy experiments on DAPI interacting to GQs. We found no DAPI fluorescence enhance with the presence of GQs, implying no interaction between them, but we have tried other frequently used ligand molecule thioflavin-T (THT) with GQs. For example, THT-dAG3(T2AG3)3 (THT-HTG22) shows 1:1 binding, 3x105 M-1 binding constant, ~110 times higher fluorescence quantum yield, ~200 times longer excited-state dynamics and with KIE. These results provide spectral and dynamics that enable to assess capacity of THT in stabilising the GQs. For objective 5: 100% achieved We have performed an integrated spectroscopic investigation where we combined fs time-resolved and steady-state spectroscopy experiments on DAPI interacting with various structure of iMs. For example, DAPI-d(C3TA2)3C3T (DAPI-HTC22) shows 1:1 binding, 2x106 M-1 binding constant, ~6 times higher fluorescence quantum yield, ~5 times longer excited-state dynamics and with KIE. These results have been used to understand the unique inter-digitised architecture and structure and binding site distinctive from dsDNA and tsGQ. For objective 6: 95% achieved By performing the investigations to achieve the objectives 1 to 5 above, we have obtained a comprehensive set of data for unveiling the general connection between the binding character and the secondary structure of the ds and tsDNA. The overall results contribute importantly for understanding the sequence specific of DNA binding as well as DNA recognition.

15302319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302319.value: We have conducted most of the experiments planned in this project. Through these measurements, expected evidences have been obtained for addressing most of the questions posed in the proposal. The results for 4’6-Diamidino-2-phenylindole binding with I-motif (iM) from MYC0 sequence (DAPI-iM) show that: (i) The binding complex shows a binding ratio of 2:1 (DAPI:iM) and two binding constants of ~3.2×105 M-1 and ~1.7×104 M-1, which indicates the coexistence of weakly binding and strongly binding between DAPI and iM; (ii) Environment dynamics (solvation) observed with binding complex includes the fast components of ~0.8 ps and ~6.5 ps due to motion of water molecules that are surrounding DAPI that can travel randomly, and slow components of ~204 ps and ~2237 ps that are contributed by movement of weakly-bound and strongly-bound water molecules near the DAPI-iM binding site, respectively; (iii) Notable enhancement (by ~8 folds) of fluorescence quantum yield is observed for DAPI-iM compared with that of free DAPI. This is in line with much longer fluorescence lifetimes from the weakly-bound DAPI (~204 ps) and in particular the strongly-bound DAPI (~2510 ps) than that of free DAPI (~139 ps). The fluorescence enhancement is due to quenching of the IPT of free DAPI caused by its binding with iM. Such a quenching mechanism is because, after interaction with iM, DAPI becomes rigid and less able to rotate into the planar structure in the excited state, especially for the strongly-bound DAPI with iM.; and (iv) Two binding modes are proposed for the DAPI-iM complex. One is that the two DAPI molecules work as a minor groove binder for the weakly binding and a major groove binder for the strongly binding, respectively. The other is that both the DAPI molecules work as a major groove binder firstly for the weakly binding, but when one DAPI molecule leaves the major groove, the size of the major groove becomes bigger and the other DAPI molecule goes deeper and thus strongly binds to iM in the major groove. 15302319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302319.value: The use of small molecules to target DNA has gained significant interest for its potential in DNA recognition, bio-nanotechnology, and creating antitumor therapies. This is largely due to their ability to specifically interact with DNA. One notable example is 4’,6-Diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI), a widely used fluorescent marker for DNA, known for its strong binding to the AT sequence in DNA's minor groove, which enhances fluorescence. Despite its widespread use, the specifics of DAPI's interaction with DNA, particularly its sequence specificity and its interaction with noncanonical DNA structures like guanine-quadruplexes (GQ) and i-motifs (iM), which are crucial in genome regulation and cancer therapy, remain poorly understood. To address these gaps, advanced spectroscopy techniques (femtosecond broadband time-resolved fluorescence and transient absorption techniques) were employed to systematically study DAPI's interaction with various DNA structures. This research has provided the first direct insights into the binding dynamics and differences in DAPI's interaction with AT versus GC sequences in DNA, as well as its interaction with GQ and iM structures. These findings significantly advance our understanding of DNA-binding mechanisms, offering valuable insights for anticancer drug development, nanotechnology, and DNA recognition.

15302419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302419.value: It is known that structural superlubricity exists in various van der Waals (vdW) layered structures, such as graphite, molybdenum disulfide, and hexagonal boron nitride, when the atomic registration between layers is incommensurate. Therefore, the easy sliding between the vdW layers can be used for the solid or mixed phase lubricant. Although solid-state lubricants (SSL) are currently used in a wide range of applications, especially under several extreme conditions like high/low pressure, high/low temperature, high speed cases, and have grown into a billion-dollar commercial market worldwide, unfortunately, a large part of SSL working mechanism is still elusive. To reveal the different contributions of friction dissipations in SSL, as well as bridging the macroscopic and nanoscale friction behaviors, we plan to use in situ TEM-AFM techniques to probe the non-uniform interfaces in SSL under friction loading. The wrinkled/rippling/creased structure that can appear in SSL will be imaged and analyzed directly. Based on the dynamical in situ TEM observations, static/dynamic friction behavior will be assessed by energy minimization, including the wrinkles or other related structures. The effect of the local atomic registry between the SSL layers on the friction will also be examined by TEM. On the other hand, the flexoelectricity effects that become appreciable at the nanoscale/atomic scale will be measured by a combined TEM and Kelvin force microscopy (KFM) method, and compared with the theoretical results calculated by density function theory (DFT). Regarding the chemical impact on friction, we plan to prepare SSL samples with different defects and functional groups or intercalations, and then use in situ TEM and AFM measurements for the friction test. We hope that through the current project, we will be able to answer the fundamental questions related to the origin of friction underestimation in SSL, the impact of atomic defect structures/wrinkled structures on friction performances in SSL, and provide methods/suggestions for achieving better performances of SSL products. 已知當層間的原子配準不相稱時，結構超潤滑性存在於各種范德華（vdW）層狀結構中，例如石墨，二硫化鉬和六方氮化硼。因此，vdW層之間的容易滑動可用於固相或混合相潤滑劑。雖然固態潤滑劑（SSL）目前用於廣泛的應用，特別是在高/低壓，高/低溫，高速情況等幾種極端條件下，並已在全球範圍內發展成為價值數十億美元的商業市場，遺憾的是，很大一部分SSL工作機制仍然不甚清楚。為了揭示SSL中摩擦耗散的不同貢獻，以及連接宏觀和納米級摩擦行為，我們計劃使用原位TEM-AFM技術來探測摩擦載荷下SSL中的非均勻界面。可以出現在SSL中的皺紋/波紋/褶皺結構將直接成像和分析。基於動態原位TEM觀察，靜態/動態摩擦行為將通過能量最小化來評估，包括皺紋或其他相關結構。還將通過TEM檢查SSL層之間原子結構對摩擦的影響。另一方面，通過組合的TEM和Kelvin力顯微鏡（KFM）方法測量在納米尺度/原子尺度下變得明顯的屈電效應，並與通過密度函數理論（DFT）計算的理論結果進行比較。關於化學對摩擦的影響，我們計劃製備具有不同缺陷和官能團或插層的SSL樣品，然後使用原位TEM和AFM測量進行摩擦測試。我們希望通過當前的項目，我們將能夠回答與SSL中摩擦低估的起源有關的基本問題，原子缺陷結構/皺紋結構對SSL中摩擦性能的影響，並實現更好的方法來提高SSL產品的性能。

15302419.label: Realisation of objectives
15302419.value: All the objectives have been satisfactorily completed. 1, For target 1, we have performed the in situ bending experiments on typical SSL such as graphene, MoS2, In2Se3, by using in situ TEM manupulator (Nanofactory). We have addressed the critical wrinkling properties, the phase transition properties, the electronic contact properties, etc., of the bended or wrinkled structures in 2D materials using in situ TEM and EELS. Please refer to the publications: ACS Nano, 2020, 14, 2137–2144; Nature Communications, 2020, 11, 3982; Science Advances, 2022, 8(42), eabo0773; Physical Review Letters 125, 246102 (2020); Science Advances 6, 47, eabc2282 (2020) 2, For target 2, we have applied in situ TEM method to investigate the interlayer interactions between the van der Waals layeres of such MoS2, InSe, In2Se3, graphene, etc. The flexoelectricty of In2Se3 have been experimentally confirmed via the iDPC STEM and 4D STEM technique. Besides, the ferroelectricity and the ferroelectricity related phase control have been clearly understood by our TEM and in situ TEM studies. Please refer to the publications: Nature Nanotechnology, 2023, 18, 55; Science Advances 8(42), eabo0773 (2022); Nature Communications 11, 3982 (2020). 3, For target 3, we have studied the friction of 2D SSL flakes by FFM and TEM, and particularly, we found the ice can greatly lower the friction on the 2D SSL flakes, thus we paved a new way to lower the SSL friction by lower the temperatures and enhance the humidities. 15302419.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302419.value: 1, For materials synthesis, we have prepared very large-scale 2D MoS2 (JACS,142, 30, 13130-13135 (2020)) and 2D In2Se3 phase controllable layers (Nature Nanotechnology, 2023, 18, 55). These synthesis studies are the solid basis of the further friction studies on the SSL material systems using advanced in situ characterization techniques. 2, We have clearly identified the elastic properties and plastic properties of the SSL materials like MoS2 and ReS2, and we have applied in situ TEM technique to study the atomic structures of the cracks, which is actually the world's first atomic scale study on the britrle crack structures and will lead a paradigm shift for the experimental study of fracture mechanics. (Physical Review Letters 125, 246102 (2020); Science Advances 6, 47, eabc2282 (2020); Advanced Science 7, 2001742 (2020)). 3, We have clearly identified the phase transition associated van der Waals intra and interlayer dynamics, for instance in the In2Se3 and InSe vdW SSL material systems. The in situ TEM combined with large scale macroscopic studies have successfully revealed the mechanical, chemical, defective and electronic effects on the interface structural changes. These findings on the memristive ferroelectric vdW layered materials can guide the future electronic device development. (Nature Nanotechnology, 2023, 18, 55; Science Advances 8(42), eabo0773 (2022)). 4, We have applied FFM and TEM to investigate the surface friction of SSL systems like graphene and MoS2, and we unveil the unexpected ultralow friction between two-dimensional (2D) ice, a solid phase of water confined to the 2D space, and the 2D molybdenum disulfides (MoS2). The friction of MoS2 and 2D ice is reduced by more than 30% as compared to bare MoS2 and the rigid surface. These new findings can be applied as novel frictionless water/ice transport technology in nanofluidic systems and promising high performance lubricants for operating in low temperature and high humidity environments. 5, We have completed two review works descirbing our previous researches on 2D material defects, and particularly, we addressed the relationship between bending/wrinkling and grain boudaries, please refer to Accounts of Chemical Research 54, 22, 4191–4202 (2021), and Accounts of Materials Reserach, 2, 10, 863–868 (2021).

15302419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302419.value: For further development of this research, the 4D STEM and DPC STEM techniques can be applied for direct atomic scale mapping of the electric fields as well as the atomic structures. The friction, and the correlated phase, stacking order, electronic performances, and the chemical dependences can be further studied and give a unified picture about the SSL and vdW layered materials. We will continue to work on these SSL systems and try to deciper the intriguing mechanical, electronic and other novel properties.

15302419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302419.value: In this project, we have clearly understood the elastic properties and plastic properties of the SSL materials such as MoS2, ReS2, In2Se3, etc., down to the atomic scale, which could provide guidance for future engineering on the mechanical and electronic applications of these emergent new materials. We have also found new routes to lower the friction of the solid state lubricants by low temperature and humid. Meanwhile, this project set a good and new example for the live, correlative study on the mechanical, electrical and chemical properties of materials using the novel in situ TEM technique. This new method would provide numerous opportunities for future material and physical science research.

15302519.label: Project Objectives
15302519.value: To introduce strategies of interfacial and defect engineering to piezoelectric layered nanosheets for enhancing their piezoelectric response. To synthesize the selected and treated layered nanosheets grown on the designed substrates and layers based on the above strategies. To characterize the synthesized samples and achieve enhancement of piezoelectric coefficient compared to that of the existing layered nanosheets. To develop flexible piezoelectric nanogenerators using the nanosheets with enhanced piezoelectric response.
rows: To introduce strategies of interfacial and defect engineering to piezoelectric layered nanosheets for enhancing their piezoelectric response.
To synthesize the selected and treated layered nanosheets grown on the designed substrates and layers based on the above strategies.
To characterize the synthesized samples and achieve enhancement of piezoelectric coefficient compared to that of the existing layered nanosheets.
To develop flexible piezoelectric nanogenerators using the nanosheets with enhanced piezoelectric response.

15302519.label: Realisation of objectives
15302519.value: 1. In order to achieve the objective 1, a variety of layered nanosheets possessing potential piezoelectric properties have been explored. In the project period, we have designed several kinds of layered nanosheets such as In2Se3, SnSe, CuInP2S6 (CIPS) and heterostructures such as In2Se3/MoS2 and In2Se3/WS2. In these layered compounds, the S or Se vacancy site has a tendency to covalently bond with functional groups; therefore, by capturing free electrons. Hence, treatments of the defects in these nanosheets are able to reduce the charge-carrier density of the layered nanosheet surface, leading to enhanced piezoelectric response of the nanosheets. Regarding the introduction of interfacing engineering, our design in the large band offset and interlayer coupling between the p-type In2Se3 and other layered materials are able to enhance electric polarization, leading to the improvement of piezoelectric response. We have constructed vdW heterostructures with type II band alignment. It is found that such type II band alignment is helpful for the interfacial charge transfer of vdW heterostructure. The DFT theoretical calculation is consistent with the experimental band alignment obtained from the ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) measurement. In addition, most 2D layered piezoelectric materials found so far possess only in-plane piezoelectricity and require the induction of stress by bending flexible substrate, which limits their integration with conventional rigid substrates such as silicon wafer. We designed the piezoelectric CIPS which is mainly based on the Cu atoms in which the high unstable displacement of Cu atoms greatly enhances the electric polarization under stress, resulting in a much larger magnitude of d33 piezoelectric coefficient than conventional 2D layered nanosheet through the engineering strategy. These works have been published in ACS Appl. Nano Mater. (2020), Nano Energy (2022), Nano Research (2023). 2. To achieve the objective 2, we have made attempts to prepare multilayer SnSe nanosheets grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD). CVD method has advantages in scalability, controllability and mass production, allowing to obtain high crystalline quality and large area single-crystalline 2D materials. The grown samples were grown on mica substrates at the downstream of the furnace. The Ar/H2 mixed gas and N2 were used as the carrier gas during the growth period. We found that the SnSe films with a lateral size larger than 10 μm could be obtained under a growth temperature higher than 700 ℃ by fast-cooling at 600 ℃. In our synthesis, the SnSe nanosheets exhibited high single-crystallinity, large area, and good stability. In addition, we synthesized the selected and treated layered nanosheets as piezoelectric responses. For mechanical exfoliation (ME), layered nanosheets were exfoliated from bulk crystals onto designed substrates. For CVD, Se and In2O3 powders as the precursors were used to make In2Se3 layered nanosheetes. Furthermore, the vdW heterostructures such as In2Se3/MoS2 and In2Se3/WS2 were fabricated by the dry transfer method. In addition, we noted that some theoretical calculation predicted piezoelectricity existed in 2D black phosphorus (BP) nanosheets through surface oxidation and interfacial strain engineering (J. Phys. D: Appl. Phys. 51 12LT01 (2018), Sci. Rep. 5, 16448 (2015)) and an experimental result on the piezoelectricity in multilayer BP (Adv. Mater. 32, 1905795 (2020). We have presented a controllable and rapid pulsed laser deposition (PLD) process to directly synthesize few-layered BP on a centimetre scale with high crystallinity and homogeneity. These works have been published in ACS Appl. Nano Mater. (2020), Nat. Mater. (2021), and Nano Research (2023). 3. To achieve the objective 3, we have employed Raman spectra, photoluminescence mapping techniques to characterize the synthesized samples. The spectra of the samples were measured by Raman spectroscopy using a Confocal Raman system. Microstructures and chemical compositions were examined by transmission electron microscope (TEM). The composition of samples was obtained by using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The UPS measurement was performed. Second harmonic generation (SHG) can be used as a probe for detecting the broken inversion symmetry of crystal structure by considering non-centrosymmertric structure is critical for piezoelectric properties. Therefore, we have used a femtosecond laser to characterize the SHG signals of samples. Piezoresponse force microscope (PFM) is usually used to measure the converse piezoelectric response. We have used a commercial atomic force microscope (Asylum Research MFP-3D) to measure piezoelectric signals and PFM images. Typically, a tip was driven with Vac=0.2−4 V under the frequency ∼300 kHz. The PFM amplitude images reveal strong piezoelectric responses, demonstrating the existence of out-of-plane piezoelectricity in these samples. The out-of-plane piezoelectric coefficient d33 of 80 nm In2Se3 onto SiO2/Si substrate is measured to be around 7.6 pm/V. Importantly, we found that the piezoelectric coefficient d33 of In2Se3/MoS2 heterostructure is measured to be approximately 17.5 pm/V, which shows enhanced piezoelectric response of layered nanosheets through interface and defect engineering. In addition, the thickness dependence of the piezoelectric coefficient is found. Importantly, few-layer CIPS nanosheet shows a high d33 piezoelectric coefficient of 17.4 pm/V, outperforming other 2D layered piezoelectrics currently reported.We have successfully observed the enhanced in-plane piezoelectric response and piezotronic effect, the piezoelectric output signals in the piezoelectric devices for effective mechanical-to-electrical energy conversion and motion monitoring are characterized. The relevant results are published in the journal of Nano Research (2023), ACS Appl. Nano Mater. (2020), Adv. Funct. Mater. (2022), and Nano Energy (2022). 4. To achieve the objective 4, we prepared nanosheet-based piezoelectric nanogenerators and examined their performances. Typically, the piezoelectric responses from the CIPS piezoelectric nanogenerator (PENG), in which the piezoelectric CIPS nanoflake is sandwiched between two Au electrodes on SiO2/Si substrate, were measured under constant vertical periodic compression and release actions, and the schematic of the home-made experimental system for mechanical force application. The thickness of the CIPS nanoflakes used for constructing the nanogenerators was controlled in the range of ~20–50 nm, with an energy harvesting active area in the range of 100–140 μm2. We fabricate 2D CIPS-based PENG through a facile and non-destructive vdW integration approach. The output piezoelectric current and voltage of the nanogenerator under uniform compression reach a maximum value of 1.7 nA and 12 mV respectively. The energy conversion efficiency of PENG based on the CVD-grown SnSe is estimated to be ~9.3%. The relevant results are published in Nano Energy (2022), ACS AMI (2020), EcoMat (2020), Nano Res. (2023). 5. In summary, we have fully achieved the four objectives of the RGC GRF project. One PhD postgraduate student, Ms. Fumei Yang financially supported by the GRF grant has been well trained in the project period and will submit her PhD thesis soon. Regarding the GRF project’s research, the postgraduate student has published an international journal paper entitled “Synthesis and enhanced piezoelectric response of CVD-grown SnSe layered nanosheets for flexible nanogenerators”, Nano Res.16, 11839 as the first author. This works as been highlighted by EurekAlert (AAAS) (https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/973826). Totally, 8 high-quality journal papers (Nano Energy, Nano Res., Nat. Mater., ACS AMI, EcoMat. etc.) including one invited review are published with acknowledgements of this project. To disseminate our results, the PI has given 1 Plenary, 2 keynote and 3 invited talks in the recognized international conferences, such as 2021 MRS Spring Meeting, AMF-13 & AMEC-13.
