15302519.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302519.value: 1. We are able to enhance the piezoelectric performance in 2D layered materials through the interfacial and defect engineering. A remarkable out-of-plane piezoelectric performance is found in the In2Se3/MoS2 vdW heterostructure with piezoelectric coefficient d33 of approximate 17.5 pm/V, which is larger than the individual In2Se3 and MoS2. By combining the experimental studies and density functional theory calculations, the enhanced piezoelectric properties are found to result from the type II band alignment, which causes a larger interfacial dipole moment. Moreover, the atomical deformation actuator based on out-of-plane piezoelectricity can be demonstrated. (see: Part C: Journal 1, Conference 3,4). 2. We achieve various layered nanosheets with large area and high-quality. These layered sheets show enhanced piezoelectric response such as SnSe layered nanosheets grown by chemical vapor deposition (CVD) or potential piezoelectric response such as 2D black phosphorus by pulsed laser deposition. The large-scale nanotheets provide an opportunity to further develop wafer-scale devices. The as-prepared SnSe nanosheets demonstrate large area and good uniformity, which contribute to a low interface scattering across the whole nanosheets. It is indicated that the importance of interface and defect engineering play an important role in enhancing piezoelectric response of nanosheets. The strong layer-dependent in-plane piezoelectric coefficient of the CVD-grown SnSe nanosheets show a saturated trend to be ~110 pm/V, which overcomes the weak piezoelectric response or odd-even effects in other layered nanosheets. (see: Part C: Journal 5,6,8 Conference 1,2,7). 3. We quantitatively investigate the layer-dependent out-of-plane piezoelectric response of CuInP2S6 (CIPS) nanosheets in the 2D regime and found the piezotronic effect in CIPS-based devices. We found that the vertical piezoelectric signals of the nanosheets enhance significantly when increasing sample’s thickness. Specifically, the enhanced piezoelectric coefficient d33 of 17.4 pm/V is observed in few-layer CIPS. Regarding the flexible nanogenerators, we obtain high performance nanogenerators using different materials and device structures via defect and interface engineering. The output piezoelectric current and voltage of the CIPS nanogenerator under uniform compression reach a maximum value of 1.7 nA and 12 mV, respectively, while peak power density reaches 70.4 nW/cm2. The energy conversion efficiency of CVD-grown SnSe nanosheets is estimated to be ~9.3%. Based on the excellent piezoelectric output, the flexible nanogenerators have been further attached to the finger and wrist of the tester to successfully verify the potential of displaying self-powered motion monitoring and energy harvesting applications. (see: Part C: Journal 2,3,4,7,8, Conference 5,6,7).

15302519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302519.value: It is suggested that the enhanced piezoelectric properties of In2Se3/MoS2 are ascribed to a larger interfacial dipole moment. In fact, the strategy of the interface and defect engineering can be extended to other nanosheets-based vdW heterostructure. Further development of tuning the band alignment has a great potential to further optimize the piezoelectric properties. In addition, a new strategy by constructing patterned nanostructures is developed in our most recent study. A high-performance piezoelectric materials and devices may be designed and developed via manipulating strain distribution engineered by the substrate. The combination of interface and substrate nanoengineering is expected to be expanded to produce more device applications based on different layered nanosheets. Our work reveals that large out-of-plane piezoelectric coefficients in 2D CIPS can be observed down to ~3.5 nm. Further developing large-scale CIPS nanosheets and thinner CIPS nanosheets is promising. It is also interesting to expand materials types of nanosheets to hybrid organic-inorganic halide perovskites via defect and interface engineering. Although perovskite polycrystalline nanosheets are hardly compatible with the mechanical deformations due to their brittleness and rigidity, a potential solution is to incorporate piezoelectric perovskite into a polymer matrix forming flexible piezoelectric nanocomposite and nanogenerator for further development.

15302519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302519.value: Technological progress has pushed increasingly miniaturized devices and systems, stimulating a search for nanoscale piezoelectric materials in response to mechanical stimuli for mechanical signal sensing and energy harvesting based on piezoelectric nanogenerators. However, the piezoelectric response of conventional layered nanosheets is quite low, which is not feasible for precise characterizations in terms of fundamental research and far from device development in terms of practical application. In this project, we have developed diverse layered piezoelectric nanosheets and van der Walls heterostructures and then enhance their piezoelectric response through introducing strategies of interfacial and defect engineering. We report on synthesizing and processing a variety of piezoelectric nanosheets by mechanical exfoliation and vapor deposition for large-scale preparation of 2D materials. Structural and physical properties of the synthesized nanosheets are characterized. Through experimental studies and theoretical calculations, enhanced piezoelectric responses are observed in the In2Se3 layered heterostructure with a larger interfacial dipole moment and some novel layered nanosheets such as CuInP2S6 and SnSe. We have demonstrated layered nanosheets-based piezoelectric nanogenerators, piezoelectric based human motion sensor. The enhanced out-of-plane and in-plane piezoelectricity in nanosheets endow them with superior opportunities for broad applications in mechanical energy harvesting and self-powered electromechanical sensing systems.

15302919.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15302919.value: Allen-Cahn型相場方程最大值原理保持的時間積分方法

15302919.label: Project Objectives
15302919.value: For general Allen-Cahn type phase field equations, we will provide a stability analysis on discrete maximum principles of the proposed ETD schemes based on our recent work on the nonlocal Allen-Cahn equation. We will develop higher order IFRK methods for Allen-Cahn type phase field equations and explore their discrete maximum principles. By using the proved discrete maximum principles, we will investigate energy stability and maximum norm error estimates for the proposed ETD and IFRK numerical schemes.

We will develop higher order IFRK methods for Allen-Cahn type phase field equations and explore their discrete maximum principles.
By using the proved discrete maximum principles, we will investigate energy stability and maximum norm error estimates for the proposed ETD and IFRK numerical schemes.

15302919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15302919.value: This project focuses on maximum principle preserving numerical methods for Allen-Cahn type phase field equations, which have been extensively used to explore phase transitions in various fields. Allen-Cahn type equations admit two intrinsic properties: nonlinear energy stability and the maximum principle. Computationally, it is highly desirable to develop efficient numerical methods that preserve intrinsic properties of differential equations as much as possible. There have been numerous works on energy stable numerical methods for Allen-Cahn type phase field equations, while investigations on maximum principle preserving numerical methods are still not enough though more and more attention has been attracted recently. The goal of this project is to develop efficient maximum principle preserving numerical schemes for numerical simulation of Allen-Cahn type phase field equations, by using exponential time differencing (ETD) and integrating factor Runge-Kutta (IFRK) methods. The equations will be decomposed into linear and nonlinear parts based on the stabilization splitting technique. ETD schemes are a set of explicit time-stepping algorithms, which solve the linear part exactly and approximate the nonlinear part by numerical integration with any desired temporal accuracy. A first order ETD scheme and a second order ETD Runge-Kutta scheme will be explored. Their discrete maximum principles will be examined for Allen-Cahn type phase field equations. IFRK schemes perform as convex combinations of some forward Euler sub-steps, which sacrifice the exponential behavior of the linear part but can provide higher order time integration schemes with discrete maximum principles. The proposed algorithms will be highly efficient due to the explicit temporal integration in combination with the fast Fourier transform technique for matrix exponentials. The main contribution of this project is the systematic analysis on discrete maximum principles of the proposed ETD and IFRK schemes for Allen-Cahn type phase field equations. Energy stability and maximum norm error estimates will also be investigated. 此項目主要研究在很多領域探索相變過程常用的Allen-Cahn型 相場方程最大值原理保持的數值方法。 Allen-Cahn型方程有兩 個內在性質：非線性能量穩定性和最大值原理。數值上，盡最 大可能保持微分方程內在性質的高效數值算法是非常需要的。 針對Allen-Cahn方程的能量穩定性數值方法已經有很多工作了， 對此方程最大值原理保持的數值方法儘管已經有越來越多的關 注，然而研究還是遠遠不足。 此項目的研究目標是應用指數時間離散（ETD)和積分因子龍格 -庫塔（IFRK)方法，針對Allen-Cahn型相場方程的數值模擬發展 高效的最大值原理保持的數值格式。基於穩定化分裂技巧，方程 將被分解為線性和非線性部分。 ETD格式是一類顯式時間離散 格式，它們精確求解線性部分，使用數值積分可以時間上任意 階逼近非線性部分。我們將研究一種一階ETD格式和一種二階 ETD龍格-庫塔格式。針對Allen-Cahn型相場方程，他們的離散 最大值原理將會被測試。 IFRK格式是一系列向前歐拉格式的 凸組合，他們雖然犧牲了線性部分的指數特性，但是能提供高 階離散最大值原理保持的時間積分格式。因為應用了顯式時間 積分和針對矩陣指數的快速傅里葉變換，我們提出的算法將會 非常高效。此項目的主要貢獻是針對Allen-Cahn型相場方程提 出的ETD和IFRK格式的離散最大值原理的系統分析。我們在此 項目中也會研究能量穩定性和最大模誤差估計。

15302919.label: Realisation of objectives
15302919.value: The objectives of this project have been achieved successfully. Under the support of this GRF grant, we have developed several energy stable numerical schemes, including ETD schemes and IFRK schemes, for Allen-Cahn type phase field equations. The stability and convergence of the proposed numerical schemes have been analyzed. The characteristic properties of the solution, -e.g. the energy decay property, the discrete maximum principles, have been conserved in numerical simulations. The proposed numerical schemes have been used in solving Allen-Cahn type equations in several applications.

15302919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15302919.value: In this project, we have studied some maximum principle preserving time integration methods for Allen-Cahn type phase field equations. The major findings and research outcome are as follows: 1. In [Ju-Li-Qiao-Yang, Journal of Computational Physics, 2021], several higher order integrating factor Runge-Kutta (IFRK) schemes have been developed for Allen-Cahn type equations. The maximum bound principle and energy stability of the numerical solution has been analyzed. 2. In recent years, the scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) method and many of its variants have attracted much attention in numerical solutions for gradient flow problems due to their inherent advantage of preserving certain discrete analogues of the energy dissipation law. However, existing SAV schemes usually fail to preserve the MBP when applied to the Allen–Cahn equation. In [Ju-Li-Qiao, SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis, 2022] and [Ju-Li-Qiao, Journal of Scientific Computing, 2022], we developed and analyzed new first- and second-order stabilized exponential-SAV schemes and generalized SAV schemes for a class of Allen–Cahn type equations, which are shown to simultaneously preserve the energy dissipation law and MBP in discrete settings. 3. In [Liu-Qiao-Zhang, SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing, 2022] and [Liu-Qiao-Zhang, Computers and Mathematics with Applications, 2023] we applied the exponential time integration methods on Allen-Cahn equations for two-phase image segmentation.

15302919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15302919.value: Further development of this research is to provide the detailed energy stability analysis for the developed high order integrating factor Runge-Kutta methods. Other high order methods, such as BDF schemes, will also be studied for Allen-Cahn type phase field models. The applications of the numerical schemes proposed in this project will be further studied for image segmentation problems and inpainting problems.

15302919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15302919.value: The Allen-Cahn equation is fundamental in phase field approaches, crucial for understanding interfacial dynamics and phase transitions across various fields. As analytic solutions are often unavailable, numerical simulation is increasingly important for studying these models. Maintaining numerical stability over time and accurately capturing interfaces is challenging but essential. The Allen-Cahn equations possess intrinsic properties of nonlinear energy stability and the maximum principle, making it crucial to develop effective numerical methods. This project aims to create highly efficient numerical schemes for solving Allen-Cahn type phase field equations. It establishes a general framework for developing high-order maximum principle preserving numerical methods, utilizing exponential time difference (ETD) and integrating factor Runge-Kutta (IFRK) methods. These methods are crucial in ensuring energy stability and maximum norm error estimates. By addressing the need for effective numerical methods, this research significantly advances our understanding of phase field models, contributing to various fields' progress.

15303019.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15303019.value: 关于一类典型的密度抑制运动模型：分析和应用

15303019.label: Project Objectives
15303019.value: Establish the existence of traveling wave solutions of the density-suppressed motility model and provide a theoretical interpretation/understanding to the experimental observations. Study the pattern formation (stationary solutions) of the density-suppressed motility model and identify the effect/role of the nonlinear motility function and cell growth rate on the pattern structures. Exploit the boundedness and blow-up of solutions to the density-suppressed motility model and explore how the cell growth and nonlinear motility collectively determine the key behavior of solutions.

15303019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303019.value: In addition to the two well-known mechanisms ``diffusion-driven (Turing) instability" and ``chemotaxis-driven instability" that have been widely advocated to explain the exquisite pattern formation observed in nature, recently a so-called ``self-trapping’’ mechanism generating pattern formation was experimentally verified in [Liu et al, Science, 334: 238-241, 2011]. The mathematical models called ``density-suppressed models" were proposed therein and in another work [Fu et al, Phys Rev. Lett., 108:198102, 2012] to reproduce/interpret the appealing patterns observed in the experiment. Apart from the biological interest, the mathematical understanding of the density-suppressed motility models large remains open except very few results obtained recently. This proposal is devoted to developing some analytical tools/ideas and hence establishing some qualitative results at first for the density-suppressed motility models, including traveling wavefront solutions, stationary pattern solutions and blowup/boundedness phenomenon. A variety of methods, such as fixed point theorem, theory of upper and lower solutions, weighted energy estimates, singular perturbation method, topological degree method, compactness argument and constructive approaches, will be employed to conduct the proposed researches. 擴散驅動（圖靈）和趨化性驅動是最為眾所周知並被廣泛應用去解釋自然界觀測到的各種精美圖案的兩種形成機制。除此之外， 最近一種所謂的“自我捕捉” 斑圖形成機制在文獻[Liu et al，Science，334：238-241,2011]中提出。一種稱為“密度抑制”的數學模型在文章[Fu et al，Phys Rev. Lett，108：198102, 2012] 中提出去重現/解釋在實驗中觀察到的精美圖案。除了在生物上有興趣，密度抑制數學模型的理論研究也很有意思，目前為止已知結果還非常少。該研究計劃就是致力去發展一些分析工具或想法去為密度抑制數學模型建立一些第一手的研究結果，包括行波解，靜態解和解的爆炸/有界現象。很多數學方法，如不動點定理，上下解原理，加權能量估計，奇異攝動，拓撲度，緊性理論和構造性方法都將用被來進行本研究計劃書提出的研究。

15303019.label: Realisation of objectives
15303019.value: All objectives have been successfully achieved. The objective 1 was completely achieved in the research output [7] where the existence of traveling wave solutions of the density-suppressed motility model has been established and numerical simulations have been performed to verify the model can generate wave pattern qualitatively same as those observed in the experiment. The objective 2 has been achieved in [5] and [9] where the stationary problems of the density-suppressed motility models have been extensively studied. In [5], we study the pattern formation of the density-suppressed motility model using global bifurcation and find various interesting patterns such as aggregation and periodic patterns. In [9], we study the effect of density-suppressed motility on the competition system and find that the resource-suppressed motility is able to produce different dynamics from the model with constant diffusion. This shows that the significance of the density-suppressed motility is a very important dispersal strategy for species movement to undertake certain tasks. The objective 3 was achieved in the research output [1], [2], [3],[4],[6],[8] and [10]. In these papers, we discuss under what conditions the solutions are globally bounded or blow up in finite or infinite time and find that the density-suppressed motility may induce the blowup depending on the decay rates of motility functions. On the other hand, some reaction terms like logistic growth may prevent the blowup.

15303019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303019.value: The major findings in our research outcomes include the following: (a) by the extensive researches from different angles like traveling waves, pattern formation, steady states, global boundedness and blowup, we find that density-suppressed motility can produce rich dynamics and various patterns depending how fast the motility of species is suppressed by the signal; (2) in our research, we develop several new general techniques to study the density-dependent motility models, such as the variable transformation, several new Sobolev type inequalities, criterion for blowup or boundedness, and so on.

15303019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303019.value: Due to the complexity and technical barriers brought by the density-dependent motility, our researches mostly focus on the one or two-dimensional domains. In the future, the three or higher dimensional problem need to be studied. Also more applications of density-dependent motility can be explored so that they can be used to describe more ecological processes, like predator-prey dynamics.

15303019.value: In addition to the two well-known mechanisms ``diffusion-driven (Turing) instability" and ``chemotaxis-driven instability" that have been widely advocated to explain the exquisite pattern formation observed in nature, recently a so-called ``self-trapping’’ mechanism generating pattern formation was experimentally verified in [Liu et al, Science, 334: 238-241, 2011]. Apart from the biological interest, the mathematical understanding of the density-suppressed motility models large widely remains open except very few results obtained previously. This research project has developed several analytical tools/ideas to establish qualitative results at first for the density-suppressed motility models, including traveling wavefront solutions, stationary pattern solutions and blowup/boundedness phenomenon. Through these researches, the significant roles of the density-suppressed motility in producing rich patterns and describing observed phenomena has been further confirmed. 15303219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303219.value: 可充電鋰離子電池（LIB）技術已然成為便攜式電子設備以及電動汽車最重要的儲能係統之一。然而，傳統鋰電池的能量密度正逐漸接近其理論極限。因此，亟需開發新電池系統和更高容量的儲能技術。針對高能量密度電池，鋰硫電池（LSBs）因其極高的能量密度、成本效益以及環保性，而被認為是最有希望滿足日益增長的儲能係統需求的技術之一。但是，多硫化鋰的擴散是造成鋰硫電池低庫侖效率、循環穩定性差和容量衰減快的根本原因之一。這種現像也被稱為“穿梭效應” 。 有鑑於此，申請人團隊開發了一種新的方法來解決LSB中的穿梭效應，即使用黑磷量子點（BPQDS）來吸附和催化多硫化物轉化。結果表明，該類型LSB可表現出比目前已報導的LSB更優越的電化學性能，譬如碳硫複合陰極材料在0.1C下200次深循環後的可逆容量為1072 mA h g-1，在4C下的高速容量為784 mA h g-1，並且在含硫量高達8 mg cm-2情況下電池容量保持率仍接近90%。儘管參數著實客觀，但要滿足實際需求，LSB仍需進一步提高硫含量（>70 wt%）和負載量（>13 mg cm-2）以及低的電解質/硫（E/S）比（<4μl mg-1）。 基於前期工作，我們擬對黑磷量子點如何抑制LSB中多硫化物穿梭效應的潛在催化機理進行系統研究，以求獲得黑磷量子點增強LSB性能的本因。通過與浦航光源（韓國）合作，採用原位、離位等X射線同步輻射技術來研究BPQD與多硫化鋰間的相互作用，以獲得材料的形貌和晶體結構在LSBs的充放電過程中的演變。本研究工作將最終使我們能開發出基於BPQD/多孔碳/陰極聚合物的具有高硫含量和低E/S比的負載的新型陰極材料。同時，還將採用更優的方法來獲得高產率BPQD。該工作的完成將為設計下一代高性能和實用化的LSB儲能係統開闢新的途徑。

15303219.label: Realisation of objectives
15303219.value: Objective 1: The objective of optimizing the fabrication process of black phosphorus quantum dots in high yield has been realized through the following results. We demonstrated the mass production of few-layer black phosphorus (BP) nanosheets by irradiating pristine BP crystals with a pulsed laser in low-boiling point solvents such as methanol, ethanol, propanol, and hexane. The BP nanosheets prepared without additional ingredients exhibited a narrow and solvent-dependent thickness distribution and large lateral size. Additionally, monodispersed nanoparticles identified as amorphous BP were also produced. The exfoliation yield reached an impressive 93.7%, the highest reported value to date. The researchers further studied the effects of solvent type, laser irradiation time, and energy on the morphology of the produced nanosheets and nanoparticles to understand the mechanism of laser-assisted liquid-phase exfoliation of BP. The thickness-controlled few-layer BP nanosheets were then used as an anode in lithium-ion batteries (LIB) to investigate their morphological influence on BP-based LIB performance. The relationship between layer number, lateral size, cycling stability, Li+ ion transfer kinetics, and diffusivity was discussed. Furthermore, we studied the half/full-cell performance of a BP/graphene-based anode. The unique edge-selective catalytic properties of BP were also explored by preparing different-sized BP flakes through probe sonication and centrifugation of bulk BP crystals in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) solution. The concentrations of the BP solutions were controlled using inductive coupled plasma with atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES). Overall, the objective of optimizing the fabrication process of black phosphorus quantum dots in high yield was successfully realized through these results. Objective 2: The catalytic mechanism of BPQDs can be understood by examining the interactions between LiPSs and BP flakes. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and ultraviolet-visible (UV-Vis) absorption measurements were used to probe the nature of these interactions. XPS analysis revealed the presence of P-Li and P-S bonds, indicating strong interactions between BPQDs and LiPSs. Additionally, a strong S-P bond was observed in the S2p spectrum. These results suggest that BPQDs strongly interact with LiPSs through both P-S and P-Li bonds, leading to high absorptivity between the materials. Static adsorption experiments further confirmed the superior absorptivity of BPQDs compared to other BP samples. The increased number of edge sites on the BPQDs is suggested to contribute to this significant difference in absorptivity. DFT calculations were performed to quantify the relative absorptivity between terrace and edge sites of BPQDs with LiPS. The results showed that LiPS adsorbed at edge sites had significantly larger binding energies compared to terrace sites. Bader charge analysis indicated a stronger covalent character of bonds formed between BP edges and LiPS, attributed to the high reactivity of under-coordinated P-atoms at the zig-zag terminated edges. The exposed edge area of BP flakes can be increased by downsizing BP, leading to a higher number of particles and improved Sedge/Swhole ratio. These findings suggest that metal-free BP flakes with QD structures and numerous edge sites are ideal for maximizing the active catalytic sites for LiPS adsorption and conversion reactions in LSBs. Objective 3: To design and fabricate high-performance cathodes that can achieve high sulfur contents and loadings with low electrolyte/sulfur ratios, we conducted in-situ Raman and optical microscope observations to understand the nucleation and growth dynamics of sulfur on a graphene substrate. We observed the formation of metastable liquid sulfur, followed by the appearance of single- and polycrystalline sulfur particles as the micro-electrochemical cells were further charged. By quantifying the growth dynamics of liquid sulfur droplets, we found that their size and number density were influenced by the applied current, while the areal capacities remained largely unaffected. This discovery suggests that the growth of liquid sulfur is less dependent on the substrate surface area, indicating the potential for fast-charging liquid-sulfur cathodes. As a proof-of-concept, we successfully prepared CNF/Li2S8 cathodes that enabled a liquid sulfur-associated Li-S system to achieve high fast charging, even at high loadings (4.2 mg/cm2) and low E/S ratio (9.5 L/mg). This performance rivals the state-of-the-art high-rate performance reported in the literature. Overall, our findings on liquid-sulfur electrochemistry open up a new avenue for the development of fast-charging Li-S batteries.

15303219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303219.value: (i) A highly efficient method for the scalable production of few-layered black phosphorus (BP) nanosheets using a pulsed laser in low-boiling point solvents has been developed. (ii) The layer number and lateral size of the nanosheets can be precisely controlled by changing the laser irradiation time, energy, and solvent type. (iii) The excellent control of the BP nanosheets enables morphological effects on Li-ion battery performance to be studied. (iv) Low layer numbers benefit both charge transfer and Li+ ion diffusion, while a high aspect ratio can improve the charge transfer and increase the Li+ ion diffusion path. (v) 1T MoS2 nanodots have been explored as powerful electrocatalysts to overcome the issue of shuttling and sluggish conversion of flooded polysulfides in high-energy lithium sulfur batteries (LSBs). (vi) The surface and Mo-terminated edges of 1T MoS2 provide stronger anchor sites for Li2S, a lower Li–S decomposition barrier, and faster Li ion migration than those for the 2H phase. (vii) In the presence of a small amount of 1T MoS2 nanodots, porous carbon/Li2S6 cathodes exhibited remarkable electrochemical performance, retaining a capacity of 9.3 mA h cm_2 over 300 cycles under high sulfur loading of 12.9 mg cm_2 and a low electrolyte/sulfur ratio of 4.6 L mg-1. (viii) Entire liquid sulfur generation on hydrogen-annealed MoS2 (H2-MoS2) has been reported, even under harsh conditions of large overpotentials and low working temperatures. (ix) The origins of the solely liquid sulfur formation are the weakened interactions between H2-MoS2 and sulfur molecules and the decreased electrical polarization on the edges of the H2-MoS2. (x) The H2 annealing treatment can induce sulfur vacancies on the basal plane and partial oxidation on the edge of TMDs, which facilitates liquid sulfur formation. (xi) Liquid sulfur can be generated on H2-MoS2 flakes at an ultralow temperature of −50 °C, which provides a possible development of low-temperature lithium−sulfur batteries. (xii) A quantitative correlation between the size and number density of liquid sulfur droplets and the applied current has been discovered. (xiii) The areal capacities exhibited less sensitivity to the applied current. (xiv) By incorporating liquid sulfur into Li−S batteries with a high sulfur loading of 4.2 mg cm−2, the capacity retention can reach ∼100%, even when increasing the rate from 0.1 to 3 C.

15303219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303219.value: The results arising from the project are highly encouraging for practical applications. Based on these findings, the proposed course of action is to scale up the fabrication process of black phosphorus quantum dots (BPQDs) and further develop lithium-sulfur (Li-S) batteries into pouch cells. This will involve optimizing the process for large-scale production of BPQDs and integrating them into battery designs. The capacity, recyclability, and fast charging ability of these Li-S batteries will be thoroughly evaluated to assess their performance and feasibility for real-world applications. By conducting these evaluations, we can gain a better understanding of the potential of these batteries and identify any areas for improvement. This will pave the way for the future development and commercialization of high-performance Li-S batteries that can meet the demands of various industries and applications.

15303219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15303219.value: We optimized the process of creating black phosphorus quantum dots (BPQDs) with a high yield using a pulsed laser and low-boiling point solvents. This resulted in the production of few-layer black phosphorus nanosheets and amorphous black phosphorus nanoparticles, achieving a record high exfoliation yield of 93.7%. We investigated the effects of solvent type, laser parameters, and energy on the morphology of the nanosheets and nanoparticles. Additionally, we studied the interactions between BPQDs and lithium polysulfides (LiPSs), finding strong bonds between them and high absorptivity. By downsizing BP, we increased the exposed edge area, leading to improved catalytic sites for LiPS adsorption and conversion reactions. In our efforts to design high-performance cathodes for lithium-sulfur batteries, we observed the nucleation and growth dynamics of sulfur on a graphene substrate. Liquid sulfur formed first, followed by single- and polycrystalline sulfur particles. The growth of liquid sulfur was less dependent on substrate surface area, indicating potential for fast-charging liquid-sulfur cathodes. We successfully prepared cathodes enabling high fast charging, even at high loadings and low electrolyte/sulfur ratios. These findings open up possibilities for the development of fast-charging lithium-sulfur batteries with high sulfur contents and loadings.

15303319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303319.value: Panel count data and interval-censored data are two types of incomplete data that often occur in event history studies. Almost all existing statistical methods are developed for their analysis separately. In this project, we investigate more complicated situations where recurrent event processes and interval-censored failure events occur together. The effect of failure events on recurrent events should be considered for these cases, and thus the joint analysis of panel count data with interval-censored data becomes more challenging since the data structure is more complicated. The aim of this project is to develop some new nonparametric and semiparametric methods for jointly analyzing panel count data with interval-censored failure time data. First, we propose a failure time-dependent mean model for nonparametric analysis of panel count data through a completely unspecified link function, develop a two-stage sieve likelihood-based estimation procedure for nonparametric estimation of a baseline mean function of a recurrent event process and an unknown link function, and discuss the asymptotic properties of the resulting estimators. Second, we construct new tests for multi-sample nonparametric comparison problem based on panel count data with an interval-censored failure event, and establish the asymptotic theory of the proposed test statistics. Third, we propose a failure time-dependent proportional mean model for semiparametric regression analysis of panel count data, develop a two stage likelihood-based inference procedure for estimation of both unknown functions and regression coefficients, and explore the theoretical properties of the proposed estimators. Furthermore, we propose a failure time-dependent nonparametric regression model for the analysis of panel count data and develop the corresponding inference procedure. The novel models can intuitively and clearly explain the relationship between the recurrent current process and the failure time. However these novel models result in complicated likelihood functions and bring new challenging theoretical and computational questions in statistics that require more innovative research efforts. These challenges will be addressed by using the modern empirical process theory for asymptotic properties and adapting a generalized gradient projection algorithm for optimizing a nonlinear objective function with linear inequality for computation. The performance of the proposed new models and estimation procedures will be evaluated by means of Monte Carlo simulation studies. Some real data sets, such as the skin cancer data that motivate the proposed research, will be analyzed and presented as illustrative examples. The proposed project will yield new methods for the analysis of panel count data in the presence of interval-censored failure event. 面板計數數據和區間刪失數據是事件歷史研究中經常出現的兩種類型的不完整數據。幾乎所有現有的統計方法都是單獨分析的。在這個項目中，我們研究複雜事件過程和區間刪失事件一起發生的更複雜的情況。對於這些情況，應考慮失敗事件對複發事件的影響，因此，由於數據結構更複雜，面板計數數據與間隔刪失數據的聯合分析變得更具挑戰性。該項目的目的是對於面板計數數據和區間刪失數據聯合分析，開發一些新的非參數和半參數方法。首先，我們通過一個完全未指定的鏈接函數提出了一個用於面板計數數據非參數分析的失效時間依賴平均模型，開發了一個基於兩階段基於似然的估計程序，用於重複事件過程的基線平均函數和一個未知的鏈接函數的非參數估計，並討論估計的漸近性質。其次，我們基於具有區間刪失事件的面板計數數據構建了多樣本非參數比較問題的新測試，並建立了所提出的測試統計量的漸近理論。第三，我們提出了面板計數數據半參數回歸分析的失效時間依賴比例均值模型，開發了一個基於兩階段的基於似然的推斷程序來估計未知函數和回歸係數，並探討了所提出的估計量的理論性質。此外，我們提出了一種失效時間依賴的非參數回歸模型，用於分析面板計數數據並開發相應的推斷程序。新穎的模型可以直觀，清晰地解釋復發事件過程與失效時間之間的關係。然而，這些新穎的模型導致複雜的似然函數，帶來新的挑戰性理論和計算問題，因此需要更多創新研究工作。這些挑戰將通過使用現代經驗過程理論的漸近性質和適應廣義梯度投影算法來優化具有線性不等式的非線性目標函數來解決。擬議的新模型和估算程序的性能將通過蒙特卡羅模擬研究進行評估。將分析一些真實數據集，例如激發所提議研究的皮膚癌數據，作為說明性示例。擬議項目將產生用於分析在存在區間刪失事件情況下的面板計數數據的新方法。

15303319.label: Realisation of objectives
15303319.value: We have worked on all four objectives of this project. First, we proposed a failure time-dependent mean model through a completely unspecified link function, while the existing methods for the informative failure event are based on the latent variable model, which provides indirect interpretation for the effect of failure event. To overcome the challenges arising from the blending of nonparametric components and parametric regression coefficients, we developed a two-stage conditional expected likelihood-based estimation procedure for model parameters based on panel count data and interval-censored data, and established the consistency, the convergence rate and the asymptotic normality of the proposed two-stage estimator. Second, we designed new multi-sample tests for panel count data with an interval-censored failure event. Extensive simulation studies were carried out and suggested that the proposed approaches work well for practical situations. Third, we proposed a sieve maximum likelihood method for estimating regression parameters in the additive hazards regression with general interval-censored data. Fourth, we developed a data driven subgroup analysis procedure for the heterogeneous Cox model by constructing a pairwise fusion penalized partial likelihood-based objective function without requiring any prior knowledge about the subgroup structure. Fifth, we proposed three model averaging approaches for the high-dimensional Cox proportional hazards regression with censored survival data. Sixth, we investigated the problem of hypothesis testing in high-dimensional linear regression and single-index models. For the ultrahigh-dimensional linear regression and single-index models, we constructed F-statistics based on lower dimensional random projections of the data, and establish the asymptotic null distribution and the asymptotic local power function of the proposed test statistics for the hypothesis testing of global and partial parameters. Seventh, we investigated a more general situation where a partly interval-censored failure event is informative to recurrent events. For the analysis of such data, we proposed a failure time-dependent proportional mean model through an unspecified link function. For estimation of model parameters, we considered a conditional expectation of least squares function to overcome the challenges from partly interval-censoring, and developed a two-stage estimation procedure by treating the distribution function of the failure time as a functional nuisance parameter and using the B-spline functions to approximate unknown baseline mean and link functions. Furthermore, we derived the overall convergence rate of the proposed estimators and established the asymptotic normality of finite-dimensional estimator and functionals of infinite-dimensional estimator. The proposed estimation procedure was evaluated by extensive simulation studies, in which the finite-sample performances coincide with the theoretical results. We illustrated our method with a longitudinal healthy longevity study and offered some insightful conclusions. Our simulation and application results demonstrated that the proposed methods perform well. We have achieved all the objectives of this project.

15303319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15303319.value: For nonparametric and semiparametric inference of recurrent event processes with panel count data in the presence of informative interval-censored failure time events, we have proposed a flexible and intuitive conditional mean model through a completely unspecified link function. We have developed a novel two-stage estimation procedure using the conditional expectation of log-likelihood to overcome the challenges arising from the complexity of data structure and likelihood function under a working model. The asymptotic properties of the proposed two-stage estimator have been established and applied to construct a class of test statistics for multiple-sample comparison. The asymptotic null distributions of the proposed test statistics have been derived and the good power properties of the tests have been demonstrated through extensive simulation studies. In particular, all theoretical results do not rely on the Poisson process assumption under a working model. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to analyze panel count data with informative partly interval-censored failure event. For the analysis, we have proposed a failure time-dependent proportional mean model for a recurrent event process with panel count data and partly interval-censored data. We have considered the conditional expectation of least squares function to overcome the difficulty arising from interval-censoring and developed a two-stage estimation procedure by treating the distribution function of the failure time as a functional nuisance parameter. We have derived the overall convergence rate of the proposed estimators and establish the asymptotic normality of both finite-dimensional estimator and functionals of infinite-dimensional estimator under the general conditions on the asymptotic properties for the estimator of functional nuisance parameter. For the analysis of general interval-censored failure time data arising from case-cohort studies, we have proposed a new and more general variable selection approach under a class of flexible semiparametric transformation models that allows for dependent interval censoring. We have developed a random projection approach for hypothesis testing in a high-dimensional linear regression and nonlinear single-index models. We have studied a class of regularized regression under the additive hazards model with censored survival data and propose a novel approach to achieve simultaneous group selection, variable selection, and parameter estimation for high-dimensional censored data. In summary, 12 research papers associated with this project have been published/submitted in international peer-reviewed journals (Journal of the American Statistical Association, Journal of Machine Learning Research, Biometrics, Bernoulli, Statistica Sinica, Electronic Journal of Statistics, Statistics in Medicine, etc.), and also presented in the international conferences.

15303319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15303319.value: (1) Our new models developed in this project can be used to make better understanding of important features from recurrent event processes. (2) The proposed approaches can be extended to dealing with more general semiparametric models with both low- and high-dimensional vectors of covariates, where a nonlinear covariate effect can be estimated by using deep neural networks instead of B-spline functions. (3) Our developed model averaging approach and greedy model averaging algorithm for the high-dimensional Cox proportional hazards regression can be extended to other high-dimensional survival models. (4) Our developed random projection-based effective approach to hypothesis testing is useful for statistical inference in high-dimensional models.

15303319.value: In this project, we have investigated nonparametric and semiparametric inference problems with a general situation where a recurrent event process is related to an informative interval-censored failure event. This research is significant in that it addresses more general situations which often occur in the real world but have not been adequately studied in the literature. A key advantage of our developed approach over existing methods is that it provides the explicit relationship between a recurrent event process and a failure event under the same observation scheme. The results of this project have a significant impact because they have filled the gap in the literature on panel count survival data analysis, and are also important to practical applications in economics, genetics, medicine, and public health. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to develop a class of tests for comparison of mean functions of panel count data with informative interval-censored failure event as well as investigate a recurrent event process with panel count data in the presence of informative partly interval-censored failure time data.

15303519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15303519.value: The bacterial cell wall is an essential structure for the survival of bacteria as it gives the bacteria their shape and protects the bacteria from osmotic lysis. The cell wall consists of peptidoglycan, which are glycan strands cross-linked by peptide linkages. Lipid II, a lipid-linked disaccharide-polypeptide, is the precursor for peptidoglycan biogenesis. Lipid II is synthesized by various enzymes in the cytoplasm. It is then transported across the cell membrane, the lipid tail is released and the disaccharide-polypeptide is polymerized to produce the peptidoglycan for cell wall construction. MurJ is the enzyme (the ‘flippase’) responsible for transporting lipid II across the cell membrane in bacteria. However, how MurJ interacts with lipid II and undergoes conformational change during the transport of lipid II from the inside to the outside of the membrane is not well understood. This proposal aims to study the structure and conformational change of the MurJ protein upon interaction with lipid II by H/D exchange mass spectrometry. H/D exchange mass spectrometry is an important methodology to probe the conformations and dynamics of proteins. Wild type MurJ which favors the inward-facing conformation and MurJ mutants which may stabilize the outward-facing conformation will be prepared by protein expression and their difference in solvent exposure will be studied by H/D exchange mass spectrometry. The interaction of MurJ with lipid II under different pH and sodium ion concentrations will also be investigated to probe whether protons and/or sodium ions are required in the flipping of lipid II. By comparing the isotope exchange pattern in D2O buffers of non-complexed protein with that of the complexed form, information on the different conformations of the protein can be obtained. The success of this project will lead to a better understanding of the mechanism and the conformational change of MurJ in the transport of lipid II across the membrane.

15304019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304019.value: In the big data era, there is a compelling need for solving increasingly larger scale mathematical optimization problems, especially those from the rapidly developing areas such as machine learning, imaging science, and statistics. Historically, convex optimization problems arising from these applications have been extensively studied from both the theoretical and computational aspects, and efficient numerical solvers for solving the corresponding convex optimization problems have been developed at a very fast pace. On the other hand, especially recently, nonconvex optimization has played an increasingly more important role in these applications. Nevertheless, even nonconvex optimization has been studied for several decades, the computational nonconvex optimization is far from its maturity, at least for the radically larger scale problems in the big data settings. Therefore, much research is needed, for dealing with the burgeoning appeals of solving nonconvex optimization problems, especially for large-scale (often nondifferentiable) problems with realistic data. In this proposal, we propose to study an important class of nonconvex optimization problems–the multi-difference-of-convex problems (MDCPs). This model includes many problems arising from contemporary big data applications such as the multi-convex optimization, the regularized matrix factorization problem and the regularized versions of the deep linear networks. Specifically, we will develop in-depth theoretical results and powerful scalable solvers for various important instances of the MDCP. Given the fact that in practice, nonconvex optimization problems can hardly be solved to global optimality, in this proposal we focus on computing sharp stationary points. In order to achieve our goals and based on the structure of the MDCP, we will design a multi-majorization-minimization (MMM) method of the block coordinate descent manner for solving the MDCP and establish the convergence of the proposed method to directional stationary points. Moreover, once the outer loops and the subproblems are determined, we will mainly pay our attention to efficiently solving them. Leveraging our previous works, we will explore various effective strategies to solve these subproblems. In particular, by exploiting the potential sparse structures such as the second-order sparsity exhibited in both the solutions and the problem data, we plan to develop sparse nonsmooth Newton-type algorithms to solve the corresponding subproblems. Additionally, we will also study the statistical properties of the computed solutions and the stochastic version of the proposed algorithms. It is highly expected that the combination of these strategies will make the MMM method to be very efficient and robust in solving large-scale MDCPs. 在大數據時代，越來越多的大規模數學優化問題急切地需要高效快速地求解，特別是來自機器學習、影像處理、高維統計等快速發展的領域中的實際問題。眾所周知，對於這些應用中產生的凸優化問題，大量的研究人員從理論和計算兩方面已進行了廣泛的研究，並迅速發展出求解相應凸優化問題的高效數值求解器。另一方面，尤其是在近年來，非凸優化在這些應用中發揮著越來越重要的作用。然而，即使非凸優化問題的研究已經進行了幾十年，其數值計算方法，至少對大數據背景下的大規模優化問題來說，還遠遠不夠成熟。因此，我們需要進行大量的研究，來處理非凸優化問題中出現的新興的需求，特別是對於具有實際數據背景的大規模（目標函數通常是不可微的）優化問題。 本研究項目將主要研究一類非常重要的非凸優化問題--多重凸差問題（MDCP）。該問題模型包括當代大數據應用中出現的多塊凸優化、正則化矩陣分解問題以及正則化的深度線性網路等問題。具體來說，我們在理論結果和強大的可擴展的數值計算求解器兩方面來深入研究MDCP的各種重要實際問題。 由於在實際應用中，非凸優化問題很難得到全域最優解，因此本研究項目首先將關注如何計算更具實際意義的穩定點。為了實現這一目標，我們將基於MDCP的結構，設計一種分塊座標下降方式的多塊主優化(MMM)方法來求解MDCP，並將完成MMM方法收斂到方向穩定點的收斂性分析。此外一旦確定了MMM方法的外部循環以及子問題的形式，我們將重點關注如何有效快速地求解這些子問題。鑒於我們已有的工作基礎，我們將探索各種有效策略來求解這些子問題。特別地，我們將充分利用子問題潛在的稀疏結構，例如子問題的解和數據中表現出的二階稀疏性，來開發稀疏非光滑牛頓型算法來求解相應的子問題。此外我們還將研究MDCP的解的統計性質，並進一步給出所提出算法的隨機版本。這些有效策略的結合，使得我們有理由預期MMM方法在求解大規模的MDCP上表現地非常高效和魯棒。

15304019.label: Realisation of objectives
15304019.value: We have achieved all the proposed research objectives of this project. Details are summarized below: Objective 1: Our investigation delves into various first-order necessary optimality conditions pertinent to nonsmooth nonconvex and multi-block optimization, with a specific focus on Frechet-stationarity, directional stationarity, and the Nash point. Objective 2: We present four distinct variants of Alternating-type Majorization-Minimization Algorithms (AMMA), each rooted in block-type over-approximations of the multi-block DC function via linearization and Bregman-type regulariza- tion. The convergence properties of the generated sequences by AMMA are rigorously analyzed, and under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property, we establish the rate of convergence. Furthermore, we elucidate the connections between AMMA and several existing algorithms. Objective 3: We developed several efficient and provable algorithms to solve the involved subproblems. In particular, for a wide class of MDCPs arising from applications (e.g., risk management, image processing), we developed the efficient nonsmooth Newton method. Objective 4: We have developed efficient solvers for several important applications, including risk management, convex regression with shape constraints, graph learning problem, image processing problems.

15304019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304019.value: Objective 1: The research has rigorously explored first-order necessary optimality conditions for nonsmooth nonconvex and multi-block optimization, focusing on Fréchet-stationarity, directional stationarity, and the Nash point (Paper 6). This exploration has led to a deeper understanding of the optimality conditions for the MDCPs, providing a theoretical foundation for further algorithmic development. Objective 2: A novel class of Alternating-type Majorization-Minimization Algorithms (AMMA) has been introduced, leveraging the block-type DC structure of the MDCP (Paper 6). The convergence properties of AMMA have been rigorously analyzed, establishing the rate of convergence under the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property. Additionally, a proximal majorization-minimization (PMM) algorithm has been developed, with theoretical guarantees for global convergence to a critical point, enhancing the algorithmic framework for solving MDCPs (Papers 1,3,,5). Objective 3: Efficient numerical algorithms have been implemented, including the design of sparse second-order methods for subproblems and the use of semismooth Newton methods (Paper 1, Paper 2, 3, 5). The research has explored several strategies to control the number of convex subproblems in each iteration, demonstrating robust performance and convergence behavior in practical scenarios such as face synthesis and graph learning under the Laplacian constraint (Paper 3, Paper 5). Objective 4: The extensive numerical experiments and the implementation of various algorithms suggest significant progress towards computational tools that could be integrated into a software package for MDCPs. These tools have been tested on both synthetic and real datasets, indicating their potential for promoting cooperation and exchange between academia and industry. The algorithms developed have shown superior performance in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency compared to existing state-of-the-art methods, particularly in applications such as convex regression, polynomial decomposition, and low-rank tensor completion (Paper 2, Paper 7, Paper 1). In summary, the project has made substantial contributions to the understanding of optimality conditions for MDCPs, the design and convergence analysis of novel algorithms, and the development of efficient numerical methods for solving complex subproblems, laying the groundwork for future software development aimed at solving MDCPs.

15304019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304019.value: 1. Generalized Optimality Conditions: Extend the study of optimality conditions to more generalized forms, such as second-order necessary and sufficient conditions, for nonsmooth nonconvex and multi-block optimization problems. 2. Algorithmic Acceleration and Complexity Analysis: Explore various acceleration techniques, such as Nesterov's acceleration, or adaptive step-size methods, to enhance the performance of Alternating-type Majorization-Minimization Algorithms (AMMA). Conduct a thorough complexity analysis to establish theoretical guarantees on the convergence rates and computational efficiency of the accelerated AMMA. 3. Higher-Order Tensor Applications: For important applications, such as robust low-rank tensor completion problems, extend the study to higher-order tensors. This is particularly relevant for real datasets that are higher-order tensors, such as color videos or traffic data.

15304019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304019.value: In the big data era, tackling large-scale mathematical optimization problems is crucial, especially in machine learning, imaging science, statistics, and so on. Traditional focus on convex optimization, with its predictable outcomes, is shifting towards the more complex nonconvex optimization due to modern data's intricacies. This project focuses on multi-difference-of-convex problems (MDCPs), prevalent in big data applications. Our goal is to advance theoretical knowledge and develop scalable algorithms for MDCPs. We've designed a multi-majorization-minimization (MMM) method to efficiently find high-quality solutions amidst MDCPs' complexities. Enhanced by algorithms that exploit data's sparse structures, our approach significantly improves solution efficiency and effectiveness. Rigorous development and testing on real-world datasets have shown our project's substantial progress in solving nonconvex optimization problems, contributing both to theoretical optimization and practical, domain-spanning algorithms.

15304119.value: Study the formation and characterization of RVG29-conjugated, diethyl sulfide modified zein nanoencapsulation of Ang-(1-7) (RDZA). (i) Synthesis of RVG29-SMCC-zein using zein, sulfo-SMCC, and sulfhydryl-containing RVG29 (RVG29-Cys) (Scheme 1). (ii) Synthesis of RVG29-SMCC-zein-Des using RVG29-SMCC-zein, 4-nitrophenyl chloroformate, 2-2’-thiodiethanol, and 2-2’-thiobis(ethylamine) (Scheme 2). (iii) Self-assembly of RVG29-SMCC-zein-Des to encapsulate Ang-(1-7) to form RZDA using phase separation method (Scheme 3). (iv) Structure characterizations of RZDA will be conducted using SEM and TEM. The size and zeta-potential of the RZDA will be measured by DLS. Study the in vitro stability and ROS-responsive triggered release of RZDA. (i) The in vitro stability of RZDA will be studied on the release of Ang-(1-7) from RZDA in PBS with and without serum, respectively. (ii) The in vitro ROS-responsive triggered release will be studied using H2O2 as the oxidation trigger. (iii) The released Ang-(1-7) will be measured using HPLC and LC-MS. The structure and size changes of the RZDA will be observed using SEM. The triggered release profiles will be built. Study the in vitro neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects, and cellular uptake of RZDA using the cell model of transient focal ischemic stroke. (i) The in vitro neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects of RZDA will be studied using the primary neuronal cell exposed to oxygen-glucose-deprivation (OGD) to mimic in vitro transient focal ischemic stroke. (ii) The neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects after RZDA treatment will be interpreted on the apoptosis and necrosis conditions of the cells, which will be visualized using a fluorescent microscope with the help of fluorescent stains, including propidium iodide (PI) and Hoechst 33258. In vivo study of the pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and neurotrophic and neuroprotective efficacy of RZDA using the MCAO animal model. (i) Normal SD rats and MCAO SD rats will be used for the in vivo studies. (ii) Pharmacokinetics: RZDA and Ang-(1-7) will be administered to SD rat model via tail vein injection. At selected time points, blood samples will be collected and measured. (iii) Biodistribution: RZDA, Ang-(1-7), and Coumarin-6 labeled RZDA will be administered to MCAO SD rat model. At predefined time points, the rats will be sacrificed and various organ samples, including brain, will be obtained and measured. In vivo imaging and CLSM images of brain tissue slices will be investigated for the biodistribution and BBB penetration of RDZA. (iv) The neurotrophic and neuroprotective efficacy: RZDA and Ang-(1-7) will be administered to MCAO SD rat model. The neurological deficits of the rats will be tested using behavioral assessments.

(i) Normal SD rats and MCAO SD rats will be used for the in vivo studies. (ii) Pharmacokinetics: RZDA and Ang-(1-7) will be administered to SD rat model via tail vein injection. At selected time points, blood samples will be collected and measured. (iii) Biodistribution: RZDA, Ang-(1-7), and Coumarin-6 labeled RZDA will be administered to MCAO SD rat model. At predefined time points, the rats will be sacrificed and various organ samples, including brain, will be obtained and measured. In vivo imaging and CLSM images of brain tissue slices will be investigated for the biodistribution and BBB penetration of RDZA. (iv) The neurotrophic and neuroprotective efficacy: RZDA and Ang-(1-7) will be administered to MCAO SD rat model. The neurological deficits of the rats will be tested using behavioral assessments.

15304119.value: 基于植物的天然食品材料具有良好的生物相容性、生物可降解性、完全無毒無副作用等優點，作為藥物載體具有巨大的潜力。屬於FDA公認的安全類別（GRAS）。作為一種藥物載體，其臨床試驗可以比其他載體更直接、更快速，對藥物的開發和遞送具有重要意義。選擇一種作為藥物載體的天然食品生物高分子，它應具有最佳的化學、生物和形態特性，以具備多功能的遞送效果。 缺血性中風是世界範圍內人口死亡或致殘的主要致病原因之一。儘管已有幾十年的研究歷史，但由於藥物的副作用、給藥過程中的對藥物保護不足以及藥物在腦缺血部位的低積累量，現時還沒有一種安全有效的藥物治療方法。靶向和刺激響應型藥物傳遞系統是治療缺血性腦卒中的重要策略，它可以將藥物傳遞到特定的疾病部位，在細胞內受到環境刺激釋放藥物。從礦權病毒糖蛋白（RVG）中選取的一種功能肽RVG29被報導能有效地增强各種藥物的腦傳遞。由於在缺血性卒中期間和之後的活性氧（ROS）的快速增加，添加與ROS易反應的二乙基硫醚（DES）單元和RVG可使得顆粒既具有靶向性又具有刺激反應性的釋放特性。此外，設計成自組裝納米粒子，利用其獨特的內吞途徑、尺寸和表面性質，在藥物負載和細胞攝取方面具有優勢。 玉米醇溶蛋白（zein）具有生物相容性好、生物可降解、不吸水、比其他天然生物大分子穩定不易被體內消化等優點，是製備藥物緩釋納米系統的良好選擇。此外，它還可以自組裝，易於修飾和與藥物和官能團結合。我們將使用模型藥物Ang-(1-7)製備RVG29結合DES修飾zein納米載藥顆粒RZDA，用於治療缺血性卒中。我們在基於玉米醇溶蛋白的生物合成產物和納米顆粒的表面改性以及體內外評估方面有著豐富的經驗。RZDA將按以下步驟形成：（i）合成zein、磺基七氯化釤和RVG29-cys以形成RVG29-SMCC-zein，（ii）合成RVG29-SMCC-zein、4-硝基苯基氯甲酸酯、2-2'-硫代二乙醇和2-2'-硫代二（乙胺）以形成RVG29-SMCC-zein-Des，（iii）RVG29-SMCC-zein-Des自組裝封裝Ang-(1-7)形成RZDA。所製備的RZDA具有以下幾個關鍵特徵：（i）通過RVG29靶向大腦；（ii）Des引起ROS反應實現觸發釋放；（iii）zein納米粒子實現長時間緩慢釋放；以及（iv）生物降解性和生物相容性。我們將使用短暫性局灶性缺血性腦卒中細胞模型，檢測RZDA的體外穩定性和ROS敏感型觸發釋放，研究RZDA的體外神經營養和神經保護作用以及細胞攝取。我們還將利用缺血性卒中動物模型研究RZDA的體內藥代動力學、生物分佈、神經營養和神經保護作用。

15304119.label: Realisation of objectives
15304119.value: 1). Study the formation and characterization of RVG29-conjugated, diethyl sulfide modified zein nanoencapsulation of Ang-(1-7) (RDZA) The objectives were completely achieved. Two particles were synthesised. (i) Synthesis a. To synthesis zein-RVG-Dac_NP (nanoparticle), Zein was reacted with sulfo-SMCC and sulfhydryl-containing RVG29. Then, the compound was reacted with 4-nitrophenyl chloroformate and 4-nitrophenyl chloroformate to form bis(4-nitrophenyl) diethyl sulfide; and then bis(4-nitrophenyl) diethyl sulfide and 2-2’-thiobis(ethylamine) was reacted with RVG29-SMCC-zein-nitrophenyl carbonate. The self-assembly of RVG29-SMCC-zein to encapsulate Dac to form zein-RVG-Dac_NP was conducted using phase separation method. b. To synthesis rPZDCu (Cu4.6O@zein-Se-Se-DHA@PLM@rt-PA), Cu4.6O was synthesized by CuCl2 and ascorbic acid. Then, ZD (zein-Se-Se-DHA) was synthesized. In brief, sodium borohydride and selenium powder mixed and stirred in ice bath. Anhydrous tetrahydrofuran solution containing 3-bromo-1-propanol was added. The products were extracted with ethyl acetate and dried. Zein was reacted with the products along with DHA. Then the solution was purified and dialyzed against DMSO and DI water to obtain ZD. Then, the Cu4.6O particle was encapsulated by zein-Se-Se-DHA to form ZDCu (Cu4.6O@zein-Se-Se-DHA), and then coated by platelet cell membrane (PLM) to form PZDCu (Cu4.6O@zein-Se-Se-DHA@PLM). Finally, rt-PA was further conjugated on the PLM to form rPZDCu. (ii) Characterizations a. The structure characterization, size, PDI, and zeta-potential of zein-RVG-Dac_NP was studied. The yield of the synthesis of each step was measured using 1H-NMR and FTIR (Figure 1 &2). The encapsulation efficiency of Dac was measured using HPLC and LC-MS. The Encapsulation Efficiency (EE) and Loading Efficiency (LE) of the zein-RVG-Dac_NP were 77.9 ± 4.7% and 60.365 ± 3.2 mg/g, respectively. The conjugation efficiency of zein and RVG29 was 97.42 ± 0.18%, which indicated that the conjugation was successful and complete. b. The structural characterization of the NPs was studied using TEM. Cu4.6O NPs had a uniform size of 3.55 ± 0.83 nm. ZDCu NPs were perfect spheres with a uniform size of approximate 150 nm. One PZDCu NP displayed a coating of PLM with the thickness of 17.56 nm. The sizes of ZD, ZDCu, PZDCu, and rPZDCu NPs, which were 185.13 ± 1.72, 209.17 ± 3.19, 213.43 ± 17.34, and 225.56 ±19.15 nm, respectively, were studied using DLS. The zeta-potential of ZD, ZDCu, PZDCu, and rPZDCu measured by DLS were -14.17 ± 0.75, -15.37 ± 0.59, -22.03 ± 0.85, and -20.25 ± 1.12 mV, respectively. The crystalline structure of the Cu4.6O was characterized with XRD. XPS was further applied to study the composition of the NPs. It demonstrated the ratio of Cu2O and Cu in the NP was 0.39:1. The composition of the proteins in the range of molecular weight of 15~310 kDa was measured. (Figure 3) 2). Study the in vitro stability and ROS-responsive triggered release of RZDA. The objectives were completely achieved. For zein-RVG-Dac_NP, the stability of particles was studied. At 4°C, the particle size of nanoparticles gradually changed from 254.86nm to 262.22nm, while at 37°C, it changed from 254.86nm to 272.6nm. The change in particle size was negligible, which showed that the nanoparticles have good stability. The released drug content in cumulative releases of drug from particles was measured. As a result, 68.7% of Dac was released in gradual process within 120 hr. The NPs showed highest release in PBS with serum-pH 6.0. (Figure 4-6) To test the stability of rPZDCu, the hydrodynamics size and zeta potential of rPZDCu in biologically relevant media over seven days were measured continuously. The results showed that in PBS, the size of rPZDCu changed from 220 nm to 240 nm approximately. In the artificial cerebrospinal fluid (ACSF), the size of rPZDCu changed from 220 nm to 260 nm approximately. The zeta potential of rPZDCu was maintained at around -21mV in both PBS and ACSF. These results indicated that rPZDCu has a good stability. The in vitro ROS-responsive triggered release was studied. As a result, while the treatment of 1 mM of H2O2 for 12 h, the release amount of Cu from ZDCu and PZDCu were 65.91 ± 1.53% and 62.89 ± 4.05%, and the Cu release became 78.45 ± 3.18 % and 74.28 ± 4.24% after 48 h. After the treatment with 10 mM GSH for 12 h, the release amount of Cu from ZDCu and PZDCu were 74.50 ± 3.93% and 69.05 ± 2.47%, and the Cu release became 83.78 ± 2.36 % and 80.97 ± 4.36% after 48 h. (Figure 3) 3). Study the in vitro neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects, and cellular uptake of RZDA using the cell model of transient focal ischemic stroke. The objectives were completely achieved. Primary neuronal cell was obtained and exposed to oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD) to mimic the transient focal ischemic strokes. As a result, after the incubation of the cells in the OGD environment, the cell apoptosis rate was 11.92 ± 0.67 %. With the addition of ZD, ZDCu, PZDCu, and rPZDCu, the cell apoptosis rate decreased to 8.57 ± 0.37, 6.54 ± 0.42, 4.39 ± 0.26, and 4.36 ± 0.20 %, further confirming the in vitro cytoprotective properties of rPZDCu. The co-staining fluorescence imaging further confirmed the protective effect of rPZDCu on the OGD model cells. It was observed that the cells showed increased red fluorescence given by the propidium iodide, which stained dead cells, after the incubation in OGD environment. While the red fluorescence reduced after the treatments of ZD, ZDCu, PZDCu, and rPZDCu (Figure 7). The treatments of PZDCu and rPZDCu NPs led to the lowest amounts of apoptotic cells. 4). In vivo study of the pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and neurotrophic and neuroprotective efficacy of RZDA using the MCAO animal model. The objectives were completely achieved. The targeting and localization of the NPs in the brain tissues were studied using the CLSM. The PZDCu group exhibited a significantly higher fluorescence of the NPs in the brain tissues, which confirmed the effective brain targeting of the PZDCu at the thrombus. The PZDCu showed the highest intensity of the overlap of the red fluorescence and yellow fluorescence, indicating that PZDCu had good targeting at the fibrin-rich microthrombi (Figure 8). The therapeutic effect of rPZDCu for the treatment of ischemic stroke was evaluated using the rat embolic middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model. The neurological scores and the beam walking scores, which could assess the recovery of the rat models from the stroke, were obtained. As shown, both the neurological scores and the beam walking scores of certain NP treatment group were generally decreased as the time increased. The rPZDCu group displayed the lowest neurological score and beam walking score among the treatment groups, indicating that rPZDCu had the best therapeutic effects. The cumulative survival results of the rat models were obtained (Figure 9). The rPZDCu group showed the highest survival time. To further verify the in vivo therapeutic effect of rPZDCu for the treatment of ischemic stroke, the learning and memory of the rat models were assessed after the NP treatments. The Morris water maze test was conducted to evaluate the recovery of the rat from the ischemic stroke. As a result, after the NP treatments, the spatial memory ability of the rat was effectively recovered. In addition, the T2 mapping images of the brain of embolic MCAO rats were obtained (Figure 9). It was observed that after the treatments of the NPs, the rPZDCu group showed the smallest size of the infarct region.

15304119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304119.value: The study developed two novel nanoparticles and explore one of them in the treatment of stroke. One particle was the reaction of zein with sulfo-SMCC and sulfhydryl-containing RVG29, followed by the formation of bis(4-nitrophenyl) diethyl sulfide and its reaction with RVG29-SMCC-zein-nitrophenyl carbonate. The self-assembly of RVG29-SMCC-zein was used to encapsulate Dac through a phase separation method. For another particle, Cu4.6O NP was encapsulated by zein-Se-Se-DHA and coated by PLM, and rt-PA was further conjugated on the PLM to form rPZDCu. Characterizations were performed to analyze the structure, size, PDI, and zeta-potential of the RVG29-SMCC-zein. The yield of each synthesis step was measured using 1H-NMR and FTIR. The encapsulation efficiency of Dac in zein-RVG-Dac_NP was determined using HPLC and LC-MS, resulting in Encapsulation Efficiency (EE) and Loading Efficiency (LE) values of 77.9 ± 4.7% and 60.365 ± 3.2 mg/g, respectively. The conjugation efficiency of zein and RVG29 was found to be 97.42 ± 0.18%. Structural characterization of the rPZDCu was performed using TEM, revealing uniform sizes for Cu4.6O NPs and spherical shapes for ZDCu, PZDCu, and rPZDCu. DLS measurements were conducted to determine the sizes and zeta-potential of the particles, with average sizes ranging from 100 to 200 nm. The zeta-potential values indicated that the particles were stable and had good dispersion properties. The vitro stability and ROS-responsive release was studied. Zein-RVG-Dac_NP showed good stability in serum solution at both 4°C and 37°C. The release of Dac from the particles was measured in different pH conditions, and the highest release was observed in PBS with serum-pH 6.0. rPZDCu demonstrated stable hydrodynamic size and zeta potential in biologically relevant media over seven days. The release of Cu from ZDCu and PZDCu was triggered by H2O2 and GSH, showing release amounts proportional to the concentration and duration of treatment. The in vitro neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects of rPZDCu was determined. The particles (ZD, ZDCu, PZDCu, and rPZDCu) exhibited cytoprotective properties in an OGD model of transient focal ischemic stroke. The treatments reduced cell apoptosis rates and showed protective effects on OGD model cells. Fluorescence imaging confirmed the protective effect of rPZDCu on cell viability, with the lowest amount of apoptotic cells observed. rPZDCu showed effective brain targeting and localization in brain tissues, particularly at fibrin-rich microthrombi. rPZDCu demonstrated the best therapeutic effects in a rat embolic MCAO model, as assessed by neurological scores, beam walking scores, and survival time. The rats treated with rPZDCu exhibited improved spatial memory ability in the Morris water maze test. T2 mapping images showed that rPZDCu resulted in the smallest infarct region and reduced water content in the stroke area, indicating a good recovery effect on ischemic stroke. In conclusion, the study successfully synthesized and characterized zein-RVG-Dac_NP and rPZDCu particles. These particles demonstrated good stability, controlled release behavior, neurotrophic and neuroprotective effects in vitro, and therapeutic efficacy in an in vivo transient focal ischemic stroke model. These findings suggest the potential of RDZA as a promising therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke treatment.

15304119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304119.value: The research on RVG29-conjugated, diethyl sulfide modified zein nanoencapsulation of Dac and zein-Se-Se-DHA nanoencapsulation of Cu4.6O nanoparticles demonstrated promising potential for further development in the field of stroke. The successful synthesis and characterization of these nanoparticles, along with their desirable physicochemical properties, sustained release behavior, low cytotoxicity, and efficient cellular uptake, highlight their suitability for therapeutic applications. To further advance this research, several courses of action can be proposed. The versatility of the nanoparticle platform can be explored by investigating its potential for encapsulating and delivering other therapeutic agents or combinations of drugs. This could open up opportunities for personalized medicine approaches, combination therapy, or targeted delivery of various bioactive molecules. In addition to stroke, the application of these particles can be extended to other neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease. By targeting specific sites, these nanoparticles could serve as a foundation for the development of targeted drug delivery systems, making a significant impact on the field of medicine. Overall, the successful development of these nanoparticles and their potential for delivering therapeutic agents to the desired sites offer exciting prospects for future research and clinical applications in various neurological disorders.

15304119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304119.value: In this research, nanoparticles loaded with active compounds were developed, showing great potential for precise and effective drug delivery. The nanoparticles exhibited favorable structural properties and size, facilitating sustained release of the drugs. Notably, the nanoparticles demonstrated low toxicity and excellent cell compatibility in laboratory settings. The application of these nanoparticles was explored in the treatment of stroke, a highly dangerous condition that can lead to death, cognitive impairment, and mobility disabilities. Animal models were employed to study the therapeutic effects of the nanoparticles. Encouragingly, the nanoparticles were found to significantly mitigate cell death, reduce brain damage, and improve memory function in stroke. Overall, this research holds immense promise for the advancement of targeted drug delivery systems utilizing nanoparticles. With further studies and refinements, these nanoparticles could be harnessed to deliver drugs with enhanced effectiveness and precision, thus benefiting patients in the future.
