15304519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304519.value: Nonlinear optics is one of the most important topics in modern optical physics. It has a wide range of applications in the frequency control of lasers, super-resolution optical microscopy, nanoscale surface optics and biosensing. Second-harmonic generation (SHG) is the first discovered nonlinear optical effect that only occurs in physical systems possessing broken inversion symmetry. SHG in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) has become an extensively studied subject since the atomic thickness of monolayer TMDCs could scale the nonlinear optical devices down to the deep sub-wavelength scale, useful for on-chip all-optical signal processing and switching. Several notable studies have demonstrated the capability of enhancing and tuning the in-plane polarized SHG in monolayer TMDCs through applying electrical fields, charges and currents. While existing reports provide us some new perspectives on the generation and control of nonlinear optical effects in general TMDCs, more explicit theoretical understanding of those intriguing nonlinear phenomena is lacked. Moreover, it still remains greatly unexplored to induce and tune the out-of-plane polarized SHG in monolayer TMDCs. The present proposal aims to develop a comprehensive theoretical scenario depicting hot-electron injection induced out-of-plane polarized SHG in monolayer WS2, and also provides experimental verification. The theoretical study of this proposal will be carried out in collaboration with Prof. Peter Nordlander, Wiess Chair and Professor of Physics and Astronomy at Rice University. Specifically, we will use comprehensive lattice symmetry analysis to develop an analytical relation between plasmon mode strength, hot-electron generation and injection efficiency, and induced second-order nonlinear susceptibility in a WS2 monolayer sandwiched in a metallic particle-on-film nanocavity. To verify the theoretical prediction, we will carry out a static “pump-probe” experiment where a continuous wave laser at the plasmon resonance wavelength will be used to pump the hybrid nanocavity system for unidirectional injection of hot electrons from the metallic nanostructures to the WS2 layer while a femtosecond pulsed laser will simultaneously excite the system for SHG. Our recent study has corroborated the efficient generation of non-radiative plasmon-decay induced hot electrons and transport into a nearby semiconductor in a similar nanocavity system. Excitation and detection polarization-resolved SHG mapping and spectroscopy measurements as well as pump-probe power dependence will be carried out to elaborate the origin of the induced SHG. This project is expected to open up a new avenue for manipulating the SHG response of atomically thin TMDCs in an all-optical manner, with great applications potentially in TMDC-based nonlinear optical devices. 非線性光學是現代光學物理最重要的研究主題之一，應用極其廣泛，包括激光頻率控制、超分辨光學成像和納米尺度表面光學和生物傳感。二次諧波產生是最早發現的非線性光學現象，其通常發生在具有中心反演對稱破缺的晶體材料中。最近，二維過渡金屬硫族化合物中的二次諧波產生被深入研究，主要原因是單層過渡金屬硫族化合物有望將非線性光學器件尺寸縮小到原子層級厚度，這對片上全光信號處理和轉換非常有用。一些前期研究已經展示了利用外加電場、電荷和電流來增強和調控單層過渡金屬硫族化合物的二次諧波特性。盡管現有的實驗研究為我們理解一般過渡金屬硫族化合物中非線性光學效應提供了新的物理思路，對這些新奇光學現象的完整理論理解還有待發展。此外，如何誘導和調控單層過渡金屬硫族化合物中的面外偏振二次諧波還沒有被研究。此項目建議發展一套完整的物理圖像來描述熱電子註入誘導單層二硫化鎢的面外偏振二次諧波產生，並提供實驗驗證。申請人會和萊斯大學的Peter Nordlander教授合作完成項目的理論研究部分。具體來講，我們的研究系統是把單層的二硫化鎢夾在一個金屬顆粒-薄膜耦合的納米腔，在對此三明治結構進行全面的晶格對稱性分析的基礎上發展一套解析關系來描述等離激元模式強度和熱電子產生和註入效率以及熱電子誘導的二階非線性極化率。為了驗證這個理論預測，在實驗上我們會用連續激光來靜態泵浦此雜化系統產生和註入熱電子，同時用飛秒脈沖激光來激發系統的二次諧波產生。我們最近的研究已經證實一個半導體-金屬納米結構雜化系統在亞帶隙白光照射下可以有效產生表面等離激元非輻射衰減誘導的熱電子並轉移到鄰近的半導體材料。為了闡明雜化系統中誘導二次諧波產生的機制，我們會進行探測和收集偏振分辨的二次諧波成像和光譜測試，並研究二次諧波信號對靜態泵浦-探測激光功率的依賴性。此項目有望對原子層級厚度過渡金屬硫族化合物中二次諧波產生的操控開辟一個全新的全光控制途徑，對基於過渡金屬硫族化合物的非線性光學器件的發展產生重要影響。

15304519.label: Realisation of objectives
15304519.value: We have achieved the proposed project objectives by undertaking the planned research activities, with details summarized as follows. Results achieved (1) We successfully quantified the influence of electric potential on the second-order nonlinear response of 2D TMDCs, and demonstrated that the electrical field induced charge redistribution breaks the crystal symmetry to induce an out-of-plane second-order nonlinear susceptibility. To achieve the objective, we used first-principles density functional theory (DFT) to demonstrate that an out-of-plane electrostatic field induces out-of-plane second-order nonlinear susceptibility (χ_zxx=χ_zyy) in monolayer TMDCs (MoS2, MoSe2, WS2, WSe2). This induced susceptibility has a magnitude comparable to their intrinsic in-plane components (χ_yyy). The susceptibility peak values (χ_zxx^*, χ_yyy^*) with incident energy around half of the C exciton energy, show a linear dependence on the field strength. This behavior results from the combined effects of field-induced asymmetric out-of-plane charge density distribution and structural deformation, with the asymmetric charge distribution being the primary factor. We introduced a structural deformation descriptor τ, which linearly correlates with χ_zxx^*, to measure the out-of-plane dipole moment. Our study offers a straightforward method for generating and tuning out-of-plane second-order optical nonlinearity in monolayer TMDCs, opening new avenues for actively controlling their nonlinear optical processes. Results were published in Physical Review B, 2024, 109(7), 075417. (2) We successfully observed room-temperature emission from charged bi-excitons through injecting hot electrons from a single gold nano-sphere to a TMDC monolayer, and demonstrated that hot-electron injection is an effective method for altering the intrinsic carrier distribution and exciton states in 2D semiconductors. Inspired by the foregoing achievements, we explored the feasibility of applying hot-carrier injection to alter charge distribution in 2D materials and hence modulate their nonlinear responses. To do so, we firstly demonstrated the efficacy of hot-carrier injection from metal nanostructures into 2D materials. Resonantly exciting a gold nanosphere of 120 nm in diameter generates localized surface plasmons which partially produce hot carriers through non-radiative decay and inject into a contacting monolayer WS2 (through the metal–semiconductor Schottky junction) to alter its carrier characteristics. We found that resonant excitation caused a pronounced red shift in the hybrid system’s photoluminescence (PL) spectral peak compared to bare WS2, with intensity showing a super-linear dependence on the incident laser power density, indicating its biexciton nature. Our theoretical model estimated the hot-electron generation time at ~0.3 ps, much shorter than the exciton lifetime (~ns), confirming sufficiently fast injection of hot carriers to manipulate the exciton state. In contrast, non-resonant laser excitation produced no PL signal from charged biexcitons, highlighting the essential role of hot-electron injection played in the formation of the charged biexciton state. This work represents the first observation of room-temperature charged-biexciton emissions in monolayer TMDCs and confirms the high-efficiency ultrafast injection of hot electrons from metal nanostructures to layered TMDCs. Results were published in Physical Review Materials, 2023, 7(5), 054002. (3) We successfully observed the existence of hot-electron injection induced second-harmonic generation (SHG) in a TMDC bilayer sandwiched in a plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavity, and utilized polarization-resolved SHG intensity measurements to demonstrate the emergence of out-of-plane second-order nonlinear susceptibility. After showing the hot-electron injection altered charge distribution in 2D TMDCs, we proposed using it as a pseudo-electric field to regulate the second-order nonlinear response in a manner similar to an external electric field. We sandwiched a MoS2 bilayer within a gold nanoparticle-on-mirror (NPoM) cavity and the dark-field optical spectroscopy of this hybrid system revealed a gap plasmon mode at 800 nm and a transverse mode at 530 nm. We then used a 532 nm continuous-wave laser to excite the transverse mode for hot-carrier injection and the injected hot electrons were mainly concentrated in the MoS₂ layer in direct contact with the gold nanoparticle, breaking the inherent inversion symmetry of bilayer MoS2 and hence enabling SHG. Simultaneously, an 850 nm femtosecond laser beam was used to generate SHG to probe the second-order nonlinear response of the hybrid structure. As expected, SHG intensity increased when increasing the 532 nm laser power density (namely, the hot-electron injection density). To fully comprehend the aforementioned experimental observations, we performed the first-principles calculations and found that the magnitude of charge redistribution in the bilayer TMDC is proportional to the perpendicular electric-field strength, as are changes in second-order nonlinear susceptibility (both in-plane and out-of-plane components). Thus, when it turns to the case of hot-electron injection induced pseudo-electric field, we can assert that the magnitude of the induced second-order nonlinear susceptibility would also be directly proportional to the hot-carrier injection density. However, our experiments revealed that the induced effective second-order nonlinear coefficient does not scale linearly with the CW laser power density. To interpret this unexpected discrepancy, we proposed that injected hot carriers could form a capacitance-like structure between the metal nanoparticle and the locally charged TMDC area, impeding further injection of hot carriers. Based on this assumption, we developed a model to link hot-carrier generation with the second-order nonlinear coefficient, matching well with the experimental findings. Furthermore, the hot-electron injection will induce out-of-plane second-order nonlinear coefficients, transforming symmetric six-petal polarization-resolved SHG patterns into asymmetric ones. Experiments confirmed these asymmetric patterns, with a deduced ratio of out-of-plane to in-plane coefficients around 0.2. A manuscript reporting these results will be submitted soon. (4) To further expand the research scope of the original project objectives, we proposed a novel strain engineering approach to dramatically boost in-plane second-order susceptibility (χ_yyy) in monolayer WSe2 via a biaxial strain that tunes two excitons (the A exciton and a high-lying exciton (HX)) into double resonance. We first identified the exciton states from the 2D Mott-Wannier model and then employed the first-principles calculations to determine the exciton double resonance state from the absorbance spectrum of a monolayer WSe2 under uniform biaxial strain. Sophisticated strain-tuning of this state can yield a ~13-fold enhancement in χ_yyy compared to the unstrained counterpart. Further fine-tuning at the K valley can induce an even larger enhancement in χ_yyy, i.e., a giant ∼93-fold enhancement in the stronger double resonance effect with a relatively small biaxial tensile strain (0.30%). Our findings suggest new avenues for strain engineering of 2D materials optical properties and for novel nonlinear optoelectronics applications. Results were published in Physical Review B 2024 109(24), 245412. (5) Finally, beyond the original project objectives, we found that the DFT remains time consuming when computing the band structure of a TMDC monolayer under an ergodic strain level. To address this long-standing issue, we developed a modified Slater-Koster tight-binding model that can incorporate the strain effect. Strain-dependent Slater-Koster parameters are employed to describe electron hopping and orbital overlap in a strained monolayer by following the Wills-Harrison suggestions. Our results align remarkably well with the DFT calculations, predicting the band structure of strained monolayer TMDCs. Building on this model, we also examined the changes in effective mass and optical conductivity of monolayer TMDCs under strain, offering new insights that can aid in the development of practical device applications utilizing these materials. Additionally, we can use this model to swiftly and precisely compute the band structure of layered TMDCs under various strains, potentially aiding in large-scale strain-related calculations. A manuscript reporting the above results will be submitted soon.

15304519.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304519.value: Major findings and research outcomes of this GRF research project are summarized in the following five aspects. (1) We theoretically quantified the impact of electric potential on the second-order nonlinear response of 2D TMDCs and demonstrate the role of charge redistribution induced by an external electric field. We found that an out-of-plane electrostatic field induces out-of-plane second-order nonlinear susceptibility (χ_zxx) in monolayer TMDCs (MoS2, MoSe2, WS2, WSe2), comparable to their intrinsic in-plane components (χ_yyy). Furthermore, the modified susceptibility peak values (χ_zxx^*, χ_yyy^*) show a linear dependence on the field strength, resulting from asymmetric out-of-plane charge density distribution and structural deformation. (2) We experimentally observed room-temperature charged-biexciton emission from a single gold nanosphere-coupled TMDC monolayer through plasmon-nonradiative-decay-induced hot-electron injection. Our calculations demonstrated that the short hot-electron generation time (~0.3 ps) confirmed sufficiently fast injection of hot carriers to manipulate the TMDC exciton states. Hence, under resonant excitation of localized surface plasmons in the gold nanosphere, we observed a pronounced red shift in the hybrid system’s PL spectral peak and a super-linear intensity dependence on the laser power density, indicating a biexciton nature of the emission. Non-resonant laser excitation produced no PL signal from charged biexcitons, highlighting the necessity of hot-electron injection in the formation of charged biexcitons. (3) We experimentally demonstrated that hot-electron injection can induce symmetry breaking in bilayer TMDCs and observed hot-electron injection induced SHG in bilayer TMDCs using plasmonic particle-on-film nanocavities, corroborating the emergence of out-of-plane second-order nonlinear susceptibility. Furthermore, DFT calculations showed that the magnitude of charge redistribution is proportional to the perpendicular electric field strength, as are changes in the second-order nonlinear susceptibility. Based on that, we hold the view that in the case of hot-carrier injection, the changes in second-order nonlinear susceptibility are proportional to the charge redistribution magnitude (namely, the hot-carrier injection density). Then, we developed a model to link hot-carrier generation number with the second-order nonlinear coefficient, matching very well with our experimental findings. In the end, measuring the polarization-resolved SHG patterns further confirmed the emergence of out-of-plane second-order nonlinear susceptibility. (4) We proposed a strain engineering approach to boost in-plane second-order susceptibility (χ_yyy) in monolayer WSe2 and find that strain tuning yields a ∼13-fold enhancement in χ_yyy, with a potential ∼93-fold enhancement with a small biaxial tensile strain (0.30%) by realizing exciton double resonance. (5) We developed a modified Slater-Koster tight-binding model incorporating strain effects, aligning well with DFT calculations, which can be used to examine the changes in effective mass and optical conductivity of layered TMDCs under various strains.

15304519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304519.value: While carrying out this GRF research project, we introduced a novel concept that leverages the property of hot-electron injection to induce SHG in bilayer TMDCs. By spatially scanning and detecting the SHG signal, we can observe the diffusion of hot carriers in 2D semiconductor materials. Additionally, the processes of hot-carrier generation and relaxation in metallic nanostructures have garnered significant research interests from the nanophotonics community. However, their observation in conventional systems is challenging due to their femtosecond-scale temporal dynamics. Building on our current findings, we have the opportunity to employ charged biexcitons or SHG signals as probes to map the dynamics of hot carriers, utilizing pump-probe techniques to discern these processes in metal nanostructures.

15304519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304519.value: In layered TMDC materials, the symmetry governs their nonlinear optical responses. Thus, altering the charge distribution in TMDCs layer is an efficient way to tune their nonlinear response. We proposed to inject hot carriers from a metal nanostructure to a neighboring TMDC layer to break the latter’s inversion symmetry and hence induce SHG with both in-plane and out-of-plane components. We achieved our objectives by firstly investigating the effects of electric potential on 2D TMDCs, demonstrating the role of charge redistribution in tuning their nonlinear optical properties. Using density functional theory, we found that an out-of-plane electrostatic field significantly enhances the out-of-plane nonlinear susceptibility in both monolayer and bilayer TMDCs. We also observed room-temperature light emission from charged biexcitons by injecting hot electrons from a gold nanosphere into a TMDC monolayer, highlighting an efficient way to alter the carrier characteristics of 2D TMDCs. Additionally, we demonstrated hot-electron injection-induced SHG in bilayer TMDCs, with polarization-resolved measurements revealing the emergence of out-of-plane nonlinear susceptibility. Lastly, we proposed a strain engineering approach to enhance the in-plane nonlinear susceptibility of monolayer WSe₂ by realizing a double-resonance exciton state. These findings, published in leading journals, offer new methods for controlling 2D materials’ nonlinear optical properties for advanced optoelectronics and photonics applications.

15304819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304819.value: XPB是一種ATP依賴型DNA解旋酶，也是TFIIH複合物的核心亞基。XPB在轉錄的啟動、核苷酸的修復和G4 DNA識別的過程中有非常重要的作用。 XPB遺傳缺陷在臨床上與一些嚴重的疾病相關，例如皮膚癌，神經變性和早衰。雖然XPB在生物體內非常重要，相關的分子機制仍然不明，這很可能是由於缺乏工具化合物和特定的XPB抑製劑。 本項目致力於開發化學探針和相關測試，用於促進XPB的生物學研究以及開發其抑製劑。由於雷公藤內酯（TL）是唯一已知的物理結合XPB的抑製劑，我們決定合成基於TL骨架的化學探針。在初步實驗中，我們獲得了“可點擊”XPB探針，成功地標記了內源性XPB，並且通過凝膠內熒光掃描和質譜分析進行了驗證。首先我們將優化檢測內源性XPB的實驗條件。接下來，我們將過度表達XPB並建立用於篩選抑製劑的體外和原位測定。在這些測定中，化學探針將能夠以快速和定量的方式檢測XPB-抑製劑的相互作用。最後，我們將篩選包括TL類似物的化合物庫，並驗證新型抑製劑結合和抑制XPB的能力。該研究有望提供低毒性、高特異性的XPB抑製劑。此外，該研究所產生的工具和分析方法將極大地促進對XPB相關生物學和疾病的研究。本項目所開發的技術平台也可以應用於其他缺乏工具化合物的蛋白質的研究。

15304819.label: Realisation of objectives
15304819.value: Objective 1: To establish an optimal approach for labeling endogenous XPB in live cells with synthetic chemical probes. We have successfully achieved this objective through the development and characterization of two novel chemical probes, TL-alkyne (TL-alk) and TL-azide (TL-az), based on the structure of triptolide (TL). 1. Design and synthesis of chemical probes: The researchers designed and synthesized TL-alk and TL-az, which maintain the 12,13-epoxide functional group of TL that can covalently bind to Cys342 of the XPB protein. The terminal alkyne or azide groups on these probes allow for further conjugation via click chemistry reactions. 2. Evaluation of probe performance: Cell-based assays were conducted to evaluate the cytotoxicity and XPB-labeling efficiency of the new probes. The results showed that TL-alk and TL-az have lower IC50 values compared to the parent compound TL, indicating increased potency. In-gel fluorescence labeling experiments further demonstrated the ability of these probes to specifically label endogenous XPB. 3. Optimization of labeling conditions: We have optimized the concentration and incubation time for efficient labeling of XPB by the TL-alk probe. We found that 1 μM TL-alk and 30 minutes of incubation time provided robust and specific labeling of XPB, as confirmed by competition experiments. 4. Demonstration of probe specificity: Competition experiments using excess TL showed that the labeling of XPB by TL-alk could be completely blocked, confirming the specificity of the probe for the target protein. In summary, the project has successfully achieved its objective of establishing an optimal approach for labeling endogenous XPB in live cells. The development and characterization of the TL-alk probe provide a valuable tool for studying the biological functions of XPB and discovering novel XPB/NER inhibitors. Objective 2: To develop in-situ assays with the probes for identifying novel XPB inhibitors. We have successfully realized this objective through the following efforts: 1. Establishment of a gel-based fluorescence scanning assay: We have developed a robust and specific probe that can effectively label the XPB protein. With this probe TL-alk, we set up a gel-based fluorescence scanning assay using this probe to screen for novel XPB inhibitors. This approach allows the detection of compounds that can compete with the probe for binding to XPB. 2. Development of an imaging-based high content screening (HCS) platform: In addition to the gel-based assay, we also established an imaging-based HCS platform for XPB inhibitor screening. This HCS platform utilizes the same specific probe and is particularly useful for screening larger compound libraries. 3. Comprehensive Screening of XPB Inhibitor Candidates: We screened over 2000 compounds from our compound library using the established gel-based assay. The compounds were selected from three categories: structure-based virtual screening, TL analogs, and FDA-approved drugs. This broad screening approach allowed us to identify promising XPB inhibitor candidates, including parthenolide and pelitinib. 4. Validation of Identified Candidates: We further validated the identified XPB inhibitor candidates through various experiments. This additional validation step ensures the reliability and effectiveness of the selected compounds as potential XPB inhibitors. In summary, we have successfully developed two complementary in-situ assays, the gel-based fluorescence scanning assay and the imaging-based HCS platform, to effectively identify novel XPB inhibitors. We have demonstrated the successful realization of Objective 2 by establishing these robust screening platforms and comprehensively evaluating a diverse set of XPB inhibitor candidates.

XPB is an important component of a larger complex called TFIIH, which plays a crucial role in the process of gene expression and DNA repair within cells. We have developed two innovative screening methods to efficiently identify potential XPB inhibitor compounds. The first method uses a special fluorescent probe to detect compounds that can bind and disrupt the XPB protein. 15304919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15304919.value: Polymer crystallization plays a vital role in today’s polymer science and the plastics industry. With molecular chains aligned to create an ordered structure, crystallization process has profound effects on polymer properties. However, molecular chains also tend to be irregularly entangled, resulting in incompletely aligned or “semi-crystalline” polymers. The detailed structure of semi-crystalline polymers is extremely challenging to probe and thus lacks understanding. In particular, it remains unclear whether a semi-crystalline polymer has an uniform structure, or is inhomogeneous with crystallinity varying spatially. Conventional analytical techniques cannot resolve the spatial distribution of crystallinity, which limits the current understanding to the homogeneous crystallinity model. Recently we have discovered initial evidence showing inhomogeneous crystallinity in poly(ε-caprolactone) spherulites using spatially-resolved Raman spectroscopy. We found that the degree of crystallinity is lowest at spherulite centers and increases significantly towards the periphery. Such a spatial distribution may reflect a general crystallization process with heavy molecules segregating as the initial nucleation. Therefore the identified crystallinity distribution could be intrinsic to many semi-crystalline polymers, and may further lead to inhomogeneity in their properties. On the other hand, as Raman spectroscopy is only an indirect method to probe crystallinity, there is an urgent need for more direct characterization approaches to validate this preliminary observation. The aim of this project is to develop a scheme to quantitatively map the crystallinity distribution in polymers, using spatially-resolved diffraction in transmission electron microscopy (TEM). With our TEM expertise, we will experiment on both selected-area electron diffraction and convergent-beam electron diffraction to find out the optimal approach. The intensity ratio between the ordered and disordered diffraction signals will be used to indicate the degree of crystallinity. To avoid beam damage, spatially-resolved diffraction will be performed at cryogenic temperature using a liquid-nitrogen-cooling holder. We will first apply the developed scheme on poly(ε-caprolactone) spherulites to verify the crystallinity distribution from Raman spectroscopy. Spherulites with different molecular-weight distributions will be examined for potential correlation between non-uniformities in crystallinity and molecular weight, which will shed light on the origin of inhomogeneous crystallinity. The universality of the inhomogeneous crystallinity will be interrogated by analyzing other semi-crystalline polymers starting with polyethylene. Influence of inhomogeneous crystallinity on polymer properties will also be investigated. The exclusive knowledge achieved from this work may open a stimulating new avenue to better understanding and engineering the structure and properties of semi-crystalline polymers, and may add a new page to the theoretical development of polymer crystallization. 高分子結晶在當今高分子科研和塑料工業中扮演著不可或缺的角色。高分子的結晶過程伴隨著分子鏈的有序排列，可以從本質上改變高分子材料的性能。而高分子鏈自身又有不規則扭曲的傾向，從而導致分子鏈排列只能部分有序，又被稱爲“半結晶”。這種半結晶結構非常難以表徵，目前仍然存在很多未知。特別是半結晶的高分子是均匀的半結晶，還是各處有著不同的結晶度，一直不爲人所知。傳統的分析表徵方法難以分辨結晶度的空間分佈，導致高分子科學目前是建立在均匀結晶度的假設上。 然而通過空間分辨拉曼光譜，我們最近發現聚己内酯球晶的不同部位有著不同的結晶度。結晶度的空間不均匀性很可能是由於球晶中心富集長分子鏈，更容易扭曲；而外圍部分更多短分子鏈，因而不規則扭曲較少，結晶度更高。由於高分子結晶大多開始於長分子鏈的聚集形核，這一結晶度分佈很可能適用於多種高分子球晶，進而導致其性能的不均匀性。然而拉曼光譜只能非直接的反映材料結構，目前急需更直接的結構表徵手段來證實這一發現。 本項目的研究目標是開發一種基於透射電子顯微鏡的空間分辨衍射技術，進而探測半結晶高分子材料内部的結晶度分佈。我們將嘗試基於電子選區衍射和匯聚束衍射兩種方法，比較高分子材料不同位置的有序和無序相的衍射强度，進而獲得其結晶度。爲了減少電子束對高分子材料的破壞，空間分辨衍射將與液氮樣品臺結合，在低溫下進行。我們計劃先將此技術應用於聚己内酯球晶來驗證拉曼光譜的發現。通過分析含有不同分子量分佈的球晶，我們可以獲得結晶度和分子量分佈的關聯性，進而探索結晶度不均匀分佈的起源。我們還會研究包括聚乙烯在内的其他半結晶高分子材料，分析不均匀結晶度的普遍性。最後我們會探索不均匀結晶度對材料性能的影響，從而為調控半結晶高分子結構來優化性能提供指引。

15304919.label: Realisation of objectives
15304919.value: The objectives have all been achieved as stated below: Firstly, we have established the so-called 4D-scanning TEM (STEM) scheme that can achieve spatially-resolved electron diffraction down to nanoscale. It was enabled by the aberration-corrected TEM/STEM (Spectra 300) installed at PolyU in 2020, which is equipped by an ultrafast direct-electron detector (ThermoFisher EMPAD) capable of taking 1000 diffraction patterns per second. It allows us to take electron diffraction at each scan position in STEM, thus achieving both real-space and reciprocal-space information simultaneously. With the liquid-nitrogen-cooling cryogenic holder (Gatan 915), such 4D-STEM can be carried out at cryogenic temperature. To analyze the spatially-resolved electron diffraction on the quantitative level, we have developed Matlab scripts to perform peak fitting and modelling, which can distinguish diffraction signals from both crystalline and amorphous polymers. By analyzing these signals at nanoscale in a 4D-STEM data set, we can map the orientation of polymer lamella and polymer chains from the positions of crystalline diffraction spots, and the amount of amorphous phase based on the intensity of amorphous diffraction peak. Secondly, to apply 4D-STEM on polymers, we have also systematically studied the electron beam effects and derived the threshold electron dose to avoid such effects. Co-I Li’s group developed an effective approach to prepare spherulite polymer films 100-200 nm thick and to transfer them onto TEM sample grids, so that no additional TEM sample preparation is needed. Based on these samples, we have derived the effects of a high-energy electron beam at both room and cryogenic temperatures, using a combination of electron diffraction and electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS), and established the optimal condition for characterizing the pristine structure of polymers. With the established low-dose condition (≤10 e-/Å2), 4D-STEM can be reliably applied on semi-crystalline polymers such as polyethylene (PE) and poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) spherulites provided by Co-I Li. Thirdly, applying the above developed 4D-STEM on PCL spherulites, we found two dominant orientations of lamella crystals along [100] and [001] zone axes. These lamella aggregate to form two types of domains intermixed with each other, which can be clearly distinguished from 4D-STEM data. Despite the orientation change, on the other hand, mostly lamella still have their b axis in-plane orientated along the radial direction, exhibiting a remarkable spherical symmetry. Considering that the lamella crystals should grow along b axis during crystallization, our observation shows that the orientation change among lamella crystals does not interrupt their radial growth along b axis to form 2D spherulites. Fourthly, we have further applied 4D-STEM on PE spherulites and successfully revealed a wealth of information on its hierarchical spherulite structure at multiscale. The structure features we unveiled include the overall spherical symmetry of the whole spherulite (~10 μm), the periodic lamella twisting with alternating [100]- and [001]-oriented lamella crystals along the radial direction – the so-called banded spherulites (~100 nm), the individual lamella crystals with edge-on orientation (~10 nm), and even the molecular chain direction inside individual lamella (molecular scale). To our best knowledge, it is the first time to unravel the characteristic spherulite structure from micrometer to nanometer scales, which demonstrates the power of low-dose 4D-STEM on analyzing semicrystalline polymers. Finally, we have mapped the distribution of amorphous phases in both PCL and PE spherulites. In principle, we could derive crystallinity using the intensity ratio between the crystalline and amorphous signals. However, the variation of lamella orientation alters the crystalline diffraction intensity, making it impractical to derive crystallinity quantitatively. Instead, we just measured the amorphous diffraction intensity that should be proportional to the amount of amorphous phase without orientation problem. Combining with the local sample thickness (including both amorphous and crystalline phases) measured by STEM-EELS, we can derive the variations of amorphous and crystalline phases on a relative scale. Excitingly, we did identify more amorphous phase at the center of PE spherulites, which gradually decrease towards the periphery. It reflects lower crystallinity at the spherulite center, consistent with previous Raman spectroscopy results. Such a distribution may reflect the fundamental process of polymer crystallization: the heavy and long molecular chains stick together first as the initial nucleation, which contain more amorphous phases with lower crystallinity, while the mobile and short molecular chains may crystallize subsequently at the periphery with higher crystallinity. Such crystallinity distribution directly affects the thermal and chemical stability of PE spherulites: in situ heating AFM revealed the initiation of melting at the spherulite center, while ex situ AFM before and after solution etching identified the initiation of dissolution at the spherulite center. On the other hand, in PCL the spherulite centers do not show higher amorphous signal, indicating different distribution of crystallinity. Understanding such difference requires further investigation on various polymer materials using 4D-STEM.

15304919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15304919.value: 1. The application of TEM on organic solids is limited by their susceptible structure that can be modified by the high energy electron beam. Understanding beam effects is essential to achieve pristine sample information with minimized artefacts. In this work, we derive the detailed beam effects in PE, PCL, and P3HT semicrystalline spherulites, including both structure and chemical bonding evolution detected from a combination of quantitative electron diffraction and spectroscopy. Both crystalline and amorphous components are analyzed. Measurements are carried out at both room temperature and cryogenic temperature (~98K), a comparison between which clearly demonstrates the effectiveness of cryo-protection on preventing the beam effects. The initial dominant beam effect in PE and PCL spherulites is identified to be the radiolysis of C-H bonds, leading to both amorphization and the formation of unsaturated polyenyl groups that further causes lattice expansion. On the other hand, P3HT exhibits an intriguing two-stage damage process that has never been reported before, with the side-chain ordering destroyed prior to the π-stacking ordering. Our results not only shed light on the detailed beam effects on structure and chemical bonding in the three polymers, but also demonstrate a powerful approach to quantitatively analyze these effects in other organic solids. This result has been published in Polymer 256, 125195 (2022). 2. Most of semicrystalline polymers exhibit spherulite structure involving periodic chain folding to form lamella crystals, which are further organized with spherical symmetry to form spherulites. Probing such manifold hierarchical structure, however, presents a grand challenge for material characterization. In this work, we demonstrate low-dose 4D-STEM as an effective technique to probe the hierarchical structure in polymer spherulites. Applying it on PE and PCL spherulites, we have obtained a wealth of structure information that can only be derived indirectly before, from the overall spherical symmetry on the micrometre level down to molecular chain orientation at nanoscale. Our observation reveals the periodic lamella twisting in the so-called banded spherulites for the first time, and indicates that the twisting primarily occurs between lamella, excluding the potential twisting inside individual lamella that has been proposed before. A new spiral growth mechanism has also been identified for PE spherulites. We also detect more amorphous phase at PE spherulite centers, reflecting lower crystallinity presumably due to the aggregation of heavy and long molecular chains to initiate the crystal nucleation. A manuscript based on these results are under preparation with the draft attached.

15304919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15304919.value: The identified more amorphous phase at PE spherulite centers proves the inhomogeneous distribution of crystallinity in semicrystalline polymers. Such nonuniform crystallinity must leads to inhomogeneity in properties of PE spherulites, which should be further tested through measurements such as nano-indentation to probe the local hardness. On the other hand, the distribution has been found to be different between PE and PCL spherulites, which demands further investigation for better understanding, especially on the factors determining crystallinity distribution such as the synthesis condition. The demonstrated low-dose 4D-STEM in this work presents an unprecedented tool to probe the semicrystalline structure of organic materials. We plan to apply this technique to other polymer materials to unravel their intriguing semicrystalline structure. It can also be extended to other organic solids such as hybrid halide perovskites in solar cells and solid-electrolyte interphases (SEIs) in batteries, to reveal the structure information that is previously inaccessible by other techniques.

15304919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15304919.value: Polymer crystallization plays a vital role in today’s polymer science and plastics industry. With molecular chains aligned to create an ordered structure, crystallization process has profound effects on polymer properties. However, molecular chains also tend to be irregularly entangled, resulting in incompletely aligned or “semicrystalline” polymers. The detailed structure of semicrystalline polymers is extremely challenging to probe and thus lacks understanding. In this project, we develop spatially-resolved electron diffraction or 4D-STEM under the low dose condition with minimized beam effects. We demonstrate this technique on spherulites, a typical structure possessed by most semicrystalline polymers, and successfully reveal their hierarchical structure at multiscale, ranging from the overall spherical symmetry on the micrometre level down to molecular chain orientation at nanoscale. We discover numerous structure features that have not been reported before, which rectifies the current structure models for spherulites. In particular, we identify inhomogeneous crystallinity whose distribution directly influences the properties of spherulites. Our work not only advances the current understanding of semicrystalline polymer structure, but also present a powerful tool to explore polymer structure for previously inaccessible information.

15305219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305219.value: Widely application of clean energy such as solar and wind relies on both efficient gathering from nature and convenient utilization by energy storage systems. High-energy-density Li-ion batteries have been the primary choices for the storage, suggested by the great success in portable electronics. For the upcoming large-scale application, such as stationary energy storage, sustainability and cost must be taken into account. The limited lithium reserves bring about concerns on the depletion of materials source. Alternative battery technologies are therefore flourished, among which K-ion battery is one of the most promising candidates. The similarities with Li-ion batteries would greatly facilitate the development of forthcoming K-ion technologies. Recent progress on the anodes and cathodes have readily demonstrated the feasibility of building a full K-ion battery, although the energy density still falls behind the Li-ion battery. High-performance electrodes are highly desired to narrow the energy density gap between them. The proposed project aims to develop high-performance alloy anodes through interface engineering. Compared to carbon anode, alloy anodes such as P, Sb, and Bi possess much higher theoretical capacity. The main issue preventing their practical application is the huge volume change, which leads to the pulverization and isolation of active particles. Electrode/electrolyte interface plays a vital role in stabilizing the alloy anodes. A compact and stable interface, either in-situ formed solid electrolyte interface (SEI) or artificial constructed one, is expected to avoid its over-growth and fracture during repeated K ion insertion/extraction. The recent work in the PI’s group has demonstrated the beneficial effect of ether-based electrolyte in improving the cyclic performance of microsized Bi anodes. Nevertheless, the underlying mechanism remains a mystery, discouraging the development of general approaches for the other materials. Herein, we will probe the detailed composition, structure, mechanics and ionic conductivity for the interfaces forming in typical electrolytes. The “structure-property” relationship will be established, based on which the microstructure will be tailored to develop robust interfaces for stabilizing alloy anodes. The successful implementation of this project will not only advance the K-ion batteries but also benefit the development of Li- and Na-ion batteries where similar issues afflict alloy anodes. 清潔能源如太陽能、風能等的廣泛使用既需要高效的能源轉化器件也依賴於可靠的能源儲存系統。因為具有較高的能量密度，鋰離子電池被考慮為首選儲能方案，但是有限的鋰資源使得它在大規模靜態儲能上受到了成本和可持續性的限制。在多種替代電池中，鉀離子電池是其中的有力競爭者，它和鋰離子電池具有類似的結構，為電極開發和工業化生產帶來了便利。最近在正負極材料方面的進展也證實鉀離子電池的研製是可行的，雖然其能量密度有待通過高性能電極的製備來進一步提高。因此，本項目致力於構建電極/電解液界面來穩定高容量合金負極。相比與傳統碳材料，合金負極如磷、銻和鉍等具有極高的理論容量。由於在合金化過程體積變化較大，在循環時有可能導致電極粉化和界面破裂，帶來容量衰減，因而開發緻密且具有高穩定性的電極/電解液界面至關重要。申請人最近的研究工作表明，在醚類電解液中形成的界面能夠明顯提高合金負極的循環壽命，但是具體作用機制尚不明確。本項目將探索合金負極在典型電解液中所形成的電極/電解液界面的組織、成分、機械性能和離子電導率等，從而建立界面的“結構-性能”關聯，為構建高強度電極/電解液界面提供指導，提高合金負極的穩定性。由於鋰離子和鈉離子電池的負極也面臨類似挑戰，本項目的成功實施也將推動合金負極在其它鹼金屬離子電池中的應用。

15305219.label: Realisation of objectives
15305219.value: The objectives of the project have been realized, which are summarized as follows: (1) we have explored the detailed nanostructure of the solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs) in classical carbonate and ether electrolytes. The stability of the alloy anodes, including Bi and Sb, in the two types of electrolytes has been examined. They show distinct electrochemical behavior due to the differences in the resulting SEIs. The chemical composition of SEIs is first explored by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), indicating that the SEIs in ether electrolytes have abundant organic species. The nanostructure of the SEIs is revealed by high-resolution transmission electron microscopy. The SEIs have a composite structure with the inorganic nanoparticles dispersed among the organic matrix, which significantly affects the kinetics and stability. The formation of such a structure is barely affected by the particle size but is closely related to the electrolytes. (2) The electrochemical and mechanical stability of the SEIs have been probed to correlate with their nanostructure. The morphology of the SEIs after different cycles is examined to investigate their stability during electrode swelling/contraction. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy is conducted to measure the charge transfer kinetics across the SEIs under different electrolytes. Moreover, the mechanical properties of the SEIs, including Young’s modulus and strain at the yielding point, are measured by atomic force microscopy-based nano-indentation tests. All of these proprieties greatly depend on the composition and nanostructure of the SEIs, with their correlation established based on the studies on several alloy anodes. (3) The unveiled structure-property relationship facilitates the development of effective electrolytes to improve the cyclic lifespan of alloy anodes. Ether electrolytes have been adopted to stabilize Bi and Sb anodes by inducing elastic SEIs due to the presence of oligomers. For instance, 1M KFSI/ethylene glycol diethyl ether electrolyte has greatly enhanced the Sb microparticles. Furthermore, a localized high concentration electrolyte based on trimethyl phosphate has been developed to stabilize the black phosphorus anode. (4) The stability of the interfaces has been investigated in both half cell and full cell. The full cells were assembled by coupling the alloy anodes (such as Sb and P) with typical cathodes, including high-capacity Prussian blue cathodes and high-voltage fluorophosphate cathodes. Their cyclic stability and rate capability have been evaluated to assess their performance toward practical applications.

15305219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305219.value: We have conducted a thorough investigation to explore the solid electrolyte interface (SEIs) formation in various electrolytes, probe their nanostructure and mechanical properties, and assess their effect in stabilizing alloy anodes. The major findings and outcomes are summarized as follows. (i) Building elastic SEIs to stabilize microsized Sb anodes in potassium ion batteries. The dimethoxyethane (DME)-based electrolytes have been adopted to boost the Bi anodes, but the extension to Sb is not satisfactory at a normal concentration. To improve the cyclic stability of high-capacity Sb anodes, we develop a new electrolyte based on the ethylene glycol diethyl ether (EGDEE) solvent, obtained by replacing the methyl in DME with ethyl terminal group. A reversible capacity of over 550 mAh/g is obtained in neat Sb anodes, showing negligible capacity degradation in 100 cycles. In comparison, the capacity decreases to almost zero in merely 50 cycles under classical carbonate electrolytes (C: Research Output No. 2). The reason lies in the more elastic SEI in the EGDEE electrolytes, which has an average yield strain of 0.92 compared to 0.44 for the one in carbonate electrolyte. (ii) Developing a localized high concentration electrolyte (LHCE) to realize the stable cycling of black phosphorus/graphite composite anode, delivering a reversible capacity of over 600 mAh/g. The LHCE preserves the benefits of high-concentration electrolytes in constructing a stable SEI while reducing the electrolyte viscosity to improve the kinetics. Furthermore, the electrolyte microscopy indicates a more homogeneous SEI is formed in LHCE, contributing to the enhanced mechanical properties by alleviating the stress concentration (C: Research Output No. 4). (iii) Proposing the “maximum elastic deformation energy” indicator to predict the mechanical stability of SEI. Based on the studies of the anode stability in various electrolytes, we demonstrate the maximum elastic deformation energy, which combines the effect of Young’s modulus and yielding strain, could accurately predict the quality of SEI in accommodating the volume change. A two-step nano-indentation test is then designed to examine the mechanical response at the elastic and plastic region for obtaining the deformation energy (C: Research Output No. 1). The indicator will facilitate the screening of electrolytes for high-capacity anodes. iv) We also extend design strategies to other anode materials and Na-ion battery systems (C: Research Output No. 3&5), demonstrating the critical roles of interfaces in realizing long-lifespan batteries.

15305219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305219.value: The results achieved in this project have substantially enhanced our understanding of the microstructure of solid electrolyte interphase and its effect on stabilizing alloy anodes in potassium ion batteries. Several electrolytes have been developed, centering mainly on the interfaces on the anode sides. Since the electrolytes affect both the anode and cathode, the interfaces on the cathodes should also be explored in future studies. This will pose new challenges to the electrolyte design, particularly for high-voltage oxidation stability. It is worth mentioning that the structure-property correlation of the interface established in this project could also be extended to the cathode-electrolyte interphase, thus promoting the rational electrolyte design with both anode and cathode compatibility.

15305219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305219.value: High-capacity alloy anodes are essential to boosting the energy density of emerging potassium-ion batteries. However, they suffer from a large volume change of up to 400%, leading to the pulverization of active materials and destruction of the electrode/electrode interface. This project is devoted to building mechanically stable solid electrolyte interphase (SEIs), which accommodate the swelling/contraction of the active particles to maintain the electrode integrity. Advanced characterization techniques are adopted to reveal the chemical composition and nanostructure of the SEIs formed in various electrolytes. We also develop a two-step nano-indentation test to accurately probe the mechanical properties of SEI and propose a new indicator to predict the long-term stability, facilitating the establishment of SEI’s structure-property relationship. Based on these, several promising electrolytes, including novel ether and phosphate electrolytes, have been designed, which outperform the classical carbonate electrolytes in constructing high-quality SEIs. Consequently, stable cycling of alloy anodes has been achieved without resorting to complex electrode design. They deliver an attractive capacity of over 550 mAh/g. The design strategies could also be extended to other battery systems. We expect the achieved results would benefit the electrolyte design for building robust interfaces toward high-energy batteries.

15305719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305719.value: 2004年，Crouzeix提出一猜想，成為近年算子和矩陣理論其中一個有趣的未解問題。其猜想斷言，對於任何作用於復希爾伯特（Hilbert）空間的有界線性算子，其數值範圍是一個完整的k-谱集，其中k數值為2。該猜想得到了學者們的廣泛關注，並在算子理論、數值分析等方面有重大影響。2018年，Crouzeix和Palencia在此問題上取得了重大進展，證明了k可為一略大於2的常數。但是，目前尚不清楚如何再進一步降低此數值。到目前為止，有許多理論和數據支持這猜想。此外，對於某些特殊類別的算子，此猜想已被証明。在這個研究項目中，團隊的目標是以矩陣理論為主軸研究此猜想。我們將首先研究數值範圍的邊界在猜想中的潛在應用。例如，我們計劃在數值範圍的邊界上估計函數的範數。其次，我們將嘗試以Cayley-Hamilton定理簡化猜想的數值研究。所有研究都會從低維數的特殊類型算子開始，進而了解一般情況。最終目標希望能改善現有常數或解決猜想。

15305719.label: Realisation of objectives
15305719.value: The objective of this project is to study Crouzeix's conjecture concerning numerical range and to develop new proof techniques and tools for generalized numerical ranges. Throughout this project, the PI has made significant progress toward these objectives and has obtained numerous mathematical results in numerical range and matrix analysis. The Co-I visited Hong Kong from late December 2020 to early January 2021 and initiated collaboration with the PI on the research project, making significant progress. Unfortunately, the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted the planned visits, including the PI's intended visit to the Co-I's institute during the summers of both 2020 and 2021, leading to their cancellation. To adapt to the challenging circumstances imposed by the pandemic, the PI maintained regular communication with the Co-I and other collaborators through online Zoom meetings. After the reopening of Hong Kong's borders in early 2023, the Co-I revisited in May 2023, allowing for in-person discussions and the finalization of some of the findings of the project, which greatly facilitated its completion. Several scheduled conference trips had to be canceled due to the pandemic, impacting the dissemination of the project's findings and potential collaborations with other researchers in the field. Moreover, the recruitment plan for the project was affected as the intended candidate was unable to assume the position in 2020. A postdoctoral fellow eventually joined the team in November 2022 and worked on the project for approximately seven months. During the initial stages of the project, the PI collaborated with colleagues to explore the geometry of the joint numerical range of a triple of observables in a three-level photonic system. This endeavor resulted in a comprehensive classification of these ranges within the context of quantum information. Additionally, the PI and the Co-I collaborated on investigating the C-numerical range. Specifically, they demonstrated that the intersection of all C-numerical ranges of T^-1AT, where T runs through all invertible matrices, is equivalent to the C-numerical range of a diagonal matrix with the eigenvalues of A as its diagonal entries. This study provides a valuable direction for examining Crouzix's conjecture, as it allows for focusing on the study of C-numerical ranges of diagonal matrices through the intersection of all C-numerical ranges under the similarity class of matrices. These works establish a solid matrix-theoretic foundation for investigating Crouzeix's conjecture and generalized numerical ranges. Furthermore, the PI participated in collaborative research to investigate the (p,k)-norm, one of the unitary similarity invariant norms. This investigation of norms further deepened the understanding of the conjecture. In summary, significant progress has been achieved in investigating Crouzeix's conjecture and exploring the associated numerical range problems within this project. However, it is crucial to acknowledge that the conjecture has not yet reached a definitive resolution, indicating the need for further work to arrive at a conclusive outcome. Therefore, rather than stating that 100% of objective 1 has been achieved, we have indicated that 80% has been accomplished to accurately reflect this situation. The project has undeniably contributed to a deeper comprehension of the conjecture and its associated numerical range problems, but the attainment of a conclusive resolution relies on continued research and collaborative efforts.

15305719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305719.value: The PI collaborated with colleagues to explore the geometry of the joint numerical range of a triple of observables in a three-level photonic system in quantum information science. Additionally, the team demonstrated that the geometric properties of different classes of numerical ranges reveal ground-state degeneracies of a Hamiltonian expressed as a linear combination of the observables. These findings have implications for quantum phases in the thermodynamic limit. The results not only contribute to a deeper understanding of the geometry of numerical ranges but also provide a versatile geometric approach for investigating the properties of higher-dimensional quantum systems, see [Paper 1]. The PI also collaborated with the Co-I on exploring the C-numerical range. The research team made significant advancements in this area by establishing that, for a given matrix A, the intersection of all C-numerical ranges of T^-1AT, where T runs through all invertible matrices, is equivalent to the C-numerical range of a diagonal matrix with the eigenvalues of A as its diagonal entries. Furthermore, it was demonstrated that when C and A are both non-scalar matrices and X is a bounded set, there exists an invertible matrix T such that X is a subset of the C-numerical range of T^-1AT. These findings represent generalizations of previously known results concerning the classical numerical range. Analogous outcomes for the rank-k numerical range are further examined in [Paper 5]. The PI then engaged in collaborative research to investigate the (p,k)-norm and its properties. Specifically, they focused on characterizing linear maps that preserve the (p,k)-norm of tensor products of matrices in bipartite systems. Furthermore, the research findings were extended to multipartite systems[Paper 2]. The PI also studied the set S of straight lines that intersect with four distinct given lines in three dimensional real space. He discovered that it could contain no, one, two, or infinitely many elements [Paper 3]. Furthermore, the PI also delved into the study of the Birkhoff polytope graph, which has a vertex set identical to the elements of the symmetric group of degree n. The PI focused on exploring the properties of maximal and maximum cliques, which are sets of elements that are pairwise adjacent, as well as independent sets, which are sets of elements that are pairwise nonadjacent, within the Birkhoff polytope graph. [Paper 4].

15305719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305719.value: The research on Crouzeix's conjecture holds immense potential for further advancement, given its profound implications in operator theory, matrix theory, and numerical analysis. As the conjecture remains unresolved, indicating the necessity for continued efforts to reach a definitive conclusion, this area of study offers ample room for further development. The existing theoretical and numerical evidence consistently supports the conjecture, reinforcing the need for ongoing investigation. By utilizing the matrix-theoretic tools developed in this project, substantial progress has been made in exploring Crouzeix's conjecture and its associated topics, including C-numerical ranges. Therefore, it is crucial to persist in further research to obtain conclusive results.

15305719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305719.value: In this research project, our main objective was to study Crouzeix's conjecture, generalized numerical ranges, and related problems in matrix analysis. Throughout our research, the research team has achieved substantial progress in this field and obtained numerous significant mathematical results. The investigation of Crouzeix's conjecture holds great significance in operator theory, matrix theory, and numerical analysis. Although the conjecture remains unresolved, the compelling theoretical and numerical evidence consistently supports its validity. The development of matrix-theoretic tools within this project has significantly contributed to the exploration of the conjecture and its associated topics. In addition to the work on Crouzeix's conjecture, the research team delved into related problems concerning numerical ranges. These include the exploration of the joint numerical range of observables in quantum information science, the (p,k)-norm and its preservation problem in bipartite and multipartite systems, as well as the Birkhoff polytope graph problem. These investigations have provided researchers with new insights and generated valuable results that contribute to the overall understanding of the conjecture. Overall, this research project has made substantial contributions to the field and has established a solid foundation for further advancements in understanding Crouzeix's conjecture, leading us closer to conclusive results.

15305819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15305819.value: Data recording, storage and security technologies are very important in our daily life. Smart luminescent materials that are responsive to external stimuli have gained much research interest in the development of data recording and storage devices. Among the various external stimuli, electric field is an important one in the field of organic optoelectronics, since it is very convenient to handle. Moreover, smart materials that are responsive to electric field are useful because they can be easily interfaced with existing optoelectronic devices. Electrochromic materials exhibiting a reversible change in their color or absorption spectrum have been extensively investigated due to their well-known applications in electronic paper and smart window/mirror based on the reversible transition between two redox states under certain voltages. Nevertheless, materials that display photoluminescence intensity or color change in response to electric field, namely, electroluminochromism (or electrochromic luminescence) are still limited. In view of the high sensitivity and easy detection of luminescence signal, rational molecular designs of electrochromic luminescent materials are hot topics because of their promising applications for fabricating new types of smart optoelectronic devices. In this project, we plan to devise two different strategies to achieve electrochromic luminescence based on transition metal complexes. One is to employ the electric field induced supramolecular assembly approach which can result in materials exhibiting different emission colors and distinct nanostructures at the same time. This would provide a new channel to observe the self-assembly of a metal complex and, most importantly, different nanostructures and optical properties of the metal complex can be simply regulated by the electric field. Another way is to use new phosphorescent molecular dyads or triads where the electrochromic luminescence can be electrochemically turned on and off by enabling or forbidding internal electron transfer between a reversible redox-active moiety and a phosphorescent chromophore. Given the ligand-dependent excited-state properties of phosphorescent iridium(IIII) and platinum(II) complexes, it is expected that their electrochromic luminescent performance can be tuned by varying the coordinated ligands as well as the counter-ions, and different luminescence-responsive modes to the electric field can be realized. In view of their ionic characteristic, high sensitivity to external stimuli and long phosphorescence lifetime, the proposed transition metal complexes hold great promise for applications in data recording and security protection. Data encryption and decryption can be achieved by using the photoluminescence lifetime imaging microscopy. 數據記錄、存儲和安全技術在我們的日常生活中非常重要。響應外部刺激的智能發光材料在數據記錄和存放設備的開發中獲得了很多研究興趣。在各種外部刺激中，電場是有機光電子領域中的重要因素，因為它處理起來非常方便。此外，響應電場的智能材料具有廣泛的應用前景，因為它們可以容易地與現有的光電器件結合。由於電致變色材料在電子紙以及智慧窗/鏡中的應用，基於在某些電壓下兩種氧化還原態之間的可逆轉變，已經廣泛研究出了其顏色或吸收光譜的可逆變化的電致變色材料。然而，可響應電場顯示光致發光強度或顏色變化的材料，即電致發光變色（或電致變色發光）仍然是有限的。鑒於發光信號的高靈敏度和易檢測性，電致變色發光材料的合理分子設計是當前的熱門研究領域，因為它們在製造新型智能光電器件方面具有廣闊的應用前景。在這個項目中，我們計畫設計兩種不同的策略來實現基於過渡金屬配合物的電致變色發光。一種是採用電場誘導的超分子組裝方法，其可以導致材料同時表現出不同的發光顏色和不同的納米結構。這將提供觀察金屬絡合物自組裝的新通道，並且最重要的是，可以通過電場簡單地調節金屬配合物的不同納米結構和光學性質。另一種方法是使用新的磷光分子二元或三元組，其中通過在可逆的氧化還原活性部分和磷光發色團之間啟用或禁止內部電子轉移，可以通過電場開啟和關閉變色發光。鑒於磷光銥（III）和鉑（II）配合物的配體依賴性激發態特性，預計它們的電致變色發光性能可通過改變配位配體以及陰離子來調節，而且可以實現對電場的不同發光響應模式。鑒於它們的離子特性，對外部刺激的高靈敏度和長的磷光壽命，所提出的過渡金屬配合物在數據記錄和安全保護中的應用具有很大的前景。通過使用光致發光壽命成像顯微鏡可以實現數據加密和解密。

A series of new electroluminochromic transition metal complexes were synthesized and characterized by spectroscopic, photophysical, thermal, structural and electrochemical methods. 15305819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15305819.value: Two platinum(II)-based soft salts were synthesized, which showed a bright NIR emission in the solid state via MMLCT transitions. One of them was employed as a NIR probe for in-vivo imaging (paper 1). Another similar soft salt was synthesized. TEM can demonstrate its capability to assemble into highly ordered nanofibers by the change of DMSO/H2O composition. SAED demonstrated the presence of Pt···Pt and π-π interactions in the self-assembled nanostructure. Next, a luminescent doped polymer film displayed distinctive emission color change from yellow to red upon heating. An anti-counterfeiting application was achieved by using emission lifetime and photoluminescence (PL) lifetime imaging (paper 2). Another soft salt showed interesting excitation wavelength dependent (Ex-De) phosphorescence. The various Pt(II)···Pt(II) distances are responsible for its Ex-De PL. Reversible on-off switching of Ex-De PL was achieved by manipulating its Pt(II)···Pt(II) distance through mechanical stress and vapor fuming. The high-level anticounterfeiting application via on-demand multicolor displays was demonstrated (paper 8). Recently, we present a multicomponent self-assembly approach, offering the potential for crafting heterometallic complexes with exceptional constitutional control. This method relies on the generation of metal ions from a sacrificial anode by using an electric field, which then coordinate with a metal complex precursor. By adjusting the intensity and duration of electric field, we achieved a variety of supramolecular structures, spanning from spherical to rod-like and even flower-like forms. Such heterometallic complex holds great promise in anti-counterfeiting application (paper 16). Some simple terpyridine-based derivatives were investigated and one of them can achieve novel multicolor emission including yellowish green light, white light, blue light, bluish green light and red phosphorescence light in a very wide wavelength range. These results provide a rational strategy for affording excitation-dependent color-tunable emission materials (paper 3). Synthetic routes to some luminescent cyclometallated polymers were developed which showed interesting emission properties (papers 4-5). Besides, a modified terpyridyl ligand was utilized to construct a soluble ionic metallo-supramolecular material whose electrochromic properties were studied (paper 9). Six luminescent conjugated polymers could realize reversible color modulation through a similar reversible chemical redox behavior accompanied by reversible color and fluorescence changes (paper 10). Vapor-phase living assembly of π-conjugated organic molecules was developed (paper 11). ELC materials based on other luminescent Pt(II) and Ir(III) cyclometallated complexes can be expected in the future study (papers 12-15). The PI was invited to contribute to two review articles on related topics (papers 6-7).

15305819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15305819.value: Many important data should emanate from this project which will make a good impact on the data recording and security protection technologies. We believe that the results will pave the way to the future design and development of electroluminochromic materials. The field is expected to remain exciting and stimulating for the foreseeable future. The following areas of research work can be further developed in the future: (1) Extension of the work to other electroluminochromic metallopolymers which can be expected to show interesting self-assembling properties. (2) Development of other optoelectronic applications based on new stimuli-responsive materials.

15305819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15305819.value: In this project, we employ the electric field induced supramolecular assembly approach which can result in materials exhibiting different emission colors and distinct nanostructures at the same time. This would provide a new channel to observe the self-assembly of a metal complex and, most importantly, different nanostructures and optical properties of the metal complex can be simply regulated by the electric field. In particular, an intriguing electric-field-assisted rapid synthesis of heterometallic complex single crystals was developed. Given the ligand-dependent excited-state properties of phosphorescent iridium(IIII) and platinum(II) complexes, their electrochromic luminescent performance can be tuned by varying the coordinated ligands as well as the counter-ions, and different luminescence-responsive modes to the electric field can be realized. In view of their ionic characteristic, high sensitivity to external stimuli and long phosphorescence lifetime, these transition metal complexes hold great promise for applications in data recording and security protection. Data encryption and decryption can be achieved by using the photoluminescence lifetime imaging microscopy.

15500019.label: Project Objectives
15500019.value: To explore ETEs using a means–end approach and its laddering interview technique. This means–end model connects abstract innate psychological needs and core values (e.g., relatedness, competence, positive relationship, virtues), personal factors (e.g., character strengths, personal interest, knowledge and skills) and consequences (memorable and meaningful experiences, emotions, motives and goals) with concrete tourism activities. To create a knowledge base of ETEs comprising a hierarchical value map that highlights related key personal and experiential factors, a collection interview quote that provides contextual background for innovation and a visual diagram and lexicon that explain existing eudaimonic models in lay terms. Given this knowledge base, to create a toolkit that can be used to integrate ETEs into the co-design practice of tourism innovation. This toolkit will establish symmetry of knowledge among co-design team members and can be used to guide the team through the integrated design processes of idea exploration and conceptualisation. In the creation of the design toolkit, to identify hurdles that impede the integration of this knowledge base with other generic design tools (e.g., persona, service blueprint, user journey map, etc.) and thereby generate an informed design via a series of iterative co-design workshops.

15500019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500019.value: The tourism experience and its contribution to tourists’ wellbeing are important considerations in tourism development. Rather than viewing tourism as a form of hedonic consumption, some tourists travel for purposes of self-exploration, pursuing a personal interest, or learning, so their experiences become particularly memorable and meaningful. The field of positive psychology recognises such an experience as eudaimonia: an experience that resonates with one’s core values, character strengths and innate psychological needs, and hence results in a more sustained wellbeing. Furthermore, offering a eudaimonic tourism experience (ETE) can create a more sustainable tourism service, as suggested by the transformation economy—an economic offering that connects consumers at the most personal level, such that they experience a sense of real personal transformation. Understandably, not all travellers are seeking an ETE, especially if obtaining this experience requires ongoing practice and deep commitment. However, traces of eudaimonic benefits can be readily observed in many popular tourism settings, e.g., in the learning and reflection that occur at dark tourism sites and museums. This study argues that the ETE can be part of any tourism innovation. Nevertheless, developing innovations that foster ETE is deemed to be more challenging because the experience must be connected to tourists’ implicit personal factors. Tourism activities and emotions are regarded as means for obtaining a more valuable end result. Therefore, incorporating ETEs in tourism services requires an explicit understanding of the mechanism and conditions that can foster such an experience. The availability of such a knowledge base will enable a co-design team with diverse backgrounds to establish a symmetry of knowledge so that ETEs can be consciously discussed, mutually explored, and strategically implemented with respect to innovative propositions. This study explores cultural tourism for its potential to offer both hedonic and eudaimonic experiences. The goal of this research is twofold. Regarding its theoretical significance, this research uses a means–end approach to extend our limited understanding of ETEs by capturing the implicit personal and experiential factors that foster them. Regarding its practical importance, we explore how the generation of this knowledge can inspire and guide co-design practices for inspiring ETE innovations via action research co-design workshops. This study contributes to tourism by establishing an ETE knowledge base and providing a common language to facilitate discussion between different stakeholders. Also, it helps to identify plausible directions for co-design processes and thus, provides design rationales for making informed decisions during the design process. 旅遊體驗及其對旅客幸福感的提昇是未來旅遊業發展的重點考慮因素。一些遊客並非將旅遊視為一種享樂消費形式，而是為了自我探索、追求個人興趣和學習而旅行。因此他們的經歷變得特別難忘和有意義。積極心理學稱該體驗為幸福感（特指以積極的方式達致自我實現所帶來的幸福），這種體驗與個人的核心價值觀、美德和性格優勢和基本心理需要產生共鳴，因而帶來持久的幸福感。此外，提供幸福感的旅遊體驗（eudaimonic tourism experience, ETE）可以創造一個更加可持續的旅遊服務，正如轉型經濟所建議的那樣—一種在個人層面上連接消費者的經濟產品，從而使他們經歷自我變革。 雖然並非所有旅行者都在尋求ETE，尤其是有些情況下旅行者須要持續的實踐才能獲得這種體驗。然而， 旅客能在一些普及的旅遊設施中獲得零碎的幸福感，例如在黑色旅遊中，遊客可從景點和博物館的展品中學習和反思。因此這研究認為，ETE可以成為未來旅遊創新的一個重要元素。 然而，把能令旅客提昇幸福感的旅遊體驗元素投放於文化旅遊設計項目是一份十分具挑戰性的工作，因為這些體驗必須與遊客潛藏的個性因素聯繫起來。而旅遊活動和其情感產生只能視為得到幸福感的手段而非最終目的。因此，將ETE納入旅遊服務中需要明確了解可以促進這種體驗的機制和條件。建立一個有關於ETE的知識庫能把不同背景的共同協作設計團隊建立有關於這種體驗的知識對稱性，從而可以在共同協作過程中使設計團隊能明確清晰地討論，共同探索及有策略地把能令旅客提昇幸福感的機制和條件融入文化旅遊項目中。 透過探討文化旅遊中享樂和幸福感的體驗潛能。本研究目標有兩方面：在理論方面，本研究採用手段與目的分析方法 （means-end approach）來建立ETE的知識庫及相關通用語，通過捕捉促潛藏的個性和體驗因素來擴闊我們對ETE的有限理解。在實踐方面，我們用行動研究（action research）指導協同設計工作坊。目的在於研發一系列有效的設計工具來幫助共同協作團隊使用知識庫的內容，從而促進設計過程。 這研究為旅遊業做出重大貢獻，通過建立ETE知識庫及其設計工具給設計團隊一種通用語，令不同專業背景的人進行有效的討論，使設計團隊明確清晰地決策及提供設計依據。

15500119.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15500119.value: Prof Choi, Jaewon Dr Wan, Kam Ming

15500119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15500119.value: This study investigates the effect of algorithm trading in the corporate bond market. The advancement in computer algorithm improves trading quality in two major channels: faster order submission and lower transactions cost. However, prior studies rarely distinguish these two channels. Corporate bond market provides an ideal setting to study the latter channel since trading is done in an over-the-counter market without a consolidated limit order book. Thus, this study provides a unique setting to study the effect of algorithm trading on transaction cost and liquidity as follows: First, we examine the time-series variation in transactions cost in the corporate bond market. We expect that the transaction cost to be decreasing over time and the decrease is particularly pronounced after the sharp increase in algorithm trading in the corporate bond market since 2016. Because machines are known to oust human traders in the corporate bond market, especially for odd-lot trades (i.e., trade sizes of less than $1 million), we expect the reduction in transaction cost to be larger for smaller sized trades in the corporate bond market. Next, we use TRACE--an enhanced dataset which can identity individual dealer with a masked ID--to sort dealers based on their participation in algorithm trading for odd-lot trades. Because algorithm trading is a main driver of the significant increase in odd-lot trading, we expect the dealers who involve heavily in odd-lot trades to be more likely to be users of algorithms. In a cross section test, we examine whether transactions cost is significantly lower for dealers who use algorithm trading than those who do not. We also conjecture that dealers who participate heavily in odd-lot trades also provide more liquidity in the corporate bond market in the recent periods. Last, because transaction cost for odd-lot trades has dropped significantly in the recent periods and traders can split large orders easily, we expect that Feldhutter’s (2012) measure of selling pressure is a less accurate measure. Feldhutter (2012) uses differences in large versus small orders to measure selling pressure. In equity markets, large institutional trades can be easily broken up into smaller trade sizes. Similarly, because smaller orders are easier (and less expensive) to trade with the rise of algorithm trading in the corporate bond market, we investigate an alternative measure of selling pressure by incorporating information on aggregate order flow from a large individual dealer than just using the price of each order.
