15503219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15503219.value: We deliver four papers to fulfill our research objectives, two of which are published in top/top-tier journals and two are undergoing review processes in some top journals. Specifically, paper 1 in Part C addresses objectives 1-3 by studying a government’s optimal subsidy design in spurring green innovation with consumer heterogeneity. Paper 2 in Part C addresses objective 3 by studying green product design and pricing issues in a product line setting with various levels of consumer heterogeneity. Papers 3 and 4 in Part C jointly fulfill objective 4 by investigating the green product design and pricing issues in a competitive environment with social interactions and learning-by-doing effect, respectively. Next, I summarize the major findings for each research objective with more details relegated to the four papers. Objective 1: We show that subsidizing different recipients makes a significant difference. Specifically, subsidizing consumers requires a smaller budget level to stimulate innovation, whereas subsidizing R&D requires a greater one. However, once the innovation is successfully spurred for a given budget, subsidizing R&D results in the highest green technology level, compared with subsidizing production or consumers. Objective 2: We show that a welfare-maximizing government leans towards subsidizing R&D when its primary focus is environmental protection and subsidizing consumers when it places a higher priority on economic performance. Compared with a single subsidy policy, although offering a portfolio can yield greater social welfare, it may not necessarily improve the firm's profit, which critically depends on how the government balances the economic gain with the environmental benefit. Objective 3: We conduct comprehensive sensitivity analysis. We depict the trend of how the optimal portfolio is constructed as focal parameters change and demonstrate that a higher budget or a larger fraction of socially conscious consumers could lead to desired social outcomes. In addition, we build another product line model and show that consumer heterogeneity may lead to some adverse impacts. Objective 4: We build two models to study green product design and pricing issues in a competitive market. Paper 3 shows that competing firms’ optimal quality differentiation is affected by social interactions, which becomes larger (resp. smaller) when social interactions enhance consumer valuation (resp. expand awareness). Paper 4 shows that competing firms may strategically charge price to leverage quality improvement, especially when the spillover of such improvement is strong. Both papers can be applied to the context of green product innovation and provide managerial insights.

15503219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15503219.value: Around the theme of this project, there are many related research topics that are worth studying in the future. For example, green technology innovation may involve significant risks, out of which technology development risk and demand risk are two primary ones. How a government should deploy different formats of subsidy schemes to both tackle such uncertainties and incentivize green innovation would be an important question to investigate. In addition, it would be interesting to extend our model into a supply chain setting, which brings additional tension of double marginalization. It is important to understand how such channel inefficiency could challenge the role of subsidy, and how to design subsidy schemes to align incentive and push the system for a more efficient green transformation. Finally, how would consumer side complexities, including consumer heterogeneity, social interactions, etc., alter the derived insights. All the above questions are not only relevant in practice, but also not fully investigated in the existing literature. Our current results lay a solid foundation for further exploring these questions.

15503219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503219.value: Encouraging green technology innovation and adoption is of great importance for governments to deal with environmental issues, in which subsidies play a crucial role. Meanwhile, there is a growing stimulus in retail markets, as consumers are becoming more willing to pay for products with green features. Carefully combining the incentives from both the government and the market is the key to promote green innovation. The central theme of this project is to provide a systematic understanding on how a firm’s green product design and pricing decisions are affected by government subsidy schemes and consumer heterogeneity in a segmented market. The research outcomes are written into 4 papers, out of which two are published in top-tier journals. Our research could provide not only suggestions for governments to stimulate green production innovation and consumption by allocating its limited budget to different subsidy schemes, but also managerial insights on how the optimal subsidy policy is altered by the government’s resource, preference, and external market conditions. In addition, our research also yields general insights on how to manage the design and sale of green products in a competitive environment with added complexities, including consumer heterogeneity, social interactions, quality improvement.

15503319.label: Project Objectives
15503319.value: To present a new mathematical model (the PAR-SEIR model) for medical relief supply in emergency, incorporating production, allocation, and/or routing into the SEIR epidemic diffusion model. We use the SEIR model to forecast the medical relief demand with the information update period by period and the impact of medical relief supply. To develop mathematical methods and solution algorithms for medical relief production, allocation, and/or routing decisions in the PAR-SEIR model for optimizing the efficacy of medical relief supply in multiple areas with appropriate goals, such as (i) to minimize the total expected penalty of oversupplies and non-fulfilment of demands, (ii) to minimize the total timing of relief deliveries, and (iii) to minimize the total operational cost. To perform sensitivity analysis of the parameters of the problem on the solutions obtained in Objective 2. To perform computer simulations to test, or mathematical analysis on, the performance of the solution algorithms derived in Objective 2, and provide management insights and knowledge for epidemic outbreaks.

15503319.label: Major findings and research outcome
15503319.value: We have met the objectives of the project and come up with results in three journal papers. (Due to COVID-19, we could not attend conferences overseas.) The details of the three journal papers are as follows. (1) In the paper “Foresighted Medical Resources Allocation during an Epidemic Outbreak”, published in Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review, we notice that efficient allocation of medical resources is always an important public policy issue for an emergency large-scale epidemic outbreak, like COVID-19. To balance the demand and supply for medical resources, we develop foresighted and myopic medical resources allocation decision models for governments during a large-scale epidemic outbreak. In the paper, we derive some important properties of these two approaches and generate useful managerial implications for public allocation policy during an epidemic outbreak. (2) In the paper “Vaccine Supply Decisions and Government Interventions for Recurring Epidemics”, published in Annals of Operations Research, we envisage that recurring epidemics, like Malaria, Cholera, and COVID-19, may occur unexpectedly and in emergency. Vaccination is the most effective method to control, prevent, or stop such recurring epidemics. However, previous research on vaccination coverage mainly focuses on the single-period model of vaccine (relief) supply, which does not reflect the recurring property of such epidemics. In this paper, we construct a multi-period vaccine demand model to study multi-period vaccine supply decisions and government interventions. We derive properties of the model and conduct numerical studies to generate practical implications of the analytical findings. (3) In the paper “Information Sharing and Coordination in a Vaccine Supply Chain”, published in Annals of Operations Research, we notice that vaccination is a well-known method to protect the public against an epidemic outbreak. In this paper, we study the cooperation between public hospitals and private clinics in terms of logistical decisions for a vaccine (relief) supply chain to cope with the outbreak of an epidemic. We model a vaccine system consisting of a public hospital, a profit-maximizing private clinic, and self-interested individuals, under three scenarios: (i) without information sharing (concerning vaccine inventory and vaccine price), (ii) with information sharing and subsidy, and (iii) with information sharing and allocation. Our results provide both theoretical and managerial insights on vaccine supply decisions.

15503319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503319.value: Large-scale epidemic outbreaks are potential and fatal threats to human public health. In response to an emergent large-scale epidemic, timely and sufficient medical relief is crucial for the success of epidemic control. This project aims to develop advanced analytical and mathematical models for improving the process of epidemic response. We have proposed novel mathematical models to provide medical relief production, allocation, and routing decisions with time-varying demand forecasting based on SEIR epidemic diffusion model. Results of this project provide important management insights for the success of controlling an epidemic outbreak.

15503519.label: Project Objectives
15503519.value: To understand the structural properties of the dynamic bundling control for the network revenue management. Distinct features associated with the bundling pricing and network topology will facilitate the design and evaluation of management policy, and overcome the “curse of dimension” in most Markovian formulations. To evaluate the performance of the proposed bundling policies via numerical study to demonstrate their effectiveness and potential for application. 15503519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15503519.value: Revenue management has become a competitive instrument across industries. In this proposal, we will study dynamic bundling in the network revenue management system. In the travel industry, bundling is a common selling method to offer a product line that consists of individual components (e.g. air ticket and hotel room) and a package of these components. This selling method has become increasingly important in the travel industry and online markets. In practice, it is a challenge to formulate a feasible policy for the supplier/seller to decide whether to accept customer request for components or packages, due to complicating factors such as the limited and changing inventory availability, remaining time for selling, and the inter-dependency between components and packages. Formulating such a problem as a dynamic programming model would inevitably subject to the curse of dimensionality. In the proposed study, we aim to overcome the above difficulties and develop effective bundling strategies in dynamic settings. Specifically, we strive to understand the dynamic system structure under bundling strategy, develop effective control policies and evaluate the potential for practical application. Our preliminary results for a simple case with two components and three products (incl. a package product) have demonstrated that there is a vast room for a fruitful study along this line. It is also worth noting that the reinforcement learning approach (a non-parametric approach) has received wide attention recently, and that it would be a promising study by connecting the approach to our revenue management problem. The proposed study would contribute to revenue management theory significantly by bridging the gap between theory and application. It is also timely as an increasing number of companies compete on analytics, calling for effective tools for attracting customers and boosting profits. 收入管理已成為各行業的競爭工具。在此提案中，我們將研究網絡收益管理系統中的動態捆綁。在旅遊業中，捆綁是常見銷售方法，它提供由單件產品（例如機票和酒店房間）及其构成的成套產品。這種銷售方式在旅遊業和在線市場中變得越來越重要。 在實踐中，由於各种複雜因素，諸如庫存有限和不斷變化，剩餘銷售時間以及产品之间相互影响，供應商/銷售商难以制定可行的策略，以決定是否满足客戶對单件或成套产品的需求。用動態規劃解决這樣的問題，將不可避免地遇到維度的难题。 在擬議的研究中，我們的目標是克服上述困難，並製定有效的捆綁策略可用于動態商业環境。具體而言，我們期望了解捆綁策略下的系統動態結構，制定有效的控制策略並評估其實際應用的潛力。我們研究了包含兩個組件和三個產品（包括套件產品）的簡單案例，初步結果表明，這條线路有很大的空間進行富有成效的研究。值得注意的是，強化學習方法（非參數方法）最近受到廣泛關注，該方法與我們的收益管理問題聯繫起來研究是有前景的。 本研究將縮小理論與應用之間的差距，顯著促進收益管理理論发展。隨著越來越多的公司强调在数据分析方面进行競爭，它们需要有效的方法來吸引客戶並提高利潤，因此我们的研究正適時宜。

15503519.label: Realisation of objectives
15503519.value: The project investigates the revenue optimization potential of mix-bundling strategies for providers with limited inventories. The strategy aims to maximize revenue for a provider who holds inventories for multiple components. Mix-bundling refers to a selling method where a retailer offers a product line consisting of individual components and bundles that comprise these components. By offering both individual components and bundled packages, the retailer can attract different segments of consumers. Package consumers are enticed by the discounted price and the convenience of making multiple purchases in a single transaction. This segmentation allows the provider to potentially increase the number of transactions and per-transaction revenue. One of the key drivers for providers to adopt mix-bundling is inventory concern. When dealing with perishable products, such as hotel rooms or airline seats, it is more effective to sell packages than to cut prices for individual components to boost sales. Selling packages helps to optimize the utilization of inventory and maximize revenue. Our study employs a quantitative approach and develops a methodology to analyze the dynamic nature of mix-bundling. It begins by formulating a discrete-time Markov Chain model to simulate consumer arrivals and product requests over a finite time horizon. This model allows for the examination of consumer behavior and the decision-making process of providers in response to these requests. The study focuses on a scenario where providers hold inventories for multiple components and adopt mix-bundling to sell a line of products comprising individual components and bundles. The research starts by considering a setting in which the provider has inventories for two components and adopts quantity-based control to manage selling. Under this approach, the provider accepts a consumer request for a product if its price is above the associated marginal value. The study analyzes the effects of inventory levels on product values and optimal policies. Specifically, it investigates the scarcity effect and the complementarity effect. The scarcity effect refers to the increase in the marginal value of a product that contains a component with a lower inventory level, while the complementarity effect refers to the increase in the marginal value of the other component with a higher inventory level. To extend the analysis to a general setting with inventories for multiple components, we adopt price-based control to manage selling. In this scenario, the product provider dynamically decides the bundle set, component selling prices, and bundle discounts. The findings from the analysis highlight that the revenue generation potential of mix-bundling depends crucially on various factors. These factors include the correlation of consumer valuations for components, as well as the availability and dispersion of initial component inventories. It provides insights into the optimal bundle selection, component pricing, and bundle discount strategies that can maximize revenue in the mix-bundling context. To address the complexity of optimizing prices for each product, we develop and apply heuristics to determine these pricing strategies. The heuristics are formulated based on the trade-offs between price levels, demand elasticity, and revenue objectives. It also provides insights into the relationship between pricing decisions and revenue outcomes. To validate and refine the heuristics, empirical analysis is conducted using simulated data generated from the formulated discrete-time Markov Chain model. This empirical analysis allows for the evaluation of different pricing strategies and their impact on revenue generation. As a result, these numerical studies provide insights into the effects of inventory levels, consumer valuations, and pricing strategies on revenue optimization in mix-bundling scenarios. These findings highlight the importance of considering scarcity and complementarity effects, as well as the correlation of consumer valuations and inventory availability, in making optimal bundling and pricing decisions. To wrap up, for the objective 1, we have carried out a thorough analysis of the structural properties of the dynamic bundling control for network revenue management. We first explore a setting with two components and three products that include each of the two components, and then extend to the multiple-component case. By characterizing optimal solution structures and providing a heuristics in a dynamic setting under inventory limits, we offer insights into mix-bundling as a method of revenue generation. For the objective 2, building on the key features we have revealed, such as the scarcity and complementarity effect, we develop heuristics for the optimal bundling control policies. The heuristics applies to dynamically decide bundle sets, component selling prices and bundle discounts. It is effective and easy to implement. For the objective 3, in addition to theoretical study, we have applied the Monte Carlo simulation to evaluate the performance of the bundling control policies. Valuable managerial insights are obtained. Overall, the research contributes to the existing literature on revenue management and bundling strategies by providing a detailed analysis of the methodology employed to study dynamic mix-bundling with limited inventories. By utilizing a discrete-time Markov Chain model and developing heuristics for pricing decisions, the study offers valuable insights into the revenue optimization potential of mix-bundling strategies for providers.

15503519.label: Major findings and research outcome
15503519.value: Mix-bundling, a popular marketing strategy in various industries, involves offering products that consist of individual components as well as bundled packages. Our research focuses on the revenue optimization potential of mix-bundling in the context of limited inventories. It investigates the challenges faced by providers, such as inventory imbalance, and the decision-making processes involved in accepting consumer requests for components or bundles. We formulate a discrete-time Markov Chain model to simulate consumer arrivals and product requests. The study employs a threshold-based policy under quantity-based control for a two-component inventory scenario. Furthermore, we extend the analysis to a general setting with multiple components, utilizing price-based control. To address the complexity of optimizing prices for each product, we develop heuristics to determine component prices and bundle discounts. A number of managerial insights are obtained in this study. For example, it reveals that the existence of scarcity and complementarity effects in the context of mix-bundling, and that the scarcity effect generally outweighs the complementarity effect in influencing optimal policies. The study also highlights the time-dependent nature of product values due to inventory imbalance. Additionally, it demonstrates the importance of the correlation between consumer valuations for components and the availability of initial inventories in revenue generation through mix-bundling. The research contributes to the existing literature on revenue management by providing novel insights into dynamic mix-bundling with limited inventories and offering practical implications for providers in terms of inventory management and pricing decisions. Part of the research results are summarized in the paper Liao et al(2023). In connection to the revenue management problem under study, we also study a marketing resource allocation problem with limited multiple resources and in a two-stage setting. It is motivated when we looked at the bundling control issues in an online retailer. The study is reported in Zhang et al.(2022). Another important problem arises from this study when the product is service and customers have to wait. In this case, what would happen if the customer may abandon the waiting? Answering this question requires an investigation of a more basic problem concerning the queueing system with abandonment. We have collected part of the results in the paper Lee et al.(2021)

15503519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15503519.value: One interesting area to explore in future studies is the idea of bundle alliances. This means that an airline and a hotel could team up and offer bundled packages to customers. In a previous study (by Wright, Groenevelt, and others), they looked at how airlines can work together through a transfer price mechanism, but they found that achieving perfect coordination is difficult. This opens up an intriguing topic to design methods that can coordinate different companies more effectively. Another aspect worth considering is the overlap between package deals and individual components. For example, when a certain component is out of stock, it could lead to customers considering alternative choices. This issue of stockout-based spillover hasn't been explicitly explored in the current study. To delve deeper into this, we would need to examine how consumers behave when their first choice is unavailable and they have to switch to their second choice. It's important to consider the strong connection between these two choices.

15503519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503519.value: We investigate mix-bundling as a revenue management strategy, combining products into packages for sale. The study focuses on optimizing component inventories to maximize revenue. Initially, we analyze a scenario with two components and quantity-based control. Then, we extend to multiple components and price-based control. There are many interesting finds. For example, in the case of two components, fewer units of a component increase its bundle value, while more units boost the other component's value; package value declines over time, while specific component value varies due to inventory imbalances. In the multi-component scenario with price-based control, we propose a dynamic method for bundle composition, component pricing, and discounts. Mix-bundling's revenue potential depends on consumer preferences and inventory availability. Overall, this study explores strategies for effective bundled product sales and inventory management to maximize revenue, considering factors like scarcity, consumer preferences, and time dynamics.

15503619.label: Realisation of objectives
15503619.value: First of all, this project is a quite challenging one, because of the breakout of pandemic and the primary data collection nature of this research. Fortunately, we managed to accomplish most of the original objectives and one additional objective. This additional objective was added mainly for fully utilizing the data collection opportunity, which was so rare in the past three years and in the hospital setting. Data Collection The main data collection was mainly conducted in a public hospital located in a southeast city in mainland, China. We got access to one Multi-Discipline Team (MDT), which focuses on digestive oncology. Every week (usually on Thursday afternoons), this MDT discussed 3-10 cases, and each meeting last for 1.5-2.5 hours. There were usually 6-10 specialists in each MDT meeting, often including histopathologists, gastroenterologist, internists, surgeons, and radiologists. Although there were some core members in this MDT, members who attended each meeting varied across time—some needed to travel, and some peripheral members were invited to attend the meeting to provide information and their opinions. We conducted interviews, observations, recording of meetings, transcript coding, and survey. Our final sample included into the regression analysis was 112 MDT case discussions from 26 meetings. Besides this main site, we also tried to get access to MDTs in another hospital located in Northern China. Although eventually we did not successfully obtain MDT meeting data, instead we got two valuable data sets—one is how leaders in hospitals help new nurses to make sense of the COVID-19 crisis and the meaning of their profession, and the other is interviews with doctors at MDTs on how diversified information facilitate creativity at work. We also conducted a series of experiments. Results and Objectives Realization Our data has shown some interesting findings regarding the micro-dynamics in MDT meetings. 1. Objective 1 (To examine whether the earliness of informal leader’s voice hinders team information exchange) and Objective 2 (To investigate the role of team status inequality in MDT meetings) Interestingly, in contrary to our prediction, we did not find any significant main effects of the earliness of informal leader’s voice or team status inequality in MDT on team information exchange tie density. Nevertheless, we found that the earliness of informal leader’s communication was negatively related to team information exchange when team status inequality was low rather than high. In other words, the two factors interact with each other in affecting team information exchange, rather than solely by either one of them. 2. Objective 3 (To explore the role of informal leaders’ cross-expertise information seeking in MDT meetings) Our results showed that in MDT case discussions, informal leader’s information seeking had a positive effect on team information exchange tie density, which was in line with our expectation. Interestingly, we also found that the proportion of informal leader’s communication was negatively related to team information exchange tie density. Moreover, the negative effect of the proportion of informal leader’s communication was alleviated by the informal leader’s information seeking. In other words, leaders’ cross-expertise information seeking in MDT meetings plays a crucial and positive role. 3. Objective 4 (To differentiate two types of team voice quality) and Objective 5 (To study the effects of team information exchange and team voice quality on MDT outcomes) These two objectives are accomplished, but with some difficulties in interpreting the meaning of MDT discussions from a professional perspective, and the challenges in tracking the real effects of MDT decisions on patients’ well-being. From our interviews with doctors, however, we initially found that both diversity and comprehensiveness influence the MDT decisions. We also found that creativity type (incremental vs. radical) is influenced by the diversity of information—the integration of seemingly unrelated information contributes to radical creativity. Meanwhile, we learned that time pressure encountered by doctors may influence how to search and integrate diversified information. Inspired by this finding, we collected survey data to empirically test this idea, and learned how time pressure influences information search and then creativity (incremental vs. radical). 4. Objective 6 (To explore how leaders' communication influence employees' professional identity, especially in crises) Our research was conducted during the pandemic period, in which healthcare workers encountered serious challenges and crises in their work. Through our interviews with doctors and nurses, we found that sensegiving (referring to the attempts of management to “influence the sensemaking and meaning construction of others) from senior doctors and leaders plays an important role in facilitating new healthcare works to interpret their professional role and find the meaning of their work. Inspired by this finding, we collected both survey and experimental data to investigate the change of new nurses’ professional identification and meaning of work, and examine how leaders’ sensegiving plays a role. We learned that crisis does not necessarily hurt newcomers’ professional identification or meaning of work, especially when leaders engage in sensegiving.

15503619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15503619.value: Major Findings Our data has shown some interesting findings regarding the micro-dynamics in MDT meetings. In particular, in MDT case discussions, the proportion of informal leader’s communication was negatively related to team information exchange tie density, whereas informal leader’s information seeking had a positive effect. Moreover, the negative effect of the proportion of informal leader’s communication was alleviated by the informal leader’s information seeking. Interestingly, in contrary to our prediction, we found that the earliness of informal leader’s communication was negatively related to team information exchange when team status inequality was low rather than high. The interviews conducted in this study also showed that (1) the integration of seemingly unrelated information contributes to radical creativity, and (2) sensegiving (referring to the attempts of management to “influence the sensemaking and meaning construction of others) from senior doctors plays an important role in facilitating new healthcare workers to interpret their professional role and find the meaning of their work. These findings inform and inspire us to conduct further two other quantitative studies, which compliment and confirm the qualitative study. Research Outcome The MDT paper went slower than we expected, but we already finished two conference papers in two prominent international conferences (one in the Bi-annual Conference of the International Association of Chinese Management Research, and the other in the Annual Conference of Society of Industrial and Occupational Psychology). We plan to submit it to Human Relations later. The two spin-off projects—one on time pressure, information diversity, and creativity, and the other on sensegiving and professional identification— are published in two high-quality journals in the field: one has been accepted by Journal of Organizational Behavior and the other has been accepted by Personnel Psychology.

15503619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15503619.value: Given the importance of the micro-dynamics of MDT meetings and different MDTs may have different processes or climate, it would be great if MDTs from other settings (such as R&D) could be investigated in the future. The benefits of doing so would be at least two-fold: first, it would be great to see if the findings obtained in this project could be replicated in different situations; and second, it would be important to check if higher-level factors, such as leadership styles and team climates, play any role in the voice processes and thus MDT outcomes.

15503619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503619.value: By integrating epistemic motivation theory and social network research, our project explores how informal leaders and status hierarchy together influence information exchange in multi-disciplinary team (MDT) meetings. These findings extend the current team research, which often neglect the micro-dynamics within teams or how team members really work together. For practices, our findings suggest how MDT meeting could be better organized and implemented. To gain more inputs from experts in different domains, the informal leaders in MDT meetings should actively engage in information seeking, and be cautious about how much they should say during the meetings. Our spin-off projects highlight the importance of information diversity and leader communication. That is, the integration of seemingly-unrelated information may stimulate radical creativity, whereas that of related information leads to incremental creativity; and how leaders help employees to interpret crisis can help employees to overcome challenges and even increase their professional identification and meaning of work.

15503719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15503719.value: The growth of the online learning industry over the last six years has been phenomenal. The number of individuals using online learning technology grew to 81 million by 2017. In the same year, the largest online learning platform, Coursera, saw paying users increase by 70%. Meanwhile, the usage of online learning technology in K-12 classrooms has also been growing rapidly. Over half a decade, the number of school districts that have adopted this new technology as a K-12 instruction tool has doubled (Science and Engineering Indicators 2018). Despite the fact that online learning technology is among the top emerging technologies in the past ten years, little is known about how the diffusion of online learning technology among offline education institutions takes place. Among the most important questions from the perspective of an online learning technology firm are how diffusion takes place and how to optimize market intervention strategies accordingly. To understand the diffusion process, it is essential to first understand how the adoption decision is made. This is because diffusion can be seen as the aggregation of a series of individual institutions' decisions by weighing the benefit of adoption against the costs. This study aims to fill this gap by first identifying a set of demand-side explanations of this diffusion process. Using a unique panel data set that combines offline institutions' adoption decisions with measures of offline institutions' teaching resources, and holding constant supply-side firm marketing activities, this paper shows how the distribution of offline institutions' teaching resources and adoption decisions made by neighborhood institutions affect an institution's adoption decision. In the end, through simulating offline institutions' technology adoption decisions under counterfactual situations, this study provides rigorous guidance to online learning technology firms on how to efficiently conduct market intervention activities. 在过去六年中，在线学习行业的发展是惊人的。到2017年，使用在线学习技术的人数增加到8100万。同年，最大的在线学习平台Coursera的付费用户增加70％。同时，越来越多的K12教育机构也开始使用在线教育。在五年内，采用这项新技术的教育机构增加了一倍。了解在线教育在离线教育机构中的传播，可以有效帮助在线教育优化市场干预策略。要了解扩散过程，首先必须要做到这一点了解采纳决策是如何做出的。本研究旨在通过首先确定一组来填补这一空白。本研究将调查采用和传播或在线学习技术的过程 确定并量化三个关键的需求方机制： (1) 在教育输出中在线教育和教育机构的资源的替代/互补效应， (2)不同地域在传播中的互相影响，以及 (3) 从早期采用者到后来采用者的溢出效应。最后通过模拟反事实的离线教育技术采用决策，为企业的新技术引入战略提供指导。

15503719.label: Realisation of objectives
15503719.value: In light of the "Double Reduction" policy implemented in China, its associated initiatives, and the impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic, numerous firms within the online tutoring and learning sector have pivoted to alternative industries. Consequently, this unprecedented environment hindered our ability to fulfill the initial objectives of our project, primarily due to the operational difficulties experienced by our partner institutions and the scarcity of accessible data. As detailed in our preceding progress report, the research team judiciously elected to realign the project's central aims into two distinct trajectories: 1. To preserve the continuity of our work in online learning, we transitioned our attention towards Educational Technology (EdTech) and initiated an investigation into the integration of intelligent chatbot systems within emerging EdTech enterprises. 2. To investigate the ramifications of the "Double Reduction" policy on the online tutoring and learning domain, this line of inquiry was contingent upon the procurement of relevant data. Regrettably, we encountered insurmountable obstacles in pursuing the second research path, once again due to the non-availability of essential data. While progress was made on the first objective, we faced significant challenges in securing a comprehensive, accurate, and dependable dataset from digital repositories, such as Crunchbase.com. In a turn of events, our exploration into smart assistant technologies in EdTech startups led us to establish a collaborative research partnership with a business enterprise. This collaboration, which focuses on the adoption and utilization of chatbot technology in commercial settings, falls outside the purview of the educational policy constraints. In light of these developments, we made a strategic decision to concentrate our efforts on this new collaborative project and to introduce an additional objective as below: New Objective: To examine the impact of users' interaction with smart assistants (chatbots) in the business context on user performance of complex tasks (product customization) We have the pleasure to have produced a draft paper, now being refined for submission to Journal of Management Information Systems, one of the top journals in the Information Systems field. We acknowledge that the project's trajectory has diverged from our original proposal. It is with a deep sense of responsibility and commitment to our research that we request the reviewers to consider the extraordinary circumstances we have navigated. We earnestly appeal for your understanding and support, allowing us to persevere in our research endeavors and to affirm the value of our findings. We extend our sincere gratitude for your consideration.

15503719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15503719.value: With regard to Objective 4 above, our paper presents a study on the impact of chatbot design on human-chatbot communication efficiency and how it influences user satisfaction and task success in a commercial context. The study focuses on two specific design features: chatbot proactivity and social identity. Major findings of the study include: 1. Chatbot Proactivity: Chatbot proactivity, which involves the chatbot initiating conversation and offering options to users, was found to decrease communication inefficiency by 15.8%. Proactive chatbots were able to reduce cognitive uncertainty in users, leading to fewer misunderstandings and more efficient communication. The positive impact of proactivity design on consumer task success and satisfaction was mediated by reduced communication inefficiency. 2. Chatbot Social Identity: Assigning a social identity to chatbots (such as a human name and intimate conversational style) did not have a significant direct impact on communication inefficiency. However, social identity design was found to weaken the negative effects of communication inefficiency on consumer satisfaction. This suggests that users may show favoritism towards chatbots with a social identity, leading to more patience and forgiveness during interactions, even when communication is inefficient. 3. User Satisfaction and Task Success: Communication inefficiency was negatively correlated with user satisfaction and the probability of task success. A unit increase in communication inefficiency led to about a 96% decrease in complex task (product customization) success probability and a 37.8% decrease in user satisfaction. Research Outcome: The study contributes to the literature by providing a measure for communication inefficiency and by applying uncertainty reduction theory to the context of human-chatbot interactions. It bridges a gap in existing research on chatbots by examining the conversational process rather than focusing solely on outcomes like purchase or persuasion. The findings have practical implications for businesses employing chatbots, suggesting that proactive chatbot design and careful consideration of social identity can improve user interactions and outcomes. In summary, the paper highlights the importance of chatbot design elements in reducing communication inefficiency, which in turn affects user satisfaction and task success in conversations with chatbots. It underscores the role of social identity in moderating users' responses to communication inefficiencies.

15503719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15503719.value: The research presented in the study offers substantial implications for the advancement of Human-AI (chatbot) interaction design and provides a fertile ground for further exploration. The potential for extending this research is substantial, particularly in examining the long-term effects of chatbot proactivity and social identity on user engagement and the retention of customer loyalty. Our course of action includes the following: 1. the submission of the paper to a top journal in the Information Systems field--e.g., Journal of Management Information Systems. We target the first submission in 6 months as we are still refining the research motivation and theoretical development. 2. we will explore future research on the impacts of chatbot design features across different cultural contexts and also assess the role of individual differences in user-chatbot interaction, considering factors like language proficiency and openness to AI. 3. Considering the rapid evolution of AI and natural language processing capabilities, especially the emerging AI agents enabled by large language models such as ChatGPT (note that our research was conducted before the advent of ChatGPT), we will take a deep dive into the role of technology advancement and how firms embrace (resist) AI agents and integrate them in their operations.

15503719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15503719.value: Customers are often chatting with a robot (chatbot) on a company's website to buy something or get help. The study in the paper looked at how the chatbot's behavior affects customer chat experience. Two things were tested: if the chatbot starts talking to a customer first with helpful options (proactive) and if it has a friendly character with a name (social identity). The study found that when chatbots take the lead in conversations, people tend to have smoother chats with fewer mix-ups. This leads to happier customers and a higher chance they'll finish what they came to do, like buying a product or getting their questions answered. However, giving the chatbot a name and personality didn't necessarily make the chats go more smoothly, but it did make people less upset when things got confusing. This paper is important because it helps companies understand how to make chatbots that customers like talking to, which can make them want to come back. This is valuable because happy customers usually mean better business, and as chatbots become more common, making them as helpful and friendly as possible is key.

15504219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504219.value: Product recalls are the outcome of severe product quality failures which typically result in significant costs to the recalling firms. Despite the negative outcomes of product recalls and the emergence of high-impact product recall events in recent years, there are limited studies on the determinants of product recalls. This proposal plans to fill in the gap in the literature by exploring the effect of financial analysts, an important information intermediary in the capital market, on the likelihood of a product recall. Analyst following has two potential effects on product recalls. On the one hand, financial analysts may serve as external monitors of managers and mitigate firm financing frictions by reducing firm information asymmetry. This makes firm investments in production more efficient and effective, which should reduce the likelihood of product recalls. On the other hand, financial analysts’ forecasts impose excessive performance pressure on managers, which could induce them to cut investments in production in order to meet short-term targets. As a result, firm investments in production would be inadequate, which should result in higher likelihood of product recalls. To explore the effect of analyst following on product recalls, we will use product recall data from four U.S. regulatory agencies. To alleviate the endogeneity concerns, we will perform difference-in-difference (DiD) tests around two exogenous shocks to analyst following. We will also conduct cross-sectional analyses to investigate whether the effect of analyst following on product recalls varies for firms with different institutional ownership, media coverage, product market competition, and analyst experience. Our study will contribute to three strands of literature. First, it will contribute to the product recall literature by investigating whether financial analysts, an important information intermediary in the capital market, have any effect on the likelihood of product recalls. Second, it will contribute to the line of research that documents the real effect of the stock market on firm operations by exploring whether activities by market participants, such as financial analysts, affect firms’ production decisions. Third, it will contribute to the analyst following literature by providing new evidence on the role of financial analysts. Our study will answer the question whether financial analysts play a positive or a negative role in firms’ production decisions.

15504219.label: Realisation of objectives
15504219.value: I have achieved all the objectives in a paper "Penny-Wise and Pound-Foolish: Does Striving to Meet Earnings Expectations by Manipulating Real Activities Trigger Product Recalls?". In this paper, we examine whether managers’ activities in striving to reach earnings targets through real earnings manipulation affect their firms’ product recalls. Our evidence implies that firms suspected of manipulating real activities in trying to meet earnings benchmarks exhibit a higher likelihood and frequency of product recalls. In cross-sectional results consistent with expectations, we find that the impact of exploiting real activities to attain earnings benchmarks on product recalls intensifies for firms whose managers have stronger incentives to manage earnings and subsides for firms subject to greater customer power and firms with more growth opportunities. Additional analysis shows that lowering product quality to meet-or-beat earnings expectations elevates investors’ skepticism about suspected firms’ earnings and undermines their future performance. Below are more details of how I have achieved the objectives. To examine the research question proposed in the paper, we hand-collect data on product recalls from four regulatory agencies in the U.S.: the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC), the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), and the U.S. Coast Guard (USCG). We gauge the earnings target with the consensus analyst forecast and designate a firm as suspected of meeting-or-beating earnings benchmarks if the difference between its actual earnings per share (EPS) and the average analyst forecasted EPS is between zero and two cents. Consistent with prior research (Cohen and Zarowin 2010; Zang 2012), we also construct an aggregate measure of a firm’s real earnings management activities. The interaction term of these two variables captures the firm’s suspected benchmark beating through real earnings management (hereafter SBBREM). In analyzing a sample of 11,434 firm-year observations covering the 2001-2017 period, we find that SBBREM is associated with a higher likelihood and frequency of product recalls. Reflecting the first-order economic impact according to our coefficient estimates, we find that, compared to non-SBBREM firms, SBBREM firms experience a 10.76% (43.57%) increase in the likelihood (number) of product recalls relative to the sample mean value. This evidence lends support to the narrative that the pressure to meet-or-beat earnings targets motivates firms to orchestrate the manipulation of real activities―by, for example, cutting investments and discretionary expenses and engaging in overproduction―that leads to more product recalls. In extensively analyzing whether our core results are robust, we continue to find supportive evidence. We also undertake several tests designed to alleviate endogeneity threats to reliable identification. The test results show that our main evidence is unlikely to stems from correlated omitted variables that drive both recalls and SBBREM. The findings so far answer the research questions outline in the first two objectives “To determine whether managers' activities in striving to meet/beat analyst earnings forecasts affect the incidence of product recalls” and “Assuming that managers' above activities do affect the incidence of product recalls, to determine the mechanisms through which these activities play a role”. Next, we explore cross-sectional variation in the relation between SBBREM and product recalls. First, we find that the impact of SBBREM on product recalls is magnified for firms whose managers have stronger incentives to manipulate earnings. Our evidence implies that these managers are more eager to manage earnings upward (e.g., Graham et al. 2005; Bergstresser and Philippon 2006), which distorts firm operations and leads to more product failures. Second, we report that the importance of SBBREM to product recalls falls for firms subject to more discipline in the form of customer power. These results suggest that powerful customers constrain managerial opportunistic behaviors in the production process by imposing stricter monitoring and threatening to end cooperation (e.g., Patatoukas 2012; Crawford, Huang, Li, and Yang 2020). Third, we find that the role that SBBREMs plays in product recalls is concentrated in firms with fewer growth opportunities. This evidence implies that investments in product quality can lead to higher future value for firms with more growth opportunities. Moreover, these firms experience less severe agency problems (Arikan and Stulz 2016), also reducing the impact of managerial opportunism on product recalls. These findings answer the research questions outline in the third objective “To determine whether other stock market and product market characteristics affect the relation between managers' above activities and product recalls”. Additionally, we examine whether lowering product quality to meat-or-beat earnings targets elevates investors’ skepticism about suspected firms’ earnings and undermines their future performance. We find that product recalls in prior years reduce the market response to suspected firms’ earnings surprises, implying that investors become more skeptical in this situation. Further, we report that the incidence of product recalls has a negative impact on firms’ future performance evident in their valuations and sales growth.

15504219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504219.value: In analyzing a sample of 11,434 firm-year observations spanning the 2001-2017 period that includes hand-collected product recall data, we find that suspected benchmark beating through real earnings management (SBBREM) engenders a higher likelihood and frequency of product recalls. In a set of cross-sectional results consistent with expectations, we find that the importance of SBBREM to product recalls rises when executives have stronger incentives to manage earnings upward, and falls for firms whose customers have greater power and firms with more growth opportunities. Other evidence implies that lowering product quality to meet-or-beat earnings targets leads to long-term negative consequences for the firm.

15504219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15504219.value: In this project, we explore whether firms have more product recalls if their managers try to manipulate firm real activities (i.e., R&D, advertising, production) to meet earnings targets set by financial analysts. We find that firms trying to manipulate real activities to meet analysts’ earnings targets indeed have a higher likelihood of announcing product recalls. The finding suggest that by meeting short-term earnings targets, firms may suffer from long-term value loss. Further, we document that the effect of exploiting real activities to meet analysts’ earnings targets on product recalls is stronger for firms whose managers have stronger incentives to manage earnings and is weaker for firms subject to greater customer power and firms with more growth opportunities. Additionally, we find that lowering product quality to meet-or-beat earnings expectations elevates investors’ skepticism about suspected firms’ earnings and undermines their future performance.

15504519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504519.value: At the point of sale, the most attention-grabbing element of a product is probably the visual aesthetics of its design, which plays a pivotal role in consumer decision-making. In this project we examine the psychological mechanism that drives consumers’ attitudes toward product color in aesthetic product design. Taking a novel perspective from contextually grounded consumer behavior, we propose that consumers have more favorable attitudes toward products with more saturated colors when they experience time scarcity. We posit that this proposed effect occurs because time scarcity drives consumers to develop a strong need for product efficacy, which results in more favorable attitudes toward products with high saturated colors which can symbolically provide a feeling of efficacy. The current research will contribute to the emerging literature on visual marketing, product design, resource scarcity, and product efficacy. It should also have significant implications for marketing practitioners, and help companies design their products in a strategic way. 在這項研究中，我們探索影響消費者產品顏色偏好的心理機制。本研究假設當消費者感覺到時間的稀缺性時，他們會對高顏色飽和度的產品產生好感。這是因為時間稀缺性促使消費者產生對於產品效用的強烈需求，而因為高飽和度的產品顏色象征高產品效用，消費者對高顏色飽和度的產品產生好感。本研究將對視覺營銷，產品設計，資源稀缺性，以及產品效用等研究領域帶來理論貢獻。同時，本研究的發現也會具有很強的實踐意義。

15504519.label: Realisation of objectives
15504519.value: The objectives of this project have been largely completed. Through a series of studies, we demonstrate that the perceived shortage of time leads consumers to prefer utilitarian products with highly saturated colors (rather than similar products with low-saturation colors), driven by consumers’ heightened need for personal efficacy under time scarcity. This effect is shown to be weakened or dismissed 1) when consumers have a high perception of self-efficacy, and 2) when consumers are in a satisficing mindset. The present research makes several contributions. First, it augments the existing literature on time scarcity by providing new insights about consumers’ visual preferences under high perceived time scarcity. Second, it adds to the extant literature on personal efficacy by demonstrating a novel factor that can trigger people’s need for efficacy: perceived time scarcity. Third, the current research complements the visual marketing literature by theorizing and demonstrating consumer inferences about products with different levels of color saturation. Managerially, the findings of this research suggest that companies may want to strategically design their product colors or arrange their product portfolios in different retail channels to maximize persuasiveness for consumers who purchase under different time perceptions.

15504519.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504519.value: A series of outcomes are yielded from this project. In the focal paper, we look at the psychological mechanism that drives consumers’ attitudes toward product color in aesthetic product design. We found that the perceived shortage of time led consumers to prefer utilitarian products with highly saturated colors (rather than similar products with low-saturation colors), driven by consumers’ heightened need for personal efficacy under time scarcity. A paper based on this project has been submitted to the Journal of Marketing (JM), but unfortunately got rejected. We are currently revising the working paper and plan to submit the revised manuscript to the Journal of Marketing Research (JMR) next. We also extended our research interest more broadly to consumers’ judgment and decision making processes. Three papers related to this broader focus were published on top-tier marketing journals. In one paper, we showed that consumers under life-role transition have more favorable attitudes towards distant (i.e., low- or moderate-fit) brand extensions compared to consumers who are not under life-role transition. The effect is driven by a sense of self-concept ambiguity associated with life-role transition, which subsequently prompts dialectical thinking that helps to improve perceived fit between a parent brand and its extension, and finally results in more favorable brand extension evaluation. This paper was published on the Journal of Marketing Research (JMR) in 2021. In another paper, we investigated the impact of brand logo colorfulness on consumer judgments toward a brand and its products. Through a series of experiments, we demonstrated that the colorfulness of a brand logo affects consumers' perception of the product variety offered by the brand. When consumers feel that a brand logo is colorful, they tend to infer that the brand offers a high variety of product options to its customers. Driven by the perception of product variety, logo colorfulness has downstream consequences on consumer attitudes, an effect that can be moderated by brand positioning. This paper was published on Psychology and Marketing in 2022. Finally, in a third paper, we investigated the effect of numerical customer identification (i.e., assigning numbers to identify customers) in the service context on the numbered customers’ reaction to service failures. We found that after being identified by a number, customers tend to exhibit a higher tolerance of service failures, and this effect is mediated by a sense of self-dehumanization among the numerically identified customers. This paper was also published on Psychology and Marketing in 2022.

15504519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15504519.value: As may be evident from the above section, this project is productive and there is great potential for further development of this research. My first priority is to push the remaining working paper through the review process and hopefully publish it in the following year. I also plan to further extend findings of some of these published papers and develop new research projects accordingly.

15504619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504619.value: 報紙，電視節目和網站上常常出現關於品牌和企業的社會責任活動的新聞報導。 例如，星巴克宣佈其承諾到2020年消除一次性塑膠吸管（www.starbucks.com）。思科為來自180多個國家的人提供IT教育以提高他們在數字經濟下的競爭力（www.cisco.com）。在閱讀這些新聞報導時，你會有什麼感覺？ 這個項目旨在研究觀察企業社會責任（CSR）活動如何影響消費者自己的親社會行為意圖，以及背後的原因。 過於的文獻只研究了影響企業進行社會責任活動的因素，以及企業的社會責任活動如果影響消費者對企業的態度和購買意願。這個項目有別於過於的研究，以一個新穎的角度來探討觀察企業的社會責任活動如何影響消費者自己的親社會行為（比如捐贈和參與志願活動）。 我們以前的研究和現有文獻表明，目睹一個美德行為（比如看到一個人為無家可歸者搭建避難所，Algoe＆Haidt2009; 或目睹一個機器人協助災難救援，Chen＆Huang，正在審查）會觸發一種他人導向性的情感—即，被感動和鼓舞的感覺。而這種正向的情感可以進而影響人們在一些不相關的領域做好事—比如為當地圖書館捐贈書籍以造福公民（Chen＆Huang，正在審查中）。在這個項目中，我們將進一步拓展過去的研究，看一看企業開展社會責任活動會如何影響消費者的親社會行為。這個問題非常值得研究，因為社會責任行為正在成為一個重要的、普遍的商業行為。 正如一開始給出的例子所講，實踐社會責任展示了公司對社會、社區、環境的關心和考慮。因此，不能想像，當消費者在新聞報導中讀到企業從事的社會責任活動時，他可能會感到鼓舞。然而，有趣的是，相反的情況也有可能發生。由於消費者的本能反應—企業的行為大多為利益驅使—消費者可能會懷疑公司從事社會責任行為的動機是為了改善社會福祉，還是簡單的讓自己獲利（比如增加銷售額、提高美譽度; Crilly, Ni & Jiang2015; Yoon,Gurhan-Canli, & Schwarz 2006）。如果消費者懷疑公司的誠意，那麼效果將適得其反—消費者不會被企業的社會責任行為感動或鼓舞，從而也不會去從事親社會行動。簡言之，這個專案旨在探究什麼情況下，目睹企業的社會責任行為能對消費者產生正面的影響，而什麼情況下，會產生負面的影響。在此基礎上進一步提出可操作的建議。 由於這項研究涉及到企業社會責任，消費者情感和親社會行為這些領域，我們將遵循我們在之前的研究中使用的範式（Chen＆Huang，正在審查中; Crilly，Ni，＆ Jiang2015）。 總體而言，這項研究將有助於我們瞭解宏觀層面的品牌行為如何影響微觀層面的消費者反應。 從實踐來講，我們的研究將有助於行銷人員瞭解應該如何披露企業的社會責任行為（一種有利可圖的商業慣例），以最大限度地提高其對消費者的積極影響。

15504819.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15504819.value: 信貸市場情緒與債務陷阱

15504819.label: Project Objectives
15504819.value: We plan to study what types of firms are more likely to be in the debt trap. We hypothesize that low-performing firms and high-levered firms are more sensitive to credit market sentiment, and that they are more likely to be in the debt trap. We plan to study whether the link of credit market sentiment to the debt trap plays roles in persistence in low performance and persistence in leverage. We plan to study whether debt-trapped firms are more likely to be acquired or delisted from the stock market. We posit that they are more likely to be acquired during high credit market sentiment (as acquirers can get capital at a lower cost) or delisted during low credit market sentiment (a tough environment for them to survive).

15504819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504819.value: 當信貸市場情緒高漲時，有充裕的資本可用，並壓低承擔信貸風險的預期回報。隨著資本成本的降低，資產價值也會增加。許多公司可能通過借貸和投資高風險專案來利用容易獲得資金的優勢，從而促進經濟增長。有趣的是，Lopez-Salido等人（2017年）顯示，t年信貸市場情緒高漲與t+2和t+3年經濟活動下降有關，而信貸利差在經濟活動收縮時擴大。其結果的基礎是信貸市場條件下存在可預測的平均回歸。因此，Lopez-Salido等人（2017年）認為，信貸市場的投資者情緒可能是商業週期的重要驅動力。 雖然公司可能會利用高信貸市場情緒，但可能導致一種稱為"債務陷阱"的現象。正如Fisher（1933年）指出的，債務陷阱的道路是容易賺錢、投機和新的投資機會。寬鬆的貨幣是過度借貸的一大原因，過度借貸會誘使成績不佳的借款人負債。原因是，隨著信貸週期和商業週期的重合，在好的時候過度借貸和投資（即高人氣和蓬勃發展的經濟）的公司可能會發現，隨著時間的推移，他們的商業環境會惡化，使得在未來償還債務變得困難，特別是在困難時期（即低信用感和經濟衰退）。為了在經濟衰退時期生存，一些公司可能被迫出售資產（"火銷售"）。隨著週期的好轉，當信貸市場狀況改善時，杠杆高的企業很可能再次借款，屆時也會有更多的投資機會。產生足夠現金流的公司可以擺脫債務陷阱。但是，對於成績不佳、杠杆高的公司來說，信貸週期和商業週期共同移動，可能會進一步推入債務陷阱。 為了表明信貸市場情緒與債務陷阱現象之間存在聯繫，並進一步瞭解企業陷入債務陷阱的原因和後果，本建議提出了我們的研究計畫。首先，我們計畫研究那些更有可能陷入債務陷阱的公司類型。我們假設，高信貸市場情緒會放鬆所有公司的借貸標準，即使對於信用風險高、經營業績低的公司來說，借貸也比平時更容易，最終導致債務陷阱。其次，我們旨在研究信貸市場情緒與債務陷阱的聯繫能否解釋一些公司的杠杆持續存在（La Lemmon等人，2008年）。第三，我們預測，這些負債累累的公司可能會從股市中除名，或者允許自己被收購。最重要的是，我們預測，在信貸市場情緒高漲時，他們更有可能被收購（因為收購者可以以較低的成本獲得資本）或信貸市場情緒低（生存環境艱難）時，他們更有可能從股市中除名。因此，我們的研究也將展示信貸市場情緒（債券市場現象）影響收購市場和從股票市場退市的管道。

15504819.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504819.value: Using the data in U.S. stock market, we measure a firm's credit sentiment beta which is the firm's price sensitivity to changes in the credit market sentiment, and classify individual firms into the sentiment-prone, insensitive and sentiment-counter groups. First, we find that sentiment-prone firms tend to be smaller, financially constrained, unprofitable and more volatile which is consistent with our “Hard-to-Value, Difficult-to-Finance” Hypothesis. Interestingly, while sentiment-counter firms have many similar firm characteristics with sentiment-prone firms, they have relatively low leverage, liquidity risk and tend to be value stocks. In addition, these firms are more likely belong to the industries whose products have rigid demand or largely depend on government spending. Second, our results show that while sentiment-prone firms’ financing and investment are affected by credit market sentiment, the sentiment has insignificant effects on the other two groups’ financing and investment. Furthermore, sentiment-prone investment leads to poor operating performance, and their delisting probability is higher. Finally, in terms of stock performance, we find that sentiment-counter firms outperform sentiment-prone firms.

15504819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15504819.value: We extend our inquiry to see whether and how credit market sentiment may affect competitive industries and consolidated industries differently. The inquiry allows us to link easy money to competitive industries’ booms and busts. Specifically, studies have documented that firms in competitive industries tend to invest inefficiently and suffer from booms and busts. We extend the literature by showing that high-sentiment signals from credit markets, an indication of easy money available, prompt firms in competitive industries to borrow and invest more than usual. The resulting excess investments collectively lead to overcapacity and, consequently, to declines in competing firms’ operating and financial performance. In contrast, we find that easy money does not lead to excess investments in consolidated industries. Our findings suggest that competitive industries’ booms and busts are largely driven by easy money from credit markets, and that (easy) financing contributes to their investment inefficiency problem.

15504819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15504819.value: In layman's term, our studies attempt to answer: What Do Firms’ Price Sensitivity to Credit Market Sentiment Tell Us About Them? As we mentioned above, we measure the credit sentiment beta which is firms’ sensitivity to the changes in the credit market sentiment and classify individual firms into the sentiment-prone, insensitive and sentiment-counter groups. First, we find that sentiment-prone firms tend to be smaller, financially constrained, unprofitable and more volatile which is consistent with our “Hard-to-Value, Difficult-to-Finance” Hypothesis. Interestingly, while sentiment-counter firms have many similar firm characteristics with sentiment-prone firms, they have relatively low leverage, liquidity risk and tend to be value stocks. In addition, these firms are more likely belong to the industries whose products have rigid demand or largely depend on government spending. Second, our results show that while sentiment-prone firms’ financing and investment are affected by credit market sentiment, the sentiment has insignificant effects on the other two groups’ financing and investment. Furthermore, sentiment-prone investment leads to poor operating performance, and their delisting probability is higher. Finally, in terms of stock performance, we find that sentiment-counter firms outperform sentiment-prone firms.

15504919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15504919.value: It is documented in the literature that the expected return on the aggregate equity market is downward sloping, i.e., the expected returns on the equity market are higher for shorter horizons than for longer horizons. The term structures of expected returns on individual stocks have not been examined in the literature. Do they have a similar pattern as the aggregate equity market? Are there cross-sectional variations among stocks? This project proposes to use data on individual stock options and stocks to examine the term structure of equity in the cross section of stocks based on a model-free approach. From options, we replicate claims to short-term dividends and estimate the expected returns for short horizons, and from stocks, we estimate the expected returns for long horizons. The understanding of the term structure of equity in the cross section helps to reconcile seemingly contradicting results in the asset pricing literature that growth stocks earn lower average returns than value stocks, but cash flows of growth stocks do not grow faster than those of value stocks. The model-free approach also helps to differentiate various specifications of asset pricing models which lead to inconsistent results regarding the term structure across stocks in the literature. 文獻顯示整體股票市場的預期回報是向下傾斜的，即股票市場的預期回報在較短期比較長期更高。個股預期回報的期限結構尚未在文獻中加以研究。它們是否與整體股票市場相似？股票之間是否存在橫截面中的變化？該研究將使用個股期權和股票的數據，根據無模型方法檢驗股票橫截面中股權的期限結構。我們將用期權複製短期股息並估算短期的預期回報，並從股票中估算長期的預期回報。對橫截面中股權的期限結構的理解有助於調和資產定價文獻中看似矛盾的結果，即增長型股票的平均收益率低於價值型股票但增長型股票現金流量的增長速度沒有超過價值型股票現金流量的增長速度。無模型方法還有助於區分文獻中導致股票期限結構不一致結果的各種資產定價模型。

15504919.label: Realisation of objectives
15504919.value: To achieve the first objective, we showed theoretically that when the term structure of a stock does not change within a short period of time, the entire term structure of the stock for that period can be estimated from returns on the dividend strips of various tenors and the return on the stock. We used stock options from the US market to synthetically construct dividend strips based on the put-call parity and calculated quarterly returns on the dividend strips. We used options with all maturities to estimate the term structure for each stock, with tenors of 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 quarters, and the long tenor of the term structure was estimated from stock returns. To minimize the errors in option prices for the estimation, we used the most at-the-money options which tend to be the most liquid and have the lowest bid-ask spreads. The whole term structures of all individual stocks with both short-term and long-term options traded were estimated. This indicates that the first objective is achieved. For the second objective, we examined the cross-sectional differences in the term structure of portfolios sorted by cash flow duration, book-to-market ratio, operating profitability, investment, and payout, because in the recent literature, the differences in cash flow duration across stocks have been applied to explaining the cross-sectional difference in stock returns associated with these variables. The results show that portfolios of stocks with a higher book-to-market ratio, operating profitability, payout yield, or lower cash flow duration, and asset growth as the measure of investment, earn higher average returns on their short-term dividend strips, and their term structure is more downward sloped. That stocks with these characteristics also earn higher average returns can be partially explained by the differences in the term structure across stocks. These results suggest that the value premium are jointly explained by the cross-sectional variations in cash flow durations and equity term structures, and thus the second objective is achieved. To achieve the third objective, we examined how the term structure varied across time. We first calculated the correlations between stock returns and returns on the short-term dividend strips at the stock level. The result shows that stock returns are positively correlated with returns on short-term dividend strips and the correlations increase with the tenors of the dividend strips. At the portfolio level, we examined the relation between the spreads of returns on portfolios of stocks sorted by the cash flow duration related variables with those of short-term dividend strips. The results indicate that when the spreads between returns on low and high duration stock portfolios increase, the spreads of returns on short-term dividend strips between these portfolios increase as well. The results further support the notion that the differences in returns between low and high duration stocks are due to the differences in the term structure of these stocks. We also examined how the level of and slope of the term structure varied with macroeconomic conditions. The results show that the level of term structure at the short (long) end is positively (negatively) related to the credit spread, measured by the difference between Moody’s seasoned Baa and Aaa corporate bond yields, or the difference between Aaa corporate bond yield and 3-month treasury bill rate. As a result, the slope of the term structure decreases with the credit spread and is pro-cyclical. These results indicate that the third objective is achieved.

15504919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15504919.value: Using a large cross section of stocks with options traded in the US market from January 1996 to June 2019, we find that the term structure of equity returns aggregated across stocks is downward sloped, consistent with the finding from derivatives on stocks indexes. We also find that the levels and slopes of the term structure vary substantially across individual stocks. While the majority of stocks have flat or download sloped term structures, quite a few stocks have significantly upward sloped term structures. We examine whether the term structure varies with cash flow duration in the cross section. We find that the time-series average returns on the dividend trips of the short duration portfolio are higher than those of the long duration portfolio, and the differences are larger for dividend strips with shorter tenors. The average slope of the term structure, defined as the difference in the average returns on the stock and on the 1-quarter dividend strip, is significantly downward sloped for the short duration portfolio, but is flat for the long duration portfolio. These results suggest that the term structure varies substantially in the cross section. The term structure of the short duration stocks is not only higher in level but also more downward sloped than that of the long duration stocks. We conduct a similar analysis for the portfolios sorted by the book-to-market ratio, profitability, investment and payout. The results show that portfolios of stocks with higher book-to-market ratio, operating profitability, payout yield, or lower asset growth, as a measure of investment, earn higher average returns on their short-term dividend strips, and the slopes of their term structures are more downward sloped. High average returns on stocks with these characteristics, as shown in the previous literature, can be partially explained by the differences in the term structure across stocks. The results can also help reconcile the seemingly inconsistent findings in the literature that growth stocks earn lower average returns than value stocks, but growth stocks do not have substantially higher future cash flow growth rates than value stocks. The cash flow duration alone is unlikely to fully explain the short cash flow duration or value premium because of non-trivial cross-sectional variations in the term structure across stocks with different cash flow durations or book-to-market ratios. A paper based on this project has been presented at 2022 Asian Finance Association Annual Conference and 2022 China International Conference in Finance.

15504919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15504919.value: The results from this project show that the term structure of equity returns varies substantially across stocks, which suggests that the cash flow duration alone is unlikely to fully explain the short cash flow duration or value premium. It may be interesting to quantify the extent to which each of the difference in the term structure of equity returns and cash flow duration explains short cash flow duration or value premium. In addition, while we document that the term structure varies cross-sectionally in a systematic pattern, a more fundamental question is what determines this cross-sectional variation. Further research may focus on the theoretical and empirical analysis of the determinants of the cross-sectional variation in the term structure.

15504919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15504919.value: The cash flow duration based explanation is proposed to explain high returns on stocks with short cash flow duration, high book-to-market-to-book ratio, profitability or payout, or low investment. For this explanation to fully account for the cross-sectional differences in stock returns associated with these variables, that the term structures of stock returns are the same as that of the aggregate market is implicitly assumed. This study estimates the term structure of stock returns in the cross section and examines whether the term structures across stocks are the same. We show theoretically that when the term structure of a stock does not change within a short period of time, the entire term structure of the stock for that period can be estimated from returns on the dividend strips of various tenors and the return on the stock. We use options to replicate short-term dividend strips of the underlying stocks, and estimate the short-end of the term structure by average returns on these dividend strips. We estimate the long end of the term structure from stock returns. We find that the term structure varies substantially in the cross section. The term structure of the short duration stocks, i.e., stocks with high book-to-market-to-book ratio, profitability or payout, or low investment, is not only higher in level but also more downward sloped than that of the long duration stocks. The results suggest that both the differences in the term structure of equity returns and cash flow duration explain short cash flow duration or value premium in the cross section of stock returns.

15505019.label: Project Objectives
15505019.value: To derive the OEM’s optimal order rationing decision and the suppliers’ corresponding wholesale pricing decisions in a one-period setting. To analyze how the remedy cost impacts the profitability of both the OEM and its suppliers. Particularly, we want to examine how the ex post quality gap and each supplier’s level of production quantity (under dual sourcing) affect the remedy cost and the performance of the OEM. We will also examine whether it is possible for the existence of remedy cost to benefit either of the suppliers. To examine the impact of uncertainty over remedy cost in a two-period setting. Specifically, we will investigate the OEM’s optimal order rationing decision for each period in situations where the OEM can only infer the remedy cost at the beginning of the first period but can actually observe that cost at the end of the first period. To analyze suppliers’ optimal levels of investment in quality in a two-period setting. To consider measures that an OEM can take to mitigate the impact of ex post quality heterogeneity.
