15505019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15505019.value: A potential consequence of dual sourcing, a strategy commonly adopted by original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), is ex-post quality heterogeneity among the final products, as the products come from different suppliers. For example, Apple sourced its iPhone 6s chip processors from two suppliers, Samsung and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), whose chip qualities actually differ from each other (Hein 2015). Customers tend to make social comparisons with their peers, and they often exhibit peer-induced fairness concerns. When ex-post quality heterogeneity exists, a customer may feel unfairly treated when she pays the same price but gets a lower-quality product than that received by a peer customer. In this situation, customer return/exchange may occur, which hurts the OEM. Suppliers can make investments to improve their product quality, but they cannot control the heterogeneity of ex-post quality relative to other suppliers. How do these issues interact and impact on OEMs’ performance? Our proposed research project will seek to investigate this question. Specifically, we aim to examine how ex-post product quality heterogeneity affects an OEM’s sourcing strategy and its suppliers’ quality investment decisions when customers exhibit peer-induced fairness concerns. First, we plan to consider a one-period setting wherein the OEM may incur a remedy cost for rectifying ex-post quality heterogeneity when adopting a dual sourcing strategy. We will determine the OEM’s optimal sourcing decisions and compare the equilibrium outcomes for cases where there is no ex-post quality heterogeneity with cases where such heterogeneity exists. The comparison will help us answer the following questions: How do ex-post quality heterogeneity and consumers’ peer-induced fairness concerns affect an OEM’s sourcing decisions? Can suppliers benefit from ex-post heterogeneity? Next, we will extend our analysis to a two-period setting that incorporates the uncertainty of remedy costs. In addition, suppliers can make efforts to improve their quality. We will re-examine the sourcing decisions of an OEM in each period along with its suppliers’ decisions regarding investments to improve quality. The results will help us identify the conditions under which dual sourcing is preferred by the OEM. Throughout this analysis, we will be able to answer the following questions: How does the uncertainty of remedy cost affect an OEM’s sourcing strategy? What is the optimal effort level for a supplier to exert? Finally, we plan to investigate the measures that OEMs can take to mitigate the impact of ex-post quality heterogeneity such as inspections before releasing the products to the end market. 原始设备制造商（OEM）通常采用的双源采购的潜在后果是最终产品的质量异质性，因为产品来自不同的供应商。顾客倾向于与其他顾客进行社会比较，并且经常表现出基于比较所产生的公平考虑。当产品存在质量异质性时，如果顾客支付相同的价格但获得的产品质量低于其他顾客所获得的产品，则可能会觉得受到不公平对待。在这种情况下，可能会发生客户退货/换货，从而伤害OEM。供应商虽然可以采取措施提高其自身的产品质量，但却无法控制其相对于其他供应商而言的质量异质性。我们将寻求调查这些问题如何相互作用并影响OEM的绩效。 我们的目标是研究当客户表现出基于社会同行比较的公平考虑，产品质量异质性如何影响OEM的采购战略及其供应商的质量投资决策。首先，我们计划考虑一个单期设置， OEM可能会产生补救成本来纠正采用双源策略产生的事后质量异质性。我们将研究OEM的最佳采购决策，并对没有事后质量异质性下的均衡结果与存在这种异质性下的结果进行比较。这种比较可以帮助我们回答以下问题：事后质量异质性和消费者社会比较所引发的公平性问题如何影响OEM的采购决策；供应商能否从事后异质性中获益。 接下来，我们将扩展到两期设置并考虑补救成本的不确定性。此外，供应商可以努力提高其产品质量。我们将重新审视OEM在每期的采购决策以及供应商相关的投资决策。有关结果将有助于我们确定OEM首选双源采购的条件 以及补救成本的不确定性如何影响OEM的采购战略和供应商的最佳努力水平。最后，我们计划研究OEM在将产品发布到终端市场之前可以采取哪些措施来减轻事后质量异质性的影响。

15505019.label: Realisation of objectives
15505019.value: We would like to point out that this project was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic period. The PI encountered the difficulty of hiring the research personnel and thus the grant was significantly underspent. The PI then trained her MPhil student to work on the problem. All the objectives have been achieved. This research project focuses on the impact of fairness concern and product quality heterogeneity on the firms’ operational and sourcing decisions. We aim to examine how quality heterogeneity and fairness concern affect the firms’ pricing, ordering and sourcing. We have considered a supply chain in which an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) sources from two suppliers with random yields and limited capacity and sells the end products to consumers who are fairness concerned and averse to disadvantageous inequality. The suppliers are ex ante identical but maybe ex post heterogeneous in their realized quality levels. When the product is released to the market, a third party tests and discloses the realized quality from different suppliers to consumers. Consumers know the quality distribution of the product before purchase, but they learn the quality of their own unit only after purchase. We find that a higher degree of consumer aversion to disadvantageous inequality reduces the OEM's incentive to dual source because of the ex post heterogeneity in quality that may arise, with resulting consumer complaints. When suppliers have sufficient capacity, this reduced incentive intensifies competition between suppliers, pressurizing the suppliers to quote lower wholesale prices. This enhances the OEM's market power against suppliers, and thus, an increase in the degree of consumer inequality aversion hurts the suppliers but benefits the OEM. Unexpectedly, consumer inequality aversion may not necessarily benefit the consumers themselves. When the degree of consumer inequality aversion is low, an increase in the degree of such aversion turns out to make consumers worse off. However, when the degree of consumer inequality aversion is sufficiently high, it impels the OEM to switch from dual sourcing to single sourcing. In this situation, the potential inequality between consumers is eliminated, thereby benefiting inequality-averse consumers and improving consumer surplus. Our analysis reveals that suppliers' capacity constraints can soften competition between suppliers and alter the interplay between consumer inequality aversion and other factors Specifically, in cases where suppliers operate at intermediate capacity levels, the OEM cannot adopt single sourcing to eliminate ex post quality heterogeneity because of the limited capacity. Meanwhile, the OEM cannot transfer the pressure arising from consumers' concerns about inequality to the suppliers fully because of the softened supplier competition induced by the limited capacity. Consequently, the OEM must bear a portion of the adverse effects stemming from consumers' concerns about inequality. Therefore, consumer inequality aversion can potentially hurt the OEM. Our analysis implies that the existence of good-will loss or the remedy cost and the increase in the ex post quality gap will make the single sourcing more likely to be adopted by the OEM, hurting the upstream suppliers. An improvement in the supplier’s quality reliability will make dual sourcing more likely and enhance the suppliers’ pricing power. It is worth pointing out that we are the first to characterize the equilibrium of supplier competition fully under limited capacity, random yields, and consumer inequality aversion. We show that the suppliers' capacity levels substantially affect the equilibrium outcomes. In particular, no pure strategy Nash equilibrium exists in the pricing game between the two suppliers when their capacities fall within a moderate range. Despite the nonexistence of a pure strategy Nash equilibrium, we can characterize a mixed strategy Nash equilibrium for this moderate capacity range. Further, we find that a higher degree of consumer inequality aversion can expand the range of suppliers' capacity in which only a mixed strategy equilibrium is sustainable, as the consumer inequality aversion intensifies supplier competition. Note that business entities also exhibit fairness concerns. Nowadays, when outsourcing, many buyers are also responsible for engaging in supplier ESG due diligence. When buyers source from the same supplier, a buyer’s ESG due diligence effort may spill over to the competing rival, which may induce the fairness concern. Specifically, we consider a supply chain consisting of two suppliers and two competing buyers with different responsibility awareness (one referred to as a strong buyer and the other a weak buyer). The two buyers can either source from their respective dedicated suppliers and manage supplier ESG practices independently, or source from a common supplier and conduct supplier ESG due diligence collaboratively. Nevertheless, such cooperation gives the weak buyer an opportunity to free ride on the strong buyer’s ESG effort (i.e., ESG effort spillover). Our analysis reveals that a fair-neutral strong buyer is inclined to collaboratively conduct supplier ESG due diligence if and only if the spillover effect is not strong. Surprisingly, we find that the fairness-concerned strong buyer may also have the incentive to partner with the rival in conducting ESG due diligence even if the threat of ESG due diligence effort spillover is great. This occurs when the cost of conducting ESG due diligence is low enough. Moreover, we show that a win-win outcome can arise. However, the impact of fairness concerns on the propensity of realizing a win-win outcome is not monotone. Our analysis reveals that fairness concerns may promote cooperation between the downstream buyers in managing supplier ESG practices. We then further study ways to help consumers better infer the firms’ quality level when making their purchase/joining decisions. First, we propose that firms can signal their quality level by either revealing or withholding their queue length information (i.e., the number of customers in the system). We show that when the high-quality and low-quality firms adopt the different disclosure strategies, customers can fully infer the quality information and thus behave in an informed way. We also show that such quality information signalling can help increase the customers’ total utility. Second, we show that a firm with uncertain quality level can use Bayesian persuasion to persuade more customers to join the system. Based on the findings in this research project, we have completed five academic papers which are listed as follows: Y Tang, X Wang, Y Wang, Sourcing Strategies in the Presence of Social Comparisons, Random Yields and Supplier Competition with Limited Capacity. Under review, Operations Research. Y. Cao, Q. Li, B. Shen and Y. Wang. Buyer Collaboration in Managing Supplier Responsibility with ESG Due Diligence Effort Spillover and Fairness Concerns. 15505019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15505019.value: The PI has trained one MPhil student. The research results have been presented at five conferences and several universities, and a Best Paper Award has been obtained. Our main findings are as follows: When the final products might differ in quality and consumers exhibit inequality aversion, we show that this reduces the OEM's incentive to dual source and intensifies competition between suppliers, thereby hurting suppliers but benefiting the OEM. Consumers, however, can be either hurt or benefited by their inequality aversion. We further show that when the suppliers have insufficient capacity, their limited capacity levels can alter the role of consumer inequality aversion. In this situation, we show consumer inequality aversion can potentially hurt the OEM and a higher degree of consumer inequality aversion can expand the range of suppliers' capacity in which only a mixed strategy equilibrium is sustainable. Related results are now under review with Operations Research; See Part C (8) Item 1. In outsourcing, when buyers engage in supplier ESG due diligence, their due diligence effort may spill over to the competitors and induce fairness concerns. We find that only a significantly low spillover effect can induce a fair-neutral strong buyer to adopt buyer collaboration. Interestingly, with the consideration of fairness concerns, the competitor can be treated as a friend in collaboratively managing the ESG practices of the common supplier. We show that fairness concerns have a non-monotone impact on the possibility of realizing a win–win outcome between the buyers. Related results are published on Transportation Research Part E; See Part C (8) Item 2. During the literature review process, we identified some interesting research along the line of incorporating players’ behavioral biases into firms’ operational decisions. We then co-organized a focused issue and wrote an editorial review about behavioral pricing on Decision Sciences; See Part C (8) Item 3. When firms’ quality level is uncertain, we show that the firm knowing its own quality level can signal this quality information to customers by revealing or concealing the number of customers in its system (i.e., the queue length). Related results are published on Manufacturing & Service Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 4. We further show that the firm can ex ante commit to an information disclosure strategy to persuade consumers to join its system. Related results are published on Production and Operations Management; See Part C (8) Item 5.

15505019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15505019.value: There are some related research topics that are worth exploring. For example, we notice that there are many online customer reviews regarding the quality of the products they have received and the responses from the sellers. It is worthwhile to collect such data and examine how they affect consumers’ purchase intentions and how sellers respond towards such quality reviews. Note that such online reviews convey the information regarding the final product’s quality distribution. We can then adopt the data-driven approach to estimate the quality distribution for the sellers’ final products, based on which we can further investigate the sellers’ strategies by data-mining their responses.

15505019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15505019.value: We show that when there exist quality differences between final products that use components from different suppliers, buyers may need to switch from dual sourcing to single sourcing when facing fairness-concerned consumers. Consumers’ inequality aversion intensifies the pricing competition between the suppliers, thereby hurting the suppliers but benefiting the buyers in most cases. Consumer inequality aversion, however, may not improve consumer surplus. A reduction in ex post quality gap will make dual sourcing more likely. When buyers engage in supplier ESG due diligence, their due diligence efforts may spill over to the competing buyers. We show that a fairness-concerned strong buyer who has a higher responsibility awareness may have the incentive to partner with the rival in conducting ESG due diligence even if the threat of ESG due diligence effort spillover is great. That is, fairness concerns may promote cooperation between the downstream buyers in managing supplier ESG practices. We further show that when firms’ quality levels are uncertain, firms can inform customers of their quality level through disclosing or withholding the information about the number of customers in the system or committing to a quality disclosure strategy to persuade customers to join the system.

15505519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15505519.value: Being proactive can impact how well employees, leaders, and teams perform and succeed in their work. So, it is important to understand the different types of proactive behaviors, how they can be combined to affect people, and also the factors that enable or hinder these behaviors. In the first study (JOB), we looked at how feeling insecure about their jobs (affective job insecurity) affects teams. We found that when most team members feel job insecurity, it creates power struggles within the team that makes it harder for them to perform well or be proactive. In the second study (JLOS), we examined how humble leaders can proactively manage teams to achieve career success. We found that humble leaders can increase subordinate voice, and these voices help humble leaders to achieve higher performance and receive reward recommendations from their superiors. In the third study (AOM), we studied how working mothers can proactively combine different lunchbreak activities to recharge energy and perform better. We found that working mothers can combine four types of lunchbreak activities (eating, socializing, relaxing, and working) differently, and these different combinations have different effects. Spending lunchbreaks mostly for socializing or multitasking are found to e most helpful for working mothers, while working through lunch withing taking a break was the most energy draining. In the fourth study (working paper), we have identified four distinct profiles of voice behaviors: high voicers, promotive voicers, prohibitive voicers, and low voicers. We fond that these different voice profiles have different relationships with job satisfaction, job performance, social integration, creativity, and how much leaders like the individuals. In summary, these studies show that being proactive can greatly impact well-being, performance, and success in the workplace.

We test the usual candidates (e.g. arctangent) and making use of the piecewise time re-scaling technique of Control Parametrization Enhancing technique to match the end points of the line integral. 15506719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15506719.value: Recent studies on behavioral finance have started to focus on investors’ beliefs to shed light on our understanding of asset prices. For example, Greenwood and Shleifer (2014) find that, consistent with extrapolative beliefs, the expectations of returns are highly and positively associated with cumulative past stock returns and the level of the stock market, but negatively with future realized returns. Barberis et al. (2015, 2018) further show that return extrapolation has the asset pricing effect on return predictability. Coibon and Gorodnichenko (2012, 2015) find that consistent sticky beliefs, professional forecasters fail to completely adjust on their expectations, leading to significant deviations from the null of full information. Moreover, Bouchaud et al. (2018) show analytically and provide strong evidence that their sticky belief model can explain the profitability anomaly as well as the price and earnings momentums. In this proposal, we propose a present-value framework that incorporates the extrapolative beliefs and sticky beliefs into the dynamics of asset prices. In the model, there are three types of investors: extrapolators, anchoring traders, and rational traders. Our framework inherits the latent variable approach within the present-value model of van Binsbergen and Koijen (2010). The novelty of our investigation is to extract the various investor beliefs and estimate the expected returns from the market prices simultaneously. Using the predictive regression framework, we test the model implications that the filtered extrapolative (anchoring) beliefs should negatively (positive) predict the future returns. Moreover, the extrapolation effect should be stronger when the anchoring effect is weaker and vice versa. Our model predicts that the extrapolator component would capture the survey expectation of returns from retail investors and the rational investor component from sophisticated investors, such as hedge funds. Meanwhile, the anchoring component would capture the frequency of forecast revisions due to the sticky beliefs. We further test our model in the cross section using a wide range of different asset classes as well as international equity markets. Our unified framework will contribute to our understanding of how investor beliefs affect the cross-country difference in value, momentum, and profitability effects (Chui, Titman, and Wei, 2010; Titman, Wei, and Xie, 2013; Chen, Sun, Wei, and Xie, 2018). The results of the project should be useful and important for retail investors and professional managers in Hong Kong and around the world. 當代行為財務學的研究關注於投資者的信念而進一步了解資產價格。例如，Greenwood和Shleifer（2014）發現，與外推的信念一致，期望的報酬率與累積的過去股票收益率以及股票水平高度正相關，但卻與未來實現的報酬率負相關。 Barberis等人(2015，2018）進一步證實外推信念具有資產定價可預測性的影響。 Coibon和Gorodnichenko（2012，2015）證實粘性信念，研究發現專業預測人員未能完全調整他們的期望，因此導致完整信息的重大偏差。此外，Bouchaud等人 （2018）分析並證實粘性信念模型可以解釋盈利以及報酬率和動能效應。 在這個提案中，我們提出了一個現值模型的框架，其中包含了 對資產價格動態的推測信念和粘性信念。在模型中，有三種類型的投資者：外推信念者，錨定交易者和理性交易者。我們的框架繼承了現值模型中的潛變量方法van Binsbergen和Koijen（2010）。本研究創新之處在於可以同時衡量各種投資者信念並估算市場價格的預期回報。使用預測回歸模型框架，實證模型所衡量出的外推（錨定）信念應該負面（正面）預測未來報酬率。當外推效應較弱的時候，錨定效應應該更強，而且反之亦然。實證模型所衡量出的外推信念應該來自散戶投資者的信念，理性投資者應該來自熟鍊的投資者，如對沖基金。同時，實證模型所衡量出錨定信念粘性則能反映分析師修訂預測的頻率。我們將進一步在橫斷面中使用各種不同的資產測試我們的模型課程以及國際股票市場。我們的統一框架將有助於我們對投資者信念如何影響跨國的資產定價差異，例如價值溢價，動能效應，和盈利效應（Chui，Titman和Wei，2010; Titman，Wei和Xie，2013; Chen，Sun，Wei和Xie，2018）。研究結果對於香港及全球的散戶投資者和專業投資經理人都有重要的含意。

15506719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15506719.value: There are four research outputs derived from the project: [1] Cassella, Stefano, Te-Feng Chen, Huseyin Gulen, and Yan Liu, Extracting Extrapolative Beliefs from Market Prices: An Augmented Present-Value Approach. Working Paper, 4th Revise & Resubmit at Journal of Financial Economics. We propose a latent-variables approach to recover extrapolative beliefs from asset prices. We estimate a present-value model of the price-dividend ratio of the market that embeds both return extrapolation and cash-flow extrapolation, alongside discount rates and rational expectations of dividend growth. We show that extrapolative beliefs extracted from prices are highly correlated with surveys, and that survey-based and price-based extrapolative beliefs share similar predictive properties for future returns, with the former improving upon the latter. [2] Chen, Te-Feng, Yan Liu, and K.C. John Wei. Anchoring, Extrapolation, and Return Predictability. Working Paper. We propose a present-value framework to recover anchoring and extrapolative beliefs from asset prices. Using the partial least square method (PLS) to infer the conditional dividend growth rates, we transform the latent-variables model into a nonlinear predictive regression model. We show that anchoring and extrapolative beliefs extracted from prices significantly predict market returns both in- and out-of sample. The significance of return predictability is held in several different sets of portfolio returns as well as in the cross-section of stock returns. [3] Chen, Te-Feng, Ye Gong, and K.C. John Wei. Instrumented Expected Profitability Premium. 30th PBFEAM (best paper award), Working Paper, CICF 2022. We use instrumented principal component analysis (IPCA) to estimate expected profitability from a conditional latent-factor model that depends on observable firm characteristics. An IPCA composite predictor aggregated from various expected profitability measures can effectively capture the expected profitability premium. [4] Chen, Te-Feng, Yusong Chen, Yao Tong, and Ruochen Yin. Profitability Shocks and the Pricing of Subjective Expectations: U.S. and Global Evidence around the COVID-19. Working Paper, AsianFA 2023. We investigate the evolution of the comovement between survey cashflow forecasts and stock prices around the COVID-19 profitability shocks. We find an increased comovement following the pandemic and a decreased comovement back-to-normal in the next following year. This relation is more pronounced among stocks with downward forecast revisions, which are more informative about current variations in stock prices and are associated with a reduced degree of price delay, compared with those with upward forecast revisions, which exhibit greater expectation stickiness. We find evidence in global markets, with stronger effects in developed markets.

15507719.value: 根據1975年《證券法修正案》（關於1934年制定的《證券交易法》）13（f）部分規定，強制要求管理規模超過一億美元（投資於13（f）所列出的證券）的基金經理需在表格13F中向證監會披露其季度持倉組合。該強制披露法案的目的是幫助投資者和政府監管部門建立一個集中記錄保管基金經理投資活動的資料庫。然而近年來研究卻發現了關於該強制披露法案所產生的意外結果，如羊群效應（如Brown and Schwarz 2013）, 強制披露基金持倉組合後基金業績下滑（Shi 2017），以及在13F表格中有選擇地披露在季度內的策略性交易（如Wang 2013）。本項目將從不同的角度出發，評估13(f)規則是否達到其預期效果。具體來說，因為大部分基金持倉組合是相對不透明的，我們將研究13F表格披露規則能否是投資者更好地評估和選擇基金。與其他關於明智的投資文獻（Gruber 1996; Zheng 1999; Sapp and Tiwari 2004）類似，我們首先檢驗相對於未披露持倉資訊基金，投資者買賣披露持倉資訊基金決策是否更加精准預測基金未來業績，即明智的投資效應是否更加顯著。同時我們將使用EDGAR資料來證明基金資金流動更能預測其未來業績不僅僅在於13F表格披露，更在於投資者對13F表格的真實關注。最後，我們計劃通過分析部分投資者（本項目中特指註冊投資於其他基金的基金（FOFs）,其也是整個基金市場的組成部分）的基金持有組合，來補充基金層面資金流動的相關研究。通過提供全面的經驗證據來表明，在難以監督基金經理行為的情況下，基金持倉組合披露使得投資者選擇基金經理更加明智，我們旨在突出基金持倉組合強制披露的積極方面，也為政策制定者提供關於13F表格披露政策效果的更加全面評價。

rows: We aim to assess whether the 13(f) rule serves its intended purposes. In particular, we ask whether the Form 13F requirement enables investors to better evaluate and select hedge funds.

15507719.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507719.value: We begin our empirical analysis with a simple portfolio sorting, where we sort hedge funds based on quarterly fund flows, but separately for 13F filers and non-filers. We find that funds in the highest flow quartile exhibit superior returns relative to funds in the lowest flow quartile, but only among 13F filers. Among non-filers, the highest-flow quartile insignificantly underperform the lowest-flow quartile. The return spread between the highest- and lowest-flow quartiles is larger among 13F filers than among non-filers by 3.50% per annum, and the difference remains significant after controlling for the Fung and Hsieh (2001) seven factors, as well as the momentum factor. To better identify the impact of 13F disclosure on investors’ fund selection ability, we take advantage of our staggered panel data structure to estimate a difference-in-differences (DiD) (as opposed to a difference) in the smart money effect. The regression results show that the sensitivity of fund performance to past fund flows increases significantly after a fund starts filing Form 13F. We find that the results are mainly driven by cases where: (1) the information about a fund’s portfolio holdings is more precise, e.g., when the fund is the only fund in the family or when the fund is the largest one in the family; (2) the information is viewed more, as measured by the number of downloads or the number of unique IP addresses making these downloads; and (3) investors have more opportunity to use the information, i.e., when the fund imposes less restrictions on redemptions and/or subscriptions. Furthermore, we estimate a placebo specification using only funds of hedge funds (FoFs), which do not hold 13(f) securities, and find no evidence that the smart money effect changes after the fund’s parent firm starts filing Form 13F. We supplement our analysis by utilizing hedge fund holdings data available for a subset of hedge fund investors, namely, registered FoFs. For each registered FoF in each quarter, we identify 13F-filing versus non-filing hedge funds that are held by the FoF and compare their returns over the subsequent quarter. We find that the average FoF earns 1.52%–1.59% per quarter from 13F filers and 1.17%–1.35% per quarter from non-filers. The difference, 0.23%–0.35% per quarter, is statistically significant after correcting for time-series and cross-sectional dependence in the data.

15507719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507719.value: We provide causal evidence that mandatory portfolio disclosure helps investors evaluate and select hedge fund managers. Using a staggered difference-in-differences analysis, we demonstrate that investor capital flows better predict fund performance among funds that publicly disclose their portfolio holdings. Additional cross-sectional analyses suggest that this gain in selection ability varies with the informational value of disclosure. Furthermore, examining investor-level allocations, we find that institutional investors earn higher returns on their allocations to disclosing funds. Overall, these results help contribute to the cost-benefit analysis of mandatory portfolio disclosure.

15507819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507819.value: Lead activists often team up with other activists or pro-activist investors in their activism campaigns (i.e. wolf pack activism). This activism practice has attracted attention from both academia and industry practitioners since it magnifies each investor’s influence over firm management. Following proxy contests launched by institutional activists to improve firms’ corporate governance, financial analysts should issue recommendations that are consistent with the proxy contests, because financial analysts are viewed as external monitors in contributing to wolf pack activism. However, we know little about whether financial analysts perform their external governance role in this process. This study will investigate whether sell-side financial analysts’ recommendations, after proxy contests launched by institutional activists against target firms, help to improve corporate governance through their influence on mutual fund voting. We focus on the effect of analysts’ recommendations on voting by mutual funds because they are a major class of investors in the target firms. Contrary to their monitoring motives for supporting proxy contests, financial analysts may be biased toward firms due to their existing business connections with the firms (e.g. the firms are held by major clients of the analysts’ employers) or their intention to get investment banking business from the firms by providing positive recommendations, leaving the net effect of analysts on governance unclear. We will first study whether analysts on average are acting effectively to improve corporate governance by examining the net effect of the above two opposite incentives for analysts’ recommendations. We will then study how cross-sectional variations in analysts’ brokerage business relationships with investors and investment banking relationships with firms influence analysts’ recommendations. After we document whether the recommendations are consistent with the proxy contests, we will then evaluate whether such recommendations affect mutual fund voting in supporting the proxy contests. As the success in institutional activism relies on the support by other investors, this investigation can suggest that financial analysts serve as external monitors through their help with institutional activists’ proxy fight. To show the monitoring effectiveness, we will also document whether analysts’ recommendations influence final outcomes of proxy contests. In addition, we will investigate the potential payoff to financial analysts who support institutional activists. This research will shed light on the effect of financial analysts on shareholder activism and enrich our understanding about wolf pack activism. This proposal will also contribute to mutual fund literature by studying how financial analysts influence their voting decisions. 领头的股东积极分子经常联合其他积极分子或积极主义投资者一起发起激进运动（即狼群活动）。这种股东激进实践吸引了学术界和行业从业者的关注，因为它扩大了每个投资者对公司管理的影响力。在机构活动家发起代理竞赛以改善公司的公司治理之后，金融分析师应该发布与代理竞争相一致的建议从而为狼群活动做出贡献。这个推论是因为金融分析师通常被视为外部监督者。但是，我们对财务分析师是否在此过程中履行其外部治理角色知之甚少。 本研究将调查在机构活动家针对目标公司发起的代理竞赛后，卖方金融分析师是否通过其对共同基金投票的影响来帮助改善公司治理。我们关注分析师对共同基金投票的建议的影响，因为他们是目标公司的主要投资者。与支持代理竞争的监督动机相反，金融分析师可能会因为与公司的现有业务关系（例如公司由分析师的主要客户持有）或者他们打算从中获得投资银行业务而偏向于公司，即发布对目标公司有利的建议。综上两种不同的推断，分析师对治理的净影响不明确。 我们将首先通过检查上述两种相反激励对分析师建议的净效应来研究分析师是否有效地改善公司治理。然后，我们将研究分析师与投资者的经纪业务关系以及与公司的投资银行关系的横截面变化如何影响分析师的建议。在我们分析了分析师的建议是否与代理竞赛相一致之后，我们将评估此类建议是否会影响共同基金投票以支持代理竞赛。由于机构行动主义的成功依赖于其他投资者的支持，这项调查可以表明，金融分析师是否通过他们对机构活动家代理权争夺的帮助来充当外部监督者。为了验证这类监控的有效性，我们还将研究分析师的建议是否会影响代理竞赛的最终结果。此外，我们将研究那些支持机构活动家的金融分析师最终会获取什么样的潜在回报。

15507819.label: Realisation of objectives
15507819.value: We empirically analyze the first three objectives, and revise the four objective due to the difficulty to obtain data. In particular, our findings of the first three objectives are: 1. "How do financial analysts respond to proxy contests?" Our findings: analysts’ stock recommendations in the month immediately prior to the annual meeting (at which shareholder voting on contested proxy proposals take place) are more pessimistic than recommendations issued in other periods, implying that analysts on average are dissatisfied with the target firm. 2. "Do financial analysts who have business relationships with institutional activists (investment banking relationships with firms) make recommendations supporting activists’ (firms’) interest around proxy contests?" Our findings: analysts issue more favorable stock recommendations when they have connection with the target firm. We focus the connection established through past underwriting service. In particular, we find that analysts affiliated with a connected brokerage house (i.e., brokerage house that has provided underwriting service to the target firms) issue more favorable stock recommendations than other analysts. 3."Do recommendations by financial analysts affect voting by mutual fund investors and final voting outcomes?" Our findings: more negative analyst recommendations are associated with a higher level of voting support by mutual fund families for activist investors. 4. "Do analysts who support institutional activists generate more commissions from these activists in the future?" Our findings: we revised this objective due to lack of data, and change it to another objective that is closer to the previous objectives. In particular, we analyze the cross-sectional variations in the third objective. We find that that the negative impact of analyst recommendations on mutual fund families’ voting support for activist is more pronounced for targeted firms when the fund family has a large ownership in the firm, firms with poorer performance (i.e., lower ROA), or weaker governance (i.e., duality of CEO and chairman role).

15507819.value: We study financial analysts’ recommendation when firms receive contentious shareholder-sponsored proposals on governance-related issues. We find that analysts’ stock recommendations in the month immediately prior to the annual meeting (at which shareholder voting on contested proxy proposals take place) are more pessimistic than recommendations issued in other periods, implying that analysts on average are dissatisfied with the target firm. However, we find that analysts issue more favorable stock recommendations when they are affiliated with a brokerage firm that has provided underwriting service to the target firms. We find that more negative analyst recommendations are associated with a higher level of voting support by mutual fund families for activist investors. 15507919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15507919.value: In a repeat-purchase market where consumers interact with a retailer season after season, consumers may learn from the retailer's past prices and form their own expectations about the future product price, known as reference price. The difference between the reference price and the actual price is perceived as a gain or loss by consumers which affects consumers' purchasing decisions. The presence of consumer reference-price effects alters a firm's focus from collecting immediate gains to maintaining high consumer expectation (and hence high profit) in the long run. Ignoring the impact of reference effects in a retailer's decision process could lead to substantial losses. A great deal of work has been conducted to study optimal pricing strategies with reference effects under the assumption that the market information is known a priori. However, such assumption is often invalid, and more practical data-driven pricing algorithms have attracted increasing research interest in recent years. The goal of this project is to study the dynamic pricing problem of a retailer when market information (such as demand function and consumers' references) is unknown. The retailer's objective is to maximize its expected profit by dynamically adjusting prices over a finite planning horizon. Because the market information required for decision making is unknown a priori, the retailer must learn such information from real data observed over time, resulting in the well-known exploration-exploitation dilemma (i.e., information learning versus profit maximization) in its decision process. If a firm spends more time in learning the information, it then has less time to maximize profit. Conversely, if a firm spends less time on learning, it is more likely to make a sub-optimal decision in the exploitation phase. By adopting existing data-driven optimization techniques and developing new methodologies, our algorithm could properly balance the exploration-exploitation trade-off and achieve asymptotic optimal performance in the long run. In short, data-driven algorithms will be developed in this study to help a retailer to identify the impact of reference effects, estimate the demand information effectively and efficiently, and make online pricing decisions as more data are revealed. By incorporating consumer behavioral features in our model and developing new methodologies for learning reference dependent demand functions using real data, the outcomes of this project should significantly contribute to the demand learning literature. From a practical perspective, our project would provide practical data-driven pricing algorithms for firms to better understand consumers' purchasing behavior and improve their profitability in the long run. 在週期性購買市場中消費者會在每個季度都到訪商店並得知當期商品價格。他們由此而可能從商品的歷史價格中學習到商家的定價策略，從而形成關於商品未來價格的預期。我們稱由此形成的價格預期爲參考價格。當實際價格低於或高於參考價格之時，其間的差值會被消費者們感知為交易的額外收益或損失，他們的購買行爲從而受影響。故當消費者參考價格效應存在時，商家決策的關注點應從獲取短期收益轉向長期維持消費者較高的價格期望（從而達至高利潤）。若商家在決策過程中忽視參考效應的影響，其有可能會受到重大利潤損失。雖然學界中已有大量研究工作探索參考效應下的最優定價策略，此類工作大多皆基於市場信息已知之假設。然而此假設通常並不成立。故更具實用性的基於數據的定價策略在近年來吸引了越來越多研究目光。 此項目之目標為研究商家在市場信息未知時的動態定價問題。在我們的研究設定中，此類未知信息包括需求函數及消費者參考效應等信息。商家須通過動態調整價格來實現最大化其於一定有限時期之期望利潤的目標。因決策所需之市場信息未能事先獲知，商家必須從實際觀察到的銷售數據中學習相關信息。由此而導致了廣爲人知的探索（信息學習）與開發（利潤最大化）之間的衝突：若商家花費較多時間在學習信息上，留給其優化利潤的時間就越少；相反地，若商家花費較少的時間去學習信息，其又會有更大的可能於開發階段作出非最優決策。在此項目中，我們將博采現有的數據驅動優化技術以及開發若干新方法，設計出能恰當地平衡探索與開發之間權衡、並在長遠規劃中達到漸近最優表現的算法。此基於數據的算法將能幫助商家在逐漸收集數據的過程中鑒別參考效應大小、有效快速地估算市場需求信息、並作出在綫定價決策。 因為本研究所涉及之模型融入了消費者行爲的要素及將會開發出新的適用於參考效應需求函數的數據學習方法，其成果會極有助於完善現有的需求學習文獻。從實踐的角度出發，此項目會為商家提供實用性的數據驅動定價算法，以使它們能更好地瞭解消費者購買行爲，從而提高長遠利潤。 關鍵詞：數據驅動的決策，動態定價，參考效應，需求函數學習，探索-開發權衡

15507919.label: Realisation of objectives
15507919.value: Because the project timeline largely overlapped with the 2019 political unrest, during which the campus was occupied by protesters, and then the pandemic, which hindered in-person exchange activities and research personnel hiring due to travel and immigration restrictions, the budget was underutilized, prompting a mid-term revision of our project objectives. Despite these challenges, we successfully achieved all the originally proposed research objectives by the project's conclusion. The following provides a detailed account. In this project, we study the dynamic pricing problem faced by a retailer serving customers with reference-price effects when demand information-such as the demand function, the reference price, the extent of reference effects, and customers' learning speed-is unknown. The firm aims to maximize expected profit by adjusting the prices over a finite planning horizon. Because the demand information required for decision making is unknown a priori, the firm must learn it from retail data collected over time, which introduces a tension between exploration (information learning) and exploitation (profit maximization) into the decision process. To address this issue, we first build a general demand model incorporating reference-price effects, characterized by (i) demand being influenced not only by the current price but also by a reference price shaped by the retailer's historical pricing, (ii) the perceived gain or loss based on the difference between the reference and actual prices affecting demand positively or negatively, (iii) consumers updating their reference price over time based on the latest price and the old reference. We assume that the demand information required for decision making is unknown a priori and the reference price is unobservable, and hence the firm must learn it from real data collected during operation. Aiming to enhance the model's applicability in real-world settings, we don't presuppose specific functional forms for demand and reference-update functions. Initially, we discovered that without accounting for reference effects, using generic online optimization algorithms could lead to suboptimal pricing and significant losses if the reference effects are present (Objective 1). This underscores the necessity of our research. The difficulty of the problem compared with demand learning problems without reference effects is that the unknown demand varies with an unobservable system state (i.e., the reference). To tackle this, we analyze the evolution of the reference under a general update mechanism and examine the property of the optimal prices curve. We show that the reference converges exponentially fast if the present price has consistent non-negligible impact on the reference update and the firm repeatedly charges a fixed price. This finding enables us to estimate the unknown reference price with high accuracy and manage learning errors effectively by fixing a price for an extended period. Building on these insights, we devise a cycle-update pricing (CUP) policy to learn the unobservable reference and unknown demand function, and to identify the optimal pricing strategy (Objective 2). This policy involves dividing the planning horizon into cycles, each consisting of two phases, to manipulate the reference price and gather sales data reflecting base demand. At the beginning of each phase, the firm manipulates the unknown reference to a desired level by repeatedly charging an identical price for some periods. Once the reference approaches the neighborhood of the price, the reference-dependent component in demand diminishes and the sales data afterward in this phase mostly reflect the base demand. At the end of a cycle, a direction of improvement can be identified based on the subgradient estimated by the effective sales data. By employing a nonsummable diminishing step size of adjustment, we ensure a balance between exploration (requiring a large enough nonsummable step size) and exploitation (requiring a diminishingly small step size), leading to the convergence of the prescribed price to the optimal level with high probability. We also conduct performance analysis of our policy and evaluate its regret, which is defined as the relative loss compared to the optimal profit of a clairvoyant firm knowing full information (Objective 4). We prove that our CUP policy achieves asymptotically optimal performance, with an average regret that diminishes in the order of O(1/sqrt(T)). Numerical experiments further validate the efficiency of our algorithms across various scenarios (Objective 5). It is observed that the prices under CUP policy successfully converge to the true optimal as long as T is large enough. This observation confirms the effectiveness of our algorithm. In general, our algorithm performs robustly in finding the optimal capacity and minimizing the asymptotic regret. To address markets where the presence of reference-price effects is unknown up front, we develop a detection algorithm (Objectives 3 and 4). Influenced by reference-price effects, the demand will exhibit a stochastically increasing trend after the price switches from a low to a high level. This phenomenon suggests that the problem of detecting the reference-price effects can be transformed to a problem of identifying trends in demand. Accordingly, we design a price experiment where the firm uses high-low pricing to look for trend in the sales data after price switch. A key question in the experiment design is the selection of the time interval for observing trends. While a longer time interval can help to cancel out the variance of random shock in identifying the trend, it may also mask the effects because the trend is only temporarily noticeable as the reference converges quickly after price switch. After designing an appropriate time length for experiment based on parameter bounds from prior belief, we develop a non-parametric statistical test for the increasing trend, which enables the firm to detect the presence of the reference effects at a desired significance level. This detection algorithm can be combined with the cycle-update pricing policy to guarantee more reliable performance. Lastly, acknowledging heterogeneity in consumer behavior in practice, we extend our model to accommodate multiple customer classes with heterogeneous demand functions and reference learning mechanisms (Objectives 1, 2, 6). Our setting is general enough to include a mixed population where some customers are influenced by reference-price effects (at different degrees) and some are not. By adjusting our CUP policy to cater to the slowest learning segment among those who learn, we demonstrated its applicability and asymptotically optimal performance in a multi-class setting, further enhancing the robustness and practicality of our approach.

15507919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15507919.value: We study the dynamic pricing problem of a retailer serving customers with reference-price effects when the demand information--such as the demand function, the reference price, the magnitude of the reference effects, and customers' learning speed--is unknown. The firm's objective is to maximize expected profit by dynamically adjusting prices over a finite planning horizon. The inherent challenge lies in the absence of complete demand information, necessitating a learning process from accumulated sales data, which in turn creates a tension between exploration (gathering information) and exploitation (maximizing profit). In this project, we develop a machine learning-based cycle-update pricing policy that learn the unobservable reference price and unknown demand function, and identify the optimal pricing strategy. The crux of this policy is the deliberate infrequency of price adjustments—executed in cycles composed of numerous periods—drawing on the observation that reference prices tend to stabilize rapidly under consistent pricing. This insight enables us to estimate the reference price with remarkable precision and effectively manage learning errors by maintaining a fixed price over a prolonged period. We establish bounds on the profit loss incurred when employing our policy versus the idealized profit of a all-knowing clairvoyant. We prove that the average loss diminishes to zero as the time horizon expands, achieving near-optimal performance over the long term. To address markets where the presence of reference-price effects is unknown up front, we develop a detection algorithm and an accompanying non-parametric statistical test. These tools facilitate pricing experiments that can confirm or refute the existence of reference-price effects, with the algorithm's design capitalizing on how consistent perceived gains and losses affect demand. Furthermore, we have adapted the algorithm to accommodate multiple customer classes, ensuring its applicability and efficacy in real-world scenarios where customer behaviors are heterogeneous. Our research demonstrates that structural properties, whether theoretical or derived from practical managerial insights, can substantially mitigate the complexity of online optimization challenges and bolster our capacity to leverage data effectively. This finding underscores the notion that while computational methods are indispensable in the realm of data science, the managerial insights drawn from operations research are equally vital for the efficient and comprehensive exploitation of data. In the retail sector, our methodologies and insights are readily applicable to various contexts where reference price plays a role, such as in the fashion, grocery, and online shopping industries. A manuscript detailing the project outcomes is in the process of being refined and will be submitted to a leading journal in the field. The related methodology was applied to study a capacity planning problem in the sharing economy, resulting in a publication in Management Science. Additionally, we have completed a paper studying a service system where customers influenced by reference effects commit the sunk cost fallacy in their decisions. This paper explores the system's optimization under full information and discusses offline learning methods for detecting reference effects under unknown information. Following a "reject-and-resubmit" decision, this work is now in the revision process for potential publication in Manufacturing & Service Operations Management. Furthermore, a research on an online retailer's strategy for product line expansion and differential pricing in the context of new retail has been published in the Omega journal.

15507919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15507919.value: Although our paper focuses on scenarios involving loss-averse or neutral customers, it establishes a foundational framework for studying a problem with gain-seeking consumers, where the optimal pricing strategy may generate a fluctuating high-low pricing pattern rather than a convergent optimal price path. The understanding of the impact of reference effects during price changes, as revealed through our detection algorithm, could prove invaluable in this extension of study. While the paper focuses on the setting where customers are loss averse or neutral, it lays out foundations for studying gain-seeking customers where the optimal price path may not converge but exhibit a fluctuating high-low pattern. The insights of the monotone impact of the reference effects obtained from the design of our detection algorithm could help the study in this case. Furthermore, it would be intriguing to examine these pricing problems within volatile or evolving market conditions characterized by time-varying demand. Another promising direction for research involves incorporating a broader spectrum of reference update mechanisms. These advancements could be pursued within a parametric framework, introducing specific functional forms into the model to accommodate additional complexity.

15507919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15507919.value: We study the dynamic pricing problem of a retailer serving customers with reference-price effects when the demand information is unknown. The firm's objective is to maximize expected profit by dynamically adjusting prices over a finite planning horizon. This task is complicated by the lack of initial demand information, which necessitates a learning process using accumulated sales data. This process introduces a trade-off between exploration (gathering information) and exploitation (maximizing profit). More time spent on exploration may reduce the time available for profit maximization, while less time spent on learning could lead to suboptimal decisions during the exploitation phase due to less accurate estimations. In this project, we have developed a machine learning-based cycle-update pricing policy that learn the unobservable reference price and unknown demand function, pinpoint the optimal pricing strategy, and secure near-optimal performance as more data is acquired over time. For situations where the presence of reference-price effects is initially unclear, we have devised a detection algorithm and an accompanying non-parametric statistical test to ascertain their presence. Additionally, we have adapted the algorithm to accommodate multiple customer classes, ensuring its applicability and efficacy in real-world settings where customer behaviors are heterogeneous.

15508219.label: Realisation of objectives
15508219.value: All the three research objectives are fully realized. Specifically, we start from 71,052 firm-year observations of A-share listed Chinese companies for the years of 2003 to 2018, and then identify 3,716 observations whose audit partner(s) are in the fourth year of their tenure during the years of 2003 to 2016. We build up a dataset on partner’s personal characteristics and social ties (objective 3). For the analysis for the audit quality of the fourth year, we eliminate 180 observations that are missing control variables, which results in a sample of 3,536 firm-year observations. There are 216 or 6.1% observations in which at least one audit partner voluntarily rotates off after the 4th year and rotates back in the 6th year. We also identify 3,415 firm-year observations from 2004 to 2010 for the analysis of the incoming audit partner’s audit quality (the 5th year) and 4,339 firm-year observations from 2005 to 2018 for the analysis of the post-rotating back audit quality (the 6th year and the 7th year), and retain 2,451 and 1,888 observations respectively after excluding firm-years missing the required firm characteristics. (Objective 1). We presume that the mandatory rotation rule could induce tenure management. To verify this, we compare the incidences of partners who voluntarily rotate off after the 4th year of their tenure but rotate back after one year between the pre- (the pre-2003) and post-mandatory rotation periods. Table 2 Panel A shows that 51 or 5.3% of the 962 firm-year observations during pre-2003 period have tenure management, while 216 or 6.1% of the 3,536 firm-year observations have tenure management in the post-2003 period. The t-test shows that the probability of having tenure management is significantly higher (p value = 0.036) in post-mandatory rotation period. Hence, the mandatory rotation rule might have induced audit partners to opportunistically rotate off before reaching the 5th year and rotate back in the 6th year. (Objective 1). We examine how audit partners’ personal characteristics affect the likelihood of tenure management but did not find any significant results. (objective 2) We use Chinese data to answer our questions for two reasons. First, similar to Hong Kong, in compliance with the requirements of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) and the Ministry of Finance (MOF), audit engagement partners and concurring review partners in China are mandated to rotate off their public company audits and observe a cooling off period of 2 years. However, unlike Hong Kong where audit partners are mandated to rotate off after 7 years, audit partners who lead an audit engagement are required to rotate off after 5 years in China. The shorter period creates more incentives to strategically managing their tenure within the Chinese audit market than in Hong Kong market(Lennox et al. 2014; Huang et al. 2015).

15508219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15508219.value: Based on 3,536 firm-year observations for the historic audit partners’ last year (the 4th year), we find 216 partners rotate off audit engagements after their 4th year and then rotate back to the engagement after one year. Our audit opinion analyses suggest that historic partners are less likely to issue modified audit opinions in the year before they voluntarily rotate off (the 4th year). We also find that these partners are less likely to issue a modified audit opinion after they return to the engagement one year later (i.e., in the 6th and 7th year). Economically, partners who engage in tenure management are 1.2% less likely to issue modified opinions in year 4, and 1.0% less likely to issue modified opinions in years 6 and 7. This effect is economically large because the mean likelihood of issuing modified audit opinions in our sample is 4.5%. One may be concerned that the negative association between audit partner tenure management and modified audit opinion is driven by the enhanced communication efficiency between the historic partners and client executives (Hoang et al. 2019). To test this alternative explanation, we examine the financial reporting quality associated with tenure management and find that the practice of tenure management adversely affects the clients’ financial earnings quality, ruling out the alternative explanation. We also examine the likelihood of issuing modified audit opinions by the new temporary partner in year 5. Lennox et al. (2014) find that in China new engagement partners are associated with higher audit quality in the period following mandatory rotation. The authors attribute this increase in quality to a “fresh-eye effect”. In addition, new engagement partners normally increase audit effort during their first year of tenure (Bedard and Johnstone 2010), which results in better audit quality. On the contrary, we show that the temporary new partners lead to poorer post-audit reporting quality, measured by discretionary accruals. It is possible that partners self-select tenure management based on the client’s prior audit quality. We conduct three additional analyses to address this concern and the results suggest endogeneity is unlikely to drive our results.

15508219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15508219.value: Comparative analysis across different countries with varying rotation requirements and regulations would shed light on the effectiveness of different approaches. Comparing the outcomes of mandatory rotation versus voluntary rotation could identify strengths and weaknesses in regulatory strategies. Exploring the perspectives of stakeholders such as auditors, regulators, shareholders, and corporate executives would provide valuable insights into their experiences and perceptions. Understanding how audit partner rotation impacts independence, trust, and decision-making processes would inform regulatory policies. Considering the policy implications, policymakers should evaluate the effectiveness of existing regulations and collaborate with researchers and industry experts. Periodic evaluations of mandatory rotation regulations, potential adjustments to rotation periods, and exploration of alternative mechanisms would contribute to evidence-based policy decisions. By pursuing these avenues and implementing the proposed course of action, researchers and policymakers can advance the understanding of audit partner rotation and develop more effective frameworks for ensuring auditor independence and maintaining audit quality.

15508219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15508219.value: In many countries, regulators require audit partners to be rotated off after a certain number of years to maintain independence and objectivity. We conducted a study using data from the Chinese market, where audit partners are required to rotate off every five years. We found that a significant number of audit partners voluntarily rotated off their engagements in the fourth year but returned one year later. We observed that these partners were less likely to issue modified audit opinions in the last year of their initial tenure and the first two years after their return. However, the quality of reporting during these years was lower compared to other periods. Interestingly, we did not find that incoming partners following such "voluntary" rotation performed better in terms of audit quality in the first year after rotation, contrary to previous findings for mandatory rotations. Our study suggests that mandatory rotation regulations can lead audit partners to manage their tenure to circumvent the regulations. This behavior compromises regulatory efforts to improve auditor independence through mandatory rotation. These findings highlight the challenges in effectively implementing mandatory rotation rules and their potential impact on audit quality and independence.

15508619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15508619.value: This project aims to analyze the coopetition strategies used in competitive intelligence (CI) practices in a sample comprised of full-service hotels in Hong Kong (HK). As a process, CI involves gathering data related to the external and internal environments of a firm, and analyzing this data to convert knowledge as a root of decision-making process. Consequently, CI practices help managers formulate and implement competition strategies to gain sustainable competitive advantages. These have been proven in a number of studies that focused on individual firms’ CI practices, as these practices are individual-based due to the nature of competition among firms. However, two issues are not clear either in the literature or in practice to create a bigger market, increase their own market share or performance, or to be more innovative. The first asks whether firms, in this case hotels, collaborate on CI practices. If they do collaborate, it is unclear how these collaborations work. Second, if they do not collaborate, under what conditions could rivals collaborate for CI practices? Therefore, forms of coopetition strategies (i.e., simultaneous competition and collaboration/cooperation among competitors to gain competitive advantages) in these two cases should be identified to enhance CI practices for competitive sustainability. Considering these research gaps, this study aims answers to the following research questions based on the viewpoints of full-service hotel managers: 1- What are the (in)formal CI practices in full-service hotels in HK? How do CI practices work in these hotels? 2- Have hotels collaborated with each other to determine or develop CI practices? If yes, how does this collaboration work? What concepts of coopetition are applied? What can others learn from this exercise? 3- If they do not collaborate with each other for CI practices, under what conditions could they collaborate? What are the motives for hotels in HK to formulate and implement coopetition strategies for CI practices? What coopetition model works? This study considers a sample of full-service hotels in HK. Hotels are considered due to their unique characteristics—the inseparability of customer participation in the service process, simultaneity, perishability, intangibility, heterogeneity, cost structure, and labor intensity. The primary reason for choosing full-service hotels is that full-service hotels use more formal CI, which can be analyzed objectively. HK has been chosen as the country/region of the sample because hotels occupy an environment of fierce competitiveness in the tourism industry. 本項目旨在分析香港全套服務酒店構成的樣本中競爭情報實踐裏使用之競合策略。競爭情報作為過程，收集公司外部和內部環境相關的資料，並且分析這些資料，將知識轉化為決策過程的根源。因此，競爭情報實踐幫助管理者制定及實施競爭戰略，獲得可持續的競爭優勢。這些在一些側重于單個公司競爭情報實踐的研究中得到了證明，因為這些實踐由於公司之間的競爭性質而基於個性。然而，無論是在文獻還是在實踐中，要創造更大的市場、提高自己的市場份額或業績、或者要更具創新性，有兩個問題尚不清楚。第一個問題是：公司(在本案中為酒店)是否就競爭情報實踐進行合作。如果它們確實合作，尚不清楚這些合作如何開展。第二個問題是：如果它們不合作，競爭對手在什麼條件下可以合作開展競爭情報實踐？因此，在這兩種情況下都要確定合作戰略的形式(即競爭對手之間既競爭又合作以獲得競爭優勢)，從而加強競爭情報實踐，實現競爭的可持續性。考慮到這些研究差距，本研究根據全套服務酒店經理觀點，旨在回答以下研究問題: 1. 香港全套服務酒店的正規競爭情報實踐有哪些？競爭情報實踐在這些酒店中如何運作？ 2. 酒店是否相互合作以確定或開發競爭情報實踐？如果是，合作如何開展？應用了哪些“合作”概念？其他人可以從這個做法中學到什麼？ 3. 如果它們在競爭情報實踐方面沒有相互合作，在什麼條件下它們會合作？香港酒店為競爭情報實踐制訂及實施合作策略的動機是什麼？什麼競合模型有效？ 本研究以香港全套服務酒店為樣本。之所以考慮酒店是由於其特點—客戶參與服務過程的不可分離性、同時性、不可儲存性、無型性、異質性、成本結構和勞力密集。選擇全套服務酒店的主要原因，是由於全套服務酒店使用更正規的競爭情報，可以被客觀分析。香港之所以被選為地區樣本，是因為酒店在旅遊業中處於激烈競爭的環境。

15509319.label: Realisation of objectives
15509319.value: Gang Hu (formal PI) passed away in September 2021, and the current PI took up the role of this project since then. In November 2021, the current PI has undergone a major surgery of cervical disc replacement of two levels, whereas the treatment and recovery process has taken at least four months for PI to resume the normal daily work. Fortunately, the medical operation went successfully, and PI has made sufficient progress and fulfilled all the proposed research objectives. There is one research work derived from the project: [1] Chen, Te-Feng, Gang Hu, and Jiulin Zhao, Information Choices and Dynamic Institutional Trading Cycles, Working paper, 2023 Sydney Banking and Financial Stability Conference. In the research work, we study the preference of information sources for different types of institutional investors using the transaction-level institutional trading data from Ancerno. We have analyzed the trading patterns of institutional investors over the dynamic trading cycles classified by strategies of stock market anomalies by measuring their market timing and security abilities (Objective 1). We study the types of information institutional investors pay attention to based on the theoretical frameworks of Kacperczyk, Slaim, and Zheng (2005), and Kacperczyk, Van-Nieuwerburgh, and Veldkamp ( 2014, 2016) on institutional investment skills. We decompose the trade performance of institutional investors into anomaly timing and selection. We examine how their market timing and stock selection skills vary over time, during earning announcement period (Objective 2). To evaluate the trading skill of institutional investors, we consider the performance of 11 prominent anomaly portfolios extensively examined by Stambaugh et al. (2012) as our benchmark. We find evidence that institutional investors tend to exploit firm-management related anomalies. (Objective 3). Our study contributes to understanding institutional investors' investment beliefs regarding market anomalies. From the perspective of information acquisition, to benefit from these 11 market anomalies requires investors to absorb firm-specific information from fundamental releases, news announcements, and past performance and then draw an accurate depiction of each firm’s future. Our study shows that institutional investors time the anomaly as they investors pay more attention to that news (Objective 4).

15509419.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15509419.value: 金字塔式企業集團的附屬公司是否存在董事會防禦？ - 來自香港股票市場的證據

15509419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15509419.value: Concentrated ownership can lead to large shareholders’ rent extraction from minority shareholders. The expropriation is often accomplished through related party transactions, which “tunnel” profits from affiliated firms to the ultimate owners. This agency problem is exacerbated by pyramidal structure as information regarding the affiliated firms in the pyramidal groups (hearafter, affiliated firms) can be opaque. Moreover, the pyramidal structure is likely to create a wedge between control and cash flow rights (hereafter, control wedge) which motivates the ultimate owners to tunnel from affiliated firms. This study investigates if corporate boards for affiliated firms in Hong Kong are entrenched. The dominant ownership structure in Hong Kong is concentrated ownership and is often with pyramidal structure. Directors for the affiliated firms are supposed to represent solely that company’s shareholders, rather than the holistic interests of the pyramidal group. However, the ultimate owners may ‘control’ the boards of the affiliated firms so they can rent extract from minority investors through tunneling. A board characteristic that is especially relevant to pyramidal structure is that the ultimate owner can affect board structure by arranging the same director to serve on boards for several affiliated firms. This arrangement may increase board entrenchment toward the ultimate owners. Figure 1 presents such a relationship; also, the figure indicates that control wedge can increase ultimate owners’ motivation to tunnel. In our empirical study, we will first contrast board characters between affiliated firms and non-pyramidal firms. We will then examine if affiliated firms in the pyramidal groups with higher control wedge will be associated with more entrenched boards as evidenced by poorer board characteristics, more tunneling and lower firm value. Follow previous literature, we propose that board entrenchment is associated with board characteristics of less independence, less meeting attendance, and less leadership. Moreover, we will develop measures to reflect shared board for affiliated firms, we expect that boards with abnormally high shared directors are likely to be entrenched. We will also treat changes in regulations regarding board independence as two natural experiments (2004 and 2012) in our investigation. Our study of Hong Kong market is important by its own right because Hong Kong is one of the largest global capital markets and is a financial gateway to mainland China. Moreover, our findings can have implications to many other capital markets as pyramidal ownership is frequently found in both developed and emerging capital markets. 股權集中式所有制結構會導致大股東壓榨小股東的現象發生。這種侵佔行為經常通過相關交易實現，從附屬公司“掏空”利益給最終控制人。此類代理問題在金字塔式集團更為嚴重，因為金字塔式集團附屬公司（下文簡稱“附屬公司”）的相關信息是不透明的。此外，金字塔式結構導致的控股股東控制權與現金流權的分離（下文簡稱“兩權分離”）更加促使掏空行為的發生。 本研究對在香港的附屬公司是否存在董事會防禦進行研究。股權集中制是香港企業所有權結構存在的主要形式，其中以金字塔式結構較為常見。附屬公司的董事應代表公司股東，而不是整個金字塔式集團的利益。然而，最終控制人可能會“控制”附屬公司的董事會，通過掏空行為榨取小股東的利益。金字塔式結構企業最典型的董事會特征就是最終控制人可以影響董事會結構，即安排相同人員在集團公司的多個附屬公司董事會。這種安排會增加最終控制人的董事會防禦，關係圖如圖1所示。同時可以看出，兩權分離能夠加劇最終控制人的掏空行為。在實證分析中，本研究首先對比了金字塔集團附屬公司與非金字塔式公司的董事會特征；其次，對具有兩權分離度較高的金字塔集團附屬公司是否存在更嚴重的董事會防禦進行檢驗，防禦行為表現為更差的董事會特征、更多掏空行為、以及更低的公司價值。 借鑒以往文獻，本文假定董事會防禦表現為較低的董事會獨立性、較低的會議出席率、及較低的領導力。此外，本研究將設計能夠衡量附屬公司董事會兼職的變量。研究結果預期，兼職程度異常高的董事會更可能存在防禦行為。在實證設計中，本研究將與董事會獨立性相關的政策變更事件（2004年與2012年）作為自然實驗。 本研究對香港市場本身的重要性在於香港是全球最大的資本市場之一，也是通往中國內地的資本門戶。同時，研究結果對其他存在金字塔式所有制結構的發展及發展中資本市場也同樣具有參考作用。

15509719.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15509719.value: 放下过去：企业记忆衰退和企业的竞争侵略性

15509719.label: Co - Investigator(s)
15509719.value: Prof Gimeno, Javier Dr GUO, Wei Vivian Prof Yu, Tieying

15509719.label: Project Objectives
15509719.value: To explore how the decay of organizational memory influences the aggressiveness of a firm’s competitive behavior. To identify contingencies that may attenuate or amplify the effect of memory decay on firm competitive aggressiveness. To explore the performance implications of organizational memory decay.
rows: To explore how the decay of organizational memory influences the aggressiveness of a firm’s competitive behavior.
To identify contingencies that may attenuate or amplify the effect of memory decay on firm competitive aggressiveness.
To explore the performance implications of organizational memory decay.

15509719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15509719.value: Understanding the conditions that influence interfirm rivalry is a fundamental issue in strategic management. Although its significance was first demonstrated nearly 30 years ago, our understanding of how managerial cognition (beyond managerial mental models) drives firm competitive behavior remains surprisingly limited. In particular, the impact of organizational memory on firm competitive behavior is poorly understood. This is unfortunate, as both anecdotal and research evidence suggests that competitors integrate what they remember from the past in their strategic decision-making. Combining insights from competitive dynamics with cognitive and social psychology, this study will explore how organizational memory decay in relation to price wars influences the aggressiveness of a firm’s competitive behavior and the important contingencies that may govern such influence. We predict that the decay of organizational memories of price wars will increase a firm’s competitive aggressiveness in a given market but that this effect is contingent upon the existence of retrieval cues. Specifically, we argue that this pro-competition effect is weaker when the focal firm repeatedly encounters the same price-war rivals in the same market, when it observes similar wars in other markets, and when external information intermediaries refer repeatedly to price war. Finally, we propose that memory decay can be beneficial when the focal firm “forgets” its previous wars and its competitors do not. We plan to test our hypotheses in the context of the U.S. domestic airline industry (1979–2018). We propose to build an extensive dataset by assembling information from sources that include the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) database; 75 Air Transport Association (ATA) annual reports (1937–2011); 720 annual reports of individual airlines (1979–2018); all price-war related articles in the Factiva database; and 23,670 articles from Aviation Daily (1989-2018), a leading trade journal. By integrating quantitative and qualitative data, we aim to test the research hypotheses and to develop a rich historical narrative that fully captures the nature of price wars and the context of this study. 了解影响企业间竞争的条件是战略管理学中的一个基本问题。尽管其重要性在30年前已经得到证实，但我们对企业经理人认知如何影响和推动企业竞争行为的理解仍然非常有限。我们对组织记忆如何影响企业竞争行为了解尤其少。这是不幸的，因为轶事和研究证据表明，竞争对手将他们过去记忆中的内容整合到战略决策中。 结合企业竞争动态与认知和社会心理学的见解，本研究将探讨与价格战相关的组织记忆衰退如何影响企业竞争行为的侵略性以及可能影响这个关系的重要突发事件。我们预测，关于价格战的组织记忆的衰退将增加公司在特定市场中的竞争激进性，但这种影响取决于组织记忆检索线索的存在。具体而言，我们认为，当公司在同一市场上反复遇到同样的价格战对手，当其观察到其他市场内类似的战争，以及外部信息中介反复提到价格战时，这种竞争效应就会变弱。最后，我们提出，当遇到公司“忘记”以前的战争而其竞争对手没有的这种情况时，记忆衰退可能对企业是有益的。 我们计划在美国航空业（1979-2018）的背景下测试我们的假设。我们建议通过汇总来自美国交通部数据库的信息来建立一个广泛的数据集; 75份美国航空运输协会的年度报告（1937-2011）; 各航空公司的720份年度报告（1979-2018）; Factiva数据库中所有与价格战相关的文章; 来自航空日报（1989-2018）的23,670篇文章。通过整合定量和定性数据，我们的目标是测试研究假设并提供丰富的历史叙述，充分体现价格战的本质和本研究的背景。
