15600219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600219.value: Service-learning, which combines meaningful service to the community with academic learning, is recognized as a high-impact educational practice. It is well-known that service-learning is effective at achieving a wide range of cognitive and affective outcomes, including intellectual skills, problem solving, critical thinking, personal skills, and civic responsibility. In Hong Kong, service-learning is incorporated in some form among all 8 UGC-funded universities. However, systematic research on service-learning in Hong Kong is almost non-existent. There has been much research into “whether”, and “what”, benefits service-learning bring to students. However, less effort has been paid to the “process” (i.e., “how”) by which service-learning imparts these learning gains to students. Although there are some guidelines of “good practices”, many are derived from anecdotal experiences. Most of the few available studies were conducted in the US and/or focus on a few selected course characteristics, often based on a single program. The few large-scale studies rely on statistical approaches testing different models, which often have difficulty handling large amounts of highly noisy, interdependent data. An added challenge is that some factors in current models are not readily measurable or quantifiable. We address this gap as follows. First, this project proposes a data-driven investigation of the factors that shape student learning outcomes in service-learning. These include curricular and pedagogical processes (e.g. project nature, location and student preparation) and human factors (student perception, inclination, interest, prior experience, and teacher perception and approach). Second, this project will assess and compare the impact of the factors upon different learning outcomes and investigate their inter-dependencies, particularly with reference to the available theoretical models on the determinants of the outcomes of service-learning. Third, the findings will be used to construct an evidence-based framework that describes the contribution and interaction of the various student, course and teacher factors that impact student learning in service-learning. This framework will be evaluated with cross-institution, cross-disciplinary and cross-year data. This study contributes to the service-learning and educational community in several ways. First, by empirically analyzing the learning process, it will validate (or invalidate) existing models for best practices. Second, systematic analysis of various pedagogical elements will lead to better understanding of the learning process. Third, there is a possibility that new best practices will be uncovered through this project. All these will lead to more effective practices and more consistent student learning outcomes. Finally, this study seeks to confirm the practical significance of service-learning to higher education institutions in Hong Kong. 將有意義的社區服務與學術學習相結合的服務學習，已成為了一種極具影響力的教育實踐。眾所周知，服務學習能够有效地實現多方面的的學習成效，包括智力技能、解决問題的能力、批判性思維、個人技能和公民責任。在香港，所有8所UGC資助的大學均以某種形式開設了服務學習。然而，香港卻幾乎沒有關於服務學習的系統化的研究。 人們對服務學習“是否”能給學生帶來好處，以及能帶來“什麼”好處進行了大量的研究。然而，卻很少有人研究學生在服務學習中的受益過程，即服務學習是“如何” 將這些好處帶給學生的。雖然有一些“成效良好”的指導方針，但大多來自於相傳的經驗。現有的研究中，大多數是在美國進行的及（或）專注於一些選定的課程特徵，通常基於單個課程。少數大規模的研究依賴於統計方法來測試不同的模型，這些模型通常難以處理大量高噪聲，相互依賴的數據。另一個挑戰是, 當前的模型中的某些因素不易測量或量化。 我們將通過下述的方法來解決這些問題。首先，本計畫提出一個數據驅動的調查，探討服務學習中影響學生學習成效的因素。這包括課程和教學過程（如項目性質、地點和學生準備）和人為因素（學生的觀感、傾向、興趣、既往經驗以及教師的觀感和方法）。其次，本項目將評估這些因素對不同學習成果的影響，以及調查它們之間的相互依賴性，並且將我們的調查發現與現有的關於服務學習成果决定因素的理論模型的結論相比較。最後，這些研究結果將用於構建一個基於證據的框架。該框架描述影響學生在服務學習中學習效果的包括學生，課程和教師等各個因素的貢獻和相互作用。我們將使用跨機構，跨學科和跨年度數據來評估這個框架。 本研究從多個方面為服務學習及教育領域作出貢獻。第一，通過實證分析學習的過程，我們將證實（或推翻）現有的模型以得到最佳的教學實踐。第二，對各種教學要素進行系統分析將有助於更好地理解學習過程。第三，通過這個項目，我們有機會發現新的最佳教學實踐。所有這些都將引領出更有效的教學實踐和更一致的學生學習成果。最後，本研究力圖證明服務學習對香港高等教育的重要現實意義。

15600219.label: Realisation of objectives
15600219.value: 5.3 Realisation of objectives 5.3.1 Project Overview and Objectives This project investigates how students achieve diverse learning outcomes in service-learning, aiming to consolidate factors influencing these outcomes into a framework. Several studies were conducted to address the four main objectives. 5.3.2 Methodology We evaluated statistical models and applied machine learning (ML) to explore factors that impact student learning in service-learning programs. These factors include pedagogical, curricular, and human factors. We predicted outcomes associated with intellectual, social, civic, and personal development using data collected across three levels, structured surveys, open-ended reflections, and dynamic multimodal behaviors. (1) Close-Ended Survey Responses: Close-ended student surveys is often used to analyze learning outcomes, where students rate pre-defined survey questions to indicate their level of agreement with items on course factors and learning experiences. Data: The data was collected from over 11,000 responses from undergraduate students who participated in service-learning courses between 2014 and 2019 at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University (PolyU). These courses covered a wide range of disciplines, with service projects varying by location, type of beneficiaries, and activities. [Journal 1, Conference 3]. Students were asked to fill out a Student Post-Experience Questionnaire (SPEQ) upon course completion. The SPEQ was developed by the university with reference to the literature review and the specific contexts of service-learning. Modeling: We first applied contemporary statistical models to examine the relationships between course and human factors, and learning outcomes (Objective 1). Traditional ML was used to predict learning outcomes and identify course and student factors with significant impacts (Objective 2). Attention-based deep neural networks were used to capture complex, non-linear dependencies between the inputs and learning outcomes. Training and evaluating these models identified key features that influenced students’ learning outcomes (using feature important scores and attention weights). These insights are important for understanding how students' experiences during the course impact their learning outcomes (Objective 2). This analysis is also useful to compare the identified important factors for different learning outcomes (Objective 3). (2) Open-Ended Text Reflection: Students’ open-ended textual responses may provide an additional tool by which to measure students’ personalized learning experiences, factors and gains from their perspectives, beyond the constraints of pre-defined structured survey items. Data: We collected from 2608 students between the academic years 2020 and 2021 at PolyU. The surveys were completed by students online after class. Both the textual responses and ratings from the SPEQ were collected. [Journal 6]. Modeling: We used BERT-based sentence embeddings and K-means clustering to analyze the open-ended textual reflection. Sentence embeddings capture the latent semantic structure of student reflections, while clustering identifies common topics. By comparing these topics with the outcomes from close-ended surveys, we gained a deeper understanding of students’ learning experiences and their relations with outcomes (Objective 2 & 3). (3) Multimodal Behaviors: Multimodal behaviors in classes and learning projects can capture students’ learning experiences in a more dynamic, direct, and objective way. Data: We collected data from large online service-learning subjects at PolyU, where PolyU students worked as Tutors to design and deliver online short courses via zoom, to primary or secondary students (Recipients). In total, we collected 250 zoom recordings, including video and audio channels, from 25 service programs. The dataset provides a rich data for multimodal behavior analysis together with students’ self-reported SPEQ ratings. Modeling: In our preliminary study, we started with modeling the transcript data extracted from the audio channel of zoom recordings. We extracted transcript features, including the linguistic and semantic features (e.g., the lexical density, polarity scores, and the count of question words). Furthermore, we also captured interaction dynamics between Tutors and Recipients, including the overall backchannel word, question word, and interaction counts between Tutors and Recipients. We trained ML models with these features to predict PolyU students’ (i.e., Tutors) learning outcomes, and identified significant features for different learning outcomes respectively (Objective 2 & 3). Working with diverse data allows us to examine the impacts of various learning experiences and course factors on students’ service-learning outcomes from different perspectives, particularly when incorporating with ML techniques. This supports the achievement of the project objectives while also leading to additional contributions beyond service-learning process understanding. (4) Other factors: Student motivation and the modality of learning will also impact students’ perception of the service project and hence their learning outcomes. Data: We collected survey data on students’ motivation and learning outcome data across a diversity of service-learning subjects using SPEQ and another instrument focusing on intrinsic and extrinsic motivation. Modeling: We employed a variety of statistical methods to analyse the data, including to delve into the predictors of students’ motivation in service-learning, and to compare student learning and experiences from online and in-person service-learning. 5.3.3 Results and Findings Our studies demonstrate that applying ML is an effective approach to model learning experiences and course factors, capturing their interrelationships and their connection to learning outcomes. This helps in identifying key factors and assess their impacts. The results expose that different learning experience do have different impacts on service-learning outcomes, and the impacts of one particular learning experience are not uniform across different learning outcomes (Objective 2 & 3). (1) Close-Ended Surveys: Analysis of close-ended survey responses revealed that there are variable impacts from factors on students’ intellectual, civic, and personal learning outcomes. Notably, interaction-focused factors have a strong impact on social learning outcomes. These results provide insights into what course and learning experiences are most important for optimizing student engagement and development. (Objective 1, 2, 3). (2) Open-Ended Text Reflection: The open-ended reflections emphasized experiences related to civic engagement and communication. These findings triangulate with the survey results, providing a deeper understanding of students’ perception of their learning outcomes. For example, students frequently highlighted the importance of interactions with service recipients and teammates (Objective 2, 3). (3) Multimodal Behaviors: Analysis of multimodal behaviors reveals that verbal interactions, such as backchannel responses and question words, are important for learning outcomes, particularly intellectual and social (Objective 2, 3). Even though the zoom recordings were captured during the pandemic and most of the participants wore masks, added challenges to extracting precise visual feature, but pilot studies revealed the potential of joint modeling of visual for inferring interaction states such as backchannel responses, engagement and eye contact [Conference 1, 2 & 4, Journal 3]. This informs future directions to integrate visual and verbal features for more robust multimodal models. (4) Other Factors: Our analysis of student motivation revealed that contrary to commonly-held perception, student motivation is not fixed but can be and is impacted by student learning experience [Journal 5]. Our analysis also revealed that in general, student learning from online service-learning was not as satisfactory as in-person service-learning [Journal 5]. Overall, the use of multiple data types (survey responses, open-ended reflections, and multimodal behaviors), enhanced our ability to model and understand the complex relationships between course factors, student experiences, and learning outcomes. This multi-dimensional approach supports the achievement of the project objectives and offers valuable insights for improving service-learning programs. The findings also suggest practical implications for course design, highlighting the importance of meaningful, engaging tasks, and strong interpersonal interactions for enhancing students' learning experiences and outcomes (Objective 4).

15600219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600219.value: Our studies demonstrate that machine learning (ML) methods are effective in modeling student learning experiences and course factors in service-learning programs, particularly for capturing complex relationships between learning factors and outcomes. By applying ML to different levels of student responses, including survey rating responses, textual reflections, and multimodal behavioral data, we identified various key learning and course factors and their impacts on student development in intellectual, social, civic, and personal domains. In particular, we found that students' learning experience and course factors regarding “Study Challenge”, “Program Value and Benefit”, and “Study Effort” significantly influence their learning across almost all the service-learning outcomes. This is especially true for intellectual, civic and personal learning outcomes. Learning experience and course factors regarding “Study Interest”, “Help & Support”, “Participant & Interaction” and “Structure & Reflection” are also important learning experience that have relative high impact on at least two learning outcomes. For example, “Study Interest” and “Structure & Reflection” are particular important for intellectual and civic learning outcomes, which are related to knowledge transfer, civic engagement and community services of service-learning courses. From these findings we see the importance of tasks that are really meaningful, challenging, interesting and valued for optimizing students' service-learning. Furthermore, we identified the strong impact of support, peer interaction and teamwork on social development, consistently across the three levels of responses. Besides, students' open-ended reflections revealed that engagement in service-learning enhanced their sense of civic responsibility, empathy, and communication skills. This aligns with their self-reported learning outcomes, demonstrating the alignment between textual reflections and close-ended ratings. In our pilot study on multimodal behavior analysis, we found that analyzing transcript data, including backchannel responses and interaction counts, helps in modeling student experience for predicting service-learning outcomes. This shows the potential of multimodal behavior-based learning process analysis. Although, there are challenges in extracting visual features in our dataset, due to masks during the pandemic, our pilot study on public datasets revealed the potential of visual features (e.g., head movements and eye contact) in enhancing human-human interaction analysis (e.g., backchannel and engagement in learning tasks). This could be extended to modeling student learning and project interaction in the future. This sheds lights on more comprehensive multimodal models to understand student learning in the future.

15600219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15600219.value: As the zoom recordings were captured during the pandemic, most of the Tutors and Recipients wore masks during the classes. This added challenges to extracting precise visual features (e.g., facial expressions and eye gaze features) for modeling. Our pilot study using publicly available datasets revealed the potential of visual features (e.g., head movements and eye contact) in enhancing human-human interaction analysis (e.g., backchannel and engagement in learning tasks). This could be extended to modeling student learning and project interaction in the future. The potential future development includes exploring visual features-based and more comprehensive multimodal service-learning process with newly collected higher-quality video data.

15600219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600219.value: This project aims to explore how students learn in service-learning programs, where they apply their academic knowledge through community service projects, such as teaching children in developing regions. By analyzing students’ experiences using close-ended survey ratings, open-ended textual reflections, and behavior during their projects, we identified key factors that help them gain improvements in service-learning programs. We found that making students feel challenging, interesting, and meaningful in service-learning courses, activities and projects are the most important. Providing proper helps and supports, and creating peer interactions and teamwork are also important especially in developing students’ social skills. Besides, we also found that students' own reflections about their experiences and gains matched the learning outcomes they reported in surveys. This demonstrates the important of offering chance to let students to report their learning journey. Our studies also highlight the importance of using advanced technologies like multimodal machine learning modeling to better understand complex, dynamic, and objective learning patterns, though more comprehensive studies are needed in the future. This includes incorporating facial expressions, body movements, eye gaze, and speech and textual features to help create a more complete picture of how students interact and learn in service-learning programs.

15600419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600419.value: Jakobsen (1959) proposed three categories of translation activities, namely, inter-lingual translation, intra-lingual translation, and inter-semiotic translation. Most empirical studies focus on processes of inter-lingual translation, while intra-lingual translation, often known as rewording or paraphrasing within the same language, has been rarely investigated and its relations with inter-lingual translation remains elusive. In this project, we aim to explore similarities and differences between inter-lingual translation and paraphrasing (one representative variant of intra-lingual translation) mainly based on data collected through eye-tracking and key-logging. The major research questions include: 1)What are the similarities and/or differences between paraphrasing and translation in cognitive processes? 2) Are there significant differences across translators with different levels of expertise during on-line processing of translation and paraphrasing? 3) In what way and to what extent do language-specific and culture-specific factors affect the cognitive processing of paraphrasing/translation? We hypothesize that 1) Paraphrasing is intrinsically related to translation: both activities require similar amounts of cognitive effort, the cognitive patterns detected in paraphrasing are also transferable to translation, and there are significant correlations between paraphrasing and translation quality. 2) On-line processing of both types of translation is impacted by level of translation expertise since there are always considerable differences in terms of cognitive effort and cognitive efficiency between professional translators and novice translators. These hypotheses will be examined in two experiments: In Experiment One, participants will paraphrase three manipulated texts from English to Chinese; in Experiment Two, they will translate three comparable English texts into Chinese. Participants’ cognitive processes, indicated by eye movement and key-logging data, will be analyzed to identify the cognitive profiles during intra- and inter-lingual translation and to depict the general behavioral patterns of professionals and novices. In addition, product-oriented analysis based on target text evaluation will also be adopted to supplement the experimental data. Driven by this experimental approach, the findings of this project are expected to enrich our knowledge on the cognitive processing of intra-lingual translation by identifying its shared ground with and differences from inter-lingual translation. Behavior or skill transfer between the two translation modes, as well as correlations between paraphrasing quality and translation quality, if corroborated by data results, can provide rigorous evidence for incorporating regular paraphrase training to translation curricula in HK-based institutions, thus enhancing efficiency of translation training. Jakobsen (1959)把翻譯活動劃分為語際翻譯、語內翻譯及符際翻譯三種。大多數相關的實證研究均為討論語際翻譯過程；而語內翻譯，亦稱為在同一語言中的重述或釋義的過程則鮮見探討。後者與語際翻譯過程之關係仍然有待探索。本研究旨在通過收集眼動儀及鍵盤記錄的數據，來探索語際翻譯與釋義（即是語內翻譯的其中一種代表活動）之間的異同。我們的研究問題如下：1)釋義與翻譯的認知行為有何異同？2）不同能力水準的譯員在其翻譯及釋義線上過程中有顯著區別嗎？3）語言及文化的特定因素在何種方式及何種程度影響翻譯及釋義的認知過程？我們的假設如下：1）釋義本質而言與翻譯相關：兩種活動都需要類似的認知努力。釋義中發現的認知模式亦可以轉移至翻譯活動之中。釋義與翻譯品質有顯著相關。2）這兩種活動的線上處理過程均受翻譯能力高度的影響，因為職業譯員與新手譯員在認識努力及認知有效性方面存在巨大差別。研究通過以下兩個實驗來驗證假設。實驗一：受試把三篇受控文本從英文釋義至中文；實驗二：受試把三篇相似的英文譯成中文。受試認知過程中所產生的眼動及鍵盤記錄資料會用於重構他們在語內及語際翻譯時的認識狀況，呈現職業及新手譯員總體的認知行為模式。同時，對實驗中得到的目標語文本會進一步採用專家評估，用於補充分析實驗所得的資料。本實驗研究的結果應會豐富我們對語內翻譯認知過程的瞭解，發現其與語際翻譯的異同。若實驗數據能夠證明這兩種翻譯模式之間的表現形式及技能的聯繫,以及釋義質量與翻譯質量的關聯，會給香港大專院校開設的翻譯課程是否應該提供恒常的釋義訓練提供嚴謹的實證證據，從而更有效地培訓譯員。

15600419.label: Realisation of objectives
15600419.value: 1. To contribute to existing understanding of intra-lingual translation by examining the cognitive process of intra-lingual translation as represented by paraphrasing and exploring its correlations with inter-lingual translation in process and product. An experimental study on translation and paraphrasing among 24 translation trainees has been conducted, combining eye-tracking, key-logging, and retrospective protocols among the MA students of translation and interpreting in Hong Kong universities. We enriched the material design to further consider the influential factor of translation directionality. Therefore, four types of tasks were included in the experiment: inter-lingual translation from English to Chinese and vice versa, and intra-lingual paraphrasing in English and Chinese. A total of 192 translations and paraphrases were performed, and retrospective interviews were also conducted for data triangulation. The cognitive processes of translation and paraphrasing tasks were demonstrated by eye-tracking metrics, including the average fixation duration, the average fixation count, and the visit count. The former two metrics reflect the amount of cognitive load, and the last one indicates the attention shift pattern during the task. These metrics have been extracted, analyzed, and compared between translation and paraphrasing at both textual and sentential levels. The modulation effects of source text genre and language types on the cognitive processing of translation and paraphrasing have also been explored. Results of these investigations have been reported in two journal articles, "A cognitive inquiry into similarities and differences between translation and paraphrase: Evidence from eye movement data" and "Global and Local Cognitive Processing in Paraphrasing and Translation —— A Comparative Study using Eye-tracking and Retrospective Protocols". The output translations and paraphrases have also been compared regarding their linguistic features, information delivery, communicative appropriateness, and overall performance. The findings have also been reported in the journal article "Comparing product quality between translation and paraphrasing: Using NLP-assisted evaluation frameworks". 2. To expand knowledge on specific skills required for intra-lingual translation by identifying those skills and behaviors. The specific behaviors and skills during paraphrasing have been identified from the eye-tracking experiment, the product quality assessment, and the retrospective interview. Paraphrasing behaviors such as attention distribution and shift patterns indicated by participants' eye-tracking metrics have been described and further compared with those in the translation task. The universal translation behaviors and unique features during intra-lingual paraphrasing have been concluded, and behavioral differences in the genre- and language-specific behaviors between the two tasks have also been reported. Paraphrasing skills have been explored based on both quantitative data (the linguistic indicators and the ratings of product quality) and qualitative data (the retrospective interviews). The output products were assessed by human raters and the natural language processing (NLP) tools, and the interviews were transcribed and analyzed qualitatively to dig deeper into participants' thoughts when they encountered processing barriers and the strategies they adopted to relieve processing difficulties. We have discussed skills that are transferable between inter- and intra-lingual translations and also those specific in paraphrasing. Their potential insights for translation pedagogy have also been discussed and concluded. These findings have been reported in three published journal articles. 3. To uncover how translation expertise relates to cognitive processing of paraphrasing by examining differences between professionals and novices in terms of their end products Originally, we planned to invite professional interpreters in the interpreting and translation department of Huawei Company based in Shenzhen to attend our experiment in 2021. However, these targeted subjects couldn't come to Hong Kong due to the long-lasting shutdown of Hong Kong and mainland China's borders during Covid-19. We could only recruit participants in Hong Kong instead, where the pool of qualified professionals for our experiment is very small. Consequently, we invited ten professional interpreters, and five attended and completed our experiment successfully in the end. This sample size was too small compared with that of the student trainees, which may undermine the validity of the comparison between the two groups. Facing this situation, we decided to make some changes to our experiment design. Instead of viewing translation expertise as a dichotomy (trainee vs. professional) as we had originally planned, we chose to treat it as a continuum from beginners to experts and grouped all the participants (29 in total). A questionnaire has been assigned to collect detailed information about their translation experience and self-declared English language proficiency. The collected information confirmed that our participants vary in their English and translation backgrounds and can meet our requirement to demonstrate a continuum of translation proficiency levels. The product quality of all the translations and paraphrases has been assessed in holistic and analytical ways. The role of translation expertise, as presented by divergent assessment results of translation performance, has been explored in the paraphrasing task by examining the correlation in product quality between the two tasks. We further narrowed our focus and targeted the linguistic features in the products of different quality. The correlation between linguistic features and output quality in each task has been investigated, and features that are most susceptible to translation expertise in paraphrases have been identified. The implications of the role of expertise in the cognitive processing of paraphrasing have also been discussed. These findings have been included in the journal article "Comparing product quality between translation and paraphrasing: Using NLP-assisted evaluation frameworks". 15600419.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600419.value: The current project uncovered the similarities and differences between translation and paraphrasing regarding cognitive processes and output products. At the textual level, translation and paraphrasing share a similar attention distribution pattern during on-line processing, accompanied by a highly correlated output performance between two tasks and shared lexical sophistication features in their products. Besides, an L1 advantage is confirmed in both tasks, evidenced by an increased processing effort and attention shift frequency in L2 comprehension and production compared to L1. However, the two tasks differ in the overall cognitive load during processing, with translation requiring a greater processing effort than paraphrasing and demonstrating a reduced L1 advantage during comprehension. This difference tends to modulate the predictive weight of textual features in the output quality, making translation quality more predictable by the breadth of the vocabulary and noun phrases and paraphrasing quality more distinguishable by the depth of lexical knowledge and the complexity of clauses. The translation is also confirmed to be more sensitive to the text genre by requiring a significantly higher cognitive load and more frequent attention shifts in the news text compared to the tourism text (Ma et al., 2022; Han et al., 2022b). At the sentential level, both translation and paraphrasing are sensitive to sentences with increased complexity, and this feature is more remarkable in translation. We also observed a similar genre-specific difference between the two tasks (Han et al., 2022a). In terms of specific behaviors and strategies, paraphrasing is typical for its meaning transfer and linguistic selection within one language and therefore relies more on the sequential processing of comprehension and production. It is also less sensitive to the text genre and fails to involve genre-specific strategies to fulfill communicative goals. In addition, a strategy of shallow processing can be observed in paraphrasing, especially when people encounter cognitively demanding sentences. As a type of translation activity, paraphrasing demonstrates shared skills and behaviors in translation, such as similar ways of allocating cognitive resources and transferable metacognitive skills (Ma et al., 2022; Han et al., 2022a). NLP-assisted frameworks for translation and paraphrasing have been constructed to investigate the effect of translation expertise on paraphrasing. Participants with a higher level of expertise tend to perform better during paraphrasing especially in the language quality, characterized by more sophisticated vocabulary with higher concreteness and contextual distinctiveness, as well as more complex noun phrases and clauses (Han et al., 2022b).

15600419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15600419.value: 1. Future research agenda The cognitive load is mainly reflected by eye movements in the current project. Future studies can also involve key-logging data by analyzing pauses and revisions during the real-time target text production to further verify our findings. Besides, the effect of translation expertise can be further investigated by recruiting more professional translators in the future and examining differences between professionals and novices in terms of their cognitive processes and end products. 2. Future translation pedagogy It is revealed in the current research project that translation and paraphrasing share similar patterns in cognitive processes and specific transferable skills. More importantly, the performance of the two tasks is highly correlated. It is therefore suggested that in the future, paraphrasing practice can be incorporated into normal translation training. New curriculums with an emphasis on paraphrasing can be developed to improve Translation&Interpreting training in Hong Kong. In addition, the NLP-assisted quality assessment frameworks for translation and paraphrasing proposed in this project could also be adopted by teachers as a tool to achieve a more systemic, reliable, and efficient evaluation of translation and paraphrasing quality.

15600419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600419.value: This project investigated the cognitive processes, production behaviors, and specific skills in paraphrasing by conducting a comparative study with translation and further explored the effect of translation expertise. The significance of the current research project is multi-faceted. Theoretically, a comprehensive inquiry into paraphrasing in process and product would enrich our understanding of the intra-lingual translation activity. Empirical comparisons between translation and paraphrasing would further provide evidence for untested assumptions on the cognitive interplay between the two types of translation and fill the research gap that most of the existing empirical research on paraphrasing is mainly drawn on European language pairs. Pedagogically, the similar cognitive processes and transferable skills would give insight into the incorporation of paraphrasing practice into translation training to sharpen the shared skills such as message conceptualization and reformulation and cognitive management ability. This would contribute to the further development of translation curricula in Hong Kong institutions. Besides, the construction of NLP-assisted quality assessment frameworks for translation and paraphrasing would assist translation teachers in assessing product quality in a more efficient and effective way.

15600619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600619.value: Important decisions often involve choices between abstract options that consist of a collection of concrete objects. For example, a couple choosing between residential districts composed of different houses or university graduates choosing between professional sectors composed of different jobs. Although these abstract options, sometimes referred to as “environments”, do not lead to immediate rewards, the choice of an environment has important consequences by placing constraints to the actual objects/choices that are available in the future. However, previous cognitive neuroscience research has largely focused on decision making between specific objects (Obj-Obj decision making) or between an environment and an object (Env-Obj decision making). This research has demonstrated that the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) and dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC) are involved in these decisions respectively. However, it is not yet known how important decisions between different environments (Env-Env decision making) are made in the brain. Our project proposes that a neural mechanism of Env-Env decision making should exhibit at least three properties. First, it should involve a brain region that represents the statistical distribution of the component objects of an environment. Second, the brain region should show activity related to the competition between two environments. Third, the neural signals should be dynamic and adaptive to changes in contextual demands. Here, we propose to conduct an experiment that involves a novel two-stage decision making task in which healthy human participants will make Env-Env decisions (Stage 1) and Obj-Obj decisions (Stage 2), while undergoing functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). We will run a three-part investigation. First, we will analyze the behavioural data and test whether people can make adaptive Env-Env decisions. Second, we will run three computational models and identify the distribution factors that influence participants’ choices, including a power model, mean-variance-skewness model and classical cumulative prospect theory model. Third and most importantly, we will examine the fMRI data and identify the critical neural regions that exhibit the three key properties of Env-Env decision making outlined above. To evaluate the feasibility of our project, we have already run three pilot studies. A model comparison also suggested that the power model outperformed the alternative models in describing Env-Env choices. Our preliminary behavioural findings suggested that people flexibly adapt their choices according to the contexts during Env-Env decisions. Finally, the preliminary fMRI data showed trends that the dACC signal was related to Env-Env decision making, whereas the vmPFC signal was related to Obj-Obj decision making. 重要的決策通常需要於抽象的選項之間作選擇，這些選項一般由較具體的對象組成。例如，一對夫婦選擇在不同房屋組成的住宅區之間選擇或大學畢業生在由不同工作組成的專業之間選擇。雖然這些抽象選項（有時稱為“環境”）不會立即帶來獎勵，但環境的選擇會限制將來面對的實際對象/選擇，而產生重要的後果。然而，先期的認知神經科學研究主要集中在特定對象（Obj-Obj決策）之間或環境與對象之間（Env-Obj決策制定）之間的決策。這些研究顯示，腹內側前額葉皮層（vmPFC）和背部扣帶皮層（dACC）分別參與了這些決定。然而，不同環境（Env-Env決策）之間的決策在大腦中是如何發生目前尚不清楚。 我們的項目提出Env-Env決策的神經機制應至少具有三個特徵。第一，它應該涉及一個腦區以表示環境中對象的統計分佈。第二，腦區的活動應與兩種環境之間的競爭相關。第三，神經信號應該是動態的以適應決策需求的變化。我們建議進行一項創新的二段決策實驗，當中健康的被試將進行Env-Env決策（階段1）和Obj-Obj決定（階段2），並同時接受功能磁共振成像（ fMRI）。我們將進行一個由三部分組成的研究。其一，我們將分析行為數據並測試人們是否可以做出自有效的Env-Env決策。其次，我們將運行三個計算模型，並確定影響參與者選擇的分佈因素，包括Power模型，mean-variance-skewness模型和cumulative prospect theory模型。其三，我們將分析fMRI數據，並確定具有上述三個Env-Env決策關鍵特性的腦區。 為了評估我們項目的可行性，我們已經開展了三項試點研究。模型比較表明，在描述Env-Env選擇時，Power模型的表現優於其他模型。我們的初步行為調查結果表明，人們根據Env-Env決策中的背景靈活地調整他們的選擇。最後，初步的fMRI數據顯示dACC信號與Env-Env決策有關，而vmPFC信號與Obj-Obj決策有關。

15600619.label: Realisation of objectives
15600619.value: Objective 1: To investigate the dissociable neural mechanisms of between-environment decision making and between-object decision making. An experiment was performed that involved twenty-six healthy participants performing a decision making task while undergoing functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). We identified that during between-environment decision-making, it involved a signal in the frontopolar cortex (FPC). In contrast, between-object decision-making involved a signal in the ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC). Objective 2: To investigate the dynamic adaptation of the neural representations of an environment to contextual demands. The decision making task required conditions in which participants had to adapt their choice based on the bonus presented. We identified that the FPC and vmPFC signals adapted as a function of the choice adaptation due to the presence of bonus during between-environment choice and between-object choice, respectively. Objective 3: To determine the key features of the object distribution in an environment that influence between-environment decision making.. We applied a mean-variance-skewness (MVS) model to analyse participants’ choice data. The results showed that participants were more likely to choose environments with greater mean and greater variance. We found that the skewness of the distribution of an environment had no impact on participants’ choices.

15600619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600619.value: This research has generated one publication (Law et al., Cell Reports, 2023), two conference abstracts and one science exhibition at the Hong Kong Laureate Forum. The project has also successfully trained one MPhil student, Chan Ka Siu, who graduated in 2023. The original proposal suggested an output of two conference abstracts and one publication at Journal of Neuroscience (IF=5.3). The current output is slightly above the proposed output as the publication appeared in a higher impact factor journal (i.e. Cell Reports, IF=8.8). Important decisions often involves choosing between complex environments that determine future item encounters. However, environment choice has been largely overlooked in previous studies, which primarily concentrate on object choice. In this study, we aim to address this gap by examining the role of the lateral frontopolar cortex (FPl) in environment choice, contrasting it with the ventromedial prefrontal cortex's involvement in item choice. Additionally, we propose a mechanism through which the FPl decomposes and represents complex environments during the decision-making process. To investigate this, we trained a convolutional neural network (CNN) optimized for choice and compared its predicted activation with the actual activity observed in the FPl. Our findings demonstrate that the FPl's high-dimensional activity breaks down environment features to effectively represent the complexity of the environment, enabling informed choices. Furthermore, we discovered functional connectivity between the FPl and the posterior cingulate cortex, suggesting the FPl's role in guiding environment choice. Further examination of the FPl's computation revealed a parallel processing mechanism that extracts multiple environment features simultaneously.

15600619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15600619.value: This research has inspired a new research idea that investigate the role of frontopolar cortex in complex decision making. I have written a research proposal about this new idea to seek support by the Collaborative Research Fund in 2023.

15600619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600619.value: Important decisions often involve choosing between different complex environments that will determine the actual choices that we will encounter in the future. However, decision neuroscience research has focused extensively on the choices we make about specific items, without considering the larger environment in which those choices are made. In this study, we wanted to understand how our brain makes decisions about which environment to choose. We found that a specific part of the brain, the lateral frontopolar cortex (FPl), is involved in this process. We used artificial intelligence to simulate how the brain might make these decisions, and compared these simulations with actual brain activity in the FPl. We discovered that the FPl breaks down the features of different environments to help us understand their complexity and make a choice. We also found that the FPl is connected to another part of the brain called the posterior cingulate cortex, which helps guide our decisions about which environment to choose. Our study suggests that the FPl uses a parallel processing mechanism to extract multiple features from the environment simultaneously.

15600919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15600919.value: Textile and apparel archaeology is an indispensable facet of Chinese history and archaeology, and is an important part of world history. Nevertheless, textile relics are perishable materials that are extremely fragile and decay rapidly after excavation. Their degradation is triggered by physical, chemical, and biological mechanisms. The cost of maintenance to simulate ideal conditions for the relics is exceedingly high and current technology does not support prompt preservation. These hinder the transport, storage and exhibition of the valuable textile relics and thus adversely affect the publicity and research on the inheritance of relics conservation. Current digital technologies are not able to monitor various conditions of the relics precisely due to the particularity of the textile relics. Textiles relics are soft, fragile, multi-layered and consist of a mixed composition of different materials. This therefore increases the complexity of textile relics conservation. Also, sensors for monitoring temperature and humidity are placed in the exhibition area rather than directly on the relics, which cannot check the environmental change during moving. Current monitoring also pays less attention to vibration and pressure. Thus, a more flexible sensor is needed. It should be “integrated” with the relics to “sense” the temperature, humidity and other relevant factors to minimize harm. This study aims to integrate organic electronics, wearable textiles technology, and traditional silkscreen conservation to prepare smart flexible fabric-based organic monitoring systems with mesh-like multi-data sensing and collection points. The technical features of wearable technology, like high flexibility, high level of diversification in structure, multi-point data collection etc., help to develop a protect cover to monitor the threating factors, like temperature, humidity, strain, light and pH value. The proposed system is case-sensitive to each relic, flexible and small in nature, and can be applied directly. The research methodology is divided into four segments: (1) study and establishment of degradation of various textile materials; (2) architecture of the flexible monitoring sensors for different uses; (3) development of the integrated system for textile relics, and; (4) testing and evaluation of the newly developed systems. It is expected that the newly developed system can acts a daily monitoring solution to achieve a real-time and prolonged control of various degradation mechanisms. It will result in a breakthrough in wearable technology, relics protection and create an innovative form of textile archaeology. This eventually helps to arouse the public attention, promote public participation in historical construction and promote future research. 紡織服裝考古學是中國歷史和考古學不可或缺的一個方面，是世界歷史的重要組成部分。然而，紡織品是易腐爛的材料，極其脆弱，在挖掘後迅速腐爛，它們的降解是由物理，化學和生物機制引發的。模擬文物理想條件的維護成本非常高，目前的技術不支持及時保存。這些都阻礙了珍貴紡織品的運輸，儲存和展示，從而對文物的宣傳和研究產生了不利影響。由於紡織品的特殊性，當前的數字技術無法精確地監控文物的各種條件。紡織品文物柔軟，易碎，多層，由不同材料的混合成分組成，這增加了紡織品文物保護的複雜性。此外，用於監測溫度和濕度的傳感器放置在展覽區域而不是直接放置在文物上，這不能檢查移動過程中的環境變化，而且對振動和壓力的監測也較少。因此，紡織品文物維護需要更靈活的傳感器，它應該與文物“整合”，以“感知”溫度，濕度和其他相關因素，以盡量減少傷害。 本研究旨在整合有機電子，可穿戴紡織品技術和傳統的絲網保護，以實現基於網狀的多數據傳感和採集點的監測系統。可穿戴技術的技術特點，如高靈活性，高水平的結構多樣化，多點數據採集等，有助於開發保護罩來監測溫度，濕度，應變，光照和pH值等威脅因素。研究內容分為四個部分：（1）研究和建立各種紡織材料的降解; （2）用於不同用途的柔性監測傳感器的結構設計; （3）發展紡織品綜合監控系統; （4）測試和評估新開發的系統。 預計新開發的系統可以對文物日常監測，實現對各種退化機制的實時和長期控制。它將在可穿戴技術，文物保護方面取得突破，並創造出一種創新的紡織考古學方法。這最終有助於引起公眾的關注，促進公眾參與歷史建設和未來的研究。

15600919.label: Realisation of objectives
15600919.value: Objective 1: To identify the mechanism of the degradation of various materials and investigate the relationship between textile materials and different risk factors, thereby control the ageing process. The primary threats in the preservation of textile artifacts are examined and summarized: The factors to consider are pH levels, microbial strain, moisture levels, temperature, and exposure to ultraviolet radiation. They have the ability to modify the chemical composition on a molecular level, alter the formation of oxidative components, affect the crystallinity and molecular weight, leading to modifications in macroscopic properties like brightness and mechanical characteristics. The findings have been published in the Journal of Historical Archaeology & Anthropological Sciences under the title "A review of silk ageing: mechanism and stimulation methods." Objective 2: To design and fabricate flexible organic monitoring sensors that form mesh-like multi-data collection points for historical textile relics to provide an alternative and integrated solution and realize a comprehensive conservation method with a high level of real-time operation and accuracy. A textile-based thermocouple temperature sensor is designed and synthesized using an industrial and technological weaving process, resulting in a flexible construction. An investigation was conducted on the viable configuration of conductive textile materials in the warp and weft directions with respect to their thermoelectric conductivity. In addition, the correlation between conductivity and bending flexibility was examined across various temperature ranges. The findings have been published in the Textile Research Journal under the title "Structural Development of a Flexible Textile-based Thermocouple Temperature Sensor." Furthermore, the pH, strain, humidity, temperature, and UV light sensing fibers have been effectively manufactured and incorporated into an integrated electrochemical fabric, forming a sensing textile. This textile material possesses exceptional flexibility and a wide range of structural variations, enabling it to establish close contact with artifacts and accurately monitor their various conditions. The findings have been published in the Advanced Functional Materials under the title "A Flexible Smart Monitoring System for the Preservation of Textile Relics." Objective 3: To achieve flawless and harmless mounting and consolidating methods with the newly developed flexible sensing based on organic semiconductors. The incorporation of the textile-based thermocouple temperature sensor into garments could provide a real-time, comfortable, skin-friendly, and flexible system for sensing body temperature. The textile-based temperature sensor's adaptability is expected to drive the manufacturing of medical garments and sportswear that enable unrestricted movement while monitoring body temperature. The newly developed flexible smart system is designed to provide flawless and harmless mounting and consolidating methods. The textile artifact can be rolled up like a scroll, allowing for convenient storage and transportation, eliminating the need for it to be kept flat. The current state of the textile artifact can be readily accessed on the auxiliary monitor of the scroll. The results have been published in the scientific journal Advanced Functional Materials with the title "A Flexible Smart Monitoring System for the Preservation of Textile Relics", and a patent has been granted in China under the name "An article holding device".

15600919.label: Major findings and research outcome
15600919.value: This study aims to enhance the importance of valuable textile artifacts by creating a novel monitoring and conservation system using flexible monitoring sensors made from fibers. The goal is to achieve comprehensive and precise supervision. There are three main research outcomes. The preservation of textile artifacts involves examining and summarizing the primary threats, which include pH levels, microbial strain, moisture levels, temperature, and exposure to ultraviolet radiation. The research results have been published in the Journal of Historical Archaeology & Anthropological Sciences with the title "A review of silk ageing: mechanism and stimulation methods." (Part C - 8 - 1). Furthermore, textile-based sensors for measuring pH, strain, humidity, temperature, and UV light are created and produced using an advanced weaving process commonly used in industry and technology. This process yields a flexible structure. This textile material exhibits remarkable pliability and a diverse array of structural modifications, allowing it to establish intimate contact with artifacts and precisely monitor their various conditions. The results have been published in the Advanced Functional Materials journal, with the title "A Flexible Smart Monitoring System for the Preservation of Textile Relics" (Part C - 8 - 3), and in the Textile Research Journal, with the title "Structural Development of a Flexible Textile-based Thermocouple Temperature Sensor." (Part C - 8 - 2) Moreover, the recently created adaptable intelligent system is engineered to offer impeccable and safe methods for installation and reinforcement. The textile artifact can be rolled up, similar to a scroll, for easy storage and transportation, eliminating the requirement for it to be kept in a flat position. The present condition of the textile artifact can be easily viewed on the secondary display of the scroll. The findings have been officially released in the esteemed scientific publication Advanced Functional Materials, under the title "A Flexible Smart Monitoring System for the Preservation of Textile Relics" (Part C - 8 - 3). Additionally, a patent has been successfully obtained in China for an invention called "An article holding device" (Part C - 11 - 2). The newly developed system serves as a daily monitoring solution to achieve real-time and long-term control of various degradation mechanisms. It leads to a significant advancement in wearable technology, preservation of artifacts, and the development of a novel approach to textile archaeology.

15600919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15600919.value: The study's success resulted in a significant advancement in the preservation of relics. This system, which is an innovative approach to textile archaeology, is not restricted to textile artifacts. It also has the potential to be applied in safeguarding historical paintings, calligraphy, and other cultural artifacts. This development offers significant advantages to the conservation of textile relics that necessitate ongoing monitoring by introducing a novel type of relic equipment and manufacturing a versatile "protective cover". Additionally, it expedites the advancement of smart textile technology for the preservation of relics. Furthermore, the flexible textile sensors can be utilized in various domains apart from archaeology. These technologies can be utilized in various sectors such as medicine, healthcare, and sports. Textile sensors have the capability to be incorporated into our garments and track individuals' health conditions. This study holds immense potential across various domains and will yield substantial benefits for a wide range of individuals.

15600919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15600919.value: Textile and apparel archaeology is crucial for Chinese and global history. However, fragile, expensive, and complex materials make preservation difficult. Current technology struggles to monitor relic conditions, and a flexible sensor is needed to integrate with relics for optimal preservation. Thus, this study develops smart flexible fabric-based organic monitoring systems using organic electronics, wearable textiles technology, and traditional silkscreen conservation. The system uses mesh-like multi-data sensing and collection points to monitor various factors like temperature, humidity, strain, light, and pH value. The system is case-sensitive to each relic, flexible, and small, and can be applied directly. The research methodology includes studying degradation of various textile materials, designing flexible monitoring sensors for different uses, developing an integrated system for textile relics, and testing and evaluating the systems. The system is able to provide real-time and prolonged control of degradation mechanisms, a breakthrough in wearable technology, relics protection, and an innovative form of textile archaeology. This also help to attract public attention, promote participation in historical construction, and promote future research.

15601019.value: 長期以來人們一直關注話語形式，功能和使用如何隨時間而變化。然而，各種研究越時語言學或歷時語言學的方法普遍面臨著與以下條件相關的問題 i）以明確和可複制的方式將時間（度量法）與話語變量聯繫起來； ii）在較短的時間範圍內處理偏自發的話語背景中的複雜變化模式；iii）將變化分析限制為少量時間間隔，而不考慮它們之間可能的相互依賴性或自相關性。 此研究應用並評估如何以時間序列分析方法（TSA）解決這些問題並開發新的話語概念.TSA方法廣泛用於金融和工程領域，以了解自然發生的變量如股票價格等關鍵成分（趨勢，季節） ，週期和不規則波動）和自相關結構。該資訊用於建立合適的時間序列模型，揭示連續觀測如何相互關聯，並根據歷史值預測未來值。 此研究將 ⅰ）顯示跨越背景和時間尺度的話語現象的頻率（例如心理療法會話中的隱喻，報紙中的主題關鍵詞或社交媒體中的代詞）類似於規範時間序列，因此可以使用TSA方法進行分析；ii）將Box-Jenkins TSA方法應用於多個話語數據庫，並批判性地評估模型與數據的匹配程度；iii）以能夠利用和豐富話語內容和結構的定性分析的方式解釋模型，以及 iv）使用時間序列模型類型作為分類的基礎來開發新的話語類型。 此研究通過在過往社會科學實證中建立而不同於話語分析的方法來提升話語分析方法論，並直接反映上述方法論的問題。它還通過將定量建模與話語的定性解釋相結合，並為將來的研究目的開發歷時話語類型的創新分類，從而做出理論貢獻。此特定的話語數據集將涵蓋一系列背景（例如心理療法，課堂話語，報紙話語，政治演講，社交媒體）和現象（例如隱喻，代詞，非信息標記，主題關鍵詞，修辭問題）以進行分析，從而進一步反映各領域的具體問題。

15601019.label: Realisation of objectives
15601019.value: The four objectives have been fully achieved as detailed below. Objective 1: To apply and critically evaluate Time Series Analysis methods for time-based discourse research A series of studies have comprehensively demonstrated the applicability and limitations of the Box-Jenkins Time Series methodology for discourse analysis in descriptive and critical contexts alike. The importance of model evaluation via statistical methods like in and out-of-sample predictive accuracy and model fit measures has been emphasized. The technical details and procedures involved in time series analysis have been imparted in a series of pedagogically-oriented publications. Objective 2: To model discourse phenomena across representative contexts and time scales using Box-Jenkins time series methodology Discourse phenomena ranging from interactional stance markers to pronouns and metaphors have been modeled in contexts including social media, psychotherapy, press conferences, political speeches, and news articles. The time scales likewise range from days to years. ARIMA models of contrasting natures have been found to fit these phenomena, and critically interpreted in their respective contexts. Objective 3: To theorize time series models as representations of discourse structure across time The main theoretical construct of discourse ‘modelability across time’ has been advanced. It is claimed that a modelable (i.e., non-random) discourse time series is interpretable as a structural signature of the underlying phenomenon across time. The various context-specific instantiations of this construct include identity construction on YouTube, interactional strategies in psychotherapy, as well as the subtle construction of ideological messages in newspapers, press conferences, and political speeches. Importantly, the need to relate discourse modelability with the (un)predictability of its underpinning background social reality has been emphasized. Objective 4: To develop a typology of discourse structures across time based on time series model types As mentioned above, the range of differently ordered ARIMA models (e.g., AR(1), AR(2), MA(1), ARMA(1,1)) that were found to fit various discourse phenomena has been theorized as a typology of structural signatures. In that way, different discourse phenomena have been found to share subtle and underexplored commonalities based on the mathematical descriptions of their common model. For example, an autoregressive model of order 1 (AR(1)) implies a directional momentum of the discourse phenomenon at hand that lasts up to one interval, which is construed as a discourse strategy of ‘short-term momentum’ in different settings.

15601019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15601019.value: The major outcome is the proposal and demonstration of the construct of ‘modelability’, where a time series model for a particular discourse time series is interpreted as a structural signature of the underlying phenomenon across time. This has been further theorized at two levels, collectively addressing the four project objectives. The first level is the general level of whether an ARIMA model could be found to fit some discourse time series, which may imply strategic discourse construction across time that dovetails with theoretical assumptions in critical discourse research. Pedagogical work that teaches how to conduct time series analysis are also relevant here. Publications emphasizing this level include: Qiu, H., & Tay, D. (2022). The second level specifically interprets each ARIMA model (i.e., order, coefficients, parameters, and variables), supported by close contextual analysis, with respect to the discourse objectives at hand. Nuanced quantitative analysis at this level is critical in developing a typology of time series models, and substantiating the claims made at the previous level. Comparative studies of ARIMA with other methods for discourse analysis have also been made. Relevant publications include: Tay, D. (2021). 15601019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15601019.value: The research project has opened new and ongoing collaborative pathways with researchers in other relevant fields like translation and NLP. The following are specific courses of further action for further development of the research: 1. Comparing the modelability of discourse phenomena in original and translated texts across time, and interpreting the results with respect to relevant theoretical notions in translation studies. 2. Combining ARIMA time series analysis with NLP methods, for example using time series features as inputs to different regression and classification algorithms for natural language. 3. At the time of project reporting, a monograph is being written to advance the use of data analytics (including time series analysis) and programming languages for discourse research. This also fulfills the important pedagogical objective of imparting important programming skills to the next generation of researchers, which aligns with a central goal of the PI's institution.

15601019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15601019.value: Language use in social contexts like media, politics, and even healthcare may seem spontaneous and creative, yet it is quite possible that difficult-to-detect patterns exist across time. For example, a YouTuber or therapist may repeat some linguistic behaviors from past videos or sessions, but this repetition tends to not go beyond a certain number of time intervals. Why is this the case, and to what extent are such patterns strategic in different settings? This project investigates language features across social contexts and time scales, by applying a statistical methodology for time series analysis known as the Box-Jenkins method. While typically used in more quantitative fields like finance and engineering, the project demonstrates that i) linguistic patterns across time can also be captured by this method, ii) linguistic behavior in many cases is almost as predictable and forecast-able as non-linguistic phenomena like sales figures, and iii) the models that describe these patterns deepen our understanding of the structural and strategic aspects of language used to fulfill social purposes. This project also led to the development of educational initiatives like data analytic and programming courses for language and humanities students, broadening their skill sets for future careers in the digital economy.

15602419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15602419.value: 背景： 針對婦女的親密伴侶暴力（IPV）對婦女和其照料下的兒童的健康構成威脅。最近的研究表明，IPV可能與較短的成人端粒長度（telomere length TL）相關，TL是衰老和疾病的生物標誌。 然而，文獻對IPV與兒童TL縮短率之間的關係知之甚少，特別是在幼兒發展期。與此同時，IPV與兒童虐待和忽視（child abuse and neglect CAN）已經證明有關，這種不良經歷也可能導致兒童TL縮短的速度。 因此，有必要進行縱向研究，以探討IPV，CAN和TL縮短的關係。 研究目標： 這項研究將探討IPV對婦女，CAN和兒童TL縮短率之間的關聯。具體而言，本研究將（a）檢查分娩前母親的IPV（IPV before birth）是否與幼兒發展期（大約3歲）兒童的TL縮短率相關（TL shortening age 3）; （b）檢查從出生到幼兒期（大約3歲）母親的IPV (IPV age 0-3）是否對 IPV before birth和TL shortening age 3之間的關聯有調節作用; （c）檢查從出生到幼兒期的CAN（CAN age 0-3）是否與TL shortening age 3相關。 研究方法： 這項研究將是對出生隊列的一項後續研究，該隊列包括2017年從香港廣華醫院招募的774名懷孕的婦女和新生兒。在基線研究期間，測量了母親在出生前的IPV經歷，收集新生兒臍帶血樣本進行TL分析。在這項基線研究後約3年的這項研究中，將聯繫母親進行IPV age 0-3，CAN age 0-3，家庭社會經濟狀況和兒童健康相關生活質量的隨訪調查。研究將使用口腔拭子收集兒童（大約3歲）的DNA樣本，以便計算TL shortening age 3。 貢獻： 本研究將加強對婦女IPV的生物後果的有限知識做出重大貢獻。它將為促進兒童健康和預防針對婦女的IPV提供支持性證據。

15602419.label: Major findings and research outcome
15602419.value: The findings are rich. Here below is an abstract of one part of the outputs. The aims of this meta-analysis were to examine the association between childhood exposure to family violence and telomere length and the moderating variables that influence this association. Relevant works published on or before 1st September 2022 were identified through a search in five major databases in English and 19 articles (N = 18,977) finally met the inclusion criteria. A meta-analysis was conducted to compute the pooled effect size (correlation; r), and moderator analyses were performed using a random effects meta-analytic model. The studies yielded a significant inverse association between childhood exposure to family violence and telomere length, with a small effect size (r = -0.038, 95% CI [-0.070, -0.005], p = 0.025). Furthermore, the strength of this association was stronger in studies examining the co-occurrence of multiple types of violence than in those examining just one type (Q = 8.143, p = 0.004). These findings suggested that victims’ telomere length may be negatively influenced by childhood exposure to family violence and that such impairment appears to be stronger for those who are exposed to multiple types of violence. Future studies are necessary to examine the moderating and mediating factors underlying the association between childhood exposure to family violence and telomere length. Another important finding is the development of a new conceptualization of IPV against mothers before pregnancy, during pregnancy, and after childbirth. We categorized pregnant women into four groups, including women with (a) sustaining abusive relationship (AR); (b) relationship with decreased violence over pregnancy (DVR); (c) relationship with stress-related violence (SVR); and (d) nonviolent relationship (NVR). Although we found an overall decline of IPV during pregnancy from 24.6% to 14.3%, there were still a considerable proportion of women reporting as a victim of IPV. We observed that a higher proportion of pregnant women were actually suffering from IPV during pregnancy and after childbirth continuously (22.3% of AR and SVR) than experiencing a termination of IPV due to pregnancy (11.4% of DVR). We also observed that more severe maternal depression, lower levels of father’s involvement, and poorer social support were significantly associated with the categories that reflected greater severity of IPV over the course of pregnancy. Our findings reflected that the complexity of IPV related to pregnancy should never be overlooked. Mere reporting of prevalence in an aggregate might not sufficiently explain the problem. Father’s involvement and social support are two important factors that might help reduce IPV related to pregnancy and childbirth.

15602419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15602419.value: Longitudinal studies are scarce, future research on childhood exposure to family violence and health should include well-designed longitudinal studies from diverse cultural backgrounds to further confirm the current findings. Furthermore, because the relationship between co-occurring types of childhood exposure to family violence and TL was found to be stronger than that between TL and a single type of violence, future studies should focus on the added negative impacts of family polyvictimization. To complete the picture, future studies should look closely at the mediating role of TL in the relationship between co-occurring childhood exposure to family violence and health-related consequences. Additional research is also needed on other potential moderators (e.g., gender) and mediators of the association between childhood exposure to family violence and TL.

15602419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15602419.value: The study has developed a new conceptualization of IPV against mothers before pregnancy, during pregnancy, and after childbirth. Individual differences in IPV across years after childbirth have been identified. Women in the VR group had poorer health conditions than those in the NVR group. Given that there are different categories of IPV from pregnancy to the postpartum years, we suggest future studies explore specific interventions and services for each category. Continuous clinical screening for violence during prenatal and postnatal care is needed. More attention should be paid to those who report IPV during pregnancy, as it is at high risk of recurring years after childbirth. When IPV is detected, timely and effective programs should be applied. A review of the effectiveness of interventions for IPV around the time of pregnancy found a significant decrease in IPV when applying home visitation programs and some multifaceted counseling interventions. More family support and partner involvement could protect women from IPV experiences. Family-based counseling has great strengths in reducing various types of violence against women by increasing couples’ awareness and improving their relationships during pregnancy.

15602619.label: Project Objectives
15602619.value: The primary objective of this proposal is to develop an integrated model for estimating solar energy potential over complex 3D infrastructures in dense high-rise cities by taking Hong Kong as a testing-bed case. The secondary objectives are: - To develop a systematic 3D GIS model to estimate solar energy on both building facades and rooftops, considering inclusively the shadowing effects and the multiple reflections of solar radiation. - To determine building surface materials and reflectivity of 3D building structures using Deep Learning, via the GIS database. - To map hourly cloud cover, cloud shadow, and aerosol optical thickness over entire Hong Kong using geostationary satellite images, where the derived images will feed into the GIS system for solar potential estimation. - To demonstrate solar energy potential of a dense high-rise city, including the variation of PV potential from each model component, i.e. building surface materials, multiple reflectances, cloud and air transmissivity.

15602619.value: 人類活動所產生的碳排放在過去二十年間日益增加，導致全球氣候模式逐漸改變，並引致極端天氣頻繁出現。大部分國家都訂立了減排目標和方針，推廣使用可再生能源取代傳統發電方法，務求盡快減少碳排放。由於香港的二氧化碳排放有百分之六十九源於發電，因此香港政府最近推行「上網電價」計劃，鼓勵市民利用太陽能發電，希望降低整體碳排放水平。本項目將會展示在香港這高樓林立、土地狹小的城市，太陽能光伏技術的應用，以及估算全港的三維太陽能光伏潛力。 基於項目團隊以往估算屋頂太陽能光伏潛力的經驗，我們將於此項目開發一套用於估計建築物外牆和屋頂太陽能光伏潛力的三維模型。這模型除了會考慮建築物的四周環境條件外，更會考慮雲層和大氣的影響。首先，此模型將會計算太陽輻射在屋頂、建築物外牆和地面間的多重反射作用。其次，我們將收集街景圖像、高精度傾斜航空影像和實地測量數據，利用深度學習算法來進行建築外牆材料的分類。第三，此模型將通過地球同步衛星影像來估算每小時的雲量和空氣污染水平。最後，我們將會進行實地驗證，以保證綜合模型的準確性。 這項研究將論證在有限的土地空間內達到更高光伏潛力的可行性，並填補這方面的研究不足，尤其是在亞洲區高層建築物密集型城市的應用。在香港政府發佈的「香港氣候行動藍圖2030+」中，香港的太陽能發電量會在2030年佔總發電量約1%至1.5%，我們預料研究結果將會提高太陽能發電的採用率，輔助政府拓展目標，並會產生其他間接的社會經濟和環境成果。

15603419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603419.value: Nowadays, more children are wearing face-related products, including face masks and eyewear. Face masks are becoming a daily necessity in some heavily polluted regions. Protective eyewear for sports and new designs for advanced technology, such as virtual reality (VR), is becoming increasingly popular and seems to be the future trend. Such devices demand a high level of fit and comfort to achieve good performance, ensure eye protection and provide entertainment for an extended time. A three-dimensional (3D) human shape can enable product development with high fitting requirements. Although, it is possible to customise the product based on an individual 3D body scan, many products must still be designed and manufactured for the larger population due to cost and target user limitations, such as usage in hospitals, cinemas or public systems. A considerable amount of research on 3D human anthropometry for designing products exists, but there is a lack of research on 3D face shape features and growth, especially for children. It is extremely important to consider children’s face changes when considering innovative developments in current and future products. In the proposed study, a 3D face model for Chinese children will be developed for face-related product design using several techniques. First, we will collect a complete range of data of the Chinese children population. This data will find applications in many areas, including product design and anatomy. A 3D model of the face shape and allometric variations in terms of size and shape will be calculated. An analysis of the differences between gender and age groups will also be carried out for face growth and then for sizing system development. An eyewear example based on different fitting requirements will be tested, and subjective evaluation information will be collected. The knowledge of the 3D shape and the results of the evaluation will be integrated to create the face templates. Using the developed template, designers and industry professionals will be able to design face-related products in an easier and more standardised manner. The output of the proposed study could potentially be applied in many industries, such as the eyewear, the respirator design and the medicine. Manufacturers will know size range to provide customers, and designers may design better styles and shapes for various groups by using age and gender information. Further, the abovementioned database and the knowledge of 3D shape variation and classification could be used in face recognition systems and growth evaluation. 越來越多的兒童開始佩戴面部產品，包括口罩和眼鏡。在一些汙染嚴重的地區，口罩是每天的必需品。運動型防護眼鏡和虛擬現實等先進技術正日益流行，並成為未來的趨勢。這些設備均需要高水平的舒適度，以便長時間地保持良好性能、提供對眼睛的保護及達到娛樂效果。三維人體模型能夠使產品開發滿足高舒適度的要求。雖然可以根據個人的三維人體掃描模型來為用戶定制產品，但由於成本和目標用戶的限制，許多產品仍然必須考慮為更多的人群設計和制造，如醫院、電影院或公共系統中的使用。雖然目前基於三維人體測量的產品設計研究有很多，但是對於三維兒童面部的形態特征和生長方面的研究卻很少。因此，在當前和未來產品的創新發展時期，考慮兒童的面部模型是極其重要的。 本研究將應用多種技術為中國兒童開發一套用於面部相關產品設計的三維面部模型。首先，我們將收集足夠完整的中國兒童面部數據。這些數據可在許多領域得到應用，包括產品設計和解剖學。三維模型的面部形狀和尺寸方面的生長變化會被分析。面部基於性別和年齡的生長差異會被進一步研究，並用於調整尺寸系統。根據不同的配戴要求，將以眼鏡為例測試用戶的主觀評估信息。上述三維模型及用戶評估的結果將用以整合創建新的面部模型。根據本研究開發的模板，設計師和專業人士將能夠用更簡單和標準化的方式來設計面部相關產品。 本研究成果可應用在諸多行業，如眼鏡設計、面罩設計和醫療行業。制造商能根據尺寸範圍更好地服務客戶，而設計師可以為不同年齡性別的客戶群體設計更好的產品。此外，上述數據庫及三維形狀變化和分類的信息還可用於人臉識別系統和生長評估。

15603619.label: Project Objectives
