15603619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15603619.value: Storytelling has long been recognized as a driving force for many games that successfully engage players with meaningful gameplay and narrative experience. To players, some story-based games are more impactful than some others are. Many of these purposefully designed games aspire to use their game stories to influence players’ thoughts, feelings and behaviours, by casting the player in a character role in the story and letting her face certain circumstances that need to be resolved. In this case, only when a player takes up her character’s perspective – not only perceptually but psychologically, can she feel for her character and act for the character accordingly with meaningful choices and actions. To achieve this, it is of great importance to understand how perspective is constructed for the game narrative and implemented for the player’s perception during the procedural presentation of the game world. This research aims to examine a series of single-player, story-based video games where perspective is strategically designed and implemented to influence players. We will demonstrate that perspective in story-based games is much more than the viewpoint a player assumes in a graphically represented game world. Instead, it is a designed complex that affects players’ narrative experience through a range of medium specific design constructs, such as the camera viewpoint, gameplay control scheme, the narrator’s position, to name a few preliminarily. The primary goal of this project is to develop a conceptual model and taxonomy of the concept narrative perspective in the context of story-based video games. We will conduct structural textual analyses of six strategically chosen game titles, each analysis envisioned to capture a set of instances of how narrative perspective is created in the game through composing together various design constructs. Taken together, the case analyses will attempt to develop a model of narrative perspective, which discerns main constructs for perspective, in the form of a taxonomy, as well as describes common styles (or variables) used for each construct in story-based games. The result of this project will contribute to the theories of game studies and interactive narrative by adding perspective as an important dimension to the methods of formal game analysis. The outcome will also shed light on the ways to design games that require a high-level capacity of perspective taking, which is of particular relevancy to serious or purposeful game design that is hinged on the player’s perception, or even empathy, towards the characters and game world. 遊戲敘事長期以來一直被認為是促成許多遊戲成功成功吸引玩家的要素 。對於玩家而言，一些基於故事的遊戲比其他遊戲更有力。很多遊戲的設計都有針對性地都=通過讓玩家扮演故事中的角色，並讓她面對一些特定的處境來影響玩家的思想，感受和行為 。在這種情況下，只有當一個玩家不僅在感知上而且在心理上接受她角色的視角時，她才能夠對她的角色感同身受，並通過有意義的選擇和行動相應地為角色行事。為了實現這一點，理解如何為遊戲敘事構建視角以及在遊戲世界裡玩家怎樣感知到這個視角極為重要。 這項研究旨在研究一系列基於故事的單人電子遊戲如何由策略地構建視角以影響玩家。我們將展示基於故事的遊戲中的視角設計遠遠不止於玩家在遊戲世界中的視點設定 。 它是一個設計複雜體，通過一系列遊戲媒體中特有的設計結構體 （例如鏡頭視角、遊戲控制方案、敘述者的位置等等）來影響玩家的敘事體驗。該項目的主要目標是以基於故事的遊戲為背景來建造一個“敘事視角”的概念模型以及分類法。我們將對六款精心挑選的遊戲進行結構性文本分析，每個分析都試圖捕捉一系列如何在遊戲中通過不同設計結構體的組合方式來創建敘事視角的具體實例。我們將這些案例分析匯總歸納以後，會開發出一個敘事視角模型，以分類的形式識別視角的主要構造體，並描述每個結構體在具體運用中的常見風格。 該項目的主要成果是將視角作為一個重要維度添加到遊戲形式分析的方法學中，為遊戲研究和互動敘事理論做出貢獻。其研究的結果還將揭示怎樣設計對觀點採擇能力要求較高的遊戲。由於嚴肅或有目的的遊戲成功與否取決於玩家對角色的感知、甚至是對角色和遊戲世界的同理心，該研究揭示的視角構建方法對嚴肅遊戲的設計研究尤其相關。

15603619.label: Realisation of objectives
15603619.value: We have achieved all objectives laid out in the original proposal. For the first objective, after an extensive literature review of narrative perspective discussion in classic and transmedial narratologies as well as game studies, we built a preliminary conceptual model that was largely drawing on Jan-Noel Thon’s model (“Perspective in contemporary computer games”, 2009) and other similar taxonomies. The preliminary model looks at game narrative perspective from three dimensions or types: spatial, actional, and ideological perspectives. To start the game analysis phase, we first conducted an initial investigation of 12 story-based games through a high-level structural analysis. Based on the representativeness and uniqueness of the games’ camera positionings and narrative situations as well as players’ ability to switch perspectives, we narrowed down the game list to a carefully selected collection of six game cases including: Ghost of Tsushima (Sucker Punch, 2020), Detroit: Become Human (Quantic Dream, 2019), Red Dead Redemption 2 (Rockstar, 2019), A Way Out (Hazelight, 2018), What Remains of Edith Finch (Giant Sparrow, 2017), and Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons (Starbreeze, 2013). We then performed an in-depth textual analysis of the six games, paying attention to spatial, actional, and ideological aspects as well as any notable design styles that influence players’ in-game perspective. For the second objective, we synthesized the findings of the textual analysis. The result greatly challenged our preliminary model, which treats varied parameters or dimensions - space, ideology, action - equally yet separately. Grouping findings into those three aspects made the analysis inconclusive on how players perceive or form a perspective and consequently enact that perspective. We found our initial taxonomical method limited the understanding of how narrative perspective is constructed interactively and procedurally between a game and its players. Interpreting what we observed in the games, we found that (1) the positionings between the camera (i.e., the focalizer), the control point, and the narrator (i.e., the voice-over) create very different subjective effects on players and (2) the environment design (e.g., the attitude of non-player characters) and characterization (e.g., with or without inner thoughts) both help shape the ideological view of the game storyworld. We therefore propose a new conceptual model for narrative perspective in games prioritizing ideology as a higher order or a defining construct of narrative perspective, through which other parameters work together to form and shape the perspective(s) conveyed by the game and/or carried by the player. In the new ideology centric model, the lower level of constructs can be classified into three groups: (1) Voice and vision – the structural set-up of narrative situation including narrator (who speaks), focalizer (who sees), the player-character(s), non-player-character(s), as well as their relational positions, often determined by the style of focalization; (2) System ideology, as manifested and/or constrained by both game rules and mechanics and narrative motifs; and (3) The relationship between the player and the gameworld - either via the player-character as the mediator or not, as formed procedurally and reciprocally between the player’s performance of gameplay and the game system’s responses. For the third objective and with the new conceptual model, we were able to regroup our game analysis findings and uncover the intricacies of how, while navigating and interacting with the gameworld, a player can have her own take of the happenings and make choices within the freedom given by the game system. Through our analysis and synthesis, we are able to contribute to the fields of game studies and interactive narrative by uncovering a variety of perspective structures and design styles. For example, our analysis of the two games Ghost of Tsushima and Red Dead Redemption 2 revealed a unique built-in ideological structure, which consists of two opposing ideologies for players to navigate in between while playing the games. This comparative analysis was published by ACM in the Proceedings of Foundations of Digital Games conference (Wei and Leung, 2021; see Part C-8.1). Additionally in a recently completed manuscript to be submitted to a journal, we have also identified – through the analysis of four other games – varied focalization methods that contribute to the construction of one or more perspectives in game narratives (see Part C-8.2). For the final two objectives, our analyses have also identified an array of techniques and motifs used to influence players’ perception of the story or their decision making (Part C-8.1), which can inform future game design that aspires to shape players’ perspective (during and post game). In particular, our aforementioned manuscript (Part C-8.2) delves deeper into how varied ways of focalization were set up to influence how players perceive and enact a perspective. Within the scope of this project, we have collected a preliminary set of perspective styles with detailed in- game examples and our own analysts’ annotations about possible effects on players. Common patterns are ready to be organized into design profiles as inputs to future studies.

15603619.label: Major findings and research outcome
15603619.value: The outcome of this short-term, small-scale research project contributes to the fields of game studies and digital interactive narrative with a theoretical model that helps deepen the formal understanding of how perspective is constructed for the game narrative and performed by the player during their procedural gameplay. The main findings from our game analyses raise two challenges to the current understanding of perspective in games in related fields. First, we found that different types of perspectives in a game - spatial/visual, actional/control, and ideological - identified by previous research do not contribute to the construction of a game’s narrative perspective equally on the same plane. Our findings show that both visual and actional parameters together with other game elements contribute to the construction of a variety of ideologies in games. It is through these ideologies that players comprehend the gameworld, form their judgment, and perform their actions accordingly. This insight was explicated through two ideology-centric case analyses in our FDG paper (Part C-8.1). Second, our findings defied one of our assumptions - formed after our literature review - that character engagement could be a pivotal aspect determining a player's perspective as performed in the gameplay and under the influence of in-game portrait of characters' views. Rather, we identified a range of constructs characterizing game narrative perspective in our model building process, of which players' engagement with their characters does not play a pivotal role in quite many games. Among the range, for example, the focalization (i.e., through which character's eyes does the player see the gameworld) structure and style can be a crucial factor influencing players' comprehension of the narrative and performance of their gameplay. Detailed findings in this regard are being reported in our manuscript attached to this report (Part C-8.2). In summary, the main research outcome of this project is a proposed conceptual model of narrative perspective in games, together with an analytical account of common and exemplar styles and structures used for varied perspective constructs as identified in our game analysis.

15603619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15603619.value: In the next stage of this line of research, our agenda will seek to observe various effects on players through empirical player studies and establish the connections between these effects and certain perspective constructs and design styles. For example, what would be the different effects on players when the game solely uses the player-character to perceive the gameworld and tell the story (i.e., internal focalization), as opposed to when the game presents every character equally from a god's point of view where the player does not have privileged knowledge of the player-character (i.e., external focalization)? These connections can further facilitate the construction of hypotheses for player experiments that aim to discover low-level design parameters and principles for creating intended effects - emotion, cognitive, or learning - in future purposeful game design.

15603619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15603619.value: Story-based video games are an exemplary medium for audiences to first-handedly experience stories and storyworlds. Stylized video games provide rich characters with personalities, abilities, goals and mental models, as well as a highly responsive gameworld to contextualize the characters, events, and happenings. To feel a cognitive or emotional impact of a game story, it is crucial for the player to take up a certain perspective - not just visually but mentally - in order to perceive and understand the happenings of the gameworld. Our research showed that this perspective taking is influenced by many factors existing in the game design. Through textual analysis of a range of story-based games, we have uncovered some of these factors and built a conceptual model of narrative perspective in games. The model identifies the high-level constructs that form narrative perspective as a designed complex. These constructs can help understand how certain design techniques and styles might influence players' perception and comprehension of the game narrative and their actions and behaviours in the gameworld.

15605219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605219.value: The rise of single-parent families has become a social issue in global and local contexts. The absence of a husband and concurrent poverty create vulnerabilities to single-mother families. During the adaptation process, a restructuring of family patterns is needed, which involves the modification of household responsibilities and renegotiation of the family relationship. Adolescent children usually take up more instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities in the family, with instrumental responsibilities referring to the fulfillment of household chores and daily caregiving for the siblings, while emotional responsibilities denoting the support for the emotional needs of family members. From the family systems perspective, child parentification is regarded as a clinical phenomenon when children perform parental caregiving roles that leads to role reversal between parents and children. Research shows that parentification is linked to adolescent pathologies such as depression, excessive guilt and social withdrawal. However, the social identity theory argues that filial responsibility is a devotion to the family and connection with family members, which is important in Chinese societies where familism, interdependence and filial piety are stressed. Cross-cultural studies show that different cultures lead to varied impact of filial responsibilities on adolescent psychosocial outcomes, with adolescents from collectivist communities (e.g., Chinese, Hispanic) reporting more positive outcomes (less distress, better parent-child relationship, better academic performance) than those from individualist-oriented communities (e.g., European American). Besides, adolescents demonstrated better psychosocial competencies (e.g., sense of responsibility, self-efficacy, social competence) through caregiving. However, there is a lack of studies using family ecological perspectives to examine the impact of adolescent filial responsibilities on parent-child relationship, maternal wellbeing and child psychosocial outcomes, and their interrelationship. Against this background, we propose a three-wave longitudinal study employing a family process model of resiliency to examine the influence of adolescent filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescent psychosocial competence in a sample of 560 mother-adolescent dyads of poor single-mother families in Hong Kong. The mediational roles of mother-child relationship and moderating effects of adolescent gender, maternal warmth and perceived fairness will also be examined. The study will provide evidence on the possible impact of adolescent filial responsibility from a family ecological perspective, which sheds new light on addressing filial responsibility as a protective versus risk factor during the family adaptation process in Chinese single-mother families. Moreover, the study addresses whether adolescents are an active agent in the family process, which is important for building family process model and informing social work practice.

15605219.label: Realisation of objectives
15605219.value: Focus of the Research: Single motherhood, coupled with poverty, creates vulnerabilities for single-mother families. During the adaptation process, adolescent children often assume greater instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities. Instrumental responsibilities pertain to household chores and daily caregiving for siblings, while emotional responsibilities involve providing support to meet the emotional needs of family members. This research was a three-wave longitudinal study employing a family process model of resilience to examine the influence of adolescent filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescents' positive development among impoverished single-mother families in Hong Kong. The study also explored the mediating roles of the mother-child relationship and the moderating effects of adolescent gender, maternal warmth, and perceived fairness. Challenges in Identifying Target Respondents and Data Collection During the Pandemic: The research project commenced on 1 January 2020, coinciding with the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic. We encountered significant challenges in recruiting respondent families and collecting data. During the first nine months of 2020, Hong Kong experienced the first, second, and third waves of the COVID-19 pandemic. Social distancing measures, remote online learning, school closures, and the suspension of community services and facilities, coupled with fears of infection and financial insecurity, severely impacted the functioning of Hong Kong families, particularly those who were underprivileged. The research was delayed until September 2020, when the situation slightly improved. We expanded our collaborative network and successfully enlisted 19 social service centres from six NGOs and The Hong Kong Single Parent Association to participate in the research. We also offered an online survey option, allowing target respondents to complete the questionnaire at home. Training was provided to social workers from the collaborating organisations. Unfortunately, the fourth wave of the COVID-19 pandemic, which lasted nearly six months, posed further difficulties in recruiting target families. Despite offering online survey options, many economically disadvantaged single mothers found it challenging to complete the survey online. Social workers mailed the questionnaires to their homes and provided instructions via phone calls. Ultimately, we received 325 sets of questionnaires (from both mothers and adolescents) from poor single-mother families in September 2021 (Time 1) through the considerable efforts of the collaborating organisations. The pandemic continued to disrupt the data collection process at subsequent time points. The fifth wave of the COVID-19 pandemic was particularly severe, infecting millions of people in Hong Kong. We suspended data collection for five months. When the situation improved in July 2022, we resumed data collection and invited NGOs to re-establish contact with the families at Time 2. However, some families chose to withdraw from the study due to the ongoing instability of the pandemic. Data collection for Time 3 was relatively smooth compared to previous time points. As the pandemic stabilised, trained social workers and research assistants engaged respondent families to conduct data collection between January and October 2023. Attrition of Target Respondents: Apart from the pandemic, we faced challenges related to high turnover among social workers and a shortage of manpower to assist with the research. Five social service centres encountered difficulties in assisting with data collection at Times 2 and 3 due to staff turnover, manpower shortages, and loss of contact with participating families. Furthermore, the prevalence of telephone scams made respondents sceptical about providing information to our research assistant, resulting in additional withdrawals. To mitigate attrition, we increased the value of supermarket coupons as compensation for respondent families and engaged them intensively. We collected 260 sets of questionnaires from respondent families at Time 2, with an attrition rate of 20%. Ultimately, we collected 231 sets of questionnaires from respondent families at Time 3, resulting in a total attrition rate of 28.9%. Attrition analyses of targeted families were conducted. Logistic regression analyses assessed whether demographic characteristics and studied variables at Time 1 (T1) were associated with sample attrition (dropout = 0, retention = 1). Results indicated that families with older adolescents were more likely to drop out of the study. However, the associations of all studied variables at T1 with sample retention were non-significant, suggesting a random dropout of respondents. Achievements of the Objectives: The objectives were generally achieved. For Objective 1, results from the cross-sectional study at T1 indicated that adolescents' instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities were positively related to positive developmental outcomes. We further examined the relationships among maternal distress, filial responsibilities, and adolescent well-being among poor single-mother families. Results indicated that instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities moderated the associations between maternal distress and adolescent well-being. A journal paper was published to disseminate these findings. However, path analysis did not show significant predictions of instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescent positive developmental outcomes over time. For Objective 2, results from the cross-sectional study at T1 indicated that the mother-child relationship mediated the associations between adolescents' emotional filial responsibilities and maternal distress and adolescents' positive developmental outcomes. For longitudinal effects, path analysis did not support the mediational effects of the mother-child relationship over time. However, results from cross-lagged model analyses identified a reversed indirect path, where prior maternal distress negatively predicted subsequent mother-child relationships, further affecting adolescents' emotional filial responsibilities. For Objective 3, results from the cross-sectional study at T1 indicated that adolescent-perceived unfairness weakened the negative relationship between adolescents' emotional filial responsibilities and maternal distress. Moreover, maternal warmth strengthened the relationship between adolescents' instrumental filial responsibilities and positive developmental outcomes. We also examined the relationships among filial responsibilities, maternal warmth, and adolescent well-being. Results indicated that maternal warmth strengthened the relationship between instrumental filial responsibilities and adolescent life satisfaction for boys but not for girls. Additionally, maternal warmth altered the relationship between emotional filial responsibilities and adolescent anxiety for older adolescents. An oral presentation was delivered at an international conference, and a journal paper was published to disseminate these findings. Merits of the Study: The study addresses research gaps by examining the influence of adolescent filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescent psychosocial competence among poor single-mother families in Hong Kong. There are several merits. First, the study focused on economically disadvantaged single-mother families, which are under-researched in social science literature. Second, in family literature, studies examining children's roles and contributions to their families are rare. Kuczynski (2003) argued that parents and children should be equally regarded as important agents in family processes. In this research, adolescents were regarded as 'active contributors' to single-mother families. Third, there are conflicting views on whether filial responsibility impairs or benefits adolescent development. The findings of this research clarify the associations between adolescents' instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities, maternal distress, and adolescent developmental outcomes in poor single-mother families, as well as the mechanisms through the parent-child relationship and the moderating roles of perceived unfairness and maternal warmth. Fourth, data were collected from both mothers and adolescents within the family, providing a comprehensive picture of family dynamics within single-mother families. Limitations of the Study: The study was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. Additionally, the sample size is small due to difficulties in identifying target respondents and collecting data during the pandemic, although it is comparable to or even larger than previous related studies (East et al., 2009; Jurkovic et al., 2005; Kuperminc et al., 2013; Walsh et al., 2006).

15605219.label: Major findings and research outcome
15605219.value: Using cross-sectional data from Time 1, we examined the associations of adolescents' instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities with positive developmental outcomes and maternal distress in poor single-mother families. While adolescents' instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities were positively related to positive developmental outcomes, they were not associated with maternal distress. Furthermore, the mother-child relationship mediated the associations of adolescents' emotional filial responsibilities and adolescents' positive developmental outcomes. Regarding the moderating roles of adolescents' perceived unfairness and maternal warmth, it was found that perceived unfairness weakened the negative relationship between adolescents' emotional filial responsibilities and maternal distress, whereas maternal warmth strengthened the relationship between adolescents' instrumental filial responsibilities and positive developmental outcomes. We further explored the relationships among filial responsibilities, maternal warmth, and adolescent well-being. The results showed that adolescents' instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities were positively associated with life satisfaction and negatively associated with depression. Additionally, maternal warmth strengthened the relationship between instrumental filial responsibilities and life satisfaction for boys, but not for girls, and also between emotional filial responsibilities and life satisfaction. Moreover, maternal warmth altered the relationship between emotional filial responsibilities and anxiety in older adolescents. These findings were presented at an international conference and published in a journal paper. We also investigated the relationships among maternal distress, filial responsibilities, and adolescent well-being in poor single-mother families. The results indicated that instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities acted as moderators, influencing the associations between maternal distress and adolescent well-being. Notably, adolescent girls with greater emotional filial responsibility reported higher anxiety than those with less responsibility when their mothers exhibited more distress. In contrast, the relationship between maternal distress and anxiety remained stable in boys, regardless of the level of emotional filial responsibility they assumed. This suggests that parentification is likely to occur in adolescent girls in poor Chinese single-mother families. These findings were also published in a journal paper. For longitudinal effects, path analysis did not reveal any significant predictions of instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities on maternal distress or adolescent positive developmental outcomes over time. Nor did it support the mediating role of the mother-child relationship in predicting the effects of instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescent positive developmental outcomes over time. However, cross-lagged model analyses identified a reversed indirect path, where prior maternal distress negatively predicted subsequent mother-child relationships, which in turn affected adolescents' emotional filial responsibilities.

15605219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15605219.value: This study addresses research gaps by examining the influence of adolescent filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescent psychosocial competence among impoverished single-mother families in Hong Kong. While the study found that instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities were positively associated with adolescent positive development concurrently, these relationships were not significant over time. However, it identified that perceived unfairness and maternal warmth might alter the influence of filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescents' positive developmental outcomes. Furthermore, the findings indicated that prior maternal distress could diminish adolescents’ emotional filial responsibilities by fostering a poor mother-child relationship. Therefore, there is a need to design family intervention programmes for economically disadvantaged single-mother families to enhance maternal well-being, effective mother-adolescent communication, and maternal warmth during their adaptation process to single motherhood and concurrent poverty. As the study was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic, the influence of adolescent filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescent psychosocial competence among poor single-mother families might differ under normal circumstances. Additionally, the duration of single motherhood and the age of children experiencing single-motherhood may also contribute to the family adaptation process, warranting further research. Hence, there is a need to replicate the study after the pandemic.

15605219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15605219.value: Single motherhood, coupled with poverty, creates vulnerabilities for single-mother families. During the adaptation process, adolescent children often assume greater instrumental filial responsibilities, such as fulfilling household chores, and emotional filial responsibilities, which involve meeting the emotional needs of family members. This research was a three-wave longitudinal study employing a family process model to examine the influence of adolescent filial responsibilities on maternal distress and adolescent developmental outcomes among impoverished single-mother families in Hong Kong. The mediating roles of mother-child relationship and moderating effects of maternal warmth and perceived fairness were also examined. The findings showed support that instrumental and emotional filial responsibilities are positively related to adolescents' positive development, with the mother-child relationship mediating the relationship between emotional filial responsibilities and adolescents' developmental outcomes concurrently. However, these effects became non-significant over time. Additionally, adolescent-perceived unfairness and maternal warmth altered the associations of filial responsibilities with adolescents' developmental outcomes and maternal distress. Furthermore, prior maternal distress negatively predicted subsequent mother-child relationships, which in turn affected adolescents' emotional filial responsibilities. These findings provide valuable insights for family scholars and social workers to better understand the mother-adolescent dynamics within poor single-mother families and to offer appropriate services for them.

15605519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15605519.value: A core function of elections is representation. Although Hong Kong is not a full-fledged democracy, elections have long played an important role in representing the voices of the local population. Since 2016, however, some voices in society have been systematically excluded from the electoral process due to various reasons. Given the recent surging popularity of the localist camp in Hong Kong, the unprecedented decisions of the government to bar a number of localist political parties/individuals from running for elections would have potentially far-reaching electoral impacts. How do citizens view the government’s decisions and the electoral system? How will the supporters of the excluded parties react? Will they abstain from voting because they feel they not being represented or would they vote for less preferred alternatives? On the other hand, how will voters who support other political camps or who have no clear political orientation view these events? Will they see the ban as an unfair practice? These are substantively important questions that will shed light on the trajectory of Hong Kong’s political development in years to come. In this proposed study, we seek answers to the above questions by studying Hong Kong citizens’ voting behavior in the upcoming elections: the 2019 District Council Election and the 2020 Legislative Council Election. Since these elections span different levels of government, collecting public opinion data across both levels is necessary for gaining a more comprehensive understanding of voting behavior in Hong Kong. Collecting such survey data involves many challenges, including low response rates, possible sample biases, and insincere responses. No single solution exists to solve all these potential problems (Weisberg, 2005). Nevertheless, social media, together with new advances in machine learning, provide researchers with powerful and cost-effective tools to tackle these issues. Our team will utilize social media and machine-learning techniques to improve the quality of the data collected from conventional survey modes in this study. Our research team has a strong track record in conducting such election surveys. Three years ago, the team launched the Hong Kong Election Study (HKES). The HKES, which was initially funded by a GRF (Ref. No.: 14615915), is a multi-wave election study. We successfully collected six waves of public opinion data from four local elections, and produced various publications based on these data. Most importantly, these data provide a basis for comparison, so that we can measure the changes in local public opinion over time. 選舉的核心功能是代表民意。雖然香港不是一個充份民主的政體，但選舉長期以來在代表當地民意方面發揮了重要作用。然而，自2016年以來，由於各種原因，社會上的一些聲音被系統地排除在選舉過程之外。鑑於近期香港的本土主義陣營越來越受歡迎，政府做了一個前所未有的決定：禁止一些本土主義政黨/個人參選。這決定可能會產生深遠的選舉影響。 公民如何看待政府的決定和選舉制度？被排斥方的支持者將如何反應？他們會否索性不投票，因為他們認為沒有人代表自己？還是他們會投票給次優的選擇？另一方面，支持其他政治陣營或沒有明確政治傾向的選民會如何看待這些事件？他們會認為這項禁令是不公平的做法嗎？這些是政治上重要的問題，將揭示香港未來幾年政治發展的軌跡。 在這項研究中，我們通過研究香港市民在即將舉行的選舉中的投票行為來尋求上述問題的答案：2019年區議會選舉和2020年立法會選舉。由於這些選舉涉及不同級別的政府，因此需要收集兩個層面的民意數據，以便更全面地了解香港人的投票行為。 收集此類調查數據涉及許多挑戰，包括低回應率，樣本偏差和虛假的答案。沒有單一的解決方案來解決所有這些潛在的問題（Weisberg，2005）。然而，社交媒體以及機器學習的新進展為研究人員提供了解決這些問題的工具，而這工具既強大且具有成本效益。我們的團隊將利用社交媒體和機器學習技術，來提高從傳統調查模式收集得來的數據之質量。 我們的研究團隊在進行此類選舉調查方面有著良好的記錄。三年前，該團隊啟動了香港選舉研究（HKES）。 HKES最初由GRF資助（參考編號：14615915），是一項多頻選舉研究。我們成功地從四次地方選舉中收集了六波輿論數據，並根據這些數據製作了各種出版物。最重要的是，這些數據為比較提供了基礎，因此我們可以衡量當地公眾輿論隨時間的變化。

15605519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15605519.value: It is of paramount importance to continue the studies of elections in Hong Kong for two reasons. The first is that Hong Kong has experienced a drastic change of its electoral institutions. Hong Kong voters' behaviors under the new electoral institutions are poorly understood. Second, Hong Kong is experiencing a drastic change of its population composition. The change of the electorate demands a systematic analysis of its impact on electoral behaviors.

15605519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15605519.value: A research project focused on the electoral behaviors of Hong Kong people holds immense significance, especially in the context of the city's recent demographic and political changes. With the backdrop of the 2019 pro-democracy protests and the implementation of the National Security Law, understanding voting turnout and preference in Hong Kong has never been more timely. The project aims to shed light on how these pivotal events have influenced the electorate and their choices at the polls. It holds the potential to provide valuable insights into the evolving political landscape, the impact of government policies, and the shifting priorities and concerns of Hong Kong citizens. By offering a solid foundation for future studies, this research project not only aids in comprehending the present but also in shaping the future of Hong Kong's electoral dynamics and democratic engagement.

15606119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15606119.value: Language is made possible in the brain by exaptation, in which existing neurobiological systems supporting specific cognitive functions are recruited to subserve language functions. Because the medial temporal lobe (MTL) memory system, especially the hippocampus, is important for initial storage of recently encountered events (episodic encoding) and their subsequent transformation into long-term episodic/declarative memory (memory consolidation), the MTL likely plays a central role in learning words for both first language (L1) and second language (L2). However, there has been surprisingly few empirical works on its role in L2 learning. Instead, many studies reported that L2 learning success is determined by regions that support working memory, e.g., inferior parietal lobe (IPL). It is unclear whether the lack of control in phonological awareness towards L2 in previous works has contributed to the emphasis of IPL over MTL. In addition, older adults are under-represented in L2 research. However, they are generally known to utilize different brain networks than younger adults, casting further doubts regarding the exact brain network that subserves L2 learning across the population. This project investigates how ageing affects the functional connections of the MTL during L2 (Italian) learning. Older and younger native Cantonese adults who have little exposure to Italian and pass a test of phonological awareness in both languages will be recruited. They will learn hundreds of L2 short phrases during a four-week L2 vocabulary learning programme. In addition, subjects will attend a pre-learning MRI session such that how the brain measures at the earliest phase of learning determine learning success can be investigated. The lexical consolidation process of newly learnt words will be tracked by event-related potentials (ERPs) at regular intervals, and by a post-learning MRI session, in which subjects will revise recently learnt L2 words or learn new L2 words. There are three primary hypotheses: (1) the individual variations in L2 learning success are strongly associated with the task-related functional connectivity between the hippocampus and other regions (e.g., IPL and ATL), (2) the relative roles of working memory and semantic memory in learning words are different across age; and (3) the lexical consolidation process is faster and more complete for younger than older adults. These hypotheses will be tested by network-based dynamic causal modelling and standard voxel-wise statistical parametric mapping for fMRI data, and by conventional ERP analysis. Collectively, our findings will clarify the functional connections of MTL structures that strongly contribute to L2 learning success during adulthood. 語言是一個非常複雜的行為，需要各個神經生理系統支援不同的語言功能。由於內側顳葉（MTL）的記憶系統，尤其是海馬體，掌管情節編碼（即儲存剛遇到的事件）以及記憶鞏固（將其轉化為長期情節／陳述性記憶），所以 MTL 很可能在第一語言（L1）及第二語言（L2）詞語學習上尤其重要。然而，有關 MTL 在L2學習中的作用的實證研究卻很少。相反，許多研究指出L2學習的成功率取決於支援工作記憶的區域，例如下頂葉（IPL）。 目前我們尚未清楚對下頂葉的這種重視是否因為之前的研究並沒有控制參加者的L2語音意識（phonological awareness）。此外，L2的文獻缺乏以老年人為對象的研究。然而，我們已知道老年人會利用與年輕人不同的大腦網絡。這進一步令我們對 L2 學習的確切大腦網絡產生疑問。 本研究旨在了解老化在學習 L2（意大利語）的過程中如何影響 MTL 的功能連結。我們會招募年老和年輕的廣東話母語者。他們需通過這兩種語言的語音意識測試，但不能有太多接觸意大利語的經驗。參加者將在為期四週的L2詞彙學習計劃中學習數百個L2短語。此外，參加者將會在計劃前參加一節磁力共振影像掃描（MRI），以便了解在最早期學習階段中的哪些大腦指標與學習的成功率特別有關。至於新學習單詞的詞彙鞏固過程，則會以事件相關電位（ERPs）定期追踪。研究共有三個主要假設：（一）L2學習成功率的個體差異與海馬體和其他區域（如IPL和ATL）之間的任務相關功能連結有密切的關係;（二）工作記憶及語義記憶於學習單詞的作用在不同年齡段是不同的;（三）年輕人的詞彙鞏固過程比老年人更快更完整。這些假設會透過動態因果建模（DCM）和標準體素統計參數圖（SPM），以及傳統的事件相關電位分析，來多方面進行驗證。總括而言，我們的研究結果將闡明內側顳葉結構中有哪些功能連結對成年期間學習 L2 特別重要。

15606119.label: Realisation of objectives
15606119.value: The medial temporal lobe, especially the hippocampus, is critical for memory formation and consolidation, as emphasized in the complementary learning systems theory (McClelland et al., 1995). In the language domain, its role in foreign language learning (FLL) has also been highlighted, e.g., in Declarative–Procedural model (Ullman, 2001, 2004), but the evidence has remained scarce. In particular, it is plausible that long-term declarative memory would be recruited to a larger extent during FLL in older than younger learners by virtue of the lifelong growth in crystallized knowledge, but this hypothesis had yet to be tested. The present project aimed to fill these gaps and examined the role of medial temporal lobe and declarative memory in FLL. Italian was chosen as the target language, mainly due to its high grapheme-phoneme correspondence and its use of the Latin alphabet. Two phases of investigation (PHASE I & II) were undertaken. In PHASE I (Months 1-18), we focused on how the surface-based morphological features of the brain such as cortical thickness are associated with FLL performance. A total of 25 older and 8 younger learners were recruited in the first phase, with the completion rate being 84% and 100%, respectively. Each learner attended a 1.5-hour introductory Italian lesson, followed by an MRI session. Each learner was then enrolled to a five-week intensive Italian programme that comprised two learning components: (1) ten intensive computerized vocabulary learning lessons, and (2) four revision sessions, for tracking the process of lexical consolidation. Although these sessions focused on vocabulary building, basic grammatical components and rules (e.g., article, gender, present tense, adjectives) were also taught. A 1.5-hour Italian final test was administered post-learning. Phonological tests on Cantonese, English, and Italian, as well as a neuropsychological test battery comprising six standard cognitive tests were administered pre- and post-learning. In PHASE II (Months 19-42), the study protocols were fine-tuned with two notable changes: (1) fMRI data were collected both pre- and post- learning; (2) a phonology lesson on Cantonese and English was given prior to all Italian learning components. Taking advantage of the affordable rate of the then new MRI facility (managed by University Research Facility of Behavioral and Systems Neuroscience, UBSN, HKPolyU), an independent cohort of 33 younger learners (YL), 34 older learners (OL), and 23 older controls (OC) was recruited. The completion rates were 69.7%, 70.6%, and 78.3%, respectively. Results achieved: Regarding Objective 1 (To identify the functional connections of the hippocampus that subserve the immediate learning success and lexical consolidation of L2 words in adulthood), we found that the old words, which had already been acquired, elicited stronger activation in the left precuneus (X=-12, Y=-66, Z=30) and left calcarine fissure (X=-12, Y = -70, Z=20), while new words, which were being learnt for the first time inside the scanner, differentially activated the left parahippocampal gyrus (X=-36, Y=-26, Z=-20) and right middle cingulate gyrus (X=4, Y=30, Z=36). This main effect of OLDNEW interacted with RUN (run 1/2) at a more medial portion of the parahippocampal gyrus (X=-16, Y=-22, Z=-18), due to the growing difference between the old and new words in the second run. Our results underlined the lexical consolidation function of the hippocampus, showing that new words are actively maintained in the hippocampus during vocabulary learning. They provided new empirical support for the CLS theory and the DP model, both of which predicted a prominent role of the medial temporal lobe in FLL. Regarding Objective 2 (To examine the age-related differences in the relative role of working memory and semantic memory in studying L2 words), in Phase I of the project, we found that in older learners, the immediate learning and post-learning dictation score were best predicted by the delayed recall. In contrast, while immediate learning scores were similarly best predicted by delayed recall in younger controls, the post-learning dictation score was most strongly associated with English phonological awareness. These findings are consistent with our hypothesis that episodic memory could play a more crucial role than phonological processes in FLL in older adult learners. In Phase II of the project, the language learners were given a 1.5-hr phonology lesson prior to all Italian learning components, such that the participants would have better phonological awareness towards both their native language (L1) and English (L2). Because of this pedagogical improvement across the two phases, we found that phonological awareness became a much more prominent predictor of the vocabulary learning performance in older adults in Phase II. Nonetheless, the roles of episodic and semantic memory towards vocabulary learning had remained highly significant. For Objective 3 (To investigate the L2 lexical consolidation process, especially with respect to the age-related differences in the initial consolidation rate and the extent of long-term memory consolidation), it was originally hypothesized that younger and older learners would show distinct trajectories of learning, with the former group showing larger improvement over time, in terms of learning new words and retaining old words. However, there were no age-related difference in the rates of long-term consolidation of old words and immediate learning success of new words. In fact, older learners were as good or even better than the younger learners in most accuracy measures of Italian learning performance. Objective 4 (To explicate the intrinsic neural factors (grey matter volume, cortical thickness and functional connectivity) that underlie the brain’s readiness to learn and retain L2 words in both younger and older adults) was investigated by analyzing how the neural factors predict translation performance during in-class quizzes and final test. Using anatomical measurements and a cognitive test battery, we examined the hypothesis that older adults may engage semantic and episodic memory functions than other cognitive functions traditionally considered the most important for FLL (e.g., working memory capacity and phonological awareness). At the cortical level, in older learners, the immediate learning success of vocabulary was most strongly associated with the morphological features of the left pars orbitalis (χ2=79.54, df=20, p<.001), while the long-term memory retention was most strongly associated with the right entorhinal cortex (χ2=48.06, df=16, p=.001), which is known to be important for memory formation. Convergent evidence was also found based on the pattern of cognitive associations. At the subcortical level, the sub-cortical volumes of both the left and right thalami were a significant predictor of the L2 vocabulary maintenance in older adults (left: χ2=14.09, df=4, p=.036; right: χ2=13.54, df=4, p=.036; FDR-corrected). Our results are consistent with a prominent role of declarative memory functions in vocabulary learning in older learners. The analysis was reported in an article in Frontiers in Human Neuroscience (Fong et al., 2022). Regarding Objective 5 (To determine the efficacies of a four-week L2 vocabulary learning programme in enhancing cognition, especially in older adults), the pre–post comparisons revealed significant improvements in a range of cognitive domains, including episodic memory (verbal list learning test), semantic retrieval (picture naming), and matrix reasoning (Raven’s SPM). However, no interaction between Group (YL/OL/OC) and PrePost (pre/post) was found. The result suggested that the L2 vocabulary learning programme could potentially lead to cognitive enhancement, but due to the absence of the Group by PrePost interaction, it could not be determined whether such longitudinal cognitive improvements presented primarily training effects or genuine learning-induced gains.

15606119.label: Major findings and research outcome
15606119.value: At the time of the report, two journal articles were published based on the data collected in the present project (in Frontiers in Human Neuroscience and Languages), along with 8 conference abstracts/presentations in international conferences and a local conference (PolyU Academy for Interdisciplinary Research Conference 2023). In particular, based on the data collected in PHASE I, we obtained new empirical support for the recruitment of episodic and semantic memory in foreign language learning (Fong et al., 2022). Based on the data collected in PHASE II, we have obtained a novel finding about the role of the parahippocampal gyrus in lexical consolidation. Currently, two manuscripts are being prepared to publish the results arising from PHASE II (as highlighted in Section 5.3 and above); they will be submitted to Q1 international journals for publication within the next year. This delay was mainly because of the pandemic and that an MRI machine was available for use only in the middle of the project. The project team has made the best use of the invaluable opportunity offered by this project, to obtain longitudinal neuroimaging data from both the learner groups and the control group. These included diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) data, which were collected both pre- and post-learning. The preliminary result based on DWI, regarding the association of vocabulary and grammar learning outcomes with three white matter structures (corpus callosum, arcuate fasciculus, and uncinate fasciculus), has been submitted to the Society for the Neurobiology of Language 16th Annual Meeting (October 24-26, 2024, Brisbane, Australia). The findings will also be written up for journal publications in due course. Another research related to second language learning has also been conducted. Specifically, code-switching is a common habit of life-long bilinguals. Previous research suggested that the comprehension of switching in language was cognitively taxing because it required the listener/reader to jump from one mental lexicon to another in order to process the words. However, our study found that prolonged reading time was only found in non-habitual use of code-switching. This finding adds to the knowledge on the organisation of mental lexicon, and eventually, on how learning a new language would affect it. The finding of this experiment was initially reported in the International Symposium of Bilingualism and later published in Languages (Hui et al., 2022).

15606119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15606119.value: The present research will be extended along three tracks. Firstly, upon further detailed analysis, the team will focus in disseminating the research findings as a series of publications in Q1 journals. In particular, we will prioritize to publish the novel findings about the roles of the hippocampus in lexical consolidation during foreign language learning. Apart from that, benefitted from the additional acquisition of diffusion MRI data in the present phase, a follow-up paper will incorporate the findings of both the structural and diffusion MRI data, to give a comprehensive account on the anatomical correlates of foreign language learning. Secondly, having established two education-matched younger and older beginners of Italian, the team now is now pushing forward the investigation on the longer-term neurocognitive changes of language learning. A follow-up research project based on an Italian booster programme was thus proposed and it has been funded by Departmental GRF. Thirdly, another project funded by the Faculty of Humanities, HKPolyU, focusing on artificial language learning, has been kickstarted. Although this research will zoom in on the linguistic functions of the cerebellum, it will further shed light on the role of medial temporal lobe in language learning.

15606119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15606119.value: The medial temporal lobe, especially the hippocampus, is well-known for its role in formation of declarative memory, including both episodic and semantic memory. Surprisingly, the empirical evidence supporting its critical role in foreign language learning (FLL) has remained scarce. Indeed, phonological awareness, roughly our ability to discriminate sounds of a language, as well as phonological short-term memory, have usually been considered the most important predictors of foreign language learning success, rather than our episodic memory functions. However, it is plausible that older adults would especially recruit declarative memory in learning a new language, to take advantage of their crystallized knowledge accumulated over their lives. The present project aimed to evaluate the roles of medial temporal lobe and declarative memory functions in learning a foreign language (Italian), especially in older adults. Results revealed that the anatomical measures of brain regions implicated episodic and semantic memory functions act as a consistent predictor of learning success in older adults, with pattern of cognitive association as convergent evidence. In addition, functional magnetic resonance imaging showed that the parahippocampal gyrus is especially active during the acquisition of new vocabularies. Our results support various prominent accounts of language learning, including the complementary learning systems theory.

15607419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15607419.value: 財政非集中化是中國改革開放後強大經濟增長的重要成因。這安排鼓勵地方政府競爭及吸引外資。城市經濟增長也成為中央評核地方總書記工作表現的指標。因為土地拍賣能創造地方經濟增長，并使地方政府獲得可用作公共財政的資金，所以地方官員有誘因去增加土地收入。 文獻中有關土地財政對城市發展的研究不少，但對有關官員進行土地拍賣的方式（招拍掛）卻甚少着墨。有關招拍掛的研究也只圍繞着土地拍賣價格，拍賣土地後的税收相對未受學者重視。此外，中央政府政策、地方官員晉升、城市間的競爭及居民福祗等因素令情況更複雜。 此研究旨在調查一）地方官員在土地拍賣的決定和二）有關決定對地方税收及經濟增長的關係。它不但能提供一個理論模型去了解内地城市土地拍賣的情況，並能協助評估地方執行中央政府政策、審核現有評核地方總書記工作表現的制度、及對不同政策範疇提供建議。

15607419.label: Realisation of objectives
15607419.value: This research proposed two different objectives, as the following: -To identify local Chinese officials’ auction type selection in land conveyance with respect to i) the Central Government’s national and regional policy directions; ii) competition from adjacent provinces/cities (in terms of economic growth); iii) the city leadership’s (i.e. party secretaries’) own career considerations; and iv) the welfare of local residents; and -To evaluate the relationship between the degree of government intervention in the land market and i) various aspects of cities’ public finance (i.e. land price and taxation) and ii) economic growth For the first objective, as the choice of whether land parcels, which was found by different Chinese scholars to affect land price, should have been leased via auction or Guapai itself could be subject to other factors (as suggested under the first objective), the research team (see Hui et al., 2023) deployed a treatment effect model for the study of land prices rather than evaluating the land conveyance decisions in separate models as originally proposed. The findings did reveal that factors relating to local government leadership (such as age, his/her existing tenure as city party secretary, and his/her tenure as a Communist Party member), economic conditions and national policies alike played significant roles in dictating these decisions, even though the impacts of these factors differed across different cities. Meanwhile, the second objective, in general, has been addressed, in that a number of studies were conducted to evaluate the impact of government intervention in the land market, through the use of Guapai rather than auctions as a means of land conveyance, on land price, taxation such as land appreciation tax (LAT), corporate income tax (CIT), and value-added tax (VAT), economic development in terms of per capita government expenditure (and the welfare of local residents in terms of per capita educational expenditure), average wage levels, and a city’s employed workforce. Nevertheless, it should be noted that, due to the non-availability of city-level data on tax revenue, the study on the tax implications of government intervention in the land market was conducted on the provincial level, whereas the study on the impact of land conveyance on economic development was conducted on a city-level.

15607419.label: Major findings and research outcome
15607419.value: With reference to the proposed objectives for this research, several studies have been undertaken to explore how land conveyance, in particular local government’s decision-making in this regard, influenced a variety of aspects, from land price, odds of winning for specific enterprises in land auctions, to tax revenue and the welfare of local residents. First, deploying endogenous treatment effect models, it was revealed that land conveyance decisions in Beijing were highly subject to national policies and the status of its City Party Secretary, but not in Shanghai (Hui et al., 2023). Also, the use of Guapai resulted in higher residential and commercial land prices in Shanghai, but lower prices for Beijing’s commercial land parcels. The findings indicate that Beijing, due to its closer proximity to the Central Government, appears to have stringently followed the national policy directions, whereas land officials in Shanghai seem to have had a higher degree of autonomy in their decisions. Additionally, the contrasting price effect of Guapai on land prices for residential and commercial land parcels enabled Beijing’s government to compensate for the latent losses in land revenue when leasing residential land parcels, due to Nation #10, by leasing commercial parcels at higher prices via tender. From a macro perspective, the research team, in two separate studies, explored the relationship between the degree of government intervention in the land market on i) land appreciation tax (LAT), corporate income tax (CIT), and value-added tax (VAT) and ii) local government expenditure for educational per person. The investigation on tax revenue revealed that, on a provincial-level, a 1% increase in the amount of land transacted under Guapai (i.e. a higher degree of government intervention in the land market) generated lower CIT (by 0.4%) and VAT (by 1.5%). This indicated that local leaders’ career aspirations are prioritized over local residents’ welfare, local government finance, as well as the central government’s revenue. The other study on education expenditure, the major findings were that, a more prevalent use of Guapai in land leasing was negatively associated not only with average wage levels and a city’s employed workforce, but also with per capita government spending in general and on education-related programmes. At best, the findings indicate that the attempt to attract investment via lower land prices did not necessarily improve the society. At worst, they alluded to the preference of local leaderships’ career interests to local residents’ welfare under the cadre evaluation system.

15607419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15607419.value: The study, as it was originally proposed, focused primarily on the level of local government intervention in the land market through the use of Guapai in land conveyance, rather than auction. The need for further infrastructure development to boost local economies, in the aftermath of the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, gave rise to the prominence of Local Government Financing Vehicles as well as the accumulation of debt on an unprecedented scale. As a result, two additional papers have been composed to explore two specific elements in this regard, namely 1) whether local governments honoured the “implicit” guarantee for debts issued by LGFVs (and the impact of their decisions on urban land leasing and land expropriation) and 2) the land bidding behaviours of LGFVs. In addition, another potential for further development of the research concerns how local governments, within the context of land financing, valued state interests and local interests upon the announcement of new national policies.

15607419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15607419.value: This research studies the conditions under which local officials interfere in a city’s land market through the use of Guapai over auctions, as well as to explore the impact of government’s land market intervention not only on land price at parcel-level, but also on various aspects of local taxation and economic growth. The study is significant, in that it provides a new theoretical framework which offers valuable insights regarding China’s land conveyance which helps predict and forecast the decision-making behaviours of city land bureau officials (and the implications of government intervention for local finance), with respect to the interplay between local governments and the Central Government, and between the city leadership’s career prospects and the welfare of local residents. They will also be instrumental in assessment of national/regional policy implementation at the city-level, in the review of the existing GDP-oriented system which evaluates the performance of city leadership, and in proffering policy implications relating to possible conflicts between local governments and the Central Government due to fiscal decentralization, preservation of local residents’ welfare and protection of rural villagers’ rights.

15610019.label: Project Title(Chinese)
15610019.value: 無人和自動商船責任和保險法律問題研究

15610019.label: Project Objectives
15610019.value: To review the legal and regulatory framework for unmanned/autonomous shipping at both national/domestic and international levels; To identify potential liability issues in relation to unmanned/autonomous ships, especially in relation to liable parties, the basis of liability, and others; To examine insurance issues that are likely to emerge as a result of the operation and navigation of unmanned/autonomous ships, particularly in relation to third-party liability insurance arising from factual and legal uncertainties surrounding unmanned/autonomous shipping; To conduct legal empirical studies to reveal the relevant industries’ perspectives on the liability and insurance issues; Based upon both theoretical and empirical studies, to develop recommendations for any legal amendments for achieving the safe and secure operation of unmanned/autonomous merchant ships.

Based upon both theoretical and empirical studies, to develop recommendations for any legal amendments for achieving the safe and secure operation of unmanned/autonomous merchant ships.

15610019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15610019.value: The unmanned/autonomous merchant ship is no longer a futuristic idea—prototypes are expected to be in service in the foreseeable future. On the one hand, unmanned/autonomous merchant ships may reduce or eliminate risks caused by human faults during a marine adventure, thus enhancing navigational safety. On the other hand, they will require changes in shipping practice, leading to new liabilities and risks. Marine insurance, the oldest of the many forms of protection against losses, traditionally provides cover against losses or liabilities incidental to marine adventure. There are increasing discussions about the legal challenges that these technological developments may introduce. Some believe that a broad interpretation of certain definitions, coupled with several necessary amendments to major international conventions, will be sufficient to address the problems. Others consider that since unmanned/autonomous merchant ships may constitute a radical departure from the existing regime, a different approach is necessary. Amongst all these discussions and debates, no dedicated study comprehensively examines liability and insurance issues that may arise from the operation of unmanned/autonomous merchant ships. Against this background, the proposed study aims to contribute to a better understanding of liability and insurance issues relating to the operation of unmanned/autonomous merchant ships and develop recommendations for addressing those issues. Within the proposed 36 months, this study will (1) look into the conceptual mystery of unmanned/autonomous merchant ships, and reveal the changes and risks that they will create; (2) investigate the various kinds of civil liability and possible challenges that unmanned/autonomous merchant ships will bring to the conventional regulatory framework; and (3) highlight a number of liability and insurance issues and analyse them in detail. This proposed study will employ multiple research methods including both theoretical and empirical research. Meanwhile, it will posit it in a regional context by mainly studying Hong Kong law, law of Mainland China, as well as all international conventions that these two jurisdictions have ratified. The expected outcome of this proposed study will serve as a valuable reference work, since legal clarity and certainty are important for the development of any new technology and innovation. It will also provide legal safeguards for the introduction of unmanned/autonomous merchant shipping in Hong Kong and Mainland China. 無人/自主商船不再是一個未來主義的想法； 它將在可預見的未來被投入使用。一方面，無人/自主商船可以減少或消除人為造成的在海上航運期間出現的故障和風險，從而提高航行安全性。在另一方面，它們將改變運輸實踐，從而產生新的責任和風險。關於相關新技術可能會帶來的法律挑戰的討論越來越多。 有些人認為對某些定義及內容進行廣泛的解釋，並加上對一些主要的國際公約的相關條文進行必要修改，將足以解決無人/自主商船即將帶來的各種問題。 其他人則認為無人駕駛/自主商船可能對現有制度構成很大的衝擊，從而有必要採取不同的規範和法律制度。 在此背景下，擬議的研究旨在對與無人/自主商船運營有關的責任和保險問題進行研究。在擬議的36個月內，本研究將（1）揭開無人/自主商船的神秘面紗，並討論它們將帶來的變化和新的風險; （2）調查與無人/自主商船相關的各種民事責任;和（3）集中研究一系列的責任和保險問題。該擬議研究將採用多種研究方法包括理論和實證研究。 同時，它將主要研究香港法律，中國大陸法律以及所有這兩個司法管轄區已批准的國際公約。 該擬議研究的預期結果將作為有價值的參考文獻，因為法律的明確和確定性對於任何新的技術創新與發展都很重要。 它還將為在香港和中國大陸引入無人/自主商船提供法律保障。

15610019.label: Realisation of objectives
15610019.value: There have been no revisions or deviations from the original objectives, and all five objectives have been successfully accomplished. To achieve Objective 1, we conducted a comprehensive review of relevant international conventions, domestic legislations, and industry reports. A ship’s liability is regulated by international conventions, while insurance is normally regulated at the domestic levels. Therefore, we compiled and analyzed all pertinent international conventions. Additionally, we examined the relevant rules from various national laws, including those of Hong Kong, the United Kingdom, Singapore, and China. The expanding liabilities of ships can be classified into contractual liabilities and third-party liabilities. Objective 2 was achieved by considering all relevant liability issues, particularly third-party liabilities. Furthermore, the operation of unmanned/autonomous ships differs from that of traditional manned ships. Accordingly, we compared and analyzed various aspects, such as the liable parties, basis of liability, nature of liability, and other related issues. Objective 3, which focuses on insurance issues, was considered important and necessary due to the introduction of unmanned/autonomous ships and the associated new risks. We examined specific aspects such as insurance providers and policyholders, and thoroughly discussed potential insurance coverages for collision liabilities, cargo liabilities, pollution liabilities, and other liabilities and risks, when the unmanned/autonomous ships are operated. To achieve Objective 4, we conducted a legal empirical study. Employing a classic grounded theory method, we conducted semi-structured interviews with senior or top managers in shipping companies to gain insights into the industry’s perspectives regarding the acceptance of maritime autonomous surface ships, including considerations related to liability and insurance. Based on both theoretical and empirical studies, we have formulated recommendations for legal amendments or clarifications, fulfilling Objective 5.

15610019.label: Major findings and research outcome
15610019.value: This research has achieved publication of five journal articles, one book chapter, one conference paper, and two seminar talks. Additionally, one manuscript has been submitted to a journal for its consideration for publication (The publication details are listed in Part C). Furthermore, it has provided support for the training of one RA for a period of three months, as well as one postgraduate research student. The major findings of the research align with the original research objectives. First, the research clarifies the conceptual mystery surrounding unmanned merchant ships from both technical and regulatory perspectives. By reviewing representative technical rules, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, relevant International Maritime Organization conventions, and representative national/domestic legislations, the research shows that “unmanned ship” will likely fall within the definition provisions in most international conventions and domestic laws, but such compliance does not enable such other aspects as, for example, collision or pollution liabilities under the current regulatory framework, to be applicable to unmanned ships (e.g., Zhu and Xing, 2021; Li and Zhu, 2021). Secondly, this research carried out in-depth studies of the navigational rights of unmanned/autonomous ships, the legal status of operators controlling vessels remotely, and the associated liabilities. It presents discussions and debates on these topics, shedding light on the legal considerations and challenges surrounding unmanned ship operations (see Zhu and Xing, 2021; Zhu and Zhu, 2023). Thirdly, despite the introduction of unmanned/autonomous ships and the emergence of new risks, the research suggests that the impact on liability insurance practices is not expected to be significant. Existing liability insurance mechanisms may accommodate the changes, although certain aspects such as cybersecurity-related risks may require further examination (See Zhu, 2022). Fourthly, a theoretical framework is developed through a legal empirical study, integrating two main categories and eight core categories that encompass 21 distinct factors influencing the acceptance of Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) by the shipping industry. It highlights the complex interactions between these factors and provides valuable insights from different perspectives. The study also presents an outlook on MASS adoption and proposes policy implications (See Li and Zhu, 2023 submitted). Lastly, the research concludes with various legal and policy recommendations aimed at ensuring the safe operation of unmanned/autonomous merchant ships. These recommendations provide guidance for addressing legal gaps and facilitating the adoption of appropriate measures to promote safety in unmanned shipping (see e.g., Xing and Zhu, 2023).

15610019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
15610019.value: The development of unmanned/autonomous shipping has gained increasing attention, presenting numerous opportunities for further research and exploration. Two notable areas deserving attention are: Cargo Liability Issues: Our completed research primarily focused on liability issues related to parties and different types of liabilities, it did not aim to cover cargo liability issues that may arise from the transportation of goods by unmanned ships. It is however also crucial to understand cargo liability issues. To address this gap, we have submitted a new research proposal to the funding body, seeking support for investigating cargo liability issues in unmanned shipping. Public Law Aspects: Investigating the public law aspects, such as the jurisdiction of flag states in regulating unmanned/autonomous ships, is also of great importance. We are currently working on a journal article that explores the challenges faced by flag states in regulating unmanned ships under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. In addition to the aforementioned areas, it is also essential to consider the environmental implications associated with operating unmanned ships etc. By addressing these research areas, we can further enhance our understanding of unmanned/autonomous shipping and contribute to the development of a benign regulatory framework for its operation.

15610019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
15610019.value: This study significantly contributes to the understanding of unmanned/autonomous merchant ships and offers well-informed legal recommendations for addressing related issues at both domestic and international levels. The research methodology employed a combination of theoretical analysis and legal empirical studies. It involved examining domestic laws of specific jurisdictions, relevant rules from international conventions, and technical regulations established by representative classification societies. Additionally, a legal empirical study was conducted to gather perspectives and insights from industry stakeholders. The research findings serve as valuable reference material for the development of unmanned ships. They enhance the understanding of unmanned/autonomous shipping and contribute to the establishment of a robust and benign regulatory framework for the advancement of unmanned shipping.

15610219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
15610219.value: This project will make use of textual and audio-visual materials in discussing the process of the establishment of the model of performance in Bangzi Opera from 1911-1937. In the period after the middle of the nineteenth century, Bangzi Opera and Beijing Opera became the two popular operatic styles. In its development, Beijing Opera has incorporated many of the artistic features of Bangzi singing. In other words, without Bangzi Opera, it is questionable if Beijing Opera would ever come to its own. However, the research effort of history of drama and history of performance have emphasized Beijing Opera to the neglect of Bangzi Opera. From the gender perspective, like Beijing Opera, Bangzi Opera came into being through the effort of male actors, but from 1911 to 1937, it gradually came to be monopolized by female actors. Why did such a change take place on the Bangzi Opera stage and not on the Beijing Opera stage? What elements of the improved Bangzi Opera in the hands of female actors are particularly suited for the female singing style? Why was Bangzi Opera overlooked by researchers in the recent performance history? All these are questions worthy of examination. Besides, performance is the most dazzling element of traditional drama, which is something difficult to capture in words. To present in a concrete way the process of development of a performance art, it is necessary to look into other materials. This project will therefore utilize gramophone records in reconstructing the historical development of Bangzi Opera and the establishment of a model of performance in order to fill in a gap in the current study of Bangzi Opera. 本計畫將討論1911-1937年間梆子腔表演典範的建立過程，將使用文字資料與視聽資料進行分析討論。19世紀中期以後，梆子腔與京劇都是非常流行的聲腔。京劇在發展過程中吸收了非常多梆子腔的表演藝術特色，換言之，若沒有梆子腔，京劇也無法成熟獨立存在。然而，近代戲劇史及表演史的研究成果，往往偏重於京劇而忽視梆子腔的存在。若是從性別角度來考察，梆子腔和京劇一樣均是原由男演員所創造的，但在1911至1937年間逐漸轉化成為女演員專門演出的劇種。為何女演員會選擇梆子腔而不選擇京劇進行改造? 女演員改良梆子腔那些要素成為適合女性演唱的風格? 為何梆子腔在近代戲劇史上受到研究者的忽視? 這些問題都值得詳加討論。此外，傳統戲劇最耀眼處在於表演。但表演藝術較難用文字具體描述，須更進一步配合相關輔助資料，才能具體地呈現表演藝術發展的歷程。本計畫除了檢視文字資料，更將透過唱片資料，重新建構梆子腔的歷史發展與表演典範過程，以彌補學界目前對於梆子腔研究的缺口。

16100219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16100219.value: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is the most common form of age-related dementia, causing memory loss, cognitive deficits and behavioral changes. Currently, AD remains untreatable and the high failure rate of clinical trials over the past decade has increased the urgency to better understand the heterogeneity of the disease in order to facilitate more personalized therapies. Females are at the epicenter of the AD epidemic, and that the better longevity found in women over men alone is insufficient to explain such phenomenon. Previous studies indicated that neurons located within AD-relevant brain regions are estrogen sensitive, and that they are also one of the extra-gonadal sites of estrogen synthesis. Our preliminary results predicted that the loss of neuronal estrogen signaling transforms a sex-biased benefit to an increased risk for pathological changes associated with AD in older women. Supported by our unsupervised transcriptomic meta-analysis using multiple public datasets, various nuclear-encoded genes for oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) components were consistently reduced specifically in neurons of AD brains. When the same analysis was further stratified based on the sex of the patients, such losses were observed only in female subjects. Mechanistically, systems analyses indicated that the loss in activity of estrogen-related receptor-alpha (ERRα) is most likely the link behind such changes in gene expression observed in AD. ERRα is an orphan receptor; our integrated ChIP-seq analysis as well as in vitro mitochondrial bioenergetics studies revealed that ERRα is an under-appreciated trans-activator of nuclear-encoded respiratory and metabolic genes in neurons. Further analyses revealed that ERRα expression was not reduced in AD, but insufficient cholesterol ligand availability due to reduced cellular uptake mechanism may render ERRα inactive, particularly in female subjects. Taken together, these data suggested an unexpected link between the infidelity of estrogen-mediated cholesterol homeostasis and mitochondrial dysfunction in female neurons. Our first goal is to conduct detailed analysis on changes in the OXPHOS system, Krebs cycle landscape and the overall physiology in ERRα-deficient neurons. Secondly we will perform biochemical analyses to elucidate how estrogen-mediated cholesterol metabolism sustains ERRα-mediated nuclear activities. Finally, we will expand an in-depth analysis regarding estrogen and ERRα biology in AD using disease-related mouse models in order to translate our findings in the context of disease relevant pathologies.
