16103719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16103719.value: Subdivision of the intracellular space into functional compartments is key to the spatiotemporal coordination of numerous biochemical reactions in cells. Recent evidence has shown that many of these compartments in cells are formed by liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), a physical phenomenon in which solutes spontaneously separate into a demixed liquid phase suspended within the bulk solvent. Lately, intriguing examples of ribonucleoproteins, transient multiprotein assemblies and multivalent signaling molecules illustrate how phase separations compartmentalize the intracellular space and regulate various cellular processes. Phase separations are also tightly linked to human diseases such as neurodegenerative disorders including amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia. In human DNA replication, large amounts of transient multiprotein assemblies are spatiotemporally assembled and disassembled to carry out complex biochemical functions. Until now, very limited information about the occurrence of LLPS in DNA replication machinery has been reported. Here we discovered that the least conserved and essential subunit of the human origin recognition complex (ORC) Orc6 could form phase-separated droplets and play an important role in human DNA replication initiation. In our preliminary study, we found that Orc6 formed phase-separated droplets only in the presence of DNA both in vitro and in vivo. The propensity of Orc6 phase separation was directly correlated to the length of DNA. After identifying the DNA binding sites of Orc6 through NMR structural study of the Orc6/DNA complex, we showed that Orc6 mutants with defective DNA binding abrogated the Orc6-mediated DNA replication and phase separation. The functionally related human specific DNA replication inhibitory protein, Geminin, can readily diffuse into the Orc6-DNA droplets while the GST protein cannot. These preliminary data imply that human DNA replication initiation may require the formation of large-scale droplets at DNA replication origins by selective recruiting other pre-replication proteins to perform effective biochemical functions. Additionally, we found that the human Meier-Gorlin syndrome-associated mutation Y232S abolished the Orc6 mediated phase separation. Compared with the wild type Orc6, we showed that Orc6 Y232S mutant was more flexible around this amino acid residue in an in vitro NMR dynamics study. In this proposed, we will further investigate the molecular mechanism and functional role of phase separations introduced by the Orc6-DNA complex through biochemical and biophysical approaches. Moreover, we will also study the role of our newly identified Orc6 inhibitors in the abovementioned investigation. The outcomes are expected to provide new insights for underlying mechanisms of DNA replication initiation mediated by Orc6 and related human diseases. 細胞內空間細分為功能區是細胞中許多生化反應的時空協調的關鍵。細胞中的許多這些功能區是通過液 - 液相分離（LLPS）形成的，這是一種物理現象，其中溶質自發地分離成懸浮在本體溶劑中的混合液相。最近的核糖核蛋白瞬時多蛋白組裝和多價信號分子的有趣例子說明了相分離如何劃分細胞內空間並調節各種細胞過程。相分離也與人類疾病緊密相關，例如神經退行性疾病，包括肌萎縮側索硬化和額顳葉癡呆。 在人類DNA複製中，大量瞬時多蛋白組裝體進行時空組裝和分解，以實現複雜的生化功能。到目前為止，已經報導了關於DNA複製機器中LLPS發生的非常有限的信息。在這裡，我們發現人類起源識別複合物（ORC）Orc6的最不保守和必需的亞基可以形成相分離的液滴，並在人類DNA複製起始中起重要作用。 在我們的初步研究中，我們發現Orc6在體外和體內存在DNA時形成相分離的液滴。在通過Orc6 / DNA複合物的NMR結構研究鑑定Orc6的DNA結合位點後，我們發現具有缺陷DNA結合的Orc6突變體消除了Orc6介導的DNA複製和相分離。功能相關的人特異性DNA複製抑制蛋白Geminin可以很容易地擴散到Orc6-DNA液滴中，而GST蛋白則不能。這些初步數據暗示人類DNA複製起始可能需要通過選擇性地募集其他預複製蛋白以執行有效的生化功能而在DNA複製起點形成大規模液滴。與野生型Orc6相比，我們發現Orc6 Y232S突變體在體外NMR動力學研究中圍繞該氨基酸殘基更加靈活。 在此提議中，我們將進一步研究Orc6-DNA複合物通過生物化學和生物物理方法引入的相分離的分子機制和功能作用。此外，我們還將研究新鑑定的Orc6抑製劑在上述研究中的作用。預計結果將為Orc6和相關人類疾病介導的DNA複製起始的潛在機制提供新的見解

16103719.label: Realisation of objectives
16103719.value: Realisation of objectives (a)Study the detailed molecular mechanisms of hOrc6 phase separation induced by DNA and hOrc6 Y232S mutant in Meier-Gorlin syndrome. 1.1 The NMR structure of Human Orc6, HsOrc6-----Recently, we solved the full length human Orc6 in apo form which contains three independent domains HsOrc6-N (residues 1–94), HsOrc6-M (residues 95–187) and HsOrc6-C (residues 188–252). The structures of HsOrc6-N, HsOrc6-M and HsOrc6-C are well defined by NMR data except for the C-terminal residues 188-230 and 243-252, which are not structured (Xu, N., et al (2020) Nucleic Acids Res.). The structures of the HsOrc6-N and HsOrc6-M domains adopt a similar folding topology containing five helices which is built on a central helix. However, the HsOrc6-C domain contains an α helix spanning residues 231-242. 1.2 HsOrc6 can specially recognize a poly-AT rich DNA sequence-----To characterize the DNA binding properties of the HsOrc6, we performed an NMR titration with a 17bp poly-AT rich oligonucleotide, and we identified a new HsOrc6 fragment containing residues 95-207 which can bind with DNA, termed as HsOrc6 DNA binding domain (HsOrc6-DBD). Notably, the residues R198, K199, R200 and K201 of Orc6-C domain is involved in direct interaction. Our structural model for the HsOrc6 in complex with 10bp poly-AT rich DNA shows that Orc6 binds DNA like a clamp through the HsOrc6-M and HsOrc6-C domains. As a result, residues including Lys168, Lys169, Lys177, Arg174 along with Arg198-Lys199-Arg200-Lys201 form a positively charged cleft and act like a clamp to grab the DNA, representing a potentially unique mechanism of DNA recognition. 1.3 The functional study on the interaction between HsOrc6 and DNA-----Based on NMR structure of HsOrc6/DNA complex, two amino acid clusters were selected for mutagenesis (aa168-173 and 198-201). Three HsOrc6 mutants were created: HsOrc6-K169A, HsOrc6-K168A/K169A/D173A and HsOrc6-R198A/K199A/R200A/K201A. Based on our structure, the HsOrc6 defective mutants HsOrc6-R198A/K199A/R200A/K201A, HsOrc6-K168A/K169A/D173A and HsOrc6-K169A failed to associate with chromosomes. HsOrc6-R198A/K199A/R200A/K201A and HsOrc6-K168A/K169A/D173A mutant proteins were not able to rescue DNA replication in Orc6 depleted Xenopus extract. In summary, for the first time, we identified the HsOrc6 DNA binding domain, HsOrc6-DBD, spanning residues 95-207. In combination with functional studies, our results suggest that HsOrc6 protein possibly acts as a targeting, positioning and an assembly factor to form a functional six-subunit ORC at the origins ultimately resulting in the formation of the pre-RC. (b) Study the functional role of phase separation by hOrc6-DNA complex in human DNA replication 2.1 Liquid droplet-like property of DNA-induced LLPS of HsOrc6-----In the previous study, we have verified that HsOrc6 solution can form a phenomenon characteristic of LLPS by adding DNA in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, we performed Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching assay. We showed that the near-complete fluorescence recovery of Orc6 in the foci indicated that Orc6 exhibits a dynamic liquid like behavior within cellular granules. 2.2 DNA-induced LLPS of HsOrc6 in living cells----Although, previously we have confirmed that the HsOrc6/DNA complex can spontaneously assemble into condensed, membrane-lacking nuclear compartments/puncta in the nuclei of 293T cells by immunofluorescent staining method, we further demonstrated the formation of LLPS of HsOrc6/DNA in vivo by transduction of Cy5-HsOrc6 into NIH3T3 cells through the peptide delivery system (ChariotTM). A large amount of fluorescent puncta formed by HsOrc6/DNA complex was observed. 2.3 The essential role of DNA-induced LLPS of HsOrc6 in DNA replication and disease------ Replication licensing starts with the formation of ORC/DNA complex and ends with the completeness of a head-to-head MCM2-7 double hexamer. The Orc6 subunit is the smallest and the least conserved among ORC subunits. In the previous study, we have demonstrated that the functionally related human specific DNA replication inhibitory protein, Geminin, can readily diffuse into the HsOrc6/DNA droplets. Furthermore, we performed SDS-PAGE analysis of the distributions of HsOrc6 and Geminin in the dilute phase/supernatant and condensed phase/pellet at different protein concentrations, the amount of protein in the condensed droplets gradually decreased with lowered protein concentrations implying the condensed phase formed by HsOrc6/DNA can enrich Geminin. The result indicates that HsOrc6/DNA droplets served as a key “driver” that could recruit DNA replication proteins including MCM2-7 and Geminin to form the pre-replication complex (pre-RC). We found that a low concentration of 2% 1,6-hexanediol significantly inhibited the DNA replication activity of Xenopus laevis egg extract. As the concentration of 1,6-hexanediol increased, the DNA replication activity further decreased. The experimental results prove that the formation of LLPS is the basis for DNA replication initiation. If LLPS is disrupted, DNA will not be able to replicate normally. It was reported that a mutation of HsOrc6 (Y232S) is associated with Meier-Gorlin syndrome (MGS) in humans. We found that HsOrc6_Y232S cannot form LLPS both in vitro and in vivo. This result indicates that the Y232S mutation disrupted the phase-separation capability of hOrc6 in the presence of DNA. Furthermore, NMR titration experiment showed weak/poor binding ability of HsOrc6_Y232S with DNA. Interestingly, several mutants including HsOrc6_Y232A, HsOrc6_Y232D, HsOrc6_Y232R and HsOrc6_Y232F can form liquid-like droplets in the presence of DNA. These results indicated the mutation of Y to S dramatically affected the property of HsOrc6. (c) Test whether or not lead compounds targeting on hOrc6 can interrupt hOrc6-DNA phase separation resulting in the abrogated human DNA replication in Hela cell 3.1 Identification of new small molecule Orc6 inhibitors through virtual screening and NMR studies-----Based on the Orc6-DNA complex structure model, a structure-based virtual screening was conducted to identify potential small molecule inhibitors of Orc6. Nine compounds were found to bind to Orc6 through the virtual screening. The molecular docking scores showed that these compounds displayed strong binding ability to Orc6, and the evaluation results. We analyzed the drug-likeness of screened compounds using DruLiTo software and found that N2-S2154, N2-S2339, N2-S2462, N2-S2577, and N2-S2680 met the requirements and showed good drugability. Using NMR titration experiments with Orc6. Three candidate compounds, N2-S2339, N2-S2462 and N2-S2680, were found to cause significant chemical shift changes in Orc6. Strikingly, it was revealed that the residues interacting with changes N2-S2680 were consistent with the ones involved in binding of Orc6 with DNA, which implies N2-S2680 is a candidate small molecule inhibitor of Orc6. The NMR titration results showed that Orc6 residues L133, F172, and L175 were bound to N2-S2680, with a Kd value of 2.15×10-5. 3.2 Compound N2-S2680 not only abolishes Orc6-DNA LLPS, but also induces growth inhibition and apoptosis in human oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)cell line Cal27------N2-S2680 was used to test its impacts on Orc6-DNA LLPS. we showed that N2-S2680 could greatly abolish the phase transition of Orc6 induced by DNA. Next, the anti-cancer effect of compound N2-S2680 was evaluated on head and neck squamous cell carcinoma model (HNSCC). Treatment of Cal27 cells with 10 µM N2-S2680 for 48 h inhibited the cancer cells proliferation and caused cell death. The cytotoxicity effect of N2-S2680 was quantified by CCK-8 assay. N2-S2680 exhibited dose-dependent manner on killing of Cal27 cells. We also found N2-S2680 induced Cal27 cell death through activation of apoptosis pathway. Treatment of Cal27 cells with 10 µM N2-S2680 induces cleavage of pro-Caspase3 into activated form. The activated caspase3 further activate apoptosis pathway and cleaved its downstream substrate PARP to induce apoptotic cell death of Cal27. As a result, residues including Lys168, Lys169, Lys177, Arg174 along with Arg198-Lys199-Arg200-Lys201 form a positively charged cleft and act like a clamp to grab the DNA, representing a potentially unique mechanism of DNA recognition. The defective mutants involving these residues were not able to rescue DNA replication in Orc6 depleted Xenopus extract. our results suggest that HsOrc6 protein possibly acts as a targeting, positioning and an assembly factor to form a functional six-subunit ORC at the origins ultimately resulting in the formation of the pre-RC (3) we demonstrated that Orc6 binding to DNA can induce liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) both in vivo and in vitro. The above DNA binding defective mutants of HsOrc6 abolishes phase transition. We also demonstrated that HsOrc6/DNA droplets served as a key “driver” that could recruit DNA replication proteins including MCM2-7 and Geminin to form the pre-replication complex (pre-RC). The HsOrc6 (Y232S) that is associated with Meier-Gorlin syndrome (MGS) abolishes the formation of LLPS indicating that it is likely that this disease may be caused by the disruption of LLPS. (4) Based on our HsOrc6/DNA structure and using structure-based virtual screening methods, we found a compound N2-S2680 not only abolishes Orc6-DNA LLPS, but also induces growth inhibition and apoptosis in human oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)cell line Cal27. We are now trying to optimize this compound for the potential treatment of human cancers.

16103719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16103719.value: In human cells, the first step of DNA replication is the binding between HsORC6 and DNA. We publish the first HsOrc6/DNA complex and revealed the key residues involved in DNA replication. We also discovered novel mechanism of Meier-Gorlin syndrome (MGS) caused by HsOrc6 Y232S mutant. Meanwhile, we discovered a compound N2-S2680 not only abolishes Orc6-DNA LLPS, but also induces growth inhibition and apoptosis in human oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)cell line Cal27. The future translation research will involve the optimization of this compound for the cancer treatment.

16103719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16103719.value: In human DNA replication, large amounts of transient multiprotein assemblies are spatiotemporally assembled and disassembled to carry out complex biochemical functions. Until now, very limited information about the occurrence of LLPS in DNA replication machinery has been reported. Here we discovered that the least conserved and essential subunit of the human origin recognition complex (ORC) Orc6 could form phase-separated droplets and play an important role in human DNA replication initiation. With the support of this grant, we have determined the novel HsORC6/DNA solution structure by NMR, elucidated the new human DNA replication mechanism mediated by liquid-liquid phase separation through DNA/HsOrc6 interaction and the molecular mechanism of Meier-Gorlin syndrome (MGS) caused by HsOrc6 Y232S mutant. Furthermore, we found a compound N2-S2680 not only abolishes Orc6-DNA LLPS, but also induces growth inhibition and apoptosis in human oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC)cell line Cal27. The future translation research will involve the optimization of this compound for the cancer treatment. These results have great advanced our understanding of HsORC6 mediated human DNA replication and provide new opportunities for anti-cancer drug development

16200019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200019.value: 伴随着互联网的发展和智能手机的普及，电子商务是很多传统工业的新趋势。在美国，欧洲和中国三大电子商务市场中，中国在2017年以5328亿美元的销售额排名第一，并且网站Statista预测中国在2022年会继续占据第一。 对在线零售商而言，一个关键的挑战是如何利用分散在各地的配送中心实时满足来自不同地理区域的巨大订单量。订单满足包含三个重要决策：（1）构建配送网络，也就是对任意的地理区域（城市，省份甚至国家），决定该由哪些配送中心供货；（2）库存分配，也就是如何分配库存到不同的配送中心；（3）实时需求满足，也就是给定配送网络和库存分配，如何实时满足不断涌现的顾客需求。以下我们将详细阐述第一个决策，鉴于剩下两个是不言自明的。 考虑一个I个配送中心供应J个需求区域的系统。相比于每个配送中心对应一个需求区域，零售商可以给配送系统加一些灵活性，也就是一个需求区域可以用多个配送中心满足。极端情形是全灵活性，也就是每个配送中心都可以服务所有的需求区域。这样的系统能完美匹配供应和需求从而最大化销售额，但是这样的系统可能运营起来十分的昂贵，从而是不切实际的。关于配送网络的研究文献已经有很多，不过大多数都关注的是离线需求满足（等需求实现以后做决策）。均衡系统（I=J）中的长链以及（Shi et al. 2016）中提出的GCG稀疏网络都已经被不同场景下证实具有和全灵活性系统接近的性能。Asadpour et al. (2016) 是唯一一篇在实时需求满足下证明长链优越性能的文章。 在这个项目中，我们将研究针对一般系统（任意数量的配送中心和需求区域）的三个决策问题，这也是反映实际电子商务的需求。我们同时意识到大部分现有研究系统灵活度的文献忽略了库存分配（实时需求）或者是产能分配（离线需求），这些将会是我们的一个研究重点。

16200019.label: Realisation of objectives
16200019.value: The massive opportunities of global ecommerce are too big to ignore and an important challenge for an online retailer is efficient fulfillment of customer orders, which involves three important decisions. (1) The distribution network, i.e., which distribution center(s) are responsible for customers in a specific location. (2) Inventory allocation, i.e., how inventory should be allocated to each distribution center. (3) Online demand fulfillment, i.e., given the network structure and actual inventory levels, which distribution center should fulfill an arriving customer order. The decision on distribution network is a design issue and strategic one, while inventory allocation is periodic in nature and demand fulfillment is in real time. Thus, all together, the problem is extremely complex and challenging. After extensive efforts leading to the proposal and in the past several years, we are able to address the main questions for well recognized conditions in the literature as well as scenarios with little work. For general systems, we establish analytically that a positive GCG (general chaining gap), which is met by the well known long chain structure under simple inventory allocation, is both necessary and sufficient to guarantee a performance gap independent of the market size compared with networks with full flexibility, extending the previous literature from the long chains to more general sparse networks. Inspired by the performance bound, we develop simple inventory allocation rules and insightful guidelines for designing such network structures. Numerical experiments including one using some real data are conducted to confirm our findings as well as some of the flexibility principles conjectured in the literature. The performance we are interested in is the expected lost sales and bounded performance guarantees system performance not divergent with the total market size. Since the performance bound is in the order of 1/GCG and independent of the total market size, a higher GCG is likely to indicate better performance and the bound can serve as an effective surrogate for performance measure when it is reasonably high given that the actual performance measure is elusive. As GCG is bounded from above by the lowest market share as we will see, it can be arbitrarily small, and hence the performance bound can be arbitrarily large as the markets become more asymmetric. Thus, the bound may no longer be an effective indicator and surrogate for system performance, respectively, when the markets are highly asymmetric. It can be easily shown that bounded performance can be achieved for arbitrary low share in some examples despite an arbitrary low GCG and arbitrary high performance bound. As it turns out in more comprehensive examples, both the network structure and the whereabouts of the low-share markets can affect the system performance. In reality, retailers often face highly asymmetric markets, i.e., a retailer needs to supply populated cities as well as remote areas. Recent economic and geopolitical developments have also led to and will cause drastic changes in the global market and supply chains, e.g., a dramatic surge in demand from some regions and a decline (but may not be a complete wipeout) in others. Thus, research on demand fulfillment under highly asymmetric markets is of real relevance and yet so far there has been little work in the literature despite the vast amount of research on process flexibility in the past decades. We are able to identify necessary and sufficient conditions, referred to as e-connectivity that takes into consideration of the market asymmetry, guarantee bounded performance of a GCG system for arbitrary high levels of market asymmetry (and hence arbitrary low GCG) when demand needs to be fulfilled immediately upon arrival or it will be lost. We also propose simple networks to reduce or eliminate the risk of e-disconnectivity. With these, we fulfilled the first two objectives. Journal paper #1 based on this research is under review with MS&OM. With these goals achieved and insights obtained, we tried to extract some guidelines for more complex scenarios under which analytical work is too difficult. In the literature, network flexibility is measured by the number of arcs and compared to the one with full flexibility. In reality, an arc also carries geographical as well as logistical cost information that has direct implications on the performance of an e-retailer. That is, the arcs are heterogeneous and fulfilling orders using one “long” arc may be a lot more expensive than using multiple “short” ones. Furthermore, the logistics costs may prevent certain distribution centers from fulfilling orders at certain locations. The insights from network design under network asymmetry provide a valuable guidelines. When the cost profiles of the arcs are known, simple rules to reassign some arcs can either minimize or significantly reduce the transportation costs under the long chain structure, taking into considerations of the geographical constraints. With the cost profile of the arcs is uncertain, a hub and spoke like network proposed to reduce the risk of e-disconnectivity can also help reducing the expected cost, which also includes the situation when there is a limit of storage capability at the resources. Thus, we believe that we have accomplished what we set out to do for this project.

16200019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200019.value: For online demand fulfillment for systems with limited flexibility, a GCG is both necessary and sufficient for achieving bounded performance. Since the actual performance measure is illusive, our bound provides an effective proxy for system performance when making inventory allocation and network design decisions when the markets are not too asymmetric. We provide guidelines for network design with limited budget for the number of arcs, reflecting the level of network flexibility. In highly asymmetric markets where GCG is no longer a good indicator, we are the first to identify e-connectivity as a necessary and sufficient conditions for bounded performance for arbitrary high levels of market asymmetry. The condition provides some important insights. For instance, bounded performance are more likely to hold when the low-share markets are located in the same region, e.g., they are ``neighbours" in a long chain, rather than spread out across the network. This is good news as, in reality, most negative events such as the spread of infectious disease, natural disasters, and political turmoils normally occur in specific regions. Furthermore, we show that the well-known long chain design may no longer be as effective in highly asymmetric markets and propose a ``hub and spoke'' like structure, with a resource in a shorter long chain formed by a set of relatively healthier markets as the hub, can mitigate the risk of e-disconnectivity as well as improving system performance. Journal paper #1 based on this is under review with MS&OM.

16200019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200019.value: The possibility that the well-known long chain structure may not be effective under certain conditions is very important. As a network is stretched too thin with a perfectly balanced network structure (each resource serves exactly two markets and each market is served by exactly two resources), it may not be able to handle "asymmetry" in supply (capacity, transportation costs, etc) and markets. Our work serves as a first step and more research is needed to look into various real scenarios involving system asymmetry.

16200019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200019.value: E-commerce is an exciting trend for many traditional industries, with the rising number of global Internet and smartphone users driving its growth. According to Statista, retail e-commerce sales worldwide amounted to $2.3 trillion in 2017 and e-retail revenues are projected to grow to $4.88 trillion in 2021. The nature of online demand fulfillment and limited supply flexibility to drive down cost is the motivation of this research. The necessary and sufficient conditions we provided provide clear guidance for network design, inventory allocation, and real time demand fulfillment. The designs we propose are insightful and simple enough to be adopted in real practice. We point out potential shortcomings for the well-known long chain structure and provide suggestions to fine tune a long chain or modify it to be a hub and spoke like network structure with a shorter long chain as a spoke.

16200419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200419.value: 即將推出的 5G 移動網絡將通過實現三種主要的新用戶類別（統稱為 5G 新無線電（5G NR），包括增強的移動寬帶，超可靠/低延遲通信和大規模機器類型通信）來徹底改變無線通信。 5G NR將為每個移動用戶提供 1Gbps 的平均數據速率和達到 10Gbps 的峰值數據速率，1ms 的網絡訪問延遲，以支持未來的應用，如連接的自動駕駛汽車，物聯網（IoT）和實時 4K 視頻流。因此，5G 無線接入網絡（RAN）必須支持 1Tbps / km2 的聚合數據流量容量，比 4G 網絡快100倍。為了滿足苛刻的速度和延遲規範，5G RAN 回程光纖連接採用了 PAM4（4 電平脈衝幅度調製）信令作為新標準，從 4G 或舊網絡中使用的傳統 NRZ（非歸零）信令升級。理論上，這種遷移在單波長光纖鏈路中的數據速率可以翻倍，使用傳統的光電子器件，模擬帶寬有限，用於 28Gbps 或更低的傳統回程。 為了滿足 5G 覆蓋要求，在許多農村或人口密集的地區，完全依賴光學連接在物理上是不切實際的並且過於昂貴。因此，已經提出使用波束控制技術和在毫米波（mmWave）頻帶中工作的定向天線的寬帶點對點無線鏈路來補充用於 5G 雲RAN（C-RAN）前端的短距離連接的光纖。 - 回程和回程這種混合光纖無線C-RAN將需要光學和無線域之間的新物理接口。物理層電路必須支持光接口和無線子系統側的 PAM4 信令，使用高級調製方案，如 16QAM（16 級正交幅度調製），以最大化頻譜效率，實現高 mmWave 頻段有限帶寬內的數據速率。由於光學和 mmWave 集成電路所需的設計挑戰和專業知識各不相同，因此在實現和實施這種創新且必不可少的光纖無線網絡的成本效益解決方案方面進展不足。 為了滿足這一需求，我們建議利用我們在光學和 mmWave 系統設計方面的豐富經驗，開發光學無線通信集成電路（OWIC）。擬議的 OWIC 將 PAM4 光信號直接調製和解調為 16QAM mmWave 信號，以 28Gbps 的速度提供前所未有的速度和效率。我們計劃的結果將為 5G C-RAN 前端和後程系統的尺寸，成本和功耗設定多個新的基準。

16200419.label: Realisation of objectives
16200419.value: The three project objectives have been achieved successfully. For objective 1, we have successfully designed and simulated an optical-wireless communication integrated circuit (OWIC) including a 28Gbps PAM4 optical receiver, a PAM4 demultiplexer, a 16QAM millimeter-wave (mmWave) transmitter, and a mmWave frequency synthesizer at 24-32GHz using standard foundry CMOS technology. The optical Rx, mmWave Tx, the LO generator, mmWave Rx and the optical Tx have been completed. The results have already published in 6 journal papers and 3 conference articles listed in Part C. For the Optical Receiver (RX) design, we have proposed a PAM-4 receiver utilizing the jitter compensation CDR (JCCDR). On the data recovery path, a two-stage continuous-time linear equalizer (CTLE) with R-C source degeneration and inductor shunt peaking architecture is implemented as the front-end to compensate for moderate channel loss. Then, input PAM-4 signal is sampled and deserialized by four sample-and-hold circuits (S/H). Next, the sampled signals are decoded using three StrongARM comparators (CMP) with individual reference voltages generated from a 6-bit current-mode DAC for slicing the top, middle, and bottom data eyes. More details can be found in Part C/8/Paper 6 and Part C/9/Paper 1. For the Optical Transmitter (TX), we analyzed the effect of fractional-spaced non-symmetric feed forward equalization on the common-mode (CM) noise and presents a novel on-chip architecture of a CM noise compensator for the application of a high-speed PAM-4 optical transmitter. Based on simulation results, we have submitted a paper to IEEE Transactions on Very Large Scale Integration Systems. More details can be found in Part C/8/Paper 1 and Part C/9/Paper 3. For the mmWave TX, we investigated the design and implementation of an ultra-broadband quadrature common-mode amplitude modulator (QCAM) to generate high power back-off efficiency 16-QAM signals. The proposed QCAM transmitter consists of I- and Q-path PAM4 modulators, which digitally modulate the power amplifier (PA) output stage to relax the linearity requirement. The 28-GHz 16-QAM transmitter test chip, implemented in 65-nm CMOS, achieved measurement results of 11.35 dBm average RF output power, 9.2% DC-RF efficiency, 16 Gb/s data rate, and -24 dB EVM. Please see Part C/8/Paper 2 and 4. For the mmWave TX and RX design, we developed an Integrated System Evaluation Engine (ISEE) based on Matlab, Advanced Design System (ADS), and Cadence simulators, for evaluating system performances of wireless communication transceiver (TRx) using high-order complex modulation schemes. The evaluation can be from either transistor-level, behavior model level, or even experimental results of modules that are already fabricated. To demonstrate effectiveness and efficiency of using ISEE for high-speed SoC design optimization, several 28 GHz direct-conversion TRx front-end systems are designed and simulated using orthogonal frequency division multiplex (OFDM) signals with sub-carriers modulated by quadrature amplitude modulation (M-QAM) scheme. The TRx system includes a Doherty transmitter (Tx) and three different receivers (Rx) for comparison. The co-simulation results reveal the merits and demerits of three Rx architectures and lead to design insights for Rx frontend circuits operated with advanced modulation formats. More details can be found in Part C/9/Paper 2 and Part C/8/Paper 3. For objective 2, we have tested and characterized the OWICs with a 28Gbps PAM4 optical input signal and a 16QAM mmWave output signal at 24-32GHz. Three test chips have been tested to verify and validate our design. The results have already published in 5 journal papers and 3 conference articles listed in Part C. For objective 3, we have trained several post-docs and PG students have contributed to this project and been trained during the process. Dr. Zhao Zhang and Dr. Xianyu Meng were major contributors to the frequency synthesizer and the mmWave transmitter design. They are now tenured faculty at CAS University in Beijing and SYSU in GZ, respectively. Dr. Weimin Shi contributed a great deal in the system-level design using the in-house developed Integrated System Evaluation Engine and improving the high-frequency power amplifier design. He is now a tenured Associate Professor at Chongqing University. Post-graduate student research associates including Li Wang, and Rehan Azmat have earned their PhD degrees under the support of this project. They learned a great deal in mmWave wireless circuit and optical communication circuit design. They have gained experience to present at top international conferences and publish in well recognized journals in the field of integrated circuit design. Dr. Kalantari now works for a local IC design company in HK Science Park. Dr. Li Wang will stay on as a post-doc fellow at HKUST in my group. Dr. Rehan Azmat now works for Huawei (HK) as a high-speed circuit designer.

16200419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200419.value: Considering the expensive IC fabrication cost, an Integrated System Evaluation Engine for evaluating high-speed system with complex modulated signals has s implemented. A 28 GHz TRx system with three different Rxs is designed and evaluated by ISEE. The demonstration shows that ISEE can enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of designing and optimizing high-speed SoC significantly. Generally, ISEE is engineered to help IC designer to evaluate their circuits at system level using practical modulated signals before fabrication, improving the success rate of chip design. And it can also help IC designers to compare and choose system architecture, saving design cost and time. In the future, ISEE can be further developed as an engine for complex system synthesis with known circuit templates. For more details, see Part C/9/Paper 2. We have designed and implemented a source-synchronous 60-Gb/s quarter-rate (1/4-rate) PAM4 receiver (Rx) with a jitter compensation clock and data recovery circuit (JCCDR) to overcome the stringent trade-off between jitter transfer (JTRAN) and jitter tolerance bandwidth (JTOL BW). The jitter compensation circuit (JCC) utilizes the delay-locked loop (DLL) filter voltage to produce a complementary control signal VLF INV , which modulates a group of complementary voltage-controlled delay lines (C-VCDL) so to negate the JTRANs on the recovered data and clock signals. The proposed 40-nm CMOS Rx test chip achieves error-free operation with PAM4 input from 30 to 60 Gb/s. The JCCDR achieves a 40-MHz JTOL BW with over 0.2-UI PP jitter amplitude while maintaining a -8-dB JTRAN. A jitter compensation ratio of around 60% has been achieved up to 40 MHz. For more details, see Part C/9/Paper 1. We have designed and implemented an ultra-broadband quadrature common-mode amplitude modulator (QCAM) to generate high power back-off efficiency 16-QAM signals. The proposed QCAM transmitter consists of I- and Q-path PAM4 modulators, which digitally modulate the power amplifier (PA) output stage to relax the linearity requirement. An interleaved differential transformer-based coupler is proposed for wide-band combination of the baseband and LO signals. The I and Q PAM4 signals are combined using an on-chip Wilkinson power combiner to generate the 16-QAM output signal. The 28-GHz 16-QAM transmitter test chip, implemented in 65-nm CMOS, achieved measurement results of 11.35 dBm average RF output power, 9.2% DC-RF efficiency, 16 Gb/s data rate, and −24 dB EVM. For more details, see Part C/8/Paper 3 and 5.

16200419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200419.value: To further the development of the research, the optical transceiver data rate needs to be raised to 56 Gbps to meet the requirement of the 5G network requirement. The more sophisticated modulation scheme beyond PAM4, such as PAM8 or coherent optical communication, should be investigated in the future to further improve the channel capacity per optical link. On the mmWave radio design, beamforming system-on-chip with ability to overcome the path loos by beam steering should be studied. The architecture-level trade-offs such as radio-frequency vs. baseband phase-shifting and analog vs. digital beamforming should be investigated. The integration of the optical communication and mmWave circuits in a single chip needs to be implemented and evaluated.

16200419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200419.value: To further expand 5G coverage, complete reliance on optical connectivity would be physically impractical and prohibitively expensive in many rural or densely populated areas. Therefore, broadband point-to-point wireless links using beam-steering techniques and directional antennas operating in the millimeter-wave (mmWave) band have been proposed to complement optical fibers for short-reach connectivity in 5G cloud RAN (C-RAN) front-haul and back-haul. Such hybrid fiber-wireless C-RAN will require new physical interfaces between the optical and wireless domain. The physical-layer circuits must support PAM4 signaling at the optical interfaces and on the wireless sub-system side, use high-level modulation schemes such as 16QAM (16-level Quadrature-Amplitude-Modulation) to maximize the spectral efficiency to achieve a high data rate within the limited bandwidth of the mmWave band. Because of the diverse design challenges and expertise required for optical and mmWave integrated circuits, there is insufficient progress towards a cost-effective solution to realize and implement this innovative and essential fiber-wireless network. The proposed OWIC can modulate and demodulate PAM4 optical signals directly to 16QAM mmWave signals delivering unprecedented speed and efficiency at 28Gbps. The outcome of our program will contribute to improve the 5G C-RAN front-haul and back-haul system size, cost, and power consumption.

16200619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200619.value: In classical frequency domain analysis of single-input-single-output (SISO) systems, magnitude (or gain) response analysis and phase response analysis go hand in hand. When we enter the multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) system era, the concept of magnitude has been extended and thrived but that of phase has diminished. The main reason for this is that the magnitude(s) or gain(s) of a complex matrix are well defined by the singular values but a suitable definition of the phase(s) of a complex matrix is an unsettled issue. Magnitude analysis leads to an optimal control theory which aims to minimize the H_infinity norm of a closed-loop system, but should we also have an optimal control theory which strives to minimize some H_infinity phase of a closed-loop system? Our preliminary study shows that for a special class of complex matrices, called cramped matrices, the phases are well defined. These phases satisfy the desired properties extending those of complex scalars. If we assume that a MIMO linear time-invariant system has cramped frequency response at each frequency, then the phase response of the system can be defined and plotted. This opens the door to a MIMO phase analysis and synthesis theory complementary to the one based on the magnitude response, completing the missing half of the frequency domain approach to MIMO system control theory. In this proposed project, we will take the initial steps in exploring this uncharted half of the frequency domain control theory. The foundation will be laid. Considering that it took decades to build the magnitude half of the theory, we expect that it will take a few more further projects before we can complete the development of this new half. An era of massive network systems is upon the world. We have strong evidence that when analyzing the stability of complex dynamical networks, especially those consisting of mechanical and electrical components, phase analysis is more convenient and scalable than magnitude analysis. In this project, we will demonstrate the power of phase analysis by applying it to complex dynamical network analysis. 在单变量系统的古典频域分析中，增益和相位并肩同行。当我们进入多变量系统的时代，增益得到发扬光大，而相位日渐式微。造成这种现状的主要原因是在数学上众所周知复矩阵的增益由它的奇异值给定，而复矩阵的相位为何物却无人知晓。增益分析引领出以优化增益为目标的H无穷最优控制理论，那么相位分析是否也会引领出以优化相位为目标的最优控制理论？ 我们的初期研究表明：狭窄矩阵的相位是能被准确定义的。假设多输入多输出时线性时不变系统在每个频率都有狭窄频率响应，那就能准确定义且绘得该系统的相位响应。这打开了多变量控制系统相位分析与综合的大门，使其与幅值理论形成优势互补，完善多变量控制系统频域分析所缺失的一半。本项目将迈出探索未知相位理论的第一步，夯实其理论基础。幅值理论的创立尚用了数十年，相位理论的完善将需经历多个研究项目的打拼。 属于大规模复杂网络系统的时代已经来临，我们坚信，相位分析对研究复杂动态网络系统，特别是由机械和电气元件的网络系统，会比幅值分析更方便且更易扩展。本项目会将相位分析方法应用于复杂动态网络系统中，来证实它的强大潜力。

16200719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200719.value: Exosomes are nanometer-scale membrane vesicles initially thought to be cellular debris but now increasingly appreciated as key vehicles of cell-to-cell communication. Shed by most cells, exosomes carry valuable cargo of proteins and nucleic acids signaling the parent cell’s state. Present in nearly all bodily fluids, they offer tremendous potential for disease diagnosis and prognosis, particularly cancer, through minimally-invasive liquid biopsy. They could also be used as vaccine candidates and drug carriers delivering therapeutic agents to target cells. Research on exosomes continues to grow with exciting discoveries gradually revealing their physiological significance and suggesting the potential for far-reaching clinical impact. The pace of discovery is limited, however, by the lack of effective preparatory and analytical techniques. Recent advances in microfluidic and nanofluidic devices (microdevices) could relieve this bottleneck, promoting a wave of progress. This project will directly address the problem by demonstrating the utility of microdevices for the isolation, concentration, and size-fractionation of exosomes from whole blood. The isolation and concentration will be achieved in two consecutive stages: plasma will be extracted from undiluted whole blood in the first stage and the exosomes in the extracted plasma will be concentrated along with other extracellular vesicles in the second stage. Both the stages will take place in a continuous-flow design that will feature silicon bulk microelectrodes with segmented sidewalls and with dimensions customized for the respective stage. The design will synergistically couple long-range electrothermal rolls and short-range dielectrophoresis. The exosomes’ size-fractionation and purification will be achieved by conducting continuous-flow electrophoresis through an artificial sieve, which will involve a periodic arrangement of nanocapillaries and microchannels. The proposed microdevices will be thoroughly characterized using test samples and whole blood. The collected elutes will be analyzed for exosome yield, size, morphology, and function through conventional techniques. Fabrication of the microdevices with a critical dimension down to 50nm will be achieved through low-resolution, high-throughput patterning. This technology can create robust silicon-based platforms, which can be batch-produced in microelectronics foundries. Furthermore, their electrokinetic mechanism will allow the microdevices to run on a compact instrument. All these characteristics render them amenable to further integration for portability and to economies of scale in production, which will promote their dissemination to laboratories and clinics. The proposed microdevices thus offer great potential for accelerating discoveries about exosomes and also will bring such discoveries closer to the bedside.

Develop a curved layer slicing algorithm for each component of the decomposition, subject to finish surface quality, gravity, the nozzle dispensing specifications, and other limiting criteria. 16200819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200819.value: The traditional three-axis volume printing process prints a volume by building planar slicing layers along a fixed build direction, which inevitably requires a support structure when dealing with overhanging features. The advent of five-axis printers has inaugurated a brand new printing configuration that allows the build direction to continuously change and the slicing layers to be curved, based on which the support structure can be mostly eliminated with appropriate process planning. Moreover, the surface finish quality is considerably improved with five-axis printing, as the signature staircase effect in three-axis printing can be all or mostly eliminated by properly adjusting the nozzle orientation at the surface of the volume. The process planning for printing a solid P on a five-axis printer involves determining a complete printing path for the nozzle, including both its trajectory and orientation, as well as other printing parameters such as the nozzle feed rate and nozzle deposition rate. When planned properly, the execution of this printing path will correctly produce a P with the desired surface finish quality and as little support structure as possible. This is an extremely complicated task involving geometric analysis and optimization, kinematics, material properties, and other physical aspects. At present it is almost exclusively done manually and case-specifically. Moreover, typically only a 3+2-axis printing process (i.e., the nozzle orientation only changes a small and finite times) is used, rather than a genuine five-axis process, thus severely limiting its potential. In this project, we will conduct a systematic study of various critical aspects of this important problem and develop an automatic process planning software system for the genuine five-axis printing of an arbitrary solid P. In addition, as an integral part of the project, we will first build a five-axis printer for non-metallic material, with which ample physical printing experiments will be carried out to assess and validate the effectiveness and limitations of the developed automatic process planning system. The first in its kind, we believe the findings and experimental results from the project will be eagerly welcomed by both practitioners and researchers in multi-axis additive manufacturing and help potentiate this emerging powerful technology.

16200919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16200919.value: Soft-material robots have attracted much interest in the research community over the last two decades because of their advantages compared to rigid-bodied robots, including conformability to objects with various shapes, adaptability to unknown environments and safe interaction with human beings without the need for complex control loops. Inspired by nature, soft robots have broadened the range of application for robots by their inherent compliance. Although considerable progress have been achieved in the soft robotics field, its continued development is hindered by several substantial challenges. One of these is the ability to vary the stiffness of soft robots to adapt to the needs of different tasks. Natural muscle tissues have tunable stiffness properties to perform various tasks and to adapt to the environment. In soft robots, tunable stiffness properties are also desirable in order to transfer reversibly between the rigid, load-bearing state and the compliant, flexible state. Taking a robotic grasping task as an example, we would expect soft robotic grippers or hands to deform freely (at low stiffness) to adapt to diverse objects’ shapes, grasp objects gently and safely and withstand heavy loads while manipulating the objects (at high stiffness), just like human hands. To realize variable stiffness in a soft robot, two approaches will be investigated in this research. The first approach is to apply materials whose rigidity is intrinsically tunable to vary the stiffness of soft robots. The second approach is to use antagonistic arrangement of active actuation elements to realize variable stiffness. The realization of variable stiffness for soft robotic manipulation is vital to promote their practical application. 柔性機器人在過去二十年中引起了研究界的極大興趣，因為它們與剛體機器人相比具有優勢，包括對各種形狀物體的適應性，對未知環境的適應性和與人類安全互動，並且無需複雜的控制迴路。受大自然的啟發，柔性機器人因為其固有的柔順性擴大了機器人的應用範圍。 儘管柔性機器人研究取得了相當大的進步，但其持續發展受到若干重大挑戰的阻礙。其中之一是如何能夠改變柔性機器人的剛度以適應不同任務的需要。天然肌肉組織具有可調節的剛度特性，以執行各種任務並適應環境。在柔性機器人中，為了在剛性承載狀態和柔性狀態之間可逆地傳遞，需要可調節的剛度特性。以機器人抓取任務為例，我們期望柔性機器人抓手或手自由變形（低剛度）以適應不同物體的形狀，輕輕安全地抓住物體，並在操縱物體時承受重物而不變形（高剛度），就像人手一樣。 為了實現柔性機器人的變剛度，本研究將研究兩種方法。第一種方法是應用剛性可調的材料來改變軟機器人的剛度。第二種方法是使用主動致動元件的對抗佈置來實現可變剛度。實現柔性機器人的可變剛度對於促進它們的實際應用是至關重要的。

16200919.label: Realisation of objectives
16200919.value: 1. Analyze the underlying mechanisms/principles for variable stiffness of soft robots based upon previous research and propose new methods of stiffness tuning; The stiffness of soft material robots is usually low, so they cannot easily output large force and bear heavy loads. Variable stiffness soft robots can make soft contact with target objects in the flexible state while possessing great strength in the rigid state and lifting heavy objects. The variable stiffness capability is an ideal feature for soft robots. The common methods of stiffness modulation mainly fall into the following four categories: glass/phase transition-based methods, viscosity-based methods, jamming-based methods, and structure-based methods. To realize variable stiffness in a soft robot, three approaches were investigated in this research. The first approach was using an antagonistic arrangement of active actuation elements to realize variable stiffness. The second approach was applying materials whose rigidity is intrinsically tunable to vary the stiffness of soft robots. The realization of variable stiffness for soft robotic manipulation is vital to promote their practical application. The third approach was employing Origami’s bidirectionality to realize the stiffness variation in the structure’s different states. We have arranged the origami tubes in a 3D arrangement. As a result, our actuator possesses a unique variable stiffness or anisotropic property, which can help adjust the design according to the task at hand. 2. Develop soft robotic grippers or hands with variable stiffness functions and establish theoretical models predicting the stiffness variation; We first studied a novel soft actuator based on mini dc motor and supercoiled polymer artificial muscle (SCPAM). The gearmotor is used to drive the finger to bend to a certain position, and then SCPAM is powered to increase the output force and bending angle. Then, we designed a proprioceptive soft robot module based on supercoiled polymer artificial muscle strings. This module can be used to construct various soft robots. We used this module to create an inchworm-like crawling robot and a soft robotic gripper and tested their crawling and grasping abilities respectively. We also established a sensing model that relates the resistance of SCPAM to the bending angle of the robot, which can be used to determine the bending shape of the robot. This module is installed with two SCPAM in an opposing configuration on the upper and lower sides, which not only achieves bidirectional bending functionality but also increases the stiffness of the module. Lastly, we also studied a novel variable stiffness and tunable bending shape soft robotic finger based on thermoresponsive polymers. This soft robotic finger has the ability of segmental stiffness modulation, allowing for multi-modal bending, sequential motion, and variable stiffness grasping. Along with the design principle of Origami-enabled gripper with stiffness variation, We introduced a bottom-up design methodology that can also be adapted for other complex movements. The material model was empirically derived by testing specimens on a universal testing machine (UTM). Theoretical analysis has been conducted for the above soft parts, fingers, gripers, and robots to understand the mechanism of stiffness variation and provide theoretical predictions. Materials modeling and FEM modeling were performed to build a baseline of the theoretical understanding of the devices. The corresponding behaviors of these soft fingers and gripers, under different heating powers or pressures, were characterized to verify our theoretical analysis. 3. Implement variable stiffness soft robotic manipulators for practical tasks such as grasping everyday objects with a wide range of weights. First, we tested the compliance and force output characteristics of a novel soft actuator based on mini dc motor and SCPAM. The compliance and force output characteristics of the three actuation configurations (single SCP/gearmotor & kite line/gearmotor & SCP) will be tested separately to verify the effectiveness and superiority of the novel actuator. The results show that the finger’s stiffness is the largest when it is actuated by the gearmotor & kite line, the finger actuated by the single SCP has the smallest stiffness. The stiffness of the gearmotor & SCP actuated finger ranges between the above two actuation methods. Force-displacement experiments the advantages of the novel driver constructed by the deceleration motor and SCP in terms of flexibility (especially compared to the deceleration motor and kite line). Only under the action of the motor, the stiffness of the finger driven by the deceleration motor and SCP driver increases slowly. By energizing to the limit position, the finger obtains a contraction stroke, which also increases its stiffness. We also conducted tests on the force output characteristics to investigate SCP ’s thermal contraction property on the output force gain under the gearmotor & SCP actuation method. The experimental results demonstrate: that after applying an initial force to the SCP and energizing it, the output force of the finger increased. Then we will use the multi-functional soft robot module to make an inchworm-like crawling robot and a soft robotic gripper, whose crawling ability and grasping ability are tested, respectively. We established a sensing model for the crawling robot to predict the crawling robot’s bending angle by measuring the resistance value of the sensor (SCPAM). Finally, we tested the stiffness modulation capability and grasping ability of the novel variable stiffness and tunable bending shape soft robotic finger. Experimental results show that the stiffness of the finger at room temperature (25 ◦C) is 10.54 times that at 70 ◦C. At the same time, the use of segmented heating in SMP enables the soft robotic finger to have the segmental stiffness modulation capability, and this allows the robotic finger to generate different bending modes under SCPAMs’ actuation and as a result, the robotic finger has the ability to bend in multiple modes, grasp with variable stiffness, and sequential motion. The multi-modal bending tests showed the soft robotic fingers have seven different bending modes. The multi-modal bending capability of the robotic finger enables it to adapt to different external contour shapes. We conducted gripping demonstrations and sequential motion demonstrations using two soft robotic fingers to form a gripper, grasping the object at a flexible state (low stiffness) and lifting the object at high stiffness. The sequential motion test demonstrated that the fingers' sequential motion provides better adaptability to objects, allowing for a larger contact area and a wider enveloping range. This significantly improves the gripping stability of the robotic gripper. Additionally, the increased contact area between the gripper and the object enhances safety and allows for a higher gripping load capacity. 16200919.label: Major findings and research outcome
16200919.value: Firstly, we have summarized the development process of soft robot and analyzed the advantages and disadvantages of existing methods for changing the stiffness of soft robots, such as glass/phase transition-based methods, viscosity-based methods, jamming-based methods, and structure-based methods. Secondly, we first studied a novel soft actuator based on mini dc motor and supercoiled polymer artificial muscle. This actuator combines SCPAM with a gearmotor. The gearmotor is used to drive the finger to bend to a certain position, and then SCPAM is powered to increase the output force and bending angle. The experiments show that the soft robotic finger driven by this hybrid SCPAM & gear motor not only has good flexibility but also further increases the bending angle of the finger and the stiffness value when SCPAM is activated. Then, we designed a proprioceptive soft robot module based on supercoiled polymer artificial muscle strings. This module can be used to construct various soft robots. We used this module to create an inchworm-like crawling robot and a soft robotic gripper, and tested their crawling and grasping abilities respectively. We also established a sensing model that relates the resistance of SCPAM to the bending angle of the robot, which can be used to determine the bending shape of the robot. We also studied a novel variable stiffness and tunable bending shape soft robotic finger based on thermoresponsive polymers. This soft robotic finger has the ability of segmental stiffness modulation, allowing for multi-modal bending, sequential motion, and variable stiffness grasping. Experimental results show that the stiffness of the finger at room temperature is 10.54 times that at 70 ◦C when the actuators are on. The performance of the finger is further validated via the sequential motion demonstration and grasping tests with variable stiffness and bending shape control capabilities, showing the proposed design’s potential in soft grippers and robotic design. Finally, we employed Origami structure’s bidirectionality to realize the stiffness variation in the structure’s different states. We have arranged the origami tubes in a 3D arrangement. As a result, our actuator possesses a unique variable stiffness or anisotropic property, which can help adjust the design according to the task at hand. Further, we combined it with a rotary actuator to achieve hybrid motion and it can adjust the gap distance between the two rotary actuators. In this way, the hybrid actuator can handle more objects in different scales.

16200919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16200919.value: For SCPAM based actuator, the variable stiffness function will be added to the soft robot module so that the configured gripper can grasp a larger range of objects. In addition, theoretical modeling will be established to study the interaction between the two-ply SCPAM actuator and the soft body. The third-order polynomial model used to predict the bending angle of the crawling robot is not from a physical perspective, resulting in inaccurate predictions. Future targets are to make the stiffness of the module tuneable within a range and to increase the output force of the module. For Origami based actuator, despite the promising results from results, our devices and actuators currently exhibit several challenges: 1. Under heavy loads, the direction of the actuator’s movement tends to deviate from the desired trajectory. This is primarily due to the initial air pressure being insufficient to generate effective startup displacement. 2. The control of the actuator remains a significant challenge. Given the material non-linearity and the complexity of the structure, currently, it can only operate in binary modes, i.e., either open or shut. Addressing these issues will be pivotal to ensuring the seamless integration and application of this actuator in real-world scenarios.

16200919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16200919.value: Soft-material robots have attracted much interest in the research community over the last two decades because of their advantages compared to rigid-bodied robots, including conformability to objects with various shapes, adaptability to unknown environments and safe interaction with human beings without the need for complex control loops. Meanwhile, tunable stiffness properties are also desirable for soft robots for better adapting to diverse objects’ shapes and loads. To realize variable stiffness in a soft robot, we investigated 1) soft materials whose rigidity is intrinsically tunable to vary the stiffness of soft robots; 2) the antagonistic arrangement of active actuation elements to realize variable stiffness; and 3) Origami-based structure design to achieve different stiffness in different states. Theoretical analysis, design, actuator fabrication, and device demonstration were conducted to successfully validate our ideas. Our achievements provided a feasibility study for the future employment of stiffness-variation soft robots in various applications.

16201019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201019.value: Due to the multidisciplinary nature of materials science, people in various fields desire to understand and design new materials with exceptional properties. Traditionally, the discovery of new materials relies on the trial-test-correction based design cycle. Human intelligence, or more precisely the engineering heuristics, guides the discovery of new materials, but the transitioning of the property from the initial discovery to the optimized one for practical use usually takes more than a decade. Here we propose to integrate the rigorous mathematical tools with the design of Cu-based shape memory alloys to achieve the lowest functional fatigue in both single and polycrystalline fashions. In previously funded GRF proposals, the underlying theory for the design of complex materials has been established by the applicant. She has validated the mathematical descriptor and corresponding mechanics criteria for materials undergoing phase transformation. Integrating the synchrotron microdiffraction experiment at the Advanced Light Source, Lawrence Berkeley National Lab with the data-driven algorithms implemented by the applicant's group, the rapid evaluation of the material descriptor and the criteria has been developed. Her group has built a new mechanical testing platform utilizing the dual-beam DIC microscopy with a μUniaxial loading device, which allows for the in-situ observation of the evolution of microstructure during phase transformation while the local deformation gradient is simultaneously quantified. Integrating the mechanics theories with our custom-made mechanical testing platform, we propose a new design strategy for the CuAlMn ternary system, which skips the conventional trial-test-correction cycle. The material descriptor can be calculated directly from the structural parameters using the StrucTrans algorithm. Then we will formulate a scalar-valued function as an indexer of certain property based on the cofactor conditions, and study the continuity, the gradients, the extremes, and the compositional dependence of this function in compositional space. Instead of repeatedly cycling between trial and characterization results many times, we can predict the tuning direction by the root-finding algorithm and then synthesizing the optimum compositions directly for further characterization. In this proposal, we will examine the enhanced functional fatigue property of the optimized candidates by 1) thermally driven phase transformation cycling experiments; 2) tensile stress induced phase transformation cycling experiments at nano-, micro- and meso-scales. 16201419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201419.value: Marine deposits are usually a mixture of soft clay and coarse aggregates, e.g., sand. The sand content of the seabed soil in the Pearl River estuary in China varies from 30% to 60%. These types of soil possess a high water content, as well as high compressibility and low shear strength. Therefore, surcharge preloading is usually adopted for improving the engineering properties of sandy marine deposits. The consolidation settlement of soft sandy soil due to surcharge loading is crucial in the functioning and safety of civil infrastructures on which they are constructed. The current methods for calculating the consolidation of sandy soils are essentially empirical, and theoretical studies are quite limited. It is widely accepted that the presence of sand particles has a significant effect on the deformation behaviour of sandy soils. However, the existing elastic visco-plastic models were proposed for homogeneous fine-grained soils. They do not incorporate the effect of sand nor the change in the inter-granular structure of the soil as it consolidates under surcharge loading. These omissions lead to a considerable error in estimating how sandy marine deposits will settle under the weight of a structure. The proposed project seeks to correct these errors in existing models through theoretical constitutive modelling, laboratory testing and field applications. A new elastic visco-plastic (EVP) model will be developed, which incorporates the finite strain concept and the sand fraction effect. The EVP model will be further implemented into the finite element code for the boundary value problems of soft sandy ground. More importantly, a simplified version of the EVP model for a practical estimation of the settlement of sandy ground will be proposed. Both the full EVP model and its simplified version will be validated based on physical model tests on sand-clay mixtures. The EVP model developed from this project will improve our fundamental understanding of the deformation behaviour of sand-clay mixtures during consolidation under the weight of structures. The laboratory tests and the modelling procedures will assist civil engineers and researchers in improving the current design methods for the estimation of the consolidation settlement of sandy marine deposits. Ultimately, the model developed in this project will make buildings safer, particularly those built on the sandy soil of the Pearl River Delta. 海洋沈積物的固體成分通常由細顆粒和一定量的粗顆粒構成。例如，珠江入海口附近海洋沈積物的粗粒含量一般介於30%到60%。這種類型的沈積物通常具有較高的含水量，因而具有高壓縮性。針對海洋沈積物特殊性，一般采用預壓固結的方法改善其工程特性，以提高其承載力並減少工後固結變形。預壓作用下沈積物的固結變形與海床上土工建築物的安全及工作性能密切相關。海洋沈積物固結變形的傳統計算方法多為經驗性，缺乏理論基礎。砂粒的存在對海洋沈積物的變形具有重要的影響，而以往的模型沒有考慮砂粒含量對土體結構的影響。因而，傳統的模型並不適用於海洋沈積物在承重作用下的變形計算。本項目擬通過理論分析提出新的模型，並將其應用於工程計算。首先提出考慮粗顆粒含量對土體結構影響的本構模型，並將該模型嵌入有限源程序用於海洋沈積物邊值問題的變形計算。為了便於工程應用，在理論模型的基礎上提出一種簡化的計算方法。該簡化方法將與有限元計算結果對比，以驗證其有效性。本項目擬提出的模型和計算方法將改善學界對海洋沈積物在承重條件下變形過程的認識。簡化模型將為工程人員和科研工作者提供新的海洋沈積物變形計算方法。最終，本項目提出的模型和計算方法，將使建在海洋沈積物之上的建築物設計更加安全，特別是珠三角地區的海床上的土工建築物。

16201419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16201419.value: The project team have been working closely over the past three years and have successfully completed all proposed objectives in the project. We have performed high-quality research and published 10 research papers in prestigious journals. Major achievements from the project are summarized below pertaining to the three objectives proposed: (a) Objective #1: (a-1) A series of laboratory tests, including the oedometer tests, direct shear tests and triaxial tests, have been conducted on gap-graded mixtures. Based on test results, we investigated the mechanisms governing the structure transition of gap-graded mixtures with increasing coarse fraction. See [J3, J4]. (a-2) We have proposed a structure variable to describe the evolution of inter-aggregate skeleton of gap-graded soils, expressed as a function of the coarse fraction, grain size distribution and natural of coarse aggregates. See [J1, J4, J5, J9]. (a-3) We have proposed two types of models for describing the compressibility of sandy clays. One is based on homogenization theory, and the other is formulated based on equivalent void ratio which may consider marine deposits with both fine-dominated structure and sand-dominated structure. Both models have been benchmarked and can be incorporated into consolidation models for time-dependent analysis of the settlement. See [J2, J6, J8, J10]. (b) Objective 2: (b-1) We have introduced an equivalent concept into the Kozeny-Carman formula to capture the effect of fines (aggregates) on the coarse-dominated (fine-dominated) structure and proposed a novel model for predicting the hydraulic conductivity of gap-graded soils. This provides a basis for describing the consolidation process. See [J7]. (b-2) We have proposed a novel elastic visco-plastic model based on Lagrangian formulation, which considers the effect of coarse fraction on the time-dependent behavior of marine deposit. The model was further implemented into finite element code for boundary value problems. (c) Objective 3: (c-1) We have done a series of consolidation tests considering the effect of initial water content and sand fraction, and have investigated the effect of sand fraction on the settlement and the evolution of excess pore water pressure of sandy clays. (c-2) The model has been verified by our experimental data in conjunction with data on the consolidation settlement of marine deposit and sand-bentonite mixtures from the literature. It is shown that the model is versatile to reproduce the time-dependent deformation of sandy clays with a wide range of initial state and sand fraction. Relevant work is summarized in a paper under preparation.

16201419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16201419.value: The project team developed experimental testing schemes and theoretical models to systematically investigate the behavior of gap-graded mixtures. The new theories and testing data enable us to accurately predict the time-dependent settlement of gap-graded marine clay. The importance of fine-coarse grain ratio to the hydraulic and mechanical response of gap-graded marine soils has been thoroughly examined to develop a novel elastic visco-plastic model for FEM simulation of boundary value problems in marine deposit. Further consolidation tests considering the effect of initial water content and sand fraction help us better understand the settlement and the evolution of excess pore water pressure of sandy clays. The research helps to advance our fundamental understanding of time-dependent consolidation and other complicated behavior of marine deposit, which play a key role in coastal land reclamation for Hong Kong and around the world.

16201819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16201819.value: In recent years, massively parallel systems such as MapReduce and Spark have been widely adopted in the industry as the de facto standard for large-scale data processing. The computational model of these systems is very different from the traditional sequential setting that programmers are used to. As a result, new algorithms will have to be designed and implemented to fully utilize the tremendous computing power and parallelism offered by these systems. On the theoretical front, the massively parallel computation (MPC) model has been proposed, giving a clean and elegant abstraction of these systems. This allows us to more easily design and analyze these algorithms. Consequently, many algorithms designed in the MPC model have been implemented in these systems and have been shown to work very well in practice. The join problem has been extensively studied in the literature. However, it remains one of the most expensive operations in database systems. This problem is particularly severe in massively parallel systems, because it is highly data-intensive, involving a lot of data shuffling. Since the MPC model focuses on minimizing the communication cost, the general consensus of the community is that it is indeed the right computational model in which join algorithms should be studied. In the database theory community, most efforts on the join problem in the MPC model have been devoted to worst-case efficient algorithms, following the traditional complexity notion in theoretical computer science. However, these algorithms are only optimal in the worst case, while worst-case instances are always join queries with a huge output size (a high polynomial function of the input size). On most typical database instances, the output size of a query is usually much smaller than the worst case, thus it is not clear if these worst-case optimal algorithms are the best choice on these instances. In this project, we aim to design MPC join algorithms whose performance depends not only on the input size, but also the output size. It is expected that output-sensitive algorithms would perform much better than worst-case algorithms on typical, non-worst-case database instances. 近年来，以MapReduce、Spark等为代表的大规模并行系统在工业界中得到广泛应用。这些并行系统所采用的计算模型和传统的串行计算模型有很大的不同，因此我们必须为这些新型系统设计专用的算法，从而可以充分利用它们庞大的并行性能。理论界所提出的“MPC”模型把这些系统进行了简化，从而可以为我们设计算法提供便利，而很多MPC算法也被成功的移植到实际系统中。 连接算法已在学术界被研究过很长时间。然而，连接操作仍然是数据库系统中最耗时的操作之一。在大规模并行系统中，由于连接操作设计大量数据的传输，这一问题尤其严重。因为MPC模型的核心正是数据传输，所以学术界的共识是MPC的确是研究MPC问题的一个正确方向。 在数据库理论界，按理论研究的传统，以往主要的研究核心为最坏情况最优算法。然而，这些算法仅在最坏情况下可以保证其最优性，而最坏情况下的数据实例通常有一个很大的输出。这些有很大输出的实例在实际数据上并不常见，所以对这些实例进行算法设计在实际中并不十分有效。在本项目中，我们的目标是设计出性能和输出大小相关的连接算法，这些算法在输出不大的典型实例中将大大优于最坏情况最优算法。

16201819.label: Realisation of objectives
16201819.value: We have achieved all three objectives of the project successfully. 1. We have laid down the theoretical foundation of output-sensitive algorithms for parallel acyclic joins. Specifically, we have achieved the following theoretical results: (1) For a large class of full acyclic joins, we have studied their circuit complexity, and give matching upper and lower bounds on the circuit size and depth. Since circuits with low depth correspond to parallel algorithms, these result carry over to the parallel setting naturally. (2) For the sparse matrix multiplication problem, we have given improved upper bounds on the load complexity in the parallel MPC model. (3) We have generalized the results on sparse matrix multiplication to a large class of acyclic joins with projection and aggregations, and given new load complexity results. 2. After laying down the theoretical foundation, we have designed new parallel algorithms for many common join queries. Specifically, we have designed new algorithms for the following class of queries: (1) For full acyclic joins, we have designed output-sensitive parallel algorithms with load cost matching the theoretical results. (2) For join-aggregate queries, we have designed output-sensitive parallel algorithms with load complexity matching the theoretical results. (3) For conjunctive queries with comparison, we have designed new algorithms. (4) We have also extended these algorithms to the secure MPC model, where parties do not trust each other. 3. Finally, we have also implemented these algorithms in Spark, a widely used large-scale parallel data processing system. Our experimental results have demonstrated significant improvement over previous algorithms. Our code has also been open-sourced.

16201819.value: Parallel query processing is a technique used in database systems to enhance query performance. It leverages multiple processors (or cores) to execute complex queries concurrently. Large-scale databases often store vast amounts of data. When users submit queries (such as retrieving sales data or analyzing customer behavior), the database must process these requests efficiently. Parallel processing allows the database to distribute the query workload across multiple processors. Each processor handles a portion of the data independently, resulting in faster execution. This project studies new algorithms on parallel query processing to reduce query response times, enhancing user experience.

16202119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202119.value: 鋰離子電池的溫度波動性和不均勻性是其在電動車中使用時的主要問題。在這個項目中，我們打算設計、模擬、製造和表徵一種由新型被動散熱器組成的電池熱管理系統。受到植物葉片中的蒸騰現象的啟發，這種吸液芯由微柱陣列（使用激光束熔融金屬3D打印方法製造）組成，呈梯度分佈，越靠近散熱器邊緣陣列間隙越小。散熱器與電池組相連以對其進行熱管理。當來自電池組的熱量通過蓋板傳遞到芯內的液體冷卻劑時，在微柱之間的每個微間隙內形成液體彎月面，產生向上吸引液體的毛細管力。分佈的微間隙的梯度將同時產生橫向毛細管力，使液體向邊緣擴散。因此，整個梯度流體結構上的蒸發保持均勻，從而在散熱器上產生均勻的溫度分佈。這種毛細管力驅動的散熱器設計簡單，沒有移動部件，易於製造，可以在所需要的範圍內自動調節電池組的工作溫度，同時保持整個電池組的均勻溫度分佈。為了確定這種新型散熱器的最佳設計，必須明確微尺度毛細管作用引起的熱液壓現象，我們將通過本項目中提出的創新的實驗和分析方法來實現。該項目的成果將加深我們對微觀結構中相變傳熱機理的理解，並提供設計這種被動式散熱器的必要信息。本項目將提供一種可靠的電池熱管理技術，以及時應對提高電動汽車的電池性能和安全性的挑戰。

16202119.label: Realisation of objectives
16202119.value: The project aimed to develop and validate a novel microfluidic heat spreader capable of enhancing thermal management in lithium-ion battery systems. The research objectives were comprehensively addressed with all planned activities successfully completed and significant results achieved. Objective 1: Conduct a Theoretical Analysis and Numerical Simulations of the Passive Heat Spreader Achievement: The project team conducted extensive theoretical analyses and numerical simulations to understand the heat transfer characteristics of the heat spreaders with various geometric parameters and material properties. The simulations provided vital insights into the optimal designs for efficient thermal management. The models successfully predicted the performance improvements, which were later validated through experimental results. Challenges and Solutions: No major challenges were encountered during this phase. The use of advanced simulation tools and techniques ensured accurate predictions and facilitated the smooth progression to experimental validation. Objective 2: Investigate Experimentally the Characteristics of the Evaporating Meniscus and In-Plane Fluid Flow Achievement: Experimental studies were carried out to examine the evaporating meniscus and in-plane fluid flow within microfluidic structures. Utilizing high-speed video imaging and advanced micro-PIV systems, the team successfully visualized and characterized fluid behaviors in microchannels of different sizes. These experiments confirmed the theoretical predictions and provided data critical for optimizing the microfluidic designs. Challenges and Solutions: One minor challenge was achieving precise control over experimental conditions to replicate the theoretical scenarios. This was addressed by refining the experimental setup and employing more sophisticated measurement techniques. Objective 3: Design and Fabricate Microfluidic Structures Based on Theoretical, Numerical, and Experimental Studies Achievement: Based on the insights gained from theoretical, numerical, and experimental studies, the team designed and fabricated several microfluidic heat spreader prototypes. These designs incorporated optimized channel geometries and materials to maximize thermal performance. Challenges and Solutions: The fabrication process initially faced challenges related to material compatibility and micro-scale precision. These were overcome by iterative testing and collaboration with experts in microfabrication technologies, ensuring high-quality prototypes. Objective 4: Test the Heat Transfer Performance of Heat Spreaders with Microfluidic Structures of Different Sizes Achievement: The fabricated heat spreader prototypes underwent rigorous thermal performance testing. The results demonstrated that the microfluidic heat spreaders consistently maintained lower temperatures and more uniform thermal distributions compared to traditional cooling methods. This confirmed the effectiveness of the designs in real-world conditions. Challenges and Solutions: The primary challenge was simulating high-load conditions in a controlled laboratory environment. Advanced testing setups were developed to mimic these conditions accurately, ensuring reliable performance data. Objective 5: Build and Demonstrate a Proof-of-Concept Battery Thermal Management System Incorporating the Microfluidic Heat Spreader Achievement: A proof-of-concept battery thermal management system was successfully built and demonstrated. This system integrated the microfluidic heat spreader with a lithium-ion battery pack, showcasing significant improvements in thermal management, safety, and efficiency under various operating conditions. Challenges and Solutions: Integrating the heat spreader with the battery system posed challenges related to system compatibility and optimization of coolant flow rates. These were addressed through iterative design adjustments and extensive testing to ensure seamless integration and optimal performance. Conclusion All research objectives were fully realized, with each phase of the project contributing to the successful development and validation of the microfluidic heat spreader. The project outcomes have not only demonstrated the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed technology but also laid the groundwork for future improvements and broader applications. This comprehensive approach ensured that the project goals were met, paving the way for enhanced thermal management solutions in various high-demand applications.
