16202119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202119.value: Overall, the project successfully demonstrated that microfluidic-structured heat spreaders could offer superior thermal management solutions, potentially revolutionizing the design and operation of thermal systems in various high-demand applications. This project investigated the development and analysis of a novel microfluidic structured heat spreader to improve the thermal management of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles (EVs). The project aimed to investigate innovative methods to effectively distribute and dissipate heat with a focus on improving safety, efficiency and performance. Development of a microfluidic heat spreader: The cornerstone of this project was the design and manufacture of a microfluidic heat spreader. This device incorporated micro-scale channels capable of precisely directing the flow of coolant, thereby optimizing heat absorption and dissipation from critical areas within lithium-ion batteries. Simulation and Optimisation: Advanced simulations were performed to model heat flow and coolant dynamics within the microfluidic structure. These simulations helped to identify optimal channel geometries and flow patterns to maximize heat transfer efficiency. Adjustments to coolant flow rates and temperatures were systematically tested to find the best conditions for heat management. Integration with battery systems: The microfluidic heat spreader was integrated into a battery thermal management system to evaluate its performance under real-world conditions. The device demonstrated significant improvements in managing temperature distribution across the battery pack, especially under high load conditions. Thermal performance testing: Experimental tests were conducted to compare the novel heat spreader with traditional cooling methods. The results showed that the microfluidic heat spreader maintained lower temperatures and more uniform temperature distribution, effectively reducing the risk of thermal runaway and extending battery life. Improving safety and efficiency: The project also investigated the safety improvements offered by the microfluidic heat spreader. The precise control of coolant flow and improved heat dissipation contributed to a safer operating environment for the batteries, reducing the likelihood of hazardous conditions. Future applications and improvements: The results of this project suggest that microfluidic heat spreaders can be effectively tailored for various applications beyond EV batteries, including electronics cooling and renewable energy systems. Further research is suggested to explore scalable manufacturing processes and integration with other thermal management technologies.

16202119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202119.value: The research on the novel microfluidic heat spreader shows promising avenues for further development and application. Future work should focus on scaling the technology for larger battery systems and exploring its adaptability to the varying operating conditions found in electric vehicles and beyond. Scalability: Investigate methods to scale the microfluidic heat spreader design for use in larger, commercial-scale battery packs. This will include optimizing channel dimensions and flow rates to maintain efficiency across different battery sizes and configurations. Materials innovation: Explore alternative materials for the construction of microfluidic channels that offer improved thermal properties, durability, and cost-effectiveness. Advanced composites or metal alloys could offer improved performance and manufacturability. Integration with renewable energy systems: Expand the application of microfluidic heat spreaders to manage thermal loads in renewable energy systems, such as solar panels and wind turbines, where efficient heat dissipation is critical to performance. Real-world testing and validation: Conduct extensive field testing to validate the performance of the microfluidic heat spreader under various environmental conditions and operational stresses typical of real-world scenarios. These steps will enhance the technology's practicality and pave the way for its wider adoption in thermal management solutions.

16202119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202119.value: Imagine your smartphone or laptop overheating, but much worse — this is similar to what happens in electric vehicles (EVs) where the batteries generate a lot of heat. Too much heat can shorten the battery's life or even pose safety risks. This research project developed a new device called a microfluidic-structured heat spreader to tackle this problem. It features tiny channels, akin to miniature rivers, through which a cooling fluid flows to efficiently carry away heat. The significance of this project lies in its potential to make EVs safer and more efficient. By improving battery temperature management, this technology could extend battery life and enhance vehicle performance. Moreover, this cooling technology isn’t limited to cars; it can also be used in other areas where electronics need to be kept cool, such as in renewable energy systems or portable electronics. Essentially, this project helps pave the way for more reliable and longer-lasting electronic devices and vehicles, contributing to advancements in sustainable technology.

16202219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202219.value: Ensuring potable water quality to safeguard public health is a fundamental goal of sustainable development. However, the task of supplying clean potable water is facing new challenges from increasing concentrations of micropollutants, such as endocrine-disrupting chemicals and pharmaceuticals and personal care product residues in source water. Many micropollutants are recalcitrant to conventional treatment processes, but heterogeneous photocatalysis using reactive, non-toxic and stable TiO2 is a promising approach for degrading these otherwise recalcitrant and toxic chemicals. However, light irradiation for photocatalysis can be scattered or occluded by aqueous constituents in full-scale reactors, and separation and recovery of photocatalysts is energy-intensive. TiO2-coated quartz optical fibers (TiO2-QOFs) can overcome these challenges by delivery UV light directly to TiO2 on the fibers’ surface to drive photocatalytic degradation. However, most of the light delivered into TiO2-QOFs from the light source tends to be extensively refracted away. As so, only a small portion of the light delivered into TiO2-QOFs activates TiO2, while the majority is wasted. This proposed research aims to develop a novel TiO2-QOF system to reduce the light wasted and enhance the photocatalytic micropollutant degradation in TiO2-QOFs by minimizing the contact between TiO2 and QOFs or depositing a metallic/polymeric interlayer on the QOFs before coating TiO2. We hypothesize that this novel coating approach can achieve a better distribution of the irradiation in TiO2-QOFs by reducing light refraction so as to enhance the intensity of evanescent waves generated during the total internal reflection in TiO2-QOFs. Four nano-scale TiO2 structures will be prepared and loaded on raw QOFs and on QOFs coated with a thin film of palladium, titanium or polyethylene (TiO2-(metal/polymer-)QOFs). The structures so fabricated will be characterized using various solid-state and spectroscopic technologies (e.g. SEM-EDX, AFM, XPS and FT-IR). Batch experiments will be conducted to evaluate their photocatalytic degradation performance and to optimize the QOFs’ diameter, the incident light angle and the light intensity to yield the highest photocatalytic degradation rates and lowest irradiation wastage. The light activation mechanisms leading to any observed performance differences will be investigated. The impacts of commonly-occurring water parameters on the photocatalytic performance of the TiO2-(metal/polymer-)QOFs will be assessed. Lastly, a prototype flow-through reactor will be developed based on the aforementioned tests to evaluate the long term performance of the TiO2-(metal/polymer-)QOFs after regeneration and reuse. The results from this study can be expected to advance the technology of photocatalytic micropollutant degradation in potable water to safeguard public health. 確保飲用水水質以保障公眾健康一直以來都是可持續發展的基本目標之壹。然而水源中不斷增加的微污染物，例如，內分泌干擾化學品以及藥品和個人護理產品，給飲用水安全帶來了新的挑戰。這些微污染物通常較難被傳統的水處理工藝去除。然而，採用活性高、無毒且化學穩定的二氧化鈦為催化劑的非均相光催化處理工藝為降解這些難降解和有毒的化學物質提供了一種方法。這種光催化處理工藝在實際運用中存在重大挑戰，因為光線會被水中的物質分散或者遮擋，從而降低光能量的利用效率，同時光催化劑的回收也會消耗較高能耗。這些挑戰都能夠被二氧化鈦塗覆的石英光纖（TiO2-QOFs）克服。紫外光可以直接通過光線傳輸到光纖表面的二氧化鈦薄膜上用來驅動光催化降解反應，從而避免光被分散和遮擋，同時減少光催化劑在回收時的能耗。但是，傳輸進入TiO2-QOFs的光會被大量折射出光纖，其中只有壹小部分光能夠有效激發二氧化鈦，大部分則被浪費。本研究旨在開發壹種新型TiO2-QOF系統，通過最小化二氧化鈦薄膜和光纖表面之間的接觸或在塗覆二氧化鈦之前先在光纖表面沈積壹層金屬或者聚合物，從而減少光的損失並增強微污染物的降解。我們推測上述新型塗覆方法可以減少光的折射，同時增強光纖中由全反射產生的漸逝波的能量，從而實現光在TiO2-QOF中更好的分布和利用。我們將制備四種納米級的二氧化鈦結構並塗覆在裸光纖以及有鈀、鈦或聚乙烯層包覆的光纖表面上（TiO2-(metal/polymer-)QOFs），並使用各種固態和光譜技術（例如SEM-EDX，AFM，XPS和FT-IR）來表徵它們的結構。我們將進行批量實驗以評估它們在光催化過程中對污染物降解的性能，並通過優化光纖直徑，入射光角度和光強度以實現最快的光催化降解速率和最少的光輻照損耗。同時，不同光纖結構下的光激活機制及其對光催化污染物降解性能的影響也會被研究。之後，我們會評估常見水參數對TiO2-(metal/polymer-)QOFs光催化性能的影響。我們將基於上述測試結果開發壹種連續推流式原型反應器，用以評估TiO2-(metal/polymer-)QOFs在長期使用時的性能以及其再生和再利用性。該研究結果有望推動光催化降解微污染物在飲用水中的應用，以保障公眾飲用水安全。

16202219.label: Realisation of objectives
16202219.value: Objective 1 was completed. The micropollutant degradation by TiO2-coated quartz optical fibers (TiO2-QOFs) with different coating structures were investigated. The coating structure was characterized by two parameters: i) TiO2 patchiness (p), defined as the ratio of the fiber surface with direct TiO2 contact to the total fiber surface, and ii) the average interspace distance between the fiber surfaces and coated layers (za). The parameters were determined by measuring the light dissipation in TiO2-QOFs substituted into a model developed in Objective 3, and then were verified by electron microscopy. The impact of coating structures was examined by degrading carbamazepine (CBZ). By reducing p to 0.034 and increasing za to 114.3 nm, refraction was reduced, and 91% of light propagated on the surface was evanescent waves, which returns to the fiber if not absorbed. Such changes in coating structures resulted in efficient interactions between TiO2 and light and thus doubled CBZ degradation rates and quantum yields (Nature Communications in 2021). When coating a platinum interlayer with thickness of 2‒10 nm to fabricate TiO2-metal-QOFs, light absorption was enhanced but most of the absorbed light was converted to heat. The remaining light used to activate TiO2 achieved higher quantum efficiency. However, the overall performance was not as good as that without metal. Meanwhile, a polymeric interlayer coating with thickness lower than one wavelength of light enables evanescent waves absorption regardless of TiO2 layer thickness or patchiness. However, such thin nano polymer coating is very difficult to be made. Objective 2 aiming to optimize light propagation in TiO2-QOFs to maximize light utilization was completed. Box-Behnken design of response surface methodology was used to investigate the impact of four tunable variables of coated fibers and light emission conditions, including p, minimum light incident angles (θm), radiant flux launched to fibers (Ei), and fiber diameter (D), on improving the light dissipation uniformity along TiO2-QOFs. Uniformity was found to increase with decreasing p, increasing θm, reducing Ei, and enlarging D, and the order of the importance follows: p > θm >> Ei ≈ D. Substantial enhancements in the quantity of evanescent waves generation were observed when decreasing p from 0.2 to 0.02 and increasing θm from 69° and 84°, resulting in uniform light dissipation which reduces light oversaturation and extend the length of TiO2-QOFs by over 10 times. Such optimizations led to a remarkable three-fold improvement in CBZ degradation rates and quantum yields. On the other hand, changing Ei and D improved uniformity but did not enhance CBZ degradation, because the percentage of evanescent waves remained the same. The fundamental discoveries of optimizing light propagation in TiO2-QOFs enhances the practicality of energy-efficient and oxidant-free photocatalysis for micropollutant degradation. These findings were presented in ACS Spring 2022 National Meeting & Exposition (Conference Paper #3). Objective 3 was completed, aiming at developing an energy balance model to quantify the evanescent waves and refracted light in activating TiO2 coated on optical fibers. Briefly, the model was developed by simulating the light propagation in TiO2-QOFs using geometrical optics and considering TiO2 coating structures (i.e., p and za) interacted with the two energy forms. In this model, light rays at different angles are emitted and each ray continuously strikes the inner fiber surfaces, which i) generates evanescent waves at the quartz/water/TiO2 interface and/or returns into the fiber, or ii) activates attached TiO2 through refraction at the quartz/TiO2 interface. The model suggests p and za are the key to control evanescent waves for manipulate light. With decreasing p and increasing za, refraction is reduced while evanescent waves are enhanced. This model was also upgraded to module the optical near fields (ONFs) of optical fibers. The model suggests over 90% of the dissipated light (Edis) is absorbed in ONFs when p is lower than 0.3, attributing to the high quantity of evanescent waves. The percentage of Edis to Ei becomes tunable from 0 to 1 if further managing the absorption of evanescent waves by regulating za from 200 to 0 nm. These modeling results were then experimentally verified. The ONF interaction could also be modulated by regulating Ʌ of evanescent waves with θm, wavelength (λ), and the refractive index of materials. The established light management strategies show potential to optimize different functional material coated optical fibers. The established model for light quantification together with the findings in Objective 1 were published to Nature Communications in 2021 (Journal Paper #1) and Water in 2023 (Journal Paper #3), and presented in ACS Fall 2019 National Meeting (Conference Paper #1). A manuscript reported the ONF management in optical fibers using this model are under preparation (Journal Paper #6). The model also offers insights to design fiber-based technologies. For example, manipulating evanescent waves with coating structures enhances the uniformity of the side-emitted ultraviolet light in silica nanoparticle coated quartz optical fibers for improving the disinfection performance. This attempt was formulated to a journal paper in Environmental Science: Nano in 2021 (Journal Paper #2). Objective 4 was completed, which investigated commonly occurring water parameters on TiO2-QOFs and their long-term performance in a prototype reactor. CBZ degradation by TiO2-QOFs was conducted to investigate the impacts of pH, sulfate, chloride (Cl−), bicarbonate (HCO3−), free chlorine, and NOM. The CBZ degradation was unaffected by Cl− and HCO3−. The CBZ degradation rate constant (k) was increased with increasing pH from 6 to 8.5. An increase of k by 62% was observed with an increase in sulfate concentration from 0 to 60 μM, because sulfate can adhere to TiO2 surfaces and trap h+ for preventing e‒ and h+ recombination. As free chlorine dosage increased from 0 to 0.5 mg/L, k increased by 3.5 times, because chlorine acts both as catalysts activated by h+ to promote hydroxyl radicals (HO•), and as a radical precursor that reacts with e− to produce HO•. Although NOM inhibits the CBZ degradation, TiO2-QOFs still outperform the TiO2 slurry system by 120‒200 times. A manuscript reported the above findings together with the study in Objective 2 was submitted to Water Research (Journal Paper #4). The prototype flow-through reactor was assembled by installing a bundle of 19 TiO2-QOFs, at p of 0.032, into a 250 mL reactor. This bundle was regulated with varying fiber spacing from 1 to 3 mm and was directly irradiated by a 3 W and 365 nm LED lamp. The reactor showed a k of 0.53 h-1 towards CBZ degradation at fiber spacing of 1 mm, which was reduced by 29% with increasing the fiber spacing to 3 mm due to the reduced collection of divergent light by the fiber when positioned away from the reactor axis. Besides, k remained unchanged for the 3 testing cycles, each lasting 4 hours, suggesting TiO2 coating was stable. A new fiber bundle reactor contained 150 individual g-C3N4 coated polymeric optical fibers (g-C3N4-POFs) with high mass-loading was also developed. This reactor showed 4 times higher micropollutant degradation rates under 420 nm irradiation than a slurry reactor, because of high mass loading, good light management, and improved pollutant mass transport. These g-C3N4-POFs maintained structural integrity even after 20 cycles of treatment (Water Research, 2023) (Journal Paper #4).

16202219.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202219.value: The major findings obtained from this study have formulated 4 prestigious journal papers (#1‒4) and 3 conference presentations (#1‒3) in three outstanding international conferences. We are also working on two other journal papers (#5‒6). This study provided training of 1 postgraduate student who obtained his PhD degree in August 2022. The specific major findings are: An energy balance model was developed by correlating TiO2 coating structures with two light energy forms (evanescent waves and refracted light) in TiO2-QOFs, which serves as a tool to simulate light dissipation in different photocatalyst-coated optical fibers (P-OFs), guide P-OF-based reactor designs, and modulate the optical near fields of optical fibers for optimizing light-driven processes (Journal paper #1, #4, and #6) and Conference paper #1. The coating structure is the key to manage light in TiO2-QOFs. By reducing TiO2 patchiness on fibers and increasing the average interspace distance between the fiber surface and TiO2 coatings, refraction is reduced, and evanescent wave generation is promoted. The generated evanescent waves either activate TiO2 or return to optical fibers if not absorbed, reducing energy losses and thus enhance micropollutant degradation (Journal paper #1 and #3 and Conference paper #1‒2). More strategies of modulating evanescent waves were explored by regulating patchiness, light incident angles, radiant flux launched to fibers, and fiber diameters. Such modulations allow uniform light dissipation in TiO2-QOFs which reduces light oversaturation and improves light transmission distances, resulting in remarkable improvement in CBZ degradation rates and energy efficiency (Journal paper #5 and Conference paper #3). The impacts of water matrices on micropollutant degradation by TiO2-QOFs were also explored. The increase in pH and the presence of sulfate and free chlorine enhances the CBZ degradation, while NOM inhibits it. (Journal paper #5). The fundaments were extended to three applications. First, manipulating evanescent waves with coating structures enhanced disinfection performance by the unform side-emitted UV light from silica coated quartz optical fibers (Journal paper #2). Second, the modulation of light dissipation uniformity and extension of the lengths in TiO2-QOFs allow the energy-efficient and oxidant-free photocatalysis to be an optimal option to combat the micropollutant challenges in water storage tanks for supplying clean drinking water (Journal paper #5). Besides, we changed the coated photocatalyst and fiber materials to develop cost-effective g-C3N4-POFs and develop a fiber bundle reactor using the g-C3N4-POFs for micropollutant degradation under visible light (Journal paper #4).

16202219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202219.value: This research shows excellent potential for further development, particularly in exploring the coating strategies and materials for other types of photocatalyst coated optical fibers (P-OFs), enhancing the developed energy balance model, and identifying other novel applications. The first course of action is to investigate strategies of coating different photocatalysts such as ZnO, WO3, and g-C3N4 for coating on optical fibers. It will also be beneficial to determine the performance of cost-effective polymer optical fibers when coupled with visible or infrared light sources. Second, with more P-OF configurations emerge, advanced light simulation methods need to be developed to accurately trace light paths and quantify the light energy in P-OFs. Wave functions could replace geometrical optics for a more precise description of light behavior at fiber interfaces. Lastly, the potential of the coated optical fiber concept extends to several applications such as groundwater treatment, photocatalytic water splitting for H2 production, and CO2 reduction. In addition, P-OFs could enhance disinfection in challenging environments and increase the energy efficiency of photovoltaic cells. A new platform using optical fiber could also provide a more accurate quantification of photocatalyst performance. Overall, these directions offer a promising future for P-OF research.

16202219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202219.value: The supply of clean drinking water is facing challenges with the increasing impacts from emerging micropollutants. Coupling TiO2-QOFs with LEDs presents a promising solution to degrade micropollutants, but is limited by light management, specifically light oversaturation and energy losses caused by excessive refraction and short light transmission distances along fibers. This research overcomes this limitation and reveals strategies to optimize the light usage in TiO2-QOFs by maximizing evanescent waves which propagate at fiber surfaces and return to the fiber if not absorbed by the coated TiO2. We fabricated TiO2-QOFs with different coating conditions and developed an energy balance model to investigate how those TiO2-QOFs impact evanescent waves. We found the coating layer structure is the key to reduce refraction and promote evanescent wave generation. We used the developed theory to modulate evanescent waves, achieving uniform light dissipation along TiO2-QOFs to reduce energy losses and longer light transmission distances to increase reactive sites for enhancing pollutant degradation rates. We tested the optimized TiO2-QOFs in water metrices and built TiO2-QOF bundle reactors which showed promising results and stability over multiple cycles. This technology could potentially be a more efficient and cost-effective way to clean drinking water.

16202519.label: Project Objectives
16202519.value: To develop and apply an analytical model to study sound attenuation by acoustic metasurfaces under non-uniform mean flows with acoustic plane waves at various incident angles and frequencies. To conduct CAA simulations of metasurfaces with non-uniform impedance distributions to validate the analytical model based on solutions of linearized Euler equations (LEE). To develop numerically stable and computationally efficient time-domain impedance boundary conditions based on the state-space realization approach. To design and construct an aeroacoustic oblique plane wave (AOPW) test rig to measure the sound field induced by plane waves across ±45 degrees interacting with various metasurfaces. To conduct aeroacoustic measurements that will provide input conditions for parallel analytical studies and computations, leading to surface impedance eduction of individual metasurface sub-structures and to assess the impedance value dependence on Mach number, Reynolds number, incident angle, and frequency. To perform experiments in a grazing incidence tube (GIT) to extend the surface impedance database developed using oblique plane waves, providing data at 90 degrees. To optimize the metasurface for maximum transmission loss across the GIT. The optimization process will rely on the surface impedance database developed in objectives 3 and 4 together with the analytical model developed in objective 1. The optimized metasurface will be uniquely configured of periodically arranged sub-structures and guide the energy-containing high-order diffraction waves to propagate along the metasurface, thereby maximizing the sound absorption.

16202519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202519.value: The proposed research focuses on the aeroacoustic physics and assessment of sub-wavelength metasurfaces. Noise attenuation devices in flow environments, such as acoustic liners used in aero-engines, are often based on Helmholtz resonators constructed of a honeycomb layer between a perforated sheet and a solid back plate. These devices offer noise reduction across a narrow band of frequencies. Metasurfaces with periodically arranged sub-structures generate a specular wave and high-order diffraction waves. By optimizing the sub-structural configuration, the angle of the high-order waves containing most of the acoustic energy can be aligned with the metasurface, resulting in near-perfect sound absorption performance. The major physics of metasurface acoustics in a stationary medium can be described by analytical models and studied by numerical simulations and experiments. However, no studies of metasurface acoustics in aerodynamic flows currently exist. Non-uniform shear flows may induce a convective effect on wave propagation and the local flows near the metasurface sub-structures, which may generate new noise sources. To attain optimal noise reduction by the metasurfaces in flow environment requires a specific phase-angle gradient, which is directly related to the impedance characteristics that are likely dependent on the aerodynamic flow properties. This research aims to provide answers and solutions to key issues by the following means. Firstly, a generalized aeroacoustic model will be developed that incorporates a generic shear layer velocity profile. Computational aeroacoustics will be used to validate the analytical model. Secondly, a new aeroacoustic oblique wave test rig will be developed and experiments conducted. This new facility will provide the means to study the reflected sound field by normal and oblique plane waves interacting with metasurfaces in flow environments. Thirdly, an impedance eduction database will be developed using measurements acquired from the aeroacoustic oblique wave test rig and a grazing flow incidence tube as well from analytical solutions. Surface impedance values at different incident angles, flow velocities, acoustic wavelengths, and material properties will be studied. Using this database, an optimal metasurface will be designed and evaluated. The research should provide a comprehensive understanding of aeroacoustic metasurface physics and develop experimental and numerical tools to explore potential applications in engineering problems. The proposed project builds on the research team's expertise and R&D experiences in aeroacoustics, materials and manufacturing sciences.

16202519.label: Realisation of objectives
16202519.value: The proposed objectives have been achieved by using theoretical, numerical, and experimental studies. The research findings from the project have been published in reputable journals, such as the Journal of Sound and Vibration, The Journal of Acoustical Society of America, Composite Structures, International Journal of Mechanical Science, and others. Additionally, a PhD student was supported, who is expected to graduate in 2024. The main accomplishments related to the stated objectives are summarized below. 1. We have theoretically investigated the flow effect on the sound reflection performance of the periodic acoustic metasurfaces (AMs). A convective generalized Snell’s law (CGSL) is derived to account for the effect of uniform mean flows on the reflection of AMs. When applying the AM to a shear flow, theoretical analysis suggests that the wave manipulation performance of the metasurface can be deteriorated under oblique incidence in the shear flow due to the convection effects. To addressing it, an AMs design method considering the mean flow profile is proposed based on the impedance transformation method. The strategy is to form a reflected phase gradient at the interface plane between the uniform and the sheared flow regions. This design method has been employed to design a porous metasurface which successfully realizes effective wave manipulation in a grazing shear flow. 2. We have numerically investigated the reflection performance of the acoustic metasurface in a grazing shear flow by using CAA simulations, in which the metasurface is modeled by a set of non-uniform impedance. Numerical results show good agreements with the analytical predictions on the orders and directions of the reflected waves by the periodic metasurface. A computationally efficient time-domain impedance boundary condition was developed based on the state-space theory. By employing the impedance model into the CAA model, the sound attenuation performance of the non-uniform impedance in a grazing flow can be accurately predicted. 3. An acoustic oblique plane wave (AOPW) test rig has been designed and manufactured in HKUST. The test rig can provide a fully-developed high-quality aerodynamic flow with a maximum speed up to 45 m/s. A plane sound wave synthesis system was embedded in the rig, which can generate a stable background plane wave sound field with incident angle varying from -45 degrees to 45 degrees. The reflected sound field of a metasurface is measured under oblique incidences at different Mach numbers. Results show that the direction of the reflected wave can be accurately predicted by the proposed convective generalized Snell’s law (CGSL). 4. In this project, we have measured the acoustic surface impedance for a kind of meta liner consisting of Helmholtz resonators with extend necks (HRENs) in an advanced grazing incidence tube (GIT) facility in HKUST. Based on the experiment, an impedance database at 90-degree sound incidence has been established for the HRENs with different geometric parameters including orifice radius, neck length, cavity size and depth. The impedance database was used to inversely determine the geometry of the HREN-based unit cell in the metasurface design. 5. In this project, we have employed the particle swarm optimization (PSO) to optimize the absorption performance of the HREN-based metasurface. The strategy is of using inhomogeneous HRNEs to achieve effective absorption in a specified frequency range. The acoustic performance of the metasurface is quantitatively evaluated by measuring the transmission loss (TL) in the GIT. A superior sound attenuation performance is achieved by the optimized metasurface compared to the conventional acoustic liner.

16202519.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202519.value: 1. An analytical model was developed to predict the sound reflection of periodic AM in a grazing uniform flow. The research outcome led to an analytical correction to the classical theory of GSL derived in a static medium. 2. A metasurface design method was developed to account for the convection effects of the grazing shear flow. This method can be used to guide the metasurface design operating in the aerodynamic conditions. 3. A surface impedance database of HRENs was established through experimental measurement. Based on the data base, an optimization method is developed to improve the sound absorption performance of the HREN-based metasurface. 4. An acoustic oblique plane wave (AOPW) test rig has been designed and manufactured which possess the capability of measuring the scattering sound filed of metasurface in a high-quality aerodynamic condition.

16202519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202519.value: 1. The proposed CGSL theories can be used for the analysis of reflection performance of metasurface in flow conditions, and the proposed design method can guide the metasurface design in non-uniform flow. The study can enhance our understanding of the aerodynamic effects on the metasurface. 2. The established surface impedance database of the HRNEs can be applied to the metasurface design in flow conditions. The effects of more complex aerodynamic environments, such as high temperature and high sound pressure level, are interesting and challenging, and can be further considered in the future. 3. The developed acoustic oblique plane wave (AOPW) test rig can support the experimental study of the performance of acoustic metasurface and other treatments in flow conditions under oblique incidence. It will be challenging to consider the acoustic behavior of the metasurface in the three-dimensional space and under the acoustic mode incidence.

16202519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202519.value: This study considers the aeroacoustic behavior of metasurfaces in aerodynamic flows. The problem is challenging because of our limited understanding of the aeroacoustic physics of metasurface, including the convection and refraction effects of the non-uniform flow on the interaction between sound and metasurface, and changes to surface impedance caused by the flow. In this project, we developed methods and the test rig that can simulate the performance of aeroacoustic structure in a non-uniform grazing flow, such as the liners or metasurface in aeroengines. We can design the metasurface operating the flow conditions with customized functionalities such as wave steering and surface wave conversion. The developed test rig in this project is also a necessary tool to apply metasurface technology to the practical aeroacoustic problems, such as the low-noise design and optimization for the aeroengines.

16202619.label: Project Objectives
16202619.value: Objective 1: Deriving Efficient Policies to Dispatch, Reposition, and Recharge EVs in EMoD systems It is widely recognized that electric vehicle (EV)-based mobility-on-demand (EMoD) systems are a promising solution to the increasing demand for mobility in future sustainable smart cities. To promote a profitable and successful business, the EMoD system needs to make decisions in three areas. First, EVs are supplied resources that need to be repositioned between service regions to meet the unbalanced demand for mobility over both time and space. Second, EVs need to be efficiently scheduled to recharge at limited charging facilities in order to maintain large enough state-of-charge (SoC) to satisfy the demand for mobility. Third, upon the arrival of a demand for mobility, which EV to dispatch to which customer must be decided when multiple EVs with different SoCs are available. To make these decisions efficiently with uncertain demands for mobility, the first objective of this project is to propose a stochastic dynamic program framework to dispatch, reposition, and recharge EVs in EMoD systems. Based on this framework, we will first solve the problem numerically for a small-scale case, and explore the structural properties of the optimal policies. For a large-scale system, we will apply certainty-equivalent and approximate dynamic programming frameworks to tackle the computational difficulties. Objective 2: Designing Incentive Mechanisms for Mobility and Energy Management of EMoD Systems In current practice, an EMoD system needs to hire a team of drivers to manually reposition EVs between service regions. The manual repositioning of EVs is costly and can significantly lower the profitability of the system. A promising idea to reduce repositioning cost is to reshape the mobility demand by providing well-designed incentives so that customers can help to rebalance the system. The second objective of this project is to design an incentive mechanism to reduce the repositioning cost, and hence improve the total profits of the EMoD system. To do so, we will propose an incentive mechanism to adjust the prices between origin and destination regions upon the arrival of each customer, based on the system state and the customers' valuations. We will integrate the pricing decisions with our proposed dynamic program to make optimal operational decisions. The reformulated problem will be challenging because of the incentive compatibility and individual rationality constraints, which naturally arise from self-interested customers. We will propose efficient algorithms to obtain the (approximate) optimal prices. Objective 3: Assessing the Value of Autonomous Driving in EMoD Systems Recent years have witnessed the rapid development and maturity of autonomous driving technology. Suppose all EVs in the EMoD system have autonomous driving enabled. The repositioning cost can be significantly reduced because of the reduced labor. Moreover the recharging cost can also be reduced because EVs can drive itself to public charging stations seeking cheap charging opportunities. The third objective of this project is to assess the value of autonomous driving in both operations and infrastructure planning for EMoD systems. Based on real data, we will assess the reduction of repositioning and recharging costs and the overall improvement of total profits for an autonomous EMoD system compared to current EMoD systems. In addition, we will propose an infrastructure planning model using the stochastic dynamic program framework. Leveraging this model, we will evaluate the influence of autonomous driving in planning infrastructure parameters such as the numbers of EVs and chargers in EMoD systems.

16202619.label: Realisation of objectives
16202619.value: (1) Realization of Objective 1: The first objective of this project is to develop efficient sequential decision-making models and algorithms tailed to manage the mobility and energy of electric vehicles (EVs) in an electric mobility-on-demand (EMoD) system, with a focus on maximizing the expected system revenue. We consider an operator of the EMoD system, responsible for making real-time decisions to manage a large fleet of EVs under the uncertainties of mobility demand and EV charger availability. Specifically, the operator makes three types of decisions over a finite time horizon: (i) Dispatching EVs: the operator dispatches EVs to fulfill mobility demand, ensuring a quality-of-service (QoS) guarantee. (ii) Repositioning EVs: in response to the unbalanced mobility demand across different time and location, EVs are strategically repositioned. (iii) Recharging EVs: EVs with low state-of-charges (SoCs) are recharged to alleviate range-anxiety. We formulate the sequential decision-making problem as a stochastic dynamic program (DP). To address the well-known curse-of-dimensionality challenge often encountered in practical EMoD systems, we identify and rigorously demonstrate that the value function (i.e., the reward-to-go function in DP formulation) exhibits a coordinate-wise concave property. Leveraging this structural property, we propose to use a separable piecewise linear function to approximate the value function and design an approximation-based algorithm to efficiently derive the decision policy. Based on the proposed algorithm, the operator can make the decisions within seconds and obtain a near-optimal system revenue. Extensive simulations validate the superior performance of our proposed algorithm compared to existing model-free approaches, including greedy heuristic and Q-learning, which overlook the structural property of the DP problem. In summary, Objective 1 of this project has been completely achieved. (100%) (2) Realization of Objective 2: The second objective of this project aims to introduce an innovative incentive mechanism to strategically reshape the mobility demand patterns within the EMoD system. This mechanism incentivizes system customers to actively balance the EV supply and mobility demand across temporal and spatial domains. Our approach centers on the development of a dynamic pricing algorithm that integrates multiple decision facets, including pricing the EMoD services, dispatching and repositioning EVs across service regions, and recharging EVs to maintain their energy levels. This comprehensive algorithm is designed based on a bi-level optimization problem. The lower-level problem focuses on ensuring the incentive compatibility of customers, where each customer makes traveling decisions by maximizing their utility. Meanwhile, the upper-level problem aims to maximize the overall system revenue and is formulated as a stochastic dynamic programming problem. In this problem, the operator initiates the process by announcing EMoD service prices, followed by operational decisions related to repositioning and recharging EVs. After receiving the prices, all customers make travel decisions in the lower-level problem. Given the temporal coupling of sequential decisions and the nonstationary nature of the policies, the decision-making process necessitates repeated solutions of computationally challenging integer programs in each step. The inherent bi-level structure of the problem further complicates the process. To obtain (near) optimal solution in a practical-scale EMoD system, we first transform the bi-level problem into a single-level one by leveraging the structure of the formulation. Additionally, we prove the coordinate-wise concavity of the single-level formulation, and then propose an approximate dynamic programming algorithm to efficiently obtain near-optimal solutions. Our proposed approach can efficiently yield dynamic pricing decisions for the EMoD system and achieve significant performance improvement compared to heuristic static pricing strategy and other existing model-free methods, such as Q-learning. In summary, Objective 2 of this project has been finished. (100%) (3) Realization of Objective 3: The previous two objectives primarily focus on real-time decision-making within a predetermined EV network infrastructure, with the purpose of enhancing system benefits. The third objective of this project is to further investigate and improve the system benefit across both real-time operations and infrastructure planning. We consider the scenario where EVs operate as autonomous vehicles instead of strategic players, who choose charging stations in a probabilistic manner based on their preferences. In this case, EVs directly follow the assignment from the operator (i.e., EVs choose the recommended station with 100% probability). For a given setup of the system infrastructure (e.g., numbers of EVs and available chargers) in the EMoD system, we leverage the real-time decision-making policies derived in the previous two objectives to assess the expected revenue of the EMoD system. We then evaluate the impact of infrastructure setup on the overall revenue in both planning and real-time operations by extensive numerical tests, which are conducted within the transportation networks of Hong Kong using real-time traffic data. To enhance our theoretical understanding of the joint decisions of planning and real-time operations, we further study a network of geographically distributed battery swapping stations (BSSs). From the perspective of the network operator, we focus on two important decisions made in two different timescales, i.e., a long-term decision on planning the initial inventory in each individual BSS, and a short-term decision on real-time vehicle-to-station (V2S) routing of EVs. We formulate a two-stage optimization problem and propose a two-step solution scheme, where the initial inventory is optimally determined in the first-step by maximizing the expected revenue of the network. Based on the optimal initial inventory obtained in the first step, we propose a randomized online recommendation-based V2S routing algorithm in the second step, without assuming any future information. Leveraging a principled primal-dual analysis, we rigorously prove the worst-case performance is theoretically bounded by a closed-form competitive ratio, parameterized by the initial inventory in BSSs. In summary, Objective 3 of this project has been completely achieved. (100%)

16202619.label: Major findings and research outcome
16202619.value: First, we introduce a novel sequential decision-making model for optimizing the mobility and energy management of EMoD systems. We frame this problem as a stochastic dynamic program, with the goal of efficiently dispatching, repositioning, and recharging EVs to maximize the system revenue. Leveraging the structural property of the dynamic program, we design an efficient algorithm to obtain the optimized policies based on approximate dynamic programing techniques. Our algorithm significantly outperforms all existing benchmark algorithms in the experiments. The research outcomes of this part have been published in the journal paper [J6] listed in Part C. Recognizing the particular challenges of EV charging in the EMoD system, we further explore the design and analysis of online algorithms for the real-time control of EV charging. We introduce a model-free deep reinforcement learning algorithm for scheduling the charging process of groups of EVs, capitalizing on historical EV charging data [J3]. Moreover, in situations where no past data is available, we have designed novel threshold-based algorithms for scheduling EV charging and proved that their performances are theoretically bounded by closed-form competitive ratios under the classical framework of competitive analysis [C2][C3][J1][J5]. Second, we develop an online pricing strategy for the EMoD system based on a bi-level optimization model. This model accounts for customers’ incentive compatibility in the lower-level problem and optimizes the system revenue in the upper-level problem. An efficient algorithm is designed to solve this problem by leveraging a reformulation technique and the problem structure [J4]. In addition, if we focus on recharging decisions, we further develop an online pricing and charging scheduling algorithm that can balance the spatial and temporal demand of customers and reduce the overall EV charging cost. The performance of the proposed algorithm is theoretically guaranteed by a competitive ratio [C1]. Third, we investigate the joint infrastructure planning and real-time operations for the EMoD system based on extensive experiments using real data [J4][J6]. To obtain theoretical understanding of this problem, we study the planning and operations for a network of battery swapping stations, in which we make a long-term decision on planning the initial inventory in each individual BSS, and a short-term decision on real-time vehicle-to-station routing of EVs. We develop a two-step solution scheme and rigorously prove that the worst-case performance of the proposed algorithm is guaranteed by the theoretical competitive ratio [J2].

16202619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202619.value: This project primarily focuses on developing sequential decision-making models and algorithms for managing the mobility and energy of EMoD systems. While our proposed model is rather general, encompassing the entire decision-making process of EMoD systems, our algorithm is crafted based on the inherent problem structure, without harnessing the historical EMoD data that is increasingly becoming available. Thus, it is a promising direction to make use of the valuable data by exploring the development of model-free deep reinforcement learning based algorithms for optimizing the policies of our proposed decision-making model. In addition, our project has yielded several theoretical results based on the worst-case competitive analysis, which makes no assumptions on future knowledge. However, in practical scenarios, additional information about the future may be predicted based on the powerful machine learning tools and historical data. Thus, further investigations are needed to study how to incorporate predictions into the design and analysis of our algorithms to achieve beyond-the-worst-case results.

16202619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202619.value: In this project, we are tackling the transportation challenges posed by the ever-growing urban population. As cities become more crowded, they bring problems like air pollution and traffic jams that directly impact our overall well-being. To address these issues, we are developing a transformative approach to urban transportation. Our focus is on self-driving electric vehicles that you can call whenever you need a ride. This innovative approach translates into fewer conventional cars on the road, resulting in cleaner air, and more convenient transportation for everyone. Our mission is to develop the key technologies to make this system operate seamlessly, like figuring out which car should pick up which passenger, reducing traffic congestion, and finding efficient ways to charge these electric vehicles. The outcomes of our project aim to make cities better places to live with a smaller environmental footprint, enhancing the quality of life for residents in smart sustainable cities.

16202919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16202919.value: The second quantum revolution is dawning. Exciting quantum science and technologies based on individual quantum systems (e.g., trapped ions, electron spins and single photons) or even ensembles of quantum systems are emerging rapidly. Research into the generation of single-photons and entangled photon-pairs has been a major subject of investigation for several decades, using various technological platforms including bulk second-order nonlinear crystals, nonlinear fiber or waveguide optics, quantum confinement structures (e.g., quantum dots), optically active defects in crystals and nonlinear photonic integrated circuits (PICs). Semiconductor-based nonlinear PICs at room temperature are likely to be a key building block for quantum technologies because of their mechanical stability, scalability and compatibility with both standard nanofabrication processes and optical-fiber networks. Integrated waveguides with a micrometer-scale cross-section and resonators with a high quality (Q) factor in PICs can increase the optical power density and thus the light-matter interaction over a small footprint substantially, enhancing the nonlinear frequency conversion and spontaneous photon-pair generation. Silicon carbide (SiC), a silicon derivative, is an attractive semiconductor material platform for nonlinear and quantum PICs. SiC has long been extensively studied for high-power, high-temperature applications, and recently for nonlinear and quantum applications. SiC features a wide indirect bandgap energy, and thus has a relatively wide transparency window. The high refractive index (~2.6) provides tight optical confinement with a silica cladding. In addition, its high thermal conductivity allows high optical pumping power. Moreover, SiC is compatible with the standard complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) fabrication technology. Of the numerous polytypes of SiC, cubic 3C-SiC is the only one that can be grown epitaxially on a silicon substrate, and hence is a suitable candidate for cost-effective photonics applications. 3C-SiC features a high second-order nonlinearity, favoring efficient nonlinear optical frequency conversion. In the proposed project, we seek to demonstrate integrated 3C-SiC-on-insulator (3C-SiCoI) waveguide-coupled cavities with high Q factors as nonlinear and photon-pair sources using a Type-I modal phase-matching scheme. We will develop fabrication processes on commercially available 3C-SiC 4” wafers. We will die-bond 3C-SiC to a silicon chip using thick silica films in order to enable integrated waveguiding on 3C-SiCoI substrates. We will examine the modal phase-matching scheme in multimode waveguides, waveguide-coupled mm-sized whispering-gallery-mode disk and ring resonators. We will explore cavity-enhanced second-harmonic generation and optical parametric oscillation, and nonlinear quantum sources including heralded single photons and frequency-entangled photon pairs in various spectral windows including ~1064 nm, 1310 nm and 1550 nm. 第二次量子革命正在發生。基於獨立量子系統（例如被困離子，電子自旋和單光子）或組合量子系統的激動人心的量子科技正在快速產生。幾十年以來，單光子和糾纏光子對產生已經成為重要的研究課題，這些技術平臺包括利用二階非線性晶體材料，非線性光纖或波導光學，量子局限結構（例如量子點），晶體中的光學活躍缺陷和非線性集成光子芯片。 基於半導體材料的室溫下工作的非線性光子芯片很可能成為量子技術的關鍵組成部分，因為其具有機械穩定性，可擴展性以及與標準納米製造工藝和光纖光學網絡的兼容性。光子芯片中微米級截面大小的集成光波導以及高品質因數的諧振器可以在小的區域內極大的提高光能密度和光-物質相互作用，從而加強非線性頻率轉換和自發光子對產生。 碳化硅，一種硅衍生物，對非線性和量子光子芯片而言是一種有吸引力的半導體材料平臺。碳化硅已經在高功率，高溫應用以及近期在非線性和量子光子芯片方面被大量研究。碳化硅是間接帶隙寬禁帶材料，因此有相對寬的透明窗口。它的高折射率（~2.6）在氧化硅包層中可提供強光學限制。同時，其高熱傳導率允許高光泵浦功率。同時，碳化硅與標準的互補式金屬氧化物半導體製造技術兼容。 在諸多碳化硅的晶型中，立方3C-碳化硅是唯一可以直接在硅襯底上外延生長的晶型，因此可作為低成本光學應用的候選。3C-碳化硅還有高的二階非線性效應，有利於高效的非線性光學頻率轉換。 在本項目中，我們旨在驗證作為非線性和光子對光源的，利用I型模式匹配原理的集成絕緣體上3C-碳化硅高品質因數諧振腔——波導耦合結構。我們會基於市面上可購得的四英寸3C-碳化硅晶圓開發製造流程。我們會利用一層厚氧化硅薄膜來將3C-碳化硅鍵合到硅片上，以實現集成的絕緣體上3C-碳化硅波導。我們將檢驗多模波導以及與波導耦合的毫米尺寸回音壁模式微盤與微環諧振器的模式匹配方法。我們將探索諧振腔強化的二次諧波產生和光學參量震盪效應，以及在不同波長窗口（包括1064 nm，1310nm與1550nm附近）的包括預報單光子和頻率糾纏光子對在內的非線性量子光源。

16202919.label: Realisation of objectives
16202919.value: Objective 1: Achievements We demonstrated an integrated 3C-SiC-on-insulator (SiCoI) photonic platform utilizing an optimized die-to-wafer anodic bonding process. We demonstrated a minute-scale processing time by applying a voltage of 1 kV across the SiC dies and the glass substrate under 380 o^C. Our method features a relaxed surface roughness requirement and a nearly 100% SiC film transferring ratio onto the glass substrate. We expect our method would be feasible for wafer-to-wafer bonding. We optimized a SF6-based dry etching recipe and achieved a near-vertical etched sidewall slope of 86^o. Using this platform, we demonstrated loaded quality (Q)-factors of up to 1.4×10^5 and 1.6×10^5 in the L- and O-bands, respectively, from waveguide-coupled circular microring resonators. These values are comparable to the state-of-the-art 3C-SiCoI work in the literature. Our experiments revealed no significant photorefractive effect upon optical pumping at an on-chip power at sub-milliwatt level. We further demonstrated a die-to-wafer atomic layer deposition-assisted molecular bonding process, which can bond the SiC dies onto Si substrates coated by a thermal SiO2 cladding layer. Based on this platform, we designed, fabricated, and experimentally tested on-chip pump-rejection long-pass filters (LPFs) exploiting the absorption of an amorphous (α)-Si layer with a thickness of 40 nm clad on the top of the SiC waveguide. We extracted insertion losses around ~1 dB for the wavelengths in the O-, C- and L-bands while demonstrating an estimated lower-bound pump-rejection ratio exceeding 230 dB/mm for the 780 nm wavelengths. This device can potentially serve as a fundamental component for future integrated quantum photonic circuits. Under-achievements We have not been able to achieve a loaded-Q factor exceeding 10^5 in the 780 nm wavelengths due to a larger waveguide sidewall roughness scattering loss in the shorter wavelengths. The highest loaded-Q we achieved is 3.7×10^4. Some microring resonators coupled with two waveguides have loaded-Q factors within 10^4 in the 1550 nm wavelengths limited by a stronger external coupling. For the LPFs, we have not quantified the absorption coefficient for 780 nm due to the high detection noise floor caused by the light scattering. Due to the same reason, we have not experimentally transmitted and measured single photons or photon pairs through these LPFs. Attempts We have been optimizing the whole fabrication process to improve the SiC etching quality. We discovered that the major process introducing the undesirable sidewall roughness is the dry etching of the SiO2 hard mask. We can potentially mitigate this issue by acquiring a more robust electron-beam lithography resist or developing a lift-off-based metal hard mask deposition process. The crystal defects in the commercial 3C-SiC wafers are another key limiting issue. These defects are generated because of the 25% crystal lattice mismatch between the Si substrate and the 3C-SiC. The density of defects decreases with the thickness of the epitaxial layer. We can partially mitigate this issue by acquiring thicker 3C-SiC epitaxially films. For the LPFs, we will optimize the device layout of the photonic chip for bending waveguide shapes to suppress the background light scattering during the measurements to better quantify the rejection efficiency of our filters. We would then be able to measure the generated photon transmissions through these filters using our on-chip photon pair sources and off-chip single-photon detectors after the light scattering issue has been addressed. Objective 2: Achievements We designed waveguide-coupled elliptical microring resonators using type-I modal phase-matching (MPM) for χ^(2)-based nonlinear and quantum light sources. We developed our original concept of leveraging an elliptical cavity shape to realize cavity-enhanced MPM for the crystal lattice featuring 4-bar symmetry. We numerically simulated the structural dependence of the MPM and adopted a 3C-SiC waveguide thickness of 800 nm and a width of 1000 nm to attain design tolerance. We designed the asymmetric waveguide couplers for the input/output-coupling of the 780 nm wavelengths from the TM00 to TM20 modes. We adopted a waveguide width of ~400 nm for propagating the TM00 mode in the bus waveguide to phase-match with the desired TM20 mode in the microring cavity. We successfully excited the targeted TM20 mode within the microring cavity as confirmed by the transmission spectra experiments and the near-field images. We experimentally demonstrated, to our knowledge, the first second-harmonic generation (SHG) in 3C-SiCoI waveguides and microresonators, with an extracted conversion efficiency of 18%/W and 1.6%/W for the C-band (1575 nm to 787 nm) and the O-band (1280 nm to 640 nm), respectively. We demonstrated sum-frequency generation (SFG) around 1575 nm to 787 nm. We demonstrated difference-frequency generation (DFG) with a non-degenerate signal-idler bandwidth of up to 97 nm. We observed DFG across a pump bandwidth of 9.5 nm around the 780 nm wavelengths. Our working device has a designed microring waveguide width of 1050 nm. Under-achievements We have not been able to observe optical parametric oscillation (OPO) on our chips. This is because our demonstrated loaded-Q factors cannot provide high enough cavity field-enhancement to exceed the OPO threshold. However, this under-achievement does not affect objective 3 because the spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is operated under a low power. Attempts The key of achieving OPO is to improve the loaded-Q factors because the OPO threshold has a cubic dependence of the loaded-Qs. We have been working to improve the device fabrication process to further reduce the waveguide sidewall scattering loss, which will increase the Q factors for lower OPO thresholds. Objective 3: Achievements Based on the same devices, we demonstrated, to our knowledge, the first SPDC-based photon pair sources on SiC materials. By pumping in the 780 nm wavelengths, we demonstrated multiple frequency generation from different devices. For the device with a microring waveguide width of 1050 nm, we demonstrated a photon-pair generation rate (PGR) efficiency of 1.32±0.07 and 0.94±0.02 MHz/mW for the photon pairs generated in the 1562~1588 nm and 1569~1581 nm channels, respectively. We fulfilled our original target of PGR at a MHz level. We demonstrated a coincidence-to-accidental counts ratio of 3361±84 for the 1569~1581 nm pair pumped at an on-chip power of 5 mW. Using the photon pairs from 1569~1581 nm, we obtained an ultra-low heralded single-photon second-order coherence gH^(2) = 0.0007±0.0008, which is among the state-of-the-art for all single-photon sources generated by various mechanisms. We generated a time-bin entanglement with a visibility of 86.0 ± 2.4 % through a free-space unbalanced Franson interferometer, with a path difference of 18 mm using our photon pair source. Our work showed the feasibility of SiC-based on-chip quantum light sources based on χ^(2) nonlinearity. Under-achievements We did not integrate on-chip microheaters because we can readily compensate for the spectral misalignments by a temperature-stabilized sample stage using thermo-optic (TO) tuning. Our microring resonators readily attained MPM at room temperatures. Although we achieved our original targeted PGR value, our PGR efficiency is lower than a few existing work on other integrated quantum photonic platforms, including lithium niobate and aluminum nitride. Attempts Using the temperature-stabilized mount, we demonstrated the TO tunability of 3C-SiC by a sensitivity of 0.044 ± 0.001 and of 0.0228 ± 0.0009 nm/o^C for the TE00 mode in the 1550 nm wavelengths and for the TM20 mode in the 780 nm wavelengths, respectively. The measured PGR is dominated by the loaded-Q factors of the microring resonators. We have been working on improving the waveguide loss and fabrication fidelity of our photonic chip platform to enhance the conversion efficiency for both the nonlinear and quantum light sources.

We demonstrated multiple nonlinear frequency generation using the waveguide-coupled elliptical microring resonator pumped in the 780 nm wavelengths. For the microring with a waveguide width of 1050 nm, we demonstrated an PGR efficiency of 1.32±0.07 and 0.94±0.02 MHz/mW for photon pairs generated in the 1562~1588 nm and 1569~1581 nm channels, respectively, which satisfied our original target of MHz generation. We demonstrated a low-noise source with a coincidence-to-accidental count ratio of 3361±84 for the 1569~1581 nm photon pair pumped at an on-chip power of 5 mW. Using the photon pairs from the 1569~1581 nm channels, our heralded single-photon experiment revealed an ultra-low heralded single-photon second-order coherence gH^(2) = 0.0007±0.0008, which is among the state-of-the-art for all single-photon sources generated by various mechanisms. (See journal publication #2 (under review) and conference publication #2) 4. Based on our SiC photon pair sources, we demonstrated time-bin entanglement using a free-space Franson interferometer. We demonstrated the entangled state by measuring a second-order interference with a visibility of 86.0±2.4 %, which exceeds the Bell inequality of 70.1%. (See journal publication #2 (under review) and conference publication #3) 5. 16202919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16202919.value: The major bottleneck limiting our nonlinear and quantum conversion efficiencies is the cavity Q factors. We have three potential solutions to mitigate this issue as follows: First, we observed that during the SiO2 hard mask dry etching significant sidewall roughness was generated. We can acquire a more robust electron-beam lithography resist which can maintain the geometry during the etching or we can develop a lift-off-based metal hard mask deposition process. Second, we can adopt thicker 3C-SiC epitaxially films because the density of defects decreases with the thickness of the epitaxial 3C-SiC layer. Third, we could use thermal oxidation and an annealing process to reduce the waveguide sidewall roughness and to potentially relax part of the crystal defects within the 3C-SiC films. As such, we have preliminarily developed a molecular bonding process to bond the 3C-SiC onto Si substrates for a high-temperature process. Lastly, we could optimize the device layout of the long-pass filters to suppress the background light scattering during the measurement to better quantify the rejection efficiency of our filters.

16202919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16202919.value: Single-photon and photon pair sources are key building blocks for emerging quantum technology systems. Second-order optical nonlinearity enables photon pair and heralded single-photon sources. Recently, researchers have been investigating various integrated photonic material platforms to attain quantum photonic sources in a compact footprint, with mechanical stability and scalability. Among those platforms, SiC polytypes are attracting attention because of their wide transparent windows, moderate second-order optical nonlinear susceptibilities and compatibility with the standard complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process. In this project, we developed the device fabrication process and the fundamental understanding for the integrated 3C-SiC-on-insulator photonic platform for nonlinear and quantum light sources. We demonstrated microresonator quality factors comparable to the state-of-the-art of this material platform. We experimentally demonstrated, to our knowledge, the first cavity-enhanced nonlinear frequency generations for this material platform. We demonstrated, to our knowledge, the first low-noise spontaneous photon pair and heralded single-photon sources on SiC polytypes. Using these photon pairs, we demonstrated time-bin quantum entanglement using a free-space unbalanced interferometer. We invented on-chip long-pass filters for future monolithically integrated nonlinear and quantum photonic chips. Hence, our work paves a way to future integrated SiC nonlinear and quantum photonic chips.

16203319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16203319.value: Medical image segmentation is a fundamental task for many computer-aided diagnosis applications, for example, pulmonary vessel segmentation for embolism detection and tumor segmentation for targeted therapy, etc. Deep learning techniques have achieved impressive results in object segmentation for natural images; however, using deep learning methods for medical image segmentation usually results in severe performance degradation due to domain shift. Domain shift is a common problem encountered in medical image analysis, as images available for analysis are often acquired from multiple centers and from a wide range of imaging protocols/equipment (each data source is called a domain), and thus have large characteristic variations (e.g., contrast, illumination, and noise). When transferring a deep learning model pre-trained on the source domain to a new target domain, segmentation performance degrades significantly. Ensuring transferability of pre-trained deep learning models with limited training data across domains is an open problem, with one promising solution being domain adaptation. Existing domain adaptation algorithms can be roughly classified into two categories: supervised and unsupervised. Supervised domain adaptation achieves better performance but requires extensive pixel-wise manual annotations of data in the target domain. This is challenging, since generating manual annotations requires years of training and expertise. In contrast, while unsupervised domain adaptation does not require manual annotations, its performance can be significantly worse. In this proposal, we aim to investigate a new approach to domain adaptation, namely, weakly supervised domain adaptation. By introducing additional constraints derived from minor manual efforts to the existing unsupervised framework, a weakly supervised approach can improve performance significantly. There exists an inherent correlation between diagnosis (which is a classification problem) and symptom detection (which is a segmentation problem). One obvious example of the existence of such a correlation is that tumors often evolve along with the development of prostate cancer. Introducing classification information to guide unsupervised domain adaptation could potentially achieve similar performance of supervised domain adaptation while alleviating expensive pixel-wise manual annotations. This study will use three clinical tasks, namely, tumor segmentation for prostate cancer diagnosis, metastasis detection for breast cancer diagnosis, and retinal vessel segmentation for diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, as the application drivers for this research. We will evaluate the impact on final segmentation performance through the introduction of various levels of classification information and constraints, such as binary classification (cancer vs. non-cancer) and multi-class classification (aggressiveness grading), and weak annotations, such as bounding-boxes and landmarks. 醫學圖像分割是很多計算機輔助診斷中的基本任務，例如肺栓塞診斷中的肺血管分割，靶向治療中的腫瘤分割等等。儘管深度學習技術在自然圖像的分割問題上已經取得重大的成果，但由於「域位移」的關係，分割效果大多未如理想。 「域位移」是醫學圖像分析領域中常見的問題，原因是圖像及數據通常來自不同機構，數據的採集方式和設備亦可能不一，所以各域(每一個數據來源被稱作一個「域」)之間可能存在很大的差異，例如對比度、光照度、噪聲程度上的差異等等。因此，當我們把一個已就某域預先訓練的深度學習模型應用到一個新的目標域的時候，醫學圖像的分割效果的準確性往往會嚴重下降。固此，如何確保深度學習模型在不同域之間的可轉移性，是一個未被完全解決的問題。我們認為其中一種可靠的解決方法是域自適應算法。 在醫學圖像分割問題上，現有的域自適應算法可以大體分為兩類，即「全監督域自適應算法」及「無監督域自適應算法」。前者可以達至的效果較好，但往往需要於目標域進行大規模像素級的人工標註。然而，要做像素級的人工標註通常需要多年的專業訓練。相較而言，無監督域自適應算法不需要目標域的人工標註，但是效果明顯不如全監督域自適應算法。 在本提案中，我們將研究一種新的域自適應算法「弱監督域自適應算法」，即透過引入目標域的輕量級人工標註到無監督域自適應算法，以大幅提高深度學習模型在目標域的性能。在醫學診斷過程中，具體診斷(註：診斷在深度學習中屬分類問題)都依賴於對某些病症的檢測(註：檢測在深度學習中屬分割問題)。一個明顯的例子是前列腺癌診斷，前列腺癌的分期診斷依賴於腫瘤在位置、形狀等特徵的變化。透過引入目標域的分類信息到無監督域自適應算法，預計可以達到近似全監督域自適應算法的效果之餘，又可免卻引入代價很高的像素級人工標註。 本研究主要基於三個臨床應用，即用於前列腺癌診斷的腫瘤分割、用於乳腺癌診斷的癌細胞擴散檢測以及用於糖尿病性視網膜病變診斷的視網膜血管分割。此外，我們將進一步研究引入不同級別標註對於提升分割效果的影響，例如二元標註（即癌症或非癌症）、多元標註（即癌症等級評分）以及其他非像素級人工標註，如邊界框標註、關鍵點標註。

16203319.label: Realisation of objectives
16203319.value: Our project has successfully developed a novel weakly-supervised domain adaptation framework for medical image (MI) segmentation that incorporates classification information as extra constraints, along with the current constraints imposed by the domain discriminator. We have investigated the impact of introducing classification information at various granularity levels to the proposed framework. Furthermore, we have also explored the potential of the proposed weakly-supervised framework for unified data fusion, catering to both MI classification and segmentation. To address practical clinical challenges and achieve the project's objectives, we have investigated the following technical and implementation aspects: multi-source decentralized MI classification via federated learning, MI segmentation adaptive pruning Transformer models, feature representation learning for semi-supervised MI segmentation, and uncertainty consistency and variational model ensemble for semi-supervised MI deep regression. Multi-Source Decentralized MI Classification Via Federated Learning In a clinical setting, privacy concerns make it difficult to collect medical data from multiple sources in one location, hindering the deployment of our weakly-supervised domain adaptation framework that requires data from different sources in a single location. To address this challenge, a distributed, federated learning approach is needed to train a MI segmentation model without compromising data privacy. However, this approach presents a new challenge: domain variations between clients due to differences in data acquisition protocols, making it difficult to learn a generalizable and robust segmentation model. To address this problem, we enhance information robustness learned from weak supervision, such as classification, at different clients without sharing data. We observed that the federated model diverges at the classifier layer due to inter-client variations, therefore we propose a customized federated learning (CusFL) framework that addresses this issue by regularizing the feature extractor learned at each client through feature alignment and recalibrating the classification layer at each client according to its characteristics. Our CusFL demonstrates superior performance when evaluated on multi-source MI datasets for clinically significant prostate cancer and malignant pigmented skin lesion classification. By extracting robust and generalizable information from weak supervision, such as classification, we can deploy our weakly supervised domain adaptation framework to learn a more robust segmentation model. This study has been published in IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics, 2022. Adaptive Pruning Transformer for MI Segmentation Vision transformers have recently sparked a new wave in the field of MI analysis due to their excellent performance on various fundamental computer vision tasks. However, recent hybrid-/transformer-based MI segmentation methods have mainly focused on the benefits of transformers in capturing long-range feature dependencies while ignoring the problems of their daunting computational complexity, high computational costs, and redundant contextual dependency. The problems become exacerbated when dealing with weakly-supervised domain adaptation tasks. To address these problems, we propose to employ adaptive pruning to transformers for MI segmentation and introduce a lightweight and effective network called APFormer. The key features of APFormer are self-regularized self-attention (SSA) to improve the convergence of dependency establishment, Gaussian-prior relative position embedding (GRPE) to foster the learning effect of positional information, and adaptive pruning to eliminate redundant computations and perception information. Specifically, SSA and GRPE consider the well-converged dependency distribution and the Gaussian heatmap distribution separately as prior knowledge of self-attention and position embedding to facilitate the training of transformers and lay a solid foundation for the following pruning operation. Then, adaptive transformer pruning, both query-wise and dependency-wise, is performed by adjusting the gate control parameters for both complexity reduction and performance improvement. Extensive experiments on the widely-used ISIC2018 and Synapse datasets demonstrate the remarkable segmentation performance of APFormer against state-of-the-art methods with much fewer parameters and lower GFLOPs. More importantly, through ablation studies, we prove that adaptive pruning can function as a plug-and-play module for performance improvement on other hybrid-/transformer-based methods. We believe that the idea of transformer pruning will inspire future work on developing ultralight and even better-performing transformers for MI segmentation. This study has been published in IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging, 2023. Feature Representation Learning for Semi-Supervised MI Segmentation This project proposes a novel two-stage learning framework for semi-supervised MI segmentation, offering a simple and effective solution. Contrary to existing state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation methods that primarily depend on pseudo supervision directly on predictions, our approach focuses on feature representation learning with both labeled and unlabeled images. This strategy regularizes a more compact and better-separated feature space, facilitating low-density decision boundary learning, and ultimately improving segmentation performance. To accomplish this, we introduce a stage-adaptive contrastive (SAC) loss and an aleatoric uncertainty adaptive (AUA) consistency regularization. The SAC loss comprises a boundary-aware contrastive loss, which leverages labeled images, and a prototype-aware contrastive loss, optimizing both labeled and pseudo-labeled images. Besides, to achieve more accurate prototype estimation, we propose an aleatoric uncertainty-aware method called AUA consistency for generating higher-quality pseudo labels. The AUA consistency adaptively regularizes prediction consistency by capitalizing on image ambiguity. Initially, AUA consistency measures spatially correlated aleatoric uncertainty by modeling a multivariate normal distribution over the logit space. To effectively utilize unlabeled images, AUA consistency promotes prediction consistency between the teacher and student models by adaptively considering aleatoric uncertainty for each image. Extensive experimental results on three publicly available yet challenging datasets including pancreas CT, colon cancer segmentation, and the left atrium MR demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach. Our approach is a fundamental and general method that is not only applicable to semi-supervised MI segmentation, but also possesses powerful feature representation learning capabilities that can be extended to fully-/un-supervised as well as weakly-supervised domain adaptation tasks. Our project can be further extended to different types of MI data, such as X-ray images, fundus images, and surgical videos. This study has been published in IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, 2023. Enforcing Prediction Consistency for Aleatoric Uncertainty Estimates Adjusting loss weightings during training on unlabeled data can be achieved using uncertainty estimates. Samples with higher uncertainty estimates typically exhibit lower pseudo-label quality, warranting a lower loss weighting during training and, consequently, emphasizing high-quality pseudo-labels. This technique is not only applicable within a semi-supervised learning framework but can also be utilized to adjust the weight distribution of different branch tasks in weakly-supervised domain adaptation by incorporating the learned loss weights, thereby achieving a balanced weighting effect. However, in regression tasks, uncertainty estimation can be challenging, and estimates may not reliably indicate pseudo-label quality, particularly. Heteroskedastic regression loss, employed for uncertainty estimation in regression tasks, involves joint estimation of the target label and the associated uncertainty value. Owing to absence of ground-truth labels for uncertainty, these estimates may be unreliable and unstable. We note that aleatoric uncertainty, which is solely associated with input data, should remain consistent for identical inputs, despite unknown true values. Consequently, we can enforce consistency between uncertainty estimates from co-trained models as an auxiliary training signal. More reliable uncertainty estimates enable better loss weighting, focusing model training on high-quality pseudo-labels. We validate this approach on two tasks: age estimation from photographs on UTKFace dataset and ejection fraction estimation from echocardiogram videos on EchoNet-Dynamic dataset. Our findings demonstrate that uncertainty consistency can efficiently enhance the quality of uncertainty estimates on pseudo-labels and improve training for other semi-supervised learning methods. This study has been published in Proceedings of AAAI, 2023. Some earlier results have also been reported in the mid-term report, which will not be repeated here.
