16207319.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207319.value: A total of 9 journal papers (J1-J8) and 4 conference papers (C1-C4) directly related to the project have been published. The PI has been invited to deliver 13 invited keynote or special talks and won two paper awards, as summarized in Section 5.3 and Part C. Most of the papers have been published in top journals in geotechnical engineering and computational mechanics. The following summarizes the major findings from the project research: (1) The new coupled MPM-DEM framework has been found robust and effective in capturing major features exhibited in large deformation geotechnical problems. It helps circumvent the needs for conventional phenomenological constitutive models while offering direct links of macroscopic observations with their underlying microstructural mechanisms. (2) The proposed framework has been applied to simulating practical geotechnical problems including (in an earlier paper) biaxial shear, rigid footing foundation, pipeline-soil interaction, column collapse, and (in J1) offshore plate anchor pullout. (3) The framework facilitates both hierarchical and concurrent multiscale modeling of geotechnical problems, as demonstrated in J2, where the far-field domain can be conveniently modeled by a conventional (efficient but less accurate) soil model while the near field by the high-fidelity hierarchical multiscale model. There is no need for tedious numerical manipulations for the hand-shaking zone between the two. (4) Further significant extensions of the framework to multiphysics problems involving saturated granular media in large deformation regime prove to be successful and useful in capturing both quasi-static and dynamic multiphysics responses in various engineering scenarios (J3 and J4). (5) The framework has been further empowered by effective and scalable MPI-based parallel computing schemes ( J5) and with implemention of novel non-spherical particles for the DEM (J6-J8). All these further efforts have greatly enhanced the predictive capabilities of the framework.

16207319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207319.value: The proposed framework has the potential to be extended further to model multiscale, multiphysics problems involving complex thermos-hydro-mechanical and chemical coupling. In this project, we have successfully implemented coupled hydromechanical multiscale modeling, which can be enriched further by incorporating thermal and chemical coupling components. The inclusion of thermal effects can account for thermal and pressure-induced phase transformation in granular media. Additionally, the introduction of chemical effects would enable the modeling of chemically reactive flow in granular media, which has broad engineering applications. Such future extensions of the proposed framework to include thermal and chemical coupling components would significantly enhance its capabilities and allow for the modeling of a wide range of complex problems. The consideration of these effects is essential in many engineering applications, and the enriched framework will find great potential to provide valuable insights into these systems.

16207319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207319.value: The increasing global energy demand has led to a surge in offshore energy exploration in deep waters. It is crucial to accurately assess the safety of offshore infrastructure under extreme loads, such as strong waves and hurricanes. This project presents an innovative numerical method and computational tool that predicts and analyzes the deformation behavior of offshore soils that support critical infrastructure. The proposed framework represents a next-generation computational and design tool that combines the direct simulation of soil particle-scale physics with an engineering-scale problem for practical applications. The multiscale modeling framework overcomes the drawbacks associated with many conventional modeling approaches used in offshore geotechnical applications while providing a sound basis on particle-scale physics. Additionally, it enables the realistic consideration of fluid flow in the pore of offshore soils and offshore structures, such as oil platforms or anchors, under wave or wind loads. Consequently, the developed framework enables the consideration of soil-structure-water-load four-way interactions in an effective and convenient manner. This multiscale, multiphase computational framework not only offers a viable numerical tool to advance our fundamental understanding of critical soil behavior but also provides a tailor-made, new-generation numerical tool for modeling soils critical to key offshore foundations and infrastructure in shallow/deep waters. The proposed framework represents a significant advancement in the field of offshore geotechnical engineering, and its application has the potential to enhance the safety and reliability of offshore infrastructure under extreme loads.

16207419.label: Project Objectives
16207419.value: Develop new algorithmic techniques for the approximation of max-min allocation of indivisible resources in polynomial time. Study different settings such as distributed processing and the temporal variant of the problem.
rows: Develop new algorithmic techniques for the approximation of max-min allocation of indivisible resources in polynomial time.
Study different settings such as distributed processing and the temporal variant of the problem.

16207419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16207419.value: Allocating indivisible resources to a group of users in a fair manner has many applications in real life. The problem, however, is very challenging because indivisibility forbids an equitable partition of a resource among the users, different users may desire different combinations of resources, and the utilities of resources need not be the same. Maximizing the minimum resource utilities received by a user is a simple, quantifiable objective to ensure fairness. This project aims to study algorithms for max-min allocations of indivisible resources with a focus on computational efficiency and theoretical guarantees for solution quality. 在現實生活中具有許多應用都須以公平的方式將不可分割的資源分配給一組用戶。然而，該問題因以下因素而非常有挑戰性：不可分割性禁止在用戶之間平均地劃分資源，不同的用戶可能需要不同的資源組合，並且資源的效用不一定相同。把用戶收到的最小資源效用最大化是一個簡單，可量化的方法去確保公平。這項目旨在研究不可分割資源最小最大化分配的算法，重點關注計算效率和解決方案質量的理論保證。

16207419.label: Realisation of objectives
16207419.value: In many applications, we need to partition a collection of m indivisible resources among a set of n players. A resource is indivisible means that it cannot be shared among multiple players, and therefore, it can only be assigned to one player. We are particularly interested in the case that a resource r has utility v(r) to any player who wants it and utility zero to players who do not want it. The total utility of a player is the sum of the utilities of the resources that the player receives. One way to produce a fair allocation of the resources among the players is to compute an allocation such that the minimum total utility among the players is maximized. This is called a maxmin allocation. That is, the poorest player should not be worse off than necessary according to the input instance, which is a typical objective in distributing public goods. This is a challenging problem, and it has been shown to be NP-hard. It is thus unlikely that there is a polynomial-time algorithm to find a maxmin allocation. Naturally, one turns to approximation algorithm with provable guarantees. An algorithm achieves an approximation ratio α ∈ (0,1) if it can construct an allocation with a minimum total utility at least α times the optimum. It has also been shown that even guaranteeing an approximation ratio greater than 1/2 is an NP-hard problem. Prior to our work, there are two known techniques for designing approximation algorithm for this problem. The first method is to round the solution of a special configuration linear program designed for the problem. This method produces an approximation ratio of Ω(log⁡log⁡log⁡ n/log⁡log⁡ n). The second method is combinatorial in nature, and it uses local search to explicitly construct an allocation with approximation 1/(6+2√10+δ) for any δ ∈ (0,1), which is less than 1/12. It is a polynomial-time approximation scheme with a running time bounded by n raised to a power of a polynomial in 1/δ. We designed a novel technique that improves the performance of the local search method. Specifically, we achieve an approximation ratio of 0.25-δ for any δ ∈ (0,1), which is substantially larger than 1/(6+2√10+δ). Our algorithm is a polynomial-time approximation scheme with a running time bounded by n raised to a power of a polynomial in 1/δ. Equally importantly, we proved that the integrality gap of the configuration linear program is at most 3.808. That is, the optimal fractional solution obtained by solving the configuration linear program for the allocation problem is no more than 3.808 times the maxmin total utility. This shows that there may still be hope for improving the approximation ratio to above 0.25, either by designing a better combinatorial algorithm or by exploiting the configuration linear program or both. We also studied the more general case when a player p has an individual utility v(p,r) for a resource r. The total utility of a player p is still the sum of the individual utilities of the resources assigned to p. This case makes natural sense because different people may rate the same resource differently. The problem is still about finding an allocation that maximizes the minimum total utility among the players. This case is considerably harder. The integrality gap of the configuration linear program is known to be Ω(√m). The best approximation ratio achieved in polynomial time so far is O(m^δ) for a running time of n^{O(1⁄δ)}. We studied the case that although the utility of a resource may vary among players, the variation may be small in some applications. A player may rate resources based on a small scale from 0 to c for a small constant c; for instance, a 0 to 5 scale. We developed two efficient approximation algorithms. The first algorithm works in the case that the scale is from 1 to c. Our polynomial-time approximation scheme achieves an approximation ratio of (1⁄c)-ε for any ε ∈ (0,1). When some resource may have zero utility for some player, we introduced an over-estimation technique and combined it with the local search method that we previously developed. It results in a polynomial-time approximation scheme that achieves an approximation ratio of 1⁄(1+3c+O(δc^2 )) for any fixed δ ∈ (0,1). Therefore, for a scoring scale with a constant upper limit, we can achieve a constant approximation ratio. Therefore, we have obtained new algorithmic and analytical techniques for the maxmin allocation problem, meeting objective 1. We studied a temporal variant in which an approximate maximin allocation is to be maintained over an infinite horizon of discrete time steps. For every resource r and every player p, v_t(p,r) denotes the utility of r for p at time t. As before, one of the goals is to maximize the minimum total utility among the players. The other goal is to encourage some stability in the solution over time. So there is a fixed reward for keeping a resource at the same player between two successive time steps. As a result, the objective is to maximize a cost function which is the sum of two terms. The first term is the sum of the minimum total utility among the players over all time steps. The second term is the sum of stability rewards over all resources over all time step transitions. Suppose that one is given a maxmin allocation approximation algorithm with approximation ratio ρ. Can we use this algorithm to provide a good solution for the temporal variant as described above? We provide a solution for the temporal variant with a w-lookahead for any fixed w≥1: when we decide the allocation at the current time t, we are also given the values of v_(t+i) (p,r) for all i ∈ [0,w] for all r and p. We can maintain an allocation such that its objective function value at any time t is at least (1-x)ρ times the optimum at time t, where x is the positive root of the equation wx^2=ρ(w+1)(1-x). For instance, when w=1, the factor (1-x)ρ is greater than ρ⁄(4ρ+2)+ρ/10. If the costs of assigning resources to players are the distances between them and the objective is to find an assignment that minimizes the maximum cost, the problem has many desirable geometrical problems that can be exploited. We proposed a general approach to solve a list of such problems. For example, we can compute a perfect matching between n players and n resources that minimizes the length of the longest edge under the L-infinity in O(n^{1+eps}) time or the L2 metric in O(n^{4/3+eps}) time for any eps > 0. Hence, we have studied different settings, meeting objective 2.

16207419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207419.value: The maxmin allocation is to assign a set of resources among n players. Each resource has a fixed utility for the players who want it and a zero utility for the other players who do not want it. Our first finding is that the maxmin allocation can be approximated within a factor of 0.25-δ for any δ ∈ (0,1) while keeping the running time bounded by n raised to a power of a polynomial in 1⁄δ. Our second finding is that the integrality gap of the configuration linear program for the maxmin allocation problem can be lowered to 3.808. So there is still hope for improving the approximation ratio to something greater than 0.25. These results appear in journal paper 1 in Section C. We also studied the more general case when different users may have different utilities of a resource on a scale of 0 to c for some small constant c. If the minimum rating is at least 1, we designed a polynomial-time algorithm that can achieve an approximation ratio of c/(1-ε) for any ε ∈ (0,1). If the minimum rating can be zero, we designed another polynomial-time algorithm that can achieve an approximation of 1⁄(1+3c+O(δc^2 )) for any fixed δ ∈ (0,1). These results appear in journal paper 2 and conference paper 1 in Section C. One often needs to perform maxmin allocations over time, and the utility of a resource to a user may also change from one time step to the next. The objective is to maximize a cost function which is the sum of two terms. The first term is the sum of the minimum total utility among the players over all time steps. The second term is the sum of stability rewards over all resources over all time step transitions. Given a maxmin allocation approximation algorithm with approximation ratio ρ and a w-lookahead for any fixed w≥1, we can maintain an allocation such that its objective function value at any time t is at least (1-x)ρ times the optimum at time t, where x is the positive root of the equation wx^2=ρ(w+1)(1-x). This result appears in journal paper 3 in Section C. We also proposed an approach to a variety of assignment problems when the costs are the distances between the players and the resources. These results appear in conference paper 2 in Section C.

16207419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207419.value: The foremost question is whether one can improve the approximation ratio to greater than 0.25. Our method may already push the local search idea to the limit, so some new ideas are probably needed. Such new ideas may possibly have other applications. Another question is whether the configuration linear program can be rounded in a way that gives a constant approximation ratio that is competitive with 0.25. This approach for obtaining an approximate maxmin allocation is attractive because rounding a configuration linear program is computationally more efficient than local search. The hardest question along this line of research is to handle the general case of every resource having an arbitrary utility for each player. We addressed the case when the utilities fall in a scale with a small constant upper bound. For the general case, the best approximation ratio achieved in polynomial time so far is O(m^δ) for a running time of n^{O(1⁄δ)}. It is open question whether this result can be improved.

16207419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207419.value: We are interested in partitioning a set of resources among some users. A resource can only be assigned to one player. In the case that a resource has a fixed utility for any user who wants it and zero utility for users who do not want it, we designed an efficient algorithm that approximately maximizes the minimum total utility among the users. The minimum total utility is at least 0.25 of the optimum. We also generalized our result to the case that different users may have different utilities of a resource on a scale of 0 to c for some small constant c. The resulting approximation ratios are reasonable constants when c is small. We also studied the problem of performing maxmin allocations over time, while avoiding reassigning resources frequently. Given a maxmin allocation approximation algorithm with approximation ratio ρ and a w-lookahead, we can maintain an allocation such that its objective function value is at least (1-x)ρ times the optimum, where x is the positive root of the equation wx^2=ρ(w+1)(1-x). We also addressed problem instances in which the assignment costs are the distances between the players and resources.

16207719.label: Project Objectives
16207719.value: To identify the aerodynamic forces experienced by tall buildings with various shapes subjected to twisted wind flows using wind tunnel pressure measurement tests. To develop a technique for taking synchronized particle image velocimetry (PIV) measurements along with synchronized measurements of the pressure on building surfaces, in order to investigate the spatiotemporal correlations and the coupling of aerodynamic loads induced by twisted wind profiles. To elucidate the interactions between tall buildings and twisted wind flows and hence the excitation mechanisms that underlie the observed effects of twisted wind flows on tall buildings.

16207719.label: Realisation of objectives
16207719.value: We identified the aerodynamic forces experienced by tall buildings with various shapes subjected to twisted wind flows using wind tunnel pressure measurement tests. An adjustable novel wooden vane system was proposed to replicate different types of twisted flow in wind tunnel, which was designed so as to achieve the project objectives. The tall building model of size 60 mm × 180 mm cross-section and 600 mm height was tested under straight wind (CWP) and two twisted wind flows (TWP15 and TWP30). Different shapes of high-rise buildings, aspect ratio, and different wind angles (i.e. −90◦ to 90◦ at intervals of 10◦) were investigated. The global and local aerodynamic features (i.e., wind load and spatial-temporal correlation) were evaluated in detail based on quantitative measurement of the building surface pressure. Specifically, aerodynamic forces include: 1. The base moment coefficients in longitudinal direction and lateral direction, torsional direction. They contain the variation of mean and fluctuating base moment coefficient with different angle of attack for three different twisted wind angle configuration CWP, TWP15 and TWP30. 2. The longitudinal, lateral and torsional local wind force coefficients along the buildings and their spatiotemporal correlation. 3. Building surface pressure (local wind forces) represents the spatial distribution of wind load. To study the effect of twisted flow on the wind pressure, the mean and fluctuating pressure distribution is compared for CWP, TWP15 and TWP30, while the fluctuating feature of pressure pattern is further elucidated by POD modal analysis. The simultaneous measurement of flow fields and fluctuating pressures are essential to investigate the spatiotemporal correlations and the coupling of aerodynamic loads induced by twisted wind profiles or other situations (e.g., tornado, typhoon etc.) in which spatiotemporal correlations are significant. To this end, PIV measurement systems were successfully synchronized to simultaneously capture flow fields at various locations. Subsequently a pressure measurement system was also synchronized with the PIV systems to obtain the asymmetric pressure distributions on the surfaces of buildings together with the flow fields in the building wake. The resulting flow field and surface pressure data were analyzed using conditional sampling technique, e.g. dynamic mode decomposition (DMD). The DMD analyzing technique can map any correlation between the velocity fields captured by the PIV systems and the wind pressures, enabling the identification of excitation mechanisms of tall buildings when subjecting to twisted wind flows. In addition, we developed a numerical simulation technique to reproduce the twisted wind flow, in order to investigate the spatiotemporal correlations and the coupling of aerodynamic loads induced by twisted wind profiles. The proposed numerical simulation technique provides comprehensive flow fields and building surface pressures for the full azimuth and 3D space. Specifically, the key aspects of numerical simulation technology include: narrowband synthesis random flow generator (NSRFG) is employed to reproduce the time-history of fluctuating wind speed. The initial inlet boundary condition is formulated by the superposition of zero-mean fluctuating velocity sequence and targeted mean wind profile. However, owing to the dissipation effect during flow transportation process, wind field characteristics are inevitably changed at the downstream of the inlet boundary. To obtain the desired flow properties, iterative adjustment has to be performed for the inflow boundary condition (IBC) in empty domain, which is based on the differences between realistic and desired wind feature of monitored points at location of interests along the height of building. The flow fields at different heights of planes and building surface pressures are monitored within certain time interval and duration. The local/global aerodynamic forces and three-dimensional flow structure were evaluated using the data-driven mode decomposition method, such as DMD and POD. The spatial morphology and temporal evolution of coherent structure were elucidated. We successfully analyzed the ten dominant modes. Five flow mechanisms were disclosed. First, Mode 1 describes the mean-field. Then, the Karman vortex shedding (KVS) is dissected into two distinct mechanisms, namely the Strouhal vortices described by Mode 2 and the Bloor-Gerrard vortices described by Mode 3. The superposition of the two types of vortices, with flow entrainment in tandem, culminate into the Karman vortex street. Thereafter, Modes 4, 5, 7, 8, and 9 describe the harmonic excitations of Modes 2 and 3. Last, Modes 6 and 10 describe the low-frequency shedding of turbulent separation bubbles (TSB), which happens concurrently but independently from the KVS. With the assistance of data-driven mode decomposition method, we systemically elucidated the interactions between tall buildings and twisted wind flows, and revealed the excitation mechanisms that underlie the observed effects of twisted wind flows on tall buildings. 1. The general mode-based wind loads analysis method was proposed to uncover the underlying link between the coherence mode and the aerodynamic forces under twisted wind flow. By employing this method, we can identify the mode-induced forces exerting on the bluff bodies, and then quantitively evaluate how much the specific mode contributing to the total forces. As we stated above, all of the flow variable can be divided into two parts, the spatial coherence mode and the time coefficients part through DPMD methods including POD, DMD, ICA, HODMD and their variants. 2. The time-averaged and instantaneous velocity fields were extracted from the numerical simulation, some essential flow dynamics such as permanent and intermittent flow separations, reattachments and span-wise vortex structures were discovered under twisted wind flow. The interrelationships between the flow fields and the aerodynamic forces associated with twisted and conventional wind flows along the vertical direction were also revealed. 3. The POD and DMD technique are the methods to identify the coordinate system that can most efficiently describe a random, multi-dimensional dynamic phenomenon. Thus, in this project, these techniques are used to discover the hidden deterministic structure of random fluctuations and the aerodynamic coupling in a fluctuating pressure field. We further mapped the spatiotemporal correlation between the velocity fields and the wind forces for each critical building shape. The two methods successfully revealed the mechanisms that underlie the effects of twisted wind flows on the aerodynamic characteristics associated with tall buildings.

16207719.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207719.value: This project reveals the flow field, spatial-temporal correlation and mode pattern of tall buildings in twisted winds. The flow filed: 1. Twisted angle and deviation angle of wake region both decay along vertical direction, the difference between them oscillating increases along building height. This phenomenon manifests that TWP has “twisted extensibility”, which can be physically interpretated that wake deviation angle is not only determined by oncoming flow direction but also highly influenced by the wake feature of adjacent height. Thus, TWP could generate stronger momentum exchange and larger vertical correlation, which could further amplify torsional responses. 2. The flow field is sensitive to the building height. The main flow pattern is dominated by near steady wake at small height, while it is less influenced by TWP along the vertical distribution. At larger heights, the strong unsteady TEVS phenomenon controls the flow pattern, meanwhile, it is largely influenced by TWP along the vertical distribution. The TEVS vortex is distorted and spirally attached on the buildings under TWP. The spatial-temporal correlation: 1. Owing to the stronger moment exchange in vertical direction, the correlation of local forces is generally amplified, possibly resulting in larger wind-induced responses. 2. The correlation of wind load components is increased, implying that lateral and torsion wind-induced responses are magnified, and thus special consideration needs to be taken for wind-resistant design for building frequently exposed to twisted wind. The mode pattern: 1. For small aspect ratio, the main mode pattern is controlled by TEV for CWP. Affected by TWP, the energy and frequency of primary mode are both distinctively reduced compared to CWP, fluctuating energy concentrates towards low-frequency region which could amplify background component of building’s buffeting response. Although large-scale coherent structures still represent Karman vortices, they inclinedly sheds in the direction approximately consistent with wake deviation angle. However, at the top position, large-scale vortex structure is broken into small-scale fragment due to combination influence of free-end and twisted effect. 2. For large aspect ratio, the main mode pattern of CWP is controlled by ILEVS and TEVS phenomenon. Whereas, the predominant mode of TWP is highly related to AEVS, and this modal pattern is reported to twists towards the wind direction with more regular shape even though it becomes less intense. Moreover, the spanwise correlation of main coherence mode at two plane of different height is also significantly enhanced by TWP.

16207719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207719.value: The current study reveals that twisted wind generates significant modification in the aerodynamic properties of a tall building compared with its counterparts of CWP and has a high probability of amplifying the wind-induce responses. For the future research, to ensure wind safety, it is suggested that the twisted wind-induced vibration should be estimated by conducting fluid-structure coupled simulations and/or wind tunnel tests under TWP. The wind-resistance design guideline specifically for tall buildings that are likely to be subjected to twisted wind profiles should be established.

16207719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16207719.value: This research project investigates how tall buildings are affected by twisted wind flows, which are common in mountainous areas like Hong Kong. Twisted wind exhibits wind directions that vary with height, thus, the aerodynamic characteristics of building under twisted wind exhibit great difference from that in the conventional wind condition. The study uses wind tunnel tests and numerical simulation on synchronized measurements of wind pressure and velocity to identify the building geometries that are most vulnerable to excessive lateral and rotational movements caused by twisted winds. By developing twisted-wind replication method and mode decomposition method, the aerodynamic forces, flow field, spatial-temporal correlation and mode pattern of tall buildings in twisted wind flows are revealed. The research sheds light on the fluid-induced interaction between twisted flows and tall building, and provides better understanding of underlying mechanism of twisted winds on high-rise structures. The research findings can be used to develop better guidelines for wind-resistant design and construction of tall buildings in mountainous areas where twisted wind flows are prevailing.

16207819.label: Major findings and research outcome
16207819.value: 1. The development of a novel energy harvesting chamber in centrifuge A novel centrifuge energy harvesting chamber was developed to be used at a high-g centrifuge environment. It allows simulating hydrate dissociation, wellbore casing deformation, and seabed subsidence during gas production from hydrate-bearing soils. The unique features of the novel energy harvesting chamber are the capability of sustaining the thermodynamically favourable conditions for hydrate formation, sustaining a continuous inflow of high pressure water at the boundaries during the dissociation, and an in-flight control of wellbore pressure and surcharge loading. Based on this new invention, two invention patents, the US one is granted and the Chinese one is still pending for final decision. With this novel energy harvesting chamber, the number of extremely expensive field trials can be greatly reduced. Also high quality of physical test data can be obtained through centrifuge tests for calibration of numerical models and design criteria. 2. New scientific findings and engineering implications Novel centrifuge tests reveal that during depressurization within a casing, the compressive load in the casing exceeds the yield strength of the modelled prototype casing. Although the induced tensile loads are smaller than the yielding strength of the casing, the cement above the perforated interval might crack in tension and jeopardize the well’s integrity. Hence, both induced compressive and tensile axial loads during long-term hydrate dissociation should be carefully considered for safe gas production in gas hydrate-bearing sediments. The adoption of fugacity as the thermodynamic state variable in our new constitutive model can simulate the kinetics of phase change of hydrates well. Phase change of hydrate may result in significant deformation of sediment. Relative movement of the sediment may induce additional loading to the wellbore to cause stability issues or result in unsafe design. High drawdown pressure should be applied if the stability of production well is to be maintained. Gas hydrate-bearing sediment at shallower water depth is more favourable to energy harvesting due to a less stable initial thermodynamic state. More details of the above finding are given in the published papers listed in Section 8 of Part C.

16207819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16207819.value: The thermo-mechanical coupling is neglected in our new constitutive model. This means that any change in soil temperature would not affect its mechanical properties. Such a simplification is often adopted in constitutive models for hydrate-bearing sediment. This is because the existence of hydrate in pores has much greater impact on the mechanical properties of hydrate-bearing sediment than the variations in soil temperature. Nevertheless, thermo-mechanical coupling is still without a doubt one of the most important aspects of soil behaviour. In particular, heat transfer is heavily involved in phase change of hydrate. Thus, this constitutive model can be further improved by incorporating thermo-elasticity via the thermal expansion coefficient of the soil skeleton. The thermo-plasticity can also be incorporated by including temperature as one of the constitutive variables. The productivity of energy harvesting events in hydrate-bearing sediment can potentially be enhanced by including more production wells instead of a single well. The spacing between each production well can potentially be determined by the evolution of the thermodynamic state of hydrate-bearing sediment as visualised using the difference in our proposed fugacity (Δf). Depressurisation with a group of production wells needs to be evaluated.

16208619.value: To develop mathematical models to capture the complex interactions between passengers’ mode choices and travel costs in a ride-sourcing market with on-demand ride-sharing programs. Based on the models, different operational strategies’ impact on the platform profit and passenger and driver welfare will be fully examined. Further, optimal operational strategies will be designed to achieve a win-win-win situation, in which all stakeholders become better off upon activation of the on-demand ride-sharing program. To investigate the impacts of the on-demand ride-sharing program on passengers’ total travel distance savings and thus traffic congestion on road networks. Among many factors, we will determine the critical mass in terms of passenger density for a sensible on-demand ride-sharing program in cities that can align with societal objectives to reduce emissions and alleviate traffic congestion. To calibrate the proposed theoretical models and verify the analytical results with actual operational mobility data from the DiDi platform for several Chinese Mainland cities. DiDi Chuxing Technology Company will provide the required data for empirical analyses (letter of support from DiDi Chuxing is attached in the proposal).

16208619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16208619.value: There has been a long history of ride-sharing, in which travelers with similar itineraries and time schedules share one vehicle. Traditional ride-sharing such as carpooling generally involves drivers who commonly commute share rides with others who are willing to share travel costs such as gasoline consumption. Much research has been dedicated to examining the various issues on ride-sharing, such as matching and cost sharing strategies between drivers and riders. With the recent rapid growth of technology-enabled mobility services, ride-sourcing platforms, such as Uber and DiDi, have launched commercial on-demand (dynamic) ride-sharing programs, allowing dedicated drivers to serve more than one passenger per ride. Without requiring the pre-arrangement of trip schedules, these programs match on-demand passenger requests with vehicles that have vacant seats. Ride-sharing platforms are expected to offer benefits both for individual users in the form of cost savings, and for society in the form of traffic alleviation and emission reductions. To this end, how platform operating strategies are designed is important. First, together with some exogenous variables, such as city size and population density, there are two key decision variables that govern a platform’s efficiency: the discounted trip fare and the allowable detour time for ride-sharing services. An appropriate discount fare attracts an adequate number of passengers for ride-sharing and thus increases the matching rate; while an appropriate maximum allowable detour time prevents passengers from being discouraged from opting into ride-sharing. Second, what are the potential implications of ride-sharing for traffic congestion? One key factor is the detour distances for picking-up and dropping-off multiple passengers, which will depend on the density of passengers. It is of great value to identify the critical density that results in a ride-sharing program that reduces driving distances and alleviates traffic congestion and emissions. The proposed project will develop theoretical models and conduct empirical studies to address these problems. The models will be used to discern platform designs with operating strategies to achieve a “win-win-win” situation, in which the platform, passengers, and drivers are all better off. These models will also be used to examine the impacts of ride-sharing programs on traffic congestion and to identify critical factors, such as passenger density, to ensure socially desirable ride-sharing programs. The actual mobility data, collected on DiDi trips, will be used to calibrate the theoretical models and verify the analytical findings. 共享出行，即多位具有相似出行路线和相近出发时间的旅客共享一辆交通工具出行，已经出现了较长时间。在传统的共享出行中，如顺风车出行，具有自己出行计划的驾驶员愿意搭载顺道的乘客，与此同时，乘客也愿意承担部分交通费用（例如油费）。过去有许多研究致力于解决共享出行中各种各样的问题，例如乘客和司机匹配的策略，乘客与司机的费用分摊方法等。随着近年来移动互联网科技的快速发展，网约车公司，像Uber和滴滴出行，已经开发了一些动态共享出行的商业服务，如滴滴拼车。不同于传统的共享出行，这些拼车服务雇佣职业司机来服务乘客，司机在每趟旅程中可以搭载多名乘客，以使得多名乘客实现共享出行，从而达到降低单个乘客出行费用、提高车辆利用率的目的。通常，这些拼车服务不要求乘客预先发布出发行程和时间，而可以接受乘客的实时订单，实现乘客需求和空余座位即时匹配。 可预期的是，一个具有良好运营策略的共享出行平台将不仅节省使用者个人的出行费用，并且产生诸多社会效益，如缓解交通拥堵和减少污染物排放。因此，如何设计平台运营策略非常重要。首先，针对共享出行服务（拼车），网约车平台可以通过两个关键的决策变量来影响平台收益和社会效益：1）乘客使用拼车服务的折扣费用；2）乘客在拼车过程中绕行时间的上限阈值。适当的折扣费用能吸引足够数量的乘客使用共享出行服务，从而提高匹配率；与此同时，适当的绕行时间上限阈值可以有效防止拼车过程中乘客遇到长时间绕路的情况，从而避免乘客放弃共享出行服务。除此之外，我们将进一步研究共享出行对交通拥堵的潜在影响。这些影响的大小取决于许多因素，一个关键因素是共享出行车辆接送多个乘客的绕行距离，因此绕行距离也会增加道路上的车流量从而增加交通拥堵。很明显，这将取决于乘客的密度：当乘客密度较大时，共享出行车辆容易找到并搭载出行路线相近的乘客，从而减少绕行距离。我们期望确定乘客密度的一个关键阈值，当乘客密度超过这个关键阈值时，共享出行可以显著降低车辆的总行驶距离（包括正常行驶距离和绕行距离），从而缓解交通拥堵和减少车辆尾气排放。 我们提出的研究项目，将通过理论建模、数据分析和实证研究来解决上述问题。我们建立的模型将会用来指导设计运营策略使平台、乘客和司机均从共享出行中获益，以实现多赢的局面。这些模型还将用于检验出行共享对交通拥堵的影响，并分析一些关键因素的影响，如乘客密度，从而确定共享出行能显著带来社会效益的场景，进而给不同城市提供不同的共享出行运营方案（如是否应该推广共享出行，如何推广共享出行，在什么地点和时间更大力度地推行共享出行）。此外，我们将使用滴滴软件中收集的实际行程数据，来校准我们的理论模型并验证分析结论。

16208619.label: Realisation of objectives
16208619.value: The project had several outcomes. First, the project developed theoretical models to examine the impact of ride-sharing programs on traffic congestion and to identify critical factors to ensure socially desirable ride-sharing programs. The models considered the pricing and allowable detour time for ride-sharing services and the probability of en-route pairing. The models were used to discern platform designs with operating strategies to achieve a “win-win-win” situation, in which the platform, passengers, and drivers are all better off. The models were also used to examine the impacts of ride-sharing programs on traffic congestion and to identify critical factors to ensure socially desirable ride-sharing programs. Second, the project conducted empirical studies using actual mobility data collected on DiDi trips. The data were used to calibrate the theoretical models and verify the analytical findings. The empirical studies helped us understand the impact of ride-sharing programs on traffic congestion and passenger demand. The empirical studies also helped us identify critical factors to ensure socially desirable ride-sharing programs. Third, the project identified optimal operating strategies for ride-sharing platforms to maximize revenue and social welfare. The strategies considered the pricing and allowable detour time for ride-sharing services and the probability of en-route pairing. The optimal operating strategies were developed based on the theoretical models and empirical studies. In conclusion, the proposed project developed theoretical models and conducted empirical studies to examine the impact of ride-sharing programs on traffic congestion and to identify critical factors to ensure socially desirable ride-sharing programs. The project was conducted in collaboration with DiDi, a leading Transportation network company (TNC) in China. The project was expected to have long-term impacts, including increasing the efficiency of urban transportation systems, reducing traffic congestion, fuel consumption, and emissions. The project findings had tremendous potential to provide an informative and in-depth point of reference for the TNCs in platform operating strategy design, helping them optimize their ride-sharing programs and improve the efficiency of urban transportation systems.

However, several intriguing issues were also identified that require further investigation. The study's mathematical models and algorithms can also be used to develop more efficient ride-matching algorithms, leading to a more sustainable and efficient transportation system. Overall, this research project provides valuable insights into the emerging field of on-demand mobility services and their potential to improve urban transportation.

16209019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209019.value: 無線通信的發展在過去的三十年間徹底改變了人們的生活，其持續的發展對滿足新服務和未來應用的需求十分重要。這個增長不僅局限於蜂窩系統中，還會出現在非蜂窩系統裡，如無線熱點(WiFi)和物聯網（IoT），預計在未來的幾年間無線通信將會持續迅速增長。為了配合這個增長，我們正在努力開發新技術。在這些新技術中，許多將廣泛依賴於多輸入多輸出（MIMO）系統的增強，包括如大規模MIMO和毫米波(mmWave) 蜂窩系統等。然而，人們經已意識到這些越來越複雜的技術也成為重要的能源消耗者。此外，在全球的所有行業中，無線通信系統的能源消耗現已被認為是增長速度最快的其中一個。因此，如何在MIMO的無線通信系統中開發降低功耗和提高能量效率的方法正成為一個重要議題。 在這裡提出的研究中，我們通過研究模擬射頻(RF)架構來解決MIMO無線系統中的能效挑戰。我們的方法是專門研究和開發用於MIMO系統的模擬RF調製和模擬RF預編碼器的新方法。由於模擬RF架構的共同使用，以上兩種方法存在顯著的協同作用，而我們將考慮三種不同的方案。首先，我們將開發全新可實現的模擬RF調製，用於使用可變無功無源負載的全MIMO空間復用。 該新方法將包括開發跨越全空間復用到空間調製（SM）的權衡，並且我們還將開發用於解決系統問題的關鍵方法，例如脈衝整形濾波器，帶寬，非線性和天線耦合。第二個方案為開發混合MIMO預編碼系統的新模擬RF架構。第 三，我們將再次研究可變電抗性負載，並且還將考慮使用高度可重新配置的像素天線來確定它們是否可用於替代模擬RF預編碼器。 這個研究的最後部分為驗證可以執行所提出的架構關鍵部分的實現。所有三種方案的重點都是滿足系統和RF的要求。這項研究的長期重要性在於它可以為未來的第五代移動通信技術(5G)和專用物聯網應用帶來全新及可實施的節能MIMO系統。

16209019.label: Realisation of objectives
16209019.value: All three objectives have been fully met and outcomes include 5 published journal papers in IEEE Transactions, one conference paper and two PhD students. The research has been performed in three key steps to meet the three objectives. For Objective 1 we have focused on approaches based on electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) and loaded modulated arrays (LMA). One of the previous significant drawbacks of ESPAR was that it was not flexible and the proposed approaches were limited by special antenna configurations. In this research we have made an important contribution that allows ESPAR to be configured for any antenna type and configuration in any array, removing a significant drawback. The approach has been published [J1]and is based on applying the concept of the Theory of Characteristic Modes (TCM). Using this approach allows us to obtain orthogonal modes that can be exploited in MIMO modulation. Results have shown that full multiplexed MIMO based on our ESPAR approach performs as well as ideal MIMO but is significantly more energy efficient. In addition we have also generalized this approach to antennas with losses and to wireless channels with any power angular spectrum [J2]. This work represents important breakthroughs as the methods in [J1,J2] provide systematic methods for the development of single-RD transmission systems. Another approach using continuous tunable load-modulated multiple-input multiple-output (LM-MIMO) transmitters has also been investigated. We have found a closed-form expression for the load values for arbitrary constellations [C1]. The lumped element topology of a continuous tunable LM is also provided. Simulation results show that the proposed continuous tunable LM is able to handle phase modulation on a hypersphere. This work was not following up further as the methods described in [J1,J2] have provided fruitful approaches for meeting objective 2. In objective 2 we have made three contributions. The first is to use our systematic ESPAR decompositions for the development of pulse shaping in space modulation using single-RF architecture. Pulse shaping is an often overlooked issue in switched antenna systems but must be provided to limit the transmission bandwidth and be suitable for commercial wireless communication use. Our technique as described in [J4] utilizes smooth transitions from ESPAR beams to limit bandwidth expansion while utilizing a single-RF architecture. We have also looked into using our approaches for designing more general MIMO-OFDM single RF systems [J5]. This has been possible by again using the systematic beam decomposition methods described in [J1,J2]. In essence we can form any MIMO signal in beamspace and this allows us to generalize or approaches to single-RF MIMO-OFDM systems. In addition we have shown that the overall structure is energy efficient as compared to the traditional full MIMO OFDM approach. Finally in relation to objective 2 we have also looked into utilizing the techniques described in [J1,J2] for beam forming in wireless communication systems [J3]. This allows the techniques to be utilized in hybrid beamforming while not requiring phase shifters and splitters providing a very energy efficient and cost effective transmission system. To meet objective 3 we have also investigated the prototyping of the proposed approaches. The key structure in the implementations is the use of a varactor to provide reactive loading. We have studied the performance of the systems when the reactive loads are limited in range as well as in specific values. Furthermore, we have investigated the use of the diodes with an inductive offset so we can achieve both positive and negative reactance. Furthermore, investigations have also shown that we can achieve switching speeds of a least 100 MHz and this meets the symbol rates we are aiming for in our wireless communication systems. The outcomes of this work has resulted in a PhD student that graduated in 2022 and another is expected to graduate in 2024. In addition 5 journal papers and one conference paper have been published.

16209019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209019.value: A significant research outcome was the development of the systematic beamspace decomposition methods described in [J1,J2]. This allows any arbitrary antenna structure to be decomposed into a beamspace. The beamspace decomposition can then be used as the basis for wireless system design in multiple input multiple output (MIMO) wireless communication systems. Previously there was no systematic method for performing this and antenna structures were limited to a very few canonical structures based on dipoles. Using this approach we then demonstrated how it can be utilized for implementing wireless communication systems in single-RF form in three applications. These are pulse shaping, OFDM and hybrid beamforming as described in [J3-J5].

16209019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209019.value: There is significant scope for further development. Two areas of interest include the development of space-time antenna systems where our beamspace decomposition can be employed to extend the capabilities of existing antenna designs. The second is in the development of further hybrid beamforming techniques including its application to reconfigurable antennas and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces.

16209019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209019.value: Modern wireless communication systems are complicated systems and require significant sources of energy to power them. In this research we have made breakthroughs that allow increases in energy efficiency and therefore save power consumption. The approach is based on new systematic decomposition methods for antenna systems that can be readily applied to designing energy efficient wireless systems. To help illuminate our technique we have provided designs for three wireless systems that can perform essential communication functions.

16209119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209119.value: 不均勻結冰是在固體表面上的結冰。它在諸多工程和科學領域有著廣泛的應用。在很多應用中, 控制結冰的能力, 包括加速或延緩結冰的速度, 起到非常重要的作用。過去很多年對不均勻結冰的研究的結果並不一致。 傳統的結冰理論也受到質疑。 本課題組近幾年通過分子動力學模擬研究不均勻結冰的動力學,發現固體的表面能和系統溫度在不均勻結冰中起到非常重要的作用。 眾所周知,水分子之間通過氫鍵相互連接形成不穩定的氫鍵網路。 在固體表面上時,水分子和固體分子的作用會打破氫鍵網路,並促使部分水分子在固體表面重新組合形成冰的結構。 這個過程從始至終受到溫度的影響。 因此溫度和固體的表面能對不均勻結冰起到至關重要的作用。 我們的模擬發現,冰的形成隻會在特定的固體表面能和溫度範圍內發生。 在這些範圍內,固體表面能和溫度的作用相若。遺憾的是這一發現還沒有得到實驗的驗證。 在本專案中,我們將通過分子動力學模擬和實驗研究固體表面能和溫度對不均勻結冰的影響。 實驗將定性驗證模擬的結果。 同時,在模擬和實驗結果的基礎上,如有可能,我們將提出用無量綱數描述的有關結冰率的關係式。

16209119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209119.value: Molecular dynamics simulations and experiments have been conducted to study ice nucleation on surfaces of different wetting properties and temperatures. It is found that ice nucleation only takes place in certain ranges of surface energies and temperatures. Outside these ranges, the interplay of surface property and temperature does not promote the formation of stable ice nucleus and eventually impede water crystallization. Simulations were also conducted to investigate ice nucleation under shear. The ice nucleation rate is calculated under various velocity gradients. It is found that the ice nucleation rate changes nonlinearly as the shear rate is varied. It assumes a maximum value at an intermediate shear rate. In addition, we also studied the effects of convex surface roughness on the ice nucleation rate and found that a surface roughness hinders the ice nucleation rate. Supplementary Information: Over-expenditure of “General Expenses”: When modifying the budget, the PI did not realize that experiments would cost so much and a small portion of the fund was proposed for experiments. Nevertheless, the total expenditure is less than HK$ 80,000, which is reasonable for a 3-year project involving experiments.

16209119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209119.value: The findings in this project provide insights into the design of surfaces for hindering or promoting ice formations in various applications. One possible area the PI is exploring is seawater desalination through ice nucleation in seawater. Some numerical simulations and experiments have been conducted. It has been found that the salt concentration in the ice formed in seawater is much lower than that of seawater. Further studies will be carried out to generate drinking water from seawater throuhg ice formation.

16209119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209119.value: The knowledge we obtained about the effects of surface properties and temperature on the ice nucleation has inspired us to explore the water crystallization in seawater to remove ions, which can be used to desalinate seawater. We have obtained some preliminary results, which will help design novel systems to advance the technology of seawater desalination through freezing.

16209519.value: 隱私保護下統一旅行需求洞察的共享共乘

16209519.label: Project Objectives
16209519.value: We will propose effective and efficient models to predict the request demand in ridesharing services. We will design effective route planning methods for workers based on the predicted request-demand to efficiently pick up as many riders as possible. We will develop novel and uniform task assignment strategies to satisfy different targets, including maximizing the quality of services, minimizing the waiting time of riders, or maximizing the revenue of the platform. We will investigate differential privacy solutions for our uniform travel-demand-aware ridesharing framework with privacy protection (UTDR-PP) to protect the location privacy of riders and drivers/workers. Last but not the least, we aim to build the whole system with our developed techniques and apply it to some novel UTDR-PP applications.

16209519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16209519.value: Recently, with the dual goals of alleviating the public traffic congestion and monetarily benefitting drivers and riders, companies (e.g., Uber and DiDi Chuxing) have been allowing their users to enjoy ridesharing services by arranging rides with other passengers within minutes. Similar services can be found in food delivery applications (e.g., Uber Eats and Meituan), which combine food delivery requests and pick-and-drop requests when they share common delivery routes. The ridesharing-related applications face several challenges: 1) the requests dynamically arrive and workers are always moving; 2) the complexity of route planning for hundreds of workers is very high but the processing delay of online services must be as low as possible; 3) the objectives of different applications may vary dramatically from one another; and 4) the location privacy of workers and requesters must be protected, especially now that there is strong public awareness of privacy protection among users. Therefore, we propose to develop a uniform travel-demand-aware ridesharing framework with privacy protection (UTDR-PP), which will learn and predict the request demands, and plan routes for workers/vehicles based on the predicted request demands. In addition, as privacy issue has become increasingly important for modern applications, we will also develop a mechanism based on differential privacy to protect the locations of both requesters and workers. We will build a prototype system based on the techniques developed as a platform for verifying their effectiveness in various UTDR-PP applications with different goals. 最近，為了達到緩解公共交通擁堵和讓司機和乘客獲利的雙重目標 , Uber和DiDi Chuxing 這樣的公司允許他們的用戶通過安排與其他乘客幾分鐘內的共乘服務。在食品遞送應用中可以找到類似的服務 （例如，Uber Eats和Meituan），它結合了食物遞送請求和揀選 當他們共享共同的交付路線時請求。這樣， 與共享共乘車相關的應用程序 將面臨幾個挑戰：1）請求總是動態到達，工人總是 移動的; 2）數百名工人的路線規劃的複雜性非常高 ,但是在線服務的處理延遲必須盡可能低; 3）目標 不同的應用可能會有很大的不同; 4）必須保護司機和共乘者的隱私，特別是現在有強大的 公眾對用戶隱私保護的意識。 因此，我們建議開發統一的旅行需求感知和具有隱私保護的共乘框架（UTDR-PP），它將學習和預測請求 需求，並根據預測的請求需求計劃共乘用戶/車輛的路線。 此外，隨著隱私問題對現代應用變得越來越重要， 我們還將開發一種基於差異隱私的機制來保護乘客和司機的位置隱私。我們將基於這些技術構建原型系統 來驗證這些開發的技術在針對不同目標的各種UTDR-PP應用中的有效性。

16209519.label: Realisation of objectives
16209519.value: 1. To achieve the first objective, we have analyzed the upper bound of real error of spatiotemporal prediction models and have proposed algorithms to minimize the real error by minimizing its upper bound [Conference Paper #6]. 2. To achieve the second objective, we have proposed demand-aware algorithms to make optimal route planning based on the prediction about requests in the future [Conference Paper #12]. 3. To achieve the third objective, we have devised several methods [Conference Paper #11, #13, #14, Journal Paper #2]. Specifically, the method in [Conference Paper #11] enhances the quality of service by effectively arranging meeting points to reduce the time needed for passengers to reach their destinations. The method in [Journal Paper #2] consolidates numerous constraints and different optimization goals into a single expression and proposes an efficient framework to achieve a solution with low waiting time and high platform revenue. The method in [Conference Paper #14] proposes a novel index to efficiently get a solution with high platform revenue. Additionally, the method in [Conference Paper #13] maximizes the fairness of task assignments. 4. To achieve the fourth goal, we have investigated privacy protection methods to protect the location privacy of riders and drivers/workers. Specifically, the method in [Journal Paper #1] maximizes worker reliability while protecting privacy. The method in [Conference Paper #1] minimizes worker movement distance while protecting privacy. The method in [Conference Paper #3] maximizes the number of successfully assigned tasks while protecting privacy. 5. To achieve the fifth goal, we have developed a prototype that integrates the key technical methods proposed in this project. We have used the prototype to test the effectiveness and efficiency of our methods.

16209519.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209519.value: In this project, we first designed effective and efficient models to predict the demand for requests in ridesharing services [Conference Paper #6]. Then, we developed some effective route planning methods for workers based on the predicted request demand, aimed at efficiently picking up as many riders as possible [Conference Paper #12]. Additionally, we devised novel and uniform task assignment strategies to satisfy different targets [Conference Paper #11, #13, #14, Journal Paper #2], including maximizing the quality of services [Conference Paper #11], minimizing the waiting time of riders [Journal Paper #2], and maximizing the revenue of the platform [Conference Paper #14]. Furthermore, we investigated differential privacy solutions for our uniform travel-demand-aware ridesharing framework with privacy protection (UTDR-PP) to safeguard the location privacy of riders and drivers/workers [Conference Paper #1, #3, Journal Paper #1].

16209519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209519.value: This research project aims to develop a new system for ridesharing services, such as Uber and DiDi Chuxing, that takes into account the demand for rides and the privacy of users. The system will use data to predict where and when people will need rides, and then plan the most efficient routes for drivers to pick them up. The privacy of both drivers and passengers will also be protected using a technique called differential privacy. This means that their locations will be kept private, even while using the service. The significance of this project is that it could help to reduce traffic congestion and provide a more efficient and cost-effective way of getting around. It could also benefit drivers and riders by providing more opportunities for work and cheaper rides. Additionally, the privacy protection aspect is becoming increasingly important in today’s world, and this project aims to address that concern. Overall, the project has the potential to make a positive impact on transportation and privacy for many people.

16209819.label: Realisation of objectives
16209819.value: Objective 1: Investigate the interface properties between 2D single-/multi-layer MoS2 and WeS2 and 3D GaN (e.g. undoped-GaN and p-type GaN) or 3D dielectric (e.g. SiNx, SiO2, high-k dielectric) MoS2 films have been transferred to SiO2/Si (i.e., (100) Si substrate coated with thermally grown SiO2) and GaN-on-Si (i.e., epitaxial GaN layer grown on (111) silicon substrate) substrates by a modified wet-transfer technique to carry out the experimental analysis. The optical microscopic images of transferred monolayer MoS2 on different substrates are captured and the different optical contrast observed in SiO2/Si substrate and GaN-on-Si substrate can be used to determine the film thickness of the transferred 2D materials. Single- and multi-layer MoS2 thin films prepared by exfoliation and chemical vapor deposition have been characterized by micro Raman spectroscopy. Clear peaks identified with 1L, 2L 4L and 6L MoS2 are observed in the exfoliated MoS2 samples, while no peaks can be found in the CVD MoS2 sample. Such an observation gave the first hint that the quality of CVD-grown MoS2 samples may not be adequate to be used as the semiconducting gate in this project, despite its advantage in large size and better uniformity (compared to the exfoliated films) that are favoured for transistor development. Objective 2: Design and prepare 2D semiconductors with various layer thickness for GaN-based SG-FET Single-layer MoS2 was transferred to AlGaN/GaN HEMT sample to demonstrate the semiconducting gate (SG) field-effect transistors (FETs) for this project. Such a device exhibits depletion-mode (D-mode) operation. The demonstrated SG-HEMT shows no penalties to the ON/OFF switching, the current driving capability, and the breakdown voltage. The semiconducting-gate structure exhibits clear evidence of being capable of clamping the effective forward gate voltage to a depletion threshold voltage of the SG, which inherently sets a limit on the maximum allowed forward gate stress. The demonstrated AlGaN/GaN SG-HEMT has validated the feasibility and superiority of SG in providing over-voltage protection. Transfer curves of the SG-HEMT after high-k dielectric passivation are measured with a relatively larger gate swing (from -10 V to 10 V). No obvious threshold voltage changes are observed after the dielectric passivation. Compared with the SG-HEMT before passivation, the gate leakage increases. This gate leakage increase can be attributed to the changes of doping conditions in MoS2 SG. After dielectric passivation, the conductivity of MoS2 SG increases significantly as a result of the increased carrier density and the boosted electron mobility (from 0.06 cm2/Vs to 6 cm2/Vs). Nevertheless, the gate leakage of SG-HEMT is still much smaller than that of MG-HEMT. The device is a depletion-mode (D-mode) HEMT with a threshold voltage of -4 V. Enhancement-mode (E-mode) operation with a positive threshold voltage is required in many circuit applications including power switches that are normally off to satisfy fail-safe requirement, n-channel FET in CMOS logic circuits, etc. Due to strong charge polarization in AlGaN/GaN heterojunctions, AlGaN/GaN HEMTs usually exhibit normally-on (or depletion-mode) operation. Inserting a p-type GaN layer in the gate stack is an effective and widely adopted approach to realizing E-mode operation, since the p-GaN layer can deplete the underlying heterojunction 2DEG (2-dimentional electron gas) channel in a similar way as in a junction FET (JFET). The operation of SG-FET, on the other hand, requires a n-type semiconductor layer on top of the n-channel. The presence of the p-GaN layer imposes additional challenge to the MoS2 semiconducting gate on the top. A p-n junction is formed between the p-GaN and n-type MoS2 layer, leading to depletion of n-type MoS2. This depletion region would further expand under positive gate bias (which is a reverse bias applied to the MoS2/p-GaN n-p junction). Since the MoS2 layer needs to remain conductive until the underlying 2DEG channel is fully turned on, much thicker (e.g., more than 40 layers) MoS2 is required even with a relatively high n-type doping concentration of 5 ×1018/cm3. Based on the current status of CVD-grown multi-layer MoS2 thin films, it is very difficult to grow high-quality thick (e.g., more than 10 layers) with good uniformity. It is even more challenging to dope the multi-layer MoS2 with high density dopants. At this juncture, several conclusions are drawn. First, single-layer MoS2 is sufficient to realize SG-HEMTs with D-mode operation as MoS2 can be sufficiently doped by introducing surface defects and it is not depleted because of the absence of p-GaN layer. Second, the present growth techniques for multi-layer n-doped MoS2 thin films cannot deliver MoS2 films with adequate thickness, doping concentration and uniformity for the development of E-mode SG-HEMTs. With further in-depth analysis and extensive device simulations, a new and more practical scheme to implementing E-mode SG-HEMT has been identified. A n-type GaN layer with a thickness of 25 nm and a doping concentration of 5×1018/cm3 is found to be able to satisfy the design requirement, delivering full gate control of the channel current and yet complete pinch-off at appropriate gate bias (e.g., at Vgs > 7 V). There are several important practical advantages in using epitaxial n-type GaN to replace multi-layer MoS2 thin films as the semiconducting gate material. These benefits include i) seamless epitaxial growth of n-GaN on p-GaN using MOCVD, ii) great controllability, uniformity and crystalline quality of MOCVD grown GaN layers, and iii) greatly improved electron mobility in n-GaN layer. Objective 3: Develop fabrication process and demonstrate enhancement-/depletion-mode 2D/3D SG-FETs based on GaN heterojunctions, Design and prepare 2D semiconductors with various layer thickness for GaN-based SG-FET；Extend the 2D/3D SG-FET demonstration to Si MOSFETs and IGZO TFTs A 6-inch GaN-on-Si wafer designed for 650-V E-mode p-GaN gate power HEMTs was designed and prepared by Enkris Semiconductor (a reliable material supplier to us) in Suzhou, China. The epitaxial structure features a 4.2-µm high-resistivity GaN buffer layer, a 420-nm un-doped GaN channel layer, a 15-nm Al0.2Ga0.8N barrier layer, a 100-nm p-GaN cap layer with an Mg doping concentration of 4 × 1019 cm−3, and a 25-nm n-GaN cap layer with Si doping concentration of 8 × 1019 cm−3. The epi-wafer has a smooth surface with a roughness root mean square (Rq) of 0.68 nm for an area of 5×5 m2. The main steps of the fabrication process of SG-HEMT have been developed. Objective 4: Conduct systematic device characterization/evaluation and develop physical/circuit models for the proposed 2D/3D SG-FET The quasi-static transfer and output characteristics of the all-GaN SG-HEMT are measured. The device is an E-mode device with a Vth of 1 V. A subthreshold swing (SS) of 119 mV/dec is obtained at VGS = 0.8 V. The ON/OFF ratio of the device is larger than 108. The RON resistance of the device is 15 mΩ·mm. The most important result is in the gate breakdown voltage, which is measured to exceed 30 V in the SG-HEMT while a conventional p-GaN Gate HEMT exhibits a forward gate breakdown voltage in the range of 10~15 V. The concept of semiconducting-gate HEMT is hence successfully demonstrated.

16209819.label: Major findings and research outcome
16209819.value: The stability, electronic and optical properties of MoS2/GaN heterostructure are systematically studied. A nitridation interfacial layer is inserted at MoS2/GaN interface and is found to generate desirable features in some applications. The results prove that with little lattice mismatch and negative formation energy, the MoS2/GaN heterostructure with a nitridation interfacial layer can be experimentally achieved. A semiconducting gate is shown to provide inherent gate over-voltage protection for field-effect transistors. The semiconducting gate scheme is experimentally demonstrated on an AlGaN/GaN HEMT, by implementing single-layer MoS2 as the semiconducting gate. The demonstrated SG-HEMT shows no penalties to the ON/OFF switching, the current driving capability, and the breakdown voltage. Most importantly, the SG can clamp the effective forward gate voltage to the depletion threshold voltage of the SG, which inherently sets a limit on the maximum allowed forward gate stress. Furthermore, because of the self-adjustable SG potential above the channel, the SG gate can even boost the ON-current, while guaranteeing the safe operation of SG-HEMT. The demonstrated AlGaN/GaN SG-HEMT has validated the feasibility and superiority of SG in providing over-voltage protection and boosting the ON-current, which can be further extended to other field-effect transistors to enhance the device reliability and stability in the future and can find potential applications in cases where the over-voltage protection is critical or a boosted ON-current is demanded. Despite the flexibility of 2D/3D heterojunctions, the continuous crystalline 2D material thin films are still limited in size of ~100 m, which is far from enough for practical usage. With the proven concept of SG-HEMT, an all-GaN SG-HEMT emerges as a much better structure for its greater potential of manufacturing. A 6-inch GaN-on-Si wafer designed for 650-V E-mode power HEMTs was designed, prepared and processed for the all-GaN SG-HEMT. The quasi-static transfer and output characteristics of the all-GaN SG-HEMT are measured. The device is an E-mode device with a Vth of 1 V. A subthreshold swing (SS) of 119 mV/dec is obtained at VGS = 0.8 V. The ON/OFF ratio of the device is larger than 1E8. The RON resistance of the device is 15 mΩ·mm. The most important result is in the gate breakdown voltage, which is measured to exceed 30 V in the SG-HEMT while a conventional p-GaN Gate HEMT exhibits a forward gate breakdown voltage in the range of 10~15 V. The concept of semiconducting-gate HEMT is hence successfully demonstrated.

16209819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16209819.value: The all-GaN SG-HEMT has a unique feature in that the gate electrode is composed of a n-type GaN layer with an exposed surface, which can be functionalized for various sensing. Previously, GaN HEMT based sensors mostly feature ungated region for sensing. Such a structure provides an exposed surface for functionalization but is lack of ways for local electrical manipulation. The all-GaN SG-HEMT could be further developed for sensing application, especially high temperatures. A RGC GRF proposal will be prepared in the coming years, e.g., in 2024.

16209819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16209819.value: Field-effect transistors (FETs) as voltage-controlled switches are the most foundational circuit elements of modern electronics and have supported a wide range of existing and emerging applications to drive the advancement of modern society. The FETs’ control terminal, i.e. the gate, has always been implemented with conducting materials such as polysilicon (for many silicon-based FETs) or metal. In this project, by taking advantage of the unique properties of 2D layered semiconductors and implementing them as the gate on top of 3D semiconductor channel, we developed FETs featuring a semiconducting gate. Such semiconducting gate FETs will deliver new features that are highly desirable in applications, e.g. an inherent over-voltage protection at the input gate. Such a voltage-clamping scheme, when inherently embedded into the gate electrode, would provide internal gate over-voltage protection without taking up additional device area, and could potentially lead to user-friendly FETs with enhanced gate robustness. The semiconducting gate FET concept has been successfully expanded to an all-GaN platform that removes the need of transferring 2D materials to the GaN platform. Substantial improvement in gate over-voltage protection, from 15 V to over 30 V has been achieved in 650-V enhancement-mode GaN power HEMT devices.

16210219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210219.value: 由水與泥土構成的泥石流經常導致人命傷亡同建築物損毀。為了在人口稠密的地區有效整治泥石流，混凝土防護牆經常被採用並建造於山腳中。然而，在土地缺乏及環境保護的因素之下，此方法的可行性日趨降低。更甚的是，在山腳中建造混凝土防護牆會導致泥石流帶走更多表面泥土，從而對該防護牆的可擋泥石流容量要求增加。 除了混凝土防護牆外，另一個可行的整治方法是沿著管道安裝多個柔性防護網。柔性防護網可以融入週邊環境，其可變形特性令可擋泥石流的容量提高。另外，在管道中的不同位置安裝多個柔性防護網可以減低泥石流帶走表面泥土的量。雖然柔性防護網有不少好處，但在缺乏具可受侵蝕泥土環境下的大型物理實驗數據的支持，以及泥石流其難以預測的特性兩個因素之下，柔性防護網的機理仍然未明。在未有明確考慮該些因素之下，柔性防護網設計的足夠程度實在難以了解。 此項目的主要及獨特之處在於大型物理實驗中，模擬在具可受侵蝕泥土的環境之下，安裝兩個柔性防護網時的表現。為了完善地研究柔性防護網的機理，該網的硬度亦將會由一個已獲專利的原創制動元件控制及改變，從而研究原型柔性防護網其複雜的動態反應。另外，一項有關柔性防護網之間的距離對減低泥石流帶走表面泥土的量的研究亦將會展開。該些大型物理實驗將會提供獨一無二的數據用作校準一個名為LS-DYNA的有限元模型作數值分析。此外，一個可執行泥石流帶走表面泥土的模型亦將會在此有限元模型內運作。最後，此項目研究所得成果將會用作編寫一本可以設計多個柔性防護網的指引。

16210219.label: Realisation of objectives
16210219.value: All of the revised objectives have been realized. First, the impact mechanisms of debris flows against multiple flexible barriers are at the core of this project and have been revealed by using observed impact kinematics and measurements from large-scale physical model test data. Second, the effects of spacing between barriers has been investigated using combined experimental and numerical results to optimize their configuration. Third, as a result of the first two objectives, a set of unique experimental evidence has been produced. Fourth, a parametric study has been carried out to fill in the gaps in the experimental data using LS-DYNA. Last, based on the above objectives, design recommendations have been proposed in journal publications stemming from this study.

16210219.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210219.value: The following key research findings and outcomes have emerged from this project: 1) An upstream barrier with a design capacity for just 20% of the initial debris volume can significantly reduce the peak discharge on a second barrier by creating several smaller overflow surges. This results in a decrease of up to 70% in impact force on the second barrier compared to scenarios without an upstream barrier. 2) Overflow drag loading on the upstream barrier may increase the total resisting forces needed. To account for this, it is recommended to increase the design impact pressure by 31%. 3) The interaction between flow, bed, and barrier is scale-dependent. Increasing the scale of an event can intensify erosion and subsequently raise impact forces on downstream barriers. Therefore, it is essential to evaluate the spacing between barriers, deformation, barrier height, and slope to optimize a multiple barrier design with an erodible bed in between. 4) Contrary to current erosion theories, erosion rates increase approximately parabolically, rather than linearly, with bed water content. This can be attributed to the nonlinear relationship between the shear strength of unsaturated soil and bed water content under capillary effects. This discovery suggests that traditional erosion theories may not always provide conservative estimates of erosion, particularly when bed water content is low. 5) While existing literature primarily focuses on basal shear stress as the driving force for soil bed erosion, this study demonstrates that collisional stresses also play a significant role. This is evidenced by the positive correlation between erosion rate and collisional stress, supporting field observation hypotheses and emphasizing the need to model flow fronts with coarse particles to replicate prototype flow dynamics. 6) There is a critical water content for generating pore water pressure. This critical value corresponds to the water content where the initial matric suction of the soil bed equals the increase in pore water pressure during undrained loading. When the bed water content falls below this value, positive pore water pressure is barely generated or detected. 7) When exposed to landslide loading, the volume contraction of unsaturated soil due to air phase compressibility mobilizes shear strength, counteracting frictional shear stress caused by flow overburden. This finding underscores the importance of considering unsaturated soil mechanisms when assessing soil bed erosion resulting from flow-type landslides, as the assumption of saturated soil beds in existing theories is unrealistic.

16210219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210219.value: To further advance this research, the following actions are recommended: 1) Incorporate boundary collisional stresses and erosion rates, which increase linearly with flow particle size and Froude number, into bed erosion models. This will enhance the prediction of erosion potential in flow-type landslides. 2) Address the complexity of modeling debris flow erosion, which arises from the non-uniform spatial distribution of collisional stresses and the nonlinear effects of water content on unsaturated soil shear strength. Improve existing rheological models by explicitly considering collisional stresses and unsaturated soil beds, as current models may be oversimplifications of the actual phenomena. Additionally, obtain high-fidelity field data on bed suction to validate unsaturated erosion models. 3) Recognize that flexible barriers in the field are permeable, while the barriers modeled in this study are mostly impermeable due to the dense fines mesh used. The impact dynamics on the second barrier in the channel may differ from those observed in this study when debris is discharged through the net. 4) Note that this study only examined linear channel configurations. Flow dynamics in curved barriers may significantly differ from those in curvilinear configurations, warranting further investigation using numerical methods.

16210219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210219.value: Prior to this project, there was a lack of scientific foundation for designing multiple flexible barriers, as impact processes were rarely observed in the field and a well-documented, reliable, and systematic collection of large-scale physical experimental data did not exist. Designs were primarily based on empirical evidence. Furthermore, the use of successive flexible barriers to reduce the entrainment of erodible beds and thus the overall volume along a channel had not been explored. Most studies focused on smooth beds, which significantly differed from actual field conditions. This project addressed existing scientific challenges in flow-barrier interaction by revealing the complex interplay between debris flow and deformable barriers, as well as the effects of multiple barriers on entrainment physics. The outcomes directly benefit engineers and scientists responsible for protecting densely populated and vulnerable mountainous regions worldwide, including Hong Kong, Italy, Japan, and the United States. The new scientific recommendations serve as a benchmark for engineers seeking sustainable alternatives to physical countermeasures against debris-flow hazards. Additionally, the unique set of large-scale physical experimental data and the calibrated finite element numerical model generated by this project hold significant value for researchers and practitioners.
