16210419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210419.value: Gas turbines are routinely used to propel aircraft and generate electricity. They are efficient and reliable, but emit pollutants such as nitrogen oxides (NOx), endangering public health and the environment by exacerbating respiratory disease and global warming. Gas-turbine manufacturers are attempting to reduce NOx emissions by switching to lean premixed combustion, but this tends to cause thermoacoustic oscillations. These are self-excited flow oscillations arising from the feedback between unsteady combustion and sound. If left unchecked, such oscillations can exacerbate noise, vibration and pollutant emissions, eventually leading to catastrophic structural failure. Existing tools available to weaken thermoacoustic oscillations fall into two categories: passive control and active control. Passive control is elegant and preferred but requires a detailed understanding of the system, which is not always attainable owing to the complexity of flame-hydrodynamics-acoustics interactions. Open-loop control can be effective even without knowledge of the system physics, but tends not to adapt well to changes in operating conditions. Closed-loop control can adapt better, but most feedback algorithms suffer from two drawbacks. First, they are designed to target periodic oscillations, which have a single frequency and amplitude. Recent research, however, has revealed that thermoacoustic oscillations can often be quasiperiodic or chaotic, with a range of different frequencies and amplitudes. Second, most feedback algorithms require a low-order model of the system, which can be difficult to obtain for complex turbulent combustors. When developing the next generation of low-NOx gas turbines, it is therefore essential to have effective model-free tools for weakening aperiodic thermoacoustic oscillations. We propose to exploit the optimization capabilities of machine learning to discover closed-loop control laws for aperiodic thermoacoustic oscillations, without using a system model. This unsupervised data-driven framework, called genetic-programming-based machine learning control (GP-MLC), has been shown to be able to discover laws for control tasks so complex that they are beyond the capabilities of conventional controllers. We will implement GP-MLC on two existing experimental rigs (one laminar and one turbulent), both of which have been shown to exhibit a range of nonlinear dynamics, including periodicity, quasiperiodicity and chaos. We will analyze the mathematical structure of the GP-MLC laws to gain insight into the flow physics, and benchmark their performance (quantified by a cost function) against that of the optimal periodic forcing strategy found previously through open-loop mapping. This study will enable new model-free control laws to be discovered for aperiodic thermoacoustic oscillations, aiding the development of the next generation of clean gas turbines. 燃氣輪機通常用於航空推進與發電。它們可靠並且高效，但會產生有害污染物，例如氮氧化物（NOx）。這會引起呼吸道疾病和全球變暖，從而危害公眾健康和生態環境。燃氣輪機製造商們正在通過改用貧油預混燃燒來減少NOx的排放，但這往往會引發燃燒室中的熱聲振盪。熱聲振盪是由不穩定的燃燒和聲波之間的反饋作用引起的自激流動振盪。如果不加以控制，熱聲振盪會加劇噪音，振動和污染物排放，最終導致災難性的結構故障。 現有用於減弱熱聲振盪的方法分為兩類：被動控制與主動控制。被動控制是簡潔且優選的方法，但使用該方法時需要對系統有詳細深入的了解。由於火焰-流體力學-聲學相互作用的複雜性，被動控制方法通常難以實現。相較而言，開環控制即使在不了解系統中物理過程的情況下也可發揮功效，但通常不能很好地適應工況的變化。閉環控制可以更好地適應工況變化，但大多數反饋算法都有兩個缺點。首先，它們原本的應用目標是具有單一頻率和振幅的周期性振盪。然而，最近的研究表明，熱聲振盪通常也可以是準週期性的或混沌的，因此系統中存在一系列不同的頻率和振幅。其次，大多數反饋算法需要系統的低階模型，這對於復雜的湍流燃燒器來說可能很難獲得。因此，在研發下一代低NOx燃氣輪機時，有必要開發有效的無模型控制方法來減弱非週期性熱聲振盪。 我們計劃在不使用系統模型的情況下，利用機器學習的優化功能來研究非週期性熱聲振盪的閉環控制法則。這種無監督的數據驅動框架被稱為基於遺傳編程的機器學習控制方法（GP-MLC）。這種方法已被證明能夠發現超出傳統控制器能力的複雜控制法則。我們將在兩個現有的實驗平台（一個層流和一個湍流）上實現GP-MLC，這兩個實驗平台已被證明具有一系列非線性動力學特徵，包括週期性，準週期性和混沌性。我們將分析GP-MLC法則的數學結構，以深入了解流動現象中的物理原理，並將其控制性能通過成本函數進行量化，最終與先前通過開環控制方法找到的最優週期激勵策略進行對比。本項研究将使得針對非週期性熱聲振盪的無模型控製成為可能，從而為下一代潔淨燃氣輪機的開發助力。

16210419.label: Realisation of objectives
16210419.value: To achieve the project objectives, we combined automated experiments with genetic-programming-based machine learning control (GP-MLC) to discover model-free control laws for suppressing periodic and aperiodic flow oscillations in thermoacoustic and hydrodynamic systems, including laminar and turbulent combustors and a low-density inertial jet. Specifically, we established two closed loops: (i) a fast inner loop for real-time control and (ii) a slow outer loop for training the GP-MLC algorithm. The real-time loop is a classic feedback control loop with four components: a system (combustor or jet), an actuator (loudspeaker), a sensor (probe microphone or hot-wire anemometer), and a programmable controller. We hosted the real-time control loop on a programmable controller running at a sample-command frequency an order of magnitude higher than the characteristic frequencies of the self-excited thermoacoustic and hydrodynamic oscillations. The GP-MLC framework uses an evolutionary algorithm to make decisions based on natural selection. Starting from an initial generation of individuals (i.e. control laws), we ranked their performance based on a cost function balancing the state cost (pressure or velocity amplitude) and the input cost (actuator power). We then bred subsequent generations of individuals via a tournament, directly forwarding elite individuals alongside genetic operations such as mutation, replication, and crossover. We implemented this GP-MLC framework in both closed-loop and open-loop forms, and benchmarked it against conventional open-loop control using time-periodic forcing. We found that, with minimal user input, GP-MLC can discover effective model-free control laws for suppressing a variety of periodic and aperiodic flow oscillations in thermoacoustic and hydrodynamic systems. By analyzing the functional form of these control laws, we were able to identify new actuation mechanisms, providing insight into the underlying flow physics. Overall, this project has opened up new pathways for data-driven feedback control of nonlinear flow systems.

16210419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210419.value: We experimentally applied genetic-programming-based machine learning control (GP-MLC) to discover model-free control laws for suppressing periodic and aperiodic flow oscillations in thermoacoustic and hydrodynamic systems, including laminar and turbulent combustors and a low-density inertial jet. For all systems, we implemented GP-MLC in both closed-loop and open-loop forms, and benchmarked it against conventional open-loop control based on time-periodic forcing. In the laminar combustor, we found that while all three control strategies can achieve similarly large reductions in thermoacoustic amplitude for both periodic and aperiodic oscillations, GP-MLC closed-loop control consumes the least actuator power, making it the most efficient. It achieves this efficiency by learning an actuation mechanism that exploits the strong heat-release-rate (HRR) amplification of the open flame at its preferred mode, even though the GP-MLC algorithm has never seen the open flame itself. This preferred mode aligns with the frequency at which the gain of the flame describing function reaches its maximum value under low perturbation amplitudes. In the turbulent combustor, we found that like in the laminar case, GP-MLC closed-loop control outperforms both GP-MLC open-loop control and conventional open-loop control based on time-periodic forcing. However, the actuation mechanism differs: the thermoacoustic amplitude is reduced via synchronous quenching without resonant amplification. The acoustic field becomes synchronized with the external forcing, and its coupling with the HRR field is disrupted. The formation of large-scale vortical structures is impeded, promoting a steadier HRR response that is more decoupled from the acoustic field. The presence of phase drifting and a decrease in the Rayleigh index substantiate the flame-acoustic decoupling, resulting in a suppression of the self-excited thermoacoustic oscillations. In the hydrodynamically self-excited jet, we found that once again, GP-MLC closed-loop control outperforms both GP-MLC open-loop control and conventional open-loop control based on time-periodic forcing. The actuation mechanism of GP-MLC closed-loop control appears to leverage multi-frequency perturbations to stabilize the global hydrodynamic mode, delaying the onset of self-excited instability. By contrast, both GP-MLC open-loop control and conventional open-loop control act by suppressing the global hydrodynamic mode with single-frequency perturbations. Overall, we have demonstrated the feasibility of using GP-MLC to discover new and more efficient model-free control laws for suppressing a variety of periodic and aperiodic flow oscillations in thermoacoustic and hydrodynamic systems, offering a promising approach to data-driven feedback control of nonlinear flow systems. This work has led to several journal publications and conference presentations, which are listed in Part C.

16210419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210419.value: This project has opened up several directions for future research. The demonstrated ability of GP-MLC to efficiently and effectively suppress various self-excited flow oscillations in thermoacoustic and hydrodynamic systems raises the possibility that it can be applied to other nonlinear dynamical systems as well. For instance, it may be possible to use GP-MLC to control the low-frequency flow oscillations behind an airfoil near stall conditions, or to mitigate vortex shedding behind bridges and high-rise buildings. Looking beyond fluid flow applications, there is potential to apply GP-MLC in other domains, notably in the field of medicine. Possible medical applications could include regulating drug delivery, controlling neuron activity through deep brain stimulation, or mitigating epilepsy via transcranial electrical stimulation. We are currently in discussions with medical researchers in Hong Kong to explore such potential applications of GP-MLC in the healthcare sector. Overall, the success of this project in discovering efficient model-free control strategies for suppressing nonlinear oscillations suggests that GP-MLC could be a versatile tool for tackling a wide range of complex dynamics. Expanding the use of this data-driven machine learning framework to new problem domains, both in engineering and in other scientific fields, presents an exciting area for future work.

16210419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210419.value: Gas turbines are widely used to generate power and propel aircraft, but they also emit pollutants like nitrogen oxides (NOx) that can harm public health and the environment. To reduce these emissions, engineers often use lean premixed combustion, but this can trigger thermoacoustic oscillations. Such oscillations are pressure fluctuations that arise from the complex interactions between the flames and the sound waves in a combustor. If severe, such oscillations can increase pollutant emissions and reduce the reliability and efficiency of the gas turbine. In this project, we developed a new data-driven machine learning approach, based on genetic programming, that can efficiently and effectively suppress thermoacoustic oscillations, as well as their associated hydrodynamic oscillations. The key advantage of this framework is that it does not require a model of the system; instead, it can directly learn control laws from experimental data. We analyzed the mathematical structure of the control laws generated by this genetic programming approach to gain insights into the underlying fluid dynamics and thermoacoustic phenomena. We also benchmarked the performance of these control laws against existing strategies. Overall, this work demonstrates the potential of model-free data-driven control strategies to advance the development of gas turbines with reduced environmental impact.

16210619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210619.value: The objective of this project is to conduct a comprehensive study of the learning-based methods with applications in networked control systems. This approach allows us to derive an optimal communication strategy that is adaptive to the channel conditions in a unified framework. In the 5G era, it is envisioned that objects of everyday life will be equipped with micro-controllers and micro-sensors for operation, as well as transceivers for remote monitoring and control. Such an exciting vision of networked control systems, however, is threatened by the potential unreliability of wireless connections due to their fading nature. Several phenomenons, such as packet drops and delays, introduce further challenges to control system engineers. A cross-layer design involving both the control system and the communication network must be developed to enhance the adaptability of the physical control system to wireless connection. Because of the uncertain nature of the communication channel, the majority of the existing research models the networked control system as a stochastic control system and utilize stochastic techniques to optimize sensor scheduling polices and feedback control laws. These works all assume that the network condition is available as the a priori knowledge. In actual applications, however, either acquiring the channel information is costly or the channel condition is slowly varying over time. We aim to design a learning algorithm for control under uncertain communication conditions and to analyze the transient performance of the UCB-based algorithms in adaptive channel selection. We will further develop a control algorithm for a multi-agent system via distributed iterative learning to reduce the communication overhead and to achieve the desired system performance. 該項目旨在全面研究如何將基於學習的方法應用於網絡化控制系統。我們能夠利用基於學習的方法，在統壹的框架下，得到壹種關於信道狀況自使用的最優通信策略。可以設想，在5G時代，日常生活中的各種設備的運行都依賴於微型控制器和傳感器以及通信傳輸接發裝置，以便實現遠程監控和控制。不過，如此激動人心的設想目前受限於不完全可靠的無線通信網絡，這是由無線信道的衰減特性導致。控制系統工程師將面臨諸如通信網絡中的丟包、延遲等現象的挑戰。將控制系統和通信系統共同考慮，進行跨層設計迫在眉睫。跨層設計的方法可以使得物理控制系統更加適應於無線連接。由於通信網絡具有不確定性，目前大多數研究都把網絡化控制系統建模為壹個隨機控制系統，並利用隨機技術優化傳感器調度策略、設計反饋控制律。目前文獻大都假設網絡的狀況是壹種先驗知識。然而在實際應用中，獲取信道信息產生額外的消耗，而且信道狀況也會隨時間緩慢變化。我們考慮設計壹種可以學習的方法，以實現未知通信狀況下的控制。我們將分析基於UCB的學習方法在自適應信道選擇中的瞬態性能。此外，我們設計控制多智能體系統的方法，並通過分布式叠代學習的方法減少通信開銷，滿足系統性能需求。

16210719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16210719.value: 下一代無線網絡需要支持移動數據流量的持續性指數增長和眾多應用，包括萬物互聯，觸覺互聯網和機器對機器通信。此類應用將具有嚴格的性能要求，例如極高的數據速率和超低延遲。網絡密集化是應對這些挑戰的關鍵技術，並被認為是實現5G及後續移動網絡的關鍵驅動。在諸如雲無線接入網絡（Cloud RAN）和宏/微小區/微微小區的密集網絡中，多個接入點（AP）之間的協作是必要的。有效的資源分配（例如功率控制和用戶調度）對於在復雜環境中有效利用有限資源也是至關重要的。在此項目中，我們的目標是開發用於協作密集無線網絡的有效的資源分配方法，其可以提供優異的性能並且實時執行。如果成功，那麼這項研究可以具有開創性和持久的影響，但這無疑是一項重大挑戰。傳統的設計方法不能直接應用於大規模密集網絡，因為設計複雜度隨網絡規模呈指數級增長。此外，密集網絡動態變化並且本質上複雜，這使得開發全面的分析模型變得難以處理。傳統資源分配算法的高計算要求也使得它們在密集網絡中的實時實現由於網絡參數的快速變化而具有挑戰性。此外，優化問題通常帶有組合變量並且是NP-hard。 機器學習是最有前途的人工智能工具之一，可用於支持智能網絡。它在處理大規模系統方面具有巨大的潛力，並且不依賴於分析模型。最近，許多研究已經應用機器學習來解決無線網絡中的資源分配問題。在此項目中，我們的目標是開發基於機器學習的創新方法，用於協作無線密集網絡中的可擴展資源分配。所提出的方法涉及使用強大的“學習優化”框架來通過模仿全局最優分支定界算法來開發數據驅動和計算有效的資源分配算法。我們致力於為複雜的優化問題獲得近乎最優的解決方案，並有效地執行用於大規模無線網絡的開發算法。為了考慮信道狀態信息（CSI）的不確定性，我們進一步研究了不完美CSI的影響並提高了所開發算法的魯棒性。最後，我們還將開發一個開源求解器作為協作密集無線網絡中資源管理的強大工具。

16210719.label: Realisation of objectives
16210719.value: In future wireless networks and particularly 6th generation (6G) mobile and wireless communication systems, machine learning (ML) is expected to play a crucial role in enhancing the performance, network capacity, and efficiency of such systems. For example, ML algorithms can help in intelligent resource allocation in wireless networks. By analyzing network conditions, traffic patterns, and user behavior, ML models can make informed decisions on how to allocate radio resources such as bandwidth, power, and channels. One of the key objectives of this project is to study this new potentially transformative paradigm by investigating the use of ML in wireless networks, as well as develop innovative ML-based methods for scalable resource allocation in wireless networks. The proposed approach involves the use of a powerful “learn to optimize” framework to develop data-driven and computationally efficient resource allocation algorithms by imitating the globally optimal branch-and-bound algorithm. Our overreaching focus was to obtain near-optimal solutions to the complex optimization problems and efficiently execute the developed algorithms for wireless communications networks. We are very pleased to report that we are extremely fortunate as we were able to obtain exceptionally important and impactful results as a result of our work in the project. In particular, we were able to • Develop a general computationally efficient machine learning-based framework for optimizing resource allocation in wireless networks. • Expand the developed framework to improve scalability using innovative techniques such as transfer learning, as well as an unsupervised LORM framework based on self-imitation. • Conduct a performance evaluation and analysis of the developed algorithms for different resource allocation problems in different networks, including Cloud RANs, device-to-device (D2D) networks, cell-free networks, and millimeter-wave (mmWave) networks. • Produce significant research results while contributing to the development of innovative technologies and training of highly qualified research students. In this regards, we were able to have multiple papers in top journals and conferences. These include - 2 papers in the IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications. - 1 paper in the IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications. - 3 conference papers in prestigious venues. We were also able to train one student on this important topic (PhD student who has already graduated in 2022.) The following is the summary of some of our completed work as a result of this project. Further details can be obtained from our published work listed in the Research Output Section. LEARN TO OPTIMIZE FRAMEWORK DEVELOPMENT Resource management plays a pivotal role in wireless communications. The existing optimization-based algorithms are often time-consuming and thus cannot be applied in real systems due to real-time constraints and the growing complexities of wireless networks. While existing works attempted to use learning to optimize methods, they treat neural networks as a Blackbox and may not be able to guarantee system performance nor be able to complete the optimization in real-time. During our study in the project, we were able to develop a learning-based framework for resource management, which we referred to as Learning to Optimize for Resource Allocation (LORM). Specifically, we designed a sample-efficient approach, namely, imitation learning, to learn the policies in the branch-and-bound algorithm and significantly reduce the required number of samples to achieve good accuracy. The imitation learning, together with the strong inductive bias by the optimal branch-and-bound algorithm, contributes to the extremely sample-efficient framework. In contrast to previous works requiring at least thousands of training samples, tens of training samples are sufficient for LORM to achieve a good performance. The proposed framework was tested in energy-efficient and Green Cloud-RANs. it was demonstrated that the proposed framework can achieve the same level of performance as the state-of-the-art solution, with a much less power consumption. Moreover, we were able to study the tradeoff between the computation time and performance accuracy, which constitutes the core part of the fundamental trade-off between latency and reliability. LORM WITH TRANSFER LEARNING (LORM-TL) To address the challenge of the distribution shifts between the training domains and test domains in learning-based wireless resource management, we designed and developed a transfer-learning based approach to adapt LORM to new scenarios. It was then shown that LORM can quickly adapt to a new environment and become near-optimal. LORM WITH SELF-IMITATION (LORM-SI) To achieve scalability, we developed an unsupervised LORM framework based on self-imitation (SI). SI takes advantage of the exploration in reinforcement learning, which leads to an unsupervised paradigm. The key idea is to explore the search tree and use the best solution found during the exploration as the label for imitation learning. In this way, the search space is enlarged and will contain better solutions than the learned policy. Our obtained results have shown that LORM-SI can achieve a 10x speedup compared to the LORM-TL. LORM with Reduced Complexity (LORM-RC) To greatly reduce the computational complexity for LORM and LORM-TL, we proposed two methods based upon the use of graphs, as well as the transformation of convex optimization problems into graph optimization problems. Our obtained results have demonstrated the merit and power of this approach. More importantly, we believe that these results are very important and will make a lasting impact in the field. DISTRIBUTED LORM To address the lack of computational power that may exist in wireless networks (e.g., in distributed MIMO and cell-free massive MIMO), we proposed model-driven graph neural network (GNN) to deal with this issue. In the layers of the graph neural networks, each agent (device or base stations) aggregates information from neighbors, and proceed with local information processing, which coincidently matches a distributed process. To guarantee the performance, we borrowed the architectures in classic communication algorithms into GNNs. GENERAL FRAMEWORK FOR OPTIMIZING RESOURCE ALLOCATION IN WIRELESS COMMUNICATIONS We developed a unified framework for applying GNNs to wireless communications. Specifically, we designed a general framework for modeling typical problems of wireless communication as graph optimization problems. For illustrations, we applied the framework to power control in device-to-device (D2D) networks, resource allocation in cell-free networks, and hybrid-precoding for millimeter-wave (mmWave) networks. To bridge the learning-based algorithms and optimization-based algorithms in wireless networks, we were able to identify an important class of algorithms for solving graph optimization problems, namely, distributed message passing (DMP) algorithms. DMP algorithms unify many classic optimization-based algorithms (e.g., WMMSE, Riemannian gradient, and belief propagation), as well as GNN-based algorithms for problems in wireless networks. It was then proved that GNNs are the most powerful DMP algorithms, i.e., they can represent any DMP algorithm with a proper choice of learnable weights, which justifies the adoption of GNNs wireless networks from an algorithmic perspective. Finally and to theoretically verify the advantages of GNNs over MLPs in solving graph optimizations in wireless communications, we provided the first generalization analysis for these two neural architectures. Specifically, based on the PAC-learning framework, we demonstrated that the GNNs’ generalization error and required number of training samples are O(n) and O(n2) times lower than those of MLPs, where n is the number of nodes in the graph. In summary, and as stated earlier we are extremely pleased that we were able to achieve excellent results which are likely to be significant with lasting impact in the field. Further details about the results can be found in our published work as listed in the Research Output Section.

16210719.label: Major findings and research outcome
16210719.value: One of the key objectives of this project is to develop innovative ML-based methods for scalable resource allocation in wireless networks. Our major findings include the following: - Development of a computationally efficient machine learning-based framework for optimizing resource allocation in wireless networks, which we referred to as Learning to Optimize for Resource Allocation (LORM). LORM is a powerful method that learns the optimal policies in the branch-and-bound algorithm based upon imitation learning. - Expansion of the developed framework to improve scalability using innovative techniques such as transfer learning, as well as the use of an unsupervised LORM framework based on self-imitation. - Development of a unified and powerful framework for applying GNNs to wireless communications optimization, consisting of graph modeling, neural architecture design, and theoretical analysis. In contrast to existing learning-based methods, we focused on the theoretically principled approaches to meet the key performance requirements, including scalability, good generalization, and high computational efficiency. Moreover, we were able to provide the first quantitative result regarding the performance gain of GNNs over classic neural architectures in wireless communication systems, which casts light on the performance analysis and principled neural architecture design of deep learning-based approaches.

16210719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16210719.value: As for future directions, it will be interesting to apply our proposed framework to more design problems in wireless communication systems. It will also be interesting to combine GNNs with model-driven deep learning approaches and extend our theoretical results to this setting. The unified GNN framework that we have developed for wireless networks has also identified the connection between the GNN architectures and the decentralized proximal methods, which are very important. Our work and investigation may therefore trigger profound implications in both theoretical and practical aspects of decentralized optimization and learning and will be worthy of further research.

16210719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16210719.value: As the adoption of 5G networks continue to grow, we are witnessing exciting global research and development activities that are establishing 6G wireless networks. 6G will revolutionize the evolution of wireless from “connected things” to “connected intelligence,” enabling interconnections between humans, things, and intelligence within a deeply intertwined and hyper-connected cyber-physical world characterized by the integration of communications, sensing, control, and computing. However, the development of 6G is not trivial and multiple complex research challenges must be overcome in order meet the stringent requirements of 6G networks. In particular, the optimization of 6G networks is expected to be very complex and it will be difficult to employ traditional model-based approaches to do so. For that reason, there has been a surge in the application of ML in order to enable end-to-end system optimization. In this project, we developed an innovative computationally efficient machine learning framework for scalable resource allocation in wireless networks. The proposed approach is potentially groundbreaking and transformative as it can become the first-ever unified ML-based method for resource allocation in large-scale wireless networks that efficiently solves many important complex end-to-end system optimisation problems, which are not feasible with the existing traditional model-based approaches.

16211019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211019.value: This project will develop a cutting-edge multi-level probabilistic framework targeting different components of real-time monitoring, including sensor placement, parameter estimation, robust prediction, input force/excitation estimation, and damage identification. It aims to reliably and robustly assess uncertainties, enhance stability and convergence, and implement the sparsity of structural damage in a multi-level Bayesian modeling framework. Moreover, this project will resolve and address significant deficiencies and challenges encountered in joint parameter/state/input estimation problems by delivering a powerful methodology to reconstruct stress/strain histories using response-only measurements. The refined real-time methodology will be integrated with the state-of-the-art constitutive models to implement fatigue damage monitoring and remaining life prognosis. Another crucial element of this project will be the development of a novel probabilistic framework for uncertainty quantification in the experimental design and optimization of sensor networks used for structural monitoring. This framework will be hyper-robust to different sources of uncertainty, including modeling, parametric, input, and measurement uncertainties. This project will also apply the proposed methodologies to multi-disciplinary problems involving multi-scale and/or multi-physics models. This application necessitates the integration of computational modeling tools with test/monitoring data collected from subcomponent and component assemblages while maintaining a certain level of confidence. Central to this framework is the development of real-time Bayesian hierarchical modeling tools and optimal experimental design methods for validating models of subcomponents, components, and their interactions, as well as implementing tools for quantifying and propagating uncertainties throughout the whole assembly process. In addition, we will attempt to release the methodologies, formulations, and algorithms in a software package providing graphical user interfaces for non-expert individuals and practitioners. We believe that this project comprising five main tasks will provide unprecedented insight and original contributions to real-time uncertainty quantification and propagation methodologies. Combining the extensive expertise of the PI in probabilistic methods, structural dynamics, structural health monitoring techniques, and hierarchical Bayesian modeling with the Co-I’s experience in sensor network design and optimization, real-time Bayesian methods, and multi-scale/multi-physics modeling ensures successful achievement of the envisioned objectives. 摘要：项目旨在开发先进的结构实时监测多层次概率框架，用于传感器布设、参数识别、稳健预测、系统输入估计及其损伤识别。基于实时监测的多水平概率模型，可以增强不确定性量化的鲁棒性和可靠性，提高算法的稳定性和收敛性，并且充分利用稀疏性进行结构损伤识别。此外，项目还将针对参数、状态和输入同步估计时产生不合理误差的挑战性问题提出新的方法，并将其用于应变和应力时程的重构。精细化的实时分析方法还将与最新的材料本构模型结合进行结构疲劳损伤监测和剩余寿命的评估。项目的另外一个主要任务是提出新的概率理论框架进行健康监测传感器优化布设与实验设计的不确定性量化；这一框架对不同类型的不确定性比如建模不确定性、参数不确定性、输入和测试不确定性等皆有超强的鲁棒性。项目还将这一理论框架用于跨学科问题，包括多尺度或者多物理模型。这一理论框架的实施需要基于结构计算模型及其构件采集到的测试数据，并保证这些模型和数据的精度在一定的置信区间。这一框架的核心是开发实时的贝叶斯分层建模方法和最优实验设计方法，用于验证子构件和构件在整个拼装耦合作用下的不确定性量化和传播分析。此外，我们还会将该理论、算法及其实现手段嵌入软件包，开发人机交换界面供非专业人员方便使用。我们坚信，项目的五个主要研究内容将为实时不确定性量化与传播方法提供原创的贡献。项目负责人（PI）在概率方法、结构动力学、结构健康监测和分层贝叶斯建模等方面的研究经验，及其项目共同负责人（Co-PI）在传感器布设、实时贝叶斯分析方法、多尺度多物理建模等方面的研究积累，为确保项目正常有序的实施和达到预期的目标提供了坚实的基础。

16211019.label: Realisation of objectives
16211019.value: To address the first and second objectives, we have developed new methodologies for long-term structural health monitoring of large-scale structures. Several multi-level probabilistic methods have been developed for addressing modal identification, model inference, response predictions, and input estimation (Conference Papers 1,3, and 6; Journal Papers 1-5, 10, and 12-13). These methodologies can robustly quantify uncertainties due to modeling errors, ambient conditions, input characteristics, and environmental factors. In this framework, the variability of structural/dynamical parameters due to varying environmental and operational conditions is considered through the introduction of a hyper-probability distribution, whose parameters (referred to as hyper-parameters) are identified from the measured data. As the environmental and operational conditions are properly taken into account through such hyper-probability distributions, a significant improvement in terms of damage detection in structures is realized. Regarding the first and the second objectives, a Bayesian Expectation-Maximization (BEM) methodology is proposed for joint input-state-parameter estimation problems (Conference Papers 2 and 4; Journal Papers 7-9). This novel framework offers an efficient tool to update the measurement and process noise characteristics and activates the full potential of Bayesian filtering techniques to provide reasonable estimations along with reliable uncertainty bounds driven from the measured data without introducing user-sensitive bias in the choice of noise covariance matrices. This achievement is important as the BEM is the first method of its kind in the context of structural identification that offers efficient real-time uncertainty quantification and estimation tools without involving any sampling methods. Additionally, a novel framework is developed for the virtual sensing of the stress/strain history outputs from sparse response measurements. These estimations are next integrated with the multi-axial fatigue damage models to monitor fatigue in structural systems and their components (Conference Papers 3 and 5; Journal Papers 6 and 11). Regarding the third objective, the stationary solutions of the BEM methodology are driven theoretically, showing how the estimated covariance matrices stabilize and converge as time goes by (Journal Papers 7-8). As demonstrated in the previous works of the PI and the Co-I, such stationary solutions can easily be used in the context of utility-theoretic methods along with stochastic searching algorithms to identify optimal sensor configurations. Along the same line of research, new observability tools are developed based on Lie algebra, which allows exploring whether one particular sensor configuration can suffice for the joint identification of dynamical systems in the presence of unknown input and parameters. Through this approach, we have proven and demonstrated the observability of dynamical systems in a few practical applications, showing the absolute minimum number of sensors required from a theoretical viewpoint (Journal Papers 7-8). Various applications were employed to realize the fourth objective, including wind turbines, multi-story structures, and bridges. Notably, in Journal papers 3 and 14, it is demonstrated that the modal frequencies of bridges can be identified from a traversing vehicle, considering vehicle-bridge interaction. In Journal paper 6, a novel application to wind turbine monitoring is explored, and the contours of fatigue damage are presented as the results. Other applications sought include a three-story shear frame tested on a shaking table (Journal Papers 1-2), a pedestrian footbridge located at HKUST's campus (Journal Paper 5), the IASC-ASCE Structural Health Monitoring benchmark structure (Journal Paper 9), and FINO3 Offshore Platform located in the North Sea (Journal Paper 10). Through these validation efforts, extensive insights have been offered in terms of the applicability and reliability of the proposed Bayesian probabilistic methodologies.

16211019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211019.value: An important achievement of this project is the development of multi-level probabilistic techniques for structural identification and monitoring, as documented in Journal Papers 1-5. The proposed methodology offers an elegant formulation along with efficient Laplace-based computational algorithms, which produce reliable estimations and reasonable uncertainty bounds. This project has also successfully tackled significant challenges in joint parameter/state/input estimation problems. It has delivered a robust methodology (the BEM methodology) for reconstructing stress/strain histories using response-only measurements (Journal Papers 7-11). This refined real-time methodology has been integrated with state-of-the-art constitutive models to implement fatigue damage monitoring and predict remaining life. Numerous applications to real-life structures are demonstrated and the potentials of the BEM are demonstrated and documented in a few journal papers published in top scientific journals (Journal Papers 3, 5, 7-9). The dummy measurement strategies and the theoretical observability tools constitute another innovative aspect of the research outcome developed under this project (Journal Papers 7-10). The former strategies allows stabilizing the outcome of Bayesian filtering techniques in the absence of displacement/strain measurements, helping to remove low-frequency drifts from the state estimations. The latter class of tools offers the potential to ensure the observability of dynamical states, input forces, and structural parameters before attempting to instrument the structure of interest and optimize the sensor network in terms of the sensor type, location, and position in the most practical cases. Another novel aspect of the research output is the development of physics-based Machine Learning tools and their integration with hierarchical Bayesian modeling techniques, as realized in Journal Papers 9, and 12-13.

16211019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211019.value: The proposed multi-level techniques have great potential to be applied to other structural systems, including buildings, towers, bridges, railways, offshore wind turbines, and historical buildings. Furthermore, the probabilistic methods developed can also be applied to system identification problems encountered in other scientific disciplines as well, where it can offer the coupled estimation of state-input-parameter-noise in a real-time and efficient manner without having to employ any sampling techniques. These two directions represent potential future directions.

16211019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211019.value: Condition monitoring and inspection of large-scale structures have posed insurmountable challenges to the management in both public and private sectors. The emergence of novel sensing methodologies has made it possible to acquire data from structures and deploy mathematical tools to characterize the health state of the structure in real-time. However, due to the varying nature of the structural properties and dynamical loads applied to the structures over their lifespan, it is essential and inevitable to establish a real-time statistical modeling framework that can process data efficiently without encountering computational overloads. This project was devoted to this challenging subject, which has led to the development of multi-level Bayesian frameworks for structural health monitoring of civil structures. In this sense, these mathematical tools benefit the public by having sustainable, safe, and resilient structures.

16211619.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211619.value: We obtained a number of results beyond the midterm report that are summarized here in two parts. Part 1. Numerous studies indicate that choice abundance can make decision-making challenging for consumers. Rather than maximizing utility, many consumers employ a satisficing decision-making approach, whereby they search for products sequentially until they find a satisfactory one. Contrary to the common belief that satisficing is a bounded rational strategy, we demonstrate that it can be a rational choice within a game-theoretic framework between the seller and the consumers. Additionally, we introduce the concept of Y-regularity and show that a seller prefers satisficers over maximizers for choice models with this property, making satisficing a Pareto-dominant strategy. These findings lead to the less explored setting of assortment optimization, in which consumers follow a satisficing approach. We first demonstrate that this problem has a polynomial time solution where all products are listed in decreasing order of revenue. However, when the consumers are impatient and cardinality constraints apply, the problem becomes APX-hard. We then demonstrate that the greedy algorithm provides an optimal (1 − 1/e)-approximation within homogeneous consumers’ patient levels. Furthermore, we provide a 6 π2 (1 − 1/e)-approximation for the assortment optimization problem within heterogeneous consumers’ patient levels. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the assortment optimization problem is NP-hard for satisficers in the context of latent class MNL models. Nevertheless, we provide a fully polynomial-time approximation algorithm for homogeneous consumers as well as a quasi-polynomial-time approximation algorithm for heterogeneous consumers for this scenario. Part 2. We address the problem of assortments optimization subject to side constraints by developing bounds and heuristics for the traditional assortment optimization problem (TAOP) with totally unimodular (TUM) constraints. Our heuristics apply to a broad class of models, use minimal choice information, are fast, and in some cases have performance guarantees. To assess the benefits of personalized assortments we introduce a clairvoyant firm that sells to each consumer the most profitable product that she is willing to buy. For regular discrete-choice models we show that the clairvoyant firm can earn up to n times more than a non-clairvoyant firm, where n is the number of products. For discrete choice models with independent value gaps we show that the clairvoyant firm can make at most two times as much. We develop sufficient conditions to extend the prophet inequality for models with dependent value gaps and show that it holds for the α-shaken multinomial logit (MNL) model that includes the MNL and the generalized attraction model (GAM) as special cases. For the latent-class MNL, we show that the ratio is at most 1.5 when the coefficients of variation of the utilities go to infinity. A clairvoyant firm may improve consumer surplus when prices are fixed, but extracts all the surplus if it has pricing power. In this case the clairvoyant firm can make arbitrarily more than a non-clairvoyant firm. For the price-aware MN model, the clairvoyant firm can earn only up to exp(1) times more than a non-clairvoyant firm.

16211619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211619.value: Issues related to sequential assortments are important in e-commerce. For the midterm report we had found that sequential assortments are more profitable for firms when consumers experience search costs for most choice models except the MNL. In the two new papers added for the final report we find that consumers who buy the first product that they prefer to the no-purchase alternative, known as satisficers, also elicit sequential assortments that are more profitable to retailers. However, the consumers may be better off in some instances from acting as satisfiers rather than acting as maximizers. In the second paper we find that when consumers are patient, sequential assortments can result in profits for the firm that can be as high as those of a clairvoyant firm. Bounds are also found to look at the benefits of personalizing assortments for firms. We find that in many cases the benefits are limited and that personalized assortments can be beneficial for consumers.

16211919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16211919.value: 與Web瀏覽器不同，混合應用程序（app）是使用WebView（Android組件）提供Web瀏覽器功能的原生Android應用程序。它們具有訪問設備資源的優勢，例如加速計，攝像頭和聯繫信息。混合應用程序很普遍。在我們準備此提案時，Google Play商店（香港）上3,144個最受歡迎的應用中，有95％是使用WebView的混合應用。 WebView通過各種通信機制支持Android應用程序的本機端和Web端之間的雙向交互。雖然WebView使Android應用程序能夠訪問Web上的資源，但其雙向交互機制可能會引發新類型的錯誤，這些錯誤會調用WebView引發的錯誤。使用WebView的應用程序性能較差。然而，WebView引起的錯誤尚未得到系統研究。現有工作主要關注WebView引發的安全問題，但不能為開發人員提供全面的了解WebView引發的錯誤或測試它們的有效技術。要了解如何WebView可以引發Android應用程序中的錯誤，我們最近對124個真實的WebView引發的錯誤進行了初步研究，並觀察了它們的根本原因，後果和表現形式。這些觀察結果為檢測WebView誘發的錯誤提供了有用的見解。 在這個項目中，我們的目標是開發一個自動化測試框架，可以生成測試，以有效地揭示混合Android應用程序中WebView引起的錯誤。我們將提出新的測試覆蓋標準以生成測試。這些標準將用於衡量與WebView實例的各種特徵相關的測試覆蓋率，例如它們與本機代碼的交互，它們的配置以及加載的網頁內容的類型。由於只有少數WebView引起的錯誤導致軟件崩潰，因此將開發機制來推算導測試預言，以確定測試是否觸發WebView引發的錯誤。該項目開發的測試框架將實現混合Android應用程序的自動化測試，從而通過在早期識別WebView引發的錯誤來幫助提高混合應用程序的質量。我們將為建議的測試框架構建工具，並將其與我們的數據集一起發布給公眾。隨著在香港和中國越來越多地使用混合Android應用程序，我們提出的測試框架可以為應用程序開發人員帶來明顯的好處。正如微信（騰訊）測試工程總監所附的支持信中所示，該項目對業界非常感興趣。

16211919.label: Realisation of objectives
16211919.value: WebViews are user interface widgets of the Android framework to display web pages in Android apps. They are instances of the android.webkit.WebView class. WebViews not only help integrate web applications developed in HTML/JavaScript into Android apps but also provide mechanisms to support interactions between the web-end (JavaScript) and the native-end (Java) of an Android app. WebViews are widely used in real-world Android apps. These apps are known as hybrid Android apps. An earlier analysis of the apps collected from Google Play store shows that 85% of them contain a WebView component. We have fully achieved the four stated objectives by carrying out the following research activities. Activities related to objective 1: We have collected over 100 popular open-source apps that use WebViews. We studied the manifestation of bugs induced by WebView components. Our study observes that the faulty interactions induced by WebView components can be commonly characterized in three parts. The first part features the invocation of an Android WebView method at the native-end that triggers the Javascript at the web-end. The heavily fragmented Android ecosystem has induced various compatibility issues in Android apps. This part also involves the processing of data by the variables that lead to the arguments of the WebView method call. Some of these arguments can be a string dynamically constructed to hold the Javascript code executed by the Web-end. The second part is the execution of the receiver method at the Web-end. Received arguments, including the string arguments that hold Javascript code, will be executed accordingly. This part often ends up with passing the control to a callback method at the native-end. The third part is the execution of the callback method at the native-end according to the arguments received. Based on the characterization, we formulate test requirements based on the call sites of WebView methods and the variables participated in the processing of the method arguments. During our empirical study, we found that many open-source projects exhibit conflicts in their imported libraries. We developed solutions to detect such conflicts and provide solutions to resolve them. The results were disseminated at a reputed research conference [C1] and reported by a feature article at the Morning Paper (https://blog.acolyer.org/2020/09/21/watchman/), a technical blog reporting influential technological advancement. Activities related to objective 2: We formulated coverage criteria based on the test requirements identified. However, the Javascript code in WebView interactions can be dynamically constructed. The variables participating in WebView interactions cannot be identified statically. As such, we designed an algorithm to identify these variables incrementally at the time the target app is being executed. We designed a graph-based model to capture the control flow anomalies caused by WebView APIs on how the associated callback APIs are invoked in response to various events. We are extending our formulation to cover those hybrid Android apps with web browser capabilities. Since the generated tests can be flaky if they involve method calls dependent on environment, we investigated the mocking of such method calls in test generation. We developed a machine learning technique that can effectively identify the method calls that need to be mocked in a test. The results were disseminated at a reputed research conference [C2]. To identify criteria for Android tests, we performed an empirical study using 135 Stack Overflow posts that discuss Android app bugs and 199 issues in popular Android app projects on GitHub. We found that many issues arose from the mishandling of dangerous permissions and the interference of third-party libraries. A taxonomy of Android app issues is proposed to facilitate test generation. The results were disseminated at a reputed research conference [C3] and a reputed research journal [J1]. Activities related to objective 3: We are developing policies to guide the Markov chain Monte Carlo search for event sequences that maximize the coverage of the test requirements incrementally found during test generation. The tests generated by our tool have successfully detected 26 new bugs induced by WebView interactions. To better detect WebView-induced bugs, we proposed WebView-specific properties based on variables that pass values from the native-end to web-end. These properties characterize WebView behaviors, and devise a cross-language dynamic analysis method to identify these properties. An evaluation on 74 real-world open-/close-source Android apps shows that our technique can detect WebView-induced bugs effectively. It successfully detected 13 previously unknown bugs confirmed by developers. The result was disseminated at a top research venue [C5]. During our research, we found that many Android app bugs arose from mistakes in the apps’ XML configuration files. To detect such bugs, we studied 196 real-world issues in 43 popular apps arising from such mistakes. We extracted rules to generate tests detecting such issues. Our technique successfully detected 107 configuration mistakes. The result was disseminated at a reputed research conference [C4]. Activities related to objective 4: We are implementing a test support framework in Java. The framework supports automatic code instrumentation to capture the test requirements of WebView interactions. We have released our tools together with benchmark datasets at four open-source repositories. - https://richardhooooo.github.io/wTest/ - https://zenodo.org/records/5717473 - https://sites.google.com/view/confdroid - https://aper-project.github.io/

16211919.label: Major findings and research outcome
16211919.value: This project led to the training of 3 research students and publication of 6 top-tier research articles. - Hybrid Android app bugs are challenging to detect. Conventional test coverages such as line coverage and branch coverage are not effective in guiding test generation to reveal these bugs. - Hybrid Android bugs mostly arise from the incorrect interaction between the native-end and Web-end. - WebView is the key Android component that handles the interaction between the native-end and Web-end. - Effective WebView specific coverage criteria can be defined by considering the variables that pass values at WebView API calls. - WebView specific coverage can be used to guide test generation for WebView induced bugs.

16211919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16211919.value: Further development of the research: Expanding the study to a larger dataset would provide more comprehensive insights into the characteristics of WebView-induced bugs and the effectiveness of the proposed testing techniques. It is useful to evaluate the effectiveness of these techniques on a larger set of real-world Android apps to assess their generalizability and scalability. Once WebView-induced bugs are detected, it is important to develop techniques for automatically repairing them. This would significantly reduce the burden on developers and improve the security and reliability of Android apps. Proposed course of action for the testing of WebView-induced bugs: Research tools and datasets can be further publicized, allowing more developers to deploy automated testing techniques to improve the coverage and effectiveness of their tests. Static and dynamic analysis techniques can be used to identify WebView-specific properties that are essential for test generation. This will help to generate more targeted and effective test inputs. Researchers and developers can collaborate with WebView developers to improve the testability of WebView and to develop better tools and techniques for detecting and testing WebView-induced bugs. By following these recommendations, developers can improve the quality and security of their Android apps and reduce the risk of WebView-induced bugs.

16211919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16211919.value: WebView is a popular Android component that allows developers to integrate web content into their apps. However, WebView-induced bugs are common due to WebView's complex cross-language interaction mechanisms. To address this issue, we conducted an empirical study on 124 WebView-induced bugs collected from 51 popular open-source Android apps. We characterized the bugs from various perspectives, including their root causes, consequences, and manifestation. Based on our findings, we proposed an automated test generation technique, which effectively detects a substantial amount of previously-unknown WebView-induced bugs. To further improve test input generation, we proposed WebView-specific properties to formally characterize WebView behaviors and developed a fully-automated WebView-oriented test input generation technique. The technique combines static and dynamic analysis to identify WebView-specific properties and guide test input generation. It outperforms existing methods in terms of coverage of WebView-specific properties and detection of WebView-induced bugs. In summary, this project produced valuable insights into the characteristics of WebView-induced bugs and proposed effective techniques for detecting and testing these bugs in Android apps.

16212319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212319.value: 便攜式設備通常由鋰離子電池供電，輸出電壓範圍從全充時的4.2V到全耗時的2.7V。為了降低功耗，模擬電路的電源電壓只需要1V，而數字電路只需要0.5V。目前，高效率電壓轉換主要由開關式電感轉換器執行，但電感器的缺點是體積大及難以在芯片上集成製造。開關式電容轉換器（SCC）用的器件是電容器和開關。而低功率設備（例如少於200mW）用的電容器甚至小得可以在芯片上製造。 針對為便攜式設備供電，研究團隊將設計高性能而又體積小的開關式電容轉換器，而使用外置電容器或集成電容器的SCC均在研究之列。高性能的標準為：（1）高效率以降低充電頻率;（2）高功率密度以缩小體積;（3）在電源或負載變動下仍輸出穩定的電壓;（4）降低輸出電壓紋波，減低電源噪音以不影響負載。 研究方案如下：（1）系統地找出使用N個飛跳電容器的電壓轉換比（VCR）為m/n（m，n為整數）的SCC拓撲，包括所有升壓的和降壓的拓撲，相位則由最低的二相到最多的N+1相。（2）電源電壓在耗盡時會降低，必須調整VCR以穩定輸出電壓，而變換VCR時要變動最少數目的開關。（3）對於大功率如10W的設備，由於要用較大值的外置電容器，其數目必須減至最少。對於低功率如1W以下的設備，則可使用集成電容器，而總電容值必須減至最小。一個電容器可以分成p個小的電容器，並以p相交錯工作以降低輸出電壓紋波。 總結一下，此研究目標為設計VCR 為 m/n的開關式電容轉換器。而適合實際應用的設計，將會製成集成電路，並測試其功能。

16212419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212419.value: In this project, we plan to use real data to study the uncertain version of the task assignment problem. In particular, we plan to take the ride-vehicle assignment problem as an example and study how to assign "proper'' driver to each rider. We will address three core issues in this study. The first is to incorporate uncertainties into the problem. The uncertainties can arise from not only demand and supply, but also travel time. Capturing uncertainties properly while delivering robust decisions is a challenging but important question. The second core issue is describing objective functions that account for risks. The deterministic assignment problem maximizes the matching efficiency. However, for the stochastic version, even specifying the efficiency function is not an easy problem. For example, only considering the average efficiency over all possible realizations does not explain all risks involved. The third issue is tractability. Since the assignment problem is generally a large-scale optimization problem, we need to guarantee that the computational complexity should not increase significantly after accounting for uncertainty and risks. We will use a robust optimization approach and the concept of risk measures to solve these issues. Based on the real data, we will establish a distributional uncertainty set to describe the uncertainties. Then, we will test different risk measures to propose a performance measure that is consistent with people's behavior. Finally, we will formulate an optimization model that optimizes the worst-case performance over the distributional uncertainty set and develop efficient algorithms to derive solutions. We plan to start from the simplest case in the assignment problem, the static matching problem, in which one driver can pick up one rider. Then we extend to study the static planning problem, in which one driver can take multiple riders. If the algorithms work well, we can generalize to study the dynamic matching problem and dynamic planning problem. Assuming promising results, the model and algorithms developed will provide clear, practical guidelines for making assignment decisions when uncertainty is important. Our results will also enrich the current literature on the stochastic version of task assignment problems. 此項目中，我們計劃基於數據研究不確定性下的任務分配問題。我們以共享經濟裡的乘車分配問題為例，科學地研究派單問題。 我們會討論本研究中的三個核心問題。首先是不確定性。在此問題中，不僅需求和供給是不確定的，行程時間也是不確定的。因此如何在正確描述不確定性的前提下，提供可靠的決策是一個重要但又具有挑戰的問題。其次是如何通過目標函數描述風險。確定性問題裡會最大化匹配效率。但對於隨機版本而言，僅如何正確描述匹配效率都成為了研究問題，例如，只考慮平均效率並不能描述任何風險因素。最後一個核心問題是求解的複雜性。因為確定性的匹配問題自身就是一個大規模整數優化問題，我們需要在考慮不確定性的前提下盡可能不增加計算複雜性。 我們將使用魯棒優化方法和風險度量的概念來解決以上描述的問題。我們將建立一個分佈不確定性集合來描述不確定性。與此同時，我們將針對不同的風險度量進行分析，並提出與人們行為決策一致的新的目標函數。最後，我們將提出優化模型用來優化基於分佈不確定性集合下的最壞的目標函數，並開發有效的算法來提出決策意見。我們計劃從最簡單的情況開始研究，即靜態一對一的匹配問題。然後擴展到靜態一對多的匹配問題，最終希望能解決動態匹配問題。 如果結果較好，此項目所開發的模型和算法將為不確定性下的任務分配問題提供清晰的使用指南。研究結果也將豐富當前關於隨機任務分配問題的文獻。

16212419.label: Realisation of objectives
16212419.value: Realisation of the Objectives 1. Examine various distributional uncertainty set and investigate travelers' risk attitude and behavior about cancellation when facing uncertainties. The first objective is achieved. To study the problem with uncertainties, we have collected real data from the company to empirically study travelers’ waiting behavior in the ride-sourcing market by taking sunk waiting time into consideration. We integrate an accelerated failure model to characterize the passenger waiting behavior while accounting for sunk waiting time, heterogeneous trip distance, as well as the delay announcement provided by the platform. Our results show that passengers are loss-averse during the waiting process. Their behavior is significantly affected by trip distance, the interaction of two variables on delay announcement, and different times of the day. Besides, we observe that passengers are affected by the sunk waiting time, their tolerance for deteriorating delay updates will increase after a long waiting time. Furthermore, our analysis demonstrates that passengers exhibit different waiting behavior during different times of the day. 2. Investigate the concept of utilities and risk measures from economic literature and propose performance measures to account for risk. The second objective is achieved. Since uncertainties are ubiquitous, we have to propose suitable objectives to evaluate the uncertain outcomes. We have tried several performance measures to better characterize travelers’ behavior and also help us develop a tractable model. We combine the concept of certainty equivalent in economics and propose new performance measure inspired by the Constant Absolute Risk Aversion (CARA) utility to evaluate the risk. We also explore the possibility of using the robust satisficing framework, which prioritizes solutions that would achieve an acceptable target based on a risk-averse objective function, even when the actual probability distribution differs from the empirical one. 3. Formulate the uncertain task assignment models in the static case. Develop efficient algorithms to solve these problems. The third objective is achieved. We first conduct literature review and connect the assignment problem with the dial-a-ride problem in the literature. We treat the vehicles and orders as the supply and demand in inventory control problem. We divide the whole area into a few zones, and find a proper policy based on the historical observation of demand and travel time to make assignments over periods and different zones. We start from a general stochastic model which captures the characteristics of ridesharing problems with uncertain demand and travel time. Then, we find proper models to represent the uncertain demand and convert the above stochastic problem to a robust one. 4. Generalize the static version to the dynamic version when supply and demand are uncertain. The fourth objective is achieved. We further extend the static model to the dynamic problem while accounting for both uncertain demand and travel time. At each time period, we seek the optimal assignment quantity among different areas to balance between the risk and cost. We further conduct numerical studies with real data collected from Didi GAIA open dataset to evaluate the performance.

16212419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212419.value: This project use real data to study the uncertain version of the task assignment problem. In particular, we take the ride-vehicle assignment problem as an example and study how to assign ``proper'' driver to each rider. Our major research findings and outcomes are listed as follows. 1. We first examine riders’ waiting behavior with real data. a. We integrate an accelerated failure model to characterize the riders’ waiting behavior while accounting for sunk waiting time, heterogeneous trip distance, as well as the delay announcement provided by the platform. The delay announcement is represented by two variables: the initial announcement and the announcement deviance. The proposed model is calibrated and examined using massive ride-sourcing order data from four metropolitan areas in China. b. Our results show that riders are loss-averse during the waiting process. Their behavior is significantly affected by trip distance, the interaction of two variables on delay announcement, and different times of the day. Besides, we observe that passengers are affected by the sunk waiting time, their tolerance for deteriorating delay updates will increase after a long waiting time. Furthermore, our analysis demonstrates that passengers exhibit different waiting behavior during different times of the day. This underscores the need for ride-sourcing service managers to consider time-of-day effects when managing their services. Output: We have finished one paper (Research Output No. 2). The paper has been submitted to two top journals in the Operations Management area (Management Science, and Manufacturing and Service Operations Management). We have collected valuable feedback and comments. Now, we are still revising the paper. 2. We build a robust optimization model to study the assignment problem. To our best knowledge, this is the first one to study the assignment problem from a robust optimization perspective. a. We start from the assignment problem with only uncertain demand, which could be formulated as a stochastic optimization model. After introducing factor-based demand model, we then apply static and linear assignment policy to reformulate the original problem to a tractable one. b. In a more general model, which considers both uncertain demand and travel time, we conduct a simple analysis where travel time varies in two possible values. We also build an optimization model under the dynamic programming framework. c. In the computational study, we use real data from DiDi GAIA Open Dataset to evaluate the performance of our model. Furthermore, the results show that our model could achieve or exceed the performance of some heuristics derived from dynamic programming. Output: This work is conducted with my Mphil student Lingyi PAN. However, due to the long review time from the top journals in the Operations Management area, we are still revising the paper (Research Output No. 1). 3. Inspired by this assignment problem, we further explore several variants about this problem. In this assignment problem, these riders are also competing for the limited resources. Essentially, it relates to the substitutability in economics, and has theoretical structure with the supermodularity problem. Hence, we also conduct our theoretical studies to investigate the relationship between distributionally robust optimization and supermodularity property. Output: Please check our Research Output No. 3, 4. 4. Furthermore, the assignment problem is closely related to the resource allocation, resource pooling with uncertain demand. My Post-doc Zheng CUI and collaborator (also research visitor) Prof. Lianmin ZHANG also acknowledge this grant with their studies. Output: Please check Research Output 5, 6.

16212419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212419.value: The problem of task assignment under demand and travel time uncertainty is a challenging issue that plays a crucial role in the ride-sharing market. Our empirical analysis on riders’ behavior, as well as our formulation and algorithm, offer a fresh perspective on this problem. However, there are still many potential avenues for future research. In particular, we believe the following two directions are the most important. 1. Extend the model to real-time decision making process. Currently, the task assignment problem under demand and travel time uncertainty is only considered in a static or aggregated version. One promising direction for future research is to develop online algorithms to solve this assignment problem. The online algorithms have been studied in the context of resource allocation problems when there is no information on the future demand. Since we have access to real demand data, we can use this information to develop innovative online algorithms that can partially anticipate future demand patterns. 2. Another potential direction for future research is to incorporate travel time as an additional dimension in the task assignment problem. Given that the ride-sharing market is closely tied to the transportation network and that tasks and demands arrive randomly, it is important to consider the time dimension in the problem formulation. This approach has been successfully applied to various classical transportation problems, such as the continuous-time service network design problem. By expanding the network to include the time dimension, we can better capture the dynamic nature of the ride-sharing market and develop more realistic and effective strategies for task assignment.

16212419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212419.value: In this project, we look at how ride-sharing companies decide which driver should pick up which passenger. We use real data to study this problem and investigate how uncertain things like how many people need rides and how long it will take to get to their destination can affect this decision-making process. We first study how riders behave when they have to wait for a ride, and identify that the trip distance, the time they have already waited, and the delay announcement provided by the platform will all affect their waiting behavior. Further, their tolerance for waiting will also be different at different times of the day. Hence, the ride-sharing companies need to take all these factors into account when managing their assignment tasks. Then we build an optimization model to help ride-sharing companies to make this assignment decision. Since riders and drivers arrive randomly and the travel time is also uncertain, we have to make our decisions immune against these uncertainties. Further, we aim to balance the service level requirement such that riders may not need to wait for a long time and also the revenue from the company’s perspective. We started with a simple version of the problem where we only had to worry about uncertain demand, and then we made it more complicated by also considering travel time. We tested our program using real data and found that it works well.

16212819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212819.value: Public transport (PT) is instrumental in addressing the transportation needs of many metropolitan areas. PT is also playing an increasingly important role in mitigating the problems associated with the current energy crises and environmental concerns. Traditionally, PT services have operated on fixed routes with fixed schedules (FRFS) regardless of the realized demand. Demand responsive services, such as taxis, have generally been regarded as too costly to serve as a substantive mode of PT. However, the rise of real-time communication and service platforms such as Uber and Didi has opened the possibility for ride-sharing (RS) services that are lower in cost and much more flexible than FRFS services. The key to the success of these platforms is to strike the narrow balance between supply and demand. To properly address this problem, it is crucial to recognize that the volume, service request location (i.e., origin and destination), and service request time properties of RS demand are intrinsically stochastic. In the proposed project, we will develop a modeling framework to incorporate these stochastic properties based on a stochastic programming approach. We will divide the service area into zones, group the stochastic service requests into zones, and then design zonal-based flexible RS services via a two-stage stochastic program. The objective will be to minimize the expected costs, including both passenger and operational costs, as the RS demand varies stochastically. The project will consist of three phases. In Phase I, we will use a simplified frequency-based approach to develop the planning of the flexible zonal-based RS services. In Phase II, we will use the time-space network approach to capture the temporal and spatial demand variations, and model the detailed operations. In Phase III, we will investigate how the zoning can be designed to optimize the service performance. Overall, the three phases will form a coherent framework for investigating the proposed research problem, from initial planning to operation, using the past demand records from a service platform as input to guide the problem formulation and development. A key element of the proposed project will be to obtain actual demand data from a service platform. Our research team established the HKUST-Didi Joint Research Lab with Didi Chuxing. We will use their data to complete the research and validate the results. Overall, this project will provide theoretically interesting and practically important results that will advance the development of RS services under the realistic assumption of demand stochasticity. 公共交通能有效地應付全球各大城市的出行需求。而隨著能源危機和環境污染問題越來越嚴重，公共交通作為舒緩以上問題的出行模式，將變得更重要。傳統公交有固定路綫和班次，不能回應當下實際的出行需求。另一方面，出租車等能直接回應出行需求的服務，價錢一般都過高，不能成為公共交通服務的主流。近年來，即時通訊的普及和優步、滴滴出行等服務平臺使既便宜又有彈性的拼車服務成為可能。而一個成功的拼車服務關鍵在於要在供給與需求中取得平衡。 事實上，出行訂單數目、他們的起點、終點和出發時間都必然有不確定性，研究拼車服務必須處理不確定性帶來的變化。在本研究中，我們將會基於隨機規劃的理論建立一個考慮上述不確定性的模型。拼車服務覆蓋的地區將會被分成子區域，需求會按照這些子區域進行分類，並以兩階段優化的方法規劃車隊的子區域路綫，以最小化預期成本，其中包括乘客的成本及運營成本。在兩階段優化中，出行需求的不確定性將會被考慮。 本研究項目分為三部分。第一部分，我們將會基於頻率的簡化方法去規劃彈性拼車服務；第二部分，我們將會以時空網絡方法去考慮出行需求的時空不確定性，而對服務作出較詳細的規劃；第三部分，我們將會研究分割子區域的方法對服務的影響，並優化子區域劃分以提供更好的服務。總的來說，這三部分形成了一個連貫的研究框架：根據服務平臺提供過往的出行記錄來建立彈性拼車服務模型，以規劃路線，並優化實際的運行。 本研究項目成功的其中一個關鍵在於要有真實的需求數據。我們研究團隊與滴滴出行成立了香港科大 - 滴滴出行聯合實驗室，將會用滴滴出行提供的數據完成我們的研究並作出驗證。總括而言，本研究項目將會提供理論上有趣及實踐中重要的結果，考慮實際需求的不確定性，使拼車服務變得更好。

16212819.label: Realisation of objectives
16212819.value: 1. We have developed a model for flexible zonal-based ride-sharing service under stochastic demand. The model minimizes the cost of flexible bus services by planning the frequency based zonal routes under stochastic demand. The flexible bus is required to detour to pick up or drop off passengers, and if any passengers cannot be picked up due to vehicle capacity or detour time constraints, taxi-like ad hoc service, which incurs extra costs, is provided to them. A two-stage reliability-based gradient solution method has been developed to minimize the total system operation cost. Numerical studies, including sensitivity analyses on vehicle capacity, detour time limit, and demand volume, demonstrated the potential of the zonal-based ride-sharing service. Finally, a scenario based on real ride-sharing data in Chengdu demonstrated the applicability of the model. 2. Based on the frequency-based model developed in 1., we have extended the model to the time-based approach by explicitly capturing the time dimension within the formulation. As the formulation becomes much more complicated, we have developed relaxations and greedy search solution algorithms to speed up the solution process, and simplified search procedures to design the service pickup sequences. The time-space model developed performs better than the frequency-based approach, as expected, at the expense of computational effort. 3. We have formulated the problem of zone shape and size optimization, which is bi-level in nature and a challenging problem, to improve the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of zone-based flexible transit under stochastic demand, developed an algorithm to solve, and illustrated its application to the case of Chengdu.

16212819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212819.value: Public transport (PT) plays an increasingly important role in mitigating the problems associated with the current energy crises and environmental concerns. Traditionally, PT services have operated on fixed routes with fixed schedules (FRFS) regardless of the realized demand. Demand responsive services, such as taxis, have generally been regarded as too costly to serve as a substantive mode of PT. However, the rise of real-time communication and service platforms such as Uber and Didi has opened the possibility for ride-sharing (RS) services that are lower in cost and much more flexible than FRFS services. The key to the success of these platforms is to strike the narrow balance between supply and demand. In this project, we developed a framework to design flexible bus services that run on regular zonal routes while at the same offer demand-responsive door-to-door services. The objective was to minimize the expected costs, including both passenger and operational costs, as the RS demand varies stochastically. The results showed that this type of new PT services can be financially viability and cost-effective.

16212919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16212919.value: 在外部機械載荷的持續作用下，高分子材料要經歷兩個主要的破壞性事件：由於分子鏈滑移導致的屈服和由於共價鍵斷開導致的破裂。檢測和修復這些材料内部演化的損傷是學術界面臨的一個巨大挑戰。而且高分子結構中局部機械態的分佈和演變過程過於複雜。在過去十年中，自主/自響應材料已經成為一個新興和快速發展的領域，途徑之一是通過設計新的力-化學單元，以了解受機械力作用的分子共價鍵之間的反應。因此，高分子材料中上述兩個主要損傷事件的原位檢測和可視化已成為自主材料領域中具有挑戰性和應用前景的課題。該項目的主要目標是設計一種新型的雙力致色變單元，通過不同的顏色變化生動地“看”到與高分子材料中屈服和斷裂事件相關的層級應力狀態。最終目標是提供一套實用的解決方案，開發具有可見應力傳感單元的自主高分子材料，可在智能紡織品，自主塗層，柔性電子設備和響應性人造皮膚發揮應用。

16212919.label: Realisation of objectives
16212919.value: [Note: For more details, please refer to the Final Report attached behind.] Advancements in mechanochromic fluorescent polymer systems, enhanced by the aggregation-induced emission (AIE) process, have been summarized to meet Objective 1. These polymers exhibit adaptability in fluorescence upon exposure to mechanical forces. The integration of AIE-generating molecules (AIEgens) into polymer matrices or their chemical bonding to polymer backbones is the typical fabrication method. However, understanding the complex molecular interactions and polymer structures for designing and modulating these polymers remains a challenge. Establishing a quantitative relationship between fluorescence modifications and local force conditions/microstructural changes is crucial and requires systematic investigations through theoretical simulations and empirical evidence. To address these challenges, computational calculations were employed to preselect suitable mechanochromophore candidates before synthesizing responsive smart polymeric materials. Cyclobutane frameworks, known for their significant ring strain and rapid response to stimuli, were explored as mechanophore linkers. Computational analysis provided insights into molecular design, utilizing potential cleavage energy barriers to estimate bond strength and predict cyclobutane ring cleavage trends. The mechanochromophore syn-hh-DPCB showed the lowest cleavage energy barriers, indicating a higher likelihood of undergoing a mechanically induced retro-cycloaddition reaction. UV-Vis spectrum analysis revealed a maximum absorbance shift upon ring opening, highlighting syn-hh-DPCB as a more effective mechanochromophore candidate than syn-ht-DPCB. For Objective 2, syn-hh-DPCB was selected as the optimal mechanochromophore motif based on simulation results. A series of syn-hh-DPCB-linked PMAs with different molecular weights were prepared using an α-bromoester bifunctionalized initiator for polymerizing methyl acrylate. Additionally, control samples were synthesized following a similar strategy. Furthermore, spiropyran (SP) was explored as another molecular mechanochromophore to probe local stresses within heterogeneous systems. SP-linked PMMA microbeads and segmented thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) with varying soft to hard segment ratios were synthesized as model systems. Despite the incompatibility between the soft and hard segments, their covalent linkage led to micro-phase separation, endowing the TPU with high strength and good elasticity. Comparative analysis of stress-strain curves revealed that the low concentration of SP negligibly affects the tensile properties of the polymer. To achieve Objective 3, significant progress was made. Following the synthesis of a series of linear hh-syn-DPCB-linked PMAs, the impact of external forces on the mechanochromophore was explored. Mechanical force-induced elongation flow was employed to stretch pendant chains and induce a retro-[2+2] cycloaddition reaction in the polymers under sonication. After 3 hours of sonication, a mechanically triggered ring-opening reaction was anticipated, leading to the formation of a 2'-azachalcone fragment-containing polymer. The hh-syn-DPCB mechanochromophore, embodying responsive and self-sensing functions, was integrated at the PMA polymer chain's center, bearing maximum stress under elongation flow. The detection mechanism was anticipated through the functional group transformation from cyclobutane ring to 2'-azachalcone under ultrasonic elongation flow, with color variation observed in both solution and solid state pre- and post-sonication. For the sensing performance of SP-linked PMMA beads, compression tests across various loading speeds and temperatures revealed PMMA beads transitioning from spherical to pancake shapes, with a visible blue color emerging post-yield at the bead's center under all conditions. The mechanochemical reaction in SP-linked PMMA beads was further analyzed semi-quantitatively, identifying three distinct regions. Mechanical behaviors of PMMA were markedly influenced by strain rate and temperature, with increased stiffness at higher strain rates and decreased stiffness at higher temperatures. A comprehensive stress analysis was conducted to link the activation process, using Eyring theory and a phenomenological model to elucidate the damage sensing mechanisms. For the SP linked TPU, the color contrast and absorption spectrum changes in the TPU samples linked with 0.03 wt% SP before and after stretching were explored. The emergence of a bright purple color upon stretching indicated a stress-induced transition from SP to merocyanine (MC). The reversibility of the SP to MC transition, alongside its ability to undergo multiple cycles of activation and recovery, is significant for reusable stress-sensing applications. The tunability of the activation threshold through molecular modifications and environmental changes offers versatility for various applications. This study also highlights the potential for selectively incorporating different sensor molecules into specific microdomains of heterogeneous materials, enhancing the material's ability to probe local stresses accurately.
