16212919.label: Major findings and research outcome
16212919.value: [Note: For more details, please refer to the Final Report attached behind.] This research presents significant advancements in the development and application of reversible dual-mechanochromophore systems for detecting stress levels in polymers through specific color changes. The study summarizes the integration of aggregation-induced emission (AIE) processes and mechanochromic fluorescent polymer systems, which adapt their fluorescence in response to mechanical forces (No.1 in Part C). By embedding AIE-generating molecules (AIEgens) or chemically bonding them to polymer backbones, these systems demonstrate enhanced diversity and performance in stress detection. Objective 1 focuses on the development of a numerical method to design the systems, emphasizing the challenge of understanding complex molecular interactions and the need for a quantitative relationship between polymer fluorescence, local force conditions, and microstructural changes. Computational analyses were employed to select appropriate mechanochromophore candidates, notably cyclobutane frameworks, for their rapid response to stimuli. The analysis predicted the mechanochromophore syn-hh-DPCB as an effective candidate due to its low cleavage energy barriers, facilitating a stress-induced retro-cycloaddition reaction. Objective 2 advances the synthesis of designed chemical architectures into polymers of varying molecular weights, using syn-hh-DPCB as the chosen motif. This objective also explores spiropyran (SP) as a molecular force sensor within multi-component systems like poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) microbeads and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), demonstrating that SP activation is sensitive to local stresses without significantly affecting the tensile properties of the polymer. Objective 3 verifies the sensing performance of these systems under mechanical stress, such as ultrasonic stretching, showing that the mechanochromophores can indicate stress failure through visible color changes. For SP-linked PMMA beads, compression tests identified three distinct regions of color change correlating with tensile stresses, while for SP-linked TPU, stretching induced a color transition from SP to merocyanine (MC), confirmed by absorption spectrum changes. The research also underscores the reversibility and tunability of these mechanochromic systems, making them promising candidates for reusable stress-sensing applications. The findings also highlight the importance of minimizing mechanophore perturbation within material structures and the potential for selectively incorporating different sensor molecules into heterogeneous materials. This work lays a foundational understanding for designing smart materials capable of detecting and responding to mechanical stress at the molecular level, offering broad implications for material science and engineering applications. During the project period, two PhD students and two Postdoc Fellows have been trained. More research outputs will be published soon.

16212919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16212919.value: The PI and Co-PI will continue to work on the related topic to further understand the mechanisms and extend the potential applications. These include but not limited to: 1. By adjusting the ratio of force-responsive groups and AIE molecules, we could regulate the material's force response threshold, find the structure-activity relationship, and obtain the proportion of groups responding linearly under high, medium, and low strains. This may prepare new materials with a linear response in the full tensile range. 2. Try to extend this kind of mechano-responsive material to industrial products and use the easy-spreading characteristics of polyurethane to apply the material to the stress display of structural parts to create a new strain gauge substitute for real-time stress distribution visualization. This technique can be applied to artificial skin.

16212919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16212919.value: This research successfully developed innovative materials capable of changing color in response to mechanical stress, offering a novel approach to monitor and detect stress in polymers. Computational modeling played a crucial role in selecting cyclobutane as an effective mechanophore due to its quick stress response, leading to the creation of polymers that visibly change color under stress. Significant advancements were made in synthesizing polymers with varying molecular weights, incorporating the selected mechanophore, syn-hh-DPCB, which demonstrated a promising ability to indicate stress through color change. Additionally, we explored spiropyran (SP) as a molecular sensor within different systems, such as poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) and thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU), to detect stress without compromising material integrity. Our findings include the successful demonstration of stress detection in polymers through color change, offering a potential for early warning systems in various applications from aerospace to medical devices. The research highlights the importance of molecular design in creating responsive materials and opens avenues for developing reusable, stress-sensing smart materials.

16213019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213019.value: An Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) consists at least one tri-axis accelerometer and one tri-axis gyroscope, providing measurement of 6-degree-of-freedom movement. Integrated with other sensors, such as magnetic compasses and barometers, IMU can create an intelligent sensing interface for people to interact with electronic devices and, furthermore, with external environments. Traditionally, Ring Laser Gyroscopes (RLG) and Fibre Optic Gyroscopes (FOG) are the most common gyroscopes for IMUs for both civilian and military applications. However, over the past decades, microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) have achieved significant success in the sensor market because of the high performance and low cost of miniaturized mechanical devices, which demonstrated tremendous impact on our everyday life and the economy of our society. MEMS motion sensors (e.g. accelerometers and gyroscopes) in consumer electronic devices such as smart phones, gaming stations and wearable electronics are few of the most famous examples. As one of the key components of IMU, MEMS vibratory rotation rate gyroscopes in consumer electronics have reasonable performance, manufactured with CMOS-compatible silicon microfabrication technology with extremely low cost. Despite of the success, MEMS gyroscopes still face the challenges in replacing RLGs and FOGs in high-end market with higher performance requirements, which mainly cover high precision inertial navigation, such as for industrial unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV’s), and for indoor pedestrians. The key requirements for these high-performance applications include: low noise and drift, high sensitivity, low cross-talk, and high resolution. Along the direction, there have been also much work done in the MEMS area, such as hemispherical resonator gyroscopes. However, many factors such as the manufacturability, robustness and repeatability, are still not satisfied for these specific applications. In comparison with traditional solid mass-spring system-based motion sensors, Molecular Electronic Transducers (MET) technology, based on sensing inertial movement of a liquid electrolyte between electrodes, has been used for high performance linear and angular accelerometers. The uniqueness of MET provides distinguished advantages, including high robustness, extremely low noise, small size and low power consumption. Therefore, we propose using similar mechanism with a structure of paired vibratory MET cells to measure the rotation rate based on the Coriolis Effect. 标准的惯性测量单元至少有一个三轴加速度计和一个三轴陀螺仪以完成运动的六个自由度的测量。在集成了包括磁场和压力传感的其它功能之后，惯性单元可以为用户提供一个与外界环境交互的智能界面，是当今物联网平台不可或缺的一个部分。传统上，光学陀螺仪用于为高端民用和军用服务提供精确的信息。而近年来基于硅工艺的微机电系统震动式陀螺仪借助其合适的性能，低成本而获得民用上的很大成功，推动了当代消费电子（如手机）的急速扩张。但是在工业应用或高精度民用领域，比如在工业无人机和室内高精度导航应用之中，此类陀螺仪却由于器件性能的不足而受到限制。虽然各种其它不同类型的陀螺仪（如半球谐振器陀螺仪）也在开发中，但大规模加工性，稳定性和重复性目前都未达到要求。因此，此项目将开发一款使用分子电学换能器原理并应用电解质液体作为惯性传感介质的陀螺仪以应对上述的问题和挑战。新开发的陀螺仪工作原理如下：在外界转动的情况下，器件内部的液体电解质会产生惯性运动。在一定的偏压下，流经浸润在电解质中的电极上的电流将随电解质的运动而变化。根据科里奥利效应，通过电流的变化读出，我们可以推导出外界的转动运动和角度，从而达到传感功能。这种依靠电解液电化学机理的传感为器件提供了独特的优点，包括高稳定性，抗冲击，低噪音，小尺寸和低能量损耗等。有望成为高精度陀螺仪在工业应用的有效解决方案。

16213019.label: Realisation of objectives
16213019.value: Task 1 Theoretical Analysis and Design of MET Gyroscopes The MET gyroscope is based on the Coriolis force. From the equation of motion in a rotating frame, the centripetal and Euler acceleration are position dependent while Coriolis is not so it is commonly used in angular velocity measurements. However, a known velocity is required to calculate the angular velocity using the Coriolis effect, which indicates the necessity of active driving. For solid-state gyroscopes, the excitation is vibratory while gyroscopes with liquid inertial mass could have a DC excitation with continuous circulation flow. Operation Mechanism The proposed gyroscope would have a cavity filled with liquid electrolytes and internal walls to separate pump and detection channels. Then, the integrated pump drives convection to sustain a circulating flow inside the cavity to provide the velocity required for Coriolis acceleration. Here, the pump used is the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) drive and the flow rate is measured based on the MET mechanism. Magnetohydrodynamic Drive Design The electrochemical Coriolis gyroscope has a liquid electrolyte mass so a liquid pump is required. However, a conventional liquid pump is large so an integrated pump mechanism is required. Here, we use the magnetohydrodynamic pump due to its simplicity which only requires a magnetic field and current to operate. MHD drive is based on Lorentz force acting on the moving charges under a magnetic field which will accelerate the charges together with the liquid molecules. The structure of the MHD pump has two platinum electrodes which are in the same plane positioned at the bottom of the cavity with one anode and one cathode respectively. A constant current is flowing between the anode and the cathode which establishes a steady current distribution. Then, a permanent magnet is placed underneath with the North Pole and magnetic field pointing up. Referring to the equation, the resulting force and flow velocity point inwards. Coriolis Measurement Mechanism Viewing from the top of the channel structure inside the gyroscope cavity filled with the electrolyte. It features a central pump channel and two detection channels, channel 1 and channel 2, containing platinum electrodes for flow rate sensing. The pumping channel employs an MHD drive that propels liquid via the Lorentz force, generated by the electrochemical reaction Faradaic current and the magnetic field of a permanent magnet as mentioned in the previous section. In this example, the current flow from the bottom anode to the top cathode, and the magnetic field is pointing outward resulting in a flow driven to the right at the pump channel. When steady, the driven flow circulates inside and equally separates toward channel 1 and channel 2 before recombining at the pump segment inlet. The circulation in channel 1 is in the clockwise direction but opposite in channel 2 (counterclockwise). Coriolis force induced by rotation thus acts oppositely in the two detection channels which will increase the flow rate in one channel but decrease in another one. Therefore, angular velocity can be measured by measuring the differential flow rate in channel 1 and channel 2 based on the MET mechanism. Simulation Before performing experiments, we use the commercial software COMOL Multiphysics to conduct a simulation to understand the gyroscope’s behavior. First, to obtain the pumping force of the MHD drive, we use the electrochemistry module to obtain a steady state current distribution between the anode and the cathode at the bottom of the middle pumping channel by applying a potential boundary condition of 0.5V. Then the resulting current distribution is input to the fluid mechanic module to generate a volume force under a constant magnetic field of 0.3T pointing in the positive z direction. Finally, a fluid mechanics study is performed by further including the Coriolis force and Euler force to examine the effect of both forces on the flow rate in the two detection channels. Electrochemistry Model To obtain the steady state current distribution in the pump channel, the Tertiary Current Distribution, Nernst-Planck, Electroneutrality interface is used. At the anode and cathode, the Bulter-Vomer model is used to describe the voltage-current relationship with their exchange current density. Task 2 Device fabrication The gyroscope assembly contains a 3D-printed housing, a silicone gasket, an electrode die, a magnet, and an acrylic plate. The housing containing the channel is 3D printed by a Stereolithography (SLA) 3D printer (Formlab Form 3) with Clear V4 resin. The 8mm high inner cavity contains one pumping channel and two shunt channels separated by two 1mm wide, 9mm long walls. The pumping channel is 3mm wide and 12mm long with two 0.3mm wide and 3mm long slits at two ends to direct the flow. The two shunt channels are 1.5mm wide and 12mm long. For the electrode die fabrication process flow, first, spin coat and pattern ~3μm thick photoresist on a 1μm silicon dioxide (SiO2) coated silicon wafer as a sacrificial layer. Sputter 50nm titanium tungsten and 200nm platinum on top. Next, immerse in acetone overnight and then ultrasonic for 30 minutes to lift off and pattern the metals. Deposit another layer of 220nm SiO2 by the plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition process as insulation. Spin coat and pattern the PR again as an etching mask. Finally, etch SiO2 with buffered oxide etchant solution to expose pads and electrodes. The 1 mm thick silicone gasket is prepared by pouring Ecoflex 00-30 elastomer (Smooth-On, Inc.) mixture into an acrylic mold and curing at room temperature for four hours. The magnet has a dimension of 12mm*3mm*4mm bonded by instant glue with the North pole pointing towards the die. Finally, fill the housing with 4M KI + 50mM I2 electrolyte by vacuum filling. Task 3 Device Testing and Optimization The angular velocity measuring device consists of two assembled MET gyroscopes placed vertically along the turntable rotating axis. The two gyroscopes have opposite excitation to cancel effects apart from the Coriolis force. The nearby readout and excitation circuits have electrical connections to external data acquisition and power supply via a shielded slip ring. For the readout circuit and electrical connection of electrodes on one side. Each detection channel has three electrodes arranged in an anode-cathode-anode (ACA) configuration to detect the flow velocity magnitude. Anodes have a constant voltage of 0.5 V with respect to the cathodes by a digital-analog converter and a voltage follower. Cathodes are connected to a virtual ground of the transimpedance amplifier (TIA) and convert the current signal into a voltage signal. Finally, the outputs from two TIAs are differentially amplified by an instrumentation amplifier with a gain of 10. To perform cancellation, two assembled gyroscopes, denoted gyro 1 and gyro 2 are stacked vertically along the rotation axis. They are driven oppositely by reversing the current direction of the MHD pump while the magnetic field remains the same. For example, top channel from gyro 1 has a clockwise flow while top channel from gyro 2 has an anti-clockwise flow. For each detection channel, only three electrodes are used and arranged in ACA configuration for only measuring the magnitude of flow rate in each channel. The electrodes from the two top channels are connected to the same circuit to obtain their differential signal after cancelling the effect from Euler force, similarly for bottom channels. Finally, the scale factor of the gyroscope is tested between 0-300o/s and the noise floor is tested with and without MHD driving.

16213019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213019.value: Findings from the numerical studies. The individual flow rates in top and bottom detection channels exhibit non-linearity and non-monotonic behaviour due to the non-uniform pumping force from the co-planar electrodes. However, their differential flow rate demonstrates monotonicity and improved linearity. For the resulting flow field in the gyroscope during rotation, due to non-uniform current density and pumping force, there is unwanted circulation from the MHD electrodes toward the top of the cavity which wasted the pumping energy. The flow field is deflected under rotation due to the Coriolis force. Then we compared the differential flow rate from centripetal at -60 rpm to 60 rpm and Euler forces at ±3o/s2 to the previous result. It shows that even the rotational speed fluctuates with ±0.5 rpm/s (3o/s2) generates cross-talk much higher than the gyroscopic signal, 0.53 ul/s against 0.016 ul/s at 60 pm by the Coriolis force. On the other hand, the centripetal force generates a negligible differential flow rate and is less than 1% of the Coriolis force. The results from the testing. From the differential voltage from the two readout circuits against angular velocity. The response at 300 o/s deviates significantly from the trend and may be considered saturated. The fitted line for data within 0-240 o/s has a slope of 0.02091 V/(o/s) and a y-intercept of -9.353 V. The large offset is due to the interaction between the MHD electrodes to the MET electrodes. The electrochemical reaction at the MHD electrodes alters the ion distribution in the background electrolyte. For example, in gyroscope 2 with the anode close to channel 2, the circulating flow will bring I3- generated at the anode to channel 2, while in Gyro 2, the cathode is close to channel 4 and the circulating flow will bring less I3- to the electrodes than usual. Therefore, the steady-state current between channel 2 and channel 4 will be different resulting in an offset. The device’s noise without driving is 0.81 o/s @ 25 Hz but becomes 10.87o/s @ 25 Hz with MHD driving.

16213019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213019.value: The electrochemical gyroscope, which has a low noise without driving, indicates its potential room of improvement but driving remains a critical issue. The MHD driving used creates inhomogeneous ion distribution resulting in drifted readings and has a weak driving force. In addition, the effect from Euler force is much stronger than the Coriolis force which will cause saturation on the MET detectors. Therefore, future work should focus on exploring new and optimizing driving mechanisms, meanwhile reducing the steady state flow rate at the MET electrodes by design to mitigate saturation. For example, design a structure with driven flow in one channel and MET electrodes in other channels which will have liquid flow only under external motion. In addition, driving mechanism other than MHD drive such as electrowetting could be investigated which may avoid the coupling between driving and the measurement.

16213019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213019.value: The gyroscope, which measures the rate of rotation, is one of the most important motion measurement instruments. MEMS gyroscopes have become very popular due to their miniature size, offering easy integration, low cost and low power consumption. However, MEMS devices have an inherent limitation on mass due to its microfabrication. Not only it is hard to increase the mass, but also a larger mass will provide a challenging requirement for the supporting beam and make the system fragile. Furthermore, because gravity is another factor affecting this mass spring system, an offsetting mechanism needs to be introduced while increasing the mass. The offsetting mechanism can produce an additional leveling requirement for the gyroscopes, resulting in a limited operation tilting angle. This applied research project has designed, fabricated and verified an electrochemical gyroscope based on the molecular electronics transducers (MET) principle. Compared with silicon MEMS inertial sensors, MET sensors use liquid as the sensing body, which enables the feasibility of increasing the proof mass of the sensing body by a significant amount. This work enhanced the understanding of MET fundamentals, such as the multi-physics interactions between microfluidics, mass-transfer, and electrochemical reactions.

16213119.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16213119.value: 利用深度學系的MIMO信道估計

16213119.label: Project Objectives
16213119.value: Objective A: Location-Assisted Hybrid Neural Networks for Realtime Massive MIMO Channel Estimation with Physical Impairments We propose a location-assisted hybrid deep neural network with a deep regenerative Bayesian network at the infrastructure and a deep discriminative network at the mobile. The unique features in the proposed architecture include the generation of channel support side information in the Bayesian network from the user location (which captures important structural properties of the underlying channels induced by the propagation environment) and the exploitation of channel support side information in the channel recovery neural network (which substantially reduces the pilot overhead in massive MIMO systems). Objective B: Location-Assisted Online Dynamic Training Unsupervised training is conducted for the deep regenerative network at the infrastructure to extract the underlying probabilistic relationship between the channel matrices and the hidden variables such as the channel support. On the other hand, a novel decision-feedback training method is proposed for the online training of the channel recovery network during real-life operation. Leveraging on the location-assisted hybrid neural network architecture developed in (A), we will develop efficient online incremental training algorithms to adapt the weights of the neural networks according to the changing environment. Objective C: System-Level Performance Evaluation Our third goal will be to conduct detailed performance evaluation of deep-learning based massive MIMO processing. Specifically, we will develop a software defined radio (SDR) system to collect raw samples from the physical channels at 2-3GHz frequency band. These raw samples will be processed to generate realistic channel realizations for massive MIMO systems. These real-life channel measurements will serve as the dataset for training the neural networks as well as for performance evaluation. The performance of the proposed deep learning based massive MIMO processing will be evaluated and benchmarked against state-of-the-art optimization-based algorithms in terms of efficiency, robustness and computational complexity under realistic LTE+ datapath.

16213119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213119.value: Massive MIMO是一種非常有效的解決方案，它通過大規模空間復用和干擾抑制技術實現高頻譜效率。因此，它是下一代無線網絡的一個非常重要的技術組件。最近，許多研究工作通過探索大規模MIMO信道的稀疏性，實現有效的信道估計。通過各種不同的稀疏重建技術，只需要比天線數量少很多的導頻資源就可以恢復大規模MIMO的信道。然而，這些現有的工作大多基於線性信號模型的假設，忽略了數據路徑中的非線性和量化等很多實際問題。如果考慮這些實際的損失，現有的稀疏恢復解決方法表現都很差。當我們將大規模MIMO中的這些實際損失以及各種不同的結構化稀疏性（如組稀疏，突發稀疏）引入到模型設計中時，信號模型會變得十分複雜。因此，設計使用優化方法的稀疏恢復算法變得十分有挑戰性，有時難以處理。受深度學習成功應用在在分類問題上的啓發，我們將在數據路徑和動態傳播環境中，探索深度學習技術在解決物理層損失下，大規模MIMO信道估計和信號處理等問題上的應用。以下是我們本次項目的目標： （1） 位置輔助的混合神經網絡對具有物理層損傷的大規模MIMO系統的實時信道估計：在第一個任務中，我們將設計專業的神經網絡架構，用於實時大規模MIMO信道估計。這種結構可以開發特定於域的特徵，非線性結構以及由MIMO信道中的傳播和用戶移動性引起的結構化稀疏性。我們提出了一種位置輔助的混合深度神經網絡，在基礎設施上採用深度再生貝葉斯網絡，在移動設備上採用深度判別信道恢復網絡。再生網絡基於用戶的位置，從傳播物理學中捕獲重要結構來生成通道支持側信息。移動設備上的信道恢復網絡利用信道支持側的信息，從接收的導頻恢復大規模MIMO信道。 （2） 位置輔助的在線動態訓練：在第二項任務中，我們將利用（1）中開發的結構化神經網絡來設計有效的在線訓練算法，該算法能夠適應由於用戶移動性引起的動態環境。信道支持側輔助信息的生成需要用戶位置和方向，這些信息通常可從移動傳感器和GPS中獲得。位置輔助信道支持輔助信息能夠使所提出的神經網絡適應大規模MIMO系統中的動態傳播環境，而無需重新訓練網絡。此外，我們還提出了一種新的決策反饋訓練解決方案，以支持實際操作期間，網絡的在線訓練數量增加的問題（儘管缺少對實際信道矩陣的瞭解）。這樣的解決方案針對任何潛在的不匹配問題，都可以自發地進行自我糾正。 （3） 系統級別的性能評估：在第三項任務中，我們將開發軟件定義無線電（SDR）平台，以收集真實的MIMO信道測量值。這些信息將作為訓練和評估的數據集。此外，還將開發一個系統級仿真平台，用於在實際的LTE +數據路徑下，對基於最新優化的算法的神經網絡系統的性能進行基準測試。 本次提出的基於深度學習的解決方案可以產生巨大的影響，因為它可以顯著提高大規模MIMO系統的性能並且具有實時處理能力。我們預計本次提出的解決方案在移動網絡的動態環境中也將非常穩定，並且縮小大規模MIMO系統中理論增益與實際限制/約束之間的差距。它將在未來的無線網絡中充分釋放大規模MIMO的真正潛力。

16213219.label: Project Objectives
16213219.value: Design efficient approximation algorithms for proximity problems with general distance functions, such as convex scaling distance functions and Bregman divergences. Examples of proximity problems we will consider include nearest neighbor searching, farthest neighbor searching, bichromatic closest pair, and diameter.

16213219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213219.value: Approximation algorithms for proximity problems have been extensively studied under the Euclidean metric. However, in many important applications of proximity problems in fields such as machine learning, data mining, data compression, and pattern recognition, the notion of similarity is based on a non-Euclidean distance measure which may not be symmetric and may not satisfy the triangle inequality. This includes Bregman divergences and convex scaling distance functions, where each site possibly defines its own distance function. Surprisingly, despite their theoretical and practical importance, very limited work has been done on these distance functions in the approximate context with provable performance guarantees. In this grant, we propose to design efficient approximation algorithms for proximity problems with such alternative distance measures. 在歐幾里德度量（Euclidean metric）下，接近度問題的近似算法已經得到了廣泛的研究。然而，在很多接近度問題的重要應用領域中，如機器學習、數據探勘、資料壓縮、圖形辨識，相似性是以非歐幾里德度量（non-Euclidean metric）來表達的。在這些度量下，對稱性和三角不等式都未必成立。例如在布雷格曼散度（Bregman divergences）和凸形縮放距離（convex scaling distance functions）這些度量下，每個點都可能獨立地定義其距離函數。這些度量在理論上和應用上都很重要，但令人感到驚訝的是，在它們的近似問題上，只有非常有限的工作具有可被證明的性能保證。在本次撥款項目中，我們將設計高效的近似算法，並以之解決在這些另類度量下的接近度問題。

16213219.label: Realisation of objectives
16213219.value: In J1, we present a novel approach for answering approximate nearest queries using non-Euclidean distances. We consider two families of distance functions: convex scaling distance functions and Bregman divergences, which generalize well-known distance functions. Our approach assumes that the convex body inducing the distance function satisfies certain fatness and smoothness conditions. We present data structures that nearly match the best-known results for the Euclidean metric, subject to mild assumptions on the growth rates of the distance functions. Our approach relies on a technique called convexification, which has not been previously used in computational geometry. We first partition space into cells using a quadtree-like approach, which allows us to establish upper bounds on the gradients and eigenvalues of the Hessians of each distance function within a cell. We then add a common convexifying function to each distance function, making all functions concave. Finally, we approximate the region under the lower envelope of the concave functions using standard techniques for convex bodies. One limitation of standard convex approximation techniques is their suboptimality when dealing with skinny convex bodies. To address this, we introduce bounds for the Hausdorff approximation of convex bodies based on their surface area and volume. Our area-sensitive bound is presented in J2, while our volume-sensitive bound is presented in C1 and J3. Our data structures for convex approximation are based on a hierarchy of Macbeath regions. In J4, we further improved the dependency on dimension of the number of Macbeath regions, which reduces the space and preprocessing time of all our data structures. These techniques also provide an optimal approximation of convex bodies with respect to the Banach-Mazur distance.

16213519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213519.value: This research addresses a problem that is encountered in early stages of architectural design. The process of converting a design idea into an initial shape model is cumbersome and time-consuming. We shall develop a method to design architectural buildings that are inspired by arbitrary shapes, including those of non-architectural objects. The user inputs a few binary images, each providing an indicative shape for the building from a different viewpoint. By selecting a particular perspective viewing point and direction for an image, we can obtain a cone embedded in 3D space. If we intersect two or more such cones (one for each input image), then the resulting solid (or solids) forms the visual hull for the images and the particular choice of perspectives. By changing the viewing point and direction, we can obtain different architectural shapes. The formulation also allows for the placement of interior spaces, such as performance theaters or halls. A voxel model of the visual hull can be generated by discretizing the 3D space and erasing any voxel that does not belong to any of the visual cones. This model is a candidate solution for our problem. By searching over all allowed view perspectives, we can obtain the optimum design. Real buildings must also obey topological and structural constraints. We shall develop a metric to evaluate a given design in terms of topological, functional and structural requirements of the building. All of these requirements are weighted to set up a single (multi-criterion) objective function and a set of geometric and physical constraints. This allows us to optimize the building shape as a function of the parameters of the projection. The problem is highly non-linear and the objective function is discontinuous. We shall to solve the problem by means of a context-aware variant of the cuckoo search metaheuristic. The outcome of the optimization shall be post-processed by utilizing a surface smoothing operation, followed by a controlled shape deformation process that is sensitive to architectural concerns, e.g., the requirement for roofs and balconies to be relatively flat. Finally, we plan to implement the above research into a user-friendly, stand-alone software system. The effectiveness of the program will be tested by means of a series of user studies. The user study will involve real architects from leading architecture firms (e.g., MAD Beijing, Zaha Hadid Architects HK). Experienced architects as well as company interns will be used to operate the software on example design case studies. 該研究解決了在建築設計的早期階段遇到的問題。將設計思想轉換為初始形狀模型的過程是麻煩且耗時的。我們將開發一種方法來設計受任意形狀(包括其他非建築物)啟發的建築物。用戶輸入一些二進製圖像，每個二進製圖像從不同的視點為建築物提供指示性形狀。通過為圖像選擇特定的透視觀察及視圖方向，我們可以獲得嵌入在3D空間中的圓錐。如果我們相交兩個或更多個這樣的錐體（每個輸入圖像一個），則生成的實體（或一些實體）形成圖像的視覺外殼和透視的特定選擇。通過改變視圖觀察點和方向，我們可以獲得不同的建築形狀。該方法還允許應用於內部空間，例如表演劇院或大廳。視覺船體的體素模型可以通過離散3D空間來生成，並且可以生成任何體素。不屬於任何視錐。這個模型是我們問題的一個解決方案。通過搜索所有允許的視角，我們可以獲得最佳設計。實際建築物也必須遵守拓撲和結構約束。我們將根據建築物的拓撲，功能和結構要求開發一個指標來評估給定的設計。所有這些要求都被加權以建立單個（多標準）目標函數和一組幾何和物理約束。這允許我們根據投影的參數優化建築物形狀。問題是高度非線性的，目標函數是不連續的。我們將通過布穀鳥搜索引導的上下文感知變體來解決問題。 優化的結果應通過利用表面平滑操作進行後處理，然後採用對建築關注敏感的受控形狀變形過程，例如屋頂和陽台要求相對平坦。最後，我們計劃實施以上研究為建立成用戶友好的獨立軟件系統。該計劃的有效性將通過一系列用戶研究進行測試。用戶研究將涉及領先建築公司的真正建築師（例如，MAD北京，扎哈哈迪德建築師事務所）。經驗豐富的建築師以及公司實習生將用於在示例設計案例研究中操作該軟件。

16213519.label: Realisation of objectives
16213519.value: In this proposal, we developed the theory and an application to address that is useful for early stage design of complex buildings. These are architectural projects that typically make landmark buildings in cities, such as museums, concert halls, convention centers, etc. Firstly, for the problem in very early stage of architectural design, we develop an approach called shape inspired architectural design. Various aesthetic and structural requirements are enforced on the 3-dimensional initial design based on a small set of inspirational images. The ShapeArchit approach was developed to assist architects in generating new designs and planning internal spaces within the design. The approach uses a modified cuckoo search algorithm and a novel iterative mesh smoothing algorithm to enforce aesthetic and structural requirements on the 3-dimensional initial design based on a small set of inspirational images. The approach also includes an interactive technique for planning the space within the given architecture model with user-specified 3D room elements. The building shape is developed to yield faithful silhouettes of the images from optimal locations by solving an energy minimization problem while encoding physical and functional constraints. The approach can run a subsequent optimization of the exterior shape if the location of optimized internal spaces is fixed. The modified cuckoo search algorithm is extended for solving multiple objective functions and improving algorithm efficiency. A user study was performed to evaluate the system's utility and usability. The system was developed in several stages. Initially, a simple interface allowed the user to input two or more shape sihouettes, for which we can create a shadow hull induced by locating them in arbitrary locations. Next, the energy function for a generated hull was developed, where the cost function is a weighted sum of several metrics, including costs for poor topology, structural strength, non-conformance to the silhouette, volume and surface area deviations from desirable values. This provided the framework for an optimization problem that is solved by a novel variation of cuckoo search. Finally, the initial voxel-based shape is converted to an equivalent mesh shape, with a new smoothing filter applied to create a final shape desirable from architectural concerns. Once the initial design of the building is confirmed, an important consideration is that of manufacturability of the building. At early stages, it is possible to modify the shape of the building skin (i.e. the façade) while retaining the overall shape characteristics, and significantly reduce the cost and risks in manufacturing the façade. This is called rationalization of the building structure. In particular, we explored the problem of clustering the set of vertices in a given 3D mesh. This corresponds to the reduction in variations of the joints, which connect the panels on the building façade to its structural framework. We first derive a max-norm based metric to estimate the geometric disparity between a given pair of vertices, and characterize the problem in terms of this measure. We show that this distance can be computed by using Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP). Next we introduce two different algorithms for clustering the set of vertices on a given mesh, respectively based on two disparity measurements: max-norm and L2-norm based metric. An equivalence is established between mesh vertices and physical joints in an architectural mesh. By replacing individual joints by their equivalent cluster representative, the number of unique joints in the facade mesh, and therefore the fabrication cost, is dramatically reduced. Finally, we present an algorithm for remeshing a given surface in order to further reduce the number of joint clusters. The framework is tested for a set of real-world architectural surfaces to illustrate the effectiveness and utility of our approach. Overall, this approach tackles the important problem reducing fabrication cost of joints without modifying the underlying connectivity that was specified by the architect. The objective (1) was accomplished by the completion of the programming of the ShapeArchit software as described above. The objective (2) was an integral part of the system: the energy cost metric used drive the shape optimization included one component that estimated the structural integrity of the current design. The objective (3) was achieved by the design of the new (modified) cuckoo search algorithm that was used by the optimization. Finally, objective (4) was met by conducting a user study including practicing architects, practicing facade design BIM engineers, and also a group of architectural students in a local university to test the efficacy of our designed computing framework.

16213519.label: Major findings and research outcome
16213519.value: The project was concluded, and resulted in the creation of an automatic design framework (a user-executable computer program running on any standard windows PC with at least 8G of RAM) that provides an interface for automated design of architectural shapes given a set of two or three silhouette shapes, together with some interior space requirements (functional requirements). The research led to the publication of two papers in top international venues. The major outcomes of the ShapeArchit system were: An integrated framework that explicitly uses aesthetic and functional requirements to generate building shapes that are structurally sound. We also developed specialized local smoothing filters that respect aesthetic requirements (e.g. edge sharpness, flatness of flat regions such as roofs/balconies). A user study with both, early stage architectural students as well as professional architects was completed to evaluate the effectiveness of the software in generating viable designs in early stage architectural projects.

16213519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16213519.value: There are two possible extensions of the project. The first is to extend the framework to incorporate other relevant criteria in the cost function. The cost function dictates the outcome of the optimization engine in our system. The most interesting extension is that of incorporation of colored and graduated photovoltaic (PV) panels on the building exterior. It is well known that such PV panels can now be produced and provide two improvements of classical PV solar panels: (1) the colors provide distinct visual and aesthetic look to the building (at the cost of solar efficiency); and (2) the colored PVs reduce the amount of solar energy transmitting into the interior of the building, thereby reducing the dependence on the air cooling in the interior, while still providing some amount of daylight. The PI is now planning a collaborated project together with co-author, Prof Pedro Sander (CSE, HKUST) and colleague, PRof Chanying Xiang, on a new research project to develop this extension. The second extension is to improve the runtime of our existing system. The current system is somewhat slow, since the cuckoo search optimization heuristic must examine a fairly large number of shapes, each of which is evaluated via a finite difference model (FDT) based on a system for dynamic simulation of soft objects. We are now considering to replace this FDT model with an alternative approach, following a system that works via fast co-rotated FEM simulator that directly works on tetrahedral meshes. This approach will significantly change our pipeline, and we need to examine how we can transition away from a voxel-based visual hull to a mesh-based approach.

16213519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16213519.value: Our research resulted in the development of a tool that allows architects to create building shapes (particularly of complex, landmark buildings, such as concert halls, museums, convention halls, etc.) in early design stages. At this stage, the architect usually has a general idea about the shape and visual effect they would wish to achieve; but from this step to making 3D models (virtual, or scaled physical ones) is a very time- and resource consuming exercise. By using our software, architects can potentially provide very simple inputs (for example, the profile shapes of a pyramid, a crescent moon, and a sphinx) and generate viable 3D building shapes (such as an Egypt museum building). Furthermore, the architect can also input requirements on interior spaces, such as shape and size of various rooms inside the building, and our system automatically creates recommended location of these spaces in the interior of the shape generated. The value of the research is to provide a new creative tool to apprentice and practicing architects.

16213819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16213819.value: Crystallization is a crucial separation and product-formation technology in the pharmaceutical industry. A key challenge is to obtain control over intrinsic crystal quality attributes such as the shape and size distribution which affect the performance of downstream processes and likely the efficacy of the final product. Cooling crystallization of an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) from solution is a standard crystallization method in the pharmaceutical industry. The crystal size distribution of the final product is determined by the interplay of various physical phenomena such as crystal nucleation, growth, agglomeration, and attrition, which are difficult to control in a large volume due to their close entanglement and a dependence on very local conditions. Scale dependence can be avoided when crystallization is confined in the droplets of an emulsion. Furthermore, the supersaturation that can be generated and consumed inside a small droplet is well defined and shear forces are minimized. Therefore, emulsion crystallization has been used as a simpler crystallization process. Traditional emulsification methods are based on vigorous stirring to produce poly-disperse droplets or on microfluidics methods which can be difficult to scale up. Membrane emulsification is frequently used to make emulsions in the food industry and for drug delivery applications. The advantage of membrane emulsification is the promise of easy scale-up and the ability to produce monodisperse droplets of controllable size. However, membrane emulsification has not been combined with cooling crystallization from solution, despite its promise. This research proposes to develop a novel process combining membrane emulsification and cooling crystallization of APIs from solution. Our preliminary experiments based on various conventional emulsification methods have demonstrated that crystals can be confined in emulsion droplets provided that the droplets are sufficiently large and shear forces are minimized. That motivates our proposal to employ membrane emulsification. An experimental cross flow membrane emulsification process will be developed tailored to facilitate cooling crystallization. The process will be characterized and optimized by changing design parameters (pore diameter) and operating variables (supersaturation) to develop guidelines for design and operation. Finally, a process model will be developed combining a membrane emulsification model with a probabilistic crystallization model to describe nucleation in the droplets, which is important to support design and control. A successful outcome of the research would provide a novel way to conduct cooling crystallization with a potential for significantly improved control over the final crystal size. 結晶是製藥工業中一種重要的分離和產物形成的技術。一個關鍵的難題是獲得對內在晶體質量屬性的控制，例如形狀和尺寸分佈這些會影響下游工藝性能，並可能影響最終產品功效的屬性。從溶液中通過冷卻結晶獲取活性藥物成分（API）是製藥工業中的標準結晶方法。最終產品的晶體尺寸分佈由各種物理現象的相互作用決定，例如成核，晶體生長，團聚和磨損，由於它們緊密聯繫並且依賴於局部條件，在過程的規模較大時很難控制。當結晶被限制在乳液液滴中時則可以避免對規模的依賴性。此外，在小液滴內產生和消耗的過飽和度可以很好的得到限制，同時使剪切力最小化。因此，乳液結晶已被用作一種更為簡單的結晶方法。 傳統的方法是通過劇烈攪拌以產生多分散液滴或者利用微流體進行乳化，其過程難以放大。膜乳化經常用於製備食品工業和藥物運輸應用中的乳液。膜乳化的優點是易於放大並且能夠生產可控尺寸的單分散液滴。然而，膜乳化還沒有與溶液中的冷卻結晶方法相結合。 該研究提出開發一種將溶液中的API乳化和API冷卻結晶相結合的新方法。我們基於各種常規乳化方法的初步實驗已經表明，只要液滴足夠大且使剪切力最小化，晶體就可以被限制在乳液液滴中。這推動了我們提出使用膜乳化的提案。我們將開發一個適用並能促進冷卻結晶的交叉流動膜乳化過程。通過改變設計參數（孔徑）和操作變量（過飽和度）來表徵和優化該過程，從而探索過程設計和操作的指導方針。最終，我們將開發一種將膜乳化模型與概率結晶模型相結合的過程模型，以描述液滴中的成核過程，這對於過程設計和控制非常重要。該研究的成果將提供一種進行冷卻結晶的新方法，其能夠顯著提高對最終的晶體尺寸的控制能力。

16214219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214219.value: Time reversal of waves is instrumental in many fields and underpins the foundation of practical equipment that, for example, is used to destroy tumor and kidney stones, to detect defects in solids, to pinpoint underground mineral deposits, and to assist in long distance communication. In the context of pipeline hydraulics, time reversal has been successfully used historically for “valve stroking” (using the desired response to determine the necessary cause) and has recently been shown by the PI’s research group to make possible efficient, robust, high resolution and noise-tolerant schemes for the detection of leaks, blockages and bursts in real pipe systems where damping (e.g., friction and visco-elasticity) is present. Herein lies a crucial and unresolved paradox; although time reversal breaks down due to the inevitable damping of real waves, it still produces superior results than other defect detection techniques. This same paradox is described in the classic waterhammer book by Wylie et al (1993), page 223: “the [waterhammer] equations are remarkably robust in calculating backward in time.... [However] the idea of calculating backwards in time defies logic since it cannot be done physically. It cannot because of the irreversibility of losses in real systems.” This proposed research will address this paradox using theoretical and experimental means. Theoretically, this research will seek a mathematical transformation that transforms the damped wave equation into an undamped one; that is, an approach to transform a non-time reversible problem (damped wave equation) into a time-reversible problem (undamped wave equation). The damping effects that will be considered include steady and unsteady friction and visco-elasticity. The resulting transformation will be solved so that the undamped response can be obtained from the measured one and used in conjunction with time reversal schemes for defect detection. Physically, the required transformation must be an amplification operation that adds back the energy that was lost due to damping. Unfortunately, this means that measurement errors will also be amplified under the transformation making the problem ill-posed. Two regularization techniques will be tested in this research. To supplement this theoretical work, the experimental aim is to provide the first ever proof that time reversal provides an efficient, robust, high resolution and noise-tolerant techniques for the detection of defects in pipes and to test the range of validity of the proposed theoretical transformation. 時間反轉法的用途十分廣泛，例如擊碎腫瘤和腎石、物體中的瑕疪的探測、地下的礦物勘探，及長距離通訊等等。在水管瞬變流中，時間反轉法一般用來找出一些閥門調校方法，以達至水管的某種特定反應。主研究員最近發現時間反轉法可以有效可靠和高精度地探測水管中的滲漏、爆裂和阻塞。而且，這些方法能在噪聲較大的環境下使用。雖然壓力波在水管的傳播中必然損耗能量，但是沒有考慮能量損耗的時間反轉法仍然比其他滲漏探測的方法優勝。在介绍水槌效應的經典著作Wylie et al 1993中，在第223頁中討論這個悖論時說：「水槌方程可以很容易地被反轉時間計算，...，不過反轉時間的計算不符合邏輯，因為物理上時間不可能被反轉。理由是供水管道內的能量耗散是一個不可逆的過程。」這項研究計劃將會找尋一個數學變換，把含有能量耗散的波動方程變換為沒有能量耗散的波動方程。換句話說，把一個不可逆的方程變換成為一個時間可逆的方程。這個變換考慮了由穩定和不穩定流所帶來的摩擦力損耗和因粘彈性帶來的能量損耗。在水管裡量度的數據可以經由這個變換變成在一個無損耗的數據並將其應用於時間反轉法中。我們可以利用這些數據和時間反轉法來探測滲漏。物理上這個變換相當於把損耗掉的能量加到訊號裡。不幸地，這樣等於把測量誤差也放大了，使這個數學問題變成不適定。這項研究會嘗試兩個正規化技巧解決這個問題。我們同時會進行實驗以證明時間反轉法可以在噪聲較大的環境下有效可靠和高精度地探測水管中的故障，和找尋這個理論的有效範圍。

16214219.label: Realisation of objectives
16214219.value: The first objective is fully achieved. To this aim, we begin with incorporating the damping terms (pipe wall friction and viscoelasticity) inside the wave equation and identify both the undamped and damped wave equation operators in the frequency domain. By comparing these two operators, we recognized that the damping terms act like a convolution to the undamped wave signal and filters the high frequency content of the signal. As such, the resulting damped signal has damping-induced dispersion (phase shift), frequency-dependent wave speed, and short bandwidth than the injected bandwidth of the signal. Thus, we sought for a mathematical transformation by performing deconvolution. However, it is noticed that this deconvolution procedure amplifies the inevitable measurement noise in the signal and leads to an ill-posed problem. This problem is resolved in objective 2 and detailed next. The second objective was to devise a stable inversion technique and has been fully achieved. In particular, we used singular value decomposition technique to regularize the deconvolution by selecting a range of singular values that are above the noise level. As such, the obtained undamped signal is found to be clean for the first few cycles of the transient waves. The third objective was to test this transformation in conjunction with time-reversal technique for defect detection. To this aim, we have tested the proposed technique for leakage and blockage detection by means of numerical simulations as well as laboratory experiments with great success. In particular, we found 84% improvement in defect resolution while 7% improvement in defect size estimation when transformed (undamped) signal was used.

16214219.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214219.value: 1) The role of unsteady friction and viscoelasticity on the spectral content of the transient signal is studied analytically. The results show that damping induced by visco-elastic behavior is prominent for frequencies that are below the viscous timescale of the pipe (i.e., the retardation time). Frequencies higher than the viscous timescale of the pipe are found to damp uniformly. The unsteady pipe-wall friction, on the other hand, is found to damp high frequency content of the injected transient signal (See PhD thesis No. 2, and Papers No. 2, 3, 5, 6 and 9 in Part C). 2) Theoretical investigation on the pipe wall friction and viscoelasticity leads to devise a non-dimensional time-reversal (TR) parameter. The significance of this parameter is that it provides the spatial extent at which the signal is time-reversible and can be used for defect localization. This proposed parameter is applicable to both metallic (e.g., ductile iron, cast iron) and polymeric (medium/high density polyethylene) pipe systems. As such, it can be used to design and evaluate transient experiments in real-field (See Paper No. 2 in Part C). 3) A noise-tolerant, computationally efficient and regularized scheme is developed to accurately recover the damping-free transient signal from its damped version. Physically, the proposed transformation is an amplification operation that adds back the energy that was lost due to the damping. This means that measurement errors will also be amplified under the transformation, making the problem ill-posed. The truncated singular value decomposition method is used to regularize the transformation. The proposed scheme is tested analytically, numerically, and experimentally (See Papers No. 2, and 4 in Part C). 4) The proposed damping-free signal extraction is tested for leakage and blockage detection using time-reversal technique. The results show that the recovered signal leads to reduction in localization error, enhancement in resolution, and 7 times improvement in blockage size estimation (See PhD thesis 1, and Papers No. 1,2,7 and 8 in Part C).

16214219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214219.value: The proposed transformation scheme is tested for single pipelines, single defects, and one-dimensional low-frequency hydraulic transient waves (LFW). Following future developments are scheduled to achieve in the near future: 1) The proposed technique will be tested for multiple defects and relatively complex pipe systems (e.g., tree-type pipe network). 2) The proposed transformation scheme will be applied to real-field pipe networks to investigate the efficiency and limitations of the proposed technique. The planned course of action is to develop a similar transformation for high-frequency waves (HFW). By HFW, we imply the waves whose wavelength is comparable to the radial scale of the pipe. As such, these HFW propagate in axial, radial, and circumferential directions. HFW undergoes different damping than one-dimensional LFW due to intrinsic dispersion behavior and the time scale of the waves. Therefore, the proposed method of this proposal is not readily applicable to HFW.

16214219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214219.value: Pressurized urban water supply systems are fraught with defects (e.g., leaks and blockage) and susceptible to catastrophic accidents if remain overlooked. Hydraulic transient-based defect detection methods offer fast, non-disruptive, and non-intrusive means to diagnose these systems. However, as the transient wave propagates inside the pipe, it undergoes damping due to pipe wall friction and the non-linear rheological behavior of pipes. Consequently, the acquired transient signal is damped and comprised of less frequency content than the injected bandwidth. When used for defect detection, the damped signal results in poor resolution and erroneous defect size estimation (e.g., leak size, blockage size). In this proposal, a mathematical transformation is sought which undoes the damping and provides a damping-free version of the signal by adding back the energy that is previously lost due to damping. The resulting damping-free signal is used in conjunction with time-reversal techniques. The results show that defect detection with a damping-free signal provides higher resolution and improves defect size estimation. The proposed transformation is tested using synthetic data as well as experimental data from laboratory-scale pipe systems.

16214519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214519.value: Earthquake-induced landslides are one of the most catastrophic effects of earthquakes, as evidenced by many historic events over the past decades. Landslides have caused significant damage to infrastructure and heavy loss of life. Therefore, realistic prediction of coseismic landslides is crucial for the design of key infrastructure and to protect human lives in seismically active regions. Coseismic landslides are complicated nonlinear, progressive, large-deformation processes triggered by ground shaking. To date, analytical methods for estimating coseismic landslides have been based on highly simplified models. Many gaps still remain in the scientific understanding of the landslide process. Considerable difficulties are encountered by conventional numerical methods in modeling large deformation. Therefore, it is urgent to develop innovative numerical schemes to address the above challenge. With the advancement of computational technology, there is an opportunity to develop a physics-based model to study the complex failure process of coseismic landslides. In this project, we will develop a multiscale, multiphase numerical method by coupling Material Point Method (MPM) and Spectral Element Method (SEM) for large-deformation analysis of coseismic landslides. On the regional scale, SEM is efficient in modeling a 3D wave field in complex topography on a scale of hundreds of kilometers. Near-field characteristics of earthquake shaking and topographic amplification can be faithfully simulated, and their effects on coseismic landslides will be studied. On the local scale, the progressive slope failure process and post-failure large-deformation behavior, including triggering, runoff and deposition of landslide masses, will be studied by MPM considering soil-water interaction, soil nonlinearity, variation of material properties and change in slope geometry. The multiscale MPM-SEM method will be the first numerical tool of its kind for integrated study of the complete coseismic landslide process. Finally, benchmark tests and case studies will be performed to calibrate and validate the proposed numerical model. In particular, two recent landslide case histories will be simulated using the multiscale MPM-SEM method, including the Hongshiyan landslide in the 2014 Ludian earthquake in China, and landslides triggered in the 2016 Kaikoura earthquake in New Zealand. These case studies will provide a valuable opportunity to revisit key factors that influence coseismic landslides using measured field data. 地震引發的滑坡是地震最具災難性的影響之一，過去幾十年来許多歷史事件都證明了這一點。山體滑坡對基礎設施造成嚴重破壞，造成重大人員傷亡。因此，真實預測地震滑坡對地震活躍地區關鍵基礎設施的設計和人類生命的保護至關重要。地震滑坡是由地面震動引發的複雜的非線性、漸進、大變形過程。迄今為止，地震滑坡的分析方法基於高度簡化的模型，對滑坡過程的科學認識中仍存在許多空缺。傳統的數值方法在模擬大變形時遇到了相當大的困難。因此，迫切需要開發新型的數值方案來應對上述挑戰。 隨著計算技術的進步，有機會開發一種基於物理的模型來研究地震山體滑坡的複雜破壞過程。在本項目中，我們將通過耦合物質點法（MPM）和譜單元法（SEM）開發一種多尺度、多相數值方法，用於地震滑坡的大變形分析。在區域尺度上，SEM可以在數百公里的範圍內對複雜地形中的三維波場進行建模；可以忠實地模擬地震震動和地形放大的近場特徵，並研究它們對地震滑坡的影響。在局部尺度上，MPM將考慮土 - 水相互作用、土體非線性、材料性質和山體幾何變化等因素，研究漸進式邊坡破壞過程和破壞後大變形行為，包括滑坡體的觸發，徑流和沉積。多尺度MPM-SEM方法將成為研究地震滑坡全過程的首創數值工具。 最後，將進行測試和案例研究，以校驗所提出的數值模型。特別是，將使用多尺度MPM-SEM方法模擬兩個近期發生的滑坡案例，包括2014年中國魯甸地震中的紅石岩滑坡，以及2016年新西蘭凱庫拉地震引發的山體滑坡。這些案例研究將利用現場觀測數據，為重新審視影響地震滑坡的關鍵因素提供寶貴的機會。

16214519.label: Realisation of objectives
16214519.value: Project objective 1 has been fully achieved. The PI and his coworkers have successfully developed a two-layer hydro-mechanically coupled Material Point Method in the framework of unsaturated soil mechanics. The method employs two layers of material points to represent coupling effects between the solid and fluid phases. Several numerical examples demonstrate unique features of the method, including free water infiltration into the unsaturated soil and dynamic soil-water interaction in an example of underwater soil collapse. Furthermore, rainfall-induced failure in unsaturated soil slopes is analyzed. The proposed method can well capture change in matric suction, development of shallow and deep-seated shear bands, and finally, large-deformation post-failure behavior. Parametric studies also demonstrate soil cohesion, dilatancy and friction angle play significant roles on the slope failure mechanisms. The results were published in Acta Geotechnica, a leading journal in the field (Feng et al. 2021a [J1]). The Material Point Method is further developed to simulate dynamic slope stability and liquefaction-induced embankment failure under earthquake loading. A fully nonlinear bounding surface soil model is implemented in the two-phase soil-water coupled MPM framework to investigate the liquefaction mechanism and associated dam failure, using the 1971 Lower San Fernando Dam as an example. The numerical results are generally comparable with the post-failure profiles obtained from field investigation, which highlight the advantage of MPM in handling liquefaction-induced large deformation. The MPM shows great promise to quantitatively assess risk and consequence associated with seismic slope failure and soil liquefaction, thereby, advance the performance-based engineering design and analysis. The results have been published in Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering (Feng et al. 2021b [J4]) and Journal of Zhejiang University [J5]. Success in objective 1 formed a solid basis for objectives 2 and 3. Project objective 2 has been fully achieved. For objective 2, a multiscale computational framework based on Spectral Element Method (SEM) and Material Point Method (MPM) has been developed for multiscale, large-deformation analysis of coseismic landslides. At a regional scale, SEM is used to model elastic wave propagation from seismic source to a local site, such that topographic amplification, soil response and near-field characteristics of earthquake shaking can be simulated. At a local scale, the progressive landslide process and large deformation behavior are simulated by a fine-scale nonlinear MPM model. The capacity of SEM for conducting regional scale seismic responses analysis in complex geological environment setting, such as mountain valley and shallow basin, has been demonstrated in a case study, published in top journal Earthquake Engineering and Structure Dynamics (Kato and Wang 2021, [J2]). In the multiscale MPM-SEM framework, the SEM and MPM models are coupled through a domain reduction method, which is validated through a benchmark example in Feng et al. (2022) [J6]. Project objective 3 has been fully achieved. In relation to project objective 3, the multiscale coupled SEM-MPM method is used to simulate the massive Hongshiyan landslide triggered by the 2014 Ms 6.5 Ludian earthquake in China, in which a whole picture from fault rupture to regional-scale seismic wave propagation to landslides triggering, runoff and deposition is simulated. The post-failure morphologies of the landslide simulation are generally in agreement with those from field investigations, showing the SEM-MPM method is a promising physics-based numerical tool for a multiscale analyses of regional coseismic landslides. The numerical simulation agrees well with recorded ground-motion time histories and observed landslide pattern. A research paper has been published in Engineering Geology (Feng et al. 2022, [J6]). Extensive coseismic landslides occurred in the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake is simulated by using the developed numerical method. The regional-scale ground motion simulation incorporated a complex kinematic fault rupture model. With consideration of soil nonlinearity and topographic amplification effects, regional scale ground motions were reasonably simulated and compared well with a few recording stations. The study revealed strong ground motion distribution in the near source area, which is directly related to numerous landslides during the earthquake. The study was published in Earthquake Engineering & Structural Dynamics (Chen et al. 2023a [J7]). In the subsequent study, the regional wave simulation is integrated with flexible sliding analysis to realistically simulate coseismic landslide distribution occurred in Aso caldera region. Overall, the simulation captures 58% of observed landslides in the inventory (using a displacement threshold of 15 cm), showing the proposed framework is a promising tool for regional coseismic landslide analysis. The work was published in Engineering Geology (Chen et al. 2023b [J8]). In summary, to date, eight papers have been accepted by top international journals, including two papers published in Engineering Geology, two in Earthquake Engineering and Structure Dynamics, others were published in Acta Geotechnica, Computers and Geotechnics, and Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering etc. List of Journal Papers Published (PI: Wang G, Co-I: Huang D) [J1] Feng K, Huang D.*, Wang G. 16214519.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214519.value: 1. The project developed a multiphase hydromechanically coupled material point method (MPM) to simulate slope failure in unsaturated soils [J1]. It demonstrated the importance of modeling solid-fluid coupling in slope failure analysis. Furthermore, a fully nonlinear soil model is implemented in the MPM framework [J4]. The MPM shows great promise to quantitatively assess risk and consequence associated with seismic slope failure and soil liquefaction, thereby, advances the performance-based engineering design and analysis. 2. The project developed a multiscale MPM-SEM coupling model for large-deformation analysis of coseismic landslides. At a regional scale, SEM is used to model elastic wave propagation from a seismic source to a local site with complex topography [J2, J7]. At a local scale, the coseismic landslide process and large deformation behavior are simulated by a nonlinear MPM model. The proposed domain-reduction technique is effective to couple two different scales. The proposed SEM-MPM model is able to model the entire coseismic landslide process, including triggering, sliding and deposition [J6]. 3. The characteristics of near fault wave patterns, topographic amplification of ground motions and soil nonlinearity are found to be closely related to coseismic landslide distribution. Predictive models for topographic amplification were developed based on topographic features [J7]. 4. The numerical platform has been extensively validated through several recent case studies, including dam failure [J4], Hongshiyan landslide occurred during the 2014 Ludian earthquake [J6], and extensive landslides during the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake [J7, J8]. The research findings have been published as eight SCI journal papers in top international journals, including Engineering Geology, Earthquake Engineering and Structural Dynamics, Soil Dynamics and Earthquake Engineering, Acta Geotechnica etc. The research findings also have been actively disseminated in local, national and international conferences, as “ISSMGE Bright Spark Lecture” [C1], “HKSTAM Distinguished Lecture” [C2], the “State of the Art and Practice (SoAP) Lecture” at 7ICRAGEE in India [C3], an invited talk at PEER International Pacific Rim Forum by UC Berkeley; and a theme lecture at PBD-IV, Beijing; Most recently, the work was presented at COMPLAS 2023 at Barcelona, Spain [C6], and as an invited lecture in The 14th National Conference on Soil Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering, Oct 2023 at Wuhan, which is a major national conference attended by more than 4000 participants. Three PhD, two MSc and one undergraduate students have been trained; one Postdoc Fellow has worked on this project.

16214519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214519.value: Although we have developed advanced multiscale MPM-SEM platform and performed several validation studies for simulating large deformation process of coseismic landslides, significant efforts are still needed to further apply the model to study more real cases. Such kind of real case histories, although still quite limited, are very valuable to further validate and refine the model. The developed model relies on large-scale scientific computing and intensive computing resources, and it is quite costly to perform such analyses. In the future, more efficient simulation tools shall be developed to predict the ground motions and associated landslides by using AI, deep learning algorithms etc., with an over-arching goal to develop fast, real-time prediction method for coseismic landslide when an earthquake strikes. It is well understood that, real time landslide prediction is more urgently needed for hazard mitigation and post-earthquake emergency management.

16214519.value: Realistic prediction of earthquake-induced landslides is critical for the design of key infrastructure. To date, numerical methods for estimating coseismic landslides have been based on highly simplified models. In this research, we develop a multiscale, multiphase numerical method by coupling Material Point Method (MPM) and Spectral Element Method (SEM) for large-deformation analysis of coseismic landslides. The multiscale MPM-SEM method is the first numerical tool of its kind that integrates the physics-based simulation of wave propagation at a regional scale and progressive slope failure process at a local scale. Two recent landslide case histories were studies to calibrate and validate the proposed numerical model, including the Hongshiyan landslide in the 2014 Ludian earthquake in China and the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake. The study demonstrated the significant advantage of the developed multiscale MPM-SEM framework in realistically predicting coseismic landslide triggering, runoff and deposition. The study provided a tool to advance the scientific understanding of the landslide triggering and post-failure large deformation behavior by considering complex topography and soil behaviors.

16214619.label: Project Objectives
16214619.value: To develop an algorithm that can perform nanophotonic structure design optimization with modeling to improve the light extraction efficiency of perovskite light-emitting diodes. The goal is to achieve nanophotonic structures with light extraction efficiency higher than 90 %. To improve the perovskite LED internal quantum efficiency by material engineering. This includes using additives for perovskite non-radiative recombination center passivation, using quantum-dots to achieve higher radiative recombination rate and smaller crystal size, using nanocrystal pinning method and exploring the quasi-2D perovskite materials. Combining material engineering and nanophotonic design, the LED device EQE can be further enhanced beyond current record of 20%. To explore flexible perovskite LED device fabrication process. Flexible LED devices are highly attractive for flexible displays in the future. Here we will explore fabrication of nanophotonic structures on flexible substrates and subsequently fabricate flexible perovskite LEDs on these substrates. To explore scalable fabrication methods for nanostructured perovskite LED devices. In addition to conventional spin coating method. We will explore roll-to-roll fabrication of the nanostructured thin films and evaporation of perovskites and charge injection layers. The goal is to prepare perovskite films with large scale uniformity which can enable future scalable LED device fabrication.

16214619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16214619.value: Metal-halide perovskite materials have attracted enormous attention in recent years for their applications in high-performance optoelectronic devices, including solar cells, photodetectors and light-emitting diodes (LEDs). The excellent color tunability, narrow emission line width and high radiative recombination rate of perovskite materials are especially favorable for LED applications. Recently, research on perovskite LEDs reached a new milestone of 20 % EQE which makes it comparable to the state-of-art performance organic LEDs. However, the light extraction efficiency in a perovskite LED is typically lower than 30 % which should be significantly improved in the future. In this project, we propose to design and fabricate novel perovskite LED devices on nanophotonic structures to address the bottleneck light extraction efficiency issue. Computational tools will be utilized for the geometrical optimization of the nanophotonic structure with fast speed and obtain rational guidelines for optimal structure fabrication. Our preliminary study already achieved a light extraction efficiency of more than 70 %. With further systematic exploration, the light extraction will be further improved to more than 90 % or even close to 100 %. Based on the theoretical study, the nanophotonic substrate will be fabricated with our well-developed electrochemical process, and the LED device will be fabricated on the nanophotonic substrate. In the same time, the internal quantum efficiency can be enhanced by material engineering of perovskite layer and injection layers. With the efforts on the improvement of both light extraction efficiency and device internal quantum efficiency, the device external quantum efficiency that will be achieved with the project is expected to be more than the current record of 20 %. Meanwhile, we will also explore non-toxic perovskite materials and approaches to improve device long-term stability, as well as develop scalable fabrication methods such as large scale vacuum deposition of the LED devices. 近年來，金屬鹵化物鈣鈦礦材料因其在高性能光電器件（包括太陽能電池，光電探測器和發光二極管（LED））中的應用而引起了極大的關注。鈣鈦礦材料的顏色可調性，窄發射線寬和高輻射複合率對LED應用尤其有利。最近，鈣鈦礦LED達到了20％外量子效率的新里程碑，這使其可與當前最佳性能的有機LED相媲美。然而，光提取效率低於30％仍然為提高效率留下了相當大的機會。在該項目中，光子晶體用作鈣鈦礦LED器件製造的基板，以解決光提取效率差的問題。計算工具將用於納米光子結構的幾何優化，具有快速和準確的指導以實現最佳結構製造。我們的初步研究已經實現了超過70％的光提取效率。通過進一步的系統探索，光提取將進一步提高到90％以上甚至接近100％。在理論研究的基礎上，採用我們完善的陽極陽極氧化工藝製備納米光子基板，並在納米光子基板上製作LED器件。同時，鈣鈦礦層和注入層的材料工程可以提高內部量子效率。通過努力提高光提取效率和器件內部量子效率，器件外量子效率可以提高很多，打破目前的20％的記錄。同時，我們對無毒鈣鈦礦材料和長期穩定性的研究也確保了我們研究成果的日常應用能力。更重要的是，我們的製造方法還包括研究LED器件的真空沉積，這對於鈣鈦礦LED的大規模生產非常關鍵。最後但並非最不重要的是，在該項目中研究的納米光子基板非常通用，不僅可以用於鈣鈦礦LED，還可以用於具有許多其他材料的LED器件。

16214619.label: Realisation of objectives
16214619.value: The objectives have been accomplished. We have developed a nano-photonic structure with over 90 % light extraction efficiency: porous alumina membrane with average pore size down to ~ 5 nm. After fabricating perovskite light emitting materials with such nanophotonic structure, the relatively low refractive index of alumina substantially has enabled an ultrahigh light extraction efficiency of up to 97.8%. We have also successfully manipulated material engineering and nanophotonic design to improve the perovskite LED internal quantum efficiency, including introducing 2D phase and quantum confinement (quantum wires) of perovskite materials for more efficient radiative recombination, adding additives (such as RbBr, BABr, PEABr, PDABr2, etc.) to passivate the defects in perovskite films. For example, by using all-vacuum evaporation method, mixed-dimensional outer layer quasi-2D PRK-3D CsPbBr3 perovskite core-shell structure is obtained after sequential evaporation of PbBr2, BABr, and CsBr, and post annealing. By controlling the ratio of BA:Cs, annealing temperature, as well as the film thickness of each layer precisely, molecular structural modulation from 3D to 2D has been achieved. Intriguingly, 2D nanoflake structured PRK with small crystal size can be achieved under a certain condition. The nanoflakes-formed thin film performs lower dimensional PRK behavior, especially for PLQY increasing. We have also fabricated perovskite quantum wires in ultrasmall-pore alumina membrane with a close-spaced-vapor-reaction method. The quantum confinement effect, in conjunction with porous alumina membrane’ passivation, resulted in significantly improved radiative recombination rate and a very high PLQY of 92 %. Based on the as-fabricated perovskite materials with high radiative recombination rate, we have achieved high-performance perovskite LEDs with EQE over 20 %. More specifically, we have successfully fabricated crystalline all-inorganic perovskite quantum wire arrays with ultrahigh density and excellent uniformity, using a generic organic ligand-free and anti-solvent-free solution method. We have achieved full color (blue, sky-blue, green and pure-red) perovskite LEDs with EQE of 12.41%, 16.49%, 26.09% and 9.97%, respectively, after introducing a dual-functional small molecule, which serves as surface passivation and hole transporting layer, and a halide vacancy healing agent. We have also demonstrated good flexibility and upscalability of perovskite LED devices. With the full evaporation method, we have demonstrated a large-scale device with a size of 1.5 cm x 2 cm with good uniformity. Based on both the vapor- and solution-phase grown perovskite quantum wires, we have demonstrated the largest 4-inch wafer scale perovskite LEDs with excellent uniformity, as well as good flexibility for 1.5 cm x 1.5 cm devices.
