16214619.label: Major findings and research outcome
16214619.value: The significant role of nano-photonics substrates in enhancing perovskite LEDs has been discovered. Through our research, we have found that by incorporating nano-photonics substrates into perovskite LED devices, remarkable improvements in light extraction efficiency and external quantum efficiency can be achieved. The maximum light extraction efficiency can reach an impressive 73.6%, while the highest external quantum efficiency can reach 17.5%. These values represent a two-fold improvement compared to ordinary planar devices. This groundbreaking research was published in Nature Communications 10 (1), 727 and has received significant recognition, consistently being selected as a highly cited paper according to ESI. Our study also delved into the mechanism of light wave propagation in perovskite LED devices, leading to the breakthrough of breaking the internal optical outcoupling limit. The key factor lies in the design of a well-optimized optical structure, which marks the first application of this design method to perovskite optoelectronic devices. This advancement opens up new possibilities for enhancing the overall performance of perovskite LEDs. Building upon these findings, we further explored the potential of nano-photonics devices. By fabricating nanowire array devices within a nanostructured framework, we were able to achieve significant improvements. The external quantum efficiency was increased from 11% to 15%, and the device lifetime at 1000 nit brightness was extended from 17 minutes to 35 minutes. This represents a remarkable two-fold breakthrough in efficiency under high brightness conditions. Additionally, the flexibility of the devices was enhanced, as they were able to maintain 30% of the initial efficiency even after undergoing 500 bending cycles. These promising outcomes were published in ACS Nano 14 (2), 1577-1585. In addition to these advancements, we successfully applied nano-photonics substrates to nano-patterned sapphire substrates, resulting in a significant improvement in the light emission efficiency of automotive white lighting. These achievements were also implemented in the products of Nation Star Semiconductors (Foshan), showcasing the practical application of our research in the industry. Overall, our research on nano-photonics substrates has demonstrated their immense potential in enhancing perovskite LEDs, paving the way for future advancements in efficiency, stability, and practical applications across various fields.

16214619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16214619.value: Regarding this research, we can consider further developments in the following areas: 1. Enhancing light extraction efficiency: Despite significant progress, there is still potential to further improve the light extraction efficiency of perovskite LEDs. This can be achieved by optimizing the design of the optical structures, improving material properties, and adjusting device fabrication processes. 2. Increasing external quantum efficiency: While some improvement in external quantum efficiency has already been achieved, there is room for further enhancement. By delving into the study of carrier transport, interface engineering, and band structure optimization of perovskite materials, we can further increase the external quantum efficiency and reduce non-radiative recombination losses. 3. Enhancing device stability: Device stability is an important consideration, especially under high brightness and long-term operation. Exploring new material synthesis methods, interface engineering strategies, and encapsulation techniques can improve the long-term stability and durability of perovskite LEDs. 4. Achieving large-scale device fabrication: To translate these research findings into practical applications, it is important to consider large-scale fabrication and industrial production of perovskite LEDs. Therefore, research and development of efficient and reliable fabrication processes, as well as exploration of device structures and processing methods suitable for large-scale production, are necessary. In summary, through further research and optimization in areas such as light extraction efficiency, external quantum efficiency, device stability, and large-scale fabrication, we can further advance the development of perovskite LED technology and realize its widespread applications in lighting, displays, and other fields.

16214619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16214619.value: In this project, we have explored the fabrication of nano-photonic structures to achieve an ultrahigh light extraction efficiency of over 90 %, which are porous aluminum oxides with optimized geometries. We have clarified the effect of pore diameters and pitches on the light extraction efficiency. Based on the optimized structures, we have fabricated perovskite light emitting films with ultrahigh PLQY of 92 %, where we have also explored material engineering and nanophotonic design by introducing 2D phase and quantum confinement for more efficient radiative recombination, and adding additives to passivate the defects. One step further, we have fabricated high-performance perovskite LEDs with high EQE, excellent up-scalability, and good flexibility. We have achieved full color (blue, sky-blue, green and pure-red) perovskite LEDs with EQE of 12.41%, 16.49%, 26.09% and 9.97%, respectively, based on solution-grown perovskite quantum wires in porous alumina membrane. We have also demonstrated the largest 4-inch wafer-scale perovskite LED device with excellent uniformity. The results of the project help researchers in the field to obtain a better understanding of nanophotonic structure design, and highly bright perovskite light emitting materials growth, as well as achievement of high-performance perovskite LED devices that will have great impact on the displays and lighting.

16215019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215019.value: Recommendation Systems (RSs) aim to recommend interesting items such as products and news to the user. Traditional RSs analyze users' access history to estimate their historical interests and recommend items that are relevant to their interests. This approach assumes that users would favor items that fit their interests, and hence clickthrough rate can be improved. However, the reality is that the user will quickly find the items too familiar and feel bored with them. Recent research on RSs has focused on recommending novel items to expand the user's interests. Although curiosity-based RSs have been shown to be effective in improving the novelty of recommendations, these systems suffer from two limitations. First, they do not consider the semantics of the items but only keywords and metatags extracted from the items. An item is considered novel when it is different from the user's previously accessed items. It is clear that keywords and metatags cannot represent contents and meanings. More importantly, an item cannot be both relevant and novel to the user because relevance requires similarity whereas novelty requires a difference between an item and the user's interest. In other words, relevance and novelty are conflicting parameters that requires a tradeoff. Second, traditional RSs do not consider the long-term goal of recommendations. Instead, they recommend items that are judged to be the best at the time of recommendation, without considering their utility in the future. To resolve these problems, we propose a novel recommendation paradigm called progressive recommendation. The novelty of our research is that we take a knowledge-centric viewpoint of RSs. That is, when an item is recommended, we are actually recommending the knowledge embedded in the item. As an item can be about multiple topics, some of which are relevant and some novel to the user, we can thus avoid the relevance-novelty conflict inherent in traditional RSs. Further, the proposed paradigm studies how a sequence of recommendations can help users in achieving some specific goals over a certain period, e.g., acquiring a specific set of knowledge about a topic. In the proposed project, we will investigate how relevance and curiosity metrics can be defined on a knowledge graph and explore recommendation strategies that can attract the user over the long run. Experiments and user studies will be conducted to evaluate the performance of various knowledge representation schemes, the corresponding metric definitions, and recommendation algorithms developed in the project. 推薦系統（RS）旨在向用戶推薦有趣的項目，例如產品和新聞等。傳統推薦系統會分析用戶的訪問記錄，以估計其過去的興趣並推薦與其興趣相關的項目。這種方法假設用戶喜歡符合他們興趣的項目，因此可以提高點擊率。然而，現實是用戶會很快發現他們對這些項目已很熟悉，並且對它們感到厭倦。最近對推薦系統的研究，主要集中在推薦新項目以擴大用戶的興趣。雖然基於好奇心的推薦系統已被證明可有效改善推薦的新穎性，但這些系統有兩個限制。首先，他們不考慮項目的語義，而只考慮從項目中提取的關鍵字和元標記。當項目與用戶先前訪問的項目不同時，該項目被認為是新穎的。很明顯，關鍵字和元標記不能代表內容和含義。更重要是，項目對於用戶來說不具有相關性和新穎性，因為相關性需要相似性，而新穎性需要項目與用戶興趣之間的差異。換句話說，相關性和新穎性是需要權衡的相互矛盾的參數。其次，傳統的推薦系統不考慮建議的長遠目標。相反，他們只考慮在推薦當下最佳的項目，而不考慮建議項目的長遠效用。為了解決這些問題，我們提出了一種稱為漸進式推薦的新型推薦範式。我們研究的新穎之處在於我們提出以知識為中心的觀點。也就是說，當推荐一個項目時，我們實際上是推薦項目中嵌入的知識。由於項目可以是關於多個主題，其中一些主題對用戶來說是相關的，而另外一些主題是新穎的，因此我們可以避免傳統推薦系統中固有的相關性 - 新穎性衝突。此外，我們研究如何產生一系列建議幫助用戶在一定時期內實現某些特定目標，例如，獲取關於主題的特定知識集。在擬議的項目中，我們將研究如何在知識圖上定義和度量相關性和好奇性，並探索可以長期吸引用戶的推薦策略。我們將進行實驗和用戶研究，以評估各種知識表示方案的性能，相應的度量定義以及項目中開發的推薦算法。

16215019.label: Realisation of objectives
16215019.value: We address the limitations of traditional Recommender System (RS) by introducing the notion of Influential Recommender System (IRS) [1]. The IRS proactively guide users towards liking specific objective items by incrementally recommending a selected sequence of items. We design multiple potential frameworks for tackling the IRS problem, covering path searching algorithms within graphs, adaptations of existing RS, and the proposed deep learning model, Influential Recommender Network (IRN) [1]. IRN is a sequential model based on Transformers, which adapts personalized strategies based on users’ historical interests and impressionability. We propose utilizing a simulated evaluator to assess user responses and introduce six performance metrics. These metrics consider both user satisfaction with the recommendations and the effectiveness in guiding users to the objective items seamlessly. This work addresses Objective 1 by designing the recommender’s architecture, Objective 2 by developing algorithms that recommend items based on the user’s reaction to the recommendation, and Objective 3 by conducting experiments to evaluate the performance. We explore advanced recommendation techniques to enhance model structures, knowledge representations, and recommendation strategies. In [1], we study the application of heterogeneous information network (HIN) to enhance Collaborative filtering (CF) based recommendation methods. It addresses challenges in capturing complex semantics and fusing information by using metagraphs for similarity computation and a "matrix factorization (MF) + factorization machine (FM)" framework. The work in [2] focuses on addressing scalability, sparsity, and cold start challenges in RSs using a flexible and scalable Side Information (SI) enhanced Skip-Gram (SISG) framework deployed at Taobao. We present a custom-built word2vec engine for training SISG, enabling the computation of item and SI embedding vectors on a billion-scale product set. These studies highlight the benefits of incorporating side information and leverage scalable embedding techniques for improved recommendation performance. . This work addresses Objective 1 by modelling the semantic of an application using HIN as the knowledge representation framework, Objective 2 by developing the recommendation algorithms, and Objective 3 by conducting experiments to evaluate the performance. To model diverse interests of users, we propose the Multi-Interest Network with Dynamic routing (MIND) approach [3], which represents a user with multiple vectors. MIND incorporates a multi-interest extractor layer based on capsule routing mechanism to cluster historical behaviors and extract diverse interests. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and a large-scale industrial dataset (Tmall) demonstrate the superior performance of MIND in modeling diverse user interests, particularly in industrial settings with large-scale user-item interactions. This work addresses Objective 1 by modelling user interests and representing them as multiple vectors, Objective 2 by developing the recommendation algorithms, and Objective 3 by conducting experiments using real data from Tmall, which was made possible by collaborating the Alibaba Research. We further study the importance of higher-order relations for more accurate and effective recommendations. In [4], we propose the use of motifs to capture higher-order relations in HIN and developing the motif-enhanced meta-path (MEMP) approach. We introduce a recommending model called MoHINRec, which utilizes MEMP-based similarities between users and items. This work addresses Objective 1 by modelling the application semantics as a HIN and capturing high-order relations with motifs, Objective 2 by developing the recommendation algorithms, and Objective 3 by conducting experiments to evaluate the performance. 16215019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215019.value: By comparing multiple progressive recommendation framework, we provide empirical evidence to assess the performance and impact of progressive recommendation. The experimental results demonstrate the superiority of IRN, indicating its effectiveness in influencing users' interests. Furthermore, case studies are conducted to gain insights into the evolving users’ interests. We analyze the actual recommendation sequence and provide a comprehensive evaluation of the progressive recommendation approach. We present a custom-built word2vec engine for training enhanced Side Information Skip-Gram SISG framework, enabling the computation of item and SI embedding vectors on a billion-scale product set. These studies highlight the benefits of incorporating side information and leverage scalable embedding techniques for improved recommendation performance. We further study the importance of higher-order relations for more accurate and effective recommendations and propose the use of motifs to capture higher-order relations in HIN and developing the motif-enhanced meta-path (MEMP) approach. We introduce a recommending model called MoHINRec, which utilizes MEMP-based similarities between users and items. We introduce motif-based PageRank (MPR), a framework that incorporates higher-order relations into the conventional PageRank algorithm.

16215019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215019.value: The progressive recommendation paradigm can be further developed through the following course of action: • Integration of contextual information: Combine contextual information such as user demographics information and item tags into the progressive recommendation system. This approach enables the system to provide more relevant recommendations that align with the user's interests and the objective. • Refinement of algorithm: While the current research primarily focuses on a single objective item, it is natural to extend the framework towards a fine-grained recommendation strategy catering to broader objectives, such as collections or topics. • Evaluation and user feedback: Deploy the progressive recommendation system on an real-life platform and conduct human evaluation to assess the performance and usability. Integrate Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) techniques to improve the user experience. • Continuous online learning: Design effective online learning algorithms for progressive recommendation system to incrementally update the model with flow data, enhancing its capability to evolving user interests and item dynamics.

16215019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215019.value: The research project focuses on improving recommendation systems, which are used in various applications like online shopping, advertising, and news websites. Most existing recommendation systems suggest items based on users' past interests, but they don't always show users new and interesting things they might like. The project developed a new approach called the progressive recommender system, which takes a proactive approach by guiding users to discover and like items they may not have known about before. The significance of this research is that it explores a novel aspect for recommendation systems. It studies how to expand users' interests and persuade them to try new things through the recommendation. By suggesting items they may not have discovered on their own, the system can increase user engagement and satisfaction. It benefits businesses by increasing customer interactions and potentially boosting sales. The study further explores more advanced and fine-grained techniques for general recommendation systems, aiming at improving the recommendation accuracy and user satisfaction.

16215119.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16215119.value: 延时(RTT)波动下的显式拥塞控制(ECN)研究

16215119.label: Project Objectives
16215119.value: Problem exploration: We will explore the problem of RTT variations in datacenters. First, we use testbed to emulate variable processing delay in the network, such as delay caused by kernel, hypervisor and middlebox. Our preliminary experiments show that a flow traversing those components can simply experience ∼3× RTT variation, leading to 119% longer tail latency for short flows according to current practice. Next, we will further understand this problem under larger-scale topologies with more real-world traffic patterns. ECN marking mechanism under high RTT variations: To solve the problem, we will propose ECN+, a simple yet effective solution to achieve both low latency and high throughput. At its heart, ECN+ marks packets based on both instantaneous and persistent congestion states. On the one hand, ECN+ inherits the advantage of current instantaneous ECN marking based on a high-percentile RTT to achieve high throughput and burst tolerance. On the other hand, to eliminate the persistent queueing caused by flows with small RTTs, ECN+ further marks packets when observing long-term queue buildups. Our preliminary simulation shows that ECN+ can effectively eliminate queue buildups by keeping the queue length 96% lower than that of the current solution (from 182 packets to 8 packets). Next, we will further validate the performance of ECN+ with large-scale comprehensive simulations. System implementation: We will implement ECN+ on the Barefoot Tofino programmable switch. We envision two main challenges in the implementation: 1) how to obtain the pre- cise system time for ECN+, and 2) how to update multiple switch states at line rate. In our proposal, we decide to emulate a 32-bit microsecond-granularity system time by storing and maintaining the high bits and low bits of time on two registers independently. We then lever- age match action tables to implement the complex control flow to update switch states at line rate. We will evaluate ECN+ using testbed experiments, and open-source our implementation.

16215119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215119.value: 显式拥塞控制（ECN）被广泛地应用于数据中心生产环境中来获得高吞吐和低时延的网络。虽然基于ECN的网络传输协议很成功，但是之前的方案都有一个显著的问题：在计算瞬时ECN标注阈值的时候，忽略了实际环境中的 RTT 波动，而是采用一个固定的 RTT 值来进行阈值计算。 在本项目中，我们通过实验指出，当前通用做法，使用一个固定的，高的 RTT 值（在RTT波动范围内）计算出的 ECN 阈值会在交换机上形成一个持续的队列，并严重影响网络的时延。例如，我们的实验数据表明，如果我们用 90th percentile 的RTT 计算得到的阈值（生产环境中的常见配置），可以获得一个高吞吐网络，但是小流的延迟因为队列而增加了119%。反过来，如果我们直接用一个低的 RTT 值计算得到的阈值则会造成吞吐量的损失。至今，现存的数据中心传输解决方案仍未全面地在它们的设计上考虑以上问题。 因此，本项目的目标是提出 ECN+，一种简单但是有效的方案，它可以在 RTT 存在较大波动的情况下同时使网络达到高吞吐和低时延。本项目将包含以下三部分： 1. 问题探索：我们将探索数据中心内的 RTT 波动问题。首先，我们用实验来模拟几种处理时延波动，比如由内核、虚拟化 hypervisor、middlebox 等组件造成的时延。初步实验数据表明，当流量通过以上这些组件，可以形成约3倍的 RTT 波动，在当前 ECN 机制下，小流会遭受119.2%的长尾延迟。其次，我们将会通过更大规模的拓扑，以及更加真实的数据流量，来进一步理解这些问题。 2. 在高 RTT 波动下的 ECN 标注策略：为了解决这个问题，我们将提出ECN+，一种简单但是有效的机制来同时实现高吞吐和低时延网络。从本质上而言，ECN +会同时根据瞬时和长期的拥塞情况来进行数据包标注。一方面，ECN+ 继承了当前基于瞬时拥塞情况标注 ECN 方案的优点，保证了高吞吐和突发流量容忍。另一方面，为了消除由小 RTT 流量造成的持续队列，ECN+ 将会进一步检测长期队列并进行ECN标注。我们初步的仿真实验结果表明，对比当前的方案，ECN+可以缩短96%的队列长度（从 182个数据包到 8个数据包）。接下来，我们会进一步通过更大规模的仿真来验证ECN+的性能。 3. 系统实现：我们将在Barefoot Tofino 系列可编程交换机上实现ECN+。我们在实现上主要面临两个挑战：1）如何获取精确的系统时间，以及2）如何线速更新交换机状态。我们提出的方案是，我们将会在两个独立的寄存器上手动存储并且维护时间的高位和低位，来模拟一个32位的微秒粒度的系统时间。同时，我们通过 match action 表，在线速前提下实现复杂的控制逻辑。我们将会通过真实的实验来评估ECN+，并在项目末期通过在线形式提供代码。

16215119.label: Realisation of objectives
16215119.value: We have realized all the 3 proposed objectives, our designed scheme is called ECN+. For the first objective, we have thoroughly explored the problem of RTT variations in datacenters. We observed that large RTT variations are common in datacenters as different flows traverse different processing components, e.g., network stack, hypervisor and middlebox. For example, compared to intra-service flows, inter-service flows experience large extra processing delays from the layer 4 load balancer. We used testbed experiments and large-scale simulations to emulate variable processing delay in the network, such as delay caused by kernel, hypervisor and middlebox. We found that a flow traversing those components can simply experience ~3× RTT variation, leading to 119% longer tail latency for short flows according to current practice. We further observed that existing solutions only adopt a fixed RTT value for ECN marking threshold calculation while over-looking RTT variations, which can cause severe problems. For example, operators get RTT distributions using tools such as PingMesh and in current practice they use a high percentile RTT (e.g., 90th percentile) to derive the threshold. While this approach can achieve high throughput for flows with different RTTs in general, for flows with small RTTs, it results in persistent queue buildups, causing queueing delay. On the other hand, directly using low percentile RTTs (e.g., 50%) or average RTT can mitigate such queueing latency, but cause flows with high RTTs to suffer from throughput degradation. We have used experiments to validate these problems. The summary is that: instantaneous ECN marking cannot deliver both high throughput and low queueing delay under RTT variations. The performance degrades more as the RTT variation grows. For the second objective, we have designed ECN+, a simple yet effective solution to address the RTT variation challenge as stated above. At its heart, ECN+ marks packets based on both the instantaneous and persistent congestion states. On the one hand, ECN inherits the advantage of current instantaneous ECN marking based on a high-percentile RTT to achieve high throughput and burst tolerance. On the other hand, to eliminate the persistent queueing caused by flows with small RTTs, ECN+ further marks packets when observing long-term switch queue buildups. This is performed conservatively in order not to affect throughput. The proposed ECN+ is essentially a new AQM solution. It marks packets based on both instantaneous and persistent congestion states. A packet is marked when either one of the following conditions decides to mark it: 1) when there is a large instantaneous queue, ECN+ aggressively marks packets to avoid buffer overflow; 2) when there is a persistent queue, ECN+ conservatively marks packets to reduce queueing delay. We further discussed why ECN+ can achieve desired performance. 1) High throughput & low queueing delay: Instead of directly using a low instantaneous ECN marking threshold to aggressively bring down the buffer occupancy at the cost of throughput loss, ECN+ uses a more conservative mechanism. By tracking the minimal queueing over a time interval, ECN+ only marks packets after it determines persistent queue buildups. These queue buildups are caused by providing excessive buffer space for flows with small RTTs, which do not contribute to the throughput but only increase the queueing delay. Eliminating these queues can benefit latency-sensitive short flows without throughput degradation. We carefully choose the interval to be around one worst case base RTT because TCP needs one RTT to react to ECN marking. Furthermore, the marking itself is conducted in a conservative way to mitigate throughput loss. Only after detecting persistent queue buildups, ECN+ marks one packet and schedules next marking after an interval. Afterwards, ECN+ checks again to see whether the queue expires or not. If not, ECN+ increases the marking frequency by reducing the interval. Through both persistent queueing detection and conservative ECN marking, ECN can achieve both high throughput and low queueing delay simultaneously. 2) Burst tolerance: ECN+ leverages the instantaneous ECN marking to achieve good burst tolerance. As discussed above, the instantaneous marking scheme enables fast response to bursty traffic, such as incast. Once the queue exceeds the threshold, it aggressively marks the packets to tame the subsequent bursts from senders and bring down the buffer usage. This scheme ensures a upper bound of buffer occupancy to avoid packet loss. Furthermore, ECN+’s instantaneous marking threshold is derived base on a high percentile RTT, which provides sufficient buffer without causing throughput loss. For the third objective, we have implemented an ECN+ prototype in the egress pipeline of Barefoot Tofino switch. ECN+ is essentially a stateful data plane algorithm as the per-packet processing involves updates of multiple switch states. Our implementation has around 500 lines of P4 code and is compiled to Barefoot Tofino switch using Barefoot Capilano SDE 6.1.1. In our implementation, we use 7 match action tables in total. The number of table entries is less than 10 (most of match action tables use default actions, so no entry is needed explicitly). To store switch updates on all the 128 ports, we use 5 32-bit register arrays and 2 64-bit register arrays. The register memory consumption is only ~37KB. Each packet needs 124-bit metadata. Our ECN+ prototype only uses little switch resource, leaving more for other network functions. We have met and successfully addressed two main challenges in our implementation: 1) how to obtain the precise system time, and 2) how to update multiple switch states at line rate. In our evaluation, we have conducted both extensive testbed experiments and ns-3 simulations to answer the following questions: 1) How does ECN+ perform in practice? Our testbed experiment results show that compared with current practice, ECN+ achieves up to 23.4% smaller average FCT and 31.2% smaller 99th percentile FCT for small flows while providing the similar performance for large flows. ECN+’s good burst control makes it largely outperform CoDel. 2) Does ECN+ scale to large datacenters? We evaluate the performance of ECN+ using large scale ns-3 simulations. Results show that ECN+ achieves up to 36.9% smaller FCT for small flows compared to current practice. 3) How does ECN+ control the queue length and react to bursty traffic? We evaluate ECN+ using simulations mixing both the background traffic and bursty query traffic. We find that compared to current practice, ECN+ keeps a much smaller average queue occupancy (182 packets to 8 packets). By changing the fanout of the incast traffic, we further show that compared to CoDel, ECN+ can support 1.75x more concurrent senders without TCP timeouts. 4) How robust is ECN+ to network settings? Through targeted simulations, we show that ECN+ is robust to parameter choices and the packet scheduler.

Our preliminary experiments show that a flow traversing those components can simply experience ∼3× RTT variation, leading to 119% longer tail latency for short flows according to current practice. Next, we will further understand this problem under larger-scale topologies with more real-world traffic patterns.

ECN marking mechanism under high RTT variations: To solve the problem, we will propose ECN+, a simple yet effective solution to achieve both low latency and high throughput. At its heart, ECN+ marks packets based on both instantaneous and persistent congestion states. On the one hand, ECN+ inherits the advantage of current instantaneous ECN marking based on a high-percentile RTT to achieve high throughput and burst tolerance. On the other hand, to eliminate the persistent queueing caused by flows with small RTTs, ECN+ further marks packets when observing long-term queue buildups. Our preliminary simulation shows that ECN+ can effectively eliminate queue buildups by keeping the queue length 96% lower than that of the current solution (from 182 packets to 8 packets). Next, we will further validate the performance of ECN+ with large-scale comprehensive simulations.

System implementation: We will implement ECN+ on the Barefoot Tofino programmable switch. We envision two main challenges in the implementation: 1) how to obtain the precise system time for ECN+, and 2) how to update multiple switch states at line rate. In our proposal, we decide to emulate a 32-bit microsecond-granularity system time by storing and maintaining the high bits and low bits of time on two registers independently. We then leverage match action tables to implement the complex control flow to update switch states at line rate. We will evaluate ECN+ using testbed experiments, and open-source our implementation.

16215119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215119.value: The major finding and the first contribution of this project is that we are among the first to reveal the non-trivial RTT variations in datacenters, their root-causes, as well as the performance degradation they incur to the current transport protocols. ECN has been widely employed in production datacenters to deliver high throughput low latency communications. However, existing ECN-based transport protocols have an important drawback: they adopt a fixed RTT value in calculating instantaneous ECN marking threshold while overlooking the RTT variations in practice. Along with our finding, we show that the current practice of using a fixed high-percentile RTT for ECN threshold calculation can lead to persistent queue buildups, significantly increasing packet latency. Meanwhile, we also show that directly adopting lower percentile RTTs results in throughput degradation. The second contribution of this project is that we have designed ECN+, a simple yet very effective solution to enable ECN for RTT variations. At its core of ECN+, we inherit the idea of the current instantaneous ECN marking (which is based on a high-percentile RTT) to achieve high throughput and burst tolerance, while further marking packets conservatively upon detecting long-term queue buildups to eliminate unnecessary queueing delay without degrading the throughput. As the third contribution of this project, we implement an ECN prototype with ~500 lines of P4 code and compile it to a Barefoot Tofino switch using Barefoot Capilano SDE. Our implementation uses little switch resource, e.g., 5 32-bit register arrays and 2 64-bit register arrays. We address two practical challenges in the implementation: 1) To ensure the correctness, we use emulation to get a 32-bit microsecond- granularity system time; 2) To update switch states at line rate, we leverage match action tables to implement the complex control flow. We then further build a 10Gbps testbed with 8 servers connected to the above Tofino switch. Our experiments with realistic workloads show that, by eliminating persistent queue buildups, ECN can deliver up to 23.4% lower average FCT and 31.2% lower 99th percentile FCT for short flows compared to DCTCP-RED (where the ECN marking threshold is based on a high-percentile RTT according to current practice) while still maintaining comparable throughput for large flows. We also have performed simulations to validate our design at large-scale. Overall, this project leads to top-tier papers published in CoNEXT, SIGCOMM, NSDI, INFOCOM, IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking and Cloud Computing, etc.

16215119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215119.value: The design of ECN+ can be incorporated into switching ASIC as a new AQM solution, which marks packets based on both instantaneous and persistent congestion states. This can effectively solve the RTT variation issue which is common in production datacenter networks. In our future work, we plan to investigate how to practically implement ECN+ in switches and adopt the proposed ECN+ framework in production datacenter network environment to tackle the real-world RTT variation problem.

16215119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215119.value: This project has presented ECN+ a simple yet effective solution that enables ECN in datacenters with high RTT variations. ECN+ marks packets based on both instantaneous and persistent congestion states. It inherits the merit of current instantaneous ECN marking based on a high-percentile RTT to achieve high throughput and burst tolerance, and further marks packets when observing long-term switch queue buildups to eliminate the persistent queueing caused by flows with smaller RTTs. We have implemented ECN+ on a Barefoot Tofino switch and evaluated it through both testbed experiments and ns-3 simulations. Our evaluation shows that ECN+ is a viable solution that achieves all our design goals. Overall, ECN+ is readily deployable and has potential to be adopted in production datacenter network environment to handle the real-world RTT variation issue.

16215319.label: Project Objectives
16215319.value: We will develop an automatic tool to trace the congestion metrics back from the physical level to the HLS IR operations and link them with the source code. Using this flow, we will aim to identify effective high-level features for congestion prediction. We will implement a real-world benchmark suite for FPGA HLS designs, which can be used to construct our dataset for training, while considering different code structures to enhance the generality of the prediction model. We will identify several informative categories of features and select the most important features to improve training efficiency. We will construct multiple promising machine learning models and investigate their trade-offs to select the most suitable one for an application with a specific code structure. To improve estimation accuracy, we will apply several machine learning optimization techniques, such as parameter tuning and data pre-processing. With our trained model, the highly congested parts of the source code can be detected accurately, and we will develop congestion mitigation methods and an integrated flow to optimize the automatic source code and HLS directive to reduce congestion and minimize the total delay.

16215319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215319.value: With the rapidly increasing demands for computing capability, field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) are increasingly used as hardware accelerators to implement various tasks due to their advantages of low power and massive parallelism. To satisfy the large demand for FPGA-based designs and to shorten the development cycle, high-level synthesis (HLS) has become a promising alternative to register-transfer level (RTL) designs due to its higher productivity. HLS speeds up FPGA-based designs and enables faster design space exploration at a higher level of abstraction. However, optimizing complex designs in HLS is challenging because some implementation issues are hard to address. One critical problem is routing congestion, which can detour the critical path and degrade design performance significantly. Previous research has mainly focused on estimating routability for RTL designs. In existing HLS design tools for FPGAs, estimation of routing congestion at the source level is absent or highly inaccurate because it is difficult to evaluate the routability in HLS without analyzing the physical information after place and route (PAR), which takes a long time. Moreover, even when the physical metrics are available, it is not easy to trace congestion back to the high-level code. However, it is beneficial to provide an early congestion prediction to guide the optimization of HLS for efficient implementation. Hence, to address this challenge, we propose a novel approach to estimate routing congestion using machine learning at the source-code level with fast speed and high accuracy. This should greatly benefit the early identification of routability-oriented bottlenecks in high-level source code without repetitively running the time-consuming RTL implementation flow. This proposal will contribute to the routing congestion estimation and mitigation in HLS from the following perspectives: (1) implementing an automatic back-tracing flow to build the relationship between congestion metrics after PAR and operations in the intermediate representation (IR) in HLS and the source code; (2) extract related features from IR and develop dataset for the prediction model construction and training in the next step; (3) developing machine learning models for routing congestion prediction with fast speed and high accuracy; (4) proposing a series of effective solutions that can efficiently mitigate routing congestion in HLS design. With this proposal, we aim to not only more accurately and conveniently predict congestion at the source-code level without repetitively running RAR, but also provide effective solutions to mitigate the congestion automatically and significantly improve the design performance. 隨著對計算能力的需求的快速增長，現場可編程門陣列（FPGA）由於其低功率和大規模並行性的優點而越來越多地用作硬件加速器以實現各種任務。為了滿足對基於FPGA的設計的大量需求並縮短開發週期，高級綜合（HLS）由於其更高的生產率已成為寄存器傳輸級（RTL）設計的有前途的替代方案。 HLS加速了基於FPGA的設計，並在更高的抽象級別上實現了更快的設計空間探索。但是，在HLS中優化複雜設計具有挑戰性，因為一些實施問題很難解決。一個關鍵問題是路由擁塞，它可以使關鍵路徑延長並顯著降低設計性能。以前的研究主要集中在估算RTL設計的路由佈局可行性。在現有的用於FPGA的HLS設計工具中，源碼級別的路由擁塞估計工具不存在或者非常不准確，因為很難在不分析佈局佈線（PAR）之後的物理信息的情況下評估HLS中的可佈線性，這需要很長時間。此外，即使物理指標可用，也很難將擁塞追溯到高級代碼。然而，提供早期擁塞預測以指導HLS的優化以用於有效實現是有益的。因此，為了應對這一挑戰，我們提出了一種新方法，使用源代碼級別的機器學習以快速和高精度估計路由擁塞。這將極大地有利於早期識別高級源代碼中面向路由可佈線性的瓶頸，而無需重複運行耗時的RTL實現流程。 該提議將從以下角度為HLS中的路由擁塞估計和緩解做出貢獻：（1）實現自動反向跟踪流，以構建PAR之後的擁塞度量與HLS中的中間表示（IR）中的操作之間以及源代碼的關係; （2）從IR中提取相關特徵，並為下一步的預測模型構建和訓練開發數據集; （3）開發快速，高精度的路由擁塞預測機器學習模型; （4）提出一系列有效的解決方案，可以有效緩解HLS設計中的路由擁塞。通過該提議，我們不僅可以更準確，更方便地預測源代碼級別的擁塞，而無需重複運行RAR，還可以提供有效的解決方案來自動緩解擁塞並顯著提高設計性能。

16215319.label: Realisation of objectives
16215319.value: The four objectives have been successfully achieved. We have developed a novel tool to predict routing congestion in HLS using machine learning and map the expected congested regions in the design to the relevant high-level source code. We have also developed several real benchmarks to evaluate the performance of the tool. Experiments demonstrate that our approach accurately estimates vertical and horizontal routing congestion with errors of 6.71% and 10.05% respectively. By presenting Face Detection application as a case study, we show that by discovering the bottlenecks in high-level source code, routing congestion can be easily and quickly resolved compared to the efforts involved in RTL level implementation and design feedback. We also extended it to cross-layer consideration of HLS and P&R stages to optimize the placement quality of HLS generated RTL design, which will greatly facilitate the later routing stage, for large designs using multi-die FPGA. To co-optimize the directives and floorplan of HLS designs on multi-die FPGAs, we propose the FADO framework, which formulates the directive-floorplan co-search problem based on the multi-choice multi-dimensional bin-packing and solves it using an iterative optimization flow. For each step of directive optimization, a latency-bottleneck-guided greedy algorithm searches for more efficient directive configurations. For floorplanning, instead of repetitively incurring global floorplanning algorithms, we implement a more efficient incremental floorplan legalization algorithm. Through experiments on a set of HLS designs mixing dataflow and non-dataflow kernels, FADO not only well-automates the co-optimization and finishes within 693X∼4925X shorter runtime, compared with DSE assisted by global floor-planning, but also yields an improvement of 1.16X∼8.78X in overall workflow execution time after implementation on the Xilinx Alveo U250 FPGA. A further extended work has focused on the placement on heterogeneous FPGAs. To enable the performance optimization of application mapping on FPGAs, certain critical path portions of the designs might be prearranged into many multi-cell macros during synthesis. These movable macros with constraints of shape and resources lead to challenging mixed-size placement for FPGA designs which cannot be addressed by previous works of analytical placers. We propose AMF-Placer, an open-source Analytical Mixed-size FPGA placer supporting mixed-size placement on FPGA, with an interface to Xilinx Vivado. To speed up the convergence and improve the quality of the placement, AMF-Placer is equipped with a series of new techniques for wirelength optimization, cell spreading, packing, and legalization. Based on a set of the latest large open-source benchmarks from various domains for Xilinx Ultrascale FPGAs, experimental results indicate that AMF-Placer can improve HPWL by 20.4%- 89.3% and reduce runtime by 8.0%-84.2%, compared to the baseline. This placement improvement will in turn greatly ease the routing congestion problem.

16215319.label: Major findings and research outcome
16215319.value: In this project, we have considered different methods to improve the routing congestion mitigation for HLS based designs on various FPGA devices, which include routing congestion prediction and mitigation, floor-plan aware HLS design to co-optimize HLS directives and floorplan, analytical placement for heterogenous FPGAs. We have developed three open-source tools, corresponding to the three optimization methods and published 4 papers in top venues of conferences and journals. The placement & routing stage is the most time-consuming stage of FPGA or ASIC designs. We found some optimizations on high-level designs may not lead to good results in the later P&R stages. It would be better to consider both high-level HLS optimization and P&R together. Hence, we have made the HLS P&R aware. Currently, we considered routing-aware for the congestion estimation in one sub-project and floorplan/placement aware in some other sub-project. Both works have achieved significant performance improvement compared to pure HLS designs. It would be best to combine these two, however, it may require longer optimization time. We leave it to the future works to further address it.

16215319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16215319.value: There are several directions the future work can further develop as the following: (1) Targeting larger design, such as multi-die FPGA or even multi-FPGAs, then problem becomes partition between multiple FPGAs and placement in single-FPGA, which gives new challenges; (2) Currently, we consider the routing congestion only, it would be better to consider the performance during routing stage even in the non-congestion situation. (3) As mentioned in the last section, it would be also better to take both P&R into consideration with HLS, which could lead to more performance improvement.

16215319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16215319.value: HLS based design is from C language describing the specification at the high level. So it cannot predict the impact from the later P&R synthesis stages. Since the final design is generated after P&R, HLS level optimization may get lost during P&R, or even lead to worse results. Hence, to generate a better final synthesized design, it would require considering the P&R impact in the HLS design. In this project, we tried to take the P&R into consideration to improve the final design quality. In some sub-projects, we estimate the routing congestion and feedback to the HLS design to make it routing-aware. In some other sub-projects, we perform the HLS-floorplan/placement co-designs to make the HLS design placement-aware. Significant improvements have been achieved compared to pure HLS designs without P&R consideration. The work can be further extended along the direction listed in 6.2.

16215519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16215519.value: Strain hardening cementitious composites (SHCC) are fiber reinforced materials exhibiting tensile strain hardening behavior up to a strain level of 3-6%, which gives rise to high deformation and energy absorption capabilities in structural applications. Under short-term loading, tensile failure is accompanied by the formation of multiple cracks with opening controlled to below 50 microns. Such fine cracks have little effect on water and chemical transport into the material. Moreover, for cracks with opening below around 100 microns, self-healing can occur in the presence of water. In conventional reinforced concrete structures, the crack opening is often beyond 0.15-0.20mm, which greatly accelerates water and chemical penetration. The strategic use of SHCC (e.g., as a permanent formwork or the surface layer of a structural component) therefore has great potential to improve the durability of concrete structures. However, the adoption of SHCC in durability design is still hampered by a major concern – in laboratory creep tests, crack width has been shown to increase significantly beyond the short-term value to harmful levels. In these tests, the member is allowed to deform without limit under constant loading, which is different from the situation of real-world members where the deflection (and deformation) at serviceability is limited by design codes. The proposed study aims to understand the crack development in SHCC in practical situations. Focus will be placed on SHCC used in permanent formwork or as the cover layer of a reinforced concrete beam. The experimental part of the study will involve the development of a new testing set-up to study the development of strain, crack number and crack opening in SHCC under very slow strain increase similar to the situation of a real-world structural member under creep. An engineering approach will then be developed to generalize the limited testing results to situations with different strain versus time histories. The derived tensile behavior will be fitted with an equivalent truss and interface model for the analysis of distributed cracking in SHCC. With this model, finite element analysis will be carried out on beams with an SHCC surface layer. The number and opening of cracks at various strain levels will be compared with test results for corresponding members. The successful completion of the project will generate new experimental data to enhance the current state of knowledge on the creep behavior of SHCC under realistic conditions, and provide an engineering approach for predicting long-term crack width in practical situations 應變硬化水泥基複合材料(SHCC)是一種纖維增強材料，通過拉伸應變硬化， 其極限應變可高達3-6%，從而在結構應用中產生大變形和高能量吸收的效果。該材料在短期荷載作用下，拉伸破壞時會有多條裂縫形成，它們的寬度可以控制在50微米以下。這些微裂縫幾乎不影響水和化學物質在該材料中的傳輸，況且，當裂縫寬度小於100微米並有水存在時，該材料可自我修復。而在傳統的鋼筋混凝土結構中，裂縫寬度往往大於0.15-0.20 毫米，這會極大地促進水和化學物質的滲透。因此，SHCC的針對性應用（例如作為永久性模板，或用於一些結構構件的表層）在提高混凝土結構的耐久性上有很大的潛力。然而，若要將SHCC考慮到耐久性設計中，尚有一定的困難，在實驗室條件下對SHCC進行的徐變測試顯示，其裂縫寬度遠大於短期荷載下的寬度，對耐久性有明顯的負面作用。在這些試驗中，構件可在常荷載下無限度變形，而實際情況下，設計標準的正常使用極限狀態則會限制構件的撓度（和變形）。 本研究計劃以理解SHCC在實際荷載情況下的裂縫發展為目的，針對用於鋼筋混凝土樑的永久性模板及用於其表層的SHCC。該研究的實驗部分將包括一種新的測試方案，用於探究在與實際徐變作用相類似的低應變增長速率下，SHCC的應變、裂縫數量和寬度的發展。接著建立一個工程方法，利用少量的測試數據，預測不同的應變歷史下的結果。為研究SHCC的多縫開裂，上述方法得到的拉伸性能可用一個等價的桁架-界面模型來擬合，從而可對SHCC覆面的梁構件進行有限元分析。最後，分析得到的不同應變下的裂縫數量和寬度可與相應構件的試驗結果作比較驗證。 本研究項目的完成可提供新的實驗數據，以深化對SHCC在實際情況下的徐變性能的認識，並且為預測實際應用中的長期裂縫寬度提供一種有效的工程方法。

16216119.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16216119.value: 使用统计转移学习技术进行轮廓监测和诊断

16216119.label: Project Objectives
16216119.value: To devise a novel Phase I modeling procedure for profiles at the start-up stage. Ancillary and target sources of profiles will be combined for an accurate estimation of in-control parameters and effective identification of sparse anomaly patterns. To implement efficient monitoring and surveillance of target profiles. We will utilize the interrelationship among various sources via a joint Bayesian prior distribution and will provide a systematic online updating scheme for the target profile parameters. To conduct post-signal diagnosis when shifts in key parameters are detected. We will adopt statistical transfer learning techniques to connect information from multiple sources for enhanced inference of the possible root cause of out-of-control scenarios.

16216119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16216119.value: With the recent progress in sensing and information technologies, automatic data acquisition is now frequently deployed in manufacturing and service processes, where multiple profiles are generated from various sources of sensors. Traditional profile monitoring techniques cannot monitor and diagnose such processes effectively in real-time due to their high variability and variety. This limitation poses new challenges and opportunities in improving the performance of conventional profile monitoring techniques when applied to data streams from various sources. To fully utilize the data characteristics, we propose to construct novel profile monitoring techniques under the statistical transfer learning framework, which enables knowledge transfer from ancillary profiles to improve the performance in the target profiles. The proposed research project aims to apply statistical transfer learning techniques to three stages of profile monitoring, namely, (1) Phase I modeling of profiles at the start-up stage, (2) Phase II online monitoring of profiles, and (3) post-signal diagnosis in profile monitoring. The essential idea of the proposed research is to establish statistical models and methodologies in a transfer learning framework to implement effective and efficient monitoring and diagnosis of profiles with high variability and variety. 随着传感和信息技术的最新进展，自动数据采集经常被部署在制造和服务过程中，其已从各种传感器源生成大量轮廓数据 (profiles)。传统的轮廓监测技术由于其高度可变性和多样性，无法实时有效地监测和诊断这些过程。当应用来自各种来源的数据流时，这为改进传统轮廓监视技术的性能带来了新的挑战和机会。为了充分利用数据特征，我们建议在统计转移学习框架下构建新颖的轮廓监测技术，该技术框架使得能够从辅助轮廓转移知识以改善目标轮廓中的性能。拟议的研究项目旨在将统计转移学习技术应用于三个阶段的轮廓监测：（1）启动阶段的第一阶段轮廓建模; （2）第二阶段在线轮廓监测; （3）轮廓监测中的信号后诊断。拟议研究的基本思想是在转移学习框架中建立统计模型和方法，以便对高变异性和多样性的轮廓数据实施有效和高效的监测和诊断。

16216119.label: Realisation of objectives
16216119.value: Our research project, "Profile monitoring and diagnosis using statistical transfer learning techniques," has effectively accomplished all the proposed objectives, which we segmented into three primary stages. For the first Objective, we developed a unique Phase I modeling procedure for profiles at the start-up stage. We combined both ancillary and target sources of profiles, which allowed us to estimate in control parameters accurately and identify sparse anomaly patterns effectively. Our novel self-starting process monitoring scheme based on transfer learning was published. We also presented a hybrid transfer learning scheme for cold-start data anomaly detection. Furthermore, we derived theoretical results for optimal sequential tests, focusing on monitoring changes in finite observation sequence distributions. The second objective of our research involved efficient monitoring and surveillance of target profiles. We established a systematic online update scheme for target profile parameters by leveraging the interrelationship among various sources through a joint Bayesian prior distribution. We also introduced an early-stage stationary data stream distribution inference scheme via transfer learning. Our team made significant strides in application-focused research, especially in Metro systems passenger flow monitoring. Notably, we conducted a robust multivariate functional principal component analysis for passenger flow pattern discovery, and a nonparametric passenger flow monitoring scheme. In the final research objective, we focused on post-signal diagnosis upon the detection of key parameter shifts. We utilized statistical transfer learning techniques to correlate information from multiple sources, enhancing the inference of potential root causes in out-of-control scenarios. Our unified framework for fast detection and accurate diagnosis was published. We also developed a real-time monitoring and diagnosis scheme for IoT-enabled devices. Our research also encompassed root-cause and passenger pattern analysis in Metro systems leading to the publication of a multi-clustering study and a community detection approach for multi-view clustering. Overall, we achieved our research project’s objectives, making significant contributions to both theoretical and practical aspects of statistical transfer learning, quality control, and monitoring. Our findings have broad implications, offering potential advancements in various fields and applications.

16216119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16216119.value: We made significant strides in three main areas: model development, efficient monitoring, and post-signal diagnosis. During the model development phase, we devised a novel Phase I modeling process for start-up stage profiles. Leveraging a combination of ancillary and target sources, we accurately estimated in control parameters and identified sparse anomaly patterns. Our innovative self-starting process monitoring scheme and hybrid transfer learning scheme for cold-start data anomaly detection were published in Wang, et al. (JQT 2022) "Journal Paper #7" and Li, et al. (TKDD 2022) "Journal Paper #10" respectively. We also derived optimal sequential tests' theoretical results (Han, et al., Statistica Sinica, 2022)"Journal Paper #3". In the efficient monitoring phase, we utilized the interrelationship among various sources through a joint Bayesian prior distribution. This allowed us to create a systematic online updating scheme for target profile parameters. A significant outcome was the development of an inference scheme for early-stage stationary data streams via transfer learning (Wang, et al., IISE Trans., 2022) "Journal Paper #4". Application-focused research advancements were made in Metro systems passenger flow monitoring, resulting in a robust multivariate functional principal component analysis (Wang, et al., IEEE Trans. ITS, 2022) "Journal Paper #6" and a nonparametric passenger flow monitoring scheme (Li, et al., IISE Trans., 2022) "Journal Paper #11". The final phase focused on post-signal diagnosis. We employed statistical transfer learning techniques to enhance inference accuracy of potential root causes in out-of-control scenarios. Our unified framework for fast detection and accurate diagnosis was published in Li et al., (IEEE Trans. Cybernetics, 2022) "Journal Paper #5", and a real-time monitoring and diagnosis scheme for IoT-enabled devices was presented in Wu et al., (IISE Trans., 2022) "Journal Paper #8". Additionally, we analyzed individualized passenger travel pattern multi-clustering (Li et al., DMKD, 2022) "Journal Paper #9" and applied a functional data-edged network community detection approach for multi-view Metro station clustering (Zheng, et al., DMKD, 2022) "Journal Paper #12". In conclusion, our research has successfully bridged theoretical advancements and practical applications, contributing to the field of statistical transfer learning, quality control, and monitoring.

16216119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16216119.value: The successful completion and accomplishments of our project has opened up numerous avenues for future research, particularly in the realm of process monitoring and diagnosis. Our next steps include deepening our understanding of the nuances and complexities of real-time profile monitoring and diagnosis. We plan to refine our existing models and develop more sophisticated algorithms capable of handling larger and more diverse data sets. Given the vast and ever-growing data landscape in today's digital age, this work will be vital in pushing the boundaries of what statistical transfer learning can achieve. Moreover, we envisage expanding the application of our research to more complex and dynamic systems beyond manufacturing and service processes. Potential areas could include advanced manufacturing systems, complex supply chains, or even large-scale IoT systems, where real-time monitoring and diagnosis are paramount. The proposed course of action is to secure funding for these future research initiatives and to foster collaborations with both academic and industry partners. This will enable us to leverage collective expertise and resources, driving further innovation and advancements in the field of statistical transfer learning.

16216119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16216119.value: In today's digital age, we generate massive amounts of data every moment, particularly in sectors like manufacturing. Imagine a bustling factory where numerous machines, each outfitted with various sensors, create constant streams of data or "profiles." Monitoring these data streams in real-time can be challenging due to their high variability and diversity. Traditional techniques often struggle to keep up, and that's where our research project comes in. We're working on a new approach called "statistical transfer learning" to improve how we handle this data deluge. If you imagine the data as students learning a complex subject, transfer learning is like a knowledgeable tutor helping the students understand better and learn faster. Our research project applies this concept to data, using information from some data profiles to help us understand and interpret others more effectively. We're focusing on three major stages: setting up the initial models, real-time monitoring, and diagnosing any unusual signals. By creating and implementing new statistical models within this transfer learning framework, we aim to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of data monitoring, potentially leading to significant advancements in how we manage and understand the vast amounts of data in our interconnected world.

16300119.label: Project Objectives
16300119.value: Set up the moduli of MSP fields for Landau Ginzburg space of Fermat type singularities, its properness and its cosection localized virtual cycles. For the moduli in 1, establish its torus localization formula; namely to obtain contributions to the virtual normal factors from each part of localization graphs. Using the Picard Fuchs equation to obtain I functions for the corresponding theory, and also its S functions by using Birkhoff factorization. Derive the algorithm for (localization) R matrices from the S functions. Obtain cohomological field theory description of the dual twisted FJRW theory in terms of pure FJRW theory. Obtain this second R matrix from the corresponding Grothendieck Riemann Roch theorem. Compose the two R matrix action in 3 and 4. Evaluate the two point functions to obtain propagators of the theory. Package the FJRW theory and point theory. Use the polynomiality of total MSP correlators, to deduce polynomiality of the FJRW correlators for Fermat singularities. For this we need an asymptotic approximation via oscillating integrals (as that did in quintic case). Use Feymann integral methods to reduce the additional type's propagators as like in quintic case. This will result in a Feynman graph sum structure of FJRW generating functions.

16300119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300119.value: The subject of ``enumerative geometry" counting geometry object in a compact variety. Recently it is realized the counting in a noncompact variety gives more fundamental aspect. A large cases of such counting is now called Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten(FJRW) invariants. The calculating method for FJRW invariants is under development. In this project, we propose to a method to package FJRW invariants for Fermat type singularities. Our method would be using a mixture of spin fielsd with P fields. “計數幾何”這門幾何分支專門研究幾何物件的個數問題. 本身是Landau-Ginzburg類的弦理論 的一個分支. 近年 一個新的觀點是分緊空間中的計數問題通常是更具本質的研究對象. 很著名的一個例子是 Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten(FJRW)不變量. 現階段 FJRW不變量並沒有很好的計算方法. 在這個計畫裡, 我們將發展一套方法來計算並且整合 ”費馬奇異點“ 的FJRW 不變量. 我們計畫使旋場以及Ｐ場合併得到的混合場來達成目標.

16300119.label: Realisation of objectives
16300119.value: All the objectives are verified for CY singularity of fermat type. For the 1st objective we set up a moduli of MSP field for fermat type LG singularities and establish its properness, with its enumerative theory. For the 2nd and 3rd objective we spell out all localization factor into explicit formulas. And we obtain their R matrices and S functions. The 4th objective has been modified into a partial cohomological field theory that enables the further objective to be accomplished. The R matrices mentioned in the 5th objective has been evaluated and its close formula has been found. Combined 1st-5th objectives and using oscillating integrals, we finish the proof of the polynomiality of total MSP correlators and that of Landau Ginzburg theories for Fermat singularities. An argument refining the graph sum is also obtained to give Feynman graph sum structure for affine Landau Ginzburg (fjrw) counting theory.

16300119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300119.value: We found that for quintic Fermat singularity the polynomiality structure conjecture, BCOV Feynman structure, analyticity conjecture are all true. This discovery is never proved in any literatures and it is historically the first complete verification for Landau Ginzburg theory's all genus structures. These results final version is under preparation in the paper "Mixed Spin P fields for singularity" and "BCOV FOR LG MODEL". However, the methods to achieve them are highly adapted from previous works in the paper "BCOV Feynman rule of quintic 3folds", under review by the journal "Duke" and Polynomial structure of Gromov-Witten potential of quintic 3-folds published in Annals of Mathematics and An effective theory of GW and FJRW invariants of quintics Calabi–Yau manifolds, published in Journal of Differential Geometry.

16300119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300119.value: Our result should be extendable to non Fermat singularity's theory of one kaehler parameter. The method we adopt and the special treatment in this phase of Mixed Spin P fields moduli can be great experience in future task on all type singularity's problem. Due to the nature that singularity theories has more fruitful relations to matrix model and mirror symmetry, we expect our discovery will have continuing interactions with such two other disciplines, and possibly lead to partial matrix model of singularities and geometric approach to high genus mirror symmetry for singularities.

16300119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300119.value: The theory of singularities has been the origin of enumerative geometry and mirror symmetry for the past thirty years, while the structure of higher-genus invariants is one of the key concerns in both mathematical physics and enumerative geometry. Our work provides the first verification of the Feynman structure of higher-genus invariants in singularities. The method of verification is universal and can naturally be applied to a large variety of other types of singularities. Furthermore, the theoretical results from this singularity perfectly match the long-established BCOV Feynman structure in A-type topological string theory on Calabi-Yau compactifications. This once again reveals the correctness of higher-genus string theory phase transitions and affirms the geometric validity of the Mixed-Spin-P Field theory we employed in proving this result under both phases.

16300919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16300919.value: Linear codes have wide applications in communication systems, computer systems, data storage systems, and consumer electronics. They are related to many areas of mathematics such as algebra, algebraic geometry, algebraic function fields, algebraic number theory, association schemes, combinatorics, finite fields, finite geometry, graph theory, and group theory. An important but challenging problem in the theory and application of coding theory is the construction of optimal linear codes and linear codes with very good parameters. Recently, the subfield code approach has demonstrated huge promise in constructing optimal linear codes and linear codes with very good parameters. However, little work has been conducted on this approach in the literature. The first objective of this project is to construct optimal linear codes and linear codes with very good parameters using the subfield code approach. The second objective is to study the properties of the subfield codes obtained in this project. Outcomes of this project would enhance coding theory and have applications in engineering. 線性碼在通信系統，計算機系統，數據存儲系統和電子消費品中有廣泛的應用。線性碼與數學的許多分支有密切的關系， 例如，代數，代數幾何，代數函數域，代數數論，結合方案，組合設計，有限域，有限集合，圖論和群論。 構造好參數的或者最優線性碼是編碼學理論及其應用的一個很重要但具有挑戰性的問題。最近的初步研究証明了子域碼方法是構造好參數的或者最優線性碼的好途徑。但是，目前這個方向的研究工作很少。 本項目的第一個目標是用子域碼方法構造好參數的或者最優線性碼。第二個任務是研究本項目得到的線形碼的性能。預期本項目的成果會加強編碼學的理論和應用。

16300919.label: Major findings and research outcome
16300919.value: A family of [q^2 − 1, 4, q^2 − q − 2] cyclic codes over F_q meeting the Griesmer bound was presented. Their duals are [q^2 − 1, q^2 − 5, 4] almost MDS codes and are optimal with respect to the sphere-packing bound. The q0-ary subfield codes of this family of cyclic codes were also investigated, where q0 is any prime power such that q is power of q0. Some of the subfield codes are optimal and some have the best known parameters. A family of [q^2, 4, q^2 − q − 1] linear codes over F_q meeting the Griesmer bound was obtained. Their duals are [q^2 , q^2 − 4, 4] almost MDS codes and are optimal with respect to the sphere-packing bound. The q0-ary subfield codes of this family of linear codes were also investigated, where q0 is any prime power such that q is power of q0. Five infinite families of 2-designs were also constructed with three families of linear codes of this project. A general construction of [q+1,2,q] MDS codes over GF(q) was produced, and the subfield codes over GF(p) of some of the [q+1,2,q] MDS codes over GF(q) were analysed. Two families of dimension- optimal codes over GF(p) were obtained, and several families of nearly optimal codes over GF(p) were produced. There is a classical construction of a family of [2^m +1, 2u-1, 2^m-2u+3] MDS codes for 1 ≤ u ≤ 2^(m-1), which are cyclic, reversible and BCH codes over GF(2^m). The quaternary subfield subcodes and quaternary subfield codes of a subfamily of the MDS codes for even m were studied. A family of quaternary cyclic codes was obtained. These quaternary codes are distance-optimal in some cases and very good in general. Furthermore, two infinite families of 3-designs from these quaternary codes and their duals were presented.

16300919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16300919.value: We may look for other applications of the subfield codes. For example, we may investigate the application of the subfield codes in cryptography.

16300919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16300919.value: It is of theoretical and practical importance to construct optimal linear codes and linear codes with good parameters over small fields. A way to do this is to select or design an optimal linear code over GF(q^m) and study its subfield code over GF(q). This is the methodology used in this project. Some families of [q+1, 2, q] MDS codes over GF(q) were constructed. Two families of dimension-optimal codes over GF(p) were obtained, and several families of nearly optimal codes over GF(p) were produced. Several other families of linear codes with good parameters were obtained. A combinatorics application of some of the linear codes obtained in this project was investigated. The outputs of this project enhance coding theory and have applications in communication and data storage systems.

16301019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16301019.value: 鈰是唯一具有穩定的+IV氧化態的稀土元素。儘管正四價的鈰化合物在有機合成中，常用來作為單電子氧化劑，但已知鈰(IV)化合物的Ce-O鍵均裂性質還沒有被廣泛研究。據最近的報導可知，可見光使鈰(IV)烷氧基化合物的Ce-O鍵均裂，產生烷氧基自由基並活化C-H鍵。申請人課題組前期研究也發現，鈰(IV)氫氧化合物被還原成Ce(III)同時產生雙氧水分子。這些結論促使我們合成具有氧化還原活性的鈰(IV)烷氧基化合物和氫氧化合物，同時揭示其Ce-O鍵均裂性質的影響因素。 本項目合成及表徵一系列具有大位阻效應的三齒氧基配體穩定的鈰(IV)烷氧基化合物和氫氧化合物，通過烷氧基和三齒氧基配體取代基改變調控鈰(IV)烷氧基化合物和氫氧化合物穩定性和反應活性，研究這些鈰(IV)烷氧基化合物和氫氧化合物和苯酚和碳氫化合物的反應動力學和反應機理，揭示鈰(IV)氫氧化合物反應產生雙氧水分子的反應途徑，本項目還研究鈰(IV)烷氧基化合物熱致和光致Ce-O鍵均裂，並確定光致裂解產物。這些研究結論將揭示鈰(IV)作為氧化劑在水溶液條件下形成O-O鍵的反應途徑，這為發展鈰基配合為作為高效、高選擇性氧化劑和光催化劑提供實驗數據和理論支持。

16301019.label: Realisation of objectives
16301019.value: The objective of this research project is to synthesize cerium(IV) alkoxo and hydroxo complexes and investigate their reactivity toward organic substrates. The factors that control the Ce-O bond homolysis and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) reactivity of cerium(IV) alkoxo complexes have been elucidated. In particular, cerium(IV) complexes supported by the Kläui tripodal ligand [CpCo{P(O)(OEt)2}3]- (denoted as LOEt-) have been studied. A new method to synthesize oxidizing cerium(IV) alkoxo complexes involving protonolysis of a cerium(IV) oxo species with alcohols has been developed. This enabled us to synthesize a series of cerium(IV) dialkoxo complexes, [Ce(LOEt)2(OR)2] (R = Me, Et, Pr), and explore their oxidation chemistry. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies revealed that the alkyl group R has very little influence on the Ce-O bond length and Ce-O-C angle, consistent with the ionic nature of the Ce-OR bonds. The HAT reactivity of cerium(IV) alkoxo complexes has been investigated. We have demonstrated that cerium(IV) alkoxo complexes can oxidize substituted phenols via proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). For instance, oxidations of 2,6-di-tert-butylphenol and 2,4-di-tert-butylphenol with the isopropoxo complex [Ce(LOEt)2(OPr)2] afforded cerium(III) complexes with an aryloxide and a mono-deprotonated bis-phenol ligand, respectively. The Ce(IV) oxidation of phenols involves Ce-O homolysis of cerium(IV) bis-aryloxide intermediates to give phenoxy radicals that are subsequently oxidized to quinones. To our knowledge, this is the first report of PCET oxidation of phenols by a molecular cerium(IV) alkoxide. In addition, we have shown that hydrolysis of [Ce(LOEt)2(OPr)2] afforded a cerium(IV) hydroxo species that was readily reduced to cerium(III) with concomitant generation of hydrogen peroxide, lending further support for Ce(IV)-O homolysis of a Ce(IV) hydroxide. To elucidate the factors that affect the stability of cerium(IV) aryloxide complexes, we have prepared [Ce(OEt)2(OAr)2] bearing various substituted aryloxide ligands. X-ray diffraction studies indicated that the substituents of the aryloxide ligands do not have a significant influence on the Ce-O bond lengths and Ce-O-C bond angles. While the phenoxide complex [Ce(LOEt)2(OPh)2] was stable with respect to Ce(IV/III) reduction, the bis(2,6-difluorophenoxide) analogue [Ce(LOEt)2(OC6H3F2-2,6)2] underwent facile Ce-O homolysis to yield an aryloxy radical that is capable of hydrogen atom abstraction. This result highlights the importance of steric effects on the stability of cerium(IV) bis(aryloxide) complexes. To our knowledge, this is the first report of sterically induced reduction of a lanthanide aryloxide complex. In collaboration with Prof. Laurent Maron, University of Toulouse, we have conducted a theoretical study to elucidate the mechanism of O-H oxidation by cerium(IV) bis(aryloxide) complexes. Density functional theory calculations indicated that a triplet excited state of the cerium(IV) bis(2,6-difluorophenoxide) complex, which can be described as a cerium(III) aryloxy radical complex, is responsible for its hydrogen atom abstraction reactivity. This triplet excited state is easily accessible (about 7 kcal/mol above the ground state) apparently owing to the multiconfigurational nature of the cerium(IV) complex. This result demonstrates the impact of the multiconfigurational character of Ce(IV) on the redox reactivity of tetravalent cerium complexes. In conclusion, in this research project the steric and electronic factors that affect the redox reactivity of cerium(IV) alkoxo and aryloxo complexes have been studied systematically. Significantly, we have shown that the steric effects plays a key role in controlling the redox reactivity of cerium(IV) alkoxide and aryloxide complexes. Cerium(IV) with sterically bulky alkoxo and aryloxo ligands are liable to Ce-O homolysis, which generates alkoxy and aryloxy radicals that are able to abstract hydrogen atoms from organic substrates, such as phenols and hydrocarbons. This finding is reminiscent of sterically induced reduction of trivalent lanthanide complexes containing sterically bulky cyclopentadienyl ligands, which is well-known in organolanthanide chemistry. The results obtained from this research project can help us to develop new oxidative organic transformations using earth-abundant cerium reagents and catalysts.

16301019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16301019.value: (1) A new method for synthesis of oxidizing cerium(IV) alkoxo and aryloxo complexes, which involves protonolysis of a cerium(IV) oxo species with alcohols and aryl alcohols, has been developed. This enabled us to systematically study the steric and electronic effects on the stability and reactivity of cerium alkoxo and aryloxo complexes. (2) We have shown that a cerium(IV) alkoxo complex can oxidize substituted phenols to give cerium(III) aryloxides and quinones via a proton-electron transfer pathway. This is a new reaction of cerium(IV) alkoxides. (3) We have demonstrated that the steric effect plays a key role in the Ce-O homolysis of cerium(IV) aryloxo complexes. Cerium(IV) complexes with 2,6-disubstitued phenoxide ligands undergo facile Ce-O homolysis to afford cerium(III) species and aryloxy radicals. This is the first report of sterically induced reduction of cerium(IV) complexes. (4) We have found that a cerium(IV) 2,6-difluorophenoxide complex underwent Ce-O homolysis in the presence of substituted phenols. The generated aryloxy radical can abstract hydrogen atoms from organic substrates, such as substituted phenols and 9,10-dihydroanthracene. This is a new reaction of a tetravalent lanthanide aryloxide that has potential applications in organic transformations. (5) Density functional theory calculations have shown that a triplet excited state, which can be described as a cerium(III) aryloxy radical complex, is responsible for the HAT reactivity of a cerium(IV) 2,6-difluorophenoxide complex. This result highlights the importance of multiconfiguration character of Ce(IV) in the radical reactivity of cerium(IV) complexes. (6) We have demonstrated that a cerium(IV) hydroxide, which was generated in situ via hydrolysis of a cerium(IV) alkoxide, underwent Ce-O hydrolysis to afford Ce(III) and hydrogen peroxide. This result highlights the rich radical chemistry of tetravalent cerium complex.

16301019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16301019.value: In this research project, we have demonstrated that steric effects plays a key role in controlling the redox stability and reactivity of cerium(IV) alkoxo and aryloxo complexes. For instance, while the cerium(IV) isopropoxide complex [Ce(LOEt)2(OPr)2] is stable isolated complex, the tert-butoxide analogue is unstable with respect to Ce(IV/III) reduction owing to steric effects. Thus, with suitable choice of substituents, reactions of cerium(IV) oxo species with alcohol-based substrates will result in Ce-O homolysis and subsequent formation of alkoxy radical species, which can find applications organic synthesis, e.g., alcohol-directed C-H heterofunctionalization of C-H bonds via 1,5-HAT. Moreover, we have shown that a cerium(IV) 2,6-difluorophenoxide complex is prone to Ce-O homolysis because of steric effects. The generated aryloxy radical is capable of oxidizing O-H bonds of phenols and C-H bonds of hydrocarbons. Thus, with judicious choice of aryloxide ligands radical-like cerium(IV) aryloxide complexes can serve as initiators for radical reactions.

16301019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16301019.value: The development of catalytic organic processes using cerium reagents is of both academic and industrial importance because cerium is an earth-abundant element and cerium compounds are relatively non-toxic. Although tetravalent cerium compounds have been widely used in organic oxidations, the factors that control the oxidation chemistry of molecular cerium(IV) complexes are poorly understood. In this research project, we have developed a new method to synthesize cerium(IV) alkoxide and aryloxide complexes. This enabled us to elucidate the steric and electronic factors that affect the redox stability and reactivity cerium(IV) alkoxide and aryloxide complexes. We have demonstrated that cerium(IV) alkoxide complexes can oxidize substituted phenols via a proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. Moreover, cerium(IV) complexes with sterically bulky aryloxide ligands undergo facile cerium-oxygen bond homolysis generating reactive radical species that can oxidize O-H and C-H bonds. To our knowledge, this is the first report of sterically induced reduction of cerium(IV) compounds. The results obtained from this project can help us develop cerium-based reagents and catalysts for organic transformations.
