16303019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303019.value: Metamaterials are made up of artificial resonating atoms with tailor-made and flexible responses, while exotic applications such as invisibility cloaking and super-resolution imaging have been demonstrated. In real-world applications, the ability to modify or tune the material response is highly preferred. It can be achieved by adding active materials, changing the structures, or loading external tunable circuit elements into the metamaterial. When an individual control of different unit cells, such as a hologram, is necessary, recent works further adopted a digital approach in which the configuration of each unit cell is limited to a discrete number of choices. Then, the geometry of the whole metamaterial has a digital representation and an external computer program automates the setting of such digitized geometry. In this project, we propose to digitize the signal itself instead of the geometry. The incoming wave arriving the atom in each unit cell is sensed and digitized, with signal processing applied and the resulting signal is further converted back to secondary radiation through antennas as a form of programmable scattering. In this way, the physical resonance of the original metamaterial atom is now replaced by a software, making its scattering response much more flexible as a programmable convolution in time. We will implement such a scheme in acoustics at the audible frequencies, where digital electronics is fast enough to cope with the signal waves. We will design a 2D programmable atom, consisting of a structural arrangement of microphones and speakers, with a coin-sized microcontroller board programmed to generate prescribed monopolar and dipolar scattering responses. Through an array of these programmable atoms assembled into a medium, we enjoy a huge reconfigurability without the need to sweep across a physical resonance. This programmable approach will be applied to generate tunable frequency bandwidth for a negative-index medium and to approach the theoretical bound on the widest possible bandwidth. We will investigate its application in active acoustic control, such as sound localization, to enhance listening experience. Furthermore, the programmable platform will allow us to investigate wave phenomena originating from a time-varying system. Non-reciprocal transmission will be used as a typical example. We will also consider a moving speaker for the sound localization application. 由人造共振原子組成的超材料具有反應靈活可量身定制等特點，在隱形和超分辨率成像等領域有重要的應用。在實際應用中，往往需要實時的改變和調節超材料的響應特性。這種調節可以通過添加活性材料，改變超材料結構或加載可調電路元件來實現。在例如全息等系統中，需要對不同的單元進行獨立調節，最近一些聲學工作應用一種數字化的方法，即每個人造原子的幾何尺寸或形狀具有有限個數的選擇。通過外部計算機程序自動調節每個人造原子的幾何尺寸或形狀，從而控制整個系統的結構。這種可以數字化選擇的超材料稱為數字化超材料。在本項目中，我們提出數字化信號本身而非數字化超材料的幾何結構的方法。在該方法中， 入射波在到達每個人造原子後被測量並數字化，然後對數字化的信號進行數字信號處理，最終將處理過的信號以一種編程散射波的形式通過天線二次散射出去。通過這種方式，軟件取代了原始超材料原子的物理共振，超材料的共振響應被數字化成為一個時間卷積，因此超材料的響應可以通過編程隨意調控，而再不受制於超材料本身的物理結構。我們將在可聽頻段中實現聲學超材料的共振響應數字化，在該頻段下數字電子設備的速度足以實現實時的信號波處理。首先，我們將設計一個二維可編程原子，該原子由按結構排列的麥克風和揚聲器組成，並與微控制器相連從而通過編程產生需要的單極和偶極散射響應。將這些可編程原子組合成一種人工介質，從而無需重組超材料的物理結構就可以實現共振散射響應的可重構性。這種編程方法將應用於實現可調頻率帶寬的負折射率現象，可調節的帶寬可以接近理論上最寬帶寬的界限。之後我們將研究可編程系統在聲學控制中的應用，例如用於增強聆聽體驗的聲音局部化。此外，可編程平台將允許我們研究時變系統所產生的波現象，例如非互易傳輸。同時我們也將考慮一個移動的聲源在聲局域中的應用。

16303019.label: Realisation of objectives
16303019.value: 1. We have developed meta-atoms consisting of a structural arrangement of speakers and microphones, interconnected through digital microcontrollers, with one microcontroller for each atom. This setup allows us to generate both monopolar and dipolar scattering responses. Additionally, a theoretical model has been developed to represent each atom with an effective polarizability matrix, incorporating the structural arrangement within each atom into the model. Objective 1 is fully implemented. 2. The meta-atoms have been implemented with hardware and microcontroller programs capable of performing tailor-made convolution in the time domain, simulating any resonating frequency response of conventional physical acoustic metamaterial atoms. Each meta-atom is self-contained from electronics to generation of scattering responses, and has been integrated on circuit board. Since the parameters stored in the microcontrollers can be programmably changed, this approach allows us to achieve highly flexible active or non-reciprocal responses. The polarizability matrix, including both monopolar and dipolar scattering components, has been successfully implemented and characterized through scattering experiment. Additionally, we have extended the atoms' capabilities to Willis coupling, which cross-couples monopolar incident waves to dipolar scattering waves, and vice versa. In the latter part of the project, this programmability has been extended to time-varying material properties. Objective 2 is fully implemented. 3. We have assembled whole systems consisting of 3 to 24 meta-atoms, with each meta-atom working independently in scattering waves using its own microcontrollers. These meta-atoms then operate cooperatively as a metamaterial within an acoustic waveguide. We have achieved resonating transmission and reflection, as well as programmable control over material gain, Willis coupling, and operational bandwidth. We have shifted our focus from negative refraction to Willis coupling as a generalization of non-trivial consitutive parameters such as a negative refractive index. Objective 3 has been fully implemented in terms of programmable control over metamaterial responses. 4. We have demonstrated sound localization, a specialized phenomenon in which sound waves generated from a sound source within an enclosed region, bounded by the meta-atoms, are damped when the waves propagate outside the region. Conversely, sound waves can still propagate freely from outside into the region. Objective 4 has been fully implemented. 5. We have demonstrated two types of non-reciprocal propagation phenomena within a one-dimensional device setting. First, asymmetric frequency conversion from forward and backward incidence has been achieved through dynamic modulation as a non-reciprocal effect. Second, we have found that by extending the Willis coupling of acoustic metamaterials into the operational regime where both active (power can be injected) and non-reciprocal conditions are met, one can obtain non-reciprocal sound propagation without reflection, thereby facilitating sound isolation applications. Objective 5 has been fully implemented.

16303019.value: 1. Tailor-made constitutive parameters: We have demonstrated programmable resonating bulk modulus and density in a one-dimensional waveguide using the meta-atoms with digital feedback in creating scattering responses. This part of work related to static yet programmable platform has acutally been completed before the formal start of this project and was published [Nature Commun. 11, 251 (2020)] in the beginning of the project. It serves as the precursor for our current project. Our aim is to attain material properties that can be both active and time-varying, through Lorentzian or anti-Lorentzian resonance. The metamaterial atoms, even at this stage, provide a wide range of tunability due to software flexibility. We have then expanded this programmability to Willis coupling (the analogy of bianisotropy in EM waves), enabling us to surpass typical size constraints, achieving active, non-reciprocal Willis coupling with programmable operational bandwidth [Commun. Phys. 4, 82 (2021)]. 2. Unidirectional amplification: Through dynamic modulation of constitutive parameters, we have demonstrated unidirectional amplification, achieving over 100% efficiency in frequency conversion to harmonics. This means amplification beyond the power at signal frequency in one direction but not in the opposite direction within a one-dimensional metamaterial [Commun. Phys. 5:18]. Alternatively in a static context, we have theoretically established parameters for exponential amplification in one direction, damping in the opposite direction, and zero reflection in both. Achieving this necessitates active, non-reciprocal Willis coupling, now achievable with our platform. We have introduced and proven the concept of such acoustic diode capable of amplification [Phys. Rev. Lett. 130, 176101 (2023)], with practical applications in sound isolation. 3. Sound localization: We have theoretically established a unique sound localization method using a ring of our metamaterial atoms. When a sound source is inside the ring, its radiation is dampened outside the ring. Conversely, if a sound source is outside the ring, it doesn't create scattering; instead, sound can pass into the region inside with an amplification ratio. This phenomenon has diverse applications in sound localization, amplified sensing, and non-reciprocal sound communication. Our work is currently under submission [arXiv:2311.09674]. 4. Temporal effective media: Our ability to dynamically modulate material parameters much faster than the signal period has enabled the realization of the concept of a temporal effective medium. This concept parallels the spatial effective medium, where signal wavelengths significantly exceed spatial inhomogeneity. We have made a groundbreaking demonstration of this concept within the acoustic domain [Phys. Rev. B 104, L060304 (2021)].

16303019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303019.value: There are two potential directions for further development. One involves a concept called 'time boundary.' Our platform can manipulate various constitutive parameters, such as density, bulk modulus, and Willis coupling, which can be turned on and off at a time interface. This allows for precise control over the forward and backward waves generated at a time boundary, leading to new ways to control sound and also to design devices. Another possibility is to explore non-Hermitian topology. Our system, equipped with active and time-varying material properties, can be used to investigate topological pumping and topological states with amplification. While these developments are not explicitly covered by the current project's scope, they can benefit from our existing platform. We plan to submit a research proposal for these new physics explorations.

16303019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303019.value: While metamaterials extend the conventional approach in materials science to incorporate a designer concept based on structures, they often exhibit static functionality or possess limited tunability. In this project, we explore a valuable direction in programmable metamaterials that embrace programmability in material properties, in controlling acoustic wave propagation for our case. Taking inspiration from robotics, we employ microcontrollers for each self-contained constructing unit (meta-attom) of the material, enabling wave interaction and the creation of a programmable material. We have demonstrated that the material parameters constructed in this manner can be active, non-reciprocal, or time-varying. This means that power can be injected into the acoustic waves through additional electronics, creating asymmetric coupling between different parts of the materials, and allowing for dynamic modulation of the material properties. These capabilities enable us to showcase tailor-made constitutive matrix parameters, achieve unidirectional amplification, explore sound localization, and delve into fundamental concepts such as the temporal effective media. These advancements open new dimensions in the field of metamaterials, particularly in our ability to control wave propagation, and also connect to applications such as sound isolation, amplified sensing, and non-reciprocal communication.

16303119.value: 具有边界条件敏感特性的光子晶体,超材料及相关系统

16303119.label: Project Objectives
16303119.value: To understand and clarify the conditions needed to realize boundary condition sensitive materials. We will focus in particular on the interplay between non-Hermiticity and non-reciprocity. To construct models of classical wave systems in which the coupling between resonating units is asymmetrical so as to realize boundary condition sensitive materials; and to design non-Hermitian non-reciprocal photonic crystals and metamaterials to realize such materials. To identify and consider the physical consequences and ramifications of such boundary condition sensitive systems and their possible applications.

16303119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303119.value: The key purpose of this project is to develop a new class of artificial materials which display a very strong dependence on boundary conditions. We shall call them boundary condition-sensitive materials. Let us use an analogy to clarify the meaning of boundary condition sensitivity. Imagine cutting open a donut, which is a ring-shaped object, so that it becomes a broken ring. The cut will of course create new donut surfaces, but other parts of the donut should feel, look, and taste the same. This is what we expect of natural materials: changing the boundary of an object (e.g. creating a truncated surface) should not change the bulk properties of the object. For the boundary condition-sensitive materials we plan to develop, however, cutting the donut will change the whole donut, not just the exposed surfaces, to the extent that it will look and feel different. This is not possible with natural materials or even most artificial materials. We seek to show that some of the elaborately designed artificial photonic crystals and metamaterials may possess such boundary condition sensitivity not found in nature. Photonic crystals are man-made crystals comprising a lattice of building blocks which have a lattice constant comparable to the wavelength of light or electromagnetic waves. If the lattice constant is much smaller than the operating wavelength, we call the artificial material a metamaterial. We have reasons to believe that a necessary condition to achieving such boundary condition sensitivity is that the wave propagating inside such artificial materials should be “non-reciprocal”, meaning that wave propagation is easier in one direction than in the opposite direction. In addition, we require the material to have gain and loss, so that energy can enter and exit the crystal. Such new materials, if they can be achieved in practice, will create many new opportunities. Their properties are outside the realm of conventional textbook physics, and they can become new platforms on which we can explore new phenomena. Many conventional concepts and useful techniques such as the so-called “Bloch theorem” and “bulk-edge correspondence” may require revision. Their properties are deeply related to certain branches of mathematics and theoretical physics. These materials will enable new applications. For example, boundary condition sensitivity implies that the system response will be strong even if the boundary is only slightly perturbed. This means that these materials can be used to build ultrasensitive sensors. 项目的主要目的是开发一类新型人造材料，其性质强烈依赖于材料的对边界条件，所以我们称之为边界条件敏感材料。让我们用一个类比来阐明边界条件敏感的含义。试想当一个甜甜圈被切开后，它的形状由一个闭合的圆环变成了一个断开的环。尽管切面使甜甜圈多出了一个新表面，甜甜圈其它部分的触感，外观和味道却不会因此改变。这正符合我们对天然材料预期：改变物体的边界 (比如创建一个新截面) 不会改变物体内部的物理性质。然而，对于我们计划构造的边界条件敏感材料，切开甜甜圈不仅会改变暴露面的属性，而且将改变整个甜甜圈的性质，它的触感和味道将变得与一个完整的甜甜圈完全不同。而这种特性不可能存在于天然材料和绝大多数人工材料之中。 我们将致力于在精心设计的人造光子晶体和超材料中实现这种自然材料所不具有的边界条件敏感特性。光子晶体是一种由周期结构单元构成的人造晶体，它的晶格常数与光或电磁波的波长大致相当。而当晶格常数远小于工作波长时，我们称相应的人工材料为超材料。 我们有理由相信实现边界条件敏感的一个必要条件是“非互易性”，这意味着波沿一个方向比沿相反方向更容易传播。与此同时，我们还需要材料具有增益和损耗，以控制能量进出晶体。如果可以在实际系统中实现，这种新材料将有广阔的用武之地。它们将呈现超出传统教科书的独特物理性质，并可成为我们探索新物理现象的平台。对于这类材料，许多在传统材料中行之有效的物理概念和技术，比如“布洛赫定理”和“体-边界对应原理”，都需要重新修正。它们的性质与数学和理论物理某些分支有着深刻的联系。这些新材料还将启迪新的应用。例如，边界敏感性意味着，即使边界只有轻微扰动，系统也会做出强烈的响应。因此，这种新材料可以用于制造超灵敏传感器件。

16303119.label: Realisation of objectives
16303119.value: Objective 1: We used various model systems to understand the conditions necessary to realize boundary condition sensitivity and related phenomena such as the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). We considered bulk boundary correspondence (BBC) for those systems. For example, we used the non-Hermitian (NH) Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model and the Creutz ladder models to understand the conditions necessary for realizing boundary condition sensitivity. We proposed a new approach to restore the BBC. Our new method can give a modified Hamiltonian which has the same spectra as the original non-Hermitian system under open boundary conditions. As a result, the modified system can serve as the valid bulk for defining topological invariants. Furthermore, we show that two types of winding numbers can be defined to account for the skin effect and topological edge states that can be applied to system systems with boundary condition sensitivity, including random systems [https://arxiv.org/abs/2304]. We also clarified the topology in non-Hermitian Chern insulators with NHSE. The NHSE can arise in materials that have asymmetric hopping, which makes the bulk eigen-spectra sensitive to boundary conditions. We established the BBC for a Chern insulator model with NHSE by combining the “non-Bloch” approach and “biorthogonal” approach. Both approaches can suppress the NHSE but they are based on different mathematical tools [Phys. Rev. B 105, 075128 (2022)]. We considered the effect of system size dependence using edge states in plasmonic meta-arrays as model systems. We designed boundary condition-sensitive plasmonic cluster systems which provides photonic edge states to control light–matter interactions. The properties of edge states depend on the geometric details and system size. We demonstrated a simple and effective strategy to construct and steer photonic edge state in such meta-arrays [Nanophotonics 11 (15), 3495-3507 (2022)]. Boundary condition sensitivity is a unique property of some non-Hermitian systems, which host points (EPs). Some boundary condition sensitive systems have EPs in open boundary conditions, but not under periodic boundary condition. We are interested in model systems that have “singular” features (e.g. cusps) of EPs and the associated topology. For example, we showed that astroid-shaped EP loops, comprising four cusps, can spawn from the triple degeneracy point in the Brillouin zone of a Lieb lattice when non-Hermiticity is introduced [Phys. Rev. B. 102, 245144 (2020)]. We also demonstrated that EPs can form a nexus that carries a hybrid topological invariant. We demonstrated with both theory and acoustic experiments an “exceptional nexus” (EX), which is not only a higher-order EP but also the cusp singularity of multiple exceptional arcs (EAs). Because the parameter space is segmented by the EAs, the EX possesses a hybrid topological invariant, which is experimentally characterized by measuring the critical behaviors of the wave functions. Our findings constitute a major advance in the fundamental understanding of non-Hermitian systems and their topology [Science 370, 1077 (2020)]. The effect of disorder is examined in some model systems. We study the Anderson localization of electromagnetic waves in gain-loss balanced random non-Hermitian and we found that the localization behaves differently from random Hermitian systems in which the backscattering is suppressed [Nanophotonics 10, 443 (2021)]. We found that a cluster of optically bound particles the force matrix is in general asymmetric, which satisfies the necessary condition to realize boundary condition sensitivity. Such matrices inevitably yield complex eigenvalues when driven beyond the EPs, where light pumps in energy that “melts” the light-bound structures. As such, forces from optical fields alone cannot bind a large cluster. Our work reveals the crucial role played by EPs, a role which was previously unknown in the field of optical manipulation [Nat. Comm. 12, 6597 (2021)]. Objective 2: We designed boundary condition-sensitive photonic and phononic crystal systems in which the properties of the edge can be used to induce chiral transport phenomena in some bulk modes. Specifically, we show that a topologically trivial 2D hexagonal phononic waveguide bounded by hard-wall boundaries guarantees the existence of bulk modes with chiral anomaly inside a pseudogap due to finite size effect. We experimentally observed robust valley-selected transport, complete valley state conversion, and valley focusing of the chiral anomaly bulk states in such phononic waveguides. The same concept also applies to electromagnetics [Nat. Comm. 13, 5916 (2022)]. We have theoretically and experimentally achieved large-area one-way transport by using heterostructures consisting of a domain of an ordinary photonic crystal sandwiched between magnetic photonic crystals, which provides a unique boundary condition. We show that such boundary-condition enabled one-way waveguide states can be used to abruptly narrow the beam width of an extended state to concentrate energy. These waveguide modes also demonstrate robustness against perturbation [Phys. Rev. Lett. 126, 067401 (2021)]. We also designed and experimentally realized wave waveguides that can perform non-Abelian braiding and logic operations. Non-Abelian braiding is regarded as an essential process for realizing quantum logic. The cyclic evolution of degenerate waveguide states induces a non-Abelian geometric phase, manifesting as the exchange of states [Nat. Phys. 18, 179 (2022)]. Objective 3: Making use of the boundary condition sensitivity of systems exhibiting exceptional surfaces, we realized a scalable strategy to realize a robust on-chip integrated visible microlaser which has robustness against fabrication errors, compressible linewidth, reducible threshold, and in-plane emission. This work lays a foundation for further development of on-chip integrated high-speed visible-light communication and processing systems [Sci. Adv. 9, eadf3470 (2023)]. We investigated properties of eigenstates and transport induced by boundary effects. We considered magnetically controllable multimode interference in topological photonic crystals. We designed a boundary condition enabled and magnetic field-controlled power splitting system. The number of topological edge states relies on the difference between the bulk Chern numbers across the boundary, and the power-splitting is controlled by engineering multimode interference tuned by magnetic field intensity or the frequency of operation [arXiv.2304.11170]. We studied photonic topological insulators with different types of gain-loss domain walls and we proposed a method to construct effective Hamiltonians for different types of photonic topological insulators and domain walls with arbitrary boundaries. Our results reveal the physics in photonic topological insulators with special boundary conditions imposed as gain-loss domain walls [Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 053903 (2022)]. Non-reciprocity and time-reversal breaking are key conditions to realize boundary condition sensitivity. We show that it has applications in radiative energy harvesting by considering the near-field radiative energy transfer between a magneto-optic medium and a substrate with the boundary condition modified by adding a graphene layer on top. The magnitude and direction of radiative heat transfer can be modulated due to the interplay between the nonreciprocal photon occupation number from the graphene and the nonreciprocal surface modes of the magneto-optic medium [Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 247401 (2021)]. We discovered the coexistence of a new type of bound state in the continuum (BIC) and a lasing threshold mode induced by PT symmetry. The BIC and lasing threshold mode corresponds respectively to the right and left eigenvectors of the non–Hermitian matrix [Sci. Adv. 6, eabc1160 (2020)].

16303119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303119.value: Boundary condition sensitivity can arise when non-reciprocity is introduced to non-Hermitian systems, resulting in complications such as the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) and modification of the celebrated bulk-boundary condition (BBC) in topological physics. To restore the BBC in systems exhibiting NHSE, we introduced a new approach called "doubling and swapping." Our approach is physically intuitive, transparent, and less involved compared to the non-Bloch approach, and can be applied to a wide range of systems in higher dimensions and even random systems. We also introduced two types of winding numbers to account for NHSE and topological edge states that are applicable to random systems. We also considered and found many interesting topological properties related to exceptional points. One fascinating set of results is the discovery of boundary condition induced robust transport. In usual topological materials, the number of topological edge modes is dictated by the topological invariants in the bulk. In order to achieve robust transport along the edge, it is necessary to make volumetric changes to numerous bulk atoms to control the properties of just a few edge atoms. However, we show that we can achieve the reverse by modifying the boundary conditions, which can guarantee chiral transport phenomena in certain bulk modes. This constitutes a conceptual breakthrough, as conventional valley-hall topological materials use the bulk to control edge transport, whereas our approach employs the edge to control bulk transport. More specifically, we have demonstrated that a topologically trivial 2D hexagonal phononic crystal waveguide bounded by hard-wall boundaries can ensure the existence of bulk modes with chiral anomaly within a pseudogap. Through our experimental setup, we have successfully exhibited robust valley-selected transport, complete valley state conversion, and valley focusing of the chiral anomaly bulk states in such phononic crystal waveguides by simply imposing specific boundary conditions. Additionally, we have applied a similar idea to achieve large-area one-way transport using heterostructures of photonic crystals. These one-way waveguide states that can narrow the beam width of an extended state and concentrate energy. This transport is robust against defects and imperfections and is immune to localization even in the presence of significant randomness. We also developed a scalable strategy to achieve a robust on-chip integrated visible microlaser with improved lasing performances. Such lasers need robustness against fabrication errors, compressible linewidth, reducible threshold, and in-plane emission. Our approach, enabled by the boundary condition sensitivity of second-order exceptional surfaces, satisfy all these conditions.

16303119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303119.value: The non-Hermitian skin effect poses a challenge to many of the established results in physics that are based on our knowledge of Hermitian and reciprocal systems, such as the bulk-boundary correspondence. Further research in this area could lead to a deeper understanding of the fundamental principles of topological physics and the development of new materials with unique topological properties. Additionally, skin effects can also occur in systems represented by real non-symmetric matrices. We have explored a few such systems in this project and exploring more of these systems could reveal even more interesting phenomena. The non-Hermitian skin effect has already been demonstrated in various photonic and acoustic systems, and continued research in this area could lead to the development of new device components with unique properties, such as robust transport against defects and imperfections, as well as new boundary conditions that can enable the manipulation of light and sound waves. One potential application of this research that is worth pursuing is the development of sensitive sensors that can detect small changes in the environment.

16303119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303119.value: In usual systems, the boundary conditions have very little effect on the properties of a system as long as the system is large enough because the number of atoms on the boundary is small compared to the bulk. However, in certain energy non-conserving systems, the boundary condition sensitivity can be strong if the system is non-reciprocal (meaning energy can travel more easily in one direction than the other). This sensitivity can cause a variety of issues, such as changes in the system's spectrum when using different boundary conditions, usually called the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) and changes to the bulk-boundary condition (BBC) in topological physics. To restore the BBC in systems with NHSE, we introduced a new approach that can be applied to a range of systems, including random systems. Boundary condition sensitivity can lead to opportunities. We discovered boundary condition induced robust transport, which allows for robust transport phenomena in certain bulk modes by modifying the boundary rather than the bulk. We successfully demonstrated this concept in some waveguide configurations. Additionally, we developed a scalable strategy for a robust on-chip integrated visible microlaser with improved performances that is enabled by the boundary condition sensitivity of exceptional surfaces.

16303419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303419.value: 在歐洲核子研究中心（CERN）的大型強子對撞機（LHC）科研計劃已到達了重要的里程碑。至2018年底，LHC的ATLAS和CMS探測器累積的數據量將達到計劃目標的約50%。雖然目前只完成了分析該組數據的一小部分，但對新物理（粒子和相互作用）已經進行了深入探索，以擴展被稱為標準模型（Standard Model）的理論框架。這種新物理的存在包括對宇宙間正反物質的不平衡，暗物質的存在以及其他在標準模型框架內無法解釋的現象。目前在LHC並沒有再發現新的粒子，因此只設定了新粒子假設質量的下限。這顯示新物理可能存在於比LHC更高的能量區間內。這樣，很可能需要從那些標準模型能準確描述的物理過程中，去觀察實驗結果與標準模型預測的偏差來發現新物理。 2012年由ATLAS和CMS共同發現的希格斯波色子(Higgs Boson)是標準模型預測的粒子中最後一個被發現的。而未來數年，發掘Higgs Boson的特性將會是LHC的首要任務。在這重大發現的幾年後，我們對此粒子的了解仍然是在標準模型中最少的。預計Higgs Boson的性質與標準模型的預測偏差會是很小。因此，將於2018年底及其後完成收集的龐大數據組為尋找這些理論預測的偏差提供了的歷史性的機會。這些研究結果將會揭示Higgs Boson如何運作，包括產生電弱對稱的破缺機制，亦是產生基本粒子的質量的機制，並提供標準模型以外新物理的線索。 此項目為GRF資助計劃的延展，透過研究Higgs Boson跟其他基本粒子的互動，來理解Higgs Boson的重要性質。基於前項目的成功，我們計劃採用有效場論的方法，來進行結構完整，並與其他理論相獨立的的方法研究。此方法將為日後整合不同的獨立測量提供基礎，以取得世界上最精確的結果。此外，我們亦計劃在這個項目中對Higgs Boson的性質作前瞻性研究，以評估未來計畫在中國建造的環形正負電子對撞機（CEPC）的潛力。 基礎物理聯合研究中心（JCFP）的ATLAS小組包括香港中文大學，香港大學和香港科技大學的成員。在過去三年中，該小組成員為收集和分析ATLAS Run 2數據作出了重大貢獻。並在建立利用有效場論（EFT）去測量Higgs Boson特性的方法發揮核心作用，並首先應用於LHC Run 2當中的部分數據。其他貢獻包括ATLAS探測器的第二階段升級（Phase 2 upgrade） 和發展重建軟件。基於我們在早期Run 2的成果，我們建議在全期Run 2的數據在Higgs Boson性質的有效場論測量中發揮核心位置的作用。為此，我們建議延長現有的高級研究員職位，以負責相應的分析工作。

16303419.label: Realisation of objectives
16303419.value: 1. The methodology to perform the full analysis of the Run-2 data was developed. The STXS measurements were done and published. The corresponding BSM EFT interpretations were presented. In addition to the main goal, the analysis of the individual BSM EFT operators was performed in two ways: a simplified approach was taken to measure CP-odd operators first. This measurement is finalised, published and currently used as input for the ATLAS-wide combination of Higgs CP-violation searches. The implementation of the full EFT analysis, starting with Run-2 data and later to be extended to Run-3 data is currently in progress. 2. The STXS framework based on the Higgs production mechanism is currently in use in the ATLAS collaboration. The extension of this framework to include the final state binning was attempted in the frame of this project. First results were recently presented at the LHC Higgs Cross Section Working group meetings. The effort will continue during the extension of the current project. The EFT basis candidates for the future combination have been studied and discussed at length. At the moment the so-called Warsaw basis seems to be best candidate, agreed among many working groups. 3. The extension of the studies for the full LHC dataset has currently started. The Run-3 data taking is on-going. The methodology of measurements was established in the frame of the current project. In the near future the preparation for studies using developed methodology for the Run 3 data and then for the full dataset including Run 2 and Run 3 data will begin.

16303419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303419.value: The implementation of this project allowed to extend the boundaries of the human knowledge of fundamental physics. It has been demonstrated that the Standard Model of particle physics remains to be the valid theory for Higgs boson interactions with gauge bosons within the available amount of data. The corresponding upper limits for new physics contributions were set and published. The results were presented in international conferences and will continue to be presented as state-of-the-art results by the ATLAS collaboration until a more precise measurement is made. The work done in the frame of this project served material for several defended phd theses.

16303419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16303419.value: An extended analysis of the Run-2 LHC data, including the CP-even and CP-odd operators is currently at its finalisation stage. This analysis will allow for at least one more journal publication, partially related to the current project. Studies performed in this project will be extended using the LHC Run3 dataset, currently been collected. It is expected that in 2-3 years a journal publication, summarising the investigation of the combined Run-2 and Run-3 data sample will be prepared. The extension of the current project has been approved by RGC through the RGC/GRF grant 16303523.

16303419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303419.value: This project has resulted in advancement of our understanding of the Higgs boson physics and more generally in our knowledge of the structure of the Universe. The existence of the Higgs boson, the particle giving other elementary particles their masses was postulated in 1960s and took over 50 years to be confirmed experimentally. Discovered in 2012, the Higgs boson represents the least studied elementary particle, whose properties are not yet fully investigated. It is hoped that in addition to its predicted properties, the Higgs boson can shed light on the origin of Dark Matter and on domination of matter over the antimatter in our Universe. This completion of this project and the publication of its results represents a step in the direction of the full characterisation of the Higgs boson. While no significant deviations from the theory predictions are currently observed, this work represents the foundation for the future precision studies, to be done with higher statistics and using cleaner Higgs decay channels. The published results are the most precise measurements in the Higgs sector to-date. They pave the road for future mega-science projects for Higgs studies: CEPC in China and FCC in Europe.

16303719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303719.value: Aristolochic acids (AAs) is one of the most potent nephrotoxin and human carcinogen produced naturally in Aristolochia plants. Because of the tradition practice of herbal medicines and the wide-spread use of AAs-containing plants as in herbal preparations, it was estimated that over 100 million people in East Asia are at risk of AAs poisoning to develop chronic kidney disease and urothelial cancers. Further, residents of rural farming villages in Balkan Peninsula is also suffering from nephropathy caused by dietary intake of AAs contaminated food. Being able to identify people at risk of developing AAs-associated nephropathy will allow early intervention and have better chance of recovery. However, method that allow early diagnosis of AAs poisoning is currently not available and there is no available biomarker for risk assessment. This goal of the proposed study is to develop protein-AA adduct as biomarker for identifying individuals whom are at risk of AA poisoning and to identify kidney disease incidents caused by AAs exposure. Protein being one of the major biomolecules in the cells and protein adducts are not being repaired by repair enzymes, it is highly possible that the protein-AA adducts may act as sensitive dosimeter for risk assessment. Using the highly sensitive and selective liquid chromatography coupled with triple quadrupole mass spectrometric method (LC-MS/MS), we will first quantitate the time- and dosage-dependent formation of protein-AA adducts in protein isolated from tissue and serum of AAs-exposed rats. In collaboration with medical doctors from China and Serbia, we will then determine the adducts in serum protein isolated from patients suffered from kidney disease, with the goal of identifying individual who are intoxified by AAs. It is anticipated that the assay developed in this proposed research will facilitate medical doctors to prognosis of AAs-induced nephropathy as well as for identifying cases of kidney disease caused by AA exposure. 存在於馬兜鈴科植物中的馬兜鈴酸是最强力的腎毒素和人體致癌物之一。長久以來，含有馬兜鈴酸的植物被廣泛地用作中草藥。據報導，東亞地區有超過一億人可能因攝取馬兜鈴酸而患上慢性腎病和泌尿上皮癌。此外，巴爾幹半島上的村民也因為攝入食物中的馬兜鈴酸而患上腎病。若能識別病人患上因馬兜鈴酸引致的腎病，醫生可及早對症下藥並提高其康復的可能。可是，現時並沒有可用的馬兜鈴酸中毒的早期診斷方法，也沒有可應用於風險評估的生物標誌物，本研究旨在開發蛋白質-馬兜鈴酸的加合物作為識別馬兜鈴酸中毒和馬兜鈴酸導致的腎病的生物標誌物。蛋白質是細胞中的主要生物大分子之一，其加合物不可以被酶修復，因此蛋白質-馬兜鈴酸的加合物可以作為風險評估的有效的標記物。利用高靈敏度和高選擇性的高效液相色譜與三重四極杆質譜聯用法（LC-MS/MS），我們首先讓老鼠進食定量的馬兜鈴酸，然後抽取老鼠的組織和血清，測定其中含有的蛋白質-馬兜鈴酸加合物，再研究加合物與時間和劑量的相關性。通過與中國和塞爾維亞的醫生合作，我們將測定腎病患者血清蛋白中的生物加合物，來鑒別由馬兜鈴酸中毒導致的疾病。在本研究中開發的方法有望幫助醫生鑒別馬兜鈴酸引起的腎病並對病情發展進行預測。

16303719.label: Major findings and research outcome
16303719.value: We developed in this research a highly sensitive and selective method to quantitate protein adducts of aristolochic acid I (AAI) as a potential non-invasive biomarker of AA exposure. The method entails the release of protein bound aristolactam I (ALI) by heat-assisted alkaline hydrolysis, extraction of ALI, addition of internal standard, and quantitation by liquid chromatography−tandem mass spectrometric analysis. After evaluating for accuracy and precision using a synthetic ALI-containing glutathione adduct, the method was used to quantitate the exposure concentration-dependent formation of ALI−protein adducts in human serum albumin exposed to AAI and in proteins isolated from the tissues and sera of AAI-exposed rats. Results from time-dependent study showed that ALI−protein adducts remained detectable in rats even at 28 days postdosing. These results showed ALI−protein adducts is a promising biomarker for AA exposure and that the developed method will fill the technical gap in diagnosing AA intoxication and facilitate the biomonitoring of human exposures to AAs. These findings were published in peer-reviewed journal (attached; Chem. Res. Toxicol. 2021, 34, 144−153) Analysis of human serum protein samples isolated from patients suffering from chronic kidney disease using the developed method also detected AL in the heat-treated samples, indicating the method can be used for clinical testing to detect people at risk of suffering from AA-induced kidney disease. A research paper documenting the above-stated findings is in preparation.

16303719.value: In July 2022, the World Health Organization called for global action to reduce AA-associated cancer risk. Method that allow early identification of people at risk of suffering from AA poisonings shall facilitate early intervention and better chance of treatment. Our developed analytical method of detecting AA-protein adduct in human serum albumin will fill the gap of identifying people at risk of suffering from AA-associated cancer and nephropathy, before the end-stage kidney disease developed.

16303819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303819.value: Recently, extensive studies have been conducted in cosmological collider physics. Cosmological collider physics aims to study high energy particle physics through the lens of cosmic inflation (a stage of the primordial universe during which the universe expanded almost exponentially). It is expected that inflation, as a collider built by nature, had a higher energy scale than current particle colliders. Thus, information from the cosmological collider can offer important hints for understanding particle physics. In particular, information about the mass and spin of the heavy particles can be read off from the energy ratio dependence and the angular dependence of the cosmological correlation functions (non-Gaussianities), respectively. The mass and spin information are robust and independent of inflation models, so long as the model predicts a nearly exponential expansion of space, as the defining feature of inflation requires. We propose to further extend the research program of cosmological collider to include processes with missing energies. It is well known that processes with missing energies can be studied on particle colliders, if some particles are very weakly interacting and thus can escape from the detector. In this case, although some particles are left undetected, those processes still provide important data for understanding the underlying particle physics. In the case of the cosmological collider, we will show in this proposed project that processes with missing energy can also be studied. A proof-of-concept toy model will be discussed in the resonance approximation. We will learn from such missing energy processes that to make full use of the data from cosmological observations in understanding cosmological collider physics, we must take processes with missing energy into account as well. We propose studying this model and its implications comprehensively. We further propose to apply the concept of missing energy to study fermions in cosmological collider physics. Unlike the case of particle colliders, in cosmological collider, the observable external states are always bosons (curvature fluctuation, primordial gravitational waves or isocurvature). Thus, without missing energy, the fermions can only run in internal loops and the loops have integral spin as a whole. The study of missing energy opens up the possibility of studying single tree-level fermion propagators on the cosmological collider. We also propose to study processes with missing energy for charged particles for a similar purpose. And we shall examine the possibility that missing energy processes might play an important role in the particle physics standard model on the cosmological collider. 近年來，宇宙對撞機物理方向的研究十分活躍。宇宙對撞機物理旨在通過暴漲（早期宇宙接近指數膨脹的一個階段）宇宙學來研究高能粒子物理。多數研究人員期待，暴漲宇宙，作爲自然界中存在的對撞機，其能量遠遠超過人造對撞機。所以，對宇宙對撞機的研究會為理解粒子物理提供重要綫索。 特別地，在宇宙對撞機上，通過測量關聯函數（即非高斯）中的能量比例和角分佈，我們可以得到重粒子的質量和自旋。這樣得到的質量和自旋信息具有魯棒性，不依賴於具體暴漲模型的選取（只要暴漲期間宇宙仍然是接近指數膨脹）。 我們建議研究丟失能量信號，以進一步擴展宇宙對撞機物理的研究。 在粒子物理領域衆所周知，如果一些粒子相互作用很弱，可以逃離探測器，則在對撞機上可以研究粒子物理過程中的丟失能量。在這種情況下，儘管一些粒子沒有被探測到，相關過程仍然為理解粒子物理提供重要信息。 在項目申請書中，我們指出，在宇宙對撞機上也可以研究類似的丟失能量問題。我們將利用共振近似，討論一個玩具模型。從這個玩具模型可以看出，爲了充分發揮宇宙對撞機的潛力，我們需要考慮丟失能量的過程。我們建議詳細研究此模型。 我們進一步建議，研究宇宙對撞機上費米子的丟失能量問題。宇宙對撞機與人造粒子對撞機的一個區別是，宇宙對撞機上，可觀測的外綫粒子總是玻色子（曲率擾動，原初引力波或等曲率擾動）。所以，如果不考慮丟失能量，則費米子只能在圈裏運動，整個費米子圈將呈現整數自旋。對丟失能量的研究，將開啓在宇宙對撞機上研究費米子樹圖的可能性。 我們也建議研究帶電粒子的丟失能量問題。我們也將研究，在粒子物理標準模型的宇宙對撞機信號中，丟失能量問題是否會起到重要作用。

16303819.label: Realisation of objectives
16303819.value: In "Chemical-Potential-Assisted Particle Production in FRW Spacetimes" (JHEP 06 (2021) 129), we have studied in detail the particle production and energy aspects for spin 0 (scalar), spin 1/2 (Fermion) and spin 1 (vector boson) with the assistant of a rolling inflaton in general FRW spacetime. This is an extensive work which is 66 pages long. In this work, we have addressed most of the objectives: how the resonant happened and how the energy transferred in general (in the sense of super-adiabatic approximation), and how this process actually happens for particles with different spins. In "Numerical prescription of early-time divergences of the in-in formalism" (JCAP 07 (2022) 07, 014), we have proposed a new sets of numerical methods to calculate the in-in integrals for the early universe correlation functions. This work complement the above analytical work by additional technique of numerical computations. In "Cutting Rule for Cosmological Collider Signals: A Bulk Evolution Perspective" (JHEP 03 (2022) 181), we show that how the particle production and energy transfer affect observation can be greatly simplified. A set of cutting rules are proposed for this purpose. Based on this, we have studied more detailed models of particle physics.

16303819.value: Particle production in the primordial universe is an extensive research area. We have worked out a set of analytical methods and numerical methods for this purpose. This can be used for studying more explicit models, for example, particle physics beyond the standard model and how they appear on the cosmological collider.

16303819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16303819.value: It is believed that our universe has underwent a period of cosmic inflation, during which the energy scale was much higher than any experiments that human can achieve. Thus it is important to study the not-yet-known particle physics using cosmic inflation as a tool. In this project, we have systematically studied the particle production with energy transfer for spin 0, 1/2 and 1 particles, simplified the existing calculation significantly, and developed numerical methods for more complicated calculations.

16303919.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16303919.value: 發展考慮記憶效應的馬爾可夫狀態理論模型研究生物大分子的構象動力學

16303919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16303919.value: Conformational dynamics of biomolecules play an important role in numerous fundamental biological processes such as protein-ligand recognition, gene transcription, and nucleosome unwrapping. In complement to experiments, Markov State Models (MSMs) built from large-scale Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations provide a powerful approach to investigate dynamics of biological macromolecules at atomic resolution. The key insight of MSMs is to model how biomolecules dynamically change their conformations via a series of Markovian transitions among different conformational states at discrete time intervals (or lag time). The key for MSM’s success is that the lag time has to be sufficiently long to allow transitions among states to become Markovian (or memoryless). This imposes a major challenge for MSM studies of complex biomolecules because the lag time is bound by the length of relatively short MD simulations available to estimate the frequency of these dynamic transitions. We propose a new scheme: Memory Markov State Model (MMSM) that can accurately predict long timescale dynamics of biomolecules, but built from significantly shorter MD simulations compared to the memoryless MSM. The novelty of our proposed scheme is to introduce the memory kernel of conformational dynamics to our model, and then propagate the dynamics using a generalized master equation. The advantage of MMSM is that the memory kernel can be obtained from MD simulations with significantly shorter length in comparison with those required to construct memoryless MSMs. Our preliminary results on alanine dipeptide and WW domain (consisted of 35 residues) show that MMSM greatly improves upon MSM by being constructed from 5-10 times shorter MD simulations. We will employ the proposed MMSM to elucidate molecular mechanisms of the nucleosome DNA unwrapping and how post-translational modifications (PTMs) may impact this dynamic process. Elucidation of such mechanisms is crucial for understanding how DNA replication and gene transcription overcome nucleosome barrier and how PTMs regulate these biological processes. An important emphasis of our theoretical work will be to generate predictions that will be tested by our experimental collaborator, and these experiments will further help refine our theoretical models. 生物分子的構象動力學在例如蛋白質和配體識別，基因轉錄及核小體展開等諸多基本生物學過程中起著重要作用。作為實驗的補充，基於大規模分子動力學（MD）模擬構建的 馬爾可夫狀態模型（MSM）為研究生物大分子在原子尺度的構象動力學提供了一種有效的方法.MSM的關鍵點是運用沒有記憶的馬爾可夫態模型描述生物分子在離散時間間隔內在 不同構象狀態之間轉換的過程。因此，MSM成功的關鍵在於模型的滯後時間必夠足夠長，以允許狀態之間的轉換成為無記憶的過程。這對複雜生物分子的MSM研究提出了重大挑戰，因為滯後時間受到可用於估算構象態之間轉換概率的MD模擬軌跡長度的約束。 我們提出了一種全新的方案：記憶馬爾可夫狀態模型（MMSM）可以準確地模擬長時間尺度下的生物分子構象動力學，同時與無記憶的MSM相比，它可以構建在大大縮短的MD 模擬軌跡上。我們提出的方案的新穎性是將構象動力學的記憶核心引入到我們的模型中，然後使用廣義的主方程來傳播動力學過程。與MSM相比，MMSM的優點在於可以從非常短的MD模擬軌跡中得到記憶核心，從而進一步模擬長時間構象動力學的過程。我們對丙氨酸二肽和WW蛋白的初步研究結果表明，構建MMSM需要的MD模擬軌跡可以縮短到5到10倍。 我們將使用MMSM來闡明核小體DNA展開的分子機制以及翻譯後修飾（PTM）如何影響這一動態過程。闡明這些機制對於理解DNA複製和基因轉錄如何克服核小體屏障以及PTM如何調節這些生物 過程至關重要。我們的工作的一個重點是理論工作的預測將被我們的實驗合作者驗證，同時這些驗證實驗將進一步幫助改進我們的理論模型。

16304019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304019.value: Real data often exhibit heteroskedasticity and heavy-tailedness. Elliptical distributions are widely adopted to accommodate such features. This project aims to develop the statistical theory for analyzing large data sets under the elliptical model. Mainly, we will study how to estimate covariance matrices under a weak moment assumption, how to estimate and make inferences about some important quadratic forms that arise naturally in practice, and how to estimate optimal portfolios, all under the high-dimensional setting. 現實數據經常帶有異方差性和重尾性。橢圓分佈被廣泛採用來刻畫這類特性。這個項目旨在發展在橢圓型分佈下基於大型數據的統計理論。我們主要將在相對弱的勢假設下研究如何估計協方差矩陣，如何估計一些在實際應用中出現的二次型和做相關的統計推斷，以及如何估計最佳投資風險組合。

16304019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304019.value: 1. Jointly with former PhD Yi Ding and Yingying Li, we propose a high dimensional minimum variance portfolio estimator under statistical factor models and show that our estimated portfolio enjoys sharp risk consistency. The paper has been published in the Journal of Econometrics. 2. Jointly with former PhD Yi Ding, PhD student Guoli Liu and Yingying Li, We propose a Degree-Corrected Block Model with Dependent Multivariate Poissonedges (DCBM-DMP) to study stock co-jump dependence. We develop an algorithm that enjoys strong consistency in community detection. Empirically, we apply our algorithm to high-frequency data of S&P 500 constituents and find insightful co-jump networks, which are shown to be helpful in stock return prediction. The paper has been published in the Journal of Econometrics. 3. Jointly with Raymond Kan and Xiaolu Wang, we developed an inferential theory for Sharpe ratios under both finite samples and large N/T asymptotics. The paper has been published in the Journal of Financial Economics. 4. Jointly with former PhD Yi Ding, we study the estimation of the high-dimensional covariance matrix and its eigenvalues under dynamic volatility models. Data under such models have nonlinear dependency both cross-sectionally and temporally. We propose a time-variation adjusted (TV-adj) sample covariance matrix and prove that its LSD follows the same Marcenko-Pastur law as the i.i.d. case. Based on the asymptotics of the TV-adj sample co-variance matrix, we develop a consistent population spectrum estimator and an asymptotically optimal nonlinear shrinkage estimator of the unconditional covariance matrix. The paper is to appear in Annals of Statistics. 5. Jointly with former PhD Mengmeng Ao, current PhD student Leheng Chen and Yingying Li, we worked on large efficient Portfolio estimation based on heteroscedastic returns. The paper substantially relaxes assumptions in our earlier work (Ao, Li and Zheng (2019, Review of Financial Studies)), which requires returns to be iid normal. By allowing returns to be heteroscedastic, our new method can utilize higher frequency data like weekly or even daily rather than monthly. The method is found to perform superiorly both in simulation and empirical studies. The paper will be submitted soon. 6. Jointly with former PhD Yi Ding, we study the estimation of high-dimensional covariance matrices under heavy-tailed elliptical factor models. We develop an idiosyncratic-projected self-normalization (IPSN) method to remove the effect of heavy-tailed scale parameters, propose a robust pilot estimator for the scatter matrix, and show that the estimator enjoys the optimal sub-Gaussian rate. We further develop an estimator of the covariance matrix and show that it achieves a faster convergence rate than the generic POET estimator in Fan et al. (2018). The paper will be submitted soon.

16304019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304019.value: Elliptical models provide an important tool to model heavy-tailedness and tail-dependence, which are prevalent in many applications, including finance and economics. This project's results provide a foundation for further research in this direction, including more advanced machine learning approaches like transfer learning and distributionally robust learning.

16304019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304019.value: The research outputs of this project are of significant value in large portfolio optimization and risk management. Our estimators of mean-variance and minimum-variance portfolios have sound theoretical properties and empirically perform well. Our inference theory of Sharpe ratios reveals a new perspective for comparing multi-factor models with CAPM. Our co-jump networks provide valuable insights into the dependency of stocks in terms of their jump risks.

16304119.label: Project Objectives
16304119.value: To set up the mixed spin P-fields of hypersurfaces in products of projective spaces, study the moduli space of mixed spin P-fileds, and carry out calculations of higher genus GW invariants via the moduli space.
rows: To set up the mixed spin P-fields of hypersurfaces in products of projective spaces, study the moduli space of mixed spin P-fileds, and carry out calculations of higher genus GW invariants via the moduli space.

16304119.label: Realisation of objectives
16304119.value: Enumerative geometry of counting curves on a variety became a branch of algebraic geometry since Schubert time in late 19th century. It became one of the hottest research area since the work of physicists Candelas et. al who used physical arguments and mirror symmetry to predict some exact formula for counting genus zero curves on Calabi-Yau quintic threefolds. It started a new research direction in mathematics called Gromov-Witten theory and its related research areas such as mirror symmetry, Landau-Ginzburg theory, etc. The new way of curve counting on the mathematical side is called Gromov-Witten (GW for short) invariants. Physicists also studied the higher genus curve counting and formulated many surprising predictions. The most important curve counting is the GW invariants of Calabi-Yau three-folds such as the quintic hypersurface in the four dimensional projective space. Genus zero GW invariants of the Calabi-Yua quintic were thoroughly studied by Givental, Lian-Liu-Yau, Bertram among others. The formula for genus one GW invariants was studied by J. Li-Zinger, Vakil-Zinger and Zinger, and finally was proved by Zinger. The case of higher genus GW invariants have been intensively studied. Many people proposed various methods to compute the GW invariants for the Calabi-Yau quintic three-fold with much success until the PI and its collaborators developed a new method which was used to solve several key conjectures on higher genus GW invariants of the Calabi-Yau quintic three-fold. There is a large collection of Calabi-Yau three-folds such as the complete intersections in toric varieties. There is a natural temptation to extend the method to these Calabi-Yau three-folds. The original work by H.L. Chang, S. Guo, J. Li, Meliisa Liu, and PI is to use variation of GIT quotients to set up a moduli problem which contains both GW invariants and Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten (FJRW for short) invariants. The theory depends on the quintic polynomial. To extend the methodology to a general setup, several difficulties have to be resolved. One of the difficulties is the definition of stability conditions for the moduli problem. In the quintic case, we use the finiteness of the automorphism group as the stability condition. It turns out that this choice is not workable for our generalization. The other difficulty is the choice of p-field stable maps. We found that, to prove the properness of the degenerate locus of the cosection of the obstruction sheaf, p-field stable maps are not a workable choice. In our joint paper ``Mixed-spin-p fields for GIT quotients'' (arXiv:2312.11174 ) and ``A boundedness theorem for principal bundles on curves'' (arXiv:2312.11197 ), we consider a much larger collection of Calabi-Yau manifolds including complete intersections in toric varieties. In fact, we started with a geometric invariant quotient of an affine variety by a reductive group. In the first paper, we found a new concept of stability which includes the finiteness of the automorphism group in the case of Calabi-Yau quintic. The issue of p-field stable maps is resolved by considering a version of p-field quasi-maps. In fact, it is not the normal quasi-maps people encounter in the literatures. It is twisted by the dualizing sheaf of the curve. The choice of stability and the choice of the quasi-maps are interrelated. In the second paper, we consider the boundedness of the moduli problem. It turns out to be related to boundedness of moduli space of principal bundles on curves. This question has been studied by many people. Nevertheless, a rigorous treatment and a proof are still needed. In the second paper, we provided a proof for this question, and as a result gave the boundedness of our moduli problem. The key result in the first paper is to prove the properness of the moduli space with some condition on the GIT quotient space. With this properness established, we can do computations on the relevant moduli spaces. Unlike quintic Calabi-Yau case where there are only two GIT quotients involved, and hence there is only one dimensional path connecting these two GIT quotients, for a general case, there are more than two GIT quotients. For example, we studied the case of a Calabi-Yau hyper-surface in the product of two projective planes. In this case, there are three GIT quotients involved. Hence the space connecting all three quotients is two dimensional. We tried to use this two dimensional space to construct an MSP setup. But this caused some trouble for our computation, i.e., the computation becomes too complicated to get a meaningful formula. Then we tried to use one dimensional path to connecting two of the three GIT quotients. It turns out that the computations are effective in this setup. This indicates the subtlety of the choice of paths between various GIT quotients. We also tried to use MSP platform to study FJRW invariants. There are two line bundles in the MSP theory, denoted by L and N. The numerical invariants are the degree of L and the degree of LN. If we choose the degree of LN to be zero, the most information we obtain from the computation in the MSP theory relates to GW invariants. In the same way, if we choose the degree of L to be zero, the most information we obtain from the computation in the MSP theory relates to FJRW invariants. In our paper ``A genus-one FJRW invariant via two methods'' jointly with J. Li, Y.F. Shen and J. Zhou, we used MSP theory for the homogeneous cubic polynomial of three variables to compute the FJRW invariants. The Calabi-Yau counterpart is the elliptic curve in the projective plane. This also suggests that one can try to work on FJRW invariants of quintic polynomials of five variables. This will be part of our future work. The Covid seriously affected the planned activities of the project. There are several reasons to push up the expense in the item ``General Expenses'' (1) Due to the quarantine policies of the HK for visitors entering HK, some visitors decided not to come to HK. Instead of inviting them to come to HK, I had to visit them. (2) I attended some conference held in China during the Covid. I had to go through the quarantine in China. The expenses of the quarantine were covered by the grant. (3) Also the air tickets were more expensive. (4) After the end of the Covid, more on-site conferences were held. As a result, I attended more conferences.

16304119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16304119.value: The main objective of this project is to extend the method of mixed-spin-P-fields theory (MSP for short) for the quintic Calabi-Yau hypersurface in the four dimensional projective space developed by the PI with several collaborators to Calabi-Yau hyperplanes in a product of projective spaces. It is not a simple routine generalization. As we outlined in the proposal, there are several key issues to be addressed such as the search for a right definition of stability and a correct adoption of moduli spaces. In the preprints ``Mixed-spin-p fields for GIT quotients'' (arXiv:2312.11174 ) and ``A boundedness theorem for principal bundles on curves'' (arXiv:2312.11197 ) jointly with H. L. Chang, S. Guo, J. Li and Y. Zhou, we found a reformulation of stability conditions on the quasi-map p-fields. As a consequence, the reformulation agrees with the stability condition of Calabi-Yau quintic three-folds. The quasi-map p-fields replace the version of p-field theory of stable maps used in the paper ``The theory of N-Mixed-Spin-P fields.'' We also expand our scope from hypersurfaces in a project of projective spaces to complete intersections in a geometric invariant theoretic quotient space obtained from an affine variety quotient out by a reductive group. The GIT quotient includes toric varieties. Hence it covers a much larger collection of Calabi-Yau manifolds. In the combination of two papers, we proved the key result for making MSP theory computational feasible, which is that the moduli space of degenerate locus of the coseciton of obstruction sheaf is proper (or compact in analytic topology) under some mild condition. This lays the foundation for studying higher genus Gromov-Witten invariants for a large collection of Calabi-Yau three-folds. In the paper, ``A genus-one FJRW invariant via two methods'' jointly with J. Li, Y.F. Shen and J. Zhou, we studied the higher genus Fan-Jarvis-Ruan-Witten invariants (FJRW for short) for the cubic polynomial of three variables. The MSP theory contains Gromov-Witten theory of Calabi-Yau hypersurface defined by a homogeneous polynomial and Landau-Ginzburg theory of that polynomial. On the Calabi-Yau sector, we calculate Gromove-Witten invariants; on the Landau-Ginzburg sector, we calculate FJRW invariants. In our paper, we used MSP platform to calculate FJRW invariants for cubic polynomial of three variables, which corresponds to an elliptic curve in the projective plane, which is a kind of one dimensional Calabi-Yau manifold.

16304119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16304119.value: For the large collection of complete intersections of toric varieties, the Picard number will be bigger than one in most of the cases. The Picard number of the Calabi-Yau quintic three-fold is one, which corresponds to the fact that there are two GIT quotients. The space connecting two GIT quotients give arise to the MSP theory. If there are more than two GIT quotients, how to connect these GIT quotients needs to be studied in details. The computations will help us to design the feasible MSP-type theory. This is a theoretic part that needs to be explored. Another issue is the computational part. The smart choice of the MSP-type theory may make computations much easier. Along the same line, we can also compute FJRW invariants using the similar method. The result of this computation may help us to understand Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg correspondence for higher genus case. Most of the work done in this area is on genus zero and genus one case. The major difficulty lies in the lack of geometric setup for effective computations. We believe that MSP theory provides such geometric platform.

16304119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16304119.value: The enumerative geometry of counting the number of curves on a space with given conditions is a century old research topic in algebraic geometry. Physicists, using high power of physical arguments, give some exact formulae for these enumerative geometric counting. On mathematical side, the research to prove these formulae using mathematical arguments has been one of the hottest topics for the last thirty years. In the 90's of last century, mathematicians successfully proved the formulae for counting genus zero and genus one curves on Calabi-Yau quintics. Higher genus counting was only recently proved using the method developed by PI and his collaborators. The current project is to extend the method to other Calabi-Yau three-folds. In the project, we constructed a right moduli space where the computations can be done effectively. It opens the door for more research on counting of higher genus curves on a much larger collection of Calabi-Yau space.

16304219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304219.value: The goal of the proposed experimental research is to study the phase coherence of self-sustained oscillations induced by dynamical backaction in micromechanical resonators. Micromechanical resonators are widely used as sensors and actuators. In resonant sensors, vibrations of the micromechanical element are often excited by a periodic drive near its resonant frequency. By tracking changes in the resonant frequencies, the devices can be used in applications ranging from inertial sensing to high sensitivity force and mass detection. When a mechanical resonator is coupled to an optical, microwave or phonon cavity, the effective damping can be changed due to dynamical backaction. By controlling the backaction so that the energy gain compensates the energy loss due to intrinsic damping, self-sustained oscillations take place even with no periodic drive near the resonant frequency. As the phase of the self-sustained oscillations can take on arbitrary values, the coherence could be lost if the oscillations decay and re-emerge. The emphasis of the proposed research will be placed on revealing the conditions necessary for generating coherent self-sustained oscillations with driving that is made of incoherent noise. Two vibrational modes of a micromechanical resonator will be involved, with the mode at higher frequency acting as a phonon cavity that plays a similar role as optical cavities. Preliminary calculations indicate that for noise of sufficiently high intensity and finite bandwidth, stable self-sustained vibrations can in fact be generated. Remarkably, the spectral width of the self-sustained vibrations is much smaller that the noise bandwidth and the damping constants of the modes. In other words, an incoherent input produces vibrations of high spectral purity. We propose to explore the dependence of the spectral width and frequency of the self-sustained vibrations on the properties of the noise. Successful implementation of the proposed projects will not only stimulate new theoretical research and verify the validity of various theoretical approaches, but could also lead to micromechanical clocks of high stability and detectors of improved sensitivity and functionality. The PI has extensive experience with fluctuational phenomena in micromechanical devices. Under the support of a GRF grant that will soon expire, his group performed an extensive investigation of the strong anti-correlation of the phase diffusion of self-sustained vibrations of the mechanical and cavity modes. The PI will work closely with Prof. Mark Dykman, a theorist at Michigan State University to reveal novel behaviors of the coherence of self-sustained vibrations in micromechanical resonators. 我們建議的實驗研究的目標是研究微機電諧振器中由於動力學反作用引起的自激振盪中的相位相幹性。微機電諧振器被廣泛應用於傳感器和驅動器。在諧振傳感器中，微機電元件的震動通常是由處在諧振頻率附近的週期性驅動信號所激發的。通過監測共振頻率的變化，器件的應用範圍涵蓋了從慣性傳感到高靈敏度的力與質量的測量。當一個微機電諧振器與光子腔，微波腔，或者聲子腔相耦合時，動力學反作用會改變系統的有效阻尼常數。通過控制這種反作用使得系統的能量輸入能夠抵消固有阻尼導致的能量耗散，在沒有外加週期性諧振驅動力的條件下也能夠發生自激振盪。 由於自激震盪的相位是任意的，當震盪衰減並重新出現時可能會失去其相幹性。提案中研究計劃的重點在揭示通過由非相幹性噪聲組成的驅動信號產生相幹性自激振盪所需要的條件。實驗將涉及到微機電諧振器的兩個振動模式，其中頻率較高的模式作為一個聲子腔，扮演了和光子腔一樣的角色。初步的計算結果表明，對於強度足夠高的有限帶寬噪聲，穩定的自激振盪確實可以被激發。值得注意的是，自激振盪的頻譜寬度比噪聲本身的寬度和震動模式的阻尼常數要小得多。換句話說，一個非相幹性的輸入信號產生了高頻譜純度的震動。我們計劃探索自激振盪的頻譜寬度和頻率跟噪聲的性質之間的關係。提案中實驗的成功實施不僅能夠推動新的理論研究，驗證多種理論方法的正確性，還能夠帶來穩定性極高的微機電時鐘，以及靈敏度和功能性都有大幅度提升的探測器。 主要研究者在微機械器件的波動現象這一領域有豐富的經驗。在即將到期的優配研究金的資助下，他的團隊在機械和腔模式中自激振盪的相位漲落的強負相關性領域做了大量的研究工作。主要研究者將會與來自密歇根州立大學的理論物理學家Mark Dykman教授緊密合作，來研究微機械諧振器中自激振盪相幹性帶來的全新現象。

16304419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16304419.value: Networks are ubiquitous and play an important role in many areas of our lives. Examples include protein interaction networks, metabolic networks, species food webs, word-document networks, and scientific publication networks. Moreover, the recent prevalence of social media, such as Twitter and Facebook, has introduced a large volume of interesting and under-explored network data. The motivation behind network analysis varies across different areas. For example, marketing directors try to identify the most influential person in a network to achieve an optimal marketing effect through direct promotion, biologists are interested in finding hidden functional proteins in protein interaction networks, computer scientists wish to separate networks of tasks into groups to improve the efficiency of parallel computing, and social scientists try to characterize the structure of relations in a network. In this proposed project, we will study two aspects of network data. The first is how to incorporate the network information in the recommendation systems, in an attempt to making recommendations more accurate. The second is how to qualify the closeness of each cluster in the community. Both problems have theoretical and practical significance. 网络数据在生活中无处不在，包括蛋白质交互作用网络，不同物种食物链网络，社交网络，科技论文引用网络。网络数据充满很多有趣问题，这些研究在实际中发挥着重要的作用。 网络在不同领域的研究动机各自不同。在市场营销中，公司关注的是人群中最有影响的人群，以便在营销发挥最大的作用。在蛋白质交互作用网络中，生物学家感兴趣的是发现那些真正有功能的蛋白质。在并行计算中，计算机科学家把任务类似的计算机放在一起，以便提高计算效率。 在目前的研究项目中，我们着重研究下面俩个问题。首先，推荐系统目前研究的非常广泛且有着众多应用。我们希望能够把网络的信息也融入推荐系统，以便提高推荐的准确性。这些问题在实际中非常广泛，包括酒店推荐，电影推荐，音乐推荐等等。其次，网络千变万化，我们希望能够找到一些简单实用的指标去刻画各种类型的网络。这些问题不仅有理论意义，而且有非常重要的实际价值。

16304419.label: Realisation of objectives
16304419.value: We have achived the project objectives listed in the original proposal, and finished several papers. Some of these papers have been published and others are under review or preparation. In "collaborative Filtering with Awareness of Social Networks", we present the NetRec method to leverage the social network data of users in collaborative filtering. We formulate two new network-related terms and obtain convex optimization problems that incorporate assumptions regarding users’ social connections and preferences about products. Our theory demonstrates that this procedure leads to a sharper error bound than before, as long as the observed social network is well structured. We point out that the larger the noise magnitude in the observed user preferences, the larger the reduction in the magnitude of the error bound. Moreover, our theory shows that the combination of the network-related term and the previously used term of nuclear norm gives estimates better than those achieved by any of them alone. We provide an algorithm to solve the new optimization problem and prove that it is guaranteed to find a global optimum. Both simulations and real data experiments are carried out to validate our theoretical findings. The application of the NetRec method on the Yelp data demonstrate its superiority over a state-of-the-art social recommendation method. In "Community Detection on Mixture Multilayer Networks via Regularized Tensor Decomposition", we study the problem of community detection in multilayer networks, where pairs of nodes can be related in multiple modalities. We introduce a general framework, that is, mixture multilayer stochastic block model (MMSBM), which includes many earlier models as special cases. We propose a tensor-based algorithm (TWIST) to reveal both global/local memberships of nodes, and memberships of layers. We show that the TWIST procedure can accurately detect the communities with small misclassification error as the number of nodes and/or number of layers increases. Numerical studies confirm our theoretical findings. To our best knowledge, this is the first systematic study on the mixture multilayer networks using tensor decomposition. The method is applied to two real datasets: worldwide trading networks and malaria parasite genes networks, yielding new and interesting findings. In "Community Detection in Sparse Networks using the Symmetrized Laplacian Inverse Matrix", we propose a new method for detecting communities in sparse networks that uses the symmetrized Laplacian inverse matrix (SLIM) to measure the closeness between nodes. The idea comes from the first hitting time in random walks, and has a nice interpretation in diffusion maps. Community membership is acquired by applying the spectral method to the SLIM. The SLIM outperforms state-of-art methods in many real data sets and simulations. It is also robust to the choice of tuning parameter, in contrast to spectral clustering with regularization. Theoretical analyses show that in sparse scenarios generated by stochastic block model, the SLIM ensures the same order of misclassification rate in E(degree) as that of regularized spectral clustering.
