16306119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306119.value: [1] Evidence for bosonization in a three-dimensional gas of SU(N) Fermions [Bo Song et al. Physical Review X 10 041052 (2020) In this work, we developed a highly sensitive detection method and measured Tan's contact in a SU(N) Fermi gas. Recent advancements in condensed matter physics and high energy physics have blurred the line between bosons and fermions. Previous studies have reported the bosonization of SU(N) fermions in 1D with exact solutions. However, two important questions remain. First, does this phenomenon occur in higher dimensions where exact solutions are not available? Second, can other quantities besides a single quantity demonstrate bosonization? Our research addresses both questions by conducting quantum simulations with multi-component fermions in 3D. We present a comprehensive approach, both experimentally and theoretically, to test bosonization in a multi-component 3D fermionic system based on the concept of contact. [2] Heurisitic machinery to uncover hidden features of SU(N) fermions with neural networks [Entong Zhao et al. Nature Communications 12 2011 (2021)] In this work, we demonstrated an alternative method of detecting Tan's contact using machine learning. We used convolutional neural networks (NNs) to uncover hidden features in quantum many-body systems. We focused on a multi-component Fermi gas with repulsive interactions within SU(N) symmetry and achieved >94% accuracy in probing spin multiplicity through machine learning (ML)-aided single shot analysis. With well-trained NNs, we revealed hidden thermodynamic features in the momentum distribution of fermions and verified them using experimental data. Our work provides a concrete example of how machine learning techniques can uncover hidden physical features in quantum many-body systems and deepen our understanding of the underlying physics [3] Topological control of quantum states in non-Hermitian spin-orbit-coupled fermions [Z Ren et al. Nature Physics 18 385-389 (2022)] Despite the significant progress in non-Hermitian physics, a SOC mechanism and related topological phases have been widely studied only in Hermitian systems [e.g., B Song et al., Nature Physics 15 911 (2019) achieved by our own group] but much less is known experimentally when the dissipation plays a major role in spin-orbit-coupled quantum systems. The better understanding of such non-Hermitian SOC is of particular importance for classifying non-Hermitian topological phases, which still remains elusive in the condensed matter physics. Nevertheless, the experimental realization of non-Hermitian SOC remains unexplored in quantum systems. In this work, we realize tunable dissipative spin-orbit-coupled bands for ultracold atoms, fully characterize the PT symmetry-breaking transition.

16306119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306119.value: A widely applicable concept in the study of strongly correlated systems is the search for a universal relation that characterizes the interaction between quantum phases. One model system that has garnered significant interest is a dilute quantum gas with short-range interactions. In this system, several observables, such as the high-momentum tail of the momentum distribution, the tail of the rf spectral function, and the energy variation with respect to the scattering parameter, can be determined universally using a single parameter known as Tan's contact. Our discovery establishes a set of universal relations that connect the microscopic short-range correlations with the macroscopic thermodynamic quantities, providing a novel approach to comprehending the behavior of interacting quantum gases.

16306119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306119.value: In the proposed project, our goal was to study the interactions between multi-component fermionic particles. To achieve this, we measured the Tan's contact, which characterizes this interaction property in a dilute quantum gas, specifically in the high-momentum tail. The findings of this project provide a solid foundation for understanding how multi-component fermions can exhibit behavior similar to bosons, resulting in the counter-intuitive phenomenon known as bosonization. These findings will contribute to a better understanding of interacting many-body systems and showcase the potential of quantum simulation using ultracold atoms.

16306319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306319.value: The development of non-fullerene acceptors have improved the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs) up to ~14% by reducing the voltage loss. There are two types of non-fullerene OSCs with small voltage loss, namely donor-acceptor systems with small offset of either lowest unoccupied (LUMO; Type A) or highest occupied (HOMO; Type B) molecular orbitals. We recently discovered how charges separate in Type A systems. During his visit to Cambridge, the project PI has developed a new approach named “pump-push-probe-electroabsorption spectroscopy” (PPP-EA) to measure charge-transfer excitons (CTEs) in non-fullerene OSCs. In conventional pump-probe spectroscopy, it is difficult to distinguish CTEs from free charges as they both appear as polarons. However, with this new PPP-EA approach, the PI successfully isolated the signal of CTEs by creating a characteristic EA signal with the additional “push” pulse. Our results show that CTEs in Type A non-fullerene OSCs have remarkably long lifetime of 100ps, and such slow but efficient charge separation is the key reason for the reduced voltage loss compared to fullerene OSCs. Our manuscript is currently under review. The goal of this project is to understand charge dynamics in Type B systems. Despite our recent findings on Type A systems, the charges dynamics in Type B systems remains unclear. Type B systems are important to study because they generally have greater photocurrent quantum yields, higher fill-factors and much stronger absorption in the near-infrared than Type A systems. Importantly, our preliminary work indicates that Type B systems could be significantly different from Type A systems. Our key findings include: 1) While Type A systems suffer geminate recombination of CTEs that reduces the short-circuit photocurrent by ~15-20%, we find less geminate recombination in Type B systems which could be related to reduced interfacial trapping due to better morphology. 2) Type B systems tend to exhibit stronger EL and lower non-radiative losses, and this could be due to better domain purity of the acceptor molecules. 3) Despite their differences, we do observe long-lived CTEs in both types of systems. In this project, we aim to study Type B systems based on the promising directions provided by our preliminary results. We target to use PPP-EA to measure CTE dynamics in Type B systems and identify the key factors that enable high performance. With improved understanding, we will establish new material design guidelines for improving OSC performance. The final goal is to work with Prof Yan to develop new materials with >15% efficiency. The development of non-fullerene acceptors have improved the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs) up to over 14% by reducing the voltage loss. There are two types of non- fullerene OSCs with small voltage loss, namely donor-acceptor systems with small offset of either lowest unoccupied (LUMO; Type A) or highest occupied (HOMO; Type B) molecular orbitals. We recently discovered how charges separate in Type A systems. During his visit to Cambridge, the project PI has developed a new approach named “pump-push-probe- electroabsorption spectroscopy” (PPP-EA) to measure charge-transfer excitons (CTEs) in non-fullerene OSCs. In conventional pump-probe spectroscopy, it is difficult to distinguish CTEs from free charges as they both appear as polarons. However, with this new PPP-EA approach, the PI successfully isolated the signal of CTEs by creating a characteristic EA signal with the additional “push” pulse. Our results show that CTEs in Type A non-fullerene OSCs have remarkably long lifetime of 100ps, and such slow but efficient charge separation is the key reason for the reduced voltage loss compared to fullerene OSCs. Our manuscript is currently under review. The goal of this project is to understand charge dynamics in Type B systems. Despite our recent findings on Type A systems, the charges dynamics in Type B systems remains unclear. Type B systems are important to study because they generally have greater photocurrent quantum yields, higher fill-factors and much stronger absorption in the near-infrared than Type A systems. Importantly, our preliminary work indicates that Type B systems could be significantly different from Type A systems. Our key findings include: 1) While Type A systems suffer geminate recombination of CTEs that reduces the short-circuit photocurrent by ~15-20%, we find less geminate recombination in Type B systems which could be related to reduced interfacial trapping due to better morphology. 2) Type B systems tend to exhibit stronger EL and lower non-radiative losses, and this could be due to better domain purity of the acceptor molecules. 3) Despite their differences, we do observe long-lived CTEs in both types of systems. In this project, we aim to study Type B systems based on the promising directions provided by our preliminary results. We target to use PPP-EA to measure CTE dynamics in Type B systems and identify the key factors that enable high performance. With improved understanding, we will establish new material design guidelines for improving OSC performance. 16306319.label: Realisation of objectives
16306319.value: During this project we have carried out a series of studies to understand electron-hole separation processes in efficient non-fullerene organic solar cell (OSC) materials designed with small HOMO-HOMO offsets. We have successfully completed all four of our project objectives, and our results have led to four publications in peer-reviewed journals (see full list below and in Part C). First, we designed and performed time-resolved optical experiments to measure exciton and charge dynamics in a series of non-fullerene OSC materials with varying degrees of HOMO offsets and photovoltaic efficiencies. These include PM6:Y6, PM6:N3, PM6:Y6-1O and PM6:Y6-2O, etc. Our results show that charge generation occurs in the following steps: (1) Exciton separation into interfacial charge-transfer (CT) states happens between ~1 to ~50 ps, with the slow timescale due to diffusion of excitons initially generated far from the interface; (2) CT states can thermally separate into free electrons and holes on the ~10 to 100 ps timescale; (3) Free carriers are transported across the blended film and can be extracted at the electrodes unless recombination events happen. Temperature dependent measurements were found to mainly affect process (2). Furthermore, by calibrating the transient absorption data with electroabsorption (EA) signal that arises from the Stark effect, we were able to extract the electrostatic binding energies of CT states in various material systems. For efficient material systems with small HOMO offsets, such as PM6:Y6, we measured a binding energy of ~100 meV [Ref. 1]. This experimental value is also in close agreement with theoretical value calculated using DFT simulations [Ref. 2]. In collaboration with other institutes, we discovered large electron-hole wavefunction delocalisation in aggregated state of Y6 molecules, due to the strong intermolecular interactions. As a result, we showed that this delocalisation effect effectively lowers CT state binding energies at the donor:acceptor interface. Such delocalisation effect also helps to explain the large exciton diffusion lengths in Y6-type molecules, as we observed in our optical experiments (process (1)). Taken together, our combination of experimental and theoretical results provide a detailed understanding of the charge generation process in state-of-the-art non-fullerene OSCs with small HOMO offsets. Our experiments reveal that OSC systems with both small LUMO and small HOMO offsets have rather similar charge generation processes and dynamics. However, by systematically comparing two model systems, namely P3TEA:SF-PDI2 (small LUMO) and PM6:Y6 (small HOMO), we found that the key difference between their charge separation efficiency lies in their differences in electron-hole binding energies at the donor/acceptor interface [Ref. 1). For P3TEA:SF-PDI2, we measured a binding energy of ~230 meV, much larger than the ~100 meV we measured for PM6:Y6. We attribute the strong intermolecular interactions of Y6 molecules as the major reason for the reduced binding energy. We performed transient photovoltage measurements to quantify charge recombination rates in a series of small HOMO offset systems. We controlled the morphology by modifying the chemical structure of the Y6 molecules, including aymmetric alkoxy and alkyl substitutions. We found that the recombination rates depend strongly on morphology, which we characterised using synchrotron X-ray measurements [Ref 3]. With alkoxy substitution, the resulting molecule (Y6-2O) shows extremely poor performance due to low solubility and excessive aggregation properties, a change that is due to the conformational locking effect of alkoxy groups. In contrast, asymmetric alkyl and alkoxy substitution on Y6, yields a molecule named Y6-1O that can maintain high PV performance (slow recombination rate) and obtain reasonably good solubility. The resulting molecule Y6-1O enables highly-efficient non-fullerene OSCs with 17.6% efficiency. Furthermore, we discovered that charge recombination rate can be further reduced by employing a multi-component blend strategy, leading to the so-called ternary or even quaternary blends. In our work [Ref. 4], we uncovered the mechanism behind the improved performance in multi-component OSC blends based on materials with small HOMO offsets. Using a combination of spectroscopy methods, we showed that the multi-component systems demonstrate a ‘‘rivers and streams’’ functional hierarchical (multi-length scale) morphology, where small domains of PTQ10 and PCBM act as separators that spatially separate PM6 and N3, which effectively suppressed charge recombination, enhanced hole transport and allow balanced charge transportation. These results reveal the correlation between charge recombination rates and molecular and morphological properties of efficient (>15%) OSC systems based on donor/acceptor materials with small HOMO offsets. Taken together, our studies uncover the photophysical mechanism for efficient charge generation in efficient nonfullerene OSC materials with small HOMO offsets, highlighting the important roles of electron-hole wavefunction delocalisation, strong intermolecular packing, CT state binding energy, hierarchical morphology, etc. Optimisation of these molecular and morphological properties are thus the key toward highly efficient OSC devices with over 15% efficiency and beyond. 16306319.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306319.value: Our results reveal the charge generation and recombination dynamics in a series of organic solar cell materials with small HOMO offsets. Using a combination of ultrafast optical spectroscopy and quantum chemistry computation, we found that strong intermolecular interactions enable delocalisation of electron-hole pairs. This lowers the electrostatic binding energy of electrons and holes at the interface, promoting free carrier generation even at the absence of large HOMO (or LUMO) offsets. Furthermore, we revealed the close relationship between molecular design and blend morphology control on the charge recombination rates. Importantly, we showed that intricate morphology control can be achieved using multi-component blend strategy, in which charge recombination can be greatly suppressed when a ‘‘rivers and streams’’ functional hierarchical (multi-length scale) morphology is achieved, leading to high OSC efficiency of ~17.7%.

16306319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306319.value: The efficiency of OSC has improved greatly from ~12% in 2015 to ~19% in 2022, matching the performance of commercial inorganic cells available in the market. However, there remains further research opportunities in this field. First, the efficiency is still limited by excessive non-radiative charge recombination loss that limit the device open-circuit voltage and therefore hinders the development of OSC devices with 20-25% efficiency. This is a fundamental and interdisciplinary challenge for the research community. Second, the device stability remains poor, typically no longer than ~1000 hours of continuous sunshine. This is fundamentally related to the thermodynamic instability of the blend morphology. Overcoming this problem is necessary for technology transfer.

16306319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306319.value: Today’s solar photovoltaic (PV) cells are based on inorganic silicon, which are costly to fabricate, have large carbon footprint and are difficult to integrate into urban environments. To address climate change and meet the target of carbon neutrality by around 2050, it is critical to develop new solar cell technologies with: 1) high solar energy conversion performance, 2) low fabrication cost, 3) small carbon footprint and 4) the capability to integrate with our environment, especially in urban areas where energy demand is highest. Organic solar cells (OSCs) have emerged as a promising candidate since they can be solution-processed at relatively low-temperatures, have tunable optical absorbance and transparency, have high mechanical flexibility and lightweight, and do not contain toxic or precious materials. However, further improvements in device efficiency and stability are needed before OSCs can be used in real products. This project targets to establish an in-depth understanding of the mechanism behind charge generation in state-of-the-art OSC materials and devices. Our results provide fundamental insights for future OSC design and development.

16306519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16306519.value: Spontaneous mutations in subpopulations of cells can lead to tumor heterogeneity or bacterial clonal diversity, which can result in diverse clinical phenotypes, such as poor prognosis or drug resistance. Early detection of these deleterious mutations is challenging not only because they are present in very low concentrations, but also because they are usually 100- or 1000-fold diluted with other cells containing only single-base differences. Therefore, their detection requires a method that is highly sensitive for detecting very low concentrations of the target, and highly selective in differentiating the target from highly abundant single-base mutant variants. Conventionally, these genetic alterations can be determined using massively parallel DNA sequencing with the accuracy increasing proportionately to the depth or the number of times each DNA sample is sequenced. However, when multiple base calls are observed in one position, it is difficult to differentiate random errors incurred during the amplification and sequencing process from a mutant variant with very low variant allele frequency (VAF). Thus, for genetically heterogeneous samples, additional short oligonucleotide sequences are usually appended to the DNA fragments prior to amplification which can subsequently be interpreted using bioinformatics tools, such as barcodes to verify whether the mutations were present in the original sample. A second approach leverages the specificity of Watson-Crick base-pair hybridization to construct nucleic acid circuitries that can selectively detect the presence of single nucleotide variants (SNVs) even at low VAFs. This approach entails calculating the thermodynamics of the DNA interactions and designing a nucleic acid probe that best differentiates the target from the SNV. Despite the rational design of the probe, some residual reaction caused by the binding of a spurious target to the probe occurs and to a greater extent because it is present at a much higher concentration. Thus, a two-step nucleic acid circuit with enhanced selectivity will be developed by coupling a rationally designed toehold-mediated strand displacement reaction with a specific endonuclease cleavage step that generates a fluorescence signal only when the target binds to the toehold probe. In addition, a heterogeneous approach will be developed in which the sample will be first allowed to flow through a monolithic column containing immobilized rationally-designed toehold probes, and then a specific endonuclease enzyme will be used to selectively release correctly-bound targets. This strategy mimics the sample purification ability and the selectivity and separation efficiency of affinity-based chromatography to detect targets with low VAFs in a complex sample matrix. 細胞亞群的自發突變可導致腫瘤的異質性或細菌克隆的多樣性，從而呈現出不同的臨床表型，如預後的差異以及細菌的耐藥問題。這類突變與正常細胞相比僅有一個鹼基的變化，並且濃度較低，通常為正常細胞的1/100-1/1000，這給有害突變的早期診斷提出了挑戰。因此，需要一種高靈敏度的方法來檢測極低濃度的目標物，同時具有高度選擇性，可以將目標物與大量的單鹼基突變體區分開來。 通常，這類遺傳變異可採用大規模平行DNA測序來鑑定，其準確度與每個DNA樣品測序的深度或次數成正比。然而，當在同一位點測得多種鹼基結果時，很難區分這樣的結果是來自低頻等位基因 (VAF)的突變體，還是由於擴增和測序過程中所產生的隨機誤差。因此，對於遺傳異質性樣品，在擴增之前，通常會將一系列短核酸序列連接到DNA片段上，這些序列在生物信息學的分析過程中被識別為條形碼，用以驗證突變是否來自於原始樣品。 第二種方法利用Watson-Crick鹼基對雜交的特異性，構建即使在低頻等位基因存在時，亦能選擇性檢出單核苷酸變異(SNV)存在的核酸分子線路。該方法需要對相互作用的DNA進行熱力學計算，從而設計出能最大程度區分靶標與單核苷酸變體 (SNV)的核酸探針。但這種方法的弊端是，儘管設計出了合適的探針，但高濃度的假靶標依然會與探針反應，從而造成檢測誤差。 因此，本研究提出一種兩步法增強型選擇性核酸分子線路，該方法將優化設計的Toehold核酸探針所介導的鏈置換反應與特異性內切酶切割反應相結合，核酸內切酶反應只會在靶標結合到Toehold探針時才發生，並產生熒光信號。樣品會首先流過固定有toehold探針的整體柱，隨後核酸內切酶選擇性地釋放特異性結合的熒光標記物。同時，本研究借鑒了親和層析技術中對樣本的純化、選擇和分離的原理實現對複雜樣本中低頻等位基因突變的檢測。

16306519.label: Realisation of objectives
16306519.value: In objective 1 we characterized a few restriction enzymes that would offer highly specific catalytic activity compatible with the design of synthetic nucleic circuits for low-VAF alleles. We identified and characterized a CRISPR/Cas12a system for the highly sensitive and specific detection of rare variant alleles. Specifically, we introduced for the first time a sensitive, protospacer adjacent motif (PAM)-independent, and ultra-selective Cas12a detection mechanism by rationally designing the probe to decouple the PAM sequence from the target sequence, and amplify the signal using a non-canonical double-stranded DNA trans-cleavage activity, to which the superior selectivity of the strategy is attributed. With this work, Objective 1 was successfully completed. Next, building on the previous method, we coupled a Cas12-based signal transduction system with nucleic isothermal amplification, termed CoLAMP (CRISPR-based one-pot detection with loop-mediated isothermal amplification). CoLAMP leverages the rationally programmed competition kinetics between LAMP and AapCas12b reactions to transduce a visual or electrochemical signal and simultaneously deplete amplifiable DNA molecules to reduce the risk of aerosol contamination. The highly specific and sensitive assay was performed in an in-house extraction-reaction-readout one-pot device leveraging sample capture and flow through a microfluidic channel with RNA immobilization and magnetic separation. This flow-based sample purification method is simpler and more efficient than the column-based strategy originally proposed, and fully achieved the Objective 2. It is to note that this device derived from our experience during the development of the Etaq-PCR platform, a portable, deployable, and cost-effective PCR electrochemical device suitable for clinical applications also developed in this research proposal. In Objective 3, it was proposed to use a hybridization purification assay and enzyme digestion to detect different DNA sequences. We coupled our Cas12-based enzymatic assay with pre-concentration and amplification steps, detecting up to 10 aM and 0.1% of the EGFR gene T790M mutation (and 10 fM of the wild type target) in a commercial cell-free DNA reference standard in human plasma. Additionally, we developed a hybridization assay for detection of SARS-CoV-2 in infected individuals in pooled samples through a barcoding strategy during reverse transcription. Unused DNA barcodes that could interfere in the downstream PCR reaction were digested by an exonuclease prior the amplification and detection step, which was carried out using melting curve analysis. This PCR-based strategy allows the identification of the infected individual in the pooled sample without retesting, which is a drawback of current pooled testing methods, such as the Dorfman test. Overall, this two research outputs successfully achieved Objective 3.

16306519.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306519.value: Our research activities in this project have yielded significant findings and outcomes with significant potential in genetic mutation detection and point-of-care molecular diagnostics. One major finding is the characterization of a CRISPR/Cas12a system for the highly sensitive and specific detection of rare variant alleles. We were the first to introduce a sensitive, protospacer adjacent motif (PAM)-independent, and ultra-selective Cas12a detection mechanism by rationally designing the probe to decouple the PAM sequence from the target sequence, and amplify the signal using a non-canonical double-stranded DNA trans-cleavage activity. This system also reduces noise from wild-type sequences, enabling the detection of mutations at sub-femtomolar concentrations with high specificity. This breakthrough allows for the early detection of genetic variants associated with diseases like cancer and bacterial infections. The research led to a paper published in Biosensors and Bioelectronics and an invited book chapter (journal paper # 1 and 2). Another key achievement was the development of Etaq-PCR, a portable real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) platform that integrates electroactive hydrolysis probes in an electrochemical-based device. Unlike traditional PCR methods, Etaq-PCR does not require complex electrode surface treatments or microfabrication, making it cost-effective and easily deployable. Importantly, Etaq-PCR demonstrated exceptional sensitivity, selectivity, and rapidity, meeting the WHO ASSURED criteria for point-of-care diagnostics. Validation experiments showed 100% accuracy in detecting drug resistance genes in clinical samples, compared with gold standard qPCR, highlighting its potential for point-of-care applications. This work was published in the Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry (Journal paper #3). Additionally, we developed an efficient and cost-effective method to detect infected individuals in pooled samples without the need for retesting, as it is required in conventional PCR with sample pooling methods (e.g. Dorfman pooled testing). Our PCR-based method relies on individual-specific barcoding during reverse transcription and decoding through post-PCR melting curve analysis. It significantly reduces the total assay time for large-scale screening without compromising the specificity and sensitivity, and was able to successfully differentiate five samples, positive and negative, in one pool with negligible cross-reactivity among the positive and negative samples. Importantly, our research addressed many other challenges in point-of-care molecular diagnostics, particularly regarding contamination risks during testing for infectious diseases such as SARS-CoV-2. Based on our 2 previous works, we developed an amplicon-depleting CRISPR-based one-pot loop-mediated isothermal amplification (CoLAMP) assay, which significantly reduces aerosol contamination by destroying amplifiable products at the end of each test. The CoLAMP assay demonstrated high sensitivity, detecting SARS-CoV-2 RNA at concentrations as low as 0.5 copies/μL in clinical samples within 40 minutes. Furthermore, we designed low-cost sample-to-result devices for fluorescence-based visual interpretation and deployed a commercial portable electrochemical platform for point-of-care diagnostics. This work was published in Biosensors and Bioelectronics (Journal paper #4).

16306519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16306519.value: Building on the foundations laid by our research activities, there are numerous potential paths for further development of our methods, technologies, and platforms, as well as the exploration of new applications. Regarding the mutation detection, our ultra-selective Cas12a-based system has shown remarkable promise in detecting rare genetic mutations. Our work in developing portable and user-friendly diagnostic platforms, such as Etaq-PCR, opens up possibilities for decentralized testing in resource-limited settings. Further optimization and validation of our system across a broader range of genetic variations and targets and sample types could enhance its utility in clinical settings. Therefore, the achievements from the Cas12a-based detection method, and the lessons learned from developing the Etaq-PCR platform, were fundamental for our research that led to the CoLAMP assay and device technology. We are currently developing enhanced detection systems to streamline these platforms and improve the robustness of Cas12a-based molecular diagnostic assays. Also, we are working on the feasibility of simple yet reliable device platforms to meet the real demands of point-of-care testing, particularly after the COVID-19 pandemic. Finally, we are collaborating with local hospitals to carry out the validation of the clinical diagnostic performance of technologies that stemmed from those here presented. Overall, the potential for further development of our research is vast, with opportunities to enhance diagnostic accuracy, accessibility, and affordability, ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes and public health outcomes globally.

16306519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306519.value: The completed research project focused on developing innovative methods for detecting rare genetic mutations, which can have significant impacts on diseases like cancer and bacterial infections. Traditional methods often struggle to detect these mutations accurately due to their low frequency and the presence of similar variations. As a result, we pioneered a highly selective Cas12a-based system, termed CoLAMP, that can detect specific mutations with remarkable sensitivity, opening new possibilities for precision medicine. Additionally, our team devised other approaches, including a portable nucleic acid detection portable PCR platform called Etaq-PCR, which can quickly and accurately identify genetic variations even in complex clinical samples, and an efficient method for sample-specific detection that can detect infected individuals in pooled samples exemplified with COVID-19. Furthermore, throughout the development of these technologies, we addressed several other challenges in point-of-care molecular diagnostics, such as reducing contamination risks during testing for diseases like COVID-19, by designing innovative and highly accurate CRISPR-based assays and affordable, user-friendly devices to detect genetic biomarkers. These advancements not only improve our understanding of sequence variations in infectious and genetic diseases but also pave the way for more effective diagnosis and treatment strategies, ultimately benefiting patient care and public health.

16306919.label: Major findings and research outcome
16306919.value: We have developed a new peptide identification method that is able to analyze multiple PTMs more accurately than state-of-the-art methods, including our own method PIPI, which offered the best performance before the new method was developed. The key finding is that, by using tags of longer length and adding fidelity measures, we can achieve better performance in terms of reliability. Also, by using a divide-and-conquer idea and an approximation of the linear programming, we have improved the accuracy of PTM identification from 40% in the previous PIPI method to more than 70% when analyzing simulated data with two PTMs. We have finished validation using simulation data, simplified protein mixture data and real data. The results have confirmed the superior performance of our new method than state-of-the-art methods. We are now drafting a paper, in which we call our new method PIPI 2.0, as described in reference [5] in part C. We also plan to file a patent on this new method.

16306919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16306919.value: In this project, we have significantly improved the performance of existing methods in identifying peptides with multiple post-translational modifications (PTMs). The best bench mark in the research community was our own published method named PIPI, which achieved an accuracy of around 40% when identifying peptides with two PTMs (checked using simulation data). Our newly developed method can improve the accuracy up to 70% according to our validation results. Given this significant improvement, it becomes now feasible to systematically study PTMs in biomedical and biological research.

16307019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307019.value: 混合維度范德華（vdW）異質結構是指單層2D材料與其他常規低維結構的集成，包括0D量子點（QD），1D納米線（NW）和3D體系。 2D單層無懸掛鍵表面使得這種集成具有很大的靈活性。傳統的低維結構和2D單層之間的耦合和相互作用為我們提供了組合，使用和操縱它們各自特性和功能的潛力。其結果是這些混合維度vdW異質結構可以揭示全新的物理現象並且可以改善各自的物理性質，從而使其具有在電子學和光電子學中有潛在的各種應用。在這個研究項目中，我們將專注於于包含半導體2D層和QD以及NW的混合維度vdW異質結構。混合維度vdW異質結構將使用兩種方法製造：剝離的2D半導體在自組裝QD和分散的QD和NW上的機械組裝，以及使用化學氣相沉積方法在具有QD和NW的基板上直接生長2D半導體。我們將利用光學測量技術研究這些混合維度vdW異質結構中的界面耦合和激子態相互作用。我們的目標是探索這些結構的新現象和新功能，以便其在電子和光電器件中有潛在的應用。

16307019.label: Realisation of objectives
16307019.value: We have fabricated hybrid ML-WS2/InGaN QDs heterostructures by transfer ML-WS2 on MOCVD grown InGaN QDs on GaN substrate. The ML-WS2 is partially covered by few-layer graphene (FLG) which serves as the top electrode. In this hybrid FLG/WS2/QDs mixed dimensional heterostructure device, we have demonstrated that either the photo-holes or photoelectrons generated in the QDs can be injected vertically into the WS2 channel, transporting laterally therein, and be collected by the FLG electrode. Ambipolar conduction of the ML-WS2 can be realized through photocarrier doping, eliminating the requirement of a gate voltage. This work is published in EDL. We have fabricated h-BN/ML-WS2/SiO2/Si structures with two Au/Cr electrodes on top of the h-BN for applying an in-plane electric field. We have conducted the spatially- and time-resolved PL measurements and observed both the diffusion and the drift of negative trions in monolayer WS2. We have estimated trion diffusion coefficient and drift velocity from our results. This work is published in Nano Lett. We have fabricated a hybrid vertical junction devices made of strained few-layer graphene and InGaN QDs. Using scanning photocurrent microscopy, we observe significant photocurrent enhancement. Optoelectronic response and photoluminescence measurements demonstrate a possible mechanism closely tied to the flexoelectric effect in few-layer graphene, where the strain can induce a lateral built-in electric field and assist the separation of electron−hole pairs. Photocurrent mapping reveals an unprecedentedly ordered hexagonal network, suggesting the potential to create a superlattice by strain engineering. This work is published in Nano Lett. We have fabricated BN/ML-WS2/BN heterostructures. We have observed a series of sharp PL peaks. In order to understand the origins of these PL emissions, the detailed measurements by applying magnetic field, changing temperature and excitation power, and applying gate voltages have been carried out. We have especially investigated the polarization behaviors of the trion states in ML-WS2 via helicity-resolved magneto-photoluminescence spectroscopy under linear-polarized laser excitation. The manuscript based on based on this work is under review for PR Applied. We fabricate monolayer WS2-InGaN QDs heterostructure and measure its PL spectra. Interfacial bound state composed of trion in WS2 and exciton in QDs is formed with the coupling of WS2 and QDs, and evidences are provided through PL spectra in many dimensions, such as power dependence, temperature dependence, helicity dependence and magnetic field dependence. The manuscript based on based on this work is in preparation.

16307019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307019.value: We demonstrated effective ambipolar photocarrier doping and lateral transport in the ML-WS2 in a hybrid FLG/WS2/QDs heterostructure device. By introducing a gate electrode on the ML-WS2 between the illuminating position and the FLG electrode, n-channel or p-channel transistors could be developed with the illuminating position as the photosource electrode and the FLG as the drain electrode. This work is published in IEEE EDL. We directly observed the diffusion and drift of trions in monolayer WS2. The effective diffusion coefficient of trions is measured to be 0.47 cm2/s at 6 K with a 50 μW excitation power. When an in-plane electric field is applied, the trions drift toward the opposite direction of the electric field with a drift velocity of 7400 cm/s with an in-plane electric field of 3 × 104 V/cm. The diffusion-induced broadening and drift induced shift of the trion emission profile show saturation characteristics due to the Coulomb attraction between mobile trions and the localized ionized donors. Excitation power and temperature-dependent trion diffusion and drift measurements reveal that the trions are scattered by other trions, electrons, and phonons in trion transport. Our study clarifies fundamental principles in electrically driven trion transport and paves the way to realize controllable photonic circuits. This work is published in Nano Letter. We demonstrate significant strain-induced photocurrent enhancement in the FLG/InGaN QD junction, which is most probably associated with a flexoelectric-driven mechanism. Our findings provide insights into the optoelectronic behaviors of 2D materials in the presence of a strain gradient. The unraveled electromechanical coupling provides exciting implications for electromechanically active materials and nanodevices based on graphene. This work is published in Nano Letter. We have observed that the magnetic-field dependence of the polarization degree of the singlet trions is negative at nondegenerate electron-density regime and becomes positive at weakly degenerate electron-density regime, while that of the triplet trions remains positive. In a bimolecular formation scenario that a trion is bound state of an exciton and an electron, we proposed a model to quantitatively analyze the polarization behaviors of the triplet and singlet trions from the valley polarizations of the electrons and excitons. This work also reveals that for the development of ML-WS2 based valley-opto-electronic devices employing trions as the carrier, samples with lower electron-density are preferred as the helicity of the emissions under linear-polarized light excitation can be tuned more effectively.

16307019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307019.value: What we have achieved so far indicate that the mixed dimensional heterostructures can offer additional insights on the atomic thin 2D materials. The properties of 2D layers can be effectively manipulated by zero dimensional quantum dots. All these results allow for further study of these heterostructures. They are promising candidates for advanced electronic and optoelectronic device applications. These should be the future focus of the research and actions to take.

16307019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307019.value: Conventional semiconductor heterostructures have been well studied over the past 40 years for their new fundamental physics phenomena and new electronic and optoelectronic device applications. While the vdW heterostructures of 2D materials have many advantages over conventional heterostructures. For example, no lattice match is required in vdW heterostructures, nor is there atomic diffusion at the sharp interfaces. The so-called mixed-dimensional vdW heterostructures are formed by combining 2D materials with conventional nanostructures like quantum dots (QDs). The dangling bond-free surface of 2D materials means that mechanical transfer or overgrowth can readily achieve this kind of integration with great flexibility. The coupling and interaction between conventional QDs and 2D materials allow us to combine, use, and manipulate their respective properties and functions in mixed-dimensional vdW heterostructures. In this research, we have studied the mixed-dimensional vdW heterostructures formed by combining 2D materials with quantum dots (QDs). Our research has shown that the existence of QDs in the heterostructure are crucial for the realization of photocarrier doping ambipolar conduction of 2D material WS2, which eliminates the requirement of a gate voltage in such a device, and the photocurrent enhancement of few layer graphene, which provides exciting implications for nanodevices based on graphene.

16307219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307219.value: Indole alkaloids are one of the largest classes of alkaloids. Many indole alkaloids (e.g., serotonin, lysergic acid) exhibit significant biological activity by acting on the central and peripheral nervous systems and some of them (e.g., vinblastine and vincristine) have been used in the treatment of various types of cancers. The medicinal and biological importance of indole alkaloids has aroused intensive and long-lasting interest in developing new methods and strategies for their chemical synthesis. Great advances in chemical synthesis of indole alkaloids have been made in the past decades. However, the generality, flexibility and efficiency of chemical synthesis remain extremely challenging. This research proposal focuses on the development of a new asymmetric three-component synthetic method for collective total synthesis of indole alkaloids. The first part of the study involves developing an enantioselective three-component reaction, called redox-A3 reaction of Amine (tryptoline), Aldehyde and Alkyne. The redox-A3 reaction was reported by three independent research groups in 2013 and exploited by our group for collective total synthesis of tetrahydroisoquinoline alkaloids (2016-2018). Extension of this redox-A3 reaction for synthesis of indole alkaloids has not been reported and necessitates the use of tryptoline as the amine, which has not been examined in a catalytic asymmetric setting. Therefore, the first part of our proposal describes optimization of reaction conditions and identification of the chiral ligand that enables the copper-catalyzed redox-A3 reaction of tryptoline to proceed in high enantioselectivity. Preliminary results show that high enantioselectivity of redox-A3 reaction of tryptoline could be achieved, representing the first example of asymmetric synthesis of alpha-alkynyl tryptoline. The second part of the study demonstrates the synthetic utility of the enantioselective redox-A3 reaction of tryptoline in collective total synthesis of three families of indole alkaloids, which have been shown in the literature to be biologically active. These three indole alkaloids are (1) pentacyclic vincamine-eburnamine-tacamine (VET) alkaloids, (2) tetracyclic corynanthe-type alkaloids exemplified by geissoschizine, geissoschizol, corynantheidine and corynantheidol, and (3) tetracyclic spirooxindoles including corynoxine, corynoxine B, (iso)corynoxeine and (iso)rhynchophylline. The spirooxindoles are biogenetically derived from corynanthe-type indoles through oxidative rearrangement. Therefore, they are proposed to be synthesized collectively in a biomimetic strategy through oxidative rearrangement of corynanthe-type compounds. In summary, the proposed research provides a general solution to the synthetic challenge of an efficient, unified, and enantioselective strategy for monoterpene indole alkaloids, and may find wide applications in organic synthesis, medicinal chemistry (drug discovery) and chemical biology. 吲哚生物鹼是天然生物鹼中最大類別之一。許多吲哚生物鹼（例如，5-羥色胺，麥角酸）通過作用於中樞和外周神經系統而表現出顯著的生物活性，並且它們中的一些（例如，長春鹼和長春新鹼）已經用於治療各種類型的癌症。吲哚生物鹼在醫藥和生物學上的重要性已經引起了人們對開發其化學合成的新方法和策略的強烈興趣。在過去的幾十年中，化學合成已經在吲哚生物鹼方面取得了巨大進步。然而，化學合成仍然極具挑戰性,特别是普遍性、靈活性和效率等問題。本研究提案的重點是開發一種新的不對稱三組分合成方法，用於集體全合成吲哚生物鹼。該研究的第一部分開發對映選擇性三組分反應，稱為胺（tryptoline），醛和炔烴的氧化還原-A3反應。於2013年，三個獨立的研究小組報告了氧化還原-A3反應，隨後我們研究小組利用此三組分反應，以四氫異喹啉生物鹼作為底物實現一系列黃連素集體全合成（2016-2018）。然而，目前尚未有文獻報導該氧化還原-A3反應的延伸，並用於合成吲哚生物鹼的，以tryptoline作為胺底物的三組分反應尚未實現不對稱催化。因此，我們提案的第一部分描述了優化反應條件和尋找合適的手性配體，使其對tryptoline的銅催化的氧化還原-A3反應能夠以高對映選擇性進行。初步結果表明，我們可以實現tryptoline的氧化還原-A3反應的高對映選擇性，這是α-炔基類tryptoline不對稱合成的第一個例子。該研究的第二部分闡明對tryptoline的對映選擇性氧化還原-A3反應在三類具有生物活性的吲哚生物鹼家族的集體全合成。這三類吲哚生物鹼分別是（1）五環長春胺 - 琥珀酰胺 - 噻嗪（VET）生物鹼，（2）四環枸杞類生物鹼，例如geissoschizine，geissoschizol，corynantheidine和corynantheidol，和（3）四環螺鞘醇，包括corynoxine，corynoxine B，（ iso）corynoxeine和（iso）rhynchophylline。螺環吲哚通過氧化重排從corynanthe型吲哚生物遺傳衍生。因此，提出通過corynanthe型化合物的氧化重排在仿生策略中共同合成它們。總之，本提案為單萜吲哚生物鹼的高效、集體式和對映選擇性全合成挑戰提出了一般解決方案。此方案將在有機合成，藥物化學（藥物發現）和化學生物學中找到廣泛的應用。

16307219.label: Major findings and research outcome
16307219.value: The asymmetric synthesis of C1-alkynyl tetrahydro-β-carbolines is rather underdeveloped in the literature and the only example (Mei method) was low yielding (<30%). Upon completion of this project, we have developed two complementary approaches for the asymmetric synthesis of C1-alkynyl tetrahydro-bcarbolines through enantioselective alkynylation of 3,4-dihydro-β-carbolinium (DHbC) ions. The first approach relies on the redox strategy to access the DHbC ions, whose reactivity and enantioselectivity of C1-alkynylation was profoundly influenced by the protecting group on the indole nitrogen atom: Electron-donating groups favored the reaction with excellent yield and enantioselectivity, whereas electron-withdrawing groups inhibited the reaction. The substrate scope of this approach was examined with 23 examples, but one major limitation is also recognized (non-aromatic aldehydes were not successful substrates). This limitation prompted us to develop an alternative approach for the generation of 3,4-dihydro-b-carbolinium (DHbC) ions: N-alkylation of 3,4-dihydro-b-carbolines. While mechanistically similar to the first alkynylation, different reaction conditions were identified, as triethylamine plays a key role in the reactivity and enantioselectivity. The second approach addresses the major limitation and greatly expands the availability of different optically active C1-alkynyl tetrahydro-b-carbolines. The synthetic utility of the enantioenriched C1-alkynyl tetrahydro-β-carbolines was demonstrated by asymmetric total syntheses of seven indole alkaloids: harmicine (5 steps, 31%overall yield), eburnamonine (5 steps, 24% overall yield), desethyleburnamonine (5 steps, 28%overall yield), larutensine (8 steps, 27% overall yield), geissoschizol (7 steps, 24% overall yield), geissochizine (7 steps, 8% overall yield), and akuammicine (7 steps, 8% overall yield). It is expected that these two catalytic asymmetric alkynylation approaches will find wide application in the chemical synthesis of indole alkaloids. This work is Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 25135–25142.

16307219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307219.value: This project has developed two complementary approaches for the asymmetric synthesis of C1-alkynyl tetrahydro-bcarbolines through enantioselective alkynylation of 3,4-dihydro-β-carbolinium (DHC) ions, which are expected to find wide applications in chemical synthesis of indole alkaloids as demonstrated in the publication. Further development of this research is to exploit this synthetic strategy for collective synthesis of a library of indole alkaloids and evaluate their biological activity, which is ongoing in our lab.

16307219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307219.value: Many indole alkaloids (e.g., serotonin, lysergic acid) exhibit significant biological activity by acting on the central and peripheral nervous systems, the medicinal and biological importance of indole alkaloids has aroused intensive and long-lasting interest in developing new methods and strategies for their chemical synthesis. This research project is focusing on the development of a new asymmetric three-component synthetic method and then apply it to the collective total synthesis of indole alkaloids. This asymmetric method has addressed the generality, flexibility and efficiency of carbon-carbon bond formation with full control of chirality. The synthetic utility of the enantioselective redox-A3 reaction of tryptoline has been demonstrated in the total synthsis of pentacyclic vincamine-eburnamine-tacamine (VET) alkaloids and tetracyclic corynanthe-type alkaloids exemplified by geissoschizine, geissoschizol, corynantheidine and corynantheidol. In summary, this project reserach provides a general solution to the synthetic challenge of an efficient, unified, and enantioselective strategy for monoterpene indole alkaloids, and may find wide applications in organic synthesis, medicinal chemistry (drug discovery), and chemical biology.

16307319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16307319.value: The proposed project will focus on the well-posedness, Sobolev regularity, and unconditional energy stability analyses of two frequently used stochastic phase field models. The two equations, the stochastic Allen-Cahn and the stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equations, are driven by general multiplicative infinite dimensional Wiener processes. The proposed study will also derive the associated unconditional energy stability and optimal strong and weak error analysis for a family of Galerkin-type fully discrete numerical schemes. Phase field models have become common in physical and chemical applications that involve the phase separation of multi-component mixtures, especially when there are multiple sources of uncertainty. Therefore, it is necessary to consider stochastic effects and to study the impact of noise on the regularities of the solutions and their long-term behaviors. More and more researchers are conducting mathematical and numerical analyses of the Allen-Cahn and the Cahn-Hilliard equations perturbed by white and colored noises. Most previous studies have concentrated on investigating the well-posedness and long-term behavior of the solutions and on designing efficient numerical schemes with strong and weak convergence rates in the mean and probability distribution senses, respectively, to complement the stochastic equations. Due to the roughness of the noise and the non-Lipschitz continuity of the potential term, there are difficulties in obtaining strong and weak convergences with optimal rates for reasonable numerical approximations of the stochastic Allen-Cahn and stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equations. To overcome this difficulty, the main tool in the proposed project will be to combine the mild solutions approach based on semigroup theory with the variational solutions approach based on variational methodology. We will discretize the spatial variable using finite element or spectral Galerkin approximations, to take advantage of the high accuracy of the Galerkin methods and the established theory for error estimates; we will discretize the temporal variable using Euler or Milstein schemes. The main goal of the proposed approach is to obtain optimal strong and weak error estimates of these schemes as applied to the stochastic Allen-Cahn and stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equations driven by possibly high dimensional white and colored noises. We also intend to examine the unconditional energy stability independent of the temporal and spatial step sizes for these schemes. We will generalize the developed methods to study other types of stochastic phase field equations, such as the coupling of the stochastic Allen-Cahn and stochastic Cahn-Hilliard equations, and solve them numerically to verify our theoretical results. 该项目将集中于两个常用的随机相场模型的适定性、Sobolev 正则性以及无条件能量稳定性分析。 这两个方程，随机 Allen-Cahn 方程和随机 Cahn-Hilliard 方程，是由一般的乘性无穷维 Wiener 过程驱动的。本文的研究还将得到一族 Galerkin 型全离散格式的无条件能量稳定性和最优强、弱误差分析。 相场模型在涉及多组分混合物相分离的物理和化学应用中已普遍应用，尤其是当存在多种不确定性来源的时候。因此，有必要考虑随机因素，从而研究噪声对解的规律及长期影响。越来越多的研究者对白噪声和彩噪声扰动下的 Allen-Cahn 方程和 Cahn-Hilliard 方程进行了数学和数值分析。以往的研究大多集中在研究随机方程解的适定性和长期行为，以及分别在均方和概率意义上设计具有强、弱收敛率的有效数值方案。由于噪声的粗糙度和位势项的非全局 Lipschitz 连续性，获得随机 Allen-Cahn 方程和随机 Cahn-Hilliard 方程的合理数值近似的最优的强、弱收敛率非常困难。为了克服这一困难，本项目的主要工具是将基于半群理论的温和解方法与变分法和基于变分理论的变分解方法相结合。 我们将使用有限元或谱 Galerkin 近似来离散空间变量，以利用 Galerkin 方法的高精度和完备的误差估计理论；使用 Euler 或 Milstein 格式来离散时间变量。这个策略的主要目标是获得前述全离散格式应用于高维白噪声和彩噪声驱动的随机 Allen-Cahn 和随机 Cahn-Hilliard 方程的最佳强、弱误差估计。我们还将研究这些格式的与时间和空间步长无关的无条件能量稳定性。我们将推广所发展的方法来研究其他类型的随机相场方程，如随机 Allen-Cahn 和随机 Cahn-Hilliard 方程的耦合，并且应用数值模拟来验证我们得到的理论结果。

16307319.label: Realisation of objectives
16307319.value: For objective 1, we have conducted well-posedness and optimal regularity analyses of the stochastic Allen-Cahn equation driven by one-dimensional multiplicative white noise [1]. We have derived sufficient and necessary conditions for the existence of the unique solution and establish its regularity. We have established a covariance operator dependent condition for the well-posedness of the stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) through the convergence analysis for a sequence of solutions of SPDEs with the noise term replaced by its spectral projections. This sequence of SPDEs also plays an important role in constructing our numerical solutions for the SPDE. We also proved existence and uniqueness of a mild solution of stochastic heat equation on a higher dimensional Riemannian manifold [2]. Specifically, we extended Funaki's theorem to a higher dimensional Riemannian manifold. We gave meaning to a certain stochastic PDE based on Davies's heat kernel estimate. We also showed that the resulting mild solution obtained by this approach is a Markov process. For the Cahn-Hillard equation, we studied the well-posedness of a modified degenerate Cahn-Hilliard type phase field model for surface diffusion with long-range elastic interaction [3] that was derived from microscopic stochastic scheme [4]. We showed that this model is able to give the correct sharp interface limit. We introduced a notion of weak solutions for this nonlinear model. The existence result is obtained by approximations of the model with nondegenerate mobilities. Well-posedness of Cahn-Hilliard equation with spatially stochastic potential under this physical background has been proved [5]. For objectives 2 and 3, we have conducted unconditional energy stability analysis with its discrete version for the stochastic Allen-Cahn and use it to derive the optimal strong convergence rate for a family of Galerkin-type fully discrete scheme in [6]. We established a general theory of optimal strong error estimation for numerical approximations of a second-order parabolic stochastic partial differential equation with monotone drift driven by a multiplicative infinite-dimensional Wiener process. The equation is spatially discretized by Galerkin methods and temporally discretized by drift-implicit Euler and Milstein schemes. By the monotone and Lyapunov assumptions, we used both the variational and semigroup approaches to derive a spatial Sobolev regularity and a temporal Holder regularity for the solution of the proposed equation. Then we made full use of the monotonicity of the equation and tools from stochastic calculus to derive the sharp strong convergence rates for the Galerkin-based Euler and Milstein schemes, respectively. Our ideas in [6-8] together with the properties of the SPDEs obtained in [1] have been applied to derive regularity and strong convergence rate of Galerkin finite element approximations for second-order stationary SPDEs [1]. A general error estimate framework has been established for the finite element approximations. Based on this framework, optimal error estimates of finite element approximations for elliptic SPDEs driven by power-law noises are obtained. It was shown that with the proposed approach, the convergence order of white noise driven SPDEs is improved by half for one-dimensional problems, and by an infinitesimal factor for higher-dimensional problems. Convergence rate of Galerkin finite element approximations for Cahn-Hilliard equation with spatially stochastic potential derived from materials science has been obtained [5]. For objective 4, we have derived a stochastic continuum model based on the Peierls-Nabarro framework for dislocations (line defects) in a high entropy alloy incorporating the atomic level randomness [9]. The Peierls-Nabarro model is a phase field type model that describes the core structure of dislocations. The obtained continuum model can be considered as a generalization of the stochastic Allen-Cahn equation and the classical, deterministic Peierls-Nabarro model. High entropy alloys are a novel class of crystalline materials that consist of random solid solutions of multiple elements in approximately equal proportions and have exhibited superb mechanical properties. We used asymptotic analysis and limit theorem in the convergence from the atomistic model to the continuum model. We have also derived stochastic continuum models for HEAs with short-range order from atomistic models [10]. A proper continuum limit is obtained such that the mean and variance of the atomic level randomness together with the short-range order described by a characteristic length are kept in the process from the atomistic interaction model to the continuum equation. The obtained continuum model with short-range order is in the form of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process. These derivations also validate the stochastic models adopted phenomenologically in the research in [11]. We have also derived boundary condition for dislocation dynamics simulation in bcc crystals based on the molecular dynamics model [12]. Continuum models for crystalline materials derived from atomistic models that incorporate the stochastic effect caused by finite temperature have been obtained based on the Cauchy-Born rule for crystals with and without defects [13,14]. Regularity and strong convergence rate of Galerkin finite element approximations for second-order stationary SPDEs have also been obtained, and a general error estimate framework has been established for the finite element approximations [1]. Convergence rate of Galerkin finite element approximations for Cahn-Hilliard equation with spatially stochastic potential derived from materials science has been obtained [5]. We have derived stochastic continuum models by convergence from the atomistic models based on the Peierls-Nabarro framework for dislocations (line defects) in a high entropy alloy (a novel class of crystalline materials), incorporating the atomic level randomness with and without the short-range order [9,10]. These stochastic models are generalizations of the stochastic Allen-Cahn equation and the classical, deterministic Peierls-Nabarro model. We have also derived boundary condition for dislocation dynamics simulation in crystals based on the molecular dynamics model [12]. Continuum models for crystalline materials derived from atomistic models that incorporate the stochastic effect caused by finite temperature have been obtained based on the Cauchy-Born rule for crystals with and without defects [13,14]. (References are given in section 5.3 of this report.)

16307319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16307319.value: In this project, most of the mathematical and numerical analyses results are based on the Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard type stochastic equations in one dimensional spatial domain. Future works may include generalizations of these approaches and results to stochastic equations in higher dimensions or with other types including but not limited to the stochastic equations in materials science derived in this project. High entropy alloys are a novel class of crystalline materials that are based on atomistic level randomness and have exhibited superb mechanical properties. The one-dimensional stochastic continuum models for high entropy alloys derived in this project may also be generalized to two- and three-dimensions.

16307319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16307319.value: Phase field models are an important class of modeling tools in science and engineering applications, and such applications often involve stochastic effects. It is essential to incorporate these stochastic phenomena in the continuum models and to understand the nature of these equations and their numerical discretization by rigorous mathematical tools. In this project, mathematical and numerical analyses have been performed for the frequently used phase field models of the Allen-Cahn and Cahn-Hilliard types. We have conducted well-posedness and optimal regularity analyses of these stochastic equations driven by white and colored noises, based on the mild solutions and the variational and semigroup approaches. We have derived optimal convergence rates for Galerkin-type discrete schemes for these stochastic equations. We have also conducted unconditional energy stability analyses with their discrete versions for these equations. Generalizations have been explored to derive stochastic continuum models by convergence from the atomistic models for the novel materials of high entropy alloys and the crystalline materials under the finite temperature effects, incorporating the atomic level randomness. The obtained results in this project provide a basis for the further analysis and numerical study for the models that describe stochastic effects in a wide range of science and engineering applications.

16308219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308219.value: Encoding information in matrices is one of the most powerful ideas in the world of modern mathematics; the language of matrices plays a major role in a wide range of areas including mathematical physics, machine learning, engineering, and theoretical computer science. The study of random matrices is very active, due to the explosive growth in mathematical descriptions in the random matrix theory literature and its plausible applications in the era of Big data. This project is motivated by fundamental questions that arise naturally in the study and analysis of large datasets. In recent years, rapid progress has been made in understanding the spectral behavior of random matrices, in particular, the universality phenomena for classical random matrix models such as Wigner matrices and random independent matrices. However, in many situations, emerging mostly from applied mathematics, the classical ensembles are of limited significance. The proposed research projects will aim to analyze random matrices whose dependency structures are more complicated than those of the classical ensembles. The principal investigator intends to continue her research program on the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of different ensembles of random matrices of a large size. The project will aim to derive refined norm estimates for the random Toeplitz and Hankel matrices, whose entries come from a sequence of independent but not necessarily identically distributed random variables. Such Toeplitz or Hankel matrices appear naturally in time series analysis, econometrics and signal processing. One basic question is to accurately describe how large the operator norms are. In particular, we will explore the interplay between the underlying geometric structure of the random model and its probabilistic behavior. This project will also build in part on the principal investigator's recent works to obtain a clear picture of the behavior and properties of the eigenvectors and singular vectors of large matrices. The project will focus on random matrix models with a low-rank deformation. One popular instance is a spiked covariance matrix model, first proposed by Johnstone, in which all of the population eigenvalues are one expect for a fixed number of eigenvalues. Other related models include the spiked separable covariance matrix, matrix denoising model, etc. It will investigate the phase transition phenomena for the eigenvectors or singular vectors of these deformed random matrices in full generality. 在矩阵中编码信息是现代数学世界中最有力的思想之一。矩阵的使用在数学物理，机器学习，工程和理论计算机科学等广泛领域中发挥着重要作用。由于近些年随机矩阵的数学理论的快速发展及其在大数据时代的众多应用，随机矩阵的研究非常活跃。该项目主要研究在大型数据集的研究和分析中自然产生的有关随机矩阵的基本问题。 近年来，在理解随机矩阵的谱行为方面（尤其是是经典随机矩阵模型的普遍性现象）取得了快速进展 。然而，这些经典随机矩阵模型在实际问题的应用有限。因此，本研究项目旨在分析有结构的随机矩阵。这些随机矩阵的元素之间有更强的依赖关系 ，本项目打算研究这类随机矩阵的特征值和特征向量。 本项目的一个方向是导出随机托普利兹矩阵（Toeplitz matrix）和汉克儿矩阵（Hankel matrix）的精确范数估计，我们假设这些矩阵的元素来自于一系列独立但不一定相同分布的随机变量。托普利兹或汉克儿矩阵在时间序列分析，计量经济学和信号处理中经常出现，其中最基本的问题是估计这类随机矩阵的范数大小。 另一方面，基于该研究者最近的关于随机矩阵特征向量和奇异向量的工作，该项目将继续研究尖峰协方差矩阵模型（ 这个模型由Johnstone提出），给出这类协方差矩阵的特征向量的相变现象的全面的刻画 。

16308219.label: Realisation of objectives
16308219.value: The project has successfully met all its objectives. We examined the operator norms of random Toeplitz and Hankel matrices, focusing on models with entries of varying variance. Using the moment method, we analyzed the traces of high powers of these matrices, employing intricate combinatorial counting to distinguish between major and minor terms in the expansion. This approach led to a precise refinement of the bounds on the operator norms of these structured random matrices, achieving optimal results in specific cases and broadening our understanding of random Toeplitz and Hankel matrices. This marks the completion of the project's first objective. Additionally, we conducted a thorough investigation into the statistical properties of eigenvalues, eigenvectors, singular values, and singular vectors across various perturbative random matrix models. Utilizing tools from random matrix theory, we gained a detailed insight into the spectral behavior of these models, fulfilling the project's second objective. Moreover, we provided an exact characterization of the limiting empirical spectral distribution for non-backtracking matrices associated with an Erdos-Renyi graph G(n,p), under the condition that np/log(n) tends to infinity. Our analysis revealed that partial derandomization of the non-backtracking matrix significantly simplifies its spectrum. By applying Tao and Vu's replacement principle and the Bauer-Fike theorem, we demonstrated that the spectrum of the partially derandomized matrix closely approximates the original. This accomplishment addresses the second objective of our proposal. The methodologies utilized in our research incorporated advanced techniques from combinatorics, probability, and geometric functional analysis, thereby also achieving the project's third objective. The relatively large expenses for "Research Staff" and small expenses for "General Expenses" as compared to the approved budget were due to the impact of Covid. I was not able to travel or invite visitors to Hong Kong because of the travel restrictions.

16308219.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308219.value: In our 2022 publication in the Annals of Statistics, we explored the spiked covariance matrix model and determined the joint distribution of the extreme eigenvalues along with their associated eigenvectors in the supercritical regime. This study is particularly significant for Principal Component Analysis, offering valuable insights from a statistical perspective. In a subsequent paper published in Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (2023), we provided a detailed characterization of the limiting empirical spectral distribution (ESD) for non-backtracking matrices associated with an Erdos-Renyi graph G(n,p). Our analysis demonstrated that partial derandomization of these matrices greatly simplifies their spectrum. By employing Tao and Vu's replacement principle along with the Bauer-Fike theorem, we showed that the spectrum of the partially derandomized matrix closely mirrors that of the original matrix. Another study, published in Mathematics (2023), delved into two distinct types of probability measures on the set of integer partitions of n with at most m parts. The first measure selects a random partition based primarily on the size of its largest part. We established the limiting distributions for all parts collectively, as well as for the largest part alone, as n increases while m remains fixed or also increases. Notably, if m increases at a controlled rate, the largest part adheres to the central limit theorem. The second measure is broader, encompassing the Dirichlet and uniform distributions as special cases. Here, we derived the asymptotic distributions of the parts by considering limits for n and m in a similar manner to the first measure. This line of inquiry originated from a discussion with my collaborator, Tiefeng Jiang, on the spectral properties of random Toeplitz and Hankel matrices. Currently, we are finalizing a paper that provides a refined upper bound on the operator norms of random Toeplitz and Hankel matrices, particularly those with entries exhibiting varied variance. This upcoming result promises to set a new benchmark for upper bounds in the study of such random matrix models.

16308219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308219.value: The PI is advancing the study of spectral behaviors in low-rank deformed random matrix models with heteroskedastic entries, crucial for statistics and applied mathematics. Concurrently, there exists a significant gap in understanding structured random matrices, like Toeplitz and Hankel matrices. The complexity of their entry correlations makes current random matrix theory methodologies inadequate. To bridge this gap, the PI plans to deepen the exploration of these matrices, necessitating the creation of new analytical tools and insights. This research aims to enhance theoretical foundations and broaden practical applications in scientific domains, by developing more effective methods to analyze structured random matrices.

16308219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308219.value: This research project focuses on studying specific types of matrices called Toeplitz and Hankel matrices, which are important in fields like time series analysis, econometrics, and signal processing. These matrices are built using sequences of random variables that are independent but not identical. The project aims to understand how large the values (norms) of these matrices can get, which is crucial for accurately analyzing data in the mentioned fields. Additionally, the project will explore how the structures of these matrices influence their behavior in probabilistic terms. This involves deepening our understanding of the properties of eigenvectors and singular vectors—the components that describe the directions and magnitudes in data transformations—in these matrices. Part of the project also looks at special kinds of matrices known as low-rank deformed matrices. These are used in statistical methods to enhance signal detection in noisy data, as seen in the spiked covariance matrix model. The research will investigate how these matrices change under different conditions, a concept known as phase transition. Overall, this project aims to provide clearer insights into the behavior of complex matrix structures, thereby improving the reliability of mathematical tools used in various scientific and engineering applications.

16308319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308319.value: 南海北部陸坡（NSSCS）位於呂宋海峽（LS）以西，毗鄰西太平洋（WPO）。通過LS的水體交換和南海（SCS）與WPO之間的營養鹽濃度差異共同調控進出SCS的營養鹽通量。 NSSCS位於SCS氣旋（逆時針）環流主通道的上游，是整個SCS的營養鹽流入和流出的重要源區。NSSCS通過氣旋環流連接SCS海盆、陸架及其他部分。由於NSSCS上的陸坡環流和地形之間的相互作用，強大的沿陸坡和跨陸坡（垂直方向）營養鹽輸運極大地影響了SCS中生態系統動力學、生物地球化學循環及海洋環境變化中營養的源和匯。NSSCS中的營養鹽輸運和生態系統動力學極其複雜，涉及到季風驅動的運輸、通過LS的黑潮入侵、跨陸坡運輸的內部動力學及上層海洋中的生物地球化學過程。目前對於調控NSSCS中營養鹽收支和基礎營養鹽動力學的機制和過程仍然知之甚少，其中與來源於本地和遠程強迫的物理和生物地球化學過程相關的營養鹽動力學存在巨大的不確定性。基於對先前研究的分析和我們的先導數值實驗，我們在此提出以下科學假設：1）由LS入侵流導致的營養鹽通量、由陸坡環流和地形相互作用導致的沿陸坡和跨陸坡通量、以及通過NSSCS北部、西部和南部邊界的通量是決定NSSCS中營養源/匯的主要控制因子；2）與世界其他海域陸坡上較弱的跨陸坡輸運不同，NSSCS中存在強烈且持久的沿陸坡和跨坡營養鹽通量，且具有高時空變化性；3）NSSCS中的營養鹽動力學主要由擴散、平流、生物生產及再礦化之間的相互作用和反饋調控。我們建議使用歷史觀測數據和定制的三維高分辨率耦合物理-生態系統-生物地球化學模型來檢驗這三個科學假設。模型結果將用於量化營養鹽輸運及收支的三維通道，確定內在的動力機制和生態系統響應，並研究它們的相互聯繫和對NSSCS海域、鄰近大陸架及整個SCS海盆的生物地球化學過程的潛在影響。本項目的研究將具有區域相關性和全球意義。

16308319.label: Realisation of objectives
16308319.value: In order to achieve the predetermined project objectives, we have made the following efforts: 1. Historical data collection and analysis We gathered remotely sensed data and recorded observation data to validate our models and conduct comprehensive analyses. The remotely sensed chlorophyll data were derived from MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) and SeaWiFS (Sea-viewing Wide Field-of-view Sensor) data set. The field observation data (salinity, temperature, NO3 and PO4) were collected from many previous cruises, such as the cruises under the CHOICE-C project (The process, mechanism and its global implication of the carbon cycling in the South China Sea), KEEP project (Kuroshio Edge Exchange Processes), and JGOFS project (Joint Global Ocean Flux Study). 2. Model development We developed a 3-D numerical modeling to simulated the physical and biogeochemical processes in the NSSCS as well as the whole SCS. The model was built on our developed China Sea Multiscale Ocean Modeling System (CMOMS) (https://odmp.ust.hk/cmoms/). The biogeochemical part of this model uses a nitrogen phosphorus co-limited biological module that developed by ourselves based on the biological module of the ROMS (Regional Ocean Modelling System). The model was initialized with winter climatological WOA13 (World Ocean Atlas 2013) salinity and potential temperature. The initial fields of nitrate and phosphate were merged from field observations and data from WOA01 data (World Ocean Atlas 2001) data). The initial field of chlorophyll was obtained from the WOA01 annual average. The other biological variables were derived from chlorophyll in fixed proportions. 3. Model validation and evaluation Based on the observational data, we improved the performance of our model and validated the model results. After systematic evaluation, the model results compared reasonably well with observations and can capture the major features of the physical and biogeochemical processes in this area. Figure 1. Comparison of observations and model results for chlorophyll and nutrients. (Please refer to the appendix in section 11 for figures) 4. Quantify the nutrient transports and budget The Southeast Asian monsoon drives the slope current over the northern slope of the SCS, and the Kuroshio intrusion from the WPO through Luzon Strait modulates the current. Strong influxes (flow into the slope zone) of nutrients through the eastern boundary are simulated. The transport in Luzon Strait has an inflow-outflow-inflow sandwich structure in the upper-middle-deep layers, respectively. Yet, the nutrient flux through the eastern boundary of our study region has inflow in all three layers. We found that after intruding onto the northern slope of the SCS region, the current flows along the steep slope around the basin and forms the basin-wide slope circulation. In the upper layer, the main portion of the slope current flows off the northern slope of the SCS along the west continental margin while a smaller portion flows southwesterly off the northern slope. The former portion eventually flows out of the SCS through Karimata Strait, and the latter portion exits the SCS through Mindoro Strait. Together, the two portions form the SCS throughflow. The nutrient flux crossing the northern boundary has a much smaller magnitude than the transports through the eastern and western boundaries due to the shallower water in the north, the oligotrophic waters of the northern region, and the relatively weak cross-slope current in the north. Nevertheless, the transport through the northern boundary is very important to the exchanges of volume and biogenic materials between the shelf and slope, quantitative analysis will be performed in the next section. The nutrient transport across the different boundaries is also strongly seasonal. The overall transport through the eastern boundary is stronger in winter when the westward intrusion of the Kuroshio is stronger because the Kuroshio Current is weaker in winter. Figure 2. Nitrate transport and budget of the northern slope of the SCS. (Please refer to the appendix in section 11 for figures) 5. Identify the intrinsic and extrinsic controlling mechanisms Cross-isobath nutrient fluxes vary along the slope, with a unique alternating distribution. Nutrient exchange pathways are fixed along the northern slope, controlled by topography. Strongest downslope transport occurs on the western side over concave isobaths. Similar pathways occur at convex/concave isobaths, resulting in alternating distribution. Sea surface elevation and pressure gradient force along the topography control cross-slope transport. Exchange weakens with decreasing water depth and weaker slope current. Vertical turbulent mixing becomes the main nutrient source in the upper mixed layer, and vertical advection becomes the major contributor of nutrients to the sub-surface layer. Biological production dominates the nutrient sink in both layers. Horizontal advection is also an important sink in winter when the slope current is the strongest due to the enhanced northeasterly monsoon and the Kuroshio intrusion. Figure 3. Controlling mechanisms and dynamics of nutrient in the northern slope of the SCS. (Please refer to the appendix in section 11 for figures) 6. Summary By utilizing results from the coupled physical-biological China Sea Multi-Scale Ocean Modeling System, this study sheds light on the critical role of slope circulation as a major 3D conveyor of momentum and biogeochemical substance for the entire SCS. We describe the dominant coupled physical-biogeochemical processes along the biophysically active slope to better understand the overall ecosystem dynamics of the northern slope of the SCS and the entire SCS.
