16308319.label: Major findings and research outcome
16308319.value: Using observed data and results from a numerical model, we investigate the coupled physical-biogeochemical processes that result from water exchanges between the South China Sea (SCS) and the western Pacific Ocean (WPO) and between the shelf and deep basin along the biophysically active continental slope. We study the nutrient transport and dynamics over the northern slope of the SCS where the main branch of the SCS basin circulation facilitates water exchange between the SCS and the WPO. Our results show that the nutrient flux consistently flows year-round into the slope region from the WPO and that the along- and cross-slope transports regulate the nutrient budget in the region. The nutrient transport concentrates mainly in the upper 1000 m and exhibits significant seasonality. We found that cross-isobath motion is key to fueling nutrients for biological production along the slope and throughout the SCS. When the persistent westward slope current interacts with the variable sloping topography, a unique upslope/downslope nutrient transport occurs along convex/concave isobaths. Vertical turbulent mixing becomes the main nutrient source in the upper mixed layer, and vertical advection becomes the major contributor of nutrients to the sub-surface layer. Biological production dominates the nutrient sink in both layers. Horizontal advection is also an important sink in winter when the slope current is the strongest due to the enhanced northeasterly monsoon and the Kuroshio intrusion. Our findings provide an insightful understanding on the critical role of nutrient transport over the slope in the overall ecosystem dynamics of the marginal SCS. 2 peer-reviewed papers have been published.

16308319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16308319.value: The research findings from this project provide valuable insights into the coupled physical-biogeochemical processes occurring over the northern shelf of the SCS, particularly along the northern slope. Temporal and spatial variations and long-term trends: The research findings suggest significant relevance to seasonal and topography changes in nutrient transport and dynamics. Exploring the temporal and spatial variations in nutrient fluxes and their connections to climate patterns, such as monsoons and ocean currents, can provide insights into long-term trends and potential impacts of climate change on ecosystem dynamics in the SCS. Long-term observational data and additional modeling studies can contribute to understanding these variations and trends. Biological responses and ecosystem modeling: The study highlights the importance of nutrient transport in fueling biological production along the slope and throughout the SCS. Further research can focus on studying the specific biological responses to nutrient availability, such as phytoplankton growth and zooplankton dynamics. Integrating these biological components into ecosystem models can help assess the overall ecological consequences of nutrient transport and provide a more holistic understanding of the ecosystem dynamics in the SCS.

16308319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16308319.value: This project aims to study the nutrient transport and dynamics in the northern slope of the South China Sea (SCS). The continental slope plays a crucial role in regulating the mixing of water in the ocean because of the strong currents and unique topography, which help exchange water and nutrients between the shallow coastal areas and the deeper basin. Through this project, we provided the first quantitative assessment of nutrient transport and budget in the northern slope of the SCS, using a three-dimensional model that considers both physical and biogeochemical processes. We advanced our understanding of nutrient dynamics in this area from sporadic and isolated observations to a more holistic and interconnected understanding. By using the computer model, the project offered an alternative method to study nutrient dynamics in complex ocean environments, which allows researchers to test their hypotheses and explore internal processes that are difficult to study in a traditional laboratory.

16308719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16308719.value: Highly substituted phenols are an interesting class of compounds which are frequently present as a key structural motif in natural products, potential drugs and materials. The development of methods for regioselective syntheses of highly substituted and densely functionalized phenols is an important but challenging topic in synthetic chemistry. The classical strategy to access highly substituted phenols is to use iterative substitution reactions of a preexisting arene. This strategy has an inherent limitation as it relies on the activating and directing effect of substituents of the preexisting arene. Alternative to this strategy of functionalization of arenes is to construct highly substituted phenols from acyclic precursors by benzannulation reactions. There has been much interest in developing such alternative strategy because it allows the synthesis of phenols with (functional groups) substituents unattainable by classical substitution reaction of arenes. Representatives of benzannulation reactions include cycloaddition reactions of Fischer vinylcarbenes with alkynes (c.f., Dötz reaction) and electrocyclization reactions of dienylketenes. These powerful benzannulation reactions have been successfully used in the total synthesis of a variety of natural products. However, the existing benzannulation reactions address only small parts of the grand challenge of chemical synthesis of densely functionalized phenols. The main goal of this project is to develop a new synthetic method for de novo synthesis of densely functionalized phenols inaccessible by prior methods. The key feature of our new method is the unprecedented stepwise transition metal-mediated [2+1+2+1] cycloaddition of alkyne, CO, alkyne and CO, which are the six-carbon source of the resulting phenols. Such cycloaddition is conceived to proceed in two stages: 1) reactions of alkyne-A and a carbonyl metal complex to form low valent CO-containing metallacyclobutadienes ([2+1+M] cycloaddition, M is transition metal) and 2) reactions of metallacyclobutadienes with alkyne-B along with simultaneous insertion of CO ([2+1+M]+[2+1] cycloaddition) to produce η5-oxocyclohexadienyl complexes, which upon treatment of water undergo hydrolytic de-metalation to provide the phenols. Preliminary results have demonstrated the viability of this new method. This proposal describes the following main tasks and efforts: (i) to optimize and expand the synthesis of various low-valent CO-containing metallacyclobutadienes, (ii) to develop strategies for selective formation of η5-oxocyclohexadienyl complexes and phenols, (iii) to explore the substrate scope, and (iv) to demonstrate the utilities of the strategy. 高度官能团化的苯酚是天然产物、潜在药物和功能材料的常见组成部分。如何选择性合成多取代多官能团化苯酚是一个重要而又具有挑战的课题。芳香化合物的取代反应是传统合成高度官能团化苯酚的主要途径，但这类取代反应要依赖芳香化合物的活化效应和定位效应，所以具有一定的局限性。非环前体苯环化是构建多取代苯酚的一类新策略。这类新策略可以制备某些传统取代反应无法得到的多取代苯酚。已知的苯环化代表反应包括乙烯基Fischer卡宾与炔烃的环加成反应和双烯烯酮电环化反应。这些苯环化反应已经广泛地应用于各类天然产物的合成。然而，现有的苯环化反应仅仅解决了小部分关于化学合成高度官能团化苯酚的问题。这个课题的主要目标是发展一种全新合成策略，用来得到以现有方法很难得到的高度官能团化苯酚。我们的新策略是：在过渡金属参与的条件下，利用[炔烃+一氧化碳+炔烃+一氧化碳]的[2+1+2+1]分步环加成反应来获得高度官能团化苯酚。本研究计划包括了下述主要的内容：（一）优化和扩展不同含羰基的低价金属四元环络合物的合成；（二）发展选择性生成氧杂环己二烯络合物和苯酚的方法；（三）探究底物适用范围以及此策略的应用。

16308719.label: Realisation of objectives
16308719.value: The main objectives of the project are (I) to synthesize low-valent CO-containing metallacyclobutadienes, (ii) to find strategies to ensure selective formation of η5-oxocyclohexadienyl complexes and phenols, and (iii) to explore the substrate scope and the utilities of the reactions. To achieve the objectives, we have carried out the following research work. We have built a library of low valent CO-containing metallacyclobutadienes starting from electron-deficient alkynes RCCE (R = alkyl, aryl, SiMe3, E = electron-withdrawing group) and NaRe(CO)5. By treating NaRe(CO)5 with electron-deficient alkynes RC≡CCO2R' followed by AcCl/R"OH, a series of alkoxymetallacyclobutadienes of the type [(OC)4Re{-C(R)=C(CO2R')C(OR")=} (1) have been obtained. We have also tried to prepare metallacyclobutadienes by using other types of electron deficient alkynes (e.g. PhC≡CCN, HC≡C-p-C6H4-CF3), and metal complexes such as the manganese compound Na[Mn(CO)5], and the rhenium complex ReCl3(MeCN)(PPh3)3, although the expected metallacyclobutadienes were not produced in these reactions. By nucleophilic substitution reactions of alkoxymetallacyclobutadies with amines, we have successfully prepared a series of low valent CO-containing aminometallacyclobutadienes. By nucleophilic substitution reactions of alkoxymetallacyclobutadies with thiols, we have successfully prepared a series of low valent CO-containing thiometallacyclobutadienes. One of the key steps for the formation of phenol in the benzannulation is the reactions of metallacyclobutadienes with alkynes to give η5-oxocyclohexadienyl intermediates. However, reactions of metallacyclobutadienes with alkynes could also give other products. We have conducted both experimental work and calculations to defines factors influencing selectivity of the products, and found that the selectivity for η5-oxocyclohexadienyl products is closely related to the substituents of metallacyclobutadienes. Using the benzannulation, we have successfully synthesized a series of polysubstituted phenols from two different alkynes and NaRe(CO)5. To explore the substrate scope of the benzannulation, we have explored reactions of variety of electron-deficient and electron-rich alkynes. In addition, we have also explored reactions of rhenacyclobutadienes with allenes. To demonstrate the utilities of the reactions, we have synthesized phenols with up to five different substituents. The project is labor intensive as it involves extensive synthetic experimental work. In order to achieve the research objectives, we have used most of the RGF research fund to support research staff, and used some HKUST internal fund to cover some of the general expenses for the project. We did not attend international conferences due to COVID.

16309019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309019.value: The Kepler problem is a mathematical model for the simplest solar system. Its solution by Newton led to a satisfactory explanation for Kepler's laws of planetary motion. As with many models in fundamental physics, the mathematical formulas underlying the Kepler problem are both simple and elegant. One might say that the Kepler problem is a model example for the unity of simplicity, beauty, and truth. The simplicity of the Kepler problem might fool people into believing that everything about the Kepler problem must was discovered a long time ago. However, as recently as 2011, it was revealed that the secret of the Kepler problem lies in a mathematical structure introduced by P. Jordan (a founder of quantum mechanics) in his attempt to provide a better foundation for quantum mechanics. As a result, a general theory has gradually emerged that unifies the Kepler problem with the oscillator problem. Moreover, the hallmarks of relativity (such as the Lorentz transformation) appear naturally in the study of the Kepler problem and its magnetized companions. (This later discovery may suggest that the universe is negatively curved, a view held by a minority of cosmologists.) For the sake of completeness at least, it would be valuable to know the list of all of the dynamic models in the general theory mentioned above. Our experience with the currently known models suggests that, up to finite multiplicity, these models are in a one-to-one correspondence with some co-adjoint orbits of simple real Lie algebras of a specific type; moreover, the trajectories of these models are plane curves of degree two or higher. The primary purpose of the proposed project is to find the complete list of the Kepler-type models associated with each simple Euclidean Jordan algebra and to solve all of them at the classical mechanics level. The proposed project is part of a long-term program that has the ultimate goal of finding clues to fundamental physics by uncovering the beautiful mathematics hidden behind the Kepler problem. If the history of past mathematical explorations of fundamental physics is a guide, this long-term program might in the future be judged to be important to our understanding of fundamental physics. 开普勒问题是最简单的太阳系的数学模型。通过解它，牛顿为描述行星运动的开普勒三大定律提供了令人满意的解释。与基础物理学中的许多数学模型一样，开普勒问题背后的数学既简洁又优雅。可以说，开普勒问题是集简洁，美丽和真理为一体的典型范例。 开普勒问题的简洁性可能会让人们相信关于开普勒问题的所有一切已被发现。然而，迟至2011年，我们发现开普勒问题的数学秘密隐藏在由P. Jordan（量子力学的创始人之一）引入的数学结构中。这一发现让我们看到开普勒问题与谐振子问题原来只是一个一般数学理论里的两个特例。此外，狭义相对论里出现的洛伦兹变换在磁化开普勒问题中也自然地出现。 至少是为了完整起见，上述一般理论中的所有模型的分类是有价值的。对一些已知模型的研究表明，这些模型与特定类型的单实李代数的一些共伴轨道对应; 此外，这些模型里的单粒子的运动轨迹是2阶或更高阶的平面曲线。 该项目的主要目的是找到与每个单Euclidean Jordan代数相关的广义Kepler模型的完整分类，并在经典力学层面上求解所有这些模型。 拟议的项目是长期研究计划的一部分，其最终目标是通过揭示隐藏在开普勒问题背后的美丽数学来寻找推动基础物理学进展的线索。如果对基础物理学的数学探索的历史是一面镜子，那么这个长期计划将来有可能会被认为对基础物理学的发展很重要。

16309019.label: Realisation of objectives
16309019.value: The project aims to classify all generalized Kepler problems (or models) in classical mechanics. Each model is characterized by a triple (V, r, m), where V represents a formally real simple Jordan algebra, r is an integer ranging from 1 to the rank of V, and m (referred to as magnetic charge) corresponds to a co-adjoint orbit of a compact Lie group G (known as the gauge group). The models are classified as magnetized or unmagnetized based on whether m equals 0 or not. The classification involves determining the magnetic charge and the corresponding phase space for each (V, r) pair. The achievements of this project thus far are as follows: 1. When V = R (the field of real numbers), r can only be 1. In this case, G = U(1), and m can be either 0 (unmagnetized model) or a positive real number (magnetized model). The phase space is either a dense open set of the future lightcone in R^{1, 2} = sl_2(R) or an elliptic orbit comprising future pointing Lorentz vectors with a Lorentzian length given by a specific positive number. This result has been fully obtained. 2. For V = Gamma (R^{2k+1}) with k > 0 and r = 1, G = SO(2k), m must be either 0 or an elliptic orbit of so(2k) that is diffeomorphic to the manifold SO(2k)/U(k). The remaining cases where r = 2 have not yet been investigated. 3. A novel regularization method has been discovered during the project from an indirect perspective. Since a Kepler motion with vanishing angular momentum cannot extend indefinitely in both time directions, a regularization is necessary. This involves adding missing points to the phase space to enable any Kepler motion to run indefinitely in both time directions. What has been found is a superior regularization known as symmetry completion. After the symmetry completion, Sigma_- (the part of the phase space where the Hamiltonian of the Kepler problem is negative) becomes the super minimal co-adjoint orbit of so(1, 4), while Sigma_+ (the part of the phase space where the Hamiltonian of the Kepler problem is positive) becomes the super minimal co-adjoint orbit of so(2, 3). This symmetry completion exhibits a duality in symplectic geometry that bears resemblance to the compact-noncompact duality for symmetric spaces in Riemannian differential geometry, such as the S^2 - H^2 duality. This achievement was unexpected as regularization for the Kepler problem was previously well-studied by esteemed mathematicians. The new regularization is deemed more elegant, prompting a referee of the paper to remark that "this will be the way we think about regularization going forward." While the ultimate goal of classifying all generalized Kepler problems has not been reached, significant progress has been made. As the project's title suggests, it has advanced towards the goal. Additionally, a surprising discovery has been made—the symmetry completion of the Kepler problem. This finding opens new avenues for exploring regularization, duality, and their quantum counterparts. In fact, a grant proposal dedicated to this research direction has just been submitted. We will continue to approach the classification of all generalized Kepler problems from various perspectives. It is believed that with time, the ultimate goal will be achieved.

16309019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309019.value: Three papers have been published or accepted for publication: In the first paper, I focused on rank-one generalized Kepler problems associated with the Jordan algebra V:= Gamma (R^{2k+1}). The classical phase space was found to exhibit two possibilities: either a dense open set of a minimal nilpotent orbit or an elliptic orbit of the TKK algebra of V (specifically, the real Lie algebra so(2, 2k+2)). This classification depends on whether the magnetic charge is zero or not. By combining these results with my previous findings, a distinct quantization method for these elliptic orbits was established, differing from the one in Reference [David Vogan, "The method of coadjoint orbits for real reductive groups," in Representation Theory of Lie Groups. IAS/Park City Mathematics Series 8 (1999), 179–238]. The second paper delved into the study of all generalized Kepler problems associated with the simplest formally real Jordan algebra, R. Similarly, the classical phase space in this case was classified as either a dense open set of a minimal nilpotent orbit or an elliptic orbit of the TKK algebra (i.e., the real Lie algebra sl_2(R)). Based on the findings from these two papers, one could conjecture that the classical phase space of generalized Kepler problems associated with any formally real simple Jordan algebra falls into one of two categories: a dense open set of a minimal nilpotent orbit or an elliptic orbit of the TKK algebra. This classification depends on whether the magnetic charge is zero or not. I believe that gaining a complete understanding of the classical phase space could enhance our comprehension of the classification of unitary highest-weight modules for real non-compact simple Lie groups. Although not directly linked to the project, the third paper emerged as a surprising by-product. It addresses the "regularization" of Kepler motions, a facet of the classical Kepler problem that has been extensively studied by distinguished mathematicians like J. Moser, J.-M. Souriau, J. J. Duistermaat, and others in the past. Previous research focused on dynamic completions of the phase space to achieve regularization. However, I discovered a further completion, referred to as symmetry completion, which renders the "regularization" even more elegant. This led a referee of the paper to remark that "this will be the way we think about regularization going forward." Consequently, a duality between specific coadjoint orbits has been established, reminiscent of the compact-noncompact duality observed in certain symmetric spaces. Moreover, intriguing mathematical structures from general relativity have surfaced in the context of the Kepler problem.

16309019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309019.value: The concept of Symmetry Completion in Paper 3 opens a door for further exploration of regularization and duality, including their quantum analogs. Indeed, I have just submitted a grant proposal devoted to this research direction. The conjecture mentioned in section 6.1, which arises from the findings in papers 1 and 2, holds significant promise on its own. I firmly believe that comprehending the classical phase space in its entirety could provide a more compelling proof of the classification theorem for unitary highest-weight modules. This line of inquiry holds tremendous potential for advancing our knowledge in the field.

16309019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309019.value: Kepler problem is the mathematical model for the simplest solar system or atom. It played a significant role in the establishment of both the universal gravitation law and the quantum theory. It also interacts with many areas of mathematics among which the most significant ones are geometry and symmetry. This project forms a part of our long-term endeavour to unveil potential clues or hints pertaining to physics beyond our current understanding. It is disheartening to note that fundamental physics has experienced limited progress over the past five decades, despite the existence of many unresolved puzzles within the field. However, history has shown us that a diligent and comprehensive mathematical examination of existing fundamental physical models and principles can serve as a catalyst for groundbreaking advancements. Consequently, this project represents a compelling exploration of the profound mathematical underpinnings inherent in the Kepler problem. Notably, while conducting this research, we have made an intriguing and unexpected revelation: certain mathematical structures inherent in Einstein's general relativity manifest within the context of the Kepler problem. This remarkable connection serves to underscore the intertwined nature of physics and mathematics, presenting us with valuable insights that can potentially propel our comprehension of the universe to new heights.

16309219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309219.value: Non-convex optimization is a ubiquitous tool in scientific and engineering research. For many important problems, simple non-convex optimization algorithms often provide good solutions efficiently and effectively, despite possible local minima. One way to explain the success of these algorithms is through the geometric analysis of non-convex loss functions on the landscape of their critical points. Recently, a number of studies have examined the landscape of non-convex optimizations in signal processing, machine learning, and imaging. In the proposed project, we will study the landscape analysis of phase retrieval and low-rank Hankel matrix completion. These two problems have been intensively investigated over the past few years. We expect to obtain results that, for a variety of non-convex loss functions of these two problems, a local minimum is also global and all other critical points have a negative directional curvature. The results of the proposed project not only will explain why simple non-convex algorithms usually find a global minimizer for these two problems, but also will be useful for developing new efficient algorithms with a theoretical guarantee by applying algorithms that are guaranteed to find a local minimum. 非凸优化是科学和工程研究中常用的工具。对于许多重要问题，尽管可能存在局部最小值，简单的非凸优化算法通常可以有效地解决这一类问题。解释这些算法成功的一种方法是分析这些非凸优化中非凸损失函数的几何地貌。最近，许多研究者分析了信号处理，机器学习和成像中的非凸优化函数的地貌。在本项目中，我们将研究相位恢复和低秩Hankel矩阵补全问题中的非凸函数的地貌分析。在过去的几年里，这两个问题都得到了深入的研究。我们期望获得以下结果：对于这两个问题的各种非凸损失函数，局部最小值也是全局的，并且所有其他临界点具有负方向曲率。这些结果不仅可以解释为什么简单的非凸算法通常会找到这两个问题的全局最优解，而且任何能找到局部最优解的算法会保证找到全局最优解，这样我们会得到许多新的保证找到全局最优解的高效算法。

16309219.label: Realisation of objectives
16309219.value: To achieve our project objectives, we took several key steps: 1. We proposed innovative nonconvex optimization models for numerical resolution of phase retrieval and analyzed their landscapes. These models, which include smoothed amplitude flow, perturbed amplitude model, and quotient intensity model, not only meet optimal sample complexity to have a favorable landscape but also ensure numerical efficiency. 2. We investigated the minimum number of samples needed for a benign landscape in nonconvex least squares fitting for phase retrieval, improving upon the original result in Sun, Qu, and Wright's pioneering paper. Our findings are nearly optimal, partially answering an open question they raised. 3. For the low-rank Hankel matrix completion problem, we introduced new nonconvex algorithms that exploit the local strict convexity of nonconvex optimization. We also studied the landscape of nonconvex optimizations outside the neighborhood of the global minimum, finding that these optimizations may not always offer a good landscape. 4. We examined the landscape of nonconvex optimization for low-rank tensor decomposition. Unlike low-rank matrix problems, non-convex low-rank tensor decomposition has non-global local minimizers. To avoid these and achieve correct low-rank tensor factorization, we proposed a unique gradient descent algorithm that can find a global minimum. 5. We expanded the application of nonconvex optimization to sparse phase retrieval, developing several novel efficient algorithms. These algorithms can achieve super-linear and finite-step convergence rates, a significant improvement over existing solutions. The development of these algorithms made use of the landscape of the nonconvex optimization problems in sparse phase retrieval. The pandemic in the past few years has halted visitor traffic to Hong Kong and restricted travel for collaboration and research. Face-to-face conferences have shifted to virtual platforms. As a result, funds initially allocated for general expenses and conferences have been redirected towards hiring Research Assistants (RAs) or Postdoctoral Researchers (Postdocs), ensuring our research and collaboration continue effectively during these challenging times.

16309219.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309219.value: 1. In Peer-Reviewed Publication 4, we proposed a non-convex optimization approach based on the smoothed amplitude flow model. Our findings demonstrate that under the Gaussian random model, and when utilizing an optimal number of samples, the model offers a well-constructed landscape. All local minima are global, and all other critical points are strict saddles. 2. Within Peer-Reviewed Publication 10, we introduced a perturbed amplitude model for phase retrieval. Our research proves that this new model exhibits optimal sample complexity to create a favourable landscape, where all local minima are global. 3. In Peer-Reviewed Publication 9, we developed a quotient intensity optimization approach for solving phase retrieval. This novel nonconvex optimization leverages an optimal number of samples to establish a benign landscape where all local minima are global. 4. In Peer-Reviewed Publication 3, we improved the sample complexity required to attain a favourable landscape of the nonconvex least squares in phase retrieval. Our sample complexity is nearly optimal, providing a partial solution to an open question raised by Sun, Qu, and Wright. 5. In Peer-Reviewed Publications 1 and 11, we proposed new non-convex optimization algorithm, ASAP and HSGD, for the completion of low-rank Hankel matrices corrupted by spike noise. ASAP and HSGD utilize the property that the non-convex optimization is strictly convex near the global minimum. We proved that an optimal number of samples suffices to drive ASAP and HSGD converge to a global minimum. 6. In Peer-Reviewed Publication 8, we examined the landscape of nonconvex optimization for low-rank tensor decomposition. Based on our landscape analysis, we proposed a gradient descent with a unique initialization to find a global minimum. 7. In Peer-Reviewed Publication 7, we introduced a non-convex optimization method, hard thresholding pursuit (HTP), for sparse phase retrieval. Our research shows that HTP is theoretically guaranteed to converge to a global minimum in a finite number of steps. 8. In Peer-Reviewed Publication 5, we proposed another non-convex optimization method, stochastic alternating minimization (SAM), for sparse phase retrieval. Our findings suggest that SAM converges to the global minimum in a finite number of steps. Additionally, empirical evidence indicates that the stochastic nature of SAM helps improve sample complexity. 9. In Peer-Reviewed Publications 2 and 6, we employed non-convex optimization methods to address challenges originating from machine learning and imaging techniques.

16309219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309219.value: Through our analysis of the landscape of nonconvex optimization for various problems, we observed that existing nonconvex algorithms, intentionally or unintentionally, exploit beneficial landscape features like strict convexity near the global minimum. This suggests that there is potential in devising more algorithms that fully utilize the favorable landscape of non-convex optimization problems. In addition, we have developed provable non-convex optimization methods for problems in areas like nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, phase retrieval, and medical imaging. Our algorithms are not only backed by robust mathematical theory but are also useful in scenarios where traditional methods fall short. There is potential to apply these algorithms in real-world applications across these fields.

16309219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309219.value: Non-convex optimization is a powerful tool used in scientific and engineering research to navigate complex landscapes and find optimal solutions. Our project focuses on analyzing these "landscapes" for some problems that are of practical interest and frequently studied. We aim to understand why simple non-convex algorithms often find the best overall solutions, despite potential pitfalls. The results of our research will not only shed light on the effectiveness of these tools but also offer a foundation for the creation of new, efficient algorithms with a solid theoretical guarantee. It's like developing a reliable guide that can navigate the complexities and challenges in various fields, from signal processing to machine learning and imaging.

16309719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309719.value: The North China Plain has severe groundwater depletion due to intensive irrigation. As summer rainfall is projected to decrease in northern China under global warming, the dependency on groundwater in the North China Plain is expected to increase in the future. While groundwater pumping assures sufficient soil wetness for growing plants, increased soil moisture alters the surface energy partitioning and water cycle through the modulation of heat, moisture, and momentum exchange between the land surface and atmosphere. Therefore, the effects of groundwater overexploitation are not restricted to the region in which groundwater pumping occurs; groundwater overexploitation can also critically affect the hydroclimatology of remote places and the global water budget. However, our knowledge of the broader impacts of pumped groundwater and of the connection between pumped groundwater and the hydrological cycle is quite limited. As a result, the dynamic interactions between the atmosphere, land surface, and subsurface in response to water table fluctuations are not accurately represented in current climate models. The proposed project will be the first attempt to quantify the impact of groundwater pumping on regional climate and hydrological cycle based on a comparative assessment using both a global climate model (GCM) and a regional climate model (RCM) that share the same land surface model (Community Land Model, CLM4.5). To improve the representation of groundwater dynamics, a new module accounting for subgrid heterogeneity in the water table and lateral groundwater flow will be incorporated into the existing groundwater scheme of CLM4.5. A focus will be given to the comparison of the climate responses to groundwater pumping in northern China simulated by GCM and RCM with the same modified CLM4.5. This comparison will help to assess the robustness of the model responses and moderate the model-dependent implications that often refers to a common deficiency embedded in the modeling study. The impact of groundwater pumping on the future climate will then be investigated by dynamically downscaling projections under business-as-usual emission scenario. In addition, the contributions of regional and global groundwater pumping to sea level changes will be quantified, which will help uncover the mechanism determining the fate of pumped groundwater. This project will strengthen our understanding of the nonlinear climate processes that occur when the atmosphere, land surface, and subsurface are perturbed by groundwater pumping, based on an unprecedented level of simulations produced using state-of-the-art GCM and RCM with a new groundwater module. 受到密集灌溉的影響，華北平原地下水已經嚴重枯竭。但在全球變暖情景下，華北地區的夏季降雨量預計將會減少，從而導致未來華北平原對地下水的依賴程度將進一步增加。雖然地下水抽灌為植物生長提供了充足的土壤濕度，但土壤水分的增加會通過調整地表與大氣之間的熱量、水分和動量交換，改變地表能量分配與水迴圈。因此，地下水過度開採的影響不僅限於地下水抽取的區域，也會對遠處地區的水文氣候和全球水量平衡造成嚴重影響。然而目前我們對抽灌地下水的廣泛影響以及抽灌地下水與水循环之間的聯繫的瞭解仍然非常有限，導致現有的氣候模型中關於地下水位波動引起的大氣、陸表和地下之間的動態相互作用的表示並不準確。 本擬議項目將首次嘗試基於比較評估耦合相同地表模型(Community Land Model, CLM4.5）的一個全球氣候模型（Global Climate Model, GCM）與一個區域氣候模型（Regional Climate Model, RCM），以量化研究地下水抽灌對區域氣候和水循环的影響。為了更好地表現地下水動態，一個考慮地下水位的子網格非均質性和側向地下水流的新模块將被納入現有的CLM4.5地下水方案中。我們將重點關注使用同樣的改進後的CLM4.5的GCM和RCM在模擬華北地下水抽灌的氣候回應上的比較。這一比較有助於評估模型響應的穩健性並減少研究結果啟示對模型的依賴， 而這種依賴被普遍認為是建模研究中的缺陷。然後，我們將通過對“一切照舊”排放情景下的氣候預估的動力降尺度，對地下水抽灌對未來氣候的影響進行評估。此外，為了揭示決定抽灌地下水的去向的機制，區域和全球地下水抽灌對海平面變化的貢獻也將被量化。本專案將通過使用帶有全新地下水模块的最先進的GCM和RCM的模擬研究，加深我們對當大氣、地表、地下受地下水開採擾動影響時發生的非線性氣候過程的理解。

16309719.label: Realisation of objectives
16309719.value: We have achieved the objectives, in the course of working on four papers in the leading SCI journals (three papers have been published and one manuscript is currently under review) and five presentations at international conferences. While performing this project, one postgraduate student was trained. She successfully completed her MPhil thesis and continued this project as her first project during the PhD. The accomplishment of the study involved four main tasks, each contributing to specific objectives. The first two tasks were dedicated to fulfilling the first and second objectives, respectively. The third task served a dual purpose, contributing to both the first and second objectives. Finally, the fourth task successfully achieved the third objective. These tasks can be summarized as follows: 1. Enhancement of the existing RCM by explicitly integrating pumped groundwater for irrigation and specifically tailoring to the targeted NCP. 2. Implementation groundwater-fed irrigation at global scale with CESM, and quantify the groundwater depletion. 3. Application of two distinct RCMs in the NCP region to investigate the impact of groundwater-related irrigation on the local climate and hydrology, particularly in precipitation. 4. Analysis of water balance on land and ocean with different irrigation and groundwater-pumping scales.

16309719.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309719.value: It is necessary to carefully select and even improve the climate models to evaluate the impact of groundwater pumping in the NCP due to its extensive cropland, high productivity, compact rotation, semi-arid climate, and severe groundwater depletion caused by intense irrigation. Therefore, two state-of-art RCMs, RegCM and WRF, carrying Noah-MP and CLM land surface schemes, as well as one GCM, CESM2, were chosen for their inclusion of essential algorithms for irrigation and groundwater dynamics, providing a suitable framework for applying or implementing groundwater pumping. The experiments using RCMs consistently demonstrated cooling and moistening effects centered over the NCP. Despite indications that irrigation-induced vertical downdraft and low-level divergence might inhibit rainfall, the dominant effect was humidification, leading to a significant increase in precipitation during April-June. The Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE) exhibits a notable increase during specific "calm days" characterized by minimal vertical moisture advection, particularly in the afternoon. This sharp increase in CAPE destabilizes the atmosphere, triggering frequent convective light rains. The intense irrigation also demonstrates great depletion in groundwater level especially among the mountains. Our findings highlight how groundwater-related irrigation affects regional climate in the NCP. Moreover, the consistent response to irrigation observed in two different RCMs and one GCM enhances the robustness of the underlying physical mechanism driving the precipitation increase. This consistency underscores the reliability of the findings and strengthens our understanding of the link between irrigation and the observed enhancement of precipitation in the NCP. By utilizing GCM in global-scale experiments, we activated groundwater-fed irrigation at various scales, including the NCP, the entire China, and globally respectively, discern different responses to the locations of the irrigation forcing. The results showed severe depletion in the NCP region, with a positive shift in rainfall from land to ocean and subsequent increases in ocean water storage. The quantification of the contributions of groundwater pumping to sea level changes strengthens our understanding of the nonlinear climate processes that arise when groundwater pumping perturbs the atmosphere, land surface, and subsurface. To further improve the model, we developed a comprehensive crop-irrigation-groundwater model in WRF. This model explicitly incorporates pumped groundwater for irrigation, specifically tailored to the NCP. The integrated crop modeling system exhibits commendable performance in simulating crop behavior under varying climatic conditions. This is evidenced by its accurate identification of crop stages, precise estimation of field biomass, reliable prediction of crop yield, and the projection of monthly leaf area index.

16309719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309719.value: The comprehensive crop-irrigation-groundwater model obtained from this project can be further employed with changing climate to enhance our understanding of the intricate relationship between agricultural development and climate change.

16309719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309719.value: The heavy reliance on groundwater-fed irrigation in the North China Plain (NCP) raises significant environmental concerns. This project evaluates the impact of groundwater pumping on regional and global climate. To achieve this, two advanced regional climate models and one global climate model are employed, considering various irrigation scenarios. The findings reveal that irrigation in the NCP has notable effects, including a significant cooling and increased precipitation during the April to June. This is achieved through the frequent triggering of light rainfall, especially in the afternoon. Furthermore, global-scale experiments demonstrate severe groundwater depletion, as well as a shift of rainfall from land to the ocean and consequent sea-level rise. The project significantly enhances our understanding of how groundwater pumping influences local climate dynamics and sea-level changes. Additionally, to better represent the groundwater-fed crop system in the NCP region, a comprehensive crop-irrigation-groundwater model is developed. This model improves the accuracy of simulating crop growth, thereby providing valuable potential for further studying the intricate relationship between agricultural systems and climate change.

16309919.label: Project Objectives
16309919.value: Investigate novel Pt complexes as potential chemotherapy drug candidates. These Pt complexes have been newly synthesized and demonstrated anticancer activity with selectivity towards specific targets. Their molecular mechanisms are difficult to be characterize by traditional bulk studies, due to the increasing complexity with larger ligands and the introduction of non-covalent bindings. Thus, we will utilize single-molecule characterization methods to bridge the gap to identify the molecular mechanisms, especially those non-covalent interactions. Investigate novel Au complexes as potential chemotherapy drug candidates. These newly synthesized Au complexes offer competitive anticancer activity with good stability under physiological conditions to unveil Pt-based drug resistance. However, their molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Hence, we will adopt single-molecule characterization methods to investigate the mechanism of these novel Au complexes-DNA interactions. Investigate novel Pt complexes as potential luminescent diagnostic probes. Theses Pt complexes shift the emission wavelength upon binding to specific mismatched DNA. We will correlative different dimensions of information in single-molecule force response, molecular extension, and vibrational fingerprint to investigate the structural changes associated with luminescence and the corresponding molecular mechanism for its DNA selectivity. Promote the single-molecule characterization methods for mechanistic investigations. When heterogeneous molecular mechanisms occur simultaneously, traditional bulk studies that only probe the ensemble average of a large number of molecules might overwhelmed the signal from rare intermediates or minor products. Our investigation will showcase a new approach to investigate the individual event at the most fundamental level, which could have the potential for a wider range of applications to shed light on analogous mechanistic investigations.

16309919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16309919.value: Metal complexes interact with DNA to combat cancers in chemotherapy medications. As a metal complex, cisplatin has achieved broad clinical successes in cancer treatment, but also exhibits severe side effects and acquired/intrinsic drug resistance due to off-target binding. It is thus imperative to improve the targeting strategies, such as optimizing coordinated ligands towards specific targets, and replacing the original Pt center with isoelectronic Au to mitigate cisplatin resistance. Moreover, certain Pt complexes have shown distinctive luminescence upon DNA interactions, promising an efficient labeling approach for cancer diagnostics through definitive recognitions of specific DNA characteristics. Therefore, an in-depth mechanistic understanding of metal complexes-DNA interactions is required to support the rational design of new metal complexes that selectively bind to target DNA. The general mechanistic basis of metal complexes-DNA interactions has been established, including various binding modes in covalent and non-covalent interactions. In the newly designed metal complexes, multiple binding modes with different kinetics are adopted to achieve better selectivity and binding affinity, thus significantly increasing the complexity of simultaneous molecular mechanisms. However, it is difficult to distinguish non-covalent binding modes and accurately characterize the metal complexes-DNA adducts by traditional bulk studies, due to several systematic and experimental challenges. To tackle the problem, we propose single-molecule characterization approaches to investigate the individual binding behaviors among heterogeneous metal complexes-DNA interactions, to provide new and comprehensive mechanistic perspectives on the development of novel metal complexes as target-specific anticancer agents. Specifically, we will utilize optical tweezers (single-molecule force spectroscopy), single-molecule surface-enhanced spectroscopy, and single-molecule force coupled Raman spectroscopy to investigate metal complexes-DNA interactions, in particular for novel Pt complexes and Au complexes as potential chemotherapy drug candidates, and novel Pt complexes as potential luminescent diagnostic probes. As proven by the preliminary data, optical tweezers can offer exclusive advantages when determining and quantifying intercalations (non-covalent interactions) at the single-molecule level. Surface-enhanced Raman spectra can encode covalent bonding, structural coupling, and intermolecular interactions. Furthermore, single-molecule force coupled Raman spectroscopy can correlate the force, molecular extension, and Raman spectra in the dynamic measurements to recognize DNA sequences, locate binding sites on the targeting base pairs, identify the chemical bonding environments, and promote the characterization of sequence-specific binding events along the natural DNA. By removing ensemble averaging, our findings will complement the traditional bulk observations to explain the detailed molecular mechanism and expand the application of single-molecule characterization methods to other heterogeneous processes. 化療藥物金屬配合物通過阻斷DNA的轉錄來殺死癌症細胞。作為金屬配合物，順鉑在癌症治療中取得了廣泛的臨床成功，但由於它缺乏特異性，也帶來了嚴重的副作用和耐藥性。因此，需要採用一些策略來改進藥物設計，比如優化配位配體來針對某些特定目標進行特異性識別，還有把處於中心的鉑替換成金來消除順鉑耐藥性。此外，某些鉑配合物在與DNA相互作用時能發出顯著的熒光，通過對特定DNA特徵的確定識別，為癌症診斷提供了有效的標記方法。所以，我們需要對金屬配合物-DNA相互作用的機理進行深入地研究，來指導新金屬配合物的合理設計，提高他們針對目標DNA的選擇性。 金屬配合物-DNA相互作用的一般機理基礎已經獲得認可，包含共價和非共價相互作用的各種結合模式。在新設計的金屬配合物中，通常會採用具有不同動力學性質的多種結合模式，以獲得更好的選擇性和結合親和力，從而極大地增加了在某一時刻同時發生的分子機理的複雜性。然而，由於若干系統性和實驗性挑戰，傳統的同時研究大量分子的方法很難區分非共價結合模式並精確表徵金屬配合物-DNA加合物。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了利用單分子表徵方法來研究金屬配合物-DNA相互作用中各種各樣的結合行為，提供新的並且更深入的機理認識，方便以後設計出特異識別性更強的抗癌藥劑。 具體來說，我們將利用光學鑷子（單分子力譜），單分子表面增強拉曼光譜和單分子力耦合拉曼光譜來研究金屬配合物-DNA相互作用，特別是研究新型鉑配合物和金配合物作為化學藥物候選物，還有新型鉑配合物作為可用於診斷的發光探針。正如初步數據所證明的那樣，光學鑷子在確定和量化單分子水平的插入結合模式（非共價相互作用）時可以提供獨特的優勢。表面增強拉曼光譜可以揭示共價鍵結合模式，結構耦合影響和其他分子間相互作用。此外，單分子力耦合拉曼光譜可以把在動態測量中的得到的應力，分子延展長度和拉曼光譜關聯起來，用以識別DNA序列，定位特定目標的結合位點，識別化學鍵及化學環境，並幫助表徵在自然DNA上發生的針對特定基因序列進行選擇性識別的結合模式。因為傳統方法只能同時測量大量分子，會造成信號干擾和模糊，我們的方法能在單分子水平上補充一些新的細節，希望能更詳細地解釋清楚分子機理，並擴展單分子表徵方法在其他混雜體系中的應用。

16309919.label: Realisation of objectives
16309919.value: In this project, we developed a novel approach that combines unique instrumental integration and special experimental design to investigate the interaction between Pt and Au complexes and DNA at the single-molecule level. Specifically, we identified and quantified the different binding modes with diverse kinetics between Pt and Au complexes and DNA through single-molecule manipulation and characterization analysis, providing new mechanistic insights for the future development of anticancer drugs and diagnostic agents. Objective 1: We characterized the interaction between DNA and the newly synthesized Pt complexes containing both chloride ligands and N-heterocyclic moieties and identified their dual DNA-binding modes involving both intercalation and covalent bond formation as key factors contributing to better anticancer efficacy. To remove ensemble averaging and access individual molecule properties in complex systems, we developed a novel single-molecule force coupled Raman spectroscopy platform as a unique tool for studying biological macromolecules with structural complexity [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292; Nature Communications, 2023, 14, 6996]. With a particular focus on non-covalent interactions that are not accessible through traditional bulk studies, we monitored the real-time kinetics and quantified individual association and dissociation events between a single DNA and platinum(II) complex with chloride ligand and bipyridine moiety, showing intercalation accompanied by DNA structural distortion [Manuscript under review]. Furthermore, we analyzed different reaction modes in the interaction between DNA and platinum(II) with chloride ligand and N-heterocyclic carbene moiety, indicating an intercalation-facilitated covalent binding mechanism as a promising strategy [Manuscript in preparation]. Objective 2: We combined single-molecule experimental and computational characterization methods to reveal the molecular mechanism underlying the interaction between DNA and anticancer cyclometalated gold(III) N-heterocyclic carbene complex as well as the influence of gold nanoparticle on protein-rich cellular environments. We determined binding affinity, identified binding modes, and simulated molecular interfaces to understand the DNA-binding properties of gold(III) N-heterocyclic carbene complex, which were dominated by the intercalative interactions from the planar aromatic ligands. From the comparison of gold(III) N-heterocyclic carbene complex and platinum(II) N-heterocyclic carbene complex, we obtained valuable insights into the role of the metal center for designing new metal complexes against Pt-based drug resistance [Manuscript in preparation]. Leveraging the biocompatibility of gold, we developed new peptide-conjugated nanoparticles for therapeutic applications to combat infectious disease [Chemical Communications, 2021, 57, 6979-6982]. Furthermore, we examined the mechanism behind the vesicle and membrane transportation in cellular matrix to explore more effective drug delivery pathways [Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 2022, 119, e2113991119]. Objective 3: We conducted systematic research on the interaction between DNA mismatches and a series of luminescent platinum(II) complexes containing halide ligands and N-heterocyclic carbene moieties and unveiled the molecular mechanism behind their DNA sequence selectivity. Under single-molecule manipulation, we monitored the molecular extension trajectories of a single DNA under different stretching forces to assess the influence of a mismatched base pair on the overall structural stability, serving as the target systems for selective recognition and fluorescent detection by metal complexes [The Journal of Physical Chemistry B, 2020, 124, 42, 9365–9370]. Utilizing our single-molecule manipulation and molecular vibrational characterization platform, we identified the binding modes between platinum(II) N-heterocyclic carbene complexes and DNA mismatches associated with DNA structural stability, particularly at the C-C mismatched site, which could facilitate the de-aggregation of these metal complexes and result in distinct emission color changes with significantly enhanced intensity as promising luminescent diagnostic probes [Manuscript in preparation]. Objective 4: We employed various single-molecule characterization methods, in particular, our single-molecule force-coupled Raman spectroscopy platform, to facilitate mechanistic investigations on complex molecular interactions. We presented a new approach to characterize individual molecules among heterogeneous mixtures to gain unique information on population and probability of specific molecule types and events, which were overwhelmed by ensemble averaging in traditional bulk studies [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292; Nature Communications, 2023, 14, 6996]. Moreover, we demonstrated the potential of our platform for mechanistic investigations through monitoring real-time binding kinetics, identifying different binding modes, quantifying binding events, and determining binding site distributions within a single DNA upon interacting with metal complexes [The Journal of Physical Chemistry B, 2020, 124, 42, 9365–9370; Manuscript under review]. With single-molecule level sensitivity, we could further utilize our platform as a versatile analytical tool for various applications [Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry, 2023, 415, 3243–3253; Analyst, 2020, 145, 5158-5165].

16309919.label: Major findings and research outcome
16309919.value: We developed an innovative approach that combines unique instrumental integration and special experimental design to achieve single-molecule manipulation and characterization of biological macromolecules with structural complexity, such as DNA, RNA, and proteins. Using our single-molecule force-coupled Raman spectroscopy platform, we characterized individual molecules in heterogeneous mixtures to uncover the population and probability of specific molecule types and events and identified distinct spatial features within a single molecule to access the quantity and distributions of intricate molecular interactions, which opened up new avenues for further research to advance our understanding of complex biological systems at the molecular level [Nature Communications, 2021, 12, 1292; Nature Communications, 2023, 14, 6996; Manuscript under review]. Leveraging single-molecule level sensitivity, we could further utilize our platform as a versatile analytical tool for various applications [Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry, 2023, 415, 3243–3253; Analyst, 2020, 145, 5158-5165]. More importantly, we quantified the structural stability of DNA mismatches and discovered that platinum(II) N-Heterocyclic carbene complexes interacted with DNA mismatches through both intercalation and covalent bond binding, particularly at the unstable C-C mismatched site. Our results indicated that these site-selective interactions promoted the conversion from aggregates to monomers of platinum(II) N-Heterocyclic carbene complexes to exhibit distinct emission color changes with significantly enhanced intensity as promising luminescent diagnostic probes [The Journal of Physical Chemistry B, 2020, 124, 42, 9365–9370; Manuscript in preparation]. We revealed the rapid and reversible intercalation of gold(III) N-heterocyclic carbene complex to DNA and the influence of gold nanoparticles on protein-rich cellular environments, demonstrating the biocompatibility of gold as an alternative metal center for designing new metal complexes against Pt-based drug resistance [Chemical Communications, 2021, 57, 6979-6982; Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 2022, 119, e2113991119; Manuscript in preparation]. We identified a dual DNA-binding mode between DNA and Pt complexes with both chloride ligands and N-heterocyclic moieties, involving intercalation and covalent bond formation. Our single-molecule analysis resolved the significant DNA distortion upon rapid and reversible intercalation from the planar aromatic ligands, followed by the formation of DNA-adducts and crosslinks associated with the release of halide ligands. We discovered that such an intercalation-facilitated covalent binding mechanism was different from the DNA-binding properties of cisplatin and its analogues, implying these novel metal complexes as promising alternative drug candidates for the development of more effective anticancer therapeutics and diagnostic strategies [Manuscript under review; Manuscript in preparation].

16309919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16309919.value: By correlating single-molecule force manipulation and site-specified surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) characterization, our platform possesses the active controllability to untangle a single metal complex-bound DNA from undesired conformations, such as intermolecular stacking and intramolecular coiling, and detect the buried interaction sites at a nanometer-scale spatial resolution, which are not accessible through conventional passive detection methods in bulk. The site-correlated readouts containing unique molecular vibrational fingerprints within a single DNA can be further interpreted as a “barcode” for bioinformatic analysis, inspiring new applications in biomolecular interactions, modification, encryption, authentication, data management, and sequencing. Moreover, our platform offers the convenient adaptability to employ specific DNA sequences or structures, such as DNA duplex, triplex, G-quadruplex, and hairpin with matched or mismatched base pairs in the follow-up studies. We expect to continue investigating the binding between novel metal complexes and DNA with the specific sequence and structures and facilitate the rational designs of new metal complexes to improve the specificity and reduce the side effects of chemotherapy drugs. Further development of this research project will facilitate early diagnosis, determine suitable therapeutic strategies, and advance the fundamental understanding of cancer developments, holding the promise to expand the toolbox for future precision medicine.

16309919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16309919.value: Current chemotherapy drugs, such as cisplatin and its analogues, exhibit potent anticancer activity through interacting with DNA to induce cell death, which is also accompanied by toxic side effects and drug resistance due to poor selectivity. Recently, new metal complexes have been discovered to target specific DNA and exhibit distinct properties, but the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Our research team has developed a unique approach to characterize the interactions between these new metal complexes and DNA at the single molecule level, gaining fresh insights into non-covalent interactions inaccessible through traditional bulk studies. By utilizing single-molecule manipulation and characterization analysis, we have examined the structural properties of specific DNA and identified the binding modes between specific DNA and new metal complexes containing different metal centers and ligands to reveal the key factors contributing to better selectivity and anticancer efficacy. More importantly, our results indicate an unconventional intercalation-facilitated covalent binding mechanism between DNA mismatches and Pt with halide ligands and halide ligands, which is different from the DNA-binding reaction of cisplatin and its analogues, implying these novel metal complexes as promising alternative drug candidates to guide the development of more effective anticancer therapeutics and diagnostic strategies.

16310019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16310019.value: The conventional method to fabricate organic solar cells is coating the active layer in one step from the solution containing both the donor and acceptor materials. Recently, a new two-step-coating method was demonstrated to achieve high efficiencies (13%), comparable to state-of-the-art devices. This new method, known as “bilayer sequential processing (BSP)”, involves two sequential solution coating steps of the donor first and then the acceptor from an orthogonal solvent. Next, it is crucial to perform a thermal annealing step on the as-cast film (which has a bi-layer structure) to introduce intermixing of the donor and acceptor materials and form the bulk-heterojunction morphology needed for OPV operation. In our preliminary study, we found that the BSP method can achieve better stability as well as comparable efficiency. The reason for the better stability could be due to that the morphology formed by the BSP is thermodynamically stable, as the thermal annealing process introduces intermixing between donor and acceptor until they reach thermodynamic equilibrium. In contrast, the films formed by conventional one-step coating of the blend solution may result in kinetically quenched and metastable amorphous phase, which was demonstrated to be one main reason for the instability of OSCs. Despite these promising results, the reported BSP OSCs have drawbacks including limited choices of solvents (need to be orthogonal solvents to polymer) and thus materials. The goal of this project is to develop efficient and stable BSP OSCs based on a family of donor polymers with strong temperature dependent aggregation (TDA) properties. The TDA polymers are particularly important to expand the scope of the BSP method, because they have temperature dependent solubility: they can be well dissolved and easily processed at high temperatures (100 oC) but the resulting film becomes completely insoluble at room temperature, which allows for the processing of overlying acceptor layer from a wide range of solvents. Thus, TDA polymer-based BSP OSCs can have a much larger window to optimise processing parameters including solvents, additives, device structure, etc. In this project, we will investigate in details the morphology forming process of BSP-based OSCs and optimise key processing parameters (e.g., solvent, additive, temperature) that have major influence on the resulting device performance. With improved understanding, we hope to develop donor and acceptor materials suitable for the BSP method. The final goal is to further increase the stability and efficiencies of OSC via the combination of BSP process optimisation and material development. 制备有机太阳能电池的传统方法，是将含有给体和受体的混合溶液一步旋涂得到活性层。最近，一种新的两步旋涂法实现了可与最先进器件相媲美的高效率（13%）。这一方法被称为“双层顺序加工”，它包含两个依次旋涂溶液的步骤，先旋涂给体，再旋涂正交溶剂中的受体。然后，对形成的薄膜（双层结构）进行重要的热退火处理，使得给受体材料互相混合，形成有机太阳能电池所需要的体相异质结形貌。 我们在初步的工作中，发现双层顺序加工法可以实现更好的稳定性和类似的效率。更加稳定的原因是，通过双层顺序加工得到的形貌是热力学稳定的，热退火过程使得给受体互相混合直至热力学平衡。与之相反的是，传统一步旋涂混合溶液得到的薄膜，会导致动力学淬火式的亚稳态非晶相，这也被认为是有机太阳能电池不稳定的一个主要原因。除了这些有前景的结果，报道的双层顺序加工有机太阳能电池也有一些缺点，它限制了溶剂（需要是聚合物的正交溶剂）和材料的选择范围。 这一项目的目标，是基于一系列具备温度聚集性质的给体聚合物，发展高效稳定的双层顺序加工有机太阳能电池。具有温度聚集性质的聚合物，对于拓展双层顺序加工方法尤为重要，因为这些聚合物的溶解性依赖于温度：它们可以在高温下溶解得很好，且加工简单，但在室温下则几乎完全不溶，这使得加工覆于其上的受体层有更加广泛的溶剂可选择。因此，基于具有温度聚集性质聚合物的双层顺序加工有机太阳能电池能有更大的空间去优化加工参数，包括溶剂，添加剂，器件结构等等。 在本项目中，我们将具体深入地研究双层顺序加工有机太阳能电池的形貌形成过程，优化对器件表现有重要影响的关键加工参数（例如溶剂，添加剂，温度）。通过深入了解，我们希望研发出适用双层顺序加工方法的给体和受体材料。我们的最终目标是希望通过对双层顺序加工方法的优化和对材料的研发，进一步提升有机太阳能电池的稳定性和效率。

16310019.label: Realisation of objectives
16310019.value: 1. We successfully characterised the morphology forming process of dry BSP method. The method offers greater control in morphology than traditional blend-casting method, achieving ideal domain size and vertical phase segregation. 2. We successfully characterised the morphology forming process of wet BSP method and optimized the annealing conditions. With the optimal processing solvent and annealing condition, a more balanced vertical phase segregation can be achieved which can lead to reduced surface recombination. 3. We have developed new TDA polymer donors and suitable molecular acceptors for the wet BSP method. Devices fabricated with these materials displayed superior performance compared with their blend-casted counterparts. 4. We have developed OSC devices with a PCE beyond 15% (17.7% for the champion device). The highest achievable mechanical, thermal and performance stabilities for developed devices are 94%, 89% and 85% respectively.

16310019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16310019.value: Firstly, we characterised the morphology forming process of dry BSP method, through dynamic secondary-ion spectroscopy (DSIMS), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS) and resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS). It was confirmed that the dry BSP method is able to retain decent polymer crystallinity and hence electron and hole mobilities, which achieving a more ideal domain size compared with the blend-casted counterparts. Further, dry BSP method also prevented excessive vertical phase segregation between donors and acceptors. Secondly, we characterised the morphology forming process of wet BSP method using film-depth-dependent light absorption (FLAS) technique. It was shown that the relative donor-acceptor distribution could be kept more uniform across the active layer compared with the blend-casted counterparts. Further, when processed by toluene at the optimal annealing condition, wet BSP devices exhibit elevated electron mobilities. After understanding the morphology forming process, several TDA polymer donors were developed for the wet BSP method. They were matched with non-fullerene acceptors we previously developed to produce high performing OPV devices which has remarkable thermal, mechanical and performance stability. The best of these devices is PM6:PY-V-γ sequentially processed with ortho-xylene, boasting a FF of 77.7% and PCE of 17.7%. This is attributed to efficient exciton diffusion dynamics, increased carrier mobilities and more balanced electron/hole mobility ratio.

16310019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16310019.value: Further development of the research should be focused on applying the BSP method to a broader number of donor-acceptor systems, as there remains few examples of BSP devices and most newly developed acceptors were not tested using the BSP method, despite its superiority to the conventional blend-casting method as proven in our research. This includes continuing the search for suitable processing solvents and developing specialized additives. On the other hand, it is currently unknown whether the molecular design of the donor or the acceptor has any synergistic effect with the BSP method. It may be worthwhile to investigate, which could lead to opportunities for molecular engineering, maximizing the benefits brought forth by the BSP method.

16310019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16310019.value: In this project, we have investigated the use of bilayer sequential processing (BSP) method for the active donor-acceptor layer of organic solar cells. We acquired better understanding of how it affects the morphology of the active layer. Our research demonstrated that the method leads to more favourable morphology, allowing us to rationalize the boost in power conversion efficiency (PCE) introduced by this method. In light of this, we have developed several donor-acceptor systems that took advantage of this method, fabricating several high-performing organic solar cell devices reaching PCE of 17.7% with great thermal, mechanical and performance stability after 1000 hours of use.

16310219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16310219.value: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMD) are a new generation of materials which exhibit novel quantum properties. A monolayer of TMD material is formed by sandwiching one atomically thin transition metal (such as W, Mo, Nb) layer by two atomically thin chalcogen (such as Te, Se, S) atom layers. Depending on the chemical composition and lattice structure, TMD materials can be insulators, semiconductors or metal. Due to the relatively high electron mobility and the two dimensional nature such that the properties can be easily tuned by gating, TMD materials were considered next generation materials for transistors. Besides its potential application as transistors, it was realized recently that TMD materials exhibit a large number of novel quantum phenomena. For example, 2H-structure TMDs such as NbSe2 are found to be superconducting down to monolayer thickness. Importantly, due to a special type of spin-orbit coupling, it was shown that the superconductor cannot be killed by the strongest magnetic fields in the laboratory. In the case of 1T’-structure monolayer WTe2, it was found to be a special type of insulator called topological insulator. Specifically, a monolayer WTe2 is insulating in the bulk but conducting on the edges. Interestingly, this material can be gated to become a superconductor as well. The combination of the conducting edge states and superconductivity can be a platform for quantum computation. However, there are experimental properties in monolayer WTe2 which are not yet explained. Two of our objectives are to study the superconducting properties of monolayer and multilayer WTe2. In the case of 1Td-structure MoTe2, it was found that the system exhibit a so-called nonlinear Hall effect, in which a voltage is built up in the y-direction when a current is passing in the x-direction. Importantly, this happens in the absence of any magnetic field. However, the nonlinear Hall signals observed are not so strong. In our proposal, we suggest that the nonlinear Hall signal can be strongly enhanced by straining a special type of TMD called polar TMD. The objectives in our proposal are very timely. Once they are accomplished, our understanding of the properties of TMD materials will be greatly enhanced and it could possibly lead to applications of this type of novel material. 过渡金属二硫属化物（TMD）是新一代具有新型量子特性的材料。一个单层的TMD材料是由一种过渡金属（例如W，Mo，Nb）的单原子层夹在两个硫属元素（例如Te，Se，S）的原子薄层之间而形成。根据其不同的化学成分和晶格结构，TMD材料可以是绝缘体，半导体或金属。由于具有相对较高的电子迁移率和易于门电调控的二维特性，TMD材料被认为是下一代的晶体管材料。 除了作为晶体管的潜在应用之外，最近人们意识到TMD材料可以呈现出大量新颖的量子现象。举例来说，如二硒化铌(NbSe2)这样的2H结构-TMD在其厚度达到单层时也可以出现超导电性。重要的是，由于一种特殊的自旋轨道耦合，其超导电性在实验室最强的磁场作用下也不会消失。对于1T'结构的单层二碲化钨(WTe2) ，人们则发现它是一种名为拓扑绝缘体的特殊绝缘体。具体来说，单层WTe2在块体内绝缘，在边界上却可以导电。有趣的是，这种材料也可以通过门控变成超导体。边界导电态和超导性的结合使其可以成为量子计算的平台。然而，有一些单层WTe2的实验特性尚未得到解释。我们的两个目标是研究单层和多层WTe2中的超导特性。 对于1Td结构的WTe2，人们发现该系统可以呈现所谓的非线性霍尔效应，即当电流在x方向通过时，在y方向上可形成电压。重要的是，该现象可以在没有任何磁场的情况下发生。然而，实验上观测到的非线性霍尔信号并不显著。在我们的提案中，我们提议非线性霍尔信号可以通过对极性TMD这类TMD材料施加张力的方法得到明显地增强。 我们提案中的目标非常及时。这些目标的实现将促进我们对TMD材料特性的理解，并可能推动这类新型材料在实际当中得到应用。

16310219.label: Realisation of objectives
16310219.value: Three objectives were proposed for this GRF project and all the objectives had been fulfilled. 1. The first objective of the project is: "Study the origin of enhancement of Hc2 in superconducting monolayer WTe2". In two recent experiments [Science 362, 926–929 (2018), Science 362, 922–925 (2018)], it was shown that superconducting monolayer WTe2 has enhanced Hc2 which is larger than the Pauli limit. However. 1T' structure WTe2 are centrosymmetric materials and it was not understood why there could be enhanced Hc2 beyond the Pauli limit. To address this question, we realised that a new mechanism, which we called the spin-orbit- parity coupling, was responsible for the enhancement of Hc2. This work is published as: Spin-orbit-parity coupled superconductivity in topological monolayer WTe2, Phys. Rev. Lett. 125, 107001 (2020). Yingming Xie, Benjamin Tong Zhou, K. T. Law* More recently, we further collaborated with experimentalists in Fudan University on this topic. The predicted Spin-orbit-parity coupled superconductivity by the above PRL paper [PRL 125, 107001 (2020)] was observed by the Fudan group in 2M-structure WS2. This work, titled " Spin–orbit–parity coupled superconductivity in atomically thin 2M-WS2" appeared in Nature Physics in 2023. “Spin–orbit–parity coupled superconductivity in atomically thin 2M-WS2” Enze Zhang, Ying-Ming Xie, Yuqiang Fang, Jinglei Zhang, Xian Xu, Yi-Chao Zou, Pengliang Leng, Xue-Jian Gao, Yong Zhang, Linfeng Ai, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Shanshan Liu, Jingyi Yan, Wei Zhao, Sarah J. The second objective of the project was "Study the anisotropic Hc2 and superconducting pairing correlations in multilayer WTe2". In the mid-term report, we reported that " This objective is under investigation with an experimental group in Fudan University. A manuscript is submitted and under review. Even though in this work, we focus on the anisotropic Hc2 of a closely related materials WS2 instead of WTe2." This work is now published as: “Spin–orbit–parity coupled superconductivity in atomically thin 2M-WS2” Enze Zhang, Ying-Ming Xie, Yuqiang Fang, Jinglei Zhang, Xian Xu, Yi-Chao Zou, Pengliang Leng, Xue-Jian Gao, Yong Zhang, Linfeng Ai, Yuda Zhang, Zehao Jia, Shanshan Liu, Jingyi Yan, Wei Zhao, Sarah J. With the support of this GRF project, we studied the nonlinear Hall effect in both twisted bilayer graphene as well as in 2H-structure TMDs. The resulted publications are: a. Giant nonlinear Hall effect in strained twisted bilayer graphene, Phys. Rev. B 106, L041111 (2022). Cheng-Ping Zhang, Jiewen Xiao, Benjamin T. Zhou, Jin-Xin Hu, Ying-Ming Xie, Binghai Yan*, K. T. More recently, we further studied: Higher-order nonlinear anomalous Hall effects induced by Berry curvature multipoles CP Zhang, XJ Gao, YM Xie, HC Po, KT Law*, Physical Review B 107, 115142 (2023). This theoretical work proposed a new mechanism to realize higher order (3rd order or above) nonlinear Hall effect due to the Berry curvature multipoles in anti-ferromagnets. Our prediction has been realized by two experimental groups. We believe that we will open a new area of study in higher order nonlinear Hall effect in anti-ferromagnets.

16310219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16310219.value: In a recent theoretical work supported by this GRF project [Physical Review B 107, 115142 (2023)], we proposed a new mechanism to realize higher order (3rd order or above) nonlinear Hall effect due to the Berry curvature multipoles in anti-ferromagnets. Our prediction has been realized by two experimental groups. We believe that we will open a new area of study in higher order nonlinear Hall effect in anti-ferromagnets. Moreover, by the support of this project, we discovered a new type of superconductivity which we named spin-orbit-parity coupled superconductivity in centrosymmetric materials. Surprisingly, we recently found that many newly discovered superconductors ( such as in kagome superconductors) are spin-orbit-parity coupled superconductors. We will continue to explore the effect of spin-orbit-parity coupling in these superconductors.

16310219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16310219.value: In this work, the PI discovered a new type of superconductor which they called spin-orbit-parity superconductors. They theoretical predictions were soon verified experimentally. This direction of work resulted in two high profile publications and attracted a lot of attention from the physics community. The PI also studied how nonlinear Hall effect can appear in two-dimensional systems. The nonlinear Hall effect is an effect that convert a longitudinal signal with frequency w into a transverse voltage signal with frequency nw where n is an integer. The PI discovered new mechanisms of generating nonlinear Hall effect and his theory is important for higher harmonic generations.

16310419.value: 電化學催化還原二氧化碳生成更有價值的化學品可以降低大氣中的二氧化碳濃度，同時存儲新能源。但是這項新進技術離大規模工業應用還有很大的距離，主要是電催化劑的性能還遠遠不夠好。在電催化過程中，有很多中產物可以生成，包括CO、多碳化合物等。其中CO可以直接應用於Fischer–Tropsch過程。 這個項目將研發兩種對CO和C2+產物有極高選擇性的模型催化劑。一種是碳基單分子催化劑。在電位高於-0.7V時，其對CO的選擇性可以達到98%以上。我們將合成各種金屬單原子（鐵、鎳、錳等）和非金屬（氮、硫、硼、磷等）參雜的碳材料來提高CO的選擇性和催化活性。另外，我們也將合成摻雜了氮、硒等原子的銅基納米催化劑用於生成C2+產物。更重要的是，我們還應用原位光譜學和顯微技術，包括表面增強紅外、表面增強拉曼、X-射線吸收譜、X-射線衍射譜、液體透射電鏡等，來研究催化反應堆中間產物，催化劑的結構、組分等。和理論計算結合，我們還將得到催化劑的物理化學性能和催化性能之間的關係。本項目所取得的結果將有助於進一步了解二氧化碳電催化還原的反應機理和設計更先進的催化劑。

16310419.label: Realisation of objectives
16310419.value: 1. To develop protocols for the synthesis of single atom-based carbon materials with heteroatom doping and doped Cu-based nanocatalysts with precisely controlled composition and structure. We have fully achieved this objective. By annealing Fe-containing ZIF-8 in an argon atmosphere, we synthesized highly dispersed nitrogen-coordinated Fe single atom sites on carbon (Fe-N-C). The resulting electrocatalyst exhibited an excellent CO FE of 93.5%, with the CO generation onset occurring at a very low overpotential of 90 mV. A protocol to synthesize oxide-derived Cu nanosheets was also developed via microwave irradiation. The morphology and chemical state of the Cu sites were tuned by modifying the copper nitrate content during the microwave-assisted reduction step. A maximum C2+ FE of 72% was achieved for the Cu-30 catalyst (synthesized with 30 wt% Cu(NO3)2 3H2O). 2. To determine the reaction mechanisms and the evolution of the catalyst’s structure and composition under reaction conditions and correlate them with the catalytic selectivity and activity during CO2RR. This objective was fully achieved. For the Fe-N-C catalyst, in situ FTIR spectroscopy was used to identify a spectator *CO species that adsorbs strongly on the metal atom sites. By combining the FTIR data with DFT calculations, we showed that the inactive *CO species form on Fe-N4 moieties anchored on bulk graphitic sites. On the other hand, the Fe-N4 sites on graphitic pores/defects are likely the active sites towards effective CO generation during CO2RR. For the oxide-derived Cu nanosheet catalyst, we were able to identify that the partial Cu oxidation and surface roughness of the electrocatalysts were key parameters that have to be maximized in order to attain a high selectivity towards C2+ products. 3. To establish guidelines for the rational design of a more advanced CO2RR catalyst by combining theoretical simulations and experimental results. This objective was fully achieved. For the Fe-N-C single atom sites, we have demonstrated the importance of graphitic defects in enhancing the electrocatalyst activity of single atom sites by promoting the CO2→*COOH→*CO→CO pathway. The conclusions made in this study can be further extended to the rational design of more advanced CO2RR single atom catalysts, such as diatom catalysts and tandem catalysts containing single atom sites. For the formation of C2+ products, we have also demonstrated how the ECSA and oxidation state of copper can be optimized in CO2RR catalysts to attain exemplary faradaic efficiencies towards C2+ products.
