16310419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16310419.value: 1. Fe single atom electrocatalysts (Fe-N-C) were synthesized through the controlled pyrolysis of Fe-doped ZIF-8, yielding well-dispersed nitrogen-coordinated Fe single atom sites (Fe-N4) hosted on a carbon matrix, as confirmed via X-ray absorption spectroscopy and scanning transmission electron microscopy. The resulting electrocatalyst exhibited an exemplary CO2RR performance toward CO, with a maximum faradaic efficiency of 93.5% at -0.5 V vs. RHE. A very positive CO formation onset potential of -0.2 V vs. RHE (corresponding to a 90 mV overpotential) was also achieved. By combining the in situ FTIR spectroscopy data with DFT calculations, we identified that the Fe-N4 sites hosted on a bulk graphitic substrate generated *CO spectator species that adsorbed too strongly on the single atom sites, preventing CO desorption and generation. It was determined that effective CO generation likely occurred on Fe-N4 sites anchored on defective graphene pores, due to the optimal *COOH and *CO adsorption energies on these active sites. This work has been published in Journal Paper #17. 2. Oxide-derived Cu nanosheets (OD-Cu NSs) were synthesized via a hydrothermal method coupled with microwave irradiation-assisted reduction. By modifying the copper nitrate content during microwave reduction, the surface roughness, ECSA, and partial oxidation of the resulting OD-Cu NSs can be carefully regulated. An impressive FE toward C2+ products of 72% at a partial current density of 55 mA cm-2 was achieved for the Cu-30 electrocatalyst. The exemplary performance was attributed to the large amount of Cu+ species and the high ECSA (93 cm2) of the electrocatalyst. This work has been published in Journal Paper #12.

16310419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16310419.value: Our current method to synthesize Fe-N-C electrocatalysts can be further developed and extended for the rational design of diatomic catalysts with dual active sites. Preliminary DFT calculations have already shown that such active sites can further improve the thermodynamics of the CO2-to-CO pathway. The atomically dispersed metal sites on carbon may also be mixed with copper electrocatalysts for the generation of advanced products (i.e., hydrocarbons and alcohols) through tandem catalysis. The OD-Cu NS electrocatalysts may further be applied at high current density applications to produce ethylene and ethanol in a flow cell or a membrane electrode assembly. Due to the enhanced CO2 mass transport and local pH in these large-scale devices, much higher C2+ faradaic efficiencies and geometric current densities may be achieved.

16310419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16310419.value: In this project, atomically dispersed Fe-N-C electrocatalysts were prepared from the pyrolysis of a Fe-loaded ZIF-8 template. The Fe-N-C catalysts showed an exemplary faradaic efficiency toward CO (93.5% at -0.5 V) during CO2 reduction with a very positive onset potential (-0.2 V, 90 mV overpotential). By integrating DFT calculations with in situ FTIR spectroscopy, Fe-N4 sites on defective graphitic pores were identified to be highly active towards CO generation. A facile method to synthesize oxide-derived Cu nanosheets via hydrothermal synthesis and microwave irradiation was also developed. By modulating the surface roughness and partial oxidation of the Cu sites, the C2+ selectivity can be optimized, reaching a maximum C2+ faradaic efficiency of 72% and a partial current density of 55 mA cm-2. This project has significantly advanced CO2RR research by providing valuable insights on the rational design of catalysts that can selectively produce CO and C2+ products.

16501019.label: Project Objectives

Investigate how variable liabilities impact decisions by firms and characterize the equilibrium liabilities chosen by strategic market regulators.

16501019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501019.value: A firm often sells a product with the same level of safety in several markets that differ in demand and cost conditions. If consumers are harmed when using the product, the firm could incur liabilities. In practice, product liability laws and safety standards often differ across markets (e.g. among states in the United States). There have been policy debates on whether a uniform liability or safety standard should be imposed. Courts in the U.S. sometimes issue a pre-emption doctrine to ban inconsistent state laws or safety regulations. Should product liability be market-specific ("variable regime") or uniform ("uniform regime") across these markets? How would the liability regimes affect investment by a firm in improving product safety? This project intends to address these questions. Based on industry examples and lawsuits, we will first formulate a theoretical framework and examine how different liability regimes impact a firm's decisions in relation to investments in product safety, market entry, and output levels. We expect to show that, under the uniform liability regime, a greater uniform liability can motivate the firm to improve product safety but can also reduce the firm's incentive to enter one of the markets or decrease output levels in different markets. These trade-offs lead to the optimal uniform liability, which may be excessive or insufficient for maximizing the social benefit in each particular market. Under the variable liability regime, each market regulator chooses the liability in his own market, trying to maximize the social benefit in that particular market. However, a unilateral increase of liability in one market can cause externalities on market entry and output level in the other market. We will characterize the equilibrium liabilities the market regulators choose. Finally, we will compare the social benefits under the two liability regimes. Compared with the uniform regime, the variable regime allows for flexible liabilities that cater to market differences and may improve product safety, but the externalities on market entry and outputs can cause a social loss, which tends to be greater when the market difference is larger. Thus, we expect to show that the variable liability regime can be more efficient when the market difference is small while the uniform regime is more efficient when the market difference is large. The potential findings will deepen our understanding of the liability impact on decisions by multi-market firms, and more importantly, provide rich policy implications on the design of liability laws.

16501019.label: Realisation of objectives
16501019.value: All the project objectives have been achieved and the findings have been included in two research articles. The first one was accepted and published by the Journal of International Economics. We also prepare to submit the second article to a journal shortly. We focus on product safety related to data protection in the first article and examine safety issues related to product defects in the second article, as detailed below. (1) The first article “International Production of Consumer Data” Firms often collect, use, and sell consumer data, which can generate extra revenue. However, such data usage may harm consumers, due to fraud or privacy breaches. The economics literature has extensive studies on data safety and related regulations or liability regimes. However, there has been little analysis of consumer data protection when firms sell products and collect data in multiple markets/countries. We collected examples of cross-country differences in consumer preference for data safety and regulations. For example, The European Union started to implement the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) in 2018, while 42% of countries did not have legislation or regulation on data protection. How would variable rules on data usage/protection affect firms’ decisions and global welfare? What is the scope for international coordination on imposing a uniform rule on data safety? We have addressed these questions in the article. Objective 1: We first formulated a theoretical model where a multinational firm sells a product and collects consumer data in two countries. The firm receives two streams of revenue, product sales and data usage/sales. The firm chooses the same data protection or data-usage level in the two countries. More data usage generates more data revenue for the firm but causes larger disutility to consumers. Consumers in the two countries have different disutility from data usage. However, they could not observe the firm’s choice of data usage, so there is a moral hazard problem: Absent liability or regulation, the firm may overuse consumer data or exert too less protection effort. When data revenue changes, the firm may adjust its prices differently in the two countries, resulting in different impacts on consumer surplus. We characterized the uniform cap on data usage that maximizes global welfare. This uniform cap can be implemented, for example, by a negligence-based liability rule under which the firm is liable only if its data usage is above the cap. Objective 2: We then considered unilateral caps on data usage imposed by the two countries. Although the caps alleviate the moral hazard problem, the variation in the caps may reduce global welfare, because the country with the stronger preference for privacy will impose a lower cap and not consider the negative externality on the output and data usage in the other country. Given these trade-offs, we showed that such variable caps would increase global welfare when data-usage transparency is low but decrease global welfare when transparency is high. We further showed that variable caps might still reduce welfare even if the firm could invest in data localization. Objective 3: Finally, we compared the uniform cap to the variable caps in equilibrium. There are substantial gains from international coordination, though a uniform map may not be globally optimal given the difference in consumers’ preference for privacy across countries. To summarize, this article contributes to the industrial-organization literature and provides implications for international policy harmonization. (2) The second article “Multimarket Firms and Product Liability: Uniform v.s. Variable Rules” Many products contain safety risks that can cause harm to consumers, though they also generate value for consumers and society. Tort law or product liability rules can motivate firms to improve product safety and protect consumers. Although many studies have examined liability design, there is no theoretical analysis of liability differences in the multimarket context. We summarized cross-market differences in tort law. In the U.S., state courts take different stances in adopting liability guidelines from the Restatement (Third) of Torts (1998), and state lawmakers impose different liability rules and safety regulations. The literature showed that courts in some states were friendly to businesses while those in other states were friendly to consumers. Federal lawmakers and the Supreme Court may impose the pre-emption doctrine to prevent variable rules. Similarly, in the European Union, the Product Liability Directive provides uniform liability guidelines, though member countries have different enforcement rules. Is a uniform or a variable liability rule across markets more desirable from social welfare perspective? We have addressed this question in the second article. Objective 1: We started with a baseline model where a firm sells a product with safety risks in two markets to inattentive consumers, who are not aware of product safety risks. The firm can make a fixed investment to eliminate safety risks with some probability. After observing the outcome of the investment, the firm sets different prices in the two markets. A federal lawmaker sets a standard liability, which would be implemented if local lawmakers or courts have no discretion (i.e. a uniform rule). However, if they have discretion (i.e. a variable rule), they may depart from the standard liability. We assumed that market 1 is consumer-friendly while market 2 is business-friendly, in the sense that, under the variable rule, the per-unit liability is larger than the standard level in market 1 but lower in market 2. The difference is determined by the level of discretion or variability. We first showed how an increase in variability would affect the optimal standard liability. The increase in variability raises the firm’s liability cost in market 1 but lowers it in market 2, so the firm’s total profit from the faultable product can increase or decrease. Depending on the market sizes, the standard liability should be lower or higher, to maintain the firm’s investment incentive while minimizing output distortion. Objective 2: We then examined the welfare effects of allowing variable liability. Given that the standard liability is set at the optimal level, the firm always makes the safety investment. A change in variability, however, would reduce output in market 1 and raise output in market 2. This not only changes total output but also causes “output reallocation” from market 1 to market 2. This output reallocation effect may increase welfare if the price (i.e., the marginal consumer’s value) in market 2 is larger than the price (i.e. the marginal consumer’s value) in market 1, but decrease welfare if otherwise. The welfare impact from the change of total output and the output reallocation depends on the price elasticity of demand and the curvature of demand. Objective 3: Finally, we compared welfare under uniform liability to welfare under variable liability. We showed that uniform liability would be socially optimal if market 2 (the business-friendly market) has weakly more elastic demand but weakly lower demand curvature than market 1 (the consumer-friendly market), while variable liability could be socially optimal if otherwise. We also showed the robustness of the results in an extended model where some consumers are attentive and aware of product safety risks. In sum, the second article contributes to the literature on both industrial organization and law and economics. It also provides policy implications on liability design for multimarket firms.

16501019.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501019.value: This project has generated theoretical findings and policy implications on the design of liability and regulation, considering multimarket firms’ actions to improve product safety related to data usage and product defects. In the application of data safety, we have constructed a model where a multinational firm sells its product and collects consumer data in two countries with differences in consumer disutility from data usage. Consumers cannot fully observe the firm’s data-usage levels. The two countries can set unilateral caps on data usage. Absent liability or regulation, the firm tends to overuse consumer data. More importantly, although the unilateral caps on data usage can solve the moral hazard problem, the country with the stronger preference for privacy will impose a lower cap, which creates negative externalities on output and data usage in the other country. The unilateral caps raise global welfare when data-usage transparency is low but reduce welfare when transparency is high. Finally, international coordination can raise welfare, though a uniform cap is not necessarily optimal. The results have been included in the article “International Protection of Consumer Data,” which was presented in a few seminars and then published by the Journal of International Economics (see part C). In the application of product defects, we have created a model where a firm sells a product with potential safety risks to inattentive consumers in two markets. Product liability motivates the firm to make a fixed investment to eliminate the risk with some probability. Federal lawmakers set the standard liability, but local lawmakers and courts may depart from it. Under uniform liability, the firm has the same per-unit liability cost in the two markets; under variable liability, however, the firm’s liability cost is larger in market 1 but lower in market 2. The standard liability is chosen to motivate the firm to make safety investments while minimizing output distortion. It is shown that variable liability not only changes total output but also causes output reallocation from market 1 to market 2. Uniform liability is optimal if market 2 has more elastic demand but lower demand curvature, while variable liability can be optimal if otherwise. These results have been included in the second article “Multimarket Firms and Product Liability: Uniform v.s. Variable Rules" (see part C).

16501019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501019.value: As mentioned above, all of the findings have been included in two articles. The first one has been published. In the short run, we plan to submit the second article to a journal and make further revisions after getting the referees’ comments. In the long run, there are a few potential directions for future research. In terms of data protection, it would be meaningful to consider the various ways for data usage to raise consumer utility and the different mechanisms (liability, regulation, reputation, etc.) in governing multimarket firms’ data protection actions. In terms of safety issues related to product defects, it would be useful to examine how variable liability rules affect multimarket firms’ entry or exit decisions and whether the comparison between uniform and variable liability rules is different for single-market firms. Finally, for both applications, our articles focus on a monopoly firm, while further analysis of competitive firms would enrich policy implications.

16501019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501019.value: Multimarket firms sell their products and collect consumer data in multiple markets. The products may contain safety risks, and data usage may cause fraud and privacy breaches. By comparing uniform and variable liability rules or regulations, this project provides valuable implications for business strategies and policy discussions. About consumer data protection, we show that variable caps on data usage unilaterally imposed by different countries can motivate multimarket firms to improve data protection. However, the country with a stronger preference for consumer privacy will impose tougher regulations, which negatively affects social benefits in other countries. The findings imply that there is a large value in international coordination on data protection, sometimes with a uniform cap on data usage. Regarding safety issues related to product defects, we have constructed a model where local lawmakers and courts may depart from the standard liability set by federal lawmakers. As compared to uniform liability (no departure from the standard liability), variable liability raises multimarket firms’ liability cost in the consumer-friendly market but lowers it in the business-friendly market, thereby reducing output in the former market while raising output in the latter. The desirability of variable liability depends on the comparison of demand conditions between the two markets.

16501419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501419.value: Since the Brexit referendum and the US presidential election in 2016, the public has been increasingly aware of prevailing information manipulation across different types of media in many countries, whether they are governed autocratically or democratically. Is information manipulation necessarily bad for the public? If not, under what conditions could information manipulation be socially beneficial? When the public is aware of information manipulation, could it lead to well-intended manipulation having unwanted consequences? We develop a formal game-theoretical model to study these questions. 自2016年英國脫歐公投和美國總統大選之後，通過各類媒體的信息操縱越來越被大眾警覺。這種信息操縱，不論是在民主國家或在極權國家，都非常普遍。但是信息操縱一定會有損大眾利益嗎？如果不一定，在哪些情況下信息操縱是有利於大眾的呢？如果大眾在獲取資訊時有意識地避免受操縱信息的影響，這會不會讓原本有利於大眾的信息操縱產生預想不到的結果？這個研究用博弈論模型去探討這些問題。

16501419.label: Realisation of objectives
16501419.value: Objectives 1 and 2 have been achieved with the general payoff structure as in Angeletos and Pavan (2007). Objective 3 and 5 have been achieved with a focus on the sender being either benevelent or malicious. Objective 4 has been achieved in applying the insights of the general model to central bank communication, where the central banker is the benevelent information interventor. Objective 6 has been achieved by developing a relative rating method. We also validate the method using an online experiment. We did not pursue objective 3 and 5 with payoff externality because this case turns out to be equivalent to a setting where the sender's and the receivers' payoffs are partially aligned with a known wedge. When the sender cannot commit to an information structure, it is not practical, in our opinion, to assume that the sender can commit to a payoff wedge.

16501419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501419.value: 1) There is always active information manipulation in equilibrium, even when sender is benevolent. 2) When the sender is benevolent, optimal information manipulation makes idiosyncratic signals more precise and shifts the mean of idiosyncratic signals away from the common prior. When the sender is malicious, optimal information manipulation makes idiosyncratic signals less precise and shifts the mean of idiosyncratic signals closer to the common prior. 3) When the sender is benevolent, information manipulation reduces social welfare if and only if the receivers have strong social aversion to dispersion and the idiosyncratic signals are noisy enough before any information manipulation. So information manipulation corrects inefficiency in the equilibrium use of information if the receivers have weak enough social aversion to dispersion or if the idiosyncratic signals are precise enough before any information manipulation. 4) When the sender is malicious, information manipulation improves social welfare if and only if the receivers have strong social aversion to dispersion and the idiosyncratic signals are noisy enough before any information manipulation. These are also conditions under which information manipulation corrects inefficiency in the equilibrium use of information. 5) In the central bank communication application, social welfare improves with the intrinsic precision of the idiosyncratic signals (the precision without any information manipulation) when the intrinsic precision is higher than a cutoff value. The cutoff value varies with the targeting rule of the central bank as the targeting rule determines the private sector's social aversion to disperson. Some of the findings above are incorporated in the paper "Creating Confusion" published at the Journal of Economic Theory. 6) The relative rating approach asks the raters to report the news articles' stand on an issues to the raters' own stand, and this approach allows us to obtain more precise aggregate rating of the news articles, as validated via an online experiment. The findings are reported in the paper "It’s All Relative! A Method to Counter Human Bias in Crowdsourced Stance Detection of News Articles" published at Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction.

16501419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501419.value: There are two potential future direction of this research. One is to look for interesting applications of the insights obtained from the general model. One example could be the information manipulation by social media platforms as it is a natural setting where the sender cannot commit to an information structure. The other is to further develop the empirical method of measuring media bias and news consumer's belief changes. I have a follow-up project that aims to establish the relation between the news consumer's own bias and their response to news articles.

16501419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501419.value: The research project aims to study the nature of information manipulation that is prevaling across various forms of media in different countries, regardless of their governance structure (autocratic or democratic). Our findings indicate that while information manipulation may originate from good intentions, its outcomes may not always align with the intended goals. We identify specific conditions in which information manipulation can have beneficial effects on society. Consequently, our research offers valuable insights on how to promote socially desirable outcomes amidst the widespread presence of information manipulation.

16501619.label: Project Objectives
16501619.value: Document the rise in knowledge intensity over time and across different industries or companies. Identify good measures of knowledge intensity for policy makers, investment professionals, and academic researchers. Potential candidates include: intangible capital, high-tech industry classification, among others. Study how knowledge intensity varies in the cross-sectional composition of risk factors, particularly those constructed using accounting variables, which may thus be affected by off-balance-sheet intangible capital such as R&D. For example, an influential paper Daniel and Titman (2006) uses intangible information (five-year return in excess of five-year change in book value) to study the value effect. We will analyse intangible information in excess of (off-balance-sheet) intangible capital to potentially make a contribution. A knowledge-intensive company like Google tends to have high valuation ratios such as its price-to-earnings ratio. When the market consists more and more of such stocks, the market valuation ratio will increase. This will help understand the recent observation of increasingly higher market valuation, which help us understand structural break documented by Lettau and Nieuwerburgh (2007). They show evidence in favor of a structural break in early 1990s, which coincides with the arrival of the Information Age and the rise of the dot-com companies. We will also analyze whether the time-series return prediction regressions benefit by explicitly accounting for the rise of knowledge-intensive firms, whose high valuation ratios may reflect their high off-the-balance sheet R&D capital hence the effect of valuation ratio on future stock returns may differ from that of industrial firms without significant R&D.

16501619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16501619.value: The world economy is increasingly dominated by knowledge, manifested as technology, R&D, and human capital, among other things. At the same time, physical capital input has become less dominant in publicly listed companies. Traditional industrial companies such as GE have ceded influence to companies like Amazon, Apple, or Tencent. Bloomberg reported that, in 2018, physical capital is less than half of the total shareholder equity of US public companies. Even this amount may under-state the rise of intangible capital input because investments such as R&D are expensed hence do not show up as shareholder equity. By our own calculations, using data from Peters and Taylor (2017) that accounts for off-balance-sheet intangible assets such as R&D, the total intangible assets for US public companies are USD 17 Trillion, which includes USD 7 Trillion in off-balance-sheet intangible assets. The intangible assets are high in comparison to the USD 24 Trillion of total common shareholder equity. Against this backdrop, this research project aims to study asset pricing implications in the knowledge economy. There are three purposes of our investigation: 1. To document the rise in knowledge intensity over time and across different industries or companies; 2. To identify good measures of knowledge intensity for policy makers, investment professionals, and academic researchers; and 3. Using the measures of knowledge intensity identified in the previous step to analyze the asset pricing implications of the recent rise in knowledge intensity. Why do we expect there will be an effect? Intuitively, this is because asset pricing is dependent on the market and its dynamics. For example, when the market consists entirely of knowledge-intensive stocks, holding knowledge-intensive stocks become riskier due to the lack of diversification. Therefore, the expected return from investing in such stocks may be higher than in a market with few knowledge-intensive stocks. As another example, a knowledge intensive company like Google tends to have high valuation ratios such as price-to-earnings ratio. When the market consists of more of these stocks, market valuation ratios will increase. This will help us understand the recent observation of higher and higher market valuations, which is documented as a "structural break" in prestigious academic publications. Our findings can provide an explanation for this structural break. It will help improve return prediction regressions based on market valuation ratios in research used by both academics and practitioners alike. 世界经济越来越多地被知识所主导，表现为技术，研发和人力资本等等。同时，物质资本投入在上市公司中地位逐渐下降。传统工业公司例如通用电气已经被亚马逊，苹果或腾讯等公司赶超。彭博社报道，在2018年，实物资本已经不到 美国上市公司的股东权益总额的一半。即便是这个数额也可能低估了无形资本投入的涨幅。因为研发等投资是费用，因此没有直接记入股东权益。根据我们自己的计算，美国上市公司的无形资产总额为17万亿美元，其中包括美元7万亿的资产负债表外无形资产。这是很高的无形资产，因为普通股股东权益总共只有24万亿美元。 在此背景下，该研究项目旨在研究知识经济下的资产定价。我们的调查有三个目的： 1.记录随着时间​​的推移知识密集度在不同行业和公司的变化; 2.比较和确定良好的知识密集度量，为决策者，投资专业人士和学术研究人员的进一步研究做准备; 3.使用前一步骤中确定的知识密集度量来分析知识密集度上升的资产定价影响。为什么我们期待会有影响？因为资产定价依赖于市场及其动态。例如，当市场中知识密集型股票逐渐增多，投资者的资金越来越多的集中于这类知识密集型股票而变得风险更大。因此，投资此类股票的预期回报可能高于知识密集型股票市场较少的市场。另外，像谷歌这样的知识密集型公司往往具有较高的市盈率。当市场包含更多这些股票时，整个市场的市盈率将增加。这会有助于解释过去十几年市场市盈率不断增高的现象。这将有助于改善用市盈率对未来投资回报的预测。

16501619.label: Realisation of objectives
16501619.value: The most striking finding of our paper is that today's economy is so knowledge intensive that companies care about secrecy of their valuable innovations to the extent that they are willing to hide such innovations from outside people including even their own shareholders, which results in a higher cost of equity funding valuable innovations than when such secrecy is absent. We believe that we are the first to reveal the tension between secrecy and the cost of equity financing innovations with high growth potential. This phenomenon is more prominent among industries or companies that have a high growth rate and whose growth relies significantly on innovation. Since the past papers identify cash-based operating profitability as the most important determinant of future firm growth, we find that such high cost of equity associated with secrecy is more pronounced for firms with high cash-based operating profitability, which is consistent with the mechanism we document. Since the profitability factor is a prominent risk factor featured in benchmark risk factor models, our finding also contributes to our understanding of risk premia particularly those from the profitability factor. We provide a measure to estimate the effect on the cost of equity from secrecy based on the announcement stock returns around patent grants. The idea is that the patent grant publicly reveals the secrecy. If investors realize that they undervalued a firm’s innovation before the revelation, the announcement return should be high. We also discuss structural reasons in patent law and regulation that impede information revelation. We also analyze the introduction of a new law (American Inventors Protection Act) that aims to promote early revelation of patents’ secrets. However, we find that firm tactics evolve over time in response to regulation. We document some firm tactics that allow them to maintain secrecy even after the new law is implemented. This also shows that secrecy continues to be important over time for innovative firms. We also analyze prominent technology companies individually such as Google, Apple, Meta, etc. We find that many such prominent innovators were among the class of firms we identify that use secrecy to protect their valuable innovation and exhibit high stock returns upon revelation of such innovation. Therefore, our findings help contribute understanding to the returns of these important innovators. The above summarizes our main findings regarding all the objectives. We are able to reveal an important aspect of an knowledge intensive economy, which is the tradeoff between the secrecy protection of innovations and the cost of such secrecy in terms of high cost of equity funding innovative research. We provide evidence across firms/industries/time [objective 1] on such tradeoff between secrecy and cost of funding. We provide a measure of such tradeoffs and analyze the effect of policy, which are useful for policymakers, investors, as well as researchers [objective 2]. We also find that such tradeoff varies in the cross section. The variation is especially strong across the profitability dimension, which is a key determinant of future firm growth [objective 3]. We show our mechanism is applicable to prominent innovators like Google and helps understand the stock market performance of such firms [objective 4]. We believe we have successfully achieved all the planned objectives.

16501619.label: Major findings and research outcome
16501619.value: We find evidence consistent with firms protecting their innovations using secrecy. The effect is stronger for more valuable innovations. However, secrecy also keeps the firms’ own shareholders in the dark and results in an under-valuation of the innovation, which translates into a higher cost of equity funding the research. We believe we are the first to document the tradeoff between secrecy and cost of equity. We measure the effect using the stock price response to patent grant announcements, which reveal the secrecy. Using our measure, we find a significant undervaluation of such innovations protected by secrecy. The undervaluation aggregates to US$5.8 billion per year, which is an economically significant amount. Our finding also helps us understand the risk premium of a prominent risk factor like the profitability factor. It also sheds light on the stock market performance of important technology firms like Google. We document our findings in a paper entitled “Patent and Latent Innovation.” We started submitting the paper to conferences from early 2024. We have received acceptance from two conferences. We will attend and present the paper in one of the conferences in June 2024. We cannot make the other conference so have to skip it. But we will provide proof of acceptance from both conferences in part C, to show that the paper has a good reception from academia. We also started submitting the paper to journals from April 2024. The paper is currently under review at a journal.

16501619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16501619.value: There is room to study how to mitigate the tradeoff between high cost of equity and secrecy protection of innovation. This will be useful for policy makers, decision makers in the innovating firms, and their investors. This will likely involve research on the competition between firms and funding of individual firms when information becomes an important input to production.

16501619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16501619.value: The important innovations are protected by secrecy. However, secrecy also blinds shareholders who then undervalue the innovations. We reveal such a tension between secrecy protection and cost of funding of important innovations. The undervaluation is large at US$5.8 billion per year, which calls for further research into mitigating such a tension that can potentially allow the research of important innovations be both protected from copycats and funded at a lower cost.

16502019.value: 在过去三十年中，行为金融作为一个领域已经大受欢迎。该领域记录了投资者行为和价格的系统模式，这些模式与心理学中的实验证据相比，与“理性”背后的传统公理更为一致。然而，行为金融的从业者和批评者都指出了一些怀疑主义的重要原因。其中最突出的一个事实是，心理学中的大多数证据 - 这是该领域的基础 - 来自于参与者几乎没有利害关系的实验。争论的焦点是，一旦我们检查高风险情况下的行为 - 比如现实世界的财务决策 - 许多记录在案的偏见可能会消失（例如，Levitt和List，2008）。 这个假设特别难以测试。人们可以指出孤立的情况，例如退休账户决策中的偏见，赌注似乎没有消除偏见;但是说更多关于赌注和错误的事情是很困难的。通过显示在实验中增加一些赌注似乎没有减少偏见，已经取得了一些进展，但批评者仍然认为预算约束意味着这些实验中的赌注仍然不足以产生影响。毕竟，很难设计出实验，其中每个参与者“正确”的奖励是数十或数十万美元，就像在现实世界中一样。 那么，关于高风险是否确实减少偏见的理想实验将是随机地大幅增加受试者的禀赋，并检查偏见是否确实像批评一样消失。在这个项目中，我们计划利用一个与理想实验非常相似的研究设计，研究由父母死亡导致的遗产引起的可投资禀赋的冲击。举个例子，假设两个父亲死亡，留下相同的遗产。然而，其中一个有两个孩子（比如A1和A2），其中必须分享继承，而另一个孩子（B）继承一切。投资错误 - 例如交易中的处置效应 - 是否会因所有继承人而减少，但相对于A1和A2，投资股票遭受更大冲击的B会减少更多吗？我们将通过审查包含丹麦全体人口投资决策的高质量行政登记数据来回答这些问题。因此，我们的估计将以一种迄今为止文献未获得的方式促成利害关系和偏见。

16502019.label: Realisation of objectives
16502019.value: Project objectives have been fully achieved. Over the past three decades, behavioral finance as a field has documented many ways in which investors systematically make mistakes, contradicting basic tenets of rationality underlying some of our most seminal theories of finance (Barberis and Thaler, 2003). One widely used justification for these theories to keep assuming rationality is that many of these financial mistakes arise in contexts with little at stake, e.g., experimental payoffs, or “play money” in discount brokerage accounts. The argument follows that if we observe the same people making decisions when stakes are higher, they might make fewer mistakes, aligning their behavior with the rational agent (Levitt and List, 2008). This issue is critical because if mistakes are largely driven by small stakes, then policies such as financial education cannot reduce the incidence of mistakes. Understanding whether mistakes are driven by personal traits (such as cognitive ability or financial sophistication) or by limited stakes requires within-person evidence on the sensitivity of investment mistakes to changes in stakes. However, such evidence on how much smarter people get when stakes are raised remains scant, despite a very large literature on investment mistakes. In this study, we exploit within-person variation in stakes arising from inheritances due to unexpected parental deaths. A key benefit of our setting is that we can observe the propensity to mistakes for each individual beneficiaries before and after the inheritance. Our key identifying assumption is that the timing of these inheritances, arising from sudden deaths, is random. This allows us to attribute changes in mistakes after inheriting to changes in stakes. Further, we examine premature deaths of adult siblings before parental bereavement, to generate exogenous differences in bequest sizes. Our key finding is that mistakes respond very little to changes in stakes, even when such changes are substantial. An important implication of this finding is that investment mistakes are not an artifact of small stakes. Rather, our evidence suggests that these mistakes arise from personal traits, which should be explicitly modelled in theories of investment behavior.

16502019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502019.value: Many follow-up studies are possible using the main dataset used. One such study we are planning concerns revisiting the evidence on whether gender matters for trading ability, using an exogenous shock to when both males and females need to start trading stocks.

16502019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502019.value: Do investors make fewer mistakes if they have more at stake? We answer this question by examining within-person changes in the propensity to make mistakes following inheritances due to sudden deaths. We find that the sensitivity of mistakes to stakes is negligible in terms of economic magnitude, even five years after inheriting. For example, our evidence on the home bias in investments indicates that it would require a windfall inheritance of 87.6 million DKK (11.8 million euros) to eliminate such bias from the average individuals’ portfolio. Tests using premature deaths of adult siblings before parental bereavement, which lead to exogenous differences in bequest sizes, confirm these findings. Overall, the propensity to make financial mistakes is a personal trait, rather than a result of small stakes.

16502219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502219.value: Ride-sharing platforms make city travel easier for passengers in regions with few taxis and buses, by mobilizing car owners as part-time drivers. With user-friendly mobile applications, efficient assignment algorithms, and IT-enabled dynamic pricing improving demand-supply matching, these ride sharing platforms are increasingly popular around the world. To extend their market share and fulfill their “greener” promise, several major ride sharing platforms now offer a carpool (or shared) service at a discounted rate. By paying a reduced fee for the carpool service, a rider may be paired with another ride whose traveling route is similar. When riders choose the carpool service and end up riding alone, they still pay at the discounted rate. This reduced rate may make drivers less receptive of the carpool service. While the regular service matches riders with drivers, the carpool service includes matching riders with other riders. To improve the matching efficiency, the platform needs to manage the information flow wisely, especially when both carpool and regular services are offered. A question to address is whether to inform drivers about the exact type of services along with pickup information that a rider requires. In the case where a drivers know the requested service type, they may decide whether to accept requests based on types whenever allowed. To eliminate discrimination, an alternative is not to inform drivers about the requested service types. It is analogous to the case where drivers are assigned to requests and cannot refuse any request. Specifically, we call the first case assignment by the transparent policy and the second case by the opaque policy. This research aims to characterize the optimal pricing strategies for ride-sharing under the opaque and transparent information policies. Solving these equilibrium strategies is non-trivial because the problem involves game theory, queueing networks, and nonlinear optimization. We will then compare policies, with particular emphasis on payoffs, revenues, drivers' satisfaction, and system efficiencies. We shall also use the analytical model to address the issue of driver satisfaction. We expect to show that blindly assigning the jobs/ orders to drivers without such considerations may be operationally simple, but it erodes drains drivers' good intentions and may make it difficult to recruit and retain drivers in a sustainable manner. These results collectively provide a holistic view of the business and social impacts of the carpool service. 共乘系統在城市規劃已經被證明可以有效地解決車輛不足與駕駛短缺的問題，然而在近期共乘產業面臨著另一個更大的挑戰: 因應給予乘客選擇單乘或共載的方案，反而使得駕駛出現不願意搭載有特定共乘需求的乘客。本研究使用賽局分析，從共乘平台的角度出發，探討是否該給予駕駛乘客共乘需求的完全訊息。我們比較兩種機制設計: 透明資訊以及模糊資訊，用排隊理論來分析這兩種平台策略下的系統動態，並且用最佳化理論決定最適定價跟車輛管理。研究主題與管理意涵側重以下幾個層面: 駕駛誘因，平台收益，以及系統效率。

16502219.label: Realisation of objectives
16502219.value: Along the development of the project, we feel that the key ingredients of the proposal can be used to study various kinds of two-sided markets and platform economy. Thus, below we describe our efforts in these dimensions. All the reported activities are published and the RGC funding is acknowledged in the published papers. # He et al., IJPE 2021, On-demand service delivery under asymmetric information This activity addresses part of Objectives 2 and 3. The two-sided feature of the proposed project is key to understanding various situations in reality. In particular, we apply this idea to study the role of on-demand service delivery. This paper develops incentive contracts with substitution or nonsubstitution strategies, consisting of steady-state scheduling rules, probabilistic routing policies, binary admission controls and pricing strategies, to maximize platforms’ revenue. Furthermore, we analyze the influence of information structures on the design of the incentive contract. Section 6 provides numerical experiments based on reasonable estimates of real parameter regions. # Chen et al., Production Oper Manag 2023, Smart navigation via strategic communications in a mixed autonomous paradigm This activity addresses part of Objectives 1, 2, and 3. The focus is on the optimal information design to navigate human workers (HWs) who cooperate with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) within an intralogistics system. We incorporate asymmetric information between AMRs and HWs in a routing game where connected AMRs are informed of the congestion state while HWs rely on information provided by the system. We use simulated numerical examples to complement the analytical results, and describe in the appendix how automated systems and smart contracts can help in this context. # Chen, Production Oper Manag 2021, Optimal design of revenue‐maximizing position auctions with consumer search This activity addresses part of Objective 2. The two-sided feature of the proposed project is key to understanding various situations in reality. We examine the impact of consumer search from the perspective of revenue-maximizing optimal auction design. We use consumer search as a structured way to describe the matching process on one side, and the auction mechanism is used to select the players on the other side. In this two-sided market, service providers are endowed with privately known qualities, and consumers incur heterogeneous search costs. Our general approach eliminates ad hoc restrictions and therefore allows us to uncover the salient economic trade-offs. We adopt the optimal mechanism design approach to examine this two-sided private information problem. The optimal mechanism design approach gives rise to the truly revenue-maximizing scheme, and yields managerial implications that are substantially different from the literature. # Guo et al., Omega 2022, Dynamic Pricing of New Experience Products with Dual-channel Social Learning and Online Review Manipulations This activity addresses part of Objectives 1 and 2. Here we focus on how information is offered through online reviews: first-party reviews are reviews published (by consumers) on a firm’s own platform, and third-party reviews are ratings and feedback generated on a third-party website (e.g., a social media profile). We consider a two-period monopoly dynamic pricing problem with dual-channel social learning (SL) and truncated review manipulations (i.e., a firm may delete extremely low and high ratings). Thus, it investigates the optimal pricing strategies under the opaque and transparent information policies (with and without reviews), and compares information provision policies. We understand that there are large expenses for staffing which deviated from the approved budget. Specifically, most expenses go to research staff and less expenses are used for general expenses. When submitting our original proposal, we planned to attend international conferences and do some research visits to exchange ideas with scholars in this field. However, the pandemic hit us badly and the university explicitly banned all non-urgent travel plans for our safety concerns. Thus, we could only use the grant to train research students and research assistants, and we hope such alternative arrangements best utilize the grant money the RGC kindly gave us.

16502219.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502219.value: Our project results in a number of published papers. Along the development of the project, we feel that the key ingredients of the proposal can be used to study various kinds of two-sided markets and platform economy. All the reported activities are published and the RGC funding is acknowledged in the published papers. In #1 of Part C (Fan and Chen, NRL 2021), we apply this idea to study the role of intermediary (platform) in the context of supply chain management. We examine the possibility of collusion between two procurement service providers (PSPs) and investigate effective contracts to collapse tacit collusion. Pricing, information provision, incentive alignments, and payoffs of different stakeholders are all incorporated in this framework. In #2 of Part C (He et al., IJPE 2021), we apply this idea to study the role of on-demand service delivery. This paper develops incentive contracts with substitution or nonsubstitution strategies, consisting of steady-state scheduling rules, probabilistic routing policies, binary admission controls and pricing strategies, to maximize platforms’ revenue. Furthermore, we analyze the influence of information structures on the design of the incentive contract. Section 6 provides numerical experiments based on reasonable estimates of real parameter regions. In #3 of Part C (Chen et al., Production Oper Manag 2023), the focus is on the optimal information design to navigate human workers (HWs) who cooperate with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) within an intralogistics system. We incorporate asymmetric information between AMRs and HWs in a routing game where connected AMRs are informed of the congestion state while HWs rely on information provided by the system. In #4 of Part C (Chen, Production Oper Manag 2021), we examine the impact of consumer search from the perspective of revenue-maximizing optimal auction design. We use consumer search as a structured way to describe the matching process on one side, and the auction mechanism is used to select the players on the other side. In this two-sided market, service providers are endowed with privately known qualities, and consumers incur heterogeneous search costs. Our general approach eliminates ad hoc restrictions and therefore allows us to uncover the salient economic trade-offs. In #5 of Part C (Guo et al., Omega 2022), we focus on how information is offered through online reviews: first-party reviews are reviews published (by consumers) on a firm’s own platform, and third-party reviews are ratings and feedback generated on a third-party website (e.g., a social media profile). We shall clarify that for #1 of Part C (Fan and Chen, NRL 2021), the first submission is very different from the ultimately accepted one. Because during the revision process we adopted many ideas from the project to change the model, the motivation, and discussions of some economic forces. In particular, the revision that took place during year 2020 incorporates pricing, information provision, incentive alignments, and payoffs that we discussed in the proposal. The revision was completed on July 19, 2020, more than six months after the project started.

16502219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16502219.value: Our study has limitations as our analysis is based on many assumptions that maintain tractability. It would be an interesting research direction to further explore the economic benefit for a warehouse facility or a platform to strategically share information with the third-party fleet and contracted drivers. Future research is needed to study the interaction between warehouse automation and information provision in a general network setting. We could also examine more refined routing advices and information strategies on human and autonomous drivers if such mix of services are offered in the future.

16502219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16502219.value: Ride sharing platforms, e.g., Uber, Didi in China and Grab in Southeast Asia, make city travel easier for passengers in regions with low capacity of taxi, by mobilizing car owners as part-time drivers. These ride sharing platforms receive trip information from riders, dispatch relevant information to drivers, and use modern algorithmic calculations to improve the demand-supply matching efficiency. We study various kinds of pricing strategies under the opaque and transparent information policies, and compare information provision policies, with particular emphasis on payoffs, revenues, driver satisfaction, and system efficiencies. We also use real data to calibrate the regions of interest and validate the theoretical predictions through numerical experiments. Going beyond this context, our approach, that combines game theory, queueing networks, and nonlinear optimization, can be adapted to devise policy recommendations for service operations, the leading sector of Hong Kong’s contemporary business. The adoption of sharing economy can substantially boost market efficiency; however, at the same time they can also create societal tension when benefit allocations are deemed unfair. Viewed in this way, the two-sided market design problem appears in numerous scenarios with practical relevance in Hong Kong, and our research provides a concrete framework to study this.

16502819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16502819.value: We propose to study a key issue for both tourism and the transport system of Hong Kong. The two theme parks in Hong Kong attract hundreds of thousands of tourists each year from around the world. The price of a 1-day ticket at both parks remains constant throughout the year, regardless of peak/off seasons (uniform pricing). By contrast, Disney parks in the US have adopted a seasonal pricing scheme, charging a higher price on peak days and a lower price during non-peak periods (dynamic pricing). The controversy over uniform pricing and dynamic pricing has drawn attention from firms, customers, regulators and the media. In a recent case, a British man took his daughter to Florida during school term time, when the theme parks are less congested and cheaper, and faced a £120 fine for his daughter’s unauthorized absence from school. He refused to pay and the case was eventually taken to the Supreme Court. The case has excited great interest among parents in England and arguably dynamic pricing of theme parks lies at the heart of this controversy. Like many big cities, Hong Kong suffers from traffic congestion. Long queues of slow moving traffic not only degrade the environment, but also damage the productivity and reputation of the city. Congestion pricing has been implemented in some cities to mitigate the problem: for example, London charges drivers £11.50 daily for entering designated zones. Intuitively, such a policy discourages those drivers who place a low value on the use of the road, thus reserving resources for the ones who value the use of the road highly. Neither the benefits to residence nor the increase in efficiency is unclear, and a socially optimal implementation has yet to be determined. In both topics, the allocation of limited resources negatively affects user experience. Can park visitors and travelers be made happier and society more efficient by pricing? In the proposed project, we seek to develop a theoretical framework which will allow us to understand the pricing pattern of the firm/government and the reaction of customers/travelers to the prices. Dynamic congestion pricing penalizes travelers at peak times and benefits them in off-peak times. It smooths demand over time so travelers incur less disutility during congestion, at the cost of a fraction of travelers giving up their travel plans. Our preliminary results imply that dynamic congestion pricing may benefit travelers and society as a whole. 香港的交通系統和旅遊行業是社會中非常重要的部分。迪士尼公園和海洋公園每年能夠吸引幾十萬的遊客。公園的門票在一年中是不變的（固定定價）。作為對比，美國的迪士尼公園會在旺季提高門票的價格（動態定價）。這種不同的定價策略在公司，顧客，和政府決策者之間引起了不小的爭論。在一個最近的案例中，一位英國家長和女兒為了避免在旺季去美國迪士尼公園而逃課被學校體罰。他們決定把起訴女兒的學校起訴到最高法院。這件事可以說歸根到底是由動態定價引起的。 像很多大城市一樣，香港的交通擁堵也是一個不可避免的社會議題。交通擁堵不僅會引起環境污染，也會讓社會的生產力下降。不少城市，比如倫敦，新加坡和曼哈頓，採用擁堵定價來控制交通。比如說倫敦對進入特定區域的車輛徵收11.5英鎊。擁堵定價可以讓對出行需求不高的人群在非高峰時間出行，從而避免擁堵。但是擁堵定價是否會損傷一部分居民的利益是一個值得思考的問題。 以上的兩個問題有很多共同之處。總共的資源都是有限的，並且無法隨著時間靈活的調節。在這種情況下，定價可以作為一種工具讓社會變得更有效率嗎？在這個研究中，我們希望提供一種分析的反尬分和思路來研究定價是否可以讓社會福利更高，並且提高生產力。我們希望從顧客入手，理解他們是怎麼應對動態定價和擁堵定價的，從而再研究政府或者是公司的定價策略。顯而易見，動態定價會讓一部分顧客選擇在非高峰出行，從而讓客流更加平滑，但是同時又會逼迫一部分出行者在不方便的時候出行。這些利弊是我們研究的重點。 通過這個研究，我們希望提供全新的視角來研究定價是否會對社會的效率產生正面的影響。如果答案是肯定的，那麼媒體和大眾需要改變他們的想法。動態定價應該在社會中更多的被使用。如果答案是否定的，那麼顧客對動態定價的厭惡是有根據的。公司也需要在公關和營收之間找一個平衡點。

16502819.label: Major findings and research outcome
16502819.value: Capacity providers such as airlines often sell the same capacity to different market segments at different prices to improve their expected revenues. The absence of a secondary market, due to the nontransferability of airline tickets, gives rise to an opportunity for airlines to broker capacity between consumers with different willingness to pay. One way to broker capacity is by the introduction of callable products. The idea is similar to callable bonds where the issuer has the right, but not the obligation, to buy back the bonds at a certain price by a certain date. The idea of callable products was introduced before under the assumption that the fare-class demands are all independent. The independent assumption becomes untenable when there is significant demand recovery (respectively, demand cannibalization) when lower fares are closed (respectively, opened). In this case, consumer choice behavior should be modeled explicitly to make meaningful decisions. In this paper, we consider a general consumer choice model and develop the optimal strategy for callable products. Our numerical study illustrates how callable products are win-win-win, for the capacity provider and for both high and low fare consumers. Our studies also identify conditions for callable products to result in significant improvements in expected revenues. To further extend the findings we consider an extension of the model to allow for model where time is implicit as this is favored by airlines, which handles time implicitly imposing fewer restrictions on the nature of randomness compared to the Poisson arrival process favored in academia. In the implicit time model, capacity providers set booking limits to protect capacity for future high-fare demand. Our numerical study identifies conditions where callable products result in significant gains in profits. We consider the problem of a firm seeking to use personalized pricing to sell an exogenously given stock of a product over a finite selling horizon to different consumer types. We assume that the type of an arriving consumer can be observed, but the demand function associated with each type is initially unknown. The firm sets personalized prices dynamically for each type and attempts to maximize the revenue over the season. We provide a learning algorithm that is near optimal when the demand and capacity scale in proportion. The algorithm utilizes the primal–dual formulation of the problem and learns the dual optimal solution explicitly. It allows the algorithm to overcome the curse of dimensionality (the rate of regret is independent of the number of types) and sheds light on novel algorithmic designs for learning problems with resource constraints.

16503219.label: Project Objectives
16503219.value: We will examine the local environmental (air and water) impact of Chinese SEZs, a prominent place-based policy. We will also examine whether the gross domestic product (GDP) growth rates in these counties, compared to those in control counties, display a similar pattern to emissions after the policy change. In so doing, we will empirically identify whether there is an environment and development tradeoff in the context of Chinese SEZs. We will further pin down the mechanism through which SEZs affect the local environment. We will decompose the overall effect into scale, technique and composition. We will also seek to show how the effects of SEZ programs vary with measures of local officials’ political incentives. We will investigate the quantitative importance of political institutions in terms of the heterogeneity of local officials’ strategies for SEZ development and resulting differences in environmental and economic growth patterns.

16503219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503219.value: The proposed project will compile and analyze data to examine the environmental consequences of China’s special economic zone (SEZ) program, one of the prominent place-based industrial policies in China. By implementing special policies in specific areas within jurisdictions, the zones aim to foster economic growth by building clusters, increasing employment and attracting technologically advanced industrial facilities. Given its decentralized implementation, the SEZ policy is deeply intertwined with local government officials. We will use a quasi-experimental design based on the gradual establishment of SEZs in various Chinese counties from 2000, incorporating the environment and political economy to shed light on the magnitudes and mechanisms of the tradeoffs between economic growth and environmental quality—still an unresolved topic for economists and policymakers. Specifically, we are interested in the following issues: is there any environmental deterioration with increased industrial activity after SEZs were established in some Chinese counties? What is the political economy of the environment in the case of Chinese SEZs? Do political institutions shape environmental outcomes by affecting officials’ strategies for developing SEZs in their jurisdictions? To address these questions, we propose to construct a novel dataset by compiling rich firm, environmental, administrative and personnel data. Methodologically, we adopt a compelling identification strategy to overcome common challenges in the evaluation of place-based policies. This project will make a unique contribution to the place-based policy literature, which so far has largely focused on evaluating the effects of spatially targeted investments on neighborhood economies in the developed world, such as the United States and the European Union; rarely are the environmental consequences of such programs considered. Environmental damage as a by-product of economic activity is a more severe challenge for the developing world, and the study of Chinese SEZs will greatly facilitate our understanding of how this type of development initiative affects the environment in a large developing country context. Given this more relevant institutional and contextual setting, the Chinese findings, particularly those related to policy implementation, could provide important policy insights for other less-developed countries. 本文中提议的项目将整合和分析详细数据来研究中国非常重要的一项区域性产业政策——经济开发区的环境影响。这些园区在特定地理区域内实行特殊的经济政策，期望形成产业集群，增加就业以及吸引高科技工业企业的经济发展目的。由于其实施过程高度分权化的特征，开发区政策与地方政府官员密切连接在一起。 在这个项目中，我们将利用自2000年以来在中国各县域逐渐成立开发区的准自然实验，综合考虑环境和政治经济学的因素，来研究理解开发区政策背景下地方政府在经济增长与环境之间的权衡——尽管这个问题很重要，经济学家以及政策制定者对此仍着墨甚少。具体而言，我们想研究以下问题：在有一些县成立开发区后，工业活动增加是否带来环境的恶化？在开发区背景下，地方政府面对环境问题时的政治经济学考量是什么？中国政治方面的选拔制度是否影响了官员们对所辖区域内开发区的发展策略，进而影响环境？ 为了回答以上这些问题，我们提议整合一系列丰富的企业、环境、行政以及官员的数据资源，从而建立一个新的数据库。方法上，我们将采用非常严谨的计量识别方法，以克服在区域性经济政策分析上会遇到的挑战。 本项目将对区域性经济政策的文献作出新的贡献。目前为止，已有文献大部分关注衡量在发达国家中 （例如美国和欧盟） 此类区域性投资对地方经济的影响；很少有文章考虑这类项目对环境产生的后果。在发展中国家，环境损害是经济活动带来的一个副产品和发展过程中非常严重的挑战。对中国开发区的相关研究将大大有助我们理解此类发展政策在全世界最大的发展中国家对环境造成的影响。中国的经验证据（尤其是与政策实施过程相关的那些发现），因为更相似可比的制度背景，将对其他发展中国家提供非常重要的政策借鉴意义。

16503419.label: Project Title(Chinese)
16503419.value: 检验高频数据中的“黑洞”与波动率预测

16503419.label: Project Objectives
16503419.value: Develop a general test for the "black holes" (BH) in the price process. Develop a new volatility forecasting methodology, which incorporates the BH test in objective 1, to facilitate better volatility forecasting.
rows: Develop a general test for the "black holes" (BH) in the price process.
Develop a new volatility forecasting methodology, which incorporates the BH test in objective 1, to facilitate better volatility forecasting.

16503419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503419.value: In this project, we aim to develop a test for "black holes" (BHs), by which we mean violations of semimartingale property in the efficient price process that are generally overlooked in jump-diffusion processes. Potential violations include, but not limited to, gradual jumps, drift bursts, and volatility bursts. Moreover, this project will pay special attention to forecasting realized volatility (RV), which is always an important part of empirical finance. In particular, we plan to develop a new volatility forecasting methodology, which incorporates our newly designed BH test, to facilitate better volatility forecasting. Finally, other than the modeling side, this project also intends to explore feasible estimation methods to deal with heteroscedasticity to further improve RV forecasting performance. 在這個項目中，我們計劃檢測高頻數據中的“黑洞”，意即在有效價格的帶跳擴撒過程中常被忽略的非半秧性質。違反半秧性質的原因包括漸變的跳，爆炸的漂移項等。另外，這個項目會特別的考慮波動率的預測這一重要問題。我們計劃給出新的波動率預測的方法，其中包含我們對“黑洞”的理解和檢測。我們也計劃進一步探索可行的更精準的波動率估計的方法，用以更好的預測波動率。

16503419.label: Realisation of objectives
16503419.value: The project objectives are 100% achieved. For objective 1, we proposed a test for pockets of extreme return persistence which are "black holes" (BH) in the price process. The test is presented in the paper "Volatility measurement with pockets of extreme return persistence" by the PI and her co-authors. For objective 2, we study different aspects of volatility forecasting, which uses data that removes BHs as described in objective 1. This step of removal of BH, either used alone, or combined with factor models, leads to improved volatility forecasts, which are demonstrated in the research papers reported: "Volatility measurement with pockets of extreme return persistence”, “Mining the factor zoo: Estimation of latent factor models with sufficient proxies”, “Factor Modeling for Volatility” and “Stock co-jump networks”.

16503419.label: Major findings and research outcome
16503419.value: We identify episodic emergence of pockets with extreme return persistence in financial markets. This notion refers to intraday periods of non-trivial duration, for which stock returns are highly positively autocorrelated. Such episodes include, but are not limited to, gradual jumps and prolonged bursts in the drift component. We develop a test for such presence of extreme return persistence and establish its statistical properties. The test is presented in the paper "Volatility measurement with pockets of extreme return persistence”. We explore the benefit of detecting such episodes through volatility forecasting from various angles. Using data that removes such extreme return persistence, we show that either in univariate forecasts based on individual price process alone, or when combined with factor models, one can see statistically and economically significant improvements in volatility forecasts. The results are collected in "Volatility measurement with pockets of extreme return persistence”, “Mining the factor zoo: Estimation of latent factor models with sufficient proxies”, “Factor Modeling for Volatility” and “Stock co-jump networks”.

16503419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16503419.value: We would continue to draw awareness of such "black holes" in the price process. And demonstrate in future research, that differenciating such periods can lead to better understanding of the risks in the financial market.

16503419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503419.value: Prior research about price process usually describes price as a combination of continuous Ito-semimartingale process and a jump process. We show that in the market, there are periods that don’t fit this description, particularly, those periods demonstrating pockets with extreme return persistence. These periods are easily overlooked but can greatly impact volatility estimation and forecasting. We develop tests for such periods, and explore volatility forecasting with such periods identified. We show that differentiating such periods with regular periods leads to statistically and economically improved volatility forecasts.

16503519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503519.value: Over the past decade, global online retailing has been growing at an average rate of 20% a year. In China, online retail sales exceeded $300 billion in 2016 and is expected to exceed $600 billion by 2021 (Economist, 2017). For online retailers, there are two commonly adopted selling formats. Under the agency selling format, an online retailer operates an agency channel (also called marketplace) that allows manufacturers to use its website to sell directly to consumers and charges them a fixed commission fee. Under the reselling format, an online retailer operates a reselling channel to buy from manufacturers and resell to consumers. Some online retailers (e.g., Amazon and JD) offers both channels in their retail platforms whereas others offers only either an agency channel (e.g. Alibaba) or a reselling channel (e.g., Zappos). For an online retailer who offers both channels (e.g., JD), some manufacturers sell through only one of the channels whereas others sell through both channels. Many big online retailers have the capabilities of collecting massive data from their retail platforms and converting it into insightful information about future demand. Some of them (e.g. Alibaba and JD) have started to share demand information with manufacturers. In the existing marketing and supply chain management, much work has been done on channel structure and information sharing. However, there is no comprehensive theory to explain when a manufacturer will sell through both the agency and reselling channels of an online retailer and the incentive for such a retailer to share information with the manufacturer. We hope to fill the gap in the literature by developing analytical models to study channel structure, information sharing and the interaction of these two decisions in online retailing. Our investigation will enrich the theory of supply chain management and provide insights to managers for improving practices related to information sharing and channel structure in online retailing. 在過去十年中，全球在線零售業以平均每年20％的速度增長。在中國，2016年在線零售額超過3000億美元，預計到2021年將超過6000億美元（經濟學人，2017）。 對於在線零售商，有兩種常用的銷售形式。根據代理銷售形式，在線零售商運營代理渠道（也稱為在線市場），允許製造商使用其網站直接向消費者銷售並向他們收取固定的佣金。根據轉售格式，在線零售商運營轉售渠道，從製造商處購買並轉售給消費者。一些在線零售商（例如，亞馬遜和京東）在其零售平台中提供兩個渠道，而其他零售商僅提供代理渠道（例如阿里巴巴）或轉售渠道（例如，Zappos）。對於提供兩種渠道（例如，京東）的在線零售商，一些製造商僅通過其中一個渠道銷售，而其他製造商通過兩個渠道銷售。許多大型在線零售商都有能力從零售平台收集大量數據，並將其轉化為有關未來需求的深入信息。其中一些（例如阿里巴巴和京東）已經開始與製造商分享需求信息。 在現有的營銷和供應鏈管理中，在渠道結構和信息共享方面做了大量工作。然而，沒有全面的理論來解釋製造商何時通過在線零售商的代理商和轉售渠道進行銷售以及這種零售商與製造商共享信息的動機。我們希望通過開發分析模型來研究渠道結構，信息共享以及在線零售中這兩個決策的相互作用，填補文獻的空白。 我們的研究將豐富供應鏈管理理論，並為管理者提供改進網絡零售信息共享和渠道結構相關實踐的見解。

16503519.label: Major findings and research outcome
16503519.value: For the first research objective, we have the following findings. We derive conditions on the problem parameters under which each of the three channel structures (agency channel, reselling channel, and dual channel) emerges in equilibrium. We show that the wholesale price in the reselling channel is reduced because of the addition of the agency channel even when both channels are equally efficient, which extends the wholesale price effect because of the addition of a less efficient direct channel in the supplier encroachment literature. Our analysis highlights the flexibility of a dual channel for firms to shift sales between the two channels, which could increase the retail platform’s incentive to exert service effort. For the second research objective, we have the following findings. Compared with the case of no information sharing, information sharing enlarges both the parametric region in which the manufacturer encroaches by adding a direct agency channel and the region in which encroachment benefits the platform. Our results show that encroachment and information sharing are complementary. When the manufacturer encroaches, it creates more incentive for the platform to share information because encroachment not only mitigates the double marginalization effect of information sharing but also increases the benefit of information sharing to the platform. When the platform shares information, it creates more incentive for the manufacturer to encroach because information sharing allows the encroaching manufacturer to adjust not only the wholesale price but also the agency channel’s retail price to respond to demand uncertainty. For the third research objective, we have the following findings. When the manufacturer does not encroach, the platform does not share information because of the negative double marginalization effect in the existing reselling channel. When the manufacturer encroaches, information sharing has an additional effect of allowing the manufacturer to adjust the agency channel’s retail price to respond to demand uncertainty, which benefits the platform. When the commission rate is low, the negative double marginalization effect is strong and dominates the positive responsive agency pricing effect because the platform has a small share of the agency channel’s revenue. When the commission rate is high, even though the negative double marginalization effect is weak, it still dominates the positive responsive agency pricing effect because of the low sales in the agency channel. Therefore, the platform has an incentive to share information only when the commission rate has an intermediate value.

16503519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16503519.value: For the models developed in this project, we consider either service effort or information sharing as a key driver for determining the channel structure of an online platform. In the future, we can consider an extension that addresses how service effort and information sharing jointly determine the channel structure of an online platform.

16503519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16503519.value: Many online retail platforms utilize multiple online channels to sell products and provide customer service to their customers. With the massive amount of consumer and demand data in hand, these platforms have started to share data with some manufacturers. Channel structure, service effort and information sharing are critical elements of the business model of online retailing. Our findings offer useful insights into how channel structure, service effort and information sharing decisions are made through the interaction between a manufacturer and a platform. Based on these findings, managers in online retailing can make better decisions to improve the performance of not only their own companies but also the supply chain.

16503619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16503619.value: Advertising analytics has received growing attention in the last decade. However, one key question related to advertising viewership remains unclear: how does a TV program’s content effect the viewership of advertisements aired immediately after a program? In this research project, we will answer this question in the context of TV shows and post-show advertising. Two key challenges to answer this research question are that first, advertising viewership is often endogenous to the content of a program; second, content is in the form of unstructured data, such as video, and hence is difficult to measure. To rigorously identify the effect of show content on post-show advertising viewership, we will leverage a unique exogenous nature of show content and advertising-slot bidding in our dataset. Furthermore, we will use state-of-the-art techniques in analyzing video data to quantify show content including image frame, audio, and text script. By doing this, we will be able to examine which specific content dimension is correlated with advertising viewership. Finally, we will analyze the value of program content in terms of advertising dollars—a critical managerial question to advertisers and TV networks. 廣告數據分析近年來愈來愈受到業界重視。節目內容如何影響廣告收視率？本研究將試圖回答這個重要的研究問題。我們將研究電視節目與節目後廣告。這項研究的難點在於廣告收視率往往是內生於節目內容。本研究將利用節目內容與廣告投標的外生性解決這個難題。同時，我們還將使用最新的視頻數據分析技術分析畫面圖禎，音頻，文本。最後，我們將量化節目內容的經濟價值。
