16601319.label: Major findings and research outcome
16601319.value: We recruited a total of 242 children between the ages of 4 and 7. Of our participants, 115 children were local Hong Kong Chinese, 84 were of Asian (i.e. South or Southeast Asian) ethnicity, and 43 were White or Biracial. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions, in which they were either shown a character depicting their ethnic ingroup as wealthy (higher status) and a character depicting their ethnic outgroup member as poor (lower status), or vice versa. Children were shown a series of tasks to examine their recall of resource ownership, inference of wealth status, socializing preferences, and explicit judgments regarding the two characters. Taken together, we find that pre-primary school children are (1) already aware of differences in ethnic groups and social status (wealth status); (2) prefer their ethnic ingroup members when they are members of the ethnic majority (i.e. Hong Kong Chinese children) but not when they are members of an ethnic minority (e.g., Hong Kong Asian and White children); (3) attend to the status of their ethnicity relative to the comparison ethnic groups as well as the status of the specific individuals presented in the study; and (4) found that family background played some (though not necessarily a sizable) role in children's decision-making. Hong Kong Chinese children made more correct inferences of wealth when the ethnic ingroup character was depicted as wealthy as opposed to poor. Hong Kong ethnic minority Asian children, on the other hand, made more correct inferences on average when the ethnic outgroup character was depicted as wealthier. White and White-biracial children’s wealth inferences were not significantly impacted by whether the ingroup or outgroup characters were wealthy or poor. Chinese children had a robust preference to socialize with the ethnic ingroup member, Asian children showed a preference to socialize with ethnic outgroup members, and White/White-biracial children did not demonstrate an observable preference between the two. The depicted wealth status of their ingroup mattered, where high wealth status of their ingroup strengthened their ingroup preference, especially for Chinese and Asian children. Our findings suggest that children’s socializing preferences and perceptions of the wealth status depend on both the immediate context (i.e., were individuals shown to be wealthy or poor?) and the status of one’s own ingroup (i.e., are children from ethnic minority or majority groups within their own society?).

16601319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16601319.value: Our present study offers initial insights into children’s sensitivity to social group information for the first time in an East Asian context. More work will be needed to understand the extent to which children consider this information and how these considerations can shape their preferences and behaviors, especially in a diverse society such as Hong Kong. If possible, further investigation should be conducted with the ethnic minority groups in Hong Kong, understanding how children's specific backgrounds can influence their thought processes.

16601319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16601319.value: In the present study, 242 Hong Kong 4- to 7-year-old children (115 Chinese, 84 South/Southeast Asian, and 43 White/biracial-White) were asked to evaluate their ethnic ingroup and outgroup members, who were shown to vary in wealth. Overall, children were sensitive to resource ownership and used ethnicity and wealth information when choosing between unfamiliar individuals with which to socialize. Chinese children made more correct inferences of wealth when the ethnic ingroup character was depicted as wealthy as opposed to poor. Asian children, on the other hand, made more correct inferences on average when the ethnic outgroup character was depicted as wealthier. White and biracial-White children’s wealth inferences were not significantly impacted by whether the ingroup or outgroup characters were wealthy or poor. In addition, Chinese children had a robust preference to socialize with the ethnic ingroup member, Asian children showed a preference to socialize with ethnic outgroup members, and White/White-biracial children did not demonstrate an observable preference between the two. Our findings suggest that children’s socializing preferences and perceptions of the wealth status depend on both the immediate context and the status of one’s own ingroup, and are shaped by their family, schools, and broader community.

16602119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602119.value: The proposed research aims to understand the attitudinal and behavioral effects of communicating the cultural impacts of climate change to the public. With the environmental changes (e.g., extreme weather events, sea level rise) it brings, climate change threatens the sustainability of both tangible aspects (e.g., heritage sites) and intangible aspects (e.g., practices) of culture. However, little research has focused on how people respond when this threat is brought into their attention. Thus, we propose to conduct three experiments to address the following questions: (1) Does communicating the impacts of climate change on cultural sustainability raise people’s concern about climate change and motivate them to engage in its mitigation? (2) Does communicating the cultural impacts in the local region vs. foreign regions have different effects? (3) Do these communication effects depend on the audience’s psychological orientations? The cultural impacts of climate change should make the issue more relevant and meaningful to the public, so we expect a message that frames climate change as a cultural sustainability issue, particularly when it refers to the local context rather than the global context, will be more effective than a message that frames climate change as an environmental issue in increasing the audience’s concern about climate change, their intention to carry out mitigation actions, and their actual contribution to mitigation efforts. Also, considering that a communication message is usually more persuasive when its contents are congruent with the recipients’ psychological orientations, we expect the effectiveness of the local and global frames to vary across individuals. The effectiveness of the local frame relative to the global frame should be less pronounced for those with a stronger cosmopolitan orientation (i.e., those who are open to other cultures, endorse universal human rights, and respect the diversity of cultures). This proposed research will contribute to the study of climate change communication by identifying a potentially effective but little understood message frame—that of cultural sustainability—and specifying the audience for which this frame is most effective. This research will also fill the gap in the study of public perceptions of climate change by demonstrating people’s attitudinal and behavioral responses to the cultural dimension of climate change. As Hong Kong is vulnerable to the threat of climate change, the proposed research may provide information for local communicators and the HKSAR government on what they can do to engage the public in addressing climate change. 本研究旨在了解通報氣候變化對人類文化的影響能否有效改變大眾的態度及行為。氣候變化帶來環境變遷，威脅人類文化中有形及無形的各方面。然而，過去的研究甚少關注大眾面對此類威脅的反應。是以本研究將會通過實驗以解答以下的提問：（1）通報氣候變化對文化永續的影響，能否提升大眾對氣候變化的關注，以及推動大眾改變生活模式以助緩和氣候變化？（2）通報氣候變化對本地文化以及外地文化的影響，會否有不同效果？（3）以上提及的效果，是否取決於受眾的心理傾向？本研究將有助識別氣候變化信息傳播的有效策略，並補足過去研究的不足。本研究亦有望為香港特區政府及環團提供相關資訊以作參考。

16602119.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602119.value: We conducted two survey studies and two experiments. In two survey studies, we observed a generally high level of awareness of the cultural impacts of climate change among our participants. Most importantly, such perception robustly predicted intentions to engage in climate change mitigation behavior and climate activism, as well as support for climate policy. We also found expected associations between such perception and some psychological and demographic variables (e.g., cosmopolitan orientation, moral inclusion, political orientation). In Experiment 1, we manipulated the climate change message by either focusing on the cultural sustainability implications of climate change (experimental condition) and the conventional environmental frame of climate change (control condition). The manipulation was effective; higher perceived threat to culture (but not other aspects) was reported by participants in the experimental condition. However, no effect was observed on all dependent variables (including evaluation of the message, concern about cliamte change, and climate action). We reckoned the possibility that the effect of message framing would be observable only among climate change non-believers. We therefore focused on such non-believer participants in the sample and found that indeed, the effect was significant in some of the dependent varaibles. That said, this effect was not reliable, as the sample size had been reduced to 24 persons only (to begin with, there were very few non-believers in the sample). In Experiment 2, we replicated Experimet 1, but we recruited only individuals who did not believe in the happening of climate change. We additionally measured cosmopolitan orientation, our hypothesized moderators. We failed to find any significant differnece between the two conditions in all of our dependent variables. We also did not observe any significant interaction between condition and cosmopolitan orientation.

16602119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602119.value: We will continue this line of research. We are considering other potential moderators of the effect of our cultural sustainability frame. A new experiment is under preparation.

16602119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602119.value: The impacts of climate change on human cultures have received increasing attention in recent years. In two survey studies, we observed a generally high level of awareness of such impacts among our participants. Also, such perception robustly predicted intentions to engage in climate change mitigation behavior and climate activism, as well as support for climate policy. These findings not only add a cultural dimension to the research on public understanding of climate change but also reveal a viable application of cultural frames as an effective climate communication strategy. However, such viability cannot be confirmed in the two experiments we have conducted thus far. We will continue this line of research by considering the potential boundaries of the effect of cultural frames.

16602319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602319.value: 本项目将大湾区（GBA）（原大珠江三角洲）的空气质量治理作为集体行动问题进行研究。现有的中国空气污染研究通常强调中央政府和省级政府的作用，而由于大湾区各地级市和特别行政区在解释和实施上级政府颁布的指令方面具有高度自治权，项目将城市作为主要参与者开展调查。 城市层面的自治允许各市级政府采取不同的治理方案，而自治会对周边城市的治理行为产生不同的影响。部分城市可能存在对环保法律执行不力的情况，这种搭便车的行为会阻碍区域的集体努力。而另一方面，当部分城市的行动强硬时，会形成领导作用，刺激邻近城市的投入更大的努力。本项目关注方法论的原因是，GBA可能被视为中国特大城市群参与集体行动的“最复杂的案例”，其中五个城市（香港，深圳，澳门，珠海和广州）具有异常高的自治水平，这在理论上对解决共同资源问题构成了障碍。这些城市实际上在争夺各种资源方面都有过一段历史。然而，GBA在控制空气污染方面取得了最大的成功，这些城市在环境方面也展现了领先地位。理解GBA集体治理的方式的将给其他地区提供分析，实证，以及面向政策的结合。 因此，我们建议通过下列任务来研究该区域集体行动的演变情况: 1) 编制各城市落实的空气污染工具政策清单(包括资源投入等); 2) 确定政策的监测和执行水平; 3) 测算减排，并与政策力度进行比较; 4) 揭示GBA在应对污染过程中形成的纵向和横向结构，以及合作和竞争机制。 该项目的创新点包括调查国家层面、省级层面和市级层面空气污染治理的动态过程，引入集体行动作为GBA区域空气污染治理的理论基础，确认最大限度减少搭便车和激励领导者的政策。这些研究成果将有助于改善需要集体行动的GBA和其他具有高度自治权地区的区域空气质量。

16602319.label: Realisation of objectives
16602319.value: The first objective to empirically determine the extent of city participation in GBA collective air pollution management has been achieved. We created a policy database that is a comprehensive source for all policies related to air pollution in the GBA. This data base enables an analysis of multi-scale interrelations of policy-making between national, provincial and city governments and impact of autonomy, competition and cooperation among the cities on policy-making and implementation. Plus, this database is a comprehensive source for other researchers. The database provides an assured accounting of air pollution policies for the eleven GBA cities. It has been extended by incorporating policy areas that are not directly related to air pollution emissions, but strongly indicate government commitment to dealing with air pollution (new energy vehicles, green buildings and emission trading policies are examples). We focused on nine policy areas: energy, industry (manufacturing), buildings and green buildings, internal combustion vehicles, non-road machinery, shipping, emission trading, and regional cooperation. Policy instruments for each of these source areas have been identified for each city and the salient features of each instrument recorded and coded for analysis purposes. Elaboration of these policies include items such as the policy making process, implementation actions, and monitoring. Matrix comparisons of policy similarities and differences among the cities and across timelines have been made; linkages to provincial and national policies constructed; leaders, followers, and laggard cities identified; and unique approaches noted. Qualitative summaries of each policy areas have also been written up. The second objective to identify the main variables promoting freeriding, competition, and cooperation in the collective governance of air pollution has for the most part being achieved. However, the understanding of the variable affecting the interrelations among the levels of government has been achieved primarily through the use of policy data base and review of secondary materials. Unfortunately, due to the 2019 protests and the extended Covid restrictions the investigators were not able to interview stakeholders to the desired extent. Workarounds were found in zoom calls, email responses and greater reliance on Hong Kong informants. Although the relationships with stakeholder were not developed to the extent thought necessary to delve into more nuanced and complex issues the configuration of coordination and competition in the region on air pollution was revealed. A further workaround was the purchase of industry analysis, specifically for the new energy vehicle industry and this was the cause of the redirection of general research funding. The third objective to design a general analytical framework that can be applied to air quality governance efforts in other mega-city regions has been achieved. Based on the policy inventory and the information received from interviewees and secondary materials we can devise a model of regional multi-level governance. This model incorporated the mechanisms of interrelations of coordination among the levels, how the mechanisms are calibrated among cities of different capacities, and how the coordination mechanisms vary among sectors. Importantly, competition among cities is incorporated into this model, as is the encouragement and response of city competition by provincial and national governance levels.

16602319.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602319.value: Collective action on air pollution in the GBA results from a combination of strong national-provincial coordination and competition among the cities, and much less on direct cooperation among the cities. That is, the national government devises air pollution goals and delegates coordination of implementation to the provinces. The provincial allocation of responsibilities to the cities and mechanisms and calibration of coordination are revealed to be nuanced and redistributive according to city capacities. As importantly the initiatives of leading cities and the responses of cities with lower policymaking and implementation capacities are revealed. Direct cooperation among the cities has been found to be weak. These findings were reflected generally in policy inventory, secondary materials and interviews with policy-makers, industry participants and academics. However, collective action occurs varies among sectors and there are distinct evolutionary pathways among each sector and in response various internal and external influences. These different trajectories are illustrated in two articles. The first on marine air pollution shows how emissions control began with a couple of city-based initiatives, but the value of these policies was quickly realized by provincial and national authorities and implemented more generally in the region and nationally. The second article on the development of the new energy vehicle (NEV) industry shows how transport air pollution control evolved into the promotion of NEVs by the national government and delegation of governance responsibility to the province on issues such as consumers subsidies, charging infrastructure and suppression of internal combustion engines. However, the singular success of the GBA NEV industry owes more to the differentiated competition among the cities on developing assembly and components supply to develop a regional NEV cluster. A subsequent paper will address the general framework of coordination, competition, and cooperation across the region and incorporate a necessity to consider the contingency of distinct evolution of governance systems based internal and external influences. The relevance of the GBA model for other Chinese regions and regions in other countries will be considered.

16602319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602319.value: The study examined the configuration of collective action among Greater Pearl River Delta Cities to reduce regional air pollution. The study found that regional collective action results from a combination of strong national-provincial coordination and competition among the cities, and much less on direct cooperation among the cities. There are two principle forces. First, the national government devises air pollution goals and delegates coordination of implementation to the provinces. The province thereby allocates responsibilities to the cities and mechanisms and calibration of coordination exercising nuanced and redistributive strategies according to city capacities. Second, the initiatives of leading cities and the responses of cities with lower policymaking and implementation capacities are revealed. On the other hand, direct cooperation among the cities has been found to be weak. How collective action evolves, however, depends on the sector and various influences affecting them. In one in-depth study, marine emissions governance was initiated by two leading cities, then propagated regionally and national by higher levels of governance. In another study, the new vehicle industry was promoted top down from the national through provincial to city governments, however, city governments did differentiate NEV development based on opportunities evolving within the regional industrial cluster.

16602619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602619.value: In an economy, policy set by the fiscal authority must be coordinated with policy set by the monetary authority in that the two sorts of policy taken together cannot violate the government consolidated budget constraint. Fiscal and monetary coordination is simple if one authority can dictate to the other (equivalently, both are subordinates to a third party that designs fiscal and monetary policy on its own) or if the two authorities have the same objective. Reality is not that simple, though. For example, the European Central Bank has institutional independence and governments of EU members often complain that ECB policy does not accommodate their needs. And while the Federal Reserve is viewed by many as a paragon of central bank independence, its actual independence may turn out to vary from time to time. When the two authorities have different objectives and one cannot be dictated to by another, by what mechanism may they achieve coordination? As a fundamental step in this project, we treat coordination as a bargaining process between two authorities. We let the objective of the fiscal authority be related to elections. We let the objective of the monetary authority be related to the economic model central bankers have in mind. As the fiscal objective is election-oriented, coordination is an outcome of policy-economy equilibrium. Within this basic framework, we intend to address the following issues. Would the coordination resulting from the bargaining process imply a better allocation than the coordination in the simple case? How is the bargaining process affected by institutional characteristics? Would some characteristics make the bargaining process more efficient? And, is central bank independence really desirable? 在一个经济体中，财政部门制定的政策必须与货币当局制定的政策相协调，因为这两种政策结合在一起不能违反政府的综合预算约束。如果一个部门可以直接命令另一个部门（相当于两个部门都是自己设计财政和货币政策的第三方的下属），或者两个部门有相同的目标，那么财政和货币协调就很简单。但现实并非如此。例如，欧洲中央银行具有机构独立性，欧盟成员国政府经常抱怨欧洲央行政策无法满足其需求。并且，尽管许多人认为美联储是中央银行独立的典范，但它的实际独立性却会不时地变化。当两个部门有不同的目标而一个不能被另一个所指示时，他们之间是通过什么机制来实现协调的？作为基本步骤，在这个项目中，我们将协调视为两个部门之间的讨价还价过程。我们让财政当局的目标与选举有关。我们让货币当局的目标与央行行长所考虑的经济模式有关。由于财政当局的目标是以选举为导向，协调是一个政治经济均衡的结果。 在这个基本框架内，我们打算解决以下问题。讨价还价过程产生的协调意味着比简单的协调情况下更好的资源分配？讨价还价过程如何受制度特征的影响？某些特征会使讨价还价过程更有效吗？而且，央行独立真的很可取吗？

16602619.label: Realisation of objectives
16602619.value: We have achieved all five objectives listed in the original application; that is, we have built a tractable basic model to accommodate our policy-economy equilibrium framework to study implications of the fiscal-monetary policy coordination on inflation, analyzed the model analytically and numerically, studied a variation with aggregate shocks, studied a variation with a different objective of the monetary authority, and studied a variation with a different political structure. Let us start with the following features of our basic model. 1. The big picture. In our model, the only fiscal action at each period is lump sum taxes that finance money withdrawal or are financed by money injection. The fiscal action is politically decided, i.e., it is determined by voting. When voting, agents have different types determined by idiosyncratic shocks; therefore, the winning majority may prefer inflation higher than ex ante optimal inflation. The monetary authority cares the average welfare of agents. In short, both the fiscal and monetary authorities have a welfare-based objective function; the political process generates a commitment problem for which independence of the monetary authority is a partial solution. 2. The economic mechanism that connects the politically-driven fiscal influence on inflation with the monetary response to that influence. In our model, the monetary authority may confine the inflation temptation of the winning majority by the nominal interest rate. For this mechanism to be effective, we design the model in a way that the nominal interest rate subtract inflation is not tied to the time-preference determined constant. Specifically, every period following the policy determination and a market trading which involves all tax collection and the government bond issuance, there is another market trading where the newly-issued bonds are illiquid. This illiquidity generates dependence of the nominal interest rate on the proportion of bonds in the total nominal asset. Importantly, the winning majority prefers a low nominal interest and the nominal interest rate that maximizes the average welfare of agents increases with inflation; therefore, it is not much costly for the monetary authority to punish the winning majority by raising the nominal interest rate in case that the winning majority pushes up inflation. 3. Departure from the Friedman rule. In our model, people have nonlinear preference on the goods in each of the aforementioned two-round market trading. (Because agents differ in types in the first round of trading, we add a third-round market trading where agent have a linear preference on the traded goods; this linear preference eliminates the distribution of wealth.) Because money cannot be retired in the second round of trade, the Friedman rule may or may not be ex ante optimal. But even when the Friedman rule is ex ante optimal, the winning majority can drive inflation positive. 4. Tractability. As described in our original application, our approach treats policy coordination as a bargaining process between the fiscal and monetary authorities. Ideally, the model shall be able to deliver closed-from solutions which can explicitly pinpoint the difference between our approach and approaches in the existing literature. Because the interaction between the market equilibrium (which takes the policy as given) and the policy selection (which takes dependence of the market equilibrium on the policy as given), there may not exist a closed-form solution even from a model which appears to be very simple. We manage to make our model tractable by adopting a few assumptions. Now let us summarize the most notable findings from the basic model. 1. Ex ante optimal inflation may or may not be the Friedman-rule inflation. In the absence of any aggregate shock, ex ante optimal nominal interest rate may or may not be zero. Even when ex ante optimal nominal interest rate is zero, it can be positive in the presence of an aggregate liquidity shock (which is realized on the second market trading). 2. The optimal inflation rate being the Friedman-rule inflation or not, the wining majority can prefer a positive inflation. Even though inflation resulting from bargaining between the authorities remains positive, it is lower than the one that is determined under the fiscal dominance. 3. With or without the aggregate shock, if ex ante optimal nominal interest rate is zero then bargaining keeps the nominal interest rate at zero; otherwise, bargaining results in a positive nominal interest rate. The working paper submitted with this report serves as a detailed (while not complete) presentation of conducted research activities and achieved objectives.

16602619.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602619.value: A classical viewpoint on inflation is that inflation is a fiscal phenomenon---inflation is inevitable if the fiscal authority has to rely on seigniorage to finance some of its expenditures. Our project is motivated by the following questions. Why does the fiscal authority choose inflation at the first place? If we allow private agents to affect the fiscal choice, would inflation prevail? And, given that inflation is a fiscal phenomenon, is the monetary authority all that passive? Our project starts with the observation that the monetary and fiscal authorities must coordinate for policy selections and the coordination is linked by the consolidated government constraint; our project intends to study coordination in form of explicit bargaining. To answer the above questions, we develop a model which makes explicit why the fiscal authority chooses certain expenditures and ordinary tax revenues, permits the monetary authority to affect the nominal interest rate given the fiscal policy, and makes explicit why the monetary authority chooses certain the nominal interest rate. The only fiscal action at each period is lump sum taxes that finance money withdrawal or are financed by money injection; that action is determined by voting. The fiscal action is determined by voting. When voting, agents have different types that are determined by idiosyncratic shocks. The monetary authority cares the average welfare of agents. The main findings are the following. 1. Ex ante optimal inflation may or may not be the Friedman-rule inflation. In the absence of any aggregate shock, ex ante optimal nominal interest rate may or may not be zero. Even when ex ante optimal nominal interest rate is zero, it can be positive in the presence of an aggregate liquidity shock (which is realized on the second market trading). 2. The optimal inflation rate being the Friedman-rule inflation or not, the wining majority can prefer a positive inflation. Even though inflation resulting from bargaining between the authorities remains positive, it is lower than the one that is determined under the fiscal dominance. 3. With or without the aggregate shock, if ex ante optimal nominal interest rate is zero then bargaining keeps the nominal interest rate at zero; otherwise, bargaining results in a positive nominal interest rate.

16602619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602619.value: To obtain closed-form solutions, we make quite a few simplifying assumptions in our basic model: 1. There are only two types of agents; 2. The aggregate shock is a preference shock that affects the liquidity value of money; 3. Bonds do not have any liquidity value; 4. The government does not have any expenditures other than lump sum transfers to agents (or lump taxes financing retiring money); 5. The two authorities have symmetric bargaining power; 6. The utility/disutility functions take special forms (that are widely used in the literature). Although we do not see that relaxing any assumption would overturn the insights drawn from the basic model, it is desirable to let the model tell what may happen under more complicated assumptions. At the very least, this can be done by numerical simulation. Another direction for the future work is to let individuals have persistent difference in wealth. This direction certainly would rely on the numerical solutions.

16602619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602619.value: What may drive inflation? It is well known to the public that inflation is a monetary phenomenon. The monetary phenomenon, however, has a fiscal root---inflation is inevitable if the fiscal authority has to rely on seigniorage to finance some of its expenditures. In a modern society, the government’s fiscal need is subject to the voters’ choices. Our project demonstrates that even though ex ante everyone is alike and, in particular, dislikes inflation, inflation may prevail because people differ at the voting time. That is, the political arrangement makes it impossible for people to commit to ex ante optimal inflation rate. Our project also shows the value of independence of the central bank. The presence of the consolidated government budget constraint demands the winning majority to coordinate with the central bank in policy choices. By way of controlling the nominal interest rate, the central bank can confine the inflation temptation of the winning majority.

16602819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
16602819.value: Housing prices in China have experienced a rapid growth in the last two decades since China's housing market reform, vastly outpacing the growth of the disposable income. This excessive housing price increase has raised several important questions. Are housing prices driven by fundamentals or by bubbles? Do housing prices crowd in or crowd out investment? Should housing price fluctuations be regulated? These questions have been heatedly debated among policy makers, academic researchers, and the general public almost on the first day since the housing market reform. However rigorous analysis is scant. The purpose of this proposed project is to systematically evaluate different hypotheses regarding the cause of China's housing boom through the lens of a cutting-edge dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model. We will construct a general equilibrium model to fit several empirical regularities that we documented in the data first. We will then use this model to evaluate many policies that the Chinese government has implemented in the past two decades to manage housing prices. These policies include the increase in the down-payment ratio, restrictions on purchasing and reselling houses, and taxes on transactions. 最近二十年房價在中國快速上漲，遠遠超購經濟增長速度。房價過快上漲激發一些問題。比如房價上漲是由基本面驅動的還是由於泡沫？房價會擠出投資還是增加投資？ 不管是老百姓還是政策制定者對這些問題都爭論不休，嚴謹的學術研究卻是十分缺乏。這個研究項目的主要目的就對中國房價上漲過快的兩種假說進行檢驗。我們會構造一個均衡模型並用數據對模型進行校準。我們然後利用該模型對中國政府一系列房價政策做反事分析。

16602819.label: Realisation of objectives
16602819.value: 1. To collect data on all land transaction in China. This objective is realized. The land transaction data is collected from the Ministry of Land and Resources, which maintains detailed records for each land parcel transaction. Over 1.6 million land transaction deals are recorded, spanning from 1999 to 2015. This dataset includes comprehensive details such as transaction price, land area, transaction date, buyer, intended land use, transaction method, and location. Our land transaction database offers precise details about land holdings of listed firms, surpassing the approximate data derived from annual reports (e.g., Chaney et al., 2012), and presents advantages over publicly available land data from government yearbooks or commercial sources like China Real Estate Information (CREI). A distinctive aspect of our database is its extension beyond the city-level data used in prior research (e.g., Chen et al., 2017) to include county-level data. This is crucial because city-level datasets typically cover only urban districts, omitting suburban counties which are vital for a comprehensive view of land market dynamics. In China, counties not only encompass larger land areas than cities but also contribute significantly to economic output, accounting for 54.2% of the nation’s total GDP in 2015. Counties, particularly in coastal and eastern regions, feature vibrant land markets. Additionally, our database uniquely classifies “development zones” as independent county-level regions due to their distinct land policies and pricing, ensuring our database accurately reflects the full spectrum of land transactions across China. In the paper entitled “The Hidden Cost of Political Connection: Evidence from China’s Stock Market Responses to Land Transactions” (RR to Economic Inquiry), we match this dataset with data on Chinese listed companies. By analyzing the stock market’s reaction to these transactions, we investigate the hidden cost of political connections for firms. 2. To document the effect of land prices on firm-level investment and employment. This objective is also realized. In a working paper entitled “Land use regulation and macroeconomic fluctuations: A tale of two countries”. Prof. Wang and his coauthors show empirical evidence that the U.S. housing boom produces a crowding-in effect on investment in the non-housing sector, by contrast, the Chinese housing boom produces a crowding-out effect on investment in the non-housing sector (See Tables 1 and 2). In addition, data shows that the U.S. residential and industrial land prices comove and increase rapidly following the housing boom, whereas the Chinese residential land price skyrockets but the industrial land price decreases slightly following the housing boom. In a paper entitled “Asset-market Sentiments and Business-cycle Fluctuations, Prof. Wang and his coauthors show that changes in perceptions about land price uncertainty led to self-fulfilling fluctuations in asset prices, resulting in self-confirmed actual uncertainty. Through entrepreneurs’ borrowing constraints, these fluctuations, in turn, are transmitted and propagated to the macroeconomy, generating boom–bust cycles in investment and employment. 3. To construct a unified DSGE model to explain the relationship between land prices and aggregate economic fluctuations in China and in the US. 4. To estimate the DSGE model using data from China and the US, respectively. Objectives 3 and 4 are completely realized. In the working paper “Land use regulation and macroeconomic fluctuations: A tale of two countries”, to explain the opposite effects of a housing boom on investment in the non-housing sector for the U.S. and China, Prof. Wang and his coauthors extend Liu et al. (2013)'s DSGE model to allow for a housing sector and a non-housing sector, with residential land being used in the housing sector while industrial land being used in the non-housing sector. They use the Bayesian method to estimate the model parameters which consists of deep those structural parameters related to the land use regulations in the US and China, and all the parameters governing the persistence and volatility of house demand shock processes. Land rezoning cost parameter plays a pivotal role in our model, Table 4(a) shows that the estimated land rezoning cost for Chinese economy is way larger than its US counterpart (12.802 vs 1.6579) which implies that it is much harder to change land uses in China than in U.S., thus validating the previous analysis. Therefore, in the U.S., private landowners pay land rezoning cost to convert land from industrial use to residential use following a housing boom. The increase in the industrial land price due to a fall in supply triggers the propagation and amplification mechanism in the spirit of Kiyotaki and Moore (1997) as well in the non-housing sector. Thus, the housing boom crowds in the investment in the non-housing sector. By contrast, in China, the local governments hardly convert land from industrial use to residential use following a housing boom. The same propagation and amplification mechanism cannot be set off in the non-housing sector as that in the housing sector. On the contrary, the credit is increasingly allocated the housing sector with the result that the housing boom crowds out the investment in the non-housing sector, and decreases the industrial land price. 5. To design optimal policies regarding land transactions. This objective is partially finished. As discussed earlier, different land rezoning cost in the US and China leads to very different implication of housing boom to investment in the non-housing sector. So a natural policy implication will be to relax the restrictions in China on converting land from industrial use to residential use following a housing boom, However, the optimal degree of relaxation still needs further quantitative analysis. Prof. Wang and his coauthors are working on that.

16602819.label: Major findings and research outcome
16602819.value: 1. Working paper “Land use regulation and macroeconomic fluctuations: A tale of two countries” Empirical evidence shows that the U.S. housing boom has a crowding-in effect on non-housing investment, while the Chinese housing boom has a crowding-out effect. In the U.S., residential and industrial land prices rise rapidly, whereas in China, residential land prices soar while industrial land prices slightly decrease. This paper extends Liu et al. (2013) by considering capital, land, and labor inputs in both the housing and non-housing sectors, along with financial frictions and land use regulation and show using Bayesian methods that land use regulation is lax in the U.S. but stringent in China, which is important to explain why the U.S. housing boom has a crowding-in effect on non-housing investment, while the Chinese housing boom has a crowding-out effect. Findings from this paper also have implication of the fiscal policy regarding land rezoning cost for Chinese economy. Prof. Wang and his coauthors are still working on the policy implications and will provide an updated working paper once it is available. 2. Paper entitled “Asset-market Sentiments and Business-cycle Fluctuations”, published in International Economic Review in 2024, This paper present a tractable model that accommodates asset-market sentiment in a standard DSGE setting to quantitatively evaluate sentiment-driven macroeconomic fluctuations. In this model, changes in households’ perceived uncertainty about housing prices lead to self-fulfilling fluctuations in housing prices, which then impact investment and output through entrepreneurs’ collateral constraints. Household sentiment shocks hence are transmitted and propagated to the macroeconomy, generating boom–bust cycles. Uncertainty, housing prices, and the real economy are linked. Quantitatively, the sentiment shock in the form of risk–panic is a crucial driver of business cycle fluctuations despite the presence of various competing shocks. 3. Paper entitled “The Hidden Cost of Political Connection: Evidence from China’s Stock Market Responses to Land Transactions”, We construct a matched database of land transactions and Chinese listed companies. By analyzing the stock market’s reaction to these transactions, we investigate the hidden cost of political connections for firms. Our results show a negative market response to land deals by politically connected companies. This suggests that potential future political or legal risks associated with the land transaction could harm the firm. To strengthen our findings, we leverage the anti-corruption campaign as a natural experiment and employ a difference-in-differences approach. This analysis yields consistent results. Furthermore, we discover that short-term and long-term investors have differing views on political connections.

16602819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
16602819.value: 1. In this project, Prof. Wang and his coauthors explores the macroeconomic implication of a sentiment shock to real estate prices. Their framework is tractable and potentially useful for future work to study sentiment in other markets (such as the bond market and the stock market) and the macroeconomic implications. 2. We plan to keep using our land transaction data as a measure of regional fiscal stance and how this will affect the economic development in Chinese economy. Our current data covers over 1.6 million land transaction deals spanning from 1999 to 2015. This dataset includes comprehensive details such as transaction price, land area, transaction date, buyer, intended land use, transaction method, and location. We plan to further expand this data which will help to explore if the slowdown in real estate market affect the fiscal stance of local government.

16602819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
16602819.value: The recent financial crisis, caused by a collapse in US housing prices, has sparked interest in understanding the relationship between housing prices and the macroeconomy. It is well-established that housing prices play a crucial role in amplifying small shocks into significant macroeconomic fluctuations through the collateral channel. However, an intriguing observation is that housing booms in the United States and China have different effects on investments in non-housing sectors. In the US, a housing boom tends to increase investments in non-housing sectors, because it is relatively easy to convert industrial land into residential land, resulting in increased prices for industrial land and encouraging investment in non-housing sectors. On the contrary, in China, the rules regarding the use of industrial land for residential purposes are more stringent. Thus, during a housing boom in China, the prices of industrial land do not increase significantly. Instead, the housing boom leads to higher interest rates, making investments in non-housing sectors less appealing and crowding out real investment. In summary, the difference in institutional arrangements, particularly land rezoning policies, explains why housing booms have different impacts for investments across two countries. Our findings have important policy implications for the land rezoning policies in China.

17100019.label: Project Objectives
17100019.value: This pragmatic trial aims to compare the effectiveness of topical application of a 38% SDF solution with that of a 5% NaF varnish as a positive control for preventing ECC in the primary upper anterior teeth when applied at half-yearly intervals over a 30-month period.

17100019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100019.value: 背景： 在香港，有55%的學童患有早期兒童齲齒（蛀牙）。其中，70% 學童前門牙嚴重破壞，長遠來說影響了他們的身體健康和生活質量。現有預防蛀牙的標準方法是使用5% 的氟化鈉漆，而此種方法并不足以預防蛀牙。有很多牙醫使用38%氟化氨銀靜止蛀牙。我們發表的研究表明氟化氨銀對乳齒和恆齒也同樣有預防作用。然而，並沒有關鍵的臨床實驗支持使用此種方法可成為預防蛀牙的新標準。 目的： 此二期，單點，隨機雙盲，兩組平行陽性對照的實用型臨床實驗的目的為評估使用38%氟化氨銀在預防新乳牙前門牙蛀牙上是否優於使用5% 氟化鈉。 方法： 此項實驗將收入730名身體健康的3歲學童并塊狀隨機分配至兩組。一組接受38%氟化氨銀治療（實驗組），一組接受5% 氟化鈉 治療（標準治療對照組），學童們每六個月接受其前門牙的塗藥治療。此樣本量足以進行較優性試驗，統計功效為90%，預計失訪率為20%。 主要研究結果為每個學童30個月后健康牙面變成患齲牙面的數量。次要研究結果為，每個學童30個月后患齲牙面因接受治療后成功靜止的數量。一名已校準的檢查員將每六個月在幼稚園進行牙科檢查以發現新蛀牙及評估靜止蛀牙，共檢查30個月。檢查員，學童及其家長將進行雙盲處理。有關學童的口腔健康相關行為和他們的社會經濟背景的信息將會通過家長收集以調整混淆因子的影響。 預期結果及臨床影響： 如與預期一致，實驗結果可幫助修改預防蛀牙的標準方法。如香港採用氟化氨銀， 其可幫助20,800（160,000名學童中的13%）名學童預防有患齲高風險的前門牙患上蛀牙，因此可顯著地降低蛀牙對兒童及因蛀牙產生的對其家庭的影響。同樣地，實驗結果可被廣泛採用并促進氟化氨銀在其他國家地區的使用以降低全球早期兒童齲的影響。

17100019.label: Realisation of objectives
17100019.value: We have completed a 30-month study comparing the effectiveness of a 38% SDF solution and a 5% NaF varnish (used as a positive control) in preventing dental caries in the primary (anterior) teeth of preschool children when applied at half-yearly intervals. The results demonstrated the semi-annual application of 38% SDF demonstrates superior caries prevention in primary upper anterior teeth compared to the semi-annual application of 5% NaF. Therefore, clinicians can confidently use a 38% SDF solution to prevent dental decay in preschool children.

17100019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100019.value: Our 30-month study compared the effectiveness of a 38% SDF solution to a 5% NaF varnish (positive control) in preventing dental caries in the primary teeth of preschool children when applied biannually. Throughout this research, we have presented our findings at seven international conferences and published fourteen articles in peer-reviewed international journals. Additionally, our work has received five research awards, including one at the annual scientific meeting of the HKU Faculty of Dentistry, another from the International Association for Dental Research meeting, a third from the Hong Kong International Dental Expo and Symposium, one more from the Tohoku University, The University of Hong Kong, and Fujian Medical University (TU-HKU-FJMU) Symposium, and a final one from the 44th Asia Pacific Dental Congress.

17100019.value: The 30-month results are currently being analysed, and the final findings will be presented at the international conference. The results will be submitted for publication. As 38% SDF has been shown to prevent dental decay in primary teeth of preschool children, further studies could explore its cost-effectiveness of caries prevention programme using SDF.

17100019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100019.value: Sodium fluoride (5% NaF) varnish is generally regarded as standard care for prevention of tooth decay. This 30-month clinical trial found that using a solution called 38% silver diamine fluoride (SDF) twice a year on the front baby teeth is better at preventing tooth decay than using 5% NaF. The study lasted for 30 months.

17100119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17100119.value: Background: Musculoskeletal (MS) problems are common in primary care and they are detrimental to quality of life. Current management of chronic MS problems focuses mainly on pain control with medications, but the outcomes are often unsatisfactory and sometimes harmful. The provision of the patient’s health-related quality of life (HRQOL) information to the doctor may trigger management to improve quality of life. Aim and Objectives: This is an effectiveness-implementation hybrid trial that aims to find out whether the implementation of routine measurement and reporting on the patient’s EQ-5D-5L HRQOL data with an electronic platform can improve HRQOL and pain in patients with chronic knee or back problems in primary care. We will also assess the acceptability of routine electronic measurement and reporting of the EQ-5D-5L in real-world primary care. Method: This is a multi-center prospective cluster-randomized controlled trial in six public primary care clinics in Hong Kong. The six clinics will be randomized to the intervention or control group. We shall recruit 1374 (229 from each clinic) subjects with symptomatic chronic knee or back problems through the attending doctors in the clinics. Subjects of the Intervention clinics will complete the electronic EQ-5D-5L at recruitment and every follow up during the next 12 months, and a report on their longitudinal EQ-5D-5L data will be shown to the doctors during the consultations. Subjects of the control clinics will receive care as usual. All subjects will complete a set of patient reported outcome measures (PRO) including the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) on HRQOL and a 10-point Pain Rating Scale (PRS), and a structured questionnaire on sociodemographics, morbidity and service utilization rates at recruitment, and at 3, 6 and 12 months by telephone. Outcome Measures and Data Analysis: The primary outcome is change in WOMAC total score. The secondary outcomes are change in pain, other PRO scores and doctor rated severity of disease. Group difference in changes of WOMAC and other outcome scores over time will be analyzed using generalized estimating equation model under intention-to-treat principle. The acceptability of routine measurement of HRQOL by electronic EQ-5D-5L will be analyzed by descriptive statistics. Potential application: Routine measurement of HRQOL by an electronic EQ-5D-5L platform can be applied to other outpatient clinics to improve care of MS problems and other conditions to facilitate more effective and patient-centered care.

17100119.label: Realisation of objectives
17100119.value: We have successfully achieved all three objectives despite the slight delay in the start of the study due to the COVID-19 outbreak in 2020. 1. We completed the 12-month single-blind cluster randomised controlled trial (RCT) to determine the effectiveness of routine measurement and reporting of HRQOL by the electronic Chinese EQ-5D-5L in improving HRQOL. We recruited a total of 1200 patients with chronic knee and/or back problems from six Hospital Authority (HA) General Out-patient Clinics (GOPC) from June 2020 to March 2022. Randomisation was performed at the clinic level, and interventions were delivered to participants recruited from the three intervention clinics and participants recruited from the three control clinics received usual care. A total of 59 clinicians from six clinics provided consent to take part in the trial. We provided three training workshops on how to interpret the e-EQ-5D-5L report to the intervention clinic staff from July to October, 2020. We collected outcome data at baseline (by face-to-face interviews) and at 3, 6, and 12 months by telephone survey administered by the HKU Social Science Research Centre. The completion rate was 100% at baseline, and was 83.42% (n=1001), 86.17% (n=1034) and 84.75% (n=1017) at 3, 6, and 12 months, respectively. 595 participants from the intervention clinics completed the electronic EQ-5D-5L before seeing the doctor at recruitment and repeated the e-EQ-5D-5L at least once during their follow-up visits within the project period. A printed report summarizing the longitudinal results on the EQ-5D-5L profile and utility and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores was generated for the participant to present to the consulting doctor. 605 participants from the control clinics received usual care without completion of the e-EQ-5D-5L. We used intention to treat (ITT) analysis to compare the changes in WOMAC scores from baseline to 12 months between the intervention and control groups. The follow-up outcome assessors and data analysts were blinded to the group allocation. Within group changes in WOMAC scores were assessed by paired t tests for any significant change over time. compared Generalized estimating equation (GEE) with linear function and working correlation matrix was used to determine the effectiveness of e-EQ-5D-5L on the outcomes from baseline to 12 months. 2. To find out whether routine measurement and reporting of HRQOL by the electronic Chinese EQ-5D- 5L will improve the pain control, overall health condition, patient enablement and SF-6D health utility in patients with chronic Knee or back problems in primary care over a 12-month period, all participants completed the Pain Rating Scale (PRS), overall health condition (Global Rating Scale (GRS), patient enablement (Chinese Patient Enablement Index-version 2 (PEI-2)) and the Short-Form Six-Dimension (SF-6D) at baseline, 3, 6, and 12 months. We used intention to treat (ITT) analysis to compare the changes in the outcome scores from baseline to 12 months between the intervention and control groups. The outcome assessors and data analysts were blinded to the group allocation. Within group changes in the outcome scores were assessed by paired t tests for any significant change over time. Generalized estimating equation (GEE) with linear function and working correlation matrix was used to determine the effectiveness of e-EQ-5D-5L on the outcomes from baseline to 12 months. 3. To evaluate the acceptability of routine electronic measurement and reporting of EQ-5D-5L data in primary care, participants also completed the questionnaires on perceived usefulness (PU) and perceived ease of use (PEOU) of the e-EQ-5D-5L, and the doctors completed a questionnaire on the perceived usefulness (of the e-EQ-5D-5L report. The summative scores of PEOU and PU were compared between baseline and follow-ups by repeated measure ANOVA. We further assessed the feasibility of routine completion and reporting of e-EQ-5D-5L by the time taken for each participant to complete the e-EQ-5D-5L survey and that reported by the doctor to review each EQ-5D-5L report in the intervention clinics. The completion and response rates of the e-EQ-5D-5L survey at baseline and follow-ups were also calculated. We also conducted semi-structured individual interviews with fifteen patients, a focus group interview with five doctors and a focus group interview with three RAs to have an in-depth exploration on feasibility and acceptability of routine measurement and reporting on HRQOL by the e-EQ-5D-5L from October to December 2021. The interviews were conducted by two members of the research team who had training in qualitative research. The audio-tapes of the interviews were transcribed in verbatim and the content was analyzed to identify the themes on feasibility and acceptability.

17100119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100119.value: 1. The WOMAC score of the intervention group (IG) increased significantly (2.27,p=0.002), and that of the control group (CG) also increased but the change was not statistically significant (0.43,p=0.515), indicating worsening in HRQOL. Adjusted analyses showed that the IG had a greater increase in the WOMAC score over the 12-months follow-up period than the control group (β=2.137,p=0.029). The results did not support our hypothesis that routine measurement and reporting of HRQOL by e-EQ-5D-5L could improve HRQOL in patients with chronic back/knee problems. A possible explanation was that most chronic knee/back problems were degenerative in nature and tend to be progressive, leading to more impairment in function and HRQOL. More patients in the control group was referred to orthopedics surgery at baseline and first six-month follow up, which might have led to more effective treatment of the condition. 2. The use of e-EQ-5D-5L was effective in moderating the change in patient enablement, measured by the PEI-2 score. The PEI-2 score decreased significantly in the CG (-1.28,p<0.001) but insignificantly in the IG (-0.24,p=0.413). Adjusted analyses showed that IG was associated with higher PEI-2 scores over the 12-months follow-up period (β=0.811,p=0.027). Moderation analysis found patient enablement attenuated the association between pain and HRQOL. We found the effect of the interaction between PRS and PEI-2 (PRS*PEI-2) on the WOMAC score was significant (β=-0.191, p<0.001). The relationship between PRS and WOMAC score was stronger for patients with lower PEI-2 (gradient=3.056) than for those with higher PEI-2 (gradient=1.746). Both groups had significantly lower PRS score after the study (IG:-0.64,p<0.001; CG:-0.77,p<0.001). The SF-6D score in the IG decreased, but had no significant change in the CG (IG:-0.03,p<0.001; CG:0.01,p=0.085). Adjusted analyses showed no change in SF6D and PRS scores between groups (SF6D:β=-0.010,p=0.293; PRS:β=0.050,p=0.773). 3. The mean completion time was 120.7 seconds at baseline, and 84.0 and 105.2 at first and second follow-up. Completion and response rates were 99.8% and 91.11% at the two follow-ups, respectively. Over 85.3% participants found the e-EQ-5D-5L useful but some had difficulties using the e-platform and in understanding or answering the questions. Doctors required less than 2 minutes to read the report and agreed the reports were easy to use (85.1%) and useful (72.0%), particularly in providing a holistic view of the patient's musculoskeletal problem. However, they felt the extra time required to address the problems shown on the report a barrier.

17100119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100119.value: Routine measurement and reporting of HRQOL by e-EQ-5D-5L can be used to promote self-care enablement among patients with chronic knee/back problems in primary care (PC). The e-EQ-5D-5L data can inform doctors on more personalized management to not only treat pain but also to address the patient’s stress and disability. Regular measurement by the e-EQ-5D-5L can be applied to monitor HRQOL and promote self-care enablement in patients with other chronic conditions, e.g. mental health problems. An audio function to read out questions and record answers, and increasing the font size can help patients with visual and literacy problems. To promote routine measurement of HRQOL by the e-EQ-5D-5L in busy PC, patients can be asked to attend the clinic 10 minutes earlier than their appointment to complete the survey so that the report can be ready for doctor’s review during the consultation. Furthermore, the e-EQ-5D-5L can be deployed into a smartphone app for patients to self-complete at home. An interface merged to existing electronic clinical medical record systems to allow clinicians’ easy access, review and tracking of the e-EQ-5D-5L data can further promote the clinical use of HRQOL as an outcome indicator of patient care.

17100119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100119.value: Information on health-related quality of life (HRQOL) can enhance patient diagnosis and management but it was rarely available in routine clinical practice. Electronic measurement of HRQOL may facilitate timely and regular communication of the impact of the illness on the patient’s life with the doctor in routine clinical practice. We showed that routine measurement and reporting on e-EQ-5D-5L data was a feasible and acceptable method of assessing HRQOL of patients with chronic musculoskeletal problems in routine primary care in Hong Kong, which can assist real-time management decisions. Our randomised controlled trial of 1200 patients found that routine reporting on the e-EQ-5D-5L results might not improve patients’ HRQOL, i.e. perceived physical pain and limitations on functionality, but it was associated with better self-care enablement in that patients felt more enabled in managing their chronic conditions. The e-EQ-5D-5L could be deployed into a smartphone application for patients to self-complete at home to monitor their own HRQOL. Further research could investigate the application of routine measurement of HRQOL by e-EQ-5D-5L in patients with other chronic conditions, and the possibility of incorporating the e-EQ-5D-5L platform into existing clinical management systems.

17100219.label: Realisation of objectives
17100219.value: During nervous system development, individual neurons sense a variety of different soluble proteins that profoundly influence their survival, outgrowth, and differentiation. The role of target-derived trophic factors, neurotrophins, has been well recognized in these processes. Skeletal muscles, the synaptic targets of motor neurons, are one of the major sources of several neurotrophins, including brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). Despite the initial well-characterized functions of BDNF in the brain, emerging evidence indicates that BDNF is also expressed in skeletal muscles and is crucial for muscle development, maintenance, and regeneration. In the early stages of muscle development, BDNF is found to be expressed in myoblasts, and its expression is repressed in differentiated myotubes. In the maintenance and regeneration of adult skeletal muscles, BDNF regulates muscle adaptation and plasticity by contributing to the functional diversity and metabolic flexibility of skeletal muscles in response to exercise and other stimuli and promotes the proliferation and differentiation of myosatellite cells during muscle repair and regeneration. The regulation of BDNF signaling is therefore essential for proper muscle growth, formation, and function. Although some previous studies indicated that BDNF can modulate synaptic activity and function in neuromuscular junction (NMJ) development and disease, the cellular mechanisms underlying the spatiotemporally controlled release of muscle-generated BDNF during initial NMJ formation remain largely unknown. In this GRF grant project, we have studied the molecular mechanisms underlying the subcellular localization, spatially restricted release, and proteolytic conversion of BDNF in skeletal muscles and its physiological functions at developing NMJs. Through a combination of molecular manipulations and cellular imaging techniques, we first demonstrated that BDNF is highly enriched at podosome-like structures (PLSs) in association with the topologically complex postsynaptic apparatus in Xenopus muscle cells cultured on ECM-coated substratum, but no preferential localization is detected in simple plaque-shaped or scattered AChR clusters with no PLS localization in muscle cells cultured on uncoated or PDL substratum. This indicated the essential roles of ECM-mediated PLS formation in the subcellular localization of BDNF in muscle cells. PLSs are specialized actin-rich structures that play a crucial role in the site-directed trafficking of postsynaptic proteins to regulate the formation and topological remodeling of postsynaptic apparatus at NMJs. PLSs are generally composed of an actin-rich core surrounded by a ring structure, consisting of cortex proteins to facilitate adhesion to the underlying substratum through integrins. Additionally, high-potassium stimulation significantly reduces the spatially localized BDNF signals at the PLS core domain in aneural AChR clusters. These data suggested that the spatial localization of BDNF is likely mediated by the ventral actin filament module of the PLS core, which may function to maintain BDNF vesicles within the reserve pool of secretable synaptogenic proteins for activity-dependent release. Consistent with our previous studies on the vesicular trafficking of MT1-MMP, we demonstrated that BDNF vesicles are transported to and captured at PLSs in ECM-induced aneural AChR clusters and nerve-/agrin-induced synaptic AChR clusters. PLSs are known to mediate the intracellular trafficking of vesicles and surface targeting of newly synthesized membrane proteins via microtubule-based cargo delivery mechanisms. Using the pH-sensitive fluorescent protein SEP, a widely used fluorescence probe for imaging single-vesicle exocytosis, we further showed that the release of BDNF vesicles is spatially restricted, occurring at aneural and synaptic AChR clusters. As revealed by live-cell time-lapse TIRF imaging, the transient bursts of BDNF-SEP signals that we observed at both aneural and synaptic AChR clusters indicate the localized release of vesicles containing diffusible BDNF proteins into the immediate extracellular environment. These results demonstrated the essential roles of PLSs in directing not only the vesicular trafficking and surface insertion of transmembrane proteins, such as MT1-MMP and AChR, but also the vesicular trafficking and release of the secretable protein BDNF at the postsynaptic apparatus. The proteolytic conversion of proBDNF to mBDNF is an important step in the regulation of BDNF signaling and function, and this process is tightly regulated by different intracellular and extracellular proteases. In human skeletal muscles, proBDNF is known to be much more abundant than mBDNF. Consistent with this, our Western blot data also showed that the expression level of mBDNF is relatively lower than that of proBDNF and is modestly reduced by BDNF MO in Xenopus myotomal tissue lysates. Our immunostaining data, however, showed a significant reduction of both proBDNF and BDNF signals at AChR clusters in BDNF MO muscle cells. More importantly, the formation of ECM-induced aneural AChR clusters and nerve-/agrin-induced AChR clusters was significantly inhibited by MO-mediated BDNF knockdown in muscles. These findings indicated that the dysregulation of subcellular localization of BDNF and the imbalanced actions between proBDNF and mBDNF signaling drastically affect the proper assembly of the postsynaptic apparatus. The physiological involvement of muscle BDNF in NMJ development in vivo is further validated by examining the aneural and synaptic AChR clusters in the diaphragm muscles of MBKO mouse embryos. Prior to innervation by motor neurons, aneural AChR clusters, termed AChR prepatterns, can be detected in the central region of muscle fibers at E13.5. In this study, we found that the number of both aneural AChR prepatterns and synaptic AChR clusters in MBKO diaphragm muscles were significantly lower than those in Fl/Fl mice at E13.5, indicating that muscle-generated BDNF is required for the initial formation of aneural AChR prepatterns, which may reduce the availability of AChR molecules for being recruited to the nascent synaptic sites during early NMJ development in vivo. Additionally, compared to age-matched Fl/Fl mice, MBKO mice also exhibited a markedly reduced axonal length in the phrenic nerve as reflected by staining with a mixture of neurofilament and synaptophysin antibodies, leading to a narrower endplate band width. These observations are consistent with the well-known functions of BDNF in promoting axonal growth and branching. At E18.5, while we detected reduced AChR cluster intensity in MBKO mice, intriguingly no significant differences were detected in the axonal length of presynaptic neurons and the number of aneural and synaptic AChR clusters in postsynaptic muscles. In agreement with our findings, a previous study that examined the localization of different postsynaptic proteins and the apposition of presynaptic and postsynaptic elements at adult NMJs reveals no significant reduction on muscle BDNF deletion. We speculate that alternative sources of BDNF may compensate for the inhibitory effects of muscle BDNF deficiency on synaptic development in both presynaptic neurons and postsynaptic muscles, considering that BDNF is also expressed in motor neurons, perisynaptic Schwann cells, and endothelial cells. In addition, we have made another important observation related to this project: BDNF functions as a myokine to optimize the metabolic properties of skeletal muscle during nutrient stress by maintaining mitochondrial quality in female mice. Mitochondrial remodeling is an important intracellular quality control process that removes damaged or dysfunctional mitochondria to prevent them from contaminating healthy mitochondria. However, the role of muscle-secreted myokines in mitochondrial quality control is poorly defined. In this study, we revealed that BDNF provokes mitochondrial fission and clearance in skeletal muscle via the PRKAA/AMPK-PINK1-PRKN/Parkin and PRKAA-DNM1L/DRP1-MFF pathways. Depleting Bdnf expression in myotubes reduced fatty acid-induced mitofission and mitophagy, which was associated with mitochondrial elongation and impaired lipid handling. Importantly, MBKO mice displayed defective mitofission and mitophagy, and accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria in the muscle when they were fed a high-fat diet (HFD). Collectively, our results highlight the essential role of BDNF in metabolic stress-related mitostasis.

17100219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17100219.value: The major findings of this project have been published in this original research article: 1. Zhang J, Kwan HR, Chan CB, and Lee CW (2024) Localized release of muscle-generated BDNF regulates the initial formation of postsynaptic apparatus at neuromuscular synapses. Cell Death & Differentiation. Nov 7. Online ahead of print. doi: 10.1038/s41418-024-01404-4. Major findings: (i) BDNF is spatially associated with the actin-rich core domain of podosome-like structures (PLSs) at topologically complex acetylcholine receptor (AChR) clusters in cultured Xenopus muscle cells. (ii) The release of spatially localized BDNF is tightly controlled by activity-regulated mechanisms in a calcium-dependent manner. (iii) BDNF-containing vesicles are transported to and captured at PLSs in both aneural and synaptic AChR clusters for spatially restricted release. (iv) BDNF knockdown or furin-mediated endoproteolytic activity inhibition significantly suppresses aneural AChR cluster formation, which in turn affects synaptic AChR clustering. (v) Skeletal muscle-specific BDNF knockout (MBKO) mice exhibit structural defects in the formation of aneural AChR clusters and their subsequent recruitment to nerve-induced synaptic AChR clusters during the initial stages of NMJ development in vivo.

17100219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17100219.value: To build upon the conclusions of our recently published work demonstrating the vesicular trafficking and surface targeting of MT1-MMP at the postsynaptic apparatus (Chan et al., eLife 2020), we have now demonstrated that BDNF vesicles are transported to and captured at PLSs in both ECM-induced aneural AChR clusters and nerve-induced synaptic AChR clusters. It would be of interest to further understand how the vesicular trafficking of various postsynaptic proteins and neurotrophic factors is tightly regulated by PLS dynamics during the structural maturation of NMJs. For example, one follow-up study demonstrated that membrane infoldings, which mirror the junctional folds of NMJs, develop in cultured muscle cells in close association with PLS-enriched perforations of aneural and synaptic AChR clusters (Kwan et al., Science Advances 2023). This suggests that dynamic PLS turnover is likely involved in the formation of postsynaptic membrane architecture. Since abnormalities in the junctional fold architecture are common phenotypes associated with several neuromuscular disorders in humans, the results of our study provide a better understanding of the molecular regulation of membrane infolding formation and maintenance at the postsynaptic apparatus. This knowledge could potentially be translated to understand how junctional fold abnormalities impair synaptic functions in various neuromuscular diseases.

17100219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17100219.value: At the neuromuscular junction (NMJ), the spatial localization of acetylcholine receptors (AChRs) at the postsynaptic apparatus enables effective communication between nerve and muscle cells. Skeletal muscles, the synaptic targets of motor neurons, are major sources of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), which is generally known to enhance neurotransmitter release during synaptic plasticity. However, whether localized release of endogenously expressed BDNF at physiological levels regulates postsynaptic differentiation in skeletal muscles remains unknown. At topologically complex postsynaptic apparatus, AChR clusters are closely associated with dynamic actin-enriched structures responsible for releasing enzymes that digest the surrounding matrix. Building upon the conclusions of our previous work, this GRF project used advanced microscopy techniques to demonstrate that these actin-enriched structures direct not only the surface protein membrane-type matrix metalloproteinase but also the secreted protein BDNF at the postsynaptic apparatus. By understanding the vesicular trafficking, spatial localization, proteolytic activation, and activity-dependent release mechanisms of BDNF in skeletal muscles, this study greatly enhances our understanding of how the physiological regulation of muscle BDNF is achieved during NMJ development. This knowledge could potentially be translated to understand how muscle BDNF deficiency impairs synaptic structures and functions in various neuromuscular diseases.
