17105119.value: We have achieved all the three objectives as stated in the proposal. Abnormal cilia in the bile ducts of BA patients We examined if the ciliary mutations correlated with cilia formation in the bile duct of the corresponding BA patients. We examined the cilia marker co-immunoﬂuorescence staining of the BA livers for patients carrying de novo stop-gain and missense RDL variants in KIF3B (BA634C) and TTC17 (BA650C), respectively compared to the liver biopsies of non-BA controls (total n = 8; including biopsies of non-tumor liver of hepatoblastoma (HB; n = 4), liver of choledochal cysts (CC; n = 4)), and non-mutant BA subjects without ciliary mutation (n = 6). In contrast to an average of 3.6 ([S.E.M.] ± 0.1) and 3.2 ([S.E.M.] ± 0.1) cilia detected per bile duct in non-BA control and non-mutant BA livers, respectively, cilium axoneme were absent in all bile ducts (n = 11 and 12) of the both mutant BA subjects. Gene knockdown resulted in reduction in number of cilia in human ﬁbroblast and cholangiocyte cells To directly assess the impact of loss of function of these ciliary genes, we further knocked down KIF3B, PCNT and TTC17 by siRNA transfection in human control cholangiocyte and ﬁbroblast cells. A signiﬁcant reduction in the number of ciliated human ﬁbroblast cells was observed compared to controls transfected with non-speciﬁc scrambled siRNA. Effect of siRNA knockdown on cilia of human cholangiocytes were also investigated by SEM analysis. Under SEM examination, primary cilia appeared as a long and thick protrusion from the cholangiocyte cell surface as compared to the surrounding short and thin microvilli. Primary cilia could be identiﬁed in 40-50% of cells in scrambled siRNA transfected cultures. In contrast, cilia were either undetected or detected at lower percentages in KIF3B, PCNT and TTC17 siRNA transfected cultures (0-2% in KIF3B siRNA transfected cultures; 0% in PCNT siRNA transfected cultures; 10–12% in TTC17 siRNA transfected cultures). This reduction in the number of ciliated human cholangiocyte cells compared to controls transfected with non-speciﬁc scrambled siRNA further conﬁrmed the effect of abnormal cilia formation caused by the depletion of the selected ciliary genes. Ciliary gene knockout leads to impaired biliary function in zebraﬁsh We assessed if ciliary gene depletion could cause BA phenotype in vivo using zebraﬁsh model. Knockout of pcnt, kif3b and ttc17 was performed by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing. Introduction of INDEL in pcnt, kif3b and ttc17 genes was conﬁrmed by T7E1 assay and reduced expression of pcnt, kif3b and ttc17 in injected embryo was demonstrated by semi-quantitative RT-PCR. The biliary development of un-injected (Cas9 protein alone) and pcnt -, kif3b - and ttc17 - gRNA injected 5-dpf um14Tg[Tg(tp1-MmHbb:EGFP)um14] larvae were studied by examining the bile duct green ﬂuorescence signal intensity under ﬂuorescence icroscope. Zebraﬁsh larvae with the knockout of pcnt, kif3b and ttc17 showed comparable biliary green ﬂuorescence signal as control larvae, which suggested that knockout of these genes did not cause gross abnormal bile duct development in zebraﬁsh. To further examine the impact of the knockout of pcnt, kif3b and ttc17 on bile ﬂow from liver to the gall bladder in zebraﬁsh, we performed PED6 bile ﬂow assay in pcnt, kif3b and ttc17 knockout non-transgenic ﬁsh. Knockout of all three genes resulted in defective bile ﬂow in ﬁsh embryos, as measured by signiﬁcantly lower integrated density of PED6 in the gall bladder in the embryo mutant groups compared to the control group. This demonstrated that BA-like phenotype of impaired bile blow in zebraﬁsh model can be ascribed to disrupted function of PCNT, KIF3B and TTC17.

17105119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105119.value: Biliary atresia (BA) is the most common obstructive cholangiopathy in neonates, often progressing to end-stage cirrhosis. BA pathogenesis is believed to be multifactorial, but the genetic contribution, especially for nonsyndromic BA (common form: > 85%) remains poorly deﬁned. We conducted whole exome sequencing on 89 nonsyndromic BA trios to identify rare variants contributing to BA etiology. Functional evaluation using patients’ liver biopsies, human cell and zebraﬁsh models were performed. Clinical impact on respiratory system was assessed with clinical evaluation, nasal nitric oxide (nNO), high speed video analysis and transmission electron microscopy. We detected rare, deleterious de novo or biallelic variants in liver-expressed ciliary genes in 31.5% (28/89) of the BA patients. Burden test revealed 2.6-fold (odds ratio (OR) [95% conﬁdence intervals (CI)] = 2.58 [1.15–6.07], adjusted p = 0.034) over-representation of rare, deleterious mutations in liver-expressed ciliary gene set in patients compared to controls. Functional analyses further demonstrated absence of cilia in the BA livers with KIF3B and TTC17 mutations, and knockdown of PCNT, KIF3B and TTC17 in human control ﬁbroblasts and cholangiocytes resulted in reduced number of cilia. Additionally, CRISPR/Cas9-engineered zebraﬁsh knockouts of KIF3B, PCNT and TTC17 displayed reduced biliary ﬂow. Abnormally low level of nNO was detected in 80% (8/10) of BA patients carrying deleterious ciliary mutations, implicating the intrinsic ciliary defects. Our ﬁndings support strong genetic susceptibility for nonsyndromic BA. Ciliary gene mutations leading to cholangiocyte cilia malformation and dysfunction could be a key biological mechanism in BA pathogenesis.

17105119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17105119.value: Our study for the ﬁrst time demonstrated rare variant contribution to non-syndromic BA, such that rare, de novo or biallelic deleterious variants in liver-expressed ciliary genes was associated with a signiﬁcant two-fold increased risk of BA. This ﬁnding suggests that deleterious ciliary mutations may underlie the cholangiocyte cilia abnormalities observed in livers of non-syndromic BA patients. The low nasal nitric oxide levels detected in most of the BA patients carrying ciliary mutations suggests a genetic predisposition to multisystem ciliary abnormalities. Therefore, non-syndromic BA patients should be examined in details to address if there are dysfuncton/anomaly in other body systems in addition to the liver.

17105119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17105119.value: This study provides novel evidence that genetic factors play a major role in a substantial proportion of nonsyndromic BA cases, and a strong genetic basis for the previously reported cholangiocyte ciliary abnormalities. Rare deleterious ciliary mutations predisposed to higher risk of nonsyndromic BA. The predisposition to ciliary dysfunction may act beyond the hepatobiliary system and genetic screening for deleterious mutations in the cilia gene set would allow patient stratiﬁcation to further assess the pleiotropic clinical features and to improve clinical management. As reﬂected by the high genetic heterogeneity of ciliary mutations uncovered in this study, the nonsyndromic BA is unlikely to have a single genetic etiology. Patient stratiﬁcation aided by transcriptomic and immune proﬁling may help leverage statistical power and elucidate the polygenic etiology of BA.

17105319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105319.value: Myocardial infarction (MI) is one of the leading causes of death in Hong Kong and worldwide, heart cells lose blood supply caused irreversible damage and necrosis. A certain proportion of patients will developed to heart failure (HF) because of left ventricular remodeling. In recent years, Cell and tissue-engineered therapies are a promising therapeutic area that may reduce MI remodeling and scar formation by providing cells and matrix materials that can integrate with native tissue to restore normal heart function. Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC) can differentiate to mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) and cardiomyocytes (CM) and significantly improved cardiac function after transplantation. But the survival rate is very low, the improvement of cardiac function is mainly through a paracrine mechanism to complete, how to improve the survival of transplanted cells is the key question for stem cell transplantation therapy. Using cardiac tissue engineering to produce cell patch replace the damaged myocardium is a new strategy for the treatment of MI, in recent years the research results showed that myocardial patch can improve survival and engraftment of transplanted cells and improve cardiac function. Placenta contains immunomodulatory stem/progenitor cells, well-preserved endogenous growth factors and exhibits a highly vascularized tissue structure, which presents a natural and attractive source of scaffold material for transplantation and tissue regeneration. Here, we plan to use pig or rat’s placenta to generate a native decellularized scaffold and then seeded the scaffold with CM and MSC differentiated from human iPSC to generate a cardiac patch, which will be subsequently evaluated in small and large model of MI. 17105319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105319.value: In this study, we have demonstrated that DP can be used as a natural scaffold with stem cells to generate a BCP for treatment of post-MI heart failure. First, our results showed that intramyocardially transplanted hiPSC-CMs or hiPSC-MSCs can improve cardiac function in small animal model of MI and big animal model on HF. Second, the ECM of DP contained many important growth and pro-angiogenic factors to enhance the survival and maturation of transplanted hiPSC-CMs and promote their paracrine functions. Third, in vitro electrophysiological studies demonstrated that a BCP had synchronized electromechanical properties with electrical stimulation. The last but not least, transplantation of a BCP in an animal model of MI improved the cellular engraftment of hiPSC-CMs, as well as their paracrine effects on neovascularization compared with direct intramyocardial injection. As a result, BCP was superior to DP or hiPSC-CMs transplantation for improvement of LV function. On the other hand, we demonstrated that pre-transplantation systemic intravenous administration of hiPSC-MSCs induced immunomodulationand facilitated the survival of intramyocardially transplanted hiPSC-CMs or hiPSC-MSCs to improve cardiac function in animal model of MI. We provide novel evidence that pre-transplantation systemic intravenous administration of hiPSC-MSCs can induce immunomodulatory effects through activation of Tregs, suppression of NK cells, and modulation of the expression of cytokine profiling of CD4+ cells to enhance engraftment and survival of cells transplanted intramyocardially for treatment of MI. Increased survival of transplanted hiPSC-MSCs or hiPSC-CMs following systemic hiPSC-MSCs pre-conditioning was associated with further improvement in LV function, likely mediated by enhanced neovascularization and reduced cellular inflammation and apoptosis at the peri-infarct zone. Finally, there was no tumor formation at the injection site or other sites over the myocardium or other organs. We also compared the therapeutic efficacy and cell survival of intramuscular transplantation of hiPSC-MSCs with or without a single or repeated intravenous administration of hiPSC-MSCs. We provide novel evidence to the best of our knowledge that a combination of repeated systemic intravenous administration and local transplantation of hiPSC-MSCs can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of stem cell-based therapy In conclusion, this project provides important insight into the development of a novel approach to improve the therapeutic efficacy of current cell based therapy for heart regeneration.

17105319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17105319.value: In this study, we found that the immature phenotypes of BCP limit their therapeutic application for myocardial regeneration. First, the survival of CMs in the infarcted myocardium and the electrical coupling of the graft to the host myocardium after transplantation remain poor several weeks after transplantation. Second, CMs display automaticity, immature action potentials, slow conduction and structurally different from mature CMs that can induce arrhythmic risk after transplantation. Third, the cell patch conduction velocity and force generation was about 1/10 (6-10 beats/min) of adult myocardium. These abnormalities may result in functional deficiency and ventricular dyssynchrony. In the future, we hope to develop a systematic approach to optimize the maturation protocol for BCP, such as cardiac optogenetics or co-culture CMs with MSC. We also should further test the benefit effect of BCP and single or repeated intravenous administration of hiPSC-MSCs in a clinically relevant porcine model of HF post-MI.

17105319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17105319.value: In summary, our results provide important proof-ofprinciple data to support the use of DP as a scaffold material to generate a BCP using hiPSC-CMs to improve their survival, maturation, engraftment, and paracrine functions for cardiac regeneration following MI. we also demonstrated that pre-transplantation systemic intravenous administration of hiPSC-MSCs induced immunomodulationand facilitated the survival of intramyocardially transplanted hiPSC-CMs or hiPSC-MSCs to improve cardiac function in animal model of MI. 17105819.label: Realisation of objectives
17105819.value: (1) Insulin as a satiety factor in goldfish & its feedforward regulation by spexin at hepatic level As a follow-up of our previous studies on the role of spexin (SPX) as a novel satiety factor in goldfish and insulin as a potent stimulant on hepatic expression of SPX, goldfish insulin was cloned and its mature peptide was found to be highly conserved with 3D protein model almost identical to human insulin. Unlike mammals, insulin was highly expressed in goldfish liver and its expression at hepatic level could be up-regulated by feeding & glucose treatment. In goldfish, IP injection with insulin reduced foraging & food consumption, and notable drops in NPY & AgRP with parallel rises of POMC, CART, CCK & leptin mRNA could be detected in the telencepalon, hypothalamus & optic tectum, which are the brain areas in fish for appetite control. Similar results were also obtained with insulin treatment in goldfish brain cell culture prepared from these brain areas and the differential effects of insulin on transcript expression of these feeding regulators were mediated by P38 MAPK & PI3K/Akt but not MEK1/2/ERK1/2 pathways. Our findings imply that insulin can act as a satiety factor in goldfish & inhibit feeding after food intake (probably via glucose uptake) by differential regulation of orexigenic/ anorexigenic signals expressed in brain areas involved in appetite control. In primary culture of goldfish liver cells, insulin expression could be up-regulated by SPX treatment but the opposite was true with SPX immunoneutralization using SPX antiserum. Among the two cognate receptors for SPX, namely GalR2 & GalR3, only the GalR2 was found to be expressed in goldfish liver. In liver cell culture, SPX-induced insulin expression could be negated by the GalR2 but not GalR3 antagonists, and the insulin response caused by SPX was mediated by AC/cAMP/PKA, PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK-II, MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades. Apparently, the MAPK cascades was working downstream of the cAMP/PKA pathway. Since the postprandial signal of insulin is known to stimulate SPX production in goldfish liver, our findings may indicate the presence of a local feedforward loop for signal amplification of SPX in the liver by SPX-induced insulin expression via GalR2 activation. (2) Somatolactin alpha & beta as novel feeding regulators & their regulation in goldfish liver by insulin & SPX In our previous studies, two forms of somatolactin (SL), SL alpha (SLa) & SL beta (SLb), were cloned in goldfish and confirmed to be expressed in the liver. In this study, hepatic expression of SLa & SLb as well as plasma levels of the two isoforms could be up-regulated after food intake or IP injection of insulin in goldfish. Using recombinant goldfish SLa & SLb produced in our lab, IP & ICV injection of the two SLs were both effective in reducing foraging activity & food intake similar to insulin. ICV injection of SLa/b could also induce rapid drops in NPY & AgRP with parallel rises of POMC, CCK, CART & leptin transcripts in brain areas including the telencephalon, hypothalamus & optic tectum. Again, similar results were obtained with SLa/b treatment in goldfish brain cells prepared from these brain areas. These findings imply that SLa & SLb may act as novel satiety signals produced in the liver and contribute to the satiation response of insulin through differential regulation of orexigenic/anorexigenic signals within the CNS. In goldfish, hepatic expression of SLa & SLb mRNA as well as plasma levels of the two SLs were also up-regulated by IP injection with SPX. In goldfish liver cells, insulin & SPX were both effective in elevating SLa & SLb mRNA levels and insulin treatment could also induce phosphorylation of insulin receptor (InsR). Besides, the SL responses caused by insulin were blocked by InsR inactivation/antagonism and insulin-induced SLa & SLb gene expression were mediated by MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways coupled to InsR activation. In our study, immunoneutralization with SPX antiserum in goldfish liver cells could down-regulate SLa & SLb transcripts and SPX-induced SLa & SLb gene expression were mediated by GalR2 activation coupled with PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK-II, MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades. Apparently, the AC/cAMP/PKA pathway was not involved. Furthermore, goldfish liver cells exposed to insulin with concurrent SPX immunoneutralization was found to inhibit the stimulatory effects on SLa & SLb mRNA levels. In parallel experiment, co-treatment of liver cells with insulin & SPX did not further enhance the stimulatory effects of the two stimulants on SLa/b gene expression. These findings suggest that SLa & SLb expression caused by local production of SPX is involved in the SL responses induced by insulin in goldfish liver. (3) Mechanisms for SPX gene transcription induced by insulin & SPX autoregulation at the hepatic level In goldfish liver cells, SPX primary transcript could be up-regulated by insulin parallel to its stimulation on SPX mRNA level and this stimulatory action was negated by InsR inactivation. The rise in SPX primary transcript caused by insulin was mediated by P38MAPK & PI3K/Akt but not MEK/ERK cascades coupled to InsR activation. Using Pol-II ChIP coupled to qPCR for SPX promoter, a rise in Pol-II association with SPX promoter was observed in chromatin samples from goldfish liver cells with insulin treatment. In HEK293 cells transfected with Luc reporter carrying the 5’promoter of SPX gene, insulin treatment could elevate SPX promoter activity and this effect was also sensitive to InsR inactivation and mediated by the P38MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades. Using 5’ deletion of SPX promoter subcloned in the Luc reporter, the insulin-responsive region for promoter activation was mapped to the location from -860 to -700 in the upstream promoter of goldfish SPX gene. These findings imply that InsR activation by insulin in goldfish liver can induce SPX gene transcription via promoter activation mediated by P38MAPK & PI3K/Akt cascades followed by Pol-II recruitment to initiate SPX primary transcript production & subsequent rise in SPX mRNA expression. In goldfish liver cells, besides its stimulatory effects on insulin & SLa/b expression, SPX treatment was also effective in triggering SPX mRNA & primary transcript expression whereas the opposite was true with immunoneutralization using SPX antiserum. In HEK293 cells with stable expression of GalR2 receptor & transfected with the Luc reporter carrying SPX promoter, SPX treatment could also elevate SPX promoter activity similar to insulin. In these two cell models, the stimulatory effects on SPX mature mRNA, primary transcript & promoter activity caused by SPX were all sensitive to GalR2 antagonism and pharmacological blockade of PLC, IP3, PKC, Ca2+ channel, CaM, CaMK-II, PI3K, Akt, MEK1/2, ERK1/2 & P38MAPK but not AC & PKA. These findings suggest that SPX produced locally within goldfish liver can exert a positive feedback on its own production via GalR2 activation coupled to PLC/IP3/PKC, Ca2+/CaM/CaMK-II, MAPK & PI3K/Akt pathways followed by SPX promoter activation & gene transcription. The SPX autoregulation operating at the hepatic level may constitute a second level of signal amplification for insulin-induced SPX expression in the liver of fish model.

17105819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105819.value: In our study using goldfish as an animal model, we have the novel findings that (1) Insulin can act as a satiety factor via central actions in fish model and its expression in the liver can be induced by SPX via GalR2 activation & associated post-receptor signaling, (2) Hepatic expression of SLa & SLb can be induced by SPX produced locally in the liver via similar mechanism for insulin response and act within the brain to inhibit food intake, which also contribute to the postprandial satiation by insulin via insulin-induced SPX expression at hepatic level, (3) The stimulatory effect of insulin on hepatic expression of SPX is mediated by InsR activation and associated post-receptor signaling followed by SPX gene transcription via SPX promoter activation & Pol-II recruitment, and (4) During the process, signal amplification also occurs in the liver by SPX-induced SPX expression via GalR2 activation & downstream signal transduction pathways. Our results, as a whole, have decipher the functional role & underlying mechanisms for the local actions of SPX on insulin & SL expression in the liver during the satiation response by insulin after a meal in a fish model. In the reviewer report for our grant application, a major criticism received was the use of an “uncommon” fish model (i.e., goldfish) but not the well-documented animal models (e.g., mouse) for our SPX project. Therefore, we have also extended our study on feeding control by SPX to the mouse model. At present, we have established the NMR solution structure of mouse SPX & its docking models with its receptor GalR2 & GalR3 and mapped both tissue/cellular expression of SPX using IHC/ICC staining in major organs involved in SPX functions/as targets for SPX regulation. In mice, serum SPX level & SPX mRNA expression in glandular stomach (especially in gastric glands in mucosal layer) could be up-regulated by feeding while IP & ICV injection of SPX were effective in reducing food intake via GalR3 activation & differential regulation of orexigenic/anorexigenic factors expressed in the hypothalamus. In mucosal gastric cells prepared from mouse glandular stomach, SPX expression could be induced by glucose but the effect was blocked by insulin via different signal transduction mechanisms. Our findings for the first time demonstrate that the role of SPX as a satiety factor is well-conserved from fish to mammals but with involvement of different tissues, SPX receptors & endocrine signaling.

17105819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17105819.value: In our promoter study with HEK293 cells, insulin could induce SPX promoter activation via the responsive region covering -860 to -700 of the SPX promoter. The functional role of cis-acting elements found within this region in mediating insulin action & coupling to signalling pathways is unclear and further investigation is clearly warranted. In our study with goldfish liver cells, we also have the novel finding that insulin could differentially regulate the two forms of IGF expressed at hepatic level, with stimulation on IGF-I but inhibition on IGF-II expression. Given that (i) the liver represents the major site for IGF production and (ii) IGF & insulin are known to have cross-reactivity at the receptor level, we suspect that local production of IGF-I can also play a role on SPX & SLa/b expression in the liver and their subsequent release into systemic circulation for sure will have an impact on feeding regulation in goldfish. We are now in the process of testing the effect of food intake on plasma level of IGF-I & hepatic expression of IGF-I. After that, we will examine the effects of IGF-I treatment on SPX & SLa/b expression in our liver cell culture.

17105819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17105819.value: Our study made use of the goldfish and mice as animal models to examine the novel mechanisms involved in feeding control by SPX triggered by food intake. In goldfish, the postprandial signal of insulin can induce local production of SPX to up-regulate hepatic expression of SLa & SLa, which can then act together with SPX & insulin via central actions to inhibit foraging activity & food consumption. During the process, two steps of signal amplification via (i) SPX-induced insulin expression and (ii) SPX-induced SPX expression also occurs at the hepatic level to further enhance SPX output from the liver. In mouse model, postprandial rise in SPX signal originated from the glandular stomach but not the liver can be observed and SPX is also effective in inhibiting food intake via central actions within the hypothalamus. The SPX response occurring in gastric glands within the glandular stomach is induced by glucose uptake after feeding and can be inhibited by the subsequent rise in insulin signal. Our results indicate that the role of SPX as a satiety factor is well-conserved from fish to mammals but the tissue involved & underlying mechanisms can be quite different.

17105919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17105919.value: 轉移可導致超過90%的腫瘤患者死亡，而揭示其潛在的作用機制則具有極高的科學意義和治療意義。值得注意的是，在轉移的過程中其效率極低，僅有不足0.01%的瀰散腫瘤細胞能夠在靶組織中定植。但這些極少數的腫瘤細胞是如何獲得轉移能力的疑問仍困擾著人們。轉移的第一個關鍵步驟是能夠成功地黏附至靶組織，而目前對這一過程起決定性作用的因子仍知之甚少。此外，腫瘤細胞必須建立一個良好的腫瘤微環境以便於腫瘤細胞定植靶組織，而促進轉移定植成功的因素仍有待挖掘。 為了克服傳統研究方法的局限性並建立一個可靠的能揭示轉移關鍵因子的體系，我們建立了一個具有不同轉移屬性的新型等基因卵巢癌模型。在我們的初步研究中，高轉移能力的腫瘤細胞(HM)可選擇性地激活腹膜間皮並營造一個適合轉移的微環境，而不具備轉移能力的腫瘤細胞(NM)則沒有出現該現象。P-鈣黏素是一種在HM腫瘤細胞中處於激活狀態的細胞黏附分子並在晚期腫瘤和腹膜轉移中都有出現。重要的是，P-鈣黏素，而非其他鈣黏素，在這些過程中扮演著不可或缺的角色。激活的腹膜間皮可以支持腫瘤細胞的生長並形成一個正反饋回路。脂肪生成是卵巢癌細胞一個獨特的特徵，我們進一步發現間皮中的脂肪生成被改變而且糖酵解有所增強。我們的基因組分析及病理學研究也進一步在體內證實了該變化。雖然P-鈣黏素被認為在器官特異性轉移中有起到一定的作用，但它在轉移定植方面尚未有報導。更重要的是，P-鈣黏素在介導轉移過程中激活微環境的潛在作用尚未清晰。我們是第一個闡明P-鈣黏素在代謝重編程中的關鍵調節作用，並揭示它在卵巢癌和間皮細胞之間的一個標誌性作用以及之前未被探索的相互依賴性。我們猜想P-鈣黏素可通過激活微環境和代謝耦合從而促進有效的轉移。 基於體內外的實驗，我們将展开以下研究: (1) 闡明P-鈣黏素誘導的HM在激活微環境中的確切作用以及相互之間的作用是如何影響腫瘤的發生; (2) 破譯代謝耦聯的分子機制，尤其是糖酵解和脂肪生成; (3) 揭示P-鈣黏素在轉移定植中的作用機制。 我們的研究將為了解P-鈣黏素在腫瘤進展中致癌性作用提供新的方向，並揭示生長優勢和代謝依賴性導致轉移成功的重要機制。

17105919.label: Realisation of objectives
17105919.value: Objective 1: To date, there is no study assessing the direct function of P-cadherin in the establishment of the metastatic niche. Using the well-controlled HM and NM of different metastatic propensities and a coculture model, we showed for the first time that metastasis-competent HM but not metastasis-incompetent NM adhered more to the mesothelium and could selectively activate the mesothelium. P-cadherin, but not other cadherins, was specifically required. HM cells activated the secretion of tumor-promoting factors, such as G-CSF, GM-CSF, IL-6, IL-8, CXCL1/GROα, and IL-1α/IL-1F1, but not NM cells. We further showed that there was a strong induction of N-cadherin and fibronectin genes upon HM-mesothelium coculture. Similar results were found using human primary mesothelial cells. The mesothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and peritoneal fibrogenesis further reinforce the metastatic process. We further studied the requirement of P-cadherin and its downstream effectors FASN, MCT1 and MCT4 in vivo using xenografts in mice. Their localization and expression closely correlated with clinicopathologic features in patients’ tumor samples. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 2: How metabolic changes may affect the metastatic process is poorly understood. Here, we found that P-cadherin rewired lipid metabolism in tutor cells. This is further supported by the expression of lipogenesis genes (ACLY, FASN, ACAT2, Lipin 1, SREBP1), oil Red O staining, and bioenergetic metabolism. Using 5-(tetradecyloxy)-2-furoic acid, a competitive acetyl-CoA carboxylase inhibitor, which is an essential enzyme in the synthesis of fatty acids, we showed that the neutral lipids were produced by de novo lipogenesis rather than being transferred from the extracellular environment. We further showed that lactate acid which was produced via glycolysis was shuttled from activated mesothelium to tumor cells as a lipid source and survival nutrients. Using 13C6-glucose-based targeted lipidomic analysis alone and in combination with the lactate importer (MCT1) inhibitor, we confirmed that lactate shuttling from the activated mesothelium to HM is essential for tumor lipogenesis. Using lipodomics, we further identified novel P-cadherin activation mediated-metabolic paths. It is also clinically relevant that high expression of MCT1 is associated with poor overall and progression-free survival in ovarian cancer patients. Targeting lactate shuttling or blocking P-cadherin-mediated tumor-mesothelium crosstalk may be a promising therapeutic strategy for peritoneal metastasis. Percentage achieved: 100% Objective 3: In search of the underlying mechanisms, we found that expression of P-cadherin could induce membrane translocation of Dvl-2, suggesting that in addition to its adhesive function, P-cadherin may transduce active signals that support lipogenesis and HM growth. We further showed the involvement of Ca2+ singling in the P-cadherin-mediated singling cascade, and the possible involvement of protein kinase Cα/bII and PKD/PKCu. We further studied the downstream signals and decipher their regulation by P-cadherin in the tumor microenvironment. HGF, which is abundant in the malignant ascites, upregulated P-cadherin levels at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels. We further showed that biophysical cues could activate P-cadherin signaling. We found that metastatic cells in physical contact with mesothelial cells possessed significantly larger rupture forces as compared to non-metastatic cells. P-cadherin regulated SREBP1 in an O-GlcNAcylation-dependent manner, a widespread posttranslational modification that acts as an important sensor of metabolic state. Percentage achieved: 100% These findings not only reveal a previously unrecognized role for P-cadherin in metastatic niche activation, but also unveil a novel role for P-cadherin as a key regulator of metabolic reprogramming, which has been recognized as the prime driving event in almost all hallmarks of cancer. As such, our findings introduce a new dimension to our existing knowledge on the oncogenic roles of P-cadherin in tumor progression and that the targeting of P-cadherin and its signaling molecules that remain to be explored by which may represent more precise targets with potential therapeutic advantage for metastatic ovarian cancer. 17105919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17105919.value: Objective 1: Here, using cancerous tissues and isogenic ovarian cancer cell models with opposite metastatic abilities, whose growth and metastasis patterns were similar to those observed in human ovarian cancer, we provide the first evidence that during peritoneal colonization, P-cadherin, but not other cadherins, in metastatic cancer cells plays specific roles in activating the niche and establishing metabolic coupling with the mesothelium. The metabolic reprogramming is essential for tumor cell proliferation, facilitating metastatic outgrowth. Notably, we also observed enhanced P-cadherin expression in ascitic tumor cells derived from ovarian cancer patients as compared to normal ovarian surface epithelium. Our in vivo experiments together with patient samples, strongly support the clinical importance of our proposed mechanisms in ovarian cancer. Publication: Journal article: #1, 2 Conference proceeding: #6 Objective 2: Transcriptomic and molecular analyses demonstrated that P-cadherin upregulated lipogenesis in HM cells. Intriguingly, P-cadherin did not affect lipogenic activity but instead promoted glycolysis in the interacting mesothelium. Targeted lipidomic analysis showed that lactate, produced by the glycolytic mesothelium, could directly serve as a substrate for lipogenesis in HM cells. The additional lipids are produced through de novo lipogenesis instead of being transferred from the extracellular environment. The enhanced phospholipid subspecies may facilitate HM proliferation upon mesothelial activation. Inhibiting MCT1/4-mediated lactate shuttling significantly reduced metastasis in mice. Kaplan-Meier curves also showed that specific MCT1/4-targeting displayed prolonged survival. Publication: Journal article: #1-3 Conference proceeding: #5, 6 Patent: 7 Objective 3: To explore the molecular mechanisms of P-cadherin in promoting tumor-mesothelium metabolic coupling, we identified membrane translocation of Dvl-2, suggesting that in addition to its adhesive function, P-cadherin may transduce active signals that support lipogenesis and HM growth. We further showed the involvement of Ca2+ singling in the P-cadherin-mediated singling cascade, and the possible involvement of protein kinase Cα/bII and PKD/PKCu. HGF, which is abundant in the malignant ascites, but not EGF or TNF, could upregulate P-cadherin levels at both transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels by enhancing its mRNA and protein stability respectively. We further showed that P-cadherin can establish a connection between cell adhesion mechanics and metabolic reprogramming in the metastatic niche. SREBP1, serves as an important mechanosensor that leads to lipid synthesis in metastatic cancer cells. O-GlcNAcylation, a widespread posttranslational modification, is linked to P-cadherin mediated SREBP1 regulation and lipogenesis. Publication: Journal article: #1-3 Conference proceedings: #4-6 Taken together, our findings not only shed new light on a new direction for understanding the oncogenic roles of P-cadherin in ovarian cancer, but may also be extended to other cancers with inappropriate activation of P-cadherin such as gastric, pancreatic, and colon cancer. Targeting of P-cadherin or its downstream signaling in this tumor-mesothelium interaction represents a promising strategy of novel microenvironmental regulation of cellular signals in metastasis, and at the same time minimize the adverse side effects and treatment resistance caused by only targeting tumor cells. Publication: Journal article: #1-3 Conference proceedings: #4-6 Patent: #7

17105919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17105919.value: We reveal a new direction for understanding the oncogenic role of P-cadherin in ovarian cancer metastasis and implicate that P-cadherin could be a promising therapeutic target. We have demonstrated the use of siRNA to efficiently and specifically downregulate MCT4 in the peritoneal mesothelium. However, one major limitation is targeted delivery of siRNA in vivo. We have developed vesicle-like nanostructures based on dendrimers as effective carriers for siRNA delivery in novel RNAi therapeutic applications. The peritoneal dissemination may in fact offer a clinical advantage in that therapeutic genes may be sensitive and specific to target cells in the peritoneal cavity. We are actively pursuing in this direction. In our pilot study, we show the potential of therapeutic targeting with a clinical grade MCT1 inhibitor AZD3965, which significantly reduced metastasis in mice. We will continue to unravel the underlying mechanisms of action and explore its development with rationally designed drug combinations. P-cadherin is also overexpressed in patients with gastric, pancreatic and colon cancer. We will expand our findings by exploring these other tumor types. These findings should highlight the functional importance of P-cadherin in impacting aggressive malignant cell behavior and implies important clinical implications.

17105919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17105919.value: One of the greatest unmet needs compromising the successful treatment of cancer is metastasis. No effective therapy is currently available, with a poor 5-year survival rate (<25%). Thus, there is a need for new therapeutic targets and a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying the progression of ovarian cancer. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer and that it could be a promising therapeutic target. (i) We show for the first time a new connection between cell adhesion and metabolic coupling at the metastatic niche via P-cadherin. (ii) We also present evidence suggesting the mesothelium has an enhanced glycolysis, which metabolically support the tumor growth via lipogenesis. (iii) We identify SREBP1, a master regulator of lipogenesis, is a specific and novel P-cadherin target that may underlie the lipogenesis, metastasis, and poor outcome in ovarian cancer. These results reveal a new direction for understanding the oncogenic roles of P-cadherin and highlight its importance as a viable therapeutic target. Targeting P-cadherin mediated metabolic coupling may thus be a useful approach to restrain ovarian cancer metastasis.

17106619.value: 研究背景： 由於功能和美學原因，越來越多的成年人正在尋求牙齒矯正治療，同時他們中的許多人患有牙周炎。為了最大限度地降低潛在的風險，在通過牙周治療成功控制所有牙周炎症之前，不能開始矯正治療。然而，治療後的牙周組織是否完全從從炎症狀態恢復，尚不確定。因此，牙周炎患者的牙齒矯正治療必須謹慎。相比于健康的牙齒矯正患者，牙周炎患者的矯正治療方式和治療目標應簡單化 。在最壞的情況下，患者的牙周情況會受到進一步的炎症刺激。 關鍵問題 我們之前GRF資助的項目研究了炎症對機械負荷下牙周膜細胞的影響。使用體外模型對健康細胞施加炎症刺激，我們發現持續的炎症與機械負荷導致骨重塑失調和組織破壞，並證明瞭EphA2-ephrinA2和EphB4-ephrinB2信號通路在調節機械和炎症刺激下的牙周組織信號通路中起關鍵作用。 牙周治療後炎症的牙周組織是否從先前的炎症狀態中恢復，這個過程是如何調節的？為了回答這個問題，僅通過對體外模型的健康細胞施加炎性刺激來模擬炎症是不夠的。我們需要一種更準確地體現臨床情況的模型。 Eph-ephrin信號在炎症狀態恢復的牙周組織中的作用是什麼？理解這一過程將使我們能夠操控Eph-ephrin信號，從而使炎症的牙周組織更有效和更可靠地恢復。 研究目的 本研究的目的旨在i) 研究治療後的牙周組織對進一步炎症刺激的抵禦能力和Eph-ephrin信號通路在此過程中的介導作用，ii) 研究機械負荷下治療後的牙周組織的骨重塑以及Eph-ephrin信號通路在此過程中的介導作用，iii) 探索幹預Eph-ephrin信號是否可以增強治療後牙周組織對炎症的抵禦能力，並調節其在機械負荷的骨重塑過程。 研究意義 此研究使用體外和體內模型以更好地類比不同牙周狀況的臨床情況，並研究牙周組織中的Eph-ephrin雙向信號通路傳導。基於Eph-ephrin信號通路的幹預可以為牙周炎患者提供安全有效的牙齒移動的新治療策略。

17106719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17106719.value: People with schizophrenia are susceptible to cardiovascular diseases, resulting in excess morbidity and mortality, but the mortality gap did not improve but appears to be widening with time. Accumulating evidence attributes the disproportionate burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD) to the disparities in the management of CVD risk factors in health care setting. Antipsychotic drugs are known to be associated with risk of CVD, but studies have shown that people with schizophrenia are under-recognised and under-treated for its risk factors. This proposed study will develop a risk prediction model of CVD by considering additional psychiatric risk factors and subsequently use the risk model to determine how treatment at different CVD risk levels may affect the outcome and healthcare cost. Study data will be drawn from the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS) of the Hong Kong Hospital Authority. We will identify a cohort of patients with schizophrenia who have received antipsychotic treatment between January 2001 and December 2018. The study has four objectives. First, we will develop a risk prediction model that estimates the absolute 10-year CVD risk, taking in account antipsychotic treatment as an additional risk factor. The performance of the risk model will be compared with the recalibrated Framingham general cardiovascular risk model. Second, we will investigate whether antiplatelet, lipid-lowering, and antihypertensive treatment reduce fatal or non-fatal CVD event. Time-dependent Cox proportional hazards models will be applied to calculate the hazard ratios for the first cardiovascular event comparing patients on early, late, and no treatment. Third, we will examine whether different service parameters such as service referral and number of clinical consultation influence the patient outcome. Last, in view of the potential increase in healthcare cost associated with psychiatric comorbidities, a cost analysis will be performed to compare healthcare cost between patients comorbid with schizophrenia and CVD and patients with schizophrenia only. We will also examine whether timely treatment of CVD risk factors reduces overall healthcare cost. In summary, this proposed study provide valuable information about the role of healthcare services in determining the cardiovascular outcome in patients with schizophrenia. 精神分裂症患者有較大機會患上心血管疾病，並因此引致過高的發病率和死亡率。這死亡率差距並未隨著時間而改善，反而似正在擴闊。愈來愈多證據表明不成比例的心血管疾病負擔源於醫護環境下管理心血管疾病風險因素的差異。我們知道抗精神病藥物會增加精神分裂症患者患上心血管疾病的風險，但研究顯示這風險並未被充分認知和治療。此研究項目擬建立一個新的心血管疾病風險預測模型，當中會考慮精神健康相關的因素，並會利用新的模型探討治療不同程度心血管疾病風險因素如何影響結果和醫療成本。此研究會在香港醫院管理局的臨床數據分析及報告系統提取研究數據。我們會挑選在2001年1月至2018年12月期間曾接受過抗精神病藥物治療的精神分裂症患者為研究對象。此項目有四個目標。第一，我們會因應服用抗精神病藥物治療而可能引起的風險，建立一個十年內心血管疾病發病的風險預測模型。我們會比較新風險預測模型的表現是否與弗雷明漢心血管疾病重新校準風險模型不同。 其次，我們將研究抗血小板藥物、降血脂藥物，和抗高血壓藥物是否可以減少致命或非致命的心血管事件。我們會以時間相依共變數Cox存活分析計算患者在早期、晚期，或沒有接受治療情況下第一次發生心血管事件的危險率。第三，我們將探討不同的服務參數，如服務轉介和臨床諮詢次數，會否影響患者的結果。最後，鑑於醫療成本可能與精神病合併症相關，我們會分析有心血管合併症和沒有心血管合併症的精神分裂症患者的醫療成本。我們亦會探討及時干預心血管風險會否減低醫療成本。總括而言，這研究項目所提供的資料有助我們了解醫療服務如何影響精神分裂症患者的心血管疾病結果。

17106719.label: Realisation of objectives
17106719.value: We have achieved 100% of objective 1, the key objective and basis for subsequent objectives, opening a new area of research that is potentially impactful for addressing inequity in health among people with schizophrenia. We have nearly but not fully achieved objectives 2 to 4, due to a delay in data retrieval during COVID-19 outbreak (as data retrieval had to be done in hospital and the process has been disrupted). As noted in our mid-term report, the problem has been addressed, and we have completed all data retrieval, with an expected delay in results analyses and publications. A manuscript has been submitted to a prestigious journal based on our findings with objective 1, and the team is continuing to work on further analyses with planned publications, in which the support of RGC will be duly acknowledged. Details of the research activities (as stated in the proposal) in relation to achieving the project objectives as follow: • Data retrieval (100% completed) • Data cleaning and processing (100% completed) • Data analysis (80% completed) Data analysis for achieving objective 1 has been completed, and the key findings have been prepared. In brief, we have identified additional risk factors for predicting CVD in patients with schizophrenia, in addition to known CVD risk factors in other populations. The newly identified risk factors include antipsychotic medications, duration of schizophrenia, and psychiatric comorbidities. Building on this risk prediction model [model 1], we are developing further models to address the remaining objectives: 2. Estimating the impact of hypertension and diabetes treatment (the two significant CVD risk factors in our model, considering psychiatric risk factors) in affecting the risk of developing non-fatal and fatal CVD events. 3. Test for dose-response relationship between service use (outpatient consultation, inpatient, medication) for hypertension and diabetes treatment and the development of non-fatal and fatal CVD events. 4. Attach monetary value to model 3 (direct cost and disability-adjusted life years) for estimating the costs of early hypertension and diabetes treatment in preventing/delaying non-fatal and fatal CVD events. With completion of model 1, the remaining analyses are relatively straightforward, which explains the reason we consider objective 2, 3, and 4 to be 95%, 90%, and 85% completed, respectively. The project team is targeting to complete all analyses in the next 3 months.

17106719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17106719.value: Our results showed that first-generation antipsychotics (FGA), longer duration of schizophrenia, and substance use disorder were associated with incident CVD. Baseline prescriptions of chlorpromazine and trifluoperazine in men were associated with higher CVD risk. Psychiatric variables might influence younger and middle-aged adults more than older patients. Our study demonstrated that psychiatric factors were useful predictors in CVD risk models: - We observed a positive association between FGA prescription at baseline and incident CVD, even after controlling for effects of baseline comorbidities and duration of schizophrenia. The potential medication treatment effect on cardiovascular outcome could not be ruled out. - To further clarify the association, we analyzed individual FGA and found baseline prescription of chlorpromazine and trifluoperazine in male patients seemed to increase their risk of CVD. - We also found that substance use disorder predicted incident CVD. - Illness duration for 2 years or more significantly predicted higher CVD risk, adjusting for the effect of age. - Subgroup analysis also found that younger and middle-aged patients were found to have higher CVD risk associated with longer illness duration. - Long-term stressful psychotic experiences might disrupt cardiac autonomic function.

17106719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17106719.value: This study made use of clinical information available from electronic health records to identify psychiatric risk factors in addition to other known risk factors for non-fatal and fatal CVD events. Our findings support several further research developments: 1. prospective observational studies to further test and provide evidence of the psychiatric risk factors for CVD 2. clinical trials on the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of early treatment of CVD risk factors in patients with schizophrenia, considering psychiatric risks 3. multinational (comparative or data linkage) electronic health record studies to understand generalisability of the psychiatric risk factors and effects of early treatment

17106719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17106719.value: In the general population, there are well-known risk factors for major cardiovascular problems, such as high blood pressure and diabetes for increasing the risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and heart failure. People with schizophrenia are known to be more likely to experience major cardiovascular problems, and are more likely to die because of them. Using anonymised electronic health record data from over 39,000 people with schizophrenia in Hong Kong over 11 years, we are able to find out if people with schizophrenia have additional risk factors on top of the well-known risk factors. These additional risk factors include use of 'older' antipsychotics, longer duration of schizophrenia, and substance use, especially in younger and middle-aged person with schizophrenia. These findings provided insight into identifying high-risk group of people in whom early intervention may be particularly important in preventing the development of major cardiovascular problems and related premature death.

17107019.label: Project Objectives
17107019.value: To characterize the molecular basis of the replication of DelNS1 viruses derived from influenza A (H5N1, 2009 H1N1 and 2013 H7N9 backbone) and influenza B strains. We found that these strains require different adaptive mutations to those previously identified in DelNS1 WSN and PR8 strains in order to support virus replication in the absence of the NS1 gene. Characterization of the molecular basis of how these adaptive mutations facilitate replication of these strains will be important for understanding the role of NS1 in influenza viruses with different genetic backgrounds. Characterization of genome wide transcriptional responses in cells infected with DelNS1 and corresponding wild type viruses. This part of the study will provide a comprehensive analysis of host gene expression in response to influenza viruses of different pathogenic backgrounds, with and without expression of the NS1 protein, using RNA-seq technology. The specific focus will be on modulation of gene expression by NS1 through epigenetic mechanisms. To characterize differential immune responses in mice infected with DelNS1 or wild type viruses. A comprehensive profile of the effects of the presence or absence of the NS1 protein on immune responses related to induction of adaptive immunity during primary infection will be compiled. The study will be focused on mechanisms related to immune responses leading to cross protective immunity induced by DelNS1 live attenuated viruses.

17107019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107019.value: 流感病毒是一種與人類疾病負擔和引起大流行的潛在相關的呼吸道病原體。不同的流感病毒株之間的毒力不同;有些只引起輕度疾病，但感染其他一些菌株可能導致嚴重或致命的後果。目前的流感疫苗不理想，所以必須採取新的策略來開發針對季節性流感和潛在的未來流行病的更有效，交叉保護和持久有效的流感疫苗。開發無毒和更具免疫原性的減毒活流感疫苗是其中一個方向。甲型流感病毒的非結構性（NS1）蛋白是病毒致病力的關鍵因子，在病毒感染中具有多種功能。除了其拮抗宿主抗病毒反應的基本功能外，NS1蛋白還參與病毒複​​製的調節。然而，目前尚不清楚NS1蛋白如何參與病毒基因組轉錄和復制，部分原因是NS1缺失（DelNS1）病毒的複制能力差限制了它們在功能研究中的用途。雖然先前已提出利用敲除NS1製備DelNS1減毒活流感疫苗，但此類DelNS1病毒無法在常規疫苗生產系統中復制，阻礙了對DelNS1病毒潛在應用的進一步評估。 我們已經建立並擴展了我們以前涉及DelNS1病毒的研究，並成功開發了一組DelNS1病毒，包括WSN（H1N1），PR8（H1N1），CA04（2009 H1N1），1194（H5N1），ZJ1（ H7N9），HK4801（H3N2）和一種乙型流感病毒。更重要的是，我們鑑定了允許複製這些DelNS1病毒繁殖的適應性突變，其中適應的DelNS1病毒在雞胚和MDCK或VERO細胞中幾乎完全恢復了複製能力，但這些DelNS1病毒失去了抗乾擾素表達的抑制能力并表現在對小鼠感染無毒性。儘管以前已廣泛研究了NS1蛋白與宿主因子之間的相互作用，但尚未對敲除NS1蛋白的情況下對來自不同致病背景的流感病毒的全基因組宿主應答進行綜合評估。這些數據將為在病毒感染期間NS1完整功能提供有價值的信息。此外，由於我們的初步研究表明在動物實驗中DelNS1病毒比同類商業疫苗具有更廣譜的交叉保護作用，因此鑑定宿主對DelNS1病毒感染的反應非常重要，研究將最終提供更有效的疫苗開發方法和研發更具交叉保護性的流感疫苗。

17107019.label: Realisation of objectives
17107019.value: The proposed objectives in the original application have been fully addressed through our comprehensive research plan. We have accomplished all the objectives and achieved the following milestones in this project: 1. This project builds upon our previous study, which identified adaptive mutations that support replication of WSN(H1N1) and PR8 (H1N1) strains with NS1 deletion in the viral genome. We further constructed and characterized DelNS1 live attenuated influenza viruses (LAIV) from other strains, including 2009 H1N1, H5N1, H7N9, and influenza B viruses. Notably, we discovered that different influenza virus strains require distinct adaptive mutations to support virus replication in MDCK cells or chicken embryonated eggs. We found that these DelNS1 LAIVs share similar properties, such as a preference for replication at lower temperatures (33°C) and causing no disease in animals. The avirulent nature of DelNS1 LAIV makes it an ideal vaccine candidate for influenza and a viral vector for expressing antigens from other viruses, such as coronaviruses. We have established a panel of DelNS1 LAIV viral vectors that cover seasonal and emerging influenza viruses, which can be used for producing vaccine candidates for seasonal flu and emerging influenza viruses. 2. To address the second objective in this study, we hypothesized that the expression of the NS1 protein reprograms the host cell's immune response to influenza virus infection. We conducted a series of experiments to characterize how and to what extent the NS1 protein regulates host cell gene expression. To understand the functions of the NS1, we created different variants containing either deletion of the NS1 or a mutant NS1 that is unable to translocate to the nucleus. We employed RNA-seq to analyze host cell expression after infection with WT and different NS1 variants (deleted NS1 or functional mutated) of the influenza virus. Among many differentially expressed genes identified, we discovered a novel expression of microRNA, miR146a, from WT influenza virus but not from DelNS1 LAIV. miR146a has multiple roles in controlling innate and adaptive immune processes. We found that miR146a expression is crucial for influenza virus replication and is induced by the NS1 protein. Our study further characterized that the induction of miR146a is associated with nuclear NS1, as an NS1 mutant that cannot be translocated to the nucleus fails to induce miR146a expression in virus-infected cells. To understand how NS1 activates miR146a expression, this project used multiple variants of NS1 mutants to infect cells and conduct epigenetic analysis. We discovered that nuclear NS1 regulates host gene expression through interaction with the Pol II complex. Through a complex analysis combining different technologies, we found that the NS1 protein interacts with the RNA transcription complex and causes readthrough of transcription to induce miR146a expression. This finding provides crucial information for understanding the molecular basis of NS1's role in immune modulation during influenza virus infection and sheds light on the function of NS1 in the nucleus during the early hours of infection. 3. In Objective 3, this study aimed to characterize the differential immune response induced by wild-type and DelNS1 influenza viruses in animal models. Since we have successfully established different strains of DelNS1 LAIV, we were able to conduct experiments using these attenuated viruses grown in MDCK cells. We found that the DelNS1 virus is replication-deficient in vivo but induces a massive type I interferon response and cytokine/chemokine expression in the airway and lung tissues. On the other hand, depletion of macrophages was observed in animals infected with wild-type influenza virus but not with DelNS1 LAIV. Furthermore, we revealed that the unique pulmonary inflammatory environment induced by the DelNS1 virus skews the preferential migration of CD103+ dendritic cells into draining lymph nodes. CD103+ dendritic cells have been established to cross-present antigens to prime CD8+ T cells, and a skewed presence of cDC1 in the lymph nodes during the priming phase suggests heightened stimulation of CD8+ T cells. Our study, using single-cell analysis, confirmed that there is a skewed migration of CD103+ dendritic cells in the draining lymph nodes of DelNS1-infected mice. We further characterized that the DelNS1 virus leads to a significant generation and deposition of tissue resident CD8+ memory T cells in the lungs and upper respiratory tract. Finally, we found that CD8 memory T cells in the lungs expand massively upon heterologous influenza challenge, resulting in controlled viral replication and suppressed pulmonary inflammation. These findings provide strong support that DelNS1 LAIV is an ideal immunogen and can serve as a better vaccine for influenza. Using DelNS1 LAIV as a viral vector, we have successfully constructed DelNS1-RBD LAIV for SARS-CoV-2 infection. One vaccine made from the DelNS1-RBD LAIV was evaluated in clinical trials and approved for emergency use in mainland China. Our research lays a solid foundation for further development of DelNS1 LAIV as a vaccine vector for influenza and other respiratory viruses.

17107019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17107019.value: We have achieved following major findings in this project: 1. We established a panel influenza viral vector with deletion of the NS1 (DelNS1) and characterized adaptative mutations which support replication of the DelNS1 live attenuated virus in vaccine production cells. Successfully culture of influenza virus with deletion of the NS1 has significant impact on influenza virus research and development of novel vaccine for influenza. Several patents have been granted or filed based on these findings. (Peer-reviewed article No 1, other impact-patent 1 and 2). 2. To understand the biological significance of the NS1 in influenza virus life cycle, we have thoroughly explored functions of the nuclear NS1 and characterized molecular basis of the NS1 in epigenetic modulation of host gene expression. Significantly we identified miR-146a microRNA as an important factor for influenza virus replication in infected cells and expression of miR-146a is regulated by the NS1 through epigenetic mechanism. We further characterized that the nuclear NS1 interacts with chromatin and leads to the transcription readthrough for activation expression of the miR146a (Recognized international conferences: 1,3,4 & 5, publications of these studies are in the processes of submission or preparation). 3. This project analyzed immunological profiles of immune response induced by wild type and DelNS1 influenza viruses and provided direct evidence to show that influenza virus utilizes the NS1 to modulate innate and adaptative immunity for influenza infection and DelNS1 LAIV is a perfect vaccine (Peer-reviewed article: 2, 6 and recognized international conference:2). 4. We have successfully made DelNS1 LAIV a viral vector for expressing antigens from SARS-CoV-2 and characterized DelNS1-RBD immunogenicity and protection of virus challenged animals. Our study demonstrated that DelNS1-RBD LAIV induces mucosal immunity targeting virus infection in airway and prevent virus replication and transmission. We, for the first time, showed influenza virus with deletion of the NS1 can be used a vaccine vector. The DelNS1-RBD LAIV was awarded the highest award of Gold Medal with Congratulations of the Jury in Special Edition 2021 Inventions Geneva Evaluation Days. One of the DelNS1-RBD LAIV vaccines has been evaluated in clinical trials and approved for human use in mainland China (Peer reviewed article: 2, 5 and 6; Recognized international conferences: 3; other impact: No 1).

17107019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17107019.value: This is a long-term project and we have been continuing characterization of the DelNS1 LAIV system, our further research focuses on following areas: 1. We are working on the optimization of DelNS1 LAIV for seasonal influenza vaccines and conducting human trials in collaboration with industrial partners. Currently, two vaccine companies are working with us to produce seasonal vaccines for clinical trials. 2. Our goal is to further engineer DelNS1 LAIV as a vector for other respiratory viruses. We have created DelNS1-RBD LAIV for COVID-19, and the vaccine has been approved for emergency use in mainland China. We are also testing DelNS1-RSV vaccine candidates. Due to its high safety profile, DelNS1 LAIV is an extremely valuable viral vector for developing next-generation vaccines, particularly for intranasal vaccination to induce mucosal immunity. DelNS1 LAIV is the only system that can provide a combined vaccine to prevent both influenza and other respiratory viral infections. 3. We will continue our immunological characterization of DelNS1 LAIV in different hosts. Findings from our study on DelNS1 LAIV will provide critical information for understanding immune evasion strategies employed by human viruses.

17107019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17107019.value: Respiratory viruses, like the flu, can repeatedly infect people. How do they manage to avoid our immune system's memory? One reason is that the viruses mutate. All successful human viruses have developed unique ways to trick our immune system, making it hard for us to develop long-lasting protection against them. We thought the NS1 part of the flu virus might be responsible for this. To test our idea, we removed the NS1 from the flu virus, creating a group of weakened viruses called DelNS1 live attenuated viruses, with deletion of the NS1 from viral genome. These can be used as vaccines for regular flu and new flu strains. Our study showed that our idea was right: DelNS1 LAIV provides better and longer-lasting protection (by activating memory T cells) than the regular flu virus. What's more, we found out that DelNS1 LAIV can be used to make vaccines for other respiratory viruses too. We successfully created a vaccine that includes a part of the SARS-CoV-2 virus (the virus that causes COVID-19). This vaccine went through clinical trials and was approved for use in mainland China. In short, DelNS1 LAIV is a new way to make vaccines for the flu and other respiratory illnesses.

17107219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17107219.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is highly prevalent worldwide and locally. It evolves through two major genetic pathways: the adenoma-carcinoma sequence and the serrated neoplasia pathway. The serrated neoplasia pathway accounts for ~20–30% of CRC, usually beginning with BRAF V600E or KRAS mutation as the early event, followed by extensive methylation of CpG islands (CpG Island methylation phenotype, CIMP). Tumors can be either microsatellite unstable (MSI) or microsatellite stable (MSS), with MSS serrated CRCs having a poorer prognosis. Therefore, identification of biomarkers and therapeutic targets are urgently needed. Most of the available transcriptome profiling studies on CRC patient stratification have been based on bulk frozen tumor tissues, for which data analysis was confounded by tumor purity and stromal components. Moreover, those studies did not take into consideration the intra-tumor heterogeneity which inherently exists within the tumor tissue of an individual and leads to tumor recurrence and drug resistance. Three-dimensional culture of tumor organoids has recently emerged as a robust representation of an in vivo tumor. This preclinical in vitro model containing purely the cancer epithelial cells, highly recapitulates the in vivo tumor, and is ideal for studying cellular heterogeneity and for molecular profiling. We have established a unique organoid cohort derived from local CRC patients. In particular, this cohort is enriched with organoids along the serrated neoplasia pathway, from pre-neoplastic to carcinoma to metastatic lesions, and they represent the most aggressive subtype of CRC with the worst clinical outcome. We have delineated their genomic landscapes via whole-exome sequencing. In this proposal, we aim to understand the intra-tumor heterogeneity and clonal evolution of serrated colorectal neoplasia using a single-cell RNA sequencing approach. Through an in-depth bioinformatic analysis integrated with genomic mutation data, we aim to identify cancer cell origin gene expression signatures for metastasis and pathogenesis of serrated neoplasia, followed by validation using publicly available datasets. Finally, we will generate a panel of clonal organoids representing different subpopulations essential for metastasis and with differential pathogenic potential. The clonal organoid lines will be an essential disease modelling and drug testing platform for the study and treatment of serrated colorectal neoplasia. 結直腸癌（CRC）在當地乃至世界範圍內都非常普遍。它通過兩個主要的遺傳途徑演變而來：腺瘤 - 癌途徑和鋸齒狀瘤途徑。鋸齒狀瘤形成通路通常佔CRC的約20-30％，以BRAF V600E或KRAS突變作為起始事件，隨後發生CpG島的廣泛甲基化（CpG島甲基化表型，CIMP）。腫瘤亞型可以是微衛星不穩定型（MSI）或微衛星穩定型（MSS），而MSS亞型的鋸齒狀CRC則具有較差的預後。因此，臨床上迫切需要鑑定其生物標誌物和治療靶點。大多數可用的關於CRC患者分型的轉錄組數據是基於冷凍的腫瘤組織，其分析結果容易受到腫瘤純度和間充質成分的影響。而且，這些研究沒有考慮到腫瘤內的異質性，它固有地存在於腫瘤組織內並最終導致腫瘤的複發和耐藥性。腫瘤類器官的三維培養於近年呈現出表徵體內腫瘤的穩健特性。這個臨床前的體內模型含有純粹的癌症上皮細胞，能夠高度概括體內的腫瘤，是研究細胞異質性和分子表徵的理想選擇。基於當地的CRC患者，我們建立了一個獨特的類器官隊列。值得強調的是，這個隊列富含鋸齒狀瘤途徑的類器官，包含從腫瘤前期到癌症到轉移性病變的不同階段，它們代表了侵襲性最強且具有最差臨床結果的CRC亞型。我們已經通過全外顯子組測序描繪了其基因組學景觀。在這個提案中，我們的目標是通過單細胞轉錄組測序手段了解結直腸腫瘤的腫瘤內異質性和鋸齒狀腫瘤病變的克隆進化。通過深入的生物信息學分析，並結合基因組突變數據，我們的目標是確定揭示癌細胞起源的基因表達特徵，從而進一步了解鋸齒狀腫瘤的轉移和發病機制，並使用公開數據集進行驗證。最後，我們將培養出一系列能夠代表轉移和差異致病潛力所必需的不同亞群的結腸癌類器官。克隆類器官係將成為一種疾病建模和藥物測試的重要平台，用於研究和治療鋸齒狀結直腸癌腫瘤。

17108019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108019.value: Hirschsprung (HSCR) disease is characterized by the absence of nerve cells in the colon, caused by the defects of enteric neural crest cells (ENCCs), leading to intestinal obstruction. We have successfully established a human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-based disease model to elucidate the disease mechanisms underlying HSCR. Transcriptomic analysis of ENCCs derived from various HSCR-iPSC lines revealed that the metabolic pathways are frequently dysregulated in the diseased cells, and associated with the neuronal lineage differentiation defect, representing the druggable targets for HSCR. In line with this observation, our single-cell transcriptomic analysis indicated that a transient activation of Hedgehog (HH) pathway during NC induction, through boosting the cellular metabolic pathways, primes hiPSC-derived ENCCs to the neural fate and significantly improves the functional competency of their neuronal derivatives. Constitutive activation of the GLI-dependent (canonical) HH pathway, on the other hand, has been shown to cause premature gliogenesis of ENCCs in mice and contribute to HSCR pathogenesis. These observations therefore raise an important possibility that selective activation of the noncanonical HH pathway may improve the differentiation competency of ENCCs, representing a new therapeutic strategy for HSCR. Here, we hypothesize that rewiring the cellular metabolism pathways of the developing ENCCs, through activation of the non-canonical HH pathway, can improve the efficiency of their neural fate acquisition and the functional competency of the enteric neurons. We will test our hypothesis by 1) defining the key HH-mediated metabolic pathways underlying the human ENCC development; 2) elucidating the implications of the non-canonical HH pathways in the neurogenic and gliogenic lineage differentiation of hiPSC-derived ENCCs; and 3) deciphering the therapeutic potentials of various HH modulators in improving HSCR-ENCC functions using hiPSC-based in vitro cell- and innervated human colonic organoid models. A better understanding of the impact of the non-canonical HH signaling in mediating the development of the healthy and diseased ENCCs expedites the potential applications of HH modulators for targeting therapies and/or for the generation of enteric neurons for functional repair. 先天性巨結腸（HSCR）疾病是由於腸神經嵴細胞（ENCC）的缺陷，引致結腸中缺乏神經細胞，導致腸梗阻。我們已經成功用人類誘導多能幹細胞（hiPSC）建立了疾病模型，用以了解HSCR相關的疾病機制。我們分析來自各種HSCR-iPSC衍生的ENCC的轉錄組學，發現代謝途徑經常在病人細胞中失調，並且與神經元譜系分化缺陷相關，因此針對代謝途徑的藥物可能對醫治HSCR有一定的效用。與此觀察結果一致，我們的單細胞轉錄組學分析也顯示，在NC形成期間，激活Hedgehog（HH）通路，能促進細胞代謝途徑，並將hiPSC衍生的ENCC加速分化成神經元，並顯著提高了神經元的功能。但另一方面，小鼠實驗顯示激活與GLI有關的HH典形途徑會導致ENCC過早分化成神經膠質，而引致HSCR。因此，針對HSCR的治療，必須選擇性起地激活非典形HH途徑才可以改善ENCC的分化能力。所以，我們假設激活發育中的ENCC的非典形HH途徑能把代謝途徑重新佈線，從而提高其神經分化的效率和腸神經元的功能。我們將通過以下的方法來檢驗我們的假設：1）了解各種HH介導的代謝途徑對人類ENCC發育的影響; 2）闡明非經典HH途徑在hiPSC衍生的ENCC的神經源性和膠質細胞譜系分化中的意義; 3）使用hiPSC分化的神經細胞和結腸類器官模型，破譯各種HH調節劑在改善HSCR-ENCC功能的治療潛力。通過理解非典形HH信號傳導是如何影響健康和病人的ENCC的發育，我們將能把各種HH調節劑應用於靶向治療和/或用於修復腸神經元。

17108019.label: Realisation of objectives
17108019.value: Followings are the key findings under each objective: 1. To define the HH-mediated metabolic pathway(s) favoring the neural fate acquisition of hiPSC-derived ENCCs. According to the transcriptomic analysis as described previously, activation of the Hedgehog pathway primes ENCCs to neurogenic lineage without altering their neuronal differentiation trajectory. In this project, we have performed various assays and demonstrated that Hedgehog/Fatty acid oxidation (FAO)/oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) axis would be the potential mechanism underlying this process, which is consistent with the preference for mitochondrial OXPHOS during the cell state transition and neuronal differentiation. The non-canonical metabolic routing represents a quick and flexible way to provide energy and prepare ENCCs for cell state transition/differentiation, but it likely requires the reinforcement by the canonical Hedgehog signaling, which further initiates a transcriptional glycolysis response and modulates the expression of the entire machinery of primary metabolism including the Hedgehog/FAO/OXPHOS axis. As supported by our own transcriptional profiling data of SAG-primed ENCCs and the data from the differentiation assays, the full activation of Hedgehog pathway by SAG treatment robustly upregulates the expression of genes implicated in various cellular metabolic pathways, and that leads to a sustainable and profound effect on cell state transition and differentiation. 2.To delineate the roles of the non-canonical HH pathway in the neuronal and glial lineage differentiation of hiPSC-derived ENCCs. We have compared the effect from a full activation of Hedgehog pathway by SAG or a partial agonism through applying a low dosage of cyclopamine (CycLow, 1nM) on neuronal lineage differentiation of hENCCs. We found that both full and partial agonism of Hedgehog pathway can significantly increase the cellular aerobic respiration of ENCCs as monitored based on the OCR accompanied by significant increases in both OCR/ extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) ratio and the maximum respiration. In addition, a specific activation of AMPK-PKM2-PDHA1 pathway was observed upon an addition of SAG or CycLow, and this pathway was blocked by a high dosage of cyclopamine (CycHigh, 100nM), which antagonizes the Hedgehog pathway. Activation of the AMPK-PKM2 pathway by the full (SAG) or partial (CycLow) agonism of Hedgehog pathway led to an enhanced ATP production, which could be abolished by an addition of PKM2 inhibitor (PKM2i). Both lactate and pyruvate levels were significantly increased upon activation of the Hedgehog pathway, and they served as substrates to support the anaerobic and aerobic cellular metabolism, respectively, resulting in a higher ATP yield. Importantly, the Hedgehog-enhanced metabolic rewiring greatly increased the survival and/or growth of ENCCs as revealed by the MTT assay. On the other hand, Hedgehog mediated FAO is essential for the neuronal lineage differentiation. Unlike glycolysis, a full agonism of the Hedgehog pathway was required for activation of the FAO pathway, where only SAG, but not CycLow, could significantly increase the FAO-associated OCR and maximum respiration. In addition, activation of FAO or Hedgehog pathway by GW9508 (a potent and selective G protein-coupled receptors FFA1 (GPR40)) and SAG, respectively, led to a significant enhancement in the mitochondrial activity as monitored by the mitotracker, while the SAG-treated cells exhibited lower mitochondrial activity when ETO was added, suggesting the involvement of FAO in SAG-mediated mitochondrial activity. More importantly, activation of FAO pathway conferred ENCCs a greater neuronal differentiation capacity and significantly more neurons (TUJ1+, NF+) were found at day 5 of neuronal differentiation when FAO pathway was activated by the addition of GW9508. Our results support an essential role of the Hedgehog/FAO/mitochondria axis in mediating the neuronal differentiation of ENCCs. 3. To decipher the therapeutic potentials of various HH agonists using iPSC-based cell and innervated colonic organoid models of HSCR. To decipher the therapeutic potential of Hedgehog agonist, we determined whether the Hedgehog-induced metabolic rewiring can rescue the differentiation defects of HSCR-ENCCs. We found that the FAO-dependent mitochondria activity in HSCR-ENCCs was elevated upon SAG treatment which was blocked by ETO. Intriguingly, activation of the Hedgehog/FAO/mitochondria axis could also greatly improve the differentiation capacity of HSCR-ENCCs and significantly more TUJ1+ and NF+ neurons were detected when FAO pathway was activated by GW9508. Based on the result from the time-course experiment as described previously, addition of SAG during ENCC induction could maximize the yield and prime cells to the neurogenic lineage with enhanced cellular metabolic rate. Therefore, we employed the same differentiation strategy to generate HSCR-ENCCs. Consistently, SAG-treated HSCR-ENCC-derived TUJ1+ neurons grew better, exhibited better differentiation competency and required a shorter differentiation time to generate neuronal subtypes, such as tyrosine hydroxylase (TH), while the migration of these cells remained unaffected. In sum, our data suggest that activation of the Hedgehog pathway promotes glycolysis and FAO to support the survival/growth and differentiation of ENCCs. Using HCO model, we previously found that SAG treatment robustly enhances the engraftment and functions of enteric neurons. In this project, we have performed the scRNAseq of cells isolated from these HCOs and found that SAG treatment greatly increases the expression of metabolic pathway genes in enteric neurons of HCOs, highlighting that the implications of metabolic pathways in ENS development. Please refer to our paper (Li, et al, Nat Com, 2023) for the details.

17108019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108019.value: Mitochondrial dysfunction leads to deficiency in oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) causes devastating diseases, including bowel dysmotility. In this project, we have revealed the implications of OXPHOS activation and neurogenic lineage differentiation of progenitors of enteric nervous system (ENS). The next important step is to further delineate how mitochondrial dysfunction affect the ENS development and aging.

17108019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108019.value: In this project, we have demonstrated that targeting the Hedgehog pathway is one of the keys for boosting up the neurogenic competency of human progenitors for enteric nervous system (ENS) via enhancing OXPHOS pathway. Therefore, it is conceivable that the timely control of Hedgehog-mediated metabolic pathway(s) can maximize the neurogenic potential of ENS progenitors with high specificity and minimal size effect, representing a promising therapeutic target for ENS recovery.
