17108119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108119.value: 預測氣候變化及其於生物上之影響乃現今科學家最重視和迫切的研究題目，因氣候變化的潛在影響，如食物保障、生態系統服務和物種保育等，皆不容忽視。此等影響在生存在極端環境(如岩岸的高潮帶)的變溫動物尤為顯著，因其身體溫度直接受到附近環境的影響。面對氣候改變，變溫動物只能隨之遷徙至合適之地，利用表現型可塑性馴化自身生理，或急速進化適應，否則只能困於不合適的生境而滅絕。全球來說，熱帶地區的變溫動物尤為易受影響，因其表現型可塑性有限，而身處的環境卻又很接近其生理可承受之極限。可是，個體間和群體間的生理反應差異對該範式提出質疑，因為物種可藉此提高整體上的生理機制靈活性，從而在極端環境中存活下來。 最近有關個體溫度反應的研究顯示，兩種熱帶的潮間帶變溫動物，包括塔結節濱螺(Echinolittorina malaccana)和方型鉗蛤(Isognomon nucleus)，均可隨溫度調節其自身生理，並適時降低代謝率。此兩種動物皆常見於岩岸的高潮帶，故長時間抵受着高溫和食物稀少的極端環境挑戰。我們提出一項假設，即在不同物種中出現如此雷同的生理機制是生活在同一極端環境中趨同演化的結果。 為了驗證以上假設，我們將測量個體間代謝率衰減的差異，以及此兩物種的溫度反應和代謝率衰減於其地理分布中的在地適應性和可塑性。故此研究將拆解可塑性和在地適應性對於代謝率衰減的影響，及其如何使物種具備對抗氣候變化的能力。此研究也會藉測量物種在其地理分布上的生理和代謝衰減差異，建立基礎，供更微觀的近因研究(如分子機制)，或更宏觀的終因研究(如生態演化的機制)，改善對極端氣候變化下物種的可塑反應預測，從而更實在和準確的預測熱帶物種受氣候變化影響的程度。

17108119.label: Realisation of objectives
17108119.value: This project quantified the inter-individual (Objective 1) and inter-population (Objective 2) variations in cardiac thermal performance curves of two tropical high shore species, a mobile snail Echinolittorina malaccana and a sessile oyster Isognomon nucleus, and investigated the mechanisms (local adaptation versus phenotypic plasticity) driving these variations in metabolic depression (Objective 3). In the original proposal, this project intended researchers to travel to locations across the geographic range of the species to collect animals for physiological experiments and deploy in-situ loggers on the shores to monitor the local thermal environment. As a result of the global pandemic traveling restrictions prevented us from following the proposed plan and caused fundamental changes in the original protocols (see revised Objectives and previous progress reports). To overcome these issues, we arranged for overseas collaborators to collect and speed-post animals to Hong Kong for physiological measurements (this sampling approach was used in a previous RGC funded project on littorinid snails (RGC782011) and shown to have limited influence on animal responses). To achieve this, we established back-and-forth communications with collaborators to standardize and confirm the methods in handling the animals and deploying loggers. We also managed the logistics and administrative paperwork including the applications for local sampling and export permits, and confirmation of official collaborative documents (e.g. MoU with the University of the Philippines – Visayas). Overall, we coordinated collaborators and helpers from five locations involving six overseas universities (see Other Research Outputs) Secondly, we changed the scope of this project to focus primarily on the snail Echinolittorina. As Echinolittorina is an abundant, widespread and well-studied species in the Indo-Pacific region, it is feasible to remotely instruct collaborators to identify the animals, establish sampling sites and collect and speed-post animals. The oyster Isognomon, however, has a more restricted distribution and requires experienced researchers to correctly identify them and locate suitable sampling sites. Although we have worked on Isognomon on Sichang Island, Thailand with collaborators for > 10 years, other collaborators have limited experience with this species and so remotely instructing them to identify suitable sampling sites did not appear to be a plausible alternative. Consequently, we proposed (and were approved; see previous progress reports) to change the scope of the project, with Echinolittorina collected from six locations spanning ~25° latitude across its geographic range, and Isognomon from only one well-established site in Sichang Island, Thailand. Specially, inter-individual (Objective 1) and inter-population (Objective 2) variations in metabolic depression and the mechanisms driving these variations (Objective 3) were investigated in Echinolittorina, whereas inter-individual variations (Objective 1) and phenotypic plasticity (Objective 3) were assessed in Isognomon. Objective 1: (100% achieved) This objective aimed to measure the field-acclimatized responses of the two high shore species and capture the variations in metabolic depression across individuals. This part of the project was to be conducted in Sichang Island, Thailand, where both species are abundant and fresh animals can be collected and measured immediately in a nearby marine station. Due to the travel restrictions, we arranged for our long-term collaborator (Dr Monthon Ganmanee) to collect and send animals to Hong Kong for measurements (see above). We eventually measured inter-individual variations in metabolic depression in Isognomon from Sichang, Thailand, and in Echinolittorina from six locations (see Objective 2) to quantify and compare the extent of inter-individual variations in metabolic depression in multiple populations. To allow efficient processing of these heart rate data, a computer algorithm integrating autocorrelation, a genetic algorithm and a tracking index was developed (see Research Output). Autocorrelation is used as the primary temporal analytic technique to identify recurrent heartbeats and calculate heart rates from their periods. It is employed on a genetic algorithm framework (as a machine-learning approach) and coupled with a tracking index to minimize noise interference and reduce errors in computation. Overall, the algorithm allows rapid and accurate processing of heart rate data to obtain average heart rates per minute and was used for subsequent analyses in this project. Objective 2: (100% achieved) This objective aimed to quantify the inter-population (spatial) variations and measure the local thermal environment as a potential explanatory variable for such spatial pattern. To achieve this objective, suitable sites with high abundances of Echinolittorina were established and temperature loggers were deployed to measure rock surface temperature in six locations. These locations were chosen to cover a large geographic area with a wide range of climatic conditions, ranging from the aseasonal tropical region (i.e. Singapore, The Philippines and Thailand) to the monsoonal, seasonal, subtropical region (i.e. Hong Kong and Taiwan). As many of these locations also had local travel restrictions across states and cities that changed rapidly and unexpectedly, we encountered last-minute change of plans and delays in sampling, and hence the need to follow up on the corresponding administrative paperwork such as renewing sampling permits. Despite the difficult situation, we managed to collect snails and temperature data from all these locations, and snails were transported to Hong Kong within 1 – 5 days of sampling (< 1% of mortality). Upon arrival they were kept in sprays tanks with local seawater temperature and their field-acclimatized responses were measured within three days. We finally measured metabolic thermal performance from 14 – 21 individuals x 2 sites x 6 locations = 234 individuals. These data allowed us to capture the variations in metabolic depression on natural shores and to partition the relative contribution of inter-population and inter-individual (see Objective 1) variations to intraspecific variations. The measured rock temperature also served as a reliable proxy of thermal environment experienced by the snails to compare the extent and variations of thermal stress experienced by the different populations. Objective 3: (100% achieved) This objective aimed to tease apart whether local adaptation and/or phenotypic plasticity drives the inter-population variations in metabolic depression of Echinolittorina, and how metabolic depression in Isognomon changed in response to acclimation. To achieve this objective, we designed a common garden experiment to acclimate the animals for one month to either a hot regime (at 30°C seawater and 42°C substrate temperature during emersion, designed to simulate) and a cool regime (at 18°C seawater and 20°C substrate temperature during emersion, designed to simulate cool, benign winter conditions experienced by snails in seasonal regions). These temperature regimes were designed based on information from local weather stations as well as previously deployed temperature loggers on the shore. In total, cardiac thermal performances were measured in 9 – 15 individuals x 2 sites (to include within-location variations) x 6 locations (Singapore; Thailand (2 sites north and south); the Philippines; Hong Kong and Taiwan) = 155 hot-acclimated individuals and 11 – 17 individuals x 2 sites x 6 locations = 172 cool-acclimated individuals. These measurements and maintenance of samples were also subject to difficulties and logistic challenges due to local pandemic restrictions. The theory behind these experiments was that by standardizing the environmental influences (including temperature, food and light cycle) during acclimation, environmentally induced variations (phenotypic plasticity) can be minimized and so persistent population differences in Echinolittorina can be attributed to local adaptation. Comparisons of post-acclimation to field-acclimatized responses of both species can also demonstrate the capability of these animals to perform physiological adjustments via phenotypic plasticity and investigate the potential benefits associated with metabolic depression.

17108119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17108119.value: Although both Isognomon and Echinolittorina delink their metabolism from rising temperature, they showed diverse depression patterns: Isognomon shows an extensive depression magnitude, while Echinolittorina shows a wide thermally insensitive zone of similar heart rates despite rising temperature. These interspecific differences highlight the potentially varied cellular pathways in achieving this convergent energy conservation strategy (see 6.2). Despite the interspecific differences, large inter-individual variations were found in both species and the extent of which was reduced after hot-acclimation in Echinolittorina but increased in Isognomon. This difference may reflect the varied reliance on physiological strategies in mobile versus sessile species to cope with thermal stress (see 6.2). With limited behavioural thermoregulatory abilities, sessile species may have to be more physiological labile and so having increased inter-individual variations may be beneficial for population viability. Large inter-population variations were also found in Echinolittorina, which generally correlated with the extent of local thermal stress (i.e. snails from north Thailand and Hong Kong had the highest heart rates and thermal tolerances, and experienced severe thermal stress). Such population differences persisted after common garden acclimation, highlighting the genetic basis of such differences and suggesting that local thermal stress may exert selective pressure to drive varied metabolic responses in these populations (i.e. local adaptation). All populations showed substantial changes in metabolic depression after acclimation (e.g. having suppressed heart rates and extended thermal tolerances after hot-acclimation), demonstrating their ability to modify their physiology in response to stress (i.e. phenotypic plasticity). Three manuscripts are ready to be submitted and one is being prepared: 1) the algorithm for efficient heart rate data processing (see Objective 1) are described in MS1, intended for Ecological Informatics; 2) the inter-population and inter-individual variations in cardiac thermal performances of Echinolittorina and the effects of local adaptation and phenotypic plasticity (see Objectives 1 – 3) are described in MS2, intended for Functional Ecology; 3) the interspecific differences in metabolic depression between Isognomon and Echinolittorina (see Objective 1) are planned to be combined with cardiac performances of other rocky shore species (e.g. Echinolittorina radiata and Lottia dorsuosa, data of which we have also collected and are currently being analysed) to test hypothesis on physiological lability in multiple sessile versus mobile species in coping with thermal stress. Insights from this project has also led to improved analyses of previous thermal performance data of the same species described in MS3, intended for Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.

17108119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108119.value: This project demonstrated large variations in metabolic depression responses and contributions of both genetic and environmentally induced components. While the current project focused only on physiological responses, the interspecific differences between the sessile and mobile species also indicate how thermoregulatory behaviours may affect body temperature, especially for mobile species. We are furthering this approach to compare and contrast the two species at Sichang Island, Thailand (since restrictions were lifted after the pandemic) where thermal responses of the mobile and sessile species are addressed in different microhabitats (e.g. solitary individuals vs aggregations), to unravel the contribution of physical environment (which is fixed for sessile species) and modifications of this via behaviour by the mobile species. Another clear direction is the use molecular methods to identify the pathways that the animals are using during metabolic depression. The genome of Echinolittorina has been assembled by one of our collaborators (Y-W Dong, Qingdao Ocean University) who is investigating this species. We are currently collaborating with JD Gaitan-Espitia (HKU) who is analysing the transcriptomic responses of Isognomon based on thermal trials we performed during this project (in Sichang, Thailand) to induce metabolic depression and identify key metabolic pathways these animals show.

17108119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108119.value: “Nature versus nurture” is a longstanding debate in biology, as it questions how species respond to local environmental changes and how genetically constrained they are to alter their responses. Understanding their relative contributions in determining functional traits can explain species survival under modern day conditions, but also under future climates. Tropical high-shore species are models to investigate this question as they live in extreme, thermal environments, and their responses can indicate how species become “winners” or “losers” under climate warming. Thermal responses of a common snail and oyster were investigated across populations from Singapore to Taiwan to understand the relative contributions of genetics and local environmental conditions to their performances. Their thermal tolerance and responses did not follow a latitudinal gradient but were related to local on-shore temperatures, and this pattern was sustained after eliminating environmental variations in the laboratory, indicating a locally-adapted response (i.e. a nature effect). These animals also varied their responses according to the environmental conditions they experienced in the laboratory (i.e. a nurture effect). The thermal response of these tropical high-shore species is, therefore, an interaction of both nature and nurture, which permits their survival in this extreme environment.

17108519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17108519.value: 肝移植是治療末期肝病和早期不可切除的肝癌的最佳選擇，而肝移植（尤其是活體肝移植）後的膽道併發症卻是一大問題，但及時的內鏡治理可以有滿意的效果。大多數的膽道吻合口狹窄都可以用「內鏡逆行胰膽管造影術」加「球囊擴張術」治理，若有需要，會插入塑料支架。內鏡治理的成功率超過七成，但通常需要進行多次（一般是四至五次）。支架的作用是支撐已被擴張處，目前最普遍的是塑料支架。塑料支架的缺點是口徑小。在一個吻合口內放置數個塑料支架，雖可解決口徑不足的問題，但所提供的支撐力卻不是渾圓、 均勻分布。另一方面，由於口徑小，支架內的阻力大，容易導致支架堵塞。許多研究表明，「自膨脹金屬支架」在通暢率方面優於塑料支架。然而，目前常用的「自膨脹金屬支架」是不可移除的，因此通常用於惡性狹窄。可喜的是，最近開發了「可回收自膨脹金屬支架」，其應用已經擴展至包括良性狀況。「可回收自膨脹金屬支架」曾用於治理二十九例膽道吻合口狹窄，結論是「安全、有效」。我中心的初步研究也顯示效果理想：五名患者置入「可回收自膨脹金屬支架」最少三個月後，吻合口狹窄完全解決，而且沒有併發症。

17108519.label: Realisation of objectives
17108519.value: During the study period, the undertaking of the project was unfortunately affected by the changeover of the study investigators. Dr KW Ma resigned from his post followed by the departure of project PI Dr SH Chok at that time in 2019. The project was then transferred to Prof CM Lo and he also subsequently departed for the government post in 2022. Moreover, the liver transplant service was severely affected by the COVID epidemic from 2019-2021 resulting in substantial drop in the number of liver transplant performed and suspension of elective ERCP service for biliary stenting. When I took over from this project, the recruitment period was already passed and the IRB approval for this study was expired. It was not feasible to continue the study project. As a result, the outcome in the mid-term report will be the same as the final report of the study. Nonetheless, despite all the difficulties and challenges, the elective service for biliary stenting resumed after the COVID lockdown and the study procedures resumed. From 1 June 2022 to 31 Dec 2023, 18 patients developed biliary stricture after liver transplantation. 17 patients received plastic stenting while 1 patient received metallic stenting. The median age of patients was 58 (30-66). The indications for liver transplants were as follow: liver cirrhosis (n=8), fulminat hepatic failure (n=2), acute-on-chronic liver failure (n=4). 7 patients received deceased donor liver transplantation while 11 patients received living donor liver transplantation. The number of sessions required for further stent revision for biliary stent was 1 (0-4) while no further stent revision was required for the metallic stenting group. There was no significant difference between the two interventions with regard to patient survival and liver graft survival (see graph) In conclusion, the effect of metallic stenting was promising as it might be associated with reduced chance of re-interventions. Further study with larger same size is warranted.

17108519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17108519.value: During the study period, 14 patients were assessed and 2 declined trial participation, therefore 12 patients (consisted of 7 male and 5 female) were recruited. Among these 12 patients, 10 had deceased donor liver transplant (DDLT) and 2 had living donor liver transplantation (LDLT). The median time from transplant to occurrence of biliary stricture was 4.8 months (2‐29) and all patients presented with graft dysfunction. Seven of these patients were randomized to conventional arm (i.e. balloon dilatation and plastic stenting) and 5 had r‐SEMS. The median age for the r-SEMS and balloon stenting followed by plastic stunting were 55.5 (43-63) and 51(39-68) respectively (p=0.683). The number of DDLT in the r-SEMS and balloon dilatation and plastic stunting group were 5 patients (100%) and 5 patients (71.4%) respectively. No patient had mortality within 30 days after procedure. None had post ERCP retroperitoneal or intraperitoneal perforation, post ERCP pancreatitis, post ERCP bleeding or cholangitis that required prolonged hospitalization or intervention. Both intervention were effective. 11/12 strictures were managed endoscopically whereas the remaining 1 patient will have follow‐up ERCP. The median number of ERCP needed for stricture resolution was 2 (2‐4) in r‐SEMS and 3.5 in balloon dilatation and plastic stenting (p=0.692). Graft and patient survival rates of the recruited patients were 100%.

17108519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108519.value: A potential for further development is to explore if dilatation followed by r-SEMS would further enhance the efficacy of r-SEMS in the treatment of biliary strictures after liver transplantation when compared with dilatation followed by plastic stenting.

17108519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108519.value: Despite the notion that retrievable metallic stenting is more effective than dilatation followed by plastic stenting in the management of biliary stricture after liver transplantation, our study did not show any statistically significant difference between the two groups of treatments.

17108719.value: 腎纖維化是驅動慢性腎病進展至終末期腎病的關鍵環節。現時針對慢性腎病的臨床治療方案選擇少、特異性差，亟需研發更高效的治療藥物。轉錄因子可以通過調控基因轉錄在疾病的發生發展中發揮重要作用，越來越多的研究證據顯示，靶向轉錄因子或許可以成為治療疾病的新策略。FoxP2已被廣泛證實是一種與語言習得相關的重要轉錄因子，但是FoxP2在慢性腎病中的作用卻從未有研究報道。我們近期的研究結果顯示，糖尿病腎病患者和慢性腎病動物模型腎組織中的FoxP2顯著升高，FoxP2還參與了TGF-β誘導的腎小管上皮細胞向促纖維化表型轉化，而腎小管上皮細胞已知為推動腎間質纖維化的重要調控細胞。上述研究結果提示FoxP2可能在腎纖維化過程中發揮了重要的調控作用。 在本研究方案中，我們將首先檢測FoxP2在各種臨床慢性腎病腎組織標本中的表達情況，從而明確FoxP2與腎組織纖維化程度的相關性。在細胞實驗部分，我們將體外培養腎小管上皮細胞，隨後利用各種分子生物學技術手段深入探討TGF-β誘導刺激腎小管上皮細胞內FoxP2表達的分子機制，並結合染色質免疫共沉澱測序技術（CHIP-seq）精確定位FoxP2的DNA結合位點，明確FoxP2的靶向調控基因。在動物實驗部分，我們將首先通過Cre-LoxP重組酶基因編輯系統構建腎小管上皮細胞條件性FoxP2基因敲除小鼠（通過將Ksp-Cre基因型小鼠和Foxp2flox/flox基因型小鼠雜交獲得），並在此基礎上進一步建立單側輸尿管阻塞（Unilateral ureteral obstruction, UUO）和糖尿病腎病(Diabetic nephropathy, DN)兩種慢性腎病動物模型深入探索和闡明FoxP2在腎纖維化和慢性腎病進展過程中的作用和機制。本項目的研究成果將有助於闡明FoxP2的上游調控機制，並明確靶向干預FxoP2能否影響其下游病理生理反應，例如靶向干預FoxP2的表達能否影響腎纖維化相關基因的轉錄和腎纖維化的進展。本項目的研究結論將進一步加深我們對TGF-β誘導腎纖維化發病機制的認識，繼而推動尋找治療慢性腎病腎纖維化的新型特異性治療藥物。

17108719.label: Realisation of objectives
17108719.value: In this project, we have completed all of our research objectives and demonstrated a novel role of Foxp2 in kidney fibrogenesis through TGF-β-mediated epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and cell cycle arrest. From our established Biobank, we successfully obtained renal biopsies from patients with diabetic nephropathy, IgA nephropathy and membranous nephropathy (n=10 for each group) and completed the expression profile of Foxp2 by immunohistochemical staining (completion of Aim 1). Since the collection of renal biopsy for research use had been temporarily suspended during 2020-2022 due to the covid-19 pandemic, our data on other CKD such as focal and segmental glomerulosclerosis and lupus nephritis have not reached statistically analysis. We will continue this part of the study. We have provided several evidence for elucidating the regulatory mechanisms of Foxp2 expression during renal fibrosis. Foxp2 was induced by TGF-β1 in cultured tubular cells via Smad3 signaling as demonstrated by analysis of the promoter activity (luciferase reporter assay), gene (real-time PCR) and protein (Western blot) expression levels (completion of Aim 1). As a transcription factor, Foxp2 regulates gene transcription by binding to specific DNA sequences. Therefore, we have conducted ChIP-sequencing and identified the putative Foxp2 binding sites for a total of 744 correponding genes. Together with the pathway enrichment analysis, our results have revealed that Foxp2 target genes were highly associated with TGF-β1and Akt signaling pathways that play key roles in kidney fibrogenesis including cell proliferation, apoptosis, extracellular matrix accumulation and EMT. The pathogenic role of Foxp2 in TGF-β1-induced fibrotic events and EMT was then confirmed by gene silencing experiment (completion of Aim 2). Finally, we have successfully generated a tubular-specific Foxp2 knockout mice by crossing floxed Foxp2 with Ksp-Cre mice and established the fibrotic model of unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO). As expected, tubule-specific deletion of Foxp2 attenuated kidney inflammation and tubulointerstitial fibrosis in UUO model, which were accompanied by reduction in cell cycle arrest (completion of Aim 2).

17108719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17108719.value: 1. Upregulation of Foxp2 in kidney tubules of human and experimental fibrotic models To determine the expression level of Foxp2 protein in the pathological condition of CKD, we performed immunohistochemical staining on human kidney biopsies obtained from patients with various CKD including diabetic nephropathy (DN), IgA nephropathy (IgAN) and membranous nephropathy (MN). Non-tumorous portions of the kidney from patients undergoing tumor nephrectomy was used as control. Our results found that Foxp2 was markedly increased in the nuclei of kidney tubules from biopsies with different etiologies. The progressive induction of Foxp2 was confirmed in the mouse experimental model of unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO), which further supported the subsequent use of the tubular epithelial cell line and the generation of tubule-specific Foxp2 knockout mice in our study. 2. Induction of Foxp2 was regulated by TGF-β/Smad3 signaling pathway To understand how Foxp2 was upregulated, we analysed the promoter sequence of Foxp2 and conducted several in vitro experiments using cultured tubular epithelial cells (TECs). First, we found that nuclear Foxp2 was significantly upregulated after TGF-β1 stimulation (key mediator of renal fibrosis), which was abrogated after pretreatment with the Smad3 inhibitor (SIS3). Second, the regulation of Foxp2 promoter activity by TGF-β1 was confirmed by firefly luciferase reporter assay. We also demonstrated that cells overexpressing Smad3 only could directly increased the Foxp2 promoter activity. Our results suggest a crosstalk between the transcription factors of Foxp2 and Smad3 during TGF-β-mediated fibrosis. 3. Foxp2 controls the transcriptional activity of fibrotic and cell cycle-related genes By means of ChIP-sequencing and database analysis, we identified several putative Foxp2 target genes including p21, p27, Collagen 1 and E-cadherin in TECs with Foxp2 overexpression. The binding of Foxp2 to these sequences was confirmed by ChIP-PCR and the transcriptional activity of Foxp2 was validated by luciferase reporter assay. Pathway analysis revealed that these Foxp2 target genes were enriched in PI3K/Akt and TGF-β signaling pathways. Indeed, gene silencing of Foxp2 upregulated basal expression of Ecad protein and rescued the loss of Ecad induced by TGF-β1 in TECs while overexpression of Foxp2 increased the cell population in G2 phase of the cell cycle. 4. Tubule-specific deletion of Foxp2 reduced kidney inflammation and fibrosis in UUO model Based on our in vitro findings, we generated the tubular-specific knockout mice (Foxp2fl/fl,Cre) in which Foxp2 was genetically ablated in tubular epithelial cells to study the role of Foxp2 in renal fibrosis. Deficiency of tubular Foxp2 was associated with reduced interstitial fibrosis and collagen deposition in the obstructed kidney as evident by a significantly downregulated fibronectin, alpha-smooth muscle actin, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and vimentin expression in Foxp2fl/fl,Cre kidneys compared Foxp2fl/fl control. Renal inflammation was also reduced with less macrophage and neutrophil infiltration and accompanied by a significant reduction of TNF-α upregulation and MAPK p42/p44 phosphorylation induced by UUO. Furthermore, Foxp2fl/fl,Cre mice exhibited less accumulation of p21, p27 and phosphorylated histone H3 in renal tubules, indicating a suppression of G2/M phase cell cycle arrest. Our results showed that ablation of Foxp2 in tubular epithelial cells attenuated kidney fibrosis following UUO. The above findings were presented in ASN Kidney Week 2022 and published in J Am Soc Nephrol S33, 2022: Page (590) and the manuscript has been submitted to the Journal of the American Society of Nephrology (IF 13.6, under major revision).

17108719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17108719.value: This study demonstrates, for the first time, how Foxp2 works as a transcription factor to mediate the TGF-β-induced pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic responses during CKD. Interestingly, we uncovered a novel role of Foxp2 in regulating epithelial cell cycle arrest, which is the important driver for maladaptive repair and kidney fibrosis. Based on our results, we will further explore the molecular mechanisms linking between Foxp2, cell cycle arrest and Akt signaling pathway. Findings from the study will provide evidence for Foxp2 as a potential therapeutic target of kidney fibrosis. Apart from this, we are currently investigating the role of Foxp2 in tumor progression of renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Dysregulation of Foxp2 is associated with the progression of various cancers including RCC. Preliminary results on RCC study suggest a regulatory role of Foxp2 in cell cycle arrest on RCC cancer cells, which have been submitted for the RGC/GRF 2024/2025 grant application.

17108719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17108719.value: Kidney fibrosis is a final, common pathway in all causes of chronic kidney diseases (CKD), ultimately leading to kidney failure, for which there are limited effective therapeutic strategies. Our study uncovered a novel role of Foxp2 in kidney fibrosis, in which Foxp2 was induced in tubular epithelial cells via TGF-β/Smad3 signaling and was found upregulated in renal biopsies from patients with various CKD. Knockdown of Foxp2 suppressed TGF-β-induced EMT and accumulation of extracellular matrix proteins while overexpression of Foxp2 inhibited tubular cell proliferation with induction of G2/M cell cycle arrest. Mice with deletion of Foxp2 in renal tubules showed reduction in inflammation and fibrosis against obstructive nephropathy. Collectively, our findings provide novel evidence that Foxp2 regulates TGF-β-induced EMT and cell cycle arrest, the key signaling pathways of kidney fibrosis, and suggest that Foxp2 may be a potential therapeutic target for kidney fibrosis.

17109019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109019.value: 糖尿病腎病（DN）是慢性炎症性疾病。NLRP3炎症小體系統是機體先天免疫受體及危險信號感受器，如身體出現高糖狀態，激發炎症及加重炎症性疾病的病理變化。 C反應蛋白（CRP）是公認炎症的生物標誌物，在糖尿病患者中顯著升高，但CRP糖尿病及其併發症中的作用機制尚未明確。我們首先發現CRP在1型及2型糖尿病小鼠模型中通過激活TGFβ/Smad和NF-κB信號通路加重了糖尿病腎病。 由此，我們提出一些問題：CRP是否通過調節NLRP3炎症小體系統加重糖尿病腎病炎症？抑制這個炎症小體系統激活是否能減輕糖尿病腎病的炎症？我們初步研究發現在CRP-db/db雙轉基因糖尿病小鼠中的NLRP3炎症小體和IL-1 β較db/db糖尿病小鼠明顯增加，并與Smad3激活成正相關。體外實驗發現CRP干預后細胞中的炎症小體隨時間顯著激活。CRP協同高糖促進細胞中NLRP3炎症小體激活。而且，糖尿病腎病中敲除Smad3后減輕CRP介導的炎症反應。基於前期結果，我們提出假設：在糖尿病腎病發病過程中，Smad3活化導致CRP介導NLRP3激活，而抑制Smad3通過可以下調CRP介導的NLRP3炎症小體激活，進而減輕糖尿病腎病的發病。 本研究的目的為通過CRP-db/db雙轉基因小鼠及體外實驗研究糖尿病腎病的發病是否通過Smad3通路，激活CRP，進而激活NLRP3。同時還會通過Smad3敲除-db/db雙轉基因小鼠及體外實驗研究抑制Smad3通路，能否減輕CRP介導的NLRP3活化引起的腎臟炎症反應。 本研究結果將揭示糖尿病腎病中NLRP3激活導致慢性炎症的機制，并為治療糖尿病腎病提供新的靶點。故該研究對臨床及基礎有雙重意義。

17109019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17109019.value: The study determined whether CRP promotes inflammation via Smad3-mediated NLRP3 inflammasome activation in diabetic nephropathy (DN). DN is the leading microvascular complication of diabetic mellitus with inflammation, fibrosis, and epigenetic modifications which are involved in different cell types [1-3]. We found that the overexpression of CRP in diabetic mice significantly enhanced kidney injuries (IL-1β, TNF-α), activation of NLRP3 inflammasome (NLRP3, NEK7, and Caspase-1) and phosphorylation of Smad3. The deletion of Smad3 alleviated diabetic kidney injury and activation of NLRP3 inflammasome in diabetic mice. Consistently, CRP induced cell injury and NLRP3 inflammasome activation in high glucose-treated TECs and MCs were reversed by Smad3 inhibitor SIS3 or CRP receptor CD32b antibody. Notably, we identified that CRP promoted NLRP3 activation by P-Smad3 binding to the NLRP3 promoter area. In conclusion, CRP promotes diabetic nephropathy via Smad3-mediated NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Smad3 is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of inflammation in diabetic patients [4-5, 9]. Furthermore, our study also found that Buyang Huanwu Decoction protects against STZ-induced diabetic nephropathy by inhibiting TGF-β/Smad3 signaling-mediated renal fibrosis and inflammation [6]. In addition, the project also supported two reviews regarding two Chinese medicines on inflammations in peripheral organs [7-8]. Research outcomes: The articles from the project: [1]. 17109019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17109019.value: This research project focused on understanding the role of a protein called C-reactive protein (CRP) in diabetic nephropathy (DN), which is a common complication of diabetes that affects the kidneys. The study aimed to investigate whether CRP promotes inflammation by activating a specific protein called NLRP3 inflammasome through the Smad3 pathway in DN. To do this, the researchers used genetically modified mice and treated human kidney cells with CRP. The results showed that increased levels of CRP in diabetic mice led to more severe kidney damage and activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. However, when the Smad3 protein was removed, the kidney damage and NLRP3 inflammasome activation were reduced. Similarly, treating kidney cells with a Smad3 inhibitor that blocks the CRP receptor reversed the CRP-induced cell damage and NLRP3 activation. Furthermore, the researchers discovered that CRP promotes NLRP3 activation by binding to a specific region of the NLRP3 gene. Our study suggests that targeting the Smad3 protein could be a potential therapeutic approach for reducing inflammation in diabetic patients with kidney problems. The findings from the project will support us in developing new techniques to remove CRP in patients with DN, e.g., nano-technique, anti-CRP drugs, or anti-CRP dialysis combined with routine dialysis.

17109419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109419.value: Mangrove forests are disappearing at an alarming rate all over the world. One of the major causes of mangrove loss in the last 50 years has been the increasing volume of contaminated runoff from urban, industrial and agricultural areas. As mangroves act as physical and biochemical barriers to contaminants transport, pollutant as heavy metals have been reported from mangrove sediments all over the world, and are particularly abundant in Southern China, impacting Hong Kong mangroves. Despite the wealth of studies documenting the concentration of heavy metals in sediments and bioaccumulation of those pollutants in plant tissues, there is very little information on their bioaccumulation and impacts on the faunal components of these ecosystems. One notable gap, especially in South East Asia and Southern China, is the impact on crabs, despite the fact that it is now evident worldwide that there are no healthy and resilient mangrove forests without diverse crab communities. Given their importance to mangrove functioning, the impacts of heavy metals on crabs could be an early indicator of ecological degradation in mangroves. The current project will, therefore use crabs as the mangrove equivalents of ‘canaries in a coalmine’ by detecting the relatively sensitive and rapid physiological and metabolic stress signals in crabs linked to heavy metals pollution. To achieve this, the project will assess at the individual level, the direct correlation between metal accumulation, physiological stress – using crab thermal performance – and enzymatic and biochemical metabolism of individuals from natural populations at sites characterised by increasing heavy metal pollution. As such, due to the intrinsic characteristics of Hong Kong mangroves (i.e. their small average dimensions, their patchy distribution and the high level of pollutants), this approach will allow a scientific overlook into the future of the mangroves of South China in the human impacted Anthropocene. In addition, to confirm the direct link between heavy metals and crab performance indicators, levels of metabolic and physiological stress will be assessed in crabs experimentally exposed to different levels of Cadmium, one of the most abundant and toxic trace metal present in Hong Kong waters. Mangroves forests do thrive in polluted areas, but do they perform their ecological function and provide their ecosystems services in such degraded sites? The present project will answer, for the first time, this unsolved key question in mangrove and coastal ecology and provide crucial data to develop efficient conservation and management strategies of human impacted mangroves.

17109419.label: Realisation of objectives
17109419.value: Details of each objective, as well as issues faced, are given below and the data are now assembled into scientific papers for publication (see outputs). Objective 1 Heavy metal concentrations in sediments, leaves of common trees and tissues of crab species at five mangrove forests of Hong Kong were monitored. Three sites were located on the west coast, Tung Chung, North Lantau, Ha Pak Nai and Mai Po, Deep Bay, and two in the eastern district of Sai Kung; Pak Tam Chung and Yung Shue O. Heavy metal concentrations in sediments were generally greater at sites on the western coast (Figure 3, Buttler et al., in prep.) indicating hotspots of contamination due to the proximity to the major sources of pollutants, represented by the highly industrialised GBA. Mai Po was the most contaminated mangrove. This is particularly concerning, as Mai Po is the largest mangrove stand found in the whole GBA and an internationally protected site due to its importance to overwintering birds. No significant difference was found in the concentrations of heavy metals within leaf tissues of mangroves among sites (Figure 4, Buttler et al., in prep.). The concentration of heavy metals within mangrove leaves was independent of that recorded in sediments, confirming that plant physiology is a greater factor than the level of sediment contamination in determining the concentration of heavy metals in plant tissues. Data on metal uptake and accumulation in mangrove crabs suggests a relationship with the species’ feeding mode, with microphytobenthos feeders and predators accumulating more pollutants (Figure 5, Buttler et al., in prep.). Overall, data revealed a subtle but strong impact of heavy metal pollution on Hong Kong mangrove forests and their resident fauna and the need of an updated and constant monitoring programme. Objective 2 In this case, the thermal tolerance tests were performed on crabs collected at four mangrove sites: Tung Chung and Mai Po as mangroves with relatively high concentrations of heavy metals within the sediment, and Yung Shue O and Pak Tam Chung as almost pristine sites. The Mai Po crab population displayed suppressed oxygen consumption compared to all other populations, in line with studies that have observed reduced oxygen consumption in crustaceans exposed to heavy metals. Although the cardiac response of crabs from the Mai Po population was not reduced or elevated in comparison to other populations, it was more irregular as observed in other studies associated with the neurotoxic action of metals such as Cd, which may directly impair cardiac function. The capacity to cope with temperature extremes in crabs exposed to heavy metals are reduced, which may be further exacerbated in tropical intertidal species with more narrow thermal windows. The impact of heavy metals on the breathing capacity of the dual-breathing P. continentale (= bidens), a widely distributed and dominant species in southern China mangroves, was strong. This suggests an impairment at the metabolic level and a weak resilience to temperature extremes, that could result in a compromise in the species’ energy budget, ultimately causing a reduction in energy demanding eco-engineering activities including burrowing, foraging, and mating. This is concerning given the ecological role of P. continentale in the wetland and mangrove ecosystem of eastern and southern China, respectively. This imbalance will impact the crabs’ functional role, with subsequent ramifications for the health and resilience of the broader ecosystem. Objective 3 Lipid mediators derived from fatty acids (PUFA) were assessed in the hepatopancreas of Parasesarma continentale (= bidens). Some of these are oxidized PUFAs that are intrinsically generated for metabolic energy. Production of these mediators can be overwhelmed by extrinsic factors such as environmental pollution and injuries leading to the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). We successfully measured 37 fatty acid methyl esters and 30 oxidized products of PUFA in the hepatopancreas tissues of P. continentale. Total saturated fats (especially palmitic and stearic acid) of samples from Yung Shue O were significantly higher compared to other samples. Eicosanoic acid (C20:0) and cis-11-Eicosenoic acid (C20:1) were only found in hepatopancreas tissues of samples from Pak Tam Chung. In total -3 and -6 PUFA were significantly higher in samples from Yung Shue O compared to other samples. It is possible that crabs in Yung Shue O have high surroundings sources of marine-based food rich in AA, EPA and DHA (Figure 1, Leung et al. in prep.). This study is the first to evaluate some of these lipid mediators in mangrove crabs. Our study showed that only Prostaglandin2 was elevated in the hepatopancreatic tissues of P. continentale from Mai Po, Tung Chung, Ha Pak Nai and Pak Tam Chung as compared to Yung Shue O. Although it is only one lipid mediator, this indicates P. continentale were under metabolic challenge in these areas compared to the lesser polluted Yung Shue O (Table 2, Leung et al. in prep.). Of the anti-inflammatory group, only PDx was elevated in the tissues from Tung Chung and Ha Pak Na; which was interpreted as the crabs responding for homeostatic control. Lipid autooxidation can also produce oxidized PUFAs in organisms. Some of these are robust oxidative stress biomarkers, in particular 15-F2t¬-IsoPs that can reflect the environmental stress experienced by the organism in their habitats. Based on this, 15-F2t¬-IsoPs levels in crab tissues from Mai Po (the most contaminated site, Objective 1) were significantly elevated compared to Yung Shue O. 9-D1-PhytoP and 16-F1-PhytoP levels were also elevated in crabs from Mai Po as compared to Tung Chung and Yung Shue O (Table 3, Leung et al. in prep.). To summarize, fatty acid profiles displayed the availability of food and perhaps the diet preferences of P. continentale. Oxidative stress of the crabs, as measured by the lipid mediators was higher in crabs from Mai Po which suggests they are less healthy (eating less) and under oxidative stress as compared to other areas, in particular Yung Shue O. Problems encountered and solutions. Initially the project was strongly impacted by the restrictions on working and research activities due to the COVID pandemic; resulting in limited access to laboratories which changed the original research objectives (especially of objectives 2 and 3, which relied on laboratory-based research). The initial scope was to assess the impact of heavy metals on the respiratory and the fatty acid metabolism of two species of mangrove crabs, Parasesarma continentale (=bidens) and Gelasimus borealis. Due to the COVID restrictions for lab research, however, we could not perform tests and analyses on both species, and so had to focus on the most abundant species of crabs, P. continentale, which is a key ecosystem engineer. Our indepth and detailed research on this dominant species is important to understand the subtle impact of heavy metal pollution on Hong Kong mangroves. In terms of Objective 1, we did not limit our assessment on the heavy metal exposure and bioaccumulation potential of mangrove crabs to P. continentale (=bidens) and Gelasimus borealis, as initially planned but extended this to cover a wide range of ecological roles, dietary preferences, and functional capacities, by increasing the number of species to eight, within 4 families. This allowed us to study bioaccumulation pathways and detect the biomagnification of heavy metals across the whole mangrove food web.

17109419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17109419.value: The project highlighted how heavy metals are a subtle but grave threat to mangrove forests, in general, and especially those in Hong Kong. The Pearl River flows through one of the most industrialised and urbanised areas on earth and inundates the western coast of Hong Kong with an annual freshwater discharge of 336 109 m3 together with its associated contaminants. Our data indicated Mai Po was the most contaminated mangrove, reporting a “very high” contamination factor and “moderate to strong” geo-accumulation index (Buttler et al in prep). This is a particularly concerning, as Mai Po is the largest mangrove stand found in the whole Greater Bay Area and an internationally protected site under the RAMSAR convention due to its importance for overwintering birds. Our data on bioaccumulation in mangrove crabs showed the transfer of heavy metals through the food web (Leung et al in prep). Such transfer has the potential to influence multiple ecosystems and is especially important for the management and conservation of ecologically significant areas such as Mai Po, where heavy metal contamination is presently at levels that pose a considerable risk to the areas ecology and may threaten already endangered species such as the black faced spoonbill (Platalea minor). Chronic exposure to non-essential heavy metals reduces crabs’ thermal windows, as illustrated by suppressed oxygen consumption in P. continentale populations from Mai Po. Using a new method that considers the relationship between heavy metal accumulation and individual thermal performance, we showed that the accumulation of Al, Cd, Cu, Pb and Zn was negatively related to the metabolic performance of the crabs. Our findings have consequences for the resilience of crabs to future climate scenarios as species with narrow thermal windows have less capacity to adapt to temperature change, especially in tropical regions and intertidal habitats where they may already be living close to their thermal limits. The findings of this study are especially concerning as P. continentale is a keystone species in mangrove systems and performs ecological roles that are vital to the health and resilience of mangroves. If keystone species and ecosystem engineers are negatively influenced by heavy metal accumulation, and/or cannot adapt to changing climates, they may fail to perform functional roles causing serious implications for the whole ecosystem. As a consequence, the contamination of mangroves by heavy metals should be considered as a serious threat to ecosystem health and functioning.

17109419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17109419.value: The levels of heavy metal contamination in the sediment of Mai Po are particularly concerning and should be further analysed and monitored. This wetland area is a critical stopover for birds migrating along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway (EAAF) and more data are needed to understand the biological pathways of heavy metal bioaccumulation and biomagnification. We were able to show that transfer of heavy metals from the sediment to the macrofauna is mainly taking place through the food web (i.e. trophic transfer) and it is imperative to understand if this bioaccumulation path is also affecting higher levels of the Mai Po food web, and especially overwintering birds. Our data on the impact of heavy metal bioaccumulation on the thermal metabolism of keystone species of crabs lay the foundations for future studies to understand the physiological mechanisms of such negative relationships. It is well known that tropical species are critically affected by climate change, due to their narrow thermal performance. Further studies are needed to understand how other anthropogenic stressors can affect such performance, which can ultimately represent a critical threat for tropical populations living in urbanised and industrialized environments.

17109419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17109419.value: As coastal areas continue to urbanise and industrialise, coastal systems are exposed to unprecedented levels of inorganic pollution such as non-essential heavy metals, which are toxic in low concentrations. Mangrove forests are no exception, since the fine mud of their sediment provide optimal conditions for the accruement of heavy metals. The main aim of the present project was to understand the impact of this subtle form of pollution on the invertebrate fauna thriving in the mangrove forests of Hong Kong. Our data show that heavy metal concentrations differed among mangrove forests but were generally greater at sites sampled on the western coast of Hong Kong. This coast is influenced by the Pearl River, which flows through the highly industrialised Greater Bay Area and represents a major source of pollutants. Mangrove crabs, which are keystone bioengineering species vital for mangrove forest health, accumulated substantial concentrations of heavy metals. These metals, in turn, impaired their metabolism and, especially, their resilience to future climate change, by decreasing their ability to cope with high temperatures. Overall, the heavy metal accumulation experienced in Hong Kong’s mangroves may be representative of the future situation for mangroves globally.

17109619.label: Realisation of objectives
17109619.value: # How the project objectives have been achieved: 1. Preparation for realization of the objective Ethical approval was obtained for this survey (UW 16-494). Invitation letters were sent to 2454 subjects who have participated in our previous surveys. Written consent has been obtained from 2112 (female: 1290; males: 822) participants. 2. Clinical data collection The participant’s oral cavity was cleaned with gauze and dental floss. All types of malocclusion, the presence of dental anomalies, and oral health status were evaluated using the same criteria. One trained and calibrated examiner performed the clinical examination using a disposable plane intra-oral mirror with a built-in LED light source. Participants’ body height was measured using a portable height measure (Seca 213, Hamburg, Germany) and body weight measured using a calibrated weighing scale (WB-8000RW, Tanita, Japan). Their BMI was then calculated. One trained and calibrated examiner (intra-class correlation coefficient (ICC) = 0.96 - 0.99 for intra-examiner reliabilities of assessing body height and body weight) performed all of the anthropometric measurements following standardised assessment procedures (Objective 3 & 4). The 3D facial images of the participants were captured using a stereophotogrammetric technique. The participants were seated at a fixed distance from the cameras, facing at a mirror placed in front of him/her. A surgical cap was used to allow for sufficient exposure of the face. The 3D facial images were captured using the 3dMDface stereophotogrammetric optical system (3dMD, Atlanta, GA, USA). This system contains three pairs of synchronised cameras, which allows for the capture of six images within 2 milliseconds. These images were merged by a triangulation algorithm to generate life-like facial images with natural surface textures (Objective 1 & 2). 3. Data processing Standardised facial landmarks were digitised on the 3D facial images to include all important facial features. Curve and surface sliding semilandmarks were also be digitised to capture the shape information of the face where there was a lack of distinct landmarks. Digitisation were performed using the Checkpoint software (Stratovan, Davis, USA) twice, separated by a minimum of two weeks, to determine the measurement error. Coordinates of landmarks and semilandmarks were submitted for Generalised Procrustes Analysis (GPA) which is a registration technique that removes information on location, orientation, and size of an object through iterative cycles of translation, rotation, and scaling. After GPA, non-shape information in the raw landmark data were eliminated and the resulting Procrustes shape coordinates captured the pure shape information. Facial shape data were then fully preserved using a revolutionary analytical package i.e. geometric morphometrics. 4. Data analysis Both original facial configurations and their reflected and re-labeled copies were simultaneously submitted for GPA. GPA was implemented through the bilat.symmetry function in geomorph package in R. Sources of variation in the resultant Procrustes shape coordinates were decomposed into three components: symmetric, FA, and directional asymmetric components (Objectives 2). The symmetric component of facial shape variation was captured by individual variations in the averages of the original and the reflected and re-labeled configurations. Gender-specific normative patterns of facial shape of the participants were established from the means of the symmetric component of facial shape. Mean facial shape was estimated using the mshape function in geomorph (Objective 1). Establishment of life course trajectories provides a unique opportunity for a dynamic view of the effect of BMI on facial FA. In addition, it obviates the issue of multicollinearity when repeated measures are simultaneously included into a regression model. To circumvent the potential issue of multicollinearity, the penalised regression technique was applied (Objective 3). Pairwise comparisons were performed, and statistical significance was evaluated through 10000 permutations. Sex-specific and pooled developmental trends of Procrustes variance were modelled through GAM. To further explore specific facial features that contribute to changes of Procrustes variance, covariance structures of facial features were examined. Proportionality of covariance matrix of shape features, in addition to statistical significance regarding differences in successive relative eigenvalues, was examined using the likelihood ratio test. False discovery rate adjustment was made to p values from tests of successive relative eigenvalues. Analysis was performed using the vcvComp package (v. 1.0.2) in R (Objective 4). # To what extent the project objectives have been achieved: The project objectives have been completely achieved. # Give reason for under-achievements and outline attempts to overcome problems, if any: Nil.

17109619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17109619.value: 2112 participants (females: 1290; males: 822) were included in this study. Gender-specific normative patterns of facial shape of the birth cohort were established from the means of the symmetric component of facial shape. The shape difference between males and females of the 18-year-old participants was statistically significant (p = 0.032). The soft tissue facial morphology generated and analysed by the 3D geometric morphometric method was considered to be valid and reliable. (Conference Abstracts 1 and Paper 1 & 2) Significant female facial changes were noted from age 4-7 to 16-18 years (p = 0.001). For males, an overall shape change was identified (p = 0.013). Trajectory analysis suggested that the direction of facial development in the multidimensional shape space is similar for both genders, as characterised by the protrusion of the nasal and labiomental region and retrusion of the forehead and cheek region. The magnitude of shape change is larger for females than for males (p = 0.006). (Conference Abstracts 2) Sexual dimorphism in facial shape emerged at 6 years of age and persisted throughout subsequent ages with differences increasing significantly (p < 0.001) and nonlinearly. Rate of facial shape development declined with age monotonically in females. In males, however, a markedly heightened rate of development was observed during 12 to 15 years of age. The fifth relative eigenvector represented shape features with the largest amount of excessive variance in 18 to 20 years of age compared with 6 to 9 years of ages. Shape features in females are characterised by contrasting local deformations in the frontal, lateral nasal and upper labial regions versus lower labial and chin regions resulting in contrasting displacement of the frontonasal and labial regions relative to other facial features. In males, contrasting local deformation was observed in the frontal and chin regions compared with the nasal lateral walls, nasal alar and columella regions, resulting in contrasting relative displacement of frontal and chin regions compared with other facial features. Concordance of spatial distribution of local deformations captured by the fifth relative eigenvector with local deformations reflecting rate of facial shape development at key developmental stages from 6 to 22 years of age was examined using the Pearson correlation coefficient. Moderate-to-high correlation with growth rates at 9, 12 and 15 years of age was observed in both sexes. No association between life course characteristics, including anthropometric measurements, at different stages and facial FA was detected. (Paper 3)

17109619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17109619.value: Sites of local deformation identified in this study are suggestive of potential facial growth factors which may aid in designing plans for orthodontic treatment and maxillofacial and plastic surgeries. For example, the effective harnessing of growth patterns can enable shorter treatment duration and less invasive procedures to ensure desirable and stable outcomes. The facial shape analysis from this project therefore serves as a useful reference for clinicians in making diagnoses and formulating treatment plans. Increasing the investigative period will allow for a more complete understanding of developmental changes of facial shape. Furthermore, increasing the variety of ethnicity, sociodemographic status, and health condition of subjects may provide a basis for comparisons in future studies.

17109619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17109619.value: The understanding of development in the craniofacial complex is essential for clinical diagnoses and treatment planning. Although cross-sectional studies provide a snap shot of the association at a particular point in time, they do not reveal the temporal trends of this association. The credibility of previous findings is further compromised by the lack of mature three-dimensional (3D) computer imaging techniques and advanced analytical tools, and very small sample sizes. This large-scale study used standardised measurement criteria and appropriate statistical analyses to establish gender-specific normative patterns of facial shape and investigate levels of facial fluctuating asymmetry (FA). The association between life course characteristics at different stages and facial FA was also comprehensively evaluated. Evidence from the findings may inform the best timing for clinical interventions, assist in the formulation of age-specific programmes, and help patients reach their full developmental potential.

17109919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17109919.value: The government has promoted Hong Kong as the Asian’s wine hub with zero alcohol tax (ethanol ≤30%) since 2008, which causes dramatic increases in alcohol drinking and binge drinking rates. Alcohol use in youth is the leading cause of disability adjusted life-years loss. Most adult drinkers start drinking at age 18-21. Evidence shows that alcohol brief intervention (ABI) is effective reducing hazardous and harmful alcohol use in university students. The proposed trial aims to enhance the ABI by incorporating information communication technologies (ICTs) such as instant messaging (IM) Apps (e.g. WhatsApp and WeChat) to provide personalized, real-time chat-based support led by nurses. No similar trials are found in PubMed, Cochrane Library and trial registries (ClinicalTrial.gov & IRSCTN) except our pilot trial which supports feasibility and preliminary efficacy. Students from different universities in Hong Kong screened by Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test (AUDIT) with a score ≥8 will be recruited and randomly assigned to the Intervention (n=335) or Control group (n=335). Both groups will receive face-to-face ABI (about 5-10 minutes), which consists of standard advices according to the AUDIT scores. Intervention group will further receive 12-week chat-based intervention using IM Apps guided by the Capability-Opportunity-Motivation Behaviour model to enhance and sustain ABI effects. Chat-based intervention includes (1) personalized messages (e-messages) based on baseline AUDIT and drinking behavioural pattern; (2) proactive query on situational or planed drinking with timely reminders before and after drinking; and (3) chat-based psychosocial support to increase motivation for reducing alcohol use and maintaining abstinence. The Control group will only receive similar intensity of regular messages on general health and reminders on follow-up surveys. To increase usage of e-messages, e-message presentation will be designed according to pilot qualitative findings in university students. Primary outcome is weekly alcohol consumption amount at 6-month. Secondary outcomes include: numbers of standard drinks, binge or heavy drinking, academic performance, planed drinking and alcohol related-harms. Qualitative interviews and mediation analysis will be done to understand the intervention mechanisms. Taxonomy of behavioural change techniques will be used to identify the causes of behaviour changes. Outcome assessors and data analysts will be blinded to group allocation. We will follow CONSORT-EHEALTH statement strictly. This trial will be the first to provide evidence on the effect of using chat-based intervention for reducing alcohol use and related-harms in university students. The intervention is highly applicable to alcohol services and other risky behaviours (e.g. drug abuse) in university students.

17111119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111119.value: Colorectal cancer is a major health care burden in Hong Kong. While most patients with metastatic disease are incurable and long-term palliative treatment including chemotherapy with or without target therapy are the norm, patients with liver metastases that are still resectable represents a highly favorable subgroup of patients with the genuine potential of cure. Compared with the 5-year survival of 5% for metastatic patients in general, patient with surgery done for their resectable liver metastasis have 5-year survival as high as 40-60%. However, even in this subgroup of patients not all enjoyed prolonged disease control and as many as 30% of patients relapsed within 6 months post-op, which makes the major surgical undertaking a futile one. Various patient stratification/ selection tools have been proposed but most are based on clinical factors eg. Fong score, and do not take into account the biology of tumor cells. An accurate system for patient selection with the incorporation of tumor biology is desirable. Circulating tumor cell (CTC) is shedded into to the circulation from both the primary and metastatic tumors and represents a novel tool for liquid biopsy of cancer. The nature of it overcomes the invasiveness and sampling error of conventional biopsy. Although enumeration has a proven role of disease monitoring and prognostication in colorectal cancer, a lot is yet to be explored for the code-breaking of the genomic landscapes of CTC. Moreover, the reasons why CTC can survive in the circulation and ultimately establish metastasis are still unknown. Thus, deciphering such mechanism through the understanding of CTCs' genomic profile would be of utmost scientific and translational values. Our team has mastered the microfluidic platform for CTC detection and has been working successfully on the sequencing of CTC in various cancer with available expertise and infrastructure. With the local epidemiology of colorectal cancer, available clinical and scientific expertise at our center, the current study is proposed to decipher and to eventually apply the genomic knowledge of CTC in patients with liver metastasis to redefine resectability. The objective is to improve patient selection for liver resection and to minimize the risk of a futile surgery in patients with metastatic cancer.

17111119.label: Realisation of objectives
17111119.value: We performed a pilot run with 5 samples with HEAT-Seq library preparation as initially proposed. However, due to the instability of enzyme performances, it was difficult to optimize the PCR cycles to control the duplication rate while generating enough library yield. Therefore, the KAPA HyperPrep for library construction and NimbleGen SeqCap EZ hybridization for target capture were chosen. The platform is more robust and allows capturing of a larger gene panel (3.53 Mbp over 429 genes). The DNA of 71 CTC-enriched and 67 unenriched blood samples which passed QC test were sequenced. The median of CTC samples’ mean target coverage was 1355x (Q1-Q3: 1008x - 1985x). After trimming and filtering out reads with low sequencing/mapping quality, duplicates, and off targets, a median of 30.5% reads were usable (Q1-Q3: 27.6% - 36.2%). One out of 71 CTC samples had both metrics below 0.01 percentile and was thus excluded in subsequent analyses. The median of reference blood’s mean target coverage was 431x (Q1-Q3: 361x - 493x). A median of 31.5% reads were usable (Q1-Q3: 30.5% - 32.5%). The 67 pairs of CTC samples with matched blood were submitted to GATK’s ContEst tool. All CTCs matched with their respective reference blood with less than 0.5% estimated contamination. To obtain the molecular profiles of CTC, we aligned the raw sequencing data to human genome (v.hg19) by BWA-MEM, marked duplicates with PiCard, recalibrated base quality with GATK BaseRecalibrator, collected QC metrics GATK CollectHsMetrics, and finally called somatic mutations with MuTect1. Variants with >=5 mutant reads were accepted and were then annotated with ANNOVAR. Public database used was 1000 Genomes Project, Exome Aggregation Consortium (ExAC), and ESP6500. Variants with population frequency of >1% were removed. To evaluate clinical significance and tumour relevance, annotation with ClinVar, Catalog of Somatic Mutations in Cancer (COSMIC), NCMI’s dbSNP, and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were performed. The final mutation list includes missense, stopgain/loss and splicing variants, which have been annotated in TCGA database. Objective 1: Overall, we called 653 mutations in 66 samples. We detected at least 1 mutation in 53 out of 62 patients. MUC16 was the top mutated gene across patients with early and late relapse. Up to 35 MUC16 variants (32 missense, 3 stopgain) were identified in 24 patients (7 relapsed within 6 months). In the early relapse cohort, after MUC16 (50% cases with mutation), the next most frequent is FAT3 (25%), followed by POLE (19%), APC (19%), SYNE1 (19%), etc. In the late relapse cohort, the top mutated was also MUC16 (26%), followed by HUWEI (15%) and SYNE1 (15%), then LRP1B (11%), APC (11%), and ATM (11%), etc. In the no relapse cohort, the top mutated is again MUC16 (42%), followed by LRP1B (37%) and SYNE1 (37%). Survival analysis of top mutated genes was performed but no association was found with outcomes among the commonly mutated genes (MUC16: p=0.7; APC: p=0.57; LRP1B: p=0.075; EP400: p=0.26; KMT2D: p=0.21; FAT1: p=0.14; FAT3: p=0.29; FAT4: p=0.77; HUWEI: p=0.86). Apart from mutation profile, the overall mutation burden of patients with early/late relapse (<6m PFS: n=13; >6m PFS: n=40; p=0.48), different CEA trends (increase: n=16; decrease: n=39; p=0.31), pre-opt CEA (positive: n=38; negative: n=17; p=0.41, have no significant difference. Patients with wt-RAS has higher mutation load (mut: n=26; wt: n=30, p=0.049). 23 putative CRC driver genes were identified. Overall, the most frequently mutated gene was APC, with 4 stopgain and 5 missense detected in 9 samples (13% cases). This was followed by POLE (9%), CHD4 (6%), FBXW7 (6%), ARID1A (6%), TP53 (4%) etc. The top mutated driver gene in early relapse patients were APC (19%), POLE (19%) and CHD4 (19%). In the late relapse cohort, APC mutations were still the most frequent (11%), but they were all missense. There were relatively few driver gene mutations in this cohort. Amongst patients who did not relapse, there was a higher frequency of TP53 mutations (11%) than overall (4%). There were 2 APC missense and 1 stopgain detected. Looking into APC stopgains, 3 out of 4 were detected in the early relapsers and marked as pathogenic by CLINSIG, whilst the one detected in patient who did not relapse was not pathogenic. At a closer look into CLINSIG pathogenic APC stopgains, 7 additional cases have low allele frequency mutation of such. We analysed the prognosis of these 10 patients and found that they had significantly shorter progression free survival (p=0.019). As the median overall survival has not been reached, there was no significance seen (p=0.71). With the same strategy, i.e. including all low allele frequency pathogenic variants, we found that TP53 (17 cases with variants) and NF1 (8 cases with variants) were also significantly mutated. However, they have no significance in either PFS (TP53: p=0.38; NF1: p=0.32) or OS (TP53: p=0.27; NF1: p=0.28). Objective 2: For the subtyping of CTC according to time of relapse (early vs late), please refer to the results above for Aim 1. Despite curative intent of the index liver resection, relapse in both hepatic and extrahepatic sites are common. In total, we have 17 (1 has no matched blood) patients who relapsed after index resection with hepatic metastasis, and 20 (1 has no matched blood, 5 metastasized before surgery) with extrahepatic metastasis. Median PFS and OS of the 17 patients with hepatic metastasis was 214 days (16/17 had event) and 808 days (4/17 had event) respectively. Median PFS and OS of the 20 patients (n=19 as CRCLM73 has no clinical info) with extrahepatic metastasis was 361 days (17/19 had event) and 842 days (5/19 had event) respectively. There was no significant difference in PFS (p=0.087) and OS (p=0.19) between these two groups of patients. MUC16 (18%), LRP1B (18%), FAT1 (18%) were the most frequently mutated in the hepatic group. The top mutated gene in the extrahepatic group was MUC16 (37%) followed by NF1 (21%). Consider only mutations on 34 metastasis-related genes, the mutation burden in patients with extrahepatic metastasis appear to be higher than that in the hepatic group, though not reaching statistical significance (p=0.105 by Student’s t test). Mutation burden of LRP1B/FAT1 is higher (p=0.035, by Student’s t test) in the extrahepatic metastasis group. Objective 3: By the time of data lock in January 2021 with a minimum of 8 months follow-up for every patient, there were 43 disease progressions and 12 deaths. 27.7% of patients relapsed within 6 months of liver resection. The median PFS of the entire group was 12.4 months (95% CI: 8.8 to 17.1 months), whereas the median OS was not reached. To conclude, sequencing of the CTC from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer is feasible with our optimized platform and methodology. All 3 objectives of the project have been achieved. Regarding objective 1, we identified MUC16 and APC as the most commonly mutated gene and CRC driver gene, respectively. Pathogenic APC, including those with low allele frequency mutation, was associated with significantly shorter PFS. Regarding objective 2, MUC16 and LRP1B were most commonly found in patients with hepatic relapse while MUC16 and NP1 were commonly found in patients with extrahepatic relapse. Mutation burden of LRP1B/FAT1 is significantly higher in the extrahepatic relapsers. Regarding objective 3, the survival outcomes of this study population is comparable to reported literature in the modern era of cancer therapy.

17111119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111119.value: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a major health care burden in Hong Kong, with over 5,000 new cases and a death toll more than 2,000 each year. While patients with metastatic disease have long been regarded as incurable, selected patients with limited extent of metastasis, in particular liver-only metastasis, have a chance of cure with contemporary surgical resection and systemic therapy. Nevertheless, early relapses within six months post-op were seen in nearly 30% of patients who underwent resection. Thus, there is an urgent need to redefine the resectability of colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) to spare patients from the futility of major operations and the associated risks. The current project has demonstrated the feasibility of utilizing circulating tumor cells as a novel liquid biopsy technique for redefining resectability. With a single pre-op blood testing for circulating tumor cells, the respective molecular profile can aid in prognostication of patient outcomes in a non-invasive manner. The knowledge of molecular characteristic of early vs late relapsers is complementary to conventional clinical model and shall facilitate clinical decision making for both doctors and patients. In summary, sequencing of the CTC from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer is feasible with our optimised platform and methodology. Good mean target coverage >1000x, usable reads ~ 30% and low estimated rate of contamination were achieved. All objectives of the project have been achieved. With respect to the molecular profile of patients with early relapse, we identified MUC16 and APC as the most commonly mutated gene and CRC driver gene, respectively. Pathogenic APC, including those with low allele frequency mutation, was associated with significantly shorter PFS. Patterns of metastasis is an important issue in patients who received liver resection since the extrahepatic metastasis are often unresectable and pertain poor prognosis. Upon further analysis, we demonstrated that MUC16 and LRP1B were most commonly found in patients with hepatic relapse while MUC16 and NP1 were commonly found in patients with extrahepatic relapse. Mutation burden of LRP1B/FAT1 is significantly higher in the extrahepatic relapsers. Overall, the survival outcomes of this study population is comparable to reported literature in the modern era of cancer therapy. To combine the results of this project with enumeration data and future comprehensive profiling of resected specimen shall decipher the metastatic cascade and recurrence mechanism in mCRC.

17111119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111119.value: Similar to the drawbacks for all other molecular studies on individual tumor specimen, tumor biopsies fall short in providing information on tumor heterogeneity with regards to both time and space. In clinical practice, the evolving molecular landscapes of tumors would be difficult to follow, even if possible to capture via repeated biopsies. CTCs, compared with conventional tissue biopsies, allow less invasive evaluation of tumour over time and is thought to be more representative of all tumours in the body. CTCs are believed to originate from the primary and metastatic tumours and can be measured quantitatively in blood. Our team has pioneered CTC research in various cancer types with the use of highly-sensitive microfluidic platform. As part of the continuous effort in optimizing the application of CTC in determining resectability in mCRC, in addition to CTC enumeration in PI’s previous HRMF project and current CTC molecular profiling GRF project, the future plan is to obtain comprehensive profiling of all resected primary tumor and metastasis from the same cohort of patients with complete long term follow up. The data generated will enhance our knowledge about CRC metastatic cascade and mechanism of recurrence, which potentially translate to a genuine cure for our patients.

17111319.label: Realisation of objectives
17111319.value: This project has four objectives. We have successfully completed all of them. For Objective 1, we have developed a novel selection method of DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) that can realize ligand discovery against endogenous membrane proteins directly on live cells. This method is broadly applicable to membrane proteins as long as a known small molecule ligand or an antibody is available to guide the selection. For objective 2, the application of the library selection method to a variety of membrane protein targets has identified many novel ligands with functional relevance. For instance, the selection of a 30.42-million-compound library has identified novel ligands for epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), a major anti-cancer target, and we have also used fragment-based DELs and discovered novel inhibitors for four protein targets of high therapeutic significance (PD-L1, STAT5b, SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein, and NSP13 helicase). For objective 3, we modified the selection method to bias the discovery of functionally active ligands, and the selection method has been applied to three membrane proteins: EGFR, thrombopoietin receptor (TPOR), and insulin receptor (INSR). A number of novel agonists have been discovered for these targets, and notably, the INSR agonists bind at a previously unexplored allosteric site, showed strong synergistic effects with insulin in activating the receptor. For Objective 4, we have summarized the research in this report. Among the research outputs, the major ones that directly arise from this grant are listed below: 1. Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 17525-17532; 2. Nat. Chem. 2021, 13, 77-88; 3. Chem. Commun, 2021, 57, 3769-3772; 4. Acc. Chem. Res. 2021, 54, 3491-3503 (review); 5. Nat. Chem. 2022, 14, 129-140 (invited perspective article); 6. ACS Omega 2022, 7, 11491-11500; 7. ACS Omega 2023, 8, 21, 19057-19071 8. Nat. Chem. 2023, accepted. The manuscript describing the selection method and the novel allosteric agonists for insulin receptor and TPOR is currently under review in a top chemistry journal. In addition, three patent applications have been filed based on the research findings.
