17111319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111319.value: a) Aberrant membrane proteins are implicated in numerous human diseases and are a major class of drug targets; however, ligand discovery for membrane proteins is highly challenging. We have developed a method that has enabled DEL selections against endogenous membrane proteins on live cells. The generality and performance of this method has been demonstrated by selecting a 30.42-million-compound DEL against folate receptor (FR), carbonic anhydrase 12 (CA-12), and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) on live cells. A series of novel ligands were identified and validated for these targets. Notably, we have identified several small molecule binders targeting the extracellular domain of EGFR. Considering the high therapeutic significance of membrane proteins, this method has the potential to facilitate membrane-protein-based drug discovery by harnessing the power of DEL. b) We have developed a protein-templated DEL selection method that can identify full ligands/inhibitors from fragment-based DELs without fragment linking by encoding the linker in the library. Two multi-million fragment libraries with were prepared and selected against four targets, which have identified novel inhibitors for: the SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein (S-protein), the non-structure protein 13 (NSP13) helicase, programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1), and signal transducer and activator of transcription 5B (STAT5b), which are all important drug targets. Collectively, the research has circumvented a significant limitation in fragment-based DELs and may provide a broadly applicable method for ligand discovery against drug targets. The results described in a) and b) lead to several major publications: Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 17525-17532, Nat. Chem. 2021, 13, 77-88, and Nat. Chem. 2023, accepted. Two patents have been filed based on the novel inhibitors discovered. We have also been invited to write two review articles on the research topics (Nat. Chem. 2022, 14, 129-140; Acc. Chem. Res. 2021, 54, 3491-3503). c) Most DEL selections identify binders, which may or may not have a functional effect on the target. Moreover, for membrane proteins, agonist discovery is more difficult than antagonists as agonists require a specific switch of the protein conformation. We have developed an approach to identify agonists for membrane proteins via cell-based DEL selections. This method connects the extracellular ligand binding with the intracellular transformation of the target, thereby biasing the selection favoring agonist identification. We have performed the selections with three proteins: EGFR, thrombopoietin receptor (TPOR), and insulin receptor (INSR). A number of novel agonists have been discovered; notably, the INSR agonists bind at an allosteric site with strong synergistic effects with insulin in activating the receptor. Collectively, this work has developed a new “functional” DEL selection method and may provide a broadly applicable method for ligand discovery against membrane proteins. The manuscript is currently under review in a top chemistry journal, and a patent has been filed based on the novel insulin receptor agonists discovered in the selections.

17111319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111319.value: We intend to perform medicinal chemistry optimizations of the insulin receptor agonists to refine their binding affinities and activities. The more downstream drug development would require collaboration and funding support from external agencies and/or companies. We plan to apply ITF seed funding to conduct drug development on some of the most promising agonists. We also envision this method to be extended to more types of membrane proteins, protein complexes, and perhaps even the whole cancer cells as the target. Future research efforts will be dedicated to the discovery of protein-complex- or cancer-cell-specific ligands, which remain unexplored in this field. For example, using the same principle, complex DNA architectures with multivalent display capabilities could be used to target protein complexes with distal binding pockets. Multiple cancer cells could be interrogated with a collection of DELs to identify the small molecule arrays specific for certain cell type, rather than individual proteins.

17111319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111319.value: Membrane proteins expressed on the cell surface perform a variety of biological functions that are vital to the cell and the survival of the organism. Not surprisingly, aberrant membrane protein functions are implicated in the pathobiology of numerous human diseases, and many of them have been long pursued as major classes of drug targets in the pharmaceutical industry. As a result, there have been innumerable efforts to screen, identify, and develop ligands against membrane proteins for disease treatment and diagnosis. In this project, by using the DNA-encoded chemical library (DEL) technology, we have developed a series of novel high throughput screening method, by which millions of compounds can be examined simultaneously to identify the ones having potential as drug candidate. The screening can be performed directly on the surface of live cancer cells. In this project, a number of membrane protein targets of high therapeutic significance have been interrogated, and many novel small molecules have been discovered for further drug development.

17111619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111619.value: 牙髓組織中的血管神經束對牙髓組織的平衡、炎症反應、創傷修復和再生起到重要作用。研究表明，血管神經束微環境支持間充質幹細胞參與牙髓組織的平衡和創傷修復、再生。 因此，血管和神經再生的早期建立，以及其相互作用是牙髓再生和功能恢復的關鍵步驟。 血管和神經再生需要組建血管的細胞和神經前體/幹細胞。我們課題組已成功誘導根尖周幹細胞成為血管內皮細胞(SCAP-iECs)和神經前體/幹細胞SCAP-iNPCs。因此， 本課題將進一步研究(SCAP-iECs)和SCAP-iNPCs的功能，以及在牙髓再生中的作用。本課題有三個研究目的：（1）及早建立血管和神經再生對牙髓組織中的血管和神經形成的促進作用；（2）體內研究體外構建的具有成血管、成神經和成牙本質的微環境組織塊促進牙髓再生能力；（3）研究植入細胞參與血管和神經再生的狀況。本研究是首次將血管、神經和牙本質再生的概念結合，並採用單一細胞（根尖周幹細胞）來源的血管內皮細胞、神經前體細胞促進牙髓組織的血管和神經再生。

17111619.label: Realisation of objectives
17111619.value: 1. Objective 1 has been fully achieved through in vitro and in vivo studies. A novel strategy utilizing small molecule compounds to directly reprogram SCAPs to ECs was employed in our study. We found that the expression of endothelial-specific genes and proteins was upregulated in SCAPs-ECs following chemical induction. Furthermore, significant endothelial transcriptional networks were evident in the SCAPs-ECs group, demonstrating the capacity of SCAPs to form functional tubular-like structures. SCAPs-ECs also exhibited a robust ability to generate blood vessels in vivo. Additionally, SCAPs-ECs expressed adhesion molecules in pro-inflammatory environments and displayed similar migration and proliferation capabilities as HUVECs. Our findings demonstrated that the combination of small molecules and growth factors could successfully induce SCAPs into endothelial-like cells. These cells exhibited essential endothelial characteristics and had the potential to generate blood vessels in vivo, suggesting their potential as a promising cell source for vascular engineering and the treatment of ischemic diseases. For neurogenesis in SCAPs, we successfully achieved efficient chemical induction of SCAPs into neuronal-like cells. Following chemical reprogramming, SCAPs underwent notable morphological changes, transitioning from a spindle shape to a rounded morphology with bipolar neurite-like branches. The mRNA expression levels of NFM, NSE, DCX, and GFAP were significantly upregulated. Moreover, protein expression levels of TAU5, MAP2, NEUN, DCX, and TUJ1 were enhanced, while NESTIN expression was suppressed. Immunofluorescence staining further confirmed these findings, demonstrating elevated expression levels of MAP2, TUJ1, and NEUN, along with decreased expression of NESTIN. These results indicate that SCAPs can be successfully induced into neuronal cells using a combination of chemical molecules. Further, we conducted investigations to explore the potential of 3D spheres in promoting the neurogenic capabilities of SCAPs. Agarose microtissue molds were employed to create three-dimensional SCAP spheres. Notable morphological changes were observed in the SCAP spheres over time. The migrating cells transitioned from a fibroblast-like morphology to neuron-like cells. Compared to traditional 2D culture, the 3D spheres exhibited significantly increased neurite length, number, and the expression of various progenitor, immature, and mature neural markers. BDNF and NGF-β were found to play significant roles in the neural differentiation of SCAP spheres. Consequently, the formation of 3D spheres enhanced the neurogenic potential of SCAPs, suggesting the advantages of utilizing SCAP 3D spheres for the treatment of neural diseases. 2. Objective 2 has been fully achieved through in vitro studies. We reported a novel strategy for constructing a 3D coculture system within a pulp-on-a-chip system to investigate the neuroregenerative potential of SCAPs under various microenvironments. SCAPs were efficiently chemically induced into neuronal-like cells. When cocultured with undifferentiated SCAPs, SCAP-derived neuronal cell spheroids exhibited upregulated expression levels of MAP2 and TUJ1. Comparatively, coculturing with Oi-SCAPs in -MEM and neurospheres cultured alone resulted in intermediate expression levels, while the lowest expression was observed when cocultured with Oi-SCAPs in osteogenic medium/NMM with hydroxyapatite nanoparticles. Notably, spheroids cocultured with undifferentiated SCAPs displayed more pronounced neurite spreading than those in the other three groups. Consequently, these findings highlight the crucial role of local microenvironments in regulating the neuroregenerative potential of SCAPs-derived neuronal cell spheroids. 3. Objective 3 has been fully achieved through in vitro and in vivo studies. Our study focused on investigating the interactions between neuronally induced stem cells from the apical papilla (iSCAP) spheres, SCAPs, and HUVECs in terms of vasculogenesis and neurogenesis. The findings revealed that the neural induction medium with small molecules rapidly induced the differentiation of SCAPs into neural-like cells. Gene expression analysis showed higher levels of Nestin, TUJ1, MAP2, NSE, and NeuN in iSCAP spheres compared to iSCAPs. Moreover, iSCAP spheres exhibited more extensive neurite formation and longer neurites compared to iSCAPs. iSCAP sphere, HUVEC, and SCAP direct coculture significantly enhanced vessel formation along with upregulated VEGF and multiple neural markers, such as Nestin, MAP 2, S100, and NG2. Additionally, in a pulp-on-chip system, the coculture of iSCAP spheres, SCAPs, and HUVECs promoted the migration of endothelial and neural cells towards each other. The assembly of alpha-smooth muscle actin-positive and CD31-positive cells further contributed to the formation of the vascular structure. Overall, the pulp-on-chip platform demonstrated the interactions of the neural (iSCAP sphere) and the vascular parts (SCAPs and HUVECs), indicating that incorporating neural and vascular cells could be potentially applied in dental pulp regeneration. To investigate the role of engrafted cells in neurovascular structure formation for pulp tissue regeneration, bio-fabricated pulp tissue constructs were created, incorporating a pre-vascularized central channel and various odontogenic, angiogenic, and neurogenic niches. These constructs were implanted in the subcutaneous spaces of immunodeficiency mice using root segments as carriers. Dental pulp-like tissue formation was observed in the apical part of the implanted roots. Histological analysis using H&E staining demonstrated that the SCAPs+HUVECs+Sphere-induced group exhibited a higher number of perfused and total blood vessels compared to the SCAPs+HUVECs and SCAPs+HUVECs+Sphere groups. Immunohistochemistry results revealed that the majority of blood vessel lumens stained positive for human CD31, indicating the involvement of implanted HUVECs in blood vessel formation in vivo. Furthermore, the percentage of TUJ1-positive cells was significantly higher in the SCAPs+HUVECs+Sphere-induced group, followed by the SCAPs+HUVECs+Sphere group, and then the SCAPs+HUVECs group. This suggests a higher neurogenic potential of induced SCAPs in the sphere-induced group during tissue regeneration. However, the pulp-like tissues were not observed in the coronal portion of the pulp chamber, indicating limitations in achieving full-length root regeneration. Further investigation is required to identify and address these limitations in future studies.

17111619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111619.value: Our study presented a novel strategy using small molecules to directly reprogram SCAPs into endothelial cells (ECs) and neuronal-like cells. The induced SCAP-derived ECs exhibited endothelial characteristics and showed potential for generating blood vessels. Additionally, SCAPs demonstrated migration and proliferation capabilities similar to HUVECs, making them a promising cell source for vascular engineering and ischemic disease treatment. SCAPs were successfully induced into neuronal-like cells, highlighting their potential for neuroregenerative therapies. Furthermore, our investigation of 3D spheres revealed their ability to enhance the neurogenic potential of SCAPs compared to traditional 2D cultures. The coculture of SCAP-derived neuronal cell spheroids with undifferentiated SCAPs resulted in increased expression of neural markers and extensive neurite spreading. This highlights the significant influence of microenvironments on the neuroregenerative potential of SCAP-derived neuronal cell spheroids. In the context of dental pulp regeneration, our study explored the interactions between induced stem cells from the apical papilla (iSCAP) spheres, SCAPs, and HUVECs. The coculture of iSCAP spheres, HUVECs, and SCAPs in a pulp-on-a-chip system promoted vessel formation, migration of endothelial and neural cells, and the development of vascular structures. This demonstrates the potential of incorporating neural and vascular cells for dental pulp regeneration. Additionally, we created bio-fabricated pulp tissue constructs with pre-vascularized channels and various niches to investigate neurovascular structure formation in vivo. The implanted constructs exhibited dental pulp-like tissue formation, particularly in the apical region of the roots. Histological analysis showed increased perfused and total blood vessels in the SCAPs+HUVECs+iSCAP sphere-induced group, along with a higher percentage of TUJ1-positive cells, indicating enhanced neurogenic potential. However, complete root regeneration was not achieved in the coronal portion of the pulp chamber, indicating the need for further research. Overall, our study contributes to the potential of SCAPs-iECs and SCAPs-iNPCs for angiogenic and neurogenic differentiation, highlighting their significance in tissue engineering, particularly in the context of dental pulp regeneration.

17111619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111619.value: This study held promising prospects for the future development of SCAP-based therapies in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. The direct reprogramming of SCAPs into endothelial and neuronal-like cells demonstrated their potential for generating blood vessels and neuroregenerative therapies. The investigation of 3D spheres showed their ability to enhance the neurogenic potential of SCAPs, suggesting the importance of microenvironments in neuroregeneration. In the context of dental pulp regeneration, the coculture of iSCAP spheres, HUVECs, and SCAPs promoted vessel formation, migration, and the development of vascular structures. Our results highlighted the potential of bio-fabricated pulp tissue for dental pulp regeneration. However, further research is needed to achieve complete root regeneration in the coronal portion of the pulp chamber. Future action should focus on exploring underlying mechanisms and further translational applications for feasible clinical application.

17111619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111619.value: Our study discovered a new method to transform SCAPs into endothelial and neuronal-like cells. These transformed cells showed the potential to generate blood vessels and aid in the regeneration of nerve tissue. Additionally, we explored how arranging these cells in three-dimensional structures enhanced their ability to develop into nerve-like cells. In the context of dental pulp regeneration, we investigated the interactions among iSCAP spheres, HUVECs, and SCAPs and found that combining neural and vascular cells promoted the formation of blood vessels and migration of cells. We also created artificial pulp tissue structures that resembled dental pulp and observed improved blood vessel formation and increased neural potential. Overall, our study emphasizes the value of bio-fabricated pulp tissue constructs for the field of tissue engineering, particularly in the context of dental pulp regeneration.

17111719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17111719.value: Although colonoscopy is usually regarded as the most accurate and sensitive method for colonic polyp detection, it is well known that up to 30% of colonic polyps could be missed by colonoscopy. These missed colonic lesions are more often in the proximal colon and could give rise to rapid development of colorectal cancer after a prior negative examination, which is called interval colorectal cancer. Interval colorectal cancer could account for up to 9% of all colorectal cancers and are also more often in the proximal colon. Various strategies have been attempted to improve the colonic adenoma detection including longer examination time, repeated tandem examination, the use of add-on devices and image enhanced endoscopy (IEE) with variable and conflicting results. In particular, various IEE modalities are commercially available which aim at enhancing colonic adenoma detection and characterization. As yet, direct head-to-head comparison of different IEE modalities for colorectal adenoma detection are sparse. To complicate this issue, repeated examination of the proximal colon has also been shown to increase proximal colonic adenoma detection. It remains unresolved whether IEE or repeated examination of the proximal colon are superior for proximal colonic adenoma detection. The proposed randomized study aims to compare the proximal adenoma detection rates by tandem examination of the proximal colon with two competing IEE modalities (narrow band imaging or blue laser imaging) and conventional white light imaging. The results would help to evaluate the role of different imaging modalities for detection of proximal colonic lesions, and to determine the incremental benefits of repeated examination of the proximal colon. 儘管結腸鏡檢查通常被認為是結腸息肉檢測的最準確和最敏感的方法，但結腸鏡檢查仍然漏檢多達30％的結腸息肉。 這些漏檢的結腸病變在近端結腸中更加常見，而且在先前陰性檢查後發現的結直腸癌進展更快，這被稱為間期結直腸癌。間期結直腸癌佔所有結腸直腸癌的比例達到9％，並且更常見於近端結腸。既往研究已經嘗試了多種策略來提高結腸腺瘤檢出率，包括延長檢查時間，重複的串聯結腸鏡檢查，使用附加裝置和圖像增強內窺鏡檢查（IEE），但效果仍存在爭議。目前市場上存在多種IEE模式，其旨在增強結腸腺瘤表面特徵，並提高腺瘤檢出率。但是迄今為止，仍然缺少直接頭對頭研究比較不同IEE模式的結直腸腺瘤檢出率。而且研究顯示近端結腸重複檢查也可提高近端結腸腺瘤檢出率。IEE或近端結腸的重複檢查在提高近端結腸腺瘤檢出中的優劣尚不清楚。本隨機對照研究旨在比較串聯檢查近端結腸與兩種IEE模式（窄帶成像或藍色鐳射成像）和常規白光成像的近端結腸腺瘤檢出率。該研究結果將有助於評估不同成像方式和重複檢查在檢出近端結腸病變中的作用。

17111719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17111719.value: Background & Aim: Blue-light imaging (BLI) is a new image-enhanced endoscopy with wavelength filter similar to narrow-band imaging (NBI). We compared the two with white-light imaging (WLE) on proximal colonic lesion detection and miss rates. Methods: It is a three-arm prospective randomized study with tandem examination of the proximal colon. We enrolled patients aged 40 years or above. Eligible patients were randomized in 1:1:1 ratio to receive BLI, NBI or WLE during first withdrawal of the proximal colon. Second withdrawal was performed under WLE in all patients. Primary outcomes were proximal polyp (pPDR) and adenoma (pADR) detection rates. Secondary outcomes were the miss rates of proximal lesions found on tandem examination. Results: 901 patients were included (mean age 64.7 years, 52.9% male) and 48.1% underwent colonoscopy for screening or surveillance. The corresponding pPDR of the BLI, NBI and WLE group was 45.8%, 41.6 and 36.6%, whereas the corresponding pADR was 36.6%, 33.8% and 28.3%. There was a significant difference in pPDR and pADR between BLI and WLE (difference: 9.2%, 95% CI 3.3-16.9%; and 8.3%, 95%CI 2.7-15.9%) or between NBI and WLE (difference: 5.0%, 95%CI 1.4-12.9%; and 5.6%, 95%CI 2.1-13.3%). BLI also had significantly lower proximal adenoma miss rate (19.4%) than WLE (27.4%; difference -8.0%, 95%CI -15.8% to -0.1%), but not between NBI (27.2%) and WLE. Conclusion: Both BLI and NBI were superior to WLE on detecting proximal colonic lesions, but only BLI had lower proximal adenoma miss rate than WLE.

17111719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17111719.value: Our findings suggest that other measures in addition to image enhanced endoscopy (IEE) would be needed to reduce the miss rate in the proximal colon. As shown in this study, repeat examination, even with WLI, could pick up >20% of these missed lesions. Recently, there were numerous studies determining the role of computer-assisted detection (CADe) in increasing polyp and adenoma detection. However, most existing commercially available CADe models were built on WLI images, and further studies are needed to determine whether there is incremental benefit of the combined use of CADe and IEE. Moreover, the role of add-on devices to increase mucosal exposure with the addition of IEE in reducing missed lesions should be determined.

17111719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17111719.value: In this randomized study comparing two different imaging modalities for detection of various colonic lesions in the proximal colon, we found that both the blue light imaging and narrow band imaging are superior to conventional white light imaging. However, both imaging modalities still missed at least 20% of proximal lesions which were only detected on repeated examination only. Further innovative technology may still be needed to enhance the colonic lesion detection rate as well as to reduce the miss rate during colonoscopy, as these undetected lesions could progress to cancer, which minimize the preventive effects of colonoscopy on colorectal cancer development.

17112119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112119.value: 真核生物細胞中，複製起始位點識別複合物ORC，通過識別並結合複製起始位點，促進複製解旋酶Mcm2-7在DNA上的組裝。ORC有六個亞基，其中Orc1-5每一個亞基都包含有一個AAA+相關元件。ORC結合ATP對於其DNA結合以及MCM組裝至關重要。然而，Orc6亞基中沒有包含AAA+元件，並且其序列同其他亞基也有較大差別。Orc6在複製起始過程中發揮關鍵作用；但是，到目前為止，Orc6參與複製起始調控的分子機制尚未完全清楚。 最近，我們利用冷凍電鏡解析了酵母ORC-DNA相關複合物3埃的結構。在此結構中，Orc1-5環繞ARS的ACS元件，跟多個DNA磷酸骨架和鹼基相互作用。然而，Orc6位於ORC的遠端，不參與跟ACS的結合，但是可以接觸B1位點DNA。其結果，複製起點DNA在B1位點被彎折，從而偏離ORC結構中DNA結合通道。目前，我們的研究表明，在缺失Orc6的情況下，DNA彎折程度明顯降低。有意思的發現是，DNA彎折的方向正好位於Mcm2-7開口處（Mcm2和Mcm5之間）。這一現象表明ORC彎折DNA對於MCM組裝的過程可能非常重要。在本項研究中，我們將深入研究Orc6在ORC結合DNA以及促進MCM組裝過程中的分子機制。相關研究成果會加深我們對複製起始調控的認識，特別是複製起始蛋白如何通過與DNA的互動，進而行使其相關功能的具體機制。

17112119.label: Realisation of objectives
17112119.value: We have realised all the objectives of this project. To understand the mechanism of origin selection, we have determined a series of cryo-EM structures of origin recognition complexes bound to origin DNA. These high-resolution structures inform us how various ORC subunits cooperate to engage with origin DNA to modulate specific DNA recognition. We also generated a collection of mutants to validate the structural information and their impact on helicase loading across the genome. The related findings have been published with two papers (Cell Discov 2020, Nat Commun 2021) and one manuscript in submission.

17112119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112119.value: Eukaryotic cells require the origin recognition complex (ORC) to initiate DNA replication by facilitating the recruitment of two minichromosome maintenance (MCM) 2-7 complexes into a head-to-head double hexamer (DH) to license origin DNA. However, the molecular mechanisms behind ORC’s ability in modulating the conformation of origin DNA to drive a stepwise licensing process are not well understood. In this project, we utilised structural and functional approaches to characterise the activities of ORC at origin DNA. We found that each ORC subunit plays a unique role in regulating origin selection and helicase loading. Mutating or deletion of certain motif/domain/subunit of ORC led to severe defect in ORC-DNA binding and pre-RC assembly.

17112119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112119.value: This work lays a foundation for us to further investigate the mechanism regulating origin licensing in human cells.

17112119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112119.value: DNA replication is a process that happens in our cells and is responsible for making sure our genetic information is copied correctly when cells divide. If there are mistakes, it can lead to serious problems, like cancer. We study DNA replication to better understand how it works and how to prevent or treat diseases like cancer. In this study, we used special technology to look at the parts of the process that find the site for assembling the machine for unzipping our DNA, which gives us important information for fighting cancer.

17112819.value: To examine the clinical response to tai chi versus CBT-I on alleviating insomnia in older adults with chronic insomnia, as assessed by insomnia severity index (ISI)
rows: To examine the clinical response to tai chi versus CBT-I on alleviating insomnia in older adults with chronic insomnia, as assessed by insomnia severity index (ISI)

17112819.label: Realisation of objectives
17112819.value: This study is a single-blind, randomized, controlled, non-inferiority trial that aims to compare the effectiveness of 3 months of CBT-I or tai chi training in alleviating chronic insomnia in older adults. Older adults with chronic insomnia were recruited from the local community through promotional activities, including leaflet distribution, poster campaigns, and health talks. Older adults who expressed interest in participation were invited to come to the laboratory at HKU medical campus to examine eligibility through semi-structured interviews. Individuals were deemed eligible if they met the following criteria: 1) 50 years or older, 2) ethnic Chinese who can communicate in Cantonese or Mandarin, and 3) fulfil the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) criteria for chronic insomnia, including difficulty in initiating sleep, maintaining sleep or non-restorative sleep, with complaints of impaired daytime functioning, sleep difficulty occurring at least three nights per week present for at least 3 months, 4) able to walk without assistive device (e.g., cane), 5) did not have somatic conditions that limit exercise participation (e.g., limb loss), 6) did not engage in regular moderate-intensity aerobic exercise or mind-body training such as tai chi, yoga, qigong or meditation (i.e., >3 times weekly for >60 minutes per session), 7) did not present serious chronic diseases known to affect sleep (e.g., cancer and autoimmune diseases), 8) did not have dementia or used dementia medications, 9) were not receiving treatment for serious diseases known to affect sleep (e.g., cancer chemotherapy), 10) did not have any chronic pain disorders known to affect sleep, 11) did not have any untreated sleep disorder besides insomnia, including obstructive sleep apnea, periodic leg movement disorder and narcolepsy, 12) previously received or currently receiving CBT-I treatment, and 13) were not shift-workers. A total of 200 older adults with chronic insomnia were recruited. Participants underwent baseline assessments after obtaining informed consent to participate in the project. During the assessments, insomnia severity, sleep quality, depressive symptoms and anxiety symptoms were assessed using the insomnia severity index (ISI), Pittsburgh sleep quality index (PSQI), and hospital anxiety and depression scale. Participants were also asked to wear a wrist actigraph 24 hours for 7 days and complete a 7-day sleep diary in order to assess participants’ sleep quantity and quality comprehensively. Sleep parameters, including sleep-onset latency, total sleep time (TST), wake time after sleep onset (WASO), number of awakenings (NOA), average awaken time (AWT) and sleep efficiency (SE), were objectively estimated based on actigraphy and subjectively estimated based on sleep diary. Participants were instructed to record their use of hypnotic medications in the sleep diary, if any. Assessments were performed again after the intervention (post-assessment) and 1 year from the completion of the intervention (follow-up assessment). Semi-structured interviews were also conducted to examine whether the participants had achieved remission of chronic insomnia (i.e., the participant no longer met the DSM-5 criteria of chronic insomnia). After baseline assessments, participants were randomized at a 1:1 ratio to CBT-I or tai chi groups. Participants in both groups received twice weekly, 60-minute sessions of the respective intervention conducted in small groups and for a total duration of 3 months. The CBT-I intervention covered all the validated elements, including sleep hygiene, sleep restriction, relaxation, stimulus control, and cognitive restructuring, whereas the tai chi intervention delivered the 24-form Yang style tai chi. Participants learned the CBT-I elements and tai chi techniques during the first two months, while the third month served as a consolidation period. Participants were encouraged to achieve a minimum of 80% attendance for their intervention. Statistical analyses were performed using SAS OnDemand for Academics. A per-protocol analysis approach was adopted for the non-inferiority tests. Non-inferiority tests were performed on the change in ISI relative to baseline at post- and follow-up assessments, with a non-inferiority margin of 4 marks of ISI (i.e. 50% of the minimal clinically important difference). All parameters were analyzed using a generalized estimating equations (GEE) model with baseline values adjustment under the intention-to-treat principle. The missing values were not replaced since GEE can accommodate missing data. A significant group-by-time interaction effect indicates a difference in change in a given outcome between interventions along with time, whereas a significant time effect along with a non-significant group-by-time interaction effect indicates both interventions induce a significant change in a given outcome along with time and the change induced by the interventions were not statistically different. Pair-wise comparisons were performed using linear contrast. Statistical significance was accepted as p<0.05. Despite the completed achievement of the objectives in this study, conducting a group-based clinical trial during the COVID-19 pandemic presented a unique set of challenges. One of the primary difficulties was the need to adapt the study design and implementation to comply with evolving public health guidelines and restrictions. At the onset of the pandemic (since early 2020), many regions imposed strict lockdowns and social distancing measures, which made it incredibly challenging to bring participants together for group-based exercise sessions. Concerns over virus transmission and the safety of both participants and researchers had to be carefully navigated. To overcome these obstacles, the research team has explored ways to deliver the exercise program remotely using online platforms and video conferencing technologies. This required developing new protocols for virtual group sessions, ensuring participants had access to the necessary equipment, and troubleshooting any technical issues that arose. Initially, both online and in-person interventions were offered to the first 60 study participants. However, after the easing of COVID-19 restrictions, all interventions resumed in an in-person format. Maintaining participant engagement and adherence to the program also became more difficult during the pandemic. With the added stresses and disruptions to daily life, some participants faced difficulties consistently attending the online sessions or completing the prescribed tai chi exercises on their own. The research team had to implement creative strategies to keep participants motivated and accountable, such as incorporating social support elements, providing regular check-ins, and offering personalized feedback and encouragement. Recruitment and enrollment also presented challenges, as potential participants were generally less inclined to join a study that required in-person or even virtual group interactions during a time of heightened health concerns. The research team had to adjust their outreach and communication tactics, emphasizing the safety measures in place and the potential benefits of engaging in physical activity during the pandemic. Despite all the above mentioned formidable challenges, the research team remained dedicated to the success of the study. Our team worked tirelessly to implement robust safety protocols, including regular COVID-19 testing, enhanced sanitization procedures, and strict adherence to social distancing guidelines. These measures allowed the group-based intervention sessions to proceed safely, even during the most restrictive periods of the pandemic. In the end, the successful completion of the project during the COVID-19 pandemic stands as a testament to the resilience, creativity, and dedication of the research team. The lessons learned from this experience will inform future studies, helping to shape more adaptable and responsive research approaches in the face of unexpected real-life challenges.

17112819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17112819.value: Among the 200 participants (CBT-I: n=100; tai chi: n=100), 166 (CBT-I: n=84; tai chi: n=82) and 167 participants (CBT-I: n=82; tai chi: n=85) completed the post and follow-up assessments, respectively. The adherence rates to the CBT-I and tai chi groups were 80.7% and 78.3%, respectively. Relative to baseline, CBT-I and tai chi induced a 65% and 41% reduction in the ISI score at post-assessment, respectively, while both interventions led to a ~56% reduction at follow-up. A significant time effect (p<0.001) and a non-significant group-by-time interaction effect (p=0.252) were observed in the GEE analysis on ISI. The non-inferiority analysis on ISI using the improvement induced by CBT-I as a reference did not reach statistical significance at post-assessment (P=0.747), but was statistically significant at follow-up (p<0.001). These results indicated that a 3-month tai chi intervention is not as effective as CBT-I in alleviating insomnia severity, although both CBT-I and tai chi interventions confer favorable benefits in reducing insomnia. Notably, the effectiveness of tai chi in alleviating insomnia severity was similar to that of CBT-I at follow-up assessment (i.e., one year after the cessation of the 3-month intervention) due to the continuous reduction of insomnia severity observed in the tai chi group and the sustained improvement in the CBT-I group. Neither CBT-I nor tai chi led to a more robust improvement than the other intervention throughout the study period. Significant time effects along with non-significant group-by-time interaction effects were observed in the NOA (time: p=0.035; group-by-time interaction: p=0.680), TST (time: p<0.001; group-by-time interaction: p=0.603) and SE (time: p=0.030; group-by-time interaction: p=0.685) estimated from the 7-day sleep diary, indicating that both interventions improved these outcomes and that the improvements were not significantly different between groups throughout the study period. Significant group-by-time interaction effect was observed in actigraph-estimated WASO (p=0.019). Pair-wise comparisons showed that CBT-I led to larger improvements in WASO compared with tai chi at post-assessment (p<0.001). However, there was no significant differences in the improvements in WASO at follow-up assessment. At follow-up, self-reported exercise habits were obtained from both groups. It was observed that participants in the tai chi group spent 70% more time doing tai chi, 22% more time doing non-tai chi mind-body exercises, 8% more time doing aerobic exercise, and 31% more time doing muscle conditioning exercises, when compared with the CBT-I group.

17112819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112819.value: Although tai chi may not be as effective as CBT-I in the short term, it may be an effective strategy for treating insomnia in the longer term. These results suggest the potential adoption of tai chi as a self-help approach for insomnia management in real-world settings, given the long waiting time for receiving CBT-I therapy in the present healthcare setting. Our findings might help to inspire further development on this research topic. Exercise interventions prescribed for improving sleep commonly last two months or more, with an intervention frequency of at least twice weekly. To control for the contact time of participants in the two interventions, the number of CBT-I sessions that participants attended in our study (i.e. 24 sessions) was much larger than what they would usually receive in real-world clinical settings (i.e. 4 to 8 sessions). A pragmatic trial can be conducted to further explore the effectiveness of these interventions in alleviating insomnia while mimicking real-life conditions. By giving participants access to either the usual CBT-I treatment or tai chi classes and assessing sleep at various time points, we could observe the impact of the interventions in alleviating the burden of chronic insomnia on the healthcare system.

17112819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112819.value: This study compared the effectiveness of Tai Chi and CBT-I in alleviating insomnia severity in older adults with chronic insomnia. Participants received either Tai Chi or CBT-I training twice weekly for three months. After the intervention, both Tai Chi and CBT-I reduced insomnia severity and improved sleep quality. Notably, CBT-I reduced insomnia severity by a greater magnitude when compared to Tai Chi. The beneficial effects on sleep conferred by both interventions were sustained for a year. Importantly, throughout the one-year post-intervention, participants in the Tai Chi group demonstrated a continued decrease in insomnia severity and reached similar reduction induced by CBT-I. This may be due to the continuous engagement in exercise after completing the Tai Chi intervention. The CBT-I group did not demonstrate a continued reduction and instead maintained. To conclude, Tai Chi did not exhibit similar effectiveness in alleviating insomnia severity compared to CBT-I after three months of training. However, after one year the reduction in insomnia severity was similar between Tai Chi and CBT-I. Thus, Tai Chi can be used as a self-help approach to manage insomnia, especially in the long term.

17112919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17112919.value: 糖尿病視網膜病變（DR）是一種破壞性疾病。DR的最明顯的臨床特徵是微血管不規則，被認為是微血管疾病。但是這一概念現已發展為神經元退化在DR中作為一個早期發生現象，並在DR的發病機制中發揮重要作用的概念。自噬早被確定為神經細胞退化的標誌。自噬是一種在進化過程中保守的機制，允許細胞降解受損蛋白質和細胞內細胞器，從而維持細胞面對逆境的調節反應。然而，當自噬過度上調時，自噬可能變得有害，導致缺血事件中的細胞死亡。視網膜缺血會損害神經元並導致不可逆轉的神經元破壞和損失，從而造成視力損害。由於挽救受損視網膜神經元的治療方案不足以至達到次優效果，因此我們的目標是確立在糖尿病視網病變中，自噬在視網膜神經元退化和視網膜缺血相關的神經元損傷中之關鍵角色，以便在未來制定針對早期DR更及時的治療方法。我們已經研究了1型糖尿病模型Ins2Akita / +小鼠中自噬標誌物的表達。這些小鼠攜帶胰島素2基因的突變，導致胰島素錯誤折疊並最終導致β細胞死亡。它們在4-5週齡時顯示出高血糖症。我們的初步研究結果顯示，在長時間高血糖條件下，6個月大的Ins2Akita / +小鼠視網膜中的自噬標記物上調。有趣的是，視網膜缺血/再灌注損傷隨著這些視網膜中自噬標記物水平的進一步增加而惡化。在暴露於高葡萄糖水平的視網膜前體細胞中，缺氧導致顯著的自噬上調，與我們的體內結果實驗結果脗合。兩項研究結果均指出自噬在早期DR中糖尿病視網膜神經變性和視網膜缺血中的重要性。有鑑於此，我們假設自噬失調對神經元存活是有害的，並且與糖尿病性視網膜變性和視網膜缺血中的神經變性增加有關。在該提議中，我們將使用Ins2Akita / +小鼠作為早期DR的動物模型1）鑑定自噬事件並評估其在早期DR中對雷帕黴素抑制視網膜神經變性的影響，以及2）研究和比較自噬視網膜神經細胞對有或沒有慢性高血糖的缺血的反應。我們的工作不僅會增加我們對DR的理解，而且還提供證據表明針對自噬途徑的神經保護可能是在DR早期發生之視網膜神經元退化的治療方案，也為未來更及時的早期DR潛在治療策略。

17112919.label: Realisation of objectives
17112919.value: In this proposal, we first aimed to identify autophagic events and evaluate the effects of its inhibition by rapamycin in retinal neurodegeneration in early-stage non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (DR). We successfully demonstrated the following findings. 1. Diabetic Ins2Akita/+ (Akita) mice were established to be a model of early-stage non-proliferative DR. 2. Diabetic Akita mice exhibited increased activation of the mTOR signaling pathway in ganglion cell layer (GCL) and inner nuclear layer (INL) of the retina compared to wild-type mice, indicating autophagy dysregulation within specific retinal neurons. 3. Autophagy-related proteins LC3B and p62/SQSTM1 were significantly upregulated in the retinas of Akita mice, suggesting the initiation of the autophagic machinery in response to chronic hyperglycemia. 4. Significant decrease in the b-wave amplitude and delayed b-wave implicit time suggested retinal dysfunction in 26-week-old diabetic Akita mice. 5. Significant thinning of the inner plexiform layer (IPL) and INL, increased apoptotic cells in the GCL and INL, loss of RGCs, and loss of bipolar cell connectivity, suggesting that the functional changes correlated with morphological findings. 6. Rapamycin treatment ameliorated retinal dysfunction, prevented retinal thinning, reduced the loss of RGCs, and preserved synaptic connectivity in the diabetic retina 7. Significant increase in activated microglia in Akita mice. 8. Decrease in microglia in the GCL and OPL but an increase in the INL and IPL 9. Rapamycin treatment decreased the number of activated microglia and restored the distribution of microglia. These results suggested that we have identified retinal neurodegeneration and autophagic events in diabetic Akita mouse retina, a model of early-stage non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy. We further demonstrated the beneficial effects of rapamycin administration in retinal neurodegeneration in early DR. We have completely achieved Objective 1. In objective 2, we aimed to investigate and compare the autophagic response of retinal neurons to ischemia with or without chronic hyperglycemia. We successfully demonstrated the following findings. 1. Established in vivo and in vitro models. Retinal ischemia (2 h) and reperfusion (2 or 22 h) was induced in wild-type and diabetic Ins2Akita/+ mice using a middle cerebral artery occlusion model. R28 retinal precursor cells were subjected to CoCl2-induced hypoxia with or without autophagic inhibitor NH4Cl. 2. Upregulation of autophagic markers in the inner retinae was seen after two hours reperfusion, with tapering of the response following 22 h of reperfusion. 3. LC3-II turnover assays confirmed an increase in autophagic flux in the hypoxic in vitro model. 4. Pharmacological autophagic inhibition under hypoxic conditions decreased cell survival. Our results suggested that autophagic activation in WT MCAO-injured retinae may have occurred earlier than that of Akita MCAO-injured retinae. More importantly, autophagy inhibition with CoCl2-induced hypoxia resulted in significantly decreased R28 cell viability, an increase in cytoplasmic vacuoles and increased alterations in cell morphology as compared with CoCl2-induced hypoxia alone. Our in vitro results using retinal precursor R28 cells that have been differentiated into a more neuronal phenotype correlated well with the increased cell death and autophagic activation seen in the inner retinae in our in vivo model. Yet, no statistically significant different autophagic responses in ischemia/reperfusion injuries were seen between the two glycemic states. We have completely achieved Objective 2.

17112919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17112919.value: We are currently compiling our data. A manuscript will be prepared and will be submitted to international journals e.g. Autography (2023 IF = 14.6, ranked 13/205 Cell Biology, top 6.3%), Diabetes (2023 IF = 8.4, ranked 20/186 Endocrinology & Metabolism, top 10.8%), Diabetologia (2023 IF = 8.4, ranked 12/186 Endocrinology & Metabolism, top 6.5%), eLife (2023 IF = 6.4, ranked 8/109 Biology, top 7.3%). Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of irreversible visual impairment and blindness in the working population. It is essential for timely intervention in the early stage. This work supports the beneficial role of rapamycin, which could be a safe option for early-stage DR patients. The results will provide us with data for future translational research.

17112919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17112919.value: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of irreversible visual impairment and blindness, affecting approximately one-third of the 539 million diabetic patients worldwide. Despite available treatments targeting late-stage DR, there is a lack of timely effective interventions for early-stage DR. DR pathogenesis involves multiple biochemical pathways triggered by prolonged hyperglycemia. One key regulatory pathway is the mTOR signaling pathway, which can be inhibited by rapamycin, a readily available FDA-approved drug with neuroprotective effects. This project investigated the effects of rapamycin on DR using Ins2Akita/+ mice as a model of early-stage non-proliferative DR. We demonstrated that rapamycin is safe and ameliorated retinal dysfunction, prevented retinal thinning, reduced retinal ganglion cell loss, and preserved synaptic connectivity, highlighting its neuroprotective potential in DR. The study also revealed that rapamycin could inhibit mTOR activation and restored autophagy activity in diabetic mouse retina, thus protecting retinal neurons from apoptosis. In conclusion, this thesis provided comprehensive insights into the beneficial effects of rapamycin in an early-stage non-proliferative DR mouse model. The findings supported repurposing rapamycin as a safe intervention option for early-stage DR patients that ophthalmologists choose to prescribe off-label at low cost before DR progresses to the irreversible late stage.

17113019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113019.value: Fifty to one hundred million cases of dengue virus infection are reported every year resulting in over 25,000 deaths (predominantly children under the age of 14), underscoring our need to better understand its underlying mechanism of pathogenesis. Infection with one serotype confers immunity against the particular serotype while increasing incidence of dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) during subsequent infections by other serotypes. DENV is transmitted by mosquito bites, principally of Aedes aegypti and is endemic to over 100 countries around the world, predominantly affecting Southeast Asian countries. The current vaccine being developed has provided mixed results in its efficacy. The recent incidence of local cases in Hong Kong have drawn attention to dengue propagation to non endemic regions and further emphasizes the need to identify cellular targets for development of antivirals in the absence of effective vaccines. The Hong Kong government has launched campaigns with advertisements in public places and residential buildings to increase awareness and caution against the spread of dengue. A molecular understanding of host cellular factors involved in dengue infection is crucial not only to provide novel insights into pathways hijacked by flaviviruses, but also for development of effective antivirals against the pathogen. Targeting virus-induced host factors has the additional benefit of avoiding potential resistance acquired in viruses by mutation and selection. The complexity of the assembly and release of dengue virus provides a potentially rich source of host targets for interference. The modus operandi of propagation of Dengue virus (DENV), Zika, West Nile (WNV) and other members of the family appears to be extensive remodeling of the ER to facilitate virus replication, trafficking, assembly and egress. However, we have been severely limited in our understanding of the role of fundamental biological pathways typically hijacked by flaviviruses. The goal of this proposal is to build on our previous data on the role of lipid droplets to investigate regulation of cellular pathways that significantly contribute to dengue biogenesis - investigated through functional studies and biochemical interactions between host factors and Dengue virus in ways not previously possible, using tools that we have developed. 每年有五亿至一亿人感染登革热病毒，造成超过25,000人死亡，突显了我们需要更好地了解其发病机制。用一种血清型感染赋予针对特定血清型的免疫力，同时在随后的其他血清型感染期间增加登革热的发生率。 DENV通过蚊虫叮咬传播，主要是埃及伊蚊，并且在全世界100多个国家流行，主要影响东南亚国家。最近香港本地病例的发病率已引起人们对登革热传播到非流行地区的关注，并进一步强调在缺乏有效疫苗的情况下需要确定抗病毒药物开发的细胞靶标。目前还没有针对登革热的有效疫苗。对涉及登革热感染的宿主细胞因子的分子理解不仅对于提供对黄病毒劫持的途径的新见解，而且对于开发针对病原体的有效抗病毒剂也是至关重要的。鉴定可以靶向开发新型抗病毒化合物的宿主因子具有避免通过突变和选择在病毒中获得的潜在抗性的额外益处。登革热病毒的组装和释放的复杂性为干扰的宿主目标提供了潜在的丰富来源。 登革病毒（DENV），寨卡，西尼罗河（WNV）和其他家庭成员的繁殖方式似乎是ER的广泛重塑，以促进病毒复制，贩运，组装和出口。然而，我们对通常被黄病毒劫持的基本生物途径的作用的理解受到严重限制。该提议的目标是建立我们之前关于脂滴作用的数据来研究其他宿主细胞途径，这些途径通过功能研究和宿主因子与登革病毒之间的生物化学相互作用研究显着促进登革热生物发生，这是以前不可能的方式，我们开发的工具。

17113019.label: Realisation of objectives
17113019.value: Specific objective 1: Functional screen to identify acylated proteins in flavivirus infection. We completed this section and provided a summary in the previous progress report. We had demonstrated that a chemical proteomics based screening strategy, using an activity-based probe targeting fatty acylated proteins is extremely efficient in uncovering those that are functionally relevant in cellular contexts such as in host-pathogen interactions and immune signalling cascades. Several kinases were identified in these screens (particularly the Src family kinases) supporting their role in the flaviviral lifecycle such as Dengue and Zika. To establish the specific stage in the lifecycle where this occurred, we also tested acylation of these kinases in cells engineered to express virus like particles to delineate assembly/secretion from that of entry and replication. For both Dengue and Zika virus like particles, acylation of these kinases could be clearly detected. To identify what these acylated kinases interacted with, we performed mass spectrometry bases analyses from cells either infected with live virus or producing virus-like particles. Potential candidates were identified by trypsin digestion, mass spectrometry, and spectral counting of peptides on immunoprecipitated material. We validated the mass spectrometry (MS) hits in lysates prepared from mock-infected, virus-infected, or VLP-producing samples. Our investigations revealed that Src-like kinases are upregulated and redistributed to Rab11 and LC3-positive compartments upon virus infection, culminating in their secretion into the extracellular medium. We therefore performed a detailed biochemical characterization on the expression, subcellular localization and turnover of these kinases in infected cells as a function of time. Findings from this aim was published in Nature Communication (Li et al, Nature Communications, 2020). Specific objective 2: Genetic validation of the role of Src-family kinases in flavivirus infection To study the role of selected SFKs in flavivirus infection, particularly in viral assembly and transport along the secretory pathway, we inhibited SFK activity using two approaches. First, we selected a commercially available SFK inhibitor – SU6656, which specifically blocks their activation as measured by the absence of their phosphorylated forms. Our results indicated that 5μM SU6656 was sufficient to cause ~10-fold reduction in viral titers. To genetically deplete SFKs, we transfected siRNA targeting the individual kinases and measured both viral titers, and secretion of VLPs Among the three kinases, depletion of Lyn had the most significant effect, with ≥10-fold reduction in viral titers for all strains, with no apparent effect on cell viability or intracellular vRNA levels. These data were reflected in the VLP-secretion assay, where a similar reduction was noted in Lyn-depleted cells. A combined depletion of Lyn with either Fyn or Src displayed an additive effect on inhibition of VLP-secretion. Collectively, these results suggested that Lyn in particular, plays a critical role in regulating secretion of viral progenies. To confirm the role of Lyn in flavivirus infections, we generated a range of Lyn-deleted cell lines using the CRISPR/Cas9 technology. Lyn-/- cells were also reconstituted with wild-type (rLyn) and a mutant variant of Lyn (C468A) through lentiviral transduction. Virus production was significantly attenuated in all Lyn-/- cells, and could be rescued in the rLyn expressing cells, but not in those expressing the kinase inactive C468A mutant. Findings from this aim was published in Nature Communication (Li et al, Nature Communications, 2020). Specific objective 3: Deciphering the role of acylated Lyn kinase function using proximity dependent labelling and biochemical fractionation SFKs are equipped with glycine and cysteine at their N-terminus, which are typically acylated with myristoyl and palmitoyl chains respectively. S-palmitoylation has been shown to dictate the spatial distribution and trafficking characteristics of several proteins including SFKs. A mutant with a cysteine to serine substitution was generated to prevent palmitoylation of Lyn. Wild-type and C3S mutant were then challenged with either the 4 serotypes of Dengue or Zika virus. We collected supernatants from mock and infected cells to measure viral titers by plaque assay and viral RNA by RT qPCR. Virus production was significantly attenuated in all Lyn-/- cells, and could be rescued in the rLyn expressing cells, but not in those expressing the kinase inactive C468A mutant or the palmitoylation deficient C3S mutant. To further characterise the secreted virus particles, we resolved the extracellular particles from [35S]cys/met-labelled wt and Lyn-deficient cells by SDS-PAGE and detected by autoradiography. We observed a significant reduction in abundance of extracellular virus particles from Lyn-deficient (C3S mutant) cells. Secreted particles also displayed a loss in prM-cleavage indicative of immature viral progenies. To verify that attenuated virus production was specifically due to defective secretion, we measured appearance of VLPs in the supernatants. For both Dengue and Zika, we observed a significant loss in VLP-secretion from Lyn-/- cells, which could be rescued in cells expressing wild-type Lyn (rLyn) but not C468A or C3S mutants, suggesting that both its kinase activity and palmitoylation are necessary for virus release. To determine how progeny virions/VLPs triggered Lyn-dependent export via secretory organelles, we determined whether the viral envelope prME alone could trigger their biogenesis. To do so, we generated stable cells secreting recombinant VLPs carrying a furin-resistant prM (H98A) and another carrying a second mutation (E E62K) that renders it furin-sensitive as reported previously. Furin-sensitive VLPs secreted from wild-type cells displayed the anticipated pattern of cleaved pr and M fragments, whereas those carrying furin-resistant VLPs comprised uncleaved prM. Interestingly, whereas wild-type and furin-sensitive VLPs followed Lyn-dependent secretion, the furin-resistant VLPs displayed no secretion defect in Lyn-/- cells, indicating that they followed a different transport mechanism Findings from this aim was published in Nature Communication (Li et al, Nature Communications, 2020).

17113019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113019.value: The research conducted has opened up news avenues that we will be developing. In particular, given the importance of the Src-family kinases in driving unconventional secretion of Dengue and Zika viruses, it will be important to determine whether this feature is universal amongst other members within the flaviviridae family and other positive sense RNA viruses such as coronaviruses and alphaviruses. Furthermore, results obtained were using in vitro infection models, which will be developed further using in vivo models to determine whether inhibiting this family of kinases can lead to attenuated infection. Lastly, this study emphasises the multiple routes of virus egress that exists in host cells. Identification of alternative Lyn-independent routes will be important to understand fundamental concepts in virus infection and the broad tissue tropism displayed by flaviviruses.

17113019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113019.value: Among the various host cellular processes that are hijacked by flaviviruses, very few mechanisms have been described with regard to viral egress. Here we screened for host factors that are specifically acylated upon infection and identified Src-family kinases; we therefore investigated how flaviviruses exploit Src family kinases (SFKs) for exit from infected cells. We identified Lyn as a critical component for secretion of Dengue and Zika infectious particles and their corresponding virus like particles (VLPs). Pharmacological inhibition or genetic depletion of the SFKs, Lyn in particular, blocked virus secretion. Lyn-/- cells were severely impaired in virus release and were rescued when reconstituted with wild-type Lyn, but not a kinase- or palmitoylation-deficient Lyn mutant. We established that virus particles were secreted in two distinct populations – one as free virions and the other enclosed within membranes. Lyn was critical for the latter, which consisted of proteolytically processed, infectious virus progenies within autophagosome-derived vesicles. This process depended on Ulk1, Rab GTPases and SNARE complexes implicated in secretory but not degradative autophagy and occurred with significantly faster kinetics than the conventional secretory pathway. Our study has therefore revealed a previously undiscovered Lyn-dependent exit route of flaviviruses in LC3+ secretory organelles that enables them to evade circulating antibodies and might dictate tissue tropism.

17113319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17113319.value: Primary Sjögren’s syndrome (SS) is an autoimmune disease characterized by lymphocytic infiltration and tissue destruction of salivary and lachrymal glands, leading to severe dry eyes and dry mouth symptoms. Due to the limited understanding of etiologies, SS patients have suffered from a lack of effective treatments in clinical management. Recent studies have suggested a critical role of cytokines in the development of autoimmune disease. Using an established murine model of experimental SS (ESS), we previously identified interleukin (IL)-17A as a critical mediator in the pathogenesis of SS. Among the 6 members of IL-17 family, the role of IL-25 (also called IL-17E) in the SS pathogenesis is largely unclear. We recently reported significantly increased IL-25 expression in the salivary glands (SG) of SS patients and mice with ESS, which was closely correlated with disease activities, but how IL-25 contributes to SS development remains to be investigated. In our pilot studies, we found that mouse plasma cells (PCs) expressed high levels of IL-17RB (the receptor of IL-25) while IL-25 treatment significantly promoted the survival of PCs in culture. In ESS mice, we observed significantly expanded autoantibody-producing IL-17RB+ PCs during disease progression. Moreover, we found that anti-IL-25 treatment markedly suppressed PC response and ESS progression in diseased mice at chronic stage. Together, our preliminary findings have provided a strong baseline for testing our hypothesis that IL-25 plays a key role in regulating PC response during ESS development. In this project, we will identify a novel function of IL-25 in regulating PC response in ESS development. Moreover, our proposed studies will elucidate the molecular mechanism underlying IL-25-mediated PC survival and function. Furthermore, we will explore new therapeutic strategy by targeting IL-25 for the treatment of SS, a disease with high social relevance in Hong Kong. 原發性乾燥綜合徵(SS)是一種由免疫細胞攻擊或破壞外分泌腺(淚腺、唾液腺等)引起腺體慢性炎症為主要病理表現的自身免疫性疾病。 SS患者的臨床症狀以明顯的口乾和眼乾為主。 SS的發病機制尚不清楚，因此在臨床治療上缺乏有效針對SS患者的方案。 近期的研究成果提示炎性細胞因子在SS的病程發展中起了重要作用。我們在前期的研究中建立了實驗性SS（ESS）的小鼠模型，並發現细胞因子中白介素（IL）-17A在ESS的病理機制中是關鍵的致病因素。而在IL-17蛋白家族成員中，IL-25（亦稱作IL-17E）在SS的病理機制中的作用尚不清楚。我們近期報導了SS病人和ESS小鼠的唾液腺中均顯著性高表達IL-25，然而IL-25是如何參與病程的發展仍需進一步研究。本課題的前期研究提示表達IL-25受體的B細胞能分泌大量自身抗體，而IL-25亦能促進漿細胞的细胞活性。在ESS小鼠中，這群表达IL-25受体的漿細胞的比例和數量隨著疾病的發展顯著性升高。我們進而發現IL-25的中和抗體亦可對處於ESS慢性期的發病小鼠有治療作用，提示了IL-25在SS的病程發展中，尤其是疾病的慢性期起了重要作用。因此，靶向IL-25可能作為治療SS患者的新方法。

17113319.label: Realisation of objectives
17113319.value: 1. To examine a role of IL-25 in regulating B cell maturation and function We first examined the expression of IL-17 receptor B (IL-17RB), the key subunit of IL-25 receptor, on various B cell subsets. Q-PCR analysis and flow cytometric profiles showed the highest expression of IL-25R in plasma cells compared with other B cell subsets while cytospin assay demonstrated the expression of IL-25R in sorting purified plasma cells. During ESS progression, the numbers of plasma cells with IL-25R expression were significantly increased. Moreover, IL-25R+ plasma cells contained almost 4-fold higher frequencies of anti-SSA IgG- and anti-M3R IgG-secreting cells. To determine an intrinsic role of IL-25 signaling in regulating PC, we purified IL-17RB+ and IL-17RB- plasma cells from ESS mice and transferred these cells into immunodeficient Rag2-/- mice, respectively. The recipient Rag2-/- mice with adoptive transfer of IL-17RB+ plasma cells showed significantly higher serum autoantibodies levels than those in the recipient mice with the transfer of IL-17RB- plasma cells as examined by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Moreover, enzyme-linked immune absorbent spot (ELISpot) assay revealed significantly higher numbers of autoreactive plasma cells in the recipient mice with adoptive transfer of IL-17RB+ plasma cells. We further investigated the histology of submandibular glands (SG) in the recipient mice. Although the severities of lymphocytic infiltration were comparable, immunoglobulin G (IgG) deposition in SG was observed in IL-17RB+ plasma cells -transferred but not IL-17RB- plasma cells -transferred Rag2-/- mice as detected by immunofluorescent staining and confocal microscopy. Similarly, sorting-purified plasma cells from immunized WT and IL-25R KO mice were adoptively transferred into B cell-deficient muMT mice. Transfer of WT plasma cells drove salivary hypofunction while IL-25R KO plasma cell transfer significantly improved saliva secretion and ameliorated SG tissue damage. Moreover, ELISPOT assay and flow cytometric analysis revealed dramatically reduced numbers of autoreactive plasma cells. 2. To determine the role of IL-25 in regulating plasma cell response during ESS development Wild-type (WT), IL-25 knockout (KO) and IL-25R KO mice were immunized with SG-derived protein for ESS induction. Compared with WT controls, IL-25 KO and IL-25R KO mice exhibited markedly improved saliva flow rates, decreased serum levels of autoantibodies against SSA and M3R, and ameliorated SG tissue inflammation. IL-25 KO and IL-25R KO mice exhibited significantly decreased numbers of autoantibody-secreting plasma cells as evidenced by ELISPOT assays. Moreover, high-paremeter flow cytometry identified plasma cells and other B cell subsets by tSNE analysis and showed significantly decreased numbers of plasma cells in spleen and bone marrow. However, germinal center B cells were not affected by deficiency of IL-25 signaling, suggesting that IL-25 directly regulates plasma cell responses. Long-lived plasma cells (LLPCs) have been recognized as important players in the pathogenesis of autoimmune diseases5. We found that the EpcamhighCXCR3- plasma cells with LLPC features displayed high expression of IL-25R while these cells were remarkably reduced in both spleen and bone marrow from IL-25 deficient mice compared with those in WT mice upon ESS induction. To investigate the direct effects of IL-25 on plasma cells, purified B cells were cultured under plasma cell polarization conditions in the presence of IL-25. IL-25 treatments did not affect plasma cell differentiation in culture. However, IL-25 markedly enhanced survival of polarized plasma cells as well as purified plasma cells from ESS mice. In addition, IL-25 treatment significantly increased the survival rates of NSI cell, an immortal cell line derived from mouse B cell lymphoblast. 3. To elucidate the molecular mechanisms of IL-25-mediated plasma cell survival and function To characterize the molecular mechanisms by which IL-25 regulates plasma cells survival during ESS development, plasma cells from ESS mice were purified by FACS sorting, followed by treatment with recombinant murine IL-25 for various time durations. Gene expression analysis showed that IL-25 enhanced the expression of various survival-associated genes, among which we identified Mcl1, a key survival gene in effector B cells, as the mostly affected one upon IL-25 stimulation. Indeed, Western Blotting (WB) analysis showed a dramatic increase in Mcl1 expression in NSI cells with IL-25 treatments. As expected, Mcl1 inhibition promoted plasma cell death. In bone marrow plasma cells, IL-25 and IL-25R deficiency resulted in significant loss of Mcl1 expression, which may account for the reduction of LLPCs in ESS and NP-immunized mice. We next performed RNA-sequencing analysis on purified plasma cells with and without IL-25 treatments. Both GO and GSEA analysis suggest an enrichment of JAK-STAT signaling in plasma cells upon IL-25 treatments. Consistently, IL-25 activated STAT3 in plasma cells while STAT3 inhibition profoundly reduced IL-25-mediated upregulation of Mcl1, suggesting that IL-25 sustains plasma cell longevity through STAT3-Mcl1 axis. The survival of LLPCs requires sufficient energy supply. By analyzing a scRNA-seq dataset on SS patients, we found high glycolysis levels in plasma cells compared with other immune populations. Moreover, plasma cells from ESS mice showed highest glucose dependence compared with germinal center B and memory B cells using SCENITH (Single Cell Metabolism by Profiling Translation Inhibition), a flow-cytometry-based method for energy metabolism profiling22. Inhibition of glycolysis led to a significant reduction of plasma cells, suggesting an important role of glycolytic metabolism in plasma cell responses. In culture, polarized IL-25R KO plasma cells showed lower expression of glucose transporter 1 (Glut1) and glucose dependence compared with WT controls while IL-25 treatment significantly increased glucose dependence in cultured plasma cells. In addition, IL-25 treatment increased glucose uptake, enhanced glycolytic gene expression, and promoted glycolysis metabolism in NSI cells. These data show that IL-25 supports glycolysis of plasma cells, which could contribute to the longevity of these cells. 4. To explore the novel therapeutic strategies by targeting IL-25 in ESS mice To determine the therapeutic potential of targeting IL-25 for treating SS, we performed preclinical evaluation on ESS development in mice with administration of neutralization antibodies against IL-25. Intraperitoneal injection of IL-25 neutralisation antibodies markedly improved SG secretory functions in established ESS mice after 4-week treatments. Consistently, histological analysis showed attenuated tissue inflammation and damage in ESS mice upon anti-IL-25 treaments. Notably, blockade of IL-25 resulted in a significant reduction of bone marrow plasma cells and CXCR3-Epcamhigh LLPCs in ESS mice, suggesting that IL-25 neutralization could serve as a strategy to target LLPCs. Moreover, we also observed reduced expression of Mcl1 in bone marrow plasma cells from ESS mice treated with anti-IL-25. Since we detected elevated expression of IL-25 in SG tissues during ESS development, we blocked SG IL-25 signaling by salivary cannulation of anti-IL-25 neutralisation antibodies in ESS mice. While Control-IgG-treated mice showed salivary hypofunction, local targeting of IL-25 enhanced saliva secretion and decreased SG glandular inflammation with a prominent reduction of SG plasma cells. Collectively, the preclinical analysis showed that IL-25 may serve as a promising target for targeting plasma cells for the treatment of SS patients.

17113319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17113319.value: Our findings reveal a novel role of IL-25 in sustaining long-lived plasma cell (LLPC) responses by regulating Mcl-1 in the pathogenesis of SS. We found that IL-25 promoted LLPC responses in ESS mice and sustained plasma cell survival via STAT3-Mcl1 axis. Long-term survival of plasma cells require complex extrinsic signals from the nitch. Since IL-25 and many survival factors rely on STAT3 activation, the synergistical effects of IL-25 with other cytokines and chemokines in LLPCs will be further investigated. Plasma cells are resistant to conventional B cell-depletion therapies such as rituximab. It is still challenging to target LLPCs due to limited understanding of their phenotypes and survival mechanisms. Our data revealed that blockade of IL-25 by SG cannulation and systemic administration of neutralisation antibodies improved SG secretory functions and attenuated SG tissue inflammation accompanied with reduced LLPC responses in bone marrow, suggesting that blocking IL-25 signaling may serve as a novel strategy to target LLPCs in the development of autoimmune diseases. We will further investigate the combinational therapy of B cell-depletion and IL-25 blockade in our well-established animal models.

17113319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17113319.value: Primary Sjögren’s syndrome (SS) is an autoimmune disease characterized by dry eyes and dry mouth. Due to the limited understanding of disease etiologies, effective treatments are still lacking. Using an established murine model of experimental SS (ESS), we previously identified interleukin (IL)-17A as a critical mediator in the pathogenesis of SS. In this project, we investigated the roles of IL-25, another key member of IL-17 family cytokines, in the development of SS. We analyzed saliva and salivary gland biopsy samples from SS patients and found positively correlation of IL-25 levels with disease severities and plasma cell responses. Moreover, IL-25 knockout (KO) and IL-25R KO mice showed ameliorated disease progression compared with wild-type (WT) mice upon ESS induction. Additionally, deficiency of IL-25 signaling resulted in attenuated long-lived plasma cell responses. In culture, IL-25 promoted plasma cell survival via STAT3-Mcl1 axis and increased plasma cell glycolytic metabolism. Preclinical studies showed that IL-25 neutralization ameliorated ESS development in mice. Together, our findings reveal a novel role of IL-25 in sustaining long-lived plasma cell responses by regulating Mcl-1 in the pathogenesis of SS. Blocking IL-25 signaling may serve as a novel strategy to target LLPCs for treating SS and other autoimmune diseases.

17114319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114319.value: Schizophrenia is a serious mental illness affecting 1% of the population and is the eighth leading cause of disability-associated life year lost. Studies have generally suggested 20-50% patients do not respond to the antipsychotic medications, mostly blocker of dopamine D2 receptors of the brain, and are considered as treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS). Individuals of this group are candidates for clozapine which has an established efficacy for TRS. The response to clozapine is on the other hand still limited, in the range of 30-70%. Those who did not respond to clozapine are termed as ultra-resistant schizophrenia. Understanding of the neurobiological mechanism of treatment-resistant and ultra-resistant schizophrenia would enhance our understanding of the neurobiological mechanisms of illness and improve the clinical management of patients by establishing neurobiological markers for these clinical stages. It has been proposed that treatment-resistant schizophrenia is likely to be an illness characterized by non-dopaminergic abnormalities. Apart from dopaminergic abnormalities, glutamatergic abnormalities have also been proposed as a possible pathophysiology of schizophrenia and treatment-resistant state. The link between GABAergic interneuron with the glutamate receptors subtypes has been proposed. Proton Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) could be used to measure the relative level of glutamate and GABA in the brain. However, there are only two MRS studies conducted to study patterns of changes of glutamate level in treatment-resistant schizophrenia and none has been conducted to study the level of GABA in this group of patients. There is no study looking at the predictive value of the metabolite level on the effect of clozapine with a longitudinal approach. The proposed study is a longitudinal case-control study exploring the neurobiological mechanisms of treatment-resistant and ultra-treatment resistant schizophrenia using spectroscopy. This could allow not only the exploration of the role of the two neurotransmitter systems in the development of treatment resistance but also look at the predictive value of the level of these metabolites. Because of the individual pharmacokinetic differences, blood antipsychotic level will be measured in the current study to improve on the accuracy of determination of the treatment-resistant state. 思覺失調症是一種嚴重精神疾病，影響約百分之一的總人口，並在失能調整生命年負擔十大原因中排行第八位。研究發現約二至五成的患者屬難治型思覺失調，他們在服用主要為多巴胺D2受體阻斷劑的典型抗精神病藥物後，病情沒有得以改善。雖然「可致律」（氯氮平）對於難治型患者具有療效，當中也只有約三至七成患者的病情得到改善，其他患者則屬於超難治型思覺失調。從神經生理學觀點來看，了解難治型及超難治型思覺失調的生理機制能加深對思覺失調症的理解，並藉著確立不同臨床階段的神經生物標記來改善患者的臨床管理。有學者認為，難治型思覺失調症和非多巴胺能系統異常有關。除多巴胺能系統功能障礙外，麩胺酸能系統失調也可能是思覺失調症及難治性的病態生理特徵；麩胺酸受體類型與γ胺基丁酸能中間神經元也息息相關。質子磁共振波譜（Proton Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy; 1H-MRS）能夠量度腦內麩胺酸和γ胺基丁酸的相對水平。然而，只有兩個磁共振波譜研究探討過難治型思覺失調症的麩胺酸變化，γ胺基丁酸的水平則有待探究。目前並未有縱向研究探討代謝物水平能否預測「可致律」的藥效。本擬議研究為縱向病例對照研究，旨在以磁共振波譜探索難治型及超難治型思失調症的腦神經生理機制，包括兩個神經遞質系統在發展藥物抗性中的角色和代謝物水平對治療藥效的預測價值。由於個體之間有藥代動力學上的差異，本研究會量度血液中的抗精神病藥物水平，以提高介定難治性的準確度。

17114519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17114519.value: 脊柱側凸是脊柱的側向偏離。青少年特發性脊柱側凸（AIS）是臨床上最常見的病例。這種疾病具有很強的遺傳病因。大約佔0.3％的青少年被診斷為其側彎角度超過40° 的AIS。研究大角度AIS中涉及的基因對於臨床了解怎樣從小角度到大角度脊柱側凸的進展非常重要。我們從一個有九個大角度患者的家庭收集數據。該家族顯示常染色體顯性遺傳模型。我們在一項由大學種子研究基金支持的初步研究中, 對9名患者和3名正常人進行了全基因組測序。發現與AIS共分離的新基因中檢測到一個變體（R593W），命名為Scohku，並預測它是人和小鼠之間保守的膜蛋白。在另一個家族中檢測到第二個（M15L）突變。然而，Scohku中的突變如何導致AIS仍不清楚。我們通過CRISPR / Cas9方法生成了攜帶人突變（Scohku中的R593W）的小鼠模型，以研究Scohku的功能。在兩個月的雜合小鼠中觀察到AIS表型，並且在該申請中提出了進一步的研究。使用AIS小鼠模型，我們將能評估該小鼠模型如何模擬人類AIS以確定側凸的起始和進展，以及AIS在組織，細胞和分子中的發病機制。我們將在體内和體外AIS小鼠中基因的發病機制。此外，AIS是一種複雜的遺傳疾病，由於基因座異質性，必須有額外的新基因引起家族性AIS。我們收集了三個沒有Scohku突變的新AIS譜系。因此，具體目標2的目的是對三個新的AIS家族進行全基因組測序以檢測新的遺傳因子。該項目可以提供有關AIS發病機制的見解，並為AIS的未來預防，診斷和治療提供見解。

17114519.label: Realisation of objectives
17114519.value: Scoliosis is a deformity characterized with lateral deviation of the spine. This abnormality can result in back pain, unsightliness, and early death from cardiopulmonary compromise, if left untreated. Adolescent Idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is the most frequently observed type of scoliosis in clinics. Inheritance patterns of AIS are complex. We have detected a mutation in a gene, which causes Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) in a family. The gene involved in AIS is glycine transporter 1 (GlyT 1), of which transports glycine in glutamatergic synapse to keep glycine concentrations below saturation level. Furthermore, we also detected two new mutations in sporadic AIS. The two rare heterozygous missense mutations (c. C1984T, p. R662W and c. A617T, p. Y206F) in the SLC6A9 gene in two pedigrees of familial AIS were identified by whole genome sequencing (WGS). Besides, eight more mutations of SLC6A9 were identified in sporadic AIS cases contributed by our collaborators from Beijing and USA. SLC6A9 encodes a glycine transporter 1 critical in the clearance of glycine in excitatory and inhibitory synapses. By clinical examinations, we found that the glycine concentrations are significantly increase in AIS affected compared with unaffected in Familial AIS. We also found that the glycine uptake activities of mutations of GLYT1 were impaired, mainly due to the impaired cytomembrane localization. Endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus retention and unstably expression in cytomembrane may be the leading causes for the impaired cell membrane localization of GLYT1 mutants. We generated a mouse model with the human mutation (R593W). We have successfully generated F0, F1 and some F2 generations. Thus, mutation was found to be fixed in the germ-line, and scoliosis phenotypes were observed in two-month heterozygous mice. X-ray examinations was conducted to investigate the spinal structure, including the bony alignment, bony spurs, and discs. However, after screening over one hundred mice, the original phenotypes of spine curve were not significant and this would be explained that mouse is quadruped animal. Therefore, we further generated a glyt1 mutant zebrafish model to address how glyt1 dysfunction may interfere with the spinal alignment in AIS. Glyt1 mutant zebrafish displayed curly body, diminished swimming with a reduced survival rate. That would be the result of disruption of left and right body axis coordination in the absent of malformation in motor circuits, skeletal muscle, and central nervous system (CNS). Interestingly, some glyt1 mutant zebrafish exhibited apparent spinal curvature that first appeared on the juvenile stage, recapitulating human AIS. Pharmacological ablation of glyt1 in wild type larvae phenocopied the spinal curvature observed in glyt1 mutant zebrafish. Furthermore, selective blockade of glycine receptor partially rescued the spinal phenotypes in glyt1 mutant zebrafish. All these data indicate that glyt1 regulates glycine concentration in CNS and thereby maintains the proper left and right coordination of the body axis, which implicated in the development of AIS. Our manuscript of this work has been submitted to Journal of Clinical Investigate (JCI) and we have answered the questions/comments from reviewers. The second version will be submitted soon. Please find attached manuscript in the section of output.
