17117519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17117519.value: This study aims to understand the mechanistic basis of pre-metastatic niche formation in lungs driven by extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The findings demonstrated an imperative role of nidogen-1 (NID1), carried by EV, in pre-metastatic niche formation in the lung by enhancing angiogenesis and pulmonary endothelial permeability to facilitate colonization of cells and extrahepatic metastasis. More importantly, EV-NID1 activates lung fibroblasts to secrete TNFR1 which subsequently facilitates the colonization, growth and motility of incoming metastatic cells. From the clinical perspective, the levels of NID1 in circulating EVs and serum TNFR1 of HCC patients display a positive correlation and association with tumor stages. Therapeutically, administration of anti-TNFR1 antibody effectively diminished extrahepatic metastasis in mice. Taken together, this study demonstrated the pivotal role of EV-NID1 induced TNFR1 in HCC metastasis and the potential application of EV-NID1 and serum TNFR1 as noninvasive biomarkers for HCC. Our findings also offer promise for a new direction of HCC treatment by blocking signals mediated by oncogenic EVs (Advanced Science 2020). The finding of this study has directly led to the generation of a neutralizing antibody against NID1 and a non-provisional patent application on Nidogen 1 as a diagnostic marker and therapeutic target of hepatocellular carcinoma, composition and methods was submitted in 2021. The findings of the study were presented in 3 international conferences, including Cold Spring Harbor Asia Meeting: Liver, Biology, Diseases & Cancer Conference 2019, The International Society for Extracellular Vesicles 2019 Annual meeting and The Liver Week 2021 virtual meeting. The student who is involved in this study was awarded the Foreign Investigator Award for her poster presentation at the international conference, The Liver Week 2021 and the Best Presentation Award at the Postgraduate Student Retreat of Department of Pathology.

17117519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17117519.value: EV research has been expanded tremendously in recent years. EVs are regarded as a molecular signature of the parental cells. Recent advancement in liquid biopsies holds the promise of implementing EV content for clinical diagnostics. Much of the current research is aimed at finding promising biomarkers of diseases through validation and better molecular candidates to maximize the potentials of targeted therapies. The identification of upregulated nidogen-1 (NID1) in circulating EVs of hepatocellular cancer (HCC) patients compared to that of healthy individuals, suggesting the potential of NID1 as a biomarker and therapeutic target of HCC. NID1 is found to localize on the surface of EVs which enables the blockage of EV-NID1 by neutralizing antibody. This background information has led to the idea of the generation of a monoclonal NID1 neutralizing antibody which is unavailable in the market. This antibody will be an essential reagent for basic and translational research and will be potentially modified for future therapeutic purpose. With the funding provided by ITSP Seed Projects (Reference number ITS/228/20), we successfully custom-made a mouse monoclonal anti-NID1 neutralizing antibody. This antibody was shown to effectively reduce HCC cell growth and motility in vitro and dampen liver tumor formation and extrahepatic metastasis to lungs. Under the same treatment conditions, the anti-NID1 antibody did not exert cytotoxicity to normal liver cell line and cause adverse effect to mice. These findings suggest the feasibility of translating the blockade of NID1 into targeted therapy of cancer patients with high blood level of EV-NID1.

17117519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17117519.value: In this study, nidogen 1 (NID1) in extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from liver cancer cells was shown to promote lung pre-metastatic niche formation by activating fibroblasts. Activated fibroblasts secreted tumor necrosis factor receptor 1 (TNFR1) facilitated lung colonization of tumor cells and augmented motility of HCC cells. Analysis of serum EV-NID1 and TNFR1 of patients revealed their positive correlation and association with liver cancer stages. Administration of anti-TNFR1 antibody effectively diminished lung metastasis in mice. These results demonstrated the interplay of tumor EVs and activated fibroblasts in pre-metastatic niche formation and the blockage of their communication inhibits distant metastasis to lungs. Results of the study revealed for the first time about the existence and critical oncogenic functions of NID1 in EVs. From the clinical perspective, the progressive increase in the levels of NID1 in circulating EVs and serum TNFR1 of patients along liver cancer progression, suggesting the potentials of these molecules as non-invasive biomarkers for the early detection of liver cancer. Lastly, our findings offer promise for the new direction of liver cancer treatment by targeting oncogenic EV components and blocking the signaling mediated by EVs derived from liver cancer.

17117619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17117619.value: 研究背景和关键问题：在牙髓再生领域，牙根的特殊解剖结构（根尖孔狭小）导致再生组织移植后即处于缺氧微环境中，因此组织工程结构的即时血管化是牙髓再生成功的关键。我们的前期研究结果表明稳定表达缺氧诱导因子1α （Hypoxia-inducible factor-1alpha ，HIF-1α）的乳牙牙髓干细胞（Stem cells from deciduous teeth，SHED) 可使细胞预适应缺氧环境，通过促进内皮细胞发芽并且发挥血管周细胞的作用促进新生血管的稳定，从而促进血管再生。虽然HIF-1α 稳定表达后VEGF分泌的增加部分解释了内皮细胞发芽增多，但不能解释SHED在缺氧条件下对新生毛细血管的稳定作用，因此我们探究了该作用发生的机制，并发现SHED在缺氧或HIF-1α稳定表达时， 轴突导向蛋白4D （Semaphorin-4D，SEMA4D）的分泌显著增加。虽然已有研究表明SEMA4D可通过激活Plexin-B1-RhoA信号轴调节周细胞的募集。然而，迄今为止SEMA4D-Plexin-B1-RhoA信号轴在乳牙牙髓干细胞对血管形态发生及成熟中的作用及机制尚未明确。 研究目的和方法： 1. 阐明稳定表达HIF1-α的SHED分泌的SEMA4D对其自身和内皮细胞的作用。将SHED和人脐静脉内皮细胞（Human umbilical vein endothelial cells，HUVEC）（对照组，Plexin-B1敲基因组以及RhoA抑制组）培养在取自稳定表达HIF-1α的SHED（对照组和SEMA4D敲基因组）的条件培养基中，检测血小板衍生生长因子-B（Platelet-derived growth factor-B，PDGF-B）和血管生成素样蛋白4 （Angiopoietin-like protein 4，ANGPTL4）的表达。 2. 研究SEMA4D-Plexin-B1-RhoA信号轴在SHED分化为功能性周细胞中的作用。 SHED将在取自HUVEC（对照组，可溶性SEMA4D处理组，Plexin-B1敲基因组，PDGF-B抗体组）的条件培养基中培养，并检测细胞的增殖、迁移，周细胞标记物的表达和在基质胶和纤维蛋白珠上血管的形态。 3. 体内研究稳定表达HIF-1α的SHED是否通过SEMA4D-Plexin-B1信号传导增强血管分布和血管周细胞募集。将包埋在基质胶中的HIF-1α 稳定的SHED（对照组，SEMA4D敲基因组，Plexin-B1敲基因组）和HUVEC（对照组，Plexin-B1敲基因组）皮下注射到免疫缺陷小鼠中，并在第7天和第14天收取样本。血管、周细胞覆盖和血管渗漏将分别通过组织学，免疫荧光和在样本取出前30分钟注射1％伊文思蓝染料至尾静脉来评估。 研究意义：本研究将探究体外和体内培养条件下稳定表达HIF-1α的SHED通过分泌SEMA4D所发挥的稳固血管结构的作用。 本实验将不仅深入探索缺氧微环境下内皮细胞和SHED之间的交互作用，而且将有助于推动牙髓再生的研究进展以及可预见性牙髓再生标准的制定。

17118119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118119.value: In the last few decades, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has spread in the world and posed tremendous healthcare burdens globally, largely attributable to its associated complications. Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a devastating microvascular complication of diabetes, is the leading cause of blindness among the working-age populations. The heritability of DR has been clearly demonstrated from twins and familial aggregation studies. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have become powerful tools to delineate the genetic basis of complex diseases since the last decade. To date, several GWAS for DR have been conducted in T1DM or T2DM patients of different ethnic groups to identify the susceptibility variants for the development of DR. However, the heritability of DR is still remained largely unexplained. We hypothesise that additional novel susceptibility variants for DR are yet to be identified. The missing heritability of DR may also be contributed by low-frequency or rare functional variants that have not been captured by the traditional genotyping arrays. The use of an Asian-focused genotyping array may allow us to detect novel Asian-specific risk variants for DR in our population. We aim to perform a comprehensive two-stage GWAS on sight-threatening DR (STDR), using the latest Illumina Infinium® Asian Screening Array (ASA) with subsequent replication and functional validation analyses. The use of ASA has allowed us to investigate the variants that are most relevant and specific to our population, which may be absent from the conventional genotyping arrays that have been built primarily on European genomes. We previously genotyped a total of 1500 Chinese patients with T2DM, including 750 cases with STDR and 750 controls without DR, using the ASA. In the discovery stage analysis, we identified a list of susceptibility loci showing suggestive associations with STDR that have not been previously reported. Some of these novel susceptibility genes are highly functionally relevant to the disease biology of DR. Furthermore, a number of the newly identified STDR-associated variants are found to be Asian-specific. Here, we propose to follow-up on these potential association signals in both the internal and external replication cohorts, totalling over 4500 patients with T2DM. Joint analysis of the discovery and replication stage data, which provide a more significant power to detect novel association signals, will then be conducted. Functional validation analysis will also be performed. Findings from this project will provide novel insights into the pathogenesis of DR. 在過去的數十年中，2型糖尿病已在全球蔓延並在各地造成巨大的醫療保健負擔。糖尿病視網膜病變是一種具破壞性的微血管併發症，更是中青年人群致盲的主要原因。從雙胞胎和家族聚集研究中已經清楚地證明了糖尿病視網膜病變的遺傳性。自過去十年以來，全基因組關聯研究已成為研究複雜疾病遺傳基礎的有力工具。迄今為止，科學家已經在不同種族的1型或2型糖尿病患者中進行了多次關於糖尿病視網膜病變的全基因組關聯研究，以鑑定糖尿病視網膜病變發展的易感基因。然而，已確認與糖尿病視網膜病變相關的基因仍然無法完全解釋此病症的遺傳性。我們假設還有更多其他與糖尿病視網膜病變相關的易感基因尚待發現。糖尿病視網膜病變尚未釐清的遺傳性也可能是由傳統基因分型芯片沒有捕捉到的低頻或罕見的功能性變體造成的。使用以東亞人群數據為基礎的基因分型芯片將可使我們能夠在東亞人族群中檢測到新的亞洲特有的易感性變體。 是次項目的主要目標是以新型的 Illumina Infinium 東亞人群基因分型芯片 Asian Screening Array（ASA)對威脅視力的糖尿病視網膜病變進行两階段的全基因組關聯研究,以及隨後的功能驗證分析。使用ASA讓我們能夠研究與我們的族群最相關的變體，這些變體可能不存在於以往主要基於歐洲族群基因組建立的常規基因分型芯片中。早前, 我們利用ASA對750名患有威脅視力的糖尿病視網膜病變的患者和750名無糖尿病視網膜病變的對照患者進行了第一(發現)階段的全基因組關聯研究。在第一階段分析中，我們發現了一些全新與糖尿病視網膜病變相關的新型易感性變體。其中一些寄往研究未能識別的易感基因在功能上與糖尿病視網膜病變的疾病生物學具有高度的相關性。此外，我們也發現一些亞洲族群特有並與威脅視力的糖尿病視網膜病變相關的變異體。在此, 我們將在本港及海外超過4500名患有2型糖尿病的華人患者中,進一步驗證在第一階段分析中發現與威脅視力的糖尿病視網膜病變相關的變異體。然後，我們將對第一和第二階段的數據進行聯合分析及隨後的功能驗證分析。是次項目的研究結果將為糖尿病視網膜病變的發病機制提供新的見解。

17118119.label: Realisation of objectives
17118119.value: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), a devastating microvascular complication of diabetes, is the leading cause of blindness among the working-age populations. The heritability of DR has been demonstrated in twins and familial aggregation studies. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have become powerful tools to delineate the genetic basis of complex diseases since the last decade. Several GWAS for DR have been conducted in diabetes patients of different ethnic groups to identify the susceptibility variants for the development of DR. However, the heritability of DR remains largely unexplained. We hypothesise that additional novel susceptibility variants for DR are yet to be identified. The missing heritability of DR may also be contributed by low-frequency or rare functional variants that have not been captured by the traditional genotyping arrays. The use of an Asian-focused genotyping array may allow us to detect novel Asian-specific risk variants for DR in our population. In this project, our major was to perform a comprehensive two-stage GWAS on sight-threatening DR (STDR), using the latest Illumina Infinium® Asian Screening Array (ASA) with subsequent replication and functional validation analyses. In this project, we defined STDR cases as patients with T2DM having either pre-PDR (grading R2) or PDR (grading R3) and the non-STDR controls were defined as patients without retinopathy or with background retinopathy (grading R1), according to the English national screening programme for diabetic retinopathy (United Kingdom National Screening Committee [NSC] classification). The use of ASA has allowed us to investigate the variants that are most relevant and specific to our population, which may be absent from the conventional genotyping arrays that have been built primarily on European genomes. In the discovery stage, we genotyped a total of 1500 Chinese patients with T2DM recruited from the Hong Kong West Diabetes Registry (HKWDR) using the ASA, which contains 659,184 variants before quality control (QC), at the Centre for PanorOmic Sciences (CPOS) of the University of Hong Kong (HKU). PLINK version 1.9 was used for data management and manipulation. Stringent quality control (QC) was applied on both sample- and SNP levels to ensure high-quality genotype calls. Sample-level QC was conducted with regard to low genotyping call rate (<99%), gender mismatch, duplication, biological relatedness, and possible contamination. The principal component analysis was conducted to examine the existence of non-Chinese samples using independent common SNPs (MAF > 0.05) and the outliers were excluded. For SNP-level QC, SNPs with more than 2% missingness, deviated from Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium (P<1x10-5), or variants originally designed for QC were excluded from the analysis. To maximize genetic coverage, in particular, the population-specific rare variants, imputation was performed using the Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine (TOPMed) Imputation Reference panel (version r2), which includes information from 97,256 deeply sequenced human genomes from diverse populations, on the TOPMed Imputation Server. Variants with poor imputation quality (INFO ≤ 0.3) or with a low population frequency (MAF < 0.01) were excluded. Following QC, 8,156,894 polymorphic SNPs were examined for their associations with STDR in 681 STDR cases and 758 non-STDR controls. GWAS on STDR was performed under the additive genetic model. The score-based test implemented in the SNPTEST v2.5.6, was employed to examine the associations of SNPs with STDR with adjustment for age, sex, duration of diabetes, haemoglobin A1c, presence of hypertension and the first 5 principal components (PCs). Genome-wide significance was defined as P<5x10-8. Ninety-three SNPs showing suggestive associations (P<5x10-5) with STDR were identified in the discovery stage and these SNPs were selected for validation in an independent set of samples. In the meta-analysis of the discovery stage and replication stage data, we identified an intronic SNP of ANXA2 as the top association. We then further conducted an in vitro functional analysis to assess the expression of ANXA2 in the primary human retinal microvascular endothelial cells. The outbreak of COVID-19 in 2019/2020 has significantly disrupted our plan to recruit additional STDR cases for the replication study. Therefore, apart from recruiting STDR cases from the Hong Kong West and Kowloon East clusters, we further extended the recruitment of STDR cases in the ophthalmology clinics of the Hong Kong East Cluster. Our research assistant, who was responsible for carrying out the experiments, was unfortunately infected with COVID-19 during the fifth wave of COVID-19 in Hong Kong in late February 2022. Our scheduled experiments have been severely delayed due to the health condition of the staff and the temporary suspension of our laboratory during the fifth wave of COVID-19 in Hong Kong. Nonetheless, we were still able to recruit enough subjects for the replication study and complete the project.

17118119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17118119.value: In the discovery stage analysis involving 681 STDR cases and 758 non-STDR controls, we identified a list of susceptibility loci showing suggestive associations with STDR. A total of 93 SNPs showing suggestive independent associations (P<5x10-5) with STDR were detected. However, none of these SNPs has reached genome-wide significance. The strongest association signal was detected at an intronic variant, rs2123830, of ANXA2 (P=1.87x10-7; OR[95%CI]:1.59[1.31-1.96]). Other top associated SNPs included PPARGC1A rs116867785, CDH6 rs145901646, MBP-GALR1 rs8090874 and LRRC4C rs79913593. The 93 SNPs showing suggestive associations were then examined for associations with STDE in the replication cohort. The replication cohort was comprised of an independent sample set of 750 STDR cases and 834 non-STDR controls. Meta-analysis of the association results of the discovery and replication stages was conducted using the “GWAMA” software. The inverse variance fixed-effect method was used to meta-analyse the summary statistics of the two stages. In the meta-analysis, ANXA2 rs2123830 again showed the strongest association with STDR (P=2.18x10-6; OR[95%CI]: 1.45[1.24-1.70]). An intronic SNP of DOC2B also demonstrated a marginal association with STDR (P=5.17x10-6; OR[95%CI]: 1.41[1.22-1.63]). Two intergenic variants located at the RPL31P11-FCRLA (P=7.25x10-6; OR[95%CI]: 1.54[1.27-1.85]) and COL6A1-COL6A2 (P=9.60x10-6; OR[95%CI]: 0.73[0.63-0.84]) loci also showed suggestive associations with STDR. A manuscript based on the results of the 2-stage GWAS is currently under preparation by the PI. Although none of the identified SNPs have shown genome-wide significant associations with STDR, we still decided to select ANXA2 which showed the strongest association with STDR in the current GWAS for further functional analysis. Indeed, annexin A2 encoded by ANXA2 has been shown to play an important role in promoting angiogenesis. We carried out an in vitro functional analysis to investigate the possible role of ANXA2 in the development of DR. The gene expression of ANXA2 was studied in primary human retinal microvascular endothelial cells (hRECs) under physiological glucose or high glucose conditions. We found that the ANXA2 expression was significantly decreased by ~30% under high glucose conditions as compared to the physiological glucose condition, suggesting that ANXA2 may play a role in the development of DR.

17118119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118119.value: As discussed above, none of the identified SNPs has reached genotype-wide significance in the current study, further validation in larger samples will be required to confirm our findings. We proposed to conduct further meta-analysis using publicly available GWAS datasets on STDR to further improve the study power and to identify additional susceptibility variants for STDR. Furthermore, we would generate a polygenic risk score for STDR, incorporating the DR-associated SNPs identified in previous publications.

17118119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118119.value: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is the most common microvascular complication of diabetes and is recognised as the leading cause of blindness among working-age populations. In this study, we conducted a two-stage genome-wide association study on sight-threatening diabetic retinopathy (STDR) in Chinese patients with T2D to delineate the genetic basis of DR in our population. In the discovery stage involving 681 STDR cases and 758 non-STDR controls, we identified a list of susceptibility loci showing suggestive associations with STDR. A total of 93 SNPs showing suggestive associations with STDR were detected in the discovery stage and were carried forward for validation in an independent sample set of 750 cases and 834 controls. In the meta-analysis, ANXA2 rs2123830 showed the strongest association with STDR. Annexin A2, encoded by ANXA2, has been shown to play a significant role in promoting angiogenesis. We also observed reduced ANXA2 expression in the human retinal microvascular endothelial cells under high-glucose conditions. Findings from this study have provided some novel insights into the genetic architecture of STDR. The valuable findings generated from this study would facilitate the identification of novel susceptibility genes and pathways implicated in the development of STDR and would provide novel targets for follow-up functional analyses.

17118519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17118519.value: Dental caries is a chronic biofilm-mediated disease. Prevention of oral biofilm-related microbial dysbiosis would reduce this disease and its associated global burden. Fluorides (F) have been the mainstay for caries control for decades. However, it has limited effect on oral biofilms. Therefore, novel strategies that supplement F to target the cariogenic biofilms in high caries-risk patients are needed. Prebiotics like arginine (Arg) exhibits endogenous caries-protective benefits by restoring oral biofilm homeostasis. Topical F varnish provides a reservoir of F adjacent to the tooth surface with a prolonged contact time between the enamel and F. Hence, the incorporation of Arg in the F varnish might enhance the caries-preventive potential of F varnish by providing an additional Arg reservoir for its biofilm modulatory effect. Thus, a series of studies were undertaken in our GRF project to examine the caries-preventive potential of Arg in a sodium fluoride (NaF) varnish. A total of four studies were conducted in our research project. The first study characterized and evaluated the mechanistic properties of Arg-F varnish in enhancing enamel remineralization. The second study examined the biofilm modulatory response of Arg released from Arg-F varnish on multi-species biofilm. The third study examined the remineralization efficacy of Arg released from Arg-F varnish using a multi-species bacterial pH-cycling model and the fourth study examined the biocompatibility of Arg-F varnish by cytotoxicity analysis. Results of the first study showed that the incorporation of 2% Arg in a 5% NaF varnish increased the viscosity and promoted retention of NaF varnish, which is beneficial for clinical application on the enamel surface. The 2% Arg-NaF varnish exhibited periodic perennial Arg/F release and showed significantly higher F release than NaF varnish. Results of the second study demonstrated that the incorporation of 2% and 4% of Arg in NaF varnish enhanced the biofilm modulatory effect of NaF varnish through released Arg and F, primarily reducing the biofilm polysaccharides. The anti-microbial activity of NaF varnish increased with higher concentrations of Arg in the varnish. Results of the third study showed that the addition of Arg in the NaF varnish enhanced enamel fluoride uptake and remineralization potential of NaF varnish. Results of the fourth study revealed that the incorporation of 2% and 4% Arg in NaF varnish exhibited good biocompatibility and was not cytotoxic to human gingival fibroblast (HGF)-1. In conclusion, the addition of arginine to fluoride varnish appears a promising ecological-based caries-preventive strategy for the future.

17118519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118519.value: There is an immense potential to explore further insights on the use of Arg-F varnish for caries prevention, given the fact that Arg has a known prebiotic effect while F has been the mainstay that facilitates remineralization and inhibits demineralization. For the next step, the remineralization potential and biofilm modulatory potential of the Arg-F varnish can be examined in an open system biofilm model as well as in an animal model, before further assessment in a clinical trial. A research proposal will be prepared for submission to GRF or HMRF application.

17118519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118519.value: Tooth decay is a chronic biofilm-mediated disease. Prevention of oral biofilm-related microbial dysbiosis would reduce this disease. Fluorides (F) have been the mainstay for tooth decay prevention. However, it has limited effect on oral biofilms. Prebiotics like arginine (Arg) protects the teeth from decay by restoring oral biofilm homeostasis. Fluoride varnish provides a reservoir of F adjacent to the tooth surface with a prolonged contact time between enamel and F. Hence, the incorporation of Arg in the F varnish might enhance the effect of F varnish in preventing tooth decay by providing an additional Arg reservoir for its biofilm modulatory effect. Results of our study showed that the incorporation of 2% Arg in a conventional sodium fluoride (NaF) varnish increased the viscosity and promoted retention of NaF varnish, which is beneficial for clinical application on the enamel surface. The addition of 2% and 4% Arg in NaF varnish exhibited good biocompatibility, reduced biofilm polysaccharides, enhanced enamel fluoride uptake and remineralization potential of NaF varnish. The Arg-F varnish restores the balance of oral microbiota and reduces tooth decay. In conclusion, the addition of Arg to F varnish appears a promising ecological-based caries-preventive strategy for the future.

17118619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118619.value: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM), the myocardial dysfunction occurring in diabetic patients, is characterized by myocardial fibrosis, cardiomyocyte death, dysfunctional remodeling, and associated diastolic and systolic dysfunction that eventually lead to heart failure. Although the underlying mechanism of DCM remains largely unknown, metabolic abnormality in the diabetic heart has been suggested to play a crucial role in its pathology. During DCM, the cardiac energy substrate flexibility is constrained and the heart relies more on mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation for its adenosine triphospate (ATP) requirements, which leads to the cardiac inefficiency and lipotoxicity. However, inhibition of fatty acid metabolism failed to improve cardiac function, as the diabetic heart still requires fatty acid metabolism-mediated ATP generation for cardiac work. Thus, examining novel therapeutic targets to maintain the balance of cardiac fuel preference has important clinical significance to combat DCM. The prostaglandin E receptor 4 (EP4) is highly expressed in the heart and participates in various pathophysiological processes. Through the downstream cAMP-dependent protein kinase A signaling, EP4 may activate FOXO1, a transcriptional factor which is essential in sustaining cardiomyocyte metabolism and cell survival. Of note, FOXO1 can positively regulate fatty acid uptake through activation of CD36 (fatty acids transporter), and further stimulate fatty acid oxidation occurred in mitochondria and promote ATP generation. Indeed, our preliminary data suggested that high fat fed EP4 knockout mice display severe cardiac dysfunction, myocardial damages, and significantly reduced cardiac ATP production, concomitant with reduced protein expressions of FOXO1 and CD36 when compared to wildtype counterparts. We therefore hypothesize that EP4 may activate FOXO1/CD36 signaling in the heart. In the absence of EP4, reduction in FOXO1 and CD36 expression and impairment in fatty acid metabolism, lead to cardiac energy deprivation with a significant reduction of ATP generation, resulting in severe diabetic cardiomyopathy. The proposed research aims, therefore, to 1. Investigate if EP4 deficiency aggravates DCM in diabetic heart; 2. Determine whether EP4 deficiency precipitates DCM by modulating cardiac fatty acid metabolism via FOXO1/CD36 signaling. The proposed studies will improve our understanding of the metabolic abnormalities in DCM. It is hoped that regulating cardiac fuel preference through EP4 signaling can be translated into an effective (stand alone or adjunct) therapy for the management of DCM which is common in diabetic patients in the future. 糖尿病心肌病（DCM）是糖尿病患者發生的心肌功能障礙，其特徵在於心肌纖維化，心肌細胞死亡，功能失調的重塑以及最終導致心力衰竭的相關的舒張和收縮功能障礙。儘管DCM的潛在機制仍然很大程度上未知，但糖尿病心臟中的代謝異常已被認為在其病理學中起關鍵作用。在DCM期間，心臟能量底物的靈活性受到限制，並且心臟更加依賴於脂肪酸氧化产生三磷酸腺苷（ATP），這導致心臟效率降低和脂毒性。然而，抑制脂肪酸代謝並未能改善心臟功能，因為糖尿病心臟仍然需要脂肪酸代謝介導的ATP生成用於心臟功能。因此，檢查新的治療靶標以維持心臟能源底物的平衡對於對抗DCM具有重要的臨床意義。 前列腺素E受體4（EP4）在心臟中高度表達並參與各種病理生理過程。通過下游cAMP依賴性蛋白激酶A信號傳導，EP4可以激活維持心肌細胞代謝和細胞存活所必需的轉錄因子FOXO1。值得注意的是，FOXO1可通過激活CD36（脂肪酸轉運蛋白）正向調節脂肪酸攝取，進一步刺激線粒體中脂肪酸氧化並促進ATP生成。我們的初步數據表明，與野生型小鼠相比，高脂肪餵養的EP4敲除小鼠顯示出嚴重的心臟功能障礙，心肌損傷和顯著降低的心臟ATP產生，並伴隨著FOXO1和CD36的蛋白表達降低。因此，我們假設EP4可以激活心臟中的FOXO1 / CD36信號傳導。在沒有EP4的情況下，FOXO1和CD36表達的減少和脂肪酸代謝的損害導致心臟能量喪失，ATP產生顯著減少，導致嚴重的糖尿病性心肌病。 因此，本課題研究旨在 1.調查EP4缺乏是否會加重糖尿病心臟中的DCM; 2.通過FOXO1 / CD36信號通路調節心臟脂肪酸代謝來確定EP4缺乏是否加劇DCM。 本研究將提高我們對DCM中代謝異常的理解。希望通過EP4信號傳導調節心臟能源底物的平衡並轉化為用於管理DCM的有效（獨立或輔助）療法。

17118619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17118619.value: Cardiac fatty acid metabolism is essential for maintaining normal cardiac function at baseline and in response to various disease stress, like diabetes. EP4 is widely expressed in cardiomyocytes and has been demonstrated to play a role in cardio function. However, its function in regulating cardiac fatty acid metabolism and especially in the pathology of diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is remained unknown. Cardiac metabolic disorder has been considered as a major mechanism of DCM. Accumulated dysfunctional mitochondria could aggravate impairment of fatty acid metabolism, including fatty acid uptake and fatty acid oxidation, and lead to reduction of ATP generation, which eventually result in cell apoptosis. EP4 is one of prostaglandin E2 receptors (EP1,2,3,4), which is expressed in different cell types in the heart, including cardiomyocytes. Of those receptors, EP4 is the one most widely distributed in the cardiac ventricles of adult mice. Although many studies suggested that EP4 receptor may affect cardiac function at multiple levels, there is currently no any reports about the role of EP4 in DCM. 1. In the current proposal, we have conducted series in vivo and in vitro studies and showed that EP4 is vital in targeting mitochondrial autophagy and fatty acid metabolism in mitochondria of diabetic heart. HFD-fed EP4-/- mice showed increased wall thickness and reductions in left ventricle systolic and diastolic volume. HFD-fed EP4-/- mice also developed cardiac hypertrophy and severe myocardial fibrosis. EP4-/- mice exhibited concentric hypertrophy and myocardial fibrosis with cardiac energy deprivation due to reduction of fatty acid uptake and inhibition of ATP generation mediated by FOXO1/CD36 signalling. Moreover, pharmacologically activated EP4 alleviated impaired fatty acid transport and insufficient ATP generation in cardiomyocytes (Refer to PART C: Research Output 8. No.1: Ying F et al. Biochem Biophys Res Commun. 2021). 2. Furthermore, we demonstrated that FOXO1 activation, through stimulating PDK4 and CPT1, shifts substrate selection from glucose to fatty acid and causes mitochondrial and cardiac dysfunction. Our findings collectively indicate that deficiency of EP4 aggravates DCM in diabetic rodents and that EP4 protects against DCM through improving FOXO1/CD36-dependent fatty acid metabolism in diabetic rodents (Refer to PART C: Research Output 8. No.1: Ying F et al. Biochem Biophys Res Commun. 2021). 3. Increased oxidative stress plays key roles in the development of DCM, we thus further explored the effectiveness of antioxidant treatment on DCM and demonstrated that the same antioxidant treatment regimen not only attenuated DCM but also attenuated diabetic liver injury and diabetic neuropathy pain, and the mechanisms are related to the inhibition of diabetes mediated overactivation of CD36, a signaling molecule that can be modulated by EP4 as we showed in the abovementioned studies (Refer to PART C: Research Output 8. No.4: Yan D et al. J Cell Mol Med. 2020. No. 5: Liu J et al. J Cell Mol Med. 2020. No.10: Jiaqi Z et al. Burns & Trauma. 2023 ). We have published nine papers with acknowledgment of this grant, and trained two research postgraduate students (Note: Dr. Zhengyuan Xia serves as the corresponding author for the majority of the publications listed in Part C. This is due to the fact that he was the principal investigator of the project, and upon his departure from the University of Hong Kong, he transferred the project to Prof. Aimin Xu).

17118619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17118619.value: The current study uncovered that EP4 tightly coordinates the rates of cardiac fatty acid uptake and ATP generation via FOXO1/CD36 signalling axis and plays a key role in the development of diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM). Given that hearts with DCM are more susceptible to ischemia-reperfusion injury and the diabetic heart ischemia reperfusion is not or less responsive to conventional therapeutic interventions that are otherwise effective in subjects without diabetes, the findings of our current study raise the possibility of 1) using existing drugs that may target EP4 in the treatment or prevention of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in functionally impaired and metabolically disturbed diabetic heart; 2) development of cardiac specific agonists of EP4 for the treatment of DCM and/or diabetic myocardial ischemia reperfusion injury. This may be of potential and particular interest for future drug development in relation to EP4, given that systemic application of EP4 has been found to be either beneficial or detrimental.

17118619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17118619.value: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM), characterized by cardiac hypertrophy, altered metabolic energetics diastolic and systolic dysfunction developed in the absence of apparent hypertension or coronary artery diseases, is a major cause of heart failure. Currently, effective treatment for DCM is lacking. In this study, we find that Prostaglandin E receptor subtype 4 (EP4), a molecule that is widely expressed in cardiomyocytes, not only play a role in cardio function under normal physiological conditions as already known, but also it protects against diabetic cardiomyopathy by modulating cardiac fatty acid metabolism via FOXO1/CD36 signaling. The current study uncovered that EP4 tightly coordinates the rates of cardiac fatty acid uptake and ATP. Further, we find that effective antioxidant treatment especially joint antioxidant treatment can attenuate myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury via mechanisms are related to the inhibition of diabetes mediated overactivation of CD36. Our findings provide clues of using existing drugs to target EP4 in the treatment or prevention of myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury in functionally impaired and metabolically disturbed diabetic heart. Also, the mechanistic insights gained from the current study shall facilitate the development of new drugs for the treatment of DCM.

17118719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17118719.value: Hoarseness of voice due to vocal fold (VF) palsy is one of the most debilitating and fearful complications after thyroid surgery. Despite the absence of VFP, up to 30% of patients have reported voice change after thyroid surgery. External branch of superior laryngeal nerve (EBSLN) palsy is one of potential cause. EBSLNs innervate cricothyroid muscle (CTM) which control the length of VFs and thus change the vocal pitch. Patients with EBSLN palsy often complain of a lowered vocal pitch, weakness of voice and require extra effort to speak. These symptoms are more noticeable in women and professional speakers, like teachers and singers. As EBSLNs locate near the upper pole of thyroid gland, they are in high-risk being injured during thyroid surgery. Investigations, like video-strobo-laryngoscopy (VSL) and electromyography, have been used to make the diagnosis of EBSLN palsy. They are either invasive & painful. Some patients cannot be tolerated and compliant with the investigations. Specialised equipment and clinicians are also needed for evaluation and interpretation. Furthermore, clinical manifestations and laryngeal finding are often subtle and sometimes inconclusive, it made diagnosing EBSLN dysfunction rather difficult. Different surgical techniques have been described to decrease the chance of injuries. Due to the absence of good diagnostic tool, researches on the efficacy of surgical techniques are deficient. Our group has demonstrated that VFs movement and laryngeal features can be evaluated by simply putting the ultrasound probe over upper neck. This technique is named transcutaneous laryngeal ultrasound (TLUSG). In patients with EBSLN injury, VFs are shortened and inferior displaced or being “asymmetry”. We previously demonstrated that patients with sonographic features of vocal fold asymmetry (VFA) on TLUSG had “vocal roughness” and poor voice outcomes on questionnaire-based assessment. As “Roughness” and decreased voice performance are commonly found in patients with EBSLN injury, we postulate that the presence of VFA on TLUSG is related to EBSLN palsy. We wonder if TLUSG could be a simple, non-invasive tool in diagnosing EBSLN injury. In this study, we evaluate the role of VFA in diagnosing EBSLN palsy. We will evaluate the laryngeal anatomical feature and voice profile in patients with or without VFA. Finding of TLUSG will be correlated with VSL, feasibility of non-invasive TLUSG in diagnosing other laryngeal pathology can also be evaluated. With structured investigations and follow-up, this study also helps in finding other causes and recovery of voice change after thyroid surgery, even if we failed in demonstrating the diagnosing ability. 17119619.label: Project Objectives
17119619.value: To elucidate the formation of celastrol-GRP78 conjugate and subsequent effects on chaperone activity and unfolded protein degradation. GRP78 senses unfolded proteins and activates ER stress signalling pathways. We for the first time discovered the formation of covalent celastrol-GRP78 conjugate. Covalent celastrol-GRP78 conjugation may help the control of unfolded protein response against lipidotoxicity. We will determine the molecular basis of celastrol-GRP78 conjugation and the potential effects on the chaperone activity and unfolded protein degradation. To determine the effects of celastrol-GRP78 conjugation on unfolded protein responses, ER stress sensing and ER-phagy. Obesity promotes the accumulation of unfolded proteins, regulates GRP78 chaperone activity and thereby induces ER stress. Our pilot results demonstrated that celastrol attenuated palmitate-induced activation of ATF6, IRE1α and PERK. Thus, the present study will determine whether celastrol-GRP78 conjugation could not only prevent the activation of ER stress signalling pathways but also activate ER-phagy towards the resolution of unfolded proteins. To discover the structure-activity relationship towards the development of specific GRP78 inhibitors. Celastrol may bind several different protein targets. Thus, this project was designed to determine whether celastrol primarily targets GRP78 against obesity and discover the structural elements for specific binding to GRP78. We performed virtual screening and developed a synthetic procedure for preparing 6-substituted celastrol derivatives. We will further determine celastrol derivatives against ER stress, inflammation, lipid metabolism and insulin resistance.

17119619.value: 持續性低度炎症常見于肥胖，前驅糖尿病和代謝綜合征。高脂飲食誘發肥胖也造成內質網應激异常。內質網應激總體協調蛋白質反應，炎症反應，代謝功能障礙和胰島素抵抗。現有的抗糖尿病藥物不能緩解內質網應激。本研究主要目的是發現有效控制內質網應激的中藥成分，以解决炎症和胰島素抵抗。最近研究確定雷公藤紅素（Celastrol）爲减肥最有效和無毒的候選藥物。在GRF（例如17100317）資助下，我們獲得一項重要發現，即Celastrol减少了內質網應激，也改善了炎症和胰島素抵抗。 因此，我們繼續關注Celastrol治療肥胖和糖尿病的分子靶點。我們率先合成小分子探針N-炔丙基雷公藤紅素醯胺從細胞培養物中分離出Celastrol修飾的蛋白質。通過藥物處理，生物素標記，親和富集和蛋白質組學鑒定，我們發現Celastrol主要修飾兩種蛋白質：葡萄糖調節蛋白78（GRP78）和丙酮酸激酶M2（PKM2）。 GRP78不僅可以感應未折叠蛋白反應，還可以决定涉及ATF6，IRE1α和PERK的ER應激信號通路。初步實驗揭示以下三個有趣的現象：1）GRP78在肥胖小鼠肝臟和脂肪組織中巨噬細胞中高表達; 2）Celastrol保留GRP78與內質網蛋白質ATF6和IRE1α共定位，預防棕櫚酸脂毒性; 3）Celastrol抑制棕櫚酸激活ATF6，IRE1α和PERK通路。因此，我們提出假設：Celastrol通過共價修飾伴侶蛋白質GRP78，可以改善肥胖症中的炎症，代謝功能障礙和胰島素抵抗。我們將圍繞三個特定目去證明GRP78是Celastrol對抗肥胖的主要目標：1）闡明Celastrol-GRP78結合物的形成及其對GRP78伴侶活性和未折叠蛋白質降解的影響; 2）確定celastrol-GRP78結合對內質網應激傳感分子（例如ATF6，IRE1α，PERK）和內質網-噬菌體對未折叠蛋白響應的影響; 3）發現不可逆GRP78抑制劑的結構 - 活性關係。這些研究將證明celastrol-GRP78共價結合物的形成是一種新的抗肥胖機制，可以解决肥胖誘導的內質網應激。該項目將不僅鞏固GRP78在編排不同細胞信號方面的作用，而且爲開發新型選擇性針對飲食誘導肥胖的不可逆GRP78抑制劑鋪平道路。

17119619.label: Realisation of objectives
17119619.value: AIM 1: To determine the formation of celastrol-GRP78 conjugate and subsequent effects on chaperone activity. The objective of this project was to characterize celastrol-GRP78 conjugate and clarify whether the covalent celastrol-GRP78 conjugation could diminish the chaperone activity for unfolded proteins. We optimized the research plan and addressed the following four key questions: 1) Does celastrol form covalent conjugate with GRP78 in a site-specific manner? 2) Does celastrol affect the chaperone activity of GRP78 to unfolded proteins? 3) Is it essential to form the covalent celastrol-GRP78 conjugate for suppressing ER stress? 4) Is it possible to trace celastrol-modified proteins in cells? To characterize celastrol-GRP78 conjugate, we synthesized N-propargyl celastrol amide as small probe. Following incubation with RAW264.7 cell lysate and Click chemistry biotinylation, the biotin-labelled proteins were isolated by affinity enrichment by magnetic Streptavidin beads and separated by SDS-PAGE. The proteins were identified by LC-MS and Western blotting. To identify the binding sites, celastrol was incubated with recombinant mouse GRP78. We employed LC-MS technology to map celastrol-modified peptides. As results, celastrol was attached to the C41 residue in the peptide of GSEEDKKEDVGTVVGIDLGTTYSC41 VGVFK. As results, celastrol was nicely docked into the binding site in a close proximity to the C41 residue. These results suggest that celastrol bound to GRP78 structure in a specific manner. To determine the effects of celastrol on the chaperone activity of GRP78. We analyzed the binding of synthetic peptide (WDLAWMFRLPVG) to recombinant GRP78 before and after celastrol saturation on BIAcore X-100 system. As results, the peptide initially bound to GRP78 with Kd value of 17.7 nM, whereas celastrol saturation increased the Kd value to 2.23μM. Such results suggested that celastrol could suppress the chaperone activity of GRP78. To examine the importance of the covalent celastrol-GRP78 conjugation, we prepared biotin-labeled celastrol and inactive analogue. After incubation with recombinant GRP78, the proteins were separated by SDS-PAGE and detected by Western blotting. As results, celastrol could readily form covalent conjugate with GRP78. To trace celastrol-modified proteins in cells, we synthesized celastrol-PEG4-alkyne. The macrophages were incubated with celastrol or celastrol-PEG4-alkyne. The covalent conjugation was detected by labeling with fluorescence dye AFDye555-picolyl azide and immunofluorescence with anti-GRP78 antibody. As results, celastrol formed covalent conjugate with GRP78 inside macrophages. AIM 2: To identify the effects of celastrol-GRP78 conjugation on the ER stress signaling pathways (e.g., ATF6, IRE1α, PERK) and ER-phagy against unfolded proteins. The goal of the present study was to determine the effects of celastrol-GRP78 conjugation on the fatty acid-induced ER stress. We addressed three questions as follows: 1) Does celastrol affect GRP78 expression in macrophages from diet-induced obese mice? 2) Does celastrol affect ER stress signal transduction? 3) Does celastrol alter lipid metabolism in diet-induced obese mice? To examine the effects of celastrol on GRP78 expression in macrophages, we harvested liver tissues and epididymal fat pads from diet-induced obese mice. GRP78 and macrophage biomarker CD68 were stained with specific antibodies. As results, we discovered that GRP78 was overexpressed in macrophages in diet-induced obesity. To determine the effects of celastrol on ER stress signaling, we further induced ER stress in macrophages with palmitate, we examined the effects of celastrol on the activation of ATF6, IRE1α, PERK XBP1 and elF2α by Western blotting with specific antibodies. As results, celastrol effectively attenuated palmitate-induced activation of ATF6, IRE1α, PERK XBP1 and elF2α. To investigate the effects of celastrol on lipid metabolism, we determined the expression of several typical biomarkers (e.g., PPAR-γ, C/EBP-α, aP2, leptin, resistin, adipisin, CTP-1, CAT, ACO, UCP2) by qRT-PCR. As results, celastrol effectively suppressed the expression of lipogenesis genes and promoted the expression of lipolytic and energy expenditure genes. by determining the expression of biomarkers (e.g., PPAR-γ, C/EBP-α, aP2, leptin, resistin, adipisin, CTP-1, CAT, ACO, UCP2) by qRT-PCR. AIM 3: To discover the structure-activity relationship towards the development of specific GRP78 inhibitors against diet-induced obesity. The aim of the present study was to develop selective irreversible GRP78 inhibitors. We developed a synthetic scheme and detected the formation of representative 6-substituted celastrol derivative Compound 3 by LC-MS. However, we failed to prepare pure 6- celastrol derivatives for biological assays. For validating the formation of covalent celastrol-GRP78 conjugate, we synthesized a celastrol analogue lacking the methide moiety and tested for the formation of covalent celastrol-GRP78 conjugate. As results, celastrol analogue lacking the methide moiety failed to form covalent celastrol-GRP78 conjugate, highlighting the potential of celastrol as a GRP78 inhibitor. Thus, we focused on the evaluation of celastrol as a potential anti-obesity drug. To examine the anti-obesity effects of celastrol, we treated diet-induced obese mice with celastrol for three weeks. At the end of treatment, we weighed body weight, measured body fat mass by NMR technique, assayed glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity. As results, celastrol effectively ameliorated diet-induced obesity. To determine the effects of celastrol on adipose hypertrophy and lipid metabolism, we examined lipid accumulation in livers and adipose tissues. We further analyzed the lipid composition of liver tissues and epididymal fat pads. As results, celastrol not only reduced lipid accumulation in livers and adipose tissues but also altered the composition of fatty acids. It remains unknown whether such alterations of fatty acid composition could affect obesity. To gain molecular insights for the anti-obesity effects of celastrol, we isolated RNAs from livers and analyzed differentially expressed genes (DEGs) by RNA sequencing and bioinformatic analysis. A total of 49 DEGs were initially identified in the livers while 49 DEGs were compared by hierarchical clustering in a heatmap. HFD upregulated nine DEGs including Apoa4, Apoc2, Thrsp while celastrol suppressed the upregulation of these nine genes and even downregulated three genes (i.e., Bhmt, Car3, Mup18) in HFD-treated mice. By contrast, HFD downregulated 21 DEGs (e.g., Cyp4a14, Mup7, Mup14, Mup15) while celastrol increased the expression of the selected genes to a certain extent and even upregulated four genes (i.e., Hamp, Mt2, Igfbp2, Serpina1e) in HFD-treated mice. Among the other 19 genes, celastrol significantly upregulated four DEGs (i.e., Lrg1, Fgl1, Mt1, Apom) and downregulated Scd1 although HFD showed little effect on these genes. Functional enrichment analysis of DEGs showed that celastrol significantly affected 6 KEGG pathways, 14 biological processes, and 5 molecular function groups. Interestingly, these functional groups mainly deal with retinal metabolism, lipid metabolism, fatty acid oxidation, cholesterol efflux, glucose metabolism, stress response, inflammatory response, oxidative stress, detoxification, PPAR pathway, kinase pathways, complement, and coagulation cascade. These DEGs were analyzed for protein–protein interaction networks by online STRING tool (https://string-db.org/). Celastrol considerably affected 4 networks of gene products including 10 DEGs for Network-1 (Cyp1a2, Cyp2a12, Cyp3a25, Cyp4a10, Cyp4a14, Cyp2c44, Mdh1, Pck1, Ugt2b5, Aldh1a1); 8 DEGs for Network-2 (Apoa4, Apoc2, Apom, C3, C8a, Creg1, Itih3, Itih4); 3 DEGs for Network-3 (Acat1, Ehhadh, Hsd17b10), and 2 DEGs for Network-4 (Mt1, Mt2). Overall, RNA-seq transcriptome profiling confirmed the effects of celastrol on inflammation, ER stress, and lipid accumulation in liver.

17119619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119619.value: The aim of this project is to determine whether botanical drug celastrol exhibits anti-obesity effects via targeting ER stress sensor GRP78. An in-house prepared N-propargyl celastrol amide was used as a small molecule probe and incubated with RAW264.7 cell lysate. The celastrol-labeled proteins were biotinylated by Click chemistry approach, enriched onto magnetic Streptavidin beads, resolved by SDS-PAGE and identified by LC-MS/MS technology. As results, celastrol formed covalent conjugate with GRP78, alleviated palmitate-induced ER stress in macrophages, and showed in vivo anti-obesity potential in a mouse obesity model. These results demonstrated that celastrol might exhibit anti-obesity effects via covalent modification of GRP78, representing a new anti-obesity mechanism. Moreover, RNA-seq transcriptome profiling confirmed the effects of celastrol on inflammation, ER stress, and lipid accumulation in liver, providing molecular insight for better understanding on the anti-obesity effects of celastrol. The results were published in eLife. In addition, this grant supported the training of two PhD students and one MPhil student, the publication of four articles and several conference abstracts.

17119819.label: Realisation of objectives
17119819.value: Periodontitis is a major oral disease burden worldwide, and badly affects oral health and quality of life. Yet, periodontitis closely connects to systemic diseases like diabetes, cardiovascular disease (CVD), Alzheimer's disease (AD) and COVID-19, via the pathways of infection, inflammation, maladaptive stem cells and lifestyle risk factors. Our recent UGC/RGC-funded study further indicates that poor periodontal status increases host susceptibility to systemic comorbidities, in line with the emerging notion of human disease networks (Zhao et al. 2019 and 2022). This project has been undertaken within the specified time frame. The findings have been reported in international conferences and published in peer-reviewed journals. Additional work would be presented internationally and submitted for publication shortly. Regarding Objectives 1 and 2, the research work and findings are highlighted below: -Porphyromonas gingivalis as the pivotal ‘keystone’ pathogen is crucially involved in periodontitis pathogenesis via driving the shift of microbe-host symbiosis to dysbiosis accounting for the disrupted host responses, leading to the development of periodontitis in susceptible individuals. On the basis of our pioneering work on identification of P. gingivalis and P. gingivalis persisters for invading human gingival epithelial cells (HGECs) (Wang et al. 2020), and P. gingivalis persisters-induced marked disturbance of the expression of both pro-inflammatory cytokines (e.g., IL-1β and TNFα) and anti-inflammatory ones like IL-10 via manipulating the FOXO1 signalling pathway and multiple downstream genes (e.g., BCL2L11, BCL6, S1PR1, TRAIL and KLF2) in HGECs (Wang et al. 2022), the extensive studies on various P. gingivalis-challenged host cells (e.g., THP-1 macrophages, human endothelial progenitor cells and human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells) have further enhanced our understanding on this keystone periodontopathogen and microbial persisters (Wang & Jin 2023). -P. gingivalis aggravates the host response in THP-1 macrophages: It is known that M1 macrophages promote pro-inflammatory activities and account for the resultant tissue destruction, while M2 macrophages exhibit the opposite functions. P. gingivalis significantly disrupts the M1/M2 ratio, such as via upregulating the expression of M1 macrophage surface receptors (e.g., CD40) and downregulating the M2 surface receptors (e.g., CD163 and CD206) in THP-1 macrophages. It highlights that P. gingivalis enables to aggravate the immuno-inflammatory response via increasing the M1/M2 macrophages ratio. As such, the polarization of macrophages may be a novel target for precisely controlling P. gingivalis-induced destruction of periodontal tissues and common inflammatory comorbidities. -P. gingivalis LPS perturbs the gene expression in human endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs): The collaborative work on RNA sequencing discloses that P. gingivalis LPS markedly upregulates 85 genes and downregulates 247 genes in the EPCs. Gene ontology (GO) enrichment analysis suggests that most of these genes are enriched in multiple pathways in translational regulation of protein synthesis (e.g., structural constituent of ribosome, nuclear-transcribed mRNA catabolic process and ribosomal subunit). These findings show that P. gingivalis LPS to some extent affects the function of EPCs that are crucial for maintaining endothelial integrity and proper cardiovascular function. The current findings enrich our knowledge on the pathogenicity of P. gingivalis that greatly affects the functions of EPCs and potentially contributes to the resultant pathogenesis of atherosclerosis in CVD. -Bismuth drugs like colloidal bismuth subcitrate (CBS) could eradicate P. gingivalis persisters synergistically combined with metronidazole (MTZ): Our experiments show that there is a biphasic pattern of killing curves against P. gingivalis, while a small subset of survival P. gingivalis persisters can survive after the harsh treatments of MTZ, amoxicillin (AMX) and CBS respectively. Importantly, the synergistic use of CBS and MTZ, even with relatively lower dosages, almost eradicates P. gingivalis persisters in planktonic and biofilm modes. Such synergistic treatment is more potent against P. gingivalis persisters, comparing with the commonly used MTZ & AMX or CBS & AMX (Wang et al. 2021). Additionally, extended work has been conducted to test the newly synthesized bismuth-organic frameworks that show potent effects against P. gingivalis biofilms (Huang et al. 2023). -P. gingivalis reduces the ubiquitination in human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells and it can be alleviated by bismuth drugs: The Proteome Profiler Human Ubiquitin Array assesses the ubiquitination profiles in P. gingivalis W83-treated neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells. The ubiquitination of several W83-affected proteins decreases up to 50% of the controls; whereas the treatment of CBS or MTZ significantly restores or even enhances the levels of ubiquitination (e.g., TrkA, Hsp70, Caspase-8 and CBL). These findings provide additional evidence on the direct involvement of P. gingivalis in AD via suppressing the ubiquitin proteasome pathway. -Bismuth drugs effectively tackle intracellular P. gingivalis and reverse the perturbed gene expression in SH-SY5Y cells: Both P. gingivalis W83 and 381 enable to invade the SH-SY5Y cells. Importantly, the treatment of CBS nearly eradicates the intracellular P. gingivalis cells. The RNA sequencing shows that there are 145 upregulated and 139 downregulated genes in W83-challenged SH-SY5Y cells, and 796 upregulated and 858 downregulated ones in CBS-treated cells, respectively. These genes involve multi-pathways (e.g., TLR/NF-κB signalling, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, complement/coagulation cascades and drug/cholesterol metabolism). Whereas, the CBS-regulated genes involve certain upregulated pathways (e.g., complement/coagulation cascades, phagosome and HIF-1, FOXO and p53 signaling), and downregulated ones (e.g., ribosome, fatty acid biosynthesis and Wnt signaling). Moreover, bismuth drugs reverse the perturbed expression of 56 genes. RT q-PCR confirms that P. gingivalis-elevated mRNA expression of KCNJ2, FBXO6, ALS2CL, ANO9, DCC and TNN is effectively alleviated by CBS, and the W83-suppressed expression of CTF1, IFITM3 and MYLK3 can be restored by CBS treatment. Yet, CBS treatment restores certain P. gingivalis-perturbed proteins in SH-SY5Y-differentiated neurons like IFITM3 and MAP2 proteins. CBS treatment dramatically reduces the levels to the uninfected and differentiated SH-SY5Y cells. Collectively, these findings show that P. gingivalis invades and perturb the gene expression and cytokine production in SH-SY5Y cells, and bismuth drugs can reverse some of the perturbed gene expression involved in neuroinflammation and AD like CTF1 and FBXO6, implying the potential use of bismuth drugs in controlling P. gingivalis-related AD. Regarding Objective 3, the research work and main findings are highlighted as follows: A series of experiments have been undertaken to assess the effects of the micro-environmental factors (e.g., hemin and temperature) on P. gingivalis pathogenicity, for mimicking healthy and diseased periodontal niches. The data-dependent acquisition (DDA) or DDA/data-independent acquisition (DIA) nano-LC-MS/MS proteomic analysis reveals 15 significantly perturbed proteins. PCA and heatmap show temperature as a major effector, and the DnaK nucleotide-related proteins (e.g., LpxC) are upregulated. DIA proteomics analysis shows 18 notably perturbed proteins, and more fimbriae are identified. Expanded STRING PPI network discloses four kmeans clusters (e.g., Kgp and RagA for cell adhesion; and major & minor fimbriae for adhesion, biofilm formation and virulence). GO analysis reveals significantly enriched ‘cell adhesion’, ‘pathogenesis’ (BP) and ‘host cell extracellular matrix binding’ (MF). Interestingly, the representatives RagA, Kgp, RgpA and ferritin in the clusters are affected by temperature and levels of hemin. Anyhow, fimbriae are upregulated at a high level of hemin. This study suggests that altered micro-environmental factors as hemin and temperature significantly affect the pathogenetic profiles of P. gingivalis like the proteins related to cell adhesion, biofilm formation and virulence factors (e.g., gingipains and fimbriae). It strongly supports the current ecological notion of microbe-host interactions for effective oral healthcare, highlighting the great importance of effect control of both plaque biofilms and inflammation in managing periodontal patients.

17119819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17119819.value: Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) is the keystone periodontopathogen, and yet it crucially contributes to systemic comorbidities like cardiovascular disease (CVD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD). Based upon our first identification of Pg persisters on invading human gingival epithelial cells, and the resultant perturbance of immuno-inflammatory responses via disrupting the FOXO1 signaling and downstream genes (e.g., BCL2L11) (Wang et al. 2020, 2022; Wang & Jin 2022), the extensive studies on the interactions of Pg with various host cells, e.g., THP-1 macrophages, human endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) and human neuroblastoma SH-SY5Y cells, advance the scientific work on Pg pathogenicity with translational potentials and application perspectives. -Pg aggravates host response, via disrupting the ratio of M1/M2 macrophages. Further study may explore the possibility of modulating macrophage polarization as a potential therapeutic target for effectively controlling periodontitis and its inflammatory comorbidities. -Pg LPS significantly perturbs the gene expression of EPCs via affecting multiple pathways in translational regulation of protein synthesis. Further investigation can clarify the potential involvement of Pg in disrupting the function of EPCs and the pathogenesis of CVD. -Bismuth drugs like CBS effectively combat Pg persisters via synergistic use of metronidazole (Wang et al. 2021). The extended work reveals that the newly synthesized bismuth-organic frameworks exhibit potent anti-Pg effects (Huang et al. 2023). Bismuth drugs and nano-based novel approaches are worthy of further translational studies and development. -Pg reduces the ubiquitination of multiple proteins in SH-SY5Y cells, and bismuth drugs could to some extent restore it, indicating an unidentified mechanism of Pg involved in AD via suppressing the ubiquitin proteasome pathway. Yet, Pg invades the SH-SY5Y cells and perturbs multi-pathways genes like TNF-mediated NF-κB signaling. Bismuth drugs restore the perturbed expression of genes relating to the ‘lysosome’ and ‘Alzheimer disease’ pathways (the journal manuscript under preparation). -Micro-environmental factors like hemin/temperature for mimicking healthy/diseased periodontal conditions affect the adhesion, biofilm formation and virulence expression of Pg. It thereby develops intrinsic strategies for better survival in host tissues, highlighting the profound importance of effectively controlling plaque biofilms and oral/periodontal inflammation in clinical practice (the abstract has been submitted for presentation in 2024 IADR meeting). -The expanded studies during COVID-19 reveal that salivary ACE2/TMPRSS2 link to periodontal status and metabolic parameters (Zhao et al, 2022), and the novel single-cell Raman spectroscopy study shows the enhanced metabolic activities of Escherichia coli persisters, facilitating further investigations on microbial persisters (Wang et al, 2022).

17119819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17119819.value: The present in vitro study demonstrates that P. gingivalis and its noxious persisters are crucially involved in periodontal pathogenesis, and yet account for common systemic comorbidities like cardiovascular disease and Alzheimer's disease. Bismuth drugs like CBS in synergistic combination with metronidazole are promising for tackling P. gingivalis persisters. It is therefore highly warranted to extensively extend the current study for maximizing the translational potentials and application perspectives in the near future. The proposed actions are briefly presented as follows: 1) Further in vivo study needs to be undertaken in animal models of experimental periodontitis and peri-implantitis, for exemplify the notable pathogenic effects of P. gingivalis and its persisters through various classic and state-of-the-art multi-omics approaches, and yet seeking novel tackling strategies and therapeutic targets. 2) Bismuth drugs should be further intensively tested on various host cells and tissues through local and systemic delivery vehicles, for effective management of oral/periodontal diseases and common systemic comorbidities like Alzheimer's disease, in line the emerging precision medicine and periodontics as well as WHO’s global healthcare framework. 3) Meanwhile, nano-based novel approaches like the synthesized bismuth-organic frameworks could be further developed for translational applications.

17119819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17119819.value: Gum disease is a major global oral disease burden and accounts for huge socio-economic impacts. Yet, it closely links to life-threatening diseases like diabetes, heart disease, Alzheimer's disease and COVID-19, through the pathways of infection, inflammation, maladaptive stem cells and common lifestyle risk factors. Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) as a key bacterial pathogen and its persisters (the tiny amount of survivors after harsh antimicrobial treatment) are crucially involved in severe gum disease and related to heart disease and Alzheimer's disease. The research team has demonstrated: -Pg and Pg persisters invade various host cells and badly disrupt host responses, via newly identified multiple molecular mechanisms; -This pathogen affects the neural cells of brain, through accumulating Alzheimer’s disease-related neurotoxic stuff; -The bismuth drugs often used for treating stomach diseases in combination with the antibiotic (metronidazole) effectively tackle Pg persisters and reverse the resultant bad effects; and -Micro-environmental/host conditions like gum inflammation significantly affect the survival strategies of Pg, indicating the great importance of controlling dental plaque and oral/gum inflammation for oral and general health. It encourages further studies to establish new preventive/therapeutic approaches to better managing oral/gum diseases and related systemic diseases, in line with WHO’s global healthcare strategies.

17120119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17120119.value: 愈來愈多的研究表明全身性炎症對神經炎症的影響，導致病理因素和認知功能障礙的積累。然而，其全身性炎症如何傳遞給神經炎症或大腦及其潛在機制仍不清楚。這是神經免疫學和神經變性的聖杯問題。我們採用剖腹手術的實驗模型用於術後認知功能障礙（POCD）。我們從老鼠身上取出腸子進行按摩，然後在沒有任何手術解剖的情況下放回腹部。我們已經證明麻醉劑的效果只是短暫的。我們的研究表明，系統性炎症不是由於麻醉劑，而是以維持小膠質細胞/星形膠質細胞的活化，長期tau磷酸化和認知功能障礙所引起的長期影響。應用抗炎藥物布洛芬(ibuprofen)可以消退所有這些效果。因此，這個實驗模型是我們研究神經免疫學關鍵問題的理想選擇。 在不同的因素中，我們最近獲得的結果顯示，alpha4beta2菸鹼乙酰膽鹼受體（nAChR）的部分激動劑可以減弱炎症反應，tau磷酸化和認知功能障礙。目前“膽鹼能抗炎通路”的概念通常主要集中在alpha7nAChR上。關於對alpha4beta2異構體的知識甚少。這項研究的目的是闡明alpha4beta2nAChR對全身炎症和神經炎症的作用。我們的工作假設是alpha4beta2nAChR可以作為治療靶點，減輕全身炎症，神經炎症，tau病理和認知功能障礙。我們將使用分子方法（cre-lox方法）專門敲除alpha4亞基，這樣就不會在巨噬細胞上形成功能性alpha4beta2nAChR，然後進行剖腹手術。一些研究小組將通過子宮內電穿孔進行拯救實驗，以回饋alpha4亞基。接下來，我們將使用alpha4beta2激動劑varienicline和TC2599於剖腹手術後來研究激動劑能否減輕全身炎症，巨噬細胞浸潤（攜帶綠色熒光蛋白），tau病理和認知功能障礙。 由於alpha7nAChR激動劑具有廣譜的生理功能，因此可能不是理想的藥用靶點。 相反，alpha4beta2nAChR激動劑可以是減輕炎症的理想藥用靶點，因為我們不能簡單地長時間關閉免疫反應和不考慮布洛芬的副作用。 我們的研究可以提升我們的知識並重塑未來的臨床實踐，以防止手術中的神經炎症，甚至可能需要手術的阿爾茨海默病患者的神經變性進展。

17120119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17120119.value: Increasing lines of evidence from ours and other laboratories have shown that immune responses in the body can be quickly transferred to the brain to initiate neuroimmune responses. Once the brain immune responses are stimulated, the activation of microglia is long lasting, partly perhaps due to the constant infiltration of activated macrophages in the brain. Therefore, we investigate a novel approach to modulate systemic macrophages via cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway. It has been shown that macrophages express both alpha-4 and alpha-7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor. We aim to investigate alpha-4 nicotinic receptor (a4nAChR) because manipulation of alpha-7 receptor can easily affect cholinergic neurons. We at first (Part 1) investigate if knockout of a4nAChR on macrophages by using cre-lox method can modulate systemic and neuroimmune responses triggered by sterile inflammation (by laparotomy). Indeed, by comparing the wild type receiving laparotomy, knockout mice did not showed any significant increase in expression of mRNA for cytokines in the liver and blood cells. Apart from systemic inflammation, neuroimmune responses in terms of gene expression of cytokines and activation of microglia/astrocytes. The knockout mice displayed less number of neuronal loss and did not show any cognitive dysfunctions. However, these kinds of immune modulation can be reversed by using a7nAChR antagonist MLA. The results suggest that a7nAChR compensate the loss of a4nAChR. The results also imply that we could not simple knockout a4nAChR by using any molecular biology techniques. Therefore, we have to move to Part 2 using pharmacological approach by a4nAChR agonist. This study stems from our previous investigation of partial a4nAChR agonist varenicline. It can significantly reduce both systemic and neuroimmune responses. In addition, it can reverse cognitive dysfunctions. Therefore, we further selected other a4nAChR agonists in our Part 2 study. Unfortunately, some agonists showed some neurotoxic effects. We finally investigated the effects of ABT594 (tebanicline, Tocris). Application of this a4nAChR agonist significantly reversed the increase of IL-6, MCP-1 and IL-10 in the liver, and IL-1beta and IL-6 in the hippocampus of the brain. It significantly reduced the cell size of microglia in dentate gyrus (DG) after laparotomy, reduced neuronal loss and cognitive dysfunctions. Therefore, ABT594 could be another ideal agonist to modulate a4nAChR in addition to varenicline. In conclusion, modulation of nAChR is a good approach to change the activation of macrophages/microglia after systemic inflammation. In order to minimize the side effects on neurons, targeting a4nAChR pave the road for future pharmacological application against neuroinflammation.

17120119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17120119.value: As mentioned, ours and other laboratories have demonstrated that systemic immune responses can trigger neuroimmune responses that can deteriorate progress of neurodegeneration. Systemic immune responses can be stimulated by infection (even oral infection as periodontitis), surgical trauma, wound injury, organ failure, stress, and obesity. More importantly, our study shows that neuroimmune responses orchestrated by microglia can be a long-lasting process even systemic immune responses return back to resting state. Therefore, we should find and discover a new and novel pathway to modulate both systemic and neuroimmune responses. From ours previous study using varenicline and other laboratories, cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway seems to be promising. However, since macrophages and microglia express both a7- and a4nAChR, we should be cautious for targeting a7nAChR because a7nAChR is the major cholinergic receptor in cholinergic neurons. A4nAChR becomes an ideal pharmacological target. Varenicline is a partial agonist of a4nAChR only. While our study shows that ABT594 seems to be effective. Its efficacy is similar to varenicline. Therefore, the next phase of development is to modify the structure of either varenicline or ABT594 to increase the specificity and efficacy of their agonistic effects. We will attempt to work with experts in chemistry to modify the structure.

17120119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17120119.value: Ours and other laboratories have shown that stimulation of body immune system because of injury, infection, trauma, organ failure or even stress can activate the immune cells microglia in the brain. Activation of immune system in the brain is not welcome because it can be harmful to neurons and accelerate progress of neurodegeneration in Alzheimer’s disease. Therefore, we should investigate a pharmacological approach to modulate both macrophages and microglia. These cells can express receptor of neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine. The receptor for acetylcholine has two subunits called a4 or a7. Since neurons express a7 and we do not want to disturb normal functions of neurons, we investigate whether we can modulate a4 subunit to minimize activation of macrophages and microglia. Indeed, our first part of results using knockout mice demonstrated that a4 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor could markedly reduce their activation, reduce neuronal loss and cognitive dysfunction. In our part 2 investigation, we could even find out a chemical ligand that binds to a4 subunit of the receptor to stimulate this receptor can reduce activation of macrophages and microglia. In conclusion, our study can pave a road for future pharmacological intervention to alleviate immune responses in the brain.

17121219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121219.value: Background Aggressive surgical resection has be advocated in Hong Kong and Asia. However, due to high patient volume the usual waiting time for HCC in Queen Mary Hospital is around 6 weeks. This provides a need and good opportunity to study the benefit of bridging treatment from diagnosis to actual liver resection. Patients with intermediate and locally advanced stage HCC will be good candidates for investigation because 1) bridging therapy is need from diagnosis to surgery to prevent tumour progression, 2) systemic treatment may potentially downstage the lesion and may improve the short term and long term outcome of surgery . Aim and hypothesis The aim of the current study is to evaluate the pathological response of neoadjuvant therapy by checkpoint inhibitor (Nivolumab) in patients with HCC undergoing liver resection. We hypothesize that this is a safe treatment option and various degree of tumour necrosis can be observed in hepatectomy specimen. Methods This is a phase 2, single-arm trial designed to assess the clinical benefit of treatment with nivolumab administered in patients with untreated, borderline resectable HCC as classified in intermediate and locally advanced HCC by HKLC cancer staging will be included. Eligible patients will receive nivolumab at 3 mg/kg on Day 1 of each 2-weekly cycle for a total of 3 cycles, with curative resection planned approximately 6 weeks after the first dose. Sample size calculation The primary endpoint is pathological response rate. There is no published clinical data available to estimate the pathological response rate of nivolumab in patients with HCC. A cohort of 20 patients is considered sufficient to evaluate any evidence of benefit, as measured by tumour responses, safety and tolerability. Timeline and feasibility Patient recruitment will be conducted over a 3-year period. The annual volume of hepatectomy in Queen Mary Hospital is around 200 cases. 80 cases will be classified into intermediate and locally advanced HCC. Patients who fall into this category can be recruit to this study. The perioperative surgical outcome, pathological response can be revaluated within 1 week after surgery. One year recurrent free survival will be evaluated. The recruitment schedule is highly feasible. Future study The findings of this study will provide fundamentals for proof of concept using checkpoint inhibitors as neoadjuvant therapy for patients with HCC. Phase III study on this area will be performed. 背景： 在香港和亞洲其他地方，普遍都倡導以切除手術治療肝細胞癌（肝癌）。然而，由於香港的肝癌患者數量眾多，在瑪麗醫院，確診後至肝切除手術的輪候時間通常長約6週。這顯示了研究在輪候手術期間進行銜接性治療的必要性，長輪候時間亦為此提供良好機會。患有中期和局部晚期肝癌的患者是理想的研究對象，因為（1）他們需要銜接性治療以防止腫瘤惡化，（2）全身性治療可能使腫瘤降期，並可能改善手術的短期和長期成果。 目的和假設： 本研究的目的是在準備接受肝切除術的肝癌患者中，評估以免疫檢查點抑制劑（Nivolumab）作術前治療的病理反應。我們假設這個治療選擇是安全的，並且在肝切除標本中可以觀察到不同程度的腫瘤壞死。 方法： 這是一項第二期、單組臨床試驗，旨在評估使用Nivolumab治療未經治療的臨界可切除肝癌（即HKLC分期系統界定為中期和局部晚期肝癌）患者的臨床益處。符合條件的患者將在每個週期的第一天接受劑量為3 mg/kg的Nivolumab，每一週期為兩星期，總共三個週期。肝切除手術預定在第一次用藥後約6週。 樣本數估算： 主要評估指標是病理緩解率。目前還沒有臨床數據可用於評估nivolumab對肝癌的病理緩解率。20名患者應足以評估治療有沒有益處，包括腫瘤反應、安全性和耐受性。 時間表和可行性： 瑪麗醫院每年的肝切除手術量約為200宗，當中約80宗分類為中級和局部晚期肝癌。屬於這一類別的患者會被招募參與本研究。手術前後期間的結果和病理反應評估可在術後1週內進行，一年的無復發存活率將會被評估。患者招募期為3年，招募計劃非常可行。 未來研究： 本研究的結果將為使用免疫檢查點抑制劑作為肝癌患者的術前治療提供概念驗證的基礎，將來可能在此領域進行第三期臨床研究。

17121219.label: Realisation of objectives
17121219.value: Objective 1. To study the efficacy and safety of nivolumab as a neoadjuvant therapy in patients with HCC. Of these 2 patients who had died, 1 patient (57 years old) died of recurrent disease, whereas the other 80-year-old patient without tumor recurrence died of toxic epidermal necrolysis >3 months after surgery (most likely related to the prolonged use of antibiotics for treatment of postoperative collections). The 1-year overall survival was 89.5% (nivo-R group: 100%; nivo-NR group: 83.3%; slightly higher in the nivo-R group), and the overall 1-year tumor recurrence rate was 36.8% (nivo-R group: 28.6%; nivo-NR group: 41.7%; slightly lower in the nivo-R group). Regarding the 3 nivo-R patients with >90% tumor necrosis, they were all alive and recurrence-free at the latest follow-up, indicating that a high degree of tumor necrosis after neoadjuvant nivolumab treatment might indicate durable response. A total of 9 patients had increased serum alphafetoprotein (AFP) levels of >20 ng/mL at baseline before nivolumab, but the baseline AFP levels were not particularly associated with nivolumab response. All nivo-R patients showed some degree of reduction in the AFP level in the course of nivolumab treatment, although not reaching statistical significance (p = 0.068). There was a trend that some of the nivo-R patients experienced a decline in AFP level. On the other hand, 5 of nivo-NR patients experienced an increase in AFP level after 3 cycles of nivolumab treatment but before surgical resection. Objective 2. To examine the relationship between pathological response and cellular and molecular profiles of patients' HCC tumors, as well as the effects of nivolumab on the tumor immune microenvironment. Pathologic analysis of liver tumors from patients treated with nivolumab showed tumor necrosis and increased immune cell infiltration. The necrosis was often hemorrhagic and accompanied by T cell infiltrate. Assessment of tumor necrosis through pathology correlated with changes in CT image size. RNA-seq analysis revealed differences in gene expression between pre- and post-nivolumab tumor tissues and PBMC samples. Cellular deconvolution analysis showed that patients with major pathologic response had increased proportions of CD8 T cells, indicating better restoration of cytotoxic T-cell infiltration. Objective 3. To derive a noninvasive biomarker from plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) that could predict the response toward anti-PD-1 ICB and may be useful to guide its administration. The study investigated the role of somatic mutations and tumor mutation burden (TMB) in predicting response to immunotherapy in hepatocellular carcinoma patients. While TMB was not found to be statistically different between responders and non-responders, mutations related to CDKN2A, epithelial mesenchymal transition, p53, G2-M checkpoint, and PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathways were associated with anti-PD-1 response. However, somatic mutations were found to be less informative than copy number variations in determining response to immunotherapy. The study also detected HBV integration in some cases but found no major differences between responders and non-responders.
