17121219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121219.value: 1. Neoadjuvant nivolumab treatment had a relatively high response rate of 36.8% in predominantly HBV-positive HCC patients with intermediate and locally advanced tumors. Almost complete (>90%) tumor necrosis was seen in about 16% of the cases. 2. The study found conspicuous hemorrhagic necrosis in the post-nivolumab resection specimens, which has not been reported in previous studies. 3. The study observed that higher CD8 T-cell infiltration was associated with a positive response to nivolumab treatment. A relative shift from resting to activated CD4 memory T cells was found in responsive cases, whereas a trend of reversed shift was observed in non-responsive cases. 4. The study identified significant overexpression of the gene signature that governs innate immunity in responsive cases compared to non-responsive cases, suggesting that the elevated antigen presentation by innate immunity may provide a favorable immunogenic environment to support the action of immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). 5. A noninvasive circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)-based anti-PD-1 score was derived in the study, which could potentially predict the response of anti-PD-1 ICB. 6. The study demonstrated that the use of nivolumab is safe and effective in the neoadjuvant setting for intermediate and locally advanced HCCs. A short course of neoadjuvant therapy may deliver durable therapeutic outcomes in a small subset of patients.

17121219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121219.value: The research could be expanded by conducting larger-scale studies to validate the findings and by exploring the neoadjuvant use of drug combinations or other second-line drugs. The study also suggests evaluating noninvasive cfDNA biomarkers to predict nivolumab treatment response and investigating the cellular and molecular basis of nivolumab response in HCC patients. Further studies could also explore the use of combined administration of agonists for innate immunity and ICB to improve treatment outcomes.

17121219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121219.value: The study investigated the use of a drug called nivolumab as a pre-surgery treatment for patients with a specific type of liver cancer called hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The researchers found that nivolumab was safe and effective in treating patients with intermediate and advanced stages of HCC. The drug helps to destroy cancer cells and boost the body's immune response against the tumor. Additionally, the study discovered a potential noninvasive blood test that could help predict how well a patient would respond to the treatment. This research is valuable because it could lead to improved treatment strategies for liver cancer patients and help identify those who are more likely to benefit from nivolumab therapy.

17121419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121419.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the fourth leading cause of cancer death worldwide and is also an endemic cancer in Hong Kong, mainland China and Southeast Asia. Cytotoxic chemotherapy does not have ideal clinical efficacy due to the emergence of highly resistant cancer stem cells (CSCs) including HCC CSCs. Our previous studies have identified that a CD133+ population of CSCs had clinical significance in promoting progression and relapse of HCC. While discovery of novel therapeutics targeting CD133+ CSCs is highly expected, currently available treatments are however reported merely targeting well-differentiated HCC cells. An alkaloid fangchinoline derived from Chinese herb, Stephania tetrandra S. Moore was shown to inhibit well-differentiated human cancer cells including HCC. Our preliminary study observed that fangchinoline could significantly suppress CD133+ CSCs population within HCC tumour orthotopically implanted to mice liver and inhibit tumour growth. Isolated CD133+ CSCs from HCC treated with fangchinoline exhibited reduced tumorsphere formation, growth and expression of CSCs markers. This new property of fangchinoline in suppressing hepatic CSCs deserves systematic study. To depict the mechanism of fangchinoline on hepatic CSCs, microarray analysis was performed to identify the transcriptomic changes of CSCs after fangchinoline treatment. We found that wt1 gene that encodes Wilms’ tumor protein (WT1) other than its paralog WT2 was the most down-regulated gene in fangchinoline-treated CD133+ CSCs. Our preliminary study to re-express WT1 in fangchinoline-treated CD133+ CSCs recovered tumorsphere formation and expression of CSCs markers. The essential role of WT1 inhibition in mediating the in vitro and in vivo repression of hepatic CSCs by fangchinoline will be examined. Furthermore, WT1-associated proteins such as Sox9 and CD133 and signalling pathways that maintain the stemness property of CSCs were repressed by fangchinoline. With the above observations, we hypothesise that inhibition of WT1 and its associated signalling mediates inhibitory effect of fangchinoline on CD133+ CSCs derived from HCC. We propose (1) to systematically investigate the in vivo inhibition of tumorigenicity of CD133+ CSCs by fangchinoline alone and in combination with chemotherapeutics; (2) to investigate the role of WT1 in mediating the suppressive effect of fangchinoline on CD133+ CSCs; and (3) to elucidate the regulatory mechanism of fangchinoline on the upstream and downstream signalling of WT1. Successful demonstration of the effect of fangchinoline and elucidation of its underlying mechanism will contribute to the development of novel therapeutics from Chinese Medicines targeting CSCs as a treatment for HCC. 肝細胞癌（HCC）是全球第四大癌症，也是香港、中國大陸和東南亞的地方性癌症，而細胞毒性化療由於HCC癌症幹細胞（CSC）的高抗性而不具有理想的臨床療效。我們以前的研究已經確定CD133 + CSCs群體在促進HCC的進展和復發方面具有臨床意義。發現靶向CD133 + CSC的新療法值得期待。來自中草藥Stephania tetrandra S. Moore的生物鹼防己諾林鹼能夠顯著抑制分化良好的人癌細胞，包括HCC細胞。我們最近的調查預測，防己諾林鹼可能會影響CSCs相關信號。在我們的初步研究中，觀察到了防己諾林鹼對原位HCC的體內抑制，且這種作用不伴隨著毒性。特別是，防己諾林鹼可以顯著抑制原位HCC中的CD133 + CSCs細胞群。從防己諾林鹼處理的HCC腫瘤中分離的CD133 + CSC表現出減少的腫瘤球形成，生長和細胞週期進展的抑制，以及減少包括Oct4、Nanog和Bmi-1的CSC標誌物的表達。我們通過cDNA微陣列分析，篩選了防己諾林鹼處理的CD133 + CSCs基因表達的變化，發現在HCC中失調的一組癌基因可能是防己諾林鹼的潛在靶標。我們發現編碼Wilm腫瘤蛋白（WT1）的wt1基因而非不是其旁系同源物WT2是CD133 + CSCs中受防己諾林鹼下調最多的基因。近來的發現表明，WT1在HCC中過表達，導致HCC細胞去分化和產生對化療的抗性。防己諾林鹼能夠抑制保持CSC幹性的WT1相關蛋白和激酶，例如Sox9和CD133。在fangchinoline處理的CD133 + CSC中重新表達WT1，恢復了腫瘤球形成能力和CSC標誌物的表達。此外，防己諾林鹼可以抑制低氧腫瘤環境下CD133 + CSCs中HIF1α相關的WT1表達。通過上述觀察，我們假設WT1及其相關信號傳導的抑制介導了防己諾林鹼對源自HCC的CD133 + CSC的抑制作用。我們將（1）系統地研究單獨使用防己諾林鹼或與化療藥物聯合抑制CD133 + CSCs的體內致瘤性; （2）研究WT1在介導防己諾林鹼對CD133 + CSCs的抑製作用中的作用; （3）闡明防己諾林鹼對WT1上游和下游信號傳導的調控機制。關於防己諾林鹼的影響和闡明其潛在機制的成功證明將有助於開發針對CSC的中藥新療法。

17121419.label: Realisation of objectives
17121419.value: Specific Aim 1: Validation of Fangchinoline's Inhibition of CD133+ CSCs Achievements: 1. Demonstrated fangchinoline's effectiveness in reducing tumor growth and inhibiting CD133+ CSCs in liver tumors. 2. Established that fangchinoline was effective against the in vivo tumorigenicity of CD133+ CSCs, as shown by its suppression of tumorsphere formation and stemness marker expression. 3. Observed significant findings regarding the combination of fangchinoline with chemotherapeutics like doxorubicin and 5-fluorouracil, offering potential for enhanced treatment efficacy. 4. Conducted thorough investigations to determine optimal doses and routes of fangchinoline administration in vivo​​. Challenges and Responses: 1. Faced complexities in isolating and targeting CD133+ CSCs, which were addressed through advanced isolation methodologies and precise experimental designs. 2. Encountered difficulties in accurately assessing the efficacy of fangchinoline in combination with existing chemotherapeutics, which necessitated extensive in vivo studies and careful monitoring of tumor development and response. Specific Aim 2: Investigating the Role of WT1 in Fangchinoline's Action Achievements: 1. Found that fangchinoline specifically suppressed WT1 expression in CD133+ liver CSCs, a key finding given WT1's link to poor prognosis in HCC. 2. Demonstrated that the re-expression of WT1 could reverse the suppressive effects of fangchinoline, highlighting the significance of WT1 in mediating fangchinoline’s action. 3. Advanced our understanding of the interaction between WT1 and other critical factors like p53 and Sox9 in the context of liver CSCs​​. Challenges and Responses: Encountered complexities in deciphering the precise molecular interactions and pathways involved in WT1 suppression, which were tackled through comprehensive in vitro studies and targeted gene manipulation techniques. Specific Aim 3: Elucidating Fangchinoline's Regulatory Mechanism on WT1 Signalling Achievements: 1. Established the influence of fangchinoline on the upstream and downstream signaling of WT1. 2. Confirmed that fangchinoline's suppression of HIF1α plays a role in targeting WT1 in CSCs under hypoxic conditions. 3. Demonstrated the compound's impact on the Wnt/β-catenin signalling pathway, a crucial aspect in understanding its overall mechanism of action. 4. Identified the effect of fangchinoline on key downstream effectors like Sox9, providing insights into its broader impact on liver CSCs​​. Challenges and Responses: Faced the challenge of linking fangchinoline’s molecular action to broader cellular effects, requiring extensive signaling pathway analysis and innovative experimental approaches. Overall Summary The project has successfully met its primary objectives, advancing our understanding of fangchinoline's potential as a novel treatment against liver cancer. While there were challenges related to the complexity of cancer stem cell biology and the intricacies of molecular interactions, these were effectively addressed through methodical research strategies and collaborative efforts. The outcomes not only reinforce the therapeutic promise of fangchinoline but also lay a robust foundation for future clinical applications.

17121419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121419.value: In our study, we have established that fangchinoline is a potent inhibitor of CD133+ cancer stem cells (CSCs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This compound not only showed the tumorigenicity of these cells in vivo but also significantly reduced their ability to form tumorspheres in vitro. Remarkably, fangchinoline achieved these effects without inducing cytotoxicity, indicating a specific action against the stemness properties of the CSCs. This is particularly important as it suggests a mechanism of action that is distinct from conventional chemotherapy, which often attacks both cancer and healthy cells. Our results are supported by extensive in vivo experiments that determined the optimal dosage and administration routes for fangchinoline, laying the groundwork for future clinical applications (Results of Specific Aim 1​​). Our investigation further revealed the crucial role of Wilms’ tumor gene 1 (WT1) in mediating fangchinoline’s suppressive effects on liver CSCs. WT1, commonly upregulated in HCC, is associated with poor prognosis due to its involvement in cell dedifferentiation and chemoresistance. We discovered that fangchinoline significantly downregulates WT1 expression, particularly in CD133+ liver CSCs, compared to their CD133- counterparts. The suppression of WT1 by fangchinoline correlates with a decrease in stem cell marker expression and a reduction in the cells' tumorigenic properties. These findings underscore the potential of WT1 as a therapeutic target in liver CSCs, and fangchinoline as a promising candidate for targeted therapy (Results of Specific Aim 2​​). Moreover, our study explored the broader regulatory mechanisms of fangchinoline on the signaling pathways associated with WT1. We observed a suppression of HIF-1α, a factor that promotes WT1 expression, particularly under hypoxic conditions that mimic the tumor microenvironment. This suppression is postulated to contribute to the downregulation of WT1 by fangchinoline, highlighting a novel mechanism of action. We also found that fangchinoline disrupts the Wnt/LEF1/Sox9 signaling cascade, which plays a crucial role in CSC self-renewal and aggressiveness. By inhibiting this pathway, fangchinoline may reduce the stemness and tumorigenic potential of liver CSCs, offering a new approach to combat HCC recurrence and metastasis (Results of Specific Aim 3​​).

17121419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121419.value: Building on the foundation of our preclinical research, we may set the stage for Phase I and II clinical trials to meticulously assess fangchinoline's safety, optimal dosage, and efficacy as a complementary therapy in hepatocellular carcinoma, particularly for cases unresponsive to current treatments. Our strategy includes biomarker analysis to precisely pinpoint which patient subsets will most benefit from fangchinoline. We anticipate that this compound, with its targeted action on cancer stem cells and potential to reduce chemoresistance, could substantially boost the potency of established chemotherapeutic protocols. It may marke a significant advancement in HCC treatment. The trials will also rigorously evaluate the safety profile of fangchinoline in conjunction with other drugs, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of its effects and side effects. The aspiration is not only to augment current therapeutic strategies but also to reimagine them, It aims to significantly improve the prognosis and quality of life for patients with HCC.

17121419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121419.value: In the fight against liver cancer by Chinese medicine, we have spotlighted a special ingredient known as fangchinoline. It targets the tricky cancer stem cells—those that cause cancer to resist treatment and return even after it seems to be gone. Our laboratory experiments have demonstrated that fangchinoline can decelerate the growth of these cancer cells and boost the effectiveness of existing cancer medications. This suggests a potential to amplify the efficacy of conventional cancer therapies, offering a hope of enhanced treatment. As we proceed, our future goal is to embark on rigorous clinical trials to affirm fangchinoline's safety for human use and to validate its effectiveness in a real-world setting, beyond the controlled conditions of a laboratory. Our aspiration with fangchinoline is to furnish a novel therapeutic option that could prevent the recurrence of liver cancer and significantly ameliorate the quality of life for those afflicted by this severe disease. By potentially reinforcing existing treatment methodologies with fangchinoline, we stand on the advancement of a new era in oncological care, one that improves the effect of Chinese medicine to confront the complexities of cancer challenges.

17121619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121619.value: Degeneration of intervertebral discs, the major connective joint tissues in the vertebral column, is associated with low back pain incidence and severity. Understanding the mechanism of disc degeneration is key to the control and management of this worldwide disease burden. Inflammation is an essential component in the process of wound healing. However, sustained proinflammatory stimuli can inhibit normal tissue repair and trigger pathological consequences. Disc degeneration has been linked to an upregulated activity of proinflammatory cytokines, in particular interleukin 1 (IL-1). Many cell culture studies have indicated a negative regulatory role of IL-1 in extracellular matrix production. Nonetheless, the knowledge of IL-1 effects is built on the bulk cell phenotype and the evaluation of selected genes. Its precise impact on cell state and fate of the disc cells remains elusive. A major obstacle that limits the investigation is the heterogeneity and ill-defined composition of the disc cells, and therefore the inability to trace the effects in individual cell subpopulations. Study in other tissue system has suggested a function of NF-kB, the downstream mediator of IL-1, in inducing cell dedifferentiation to a progenitor-like state. Our recent in vivo cell lineage tracing study has also indicated that local disc cells may acquire a fibroblastic state after puncture induced injury, supporting disc degeneration involves a process featuring cell dedifferentiation. We hypothesize that cellular dysfunction in IVD degeneration is associated with a de-differentiation program mediated by IL-1. In this study, we aim to take advantage of the single-cell RNA sequencing to obtain genome-wide transcriptome data from individual cells and delineate the impact of IL-1 on disc cell subpopulations. The findings will be subsequently validated in clinical samples. This large data set generated will allow us to construct a cell fate profile and lineage hierarchy under the effect of IL-1. Overall, the outcome will advance our understanding in how this key proinflammatory molecule modulates disc degeneration at the level of cellular composition. The success of this study will lead to a more sophisticated way to evaluate the impact of biological stimuli or environmental factors on disc cells, facilitating the development of better disc regeneration approaches in future. 椎間盤的退變與腰痛發生率和嚴重程度相關，了解椎間盤退變的機制是控制和管理這種全球疾病負擔的關鍵。炎症是傷口癒合的重要過程，然而，持續的炎症刺激會抑制正常的組織修復並導致病變。椎間盤退變與促炎細胞因子，特別是白細胞介素1（IL-1）的上調活性有關。細胞培養研究表明IL-1在細胞外基質產生中有負面調節作用。儘管如此，我們對IL-1效應的了解都建立在整體細胞表型和所選基因的評估之上，它對個別細胞狀態和椎間盤細胞命運的精確影響仍然不清楚。研究的主要障礙是由於椎間盤細胞的異質性和其不明確的組成，因此無法追踪單個細胞亞群的影響。在其他組織系統中的研究已經表明NF-kb（IL-1的下游介質）於誘導細胞去分化成祖細胞狀態的功能。我們最近的體內細胞譜系追踪研究亦表明，局部椎間盤細胞可以在穿刺損傷後獲得成纖維細胞狀態，支持椎間盤退變涉及細胞去分化這立論。我們假設椎間盤退變中的細胞功能障礙與IL-1介導的去分化程序相關。本研究中的目標是利用單細胞RNA測序從單個細胞獲得全基因組轉錄組數據，從而分析IL-1對椎間盤細胞亞群的影響，並隨後在臨床樣本中驗證。生成的大數據將允許我們構建IL-1作用下的細胞命運和譜系層次結構。總體而言，結果將促進我們理解這關鍵促炎分子如何在細胞組成的層面上調控椎間盤退變。這項研究的成功可帶來更有效評估生物或環境因素對椎間盤細胞影響的方法，促進椎間盤再生研究的發展。

17121619.label: Realisation of objectives
17121619.value: Intervertebral discs (IVD) play a critical role in spinal movement and shock absorption and its injury or degeneration can lead to back pain. Interleukin-1 (IL-1) is regarded as the major proinflammatory cytokine that associates with intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD). Other than a role in catabolism, IL-1 is capable of cell fate control, such as de-differentiation of chondrocytes and epithelial cells. Many studies indicated IL-1 could attenuate the matrix production capacity and induce matrix degradation in the nucleus pulposus (NP), the core of IVD. In degenerative human IVD, however, the nucleus pulposus cells (NPC) were reported to be heterogenous, containing a spectrum of phenotypes resembling progenitor-, macrophage-, and fibroblast-like cells. The cause of such NPC heterogeneity and the possible impact of pro-inflammatory signals of IL-1 on the fate of individual NPC populations, especially how they become de-differentiated, remains elusive. Objective 1: To consolidate the temporal and dosage effect of IL-1 on human NP cell state We previously showed that NPC cultured in alginate present an enhanced extracellular matrix production and reduced cell de-differentiation. In current study, we performed bulk RNA sequencing and found that alginate culture of NPC increased transcriptional diversity and enrichment of endothelial and macrophage markers, while markers of fibroblastic and hypertrophic differentiation were reduced. Notably, alginate maintained the inflammatory responses of NPC, suggesting that alginate present a superior cell culture model for exploring IL-1 function. In colony formation assay, which was adopted to assess the progenitor activity, IL-1 treatment robustly enhanced (1.79 folds) the spheroids formation (CFU-S) despite large or small sized. Intriguingly, albeit a higher number of CFU-S formation in monolayer culture (19 vs 9.8), the NPC presented a similar fold change (1.75 folds) in CFU-S formation, implying a comparable reprogramming process. Transcriptome analysis found that the monolayer and alginate culture systems displayed shared and distinct effects on gene expression upon IL-1 treatment of human NPC. Objective 2. To construct an IL-1 induced cell fate hierarchy using scRNA-seq analysis We conducted single cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) with the abovementioned treatment regime. After 10X Genomics Chromium 3’ RNA sequencing, low-quality reads were filtered out via Cell Ranger. PCA analysis on 20,089 cells identified 9 cell clusters. Genes highly expressed in cluster 0 (IL1B; CCL20; CXCL8; MMP3) were mostly IL17 and TNF signaling components and related to cytokine and chemotaxis. Cluster 1 expressed genes pertaining to extrinsic regulation of apoptosis and thus considered as apoptotic cells. Differential expressed genes (DEGs) in cluster 2 were related to oxidation phosphorylation and ATP synthesis, which are known to associate with a variety of diseases, such as diabetic cardiomyopathy, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and rheumatoid arthritis. Interestingly, cluster 3 highly expressed pericyte markers TAGLN and ACTA2. Cluster 4 expressed genes involved in catabolic processes and proteosome, and were therefore speculated to be the IL-1-mediated effector population for matrix degradation. Cluster 5 expressed PAX1, PRG4, DNER, MELTF, DDR2 and MYL2, indicating a fibroprogenitor-like population and appeared insensitive to IL-1 treatment in the alginate system. Cluster 6 expressed CD74, IL1R, SERPINH1 and FOXP1, suggesting their endothelial nature and has an angiogenic function. Cluster 7 expressed genes related to chromatin/histone modification and enriched in cellular senescence and tumorigenesis. Higher level of this cluster in IL-1 treated samples may be indicative of enhanced cell aging. Cluster 8 cells presented a remarkably high level of TOP2A expression, indicating actively proliferating cells. Overall, NPC from both alginate and monolayer system displayed different cellular heterogeneity, with a significant higher number of apoptotic cells (cluster 1) in the alginate cultured cells. IL-1 treatment in alginate system significantly increased cluster 0 and 4, suggesting IL-1 could enrich NPC with roles in inflammatory response and matrix degradation. In comparison, IL-1 treatment under monolayer culture reduced inflammatory NPC (cluster 0), yet stimulated disease-related phenotype (cluster 2). The higher abundance of TOP2A+ NPC in monolayer-cultured NPC and its increase after IL-1 treatment might be related to NPC dedifferentiation. Altogether, our scRNA-seq analysis supported that alginate culture could maintain NPC heterogeneity, and therefore better simulate inflammatory responses to IL-1 treatment. In contrast, NPC in monolayer system showed reduced apoptotic cells and appeared more pericyte-like, and could be programmed to proliferative cells under presence of IL-1. Objective 3. To validate the hierarchy in clinical samples and induced IDD model Through an integrative analysis of 4 published human IDD scRNA-seq datasets, we identified multiple existing NPC phenotypes based on gene expression of ACAN, COL2A1 and SOX9: ChonNP (COL2A1+; CYR61+), FibroNP (COL1A1+; COL3A1+; POSTN+; ASPN+), RegNP (MMP3+; GPX3+), CyclingNP (TOP2A+; STMN1+) and ProgNP (PDGFRA+; PLA2G2A+). Of them, the proportion of FibroNP significantly increased with the IDD severity. In addition, immune related cells were also clustered as neutrophils (LYZ+), myeloid derived suppressor cells (MDSC+; MPO+), macrophages (CD68+), T cells (TRBC2+), endothelial cells (CD34+ and PECAM1+), pericytes (RGS5+ and ACTA2+), and erythrocytes (HBB+). We also observed increased CyclingNP in IDD samples, which is consistent to the IL-1 induced proliferative cells observed in vitro.

17121619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121619.value: In conclusion, our study showed that human NPC under alginate and monolayer system could undergo a comparable progenitor-like reprogramming process. However, transcriptome analysis found the two systems displayed shared and distinct effects upon IL-1 treatment. NPC displayed different cellular heterogeneity in alginate and monolayer system. Compared with monolayer cultured NPC, encapsulation and cultivation in alginate could better maintain cellular heterogeneity and their capacity for inflammatory and catabolic responses to IL-1. Integrative scRNA-seq analysis indicated the involvement of immunocytes and fibroblastic NPC in human IDD. Combining with the cell culture data, we propose that the emergence of proliferative NPC in IDD could be resulted from the presence of inflammatory cytokine, such as IL-1. We have submitted a manuscript about the findings to pre-print server as well as peer-reviewed journal for publication.

17121619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121619.value: Our findings have built a foundation of an in vitro system with characterized cell identity in relation to IDD and their behavior towards IL-1 at single cell level. In the future, the system can be utilized for investigating the mechanism of existing biologics or screening of new drugs for treating IDD. For instance, we can test the action of the candidate small molecules we previously identified from chemical libraries that have IDD modifying properties (under ITF-MRP project). This can be of translation value and facilitate new application of funding for further applied research.

17121619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121619.value: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is a common and may lead to back pain and disability. IDD is mediated by a loss of function of nucleus pulposus (NP) cells under chronic inflammatory condition. Interleukin-1 (IL-1) is a pivotal inflammatory mediator in IDD pathology. How IL-1 influence NP function and contribute to IDD at cellular level is not clear. By use of different cell culture systems and transcriptome study of IL-1 stimulation which cross-referenced to human IDD datasets, our study indicated that 3D hydrogel system may better maintain the activity of human NP cells in vitro and provide a more relevant model of response to IL-1 to study IDD pathology. Our findings suggest that human IDD involved an array of immune cells which may relate to the cytokine production. Our work propose a model where IL-1 might reprogram NPC to a dedifferentiated proliferative state, therefore leading to loss of function of the disc that prone to degeneration.

17121819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17121819.value: Type-2 diabetes is a major type of non-communicable diseases affecting approximately 10% of adults globally. Diabetic complications, including macrovascular and microvascular diseases and several types of cancer, are the top causes of death and disability among senior citizens in Hong Kong. Insulin is the principal hormone responsible for maintaining glucose homeostasis. Impaired insulin actions and defective insulin secretion by pancreatic β-cells are the two primary contributors to the development of type-2 diabetes. Insulin secretion is tightly regulated by a complex metabolic and hormonal network in response to nutrient loads in pancreatic β-cells. However, the molecular machineries which control the generation of metabolic coupling factors to induce insulin secretion remain poorly defined. β-klotho is a single-pass plasma membrane protein highly expressed in several metabolic tissues including pancreatic islets. The classical function of β-klotho is to act as an obligatory co-receptor for fibroblast growth factor (FGF)21, a hormone with multiple metabolic benefits on glucose/lipid homeostasis and insulin sensitivity. Unexpectedly, we have discovered an FGF21-independent function of β-klotho in regulating glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) in pancreatic β- cells. Our results showed that neither genetic ablation of FGF21 nor supplementation of recombinant FGF21 has any effects on GSIS, whereas β-cell-specific β-Klotho knockout mice exhibit a marked impairment in GSIS and glucose tolerance. By comprehensive analysis for the major regulatory steps of GSIS, we found that β-Klotho deficiency causes markedly reduced expression of several glucose-sensing genes (especially glucokinase), leading to defective glucose glycolysis and ATP production in pancreatic β-cells. Furthermore, we have obtained preliminary evidence showing that hypoxia-inducible factor-1 as a possible transcription factor that mediates the regulatory effects of β-Klotho in the induction of several glycolytic genes for insulin secretion in β-cells. Therefore, we propose that β-klotho is a key component of the molecular machineries controlling insulin secretion by coupling extracellular signals to glycolysis in β-cells. Reduced β-klotho expression in pancreatic islets is a causal contributor to defective GSIS, glucose intolerance and β-cell dysfunction in type-2 diabetes. We will test this hypothesis by comprehensively investigating the impact of β-klotho deficiency and overexpression on insulin secretion and glucose homeostasis in mice with type-2 diabetes, and will elucidate the FGF21-independent receptor and post-receptor signaling events whereby β-klotho enhances glycolytic pathways leading to insulin secretion in β-cells. The findings will deepen our understanding on pathophysiology of insulin secretion, and will answer whether β-klotho agonists can be developed as an insulin secretagogue drug for treatment of type-2 diabetes.

17121819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17121819.value: This study uncovers a novel role of β-klotho (KLB) as a key cell-surface regulator of GSIS by coupling the GP130 receptor signaling to glucose catabolism in β-cells independent of FGF21 action and represents a promising therapeutic target for diabetes, as summarized below. 1. Pharmacological treatment of FGF21 had no effects on GSIS in either intact islets or pancreatic β-cells. Genetic deletion of FGF21 also had no effects of GSIS in mouse. 2. β-cell-specific Klb KO (KlbRIP) mice displayed impaired GSIS and glucose control under either STC or HFD feeding. Downregulated KLB expression was correlated with decreased GSIS in diabetic islets while restoration of KLB was able to reverse impaired GSIS in diabetic islets. 3.KLB deficiency in pancreatic β-cells disrupts IL-6-evoked STAT3-HIF1α signaling and downstream glycolytic flux and GSIS. Restoration of active STAT3 or HIF1α could reverse impaired glycolysis and GSIS in KlbRIP islets. 4. STAT3 controls HIF1α expression via binding with STAT3-inducible elements within proximal promoter of murine Hif1α gene and activating transcription of Hif1α gene. 5. KLB interacts with GP130 and inhibits ubiquitin-dependent lysosomal degradation of GP130, therefore facilitating IL-6 singling transduction in pancreatic β-cells. In summary, our study identifies KLB as an important GSIS modulator in pancreatic β-cells beyond its original role as a co-receptor of FGF21. The findings shed new light on how a cellular membrane protein facilitates insulin secretagogue signaling and modulates GSIS in pancreatic β-cells. Additionally, we have uncovered a unique anti-insulin receptor autoantibody, which mimics insulin to bind and activate the insulin receptor, thereby triggering hypoglycemia in patient. This discovery paves the way to develop novel antibody-based anti-diabetic therapies. These findings have been published in Nature Metabolism, Frontiers in Endocrinology (see part-C, section 8). Additionally, we revealed KLB is a highly N-glycosylated protein and the N-glycosylation modulates KLB protein stability and cell membrane localization. The related findings have been summarized in a manuscript, which is being under submission to a peer-reviewed journal (see part-C, section 8). This project has provided opportunities for training four postgraduate students, including three PhD student and one MSc student (see part-C, section 10).

17121819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17121819.value: Traditionally, β-klotho was considered as a co-receptor for endocrine FGF19/21 and mediated their effects on glucose-lipid homeostasis, energy expenditure, bile acid metabolism and etc. Our study is the first to uncover that β-klotho is likely to be an independent modulator of glucose homeostasis and metabolic dysfunction beyond its role as a co-receptor for endocrine FGFs. Our findings open a new field in the exploration of β-klotho’s effects and functioning mechanisms. Considering various diseases, for example liver and lung cancer, reproductive disorders, bowel syndrome, and fatty liver diseases, have been linked with mutations of β-klotho, the independent roles and working mechanisms of β-klotho in these diseases will be further investigated. Meanwhile, we found β-klotho was highly N-glycosylated during post-translational modification in our previous experiments. The pathophysiological roles of such N-glycosylation of β-klotho will be elucidated in our following studies. We have obtained a RGC Area of Excellence (AOE728/18-M) to further expand the study of this exciting area, with the long-term objectives of developing more effective therapies for obesity-related insulin secretion defects by targeting β-klotho.

17121819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17121819.value: Increased blood glucose after meal can quickly stimulate pancreatic beta cells to secrete insulin to promote glucose uptake and utilization in major metabolic organs to maintain systematic glucose homeostasis. However, glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) is impaired in type-2 diabetic patients through mechanisms that have not been fully understood. In this study, we found that the single-transmembrane protein β-klotho is a key regulator of GSIS in both mouse and human islets. Reduced β-klotho expression contributes to impaired GSIS in beta cells in several different models with diabetes, whereas. overexpression of β-klotho in beta cells is able to alleviate impaired GSIS in diabetic mice, suggesting β-klotho is a potential therapeutic target for this disease. Mechanistically, our study reveals that β-klotho modulates GSIS through enhancing the cytokine interleukin-6-evoked glycolytic pathway, independent of its classical roles as the FGF21 coreceptor. In sum, our results not only uncover a novel therapeutic target for diabetes, but also shed new light on biological mechanism underlying insulin secretion.

17122019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122019.value: The organization and contraction of the artery play important roles in maintaining the circulation of nutrition in the body. Vascular smooth muscle cells are the fundamental building block of the artery. When there are stiffness changes of arteries due to vascular injuries or excess deposition of cholesterol plaques, vascular smooth muscle cells will start to assemble podosome and migrate. Podosome is one type of cell-matrix adhesions and contains protrusive F-actin network to degrade and penetrate through different layers of arterial wall. The irregular migration of vascular smooth muscle cells often marks the early stage of atherosclerosis. Therefore, it is particularly important to understand how stiffness of the extracellular microenvironment controls cell migration and podosome assembly in vascular smooth muscle cell. In this proposal, we will focus on stiffness-dependent regulation of F-actin assembly at the podosome, such as cofilin. Cofilin is an actin-depolymerizing factor (ADF) and can promote F-actin depolymerization by cutting actin filaments. Our pilot study suggests that cofilin phosphorylation and F-actin stability is dependent on the microenvironment stiffness of A7r5 vascular smooth muscle cells. Phosphorylated cofilin loses actin severing capability, and F-actin assembly at the podosome becomes more stable on the stiff substrate. It is known that Cdc42 GTPase can promote cofilin phosphorylation via the activation of PAK-LIMK pathway. Alpha-PIX is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor of Cdc42 and dynamically recruited at the podosome. Here, we seek to demonstrate that alpha-PIX serves as the upstream mechanosensitive signal to promote Cdc42-mediated cofilin phosphorylation and podosome stability. With the combination approaches in molecular biology, mutagenesis, and fluorescence imaging, we will carry out the scientific investigation and elucidate the functional role of alpha-PIX in stiffness-dependent Cdc42-PAK activation. We aim to reveal the mechano-biological mechanism of how stiffness of the extracellular substrate regulates the plasticity and podosome assembly of vascular smooth muscle cells. Our finding will provide a better understanding of cell biological mechanisms in pathogenic vascular remodeling and diverse vascular diseases. Pharmaceutical and biotech industries will be potentially interested in applying our findings to develop new compounds and technologies. 細胞足體主要由肌動蛋白組成，為細胞與胞外基質的黏附點，負責調控細胞遷徙與降解胞外基質。胞外基質的物理特性，可影響細胞足體的形成及穩定性，例如胞外基質硬度變化，可導致動脈粥樣硬化與癌瘤轉移等相關疾病。本團隊將利用A7r5血管平滑肌細胞，研究細胞足體與胞外基質硬度的關係，解析Rho GTPase與肌動蛋白解聚因子cofilin之交互作用，以生物力學角度，為胞外基質硬度變化所導致的疾病，探討其調控機制。

17122019.label: Realisation of objectives
17122019.value: Summary of the investigation: Atherosclerosis is a condition of narrowing arteries caused by gradual plaque buildup. Major risk factors of atherosclerosis include ageing-associated changes in arterial wall stiffness and hypertension. The phenotypic switching, proliferation, and apoptosis of vascular smooth muscle cell result in the intimal thickening and mark the first stage of atherosclerosis. However, the molecular mechanisms of how vascular stiffness and blood pressure changes promote the phenotypic switch of vascular smooth muscle cell remain largely unknown. In this investigation, we combine the proteomic and microscopy approach and find that the combination of cyclic hypertensive pressure stimulation and matrix compliance in extracellular microenvironment is necessary to give rise to a full phenotypic switch of vascular smooth muscle cell, including significant changes in atherosclerosis-associated protein expression, cytoskeletal organisation, and the formation of podosome. The underlying principle of mechanosensitive response is orchestrated by cofilin, a cytoskeletal protein that regulates actin nucleation. The dephosphorylation status, rather than the expression, is known to be the key factor to regulate cofilin activities. Here, we identify the mechano-biological pathways that modulate cofilin phosphorylation in vascular smooth muscle cells. Specifically, pressure stimuli initiate the activation of calcium-dependent phosphatase slingshot that dephosphorylates cofilin, while the reduction of substratum stiffness suppresses the signal cascade of RhoA-ROCK2-LIMK2 and restrains cofilin phosphorylation. Collectively, higher pressure and softer substratum cause the decrease of cofilin phosphorylation, promote actin nucleation, and accelerate in the oscillatory nature of podosome. The formation of fast-oscillatory podosome, the signature event of the phenotypic switching of vascular smooth muscle cells, elevates the matrix degradation and vascular microenvironment disorganisation, and results in the early progression of atherosclerosis. This work also demonstrates a successful international collaboration (University of Hong Kong and Queen Mary University of London) and has been published in a peer-reviewed journal^. ^ Pamela Swiatlowska‡, Brian Sit‡, Zhen Feng‡, Emilie Marhuenda, Ioannis Xanthis, Simona Zingaro, Matthew Ward, Xinmiao Zhou, Qingzhong Xiao, Cathy Shanahan, Gareth E Jones, Cheng-han Yu*, and Thomas Iskratsch*. “Pressure and stiffness sensing together regulate vascular smooth muscle cell phenotype switching”. Science Advances 2022, 8, eabm3471. ‡first authors; *corresponding authors [Objective 1] Define the matrix stiffness-dependent regulation of Rho GTPase and cofilin in vSMC Percentage of completion: 100%. We examine the Rho GTPase activity and find that the activity of RhoA, rather than that of Cdc42, changes when A7r5 cells are placed on various stiffness-defined substrates. Specifically, RhoA-GTP levels are higher when A7r5 cells adhere on the stiff substrate (fibronectin-coated glass), decrease on 130kPa fibronectin-coated PDMS, and further drop on 10kPa fibronectin-coated PDMS. We also performe the FRET measurement of RhoA activity and confirmed the spatiotemporal regulation of RhoA at the A7r5 podosome. Likewise, the phosphorylation level of cofilin also gradually declines as the substrate stiffness decreases. Phosphorylated cofilin become weakly associated to the podosome. At the same time, the podosome assembly becomes persist and less dynamic. It appears that RhoA-GTP levels is positively correlated to cofilin phosphorylation and podosome persistency. Therefore, we have achieved the investigation of Objective 1. [Objective 2] Investigate the role of PAK and ROCK in cofilin regulation and podosome assembly. Percentage of completion: 100%. We firstly examine the impact of substrate stiffness on the activation of LIMK, PAK and ROCK. It is known that LIMK is the key kinase to phosphorylate cofilin. We find that phosphorylation levels of LIMK also declines as the substrate stiffness decreases. By the shRNA knockdown approach, we identify LIMK2, rather than LIMK1, is responsible for cofilin phosphorylation in A7r5 cells. Next, while the activation of LIMK can be regulated by either PAK or ROCK, we find that the activities of group I and II PAK remain steady and are independent of substrate stiffness. Knockdown of ROCK2, on the other hand, effectively blocks the cofilin phosphorylation. Similar to the effect of soft matrix microenvironment, each knockdown of ROCK2 and LIMK2 resulted in shorter podosome lifetime in A7r5 cells. We confirm the signalling axis of ROCK2-LIMK2 to phosphorylate cofilin and prevent the F-actin turnover in the podosome. Therefore, we have achieved the investigation of Objective 2. [Objective 3] Determine the molecular mechanism of Rho GTPase activation by matrix stiffness. Percentage of completion: 100%. We investigate calcium-dependent feedback mechanism to modulate RhoA-mediated cofilin phosphorylation. Specifically, calcium-dependent phosphatases, such as slingshot, can dephosphorylate cofilin and accelerate the dynamics of podosome assembly. Indeed, we find that mechanical stimuli, such as cyclic pressure, can initiate the slingshot activation that dephosphorylates cofilin, while the reduction of substratum stiffness suppresses the signal cascade of RhoA-ROCK2-LIMK2 and down-regulate cofilin phosphorylation. Collectively, higher pressure and softer substratum cause the decrease of cofilin phosphorylation, promote actin nucleation, and accelerate in the oscillatory nature of podosome. Therefore, we have achieved the investigation of Objective 3.

17122019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122019.value: Atherosclerosis is an emerging cardiovascular disease, and the phenotypic switching of vascular smooth muscle cell, from contractile to migratory, is one of the signature events in the early phase of atherosclerosis. While mechanical stimuli, such as arterial stiffness and blood pressure, have been strongly implicated in atherosclerosis, the molecular mechanism remains unclear. Here we demonstrate that mechanical stimuli of substrate stiffness and cyclic pressure collectively control the activity of cofilin by modulating RhoA-GTP and intracellular calcium levels. Activations of cofilin, the key actin nucleator and severing factor, trigger the dynamical assembly of podosome and promotes the migration of vascular smooth muscle cell. Mechanistically, we identify the substrate stiffness dependent pathway of RhoA-ROCK2-LIMK2 that regulating the level of phosphorylated cofilin. Stiff substrates result in more phosphorylated cofilin and impede the dynamical F-actin turnover of the podosome. In addition, the microenvironment with higher cyclic pressure causes the elevation of intracellular calcium levels and activates calcium-dependent phosphatase slingshot that dephosphorylates cofilin. Collectively, low substrate stiffness and high cyclic pressure act together to facilitate cofilin dephosphorylation, accelerate the dynamics of podosome assembly, and promote the migration of vascular smooth muscle cells. These results have been published in Science Advances in 2022 (PMID 35427166), and here are the major findings. 1) The phenotypic switch of VSMC is regulated through hemodynamic pressure and matrix stiffness 2) Vascular smooth muscle podosomes are mechanosensitive 3) Podosomal actin turnover in VSMC is controlled by substrate stiffness 4) Podosomal cofilin is regulated through RhoA, ROCK2, and LIMK2 in a stiffness-dependent manner 5) Pressure and PDBu stimulate cofilin dephosphorylation and podosome formation through calcium ion and slingshot

17122019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122019.value: Our current work suggests an upstream mechano-dependent pathway which leads to the activation of RhoA and point toward a role for a negative regulator of RhoA activity in the podosome adhesion ring. ARAP3, a dual GTPase-activating protein (GAP) for RhoA and Arf, is dynamically recruited to the podosome in phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase dependent manner. Our quantitative proteomics analyses find that ARAP3 is strongly up-regulated after pressure stimulation, especially on soft surfaces, consistent with a higher dynamicity of podosomes. Other BAR domain containing RhoA GAPs, such as srGAP1, RICH1, and GMIP, may sense the change of membrane curvature during the podosome formation and regulate local RhoA activity. However, future experiments are needed to untangle the stiffness-dependent regulation of RhoA activation at the adhesion ring. In addition, the current study primarily used two-dimensional cell culture models, which enabled the detailed analysis of VSMC mechanosensing pathways. However, arteries are three-dimensional structures and cells in the arterial wall are surrounded by extracellular matrix and exposed to forces in all directions. Thus, future work will be needed to further disseminate the regulation of VSMC mechanosensing in three-dimensional models.

17122019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122019.value: Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of vascular disease worldwide. Ageing-associated changes in arterial wall stiffness and high blood pressure are the common risk factors of atherosclerosis. Here, we report that cyclic hypertensive pressure stimulation and matrix compliance in extracellular microenvironment collectively trigger the migratory transition of vascular smooth muscle cell, including atherosclerosis-associated protein expression and the cofilin-dependent podosome formation. Cofilin is a cytoskeletal protein that controls the nucleation and severing of actin filament. We find that higher pressure and softer substratum regulate cofilin dephosphorylation in a RhoA and calcium dependent manner and jointly enhance actin nucleation. As a result, higher levels of dephosphorylated cofilin accelerate the oscillatory nature of podosome and promote the migration of vascular smooth muscle cell. In summary, our findings highlight the role of extracellular microenvironment and underlying pressure and rigidity sensing mechanisms involved in atherosclerosis progression. While regular exercise and balanced diet can effectively prevent or slow the progression of atherosclerosis, cofilin can be a potential target for mitigating atherosclerosis at early phase, paving the way for new therapeutic opportunities.

Sci Adv. 2021;7(20):eabg2099. doi: 10.1126/sciadv.abg2099) Briefly, we identified that CUL3-KBTBD7 regulates the abundance of Vangl2 through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Recruitment of KBTBD7 to Vangl2 in the ER results in Vangl2 poly-ubiquitination and endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD). Vangl2 was mainly modified by K48-linked poly-ubiquitination chains at K300/306 residues. 17122119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122119.value: In this project, by proteomic and biochemical analysis, we have identified that a Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligase complex, CUL3-KBTBD7, regulates Vangl2 stability through the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Vangl2 directly bound p97/VCP via a highly conserved VCP-interacting motif (VIM). This interaction governed the access of KBTBD7 to Vangl2, resulting in Vangl2 poly-ubiquitination and endoplasmic-reticulum-associated degradation (ERAD). We further found that Wnt5a/CK1-induced phosphorylation of Vangl2 prevented Vangl2 ubiquitination by promoting its transport from the ER to the plasma membrane, and thereby Vangl2 escaped ERAD, highlighting the importance of Wnt signaling and ERAD in the quality and activity control of PCP proteins. In zebrafish, expression of KBTBD7 also degraded Vangl2, leading to an inhibition of convergent extension (CE) movements, a classical PCP phenotype, while knockdown of KBTBD7 increased Vangl2 protein level. Elevated Vangl2 expression has been previously found to be associated with poor patient outcomes in breast cancer. We further showed that KBTBD7 overexpression inhibited mammary tumor growth and metastasis by promoting Vangl2 degradation and the expression level of KBTBD7 is associated with the prognosis of breast cancer patients, indicating a tumor suppressive role of KBTBD7. Our findings reveal a new regulatory mechanism of Wnt/PCP signaling through the ubiquitin-mediated ERAD pathway that is important in both development and tumor suppression.

17122119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122119.value: In our studies of KBTBD7-mediated Vangl2 ubiquitination, we unexpectedly found that p97/VCP-mediated ERAD pathway is critical in regulating the abundance of Vangl2 proteins. Although this was not proposed in our original proposal, we further delineated the detailed underlying molecular mechanism. We found that p97/VCP is directly associated with Vangl2 via a highly conserved motif and recruits the E3 ligase KBTBD7 via its UBA-UBX adaptors to promote Vangl2 ubiquitination and ERAD. This represents a potential new protein quality control (PQC) mechanism through the p97/VCP-substrate direct interaction in the process of ERAD. As ERAD is a principal PQC mechanism that detects and eliminates misfolded/unfolded proteins in the ER and a large amount of newly synthesized wild type Vangl2 is degraded by ERAD, it is very likely that the PQC of Vangl2 occurs in the ER before they can reach the cell surface to function as key PCP signaling molecules. Based on our novel findings in this project and other preliminary data, we propose to further study this potential new PQC mechanism - how it monitors Vangl2 in the ER to ensure the correct folding and assembly and whether it also regulates other ERAD substrates. These will provide new molecular insights into the regulatory mechanism of PCP signaling and advance our basic knowledge of PQC.

17122119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122119.value: PCP signaling plays critical roles in cellular, developmental, and physiological processes and its dysregulation causes a growing list of human diseases such as spina bifida, skeletal disorders, neurological disorders, and various cancers. Here, our studies identified a negative regulatory mechanism of PCP signaling through targeting Vangl2 by E3 ubiquitin ligase KBTBD7 and showed that KBTBD7 can inhibit mammary tumor growth and metastasis. As aberrant activation of PCP signaling is strongly implicated in various cancers, our findings provide new strategies for therapeutic intervention of Vangl2-associated cancers, such as breast cancer and rhabdomyosarcoma.

17122519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122519.value: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is one of the most common aggressive cancers in Southeast Asia and Southern China. The mechanism underlying the development and progression of NPC remains largely unknown. Interleukin (IL)-17 is a critical inflammatory cytokine mainly secreted from T cells in tumor microenvironment. The roles of IL-17 and IL-17-producing T cells on tumor development and progression are still controversial. Both pro-tumor and anti-tumor activities of IL-17 have been reported in different studies. It is believed that the conflicting results of IL-17 on tumor development and progression may rely on its cellular source, cancer cause, type and location. IL-17-producing αβ-T cells have been identified in the tumor tissue of NPC patients. However, no data are available for IL-17-producing γδ-T cells in NPC patients although γδ-T cells are very highly enriched in NPC tumor tissues. Little is known about the roles of IL-17 and IL-17-producing γδ-T cells on NPC development and progression. Exosomes are endosome-originated small extracellular membrane vesicles that carry nucleic acids, lipids and proteins from originating cells. Tumor-derived exosomes can transfer cancer exosomal contents to mediate intercellular communication and regulate tumor immunity. However, it is unclear whether NPC-derived exosomes can affect the differentiation of IL-17-producing T cells. In our preliminary study, we found that IL-17-producing γδ-T cells were enriched in tumor tissues from undifferentiated NPC patients. NPC-derived exosomes could induce the production of IL-17-polarizing cytokines from dendritic cells and polarize naïve γδ-T cells to differentiate into IL-17-producing γδ-T cells. More importantly, compared with those from well-differentiated NPC cells, exosomes derived from undifferentiated NPC cells were more potent to induce the productions of IL-17-polarizing cytokines from dendritic cells and IL-17 from γδ-T cells. Using blocking assays, we also demonstrated that IL-17 secreted from γδ-T17 cells could promote the migration of NPC tumor cells. Here, we will test our hypothesis that NPC-derived exosomes can polarize naïve γδ-T cells to differentiate into IL-17-producing γδ-T cells, which in turn affect NPC development and progression. Furthermore, we will explore the mechanisms underlying the induction of IL-17-producing γδ-T cells by NPC-derived exosomes. This study will improve our understanding of tumor-derived exosomes-mediated immunoregulation and provide potential novel bio-markers and therapeutic targets for NPC. 鼻咽癌是東南亞和中國南方最常見的侵襲性腫瘤之壹。迄今為止，鼻咽癌進展的潛在機制很大程度上未闡明。白細胞介素(IL)-17是壹種關鍵的炎性細胞因子，在腫瘤微環境中主要由T細胞分泌。IL-17和產生IL-17的T細胞在腫瘤進展起到的作用仍存在爭議。IL-17的促腫瘤和抗腫瘤活性在不同的研究中皆有報告。據信，IL-17在腫瘤進展中的矛盾結果可能依賴於其細胞來源，以及腫瘤發生的原因、類型和位置。在鼻咽癌患者的腫瘤組織中已發現了產生IL-17的αβ-T細胞。然而，雖然γδ-T細胞在鼻咽癌組織中非常富集，但產生IL-17的γδ-T (γδ-T-17) 細胞在鼻咽癌中的存在情況及其在鼻咽癌進展中的作用知之甚少。外泌體是核內體起源的小細胞外囊泡，它能攜帶母細胞的核酸、脂質和蛋白質，並介導細胞間通訊。腫瘤來源的外泌體可以轉移腫瘤細胞的內容物，以介導細胞間通訊並調節腫瘤免疫。然而，尚不清楚鼻咽癌外泌體是否會影響產IL-17 的T細胞的分化。在初步研究中，我們發現γδ-T-17細胞富集在未分化型鼻咽癌患者的腫瘤組織中。鼻咽癌外泌體可以誘導樹突狀細胞分泌更多的IL-17極化細胞因子，並使幼稚型γδ-T細胞分化成γδ-T-17細胞。更重要的是，與分化良好的鼻咽癌細胞相比，未分化型鼻咽癌細胞的外泌體能更有效地誘導樹突細胞產生IL-17極化細胞因子，並使γδ-T細胞產生更多的IL-17。通過阻斷實驗，我們還證明了γδ-T-17細胞分泌的IL-17可以促進鼻咽癌腫瘤細胞的遷移。在這裏，我們將檢驗這個假設，即鼻咽癌外泌體可以誘導幼稚型γδ-T細胞分化成γδ-T-17細胞，進而影響鼻咽癌的進展。此外，我們將探索由鼻咽癌外泌體誘導出γδ-T-17細胞的機制。這項研究將提高我們對腫瘤外泌體介導的免疫調節的理解，並為鼻咽癌提供潛在的新型生物標誌物和治療靶點。

17122519.label: Realisation of objectives
17122519.value: Objective 1. By immunofluorescent staining using anti-human TCR γ/δ and anti-human IL-17 antibodies, we found that IL-17-producing γδ-T cells were enriched in the tumor tissues from NPC patients. Then, we investigated whether NPC-Exosomes could promote antigen-presenting cells to produce IL-17- polarizing cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-23), which are indispensable for inducing IL-17-producing cells. Exosomes derived from immortalized normal nasopharyngeal epithelial cells (NP69) or NPC cells (NPC43-EBV, C666-1) were used to treat dendritic cells (DCs) for 24 h. The data revealed that NPC-derived exosomes (NPC43-Exosomes, C666-1-Exosomes), but not NP69-exosome, could significantly promote DCs to produce IL-17-polarizing cytokines, including IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-23. Next, we purified γδ-T cells from human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and cocultured them with autologous DCs, in the presence of PBS, NP69-exosomes, NPC43-exosomes or C666-1-exosomes. 7 days later, the result of flow cytometry analysis revealed that more IL-17-producing γδ-T cells were induced by NPC-exosomes than NP69-exosomes. Further analysis identified that NPC-exosomes could induce IL-17 from both Vδ1 and Vδ2-T cell subsets, which consist of the majority of human γδ-T cells. Taken together, these data suggest that NPC-derived exosomes can induce IL-17-producing γδ-T cells. Objective 2. In addition to induce IL-17-polarizing cytokines from DCs, NPC-exosomes also downregulated the expression of the interleukin 2 (IL-2) receptor alpha chain (CD25) on γδ-T cells when compared with NP-exosomes or PBS treatment. As IL-2 pathway plays an critical role in T cell differentiation, we further determined its effect on the induction of IL-17-producing γδ-T cells. Purified γδ-T cells were cultured in the supernatant of NPC-exosomes-pretreated DCs, then different concentration of human recombinant IL-2 (rIL-2) or neutralizing anti-rIL-2 antibody was added into the culture system. Data showed that rIL-2 inhibited the induction of IL-17-producing γδ-T cells in a dose-dependent manner, while the blockage of rIL-2 in the cultured system enhanced the induction. In addition, the induction of IL-17-producing γδ-T cells was significantly enhanced in the presence of neutralizing anti-CD25 antibody. These data suggest NPC-exosomes can downregulate the expression of CD25 on γδ-T cells and inhibit IL-2 pathway to induce IL-17-producing γδ-T cells. Considering that exosomes carry abundant microRNAs (miRNAs) that regulate cell behaviors, including immune cell differentiation, we then investigated whether the exosomal miRNAs were involved in the induction of IL-17-producing γδ-T cells by NPC-exosomes. Next-generation sequencing was used to compared the small RNA profile of C666-1-exosomes with NP69-exosomes. The sequencing results found abundant miR-15a in C666-1-exosomes, but not in NP69-exosomes. Validation experiments by qPCR also confirmed that miR-15a was enriched in NPC-exosomes. As miRNA target prediction database (miRWalk 2.0) indicated that miR-15a may bind to CD25 gene and inhibit its expression, we then used miR-15a mimics or negative control (NC) mimics to treat γδ-T cells and evaluated their effects on CD25 expression of γδ-T cells. Interestingly, miR-15a significantly downregulated CD25 expression on γδ-T cells, but NC mimics not. Therefore, the findings suggest that the exosomal miR-15a of NPC-exosomes can inhibit IL-2 signaling pathway via CD25 downregulation to promote IL-17-producing γδ-T cells induction. Objective 3. As the effects of IL-17 on tumor development and progression may vary according to cellular source, cancer cause, type and location, we further evaluated the effects of γδ-T cells-derived IL-17 on the cell behaviors, including proliferation, migration and invasion of NPC tumor cells. NPC-exosomes was used to induced IL-17-producing γδ-T cells as described above, then the cells were collected, washed with PBS and incubated in serum-free medium. 48 h later, the supernatant derived from IL-17-producing γδ-T cells were harvested and subjected to further experiments. To determine cell migration, a wound healing assay was used. NPC cells were pretreated with culture medium, γδ-T17-derived supernatants, γδT17-derived supernatant plus anti-IL-17 neutralizing mAb, or γδT-17-derived supernatant plus isotype control mAb. After 3 days treatment, the NPC cells were then scraped by a sterile micropipette tip to generate a scratching wound and washed by PBS to eliminate non-adherent cells. Cell migration into the wounds were imaged at 0 h and 18 h by a phase contrast microscope. The data revealed that γδ-T17-derived supernatants significantly increased the cell migration of NPC cells compared with culture medium, while neutralizing IL-17 in the γδ-T17-derived supernatants reversed this effect. These findings suggest that γδ-T cells-derived IL-17 can promote NPC cell migration. We further found that IL-6 from NPC-Exosomes-treated macrophages could promote the colony formation, migration and invasion of NPC cells. Therefore, our results suggest that NPC exosomes-induced IL-17 and IL-6 could promoted the malignant behaviors of NPC cells. Considering IL-17 is a critical cytokine initiating chronic inflammation that can affect the therapeutic responses of cancer cells, we further determined the effects of NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells on NPC radiotherapy. Firstly, robust expression of the IL-17 receptor was found on NPC cells, providing the molecular basis to respond to NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells. Next, recombinant IL-17 inhibited the radiation-induced apoptosis of NPC cells in a dose-dependent manner. More importantly, the supernatant from NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells significantly reduced the radiation-induced apoptosis of NPC cells. In contrast, blockage of IL-17 in the supernatant restored radiosensitivity. Further experiments found that IL-17 secreted from γδT-17 cells increased the expression of an anti-apoptotic protein BCL-2, which can promote radioresistance of cancer cells. These data indicate that NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells can secrete IL-17 to promote NPC radioresistance both in vitro. Objective 4. Using Rag2−/−γc−/− immunodeficient mice, we established NPC tumor-bearing Rag2−/−γc−/− mice. NPC tumor-bearing Rag2−/−γc−/− mice were irradiated at 0 or 4 Gy and injected intraperitoneally with complete medium or the supernatant of NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells. Three weeks later, tumors were excised and photographed. We found that treatment with supernatant from NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells increased the radioresistance of NPC tumors. However, blockage of IL-17 in the supernatant recovered the radiosensitivity of NPC tumors. Taken together, these data indicate that NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells can secrete IL-17 to promote NPC radioresistance in vivo.

17122519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122519.value: Our study identifies we revealed a novel cell-cell communication pathway among NPC and γδ-T cells. Abundant miR-15a in NPC-Exos can promote γδT-17 cell induction and confer radioresistance to tumor cells. This novel route not only helps better understand the immunoregulatory mechanism of NPC but also provides implications for developing new approaches to overcome radioresistance in NPC patients, i.e. targeting tumor-exosomal miR-15a as a potential therapeutic strategy to improve radiotherapy against NPC.

17122519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122519.value: γδT-17 are crucial cellular sources of IL-17 in the tumor microenvironment and influence tumorigenesis or therapeutic outcomes in tumors. However, the existences and functions of γδT-17 cells in NPC are still unclear. Although IL-17 can affect tumor cell proliferation and migration, it remains unknown about the impacts of γδT-17 cells on radiotherapy, which is the first-line therapy for NPC patients. In this study, we identified abundant γδT-17 cells in NPC tissues. Exosomes derived from NPC cells (NPC-Exos) polarized γδ-T cells to differentiate into γδT-17 cells. The NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells promoted NPC radioresistance both in vitro and in vivo. Blockage of the IL-17 secreted from NPC-Exos-induced γδT-17 cells recovered the radiosensitivity of NPC cells and increased radiation-induced cell death. Interestingly, the mechanistic study found that NPC-Exos not only upregulated the secretion of IL-17-driving cytokines IL-1β, IL-6 and IL-23 from DCs, but also inhibited CD25/IL-2 signaling on γδ-T cells, thus promoting γδT-17 cell differentiation. The inhibition of CD25/IL-2 signaling in γδ-T cells was mediated by NPC exosomal miR-15a. In addition, miR-15a inhibitor could suppress the induction of γδT-17 cells by NPC-Exos. Our study demonstrates a novel immunoregulatory effect of NPC-Exos and provides implications to overcome NPC radioresistance.

17122819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17122819.value: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic debilitating autoimmune disease, characterized by loss of tolerance to self-antigens and persistent systemic inflammation. Patients with SLE exhibit a gene expression signature characterized by type-I interferon (IFN-I)-response gene transcripts in their blood and tissues. IFN activity corresponds to disease activity, and many immunopathological features of SLE are a consequence of persistent immunodysregulation driven by IFN-I, particularly IFN-alpha. Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDC) and IFN-I are key pathogenic mediators of SLE. The mechanisms of pDC dysregulation in SLE are not fully understood. Targeting IFN-I pathway is increasingly recognized as a promising treatment approach. However, therapeutic strategies in downregulating pDC activity have not been thoroughly investigated in SLE. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) are fibroblastoid prognenitor cells which are isolated from bone marrow (BM), adipose tissue or umbilical cord. They have low immunogenicity, and are able to suppress various immune effector cell functions and promote immune regulation. Tumor necrosis factor-inducible gene-6 (TSG-6) has been identified to be a biomarker that predicts efficacy of human MSCs in modulating inflammation. Our previous work showed that TSG-6 downregulates IFN-alpha and TNF-alpha expression by suppressing interferon regulatory factor 7 (IRF7) in human pDC. The role of MSC in suppressing pDC functions has not been investigated previously. We hypothesize that MSC exert an immunosuppressive effect on TLR7 or TLR9-activated pDC in a TSG-6 dependent manner. Using hTERT-MSC, an immortalized human BM-derived MSC cell line and GEN2.2, a human pDC cell line, we first investigate the effect of MSC on TLR7 and TLR9 signaling pathway upon activation by their respective agonists CpG-A and R837. Next, we investigate whether downregulation of TLR7/TLR9-mediated cytokine response is dependent on TSG-6 by co-culturing TLR7 or TLR9-activated GEN2.2 with TSG-6-knockdown-hTERT-MSC, or primary human BM-MSC with varied basal TSG-6 expression. To explore the potentials of MSC as disease-modifying therapy for lupus nephritis, we will treat NZB/NZW F1 mice, a well-established lupus model with IFN-I hyperactivation, with TSG-6, hTERT-MSC or TSG-6 knockdown hTERT-MSC. pDC numbers and immunophenotype will be evaluated, and therapeutic efficacy will be determined by clinical and histological scoring for lupus nephritis. Finally, TSG-6 knockout mice will be treated with repeated injection of apoptotic cells to induce lupus-like autoimmunity, and we will find out if rescue of disease phenotype is possible with TSG-6 or MSC administration. This study will provide novel insights in MSC biology and the therapeutic role of MSC in treating autoimmune disorders with IFN-I signature.

17122819.label: Realisation of objectives
17122819.value: Objective 1: 1.1 MSC TSG-6 expression correlates with its immunosuppressive ability in reducing IFN-α and IL-1β expression of TLR9 activated pDC We screened for TSG-6 expression amongst various MSC candidates (htMSC, human bone marrow MSC (BM-MSC) obtained from adolescent and adult donors) and found that htMSC expressed the highest amount of TSG-6 compared to lowest expressing BM-MSC, and was most effective in suppressing IFN-α and IL-1β expression of CpG-A stimulated human pDC. Thus, htMSC was chosen as an ideal candidate for subsequent testing of immunosuppressive function in pDC type-I IFN dependent pathway. 1.2 The CD44 receptor-mediated immunosuppressive effect of MSCs on pDCs is dependent on TSG-6, which functions by reducing IRF7 expression and inhibiting NFκB activity Previously, we have shown that TSG-6 exerts an immunosuppressive effect on activated pDC via CD44, by reducing IRF7 phosphorylation activity (Kui, Chan, and Lee 2017). Here, we investigated if the immunosuppressive action of htMSC on TLR9 activated pDC is via the same pathway. We found that htMSC exert a pronounced immuno-suppressive effect on TLR9 stimulated pDC, with significantly suppressed IFN-α and TNF-α mRNA expression. When TSG-6 gene was knocked-down in htMSC, and co-cultured with CpG-A stimulated pDC, we saw a reduction in the immuno-suppressive activity of htMSC, in IFN-α and TNF-α mRNA expression. This suggests that TSG-6 expression in MSC is key in modulating TLR9 stimulated pDC inflammation. In TLR9 pathway, type-I IFN expression is regulated by the transcription factor IRF7, and pro-inflammatory cytokines production is mediated via the NFκB pathway. We found that htMSC significantly suppressed TLR9 stimulated pDC total IRF7 from the activated state of mean value +/- SEM 9.295 to 3.3825 (***P<0.001), moreover, phospho-IRF7 was also down-regulated from mean value +/- SEM of 51.3 to 35.25 (*P<0.05), returning both total IRF7 and phospho-IRF7 back to quiesence. This shows that MSC can regulate type-I interferon expression in pDC TLR9 mediated pathway by modulating the key transcription factor IRF7. Similarly, to evaluate whether NF-kB pathway in activated pDC was affected, we co-cultured htMSC with CpG-A stimulated pDC for 1 hour, and then compared by western-blot, the expression of key proteins involved in the NF-kB pathway: phospho-IKKβα, phospho-p65, IKKα and IKβα, in the cytoplasmic and nuclear extract of pDC. Expression of phospho-p65 and IKβα was increased in the nuclear extract of TLR9 stimulated pDC co-cultured with htMSC, suggesting htMSC regulated pro-inflammatory cytokine expression via blocking NFκB pathway. Objective 2 Attenuated type-I IFN expression, increased tolerogenic CCR+ expression in splenic pDC, and altered thymic T-cells profile of mice treated with MSC and its secretome We investigated whether MSCs and its secretome could alter the phenotype of splenic pDC due to the importance of pDC in the pathogenesis of SLE. BM-MSC, htMSC, htMSC-EV, htMSC-derived extracellular vesicles (EV) or murine TSG-6 treatment significantly suppressed intracellular IFN-α expression in splenic pDC of mice compared with control group (Fig 4A and B). We also saw a significant increase of tolerogenic CCR9+ expression in splenic pDC of mice treated with BM-MSC, htMSC, htMSC-EV and htMSC-derived conditioned medium (CM). Thymic T-cells profile was also significantly altered. htMSC, BMMSC03, htMSC-EV, htMSC-CM and mTSG-6 treatment significantly reduced CD3+ CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells and CD25+ CD4+ FoxP3+ Tregs. However, no significant change was observed in B220+ CD19+ thymic B-cells, except for the mice treated with BMMSC03, which has significantly increased thymic B-cells. Objective 3 3.1 htMSC and its secretomes improved lupus mice survival and phenotype At week-16 of age, NZB/W F1 female lupus mice were injected via tail-vein twice (week 16 and week 18) with PBS, htMSC (0.1 million cells), htMSC-EV (1x1010 particles) or htMSC-CM (from 0.1 million cells). Their weight is monitored and serum collected once fortnightly. At week 32, the mice were sacrificed, and kidney harvested for histology. 100% of PBS treated mice died at week 29, and in contrast, all mice treated with htMSC and its secretomes have increased survival past week 30 (60%-80% survival compared to PBS group). Moreover, PBS treated mice started to lose a significant amount of weight (P<0.05) at week 17 when compared to htMSC treated mice, and continued to deteriorate at week 23, losing more than 20% of initial body weight (****P<0.0001 compared to htMSC, htMSC-EV and htMSC-CM groups). Mice treated with htMSC and its secretome maintained a steadily bodyweight gain through week 25. Furthermore, we also saw an improved phenotype in the htMSC, htMSC-EV and htMSC-CM treated NZB/W F1 mice, in terms of significantly reduced serum ds-DNA ab levels (significantly reduced **p<0.01 from week 30 to week 32 compared to PBS group), Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) level (htMSC **p<0.01, htMSC-EV ***P<0.001, htMSC-CM **P<0.01 compared to PBS group) and Creatine level (htMSC ***p<0.001, htMSC-EV ***P<0.001, htMSC-CM *P<0.05 compared to PBS group) at week 32. These data demonstrated that htMSC and its secretome could effectively attenuate SLE disease progression in female NZB/WF1 mice and with survival. 3.2 htMSC, htMSC-EV and htMSC-CM treatment attenuated nephropathy in NZB/WF1 mice Survival of NZB/WF1 lupus mice is dependent on the severity of renal pathology, thus we analysed kidney biopsy harvested from mice of various treatment groups, euthanized at week 32. Frozen sections of kidneys from all 4 groups were stained with fluorescein-conjugated anti-mouse IgG or C3 antibody. A random selection of images from 7 high-power fields was taken from three independent cohorts (n=5 -10 per group) and quantified as corrected total cell fluorescence (CTCF) = Integrated Density – (Area of Selected Cell x Mean Fluorescence of Background readings), using ImageJ software. The results showed a significant reduction of IgG and C3 deposit in glomeruli of mice treated with htMSC, htMSC-EV or htMSC-CM compared to PBS group. Similarly, with H&E staining of kidney sections, we found that the htMSC, htMSC-EV and htMSC-CM treated groups had significantly improved renal pathology score as compared to PBS control mice. These data showed that htMSC and its secretomes are also effective in attenuating nephropathy in NZB/W F1 mice.

17122819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17122819.value: TSG-6, a biomarker for selecting anti-inflammatory human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs), is a promising therapeutic strategy for type-I interferon mediated autoinflammatory diseases like lupus. Previously, we have characterized the mechanistic role of TSG-6 in regulating type-I interferon and proinflammatory cytokines in TLR9 and TLR7 activated human plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs), mimicking lupus pathogenesis. In this study, htMSC was selected based on its high TSG-6 expression, and its immunosuppressive effects on pDCs, downregulating IFN-α and TNF-α via CD44 and reducing IRF7 activation. Culture conditions were optimized to enhance MSC immunosuppressive potential, and htMSC secretomes (conditioned-medium and extracellular vesicles) were crucial in downregulating IFN-α, TNF-α, and suppressing T-cell proliferation. In NZB/W F1 lupus mice, treatment with htMSC and secretomes improved survival, maintained bodyweight, reduced ds-DNA, blood urea nitrogen, and creatinine levels, and ameliorated renal pathology with decreased C3 and IgG deposition. These findings highlight TSG-6 significance as a marker for immunosuppressive MSCs and shed light on the mechanism by which MSCs and their secretome regulate activated pDCs during lupus progression, providing potential for improving lupus management.

17122819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17122819.value: MSC transplants have been explored by different groups in clinical trials, showing the effectiveness in improving proteinuria and amelioration of lupus disease outcome, by suppressing inflammation by upregulation of tolerogenic DCs. However, MSC transplant do come with several risks, associated with the development of malignancy due to the phenotypical difference of MSC source and the sensitive nature of MSC to the microenvironment; and rejection due to development of antibody against allogeneic MSC. It is therefore important to optimize the efficacy of MSC therapy of the treatment of lupus. Thus, our study demonstrated selection of TSG-6 expressing MSC, and conditioning of cells in serum-deprived medium (CPDF) would maintain the immunosuppressive effect of the cells. Moreover, treating NZB/WF1 mice with htMSC secretome (htMSC-EV, htMSC-CM or TSG-6) alone would be as, or more effective as giving htMSC cellular therapy. Moving forward, MSC secretome therapeutics could potentially overcome problems associated with cellular therapy. A limitation to the study is that we could not increase the dose of htMSC therapy to 1x106 cells as the mice did not survive the dose (data not shown). Therefore, as a comparative study we used htMSC-EV, and htMSC-CM harvested from 1x106 htMSC throughout the experiment. We predict that htMSC-EV and htMSC-CM at a higher dose will have a better therapeutic effect on mice, and there should not be any side effects associated with the treatment. Another area of study would be to combine existing SLE treatment of mycophenolate mofetil with MSC secretome, where MSC secretome could be used as a maintenance strategy for SLE patient.

17122819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17122819.value: In our study, we looked at a specific gene called TSG-6, that is highly expressed in some human stem cells, and use it to select for stem cells with therapeutic potential in treating SLE. We found that these stem cells that have high levels of TSG-6 can help suppress the immune system and reduce inflammation in cells that contribute to lupus. We also discovered that the substances secreted by these stem cells, known as secretomes, can also have similar effects. To test these findings, we conducted experiments using mice with lupus-like symptoms. We treated them with the stem cells and their secretomes and found that they had improved survival rates, no weight loss due to SLE, and showed reduced kidney damage. Impact: These results suggest that TSG-6 is a good biomarker for selecting SLE therapeutic stem cell, and that these cells and its secretomes have potential used as therapy, leading to new ways of managing and treating lupus.

17123319.label: Project Objectives
17123319.value: Objective 1: To investigate the role of CK2 in ZIKV infection. Extending from our identification of CK2 as the most activated kinase in ZIKV-infected glial cells which affects virus replication, we will detailedly investigate its role in ZIKV infection in Objective 1. -Objective 1.1: To understand the biology of CK2 upon ZIKV infection: how the expression/activation of CK2 is modulated by ZIKV, cellular distribution of CK2 in ZIKV-infected cells, and the effect of CK2 overexpression on ZIKV replication. -Objective 1.2: To characterize the function of CK2 in ZIKV infection: CK2’s effects on multiple ZIKV strains in different cell types including human neural progenitor cells. -Objective 1.3: To dissect the mechanism of how CK2 affects ZIKV replication: the step(s) of the ZIKV replication cycle CK2 is involved in. Objective 2: To evaluate the effects of CK2 inhibitors as novel treatment options for ZIKV infection. Our preliminary data showed that the CK2 inhibitor, silmitasertib, has in-vitro and in-vivo anti-ZIKV effects. In Objective 2, we will validate this finding and thoroughly assess the anti-ZIKV effects of silmitasertib and other CK2 inhibitors using a lethal mouse model (survival) and additionally a pregnant mouse model (vertical transmission). In particular, we will detailedly investigate the anti-ZIKV effects of CK2 inhibitors on neurogenesis and testicular damage. -Objective 2.1: To investigate the in-vitro anti-ZIKV activity of CK2 inhibitors: to select the drugs with the best in-vitro anti-ZIKV properties for in-vivo evaluation. -Objective 2.2: To assess the in-vivo anti-ZIKV activity of CK2 inhibitors: in lethal and pregnant mouse models, and study the effects of CK2 inhibitors in reverting ZIKV-associated disruption in neurogenesis, testicular damage, and apoptosis.
