17123419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123419.value: Brown adipose tissue is specialized to dissipate energy in form of heat by its hallmark protein Uncoupling Protein 1 (UCP1), which achieves this through uncoupling ATP production and proton transport. However it was believed that brown adipose is only present in new born baby and disappears after birth. Recent advancement in imaging techniques revealed that white adipose tissue in adult human and mammals is plastic to brown-like remodelling as a potential approach to dissipate energy and maintain metabolic health. Moreover, the underlying mechanisms are not exclusively rely on the brown adipose marker UCP1. However, the identity of these UCP1-independent effectors, along with the physiological stimuli are largely unclear. Thyroid hormones are tyrosine-based hormones that facilitate adaptive thermogenesis through enhancing UCP1 expression in brown adipose tissue. However whether thyroid hormones arouse thermogenesis in white adipose tissue in UCP-1 independent manner is unclear. Our preliminary studies found that: (1) Mice deficient of UCP1 are still thermogenic competent, accompanied by remarkable elevation of DIO2, the enzyme for producing the active form of thyroid hormone, in inguinal white adipose tissue; (2) When depleted of endogenous thyroid hormones, Ucp1 knockout mice are no longer cold tolerant; (3) Supplementation of thyroid hormone arouses strong thermogenic response in white adipose tissues and fat mass reduction in absence of UCP1 at thermoneutrality; (4) RNAseq analysis reveals Na+K+ transport genes are induced by thyroid hormones in white adipose tissue; (5) In vitro treatment of T3 caused elevated energy utilization, which is readily abolished by inhibition of Na+K+ ATPases. Therefore we propose that thyroid hormone is capable of engaging alternative thermogenic program beyond the classical UCP1-mediated thermogenesis in white adipose tissue. By potentiating the expression of Na+K+ ATPases and leak channels, thyroid hormone engages a futile cation transport cycle and thereby dissipate energy into heat. In the current study, we will validate the thermogenic potential of T3-evoked cation transport cycle, identify the thyroid hormone receptor subtype mediating this UCP-1 independent effect, and the co-activators/co-receptors that facilitate the white adipose specific action of thyroid hormone. The mechanism underlying DIO2 induction in inguinal white adipose tissue is also examined. The findings of the study will establish futile cation transport cycle as new mechanism underlying white adipose tissue thermogenesis, in a manner independent of UCP1. The study will also facilitate a better understanding on thyroid hormone, and aid in further application of thyroid hormone-related anti-obese and anti-metabolic diseases therapies. 棕色脂肪組織表達標誌性蛋白質解耦聯蛋白1（UCP1）。它通過解偶聯ATP生成以及質子轉運，從而將能量以熱量形式消耗。過去人們認為棕色脂肪僅存在於新生嬰兒，並隨成長逐漸消失。近期，最新的成像技術發現由白色脂肪組織經重塑形成的“類棕色”脂肪組織在成年人以及其它哺乳動物中的存在，從而提示其代表壹種消耗能量、維持健康代謝的途徑。 值得壹提的是這種潛在機制並不僅僅依賴於UCP1，然而其獨立於UCP1的機理仍然在很大程度上未知。甲狀腺素是酪氨酸衍生的激素，它能夠通過增強棕色脂肪組織中UCP1的表達來促進適應性產熱。然而甲狀腺激素是否參與白色脂肪中獨立於UCP1的產熱過程尚不清楚。 我們的前期研究發現：（1）缺乏UCP1的小鼠仍然具有產熱能力，同時在其腹股溝白色脂肪中，促進產生活性態甲狀腺素的酶DIO2顯著升高。（2）當內源性甲狀腺素去除後，UCP1敲除小鼠不再耐寒。（3）在熱中性環境下，補充甲狀腺素能夠增強UCP1敲除小鼠白色脂肪中的產熱反應並降低脂肪量。（4）轉錄組表達分析顯示甲狀腺素引起白色脂肪組織中鈉鉀轉運蛋白基因表達量的升高。（5）在體外實驗中，T3引起能量利用率的升高，且抑制鈉鉀ATP酶可逆轉該變化。 因此，我們提出假說：在白色脂肪組織中，甲狀腺素介導的適應性產熱不僅局限於經典的依賴於UCP1的機制。通過增強鈉鉀ATP酶以及其它質子滲漏通道的表達，甲狀腺素能促進陽離子的無效循環從而使能量以熱能形式耗散。在本研究中，我們將驗證由T3介導的陽離子運轉循環，鑒定介導這種獨立於UCP1的作用的甲狀腺素受體亞型，以及促進其白色脂肪特異性效應的共激活劑及共同受體。同時，對於在腹股溝白色脂肪組織中的DIO2介導機制也會進行進壹步檢驗。該項研究的結果將有助於建立在白色脂肪組織中，獨立於UCP1,以無效陽離子循環為運作方式的產熱新機制。該研究還將有助於更好的了解甲狀腺素功能，並有助於未來進行的甲狀腺激素相關聯的肥胖及代謝疾病治療研究。

17123419.label: Realisation of objectives
17123419.value: The project objectives have been successfully completed. Objective 1. To address whether or not Na+K+ ATPases are alternative thermogenic effectors for T3-evoked energy expenditure in WAT. We have demonstrated that Na+K+ ATPase plays an important role in mediating T3-evoked heat production in WAT in an UCP1-independent manner. (1) The activity of Na+K+ ATPase was potentiated in inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) after cold exposure and after supplementation of T3. (2) Gene expression of the key subunit in Na+K+ ATPase, Atp1a2, was induced in iWAT after cold exposure and after supplementation of T3. (3) Lentiviruse-mediated knock down of Atp1a2 in iWAT was conducted in WT and Ucp1 KO mice. In Ucp1 KO mice, knock down of Atp1a2 compromised the heat generation in iWAT of the mice. (4) Atp1a2 gene was deleted using CRISPR/cas9-based in immortalized iWAT stromal vascular cells and differentiated in vitro. The response to T3 was significantly alleviated upon deletion of Na+K+ ATPases. (5) When treated with the Na+ and K+ ion ionophores to elevate the activity of Na+ and K+ leak channels, the adipocytes exhibited higher energy expenditure rate. Objective 2. To elucidate the underlying mechanism by which thyroid hormone induces white adipocyte-specific thermogenic programme. We have revealed the molecular mechanism in terms of why thyroid hormone exerts a selective action on WAT to enhance energy expenditure. (1) Atp1a2, the key subunit in Na+K+ ATPase, was selectively elevated in iWAT but not in BAT after either cold exposure or by T3 treatment. (2) We identified that thyroid hormone receptor beta (TRbeta) is the major isoform responsible for T3-induced Na+K+ ATPase expression and energy expenditure in WAT. (3) TRbeta promoter-driven luciferase activity of potentiated by T3 in vitro. (4) Furthermore, while administration of T3 in mice led to increased sympathetic nerve growth in iWAT, the sympathetic nerves were degenerated in BAT of the mice. Together, these events collectively contribute to the selective activation of energy expenditure by thyroid hormone in WAT. Objective 3. To clarify whether or not SNS is involved in thyroid hormone-elicited thermogenesis. We have demonstrated that sympathetic nerve system (SNS) plays an indispensable role in thyroid hormone-elicited thermogenesis. We found that (1) Sympathetic nerves were more potently innervated in inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) of Ucp1 KO mice, after cold acclimation. The sympathetic nerve biogenesis was positively correlated to the browning extent in WT and Ucp1 Ko mice. (2) Denervation of sympathetic nerves in the iWAT abolished cold-induced browning in Ucp1 KO mice. (3) By screening the genes upregulated by norepinephrine, the neurotransmitter produced by the sympathetic nerves, we found DIO2, the key enzyme synthesizing the active form of thyroid hormone T3, was among the most potent genes upregulated by norepinephrine. (4) Furthermore, denervation of sympathetic nerves abolished the induction of Dio2 in iWAT.

17123419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123419.value: This project aims to clarify the mechanisms underpinning brown remodeling in white adipose tissue (WAT). In particular we focused on how thyroid hormone elicits a non-classical energy expenditure in iWAT. Our findings demonstrated that WAT is capable of engaging both UCP1-dependent and UCP1-independent heat generation mechanisms. Sympathetic nerve induces local thyroid hormone biogenesis, which in turn stimulate Na+ K+ transport in WAT as an alternative way of energy expenditure. The major findings and research outcome are described as follows: 1. Expression of UCP1 is a golden standard for evaluating adipose tissue browning. To examine the activation of UCP-1 independent adipose browning, we established the method to quantify adipose browning using [18F]FDG uptake, which serve as a reliable and non-invasive imaging method to monitor UCP1-dependent and -independent adipose browning. Using this method, we found cold exposure and β3-adrenergic receptor agonist preferentially stimulated the glucose uptake in BAT. However, when BAT was dissected, or in Ucp1 knockout mice, glucose uptake was induced in iWAT. This study on one hand established a useful method to enable the monitoring of UCP1-independent energy expenditure in adipose tissue. On the other hand, using this method, we found UCP-1 independent energy expenditure is mainly present in iWAT (Liu et al., Jove 2021). We also used single cell sequencing to characterize the pathways involved in WAT browning (Liu et al., Research 2023). 2. Sympathetic nerve system (SNS) plays an indispensable role in thyroid hormone-elicited thermogenesis. More sympathetic nerves were innervated in iWAT of Ucp1 KO mice after cold acclimation. DIO2 was potently upregulated by norepinephrine. Furthermore, denervation of sympathetic nerves abolished the induction of Dio2 and adipose browning in iWAT (Liu et al., manuscript under preparation). 3. Using T3-administered WT and Ucp1 KO mice, we found T3 induces energy expenditure in IWAT to a comparable manner in WT and Ucp1 KO mice, indicating thyroid hormone is capable of inducing UCP1-independent energy expenditure. Furthermore, both gene expression and activity of Na+K+ ATPase were potentiated in iWAT after cold exposure and T3 supplementation. Inhibition of Na+K+ ATPase by different means abolished cold- or T3-induced energy expenditure in Ucp1 KO condition both in vitro and in vivo. Elevating the activity of Na+ and K+ leak channels increased the energy expenditure rate. These findings uncover Na+ K+ transport as a non-canonical energy expenditure in iWAT (Liu et al., manuscript under preparation).

17123419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123419.value: In this project, we have uncovered that thyroid hormone elicits a non-classical energy expenditure in iWAT. Our findings demonstrated that WAT is capable of engaging both UCP1-dependent and UCP1-independent heat generation mechanisms. Sympathetic nerve induces local thyroid hormone biogenesis, which in turn stimulate Na+ K+ transport in WAT as an alternative way of energy expenditure. Since we uncovered the key role of Atp1a2 in mediating UCP1-independent energy expenditure, we also established collaboration with Shanghai Jiaotong University and explored the clinical implication of ATP1A2. We have found that ATP1A2 expression in human adipose tissue is negatively corelated with body mass index (BMI). Furthermore, we have identified a missense variant p.Arg65Leu in the ATP1A2 gene linked with glucose and lipid metabolism. These studies suggest that ATP1A2 is a feasible target for treating obesity and its associated metabolic diseases. In future, we will continue to examine whether the missense variant p.Arg65Leu of ATP1A2 gene abolished the energy expenditure in beige adipocytes by generating cell and mouse models. Furthermore, we will explore whether ways enhancing Na+ K+ ATPase serve as new therapy to combat obesity and metabolic diseases.

17123419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123419.value: Obesity is now becoming a global epidemic. Enhancing energy expenditure in adipose tissue holds the therapeutic value to combat obesity, along with its associated metabolic disorders. Uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) has long been known as a major effector to dissipate energy. However, emerging evidence suggests the presence of non-classical, UCP1-independent way to burn off energy in adipose tissue. In the current project, we found that thyroid hormone not only induces the expression of UCP1, but also enhances energy expenditure in UCP1-independent manner. In white adipose tissue (WAT) of the mice receiving thyroid hormone, both the expression and activity of Na+ K+ ATPase were induced. Furthermore, blockade of Na+ K+ ATPase abolished energy expenditure in WAT stimulated by both cold exposure or thyroid hormone. We have also obtained evidence that ATP1A2 is clinically relevant to obesity and metabolic diseases in human. Therefore these findings uncover thyroid hormone-Na+K+ ATPase axis as a new mechanism in achieving energy expenditure. In future strategies aiming to enhance Na+ K+ ATPase activity may serve as a new therapy to treat obesity and metabolic diseases.

17123819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17123819.value: It is increasingly recognized that epigenetics plays a critical role in pathogenesis of many diseases as well as genetics. Epigenetics refers to the stable and heritable gene expression change without alterations of underlying genomic composition. Chromatin structure and DNA methylation are the two main aspects of epigenetics, regulated by chromatin remodelers, epigenetic enzymes, and non-coding RNA. These factors intimately interact with each other to define the epigenome landscape. These factors act in concert to regulate gene expression in response to environment cues by reading, writing, and erasing epigenetic marks. Epigenetics serves as the bridge by which environment and lifestyle exert its effect on the cellular machinery at the molecular level. The fascinating part is how the interplay between genetics and epigenetics defines cell differentiation, lineage specification, organ development, and its implications in pathogenesis, such as tumorigenesis. The reversible nature of epigenetic modifications make them very attractive therapeutic targets. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common subtype of liver cancer, and the third leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. In this proposal, we propose to test one chromatin regulator, VPS72, identified by us recently as an oncogenic driver amplified in liver cancer with effect on global DNA hypo-methylation. Our preliminary data analysis indicated that VPS72 was aberrantly overexpressed in TCGA liver cancer LIHC, which was caused by copy number gain. VPS72 overexpression in LIHC was positively correlated with cancer grade, and associated with poor prognosis. We hypothesized that overexpression of VPS72 may lead to DNA hypo-methylation of the regulatory sites of some cancer master regulator genes and the subsequent aberrant expression regulation of these genes. We set out to test these hypotheses, aiming to unravel the details and mechanism how VPS72 overexpression causes HCC. 人們越來越認識到表觀遺傳學在許多疾病和遺傳學的發病機理中起著關鍵作用。表觀遺傳學是指穩定和可遺傳的基因表達變化而不改變基礎基因組組成。染色質結構和DNA甲基化是表觀遺傳學的兩個主要方面，由染色質重塑（CR），表觀遺傳酶和非編碼RNA調節。這些因素彼此密切相互作用以定義表觀基因組。這些因子協同作用，通過閱讀，書寫和擦除表觀遺傳標記來調節基因表達以響應環境變化。表觀遺傳學是環境和生活方式在分子水平上對細胞機器發揮作用的橋樑。令人著迷的部分是遺傳學和表觀遺傳學之間的相互作用如何定義細胞分化，譜系規範，器官發育及其在發病機制中的意義，如腫瘤發生。表觀遺傳修飾的可逆性使它們成為非常有吸引力的治療靶點。 肝細胞癌（HCC）是肝癌最常見的亞型，也是全球癌症相關死亡的第三大原因。在這個研究計劃中，我們測試一種CR，VPS72基因，我們最近鑑定為一種在肝癌中擴增的致癌驅動因子，對全DNA低甲基化有影響。我們的初步數據分析表明，VPS72在TCGA肝癌樣本（LIHC）中異常過表達，這是由拷貝數增加引起的。 VPS72過表達與癌症分級呈正相關，與預後不良有關。VPS72的過表達可能導致某些癌症主調控基因調控位點的DNA低甲基化以及這些基因的異常表達調控。在這個研究計劃中, 我們測試這些假設，旨在揭示VPS72過表達如何導致HCC的機制。

17123819.label: Realisation of objectives
17123819.value: The proposed objectives have been successfully achieved with two manuscripts prepared for submission. 1. To characterize the oncogenic role of VPS72 in liver tumorigenesis and cancer stemness We examined TCGA LIHC patient data to assess VPS72 copy number, expression levels, and survival data. Analysis revealed that over 70% of patient samples contained extra copies of the VPS72 gene. Survival analysis, comparing the top and bottom quartiles based on VPS72 expression, indicated a strong correlation between high VPS72 expression and poor overall survival. To validate the oncogenic potential of VPS72 in HCC cells, we conducted overexpression and knockdown experiments in Huh7 and PLC/PRF/5 cell lines, respectively. VPS72 overexpression accelerated cell migration (by transwell and wound-healing assays) and proliferation (by MTT and colony formation assays). Enhanced stemness gene expression along with increased spheroid number and size were observed upon VPS72 overexpression. There is no ChIP-grade anti-VPS72 available. To solve this issue, a CRISPR-Cas9 system-based knock-in of epitope FLAG tags was performed at the end of the endogenous VPS72 protein coding sequence. Knock-in of FLAG epitope tag on the tail of endogenous VPS72 has been achieved. Pan-omics (RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and ATAC-seq) analysis of gene expression regulation by VPS72 has been conducted. 2. To characterize the interaction between VPS72 and H2A.Z and the impact on DNA methylation The knockdown of VPS72 using a doxycycline-inducible lentiviral system suppressed the migration and proliferation abilities of PLC/PRF/5 cells. Similar suppression of migration was observed in HepG2 cells following VPS72 knockdown. The knockdown of H2AFZ (encoding H2A.Z) was performed in PLC/PRF/5 cells as a reference to substantiate the findings further. The migration and proliferation abilities were inhibited upon doxycycline treatment, consistent with the known oncogenic role of H2A.Z in HCC as reported by previous studies. VPS72 activates lipogenesis in HCC cells To comprehensively investigate the regulatory role of VPS72, RNA-seq was performed on Huh7 cells overexpressing VPS72. Using a cutoff of |log2FC| > 0.5 and P < 0.05, we identified 182 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) upon VPS72 overexpression. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed a significant overrepresentation of biological processes related to sterol/cholesterol biosynthesis and homeostasis, as well as lipoprotein-associated processes. Additionally, hallmarks such as E2F targets, mTORC1 signaling, and MYC targets were prominently represented. To validate the activity of the lipogenesis biological process regulated by VPS72, we examined the expression levels of key lipogenic and lipoprotein-associated genes using RT-PCR in Huh7 cells overexpressing VPS72. The upregulation trends were consistent with RNA-seq results. These findings were further confirmed in LO2 cells by RT-PCR. SREBF1 and SREBF2 are key transcription factors controlling lipid biosynthesis, activating the expression of FASN, ACLY (ATP Citrate Lyase), and SCD (Stearoyl-CoA Desaturase), which are crucial enzymes in the lipid biosynthesis process. Although gene ALDH1A1 is not a core participant in lipogenesis, its transcription is reportedly activated by SREBF1. The activation of ALDH1A1 expression further supports the transcriptional activation of SREBF1 target genes. Given the importance of these activated lipogenic genes, it is reasonable to presume that lipid homeostasis in HCC cells is affected by aberrant VPS72 expression. We further validated that VPS72 overexpression led to lipid droplet accumulation in Huh7 cells, while VPS72 knockdown in PLC/PRF/5 cells resulted in fewer lipid droplets per cell. 3. To identify the downstream targets and pathways of VPS72 VPS72 promotes lipogenesis by activating mTORC1 signaling Next, we aimed to investigate the upstream pathway involved in lipogenesis mediated by VPS72. GSEA analysis of our RNA-seq data revealed significant activation of the mTORC1 signaling pathway upon VPS72 overexpression. The mTORC1 pathway is a central regulator of cell metabolism, growth, proliferation, and survival. Notably, mTORC1 has been reported to activate the expression of lipogenic enzymes through the regulation of SREBF1. To validate mTORC1 activity, we employed a fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-based kinase activity biosensor reporter system, TORCAR. Western blotting was also performed to assess the phosphorylation level of the mTORC1 substrate S6K. Both FRET and western blot results indicated elevated mTORC1 complex activity upon VPS72 overexpression in Huh7 cells. Conversely, repression of mTORC1 activity was observed in PLC/PRF/5 cells with VPS72 knockdown. Interestingly, the Akt reporter showed no significant difference upon treatment. Given that Akt is a substrate of the mTORC2 complex, this suggests that VPS72 may not significantly influence mTORC2 activity, which has also been reported to regulate lipid metabolism in HCC. VPS72 represses ATF3 expression to activate mTORC1 signaling ATF3 is known to repress mTOR activity in hepatic cells and was one of the top DEGs identified in our RNA-seq results. It is highly likely that ATF3 links VPS72 to mTORC1 regulation. We first validated the regulatory effect of VPS72 on ATF3 expression. In Huh7 cells, ATF3 levels were significantly repressed by VPS72, as demonstrated by both RT-PCR and western blot. Notably, ATF3 mRNA levels in LIHC patients are significantly lower than in normal tissues, indicating recurrent repression of ATF3 expression in HCC. Furthermore, the knockdown of VPS72 in PLC/PRF/5 and Hep3B cells resulted in activated ATF3 expression, as shown by RT-PCR (Figure 5C, D). These results collectively indicate that VPS72 negatively regulates ATF3 expression in HCC cells. VPS72 repressed ATF3 expression by inducing ATF3 promoter methylation ATF3 variants are reported to be transcribed from two promoters, with the two respective full-length variants (variant 1 and variant 3) encoding the same protein isoform 28. From our RNA-seq results, we identified that Huh7 cells express variant 1 of ATF3 (Figure 6A). Consequently, ChIP-seq and ATAC-seq signals surrounding the promoter for variant 1 were studied to investigate the repression of the ATF3 promoter. VPS72 is known to act as a chaperone for H2A.Z in cells, likely regulating gene expression by replacing H2A with H2A.Z in nucleosomes at regulatory loci on chromatin. It is plausible that VPS72 directly regulates ATF3 expression by manipulating H2A.Z at the ATF3 promoter region. ChIP-seq results showed enriched H2A.Z signals flanking the TSS of ATF3. In control cells, H2A.Z was more abundant downstream of the TSS, whereas in VPS72-overexpressing cells, H2A.Z signals shifted upstream. Despite no significant changes in the conventional activation marker H3K27ac upon VPS72 overexpression, the acetylated H2A.Z signal—commonly recognized as an activation marker—was significantly decreased in the VPS72 overexpression (OE) group, indicating repression of promoter activity. Interestingly, the H3K4me1 signal, associated with enhancer activity, was upregulated in the OE group, which contradicts the repressed expression of ATF3. To demonstrate that hypermethylation of the CpG island could cause repression of ATF3, we manipulated the DNA methylation level at the CpG island region using a dCas9-DNMT3A-L system. Results showed that the expression level of ATF3 was significantly suppressed by sgRNA1 and sgRNA6. Taken together with the observed upregulated DNA methylation level upstream of the TSS of ATF3, these results suggest that hypermethylation of DNA regions upstream of the TSS could, to some extent, contribute to the repression of ATF3 expression. However, the major cause of the repression is more likely to be the excessive incorporation of H2A.Z upstream of the TSS and the decreased acetylation level of H2A.Z around the TSS site.

17123819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17123819.value: Dysregulated lipid metabolism in hepatocytes results in abnormal lipid accumulation, contributing to HCC pathogenesis. While VPS72, a component of the histone acetyltransferase complex, has been implicated in HCC development, the underlying oncogenic mechanisms and its role in lipid metabolism remain elusive. Our bioinformatic analysis reveals that VPS72 upregulation is associated with poor prognosis in HCC patients. Functional assays further demonstrate that VPS72 enhances HCC cell proliferation and migration. RNA-Seq analysis shows that VPS72 overexpression activates mTORC1 signaling and lipid synthesis in HCC, findings corroborated by subsequent experimental validation. We identify ATF3 as a downstream transcription factor involved in mTORC1 inhibition. Mechanistically, VPS72 increases methylation of the ATF3 promoter, repressing ATF3 transcription. This repression alleviates the inhibition of mTORC1, thereby promoting lipogenesis. Our study elucidates the epigenetic regulatory pathway involving VPS72, ATF3, and mTORC1 in HCC, establishing a connection between HCC progression and dysregulated lipogenesis. These insights provide potential therapeutic targets for HCC treatment. While ATF3, a transcription factor, has been implicated in tumorigenesis and lipid metabolism regulation, its specific role in HCC advancement and lipid biosynthesis remains elusive. Through comprehensive functional assays in ATF3-overexpressing and -knockdown HCC cell lines, we elucidated ATF3's function as a tumor suppressor in HCC. Transcriptomic analysis of HCC patients revealed that elevated ATF3 expression correlates with diminished lipid synthesis, a finding validated through experimental and bioinformatics approaches. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that ATF3 impedes lipid biosynthesis by suppressing mTORC1 signaling, with SLC7A7 emerging as a key mediator in this regulatory axis. Specifically, ATF3 interacts with the enhancer region of SLC7A7, promoting its transcriptional activation, thereby restraining mTORC1 activity. Our study delineates ATF3's inhibitory role in lipogenesis and HCC progression, shedding light on an underlying mechanistic pathway. Furthermore, our findings underscore the link between dysregulated lipid metabolism and hepatocarcinogenesis, offering potential therapeutic targets for clinical intervention in HCC management.

17123819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17123819.value: From our pan-omics analysis of gene expression regulation by VPS72, we identified the key signaling pathways underlying the tumorigenesis of VPS72. In this study we reported the overexpression of VPS72 in HCC caused by its copy number variation activates the biosynthesis of lipid and results in the accumulation of lipid droplets through ATF3/mTORC1/SREBF1 regulatory axis. VPS72 repressed the expression of mTORC1-inhibitory gene ATF3, leading to the activation of mTORC1 and downstream SREBF1-controlled lipogenic genes. We also validated that the treatment with metformin could reshape the aberrant lipid metabolism and reverse the malignancy induced by VPS72. Our study elucidates the epigenetic regulatory pathway involving VPS72, ATF3, and mTORC1 in HCC, establishing a connection between HCC progression and dysregulated lipogenesis. These insights provide potential therapeutic targets for HCC treatment.

17123819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17123819.value: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common type of liver cancer in adults and is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. The dysregulated epigenetic regulation network is considered as the main cause of the transformation of cells towards cancer. In eukaryotic cells, gene expressions on chromosome DNA are orchestrated by a dynamic chromosome structure state that is largely controlled by chromatin-regulating proteins namely chromatin regulators. In this study, we followed the hints provided by our previous work and investigated the mechanisms of two dysregulated chromatin regulators VPS72 and ATF3 in the progression of HCC. The histone variant H2A.Z chaperon protein VPS72 is a shared subunit of two chromatin remodelers SRCAP and TIP60. It catalyzes the incorporation of H2A.Z into nucleosome and mediates the structural change of the chromatin. In this study we reported the overexpression of VPS72 in HCC caused by its copy number variation activates the biosynthesis of lipid and results in the accumulation of lipid droplets through ATF3/mTORC1/SREBF1 regulatory axis. VPS72 repressed the expression of mTORC1-inhibitory gene ATF3, leading to the activation of mTORC1 and downstream SREBF1-controlled lipogenic genes. We also validated the treatment with metformin could reshape the aberrant lipid metabolism and reverse the malignancy induced by VPS72.

17124219.label: Realisation of objectives
17124219.value: In the current study, we have investigated the association of MDSC population and CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 expressions both in clinical transplantation cohort and rat liver transplantation model. The molecular mechanisms of monocytic/granulocytic MDSCs recruitment by CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 have been also explored. We have suggested that the accumulated MDSC population are accompanied with CXCL10/TLR4 increase by both clinical and animal studies. Monocytic MDSCs (not granulocytic MDSCs) are significantly decreased in CXCL10-/- and TLR4-/- mice of hepatic IRI model (interestingly, no obvious change in CXCR3-/- mice). We have demonstrated the significant association of intrahepatic CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 up-regulation and MDSCs accumulation on promoting cancer recurrence. The molecular mechanisms recruiting MDSCs by CXCL10 signals have been studied by a series of gene knock-out mouse models and in vitro studies. It is demonstrated that the therapeutic potentials of TLR4 inhibitors and CXCL10 neutralized antibodies in inhibiting MDSC recruitment and cancer recurrence have been also explored in mouse models and cells. In summary, we have achieved following aims of the study through our integrated clinical, basic and animal studies (with 3 original articles – details please refer to research outcomes): 1. Investigated the association of MDSC population and CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 expressions both in clinical transplantation cohort and rat liver transplantation model. 2. Studied the mechanisms of MDSC recruitment by CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 signaling through in vivo (mouse mode with gene knockout mice) and in vitro experiments. 3. Explored the potential therapeutics to attenuate liver graft injury and cancer recurrence by targeting the interactions of CXCL10/TLR4 and MDSC in animal model.

17124219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124219.value: We have investigated the association of MDSC population and CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 expressions both in clinical transplantation cohort and rat liver transplantation model. The molecular mechanisms of monocytic/granulocytic MDSCs recruitment by CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 have been also explored. Briefly, we have analyzed 331 HCC patients who received liver transplantation, the patients with small graft had higher tumor recurrence. MDSCs and CXCL10/TLR4 levels were significantly increased in patients with small liver graft or tumor recurrence. These findings were further validated in our rat orthotopic liver transplantation model. In CXCL10−/−and TLR4−/− mice of hepatic ischemia/reperfusion injury plus major hepatectomy (IRH) model, monocytic MDSCs, instead of granulocytic MDSCs, were significantly decreased. Importantly, CXCL10 deficiency reduced the accumulation of TLR4+monocytic MDSCs, and CXCL10 increased MDSC mobilization in the presence of TLR4. Moreover, MMP14 was identified as the key molecule bridging CXCL10/TLR4 signaling and MDSC mobilization. Knockout or inhibition of CXCL10/TLR4 signaling significantly reduced the tumor growth with decreased monocytic MDSCs and MMP14 in the mouse tumor recurrent model. We demonstrated that monocytic MDSCs were mobilized and recruited to liver graft during acute phase injury, and to promote HCC recurrence after transplantation. Targeting MDSC mobilization via CXCL10/TLR4/MMP14 signaling may represent the therapeutic potential in decreasing post-transplant liver tumor recurrence. (Liu et al. Cell Death & Disease 2021) The high incidence of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease resulted in the frequent application of steatotic donor in liver transplantation. We showed that the patients underwent liver transplantation using fatty grafts experienced higher tumor recurrence. Therefore, we have further explored the association of MDSC populations and nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome levels in a clinical cohort and a rat liver transplantation model with fatty liver graft. The mechanism of NLRP3 activation by specific fatty acids was explored in mouse hepatic ischemia/reperfusion injury (IRI) with tumor recurrence model and in vitro studies. We have found that arachidonic acid activated NLRP3 inflammasome in MDSCs through FATP2 during fatty liver graft injury, which led more IL-17 secretion of CD4+ T cells and promote tumor recurrence post transplantation. The inflammasome activation by aberrant fatty acid metabolism in MDSCs bridged the acute phase fatty liver graft injury and liver tumor recurrence (Liu et al. JH Report 2023). In addition, we also demonstrated that postoperative plasmacytoid dendritic cells secrete IFNα to promote the recruitment of MDSCs and drive liver cancer recurrence (Pang et al. Cancer Research 2022).

17124219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124219.value: It will be worthwhile to further explore the other potential therapeutic strategies on the regulation of hepatic immune environment after surgical treatment of liver cancer. The interaction of MDSC and other immune cells such as regulatory T cells and CD4 and CD8 T cells will be also important for the development of new immune therapies. It is feasible to investigate the clinical association and underlying mechanism using clinical cohorts and in vitro and in vivo models. It is also possible to explore the new treatments in animal models. We will design and conduct the related clinical, basic and translational research plan for targeting MDSCs on cancer recurrence after surgical treatment of liver cancer.

17124219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124219.value: The understanding of the mechanism of cancer recurrence after liver transplantation (LT) for the patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) will be critical to develop new therapeutic strategies for preventing HCC recurrence after LT. In this project, we have investigated the clinical association of myeloid derived suppressor cells (MDSC) populations and CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 expressions in HCC patients underwent LT. The molecular mechanisms of monocytic/granulocytic MDSCs recruitment by CXCL10/CXCR3/TLR4 have been also explored. We have demonstrated that the accumulated MDSC population are accompanied with CXCL10/TLR4 increase in both clinical and animal studies. The molecular mechanisms recruiting MDSCs by CXCL10 signals have been also studied by a series of gene knock-out mouse models and in vitro studies. The therapeutic potentials of TLR4 inhibitors and CXCL10 neutralized antibodies in inhibiting MDSC recruitment and cancer recurrence have been explored in mouse models and cells. In summary, we have explored the molecular mechanism for CXCL10 signaling regulating MDSC accumulation and promoting tumor recurrence after LT. Elucidating the precise molecular mechanism for liver graft injury facilitating tumor recurrence will lay the foundation for further development of therapeutic strategies to alleviate liver graft injury and reduce cancer recurrence.

17124719.value: 無論是在自然界還是在入侵的動物宿主内，微生物主要是以一種由自身產生的胞外多聚物包裹的生物被膜的形式存在的。一旦形成，生物被膜內的細胞會耐受各種抗菌物質，比如抗生素，除菌劑，噬菌體，以及哺乳動物的免疫侵襲等。從而對環境和臨床上病原體的控制造成極大的問題。大約80%的感染性疾病是由病原體形成的生物被膜引起的。除了人體組織，病原體還可以在一系列非生物表面形成生物被膜，比如植入的義肢，呼吸機，導尿管，非潔淨的醫療器械等。這些病原體生物被膜在公共衛生領域造成了很嚴重的問題。 銅綠假單胞杆菌因其超強的生物被膜形成能力而成為一種研究生物被膜的模式菌株。盡管已經有數個調控生物被膜形成的通路被闡明，我們對生物被膜的形成和調控的整體過程遠未了解。非常有趣的是，我們的前期研究發現63%的臨床菌株在室溫下比在37oC表現出更強的形成生物被膜的能力。一株常用的實驗室菌株ATCC 27853也表現出了類似的現象。 因此，本課題擬利用ATCC 27853為研究對象，從以下三個方面來闡明溫度如何調控銅綠假單胞杆菌生物被膜形成：1）研究由c-di-GMP 和RpoS介導的轉錄水平的調控；2）由sRNA和RNAT介導的在蛋白翻譯水平的調控；3）全基因組水平的其它為止的調控通路。這一系列研究不但將會闡明一條生物被膜調控的新途徑，還會豐富我們對溫度調控病原體的生理，致病性，以及耐藥性的總體認識，並將為發展抗被膜形成藥物提供新的靶點

17124719.label: Realisation of objectives
17124719.value: Objective 1. Examine c-di-GMP and RpoS mediated transcriptional regulation. Confirmed Psl production to be primarily responsible for the enhanced biofilm formation at RT in P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853: We constructed a Ppsl-lux transcriptional fusion in ATCC 27853 and identified that the Ppsl-lux activity was significantly higher at RT than at 37°C after 10 h during the 48-h assay. Western blot revealed that PslD production was significantly higher at RT than at 37°C. We stained ATCC 27853 biofilm cells using TRITC-HHA (for Psl) and TRITC-WFA (for Pel), respectively, and performed CLSM. Psl production was found to be ~5-fold higher at RT than at 37°C, while Pel production was lower at RT than at 37°C. We constructed isogenic psl, pel mutants. ΔpslD led to a significant reduction of biofilm biomass at RT. In contrast, ΔpelF almost had no effect on the formation at RT. ΔpslDΔpelF completely abolished biofilm formation, suggesting enhanced Psl production was primarily responsible for the enhanced biofilm formation at RT. Identified c-di-GMP/FleQ pathway to be primarily responsible for enhanced Psl production at RT and RpoS is not involved in the regulation: To investigate the regulation of psl expression at RT, we deleted all three known psl transcriptional regulators, RpoS, AmrZ, and FleQ in ATCC 27853, respectively. Deletion of rpoS or amrZ had no effect on biofilm biomass, but deletion of fleQ resulted in 61% reduction on biofilm biomass at RT. Deletion of any of the three genes had no effect on biofilm formation at 37°C, suggesting that FleQ plays an important role in enhancing the biofilm formation of ATCC 27853 at RT. Next, we monitored the activity of the chromosomal Ppsl-lux reporter and found that deletion of fleQ abolished the transcription of Ppsl-lux at RT. We reasoned that c-di-GMP effector FleQ regulate psl transcription in response to the elevated c-di-GMP level at RT relative to 37°C as detected in our preliminary investigations. Objective 2. Examine sRNA mediated translational regulation. To investigate post-transcriptional regulation of temperature-responsive biofilm formation, we surveyed currently known sRNA and RNATs in P. aeruginosa. Although all seven RNATs identified in P. aeruginosa mainly respond to temperature upshift, a sRNA ErsA was reported to promote the translation of psl transcriptional repressor AmrZ and displays an increased transcription upon temperature upshift (from 20°C to 37°C). In this study, we deleted ersA in ATCC 27853 and conducted a biofilm assay. However, ersA deletion had no effect on biofilm biomass of ATCC 27853 at RT or 37°C, suggesting that ErsA does not modulate the process. This result is consistent with the observation that ΔamrZ had a negligible effect on the temperature-responsiveness of biofilm in ATCC 27853 as identified in Objective 1. Objective 3. Genome wide mining of novel thermo-regulators: RNA-Seq and SHAPE-Seq. RNA-Seq revealed that a large number of genes involved in c-di-GMP metabolism were differentially expressed between RT and 37°C: Comparative RNA-Seq was conducted in P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 biofilm cells cultured at RT and 37°C. 1346 genes (21.2%) were found to be differentially expressed between RT and 37°C, suggesting a global gene expression change during this process in ATCC 27853. As expected, the RNA level of the pslL gene in the psl operon was upregulated 2.3-fold at RT relative to 37°C. Interestingly, QS systems (Las, RHl, PQS), virulence factors (pyocyanin, pyoverdine, pyochelin) and secretion systems (T1SS, T3SS, and T6SS) were down-regulated at RT compared with 37°C, while multidrug efflux systems (mexAB-oprM and mexEF-oprN), ribosomal protein synthesis and ATP synthesis were up-regulated at RT. DE genes are distributed in 104 KEGG pathways. Notably, we found that a large number of genes involved in c-di-GMP metabolism, including diguanylate cyclases (DGCs) which catalyze its synthesis and phosphodiesterases (PDEs) which catalyze its degradation, were differentially expressed between RT and 37°C. Identified the DGC activity of SiaD in the SiaABCD signaling module as the primary cause for the elevated c-di-GMP and biofilm formation at RT: Based on RNA-Seq analysis, we conducted gene deletion on 19 genes encoding DGCs or PDEs. Analyzing the biofilm formation of wild-type and mutant strains using a scatter plot revealed that ΔsiaD, which encodes a DGC, was clustered together with ΔfleQ and ΔpslD, which predominantly decreased biofilm formation at RT. LC-MS/MS analysis revealed that ΔsiaD caused ~42% reduction in cellular c-di-GMP level at RT. Furthermore, ΔsiaD led to a reduction of Ppsl-lux activity at RT but had no effect at 37°C. Recently, siaABCD was reported to be co-transcribed as an operon and regulate aggregation/biofilm formation in PAO1 in response to SDS. Phosphatase SiaA and kinase SiaB control the reversible phosphorylation of SiaC. Unphosphorylated SiaC induces the DGC activity of SiaD and phosphorylated SiaC inhibits the DGC activity of SiaD. In ATCC 27853, deletion of siaA or siaC resulted in a significant reduction of biofilm biomass at RT, similar to that of ΔsiaD. Deletion of siaB caused a negligible effect on biofilm biomass at RT. Overexpression of siaB reduced biofilm formation at RT in both the wild-type and ΔsiaB background, but not at 37°C. Furthermore, introduction of the phosphomimetic SiaC variant (SiaCT68D) significantly abolished the biofilm formation at RT, while introduction of the phosphorylation-deficient SiaC variant (SiaCT68A) led to comparable mature biofilm biomass as the wild-type. Phos-tag SDS-PAGE showed that SiaC existed primarily in the phosphorylated form at 37°C and unphosphorylated form at RT, suggesting the activation of the SiaABCD pathway at RT. Notably, ΔsiaA also reduced biofilm formation in another clinical strain PA150663 at RT, suggesting a conserved pathoadaptative mechanism. Identified that the transmembrane domains (TMs) of SiaA in the SiaABCD signal transduction module play an important role in the temperature-responsive biofilm formation at RT: Membrane-sensitive probe PI-BactD indicated that ATCC 27853 displayed distinctive membrane features at RT and 37°C, while that of PAO1 were similar at RT and 37°C. We predicted the full-length SiaA structure using tFold and simulated its interaction with phospholipids bilayer. We found TM1 (residues 9–31) of SiaA displays an unusual amphipathic feature. Expressing of chimeric SiaA variants with the region from the N-terminus to the end of TM1 (CusS-T1-SiaA), or the N-terminus to the end of TM2 (CusS-T1-2-SiaA), being substituted by the corresponding regions in the well-studied membrane sensor protein CusS failed to rescue the biofilm defect in ΔsiaA. Western blot analysis suggested the failure to rescue ΔsiaA by the CusS-T1-2-SiaA was due to the inactivity of this variant, but that of CusS-T1-SiaA was due to failure of expression. We examined the TM sequences of SiaA and identified three polar amino acids, R8, K10, and S11, which are similar to the temperature-sensing SB motif in B.subtilis DesK. Substitution of hydrophilic amino acids to hydrophobic residues in SiaA (R8A, K10A, S11L) significantly reduced the biofilm formation at RT, suggesting the SB motif in SiaA TM1 played an important role in responding to temperature downshift. Collectively, our studies revealed that majority of P. aeruginosa isolates display enhanced biofilm formation in response to temperature downshifts from host-relevant 37°C to RT, and that the SiaABCD/c-di-GMP/FleQ/Psl pathway plays an important role in the process. All objectives are executed.

17124719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17124719.value: P.aeruginosa is a highly adaptable Gram-negative pathogen known for its remarkable capability of forming biofilms, which contribute to its survival, antibiotic resistance, and transmission. Temperature fluctuations are a universal environmental cue encountered by pathogens during infection and transmission cycles. Yet, stress adaptation to these fluctuations, especially temperature downshifts, remains poorly understood. In this study, we screened the biofilm-forming capabilities of 52 clinical P. aeruginosa isolates from the Queen Mary Hospital, Hong Kong, and found that a temperature downshift from host-related 37°C to room temperature (21°C) promoted biofilm formation in the majority of strains. We employed P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 with high biofilm-forming and temperature-responsive capabilities as a model strain. Scanning electron microscopy, gene and protein expression, and immunostaining analysis showed the enhanced production of exopolysaccharide Psl was primarily responsible for the enhanced biofilm formation in ATCC 27853 at RT. We deleted all known psl transcriptional regulators and identified that c-di-GMP receptor FleQ is majorly responsible for enhanced psl transcription and biofilm formation at RT in ATCC 27853. LC-MS/MS analysis revealed that the secondary messenger c-di-GMP, a key factor controlling the motile-to-sessile lifestyle transition, was elevated at RT compared to 37°C. We constructed a mutant library encompassing deletion of 19 genes encoding c-di-GMP metabolic enzymes. Screening the library revealed that the DGC SiaD is primarily responsible for the elevated c-di-GMP content and enhanced biofilm formation at RT via the c-di-GMP/FleQ/Psl pathway. In the SiaABCD signaling module, the phosphatase SiaA and the kinase SiaB control the reversible phosphorylation of SiaC, and unphosphorylated SiaC activates the DGC activity of SiaD. Construction of phosphomimetic and phosphorylation-deficient SiaC variants, as well as Phos-tag SDS-PAGE confirmed the activation of the SiaABCD pathway at RT. Employing SiaA-CusS chimeric constructs, we demonstrated that the transmembrane domain of the signal-perceiving protein SiaA played a crucial role in adaptive biofilm formation at RT, presumably by sensing membrane perturbations at lower temperatures. Applying a membrane-sensitive probe PI-BactD revealed that temperature downshift from 37°C to RT resulted in a dramatic change on the membrane features of ATCC 27853 as opposed to a minimal membrane perturbation in the reference strain PAO1, correlating to their capability of biofilm formation upon temperature downshifts. Our findings establish an essential pathoadaptation mechanism in P. aeruginosa's infection and transmission cycle and identify the first c-di-GMP-modulating pathway responsive to temperature downshifts, providing potential targets for managing biofilm formation and preventing pathogen transmission.

17124719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17124719.value: Our studies have demonstrated that temperature downshift represents a common signal to enhance biofilm formation in the majority of tested clinical and environmental P. aeruginosa isolates. We showed that the SiaABCD/FleQ/c-di-GMP-regulated Psl production was primarily responsible for the enhanced biofilm formation at RT compared to 37°C in the model strain P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853. The next question to address is the detailed interactions between the inner membrane and SiaA during temperature downshifts, as well as the potential role of the periplasmic domain of SiaA in temperature perception. Currently, only the structure of the cytoplasmic SiaA-PP2C has been resolved. To address these points, we plan to resolve the structure of full-length SiaA, simulate its interaction with the membrane at different temperatures, and investigate potential conformational changes through FRET-based assays. Furthermore, we have detected distinctive membrane features in clinical isolates P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 and laboratory strain P. aeruginosa PAO1 during temperature downshifts. We plan to perform lipidomics to investigate the structural and compositional differences in their membranes, which could provide further insight into the pathoadaptive mechanisms in P. aeruginosa. This research will form the basis of another exciting GRF grant proposal, which we intend to prepare in the near future.

17124719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17124719.value: Bacterial biofilms shield pathogens from host immune responses and antimicrobial agents, thereby facilitating their survival and disease transmission. To effectively manage biofilms, it is crucial to identify the environmental signals that trigger their formation and to understand the underlying regulatory mechanisms. A universal signal encountered by pathogens during infection and transmission cycles is temperature fluctuations. Yet, stress adaptation to these fluctuations remains poorly understood. In this study, we revealed that a temperature downshift from a host-related 37°C to room temperature promoted biofilm formation in majority of P. aeruginosa clinical and environmental isolates. We elucidated that the SiaABCD signal transduction module and its downstream effector pathway c-di-GMP/FleQ/Psl are responsible for the enhanced biofilm formation during temperature downshifts. We identified that the transmembrane domain of the signal perceiving protein SiaA senses membrane perturbations caused by the temperature downshifts and activates the c-di-GMP cyclase SiaD to elevate c-di-GPM and enhance biofilm formation. Our findings establish an important pathoadaptation mechanism in P. aeruginosa in response to temperature fluctuations during host-environment transmission and identify the first c-di-GMP-modulating pathway responsive to temperature downshifts. This study offers a framework to untangle the complex c-di-GMP signaling network and its impact on adaptive biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa.

17125419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17125419.value: Background: Incidents of poisoning (intentional and unintentional), whether by medication or chemical means, are three times more likely to occur in patients with ADHD. Medication treatments for ADHD reduce symptoms of hyperactivity, impulsiveness and inattentiveness. Theoretically, medication could reduce the incidence of poisoning in patients with ADHD. However, current evidence suggests that the recent increase in prescriptions of ADHD medication is associated with an increase in poisoning linked to ADHD medications in the USA, Australia and Hong Kong (HK). Therefore, the association between ADHD medication and poisoning in patients with ADHD remains unclear. A recently published meta-analysis (August 2018) has called for research into poisoning linked to ADHD medication. Primary objectives: 1) To conduct an ecological analysis of secular trends in reports of poisoning cases from ADHD medications and the number of prescriptions issued by the HK Hospital Authority (HA) between 2009 and 2018. 2) To conduct a self-controlled case series (SCCS) to evaluate the risk of accident and emergency and/or hospital admission due to poisoning during periods of exposure to ADHD medications compared to periods of non-exposure in patients with ADHD. Secondary objectives: 1a) To conduct a narrative review of cases poisoned with ADHD medication in patients with ADHD and subjects without ADHD. 2a) To explore how comorbidities modify the risk of poisoning in patients with ADHD. Method: TAPPER consists of two studies. Study I and Study II addresses Objectives 1 and 1a and Objectives 2 and 2a, respectively. Study I: TAPPER will examine the prevalence of poisoning from ADHD medications reported to the HK Poison Information Centre and the prevalence of prescriptions dispensed by the HA using secular trend analysis. TAPPER will examine the relationship between the two prevalence trends using the cross-correlation coefficient, the Stock-Watson test for cointegration and the Granger causality test. TAPPER will then conduct a narrative review to evaluate the extent and nature of ADHD drug poisoning. Study II: 90% of prescribed ADHD medication in HK is methylphenidate (MPH); therefore, TAPPER will focus on MPH only. TAPPER will conduct a SCCS using patient-based data from the HA Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System. The risk of poisoning during periods of exposure to MPH compared to non-exposed periods will be measured in patients with ADHD. Impact: Pending study findings, we will develop appropriate strategies to prevent and manage poisoning with ADHD medications. 背景：專注力不足或過度活躍症(ADHD)患者有意或無意服用藥物及其他化學物品導致中毒的風險為常人的三倍。治療ADHD的藥物可減少過度活躍、衝動和專注力不足的症狀。理論上，藥物治療可以改善ADHD病情以及各種相關症狀，從而降低病人中毒的風險。然而，在美國，澳洲和香港的醫學文獻指出有關ADHD病人中毒事件與近年來藥物使用量增加有關。於2018年8月發表的最新一項關於ADHD與中毒風險的薈萃性分析中指出，ADHD藥物使用與患者中毒風險之間的關係尚未明確，有必要對有關藥物使用與中毒風險作進一步的研究。 TAPPER的主要研究目標為： 1. 分析醫院管理局（醫管局）于2009年至2018年間有關ADHD藥物中毒個案、相關藥物處方數目及長期流行趨勢。 2. 運用自身病例對照系列研究方法，對比ADHD藥物使用前後因中毒事件導致急症或入院風險的差異，明確ADHD藥物使用與患者中毒風險之間的關係。。 次要目標為： 1a. 對患者與非患者使用ADHD藥物的中毒病例進行描述性綜述。 2a. 分析ADHD患者中各類並發症對中毒風險的影響。 研究方法： TAPPER主要由兩項研究組成，研究I和研究II分別討論了目標1和1a以及目標2和2a。 研究I：TAPPER將利用香港中毒諮詢中心報告的ADHD藥物中毒數據研究相關中毒風險，并使用醫管局處方藥物數據進行長期流行趨勢分析。TAPPER將使用交叉相關係數，Stock/Watson協整檢驗和Granger因果關係檢驗來驗證兩種流行趨勢之間的關係。並對ADHD藥物中毒病例的程度和性質進行敘述性評估。 研究II: 哌醋甲酯/利他能（MPH/Ritalin）佔香港治療ADHD的藥物處方約百分之九十。因此，TAPPER將集中研究MPH的中毒風險。TAPPER將使用醫管局的臨床數據分析與報告系統，應用自身病例對照系列研究，比較ADHD患者在使用及未用MPH期間的中毒風險。 影響： 基於是項項目的研究結果，我們將制定適當的策略來預防和控制ADHD患者中毒風險。

17125419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17125419.value: We used the electronic health record database from the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System in Hong Kong to evaluate the incidence rate ratios (IRRs) of all-causes poisoning during the ADHD medication (methylphenidate) treatment and non-treatment periods. We found higher risks of poisoning during the 30 days before the first methylphenidate prescription (IRR=2.64), as well as exposure periods within 30 days of the first prescription (IRR=2.18) compared to other non-exposure periods (baseline). Notably, the poisoning risk returned to baseline levels during the period of subsequent methylphenidate treatment. The increased risk before the first methylphenidate prescription is probably the reason that prompted the prescription whilst the increased risk after the first methylphenidate prescription may be related to the suboptimal treatment of ADHD symptoms during the titration of methylphenidate. Overall, our results do not support an association of methylphenidate use with an increased risk of poisoning in children and adolescents with ADHD. Bringing all the current evidence together from our study and published ecological studies, a logical explanation to the increased number of poisoning cases from ADHD medication may be due to the poor management or storage of ADHD medications in the household. Our study findings can raise awareness and spark further research on this topic to develop public health strategies to address the increasing occurrence of ADHD medication poisoning.

Furthermore, we have been given a Knowledge Exchange fund to set up a website and training materials. We will use this opportunity to emphasize the importance of safe storage of ADHD medications.

17125419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17125419.value: Our study used information from the Hospital Authority and Hong Kong Poison Information Centre to find out whether prescription of methylphenidate increase the chance of poisoning. Methylphenidate is a medication for children and adolescentswith attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). We know that people with ADHD are very prone to accidents and poisoning, there are some studies reported increasing used of methylphenidate may be the cause of increasing poisoning case to poison centres in other countires. Overall, our results do not support an association of methylphenidate use with an increased risk of poisoning in children and adolescents with ADHD. Bringing all the current evidence together from our study and published studies, a logical explanation to the increased number of poisoning cases from ADHD medication may be due to the poor management or storage of ADHD medications in the household. Our study findings can raise awareness and spark further research on this topic to develop public health strategies to address the increasing occurrence of ADHD medication poisoning.

17126119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126119.value: 椎間盤疾病（IDD）是一種主要的增加醫療負擔的衰老疾病。在IDD中，椎間盤的機械強度和減震能力下降，相應的結構性退化會導致身體殘疾。引起IDD發病的機制可能是椎間盤（IVD）組織修復能力的喪失。雖然有證據表明人類、兔子、囓齒動物和豬的椎間盤中存在骨骼祖細胞，但對這些細胞如何維持健康椎間盤的的生物學和功能知之甚少。通過小鼠發育的研究表明，構成椎間盤核心的凝膠狀髓核（NP）中的不同類型的細胞來源於胚胎脊索中的祖細胞群。脊索作為支撐身體軀幹縱向生長的主要結構支架，以及驅動周圍組織形成的信號源，是脊椎動物發育所必需的。 在椎間盤的發育過程中，髓核由兩種不同的細胞類型組成：帶有較大空泡的脊索樣細胞（NCL）和較小的分散的軟骨樣細胞（NPC）。它們的細胞後代一起合成正常椎間盤所必需的胞外基質（ECM），但每種細胞類型的功能尚不清楚。脊索樣細胞在出生後存在於髓核中，但隨著年齡的增長而迅速減少。青春期後很少有脊索樣細胞殘留，而軟骨樣細胞成為主要的細胞類型。相比之下，脊索樣細胞可以持久存在於不易發生椎間盤退化的動物（例如小鼠）中。因此，脊索樣細胞是一群維持髓核功能的早期祖細胞。在人類髓核中，脊索樣細胞的減少和成纖維細胞的出現，跟衰老導致的椎間盤退化同時發生。 這種相關性讓我們設想脊索樣細胞是靜止的祖細胞，需要保存和激活以替換衰老細胞以預防或改善椎間盤退化。 我們的研究表明，成年髓核由長壽命緩慢分裂細胞（即不經常分裂）和短壽命快速分裂細胞（緩慢分裂細胞的後代）組成。這兩種細胞類型的譜系關係支撐著它們對常見組織譜系的貢獻。我們的研究結果揭示了小鼠髓核在發育過程中這兩種細胞群的相對豐度的異質性，但它們在維持髓核功能的作用尚不清楚。對單個髓核細胞的基因譜分析揭示了慢分裂細胞中Notch信號通路的富集，指出髓核細胞對缺氧環境的適應。 對Notch信號通路的抑制結果突出了這一關鍵屬性，即使在不易發生椎間盤退化和髓核中緩慢分裂細胞富集的小鼠中也會引起早期椎間盤退變，這表明它們的增殖狀態可能被封鎖了。在這個項目中，我們利用小鼠模型，通過基因敲除和過表達的譜係分析，單細胞轉錄組學和細胞分化檢測等方法，以確定Notch信號通路對髓核祖細胞的生物學功能的影響，以及髓核祖細胞的功能改變和椎間盤退化的關係。該項目的成果將對椎間盤退化的研究和臨床治療，以及將來再生醫學產生廣泛的影響。

17126119.label: Realisation of objectives
17126119.value: Challenges faced in the project The project has faced challenges which resulted in delays and changes in achievement: a) There was delay in recruitment of a postdoc, because of difficulties arising from the protests in Hong Kong. Later, the COVID pandemic restrictions delayed her arrival from mainland China. b). During the protests in 2019, the Laboratory Animal Unit (LAU) was closed intermittently delaying the importation of mice for the project. In 2020, because of the pandemic, our collaborators in Canada and USA could not send us mice. During the COVID pandemic, access to the LAU was further restricted, affecting mouse experiments. Furthermore building works carried out in the LAU redevelopment resulted in severe stress on mice leading to repeated failed pregnancies. Therefore we were unable to establish the lines of mice: Cdk1-loxP-TKmCherry from Toronto, Canada; and Hes1-creERT2 from University of Michigan. Because of all these difficulties the lineage tracing and NP cell killing experiments (Objective 2) were severely delayed. In 2022. Cdk1-loxP-TKmCherry mice were finally obtained and established successfully. The mouse line took 12 months to establish (after quarantine and expansion of line). Despite these challenges we have adopted alternative strategies. We have been able to obtain new insights into the attributes of progenitors in the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc in postnatal life and in IDD. Therefore we have ADDRESSED all the objectives and the results contributed to one paper published in 2024 and a further paper on the fate of label retaining cells (LRCs) in a mouse model of premature disc degeneration is in preparation for submission. Realisation of Objectives 1. Lineage trajectories, molecular and functional characteristics of cycling cells in the NP. To define the characteristics of the putative NP progenitors, we analysed the transcriptomes of 420 single cells isolated from 18 week old mice in which cycling NP cells were previously labelled with GFP by doxycycline treatment for 4 weeks followed by 8 weeks of no doxycycline (pulse and chase approach). We found the majority of GFP+ NP cells (n=449) which expressed high levels of T (Thigh) and a small number (n=15) were negative for T (TLow). However which cells in the NP are likely to be progenitors was uncertain. We identified 114 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) that were enriched in the TLow subpopulation compared to the Thigh. Interestingly amongst the positively expressed DEGs in the TLow cells, these all expressed genes characteristic of progenitors e.g. cell cycle regulator Cdkn1a (p21 protein) and ATF4, Pou5F1, Hmga1 transcription factors and CD44 . 2. Functional attributes of cycling NP cells as progenitors. The role of Notch signaling. We tested the role of Notch signaling in NP progenitors in adult mice by applying DAPT, an inhibitor of Notch signaling, every 2 days throughout the course of DOX treatment for 4 weeks. Inhibition of notch signaling resulted in severe degeneration of the NP compared to control IVD in which no disc degeneration was observed. These data suggest that Notch inhibition may compromise NP integrity and appropriate Notch signaling may be important for NP cells homeostasis. We found inhibition of Notch signaling altered the NP population dynamics resulting in a change in the proportions of Sox9 and T expressing GFP label retaining cells. The proportion of the GFP+Sox9-Tlow and GFP+Sox9+Tlow cells are decreased while the proportion of GFP+Sox9+T+ cells are increased. The changed proportions of Sox9 and T expressing cells suggests that Notch signaling may be important to maintain the progenitor homeostasis and appropriate proportions of different cell types in NP. The data raise the possibility that Notch signaling maintains NP progenitors by inhibiting their differentiation or entry into senescence. Inhibiting Notch could trigger differentiation or senescence, resulting in exhaustion of progenitors for maintaining the NP. These changes could culminate in premature IDD. Ablation of proliferating cells in the NP. We generated the Foxa2-Cre; Cdk1-TK-mCherry and Noto-Cre; Cdk1-TK-mCherry mouse lines to facilitate the ablation of proliferating cell population in the NP. The expression of mCherry is triggered by the Cre activity that places it under the control of the Cdk1 gene, thus it labels the proliferative cells of a specific lineage. We found the expression of mCherry in Noto-Cre; Cdk1-TK-mCherry lasts until postnatal day 14 while in Foxa2-Cre; Cdk1-TK-mCherry mouse NP, the expression of mCherry can be found even at 6-week-old. At p14, more cells express mCherry in the Foxa2-Cre; Cdk1-TK-mCherry mouse NP, compared to the Noto-Cre; Cdk1-TK-mCherry. Thus we successfully labelled a proportion LRCs which could potentially be ablated by treatment with ganciclovir (GCV), thereby enabling ablation in proliferating cells in postnatal NP. Unfortunately GCV treatment could not eliminate mCherry-expressing NP cells at P14. Because the length of time needed (more than 1 year) and exhaustion of resources we were unable to continue to label the slow-cycling cells with the doxycycline diet, to study the abundance and behavior of the label-retaining cells after early postnatal NP proliferative cell ablation. 3. Population dynamics, lineage trajectories and molecular attributes, of cycling cells in the NP during IDD. Identification of progenitors in the NP that are lost with disc degeneration. To determine the abundance of LRCs in disc degeneration we employed the 13del premature IDD model mice in which premature degeneration is observed at 6 months. We labelled LRCs by crossing 13del mice with R26-rtTA; TetO-H2B-GFP label-retaining gene carrying mice. We performed a pulse-chase cell proliferation assay and found significantly fewer GFP-label retaining cells in the 13del mutant mouse NP at disc level T8/9. These results point to a loss of LRCs during disc degeneration. To aid the identification of putative progenitors we compared the transcriptome signatures of NP populations isolated from non-degenerated and degenerated discs of human and mouse. We identified cells expressing a set of genes associated with progenitors and Brachyury (T) that were preferentially associated with non-degenerated NP in both mouse and human. These cells were characterised by Tagln, which is associated with skeletal stem cells and were located in the peripheral region of the NP. Lineage tracing using Tagln-CreERt2 mice, showed that these cells, termed PeriNP Tagln+ cells, could differentiate and populate the entire NP during development and growth and were diminished with aging and in injury-induced IDD. We found the PeriNP Tagln+ cells were derived from the notochord using a notochord-specific Foxa2mNE-Cre mouse (Foxa2mNE-Cre;R26RTd/+) and were actively proliferating. These cells were positive for Ki67 (Ki67+ cells) and were labelled by BrdU and EdU double-labeling assays. To determine the molecular signature of PeriNP cells and gain insights into the mechanisms, we analysed the molecular signatures of single-cells by RNA-seq on the lumbar and proximal tail IVDs of Tagln-CreERt2;R26RTd/+ mice, which were treated with tamoxifen at P5 stage and collected at P10 and 8-week stages. We identified 4 and 7 cell populations at P10 and 8 weeks respectively that were derived from PeriNP cells. These analyses suggested a maturation path from PeriNP towards the centre of the NP controlled by the TGF-β pathways. Notochord specific removal of TGF-β/BMP mediator Smad4 caused a loss of Tagln+ cells and abnormal NP development. Taken together studies have identified a population of proliferating Tagln+ PeriNP cells which are potential progenitors crucial for the healthy NP.

17126119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126119.value: Nucleus pulposus (NP) cells in the disc are derived from the embryonic notochord. Knowledge of NP progenitors and their contribution to the maintenance of a healthy NP is limited. In humans many notochord like cells (NCLs) are present in the NP after birth but these reduce rapidly with age and few remain during adolescence. In the adult NP there is a reduction of NCLs that coincides with the age-onset of Intervertebral Disc Disease (IDD). NCLs could therefore represent a pool of NPC progenitors that serve to maintain NP function and protect against IDD. Loss of progenitors of the NP in the IVD could be the underlying cause. In this project we aimed to identify, characterise potential progenitors in the NP and gain insight into their role in maintaining a healthy disc. In adult tissues, infrequently dividing cells (slow cycling, SCy) are long-lived “stem” cells that generate rapidly dividing (fast cycling), short-lived progenitor cells. Both fast cycling and slow cycling stem cell populations can also produce unique differentiated lineages. We tested for SCy cells (label retaining cells, LRCs) in mice by H2B-GFP retention analysis in which dilution of H2B-GFP with cell division is used as an indicator of the speed of cell division and the GFP signal is retained preferentially in LRCs. We studied the global transcriptomic changes that occur in postnatal day 10 and 8 week old NP cells. By single cell transcriptomics we found considerable cell heterogeneity in the adult mouse NP, with both fast cycling and slow cycling cells being present. Comparing mouse and human datasets, cycling NP cells expressing mitotic genes were present in both, suggesting cell proliferation occurs in adolescent NPs. By lineage tracing in mice we identified a population of cycling Tagln+ cells located in the periphery of the NP (PeriNP cells) which are potential progenitors that contribute to the whole NP. Tagln+ cells and their descendants were diminished in aged NP or puncture-induced disc degeneration. To determine the abundance of LRCs in disc degeneration we employed the 13del premature IDD model mice in which premature degeneration is observed at 6 months. We labelled LRCs by crossing 13del mice with R26-rtTA; TetO-H2B-GFP label-retaining gene carrying mice. And used pulse-chase cell proliferation assays in mice. We found significantly fewer GFP-label retaining cells in the 13del mutant mouse NP at disc level T8/9. These results point to a loss of LRCs during disc degeneration.

17126119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126119.value: The identification of proliferating progenitors maintained by TGFbeta and Notch signaling, that go on to populate the entire NP but are lost during disc degeneration, has significant implications for the future development of therapeutic approaches for IDD. In the future important questions to be answered are a) additional signaling pathways and factors that are critical for maintaining these NP progenitors; b) identifying molecules/factors that may be used to reprogramming cells within the degenerated NP. Screens for small molecules that can be used to maintain NP cells in the young state or reprogramme cells in the degenerated NP may be used,

17126119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126119.value: The intervertebral disc (IVD) acts as a shock-absorber in the spine. In the core of the IVD, the nucleus pulposus (NP), plays a critical role in combatting the degeneration of the disc that leads to back pain. In humans many cells morphologically similar to embryonic precursors (NCLs) are present in the NP after birth but these reduce rapidly with age and few remain during adolescence. In the adult NP, the reduction of NCLs and appearance of myofibroblast-like cells in human NP coincides with the age-onset of Intervertebral Disc Disease (IDD) in which functional capacity of the disc declines and is associated with back pain. Loss of progenitors of the NP in the IVD could be the underlying cause. In this study we aimed to identify populations of NP progenitors that could serve to maintain NP function and homeostasis and protect against IDD. We focused on creating an in vivo model in which the proliferating progenitors can be identified. Using a pulse and chase method in which NP progenitors would be labelled we identified slowly cycling cells in the NP and studied the transcriptomic changes that occur, as the early NP matures. We found a reduction of these slow cycling cells in a premature IDD mouse model mice. Intriguingly we found TAGLN (transgelin), in combination with the notochordal marker T, were preferentially localized in the peripheral boundary of the NP (PeriNP). Lineage analyses mice showed that in the postnatal NP, the majority of cells were derived from PeriNP Tagln+ cells. The PeriNP cells were proliferative and could differentiate into the central NP (CentNP). These Tagln+ cells and their descendants were diminished in aged NP or puncture-induced disc degeneration. PeriNP Tagln+ and slow cycling cells may be NP progenitors that contribute to the maintenance of a healthy disc.

17126319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126319.value: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) can lead to a diversity of problems including low back pain and sciatica as two very painful symptomatic outcomes. It is a leading burden in community heath for quality of life in an ageing population globally. Currently, there are no biological treatments for IDD, and surgical interventions are salvage procedures when function of the disc has failed, and the defective disc is removed, and the vertebral segments are either fused, or an artificial disc is implanted. While there are environment factors such as life style and ageing will contribute to an accelerated outcome, studies have shown that genetic has a major effect with an hereditary index up to 70% from familial and twin studies. While a goal in genetic studies is to identify risk factors that will provide vital clues to the cause of the disease, finding protective factors are equally, if not more important, from a therapeutic perspective. There are indeed “super normal” individuals in our population who are protected against the strong effect of aging from IDD. However, to study the genetics of these individuals is limited from small size cohort of the super-normal individuals. Here, we will take advantage of a mouse model that we have generated, expressing a known human genetic risk factor, ASPN, in the mouse disc, causing cellular and extracellular matrix changes consistent with degeneration. Importantly, when breed into the genetic background of a super healer mouse strain, LG/J, the degenerative process is minimized or prevented, and the underlying reason must be related to the genetic variants in key genes/pathways the LG/J mice conferring such a protection. Together, these mouse models provide an ideal opportunity to map/decipher the genes providing the protective effect, and aim to perform a linkage study using these mice to decipher the protective factors for a human risk factor for IDD, ASPN. We will also use state-of-the-art next generation sequencing for genetic mapping, combining with single cell RNA sequencing to understand the impact on cellular outcomes; thus providing mechanistic insights, correlating protective genetic variations to IDD outcomes for discovering potential new therapeutic strategies. 椎間盤退化（IDD）可導致多種健康問題，包括下背痛和坐骨神經痛等痛症。這些症狀為全球老化人口帶來社區健康及生活質素的負面影響。可惜目前沒有針對IDD的有效治療，病人只能接受以手術移除退化的椎間盤再將椎骨接合或者植入人造椎間盤。雖然生活習慣或自然衰老等環境因素均會加劇病情，但家族及雙胞胎研究顯示遺傳因素佔了70%的發病比重。在遺傳學研究中，找出「風險因素」目的在於提供成病的線索，但另一方面，找出「保護因素」對治療角度來說是同樣或者更為重要。在我們當中，「超級正常」人士確實存在，他們能免除於自然衰老而導致的IDD。可惜此類人士為數不多，局限了相關的遺傳學研究。在這項目中，我們在小鼠的椎間盤中表達風險因子ASPN，以導致細胞和細胞外基質形成IDD狀態。但當把牠們繁殖到「超級癒合」品系LG / J時，IDD的形成被減低或者防止了，顯示了預防IDD的機制跟LG / J的遺傳背景差異有關。我們的小鼠模型提供了破解預防疾病基因的重要契機。此項目旨在利用遺傳連鎖分析以理解IDD風險因子ASPN的相對保護因子。我們將使用最先進的新一代測序進行遺傳作圖，結合單細胞RNA測序來了解因子對細胞的影響。從而理解病理機制，找出遺傳密碼中保護性變異與IDD的聯繫，以提供新的治療策略。

17126519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126519.value: Chondrosarcoma is the second most prevalent malignance of bone after osteosarcoma and represents around 26% of all primary bone cancers. There are currently no clear molecular marker for chondrosarcoma and diagnosis is made based on histologic characteristic such as invasiveness, replicative activity, cellularity and matrix change. In addition to chondrosarcoma there are enchondroma and osteochondroma are the benign cartilaginous tumours. Importantly, enchondroma and osteochondroma could give rise to conventional central and peripheral chondrosarcoma. While conventional chondrosarcoma could give rise to aggressive dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma. Therefore, development of a clear molecular marker for chondrosarcoma could lead to early detection of malignant change resulting in early intervention to improve the outcome of patients suffering from chondrosarcoma. Therapeutic strategies for chondrosarcoma have not been significantly improved in the past decades. Wide local resection with limb salvage surgery or amputation which are associated with high level of disability and morbidity for the patients are currently the main treatment for chondrosarcoma. Furthermore, chondrosarcoma are thought to be resistant to chemotherapy and radiotherapy since neoplastic chondrocytes are enveloped by cartilage matrix which is a nature barrier for the diffusion of drugs. In addition, lower proliferation rate attributes to insensitivity of chondrosarcoma to most of conventional drugs targeting DNA replication. Therefore there is a significant need for the development of new treatment strategies for the treatment of chondrosarcoma. The current proposal is the first to show single-cell transcriptomic data of chondrosarcoma and have reveal key information regarding distinct sub-populations of cells found within chondrosarcoma based on their transcriptome. In this proposal, we plan to do scRNA-Seq on different grade of chondrosarcoma, enchondroma, human foetal femur derived skeletal stem cells and chondrocytes aimed to develop a set of molecular markers for the diagnosis and grading of chondrosarcoma. Second, we propose to interrogate the functional significance of the THY1+ cell population found in our scRNA-seq analysis using mouse xenograft model. Finally, we plan to explore the role of FGF7 in the development and progression of chondrosarcoma in vitro by using siRNA against FGF7 and recombinant FGF7 in THY1+ and THY1- cells found in chondrosarcoma to inform new treatment strategies for chondrosarcoma. This study will contribute to the development of new diagnostic and treatment strategies and in turn improve the outcome for patients suffering from chondrosarcoma. 軟骨肉瘤是繼骨肉瘤後的第二大骨骼惡性腫瘤，約佔所有原發性骨癌的26％。目前對於軟骨肉瘤沒有明確的分子標記，其診斷基於組織學特徵（例如，侵襲性，複製活性，細胞性和基質變化）。除軟骨肉瘤外，內生軟骨瘤和骨軟骨瘤是良性軟骨腫瘤。內生軟骨瘤和骨軟骨瘤會分別演變成傳統的中央和外周軟骨肉瘤。而傳統的軟骨肉瘤可能會進一步形成侵襲性去分化軟骨肉瘤。因此，開發明確的軟骨肉瘤分子標誌物可以在早期發現惡性變化，進行早期干預，從而改善患軟骨肉瘤的患者的預後。 在過去的幾十年中，軟骨肉瘤的治療策略沒有得到顯著改善。目前，對於患有軟骨肉瘤的主要治療方法是廣泛的局部切除術與肢體搶救手術或截肢相關，這些治療方法會導致患者高度殘疾和高複發率。此外，軟骨肉瘤被認為對化學療法和放射療法具有抗性，因為腫瘤軟骨細胞被軟骨基質包裹，軟骨基質是藥物擴散的天然屏障。此外，較低的增殖率歸因於軟骨肉瘤對大多數靶向DNA複製的常規藥物的不敏感性。因此，有必要開髮用於治療軟骨肉瘤的新治療策略。 本研究首次顯示軟骨肉瘤的單細胞轉錄組數據，並基於其轉錄組揭示了軟骨肉瘤中的不同細胞亞群的關鍵信息。我們計劃對不同等級的軟骨肉瘤，內生軟骨瘤，胚胎來源的骨骼幹細胞和軟骨細胞進行單細胞轉錄組測試，旨在尋找一套用於軟骨肉瘤診斷和分級的分子標記物。其次，我們建議使用小鼠異種移植模型研究我們在單細胞轉錄組的分析中發現的THY1+ 細胞群的功能。最後，我們計劃通過在軟骨肉瘤中發現的THY1+ 和THY1- 細胞中使用FGF7的siRNA和重組FGF7來體外研究FGF7在軟骨肉瘤發展和進展中的作用，以為軟骨肉瘤的新治療策略提供信息。該研究將有助於開發新的診斷和治療策略，從而改善患有軟骨肉瘤的患者的治疗。
