17126519.value: 1. To characterize different histological grade of chondrosarcoma using scRNA-seq technology. (100%) We generated the first single-cell atlas of chondrosarcoma, using samples from six cartilage tumors and one chondroblastic osteosarcoma. This cell atlas consists of eight cell clusters: six neoplastic cell clusters (Chon1, Chon2, High1, High2, Cos, and Prol), a Leukocyte (Leuk) cluster, and a Stromal (Stro) cluster (Fig. 1-3). To compare chondrosarcoma cells with developing chondrocytes, we have generated scRNAseq data on one human fetal femur containing chondrocytes at different developmental stages (Fig.4). For well-differentiated cartilage tumors, including benign, low, and medium-grade tumors, the neoplastic cells are enriched in two identified populations: Chon1 and Chon2. Cells in the Chon1 clusters resembles resting chondrocytes from the fetal femur, while Chon2 cells was found in low to medium histological grade chondrosarcoma (Fig.5). These data suggest cells in Chon1 and Chon2 clusters is involved in the malignant transformation from benign cartilage tumor to chondrosarcoma. A new batch of cartilage tumor samples collected after the COVID pandemic further supports the presence of Chon2 cells in malignant cartilage tumors (Fig. 6). Differential gene expression analysis between Chon2 and Chon1 identified potential markers for malignant transformation in chondrosarcomas (Fig. 5-6). High-grade tumor cells are clustered by patient, indicating high inter-tumoral heterogeneity. The unique clustering of the high-grade chondrosarcoma sample suggest little to no resemblance to chondrocytes and could have undergone de novo tumorigenesis (Fig. 7). In addition to neoplastic cells found in our chondrosarcoma samples, a diverse stromal cell population consisting of cancer-associated fibroblasts (THY1+ cells), endothelial cells, macrophages, T cells, osteoclasts, vascular smooth muscle cells, and aberrant chondrocytes was also characterized (Fig. 8-9). In summary, we performed single-cell transcriptomics analysis on nine cartilage tumors of varying grades, one chondroblastic osteosarcoma, and one fetal femur sample to characterize intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneities. 2. To perform functional characterization of a progenitor-like cell population expressing THY1 found in chondrosarcoma in vitro. (100%) The presence of THY1+ cells was validated in primary tumor tissues and primary cell culture samples from a low-grade chondrosarcoma L28 (Fig. 10). THY1+ cells have a higher proliferation rate than THY1- cells in primary cell culture (Fig. 11a). As a result, the proportion of THY1- cells dramatically decreased in passage 1 (10%) compared to passage 0 (60%) and eventually disappeared in later passages (Fig. 11b). We further examined THY1+ cells in three additional chondrosarcomas. Immunocytochemistry staining of primary tumor cell cultures confirmed the presence of both THY1+ and THY1- cells (Fig. 12a). EdU proliferation assays showed that THY1+ cells had a higher proliferation index compared to THY1- cells (Fig. 12b). These observations suggest that monolayer cell culture can effectively enrich THY1+ cells for further study. 3. To perform functional analysis of progenitor cell population in vivo using mouse human xenograft model. (100%) To investigate whether THY1+ cells are progenitor cells that can give rise to a tumor in vivo, we injected primary cancer cells from different passages into NOD SCID mice. Only P0 cells were able to generate a xenograft in the mouse model (Fig. 13a), while later passages enriched for THY1+ cells failed to develop a tumor. This data suggests THY1+ cells cluster did not contain neoplastic cells but rather tumor associated stromal cells. To further investigate the nature of THY1+ cell population, we generated patient-derived xenograft (PDX) mouse models using primary tumor tissues from three chondrosarcoma samples (Fig. 13b). We performed single-cell analysis on the third generation of the L44 tumor. The results revealed that THY1+ cells (which turned out to be cancer-associated fibroblasts; CAF) of human origin were not detected in the xenograft from the PDX mouse model. Instead, the THY1+ cells (CAF) found in the xenograft originated from the mouse (Fig. 14, 15). In conclusion, THY1+ cells were not essential for the development of chondrosarcomas in vivo, indicating that THY1+ cells are not progenitor-like cells for the development of chondrosarcoma. 4. To examine the role of fibroblast growth factor pathways on the development and pathogenesis of chondrosarcoma. (0%) The decision to shift focus from examining fibroblast growth factor (FGF) related mechanisms in chondrosarcoma was primarily driven by a strategic redirection in response to emerging scientific knowledge. In 2020, a substantial body of research on single-cell studies in various primary cancers was published, revealing that the THY1+ cluster in chondrosarcoma shared strikingly similar expression profiles with cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) observed in other cancer types. This resemblance prompted a pivotal realization that the THY1+ cluster may not be unique to chondrosarcoma and could represent a more broadly recognized component of the tumor microenvironment in multiple cancer types. Therefore, to maximize the research's potential impact and relevance, the decision was made to shift the research focus toward developing a prognostic model and exploring the complex area of chondrosarcoma metastasis, where the findings could have broader applicability and therapeutic implications for a wider range of cancer patients. This strategic pivot underscores the adaptability and responsiveness of the research team to the evolving landscape of scientific knowledge and the dynamic nature of cancer research. Additional objective 1. Establishing a prognostic model based on single cell signature of Stro, Leuk, and Pro. (100%) We analyzed a large publicly available bulk microarray dataset consisting of 88 chondrogenic tumor samples to validate and support the cell type definitions identified in our chondrosarcoma and benign enchondroma samples. Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) analysis stratified patients into five robust groups based on the single-cell signature composition of proliferating cell populations (i.e., Prol) and tumor stromal cells (i.e., Stro and Leuk), generating a prognostic model. In this model, we were able to stratify patients with benign, low, and medium-grade tumors, whose gradings are subject to interobserver variability, into two groups with distinct clinical outcomes for clinical decision-making (Fig. 16). Furthermore, the novel prognostic model provides molecular insights into patients stratified into different groups, allowing for further mechanistic studies (Fig. 17). Additional objective 2. Chondrosarcoma metastasis. (100%) Both HA15 and ISRIB compounds were used to conduction functional analysis of the ER stress pathway, demonstrated the ability to influence cell viability at 24 and 48 hours, marking their potential significance in chondrosarcoma treatment. RT-qPCR analysis of ER stress and metastasis-related genes revealed distinct patterns in high-grade versus low-grade chondrosarcoma, with lower ER stress levels but upregulated MMP2 and MMP9 genes in high-grade cases. HA15 was found to induce ER stress, especially in low-grade chondrosarcoma, with a higher sensitivity to HA15-induced ER stress and potential implications for promoting cell migration through the RAC1/ROCK1 pathway. Conversely, ISRIB acted to inhibit global ER stress-related genes in both low and high-grade chondrosarcoma. Moreover, this study demonstrated that changes in ER stress could significantly affect the migration of chondrosarcoma cell lines, with HA15-induced ER stress promoting migration while ISRIB restrained it. In vivo imaging of SW1353 PDX orthotopic models further underscored the role of HA15-induced ER stress in promoting metastasis. These findings illuminate the intricate interplay between ER stress and chondrosarcoma metastasis, offering valuable insights for potential therapeutic strategies and highlighting the need for further investigation (Fig. 18).

17126519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126519.value: Zezhuo Su, Joshua Ho, Raymond Yau, YingLee Lam, Tony Shek, Maximus Yeung, Hongtai Chen, Richard Oreffo, Kathryn S. E. Cheah, Kelvin S. C. Cheung. Single cell analysis reveals endoplasmic reticulum stress as a marker for malignant transformation in chondrosarcoma. Communications Biologist. (IF: 6.3; Top 13%; Under miner revision; 2/3 reviewers accepted) Major Findings and Research Outcome 1. Single-Cell Atlas of Chondrosarcoma: We achieved a groundbreaking milestone by constructing the first single-cell atlas of chondrosarcoma. This atlas encompassed a diverse array of cell populations, offering a comprehensive view of the disease's cellular landscape. Notably, we identified and characterized various cell populations in benign, low, medium, and high-grade tumors. This accomplishment has provided a critical framework for understanding chondrosarcoma, unraveling the complexity of different tumor grades, and discerning intra- and inter-tumor heterogeneities. The single-cell atlas serves as a valuable resource for researchers worldwide, facilitating further investigations into chondrosarcoma's pathogenesis and potential therapeutic targets. 2. Prognostic Model for Chondrosarcoma: The development of a prognostic model marks a significant advancement in the clinical management of chondrosarcoma. Leveraging single-cell signatures of Stromal, Leukocyte, and Proliferative cell populations, we successfully stratified patients with benign, low, and medium-grade tumors into distinct groups with divergent clinical outcomes. This model holds great promise for enhancing clinical decision-making and personalizing treatment strategies for chondrosarcoma patients. Furthermore, it provides valuable molecular insights into the patient subgroups, offering a foundation for further mechanistic investigations and the development of targeted therapies. 3. Chondrosarcoma Metastasis Insights: Our research delved into the intricate mechanisms governing chondrosarcoma metastasis. Notably, we discovered that compounds HA15 and ISRIB influenced cell viability, indicating their potential significance in chondrosarcoma treatment. We unveiled distinct gene expression patterns in high-grade and low-grade chondrosarcoma related to ER stress and metastasis. The study showcased that HA15-induced ER stress could promote cell migration, particularly in low-grade chondrosarcoma, revealing its potential implications in metastasis through the RAC1/ROCK1 pathway. Conversely, ISRIB demonstrated the ability to inhibit global ER stress-related genes in both high and low-grade chondrosarcoma. In vivo imaging of SW1353 PDX orthotopic models underscored the role of HA15-induced ER stress in enhancing metastasis. These findings shed light on the intricate interplay between ER stress and chondrosarcoma metastasis, providing valuable insights for potential therapeutic strategies. This research not only deepens our understanding of chondrosarcoma but also emphasizes the need for further exploration of the molecular mechanisms governing metastasis and potential therapeutic interventions. In conclusion, our research has significantly advanced the field of chondrosarcoma by creating a foundational single-cell atlas, developing a prognostic model, and shedding light on the complex mechanisms underlying metastasis. These findings collectively offer hope for improved diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes for chondrosarcoma patients, while also opening up new avenues for further research and therapeutic development in the field.

17126519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126519.value: The findings from this research open up several exciting avenues for further development and exploration in the field of chondrosarcoma. To capitalize on these discoveries, the following proposed course of action should be considered: 1. Refinement of Prognostic Model: Further refinement and validation of the prognostic model can enhance its accuracy and clinical applicability. This involves expanding the patient cohort for validation and incorporating additional molecular markers for a more comprehensive assessment of patient outcomes. 2. Mechanistic Studies: In-depth mechanistic studies are warranted to understand the precise role of ER stress and metastasis-related genes in chondrosarcoma progression. Investigating the pathways through which HA15 and ISRIB influence these processes can provide valuable insights for targeted therapeutic interventions. 3. Therapeutic Development: Building on the knowledge gained about compounds like HA15 and ISRIB, research can focus on the development of novel therapeutic agents targeting ER stress and metastasis in chondrosarcoma. Pre-clinical and clinical trials should be explored for their efficacy and safety. 4. Single-Cell Atlas Expansion: Expanding the single-cell atlas to include a larger and more diverse dataset of chondrosarcoma samples can offer a deeper understanding of the disease's heterogeneity and may reveal additional cell populations or therapeutic targets. 5. Patient-Derived Models: Establishing patient-derived models that closely mimic the in vivo microenvironment of chondrosarcoma can aid in testing potential therapies and studying tumor behavior in a more clinically relevant context. In conclusion, the potential for further development in chondrosarcoma research is promising, with opportunities to refine diagnostic and prognostic tools, uncover molecular mechanisms, and advance therapeutic strategies. This multi-pronged approach can significantly contribute to improved patient outcomes and the ultimate goal of finding effective treatments for chondrosarcoma.

17126519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126519.value: This research project focused on understanding the 2nd most common and challenging bone cancer called chondrosarcoma. Think of it as creating a detailed map of the cancer's inner workings. We discovered that chondrosarcoma isn't just one type of cancer but has different "grades" like high and low, and these are like different neighborhoods in the map. We also found a way to predict how chondrosarcoma patients might do, which is like having a weather forecast for your disease. This helps doctors make better decisions about treatment. One exciting discovery is about two special medicines, HA15 and ISRIB. These medicines affect how the cancer cells act. We learned that HA15 can make cancer cells move around more, which is not good, while ISRIB can calm them down, which is better. This research is vital because it provides hope for better treatments and personalized care for chondrosarcoma patients. It's like finding the keys to unlock the secrets of this cancer and gives us a brighter path towards improving the lives of those affected by it.

17126819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126819.value: Lung cancer is one of the most common cancer with high mortality rate in developed countries. At the time of presentation with symptoms, most of the cases are already in advanced stage. Even for earlier stage, recurrence rate is high after resection. A significant portion of patients are not eligible for surgical resection due to age, comorbidity, or suboptimal lung function. Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is the most common type of lung cancer. Medical treatment is stratified by the presence of targeted mutations such as EGFR or ALK – patients with targetable genetic changes would receive tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), with an initial response rate in the range of 70-80% and median profession-free survival (PFS) around 10 to 18 months. For patients who develop resistance later to available TKIs, the standard treatment is chemotherapy. Yet most patients don’t respond well and their condition rapidly deteriorate. Immunotherapy with anti-PD1 antibody is a breakthrough therapy for metastatic lung cancer. For NSCLC without targetable mutations, especially tumors that harbour PDL1 overexpression, it has superior efficacy compared with traditional chemotherapy. Immunotherapy as single agent, however, did not show benefit in NSCLC with targetable mutation. A recently published paper showed that addition of immunotherapy atezolizumab to bevacizumab and chemotherapy significantly improved PFS (hazard ratio (HR) 0.62, p<0.001). This study included patient with EGFR or ALK genetic alteration. Subgroup analysis demonstrated a HR of 0.59 in these patients. Although this is a small group of patients within this study, it becomes the first preliminary evidence that anti-VEGF agent and chemotherapy might potentiate the response of immunotherapy in NSCLC patients with targetable mutations. EGFR mutation is found in around 20% of NSCLC in Western population, yet its prevalence is as high as 50% among Asian lung cancer patients. Developing better treatment strategy for NSCLC patients after failure of standard TKIs is an imminent need especially in this locality. This is a phase 2 study aiming to explore the preliminary efficacy of combination immunotherapy pembrolizumab with anti-VEGF lenvatinib with chemotherapy in NSCLC patients with EGFR or ALK mutations refractory to standard targeted therapy. 非小細胞肺癌是最常見的肺癌，大部份病人在確診時已經是第四期；早期確診的病人，術後復發的機會也大；這是一個死亡率很高的癌症。今天，肺癌的治療可以按其基因變異分類 - 有EGFR或ALK變異的可以用口服TKI標靶；沒有基因變異的，可以考慮使用免疫療法或化療；在西方國家，有EGFR或ALK變異的肺癌只佔20%，但在亞洲，這類肺癌佔了大概50%；很多研究已經指出當這些肺癌對TKI標靶產生抗藥性，單一免疫治療或者化療的療效都不太理想；對這類病人，尋求更有效的療法已是刻不容緩。 去年有一個臨床研究混合免疫療法Anti-PD1，抗血管單抗及化療。小組分析發現這組合對帶EGFR或ALK變異的肺癌有不錯的療效；從治療其他腫瘤的經驗也指出，抗血管類標靶藥或可提升免疫療法的效能，加上前期研究亦指出新一代抗血管類TKI標靶藥對EGFR抗藥性有一定作用，這些口服抗血管類TKI標靶藥或許是抗血管標靶更好的選擇。有見及此，本第二期臨床研究將探討混合免疫療法pembrolizumab，抗血管TKI lenvatinib 及化療對EGFR/ALK標靶抗藥性非小細胞肺癌的治療作用。

17126819.label: Realisation of objectives
17126819.value: First, Dr. Chiu (original PI) had a change in contract to practice track with HKU, thus a change in grant holder to Dr. Ho (original co-I) was initiated and approved by October 2020 with retrospective effective date on 1 February 2020. With the unprecedented impact of COVID-19 pandemic right at the initiation of this grant in early 2020, our subsequent preparatory work for the start of this clinical trial was severely delayed. The arrangement of tumour assessment imaging in the public hospital setting was deemed not feasible especially with the priority of the health care system in tackling COVID waves in Hong Kong. We also failed to secure hospital support in providing imaging service via special radiology research project due to extreme shortage of manpower in Radiology Department. Eventually, special arrangement with private radiology vendors was established in which trial subjects would need to bear the cost of imaging unless financially constrained. In this investigator-initiated clinical trial, we obtained initial interest from pharmaceutical company in providing free trial medications (pembrolizumab and lenvatinib) at the time of grant application, otherwise the budget would exceed the grant limit. Upon approval of this grant, a full study protocol was drafted and submitted to the company on 6th March 2020. Subsequent rounds of comments and amendments of the study protocol were severely delayed as a result of global impact of COVID-19 pandemic on closing overseas offices and absence from work. Final study protocol was approved on 20th February 2021. Similarly, shipment of study drugs was delayed for more than 6 months, with the first batch only arrived in mid-October, 2021. Unfortunately, the 5th wave of COVID-19 in Hong Kong had paralyzed the health care system for the first 6 months of 2022, making our subject recruitment for this trial even more challenging. With the approved extension of grant period, we have at least achieved partially our set objectives. The primary objective was to explore the efficacy of combining pembrolizumab, lenvatinib and chemotherapy in patients with advanced stage NSCLC harbouring sensitizing EGFR or ALK genetic aberration after failure of standard targeted therapy. The initial stage of the research plan was to recruit 15 patients treated with this investigational regimen to decide whether there was sufficient efficacy signal to proceed further. Despite the significant aforementioned hurdles, we recruited 18 patients, though only 13 were deemed eligible according to trial criteria, and 9 were evaluable for treatment response so far (data cut by 27 May 2023). Over one quarter of the screened patients could not join this trial due to the presence of brain metastases (pre-defined exclusion criterion). We could have re-screened them after completing radiotherapy for brain metastases. Nonetheless the public health care system could not provide timely radiotherapy treatment and many of these patients lost to follow-up eventually due to disease deterioration. Besides the 3 patients who had complications due to disease after cycle 1 treatment, the rest of the patients remained on study. We did not encounter fast and deep responses among our subjects, but many had rather durable stable disease on radiologic reassessments. More follow-up time will be needed to determine the true best responses in these patients. Though we have not yet completed this part as per the original research plan, we believe our current data has already given us very good insight into the efficacy of this novel regimen (see details under “Major findings and research outcome”). Since we are continuing our efforts in this clinical trial beyond the expiry of this GRF funding period, the initial efforts supported by this research grant will substantially contribute to the overall investigation of this novel treatment regimen. Our experience with recruited trial patients who received at least the first cycle of this novel treatment regimen (intent-to-treat population) would allow us sufficient evaluation of the toxicity and tolerability of this regimen (the secondary objective). We had 3 drop-out subjects after cycle 1. These patients had significant disease burden and the chemotherapy in this regimen might impose them with extra stress. However, all other patients continued dosing without much complaint. We consider this regimen being a safe and tolerable combination (details refer to “Major findings and research outcome”).

17126819.value: From Oct 2021 to May 2023 (i.e. 19 months), a total of 18 patients were screened, in which 5 (27.8%) were deemed screen failures due to significant brain metastasis. Thirteen patients received the first dose of the study treatment (median age 64 yrs, 7 females). Most had EGFR mutations (92%, n=12) and 1 with ALK-rearrangement (8%). Three patients aborted further treatment after dosing of cycle 1 due to disease-related complications. A total of 85 cycles of treatment were given to the evaluable patients. Nine patients received at least 2 cycles and had at least the first radiological reassessment – 2 patients had partial response (PR), 1 had stable disease (SD) as the best response, and 6 were still on treatment with preliminary stable disease on radiological assessment. One patient stopped treatment due to immune-related nephritis (grade 2) and treatment was stopped after 9 months and proved to have disease progression after 12 months. Median follow-up was 7 months. Nine patients were still on treatment at the time of this report. The duration of treatment so far ranged from 1 – 13 months. As of the data cutoff by the end of May 2023, there were no complete response, 2 partial responses (22%), 1 stable disease (11%), and 6 remained on treatment pending further assessment out of a total of 9 evaluable subjects. The objective response rate is 22% up to data cutoff. Adverse events (AEs) were evaluated in all patients who had received at least 1 dose of the study drugs. There were 6 grade 3 or above AEs – vomiting (n=1), poor oral intake (n=1), pleural effusion (n=2) (these were unrelated to study drugs), neutropenia (n=1) and thrombocytopenia (n=1). For those who tolerated cycle 1 treatment, the majority could continue treatment without clinically significant toxicities. Four patients needed interruption or dose reduction of chemotherapy and 2 patients had dose reduction of lenvatinib to 4mg daily. The combination treatment was considered tolerable. There were no treatment-related deaths.

17126819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126819.value: As per our initial statistical calculation in the GRF grant application, at least 6 documented responders out of 15 evaluable cases would indicate potential efficacy signal for further development. We have so far 2 confirmed PRs and 6 patients are having ongoing treatment (tentatively SD as the best response). This clinical trial is ongoing with further subject recruitment. In the remaining evaluable subjects (6 more), one would need 4 responders to reach the bar of being potentially efficacious treatment regimen. Though this is considered unlikely, we will need more time to reach a definitive conclusion on this. Nonetheless, our experience with this regimen supports a safe and tolerable treatment.

17126819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126819.value: While immunotherapy has been proven to be useful in many cancers including lung, its use in those having predominant genetic aberrations (driver oncogenes especially EGFR and ALK) is still controversial or undefined. There is good biological rationale to indicate a potentiating effect on immunotherapy by interrogating tumour-related abnormal blood vessels (i.e. anti-angiogenesis) notably with anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) agent. This research explores the combination of chemotherapy with immunotherapy and anti-angiogenic agent in patients with lung cancers driven by EGFR or ALK alterations. Our results suggested that this combination regimen was well-tolerated in most patients, with demonstrable preliminary clinical activity. Interestingly, although most patients were not rapid responders, many of them appeared to have stable disease since starting treatment. More time is needed to determine the true potential of this regimen. This research was started during COVID-19 pandemic where regular research activities were much affected and delayed. We also did not anticipate more than ¼ of potential candidates having brain metastases at screening thus failed to join this study. It shows not only the challenge of designing clinical research for these patients, but also the challenge of treating these patients in real-world practices as brain metastases are frequent.

17126919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17126919.value: 長期以來，香港特別行政區和中國大陸一直受到新發傳染病的困擾，包括禽流感（H5，H9，H7和H10等多種亞型），沙士疫潮，腸道病毒感染引起的手足口病和最近出現的寨卡病毒感染等。然而，目前針對病毒感染的治療手段仍然有限。它們通常廣譜性較差且效果一般，在病毒抗藥性出現後很快失效。病毒被喻為細胞內的“寄生蟲”，它們必須利用宿主提供的材料和機制來複製病毒自身的遺傳物質，組裝新的病毒顆粒，並破壞宿主細胞的免疫效應。病毒學的一個新興領域是通過短時間內靶向宿主細胞蛋白，而這些宿主蛋白又在病毒生物學中起著關鍵的作用，從而達到控制病毒病特別是急性感染的目的。因此，針對大多數RNA病毒共同使用的宿主蛋白作為藥物靶點，進而開發形成廣譜抗病毒藥物有望成為控制新發傳染病的新策略，並具有更好的臨床前景。 通過轉錄組學和脂質組學聯合分析，我們最近證實了細胞脂質代謝在MERS冠狀病毒 （又稱中東呼吸綜合症病毒）感染後顯著上調。我們接著篩選了一個脂質代謝相關的小分子化合物文庫，進而鑑定了AM580一種有效抑制多種RNA和DNA病毒複製的廣譜抗病毒藥物。 AM580的抗病毒效果在不同細胞系中具有很高的選擇性指數，在小鼠模型和人類類器官模型中具有安全有效的抗MERS和抗流感治療效果。同時，我們還鑑定了甾醇調節元件結合蛋白（SREBPs）, 一種調節細胞脂質穩態的轉錄因子，作為AM580的藥物靶標。重要的是，我們發現SREBPs介導的脂質生物合成與人類病毒感染廣泛相關，並且易受抗病毒藥物的干預。 在這個項目中，我們將繼續探索病毒是如何操縱宿主細胞的生物學網絡來上調SREBP介導的脂質合成，我們將會著重研究MERS冠狀病毒，腸道病毒A71和寨卡病毒。首先，我們將在體外細胞培養和小鼠模型兩個層次全面分析病毒感染所導致的脂肪生成途徑是否上調。其次，我們將進行功能篩選從而鑑定和分析那種病毒蛋白質承擔著激活SREBP介導的脂肪合成的生物學功能。再次，我們將確定所選病毒蛋白是如何誘導SREBP激活的機制。最後，我們將在體外細胞和小鼠模型中評估阻斷SREBP激活對病毒複製的影響。綜上所述，我們的工作將為開發新一代廣譜抗病毒治療提供新的策略和更多的選擇。

17126919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17126919.value: 1. Utilizing three virus species with distinct characteristics, i.e., MERS-CoV, EV-A71 and ZIKV, we have confirmed that up-regulation of lipogenesis pathway have a broad relevance in various virus –infected cell cultures, which are evidenced by accumulation of host lipid droplets and general upregulation of lipogenic genes. We also prioritized HMGCS-Luc reporter gene assay as a tool for detection of SREBP-mediated lipogenesis activation, through which we identified confirmed that MERS-CoV-NSP14, EV-A71-3C and ZIKV-NS3 are the proteins responsible for each virus-induced SREBP activation. 2. In an effort to clarify the mechanism of SREBP activation, we found different viruses may employ distinct mechanisms. In this project, we found that MERS-CoV-NSP14 and ZIKV-NS3 activate SREBP via direct cleavage of the pre-SREBP protein, which is evidenced by an S1P cleavage assay. In the case of EV-A71, however, EV-A71-3C indirectly trigger the S1P cleavage on pre-SREBP that are bridged by ER-stress, which is evidenced by the fact that co-transfection of EV-A71-3C and pro-capsase2 plasmids increase the amount of cleaved caspase-2. 3. We collected a panel of inhibitors that may block SREBP activation, including SREBP processing inhibitor Betulin, S1P specific inhibitor PF-429242, and Caspase2 inhibitor Z-VDVAD-FMK. We tested their antiviral activities against different viruses and found that both PF-429242 and Betulin exhibited broad-spectrum antiviral coverage against MERS-CoV, EV-A71 and ZIKV; whereas Z-VDVAD-FMK was not effective against any of the viruses tested. Subsequently, we performed an antimicrobial synergy testing/checkerboard assay combining the FDA-approved anti-COVID-19 agent remdesivir (GS-5734) and either PF-429242 or Betulin. Our results indicated that both drug compounds can achieve anti-SARS-CoV-2 synergy when combining with remdesivir. It is likely due to the different antiviral modes of action of these drugs, in which remdesivir targets to virus RdRp replication machinery whereas PF-429242 and Betulin targets to host SREBP activation. 4. Because Betulin exhibits very low water solubility (< 0.1 mg/mL), whereas PF429242 dihydrochloride, a dihydrochloride form of PF429242, can achieve good water solubility of 50 mg/mL, we prioritized PF429242 dihydrochloride in the in vivo antiviral experiment. Our results showed that intraperitoneal injection of 30 mg/kg/day PF429242 dihydrochloride from 0dpi to 5dpi would improve ZIKV-infected A129 mice survival from 0% to 50%; whereas the same regimen could cause delayed death of MERS-CoV-infected hDPP4 mice with 2 more days of median survival.

17126919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17126919.value: 1. PF429242 might be reformulated or modified for better antiviral potency and bioavailability. 2. PF429242 shall be considered for broader antiviral evaluation against other medically important viruses such as influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2 and Respiratory Syncytial Virus, in vitro and in vivo.

17126919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17126919.value: Viruses are obligate intracellular parasites and require aspects of host cell to replicate their genetic material and assemble new virus particles. An emerging area in virology is to transiently target host cell proteins that play critical proviral roles in virus biology, especially for acute infections. Therefore, a broad-spectrum antiviral drug targeting against a host protein used by most RNA viruses would be strategic for epidemic control and early treatment with better clinical outcome. In this project, we established how viruses manipulate the host networking to upregulate the SREBP-mediated lipid biosynthesis with focusing on the MERS coronavirus, Enterovirus A71 and Zika virus. We confirmed that up-regulation of lipogenesis pathway have a broad relevance in various virus –infected cell cultures. Mechanistically, MERS-CoV-NSP14 and ZIKV-NS3 proteins activate SREBP via direct cleavage of the pre-SREBP protein, whereas EV-A71-3C indirectly trigger the S1P cleavage on pre-SREBP that are bridged by ER-stress. Importantly, blockade on SREBP activation by a S1P specific inhibitor PF-429242 has been found antiviral effective both in vitro and in mouse models. Our study provides new strategies and lead agents for broad-spectrum antiviral therapy.

17127019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127019.value: 對外來入侵或內部損傷核酸分子的感應是固有免疫中高度保守的防禦機制。哺乳動物細胞的細胞質中的病毒核酸通常由兩類模式識別受體所感應。RNA病毒由RIG-I和MDA5感應，而環鳥腺苷酸(cGAMP)合酶 cGAS則是皰疹病毒等DNA病毒及逆轉錄病毒的主要感應蛋白。RNA與DNA感應蛋白接受刺激後可激活IRF3和NF-B信號通路，調控I型干擾素、干擾素刺激基因及其他細胞因子的表達，以介導抗病毒反應及機體病變。 RNA病毒不能激活cGAS的傳統觀點最近已受到挑戰，作為正鏈RNA病毒的登革病毒已被發現可誘導線粒體DNA釋放到細胞質，從而激活cGAS。此外，cGAS對於帶有正鏈RNA的甲病毒原型辛德比斯病毒（SINV）也會呈現抗病毒活性。cGAS是否可被SINV激活而cGAS又如何發揮抗病毒作用仍有待深入研究。 我們的前期研究結果表明在SINV感染的小鼠細胞中,cGAS mRNA和蛋白在感染的極早期就被誘導產生，而且產生的時相與IFN-β完全不同。正反兩方面的結果都表明cGAS確為限制SINV復制所必需。更值得註意的是，內源性逆轉錄元件的cDNA水平有所升高，導致DNA在細胞質內積聚。確證內源性逆轉錄元件的激活為細胞質cGAS配體的另一個來源，可望為本領域研究帶來另一個觀念性突破。 本項研究將就SINV對cGAS信號轉導通路的激活進行深入研究。首先，我們將闡明SINV誘導cGAS表達的機制，確定I型幹擾素及MAVS等其他信號轉導蛋白的作用，並揭示可誘導cGAS表達的病毒蛋白。其次，我們將研究cGAS激活在SINV感染細胞的生物學作用。cGAMP水平的升高及STING與I型干擾素的必要性可望得到逐一確定。我們也將對SINV和其他RNA病毒進行比較。最後，我們將闡明SINV激活cGAS的機制，分別確定線粒體完整性及線粒體DNA的泄露、cGAS配體的特性，以及對逆轉錄及逆轉錄轉座作用的影響。 本項研究可提供新觀點解釋RNA病毒對cGAS信號傳導通路的激活，不僅可進一步了解病毒與宿主相互作用的原理，也為疫苗及抗病毒藥物的研究提出新的思路。我們的研究結果對自身免疫病也有一定意義。

17127219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17127219.value: The pig is an important farm animal and a useful experimental model for studying human disease due to its physiological and immunological similarity with humans. The pig also holds great potential for testing the safety and efficacy of stem cell application and organ transplantation. Embryonic stem cells have the potential to differentiate to various types of cells and provide cell resources for basic research and clinical applications. Despite mouse and human ESCs have been used in research for many years, the efforts to establish ESCs of most mammalian species, based on the knowledge learned from mouse and human ESCs, have not been very successful. For example, no bona fide pig ESCs are reported even after intensive efforts by the stem cell community. We previously reported that new stem cells, named as expanded potential stem cells or EPSCs, were derived from mouse preimplantation embryos by inhibiting key developmental signals. Specifically, mouse EPSCs are established from 4-cell and 8-cell embryos, have enriched molecular features of these embryo cells and can differentiate to all cell types including trophoblasts. We hypothesized that a similar strategy might be applicable to establishing stem cell lines of other mammalian species. In our preliminary data for this proposal, we have identified via small molecule inhibitor screens the culture conditions that allow us to derive stem cells with robust endogenous pluripotency gene expression from porcine preimplantation embryos. These pig cell culture conditions are essentially the same as mouse EPSCs. The new pig stem cells proliferate robustly in culture, are compatible with efficient genome-editing, and differentiate to various cell lineages once they are returned to pig host preimplantation embryos. Importantly, the pig stem cells have the developmental potential to generate primordial gem cell-like cells and trophoblasts. These cells are thus named pig EPSCs. It is anticipated that pig EPSCs would have broad applications in basic biomedical research and translational medicine, in biotechnology and agriculture. We propose to systematically characterize pig EPSCs, and to use them for studying development and human disease. Specifically, we aim to: 1. systematically analyze pig EPSCs and to better understand their biology 2. derive and characterize pig haploid EPSCs, which can facilitate using the pig in biomedical research in the future 3. use pig EPSCs to investigate normal development and to study human disease specifically inherited cardiovascular diseases 小鼠和人的胚胎幹細胞有多能性，能產生在我們身體裡的所有細胞類型。但經過科學家幾十年的努力，絕大多數的哺乳動物仍然沒有建立真正的胚胎幹細胞。我們在2017年首次建立了小鼠的擴展潛能幹細胞 (EPSCs). 這種新型的胚胎幹細胞不同於現有的幹細胞。 它們具有發育的全能性， 即能產生我們身體裡的所有細胞類型以及胎盤的滋養層細胞。重要的是我們在世界上第一次從豬的著床前胚胎成功的建立豬的擴展潛能幹細胞 (EPSCs). 豬和人在生理和解刨結構及遺傳基因很相似。豬的擴展潛能幹細胞的建立可以讓科學家利用豬來研究人的疾病。豬的擴展潛能幹細胞更可以用於再生醫學研究。 本研究項目計劃近一步研究豬的擴展潛能幹細胞的分子特性和功能。並探討用豬的擴展潛能幹細胞體系，建立豬的單倍體的擴展潛能幹細胞。 單倍體幹細胞將會促進基因編輯和基因功能研究。最後， 我們計畫利用豬的擴展潛能幹細胞研究遺傳性心臟病的分子和細胞機理。

17127219.label: Realisation of objectives
17127219.value: We have substantially optimised the porcine EPSC system so that the system is robust and user-friendly We have studied all three Aims. For Aim one, we have published, submitted and prepared manuscripts on porcine EPSC's molecular identity. On Aim 2, w have derived new EPSC lines from porcine embryos in collaboration with colleagues in Germany since there are no pig embryos to use in Hong Kong. However, the haploid cells are rare and need more efforts to develop a stable system for these cells. We have been using the system to perform multiple rounds of genome-editing which include knock-out four porcine genes and knock in 9 human cDNAs in our ongoing effort to make stem cells for generating xenotransplantation pig donors. This system is still the only stem cell system derived from porcine preimplantation embryos. We have used porcine EPSCs to study gene functions in porcine early development. For example, p53 is an important tumor suppressor genes. However, recent clinical data indicate that the p53 gene might have functions in reproduction but no clear mechanisms are investigated. We find that knocking out p53 in both human and porcine EPSCs causes severe trophoblast defects thus potential placenta problems in pregnancy, revealing an evolutionarily conserved p53 function critical in life. .

We have substantially optimised the porcine EPSC system so that the system is robust and user-friendly. We have been using the system to perform multiple rounds of genome-editing which include knock-out four porcine genes and knock in 9 human cDNAs in our ongoing effort to make stem cells for generating xenotransplantation pig donors. This system is still the only stem cell system derived from porcine preimplantation embryos. We have used porcine EPSCs to study gene functions in porcine early development. For example, p53 is an important tumor suppressor genes. However, recent clinical data indicate that the p53 gene might have functions in reproduction but no clear mechanisms are investigated. We find that knocking out p53 in both human and porcine EPSCs causes severe trophoblast defects thus potential placenta problems in pregnancy, revealing an evolutionarily conserved p53 function critical in life. We have derived new EPSC lines from porcine embryos in collaboration with collaborators in Germany.

17127219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17127219.value: We have submitted a manuscript to Nature Protocols detailing the improved pEPSC system. This manuscript is submitted in parallel with our new human EPSC system manuscript. Importantly, a new PCT was filed by the HKU to cover the IPs of the new porcine and human EPSCs. Our collaborators in the UK (Roslin Institute, Edinburgh) have developed a system to generate macrophages from porcine EPSCs. These stem cell-derived macrophages are being used by several research groups for studying swine virus. We have published additional scientific papers on porcine EPSCs We have been approached by a number of labs around the world for pEPSCs and related reagents.

17127219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17127219.value: The porcine EPSCs carrying the genome edits are being used in in vitro characterization and for generating humanised pigs for xenotransplantation. Since the current finding does not cover the generation of the pigs, we will collaborate with colleagues in Germany and potentially with biotech companies to carry on the project. We develop an efficient protocol to generate blastoids, the blastoscyst-like structures, which will be published in a scientific paper. We will in the future to apply for specific funding for in vivo work.

17127219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17127219.value: The pig is being increasingly used in biomedical research as an in vivo surrogate of human being to study human disease and for testing drug candidates. Moreover, in recent years, pig is being genetically engineered so that the organs can be used for transplantation to patients. This engineering includes removing certain pig genes and adding some human genes. Consequently, organs and cells from this pig can survive and function in a monkey and potentially in the future in a human patient. The major technical challenge in this research field has been lack of suitable pig stem cells to perform the complex genome editing. We are the first one who developed the porcine stem cells called EPSCs. This current funding has enabled us to substantially improve the system and made using them in xenotransplantation a reality. Porcine EPSCs are useful and to some extent critical for studying swine infection which is important for both agriculture and human health (pandemic).

17200019.value: 藉計算光學成像和單光子圖像傳感器實現的低光數字全息技術

17200019.label: Project Objectives
17200019.value: Our first objective is in the demonstration of low-light digital holography. This includes two forms, with coherent light using phase-shifting digital holography, and with incoherent light, using the setup known as Fresnel incoherent correlation holography. We intend to set up the respective imaging systems with dark enclosure, capture data using single-photon image sensors, and reconstruct the holograms of the object. We will also characterize the resulting image quality and investigate techniques for improvement. Our second objective focuses on the computational optical imaging algorithms. We aim to advance the current optimization-based 2D image reconstruction methods to holographic data. In addition, we also target to widen the toolset to include machine learning algorithms. We will investigate different neural network architecture and schemes, and their practical implementations to deliver efficient and powerful methods that reconstruct the hologram from the raw jot data, and furthermore the sectional images of the original object. Our third objective is on extending the low-light digital holography to cater for an inhomogeneous medium in the imaging environment. We aim to advance the computational algorithms, particularly the deep learning methods, to cope with this challenging scenario. Furthermore, we also plan to make the dataset available for the research community to further explore new techniques.

17200019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200019.value: Light enables imaging in the visible spectrum. Low-light level is therefore challenging, and conventional imaging systems with either charge-coupled device (CCD) or complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) image sensors typically result in very noisy images. Imaging in scattering media presents additional difficulties, as light is diffused and does not reach the sensor in a straight path. Nevertheless, this is a realistic scenario if one wants to develop autonomous vehicles that can drive or drones that can fly at night amidst haze, mist, fog, rain, or snow streaks. In vivo biomedical imaging also shares the challenge of imaging with a dim light in an optically inhomogeneous medium, especially as one aims to see more deeply into tissues. In this proposal, we seek not only to enable low-light imaging through a possibly scattering media, but to achieve this in a holographic setting -- capturing the optical wavefront of an object, which allows for three-dimensional reconstruction. Due to differences in application environment, we target to develop low-light digital holography for both coherent and incoherent light source. Our main tools are twofold: one is by utilizing the single-photon image sensor, which is an emergent type of electronic sensor capable of delivering very high sensitivity, even at one photon per pixel. Previously, such sensors have insufficient spatial resolution, but new technologies have shown initial results that are promising for high-speed (and therefore low-light) imaging. The use of single-photon image sensors in digital holography however is a new direction, and can open up novel applications of this sensor technology, such as in holographic microscopy. The second tool is computational optical imaging. Advanced computational algorithms have demonstrated success in reconstructing high-dynamic-range images from data captured with single-photon image sensors, and continuous improvements in the computation further enhance other aspects of the image quality, such as spatial resolution. We aim to leverage on our experience in digital holographic reconstruction and sectioning to develop robust and computationally efficient techniques for use with this new type of electronic sensor. Furthermore, while many reconstruction algorithms are model-based, in recent years data-driven methods involving machine learning become complementary, and in many cases, showing superior performance in image reconstruction tasks. We have an ambitious goal of seeking to harness both model-based and data-driven techniques in order to push low-light holographic imaging for best image quality, toward the ultimate goal of tackling the challenging scattering media environment. 要成像就要有光。因此，低光照水平對成像系統具有挑戰性，而使用傳統的電荷耦合器件或互補式金屬氧化物半導體圖像傳感器通常導致非常嘈雜的圖像。散射介質中的成像存在額外的困難，因為光會擴散而不會以直線路徑到達傳感器。不過，這正是自動駕駛車輛或無人駕駛飛機在陰霾，霧，雨等環境中夜間航行要面對的挑戰。體內生物醫學成像，特別是當人們想要更深入地了解體內組織，也要面對相若的困難。 我們冀望進行研究，不僅在散射介質進行低光成像，更要拍攝全息圖像，好捕獲光的波前，允許三維重建。由於在應用環境的差異，我們的目標是開發低光數字全息用於相干和非相干光源。我們的主要工具有兩個：一個是利用單光子圖像傳感器，能夠提供非常高的靈敏度，即使每像素一個光子也可以。以前，這些傳感器的空間分辨率不足，但新技術顯示結果有望用於高速（因此低光）成像。數字全息術中的單光子圖像傳感器是一個新的方向，可以開闢了這種傳感器技術的新穎應用，例如全息顯微鏡。第二個工具是計算光學成像。先進的計算算法已經在從數據重建用單光子圖像傳感器拍攝高動態範圍圖像方面取得了成功，並持續增強了圖像質量的其他方面，例如空間解析度。我們的目標是利用我們在數字全息重建和切片方面的經驗，開發出穩健且計算效率高的技術。此外，雖然有很多重建算法基於模型，近年來涉及機器學習的數據驅動方法變得互補，並且在許多情況下，在圖像重建中表現優越。我們致力尋求利用基於模型的方法和數據驅動技術，以推動低光全息成像圖像質量，朝著解決具有挑戰性的散射媒體最終目標邁進。

17200019.label: Realisation of objectives
17200019.value: This project consists of 3 objectives: demonstration of low-light digital holography, development of computational optical imaging algorithms, and digital holographic imaging through a challenging inhomogeneous medium. These objectives have been realized with the conclusion of this project. Regarding the first objective, we reported a 50% completion in the mid-term progress report. As explained in that report, we had an inline digital holographic setup and an incoherent optical scanning holography, as well as a light field imaging system, where we had demonstrated their applicability in low-light imaging through the development of advanced computational reconstruction methods. Since then, we have put in significant efforts to investigate the combination with single-photon image sensors for the data capture. As explained in the grant proposal, we anticipated the use of the quanta image sensor (QIS), which at that time was soon to be commercialized. The data captured would be a stack of binary holographic frames, and we endeavored to develop computational reconstruction algorithms to recover the object wavefront. A challenge we encountered was that because of the pandemic and the geopolitical tension between U.S. and China, the sensor was not yet fully commercialized and was not available for our experimentation. Fortunately, we collaborated with a team at Purdue University and overcame this issue. Eventually, we developed what we termed a “photon-starved snapshot holography”, which is a digital holographic imaging system capable of operating at an ultra-low photon level (less than one photon per pixel), with computational methods combining the mathematical imaging model and the data-driven processing, an approach that we called PSHoloNet. The work was presented in the Optica Digital Holography and Three-Dimensional Imaging meeting, and published in the APL Photonics journal (see the list of publications in the section below). The journal selected our work to detail in its highlight, known as Scilight, in May 2023. (“Capturing holographic images in extreme light-starved environments” https://doi.org/10.1063/10.0019363) Regarding the second objective, we reported a 30% completion in the mid-term progress report. As stated in the grant proposal, traditionally holographic reconstruction consists of various optimization-based inverse imaging methods, with major efforts on the design of regularization and the efficiency of the optimization iterations. However, with this grant, our main effort shifted to the use of learning-based techniques to bypass the handcrafted nature of the regularization and the often heavy iteration steps. Since the midterm report, one algorithm we developed for low-light imaging was a two-stage deep learning framework for light field restoration, which consisted of a multi-to-one (MTO) network for individual view restoration, and an all-to-all (ATA) network to reconstruct the full spatial-angular information. This work has resulted in a journal paper in Neurocomputing. Further on, the PSHoloNet mentioned above was a more recent development. A main difference was that it incorporated not only learning from data, but also the mathematical model of the imaging, specifically in the binary data capture with a Poisson model and the Gabor imaging setup using Fresnel approximation, and incorporating both in the subsequent physics-informed network. Regarding the third objective, we reported a 25% completion in the mid-term progress report. Further along our earlier investigations, we tackled in particular underwater imaging, as a challenging low-light scenario for holographic capture with significant scattering. Our approach consisted of adding polarization capability in our capture, and through developing an underwater image formation model to compute the Stokes vectors and consequently the total scattering light irradiance, together with an untrained network based on U-Net to learn the critical parameters, we demonstrated capability of full scene underwater imaging, as reported in the OSA Digital Holography and Three-Dimensional Imaging meeting, and published in the Optics Express journal.

17200019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200019.value: In this project, the major findings and research outcome center on extending the applicability of digital holographic imaging to low-light scenarios, through the development of bespoke computational optical imaging algorithms and advanced electronic sensors. It is generally accepted that holographic imaging is a powerful optical imaging method, with its capability of preserving wavefront information and therefore allowing three-dimensional capture. However, to record the necessary interference patterns, a relatively high signal-to-noise ratio is needed, which precludes the use in very dark environments. As such, our work is significant to push the technological frontier of low-light digital holography. As shown in the research output given in Part C, particularly the work on photon-starved snapshot holography, we demonstrated a digital holographic imaging system capable of operating at an ultra-low photon level (less than one photon per pixel), with our computational scheme known as PSHoloNet, which combined the mathematical imaging model and the data-driven processing. In addition to PSHoloNet, we also advanced low-light light field imaging, which is closely related to digital holography, by cascading a multi-to-one network for individual view restoration and an all-to-all network to reconstruct the full spatial-angular information. Furthermore, we added polarization imaging to complement the holographic capture, which was shown to be effective in underwater imaging with significant scattering.

17200019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200019.value: The research has room for further development on a couple of directions. In terms of applications, there are a wide array of situations that can benefit from low-light imaging. Our experiments were conducted on microscopy of small plastic fragments, and further work can extend to applications such as in vivo microscopy and remote sensing. In terms of computational algorithms, the speed of training and inference has room for improvement, and as more advanced deep learning algorithms are being developed, they will likely enable further denoising of the raw data, allowing for a further reduction of the photon budget. Furthermore, the use of the quanta image sensor in holographic imaging is still nascent, and further development is possible to extend this combination for other desirable imaging characteristics, such as high dynamic range imaging. This is an area that we aim to foster further collaboration with researchers in the electronic sensor community.

17200019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200019.value: Three-dimensional imaging and seeing in the dark are two desirable goals in optical imaging. One solution to the former is digital holography, which consists of an ingenious way to allow for the capture of phase information, and with appropriate reconstruction methods, can recover the object with full depth information. The challenge with the latter is noise, and the key generally lies in better electronic sensors and more advanced computational algorithms. In this project, we successfully achieved low-light holographic imaging, by harnessing a new type of single-photon image sensor and developing sophisticated reconstruction methods. This is significant because it enables various applications, from underwater imaging to in vivo microscopy.

17200119.label: Project Objectives
17200119.value: Propose a methodology for managing and analyzing dynamic multimodal transportation networks with bike-and-ride. Examine various multimodal market regimes. Analyze planning, operational, and management strategies from the perspectives of the government and the private operators.
rows: Propose a methodology for managing and analyzing dynamic multimodal transportation networks with bike-and-ride.
Analyze planning, operational, and management strategies from the perspectives of the government and the private operators.

17200119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200119.value: Road transport generates many roadside emissions that are harmful to human health and contribute to global warming. Therefore, there has been significant effort to reduce such emissions. Promoting cycling via introducing bike-sharing systems, encouraging bike-and-ride (the combined use of bikes and transit), and introducing toll charging are main examples. Yet three research gaps remain. First, the main issue of bike-sharing systems is that there is a mismatch between demand for and supply of shared bikes over time and space. Moreover, in station-based bike-sharing systems, insufficient parking spaces at return stations are often a problem in reality. Bike repositioning is needed to meet both bike and space demand. In practice, there are two types of repositioning: user- and vehicle-based. The former often uses discounts to attract cyclists to get shared bikes from or return them to designated locations. The latter uses repositioning trucks to transport shared bikes from stations with an oversupply of bikes to those with an undersupply. Both types of repositioning are used simultaneously in practice but there is as yet no methodology to help the operator optimize both concurrently. Second, there has been no comparison and analysis of the performance of station-based, dockless, and hybrid station-based and dockless bike-sharing systems, despite their existence in reality. Third, although the coexistence of bike-sharing, rail, and toll road operators can be found in a realistic single multimodal transportation market, there is no methodology for analyzing their coexistence and managing the market. The aim of this project will be to propose a methodology for new and theoretically difficult network design problems: managing and analyzing dynamic multimodal transportation systems with bike-and-ride and the coexistence of toll road, bike-sharing, and transit operators. The bike-sharing operator will perform both user- and vehicle-based repositioning. Different market regimes will be formed and analyzed based on whether each of the operators is private or public. Various competition, cooperation, subsidization, dynamic pricing, and regulatory strategies will be examined in these regimes to obtain useful strategies and insights for the system operations and management, promoting bike-and-ride, and increasing the market shares of green transportation modes. To obtain policy and managerial insights for regulating and improving the Hong Kong multimodal market, the districts around East Rail Line will be used as a case study. Critical factors that affect travelers’ use of bike-and-ride and bike-sharing systems in Hong Kong will also be identified. Different types of bike-sharing systems will be compared. 道路交通產生大量的路邊廢氣，不僅對人體健康有害，而且會導致全球變暖。因此在減少此類排放方面人們已經做出了大量努力。主要例子包括：通過引入自行車共享系統來促進騎行，鼓勵自行車換乘（自行車與公共交通的結合使用），以及引入公路收費。然而依舊存在三個研究缺口。第一，自行車共享系統的主要問題是，隨著時間和空間的推移，共享單車的需求和供應之間存在不匹配。此外，在基於站點的自行車共享系統中，歸還站的停車位不足往往是現實中存在的一個問題。因此自行車需要被重新佈局以同時滿足用戶對自行車和停車位的需求。在實踐中，有兩種​​類型的重佈局方法: 基於用戶和基於車輛。前者通常利用折扣來吸引用戶從指定地點獲取共享單車或將自行車歸還至指定地點。後者使用卡車將共享單車從自行車供應過剩的站點運送到自行車供應不足的站點。這兩種類型的重佈局在實踐中同時使用，但目前還沒有方法來幫助運營商同時優化兩者。第二，基於站點、無站點、以及兩者混合的自行車共享系統雖然在現實中存在，但它們的性能並沒有得到比較和分析。第三，雖然在現實的單一多式聯運市場中可以發現自行車共享系統、軌道交通和收費公路運營商們的共存，但是並沒有可以分析它們的共存以及管理市場的方法。 本項目的目的是為這種新的並且理論上困難的網絡設計問題提出一種方法: 管理和分析包含自行車換乘的動態多模式交通系統，以及收費公路、自行車共享系統、和公共交通運營商們的共存。共享單車運營商將同時使用基於用戶和車輛的自行車重佈局。根據每個運營商是私營的還是公共的將會形成不同的市場機制並加以分析。在這些機制中將研究各種競爭、合作、補貼、動態定價和監管策略，以此獲取對系統運營和管理有益的策略和見解，促進自行車換乘，增加綠色交通模式的市場份額。為獲取可以規管及改善香港多式聯運市場的政策及管理方面的見解，本研究將以東鐵線周邊地區為研究對象。此外，我們亦會找出在香港影響旅客使用自行車換乘和自行車共享系統的關鍵因素。不同類型的自行車共享系統也會被比較。

17200119.label: Realisation of objectives
17200119.value: Due to Covid 19, Hong Kong has been seriously affected since 2020. The university environment is no exception. Some existing non-local research students and research assistants preferred or had to stay in their home towns rather than Hong Kong after the Chinese holiday of 2020 because (1) the Hong Kong Border was closed and (2) they thought that Mainland China was safer than Hong Kong because of having better control on the number of infected cases in most parts of Mainland China. In almost earlier two years, the closure of the Hong Kong border and the lower number of infected cases in Mainland China also created difficulty in hiring new non-local research assistants or recruiting new non-local research students to work on this project. Moreover, local civil engineering students did not prefer to pursue MPhil or PhD degrees as the job market was good. Therefore, the PI could only rely on existing human resources and his research collaborators at other universities to work on the project and delivered project outputs as many as possible. Up to now, a PhD student graduated under the support of this project and became an Assistant Professor at Huazhong University of Science and Technology. Another MPhil student graduated too. This project considers managing a multimodal transportation system including a bike-sharing system. A bike-sharing system always faces a demand-supply imbalance problem. The operator is therefore required to rebalance the bike-sharing system from time to time. The operator has two strategies for rebalancing: vehicle-based and user based. For the former, the operator uses repositioning trucks to transport bikes from surplus stations to deficit stations. The operator is required to determine the routes of repositioning trucks and loading and unloading quantities at each visited station to balance the bike-sharing system. The problem is referred to as a vehicle-based bike repositioning problem. For the user-based counterpart, the operator is required to give incentives to users to encourage them to ride bikes from surplus stations to deficit stations. For both types of problems, the operator requires a mathematical model and a solution method to tackle them effectively and efficiently. Moreover, for each type of problem, there are two types of repositioning: static and dynamic. The former assumes the demand is relatively fixed and the latter assumes the demand is time-varying or dynamic. Therefore, the first assumption is suitable for modeling nighttime repositioning whereas the second is suitable for modeling daytime repositioning. [J1] was prepared and published to analyze the operational strategies of nighttime repositioning of a fossil-fueled repositioning truck to reduce vehicle emissions and considered the existence of broken bikes in the bike-sharing system. [J4] and [C1] extended [J1] to additionally consider light carriers. [J2] and [D1] extended [J1] to consider the operational strategies of daytime repositioning by multiple electric repositioning trucks, including recharging strategies. These three papers [J1, J2, J4] and [D1] are related to objective 3 about analyzing the operational and management strategies of private and public bike-sharing operators, and objective 1 about modeling and solution methodology. All these papers [J1, J2, J4] involve the development of a mixed-integer nonlinear program, and [J1, J2] developed a modified artificial bee colony algorithm for the analysis. For user-based repositioning, a conference paper [C2] was prepared and presented at an international conference. An MPhil dissertation [D2] was then written, which proposes a mixed integer nonlinear and nonconvex programming model to consider user inequity. A new effective inner-approximation method and an artificial bee colony heuristic were proposed to solve the problem. To improve transit usage, reduce traffic congestion, and reduce vehicle emissions in a multimodal transport system, the government can promote bike-and-ride. Therefore, this project also considers bike-and-ride in a multimodal transportation system with autos, transit, and shared bike modes. [J3] has been recently prepared to model, analyze, and design a simplified multimodal transportation system with bike-and-ride. Some analytical insights are derived to help the government to manage the system, for example using pricing policies, and help the private operators to run the system. This paper is very relevant to objective 1 about proposing a methodology for planning, managing, and analyzing a multimodal transportation system with bike-and-ride and objective 3 about analyzing planning and management strategies from the perspectives of the government and the private transit operator. This paper also presents the analysis of two multimodal market regimes, social cost minimization and profit maximization regimes, which are related to objective 2. Another bike-and-ride scenario was considered by [J6] and presented at an international conference [C3]. A multi-modal transportation network consisting of feeder buses, shared bikes, and walking was considered. Travelers select one of the three modes to reach a bus rapid transit (BRT) station. If they select shared bikes, they indeed chose bike-and-ride for their trips. [J6] proposed a bi-level mixed-integer programming model to simultaneously design the locations of shared bike stations as well as the routes and station locations of feeder buses. A modified genetic algorithm is developed to solve the model for large network applications. This version was extended to consider the whole multi-modal transportation network with 3 single travel modes, including bike, bus, carpool, and two combined modes, i.e., bike transfer to transit and bike transfer to carpool [J7]. This paper proposes a tri-level multimodal discrete network design problem for the optimal deployment of bike lanes, high-occupancy vehicle lanes, and bike-and-ride interchanges in urban networks. A cross-nested logit model is used to capture users' mode choice behavior while a complementary problem based multimodal traffic assignment model with user equilibrium principle is developed for route choice behavior. An efficient surrogate-based optimization method is proposed using Kriging function approximation and a modified Evans' algorithm is embedded to solve the combined mode choice and traffic assignment. Both [J6] and [J7] are related to objectives 1 and 3. In the multi-modal transportation market of Hong Kong, the two types of minibuses mainly serve as feeder buses. To examine the multi-modal market, which is related to objective 2, it is essential to analyze the performance of these types of minbuses in Hong Kong. [J5] was, therefore, prepared to understand how passengers perceived the service quality of these two types of minibuses. The proposed methodology can be easily extended to consider the performance of shared bikes in Hong Kong, which is another feeder service. To sum up, all objectives have been achieved successfully.

17200119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200119.value: The research outcomes (in form of the modeling frameworks, solution methodologies, and properties of studied models) and major findings were found in 7 journal papers [J1]-[J7] and two dissertations [D1]-[D2]. Some of them were presented at international conferences [C1]-[C3]. The following summarizes the major findings and managerial insights. 1. The joint design of bus and bike systems has a better performance than the separate design of the two systems from the view of the whole society. However, some operators can lose their profits while different passengers gain benefits from the joint design to different extents. Moreover, the joint design can lead to a non-negligible loss to private operators than the isolated design. This implies that the introduction of the second type of feeder service to the unimodal system by the public sector may bring a strike by the private operator and a subsidy is recommended to give to the operator to compensate for its loss. 2. The passengers of Hong Kong were less satisfied with the demand-responsive public light bus services in general. The in-vehicle environment, waiting time, driver’s attitude, and safety hold a higher improvement priority. 3. Incorporating light carriers into the repositioning fleet can reduce both the total cost and fuel consumption compared to using heavy carriers solely under the following circumstances: 1) some stations are hard to access for heavy carriers; 2) the traffic on the main roads is congested. 4. By charging private operators a high cost for emissions, using more light carriers can be beneficial in reducing both the total cost and the fuel consumption, but user satisfaction and profits for the private operators are sacrificed. This implies that a subsidy to the private operators may be called for if environmental considerations are imposed on their repositioning decisions. 5. The provision of bike-and-ride facilities can always improve the profit of the rail operator under both the objectives of profit maximization of the rail operator and social cost minimization but the social cost may not be reduced under the profit maximization objective. 6. Bike-and-ride can be profitable to the operator and socially beneficial at the same time. 7. The modal share of bike-and-ride mode is larger when the total demand is larger or more travelers reside at the upstream of the traffic corridor.

17200219.label: Project Objectives
17200219.value: To implement a high-energy TAOPO as the source for the PAM system The proposed TAPAS, in the form of a thulium-doped optical parametric oscillator (TAOPO), has been previously demonstrated in the 1.7-µm wavelength window as the pulsed source, specifically for the strong PA signal that can be generated from the lipids. Additional spectroscopic information as functional imaging will further be available through a fast wavelength-swept (i.e., time-division multiplexed) version of TAOPO. At this stage, we will implement a high-energy pulsed source in the 1.7-µm wavelength window for the PAM system, together with TAPAS, for implementation and optimization in later stages of the research. To design and fabricate a microfiber-based TAPAS as the PAM detector A microfiber-based TAPAS prototype to be pumped initially in the 1.55-µm wavelength window as the detector for PAM system will be designed and fabricated and its performance thoroughly characterized in a number of aspects, including operating wavelength, detection sensitivity, and ultrasonic bandwidth. This stage provides a well-characterized 1.55-µm TAPAS prototype for PAM application that can be extended to other wavelength windows by tailoring the zero-dispersion wavelength of the microfiber and a development platform for the last phase of the research. To explore an integrated endoscopic PAM based on the optimized TAPAS Leveraging the previous two phases, we will explore an alternative TAPAS based on thulium-doped microfiber (TDMF) to enhance the sensitivity by exploiting the birefringence effect. In particular, highly efficient TDMF (with strong absorption of pump wavelength) will enable a short microfiber cavity to realize an optimized design of TAPAS that will be further integrated with the potential endoscopic PAM. Thorough study of this aspect of TAPAS performance will lay the foundation for its use in capturing spectroscopic PA images in an endoscopic manner towards the end of the project.

17200219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200219.value: Over the past decade, the growing demand for healthcare solutions has necessitated substantial advancements in optical bioimaging technologies. The availability of high-speed photonics technologies in telecommunications has invigorated the biomedical imaging arena through various optical imaging modalities. Photoacoustic microscopy (PAM), especially one version of optical-resolution (OR-PAM), is capable of achieving cell-level functional imaging, by leveraging intrinsic optical absorption contrast provided by visible light in biological tissues. Furthermore, OR-PAM has proven to be promising by rendering label-free vascular imaging with high resolution. However, the sensitivity is primarily limited by the conventional piezoelectric transducer, while the imaging depth is inherently limited by the visible light wavelength. The practical application of OR-PAM is, therefore, yet to be achieved. The thulium-assisted parametrically amplified system (TAPAS) proposed in this project offers a promising platform for photoacoustic imaging applications. Through a three-phase approach, we will demonstrate TAPAS as a core technology to meet some of the critical challenges of next-generation photoacoustic imaging systems. First, we plan to demonstrate a specific implementation of TAPAS in the form of a thulium-doped optical parametric oscillator (TAOPO) in the 1.7-µm wavelength window as the pulsed source, specifically for the strong photoacoustic signal that can be generated from the lipids. Additional spectroscopic information as functional imaging will further be available through a wavelength-swept (i.e., time-division multiplexed) version of TAOPO. Second, we propose to design and fabricate a microfiber-based TAPAS prototype to be pumped initially in the 1.55-µm wavelength window as the detector for PAM. Its performance will be thoroughly characterized in a number of aspects, including operating wavelength, detection sensitivity, and ultrasonic signal bandwidth. The versatility of tailoring the zero-dispersion wavelength of the microfiber is promising in translating the detection wavelength beyond the 1.55-µm wavelength window. Third, we will explore the possibility of an alternative TAPAS based on a highly efficient thulium-doped microfiber and thereby realize a short microfiber cavity in order to identify an optimized and integrated TAPAS as a detector for the potential endoscopic PAM towards the end of the project. The proposed project thus constitutes advancement in photoacoustic imaging technology in the context of deeply penetrated optical excitation, additional spectroscopic information as functional imaging, and a highly sensitive microfiber-based detection scheme. The wide spectrum of knowledge generated in the project will thus contribute to both the research community and industry. 在過去十年中，隨著對醫療保健的需求不斷提升，光學生物成像技術的發展已經迫在眉睫。將已有的通信高速光子技術引入到光學成像中，使得各種模態的生物成像也得到了飛速發展。光聲成像（PAM），特別是光學像素光聲成像（OR-PAM），通過利用可見光在生物組織裏發生的本征光學吸收差異獲得細胞級的功能性成像。並且，OR-PAM已經被證明在無標記高像素血管成像中具有較高的應用前景。然而，OR-PAM的靈敏度還主要受限於傳統壓電傳感器，同時成像深度也固定受限於可見光波長範圍。因此，OR-PAM的實際應用還亟待被深入發掘。 本項目中提出的銩輔助參量放大系統（TAPAS）為光聲成像提供了壹個非常有潛力的應用平臺。我們將從三個步驟來演示TAPAS作為核心技術是怎樣達到下壹代光聲成像系統的關鍵要求。首先，我們計劃演示壹種特殊的TAPAS裝置，它是工作在1.7-µm波長窗口下的摻銩光學參量振蕩器（TAOPO）脈沖光源，該波段脈沖光源可以被用來在脂質中產生較強光聲信號。除此之外，通過使用波長掃描（時分復用）摻銩光學參量振蕩器，還可以獲得用於功能性成像的光譜信息。其次，我們計劃設計和制作壹種基於微光纖，泵浦波長在1.55-µm波段的TAPAS原型樣機作為PAM的探測器。我們將通過幾個方面來測試該樣機的性能，包括操作波長，探測靈敏度以及超聲信號帶寬。微光纖在控制零色散波長方面的多功能性可以將探測波長轉移到1.55-µm以上。第三，我們將探索基於高效率摻銩微光纖TAPAS的可能性，實現壹種短的微光纖腔，從而在項目最終獲得可以用於PAM內窺鏡的高度優化和集成的TAPAS。 因此，本提案主要在高深度光學激發方面，作為功能性成像的附加光譜信息方面，以及高靈敏度微光纖探測方面深入發展光聲成像技術。項目產出的知識將為研究團體和工業界作出巨大的貢獻。

17200219.label: Realisation of objectives
17200219.value: 1. To implement a high-energy TAOPO as the source for the PAM system We have already demonstrated a thulium-doped optical parametric oscillator (TAOPO) in the 1.7-μm wavelength window as the pulsed-source form of the proposed TAPAS, specifically for the strong PA signal that can be generated from the lipids. Additional spectroscopic information as functional imaging will further be available through a fast wavelength-swept (i.e., time-division multiplexed) version of TAOPO. We have implemented a high-energy pulsed source in the 1.7-μm wavelength window for the PAM system, together with TAPAS, for implementation and optimization in later stages of the research. 2. To design and fabricate a microfiber-based TAPAS as the PAM detector We have designed and fabricated microfibers as the TAPAS prototype to be pumped initially in the 1.55-μm wavelength window as the detector for PAM system, while the performance has been enhanced through the dual-comb multiheterodyne interferometry (DCMHI). By sensing the phase shift induced by the ultrasound without any resonators in the medium, the DCMHI boosted the phase sensitivity by coherent accumulation without any magnitude averaging and extra radio frequency amplification. We also demonstrated a Grüneisen relaxation photoacoustic microscopy (GR-PAM) of lipid-rich tissue imaging at the 1.7 μm band, implemented with a high-energy TDFL and a fiber-based delay line, and another more recent scheme denoted as hybrid optical parametrically-oscillating emitter (HOPE) to image the water content in the phantom and the biological tissue in vitro. Our 1930-nm PAM could map the water content in the complex tissue environment at high spatial resolution, deep penetration depth, improved sensitivity, and suppressed artifact signal of the lipid. 3. To explore an integrated endoscopic PAM based on the optimized TAPAS We have explored an alternative TAPAS by exploiting the near-infrared-III double illumination optical-resolution photoacoustic microscopy (DIOR-PAM) for enhancing the sensitivity of label-free lipid imaging. Using the same laser, DIOR-PAM can enhance the sensitivity by nearly 100%, which we prove in the Monte Carlo simulation. In addition to that, the endoscopic feature has been implemented through a photoacoustic remote sensing (PARS) scheme. In particular, the pump wavelength was selected to overlap the first overtone of the C-H bond in response to the intensive absorption of lipid molecules, which introduces a much-enhanced SNR (55 dB) onto PARS signals. Taking the merits of the high detection sensitivity, deep penetration depth, broadband detection, and high resolution of the PARS system, high-quality tissue scale lipid imaging was demonstrated in a model organism and brain slice.

Then, another more recent scheme denoted as a hybrid optical parametrically-oscillating emitter (HOPE) was demonstrated to image the water content in the phantom and the biological tissue in vitro. Our 1930-nm PAM could map the water content in the complex tissue environment at high spatial resolution, deep penetration depth, improved sensitivity, and suppressed artifact signal of the lipid. Last, we demonstrated the sensitive enhancement while the performance has been enhanced through the dual-comb multiheterodyne interferometry (DCMHI). By sensing the phase shift induced by the ultrasound without any resonators in the medium, the DCMHI boosted the phase sensitivity by coherent accumulation without any magnitude averaging and extra radio frequency amplification. The wide spectrum of knowledge generated in the project will thus contribute to both the research community and industry.

17200519.value: To investigate the fabrication of novel bijels-derived hybrid hydrogel structures for tissue engineering applications using the templating-on-bijels approach.
