17200519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200519.value: Many medical conditions require urgent development of new medical technologies because they cannot be treated effectively by current methods. Tissue engineering (TE) has been a highly innovative scientific field which investigates new approaches for repairing damaged or diseased human body tissues. Scaffold-, growth factor (GF)-, or cell-based TE strategies are employed for tissue regeneration and the field is dominated by scaffold-based TE. TE scaffolds play crucial roles for cell proliferation and differentiation and new tissue formation. Recent advances also require TE scaffolds to have abilities of GF delivery and live cell incorporation. Enabling technologies such as scaffold fabrication techniques are essential for TE development, and new technologies such as 3D printing are intensively studied for fabricating advanced TE scaffolds. For some particular situations in human tissue regeneration, hydrogel membranes which can deliver GF and/or cells have significant advantages. Therefore, advanced membrane fabrication methods should be investigated. Bicontinuous interfacially jammed emulsion gels (“bijels”), which possess bicontinuous structures, are a new discovery recently. Using the approach of templating on bijels, bijels-derived structures consisting of two continuous interlocking phases can be made. Such unique bicontinuous structures have distinctive advantages over conventional TE scaffolds for tissue regeneration. This project aims to investigate new fabrication technologies and create novel hybrid hydrogel structures, which are based on bijels’ bicontinuous architecture, for tissue engineering applications. Taking advantages of the unique two-phase bicontinuous structure, drug, GFs and cells will be encapsulated separately in two hydrogels, which have different degradation rates, in bijels-derived hybrid hydrogel membranes for their sequential release in vivo. To explore the adaptability of new fabrication technologies and assess the application potential of products fabricated, two types of multifunctional membranes of different designs will be investigated for skin and peripheral nerve (PN) regeneration, respectively. Furthermore, for PN regeneration, bijels-derived fibers encapsulated with two GFs will be studied. The different hybrid hydrogel membranes and fiber are designed for achieving controlled release of GFs and cell to enhance skin or PN tissue regeneration and for antibacterial ability in skin TE. The membranes and fibers produced at different stages will be evaluated for their structure, properties and biological performance. Drug and GF release behaviours from membranes and fibers will be investigated. Interplays between GFs, cells, and hybrid hydrogel structures will be studied. This project is at the forefront of research in the field and opens up the exploration of the unique bijels-derived structures for tissue engineering applications.

17200519.label: Realisation of objectives
17200519.value: Through RGC’s grant support, the proposed work was performed over 42 months and all project objectives have been realized. (The original project duration was 36 months. Due to delays in experimental work and also the additional explorations in the research topic area performed by PI’s team with the full use of funds provided by the RGC, an extension of 6 months was applied for and subsequently granted by RGC.) A good number of journal articles and conference papers have been published for the results obtained in this project, two new manuscripts have been submitted to journals, and several more manuscripts are planned and will be prepared for submission to journals. The PI (M.Wang) supervised the research and ensured the progress of the whole project and publication of results, and the Co-I (W.W.Lu of HKU’s Faculty of Medicine) had contributed to this project. Furthermore, another of PI’s long-term collaborators (Dr. L.Zheng, an associate professor in HKU’s Faculty of Dentistry) was involved in some parts of this project, assisting in the in vitro research work. The research conducted in this project has addressed a range of problems/issues in the research topic area of this project. On the scientific side, research was performed in areas such as the formation of pure bijels and nanoparticle-containing bijels, formation of bijels-derived porous structures, influences of different factors on bijels formation and on the formation of bijels-derived structures, biodegradation behavior of bijels-derived structures, controlled release of incorporated growth factors, controlled delivery of living cells (different types of cells), dual delivery of growth factors and cells, release or delivery kinetics, cell-material-porous structure interactions, etc. On the technological side, three technologies were investigated and developed in this project: (1) fabrication of pure bijels using the phase separation technique, (2) fabrication of functional nanoparticle (or nanofiber)-containing bijels [an example is multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-containing bijels] using the phase inversion technique, and (3) fabrication of bijels-derived porous structures for biomedical applications in general and for tissue engineering applications in particular. In addition, this project also supported PI’s pursuits in developing new biomaterials for tissue engineering, in electrospinning in tissue engineering and in additive manufacturing in tissue engineering. The design and fabrication of growth factor-incorporated and cell-encapsulated complex scaffolds for regenerating the targeted body tissues and many other aspects of constructing complex scaffolds were investigated. On the medical side, growth factor-incorporated and cell-encapsulated complex scaffolds for regenerating the targeted body tissues (e.g., skin and peripheral nerve) were successfully made, and their in vitro biological performance was assessed. All of aforementioned research has contributed to realizing the project objectives. The RGC funding for this project has partially supported the research of three PhD students (SUN Haoran, LI Junzhi and LI Huihua) and one research assistant (LAI Jiahui). In addition, a number of MSc students and undergraduate final-year students were involved in this GRF project with their respective MSc or FYP projects. The PhD students and research assistant (as well as MSc and FYP students) were well trained in their respective research areas and their work also contributed to the successful completion of this RGF project. The PhD students had attended several international conferences, including premier conferences in our field, to present their research work and had won one international award.

17200519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200519.value: 1. Fabrication of pure bijels using the phase separation technique and production of bijels-derived porous structures Different polymer mixtures and different fabrication parameters were used to investigate the fabrication technique and evaluate the parameters for bijels formation. Optimal parameters were obtained for bijels fabrication. Subsequently, materials and process parameters were studied for obtaining bijels-derived porous structures. Biocompability and biodegradation of bijels-derived porous structures were evaluated. Some results have been presented in the publications (see Part C). 2. Fabrication of nanoparticle-containing bijels using the phase inversion technique and production of bijels-derived porous structures Similar to the above, the process and parameters were investigate to form stable nanoparticle (e.g., MWCNT)-containing bijels. The dynamic formation processes were captured and mechanisms of bijels formation were explored. Also, materials and process parameters were studied for obtaining bijels-derived, nanoparticle-containing porous structures which could be used for biomedical applications. Some results have also been presented in the publications (see Part C). 3. Formation of drug-containing, growth factor-incorporated and/or cell-encapsulated structures based on bijels-derived porous structures For potential biomedical applications, anticancer drug, growth factor and living cells were separated or concurrently put into bijels-derived porous structures through the infiltration of a biocompatible and biodegradable polymer that carried the drug, growth factor or living cell. Different designs and combinations were used, depending on the targeted application. This is a very important part of the project, which has resulted in some journal and conference publications (see Part C). 4. Scientific and biomedical studies of drug-containing, growth factor-incorporated and/or cell-encapsulated structures Various systems based on bijels-derived porous structures were investigated for controlled release/delivery of drug, growth factor and/or cell. They could be separately released from the systems, and factors affecting their release and release kinetics were studied. For systems containing both growth factor(s) and living cells, the effects of released growth factor on locally delivered cells were studied. Dual delivery of growth factors were also investigated. Some results have been presented in conferences (see Part C) and several manuscripts based on PhD students’ work have been planned and will be submitted to good journals. 5. Extended research The PhD students and research assistant involved in this project also performed research in other areas in tissue engineering, complementing the originally proposed research for this project. 6. Publications Many journal and conference publications arising from this project have already appeared. New manuscripts have been planned and are/will be prepared for journal publication.

17200519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200519.value: There are quite a few areas in which significant developments can be made following the research conducted in this project. First, the new fabrication techniques for bijels can produce stable and large-size bijels membranes. Bijels are soft matters and they themselves cannot be used directly in the tissue engineering field. However, the unique bicontinuous feature of bijels can be very useful for bijels acting as nano-reactors. On the other hand, the bicontinuous structures of bijels-derived porous structures (the pores in these structures are one phase which provides interconnecting channels) can be good filtration membranes which are needed in several industries (including biomedical). These are potential application areas for the fabricated bijels and bijels-derived porous structures. Even in the tissue engineering field itself, following the research of this project, with the ease of fabrication of bijels-derived porous structures, different drug-, biomolecule (including growth factor)-, and/or cell-containing systems can be produced, aiming for different applications or for generating different body tissues. The materials that can form bijels are still very limited. Therefore, future research should develop new materials for bijels and new biocompatible materials for bijels that are intended for the biomedical field.

17200519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200519.value: In scaffold-based tissue engineering, scaffolds possessing interconnecting pores play crucial roles in regenerating human body tissues. Different technologies, including electrospinning and 3D printing, can produce porous scaffolds. Recent advances in tissue engineering require tissue engineering scaffolds to have abilities of growth factor delivery and living cell incorporation. Bicontinuous interfacially jammed emulsion gels (“bijels”), a new discovery recently, possess bicontinuous structures. Templating on bijels, bijels-derived structures consisting of two continuous interlocking phases can be made. Such unique bicontinuous structures have distinctive advantages over conventional tissue engineering scaffolds for body tissue regeneration. In this project, techniques were developed to fabricate pure bijels, functional nanoparticle-containing bijels and bijels-derived bicontinuous structures. Taking advantages of bicontinuous structures, drug, growth factors and living cells were encapsulated separately in two hydrogels, which had different biodegradation rates, in bijels-derived hybrid hydrogel membranes for their sequential release in vivo. Multifunctional membranes of different designs were investigated for skin and peripheral nerve regeneration, respectively. Furthermore, for peripheral nerve regeneration, bijels-derived structures encapsulated with two growth factors were studied. Live cells and bioactive growth factors could be released from the structures through structural biodegradation. This project opens up the exploration of bijels-derived structures for tissue engineering applications.

17200719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17200719.value: Microbially induced concrete corrosion (MICC) is the main degradation mechanism in urban wastewater infrastructure. The generation of acid and sulfate due to microorganism activity creates a highly corrosive environment that deteriorates the applied concrete materials. The high cost of repairing and maintaining aging wastewater infrastructure raises an urgent demand for sustainable materials that are far more durable than conventional concrete. Geopolymer concrete is a green and innovative alkali-activated material with superior acid and sulfate resistance, thus being a promising next-generation construction material for wastewater systems threatened by MICC. In comparison with conventional concrete, geopolymer concrete derived from industrial waste is less energy intensive in terms of its manufacture and more cost-effective when the local supply of raw materials is abundant. Despite some tests demonstrating the remarkable acid and sulfate resistance of geopolymers, their widespread application in wastewater infrastructure is still hindered due to their unknown long-term performance under MICC. This project will fill the knowledge gaps in understanding the interaction mechanisms between geopolymers and microorganisms and will advance the innovation of geopolymer technology via functionalization with antimicrobial cations and layered double hydroxides (LDHs). This project will first investigate the anti-biofilm performance of geopolymers using a newly-designed apparatus, revealing the decisive physiochemical parameters that control the microorganism adhesion, biofouling, and kinetics of acid production at the contact surface. The original and altered microstructure, gel composition, and spatial distribution of damage in specimens due to biogenic acid attack will be characterized using various advanced techniques (e.g., quantitative XRD, nanoindentation) at multi-length scales. Further linking the materials’ antimicrobial performance to their composition and microstructural features will pave the way for the mixture design optimization of durable geopolymer systems. Geopolymers will be functionalized with the anti-biodegradation attribute through (1) limiting biogenic acid production by inhibiting microbial activities; and (2) maintaining the structural and compositional stability of geopolymeric gel in acid. Based on preliminary investigations, geopolymers, if properly formulated, can be functionalized with antimicrobial capacity without compromising their long-term mechanical properties. In this project, a number of innovative geopolymer mixtures will be systematically designed, characterized, evaluated, and optimized. This work will involve close collaboration among researchers across multiple disciplines, including geopolymer chemistry and technology, biological science, and materials engineering. The success of this research will advance state-of-the-art geopolymer technology and promote the sustainability and resilience of wastewater infrastructure for a new platform. 微生物引起的混凝土腐蝕（MICC）是城市污水處理設施性能退化的主要原因。通常情況下，旺盛的微生物代謝活動會產生大量的酸性物質和硫酸鹽等，形成高腐蝕性環境，從而使其中的混凝土材料性能發生嚴重退化。修補和維護老舊污水處理設施的高昂成本使得研發一款耐久性能遠超傳統混凝土的可持續建築材料成為當前的一個迫切需求。地聚物混凝土作為一種環保、創新的堿激發材料，具有優異的耐酸、抗硫酸鹽等特性，被認為是一種非常有前景的可應用於污水處理設施的建築材料。由於原材料基本都來源於工業廢渣，與傳統混凝土相比，地聚物的製備能耗顯著降低；同時，在原材料供應充足的情況下，其經濟效益尤為突出。迄今為止，儘管已有大量的試驗表明地聚物具有卓越的耐酸性和抗硫酸鹽特性，但它在微生物腐蝕環境中的長期性能仍然未知，導致其在污水處理設施中的廣泛應用仍然受到質疑。 本項目將填補地聚物混凝土與微生物相互作用機理的空白，並通過抗菌陽離子和層狀雙氫氧化物的功能化來推動地聚物相關技術的創新。本項目將首次利用全新設計的設備裝置研究地聚物的抗生物膜形成性能，揭示控制微生物粘附、淤積和接觸表面產酸動力學的關鍵理化參數。為達到這一目標，將利用多種先進技術（如定量X射線衍射，納米壓痕等）對試樣的初始狀態和微生物侵蝕後微觀結構和凝膠成分的改變，以及損傷的空間分佈進行多尺度表征，並將上述特征與抗菌性能進行進一步的關聯，這將為地聚物混凝土耐久性的配合比優化設計鋪平道路。 地聚物混凝土將通過（1）抑制微生物活性來限制生物酸的產生，和（2）保持地聚物凝膠在酸性環境中結構和組分依舊穩定，從而具備抗微生物腐蝕退化的特性。初步研究結果表明，如果配製得當，地聚物混凝土可以具備優異的抗微生物能力而不損害其長期力學性能。本項目將系統地設計、表征、評估和優化一系列全新的地聚物混凝土配合比。這項工作將涉及多個學科的研究人員之間的密切合作，包括地聚物化學和技術、生物科學和材料工程，研究工作的成功將推動最前沿的地聚物技術的發展，並提升污水處理設施的可持續性和可恢復性至一個嶄新的平台。

17200719.label: Realisation of objectives
17200719.value: We have successfully addressed all the objectives of this project. Eight journal papers were generated directly from this project and were published in the top journals in the field of concrete materials and geopolymer chemistry, including Cement and Concrete Research, Cement and Concrete Composites, and Dalton Transaction. Realization of Objective 1: We have developed a testing protocol to evaluate the antimicrobial performance of geopolymer materials, which enables the identification of critical micro-structural parameters of geopolymer that govern its anti-MICC resistance. Realization of Objective 2: By using the testing protocol developed in this project, we have established the relationships among material composition-structure-property of geopolymers. This was realized by integrating an extensive laboratory testing program with our knowledge and understanding of geopolymer behaviours. Realization of Objective 3: We have incorporated zinc and copper into various geopolymer systems, including high-calcium alkali-activated slag materials and low-calcium metakaolin-based geopolymers. We have characterized the nanostructure and quantify the chemical composition of zinc-doped calcium-deficit geopolymers and copper-doped calcium-enriched geopolymer gels, using various advanced techniques (such as X-ray synchrotron facilities, TEM). Realization of Objective 4: We have synthesized a new antibacterial zeolite nano-material (named as Sor-zeo) and added it into fly ash-based geopolymers to enable nuclei effects while endowing antimicrobial properties. The results have successfully demonstrated that the incorporation of Sor-zeolite increases the strength and densifies the pore structure of fly ash/slag-based geopolymer owing to the seeding nuclei effects during the geopolymerisation process. Realization of Objective 5: We have successfully developed a new antimicrobial alkali-activated slag (AAS) geopolymer material with the in-situ formation of benzoate-intercalated layered double hydroxides (BZ-LDHs). The benzoate anions are spontaneously intercalated in a bilayer manner in the interlayers of LDHs during alkaline activation process. The proposed idea has been demonstrated in this project.

17200719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17200719.value: The major findings related to each research objective are summarized as follows: Findings related to Objective 1: The decisive physiochemical parameters of geopolymers that control the microbial dynamics on contact surfaces under MICC are the microstructure compactness and antimicrobial efficacy of the reacted products. Biofilms provide habitable locations for bacterial colonisation and aerobic interaction, where in situ microorganisms constantly producing biogenic sulfuric acid, exacerbating the effects of microbial corrosion. Findings related to Objective 2: There exist a close relationship between the composition, microstructure, and anti-MICC property of geopolymer materials. It has been successfully demonstrated in the project, that by incorporating antimicrobial ingredients and/or densifying the microstructure of geopolymer matrix, the MICC resistance of geopolymer can be improved significant, at least for the initial stage. Findings related to Objective 3: The incorporation of copper oxide or copper nitrate in alkali-activated slag (AAS) increases the degree of hydration of slag but reduces the mean chain length of Cu-modified C-A-S-H. The Cu-doped AAS pastes show excellent antimicrobial efficiency, in particular, the CuO-doped AAS demonstrates 100% effectiveness in inhibiting biofilm formation, with the corrosion depth significantly reduced by a factor of 10. The Cu ion is released initially from the outer surface of C-A-S-H due to its low bond dissociation energy, followed by the weak position, namely the AlO4-tetrahedra at the bridging position, rendering the rupturing of the C-A-S-H structure. Findings related to Objective 4: The incorporation of Sor-zeolite increases the strength and densifies the pore structure of fly ash/slag-based geopolymer owing to the seeding nuclei effects during the geopolymerisation process. The enhanced dissolution of FA and slag by the seeding effects of Sor-zeolite, accelerates and enriches the precipitation of geopolymerisation products, mainly a mixture of K-A-S-H and C-A-S-H (abbreviated as K-(C)-A-S-H). The Sor-zeolite-functionalised geopolymer possesses outstanding antibacterial properties against sulphur oxidising bacteria Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans, inhibiting biofilm formation on the surface and reducing corrosion depth. Findings related to Objective 5: A new antimicrobial alkali-activated slag (AAS) material system with the in-situ formation of benzoate-intercalated layered double hydroxides (BZ-LDHs) is synthesised. The results evidence the in-situ formation of BZ-LDHs in AAS incorporating sodium benzoate during alkaline activation. The benzoate anions are spontaneously intercalated in a bilayer manner in the interlayers of LDHs, with an average basal spacing of 1.568 nm. The incorporation of BZ slightly lowers the reaction degree of slag in AAS, but barely affects the composition and structure of calcium-aluminosilicate-hydrate (C-A-S-H) formed. The developed antimicrobial AAS with BZ-LDHs demonstrates remarkable efficacy with a 95.0% bactericidal efficiency (when admixed with 3% BZ) in suppressing the growth of sulphur-oxidising bacteria Acidithiobacillus thiooxidans and inhibiting biogenic acidification. The BZ-modified AAS demonstrates excellent microbial corrosion resistance with greatly suppressed production of deleterious gypsum and corrosion depth.

17200719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17200719.value: (1) It is recommended that the long-term performance of BZ-modified AAS (e.g., effective duration of antimicrobial effect) and solution chemistry of BZ-modified AAS under biogenic sulfuric acid attack will be test. Also, the fresh properties and curing conditions of BZ-modified AAS and detailed manufacturing process needs more attentions and will be systematically investigated in the future. (2) The antimicrobial performance of synthesised functional geopolymers in this thesis under the real sewer situation (e.g., filed site experiment) or multi-variable laboratory biotic simulation test is suggested to be studied in the next stage for the application of the novel materials in sewer. (3) It is recommended that the antimicrobial performance of these antimicrobial geopolymer mortar and concrete systems be evaluated. The structural performance of structural components or structural systems adopting the proposed antibacterial geopolymers needs further consideration. (4) The cost for large-scale implementation in real-world structures, long-term durability of functionalised geopolymers under real wastewater conditions, and industrial manufacturing are suggested to be further investigated for their large-scale application.

17200719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17200719.value: Microbially induced concrete corrosion (MICC) is the primary deterioration mechanism in the urban wastewater infrastructure, which rises significant expenditure for restoration and upkeep. As an alternative to ordinary Portland cement, geopolymer is a potential solution to the issue of MICC in wastewater infrastructure. However, one of the major challenges hindering the industrial acceptance and practical application of geopolymers in sewerage facilities is the uncertain long-term durability performance of geopolymers under microbial attack, as well as their formulation techniques against microbial corrosion. This research aims to advance our understanding of the degradation pathways and mechanisms underlying geopolymer under microbial corrosion, and to develop novel functionalised geopolymers to maximise their anti-MICC capacities. The findings from this research provide valuable insights into the mechanisms of geopolymer-microorganism interactions and inform the development of novel antibacterial geopolymers for sustainable wastewater infrastructure. Ultimately, these new propositions promote widespread application of sustainable geopolymer in wastewater infrastructure by addressing current knowledge gaps surrounding bio-degradation processes and functional geopolymer with long-lasting antibacterial efficacy.

17201019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201019.value: 本項目旨在（1）闡明有機無機雜化鈣鈦礦中極化轉子對聲子的散射機制；（2）通過有機陽離子旋轉模式調控CH3NH3PbI3、H2NCHNH2PbI3與CH3NH3PbBr3化合物的熱輸運性質。雜化鈣鈦礦中的極化轉子可以有效地散射聲子並影響材料的光電與熱電能量轉換效率；然而，由於鈣鈦礦的雜化特性與常規實驗設備和理論方法的局限性，目前對其微觀聲子散射機制還缺乏深入理解。在本項目中，我們將結合準彈性與非彈性中子散射大實驗裝備、熱輸運性質測量、電子與原子尺度的模擬計算開展研究。 申請人及其團隊的前期研究表明CH3NH3PbI3的熱輸運性質受[CH3NH3]+陽離子的極化旋轉影響較大。雜化鈣鈦礦的熱性質對包括熱電與光電能量裝換在內的許多工程應用都具有重要意義。申請人發現CH3NH3PbI3中有機陽離子較局域的四重旋轉模可以同時強烈地散射聲學與光學聲子，這與方鈷礦中填充原子所具有的局域振動模式截然不同。初步研究結果還表明雜化鈣鈦礦中的聲子散射對外場非常敏感，在本項目中，申請人將通過非簡諧晶格動力學計算與中子散射大科學裝置進一步研究晶格壓縮與外電場對聲子散射的調控機制。申請人堅實的前期研究基礎表明本項目是切實可行的。 已有研究表明雜化鈣鈦礦中有機陽離子的極化旋轉模對化學組分非常敏感。因此，通過摻雜可以實現極化旋轉、聲子散射與熱輸運性質的調控。在本項目中，申請人將通過理論計算模擬篩選合適的摻雜元素，從而為進一步的實驗研究提供指導。本項目的成功執行將加深雜化鈣鈦礦中極化轉子對聲子散射機制的認識，從而為熱輸運性質的有效調控奠定基礎。通過摻雜對雜化鈣鈦礦的熱輸運性質進行優化，將可以促進其在可持續能源領域的應用。

17201019.label: Realisation of objectives
17201019.value: Objective 1: We have studied hybrid crystal MAPbI3 with inelastic neutron scattering experiments and molecular dynamics simulations with a first-principles-based interatomic potential to better understand its lattice dynamics and the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal phase transition. Inelastic neutron scattering experiments were performed at 180 K using a single crystal sample to obtain the dynamics structure factor. Harmonic phonon properties at 0 K have been computed from first principles using the small displacement method. We reveal a dramatic change of the optical phonon lifetime accompanying the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal phase transition in MAPbI3. It is also found that the jumping rotational mode of organic cations plays a dominant role in determining the phonon properties. Objective 2: We have obtained the linewidths of the optical phonons of the tetragonal phase of MAPbI3 based on molecular dynamics simulations and the mode decomposition technique. The theoretical results were compared with experimental measurements, and they were found to be consistent. A dramatic change in the optical phonon lifetime was found to accompany the orthorhombic-to-tetragonal phase transition. The rotational mode of organic cations plays a dominant role in determining the phonon properties. We have also synthesized high-quality samples of layered Ruddlesden-Popper inorganic perovskite Cs2PbI2Cl2 and Cs2SnI2Cl2 and measured their thermal conductivities in a wide temperature range. Combining state-of-the-art theoretical models and experiments, we thoroughly investigate the nature of lattice dynamics and the thermal transport mechanisms in perovskites. Objective 3: Phonon scattering in the tetragonal phase of hybrid crystal MAPbI3 is found to be sensitive to hydrostatic pressure. A 6 kbar pressure can lead to a change of phonon lifetime for over one order of magnitude. This large tuning effect on phonon scatting strength is related to the four-fold rotation of the MA+ cations around the C-N axis. We find that the thermal properties are closely related to the combined characteristics of the inorganic framework lattice vibrations and the organic cations’ rotational modes. The optoelectronic and thermoelectric properties of hybrid perovskite crystals can be further improved via alloying. Our results provide a better understanding of the lattice dynamics of MAPbI3 and important insight into the phonon properties. We establish new design principles for engineering the lattice dynamics and thermal properties of hybrid crystals.

17201019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201019.value: Hybrid crystal MAPbI3 and layered Ruddlesden-Popper inorganic perovskites Cs2PbI2Cl2 and Cs2SnI2Cl2 have been systematically studied based on first-principles calculations, inelastic neutron experiments, and transport property measurements. The complete mode-based phonon lifetimes have been obtained, including those of the optical modes which are inaccessible from experiments because of the very large linewidths. We discover that phonon scattering in the tetragonal phase is extremely sensitive to compression. A hydrostatic pressure as low as 6 kbar can lead to a dramatic change of phonon lifetime for over one order of magnitude. This giant tuning effect on phonon scatting is found to be related to the four-fold rotation of the MA+ cations around C-N axis. Our results also suggest the importance of the fourth-order lattice anharmonicity and the diffusive thermal transport in layered Ruddlesden-Popper perovskites. We have provided a comprehensive understanding of the complicated lattice dynamics, facilitating accurate evaluation of the phonon and thermal transport properties. Additionally, we introduce a state-of-the-art and comprehensive scheme to study the anharmonic lattice dynamics of hybrid crystals and perovskites.

17201019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201019.value: The tight connection between optoelectrical properties and phonon behaviors in perovskites, such as hot carrier cooling mechanisms and acoustical-optical phonon up-conversion, requires a thorough understanding of the anharmonic lattice dynamics. However, the interplay between strong lattice anharmonicity and the phonon transport mechanisms in hybrid perovskites is yet to be further studied. This project provides a better understanding of the lattice dynamics of MAPbI3 and important insight into the pressure phonon relationship. Further studies of new strategies for phonon engineering and thermal optimization of hybrid crystals and the related perovskites are needed to facilitate practical applications.

17201019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201019.value: To better understand the thermal properties of hybrid crystals, we combine molecular dynamics simulations and neutron scattering measurements to study the lattice dynamics. A large pressure tuning effect on phonon scattering is discovered in MAPbI3. Using the mode decomposition technique, we obtain the linewidths of the optical phonons in the tetragonal phase, circumventing the experimental difficulties. This study indicates that significant phonon frequency renormalization that originates from the lattice anharmonicity in perovskites Cs2PbI2Cl2 and Cs2SnI2Cl2 can considerably amend the phonon linewidths, strongly affecting the lattice thermal conductivity. The conventional transport theory is found to break down in these perovskites, and a two-channel thermal transport behavior triggered by normal and diffuson-like phonons plays a critical role. The large pressure response of phonon scattering discovered in this project paves the way for further thermal engineering of hybrid perovskites.

17201219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17201219.value: 近年來，信息物理系統受到越來越多的關注。該系統中的信息通過網絡在傳感器、控制器和執行器之間交換。網絡的引入帶來很多優勢，如降低安裝維護費用，增加系統靈活性，以及極大地减少布綫。這些優勢促進了信息物理系統在很多領域中的廣泛應用，如航天航空控 制、智能交通和智能電網等。然而，由于計算機系統和網絡協議存在不可避免的缺陷，信息物理系統將受到惡意網絡攻擊的危險，如SQL Slammer 和Stuxnet 網絡攻擊。它們可能導致不可挽回經濟損失，甚至危害人們的生命。因此，信息物理系統的安全成爲一個關鍵的問題幷受到諸多國家和安全機構的關注。目前，信息物理系統安全問題已經在計算機和信息科學領域被廣泛地研究，這些研究關注信息保護，但相對少的研究從控制系統的角度保護系統。估計和控制器的設計是控制系統綜合的基本問題。在現有的信息物理系統估計和控制器設計的工作中，通常假設系統只受到一種攻擊且知道該攻擊的參數，而且假設執行器可以通過不受攻擊的信道來回饋攻擊的信息。這些假設便于數學方面的處理，但在現實應用中不一定能滿足。因爲，信息物理系統通常分布在一個很廣的區域，不同區域會受到不同類型的網絡攻擊。而且，有時不能保證存在上述提及的不受攻擊的通道，因爲大部分情况下，所有的通道都可能受到攻擊。因此，很多現有的控制理論的方法在應用于實際信息物理系統時具有局限性。鑒于大量的信息物理系統的應用以及它們的安全考慮，亟需安全的設計估計和控制器的方法，但這通常會遇到新的技術難題。因此，從理論和實際應用的角度，需要新的技術來設計組合網絡攻擊的檢測器，然後開發安全的估計和控制器。這是本項目主要的目的。本項目的基本成果將爲信息物理系統在工程領域中的應用提供一個安全的環境。

17201219.label: Realisation of objectives
17201219.value: All project objectives have been accomplished, with the details listed below. The project has successfully developed theoretical designs for detectors, secure estimators, and secure controllers in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) under diverse cyber-attacks. Effective detection mechanisms have been proposed for CPSs exposed to mixed cyber-attacks, accurately discerning attack types and estimating corresponding parameters. With these detectors, secure estimators have been designed for CPSs under cyber-attacks, with performance and resilience against such attacks analysed. Additionally, these detectors have been employed to develop secure controllers, achieving various control performances. Extensive studies have been conducted for designing detectors under diverse cyber-attacks. CPSs frequently face two primary types of cyber-attacks: Denial of Service (DoS) and deception attacks. For CPSs experiencing stealthy DoS attacks, an optimal estimating method has been established to identify the attack parameter. However, its practical implementation is hindered by the exponentially increasing computational time. Motivated by this, an approximate optimal estimating method has been proposed for stealthy DoS attacks, enjoying an improved computational efficiency compared to the optimal estimating method. For the first time, the approximate estimating method's stability condition and performance analysis have been presented in a theoretical framework. For CPSs subject to stealthy deception attacks, a binary hypothesis-based approach has been applied to formulate the optimal detector. However, this optimal detector results in low computational efficiency due to its exponentially growing number of linear Gaussian hypotheses. A suboptimal estimating approach has been introduced to overcome this limitation based on the interacting multiple models. This result has been further advanced to the mixed cyber-attack scenario where CPSs stealthily suffer from DoS and deception attacks. Building upon these detection methodologies, secure estimators for CPSs under various cyber-attacks have been extensively designed, and their stability and performance have been analyzed. Notice that most existing optimal estimators (OEs) are effective for DoS attacks wherein the attack success follows a Bernoulli process. However, this may be impractical, as real communication channels often exhibit time-correlated behavior. To address this limitation, an optimal linear filter (OLF) has been devised for CPSs under stealthy DoS attacks, in which the communication channels follow a two-state Markov model, referred to as Gilbert–Elliott channel. The estimation performance has been characterized, which shows how the DoS attack success rate affects the estimation performance. Along this line, a secure estimator has been developed for multi-channel CPSs under stealthy mixed DoS and deception attacks. Using a generalized pseudo-Bayesian algorithm, a centralized approximate optimal estimator (AOE) has been developed, with its stability and performance presented. The result has shown that the proposed AOE remains stable for unstable systems only if the attack success rate is below a certain threshold. Several controllers have been developed for different systems with desired performances maintained. For quadrotor aircraft with constrained controls, two bounded feedback controllers have been respectively crafted using tailored linear transformation. These controllers incorporate saturation functions, which effectively accommodate physical limitations and security requirements inherent to quadrotor aircraft. The stability conditions have been established, and some adjustable parameters have also been introduced into these controllers to enhance the system performance. Additionally, to optimize the stability properties of positive systems, a geometric programming framework has been presented. Within the proposed framework, both the problem of designing a robust controller under structural uncertainties and the problem of mixed-constraint parameter tuning for delayed positive linear systems can be resolved. These controller design methodologies have been integrated into designing secure controllers for CPSs under various cyber-attacks, yielding fruitful results. Several secure controllers have been established for CPSs experiencing deception attacks. For interval type-2 (IT2) fuzzy systems, the design of secure controllers under deception attacks has been explored, wherein attackers may launch attacks on only a part of the transmission nodes at some instant. To handle the scenario that the system state exceeds the modelling domain caused by attacks, an IT2 fuzzy sliding mode security controller has been designed based on a reconstruction method of the controller’s membership functions. An adaptive event-triggered mechanism has been integrated into designing a secure controller of nonlinear CPSs under stealthy deception attacks to save computing energy. By the Lyapunov–Krasovskii method, the stability conditions have been derived. This result has been extended to master-slave neural networked systems under deception attacks modelled by Markov processes. In addition to deception attacks, other cyber-attack types have been considered in the secure controller design for CPSs. Shifting attacks, which endeavour to modify the control policy by conveying false information to the controller after obtaining the output measurement, have been examined for hidden Markov Boolean networked control systems. By formulating such attacks in a permutation of the original output feedback control, a secure controller under shifting attacks has been established with its stability conditions derived. For the first attempt, interchanging attacks have been investigated for multi-loop networked systems. Such attacks swap transmitted information between different control loops. A unified framework has been proposed to describe the system under interchanging attacks, which also applies to DoS attacks. The stability conditions have been presented based on this framework and using Lyapunov–Krasovskii theory and stochastic analysis techniques. Lastly, mixed cyber-attacks have been examined for the master-slave synchronisation problem. These systems are subject to joint deception, replay, and DoS attacks. By representing mixed cyber-attacks in a unified Markov Jump framework, an event-triggered secure static output feedback controller has been established. The stability conditions have been Deduced using the Lyapunov–Krasovskii theory and stochastic analysis techniques.

17201219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201219.value: Theoretical designs of detectors, secure estimators, and secure controllers have been developed for diverse Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) experiencing various cyber-attacks, with their performance and stability examined. An approximate optimal estimating method for CPSs under stealthy DoS attacks has been proposed to detect attacks, offering improved computational efficiency [6]. For CPSs under stealthy deception attacks, a suboptimal detector based on the interacting multiple model has been introduced [2], which has been extended to mixed cyber-attack scenarios [3]. These detection ideas have extensively designed secure estimators for CPSs under various cyber-attacks. Considering time-correlated communication channels, an optimal linear filter has been devised for CPSs under stealthy DoS attacks [9]. A centralised approximate optimal estimator has been developed for multi-channel CPSs under stealthy mixed DoS and deception attacks [13]. Controllers have been devised for different systems, maintaining desired performances. For quadrotor aircraft, two bounded feedback controllers have been designed using tailored linear transformation [8]. A geometric programming framework has also been proposed to optimise positive systems' stability properties [1]. Based on the proposed controllers, secure controllers have been established for CPSs under various attacks. For fuzzy systems, a secure controller under deception attacks has been presented [12]. To save energy, an event-triggered secure controller has been formulated for nonlinear CPSs under stealthy deception attacks [4]. This result has been extended to master-slave neural networked systems under deception attacks modelled by Markov processes [7]. In addition to deception attacks, other types of attacks have been considered. Shifting attacks have been examined for hidden Markov Boolean networked systems [10]. Furthermore, interchanging attacks have been investigated for multi-loop networked systems [11]. Lastly, for mixed cyber-attacks, an event-triggered secure static output feedback controller has been established within a unified Markov Jump framework [5].

17201219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201219.value: The project has yielded several significant outcomes, offering promising avenues for future exploration and enhancement. 1) Exploring fully distributed attack detection methods. While most current detection systems rely on centralised architectures, there's a growing interest in fully distributed solutions. These alternatives offer improved scalability and efficiency by minimising network resource usage. Therefore, developing and assessing fully distributed attack detection strategies for CPSs is crucial. 2) Expanding the designs of secure estimators and controllers to accommodate network-induced challenges. CPSs frequently encounter limitations due to imperfect communication networks, which can introduce time delays, network switching, and packet disorders. These issues can significantly impact system performance, underscoring the need for meticulously designed secure estimators and controllers considering these factors. 3) Creating data-driven secure estimators and controllers for CPSs facing a variety of cyber-attacks. Traditionally, secure estimators and controllers have been developed through model-based analytical methods. However, accurately modelling some CPSs can be challenging due to their inherent uncertainties and complexities. These directions highlight the project's success in establishing a foundational understanding of CPS security and underline the importance of continued innovation in addressing the evolving landscape of cyber-physical threats.

17201219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201219.value: The increasing adoption of cyber-physical systems (CPSs) has coincided with a significant rise in cyber-attacks targeting these network-dependent systems. While security is a well-explored domain within computer science, a notable gap exists in control-theoretic security mechanisms designed explicitly for CPSs subjected to diverse cyber-attacks. This project seeks to address this deficiency by developing robust attack detectors, secure estimators, and controllers tailored for CPSs under various cyber-attacks, ensuring their reliable performance. Key achievements include establishing effective detectors for multiple cyber-attacks, including Denial-of-Service (DoS), deception, and mixed attacks. Notably, two detectors offering computational efficiency have been introduced for CPSs encountering stealthy DoS and deception attacks, with these approaches further adapted to scenarios involving mixed cyber-attacks. Building on these advancements, secure estimators have been crafted for CPSs, considering stealthy DoS attacks on time-correlated communication channels and hybrid attacks on multi-channel systems. Furthermore, controllers have been devised for diverse systems, such as quadrotor aircraft and positive systems, aiming to meet specific control objectives. Leveraging these foundational developments, secure controllers have been engineered to safeguard CPSs against various cyber-attacks, including deception, shifting, interchanging, and mixed attacks. This project's outcomes are critical in enhancing cyber-physical systems' security against various cyber threats, ensuring their desired operational performance.

17201419.label: Realisation of objectives
17201419.value: The three objectives of the project have been fully achieved. First, we have developed a novel mechanistic model that can simulate mixed-mode (tensile and shear) fractures in 3D rocks. At the core of this work is the double-phase-field method, which allows one to simulate and naturally distinguish between complex tensile and shear fractures in rocks. Second, we have validated the newly developed model of rock fracture using an extensive set of laboratory test data from Co-I Wong and other studies in the literature. The validation shows that the model can well reproduce rock fracturing processes, in both qualitative and quantitative manners. Lastly, using the newly developed model, we have investigated how cracking processes and mechanisms in 3D rocks under a variety of true triaxial conditions.

17201419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201419.value: The project has produced two main outcomes: (i) a technology for computer simulation of 3D rock fracturing processes in digital rock specimens, and (ii) new physical insights into rock fracturing processes under true triaxial conditions. The first outcome is based on the double-phase-field method that the project team has developed (Fei and Choo, 2021). This method enables one to simulate the complex topology of 3D tensile and shear cracks without any algorithms. Furthermore, it allows one to distinguish between tensile and shear fractures without any tools, which is highly attractive for studying the nature of rock fractures. The second outcome has been attained using the developed simulation technology. We have systematically investigated how the intermediate principal stress controls the 3D cracking behavior of rock specimens with preexisting ﬂaws (Sun et al., 2023). Our results show that both the orientation and magnitude of the intermediate principal stress exert dominant control over the cracking pattern and peak stress. Also, the eﬀects of the intermediate principal stress magnitude manifest diﬀerently depending on the orientation of principal stresses with respect to the ﬂaw. In addition, we have investigated energetic size effects on the compressive strength and cracking behavior of ﬂawed rocks through high-ﬁdelity simulations of mixed-mode fracture in quasi-brittle materials (Choo et al., 2023). We have found strong size effects on both the uniaxial compressive strength and cracking patterns. These ﬁndings of this work provide important insights into how the intermediate principal stress controls rock fracturing processes and how they manifest differently across scales. In terms of publications, we have produced 7 journal papers (6 published, 1 in preparation) and 1 conference paper.

17201419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201419.value: The research would be developed further as follows. First, the computational cost of the simulation methodology needs to be reduced dramatically. Even though the current methodology allows one to simulate 3D rock fracturing processes reliably, its computational cost is quite high. To make the methodology more practical, it is necessary to decrease the computational cost significantly. Another line of important future work is to shed more light on the effects of the intermediate principal stress on 3D rock fracturing processes. Particularly, it is recommended that one studies how the intermediate principal stress controls rock fracture in real-world 3D rock masses at the field scale.

17201419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201419.value: Crack initiation, growth, and coalescence in rock masses are responsible for the majority of failures of natural and engineered rock systems. Therefore, many rock engineering problems require us to analyze, predict, and control these rock fracture processes. Numerous studies have investigated the mechanisms and processes of cracking from pre-existing flaws (discontinuities) in rock masses. However, under true triaxial stress conditions, which are typical of rocks in the field, very little is understood about the mechanisms and processes of 3D fracturing. This knowledge gap is rooted mainly in our inability to characterize 3D rock fracturing processes under true triaxial stress conditions. To tackle this limitation, this project has developed a new technology for computer simulation of 3D fracturing processes in digital rocks. Using the new simulation technology, the project has produced new physical insights into 3D rock fracturing processes under a variety of true triaxial stress conditions. The outcomes will help address many rock engineering problems including the stability of rock caverns.

17201819.label: Project Objectives
17201819.value: Enlarging perovskite grains beyond the film thickness regime while maintaining good film quality. Perovskite grain size is limited to the film thickness by the “specimen thickness effect”. Meanwhile, grain enlargement in crystallization/recrystallization inevitably leads to poor film quality due to surface tension-driven shrinkage. To simultaneously achieve grain enlargement and maintain good film quality in perovskites (e.g., good morphology, well-packed grains, low density of voids/cracks, etc.), we will study exaggerated grain growth in perovskites and control the growth by modifying the adjacent layers of perovskites. We will also study the grain size enlargement to understand the growth mechanism. Consequently, we target to enlarge grains while maintaining high film quality, and obtain the foundational knowledge for improving the quality of polycrystalline perovskite films and device performances. Unique mono-core growth for substrate-integrated SGC perovskite films. By leveraging the know-how on exaggerated grain growth, we propose a new concept of mono-core growth in MVAD for controlled growth of SGC perovskite films from one small core to a large area in a metastable state triggered by exotic energy perturbation. The “mono-core” concept relies on the fact that thermodynamically less-stable small grains are swallowed by large grains during the growth of a plurality of grains (which were formed after energy perturbation). We will study the perovskite transformation in MVAD. Then the stable state will be studied experimentally as described in “Plan and Methodology, Part II-2(b)”. We will promote one core growth to form SGC films and eliminate polycrystalline perovskites by avoiding the transformation at unstable state where multi-nucleation occurs. Perovskite films made by MVAD are compatible with substrates because of the bridging effect of inorganic halide films. Thickness of perovskite SGC films will be controlled by tuning film formation parameters of the inorganic layers. Consequently, we aim to achieve different on-substrate crystalline perovskite films for device applications, and gain the knowledge of nucleus formation, grain growth and crystal film formation. Fundamental investigation on interfaces. We will comprehensively study the interfaces (i.e., GBs and interfacial contacts between perovskites and interface layers), which are critical for understanding grain growth and optimizing device performances and stability. Notably, GB migration holds the key to exaggerated grain growth and mono-core growth of the crystalline films. By combining with the understanding of grain growth in Objective (1), we will investigate GB migration and convection in quasi-solid films. We will then study GB and bulk diffusion of typical ions (i.e., organic cations, inorganic anions and metal ions) in crystalline perovskite films. Meanwhile, we will study the interfaces to achieve the good interfacial contacts with decent electrical transport/collection. Consequently, we will conclude the influences of GBs, defects, SGC quality, and interfaces targeted for exploring performance limits of SGC perovskite devices, which also address the myth of low efficiency of SGC perovskite devices nowadays.
rows: Enlarging perovskite grains beyond the film thickness regime while maintaining good film quality. Perovskite grain size is limited to the film thickness by the “specimen thickness effect”. Meanwhile, grain enlargement in crystallization/recrystallization inevitably leads to poor film quality due to surface tension-driven shrinkage. To simultaneously achieve grain enlargement and maintain good film quality in perovskites (e.g., good morphology, well-packed grains, low density of voids/cracks, etc.), we will study exaggerated grain growth in perovskites and control the growth by modifying the adjacent layers of perovskites. We will also study the grain size enlargement to understand the growth mechanism. Consequently, we target to enlarge grains while maintaining high film quality, and obtain the foundational knowledge for improving the quality of polycrystalline perovskite films and device performances.

17201819.label: Realisation of objectives
17201819.value: For objective 1, we previously reported a facile process based on introducing a PDMS cover on precursor and controlling the precursor with high viscosity and concentration to form MA-based perovskite single crystals. Recently, we further extended our work to introduce upside-down PDMS molding method with different periodic photonic patterns such as 2D grating and 3D grating patterns form the crystalline MA film. Interestingly, we achieved very good quality perovskite grating structures which can even show lasing with a remarkable threshold of 15.3 μJ/cm2 and linewidth of around 0.52 nm under pulsed excitations. Our work provides a strategy to fabricate geometrical parameter-controllable perovskite photonic resonators at room temperature. It suggests the promising applications of solution-based perovskites on different substrates including rigid and flexible ones. We believe that this new approach can inspire the industry in commercializing high-quality perovskite-based devices, such as solar cells, LEDs, and lasers [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2021, 13, 27313]. While a long-term operational stability of perovskite is an important topic, we demonstrated β-CsPbI3 single crystals with highly efficient and prolonged stability for LED applications through the incorporation of poly(maleic anhydride-alt-1-octadecene) in synthesizing the single crystals. Benefiting from the improved crystal phase quality, the photoluminescence quantum yield for β-CsPbI3 single crystals film remarkably increases from 34% to 89%. The corresponding red-emitting perovskite LEDs achieves a high external quantum efficiency of 17.8% and superior operational lifetime reaching 317 h [Adv. Mater. 2021, 33, 2008820]. We also studied single crystals of 2-dimensional perovskites with organic spacer ligands which are promising materials with superior stability and diversity for various photovoltaic devices. While traditional perovskite precursor solutions using high boiling point solvents easily cause poor uniformity, we demonstrate a new method for rapid crystallization of 2D perovskite by adopting low boiling point solvents. Our results show that 2D perovskite single crystals have a high quality and their processing is simplified and shortened. Photoconductors are made based on the 2D perovskite films and applied in visible light and X-ray detection effectively. These findings suggest the easily processed 2D perovskites promising for practical optoelectronic applications [Proc. SPIE, 1220903, 2022, doi:10.1117/12.2632581] For Objective 2, we achieved controllable crystallization for growing block like crystals as high-quality films with the improvements of increased crystallinity and strengthened preferred orientation through introducing rubidium cation into MA-based SnPb perovskites. The perovskite formed in a normal device structure and functioned as good UV-VIS-NIR (300-1100 nm) photodetectors simultaneously achieving larger photocurrent, lower noise current, high linear dynamic range of 110 dB and 3-dB cut-off frequency reaching 1 MHz. This work contributed to enriching the cation selection in Sn-Pb perovskite systems and offering a promising candidate for low-cost UV-VIS-NIR photodetection [Adv. Funct. Mater., 31, 2010532, 2021.] We further addressed the easy oxidation problems of Sn-based perovskites and developed a high-detectivity near-infrared photodetector using a tailored SnPb perovskite structure. Notably, we employed tin thiocyanate to form a double-side surface-preferred distribution in SnPb perovskites, in which the majority locates at bottom and top surfaces, and the tiny minority positions inside the films. The tailored perovskite structure with the unique additive distribution significantly improves the film morphology and antioxidation ability. Finally, self-powered SnPb perovskite photodetectors achieve a peak responsivity of 0.57 A W-1and a detectivity of 8.48 × 1012 Jones at 910 nm, a large linear dynamic range of 213 dB, accompanied by outstanding lifetime of 2300 h. This work opens a new avenue to developing high-performance near-infrared photodetectors. [ACS Energy Lett., 8, 577, 2023.] We also continued our work to achieve unencapsulated and stable devices from 2D perovskites. While it is difficult to achieve high quality in low-n-value (MA-free) FA-based Dion-Jacobson (DJ) 2D perovskites due to their low crystallinity and disordered orientation, we presented a novel 4APP(FA)3Pb4I13-based DJ-2D perovskite, where 4APP is 4-aminopiperidinium. The remarkable rigidity of 4APP and its strong hydrogen bonding with the perovskites prolong the perovskite intrinsic stability. The power conversion efficiency (PCE) of unencapsulated n=4 perovskite solar cells (PSCs) enhanced by 48%, representing one of the highest values in MA-free DJ 2D perovskite with n≤4. Remarkably, the unencapsulated devices retain 95% of their initial PCE after 2000 hr of operation under 1-sun illumination at 40°C, and 3000 hr exposure in the air at 85°C and 60-90% relative humidity. [Adv. Energy Mater., DOI: 10.1002/aenm.202302774.]. For Objective 3, it is highly desirable to address the high concentrations of defects at interfaces between perovskites and charge transport layers (CTLs) with an amount about 100 times more than inside the bulk perovskites, which substantially reduces both the efficiency and stability of the devices. We developed a solid-solid contact strategy to construct a multifunctional ion-lock layer with strongly chemical interaction to perovskites. Such multifunctional ion-lock layer significantly reduces the interface defects and tunes the work function, contributing to enhancing carrier extraction, high photovoltage, and photocurrent. Moreover, the multifunctional ion-lock layer successfully locks ions from movement and thus improves the stability of the devices. Finally, with multifunctional ion-lock layer, the open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current and fill factor of PSCs improve and thus power conversion efficiency increases together with a desirable long-term operational, storage, and humidity stability. Our findings provide guidelines for designing defect-minimizing interfaces between metal halide perovskites and hole transport layers. [Adv Funct. Mater., 2200473, 2022.] Besides, the use of interface passivation strategy to reduce the defects at the surface inorganic CTL and interface between CTL and perovskite layer is an effective approach to enhance the performance and device stability of PSCs. We advanced the interface by introducing imidazole bromide functionalized graphene quantum dots (I-GQDs) was employed as a interface modifications layer to passivate surface of SnO2 electron transport layer (ETL) and interface between SnO2 and perovskite layer. The I-GQDs play a multifunctional role with improving the conductivity of ETL, achieving a better energy level alignment, reducing the interface defects, providing a better growth substrate perovskite, and stabilizing perovskite. Correspondingly, I-GQDs-based devices can show improved efficiency with enhanced short-circuit current, fill factor, open-circuit voltage and long-term stability for FA-based PSCs. [Adv. Funct. Mater., 31, 2101438, 2021.] We further advanced hole transport layers (HTL) to realize large-area, flexible and high-performance PSCs. We demonstrated a self-assembled gradient Ti3C2Tx MXene incorporated PEDOT:PSS HTL to achieve high-performance large-area PSCs by establishing half-caramelization-based glucose-induced MXene redistribution. Through this process, the Ti3C2Tx MXene nanosheets are spontaneously dispersed and redistributed at the top region of HTL to form the unique gradient distribution structure composed of MXene:Glucose:PEDOT:PSS (MG-PEDOT). Our results showed that the MG-PEDOT HTL not only offers favorable energy level alignment and efficient charge extraction, but also improves the film quality of perovskite layer featuring enlarged grain size, lower trap density, and longer carrier lifetime. Consequently, the PCE of the flexible device based on MG-PEDOT HTL is increased by 36% compared to that of pristine PEDOT:PSS HTL. The encapsulated modules show remarkable long-term storage stability at 85 ℃ in ambient air and enhanced operational lifetime (~90% efficiency retention after 200 hours). This new approach shows a promising future of the self-assembled HTLs for developing high-performance and reliable flexible optoelectronic devices [Adv. Funct. Mater., 33, 2210063, 2023]. It should be noted that the outputs stated in this progress report are achieved through the financial support from this GRF fund together with some other research funds from RGC.

17201819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17201819.value: In the project, 38 research articles have been published in international peer-reviewed journals. We successfully develop facet approach to grow high quality perovskite single crystals. Interestingly, photonic structures can be incorporated to the perovskite crystals to introduce optical resonance effects and enhance the optical properties of the perovskite. We also proposed 2-dimensional perovskite crystal with organic spacer ligands with superior stability and diversity for various photovoltaic devices. The 2D perovskite single crystals have a high quality. Also their processing is simplified and shortened. Photoconductors are made based on the 2D perovskite films and applied in visible light and X-ray detection effectively. These findings suggest the easily processed 2D perovskites promising for practical optoelectronic applications. For device applications, it is important to form perovskite crystals on different substrates and CTLs. Our results show that by simple solution process, we can form block-like perovskite crystals on widely used hole transport layers for SnPb mixed perovskites with tunable bandgaps and thus wider optoelectronic applications. We further suppress the oxidation of Sn2+ ions and thus enhance material and device stability. Interestingly, we identify useful additives which can uniquely passivate the top and bottom surfaces of the SnPb perovskite to significantly diminish the oxidation and yet passivate the surface defects. To further enhance the stability, we successfully develop single-phase high-quality 2-dimensional perovskite crystals. The unencapsulated device show remarkable stability under high temperature and high humidity. To improve device performances, it is critical to have good electrical contact at the perovskite top and bottom surfaces. In this work, we developed interfacial engineering to passivate perovskite surface and grain boundaries. In addition, our results show that the modification of the interface can provide a good condition for promoting the perovskite formation. We can also tune the band structure to improve the carrier transportation between perovskite active layers and electrodes and thus the device performances. It should be noted that the outputs stated in this progress report are achieved through the financial support from this GRF fund together with some other grants from RGC as stated in the acknowledgement of the publications.

17201819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17201819.value: While the high throughput fabrication of perovskite optoelectronic devices particularly for photovoltaic devices is very important. The development of material libraries for electron and hole transport layers as well as electrodes is very important for the use of perovskite devices in practical applications. The materials can not only offer good band alignment with perovskites for carrier transportation but also favor the crystallization of perovskites and suppress defects. Meanwhile, the solution process approaches of the materials shall be established so that all-solution processes of perovskite device from electrodes to active layers can be realized for high throughput fabrication. The solvents, methods and conditions of the solution process approaches shall be compactable to the solution-based perovskites without degrading the optical and electrical properties of perovskites. With the achievement of the above research projects, it is in a good position to advance the scale up technologies such as blade coating and slot die for developing the recipes and inks for large scale fabrication of perovskite modules. The realization of the modules can not only reduce the power consumption and cost in fabrication but also offer in performances for not only meeting carbon neutrality but also advancing sustainable and dynamic society.

17201819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17201819.value: While perovskite materials have shown potentials for realizing high performance optoelectronic devices, it is very important to develop approaches for realizing crystalline perovskites and understand mechanisms of the formation and the optical and electrical properties of perovskites. Here, we have developed facile solution-process approaches for forming perovskite single crystals using perovskite precursors with high viscosity and concentration with simple polymer covers. We further enhance the optical properties by introducing grating-patterned covers. The good electrical contact of perovskites with CTLs is also demonstrated for the use of perovskites in optoelectronics by advancing the solution processes. Notably, the perovskite materials cover SnPb alloy and 2-dimensional nanomaterials for tuning the bandgap and improving the stability. To further improving electrical properties of perovskite devices, several interfacing engineering methods have been realized for good electrical contacts with perovskite surfaces by reducing defects, promoting perovskite crystallization and improving the band alignment. The influences of the solution processes on perovskite materials and optoelectronic properties have also been investigated. Consequently, the work contributes to not only develop perovskite single crystal for high-performance devices but also the fundamental understanding of the perovskites and their optical and electrical properties for the practical applications of perovskites for emerging photovoltaics and photonics.

17202019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202019.value: 本項目將研究完全在線匹配模型下的在線算法及其競爭比。完全在線匹配問題是經典的二分圖在線匹配問題的推廣形式。許多新興的電子平台服務比如叫車、拼車等場景中的匹配問題都是完全在線匹配問題的特例。我們的初步研究結果表明經典的二分圖在線匹配算法比如Ranking和Water-filling算法都能被推廣為完全在線匹配模型中的在線算法，并進行相應的理論分析。本項目將進一步在如下三個方面進行研究： 1. 不帶權值的二分圖上的最優算法及競爭比刻畫： 這個問題又可以細分以Water-filling為代表的分數算法，以及以Ranking算法為代表的整數算法兩種。分數算法中目前最好的競爭比為58.5%，而相應的上界為63.2%。而整數算法中目前最好的競爭比為56.7%，而相應的上界同樣為63.2%。我們將提出和Water-filling以及Ranking不一樣的算法從而改進這些競爭比。 2. 不帶權值的一般圖上的最優算法及其競爭比刻畫，以及與二分圖的對比： 我們的初步研究結果表明一般圖上的算法及其競爭比分析比二分圖要困難許多。然而目前並沒有任何結果能嚴格證明在一般圖上的最有算法及其競爭比會比二分圖的情形下要差。因此，本項目的第二個目標是對一般圖上的競爭比，尤其其上界作進一步的研究，并以此為出發點釐清完全在線匹配問題在二分圖及一般圖上的異同。 3. 帶權值的完全在線匹配問題： 在叫車、拼車等場景， 允許邊帶有權值是非常自然甚至必須的假設。因此，我們將進一步將無權圖上的結果推廣到帶權值的完全在線匹配模型中，從而研究在後者中最優算法及其競爭比。 最後，我們將在模擬及實際數據中測試本項目中提出的算法，以驗證其成效。

17202019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17202019.value: We have studied bipartite and general unweighted graphs, have given algorithms beyond the classical ones, and have provably established the superiority of our new algorithms. Specifically: - In FOCS 2020, we published a paper that introduced two new online algorithms that provably outperform the classical ones (Ranking and Balance) in terms of worst-case competitive analysis. Conceptually, this opens up new research directions for exploring further algorithmic ideas in our new fully online matching model. - In JACM, we gave tight competitive analysis for classical algorithms (Ranking and Balance), and established that the fully online matching problem is strictly harder than the original online bipartite matching problem, in the sense that the best achievable competitive ratio is smaller. The results from the above two papers successfully addressed the first two objectives. - Regarding the third objective, we have studied the first-in-first-out (FIFO) model and the special case of unweighted graphs, as an initial step toward understanding the weighted case which also makes the FIFO assumption. This study has led to several preliminary results including a competitive online algorithm, which has the potential of further developing into a research paper. The results from the third objective are still a work in progress that will likely lead to another research paper. - Regarding the fourth objective, we have implemented the algorithms from this project and those from previous works, and have evaluated them on graphs generated from real-world datasets. Other than confirming the superior performance of our algorithms, we also found two empirical algorithms with promising performance in our experiments. This finding has triggered a new research project to provide a theoretical explanation for their good performance. The results from the fourth objective serve as the empirical section of a research paper that is currently under submission.

17202019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17202019.value: As mentioned above, the findings in this project have triggered a new research project on providing a theoretical explanation for two empirical algorithm's good performance. The PI will further investigate in this direction and seek funding support either from RGC or from NSFC to support this new project.

17202019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17202019.value: In sum, the project has systematically studied the design and analysis of algorithms in a new online matching model called fully online matching, which was proposed to capture applications such as ride-sharing and ride-hailing. The project has successfully provided a tight analysis of classical online algorithms from the original online matching model and has proposed new algorithms with superior performance. The project has further implemented the algorithms and empirically evaluated them on real-world data.
