17202719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17202719.value: Close contact is known to be the primary route for transmission of respiratory infections, e.g. influenza, as the proximity facilitates a direct and rapid transfer of pathogens emitted by exhalation and in respiratory secretions from the infected person to a susceptible person, limiting the influence of viral inactivation. However, there is less understanding of the mechanism(s) in the close contact route than the long-range airborne or fomite routes. Contradictory recommendations have been made by the WHO and US CDC to prevent influenza transmission, in part because controversy remains on the most effective disease transmission route(s). Infectious pathogens originate from the expiratory activities of the infected person, such as coughing, sneezing, talking and breathing, and are dispersed by expiratory air streams, body thermal plumes and room airflow. When in close contact, transmission may occur through multiple pathways. Large droplets are deposited on the skin, clothing, and personal belongings of the susceptible person (i.e., the immediate surface subroute) and on the mucosa of the mouth, nose, and eyes of the susceptible person (i.e., the large droplet subroute), and fine droplets or droplet nuclei in the expiratory air streams are directly inhaled (i.e., the short-range airborne subroute). The latter two subroutes have been studied separately in standing/sitting situations, whereas the immediate surface subroute has not been studied. We plan to study the relative magnitude of exposure occurring through three subroutes (large droplets, short-range airborne, and immediate surface) during close contact, using influenza viruses as an example. Although the large droplet route is traditionally believed to dominate, we hypothesize that the short-range airborne and immediate surface subroutes are at least as important if not dominant. Our preliminary studies show that close contact involves body and head movement, and possible breathing synchronization, which can significantly modify the expiratory flow and/or the body plume. We propose to perform the first detailed observational study of close contact behavior with a focus on body/head movement. The new data will be applied to understand exposure to the exhaled droplets due to face-to-face close contact using both laboratory and computational fluid dynamics simulations. A new simple close contact model will be developed for integration into our existing unique multi-route model of respiratory infection, which will be used to analyze existing influenza outbreaks to gain further insights. The relative contribution of individual close contact subroutes will be compared and quantified, and effective intervention methods can be chosen or developed. 密切接觸是呼吸道感染傳播的主要途徑，密切接觸有助於將呼氣和呼吸道分泌物中發出的流感病原體從感染者直接快速轉移到易感人群，從而限制病毒滅活。然而，對密切接觸感染途径機制的理解比遠程空气或表面传播的理解要少。世界衛生組織和美國疾病預防控制中心曾提出防止流感傳播相互矛盾的指南，部分源于有效疾病傳播途徑的爭議。 傳染性病原體起源於感染者的呼氣活動，例如咳嗽，打噴嚏，說話和呼吸，並且通過呼氣氣流，身體熱羽流和室內氣流扩散。當密切接觸時，病原體可以通過多個途徑進行傳播。大水滴可沉積在易感人皮膚（直接表面子路徑），衣服和個人物品上以及易感人的口腔，鼻子和眼睛粘膜（大液滴子路徑）上，直接吸入呼氣氣流中的細小液滴或液滴核（即短程空氣傳播子路徑）。後兩個子路徑已在站立/坐姿情況下被分別研究，而直接表面子路徑尚未被探索。 我們計劃以流感病毒為例，研究在密切接觸過程中通過三個子路徑（大水滴，短程空气和直接表面）暴露的相對大小。雖然傳統上認為大液滴路徑占主導地位，我們假設短程空中和直接表面子路徑至少同樣重要。 我們的初步研究已表明，密切接觸涉及身體和頭部運動，以及可能的呼吸同步，這可以顯著改變呼氣流量和/或身體羽流。我們建議首先進行密切接觸行為的詳細觀察研究，重點是身體/頭部運動。新數據將用於理解由於使用實驗室和計算流體動力學模擬進行面對面密切接觸而對呼出液滴的暴露。將開發一種新的簡單密切接觸模型，用於整合我們現有的獨特呼吸道感染多路徑模型，該模型將用於分析現有的流感爆發，以獲得進一步的理解。我们还將比較和量化各個緊密接觸子路由的相對貢獻，並且可以用于選擇或開發有效的干預方法

17202719.label: Realisation of objectives
17202719.value: Objective 1: To obtain new data and characteristics of close contact behavior in a student office, including conversation (using sound intensity) and body/head movements (Tasks 1 - 2) The work in this task is the foundation of the project. We synthesized the existing understanding of the mechanisms of close contact transmission and proposed the existence of three sub-routes of transmission including a new immediate body-surface contact. We also distinguish a “body contact from close contact. We identified that the timescales over which data should be collected to assess the transmission risk during close contact events are much shorter than those required for the distant airborne or fomite routes (Zhang et al, 2020, Indoor Air). This was followed by a field study in postgraduate student office with a new device for detecting and recording head and body motions of each student. They spent 9.7% of time in close contact, with 4 close contacts/h. Additionally, we analyzed change of travel data (close contacts in subways) before and during the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong (Zhang et al., 2021, CID and Cities). Four journal papers were published including a review. Importantly, as we proceeded with the experimental study, we immediately realized the need for a theoretical framework for comparing the short-range airborne and large droplet transmission. The mechanism of exposure to droplets expired at close contact, however, remained surprisingly unexplored. We developed a simple mathematical model of expired flows and droplet dispersion/deposition /inhalation. The most significant finding is that the short-range airborne route dominates at most distances studied during both talking and coughing. The work was published in early 2020 (Chen et al., 2020, Building and Environment, 106859), which has received considerate interests among the international peers, and became the foundation for WHO to recognize the importance of short-range inhalation route for SARS-CoV-2 in late 2020. Objective 2: To study the proximity effect on exposure due to the immediate surfaces and short-range airborne subroutes as compared to the large droplet exposure, as affected by head/body movement. (Task 4) Head movement alters the direction of people’s expired air flow, therefore affecting their conversational partners’ level of exposure. We used a dynamic meshing method in computational fluid dynamics to simulate the head movement of a human-shaped thermal manikin and considered two basic head movement, i.e. shaking its head (saying no) or was nodding its head (saying yes). The target manikin’s level of exposure was significantly reduced due to a new sweeping mechanism (Chen et al., 2022, . Journal of Hazardous Materials, 130406). We have realized the importance of exhaled droplet origins in close contact transmission. We found from CFD modelling that the bronchiole-originated droplets in the lower airways deposit as they travel upwards in the airway during exhalation process, and only very fines can survive the journey (Yu et al., 2020, Journal of Aerosol Science). Objective 3: To investigate the effectiveness of intervention methods to prevent exposure such as surgical masks, N95 masks, hand hygiene, oral hygiene, and personalized ventilation. (Tasks 5-6). Due to the COVID pandemic urgency, we have focused on this objective. With the support of the new SARS-CoV-2 transmission data, we developed a new short- and long-range airborne continuum model (Li et al, 2022, Indoor Air, e12946). One surprising major finding is that the room ventilation rate significantly affects the short-range airborne route, in contrast to traditional belief. A ventilation rate of 10 L/s per person provides a similar concentration vs distance decay profile to that in outdoor settings. This was the scientific basis for a ventilation standard for infection control. The model was refined later in Jia et al (2022, Building and environment, 109166), by developing a two-stage jet model. Both physical distancing and adequate ventilation are essential for minimising infection risk, especially in high-intensity activity or densely populated spaces. We applied our understanding to investigate a few COVID-19 outbreaks including a hospital outbreak in Nanjing (Ding et al., 2021, Science of the Total Environment, 141710), a high-rise housing outbreak (Kang et al., 2020, Annals of Internal Medicine. 173, 974-980), a restaurant outbreak (Li et al., 2021, Building and Environment, 196, 107788) and the Diamond Princess cruise ship outbreak (Xu et al., Building and environment, 198, 107839). We provided the first evidence for airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2, paved the way for WHO’s eventual recognition. In early 2020, the PI led a large team including his past team members and hundreds of students in gathering online official data in 320 prefectural municipalities in China (Qian et al, 2021, Indoor Air, 31, 639-645), and identified more than 300 outbreaks and found that SARS-CoV-2 were transmitted indoors. Their work identified and confirm that improving dilution including ventilation, social distancing and mask wearing are the most important intervention methods. To disseminate their work, the PI also published a number of editorials and perspectives (Li, 2021, Indoor Air, 3 papers, and Li et al., 2021, Chinese Science Bulletin, 66). Importantly, they re-defined transmission routes into aerosol inhalation, drop spray and surface touch, which was almost immediately accepted by US CDC and currently being considered by a WHO working group that PI serves as Co-chairman. Note: This project together with a related (completed) CRF project has become probably the most important project in PI’s academic career.

17202719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17202719.value: Close contact is known to be the primary route for transmission of respiratory infections, but before this project, the large droplet route has been considered as the predominant route for more than a century. This proposal was originally developed following the contradictory recommendations by the WHO and US CDC to prevent influenza transmission, in part because controversy remains on the most effective disease transmission route(s). There are at least two major and revolutionary findings that have shifted the major recommendations by the world leading health authorities. First, the short-range airborne transmission predominates the close-contact route of respiratory infection. This was achieved by developing a simple mathematical model of expired flows and droplet dispersion/deposition /inhalation. The new finding, published just at the start of the pandemic, was confirmed by the infection data of the pandemic, and currently widely accepted. Second, building ventilation also reduces the short-range airborne exposure in contrast to traditional belief, which explains why most SARS-CoV-2 transmission occurred indoors but not outdoors (also first identified by our team). This finding was made with the support of the new SARS-CoV-2 transmission data and development of a new short- and long-range airborne continuum model. For the first time, our work defined the close-contact behavior (distance, direction and head/body movement, expiration/inspiration) for respiratory infection, and their association with short-range transmission of respiratory infection such as COVID-19. We also redefined the transmission routes for respiratory infection, inhalation, spray, and touch instead of airborne, large droplets and fomite routes. A new expired sweeping jet mechanisms was identified to explain a reduction of airborne exposure during conversation with head shaking (saying no) and head nodding (saying yes), which also demonstrates the complexities during general conservational scenarios. We applied our understanding to investigate a few COVID-19 outbreaks including a hospital outbreak in Nanjing, a high-rise housing outbreak, a restaurant outbreak and the Diamond Princess cruise ship outbreak. We provided the first evidence for airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2, paved the way for WHO’s eventual recognition. Both physical distancing and adequate ventilation are essential for minimising infection risk, especially in high-intensity activity or densely populated spaces. Our identification of more than 300 outbreaks in early 2020 in China with three or more secondary infections 2020, revealed for the first time that SARS-CoV-2 were transmitted indoors. Our work identified and confirmed that improving dilution including ventilation, social distancing and mask wearing are the most important intervention methods.

17202719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17202719.value: Our work demonstrated for the first time, that inhalation exposure predominates at close range. This has at least two major implications. First, there is a further need to study the relative infection risk between short-range inhalation and long-range inhalation. This is a complex task, but important in intervention in terms of identifying the most effective and economic intervention methods. The most important is probably the population (people and buildings) data of close contact, and sharing indoor space. This population data differs from occupant data such as in an office as studied in this project. Such population data will not become available before sensors with privacy protection is available in many indoor spaces. The PI currently developing a new technology in an existing CRF project with this application in mind. Second, the most important implication is in the need of paradigm change in infection prevention policy. There is a growing recognition of the inhalation transmission of respiratory infection not only for SARS-CoV-2, but also for many other respiration infections including influenza. This will need a collective effort, and as an individual, we shall do our share by further research and participating in various activities in leading health organizations and professional societies.

17202719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17202719.value: Close contact offers the highest possible exposure risk of expired droplets. The large droplet route has been considered as the predominant route for more than a century, e.g. there has been contradictory recommendations by the WHO and US CDC to prevent influenza transmission before and during the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic. Two revolutionary findings have shifted the major recommendations by the world leading health authorities during the COVID-19 pandemic. First, the short-range inhalation predominates the close-contact route of respiratory infection. Second, building ventilation also reduces the short-range inhalation in contrast to traditional belief, which explains why most SARS-CoV-2 transmission occurred indoors but not outdoors as first identified by our team. For the first time, our work defined the close-contact behavior for respiratory infection. We also redefined the transmission routes for respiratory infection, inhalation, spray, and touch instead of airborne, large droplets and fomite routes. A new expired sweeping jet mechanisms was identified to explain a reduction of airborne exposure during conversation. We provided the first evidence for airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2, providing evidence for WHO’s eventual recognition. Our work identified that improving dilution including ventilation, social distancing and mask wearing are the most important intervention methods.

17203119.label: Realisation of objectives
17203119.value: Objective 1: We created a largescale synthetic dataset for photometric stereo using shapes from 2 existing 3D datasets and BRDFs from an existing real-world material dataset. We rendered each shape under 1,296 regularly-sampled views, 2 randomly selected BRDFs, and 64 random directional lights using a physics-based raytacer. This gave us a dataset of 85,212 samples, each with 64 images rendered under different light directions. This dataset was employed for training and testing the models developed in Objectives 2, 3, and 4 respectively. Objective 2: We proposed a flexible fully convolutional network, named PS-FCN, for estimating a normal map of an object from calibrated photometric stereo images. Compared to previous per-pixel methods, PS-FCN inherently takes observations in a neighborhood into account in computing the feature map, making it possible to take advantage of local context information (e.g., surface smoothness prior). PS-FCN is composed of three components, namely a shared-weight feature extractor for extracting feature representations from the input images, a fusion layer for aggregating features from multiple input images, and a normal regression network for inferring the normal map. Thanks to the fusion layer, PS-FCN can take an arbitrary number of photometric stereo images with their associated light directions as input in an order-agnostic manner, and predicts a normal map of the object in a fast feed-forward pass. Further, we introduced a pre-processing step for normalizing the per-pixel observations to allow PS-FCN handle surfaces with spatially-varying BRDFs. Extensive experiments were carried out to validate the effectiveness of PS-FCN and SOTA results were achieved. Objective 3: We proposed a light calibration network, named LCNet, that takes an arbitrary number of photometric stereo images as input and estimates their corresponding light directions and intensities. LCNet exploits both local features extracted from a single image and global features aggregated from all input images to predict the light direction and intensity for each image. Specifically, LCNet is a multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) network. It comprises three components, namely a shared-weight feature extractor for extracting local features from the input images, an aggregation layer for aggregating global features from multiple input images, and a shared-weight lighting estimation sub-network for predicting per-image light direction and intensity from both local and global features. It takes the observations of the object together with the object mask as input, and outputs the light directions and intensities in the form of softmax probability vectors. These vectors are then converted to 3-vector light directions and scalar intensity values by simply taking the middle value of the range with the highest probability. Experiments on both synthetic and real datasets showed that our method significantly outperformed previous methods. Objective 4: We integrated our LCNet (light calibration network developed in Objective 3) with our PS-FCN (normal estimation network developed in Objective 2) for predicting the normal map of an object under uncalibrated lightings. We normalized the input images by the light intensities predicted by LCNet and retrained the normal estimation network using the ligth directions predicted by LCNet as input to make it robust to inaccurate lighting information. Experiments on both synthetic and real data were carried out to evaluate the performance of our networks for uncalibrated photometric stereo. Through detailed analysis, we found the features learned by LCNet closely resemble attached shadows, shadings, and specular highlights. Based on this observation, we further proposed a guided calibration network, named GCNet, that explicitly leverages object shape and shading information (obtained from the output of the normal estimation network) as input for improved lighting estimation. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets showed that GCNet achieves improved results in lighting estimation for uncalibrated photometric stereo. Objective 5: We created a synthetic dataset using 10 complex objects from 3 existing 3D datasets. We constructed a scene with a horizonal plane and a vertical plane and placed the object on the horizonal plane to minic an object sitting on a desk in front of a wall. We rendered each scene using physics-based raytracers which also rendered cast shadows onto the desk and wall. Each scene was rendered under 128 uniformly sampled near point lights. This dataset was employed for training and evaluating the model developed in Objective 6. Besides, we created another synthetic dataset with 2 objects using a physics-based raytracer. We rendered objects under two sets of lightings, one with directional lights and the other with environment maps. We randomly sampled 20 viewpoints on the upper hemisphere, with 15 viewpoints used for training and 5 viewpoints for testing the model developed in Objective 7. Objective 6: We introduced a method, named S3-NeRF, to optimize a neural reflectance field for a non-Lambertian scene from single-view images captured under different near point lights. Our method jointly recovers the geometry (i.e., occupancy field) and BRDFs of the scene by fully utilizing the shading and shadow cues with a physics-based rendering pipeline. Interestingly, our results on scenes with complicated shapes and materials show that complete scene geometry can be faithfully reconstructed just from single-view photometric stereo images. Moreover, comprehensive method analysis demonstrated that our method is robust to scenes with different geometry, materials, and light distributions. Our method supports downstream applications like novel-view synthesis and scene relighting. Objective 7: We introduced a neural inverse rendering method, named PS-NeRF, for multiview photometric stereo under uncalibrated lights. We first represent an object with a neural radiance field whose surface geometry is regularized by the normals estimated from multi-light images. We then jointly optimize the surface normals, BRDFs, visibility, and lights to minimize an image reconstruction loss based on a shadow-aware rendering layer. Experiments on both synthetic and real dataset showed that our method outperforms existing multi-view photometric stereo methods and neural rendering methods. Notably, our method can recover high-quality surface using as few as 5 input views.

17203119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203119.value: For calibrated photometric stereo, we introduced the first data-driven all-pixel method, named PS-FCN, which can take an arbitrary number of photometric stereo images with their associated light directions as input and predicts a normal map of the object. Compared to previous methods, PS-FCN allows the number, order, and directions of lights in testing different from those used in training, making it much more practical. This work was published in a conference paper in ECCV [1]. Our code and model can be found at https://github.com/guanyingc/PS-FCN. We further extended this work to handle surfaces with spatially-varying BRDFs by introducing a pre-pocessing step to normalize the per-pixel observations. This extension was published in a journal article in TPAMI [1]. Our code and model can be found at https://guanyingc.github.io/SDPS-Net. For uncalibrated photometric stereo, we proposed a two-stage model, named SDPS-Net, which comprises LCNet for light estimation and PS-FCN for normal estimation respectively. By explicitly learning to estimate light directions and intensities, our model can take advantage of the intermediate supervision, resulting in a more interpretable behavior compared to the end-to-end approach. Besides, our LCNet can also be seamlessly integrated with other exisiting calibrated photometric stereo methods, enabling them to deal with unknown lighting conditions. This work was published in a conference paper in CVPR [2]. Our code and model can be found at https://guanyingc.github.io/SDPS-Net. We further extended LCNet and proposed a guided calibration network, named GCNet, that explicitly leverages object shape and shading information obtained from the normal estimation network for improved light estimation. This work was published in a conference paper in ECCV [3]. Our code and model can be found at https://guanyingc.github.io/UPS-GCNet. Other than directional lights, we also studied the photometric stereo problem under alternative lighting conditions, including near point lights and environment maps. We proposed a novel method, named S3-NeRF, to recover a non-Lambertain scene from photometric stereo images captured under different near point lights. Our method adopts a neural reflectance field representation and a physics-based differentiable rendering pipeline, and jointly optimizes the scene geomtery and BRDFs using the information-rich shading and shadow cues. This work was published in a conference paper in NeurIPS [4]. Our code and model can be found at https://ywq.github.io/s3nerf. We also proposed a neural inverse rendering method, named PS-NeRF, for multi-view photometric stereo under uncalibrated lights. Our method jointly optimizes the surface normals, visibility, spatially-varying BRDFs, and lights, and achieves SOTA results in multi-view photometric stereo. This work was published in a conference paper in ECCV [5]. Our code and model can be found at https://ywq.github.io/psnerf.

17203119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203119.value: Although state-of-the-art results have been achieved, our proposed solutions, like most of the exisiting works, have ignored inter-reflection effects in image formation in order to make the our problem more managable. However, inter-reflections can often be observed in real images of objects with reflective surfaces. Ignoring inter-reflection would definitely result in degraded performance for such objects. In the future, we would like to further extend our work by explicitly taking inter-reflections into account. One possible direction would be considering reflected rays in differentiable rendering while optimizing the neural surface representation.

17203119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203119.value: This project studies the problem of photometric stereo, which aims at recovering fine-grained surface details of an object by observing it under different lightings. We have proposed deep-learning-based solutions under different settings, including known directional lights, unknown directional lights, known near point lights, and multi-view unknown lights. Our solutions have achieved state-of-the-art results and have been published in top conferences and journals in computer vision and machine learning. In particular, our solutions for unknown lights settings eliminate the need for light calibration, which is the most tedious and delicate step in photometric stereo, making photometric stereo technique much more user-friendly and less expert-dependent. The recovered geomerty and appearance can support novel-view synthesis, scene relighting, and material editing. It has important applications like surface inspection, augmented reality, 3D animation, cultural heritage preservation, etc.

17203219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17203219.value: Over their life cycle, buildings contribute significantly to carbon emissions. Hong Kong has the highest density of population in the world, so building high-rise blocks for housing is the norm, and the Hong Kong government has adopted a prefabrication strategy for all public housing developments. In theory, the use of prefabrication should lead to a reduction in buildings’ life cycle carbon emissions, by reducing the carbon footprint of materials and products, improving the efficiency of construction processes, and enhancing the quality of constructed facilities. However, there is a lack of systemic understanding of prefabricated buildings’ embodied carbon. According to our preliminary reviews, the system boundaries of prefabricated buildings’ carbon assessment have seldom been made explicit. Different models, methods and units of analysis are employed, hampering meaningful benchmarking. The estimation of buildings’ embodied carbon emissions remains a labor-intensive process, with limited accountability. The aim of this project is to develop a smart-tech integrated system for estimating and benchmarking ‘cradle-to-end of construction’ embodied carbon emissions of high-rise prefabricated public residential buildings in Hong Kong. This system consists of three components: Novel systemic multi-levelled SimaPro-based models, a smart-tech platform, and emission key performance indicators (KPIs). The project will be carried out over a 36-month period in three interrelated stages. First is the development of the emission estimating models, which will cover five levels of prefabrication, namely, material, component, assembly, flat and building. Cradle-to-gate embodied carbon emissions will be calculated using SimaPro software, and transport and construction-related carbon emissions will be measured using the process analysis method. Second is the establishment of the smart-tech platform, which will integrate Internet-of-Things (IoT) technologies, including radio frequency identification (RFID) and smart meters for automated data collection, and application program interfaces (APIs) for data transfer and conversion among the IoT, building information models and SimaPro software. The platform will be tested using a real-life building project. Third is the development of emission KPIs at the five levels of prefabrication among wide housing projects. The multi-levelled SimaPro-based models will provide a novel systemic approach for achieving more reliable and valid estimations of prefabricated buildings’ embodied carbon. The smart-tech platform will help to achieve better quality carbon inventory data and more efficient emission estimations. The KPIs will help to achieve meaningful benchmarking of embodied carbon emissions among public residential buildings in Hong Kong. The system can be adapted to develop scalable solutions for significant carbon reductions in the building sector. 建築物全生命周期的碳排持續而顯著。香港擁有世界城市最密集的人口， 高層住宅建築應用非常普遍；同時預製技術也通過政策扶持在公共建築中全面實行。理論上，采用預製技術能夠減少建築材料的碳足跡，提高建造效率，改善工程質量，從而減少全生命周期碳排放。但是，目前對於預製建築的隱含碳排放缺少系統性理解。根據我們的初步探索，在預製建築碳排放評估過程中，系統邊界未被準確理解應用。不同的模型，方法和統計單位被不同的研究所采用，不利於有效碳排評估與比較。目前對於建築物隱含碳排放的評估還停留於“評估中頗費周折，評估後鮮有斟酌”這一階段。 該項研究的目的是建立一個智能技術綜合系統，用於估算和標準化“建築從材料生產到建造結束”階段的香港高層預製公共住宅建築的碳排放。該系統由三個部分組成：系統化多層級的基於SimaPro的碳排放模型，智能技術平臺以及碳排放關鍵性能指標（KPI）。該項目開展時間為36個月。第一階段是從五個層次建立碳排放估算模型，即材料，平面構件，3D構件，建築單元和整棟建築。原材料生產到預製件生產的碳排放是基於SimaPro軟件進行計算，而過程分析方法將被用於計算與運輸和現場安裝相關的碳排放。第二階段是基於物聯網（IoT）的智能技術平台的建立，包括射頻識別（RFID）和自動數據採集的智能儀表的安裝，以及用於數據傳輸的應用程序接口（API）的开发。該平台將使用實際建築項目作为案例進行測試。第三阶段是在廣泛的住房項目的五個預製水平上製定碳排放關鍵績效指標。 多層級SimaPro模型將采用創新的基於系統理論的方法，從而得到更准確可靠的預製建築隱含碳排放的評估結果。這一智能技術平臺將有助於研發更好的碳排清單和進行更有效地碳排放評估。這些碳排表現評估係數將有效促進香港預製高層公屋的碳排定額。這一體系也將爲建築減排提供多種彈性解決方案。

17203219.label: Realisation of objectives
17203219.value: All three project objectives have been successfully achieved. Actually, the project went beyond by delivering more good-quality research outputs and paving a solid foundation for further research on the topic of prefabrication and life cycle carbon assessment and reduction. For achieving Objective 1, we first defined the LCA system boundary as the cradle-to-end-of-construction stage for this project, building upon our prior research on the carbon emissions of high-rise prefabricated buildings (GRF 17207115). A detailed list of embodied carbon-related information during cradle-to-end-of-construction was determined and summarized, including the construction process, activities, specified procedure, data categories, and data sources. Subsequently, we constructed a multi-level framework of prefabricated buildings, namely, material (e.g., concrete, steel), component (e.g., a precast slab and a staircase), assembly (e.g., a non-volumetric precast facade panel completed with window and a volumetric precast bathroom/kitchen pod), flat (a residential unit) and building (the entire building). This framework facilitated the development of corresponding multi-level carbon emission models. A reference prefabricated building was selected as the case study to calculate the cradle-to-end-of-construction embodied carbon at the five aforementioned levels. The embodied carbon of the case building was calculated using SimaPro software, and sensitivity analysis was conducted by evaluating the parameter, scenario, and model uncertainties. The results have been published in Building and Environment (IF=7.4) (Teng and Pan 2020). For achieving Objective 2, we adopted a three-step research approach that combined literature review, model development, and case studies. First, we conducted an extensive literature review and performed on-site visits to thoroughly examine the production, prefabrication, and construction processes. We determined the sensor types for automated data collection, analysis, and monitoring for prefabricated buildings’ embodied carbon assessment. Second, we examined the automated data transfer and conversion mechanisms between BIM and LCA software. A systematic literature review was conducted, and a framework was developed to understand the knowledge of BIM-integrated LCA in the concept, methodology, and value dimensions. Through analyzing case studies involving 82 buildings from selected publications, three types of methods for BIM-integrated LCA were identified, i.e., integrating data into a third-party application or tool (I), importing a bill of quantities report generated from the BIM model into a dedicated LCA tool (II), and using plug-ins with LCA data for BIM software (III). Two approaches were suggested to improve the interoperability between BIM and LCA: adapting the BIM data to the LCA data structure and developing a simpler BIM tool. The results have been published in Building and Environment ( IF=7.4) (Teng et al. 2022). Based on the review results, we developed a BIM-integrated LCA solution to automate the embodied carbon assessment of prefabricated buildings based on the five-level framework established in Objective 1. The solution framework involved three modules: (1) BIM data preparation, (2) data extraction and integration, and (3) embodied carbon assessment. An Industry Foundation Classes (IFC)-enabled data transfer tool was developed to automatically adapt BIM data to the LCA data structure. The method for addressing data interoperability between BIM and LCA was presented in the ARCOM Conference (Xu et al. 2021). Then, a real-life prefabricated building in Hong Kong was used to validate the feasibility of the developed solution by comparing it with the traditional LCA method. The results indicated a dramatic time reduction in the LCA modeling process from 729 min to 62 min, achieving a 91.5% efficiency improvement. It can thus practically increase practitioners’ willingness to conduct LCA at an early design stage with quick feedback. The results have been published in Journal of Cleaner Production (IF=11.1) (Xu et al. 2022). The developed BIM-integrated LCA solution was then adopted to examine the trade-off between embodied carbon and operational carbon of a typical 30-story public residential building in Hong Kong based on different low carbon design scenarios. Among these scenarios, low carbon concrete was identified as an effective approach for not only reducing the embodied carbon by 5%-15%, but saving a mild percentage of operational carbon. The methods and results were presented in the CIB WBC (Pan et al. 2022). Third, we established an IoT-BIM integrated embodied carbon monitoring system (ECMS) for prefabricated buildings to achieve carbon traceability and visibility at multiple spatiotemporal levels of prefabricated buildings. The embodied carbon quantitative model was optimized to multiple spatiotemporal levels of prefabricated building products to serve as the theoretical foundation of the system. An IoT-aided data collection scheme was then proposed by developing technical solutions for three types of sensors (i.e., RFID, acceleration transducer, and GPS) to provide technical support. Three layers, including infrastructure, computing, and application layers, of ECMS were developed to realize the system. The proposed system was presented in the CIB WBC (Xu et al. 2022). A real-life prefabricated building in Hong Kong was adopted as the case study to verify the system. The developed ECMS proved effective and efficient in conducting comprehensive carbon analysis and forming reasonable carbon control measures through three sets of CDSs. The carbon traceability service provided a dynamic record of precast elements’ embodied carbon in correspondence with the prefabrication progress and a comparison between real-time embodied carbon and estimated embodied carbon from designs. The carbon visibility service visualized precast elements’ embodied carbon by integrating 2D and 3D representations. The BIM-based tool recorded precast elements’ carbon and progress information to facilitate data storage and exchange among various stakeholders. The carbon distribution analysis service depicted a comprehensive carbon distribution map from multiple spatiotemporal levels of prefabricated buildings. The results indicated that construction material is the most significant carbon source, whereas embodied carbon generated from transportation and electricity consumption of equipment should not be underestimated. Logistics and equipment management should also be emphasized to achieve low-carbon construction. The results have been published in Building and Environment (IF=7.4) (Xu et al. 2023). For achieving Objective 3, we investigated how embodied carbon assessment is affected by different variables and what the exact numerical influences are. A framework was established to examine variables in four methodological dimensions, i.e., temporal differences, spatial disparities, procedural inconsistencies, and physical diversities. Based on this framework, a three-step normalization was conducted to minimize the discrepancies in different variables among 244 case studies published between 2000 and 2020 to ensure they could be compared on the same scale. Eleven variables affecting the results were identified. The average embodied carbon for various building types has been calculated, providing the groundwork for cross-case comparisons and establishing benchmarks. Following the normalization process, the average embodied carbon for the 244 case buildings during the manufacturing, transportation, and construction stages was determined to be 443 kg CO2e/m2. When considering various building types, concrete buildings exhibited an average of 447 kg CO2e/m2 in carbon emissions, timber buildings averaged 281 kg CO2e/m2, and steel buildings had an average of 435 kg CO2e/m2. It is noteworthy that high-rise buildings displayed a notably higher average embodied carbon compared to their lower-rise counterparts. The results have been published in Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews (IF=15.9) (Pan and Teng 2021).

17203219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17203219.value: The major findings are reported in 5 journal articles (3 in BaE with IF of 7.4; 1 in RSER with IF of 15.9; 1 in JCP with IF of 11.1), and 3 international conference papers. Regarding the influences of input parameters, scenario assumptions, and choices of analytical uncertainty models to embodied carbon of prefabricated high-rise buildings, the major findings and outcomes include: The embodied carbon of the case averages 561 kg CO2/m2; When considering both deterministic results and parameter uncertainty, the key processes are identified as being the production of concrete, steel, and timber, as well as transportation activities; Combining the pre-defined scenarios can possibly reduce 31.6% of the embodied carbon; The selection of transformation coefficients in the analytical uncertainty model significantly affects the variances of the results (Teng and Pan 2020). Regarding the concept, methodology, and value dimensions of BIM-integrated LCA: the major findings and outcomes include: Three types of methods for BIM-integrated LCA have been identified: integrating data into a third-party application or tool (I), importing a bill of quantities report generated from the BIM model into a dedicated LCA tool (II), and using plug-ins with LCA data for BIM software (III); Two means have been suggested to improve the interoperability between BIM and LCA: adapting the BIM data to the LCA data structure and developing a simpler BIM tool (Teng et al. 2022). Regarding automated LCA, the major findings and outcomes include: A BIM-integrated LCA solution is developed to automate the embodied carbon assessment of prefabricated buildings based on a five-level framework: material, component, assembly, flat, and building; A dramatic time reduction in the LCA modeling process from 729 min to 62 min, achieving a 91.5% efficiency improvement (Xu et al. 2022); An IoT-BIM integrated embodied carbon monitoring system for prefabricated buildings to achieve carbon traceability and visibility at multiple spatiotemporal levels of prefabricated buildings (Xu et al. 2023); Construction material identified as the most significant carbon source, whereas EC generated from transportation and electricity consumption of equipment should not be underestimated. Regarding cross-case comparisons and benchmarking, the major findings and outcomes include: Remarkable variations in the assessment results are seen because of changes in modeling approaches (e.g., 200% increases from process-based to hybrid method), emission factor databases (e.g., 282% for steels in ICE), and building structures (e.g., 166 kg CO2e/m2 for concrete and timber buildings) (Pan and Teng 2021).

17203219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17203219.value: The developed embodied carbon monitoring system for prefabricated buildings can facilitate carbon traceability and visibility at multiple spatiotemporal levels of prefabricated buildings. However, further developments should be made to maximize the system’s functions. For example, the accuracy of sensor data can be increased such as developing more reliable algorithms using machine learning technologies to accurately estimate equipment operation time. Moreover, carbon alert and prediction services can be further developed to help project managers with decision-making. Although the system can provide carbon traceability and visibility during prefabricated construction, more conclusive functions are needed. A carbon emission benchmark at multiple levels can be delivered to identify carbon deviations and issue timely alerts if excessive carbon has been produced. Historical data collected earlier can also be utilized to predict the total embodied carbon. Such services will assist project managers with carbon strategies more efficiently and comprehensively.

17203219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17203219.value: This research project focuses on the estimation and benchmarking of embodied carbon emissions of prefabricated public residential buildings in Hong Kong through adopting smart technologies. Theoretically, it proposes three frameworks: (1) a five-level framework of prefabricated buildings, i.e., material, component, assembly, flat, and building, for systematic calculation and reporting on the embodied carbon of prefabricated buildings; (2) a system framework of methodological variables of embodied carbon assessment of buildings with eleven variables providing a theoretical foundation for cross-case comparisons and benchmarking; and (3) a framework for systematically reviewing the body of knowledge on BIM-integrated LCA addressing “what BIM-integrated LCA is”, “how to integrate BIM with LCA to simplify and automate data input”, and “what applications of BIM-integrated LCA are”. Practically, the developed BIM-integrated LCA solution extends the knowledge of automatic BIM-integrated LCA by addressing data interoperability using the IFC standard, which can increase practitioners’ willingness to conduct LCA at an early design stage with quick feedback. The developed embodied carbon monitoring system advances knowledge in achieving carbon traceability and visibility and depicts a comprehensive carbon distribution map, which should help government authorities and project managers form effective carbon strategies.

17204419.value: 交易税: 減低還是增加房地產市場波動性?

17204419.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17204419.value: Prof Chau, Kwong Wing Dr Deng, Kuang Kuang Dr Tse, Kwok-Sang

17204419.label: Project Objectives
17204419.value: To investigate possible mechanisms through which transaction taxes affect real estate price volatility and dispersion. To develop empirical models, based on changes in transaction tax rates and rules, to test the theoretical implications of the mechanisms.
rows: To investigate possible mechanisms through which transaction taxes affect real estate price volatility and dispersion.
To develop empirical models, based on changes in transaction tax rates and rules, to test the theoretical implications of the mechanisms.

17204419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204419.value: While the primary purpose of taxation is to finance government expenditures, transaction taxes, which are levied ad valorem at the time a good is transacted, can also be used as a policy instrument to maintain economic stability. The stabilization motive is particularly strong when it comes to real estate because any extreme price movements will greatly affect households’ wealth and affordability. The key question this research seeks to answer is whether imposing a transaction tax can really stabilize real estate prices. Two alternative mechanisms that generate opposite effects will be critically examined. On the one hand, a trader-type mechanism suggests that a higher tax rate should reduce price volatility because the extra transaction cost on real estate investment makes short-horizon investors, especially speculators or noise traders, less responsive to economic shocks. On the other hand, an information-based mechanism suggests that a higher tax rate dampens trading volume and hence availability of price information. Consequences for the real estate market could be greater price dispersion, greater price volatility, or both – which effect should dominate or take the lead has yet to be clarified. Empirically, this research will use the Hong Kong real estate market for investigation not just because its real estate transaction tax (stamp duty) rates have changed from time to time, but also because different types of transaction taxes have been introduced to target specific market segments and trading behaviors. This facilitates us to design more rigorous tests on the stabilization or destabilization effect of transaction taxes through quasi-experiments. The results of this research can help clarify whether a transaction tax policy is a double-edged sword – it may ‘kill’ not just the uninformed traders who bring noise to a market but also the informed traders who provide liquidity and information to all other market participants. 雖然稅收的主要目的是為政府支出提供資金，但交易稅（商品交易時征收的從價稅）也可以作為維持經濟穩定的政策性工具。穩定房地產市場尤其重要，因為任何極端的房價變動都會極大地影響家庭的財富和負擔能力。這項研究試圖回答的關鍵問題是，征收交易稅是否能真正穩定房地產價格。兩種產生相反效果的替代機制將被檢驗。一方面，根據交易者型機制，較高的稅率應會降低價格波動，因為房地產投資的額外交易成本使得短期投資者–特別是投機者或非理性交易者–不容易左右樓市的短期變動。另一方面，基於市場信息機制，較高的稅率會抑制交易量，從而抑制價格的資訊性。對房地產市場產生的後果可能是更大的價格分散，更大的價格波動，或兩者兼而有之–其中哪類影響應該佔主導地位或產生主要影響還有待澄清。這項實證研究將利用香港房地產市場進行調查，不僅因為香港房地產交易稅（印花稅）稅率在不斷地發生變化，另外還因為香港針對特定細分市場和交易行為引入了不同類型的交易稅。這有助於我們通過準實驗方法設計更為嚴謹的實驗來分辨交易稅的穩定或不穩定效應。這項研究的結果有助於澄清交易稅政策是否是一把雙刃劍 - 它可能不僅阻止了不知情交易者向市場帶來的交易雜訊，還阻礙了知情交易者為所有其他市場參與者提供的流動性和信息。

17204419.label: Realisation of objectives
17204419.value: Objective 1 is to investigate possible mechanisms through which transaction taxes affect real estate price volatility and dispersion. To achieve this objective, we have reviewed the literature on relevant theoretical works on real estate pricing (research output 1-4), established a theoretical model with different mechanisms on how prices adjust to news and noise (research output 2), enriched the model with ‘search’ features to explain the behavior of short-term traders most affected by transaction taxes (research output 1), and incorporated ‘momentum’ into the model to derive possible effects on price volatility and dispersion (research output 4). Objective 2 is to develop empirical models, based on changes in transaction tax rates and rules, to test the theoretical implications of the mechanisms. To achieve this objective, we have reviewed the literature on relevant empirical works on real estate price adjustments (research output 1-4), identified changes in transaction tax policy in Hong Kong, including Special Stamp Duty, Buyer’s Stamp Duty, and Double Stamp Duty (research output 3-4), collected extensive data on property transactions to compile property price indices (research output 3), applied an error correction model to assess the tax effects in the short run (research output 3), and developed a quasi-experiment to test the theoretical implications on price volatility and dispersion (research output 4). Both objectives have been fully achieved, as shown in the four research outputs.

17204419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204419.value: Research output 1 develops a theoretical model for the real estate price generating process with two key features. First, it allows transaction prices to deviate from intrinsic value as a result of transaction noise. Second, it allows news to incorporate into intrinsic value gradually over time as a result of market inefficiency. With this model, we are able to explain the positive and negative autocorrelation of real estate returns. Empirical tests confirm that the apparent sluggish adjustments in some sub-markets are due to transaction taxes. Research output 2 further develops the model by connecting transaction noise with the search intensity of buyers and sellers. It predicts that traders with a ‘search’ advantage would earn an excess return in short-term trading. With high-frequency property transactions in Hong Kong, we show that those buying and reselling within three months performed better when comparable transactions are scant and prices are more dispersed, as if they were arbitrageurs. Their advantage, however, would diminish with the implementation of transaction taxes. Research output 3 examines whether transaction taxes were able to cool down the overheated housing market in Hong Kong. A set of constant-quality housing price indices have been compiled for different property segments. Through an error correction model, we find that credit tightening was able to curb house price growth in the high-price segment, while transaction taxes could not. An implication is that the effectiveness of macroprudential measures hinges on whether policy compliance can be easily monitored and enforced. Research output 4 extends the previous models and findings by examining whether short-term trading would stabilize or destabilize real estate returns. Based on a policy shock that substantially raised the cost of short-term trading in Hong Kong, we estimate ‘real estate risk’ with and without short-term trading based on return predictability, return volatility, and price dispersion. Our quasi-experiment results show that as short-term investors exit the market, market returns are less predictable and less volatile, while prices are less dispersed cross-sectionally. Consistent with herding models in behavioral finance, the findings suggest that short-term investors are momentum traders who do not enhance price efficiency.

17204419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204419.value: The research can be further developed to study whether transaction taxes would have different effects on the first-hand and second-hand housing markets. Property developers, with their market power, might find ways to shift the tax burden to buyers. Meanwhile, developers also face more regulatory constraints on how first-hand properties are marketed and sold. This is an area in need of theoretical development and evidence, and would be an interesting topic for the next research grant proposal.

17204419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204419.value: Among many Asian economies, Hong Kong has experienced the highest real growth in house prices since the 2010s. Transaction taxes (stamp duty) were introduced to cool down the overheated housing market. This research provides empirical evidence to show that transaction taxes were not able to curb house price growth. However, there may be a behavioral argument for using transaction taxes to enhance market efficiency. After imposing a stamp duty on short-term trading, real estate returns tend to be less volatile and real estate prices tend to be less dispersed. This research gives policymakers a comprehensive assessment of the possible effects of a transaction tax and real estate investors a better understanding of the price adjustment mechanism.

17204519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204519.value: The anaerobic ammonium oxidation (anammox) process is one of the most innovative and energy efficient biological ammonium removal processes. Among the operating anammox installations, a majority of them have been applied for the treatments of wastewater streams with high ammonium concentration, such as the reject water of anaerobic digester and landfill leachate. However, only limited studies reported the start-up and long-term operation of anammox processes treating saline wastewater. The anammox processes that treating saline wastewater need more comprehensive studies, particularly considering the fact that 85% of the population in Hong Kong are using seawater for flushing. Although the anammox processes had been applied in some full-scale wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), the complex microbial community interactions and the rapid way to predict the microbial dynamics in anammox sludge have not yet been well investigated. The development of 2nd generation sequencing technologies has facilitated the studies of microbial communities and interactions in lab-scale and full-scale wastewater treatment systems. In recent years, the 3rd generation sequencing technologies provide efficient ways to have rapidly in-situ sequencing. These sequencing technologies, therefore, could be used to further expand our understanding of the anammox process for the treatment of saline reject water in full-scale WWTPs. In this project, we will investigate anammox process for saline reject water of sludge dewatering, 1) to develop a side-stream partial-nitritation anammox (PNA) process for the treatment of saline reject water of anaerobic digester; 2) to study the microbial community dynamics and interactions in the developed PNA system; 3) to build microbial interaction models that could predict the trends of anammox systems; 4) to develop a rapid in-situ microbiological analysis pipeline that mainly based on the established models and third generation sequencing platform (Nanopore sequencing). The development of anammox process for saline reject water of anaerobic digester, and microbial interaction models will provide new insights into the anammox process and guidance for the full-scale treatment process.

17204519.label: Realisation of objectives
17204519.value: Objective 1: To develop a side-stream partial-nitritation anammox (PNA) process for the treatment of synthetic reject water of anaerobic digester. Two-stage and one-stage PNA lab-scale bioreactors had be designed and inoculated with anammox sludge already enriched in the PI’s lab. The synthetic wastewater have treated using these two designed anammox systems. Based on nitrogen removal performance, partial-nitritation anammox (PNA) process will be retained for further studies. One lab-scale UASB reactor (anammox bioreactor) with a working volume of 1.5 L was initially inoculated with anammox biomass in December 2017 and has been in operation for almost 2 years before this study. Synthetic wastewater containing ammonium bicarbonate and sodium nitrite was used as the nitrogen source to sustain the growth and reproduction of anammox bacteria. Mineral salt and trace elements were added to provide elements for the microbial growth. Granular sludge samples were collected from the same sampling point in the UASB reactor at each specific time point for subsequent DNA and RNA extraction and sequencing. Thus, the Objective 1 is realized. Objective 2: To study the microbial community dynamics and interactions in the developed PNA system. An integrated multi-omics, i.e., metagenomics, metatranscriptomics and metaproteomics, has be applied to recover the metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) of the microbial community and reconstruct the metabolic interactions in the studied anammox process. The metabolic capacities of anammox bacteria and associated microbial community interactions in partial-nitritation anammox (PNA) reactors have received considerable attention for their crucial roles in energy-efficient nitrogen removal from wastewater. However, a comprehensive understanding of how abiotic and biotic factors shape bacterial community assembly in PNA reactors is not well reported. Here, we used integrated multi-omics (i.e., high-throughput 16S rRNA gene, metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metaproteomic sequencing) to reveal how abiotic and biotic factors shape the bacterial community assembly in a lab-scale one-stage PNA reactor treating synthetic wastewater. Analysis results of amplicon sequences (16S rRNA gene) from a time-series revealed distinct relative abundance patterns of the key autotrophic bacteria, i.e., anammox bacteria and ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), and the associated heterotrophic populations in the seed sludge and the sludge at the new stable state after deterioration. Using shotgun metagenomic sequences of anammox sludge, we recovered 58 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), including 3 MAGs of anammox bacteria and 3 MAGs of AOB. The integrated metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and metaproteomic data revealed that nitrogen metabolism is the most active process in the studied PNA reactor. The abundant heterotrophs contribute to the reduction of nitrate to nitrite/ammonium for autotrophic bacteria (anammox bacteria and AOB). Genomic and transcriptomic data revealed that the preference for electron donors of the dominant heterotrophs in different bacterial assemblages (seed and new stable state) varied along with the shift in anammox bacteria that have different metabolic features in terms of EPS composition. Notably, the most abundant heterotrophic bacteria in the reactor were more auxotrophic than the less abundant heterotrophs, regarding the syntheses of amino acids and vitamins. In addition, one of the abundant bacteria observed in the bacterial community exhibited highly transcribed secretion systems (type VI). These findings provide the first insight that the bacterial communities in the PNA reactor are defined by not only abiotic factors (operating mode) but also metabolic interactions, such as nitrogen metabolism, exchange of electron donors, and auxotrophies. It is of critical importance to understand how anammox consortia respond to disturbance events and fluctuations in the wastewater treatment reactors. Although the responses of anammox consortia to operational parameters (e.g., temperature, dissolved oxygen, nutrient concentrations) have frequently been reported in previous studies, less is known about their responses and resilience when they suffer from nutrient interruption. Here, we investigated the anammox community states and transcriptional patterns before and after a short-term nutrient starvation (3 days) to determine how anammox consortia respond to and recover from such stress. The results demonstrated that the remarkable changes in transcriptional patterns, rather than the community compositions were associated with the nutritional stress. The divergent expression of genes involved in anammox reactions, especially the hydrazine synthase complex (HZS), and nutrient transportation might function as part of a starvation response mechanism in anammox bacteria. In addition, effective energy conservation and substrate supply strategies (ATP accumulation, upregulated amino acid biosynthesis, and enhanced protein degradation) and synergistic interactions between anammox bacteria and heterotrophs might benefit their survival during starvation and the ensuing recovery of the anammox process. Compared with abundant heterotrophs in the anammox system, the overall transcription pattern of the core autotrophic producers (i.e., anammox bacteria) was highly resilient and quickly returned to its pre-starvation state, further contributing to the prompt recovery when the feeding was resumed. These findings provide important insights into nutritional stress-induced changes in transcriptional activities in the anammox consortia and would be beneficial for the understanding of the capacity of anammox consortia in response to stress and process stability in the engineered ecosystems Objective 3: To develop a rapid in-situ microbiological analysis pipeline that mainly based on the established models and third generation sequencing platform (Nanopore sequencing). Genome-centric approaches are widely used to investigate microbial compositions, dynamics, ecology, and interactions within various environmental systems. Hundreds or even thousands of genomes could be retrieved in a single study contributed by the cost-effective short-read sequencing and developed assembly/binning pipelines. However, conventional binning methods usually yield highly fragmented draft genomes that limit our ability to comprehensively understand these microbial communities. Thus, to leverage advantage of both the long and short reads to retrieve more complete genomes from environmental samples is a must-do task to move this direction forward. Here, we used an iterative hybrid assembly (IHA) approach to reconstruct 49 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), including 27 high-quality (HQ) and high-contiguity (HC) genomes with contig number ≤ 5, eight of which were circular finished genomes from a partial-nitritation anammox (PNA) reactor. These 49 recovered MAGs (43 MAGs encoding full-length rRNA, average N50 of 2.2 Mbp), represented the majority (92.3%) of the bacterial community. Moreover, the workflow retrieved HQ and HC MAGs even with an extremely low coverage (relative abundance < 0.1%). Among them, 34 MAGs could not be assigned to the genus level, indicating the novelty of the genomes retrieved using the IHA method proposed in this study. Comparative analysis of HQ MAG pairs reconstructed using two methods, i.e., hybrid and short reads only, revealed that identical genes in the MAG pairs represented 87.5% and 95.5% of the total gene inventory of hybrid and short reads only assembled MAGs, respectively. In addition, the first finished anammox genome of the genus Ca. Brocadia reconstructed revealed that there were two identical hydrazine synthase (hzs) genes, providing the exact gene copy number of this crucial phylomarker of anammox at the genome level. Our results showcased the high-quality and high-contiguity genome retrieval performance and demonstrated the feasibility of complete genome reconstruction using the IHA workflow from the enrichment system. These (near-) complete genomes provided a high resolution of the microbial community, which might help to understand the bacterial repertoire of anammox-associated systems. Combined with other validation experiments, the workflow can enable a detailed view of the anammox or other similar enrichment systems. Thus, Objective 3 is realized.

17204519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204519.value: In the future the studies could focus on more abiotic factors and metabolic interactions which may define the bacterial communities in the PNA reactor, especially effects of nitrogen metabolism, exchange of electron donors, and auxotrophies on bacterial communities. Additionally, nutritional stress-induced changes in transcriptional activities in the anammox consortia need to be further studied and the results would be beneficial for the understanding of the capacity of anammox consortia in response to stress and process stability in the engineered ecosystems. Finally, more researches on the high-quality and high-contiguity genomes in PNA reactors need to be further explore using the IHA workflow established in this project to provide a high resolution of the microbial community, which might help to understand the bacterial repertoire of anammox-associated systems.

17204519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204519.value: Partial-nitritation anammox (PNA) reactors has been widely studied and has a great potential for real applications in wastewater treatment. To understand well this process which have crucial roles in energy-efficient nitrogen removal from wastewater, we used integrated multi-omics to reveal factors affect the microbial community in the reactor. Analysis results revealed the key autotrophic bacteria, i.e., anammox bacteria and ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB), and the associated heterotrophic populations in the process. Additionally, we conducted experiment to understand how these microorganisms responded to disturbance events and fluctuations in the wastewater treatment process and find that the remarkable changes in transcriptional patterns, rather than the community compositions were associated with the nutritional stress. Genome sequencing is powerful tool to get the genomes of these microorganisms and understand them in a better way to control the reactor performance. We developed new methods to get more genomes and demonstrate it application in the operations of the reactors and the potentials in the engineering application of genomic analysis methods.

17204619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204619.value: This project designs efficient resource schedulers for distributed machine learning (ML) clusters, using deep learning-driven strategies. Most leading IT companies have deployed large clusters of GPU servers, where they run distributed ML frameworks to train ML models over large datasets, for providing various AI-driven services. For example, Google uses TensorFlow to power products such as Google Photos and Google Cloud Speech, Microsoft employs CNTK for speech recognition and image processing, and Baidu extensively uses PaddlePaddle for advertising, group shopping, etc. In a distributed ML framework (such as TensorFlow and MXNet), an ML model is trained in parallel by multiple concurrent workers. Each worker computes model parameter updates using allocated data, and exchanges updates with each other directly or through parameter servers (PSs). Training a state-of-the-art ML model is resource intensive and time consuming even in parallel, e.g., it takes 2-3 days to train a DeepSpeech2 model on the LibriSpeech dataset using 4 servers with 32 TITAN X GPUs. A large ML cluster is commonly shared by various training jobs submitted at different times. A fundamental task of the cluster operator is to efficiently schedule resources to run jobs, for maximal resource utilization of the expensive ML cluster that expedites job completion. In existing production ML clusters, jobs are largely scheduled using general-purpose schedulers (e.g., Borg and Yarn), similarly as other cloud jobs. Each job is allocated a fixed amount of resources, and cannot benefit from extra resources when they become available, unless the operator or the job owner manually reconfigures its resources and restarts it anew. Job placement on physical machines is typically carried out in an interference-oblivious manner, not taking care of implicit interferences among co-located jobs. Significant opportunities exist in improving resource utilization and training efficiency in modern ML clusters, by automatic, elastic resource allocation and interference-aware placement of workers/PSs, that exploit characteristics of distributed training jobs. This project advocates deep learning approaches for designing efficient schedulers in shared ML clusters. Exploiting iterativeness of ML jobs, we design reinforcement learning-based approaches for adjusting resource allocation to concurrent jobs throughout their training courses, as well as deciding their worker/PS placements on physical machines. The goal is to achieve average training time minimization in the entire cluster through most efficient resource utilization and interference minimization. We pursue real-world implementation of our schedulers on state-of-the-art cluster management systems and compare them with representative cluster schedulers under real-world workloads. 該項目使用深度學習技術來為分佈式機器學習集群設計高效的資源調度器。當今大多數領先的IT公司已經部署了大型GPU服務器集群，運行分佈式機器學習框架在大型數據集上進行模型訓練，從而提供各種AI驅動的服務。例如，Google使用TensorFlow為Google Photos和Google Cloud Speech等產品提供支持，Microsoft使用CNTK進行語音識別和圖像處理，百度廣泛使用PaddlePaddle支持廣告、團購等業務。 在分佈式機器學習框架（例如TensorFlow和MXNet）中，機器學習模型由多個並行workers進行訓練。每個worker使用被分配的數據進行模型參數更新，並直接或間接通過參數服務器互換更新。訓練最先進的機器學習模型資源消耗巨大，即使並行計算也是耗時良久。例如，使用具有32個TITAN X GPU的4台服務器在LibriSpeech數據集上訓練DeepSpeech2模型也需要2-3天。大型機器學習集群通常由在不同時間提交的各種訓練作業共享。集群運營商的一個基本任務即是有效地調度資源以運行作業，以最大限度地利用昂貴的機器學習集群，加快各種作業的完成速度。 現有的生產級機器學習集群主要使用通用的調度器（例如Borg和Yarn）來對其作業進行調度。每個作業都被分配了固定數量的資源，無法從額外出現的可用資源中受益，除非操作員或作業所有者手動重新配置其資源並重新啟動它。此外，物理機器上的工作放置通常是並未考慮相互乾擾。在機器學習集群中，在自動、彈性作業資源分配，以及利用分佈式訓練作業的特性來進行避干擾放置等方面存在重大機會，以大大提高資源利用率和訓練效率。 該項目將致力於使用深度學習方法為共享機器學習集群設計高效的調度器。利用機器學習作業的迭代性，我們設計了基於強化學習的方法，用於在整個訓練過程中調整併發工作的資源分配，以及確定他們在物理機器上的部署位置。我們的目標是通過最有效的資源利用和乾擾最小化來實現整個集群中的平均訓練時間最小化。我們將在先進的集群管理系統上實現我們的調度程序，並將它們與有代表性的集群調度程序在實際工作負載下進行比較。

17204619.label: Realisation of objectives
17204619.value: For Objective 1, regarding tasks a), b) and c), we proposed DL2, a DL-driven scheduler for deep learning clusters, targeting global training job expedition by dynamically resizing resources allocated to jobs. DL2 advocates a joint supervised learning and reinforcement learning approach: a neural network is warmed up via offline supervised learning based on job traces produced by the existing cluster scheduler; then the neural network is plugged into the live DL cluster, fine-tuned by reinforcement learning carried out throughout the training progress of the DL jobs, and used for deciding job resource allocation in an online fashion. We have also enabled dynamic scaling to adjust the worker numbers in a live training job, with dynamic batch size adjustment. The results were reported in publication 1 in Part C-8. In a following work, we further addressed a varying number of input job types where jobs can use either PS or AllReduce for parameter synchronization, and re-designed the neural network structure to handle input job sequences with variable lengths. Specifically, we adopt a Transformer-based NN structure to encode job status from a variable-sized job sequence and use a decoder network to generate resource allocation decisions for each job one by one. We also add multi-head attention to capture the correlation between concurrent jobs. The results were reported in publication 5 in Part C-8. For ML job scheduling in large-scale ML clusters, we have designed a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) method for making distributed scheduling decisions under realistic datacenter topologies, with results in publication 4 of Part C-8. In the same work, we eliminate the need of knowing the exact number of epochs for training to converge as input to the reinforcement learning model, but only need an estimated total epoch number to use in the reward computation. Besides, we adopted optimization approaches to propose a new computing cluster resource scheduling algorithm that leverages the special layered structure of DNN jobs to significantly improve ML job completion time. The results were reported in publication 1 of part C-9. In an online setting for ML cluster scheduling, we proposed an efficient online scheduling algorithm to decide each ML job’s execution time window, the number and the type (corresponding to a set of hardware configurations) of workers and parameter servers for each job upon its arrival, with a goal of minimizing the weighted average completion time. Our online algorithm consists of an online scheduling framework that groups unprocessed ML training jobs into a batch iteratively, and a batch scheduling algorithm that configures each ML job to maximize the total weight of scheduled jobs in the current iteration. The results were reported in publication 2 of part C-9. For Objective 2, Task a) has been completed in publication 5 of part C-8: We built a deep learning-driven ML cluster scheduler that places training jobs in a manner that minimizes interference and maximizes performance (i.e., training completion time), based on a carefully designed deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework augmented with reward modeling. The DRL employs state-of-the-art techniques to stabilize training and improve convergence, including actor-critic algorithm, job-aware action space exploration and experience replay. In view of a common lack of reward samples corresponding to different placement decisions, we build an auxiliary reward prediction NN model, which is trained using historical samples with supervised learning and used for producing reward for unseen placement. Besides, we have further investigated a generative adversarial network (GAN) to produce samples by approximating patterns seen in available traces, in an online resource allocation problem setting, with results presented in publication 2 of part C-8. For Tasks b) and c), we have worked on worker/PS placement in hybrid data and model parallel training in heterogeneous machine learning clusters. We adopt GNN-based RL and combinatorial optimization to identify the near-optimal fine-grained device placement and execution order of operations, which takes into consideration various environmental factors (proximity to training data replicas, inter-server network connectivity, etc.) in deciding the rewards for reinforcement learning. The GNN model also produces decisions on using PS or AllReduce for parameter synchronization. The results were reported in publications 3 and 4 of part C-9. Beyond PS or AllReduce, we have dedicatedly investigated the best parameter synchronization topology and schedule among workers for most expedited communication in distributed DNN training. We show that the optimal parameter synchronization topology should be comprised of trees with different workers as roots, each for aggregating or broadcasting a partition of gradients/parameters. We identify near-optimal forest packing to maximally utilize available bandwidth and overlap aggregation and broadcast stages to minimize communication time. The results were reported in publication 5 of part C-9. For Objective 3, regarding Task a), in publication 1 of part C-8, we studied dynamic worker scaling with varying worker numbers. Previous worker/PS placements have been considered among the input to our reinforcement learning in publication 5 of part C-8. In publication 4 of part C-8, we carry out multi-agent reinforcement learning for resource allocation in a hierarchical manner: we design a hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) with edge information encoded to capture the cluster/data center topology, server architectures and link status; following the GNN hierarchy, the schedulers aggregate local observations by exchanging with other schedulers, and make topology-aware job placement decisions using reinforcement learning. For Task b), we have proposed a dynamic parameter server load distribution scheme, to mitigate PS straggler issues and accelerate distributed model training in the PS architecture. An exploitation-exploration method is carefully designed to scale in and out parameter servers and adjust parameter distribution among PSs on the go, and an elastic PS scaling module has been designed to carry out our scheme with little interruption to the training process. The results were reported in publication 6 of part C-9. For Task c), our MARL scheduler design in publication 4 of part C-8 targets to handle the scheduler scalability issue in large ML clusters. With the proposed MARL model, our scheduler agents are distributed, while interacting among each other with necessary information exchange to achieve global scheduling. We have also developed online scheduling algorithms to optimize resource allocation decisions for distributed ML cluster scheduling, with results in publications 3 and 6 of part C-8 and publication 7 of part C-9. For Objective 4, we have evaluated our algorithms and systems in the publications using our testbed system, with workloads produced following the Alibaba GPU cluster usage data and other real-world traces. We reported evaluation results in terms of average job completion time, scheduling overhead, worker/PS scaling overhead, DNN training accuracy/loss, training speed/per-iteration training time, etc. We have carefully compared our design with state-of-the-art representative designs in the respective work. For example, in publication 1 of part C-8, we compared DL2 with Dominant Resource Fairness (DRF), Tetris, Optimus and OfflineRL schemes; in publication 5 of part C-8, we compare our placement schemes with Load Balancing and Least Interference First (LIF-Line, LIF-Quad) based on analytical interference models; in publication 3 of part C-9, we carefully evaluated our GNN model in making decisions for unseen job types; etc. We have also deployed our designs onto Alibaba and ByteDance's AI clusters for evaluation under more realistic system scales and live workloads.
