17204619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204619.value: In publication 1 of Part C-8, we designed a DL-driven scheduler for deep learning clusters, advocating a joint supervised learning and reinforcement learning approach and targeting global training job expedition by dynamically resizing resources allocated to jobs. In publication 5 of Part C-8, we further designed a scheduler that addresses a varying number of input job types where jobs can use either PS or AllReduce for parameter synchronization, and re-designed the neural network structure to handle input job sequences with variable lengths. In view of a common lack of reward samples corresponding to different placement decisions, we built an auxiliary reward prediction NN model, which is trained using historical samples with supervised learning and used for producing reward for unseen placement. In publication 2 of part C-8, we further investigated a generative adversarial network (GAN) to produce scheduling samples by approximating patterns seen in available traces. In publication 4 of Part C-8, we adopted multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) for ML job scheduling in large-scale ML clusters, that makes distributed scheduling decisions under realistic datacenter topologies. We designed a hierarchical Graph Neural Network (GNN) with edge information encoded to capture the cluster/data center topology, server architectures and link status; following the GNN hierarchy, the schedulers aggregate local observations by exchanging with other schedulers, and make topology-aware job placement decisions using reinforcement learning. In publication 5 of part C-9, we identified optimal parameter synchronization topologies using multiple trees. In publications 3 and 6 of part C-8 and publication 1,2,7 of part C-9, we adopted optimization approaches and proposed (online) optimal cluster resource scheduling algorithms, achieving minimal training job completion times. In publications 3 and 4 of part C-9, we adopted GNN-based RL and combinatorial optimization to identify the near-optimal fine-grained device placement and execution order of operations, which takes into consideration various environmental factors (proximity to training data replicas, inter-server network connectivity, etc.) in deciding the rewards for reinforcement learning. In publication 6 of part C-9, we proposed a dynamic parameter server load distribution scheme, to mitigate PS straggler issues and accelerate distributed model training in the PS architecture. An exploitation-exploration method is carefully designed to scale in and out parameter servers and adjust parameter distribution among PSs on the go, and an elastic PS scaling module has been designed to carry out our scheme with little interruption to the training process.

17204619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204619.value: This project designs efficient resource schedulers for distributed machine learning (ML) clusters, using deep learning-driven strategies. Efficient schedulers are crucial for resource efficiency in the very expensive ML clusters and training speed/quality of the ML models to derive. Our studies model distributed ML in a black-box manner, and design practical and general approaches for better resource scheduling among ML workloads. The designed methodologies can contribute significantly to performance improvement and cost reduction of real-world AI clouds.

17204919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17204919.value: Walkability is an essential element of the sustainable development of urban cities and particularly for high-density metropolises because of the intense interactions between traffic and pedestrian movement. However, urban street design is primarily traffic-oriented. A higher priority is given to traffic movement than to pedestrians, who are often ignored in the planning, design, and operation of a signal-controlled network. To enhance walkability in urban street systems, we will establish a comprehensive framework for area traffic-pedestrian control (ATPC), with due consideration given to both traffic and pedestrians. We will adopt a discrete/continuum approach to model traffic and pedestrian flows, where traffic will be modeled as a discrete network and pedestrians described as inhabiting a two-dimensional continuum space, and represent their interactions using appropriate boundary conditions at mid-block and crosswalk locations. A macroscopic approach will be used to model both traffic and pedestrian movement to describe their aggregate behavior. In addition to travel and walking times, appropriate representations of crash and injury risk for traffic and pedestrians will be set out to describe the interaction effects in their route choice decision processes. Both traffic and pedestrian demands are time varying, and their macroscopic variables, flow, density, and speed are time-dependent and governed by conservation law. Together with the stochastic variability of parameters in the fundamental relationships between these variables, the models will be formulated as two dynamic-stochastic user equilibrium models, one for the discrete traffic network and the other for pedestrians’ two-dimensional continuum system. These models will be solved using efficient uncertainty quantification algorithms. A fixed-point procedure will be derived to obtain consistent traffic and pedestrian movement patterns, based on which a performance index comprising a weighted sum of the travel/walking times and crash/injury risks will be obtained to measure system performance. We will establish a group-based signal optimization framework to search for an optimized signal plan that minimizes this performance index, subject to both the safety and operational constraints of the group-based control variables for both traffic and pedestrian signal aspects. The solution to this ATPC problem should help to improve both traffic and pedestrian progressions along their route trajectories between their origins and destinations and provide useful information for street furniture design. Furthermore, it should improve the walkability of urban environments without compromising the efficiency of traffic movement in the street system. 在現代城市，尤其是人口高度密集的都市，車來人往，行人友善的環境是城市可持續發展的重要環節。然而，目前城市街道設計主要以車為本。在信號控制網絡的規劃、設計以及運行方面，行人的利益往往被忽視，而車輛總是享有更高的優先權。為了提升城市道路系統的步行環境，我們將同時考慮車輛和行人的利益，建立一個全面的車輛-行人區域控制框架。我們將對車流和行人流建立離散/連續的數學模型。其中，車流將基於離散網絡建模，而行人流則基於二維連續空間建模，而二者的相互作用則通過在路口和行人過路處設置的適當的邊界條件進行控制。車流和行人流的整體行為將採用宏觀數學模型進行模擬。在車輛和行人的路徑決策中，不僅車輛行程時間和行人步行時間的影響會被考慮，事故及傷亡風險也會被合理地表達，用以衡量車流和行人流的相互作用。所有車輛和行人的需求隨時間變化，其相關的宏觀指標（如流量、密度和速度）均為時間變量，且滿足守恆定律。考慮到流量-密度-速度基本關係中的隨機參數，我們將對車輛的離散網絡和行人的連續二維空間分別建立動態隨機用戶均衡模型。高效的不確定性量化算法將被應用對模型進行求解。我們將推出不動點方法以獲取連續的車流和行人流運動模式，並以此得到包含不同權重的車輛行程/行人步行時間、事故/傷亡風險的綜合評價指標。我們將構建基於交通燈組的信號優化框架，在車輛和行人信號控制變量的安全和運行因素共同限制下，以綜合評價指標最小化為目標來尋求最優的信號方案。車輛-行人區域信號控制問題的解決方案將有助於提升車流和行人流的效率並貫穿全程，同時為街道設施設計提供有用的信息。而且，這還可以在不犧牲車輛行駛效率的前提下，進一步提升城市的行人友善環境。

17204919.label: Realisation of objectives
17204919.value: To achieve Objective (1), we adopted a comprehensive approach to develop a continuum model for pedestrian flow. This process commenced with the introduction of a second-order pedestrian model that incorporated both continuity and transport equations. We then performed a linear stability analysis to ascertain stability requirements and pinpoint appropriate parameters for the model. Subsequently, we used a third-order weighted essentially non-oscillatory scheme in a characteristic-wise manner to resolve the second-order system. We employed the fast-sweeping method to solve the Eikonal equations and extensively examined the numerical properties of the proposed model. Lastly, we expanded this approach to model crowd pressure and turbulence by implementing a mixed-type continuum approach for multidirectional pedestrian flow. We integrated the stochastic variabilities in pedestrian flows into a dynamic continuum modeling approach by developing mathematical models for stochastic pedestrian dynamics. These proposed models accounted for both demand and behavioral stochasticity. The system was represented by a set of time-dependent stochastic partial differential equations. To solve these equations, we employed Monte Carlo (MC) or Quasi Monte Carlo (QMC) methods in conjunction with efficient numerical schemes. We designed benchmarking scenarios and simulations to showcase the convergence and computational performance of the MC and QMC methods in capturing stochastic variabilities in pedestrian flows. To further enhance computational efficiency, we employed the generalized polynomial chaos expansion approach. We constructed a two-dimensional continuum dynamic pedestrian flow model that considered demand stochasticity. The system was formulated as time-dependent partial differential equations with random inputs. We utilized a multi-element probabilistic collocation method (ME-PCM) based on pseudo-projection and efficient numerical schemes to solve the system. We demonstrated the effectiveness of the ME-PCM through numerical examples. By comparing the ME-PCM to traditional methods, such as Monte Carlo and generalized polynomial chaos expansion approaches, we showcased the advantages of the ME-PCM in terms of computational efficiency and accuracy. Consequently, we successfully developed and tested a robust and efficient dynamic continuum model for capturing stochastic variabilities in pedestrian flows. We rigorously examined the analytical properties of continuum modeling to gain a deeper understanding of this approach. We investigated the existence and uniqueness of solutions to the partial differential equations (PDEs). To enhance the continuum model's applicability to more general geometrical configurations in real-world problems, we introduced positivity-preserving discontinuous Galerkin methods on triangular meshes for macroscopic pedestrian flow models. We presented numerical examples to demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed solution algorithm. Through these investigations, we achieved a comprehensive understanding of the continuum modeling's analytical properties and significantly improved its applicability to more complex geometrical configurations in real-world problems. To achieve Objective (2), we developed a stochastic fundamental diagram, a primary component of traffic flow. We accomplished this by creating a stochastic link-based fundamental diagram (FD) that explicitly considered speed heterogeneity and rainfall intensity. We then enhanced the traffic stream model by incorporating speed heterogeneity using a stochastic structure. We proposed a two-stage calibration based on Bayesian inference for estimating the stochastic link-based FD parameters, which proved useful for studying travel time variability. Furthermore, we introduced a new method for estimating lane-based travel time distributions, considering different vehicle types. We conducted vehicle re-identification through a lane-based bipartite graph matching technique. To test the proposed method, we carried out a case study on a congested urban road in Hong Kong. We initiated the development of a macroscopic dynamic-stochastic traffic flow model for discrete links with a comprehensive study of the Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (LWR) model's analytical properties. We established the correlation between the total number of vehicles and the steady-state solution, and we proved the uniqueness of the solution by introducing priority coefficients when shocks appear. We developed an analytical solving procedure for the steady-state solution and designed a numerical scheme for the LWR network model to converge the traffic flow into the discussed steady-state solution. Building on these findings, we developed a dynamically bi-orthogonal solution method for stochastic Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (SLWR) traffic flow models. This new framework for macroscopic traffic flow modeling addressed the stochasticity in traffic flow by randomizing free-flow speed. This represented the heterogeneity in the driver population and allowed individual drivers to maintain consistent and rational behavior along the road section. The SLWR model followed a conservation law of stochastic traffic density and flow and was formulated as a time-dependent stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE). To solve the highly non-linear SPDE, we employed the dynamically bi-orthogonal (DyBO) method, based on a spatial basis and stochastic basis. We simulated various traffic scenarios using the SLWR model and compared them with the Monte Carlo method to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed model. These advancements in traffic flow modeling provided valuable insights and tools for better understanding and managing traffic congestion and flow on discrete links. To achieve Objective (3), we first explored group-based adaptive traffic control systems for optimizing traffic signal timings. These systems employed a strategic time-dependent optimization scheme, developed through the creation of a multiresolution architecture for adaptive traffic control systems, consisting of strategic, tactical, and local control methods. To account for the inherent variability in traffic systems, we adapted the optimization process of signal timings to incorporate the uncertainty of traffic information. We achieved this through the development of a probabilistic penetration rate model to estimate the variability of results generated by the single-source data penetration rate estimator. We used VISSIM procedures and next-generation simulation data to demonstrate the accuracy of the calibrated models. By following this approach, we effectively addressed the optimization of traffic signal timings while considering the stochastic nature of traffic systems. We developed a stochastic optimization model for adaptive signal control at isolated intersections with partial connectivity to optimize traffic signal control in congested urban environments. We achieved this by introducing a connected vehicle-based adaptive signal control framework. This innovative framework eliminates the need for costly on-road detectors, which can be expensive to install and maintain. This approach led to a high-dimensional, non-convex, and stochastic optimization problem. To tackle these challenges, we introduced an analytical stochastic delay model that utilized generalized polynomial chaos expansion and a gradient-guided golden section search algorithm for solving the problem. We extended the framework to the area-pedestrian traffic control system through the development of group-based adaptive area-pedestrian traffic control with partial connectivity. Our aim was to enhance control efficiency by proposing a novel connected vehicle-based adaptive area-pedestrian traffic control (CVAAPTC) framework. This framework leverages partial CV information, capitalizing on CV technologies to estimate real-time traffic conditions. The CVAAPTC model calculates real-time delays and incorporates group-based traffic and pedestrian constraints. This model is a non-convex, high-dimensional optimization problem that allows for the integration of various pedestrian demand estimation models for dynamic pedestrian flow management. We introduced the Bayesian delay optimization method as an efficient optimization approach to solve the CVAAPTC model, assuming a Gaussian process as the surrogate model. We also proposed an orthogonal random signal generation method to explore the feasible region as widely as possible, increasing the chances of finding a better local minimum.

17204919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17204919.value: Continuum models have been developed to evaluate crowd management strategies and predict crowd states in real-world scenarios [J1, J8]. Significant differences have been observed between stochastic and deterministic outputs, emphasizing the importance of incorporating stochasticity in practical applications [J10]. Methods like ME-PCM have demonstrated excellent convergence, computational performance, and improved efficiency compared to traditional methods [J12]. The analytical properties, such as existence and uniqueness, of the continuum model were studied [J3]. Additionally, the positivity-preserving discontinuous Galerkin method on triangular meshes has proven efficient and reliable in solving various pedestrian dynamic models [J7, C2]. Overall, these models provide valuable insights and tools for designing and improving pedestrian facilities. Discrete models have been developed to enhance the management of traffic flow. The random-parameter model, which considers speed heterogeneity, performs better in terms of goodness-of-fit and predictive accuracy. It can aid transportation planning, management, network design, vehicle routing, and traffic control [J2, C1]. The lane-based estimation method shows promising results in estimating lane-level travel time distributions by vehicle type using low-resolution video images [J4, C3]. The steady-state solution to the LWR model provides preliminary ideas for extending the model to the stochastic paradigm [J9]. The SLWR traffic flow model effectively describes dynamic traffic evolutions and reproduces commonly observed traffic phenomena, such as capacity drop. Unlike the classic LWR model, the SLWR model adapts well to heterogeneous road sections and can help users explore the stochastic paradigm, benefiting traffic planning, design, and real-time management [J5, J11, C5, C6]. The implementation of group-based adaptive traffic control systems has shown promising results in optimizing traffic flow and managing recurrent traffic patterns, persistent fluctuations, and transient vehicular arrivals [C4]. One study focused on the uncertainty estimation of connected vehicle (CV) penetration rate. Incorporating CV penetration rate uncertainty in system optimization can potentially improve results, as demonstrated by a simple illustrative application of CV-based adaptive signal control [J6]. The CV-based adaptive signal control framework optimizes traffic signal control using partial connected vehicle data. By considering CV penetration rate uncertainty, the framework can achieve optimal solutions for adaptive signal optimizations [J13]. Additionally, this framework has been extended to group-based adaptive area-pedestrian traffic control with partial connectivity, showing that the CV-based area-pedestrian traffic control framework effectively manages traffic and pedestrian flows in an area traffic control setting [J14]. Overall, these findings contribute valuable insights to CV-based applications and have a direct impact on the field of area-pedestrian traffic control.

17204919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17204919.value: This study highlights the significance of stochasticity in pedestrian flow modeling by developing a two-dimensional model that considers variable parameters in pedestrian movement. The research has broader implications for urban planners and transportation engineers who face challenges in reliable land use and transportation planning (RLUT) in cities. These challenges often arise from uncertainties in predicting factors such as future population growth and long-term implementation costs at the city level. The findings from this research illuminate the role of stochasticity in RLUT for urban cities. In densely populated urban environments, the transportation system can be viewed as a continuum, with land use attributes and travel demands consistently distributed across the city. Building on the experience gained in this study, it helps to develop effective and efficient numerical solvers for complex stochastic problems. Reliability analysis can provide crucial information for informed and effective planning decisions. A research proposal focusing on RLUT issues has been submitted to the Research Grants Council's General Research Fund and was awarded in the 2023/24 round. The foundation established by this project will significantly contribute to RLUT research, ultimately leading to meaningful results that address the complex challenges of land use and transportation planning within the stochastic paradigm.

17204919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17204919.value: This research project aimed to enhance transportation systems in urban cities by developing a comprehensive framework to optimize the performance of both traffic and pedestrian facilities within the stochastic paradigm. Focusing on dynamic-stochastic models for continuum pedestrian systems and discrete traffic networks, the project addressed challenges arising from the stochastic variability of real-world environmental factors. This approach represents a paradigm shift from conventional transportation analyses by explicitly modeling the stochasticity effects on traffic dynamics for both vehicle and pedestrian movements. The project also incorporated a group-based signal optimization framework to identify optimal signal plans that maximize road system performance for both traffic and pedestrian movements. Consequently, the research provided valuable insights into designing signal settings for area-wide street systems, improving traffic and pedestrian progressions between origins and destinations. By enhancing urban walkability and informing street furniture design, this project contributes to sustainable urban development and promotes active transportation. By providing adequate facilities for pedestrians, the project creates a more inclusive and safer environment for all. Overall, this research has developed a comprehensive framework for modeling and optimizing both traffic and pedestrian movements in urban street design, thereby promoting walkability, sustainable urban development, and a safer, more inclusive environment for everyone

17205419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205419.value: Heat dissipation would be a bottleneck to the development of microelectronic technology because the continuing trend of increasing the number of transistors in a densely integrated circuit dramatically increases the chance of overheating. Heat sink is an essential component to dissipate heat, but it is not easy to get around this bottleneck by the existing technology, and therefore a bio-inspired approach is proposed in this project. It is observed that, under heat stress, birds pant and breathe in and out rapidly to get a cooling breeze. In physical terms, the cooling effect is due to forced convection by increasing airflow over skin. As heat load increases, instead of further increasing the airflow, some birds supplement the heat loss by fluttering the gular region. This phenomenon dramatically increases the cooling effect. Meanwhile, the gular vibrates under its natural frequency, thereby requiring minimal amount of calories. Flutter is a complicated self-excited flow-induced flapping motion that usually occurs in a thin and elastic structure. A computational simulation has been conducted by the team to model a fluttering flag at the upstream of a channel with the setting of a standard straight fin heat sink. The result shows that a six-fold increase of heat dissipation can be achieved with the flutter. Inspired by this phenomenon and the promising preliminary simulation result, it is proposed to develop an enhanced heat sink technology by simply inserting fluttering flags in the cavities of a heat sink. To achieve this, a novel material with both high thermal conductivity and low rigidity must be designed. Inspired by the thin gular membrane with blood vessels of a bird, composite material made of a soft material sandwiched between meshes of a thermally conductive material is proposed. Different meshing patterns will be tested. This project will then investigate the dynamics of the fluttering flags and its corresponding thermal effect. The length and the rigidity of the flag are the key parameters to study because they control the fluttering frequency that dominates the heat transfer. A series of experiments will be carried out and a simulation model will be developed. The model will be used to optimize the parameters so as to maximize the cooling effect. A novel enhanced heat sink using a bio-inspired fluttering mechanism will finally be fabricated and its performance will be examined. The findings of this project will determine a new direction for the development of heat sink technology. 密集積體電路中電晶體數量的持續增加會導致晶片極容易過熱，如何加快散熱已成為微電子技術發展的瓶頸。散熱器是晶片散熱模組的重要組成部分，但現有技術難以達到理想的散熱效果，因此本項目提出了一種基於仿生顫振機制的被動式強化散熱技術。據觀察，在熱應激下，鳥類快速呼吸以獲得涼風。在物理機理方面，氣流通過皮膚的強制對流換熱，從而提高了冷卻效果。隨著熱負荷的增加，一些鳥類並不是進一步增加氣流，而是通過使角膜區域顫動來增強散熱。這種現象大大增加了冷卻效果。同時，角膜在其固有頻率下振動，只需要極少的能量。顫振是一種複雜的自激的流動引起的類似薄膜拍打的運動，通常發生在薄而有彈性的結構中。本團隊已經在標準直翅散熱器環境下模擬了通道上游的顫動薄片的散熱效果。結果表明，顫振可以使散熱增加6倍。受這種現象和初步模擬結果的啟發，本專案提出通過簡單地在散熱器的空腔中插入顫振薄片來開發一種新型的強化散熱技術。首先需要設計具有高導熱性和低剛性的新型材料，受到具有鳥類血管的薄膜的啟發，提出了將柔性材料嵌入在高導熱材料網路之間製成複合材料，並研究不同的網路結構的影響。其次，本專案將研究不同長度和剛度顫振薄片的流動特性及其相應的熱性能，並在一系列實驗研究的基礎上開發數學模型以優化其結構參數來獲得最優冷卻效果。最終，設計一種基於仿生顫振機制的新型強化散熱器，並對其性能進行檢驗。本項目的研究結果將有助於探討散熱器技術發展的新方向。

17205419.label: Realisation of objectives
17205419.value: The overall objectives have been achieved. Different kinds of materials with low rigidity for flutter and high thermal conductivity for heat transfer were developed and tested. Then, the dynamics behavior of fluttering flags was investigated. The effects of the fluttering flags on heat transfer in a channel were studied. Finally, some novel heat sinks were designed, and their performances were evaluated. Some key results are shown below. A wood-based material has been fabricated based on a two-step treatment method. Wood slices were polished using 120-grit sandpapers and immersed in a boiling aqueous solution of NaOH and Na2SO3 solution for several hours to obtain different degrees of delignification wood, followed by immersion in boiling DI water for several times to remove the remaining chemicals. Next, the wood slices were pressed at 100 ℃ for ~12 h to remove the water content in the wood and dramatically reduce the thickness of the wood slice. After fabricating the wood-based flexible flag, silver nanowires disperse solution was casted on the flexible wood. The fluttering behaviour of the wood-based flag was tested in a wind tunnel and observed under a high-speed camera. It was found that the anisotropic mechanical properties of the flexible wood allow it to have orderly two-dimensional fluttering motion even under high fluttering frequency. An experiment to study the effect of the flexibility of the flagpole was conducted. The influence of wind velocity, thickness of flag, channel width and flag length were investigated systematically. The fluttering dynamics of the flags with rigid (glass) and flexible (polyethylene terephthalate) flagpoles have been compared and recorded by a high-speed camera. It was found that when the flag flutters, the flagpole also undergoes aerodynamic force. The lift force generated from the fluttering flag applies a periodic moment on the flexible flagpole and causes the flagpole to vibrate. The vibration of the flagpole, in turn amplifies the flutter of the flag. Thus, by substituting the rigid flagpole with a flexible flagpole, a larger amplitude and a lower critical velocity for fluttering can be achieved. This finding was not only applied to the heat sink technology, but also employed to develop an innovative flutter-driven triboelectric nanogenerator for energy harvesting. A flexible flag with multiple splitting strips was investigated experimentally. Four scenarios were studied: a channel without flag; a channel with a 4cm×4cm×25um flag with different strip widths of 2cm, 1cm, 0.5cm, 0.25cm; a channel with a flag with different strip lengths of 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm; a channel with a flag with different strip thicknesses of 25 um,50um, 75um. Results showed that the splitting strips decreased the streamwise pressure drop and increased the crosswise flow mixing, thus increased the heat dissipation. Empirical correlations among pressure drop, wind velocity, friction factor, and Nusselt number were proposed. A dimensionless synthetic thermal-hydraulic performance factor was used to evaluate the overall benefits of each stripped-flag design compared to the case without the flag. It was found that the optimal value of the strip length was 4 cm, and that of the strip width was 1cm. The critical fluttering velocity has also been examined, and it was demonstrated that that flag with multiple strips can be actuated by a lower velocity than an uncut flag. The results indicated that a flag with multiple splitting strips provided a method to design a novel heat sink in an energy-efficient way. Minimizing the critical flapping velocity of the flags without sacrificing the heat transfer performance is needed. The fluttering flag was tested in an inverted configuration (i.e. the flag tail in the upstream wind direction and the flagpole in the downstream direction) in a channel flow. The inverted flag motion, the Nusselt number, the friction factor, and the thermal-hydraulic performance of a channel flow with an inverted flag were examined with different flag thicknesses and flow Reynolds numbers. Three different motion modes were identified: straight, flapping, and deflected modes. The flapping motion of the flag yields the increase in flow friction, and the highest flow friction occurs at the straight-flapping mode transition. The Nu augmentation achieved as high as 200% compared with the clean channel. The numerical simulation showed the high dependence of the flag motion on the wall vorticity. The largest vorticity was observed under the flapping mode, leading to the highest heat dissipation effect compared with other two modes. The enhancement of thermal-hydraulic performance was 16% and appeared at the straight-flapping mode transition for the thinnest flag with a thickness of 25 μm. Besides, the critical velocity was as low as 1.5 m/s, which was far lower to the conventional flag. Therefore, the high potential in enhancing the heat dissipation performance by inserting inverted flags into heat sinks was realized in this work, including lower critical velocity and superior heat transfer performance. A 9-channel standard straight fin heat sink with a hydraulic diameter of 10mm for each channel and fin length of 150mm, inserted with fluttering flags was designed. The effects of the length of the flag, the number of flags and the positions of the flags on the heat transfer performance were investigated. Experimental results showed that the performance was the best when the flag length was 6mm and three rows of flags (i.e. 37.5mm apart) were placed. The higher number of flags, the higher the heat transfer efficiency, but the dynamic pressure reduced 10-30% for each additional row of flags added. (Luo Yi, 2021, Heat Sink Enhancement by Passive Fluttering Mechanism, MSc Dissertation, HKU.) Another fluttering plate heat sink was also developed by using piezoelectric fan for its compact size and high energy efficiency. It simplified the setting by integrating the fan and aeroelastic plate as a single piezoelectric fan. The effects of fan location and channel configuration on heat transfer were studied. It was found that both the channel width and the fan position in the channel affected the heat transfer performance, and a maximum heat transfer enhancement of 55% compared with natural convection was achieved. The effect was credited to the enhancement of streamwise velocity. Moreover, the effects of the channel configuration, including expansion and contraction configurations, were examined. In the contraction configurations, jet flow patterns were identified in the channel outlet. The streamwise velocity was greatly improved from 0 to 0.7 m/s. In the expansion configurations, stronger spanwise propagations were detected, by quantitively examining the spanwise velocity and the spanwise propagation area. Besides, more and stronger vortices were induced by this configuration. Since either streamwise velocity enhancement or the spanwise propagation enhancement contributed to the channel flow heat transfer, the piezoelectric fan cooling was further improved by adopting either configuration. The maximum enhancement compared with natural convection was 70%, i.e., further improved by 10% from the first step.

17205419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205419.value: The effects of the fluttering flags on heat transfer in a channel were extensively studied. Since their heat transfer enhancement is only effective when they exhibit flapping behaviors, minimizing the critical flapping velocity of the flags, maximining the heat transfer performance without scarifying the pressure drop is critical. Many useful techniques were identified in this project, and two of them are pinpointed here. Flags with different strip widths were compared with a full flag on the performance of pressure drop and heat transfer. A high-speed camera was used to investigate their fluttering motion. The results showed that the performance of a flag with multiple strips outperformed that of the full flag for its lower pressure drop and higher heat dissipation effect. The performance of split flag was not linear with the strip number, and the optimal way in our study was to split the full flag into 4 strips. The maximum thermal-hydraulic performance factor of the split flag was 1.91, which was 26% higher than that of the full flag. Besides, the split flag started fluttering at a lower wind velocity. All these results demonstrate that the split strategy of a flag acting as a vortex generator is of great potential for improving the heat sink performance (Zhong et al. 2022a). Flag configuration plays a critical role in the fluttering dynamics. The cases of inverted flags with different thicknesses in a channel flow were studied. Three flag motion modes were identified by a high-speed camera with increasing flow velocity. In the first mode transition, i.e., when the flag started flapping, the heat dissipation had the highest enhancement. A 2D numerical model was built to further investigate the thermal-fluid-structure interaction of the fluttering flag. The model was validated using a benchmark case. Numerical simulation revealed that compared to the other motion modes, the flapping mode had the strongest average vorticity along the channel wall, leading to the highest heat dissipation among all flag motion modes. Experimental results showed that the critical velocity can be as low as 1.5 m/s, at which the heat dissipation enhancement can be as high as 100%. The findings in this work significantly benefit the application of flexible vortex generators in heat sinks, by enabling a decrease in critical velocity and a good enhancement in heat dissipation (Zhong et al. 2022b).

17205419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205419.value: This project focused on the fluttering dynamics and its heat transfer effect on a straight channel. The geometrical configurations (e.g. expansion and contraction) have been briefly studied but were found to have significant effects on the flow field and hence the fluttering dynamics. Since there are various fin-type designs in heat sink, other than the parallel plate type, it is suggested focusing on the heat transfer effect of geometrical configurations in the future. After identifying the flag-fluttering modes in the experiments and developed empirical correlations, it is about time to develop theoretical models and analytical solutions for the formulation, which are also geometrical configuration dependence. During the study of flapping amplitude and the distance between the channel wall and fluttering flag, we frequently encountered the phenomenon of wall touching by the fluttering flag, which will dramatically increase the pressure drop and is an adverse effect for heat sink design. However, it could be an advantage for developing a flutter-driven triboelectric nanogenerator, which used the touching effect between tribo-positive and tribo-negative materials to generate electricity. Suitable pair of triboelectric materials, power management circuit design, energy storage system, incorporating with the understanding of the fluttering dynamics are some possible future research topics.

17205419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205419.value: In this project, a bio-inspired approach was employed to improve the performance of a heat sink, which is an essential component for heat dissipation in microelectronics. It is observed that, under heat stress, birds pant and breathe in and out rapidly to get a cooling breeze. As heat load increases, instead of further increasing the airflow, some birds supplement the heat loss by fluttering the gular region. This phenomenon dramatically increases the cooling effect. Flutter is a complicated self-excited flow-induced flapping motion that usually occurs in a thin and elastic structure. Inspired by this phenomenon, an enhanced heat sink technology was developed by simply inserting fluttering flags in the cavities of a heat sink. The dynamics of the fluttering flags and its corresponding thermal effect were investigated. A series of experiments were carried out and a simulation was developed. The results indicated that flutter can be actuated by a lower velocity by a flag with multiple strips than an uncut flag. Inserting such a fluttering flag is an efficient way for improving the thermal-hydraulic performance of a heat sink. The findings of this project provide a new direction for the development of heat sink technology.

17205619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205619.value: The development of GaN vertical cavity surface emitting lasers (VCSEL) has been hampered by the difficulty of embedding mirrors between the GaN epitaxial layers and the foreign substrate, typically sapphire. Nevertheless, VCSELs offer many advantages over the edge-emitting variant as evident from the successes of GaAs-based infrared VCSELs, including low thresholds and high scalability. In order for VCSELs to emit at visible and ultra-violet wavelengths, quantum wells based on the III-nitrides would be excellent candidates. Instead of employing the typical epitaxial-grown AlGaN/GaN DBRs, GaN high-contrast gratings (HCGs) are employed in our proposed design. Additionally, the optical cavity is formed on a GaN thin-film structure processed by laser-liftoff of the sapphire substrate, so that the HCGs can be fabricated on both faces of the cavity. Being processed onto the same slab of semiconductor as the gain region, the monolithic HCGs are electrically conductive, thus allowing direct current injection through the mirrors. Just as importantly, the VCSELs can be fabricated from typical InGaN/GaN multi-quantum well (MQW) wafers grown on patterned sapphire substrates, a mature platform that is proven to produce light-emitting diodes with extremely high efficiencies that has been driving solid-state lighting. Thin-film devices are inherently outstanding at heat-sinking, especially for laser diodes including VCSELs which are higher temperature-sensitive. As can be seen, the proposed solution is superior in many different aspects compared to existing approaches, which can facilitate commercialization of GaN VCSELs benefiting a range of applications including laser lighting, laser displays and visible-light communications. GaN垂直腔表面發光射激光器（VCSEL）的發展受到在GaN外延層和異質襯底（通常為藍寶石）之間嵌入反射鏡的困難的阻礙。然而，從基於GaAs的紅外VCSEL的成功，包括低閾值和高可擴展性，VCSEL提供了許多優於邊緣發射變體的優勢。為了使VCSEL在可見光和紫外波長下發射，基於III-氮化物的量子阱將是極好的候選者。在我們提出的設計中，採用GaN高對比度光柵（HCG）代替採用典型的外延生長AlGaN / GaN DBR。另外，光學腔形成在通過藍寶石襯底的激光剝離處理的GaN薄膜結構上，使得HCG可以製造在腔的兩個面上。加工到與增益區域相同的半導體板上，單片HCG是導電的，因此允許通過反射鏡直接注入電流。同樣重要的是，VCSEL可以採用在圖案化藍寶石襯底上生長的典型InGaN / GaN多量子阱（MQW）晶圓製造，這是一個成熟的平台，經證明可生產具有極高效率的發光二極管，國家照明。薄膜器件在散熱方面具有突出的優勢，特別是對於包括對溫度敏感的VCSEL的激光二極管。可以看出，與現有方法相比，所提出的解決方案在許多不同方面是優越的，這可以促進GaN VCSEL的商業化，從而有益於包括激光照明，激光顯示器和可見光通信在內的一系列應用。

17205619.label: Realisation of objectives
17205619.value: Efforts have been undertaken to realize the project objectives. In fact, the objectives have been exceeded. Instead of sticking to the originally proposed structures, additional structures have been explored. Instead of only developing GaN based gratings, we have also explored oxide based gratings as well as hybrid gratings in order to find the optimal mirror for various GaN based laser devices. Laser devices employing the novel gratings have also achieved extremely high Q-factors of >10000. Using novel device structures, electrical-injection to the laser structures has also been demonstrated.

17205619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205619.value: Several different types of gratings have been developed in this project. These can be grouped into three major categories: (a) high contrast gratings, (b) GaN gratings and (c) hybrid gratings. (a) High contrast gratings This is a type of grating involving oxide materials coated over the semiconductor cavity for achieving optical confinement. However the grating must be "floated" over the microcavity in order to achieve the high contrast. In our work we deposited two different oxide layers, namely, titanium dioxide and silicon dioxide, over the GaN material. The grating is formed on the titanium dioxide top layer, and the bottom silicon dioxide layer is selectively removed so that the grating is floated over the cavity. However, robustness of the grating structure is poor as there is little support for the thin grating layer. (b) GaN monolithic gratings Instead of relying on foreign materials deposited over GaN, the active material of the semiconductor cavity device, the reflector gratings are fabricated directly onto the GaN material itself. We designed and fabricated a n-GaN grating to serve as a electrically conductive reflector. The structure was fabricated on thin GaN films, which is a GaN epi-layer film bonded eutectically to a Si substrate with n-GaN exposed, with the sapphire substrate removed by laser liftoff. The fabrication of the grating reflector on n-GaN is inherently the simplest configuration which provides optical reflection meanwhile achieving electrical conduction. The sample was optically pumped with a 349 nm pulsed diode laser. The PL emission is partially polarized from 430 to 465 nm. TM polarized (electric field perpendicular to grating line) is preferably reflected and leads to a weaker TM PL signal, and vice versa for TE polarization. (c) Hybrid gratings To realize the high-quality thin-film GaN microdisk lasers with superior optical isolation from the substrate, several pairs of DBR is inserted between the high refractive index material cavity and the metallic layer which is needed for wafer bonding process. This configuration could provide high reflectivity with low absorption losses across a large angular range for the cavity. In this project, we demonstrate a GaN microdisk laser with a hybrid omnidirectional reflector (ODR) structure combining an 8-pair SiO2/TiO2 DBR with an Al mirror to achieve bottom optical confinement. This hybrid ODR not only provides a higher reflectivity across a wide range of angles; this non-suspended structure also opens up possibilities for the design of subsequent electric injection structures.

17205619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205619.value: Lasers are ubiquitous in our everyday lives, and the fabrication of lasers is a complicated process. We developed novels mirror gratings which have potentials for simplifying the laser fabrication process, as well as to improve the cavity optical confinement. This is particularly suitable for the GaN-based lasers, which can laser at a wide range of wavelengths from the ultraviolet to to visible. The gratings developed in this project can be employed to build lasers will novel structures that may be suitable for new applications.

17205619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205619.value: Different grating structures as mirrors for laser cavity devices have been developed in this project. This includes oxide based gratings, semiconductor based gratings as well as hybrid gratings consisting of a combination of materials. Electrical conductivity can also be achieved with certain materials, including conductive oxides and semiconductors. These gratings have been deployed in microcavity laser structures as novel mirrors. The findings of this project paves the way towards novel laser devices with enhanced range of applications.

17205919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17205919.value: 肝癌是第六大最常見的癌症類型，也是癌症相關死亡的第四大常見原因。2018年，僅亞洲就佔全球發病率和死亡率的72%。肝細胞癌（HCC）是原發性肝癌中最常見的一種，有研究報道其5年生存率爲40-50%。對於沒有肝硬化（由疾病引起的肝臟瘢痕）的HCC患者，首選的一線治療是切除肝臟，切除HCC感染區域和周圍的肝組織，通常切除手術範圍大，以儘量減少復發。對於肝功能受損的肝硬化患者，可以提示肝移植，但肝捐贈者短缺和慢長的輪候選時間限制了肝移植的廣泛應用，甚至可能導致實際結果惡化。一般來說，HCC手術治療的嚴格選擇標準將手術候選人的比例限制在5-10%，其餘病例可能無法進行手術切除。對於晚期病例，最常見的治療方法是射頻消融（RFA）。在RFA中，高頻能量通過針傳導，以熱力殺死細胞，通常通過超聲引導。然而，位於大血管或內臟（如膽囊）附近的腫瘤可能會導致管道收縮、熱器官損傷或不完全消融的風險。儘管RFA和局部治療技術不斷進步，HCC 5年的複發率仍然高達70%。這促使對開發更完整的消融技術的需求，特別是對於接近血管和器官等關鍵結構的腫瘤。相對於RFA，經皮激光消融（LA）是HCC的一種選擇性局部消融治療方法，儘管治療結果相似，但其普及性已有所下降。 本項目的總體目標是開發和驗證一個用於MRI引導和腹腔鏡輔助HCC激光消融的機器人系統。該機器人系統將包括一個用於針瞄準的軟機器人立體定向框架，以及一個由液體和肌腱驅動的、用於肝臟收縮的磁共振條件腹腔鏡。實時磁共振測溫結合腹腔鏡視覺反饋將指導光纖植入和基於機器學習的腫瘤消融。將軟機器人立體定向框架直接固定在患者身上，通過全方位的磁共振跟蹤單元實時跟蹤患者的位置，可以在術中對患者的運動（如呼吸）進行糾正定位。該系統的驗證將在基於實驗室和基於MRI的測試中進行，使用假體肝臟模型、離體豬肝臟和活豬標本。這項研究可能是磁共振引導機器人輔助激光消融的第一步，並有可能成爲減少早期至中期肝癌的一種新模式。

17205919.label: Realisation of objectives
17205919.value: 1. MR-conditional robot platforms for tele-manipulation of laser probe The overall goal of this project is to develop and validate a robotic system for MRI-guided and laparoscopic-assisted laser ablation of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). PI and his collaborators have proposed an MR-safe robotic system for MRI-guided transoral laser microsurgery. The system provides a stable platform for laser beam delivery and navigation to the targeted lesions under MRI guidance. Owing to its miniature size (∅12 × 100 mm), inherent compliance, and 5 DoFs, the soft robot ensures zero electromagnetic interface with MRI and enables safe and dexterous operation within the confined oral and pharyngeal cavities. The laser manipulator was rapidly fabricated with hybrid soft and hard structures and was powered by microvolume (<0.004 milliter) fluid flow to enable laser steering with enhanced stiffness and lowered hysteresis. Submillimeter laser steering accuracy was demonstrated with a mean error < 0.20 mm. MRI compatibility testing demonstrated zero observable image artifacts during robot operation. Ex vivo tissue ablation and a cadaveric head-and-neck trial were carried out under MRI, where the team employed MR thermometry to monitor the tissue ablation margin and thermal diffusion intraoperatively. PI and his collaborators have also developed a tele-operated robot platform for magnetic resonance-guided focused ultrasound (MRg-FUS) treatment in abdominopelvic organs. Manual positioning of the FUS transducers is challenging, and the HIFU spot would have to be “steered” to ablate (>∅3.5 cm) large or multiple tumors (e.g., in liver). To this end, a hydraulic actuation design was implemented to enable 5-DoF manipulation of the FUS transducer, empowering the foci to be steered in a wide spatial coverage (100 mm × 100 mm × 35 mm) of major abdominal or pelvic organs. Accurate manipulation (0.2 mm in translation, 0.4° in rotation) of the FUS transducer holder was also achieved using the rolling diaphragm-sealed hydraulic actuators. Owing to its compact design (240 mm × 180 mm × 190 mm), the designed robot is capable to be accommodated in the water tank inside the MRI operating table for patient prone position. 2. A Fast Soft Robotic Laser Sweeping System PI and his collaborators have also proposed a compact two-segment soft robot for flexible laser ablation. The proximal hydraulic-driven segment can offer omnidirectional bending so as to navigate toward lesions. The long (56.4 mm) hydraulic-driven segment was composed of three spring reinforced chambers, enabling larger (∼70°) and slower (∼0.75 Hz) omnidirectional bending, relative to the steering motion of noncontact laser collimator centered at the short distal cap. A soft robot modeling and control scheme based on Koopman operators was proposed, with a disturbance observer designed to incorporate the controller feedback with real-time fiber optic shape sensing. Experimental validation is conducted on simulated or ex-vivo laser ablation tasks, thus evaluating our control strategies in laser path following across various contours/patterns. Such a simple compact laser manipulation can perform up to 6 Hz sweeping with precision of path following errors below1mm. The scheme could also be used on an endoscopic laser ablation robot with unsymmetric mechanism driven by two tendons. 3. Automated tracking under MRI for fast imaging To improve the positioning accuracy and tracking responsiveness, the proposed manipulated positioning system is equipped with wireless MR markers to localize the robot end-effector in MR image coordinates and incorporates a model-based robot control algorithm for actuation command calculation. The markers were made of cylindrical glass tubes (∅3 × 8 mm) with Gadolinium-doped water (concentration: 10 mM) sealed inside to provide signal source. Miniaturized RF-coil (1.5 mm × 6.7 mm) was attached on the tubes to locally amplify MR signal, thus offering high image contrast against background. Analytical forward kinematics of the robot was developed to predict the end-effector pose and combine with measured value from makers via Kalman filtering. The robot control responsiveness (from 0.1 to 0.4 Hz) was also evaluated to show the potential to compensate for the spot-tracking error induced by respiratory motion. The use of wireless radiofrequency (RF) markers was demonstrated to continuously register the robot task space in the MRI coordinates. 4. Learning-based modulation and hybrid control for MRI-guided FUS treatments The team has proposed a learning-based modulation and control framework for widespread MRg-FUS treatments without prior knowledge of heterogeneous media. The model ensured rapid (2.65 ms) full-wave correction on phase and amplitude aberrations simultaneously. This enabled high targeting accuracy (mean 0.35 mm, max. 0.65 mm) under the clinical requirement, thus alleviating off-target heating. Besides, the unwanted grating lobes could be effectively suppressed, and the focal obliquity was “aligned” to only 2.7°, thus reducing the risk of tissue damage. A hybrid control framework which combined fast phase estimator and closed-loop robust controller for LIFU was also proposed, which ensured tracking accuracy (0.30 mm) along an intended trajectory, even under unknown disturbance. The robust tracking performance demonstrated its adaptability inside the human body in LIFU applications. The estimator could offer a computationally efficient phase actuation (<3 ms) for the robust controller to facilitate real-time beam motion control. 5. MRI-guided semi-automated robot for percutaneous needle procedures PI and his collaborators have developed a semi-automated robotic system for MRI-guided percutaneous needle procedures. Owing to its compact size (Ø108 mm × 115 mm height) and lightweight (189 g), the robot allowed mounting on the patient and operation with standard loop coils under MRI, even for simultaneous needle targeting at multiple locations. Fine adjustment was performed by soft fluid-driven actuators to ensure minimal MR imaging artifacts. Granular jamming was also implemented to lock the needle position in place once after the fine-automated adjustments were made. Accurate (0.89 ± 0.31 mm) needle navigation was achieved by incorporating soft fluid-driven actuators with feedback control and stiffness modulation capabilities. The 3D location of the needle guide was reconfirmed by wireless MR tracking coils. The combined stiffness of the granular jamming and soft actuator was experimentally found to reach 2.337 N/mm. A needle insertion test was conducted, in which a targeting accuracy <0.9mm can be achieved. Negligible interference to MR imaging was also validated by an MR compatibility test. 6. Feedback closed-loop position tracking under MRI The feedback control of the soft fluid-driven actuator was conducted. To obtain the angular position of the needle guide, two MR safe optical absolute rotary encoders with a resolution of 0.044° were incorporated. The positional information was used for feedback control of the soft actuator with a PID controller. A manipulation task was conducted to evaluate the feedback control performance of the soft fluid-driven actuator. The coarse adjustment was locked, such that the needle guide can only be manipulated by the soft actuator. The position of the actuation block and the angular position of the needle guide can be converted to each other according to the kinematics mapping. The two absolute MR safe optical encoders were used to record the angular positions of the needle guide along two perpendicular axes for feedback control. A simple PID controller was implemented to control the orientation of the needle guide within the motion range of actuator. The needle guide can finally be manipulated and kept around the target orientation steadily with an error less than 0.2°, which also demonstrates the capability of precise actuation by the soft actuator.

17205919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17205919.value: PI and his collaborators have developed an MR-safe robot system for MRI-guided transoral laser microsurgery. The system provides a stable platform for laser beam delivery and navigation to the targeted lesions under MRI guidance. The robot is compact and lightweight, enabling mounting on the patient and operation with standard imaging coils under MRI. A hydraulic-driven tele-operated robot platform that enabled 5-DoF manipulation of the FUS transducer array. The model-based manipulation controller have been developed for MRg-FUS treatment in abdominopelvic organs. It would be the first of its kinds facilitating the largest acoustic window to track HIFU spot inside patient body, as well as the most degree of flexibility to avoid residual sonication-induced skin burn. Accrediting to the hydraulic actuation with fast-response (4.5-Hz bandwidth, 100-ms delay), this robot has the potential to compensate physiological motion, thus enabling to track a moving lesion target to provide safe and clinically effective treatment. High positioning accuracy w.r.t. translation (max. error: 0.2 mm) and rotation (max. error: 0.4°) indicated that the developed system satisfies the typical accuracy requirements in clinical HIFU. A closed-loop hybrid control scheme and a learning-based modulation model for robot-assisted MRg-FUS treatments have been proposed. The model enabled rapid (2.65 ms) phase-amplitude modulation and precise targeting (mean 0.35 mm, max. 0.65 mm), meeting clinical standard. Focal obliquity was significantly “aligned” to only 2.7°, reducing the risk of tissue damage. A machine-learning-enabled transducer design was developed, which enabled rapid modulation to significantly reduce the time required. This could not only efficiently determine the appropriate transducer size, but also balance the trade-off between computational cost and fabrication cost. Once trained, the model can be repeatedly employed for design in particular applications. A semi-automated robotic system for MRI-guided percutaneous needle procedures has been developed. The system provides semi-automated needle positioning, thus interactively guiding the surgeon to adjust the needle towards the target lesions, followed by automatic fine adjustment through closed-loop control of the soft robotic actuator. The compact and lightweight design allows not only the direct mounting of the robot to the body of the patient, but also simultaneous needle targeting at multiple locations with several robots alongside the loop coils. Granular jamming was also implemented to lock the needle position in place once after the fine automated adjustments have been made.

17205919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17205919.value: In future work, we will conduct more extensive testing in preclinical in-vivo/ex-vivo HIFU with the presented robot, which would improve the system’s capability for MRg-FUS abdominopelvic treatment. In addition to HIFU technology, recent advances of FUS technology also facilitates other treatments, such as hyperthermia mediated drug delivery. We will also investigate the transducer phase modulation (i.e., electronic steering), and its combination with robotic steering, which would deliver the relevant FUS applications, such as particular acoustic pattern forming under intra-op MRI. Besides, utilizing the ML-powered design method to further optimize the transducer configuration (e.g., saddle shaped transducer) will be a promising solution. Additionally, we will test the robot on liver/abdomen phantoms under MRI guidance to validate the proposed surgical workflow and more thoroughly analyze robot performance under mimicked surgical scenarios. we will have a focus on integrating other technologies that can complement the automation and precision offered by robotics, such as haptics for tele-operative needle insertion and augmented reality for guiding needle placement and insertion paths. The successful integration of MRI-guided, robot-assisted percutaneous ablation would present a timely improvement over current first-line treatments for hepatocellular carcinoma.

17205919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17205919.value: The proposed hydraulic-driven tele-operated robot platforms can achieve the close-loop actuation control of a laser probe, 5-DoF manipulation of ultrasound transducer arrays, enabling the most degree of flexibility to avoid excessive ablation or ultrasound skin burn. In our extended work for MRg-FUS treatment, the developed model-based controller in abdominopelvic organs could provide the largest acoustic window to track HIFU spot inside patient body. The proposed closed-loop hybrid control scheme and a learning-based modulation model for robot-assisted MRg-FUS treatments, can achieve rapid (2.65 ms) phase-amplitude modulation and precise targeting (mean 0.35 mm, max. 0.65 mm), meeting clinical standard. Focal obliquity was significantly “aligned” to only 2.7°, reducing the risk of tissue damage. The proposed MRI-guided semi-automated robotic system for percutaneous needle procedures can guide the surgeon in adjusting the needle towards the target lesions, followed by automatic fine adjustment by the soft robotic actuator. The compact and lightweight design allows the robot to be mounted directly onto the body, and also allows needle targeting at multiple locations.

17206119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206119.value: Hydraulic fills play an important role in a variety of infrastructure development such as harbours, airports and residential areas. As a result of the accelerated urbanization and rapid economic growth, a number of large-scale land reclamation projects have been completed around the world, particularly in densely populated coastal areas. Hydraulic fills are freshly deposited, very young water-born sediments, characterized by low relative density and low strength. These characteristics bring many challenges to engineers and researchers. In current practice, the in situ relative density (Dr) is considered as a key factor controlling the quality and performance of hydraulic sand fills and is commonly adopted as an index for the acceptance criteria. The in situ density of hydraulic sand fills is influenced by many factors, especially the method of placement and the presence of fines. The CPT-based method that is widely used in current practice, however, does not account for these factors properly and, therefore, does not necessarily lead to safe or economical design and construction. A promising alternative, or supplement, to the CPT-based method is provided by in situ measurement of shear wave velocity (Vs). Compared with the penetration test, Vs is a basic material property with clear physical meaning. This proposed research aims at addressing a number of critical issues relating to the use of Vs to determine the in situ state of hydraulic fills. The research integrates three important aspects: a structured experimental program on the characteristics of Vs in sands under a variety of conditions, a detailed analysis of experimental data in a sound theoretical framework, and an assessment of the applicability of the new Vs-based method using well-documented case histories. The outcome of this research will contribute to safer and more economical hydraulic fill projects. 水力吹砂被廣泛應用於人造島嶼的建設和填海造地中。水力吹填砂土沈積時間短、相對密實度低，且通常含有細顆粒，容易導致流滑破壞或液化。合理評估沈積砂土的密實度以及流滑破壞或液化的風險是有關工程設計及質量控制的重要課題。與粘土不同，高質量的非擾動原狀砂土樣品極難獲取且成本高昂，這使得評估砂土原位狀態成為巖土工程中的長期難題。此項研究旨在發展壹種基於剪切波速評估砂土原位狀態以及液化可能性的新方法。該方法將建立在系統土工實驗及臨界狀態土力學分析基礎上，涵蓋純凈砂及不同細顆粒含量的粉砂以及不同試樣制備方法，並將應用於工程實例。由於剪切波速度可以在實驗室和現場進行可靠測量，新方法預計在巖土工程實踐中具有廣泛應用前景。

17206119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206119.value: The project has created a large volume of high-quality data and resulted in some new findings as summarized below. Two papers have been published in the world’s premier geotechnics journal, one paper will be published as a book chapter by Springer Nature, and another two papers are under preparation. In addition, the project results contribute to two keynote lectures by the PI at two international conferences (one in Osaka, Japan and one in Bochum, Germany). Two PhD students, one post-doc and two undergraduate students have been trained in the framework of this project. • For each clean sand tested, its shear wave velocity is affected by the quantity of fines apart from the void ratio and confining stress. Under similar confining pressure and void ratio, the shear wave velocity decreases with fines content. By using the state parameter in the critical state theory, a unique relationship has been established between the stress-corrected shear wave velocity and the state parameter regardless of fines content. The relationship contains three constants that reflect particle characteristics. For in situ anisotropic stress conditions, an alternative form of the relationship has been established, and the concept of state profiles in terms of state parameter in the plane of shear wave velocity versus effective overburden pressure is put forward. The state parameter has proven a useful state variable for characterizing soil behavior under both cyclic and monotonic loadings. • Four sample preparation methods have been studied in the laboratory to mimic the different placement methods in construction of hydraulic fills. The reduction of shear wave velocity or small-strain shear modulus with fines can be quite different when different sample preparation methods are used. For specimens prepared by the dry deposition (DD) method, a marked reduction of shear wave velocity or small-strain shear modulus is observed compared with the specimens prepared by the moist tamping (MT) method, and the difference tends to become more significant when smaller fines are present. For specimens prepared by two water sedimentation methods, the measured shear wave velocities approximately locate between those of DD and MT specimens. • The unified relationship between shear wave velocity and state parameter has been confirmed by the discrete element simulations of both small-strain wave propagation and large-strain triaxial testing. The possible microscopic mechanism has been found to be the unique relationship between the mechanical coordination number and the stress-corrected shear wave velocity.

17206119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206119.value: The fines contents studied in the project are typically less than 30%. It would be of interest to study the case of higher fines contents and to examine whether the unified relationship applies to such case. The impact of size disparity ratio is another issue that deserves further investigation. Application of the proposed method to more case histories and identification of the possible areas of improvement would also be worthwhile.

17206119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206119.value: Hydraulic fills play an important role in a variety of infrastructure development such as harbours, airports and residential areas. As a result of the accelerated urbanization and rapid economic growth, a number of large-scale land reclamation projects have been completed around the world, particularly in densely populated coastal areas. In current practice, the in situ relative density is considered as a key factor controlling the quality and performance of hydraulic sand fills and is commonly adopted as an index for the acceptance criteria. This project was aimed to develop a new method for the evaluation of the quality of the hydraulic fills. The method involves the use of shear wave velocity and is built on systematic experimental data in conjunction with a sound theory. Several critical questions of both academic interest and practical importance have been addressed in the project, and the areas of further research have been identified. The outcome of this research contributes to safer and more economical design and construction of hydraulic fills.

17206519.value: 應用氧化還原對的熱電化學電池在等溫操作下回收低溫廢熱

17206519.label: Project Objectives

Demonstrate the feasibility and practical applications of aTEC for harvesting solar thermal energy to power smart windows in hot weather

17206519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17206519.value: 低熱量可以以廢熱或環境的形式大量供應。將低等級熱量有效轉化為電力是一項巨大的挑戰。固態熱電（TE）設備是一種廣泛使用的熱電轉換器，但在低等級加熱狀態下運行時能量轉換效率較低。基於液體的熱電化學電池（TECs）可能為低等級熱量收集提供經濟有效且可擴展的方法，因為它們的溫度係數（mV / K）比TE半導體高一個數量級。目前對TECs的研究主要集中在熱梯度或熱循環的開發上，但這種方法的潛力受到效率低下或外部電力需求的限制。通過縮短熱電極和冷電極之間的距離以改善離子質量傳遞可以增強器件性能，然而這使得難以保持足夠的溫差以在電極的兩側連續維持所需的氧化還原反應。因此，TEC系統的兩難困境是如何改善液體電解質的電導率，同時確保在電池中發生所需的反應。在過去的一年中，我們發明了一種新的不對稱熱電化學電池（aTEC），僅在加熱時進行熱電轉換，而不是使用熱梯度或熱循環。使用氧化石墨烯（GO）陰極和KCl水系電解液及聚苯胺（PANI）陽極的aTEC袋電池可以在開路條件下進行熱充電。在等溫操作下，兩個電極之間具有很短距離的電池構造可用於改善電解質傳導性和快速加熱/冷卻。需要進一步研究以提高器件在實際應用中的性能。 本項目旨在了解GO-電解質界面上關於熱電壓產生的電容反應，並使用GO /納米鉑顆粒（PtNPs）陰極，PANI陽極和摻有氧化還原對的電解質構建基於氧化還原對的aTEC以增強放電容量。此外，我們將展示aTEC在炎熱天氣下收集太陽能熱能為智能窗供電的可行性和實際應用。初步實驗證實，所提出的方法可以在70℃下實現4.58％的熱電轉換效率，相當於卡諾效率的35％。通過進一步的研究和開發，我們相信aTEC具有成為低溫熱回收關鍵技術的巨大潛力。

17206519.label: Realisation of objectives
17206519.value: We have successfully realized our objectives and achieved our goals. Our team has made significant progress in constructing a redox couple-based aTEC (aqueous thermogalvanic cell) by utilizing a GO/PtNPs cathode and PANI anode. Additionally, we have incorporated an electrolyte with a redox couple to enhance the discharge capacity of the cell. Moreover, we have demonstrated the feasibility of our aTEC and its practical applications for harvesting solar thermal energy. Specifically, we have utilized this technology to power smart windows during hot weather conditions. This breakthrough has paved the way for efficient utilization of renewable energy sources and has the potential to revolutionize the field. In addition to our research achievements, we have actively disseminated our findings. We have published papers in reputable scientific journals, contributing to the knowledge and understanding of aTECs. Furthermore, we have participated in various competitions related to our research topic and received awards in recognition of our innovative work.

17206519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17206519.value: 1. In this project, we report a DTCCNCF using GO cathode and NiHCFeII or PANI anode with an environmentally friendly KCl electrolyte for low-grade heat recovery. 2. Using NiHCFeII as the anode not only improves the discharge capacity but also allows the device to be recycled. 3. The fundamental thermodynamics and kinetics process of electrodes at different temperatures has been systematically studied. 4. The thermal cell achieves a high heat-to-electricity conversion efficiency of 3.59% (equivalent to 26.2% of Carnot efficiency), which is in a leading position compared with the existing technologies in low-grade heat regimes. 5. Through thermal charging and electrical discharging cycles, an areal power density of 10 µW/cm2 can be reached for more than 100 cycles. 6. The module (with 10 cells) can harvest heat from solar irradiation in the daytime and power smart windows to regulate the solar irradiance transmission so as to reduce the energy consumption in air conditioning system

17206519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17206519.value: 1. After long-term cycling (>500 cycles or more), the cell can be disassembled and then reassembled for the next life cycle because GO and NiHCFe or PANI electrodes can be regenerated by simple chemical treatments, realizing green technology and circular economy. 2. This work also demonstrates the great applicability of this new-type thermal cell, which provides an alternative way for effectively harvesting low-grade heat in various applications. Other PBA analogues or their composites with negative α can be used to further improve device performance in the future

17206519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17206519.value: Ubiquitous energy input is dissipated as waste heat to the ambient in industry, power plants, data centers, and combustion engines. A large portion of the waste heat occurs as low-grade heat below 100 oC, the conversion of which is still inefficient due to the low-temperature differential. We have reported a thermal cell (TEC) using graphene oxide/platinum (GO/PtNPs) cathode and PANI or NiHCFe anode with aqueous redox electrolyte for efficient heat-to-electricity conversion. The cell has a unique feature of thermal charging and electrical discharging under high temperatures, and then the system can be self-regenerated when cooled down, which allows cyclability.
