17207119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207119.value: Back in July 2018, the number of monthly failures of peer-to-peer (P2P) lending platforms in China reached its peak in the past two years. Until then, the cumulative failures was 4,334 and this number continued to grow at a fast pace. This indicates that, among China's $10 trillion shadow-banking system, the P2P lending industry is among the riskiest and least-regulated parts. The higher financial risk borne by the P2P lending platforms can be attributed to the fact that most of them in China not only act as information intermediaries but also play similar roles to that of traditional banks, even in the absence of deposit insurance. The Chinese authority had tried to rectify this situation by imposing the Interim Measures on Online Lending back in 2016. These measures restricted each internet finance platform to be just an online lending information intermediary. Although doing so might effectively reduce the financial risk for the lending platforms, at the same time, it might hinder the growth of internet finance industry. Therefore, it is crucial to develop a framework that balances the trade-offs between the growth in internet finance industry and the financial risk for internet finance platforms so as to obtain the optimal risk management strategies that serve as guides to policymaking. My contribution to this proposed project will be twofold in both building up a tractable risk management framework and improving the quality of policymaking. To the PI's best knowledge, this project is among the first attempt to develop the tractable game-theoretical model that analyzes the interaction between the regulator and internet financing providers, and further determines the equilibrium financing budgets allocated by the regulator and loan repayments committed by the providers. Moreover, the PI aims to establish a financial network model that examines the default clustering phenomenon empirically observed in the Chinese P2P lending industry and explores the sources of default clustering. Using these two models, the PI will further investigate, in an internet finance industry, what the optimal number of service providers should be, what the value of information sharing among the agents is in terms of the reduction in default risk, and what types of common asset holdings that drive the default clustering are. The results obtained from the proposed models will directly lead to the policy implications related to the optimal size of internet finance industry and the prevention of default clustering in internet finance platforms. 2018年7月,中國網絡借貸平台公司（後文簡稱平台）單月倒閉的數量，攀升至歷史以來的最高峰。截至當時，累積倒閉的公司數量已高達4,334間，且這數目還在快速增長中。這顯示了，在中國10兆美元的影子銀行系統中，網絡借貸產業風險最高，且最不受規範約束。其高風險來自於平台不只扮演了中介借方和貸方的平台，它們同時在沒有任何保險機制的保護下，扮演了傳統銀行的角色：它們將自有資本借予客戶，並將債權證券化售予投資人。原屬於借款人該承擔的信用風險轉移至平台，因而增加了平台倒閉的風險。有鑒於此類非典型平台應該有的商業模式，2016年中國政府實施了【網絡借貸信息中介機構業務活動管理暫行辦法】，用以規範網路借貸產業。此辦法限制每間平台只能中介借貸，不能從事金融機構承辦的其他業務。此規定雖然降低了平台的倒閉風險，另一方面卻減少了平台可從事的業務，限制了網絡借貸產業的發展，長期以往，可能進一步影響中國的經濟成長。因此，開發一個可以權衡網絡借貸產業的成長及風險、擬訂最佳風險管理策略、進而作為政策制定參考的模型，至關重要。本項目將研擬出一套可行的風險管理架構，用以增進制定相關政策的品質。具體來説，本項目將開發一個以博弈論爲基礎的模型，用以分析監管單位和平台公司的互動，決定各平台公司可借出自有資本的總金額；和各平台公司將債權證券化後，收取的利息。再者，本項目要建立一個金融網絡模型，用以分析平台倒閉潮，發掘造成倒閉潮的原因。應用這兩個模型，本項目將進一步探究，在網絡借貸產業中，最佳的的借貸平台數量、信息共享的價值、造成倒閉潮的共同持有資產類型。本研究成果，可直接作爲與網絡借貸產業規模，和避免倒閉潮相關政策的參考。

17207119.label: Realisation of objectives
17207119.value: Objective 1: Propose a tractable model that leads to the optimal risk management strategies which balance the trade-offs between the growth and risk. The growth and risk level within the P2P lending industry are influenced by the implementation of disclosure requirements by online P2P platforms. These requirements play a dual role. Firstly, they determine the level of effort borrowers must exert to secure funding, consequently impacting the demand that can be met by the market. Secondly, disclosure requirements dictate the information available for loan screening, directly influencing the default risk associated with funded loans. Using a signaling game theoretic model, I analyze the trade-offs between growth and risk levels across four competing disclosure requirements in the P2P lending industry. These requirements include: mandatory disclosure of soft information, mandatory disclosure of hard information, mandatory disclosure of both soft and hard information, and mandatory disclosure of hard information with optional disclosure of soft information. Through my analysis, I establish the following findings: Under the requirement of mandatory soft information, there is a high likelihood of securing financing. However, this is accompanied by a high level of default risk. Conversely, under the requirement of mandatory hard information, there is a low likelihood of securing financing and this is coupled with a low level of default risk. Requiring both soft and hard information strikes a balance between the likelihood of securing financing and the default risk. This approach yields a medium likelihood of securing financing and a medium level of default risk. Additionally, the optionality of disclosing soft information does not significantly impact the trade-offs between likelihood of securing financing and default risk. The findings outlined above have important policy implications for the P2P lending industry. During periods of credit expansion, when the primary goal is market growth, it is advisable to implement the requirement of mandatory soft information across the entire market. This approach will facilitate a higher likelihood of securing financing and support the desired growth objectives. Conversely, during periods of credit contraction, when the focus is on risk reduction, it is recommended to adopt the requirement of mandatory hard information. This will help mitigate default risk and align with the objective of reducing overall risk levels in the market. This objective is fully addressed. These results have been thoroughly explored and documented in a research paper titled "Information Disclosure Requirements in Peer-to-peer Financing Markets". The paper has been prepared for submission to the journal Production and Operations Management. Objective 2: Establish a tractable model that examines the default clustering phenomenon observed in the Chinese P2P lending industry, and Objective 3: Determine the policy related factors: the optimal size of an internet finance industry, the value of information sharing and sources of default clustering. Both objectives are fully addressed. The findings are reported in (1) a paper titled "Information Disclosure Requirements in Peer-to-peer Financing Markets" that has been prepared for submission to the journal Production and Operations Management, and (2) a paper titled " Effects of Inconsistent Information in Peer-to-peer Markets" that has been prepared for submission to the journal Production and Operations Management. Since 2017, the P2P lending industry in China has faced an unexpected crackdown by Chinese authorities due to widespread fraud and defaults within the sector. This has resulted in the complete elimination of the P2P industry in China by November 2020. The focus of this project is to investigate the underlying causes behind the abnormally high default rate observed in the Chinese P2P lending industry. In Paper (1), it is demonstrated that the requirement of mandatory soft information contributes significantly to the high default risk experienced in the Chinese P2P lending industry. Many P2P lending platforms in China have placed a strong emphasis on borrowers providing soft information, while lacking robust mechanisms to verify hard information. This imbalance has contributed to the elevated default rates observed in the industry. In Paper (2), I offer additional validation of the aforementioned findings by exploring how lenders aggregate different types of information for loan screening purposes. I delve into the effects of inconsistent soft and hard information within P2P lending markets. The results reveal that lenders tend to assign more weight to soft information compared to hard information. However, when there is a discrepancy between the two types of information, the effectiveness of soft information is weakened. In the context of the Chinese P2P lending industry, where reliable hard information is lacking as a benchmark for loan screening, lenders heavily rely on soft information. Unfortunately, this reliance on potentially unreliable soft information can lead to the inclusion of disinformation in the decision-making process. Consequently, the default rate within the Chinese P2P lending industry is significantly higher compared to that observed in the United States or Europe. Both Paper (1) and Paper (2) highlight the lack of validated hard information as a key factor contributing to the clustering of defaults within the P2P lending industry. The presence of validated hard information can significantly mitigate default risk. It not only enables the implementation of mandatory disclosure requirements for hard information but also serves as a benchmark for lenders to cross-check the accuracy of soft information, leading to better assessment of borrowers' creditworthiness. Utilizing data from multiple P2P platforms for validation purposes often leads to more effective verification of hard information, as opposed to relying solely on information from a single platform. Paper (1) and Paper (2) offer a framework to quantify the value of information sharing between P2P platforms. This value can be measured by the reduction in default risk achieved through the use of better-validated hard information. Objective 4: Provide guidance for policymaking and evaluate the effectiveness of the existing measures imposed by the Chinese authority. This objectives is fully addressed. The findings are reported in (1) a paper titled "Information Disclosure Requirements in Peer-to-peer Financing Markets" that has been prepared for submission to the journal Production and Operations Management, and (2) a paper titled " Effects of Inconsistent Information in Peer-to-peer Markets" that has been prepared for submission to the journal Production and Operations Management. The Chinese authorities took a significant step in addressing the challenges of the P2P lending industry by closing down all P2P platforms within a four-year period, starting in 2017. However, this action has posed challenges when evaluating the effectiveness of this measure. While it eliminated default risk associated with the P2P industry, it also eliminated the entire sector. Despite this challenge, Paper (1) and Paper (2) offer valuable guidance for policymakers to develop the P2P industry: - Mandatory soft information requirements support growth objectives during credit expansion. - Mandatory hard information requirements mitigate default risk during credit contraction. - Mandatory disclosure requirements balance growth and risk levels in the P2P industry for market stability. - Information sharing among P2P lending platforms improves the effectiveness of hard information in loan screening.

17207119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207119.value: In this project, I have established the following findings: - Mandatory soft information requirements increase the likelihood of securing financing but also come with a higher default risk. - On the other hand, mandatory hard information requirements lower the likelihood of securing financing but also reduce default risk. - Requiring both soft and hard information strikes a balance, resulting in a medium likelihood of securing financing and a medium level of default risk. - The optional disclosure of soft information does not significantly affect the trade-offs between securing financing and default risk. - Inconsistent soft and hard information within P2P lending markets leads lenders to give more weight to soft information. However, when there is a discrepancy between the two types of information, the effectiveness of soft information is weakened. These findings are discussed in two papers titled "Information Disclosure Requirements in Peer-to-peer Financing Markets" and "Effects of Inconsistent Information in Peer-to-peer Markets," both prepared for submission to the journal Production and Operations Management.

17207119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207119.value: Further development of the research can be pursued by considering the following directions: - Explore the impact of counter signaling behavior exhibited by borrowers with high creditworthiness. This behavior is expected to influence the evaluation of information disclosure requirements, particularly in terms of the likelihood of securing financing and risk levels under mandatory hard information requirements with optional soft information. Additionally, examine how lenders aggregate both soft and hard information in light of this behavior. - Extend the current findings to encompass P2P loan auction platforms. Design and conduct a field experiment to investigate the aggregation of soft and hard information among lenders in these platforms and examine the effects of inconsistent information. Evaluate the effectiveness of the four competing information disclosure requirements for P2P loan auction platforms.

17207119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207119.value: The objective of this research project was to investigate the root cause of the default clustering phenomenon observed in the once-thriving P2P lending industry in China. The study revealed that defaulted P2P platforms often had a high default rate of funded loans, which was primarily attributed to the lack of validated hard information in the loan screening process. When loan screening relied solely on soft information, there was a high likelihood of securing funding with a corresponding high default risk. This was because lenders lacked a benchmark to cross-check the validity of soft information, making it difficult to identify disinformation and fund loans requested by borrowers with low creditworthiness. The findings highlight the need for information sharing between P2P lending platforms to enable better-validated hard information for loan screening. Despite the elimination of the P2P lending industry in China, the research provides valuable guidance for policymaking in other areas or for a potential future restart, if any, of the P2P lending industry in China.

17207419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17207419.value: Nearest-neighbor pairs of impurity nitrogen atoms and carbon lattice vacancies in diamond, as known as nitrogen-vacancy (NV) color centers, are promising sensing probes for detection of physical quantities, such as magnetic, electrical, and temperature fields, with nanoscale spatial resolution. Such detection is of great importance in both fundamental science and practical applications. For example, mapping the temperature distribution in living cells and imaging of magnetotactic bacteria using NV centers help understand fundamental biochemistry mechanisms in biology research. NV centers’ sensing capabilities arise from a number of intriguing properties, including long spin coherence time at room temperature, easy optical readout, atomic size, stability in a wide temperature range and compatibility with most biological and chemical environments. However, a major challenge in building NV-center-based quantum sensing devices is to accurately place NV centers at specific locations with desirable quantity and quality. Existing works mostly employ NV-center-containing nanodiamonds as the sensing probes. Although they are useful for laboratory-level scientific research, their random placement significantly hinders their applications in scalable sensing devices. A widely adopted method for creating NV centers in sensors fabricated on bulk or thin-film diamond substrates uses nitrogen implantation and annealing. However, the spin and optical properties of high-density NV centers created by this method are poor, mainly due to the heavily damaged diamond lattice with clustered vacancies. This project applies our team’s intensive experience in focused helium ion beam lithography to creating and patterning NV centers in diamond. We have proposed and first demonstrated the creation of NV centers using HIBL on nitrogen-containing diamond and observed superior spin and optical properties on these NV centers, mainly owing to the less clustered lattice damages. Based on our previous results, the targets of the proposed project are to 1) experimentally characterize the quantity and the three-dimensional distribution of these HIBL-patterned NV centers, 2) elucidate the mechanisms governing the NV center formation and distribution through numerical modeling, and 3) explore an innovative approach for self-aligned patterning of NV centers on nanostructured diamond surface with enhanced placement accuracy and photoluminescence extraction. Successful completion of the proposed project will provide a fundamental understanding of high-resolution placement of NV centers through systematic characterization and modeling of their spatial distribution, and as a result, invent new approaches to creating patterned NV centers with improved placement accuracy and properties for sensing applications. Ultimately, it will contribute to develope the new-generation NV-center-based quantum sensing and quantum information processing devices.

17207419.label: Realisation of objectives
17207419.value: The PI’s team has addressed all the objectives in this project. Although most of the project implementation was during the pandemic and the planned research activities, particularly those requiring collaboration outside HK, were significantly affected, the team tried alternative solutions to achieve the planned objectives. 1) We completed the characterization of the three-dimensional spatial distribution of NV-centers created by patterned implantation using a focused helium ion microscope in Nanjing University. We used various characterization methods, including confocal fluorescence microscope at HKU, and a super-resolution stimulated emission depletion microscope (STED) at Peking University, to investigate the volume size of the NV centers created using helium ion implantation with different doses. 2) Based on the high-resolution microscopic characterization results, we estimated the quantity of NV centers in the sample under different helium ion implantation doses. 3) We also developed a hybrid numerical model including Stopping and Range of Ions in Matter (SRIM) and three dimensional lattice Monte Carlo (3D-LMC) to investigate the quantity and distribution of NV centers by considering three factors: the scattering of helium ions in diamond, the vacancy diffusion when annealing and trapping of diffusing vacancies by substitutional nitrogen atoms. Our numerical model can agree with the experimental characterization results. 4) Our planned task of developing a self-aligned approach to create near-surface NV centers on nanostructured diamond surface is achieved by using numerical simulation. Our method uses focused helium ion beam to implant helium ions through a layer of hydrogen silsesquioxane (HSQ) of a few hundred nm thick. This will simultaneously form the NV center ensemble near the surface, and the top solid lens-like structure of cured HSQ which plays the light extraction function. Our numerical modeling shows that such a self-aligned method can improve the photoluminescence extraction. Overall, the successful completion of our work established a solid ground to further explore the application of helium ion implantation induced NV centers in quantum sensing applications. Some of the numerical modeling approaches developed in this project inspired and facilitated the exploration of other lithographic patterning technology in our team.

17207419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207419.value: 1. Created near-surface NV center ensembles using focused helium ion implantation. The NV centers can be confined within tens of nanometers near the diamond surface and with high placement accuracy. 2. Developed a numerical model that combines Stopping and Range of Ions in Matter (SRIM) and three dimensional lattice Monte Carlo to investigate the quantity and distribution of NV centers by considering the scattering of helium ions in diamond, the vacancy diffusion when annealing and trapping of diffusing vacancies by substitutional nitrogen atoms. 3. Elucidated key mechanisms determining the spatial distribution range and quantity of NV centers using the above numerical model and experimental characterization results. 4. Proposed and numerically modeled a lithographic patterning method using focused helium ion beam to created near-surface NV centers self-aligned with simultaneously fabricated HSQ solid lens for enhanced photoluminescence extraction.

17207419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207419.value: Based on the achievements in this project, more development towards practical applications can be expected. For example, applying the near-surface NV centers with high quantity and high quality in magnetometry applications is promising. The capability of creating near-surface NV centers with precise three-dimensional placement accuracy may also open the venue towards the integration of NV-based quantum emitters with integrated photonic circuits. Our project designed and investigated the self-aligned formation of NV centers and light-extracting nanostructures, which may be further developed into nanostructures with more photonic functions such as optical cavities, resonant antennas, etc. Moreover, the techniques developed in this project and the training provided to students also enable further exploration in our interference lithography nanopatterning, structural color, and many other relevant areas.

17207419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207419.value: This project addressed the accurate placement of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers near the surface in a bulk diamond. NV centers are promising sensing probes for detection of physical quantities, such as magnetic, electrical, and temperature fields, and have been widely explored for unprecedented detection sensitivity and spatial resolution. Many of these applications require the NV centers to be placed near the diamond surface with controllable quantity and precise placement. Our project used high-resolution and super-resolution optical microscopy imaging tools to investigate the spatial distribution and quantity of the NV centers created using focused helium ion beam implantation, developed numerical models that combine 3D lattice Monte Carlo and ion scattering simulation to understand the NV center quantity and distribution, and also investigated a new self-aligned fabrication approach that couples the formed NV centers with other nanostructures for more efficient photoluminescence light extraction. This project established a solid ground to further explore the application of helium ion implantation induced NV centers in quantum sensing applications.

17207719.label: Realisation of objectives
17207719.value: 1. To fabricate and characterise the material and surface properties of the coatings embedded with Ag/Ag@AgCl/ZnO nanostructures and arginine-glycine-aspartic acid-cysteine (RGDC) on titanium biomaterials, e.g., surface structures, photocatalytic properties and ion release profile. The 1st objective has been fully achieved in this research. The preparation of the coatings embedded with Ag/Ag@AgCl/ZnO nanostructures and arginine-glycine-aspartic acid cysteine (RGDC) on titanium biomaterials involved a two-step treatment (i.e., ultraviolet reduction and atomic layer deposition (ALD)). The phase structure of the coating was confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD). Apart from XRD, the morphology and composition of the coatings was determined using a scanning electron microscope (SEM) equipped with an energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometer (EDS). Furthermore, the microstructures of the coatings was investigated using a transmission electron microscope (TEM) and selected-area electron diffraction (SAED). The deposition of Ag/Ag@AgCl/ZnO could greatly enhance the generation of singlet oxygen in this system. An initial burst of Ag+ and Zn2+ was released within the first 3 days followed by a slower release from the coating. 2. To systematically evaluate the antibacterial activity, cytotoxicity, bioactivity and bio-functional properties of the coatings on titanium biomaterials by using in vitro approaches. The results have demonstrated that the coating quickly and effectively killed bacteria due to the enhanced generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). The results of real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-QPCR) suggested that the coating significantly promotes the expression of genes involved in osteogenesis, including ALP, RUNX2, and OCN. 3. To comprehensively investigate the antibacterial activity and osteogenic biological properties of the new coatings in vivo (i.e., antibacterial capability, inflammatory response, tissue toxicity and the capability to form new bone) by using established mouse models. A mouse model with bone implant, which replicates the clinical scenario, was selected to investigate the antibacterial activity and osteogenic biological properties of the new coatings. The quantity of the newly formed bone was characterized by using micro computed tomography, whereas the quality of new bone was examined by histological and immunochemical analyses. Additionally, the mechanical properties were also determined by using nano-indentation approach. Therefore, the Young's modulus of the newly formed bone could be obtained and compared with others.

17207719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17207719.value: In this GRF project, we have successfully established a coating embedded with Ag/Ag@AgCl/ZnO nanostructures and arginine-glycine-aspartic acid-cysteine (RGDC) on titanium biomaterials. This specifically treated bone allograft proposed an advanced bactericidal technology, namely antibacterial photodynamic therapy (aPDT). Furthermore, this coating was able to facilitate in vitro cell proliferation, osteogenic differentiation, as well as new bone formation and osseointegration of the allograft to host bone. Lastly, this study identifies a robust approach that can simultaneously facilitated in situ bacterial killing and effectively enhance the bioactivity of an allograft bone and its subsequent osseointegration to a host bone without the aids of biological growth factors or stem cell therapy. In addition to the invited talks in several international conferences, the PI and his team have also published 5 SCI journal papers.

17207719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17207719.value: In addition to the implant in femur, we are confident that our findings can also apply to other bone implant models, e.g., mandible bone and cranial bone. Prior to the application, we have to identify the pathway of bone formation induced by the coating that may help address the problem of potential carcinogenicity. In addition, a comprehensive evaluation with the use of large animal model is needed before we apply for human clinical trials. Also, our approach should benchmark with the commercially available products such as the bone graft embedded with bone morphogenetic protein 2 or beta-tricalcium phosphate granules for head-to-head comparison. If successful, we may commercialize this bone graft together with relevant industrial partners in the future.

17207719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17207719.value: Bone healing or repair is a biological process that can take weeks to months and patients suffering from bone fractures in particular to those with osteoporosis usually require extended time off from work or school and away from normal activities. There have been many attempts to enhance bone repair by mechanical means such as insertion of novel metallic implants and by biological means such as the use of stem cell therapy. However, bacterial infection and unsatisfactory integration at the bone-implant interface remain two major post-operative complications. Due to these complications, implant loosening, the malunion or nonunion of the bone fracture and the failure of the implant are sometimes documented following surgical implantation. Hopefully, we have recently developed a new coating to reinforce the antibacterial effects of Ag and ZnO subject to low dosage release to against the infections induced by E. coli and S. aureus, respectively. Furthermore, when this antibacterial coating embeds with RDGC, it can effectively promote bone-implant integration via the upregulation of ALP, Runx2, OCN genes expressions . Our team has further demonstrated that no adverse biological effect has been found in the major organs, indicating that the newly developed antibacterial system is biologically safe.

17208019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208019.value: This project studies an innovative data centric approach for the design and implementation of significantly better tools for constructing multiple sequence alignments. To align a multiple of protein sequences, we need to insert spaces into the sequences to make their lengths equal, and then stack them up one on top of the others so that homologous residues originated from a common ancestral residue would be aligned at the same column. Such an alignment usually reveals important information about a protein family. For example, the homologous regions in the alignment might have been conserved over several millions years of natural selections; thus they must be important to survival and are very likely to have some structural or functional purposes. Despite decades of efforts, the alignments constructed by existing computational tools still have much room for improvement. However, in the last few years there was no fundamentally new techniques proposed for improving MSA construction. It seems that we have almost exhausted all mathematical and algorithmic techniques that can be applied for MSA construction. We observed that the algorithm-centric approach, which the MSA research community has been using so far, is not appropriate for the problem because the problem is data-centric in nature; to capture the millions years of mutation events of various species by some simple abstract model is obviously not enough. In this project, we go back to the data themselves and propose a data-centric approach; we propose to use deep learning methods to learn from the protein family data how to construct better alignments. In our preliminary study, we have tried to design and implement various deep neural networks for various classification tasks that give helpful advises for us to construct better alignments. We have many testings on this approach, and the results are very encouraging. This project will further develop this approach, finding other ideas and methods based on this approach for improvement. We will also develop an online Web system that implements all results in this project so that users can use our first data-driven MSA construction tools for their analyses. 本項目創新性的通過以數據為中心研究多序列比對，目標是設計和開發性能遠優於現有技術的軟件工具。為了對齊多個蛋白質序列，我們需要在輸入序列中插入空格以使它們的長度相等，然後將其疊加，以便使源自於共同祖先殘基的同源殘基在同一列上對齊。這種比對通常能夠揭示蛋白質家族的重要信息。例如，比對中的同源區域可能是在數百萬年的自然選擇中保存下來的，因此，它們對物種的生存具有重要意義，並且很可能具有一些特定的結構或者功能。雖然經過了數十年的努力，利用現有計算工具構建的序列比對在性能上依然有著很大的改進空間。在過去幾年中，我們幾乎已經窮盡了所有可用於MSA構建的數學和算法技術，然而，並沒有從根本上提出改進MSA構建的新技術。我們觀察到，MSA問題的本質是以數據為中心。迄今為止在MSA研究中一直使用的以算法為中心的方法並不適用於該問題。通過一些簡單的抽象模型來刻畫物種數百萬年的基因突變顯然是不夠的。在本項目中，我們回到數據本身，並提出一種以數據為中心的方法。我們將通過深度學習技術從蛋白質家族數據中學習如何構建更好的比對。在本項目的前期研究中，我們針對多種分類任務設計了多類深度神經網絡，為構建性能更好的比對提供了有益的啟發。我們對這類方法進行了大量實驗，實驗結果非常令人鼓舞。本項目將圍繞這類方法進行更深入的探討，尋找進一步改進比對性能的高質量方法。我們還擬將本項目的所有結果集成到一個在線互聯網系統，以便用戶可以使用我們開發的首個數據驅動的MSA構建工具進行研究。

17208019.label: Realisation of objectives
17208019.value: Objective 1: A critical first step in PnpProbs involves determining fundamental structural properties of its input using empirical heuristics. Based on these properties, PnpProbs aligns the input sequences using suitable methods. This immediately suggests the possibility of employing machine learning (ML) techniques instead of heuristics to determine structural properties. Our experiments incorporated the training of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), models that have achieved significant success in computer vision. It is important to note that a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) can be compared to a 2D image, as both possess hierarchical structures. For example, an MSA contains conserved columns that form conserved regions, similar to how points in an image combine to create lines, which then form shapes. Identifying the structural characteristics of an MSA instance to determine the optimal alignment of its multiple sequences is comparable to discerning whether an image depicts a dog or a cat. In addition to CNN models, our experiments also explored ML methods for Natural Language Processing. Determining the structural properties of an input instance of PnpProbs can be considered as a classification problem. The simplest approach is to categorize the input as either divergent or conserved. We attempted to treat this as a sentiment analysis problem: given the input, we determined whether its sentiment was positive (conserved) or negative (divergent). We applied various advanced tools for sentiment analysis, including BERT, BiLSTM, Flair, and Vader. Preliminary results of our experiments showed that ML methods improve the accuracy of PnpProbs alignments. Although the improvement was not significant, we believe that the ML approach is promising. Our experiments and results are summarized in a poster published in the 11th ACM Conference on Bioinformatics, Computational Biology and Health Informatics (ACM-BCB 2020). Objective 2: Our ML approach may be suitable for other MSA tools that also need to determine fundamental structural properties of the MSA input instance. We have applied this approach to several tools, including GLProbs, MSAProbs, QuickProbs, and ProbAlign, and have observed similar improvements. Objective 3: As mentioned in Objective 1, the improvement of our ML approach was not as significant as desired. We observed that the main reason for this was our method adopts a "global view," which involved training various advanced Machine Learning models on the entirety of an MSA problem instance. Although this approach is theoretically sound, there is not enough training data available to build practically useful models. Most available MSAs were constructed manually by biologists, and a single MSA instance may contain hundreds of protein sequences, each with hundreds or more residues. Consequently, constructing an acceptable MSA is a daunting and tedious task. In the beginning of this project, there were only about 6,000 MSA instances (with commonly agreed correct alignments) available in benchmark databases, insufficient for training our Deep-ML models effectively. Our innovative idea is to handle the task locally. Instead of determining the structural properties of the entire MSA input instance, we divide it into much smaller regions, training ML models to determine whether these smaller regions are conserved or divergent. This allows us to handle each region using appropriate methods. In addition, we decided to use traditional simple ML methods, such as Random Forest, instead of deep ML learning models like CNN and LSTM. These ideas led us to design and implement an alignment tool called MLProbs, which we compared with ten other existing, popular MSA alignment tools. Our results showed that MLProbs' accuracy is more than 2% better than the next best tool (different input instances have different next-best tools). This improvement is significant because, over the last decade, MSA tool research has stagnated. Our tool breaks through the barrier, providing a notable enhancement in performance. Our results have been published in the journal IEEE/ACM Transactions on Computational Biology and Bioinformatics, 2023 Objective 4: We have developed a user-friendly website that enables users to upload their MSA problem instances. Our website utilizes MLProbs to construct the MSA, which can be easily downloaded by the user.

17208019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208019.value: MSA construction is common in a lot of biological analyses and post-genomic research. Biologists sometimes need to construct MSA for hundreds of sequences, each with hundreds of residues. To help handle these daunting and tedious tasks, a lot of research effort has been devoted to automating the construction process. Since the early 80s, the problem has been tackled using the algorithmic-centric approach: algorithms are designed to solve a combinatorial optimization problem, in which every possible column of residues is associate with a column score, and the objective is to find the alignment with the largest sum of column scores. It seems that after decades of research, the research community has run out of idea and in the last decade, no fundamentally new technique has been proposed and no better MSA tool had been implemented. To strive for a breakthrough, we explored a different approach: we study how to apply machine-learning algorithms to learn models from protein family data and use them to help construct better MSAs. We believed that the algorithmic-approach was not suitable to tackle the MSA problem because the problem is data-centric in nature. An MSA is basically a statement of homologue, identifying various sets of residues in a protein family so that all residues in a set are evolved from the same ancestor residue after a long sequence of mutation events spanning thousands or even millions of years. The algorithmic approach attempts to capture these events with abstract models, from which it formulates feasible computational problems. Therefore, the models have to be simple, but then they are not general and powerful enough. The major result of this project is the design and implementation of a first, innovative MSA tool called MLProbs that uses a data-centric approach to construct MSAs. We conducted a comparison of MLProbs with ten other popular MSA tools, namely PnpProbs, QuickProbs, GLProbs, PicXAA, ProbCons, MSAProbs, MAFFT, Muscle, Clustal_Omega, and ProbAlign. Our findings revealed that the alignment accuracy of MLProbs outperformed the others, with an improvement of nearly 2% over the second-best tool. This is a significant achievement as the research on MSA tools has been stagnant over the past decade, and MLProbs is the first tool to break this barrier. In addition, we have developed a user-friendly website that allows users to upload their MSA problem instances. Our website utilizes MLProbs to construct the MSA, which can be easily downloaded by the user.

17208019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208019.value: As mentioned above, in the beginning of the project, there were only about 6,000 protein families available for training Deep-ML models. Thus, we determined to train instead traditional simple ML model, namely Random Forest. Now, after several years, we witnessed a significant increase in the number of protein families available for training. Hence, it would be interesting to study training Deep-ML models like CNN and LSTM to find out whether these powerful deep-learning models can further improve the accuracy of our MSA tool.

17208019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208019.value: A Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) of a family of protein sequences is a table constructed by putting each sequence into a distinct row of a table with spaces appropriately inserted. The MSA problem involves constructing an MSA so that among the sequences in the table, homologous residues that originated from a common ancestral residue are aligned in the same column of the table. Since the early 80s, tremendous research efforts have been put in implementing software tools to construct the MSA automatically. However, in the last decade, no fundamentally new technique has been proposed and no better MSA tool had been implemented. In this project, we explored a different approach, namely the data-centric approach, to tackle the MSA problem: we study how to apply machine-learning algorithms to learn models from protein family data and use them to help construct better MSAs. Our major result is to implement MLProbs, the first MSA construction tool that apply ML methods to construct MSAs. We conducted a comparison of MLProbs with ten other popular MSA tools. Our findings revealed that the alignment accuracy of MLProbs outperformed the others, with an improvement of nearly 2% over the second-best tool.

17208319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208319.value: The 5G network connecting billions of IoT devices will make it possible to harvest an enormous amount of real-time mobile data. Furthermore, the 5G virtualization architecture will enable cloud computing at the (network) edge. The availability of both rich data and computation power at the edge has motivated Internet companies to deploy AI there, creating the hot area of edge-AI. Edge learning, the theme of this project, concerns training edge-AI models, which endow on IoT devices intelligence for responding to real-time events. However, the transmission of high-dimensional data from many edge devices to access points (edge servers) can result in excessive communication latency, creating a bottleneck for edge learning. Traditional wireless techniques designed for only radio access are ineffective in tackling the challenge. The proposed research aims at designing a novel framework of intelligent radio resource management (RRM) to eliminate the communication bottleneck in edge learning. The design will rely on the integration of machine learning and wireless communication. While prior work focuses on using learning to assist communication, the reverse has received scant attention but is the underpinning principle for this research. Specifically, we will adopt metrics measuring data importance from active learning (e.g., classification uncertainty and data diversity) and apply them to RRM for active data acquisition. The resultant framework of “importance aware RRM” will comprise a rich set of retransmission and scheduling techniques that support two edge-learning paradigms, namely centralized and federated learning. One impact of this research is to shift the traditional RRM paradigm that is “rate-centric” towards a new one that is “learning-centric”. Wireless data acquisition for fast edge learning is an emerging and largely uncharted area. The broader impact of this research is making pioneering contributions to this area. Last, we believe that our cross-disciplinary research will interest both the wireless communication and machine learning communities. 連接數十億物聯網設備的5G網絡將可以收集大量的實時移動數據。此外，5G虛擬化架構將在（網絡）邊緣實現雲計算。邊緣豐富數據和計算能力的出現促使互聯網公司在那裡部署AI，創​​造了邊緣AI的熱門領域。邊緣學習是該項目的主題，涉及訓練邊緣AI模型，為物聯網設備提供智能以響應實時事件。然而，從許多邊緣設備到服務器的高維數據的傳輸可能導致過多的通信延遲，從而成為邊緣學習的瓶頸。僅用於無線電接入的傳統無線技術來應對該挑戰方面是不夠的。 擬議的研究旨在設計一種新的智能無線電資源管理（RRM）框架，以消除邊緣學習中的通信瓶頸。該設計將依賴於機器學習和無線通信的集成。雖然之前的工作重點是利用學習來協助溝通，但反過來卻很少受到關注，這卻是本研究的基礎原則。具體而言，我們將採用度量來衡量主動學習中的數據重要性（例如，分類不確定性和數據多樣性），並將它們應用於RRM以進行有效數據採集。由此產生的“重要性感知RRM”框架將包括一組豐富的重傳和調度技術，這些技術支持兩種邊緣學習範例，即集中式和聯合式學習。 這項研究的一個影響是將“以速率為中心”的傳統RRM範式轉變為“以學習為中心”的新範式。用於快速邊緣學習的無線數據採集是一個新興領域，在很大程度上是未知的。這項研究的更廣泛影響是為這一領域做出了開創性的貢獻。最後，我們相信我們的跨學科研究將激起無線通信和機器學習領域的興趣。

17208319.label: Realisation of objectives
17208319.value: Objective 1: Designing a new class of techniques called data-importance aware retransmission for active data/update acquisition to accelerate edge learning. The objective has been achieved by developing a data-importance aware retransmission protocol to accelerate edge learning [7]. The principle is generalized for distributed learning in wireless networks in [4] and extended to mobile edge computing in [2]. The results are reported in high-impact journals including IEEE JSAC (i.e., [4]) with an Impact Factor (IF) of 16.4 and IEEE TWC (i.e., [2, 7]) with an IF of 10.4. In [7], the seminal retransmission protocol, called data-importance aware automatic-repeat-request (ARQ), is proposed. Unlike the classic ARQ focusing merely on reliability, importance ARQ selectively retransmits a data sample based on its uncertainty which helps learning. The policy is derived based on the uncertainty measure of data samples. Experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness in coping with channel fading and noise to accelerate model convergence. The principle of importance aware retransmission as established in [7] is generalized in [4] for distributed machine learning (ML) in next-generation wireless networks. Techniques building on this principle are shown to have the capability of attaining a new height in terms of communication efficiencies. In another direction, we further develop data-importance retransmission for mobile edge computing (MEC) [2]. Objective 2: Designing a new class of techniques called importance aware scheduling for active data acquisition for the paradigm of centralised edge learning. We have achieved this objective by proposing in [8] a novel technique for importance aware scheduling for active data acquisition targeting centralised edge learning. Then the technique is extended to a popular edge learning approach called partitioned edge learning [5]. To increase the impact of our work, the concept of importance aware scheduling is generalized in [1] as a solution to achieve time sensitive machine learning in 6G networks. It is worth mentioning that [1] is published in the Processings of IEEE, is the flagship IEEE publication with an impact factor of 20.6. Specifically, in [8], we propose a novel user scheduling algorithm for data acquisition in edge learning, called (data) importance-aware scheduling. A key feature of this scheduling algorithm is that it takes into account the informativeness of data samples, besides communication reliability. As demonstrated via experiments using real datasets, the proposed importance-aware scheduling can exploit the two-fold multi-user diversity, namely the diversity in both the multiuser channels and the distributed data samples. This leads to faster model convergence. The real-time requirements in 6G become more stringent. In view of insufficient latency of state-of-the-art techniques to meet all real-time requirements, we generalise in [1] the approach of importance aware scheduling as an underpinning principle for designing next-generation communication techniques. To empower multiuser scheduling techniques with data importance awareness promises to substantially reduce communication overhead such that the challenges arising from spectrum scarcity can be overcome. To leverage distributed computation resources at devices, a 6G approach of intelligence distillation is partitioned edge learning (PARTEL) that dynamically partitions a global model under training into parametric blocks for separated updating at devices. To overcome the communication bottleneck, we extend the technique of importance-aware scheduling to PARTEL. The resultant technique is capable of supporting the joint control of parameter allocation, scheduling, sub-channel allocation, and power control to improve the communication efficiency. Objective 3: Designing a new class of techniques called importance aware scheduling for active update acquisition for the paradigm of federate edge learning. We have achieved this objective by successfully developing the proposed importance aware scheduling for active update acquisition for federate edge learning, a usage scenario of 6G [9]. Subsequently the algorithm was further developed for federated learning with dropout and PARTEL discussed earlier. The results are reported in [3] and [10], respectively. Another direction we have explored is to consider practical mobile computation architecture, namely CPU-GPU Heterogeneous Computing. In this case, we generalized importance aware scheduling into importance aware resource management targeting multi-user systems with the mentioned architecture deployed on devices [6]. Specifically, in [9], we have achieved the objective by proposing a novel scheduling policy is proposed to exploit both diversity in multiuser channels and diversity in the “importance” of the edge devices’ learning updates. First, a new probabilistic scheduling framework is developed to yield unbiased update aggregation in FEEL. The importance of a local learning update is measured by its gradient divergence. If one edge device is scheduled in each communication round, the scheduling policy is derived in closed form to achieve the optimal trade-off between channel quality and update importance. The above scheduling technique is extended in two cases — federated learning with dropout and PARTEL. In[3], importance aware scheduling for federated learning is enriched with the incorporation with dropout, a classic scheme for random model pruning. Th key design feature is to jointly consider data and model-parametric importance in scheduling and controlling model dropout ratios. On the other hand, importance aware scheduling is generalized to propose joint parameter-and-bandwidth allocation for PARTEL systems [10]. Publication List: [1] P. Popovski*, F. Chiariotti, K. 17208319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208319.value: Traditional communication techniques have been designed based Claude Shannon’s approach that largely aims to maximise communication rates. Such an approach does not discriminate importance of bits and hence lack the desired efficiencies for supporting 6G edge learning and AI applications [1]. On the other hand, in computing, data samples have varying importance due to their, e.g., uncertainty levels [4], [7], [8]. Our main finding is that taking into account of data importance can achieve very significant performance gains as opposed to conventional rate-maximisation designs. This new principle is applicable to many goal-oriented communication techniques ranging from retransmissions [7] to scheduling [8], [9], to resource allocation [6],[10], targeting usage scenarios such as federated edge learning, PARTEL [5], [10], centralised learning, model dropout [3], and mobile edge computing [2], [6]. Our project also contributes to the establishment of a new communication-computing integrated design approach (see, e.g., [7-10]). What we found is that the integration as opposed to the traditional separation approach can lead to significant gains in terms of end-to-end performance such as inference and learning accuracies. Another major finding is the fusion of channel diversity in multiuser channels and diversity in the “importance” of the edge devices’ learning updates. This integrated diversity is aligned with the above mentioned communication-computing integrated design approach. The probabilistic scheduling framework is then extended to allow scheduling multiple edge devices in each communication round.

17208319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208319.value: The development of 6G mobile networks is witnessing a paradigm shift towards integration of communication and computing as well as the ubiquitous deployment of AI in mobile networks. The further development of the research can be in several promising directions as listed below: 1) Understanding the effects of non-i.i.d. data distribution on the performance data-importance aware scheduling for both centralized and federated edge learning. The man challenge lie in selecting users with sufficient data diversity to ensure the total data importance is maximised. This also requires design of messaging passing to learn about each other’s data distribution and semantics. 2) How to design edge AI networks to support centralized or federated edge learning? There are many interesting issues beyond the scope of this project but warrant further investigation. Examples include fine tuning of large-language models, AI model downloading and AI in space-ground integrated networks. 3) The consideration of new mobile computing architecture for mobile devices in the design of centralized or federated edge learning systems. For instance, neuromorphic computing using in-memory computing circuits are seeing rapid advancements. The design of neuromorpphic integrated communication and computing (learning and inference) would be a promising direction to explore.

17208919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17208919.value: 三維打印光子/電子電路可以開啟顯示設備，可穿戴器件以及生物醫學設備應用的新紀元。其中一個要求是可打印材料的多樣性。這裡，我們提出研究納米級的“新光電子材料”的三維打印。 在過去數十年中，有機-無機雜化鈣鈦礦因其優異的光電性能，低成本以及室溫生產的特性，吸引了極大的關注。與已建立的矽技術相比，鈣鈦礦材料已經拓寬了它們在各種光電器件中的潛在用途，例如太陽能電池（能量轉換效率高達22.1%），光電探測器，發光二極管以及激光器。對於這些鈣鈦礦器件的實際實現需要對其形狀以及成分和結晶性進行高度控制。現在廣泛使用的薄膜鈣鈦礦，其通常通過旋塗以及氣相沉積製造。此外，最近的研究已經設計出從塊狀晶體，膠體到納米線的各種形式的巧妙合成/製造方法。然而，在納米尺度上實現三維飛躍仍然是一個挑戰。 在研究提案中，我們計劃開發一種按需納米級三維打印方法，用於有機 - 無機鹵化鈣鈦礦。其核心思想是在納米管上形成飛升彎液面並引導其在溶劑快速揮發下結晶。在三維中持續引導局部結晶使得納米級添加製造鈣鈦礦成為可能。如本提案所附，我們的初步實驗結果清楚地證明了彎液面引導的三維鈣鈦礦晶體生長的可行性。 該項目旨在（1）探索飛升彎液面上由蒸發誘導的鈣鈦礦結晶動力學，（2）建立納米尺度層層打印鈣鈦礦技術。在這項研究中，我們計劃建立高質量的溶液介導結晶增材製造的工程基礎。此外，我們期待該項目的成果帶來有關新三維光電子電路的有趣研究課題。

17208919.label: Realisation of objectives
17208919.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1) We investigated the crystallization dynamics of metal halide perovskites inside a femtoliter solution meniscus, establishing the engineering basis of a nanoscale 3D printing method. With the aid of numerical simulation, we developed novel strategies to control the supersaturation field in the femtoliter meniscus, which is the main driving force for perovskite crystallization. Our study revealed that this depends on how precisely solvent evaporation is controlled on the meniscus surface. 2) We for the first time developed a nanoscale 3D printing for metal halide perovskites based on the meniscus-guided crystallization. The method created previously unseen freestanding perovskite nanostructures with programmed shapes such as vertical pillars, stacked walls, meshes, junctions, serpentines, and material composition, for example, heterojunctions. This research work opens the new potential to manufacture three-dimensional nanopixels for enhancing pixel brightness or data encryption level without sacrificing lateral resolution.

17208919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17208919.value: Major research outcomes include 1) the development of a nanoscale 3D printing method for metal halide perovskites with programmed shape and material composition, 2) the development of 3D perovskite nanopixels for high-resolution and high-brightness color displays, and 3) the development of a dual 3D printing method for fabricating perovskite heterostructures. Most of the results have been published in internationally recognized journals such as Advanced Materials, Advanced Functional Materials, Nano Letters, and so on, and presented in MRS Fall Meetings. A US patent for this invention has been filed (US 17/647,709). Some of the project outcomes also benefit other research projects indirectly.

17208919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17208919.value: The completed research demonstrated the potential to realize freeform manufacturing of metal halide perovskite micro/nanostructures for advanced displays. Based on the nanoscale 3D printing method developed here, we propose to create new-concept perovskite optoelectronic components such as LEDs and lasers with direct device integration, facilitated by research grants such as the General Research Fund (GRF) and the NSFC/RGC Joint Research Scheme. The developed method will facilitate a broad range of functional crystalline materials, not limited to specific perovskite materials.

17208919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17208919.value: In this project, we explored a strategy to develop a nanoscale 3D printing method for metal halide perovskites. The research delivered some clever ideas on how to incorporate perovskite crystallization pathways into the 3D printing process. We demonstrated 3D printing of perovskite nanopixels with high brightness and high resolution. The outcome of this project suggests a number of interesting applications of 3D printing for manufacturing freeform, new-concept optoelectronic devices.

17209219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209219.value: The increasing greenhouse gas emission partly caused by fossil energy generation has pushed our environment to a very dangerous edge. We have already suffered from the growing destruction and deterioration of environment and dramatic climate changes in the past decade. These environmental changes in turn have significant impacts on modern power system operation by increasing the possibility of extreme weather events that may cause serious damage on power system infrastructures and lead to large-scale blackout. On the other hand, to save the environment, countries worldwide announced to increase renewable capacities. However, the integration of renewables will change power systems from the traditional paradigm to a completely new paradigm: distributed power generation, bi-directional power flow, and active electricity distribution. Further, the high inter-temporal variation and limited predictability of renewables will limit the controllability of generation and challenge the capability of the traditional demand-driven operation paradigm. Therefore, how to operate a reliable power system and deliver uninterruptible, clean, and cost-effective power to customers is becoming an increasingly important issue. The concept of microgrids provides new opportunities to solve all these issues. In particular, microgrids can operate in grid-connected, islanded, or networked modes, and have ability to manage local power balance and continue to provide power service to end-users in case of utility grid failures. Moreover, microgrids are also considered as a key module of future power grids, where distribution systems with distributed generators can be clustered into connected microgrids. By coordinating all these connected microgrids properly and solving problems locally within each microgrid, one may expect an economic and reliable power system in the future. Then, the fundamental problem becomes how to safely and economically operate a microgrid. This project aims to develop a new control framework for microgrids by combining hierarchical control with distributed control such that a microgrid with high renewables can be operated in a stable and cost-effective way. Particularly, we will build a three-layer hierarchical control system for each microgrid in a networked microgrid system, where the three layers aim to optimally coordinate interactions between microgrids, optimally manage different controllable devices within the microgrid, and stabilize the microgrid in case of disturbances, respectively. Within each control layer, distributed control/optimization algorithms will be developed to realize the corresponding functionality. The integration of different control layers and controllers of different microgrids will be carried out carefully to form a distributed hierarchical control system for the networked microgrid system. 全球環境變化與現代電力系統的穩定運行密切相關。一方面，由化石能源發電引起的持續性溫室氣體排放對自然環境造成嚴重危害。過去十年來，人類社會面臨著日益突出的環境破壞和污染問題，全球氣候變化不斷加劇。另一方面，環境惡化往往容易誘發極端天氣事件，某些情況下，可能嚴重破壞電力系統基礎設施並引發大規模停電事故，給現代電力系統安全運行帶來嚴重威脅。 為應對環境惡化問題，世界各國紛紛提出大力開發和利用可再生能源，提高可再生能源在現代電網中的比重。然而，大規模可再生能源的接入將使電力系統從傳統的運行模式轉變為包含分佈式發電、潮流雙向流動和主動配電網等新特性的全新運行模式。此外，可再生能源的強時變性及其難以預測的特點將大大降低發電側的可控性，導致發電跟隨負荷的傳統運行模式不再適用。因此，如何提高現代電力系統運行的安全性和可靠性，為用戶持續提供清潔、經濟和高效的電力服務是當前電力行業亟待解決的重要問題。 微電網的理念為解決上述問題帶來了新的契機和思路。微電網具有良好的平衡本地電力需求的能力，可在併網、孤島、互連等多種方式下靈活運行，並在主網發生故障後仍可為終端用戶繼續提供可靠的電力服務。此外，包含分佈式發電的配電網可以聚集成互連的多微電網系統，因此微電網也被認為是構建未來電網的關鍵模塊。若能有效地協調多個互連微電網，使各個微電網在分佈自治的基礎上相互支援，將有望進一步提高現代電網運行的經濟性和可靠性。為此，微電網的安全和經濟運行變得尤為重要。 本項目將通過融合分層控制和分佈式控制方法建立一種全新的微電網控制框架，切實保障具有高可再生能源滲入的互連微電網系統運行的穩定性和經濟性。特別地，將在互連微電網系統中建立三層控制體系，其中上層控制系統用於協調多個互連微電網的優化運行，中層控制系統用於優化各個微電網內部的運行，下層控制系統則用於提高各微電網在遭遇事故和擾動後的穩定性。在每一控制層中，將根據各層的不同功能系統地設計分佈式優化和控制算法。在此基礎上，通過有機整合、協調系統中不同控制器和不同控制層的功能，以分層、分佈方式實現互連微電網系統的整體優化運行與控制。

17209219.label: Realisation of objectives
17209219.value: This project has proposed a new hierarchical and distributed control for networked microgrid systems. The four objectives of the project have been divided into small targets, which are accomplished step by step. The following are the details of the realization of each step with small targets. 1.1 Distributed algorithm for power balance control. A crucial problem in power system balancing control, i.e., the multi-time slot economic dispatch (MTSED) problem, is studied. The target is to optimally coordinate all controllable units' active/reactive power outputs to meet a forecast net demand profile over multiple time slots within a receding finite time horizon. The MTSED task is formulated as an optimization problem with operational constraints, including the limits on the output of each controllable unit, ramping rates of generators, energy levels of storage devices, and bus voltages. 1.2 Distributed model predictive frequency control for microgrids. A distributed frequency control method is developed for an off-grid inverter-based networked microgrid system with loads, renewable generators, and energy storage devices. The frequency regulation problem is formulated as a model predictive control (MPC) problem that aims to maintain the supply-demand power balance within each microgrid and scheduled net power interchange among connected microgrids at minimal regulation costs. The charging/discharging efficiencies, energy capacities of energy storage devices, and constraints on bus voltages are considered. 1.3 Distributionally robust OPF: To solve the problem of voltage security caused by uncertainties of renewables, a conditional value at risk (CVaR)-averse distributionally robust chance-constrained optimal power flow is proposed, which considers the voltage regulation from a risk perspective. The CVaR of voltage violation is used as an additional penalty term in the objective. 2.1 Stability enhancement OPF. A BESS droop tuning scheme in an inverter-based microgrid is established to enhance the microgrid's stability under small disturbances. Instead of treating BESS as adjustable power injections, a droop control scheme is introduced into BESS to provide both power injection support under steady-state conditions and dynamical support under disturbances. 2.2 Chance-constrained OPF with power flow routers. To regulate microgrids' voltage profile, a chance-constrained optimal power flow (CC-OPF) problem with power flow routers (PFRs) is proposed. Compared with the normal CC-OPF, which relies on node power flexibility only, the proposed model introduces a new dimension of control from the power network to enhance system performance under renewable uncertainties. 2.3 Consensus-based control. A distributed consensus-based control method is proposed for voltage and frequency control of islanded microgrids. The proposed method includes active power sharing in voltage control to improve the accuracy of reactive power sharing. Thus, it generalizes some existing secondary frequency and voltage control methods and offers a tunable trade-off between voltage regulation and active and reactive power-sharing accuracy. 2.4 MPC-based control. Firstly, an optimization-based method is proposed to enable wind turbines to respond to frequency variations. Instead of relying on energy storage systems, the wind turbine’s kinetic energy storage and self-regulation capabilities are leveraged to optimize the trade-off between providing frequency regulation and maximizing wind power yield. Secondly, a switched MPC controller is designed to make generators work with loads for frequency and bus voltage regulation. 2.5 Distributed feedback optimization-based control. A novel distributed feedback optimization (FO) based control method is proposed to control grid‐forming inverters (GFMIs) in islanded AC microgrids. The proposed controller has two control layers. The upper layer uses FO to calculate the frequency and voltage setpoints of GFMIs, whereas the lower layer makes GFMIs track these setpoints. It regulates the system frequency, maintains both active power and reactive power sharing accuracies, keeps bus voltage within the allowable range, and preserves the optimality of the closed‐loop system in terms of optimal power flow. 2.6 Data-driven frequency control. Model-free frequency control methods are proposed using only data to deal with unknown system models or model uncertainties. Firstly, a modified data-enabled predictive control (DeePC) algorithm to solve the frequency control problem. Then, a multi-agent reinforcement learning-based frequency control method with DeePC-guided policy search is proposed. 3.1 Dispatchable control methods for renewable generators. One solution is to operate renewable generators as “semi-dispatchable” resources to overcome the variability and uncertainty of renewables. Effective control methods for wind turbines are established. These include a concurrent control scheme to minimize the detrimental shortfall of active power during low-voltage-fault events, a robust optimal power regulation scheme to mitigate the negative impacts caused by uncertainties of wind power, and a learning-based active power control by simultaneously coordinating rotor speed control and pitch angle control. 3.2 Time-driven adaptive control for switched systems. A novel time-driven adaptive switching controller is established such that the tracking error asymptotically converges to zero, and all the signals in the error dynamic system are bounded under an achieved disturbance attenuation level. This idea will be further extended to solve the two targets of the LCS, i.e., tracking the set points if no disturbance happens and stabilizing the MG if any disturbance happens. 3.3 Data-driven H-infinity control. The problem of designing a data-driven controller is studied. Firstly, an H∞ controller is designed using a group of input/state/output data without any model information for linear time-invariant systems. The obtained results are further applied to the ARX systems using only input/output data. Then, this method is extended to deal with piecewise affine (PWA) systems. The main advantage of the proposed controller is that it can balance the trade-off between the robustness and control performance of the closed-loop system by choosing the number of data sequences and the length of each sequence. 4.1 Dynamically event-triggered sampling mechanism. A dynamically event-triggered sampling mechanism has been proposed to investigate the bumpless transfer event-triggered H-infinity control problem for switched systems. A bumpless transfer constraint is proposed to restrict the control bumps among different switching controllers, and a dynamic event-triggered sampling mechanism is put forward to save communication resources. 4.2 Enhancing flexibility using PFRs. A chance-constrained optimization model is proposed to estimate the flexibility area at a transmission-distribution interface. In this model, network flexibility is involved and facilitated by introducing PFRs into the distribution system. The mechanism of network flexibility is exploited, revealing that it significantly reduces the voltage standard deviations, which cannot be achieved by node power flexibility. 4.3 Self-organization cooperative output regulation: Cooperative output regulation is investigated for a multi-channel system with multiple agents communicating in a network, where each channel is managed by an agent. A novel cooperative output regulation framework is proposed to ensure that each agent can self-design and self-exert its input on the multi-channel system based only on local system information and local interaction with neighbors. Communication safety and privacy issues are considered in the proposed algorithm. 4.4 Cyber-security issues. A novel method is proposed to launch a stealthy load redistribution attack (LRA) without requiring knowledge of the power network's admittance matrix. Initially, equations involving the admittance matrix in the conventional LRA model are substituted with equivalent conditions of the power transfer distribution factor (PTDF) matrix. Subsequently, a ridge regression approach is applied to estimate the PTDF matrix based on the hijacked data. Further, an LRA for systems with high penetration of electric vehicles (EVs) is proposed. The target is to induce massive EV users to charge simultaneously and cause a spike in loads at peak hours.

17209219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209219.value: The research accomplishments are highlighted in 11 officially published journal papers, with two additional papers under review, and ten conference papers. Notably, three published papers appeared in IEEE Trans. on Power Systems, with one each in IEEE Trans. on Smart Grid, IEEE Trans. Industrial Informatics, IEEE Trans. on Cybernetics, and IEEE Trans. on Energy Conversion. Additionally, two papers were published in the International Journal of Electrical Power and Energy Systems, with one in the IET Smart Grid. An invited paper was also published in the Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems. The project's key findings are related to four objectives. Firstly, the project proposes new algorithms for developing a UEMS to optimize power trading between the microgrid, utility grid, and neighboring microgrids. These algorithms include a distributed algorithm for the power balance control method [Js1], a distributed model predictive frequency control [J11], and a distributionally robust OPF-based method [J5]. Secondly, the project offers new algorithms to design a MEMS to optimally manage controllable devices in the MG so that the total power can track the control command from the UEMS. These algorithms include stability enhancement OPF-based method [C6], chance-constrained OPF method with power flow routers [J8], consensus-based control method [C7], MPC-based control method [J9, C1], distributed feedback optimization-based control method [J6, C8], and data-driven frequency control method [C2, C5]. Thirdly, the project proposes new algorithms to design an LCS that enables all controllable devices in the MG to follow the control command from the MEMS and stabilize the MG in the event of any disturbance. These algorithms include dispatchable control methods for renewable generators [J1, J2, J3], the Time-driven adaptive control method [J4], and the data-driven H-infinity control method [C4, C10]. Finally, the project presents algorithms to integrate the proposed three layers to form a distributed hierarchical control system that enables the networked MG system to autonomously and optimally operate in all three modes and seamlessly transition between different modes. These algorithms include a dynamically event-triggered sampling mechanism [Js2], enhancing flexibility using PFRs [J7], Self-organization cooperative control [C3], and cyber-security issues [Js2, C9].

17209219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209219.value: Microgrids and networked microgrid systems face significant challenges such as low inertia, high uncertainties, switching, and unknown device dynamics. To address these issues, future work will focus on integrating optimization theory, hybrid system theory, and data-driven control. Additionally, it is imperative to implement the proposed methods in real systems. Therefore, potential collaborations with industry partners will be pursued to achieve this goal.

17209219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209219.value: A microgrid is a power network comprising of distributed generators, energy storage, and flexible loads operating at low/medium voltages. It offers a local control platform to solve problems locally and can operate in either an autonomous or connected mode. Microgrids can also be connected to form a networked microgrid system to enhance operational flexibility. By properly controlling numerous connected microgrids, maintaining local power balance, and facilitating mutual assistance among microgrids, a new control framework can be established for future power systems. This approach allows for addressing issues locally, minimizing the need for the utility grid to deliver power and control signals from the top. Therefore, the stable operation of microgrid and networked microgrid systems is essential. This project aims to develop a hierarchical and distributed control framework for networked microgrid systems. Novel energy management systems, detailed control systems for individual devices, and coordination algorithms are designed to ensure the economical and stable operation of networked microgrid systems, integrating power system theory, control system theory, and optimization theory. Ultimately, the proposed framework enables the creation of more sustainable and resilient power systems, reducing the dependence on traditional energy sources while providing reliable and affordable electricity to local customers.
