17209419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209419.value: This project is motivated by one of the most challenging problems in modern engineering, which is how to plan and operate an electrical power grid into future decades that can deliver non-disruptive and socially acceptable costs and energy security yet deliver the improvements to emissions that are needed to seriously arrest climate change. The point of view taken is that addressing this challenge at all levels is a clear science and engineering task where targets can be reached in an optimised way. The relevant basic questions have scientific answers that can raise the level of debate and planning to that of an ordered determination of future energy supply. The emphasis in this proposal is on improving grid flexibility and security for low emission systems. (A follow-up project is planned to investigate achieving low electricity prices for low emission systems where carbon pricing and market mechanisms interact). 面對當前氣候變暖的嚴峻形勢，如何在未來數十年內高效地規劃和運營現代電網，在社會可接受的成本下和滿足能源安全性要求的基礎上實現電能的無間斷傳輸，進而提升節能減排的效率，是目前工程中最實際、最具挑戰性的問題之一。為此，本項目著重研究未來電網的規劃問題，在多個層面以系統而科學的優化方法來解決這工程一大挑戰。通過科學性分析和探討本項目各個相關的基本問題，將有望提升未來電網的規劃運行水平，進而制訂高效而有序的能源供給方案。在節能減排的背景下，本項目聚焦於如何提升低碳電力系統運行的靈活性和安全性（後續項目將進一步研究在碳定價和市場機制的相互作用下如何實現低碳電力系統的低電價營運）。

17209419.label: Realisation of objectives
17209419.value: Throughout the project period, we successfully completed all tasks and expanded some of our research tasks beyond the initial proposal. Our achievements have been documented in 20 top-tier journal papers with acknowledgement of the support from this RGC GRF project, including eight papers in IEEE Trans. on Smart Grid, two in IEEE Trans. on Power Systems, four in Applied Energy, and one in each of the following journals: IEEE Trans. on Circuits and Systems II: Express Briefs, Journal of Modern Power Systems and Clean Energy, IEEE Internet of Things Journal, Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, Journal of Economy and Technology, and IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics. The PI was invited as the Chair to share the research accomplishments of this project at some prestigious conferences, including (i) Panel Chair “Renewable Energy Planning and Operation with Decision Dependent Uncertainty”, 2021 INFORMS Annual Meeting. (ii) Panel Chair of “Converter-Interfaced Devices for Power System Restoration with High Penetration Renewables” in 2022 IEEE PES General Meeting. (iii) Panel Chair “Strategic Behavior in Renewable-dominated Energy Systems”, 2022 INFORMS Annual Meeting. (iv) Panel Chair “Enhancing Climate Resilience of Renewable-Dominated Power Grids”, 2023 INFORMS Annual Meeting. (v) Panel Chair “Carbon-centric Power System Operation and Transaction”, 20223 INFORMS Annual Meeting. For the implementation of the proposed methods, the NSFC Major Programme has commissioned the PI to implement the proposed methods in a project entitled "Supply-demand Balance Methodologies Enabling Renewable Energy Dominated Power Systems (U1966601)." The findings from this project have been applied to wind farm planning in the Gansu power grid. The PI manages RMB 3.8 million of the total RMB 15 million in funding support. Additionally, the PI is leading a Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Macau Science and Technology Program called "Key Technology for Constructing Cloud-Edge Merged Green Smart Building Cluster and Its Practice," which has received RMB 3 million. The findings from this project will be applied to the Shenzhen power grid to support the integration of smart loads. During this project, PI led prestigious organizations in academia and industry, including chairing the IEEE PES Task Force on "Power System Restoration with Renewable Energy Sources," co-chairing the IEEE PES Working Group on "Power System Restoration," serving as an expert in the IEC SC8A Working Group on renewable energy generation and chairing the Operation Group of the Technical Committee on Renewable Energy Integration and Operation in the Chinese Society for Electrical Engineering. The research findings are summarized as follows: -Developing a new model for future grids to evaluate emissions and security indicators and allow for trade-offs in overall costs (1) Climate-adaptive transmission network expansion planning (TNEP): we developed a climate-adaptive model to address uncertainties in power systems caused by weather-sensitive resources and unpredictable climate change. The model uses a climate-adaptive uncertainty set (CUS) to account for the evolving probability distribution of weather-sensitive resources. The CUS determination process involves modelling future unknown distribution under climate change and solving a distributionally robust optimization problem. The overall climate-adaptive model is solved using a column-and-constraint-generation method with a tailored multi-loop algorithm for CUS. [Part C: J20]. (2) Multi-timescale multi-objective economic-environmental planning and operation: this work solves the "fast computation or good balance" dilemma through an intra-day offline-online coordination framework. The method calculates intra-day Pareto fronts (PF) offline and requires a simple single-objective optimization online. Error bounds are quantified, and operational conditions ensure offline PF closely approximates the accurate online PF despite forecast errors. A new multi-objective algorithm, basis changing boundary intersection (BCBI), is proposed to improve PF computational efficiency at offline stages, achieving fast and balanced economic-environmental trade-offs[Part C: J19]. -Developing future grid planning strategies (1) Construct a resilient and flexible future grid. A reliable power supply is critical for the future energy infrastructure. (i) To develop a resilient grid before the extreme events, we proposed a method to harden the network. The dynamic thermal rating (DTR) is used to mitigate risk of cascading failures. This study proposes a novel two-stage submodular optimization (TSSO) of DTR for risk mitigation, considering placement and operation schedules. The submodularity of the total objective function was proven, and an efficient solving algorithm was developed, offering better approximation guarantees than previous methods[Part C, J12]. We proposed a stochastic geometry-based method to evaluate the effect of mobile emergency generator deployment. The method uses distance measures, point processes, and Voronoi tessellation to assess network survivability and resilience [Part C, J17]. Network connectedness is crucial for resilience. We proposed linear connectedness constraints using the vertex potential equation of an electrical flow network. A reduced version improves computational efficiency. Numerical studies revealed the deficiency of OTS models without network connectedness and demonstrate the proposed constraints’ effectiveness[Part C, J3]. In addition, a bi-directional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) deep transfer learning approach was proposed to identify resilient structures with better short-term voltage stability (STVS) performance efficiently. An improved voltage recovery index quantifies STVS, while a BiLSTM-based evaluation machine predicts STVS without time-consuming simulations and adapts to new systems[Part C, J7]. (ii) After extreme events, we proposed a distributionally robust model for three-phase unbalanced distribution network reconfiguration to obtain the optimal configuration under the worst-case[Part C, J2]. Considering uncertainties during restoration, we modelled decision-dependent uncertainty and distributional ambiguity by developing scenario-wise decision-dependent ambiguity sets and formulating a two-stage tri-level decision-dependent distributionally robust resilient enhancement model[Part C, J10]. (2) Construct a cyber-physical resilient future grid. In the future grid, cyber system security will continue to grow in importance, particularly as the integration of power electronics-interfaced renewables and loads increases[Part C, J16]. For large-scale systems, we proposed a two-timescale model to evaluate the impacts of cyber-attacks and an event-triggered cyber-defense strategy. The proposed method can effectively mitigate multiple non-simultaneous cyber-attacks[Part C, J18]. The small-signal angle stability (SSAS) of a power system can be compromised by false data injection (FDI) cyber-attacks that mislead optimal power flow and operation points. We proposed a stealthy SSAS-oriented FDI cyber-attack model and investigates its damaging effects on stability and operation costs while prioritizing SSAS margin[Part C, J15]. We proposed a cost-effective cyber-defense strategy for hybrid AC/DC grids, addressing vulnerabilities in voltage-sourced-converters (VSC) to false data injection cyber-attacks. A spatial-temporal dual cyber-attack evaluation model was established, and a VSC commitment problem was solved to balance defense benefits and costs, enhancing grid cybersecurity[Part C, J13]. -Developing methods for assessing integration limits for the future grids For the future multi-energy system, we developed an equivalent model of district heating networks. A non-iterative solution for efficient coordination and assessment between energy sectors in integrated electricity and heat systems was established [Part C, J6]. We studied methods to encourage district heating network (DHN) operators to utilize pipeline energy storage fully. A bi-level model is proposed and shows that the incentive-based coordination mechanism effectively improves social welfare by lowering total costs in both EPNs and DHNs while efficiently reaching Stackelberg equilibrium[Part C, J4]. For cyber-physical systems, we proposed a method to maximize the cybersecurity margin. The strategic selection and protection of a large measurement subset that requires adequate cyber-defense resources are proposed to minimize FDI cyber-attacks [Part C, J9].

17209419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209419.value: This project aims to tackle the intricate challenge of designing and managing a future electrical power grid that guarantees cost-efficiency, energy security, and substantial emission reductions to combat climate change. The primary focus of this project is on improving grid flexibility and resilience. To achieve a balance among cost, emissions, flexibility, and cyber-physical resilience, the project proposes a systematic approach. Firstly, climate change and its related uncertainties significantly impact power system planning. To investigate this issue, we examined how climate change introduces ambiguity into renewable energy sources, which are expected to be the primary sources for future power systems. To tackle this crucial planning problem, we proposed a climate-adaptive transmission network expansion plan that includes a climate-adaptive uncertainty set to quantify the ambiguity caused by climate change. We validated our proposed methods using realistic data from Australia and scenarios provided by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). Additionally, we discovered that failing to consider this climate-induced ambiguity could lead to misconceptions about future operational scenarios[J20]. Additionally, conflicts arising from multiple timescales and competing economic-environmental objectives during planning and operation are addressed through efficient and balanced trade-off strategies. By combining offline estimation with online refinement, the accurate Pareto front for multi-objective economic-environmental goals can be determined with reasonable computational demands[J19]. Secondly, multi-energy resources and cyber systems will be key components of future grids. In multi-energy systems, an equivalent model-based non-iterative method quantifies the feasible region of integrated electricity and heat systems [J6]. The incentive-based coordination mechanism encourages pipeline energy storage utilization, effectively achieving Stackelberg equilibrium in a distributed environment and enhancing energy efficiency [J4]. In cyber systems, potential risks of systems with numerous power electronics-interfaced devices are identified [J16]. For large-scale systems, methods to counter cyberattacks on coordination among multi-feed HVDC systems [J18] and false data injection that deteriorates small-signal stability [J15] are proposed. Additionally, the cost and benefit of hybrid AC/DC cybersecurity are quantified [J13]. Thirdly, we developed methods for designing resilient future systems. Grids' inherent resilience can be assessed using a stochastic geometry-based method [J17], while a bi-directional LSTM deep transfer learning approach can identify structures with improved short-term voltage stability [J7]. A two-stage submodular method addresses the combinatorial optimization in resilience enhancement [J12]. We also recognized decision-dependent uncertainties during system restoration and proposed scenario-wise decision-dependent ambiguity sets for quantification. A two-stage tri-level decision-dependent distributionally robust approach can solve this issue [J10].

17209419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209419.value: This project has systematically developed planning strategies for the future power grid, aiming to achieve a balance between cost, emissions, flexibility, and cyber-physical resilience. The accomplishments of this project, which focuses on key technologies for emerging energy systems, offer numerous applications with significant potential for future advancements. These applications include, but are not limited to: (1) Planning methods with various uncertainties. Future grid designs should address increased uncertainties compared to traditional power systems. These include aleatoric uncertainties from natural fluctuations, epistemic uncertainties from knowledge gaps[J20], and decision-dependent uncertainties in new paradigms[J10]. The identified technologies can be broadly applied to address planning and operational challenges in these future grids. (2) Power electronics-interfaced devices as key components. The method proposed in this project can be extended to address novel physical features and cyber issues[J13, J18]. In the future grid, cyber systems will be as important as physical systems. New ideas for cybersecurity may build upon the current work[J9, J16]. (3) Constructing resilient future grids requires novel ideals. It needs different ideals from traditional reliability-oriented planning. Building resilient grids may integrate technologies proposed in this project [J2, J3, J10].

17209419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209419.value: To address global warming and achieve sustainable development, it is crucial to establish an affordable, environmentally friendly, flexible, and resilient energy system. This project involves a systematic study of planning methods for the future power grid, which will meet these requirements by incorporating a high percentage of renewable energy sources and power-electronics-interfaced devices. Moreover, climate change leads to heightened demands for a resilient power grid that incorporates climate-related renewable energy sources. This project systematically confronts these crucial challenges. Firstly, we developed methods to plan power systems accounting for uncertainties from unpredictable climate changes, incorporating power, heating, renewable energy, and cyber systems for future grids. Secondly, we studied secure operation methods for power-electronics-interfaced devices, proposing secure coordination methods among them to build flexible, cyber-physically resilient future grids. Thirdly, we identified new device integration limits based on our planning and resilient operating strategies, offering key technologies to design a trajectory towards net-zero emissions. We believe that the success of this project will bring significant benefits to Hong Kong, a coastal international financial centre that heavily relies on a consistent and sustainable energy supply for its prosperity.

17209519.value: 面向对象编程（OOP）被数百万程序员用于开发遍布社会的应用程序。面向对象的语言（例如Java，C＃，C ++或Scala）构建在诸如子类型或继承之类的概念上。子类型和继承对于实现OOP特性的重用和模块化形式至关重要，并提高了这些语言中程序员的工作效率。 许多OOP语言都是静态类型的。也就是说，他们有一个类型系统可以分析程序并检测某些类型的（类型）错误。例如，类型系统将检测到向布尔值添加数字，并在程序运行之前向用户报告。类型系统提供轻量级验证的形式。虽然类型系统无法检测到各种错误，但它可以检测某类错误并防止程序中可能出现的错误。早期检测错误是好的，因为修复错误的成本大大降低。此外，高级类型系统还有助于模块化和重用，从而减少了编写代码并提高了软件的生产率和可靠性。类型系统的一个吸引人之处在于，与其他几种更强大的验证技术不同，类型系统被程序员广泛使用和接受，他们经常在程序上编写类型注释。 近年来，依赖类型已经成为编程语言研究和功能编程的热门话题。依赖类型增加了类型系统的表现力，使类型系统能够捕获更大类的错误。例如，对于依赖类型系统，可以静态地检测越界错误。诸如传统主流编程语言所使用的类型系统之类的简单类型系统无法检测到这种类型的错误。此外，依赖类型可以编写更强大的程序属性。例如，在对银行账户进行建模时，可以表明余额应始终为正。通常，许多形式的前/后条件或不变量可以用依赖类型表达。依赖类型有用的另一个原因是它们自然允许统一类型和术语。各种不同语法级别（例如术语和类型）的统一消除了各种语法级别的语言结构的冗余。与更传统的编程语言相比，这导致了概念的经济性，这些语言具有不同的分层语法水平。反过来，在研究这些语言的元理论时，概念的经济性导致一个更紧凑的元理论，更少的关系和规则，并且还可以导致减少编译器的必要实现工作。 不幸的是，将依赖类型合并到OOP语言中很难。一般的挑战是依赖类型以非平凡的方式与其他编程语言特征进行交互。特别是对于OOP，有两个直接的挑战。第一个挑战，一般适用于编程语言（不仅仅是OOP），是一般递归和依赖类型之间的相互作用。基本上递归会破坏强规范化，这是依赖类型语言中的许多常见属性所依赖的。第二个挑战是如何顺利地组合依赖类型和子类型是一个广为人知的难题。子类型与传统的依赖类型语言有很大不同，后者通常没有这种特征。 本提案的工作起点是PI在APLAS 2016上关于iso-types的统一语法的论文，以及关于统一打字和子类型的OOPSLA 2017。这两篇论文提供了有前途的解决方案，以克服在OOP语言中集成依赖类型的两个直接挑战。简而言之，iso-types提供了一种简单的解决方案来解决依赖类型和递归之间的交互，而统一子类型解决了集成依赖类型和子类型的关键难点。 虽然此类先前的工作确实提供了良好的初始基础，但依赖类型与其他编程语言特征之间的交互的一般问题仍然存在。由于现代OOP语言除了子类型和递归之外还包含其他几个特性，因此需要解决许多研究挑战，以便将依赖类型集成到现实的OOP语言中。该提议将表明，通过统一的子类型和iso类型，我们可以开发可以在现代OOP语言中建模高级特征的计算和类型系统（包括高阶多态，交集类型和路径依赖类型）。特别是在该提议中有三个主要目标：1）扩展OOPSLA工作，支持递归类型，子类型方差和按值调用语义; 2）研究对多重继承和交集类型的支持。

17209519.label: Realisation of objectives
17209519.value: Regarding objective 1, our first major result was a POPL 2020 paper which discussed kind inference for a language with recursive types, dependent types and a form of subtyping. This paper won a distinguished paper award, which is quite an achievement since POPL is considered to be the top conference in the field (along with PLDI). Furthermore, a problem that we encountered early on was that the theory for subtyping of recursive types themselves was not well-developed enough. In particular, we identified an important gap in the theory of iso-recursive subtyping, where previous work did not account for important properties, such as transitivity of subtyping. Thus, we developed a new theory for subtyping recursive types, leading to an OOPSLA 2020 publication. We have further developed this theory in an extended TOPLAS 2022 publication. Our new approach to iso-recursive subtyping has all the desirable properties, including transitivity of subtyping, and overcomes a major problem that was open for the last 30 years. We have also published a calculus with the Science of Computer Programming (SCP 2021) journal that includes recursive types, dependent types and subtyping. Furthermore, we have developed a new approach to subtyping relations in an ECOOP 2020 paper, which will be helpful in developing complex subtyping relations with dependent types. Overall, for Objective 1, we believe that we have obtained major results, surpassing our initial expectations and objectives, as well as obtaining several top-conference and journal publications, which should have a lasting impact. Regarding objective 2, we have continued to develop the theory related to disjoint intersection types to further integrating it with dependent types. We had a quite a number of publications, including ECOOP 2020 (2 papers); OOPSLA 2020; ECOOP 2021; JFP 2021 and ECOOP 2022 (2 papers) on this topic. A problem that we have encountered was that the previous approach in past work (an elaboration semantics approach to calculi with disjoint intersection types) was hard to scale up with features like dependent types. Thus we spent some effort in studying a new approach that is based on a direct semantics, called Type-Directed Operational Semantics (TDOS). We laid down the foundations for this approach in one of the ECOOP 2020 papers, and extended this work into a journal publication at the Journal of Functional Programming (2021). We managed to reformulate previous calculi with disjoint intersection types with the new TDOS approach. Our ECOOP 2022 paper on Direct Foundations for Compositional Programming has a complete reformulation of a calculus with disjoint intersection types, disjoint polymorphism and distributive subtyping all in terms of a TDOS. Moreover we have extended the TDOS approach to other domains. Our ECOOP 2021 paper shows how the TDOS approach can be used for gradually typed languages, and enables a direct semantics for gradual languages. This is in contrast with previous work where the semantics of gradually typed languages is typically given indirectly via a type-directed elaboration. Overall we also feel that we were very productive for objective 2, managing to tackle our objective and at the same time being able to publish several publications in both conferences and journals. For objective 3, we completed 2 publications. The first publication, at APLAS 2022, showed how to integrate iso-recursive types into a calculus with disjoint intersection types. This is an important step towards supporting powerful forms of modularity, since recursive types are needed to model so-called binary methods, which are operations where arguments are of the class being defined. This integration is important as a step towards path-dependent types, which enable a powerful form of recursive types via the self-reference and the use of a simple form of dependent types. Our second publication, at ECOOP 2023, entitled "Dependent Merges and First-Class Environments" provides an important step towards dependent sums. It allows merges from our previous work to be dependent, so that a component of a merge can dependent on a previous component. One interesting application of this idea is that it enables a programming language to support first-class environments, where the environment that contains information of local variables can be captured, created and passed around as arguments. While not as productive as in the previous 2 objectives, we believe that we accomplished the essential goals for objective 3.

17209519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209519.value: To summarize the main findings of the project were: 1) The development of a kind inference algorithm that works in the presence of recursive and dependent types. This work has been implemented in both the GHC Haskell compiler and Purescript. 2) The development of a new theory for iso-recursive subtyping, which overcomes a 30 year long challenge. 3) The development of a new calculus with dependent types and subtyping. 4) The development of a new approach for languages with a type-directed semantics called TDOS. This step is fundamental to overcome difficulties in extending previous work with recursive types and dependent types. 5) The developement of a new calculus with dependent merges and first class environments. In terms of research publications and outcomes we have several things to report: 1) Our work, published at POPL, won a distinguished paper award; 2) Several journal publications (including at TOPLAS, SCP and the JFP); 3) Additionally, we have a few journal publications at the Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages, which is where top ACM SIGPLAN conference publications are published. These publications were presented at POPL and OOPSLA. 4) Several conference publications (at the ECOOP and APLAS conferences).

17209519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209519.value: The major direction for extending this research is putting this work into practice and implementing a programming language that accounts for all the features that we have developed. There are major challenges here, especially in terms of how to compile programs into efficient executables. The main challenge is that the semantics that we have been investigating is type-directed and subtyping is coercive. Thus, we require several optimizations to eliminate the overhead introduced by coercions. The possible course of action is to identify coercions that do not have a runtime impact and therefore do not need to be produce runtime overhead.

17209519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209519.value: Dependent types are presently a state-of-the-art feature in academic programming language research. Academic languages, such as Agda or Idris have shown numerous applications where dependent types can significantly increase the static guarantees and prevent dangerous bugs (for example out-of-bound errors). However most languages with dependent types have, so far been developed in a functional programming context. The current software engineering practice is still based on Object-Oriented Programming. Therefore to enjoy the benefits of dependent types in practical programming languages, the question of how to integrate dependent types and OOP features becomes crucial. This project has been conducted to investigate the foundational theory that enables the development of such languages. We have investigated several aspects that are relevant for future programming language implementations, including type inference, and the integration of dependent types, recursive types and subtyping. Those foundations are important for future developments of programming languages with dependent types and OOP features that will enable mainstream programmers to enjoy the benefits of dependent types.

17209819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17209819.value: Vegetation plays a key role in the budget of atmospheric constituents. Urban greenery is commonly employed to rectify various environmental problems in cities such as urban heat island. Plants emit biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) whose transport to the atmospheric boundary layer (ABL) aloft is governed by the dynamics over and inside vegetation canopies. Recent studies revealed that there exists a characteristic roughness sublayer (RSL) right over vegetation canopies in which the motions are influenced by individual plants (roughness elements), resulting in a turbulent length scale different from that of atmospheric surface layer (ASL). Under this circumstance, the conventional Monin-Obukhov similarity theory (MOST) has to be interpreted cautiously. The commonly adopted eddy-diffusivity models, which measure the flows and transport processes, are no longer fully applicable. The interactions are further complicated by chemically reactive species. To bridge the aforementioned knowledge gap, this project is conceived to elucidate the dynamics and transport processes in the RSL over vegetation canopies together with the subsequent modification on the chemical composition of reactive pollutants in urban areas. As a pilot attempt, hypothetical urban greenery and generalized gaseous chemistry mechanism will be employed to address the core scientific question: “How the configuration of vegetation canopies affects the dynamics and chemical kinetics in the RSL aloft together with their implication to ASL/ABL budgets”. Our experience earned in urban canopies will be extended to vegetation canopies to derive the analytical formulation of RSL flows, paving the theoretical skeleton. A complementary solution approach consisting of wind-tunnel measurements and mathematical modeling will be sought for an in-depth, fundamental understanding of the physics and chemistry coupling. In particular, we are most interested in characterizing the flows and primary/secondary pollutant composition in RSLs. Sensitivity to various configurations of vegetation canopy and anthropogenic/biogenic emission will be tested using large-eddy simulation (LES), formulating a solid knowledge base. This project will arouse the scientific community by the unprecedented findings of RSL physics/chemistry. It will also elucidate the RSL transport processes in response to the aerodynamic properties of vegetation canopies. The findings will help refine the current land-surface models, providing more reliable information (surface fluxes of various atmospheric constituents) to professionals. The data archive will advance our understanding so as to improve the current urban planning practice and environmental management strategies. The research output will address our major concern that utilizes urban greenery to cool down our cities without any environmental drawback. 植被在大氣成分預算中起著關鍵作用。城市綠化通常用於糾正城市的各種環境問題熱島。植物會釋放出生物成因的揮發性有機化合物（VOCs），其運輸到高空的大氣邊界層（ABL）受到植被冠層內外動力學的控制。近年的研究表明存在特徵粗糙子層（RSL）在植被上，其中運動受到影響單個植物（粗糙元素），導致湍流長度尺度不同於來自大氣表層（ASL）。在這種情況下，常規的Monin-Obukhov相似理論（MOST）必須謹慎解釋。其中通常採用的渦流擴散模型，測量流量和運輸流程不再完全適用。這種相互作用引致更加複雜化學反應物種。 為彌合上述知識差距，本項目旨在闡明粗糙子層中的動態和運輸過程及隨後其與植被冠層一起修改城市反應性污染物的化學成分區域。作為試點嘗試，假設城市綠化和廣義氣體化學機制將用於解決核心科學問題：“如何植被冠層的配置影響了植被的動力學和化學動力學粗糙子層及其對大氣表層/大氣邊界層預算的影響“。我們在城市冠層的研究經驗將擴展到植被冠層，以得出分析粗糙子層流程的製定，鋪平理論框架。補充解決方案由風洞測量和數學建模組成的方法將是尋求對物理和化學耦合的深入和基本的理解。特別是，我們最感興趣的是描述流量和流量粗糙子層中的一級/二級污染物組成。大渦模擬（LES）將會用末測試植被冠層和人為/生物排放對各種配置的敏感性將使用，制定紮實的知識庫。 該項目將通過對粗糙子層前所未有的發現喚起科學界對物理/化學的關注。它還將闡明粗糙子層傳輸過程以響應植被冠層的空氣動力學特性。調查結果將有助於改進當前地表模型的情況，提供更可靠的信息（各種大氣成分的表面通量）給專業人士。數據存檔將推進我們的理解，以改善目前的城市規劃實踐和環境管理策略。研究成果將解決我們的主要問題：沒有任何環境缺陷地利用城市綠化讓我們的城市降溫。

17209819.label: Realisation of objectives
17209819.value: 1. Develop the analytical formulation of RSL dynamics over vegetation canopies The dynamics in the roughness (RSLs) and inertial (ISLs) sublayers of turbulent boundary layers (TBLs) over idealized urban surfaces are investigated both analytically and experimentally. An analytical solution is derived to the mean velocity profile that is applicable to both sublayers over vegetation canopies in isothermal conditions and develop a modified mixing-length model for sublayer transport that explains how surface roughness affects the turbulence motions. Wind tunnel experiments are conducted to measure the vertical profiles of mean and fluctuating velocities, as well as momentum flux, over various configurations of surface-mounted roughness elements using hot-wire anemometry (HWA). The analytical solution agrees well with the wind tunnel results, improving the estimate of the mean velocity profile over urban surfaces and TBL dynamics. The height of the RSL/ISL interface is found to be a function of surface roughness. Moreover, examining the direct physical influence of roughness elements on near-surface RSL flows reveals that TBL flows over rough surfaces exhibit turbulence motions of two different length scales which are functions of the RSL and ISL structure. Furthermore, the rougher the surface, the higher the RSL intruding upward, which would thin the ISL up to 50%. Therefore, the conventional ISL log-law approximation to TBL flows over urban surfaces should be applied with caution. Besides, reduced-scale physical modeling in a wind tunnel is employed to examine the dynamics in hypothetical urban areas in the form of identical surface-mounted ribs in crossflows (two-dimensional idealized scenarios) to improve our understanding of street-level ventilation mechanism. The study compares the flow behaviors over rough surfaces with different aerodynamic resistance. It is found that the friction velocity is appropriate for scaling the dynamics in the near-wall region but not the outer layer. The drag coefficient is able to characterize the turbulent transport processes over hypothetical urban areas. Moreover, linear regression shows that street-level ventilation, which is dominated by the turbulent component of the air change rate, is proportional to the square root of the drag coefficient. This conceptual framework is then extended to formulate a new indicator, the vertical fluctuating velocity scale in RSLs, for breathability assessment over urban areas with diversified building height. Quadrant analyses and frequency spectra demonstrate that the turbulence is more inhomogeneous and the scales of vertical turbulence intensity is larger over rougher surfaces, resulting in more efficient ground-level ventilation. 2. Adopt both laboratory experiments and mathematical modeling to study RSL transport in response to the configuration of vegetation canopies Atmospheric flows in the inertial sublayer (ISL) and roughness sublayer (RSL) are influenced by vegetation canopies, modifying momentum and tracer fluxes between plants and the atmospheric surface layer (ASL). Wind tunnel experiments are used to model the flows over vegetation canopies and the mean winds and turbulence are measured by hot-wire anemometry (HWA). The analytical solution for the mean-wind-speed profile is developed and verified in which the RSL constant values are larger than those over urban canopies. RSL momentum transport is governed by high-speed downdrafts and low-speed updrafts, contrasting the dissimilarity between ISL and RSL. RSL velocities are positively skewed with high kurtosis, and high-speed downdrafts contribute most to RSL vertical momentum flux. Fresh air entry is driven by spurlike downdrafts, while ground-level aged air is removed by massive uprising currents. 3. Elucidate the RSL pollution physics/chemistry coupling over vegetation canopies and refine the current practice of land-surface parameterizations The momentum transport and pollutant dispersion in the atmospheric surface layer (ASL) over vegetation canopies are governed by a broad spectrum of turbulence structures. Whereas, their contributions have not been explicitly investigated in the context of motion scales. We elucidate the contributions from different types (frequency and strength) of eddies in the ASL over vegetation canopies to provide the reference of planning, realizing more favorable ventilation and pollutant dispersion. The tree-resolved large-eddy simulation (LES) dataset of winds and pollutants is decomposed into a few intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) via empirical mode decomposition (EMD). EMD is a data-driven algorithm that has been successfully implemented in many research fields. The results show that four IMFs are generally enough to capture most of the turbulence structures in the ASL over vegetation canopies. In particular, the first two IMFs, which are high-frequency signals initiated by individual trees, capture the small-scale vortex packets that populate within the vegetation. On the other hand, the third and fourth IMFs capture the large-scale motions (LSMs) detached to the ground surface that are highly efficient in transport. They collectively contribute to nearly 40% of vertical momentum transport even with relatively low vertical turbulence kinetic energy (TKE). Large-scale motions (LSMs) are long, streaky structures that mainly consist of streamwise TKE components. It is found that the open areas and space promote the portion of streamwise TKE in LSMs, improving the vertical momentum transport and pollutant dispersion. In addition, these streaky LSMs are found to play a crucial role in pollutant dilution in the near field after the pollutant source, while the small-scale vortex packets are more efficient in transport in the mid-field and far-field.

17209819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17209819.value: This study investigated the wake generated by a fractal tree with two generations and three branches using large-eddy simulation (LES) to improve our understanding of the flow behavior and momentum transport characteristics in the wake. The study found that the near-wake flow is classified into the updraft at the crown area and the downdraft at the trunk area, affecting the near-ground transport and implying that wind erosion models should consider the diameter of the trunk. The study also showed that a shorter recovery distance suggests a shorter planting spacing or selecting taller tree species to prevent wind erosion. The coherence of vertical momentum varying with distance is revealed by the quadrant analysis, which can help refine the design of urban green infrastructure (UGI) planting density. The study also suggests that the spatial sampling spacing should be smaller than x = 0.75h (streamwise); y = 0.2h (spanwise); and z = 0.05 (vertical; where h is the tree height) to preserve the susceptible polluted region in urban environmental assessment. Furthermore, the study illustrated the detailed three-dimensional (3D) spatial distribution of flow behavior and momentum transport characteristics in the wake. The results suggested the importance of considering the structure difference between the crown and the trunk, mitigating the turbulence intensity, and emphasizing the importance of the crown structure. The study also showed that the scalar accumulates at the vortex cores and the streamline separation regions and is uniform in the recirculation region due to the mixing with the reversed flow. Finally, the study visualized the mean and turbulent scalar flux, indicating that the region beside the trunk primarily dilutes scalar concentration while the vertical component mostly contributes to enhancing the scalar concentration. The study suggests that if there are other pollutant sources near the side of the trunk, the vertical velocity can still accumulate the pollutant in this region. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into the flow behavior and momentum transport characteristics in the wake of a fractal tree, which can be useful in designing urban green infrastructure and mitigating wind erosion.

17209819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17209819.value: The study highlights the importance of involving multi-scale geometries of trees in urban environmental studies and the use of high-resolution flow fields to improve the accuracy of urban environmental prediction and assessment. This study also suggests that the configuration of the crown and trunk of trees deserves attention, as it can lead to intense fluctuation and scalar accumulation. This study proposes a spatial sampling resolution for urban environmental prediction and assessment to preserve susceptible polluted regions induced by vegetation geometries to improve accuracy. However, it notes that the geometries and types of scalars are not fully enumerated, and the contribution of different geometries to the wake and scalar transport needs further examination to improve land-surface parameterization for sustainable urban environment. Therefore, there is potential for further research to explore the contributions of different geometries and scalar types to the wake and transport in urban environments, and to improve land-surface parameterization for refined sustainable development. This could lead to improved accuracy in urban environmental prediction and assessment, as well as provide guidance for proper arrangement of urban green infrastructure to prevent wind erosion and elevated transport efficiency of pollutants.

17209819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17209819.value: This projects explains how vegetation plays a significant role in the atmosphere and how urban greenery is used to address environmental problems in cities, such as urban heat islands. Plants emit biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs), which can impact the atmosphere. Recent research has found that there is a roughness sublayer (RSL) above vegetation canopies, which affects the transport of these compounds to the atmosphere. This means that traditional scientific theories and models do not fully apply in these circumstances. To bridge this knowledge gap, this project studies the dynamics and transport processes in the roughness sublayer over vegetation canopies and how it affects chemical composition and ultimately, the atmosphere. The project uses hypothetical urban greenery and generalized chemistry mechanisms to understand how the configuration of vegetation canopies affects these processes. It uses wind-tunnel measurements and mathematical modeling to gain an in-depth understanding of the physics and chemistry involved. The outcome of this project helps refine current land-surface models, provide reliable information on surface fluxes of atmospheric constituents, and ultimately, improve urban planning and environmental management strategies.

17210219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210219.value: The conventional secondary biological wastewater treatment process is not only an energy-intensive operation but also unable to recover resources from wastewater. As an alternative, chemically enhanced primary sedimentation (CEPS) diverts organics and nutrients, especially P, from wastewater into the sludge, which can effectively reduce the pollutant load on the downstream treatment and increase the potential of resource recovery. Hong Kong has the largest CEPS treatment plant in the world dosing FeCl3 to treat 1.7 million m3/d of municipal wastewater. The large amount of organics and nutrients in the CEPS sludge are valuable resources that should be recovered other than wasted to landfilling or incineration. In our recent development, side-stream acidogenic fermentation has been applied to recover soluble organics and P from the CEPS sludge. The organic-rich supernatant is then returned to the mainstream to provide the organic carbon source for denitrification. However, new issues are raised during the development: (i) if the wastewater contains heavy metals, even at a low level, the CEPS sludge and P precipitates would be contaminated by heavy metals; and (ii) the high ammonium content in the fermented sludge liquor brings the nitrogen load back to the mainstream wastewater flow. This research project is proposed to develop new technologies for treating heavy metal-containing CEPS sludge, aiming at recovery of organic resources, nutrients (N and P) and heavy metals, with the benefits of sludge reduction and stabilization. The CEPS sludge will be fermented to produce volatile fatty acids (VFAs) and extract heavy metals and nutrients into the supernatant. To improve the fermentation result, carbohydrates-rich food waste will be added for co-fermentation and enhanced acidogenesis. The supernatant of the fermented sludge will then be treated with capacitive deionization (CDI) cells to separate phosphate, ammonium and heavy metals from the VFAs-rich solution. The carbon-based porous electrodes will be experimented and optimized for effective material separation. The final products will include VFAs and organic solution for denitrification, vivianite for P-fertilizers, ammonium solution for N-fertilizers, heavy metal precipitates for further recovery, and stabilized sludge with a much low heavy metal content for safe disposal. The technological innovation will greatly improve the capacity and performance of municipal wastewater treatment for enhanced nutrient and heavy metal removals, together with energy-saving and resource recovery, in Hong Kong, China and elsewhere. 傳統的污水二級生物處理工藝能耗高，且不能回收污水中的寶貴資源。化學強化混凝沉澱（CEPS）作為傳統重力沉澱的替代工藝，可以高效地將有機物和營養資源，尤其是磷（P），從污水轉到到污泥中實現濃縮。 CEPS不僅減小後續處理環節的污染負荷，而且提高了污水資源回收利用的潛力。香港擁有全世界最大的CEPS污水處理厂，日處理水量達到180萬噸，通過投加三氯化鐵（FeCl3）強化污水處理效果。CEPS污泥中蘊含了大量的有機物和營養物資源，值得採用一定的手段進行回收利用，而不是現有的填埋或者焚燒處理方式，這是資源的浪費。本課題組近期研究成果發現，將CEPS污泥進行旁路酸化發酵可以有效回收其中的有機碳和P。富含有機物的酸化污泥上清液回流至污水處理主流系統，為反硝化脫氮處理補充所需要的碳源。然而，這一新工藝面臨了新的問題：（1）若污水含有重金屬，即使是低濃度，CEPS污泥和P的回收產物均會被重金屬污染，影響回收產物的價值；（2）酸化污泥上清液中含有高濃度的氨氮，若不經過回收就直接回流至主流污水處理工藝，則會增加氮的負荷，降低脫氮效率。 基於上述問題，本項目提出了新的技術用於處理富含重金屬的CEPS污泥，在污泥減量和穩定化過程中，同步回收其中的有機物、營養物和重金屬資源。首先採用酸化發酵工藝對CEPS污泥進行處理，促使污泥中的有機物轉化為揮發性脂肪酸（VFAs）, 同時釋放其中的重金屬和營養物質至上清液。為了提高污泥的酸化效果，採用碳水型餐廚垃圾與污泥共發酵。然後採用電容去離子（CDI）工藝將P、氨氮和重金屬從富含VFAs的污泥上清液中分離、濃縮、回收。CDI處理單元將採用碳基的多孔電極材料，優化材料製備工藝以提高目標物質的分離效率。工藝的最終產物包括富含VFAs的上清液用於反硝化，富含磷酸鐵的磷礦原料，富含氨氮的溶液用於氮肥，重金屬沉澱產物，和去重金屬的穩定污泥。該創新技術將極大提高市政污水的處理效率，並回收其中的寶貴資源，降低處理能耗，適用於香港，中國及其他地區。

17210219.label: Realisation of objectives
17210219.value: All of the research objectives have been well achieved. Following the proposal, experimental studies have been carried out for the realization of the objectives. 1. Development of a novel co-fermentation-CDI process for treatment of CEPS sludge for energy-saving, resource recovery and sludge stabilization in municipal wastewater treatment (i) Optimization of Fe dosage for organic and P removal from wastewater by CEPS: Laboratory experiments were carried out to determine the chemical (FeCl3) dosing scheme to concentrate organics and P into the CEPS sludge. Simple primary sedimentation (0 mg Fe/L) only reduced TOC (total organic carbon) by 38.8% and PO4-P by 5.9% on average from the domestic wastewater. With FeCl3 flocculation, the CEPS significantly enhanced both organic carbon and PO4-P removal. At a dosage of 20 mg-Fe/L, the TOC and PO4-P removal efficiencies increased to 75.6% and 99.3%, respectively. Compared to the primary effluent, the average TOC and PO4-P concentrations of the CEPS effluent decreased from 90.1 to 36.0 mg/L and from 3.7 to 0.03 mg/L, respectively. Overall, more than 70% of total organics and 95% of phosphate were removed from wastewater by CEPS into the sludge. (ii) Enhancement of CEPS sludge fermentation by food waste addition: Two typical chemical sludges, the Fe-dosed activated sludge (FeAS) and the Fe-enhanced primary sludge (FePS), were collected for acidogenic co-fermentation. To facilitate acidogenic fermentation of the sludge, typical food waste was added at a predetermined loading rate for co-fermentation. Acidogenic fermentation produces VFAs and thus creates a weak acidic condition for the dissolution of Fe-P precipitates. The degradable organics in FePS contributed to fermentation and resulted in greater production of soluble organics (>2.0 g-COD/L) than the amount of food waste added (1.5 g-COD/L) in this phase. The main species of VFAs were acetate and propionate. (iii) Phosphorus release and recovery by co-fermentation of CEPS sludge and food waste: During acidogenic fermentation, the Fe(II) compounds in acidic conditions are much more soluble than their Fe(III) counterparts. At a low pH (4-5), the reduced Fe(II)-P complex can be dissolved to release Fe(II) and orthophosphate ions into the solution. The iron reduction in the fermentation of FePS (75%) was more efficient than that in FeAS (39%). As a result, more P was released into the supernatant from FePS. For FePS, the main P species were found to be reducible Fe-P (79.5%) and organic P (15.4%). The P-rich supernatant was processed in the precipitation tank for P recovery, and more than 99% of the P in fermented supernatant was re-precipitated with Fe into the solid phase for recovery in the form of vivianite. 2. Fabrication of innovative CDI cells without membranes to effectively separate phosphates, ammonium-nitrogen and heavy metals from the VFAs-rich sludge liquor for multiple resource recovery; (i) Selectively ammonium removal and recovery by flow-electrode capacitive deionization (FCDI): Potassium dititanate (K2Ti2O5 or KTO) particles prepared by the electrospray method followed by calcination were mixed with activated carbon (AC) powder to form a novel KTO-AC flow-electrode for selective NH4+ removal over Na+. The mixed KTO-AC electrode exhibits a much higher speciﬁc gravimetric capacitance in NH4Cl solution than in NaCl solution. Compared with the pure AC electrode in the FCDI tests on NH4+ removal from synthetic wastewater, 25 wt% KTO addition in the electrode mixture increases the adsorption selectivity from 2.3 to 31 towards NH4+ over Na+, achieving selective NH4+ recovery and effective electrode regeneration. (ii) Enhanced NH4+ removal and recovery from wastewater using Na-zeolite-based FCDI: Low-cost Na-modified zeolite (Na-zeolite) was used to prepare a composite flow-electrode (FE) suspension with a small amount of highly conductive carbon black (CB) to remove and recover NH4+ from synthetic and actual wastewater (200 mg-N/L). Compared with conventional activated carbon (AC), the Na-zeolite electrode exhibited a 56.2−88.5% decrease in liquid-phase NH4+ concentration in the FE suspension due to its higher NH4+ adsorption capacity (6.0 vs. 0.2 mg-N/g). The resulting enhancement of NH4+ diffusion to the electrode chamber contributed to the improved performance of FCDI. The addition of CB to the FE suspension increased the conductivity and facilitated Na-zeolite charging for NH4+ electrosorption. NH4+-rich zeolite can be easily separated by sedimentation from CB in the FE suspension, producing a soil conditioner with a high N-fertilizer content suitable for soil improvement and agricultural applications. (iii) Embedment of graphene in binder-free fungal hypha-based electrodes for enhanced CDI: Freestanding carbon electrodes that do not use binders are suitable for realizing high-performance CDI. In this study, a freestanding and binder-free electrode was developed from the fungal hyphae of Aspergillus niger with embedded graphene (G-FhEld) or activated carbon (AC-FhEld). When used in CDI cycles, the G-FhEld outperformed AC-FhEld and the electrodes without graphene or AC. Fungal hyphae can be mass-produced from food waste and separated by simple filtration to prepare the precursors of the electrodes, and thus, G-FhEld is highly scalable for large-scale CDI applications. 3. Integration of the CEPS, co-fermentation and CDI units with the secondary wastewater treatment system. (i) Efficient electrochemical degradation of emerging organic pollutants by freestanding 3-dimensional macro-porous SnO2 electrodes: Novel freestanding and highly-stable 3-dimensional SnO2-Sb anodes with macro-pores (3D MP SnO2-Sb) were fabricated by simply compressing the precursor of SnO2-Sb and carbon fibers followed by one-step sintering. Compared with the conventional 2D SnO2-Sb/Ti anode, the 3D MP SnO2-Sb anode featured a more than 100-fold increase in electro-active surface area, which greatly improved the EC efficiency for antibiotic oxidation and mineralization. Nearly 100% of ciprofloxacin (CIP, 20 mg L-1) in the wastewater was degraded by the 3D MP SnO2-Sb anode at a very low current density of 5 mA cm-2. The 3D MP SnO2-Sb anode exhibited a high stability (>200 cycles) and performed well in treating actual wastewater. (ii) Ceramic membrane surface modification for electrically assisted membrane fouling control: A flat sheet CM was first coated with dopamine to form an intermediate adhesive layer, and this was then with oxidized carbon nanotubes (CNT), followed by calcination in an argon atmosphere to form a conductive CNT-coated CM. The flat sheet conductive CM enabled electrically enhanced membrane filtration of synthetic wastewater containing inorganic matter (kaolin solution) or organic pollutants (oil emulsion). The application of a negative charge at a DC 2.0 V on the flat sheet CM decreased the membrane fouling rate by approximately 50% compared to that without a DC supplied. The electric field exerted an electrostatic force on the negatively charged pollutants, which prevented the foulants from approaching and attaching to the membrane surface during the wastewater treatment process. (iii) Dual-functional single-atomic Mo/Fe clusters–decorated C3N5 for tandemly removing contaminants from wastewater: Dual-functional atomically dispersed Mo–Fe sites embedded in carbon nitride (C3N5) (i.e., MoFe/C3N5) were synthesized via a facile SiO2 template method. The MoFe/C3N5 catalyst on the cathode exhibited a remarkable catalytic activity toward the three electron-dominated oxygen reduction reaction in sodium sulfate, leading to a highly effective electro-Fenton (EF) reaction with a low overpotential for the removal of organic contaminants from wastewater. The new catalyst showed a superior performance over its conventional counterparts. DFT analysis revealed that the dual-functional 50-MoFe/C3N5 catalyst enabled a synergistic action of the Mo–Fe dual single atomic centers for effective organic oxidation during the EF process in wastewater treatment.

17210219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210219.value: 1. Sludge fermentation: The surfactant-assisted thermal hydrolysis pretreatment (THP) of waste activated sludge was developed. The surfactant addition increased the sludge disintegration for VFAs production during the THP-fermentation process (Shi et al., 2021). THP together with a one-time alkali pretreatment further increased the VFAs production. Compared with non-pretreatment cases, the THP&alkali–fermentation system performed better in fermentation and VFAs production, without the daily alkali addition to control pH (Wen et al, 2022). In addition, the TH supernatant of the sludge can be used as the substrate for the cultivation of oleaginous yeast to produce intracellular bio-lipids for value-added recovery of organic resources from waste sludge (Wen and Li, 2022). Moreover, by fungal fermentation, waste organics in the hydrolyzed sludge liquor can be converted into hyphae fibers for effective resource recovery (Liang et al., 2022). 2. CDI technology: Potassium dititanate (KTO) prepared by the electrospray method followed by calcination was mixed with activated carbon (AC) powder to form a novel KTO-AC flow-electrode for selective NH4+ recovery from wastewater as well as effective electrode regeneration during the CDI process (Lin et al., 2020). For improvement, low-cost Na-modified zeolite was used to prepare a composite flow-electrode suspension with a small amount of CB addition to recover NH4+ from synthetic and actual wastewater. NH4+-rich zeolite can be easily separated by sedimentation from CB in the FE suspension, producing a soil conditioner for agricultural applications (He et al., 2023). Furthermore, a freestanding and binder-free electrode was developed from the fungal hyphae with embedded graphene. The electrode outperformed the AC-based electrodes for CDI applications (Chen et al., 203). 3. Wastewater treatment: Novel freestanding and highly-stable 3D SnO2-Sb anodes were fabricated by simply compressing the SnO2-Sb precursor and carbon fibers followed by sintering. The new 3D anodes featured a more than 100-fold increase in electro-active surface area for efficient wastewater treatment (Yang et al, 2021). A novel flow-through SnO2-Sb reactive membrane electrode (RME) was also developed for wastewater treatment and disinfection (Yang et al., 2022). Besides, an innovative electrochemical technology was developed that employs packed bead-electrodes (PBE) as a dynamic electrocatalytic filter to largely expand the electroactive volume (Yang et al., 2023). Moreover, dual-functional atomically dispersed Mo–Fe sites embedded in carbon nitride (C3N5) (MoFe/C3N5) were synthesized via a facile SiO2 template method. The MoFe/C3N5 catalyst showed a superior performance over its conventional counterparts for electro-Fenton reaction for wastewater treatment (Dong et al., 2023).

17210219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210219.value: 1. Cost-effective analysis of the treatment and resource recovery process: The cost of co-fermentation and CDI for the wastewater and sludge treatment needs to be evaluated. The benefits of resource recovery, such as VFAs and nutrients-fertilizers should also be estimated. Overall, the cost and benefit of the innovative system, as well as the environmental advantages, need to be compared with the conventional sludge treatment and disposal methods, such as incineration and landfilling. 2. Application of the CDI technology in treatment of other waste streams for resource recovery: Traditionally, CDI is a desalination technology. With the continuous development, in addition to wastewater treatment, CDI can be applied for treatment of other waste streams for the purpose of resource recovery. Potential waste streams include food processing wastewater, surface plating and electronic industry wastewater, and wastewater of food waste. Successful CDI application will provide effective technical means for achieving circular economy and environmental sustainability.

17210319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210319.value: 微馬達是能夠將能量轉化為有效運動的微型裝置，屬於新興領域，具有廣泛的潛在應用，例如能源儲存、環境監測/修復、健康診斷和醫療干預。然而，傳統的製備方法對微結構的精確加工及其性能的調控尚有不足，導致微馬達的功能無法滿足應用要求。我們提出一種可擴展的微流控方法，通過固化受纖維約束的微液滴來精確製造微馬達：控制微流控系統的進料液體、微液滴的大小和變形，可準確、獨立地控制並調節微馬達的成分、尺寸和形狀。利用該方法，我們可在微馬達中摻雜鉑-鐵（Pt-Fe）殼-核納米顆粒，其中Pt殼可催化過氧化氫分解產生氧氣氣泡，Fe可對外部磁場產生響應，繼而分別用於驅動和引導微馬達。該方法的優勢在於充分利用了液滴微流控技術的可擴展性、對微小體積流體的精確處理能力、以及在微纖維約束下微液滴的精確變形，從而實現了精確、可控和大批量製備豐富多樣的微馬達。我們的目標是檢驗液滴微流控技術精確製造多樣化微馬達的潛力。具體地，我們將首先製備兩種微馬達：基於聚二甲基矽氧烷（PDMS）和聚乙二醇雙丙烯酸酯（PEGDA）微顆粒進行Pt-Fe殼-核納米顆粒的不對稱摻雜。在此基礎上，我們會研究微馬達的加工參數、形貌和組成對其運動動力學（包括遊動速度和方向）的影響。由於PDMS和PEGDA 具有良好的生物相容性，因此它們在輸送疏水（PDMS）和親（PEGDA）藥物方面具有潛力；選擇Pt-Fe殼-核納米顆粒是因為Pt和Fe可分別為微馬達提供催化推進和磁性導航。該專案的成功將為製造高精度、多功能和高性能的微馬達提供一種新方法。該項目還將研發革命性的微型馬達，這些馬達將推動其在生物醫藥領域的應用，比如藥物和其他生物活性物質的靶向輸送。該專案的研究結果將為合理設計微馬達並精確調控其結構和運動以滿足特定的應用需求提供良好的借鑒思路。

17210319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17210319.value: The project has been completed successfully. The major findings have been published in 4 PhD theses, one book and 17 papers in various prestigious Journals including Chemical Reviews (IF=72.087), Progress in Materials Science (IF=48.16), Nature Nanotechnology (IF=39.213), Advanced Materials (IF=30.849), Materials Today (IF=26.416), ACS Nano (IF=14.588), Science Advances (IF=14.136), Materials Horizons (IF=12.319), and Nature Communications (IF=14.919). One patent was filled and received the 2021 Gold Medal of the International Exhibition of Inventions of Geneva. A droplet-based microfluidics approach was developed to precisely fabricate micromotors with well-controlled 3D structures and compositions. In particular, microfluidic droplets were produced using a glass capillary microfluidic device and then subjected to shape deformation via microfiber confinement, and solidified to create anisotropic microparticle motors. It offered precision and controllability over emulsion templates to enable accurate fabrication of highly uniform and well-defined micromotors. The motor’s composition, size, and shape were precisely defined and varied independently in the microfluidic device by the feeding liquids, the droplet size, and the microfiber-confined shape deformation of droplets, respectively. The synthetic micromotors were made anisotropic by their structure and material composition through controllable deformation of droplets and use of versatile emulsion templates. Typical micromotors included spindle, drum, zig-zag, and 3D polyhedral microparticles with tunable sizes.

17210319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17210319.value: The technology developed in the project is of potential practical applications; the PI is going to continue the work of applying the technology in effectively fabricate micro-particles/motors/robots that would offer some tools/solutions in addressing multiple challenges arising from climate change, food safety, an ageing population, COVID-19 and other public health concerns and in meeting the demand for the Fourth Industrial Revolution.

17210319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210319.value: Micromotors are microscale devices capable of converting energy into movement. They represent an emerging field with wide potential applications from energy storage and environmental monitoring/remediation to health diagnostics and medical interventions. However, the functional outcomes of existing synthetic micromotors have not been satisfactory because of inadequacies in conventional fabrication approaches for engineering microstructures and properties of such micromotors. With this project, a scalable approach was developed for the precise fabrication of well-defined micromotors via solidifying microfiber-confined microfluidic droplets. The micromotor’s composition, size, and shape can be accurately and independently controlled/tuned in the microfluidic system by the feeding liquids, the size of microfluidic droplets, and the shape deformation of microfluidic droplets subject to microfiber confinement, respectively. The approach also allows precise doping with platinum-iron (Pt-Fe) shell-core nanoparticles (NPs), which propel and guide the motor via bubbles from Pt-catalyzed decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) and through the response of Fe to external magnetic fields, respectively. The approach has taken full advantage of the capabilities of droplet microfluidics in terms of scalability and precise-handling of small fluid volumes and precise shape deformation of microfluidic droplets under microfiber confinement, leading to precise, controllable, and scalable fabrication of a myriad of micromotors.

17210419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17210419.value: Many people suffer from malalignment of teeth, such as crowded teeth or overjet, which compromise mastication (i.e. chewing) and causes aesthetic problems, so may benefit from orthodontic treatment. Due to elevated awareness of dental health and improved standard of living, the demand for orthodontic treatment is on fast and steady rise, especially in developing countries, such as the mainland China. However, traditional orthodontics is a combination of science and art. It depends heavily on the experience of individual orthodontists and involves laborious manual works. The treatment is costly and takes long time (typically 2 years), and the outcome is often of uncertain quality. All this gives rise to digital orthodontics, a rapidly advancing field in which computer technology is used to facilitate various tasks in orthodontic treatment and so to better meet the demand of an increasing population seeking orthodontic care. In this project we will focus on developing efficient computational methods for generating high-quality tooth alignment, which is the central issue in digital orthodontics. Specifically, we address the following two outstanding problems: (1) How to generate the optimal target tooth alignment for a specific patient? This is in fact the task of defining the treatment goal; (2) How to produce feasible motion paths for all the teeth from their initial arrangement before treatment to their target arrangement? Well designed motion paths of teeth are critical since they are needed for modeling sequential clear aligners or for designing customized brackets. These problems are challenging because it is difficult to specify the orthodontist's experience in algorithmic terms and there are so many requirements and constraints to meet in reaching an optimal solution, including all the anatomical, bio-mechanical and aesthetic considerations in defining and achieving an optimal tooth alignment. We propose to solve these problems by develop novel and efficient methods based on machine learning and geometric optimization. In this proposal we will present the detailed methodology of our study and demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach with promising preliminary results. We will also discuss the key research tasks and the validation plan. The outcome of this project will represent significant advances in digital orthodontics and help to make orthodontic care better and more accessible to the public. 牙齿排列不齐是困扰大众的重要问题，其中牙列拥挤或牙齿过多尤为突出，严重影响牙齿的美观与健康。随着人们口腔健康意识的增强及生活水平的提高，牙齿正畸需求稳步增长，特别是在发展中国家（如中国）。然而，传统正畸治疗需综合科学以及美学因素进行考量，严重依赖正畸医师的个人经验并耗费大量的人力资源。同时，正畸治疗花费高、周期长（一般需两年），且治疗结果参差不齐。基于上述问题，数字化正畸技术变得至关重要，其将许多相关的计算机技术应用于正畸任务中，以满足日益增长的牙齿矫正和护理需求。 在本项目中，我们将主要关注数字正畸的核心问题——生成高质量牙齿排列方案的方法的研发。具体而言将解决以下两个突出问题。（1）如何为病人生成个性化的最优牙齿排列方案？解决这一问题为正畸治疗提供了最终目标；（2）如何获取所有牙齿从治疗前的初始位置至治疗后的目标位置的可行运动路径？合理的牙齿运动路径对于设计后续的隐形调整器至关重要。解决上述问题的挑战性在于如何将正畸医师的经验描述为特定的算法语言，并同时考虑解剖学、生物力学等约束条件及美学等多种需求，以获得最优的正畸方案。 本项目提出一种基于机器学习和几何优化的高效方法解决上述问题。首先将详细介绍所提出的方法，并通过初步结果展示所提方法的可行性。其次将讨论关键研究任务与检验方案。本项目期望能够大力推动数字口腔正畸研究的发展，并为公众提供更高质量且更易获取的口腔护理技术。

17210419.label: Realisation of objectives
17210419.value: All the objectives of the project have been accomplished and presented in six publications - four published and two under reviews. Objective 1 [100%]: We have developed an innovative pipeline for predicting the target/destination tooth alignment. The pipeline has two steps. In the first step, we collected hundreds of pairs of orthodontic treatment models to train a neural network to a target tooth alignments of high aesthetic quality, from the tooth arrangement of unseen patient. However, such an arrangement may contain intersections between the teeth, which is not allowed in physical treatment. Therefore, in the second step, we developed a rule-based method to refine the output from the first step to ensure that the teeth are free of intersection and gaps, as well as satisfy several other clinical requirements. Objective 2 [100%]: Assuming that the satisfactory target tooth alignment has been obtained, we developed a method that extends the L-J potential energy for planning the motions of the teeth from their initial untreated positions to the target positions. Our method is automatic and takes only a few minutes to produce smooth, intersection-free motions of the teeth, which used to be a tedious manual task taking hours to accomplish. Objective 3 & 4 [100%]: We have proposed a data-driven method for detecting the tooth features to inform digital orthodontic diagnosis and treatment. The paper has been published in the journal Computer Graphics Forum. Furthermore, going beyond individual teeth, we developed algorithms for cephalometric landmark detection both in 2D and 3D, leading two papers which were presented at MICCAI and published in IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging, respectively.

However, such an arrangement may contain intersections between the teeth, which is not allowed in physical treatment. Therefore, in the second step, we developed a rule-based method to refine the output from the first step to ensure that the teeth are free of intersection and gaps, as well as satisfy several other clinical requirements. The paper has been submitted to IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging. Paper #2: A Potential Field Method for Tooth Motion Planning in Orthodontic Treatment, under review by IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics. Assuming that the satisfactory target tooth alignment has been obtained, we developed a method that extends the L-J potential energy for planning the motions of the teeth from their initial untreated positions to the target positions. Our method is automatic and takes only a few minutes to produce smooth, intersection-free motions of the teeth, which used to be a tedious manual task taking hours to accomplish. The paper has been submitted to IEEE TVCG. Paper #3: SRF-Net: Spatial Relationship Feature Network for Tooth Point Cloud Classification, Computer Graphics Forum, 2020 Paper #4: Cephalometric Landmark Detection by Attentive Feature Pyramid Fusion and Regression-Voting, MICCAI, 2019 We have proposed a data-driven method for detecting the tooth features to inform digital orthodontic diagnosis and treatment. The paper has been published in the journal Computer Graphics Forum. Furthermore, going beyond individual teeth, we developed algorithms for cephalometric landmark detection both in 2D and 3D, leading to two papers which were presented at MICCAI and published in IEEE Transactions on Medical Imaging, respectively.

17210419.value: We plan to build a software system to automate the entire pipeline of digital orthodontic treatment, from diagnosis, to treatment planning, and to aligner fabrication.

17210419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17210419.value: This project aims to use advanced computational technologies (AI and optimization) to facilitate the orthodontic treatment, which is now a tedious and costly process with unreliable results. Specifically, we develop a learning-based method for automatically generating the optimal target tooth alignment to achieve normal occlusion. Then, given the planned target tooth alignment, we develop an optimization-based method for automatically generating high-quality, smooth, and feasible motion paths of all the teeth from the initial arrangement before treatment to the target arrangement. The results of motion planning provide the 3D digital models for fabricating clear aligners for orthodontic treatment.

17300319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300319.value: 隨著我們在基因表達調控方面的知識不斷擴大，目前出現了許多基於核酸的治療方法，可用於治療多種疾病，包括遺傳性疾病，癌症和感染。 它們幾乎可以靶向任何與疾病相關的蛋白質，這是小分子藥物或蛋白質治療無法實現的。 然而，由於缺乏安全有效的遞送系統，這些技術目前難以轉化為臨床應用。 其中，通過肺部遞送以治療肺部疾病的核酸療法的研究尤為有限。吸入核酸療法的成功與否很大程度上取決於核酸的轉染效率，遞送系統的安全性，製劑能否達到有效肺沉積的霧化性能，以及核酸克服粘液屏障的能力。 受可促進納米顆粒在氣道中的轉運的肺表面活性物質的啟發，我們研究了以表面活性蛋白B為模型的KL4多肽成為肺部核酸遞送的非病毒載體的潛在可能性。 我們的工作表明，這種由21個氨基酸合成表面活性多肽可與RNA結合形成納米複合物，並有效地將RNA 轉染到肺上皮細胞中。 然而，其應用受到低溶解度和傳遞到小鼠肺部後引起的輕度免疫原性應答的限制。 我們推測聚乙二醇（PEG）聚合物與KL4的結合具有三重益處：（i）改善多肽的溶解度 ; （ii）降低免疫原性; （iii）克服肺部的粘液屏障的同時不影響KL4的轉染效率。 我們的預實驗取得了較好的結果，水溶性的PEG化KL4多肽在氣管內給藥後，有效的在小鼠肺部內轉染RNA， 並且沒有毒性和免疫原性反應的跡象。 本專案旨在開發作為肺部遞送的新型非病毒載體的PEG化KL4系統，特別關注于通過RNA干擾（RNAi）進行基因沉默的小干擾RNA（siRNA）。 通過改變PEG的分子量和結構，優化系統的傳遞效率和安全性。 根據本課題組在肺部給藥方面的專業知識和研究經驗，我們將以噴霧乾燥技術製備吸入式處方，並優化其霧化性能。 此外，我們將進一步探索PEG化KL4系統在介導CRISPR / Cas9 傳遞以進行基因編輯方面的潛力。 本專案的成果是研究出一種新型多功能肺部遞送平臺。 該平臺可廣泛應用於不同的RNA療法，包括但不限於siRNA，microRNA，信使RNA（mRNA）和基於CRISPR的治療方法，從而治療不同的肺部疾病。

17300319.label: Realisation of objectives
17300319.value: 1. Although KL4 peptide, a synthetic cationic peptide with a repeating KLLLL sequence, exhibits good in vitro siRNA transfection efficiency on lung epithelial cells, its therapeutic potential is limited by its poor aqueous solubility due to the presence of a high proportion of hydrophobic leucine residues. In this study, we aim to address the solubility issue, designing five different modified peptides by replacing the hydrophobic leucine with alanine or valine, and assess their potential as siRNA delivery vectors. While the modified peptides retain the overall cationic property, their siRNA binding is also affected and their transfection efficiency is inferior to the parent KL4 peptide. A closer examination of the conformation of these peptides by circular dichroism shows that substitution of leucine residues leads to the change of the secondary structure from a-helical content to either b-sheet or more disordered, b-turn conformations. Relatively conservative amino acid substitutions, in terms of hydrophobicity bulk, lead to substantial conformational alteration, heavily impacting siRNA binding and release, cellular uptake, and transfection efficiency. Although the peptide modification strategy employed in this study was unsuccessful in developing an improved version of KL4 peptide for siRNA delivery, it highlights the importance of the a- helical conformation for efficient siRNA transfection, providing useful insights for future development of peptide-based RNA delivery system. 2. To overcome the water solubility issue while retaining the transfection efficiency of the KL4 peptide, we further modified the peptide by covalent attachment of monodisperse poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) to KL4. This approach improves the solubility of KL4 and the uptake of its complex with siRNA into lung epithelial cells, such that very robust silencing is produced. All PEGylated KL4 peptides, with PEG length varying between 6 and 24 monomers, could bind and form nanosized complexes with siRNA, but the interaction between siRNA and peptides became weaker as the PEG chain length increased. All PEGylated KL4 peptides exhibited satisfactory siRNA transfection efficiency on three human lung epithelial cell lines, including A549 cells, Calu-3 cells, and BEAS-2B cells. The PEG12KL4 peptide, which contains 12 monomers of PEG, was optimal for siRNA delivery and also demonstrated a low risk of inflammatory response and toxicity in vivo following pulmonary administration.

17300319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300319.value: This study investigates the effect of PEGylation on KL4 peptides for siRNA transfection. Monodisperse PEG, with different numbers of monomers, was covalently attached to the KL4 peptide and the performances of the modified peptides as siRNA delivery vector were compared. The increase of the PEG chain length resulted in improved water solubility, better colloidal stability, and higher cellular uptake of siRNA. Based on the in vitro studies, the water-soluble PEG12KL4 peptide showed the optimal characteristics as the siRNA delivery vector. It could bind with siRNA with desirable affinity and mediate robust transfection and efficient intracellular transportation, along with a low risk of inflammatory response and toxicity in vivo following pulmonary administration. Overall, PEG12KL4 has a considerable potential to be developed as a nonviral vector for siRNA pulmonary delivery. Future studies will focus on investigating the in vivo siRNA transfection efficiency of the PEG12KL4 peptide following pulmonary administration. To conclude, KL4 and PEGylated KL4 peptides are promising candidates for delivering RNA therapeutics in the clinic. Future studies will focus on applying the delivery system to disease models to evaluate their therapeutic potential.

17300319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300319.value: The objective of future study is to develop this delivery system as a platform technology so that it can be applied to other RNA therapeutics, for different therapeutic indications such as respiratory infections, vaccines, lung inflammatory diseases, acute lung injury/ pulmonary fibrosis and lung cancer. Optimization of dry powder formulation will be carried out, and pharmacokinetic studies will also be performed to gain a better understanding on the performance of the inhaled dry powder formulations as compared to other routes of administration.

17300319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300319.value: Inhalation of RNA therapeutics has gained considerable attention for the treatment of a wide range of respiratory diseases. The delivery of RNAs presents a major obstacle that hinders their further development. A safe and effective vector is needed to mediate robust RNA transfection in the lung. In this study, the potential of KL4 to deliver siRNA was firstly evaluated. KL4 was able to bind to siRNA and form nano-sized complexes through electrostatic interaction. KL4/siRNA complexes showed superior stability in pulmonary surfactant and they mediated effective siRNA transfection in vitro on human lung epithelial cells. There was no significant sign of inflammatory response and toxicity in vitro at the tested dose. However, the high leucine content of KL4 renders it insoluble in water and limits its application as a delivery vector. To address this problem, PEGylation strategy was applied by covalently attaching monodispersed polyethylene glycol (PEG) to KL4. Three PEGs with length varied between six to 24 monomers were employed to investigate the impact of PEGylation. The increase of PEG chain length resulted in higher water solubility, improved colloidal stability and enhanced transfection efficiency in vitro. Among all the peptides, PEG12KL4 peptide, which contains 12 monomers of PEG, was identified to be optimal for siRNA delivery as it attains a balance between good solubility, efficient transfection and high safety profile.
