17300619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300619.value: Although river networks comprise less than 0.5% of the Earth’s land surface, large quantities of carbon are washed from the terrestrial environment into rivers and the resulting carbon fluxes constitute a significant component of the global carbon cycle. Recent research suggests that river systems act not only as land-to-ocean vectors, but also as dynamic conduits degassing greenhouse gases (GHGs) into the atmosphere. However, uncertainties on current flux estimates are large due to the absence of comprehensive, spatially resolved measurements of riverine carbon cycle. Existing studies are primarily concerned with American and European rivers, while East Asian rivers are substantially under-represented in the literature. Global estimates of riverine carbon export and GHG emissions are hampered by the lack of a clear understanding of geographical variability of the riverine carbon cycle. The Dongjiang River in subtropical South China is a primary tributary of the Pearl River and an important water source for Hong Kong, meeting 70–80% of its annual water demand. Owing to climate change and anthropogenic perturbations, the Dongjiang River Basin (DRB) has experienced significant changes in catchment environment and fluvial transport of water, sediment, carbon, and other nutrients over the past decades. While extensive studies have investigated its water and sediment transport, relatively little is known about the associated carbon and nutrients, which could significantly impact water quality. Together with the environmental features (e.g., strong chemical weathering and high flow from monsoonal rainfall) of the DRB, the proposed project aims to explore its riverine carbon cycle and GHG emissions. We will quantitatively investigate the spatial and temporal variations in downstream carbon export and the dynamics of GHG exchange at the water-air interface to comprehend their underlying mechanisms and response to human activity such as land-use change and damming. This will be the first integrated research project undertaken to investigate the riverine carbon cycle in the entire DRB, including downstream carbon export into the South China Sea and GHG emissions into the atmosphere. Building on our research experience, we will analyze the riverine carbon cycle and GHG emissions and assess their biogeochemical implications. Since the DRB’s riverine carbon cycle may have been affected by pollution, this analysis will also provide an opportunity to evaluate the challenges and risks to its water quality. As the Dongjiang River is Hong Kong’s primary water source, the proposed research will be highly relevant to policy makers involved in Hong Kong’s water resources management. 盡管全球河流水面積只占據了陸地總面積的不到0.5%，河流系統卻是全球碳循環過程中的壹個重要組成部分。每年有大量的陸源碳從陸地生態系統進入河流系統裏。近年來的研究表明河流系統不僅是簡單地把陸地生態系統的碳輸送至海洋系統中去，河流系統也是大氣溫室氣體的壹個重要釋放來源。然而，受限於在空間尺度上對全球河流碳循環監測的缺乏，當前關於河流碳輸移通量的研究仍存在較大的誤差。現有的研究多針對美洲和歐洲地區的河流系統來開展的，而缺乏對東亞地區河流碳輸移過程的認知和理解。由於不同地區間巨大的地理空間差異，針對不同地區間河流碳輸移過程研究的缺乏已成為當前全球河流碳輸移通量估算的壹個重要誤差來源。 位於華南亞熱帶地區的東江既是珠江流域系統的壹個重要支流，也是香港飲用水的重要來源地。香港地區每年消耗的淡水中高達70–80%來源於東江流域。然而，受近幾十年來氣候變化和人類活動的雙重影響，東江流域的流域環境和河流水、沙、碳及其它營養鹽輸移動態都發生了顯著變化。值得註意的是盡管針對東江流域的水、沙輸移已引起學術界廣泛的關註和研究，然而對於相應的河流碳及營養鹽輸移及其對東江水質影響的研究卻仍很缺乏。結合東江流域獨特的環境特征（比如劇烈的化學風化過程和季風氣候影響下的強降雨-徑流過程），本項目將首次針對東江流域的河流碳輸移過程和水-氣界面溫室氣體逸出開展相關的深入研究。本研究項目將定量分析東江流域河流碳橫向輸移過程的時空變化特征，並探究水-氣界面的溫室氣體逸出通量及過程，進而辨析其內在機理及其對流域內人類活動（諸如土地利用變化和河道水壩建設）的響應。 作為針對整個東江流域河流碳橫向輸移過程及水-氣界面溫室氣體逸出的首次系統性探索研究，本項目對於理解河流碳循環過程具有重要的理論意義。基於項目申請者前期關於土壤侵蝕、泥沙輸移和河流碳循環的研究結果，本項目將全面而系統地探討東江流域河流碳輸移過程及其生物地球化學意義。此外，鑒於東江流域的河流碳循環過程極有可能已受流域內水汙染的影響，本項目還將評估其水資源管理所面臨的挑戰和風險。因此，作為香港地區重要的飲用水源地，本項目的研究結果將有助於香港特區政府相關的政府決策者更準確地評估其水資源並制定相應的對策。

17300619.label: Realisation of objectives
17300619.value: River systems transport huge quantities of carbon and other materials into the coastal ocean and represent an important component in the global carbon cycle. During the implementation of this research project, my team has performed five sampling campaigns in the subtropical Dongjiang River Basin (DRB). Three campaigns were performed in the wet season (April–September) and the remaining two in the dry season (October–March). In each campaign (~16 days), we visited 43 sites across the DRB to examine the spatiotemporal variation in its riverine carbon cycling and GHG emission dynamics as well as their underlying mechanisms. Major research activities during the fieldwork included water and sediment sampling, measurement of water quality indicators, collection of gas samples, deployment of portable probes for measuring dissolved GHG concentrations, and in-situ measurement of GHG emissions. We have collected >4100 samples (soil, sediment, and gas) and completed all laboratory work. The obtained datasets were stored at the HKU DataHub. Below, I briefly summarize the state how and to what extent the listed four objectives have been achieved. For Objective 1: Both downstream carbon export into the South China Sea and GHG emissions in the DRB were found to exhibit pronounced spatial and seasonal variations. For downstream carbon export at the outlet (i.e., the Boluo Hydrological Gauge), dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) is the major carbon species due largely to its unique lithological composition. DIC concentrations ranged from 21 to 65 mg/L and were generally 10 times higher than dissolved organic carbon (DOC). Content of particulate organic carbon (POC) in sediments was low, which reflects the low soil erosion intensity within the basin. The total downstream carbon export in the DRB was 0.462 Tg C/year, including 0.065 Tg as DOC, 0.028 Tg as POC, and 0.369 Tg as DIC. We observed a significant seasonal variation in the carbon concentrations and fluxes. For example, both the dissolved and particulate carbon concentrations were significantly lower during high flow periods due largely to the ‘dilution effect’. However, the high flow periods played an important role in delivering riverine carbon on the annual timescale. All the surveyed streams were net carbon dioxide (CO2) sources for the atmosphere. Similarly, the dissolved CO2 partial pressure (pCO2) exhibited pronounced spatial and temporal patterns, which were affected by terrestrial carbon inputs (i.e., organic and inorganic) and in-stream metabolism, both of which varied due to different land covers, topography, and seasonality of precipitation and temperature. The mean CO2 ﬂux was 300.1 and 264.2 mmol/m2/day during the wet season for large and small rivers, respectively, which were 2-fold larger than that during the dry season (see: Liu et al., 2021. Biogeosciences, 18, 5231-5245; Liu et al., 2023. JGR: Biogeosciences, 128, e2022JG007291). For Objective 2: Our study shows that lateral carbon derived from decomposition of organic matter and rock weathering played a central role in controlling the variability of riverine pCO2 and CO2 emissions (see: Liu et al., 2023. JGR: Biogeosciences, 128, e2022JG007291; Ran et al., 2021. Nature Communications, 12, 1-9; Chan et al., 2021. Frontiers in Earth Science, 9, 741678). By classifying the river networks into small and large rivers, we found small rivers are major contributors to CO2 emissions, even with relatively low pCO2 levels and small water surface areas. They contribute disproportionately to 74.4% of the total CO2 fluxes due largely to high gas transfer velocities (k). Furthermore, land use and land cover change can significantly alter the CO2 emission dynamics. Our results show that land use changes have substantially enhanced CO2 emissions from the DRB. Normalized areal CO2 fluxes in the urban- and cropland-dominated middle and lower DRB (27.6 and 39.4 g C/m2/year, respectively) were two and three times higher than the 9.1 g C/m2/year in the forest-dominated upper DRB. Due to the larger water surface area and higher gas transfer velocities caused by monsoon-induced precipitation, the DRB acted as a stronger carbon source during the wet season, emitting 0.67 Tg C, which is about twice that during the dry season (0.33 Tg C). Our study illustrated how monsoon climate and land use in the DRB had regulated its riverine GHG emissions. Our findings also provided a mechanistic understanding of the role of small rivers in the basin-wide carbon cycle. For Objective 3: By using the carbon isotope techniques, we determined the sources of riverine DOC, POC and DIC. To better capture the spatial heterogeneity in hydrology, climate, and human impacts (e.g., land use change, damming, and eutrophication), we conducted sampling at representative locations in the upper, middle, and lower DRB. Our unpublished results show that most of the riverine organic carbon in the DRB is derived from decomposition of recently fixed organic matter. For the POC in small rivers, the contribution of petrogenic carbon is non-negligible. For riverine DIC, it is largely derived from chemical weathering, but the contribution of in-stream processing of organic matter via microbial respiration is likely substantial. Our research findings provided valuable insights into the origin, transfer mechanisms, and natural/human influences on the riverine carbon in the DRB and other river basins under similar environmental settings (see: Chan et al., 2022. Science of the Total Environment, 856, 159047). Part of these results have contributed to our national-scale assessment of CO2 emissions from Chinese inland waters (see: Ran et al., 2021. Nature Communications, 12, 1-9). For Objective 4: The DRB provides >70% of Hong Kong’s fresh water supply, and it is therefore essential that this supply is reliable. Our study throughout the DRB shows that its water quality exhibited significant spatial variability with generally better water quality in the upper reach where forest is the predominant land cover (see: Liu et al., 2023. JGR: Biogeosciences, 128, e2022JG007291). In comparison, the middle and lower reaches showed localized water pollution with the dissolved oxygen (DO) reaching as low as 2.85 mg/L in the dry season and 3.87 mg/L in the wet season, especially for the segment below Huizhou. This largely reflects the impact of human activities (e.g., urban sewage, industrial waste discharge, and agricultural fertilizer use). The pH varied in the range 6.50–7.85 and 6.38–9.26 in the dry and wet seasons, respectively, and the average DO was 9.20±2.27 mg/L and 7.28±1.21 mg/L in the dry and wet seasons, respectively. Furthermore, high Chl a concentrations (>15 mg/L) were typically observed in the lower reach, which further suggests water pollution due to high nutrient loading. Eutrophication in the lower DRB has become a pressing environmental challenge for the local authorities. In-stream decomposition of terrestrially derived organic matter (caused by both natural processes and human activities) has likely affected the water quality. Our results highlight the necessity of soil conservation to reduce sediment and carbon losses. Furthermore, effective environmental management is needed to mitigate water pollution, especially for non-point source pollution from agricultural activities. Overall, all the four research objectives have been successfully achieved. Our results have critically examined the riverine carbon cycling and GHG emission dynamics in the DRB. These findings have not only filled the knowledge gaps regarding aquatic carbon cycling in this important river basin, but also provided insights into future studies on carbon cycle in other rivers with similar environmental characteristics and anthropogenic perturbations.

17300619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300619.value: Our research based on five intensive sampling campaigns across the DRB indicates that both downstream carbon export and vertical CO2 emissions exhibited pronounced spatial and seasonal variations, which were collectively controlled by hydrological regime, geomorphological landscape, and human activity. For downstream carbon export, DIC is the predominant carbon species. The river water DIC concentrations (21–65 mg/L) were ~10 times higher than the DOC concentrations (<4 mg/L). Although a significant ‘dilution effect’ by flow discharge was observed, the high flow periods played a dominant role in delivering riverine carbon. For the first time, we quantified the downstream carbon export using weekly sampling results. The total flux was 0.462 Tg C/year, with organic carbon accounting for only 20.1% of the flux. In comparison, DIC played a dominant role, representing ~79.9% of the flux. This is primarily because of the widespread outcrops of silicates and carbonates within the DRB that, after chemical weathering, release large quantities of DIC into the river systems. The river water pCO2 ranged from 15 to 6323 µatm and it exhibited an increasing trend from headwaters towards the mainstream with the pCO2 in large rivers (2250±1178 µatm) being 76.3% higher than that in small rivers (1276±796 µatm). All surveyed streams were CO2 sources on the annual scale. Small rivers contributed disproportionately to 74.4% of the total fluxes due to high gas transfer velocities (k) caused by steep stream channels. Land use changes have substantially enhanced CO2 emissions. For instance, the areal riverine CO2 fluxes in the urban- and cropland-dominated reaches (27.6 and 39.4 g C/m2/year, respectively) were 2–3 times higher than that in the forest-dominated reach (9.1 g C/m2/year). Owing to the larger water surface area and higher k values due to monsoon-induced precipitation, the DRB functioned as a stronger carbon source in the wet season, emitting 0.67 Tg C into the atmosphere, which is about twice that during the dry season (0.33 Tg C). Our results provide a mechanistic understanding of how monsoonal climate and land use in the subtropical DRB mediate its riverine carbon cycling. Based on these results, nine peer-reviewed research articles have been published in prestigious journals. I have also attended three local/international conferences to share these research results. This research project has partly funded three postgraduate students. Of them, an MPhil student has successfully graduated in 2021 and a PhD student has passed his oral defense.

17300619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300619.value: Our research in the DRB shows the disproportionate importance of headwater streams in basin-wide GHG emissions. Thus, a mechanistic understanding of GHG dynamics in headwater streams is of paramount importance for assessing their biogeochemical implications for land-atmosphere carbon exchange. I have submitted a GRF proposal entitled ‘Greenhouse gas dynamics and aquatic carbon cycling in (sub)tropical headwater streams’ in 2023. In this research project, I aim to critically examine GHG (CO2, CH4, and N2O) production and emissions in (sub)tropical low- and high-gradient headwater streams under contrasting environmental settings. Furthermore, I aim to mechanistically understand hydrological and geomorphological controls and human influences on aquatic carbon cycling and GHG emission dynamics in (sub)tropical headwater streams. I will also develop reliable empirical models to estimate the gas transfer velocity in headwater streams for future upscaling studies for the estimation of GHG emissions. Additionally, based on the CO2 emission results in the Xinfengjiang Reservoir, I have submitted an NSFC/RGC proposal on GHG emission dynamics in aquaculture ponds in the Greater Bay Area this year. This proposed research aims to quantitatively understand the magnitude and drivers of GHG emissions from subtropical aquaculture ponds and assess their significance and role in the global carbon cycle.

17300619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300619.value: Increasing evidence suggests that river systems play an important role in the global carbon cycle. They act not only as land-to-ocean vectors, transporting huge quantities of carbon, but also as dynamic conduits that release greenhouse gases into the atmosphere during fluvial transit. Nevertheless, while most existing studies have been conducted in temperate and arctic regions, little is known on the aquatic carbon cycle and greenhouse gas dynamics in (sub)tropical rivers. Our results based on intensive sampling in the Dongjiang River Basin indicate that both downstream carbon export and CO2 emissions exhibited pronounced spatiotemporal variations, which are collectively regulated by hydrological regime (e.g., monsoon-induced rainfall), geomorphological landscape (e.g., channel steep and land-river connectivity), and human activity (e.g., land use change, urbanization, reservoir operation). Particularly, headwater streams contributed disproportionately to 74.4% of the total fluxes in the Dongjiang River Basin due to their high gas transfer velocities. Land use changes have substantially enhanced CO2 emissions from river networks with the emission rates in urban- and cropland-dominated rivers being 2–3 times higher than that from forest-dominated rivers. Our results reinforce the urgency to mechanistically understand the aquatic carbon cycling processes in (sub)tropical rivers and unravel their driving factors under global change.

17300719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17300719.value: The proposed project is basic research on fundamental processes related to the changing environment of the near-Earth space, which is also know as space weather driven by the supersonic charged particle flow from the Sun’s upper atmosphere. A better understanding of these processes is needed to accurately predict the impacts of geomagnetic storms on society. These impacts include ionospheric effects on satellite drag that complicates the prediction of satellite orbits and the prevention of collisions, radio wave absorption by the lower ionosphere that prevents HF communication with aircraft, scintillation and index of refraction gradients in the magnetosphere-ionosphere system that disrupt communication and navigation signals, and fluctuating magnetic fields that can induce currents in the power grid. The prediction of any one of these hazards requires an understanding of the entire coupled system since so many feedback mechanisms exist between the coupled solar wind-magnetosphere-ionosphere (SW-M-I) system. Numerical simulations of the near-Earth space environment (also known as the geospace) play an important role in understanding the dynamics of space weather. A key feature of most numerical geospace models is the implementation of terrestrial sourced ions not originating from the solar wind. However, one deficiency of most community global geospace simulation codes is the lack of systematic understandings of the role(s) of these terrestrial-sourced plasma populations on the geospace system dynamics, especially during geomagnetic storms. Thus this project is going to investigate physical processes related to these ion populations that are necessary to facilitate the understanding of the dynamics of the whole geospace system and to improve the capability of future space weather forecasting. The theory and modeling approach of this project will provide new understandings of the dynamics of space weather. The methodology is novel and it makes transformational scientific progress to study the Sun, Earth, and heliosphere as a coupled system, which potential contributions to a integrated, whole geospace model for future space weather applications. The new understanding realized from the anticipated results will directly address the space physics goals to determine the dynamics and coupling of Earth’s magnetosphere, ionosphere and upper atmosphere and their response to solar and terrestrial inputs. The anticipated results from the project will also provide new understanding of the ways that space storms are fueled by oxygen originating from Earth’s own atmosphere, which also have broad impacts in the research field of planetary and exoplanetary sciences. 在太陽風-地球磁層-電離層相互作用的過程中，磁重聯作為等離子體對流的驅動和電磁能量的轉化起到了重要的作用。因此關於磁重聯的物理過程研究是空間物理和空間天氣的重點之一。最新的理論模擬研究表明，地球日側磁層頂的重聯過程由太陽風（全球）或者局部過程（本地）共同控制，但是在這兩個物理過程轉換的過渡區域目前尚未有系統性的研究。本課題將通過使用全球磁流體力學模擬程序LFM，聚焦於全球控制/本地控制兩個物理過程中的過渡區域，尤其是來自於地球電離層和等離子層的帶電粒子對於日側磁重聯過程的影響。通過設計對照的數值模擬試驗，定量分析日側磁重聯過程對於等離子體數量和成分的響應，並且使用響應的衛星觀測數據對模擬結果進行驗證。系統性的模擬研究 將解答以下三個基礎和應用問題：1如何定量研究地球等離子體成分對於日側磁重聯過程的控制作用；2如何量化地球等離子體對於磁暴過程的影響；3如何把地球等離子體對磁重聯影響集成到空間天氣預報中。

17300719.label: Realisation of objectives
17300719.value: The first objective has been accomplished through collaborative model development. By working together with scientists from the National Center for Atmospheric Research, the PI has successfully completed the coupling between the multi-fluid version of the LFM global magnetosphere model (MFLFM) and the Ionosphere Polar Wind model (IPWM). The resulting coupled model can now effectively simulate terrestrial-sourced heavy ion outflow (O+) and its impact on the reconnection process. The second objective has been achieved through meticulous data-model comparison, which was based on the coupled model developed for Objective 1. By utilizing the outflow mass loading module, we have discovered the significance of the location and intensity of O+ ion outflow in generating magnetospheric sawtooth oscillations. This impact is particularly evident in influencing the rate of magnetopause reconnection, particularly on the dayside. However, it should be noted that for CME storms, the presence of O+ ion outflow is not necessarily a prerequisite for generating the observed sawtooth substorm as detected by satellites. The third objective has been accomplished through theoretical studies on the influence of magnetospheric-sourced plasma on solar wind-magnetosphere coupling. We have employed the coupled model to study space weather events, specifically the start-link event, although the effect of O+ outflow was found to be insignificant. Furthermore, we have utilized the coupled global model to aid in the development of a machine-learning-based framework for space weather prediction.

17300719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17300719.value: Model Development: through the development of this project, we have been collaborating with teams at the National Center for Atmospheric Research and finished the two-way coupling of the multi-fluid global magnetosphere model (MFLFM) and the ionosphere polar wind model (IPWM). This is done by re-writing the coupling interface between the MHD code and the topside ionosphere code (Paper #1 Zhang et al and Paper #2 Pham et al., 2021). The new coupling framework is updated from a file-exchange style into a subroutine type of coupling, which works much faster and more stable during strong driving conditions. The coupled ion outflow global model development is also included in a book chapter (Paper #4 Zhang and Brambles, 2023), while the numerical techniques used through the model development have also been applied to simulate ionospheric ion irregularities (Paper #5, Li, Lei and Zhang, 2021), and planetary O+ ion escape processes (Paper #9, Dang et al., 2022). Scientific findings: 1) Using the outflow module developed through this project, we have studied the impact of O+ ion outflow on magnetotail dynamics and explored a very fundamental magnetospheric physics question on whether O+ ions are required to produce magnetotail sawtooth oscillations (Paper #1 Zhang et al., 2021). Using numerical experiments, we have shown that cusp O+ outflow alone can induce magnetospheric sawtooth oscillations with CME-type driving conditions. 2) Using the two-way coupled magnetosphere-ionosphere simulation (MFLFM-IPWM), we evaluated the importance of ionospheric outflows relative to electrodynamic coupling in the thermosphere’s impact on geospace dynamics. From the ion outflow side, we have found that thermospheric states influence the distributions (Pham et al., 2021), fluxes and other properties of O+ outflows and their feedback on geospace dynamics. This process is also related to the EUV irradiance which manifests the ion composition, shape, symmetries, and magnetic merging of the magnetosphere through changing the dayside and magnetotail reconnection. 3) For space weather applications, we have used the coupled geospace models to show the non-linear response of the cross polar cap potential by influencing the magnetopause and magnetotail reconnection when terrestrial-sourced ions are included in the global model (Paper #3 Yang et al., 2020). We have developed a combined parameter of IMF and solar wind density and other parameters to better incorporate the effects of SW density on the polar cap potential. Moreover, the coupled global model has been used to study the system response of different space weather events (Paper #7, #8 and #9).

17300719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17300719.value: The model development throughout this project research has been the foundation of multi-fluid planetary magnetosphere models that the PI is currently working on. For example, the coupled multi-fluid MHD magnetosphere model has been adapted to other planets such as Venus and Jupiter, and the module for incorporating O+ ion outflow has been adapted to include moon-sourced mass loading processes for simulating the Jovian and Kronian magnetosphere. Moreover, through the collaboration with scientists from the University of Science and Technology of China, a new multi-fluid MHD model of Venus has been developed (Dang et al., 2023). This model is currently under further development for simulating the space environment of Mars.

17300719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17300719.value: We have been working with a team at the National Center for Atmospheric Research to study how the Earth's magnetic field interacts with the atmosphere. We developed a new way to connect two computer models that simulate the different parts of this system, which makes the simulations faster and more accurate. Through our research, we have made some interesting discoveries. We found that a certain type of ion in the atmosphere can cause a specific type of oscillation in the magnetic field, even without other factors present. We also learned that changes in the atmosphere can affect how ions flow out into space, which can in turn affect the magnetic field. Finally, we developed a way to predict how changes in the solar wind and other factors can affect the magnetic field and the atmosphere. This can be useful for understanding space weather and its effects on Earth.

17301319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301319.value: Oxetanes are strained, stereochemically-rich compounds, whose current applications in organic synthesis are largely limited to nucleophilic ring openings for generating acyclic compounds, or ring expansions to heterocycles. Their potential to undergo other types of reactions have not been fully explored or realized. Our preliminary results in investigating oxetane reactivity have provided the first examples of engaging oxetanyl enolsilanes in cycloaddition reactions to form carbocycles. Cycloadditions are efficient strategies for the synthesis of ring compounds, and based on our previous experience in cycloadditions using epoxy enolsilanes, we will further exploit oxetanyl enolsilanes for cycloaddition reactions to generate compounds of a range of ring sizes found in natural products. Studies on oxetanyl enolsilanes provide opportunities to examine the synthesis of novel (4+3) or (3+2) cycloadducts with functional groups normally resulting from umpolung reactivity. Tethering the diene or alkene to the distal position of the oxetane could facilitate the synthesis of cyclooctanoids, thus allowing us to possibly tackle the synthesis of medium-sized 8-membered carbocycles that are particularly challenging to construct due to entropy. Finally, these reactions can generate optically-enriched cycloadducts, as directed by the oxetane stereochemistry, or by exploring their exceptional hydrogen bond accepting ability for chiral acid or chiral anion catalysis. 氧雜環丁烷具有較大環張力及立體中心富集的特性，但其目前在有機合成的應用中僅限於親核性開環製備非環狀化合物及擴環製備雜環化合物。該化合物在其它反應上還未有得到充分的研究。 在探究氧雜環丁烷反應活性上，我們的初步結果證實了該化合物可以應用於環加成反應，合成碳環化合物。近年來，有效構建環狀化合物的環加成反應在有機合成中取得廣泛的應用。基於我們前期對環氧烯醇矽醚應用於環加成反應的研究經驗，我們 將進一步研究環加成反應中氧雜環丁烷烯醇矽醚的活性，獲得一系列在天然產物中的環狀結構。借著對氧雜環丁烷烯醇矽醚研究的機會，我們可以研究因其極性反轉活性構築的新型多官能團的（4+3）或（3+2）環狀產物。將二烯或烯烴連接到遠離氧雜環丁烷一端，可以合成環辛烷類似物。這也有助於我們解決由於熵而難以合成的8元碳環的困難。最後，這些反應可以通過氧雜環丁烷立體化學或者氧雜環丁烷於手性酸或手性陰離子催化劑之間的氫鍵作用，直接產生具有光學活性的環加成產物。

17301319.label: Realisation of objectives
17301319.value: 1. Devising a synthesis for the 2-substituted oxetanes was more challenging than their epoxide counterparts. The syntheses were finally achieved but the route was long, and some of the intermediates were also harder to handle due to the volatility. To tackle the synthetic challenges, we designed 2-substituted azetidinyl enolsilanes as related substrates for the study, and these were synthesized much more readily. Thus we were able to finally synthesize and amass a total of 10 different oxetanyl and azetidinyl enolsilanes for examining their intermolecular (4+3) cycloaddition reactions. 2. The optimizations for the intermolecular cycloaddition are complete and the reagents and conditions are similar to those used for the activation and reaction of the parent epoxy or aziridinyl enolsilanes. We examined the cycloadditions of the nine substrates with a variety of dienes—furan, 2,5-dimethyfuran, cyclopentadiene and 1,3-cyclohexadiene. However, the lower reactivity of the oxetanes and azetidines was such that five out of the ten substrates were almost completely unreactive for cycloaddition. It was found that only the subset of substituted oxetanyl and aziridinyl enolsilanes engaged in cycloaddition reactions efficiently. For these substrates, however, cycloadditions are effective and can occur with yields even up to 96%. These results have resulted in a publication that has been reviewed favorably, and undergoing final revisions. 3. We have designed routes for the synthesis of two series of oxetanyl intramolecular cycloaddition substrates tethered to furans as dienes. One series tethers the enolsilane and the diene at the 2,2-position of the oxetane. A second series tethers the enolsilane and diene at the 2,3-positions of the oxetane. For both of these series, intramolecular cycloadditions proceeded but the yields and diastereoselectivities were much lower than those of the corresponding enolsilanes. Nevertheless, the proof of concept was realized. 4. Synthetic routes for this series of intramolecular cycloaddition substrates in which the enolsilane and the diene is tethered at the 2,4-positions of the oxetane have been explored, but so far, a stereoselective route has not yet been realized. Reasons for under-achievement: This research project was started just as COVID became a local and global issue; the project progress severely delayed due to COVID and its repercussions on the research team, working time and our supply lines. COVID and the subsequent shut-down of traffic in and out of China severely impacted our chemical supplies. In particular, COVID also had an impact on the student who was in charge of this project and its completion. The PhD student enrolled in PhD studies in September 2019, but during his studies, he returned to China multiple times, and additionally, took several long, unpaid leaves—this is on his record. For his PhD, he has already extended his studies more than once. He is originally supposed to complete work and graduate in December 2023—but as of today, he has still not graduated due to delayed progress and productivity. To spur on his progress, a postdoctoral fellow has already been assigned to follow his project and work more closely. To be fair, the student’s research progress was also further impacted by the renovation of our laboratory. The lab renovation left us with no appropriate space to conduct research for 8 months. Even after we moved back into lab, it was still not in full working condition, and the shipping of needed parts for fixtures was delayed due to the lockdown situation in China. In the Appendix, the Technical Manager of the lab renovation project provided a statement describing the renovation of the labs and also the subsequent problems that prevented us from doing research efficiently after moving back in, including a power shortage event that damaged many pieces of equipment. Together with the effects and after-effects of COVID, all these represent a huge percentage of down time that led to the inefficiency in conducting the proposed project and the shortfall to reach the targets. Due to these delays, the research output has been significantly affected, because the publications and conference presentations based on the research results were also late in coming due to the slow progress. The student in the past years has not amassed enough data to present the work on his own in international conferences like his peers in the group.

17301319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301319.value: 1. The synthesis of oxetanyl enolsilanes was explored and were successfully synthesized. They were found to undergo the proposed (4+3) cycloaddition with furans, and cyclopentadienes, and other dienes, under silyl triflate catalysis at low temperatures. The products are cycloadducts with one carbon extended and whose oxidation pattern is an umpolung relationship. The proof of concept has been achieved. Importantly, and in contrast to the epoxides, it was found that only those oxetanyl enolsilanes that are substituted reacted efficiently, in some cases with yields up to 79%. On the other hand, unsubstituted enolsilanes reacted with yields of <20%. This cogently demonstrates the lower reactivity of the oxetanes, compared to the more strained epoxides. 2. Due to the difficulty to prepare oxetanyl enolsilanes, tosylated azetidinyl enolsilanes were designed and examined for reaction, although this was not a part of the original proposal. The azetidinyl enolsilanes were much more readily prepared and we were able to prepare more than half dozen of them. They were also found to react under similar conditions to afford aminated (4+3) cycloadducts. The proof of concept for the (4+3) cycloadditions of azetidinyl enolsilanes has been achieved. Like the oxetanes, only those enolsilanes which are substituted underwent cycloaddition, and with up to 96% yields. Unsubstituted enolsilanes were not observed to yield any cycloadducts. The results of the intermolecular cycloadditions have been written up as a publication for the ACS journal Journal of Organic Chemistry as a full paper; it was reviewed favorably, and should be accepted after revisions. The results will also be presented in the upcoming International Conference on Cutting-edge Organic Chemistry in Asia, in November 2024. 3. One series of intramolecular cycloaddition substrates tethers the enolsilane and the diene geminally at the 2,2-position of the oxetane. These substrates underwent cycloaddition successful, albeit with low endo/exo selectivity. 4. A second series intramolecular cycloaddition substrates tethers the enolsilane and diene vicinally, at the 2,3-positions of the oxetane. Four such substrates were prepared. For this series, intramolecular cycloadditions proceeded but the diastereoselectivities were also lower than for the epoxides. Nevertheless, the proof of concept of intramolecular cycloadditions employing oxetanes was realized. Eventually, these results on the intramolecular cycloaddition should result in an additional publication.

17301319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301319.value: Due to the challenges of synthesizing the appropriately substituted oxetanes and azetidines in a concise manner, the development of novel methods to address these challenges is an additional useful direction for future research.

17301319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301319.value: The efficient synthesis of carbocyclic frameworks is an important goal in organic synthesis of many target molecules including natural products and bioactive compounds. For the less accessible seven-member carbocycles, we have been exploring (4+3) cycloadditions as a convergent and direct route towards these structures. Extending our previous work on epoxides and aziridines as the strained component in the reactive precursor, we have now demonstrated that oxetanes and azetidines, the four-membered ring analogues, can also be substrates for (4+3) cycloadditions with dienes such as furan, cyclopentadiene and cyclohexadiene. Due to the attenuated strain, substituted enolsilanes are needed to activate oxetanes and azetidines for efficient reactions. However, under the optimized conditions, these (4+3) cycloadditions can occur with up to 96% yields.

17301519.label: Project Objectives
17301519.value: To establish conditions for unique identification of a PBN with three classes of Boolean functions and theory for sample complexity. To propose novel definitions for stable attractors, and design controllers for the identification of BNs/PBNs with stable attractors and network structures. To develop efficient and robust algorithms for identifying the minimum set of nodes to discriminate attractors in a BN with noisy nodes, and provide a complexity analysis for the proposed algorithms. To apply the developed results in three real-world problems: biomarkers identification, healthcare service management, and default risk modeling.

17301519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301519.value: Boolean network (BN) and its extension probabilistic Boolean network (PBN) have been widely used in studying genetic regulatory networks, manufacturing systems and credit risk models because they are able to capture the logical interactions and characterize their steady-state behaviors. Three major identification problems in BNs/PBNs will be studied in this project. Efficient algorithms together with complexity theory will be developed and established for the captured problems. We first focus on identifying the structure of a PBN from a small number of observations under two models, i.e., full information and partial information models. Then, identification problem with network stability in the presence of noise will be studied, and strategies for designing controllers will be proposed to identify stable network structures. Finally, the network behaviors are analyzed by identifying the minimum number of nodes to discriminate different attractors. The project results are expected to show that a small set of sensor nodes will be good enough to discriminate different attractors. To demonstrate the applicability and impact of our results, the proposed theory and methods will be applied to three real-world problems: biomarkers identification, healthcare service management, and default risk modeling.

17301519.label: Realisation of objectives
17301519.value: In Sun et al. (2020, 2021) [1,7], we investigate the global stability of Boolean control networks (BCNs) under aperiodic sampled data control (ASDC). It is known that a BCN under ASDC can be transformed into a switched Boolean network (SBN), and further global stability of the BCN under ASDC can be obtained by studying the global stability of the transformed SBN. The SBN can also be stable with appropriate switching laws designed, even if all subsystems are unstable. We proposed a novel method for the global stochastic stability analysis of aperiodic sampled-data Boolean control networks (BCNs). A sufficient condition for the global stochastic stability of BCNs under ASDC is provided. In Cheng et al. (2021) [9], we study the observation problem of the internal state of a Boolean network (BN) using a small number of sensor nodes. We focus on the problem of determining the minimum number of sensor nodes for discriminating attractors under the assumption that each attractor has at most K noisy nodes. We present exact and approximation algorithms for the minimization problem. The effectiveness of the algorithms is also demonstrated by numerical experiments using both synthetic and real data. In Sun and Ching (2022) [14], stabilization and reconstruction of sampled-data BCNs under noisy sampling interval is studied. A sampled-data BCN under noisy sampling interval is first converted into a probabilistic Boolean network (PBN). We obtain some necessary and sufficient conditions for global stochastic stability of the considered sampled-data BCN under two types of noisy sampling intervals. Moreover, based on the given steady-state probabilities of the transformed PBN, the reconstruction problem of large-scaled sampled data BCNs under noisy sampling interval can be well solved as a linear programming problem. In Sun et al. (2023) [18], we investigate the synchronization design problem for both BNs and singular BNs. The problem for designing state observers can be transformed into the problem of constructing response (singular) BNs that achieve synchronization with a given real (singular) BN, and the gain matrix of the designed state observer can be obtained by solving a matrix equation. In Guo et al. (2022) [10], we study the distribution of successor states in a BN of n nodes. We focus on BNs consisting of three classes of functions: exclusive OR (XOR) functions, canalyzing functions, and threshold functions. We show that there exists a BN consisting of d-ary XOR functions which preserves the entropy if d is odd and n > d, whereas there does not exist such a BN if d is even. In Melkman et al. (2022) [13], we explore the compressive power of autoencoders that are Boolean threshold networks by studying the numbers of nodes and layers that are required to ensure that each vector in a given set of distinct input binary vectors is transformed back to its original. It is shown that for any set of n distinct vectors there exists a seven-layer autoencoder with the optimal compression ratio, but that there is a set of n vectors for which there is no three-layer autoencoder with a middle layer of logarithmic size. In addition, we present a kind of tradeoff: if the compression ratio is allowed to be considerably larger than the optimal, then there is a five-layer autoencoder. Our results also suggest that the decoding part is the bottleneck of autoencoding. In Xiao et al. (2022, 2022) [11,12], we consider the construction of a sparse PBN from given experimental data. A modified orthogonal matching pursuit is proposed for solving the problem and we provide some conditions under which the proposed algorithm can recover a sparse PBN. We then extend our algorithm to solving sparse nonnegative matrix factorization problems for stochastic matrices. The proposed algorithms are shown to be convergent globally. Numerical experiments on both synthetic and real data sets are given to demonstrate their effectiveness. In Qiu et al. (2021) [5,6], we consider clustering tumor metastasis samples from gene expression data when the number of experimental samples is small and the number of genes is huge. We focus on the prediction of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), novel models are proposed for predicting EMT based on multi-dimensional scaling, integrating entropy and random matrix detection and inductive matrix completion, to determine the optimal reduced number of dimension in low dimensional space. In Qiu et al. (2022) [8], a novel method for RBP-AS target prediction is proposed based on weighted data fusion with sparse matrix tri-factorization simultaneously decomposes heterogeneous data source matrices into low-rank matrices to reveal hidden associations. Our proposed method can effectively predict RBP-AS event associations with higher accuracy than existing methods. In Sun et al. (2023) [15], we consider a pseudo-temporal causality-based Bayesian approach to identify EMT-associated regulatory relationships of AS events and RBPs during breast cancer progression. Our study sheds light on facilitating the regulatory network-based approach to identify key RNA-binding proteins or target alternative splicing events. In Li et al. (2023) [16], we propose a novel embedded Boolean threshold network method called LogBTF, which effectively infers gene regulatory networks by integrating regularized logistic regression and Boolean threshold function. To overcome the multi-collinearity and over-fitting problems, an effective approach is designed to optimize the network topology by adding a perturbation design matrix to the input data. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of LogBTF method. In Zhao et al. (2023) [17], we extend the traditional structural equation modelling (SEM) framework by considering a flexible noise modelling strategy. We employ the Gaussian mixtures to approximate the complex stochastic nature of a biological system. Numerical results indicate that the strategy can improve the performance of traditional Gaussian SEM model and NG-SEM outperforms other state-of-the-art methods. In Leung et al. (2021) [3], we study a healthcare problem. We proposed models for planning the optimal size and mix of nursing teams and scheduling in nursing homes and solved the integrated nursing staff demand modelling and scheduling problem. A case study of a subvented nursing home in Hong Kong was conducted to illustrate the effectiveness of the model and framework. Results show that the total overtime work (in hours) was minimized, while the nurse-to-resident ratios were significantly improved. In Guo et al. (2020, 2021) [2,4], a fuzzy portfolio selection model is considered with a view to incorporating ambiguity about model and data structure. A bi-objective mean-variance model is formulated, and a time varying numerical integral-based particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed to solve the efficient frontier of the portfolio in the sense of Pareto dominance. The results are extended to case that the market state follows a high-order Markov chain. The research results have been published in top and leading international journals such as Automatica, Bioinformatics, Briefings in Bioinformatics, IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, PloS Computational Biology, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications, Technological Forecasting & Social Change, etc.

17301519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17301519.value: We proposed a novel method for analyzing global stochastic stability of aperiodic sampled-data Boolean control networks (BCNs) with a sufficient condition for the global stochastic stability (Sun et al., 2020, 2021). In (Ching and Sun 2022), some necessary and sufficient conditions are obtained for the stabilization of sampled-data BCNs under noisy sampling interval and a linear programming based algorithm was developed for solving the reconstruction problem. We proposed novel methods for designing state observers for both BNs and singular BNs. Efficient exact and approximation algorithms, with complexity analysis, were developed for the observation problem of determining the minimum number of sensor nodes for discriminating attractors (Cheng et al., 2021). In (Guo et al. 2022), we studied distribution of successor states in BNs in terms of preservation of the entropy for three classes of Boolean functions. It provides insights for analyzing how entropy is kept and lost in layered neural networks and gene regulatory networks, and the mechanism of information encoding and decoding in autoencoders. The compressive power of autoencoders that are Boolean threshold networks was studied in (Melkman et al., 2022), it is shown that for any set of n distinct vectors there exists a seven-layer autoencoder with the optimal compression ratio, but that there is a set of n vectors for which there is no three-layer autoencoder with a middle layer of logarithmic size. In (Xiao et al., 2022, 2022), a modified orthogonal matching pursuit was proposed for constructing a sparse PBN under some conditions The idea was then extended to solving sparse nonnegative matrix factorization problems for stochastic matrices. The proposed algorithms are shown to be convergent globally. A novel embedded Boolean threshold network method, LogBTF, was proposed in (Li et al. 2023) which can effectively infer gene regulatory networks by integrating regularized logistic regression and Boolean threshold function. Effective matrix completion and sparse factorization methods are proposed for the prediction of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) (Qiu et al. 2021, 2022, Sun et al. 2023). In (Leung et al. 2021), we proposed models for planning the optimal size and mix of nursing teams in nursing homes, and solved the integrated nursing staff demand modelling and scheduling problem. The research results have been published in top and leading international journals such as Automatica, Bioinformatics, Briefings in Bioinformatics, IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems, PLoS Computational Biology, SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications.

17301519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17301519.value: Currently, we still have two Ph.D. students working in the research project. We shall continue working on (i) designing efficient algorithms for the construction of sparse probabilistic Boolean networks, (ii) inferring gene regulatory networks by constructing Boolean threshold network models, (iii) analyzing sparse single-cell RNA sequence data by using and developing non-negative matrix factorization methods.

17301519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17301519.value: Probabilistic Boolean network (PBN) is a useful mathematical model (framework) which employs rule-based representation for the modelling of complex biological networks with uncertainty such as genetic regulatory networks. In this project, we have obtained a better understanding of PBNs and their relations to control theory, dynamical systems, and numerical algorithms, etc. Novel and efficient numerical algorithms have been proposed for the construction, discrimination and identification of PBNs with various applications. We have also established mathematical theory and complexity analyses for the proposed numerical algorithms. The performance of the algorithms was also confirmed by numerical experiments with both synthetic and practical data sets. The project has also generated new challenging research directions with potential applications for further investigation.

17301619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17301619.value: We propose to design and synthesize different types of conjugated polymers incorporated with metal complexes on the main chain. Conjugated polymers are known to have application potentials as photoconductors, light emitters, and sensing materials. They have been demonstrated to be the active materials in organic solar cells with high efficiency. In addition, conjugated polymers can also be use as dispersants for carbon nanotubes, which are extremely difficult to form stable suspension in solution due to the strong interaction between different nanotube bundles. Here we propose to incorporate metal complexes with planar geometry into conjugated polymer main chains such that the resulting materials able to disperse carbon nanotube due to the specific geometry of the complex. For transition metal complexes, it is also well known that they exhibit highly interesting photophysical and electrochemical properties. Therefore, it will be very interesting to study how the electronic interaction between the metal complexes and conjugated polymer systems. By using a variety of spectroscopic characterization techniques, we hope we will be able to follow how the excited species are formed and decay upon photoexcitation. In addition, we will also attempt to study the interaction between the metal complexes and carbon nanotubes, and the role of metal complexes in the dispersion process. In the later stage, we will conduct preliminary studies on the use of our the target polymers for the dispersion of other 2-D nanomaterials such as graphene, and the application potentials of applying the hybrid materials for light driven multi-electron catalysis. 17302019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302019.value: Quantum key distribution (QKD) --- the art of sending provably secure keys by quantum mechanical means --- has moved from pure theoretical studies using ideal apparatus in the infinite sifted key length limit to practical investigation and experimental demonstration using realistic apparatus in the finite sifted key length situation. Powerful techniques such as decoy state, measurement-device-independence, smooth entropy and very lately twin field method have been developed; and both ground- and satellite-based QKD experiments have been reported. Here I plan to compare the optimized secret key rates of various qubit- and qudit-based QKD protocols, old or new, over long distances without the use of quantum repeaters using lately developed techniques including twin field, more than three decoy state intensities and McDiarmid inequality as well as more aggressive treatment of fluctuation of the quantum channel due to factors such as atmospheric turbulence, cloud and haze beyond the simple rejection of data with low signal to noise ratio. 量子密鑰分發（QKD）是通過量子力學發送可證明安全密鑰的技術手段。QKD已經從純粹的理論研究逐漸變成而實驗與理論相結合的科學。強大的技術手法，如誘餌狀態，測量裝置獨立性，平滑熵和最近的雙胞胎場方法已經開發出來。通過衛星的QKD實驗已被發表。在這裡，我計劃比較優化各種基於qubit和qudit的QKD安全密鑰傳遞率，包括在雙胞胎場，超過三個誘餌狀態強度和利用McDiarmid不平等以及對於大氣湍流，雲和湍流等因素引起的量子雜信作更主動的處理。

17302019.label: Realisation of objectives
17302019.value: Atmospheric turbulence lower the signal transmission rate in free-space optical communication. Although many works have been done for the cases of static or nearly static sources, effective ways to deal with the case of rapidly moving sources have not been intensively studied. This project succeeded in solving the problem of satellite to ground downlink optical communication for moving sources. The idea is that we spatially separate the beacon beam and the signal beam on the satellite so that the beacon beam is placed slightly ahead of the signal beam along the direction of motion of the satellite. The adaptive optics system in the ground-based detection system can be used to compensate the atmospheric turbulence of the beacon beam. The prototype idea was discovered in the first half of this grant period. More refined analysis, improvements and explanations were done in the second half of this grant period. The most important innovation of this second half period was the following discoveries. By suitably choosing the spatial separation and the delay time between the beacon and the signal beams, this adaptive optics compensation protocol can correct the turbulence effect of the signal beam, too. The beauty of this scheme is that it works for signal beam of any intensity provided that the intensity of the beacon beam is strong enough for reliable estimation of the signal disturbance. Hence, the method works not just for quantum communication as stated in the first objective. It also works for classical communication system as well as airplane to ground communication. Along the same line, the secure key rate of this setup in standard decoy state quantum key distribution has been computed using standard atmospheric turbulence models. For satellites within 30^circ from the zenith, the downlink key rate increases by at least 21.5% and 40% when the satellite altitudes are 400 and 800 km, respectively. This fulfills partially the objective 2 of this proposal. These results have been published in AIP Advances. In fact, it was picked as one of the editor's highlights in that issue. Since this finding is clearly of commercial value, patent applications have been filed to the PCT shortly before the end of the first half of the grant period. A revised PCT was filed about a year later. And to fully protect our IPR, patent applications had been filed to the relevant authorities in China, Canada, Europe, Japan, Taiwan and the USA.

17302019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302019.value: Together with my ex-graduate student, we discover a way to use adaptive optics to combat atmospheric turbulence in satellite to ground (technically called the downlink) communication that is effective for moving targets. Most importantly, this method works for both classical and quantum communication. It works in the case of airplane to ground communication as well. Furthermore, the faster the angular speed of the satellite moves relative to the detector on the ground, the better our method. In addition, by performing standard decoy state quantum key distribution in this way, the provably secure key rate can increase by at least 21.5% and 40% for satellite within 30^circ from zenith with satellite altitudes of 400 and 800 km, respectively. Our findings has been published in AIP Advances. In fact, it was selected as one of the editor's highlights in that issue. This finding clearly has potential commercial value. Hence, we have filed to the PCT and recently formally applied for patent protection in regions that are currently very active in quantum communication research, namely, Canada, China, Europe, Japan, Taiwan and the USA.

17302019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302019.value: Further refining the scheme to the case of ground to satellite (that is, the so-called uplink) communication as well as further methods to increase the quantum communication key rate in realistic satellite communications should be done. In fact, my ex-student, who is now working in the Canadian Research Council, will take up part of this project as Canada has more experience on the actual optical communication setup using adaptive optics. In fact, to continue this project requires actual experimental data that cannot be done in Hong Kong as we do not have such kind of setup and engineering know-how. Another direction is the commercialization of this concept. We are trying to contact relevant industries to explore various possibilities from patent licensing to collaborative works on further improvements.

17302019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302019.value: Atmospheric turbulence can greatly reduce the communication rate. This is particularly true when the source is moving rapidly. In this project, we discovered an adaptive optics based method to reduce the effect of atmospheric turbulence on the communication rate for both classical and quantum optical communications from satellite to ground. This method is particularly effective for low earth orbit satellites that move quickly relative to the ground. We are filing patents in Canada, China, Europe, Japan, Taiwan and the USA to protect our rights. And we plan to commercialize this idea by exploring possibilities of industrial collaborations and patent licensing.

17302119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302119.value: 聯合國教科文(UNESCO)世界文化遺產是全世界全人類 不同文明的重要文化文明載體和記錄見證。 其中曾於9至12世紀達到鼎盛的覆蓋著現在東南亞大部分地區的古高棉文明， 歷經數代帝王建立了大量的恢弘的城市和瑰麗的建築並且其中許多遺跡存留至今。其中最為當今世人所知的遺跡包括有吳哥窟和吳哥大城的巴戎寺。這些遺跡和寺廟因為其表面精美的砂岩石刻壁畫極具觀賞和研究價值而使它們成為了記錄著古高棉文明輝煌歷史的極珍貴的文化遺產。1992年，這些古高棉文明吳哥時期的遺址建築被正式列入聯合國教科文組織世界文化遺產名錄，並在當年開始立即啟動了針對遺址的保護和修復。由日本政府資助的研究團隊主要負責吳哥大城中巴戎寺的考古和保護工作；而微生物的研究是該項研究工作的重要組成部分。 砂岩的侵蝕退化受材料的物理結構和化學組成影響，也包括多孔材料上水的反復侵染和微生物群落的定殖等共同作用。吳哥大城裡的巴戎寺表面覆蓋著具有不同生理特徵和適應功能的微生物所構成的微生物群落並且在其表面顯現著斑斕多樣的顏色。這些微生物群落中的產酸的硫氧化細菌和真菌對砂岩材料最開始的酸性腐蝕至少部分地與其砂岩建材的退化崩解過程相關。在現柬埔寨境內的吳哥窟、巴戎寺及其他的遺址中均可以觀察到這一現象。另外， 在巴戎寺中仍有屋頂存留的砂岩石刻壁畫長廊中發現有高濃度的硝酸鹽的累積，而氨和亞硝酸鹽卻並沒有發現累積；但相對應無屋頂壁畫長廊中則沒有觀察到這三種氮化物累積。這一現象在近年的研究中證實。自然界將氨鹽氧化成硝酸鹽的過程主要由氨氧化古菌（AOA）和氨氧化細菌（AOB）來完成。在針對若干吳哥遺址的微生物研究中，均檢測到了高豐度的氨氧化古菌（AOA）而氨氧化細菌（AOB）的豐度則相對非常的低甚至未能檢測到。近期使用穩定同位素-氮15技術的研究發現，氮的去除過程在遺跡表面的微生物群落中相對較弱。這一結果表明遺跡表面的硝酸鹽生化去除過程要相對弱於硝酸鹽的生化產生，從而導致了這些砂岩遺跡表面的硝酸鹽的大量累積。 因此，對於導致石質遺跡退化的硝酸鹽累積過程的基礎認識和參與該累積過程的微生物及其生理生化過程的認識將有利於未來制定更合理有效文物保護措施和策略。該研究的目的在於：1）在轉錄水準對參與硝酸鹽生成過程的氨氧化細菌和古菌的基因豐度和參與硝酸鹽去除過程的反硝化和厭氧氨氧化的微生物的基因豐度進行定量；2）通過二代深度測序技術獲取微生物群落和組成信息；3）通過氮-15穩定同位素標記技術研究反硝化過程和厭氧氨氧化過程在硝酸鹽去除過程中的貢獻率。該研究所得到的結果將有利於更深入的瞭解吳哥砂岩遺跡表面硝酸鹽累積現象的生理生化基礎並且提供更合理有效文物保護措施和策略。這些結果將在類似的石質文物退化的防治維護領域有廣闊的應用前景.

17302119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302119.value: The general characteristics of the microbiome on these monuments were revealed, and the association between the environmental geo-ecological feature and the indigenous microbiome was delineated. The most common microbial groups included 6 phyla, namely Acidobacteria, Actinobacteria, Gemmatimonadetes, Nitrospirae, Proteobacteria and Verrucomicrobia on the monuments. In particular, functions associated with photosynthesis and UV resistance were identified from geographical locations on Angkor monuments. The distribution of key microbial determinants responsible for stone deterioration was linked to survival under extreme environmental conditions and biochemical capabilities and reactions. Among them, biochemical reactions of the microbial nitrogen and sulfur cycles were most predominant. These stone-dwelling microbiomes on historical stone monuments were highly diverse and self-sustaining driven by energy metabolism and biomass accumulation. And metabolic products of the internal geomicrobiological nitrogen cycling on these ancient monuments play a unique role in the biodeterioration of stone monuments. The genetic information on the presence of acid-producing processes by sulfur- and ammonia oxidizing bacteria and archaea in this metagenomic dataset suggested that the microbial flora in these samples has the potential to participate in the degradation of sandstone cultural heritage by producing acids. These results highlight the significance of identifying the essential microbial biochemical reactions to advance the understanding of stone biodeterioration for protection management. Our metagenomics datasets on these monuments reveal a rich microbiome and abundant microbial nitrogen transforming reactions of ammonia oxidation and nitrite oxidation, Comammox and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA), and these results support an internal recycling mechanism between ammonia/ammonium and nitrate by AOA, AOB, Comammox and DNRA on the stone monuments to support the microbial community. Though a wide range of AOB and AOA lineages together with Comammox were retrieved from these metagenomes as the potential ammonia-oxidizers, only AOA and Comammox were most abundant, likely to contribute to the biochemical processes of ammonia oxidation. The RNA-based qPCR quantification of the functional gene amoA in this study showed that AOA were the more active ammonia oxidizers over AOB in the microbiome of these Angkor sandstone monuments. In addition, a rich population of nitrite/nitrate producing AOA and Comammox drove the sequestration of CO2 onto the stone and this process was in turn supported by DNRA to provide the substrate ammonia/ammonium for a further cyclic reaction to take place continuously between ammonia/ammonium and nitrate. N-15 isotope amendment and incubation analysis results confirmed the low active of denitrification at Angkor monuments. These results are important for our knowledge on the microbial community composition and microbial biodeterioration processes affecting this sandstone cultural heritage and will aid in the protection and management of the ancient Angkor monuments. This model is further supported by the high enrichment of stable isotope 15N signature of NO3− in sandstone surface biofilms. The findings of our study are insightful for elucidation of nitrate accumulation by an internal N cycling mechanism proposed, and are important for understanding the sustainable microbial community and protection management of stone cultural heritage.

17302119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302119.value: The Angkor Archaeological Park covers a vast area and is in a tropical monsoon jungle environment, with microbial communities actively thriving on these Angor monuments. The study need to be conducted on typical Angkor monuments exposed to different intensities of tourism development. The response features of microbiome to environmental, geographic, and ecological factors; and the responsive microbial taxa and their functional traits that can indicate the effects of environmental factors on these monuments need to be revealed. The microbial signatures of potential health risks on these Angkor monuments need to be revealed.

17302119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302119.value: The colossal stone monuments in the Angkor Archaeological Park are world-renowned for being of significant historical and artistic value. The presence of acid-producing processes by sulfur- and ammonia oxidizing bacteria and archaea in the microbial flora on Angkor monuments has the potential to participate in the degradation of sandstone cultural heritage by producing acids. A rich population of nitrite/nitrate producing AOA and Comammox drove the sequestration of CO2 onto the stone and this process was in turn supported by DNRA to provide the substrate ammonia/ammonium for a further cyclic reaction to take place continuously between ammonia/ammonium and nitrate. The findings of our study are insightful for elucidation of nitrate accumulation by an internal N cycling mechanism proposed, and are important for understanding the sustainable microbial community and protection management of stone cultural heritage.

17302419.label: Project Objectives
17302419.value: Synthesize the new Dumbbell-shaped (Weight and Bar) Pt-containing oligomers with different bar length and study the spectroscopic properties of oligomers by the femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA), femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence (fs-TRF), nanosecond time-resolved transient absorption (ns-TA) and nanosecond time-resolved emission (ns-EM). Comparing the differences between the oligomers with a well-studied model Pt complex, especially their photophyscial properties. Those results will be the benchmark to better understand the effect of the Bar length on the exciton diffusion mechanism for further study as shown below. DFT and Time-dependent DFT will be employed to estimate the electronic configuration and orbital distribution for the Dumbbell-shaped Pt-containing oligomers with different Bar chain length. These results will help better elucidate the mechanism of the exciton transfer process induced by the photoexcitation. Design the Dumbbell-shaped Pt-containing complexes with different Bar structures and study the spectroscopic properties of those system by similar time-resolved spectroscopic methods and DFT calculations. Comparing the differences between the exciton diffusion rates with the results obtained in objective 1. These results will help us to better elucidate the effects of the Bar structures on the exciton diffusion mechanisms. Synthesize the metal complexes, like Ru complexes, Ir complexes. Investigate the photophysical properties by employing the fs-TA, ns-TA, fs-TRF and ns-EM. This part of our project will focus on the ISC rates and the lifetime of the triplets and the complexes with faster ISC process and longer triplet lifetime will be selected to be the new Weight in the Dumbbell-shaped systems for further study. New Dumbbell-shaped Ru-containing, Ir-containing complexes and oligomers by employing the new Weight and Bar structures will be synthesized according to objectives 1-4. Fs-TA, fs-TRF, ns-TA and ns-EM will be employed to study the triplet diffusion process and calculate the diffusion length of those oligomers. These results will help better elucidate the triplet exciton transfer mechanism. Nanosecond time-resolved resonance Raman (ns-TR3) will be employed to acquire the vibrational information for the triplet excitons after excitation. The Raman spectra will bring more geometric information for the involved transient species. If time and resources permit, the most potential Dumbbell-shaped system obtained from objectives 1-6 will be selected to be the triplet sensitizer with suitable accepter for the triplet-triplet annihilation (TTA) photon upconversion approach. These experiments will provide deeper insights into the application for the converting low energy solar energy photons into higher energy photons.

17302419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302419.value: 近日，三重態光敏劑在材料、能源和光生物領域得到了廣泛地關注。與單重態光敏劑相比，具有較高三重態量子產率的有機材料在光伏裝置表現特性上具有更優異的性能，主要是因為其較長的壽命和光子傳播長度。儘管如此，針對三重態光敏劑的光子傳輸機制的相關研究卻十分有限。因此，我們認為設計並合成一系列新型的三重態光敏化合物，並且研究其三重態激子的遷徙過程具有十分重要的意義。在本研究計劃中，我們設計了新型的槓鈴式結構的金屬鉑、釕以及銥配合物體系，此類新型的槓鈴式結構不僅可以延伸體系的吸收光譜寬度，同時還擁有“鈴”和“槓”兩部分髮色團。該體系的設計初衷是利用“鈴”和“槓”結構的特殊性實現定量的能量轉移和激發態光激子轉移。同時我們可以利用飛秒時間分辨吸收光譜和飛秒時間分辨熒光光譜技術直接捕捉該槓鈴體系的單重激發態、三重激發態、係間穿越和光激子轉移等光引導過程。該創新性的研究可以幫助我們更好地理解該體系光物理過程和其化學結構的關係和相關機理。緊接著，我們將利用納秒時間分辨吸收光譜和時間分辨發射光譜同時研究該槓鈴式的金屬配合物體系的相關光譜特征。此外，時間分辨共振拉曼和密度泛函理論計算將被用來採集該槓鈴體系的指紋特征信息。這些實驗和計算結果可以幫助我們更好的理解“鈴”和“槓”結構對槓鈴式的金屬配合物的光物理過程的影響。因此，本研究計劃可以幫助我們更好地設計新型的三重態光敏集光材料，該材料不僅可以更有效地利用光能，同時可以更好地抑制光電轉化過程中的能量損失。

17302419.value: For Objectives 1, 2 and 3 we have performed femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA), nanosecond time-resolved transient absorption (ns-TA), timeresolved resonance Raman (nsTR3) and other methods to characterize the spectroscopic properties of selected diarylnitrenium ions in various solvents and also their reactions with nucleobases like guanosine time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA) and spectroscopies in a variety of solvents. We also compared these new results to investigate the differences between the diarylnitrenium ions with the more well-studied arylnitrenium ions literature results. We have demonstrated that diarylnintreniums react with guanosine at a different position (N7) to form a different intermediate compared to singlet arylnitrenium ions studied in the literature which attack guanosine at the C8 position to produce C8 intermediates. However, these different reaction pathways and intermediates both lead to formation of C8 adduct final products. In addition to address Objective 4, we have done DFT and time-dependent DFT computations to examine the reaction pathways for the diarylnitrenium ions reacting with selected DNA bases and compared these results to the experimental data above. These new experimental and computational results for diarylnitrenium ions have addressed Objectives 1, 2, 3 and 4 and have been reported mostly in publications 1, 2 and 3 of this report. For Objectives 5 and 6, we performed time-resolved spectros For Objective 1 we have synthesized the new Dumbbell-shaped (Weight and Bar) Pt-containing oligomers with different bar length. We next examined the spectroscopic properties of these new oligomers using femtosecond time-resolved transient absorption (fs-TA), femtosecond time-resolved fluorescence (fs-TRF), nanosecond time-resolved transient absorption (ns-TA) and nanosecond time-resolved emission (ns-EM and compared the differences between the oligomers with a well-studied model Pt complex, especially their photophyscial properties to become a model prototype to better elucidate the effect of the Bar length on the exciton diffusion mechanism. For Objective 2, we performed DFT and Time-dependent DFT computations to simulate the electronic configuration and orbital distribution for the Dumbbell-shaped Pt-containing oligomers with different Bar chain length to deeper understand the mechanism of the exciton transfer process induced by the photoexcitation. For Objective 3, we examined the spectroscopic properties of those system by similar time-resolved spectroscopic methods and DFT calculations. Comparing the differences between the exciton diffusion rates with the results obtained in objective 1. These results will help us to better elucidate the effects of the Bar structures on the exciton diffusion mechanisms. These new experimental and computational results for diarylnitrenium ions have addressed Objectives 1, 2, 3 and have been reported mostly in publications 1, 2, 3 and 4 of this report. For Objective 4, we synthesized and characterized selected target metal complexes, like Ru complexes, Ir complexes. Investigated their photophysical properties by using the fs-TA, ns-TA, fs-TRF and ns-EM. This part of our project examined the ISC rates and the lifetimes of the triplets and the complexes with faster ISC process and longer triplet lifetimes that were then will be used to be the new Weight in the Dumbbell-shaped systems for further investigation. For Objective 5, we next employed these new Dumbbell-shaped Ru-containing, Ir-containing complexes and oligomers as the new Weight and Bar structures will be synthesized according to objectives 1-4. Fs-TA, fs-TRF, ns-TA and ns-EM will be employed to study the triplet diffusion process and computed the diffusion length of those oligomers. These results gave insight into the triplet exciton transfer mechanism in these new systems of interest. These new experimental and computational results have addressed Objectives 4 and 5 and have been reported mostly in publications 4, 8 and 9 of this report. For Objective 6, we have performed nanosecond time-resolved resonance Raman (ns-TR3) to obtain the vibrational information for the triplet excitons after excitation and these Raman spectra provide more geometric information for the involved transient species. For Objective 7, we have extended our work and results to explore related systems for experiments that provide deeper insights into the applications for photocatalysis of hydrogen from water and also the upconversion of low energy solar energy photons into higher energy photons. These new experimental and computational results have addressed Objectives 6 and 7 and have been reported mostly in publications 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12 of this report.

17302419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302419.value: Tetraphenylethylene (TPE) was the was the first reported aggregation induced emission generator (AIEgen) and has been studied a lot to better understand its AIE properties and applications. Recently, hybrid materials combining TPE with metals have received much interest and present a new opportunity for new applications and intriguing properties to use. In particular, we become interested in the lack of research looking into studies of the triplet excited state properties of TPE or TPE involved compounds. The research supported by this grant here initially and systematically explored the photophysical properties of TPE containing Pt(II) acetylide complexes by employing UV−vis absorption spectroscopy, resonance Raman spectroscopy, fs-TA, ns-TA and quantum chemical simulations. The RR spectra found structural evidence for the coexistence of two MLCT electronic transition states [dπ(Pt) → π*(tpy/bpy) and dπ(Pt) → π*(TPE)] after 368.9 nm excitation. The photophysical processes of Pt-3 after excitation were schematically investigated and elucidated to be two diﬀerent 3MLCT [dπ(Pt) → π*(tpy/bpy) and dπ(Pt) → π*(TPE)] excited states with diﬀerent characters are observed directly. The TPE involved triplet excited states, 3MLCT [dπ(Pt) → π*(TPE)] excited states, are short-lived triplet excited states (<50 ns), that are mostly due to the intramolecular rotations of the phenyl rings of TPE and this research gives solid evidence with promising demonstrations on TPE based triplet excited state properties that can give rise to new kinds of TPE based materials that contain a ﬂexible molecular design of TPE based chromophores. Another major finding of this project was the design and synthesis and characterization of new push−pull ligands (L1 and L2) with bithiophene (bth) as a donor and phenazine (phz) or quinoxalino[2,3-b]quinoxaline (qxq) as acceptors were synthesized and also incorporated with a bipyridyl Ru(II) complex to give Ru1 and Ru2, respectively. We performed ultrafast time-resolved spectroscopy experiments to characterize the photophysical properties of of the ligand and their respective Ru(II) complexes were and also did quantum chemical calculations to better understand the results. Photoinduced charger transfer (CT) and intersystem crossing (ISC) processes were directly observed for L1 and L2 and the interplay of three different triplet excited states were directly seen in these new Ru(II) complexes. The lowest-lying triplet excited states of the ligands and their respective Ru(II) complexes were assigned to the CT transitions from donor (bth) to acceptor (phz or qxq) and give rise tp 3ICT (intramolecular charge transfer) and 3ILCT (intraligand charge transfer) excited states, respectively.

17302419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302419.value: In this project we have prepared and characterized a number of new complexes that consist of dumbell shaped bar and weight structured complexes of varying sizes that contain Pt or Ru or Ir metals that can be used for applications for upconversion of low energy photons to high energy photons and also for photocatalysis of water to hydrogen generation processes. We used a number of experimental methods including time-resolved spectroscopic techniques to study the photophysical properties of these new systems and related these to their structures and properties. There is still much potential to continue research in this area and extend it into several new directions. First, one can begin to investigate new metals that can be employed in related complexes for comparison to previously studied systems. Second, new ligand systems may be employed to prepare new complexes and examine them to see if they have improved properties or not. Third, new applications can be investigated for related complexes. For example, Singlet fission processes and other photocatalysis reactions may be studied in the future.

17302419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302419.value: In this project we synthesized and characterized a number of different Pt, Ru and Ir metal containing complexes with varying dumbbell structures of selected bar and weights ligands. We further studied their key photophysical properties with several kinds of time-resolved spectroscopy methods and computational techniques. Thee studies gained more insight into the structure and properties relationships for the photohysical properties of these complexes in particular for the formation of relative triplet states that could be utilized for energy conversion processes of solar light like triplet-triplet upconversion and photocatalysis of water to produce hydrogen fuel. This work can be expanded and extended in the future to improve related complexes for these types of applications.
