17302919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17302919.value: X-chromosome inactivation and genomic imprinting are two important epigenetic factors in the study of complex traits. X-chromosome inactivation is the mechanism by which gene dosage compensation is achieved between male mammals with a single copy of the X-chromosome and female mammals with two copies of the X-chromosome by inactivation of one of the two copies of the X-chromosome during early embryonic development. Genomic imprinting, also known as the ‘parent-of-origin’ effect, is an epigenetic phenomenon where certain genes are expressed depending on their parental origin. It is believed that about 1% of all mammalian genes are imprinted. Imprinting effects have been demonstrated in diseases such as Angelman syndrome, Turner’s syndrome and mental disorders. In the literature, statistical methods have been constructed to investigate these two epigenetic factors individually. However, no statistical tests are available yet for jointly studying both factors. In this project, we will fill the gap by proposing statistical tests for association on the X-chromosome accounting for the two epigenetic factors, X-inactivation and imprinting. Both common and rare variants will be considered. Moreover, qualitative (binary) as well as quantitative (continuous) traits will be investigated. Based on the constructed regression models, we aim to establish a theoretical and empirical framework for X-chromosome association testing of common and rare variants, allowing for different degrees of X-inactivation and imprinting. Finally, we will apply the proposed methods to analyze real data sets such as for rheumatoid arthritis and type 2 diabetes. 在研究X染色體相關的複雜性狀時，X染色體失活以及染色體印記是兩個重要的表觀遺傳因素。 X染色體失活發生在女性哺乳類動物的胚胎發育早期，期間女性的兩條X染色體之中的一條發生失活，從而使女性的兩條X染色體與男性的一條X染色體在基因表達水平上達到了劑量補償。染色體印記（也稱作親源效應）是指基因的表達取決於其親本來源的一種表觀遺傳現象。普遍認為，哺乳類動物中有接近1%的基因存在染色體印記。目前，在許多疾病之中已證實了印記效應的存在，例如安格爾曼綜合症、特納氏綜合症與精神障礙症等。在統計學研究中，已有分別針對這兩種表觀遺傳機制的方法研究。然而，目前尚無統計學方法可同時考慮以上兩種因素。 在本研究項目中，我們將在X染色體關聯分析中合併兩種表觀遺傳因素（X染色體失活與染色體印記）以填補這一研究領域的空白。其中，我們將基於常見與罕見的基因突變進行研究。此外，我們將考慮關於定性（二分類）和定量（連續型）性狀的方法。基於所構建的回歸模型，我們通過考慮不同程度的X染色體失活與印記效應，為X染色體常見與罕見變異的關聯分析方法提供理論與經驗框架。最後，我們擬將提出的方法應用於真實數據的分析中，如類風濕性關節炎和二型糖尿病。

17302919.label: Realisation of objectives
17302919.value: The X chromosome is known to play an important role in many sex-specific diseases. However, only a few single-nucleotide polymorphisms on the X chromosome have been found to be associated with diseases. Compared to the autosomes, conducting association tests on the X chromosome is challenging due to the difference in the number of X chromosomes between females and males. Moreover, X chromosome inactivation (XCI), a process where one of the two X chromosomes in females is silenced to match the gene expression level of males, further complicates association tests. Imprinting effects may also be related to certain diseases, but current approaches do not account for these effects. The first objective of this project was to develop powerful statistical tests that consider XCI and imprinting for the genetic association of common variants on the X chromosome for qualitative traits. This objective was achieved through papers 1 and 2. In paper 1, an extended likelihood ratio test MLR_XCII was constructed based on a logistic regression model. Since the asymptotic distribution of the test statistic was intractable, the p value was obtained through permutation methods. Paper 2 proposed a more complex method where a test statistic was derived for each gender, and a weighted average of these statistics was obtained to yield a test statistic Z. The test Z_XCII was then proposed as the maximum of the two test statistics assuming g and h as the risk allele, i.e., Z_XCII = max (Z_g, Z_h). The p value of Z_XCII can be obtained analytically without requiring simulation. Paper 5 involved statistical tests for association with quantitative traits on the X chromosome (objective 3). However, existing tests either do not incorporate male information or only detect heterogeneity. To address this, we proposed four novel methods that effectively incorporate X chromosome inactivation information. In paper 4, we introduced a Bayesian method to estimate the degree of skewness of XCI, which has been associated with X-linked diseases. Our method utilized prior information that the degree of skewness falls between 0 and 2. Additionally, we explored rare allele-based estimation of the degree of skewness for genes in paper 3 (objective 3). To evaluate the proposed tests, we conducted simulations and analyzed real data sets (objective 4). Specifically, we examined substance abuse and related psychopathology data from the Minnesota Center for Twin and Family Research in papers 3-5, as well as Grave's disease data in paper 4. We are pleased to report that all objectives have been successfully achieved.

17302919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17302919.value: The primary aim of the project is to develop novel statistical tests for genetic association on the X chromosome, while considering X chromosome inactivation and genomic imprinting. Various test statistics have been proposed for qualitative traits in papers 1 and 2, and for quantitative traits with X chromosome inactivation in paper 5. Skewed X chromosome inactivation has been reported to be associated with some X-linked diseases, and a Bayesian method was devised in paper 4 to determine the point estimate and credible interval of XCI skewness. In situations where rare alleles on the X chromosome need to be considered for association, an estimate of gene skewness based on rare alleles was obtained in paper 3. These methodologies were applied to real datasets, yielding satisfactory results. The R packages for this project are freely accessible at the following links: https://github.com/Meng-KaiLi/GEXCIS, https://github.com/Wen-YiYu/BEXCIS, and https://github.com/yuxinyuanqt/QMVtest

17302919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17302919.value: Opportunities for further development include expanding the proposed tests in papers 1 and 2 from trio data to pedigree data, potentially increasing the power of the tests. While the validity of these tests has been investigated under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and the inbreeding model, exploring their effectiveness under the population stratification model could be beneficial. Additionally, developing new test statistics to address the assumptions made in paper 5 (the risk alleles in females and males are the same, and the genetic effect of heterozygous females is between those of two homozygous females) could be worthwhile. Papers 3 and 4 also offer potential avenues for further exploration, such as investigating a Bayesian analysis of gene skewness in paper 3. However, as the author has already retired, there is no proposed course of action.

17302919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17302919.value: Research has revealed that many intricate diseases are sex-specific. When examining genetic association studies on the X chromosome, two crucial epigenetic factors need to be considered concurrently: X chromosome inactivation and genomic imprinting. While various association tests currently account for the information on X-chromosome inactivation, they fail to consider imprinting effects. Our project introduces original association tests that incorporate both X-chromosome inactivation and imprinting effects. Furthermore, we have designed new association tests for quantitative traits on the X chromosome. The extent of skewness in X chromosome inactivation is a quantity of interest to geneticists, estimated through likelihood and Bayesian approaches. The proposed methods were tested through simulations and real data analysis, resulting in satisfactory outcomes.

17303019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303019.value: Quantum criticality and related dynamical properties are frontier topics in condensed matter physics, with phenomena ranging from fractionalization and emergent gauge fields at deconfined quantum critical points (where quasi-particles fractionalize) to spectral and transport anomalies at itinerant quantum criticality and signatures of anyonic excitations in the dynamic response functions of frustrated magnets, to mention some areas closely related to this proposal. These emergent features of correlated electronic systems are inherently non-perturbative, and large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations and field theoretical calculations are becoming the most prominent and indispensible techniques to tackle such difficult problems and reveal new phenomena and paradigms. The PI of the proposal is one of the leading experts in large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations and through collaboration works closely with field theorists in quantum many-body systems, and has contributed several influential works in the aforementioned areas during the past several years. The target of this proposal involves numerical investigations of specifically designed prototypical model systems (lattice Hamiltonians without 'sign problems' in quantum Monte Carlo simulations) for which unbiased methods exist that have favorable system-size scaling properties to reliably reach the sought behaviors in the thermodynamic limit. The physical phenomena to be studied fall primarily into three related categories: 1) deconfined quantum criticality and its important experimental dynamical signatures, 2) anomalous transport and other key non-Fermi-liquid properties of itinerant quantum critical points, 3) signatures of anyonic excitations in the dynamic response functions of frustrated magnets, to provide smoking-gun signature of material realization of topological orders. With the superior supercomputing facilities available in China, the term of PI will address these fundamental, timely issues, which go beyond the traditional Landau-Ginzburg-Wilson and Fermi-liquid paradigms of condensed matter physics. The efforts of this proposal will consequently improve our fundamental understanding of quantum many-body physics, stimulate and support the development and application of low-energy quantum field theories, and guide experimental investigations of novel quantum materials. 量子动力学和临界现象是关联电子系统研究的重要课题，它们涵盖了分数化和衍生规范场（以去禁闭量子临界点为例），迅游电子量子临界区域中的新奇输运结果，以及阻挫磁体和量子自旋液体中的任意子激发的谱学表现等等新的物理内容。 这样关联电子系统的涌现现象体现出量子多体物理学具有的强关联和非微绕的特点，传统的以平均场处理方法为代表的解析手段无法获得定量甚至是定性正确的结果。本项目的申请人，近年来致力于发展以量子蒙特卡洛方法为代表的大规模数值计算手段，在量子多体物理学研究方面已经取得了国际瞩目的成绩。 在本项目中，申请人团队将会进行如下方面的研究： 1. 去禁闭量子临界现象的动力学计算研究，以期指导相关凝聚态物理系统实验推进。 2. 非费米液体和迅游电子量子临界区的输运性质计算。 3. 阻挫磁体模型中的任意子激发的谱学体现，指导量子磁体中的中子散射、核磁共振等等实验的推进。 通过本项目的顺利进行，申请人希望推动香港地区大规模数值计算方向的发展，推动量子物质科学新范式的建立。

17303019.label: Realisation of objectives
17303019.value: During this reporting period, our research efforts have been highly successful, resulting in the publication of 61 research papers, including 17 high-profile publications in prestigious journals. Specifically, we have published 5 papers in Nature Communications, 3 papers in NPJ Quantum Materials, 1 paper in NPJ Quantum Information, 6 papers in Physical Review Letters, and 1 paper in Physical Review X. Additionally, one paper has been accepted for publication in Nature Physics. In Objective 1, our primary focus was on designing lattice models specifically tailored for studying quantum critical points and determining experimentally measurable quantities. One notable achievement in this area was our in-depth exploration of the entanglement properties observed at deconfined quantum critical points. The groundbreaking findings resulting from this research were published in respected scientific journals such as SciPost Phys. 13, 123 (2022) and NPJ Quantum Materials 7, 69 (2022). To investigate the entanglement properties, we developed standardized tools that allowed us to measure various aspects of entanglement in quantum many-body systems. These tools encompassed the analysis of the disorder operator, entanglement entropy (Nature Communications 14, 2360 (2023)), and entanglement spectra. Through our research, we captured the fundamental and crucial role played by these entanglement properties in different quantum systems, particularly at deconfined quantum critical points. This rapidly evolving toolkit has opened new avenues for us to unravel the intricate nature of quantum effects and advance our understanding of quantum many-body physics. By utilizing these innovative measurement techniques, we have gained deeper insights into the complex interplay between entanglement and quantum criticality, as shown in our publication in Phys. Rev. Lett. 128, 010601 (2022). Our research has provided valuable contributions to the field, shedding light on the fundamental nature of entanglement in diverse quantum systems. These findings have not only expanded our knowledge but have also paved the way for further investigations into the profound impact of entanglement on quantum phenomena. Objective 2 involved a comprehensive study of the impact of thermal fluctuations on non-Fermi-liquid behavior at an itinerant quantum critical point. Our research work, published in NPJ Quantum Materials 5, 65 (2020), provided valuable insights into non-Fermi-liquid phenomena and opened up new avenues for Quantum Monte Carlo studies of quantum critical metals. In Objective 3, our research endeavors were focused on conducting large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations to accurately calculate and identify signatures of anyonic excitations in the dynamic response functions of frustrated magnets. Along this exciting path, we have achieved several groundbreaking breakthroughs that have significantly enhanced our understanding of quantum many-body systems. One notable accomplishment was the identification of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) phase and its topological excitations in a material exhibiting frustrated magnetism. This important discovery, published in Nature Communications 11, 5631 (2020), shed light on the unique properties and behavior of the BKT phase and its topological excitations. Through our simulations, we were able to precisely characterize the dynamic response functions associated with these excitations, providing a deeper understanding of their role in frustrated magnet materials. Additionally, our research efforts led us to explore novel excitations in quantum many-body systems. We investigated a Gross-Neveu quantum critical point, unraveling its intriguing properties and implications. This work, published in Phys. Rev. B 106, 115149 (2022), contributed to the growing understanding of quantum critical phenomena and their manifestation in various physical systems. Moreover, we explored the potential emergence of a Dirac quantum spin liquid, a fascinating state of matter with unique properties and promising applications. In Objective 4, our dedicated efforts, supported by high-performance computing facilities, have elevated the level of computational quantum many-body physics in Hong Kong. The exceptional achievements of our Principal Investigator were recognized with the prestigious 2020 "Tianhe Star Award" for their significant impact and fundamental value in large-scale quantum Monte Carlo simulations. Furthermore, the establishment of the "blackbody" computation cluster, boasting over 2000 cores in the Department of Physics at the University of Hong Kong, solidified the university's position as a leading center for international computational physics. Overall, our research activities have yielded remarkable results, increased the international exposure of computational quantum many-body physics and contributed to advancements in various areas of the field. Through our collective efforts, collaborations, and cutting-edge methodologies, we have made significant strides in unraveling the mysteries of quantum critical points, non-Fermi-liquid behavior, and novel excitations in quantum many-body systems. Looking to the future, the development of measurement techniques for entanglement entropy and other related entanglement properties has opened up new possibilities within the realm of quantum many-body systems. This situation has inspired us to delve into the exploration of novel quantum phenomena, such as the deconfined quantum critical point. With the rapid improvement of the tech for measuring entangling properties, Hong Kong's importance in the field of computational physics is growing significantly.

17303319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303319.value: Multidrug bacterial resistance is a serious public issue worldwide. Unfortunately, the development of new effective antibiotics is lagging far behind. Different strategies should be used to search for new antibacterial agents. Malacidins have been recently discovered from nature and have potent antibacterial activities. Malacidins consist of a cyclic nonapeptide anchored with an amino acid linked to an unsaturated C9 or C10-lipid. There are several non-proteinogenic amino acids present, including methyl-aspartic acid (MeAsp), hydroxyl-aspartic acid (HyAsp), methyl-proline (MePro) and methyl-diaminopropionic acid (MeDap). However, the stereo-configurations of the amino acids in malacidins have not been fully established, which leaves a big knowledge gap. In this project, we aim to develop a strategy for the total synthesis of malacidins and then study their medicinal chemistry. In particular, we will explore a new HyAsp ligation-mediated peptide cyclization for malacidin A synthesis. By synthesizing and using stereochemistry-defined amino acid building blocks, we will prepare different diastereomeric malacidin A forms. By comparing the NMR spectra of these synthetic malacidins with those already reported, we will be able to establish the bona fide structure of malacidin A. Three synthetic routes have been proposed for the total synthesis of malacidin A, one of which is to use the in-house Ser/Thr ligation-mediated peptide cyclization. We have long-term research interests in cyclic peptide antibiotics, and have laid a good foundation for completing the proposed objectives. Our long-term goal is to develop malacidin A analogues with improved pharmacological properties as new antibacterial drug candidates. 全球逐漸氾濫的多重抗藥性細菌已然成為威脅人類生命健康的重大問題。然而不幸的是，新型抗生素的研究研發進展卻進入了瓶頸期。為此，人們應該嘗試各種各樣的策略去發現和開發新型抗生素藥物。最近，一個具有高效抗生素活性的化合物家族Malacidin被發現和分離出來。這類化合物由一個環九肽結構與一條連接在一個氨基酸上的不飽和脂肪鏈組成。在組成它們的氨基酸中，共有數種非天然氨基酸，包括甲基天冬氨酸（MeAsp）、羥基天冬氨酸（HyAsp）、甲基脯氨酸（MePro）以及甲基二氨基丁酸（ MeDap）。但是，這些非天然氨基酸的立體構型並沒有被完全表徵，因此這方面還有很大的空間需要探索。在這一個項目中，我們計劃發展一套化學全合成Malacidin的策略，然後通過結構對比來確定Malacidin的絕對構型，並更進一步研究它的藥物化學包括其構效關係。為此我們設計了三種不同的合成路徑，其中一種是基於我們之前報導的絲氨酸/蘇氨酸偶聯法（STL）來嘗試發展HyAsp介導的多肽環化技術來化學全合成Malacidin A。開發新一代環肽抗生素是我們組的長遠目標，我們有著良好的基礎以完成所述項目。我們的一個長期目標便是發展具有更高藥物活性的Malacidin A衍生物作為新型的抗生素藥物候選化合物。

17303319.label: Realisation of objectives
17303319.value: Malacidin A consists of a cyclic nonapeptide anchored with an amino-acid-linked unsaturated C9-fatty acid, as well as one D-Val and five non-proteinogenic amino acids, including β-methylaspartic acid at position 1 and 8 (MeAsp-1 and -8), β-methyldiaminopropionic acid-2 (MeDap-2), β-hydroxyaspartic acid-5 (HyAsp-5) and γ-methylproline-10 (MePro-10). Based on NMR characterization, the configuration of the lipid tail was readily determined as 2E,4Z-methyl-nonadienoic acid. Combining NMR technique with the Marfey’s analysis, configurations of MePro-10 and HyAsp-5 were suggested as L-(4R)-MePro and L-HyAsp-5. Bioinformatically, MeDap-2, MeAsp-1, and MeAsp-8 were predicted as L-MeDap-2, L-(3S)-MeAsp-1 and D-(3S)-MeAsp-8 respectively. However, the β-stereochemistry of L-MeDap-2 and L-HyAsp-5 remained uncertain and needed further investigation. This left four possible diastereomeric structures of malacidin A. Starting from a commercially available building block of l- aspartic acid, we developed a concise synthesis of (2S,3S) and (2S,3R) HyAsp building blocks in 5 steps. The (2S,3S) and (2R, 3S) MeAsp building blocks were synthesized from glutamic acid in 3 steps. The (2S,3S) and (2S, 3R) MeDap building blocks were prepared from l-Thr or l-allo-Thr, respective, in 6 steps. The (2S, 4R)- γ-methyl proline building block was synthesized from pyroglutamic acid in 7 steps. The fatty acid building block was obtained in 5 steps. With all the building blocks in hand, we proceeded towards the total synthesis of malacidin A. Our first attempt used solid phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) followed by in-solution peptide cyclization failed, mainly due to the significant aspartimide formation during Fmoc-SPPS. To avoid the aspartimide formation, an on-resin cyclization synthetic plan was attempted in which the side chain of the HyAsp building block was directly anchored to the resin. Unfortunately, the cyclization precursor was found to fall off the resin under the C-terminus carboxylic acid allyl deprotection conditions. In the end, we turned to an unconventional peptide cyclization synthetic route that relied on chemical ligation. The linear peptide with a C-terminal salicylaldehyde ester and an N-terminal β-hydroxyaspartic acid was synthesized via Fmoc-SPPS, which underwent ligation to produce the desired cyclic peptide product. Using this strategy, all four possible diastereomeric structures of malacidin with different combination of (2S,3S) or (2S,3R) HyAsp building blocks, and (2S,3S) or (2S, 3R) MeDap building blocks have been synthesized. Based on the comparison of NMR spectra and antibacterial activity, the absolute stereocenters of these two non-proteinogenic amino acid residues are suggested as (2S, 3R)-MeDap2 and (2S, 3R)-HyAsp5. In addition, we have completed the syntheses of 16 diastereomeric forms of malacidin A. To further confirm these results, we collaborated with Prof. Sean Brady’s group and carried out an advanced Marfey’s analysis on the natural malacidin A. His group also conducted the antibacterial activity testing of our synthetic malacidin A analogues. This analysis validated the stereochemical predictions suggested by our total synthesis studies. Thus, we have successfully developed the first total synthesis of malacidin A with which we also established the absolute structure.

17303319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303319.value: In summary, the major findings and research outcomes include the discovery and characterization of Malacidin A, a cyclic nonapeptide with potential antibacterial properties. This compound consists of a unique combination of non-proteinogenic amino acids, including β-methylaspartic acid, β-methyldiaminopropionic acid, β-hydroxyaspartic acid, and γ-methylproline, as well as an unsaturated C9-fatty acid. The researchers developed a concise synthesis approach for the various building blocks of Malacidin A, starting from commercially available amino acids. However, initial attempts at solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) and in-solution peptide cyclization were unsuccessful due to aspartimide formation. An on-resin cyclization strategy was also attempted but was hindered by the cyclization precursor falling off the resin. Ultimately, we developed an unconventional peptide cyclization synthetic route that relied on chemical ligation. Using this strategy, we synthesized all four possible diastereomeric structures of Malacidin A. By comparing NMR spectra and antibacterial activity, the researchers suggested the absolute stereocenters of the non-proteinogenic amino acid residues as (2S, 3R)-MeDap2 and (2S, 3R)-HyAsp5. In total, 16 diastereomeric forms of Malacidin A were synthesized. Collaboration with Prof. Sean Brady's group allowed for advanced Marfey's analysis on the natural Malacidin A and the testing of the synthetic Malacidin A analogues' antibacterial activity. This analysis validated the stereochemical predictions suggested by the total synthesis studies. The successful development of the first total synthesis of Malacidin A and the establishment of its absolute structure were published in Angewandte Chemie. This research has significant implications for the development of novel antibiotics and the understanding of the unique structure and properties of Malacidin A.

17303319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303319.value: The research on Malacidin A has shown great potential for further development, particularly in the field of antibiotic drug discovery. With the successful total synthesis and determination of the absolute structure of Malacidin A, we can now focus on performing its medicinal chemistry studies. These studies will help determine the feasibility of Malacidin A-based compound as a therapeutic agent and may lead to the development of novel antibiotics effective against multidrug-resistant pathogens. Additionally, the synthesis of the 16 diastereomeric forms of Malacidin A provides an opportunity to explore structure-activity relationships (SAR) of this unique compound. By assessing the antibacterial activity of these analogues, researchers can identify key structural features that contribute to Malacidin A's potency and specificity. This information will guide the design of new and improved antibiotics based on the Malacidin A scaffold. The proposed course of action includes conducting detailed biological studies on Malacidin A and its analogues to assess their potential as therapeutic agents. Concurrently, the development of more efficient and scalable synthetic routes for Malacidin A will facilitate its production for further studies and potential future clinical applications.

17303319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303319.value: The research project focused on a unique compound called Malacidin A, which has potential as a new antibiotic. Antibiotics are crucial in treating infections, but many bacteria have become resistant to existing drugs. This makes the discovery of new antibiotics like Malacidin A extremely important. Malacidin A is a complex molecule made up of unusual building blocks called non-proteinogenic amino acids. We successfully developed a synthetic method to create Malacidin A in the lab and determined its precise structure, which is essential for understanding how it works and how it can be improved. The team also synthesized 16 different forms of Malacidin A, which could help identify the specific features that make it effective against bacteria. This information will guide the development of new antibiotics based on Malacidin A's structure. The next steps in this research include studying Malacidin A's mode of action and safety, as well as testing its effectiveness in animal models. This project holds significant value in the ongoing search for new antibiotics to combat drug-resistant infections, which pose a major threat to global public health.

17303519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303519.value: Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD)-derived nutrients through beach aquifers and benthic sediments have significant influences on marine environments and ecology. Beach aquifers and benthic sediments have different driving forces of SGD and different biogeochemical environments for nutrients. Although SGD through beach aquifers and its associated geochemistry have been widely studied, benthic sediments, especially those far from the shoreline have received much less attention. Biogeochemical pathways of the nutrients and the nutrient cycle between groundwater and seawater can be best understood only by rigorous studies of both beach aquifers and benthic sediments. Based on statistical analyses or spatial and temporal correlations between SGD and red tide, some studies suggest that SGD-derived nutrients may be responsible for algal blooms. However, almost no studies have investigated whether the nutrients taken up by red tide species are actually from SGD. Likewise, little is known about the mechanisms by which SGD-derived nutrients actually cause algal blooms, probably because such a study is very challenging and difficult. This project will study the nutrient cycle through the seawater-groundwater interface, including the generation, transformation transport, and removal of nutrients in both beach aquifer and benthic sediments, and the effect of SGD-derived nutrients on algal blooms using Tolo Harbour as a case study (Figure 1). The sources of nutrients in various water endmembers will be identified via stable isotope of nitrogen (δ15N). Nutrient loading through the beach aquifer and benthic sediments will be estimated, respectively, using two multilevel sampling and monitoring systems (MSMS) and 224Ra/228Th disequilibrium in bottom sediment cores. The production kinetics and transformation pathways of nutrients will be investigated through flow-through-reactor (FTR) experiments. The abundance and diversity of microbial communities related to the nitrogen cycle and the function genes of different biogeochemical transformations in beach and benthic sediments will be investigated using the methods of 16S rRNA gene sequencing and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR). To explore the connection between SGD-derived nutrients and algal blooms, the δ15N of groundwater nutrients and red tide species will be identified and compared, and a series of incubation experiments will be carried out to examine the contribution of SGD-derived nutrients to the growth of phytoplankton. A successful completion of this project will provide not only a comprehensive understanding of the land-sea nutrient cycle and its ecological impact on algal blooms but also a scientific basis for the marine environmental management in Hong Kong and elsewhere. 海底地下水通過海灘含水層和海底沉積物釋放的營養物質對海洋環境和生態有著重要的影響。位於海灘含水層和海底沉積物環境下的海底地下水排泄，由于不同的驅動力，營養物質產生的生物地球化學環境也有巨大差異。目前對於通過海灘含水層的海底地下水排泄過程及其相關的地球化學過程進行了廣泛的研究，然而對海底沉積物環境，特別是遠離海岸線的沉積物中的海底地下水排泄卻關注甚少。因此，通過結合對海灘含水層和海底沉積物兩種環境下的觀測研究，才能更全面地認識地下水和海水之間營養循環及其生物地球化學過程。統計資料表明，海底地下水排泄與赤潮具有較強的時空相關性， 地下水排泄帶來的營養物質可能是引起赤潮的主要原因。然而，目前尚未證實赤潮物種所吸收的營養物質是否真的來自地下水。同樣，對於海底地下水排泄的營養物質導致藻華的機制知之甚少。因此，開展本項研究非常具有挑戰性和難度。 本項目將以吐露港為例，研究海水-地下水界面的營養循環，包括海灘含水層和海底沉積物中營養物質的產生、轉化、運輸和去除，以及海底地下水排泄的營養物質對藻華的影響。擬通過氮的穩定同位素（δ15N）來識別不同的營養來源。將分別在沿岸安裝多層採樣系統（MSMS）和底部沉積柱進行採樣，利用Ra的質量平衡模型及孔隙水中224Ra/228Th非平衡過程，估算海灘含水層和海底沉積物的營養鹽。建立來自海底地下水排泄的營養物質與浮游植物之間關係，對地下水營養素與赤潮物種的δ15N進行了鑑定和比較，並將進行一系列培養試驗，探討地下水帶來營養物對浮游植物生長的貢獻。這一項目的開展，不僅能全面了解海-陸間的營養循環過程及其對藻類水華的生態影響，更能為香港及周邊地區的海洋環境管理提供科學依據。

17303519.label: Realisation of objectives
17303519.value: 1. Estimation of benthic nutrient flux to Tolo Harbor by field sampling We employed the approaches of 224Ra/228Th disequilibrium to quantify the porewater exchange (PEX) and benthic fluxes of nutrients in Tolo Harbor. We have obtained the high-resolution nutrient profiles from the porewater of marine sediments in Tolo Harbor. By integrating the results of 224Ra/228Th disequilibrium, we finally quantify the benthic fluxes of nutrient and carbon components in the study areas. We further compared the relevant importance of SGD and PEX in delivering the nutrients to the coasts. Generally, both SGD and PEX fluxes were at the same magnitude and had significant seasonal variation in which high discharge rate in wet season was observed. SGD rate was (3.07±2.32)×106 and of (2.37±3.07)×106 m3 d-1 in wet and dry seasons, respectively, while PEX rate was (3.90±1.64)×106 and (2.18±4.30)×106 m3 d-1 in wet and dry seasons respectively. Irrigation in the sediment is the major process that regulate PEX fluxes, compared to molecular diffusion and bioturbation. PEX of bottom sediment is an important source of NH4+ and PO43-, while SGD and riverine input are major source of NO3- and SiO42-. Instead of being a type of SGD, PEX is suggested to be viewed as a separate pathway for the regenerated components of benthic respiration. 2. Estimation of nutrient composition and flux to Tolo Harbour through beach aquifer using water table and hydrochemical data Our results indicate that the saline freshwater interface in beach aquifers is sensitive to diel and seasonal hydrologic variation due to the variation of land-sea hydraulic gradient. The nutrient (NH4+, NO2-, NO3-, and PO43-) dynamic in coastal groundwater mixing zone is found to be fluctuated with tidal oscillation due to the change of redox conditions, organic matter supply and salinity regimes impacted by tidal fluctuations. The inventory of NOx- and PO4 3- in the intertidal aquifer has a clear seasonality with a large inventory in summer, a small inventory in spring, and a median inventory in autumn and winter, respectively. Differently, the inventory of NH4+ is large in winter and summer and small in spring and autumn, which results from the coupled effects of seasonal change of both production and removal of NH4+ in the aquifer. The SGD-derived nutrient (NH4+, NOx-, and PO43-) flux is the highest in summer and is the lowest in spring. The majority of SGD-derived nutrient flux is supported by the local remineralization of organic matter along with seawater infiltration. In autumn, the recharge of seawater induced by tidal pumping significantly shifts the biogeochemical balance of nutrients and is the major source of groundwater nutrients in the intertidal aquifer. Among the various nutrient fluxes (SGD, river discharge, atmospheric deposition, and benthic sediment diffusion) to Tolo Harbor, SGD-derived PO43- flux is the second major source of seawater PO43- in addition to benthic sediment diffusion. The PO43- loading via SGD is of significance to the primary production in the phosphorus-limited environment in Tolo Harbor. 3. Identification of nutrient sources through δ15N signature in different endmembers A series of field campaigns were carried out in Tolo Harbour, Hong Kong in wet and dry seasons. The collected water samples included fresh groundwater from springs, nearshore saline groundwater from intertidal aquifers, river water, seawater (harbour and open sea), benthic sediment porewater, and rainwater. Dual isotopes of NO3- - δ15N-NO3- and δ18O-NO3- were determined by bacterial denitrifier method and measured by a GasBench II coupled with a continuous flow isotope ratio mass spectrometer (IRMS, Thermo Delta V Advantage). A Bayesian mixing model was adopted to estimate the proportion contributions of NO3- in surface harbour water from six water sources in wet and dry seasons, respectively. In wet season. due to the constraint of vertical stratification, precipitation NO3- loadings were bounded at the surface harbour water, and served as the major contribution of NO3- in the surface harbour water. With the relief of stratification and intensified vertical mixing in wet season, NO3- in the surface harbour water can be mainly contributed by benthic input. Benthic input became a major water source inferencing NO3- in surface harbour water, due to the strengthened nitrification in the water column under intensified vertical mixing and continuous benthic NH4+ supply. The mass balance model of NO3- were constructed to secure the closure of NO3- in the bulk water body in Tolo Harbour. The major NO3- source and sink were found to biogeochemical reaction (i.e., nitrification) and biological removal. 4. Identification of abundance and diversity of microbial communities responsible for the nitrogen cycle in beach and benthic sediments To delineate the microbial controls of biogeochemical reactions of Tolo Harbor, we conducted the analysis of seawater rather than the marine sediments. Generally, seawater samples (2L) were collected and then filtered by 0.2 mm cellulose acetate filter for microbial community analysis. Based on the microbial community analysis, we found that nitrification is primarily driven by microbes and relative abundance of nitrifying bacteria can be an indicator of nitrification. Therefore, abundance of various microbial communities of the surface harbour seawater was analyzed to identify the existence and evaluate the intensity of nitrification in the water column. The first step of nitrification (ammonia oxidation) is performed by ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) and ammonia-oxidizing archaea (AOA). AOB can be found among the classes of β-proteobacteria and γ-proteobacteria. In the second step of nitrification (nitrite oxidation), nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) is responsible for the oxidation of nitrite to nitrate. NOB belongs to some genera of the phyla Proteobacteria, Nitrospinae and Chloroflexi. Proteobacteria is a group of bacteria that plays a considerable role in both steps of nitrification. In the microbial community in surface harbour water, proteobacteria was observed in all stations and its relative abundance showed a positive correlation with the NH4+:NO3- ratio). In other words, more proteobacteria presented in the environment with high reactant (NH4+)-production (NO3-) ratio. 5. Development of field experiments to reveal the relationship between the nutrient components in SGD and phytoplankton species We leveraged both extensive field investigations and laboratory incubations to explore the co-effect of SGD and runoff on the phytoplankton biomass and community structure. Annually, temperature is found to be mostly responsible for seasonal fluctuations of the phytoplankton biomass. Within a given season, phytoplankton biomass is mainly governed by the concentrations of limited nitrogen or phosphate, while salinity and NH4+:NO3- are strong determinants of phytoplankton community structure. Runoff and SGD tend to regulate the phytoplankton biomass and community structure by changing salinity and nutrient regimes. However, hydrodynamics will further modulate the impact area and magnitude of runoff and SGD. In wet season, large river discharge and fresh SGD initiate high nutrient concentrations in the harbor and offshore current induced by southwest winds contributes to the expansion of impact area of freshwater input. Consequently, total phytoplankton biomass presents seaward decreasing trend. Meanwhile, river discharge and fresh SGD create a NH4+:NO3-<1 environment that favors the predominance of diatom group. Comparably, in dry season, along with the change of wind direction and the reduction of precipitation, the overall landward inflow current reconciles the influences of terrestrial input, creating a mixing front with elevated phytoplankton biomass offshore.

17303519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303519.value: We have investigated various aspects of coastal pollution related to groundwater and the impact of microbial pollution on public health. We challenged the traditional understanding that nutrients from river and sedge are the primary sources of coastal pollution and instead highlighted the importance of coastal groundwater flow and chemistry in controlling ecological and pollution problems. We also proposed a new approach to monitoring E. coli pollution using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) and thermal remote sensing, which was validated against 50 beaches in Hong Kong and proved to be reliable. We explord the mechanism of microbial transport and occurrence in the beach groundwater system and found that the unique relationship between radon-222 and E. coli can provide additional critical context to microbial water quality assessments. Finally we investigated the impact of storm events on subsurface E. coli growth and exports to coastal waters. Results indicate that storm events can stimulate E. coli growth and accelerate exports into the receiving water, providing new insight for the stress of storm events on microbial pollution in coastal waters. Overall, these findings are constructive to the prevention of beach ecosystem pollution and can pave the way for coastal safety management to future extreme weather.

17303619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303619.value: The Kloosterman sum was borne in 1920's, and today they are playing in stages of modular forms, geometric Langlands program, coding theory and network design, etc. One of the famous conjectures is about a bound on their size in absolute value, which was solved by Andre Weil, and the result is nowaday known as Weil's bound. The unsolved conjectures such as Katz's problem are in general difficult, perhaps still beyond reach. On the other hand, the function field analogue of Kloosterman sums is more tractable, which was observed and solved by C.-L. Chai and Winnie Li almost two decades ago. The Hurwitz class number has a history of four decades longer than Kloosterman sums. But it is still vivid, and a modern interest is about the relation with mock modular forms. Mock modular forms are already known to play roles in the quantum theory of black holes. In this project, we study the difficult problems for Kloosterman sums in the function field case, and the outcome will be used to demonstrate, in future, the similarity and difference between the Kloosterman sums in the two regimes (of the classical case and the function field case). We also further explore the modularity hidden in sums of Hurwitz class numbers which is indeed of interest not limited to number theorists. Another goal of the project is to establish the connection between the Hurwitz class numbers and the (classical) Kloosterman sums with analytic methods, which gives one more way to understand the Hurwitz class numbers. Kloosterman和誕生於1920年代，今天他在模形式，幾何Langlands program，編碼理論和網絡設計等擔當重要角色。Kloosterman和有一個關於它們絕對值大小的著名猜想。這個問題已由 Andre Weil 解決了，這結果現被稱為 Weil 界限。不過, Kloosterman和仍有其他尚未解決的困難猜想如Katz問題。另一方面，約廿年前 C.-L.Chai和Winnie Li 發現在函數域上的Kloosterman和是更易於處理，他們解決了這情況下的Katz問題。 Hurwitz class number 的歷史比 Kloosterman和長約四十年。但我們對它仍然是充滿興趣, 特別是它與 mock 模形式的關係。Mock 模形式在黑洞量子理論中扮演重要角色。 在這個項目中，我們研究在函數域中有關Kloosterman和的難題，結果將用於比較Kloosterman和在數域及函數域中相似和差異之處。我們還進一步探討隱藏在 Hurwitz class number 中的模形式性質。項目的另一個目標是用分析方法建立Hurwitz class number 和（經典）Kloosterman 和之間的聯繫, 從中了解更多 Hurwitz class number。

17303619.label: Realisation of objectives
17303619.value: 1. We established a quantitative version of equidistribution theorem for a collection of Kloosterman sums at the places whose corresponding irreducible polynomials are lying in a short interval around a certain fixed polynomial or an arithmetic progression. This quantitative version gives explicitly the rate of convergence toward the probability distribution. 2. We performed several numerical experiments and attempted to speculate relations between Hurwitz class numbers and Kloosterman sums for the case of general primes. But the numerical results do not show strong pattern or evidence for us to formulate a plausible relation. On the other hand, the evaluation of a weighted sum of Hurwitz class numbers over an arithmetic progression could be managed with the tool of mock modular forms. 3. The Hurwitz class number is associated to a mock modular form and a method has been developed to compute the asymptotic formulas for a family of weighted sum of Hurwitz class numbers over an arithmetic progression. These formulas provide the moment values for a distribution function, and consequently a statistical result was proved. 4. PhD students and postdoctoral fellows were supported with the fund. The student Jiang learned the background knowledge of this project when I was his primary supervisor, and he chose to write a thesis under another (primary) supervisor. Finally the project PI served as the co-supervisor and the student completed his PhD study successfully.

17303619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303619.value: In output 1, we studied horizontal Sato-Tate distributions of Kloosterman sums over function fields by using Lafforgue's result on the symmetric power L-functions associated to the automorphic representation. Specifically, we formulated and showed an equidistribution result in function field analogue of primes on arithmetic progressions. Moreover, we established a result of equidistribution over short intervals. In the Appendix which was recently completed, we gave an alternative using Katz-Deligne's equidistribution result. A salient point is the association of Kloosterman sums over function fields with a Kloosterman sheaf. In output 2, the Selberg limit's theorem for L-functions over a family of GL(n) Hecke-Maass forms was established. In output 3, a first sign change result of the Fourier coefficients of a general holomorphic cusp form is derived.

17303619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303619.value: In the study of a certain weighted sum of Hurwitz class numbers over an arithmetic progression, it is found that one needs to consider the Rankin-Cohen brackets of a harmonic Maass form and a theta function. This case (of weights (3/2, 1/2)) was successfully treated by Mertens, but for further generalizations, say the case of weights (3/2, 3/2), the treatment of the corresponding Rankin-Cohen bracket is merely partially successful. We will study these incompletely solved cases.

17303619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303619.value: This project focuses on the study of mathematical concepts called Kloosterman sums and Hurwitz class numbers. Kloosterman sums. We have studied the complex problems of Kloosterman sums specifically for a more tractable version called the function field case. We are able to give results on the equidistribution property for some families of Kloosterman sums. A statistical behaviour of the cumulated Hurwitz class numbers over an arithmetic progression is now also proved.

17303819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303819.value: Quantum matters with multi-degrees of freedom provide a rich arena for both experimental and fundamental research, and can eventually have technological applications. Experimentally, there exists an abundance of quantum materials in which several distinct degrees of freedom come into play. These include, for example, metallic systems with both itinerant electrons and local moments, Mott insulators with magnetic multipolar structures, transition metal oxides with active spins and orbitals, etc. The interaction and the interplay between distinct physical degrees of freedom give rise to rich and remarkable experimental phenomena. To illustrate, for metallic systems with both itinerant electrons and local moments, the magnetic order of local moments could reconstruct the band structure of the itinerant electrons, leading to Weyl semimetal and other topological bands; the fluctuation of the local moments could induce a pairing instability and superconductivity for the itinerant electrons. Therefore, these physical systems are natural places to search for novel experimental phenomena and/or new quantum phases of matter. Theoretically, many theories of condensed matter deal with quantum many-body systems with single flavor of degrees of freedom. The study of quantum matters with multi-degrees of freedom is quite limited, and the physical models for such systems have never been constructed nor studied carefully. Thus, the study of these systems may open up a brand-new direction for theoretical condensed matter physics. From the perspective of application, controlling one degree of freedom could impact other degrees of freedom indirectly through the internal coupling between these two degrees of freedom. This kind of idea is precisely the one behind the phenomena of giant magnetoresistance in many systems, where the external magnetic field controls the spin degrees of freedom and indirectly modifies the transport and resistivity of itinerant electrons via the spin-electron coupling. Similar thoughts also occur in systems called multiferroics with both magnetism and electric polarization. Over there, the magnetic field couples to the magnetism and influences the electric polarization, and the electric field couples to the electric polarization and modifies the magnetism. All these require a fundamental understanding of the interplay and the interaction between distinct degrees of freedom in various physical systems, and thereby justify our choice of this research topic. 多自由度的量子物質提供了凝聚態物理研究的豐富而且重要的實驗和基礎理論研究的平台，並且同時具有技術上的潛在應用。從實驗的角度看，自然界中存在大量的量子材料，這些量子材料同時擁有幾種不相同的物理自由度。這裏包括，比如 帶有巡遊電子和局域磁矩的金屬體系，帶有磁多極矩的莫特絕緣體，同時擁有活躍的自旋和軌道自由度的過渡金屬氧化物等等。不同自由度的相互交織的影響導致了豐富而又奇異的實驗現象。為了說明的需要，我們首先討論带有巡游电子和局域磁矩的金属体系。局域磁矩的磁有序可以对巡游电子的能带结构造成重构，使其出现威尔半金属和其他的拓扑能带结构，局域磁矩的漲落又可以誘導出傳導電子的配對以及超導的屬性。因此，這些物理系統是尋找新型實驗現象以及新的量子態的自然的場所。理論上說，許多凝聚態物質都是研究單個物理自由度的多體量子力學系統。 對於多重自由度的量子物質的研究現在還很有限，許多物理系統的模型並沒有得到構建。因此，對這類系統的研究工作可能會打開凝聚態理論研究的全新方向。 從應用的角度，控制一種自由度會對其他自由度產生間接的影響，這是通過這兩種自由度之間的內部相互作用導致的。這樣的想法和觀察其實是許多巨磁阻行為的物理機制。在這些相關的體系中，外部磁場通過控制自旋自由度間接影響傳導電子的輸運行為。與之類似的想法也可以出現在多鐵材料中，這樣的系統同時擁有磁性和電機化。在那裏，外磁場和磁性耦合同時影響電極化，外電場和電極化耦合同時改變磁性。所有這些系統和現象需要對多樣的物理體系中的不同自由度的相互作用有深入而仔細的理解。

17303819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303819.value: We developed a rather systematic understanding of the theremal Hall effects in quantum magnetic systems, ranging from pyrochlore quantum spin ice materials to spinon Fermi surface U(1) spin liquids, to Kitaev spin liquid materials. In the pyrochlore spin ice systems, we identified the magnetic monopole topological thermal Hall effect from the three-dimensional electromagnetic duality. For the two-dimensional U(1) spin liquids, we noticed that, the combination of the Zeeman coupling and the antisymmetric Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction generates the internal U(1) gauge flux for the spinons, and is responsible for the spinon thermal Hall effects. We further make the connection the Kitaev materials where it was shown by others that the finite field could induce an intermediate U(1) spin liquid. We apply our theory to this regime and explain the thermal Hall signal in this context. We have developed a comprehensive theory of the intrinsic quantum Ising model for the rare-earth quantum magnets, and made the specific connection with TmMgGaO4. Initially inspired by inelastic neutron scattering measurements in the triangular lattice antiferromagnet TmMgGaO4, we provide the physical model to this system. Based on our model, the magnetic excitation was found to be quantitatively consistent with the experiments. We further explored the finite field and finite temperature phase diagram and computed the physical properties in different regimes. We were also making connection with the BKT phase that is related to the 2016 physics Nobel prize. The intrinsic quantum Ising magnets and model were shown to be widely applicable to many quantum magnets with the non-Kramers doublets. In a series of papers, we studied the multipolar degrees of freedom in frustrated quantum magnets and quantum spin ices. In the former, we have developed a close collaboration with the resonant X-ray scattering experimentalists at RIKEN Japan, where they observed the presence of the hidden multipolar order. This result is remarkably consistent with our theoretical prediction. Moreover, we observed that the presence of multipolar degrees of freedom in quantum spin ice actually makes the experimental identification of certain exotic quasiparticle more accessible. Such a prediction was experimentally realized by researchers in Swiss. In addition, we have made progress in writing and deleting magnetic skyrmions that is potentially useful for quantum technology, in classifying spiral spin liquds, in nonsymmorphic nodal line semimetal, cluster Mott insulators, SU(N) chiral spin liquids, and frustrated criticality and competing spiral magnetism.

17303819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303819.value: The research of the group is a bit broad, and many of the current interests can be further expanded. The cluster Mott insulators were found to be quite relevant to many moire heterostructure which is under the very active exploration around the world. The cluster localization and the correlation should bring many interesting physics in these systems. The SU(N) Mott insulator were found to be relevant in twisted bilayer graphene and the ultracold atom systems. The actual physical materials could have additional interactions that can further enrich the results that have been obtained by us. The resonant inelastic X-ray scattering needs further theoretical understanding. The existing theoretical framework seems insufficient to catch the rapid development of the experiments.

17303819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303819.value: In this project, we were able to bridge the fundamental quantum many-body theories with the forefront experiments, and establish the mutual feedback between each other. Some of the research have reached the level of quantitative agreement between the theory and the experiments. Unlike the non-interacting systems, such type of agreement can often be quite different in strong correlation physics. This may serve as the prototype research for the future references. The systematic analysis of the physical origin for thermal Hall effects can serves a useful booklet for both theorists and experimentalists. The identification of the relationship between the microscopic physical degrees of freedom and the emergent degrees of freedom in exotic quantum phases is particularly useful for the understanding of the physical properties, and is quite important for the application of quantum control and quantum engineering in the future.

17303819.value: Month/Year/City Title Conference Name online "Thermal Hall effects in Mott insulators and a non-Fermi liquid" is the title of my talk. Abstract: Strong correlated Mott insulators could harbor various magnetic excitations that are charge neutral and hidden from usual electrical transport measurement, while thermal transport is powerful to detect the elementary excitations therein. Besides the more conventional and well-understood magnon excitations in the ordered state, here we discuss thermal Hall effects of the appealing fractionalized excitations in the quantum disordered spin liquid phase, which reveal the intriguing couplings between emergent gauge fields and fractionalized spinon or “magnetic monopole”, and provide strong evidence to confirm spin liquids. In the second part of the talk, we discuss a novel type of non-Fermi liquid (NFL) in itinerant magnets in 3D. Unlike the conventional hotspot and patch theory, the gapless fermions from the conduction electrons are coupled with infinite many critical boson modes. We show that the magnetic moments fluctuate near a 2D boson surface in the momentum space at low energies when the system approaches an ordering transition. The infinite number of critical modes on the boson surface strongly scatter the conduction electrons on the Fermi surface and convert the metallic sector into a NFL. Various physical consequences of in this NFL are explored, including the thermodynamic, spectroscopic, transport properties. 17303919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17303919.value: In the Standard Model (SM) of particle physics, massive fundamental particles obtain masses through their interactions with the Higgs field during Electroweak Symmetry Breaking (EWSB). In 2012, the Higgs boson was discovered in the A Toroidal Large Hadron Collider Apparatus (ATLAS) and the Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiments at the Large Hadron Collider(LHC), which was named as a scientific breakthrough of the year. The discovery of the Higgs boson is a milestone for understanding the EWSB. However, the mechanism of the EWSB is still not fully understood. One of the primary physics goals of the LHC is to discover new physics which provide satisfying solutions to the mechanism of the EWSB. After an upgrade, a Run II of the LHC began in 2015 and ended in 2018. In Run II, the LHC reached a proton-proton collision energy of 13 TeV and collected about 150 fb^-1 data. With such collision data the experiments will be able to perform improved measurements of known particles, and look for new physics with an increased discovery potential. The Run III and High Luminosity LHC operations will happen between 2021 to 2030, during which the integrated luminosity will be 300 fb^-1 and 3000 fb^-1 respectively. Such a high integrated luminosity will further increase the potential for observing the SUSY particles and beyond the SM Higgs bosons. 在粒子物理的標準模型中，基本粒子通過在電弱對稱性破缺過程中與希格斯場的相互作用獲得質量。作為2012年的科學突破，希格斯玻色子在位於歐洲核子中心（CERN）的世界最大和最高能量的大型強子對撞機（LHC）上被發現， 這個發現是理解電弱對稱性破缺的重要里程碑，但是電弱對稱性破缺的理論機制並沒有被完全理解。LHC的一個基本物理目標就是尋找為電弱對稱性破缺提供滿意解釋的新物理。 升級後的LHC從2015年運行到2018年（RUN II）。在RUN II 期間， LHC 達到對撞能量13 TeV，收集了大約150 fb^-1 數據。這些數據將為精確測量已知粒子和尋找新物理提供非常好的機會。LHC將在2021到2030 年期間進入RUN III和高亮度碰撞時期，屆時LHC 會採集300 fb^-1 到 3000 fb^-1數據， 因此找到超對稱物理以及新希格斯粒子的可能性會進一步增強。

17303919.label: Realisation of objectives
17303919.value: The objectives of this project are to search for the SUSY and the beyond Standard Model Higgs bosons in the final state with a same-sign lepton pair with full Run II ATLAS data and prepare for early Run III analyses. The objectives have been achieved in the following way: 1. A search for the direct production of winos and higgsinos is conducted in final states with either two leptons (e or μ) with the same electric charge, or three leptons. The analysis uses 139 fb−1 of pp collision data at centre of mass energy 13 TeV collected with the ATLAS detector during Run II of the Large Hadron Collider. Simplified and complete models with and without R-parity conservation are considered. 2. A search for a new heavy scalar or pseudo-scalar Higgs boson (H/A) produced in association with a pair of top quarks, with the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of top quarks is performed. The search targets a final state with exactly two leptons with same-sign electric charges or at least three leptons. The analysed dataset corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb−1 of proton–proton collisions collected at 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector. 3. A search is performed for four-top-quark production using an integrated luminosity of 139 fb−1 of proton-proton collision data at 13 TeV collected by the ATLAS. Events are selected if they contain a same-sign lepton pair or at least three leptons (electrons or muons). The results of the analyses are published/submitted on/to top journals in the field. They are two published papers and one submitted paper. The post-doc Daniela Katherinne Paredes Hernandez is the analysis contact of the beyond Standard Model Higgs analysis. She is also in charge of the statistical tools in the SUSY group. The Ph.D student Shuhui Huang is the derivation contact in SUSY working group. She will submit her thesis with title" Search for pair production of supersymmetric particles with two same-sign or three leptons final states using 13 TeV pp collision data with the ATLAS detector" by the end of this month. The following talks or posters are presented by my post-doc and students in the group: 1. (Young Scientist Forum Talk) “Searches for supersymmetry with two same-sign or at least three leptons”, The 57th Rencontres de Moriond 2023 on Electroweak Interactions and Unified Theories (MoriondEW2023). 2. (Talk) “ATLAS searches for supersymmetry with prompt particles”, The 11th International Conference on New Frontiers in Physics (ICNFP2022) 3. (Poster) “Search for direct production of electroweak gauginos in events with two same-sign or three leptons in 13 TeV pp collision data with the ATLAS detector”, The 11th International Conference on New Frontiers in Physics (ICNFP2022) 4. (Poster) “Search for ttH/A → tttt production in the multilepton final state in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV with the ATLAS detector”, The 10th Annual Large Hadron Collider Physics Conference (LHCP2022)

17303919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17303919.value: 1. In SUSY search, in topologies with intermediate states including either Wh or WZ pairs, wino masses up to 525 GeV and 250 GeV are excluded, respectively, for a bino of vanishing mass. Higgsino masses smaller than 440 GeV are excluded in a natural R-parity-violating model with bilinear terms. Upper limits on the production cross section of generic events beyond the Standard Model as low as 40 ab are obtained in signal regions optimised for these models and also for an R-parity-violating scenario with baryon-number-violating higgsino decays into top quarks and jets. The analysis significantly improves sensitivity to supersymmetric models and other processes beyond the Standard Model that may contribute to the considered final states. 2. The results are interpreted in the context of a type-II two-Higgs-doublet model. The observed (expected) upper limits at 95% confidence level on the ttH/A production cross-section times the branching ratio of H/A → tt range between 14 (10)fb and 6 (5)fb for a heavy Higgs boson with mass between 400 GeV and 1000 GeV, respectively. Assuming that only one particle, either the scalar H or the pseudo-scalar A, contributes to the tttt final state, values of tan β below 1.2 or 0.5 are excluded for a mass of 400 GeV or 1000 GeV, respectively. These exclusion ranges increase to tan β below 1.6 or 0.6 when both particles are considered. 3. The four-top-quark production cross section is measured to be 24+7-6 fb. This corresponds to an observed (expected) significance with respect to the background-only hypothesis of 4.3 (2.4) standard deviations and provides evidence for this process.

17303919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17303919.value: The LHC started its new run period Run III in 2022. It will run for almost 4 years at the record collision energy of 13.6 TeV. The ATLAS is expected to record more collisions during Run III than in the two previous LHC physics runs combined. The potential of discovering SUSY or beyond SM Higgs bosons is expected to increase with more data and higher collision energy. In addition, in Run II, some common analysis strategies and tools were developed for analyses with the same-sign lepton pair. Those strategies and tools are going to be used for analyses with similar final state in Run III, with some improvements to increase sensitivity.

17303919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17303919.value: The standard model (SM) describing the law of the fundamental particles and their interactions has been very successful in explaining and predicting various experimental results. However, it is not the ultimate theory of particle physics because it fails to answer some fundamental questions, e.g. what is origin of the mass? What is the dark matter? Can strong, weak and electromagnetic forces be unified? This research project aims to search for new physics which answer the open questions in the SM. Those new physics models include SUSY and two-Higgs-doublet models etc. Our research provides important constraints to these theoretical models, which will guide the understanding of fundamental problems in the particle physics field.

17304019.label: Realisation of objectives
17304019.value: In accordance with the foregoing objectives, we have published 8 papers (in which one is a review article) in leading international chemistry journals including three in Angewandte Chemie International Edition, one in ACS Catalysis, one in Organic Letters and two in Organic Chemistry Frontiers. Objective 1: The synthesis and reactivities of sterically encumbered trans-dichlororuthenium(IV) complexes [RuIV(salen)Cl2] containing salen ligands are described. The catalytic reactivity of [RuIV(salen)Cl2] towards oxidation of hydrocarbons was studied and the mechanism of [RuIV(salen)Cl2]-catalyzed C–O bond forming reaction was investigated by high-resolution ESI-MS experiment. Electron paramagnetic resonance measurement lends support for the formation of Ru(V)-oxo intermediate [RuV(tBu-salch)(O)(Cl)]. The findings are described in Dr. Chi-Lun Lee’s PhD thesis and a manuscript is in preparation. Objective 2: We reported the preparation of Ru(=NCOR) intermediates in C−N bond formation catalyzed by [RuIV(Por)Cl2]/N3COR, a catalytic method applicable to aziridine/oxazoline formation from alkenes, amination of substituted indoles, α-amino ketone formation from silyl enol ethers, amination of C(sp3)−H bonds, and functionalization of natural products and carbohydrate derivatives (up to 99 % yield). Experimental studies, including HR-ESI-MS and EPR measurements, coupled with DFT calculations, lend evidence for the formulation of the Ru(NCOR) acylnitrenoids as a RuV-imido species. This work is published in Angewandte Chemie International Edition. With the electron-rich corrole ligand, relatively stable and isolable Ru(V)–arylimido complexes [Ru(tBu-Cor)(NAr)] (H3(tBu-Cor) = 5,15-diphenyl-10-(p-tert-butylphenyl)corrole, Ar = 2,4,6-Me3C6H2 (Mes), 2,6-(iPr)2C6H3 (Dipp), 2,4,6-(iPr)3C6H2 (Tipp), and 3,5-(CF3)2C6H3 (BTF)) can be prepared from [Ru(tBu-Cor)]2 under strongly reducing conditions. This type of Ru(V)-monoarylimido corrole complex with S = 1/2 was characterized by high-resolution ESI mass spectrometry, X-band EPR, resonance Raman spectroscopy, magnetic susceptibility, and elemental analysis, together with computational studies. Under heating/light irradiation (xenon lamp) conditions, the complexes [Ru(tBu-Cor)(NAr)] (Ar = Mes, BTF) could undergo aziridination of styrenes and amination of benzylic C(sp3)–H bonds with up to 90% product yields. This work is published in Chemical Science. Objective 3: We reported chiral iron complexes of meso- and beta-substituted-porphyrins that can catalyze asymmetric intramolecular C(sp3)−H amination of aryl and arylsulfonyl azides to afford chiral indolines (29 examples) and benzofused cyclic sulfonamides (17 examples), respectively, with up to 93 % ee (yield: up to 99 %) using 410 nm light under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies, including DFT calculations, for the reactions of arylsulfonyl azides reveal that the Fe(NSO2Ar) intermediate generated in situ under photochemical conditions reacts with the C(sp3)−H bond through a stepwise hydrogen atom transfer/radical rebound mechanism, with enantioselectivity arising from cooperative noncovalent interactions between the Fe(NSO2Ar) unit and the peripheral substituents of the chiral porphyrin scaffold. This work is published in Angewandte Chemie International Edition. Objectives 3 & 4: Five fluorinated porphyrin-based zirconium metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), F16PMOF-M (M = H2, Pd, Ru(CO), Co, FeCl), featuring ftw-a topology with 2.5 nm cubic cages, were prepared. F16PMOF-FeCl was found to be an effective and recyclable heterogeneous catalyst for direct C(sp3)−H amination of alkyl azides (including azides with benzylic, allylic, secondary, tertiary, and primary C-H bonds) to generate saturated N-heterocycles with up to 91% yield. Notably, F16PMOF-FeCl led to higher product yields than its homogeneous iron-porphyrin molecular catalysts and the unfluorinated isostructural MOFs. F16PMOF-FeCl also catalyzed the C−H amination of aryl azides. Additionally, a “F16PMOF-FeCl + aryl azide + visible-light” protocol was developed for effective intermolecular C–H bond amination of indane and ethylbenzene. The findings is reported in Dr. Yuen Wu’s PhD thesis. Objective 5: We demonstrate that [FeIII(TDCPP)(IMe)2]I (H2TDCPP = tetrakis(2,6-dichlorophenyl)porphyrin, IMe = 1,3-dimethylimidazol-2-ylidene), which was reported previously by us, effectively catalysed C(sp3)–H amination with alkyl azides. This approach offers a complementary approach for the synthesis of structurally complex organic compounds as exemplified by the synthesis of a panel of nitrogen-containing skeletons that are representative examples of various families of natural products and bioactive compounds. This work is published in Organic Chemistry Frontiers. We report that a robust Fe(Cor) complex [Fe(Tp-OMePC)Cl] can catalyze the reactions of a variety of alkyl azides for intramolecular C(sp3)–H (including benzylic, O- and N-adjacent) aminations to afford various 5-, 6- and 7-membered N-heterocycles with up to 3880 TONs and excellent diastereoselectivity, and [FeIII(Tp-OMePC)] (in situ generated by reduction of [Fe(Tp-OMePC)Cl]) gave similar performance. A corrole-supported Fe(V)-alkylimido species that is reactive towards C(sp3)–H bonds was prepared and characterized by various spectroscopic studies. This, together with DFT calculations, supports the Fe(V)-alkylimido species as a key reactive intermediate involved in the Fe-catalyzed intramolecular C(sp3)–H amination reactions of alkyl azides. A manuscript on this work has been submitted for publication. We have designed and synthesized the chiral FeIII-BPsalan complexes for various catalytic organic transformation reactions. A practical, highly efficient iron-catalyzed asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction of various alkylidene β-ketoesters with dienes was developed. Both cyclic and acyclic alkylidene β-ketoesters underwent the reaction well with the Fe-BPsalan complex as the catalyst to afford the addition products including estrone analogues in excellent yields, good to high diastereoselectivities and excellent enantioselectivities under mild reaction conditions. DFT calculations revealed the critical role of the steric effect in directing the reaction selectivity. This work is published in Organic Chemistry Frontiers. We have also designed and synthesized the chiral FeII(N4) complex (N4 = (R,R)-N,N′-bis(2-isopropylquinolin-8-yl)-1,2-diphenylethane-1,2-diamine) for the asymmetric conjugate addition of silyl enol ethers, including both acyclic ones and cyclohexenone-derived ones, to α,β-unsaturated 2-acyl imidazoles. This FeII complex is an effective chiral Lewis acid and was applied in the synthesis of an array of chiral 1,5-dicarbonyl synthons and cyclohexenone derivatives with high yields and enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). This work is published in Organic Letters. We also reported the generation of Fe porphyrin nitrido species by nanosecond laser flash photolysis (LFP) of its FeIII-azido precursor supported by a bulky bis-pocket porphyrin ligand. The hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) reactivity of this Fe-nitrodo species was studied in solutions at room temperature. C−H bonds with bond dissociation enthalpies (BDEs) of up to ≈84 kcal mol−1 could be activated, and the second-order rate constants (k2) are on the order of 102–104 s−1 m−1. The Fe-amido product formed after HAT could further release ammonia upon protonation. This work is published in Angewandte Chemie International Edition. An FeIV-oxo corrole π-cation radical complex, [FeIVO(TTPPC+•)] (TTPPC = 5,10,15-tris(2,4,6-triphenylphenyl)corrinato(3-)) was identified, which belongs to [FeIVO(corrole+•)] species previously proposed as the active intermediate in [FeIII(corrole)]-catalyzed oxidation reactions. Complex [FeIVO(TTPPC+•)] was generated by oxidizing [FeIII(TTPPC)] with excess sPhIO (sPhIO = t-BuSO2PhIO). Treatment of [FeIII(TTPPC)] with 1 equiv of sPhIO gave [FeIII(TTPPC)(sPhIO)] adduct (identified by UV-vis, 1H NMR, IR, and EPR spectroscopies). Complex [FeIVO(TTPPC+•)] was spectroscopically characterized by UV-vis, ESI-MS, 1H NMR, and EPR, along with good reactivity in alkene epoxidation. Oxidation of C-H bonds by [FeIVO(TTPPC+•)] was also observed, in which hydrogen atom transfer is the rate-limiting step as evidenced by kinetic isotope effect and a linear relationship between log k and the C-H bond dissociation energy. This work is reported in Dr. Bin Zheng’s PhD thesis

17304019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304019.value: [1] 8 publications (in which one is a review article) in leading international chemistry journals namely Angewandte Chemie International Edition, ACS Catalysis, Organic Letters, Organic Chemistry Frontiers and European Journal of Inorganic Chemistry. [2] We developed [Ru(IV)(Por)Cl2] as effective catalyst for various C–N bond formation reactions. Experimental studies, including HR-ESI-MS and EPR measurements, coupled with DFT calculations, lend evidence for the formulation of the Ru(NCOR) acylnitrenoids as a RuV-imido species. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 18619-18629) [3] We employed the trianionic corrole ligand to stabilize the highly reactive high valent Ru(V)-arylimido species. A series of [Ru(tBu-Cor)(NAr)] has been synthesized and characterized spectroscopically. Under heat/light irradiation conditions, [Ru(tBu-Cor)(NAr)] could transfer its imido ligand for aziridination of styrenes and amination of benzylic C(sp3)–H bonds with up to 90% product yields. (Chem. Sci. 2023, 14, 10602-10609) [4] We designed and synthesized a chiral iron(III) complex of meso- and beta-substituted-porphyrins for asymmetric intramolecular C(sp3)−H amination of aryl and arylsulfonyl azides using 410 nm light under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies, including DFT calculations, reveal the generation of Fe(NSO2Ar) intermediate in situ under photochemical conditions, which subsequently reacts with the C(sp3)−H bond through a stepwise hydrogen atom transfer/radical rebound mechanism. Enantioselectivity arising from cooperative noncovalent interactions between the Fe(NSO2Ar) unit and the peripheral substituents of the chiral porphyrin scaffold. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202218577) [5] Several Fe-based catalysts (such as chiral FeIII-BPsalan, chiral Fe(II)(N4), [FeIII(TDCPP)(IMe)2]I, FeIII(corrole)) have been prepared for asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction (Org. Chem. Front. 2021, 8, 1910-1917), asymmetric conjugate addition of silyl enol ethers (Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 6993-6997), C(sp3)–H amination reaction (Org. Chem. Front. 2021, 8, 1910-1917) and C-H bond oxidation reaction (unpublished results). With the use of our previously designed [FeIII(TDCPP)(IMe)2]I as catalyst, a panel of nitrogen-containing structurally complex skeletons that are representative examples of various families of natural products and bioactive compounds has been synthesized. [6] We have generated the Fe porphyrin nitrido species by nanosecond laser flash photolysis (LFP) of its FeIII-azido precursor supported by a bulky bis-pocket porphyrin ligand, which could undergo hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) with C–H bonds. (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 60, 4796-4803) [7] An extra work related to the synthesis and characterization of Ru heterobridged molecular wheels from Ru3(CO)12, 2,4,6-triisopropylbenzenethiol (HSTrip) and HX (X=Cl, Br) or I2. These hexa- and octanuclear heterobridged wheels featuring thiolate/halide mixed bridging ligands have all been characterized by X-ray crystallography as well as spectroscopic means including NMR, IR and ESI-MS. (Eur. J. Inorg. Chem. 2022, 2022, e202200499)

17304019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304019.value: With the results from this project, iron-porphyrin-catalyzed highly enantioselective alkylnitrene transfer reactions that proceed under ambient temperature were achieved by visible light irradiation. The use of metalloporphyrin-based MOFs as heterogeneous catalysts also ease the separation of the catalyst from the reaction mixture and recycling of the catalysts. These could highly facilitate the Practical synthesis of natural products, pharmaceuticals and/or fine chemicals. Further investigation of the potential of chiral Fe(N4) and Fe-BPsalan catalysts on other enantioselective organic transformation reactions will be also be performed. Meanwhile, valuable information about the high valent metal-nitrene and –oxo intermediates have been obtained during the course of this project. We are planning to expand our study to establish the relationship between the identity of the intermediate (metal-imido/imidyl radical/nitrene) and the electronic property of the ligand. We envision that by modifying the ligand systematically, the nature of such intermediates could then be fine-tuned to achieve enantioselective C–H amination and oxidation reactions.

17304019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304019.value: N- and O-group transfers to inert saturated hydrocarbons streamline syntheses of bio-active molecules and pharmaceuticals, and minimize the use of protecting/deprotecting reagents and production of by-products and wastes. However, direct C-H functionalization always requires harsh reaction conditions and the use of toxic reagents (e.g. halogen-containing compounds). One of the key elements to develop efficient and green synthetic methods for organic transformations is to employ novel metal catalysts, in which their catalytic properties can be fine-tuned by sophisticatedly designed supporting macrocyclic ligands. In this project, we have successfully developed various Ruthenium and Iron catalysts for nitrene and oxo transfer reactions. The use of iron-based catalysts earns extra credits from their inexpensive price and biocompatibility. In particular, we have successfully applied the developed nitrene transfer reaction on the synthesis of structurally complex N-containing natural products and bioactive compounds. We also isolated and characterized the reactive high valent metal-imido intermediates, enriching our understanding on the properties of such species. Such remarkable findings were published in leading international chemistry journals including Angewandte Chemie International Edition, ACS Catalysis, Organic Letters and Organic Chemistry Frontiers. From a macroscopic point of view, the aforementioned achievements expedite the development of metal-catalyzed organic transformation reactions in a world-class level.

17304519.label: Project Objectives
17304519.value: Construct lens models for, especially, non-viriliazed clusters in the Reionization Cluster Lensing Survey (RELICS) with the Hubble Space Telescope, and clusters of interest from other surveys. Our free-form approach serves as an important check on the fidelity of the lens models produced by the RELICS team using a parametric or light-traces-mass approach. Determine the geometric redshifts of candidate distant galaxies having uncertain if not ambiguous redshifts discovered in the RELICS program and other surveys. Directly weigh supermassive black holes in distant lensing galaxies, focusing on cases where it is possible to break the degeneracy between a SMBH and a varying mass-to-light ratio in the lensing galaxy, as in our previous work. Expand upon our work to study the properties of galaxies in the early Univers using a larger sample of lensed galaxies discovered in the RELICS program, and to use the results to test ψDM vs CDM. Complete our ongoing theoretical and observational work to test whether Dark Matter exhibits strong and fine granulations.
