17304519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304519.value: 宇宙中大部分的质量以暗物质的形式存在。星系和星系团形成于暗物质晕中，而暗物质也保证了星系团有足够的引力维持其物质组成和形状。但是，究竟什么是暗物质？在暗物质晕中的气体是什么时候开始形成恒星，并演化为如今可见的星系的？而宇宙早期的星系又有怎样的性质？当我们通过引力透镜现象去研究暗物质的物理性质时，我们也同时在观测被引力透镜现象放大了的早期星系，因此我们可以同时研究以上提到的问题。 在过去的五年中，我们在香港大学组建了一个不断壮大的科研团队，训练了一批有才华的学生来研究引力透镜在天文学上的应用。我们的学生在本科期间就开始接受相关训练，并逐渐开展科研项目，最终将项目发展为研究生或博士阶段的课题。很多相关课题都由我们的研究组首次提出。我们的研究组利用大质量的星系或星系团形成的引力透镜，而数据则来源于哈勃望远镜，是目前世界上最高质量的相关数据。 （1） 暗物质的结构： 在进行2016RGC/GRF的研究工作时，我们已经为Hubble Frontier Fields（HFF）项目中的全部六个星系团和Cluster Lensing And Supernova survey with Hubble (CLASH)项目中的部分星系团创建了透镜模型。这些模型准确地描述了暗物质在大尺度上的空间结构。我们通过研究模型是否能准确预测透镜成像的位置和形状，成像光源的红移，以及不同的像之间的相对亮度来判断我们的透镜模型的准确度。我们的模型成功预测了首次被引力透镜折射形成多个像的超新星的成像位置和时间。我们计划将相关研究延续到Reionization Cluster Lensing Survey (RELICS)项目，这是哈勃望远镜最新的大范围引力透镜星团项目。 （2） 宇宙早期的星系： 宇宙早期的星系能谱与中红移的椭圆星系的能谱非常相似，因此很难分辨出宇宙早期的星系。当没有光谱红移的时候，单纯通过引力透镜几何结构来推测的红移能够比能谱更准确地推测出星系的红移。我们计划将进一步发展此项先驱研究，以准确测量RELICS项目中的遥远星系的几何红移。 （3） 测量超大质量黑洞的质量： 星系是否与星系中心的超大质量黑洞同步演化？要回答这个问题，我们需要先了解超大质量黑洞随着宇宙演化的质量分布。我们之前的研究已经验证了引力透镜现象可以被用来直接测量遥远星系中超大质量黑洞的质量。我们计划将这项研究扩展到新发现的适用的数据上。 （4） 暗物质的观测性测试： 我们已经证实了哈勃HFF项目中的引力透镜光源星系的空间密度在低亮度的范围内并不持续增加。相比冷暗物质，这一现象更加符合波暗物质的理论预测。相关测量还预测了玻色子的质量，并解释了在本星系群中的暗物质主导的低质量星系的核机构。我们还发现了在再电离阶段的中期，高亮度的星系的空间密度显著增加。我们计划用RELICS项目中更大量的远距离星系的数据来延展此项研究。 （5） 波暗物质的米粒组织： 组成波暗物质的玻色子在量子干涉下会形成米粒组织，这是波暗物质的独特性质。我们认为我们在此方面的先驱研究可以解释引力透镜现象中在小尺度上的亮度变化，并正在开展大质量星系和星系团透镜的观测研究来验证这一推测是否正确。

17304519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304519.value: Demonstration of the need for Dark Matter around galaxies based purely on the geometry of gravitational lensing (Chen et al. 2020, ApJ); dynamical arguments for Dark Matter (DM) can be equally well explained by alternative theories of gravity. Analytical framework for density modulations induced by quantum interference of ultra-light DM particles, and its effects on gravitational lensed images (Hiroki et al. 2022, ApJ). Computer simulations of gravitationally-lensed images generated by galaxies possessing halos comprising ultra-light DM particles - showing that this form of DM is able to resolve long-standing lensing anomalies left by lens models based on ultra-massive DM particles. The ability of such wave-like DM to resolve lensing anomalies, together with its success in reproducing other astrophysical observations, tilt the balance toward new physics invoking axions. The latter has been invoked to alleviate deficiencies in the Standard Model of particle physics, and is one of the two leading contenders (along with WIMPs) for DM (Alfred et al. 2023, Nature Astronomy). Also, the PI took a foray into a dynamical test of DM, so as to better understand the relative merits of different tests for the nature of DM (Pozo et al. 2021, MNRAS).

17304519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304519.value: Accepting the Theory of General Relativity as the correct theory of gravitation requires a leap of faith: that much of the matter in the Universe, whether it be located in galaxies, small groups of galaxies, large cluster of galaxies, or in cosmic filaments, is in a form that neither emits nor absorbs light and which interact with ordinary matter only through gravity (so far as we can tell). This invisible form of matter is known as Dark Matter (DM). Alternatives to the Theory of General Relativity that do away with DM (hence, for which all gravity is associated with visible matter) are plentiful, perhaps the best known of which is Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND). The existence, and nature, of DM are not just esoteric debates among astronomers: the existence of DM is the clearest evidence that the Standard Model for particle physics is far from complete. Theoretical extensions to address deficiencies in the Standard Model predict hypothetical particles (e.g., WIMPs and Axions) that have been proposed as candidates for DM. Identifying the nature of DM, widely regarded as the most important problem in all of physics, therefore promises to point the correct path towards New Physics. In our work, we showed the need for DM around galaxies based purely on the geometry of gravitational lensing. Next we developed an analytical framework for density modulations induced by quantum interference of ultra-light DM particles, and its effects on gravitational lensed images. Finally, we conducted computer simulations showing that such wave-like DM is able to resolve long-standing lensing anomalies left by lens models based on ultra-massive DM particles. The ability of such wave-like DM to resolve lensing anomalies, together with its success in reproducing other astrophysical observations, tilt the balance toward new physics invoking axions.

17304619.label: Project Objectives
17304619.value: To test the hypothesis that ocean acidification (OA) alters crystal orientation in oyster shells through the production of crystal orientation rotating shell matrix proteins (CR-SMPs). To isolate and identify CR-SMPs from OA exposed shells using the power of shotgun proteomics and bioassay-guided fractionation techniques. To define CR-SMPs function as crystal orientation rotating macromolecule using in vitro crystallization bioassays. To validate CR-SMPs function using in vivo with RNA interference experiments. To correlate CR-SMP genes and protein expressions to shell microstructure and mechanical properties to test the hypothesis that the oyster mantle tissue regulates CR-SMPs expression to compensate for the negative OA effects on shell structure and mechanical properties. To integrate current and previous project data in order to project the impact of OA on biomineralization in oysters.

17304619.value: 食用牡蛎具有令人难以置信的复杂的壳微结构，具有令人难以置信的高机械强度。 这种外壳是通过称为生物矿化涉及壳基质蛋白(SMPs)促进、加速和抑制碳酸钙(CaCO3)晶体的成核的生化过程中形成的。 尽管SMPs仅占壳总重量的<5%，但它们控制晶相切换和取向，从而控制壳的微观结构和机械性能。 这些SMPs的表达是由遗传和环境因素之间的相互作用来控制的。 在过去的一个世纪中，这种生物控制的矿化过程一直是一个热门的研究课题，并吸引了跨学科的科学家从材料科学、海洋生物学和机械工程的多项研究。 然而，只有在最近几年，我们已经能够向前移动领域，由于更多地获得新的高科技分子技术。 因此，到目前为止，只有几个SMPs已被纯化和功能特征探索其诱导和控制CaCO3晶体形成的能力。 我们不完全知道这些蛋白质是如何相互作用，结合离子，核，并在海洋壳，这将是应用和基础研究具有重要意义的控制晶体方向。 目前，海洋生物矿化的一个详细的了解是特别相关的CaCO3资源在海洋枯竭，由于当前和未来的气候变化引起的海洋酸化（OA）的过程。 我们的研究小组在过去的几年中已经成功地研究了OA下的牡蛎生物矿化。 我们已经验证了较低的CO3-2饱和状态的海水诱导OA导致牡蛎壳微观结构的变化。 根据我们最近的研究结果，以优良的肉品质养殖的香港(香港)马加拉那(Magallana hongkongensis)的食用和特有的牡蛎品种，往往会以有利的方式改变晶体取向，以提高OA下的壳体机械强度。 具体而言，我们发现晶体取向在OA下从θ40o改变到θ70o。 我们知道SMPs控制牡蛎壳的微观结构，但SMPs和CaCO3晶体取向之间的关联尚未阐明。 在此拟议的研究中，我们将表征SMPs参与控制晶体的方向，目的是研究oa对使用牡蛎壳作为模型的晶体SMPs功能相互作用的调制效果。 为扩阔我们对CaCO3生物质能的了解，并提升其在材料科学的适用性，我们建议找出SMPs在控制香港蠔_unk_蠔壳的晶体方向及决定生物质能的命运方面的作用。 这个目标可以通过以下步骤实现: 步骤1：在不同CaCO3饱和水平（对照和OA处理）下生长牡蛎-实验状态：已完成。 第二步：了解在不同处理条件下生长的牡蛎壳的微观结构和晶体取向-实验状态：已完成。 第3步：使用壳牌蛋白质组学和生物化学识别涉及改变壳牌晶体取向的SMPs-实验状态：初步工作开始。 第4步：功能表征和鉴定SMPs的验证同时使用体外CaCO3结晶和体内RNA干扰（基因沉默）检测-实验状态：本次研究的重点。 这项研究的结果与我们和其他人以前的研究结果相结合，将使我们能够准确确定CACO3生物学家在OA面前的命运。 重要的是，从牡蛎壳的微观结构和晶体组装的interlay获得的知识也将为组织工程应用的强光CaCO3材料的设计提供新的见解，从而加快牡蛎激发生物材料的发现。

17304619.label: Realisation of objectives
17304619.value: We have successfully and productively accomplished all the six goals and objectives of this project. This success was possible because of the recruitment of the highly talented graduate student from interdisciplinary background and great cooperation from both local (Kelvin Yeung from HKU) and overseas collaborators (Michio Suzuki from University of Tokyo). Our team has also brought few other collaborators to make sure we have made use of the all the data collected from this project – e.g. we have collaborated with a mechanical engineering expert from Hong Kong Polytechnic University (Haimin Yao) and an oyster aquaculture expert from Chinese Academy of Science (Zinu Yu). The students who has worked for this project had great access to work in three different institutions, the University of Hong Kong, Polytechnic University of Hong Kong and South China Institute of Oceanology – as a result we have accomplished more than what was promised to deliver for this project – e.g. published 9 high quality papers (all attached with this report), two more are under review and trained over three graduate students (also listed here). One of the major outcomes of this project is interdisciplinary (science and engineering) and comparative (two different species) approach adapted to achieve all the six objectives. The listed papers in this report show such interdisciplinary and inter-institutional collaboration. Although, COVID restrictions and social impacts, have severely affected the smooth progress of this project, we managed to successfully complete the projects – thanks to our resilient interdisciplinary collaborative lab members and research team. Here, we will briefly explain how we have accomplished those six objectives. Objectives 1and 2; 5 and 6 (Crystal orientation in oyster shells – modulating effect of ocean acidification): This is one of the key and major objectives of this project. Our graduated student (now working as senior Post doctoral fellow in City University of Hong Kong), Dr Kanmani – served as a backbone for the execution of this project. She has come with biominerlization background and then we have trained her basic skills required for shell structural analysis, proteomics and also to run ocean acidification experiments. She has quickly learned those biological skills. Immediately, she had run ocean acidification experiments to collect shell samples of the two oyster species. Then, she has employed variety of material analysis tools, e.g. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and Electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) – to study crystal orientation in oyster shells of two different species. In no time, she has become a local expert in EBSD analysis – thanks to her visit to UK (University of Glasgow to work with Prof Maggie and Dr Susan) for training Kanmani on those techniques. As a result, she has published FOUR high quality papers (in Global Change Biology and in Royal Society B) and also successfully defended her PhD thesis in 2022. Objective 2 (oyster shell proteomics and crystal orientation rotating protein): Realization of this objective is one of the difficult part of this project. This is because, extraction of adequate amount of proteins from oysters shells which is having only less than 5% of its volume, especially from tiny early life stages. Therefore, we are forced to recruit another graduate student, Miss Alessia Cairini, using RGC-HKPF support, to carry out this task. She has made good progress and developed a methodology to isolate adequate amount of proteins from oyster shells using unique protocol (published in Limnology and Oceanography). Moreover, our other graduate student, Miss Kanmani Rajan, was able to use this protocol and isolated proteins from oyster shells to study ocean acidification effects on oyster shell crystal orientation changing proteins (find attached her PhD thesis chapter). Objectives 3 and 4: These two objectives are highly interlinked and heavily dependent on tools borrowed from our Co-investigator of the project, Prof Michio Suzuki from Tokyo University. We have specifically recruited a PhD student, Mr Li Yang, to execute this part of the project. These objectives involved knockdown of shell proteins and then validation of the differentially expressed proteins using RNA interference experiments. This also involved crystal formation bioassays using those isolated shell proteins. The COVID lockdown and serious travel restrictions has significantly affected this part of the work. Nevertheless, Li Yang has managed to perform these experiments and collected good amount of data to just complete this part of the objectives of this project. However, Mr Li Yang, unfortunately, has got some issues and then changed his research topic. But, we are continuing this work and highly confident of publishing those data in coming few months. Overall outcome: 1) Besides 9 publications, three PhD thesis report have been completed; 2) A post doc was trained, Dr Kanmani Chandran 3) The result has been used to develop hypothesis for a new RGC-GRF proposal to study transgenerational effects of ocean acidification on shell proteomics, including crystal orientation rotating proteins. The outcome of this project leads us to develop new Collaborative Research Fund (CRF) proposal. Briefly, the data collected from this project helped us to develop a new proposal on “Oyster inspired 3D-printed biomimetic scaffold for bone tissue engineering”. This proposal details the development of oyster shell microstructure inspired biomimetic material that will serve as scaffolds for bone tissue engineering. Knowledge Exchange and Societal Impact: • Impact case study and knowledge exchange activities: This project has helped us to move forward with knowledge exchange related activities, i.e. we are currently investigating the significance of community engagement for the sustainability of local oyster aquaculture under climate change – and use this new approach to transfer technology from academics to stakeholders to provide integrated solutions to manage the impacts of climate change. This project results has helped us to develop a new impact case study for our school as follows: Draft Impact case study: Over the years, we have established stable research collaboration with (1) local and international oyster scientists, (2) oyster aquaculture growers in both Hong Kong and South China, (3) government departments who are implementing policy over coastal aquaculture in Hong Kong, and (4) oyster hatchery around the world. As a result of such strong multi-stakeholder interaction, we have produced research services and outputs that have started showing an impact on oyster aquaculture locally in Hong Kong (e.g. growers able to depurate oysters and sell into the local market for significantly higher price than before our intervention). We have several rounds of discussion with various stakeholders in this regard, and have started collecting evidences of the impact that our research is having on aquaculture. We will continue to work in this direction.

17304619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304619.value: Key Finding 1 (Global Change Biology, 2021; PhD thesis of Kanmani, 2022): Edible oysters are well known not only nutritious delicacies, but also for their ability to produce shells with incredible structural complexity and remarkable mechanical strength. Oysters have evolved sophisticated biomineralization machinery to assemble CaCO3 crystal units into a structurally complex shell microstructure that is several-fold stronger than the inorganic constituents. Shell matrix proteins (SMPs) embedded within the shell crystals play important functions in determining crystal size, morphology, orientation, and thus shell hardness, elasticity, and fracture toughness, despite only accounting for a small proportion of the shell weight (<5%). In this highly comprehensive and comparative approach, we have shown how global climate change imposed stressors, such as ocean acidification, affect this critical process of mineralization in various oyster species. This paper in one of the high impact factor journals in our field, showed how swell crystal orientation rotating proteins and other shell matrix proteins functionally interplay to affect microstructures and mechanical properties in oyster shell. Through this project, it has been well established that there is change in shell crystallography as a response to environmental stressors which is referred to as Crystallographic Vital Effect (CVE). This change in crystal orientations is also known to be controlled at molecular level. There is also some basic evidence for ion transporting mechanisms in oysters. In this integrated study, we have used DNA methylation, mRNA sequencing and CVE to understand oyster biomineralisation under ocean acidification (OA) using a moderately resilient, estuarine, and commercial species Crassostrea hongkongensis. Finding 2 (Proc Royal Soc B 2023): Shells produced by marine organisms under ocean acidification (OA) are expected to be corroded with disorganized or impaired crystal orientation or microstructures with reduced mechanical strength. We have tested this hypothesis using two oyster species that tend to make shells with different mechanical and structural features. Our comparative study revealed bottom-up deterioration induced by OA on oyster shells, especially in their early juvenile life stage. This knowledge is critical to forecast the survival and production of edible oysters in future ocean. Finding 3 (Limnology and Oceanography, 2023; PhD Thesis of Cairni Alessia): We have identified a novel methodology to isolate organic matrix proteins from shells of the two oyster species. Also we have characterized those shell proteins and identified their functional role in shell making process using variety of modern proteomics tools (see the attached PhD thesis report of Dr Kanmani Rajan and Dr Cairini Alessia). These results have implications on understanding progression of oyster shell formation in future oceans with high variability in OA.

17304619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304619.value: Discovered a new finding (Science and Total Environment 2021; Mar Environ Res 2021; Molecular Ecology 2023): This project discovered using the transgenerational (parents to offspring) studies that oysters are able to adjust and improve their acclimation capacity to survive ocean acidification through transgenerational plasticity (TGP). Based on this KEY finding, we have proposed and obtained another GRF grant to understand benefits of such OA-induced epigenetic TGP adaptations of oysters within a few generations, the longevity of these adaptive traits over multiple generations and the molecular mechanisms that mediate these important responses. Thus, this project result has helped to explore the TGP adaption potential, as well as the underlying mechanisms, and trade-offs to determine whether oyster species living in a variable environments can adapt to OA.

17304619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304619.value: Oyster shells, which are made of ~95% calcium carbonate and 5% organic molecules are incredibly strong with unique structural features. This superior mechanical strength is achieved through secretion of shell matric proteins, which are governing growth and arrangement of crystals in oyster shells. This project in collaboration with material scientists and biomedical engineers, has studied oyster shell structure and associated proteins, especially those crystal orientation changing matrix proteins. We have found that Hong Kong oysters when comparing a closely related sister species Portuguese oyster has better mechanical strength because of the interdigitation pattern observed in the folia layer of Hong Kong oyster shells and they possess a species specific highly shell matrix proteins. This project precisely determined the specific role of oyster shell proteins on crystal growth, especially when oysters are under ocean acidification stress. The knowledge gained from the interlay of microstructure and crystal assembly in oyster shells has provided novel insights for the design of strong and light CaCO3 materials for tissue engineering applications and thus, accelerated the discovery of oyster-inspired biomaterials.

17304719.label: Project Objectives
17304719.value: We will construct the appropriate hydrodynamic equations for charge and spin transport in a spin-orbit coupled Bose gas using kinetic equation approach and identify the microscopic scattering amplitudes that enter the collision integral for spin current relaxation. We will discuss the effects of umklapp scattering in spin conductivity in optical lattices and also the role of forward scattering amplitude in spin dynamics.

17304719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17304719.value: The study of relaxation dynamics occupies a unique position in many-body physics. It reveals the underlying scattering mechanism in many-body systems and offers crucial insights into the microscopic details of the system such as symmetries and conservation laws dictated by the microscopic Hamiltonian. As an example, the Korringa relation that relates the spin relaxation and Knight shift in nuclear magnetic resonance tells us how strong the correlation effects are in the system. In the past decades, due to impressive advances in the trapping and manipulating of cold atoms in a harmonic trap or in an optical lattice, the study of dynamic and in particular, relaxation phenomena in cold atoms has emerged as a frontier in cold atom research. As compared with studies in condensed matter system, there are a few distinctive advantages especially with the realisation of single site imaging technique in cold atoms. Recently, there have been several studies of charge/spin relaxation of a two-component Fermi gas in optical lattice which revealed, among other things, the temperature and interaction dependences of the relaxation rate and their implications. In this proposal, we will investigate spin relaxation in two systems where certain symmetry is broken. In the first case, we study the spin current relaxation in a spin-orbit coupled Bose gas in its normal state. This relaxation is more complicated than the usual spin relaxation due to breaking of su(2) spin rotation symmetry. The following aspects will be investigated: (1) The construction of spin dynamical equations via Boltzmann transport equation and (2) The explicit computation of collision integral that determines the spin relaxation time. In the second case, we will study the spin transport in an optical lattice that breaks the translational symmetry and determine the relative importance of umklapp scattering as compared with normal scattering in damping the spin current. In this part, we will be mostly interested in the weak coupling limit and investigate its temperature dependences. In both parts, we will try to take into account the effects of forward scattering (Hartree-Fock mean field effects) in relaxation dynamics. 弛豫现象是凝聚态物理中一个重要的研究方向。它给出了多体体系中的微观散射机制以及对称性和守恒律。例如Korringa以及Knight定律描述的自旋弛豫给出自旋关联的强度。最近几年来，由于光晶格和谐振子势中冷原子调控的进步，研究冷原子中的输运以及弛豫现象称为一个重要的前沿方向。例如最近几年来，实验学家利用原子显微镜研究了原子和自旋的输运行为，尤其是相互作用和温度的影响。在这个项目中，我们将研究自旋输运行为，尤其是当一些对称性被破坏之后。我们在这里将选择研究两类例子，一类是研究自旋轨道耦合中的自选流衰减行为。另外一类是研究无平移对称性的情况下自旋输运行为。在这两个研究中，我们将注意温度以及相互作用的影响。

17304719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304719.value: In this proposal, the following are achieved: 1. An investigation based on hydrodynamic equations on the expansion dynamics in the presence of time-dependent interaction in unitary Fermi gas is carried out with effects of scattering taken into account. This work is published in PRL in 2022 (paper 1). 2. In the second work, we worked on the low-energy hydrodynamic theory (non-linear Luttinger liquid) and investigate the effects of scattering on the transport quantity, namely bulk viscosity and found that to second order in the the coupling constant at weak coupling and 1/coupling constant in the strong coupling, there is no Drude weight. We calculate the regular part of the viscosity spectral function across the BEC-BCS crossover at low and high temperature. This work is published in PRA (paper 4). 3. An experiment-theory collaboration on the 1D Fermi gas explored its correlation function and the emergence of s-wave interaction. It is related to the spin relaxation (in this case, isomorphic to the band relaxation) in the strongly interacting regime (paper 5). 4. We explored the effects of feedback induced coupling between spins in different cells and found that they generate various different dynamical phases. The relevant dynamic equations are the standard Bloch equation and the spin relaxation are included in the standard approximation (paper 6). 5. In addition, the project also supported partly the work that were done by postdoc Xinloong Han (I am not a co-author) and published as paper 2 and paper 3. It is related to the dynamics of unitary Fermi gas and its chaotic behaviour. 6. I also worked with my postdoc Xinloong Han on the effect of Umklapp scattering in spin dynamics. The relevant paper is under preparation.

17304719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304719.value: This proposal has seeded many further research work that I am working on now. For example, the most important direction is the calculation of viscosity Drude weight that we are looking at now. In our previous work (paper 4), we found that a naive second order perturbation calculation gave no Drude weight in viscosity spectral function. It thus become important to explore the Drude weight to higher orders. This is what we are doing now using Bethe Ansatz and generalized hydrodynamics. The transport explored in paper 1 has now led to experimental efforts in Wuhan institute of Mathematics and Physics where relevant effects are now actively explored.

17304719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17304719.value: Spin dynamics are relevant in many areas in physics and have many potential applications. For example, in NMR (or MRI), the spins of proton are being monitored during the dynamical process that give information about the organic or inorganic compounds. In more sophisticated cases, interactions between spins are important and lead to more sophisticated spin dynamics, and must be included. The proposal aims to explore some properties of spin related physics in a many-body system and understand how interaction might be important. This has been an active field of research in cold atom research. Particularly, we have been able to show how low-energy hydrodynamics can be an effective way to describe the spin dynamics and calculated the macroscopic parameters that enter into the hydrodynamic theory.

17304919.value: 质谱多肽裂解基础研究可以发挥关键作用。不仅为基于下一代质谱（MS）的测序技术和快速蛋白质鉴定提供科学基础，而且还为一般意义上的自由基介导的蛋白质反应提供科学基础，包括与推动自由基介导的肽化学过程相关的可能的自由基介导反应途径；例如，氧化翻译后蛋白质修饰 - 自由基诱导的化学蛋白质修饰 - 由于细胞活性自由基氧化物和氮化物的普遍存在而在体内和体外产生，并改变蛋白质结构和/或功能。氢原子转移（HAT）和质子转移是测定后续自由基介导肽反应途径的关键步骤。该项目的目标是通过HAT获得在原子水平上对肽异构体之间相互转换的实验结果。我们计划阐明控制异构化过程中自由基迁移可行性的内在因素。我们将整合不同实验方法，包括（i）气相中合成各种典型自由基母离子异构体结构; （ii）表面或碰撞诱导解离[（S / C）ID]及同位素标记;（iii）红外多光子解离（IRMPD）和紫外 - 可见光作用光谱，以检测其在气相中的结构，并将其与基于B3LYP和M06-2X功能的密度泛函理论（DFT） - 计算光谱进行比较; （iv）Rice-Ramsperger-Kassel-Marcus（RRKM）建模，以研究和确定电荷和自旋分布对母离子和产物结构的关键作用。特别地，我们将重点关注具有明确定义的初始自由基位点的原型肽，（a）使用串联质谱确定多肽主链和侧链残基内促进多肽内部HAT的异构化障碍;（b）研究肽自由基阳离子中明确定义的初始自由基位点如何转移到具有相对高（约50kcal / mol）和低（<30kcal / mol）DFT理论相互转换屏障的其他自由基位点（在项目的最后阶段，我们将进行实验研究，专注初步探索于模型系统，这些相互转换来自其选定的单键解离产生的碎片产物）；（c）初步探索其结构如何在量上影响简单原型自由基肽系统异构化屏障的动能学和动力学。这些研究将为在控制HAT并促进选定的异构化过程中基本位点和自由基移动的作用的内在因素提供有非常有价值的见解。

17304919.label: Realisation of objectives
17304919.value: The objective of this project was to obtain an experimental understanding at the atomic level of the interconversions between radical peptide isomers. The project aimed to use an integrated approach involving gas-phase synthesis of a variety of prototypical radical precursor isomeric structures, tandem mass spectrometry, action spectroscopy, isotopic labeling, and theoretical calculations. The project focused on prototypical peptides featuring well-defined initial radical sites to determine the isomerization barriers that facilitate hydrogen atom transfers (HATs) within peptides, examine how the well-defined initial radical sites of peptide radical cations propagate to other radical sites, and explore how their structures quantitatively impact the energetics of the isomerization barrier of a simple prototypical radical peptide system. Key Findings: The research project aimed to understand how structural features lead to radical-induced backbone and side-chain bond cleavages during isomerizations via HAT propagation, which is the scientific basis of radical-induced peptide chemistry during biological processes under oxidative stress. The project successfully achieved its objectives by using an integrated approach that involved gas-phase synthesis of a variety of prototypical radical precursor isomeric structures, featuring well-defined initial radical sites, and investigating the isomerization barriers that facilitate hydrogen atom transfers (HATs) within peptides, along the peptide backbone and within the side-chain residues. The project achieved its objectives by deciphering structural details of the mass-isolated cationic precursor, product, and potential intermediate, which were further characterized by the action spectroscopic properties of model isomeric systems of radical peptide analogs in conjunction with theoretical DFT calculations. The project also examined how the well-defined initial radical sites of peptide radical cations propagate to other radical sites with relatively high (ca. >50 kcal/mol) and low (<30 kcal/mol) DFT-calculated interconversion barriers. Moreover, the project explored how their structures quantitatively impact the energetics and kinetics of the isomerization barrier of a simple prototypical radical peptide system. Some of those results were published in the list of publications 1-6. These results provide fundamental insight into the radical-induced backbone and side-chain bond cleavages during isomerizations thought hydrogen and/or proton transfer(s). The project's postgraduate students were trained in experimental and computational approaches on radical-mediated fragmentation mechanisms regarding structural, energetics, and kinetics aspects. The project successfully achieved its objectives by providing valuable insight into the intrinsic factors that govern HATs and promote selected isomerization processes. The project's postgraduate students were trained in experimental and computational approaches on PTN mechanisms regarding structural, energetics, and kinetics aspects. Two postgraduate students, Alex Li and MengZhu Li, who published research outputs 1-6, were involved and trained to perform research in fundamental and biological mass spectrometry. They were co-supervised by the Co-I of the project, Andy Siu, from the Department of Biology and Chemistry at City University of Hong Kong, for our interdisciplinary mass spectrometry-DFT calculation research. However, detecting PTN-modified peptides with mass spectrometry is challenging due to their low abundance. To fully understand this modification, it is necessary to increase the number of known PTN sites, which can be achieved by improving mass spectrometry instrumentation and liquid chromatography sensitivity and utilizing bioinformatic analyses. Armed with the aforementioned results, the team also developed a bioinformatic tool, rPTMDetermine, to retrieve post-translationally modified peptide identifications using a machine learning algorithm. They invested efforts in developing new liquid chromatography separation technologies to improve proteomics experiments' duty cycle usage, leading to a 10% increase in peptide and protein identifications. Overall, the project was a success and achieved its objectives by using an integrated approach that combined experimental and theoretical methods to investigate the interconversions between radical peptide isomers with well-defined initial radical sites. They also provided structural details of the mass-isolated precursor and product cations, which will have significant implications for the field of radical-mediated protein chemistry and will contribute to the development of new strategies for controlling radical-mediated protein modifications involving radical isomerization via hydrogen atom transfers. Radical-induced protein reactions have a significant impact on biological systems by modifying protein functionality post-translationally, altering cellular mechanisms, and contributing to the progression of diseases. Identifying the specific location of radicals on a protein is crucial in understanding the site-specificity and regioselectivity of radical-mediated processes and their role in disease. This knowledge serves as a scientific foundation for studying the function of protein radicals in biochemical processes. In particular, the research findings have also helped to understand the regioselectivity of radical-mediated tyrosine nitration processes in biology. The project outcomes will also be useful for the development of new radical-based protein modifications with tailored properties.

17304919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17304919.value: Our research aims to gain a comprehensive understanding of radical-induced peptide chemistry and its role in backbone and side-chain bond cleavages. The hallmark of this research is to elucidate the underlying mechanisms of these processes during isomerizations via HAT propagation. We aim to systematically design, generate, and characterize radical peptide systems that lead to the gas-phase formation of stable radical-mediated modified peptides. Our publications shed light on different aspects of the proposal's objectives, including the systematic characterization of the action spectroscopic properties of model isomeric systems of radical peptide analogs and the determination of the structures, energetics, and dynamics of single-channel product formation via selective bond cleavage. In collaboration with Co-Is, we have presented the first evidence for the elementary radical-mediated reaction mechanism of gas-phase tyrosine nitration (Publications 1-4). The published results have helped to understand the regioselectivity of tyrosine nitration in biology, explored the gas-phase dissociation of a prototypical system, and indicated that PTN is possible for various precursor tautomers. Publication 3 provided experimental evidence for the elementary steps of the radical-mediated mechanism in the gas phase, which provided fundamental insight into the regioselectivity of biological tyrosine ortho-nitration. Publication 2 elucidated the mechanism of formation of the captodative tyrosyl-containing radical species with the charge site separated from the radical site and suggested that the Cα-Cβ bond cleavage of the tyrosine residue in the radical cationic precursor involves through-space electron transfer between the indolyl and phenolic groups. Publication 1 reported the first detailed study of the mechanism of redox reactions occurring during the gas-phase dissociative electron transfer of prototypical ternary copper(II) peptide complexes and provided structural details of the mass-isolated precursor and product cations. The results provided valuable insights into the mechanisms of radical-induced cleavages and redox reactions occurring during the gas-phase dissociative electron transfer of peptides, which can be used to gain a comprehensive understanding of radical-induced peptide chemistry. Our research team hopes that these findings will ultimately assist in understanding radical behavior in protein systems and its role in biological processes under radical-mediated post-translationally modified proteins. The project also serves as a training tool for introducing graduate students to experimental (MS and IRMPD) and computational approaches (DFT calculation) on radical-mediated mechanisms, including structural, energetic, and mechanistic aspects.

17304919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17304919.value: Our research, as described in publications 1-4, indicates that radical-mediated reaction is possible for various precursor tautomers with favorable isomerization barriers including 3-nitrotyrosine formation. However, detecting protein tyrosine nitration (PTN)-modified peptides with mass spectrometry is challenging due to their low abundance. To fully understand this modification, it is necessary to increase the number of known PTN sites. This can be achieved by improving sensitivity, as well as utilizing bioinformatic analyses. We have developed new liquid-chromatography separation technologies, as described in publication 6, such as multiple fraction concatenation 2-dimensional liquid chromatography, which improve proteomics experiments' duty cycle usage and lead to improved peptide and protein identifications. In addition, our bioinformatic tool, described in publication 5, retrieves post-translationally modified peptide identifications using a machine learning algorithm. The published results have also provided structural details of the mass-isolated precursor and product cations, which will have significant implications for the field of radical-mediated protein chemistry. These findings will contribute to the development of new strategies for controlling radical-mediated protein modifications involving radical-isomerization via HATs. Radical-induced protein reactions are the scientific basis for radical-mediated post-translational modifications of protein functionality in biological systems. These modifications alter cellular mechanisms and contribute to the progression of diseases.

17305019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305019.value: The middle Miocene Climatic Optimum (MCO) from ~17 to 14 million years ago (Ma) is one of the substantially warm periods in Earth’s climate history. Global temperatures based on computer model simulations were about 7°C warmer than today, while atmospheric CO2 level at the time has recently been estimated at 300-600 ppm. As our current CO2 level has just reached 400 ppm and will continue to rise due to human activities, how the Earth’ climate, as well as ocean chemistry and marine ecosystem, will respond to the greenhouse gas forcing, is thus a critical scientific question and has important societal values. Although they may not be a good analog to our future climate, studies of past warm climates would gain insights into key climatic processes and mechanisms that maintain such a warm status and thus help improve our ability to project future climate change. Although we have a general understanding of the substantial warmth during the MCO, much remains poorly known, including sea surface temperature (SST) and ocean circulation. The SST field during the MCO is extremely understudied. The MCO latitudinal SST gradient based on earlier limited datasets, in light of recently reported dataset, needs to be updated urgently. Ocean circulation pattern during the MCO also remains controversial. MCO climate simulations from computer models, the same used for projecting our future climate, remain to be validated, partly due to insufficient paleoclimate records available. Taking advantage of the development and new findings from a previously funded project on reconstructing SST and CO2 changes in an earlier period, the PI here proposes to use biomarkers, specifically alkenones and Glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers (GDGT), to reconstruct SST changes and ocean stratification status respectively during the MCO. The alkenone-based temperature proxy is well established, while our previous work suggests that GDGT-based indices, so-called source indicators, could indicate ocean stratification status. Four main oceanic sites from mid- and high latitude oceans will be selected for this study. Key issues we wish to include are: (1) to generate mid-latitude MCO SSTs to form a continuous, composite Cenozoic SST record, (2) to refine the latitudinal temperature gradient during the MCO for better data-model comparison, and (3) to reconstruct ocean stratification status at various oceanic settings and integrate them with available records to infer MCO ocean circulation changes. Our previous and preliminary work shows great promise that major objectives in this proposed study can be successfully achieved. 17到14百萬年前間的中中新世大暖期是地球氣候歷史上的一個相當溫暖的時期。基於計算機模式模擬得出的全球平均溫度要比現在高大約7°C，而當時的大氣CO2估計在300-600 ppm。目前大氣CO2已達到400 ppm，由於人類活動的影響將會持續增加，因此研究地球氣候，以及海洋化學和生態，怎樣響應溫室氣體的增加是一個很關鍵的科學問題，並且有社會價值。儘管過去溫暖氣候不一定是將來氣候變化的好類比，研究過去問暖期氣候可以知悉用來維持暖期狀態的關鍵氣候過程和機制，也將會提高我們預測將來氣候變化的能力。儘管我們對中中新世大暖期的溫暖程度有所了解，我們此大暖期的許多方面，例如海表溫度和海洋環流，還知之甚少。大暖期時的緯向海表溫度梯度多數基於早期的研究需要及時的更新。此大暖期時的海洋環流變化模式也是爭議的。用來預測將來氣候變化的計算機模式模擬出來的中中新世氣候結果也需要更多的地質學證據證實。 申請人前一個得到資助的項目是研究另一時段的海表溫度和大氣CO2變化。受益於此項目的一些新的發現，申請人這裡提出希望用生物標誌物，特別是長鏈烯酮和甘油二烷基甘油四醚（GDGT），來重建中中新世大暖期時的海表溫度和海洋層話狀態。基於長鏈烯酮的海表溫度指標已經很好地建立了，而我們之前的工作顯示基於GDGT的指標，也稱為來源指標，可以用來指示海洋分層狀態。我們在此研究中從中高緯度地區選取四個代表性地點。關鍵的科學問題包括：（1）重建中緯度的中中新世海表溫度已形成一個新生代以來的合成海表溫度曲線， （2）重建中中新世時的緯向溫度梯度可提供更好的數據-模擬結果的對比，（3）研究不同海洋環境下的海洋分層狀態，並整合目前已有的中中新世環流研究結果。我們以前的初步研究結果顯示我們這裡的主要研究目前都可以成功實現。

17305019.label: Realisation of objectives
17305019.value: 1. We have analyzed biomarkers (alkenones and GDGTs) in ~400 samples from 5 oceanic sites, ranging from tropics to polar regions, to reconstruct SST changes and ocean stratification status. 2. We have synthesized available SST records together with the new results generated from this project. Latitudinal SST changes have also been updated, for data-model comparison. 3. We have used the new SST records, mainly from mid-latitude oceans, generated from this project, to combine existing records to obtain a continuous composite Cenozoic SST record. 4. We have analyzed the GDGT results generated from this project, and combined with existing records. The results seem to suggest that stratification in tropical and high-latitude oceans responded to global climate change differently. 5. We have successfully trained one PhD student.

17305019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305019.value: Our major findings from this project include: 1. Exceptionally warm sea surface temperature occurred during the Mid-Miocene Climate Optimum. Temperature at mid-latitude oceans at the time was about the same as today's tropics. Partial result was published in Item 5 of Part C. 2. Surprisingly we have found that the ocean stratification status in the tropics and high-latitude oceans changed in opposite directions. We tend to interpret this opposite behavior to be controlled by different processes in high vs. low latitude oceans. That is, in the tropics, surface temperature controlled stratification, while (deep) ocean circulation controlled high latitude oceans. 3. The refined latitudinal temperature changes support a diminished temperature gradient during the Mid-Miocene Climate Optimum and the composite SST record resembles the benthic oxygen isotopic record, indicating the close relationship between the ice sheet development and global temperature. With the support of this project, we also extended our study into terrestrial regime around about the same time period. So far we have published 6 papers (Part C). A couple of more publications to cover Finding 2 & 3 are expected.

17305019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305019.value: We initially proposed that those GDGT-based source indicators could be used to reflect ocean stratification status. Now we recognize that the the stratification status may be also linked to (de)oxygenation in subsurface waters. Studies of (de)oxygenation in past warm conditions may provide clues how it will change in the anticipated future warming world. Further, (de)oxygenation changes at different ocean water depth may not follow the same direction. Future research projects could be developed to study oceanic deoxygenation in the past warmer conditions.

17305019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305019.value: The middle Miocene Climatic Optimum (MCO) from ~17 to 14 million years ago (Ma) is one of the substantially warm periods in Earth’s climate history. Global temperatures based on computer model simulations were about 7°C warmer than today, while atmospheric CO2 level at the time has recently been estimated at 300-600 ppm. As our current CO2 level has just reached 400 ppm and will continue to rise due to human activities, how the Earth’ climate, as well as ocean chemistry and marine ecosystem, will respond to the greenhouse gas forcing, is thus a critical scientific question and has important societal values. The SST field during the MCO is extremely understudied. The MCO latitudinal SST gradient based on earlier limited datasets, in light of recently reported dataset, needs to be updated urgently. Ocean circulation pattern during the MCO also remains controversial. MCO climate simulations from computer models, the same used for projecting our future climate, remain to be validated, partly due to insufficient paleoclimate records available. This project utilizes biomarkers, alkenones and glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers (GDGTs) to reconstruct sea surface temperature and ocean stratification status.

17305319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305319.value: High-dimensional time series are arguably the most common type of ``big data" with revolution, and can be found at many areas, including meteorology, genomics, chemometrics, connectomics, complex physics simulations, biological and environmental research, finance and econometrics. The classic vector autoregressive model is a fundamental tool for multivariate time series with fixed dimensions. However, it will involve too many parameters for high-dimensional time series, and hence suffers from the curse of dimensionality. This project rearranges the parameter matrices of a vector autoregressive model into a tensor form, and uses the Tucker tensor decomposition to restrict the parameter space from three directions. Comparing with the reduced-rank regression method, which can limit the parameter space from one direction only, the proposed method dramatically improve the capability of vector autoregressive models in handling high-dimensional time series. An alternating least squares algorithm is suggested to search for the estimates. Moreover, for the case with much higher dimension, we further assume the sparsity of three factor matrices, and the regularization method is thus considered for estimation and variable selection. The alternating least squares algorithm, together with the ADMM, is used to calculate the estimates. Thirdly this project also proposes a so-called matrix autoregressive model to fit the matrix-valued time series. Based on the tensor decomposition, we can easily reduce the dimension of the parameter space, and hence make it possible the corresponding statistical inference. 高維時間序列數據一般來講是最常見的隨時間演化的“大數據”類型，可以在許多領域找到，包括氣象學，基因組學，化學計量學，連接組學，複雜物理模擬，生物和環境研究，金融和計量經濟學。經典向量自回歸模型是用來分析多元時間序列的基本工具。然而，當分析高維時間序列時，它將會涉及到過多的參數，從而失去應有的可靠性。 該項目將向量自回歸模型的參數矩陣重新安排成為一個Tensor，並應用Tucker分解，從而從三個方向來限制參數空間。傳統的降秩回歸方法僅從一個方向來限制參數空間，因此該方法顯著提高了向量自回歸模型處理高維時間序列的能力。該項目提出了一個交替最小二乘算法來搜索估計。 另外，對於具有更高維數的數據，該項目進一步假設三因子矩陣是稀疏的，並且使用正則化方法來同時進行估計和變量選擇。該項目還提出了用交替最小二乘算法與ADMM一起來計算估計。 最後，該項目還提出了一種矩陣自回歸模型來擬合矩陣形式的時間序列。基於Tucker分解，我們可以容易地減小參數空間的自由度，從而可以進行相應的統計推斷。

17305319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305319.value: 1) This project proposes to rearrange the transition matrices of AR(P) models into a tensor form such that the parameter space can be restricted along three directions simultaneously via tensor decomposition. In contrast, the reduced-rank regression method can restrict the parameter space in only one direction. Besides achieving substantial dimension reduction, the proposed model is interpretable from the factor modeling perspective. Moreover, to handle high-dimensional time series, this project considers imposing sparsity on factor matrices to improve the model interpretability and estimation efficiency, which leads to a sparsity-inducing estimator. This finding was published at the Journal of American Statistician Association (one of top 4 statistical journals); see Wang, Zheng, Lian and Li (2022) at Part C. 2) This project proposes a new method to efficiently model and forecast high-dimensional tensor-valued time series, and a new modeling framework is considered to accomplish this task via autoregression (AR). By considering a low-rank Tucker decomposition for the transition tensor, the proposed tensor AR can flexibly capture the underlying low-dimensional tensor dynamics, providing both substantial dimension reduction and meaningful multidimensional dynamic factor interpretations. For this model, we first study several nuclear norm-regularized estimation methods and derive their non-asymptotic properties under the approximate low-rank setting. This piece of work was published at the Journal of Econometrics (ranking No.2 among all econometric journals); see Wang, Zheng and Li (2024) at Part C. 3) This project proposes a nonparametric quantile regression method for homogeneity pursuit in panel data models with individual effects, and a pairwise fused penalty is used to automatically select the number of groups. The asymptotic properties are established, and an ADMM algorithm is also developed. This finding was published at the Journal of Business and Economic Statistics, one of ASA journals; see Zhang, Wang, Lian and Li (2023) at Part C. 4) Momentum methods have been shown to accelerate the convergence of the standard gradient descent algorithm in practice and theory. In particular, the random partition based minibatch gradient descent methods with momentum (MGDM) are widely used to solve large-scale optimization problems with massive datasets. Despite the great popularity of the MGDM methods in practice, their theoretical properties are still underexplored. To this end, this project investigates the theoretical properties of MGDM methods based on the linear regression models. This piece of work was published at the Journal of Computational and Graphic Statistics, one of ASA journals; see Gao, Zhu, Qi, Li, Zhang and Wang (2023) at Part C.

17305319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305319.value: This project can be extended in several directions. First, the proposed estimators do not consider the possible correlation structure among components of errors, which will reduce the estimation efficiency. We may alternatively consider the generalized least squares loss. Second, the tensor technique potentially can be applied to many variants of the VAR model, for example, those with a nonlinear dynamic structure such as the threshold VAR model and the varying coefficient VAR model. Finally, heavy-tailed distributions and outliers are commonly observed in empirical economic and financial datasets. Robust estimation methods against the heavy-tailed distribution for high-dimensional VAR models have been investigated recently, and it is of practical importance to investigate the robust methods for the proposed model.

17305319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305319.value: This project proposes a novel idea to rearrange the parameter matrices of a vector autoregressive model into a tensor form, and uses the Tucker tensor decomposition to restrict the parameter space from three directions. As a result, the proposed method dramatically improves the capability of vector autoregressive models in handling high-dimensional time series. Moreover, for the case with much higher dimension, this project further assumes the sparsity of three factor matrices, and the regularization method is thus considered for estimation and variable selection. The accomplishment of this project provides more tools in handling high-dimensional time series, which are arguably the most common type of ``big data" with revolution and can be found at many areas, including meteorology, genomics, chemometrics, connectomics, complex physics simulations, biological and environmental research, finance and econometrics. On the other hand, the methodology of this project also provides a trying to use tensors to handle big time dependent data, and more similar methods may be expected in the near future.

17305419.value: 自古以來，天文學在很大程度上依賴於觀測自天空的電磁波。電磁波攜帶的訊息除了方向，時間，能量之外，還有偏振。後者可以有效地顯示輻射機制和物理條件，例如磁場方向。偏振的觀測一般是在射電和光學頻譜進行，X射線波段的偏振測量仍在研發階段。之前唯一的X射線偏振儀已是四十多年前發射上太空。最近，技術上的突破大大改善了X射線偏振儀的靈敏度及空間分辨率。X射線偏振成像探測器（IXPE）是第一個利用這項新技術的太空觀測站，它將會在2021/2022左右發射。這革命性的望遠鏡將開啟X射線偏振之門，及作出重大發現。 在這個項目中，我們將使用IXPE來研究銀河系中的高能粒子。它們普遍相信是在脈衝星，脈衝星風星雲（PWNe），及超新星殘骸（SNRs）中加速，但確切的機制仍不很清楚。這些高能粒子會發出高度徧振的同步X射線輻射，而徧振的角度則會直接顯示磁場的方向。因此，IXPE的觀測將提供非常有用的資訊去解開這些粒子的加速原理。具體來說，徧振的幅度可反映磁場的波幅，理論預測這波幅對於磁場的耗損和放大起了關鍵作用，為粒子加速機制中重要一環。IXPE的觀測也將揭示磁場的結構，可以跟模擬數據作對比。此外，我們將測量脈衝星的徧振方位跟相位的變化，以確定粒子加速位的位置，電荷密度，及磁場的分佈。

17305419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305419.value: The IXPE observations reveal the magnetic field structure of pulsar wind nebulae (PWN) and supernova remnants (SNRs) near the particle acceleration site. High degree of linear polarization with toroidal magnetic field configurations are found in young PWNe, which is consistent with theoretical expectation. On the other hand, SNRs show low degree of polarization, which is unexpected. This suggests turbulent magnetic fields, providing insights into the field amplification by turbulence in the shock acceleration model.

17305419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305419.value: The result of this project demonstrates the superb ability of the IXPE telescope. More observations can be performed to build a comprehensive sample, which will set the stage for theoretical modeling and numerical simulation works.

17305419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305419.value: In this project, we study the acceleration of energetic particles in the Universe using new data from the IXPE telescope. The results demonstrate the importance of magnetic turbulence in the acceleration process in astrophysical shocks, including supernova remnants and pulsar wind nebulae.

17305619.value: 非平稳矩阵时间序列分析

17305619.label: Project Objectives
17305619.value: To propose a new test for the mean stationarity of the matrix time series. This test will be constructed based on the kernel smoothing method, and it will be shown to have a standard normal null distribution. This test will also be shown to have non-trivial power in detecting local alternatives. Simulations will be conducted to assess the finite-sample performance of this test. To construct a new non-stationary matrix time series model and investigate its probabilistic properties and statistical inference. The probabilistic properties of the model will be derived. A two-step estimation procedure will be given for the model, and the asymptotics of all estimators will be studied. Simulations will be offered to examine the performance of all estimators in the finite-sample. To propose three other new non-stationary matrix time series models. These three new models will have a multiplicative structure to capture non-stationarity. Their statistical inference methodologies will be given, and the corresponding asymptotics will be established. To apply the proposed models and their related methodologies in various applications. Some well-known matrix time series data sets will be examined by the newly proposed test for mean stationarity. Once the mean stationarity is rejected, the newly proposed non-stationary models will be used to fit the data set, and insightful prediction models will be expected.

17305619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305619.value: Matrix time series models are important tools to study the interactive effects in dynamical systems. However, most of existing models are stationary, and they could result in severe misleading conclusions by overlooking the structural instability of the time series. To overcome this deficiency, this project constructs a new powerful test to check whether the matrix time series is mean stationary. If mean stationarity is rejected by the test, the considered matrix time series can be fitted by a new multiplicative non-stationary model proposed in this project. This new model not only captures the long-run mean structure evolving over time, but also takes the short-run mean dynamic into account. Moreover, this project provides three other new non-stationary matrix time series models, which can either enhance the prediction ability or explore some core characteristics of the matrix time series. Finally, this project establishes the statistical properties of all newly proposed methodologies, and demonstrates their usefulness by a myriad of applications. 矩阵时间序列模型是研究动态系统中多个变量交互作用的重要工具。但是，现有的平稳矩阵模型忽略了时间序列存在结构变化的可能性，因而可能导致错误的结论。为了克服这一不足，本项目首先拟构造一个新的统计方法来检验矩阵时间序列是否平稳。其次，本项目拟提出一类具有乘性结构的非平稳矩阵时间序列模型，此类模型可以同时刻画均值的长期结构变化和短期动态变化。更进一步，此项目拟提出另外三类非平稳模型用来得到更好的预报效果或描述矩阵数据的其它重要特征。最后，本项目拟得到所有模型相关推断方法的统计性质，并用大量数据分析表明它们的重要性。

17305619.label: Realisation of objectives
17305619.value: 1. My published paper Jiang, Li, Li and Zhu (2023, Statistica Sinica) has achieved the Objective 1. In this paper, my co-authors and I have proposed a new generalized Hausman test to examine whether the mean of a positive definite matrix time series has the structural change. Under some regularity conditions, we have proved that this generalized Hausman test converges to the standard normal distribution under the null hypothesis of mean stationarity. As the proposed generalized Hausman test depends on the kernel smoothing technique, we have given the guidance on how to choose the bandwidth. Moreover, we have shown that this generalized Hausman test can have nontrivial power to detect a broad of local alternatives. Finally, we have demonstrated the good performance of this test by simulation studies. 2. My published paper Jiang, Li, Li and Zhu (2023, Statistica Sinica) has also achieved the Objective 2. In this paper, my co-authors and I have constructed a new time-varying BEKK (TVB) model to take the mean non-stationarity into account. Our TVB model seems to be the first try in the literature to study the non-stationary positive definite matrix time series. Moreover, we have designed a two-step estimation method for the TVB model. Under some regularity conditions, we have proved the consistency of both the kernel estimator (from step one) and the profiled QMLE (from step two). Our proof techniques for the profiled QMLE are not trivial, because the BEKK-type process depends on all past unobserved lagged variables in our TVB model. Our simulation studies have found that the proposed two-step estimator above has a good finite-sample performance for many examined TVB models. 3. My published paper Jiang, Li and Zhu (2021, Journal of Econometrics) has achieved the Objective 3. In this paper, my co-authors and I have proposed a new non-stationary semiparametric GARCH (S-GARCH) model, which allows the parameters in the classical GARCH model to change abruptly or smoothly. For this S-GARCH model, we have provided a two-step estimation procedure: At step one, the unknow long-run component is estimated by the kernel method; At step two, the GARCH parameters in the short-run component are estimated by the QMLE method. Under some regularity conditions, we have shown that the QMLE of the GARCH parameters has an interesting adaptive feature, meaning that the efficiency of QMLE for the short-run component is adaptive to the form of long-run component. Moreover, we have extended the idea of S-GARCH model to form some interesting non-stationary multivariate GARCH models. Finally, we have examined this adaptive property by simulation studies. 4. I have achieved the Objective 4 by applying the proposed tests and models to study some real data sets in the aforementioned two papers. Specifically, my co-authors and I have applied the generalized Hausman test to check the mean stationarity of the RCOV data in Lunde, Shephard and Sheppard (2016, Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 34, 504-518.). Our testing result finds that there is a structural change in this RCOV data. Hence, we have further fitted this RCOV data by using our TVB model, and found that our fitted TVB model can give better out-of-sample predictions than its competitor. Moreover, we have applied our proposed S-GARCH model to the US dollar to Indian rupee (USD/INR) exchange rate series and FTSE-index series in Truquet (2017, Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B 79, 1391-1414). Compared with the locally stationary ARCH model and semiparametric ARCH model, our fitted S-GARCH model can have a significantly better out-of-sample performance according to the results of Diebold and Mariano test.

17305619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305619.value: This project has delivered 13 published papers, including 4 papers in Journal of Econometrics (JoE), 4 papers in Journal of Business & Economic Statistics (JBES), 4 papers in Statistica Sinica (SS), and 1 paper in Journal of Time Series Analysis (JTSA). The first major research outcome from my published paper Jiang, Li, Li and Zhu (2023, Statistica Sinica) is that our generalized Hausman test provides a formal tool to test the stationarity of positive definite matrix time series in the literature for the first time. Using this test, we are able to examine whether the observed long memory phenomenon in the RCOV data is spurious or not. Considering the importance of RCOV data in learning the financial volatilities, our proposed generalized Hausman test should be useful in risk management. The second major research outcome from my published paper Jiang, Li, Li and Zhu (2023, Statistica Sinica) is that our proposed TVB model is the first try in the literature to depict the structural change of positive definite matrix time series. Through the modelling of the structural change, we can better understand how the business cycle, technological progress, preference change and policy switch affect the dynamics of targeted matrix time series. This could generate many interesting insights for practitioners. The third major research outcome from my published paper Jiang, Li and Zhu (2021, Journal of Econometrics) is that our proposed S-GARCH model has the adaptive feature. This adaptive feature is unexpected, and it gives us the convenience to make statistical inference for the GARCH parameters in the short-run component. Due to tis adaptive feature, it is always desirable to use our proposed two-step estimation method, since it avoids the possible risk of structural change in the GARCH model, and at the same time, it can be as efficient as the classical variance target estimator for the stationary GARCH model in the literature. Owing to the financial support from this project, I also have many other interesting research outcomes for non-stationary time series analysis in my other published papers. In Wang and Zhu (2020, SS), we have proposed the portmanteau tests to check the adequacy of the nonlinear co-integrating regression with correlated errors. In Wang, Zhu, Li and Li (2022, JoE), we have studies the asymptotics of quantile estimator for the non-stationary asymmetry power GARCH model. In Liu, Zhu and Zhu (2022, JBES), we have constructed wavelet-based tests to check the white noise hypothesis for the non-stationary data. In Zhu (2023, JoE), I have given an entire statistical inference procedure for the generalized exponentially weighted moving average quantile model.

17305619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305619.value: Based on the current outputs from this project, I expect some further related research developments in future. For example, one of the possible future works is to test the mean stationarity of the general matrix time series by removing the positive definite restriction. The resulting test can have a much larger application scope than the test proposed in this project. Another possible future study is to propose a novel threshold matrix time series model. By using some macroeconomic variables as the threshold, the threshold matrix time series model has the chance to investigate many interesting non-linearity phenomena in practice. Of course, the difficulty of the threshold matrix time series model is how to do the inference for the threshold variable, and it may deserve some new developed proof techniques.

17305619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305619.value: More and more attentions have been given to study the matrix time series models in the literature. However, existing models are typically stationary, which can lead to inaccurate conclusions if the commonly observed structural instability of the time series is ignored. Hence, checking the stationarity of the matrix time series is important, and it is fulfilled by the proposed generalized Hausman test in this project. Moreover, if the non-stationarity is caused by the structural change, a model to take this phenomenon into account is necessary, and the TVB model as well as the S-GARCH model are formed to achieve this goal. Overall, both tests and models proposed in this project fill the gap in the matrix time series analysis, and they could have a large application scope in terms of both in-sample fitting and out-of-sample prediction.

17305819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17305819.value: Interval censored data arise commonly in many epidemiological and biomedical research that interventions are often assessed using surrogate outcomes based on periodically observed laboratory measurements. A typical example is the study of HIV/AIDS. The surrogate outcomes are known only to occur between two measurements, and hence these data are considered interval censored survival data. Another important quantity is the onset age of many human complex diseases like cardiovascular disease, breast cancer and Alzheimer’s dementia as there is a tendency that patients are getting younger leading to a shift in the onset age distribution. However the age of onset of these diseases are very often interval censored because the exact times to onset are virtually unobservable. This project considers a very flexible class of semiparametric transformation model which includes the well-known classes of semiparametric proportional hazards and proportional odds models as special cases, characterized by a transformation parameter. However no attempt has been made to estimate this transformation parameter in the literature, but researchers mainly focused on the estimation of the finite dimensional regression and/or dependence parameter. We consider several important extensions of the semiparametric transformation model to accommodate (i) interval-censored data with a cured subgroup; (ii) clustered interval censored data; and (iii) clustered interval censored data with a cured subgroup. Simple sieve maximum likelihood estimation method is proposed to estimate the parameters simultaneously including the transformation parameter. The loglikelihood function is shown to be extremely simple with close form in all cases, and hence the proposed method is expected to be computationally efficient. Finally in the case where an explanatory variable has a nonlinear effect on the response, a partially linear component will be included into the regression part to give a class of semiparametric partially linear transformation model. The asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators will be studied. This project aims to help answering some important clinical questions like the modeling of genetic frailties, particularly in linkage analysis for the ages of onset of a certain disease among individuals within a family. 區間刪失數據通常出現在許多流行病學和生物醫學研究中，事 件發生往往使用基於定期觀察的實驗室測量的替代結果進行評 估。一個典型的例子是艾滋病毒/艾滋病的研究。已知替代結果 僅在兩次測量之間發生，因此這些數據被認為是區間刪失的存 活數據。另一個於許多人類複雜疾病頗為重要的因素是發病年 齡，如心血管疾病，乳腺癌和阿爾茨海默氏癡呆症，因為患者 越來越年輕，導致發病年齡分佈發生變化。然而，這些疾病的 發病年齡經常被區間檢查，因為確切的發病時間幾乎是不可觀 察的。這項目考慮了一類非常靈活的半參數變換模型，該模型 包括眾所周知的半參數比例風險類和比例賠率模型作為特殊情 況，其特徵在於變換參數。然而，在文獻中研究人員主要關注 有限維回歸和/或依賴參數的估計，而沒有嘗試估計該變換參數。 我們考慮半參數變換模型的幾個重要擴展，以容納（i）具有固 化子群的區間刪失數據; （ii）集群區間刪失數據; （iii）具有治 愈亞組的聚類區間刪失數據。提出了簡單篩選最大似然估計方 法來同時估計包括變換參數的參數。在所有情況下，對數似然 函數顯示為極其簡單且具有緊密形式，因此預期所提出的方法 在計算上是有效的。最後，在解釋變量對響應具有非線性影響 的情況下，將部分線性分量包括在回歸部分中以給出一類半參 數部分線性變換模型。將研究所提出的估計量的漸近性質。該 項目旨在幫助回答一些重要的臨床問題，如遺傳系統的建模， 特別是在一個家庭中個體的某種疾病發病年齡的連鎖分析中。

17305819.label: Realisation of objectives
17305819.value: This project aimed to study various types of interval-censored data, namely (a) Simple univariate case; (b) Univariate case with a cure subgroup; (c) Clustered or multivariate case; and (d) Clustered case with a cured subgroup; based on the semiparametric transformation model where we assumed the class of Box-Cox transformation model for the function G. The 7 stated project objectives have been achieved in more than one type of interval censored data. The applications mainly focused on the multivariate interval-censored data from dental research. Two publications were generated from this project, one in Biometrics (A) and one in Statistics in Medicine (B). Paper (A) mainly deals with the clustered or multivariate interval-censored data at which the univariate interval-censored data is a special case, while paper (B) deals with the univariate and clustered case with a cured subgroup. Objective 1: Estimation of the cumulative intensity function and hence the transformation parameter in the basic semiparametric transformation model based on interval censored data. This objective is achieved in both papers (A) and (B). In (A), a piecewise-linear function is used to approximate the cumulative intensity function in clustered or multivariate interval-censored data. In (B), a Bernstein-Polynomial is used to approximate the unspecified distribution function F in the marginal promotion time model to accommodate the cured subgroup in the population. Objective 2: To derive the asymptotic properties of the proposed estimator. This objective has been achieved in both (A) and (B) that the estimators of the Euclidean parameter in the two papers are both shown to be normally distributed asymptotically. The rates of convergence of the estimator of the nonparametric components of the two estimators were also derived. Objective 3: Extension of the basic semiparametric transformation model to include the partially linear component in the regression part. This is achieved in (A) that a particular continuous explanatory variable can assume a nonlinear relationship with the outcome variable of interest through a nonparametric function. The function is approximated by another piecewise-linear function with highly satisfactory performance. Objective 4: Extension of the basic model to accommodate clustered interval censored data based on a positive stable or a gamma frailty distribution. This is achieved in (A) based on a random effects approach while the positive stable frailty distribution is considered in the simulation section of (B) to generate dependence among subjects from the same cluster. Objective 5: Extension of the basic model to accommodate interval censored data with a cure group, both in the univariate and clustered cases. This is achieved in (B) with both the univariate and clustered cases using a marginal distribution approach based on the generalized estimating equation method. Objective 6: A unified approach to the estimation of the frailty semiparametric transformation model will be considered and its asymptotic properties will be derived. This is achieved in (A). The unified approach can be applied to the general frailty semiparametric transformation models provided that the Laplace transform of the frailty variable has a closed form expression. The asymptotic properties were derived and it has been shown that the Euclidean parameter estimator is efficient and has a normal distribution asymptotically. Objective 7: Finite sample performance of the proposed estimators will be studied by simulation The finite sample performance of the two proposed estimators were studied extensively through simulation, and it was shown that the two estimators performed satisfactorily. In general, the transformation parameter cannot be estimated easily in the literature. The proposed estimator of the transformation parameter has shown to asymptotically normally distributed and has excellent finite sample performance that statistical inference on the transformation parameter can also be made. In the literature, the transformation parameter is estimated using the profile likelihood by searching over the real line but no statistical inference can be made. This is one of the remarkable results of this project.

17305819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17305819.value: In paper (A), we proposed a class of semiparametric partly linear frailty models for the analysis of clustered interval-censored data. The two nonparametric functions, which characterize the baseline survival function and the nonlinear effect of a covariate, are estimated using sieve maximum likelihood estimation method. We proved that the sieve maximum likelihood estimator of the Euclidean parameters is strongly consistent and asymptotically normal, and the estimators of the two nonparametric functions are also strongly consistent and attain optimal rates of convergence. In particular, we demonstrate theoretically and through empirical studies that the transformation parameter, which is typically assumed to be known in the literature, can also be consistently estimated with a valid inference procedure. It would allow one to test whether a frailty proportional hazards model or a proportional odds model is more appropriate. A key difference between the proposed model and some existing transformation models for multivariate survival data is that the frailty acts multiplicatively in the transformation function G instead of the argument of G. Our formulation results in a closed-form expression for the likelihood whenever the frailty distribution has an explicit Laplace transform. This simplifies the computation of the sieve maximum likelihood estimator and allows for direct maximization of the log-likelihood function using gradient methods. The potential nonlinear relationship between a continuous explanatory variable and the outcome variable can also be identified using the sieve maximum likelihood approach. The above method can be applied to general clustered interval-censored data. However it may not be efficient or feasible if the cluster size is large as in dental research, not to mention the case with informative cluster size (ICS). A marginal approach is proposed in paper (B) to address these concerns. A class of semiparametric transformation cure models as a generalization of the promotion time model for marginal analysis of clustered current status data. Under ICS setting, the traditional GEE approach yields biased estimation even if the marginal model is correctly specified. We propose a weighted GEE approach that weights a cluster by the inverse of the cluster size. A sieve-MLE approach is adopted by approximating the the nonparametric unspecified distribution function by a Bernstein polynomial. The proposed estimators are shown to be consistent and asymptotically normally distributed. Finite sample performance is highly satisfactory based on large scale simulation studies.

17305819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17305819.value: One possible extension based on paper (A) is to extend the framework to allow for the two-parameter family of frailty distributions. A more challenging extension is to consider a nonparametric transformation function G. Moreover one may also consider a more general multivariate frailty distribution instead of the shared frailty. For the nonlinear part, one possible extension is to consider a single index model instead of the nonlinear association between a continuous covariate and the outcome variable. For paper (b), one may consider a joint modeling approach that regress both the cluster size and survival times on the same or different sets of covariates. In such a model, the association between the cluster size and interval-censored survival outcomes can be modeled via a shared frailty term in both regression models. One advantage of a joint-modeling approach is that, under a correctly specified model and regularity conditions, the regression parameters can be estimated with optimal statistical efficiency. Moreover, one possible extension is to develop a statistical test to detect the presence of informative cluster size with general interval-censored data with a cured proportion. Finally, one may consider dependent censoring time using a copula or frailty approach to model their association.

17305819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17305819.value: Modeling interval-censored survival data is generally difficult even with simple models like Cox proportional-hazards regression or semiparametric proportional-odds model. Clustered or multivariate interval-censored data with or without a subgroup of cured subjects are more challenging, particularly when the cluster size is huge and/or the cluster size is informative. This project proposes two estimation methods for clustered interval-censored data with univariate interval-censored data as a special case. A more flexible class of semiparametric partly-linear frailty transformation models, which includes the frailty Cox proportional-hazards and semiparametric proportional-odds models as special cases, is proposed for the analysis of clustered interval-censored data which arises naturally in dental research. A special feature of this model is that it allows a continuous covariate to be nonlinear associated with the outcome variable. In the literature, the transformation parameter (univariate or multivariate) cannot be estimated but is assumed to be known. We demonstrated theoretically and empirically that the transformation parameter can be estimated consistently with a valid inference procedure. Marginal analysis of clustered interval-censored data with informative cluster size and a subgroup of cured using a class of semiparametric transformation cure models is considered. The estimators were shown to have good performance empirically.
