17307819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307819.value: High-dimensional linear regression analysis is a prominent research area which has seen a proliferation of theoretical results and statistical tools suited to the big data era. Drawing on training data of a relatively small size, n say, penalised estimation methods, especially the lasso and its variants, have enjoyed increasing popularity as standard tools for selecting and estimating relevant signals among a large number, p say, of candidate signals conjectured for modelling the response variable. This amounts to the well-known “large p small n” problem. Theoretical justification of most of the existing methods rests upon certain conditions on signal strength and correlations, assumptions which are too strong to be credible in reality. Relaxation of such assumptions usually throws the well-established desirable properties of the estimators and their accompanying inference procedures into disarray, rendering the inference output no longer valid. This project aims at developing a theoretically valid, computationally feasible, procedure for inference about the relationships between strong signals and response variables. The procedure is designed to function well without assuming strong conditions on signal strength and correlations. In particular, we allow for the presence of many weak signals or a few moderate signals that are non-distinguishable from sampling noise. The procedure consists of two key components: (1) a revised estimator constructed by correcting the bias of a nonconvex penalised estimator, and (2) a paired bootstrap method for estimating the distribution of the revised estimator. Our theoretical investigation provides justification for asymptotic validity of the proposed procedure, which is tested empirically via large-scale simulation studies as well as with real-life data. On successful completion, the proposed project is anticipated to deliver a practically reliable inference procedure for high-dimensional regression data under very general conditions, with applications to big data problems. 隨著大數據時代的到來，適用於大數據的相關理論和統計工具層出不窮，高維線性回歸分析成為了一個十分突出的研究領域。在高維數據中，訓練數據的樣本容量（n）相對較小，而用於推測響應變量的候選信號規模（p）龐大，懲罰估計方法是選擇和估計重要信號的標準工具，特別是以lasso及其變形為主的一系列方法越來越受大家的歡迎。這也就是眾所周知的“大p小n”問題。大多數現有方法的理論依據都建立在信號強度和相關性的特定條件上，這些假設過於嚴格，以至於這些方法在現實中並不完全適用和可信。但是對這些假設的放寬通常會讓估計量及其推斷過程失去它已有的良好性質，從而導致相應的推斷結果不再有效。這個項目旨在開發一個理論上有效、計算上可行的方法來推斷強信號和響應變量之間的關係。即使無需對信號強度和相關性作出那麼強的假設條件，該方法仍可行。特別地，我們還允許數據中存在較多弱信號或一些無法與採樣噪聲區分開來的中等信號。該方法由兩個關鍵部分組成: (1)針對現有的非凸懲罰估計量，我們通過糾正其偏差來構造改良版本的估計量，(2)提出一套成對抽樣的自助法（paired bootstrap method）用於估計改良估計量的分佈。我們的理論研究將會為該方法的漸近有效性提供依據，同時，該項目會通過大規模的模擬仿真和實際數據進行實證檢驗。成功完成後，該項目將能應用到大數據問題中，為一般條件下的高維回歸數據提供一個實用可靠的統計推斷方法。

17307819.label: Realisation of objectives
17307819.value: Objective 1: We provide a holistic assessment of the selection and convergence properties of nonconvex penalised estimators from a local asymptotic perspective, under a framework which accommodates existence of many weak signals and heavy tail conditions on covariates and random errors. We then show that post-selection least squares estimation has the beneficial effect of removing the bias incurred by nonconvex penalisation of moderate signals. Objective 2: We consider a variety of residual bootstrap procedures for inference about regression coefficients based on nonconvex penalised estimators and their corresponding post-selection OLS estimators. Specifically, we consider the conventional as well as a re-centred bootstrap residual methods to estimate the distributions of the nonconvex penalised regression estimator and the post-selection OLS estimator. Conditions for bootstrap consistency and the convergence rates of the bootstrap regression estimators have been established. Objective 3: Empirical studies have been conducted to compare the various procedures proposed in this project with existing methods. Problem settings under study include both parametric and nonparametric regressions, partially linear regression models, multiple index models and nonparametric regression in the presence of missing data and general nonparametric regression under convex losses. The bootstrap procedures are empirically investigated under the setting of high-dimensional linear regression regularised by SCAD, in the presence of Gaussian noises.

17307819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307819.value: (Attached paper 4) By adopting a local asymptotic framework, we provide theoretical explanation for the breakdown of oracle property of nonconvex penalisation in the presence of many weak signals and/or a few moderate signals. We then show that post-selection OLS offers an effective remedy. Empirical results obtained from large-scale simulation studies corroborate our theoretical findings. Post-selection OLS is found to improve on nonconvex penalised estimation, especially under heavy-tailed settings. The above theoretical results pave the way for developing valid residual bootstrap procedures for inference based on nonconvex penalised estimators. We establish consistency and convergence rates for the bootstrap regression estimators. These results, contained in the last part of Xu's PhD thesis, are being written up for submission to a peer-reviewed journal. (Attached paper 1) We combine nonconvex penalised linear regression and local polynomial regression into a novel procedure for high-dimensional regression under a setting of partially linear model where the linear components are unknown. Our theory is established under a general nonparametric regression framework, where signal strength is embedded in a continuous spectrum scaled by asymptotic orders, and a weak sparsity condition which allows for the presence of many weak, non-detectable, signals. Our procedure is shown to be consistent in detecting strong signals. We also establish its error rate in estimating the regression function. The above research evinces the power of nonconvex penalisation in a nonparametric regression context when it is applied to regularise bandwidths in some local polynomial procedure. We further explore such possibilities and obtain encouraging results under a variety of problem settings, which include high-dimensional local polynomial regression under convex losses (e.g. quantile regression) (attached paper 5), nonparametric regression in the presence of missing covariate data (attached paper 2), and simultaneous variable selection and dimension reduction under a multiple index model (attached paper 3). In the above three works, novel nonparametric regression procedures, all based on nonconvex bandwidth regularisation, are proposed and shown to enjoy desirable theoretical and empirical properties.

17307819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307819.value: 1) Develop bootstrap inference procedures for bandwidth-regularised nonparametric regression estimators proposed in the project. 2) Explore computationally more efficient algorithms for high-dimensional nonconvex bandwidth regularised nonparametric regression.

17307819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307819.value: The project succeeds in deepening our understanding of nonconvex penalised regression under high dimensions. Importantly, a local asymptotic theory is developed to demystify the workings of the much acclaimed oracle property offered by nonconvex penalisation, which could be highly questionable under high dimensions in the presence of many weak signals. A practical remedy, in the form of post-selection ordinary least squares, is proposed to restore partially the oracle property under unfavourable circumstances. Moving beyond the parametric framework set in its original objectives, the project also delivers a variety of novel applications of nonconvex penalisation in both semi-parametric and nonparametric regression settings. The proposed procedures can be applied to a partially linear model with an unknown mix of linear and nonlinear components, to a high-dimensional nonparametric quantile regression model (or any similar model subject to convex loss), to a multiple index model and to a nonparametric regression model in the presence of missing data. These procedures are all theoretically justified. Empirical results suggest that they outperform existing methods in general.

17307919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17307919.value: Viruses are the most abundant biological entities on earth and a major reservoir of genetic diversity and complexity across habitats. Moreover, viral infectious influenza remains a constant threat to human health and is a major cause of death across the globe. Despite the role of viruses in the ecosystem and disease prevention, current virus assays are mainly based on large populations, with important temporal data thus lost in the process of averaging signals. Further, the heterogeneity of viral communities is only just beginning to be elucidated owing to the lack of effective methods to isolate and study individual viruses. Although advances in detection and sorting techniques have inspired a series of studies on single-cell analysis, most current single-cell isolation techniques fail to manipulate single viruses because of their small size and weak signal for detection. Through the adoption of a segmented flow, droplet microfluidics enable the separation of single targets within pico- to nanoliter-sized compartments, thus demonstrating great potential for single-virus isolation. Furthermore, maintaining a high degree of purity in emulsion droplets enables multiple sample manipulation functions to be performed on the encapsulated virus, including reagent injection, polymerase chain reaction, and droplet sorting. Despite the sophistication of on-chip processing, however, the difficulties in efficiently collecting and releasing processed target samples on demand have significantly hampered in-depth genomic analysis of the encapsulants using established biological techniques, limiting the information that can be obtained. Hence, there is an urgent need for an effective approach to quantitatively isolating individual droplets and extracting encapsulated single viruses with a specific pretreatment. The aims of the proposed project are to (1) develop an automated system for on-demand droplet collection (ODC) with accurate droplet quantity, (2) realize single-virus isolation and recovery through single-droplet collection, and (3) demonstrate single-virus analysis by integrating droplet manipulation into the ODC platform. In the short term, the project will unveil an efficient technique for collecting single droplets for the isolation and genomic analysis of individual viruses, offering a fundamental understanding of viral sequence diversity in different passage conditions at the single-genome level. In the long term, it will contribute to the exploration of viral-host interaction and the design of new approaches to disease control by, for instance, enhancing understanding of viral infection for influenza prevention. 病毒是地球上最為豐富的生物圖，且有著複雜的基因多樣性。同時，病毒性流感一直是人類健康的一大威脅，并在全球範圍內持續造成死亡。然而，儘管病毒在生態系統及病毒防治方面十分重要，目前的病毒研究大多基於較大的群體，從而導致重要的瞬態參數在平均分析的過程中被忽略掉。同時，由於缺乏有效的技術來分離并研究單個病毒，對病毒多樣性的研究也進展緩慢。儘管各種檢測篩選手段在單細胞研究方面發揮了重要作用，這些方法大多並不適用於尺寸微小且信號微弱的病毒。而通過使用分段式流體，液滴微流控可以實現將單個靶材分隔入皮升到納升的微小區間內，在單病毒分隔方面呈現了巨大的潛能。此外，這一區間化操作可以在後續反應中時刻保持穩定的高純度，從而對單病毒進行樣品注入，PCR擴增以及熒光篩選等處理。儘管在微流控操作方面展現出巨大的優勢，低效的後續收集及提純阻礙了進一步的線下分析。因此，目前亟需一種有效的方法來實現對液滴的定量收集，并無損地提取出內含的單病毒產物。針對此，本項目主要目標為：（1）研發一套用於定量收集液滴的自動化系統；（2）實現單病毒的隔離及提取；（3）進一步利用液滴操縱來實現對單病毒的分析。短期內，該項目將開發一種新型的單液滴收集技術並對單病毒進行分析，進而對病毒基因的多樣性進行更深入的了解。而從長遠角度考慮，該項目可以對病毒宿主之間的相互作用關係進行揭示，并通過提高對流感病毒感染的認知來促進疾病防治。

17307919.label: Realisation of objectives
17307919.value: The objectives have been achieved: 1. We have constructed an automated system for accurate collection of droplets with a defined number. The core technique to realize the targeted quantitative droplet collection is alternate operations in multiple branch channel, thus leaving enough time interval to complete each collection. Employing the alternate-operation strategy, this system enables a high throughput of 20 collections/ min, without significant sample loss or microfluidic interruption. Through the fluorescence detection-based accurate droplet counting, the droplet number can be precisely controlled at single-droplet resolution. 2. We have developed a single-droplet extraction system to isolate, process, and analyze single viruses. Individual viruses are encapsulated into the droplets, with their genomes amplified to generate detectable signals. Then, the single viral genomes are collected from individual droplets and isolated into arrays of microtubes. Through further fragmentation and amplification, the processed genomes are barcoded and sequenced, providing a library of single-virus genotypes at whole-genome level. 3. We have collected and analyzed single viruses. Influenza viruses with 8 separate segments of genomes are sequenced at single-virus level. A/PR/8/34 (H1N1) is used as a model system to test the efficiency of the single-virus analysis. Most coverage of the whole genomes of influenza viruses can be sequenced, and the gap can be filled by further modifications. The sequences of single influenza viruses can thus be efficiently applied in analyzing the reassortment of recombinant viruses for virological and pathogenic studies.

17307919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17307919.value: - Set up a microfluidic platform to collect a defined number of droplets down to single one. - Develop strategies to extract the droplet contents into aqueous phase for downstream biological analyses, such as cell culture and sequencing analysis. - Investigate the ratio of droplets encapsulating single encapsulants under different experimental conditions to establish the understanding required for robust single-virus encapsulation. - Develop a pipeline for isolation, processing, and collection of single viruses. - Demonstrate the capacity of analyzing single viruses by collecting and conducting sequencing analysis of single influenza viruses. Most of the results have been presented in various international conferences (e.g. MicroTAS 2020, ACS Spring 2021, MRS Fall 2022, AIChE Annual Meeting 2022, International soft matter conference 2023, etc.) and published in respected international journals (e.g. Nature Communications, Microsystems and Nanoengineering, ACS Nano, Small, Lab on a Chip, Chemical Society Reviews, Advanced Science, JACS, etc.), as shown in Part C. While some papers have been submitted and are being reviewed, other results are being integrated with other applications and wrapped up for publication due to their potential to combine for a greater impact. The potential of droplet-based platform for single-virus analysis, such as proteins, is impactful, and more works should be done in this direction. Some of the project outcomes also benefit other research projects indirectly.

17307919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17307919.value: The completed research project demonstrates an automatic platform for isolation and analysis of single biological targets. The demonstrated single-virus sequencing is just one branch, there are more fascinating applications beyond that. On the one hand, it provides a powerful tool to isolate some other tiny targets, such as bacteria and even DNA molecules, that cannot be sorted using current techniques. This allows in-deep analysis of the whole genomes to probe the heterogeneity and reveal the pathogenicity mechanism of some diseases. On the other hand, the interactions between individual targets can also be studied with high throughput. For example, the interactions between viruses and host cells can be thus analyzed, which may reveal the signaling pathways of virus infectivity. We will seek appropriate biological collaborators and apply for potentially relevant fundings from agencies, such as the Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong, to further engage in these studies. Moreover, the built platform has good potential to be developed into commercial instrument. This type of machine can be used by biologist and physicians without microfluidic expertise for research and clinical use. We propose to explore these through collaborations with industries, facilitated by research grants, such as the RGC and Innovation and Technology Fund (ITF).

17307919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17307919.value: Viruses are one of the most abundant biological entities on earth, influencing almost all aspects of our lives by shaping ecological systems, causing infectious diseases, and stimulating immune responses. Analysis of viral evolution and diagnosis of viral diseases require a comprehensive understanding of the viral genotypes at single-virus level. Traditionally, the genomic analysis of viruses is conducted on large populations to measure the averaged signals, failing to probe the heterogeneity among individuals. Consequently, the specificity and diversity of viral genotypes is rarely elucidated owing to the lack of effective approaches to analyze individual viruses. In this project, we develop an on-demand droplet collection system to isolate, process, and analyze single viruses. We start by collecting a defined number of droplets; we then encapsulate single viruses and extract single viral genomes; we finally do sequencing analysis of the collected viruses. This system provides a functional tool for comprehensive understanding of basic virology, host-virus interactions, and infection-triggered host immune responses. Moreover, the demonstrated single-virus analysis illustrates the capability of the platform, which can be adapted to further benefit the study of other biological targets, including single cells, single bacteria and even the interactions between different targets.

17309419.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17309419.value: 以化學生物學方法闡明先天免疫中脂質A分子識別

17309419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17309419.value: Innate immune system in human provides a rapid-responding first line of defense against invading pathogens. Host receptor proteins function as molecular sensors and detect structurally-conserved chemical entities that are common but crucial to microorganisms. Honed by natural selection, different receptors in distinct cellular compartments respond exquisitely to their ligand and mount a coordinated response upon activation. This results in pathogen clearance through inflammation, recruitment of immune cells and potentiation of adaptive immunity. An aberrant activation, however, can lead to immunodeficiency, septic shock or induction of autoimmunity. Uncovering the dynamics underlying these interactions is therefore critical to tackling immunological disorders where the balance is disrupted. Lipid A is the glycolipid anchor of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) found in the outer membrane of most Gram-negative bacteria and is capable of activating our innate immune system even at picomolar levels. According to the current understanding, detection of LPS, predominantly through lipid A recognition, can be carried out by TLR4–MD-2 on plasma membranes and caspase-4/-5/-11 in cytosol. To counteract the multilayered defense, bacteria evolved to modify the structure of lipid A to evade host immuno-surveillance, adapt to hostile niche, establish an infection, secure nutrients, and ultimately lead to chronic inflammatory systemic diseases; however the basis of molecular recognition through which this modulation of bioactivity is imparted is not well understood. The major challenge in this field of study is the difficulty in dissecting the biological effects of lipid A modifications from a heterogeneous mixture. Some confounding results in previous studies have been attributed to contributions from minor but disproportionately bioactive contaminants. To this end we propose to prepare structurally homogeneous and well-defined lipid A through total synthesis. We aim to improve on current synthetic strategies, specifically to enhance functional group compatibility to allow more efficient syntheses and enable a wider range of natural and unnatural analogues to be prepared. Specifically, we aim to verify the structure of a recently reassigned lipid A isoform from Porphyromonas gingivalis and compare its biological activity with its originally purported structure to examine the effect on the positional isomerism. Building on the strategy, we plan to construct a library of lipid A corresponding to enzymatically modified structures to investigate their functional outcome with various biological targets utilizing well-established functional assays. We also propose to synthesize protein-profiling probes based on lipid A with disparate biological activities to uncover the molecular basis of lipid A recognition in a range of receptor proteins. 先天免疫系統提供迅速免疫應答，是人體對抗病原體入侵的第一道防線。宿主的受體蛋白充當分子傳感器，負責檢測微生物中普遍但關鍵的結構保守化學實體。通過自然演化，不同的受體在不同細胞區室中對其配體產生特異性響應，且在激活時產生協同應答，最終透過炎症反應、動員免疫細胞和增強適應性免疫清除病原體。然而先天免疫系統的激活異常可導致免疫缺陷、感染性休克或引發自身免疫疾病。因此，揭示「受體—配體」相互作用的動態變化，對於治療免疫失衡引發的疾病至關重要。 絕大多數革蘭氏陰性細菌的外膜上都含有脂多醣，而其醣酯錨定部分——脂質A——即使在皮摩爾水平也能夠激活人體先天免疫系統。根據目前的研究，脂多醣的檢測主要依賴質膜上的TLR4–MD-2和細胞質中的半胱天冬酶-4/-5/-11識別脂質A。為抵禦多重防線，細菌進化出修飾脂質A結構的能力，以逃避宿主免疫監視、適應惡劣生態位、建立感染、確保養分，並最終導致慢性炎性全身性疾病。然而，對此類通過結構修飾來調節生物活性的機理我們仍缺乏分子層面的了解。 本研究領域的主要挑戰在於難以從異質混合物中剖析特定脂質A修飾的生物效應。少量高生物活性的污染物曾導致研究結果產生混淆。為此，我們提出以全合成製備結構均一而且明確的脂質A。我們致力於改進目前的合成策略，特別是增強官能團相容性，從而提高合成效率，並廣泛應用於製備多種天然脂質A及其非天然衍生物。具體來說，我們旨在驗證牙齦卟啉單胞菌一脂質A最近被修正的結構，並將其生物活性與原始報導中的結構進行比較，以研究該位置異構的影響。在此基礎上，我們計劃構建一個囊括對應各類酶修飾產物的脂質A化合物庫，並利用現有成熟的功能測定法研究其生物靶標作用。此外，基於不同生物活性的脂質A，我們將致力於研發蛋白質分析探針，以揭示各種受體蛋白對於脂質A識別的分子基礎。

17500219.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17500219.value: 內部激勵機制與企業文化

17500219.label: Project Objectives
17500219.value: Develop a theory of corporate culture based on intrinsic motivation and optimal contracts; Develop a tractable theoretical model of multiple agents and multiple tasks; Analyze the factors, channels and mechanisms of how corporate culture affects firm performance; Generate testable empirical implications of the effects of corporate culture on firm performance; Help shed light on how firms should think strategically of corporate culture.
rows: Develop a theory of corporate culture based on intrinsic motivation and optimal contracts;
Develop a tractable theoretical model of multiple agents and multiple tasks;
Analyze the factors, channels and mechanisms of how corporate culture affects firm performance;
Generate testable empirical implications of the effects of corporate culture on firm performance;
Help shed light on how firms should think strategically of corporate culture.

17500219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500219.value: This research project aims to provide an economic analysis of corporate culture based on optimal contract theory to understand several questions about corporate cultures. Why do similar firms in a same industry adopt different corporate cultures? How does corporate culture interact with incentives and organizational structure? How does corporate culture affect firm performance? Is there a dominant corporate culture that maximizes firm value? If yes, why not all firms adopt it? Building on Benabou and Tirole (2016), we consider a model of multiple-agents with multi-tasks in which one firm hires two agents (e.g., division managers), each undertaking two tasks. One task is a cooperative effort, to which individual contributions cannot be measurable and thus cannot be part of a formal compensation scheme. Cooperative efforts by the agents are complementary in that higher cooperative effort by one agent makes that of the other agent more valuable. The firm values cooperative efforts of the agents (organization value of cooperation), and the agents have intrinsic motivation of exerting cooperative efforts (personal values of cooperation). We define corporate culture as the level of cooperation achieved by cooperative efforts of the agents. The other task is measurable and hence contractible (e.g., through division profits). But incentive provided to this task will discourage cooperative effort, as cooperative and individualistic efforts are assumed to be substitutes. In the benchmark model with complete information, we show that the optimal contract crucially depends on the underlying parameters, in particular, on how the firm and agents value cooperation. We have several findings. First, similar firms can have quite different corporate cultures due to a discontinuity in contract design as a function of the parameters. Second, cooperative corporate culture is associated with lower explicit incentives. Third, firm profits and social welfare do not always increase with the level of cooperation. That is, no corporate culture is always dominant. Forth, firm profits and social welfare are maximized when personal values and organizational values are congruent. For example, when the firm and agents all value cooperation highly, the firm will optimally offer lower explicit incentives and promote a strong corporate culture of cooperation. However, if the firm values cooperation but agents have lower intrinsic motivation, the firm may have to give up on promoting cooperation. In future research, we are going to investigate how other factors, such as asymmetric information and organizational structure affects the optimal contract and cooperate culture. 本研究課題致力於在最優契約理論的基礎上，提供關於企業文化的經濟學分析，理解關於企業文化的幾個問題：為什麼同一行業類似的公司會採用不同的企業文化？企業文化是如何與激勵機制以及組織結構相互影響？企業文化如何影響企業的業績？是否存在一個能夠最大化企業價值的主導企業文化？ 如果有，為什麼不是所有的公司都採用這種企業文化？ 在Benabou和Tirole (2016)的基礎上，我們考慮採用一個企業僱用兩個代理人（如部門經理），每個代理人負責兩個任務的多代理人和多任務模式。在這個模式中，一種是合作型任務，個人的貢獻無法被考核衡量，也因此無法納入正式的薪酬制度中。代理人之間的合作性付出是互補的， 一個代理人在合作型任務中付出越多努力會使另一個代理人在合作型任務中的努力更具價值。企業重視代理人在合作型任務上的付出（企業的合作文化），代理人也具有在合作型任務上付出努力的內在動力（個人的合作精神）。我們將企業文化定義為代理人為合作型任務付出的努力從而達到的合作程度。另外一種任務是可（通過部門利潤）衡量，因此可以納入正式的合約裡。然而由於合作型付出和個人型付出被假定為相互替代的，這一類任務的內在激勵會減少合作型付出。 在完全信息下的基準模型中，我們發現最優合約取決於相應的參數，具體來說，取決於公司和代理人對合作的重視程度。我們有以下發現。首先，由於合約設計受參數變化影響具有不連續性，類似的公司也能夠擁有不同的企業文化。其次，倡導合作的企業文化與更低程度的明確激勵有關。第三，企業利潤及社會福利並不總是隨著合作的增強而增加。也就是說，沒有一直占優的企業文化。第四，當個人價值和企業價值一致時，企業利潤及社會福利將得到最大化。舉例來說，當企業和代理人都非常重視合作時，企業將最優地提供更低的明確激勵並且大力促進合作型企業文化。然而，當企業重視合作，個人卻有較低的內在合作動力時，企業或許只能放棄倡導合作。 在之後的研究中，我們將探討其他因素，如不對稱信息和企業組織結構，如何影響最優合約及企業文化。

17500219.label: Realisation of objectives
17500219.value: 5.2 Revised objectives The objectives listed in the original application have almost been achieved in the theoretical part of our research. When the theoretical framework is applied to the mergers and acquisitions (M&As) setting, interesting empirical implications are delivered. Comments from the seminar audience and the literature check make us realize that the importance and novelty of the application setting go far beyond what we intended to explore within the theoretical framework from the perspective of information economics. New direction not only speaks to the research gap which barely studied in existing literature concerning the interaction between the corporate culture and the explicit performance incentives, but also sheds light on business practices and thus is of much greater significance. On a related note, the emergence of machine learning techniques makes it possible to test our model with financial data. We thus extend the analysis and even further shift the focus to the M&As application setting as a featured highlight and supplement the existing theoretical analysis with empirical evidence. On top of original objectives, which have been degraded as the benchmark framework as well as the starting point for further analysis, we have more objectives added and listed as below: 6. Disentangle the mechanism of how culture differences influence the M&A firm performance under the previously proposed framework. 7. Supplement the theoretical prediction with empirical evidence and test the validity of the theoretical modelling. 8. Explore the possible means to promote post-merger integration process via the channel of compensation design. 5.3 Realisation of objectives For objectives 1, 2 and 4, we develop an optimal contract model of multi-agents and multi-tasks based on game-theoretical approach with intrinsic motivation as the key element of corporate culture. We fully characterized the equilibrium outcome of the benchmark model under complete information with symmetric types. In the benchmark framework, the determinants of corporate culture adopted by firms have been explored, and it is found that the firm can adopt different corporate cultures with different levels of cooperation. Comparative static analysis also shows that when the agents share higher intrinsic motivation, more cooperative corporate culture will be induced, which lays the foundation for our application to the M&A setting. Minor heterogeneity in cultural differences is considered when applied to the M&A setting and we evaluate its effects on M&A benefit. We characterize a novel but intuitive tradeoff behind the M&A firm performance and identify a sufficient condition for the culture difference to be the cultural clash. The theoretical analysis generates four testable hypotheses centering around corporate culture, incentive pay and M&As, which are listed as follows: H1: Corporate culture and compensation design Firms with stronger corporate culture are associated with a lower incentive pay. H2: Pre-merger deal incidence The probability of deal incidence decreases with acquirer-target corporate cultures differences. H3: Post-merger gain loss In the M&A pairs, the firm pair with larger culture differences suffer more in the post-merger performance. H4: Acculturation after deal completion The incentive pay of the M&A pair with stronger(/weaker) corporate culture will be increased(/decreased) in post-merger phase. For objectives 3 and 5, the effects of how corporate culture impact M&A outcome and firm performance have been studied in the theoretical part and fully explored in hypotheses H2 and H3. The tradeoff newly identified in our research project provides an integrated and compatible framework to understand the seemingly contradictory findings related to this topic in literature from areas in management, finance, and accounting. As the most significant point to reveal the mechanism of how culture differences influence the M&A firm performance as well as the featured highlight of this research project, H4 provides insights on the role that incentive design plays in the post-merger integration process when cultural clash exists. It also implies a channel to "negotiate" culture via managerial incentives, which sheds light on the management practices for the executives in the industry. For objectives 6 and 7, we have finished the data collection work from open sources online and data cleaning work needed for empirical analysis. Much work has been done to enrich the empirical part with solid analysis and ample evidence on the basis of the preliminary results we obtained since last reporting period, which is listed but not limited to: 1. Explore and determine the suitable regression specification to fit with the highlighted theoretical prediction. 2. Replace the dependent variable with other proxies to conduct robustness tests. 3. Apply the regression setting to groups with different sample size to test the validity of the theoretical prediction. The empirical results are almost consistent with the theoretical predictions for the first three hypotheses (H1/H2/H3). For H4, since the statement itself is concerning the adjustment process of corporate culture accompanied with the intended direction of compensation design, the intertwined relationship is complicated and not as clear to be tested with data directly. The complexity to test H4 in a direct and clear way and its significance to this project add to the difficulties in achieving 100% goal regarding objectives 3, 5, 6, 7 and 8. It calls for delicate thinking to disentangle the mechanism step by step and convert the statement to several testable clear-cut relationship between two variables. With the attempts to decompose the mechanism into several testable associations, we expect the last hypothesis testing completes the whole story.

17500219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500219.value: We currently have a working paper which arises directly from this research project. It integrates theoretical analysis and empirical evidence together, with major findings listed as below: 1. We show that the firm can adopt different corporate cultures with different levels of cooperation. Both how firm values the different tasks and the degree of the effort substitution play a role in the adoption of corporate culture. 2. In addition, corporate cultures (cooperation) are tightly linked with incentives in the firm. Stronger cooperation is associated with lower explicit incentives. The empirical result suggests that firms with a strong culture are associated with a 7.2 -percentage-point lower incentive pay measured by scaled WPS than their counterparts whose culture is below the upper quantile. 3. Comparative static analysis also shows that when the agents share higher intrinsic motivation, more cooperative corporate culture will be induced, which lays the foundation for our application to the M&A setting. In the M&A setting, we identify a novel tradeoff underlying the cost and benefit following the cultural clash which reveals the mechanism behind the interplay of corporate culture and incentive pay. 4. The merger outcome will be worsened with larger culture difference leading to greater incentive adjustment only when the substitution effect overwhelms the complementarity effect. The empirical evidence shows that when the measure of cultural distance increases by one standard deviation, the likelihood of a firm-pair becoming an acquirer-target decreases by 5.43%. If the post-merger performance is quantified by the change in operating cash flow ratio, we find when the measure of cultural distance increases by one standard deviation, it is associated with the decrease of 11.7% of a standard deviation in post-M&A performance, ceteris paribus. 5. Our analysis also speaks to the direction of optimal compensation design in the face of cultural integration. The incentive pay of the M&A pair with stronger(/weaker) corporate culture will be increased(/decreased) in post-merger phase.

17500219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500219.value: The findings of our research may help firms formulate their strategy of compensation scheme design to minimize the high risk of merger failure and large value loss resulted from corporate culture issues in M&A activities, which is barely studied in the existing literature. The value of the research project has transformed itself from an applied theory work to a corporate finance work with theoretical foundations. In the future, we intend to have actions listed below: 1. Accomplish the hypothesis testing of H4 and achieve all objectives to 100%. 2. Circulate the working paper and receive more comments from audience in seminars and conferences. 3. Further polish the paper until it gets published.

17500219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500219.value: This paper offers a new perspective on corporate culture which bridges the economic approach with the management literature. By studying an optimal contract model of multi agents and multi-tasking with corporate culture as a key element, our model provides a different explanation in that firms adopt different corporate cultures as optimal responses to trade off between the incentive issues of individual tasks and the intrinsic motivations of cooperation. As an application to the context of mergers and acquisitions, our model explores the mechanism of how incentive design as a powerful tool in organizations may affect corporate culture and further impact firm performance when cultural clash exists. With the emerging breakthrough in machine learning techniques to score corporate culture, suggestive empirical evidence is further presented to supplement our theoretical analysis.

17500619.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17500619.value: Dr Nie, Jun Dr Wang, Gaowang

17500619.label: Project Objectives
17500619.value: The main objective of this project is to develop a tractable continuous-time consumption-portfolio choice model with the Duffie-Epstein SDU, uninsurable labor income, and borrowing constraints to to explore how the interactions of Knightian uncertainty with the separation of risk aversion and intertemporal substitution, borrowing constraints, and incomplete markets affect individual households' optimal consumption-asset allocation decisions. We solve the model explicitly (for the complete-market case) and numerically (for the incomplete-market case), and then quantitatively explore the relative importance of ambiguity aversion, risk aversion, intertemporal substitution, and borrowing constraints in determining the marginal propensity of consumption, precautionary saving, and portfolio choice. Using the U.S. household data (SCF and PSID) on consumption, labor income, and asset holdings, we plan to adopt the detection error probability method to calibrate the empirically plausible amount of Knightian uncertainty and degree of ambiguity aversion and robustness, and then examine how our model can better match the data than the otherwise standard Merton-type model in the aspects of the joint behavior of consumption, income, and wealth. We would like to link the education level to the degree of ambiguity aversion and Knightian uncertainty and the observed stockholding behavior of households with different education. We use the quantitative model to compute the welfare costs of Knightian uncertainty for a typical US household for plausible parameter values. We plan to use our model to explore the importance of Knightian uncertainty in explaining the households' behavior in the Chinese economy if we can find reliable data on Chinese households' asset holdings.

17500619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500619.value: Ordinary households face massive uncertainty in the reality, and need to make optimal consumption-portfolio decisions in an environment in which they are uncertain about the structure and stochastic properties of their model economy. While the uncertainty about future stochastic labor income and asset returns is modeled as risk that households understand and can model in the traditional consumption-portfolio choice models (e.g., Merton 1969, 1971), uncertainty about the data-generating process represents households' pessimism about their ability to identify the correct model. This type of uncertainty is called model uncertainty (or Knightian uncertainty) due to ambiguity aversion and preferences for robustness. There is direct experimental evidence for ambiguity aversion of this sort; for example, Ahn, et al. (2014) used experimental data to estimate a portfolio-choice model and found that about 40 percent of subjects display either ambiguity aversion or statistically significant pessimism . Caballero (2010) also emphasized the importance of understanding model uncertainty for macroeconomics after the 2007-2009 financial crisis. The failure of macroeconomists to predict the recent 2007-2009 Great Recession also suggests possible misspecification of existing macroeconomic models. It is therefore important for us to understand how risk- and ambiguity-averse households make optimal financial decisions when they face uninsurable labor income and how model uncertainty affects the dynamics of consumption, labor income and asset returns as well as the welfare costs due to model uncertainty. Hansen, Sargent, and Tallarini (1999) first introduced model uncertainty due to ambiguity and robustness into economic models, and argued that it provides a new insight about the joint dynamics of aggregate consumption and asset returns. Specifically, households with this preference are concerned that their model may be misspecified; consequently, to minimize their utility as if the subjective distribution over shocks had been chosen by an evil agent. In the proposed project, we plan to construct a tractable continuous-time consumption-saving-portfolio choice framework to explore how the interactions of model uncertainty due to robustness, the Duffie-Epstein (1992a) type of stochastic differential utility, and stochastic income affect the optimal consumption-portfolio decisions and the joint dynamics of consumption, labor income, and asset returns. We plan to first solve the model explicitly (for the complete-market case) and numerically (the incomplete-market case), and estimate and calibrate the key model parameters. Using the plausibly parameter values, we then quantitatively evaluate how our model with Knightian uncertainty can better explain the observed behavior of consumption, savings, and portfolio choice in the reality. 普通家庭在现实世界中面临普遍的不确定性,必须在不确定其模型经济结构和随机特性的环境中做出最优消费组合决策。虽然未来随机劳动力收入和资产回报的不确定性被建模为家庭理解的风险, 并且可以在传统的消费组合模型中建模(例如,Merton 1969、1971), 但数据生成过程的不确定性代表了家庭识别正确模型的能力的悲观情绪。这种不确定性被称为模型不确定性(或奈特不确定性),因为歧义厌恶和对鲁棒性的偏好,这种不确定性被称为模型不确定性(或奈特氏不确定性)。这类歧义规避有直接的实验证据; 例如,Ahn、Choi、Gale 和 Kariv (2014) 使用实验数据来估计投资组合选择模型,发现大约 40%的受试者表现出统计上显著的悲观或模糊规避。宏观经济学家未能预测到最近的 2007-2009 年金融危机导致的大衰退,这也表明现有宏观经济模型可能存在误判。因此,重要的是我们要了解,当家庭面临不可予以保障的劳动收入时,规避风险和模糊的家庭如何做出最佳的财务决策,并且这些类型的不确定性如何影响消费、劳动收入和资产价格的动态以及当存在奈特氏不确定性时社会福利支出。 Hansen 和 Sargent(1995)首先在经济模型中引入了由于模糊性和稳健性导致的模型不确定性,并认为这为总消费和资产价格的联合动态提供了新的视角。具体来说,具有这种偏好的家庭担心他们的模型可能被错误地指定;因此,要尽量减少他们的效用, 就好像是一个邪恶的代理人选择了主观分布的冲击。在所提出的项目中,我们计划建构一个易处理的连续时间消费、储蓄和投资组合框架,以探讨由于鲁棒性、Duffie-Epstein 类型的递归效用和随机收入模型不确定性对最优消费投资组合决策和消费、劳动收入以及风险资产回报联合动态的影响。我们计划首先对模型进行数值求解,然后对关键模型参数进行估计和校正。使用合理的参数值,我们可以定量评估我们的模型如何更好地解释观察到的美国经济中的消费、储蓄和投资组合选择行为。

17500619.label: Realisation of objectives
17500619.value: The objectives proposed in the original application have been realized in our complete working paper entitled: "Ignorance, pervasive uncertainty, and household finance." Specifically, in the paper we examined how the two types of uncertainty due to ignorance, parameter and model uncertainty, jointly affect strategic consumption-portfolio rules, precautionary savings, and welfare. We incorporated these two types of uncertainty into a recursive utility version of a canonical Merton (1971) model with uninsurable labor income and unknown income growth, and derive analytical solutions and testable implications. We showed that the interaction between the two types of uncertainty plays a key role in determining the demand for precautionary savings and risky assets. We derived formulas to evaluate both marginal and total welfare costs of ignorance-induced uncertainty and show they are significant for plausible parameter values.

17500619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17500619.value: In the main paper generated from this project (Ignorance, pervasive uncertainty, and household finance), we have studied the implications of two types of ignorance-induced uncertainty, parameter and model uncertainty, for consumption-portfolio rules and precautionary savings in a continuous-time recursive utility model with uninsurable labor income. Specifically, we explicitly solved the model to explore how the two types of ignorance-induced uncertainty interact with intertemporal substitution, risk aversion, and the correlation between the risky asset and labor income. We show that they have distinct impacts on households’ decisions on consumption, precautionary savings, and strategic asset allocation, and can help the model better explain the data on household portfolios. Finally, our analysis suggests that the welfare gains from reducing the amount of induced uncertainty due to ignorance can be significant.

17500619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17500619.value: Our study is related to the literature on uncertainty and household finance. We contribute to this literature by presenting a tractable but comprehensive model and linking the model's predictions to the empirical counterpart. The main results generated from this project can be extended to study heterogeneity we observed in other developed economies as well emerging economies who face more induced-uncertainty.

17500619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500619.value: Ordinary households face pervasive uncertainty in the real world, and have to make optimal consumption-portfolio decisions in an environment in which they are uncertain about the structure and stochastic properties of their model economy. While the uncertainty about future stochastic labor income and asset returns is modeled as risk that the households understand and can model in the traditional consumption-portfolio models, uncertainty about the data-generating process represents households' pessimism about their ability to identify the correct model. This type of uncertainty is called model uncertainty due to ambiguity aversion and preferences for robustness. There is direct experimental evidence for ambiguity aversion of this sort; for example, Ahn, et al. (2014) used experimental data to estimate a portfolio-choice model and found that about 40 percent of subjects display either statistically significant pessimism or ambiguity aversion. Caballero (2010) also argued that the failure of macroeconomists to predict the recent 2007-2009 Great Recession due to the financial crisis also suggests possible misspecification of existing macroeconomic models. It is therefore important for us to understand how risk- and ambiguity-averse households make optimal financial decisions when they face uninsurable labor income and how these types of uncertainty affect the dynamics of consumption, labor income and asset prices.

17500719.value: 具有不可观测个人特定阈效应的面板阈回归

17500719.label: Project Objectives
17500719.value: We will develop a correlated random effects estimation method when the individual-specific effects are regime-dependent. Specification tests will be constructed to check the sufficiency of the assumed correlated random effects framework to control endogeneity and to determine whether the individual-specific effects are indeed regime-dependent. Our estimation and testing methods will be extended to handle more general patterns of endogeneity in panel data. Simulation studies will be conducted to check the validity and finite sample performance of our estimation methods and tests. The methods will be applied to a real data set to check their performance and assess the importance of endogenous and regime dependent thresholding in practical work.

17500719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17500719.value: 基于面板数据的估计和推断在计量经济学中非常流行。由于数据结构更丰富，面板数据可以回答比横截面数据更多的问题。首先，面板数据可以轻松处理可能诱发内生性的个体特定效应。其次，面板数据可以模拟动态效应，这对于横截面数据是不可能的。最近关于面板阈值回归（PTR）的文献增加了面板数据的阈值效应，因此允许因变量和自变量之间存在非线性关系。静态面板和动态面板模型都有在文献中考虑，但在所有现有文献中都存在一个关键限制，即个人特定效应不依赖于(阈变量)区域。如果因变量与可观察的自变量之间的关系是与区域有关的，则很难相信它与不可观察的个体特定效应的关系是与区域无关的。该项目试图将静态和动态面板阈值回归扩展到这个更现实的情形。换句话说，我们允许不同区域有不同的个体特定效应。 当个体特定效应与区域无关时，可以应用通常的除均（或差分）方法，这是所有PTR文献的估计策略。然而，当个体特定效应与区域有关时，该策略不能直接应用。所以我们首先使用张伯伦 - 蒙德拉克的相关随机效应（CRE）策略来控制内生性，该策略本质上是一种控制函数方法。在控制内生性之后，可以应用通常的最小二乘法来估计阈值点和斜率。通过扩展现有文献可以实现所有的渐近分布和统计推断。 CRE估计中的一个关键假设是内生性完全受控，否则估计量不一致。因此，我们进一步检验假设的CRE是否足以控制内生性。该检验用于测试一组条件均值独立（CMI）假设。这个检验有三个困难。首先，面板数据中条件变量的维数很大，因此通常的CMI检验将遭受维数的诅咒。其次，我们需要联合检验多个CMI假设。第三，目标变量是阈值参数的不连续函数。作为对这些困难的回应，我们将最近提出的基于MDD的检验扩展到当前情形。如果该检验通过，我们可以进一步检验个体特定性效应是否确实依赖于区域。 除了基本的CRE方法外，我们进一步讨论如何将除均（或差分）方法扩展到特定于区域的除均（或差分）方法，以及将CRE策略扩展到特定于区域的CRE策略以处理更一般的内生模式。

17500719.label: Realisation of objectives
17500719.value: In this project, we study the estimation and inferences in panel threshold regression with unobserved individual-specific threshold effects which is important from the practical perspective and is a distinguishing feature from traditional linear panel data models. We finished all objectives on time. We actually did more than planned. For example, we show the within-regime differencing in the static model or the within-regime first-differencing in the dynamic model cannot generate consistent estimators of the threshold, we propose an adaptive Bonferroni inference on the slope parameters, and we also propose a test for the existence of the unobserved individual-specific threshold effects. Due to COVID-19, we presented this paper only in the 2021 China Meeting of the Econometric Society, and will present this paper in the 2022 Asia Meeting of the Econometric Society.

17500719.value: During the project, we find another potential problem to solve. The correlated random effects in this project take a parametric form, but what will happen if they take a nonparametric form? We are currently preparing another paper where BART is grafted to nonparametric panel threshold regression to obtain an efficient estimator of the threshold; we are trying to establish conditions under which the posterior credible intervals have frequentist validity and establishing semiparametric Bernstein-von Mises theorems for the threshold.

17500719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17500719.value: This project is the first attempt to solve the estimation and inference problem in panel threshold regression with unobserved individual-specific threshold effects. It is surprising to see that the usual differencing method in linear panel data models fails, which provides an essential difference between panel data models with threshold effects and the tranditional linar panel data models. Such a difference was not observed in the literature.

17501219.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17501219.value: 行贿有益于中国企业绩效吗？对市场能力副作用的研究

17501219.label: Project Objectives
17501219.value: To understand the direct effect of bribery on performance and its indirect effect on performance through market capabilities. To understand how institutional factors (i.e., government purchase power and government intervention) moderate the effects of bribery on market capabilities. To understand how organizational characteristics (i.e., state ownership and organizational slack) moderate the effects of bribery on market capabilities. To provide managerial implications for firms to caution against the dark-side of bribery and understand how to enhance their market capabilities to foster performance in China.

To understand how institutional factors (i.e., government purchase power and government intervention) moderate the effects of bribery on market capabilities.
To understand how organizational characteristics (i.e., state ownership and organizational slack) moderate the effects of bribery on market capabilities.
To provide managerial implications for firms to caution against the dark-side of bribery and understand how to enhance their market capabilities to foster performance in China.

17501219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17501219.value: Market capabilities, a firm’s ability to deploy and use its resources to generate valuable output to compete in the marketplace, is critical to long-term growth and success. However, the institutional voids in emerging economies, such as the weak factor markets and lack of intellectual property protection, seriously challenge the efficacy of market capabilities. Accordingly, firms proactively employ nonmarket strategies, such as lobby, litigation, bribery, etc., to overcome institutional voids, among which bribery is particularly prevalent in emerging economies. The world’s four major emerging economies—Brazil, Russia, India, and China—consistently rank among the most corrupt nations (Transparency International 2017). While the detrimental effect of bribery on macro-level economic growth is well recognized, controversy exists regarding how it may affect firm-level performance. Extant literature offers two competing views, regarding bribery as either the “grease” or “sand” in the wheels. The grease view suggests that bribery helps firms deal with institutional voids and hence facilitates business activities that would be hampered by bureaucratic delay. In contrast, the sand view argues that bribery creates rather than corrects inefficiencies such that the bribing firms face the risk of request for more bribes, uncertainty of the promised returns, and intervention from corrupt officials. Moreover, prior research overlooks how bribery as a nonmarket strategy would affect firms’ market capabilities, which is a critical driver of sustainable advantage. To address these research gaps, our project investigates the relationships between bribery, market capabilities, and firm performance in China. We propose that although bribery may foster firm performance, it hurts the development of market capabilities and in turn decreases firm performance indirectly. Moreover, we examine how institutional factors and organizational characteristics moderate the bribery–market capabilities relationships. Specifically, we consider the following research questions: (1) How does bribery affect market capabilities and firm performance? (2) How do institutional factors (i.e., government purchase power and government intervention) moderate the effects of bribery on market capabilities? (3) How do organizational characteristics (i.e., state ownership and organizational slack) moderate the effects of bribery on market capabilities? By examining the links between bribery, market capabilities, and firm performance, this project will provide a more holistic view of bribery. Its findings will offer important managerial implications for firms to caution against the dark-side of bribery and understand how to enhance their market capabilities to foster performance in China. 市场能力是企业长青之道。但是，新兴市场中的制度缺陷，例如弱要素市场及法制保护不完善，极大地挑战了市场能力的作用。所以，企业往往采用非市场战略，例如游说，立法，行贿以应对制度缺陷。其中行贿最为普遍，世界上四大新兴市场—巴西，俄罗斯，印度，和中国—都是腐败严重的国家。 尽管腐败对经济增长的危害众所周知，行贿是否有益于企业绩效存在争议。现有文献对腐败有两种观点：润滑剂论vs. 砂子论。前者认为行贿能帮助企业应对制度缺陷并促进商业活动，而后者认为行贿阻碍了效率并增加了运营风险。现有研究还忽略了行贿作为非市场战略如何影响市场能力，企业长青的关键因素。 为解决这些问题，我们将研究行贿，市场能力，和企业绩效之间的关系。我们认为虽然行贿可能能增加绩效，行贿同时会降低市场能力并间接地降低绩效。我们还会研究制度要素和组织特性如何调节行贿与市场能力之间的关系。研究问题如下： （1） 行贿如何影响中国企业的市场能力和绩效？ （2） 制度要素(政府购买力和政府干预)如何调节行贿与市场能力之间的关系？ （3） 组织特性(国有制和组织冗余)如何调节行贿与市场能力之间的关系？ 本项目的研究结果将揭示行贿对企业绩效的全面影响；这不仅会丰富行贿之文献，还会对在华企业如何避免行贿并获得市场能力以及卓越绩效提供重要的指导。

17501219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17501219.value: Major findings: 1) We find that even though bribery may provide a means to deal with institutional voids, such that it fosters firms’ short-term performance (i.e., sales growth), it hinders long-term performance reflected in market capitalization. In addition, nonmarket strategy (i.e., political ties) hurts the development of market capability such as operational efficiency. 2) When institutional factors are improving (i.e., less government power and intervention), the positive effect of bribery on sales growth decreases and its negative impact on market capitalization increases. 3) Foreign ownership reduces corporate bribery expenditures, reflecting the disciplinary role of foreign investors. Moreover, the effect is weakened by regional corruption and regional gambling prevalence, while it is enhanced by top executive overseas experience. 4) These findings caution about the use of bribery to achieve performance and offer important insights into how international investors affect bribery in investee firms in consideration of local institutional environments. Outcome: Three papers published in peer-reviewed journals. 1) Zhou, KZ, K Wang, D Xu, E Xie (2022), “Drinking Poison to Quench Thirst: Does Bribery Foster Firm Performance in China?” Journal of Business Research, 147: 505-517. 2) Shen L, KZ Zhou, K Wang, and C Zhang (2023), “Do Political Ties facilitate Operational Efficiency? A Contingent Political Embeddedness Perspective,” Journal of Operations Management, 69(1): 159-183. 3) Jiang W, K Wang, KZ Zhou (2023), “How Political Ties and Green Innovation Co-Evolve in China: Alignment with Institutional Development and Environmental Pollution,” Journal of Business Ethics, forthcoming. Outcome: one working paper under review at peer-reviewed journal 1) “Foreign Ownership and Corporate Bribery in Emerging Markets: An Institutional Perspective”, under 3rd review at Journal of Business Research.

17501219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17501219.value: One potential way is to study how female entrepreneurship affects the use of nonmarket strategies (e.g., bribery) and market strategies (e.g., innovation) in emerging markets. Given the challenges brought by institutional voids in emerging markets, it is interesting to examine what strategies female entrepreneurs would take to address these challenges.

17501219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17501219.value: This project examines how bribery affects firm performance in China. In particular, we have the following major findings: 1) While bribery helps boost a firm’s short-term performance in terms of sales growth, it is detrimental to its long-term performance. 2) Nations should improve their institutional development in order to reduce the benefits of bribery and aggravate its negative performance impact. 3) Local firms are encouraged to attract foreign investors such that foreign ownership can help reduce bribery expenditure. 4) Firms should fully recognize the dark side of bribery and try to develop alternative strategies in order to achieve long-term success. The findings of this project not only enrich our understanding of the roles of bribery in emerging markets, but also provide important managerial implications for firms to employ proper strategies to achieve long-term performance.

17502219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17502219.value: 税收是政府重新分配财富和收入的重要手段。因此，政府对于再分配税收的偏好会影响税收政策和公司税收规避。尽管之前的文献研究了各种不同的利益方便好对于税收规避的影响，政府在其中所起的作用仍然不是很明确。在这个项目中，我们尝试填补这个空白，研究政治家个人意识形态中再分配的偏好对于够公司税收规避的影响。 为了解决这个问题，我们研究中国的企业。因为中国地方政府对当地的企业税收有很大的影响。我们用中国1978年改革开放作为一个实验，因为改革开放显著的改变了中国的意识形态。我们预期当地市委书记在1978年之前入党的，被灌输的比较强的社会主义意识形态，从而有着对税收更强的偏好。这个想法是基于之前的社会学研究发现，人的意识形态是在他们早起生活中加入政党形成的。 我们会首先提供直接的证据，公司在1978年之前入党的市委书记管制下，有效税率更高。然后我们会通过横断面方法来研究意识形态是如何影响公司税率的。最后，我们会研究当地政府是否有更高的花费。我们会用psm和heckman检验来减小内生性的顾虑。

17502219.label: Realisation of objectives
17502219.value: First of all, we would like to thank RGC for providing funding for this project. Before I elaborate on the realization of the objectives, I would like to take this opportunity to clarify and explain some of the incidents happening throughout the funding periods, which have led to the under-spending of the funding as well as the delayed outcome of publication: currently we have a Revise and Resubmission from Management Science, by the time of submitting this completion report. The project was set to commence on Jan 1st 2020. Despite the early disruption of the pandemic, the project was carried on as the earlier work could be undertaken at home office, such as literature review, gathering and analyzing second hand dataset. Also initial discussion among the co-author teams could be regularly arranged as we were all based in Hong Kong. We have finished almost half of the project during the one and half year. However, the project went through significant changes as the initial PI, Dr Ke Na was relocated to Beijing from Hong Kong in the summer of 2021, and the Co-I Dr Danqing Wang took off the project as PI in late 2021. Such change has caused some delays in transferring the funding to different institutions, which also delayed the whole process of hiring new RAs to collect more data required by the reviewers from journal submission. What was worse was the continuation of the pandemic and the quarantine and travel restriction policy both in mainland China and Hong Kong until the end of 2022. Some RAs failed to come to Hong Kong. Per HKUST’s policy, we can only pay a RA if she/he is physically on campus. Finally a RA was hired in the summer of 2022, thanks to RGC’s approval to extend the project for another year until the end of 2022. Meantime, the PI could not travel to the U.S. for conferences. Those unexpected policies led to the under-spending of the funding. Despite the above mentioned challengers and changes, we managed to move forward the project. For example, we still attended a significant conference on line and also submitted the paper to several top journals to gain feedbacks. Finally the paper received a revise and resubmission decision from Management Science in early 2023. Unfortunately, the funding has already ended by Dec 31st of 2022. Then, I would like to elaborate on the realization of objectives set in this project. First, we spent funding in hiring RAs to collect data on the party secretaries’ speeches in important events to assess their corresponding political ideology. For example, we have collected all the headlines of city daily newspapers reporting the activities of the incumbent party secretaries and coded relevant words reflecting their communist political ideology. Such data collection efforts have greatly strengthened our measurements on political ideology in addition to measuring it using the timing of joining the party. This is to help achieve the first objective. Second, we have also collected more types of taxation behaviors. By differentiating the entities who are collecting the taxes, we find that party secretaries’ ideology has a stronger effect on those local taxes, in a way that firms engage in less tax avoidance if the tax is collected by the local tax authorities. But we do not see much difference if the tax is collected by the central agency. Such a finding provides strong support for objective one as well. Third, we have also collected more newspaper reports to provide more qualitative evidence on how party secretaries are influencing the local tax policies. Further, we refined the empirical analysis on how ideology affects tax avoidance through tax benefit provision and enforcement of tax rules. For example, we have collected new data on what the exact tax benefits qualified firms may obtain. Those efforts are used to achieve objective two. Forth, we have also deepened the analysis on the interaction between economic interests and ideological preferences in shaping tax avoidance. On the one hand, we find that ideology can reduce the benefits of political connections for firms to engage more in tax avoidance. Thus we provide more insights that ideological preferences can trump economic interests. On the other hand, we are also doing more analysis on the interaction between political incentives and ideological preferences. This is consistent with objective three, but potentially disclosing additional facet for politicians’ incentives and preferences. During the time of preparing this completion report, we are about to submit back the revised version of this paper for Management Science, with the hope that we can get another minor revision before it can be finally published.

17502219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17502219.value: This project examines the impact of politicians’ ideologies on corporate taxation. Our tests exploit the implementation of the 1978 Reform and Opening-up policy in China that significantly weakens the communist ideology. Using textual analyses of city secretaries’ speeches during corporate visits and the headline stories reported by the city daily newspaers, we first establish that individuals who joined the communist party before the 1978 reform continue to have a stronger communist ideology after they become city secretaries. We next show that, in the post-reform period, the effective tax rates of firms in cities whose secretaries joined the communist party before the reform are significantly higher than those of firms with secretaries joining the communist party after. Also, we find consistent evidence that such effect is stronger with locally collected taxes, such as property tax; not with the taxes that are collected by the central government, such as customs duty. Secretaries’ communist ideology also acts as a commitment device mitigating the effect of firms’ political connections on corporate taxation. Additional tests reveal that secretaries’ ideology affects corporate taxation through both tax benefit provisions and enforcements of tax rules. A regression discontinuity design approach exploiting the age qualification of party members provides consistent results

17502219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17502219.value: 1. we need more analysis to establish that the assignment of party secretaries to different cities is not related to their ideology. 2. we can also provide more illustrations on how party secretaries decide the taxation policies and how they intervene into the process, e.g., what kinds of firms can receive more or less tax benefits. 3. we can also analyze more regional variations and also generational shifts. 4. Relatedly, we can also provide the analysis of the effect of ideology on other policies: such as education, welfare provision to show the ranges of its impact.

17502219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17502219.value: The project shows that politicians' ideology matters on economic activities. Ideology shapes how individuals perceive the world and how the economic welfare is produced and distributed. Using China as a context which underwent a dramatic ideological shift in 1978, we find evidence that politicians' communist ideology decides the taxation behaviors of firms located in their adminstrative reign. Specifically, secretaries who were socialized into the party before 1978 were imprinted with a very strong communist ideology and thus believed in common wealth and egalitarianism. Thus the effective tax rates were found higher for firms under their regions, compared with firms located in regions with secretaries who were imprinted with a more market-oriented ideology.

17503019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503019.value: Ample regulatory resources have been devoted to improving financial information, for example, to enhance financial reporting and audit quality. Many scholars, however, doubt the current efficacy of such regulations. One criticism is that current regulations overlook the fact that corporations and audit firms strategically compete for talented workers and that human capital is an important element in determining the effectiveness of auditing and the quality of financial statements (e.g., Barth, Caprio, and Levine, 2012). Little attention has been paid to the allocation of human capital (i.e., accounting experts) across corporations and audit firms, even though the search for the optimal regulation has received much attention. In this project, we study the effect of the labor market for accounting experts on strategic actions by corporations and audit firms in a model in which their decisions about human capital are interdependent. More specifically, we investigate 1) what determines the allocation of human capital between corporations and audit firms and 2) how the labor market influences corporate financial reporting and investment efficiency. To explore the interaction between accounting information and labor decisions, we develop a labor market model with heterogeneous ability levels in agents. The corporations and audit firms compete for expertise in the labor market, and their incentives to hire highly skilled and experienced labor depend on the state of the economy. The model predicts that corporations might have more incentives to attract high-skilled labor away from audit firms when the economy is strong, which could thus trigger a stylized pattern of financial reporting quality and capital allocation that has been observed in boom-bust cycles. The analysis highlights the impact of not only the externality of labor decisions but also the aggregated accounting information. This proposed project will make a number of significant contributions. First, it will provide new explanations for the puzzling patterns of corporate financial reporting and investment decisions by investigating the labor market for accounting experts. To our best knowledge, this research will be the first attempt to introduce the labor market into the literature on financial reporting and capital allocation. Second, it will help standard setters implement appropriate measures under changing economic conditions by providing insights on how the labor market equilibrium, which can potentially affect financial information quality, evolves with the state of the economy. Lastly, the project will offer important guidance for future empirical research on labor choice, financial reporting, and investment decisions. 大量的监管资源被用于改善财务信息以提高财务报告和审计质量。然而，许多学者对这些法规的现行效力表示怀疑。一种批评是现行法规忽略了这样一个事实：企业和会计师事务所战略性地进行人才竞争，而人力资本是决定审计有效性和财务报表质量的重要因素（如Barth、Caprio和Levin，2012）。尽管寻找最优的监管受到了广泛重视，但人力资本（如会计专家）在企业和会计师事务所之间的分配问题几乎没有受到关注。在这个项目中，我们构建了一个企业和会计师事务所的人力资本决策相互依赖的模型，并借此研究了会计专家劳动力市场对企业和审计公司战略的影响。更具体地说，我们研究了1）企业和审计公司之间人力资本分配的决定因素；2）劳动力市场如何影响公司财务报告和投资有效性。 为了探讨会计信息与劳动力决策之间的相互作用，我们构建了一个存在不同专业水平代理人的劳动力市场模型。企业和会计师事务所在劳动力市场为专家人才而竞争，他们雇佣高水平员工的意愿受经济状况的影响。该模型预测，当经济强劲时，企业可能会有更强的动机去吸引高水平劳动力离开会计师事务所，这会进而引发一种在繁荣-萧条周期中观察到的财务报告质量和资本分配的规律性模式。本文分析不仅突出了劳动决策的外部性而且也强调了加总性的会计信息的影响。 本项目将做出数个重要贡献。首先，通过探索会计专家劳动力市场，本项目将为企业财务报告和投资决策的令人费解的模式提供新的解释。据我们所知，本研究将是把劳动力市场引入财务报告和资本配置文献的首次尝试。第二，本项目将提供劳动力市场均衡如何随经济形势变化的见解，且我们考虑到劳动力市场均衡可能影响财务信息质量，这将有助于准则制定者在不断变化的经济条件下实施合适的度量方法。最后，该项目将为未来有关劳动力选择、财务报告和投资决策的实证研究提供重要指导。

17503219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17503219.value: Population aging is widely observed in many countries. It brings benefits to most individuals, but it may also cause problems, particularly if citizens do not adjust their behavior appropriately. A potential problem is that individuals may outlive their resources and face financial inadequacy during old age. People may hedge longevity risk (the risk of outliving one’s financial resources) by purchasing annuities. Alternatively, citizens in countries adopting the pay-as-you-go (PAYGO) retirement pension system may rely (at least partially) on its benefits. However, neither solution seems to solve the problem satisfactorily. In this project, I plan to understand the “annuity puzzle” (that few retirees spend a substantial portion of their wealth on annuities) and analyze some welfare-improving solutions to deal with longevity risk. In particular, I plan to consider a public annuity (PA) scheme, an alternative to private annuities and the PAYGO system. The first task is to set up a simple analytical model of a PA scheme and examine some major factors relevant to understanding the annuity puzzle. Based on the literature about the annuity puzzle, I plan to combine heterogeneity in survival probability with bequest heterogeneity (and perhaps other factors too) and study the relative importance of these factors in affecting adverse selection in annuities. The second task is to focus on the policy design for a PA. Based on the literature review and the actual PA practices, I have identified some interesting aspects related to the form and number of pubic annuities. For example, a maximum amount of PA purchase is imposed in Singapore and Hong Kong. As adverse selection arises from individuals’ choice in the presence of asymmetric information, imposing restrictions on the maximum amount of annuity purchase may be beneficial. On the other hand, imposing restrictions on buyers’ choices is welfare-reducing generally. It is interesting to study the combined effect. Economists have long argued that conventional economic factors may not fully explain the annuity puzzle. I plan to see how a particular behavioral factor, loss aversion, may interact with the bequest motive to affect the annuitization decision. I will compare the benefit of a greater guarantee amount of the PA under the behavioral assumption of loss aversion with that under the conventional approach. A hypothesis in this context is that when loss aversion is important in the utility function of some annuity buyers, a higher level of the guarantee clause may lead to a higher level of annuitization. 近年來,我們看到不同國家的人均壽命增長了。一方面, 市民有更多時間去享受生活。另一方面,長壽也可帶給長者生活上的困難,包括晚年時可能經濟資源不足。 市民預期將來面對「長壽風險」(即活得比預期長但年青時儲蓄不足),可以向私人財務機構買年金。另外,在實施「隨收隨付」退休金制度的國家,國民可以部份倚靠這制度提供的福利去應付「長壽風險」。可是,這兩種方法都不足以充分應付「長壽風險」。 由於以上兩種方法都有不理想之處,我打算在這計劃中研究另一選擇：「公共年金」。這研究計劃有兩個目標:第一,我打算分析為何很少長者買年金;第二,我打算研究何種方法可以有效幫助長者面對「長壽風險」。 研究計劃第一項工作是制定一個簡單而合適的數學模型去分析公共年金,並且用這模型去研究為何很少退休人士買年金。這模型建基於以下兩個重要因素：市民不同程度的「健康狀態」和「遺贈動機」。我打算用這模型去研究不同因素如何影響年金市場的運作,特別是年金市場逆向選擇的程度。 這計劃第二項工作是研究公共年金的設計。基於學者的研究結果和不同地方的公共年金安排,我打算研究公共年金的型態和數目。舉一個例子,公共年金計劃中之「最高保費金額」安排可能減低年金的逆向選擇嚴重程度,但這種限制亦會令某些長者不能選擇他們最理想的年金份量。我會研究那種安排可以較有效平衡利弊。 經濟學者多年前已指出傳統經濟理論未能完全解釋為何長者很少購買年金。我在這計劃中可能探討其中一個「行為經濟」因素：「損失規避」。我打算探討這因素和遺贈動機互動下如何影響年金購買的數量,並比較根據「損失規避」的假設和傳統經濟因素的假設下, 公共年金之「保證條款」安排有什麼不同效果。

17503219.label: Realisation of objectives
17503219.value: Objective 1: "To construct a simple theoretical framework to explore the explanatory power of various factors for the annuity puzzle, such as adverse selection, bequest motive, liquidity concern, and precautionary motive." We are able to construct a simple but useful framework to examine issues related to retirees' annuitization decisions. After various attempts, we finally settled down in choosing a two-period model with survival probability heterogeneity. Together with the empirically relevant assumption of asymmetric information, the outcome of adverse selection in annuity purchase is obtained. This feature appears in two papers (co-authored with Qilin Zhang) in this project. They are “A common thread linking the design of guarantee and non-escalating payments of public annuities” (Journal of Risk and Insurance, 2023) and “Severity reduction and private market distortion effects of voluntary and mandatory public annuity plans” (Macroeconomic Dynamics, forthcoming). Bequest motive, the other factor relevant to annuitization choice, also appears in the former paper. According to our assessment, 100% of Objective 1 is achieved. Objective 2: "To study systematically policy design issues of public annuities, by evaluating different policies based on welfare comparison and feasibility concerns." In this project, we analyze policy design issues of public annuities at two levels. First, the paper “Severity reduction and private market distortion effects of voluntary and mandatory public annuity plans” analyze the similarities and differences of voluntary public annuity with ceiling (VPAc) plan and mandatory public annuity with flexibility (MPAf) plan. Introducing either plan reduces the severity of adverse selection in public annuities, but further distorts the private annuity market. These two plans have systematically different effects on retirees’ utility levels: the good health group are adversely affected and the average health group benefits. On the other hand, the poor health group benefits from the VPAc plan but may be adversely affected under the MPAf plan. On the other hand, the paper “A common thread linking the design of guarantee and non-escalating payments of public annuities” analyze two empirically observed features: (a) a guarantee feature which bundles annuity income and bequeathable wealth components, and (b) non-escalating payments. The results have useful implications regarding the design of public annuities. According to our assessment, 100% of Objective 2 is achieved.

17503219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17503219.value: Many economies have recently adopted the defined-contribution retirement financing system, but one disadvantage of this system is that retirees have to bear longevity risk. As a result, several economies have also introduced the public annuity plans. Motivated by recent experiences in economies adopting the defined-contribution pension system, we study public annuities in this project. In the paper “A common thread linking the design of guarantee and non-escalating payments of public annuities” (co-authored with Qilin Zhang), we found that the difference of annuitization-weighted and unweighted averages of survival probabilities is a useful measure of the severity of adverse selection. We then examine public annuities with a guarantee feature which bundles annuity income and bequeathable wealth components. We show that when the heterogeneity in survival probability is limited, the magnitude of guarantee proportion is irrelevant. On the other hand, an increase in the guarantee proportion mitigates adverse selection when the extent of heterogeneity is sufficiently large, because the share of annuity purchase by retirees with lower (resp. higher) survival probabilities is increased (resp. decreased). We also obtain a similar set of results for public annuities with non-escalating payments. The results have useful implications regarding the design of public annuities. This paper was published in Journal of Risk and Insurance Vol. 90(3), September 2023, 703-742. In the paper “Severity reduction and private market distortion effects of voluntary and mandatory public annuity plans” (co-authored with Q. Zhang), we analyzed the similarities and differences of voluntary public annuity with ceiling (VPAc) plan and mandatory public annuity with flexibility (MPAf) plan that are empirically observed. Introducing either plan reduces the severity of adverse selection in public annuities, but further distorts the private annuity market. These two plans have systematically different effects on retirees’ utility levels: the good health group are adversely affected and the average health group benefits. On the other hand, the poor health group benefits from the VPAc plan but may be adversely affected under the MPAf plan. This paper has been accepted for publication by Macroeconomic Dynamics (https://doi.org/10.1017/S1365100523000093).

17503219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action

17503219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17503219.value: Many economies have recently adopted the defined-contribution retirement financing system, but one disadvantage of this system is that retirees have to bear longevity risk. As a result, several economies have also introduced the public annuity plans. We study public annuities in this project, and found that the difference of annuitization-weighted and unweighted averages of survival probabilities is a useful measure of the severity of adverse selection. Applying this idea, we analyzed the similarities and differences of voluntary public annuity with ceiling (VPAc) plan and mandatory public annuity with flexibility (MPAf) plan that are empirically observed. Introducing either plan reduces the severity of adverse selection in public annuities, but further distorts the private annuity market. These two plans have systematically different effects on retirees’ utility levels. We also examine issues regarding the design of public annuities. Specifically, we study public annuities with a guarantee feature which bundles annuity income and bequeathable wealth components. We also study public annuities with non-escalating payments. The results have useful implications regarding the design of public annuities.
