17600419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17600419.value: The project's objective has been fully achieved. The project's results also provided major research findings and outcomes to evaluate our hypothesis. Research findings and outcome to evaluate our hypothesis (Objective): Older adults who completed the external attention focus walking training during gait re-education will have lower real-time conscious motor processing propensity and better rehabilitation outcome than older adults who completed the internal or no attention focus walking training. Only external attention focus walking group (EAFWG) showed significant reduction in real-time conscious motor processing (EEG T3-Fz coherence) immediately after the walking training programme. This was indicated by a significant Group x Time interaction effect on the T3-Fz EEG coherence (a measure of real-time conscious motor processing), where only EAFWG showed significant decrease in EEG T3-Fz coherence immediately after training. This finding supports our hypothesis, indicating that the primary outcome of real-time conscious motor processing can be diminished following an external attention focus walking training. Thus, it accomplishes the primary objective of this study. Additionally, all groups showed significant improvements in functional balance and gait and balance ability immediately after training. This was indicated by significant main effects of time observed for the Tinetti Balance Assessment Tool (POMA) and Berg Balance Scale (BBS), respectively. The scores significantly improved across all groups (EAFWG, IAFWG, and NAFWG) immediately after walking trainings. Despite the limited interaction effects among the three groups regarding these secondary physical outcomes immediately post trainings, only EAFWG showed significant improvement in functional balance and gait in the long-term (6 months after training) compared to baseline. This adds support to the hypothesis of achieving better physical rehabilitation outcome (functional balance and gait) in EAFWG compared to the IAFWG and NAFWG as a long-term effect of external focus walking training. All groups showed no significant changes in other psychological fall-related secondary outcomes including MSRS-C and FES-I (Ch) scores. This was indicated by an insignificant Group x Time interaction effect, main effect of time and group for all these measures. In summary, our research findings suggested that use of external focus instructions during walking training could immediately reduce real-time conscious motor processing as well as improve functional balance and gait and balance ability among older adults with moderate-to-high risk of falling. In particular, the gains in functional balance and gait can be sustained for a longer period of 6 months with the use of external focus training, potentially further reducing their risk of falling.

17600419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17600419.value: Results of this research project demonstrated the beneficial immediate training effect of external focused instructions on real-time conscious motor processing as well as functional balance and gait and balance ability among older adults with increased risk of falling when compared to internal focused and no focused instructions. Improvements in functional balance and gait were sustained for a period of 6 months under the use of external focused instructions during walking training, which demonstrated the potential long-term benefits with the use of external focused strategy during gait training. It suggested novel and important information to healthcare professionals about the potential benefits of external attention focus instructions to patients in the clinical settings, such as geriatric gait rehabilitation. Targeted rehabilitative interventions, involving external attention focus instructions, could be adopted to enhance fall prevention as an adjunctive treatment strategy in addition to traditional falls prevention training such as balance and strengthening exercises. Further research could determine the best dosage and intensity of the training protocol, investigate the integration of psychological interventions such as cognitive behavioral therapy to target psychological fall-related outcomes, and evaluate the potential extended effects on other fall-related rehabilitation outcomes for solidifying its therapeutic potential in the field of falls prevention.

17600419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17600419.value: Walking usually requires minimal attention. However, older adults may consciously direct their attention more towards their body movements internally, when encountering movement difficulties or fear of falling. Focusing externally during walking may promote the automaticity of motor coordination, which could potentially improve motor performance and reduce the risk of falling. This research project aimed to examine the effect of different attentional focus walking training strategies on both physical and psychological fall-related outcomes among older adults at risk of falling so as to develop a potential fall prevention approach for the community. This current project contributes significantly to our understanding of the beneficial effects of gait training with external focus instructions on improving fall-related outcome performance among older adults with higher risk of falling. It could facilitate the planning of rehabilitative gait training that incorporates external attention focus instructions, aiming to reduce the tendency of conscious involvement during movements and improve functional balance and gait, reducing their risk of falling. Our findings indicated that healthcare practitioners in clinical settings may adopt external attention focus instructions that distract individuals from body movements, as an additional training strategy to traditional approaches during gait rehabilitation and/or fall prevention programs for older adults.

17600619.label: Project Objectives
17600619.value: to critically analyse representative nineteenth-century authors’ travelogues alongside their novels; to contribute to ongoing scholarly discussions about form, genre and poetics in relation to the (nineteenth-century) novel; to show, by way of exemplification, the importance of a scholarly focus on form, genre and poetics in the context of travel writing; to trace the genesis of the modern novel form by way of the older travel writing genre; to complete a series of articles in international, peer-reviewed journals and prepare a single-authored monograph for publication with an international university press.

17600619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600619.value: Mikhail Bakhtin describes the modern novel as a quarrelsome, rude, even cannibalistic newcomer that appropriates, reinvents and sometimes replaces older aesthetic traditions in its own endeavour to write new and relevant stories for a contemporary, changing world (1981, 4). However, neither Bakhtin nor later scholars of the novel mention travel writing as one of the older genres from which the modern novel borrowed and benefited – which my proposed project suggests. Likewise, travel writing scholars have failed to focus on the poetic and generic rules and range of the travelogue. Jonathan Raban’s famous characterisation that travel writing is ‘a notoriously raffish open house where different genres are likely to end up in the same bed’ (1988, 231) mirrors Bakhtin’s characterisation of an equally inviting and loose novel and compels my analysis of the form of the travelogue and its place in the evolution of narrative. A single study to date – Percy Adams’s 1983 ‘Travel Literature and the Evolution of the Novel’ – has brought the genres together, albeit not into dialogue. The shortcoming of Adams’s book is that it is simply an archive: Adams identifies hundreds of travelogues in all major European languages between the early modern period to around 1800 but his discussion of how the novel learned from the travelogue is restricted to extremely basic claims – albeit true – that they both walk a fine line between ‘truth’ and ‘lies’ and both feature a plot, characters, the tropes of departure and arrival, the idea of development and moments of heightened activity alongside moments of stasis. There is no space in Adams’s recovery project for a focus on specific authors, let alone a sustained literary-critical analysis with sophisticated theoretical parameters. Such an omission in scholarship is surprising: the best novelists were also travel writers, especially in the nineteenth century when the modern novel was, arguably, brought to maturity. This proposed project therefore attempts to fill a gap. In a monograph consisting of 5 chapters plus Introduction and Conclusion, the works of novelist-travel writers Charles Dickens, George Eliot, Elizabeth Gaskell, George Gissing, Eliza Lynn Lynton, Robert Louis Stevenson, William Makepeace Thackeray and Fanny Trollope will be analysed in detail. This focus on specific authors and their respective texts will then help draw theoretical conclusion about the genesis of the modern novel as well as illuminate the poetic side of the travel genre.

17600619.label: Realisation of objectives
17600619.value: The project was an attempt to read travelogues and novels from the heyday of the prose genre in comparison, to analyse what narrative strategies the modern novel learned from the older travel genre. Various authors were explored, critical essays published and multiple keynote speeches and conference papers given, to analyse these objectives. While the project underwent some challenges and subsequent changes - intellectual and logistical due to Covid travel restrictions - all objectives were, in the end, met and completed.

17600619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17600619.value: I have worked for several years now on nineteenth-century novelist who were, at the same time, travel writing scholars. The goal is always to see how narrative features (protagonist, setting, plotting...) translate between genres and how, specifically, the modern novel form is indebted to the older travel genre. Turning to the basic tropes and narrative features of the travelogue was therefore a central goal. The major findings are, perhaps, what one might have expected: travelling novelists and novel-writing travellers use comparable strategies in their novels and travelogues for place making, journey telling/ diegesis, the development of the protagonist/ traveller, the 'reality effect' necessary for (fictional) world-making. The origins for these strategies are, arguably, established in the eighteenth century (esp. the picaresque and adventure novel genre and the literary travelogue of esp. Grand Tourists that moves beyond the journal entry of earlier times). It is, however, in the nineteenth century (George Eliot, Charles Dickens, Fanny Trollope, Anthony Trollope, George Gissing, William Makepeace Thackeray et al) that these narrative strategies are perfect and both the novel and the travelogue come to a state of literary completion and climax.

17600619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17600619.value: I have given many papers related to this GRF project - which was also further expanded in an HSSPF - and written multiple critical essays, in peer-reviewed journals and edited collections. The monograph I envisaged has turned into a Cambridge Elements monograph which is due for submission (contracted) for end February 2024. The monograph is different from what I had originally planned - even better, I would think - as the work done in conference and published papers has led to a meta-level analysis of genre and poetics in the contracted Cambridge Elements monograph. Building on and including the 4 articles I published in this GRF project, I may in the future go back to the original idea of a monograph that is author-focused. But, for now, the genre focused shorter CUP Elements book is where I have ended up with this GRF project.

17600619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17600619.value: This project looked at travelling novelists and novel-writing travellers in the nineteenth century when, arguably, both genres achieved new heights in terms of their narrative sophistication. This GRF project was interested in form rather than content - poetics. This poetic focus is a focal area in current studies of the nineteenth-century novel where neoformalist approaches are common. In contrast, form-oriented approaches are hitherto neglected in travel writing studies where the WHAT is still generally prioritized over the HOW. My GRF project thus had an original trajectory in combining, contrasting and comparing forms in the novel and travelogue. The outcomes are both what literary scholars might have expected - i.e. that the novel and the travelogue use similar poetic forms for their world-, place-, story- and hero-making - but also original in so far as such an approach has neither been done individually for the travelogue or comparatively for the novel and travelogue together.

17600719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600719.value: 孩子願意花最多時間進行的日間活動，或許就是遊戲。遊戲不單純是玩樂，更有助孩子的發展，故獲廣泛應用於幼兒教育中。然而，不同類別的玩具會為孩子提供不一樣的學習經歷，而男孩和女孩對玩具類別的喜好亦普遍有明顯分別。一般來說，男孩較喜歡包含空間組合和攻擊元素的玩具（如積木和武器），女孩則較喜歡帶關愛元素的玩具（如洋娃娃）。因此，很多研究人員一直希望了解性別定型的遊戲方式會否造成男孩和女孩在各方面發展的差異，例如空間認知及數理能力、攻擊行為、照顧他人的表現，甚或是個人的性傾向。 可是，過去的研究有幾項限制。一，大多研究局限於討論遊戲對空間認知的影響，只有少數談及遊戲與社交發展的關係。二，儘管同樣適合男孩和女孩的中性玩具或能幫助孩子發展多元技能，有關研究卻相當缺乏。三，現有的文獻大多倚靠「橫斷式」的研究方法，當中使用的量度工具亦未能顯示預期的性別差異。而少數以實驗方法去探討傳統玩具如何影響孩子的研究，也受到不同方面的限制。四，即使部分文獻採用「縱向式」的追蹤研究方法，它們鮮有在起始階段和其後的追蹤過程重複測量結果，故與橫斷式研究相比，它們並未能進一步闡明遊戲和能力發展兩者的關聯。 有見及此，本研究將採用「交叉延宕」的長期追蹤研究方法，去探討性別定型的遊戲行為和形成性別差異之間，會否存在單向或雙向的關係。644位曾在5至6歲參加首次測試的兒童，會獲邀在11至12歲時接受第二次測試。是次測試，我們會運用適合此年齡組別和能針對性別差異的量度工具，再次檢測他們在少年期的遊戲喜好、空間認知、數理能力、攻擊行為、同理心和安慰他人的表現，更會檢測他們的性傾向。除了分析遊戲的類別怎樣影響孩子的發展，我們亦會細查特定玩具對成長的作用。 這項研究所提供的寶貴數據，將能闡釋遊戲對能力發展的長遠影響，以及兩者之間的單向或雙向關係。研究結果亦能為有關遊戲的理論提出佐證，且有助了解男性和女性在空間認知、數理和社交能力等方面的差異是如何發展而成，這些技能對學習表現、人際關係和事業成就都十分重要。專家可根據是次結果，在研究領域、學校和家庭單位推動有關措施，以促進孩子在各方面能力的發展。 關鍵詞：發展心理學、性別差異、性別定型、玩具及遊戲、認知及社交能力、性別行為

17600819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600819.value: In 1842, Hong Kong Island was ceded to Britain under the Treaty of Nanking. British Admiralty law began to be enforced in the Crown Colony under the Vice-Admiralty Courts Act 1863 and the Colonial Courts of Admiralty Act 1890. The Treaty of Nanking also established five treaty ports at Shanghai, Guangzhou, Ningbo, Fuzhou and Xiamen. The British Supreme Court for China was established in Shanghai in 1865. It had the jurisdiction to apply the British Admiralty law and commercial law to resolve a whole range of shipping disputes concerning maritime, insurance and commercial matters. The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in Britain heard appeals from the Hong Kong Supreme Court and the British Supreme Court for China. In this project, we will review a significant number of reported legal cases together with correspondence and private papers found in original legal archives. The applicable British legislation such as the Merchant Shipping Act (1854), Bill of Lading Act (1855), Bill of Exchange Act (1882), Sale of Goods Act (1893) and Marine Insurance Act (1906) will also be examined to see how they filled a legal vacuum caused by the scanty and primitive coverage of these important legal principles in the Great Qing Legal Code (1644-1912). We will trace the establishment and administration of British Admiralty law in Hong Kong and other treaty ports, and test the hypothesis that the application of British Admiralty law contributed significantly to the removal of the risks, barriers and uncertainties encountered by foreign merchants trading with China. We argue that the original founding purpose of Hong Kong and the treaty ports in the 19th century was to reduce international trade risks for the British Empire and its merchants. This project will advance our understanding of the role played by British Admiralty law in shaping the economic development of modern China as free trade began to flourish along with China’s opening up to the outside world. This project will also allow scholars to better comprehend the complex history of the Sino-British economic relations and British colonial justice in general. N/A

17600919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17600919.value: Background: Comorbidity of insomnia and depressive and anxiety disorders is common and associated with worse prognosis and increased health risks. The pathway from insomnia, depressive and anxiety disorders to poor physical health involves physiological systems that fail to efficiently and effectively adapt to internal and external demands and result in “allostatic overload”. Studies have shown that high allostatic load predicts a range of adverse health outcomes, while reduction in allostatic load leads to lowering of all-cause mortality risk. There are opportunities to reduce allostatic load before morbidity occurs, with insomnia, depressive and anxiety disorders as targets for intervention. Cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) is a transdiagnostic, effective, and durable treatment for comorbid insomnia and depressive and anxiety disorders. Aims: To investigate whether (1) CBT-I reduces the severity of insomnia, depressive and anxiety disorders, (2) CBT-I reduces allostatic load, and (3) reduction in insomnia, depressive and anxiety symptoms mediates reduction in allostatic load. Methods: Ninety patients will be recruited from a regional psychiatric clinic and randomly assigned to 4 sessions 90-minute nurse-administered, manual-based small-group CBT-I or sleep hygiene education (active control) over 8 weeks in a 1:1 ratio. Efficacy outcomes will be assessed at baseline, immediate post-treatment, and 6 and 12-month post-baseline; for allostatic load, assessments will be conducted at baseline and 12-month post-baseline. Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) is the primary insomnia outcome. Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) is the primary anxiety and depressive symptom outcome. Allostatic load will be based on 22 biomarkers representing the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, inflammation, cardiovascular system, and glucose and lipids metabolism. Actigraphy and polysomnography will be used as objective assessments. Data analysis: Differences between CBT-I and sleep hygiene education will be assessed using mixed-effects group by time interaction and chi-square test. Changes in ISI and HADS scores from baseline to 6-month post-baseline on allostatic load score at 12-month post-baseline will be tested using simple and multiple mediation analyses with age, gender, marital and economic status, educational level, and baseline level of allostatic load, dietary intake and exercise, physical health, perceived stress, and the exposure to psychotropic medications with weight gain liability as covariates. Significance: This is a study on the clinical and biological effects of CBT-I. Nurse-administered 4-session CBT-I, if proven effective in reducing symptom severity and allostatic load, will be provided as a routine intervention to reduce the morbidity and mortality in patients with comorbid insomnia and depressive and anxiety disorders. 背景：合併性失眠、抑鬱和焦慮症是很常見，而其預後會較差和增加健康風險。失眠、抑鬱和焦慮症會影響生理系統不能有效地適應內在和外在的需求，並加重了身體調適負荷，以致影響身體健康。研究表明，高身體調適負荷可預測一系列不良的健康後果，而減少身體調適負荷則可降低全因死亡風險。以失眠、抑鬱和焦慮症為治療目標，有機會在發病前減少身體調適負荷。而失眠認知行為治療是一種對合併性失眠、抑鬱和焦慮症有效和持久的跨診斷治療。 目的：研究（1）失眠認知行為治療能否降低失眠、抑鬱和焦慮症的嚴重程度， （2） 失眠認知行為治療能否降低身體調適負荷，（3）減少失眠、抑鬱和焦慮症狀能否介導身體調適負荷的減少。 研究方法：將從地區精神科診所招募九十名患者，並以一比一的比例隨機分配到為期八個星期，共四次，每次九十分鐘，由護士帶領的失眠認知行為治療小組或睡眠衛生教育。將在基線、完成治療後以及基線後六個月和十二個月評估療效；而身體調適負荷將只會在基線和基線後十二個月進行評估。失眠嚴重指數 (ISI) 是失眠的主要指標，而醫院焦慮及抑鬱量表(HADS) 是焦慮和抑鬱症狀的主要指標。身體調適負荷將基於二十二個生物標誌物，代表著副交感神經系統、下丘腦─垂體─腎上系統、免疫系統、心血管系統、葡萄糖代謝系統和脂質代謝系統。而腕動計和多項睡眠電圖檢查將作為客觀評估。 資料分析：失眠認知行為治療與睡眠衛生教育的差異將以與時間交互的混合效應組和卡方檢驗進行分折。我們將以多重的中介分折來分折基線和基線後六個月的失眠嚴重指數和醫院焦慮及抑鬱量表分數的變化對基線後十二 個月的身體調適負荷分數的影響，並以年齡、性別、婚姻狀態、經濟狀況、教育水平、基線的身體調適負荷分數、飲食攝入量和運動量、身體健康情況、感知壓力以及接受精神藥物治療後的體重增加作為共變量。 重要性：這是一項關於失眠認知行為治療的臨床和生物學影響的研究。如果證明了共四次由護士帶領的失眠認知行為治療能夠有效地降低症狀的嚴重程度和身體調適負荷，那失眠認知行為治療將可作為常規治療，以降低合併性失眠和抑鬱和焦慮症患者的發病率和死亡率。

17601019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601019.value: With increasing global demand for English and Chinese language education, the existence of language variation (and varieties) has focused scholarly attention on the choice of language standards, norms and models. Over the past four decades, World Englishes (WE) and English as a lingua franca (ELF) research has documented the changing functions and forms of English use in different social contexts, which points to the need to reform contemporary English language education. As non-native speakers (NNSs) are nowadays the majority in English communication worldwide, WE/ELF scholars have argued that the traditional native-speaker (NS) norm (British/American English) should no longer be the sole learning target because it is unattainable, inappropriate and irrelevant in most international settings. Alternatively, it is proposed that local English varieties should be recognised in language education as they are more reflective of the local and global needs. Nevertheless, research has shown that the successful implementation of these proposals highly depends on people’s attitudes towards local versus NS English varieties, which are affected by factors such as the social values of the varieties and one’s cultural identity. With the growing global visibility and extensive usage of Chinese, this proposed study seeks to extend the work of WE/ELF research to the investigation of people’s attitudes towards Chinese varieties. Specifically, it aims to compare key stakeholders’ (i.e. users and learners) attitudes towards various major English (British/American/Hong Kong English) and Putonghua varieties (Beijing/Shanghainese/Hong Kong/Taiwanese Putonghua) and towards adopting them as alternative pedagogical models in Hong Kong. Both English and Putonghua play an important role under Hong Kong’s ‘biliterate, trilingual’ language policy. The participants will involve university students and professionals who are major users (and learners) of both these languages in the academic and professional discourse. The study will adopt a mixed-methods design, which consists of two mutually complementary investigative approaches in language attitude research, namely, direct (questionnaire, interview) and indirect (verbal-guise technique) measures. These research methods will yield both quantitative and qualitative findings for triangulation. By comparing language attitudes in the world’s two big languages, the study will explore the possibility and appropriateness of applying the long-developed WE/ELF theoretical framework to the investigation of the Chinese language and, hence, (re)examine the choice of standards, norms and models, which is a long-standing controversial debate in language education policy. The study will potentially lead to a future research and educational agenda for investigating both the Chinese language and Chinese language education.

17601719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17601719.value: This is a historical project with present relevance. It takes as its primary object of study a corpus of US legal decisions made between 1875 and 1945 concerning race and naturalization law. The Naturalization Law of 1790 made the status of ‘free white person’ a necessary qualification for naturalization as a citizen. The Naturalization Law of 1870 extended this to ‘aliens of African nativity and to persons of African descent’. The closing decades of the nineteenth century saw the rise of scientific racism, that is, theories of human race endowed with the authority of science. Racial thinking began to have an impact on policy, notably the dynamics of global population (understood as a competition between the races), fear of miscegenation, colonial governance and migration policy, and the equation of lower classes with inferior racial stock. In naturalization cases, courts were required to decide whether particular individuals met the criteria of being white or of African descent, and in so doing they had to look for a source of authority. In this context the scientific approach to classification has been termed ‘scientific evidence inquiry’. It is often contrasted with what is termed a ‘common-knowledge test’, that is, a commonsense or plain person’s understanding of race. Both these approaches could find support in the Biblical account of human diversity, in particular the belief that God had created the races as separate. In addition to these two basic approaches, scholars have identified a ‘performative test’, i.e. judicial scrutiny of self-presentation, social comportment and ability to assimilate. There is a rich and extensive academic literature on the interaction between law and race in the United States. The contribution I wish to make is in four interrelated areas. First, I will profile the intellectual context, primarily in terms of race theory, but also contemporary jurisprudential discussions. Second, I will draw parallels with court decisions on transgender identities, where the same sources of authority (common knowledge, scientific evidence, performativity, Biblical authority) can be discerned. Third, I will show that from these naturalization decisions emerged a move towards ordinary language as the decisive framework. The key case is United States v. Bhagat Singh Thind, 261 U.S. 204 (1923), where the ‘plain and ordinary’ meaning rule was applied (see Anon 1958: 578). Fourth, I want to look critically at the notion of the legal construction of race, asking what this actually means in concrete historical and legal terms. 這是一個具有現實相關性的歷史項目。其主要研究對象為美國在1875年至1945年間關於種族和歸化法的語料庫。十九世紀的最後幾十年見證了科學種族主義的興起。種族思維開始對政策產生影響，特別是全球人口的動態（被理解為種族之間的競爭），對異族間的性關係的恐懼，殖民治理和移民政策，以及把低級階級和低等種族畫上對等。在歸化案件中，法院需要決定個人是否符合“白人”或“非洲人後裔”的標準。因此, 他們必須尋找權威來源。在這種情況下，科學的分類方法就被稱為“科學證據查究”。這就和“普遍知識測試”形成鮮明對比，亦即普通人對種族的理解。在該項目中，我將介紹以上議題的知識背景，主要是在種族理論方面，以及當代法學討論。其次，我將與法院關於跨性別身份的判決作對比，其中可以看出相同的權威來源（常識，科學證據，展演性，聖經權威）。第三，我將表明從這些歸化決策出現了朝著普通語言邁進的決定性框架。 關鍵的案例是United States v. Bhagat Singh Thind, (1923)，其中適用了“淺白和普通意義”的規則。第四，我想批判地研究關於種族的法律建構概念，詢問這在具體的歷史和法律術語中實際意味著什麼。

17601719.label: Realisation of objectives
17601719.value: This project involves an in-depth historical study of the so-called "racial eligibility" US federal law cases from the late nineteenth century to the mid-twentieth century. "Racial eligibility" refers to the requirement under US naturalization law, beginning in 1790, that petitioners be "free white persons", a restriction that was later enlarged in 1870 to include person of African descent or nativity. In the course of this project I have assembled a vast database of case reports, briefs, commentaries, scholarly articles, newspaper reports, as well as gathered and analyzed a large quantity of scholarly writings on race from the early 19th to the mid-20th century. In addition I have collected and analyzed what I believe to be almost the entirety of the secondary literature on this topic, including discussions of individual cases by scholars writing in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. I have met the original requirement of producing four articles for this project. These deal with the status of scholarly terminology concerning race and identity within linguistics and law and with a sub-set of the relevant law cases. This was to meet the requirements under Objectives 3 and 4. In parallel with this, I produced a book-length study of terms such as "Aryan" and "Caucasian", since I realised that in order to make an original contribution to the secondary literature on this topic I needed to have a better understanding of the scholarly texts to which the judges were appealing, as they sought external authority for deciding who is or is not a "white person." Some of the opinions and briefs make reference to a very wide range of Us and European theorists, as well as devoting many pages to the history of peoples or races in various parts if the world, beginning in ancient times. My investigation of the scholarly background went into much more detail than originally planned, but I believe this is paying off in the second book. This aspect of the project was to meet the requirements under Objective 1. This book is complete and is in press with Oxford University Press, and is due to go into production shortly, though this has been delayed for reasons beyond my control. A second book is substantially complete, to be entitled "Law and the Language of Race". I underestimated the sheer volume of materials which need to be studied and analyzed for this aspect of the project. I discovered that there were many more cases than the secondary literature suggests but that not all these cases were reported, and in other cases substantial briefs were prepared which have proved very difficult to obtain. It has not been possible for professional and family reasons to travel to the US, and these materials are in any case spread across all the different jurisdictions, including Hawaii. Fortunately some are available online and others have been published, and some insight can be gained from detailed newspaper reports. My tactic has been to write up the cases as far as possible, and put the framework for the book in place. Although some legal materials have proven hard to obtain, there is a wealth of other electronic (corpus) data available, in particular relating to the history of usage of Caucasian and related terms. My argument is that these cases reflect uncertainty in relation to a common language and set of concepts, and I see the legal problems generated by the term "white person" as embedded in a long history of linguistic and conceptual contestation. I also realized that naturalization is dependent conceptually on the notion of citizenship, and citizenship has been extraordinarily ill-defined in US history. The project, which was funded at a very modest level, will in due course have a much more substantial set of outputs that was originally proposed. Four articles are published or in press, one book is in press, and a book draft of over 80,000 words has been completed.

17601719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17601719.value: This project makes a number of interventions in the scholarly literature: (1) It seeks to highlight the fact that that scholarly works on race played an ambivalent role, and in some cases offered a framework which supported claims by petitioner to be "white." Judges drew on a wide array of scholarly sources, often in a genuinely good faith attempt to apply the vague and problematic term. (2) Judges have been the major target of critique, and in some cases they made evidently racist or derogatory remarks - however many actually sought to find ways to offer naturalization to petitioners. Until the Attorney General's office began challenging naturalization decisions judges appear to have been on the whole extremely liberal. (3) The proper target of critique is Congress itself and the Attorney General's office, which perpetuated racist naturalization law, and policies. This law had devastating effects on various groups once it was combined with property and other professional restrictions on individuals ineligible for citizenship (e.g. Chinese and Japanese in California). (4) The secondary literature fails to analyze these cases as examples of statutory interpretation, where a particular term is subject to analysis and where various forms of expertise and knowledge are in play. The cases are treated as morality narratives, ignoring questions of legal interpretation and the interpretative culture of law, and the institutional and professional constraints on judges. (5) The role of ordinary language as a key methodological and theoretical concept has been systematically ignored – in my book in progress I put this concern with ordinary language in the context of US debates about race and racial terminology, and the desire from its inception for the US to develop a common language and a shared set of concepts. (6) The book will offer for the first time a complete survey of the major decisions in this area of law, and in this way enable them to be set in the evolving landscape of US debates about immigration and naturalization.

17601719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17601719.value: To complete the second book arising from this project, I still need to obtain some materials from the US. In going through the dozens of cases, I discovered that often very lengthy briefs were produced, and these go deeply into the scholarly literature as to race within intellectual history. The overall framework of the book is complete, and this final stage would involve filling in a few missing sections. This phase of the project draws on my earlier work on ordinary language in legal reasoning, especially my book The Tyranny of Ordinary Meaning (Palgrave, which concerned a key case in the definition of legal sex. My argument is that legal academics do not take the category of “ordinary language” seriously, treating it as a mere tool of analysis. My view is that in cases where deep ideological or identitarian issues are at stake, ordinary language plays a fundamental and decisive role, while at the same time courts have no agreed procedure to determine ordinary meanings and no theoretical framework within such inquires take place. This argument will be set out in the conclusion.

17601719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17601719.value: This book, and the project of which it is a part, takes an outsider’s view on the debate about the historical nature of US law and society, currently highly polarized between those who see racism as built into the DNA of the US, as fatally marked by the genocide of the indigenous population and slavery, and those who defend it as a society that has built on the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution, including the Bill of Rights, as well as fought a Civil War over slavery, and thereby evolved into a society that offers freedom and opportunity, and attracts migrants from all over the world. The racial eligibility cases reflect this double-sided legacy, since they contain both racist language and opinions on the part of judges, but also judicial creativity in seeking to allow for the naturalization of the individuals before them.

17602219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602219.value: The main objective of the proposed project is to produce the first substantial study on Sinophone literary art through the lens of translanguaging. Why translanguaging and the Sinophone? Because translanguaging highlights the dynamic creativity of language practice, in particular the way it manipulates the ambivalent spaces between languages, between sensory modes, and between media of representation. The Sinophone, on the other hand, represents the articulation of creative forms of literary art based on Chinese language and cultural resources, but inflected with locale-specific sensibilities that negotiate the dynamic between centre and periphery. By using translanguaging as a theoretical perspective to examine different genres of Sinophone literary art, this project endeavours to examine how authors and artists working with Chinese language and cultural resources achieve a “trans” aesthetics in transcending different kinds of borders (linguistic, semiotic, media) and transforming their texts and readers in the co-production of literary-aesthetic meaning, within a transdisciplinary frame that combines perspectives from literary criticism and sociolinguistics. The proposed project focuses on three representative authors/artists who do not operate squarely within the PRC literary-artistic establishment: Taiwanese poet Chen Li, transnational Chinese artist Gu Wenda, and US-based sinologist-translator John Cayley. The aim of this project is to understand how each of these individuals articulates his Sinophone identity in a uniquely transgressive way. We do this by using translanguaging to provide a rigorous structure to an analysis of their representative works, in particular the techniques they use to manipulate Chinese language and cultural resources across borders to creative and critical ends. By triangulating three authors/artists and three genres of literary art, it is believed that this project can make a meaningful theoretical intervention by bringing the concept of translanguaging (borrowed from linguistics) to Sinophone studies, and, conversely, by bringing exemplary data from Sinophone literary art to enrich the concept of translanguaging. Ultimately the project seeks to arrive at a linguistic-semiotic understanding of what it means to be Sinophone beyond its cultural and identity politics. 此項研究將首次從超語行為（translanguaging）的視角對華語語系文藝（Sinophone literary art）進行深入的實例探究。選題的理由一方面是因為超語行為突出語言實踐的動態創新，對不同語言、感官和再現媒介間的游移地帶有著獨特的操縱方式，另一方面則由於華語語系所囊括的各種創新文藝形式雖然皆植根于漢語言及其文化資源，但不同華語語境在調和中心—邊緣關係的過程中融入了多樣的在地特色。 本研究將超語行為的概念作為理論視角來審視華語語系文藝的不同體裁，並在文學批評和社會語言學共同構建的跨學科分析框架內，考察不同作者和藝術家如何基於漢語言及其文化資源，跨越語言、符號、媒介等不同邊界，在與讀者共同創造文學和美學意義的過程中重塑文本與讀者，從而形成一種獨特的“越界”美學。 本文聚焦台灣詩人陳黎、跨國藝術家谷文達、以及美國漢學家兼譯者約翰•卡雷（John Cayley）等三位極具代表性的、在中國大陸以外地區進行創作的作家/藝術家，討論他們如何以各自獨樹一幟且顛覆傳統的方式來彰顯自己華語語系創作者的身份。本文運用超語行為的理論框架分析三人的代表作，著重探討他們採用了哪些手法跨界操縱漢語語言及其文化資源，藉此來實現作品的獨創性與批判性。 通過分別考察分析三位作者/藝術家及其代表的三類文藝類型，本研究將超語行為這一語言學概念引入華語語系研究，可以為後者提供一個重要的理論切入視角，反過來，引入華語語系文藝創作中的生動樣例也能豐富超語行為的概念內涵。本研究的最終目標是力圖在文化政治與身份認同政治的維度之外，從語言符號學的角度來闡釋何為華語語系。

17602219.label: Realisation of objectives
17602219.value: Through this project I have studied and analysed in detail the work of Chen Li (poetry), Gu Wenda (text-based multimedia installation) and John Cayley (digital literary art). Through the lens of translanguaging, I have been able to capture the multilingual and multimodal dimensions of their work, more specifically: Chen Li's use of concrete poetry as a means to deconstruct the organicity of the Chinese character (Objective 1); Gu Wenda's unique blending of translation/transliteration in his artwork as a critique of an essentialist notion of Chineseness (Objective 2); and John Cayley's use of transliteral morphing as a means of complicating classical Chinese poetry, both interlingually and intersemiotically (Objective 3). Together, the three case studies dovetail into an enhanced understanding of Sinophone cultural productions from a semiotic perspective (Objective 4). I have been unable to participate in the Taipei Poetry Festival in person due to travel restrictions under the pandemic during the research period. However, this has been compensated by the material made available on the organiser's website, among other sources, such that I have been able to keep up to pace with new developments in the experimental literary arts (Objective 5). Part of the findings of this project have been published in the book Translation as Experimentalism, published by Cambridge University Press (Objective 6).

17602219.label: Major findings and research outcome
17602219.value: First, on the level of theory this project has made inroads in respect of the notion of translanguaging. In collaboration with internationally renowned linguist Li Wei (one of the pioneers of translanguaging as a sociolinguistic concept), translanguaging is discussed in relation to evidence from the Sinophone world (see “Translanguaging and Creativity with English in the Sinophone world”). Second, this project has found a theoretical connection between translanguaging (from sociolinguistics) and the idea of “distribution” (from cognitive linguistics). As reported in the paper “Distribution and Translation”, “distributed thinking” helps us understand translation (or rewriting in general) as partaking of an assemblage—a creative network of production within which a text operates as a node—alongside human and non-human agents. This understanding is further applied to a study of experimental Sinophone literary art in the paper “Memesis in contemporary Chinese poetics”. In the latter paper, Chen Li’s poems are understood not as discrete texts; rather, each poem is conceptualised as one component of a proliferation of multiple and multimodal rewritings or remediations. Third, all the above strands are drawn together in the paper “Spectacles of the Sinograph in Chinese Literature and Art”, which espouses the Sinograph (the written Chinese character) as a method in Sinophone literary art. The idea of translanguaging is involved here as the method in question involves the transcending and transgressing of the standard Chinese character to produce identity effects pointing to Sinophone sensibilities. It is found that the Chinese character is often “trans-scripted” to create playful visual-verbal formations, speaking to a poetics of translanguaging in Sinophone cultural production. Finally, the new understanding of experimental poetics emerging from this project culminates in a book titled Translation as Experimentalism. The book investigates how avant-grade authors and artists in the like of Chen Li, Gu Wenda, and John Cayley practice translanguaging (entailing translation) by engaging with literature using a full range of resources, both linguistic and nonlinguistic, in their repertoire.

17602219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17602219.value: First, the project can be extended by way of case studies on other authors and artists in the Sinophone world who design their work around the Chinese script, for example, in the dance theatre of Lin Hwai-min and the fiction of Wang Wen-hsing. Second, future developments can include discursive-performative domains beyond the literary arts, for instance, in Sinophone religious settings, where writing-as-doodling is central to the operation of rituals or in the context of social media writing, where netizens distort Chinese characters with intercultural elements to produce ludic effects. Third, the Chinese script can be contextualised in specific sociopolitical settings, particularly in postcolonial cities, with a view to investigating the interaction between representations of writing in Chinese and non-Chinese languages.

17602219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17602219.value: This project studies Sinophone literary art using a concept called “translanguaging”. Translanguaging highlights the dynamic creativity of language practice, in particular the way ambivalent spaces between languages, between sensory modes, and between media of representation are manipulated to creative and critical effects. The Sinophone, on the other hand, is represented by literary art based on Chinese language and cultural resources, but inflected with locale-specific sensibilities. By using translanguaging as a theoretical perspective to examine different genres of Sinophone literary art, this project examines how authors and artists working with Chinese language and cultural resources achieve a “trans” aesthetics in transcending different kinds of borders (linguistic, semiotic, media) and transforming texts and their readers in the co-production of literary-aesthetic meaning. The project analyses three representative authors/artists: the Taiwanese poet Chen Li, transnational Chinese artist Gu Wenda, and US-based sinologist-translator John Cayley. It makes a case for how these individuals articulates their Sinophone identities in novel and transgressive ways. By triangulating three authors/artists and three genres of literary art, this project makes a theoretical intervention by bringing the concept of translanguaging to Sinophone studies, and, conversely, by bringing data from Sinophone literary art to enrich the concept of translanguaging.

17602519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17602519.value: Global recognition of the importance of the early childhood period for human and societal development is reflected in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) Target 4.2 (by 2030, all girls and boys have access to quality early childhood development, care and pre-primary education so that they are ready for primary education). High quality data are needed to monitor progress towards all SDG Targets. However, the Inter-Agency and Expert Group on SDG indicators has deemed internationally established methodology and standards are not yet available for SDG Target 4.2.1 (percentage of children under age 5 years who are developmentally on track in health, learning and psychosocial well-being). Against this background, the project will develop and validate tools to monitor countries’ progress toward Target 4.2.1 One challenge in assessing whether young children are developmentally on track is a dearth of measures that are appropriate for application across and within countries. Currently, UNICEF is refining a parent-report measure to support assessment of Target 4.2.1 but direct assessment by trained researchers is considered the “gold standard”. This project complements but moves beyond UNICEF’s efforts by validating adult-report measures with direct child assessment. To our knowledge, this is the first study to compare concordance among teacher report, parent report and direct assessment of young children’s developmental status. In Wave 1, 1,200 children, aged from three to five years from urban and rural areas in China and India, will be individually assessed. Their parents will be surveyed on items that correspond to the child assessment. Findings will inform the development of a teacher survey. In Wave 2, conducted 12 months later, 800 children and parents from Wave 1 will be re-assessed on the measures completed in Wave 1. In addition, the children’s teachers will be asked to complete a survey. A direct child assessment and parent report measure for 2-year-olds will be developed based on the findings. In Wave 3, 100 2-year-olds from urban and rural areas in China and India and their parents will be surveyed. This project fills a lacuna in the child development literature; supports efforts to develop internationally comparable measures of young children’s developmental status; will help determine the most efficient way to measure progress against Target 4.2.1; contributes to developmental science by permitting an understanding of diversity in early development across contexts given its focus on non-Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) countries; and may inform public policy. 幼兒階段對於個人和社會發展的重要性得到了全球的認同。這認同亦反映在聯合國可持續發展目標（SDG）目標4.2中（到2030年，不論男女，所有兒童均可以獲得優質的幼兒發展、照顧和學前教育，為小學教育作好準備）。高質素的數據有助監測可持續發展目標的進展。然而，參與可持續發展目標的指標機構及專家小組均認為，目前尚未取得能夠衡量可持續發展目標4.2.1（5歲以下兒童在健康、學習和社會心理健康方面正常發展的百分比）進展國際公認的方法和標準。因此，此項目將發展和驗證相關工具，從而監測各國在實踐目標4.2.1的進展。 評估幼兒發展是否正常的其中一個挑戰，就是現行缺乏適用於不同國家以及國家內部不同地區的測量工具。目前，聯合國兒童基金會正致力優化家長評價量表，用以評估目標4.2.1的進展。但是，由經訓練的研究人員對兒童進行直接評估的方法仍被視為評估兒童發展的“黃金標準”。本研究將在聯合國兒童基金會的家長評價量表的基礎上，透過同時對兒童進行直接評估，進一步完善及驗證成人評價量表。據我們所知，這是首次利用教師報告、家長評價及對兒童發展狀況作直接評估的一致性進行比較。 在研究的第一階段，我們將對1,200名來自中國和印度城市及農村地區的3至5歲兒童進行個別評估，而他們的父母將完成一份與兒童評估項目相對應的調查問卷。調查結果將用於發展教師問卷。第二階段將會在十二個月後進行，800名一階段的兒童和其父母將再次參與和第一階段相同的評估。此外任教該批兒童的教師也將完成問卷。根據調查結果，我們會發展一套適用於2歲兒童的直接評估工具和家長評價量表。在第三階段，100名來自中國和印度城市及農村地區的2歲兒童及其父母將會分別參與評估和填寫問卷。 此項目將彌補幼兒發展文獻的不足。項目不僅能夠進一步發展適用於比較不同國家兒童發展狀況的工具，並有助找出評核目標4.2.1進展最有效的方式。此外基於本研究對非西方、受教育、工業化、富有、民主WEIRD；Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic）國家的關注，研究結果將有助進一步了解兒童發展科學的多樣性，為政策制定提供依據。

17603119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603119.value: Over 70% of the population of Mongolia’s capital city live in the Ger Districts – settlements made of traditional felt tents and single story houses. The majority of this population do not have centrally supplied water, heating or sewers (Galimbyek, 2015). The very cold winters reaching temperatures of -40° C mean that inhabitants resort to the cheapest available fuel source –unrefined coal– as their main heating source, contributing to 80% of the city’s air pollution (World Bank, 2010). As a result, UNICEF Mongolia has reported that this has led to “300,000 registered cases of respiratory tract related diseases, 50% of them children under five”, (UNICEF Mongolia, 2017). Despite attempts to implement large scale planning strategies, for example: the Asian Development Bank has provided a loan to the Mongolian government for the Ger Areas Development Investment Program (GADIP), it has faced difficulties in procurement and construction has not yet been initiated, (Asia Development Bank, 2017). Also, even if this plan is successfully implemented, many ger district inhabitants will not be affected by this proposal. We estimate that this amounts to over 245,000 people that will be still without basic infrastructure and continue to contribute to poor air quality. Around 35,000 people move to Ulaanbaatar each year (National Statistics Office, 2016). The World Bank reported that 87% of new expansion from 2000 to 2013 occurred in the Ger districts (World Bank, 2017). As this number continues to grow as people migrate to the city, it is urgent that a viable strategy for densification in these fringe districts is implemented that addresses short, medium and long term objectives (Bolchover, Monu, 2017). This is our target: to demonstrate how ger districts can be incrementally developed holistically by the residents to include infrastructure, better housing, community facilities and an alternative energy provision to coal to improve air quality. The intention is to produce a manual complete with design options, environmental systems, construction costs and financial plans showing necessary investment and projected returns. Within this manual, residents will be offered a series of choices depending if they want to develop alone or with their neighbours. The outcome of the research can provide high impact to multiple residents and radically shift the policy for ger district redevelopment of the government and funding agencies, such as the Asian Development Bank. This provides a new approach and useful contribution to the current discourse on upgrading strategies of informal settlements. 在蒙古首都，70%以上人口住在蒙古包區 – 由傳統毛氈帳篷和單層房屋組成。大多數人沒有自來水，供暖和排污設備（Galimbyek，2015）。冬季時，氣溫低至零下40°C，非常寒冷，居民使用最便宜，卻未經提煉的煤炭作為主要熱源，導致城市空氣污染80%（世界銀行，2010）。根據聯合國兒童基金會蒙古報告指出，污染引致30萬個和呼吸道相關的病例，其中50％為5歲以下兒童，（兒童基金會蒙古，2017年）。儘管有關方面試圖推動大的戰略規劃，例如亞洲開發銀行向蒙古政府提供貸款，用於蒙古包地區發展投資計劃（GADIP），但在採購方面遇到了困難，令建設未能啟動（ 亞洲開發銀行，2017年） 。即使計劃成功推行，許多蒙古包區居民也不會受惠。我們估計仍有超過245,000人沒有基礎設施，空氣污染依舊。 每年約有35,000人遷往烏蘭巴托（國家統計局，2016年），據世界銀行報告稱，從2000年到2013年87％的遷移人口都在蒙古包區（世界銀行，2017年）。隨著遷移到城市的人數增加，在這些邊緣地區進行既細緻又可行的發展戰略，實現短、中、長期目標都顯得十分迫切（Bolchover，Monu，2017）。我們的目標是把蒙古包區，全面發展成有基礎設施，有較佳的住房和社區設施，而且有取代煤炭的能源供應，以改善空氣質量。我們會提供手冊，包括設計選擇、環境系統、建築成本和財務計劃，還有相關投資和預計回報等。在手冊中，居民還可以選擇他們是單獨發展，抑或和鄰居共同發展。 研究結果將對許多居民有巨大影響，並且會根本上改變政府和資助機構（如亞洲開發銀行）對蒙古地區的重建政策。 這亦對目前為這些非正式房屋的改革策略，提供新的發展方向和具體貢獻。

17603119.label: Realisation of objectives
17603119.value: Objective 1 Between January 2020-January 2021, a baseline study of comparable data for twelve households in three different clusters was conducted to record: internal and external temperatures with HOBO MX1101 data loggers every two hours; monthly water consumption, electrical costs, medical costs, and coal use of each household. The sample households were identified through surveys with 38 potential families conducted to understand existing site conditions, demographics, and willingness to participate in the project. A scoring system was then used to evaluate the households and select 12 households, living in three clusters of different spatial typologies, for the baseline. Larger sets of studies were also conducted in 2020 involving interviews with 59 randomly sampled residents to establish the financial potential of ger district residents, their preference to move to a city apartment or to remain in the ger districts, and their willingness to borrow. A further 178 households were surveyed on specific housing improvement plans to deduce market demand. Key findings are presented in the paper “Manual for Mongolia: District upgrading along the fringes of Ulaanbaatar” (Topos) and conference “Incremental Development Manual: The Ger Innovation Hub, Mongolia” (ACSA). Objective 2 The scope and specifications were established through research at different scales with different stakeholders. 12 selected households were surveyed using drone imaging and LiDAR scanning to analyse spatial transformation over time, and to establish plot sizes, topography, and areas available for development. In-depth interviews investigated family structure, relationships with neighboring plots, employment, financial capacity, and future construction. As a result, specific housing typologies were designed to meet their needs. The criteria for environmental performance was established based on the requirement to provide 20% improvement on energy efficiency compared to Mongolian national standards in order to qualify for low-interest rate green loans. At a 4-plot scale, density scenarios were developed using existing government and Asian Development Bank target densities. In collaboration with environmental consultant, Dr Shelley W.W. Zhou, a feasibility study identified systems and optimal sizes for septic tanks, water tanks, heating systems, and renewables which were incorporated into the design strategy. The growth of Songino Khairkhan-43 was identified by comparing Google Earth historical images with current drone images. Using the baseline research, three strategies were developed, one for each research cluster. A resident workshop in November 2021 presented the housing typologies, and the idea of sharing infrastructure. The district governor and community leaders were consulted in February 2022. Cluster-specific workshops were then conducted in March 2022 at the governors office, and in July/August 2022 at their plots to present the development scenarios and obtain feedback. The determined scope and specifications for the scale of upgrading, density, and housing typologies, was published in the paper “Manual for Mongolia: District upgrading along the fringes of Ulaanbaatar” (Topos), whilst paper “The Ger Plug-In Housing Prototype: Demonstrating a Sustainable and Affordable Dwelling Model for Ulaanbaatar’s Fringe Districts” (ARQ) presented with environmental and infrastructural specifications. Objective 3 Over 270 households were surveyed to establish the financial potential of ger district residents, their preference to move to city or stay in ger districts and their willingness to borrow. Meetings were conducted with financial institutions to identify green mortgage terms, new initiatives, and discuss alternative financing models. Five meetings were held with XacBank EcoBanking Department (leader in ecobanking in Mongolia, and a Green Climate Fund Accredited Entity) in January 2020, July 2020, January 2021, and March 2021. Two meetings were held in February 2021, and July 2022 with each of the following NGOs: The Global Green Growth Institute (who works closely with the government to support their National Green Development Policy, NDC, and Long-term policy, which includes developing alternative financial proposals for projects), Geres (who have established a retrofitting project tied to green loans), and The Asia Foundation (who are funding a pilot project for renewable energy and carbon crediting). Critical meetings to understand the viability of our model were organized in September 2020, May 2021, and July 2022 with the Mongolian Sustainable Finance Association (ToC), an organization that collaborates with 15 banks operating in Mongolia to create a green financing system, and Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), a federally owned development agency that performs energy audits for housing products to qualify for Energy Efficient Mortgages. A local contractor completed cost estimations and construction optimization to meet the target 45% debt-to-income ratio of monthly payments. Two local factories, one specializing in prefabricated concrete panels and another in metal frame and insulated metal panel construction, were engaged between December 2020 to September 2021 to evaluate material alternatives based on production capacity and cost. An engineer from GIZ was engaged to independently audit the housing typologies to prove that they meet the 20% energy use reduction criteria required to qualify in the Energy Efficient schemes. After conducting desktop research community led development approaches, including understanding operations relating to land and financing (e.g. Community Land Trusts, Housing Cooperatives, and Building Societies), the Mongolian National Co-operative Association (Vice Chairman, Director of Mongolian Cooperative Training and Information Centre) was engaged in August 2022. The meeting covered what the cooperative framework in Mongolia is, what they attempted before and why it did not work. The financial and business model for how ger district communities can upgrade their neighborhoods themselves using a system of cooperative management as a result of these findings are presented and discussed in the journal paper “Incremental Development Manual: Toward a Cooperative Model of Housing in Ulaanbaatar (Mongolia)” (The Plan Journal TPJ vol. 7 [2022], no. 2). Objective 4 The results from Objectives 1,2, and 3 led to the creation of an Incremental Development Manual containing an in-situ upgrading strategy for 4-plots. The Manual has been published in “Becoming Urban: The Mongolian City of Nomads” and online (link provided). 100 executive summary copies were printed and distributed to local residents via two district offices. To demonstrate how the strategy is a new contribution to current discourse, existing approaches and development mechanisms were studied. As an in-situ and incremental approach it presents an alternative pathway to current practices. The strategy was discussed at meetings in March 2023 with key stakeholders involved in ger district redevelopment. These included: the financial sector (Mongolian Sustainable Finance Association; Xacbank; Khan Bank and Golomt Bank); government policy makers (Director General of the Climate Change Department of the Ministry of Environment and Tourism, Head of Green Housing of the Policy Planning Department of the Ministry of Construction and Urban Development, Head of the Housing Policy Agency of the Municipality of Ulaanbaatar, GCF National Focal Point in Mongolia; and development agencies such as the Head of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development in Mongolia. The position of the proposed strategy against the current discourse and conclusions related to this objective are discussed in the journal paper “Incremental Development Manual: Toward a Cooperative Model of Housing in Ulaanbaatar (Mongolia)” (The Plan Journal). The chapters “Becoming Urban, (pp7-23), Incremental Urban Strategy (pp 127-140), and Incremental Development Manual (pp 140-172) in Becoming Urban: The Mongolian City of Nomads” specifically addresses the outcomes of the GRF project.

17603119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603119.value: The research evidences that of the 233,000 households living in the districts, 78.2% or 182,206 plan to build a house, and out of those, 43.8% or 79,806 are within the income bracket to afford to do so within the next five years. The majority of ger district residents wish to improve their housing whilst remaining on their land and confidence in the successful implementation of current development models is low. This demonstrates the need for an alternative development strategy for the ger districts, (The Plan Journal TPJ vol. 7,2022, no. 2). Detailed site surveying; analysis of resident needs and financial capacities; and feasibility studies from environmental specialists established the scope and specifications of upgrading and densification scenarios. The outcome is an Incremental Development Manual containing in-situ redevelopment strategies for 4-plots; energy efficient housing components; and indicative costs and mortgage payments for residents. The approach to the upgrading of informal settlements, in-situ and incrementally, presents an innovative contribution to the discourse. This outcome is disseminated in the sole-authored published book “Becoming Urban: The Mongolian City of Nomads (2023)”. The development of the Ger-Plug In prototype is a new approach that is culturally specific in how it integrates the ger into an affordable and sustainable housing type. Our surveys indicate that 83.3% of residents planning to build a house are interested in purchasing a Ger Plug-In, equaling a potential impact to provide 66,479 households with affordable, energy efficient housing with access to infrastructure. The findings are published in “The Ger Plug-In Housing Prototype: Demonstrating a Sustainable and Affordable Dwelling Model for Ulaanbaatar’s Fringe Districts” (ARQ). The long-term goal is to have the strategy accepted by residents, government, and development agencies in order to initiate implementation. The outcome of this research project demonstrates that the Incremental Development Manual is a viable alternative to current practices. However, the economic slide and increased inflation caused by COVID-19 financially impacted ger-district residents in 2021, with monthly incomes dropping by 4% while costs for construction materials rose by 52%–92%. The setting up of Mongolian based implementation company, Energy Efficient Design Build is a key step to assist in lowering costs and to realize the outcomes of this research project at scale. (The Plan Journal TPJ vol. 7,2022, no. 2, “Becoming Urban: The Mongolian City of Nomads”, 2023).

17603119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603119.value: In order to deliver scalable impact, further development in the following areas needs to occur. Firstly: the project has to become more affordable to residents. This can be done by researching efficiencies in the construction process; looking for alternative financial investment mechanisms; or, by convincing development agencies and government to pay and be responsible for the infrastructure. Next steps include helping to set up a local implementation agency in Mongolia, Energy Efficient Design and Build (EEDB), to assist in scaling the construction process to make it more economical. Additionally, discussions have started with climate tech start-up, Ureca, about using carbon credits to collateralize against bank loans, reducing the total loan amount and therefore monthly payments, whilst providing an additional income stream for residents. Further discussions with development agencies (EDRD, ADB) and government departments to switch the cost responsibility of infrastructure to these agencies is also ongoing. Furthermore, a critical next step is to realize a demonstration pilot project to evidence proof of concept to residents and stakeholders, alongside evaluating its thermal performance during the winter. This would help prepare for scaling-up and we have garnered the support of the UN Environment Programme Copenhagen Climate Center to provide technical assistance.

17603119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603119.value: There are 840,000 people living in the ger districts of Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. 70% of these households live in just a ger and use an average 4.1 tonnes of coal to heat their homes each winter. The resulting toxic air makes Ulaanbaatar the most polluted capital in the world. There is no sewage infrastructure in the ger districts, and 95% of residents use pit latrines. The research outcome is an alternative model for sustainable in-situ upgrading that demonstrates a collaborative approach for neighbouring families to provide decentralized infrastructure and energy efficient housing, with improved thermal performance, reduced carbon emissions, and with built in sanitation. The solution is unique as it integrates the traditional ger with contemporary house construction and allows people to improve their living condition without leaving the land that they own. The Manual guides residents in attaining energy efficient housing solutions that best suit their needs; and how they can upgrade their plots with infrastructure. In summary: the aim is to influence how ger districts can be upgraded in-situ, affordably, and sustainably, so that air quality will improve, residents will have access to sanitation, and the health and well-being of communities will be ameliorated.

17603319.label: Project Objectives
17603319.value: To identify the typologies of money laundering and the motivations of offenders in money laundering cases prosecuted in the District Court and Magistrates Court of Hong Kong from 2009 to 2019. To assess whether there should be any reform of the criminal offence of money laundering, particularly whether its scope should be narrowed, having regard to the types of cases and defendants currently caught by the offence. To assess the merits of introducing non-criminal law alternative measures (e.g. civil penalties, injunctions, disqualifications, confiscation) to address money laundering, particularly whether such measures would be compatible with Hong Kong's international anti-money laundering commitments. To publish at least two articles in refereed international journals on the empirical findings of money laundering offending and on proposals for possible law reform of the money laundering offence including the introduction of alternative measures.

17603319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603319.value: I aim to study money laundering offending in Hong Kong, its causes, typologies and implications for law reform. I am interested in why and how money laundering is done in Hong Kong and how our criminal law captures offenders within its net. My main question is whether there should be alternative legal measures not involving criminal prosecution and punishment to address money laundering in non-high profile cases. Would such alternative measures be sufficiently effective to be compatible with Hong Kong's international commitments and would they be acceptable to the local community? Prosecutors can bring money laundering cases in one of three levels of court: (1) High Court, where the maximum sentence is 14 years imprisonment, (2) District Court, maximum of 7 years imprisonment, and (3) Magistrates Court, maximum of 3 years imprisonment. I will study cases prosecuted in the District Court and, where judgments are available, the Magistrates Court. There are approximately 600 District Court money laundering decisions (English and Chinese) in the Hong Kong Judiciary's database available since 2009. The decisions are of two kinds: reasons for sentence, typically where there has been a guilty plea, and reasons for verdict (guilty and not guilty). I will read and analyse these decisions both qualitatively and quantitatively. I aim to generate a body of knowledge of the characteristics of offenders who commit money laundering, the ways in which they commit the offence (typologies), their motivations and reasons for offending, the sentences imposed, the cases in which the prosecution could only prove the lower standard of having reasonable grounds to believe, and the circumstances giving rise to acquittals. From these empirical findings, I will publish at least one referred output in an international journal. I also plan to use the empirical findings to inform law reform thinking, particularly the feasibility of introducing non-criminal law measures to address money laundering. The offence is often criticised for casting the net of criminal liability too wide. From interviews with experienced defence lawyers, prosecutors, law enforcement agents and other government officials, I hope to gain their perspectives on possible alternative measures such as civil penalties, injunctions, disqualifications, confiscation and other coercive orders. The knowledge gained from these interviews will help to frame and assess reform options. I will publish at least one referred output in an international journal that discusses reform options and their compatibility with international standards. 筆者希望探討在香港洗錢罪案的現況、起因、類型，以及後續可能的法律改革。筆者對於洗錢罪案為何和如何在香港發生，以及我們的刑事司法系統如何將罪犯繩之於法的問題特別感興趣。筆者的主要問題在於為何應以替代性的且不牽涉刑事檢控和刑罰的法律措施去處理一些較為不受關注的案件。這些替代性的措施是否足夠配合香港的國際責任？這些措施是否被本地社區所接納？檢控官可以在以下三個級別的法院就洗錢案件提訴：（1）高等法院，其可判處最高刑罰為監禁十四年；（2）區域法院，其可判處最高刑罰為監禁七年；（3）裁判法院，其可判處最高刑罰為監禁三年。筆者研究了在區域法院和有判決可供參考的裁判法院的洗錢案件。現時，香港司法機構的資料庫收載了從二零零九年起計的大約六百宗區域法院的中英判決。這些判決可分為兩個類型：判刑理由（通常於被告認罪時發下），和裁決理由（罪成與否）。筆者將研讀，並從質性和量性角度分析這些判決。筆者希望能歸納出一包含以下資訊之知識體系：犯下洗錢罪行之涉事者的特質、犯案的形式（類型）、犯案動機和理由、被判處刑罰、控方只能證明被告有理由相信的較低舉證程度的情況，以及引致被告脫罪的因素。就這些實證研究結果，筆者將於設同儕審查的國際學術期刊發表最少一份論文。筆者亦希望以這些研究結果推動尤其是關於以非刑事措施處理洗錢的可行性方面之法律改革。洗錢罪行素來被指刑網過闊，透過訪問有經驗的辯護律師、檢控官、執法人員和其他政府官員，筆者希望就可能的替代性措施，例如民事懲罰、禁制令、資格取消、沒收、和其他強制命令等，取得他們的觀點。從訪談中歸納出的資料將有助塑造及評估法律改革方案。筆者將於設同儕審查的國際學術期刊發表最少一份探討法律改革方案及其與國際水平相容性的論文。

17603619.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17603619.value: 融合工程設計流程於小學科學教育中：以設計式研究探究學生的建構主義式學習

17603619.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17603619.value: Dr Churchill, Daniel Prof Cope, William Prof Tisdell, Christopher

17603619.label: Project Objectives
17603619.value: Investigate the feasibility of a constructionist approach using CAPE in the learning of STEM-related subjects in primary schools, and explore how such an approach can be co-designed by the researchers and the teachers; Explore how the constructionist approach using CAPE can motivate primary school students to learn the techniques of real-world problem-solving; Develop a longitudinal trajectory with empirical foundation for the theoretical, curricular and pedagogical development of integrated STEM education that will contribute to integrative learning knowledge.
rows: Investigate the feasibility of a constructionist approach using CAPE in the learning of STEM-related subjects in primary schools, and explore how such an approach can be co-designed by the researchers and the teachers;
Explore how the constructionist approach using CAPE can motivate primary school students to learn the techniques of real-world problem-solving;

Develop a longitudinal trajectory with empirical foundation for the theoretical, curricular and pedagogical development of integrated STEM education that will contribute to integrative learning knowledge.

17603619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17603619.value: 在香港的小學教育，STEM（科學，科技，工程，數學）已經在常·識課程及數學課程中得到實踐。與其他全國性課程相似，這些課程較為重視科學、科技以及數學部分，而對於實施小學階段的工程教育和研究卻缺少關注。此次研究目標是為了探究如何通過應用工程設計流程（Engineering Design Process, EDP），將STEM教育介紹給小學生。 由於其跨學科特性帶來的教學和學習設計上的複雜性，小學科學教育中專注整合工程教育的教學方法鮮少被研究。為了達到我們的目標，我們設計並試用了名為建構主義方法下的工程設計流程教學設計（Constructionist Approach to Pedagogical Design with EDP, CAPE）的教學框架。這個方法基於建構主義學習及設計思維，通過協作式問題解決能力整合了工程設計流程與STEM知識。兒童們運用工程設計流程建造可觸摸的作品，學會將學科知識與解決現實生活問題結合，這是CAPE理論框架所構思的目標。這個綜合性方法，在藉助數學和電腦技術的輔助下，將科學概念和實踐帶入到工程設計流程中，這將提高學生的問題解決能力，設計思維能力和學習動力。 縱向的、基於設計式研究方法將會被實施在香港一所經過任意分層抽樣所得的男女混合小學中。本次研究將跟進約130個學生（起始年齡範圍9-10歲）在第二關鍵階段的學習（即：從四年級起始的三年），來逐年瞭解他們在科學和工程方面的學習成果和動機方面的改變。每學年將會有四位老師經校方安排參與項目，他們將使用CAPE模型，與研究員合作設計每一年的工程設計流程學習活動和教學方法。活動基於某一個話題，由各個年級的所有老師實施。透過基於設計的研究方法中「設計-實施-分析-再設計」的步驟，老師們將和研究員們一起學習如何設計含有工程設計流程的課程，來優化學生對科學和工程學科的學習。 每一年，質性的和量化的數據皆會被收集、分析，以及結合研究發現進行三角分析，從而改進下一年的學習設計。項目成果將會啟發整合的STEM教育如何能夠通過構建主義流程被啟動、設計、和實施。研究發現將有助於理解兒童通過整合式學習的認知發展。

17603619.label: Realisation of objectives
17603619.value: The three-year longitudinal, design-based approach was implemented in one co-educational primary school in Hong Kong by convenience stratified sampling method to warrant the students’ learning ability for new approaches. The General Studies for Primary Schools Curriculum Guide published by the Education Bureau was used for reference and the focus area will be “Strand 3: Science and Technology in Everyday Life” in Key Stage 2 (equivalent to P4–P6). The detailed learning and instruction design for each topic in this strand was a part of the design-based research. The student cohort: A total of 138 students participated in the programme in the 2020 school year (P4), and 45 students transferred to other schools in the 2021 school year (P5). 82 students were still in the programme in the 2022 school year (P6). Students were divided into different teaching approaches (collaborative and individual learning). 1. Investigate the feasibility of a constructionist approach using CAPE in the learning of STEM-related subjects in primary schools, and explore how such an approach can be co-designed by the researchers and the teachers During the project, the CAPE iterative cycle was implemented throughout each academic year. In the first phase (the 2020 school year), Design, the students in P4 were targeted. Their teachers (practitioners) in the General Studies (GS) subject met with the research design team, comprising experts in the multi fields(e.g., primary education, educational technology, natural science). The team members met with the teachers in the school regularly before, during, and after the intervention, with each outcome-based meeting to lead the teachers in group discussion of the lesson plans (learning objectives, intended learning contents, learning outcomes, pedagogical designs) and to impart related science and engineering knowledge to enrich their knowledge base. Prior to the start of each academic year, one to two topic(s) were selected for the intervention. The team provided suggestions on how to design a series of EDP activities around the selected topics. Upon agreement between the teachers and the team, the teachers then developed the details of the activities and teaching aids, including student worksheets for student note-taking and learning progress-reporting. The team continued to communicate with and support the teachers via an instant messaging group for the school until the design of the intervention lesson plan and activities was complete. To implement the learning design, the teachers first taught the relevant science knowledge based on the regular lesson plans. The pre-test and motivation questionnaire were administered to assess the students' science knowledge base and science learning motivation before they begin the engineering design activities. Then, students went through the EDP stages in multiple lessons and constructed an artifact as a part of the major implementation (Enactment). After the intervention, the data (i.e., motivation questionnaire, post-test) were collected for analysis of the effectiveness of the learning and instructional design in terms of the learning outcomes achieved (Analysis). By the end of the academic year, the team hosted an interim discussion to review the results of the analysis and to further carry out the P5 lesson plan in the second year, targeting the remaining students of the same cohort (Redesign).This one-year cycle was repeated in the second and the third year of the project as the same cohort of remaining students progressing to P5 and P6. By utilizing the CAPE framework, the learning and instructional design packages were developed based on school-based experiments, drawing from three years of experience grounded in theory-driven design, relevant research, theory, and practice. As one of the deliverables, these packages demonstrate the feasibility of the approach, which was co-designed by researchers and in-service teachers. 2. Explore how the constructionist approach using CAPE can motivate primary school students to learn the techniques of real-world problem-solving As the CAPE framework unfolded, three projects were carried out based on the joint contribution from both the research team and the school teachers. These projects were "Water Filter" for P4, "Rubber Band Powered Car" for P5, and "Comfortable Slippers for the Elder" for P6. The topics were familiar to upper primary school students, allowing them to apply their knowledge in practice. Each topic was introduced to the students at the beginning of each intervention, along with an engineering problem to be solved. For instance, students were asked to build a rubber band car capable of carrying a block at least two meters in distance to achieve non-contact delivery under pandemic restrictions (P5). The scenarios were realistic, motivating the students to produce a workable artifact that met the engineering requirements. In interviews conducted after the intervention, some students mentioned that solving authentic problems brought them a sense of achievement, which made them more interested in these types of activities. We also focused on designing the learning environment and a set of ritualized and sequenced activities according to the CAPE framework, helping students to acclimate to the new learning culture in a highly collaborative, learner-centered, and inquiry-oriented environment. Each year's experience contributed to the subsequent year by making adjustments in the learning environment setting based on classroom observations and interviews. Students reflected that the comfortable learning environment was one of the reasons they enjoyed the EDP learning activities. 3. Develop a longitudinal trajectory with empirical foundation for the theoretical, curricular and pedagogical development of integrated STEM education that will contribute to integrative learning knowledge To develop a longitudinal trajectory for the theoretical, curricular and pedagogical development of integrated STEM education that will contribute to integrative learning knowledge. We focused on investigating the engineering habits of mind (EHoM) and accessing student’s CPS skills in the learning process. The framework for EHoM from the Royal Academy of Engineering consists of six primary habits and twelve secondary habits, with each primary habit having two associated secondary habits. These habits illustrate the specific thought processes and actions of engineers in the EDP learning experience. In the P5 study, this framework was employed as a coding scheme for carrying out an epistemic network analysis (ENA) and a content analysis (CA) to investigate the progression of disciplinary literacy throughout the learning process. The findings demonstrate the emergence and co-occurrence of EHoMs within the learning process, suggesting an enhancement in disciplinary literacy. In the P6 study, the EDP-CPS framework was used to analyse students' CPS skills in peer collaboration. The EDP-CPS framework was created based on the PISA 2015 framework (OECD, 2016) to assess student’s performance in each stage of EDP, and abilities in CPS, which are basically social skills and cognitive skills. The EDP-CPS framework indicates the quality in each cross-referenced skill yielding a 5 x 3 matrix with 15 performance outcomes. A lag sequential analysis (LSA) was conducted to analyse students' behaviour during the interactions with peers. The study focus on the five steps of situating and socail constructionist learning (ask, imagine, plan, create, and improve) and how students collabrative in the activity. The developed EDP-CPS framework is well applied in collaborative situations by the study. Due to the delay posted by COVID-19 and school closure during our project duration, we are preparing to complete additional three major manuscripts for the journal publications to report these objectives.
