17603619.label: Major findings and research outcome
17603619.value: Students’ STEM motivation The pair-sample T-test results show that both science (t = 2.238, p = .027) and engineering (t = 3.630, p < .001) learning motivation has been significantly improved in P4. For science learning motivation, the mean of the pre-test was 27.72 (SD = 6.76) while the mean of the post-test was 29.10 (SD = 7.39). For engineering learning motivation, the mean of the pre-test was 24.89 (SD = 8.43) while the mean of the post-test was 28.00 (SD = 8.38). However, the changes in both in science and engineering learning motivation were not significant in P5 and P6. A group analysis was conducted to explore the difference between collaborative and individual learning approaches in STEM motivation. The result shows that students (n = 98) with a collaborative learning approach improved significantly compared to individual learning (n = 30) both in science (p = .002) and engineering learning (p < .001) motivation in P4. In P6, there is a significant difference between the individual and collaborative approach (p = .038). Students who used the individual learning approach have improved their engineering motivation, while students' engineering motivation has decreased with the collaborative learning approach. Collaborative Problem Solving (CPS) skills Students only took a post-test in P4, with a mean of 62.36 (SD = 12.44). In P5 and P6, both pre- and post-tests were completed. In P5, the mean pre-test score was 59.16 (SD = 12.34), while the mean post-test score was 56.11 (SD = 13.94), showing a significant decrease (t = -2.355, p = .021). In P6, the mean pre-test score was 58.06 (SD = 13.40), while the mean post-test score was 60.32 (SD = 11.13), showing an increase, but there was no significance (t = 1.763, p = .082). Attitude toward EDP scientific learning Most students had a positive attitude towards EDP scientific learning in interviews. They liked this type of learning and believed they could have a better understanding of science and engineering through EDP scientific learning. The following shows the reason why students like EDP scientific learning: hands-on learning (performing scientific experiments, constructing works), feelings of achievement, solving authentic problems (specific users, open-ended issues, offering help, improving work, close-to-life topics), project autonomy (self-determination of materials, self-determination of design), acquiring more knowledge, brainstorming to unleash creativity, and a comfortable learning environment (positive learning atmosphere, accessing to tools and materials, good collaboration with peers, teacher support, parent support), etc.

17603619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17603619.value: In the previous study, we can see both teachers and students can embrace EDP teaching and learning as a regular curriculum component. To further integrate EDP into science education for upper primary school students, we can explore how different types of topics can impact students’ learning. We have also found, in the activities requiring each student to create their own work based on the group’s design had ensured everyone's participation; while requesting each group to complete shared work could demand a greater level of collaboration and task delegation skills. We assume that the former approach be used as a scaffold for the latter in fostering students' collaborative skills: for younger learners, teachers can implement less challenging tasks and require each student to create a work based on a common group design, initially nurturing their communication and CPS skills; for older learners, they can attempt more difficult and complex tasks, collaborating to complete a project and resolve issues. Based on the above findings and hypothesis, we propose to continue the design-based research with the schools having adapted to the EDP approach, carrying out different activities for the intervention to further explore EDP in science education.

17603619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17603619.value: With the development of techonology, STEM education at K-12 has attracted public and research attention internationally. The growing public interest in STEM education as part of the compulsory K-12 curriculum calls for exploration of the integrative learning approach to determine whether it offers benefits for children’s problem-solving and learning ability in the STEM subjects. In additional, schools need to focus more on engineering problem-solving activities in implementing integrated K-12 STEM education by emphasizing the importance of engineering challenges and learning from failure, which can be linked to science education. Our previous work indicated that that the EDP pedagogical approach has the potential to facilitate students to solve engineering problem collaboratively throughout the process by observation. In this study, we focus on science learning involving engineering content and CPS activities in order to investigate the benefits of such interdisciplinary learning. Such a new paradigm will be especially valuable for exploring the students' collabrative solve problem in the context increased techological globally.

17604119.label: Project Objectives
17604119.value: To ascertain the factors that influence PhD students’ career imaginary and focus and PhD holders’ career paths to better understand expected and current career trajectories of doctoral students and graduates of research universities in mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan. To better understand the distinctions and relation between doctoral program experience and generic socio-economic factors in shaping these students’ and graduates’ expected and current career paths. To extend and develop the theoretical contributions of life-course theory and academic-identity trajectories by applying them to highly educated people, considering the relevance of time and generational changes, in order to understand the relevance of different factors in shaping their expected and current careers over time. To disseminate project findings among government funders, PhD program coordinators, supervisors and university managers so that the understanding of critical educational and career-building elements to be identified in this research can be integrated into doctoral programs enabling better-informed career choices.

17604119.label: Realisation of objectives
17604119.value: The objectives proposed in this project were fully met. The project findings are based on 165 interviews (PhD students, 117 PhD graduates, 48), mainland China (48), Hong Kong (49), Macau (40) and Taiwan (28). The Co-PIs also facilitated access to supervisors and potential students in their own jurisdictions. As the interviews were being conducted two important issues arose: 1) there was the need to better understand how the academic profession was gendered in China, since the perspectives of male and female PhD students and graduates’ decision-making and ambitions were shaped by the way the academic work and incentives was perceived. This led the PI to associate a doctoral student that was starting her PhD supervised by the PI, to the topic of academic women in mainland China to assess the attitudes, understandings and behaviors of male and female academics regarding the working context and how it shaped their career-decision-making and imaginaries. By doing this, one could compare the perceptions of PhD students and of actual academics (males and females) concerning the academic profession and work. This focus also permitted to create a time-retrospective relation between the professional, the personal and the social, which contributed decisively to understanding how gender shapes decisions since even at the start of the PhD journey. 2) to better understand the creation of specific imaginaries, the researchers in the project, had to understand how previous personal and educational experiences shaped the understanding of the current PhD students about (1) the social and learning experience that they were having, (2) the extent to which particular events or structures affected their entry to the doctoral programs, and (3) the efforts that they were envisioning for their present and future careers and development. This led to the PI to set an unplanned collaboration with Dr. Jisun Jung from HKU, who has an interest in postgraduate education and accessibility at both the master and doctoral education levels. As the interviews progressed it became obvious that the main labor market for the interviewees were the mainland Chinese academic labor market (the case of Taiwan was different and was analyzed somewhat separately; an article was published solely focusing on the Taiwanese case). The reason for the relevance of the Chinese academic labor market became straightforward considering that most of the PhD students that embarked in doctoral studies in the jurisdictions under study originate from mainland China. The mainland Chinese academic market is the most vibrant academic labor markets currently in existence. The Hong Kong academic labor market was perceived as overly competitive and no other sectors of relevance to provide jobs to PhDs, while the labor market in Macau was understood to be too small to be considered of interest by the interviewees. Therefore, much of the analysis was influenced by the priority that PhD students placed on academic jobs and on attaining them in the mainland Chinese academic labor market. The interviews and analysis thus, reflects the aspirations, concerns, goals, and challenges that mainland Chinese PhD students and graduates have when considering the requirements of the mainland Chinese academic market first, and then working in other sectors of activity also – and mostly – in mainland China. In this context, requirements (real or perceived) of professional pathways were much more important than any other issues, including those relative to the setting of familial or social journeys or the conjoint journey between the social, the familial and the professional that life-course theories tend to emphasize. The analysis of the interviews found that career scripts completely dominate life scripts. This affected female PhD students the most (underlining the need to understand the gender role in life journeys). PhD students (and even graduates) were constrained by career scripts determined by ultra-competitive factors that would be determinant for long-term professional and social “success”. This was also determined by age constrains that were situated in a continuum between the expected age conclusion of the PhD and the ability to entry the academic career, and when in the academic career, determining the chances to move onwards and upwards or stagnate. These age-related constrains were formally set in the Chinese academic labor market by age thresholds to enter the academic profession and to gain access to types of competitive funding grants (key to ensure career promotion and/or tenure). Therefore, the decision-making for PhD students was determined to a large extent by the intersectionality’s of gender and age. The analysis also showed the relevance of another element in this intersectionality: ‘publish or perish’ dynamics completely overwhelmed the priorities and experiences of PhD students. The understanding that publications were an almost mandatory requirement of doctoral students (as perceived by the students) was that accumulation of publications in indexed international-peer reviewed journals was the key to ensure a job in academia. This phenomenon was narrowing down the objectives of doctoral education, placing generation of new knowledge as a secondary priority versus publishing for the sake of having a concrete evidence of the ability to publish, but it was also diverting PhD students to engage with motivation in learning experiences such as serving as teaching assistants (and therefore, learn about teaching practices), engaging with stakeholders outside of the university (thus, mitigating the opportunity to learn about knowledge exchange practices), and even to participate in conferences (where they could learn with others and strive to become part of international and national scholarly communities). The project led to a theoretical development of identity theory and life-course theories when considering the trajectories and identity formation of PhD students by 1) situating the start of the PhD trajectory in the earlier stages of the educational process and trajectory; 2) stressing life scripts to be completely dependent on professional scripts. Professional scripts associated with age, gender and ‘publish or perish’ determined life imaginaries, and were more powerful than educational, social and familial scripts, 3) the dominance of the intellectual strand (i.e., publishing) relative to the networking and institutional strands in the formation of professional identities, 4) the centrality of the research identity even for those PhD graduates that ended up working outside academia in non-researcher oriented professions, 5) proposed a typology of academic career choices of PhD students based on four quadrants: the Materialists, The Academic Strivers, the Comfort Seekers, and the Undecided. Besides the results having been disseminated in interest group circles related to academia, PhD education, higher education, and science in social media in China and internationally, the findings also capture the interest of more mainstream media. For example, in China an article was written about this project in the Tourism and Hospitality Prospects magazine: https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/Jg_ZkUZPOo3D4RFuCBI2TA. Internationally: “´Publish or perish’ culture continues to distort research” in University World News: https://www.universityworldnews.com/post.php?story=20221027134017309 and “When publishing becomes the sole focus of PhD programmes academia suffers” in the London School of Economics (LSE) Blog: https://blogs.lse.ac.uk/impactofsocialsciences/2022/12/05/when-publishing-becomes-the-sole-focus-of-phd-programmes-academia-suffers/. The findings of the project were sent to all the supervisors including those who never responded or declined to participate. The PI was invited to give a keynote to the HERA conference participated by policymakers, university managers and researchers in Taiwan, and was invited to present the results in the department of Physics of the University of Hong Kong.

17604119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17604119.value: The main findings are that career/professional scripts took over completely and dictate much of the thinking and behaviors of PhD students. This leads them to be concerned with trying to conclude their PhDs as fast as possible and at the same time publishing as much as they can, particularly publishing articles in peer-reviewed international journals indexed by the Web of Science (and Scopus to a lesser extent). This makes them to overwhelmingly dismiss any other type of activities and learning within doctoral studies, such as teaching experiences, engagement with non-academic stakeholders, getting integrated in scholarly and scientific communities, and even participating in conferences. Supervisors are increasingly perceived as publication facilitators rather than mentors, and knowledge creation is not the main goal, but rather publishing (publications are indirectly perceived to “have new knowledge”). The career script is related to age – age limits in terms of recruitment, and age limits in terms of access to key funding grants that are essential to guaranteeing promotion and tenure (or contract safety). This places a tremendous amount of stress on PhD students and newly minted PhD graduates, particularly on female PhD students but not only, that apparently continue through the early to the mid-stages of academic career progression. The academic profession and working conditions are perceived by PhD students as deteriorating, but still they continue to be focused on careers in academic because jobs outside academia are understood to be even harder for work-life balance, while at the same time, they build or enhance their “research identity” strongly during the doctoral studies and it is an identity that remains constant and strong thereafter. The structure of the academic recruitment process and career is affecting agency. In terms of research outcomes, 14 publications in international peer-reviewed journals were concluded and published. This accrues to presentation of the findings in 7 international conferences, and the dissemination of the findings through social and mainstream media. Two PhD students completed their PhDs, one that worked as RA for the project, and other who indirectly developed her PhD thesis in relation to this project, and one that the PI of the project considers to be a full member of the project considering how relevant her research was to determine the matching between perceptions of the academic labor market and conditions with the ones perceived by the PhD students that were interviewed for the project.

17604119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17604119.value: The project gained a wide interest internationally. Prof. John Wideman, from the University of Pittsburgh, and a leading expert on socialization of doctoral students, visited HKU and expressed his interest in collaborating with the PI of the project on developing the analysis further. Prof. Montserrat Castelló, from the Universitat Ramon Llull of Barcelona, is also in contact and will send a PhD student, Marina Gorante to work with the PI on a research collaboration that can use the same theoretical and methodological approach used in this project and eventually start a comparative project between the PI’s team and Prof. Castello’s team. The student (Marina) visit to HKU will be fully supported by the Spanish university. Prof. Giulio Marini from the University of Catania also expressed interest in a collaboration on the job interests and preferences of PhD students, comparing Italy with China and Hong Kong. It is probable that an international research team with the HKU team leading a future project will be created to establish comparative studies on the trajectories of PhD students and their career preferences involving cases in East Asia, US, and Europe.

17604119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17604119.value: The study contributed to better understanding the factors influencing the career choices (and relative thinking, priorities, and behaviors) of PhD students. This was done from a perspective that takes their life cycle into account, and considered the possibility that the career choices of these students could be influenced by a broader set of forces (some professional, some social, some familial). The project had several findings, which can be broadly summarize as follows: 1) the learning experiences pre-PhD influence the thinking and actions of the students during the PhD; 2) The vast majority of PhD students want to become academics, and focus the outcomes of doctoral studies on this goal; 3) They learn the rules of the game and a near-obsession with publishing emerges as a response to perceived requirements to enter the academic profession; 4) This does not prevent PhD students from creating a “researcher identity” that remains strong after the conclusion of the degree; 5) Professional scripts associated to structural rules dictated by academic recruitment are more powerful than any societal or familial scripts; and 6) female PhD students tend to be more affected by these scripts that are strongly rooted in ageism.

17604319.value: 大規模的宗教復興是改革開放以後中國社會轉型的一個重要維度。但宗教復興並非是將固化的、一成不變的，且在毛時代被壓制的宗教傳統重新挖掘出來的過程，而是涉及到宗教與快速現代化和市場化的社會條件之間的複雜交換和互動。是項研究的出發點認同宗教必須被理解為當代中國市場轉型的一個不可或缺的維度。宗教越來越被視為能夠指導人們生存並最終在市場轉型中獲得成功的智慧源泉。同時，宗教不斷參與到複雜的開發、建設與營銷項目，并以大規模投資和大眾消費為特徵。是項研究基於最近在宗教地理學和同源學科之間的討論，并以此理解宗教與市場經濟之間的交叉和相互作用。研究聚焦於中國大陸的漢傳大乘佛教，以市場文化和企業型宗教的概念為基礎，對市場轉型過程中佛教實踐的範式變化進行解釋。我們的目標是繪制一條新的理論路徑，即從教條式的信仰（教條主義）到實踐的信仰（實踐主義），系統地理論化宗教與政治經濟之間的複雜糾纏，以及宗教被不斷再發明和創新的方式和過程。 該項目預計對企業型宗教進行系統而細緻的實證研究，以闡明現存研究中尚未充分解決的重要理論問題。第一，是什麼地理-歷史語境、影響因素和力量，催生了宗教的企業化實踐？第二，是什麼神學改革推動並合理化了宗教的企業化實踐？第三，為了在現代社會中建立信仰立足點，宗教品牌營銷的策略是什麼？第四，宗教企業型項目在促進城市與區域發展規劃方面有何作用？ 這個為期36個月的項目將分別考察位於北京，南京和杭州的3個宗教場所。在這三個案例中，佛教的企業式實踐尤為突出。研究遵循多地點案例研究的方法論，並綜合運用多種研究方法，包括檔案研究、文本和視覺方法、深度訪談、焦點訪談和參與式觀察。是項研究將關注佛教企業型項目的起源和演變，以及這些項目如何反映新的神學取向和佛教品牌營銷的新方法，為改革時期的中國宗教研究貢獻新的知識。它還將為中國內地和香港的宗教人士、政策制定者和商界提供基於佛教的大型城市開發項目的第一手資料。

17604319.label: Realisation of objectives
17604319.value: During the project period, the team dutifully and faithfully executed the research plan as proposed in the original proposal, and fulfilled the field investigation of the three field study sites in Beijing, Nanjing, and Hangzhou, respectively. The four research objectives have been fully addressed. Some modifications to the research plan were adopted during the research process, mainly due to disruptions to travel during the Covid-19 pandemic. For example, some field-based methods were replaced by Internet-based interactions and interviews. Also, continued travel restrictions made conference funding exceed what we could actually spend, as physical attendance was not possible. The 8% of the funding that was not spent was largely due to the same reasons. Given that the need for travel cost was reduced, the project team proposed a budget change, and some of the travel and conference budget was transferred to outsourcing, so that an RA based in Mainland China could be contracted to undertake extra fieldworks on Buddhism-themed urban development projects in Chengdu and Xi’an, in order to make the use of the project funding more efficient and productive. Research outputs emerging from the project are listed as follows: 1. Zhang H, Qian JX. 2020. This-worldly Buddhism: social media and religiosity in China. Blurring the Interface of Religiosities and Platform Urbanism: “Wanghong Temples” and Community Renewal in Hangzhou, China, under preparation Delivery of project objectives Objective 1: The realisation of Objective 1 is mainly based on the collection of second-hand data and first-hand interview data that helped delineate a broader social context of the emergence of entrepreneurial religion. Factors such as middle class people’s aspiration for spirituality amidst market transition, the group’s spatial proximity to major religious shrines, religion’s embeddedness in urban cultural and creative development, and its alignment with urban planning initiatives are revealed to have contributed to the making of entrepreneurial practices of Chinese Mahayana Buddhism. This objective is investigated in Research Outputs 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7. Objective 2: The realisation of Objective 2 is mainly based on the analysis of second-hand materials collected from the field sites and first-hand data based on observation, focus group, and interview. The primary finding is that Buddhism in China is making the transition from emphasising the accumulation of merit for the next life to the provision of this-worldly benefits such as spiritual guidance and the cultivation of the self for Buddhist followers and believers. In other words, Buddhism nowadays is not so much a moral and ethical framework that defines community and collective identity as a lifestyle choice and technology of the self. This objective is investigated in Research Outputs 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7. Objective 3: The realisation of Objective 3 is mainly based on the analysis of second-hand data collected from the field and online sources and first-hand data based on observation, focus group, and interview. The project has revealed a broad diversity of means and approaches through which Buddhism brands itself as relevant to and fulfilling for the lives of modern urban people. These strategies include heavy reliance on social media and repackaged cultural images of Buddhism, the construction of spectacular and well-deigned material spaces to project symbolic and aesthetic power, the operation of training courses based on reinvented theological teaching, and even direct engagement with the market economy through entrepreneurship, finance, start-up funding, technological innovation, etc. This objective is investigated in Research Outputs 1, 2, 4, 6, 7, and 8. Objective 4: The realisation of Objective 4 is mainly based on the analysis of second-hand data such as planning documents and business reports and first-hand data based on observation, focus group, and interview. The project has affirmed the active role played by Buddhism in a variety of urban planning and development projects, and its close alignment with other urban development strategies such as cultural and creative industry development and the making of cultural cities. The project has also probed into the scale of land development and investment, as well as the potential economic utilities that are envisioned. This objective is investigated in Research Outputs 3, 4, and 5.

17604319.label: Major findings and research outcome
17604319.value: The GRF project investigates the reinvention of religious theologies, practices, and spaces vis-à-vis the rise of a market society, through a geographical exploration of Chinese Mahayana Buddhism as an entrepreneurial religion. The post-reform era of China has witnessed the convergence of secular modernity and a growing religious revival, leading to the emergence of various entrepreneurial religions. The project critically examines the complex interplay between Mahayana Buddhism and the diverse conditions of secular modernity. Some major findings and contributions are made by the projects, which are explained as follows. First it contributes to identifying the spatial conditions conducive to entrepreneurial religion, delving into its geographical dimensions and implications of religious reform. This project sheds light on the evolving role of religion in urban development and the facilitating conditions within urban environments for the change of religious subjectivities, such as proximity to middle class aspiring for spirituality and the broad context of creative and cultural industry development in cities. Second, it elucidates how the socioeconomic conditions of capitalist modernity have catalysed the entrepreneurial orientation of Mahayana Buddhist organizations, as manifested through the reform of organization/management, theological innovations, and the changes of material landscapes in their engagement with secular forces, to make religion more compelling to modern consumers and integral to urban planning and development. Lastly, this project scrutinises the fluid and porous interface between religiosity and secularity by exploring how religious and non-religious logics intertwine and how new theological discourses circulate, largely based on popular cultures and emerging social media. It underscores how entrepreneurial religion engenders new religious subjectivities, intertwined with the variegated conditions of secular modernity and multi-scalar contextual factors. In summary, the multifaceted exploration of entrepreneurial religion further enhances the understanding of religion and religiosity. It highlights the unique dynamics of religious innovation and space production in a non-Western context, contributing to a more comprehensive and nuanced perspective on the interplay between religion, culture, and societal dynamics. On the one hand, the project contributes to comprehending entrepreneurial religion and its interactions with social, economic, and cultural contexts by providing a hybrid and negotiated epistemological space for reconciling seemingly divergent concepts and ontologies. On the other hand, it provides valuable insights for religious practitioners, policymakers and corporate entities, and lays the groundwork for informed decision-making processes, urban planning strategies, and collaborative initiatives that capitalise on the convergence of Buddhism, culture, and urban revitalisation to foster mutually beneficiary relationships and sustainable development.

17604319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17604319.value: The research team aims to further advance this research agenda in the following directions: 1. To develop more case studies in the context of Chinese Buddhism in order to synthesise a theoretical framework of religious innovation and reform vis-à-vis urban and regional development amidst market transition. 2. To develop comparative research between Buddhist practices in places of varying status of social and economic development in China in order to better appreciate the contextual contingency and variation of Buddhist entrepreneurialism. 3. To move beyond the focus on China studies and deepen the engagement with literatures on religious change, innovation, and reform with reference to diverse contexts across the world, to better furnish the potential theoretical contribution of our research agenda.

17604319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17604319.value: The project investigates the innovations in theologies, practices, and spaces that Chinese Mahayana Buddhism has adopted to make itself relevant to the lived experiences of urban people navigating the vicissitude of market society. Our mission is to develop a conceptualisation and theorisation on entrepreneurial religion, and its theological, economic, cultural, and spatial manifestations. Focusing on a variety of case study sites across Beijing, Nanjing, Hangzhou, Chengdu, and Xi’an, and mixing a diversity of qualitative research methods, the project emphasises three dimensions under this overarching theoretical mission. First, it reveals the reforms in theologies, underscoring the transition from a focus on the accumulation of merit for the next life to the provision of thisworldly benefits. Second, it probes into a diversity of strategies and approaches that Buddhist institutions and clergies have adopted to brand a novel cultural image of Mahayana Buddhism, ranging from the use of social media to direct engagement with the logics of market and profit. Finally, we investigate the alignment between Buddhism and urban planning initiatives in terms of the development of urban land and space, showcasing how Buddhist entrepreneurialism is embedded in urban strategies such as cultural and creative industry development and the making of cultural cities.

17604919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17604919.value: “Medicalising Ethiopia” aims to understand the notions and intertwined relationships between medicine, health and disease in Ethiopia following the introduction of Western medical practices in the late 19th century. By taking the example of Ethiopia, a country that remained independent from colonial occupation but that was enmeshed in relations with European powers, this study is a necessary component to provide a fuller picture of the dynamics in 19th century Africa. This project intends to provide a closer look at the pre-19th century medical scene of Ethiopia using the particular moment of the sickness of Emperor Menelik II and the introduction of western medical practices as points of entry. Emperor of Ethiopia between 1889 and 1913, Menelik II is famous for having led the first successful African campaign against a European colonial army (Battle of Adwa 1896). Although he was generally suspicious of colonial powers’ intentions, his vision for Ethiopian modernization made him also a fervent admirer of European technological advancements and their potential for his country. As his frail health was showing clear signs of deterioration, more than two-dozen physicians from various European countries were given access to Emperor Menelik II alongside traditional healers between 1880 and 1913. At the time, medical doctors had an easier access to the imperial court than their diplomatic representatives who were carefully kept at bay. Having arrived in Ethiopia as medical nomads or medical diplomats, these doctors dispensed medical services to the emperor, his entourage and the population at large. This study offers an opportunity to present Ethiopian history as well as the country’s encounter with European colonialism from a new angle by unpacking the work that was actively being done in the medical field by these doctors and traditional medical practioners. Furthermore, it is attentive to establishing the roles of Africans in making choices, acting and reaching to European influence and power. The study will employ a multidisciplinary approach that will put European medical interventions and traditional Ethiopian medicine at the center of the analysis and unpack the complex ties that bind them all together. Engaging with colonial archives and local sources, it will look into the larger impacts resulting from these interactions. The resulting research monograph will contribute to advancing the integration of history of medical and public health in Africa into the larger literature that makes science and policy issues salient subject in modern history. “醫療化埃塞俄比亞”希望理解19世紀末，當埃塞俄比亞在引入了西方醫療實踐之後所產生的一些概念以及在醫藥、健康，疾病之間交織的關係。以埃塞俄比亞這樣一個雖然在當時保持獨立，但卻不可避免地掙扎于歐洲列强的非洲國家作爲案例，本研究將爲構建一個更完整的19世界非洲歷史作出貢獻。 此項研究將細緻地審視19世紀之前埃塞俄比亞的醫療觀念，同時也將皇帝孟尼利克二世患病而引入西方醫學作爲研究的一個關鍵時間點。作爲在位于1880至1913年的皇帝，孟尼利克二世因成功領導第一場非洲國家戰勝西方殖民軍隊的戰爭而聞名（1896年的阿杜瓦戰役）。雖然他對殖民者一直抱持著深度懷疑，但同時他也是一個埃塞俄比亞必須現代化的堅定支持者。他被歐洲的科技深深吸引，同時也相信科技對埃塞俄比亞國家社會發展的潛在作用。當他身體日漸衰弱時，有超過20個來自歐洲各個國家的醫生獲准為皇帝診治。同時，皇帝也接受來自國内傳統醫療的照顧。在當時，醫生，相比那些被小心安置在港口的外國使節，更容易接近埃塞俄比亞宮廷。這些兼具醫療游牧者和醫療使節身份的西方醫生，不僅提供皇帝醫療服務，也在他的鼓勵下，在埃囯民間推廣西方醫療。 本研究有機會用一個新的角度，通過分析這批歐洲醫生在當時的著作以及埃塞俄比亞本地的傳統醫學，重新切入埃囯以及它和西方殖民主義相遇時的那段歷史。另外，本研究也將試圖展現一個非洲國家在面對歐洲强權及其影響時，自主作出的選擇的新形象。 此項研究將采用跨學科的研究方法，以歐洲醫學實踐以及埃塞俄比亞本國傳統醫學作爲核心案例，去試圖解析在當時兩者之間複雜而纏繞的關係。利用殖民者的記錄和本地資源，本研究將關注醫療技術引入埃囯帶來的更大的其他社會面嚮的影響。未來研究產生的專著將有機會將非洲的醫療和公共衛生史整合進一個更大的學術文本體系，從而强化科學和政策在現代歷史中的地位。

17605119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605119.value: Background: In a super-aging society like Hong Kong, a huge number of older couples are getting frail together. Current research on informal carer dominantly takes a spousal caregiving perspective by clearly distinguish between roles of caregivers and care-receivers, overlooking a prevalent phenomenon that both spouses are at risk of functional decline and help with each other in daily life. Despite there is a few literature on the concordant health outcomes between spouses, no systematic research has been conducted to examine couple’s experiences of handling daily stressors and its well-being impacts. To address these research gasps, the proposed study advocates a paradigm shift from an individual-based examination of caregiver and care-receiver to investigating collaborative care arrangements within older couples and takes a first step to investigate the vivid experiences of how functionally impaired couples dealing with daily stressors. Objectives: The study aimed to test specific functions of couple’s collaborative dynamics in mastering daily stressors that could facilitate more positive individual and relational well-being outcomes, and whether the effectiveness of collaboration varies as a function of perceived control of self and spouse during collaboration. By integrating interdependence theory and frameworks of dyadic coping, this study will test two sets of hypothesizes: (1) spousal collaboration buffers the temporal relationship between daily stressors and psychophysiological responses, and such buffering effects are enhanced when spouses exhibit a reciprocal pattern of control in collaboration; and (2) more frequent use of collaboration to deal with daily stressors is prospectively associated with greater well-being and marital satisfaction. Methodology: We propose to use a combined research design comprising a longitudinal survey and ecological momentary assessment (EMA). The EMA research protocol has been validated in our previous work as a feasible and reliable method for studying real-life experiences of community-dwelling older adults. A sample of 75 older couples wherein both spouses reported functional decline will be recruited to participate in a baseline survey, a 14-day EMA, and a 12-month follow up survey. During the 14-day EMA period, each participant will be instructed to use mobile devices to provide self-report data (e.g., daily stressors, affect) and cardiovascular recordings four times daily. Conclusion: The findings of this study will serve as the first evidence of the phenomenon of collaborative dynamics of functionally impaired couples’ mastering on daily problems. Findings will also inform the development of couple-centered care models that address the joint health needs of both spouses in super-aging societies globally. 面對超高齡社會的來臨，越來越多的老年夫婦會一起攜手經驗老化的過程。以往關於照顧者的研究一般會假設夫妻中有需要照顧的一方，另一方為主要照顧者。但是在日常生活中經常觀察到的是夫婦一起經驗老化的日常，有時候你照顧我，有時候我照顧你，有時候互相照顧，區分照顧者和被照顧者在理論上和實際上都未能解釋夫妻共老的實際經驗，夫妻在健康層面互相影響的研究也非常有限。本研究提出照顧者研究需要一個新的研究範式 – 系統研究夫妻兩人如何協同應對老化中的日常挑戰，特別是在當夫婦體驗到功能健康逐漸衰落的情境下。 故此，本研究目的是1）探索夫妻在面對共同老化的日常過程中如何運用協同應對策略；2）在協同應對過程中對自己及對方行為的控制感是有效協同的關鍵。為了實現這兩個研究目的，擬檢驗以下的兩個假設：首先，夫妻間的協同能緩衝老化過程日常的挑戰與健康指標之間的關係，這種緩衝會在夫妻有協同應對策略的情境下得到強化；其次，在日常生活中越多運用協同應對策略，越有機會有良好的健康與婚姻滿意度。 在本研究團隊發展的一套有效生態瞬間評估方法實踐步驟的基礎上，本研究綜合運用生態瞬間評估及長期問卷調查的方法。擬在社區招募75對老年夫婦，邀請參與夫婦在12個月間隔前後參與標準化的問卷調查，並在兩次調查之間參與14天的生態瞬間評估。 本項目是首個系統探索夫妻協同應對老化日常中挑戰的研究專案，預計研究結果將對瞭解及預測夫妻共同應對老化的理論和實際有建設性的影響，深化照顧者研究理論及為支援照顧者政策和服務的實際提供實證基礎。

17605119.label: Realisation of objectives
17605119.value: All three project objectives were fully achieved. Research design: This study adopted a multiple method approach by integrating longitudinal design and Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) with three main components: (1) a baseline interviewer-administered geriatric assessment, (2) a 14-day EMA, and (3) a 12-month follow-up assessment. This multiple method approach was initiated and tested by our research team, and a pilot study was successfully implemented in a sample of community-dwelling Chinese elderly to study the procedure protocol and collect biopsychosocial data in 2020. Recruitment: Recruitment took place from Nov 2020 to Aug 2021. Of 174 (87 couples) eligible participants with functional decline (PwFD) from four elderly community centers, 166 participants (83 couples) consented to participate [mean age (SD) = 77.33 (6.83); mean marital year (SD) = 50.14 (8.10); independence in ADLs = 65.1%]. Male PwFD were slightly older [mean age (SD) = 79.2 (6.69)] as compared to their female partners [mean age (SD) = 75.5 (6.50)]. Male PwFD also experienced lower independence when performing ADL [mean (SD) = 95.6 (10.0)] then their wives [mean age (SD) = 96.2 (7.49)]. Data collection and analysis: Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, baseline data was collected by either face-to-face interview or online survey, we over-recruited 16 PwFD to cover the underestimated attrition (10.7%). A 14-day EMA was conducted, with a total of 156 PwFD (78 couples) finished the EMA, equivalent to 6% attrition rate. Additionally, we successfully collected a 1-day EMA one week after, with 154 PwFD (77 couples) to understand the changes in psychosocial well-being. The 12-month follow-up assessment was conducted with 129 PwFD (64 couples plus one male; attrition rate = 22.3%). No missing data was reported. Due to social distancing and closure of community centers, we collaborated with Central South University to collect physiological data using an electrocardiogram (ECG). For objective 1, we proposed one hypothesis. H1: Spousal collaboration buffers the temporal relationship between daily stressors and affective responses, and such buffering effects are enhanced when spouses exhibit a reciprocal pattern of control during collaboration. In this model, spousal collaboration refers to common dyadic coping (CDC) measured using a subscale of the Dyadic Coping Inventory (range: 1-15). CDC are coping strategies in which the couples participate complementarily which can be either problem-focused or emotion-focused, when dealing with daily stressors. A total of 21 daily stressors were identified from the Daily Inventory of Stressful Events (DISE) and the stress experienced by PwFD was averaged to obtain a continuous score (range: 1-5). Affective responses were measured using 10 selected items from the Positive and Negative Affect Scale (PANAS), mean score of positive affect (range: 1-5) and negative affect (range: 1-5). As daily stressors can be transmitted between couples, spousal collaboration was hypothesized to enhance positive affect and reduce negative affect. Figure 1 illustrated the differences in positive and negative affect among couple, showing support to the use of EMA as data collection method. Positive affect. Our analysis showed that number of daily stressors (b = -.04, 95% CI [-.06, -.03], z = -.51, p < .001) and spousal collaboration (b = .16, 95% CI [.14, .18], z = 13.82, p < .001) has a direct effect on positive affect, respectively. Spousal collaboration was found to moderate the relationships between the number of daily stressors and positive affect (b = .01, 95% CI [.00, .01], z = 4.19, p < .001). PwFD with a higher spousal collaboration experienced higher positive affect when dealing with daily stressors, while PwFD with lower spousal collaboration experienced lower positive affect when dealing with daily stressors. Negative affect. Our analysis showed that number of daily stressors (b = .09, 95% CI [.08, .10], z = 17.03, p < .001) and spousal collaboration (b = -.06, 95% CI [-.08, -.04], z = -6.84, p < .001) has a direct effect on negative affect, respectively. Spousal collaboration was found to moderate the relationships between the number of daily stressors and negative affect (b = -.01, 95% CI [-.02, -.01], z = -10.23, p < .001). PwFD with a higher spousal collaboration experienced lower negative affect when dealing with daily stressors, while PwFD with lower spousal collaboration experienced higher negative affect when dealing with daily stressors. For objective 2, we proposed one hypothesis. H2: Spousal collaboration buffers the temporal relationship between daily stressors and cardiovascular activation, and such buffering effects are enhanced when spouses exhibit a reciprocal pattern of control during collaboration. Perceived control is an understudied temporal aspect of collaboration that may be of importance in postulating collaborative outcomes. Feeling controlled or over-dominated by one’s spouse has been found to associate with psychophysiological arousal. A prolonged corrected QT (QTc) interval refers to an irregular heart rhythm that can be detected using an ECG. QT interval prolongation is associated with increased mortality, especially among adults over age 40. Due to the pandemic, we experienced social distancing and closure of community centers (which prevented on-site support for data collection using ECG), as well as delay of delivery of ECG machines (Checkme Pro F5 Health Monitor; ordered in Sep 2020, and delivered in Feb 2021). We contacted one of the Co-Is to collect data in China (n = 6; 20-day EMA and ECG; twice per day), under the Central South University, resulting in a total of 240 valid data points. Following Hodges’ formula, we transformed QT interval (in milliseconds) using standard heart rate: QTc = QT + 0.00175 * (heart rate – 60). Cardiovascular activation. Our analysis showed that number of daily stressors has no significant direct effect on QTc interval among PwFD (b = -9.32, 95% CI [-20.00, 1.40], z = -1.7.0, p = .088). Spousal collaboration has a direct effect on QTc interval (b = 28.94, 95% CI [25.0, 32.89], z = 14.37, p < .001). Spousal collaboration was found to moderate the relationships between the number of daily stressors and QTc interval (b = -29.44, 95% CI [-33.1, -25.74], z = -15.57, p < .001). PwFD with a higher spousal collaboration experienced shorter QTc interval when dealing with daily stressors, while PwFD with lower spousal collaboration experienced longer QTc interval when dealing with daily stressors. For objective 3, we proposed two hypotheses. H3: More frequent use of spousal collaboration to deal with daily stressors is prospectively associated with greater individual well-being. In this model, individual well-being refers to depressive symptomatology. This outcome was measured using the Chinese version Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9; range: 0-27), with baseline mean score (SD) = 4.46 (4.28). Among the 166 PwFD, 28.9% reported mild depression, 8.4% reported moderate depression, 2.4% reported moderately severe depression, and only 0.6% reported severe depression. Among these PwFD, female participants [mean (SD) = 5.18 (4.59)] reported significantly higher depressive symptoms than their husbands [mean (SD) = 3.73 (3.83)], t(164) = 2.20, p = .029. Another hypothesis concerns the prediction on marital satisfaction. In this study, marital satisfaction was measured using the 7-item Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS; range: 5-35), with baseline mean score (SD) = 28.9 (5.48). Among the 166 PwFD, female participants [mean (SD) = 27.3 (6.28)] reported significantly lower marital satisfaction than their husbands [mean (SD) = 30.5 (3.97)], t(164) = -3.90, p < .001. We used regression analyses to predict 1-year depressive symptomatology and marital satisfaction among the PwFD, an average score of RAS was computed for subsequent analysis.

17605119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17605119.value: PwFD who reported higher than average levels of CDC experienced a lower negative affect when dealing with daily stressors (b = .03, 95% CI [.02, .05], z = 3.84, p < .001). On the other hand, PwFD who reported lower than average levels of CDC experienced a higher negative affect when dealing with daily stressors (b = .15, 95% CI [.14, .16], z = 22.08, p < .001). From these results, it can be concluded that the effect of daily stressors on negative affect is moderated by CDC. Overall, H1 is supported. Our results showed that PwFD in China who reported higher than average levels of CDC experienced a lower effect of daily stressors on QTc (b = -87.4, 95% CI [-112.7, -62.02], z = -6.75, p < .001). Also, PwFD who reported lower than average levels of CDC experienced a higher effect of daily stressors on QTc (b = 56.3, 95% CI [31.1, 81.53], z = 4.37, p < .001). From these results, it can be concluded that H2 is supported. Spousal collaboration buffers the temporal relationship between daily stressors and cardiovascular activation (in terms of QTc interval in milliseconds). The mean score of PHQ-9 for all participants’ baseline and follow-up was 4.46 (SD = 4.28) and 4.35 (SD = 5.05), respectively. For female participants, the CDC is a predictor for their follow-up PHQ-9. When they use CDC more frequently, their PHQ-9 score will decrease to some degree (B = -6.123, 95% CI [-11.71, -.54], p =.032). CDC affects females in dealing with daily stressors but not males. Males are more affected by demographic factors including age (B = -2.437, 95% CI [-4.61, -.26], p =.029) and ADL conditions (B = -4.216, 95% CI [-7.75, -.69], p = .020). Their PHQ-9 will decrease to some extent if they are more independent, and with age increases. The mean score of marital satisfaction (measured by RAS) for all participants’ baseline and follow-up was 4.13 (SD = 0.79) and 4.18 (SD = 0.82), respectively. For all participants, the baseline RAS score (B = 0.992, 95% CI [.78, 1.21], p < .001) is a strong predictor for their follow-up RAS score. For female participants, the CDC is a predictor for their follow-up RAS. When they use CDC more frequently, their RAS score will increase (B = 1.472, 95% CI [.44, 2.51], p = .006).

17605119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17605119.value: In a super-ageing society like Hong Kong, our study addressed important research gaps regarding older couples’ experiences of getting frail together. This project has generated a theory-driven and evidence-based predictive model to explain the manifestation of CDC in managing daily stressors among older couples with functional decline. It enriches the conceptualisation of daily stressors, collaborative dynamics, and well-being outcomes, by integrating interdependency theory and the current collaborative coping framework. The findings call for a paradigm shift from ‘focusing on spousal caregiving in ageing’ to ‘enhancing spousal collaboration among older couples experiencing frail together’. The PI applied research findings from this project to inform interventions of another project entitled “YWCA Jockey Club Joyful Marriage Project” in 2021, to enhance marital satisfaction and well-being among older adults. The PI will also transfer knowledge to a territory-wide caregiver support project (funded by The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust; amount > HKD25 million). An intervention program will be developed to optimise CDC, stressed on mutual support, mutual goal-setting, mutual caregiver training, and marital enhancement therapies, for older couples. Additionally, the purchased ECGs will be fully utilised in other projects led/co-led by the PI, including health talk, intelligent robotics development, balance sensor development, etc.

17605119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17605119.value: Spousal collaboration is a valuable strategy to buffer the negative affect, cardiovascular-related mortality risk, depressive symptomatology, and marital dissatisfaction. Research on spousal interdependence focuses on ameliorating the negative effects of a caregiver, least attention is paid to understanding how older couples depend on each other when they aged, due largely to functional decline and loss of independence in daily living. This multimethod study explores the buffering effect of common dyadic coping (CDC) in dealing with daily stressors among older couples. From Nov 2020 to Aug 2021, 166 older couples completed a survey at baseline. Among them, 156 joined a 14-day EMA data collection. Additionally, 129 completed a 12-month follow-up survey. Data analysis indicated that CDC moderates the relationships between daily stressors and positive and negative affect, respectively. More importantly, more frequent use of the CDC predicted lower depressive symptoms and higher marital satisfaction. Coaching older couples to employ CDC as a strategy to manage daily stressors is crucial to render older couples find the right balance and age gracefully together. The findings inform the development of an intervention program in a territory-wide caregiver support project. Consequentially, facilitates older couples to have and hold each other ‘in sickness and in health’.

17605419.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17605419.value: 面臨死亡：中國臨終照護的道德挑戰和文化實踐

17605419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17605419.value: Following over three decades of market reforms and stringent birth planning policies, the People's Republic of China is undergoing a dramatic demographic and cultural transformation that has significant ramifications for the care of older people and the critically ill. By focusing on fraught debates over the use and termination of costly medical technologies in Chinese hospitals, this research project will provide fresh data on emerging caregiving practices and health-seeking strategies. The project will produce the first research monograph on the culture and ethics of critical care in urban China, linking transformations in family-based caregiving with the growing medicalization of death in Chinese hospitals. The interdisciplinary impact of this project is far-reaching, with important insights for understanding the role of medical technology in the context of a rapidly ageing society and an unevenly privatized health care system. Drawing on approaches from sociocultural anthropology and the medical humanities, the principal investigator will utilize mixed methods (including ethnographic observation, interviewing, surveys, and archival work) to collect comparative data on end-of-life treatment in tertiary care hospitals located in Beijing, Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Zhengzhou. With over half of all deaths in urban China now occurring in medical facilities, these sites for critical care offer a crucial window on how the medicalization of dying is transforming the ways in which Chinese patients, families, and medical professionals confront mortality. The project will integrate qualitative and quantitative data to provide a rigorous analysis of the challenges involved in caring for the critically ill in urban China. This research project builds upon the principal investigator's previous work on the culture and ethics of transnational biomedical technologies. While the principal investigator's first book (Biomedical Odysseys, Princeton 2017) focuses on the efforts of terminally ill patients and their families around the world to pursue experimental stem cell therapies in urban China, this new research study goes beyond the pursuit of curative medicine to examine what happens when technological interventions are no longer able to restore health. By shifting the focus from cure to care, this project will illuminate the ways in which Chinese patients, family members, and health care providers negotiate the practical and moral challenges of care at the limits of medicine. 這是一項關於中國重症監護的文化實踐和倫理道德觀的研究項目。經過三十多年的改革開放和計劃生育政策，中華人民共和國正在經歷一場巨大的人口和文化轉型。人口高速老齡化和醫療衛生系統的改革對老年人和重症病人照顧的理念和技術產生了深遠的影響和改變。通過對醫療技術使用中人們面臨的問題和挑戰的調查，本研究將探討中國有關護理技術以及健康策略的趨勢和變化，並進一步對家庭護理、醫院臨終照顧、以及中國城市的重症照顧理念和倫理的轉變等方面提供新的見解。 本項目將採用社會科學和醫學人文的研究方法，包括深度訪談、問卷調查、檔案研究、參與觀察等來收集、比較和分析位於北京、上海、深圳和鄭州四地醫院的臨終治療方式。對重症監護中臨終治療的研究為理解醫技術的發展和應用是如何影響重症患者、其家庭以及醫療專業人員應對死亡的挑戰提供了一個重要的窗口。通過量化與質化的綜合分析，本研究將深刻探討對重症患者的照護過程中人們所面臨技術選擇、生存挑戰及道德困境。 本研究將以主研究者之前關於跨國生物醫學技術的文化和倫理的研究著作為基礎 (2017 年由普林斯頓大學出版社出版專著 Biomedical Odysseys: Fetal Cell Experiments from Cyberspace to China)，將研究重點從有藥可醫的疾病治療進一步轉移到無法挽救的臨終護理，以闡明中國重症患者、家庭成員和醫療人員，是如何在醫學技術的限制下就護理的實際需要和道德挑戰與死亡進行艱難交涉的。

17607019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17607019.value: Through the principle of legal extraterritoriality the US projected jurisdiction across the continental frontier, the American hemisphere, and into China. Extraterritoriality cast long shadows on diplomatic, commercial, and cultural relations between the two countries. Through writings of 19th-century US diplomats, this project develops the international significance of these shadows. Literary interpretation of neglected print materials evinces extraterritoriality's many shades of significance for the geographical imaginary of the developing US that linked territorial expansion in the "Far West" to commercial influence in the "Far East." The US diplomats to China were of various professions, political parties, and regional affiliations. Their particular styles of writing addressed layers of national and international audiences. For example, the Massachusetts Congressman Caleb Cushing was prolific legal scholar before he negotiated the Treaty of Wangxi (1844) in Macao. He changed the course of diplomatic history by wrongly declaring that the treaty had won China's concession of "absolute and unqualified" extraterritoriality." Such bravado echoes in his earlier legal writings on Cherokee Removal-- this proposal explains how his mode of argumentation and selective citation stabilised a demonstrably false but influential claim. Two decades later the abolitionist Massachusetts congressman Anson Burlingame reworked Cushing's version of extraterritoriality into a "cooperative policy" through a very different style of diplomatic writing that roused audiences but lacked an attention to administrative detail. Burlingame's successor J. Ross Brown confounded Burlingame's diplomatic efforts by returning to journalistic modes of expression that he had honed on a whaling expedition and in Oregon Territory as an Indian Agent. The content and styles of diplomats' writings connects Chinese Treaty Ports to centres of governance and investment in the US, lending new insight on China's importance for understanding the development of the Monroe (1823) and Tyler (1842) Doctrines, the Open Door Policy (1899), and notions of free trade and international law. This intercultural history of extraterritoriality illustrates how US diplomatic efforts reflected (and affected) the development of US culture in an era of westward continental expansion. 根據治外法權理論，美國外交官預測了北美和中國的管轄權。治外法權影響了兩國之間的外交，商業和文化關係。該項目分析了19世紀美國外交官的著作。該項目採用文學解釋方法探索中國貿易與北美命運之間的聯繫。外交官包括：Caleb Cushing, William B. Reed，Anson Burlingame，J。Ross Browne，Frederick Low，Benjamin Avery，George F. Seward，James B. Angell，John R. Young和Charles Denby。在不同時期，他們與美國國務卿合作，重新談判治外法權，企圖加強中國的國家貿易，同時阻止“條約大國”分裂中國。這些美國外交官都是有影響力的白人，他們往往來自上層階級家庭。然而，在政治信仰和國家發展的地理觀點方面，它們有著驚人的不同。例如，里德是賓夕法尼亞大學歷史學教授和支持奴隸製作為國家權利的民主黨人;相反，Burlingame是一位直言不諱的反奴隸制政治家，代表馬薩諸塞州眾議院。布朗是一位出生於愛爾蘭的文學家，來自肯塔基州，他搬到了加利福尼亞州，在那裡他發表了關於他在捕鯨船上的經歷並成為印第安事務的代理人。艾弗里曾是加州州長。詹姆斯安吉爾是密歇根大學的校長。他們都是多產的作家。 該研究還考慮了幫助外交官的美國傳教士的作用。在結論中這個研究項目 閱讀他們的形式和內容的寫作，以了解他們作為反帝國主義的域外性的各種理由。這項研究表明了中國對門羅主義（1823年），泰勒主義（1842年）和門戶開放政策（1899年）發展的重要性。

17607119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17607119.value: Inclusive access to credit is of paramount importance to reducing poverty. The expansion of credit has been supported by ambitious law reforms particularly in developing economies. By and large, these initiatives adhere to international legal standards and aim to reduce the risk of lending to micro and small businesses, individuals and, more generally, groups that are disenfranchised from society’s formal financial system. A conspicuous number of jurisdictions have embarked on reforming domestic laws to promote the use of secured transactions, whereby assets commonly available to micro and small businesses may be used as collateral for a loan, without requiring their delivery to the creditor. Yet, it remains unclear to what extent these reforms have succeeded in incentivising financiers – banks in particular – to provide new credit and promote financial inclusion. The effectiveness of such reform efforts is further challenged by profound political, economic, and technological changes that ushered the dawn of the new millennium. Specifically, the 2007-2008 global financial crisis and current concerns over the stability of emerging markets indicate the fragility of credit-based economies; whilst, the emergence of disruptive technologies in finance, commonly referred to as FinTech, is reshaping credit markets. This project, drawing from our research and direct involvement in the international and national policymaking processes, calls into questions dominant assumptions on the role of law in creating credit by carrying out the first comprehensive and comparative study on how law reforms are implemented across over 30 jurisdictions, mostly emerging economies. Common patterns in the strategies and methods deployed by law reformers are isolated to offer a new conceptual paradigm explaining the relationship between legal change and credit creation. To this end, the fundamental tension between access to credit and financial stability is gauged in different economic and legal contexts. Moreover, the project reassesses the relationship between law reforms and technology, as the very need to acquire collateral in order to reduce credit risk is probed by the advent of solutions based on artificial intelligence, smart contracts, and distributed ledger technology. Through this prism, our research indicates new pathways for policymakers to balance the need to expand the credit availability with the necessity of curbing the overaccumulation of debt. Specific suggestions are distilled to inform the debates concerning law reforms in key jurisdictions of the Asia Pacific region, including China, Hong Kong, and Japan. 包容性獲得信貸對減少貧困至關重要。信貸擴張得到雄心勃勃的法律改革的支持，特別是在發展中經濟體。總的來說，這些舉措符合國際法律標準，旨在降低向微型和小型企業，個人以及更普遍的社會正規金融體系剝奪權利的群體提供貸款的風險。顯著數量的司法管轄區已著手改革國內法以促進擔保交易的使用，通過微型和小型企業普遍可用的資產可用作貸款的抵押品，而無需將其交付給債權人。然而，目前尚不清楚這些改革在多大程度上成功地激勵金融家 - 特別是銀行 - 提供新的信貸並促進金融包容性。這一改革努力的有效性進一步受到了迎來新千年曙光的深刻政治，經濟和技術變革的挑戰。具體而言，2007 - 2008年全球金融危機和當前對新興市場穩定性的擔憂表明信貸型經濟體的脆弱性;而金融領域的顛覆性技術 正在重塑信貸市場。 該項目借鑒我們的研究並直接參與國際和國家政策制定過程，通過對30多個司法管轄區如何實施法律改革進行第一次全面和比較研究，提出了關於法律在創造信貸方面的作用的主要假設問。法律改革者所採用的戰略和方法中的共同模式被孤立，以提供一種新的概念範式，解釋法律變革與信用創造之間的關係。為此，在不同的經濟和法律背景下衡量獲得信貸和金融穩定之間的根本緊張關係。此外，該項目重新評估了法律改革與技術之間的關係，因為基於人工智能，智能合約和分佈式賬本技術的解決方案的出現，探索了獲取抵押品以降低信用風險的非常需要。 通過這一棱鏡，我們的研究為政策制定者提供了新的途徑，以平衡擴大信貸可獲得性的必要性和抑制債務過度積累的必要性。提出具體建議，以便為包括中國，香港和日本在內的亞太地區主要司法管轄區的法律改革辯論提供信息。

17607119.label: Realisation of objectives
17607119.value: All seven objectives have been achieved. As noted in mid-term report and in line with the comments received, adjustments to the project were implemented to minimise the impact of COVID-19 on both the scheduled activities and the research without departing from the main objectives. Regarding the activities, traveling has been postponed and concentrated in February-July 2022 (Columbia Law School, World Bank, and UNIDROIT); an additional research trip has been conducted in October 2022 (National University of Singapore, Faculty of Law). This plan was facilitated by the teaching relief and created synergies between ground research, outreach and dissemination activities. Nonetheless, the project had to face the increased costs of traveling, requiring adjustments to the budget allocated for RA, with less than a 20% deviation in compliance with HKU and RGC policies. Throughout the project, the PI and the Co-PI worked in coordination, engaging in research meetings and presenting their research to scholars and policymakers remotely. With respect to the research, the project had to take into account the renewed role of credit, regulation, and technology during COVID-19. Notably, the adverse economic impact of COVID-19 was primarily averted through the implementation of exceptional public measures to ease access to credit, further highlighting the importance of coordination between different branches of the law and the role of technology. As the process of creating credit through law reforms took new, still unfolding, directions, the project continued the planned analysis and monitored the developments in order to produce publications and policy recommendations in areas that became relevant for scholars and policymakers. This approach ensured the attainment of all objectives, as illustrated next. 1. Systematically analyse the processes of reforming secured transactions laws; when those are guided by international soft-laws. The analysis focused on understanding how the impact of exceptional measures and the accelerated digitalisation process changed fundamental variables within the law reform framework. The outcomes of this analysis fed, as planned, the second objective and have been presented at the National University of Singapore, Faculty of Law with a working paper titled “Post-COVID19 Recovery Through Law: Credit, Regulation, and Technology”; whereas the analysis of the connection between international soft-laws and access to credit has been accepted for publication in the Elgar Companion to UNIDROIT (Output 5). 2. Isolate common patterns and key issues affecting the creation of credit through law reforms. Common patterns were isolated, leading to identify two fundamental coordination issues: (i) private law and regulatory rules governing the extension of credit; and (ii) the emergence of ad hoc regulatory regimes governing data and data flows and access to credit policies. The analysis of these issues has been further expanded in Output 1, introducing the notion of Commercial Law Intersection, as well as in Output 3 and in Output 4, offering a comparative analysis of the legal and regulatory reforms promoting inclusive access to credit in China, India, the European Union, and the United States. 3. Shed new light on the tension between access to credit and financial stability. The tension between access to credit and financial stability has been explored through a new analytical framework, developed in three phases and contained in different policy-focused outputs. First, at the beginning of the project, the problematic tension between access to credit and financial stability has been presented at the III Conference on International Coordination of Secured Transactions Law Reforms (February 2020, Cartagena, Colombia), organised by the World Bank Group and by Esternado University. As the research progressed, the CLI theory (Output 1) has shown that the tension between access to credit and financial stability can be ascribed to the lack of coordination between legal and regulatory rules. This new perspective has been presented at the European Central Bank (ECB): Directorate General on Macro-Prudential Supervision Seminar Series, in June 2021. Finally, the applicability of the CLI theory to shed new light on the tension between access to credit and financial stability has been also noted in a policy paper issued by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) of the World Bank Group on the coordination between secured transactions law reforms (enacted to promote access to credit) and prudential regulation (enacted to support financial stability). 4. Assess the impact of new technologies on domestic legal and regulatory frameworks. This assessment has demonstrated that domestic policymakers are establishing their sovereignty on data and data flows through the enactment of new regulatory measures. With specific attention to China, the European Union, and the United States, Output 3 demonstrates that the measures adopted in each jurisdiction reflect patterns of specific cultural, political, economic, and legal characteristics. The result is the emergence of a global data governance framework that is transnational in nature by increasingly fragmented. This analysis complements the findings contained in Output 1 (CLI) and Output 4 (Financial Data Governance), as the implementation of new technologies to promote inclusive access to credit is dependent on the existence of suitable regulatory regimes governing data, domestically and internationally. 5. Distil policy suggestions addressing the needs of jurisdictions in the Asia Pacific region. Policy suggestions have been contained in all published research and presentations. While Output 1 presents a novel solution to resolve coordination issues in any jurisdiction, the other outputs have focused on the Asia Pacific region. Output 2 examines the Japanese experience to indicate that coordination between regulatory measures (public guarantee schemes) and secured transactions law is key to ensuring inclusive access to credit; Output 3 advances a solution to allow the circulation of data within regional boundaries, having in view the regional influence of China; whereas Output 4 presents recommendations in consideration of the needs of China and India to promote digital financial inclusion. Moreover, policy recommendations have been distilled through a series of papers delivered at (i) the UNCITRAL conference (Macau and Shanghai, December 2021) on Conquering the COVID: Enhancing Economic Recovery through Harmonization of Law Governing MSMEs, (ii) APEC meeting (Tokyo, May 2022) on Modernizing Secured Transactions Legal Regimes in APEC Economies through International Instruments and Effective Dispute Resolution Mechanisms; and (iii) IFC conference (Ho Chi Minh, December 2022) on International Best Practices on Secured Transactions Enforcement. 6. Produce a book for publication in a reputable university press or, alternatively, produce two articles for submission to top-tier law journals. Owing to the impact of COVID-19 on the creation of credit and in consideration of the unfolding perils related to excessive indebtedness, it was preferred to produce two substantive articles (over 50 pages each). Both articles (Output 1 and Output 4) were published in the Hastings Law Journal (University of California) which is ranked “A” by the Israeli Inter-university Committee Ranking of Legal Publications of 2021. 7. Produce an additional article for submission to a top-tier law journal. An additional article was published in the Berkeley Technology Law Journal (2023) (Output 3), ranked as “A” by the Israeli Inter-university Committee. Furthermore, an article was published in the Butterworths Journal of International Banking and Financial Law (2021) (Output 2), a journal widely circulating among policymakers and practitioners; and a book chapter will be published in the Elgar Companion to UNIDROIT (Output 5), a point of reference for the study of international instruments promoting access to credit.

17607119.label: Major findings and research outcome
17607119.value: The major findings of this research can be regrouped into three areas. 1. New theory to understand and resolve policy tensions. Output 1 introduced a novel theoretical framework, the CLI theory, to explain why coordination issues between law and regulation emerge and how they can be addressed by lawmakers (domestically and internationally) and interpreters (such as courts and regulators). The theory has been presented at (i) the University College of London, Faculty of Law, and (ii) at the University of Zurich, Faculty of Law, within the University’s Research Priority Programme in Financial Regulation. The potential impact of this contribution is evidenced by the interest of international policymakers - such as the ECB and UNCITRAL - and by the direct citations in three policy papers issued by the World Bank Group. 2. Identification of new dynamics to explain the relationship between technology, regulation, and inclusive access to credit and predict the role of regulation. Output 3 identifies a series of variables to demonstrate that the domestic approaches deployed to govern the digital domain define specific “data governance styles”. Output 4 builds on this understanding to introduce the notion of “financial data governance” defining the intersection between financial regulation, new regulatory policies promoting open banking, and data governance styles. With specific attention to China, India, the EU, and the US, these outputs offer three main contributions by (i) mapping regulatory trajectories vis-à-vis technology, (ii) isolating the impact on financial inclusion and access to credit, and (iii) offering solutions to address international and domestic coordination issues. The research has been presented at (i) the Graduate School of Law of Nagoya University (November 2021); and (ii) the 50th Anniversary Conference of the Ecole Polytechnique of Paris (February 2022). 3. Policy suggestions to promote inclusive access to credit. To complete the analysis with specific policy suggestions, two additional outputs have been completed. Output 2 draws from the Japanese experience to examine how public guarantee programmes affect secured transactions law reforms, suggesting specific solutions to ensure their harmonious interaction. Output 5 examines the role of UNIDROIT instruments to promote access to credit. In particular, this publication indicates that UNIDROIT instruments should further evolve to promote coordination with different areas of the law, such as regulation and insolvency law. These findings and related recommendations have been presented at international conferences with an Asia Pacific focus organised by UNCITRAL and APEC.

17607119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17607119.value: This project has opened new research avenues. First, the connection between pandemic-related regulatory policies and credit creation needs to be further studied as emergency measures are phased out and a new paradigm to promote growth through law emerges. Second, the mechanisms to ensure coordination at the international level among different standard-setters require deeper studies, to suggest a reconfiguration of the current global governance framework addressing the risks of digitalised finance and curbing an uncontrolled expansion of credit. Finally and more broadly, as credit expansion engenders an accumulation of debt, deeper analyses are required to understand the legal and regulatory framework protecting the financial system from impending crises. These aspects should be addressed through new and different research projects. Taking as a point of reference the last area for further development, the PI has prepared and submitted a new GRF proposal (Ref. 17610623) to examine the governance of financial systemic risks vis-à-vis emerging sustainability crises. In consideration of the current banking crises, connected to the expansion of debt, such a proposal complements the findings of this (completed) project on credit creation by looking at systemic risk – an aspect that was not part of this project.

17607119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17607119.value: Inclusive access to credit is of paramount importance to reducing poverty and stimulating economic recovery. Yet, the legal approaches used by policymakers to achieve these goals have evolved. Traditionally, ambitious law reforms have been enacted to support access to credit by facilitating the use of collateral. More recently, policymakers have opted for approaches promoting the extension of credit more rapidly through (i) direct regulatory interventions, and (ii) digital means. Through qualitative and comparative analyses, this project demonstrates that traditional and novel approaches must address a fundamental problem of coordination within and among different branches of the law. Through this prism, it is shown that a lack of coordination between law and regulation fuels the tension between otherwise compatible policy goals, namely, financial stability and access to credit. Moreover, contrary to common perceptions, this research indicates that the diffusion of new technologies has heightened coordination problems, given that new and conflicting regulatory regimes have been enacted in different jurisdictions to govern the data flows underpinning any financial transaction. By providing a novel method to resolve these issues, the research significance has been evidenced by its broad applicability leading to distil specific suggestions, acknowledged internationally organisations and in the Asia-Pacific region.
