17607619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17607619.value: Chronic non-communicable diseases such as diabetes are a pressing issue for society. More than one in ten adults in Hong Kong and mainland China have type 2 diabetes, with another 35% (388 million) in China classified as having pre-diabetes. Lifestyle modification is a key strategy for public health and diabetes control. According to clinical best practice guidelines, the first management step for a person newly-diagnosed with type 2 diabetes is an intensive lifestyle intervention programme of healthy diet, physical activity and smoking cessation. However, these programmes are often designed using standard economic models of behaviour that rely on the assumption of rational decision-making. Sustaining healthy lifestyles choices may be relatively straightforward for the already motivated but is likely to prove difficult for those that have developed chronic health conditions linked to their lifestyle. Insights from behavioural economics have the potential to “nudge” individuals towards behavioural change. Techniques based on behavioural economics have been used to improve adherence to chronic disease management but have not been tested at the early stages of disease, where there lies an opportunity to delay or reverse the onset of type 2 diabetes for newly diagnosed people undergoing the initial lifestyle modification programme. We will conduct a 9-month, three-arm, randomised control trial in adults newly-diagnosed with type 2 diabetes to compare the effectiveness of incentives (designed using insights from behavioural economics) against a control group receiving standard care (risk assessment and management programme). The two intervention arms to encourage healthy lifestyle behaviour over 6-months are: (A) financial incentives alone, or (B) financial plus non-financial incentives. Financial incentives will be framed around loss aversion and the endowment effect. Non-financial incentives will include peer performance feedback, social influence, priming and gamification. Both intervention groups will receive individualised feedback with gradual increases in their step count target each week. We follow-up for 3-months after cessation of incentives to assess the sustainability of lifestyle changes. The primary outcome measure is the change in intra-individual blood sugar (glycaemic control/HbA1c). Secondary outcome measures of lifestyle change include blood lipid levels, weight loss, physical activity, calorie intake, and smoking cessation. Delaying or reversing the onset of chronic disease can deliver downstream health care savings that outweigh the cost of providing financial incentives. This study will provide direct evidence of scalable measures to increase healthy behaviour choices and potentially guide population level strategies for the rest of China. 慢性非傳染性疾病（如糖尿病）是社會面對的一個緊迫問題。在香港和中國大陸，超過十分之一的成年人患有2型糖尿病。在中國，35％的人口（3.88億人）被列為糖尿病的前期患者。 改變生活方式是公共衛生和糖尿病控制的一項重要策略。根據臨床最佳實踐指南，對新診斷的2型糖尿病患者的第一個管理步驟是一個包括健康飲食，運動和戒烟的生活方式強化干預 計劃。然而，這些計劃通常根據以理性決策為前提的標準的經濟行為模型來設計。對於已經有動力的人來說，維持健康的生活方式可能相對簡單，但對於那些已經患有與生活方式相關的慢性病的人來說，這可能會比較困難。 行為經濟學的見解有可能會“推動”個人改變行為。基於行為經濟學的技術已被用來促使病人遵守對慢性病的管理，但尚未在疾病的早期階段測試過。對於參與初始的生活方式改變計劃的新診斷人群，在這個階段有機會延遲或者逆轉2型糖尿病的發作。 我們將對新診斷患有2型糖尿病的成年人進行為期9個月的三臂隨機對照試驗，比較（使用行為經濟學的見解所設計的）激勵措施相對於接受標準治療的對照組（風險評估和管理計劃）的有效性。激勵為期6個月以上的健康生活方式的兩個干預措施是：（A）純財務激勵，（B）財務加非財務激勵。財務激勵措施圍繞“損失厭惡”和“禀賦效應”設計。非財務激勵措施包括同事的績效反饋，社會影響力，事先提供消息和遊戲化。兩個干預組都將收到個性化的反饋，並逐步增加每週的步數目標。激勵措施停止後，我們進行3個月的定期復查，以評估生活方式改變的可持續性。主要療效指標是個體內血糖的變化（血糖控制/ HbA1c）。生活方式改變的次要結果指標包括血脂水平，體重減輕，體力活動，熱量攝取和戒烟。 延緩或者逆轉慢性病的發病，可以節省下游的醫療保健開支，而節省的開支將大於提供財務獎勵的成本。本項研究將提供增加健康行為選擇的可擴展措施的直接證據，並可能為中國其他地區提供人口層面的戰略指導。

17608419.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17608419.value: 年輕英語學習者從小學到中學的積極性動力

17608419.label: Co - Investigator(s)
17608419.value: Dr Gao, Andy Prof Murphy, Victoria

17608419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608419.value: There is a need to better understand the English Language learning motivation (ELLM) of young learners, given the significance of motivation in learning success and the foundational importance of the early years of education, for learning throughout the trajectory. Evidence of motivational decline as learners progress through schooling indicates an important and urgent need to better understand the factors associated with this phenomenon. This study examines young learners’ ELLM and its interplay with instructional factors at an important point of educational transition. This study explores ELLM in the interplay between language attitudes, the learner and the classroom context, specifically seeking to understand the motivational orientations of young learners of English as they transition from primary to secondary schooling. Self-Determination Theory provides the framework for the study, viewing competence, autonomy and relatedness as prerequisites for motivated behaviour, A motivation survey (N≈ 730), administered at the beginning and end of the first year of secondary school, will contribute to understanding the broader motivational context for twelve longitudinal case studies, tracking children’s English Language learning motivational dynamics from their final primary school year to the end of their first year at secondary school. A proficiency test administered to survey participants will provide a direct measure for analyzing survey findings, providing a means of triangulating self-report motivation data. Paired-samples t-test will identify changes in motivational outcomes over the transition period. Single level regression modelling will examine the relative effects of student and classroom variables on ELLM, as well as the nature of the motivation-proficiency relationship in the context of Hong Kong young learners. Drawing on observations, interviews and document analysis, case studies will explore learners’ motivational trajectories (Dörnyei, 2014). Each of the twelve case participants will be interviewed once during their final term of primary school and once during each of the first two terms of year one at secondary school, totalling thirty-six interviews across participants. Network analysis will enable examination of the interplay between the contexts and factors that converge on learners’ motivation (Bliss et al., 1983), integrating qualitative and quantitative data, enabling mapping of networks of individuals, institutions, events and contexts and the connections between these various players (Wellman, 1990; Edwards, 2010). The study is unique in adopting a longitudinal, qualitative approach to understanding young learners’ ELLM at a pivotal stage of education, promising to yield significant insights into a phenomenon of theoretical, empirical, and pedagogical significance. 鑒於強有力的證據表明動機是語言學習成功的關鍵預測因素，我們有必要瞭解和發展與動機策略相關的語言教學實踐。迄今為止，語言學習動機方面的研究主要集中於瞭解學生的動機傾向，而很少關注語言教師的角色以及他們如何理解和處理學生的動機。實際上，語言教師教育方向的學者們已經呼籲進行相關研究，來記錄教師們在教學情境下的實踐以及他們是如何將自己的個人教學理論與相關領域的成熟理論緊密結合的。該方向的語言學習動機研究能夠通過社會文化視角對語言學習動機的理論化作出重要貢獻。 最近出台的微調政策給香港的語言教育帶來了挑戰和機遇。獲得更高的教育水平和更具吸引力的就業機會對於語言能力都有一定的要求，這些要求與不同語言之間的相互影響，給語言教師帶來了機遇和挑戰。在當前的環境下，學生可以將英語或者中文作為學習媒介，有時候在同一所學校學生也可能用中英文結合的方式學習，因此老師們如何理解動機的動態性和情境性以及他們是否能調整教學法來適應不同語言情境下學生們的多樣化需求是一個值得探討並且亟待解決的問題。 本研究旨在探討語言教師對於學生動機提升與發展的認知和實踐。具體而言，橫斷面比較案例研究將用於探究5名香港的中學語言教師在教授通過中文媒介學習的學生和中英文結合來學習的學生的過程中的動機策略。本研究將考察英語教師在教授不同學生群體時是否以及如何調整他們的動機策略以適應學生的語言環境，同時也會探討教師動機策略與學生動機之間的關係。本研究將對學生的語言學習動機進行調查，同時也將對5位參與教師中的每一位分別進行12次結構化課堂觀察（兩個學生組分別6次），以用於記錄教學中的動機策略以及探索它與學生動機之間的關係。刺激回憶法將在課堂觀察後進行，以探究教師的認知和教學決策，這種方式能更好地瞭解他們的教學實踐以及影響實踐的因素。此研究將對語言學習動機理論和研究作出重要貢獻，同時也會對香港及其他背景的教師教育研究領域起到影響作用。

17608519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608519.value: One of the most productive areas of visual perception and visual cognitive neuroscience is the perception of the human face. As a visually-directed species that live socially, understanding how we perceive and recognize faces is of fundamental importance. A dominant concept in face perception is "holistic processing", which is the finding that perceiving a face seems to involve the whole face as a perceptual unit, rather than perceiving the face as a set of individual features. Holistic face processing dominates many theoretical foundations of face perception. In this grant application, however, I will show fundamental problems, both conceptual and empirical, with the concept of "holistic face processing." We will show that different conceptions of holistic face processing are incompatible with each other, and that there is no consistent empirical signature. We will then propose a suite of experiments that will elucidate the ways in which different regions of a face interact perceptually. The work in this grant application should give us a fundamentally new understanding of human face perception, and what differentiates it from other types of object perception. 面孔感知是视觉感知和视觉认知神经科学中最活跃的领域之一。人类是社会性动物且以视觉为导向，理解我们如何感知和识别面孔是至关重要的。面孔感知中一个重要的概念是“整体加工”，即感知面孔是将整个面部作为感知单元，而不是将面部视为多个个体特征的集合。整体加工在面孔感知的诸多理论中占主导地位。然而，在这项新的研究中，我们将讨论 “面孔整体加工”这一概念还存在的理论和实证问题。我们将指出关于面孔整体加工的各个概念并不相容，并且没有一致的实证指标。此外，我们还将提出一系列实验，探究对面孔不同区域的感知是如何相互影响的。这项基金申请的工作将让我们对面孔感知，以及它与其他物体感知的区别有一个全新的理解。

17608519.label: Realisation of objectives
17608519.value: After a challenging start to the project due to the COVID-19 pandemic emerging just as data collection was planned to occur, we managed to make excellent progress as Hong Kong started to open up from 2021. Overall we were able to fully address all three objectives, producing high quality publications and several more papers still under review. Objective 1: Develop a common methodology for the composite task and the part-whole task, then evaluate the extent to which they each measure holistic processing. We conducted several projects to examine the nature of holistic processing as it is assessed by several different tasks, including but not limited to the composite task and the part-whole task. Across several experiments we successfully instantiated a common methodology for assessing holistic processing combines insights from the composite task and part-whole task. This work was written up and submitted to Psychonomic Bulletin and Review, one of the top journals in Experimental Psychology. At time of submitting this report we are preparing it for a 3rd round submission, which we expect to be successful in the near future. We also demonstrated that the concept of holistic face processing is closely related to conscious processing. Using a binocular manipulation, we were able to present some information about the human face to a participant’s visual system but outside their conscious awareness. In doing so we were able to demonstrate that the composite face effect of holistic face processing was reduced but not eliminated. Finally, we studied individual differences in holistic processing, as related to idiosyncratic eye-movement strategies when viewing faces. We found that observers who prefer to look at the eyes when viewing faces show reduced holistic processing when fixating other parts of a face, whereas those who prefer to look away from the eyes show relatively consistent holistic processing regardless of fixation. Objective 2: Determine the detectability of feature changes over differences in distance from attentional focus and/or fixation. We addressed this objective with a study to determine observers’ sensitivity to feature changes in groups of faces. By using face groups we were able to ensure that observers had to spread their attentional focus across the entire face rather than focusing on individual features. We observed that participants had good insight (metacognitive awareness) of their ability to judge the identity of individual faces that were present in the group, but they lacked awareness of their ability to judge whether averages of the original faces were presented as a test stimulus. Objective 3: Map the spatial extent of precision of judgments about pairs of visual stimuli on a face. This objective was designed to investigate how holistic processing would affect identity judgments of visual elements (gabor patches, letters) superimposed on a face. A series of pilot experiments showed that this particular methodology was very difficult to implement in a way that showed them integrated into the face; rather, the visual elements remained perceptually segregated from the face, which meant judgments about them were unaffected by the face. Given this methodological issue, we chose to address this objective in a different way. Using electroencephalography, my former PhD student Haiyang Jin and I measured the influence on the N170, a deflection in electrical potentials caused by face-specific neural populations, of lengthening stimulus presentations. The N170 is known to be a marker of holistic face processing, and so this paradigm allowed us to understand how holistic face processing emerges as a face is first perceived. Using sophisticated statistical methods, we were able to report that the N170 emerges qualitatively complete as soon as it is observable, showing that is distinct from other forms

17608519.label: Major findings and research outcome
17608519.value: 1. Holistic processing is largely, but not completely, reliant on consciousness (Reference 3) 2. Holistic processing can be conceptualised by a single task that integrates very different current paradigms (Reference 5) 3. Holistic processing efficiency varies across the population depending upon the observers' eye-movement strategy for looking at faces (Reference 4) 4. Observers have insights into holistic processing of individual faces, but not processing of averages of groups of faces (Reference 1) 5. Face-specific neural markers of holistic face processing (specifically, the N170 ERP component) arise qualitatively complete as soon as they emerge during perceptual processing (Reference 2).

17608519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17608519.value: We will continue to study the nature of holistic face processing, particularly in terms of individual differences based upon patterns of eye movements. My most recent GRF submission proposes a number of experiments to understand how eye-movement strategies affect face processing, including holistic face processing. In a new project about to start on 1 January 2024, we will extend the work of this grant to understand how familiarity of faces affects face processing. We will study holistic processing of familiar faces as one component of this project.

17608519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17608519.value: The human face is one of the most important visual stimuli that we need to understand. For this reason, the human brain has significant specialised neural regions dedicated to face processing, with associated specialised cognitive processes. In this project, we integrated several different tests of these psychological holistic processes into a new, unified framework. In addition, we studied how conscious and metacognitive processes relate to holistic face processing, and we studied the underlying neural correlates. Taken together, we have made major theoretical advancements in our understanding of human face processing.

17608719.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17608719.value: 1805-15年間廣州及澳門對外漢語的教與學：嚴先生、《漢字西譯》與英美社群

17608719.label: Project Objectives
17608719.value: To conduct, from the perspective of an important teaching tool compiled for Westerners learning Chinese, the first comprehensive enquiry into Barilico de Glemona’s (1648-1704) H-t-s-y, focusing on its impact on the Anglo-American community’s Chinese learning and acquaintance with China. – To provide a detailed investigation into Yen’s copies of H-t-s-y and collect other transcribed copies; describe the circulation of H-t-s-y in 1805-15; give an account of how the copies differ from one another; and accentuate the dictionary’s important value as a teaching tool. – To transcribe the Chinese words and their derivatives transliterated into the Latin alphabet in H-t-s-y back into Chinese; investigate the quotation sources; analyse statistical data on the number of Chinese characters in H-t-s-y; compare H-t-s-y with the dictionaries of Morrison, John Francis Davis (1795-1890) and others; and discuss the learning priorities of the Chinese words and vocabularies set for English learners. To uncover, from the perspective of the history of teaching/learning Chinese as a second language for Westerners, the life of Abel Yen and re-evaluate his performance as an instructor. – To analyse the relation between Yen’s social network and his teaching activities and explain the multiple roles he played in helping Westerners to learn Chinese and understand China at a time when the Qing government prohibited foreigners from learning Chinese. – To emphasise that examining the Anglo-American community’s Chinese-learning activities, with Yen as the core of those activities, can make a breakthrough in addressing the inadequacies of previous discussions adopting the learner’s standpoint alone and adopt a new means of inquiry that focuses on reassessing Yen’s qualities as an instructor. To explore, from the perspective of Chinese-Western contacts in connection with the Canton trade, the learning situations of the British and Americans. – To expand the research domain of the “the British community and Canton trade” by illustrating, through the remarkable examples of the dictionaries of Thomas Manning (1772-1840) and Matthew Raper, Jr. (1740?-1827?), how those who came to China brought about deep cultural understanding and interchange through language learning. – To examine the situation of Benjamin Bowen Carter (1771-1831) as an early American learner of Chinese to use his case to explore how the Americans developed their own ways of learning Chinese. In tangible terms, the above-mentioned objectives will result in two electronic databases and two journal articles. The ultimate objective is a monograph that will give a comprehensive picture of the teaching and learning of CSL and the role it played in early China-West contact.

17608719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608719.value: While we know that traditionally the Chinese valued education and students spent an inordinate amount of time learning to read and write the characters, little is known about how the Anglo-American community who engaged in the Canton trade in the early-19th century study Chinese learned characters. How did these Westerners study the language? Answers to this seemingly simple question involves exploring important academic domains such as the history of Sino-Western relations, Anglo-Chinese translations, the Canton trade and teaching/learning Chinese as a second language. Based on newly discovered sources, the proposed project will shift from the commonly adopted learner’s perspective that highlight the experience of a few well-known learners such as Robert Morrison (1782-1834) to the instructor’s perspective that highlight the teachers and teaching materials used. During the 1805-15 period, Morrison’s Chinese instructor, Abel Yen, actively participated in teaching-related activities through circulation of his manuscripts of the famous Chinese-Latin dictionary Hán-tzé-sin-yih 漢字西譯 (“Hanzi xiyi”, Western Translation of Chinese Characters, H-t-s-y). Yet, while much has been written on Morrison, there is little on Yen. Research on Yen and his manuscripts will shed new light on three largely unexplored issues: H-t-s-y’s impact on Western Chinese learning, the multiple roles Yen played in the language-based instruction of Westerners, and more importantly, the differences and similarities of the learning activities of the community at that time. By focusing on Yen and H-t-s-y, this project will correct the hitherto neglect of the role of the Chinese instructors and in the process yield new and significant insights on Sino-Western relations. In accordance with those concerns, the project’s three objectives are (1) to explore, from the perspective of the educational value of teaching material, the “Chinese elements” of H-t-s-y; (2) to disclose, from the perspective of the history of teaching Westerners Chinese, details of Yen’s life and reassess his teaching activities; and (3) to broaden, from the perspective of Chinese-Western contacts, the scope of investigation into British learning of Chinese and launch the first inquiry into how the Americans conduct such learning in the early nineteenth century. An annotated electronic version of H-t-s-y will be compiled, with transliterated Latin entries transcribed back into Chinese and source information provided, and an electronic database of selected Chinese characters, examples and derivatives to allow comparison with the features of other contemporary dictionaries. As well as providing a platform for international collaborative research, these electronic resources will be immensely useful for teaching and research purposes.

17608719.label: Realisation of objectives
17608719.value: 1. In meeting the first objective, this project achieved highly satisfactory results. (1) Regarding the investigation of H-t-s-y, the PI had consulted two transcribed copies available online at Brown University and one copy available at the Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin. Due to Covid-19, the proposed visit to Europe was cancelled. An overseas research assistant was employed, and with the assistance of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (RAS), three handwritten copies of H-t-s-y housed in RAS and the British Library were duplicated and thus the problem regarding the collection of first-hand sources was all solved. Based on a detailed investigation of Carter’s Dictionarium, Manning’s Dictionary (both transcribed by Yen), and other archival documents, the PI re-sharpened our image of Carter as an American pioneer in Chinese studies, re-evaluated Yen’s roles as advisor, teacher and translator to Westerners, and explored the significance of these important manuscripts in the history of China-West cultural relations. (2) As anticipated by the PI, the first task necessary to achieve this sub-objective was to make a comparative study of the knowledge about Chinese culture incorporated in H-t-s-y and Morrison’s Dictionary, which is the best way of investigating what was deemed to be the crucially important information about China that the dictionary compilers in different generations expected Western learners of Chinese to know. The PI had pursued two lines of inquiry: (i) an investigation into the transcription and circulation of H-t-s-y in Canton and gave an account of how the manuscript copies differ from one another. The two copies transcribed by Yen were selected for a detailed comparison; (ii) an analysis of the “Chinese elements” of H-t-s-y by examining its entries and illustrative quotations (in Latin transliteration) and investigating their sources. The PI believes that only through such an investigation can we clearly understand what the selected Chinese expressions meant to Western learners, and what they had to say about Chinese thought, culture, and social customs in those days. 2. Regarding the second objective: This project achieved highly satisfactory results in the key issues under study, and the PI gained deeper insights into the objective. (1) As the PI has shown, Yen was not only an instructor who taught Mandarin, but also the transcriber and circulator of copies of both volumes of H-t-s-y, which he used as important teaching materials. He was actually the center of a social network comprising his students and their companions, the Catholic missionary circle, his Catholic subordinates, and himself. In addition, the dictionaries belonging to Carter, Manning, Alexander Pearson, and John F. Elphinstone were all transcribed by Yen, and these copies were further circulated among other members of the community. It can thus be said that Yen was a key resource for Anglophone students of Chinese in 1805–1809, a period which the Qing government prohibited unauthorized Chinese subjects from teaching Westerners. (2) Based on Morrison’s repetition of information he received from George Thomas Staunton, a number of researchers think that Yen’s level of Chinese proficiency was not high. However, the PI believes that the discussion of Yen in this project has demonstrated the importance of looking at a question from a different standpoint, or from reversed standpoints, in cross-cultural exchanges. As an experienced instructor, Yen was able to translate a document from Latin into Chinese for Carter, and he was able to transcribe the Chinese characters in the copies of H-t-s-y he prepared for his students. In addition to using H-t-s-y to teach his students, he also helped Carter in a translation task to prepare a Chinese remonstrance to be submitted to the Qing governor-general at Canton. The process whereby the remonstrance was translated sheds light on Yen’s multifunctional career as a language instructor and Chinese proficiency being a means to help with China-America diplomatic relations. 3. With respect to the third objective, this project achieved highly satisfactory results. (1) Regarding the life of Manning and Raper and their interest in Chinese, a synthesized understanding was obtained from the first- and secondhand historical documents which had been collected. Raper’s Dictionary and Manning’s Dictionary are critical documentary evidence which show how Raper and Manning and their English contemporaries, especially those who had stayed or lived in Canton, learned Chinese or were involved in the promotion of Chinese language. The PI emphasizes that the development of sinology involves not only sinologists, but also a group of people with diversified background surrounding them, whose contributions in collecting, organizing and circulating literature, promoting and exchanging knowledge of sinology, and bringing together groups of people with common interests should not be overlooked. It can be said that, from Manning’s Dictionary to Raper’s Dictionary to Morrison’s Dictionary, no matter in terms of Chinese learning or the development of British sinology, it is a stage of “inheritance and innovation” which deserves our further investigation. (2) Until recently, it was believed that the Americans were uninterested in studying Chinese at the beginning of the 19th century. However, the discovery of the manuscripts and documents which belonged to Carter disproves this assumption and at the same time offers an American perspective on teaching and learning Chinese as a foreign language at Canton. The PI had investigated Carter’s study of written Chinese and his reading of Chinese literature, discussed his study of the spoken language, and traced how his interest in learning Chinese developed from an intellectual curiosity to his subsequent advocating the use of Chinese proficiency to protect the American interest in China. The PI believes that Carter is a pioneer in Chinese studies and therefore the birthplace of American Chinese Studies was Canton, and not New Haven, as many accounts have it. In addition, Carter’s experience of studying Chinese helps us to better understand not only the British experience by way of contrast, but also early Sino-American (cultural) relations. 4. The fourth objective of this project also achieved highly satisfactory results. (1) This report presents the fruits of about four years of the PI’s research on the early history of Anglo-American community learning Chinese in the context of early China-West relations. The PI explored, from the perspective of Chinese-Western contacts connected with the Canton trade, the learning situations of the Anglophone students. By analysing the instructor-learner-peer relationships, the PI argues that the British and American learners did not form a community; rather, what united them was their use of H-t-s-y and their reliance on Yen for assistance with their studies. (2) My Brill monograph was published in 2021. Chapters 3 and 4 of the book focus on the investigation into H-t-s-y as well as the details of the teaching and learning of Chinese among the Chinese instructors and their Anglophone students. The PI believes that these two consecutive chapters can better focus on the new research findings achieved in this project than two individual journal articles and can have a greater impact on the academic world. In addition, the electronic version of Raper’s Dictionary collated as part of the research plan, will be appeared in the PI’s Wix site (https://www.teaching-learning-chinese-Canton-Macao-1805-15.hku.hk/) by August 2023. Finally, it is also the PI’s plan to submit a journal article, with an examination of Raper’ Dictionary as the focus, to Newsletter for Research in Chinese Studies for publication recently as an additional research output of the present project.

17608719.label: Major findings and research outcome
17608719.value: (1) Regarding the investigation of H-t-s-y: the PI made a detailed comparison of some commonly used Chinese characters in Carter’s Dictionarium, John Francis Davis’s A Dictionary of the most useful words of the Chinese language and Morrison’s Dictionary, inclusive of their meanings, related examples and extended meanings, and got an in-depth understanding of the learning priorities of the Chinese words and vocabularies set for English learners. [Monograph chapter 3, Public Lecture, Hawai‘i paper] (2) Regarding Abel Yen’s life, his social network and his roles as a language teacher: the PI had ascertained from Manning’s letters that his Chinese name was 嚴本明, a discovery conducive to further investigation of his life. By exploring the historical documents from Carter, Morrison and Manning, it is found that Yen was the most respected of the Chinese instructors at his time in Canton. Carter’s documents show that he and Yen assisted the US Consulate to translate the first official document in Chinese to be presented to the Qing officials. [Monograph chapter 4, AOS paper] (3) Regarding the topic of Chinese-language education among Canton’s British community: the PI had conducted a detailed investigation into what and how the community learned, how they endeavoured to disseminate new knowledge to their countrymen and European societies, and to investigate their contributions to the development of Britain’s Sinology and the history of Chinese-language education among Westerners. [Monograph, Public Lecture, Hawai‘i and AOS paper] (4) Regarding how Carter’s case helps to re-interpret America’s tradition of Chinese studies and Sino-American relations: the PI had launched an enquiry into the multilingual curriculum Carter met with, and the relationship between his studying Chinese and protection of the American interests in China. [Monograph chapter 3-4, AOS paper] (5) Regarding the academic significance and value of the study of the history of teaching and learning Chinese as a secondary language (TLCSL): The study not only helps to reconstruct the history of TLCSL, but it also interconnects four major research domains—Sino-Western diplomatic relations, the Canton trade, the propagation of Christianity, and the history of cross-cultural translation—so as to re-portray the history of China-West relations in the early 19th century. [Monograph, Public Lecture, Hawai‘i and AOS paper] (6) A collated electronic version of Raper’s Dictionary to be appeared in my Wix site will fully illustrate the value and significance of this version as the first complete Chinese-English dictionary in history.

17608719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17608719.value: (1) The PI believes that there are still a certain number of historical materials on teaching and learning Chinese preserved in other libraries and academic institutions all over the world (especially in North America), and that only by continuing to track down and collate these texts can we enhance our knowledge of this topic. (2) Through this research project, the history and process of the Chinese instructors’ contacts with the Anglo-American learners is well understood. But the history of their contacts with other European learners is still little known, and this question will be explored in subsequent research. (3) The study of the history of American sinology should be considered against the background of the history of China-US relations as a whole and Carter’s story forces a rewriting of that history in its early stage. A further attempt to break through the barrier between the study of language and the study of history and to include in its discussions various academic topics, such as cross-cultural interactions, Americans’ acquaintance with China and the Chinese language, translation of language and culture, and dissemination and exchange of knowledge will definitely attract the attention of a wide range of global readers.

17608719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17608719.value: The topic of Chinese-language education among Canton’s Anglo-American community around the beginning of the 19th century involves important research domains including Sino-Western diplomatic relations, the Canton trade, the propagation of Christianity, and the history of cross-cultural translation, all of which have long absorbed international researchers. This project focuses on the investigation into teaching and learning materials, including (1) dictionaries (especially Hán-tzé-sin-yih [Western translation of Chinese characters]), textbooks, reading materials and reference books used by learners; (2) their letters, notes and remarks concerned with Chinese-language education and knowledge about China; and (3) the works they (especially the Chinese instructor Abel Yen) compiled or published for educational purposes, popularizing Chinese, and propagating knowledge about Chinese studies. In other words, the project attempts to sort out the historical documents regarding “teaching and learning” mentioned above during the Canton System period, including those related to Chinese and European languages, to make enquiries into the issues such as what and how the community learned, how they transformed old knowledge and brought about innovations, how they endeavoured to disseminate new knowledge to their countrymen and European societies, and to investigate their achievements in the development of Sinology and the history of Chinese-language education among Westerners.

17608819.value: To document, describe, and compare standardization processes in the English-lexifier contact languages (AECs) of West Africa. To analyze and theorize these processes in aspects like the development of orthographies, lexical modernization, and grammatical description, as well as the uses of the AECs for education, government, in the media, digital communication, and the entertainment industry. 17608819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608819.value: This project studies processes of linguistic standardization in Nigerian Pidgin (80 million speakers), Cameroon Pidgin (10 million) and Krio (Sierra Leone, 5 million). These African English-lexifier contact languages (AECs) are mutually intelligible varieties and have more than a hundred million speakers. They share common origins and the bulk of their vocabulary is derived from English. Contact languages emerge in multilingual societies and often have humble beginnings as mediums of communication outside of the home. They therefore suffer from negative language attitudes and are often marginalized by official language policies. Calls by academics and language activists to standardize these languages and introduce them into schools as mediums of instruction or promote them to official functions in government and administration have therefore gone unheeded. The three AECs have nevertheless seen a dramatic expansion in speaker numbers and in their social functions in the last few decades. This has gone hand in hand with their use in new domains once reserved for English or other African languages. The three AECs are now increasingly used in TV shows and radio programs, they are widely used in the burgeoning pop music and movie industries of West Africa, and have penetrated the sphere of writing through the proliferation of vernacular (unstandardized) orthographies. The key objective of this project is to understand how self-authored and decentralized (hence not state-led) processes of standardization have accompanied the expansion of the social functions of the AECs in the three countries. This includes analysing bottom-up initiatives in the codification of orthography, lexicon, and grammar. It also includes looking at organized and unorganized uses of the AECs in education, as well as the emergence of the AECs as languages of the media, digital communication, and popular culture. Further, it entails the study of the actors, institutions, ideologies, and discourses underlying processes of standardization. This project seeks to achieve significant empirical and theoretical advances in the study of contact languages, as well as in knowledge exchange and teaching. 此項目研究尼日利亞皮欽語（8000萬使用者）、喀麥隆皮欽語（1000萬使用者）和塞拉利昂克里奧爾語（500萬使用者）的語言標準化進程。這些以英語為基礎的非洲接觸語言 (African English-lexifier contact languages or AECs) 是能相互理解的語言變體，擁有超過一億使用者。接觸語言出現在多語言社會中，通常起源於家庭之外、較為卑微的交流媒介。因此，人們對接觸語言持較負面的態度，官方的語言政策亦經常將它們邊緣化。亦因此，一些將接觸語言標準化及列為學校的教學語言、將其推廣到政府和行政部門作為官方職能的訴求，並未獲得重視。 然而，這三種AECs在使用者數量和社會功能方面都在急劇擴張中。這是由於它們在新通訊領域被頻密地使用著。這些語言現在越來越多地出现在電視節目和廣播節目中，並被廣泛用於西非的流行音樂和電影業。人們還通過非標準化拼寫將這些語言滲透到寫作領域。 本研究的主要目的是了解自我編寫和去中心化（非國家主導）的標準化過程如何伴隨著此三國的AECs在社會功能方面的擴展。這包括分析AECs自下而上的正寫法、詞彙和語法的編纂，觀察AECs在教育中的有組織及無組織的使用，以及檢視媒體、電子通信和流行文化採用AECs的時序。此外，本研究還會對標準化過程中的參與者、制度、意識形態和話語作出分析。總而言之，本研究旨在推動接觸語言研究的實驗方法和理論方面的進展，並為知識交流和教學方面作出重要的貢獻。

17608819.label: Realisation of objectives
17608819.value: The present project successfully investigated bottom-up standardisation processes in the English-lexifier contact languages of West Africa (also known as West African Pidgin). The main objective to compare, describe and typologise processes of standardisation could be achieved in spite of formidable challenges due to COVID-19. In spite of the restrictions on travelling it was nonetheless possible to do field research in Ghana. The body of data collected in Ghana was compared with the situation of standardisation of Swahili in Kenya and East Afric. The PI conducted in-depth research in Ghana in which the role of Ghanaian Pidgin was investigated through linguistic data collection and sociolinguistic interviews with stakeholders and users of the language ranging from all walks of life (e.g., teachers, pupils, students, traders, linguists, policy-makers). The P I also conducted research in the Ghanaian music scene in order to understand better how the proliferation of Ghanaian pidgin English as a language of entertainment culture, as well as in advertising has impacted views about the language. Further, the PI also travelled extensively within the country to all the major Ghanaian cities in order to understand how far the language was spoken geographically and how much it had penetrated diverse social formations. Although research could not be conducted in Nigeria and Cameroon as planned -in the former country due to the Covid emergency and in the latter due to an ongoing armed conflict in the part of the country where pidgin English is spoken- it was nonetheless possible to draw on the extensive data that the PI had already collected in the two countries in a preceding GRF project. This data was complemented through online interviews and the work of research assistants on the ground who collected data and conducted interviews in these two countries. Overall, a body of data was collected that gives a sufficiently elaborate picture of the current process of expansion and bottom-up standardisation of Pidgin across West Africa as witnessed in Ghana, Nigeria and Cameroon. The project was used to train undergraduate students as outlined in the objectives. Students participated in data curation, worked on elements of the project description for an upcoming website, and some of the findings were fed into a student-led documentary film production realised in 2020. Results from the project also fed substantially into teaching units of an HKU Common Core Course newly developed by the PI (The Life and Death of Language, CCGL9024). The significant publications that have resulted from this project have contributed to the ongoing consolidation of the study of West African Pidgin and the growing perception that these languages constitute serious objects of study besides varieties of colonial languages spoken in the region as well as other African languages. This is important due to the detrimental effects of educational policies in the region that are almost exclusively based on the former colonial languages incl. English.

17608819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17608819.value: Several significant findings emerged from the research and data collected. One major finding of this project is that West African Pidgin has expanded considerably more in terms of its speaker numbers across the region, far beyond what was thought. Languages like Ghanaian Pidgin, Nigerian Pidgin, and Cameroon Pidgin have conquered new domains in the media, the radio, private TV stations, and the pop music scene that exponential growth rates. The PI could establish, for example, that Ghanaian Pidgin is spoken to a much greater extent than hitherto described in the literature. The languages has spread beyond the coastal zone where the language first came to be used into the inland. Against all expectation, the languages is also regularly used in families among siblings in particular, hence for horizontal but not necessarily for vertical communication with parents and caretakers. Another finding is that these languages still suffer from perceptions that construct them as inferior varieties of English. There is therefore a tension between their actual use as languages of wider communication and the language ideologies that shape views about them. A further finding is that there is a great reluctance by educators and administrators to acknowledge the exponential growth of these languages and their potential to serve as languages of instruction, political communication, and administrative use. The discrepancy between the actual distribution of these languages and the language ideologies that demote them is therefore growing. Bottom-up language standardisation through accommodation of individual speakers within their everyday social networks, through the vibrant pop music and movie industry will therefore continue. In view of the demographic and urbanisation dynamics of West Africa, it is very likely that Pidgin will become one of the most widely spoken languages of the southern hemisphere in the next few decades.

17608819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17608819.value: This project has great potential for further development and complementary research. The PI has applied for a major GRF grant in the current exercise in order to look at the processes that were described in this project in comparison with other highly dynamic and growing languages of the southern hemisphere, namely Swahili, Hindustani, and Malay/Indonesian. This project has been instrumental in identifying the key factors and hypotheses that have fed into the current GRF application. The high number of significant publications in high impact journals and edited books with prestigious publishers has also assured a growing visibility of the research topic and the PI. It is therefore very likely that the future will bring new research opportunities and a consolidation of this research field within the broader area of the study of World Englishes and language contacts studies.

17608819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17608819.value: This project looks at the evolution of the group of contact Englishes commonly known under the name (West African) Pidgin. The activities conducted under this project involved research in Ghana, Nigeria, and Cameroon. The project is particularly interesting and significant because of the galloping demographic growth in these countries, the high rate of urbanisation, and the general economic vibrancy of the populations in these countries. This has led to equally exponential growth rates in the speakers of these languages. The project managed to establish out that the expansion of these languages is much more substantial than expected. Speakers begin acquiring these languages at an earlier age than before, are found in all social classes, and the languages are spoken in a larger geographical region than assumed. There has also been a significant bottom-up convergence of these varieties which are mutually intelligible. The entertainment industry, and popular music in particular, has been crucial in this regard. As a consequence, a linguistic space has emerged in which Pidgin has become the largest international language of West Africa. This project offers exciting possibilities for further research on one of the most dynamic languages of the 21st-century.

17608919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17608919.value: Research into the history of the ancient qin, a type of silk-stringed zither, has been completely reformed by several ground-breaking excavations in recent decades. The first of these came in 1973, with the unprecedented unearthing of an ancient specimen radically different in design to the Medieval or modern version, being divided into five registers, each with a separate shape and function, rather than the oblong-shaped unified whole of the Medieval qin furnished with thirteen hui indicating the acoustic nodes. Conservative resistance to paradigm change meant that this discovery and a subsequent four others were all hived off as “Chu” qin and regarded as an evolutionary dead end separate from the qin of the Central Plains that eventually developed with barely a change into the Medieval qin. Excitingly, in only the last three years, the picture has been transformed yet again with the excavation of qin in Haihun and Guojiamiao, and I was lucky to be part of these investigations. Five qin were unearthed from Haihun and one from Guojiamiao that together have conclusively demonstrated that the ancient qin spanned a period of approximately 650 years from c.700 BCE onwards and that it was played across ancient China. Much remains to be done. Poor practice at earlier sites has meant that artefacts have not been well preserved, and new protocols are urgently required to ensure this does not continue. Particularly questionable techniques are over-zealous dehydration and the reassembling of fragmentary parts. To make a fuller account of not just the surface appearance of a qin, but also its internal structure and composition, digital imaging techniques are required, such as CAT scanning, x-ray, endoscopy, and infra-red photography, as well as dendrochronology. A closer assessment of qin in relation to other grave goods and the tomb occupants themselves will put all items into appropriate cultural contexts, whilst text recorded on bamboo slips and other media will be read and its relevance assessed. The aim is to move towards a comprehensive history of ancient qin music and its relationship to the culture in which it survived, entirely written from a personal and critical experience of all relevant first-hand sources. This paradigm will also be designed not to repeat past mistakes, but instead structured so as to absorb new discoveries, the whole effort embedded in a desire to promote good archaeological practice for the sake of future generations.

17608919.label: Realisation of objectives
17608919.value: Following multiple visits to Liu He’s tomb and careful sifting through some three thousand fragments of lacquerware unearthed there and matching between them, a total of five qin could be assembled. Together with the earliest qin specimens found in Guojiamiao, these five have allowed the entire timeframe of qin evolution to be significantly extended at either end, and their structure fits perfectly into my paradigm of Type I and Type II qin as outlined in my previous research articles. Detailed observation indicates that these five from Liu He’s tomb were not made at the same time. Some, if not all, were likely made when Liu He was Prince of Changyi in Shandong instead of during his short sojourn as Marquis of Haihun in Nanchang in Jiangxi, which is where he died and his tomb is to be found. These newly discovered examples not only contribute significantly to the overall paradigm of ancient qin evolution but also furnish crucial evidence that allows modern scholarship to reevaluate Medieval assessments of the form of the ancient qin. Close scrutiny of the only source that was claimed as contemporary to the ancient qin and used to support these assessments reveals that it is in fact a late Ming dynasty forgery. This discovery coupled with archaeological evidence proves that the ancient qin cannot be regarded as a regional variant found in the territory of Chu. Apparent discrepancies between archaeological evidence and literary sources are thus persuasively and conclusively resolved. The ancient and classical qin can now be demonstrably regarded as belonging to the same continuum. Between the most recent ancient qin of the first century CE and the oldest classical qin of the seventh century CE, a connection that spans the lack of excavated specimens between these two dates can now be forged. The two seemingly useless indentations characteristically found at the waist of the classical qin are now found to be presaged by equivalent structures on the ancient qin. Preservation of ancient artifacts is a moral duty that researchers owe future generations. With this in mind, I went to the Jingzhou Artefact Preservation Centre where all the specimens of ancient qin have been assembled and agreed with a team of conservators and archaeologists in establishing protocols regarding how these instruments should best be preserved. Particular attention was paid to issues of dehydration processes and ensuring that unearthed specimens were kept intact and not subject to unnecessary repair, all accomplished within the paradigm of mininum intervention for maximum impact.

17608919.label: Major findings and research outcome
17608919.value: Incorporation of recently discovered qin into my previous paradigm of qin evolution has met with a perfect match and demonstrated its efficacy as well as expanding its timeframe significantly at either end. This is fully discussed in “Chapter 2: Archaeology: Truths Gradually Revealed” of my book Dragon’s Roar. All excavated qin specimens conform to the same fundamental pattern, whether inside or outside the territory of Chu, which means that it does indeed represent the paradigm of the ancient qin and is not a regional abberation. This means that there is a significant contradiction between classical text and excavated example, and the texts, which were formed in the Medieval period, are therefore rendered unreliable. This is fully discussed in my book chapter entitled “Musical Archaeology and the Prehistory of Chinese Music” in The Oxford Handbook of Music in China and the Chinese Diaspora. The most recent example of the ancient qin dates to the first century CE and the earliest classical qin to the seventh century CE. Through comparing them, a striking link between them is to be observed to the extent that both examples can be situated at different locations along a continuum. This is fully discussed in “Chapter 6: No Longer an End Without a Journey” of Dragon’s Roar. Following my visit to the Jingzhou Artefact Preservation Centre and discussions with the conservation team and archaeologists there, new protocols has been established to preserve their assembled corpus of qin in their excavated state without applying reconstructive work.

17608919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17608919.value: Having clarified the structure of ancient qin, vestigial elements of it may nonetheless be retained in the Medieval qin. Having surveyed approximately twenty editions of “The Manual of Qin Types of Past Dynasties” from the early Ming to the late Qing dynasties, a few qin templates, for example the one labelled “Boya”, still retain the ancient silhouette. The most immediate and important characteristic of the Boya template is the absence of hui. In addition, by comparison from the Classical qin where the tail and upper bouts of the instrument form continuous straight lines, the tail is noticeably narrower here and manifests itself as a separate section or “register”. This notion of being divided into registers as opposed to consisting of a unified whole, as is the case with the Classical qin, is carried on higher up on the instrument. Is this simply a coincidence? Or can they be traced back to the Han dynasty? This is a question for future research.

17608919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17608919.value: This project has significantly expanded the potential evolutionary timeframe of ancient qin. In 2016, excavation of a qin from a tomb in Guojiamiao dated to c.700 BCE added almost 400 years onto the early period covered by the project, while five qin unearthed since 2015 from a tomb in Haihun—whose occupant Liu He was buried in 59 BCE—have increased the span by more than a century at the other end. A total of eleven qin covering approximately 650 years formed the raw research material, and detailed examination of these newly discovered specimens has now been accomplished. Precise chronology of the evolution of the ancient qin from the early Eastern Zhou (770–256 BCE) to the Western Han (206 BCE–24 CE) has been carried out, and newly excavated specimens, particularly those of the Liu He tombs, are inserted into the scheme. Apparent discrepancies between archaeological and literary evidence from the Chinese classics have been resolved, for example, whether they had arisen due to geographical factors or cultural delineation, and artifact and text can now be used in conjunction. This rational interpretation enables enhanced understanding of the relationship between the ancient qin and Classical qin.

17609419.label: Project Objectives
17609419.value: To provide a systematic comparative review of the public policy exception and how its indeterminacy in definition hinder the formation of an integrated economic region under the BRI. To contribute to the international comparative literature on harmonization of public policy in international commercial arbitration in context of the BRI Asia with (a) EU and (b) OHADA as the comparators, both of which adopted a “regional public policy exception”. To study the theoretical foundation for harmonizing the public policy exception, with reference to (a) “Three Metaphors of Norm Migration” of international legal norms proposed by Roderick A. Macdonald; and (b) the competing paradigms of “seat theory” and “delocalization theory” of international commercial arbitration. To examine dispute resolution circumstances among BRI Asia nations, and formulate recommendations of framing those circumstances for the reform of the “regional public policy exception” in context of BRI Asia, with China taking the lead.

17609419.label: Realisation of objectives
17609419.value: In the original GRF research proposal, the PI set forth four project objectives. Despite facing unforeseen global challenges, the project has achieved significant milestones, though with some adaptations in methodology and execution. First, the project has successfully conducted a comprehensive comparative review of the public policy exception in the context of the BRI. This was accomplished through extensive doctrinal research and analysis of relevant international arbitration laws and practices in BRI Asia. The review highlighted the indeterminacy of the public policy exception, underscoring its impact on economic integration under the BRI. Second, the project has made a significant contribution to the international comparative literature on the harmonization of public policy in international commercial arbitration. Comparisons with the European Union (EU) and the Organization for the Harmonization of Business Law in Africa (OHADA) provided valuable insights. While in-person workshops with European and African legal experts were limited due to travel restrictions, virtual conferences and online collaborations proved to be effective alternatives. Third, the theoretical exploration of harmonizing the public policy exception has been conducted rigorously and thoroughly, with particular reference to the "Three Metaphors of Norm Migration" and the competing "seat theory" and "delocalization theory." The PI has successfully navigated these complex theories and contextualized them within the BRI framework. Fourth, the examination of dispute resolution circumstances among BRI Asia nations has faced some logistical challenges due to the COVID-19 travel restrictions. However, the PI creatively adapted by utilizing innovative digital methodologies and virtual platforms. While physical field visits were not feasible, virtual interactions with the local legal experts in the BRI jurisdictions provided rich information, enabling the formulation of comprehensive recommendations for reforming the regional public policy exception. To be more specific, the PI has initially planned several research trips or field visits to selective leading arbitration jurisdictions in context of BRI Asia (e.g., Beijing, Shenzhen, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Dubai). These trips were integral to the project's original design, intended to gather firsthand insights and data from key BRI Asia jurisdictions. However, due to the global COVID-19 pandemic, travel restrictions were imposed, making overseas travels and physical attendance at international research conferences unfeasible. This unprecedented situation significantly limited the PI's ability to conduct these planned field visits. Consequently, the budget allocated for overseas travel and conferences remained largely unutilized. In response to the constraints imposed by the COVID-19 pandemic, the PI took proactive steps to adapt to these constraints and adeptly pivoted to alternative methods of engagement and research, reallocating resources to enhance digital research tools and access to virtual conferences and online databases. Although extensive travel outside of Hong Kong for field trips and research visits was not feasible, the PI actively participated in numerous virtual conferences closely aligned with the project's theme. These digital platforms facilitated valuable interactions and exchanges with experts and practitioners from various BRI jurisdictions, effectively compensating for the inability to conduct in-person visits. Furthermore, the PI's esteemed position as a listed arbitrator in several leading arbitration institutions across key BRI Asia jurisdictions, including Beijing, Shenzhen, and Hong Kong, significantly bolstered the research. This prominent role enabled the PI to maintain and deepen connections with arbitration experts, not only within these cities but also in other critical jurisdictions like Singapore and Dubai. These connections and the insights gained through virtual engagements have proven instrumental in overcoming the limitations brought about by the travel restrictions, ensuring the continuity and richness of the research despite the unprecedented global challenges. In addition, the PI has benefited tremendously from the GRF budget item, “Research Assistants”. The budget for hiring research assistants (RAs) has been deployed effectively in the sense that the RAs helped a lot in collecting literature in the initial period of research. The RAs were also critical in the footnote checking and bibliography compilation stage when the manuscripts were completed to be submitted to journals and book publishers. However, it is worth mentioning that the PI had a big eye surgery in November 2022. Before the eye surgery, there were eye discomforts and pains due to the diagnoses of macular hole, starting in the second half of 2022. The eye pains and disease had prevented the PI from hiring more RAs and working with RAs in the later stage of the project. To conclude, the PI is happy to submit that despite the challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic and the PI’s own health conditions, the research objectives have all been satisfactorily achieved, and the research funds are properly used. Major findings and research outcomes arising out of the GRF project will be summarized below, under Section 6.

17609419.label: Major findings and research outcome
17609419.value: First, an important finding is the need for harmonizing the public policy exception in arbitral enforcement in the BRI Asia. This project finds that there is a significant level of harmonization in arbitration laws among BRI countries, primarily due to the widespread adoption of the New York Convention and the UNCITRAL Model Law. Such harmonization would enhance legal certainty and investor confidence, crucial for the success of the BRI. This project unveils the necessity of harmonization of legal norms from the dual standpoints of a normative jurisprudential perspective, and the practical benefits of enhancing commercial efficiency under the BRI. Second, the project envisages the future development in terms of the possible substantive contents of a regional or transnational public policy exception. With reference to similar harmonization efforts of the EU and the OHADA, this project proposes a “negative list” approach could be utilized in establishing the harmonized public policy exception. Third, this project unveils China’s pivotal role in the proposed harmonization initiative. As the leading nation in the BRI, China’s approach to arbitration, particularly its stance on the public policy exception is found to have a substantial influence on the overall effectiveness of dispute resolution within the BRI framework. The changing power dynamics of the Asian region developing under the BRI could also be analyzed as forming the catalyst for China’s increased role in pioneering international legal norms. Fourth, this research finds the correlation between the developmental stages of arbitration and the judicial interpretation of the public policy exception in BRI jurisdictions. While most countries are member states of the New York Convention, the actual enforcement records show variations. This project reveals that the judicial approach to the public policy exception is closely correlated with each jurisdiction’s stage of development in arbitration practices. This insight is crucial for understanding the nuances and complexities of arbitration enforcement in the BRI context. This project's findings not only benefits China but also have far-reaching effects on the global arbitration landscape. The research further lays a solid foundation for ongoing dialogue and development towards a more harmonized and effective legal framework for arbitral enforcement within and beyond BRI Asia. These findings offer valuable insights for policymakers, legal practitioners, and scholars, contributing significantly to the discourse on legal harmonization and economic integration in Asia.

17609419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17609419.value: This research opens several avenues for future exploration, particularly in the dynamic and evolving context of the BRI. One potential direction is the deepening engagement with the spirit of the New York Convention (NYC), particularly in promoting and facilitating the enforcement of arbitral awards within the BRI context. This would involve researching how BRI countries can align their arbitration practices more closely with the NYC's principles, ensuring more efficient and consistent enforcement of arbitral awards. Another area for future research is the reconciliation of arbitral awards with cross-border mediation. Because of the recent enactment of the Singapore Mediation Convention, there emerge a number of cross-border mediation enforcement in light of the BRI context. The exploration of how cross-border mediation enforcement interacts with arbitration will become an important research area. This future research would propose ways to reconcile these two dispute resolution mechanisms within the BRI framework, ensuring that arbitral awards resulting from combined arbitration-mediation processes are effectively recognized and enforced. These prospective research paths not only promise to extend the academic discourse but also have the potential to offer insights for policymakers and legal practitioners engaged in the BRI.

17609419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17609419.value: This project delves into how Asian countries involved in China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) handle international commercial disputes through arbitration, focusing particularly on the complex issue of ‘public policy exception’. The New York Convention and the UNCITRAL Model Law have harmonized arbitration laws, yet “public policy” remains a grey area. As each country has its own different and varied interpretations of this term, it leads to unpredictable outcomes and higher transaction costs in resolving cross-border business disputes, which is against the BRI’s goal of economic integration and commercial certainty. Drawing upon experiences of the EU and OHADA, this study proposes ways to make the interpretations of "public policy" more consistent across countries, and further advocates for the creation of a “transnational public policy”. It argues that the BRI provides a golden opportunity for China to take the lead in considering the possibility of harmonizing the public policy exception in international commercial arbitration within the Asian Belt and Road nations. This study is significant not just in an academic sense but also practically, offering guidance to legal professionals and policymakers in fostering a unified economic region across Asia.

17609519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17609519.value: The research project is a multi-site anthropological study on the politics of the spread of Japanese popular culture in China since the reform period with the primary aim to enrich the scholarship on Japanese popular culture in China by illuminating the political dynamics underpinning the dissemination of Japanese cultural products in China, the roles of the intermediaries involved and the interaction between the Chinese cultural policy and the domestic media industry in the specific local contexts. Not unlike her neighbors in Southeast Asia, China experienced the influx of the Japanese popular cultural products in the 1990s. Although the Japanese wave was later subsumed by the Korean wave (Hallyu) in the early 2000s, the spread of Japanese popular culture still has pervasive influence on the Chinese society today. At the same time, it is a highly politicized issue in China as the dissemination of Japanese popular culture has been strictly regulated by the Chinese government and shaped by the fluctuating Sino-Japanese relations. There are very few English published works on the spread of Japanese popular culture in China while the Chinese literature largely focuses on textual analysis and audience reception. The majority of the previous studies has failed to clarify the political dynamics underpinning the dissemination of Japanese cultural products in China and to explain the actual processes taken place in the specific local contexts. We aim to fill in the research gap by conducting an anthropological study of the spread of Japanese anime, manga and television drama in Guangzhou, Hangzhou and Beijing since the 1980s. In this project, instead of focusing on the texts or the audience, we emphasize the role of the Chinese party-state in shaping the dissemination of Japanese popular culture in China and the mediation among the state and other actors. We shall conduct intensive fieldwork in the three Chinese cities and in-depth interviews with key actors involved in the circulation of the Japanese cultural products. We shall also conduct comprehensive literature review and archival research to examine the social, political and economic contexts in which the dissemination of Japanese popular culture took place. The project provides valuable empirical data on the spread of Japanese anime, manga and television drama in the specific Chinese local contexts. It will help enhance our understanding not just of Japanese popular culture in China but also of the relationship between the state and the process of cultural production in the Chinese context. 本研究利用多場域人類學研究的方法，探究自改革開放以來日本流行文化在中國的傳播。本研究旨在通過闡明日本流行文化產品在中國傳播背後的政治動力、相關中介的作用以及中國文化政策在特定的本土語境下與當地媒體產業之間的互動，以期豐富關於日本流行文化在中國的學術研究。 與東南亞鄰國一樣，日本流行文化自1990年開始湧入中國。縱然日本浪潮在新世紀被“韓流”超越，日本流行文化在中國社會依然發揮著巨大的影響力。與此同時，日本流行文化的傳播在中國也是一個高度政治性的議題，往往受制於中國政府的嚴格管制的，並受到中日關係波動的影響。 關注日本流行文化在中國的英文學術出版相對較少，相關的中文學術出版主要側重文本分析及受眾反應。以往大部分研究都未能釐清日本流行文化產品在中國的傳播背後的政治動力，也未能闡明在具體的本土語境下其具體的流通過程。 我們旨在通過對20世紀80年代以來日本動畫、漫畫及電視劇在廣州、杭州及北京的傳播進行人類學的研究來彌補現行研究的不足。此研究並非單獨關注文本或受眾，而是著重分析國家機關在日本流行文化的傳播的過程中扮演的角色及國家機關與其他參與者之間的互動。我們會在以上三個中國城市進行密集的田野研究，深度采訪日本文化產品傳播的主要參與者。我們還將進行完整的文獻梳理及檔案研究，從而探索日本流行文化在中國傳播的社會、政治及經濟語境。本研究為日本動畫、漫畫及電視劇在特定的中國本土背景下的傳播提供重要的實證性數據。本研究不僅加深我們對日本流行文化在中國的了解，也有助於加深我們對中國語境下國家與文化生產之間關係的理解。

17609519.label: Realisation of objectives
17609519.value: It is crucial to recognize that the COVID-19 pandemic has substantially impacted the project and required us to adapt our research plan accordingly. Despite the unforeseen circumstances and constraints, we have managed to navigate the challenges and adjust our strategies to continue making progress towards our project objectives. While we may not have achieved every project objective to the highest degree due to the impact of the pandemic, we have been successful in addressing the key aspects of our research and producing valuable insights into the politics of Japanese popular culture in China since the 1980s. We will explain the problems we faced, our strategies to overcome these problems, and how we attempted to achieve the project objectives. In the original research proposal, the research project was divided into two key phases. In the first phase, we would focus on collecting literature and policy documents related to the spread of Japanese popular culture in China. In the second phase, we would conduct intensive fieldwork in the three cities, including site visits, observations, and face-to-face in-depth interviews. We conducted our first phase of research as planned. We focused on identifying the key patterns of the spread of Japanese anime, manga, and television dramas in China since the 1980s, the key geopolitical circumstances, and the key Chinese policies shaping the process, as well as the core state and non-state actors involved in the process. Following the outbreak of COVID-19 and the imposition of lockdowns and travel bans in 2020, we were not able to travel to China and carry out any physical research there as planned. It is important to point out that the travel restrictions to China remained in effect throughout the project period. To cope with these challenges, we first attempted to recruit informants from Guangzhou, Hangzhou, and Beijing residing in Hong Kong to conduct in-depth interviews instead. However, due to the lockdowns, recruiting informants proved difficult. In order to make progress and achieve the research goal, we decided to change our strategy. Instead of conducting multi-site research in China, which had become unfeasible, we attempted to conduct a key case study instead. Based on the data we collected in the first phase, we identified that the entry of Astro Boy, an influential Japanese manga and animation series, into China can serve as a good case study. The Astro Boy case is illustrative of the politics of Japanese popular culture in China for several reasons. First, Astro Boy was the first Japanese animation officially imported into China, marking the beginning of the influx of Japanese popular culture into China between the 1980s and 1990s. Second, different versions of Astro Boy, in various cultural forms, have been imported into China during different periods of time. The formation of the 'social life' of Astro Boy in China helps us understand the change in the interrelationship between the transformation of Chinese society, geopolitical circumstances, and the development of media industries in China and Japan since the 1980s. After identifying Astro Boy as our key case study, we proceeded to collect existing literature, policy documents, relevant news reports, articles, and online resources related to the spread of Astro Boy in China between the 1980s and 2010s. Our goal was to examine how the geopolitical circumstances, changing structures of media industries in China and Japan, and the development of Chinese cultural policy shaped the trajectories of Astro Boy's entry into China. Additionally, we sought to identify the key intermediaries involved in the process and the changes in channels through which Astro Boy has been circulated. As a result, we have collected existing English, Chinese, and Japanese literature on 1) the geopolitical context shaping the spread of Japanese popular culture in China; 2) the spread of Japanese popular culture in China in general; 3) the spread of Japanese animation, manga, and television drama in China; 4) the spread of Japanese popular culture in Guangzhou, Hangzhou, and Beijing; 5) the spread of different Astro Boy products in China; 6) the development of national and local media industries in China; and 7) the export of Japanese popular culture. We have also gathered relevant cultural policy documents, key speeches of Chinese officials, and official yearbooks on Chinese film industries, animation industries, television industries, and publishing industries. Additionally, we conducted extensive online research to collect relevant news reports, articles, video clips, and fan posts in different forums about Astro Boy products in particular and other Japanese animation, manga, and television drama in general. The data collected enable us to achieve the six project objectives: Objectives 1 & 2: We have managed to identify the key trajectories of the spread of Japanese animation, manga, and television dramas in China between the 1980s and 2020. We have categorized the spread of Japanese popular culture into four key periods: 1978-1991, 1992-2003, 2003-2010, and 2011-2020 based on the key patterns identified. We have also compiled a chronicle of Japanese popular culture in China during the period. In the chronicle, we have recorded detailed information on 460 Japanese cultural products (including animation, manga, film, and television drama) imported into China. We have also identified the key trajectories of the spread of Astro Boy cultural products into China and compiled a chronicle thereof. We have identified various key state and non-state actors involved in the spread of Japanese anime, manga, and television drama in China. Specifically, we have identified the key intermediaries, such as overseas Chinese businessmen, Japanese advertisers, Chinese broadcasters, Chinese online video platforms, Chinese and Hong Kong multi-media companies, and their roles in the import and dissemination of Astro Boy in China. As we were not able to conduct fieldwork in Guangzhou, Hangzhou, and Beijing, we could only partially achieve these project objectives, as we were not able to conduct face-to-face interviews with practitioners and fans on the spread of Japanese cultural products and the key intermediaries involved in the process at the specific city level. Objectives 3, 4 & 5: We have identified how the spread of Japanese popular culture in China has been shaped by changing geopolitical circumstances and Chinese cultural policies. We have identified the key changes in Sino-Japanese relations between the 1980s and 2020 and how they shaped the Chinese government's attitude and strategies regarding the import and dissemination of Japanese animation, manga, and television drama. Specifically, we have identified how Japanese popular cultural products served as instruments for diplomacy and were later transformed into instruments for promoting Chinese nationalism. We have examined how the transformation of Chinese cultural policy has played a core role in shaping the trajectories of the spread of Japanese popular culture during different periods of time. Specifically, we have identified how the development of policies on animation, film, television, advertising, publishing, and internet video industries in China shaped the dissemination of Japanese popular culture. We have also identified how different state agencies were involved in the process. Objective 6: We have identified how the official and unofficial circulation channels of Japanese popular culture in China have emerged and evolved since the 1980s. Specifically, we have examined how the Chinese state's regulation of the animation, television, film, publishing, and internet video industries has shaped the changes in circulation channels of Japanese popular culture in China.
