17621819.label: Major findings and research outcome
17621819.value: In accounts, intersex interviewees in plurilingual Hong Kong find English and Mandarin terms socially problematic, stressing the need for localized, non-stigmatizing terms that take into account both written and spoken forms. The distinct features of Cantonese homophones, tonalities, and semantic prosodies all play a role. To avoid social pitfalls, terms from the English-speaking world and mainland China must be scrutinized. In their accounts, doctor interviewees report relying on what appears to be scientifically inaccurate discourses to maintain conversational boundaries when informing parents of their child's intersex traits. They aim to help manage parents' emotions to keep communication going. However, doctors' accounts at the same time often indirectly frame intersexuality as a disorder or manifestation of disease, leaving little room for non-medicalized interpretations. Doctors position themselves in accounts as capacitators for these babies, but to have a role, they arguably must first discursively debilitate the children, not allowing for the possibility of leaving them be. This approach is rationalized as being for the child's welfare. Emotion management emerges as another theme from doctor accounts. They report noticing parents' affective responses and reacting. Emotion management is traced through the 'sociolinguistic fixing' of parents' affective experiences, with doctors seemingly transforming parents' affective experiences into emotions on their behalf. Patients and their parents are potentially being 'made' as part of a complex and fraught conversation. The overlapping and colliding frames of diagnosis, counseling, and prognosis also become entangled in doctor accounts, adding to the already unequal power relations inherent in biomedical encounters. Doctors talk in accounts about an orientation away from disorder and from the urgency of surgery, yet their accounts also convey disordered, ill embodiments for the child. Parents are positioned as decision-makers, but the doctors' roles is de-emphasized, making it difficult for parents to choose a non-surgical pathway. Doctors also face difficulty translating medical English terms into Cantonese when discussing their child's non-normative innate sex characteristics with parents. This often results in parents becoming upset or withdrawn due to anxiety and embarrassment. As a solution, doctors use biomedical terms in English, which are less alarming than their Cantonese translations. This dilemma is exacerbated when speaking to lower social class parents, who may struggle to comprehend biological concepts. Parents are recruited into managing their intersex child's body, with their perceptions shaped at the intersection of language and social class. This disparate ratification process has significant and profound implications for intersex babies.

17621819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17621819.value: It was predictable that recruiting intersex interview participants, as part of a sensitive topic, would be a challenge, and indeed there was a shortage of intersex participants who came forward in the end. Further development in this regard is most likely to be through conducting a much more in-depth, biographical case study based on Small Luk's life history around this topic (the main intersex participant in the present study). Such an approach will complement the insights gathered from the interviews with doctors in the current project and greatly expand on Luk's earlier contribution. Furthermore, the interview approach has provided access to the linguistic and professional ideologies that sit behind doctors' accounts. Such an approach is merely a strong start, however, and follow-up research in which the researcher accompanies the doctors as they speak to parents and intersex children and/or adults (ideally audio or video recording these interactions) seems the logical continuation of this research trajectory. It is time to investigate what they actually do say, thus gaining access to habits or strategies of which they may not be aware, and gain insight into how their aspirations and impressions eventuate in professional practice.

17621819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17621819.value: Intersex individuals in Hong Kong find English and Mandarin terms difficult and socially problematic. They emphasize the need for local, non-offensive terms that consider both written and spoken Cantonese language features. Doctors in the study use inaccurate language to communicate with parents of intersex children, aiming to manage parents' emotions and perceptions. However, they often describe intersexuality as a disorder or disease, leaving no room for alternative understandings. Doctors try to understand parents' feelings and respond accordingly, but this creates an unequal relationship between doctors and parents. The complex conversation further complicates power dynamics in medical situations. Doctors discuss the non-urgency of surgery, but their language still implies the child is unwell. Parents are seen as decision-makers, but it is difficult for them to choose a non-surgical option. Doctors also struggle to translate medical English terms into Cantonese, causing anxiety and embarrassment for parents. Using English terms seems less alarming, especially for lower social class parents who may not understand biology. Parents are involved in managing their intersex child's body, with their perceptions influenced by language and social class. This process has significant consequences for intersex children from all social backgrounds, highlighting the challenges in addressing intersexuality in plurilingual Hong Kong.

17621919.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17621919.value: 中國臉：毛澤東時代肖像攝影研究

17621919.label: Project Objectives
17621919.value: • Use photographic portraits and related visual and verbal material to delineate how a socialist face is “trained” alongside a socialist body; • Use photographic portraits and related visual and verbal material to define key components in this “training” program; • Depict how photography as a key visual medium captures a tempered and disciplined face, in connection to and in contrast with other visual mediums of the time.
rows: • Use photographic portraits and related visual and verbal material to delineate how a socialist face is “trained” alongside a socialist body;
• Use photographic portraits and related visual and verbal material to define key components in this “training” program;
• Depict how photography as a key visual medium captures a tempered and disciplined face, in connection to and in contrast with other visual mediums of the time.

17621919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17621919.value: “Framing a Socialist Face” focuses on the photographic portraiture as a key genre of image production in Mao-era China. In the vast visual output of the entire Mao period, a socialist subject emerged as both politically mobilized and distinctively Chinese. The spectacular revolutionary model ballet, for instance, showcased how a socialist body could be toned, disciplined, and recast following a set of political and aesthetic directives. Other fine examples abound to illustrate how a socialist body became politicized, aestheticized, and set to motion throughout the three decades under Mao. If the body can be trained and molded, what about the human face? My preliminary survey of photographic portraits produced during the Mao period indicates that the socialist face was tempered, disciplined, and refashioned along with the revolutionized body. My project begins by asking a series of questions that are rarely addressed in studies of Mao-era culture. What kind of cultural mechanisms were at work behind the myriad of faces that adorned glossy pages of visual propaganda from the period? What constitutes a socialist face? And what are socialist faces with Chinese characteristics? I argue that the stylized face was a composite, a confluence of a diverse modern body culture shaped since the beginning of the twentieth century. How the human face could be recognized as both distinctively socialist and Chinese required decades of experiments in the hands of several generations of Mao-era portraitists. While the project addresses the entire Mao period, the focus is on the 1970s, seen as a transitional period in China. To set my inquiry in this transitional moment is strategic as both stabilization and destabilization of visual conventions can be illuminated. My hypothesis is that by the 1970s, the highly disciplined and stylized face of socialism was set loose a bit, while body training programs gradually destabilized. The catalyst of this subtle shift in socialist image-making was the close affinity formed between portraiture and the revived film culture of the early 1970s. Photography’s close ties with film culture can never be underestimated. Fixing film stars of late Mao China in a photographic frame helped elevate commercial photographers onto the artist’s pedestal. In China of the 1970s, it was the revived film industry and a broadened spectatorship that fueled the energy and techniques in portrait making. 《中國臉：毛澤東時代肖像攝影研究》從一個具體的角度切入社會主義中國的影像文化。在50到70年代的大批量的影像生產中，湧現出一個特定的主體形象，他/她是中國的，也是社會主義的。這個形象中究竟是哪一些視覺和非視覺的元素使得它們被清楚的識別為中國的、社會主義的臉和身體呢？我們目前的研究中缺乏足夠的分析，這些元素也沒有被細緻的識別、定義、分析。這個研究項目希望能填補這個空缺。 對社會主義的身體已經有相關的研究，比如近年來對於毛時代表演藝術的研究，對60和70年代的革命現代芭蕾舞劇的研究就是一個很好的範例。社會主義的身體是可以鍛鍊和塑造的，那麼社會主義的臉呢？《中國臉》的主要出發點是，社會主義的臉也是可以塑造、定型、加固的。攝影，尤其是人像攝影，在這裡就起了一個舉足輕重的作用。70年代初開始的中國人像攝影更是與復甦的電影文化一起，為轉折時期的主體形象塑造提供了一系列的影像語彙。

17622019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17622019.value: This research is about legislative and executive efforts to limit or control the power of courts, a phenomenon known as “court curbing”. The topic is both perennial and timely. Even in longstanding and stable constitutional democracies, courts may have their jurisdiction curtailed or their resources cut. In more extreme cases, the judges themselves may be impeached and replaced by more docile alternatives. Recent events in Poland and elsewhere have made questions of judicial independence and court curbing more pressing than ever. Although this latest wave of court curbing may appear to reflect a broadly “populist” hostility to judiciaries, I will show how court curbing is driven primarily by the interests of political elites and their frustration with independent courts. To this end, I use cross-national data to investigate how court curbing might be predicted in advance, testing hypotheses that court curbing will be prefigured by episodes of non-compliance with judicial decisions and proactive efforts by political elites to turn public opinion against the courts. I will also look closely at how anti-court discourse is employed to justify and legitimate court curbing in recent examples from Poland, Turkey, and the United Kingdom. Ultimately, these two lines of inquiry will come together to show how court curbing is motivated and shaped by elite interests. 此研究與「司法遏制」有關，意指立法及行政機關嘗試限制或控制法院的權力。此題目具迫切性及深遠影響。即使在歷史悠久及穩定的民主體制，法院仍會面對其管轄權被限制或資源被削減的風險。在更極端的情況下，法官更有機會被彈劾並被其他相對溫順的人選取締。近期於匈牙利、波蘭及土耳其的發展令司法獨立及司法遏制的問題變得更迫切。雖然近年的司法遏制浪潮似是民綷主義對司法機構呈現的敵意，我認為司法遏制是源於政治精英的利益及他們對於司法獨立的不滿。為此，我將利用跨國數據研究如何預測司法遏制及測試於司法遏制發生之前通常會先出現不遵守法院判決及政治精英積極將民意放於法院的對立面上的假設。另外，在波蘭、土耳其及英國的例子中的，我會研究「反法院」的論述如何被建立並合理化司法遏制。以上兩個研究問題將顯示司法遏制是如何被政治精英的利益推動及成形。

17622019.label: Realisation of objectives
17622019.value: I left my position at the University of Hong Kong prior to the completion of this project. Nevertheless, several objectives have since been achieved. With respect to Objective #1, the research identified and described categories of court curbing discourse across three diverse contexts (Poland, The United Kingdom, and Turkey) showing how populist framing is employed strategically to facilitate court-curbing policies. With respect to Objective #4, the research led to the completion of a monograph proposal for Cambridge University Press. Cambridge University Press has awarded me the contract to produce the monograph, tentatively titled Populist Court Curbing, to be published in their prestigious series on comparative constitutional law and policy. Five of the nine planned chapters for the monograph are now complete and the monograph is expected to be published in 2024. With respect to Objective #5, the global pandemic interfered with conference plans but eventually research findings were presented at the annual meeting of the International Society of Public Law in 2022 in Wroclaw, Poland (July 4-6) and at the Launch Event for the Empirical Network on Law and Judicial Politics at University College London in 2023 (4-5 May). With respect to Objectives 2, 3, and 4, the original plans were interrupted by my move from HKU to the University of Glasgow, but I will take these forward in the coming year.

17622019.label: Major findings and research outcome
17622019.value: The project's major findings derive from both quantitative cross-national analysis and qualitative comparative case-study analysis. Using fixed effects regression models - and controlling for several variables thought to have an influence on the incidence of court curbing - the cross-national quantitative analysis confirms the expectation that governments that use populist rhetoric are relatively more likely to engage in court curbing. The analysis also suggests that modelling populism as dynamic rhetorical behaviour (as opposed to a static characteristic of political leaders) does a better job of accounting for the relationship between populism and court curbing. Qualitative case studies of Poland, Turkey, and the UK show how populist rhetoric facilities court-curbing plans and how the power of Populist court-curbing frames is conditioned by local cultural resonance. In contrast to Poland and Turkey, the research finds that anti-court populism fails to resonate in the UK and this feature of the broader political culture helps to insulate the British judiciary from court curbing. These findings are presented in the forthcoming monograph (see Part C).

17622019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
17622019.value: A promising path for further research, building on this project, is to investigate more broadly the ideational factors that motivate or constrain threats to independent judicial power. Scholars of judicial politics often acknowledge that court curbing might be influenced one way or another by values and informal norms, but they have tended to favor rational-strategic (as opposed to ideational) explanations. This emphasis is understandable; rational-strategic explanations often generalize well across contexts, whereas ideational explanations tend to be more idiographic. But ideational factors are likely to interact with rational-strategic factors in important ways that should not be neglected. For example, one of the blind spots in the existing scholarship on how political competition influences judicial independence is the assumption that rival politicians and political parties in a given context are similarly positioned with respect to the costs and benefits of independent judicial power. But the putative insurance value of judicial independence is likely to vary with the ideology of competitors. The logic of judicial independence as political insurance would, for example, apply very differently to a party with illiberal preferences than to a competitor party intent on positioning itself as the liberal or establishment choice.

17622019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
17622019.value: This research investigates how governments use populist rhetoric to legitimate policies that curb the power and/or independence of courts. The research advances several related claims. First, the success of court curbing depends on how it is framed; policies that limit the power or independence of courts cannot be sustained unless they are presented as appropriate remedies for real and pressing problems. Second, the choice of how to frame court-curbing policies has a strategic dimension; it is a choice structured by the expected reactions of other actors. Framing strategies can therefore be analysed in terms of how they anticipate and manage opposition to court curbing. Third, populist rhetoric provides an especially powerful frame for the purposes of court curbing—not only does it help to justify court curbing, by vilifying judges as morally blameworthy enemies of the righteous people, but it also provides a ready-made counterattack to criticism by casting opponents as self-serving elites (this is a framing strategy that politicians who have already had some success using populist frames are especially well-placed to exploit). Finally, populist court-curbing frames are not uniformly effective; they are effective to the extent that they resonate with pre-existing beliefs, values, and narratives in particular contexts.

17622519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
17622519.value: 在晚期肝細胞癌病人使用Polo-like Kinase 4（PLK4）抑制劑CFI-400945併尼伏人單抗（Nivolumab）的1/2期臨床研究

17622519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
17622519.value: Introduction: Liver cancer is the second most common cause of cancer-related death in Asia-Pacific region. There is a high unmet medical need to develop more effective systemic therapy for patients with advanced liver cancer. Recently, this is an emerging role of immunotherapy, especially the use of checkpoint inhibitors in management of advanced liver patients. The pivotal phase 1/2 CheckMate-040 study demonstrated the safety and encouraging efficacy of nivolumab in treating advanced liver patients. On the other hand, Polo-kinase 4(PLK4) represents another attractive therapeutic target in cancer treatments as liver cancer cells heavily rely on PLK4 to reproduce centrosomes for cell division. Our provocative laboratory data clearly demonstrated that combining PLK4 (CFI-400945) together with an anti-PD1 antibody (nivolumab) should be an attractive and important approach in treating advanced HCC patients. Thus, we propose a phase 1/2 study of CFI-400945 in combination with nivolumab in determining the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and safety in advanced HCC population in the phase 1 dose part . It will then further evaluate for efficacy, tolerability and potential biomarkers in the phase 2 cohort. Settings: This trial will be conducted at the Phase 1 Centre at the Queen Mary Hospital, The University of Hong Kong. Subjects: Advanced liver cancer patients not suitable for surgery or various loco-regional therapies and are refractory to sorafenib or lenvatinib will be recruited. Study Design: This is an open label, single center, Phase 1/2 study.. Nivolumab dosage will be kept at 3mg/kg and dose escalation of CFI-400945 will follow a standard 3+3 cohort design until the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) is determined. Once the MTD was determined, an additional 26 patients will be recruited to receive the combination with CFI-400945 at the MTD in the phase 2 cohort. Immunohistochemistry study of PTEN and PD-L1 expression level in the biopsy tissues will be assessed and correlated with outcomes. Sample size: The sample size determination used is per standard Phase 1 “3+3” dose escalation format to determine the MTD. Once the MTD is reached, up to a total of 26 patients will be enrolled at MTD in the phase 2 part. Objectives: The primary objective is to determine the MTD and safety of CFI-400945 in combination with nivolumab in advanced HCC patients Implications: We believe the results of this study would be of major impact in guiding the future development of systemic therapy in advanced liver cancer patients. 簡介：肝癌是亞太地區的第二常見的癌症相關死因。對於晚期肝癌患者，更有效的全身治療仍是未被滿足的醫療需求。近年免疫療法興起，尤其是免疫檢查點抑制劑，在晚期肝癌患者的治療的角色漸現。關鍵的1/2期研究CheckMate-040展示了尼伏人單抗（Nivolumab）用於治療晚期肝癌患者的安全性和令人鼓舞的療效。另一方面，Polo-like kinase 4（PLK4）是另一個吸引的癌症治療靶點，因為肝癌細胞嚴重依賴PLK4來複製中心體以進行細胞分裂。根據我們在實驗室測試的數據，將PLK4抑制劑（CFI-400945）併用抗PD1抗體（尼伏人單抗）是治療晚期肝癌患者的一個具吸引力且重要的方法。因此，我們提出CFI-400945併尼伏人單抗組合的1/2期研究——1期劑量遞增部分將確定組合在晚期肝癌患者的最大耐受劑量和安全性，然後在2期部分進一步評估組合的療效、耐受性和潛在的生物標記。 設置：本項試驗將在位於瑪麗醫院的香港大學一期臨床試驗中心進行。 受試者：不適合進行手術或各種局部區域治療且索拉非尼（Sorafenib）或樂伐替尼（Lenvatinib）治療無效的晚期肝癌患者將被招募。 研究設計：這是一個開放標籤、單中心的1/2期臨床研究。尼伏人單抗將以標準劑量給藥，CFI-400945的劑量遞增將遵循標準的「3+3」劑量遞增設計，直到確定最大耐受劑量。一旦確定最大耐受劑量，將招募另外26名患者在2期部分接受最大耐受劑量的CFI-400945和尼伏人單抗。活檢組織的PTEN和PD-L1表達水平將以免疫組織化學染色法評估並與治療結果聯繫。 樣本數估算：樣本數是按照標準的1期研究「3+3」劑量遞增設計以確定CFI-400945的最大耐受劑量。一旦確定最大耐受劑量，共有26名患者將參與試驗的2期部分。 目的：研究主要目的是確定CFI-400945併用尼伏人單抗治療晚期肝癌患者的最大耐受劑量及安全性。 意義：我們相信這項研究的結果將對晚期肝癌患者全身性治療的未來發展有重要影響。

18200219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18200219.value: Distance running has become one of the most popular physical activities around the world. However, distance runners, in particular for novice runners, experience a remarkable incidence of running related injuries (RRIs). During running, there always exists small fluctuations between strides. The stride-to-stride variability has been considered a by-product of long-range dynamics, and reflects flexibility and adaptability of the locomotor system to ever-changing internal and external environments during running. Although there are numerous studies that have suggested that there is a connection between stride-to-stride variability and RRIs, the understanding of stride variability during prolonged running is very limited. Experience and progressive fatigue are two common risk factors connected with RRIs. Previous studies have found that stride variability was affected by progressive fatigue during running. However, in those studies, fatigue was induced by running a relative short distance and none of previous studies have yet investigated the effects of fatigue on the stride variability during a full marathon race. Experience in performing a full marathon race provides runners with greater understanding of extreme fatigue that their bodies have never experienced before. This kind of experience may enhance the capacity of runners in response to constraints due to ever-changing internal and external environments. This study aims to investigate the relationships between stride variability at both the execution (i.e. lower-limb coordination variability) and outcome levels (i.e. stride time variability) as a function of running experience during a full marathon race. Based on existing laboratory-based data, it is first hypothesised that the correlation between the stride time variability and lower-limb coordination variability can be replicated in a naturalistic setting. Moreover, it is also expected that stride time and lower-limb coordination variability will fluctuate less (i.e. be less adaptable) during the full marathon race in first-time marathon finishers than in the experienced marathon finishers. The long-term impact of the proposed project stems from the potential association between the stride-to-stride variability during running and RRIs. This correlation would bring about insights into how the stride variability could benefit different groups of running population, and help formulate interventions that are more effective and easier to implement for prevention of RRIs. The findings of the proposed study will serve as reference for understanding the stride-to-stride variability during a prolonged run, provide insights of marathon participation into the stride time variability during a full marathon run, and help predict RRIs.

18200219.label: Realisation of objectives
18200219.value: Due to the social unrest and outbreak of Covid-19, there was a significant delay in the research plan and process towards achievement of objectives of this research. Social distancing measures, closure of sport facilities and running tracks affected subject recruitment and data collection. Cancellation of marathon and similar events in the last two years over public health concerns delayed the project as a whole. However, with the improvement of conditions, we were able to do data collection. With reference to objectives 1 and 2, an experimental study for investigating the relation between over-ground and treadmill running was conducted using MyoMotion (Noraxon) and IMeasureU (Vicon) sensors. In total 28 participants were recruited to run on treadmill and track. In addition, 14 participants also participated in marathon running. In the first part, 10 participants participants were asked to run on a treadmill at speeds of 2, 2.5, 3 and 3.5m/s each for three minutes and on track for three minutes at their self-preferred speed. They were attached 7 MyoMotion sensors at their L5S1, thighs, Shanks and feet. In addition, we also attached one additional IMeasureU sensor at the anteromedial side of the subject’s tibia. In the second part, 28 participants were asked to run on a treadmill at their self-preferred speed for 31 minutes and 10 participants ran on track for 31 minutes at their self-preferred speed. They were attached 9 Inertial Movement Units (IMU) (Opal sensors) at their L5S1, thighs, Shanks, tibial tuberosity and feet. First part has 2 phases. The objective of the first phase was to determine the correlation between the kinematic data acquired by the two sensor systems and see whether we able to predict the kinematics of the right limb based on the single sensor attached to the right tibia in the sagittal plane. Also, as the speed for a subject running on a treadmill can easily be manipulated, we also wanted to know whether the lower limb kinematics of the subject running on the level ground can be predicted from data from treadmill running. Results show that prediction of joint kinematics for over-ground running can be done by hip and knee joints data from treadmill running. The goodness of fit denoted by the R-Square values were shown to be good to very good with a range from 0.73 to 0.96 for predicting hip and knee joint kinematics using the signals from either the accelerometer or the gyroscope. It was also shown that gyroscope data from sensor is a better predictor as compared to the accelerometer data in such prediction. In the second phase we continued to investigate whether we are able to use the sensor attached to the right tibia to also predict the kinematics of the left limb, i.e. the opposite limb (cross-leg prediction) and with what accuracy? When we looked at the results as a whole, the R-square values had a range from 0.651 to 0.961. From our findings, we were able to conclude that it is reasonably accurate for cross-leg prediction of running kinematics using a single wearable sensor. The results of these studies have been published in the form of a manuscript in the Sensors and Symmetry journals recently. In the second part of the study we continue to compare the relationships between stride-to-stride variability at movement execution and outcome levels while treadmill and over ground run. A scoping review was conducted about running variability and its role in development of injuries while running. It also discussed how fatigue and running speed can affect variability and highlights the literature gap for the application of stride time estimation through inertial measurement unit to predict running injuries and the optimal movement variability hypothesis. Researchers must clarify the correlation between stride variability at the movement outcome and execution levels, and examine the characteristics of stride variability during long runs in a natural environment as a function of running experience. Studies should investigate the practicality of using inertial measurement units for on-field kinetic and kinematic measures of various tasks and across different surfaces. Advantages and disadvantages of linear and nonlinear measures of variability that have not been considered in the existing studies are also discussed. Finally, several directions for researching running variability and inertial measurement units are proposed. This scoping review has been submitted in BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation.

18200219.label: Major findings and research outcome
18200219.value: We were able to demonstrate that it is feasible to use just one single sensor attached to the right tibia to predict the kinematics of the right limb. We also demonstrated that it is feasible to predict level ground lower limb kinematics using the single sensor data acquired while treadmill running. Cross-leg prediction of running kinematics is feasible using a single wearable sensor. Further research using inertial measurement units for on-field kinetic and kinematic measures of various tasks and across different surfaces are required.

18200219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18200219.value: While reviewing the whole study, we identified several limitations. We found that IMeasureU sensors were quiet sensitive to the metallic environment during the treadmill running. We tried to use other sensor systems provided by other manufacturers that use enhanced algorithms. We developed our model using only healthy recreational runners, it would be worthy to study the validity of these models in subjects with injuries or after fatigue. Moreover, we only investigated the lower limb kinematics only in the sagittal plane. It would be interesting to explore whether we could also predict the running kinematics in other anatomical planes. Finally, we attached the sensor to the anteromedial side of the tibia. This may cause some discomfort to the subjects, especially runners. It would be useful to explore whether there can be any better placement for sensors, for instance, embedding it in the running shoes. The literature gap for the assessment of gait and running variability was identified and several directions for future research especially those using inertial measurement units are proposed.

18200519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18200519.value: 以潛變量模型作多面子空間聚類

18200519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18200519.value: We have witnessed an explosion of data available from multiple sources and modalities. Although data sets today usually have a high dimension, it has been observed that their intrinsic dimension is often much smaller and that interesting patterns can be found in lower dimensional subspaces. Subspace clustering exploits the above observed property and finds groups of data points residing in different subspaces. It has found successful applications in various domains including image segmentation, motion segmentation, face clustering, and gene expression data clustering. Many of the recent subspace clustering methods, however, suffer from one major drawback: they attempt to find only a single partition of data and thus may not suffice to handle high-dimensional data that are often multifaceted. For example, while subspace clustering methods can accurately group face images based on subjects, it may ignore other meaningful groupings of face images such as those grouped facial expressions and/or by the existence of sunglasses. In this project, we aim to develop a solution for the problem of finding multiple clusterings of data points residing in different subspaces on a data set. We refer to such a problem as multifaceted subspace clustering. The solution will be based on probabilistic models due to their sound statistical basis. The proposed models will contain multiple discrete latent variables to represent multiple clusterings along different facets. To represent the local subspaces in each clustering, we will consider model structures based on conventional dimension reduction techniques. To represent the probabilistic relationships among the clusterings, we will consider two kinds of network structures with varying levels of complexity. We will develop inference algorithms as well as parameter and structure learning algorithms for those variants of models. The model variants will be evaluated and compared on various kinds of data sets where multiple meaningful clusterings are known to exist. The successful completion of this project will result in a solution for multifaceted subspace clustering, which currently receives insufficient research effort. A successful solution could find many meaningful applications in real world situations. It could attract more attention to this new research direction and could lead to future commercialization. Besides, the proposed models may produce better clustering performance over state-of-the-art subspace clustering methods and those producing multiple clusterings, respectively. Moreover, the proposed method can also automatically determine the numbers of clusterings and subspaces. It could be used for automatic categorization of vast amount data based on multiple aspects without any manual input. 我們正目睹來自不同源頭及不同形式的數據爆炸。雖然今時今日的數據集通常也有高維度，但它們的內在維度常常也是細小很多，而有趣的模式也可在較低維度的子空間找到。 子空間聚類利用上述的特性來找出處於不同子空間的多個數據分組。它被成功地應用於不同領域，包括圖像分割，動作分割，人臉聚類及基因表現數據聚類。不過，很多近期的子空間聚類也擁有一個重要的缺點：它們只嘗試找單一的數據分割，因此它們或不足以處理往往多面的高維度數據。例如，子空間聚類方法能準確地基於對像將人面分類，但它們或會忽略其他對人臉圖像有意思的分類，諸如基於面部表情及/或有否戴太陽眼鏡的分類。 在這項目，我們旨在開發一個方案，以解決於數據集之中尋找多個存於不同子空間的群組的問題。我們將這個問題稱為多面子空間聚類。這方案將會是基於概率模型，因為它們穩妥的統計基礙。倡議的模型將包含多個離散潛變量，用以代表處於不同方面的分組。為表達每一分組的局部子空間，我們會考慮使用基於常規降維技巧的模型結構。為表達分組之間的概率關係，我們會考慮兩種有不同複雜程度的模型結構。我們將會開發用於那些模型變體的推斷算法以及參數與結構學習算法。我們將會用一些已知有多個有意思分組的數據集，用來評價及比較那些模型變體。 目前多面子空間聚類未有得到足夠的研究努力。若這項目能成功，成果能為這問題帶來一個解決方案。而這方案或能在真實世界找到很多有意義的應用。它亦或能帶來對這問題更多的研究關注和引致將來的商業化。此外，分別對比最先進的子空間聚類方法和那些產生多分組的聚類方法，倡議的模型或會帶來更佳的聚類效能。另外，倡議的方法亦可以自動斷定分組和子空間的數目。它或能基於不同的範籌將大量的數據自動分類而不需要人手的輸入。

18300019.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18300019.value: 海洋野生動物中新興的有機阻燃劑

18300019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18300019.value: Organic flame retardants (OFRs) have been used in myriad applications to reduce fire hazards. Reports of increasing levels of OFRs in human and wildlife tissues from the 1980s onwards and the publication of studies demonstrating the toxicity of these chemicals to vertebrates prompted regulation in various countries of the use of polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) and hexabromocyclododecanes (HBCDs). The phase-out of these two most well-known OFRs is expected to reduce the world market demand for these compounds, but other emerging OFRs must consequently take their place in product manufacturing. A few candidates for this purpose such as decabromodiphenylethane (DBDPE), 1,2-dibromo-4-(1,2-ibromoethyl)cyclohexane (TBECH) and organophosphate esters (OPEs), have been reported in a wide range of environmental samples at levels comparable to those of the widespread PBDEs and HBCDs. A recent monitoring program on local cetaceans reveals that the levels of conventional persistent organic pollutants (POPs) including DDTs and PCBs were still the most predominant in blubber samples. However, these were closely followed by PBDEs and HBCDs, which are OFRs more recently added to the POPs list, suggesting the coastal area of Hong Kong and the Pearl River estuary is significantly contaminated by these persistent and toxic substances. Although PBDEs and HBCDs have been measured in Hong Kong and China, there is a lack of comparable data about alternatives for these banned chemicals, prompting our group to start monitoring these emerging chemicals in south China. The results indicated relatively high concentrations of DBDPE and Dechlorane Plus (DP) in local cetaceans. Additionally, significantly increasing temporal shifting trends of banned OFRs to their corresponding replacements were observed in blubber samples over the past decade. This indicates the increasing use of newer and re-emerging OFRs since the restriction of the production and use of PBDEs and HBCDs, and raises the possibility that other emerging OFRs are also present in local marine wildlife. It is therefore imperative to investigate novel and understudied OFRs in the local environment, particularly in cetaceans, sea turtles and corals that have great conservation value, in order to increase the reliability and integrity of the overall assessment of OFRs in the environment. The overall aim of this study is consequently to identify and quantify known, and emerging OFRs, in different marine wildlife and to evaluate the relative proportions of these in the target species for exposure assessments of OFRs in Hong Kong marine organisms. 18300919.label: Project Objectives
18300919.value: To quantify levels and species of EDCs in urine and evaluate endocrine disrupting effects of children’s urine samples by in vitro bioassay in Hong Kong and Belgium; To identify the key EDCs to which children are exposed using the EDA method, which combines in vitro bioassay, target analysis and non-target analysis/screening; To estimate total daily uptake of EDCs by child population (ng/kg BW/per day), and estimate the resulting health risk; To intercompare and discuss the results with Belgian researchers to find the possible exposure routes for developing future health policies related to EDCs.

18300919.label: Realisation of objectives
18300919.value: During the project starting date 1 Jan 2020 to 31 Dec 2023, the following activities have been done. Morning urine samples and hair samples of children between 3-12 years old in Hong Kong and Belgium were sampled. Fifty-three samples were collected in both places. Bisphenol A, phthalates, organophosphate flame retardants (OPFRs), perfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) and their metabolites which are high exposure and high production volume EDCs are selected as targets. Urine samples are first fractionated to reduce complexity, then in vitro estrogen/ thyroid receptor bioassay identifies the active fractions and guides the targets and non-targets, afterwards targets were analyzed by LC-triple quadrupole MS techniques (LC-QQQ-MS). If the key contributes EDCs can not be found by target analysis, non-target analysis using LC-quadrupole-time-of-flight MS techniques (LC-QTOF-MS). In the end, the suspected EDCs were confirmed by re-establishing their dose-response relationships and establishing potency balance. It was helpful in making out the species and amount of EDCs burden on Hong Kong and Belgian children. Firstly, seven perfluorinated and polyfluorinated substances (PFASs) were evaluated in urine and hair samples from children. The analytical results suggested widespread PFAS contamination. All target PFASs were detected in at least 32% of urine samples, with geometric mean (GM) concentrations ranging from 0.18 to 2.97 ng/L. Although PFOS and PFDDA were not detected in hair or air samples, the other target PFASs were detected in 48-70% of hair samples (GM concentrations: 2.40-233 pg/g). In summary, PFOA was the major PFAS detected in hair, and urine, Although a significant difference in PFAS concentrations in hair samples was observed between boys and girls (p<0.05), no significant sex-related difference in urinary PFAS or paired PFAS (hair/urine) concentrations was observed. Secondly, common plasticizers (phthalates and their metabolites) and new alternatives (bisphenol analogs, t-butylphenyl diphenyl phosphate (BPDP) and bisphenol A bis(diphenyl phosphate) (BDP)) were quantified in urine and hair samples from Hong Kong children and in drinking water and airborne particles in 17 Hong Kong kindergartens. The results suggested that local Hong Kong children were exposed to a range of these common plasticizers and new alternatives. High concentrations of BPDP and BDP were present in most matrices. The concentrations of phthalates in urine were lower than those detected in Japanese and German children in previous studies, but higher in these matrices compared with other target chemicals. Bisphenol analogs were detected in 15% to 64% of urine samples in geometric mean (GM) concentrations ranging from 5.26 ng/L to 98.1 ng/L, in 7% to 74% of hair samples in GM concentrations ranging from 57.5 pg/g to 2390 pg/g, in 59% to 100% of kindergarten air samples in GM concentrations ranging from 43.1 pg/m³to 222 pg/m³, and in 33% to 100% of tap-water samples in GM concentrations ranging from 0.90 ng/L to 3.70 ng/L. The estimated daily urinary excretion (EDE) values of bisphenol analogs by children showed that tap water and airborne particles in kindergarten air in Hong Kong might be an important source of children's exposure to bisphenol analogs. Thirdly, the urine levels of phthalate esters metabolites (mPAEs) and bisphenols (BPs) in kindergarten children were measured.The geometric mean concentrations of mPAEs and BPs in children’s urine were 93.7 μg/gcrea and 2.9 μg/gcrea. NTA identified a total of 1069 compounds, including 106 EDCs, commonly detected in food, cosmetics, and drugs. The potential sources of EDCs included dietary and cosmetic additives, toys, flooring and dust, as well as differences in lifestyles, diet, and living environment. However, age was found to significantly impact EDC exposure. Moreover, the presence of caffeine in children’s urine, which exhibited higher detection rates in children from Hong Kong with 95.6%, warrants further attention. The health risks of children’s exposure to mPAEs and BPA were also assessed, and it was found that 60% of children’s cumulative risk of exposure to these EDCs was at a possible risk level, and mPAEs were the primary one compared with BPs, accounting for more than 96% of the total exposure, while BPs only accounted for less than 4%. The daily exposure of BPA was significantly higher than other BPs, indicating that despite the use of BPA substitutes, BPA remains the primary source of children’s daily exposure to BPs, diet and toys as potential main sources. Lastly, NTA identified a total of 1069 compounds, including 106 EDCs, commonly detected in food, cosmetics, and drugs. Notable regional differences were observed between Guangzhou and Hong Kong with potential sources of EDCs including dietary and cosmetic additives, toys, flooring, and dust, as well as differences in lifestyles, diet, and living environment. In conclusion, although the health risks associated with the EDCs exposure encountered by children in Hong Kong through water and air intake in kindergartens did not appear to be concerning, the health effects of low-dose and long-term exposure to these chemicals cannot be neglected.

18300919.label: Major findings and research outcome
18300919.value: Seven perfluorinated and polyfluorinated substances (PFASs), namely perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA), perfluorodecanoic acid (PFDA), perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA), perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS), perfluoroheptanoic acid (PFHpA), perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA), and perfluoro-1,10- decanedicarboxylic acid (PFDDA), were evaluated in urine and hair samples from children (age: 4-6 years), airborne particles sampled at 17 kindergartens, and tap water and bottled water samples. All target PFASs were detected in at least 32% of urine samples, with geometric mean concentrations ranging from 0.18 to 2.97 ng/L. PFOA was the major PFAS detected in hair, urine, and drinking water samples. In airborne particles, PFOA, PFDA, and PFHpA were dominant. The highest PFAS concentrations were detected in airborne particles in kindergartens. Although a significant difference in PFAS concentrations in hair samples was observed between boys and girls, no significant sex-related difference in urinary PFAS or paired PFAS (hair/urine) concentrations was found. The estimated daily intakes of PFASs through drinking water and airborne particles indicated potential health risks. The study concluded that PFASs are ubiquitously present in the studied samples, and the health effects of low-dose and long-term exposure require further attention. Children from 17 kindergartens in Hong Kong are exposed to various forms of plasticizers (phthalates, bisphenol analogs, BPDP, and BDP). The EDIs of bisphenol analogs through water intake and air inhalation in kindergartens could account for up to 6.4% of the daily exposure of children in Hong Kong, as determined by back-calculations from the concentrations of these analytes in samples of the children’s urine. These data indicate that non-dietary exposure may serve as a route of human exposure to these potentially harmful compounds. Investigating the exposure of children to EDCs found that children are more susceptible to EDC exposure than adults, which can lead to various health risks, including developmental issues, reproductive impairment, and obesity. The geometric mean concentrations of phthalate esters metabolites (mPAEs) and bisphenols (BPs) in children's urine were determined. The levels were consistent with global averages. Non-target analysis identified a total of 1069 compounds, with 106 being EDCs commonly found in food, cosmetics, and drugs. Potential sources of EDCs included dietary and cosmetic additives, toys, flooring, and dust, as well as differences in lifestyle, diet, and living environment. Notably, age was found to have a significant impact on EDC exposure. The quantified EDCs, specifically mPAEs and BPs, were found to pose possible health risks to 60% of the children. Additionally, the presence of caffeine in children's urine was a notable finding that warrants further attention. Family clustering was observed for mPAEs, suggesting the role of family diet structure and habits. For BPs, differences in levels and correlations were noted between the different regions.

18300919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18300919.value: 1.To ensure that children’s health can be protected, an examination of the exposure of children to emerging plasticizers is urgently needed. Such an investigation should evaluate the toxicological characteristics of these chemicals and investigate all possible routes of exposure. 2.To fully confirm the sources of EDCs exposure, future studies should sample and analyze the indoor environment, as well as children’s toys and food. This information will help inform policies and practices aimed at reducing exposure to EDCs and mitigating potential health risks.

18300919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18300919.value: The research investigated endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) such as plasticizer contamination, perfluoroalkyl substances, phthalate esters metabolites (mPAEs), and bisphenols (BPs) found in the urine and hair of preschool children, highlighting serious health implications. Plasticizers, commonly used in toys and containers, are present in children’s urine and hair in Hong Kong. This raises concerns about potential health risks, as these chemicals can disrupt hormonal functions and affect child development. Perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), are used in products like non-stick cookware and food packaging. The study showed that preschool children are exposed to these harmful substances, which may lead to various health issues, including developmental delays. Exposure levels of EDCs in the urine of children, between families in different regions were compared. EDCs can interfere with hormones, posing risks for growth and development. Overall, the study emphasized the urgent need to monitor and minimize chemical exposure in young children to safeguard their health and future. They underline the significance of understanding how everyday products can impact vulnerable populations.

18301119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18301119.value: The rapid development of deep learning in the past decade has led to many remarkable applications, ranging from speech recognition, which achieved human-level performance, to Go-playing algorithms, which beat top professional players. Surprisingly, despite the increasing number of applications using deep learning, we only have a limited understanding of their remarkable performance. In particular, many deep learning applications apply deep neural networks (DNN) to infer the non-trivial input-output relations on labeled datasets. The internal representations in DNNs, the mechanism by which they arrive at good decisions, and how the over-parametrized DNNs avoid over-fitting and achieve high generalizability are not fully understood. This incomplete understanding may cause fatal dangers, as deep learning is now commonly applied to vital applications such as medical image analyses and self-driving cars. In the proposed project, we will apply tools in statistical physics to derive a fundamental understanding of DNNs, which can be applied to boost their performance and most importantly reduce any risks when DNNs are used in vital applications. We remark that statistical physics tools have already been applied to analyze shadow neural networks to obtain their macroscopic properties inaccessible by tools in other areas, but the understanding of DNNs via statistical physics is far from complete. Here, we aim to (1) develop an improved fundamental understanding on DNNs in terms of their loss landscape, training dynamics, and most importantly their remarkable generalization performance; (2) establish theoretical frameworks to analyze DNNs, by drawing an analogy with spin glasses and disordered systems; these frameworks will play a crucial role in the future theoretical studies and understanding of deep learning; (3) understand and leverage the dilemma of exploration and exploitation in training DNNs, and introduce new protocols to be used in combination with the state-of-the-art algorithms for better training and generalization of DNNs. The above tasks are challenging, but our successful attempts will be highly rewarding, as they will provide a fundamental understanding to resolve the mystery underlying DNNs, which will lead to important insights on a wide range of existing and future deep learning applications. 深度學習在近年的快速發展為我們帶來了很多重要應用，例如語音識別及圍棋算法等。儘管它的應用越來越多，我們郤對其了解其有限。深度學習一般利用深層神經網絡（Deep Neural Networks, DNN）來推斷數據標記，但我們對DNN的內部處理，達成良好決策的機制，及其如何避免過度擬合併達至高預測能力尚未完全理解。雖然深度學習的應用大多有良好表現，但我們對其理解的不足，可能會在重要應用如醫學圖像分析和自動駕駛汽車等帶來危險。 在本項目中，我們將應用統計物理學的工具來分析DNN。統計物理工具已被應用於分析淺層神經網絡，並獲得了重要成果。這次我們以統計物理工具來分析DNN，研究成果將有利於提高深度學習應用的效能，並且降低其使用風險。 我們的研究目標如下：（1）增加對DNN的基礎理解；（2）通過參考自旋玻璃和無序系統的分析，建立分析DNN的理論框架；這些框架將在未來對DNN的理論研究中發揮重要作用；（3）平衡DNN學習階段中優化算法的探索和聚焦，從而引入新的優化策略。雖然研究目標不易達到，但成果將有助於我們對DNN建立基礎理解，並對其日益廣泛的應用有著重要影響。

18301119.label: Realisation of objectives
18301119.value: OBJECTIVE (1) (a) In [1] (Liao et al, and Yeung*, under review by NeurIPS, formerly NIPS, one of the most prominent conferences in machine learning and computational neuroscience), we introduced new approaches to analyze the loss landscape of deep neural networks (DNNs) and gained new understandings, which include (1) the absence of large barriers in the loss landscape between any pair of permutated but identical trained solutions of DNNs; (2) with an increasing width of the DNN hidden layers, the transition from uni-modal to multi-modal distribution of the Euclidean distance between pairs of trained solutions; the multiple solutions are trained for the same DNN architecture based on the same dataset; (3) the similarity between the dendrograms obtained from the hierarchical clustering of DNN trained solutions and those dendrograms obtained for the low-energy states of spin glass, (4) the increase of the ruggedness of DNN loss landscape with the width of their hidden layers, etc. These results provide a new macroscopic understanding on the DNN loss landscape, leading to implications on their training and generalizability. (b) In [2] (Tamanna and Yeung*), we utilized interpolation and dimensionality reduction to visualize the loss landscape of DNNs, especially the dependence of the number of local minima and the height of loss barriers in the loss landscape, on the amount of data. This again provides a new understanding on the loss landscape of DNNs. (c) In [3] (Po and Yeung*), we developed a new approach called “Coarse-grained Energy Landscapes” (CELs) to reveal completely the energy landscape of small spin glass and combinatorial optimization problems, which also shows that the system can be trapped in sub-optimal states for a long time; CELs can be adopted to visualize the loss landscape of DNNs, and hence the trapping dynamics in sub-optimal solutions. OBJECTIVE (2) (a) In [2] (Tamanna and Yeung*), we revealed that the ruggedness of the loss landscape of DNNs, indicated by the number of local minima within a specific distance, is largely dependent on the nature and the size of the datasets, which are difficult to be authentically modeled/represented in theoretical analyses. Thus, random datasets are usually assumed to facilitate theoretical analyses, which may lead to a large discrepancy between theoretical results and real DNNs in practise. (b) In [4] (Li and Yeung*), we examined the discrepancies between the simulation, and the theoretical results of multi-armed bandits obtained from the path-integral framework, i.e. the one applied by Li on the analyses of DNNs in 2018. In [4], we concluded that the assumptions made under the large deviation principle are the main cause of the discrepancies between the theoretical and simulation results, which have important implications on the analyses of DNNs by the same path-integral framework. (c) In [6] and [7], we have analyzed big datasets including consumers’ ratings on Amazon products and Netflix movies, the citation network of the American Physical Society (APS), scientist co-authorship networks and Facebook friendship networks. These datasets can be used for analyses by DNNs to reveal the discrepancies in the theoretical analyses of DNNs. OBJECTIVE (3) (a) In our submitted manuscript entitled “Exploring Loss Landscapes through the lens of Spin Glass Theory” [1] (Liao et al, and Yeung*, under review), we established new approaches to analyze DNNs’ loss landscape by drawing an analogy with spin glass, in particular borrowing methodologies developed in the studies of spin glass to analyze DNNs. Especially, our new approaches include (1) protocols of real-variable random walk on the DNN loss landscapes, (2) newly introduced permutation-interpolation protocols, which overcome the degeneracy caused by the permutation of nodes in the hidden layers, (3) dendrograms based on the hierarchical clustering of multiple trained solutions for the same architecture of DNNs based on the same dataset, (4) analysis of the dependence of generalizability on the ruggedness of loss landscapes. All these are new approaches for the analysis of DNNs. (b) In [4] (Li and Yeung*), the theoretical path-integral framework has been applied to analyze the dynamics of multi-armed bandits for the first time, the results and insights obtained, e.g. the agreement and discrepancies between the theoretical and simulation results, are relevant to the analyses of the multiple layers in DNNs by the same path-integral framework. (c) In [5] (Li*, Saad* and Yeung*), we examined bilevel optimization, i.e. co-optimization of two levels of variables interdependent on each other. New message-passing algorithms were derived in [x] and applied on two exemplar flow networks. Such bilevel optimization is relevant to the co-optimization of the two levels of variables in DNNs, namely hyper-parameters and the weight variables. (d) In [3] (Po and Yeung*), we introduced the method of course-grained energy landscapes (CELs) to reveal the complete energy landscape of small spin glass and combinatorial optimization problems. By formulating the complete transition matrix between the nodes in CELs, the dynamics of the systems at an arbitrary temperature for an arbitrarily long-time can be obtained, leading to results such as the decrease in ground-state probabilities as temperature decreases. Such new approaches will provide a platform for analyzing the training dynamics and the generalizability of DNNs, a unique framework focusing on small systems and may lead to analytical results out of reach by existing approaches. OBJECTIVE (4) (a) In [4] (Li and Yeung*), we analyzed the exploration-exploitation dilemma in multi-armed bandits, a representative model which exhibit exploration-exploitation dilemma; specifically, both of our theoretical and simulation analyses showed that an unlucky initial condition with a strong exploitation leads to a long stay on the sub-optimal choice before discovering the optimal ones. These systems share similarity with the training process of DNNs, since only a finite time is provided to train the DNNs to identify a set of parameters with sufficiently small loss, leading to a new understanding on the exploration-exploitation dilemma in training DNNs. (b) In [3] (Po and Yeung*), by constructing the complete transition matrix among all states in small optimization problems, we found that a rapid exploitation traps the system in sub-optimal states for a long time. Interestingly, we found that instead of pure exploitation, there is an optimal trade-off between exploration and exploitation (i.e. a small but non-zero temperature in [3]) in efficiently identifying the optimal states. This again provides an improved understanding on the exploration-exploitation dilemma in DNNs. OBJECTIVE (5) (a) In [1] (Liao et al, and Yeung*), we found that DNNs with a flatter loss landscape has a higher generalizability. These results lead to algorithmic implications on the training of DNNs if one can smoothen the loss landscape, e.g. adding regularization to the loss/cost function for training DNNs. (b) In [3] (Po and Yeung*), we showed how an over-rapidly decreasing temperature can trap the optimization process in local minima. The established framework of coarse-grained energy landscapes (CELs) and the derived transition matrix [3] can provide insights on how noise can be reduced, e.g. in stochastic gradient descent (SGD) studied in [1], in training DNNs to improve the training speed or the resultant generalizability. (c) In [4] (Li and Yeung*), the theoretical path-integral frameworks allow us to optimize the exploration and exploitation parameters for optimizing the final outcome, which leads to new paradigm in tuning the exploration and exploitation parameters in training DNNs.

18301119.label: Major findings and research outcome
18301119.value: (1) IMPROVED UNDERSTANDING (a) In [1] (Liao et al, and Yeung*), we revealed the dependence of (i) dendrograms and hierarchical clustering of trained DNN solutions, and (ii) Euclidean distance between solution pairs, on the width of the hidden layers; such observations may suggest the existence of different phases in DNNs as in spin glass. (b) In [1] (Liao et al, and Yeung*), remarkably, we found that there is no large loss barriers between any pair of permutated but identical trained solutions of DNNs. (c) In [2] (Tamanna and Yeung*), we revealed that the ruggedness of DNN loss landscape, as indicated by the number of local minima, is largely dependent on the nature and the size of the datasets. (d) In [4] (Li and Yeung*), we revealed that for systems with exploration-exploitation dilemma, such as the training of DNNs, an unlucky initial condition with a strong exploitation leads to a long stay in sub-optimal choices. (e) In [3] (Po and Yeung*), we showed how an over-rapidly decreasing temperature can trap the optimization process in local minima for a long time. (2) ADVANCES IN METHODOLOGY (a) In [1] (Liao et al, and Yeung*), we introduced new methodologies to analyze DNNs borrowed from the analyses of spin glass, representing a new perspective and a new set of tools to analyze DNNs. (b) In [4] (Li and Yeung*), we adopted a path-integral framework to analyze the dynamics of a multi-armed bandits, especially relevant to the understanding of the exploration-exploitation dilemma. (c) In [5] (Li*, Saad* and Yeung*), we applied message-passing approaches for bilevel optimization, a potentially new perspective and framework to co-optimize the hyper-parameters and the weight variables in training DNNs. (d) In [3] (Po and Yeung*), we introduced a new method of course-grained energy landscapes (CELs) to reveal the complete energy landscape and transition matrix of small spin glass and combinatorial optimization problems, enables us to reveal the non-equilibrium dynamics of the systems for an arbitrarily long-time out of reach by existing approaches. (3) APPLICATIONS (a) In [1] (Liao et al, and Yeung*), we found that DNNs with a flatter loss landscape have a higher generalizability, leading to algorithmic implications on training DNNs such as adding regularization to smooth the landscape (b) In [3] (Po and Yeung*) and [5] (Li and Yeung*), both CELs and the path-integral approaches can be used to provide algorithmic insights to optimize exploration-exploitation dilemma in training DNNs.

18301119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18301119.value: We will continue to strengthen the analyses of deep neural networks (DNNs) by drawing analogy with the theoretical and empirical analyses of spin glasses, especially on the analyses of loss landscapes, as this research direction provides insights on DNNs from a physics perspective, leading to a more fundamental understanding on DNNs’ high generalizability and its ability to overcome over-fitting out-of-reach by conventional analyses. Building on the findings and the theoretical frameworks developed in the project, we will (a) extend the analyses to DNNs beyond the feed-forward architecture, such as graph neural networks, recurrent neural networks, etc., to further understand their generalizability and emergent behaviors based on the difference in their loss landscapes (b) generalize the theoretical frameworks developed in this project to analyze complex systems other than DNNs (c) apply the algorithmic approaches on the training of DNNs for different applications, to verify the benefits brought by an improved trade-off between exploration and exploitation (d) further examine the impact of the nature of input datasets on the loss landscapes of DNNs and thus on their training and the generalizability, Collaboration with existing collaborators and other research groups is being explored to achieve the above future objectives.

18301119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18301119.value: Deep learning has been developing rapidly in the past decade and has led to many remarkable applications. Nevertheless, our understanding of their remarkable performance is incomplete, which may cause fatal dangers in vital applications such as medical image analyses and self-driving cars. In this project, we applied tools in statistical physics to derive a more fundamental understanding of DNNs, especially through the analyses of the loss landscape of DNNs by drawing an analogy with and borrowing tools from the analyses of spin glass. In particular, we found that the inter-relationship among the trained solutions of DNNs shares similarity with the low-energy states in spin glass, suggesting a similarity between their fundamental mechanism. In terms of methodologies, several analytical approaches have been introduced in this project and applied to analyze systems related to training DNNs. In terms of applications, insights obtained from the theoretical and the empirical analyses in this project have led to insights on improving training algorithms of DNNs, especially on the balance between exploration and exploitation. All in all, this project has improved our fundamental understanding, established new analytical tools and algorithmic implications on DNNs through the lens of statistical physics.

18600019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18600019.value: 學生自我評估是目前評估改革的核心內容。許多國家包括美國、英國、澳大利亞和新西蘭等的教育政策都提倡學生自我評估，強調評估的形成性目的和技能的發展，以滿足未來社會的需求。香港現行的評核政策亦期望教師讓學生參與課堂評估活動。學生應該依靠自我評估，而不是頻繁的考試，去了解自己的學習需要、學習重點和優勢。研究指出，自我評估能提高學生的評估判斷能力、自主學習能力和終生學習能力。然而，有什麽具體課堂活動能促進學生自我評估，我們知之甚少。此外，對於自我評估過程與認知/元認知（例如，自主學習，學業表現）和學習的情感方面（例如，學業情緒）的動態交互作用，研究也較少。因此，本研究的目標是通過實驗來探究兩種不同的促進學生自我評估方法的效能，以及揭示自我評估過程如何影響學生學習的機制。通過在自然情境中進行研究，可以較好地確定這些方法的可行性和實用性。本研究的結果將有助理解學生自我評估的過程如何作為一種學習的策略，以致在政策和實踐方面被廣泛採用的潛力，還有其對促進學習評估的重要性。 在先導研究結果(Yan, Chiu, & Ko, under review)的基礎上，本研究採用準實驗設計，將參與者進行配對(King, Nielsen, Coberley, Pope, & Wells, 2011)，并收集時間序列數據 (Schmitz & Perels, 2011; Schmitz & Wiese, 2006)。本研究包括兩個實驗。實驗一將考察兩種介入措施（即是：自我評估日誌和自我評估訓練）的效果，並探究自我評估過程與學生學習的動態交互作用。參加者將包括同年級三個班的中學生（N=90）以及同年級三個班的小學生（N=90）。三個班級將會被隨機分配到兩個介入組或控制組。在實驗二中，我們將會檢驗自我評估過程中不同活動各自的效能。實驗組將實施一個綜合介入措施（即是：自我評估日誌加上自我評估訓練）。同年級兩個班的中學生（N=60）以及同年級兩個班的小學生（N=60）將會被隨機分配到介入組或控制組。在這兩個實驗中，所選的班級將根據學業能力進行配對，並且由同一名教師授課。實驗將安排在每周有頻繁課次和作業的科目（例如，核心課程語文、英文或數學），以便最大限度收集數據。 本研究的一個特點是期望能盡量發揮對教育政策和實踐的影響。在自然學習情境中進行研究，確保了自我評估為學生提供真實的學習機會，並能被教師有效運用於真實情境中。這些情境有助於揭示自我評估如何促進學生的自主學習、帶來更佳學業情緒和促進更好學習結果的機制。研究亦會考察自我評估的準確性，以及自我評估與學業情緒的關係。了解這種關係將有助於向教師提供教學建議，以幫助學生進行有意義的自我評估。更重要的是，本研究有可能進一步發展自我評估理論，幫助學生改善形成性評估以指導他們的學習，並為教育政策的制訂和家長角色的定位提供參考。

18600019.label: Realisation of objectives
18600019.value: All three objectives have been 100% achieved. Two experiments using intact classes have been conducted. Both experiments were conducted in one secondary school and one primary school. Experiment 1 addressed Objectives #1 and #2, while Experiment 2 addressed Objective #3. Experiment 1: This experiment has two sub-experiments: one conducted on Primary 4 (Experiment 1-a) students and one on Secondary 5 students (Experiment 1-b). In Experiment 1-a and Experiment 1-b, three classes of Primary 4/Secondary 5 students, with comparable academic ability and taught by the same teacher, were recruited, respectively. They were randomly assigned to one of the three conditions: self-assessment diary condition (Nprimary4 = 34; Nsecondary5 = 33), self-assessment training condition (Nprimary4 = 38; Nsecondary5 = 31), and control condition (N primary4 =31; Nsecondary5 = 28). The total sample size is 195, while the proposed sample size is 180. Participants’ academic performance, self-assessment accuracy, self-assessment practice, self-regulated learning, and academic emotions were assessed through pre-, post-, and delayed post-tests/surveys. Objective #1: The results showed that the two different self-assessment interventions (i.e., self-assessment diary and self-assessment training) significantly enhanced students’ academic performance, self-assessment practice, and self-regulated learning for both primary and secondary students. However, the effects of self-assessment interventions on self-assessment accuracy and academic emotions were not significant. Objective #2: The diary data permit a time-series of students’ self-assessment data to uncover relationships among different learning variables. We conducted linear trend analyses with diary (time) as the predictor and self-assessment practice and self-assessment accuracy as dependent variables. We also tested for significant differences in the self-regulated learning processes, in particular Plan to Improve, across diaries and students. The results showed a significant positive linear trend over the intervention period for self-assessment practice, but not for self-assessment accuracy. Furthermore, students who were younger or used their own standards to self-assess were less likely than others to plan for learning. A journal article based on the findings of Experiment 1 is currently under preparation. Experiment 2: This experiment also has two sub-experiments: one conducted on Primary 6 (Experiment 2-a) students and one on Secondary 2 students (Experiment 2-b). In Experiment 2-a and Experiment 2-b, two classes of Primary 6/Secondary 2 students, with comparable academic ability and taught by the same teacher, were recruited, respectively. They were randomly assigned to one of the two conditions: experimental condition (i.e., self-assessment diary + training; Nprimary6 = 25; Nsecondary2 = 32), and control condition (N primary6 =23; Nsecondary2 = 35). The total sample size is 115, slightly lower than the proposed sample size 120. Participants’ academic performance, self-assessment accuracy, self-assessment practice, self-regulated learning, and academic emotions were assessed through pre-, post-, and delayed post-tests/surveys. Objective #3: The results of the experiment-control comparison were similar to experiment 1. The combined self-assessment interventions (i.e., diary + training) significantly enhanced students’ academic performance, self-assessment practice, and self-regulated learning, but not for self-assessment accuracy and academic emotions. Interrupted time-series analyses were applied to test the eﬀect of each training session separately. The results showed that the “feedback-seeking” training session significantly increased students’ feedback-seeking behaviour; the “determining assessment criteria” and “self-reflection” training sessions did not bring significant changes. A journal article based on the findings of Experiment 2 is currently under preparation. Other outcomes In addition to the proposed experiments, we have extended our research agenda around the project’s overall theme. For example, we have conducted a comprehensive review of the effects of self-assessment and peer-assessment interventions. Two meta-analysis articles have been published, including “The effect of self-assessment on academic performance and the role of the explicitness: A meta-analysis” in Assessment & Evaluation in Higher Education (Yan, Wang, Boud, & Lao, 2021) and “Effects of self-assessment and peer-assessment interventions on academic performance: A meta-analysis” in Educational Research Review (Yan, Lao, Panadero, Fernández-Castilla, Yang & Yang, 2022). We also developed short self-assessment practice scale and published a journal article “Developing a short form of the Self-assessment Practices Scale: Psychometric Evidence” in Frontiers in Education (Yan, 2020). This instrument has greatly facilitated the implementation of the experimental studies. As the proposed study extensively investigated the relationship between self-assessment and feedback seeking, we have published a conceptual paper “Self-assessment is about more than self: The enabling role of feedback literacy” in Assessment & Evaluation in Higher Education (Yan & Carless, 2022). Furthermore, we extended this line of research by exploring self-assessment interventions other than diary. We have conducted an additional small experiment examing the effect of self-assessment mindmaps on student learning and published an article “Enhancing students’ self-efficacy in creativity and learning performance in the context of English learning: The use of self-assessment mind-maps” in Frontiers in Psychology (Yan, Lee, Hui, & Lao, 2022).

18600019.label: Major findings and research outcome
18600019.value: The major findings generated from this project have the potential to inform theoretical development, classroom practices, and policy-making related to self-assessment. • Key finding 1 (effects of self-assessment interventions): Yan et al.’s (2022) meta-analysis of 227 effect sizes from 69 independent studies indicated that, in general, self-assessment intervention (g = 0.585) had meaningful effects on academic performance. However, self-assessment process is complex, and the positive impact comes only with appropriate design and implementation. Yan et al. (2021) highlighted the importance of making self-assessment explicit because self-assessment interventions involving explicit feedback from others on students’ performance had a significantly larger effect size (g = .664) than those without explicit feedback (g = .213). The two experiments further verified the positive impact of self-assessment interventions on students’ academic performance, self-assessment practice, and self-regulated learning. Significance: Despite the conceptual consensus on the benefits of self-assessment, empirical evidence is not conclusive. The published two meta-analyses and the two experimental studies (under preparation) offered a systematic account of the effect of self-assessment on student learning. More importantly, the design and successful implementation of an effective, low-cost intervention (i.e., self-assessment diary) shed light on how to create sustainable changes in classrooms. Nevertheless, the non-significant effect on self-assessment accuracy and academic emotions reminded us that these interventions could be further improved. • Key finding 2 (the dynamic relationship among students’ demographics, self-assessment practice, and self-regulated learning): The results showed students’ self-assessment practice could be enhanced through structured, explicit activities. But self-assessment accuracy appeared more difficult to be improved. Given that students’ academic performances have increased, this finding echoes the argument, including the PI’s studies, that engagement in self-assessment itself, regardless of its accuracy, can improve learning performance. We also found that students who were younger or used their own standards to self-assess were less likely than others to plan for learning. Significance: Most studies do not track student use of self-assessment throughout a course of learning, so the dynamic nature of students’ evolving self-assessment capabilities in light of task performance is unknown. This study explored the dynamic relationship between the self-assessment process and various learning variables including academic emotions, self-regulated learning, and academic performance. Our findings on the predictors of plan to improve, which is a crucial link of different self-regulation circles, show the importance of a complex model of demographics, assessment criteria, and self-knowledge for informing interventions to promote sustainable self-regulation. • Key finding 3 (the roles of different actions in self-assessment processes): Yan and Carless’s (2022) conceptual paper highlighted the important role of feedback-seeking in the self-assessment process. Experiment 2 further proved that feedback-seeking training had the most significant impact. Significance: Previous studies treat self-assessment, mostly as a whole, as the independent variable, without disentangling its component processes. Less is known about how different actions in the self-assessment process interact with learning processes and outcomes. Our findings filled this research gap and informed the design of self-assessment activities.

18600019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18600019.value: This project has contributed to an in-depth understanding of the process and effect of self-assessment practices students engage in during learning. The findings of this study shed light on the mechanism by which the self-assessment process influences students’ learning outcomes and have the potential to inform the design of effective and sustainable self-assessment interventions in classrooms. There are three directions to develop this line of research further. First, the findings of this project justified the inclusion of self-assessment in schooling. Future studies can explore more diversified self-assessment strategies, instruments, and tools, taking into account student characteristics and contextual factors with an aim to maximise the positive impact of self-assessment on student learning. An initial attempt has been made by the project team. We have explored the effect of a new self-assessment intervention, i.e., mindmaps, on student learning and published a journal article in 2022. Second, most studies focus on the pedagogical aspects of the self-assessment process, leaving psychological antecedents and consequences of self-assessment processes largely understudied in literature. The non-significant impact of self-assessment on academic emotions revealed in this project should not discourage attention to this line of research. In contrast, more research is necessary for this direction to unpack the psychological mechanism of self-assessment. Third, as both teachers and students play important roles in the self-assessment process, it is crucial to develop the formative assessment literacy of teachers and students in order to optimise the impact of self-assessment activities. Thus, it will be meaningful to design teacher professional development programmes based on the findings of this project and evaluate the effectiveness of the developed programmes.

18600019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18600019.value: Student self-assessment has become a central agenda of assessment reform in the Hong Kong education system because it promises to enhance learner agency and self-regulated learning. This project has addressed three important issues: 1) investigating the effect of two self-assessment interventions on students’ learning outcomes; 2) exploring the dynamic relationship between the self-assessment process and various learning variables; and 3) disentangling the self-assessment process and examining the distinct effect of different actions in the processes. This project has contributed to an in-depth understanding of the process and effect of self-assessment practices students engage in during learning. The positive effect of self-assessment demonstrated in this study justified its inclusion in schooling at the classroom practice and policy-making levels. The findings of this study shed light on the mechanism by which the self-assessment process influenced students’ learning outcomes and laid a foundation for future research in this field. By informing the design of effective and sustainable self-assessment interventions in classrooms, this study can contribute to the long-term goal of worldwide assessment reform focusing on the formative purpose.

18600319.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18600319.value: 漢代(公元前206−公元220年)古玻璃探究

18600319.label: Project Objectives
18600319.value: to identify and archive different glass items that are in the form of Chinese ritual objects to understand the reasons incentivised the choice of adopting glass to manufacture the objects to investigate the contemporary socio-cultural notions and beliefs embedded in the material of glass to evaluate the status and materiality of glass in relation to other materials in the contemporary context
