18600319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18600319.value: Most research of early Chinese glass has focused on the issues of origin and considered this medium primarily as an evidence of China’s contacts with outside civilisations. This research, on the contrary, will explore the subject of glass in "Chinese form", which is generally agreed was locally manufactured. Because of the ostensive resemblance, many glass objects unearthed in Han burial sites have been confused with stone or ceramic materials, and some even have been mistaken for jade in archaeological reports. Therefore, this project will first cautiously investigate the feature descriptions and documentation of the relevant items in the reports and conduct firsthand study of the objects. A rigorous re-examination of the information will bring the glass pieces that have been disregarded and excluded in previous studies into the research. Because of its similarity to jade, glass had been generally perceived as a less precious substitute material for jade in ancient China. But judging by recently discovered glass pieces, the use of glass during the Han period, particularly in burials, was not that simple and did not necessarily follow that logic. By relying on archaeological material and reports of scientific analyses, and adopting the interdisciplinary approach of art historical stylistic analyses and contextual material studies, this research will address the importance of glass in Han burial rituals. It may illuminate the role of glass in contemporaneous perceptions of immortality, and will review the hierarchy of material in the ritual context. 至今大部分關於中國古玻璃的研究，都集中於討論其起源問題，亦將古玻璃物料的出現，視作當時中外文化交流的憑證。然而，本研究聚焦探討那些視為中國本地製作、形制亦為中國所特有的漢代古玻璃製品。由於中國古玻璃物料的外觀與玉石和陶器肖似，因而古玻璃製品不時與玉石或陶器混淆。因此，本研究首先會將不同的資料謹慎比對和進行實物觀摩，以圖重新檢視和釐清報告當中被混淆的古玻璃器物。此外，同樣由於外觀相近，中國古玻璃一直被視為玉器的廉價替代品，但是從一些考古材料顯示，此情況不是如此簡單和必然。此研究將會依據考古出土材料和相關的分析報告，以物質文化及風格分式等研究方法，重塑漢代墓葬中古玻璃的使用情況和意義，並探究當時古玻璃這種物質與長生思想的關聯，從而審視不同物料在漢墓中所擔當的角色。

18600719.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18600719.value: 校本價值教育課程中的權力共享：對批判教育學實踐的啟示

18600719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18600719.value: 本研究旨在把批判教育學的理論和實踐連接，以及深入了解如何透過加強學生的批判思維技巧以達至教育目標。專於批判教育學的學者探究了對“儲存式教育”（Freire, 1996）的解解決方案，並提供多種對學校教育的建議，例如“提問式教育”、“對話”（Freire, 1996）、“批判意識”（Freire, 1974/2005）、“參與性教學”（hooks, 1994）及民主教室文化（Shor, 1996）。然而，批判教育學仍未得到充分研究，對其之理解仍局限於理論層面，並主要集中在社會教育及語言教育的學科。相比在高等教育的批判教育學研究，較少研究在小學教育和非英語教學的教室中。在香港小學教育中，對批判教育學實踐的研究更是罕見。即使Moorhouse（2014）曾以批判式讀寫理論把批判教育學實踐於香港小學的教室，在香港的研究仍主要集中在理解英語教室的文化（e.g., Lin, 1999, Lin, 2007, Sinn, 2010）。近年香港在政治、社會及教育系統上的緊張局勢使香港學校成為研究教育與社會發展關係的有趣個案。利用批判教育學有助理解學校的社會文化層面，以及它們在促進人文社會進步中的角色。研究將採用個案研究模式全面了解所探討的個案。研究場所將會是五間小學的二十個教室，並主要集中在校內不同科目中的校本價值教育課程（如道德教育、宗教教育和常識科）。數據將通過文件分析、課堂觀察及分析，以及與校長、課程主任、教師和學生的訪談來搜集。期望研究成果會為批判教育學的理論框架作出貢獻。同時，並加深了解校本價值教育課程作為非語言科目，其於小學實踐的機會與困難，以補充西方和香港這課題的文獻。

18601219.label: Project Title(Chinese)
18601219.value: 政策轉移與政策趨同:多邊組織與亞洲的競爭規制政策轉移

18601219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18601219.value: Historically, scholarship into policy formulation and policy design has been strongly influenced by Weberian conceptions of bureaucracy. At the apex of bureaucratic hierarchies, political leadership and senior bureaucrats formulate policy, while ministries and other organs of the state manage functional issues associated with implementation and day-to-day administration. Policy scientists have thus focused their theory building efforts on elite bureaucratic actors who are seen to manage the policy formulation process, control information inputs, structure and interpret the policy problem and provide policy designs for their management and political accommodation. In the contemporary era, however, these theoretical frameworks are increasingly problematic. Substantial growth in the number of transnational policy regimes that govern complex exchange activities (e.g., trade, product certification, food safety and manufacturing standards) along with an expanding number of activities subject to extra-territorial policy coordination, often by multilateral organisations (e.g., exchange rate and macro-prudential regulatory standards, accounting standards), is causing the locus of policy knowledge, policy formulation and policy design to originate in non-traditional and non-domestic settings. As a consequence, the sources of policy knowledge, expertise and ideas are becoming more exogenous; situated in specialist transnational communities of practice, technical and professional associations and multilateral organisations. These developments both facilitate and deepen international policy coordination and policy diffusion, with policy makers now more likely to source or adopt policy knowledge and policy designs from other jurisdictions or expert knowledge communities, leading to what some analysists have identified as the increasing prevalence of policy convergence. This project seeks to understand and map the impact of exogenous policy knowledge on policy formulation, policy design and practice and the prospects of policy convergence. It does so by analysing the formulation of competition policy in three case study countries, Indonesia, Malaysia and South Korean. Specifically, it seeks to analyse the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and the role it plays in ideational formation and how this impacts and shapes the policy preferences of domestic policy actors leading to the adoption of specific competition policy designs and practices. 從歷史角度來，關於政策規劃和政策設計的研究受到韋伯主義官僚制理論的深刻影響。在官僚體制的頂端，政治領袖和高層官僚規劃政策方案，而政策部門來負責執行和日常行政的具體事宜。因此，政策科學家將理論構建的核心聚焦於那些在官僚體系中進行政策規劃和設計的精英們。 然而，在當今時代，這些理論框架越來越難以解釋現實世界。應對複雜問題的跨國政策體制和以多邊組織為代表的跨境政策協調如雨後春筍般快速增長。與此相應，政策規劃和政策設計的知識理論需要在非傳統和非內政情境下進行發展。因此，政策科學的理論知識和理念變得越來越來自於跨國團體、專業協會和多邊組織，因而更具『外生性』。所有這些發展都加速和深化了國際政策協調和政策擴散。政策制定者越來越多採用其他國家和地區的政策理念。很多觀察家發現，全球範圍內出現越來越多的政策趨同現象。 本研究計劃旨在分析『外生性』的政策理念和政策設計，以及政策趨同問題。本研究聚焦亞洲範圍內三個國家競爭政策的規劃設計，包括印尼、馬來西亞和韓國。具體來說，我們將深入分析經濟合作與發展組織 (OECD)如何形塑這些國家的政策理念，以及如何影響它們在競爭政策制定過程中的想法和偏好。

18602119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18602119.value: Reading comprehension is conceptualized as the capacity to extract or construct an appropriate mental representation or situational model from written text (Hoover & Gough, 1990). As one of the most influential models in the field, the Simple View of Reading (SVR) postulates that reading comprehension (R) is a product of decoding (D) and linguistic comprehension (L) skills, and can be expressed as: R = D x L (Gough & Tunmer, 1986; Hoover & Gough, 1990). A recent Direct and Indirect Effect Model of Reading (Kim, 2017) expanded the SVR and revealed that word reading and linguistic comprehension completely mediated the relationship of language and cognitive skills to reading comprehension. That is, language and cognitive skills predict reading comprehension completely through word reading and linguistic comprehension. The proposed study investigates the direct and indirect associations of executive functioning (i.e., working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility), lexical quality (i.e., morphological awareness, orthographic awareness), with word reading and linguistic comprehension, in predicting reading comprehension among Chinese primary school grade 3 students across Hong Kong (with inconsistent oral-written language arising from linguistic distance (differences between spoken and written languages)) and Shenzhen (with perfectly consistent oral-written language). Three possible models are hypothesized. First, executive functioning predicts reading comprehension directly beyond word reading and linguistic comprehension. Second, executive functioning predict reading comprehension indirectly through lexical quality, word reading and linguistic comprehension. Alternatively, there may be both direct and indirect roles of executive functioning in Chinese reading comprehension. Given previous literature (Chung & McBride- Chang, 2011; Kim, 2017), the second or third possibility involving indirect effects is more likely to be supported. Notably, we expected that executive functioning likely plays a more salient role in reading comprehension in Hong Kong than in Shenzhen, because linguistic distance may heavily tax cognitive resources. The study can impact the field in three aspects. First, it potentially establish executive functioning as a fundamentally essential component in the reading theories. Second, with the evidence from a deep orthography (i.e., Chinese), it contributes to the understanding of the role of writing system variation in reading universally (Daniels & Share, 2018). Third, it leads ultimately to a better understanding of reading comprehension challenges in the Hong Kong context arising from the linguistic distance. Findings of the project offers important implications on effective practice in education in Hong Kong, particularly on how linguistic distance taxes cognitive resources in language learning.

18602119.label: Realisation of objectives
18602119.value: The study recruited two groups of primary school students: 266 native Cantonese-speaking students from Hong Kong (mean age: 111.7 months) and 213 native Mandarin-speaking students from Mainland China (mean age: 116.1 months). All participants had no developmental disorders or deficits in hearing, vision, or color perception. Various measures were successfully administered, including tests for working memory (digit span and corsi span), inhibitory control (color-word stroop and stimulus-response compatibility task), cognitive flexibility (dimensional change card sort and Wisconsin card sorting task), Chinese word reading, listening comprehension, and Chinese reading comprehension. Trained examiners in psychology or education administered the tests in both Hong Kong and Mainland China, using parallel tasks. Structure equation modeling was used to test two objectives. The study examined the direct role of Chinese listening comprehension and Chinese word reading accuracy, as well as the indirect role of executive functioning components in Chinese reading comprehension for both groups of students. Age and gender were included as covariate variables. The results showed that executive functioning indirectly influenced reading comprehension through word reading and linguistic comprehension in both Hong Kong and Mainland China students. Additionally, there were variations in the indirect prediction model between the two groups. Specifically, cognitive flexibility was crucial for reading comprehension via word reading and listening comprehension in Cantonese-speaking students in Hong Kong, who were learning Chinese as an inconsistent oral-written language due to linguistic distance. However, this was not the case for Mainland China students learning Chinese as a consistent oral-written language. The study contributed theoretically by elaborating on the connections of executive functioning in the Simple View of Reading model, and provided empirical evidence on the specific roles of executive functioning components in learning a language with linguistic distance. From a practical standpoint, the study shed light on the challenges faced when learning Chinese in Hong Kong, particularly the cognitive resources required for learning languages with linguistic distance.

18602119.label: Major findings and research outcome
18602119.value: The study investigated the direct and indirect associations of executive functioning, Chinese word reading, and linguistic comprehension in predicting Chinese reading comprehension among primary school students in Hong Kong and Mainland China. The findings supported the hypothesis that executive functioning indirectly influences reading comprehension through word reading and linguistic comprehension in both groups of students. In particular, working memory and inhibition were found to be important predictors of reading comprehension in both groups of students. However, there were differences between the two groups. Cognitive flexibility was specifically critical for reading comprehension through word reading and listening comprehension in Hong Kong Cantonese-speaking students, who learn Chinese as an inconsistent oral-written language due to linguistic distance. On the other hand, cognitive flexibility did not have the same prediction to reading comprehension for Mainland China students who were learning Chinese as a consistent oral-written language. Notably, Mainland China students relied more on visual working memory rather than verbal working memory, compared to Hong Kong Cantonese-speaking students, for achieving reading comprehension through listening comprehension and word reading accuracy. Inhibition played a more important role in reading comprehension through word reading and listening comprehension for Mandarin-speaking Mainland Chinese students compared to Hong Kong Cantonese-speaking students. These findings elaborated the Simple View of Reading by supporting an indirect model of executive functioning in Chinese reading comprehension via word reading and listening comprehension. In addition, it highlighted cognitive flexibility as a key underlying mechanism for predicting reading comprehension in languages with different linguistic distances.

18602119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18602119.value: For further development of research on this topic, the following two aspects could be considered: 1. It would be beneficial to conduct further studies and expand the ideas in languages with varying levels of linguistic distance. With languages with different levels of linguistic distances, it would help to explore and elaborate on the specific roles of executive functioning components in the Model of Simple View of Reading. 2. Given the rapid development of cognitive abilities in children, it would be interesting to investigate DEVELOPMENTALLY how the components of executive functioning may play different roles in the Model of Simple View of Reading in languages with different levels of linguistic distances.

18602119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18602119.value: Working memory, inhibition, and cognitive flexibility are generally considered three key components of executive functioning. The project tested two groups of primary school students: one from Hong Kong learning Chinese as a inconsistent oral-written language and the other from Mainland China learning Chinese as an consistent oral-written language. The project found that working memory and inhibition played an indirect role in reading comprehension through word reading accuracy and listening comprehension in both groups. However, interestingly, Hong Kong students relied significantly more on cognitive flexibility in Chinese reading comprehension compared to students from Mainland China. Cognitive flexibility refers to the capacity to shift or switch one's thinking and attention between different tasks or operations, typically in response to a change in rules or demands. The findings of the study highlight how linguistic distance of a language can tax cognitive resources in language learning. The findings contribute to understand Chinese reading comprehension challenges in the context of Hong Kong and bring some practical pedagogy implications, such as the medium of instruction in teaching and learning Chinese.

18603119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18603119.value: The study explores the shapers and impacts of privatisation in the disregarded area of English education for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL), and identifies ways to ensure the quality of education without compromising equity. Many governments, including Hong Kong, have recently adopted a new line of privatisation through educational reforms, allowing for third parties’ participation in curriculum delivery in public schools funded by public monies, i.e., New Education Privatisation (NEP) in Burch’s (2009) definition. In addition to general privatisation trends, within-country NEP and its cross-national development at the government/supranational level have rightly attracted scholarly attention. However, the conditions which enable its infiltration into individual schools in the complex nexus of global/local relations has not received due attention, particularly for ESOL. ESOL requires special attention as equity issues can be heightened in it, English being crucial, but not readily accessible, social capital to enhance life chances for marginal groups of students, and is an attractive area for NEP. Furthermore, previous research has aptly provided criticism of NEP-induced changes in teacher professionalism (e.g., fragmentation of the teaching force) and educational quality and equity; however, there is little discussion of how schools and teachers should be prepared for NEP. This study will make an original contribution by identifying the shapers and impacts of NEP in ESOL through comparison of NEP in four countries, i.e., China, Japan, Australia and Greece, which have had divergent histories of, and relationships with, ESOL and NEP. Building on the research team’s previous work, this investigation seeks to answer the following research questions (RQs): 1. What ideas and material and structural conditions (global and local) have enabled/shaped the NEP in ESOL in schools in the four national case contexts? 2. In what ways, does NEP in ESOL change teachers’ practices, their professionalism and public schooling? 3. What quality is sought in privatised ESOL and how does it affect equity in education? 4. What lessons can be drawn from the cross-country analysis for the theorisation of NEP in ESOL and its appropriate use in public school systems? The sequential mixed-method study consists of analysis of supra-national, national, and sub-national policies concerning ESOL NEP; case studies in ten schools; a survey with 330 schools; and synthesis of findings through comparative analysis. It will extend the theorisation of NEP and debates about relevant policies, pedagogy and teacher education, in order to develop partnerships between public schools and third parties that will enhance quality education for all. 本研究探討操其他語言者英語教學(ESOL)中私有化的形塑及影響，並藉此提出在不影響公平的前提下，提高教育質素的方法。包括香港在內，近年來很多政府透過教育改革採用了一種嶄新的私有化模式，容許第三方機構參與公營學校的課程發展及教學，亦即Burch (2009) 所定義的新教育私有化(NEP)。除了一般的私有化趨勢，NEP在國家內部層面及政府/超國家層面的跨國發展亦吸引了學術界的關注。然而，促使其在全球/地方關係的複雜聯繫中滲透到各個學校的條件並未獲得應有重視，特別是在ESOL而言。由於在公平的議題上，英語作為提高邊緣學生的生命機會中相當重要的社會資本並不容易獲得，令NEP在ESOL中成為一個需要特別關注的範圍。此外，過往研究就NEP所帶來的對教師專業化(例如教師間的分裂)、教育質素及平等的變化提供了適切的批評；但有關學校和教師應如何為NEP做好準備的討論卻相對匱乏。 是次研究將聚焦於四個在ESOL和NEP上有著不同發展歷史及關係的國家，亦即中國、日本、澳洲及希臘，透過比較她們各自NEP的狀況，並對辨別出NEP在ESOL中的形塑及其影響上作出原創性的貢獻。在研究團隊以往的工作基礎上，是次研究旨在回答以下研究問題： 1. 在這四個國家案例中，什麼想法及物質結構條件(國際性及地方性)促使或形塑了校內ESOL中的NEP? 2. ESOL中的NEP怎樣改變了教師的實踐及其專業，和公營學校教育? 3. 私有化下的ESOL追求了怎樣的質素及其如何影響教育中的平等? 4. 對於理論化ESOL中的NEP及其在公營學校教育系統中的適當使用上，我們可以在這個跨國分析中吸取哪些經驗? 這個按順序的混合方法研究包含了超國家層面/國家層面/國家以內層面的ESOL NEP的政策分析、十個學校個案研究、涉及330間學校的調查、以及通過比較分析所集結而成的研究結果。它將擴展NEP的理論化以及對相關政策、教學法和教師教育的辯論，促使所建立的公立學校和第三方機構之間的夥伴關係能夠達致提高全民品質教育。

18603119.label: Realisation of objectives
18603119.value: The project objectives have been successfully achieved in full (100%) as outlined in the initial project plan. All planned activities were carried out within the designated timeframe, and the expected outcomes were met to the highest standards. While the pandemic posed some challenges, the objectives were met without deviation from the planned strategies. Strong teamwork built through regular meetings, setting small targets and reviews of progress, and seeking mentorship helped in maintaining focus on the desired outcomes, and proactive planning ensured that the project ran smoothly from start to finish. The details of how the individual objectives were met are detailed below: Objective 1. Identify ideas and material and structural conditions at the supra-governmental, national and local levels that enable and shape the trajectories and strategies of NEP in each national case and in individual schools, specifically in ESOL The neoliberal ideologies commonly shaped policy agendas at supra-governmental, national, and local levels across the four case contexts. The discourse equates the private with quality and effectiveness. However, how they were actually introduced, perceived and translated into actual executive plans differed across the contexts, dependent upon the historical relationship between the private and the public, and structural conditions such as available resources. To illustrate, Hong Kong’s government embraced the neoliberal strategy openly, integrating public accountability measures and financial arrangements that facilitated transparency, and the public did not have much resistance against the private joining force in delivering the school curriculum. In contrast, Australia faced an open resistance toward creating a market within the public sector, as it was seen as a threat to the publicness of the education and also because it impacted upon the job security of teachers ofEnglish for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL). Objective 2. Investigate the impact of NEP in contemporary public schooling and on teachers’ practices, and their professionalism, particularly in ESOL Objective 2 of the study aimed to investigate the impact of New Education Privatisation (NEP) on public schooling, teachers’ practices, and professionalism, particularly in English Education for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL). The findings successfully addressed this objective by illustrating how NEP policies have had varied effects on schooling, teachers’ practices and teacher professionalism across the four countries studied. Schooling The research revealed that while NEP can enhance resource access in underfunded settings, and bring in expertise that is not available from the school staff, thus, diversifying the curriculum, it also led to challenges such as misalignment between schools and outsourcing providers, increased teacher workload, and threats to job security in certain contexts, particularly in Australia. Furthermore, the study showed that the quality of learning outcomes and care for marginal students were highly dependent on the coordination between schools and external service providers, with stronger collaborations yielding better outcomes. These findings underscore the need for clear contracts, professional development for teachers, and a more strategic approach to resource allocation to mitigate the risks associated with NEP and ensure equitable outcomes for marginalized students. Teacher professionalism Teacher professionalism was influenced by how outsourcing was used concerning ESOL teacher roles and their status. For instance, teachers in Japan, Hong Kong and Greece felt relatively secure about their jobs, as the service providers were positioned as extra resources that complement schoolteachers. However, in Australia, NEP practices undermined the job security and professional stability of ESOL teachers, as they used to serve educational boards but now are hired by individual schools with the discretion of school leaders. Outsourcing teachers’ professionalism was influenced by the leadership of the school leaders and individual teachers. If the leaders paid attention to what happens in the outsourced programmes, teachers would pay more attention to the learning experience of students, which would provide more opportunities for outsourcing teachers to express their concerns and needs. If not, individual teachers’ discretion and attitude affected what happened with their work conditions. Across all countries, the government did not monitor the practice first-hand, which left the professionalism condition of the outsourcing teachers to vary across schools and programmes. Objective 3. Investigate ways to ensure the quality and equity of ESOL provision under NEP Objective 3 of the study focused on identifying ways to ensure the quality and equity of ESOL provision under NEP. The quality and equity of outsourced programmes can be improved through taking the following measures. Enhance the coordination mechanisms between schools, service providers, and policymakers. This includes introducing policies that directly monitoring the quality and equity of outsourced programmes, in addition to those monitoring financial transparency. The policy also needs to ensure that the new context brought in through NEP does not hinder teacher professionalism, whether they belong to the school or the service providers. For service providing teachers, the lack of opportunity to professionally develop was identified as the most significant issue. Objective 4. Extend the theorisation of NEP in ESOL by investigating its appropriate use in public school systems to ensure quality education for all. The study reveals that while NEP policies can improve access to resources and services, their impact on equity and quality depends on the coordination between schools, service providers, and policymakers. The challenges identified—such as misalignment between outsourcing agencies and schools, underutilized funds, and increased teacher workload—demonstrate the need for a more nuanced approach to privatization in public education. Future research should focus on developing frameworks that prioritize student needs over cost-saving measures, ensuring that outsourcing practices align with educational goals of equity and inclusion. By integrating these considerations into the theorization of NEP, we proposed a model that informs the design of relevant policies and executive initiatives, so that the educational programmes delivered in partnership with third parties will have high-quality while addressing the needs of marginalized students and safeguarding teacher professionalism in public school systems.

18603119.label: Major findings and research outcome
18603119.value: The major findings of the research on New Education Privatisation (NEP) in English Education for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) highlight several key issues. First, the study identified that NEP policies, while introduced to increase the quality of education and address educational inequities, have had mixed results. In some cases, they have improved access to resources and services thus levelling the ground for those targeted marginal students, but the implementation often faces challenges such as misalignment between schools and service providers, overburdened teachers, which compromised the quality of the programmes provided in collaboration with third parties, and underutilized funds meant lost opportunities to support marginalized students. The lack of coordination between schools and outsourcing agencies is one of the main factors that contributed to these issues, which impacts the quality-of-service delivery, leading to inconsistent outcomes in terms of equity. Moreover, NEP has contributed to commercialization trends in education, with private actors increasingly influencing how education services are delivered, particularly in ESOL contexts. The findings indicate that while outsourcing can fill gaps in resource-poor settings, it raises a new issue concerning the meaning of public education. The research outcomes highlight the need to closely monitor resource distribution (going beyond access but concerning outcome of learning), program sustainability, and teacher development are necessary for a more equitable and high-quality outsourcing system. To improve equity, resource allocation can be focused on the outcome of learning, using models like Australia’s Schooling Resource Standard (SRS), rather than per capita model. To realise equity in terms of the learning outcomes, culturally responsive teaching and safe spaces are essential to support their engagement. For quality improvement, outsourcing should prioritize student needs over cost-saving measures. Governments must allow flexible fund usage and ensure clear contracts between schools and service providers, supported by teacher training in contract management to ensure mutual understanding of learning objectives and reducing potential conflicts. Teacher professional development is critical, ensuring outsourced teachers are well-qualified and continuously improving to deliver quality education. Throughout this project, we worked with international organisations including the Asian Productivity Organisation, eight Korean English language teacher associations and one Japanese teacher association, and the Australian TESOL, to widely disseminate the findings and recommendations from the study. Our knowledge transfer activities and engagement strategies raised awareness of the issues, and informed design of relevant policy at the intergovernmental/national/regional and potentially school level in each of the research contexts and across them, and English Education for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) pedagogy and professional development programmes in the NEP context.

18603119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18603119.value: The potential for further development of this research lies in strengthening the exploration of how NEP policies can be adapted to better support educational quality, equity, and teachers’ professional development in diverse contexts. Future studies could focus on refining and improving the coordination mechanisms between schools, service providers, and policymakers to address gaps identified in this project. As the current study used perception data, future studies can use student performance data and longitudinal studies to evaluate the effectiveness of education outsourcing programs and their contribution to educational equity. Moreover, as education is rapidly digitizing globally and the integration of generative AI is increasing in schooling, further research can investigate how education outsourcing practices will be affected, particularly regarding policy enactment and online social networks. A proposed course of action includes developing robust frameworks for monitoring and evaluation to ensure that NEP practices align with the educational goals of equity and inclusion. Engaging a broader range of stakeholders such as teachers, students, and local communities will also be crucial to shaping policies that are context-sensitive and sustainable. Furthermore, expanding the research to include longitudinal studies could provide deeper insights into the long-term effects of NEP on educational outcomes and the evolving roles of public and private actors in education.

18603119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18603119.value: The study examines the impact of public-private partnerships in education, focusing on how the privatization of English for Speakers of Other Languages (ESOL) affects teacher professionalism and educational equity across four countries: Hong Kong, Japan, Australia, and Greece. The research reveals that the effects of privatization are shaped by interactions with policy actors and the resources available in each country. While privatization can offer essential services in underfunded schools and strengthen the school curriculum through adding diversity, etc., it can also lead to coordination issues between schools and providers and increase teacher workload. Significant differences in teacher professionalism were observed: in Japan and Hong Kong, teachers received strong support; in Greece, privatization did not threaten professionalism; but in Australia, it undermined job security. Regarding equity, the varied use of funds and monitoring of marginalized students’ learning influencing educational outcomes. Quality of learning was subject to school-service provider collaboration, e.g., alignment between the outsourced and regular curriculum. This study is crucial for helping governments, policymakers, and education leaders make informed decisions about outsourcing, ensuring that the implementation of privatization is equitable and supports quality education for all students.

18605019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18605019.value: 本研究旨在藉由追蹤與比較香港及台灣的學童的發展來檢驗聲韻系統訓練（如漢語拼音或注音符號）是如何影響學前學童學習閱讀。 看說法教學法是香港學童（母語為粵語）在習得中文字時最常見的方法；相對而言，大陸與台灣學童（母語為普通話）則通常是透過聲韻系統訓練來學習中文字。雖然過去研究已經證實聲韻系統訓練是如何影響聲韻覺識，其機制卻未有清晰的證據。缺乏對此議題清楚地認識，家長及教師在設計教學策略以促進學童學習閱讀時就容易不夠完整。因此，本研究旨在針對此議題進行較完整的檢驗。 當中，聽覺瞬時處理，亦即對於正確偵測快速呈現聲音的能力，對於聲韻處理（如聲韻覺識及快速唸名）與閱讀（如識字）的重要性在拼音語系（如英文）國家中已被廣泛證實。而此重要性被認為與拼音語系對於聲韻處理的高度依賴有關。 然而，考慮到不同語言的獨特特性，聽覺瞬時處理對非拼音語系（如中文）閱讀的重要性可能存在有別於拼音語系國家閱讀的機制。在中文中，僅有少數針對聽覺瞬時處理與閱讀的關係進行檢驗，且其結果存在著明顯的不一致。而此不一致，很明顯地與受試者的生長地區（香港v.s.大陸或台灣）有關。因此，我們得以合理推論此不一致與學童習得中文字的方法差異有關。 本研究計畫以縱貫性研究配合組間比較，以追蹤並比較香港及台灣學童的聽覺瞬時處理對於聲韻處理及閱讀之間的關係。本研究計畫將持續二年以探討學童在接受聲韻系統訓練之前的狀態，以及證實聲韻系統訓練對閱讀學習在不同時間點的影響。明確地說，本研究將檢驗（1）比較香港及台灣學童在不同時間點的聽覺瞬時處理、聲韻處理、及閱讀表現；（2）檢驗香港及台灣學童在不同時間點的聽覺瞬時處理對於聲韻處理及閱讀表現之間的關係。 我們計畫在香港及台灣總共招募200名正常發展的學前學童（初始年齡約為4歲）為研究受試者，且考量縱貫性研究的樣本流失率，於初始時間點時預計將招募240名。此年齡的挑選乃因為台灣學童在5至6歲時學習注音符號。所有潛在受試者將會被以三個測驗進行篩選，而兩組的正式受試者則會以其人口統計的資訊（如性別、年齡）進行配對，並給予每次六至七個認知與閱讀相關測驗，共計三次，每次間距約為七個月。 本研究的結果將擴展我們對於聲韻系統學習重要性的認識，特別是對學前學童而言。在實踐層次而言，這些結果將能幫助教學實踐者更好地促進其區分性中文教學策略的實施與調整，這能提供另一個工具及觀點，可能對於預防高風險學童的的閱讀困難有所幫助。

18605019.label: Realisation of objectives
18605019.value: The intricate relationship between auditory temporal processing, phonological processing, and character reading has been a subject of considerable interest in the field of educational psychology. While alphabetic languages have shown a consistent relationship between these variables (Wagner & Torgesen, 1987; Tallal & Gaab, 2006), the dynamics in non-alphabetic languages like Chinese remain less understood. The present study aims to fill this gap by investigating these relationships in children from Hong Kong and Taiwan, who differ in their exposure to phonetic system training. Research in alphabetic languages has established auditory temporal processing as a fundamental predictor of phonological processing and, consequently, reading performance (Catts et al., 2002; McBride-Chang, 1996). However, the role of auditory temporal processing in Chinese character reading is less clear, with studies showing contrasting results (Meng et al., 2005; Zhang & McBride-Chang, 2014). This inconsistency may stem from the different methods of learning to read Chinese (i.e., either through a look-and-say method, as in Hong Kong, or through phonetic system training, as in Taiwan) or the language complexities (i.e., Cantonese used in Hong Kong is relatively complicated than Mandarin used in Taiwan). Objective 1: Cross-Regional Comparisons The first objective aimed to compare auditory temporal processing, phonological processing, and character reading across children from Hong Kong and Taiwan at different testing times. The findings revealed no significant differences in auditory temporal processing between the two groups at Time 1 and Time 3. This is particularly interesting given the literature's emphasis on the role of auditory temporal processing in alphabetic languages (Wagner & Torgesen, 1987; Tallal & Gaab, 2006). The absence of a significant difference suggests that the influence of auditory temporal processing may be modulated by other factors, such as the method of learning to read in non-alphabetic languages like Chinese. Rapid naming was found better in the Hong Kong group at Time 2. This aligns with the literature suggesting that the complexity of Cantonese, the mother language of Hong Kong, could facilitate rapid retrieval of character names (Ho, 2010). The methodological focus could contribute to the observed temporal fluctuation in rapid naming skills. Verbal short-term memory showed an underperformance in the Hong Kong group relative to the Taiwanese group at Time 2 and Time 3. This phenomenon could indicate the potential influence of phonetic system training, which is more common in Taiwan, on verbal short-term memory (Huang & Hanley, 1997). Phonological awareness was initially higher in the Hong Kong group but reached parity with the Taiwanese group at Time 3. This could be due to (1) the language complexity of Cantonese used in Hong Kong and (2) the potential influence of the catch-up effect facilitated by phonetic system training in Taiwan, which emphasizes grapheme-phoneme conversion (Ho, 2010). Lastly, the Hong Kong group consistently outperformed the Taiwanese group in Chinese character reading across all time points. This persistent difference underscores the potential influence of educational systems in which children in Hong Kong attend primary school at the age of six. Objective 2: Developmental Trajectories The second objective aimed to examine the developmental changes within each group. Both groups remained stable in auditory temporal processing, consistent with previous research suggesting that auditory temporal processing may be relatively resistant to developmental changes (Amitay et al., 2002). This stability across time points may indicate that auditory temporal processing is a foundational skill that is established early and remains consistent, irrespective of educational methods. Rapid naming improved from Time 1 to Time 2 in both groups, possibly indicating a developmental milestone. This improvement could be a universal feature of cognitive development, not necessarily tied to the complexity of language or the impacts of the learning method to read. Verbal short-term memory remained constant in the Hong Kong group but showed improvement in the Taiwanese group from Time 1 to Time 2. This divergence in developmental trajectories could be attributed to the potential influence of phonetic system training in Taiwan, which may activate auditory sensitivity and impact verbal short-term memory (Lee & Ko, 2009). Objective 3: Direct and Indirect Effects The third objective focused on the direct and indirect effects of auditory temporal processing on character reading, mediated by phonological processing. The pathway from auditory temporal processing at Time 1 to verbal short-term memory at Time 3, and subsequently to Chinese character reading at Time 3, was significant for the Hong Kong group but not for the Taiwanese group. This finding is groundbreaking as it reveals a conditional causal relationship between auditory temporal processing and Chinese character reading. The significance of this pathway in the Hong Kong group but not in the Taiwanese group could indicate the different cognitive or educational mechanisms at play in the two regions. It suggests that in the absence of the potential influence of phonetic system training, as in Hong Kong, auditory temporal processing may have a more pronounced impact on character reading mediated through verbal short-term memory. In summary, the extended discussion of the three objectives provides a nuanced understanding of the complex interplay between auditory temporal processing, phonological processing, and Chinese character reading in children from Hong Kong and Taiwan. The findings have important implications for educational practices and offer a rich context for future research to explore these relationships further.

18605019.label: Major findings and research outcome
18605019.value: In general, all three objectives have been achieved. Specifically, for the first research question, we found no significant differences between the Hong Kong and Taiwanese groups at Time 1 and Time 3 on auditory temporal processing and rapid naming abilities. Verbal short-term memory was equivalent between the two groups at Time 1 but showed a decline in the Hong Kong group compared to the Taiwanese group at Time 2 and Time 3. Phonological awareness was higher in the Hong Kong group at Time 1 and Time 2 but equalized with the Taiwanese group at Time 3. Lastly, the Hong Kong group consistently outperformed the Taiwanese group in Chinese character reading across all three time points. Regarding the second research question, the results indicated that both groups remained stable in auditory temporal processing across the two time points. Rapid naming improved from Time 1 to Time 2 and stabilized thereafter in both groups, but there was no significant difference between Time 2 and Time 3 for both groups. Verbal short-term memory remained constant in the Hong Kong group but improved in the Taiwanese group from Time 1 to Time 2. Phonological awareness improved in the Hong Kong group from Time 1 to Time 2, whereas the improvements happened in the Taiwanese group a bit later, that is, from Time 2 to Time 3. Chinese character reading improved only in the Hong Kong group from Time 1 to Time 2, remaining stable in the Taiwanese group. Moreover, we found the contributions from Time to all these three skills for both the Hong Kong and Taiwanese groups were all significant, but the Taiwanese group’s improvements in them across three testing times outperformed the Hong Kong group. On the contrary, the contributions from Time to Chinese character reading were significant for both groups to a similar extent, so the group differences were not significant. This result suggested the Chinese character reading of the students in both places showed clear and similar improvements over time. Our results of the third research question found the pathway from auditory temporal processing at Time 1 to verbal short-term memory at Time 3, and subsequently to Chinese character reading at Time 3, was found to be significant for the Hong Kong group but non-significant for the Taiwanese group. This result is inspiring and, among the first, reveals the conditional causal relationship between auditory temporal processing and Chinese character reading.

18605019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18605019.value: The current study has successfully achieved its objectives, and the findings also open up two avenues for further research, thereby extending the scope and depth of our understanding in this domain. Given the study's educational implications, another course of action would be to develop targeted interventions based on the findings. For instance, if phonetic system training impacts verbal short-term memory and phonological awareness significantly, educational curricula could be designed to incorporate these elements more effectively. Such interventions could be tested in a controlled environment to evaluate their efficacy in improving character reading skills. Also, the research has the potential to inform educational policy, particularly in regions where the method of learning to read Chinese is under debate. The findings could serve as empirical evidence for policymakers to consider the benefits and drawbacks of different educational approaches, such as the look-and-say method versus phonetic system training. The potential for further research from the current study is vast. By extending the study, developing educational interventions, and influencing policy, the research could have a far-reaching impact on the academic community and society.

18605019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18605019.value: This study examined how children in Hong Kong and Taiwan learn to read Chinese characters and how their ability to understand sounds and language plays a role in this process. We were interested in three main things: how kids from both places differ in their reading and language skills, how these skills change as they grow, and how understanding sounds affects their reading abilities. We found that children from Hong Kong and Taiwan are similar in how they process sounds, but there are differences in other language skills. For example, Hong Kong children were better at quickly naming objects and had a stronger memory for spoken words at certain times. However, these skills changed as the children grew older, and some of these differences became less noticeable. Also, only Hong Kong children’s good understanding of sounds could help them remember spoken words, but not Taiwanese children. These findings are significant because they can help teachers and policymakers understand how best to teach children to read Chinese characters. It also opens the door for more research to understand why these differences exist and how to use this knowledge to improve education.

18605319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18605319.value: Do immigration policies shape the attitudes of native citizens toward highly skilled immigrants? This is an important question because policy makers, especially those in rapidly evolving economies, often struggle between policies that restrict highly skilled immigration and those that grant preferential treatment to foreign professionals. Past research on immigration attitudes has treated immigration policies as an outcome rather than a determinant of natives’ immigration attitudes. In particular, no research to date has distinguished between highly skilled immigrants admitted under restrictive and liberal immigration policies, even though this distinction is a critical component in the theoretical story about natives’ responses to immigrants. Guided by untested assumptions, many countries impose tight restrictions on highly skilled immigration, which in most cases undermines their ability to compete in the international labor market and runs against the needs of the economy. This project will disentangle the complex relationships between immigration policy and natives’ attitudes toward skilled foreign workers by a survey experiment (N=1,800) conducted in Hong Kong, where the government is eager to develop high-tech industry and adopts both restrictive and preferential policies toward highly skilled immigrants, particularly those from mainland China. Building on validated and pilot tested vignette experimental design, the survey will randomly assign respondents to review immigration schemes that impose different levels of restriction on labor market participation, cultural assimilation, and subsidies provision. Participants will then report their attitudes toward immigrants admitted under those schemes. To supplement the survey findings, we will conduct in-depth interviews with Hong Kong residents working in industries with different levels of protection against skilled immigration. Taken together, the findings will introduce a new dimension to the debate on the determinants of immigration attitudes, articulate the links between policies and public opinion, and provide much-needed evidence for evaluating the attitudinal effects of immigration policies in the midst of global competition for talent. 是次研究旨在了解移民政策與香港本地人對高技術移民的態度之間的關係。我們將隨機向受訪者展示不同程度限制的移民計劃，並量度他們對移民的態度。另外，我們會與不同行業工作的香港居民進行深入訪談。調查結果將闡明政策與市民意見之間的聯繫，並為政府在全球競爭中設計移民政策提供有用的證據。

18605919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18605919.value: Over the past few years, increasing scholarly attention (Chee, 2018; Gao, 2017; 2018) has been paid to the low-enrolment of ethnic minority (EM) students in post-secondary education (PSE) in Hong Kong (HK), affirmed by official statistics and heated policy debate (CSD, 2017; HK Unison, 2015). Although education reforms and the massification of PSE have extended access to PSE, enrolment rates remain stratified. EMs are the least represented in local PSE institutions (EDB, 2017). Low PSE enrolment contributes to poor social integration and mobility which can increase unemployment and poverty within EM populations (Government of the HKSAR, 2017), and undermine the image of HK as “Asia’s world city” and as inclusive, diverse and equitable (Lam, 2017). Thus, finding ways to support EM students and reduce the disparities in PSE enrolment is a persistent, pressing social and economic problem for HK (EOC, 2017). In addressing low PSE-enrolment in sociology of education, the liberal status attainment tradition views the EM family and community as full-closure networks that consequently play a limited role in academic and informational assistance (Perna & Titus, 2005). For these EM youths, therefore, school is the dominant extra-familial institution that, in principle, gives them access to institutional resources defined as school-based social capital (SBSC) (Ceja, 2006). SBSC consists of “resources, opportunities, privileges, and services” embedded in one’s networks with school personnel (teachers, counsellors and other staff) for expected returns – health, academic success, and life chances (Stanton-Salazar, 2011, p. 17). Yet, few studies account for how SBSC is interpreted and enacted in secondary schools or identify mechanisms that condition EMs’ access to SBSC in PSE transition (Lee, 2014). SBSC remains under-theorised and less explored. This study addresses this significant research gap. Making use of the theories of SBSC (Lin, 2000; Stanton-Salazar, 2011) and school structure and culture (Conchas, 2006), we propose to employ multiple, qualitative case studies (Stake, 2005) to examine: a) institutional provision of SBSC; b) the resulting benefits and challenges that EM students interpret and experience as they navigate PSE decision-making and application processes; and c) the school structural and cultural factors that impede or facilitate EMs’ access and use of SBSC. This study will advance SBSC theory in the school-to-PSE transition literature. The findings will provide an empirical data base for advancing school interventions and policy reforms, thus widening PSE enrolment among EMs and helping to promote their well-being, economic and social inclusion for the longer term. 在過去幾年，越來越多的學者 (Chee, 2018; Gao, 2017; 2018) 開始關注香港少數族裔學生專上教育的低入學率，官方數據和激烈的政策辯論亦清楚反映情況 (CSD, 2017; HK Unison, 2015)。雖然專上教育普及化及教育改革令本港學生接觸專上教育的機會提升，但是專上教育的入學率仍然維持等級分化。少數族裔學生是在本地專上教育制度中佔比最少的 (EDB, 2017)。過低的專上教育入學率導致較差的社會融入和向上流動性，進而導致失業率上升並加劇少數族裔的貧窮狀況(Government of the HKSAR, 2017)，更甚損害香港作為「亞洲國際都會」的包容，多元和公正的形象 (Lam, 2017)。所以，對香港來說，尋求方法支持少數族裔學生，收窄專上教育的入學率差距，是一個持續並迫切的社會和經濟問題 (EOC, 2017) 。 在教育社會學領域，傳統的地位實現模式認為少數族裔家庭和社區作為全面封閉系統，因此，在學術和資訊支援上扮演著一個較限制的角色 (Perna & Titus, 2005)。所以，為這些少數族裔青年來說，學校是最主要的家庭以外的機構，在原則上，為他們提供制度上的支援，定義為「校本社會資本」 (Ceja, 2006)。「校本社會資本」包含了蘊含在個人和學校人員（老師，輔導員和其他職員）關係網絡上的「資源，機會，權利和服務」，這些資源能轉化為預期回報－健康，學業成就和生活機會 (Stanton-Salazar, 2011, p.17)。 然而，很少研究清楚解釋何謂「校本社會資本」，「校本社會資本」如何在中學裏實施或分辨機制導致少數族裔學生未能在升讀專上教育的過渡期接觸到「校本社會資本」(Lee, 2014)。「校本社會資本」仍然未被理論化和較少被探究。今項研究將解決這個明顯的研究漏洞。利用「校本社會資本」理論 (Lin, 2000; Stanton-Salazar, 2011)和學校結構和文化理論 (Conchas, 2006)，我們建議採用多重學校個案研究(Stake, 2005): a）學校提供的「校本社會資本」，b）升讀專上教育的決策和申請過程中，少數族裔學生詮釋和體驗其因而發生的好處和接觸到「校本社會資本」的挑戰，和c）學校架構和文化上會阻礙或促進少數族裔學生接觸和利用「校本社會資本」的因素。 這項研究將會推動升讀專上教育所需之校本社會資本的理論構建。研究所產生之數據庫，有利於本港學校的乾預和政策優化，藉此提高少數族裔學生專上教育的入學率同時協助他們提升身心健康，在長遠上，經濟和社會上的融入。

18605919.label: Realisation of objectives
18605919.value: We proposed to employ multiple, qualitative case studies to 1) explore SBSC offered to EM students by secondary schools; 2) set out EM students’ perceptions on the influence of the SBSC on their transitions to PSE; 3) illustrate the impact of school structural and cultural factors on EM students’ access and use of SBSC; and 4) provide the conceptual and practical implications of the findings for advancing local and international scholarship and provision of SBSC. During the period of study, we sought information-rich cases and variation sampling and conducted research in six local secondary schools. In each school, we collected school-level documents including mission statements, policy briefs, and other documents e.g., meeting minutes, brochures, and posters, which illustrated school missions and practices that fostered staff-student relationships and facilitated resources to EM students’ PSE transition. Non-participant focused observations were conducted of PSE-related interactive activities and events when the teaching was resumed and the schools were reopened. In addition, in each school, we conducted individual interviews with teachers and focus group interviews with EM students. As mentioned in the previous report, COVID pandemic to some extent has prevented the possibility of face-to-face interviews. Hence, under a careful consideration, we agreed on a degree of flexibility regarding the means of conducting interviews. We were open to face-to-face interviews (e.g. the focus group interviews conducted with EM students) and telephone interviews. All interview procedures and protocols have been seriously reviewed prior to the beginning of research activities. We also used background surveys to collect demographic information from teachers and EM students involved in order to facilitate the following interviews. The preliminary data analyses involved member checking and inter-rater reliability in order to ensure trustworthiness of the collected data. We then integrated the findings from the different data sources and contrasted and compared the responses within and across schools in order to capture SBSC resource and mission similarities/differentials between schools, and identify factors that account for commonality/variance in EM students’ access and use of SBSC in and across the six schools. The comparisons were analysed within the political, social and economic contexts of the HK society, and its education system so that the study’ s findings could advance SBSC theory in the school-to-PSE transition literature as well as shed light on the policy reforms and practical interventions in order to maximise SBSC access and mobilisation to meet the needs of the minority student population. As such, despite the influence of COVID pandemic, the project has basically achieved all the objectives we originally proposed.

18605919.label: Major findings and research outcome
18605919.value: This study employed the theory of school-based social capital (SBSC) and compared the ways in which PSE-relevant institutional resources and support were rationalised and enacted by staff and perceived and experienced by minority students in de facto segregated and desegregated school contexts. The comparative case studies disclose a distinct typology of SBSC in desegregated and segregated schools. The gathered data presented the shortage of an intersecting supply of SBSC at desegregated mainstream schools. In the mainstream schools with a very limited number of minority students, teachers rarely made PSE a viable option for minority students and student-staff relationships failed to embed these students in a system of institutional support. In those desegregated schools with a certain number of minority students, findings show that school personnel could counteract the stereotypical image of minority students as a deficit and commit to multiple (inspirational, pastoral and informational) responsibilities for minority students. However, they were overtly preoccupied with Confucian justice and integration and considered that tailored treatment would jeopardise the ideal of self-sufficiency and impartiality in Chinese society. In contrast, de facto segregated schools who often cater for a large number of minority student populations, displayed a school-wide going-to-PSE vision. Teachers served as empowerment agents to connect minority students with valuable university/college information and support networks within the PSE-for-all framework. Case studies of local secondary schools lead us to argue that desegregation is only effective when institutional structure, culture and agents empower minority students through access to instrumental resources and support for the pursuit of PSE.

18605919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18605919.value: The study’s findings support the argument that ethnic forms of desegregation at the institutional level do not automatically translate into educational equity and justice. Less well-off minority parents who predominate the minority population of Hong Kong explicitly desire to integrate their children into mainstream schools and society in order to achieve upward mobility. Then what leads to effective desegregation? This study, through comparatively unpacking SBSC in the desegregated and de facto segregated school settings, suggests that racial/ethnic desegregation needs to coincide with an authentic willingness to promote the success of minority students. This requires ample resources from the school institutions in which minorities enrol. Equally, if not more important, is the need to nurture a professional culture where school personnel can self-identify as institutional, empowering agents who are able to provide personalised guidance to their minority students, including about where and what to study, in addition to strategies to help them to prepare for university or college. Without more systemic changes to the school climate and its core values, we are unlikely to avert de facto continuing segregation. Future studies could explore how minority students with a spectrum of racial/ethnic backgrounds engage in agentic navigation through the PSE choice process.

18605919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18605919.value: Over the past few years, increasing scholarly attention has been paid to the low-enrolment of ethnic minority (EM) students in post-secondary education (PSE) in Hong Kong, affirmed by official statistics and heated policy debate. For these EM youths, school is the dominant extra-familial institution that, in principle, gives them access to institutional resources defined as school-based social capital (SBSC). Yet, few studies account for how SBSC is interpreted and enacted in secondary schools or identify mechanisms that condition EMs’ access to SBSC in PSE transition. SBSC remains under-theorised and less explored. This study addresses this significant research gap. Making use of the theories of SBSC and school structure and culture, we employ multiple, qualitative case studies to examine: a) institutional provision of SBSC; b) the resulting benefits and challenges that EM students interpret and experience as they navigate PSE decision-making and application processes; and c) the school structural and cultural factors that impede or facilitate EMs’ access and use of SBSC. This study could advance SBSC theory in the school-to-PSE transition literature. The findings advance school interventions and policy reforms in order to widen PSE enrolment among EMs and promote their well-being, economic and social inclusion for the longer term.

18607219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18607219.value: Ethnic minority education in Hong Kong has been in the spotlight since the passing of the Racial Discrimination Ordinance in 2008. As Bhowmik (2014) shows, ethnic minority students are concerned about peer relationships, racism and future employment. This suggests more needs to be known about how schools address these concerns about identity and sense of belonging. However, as Fiske (2004) and Kune (2011) argue, the needs of ethnic minority students cannot be fulfilled unless they feel they belong to and are accepted as members of their school, community and Hong Kong society. From the perspectives of the social construction of reality and symbolic interactionism, this study will examine how Hong Kong’s ethnic minority students perceive and experience a sense of belonging in the contexts of school, home and community. Consistent with symbolic interactionism, belonging will be examined as an everyday practice both within and beyond schools. Studies suggest that ethnic minority students’ school and community engagement is low (Willms, 2003; Kuang, 2015), and that their sense of belonging intersects with their sense of identity (Anthias, 2001), language, socio-economic circumstances, as well as social categorizations and power in society (Yuval-Davis, 2011) as they explore the space between the dominant culture and other minoritized cultures. The impact of these multiple contextual influences will be the major focus of this proposal. We will use a mixed methods research design to examine ethnic minority students’ sense of belonging. Quantitatively, a student survey in four schools (n=1200) will be conducted using the Hemingway Measure of Adolescent Connectedness (MAC 4). To provide qualitative in-depth insights with the use of participant observation, interviews and textual analysis, two case-study schools will be chosen, where the findings of the survey indicate highest and lowest levels of belonging. The identified students will be interviewed and their narrative and constructs will be compared with teachers' and parents' perceptions of these students' sense of belonging. The methodology adopted will not only cross-check the survey data but also gain more insights into ethnic minority students’ sense of belonging (Phinney, 1992; Robert et al., 1999). The results will shed light on a missing dimension in the study of ethnic minority students in Hong Kong, and address a gap in the current research relating to ethnic minority education. “種族歧視條例” 自2008年通過以來，少數族裔學生在香港所接受的教育一直是備受關注的議題。正如Bhowmik（2014）研究所得，少數族裔學生的學習和成長歷程往往受到朋輩關係、種族主義和就業前境所影響。這反映學校需要更深入地了解如何提升學生的身份認同感和歸屬感，繼而Fiske（2004）和Kune（2011）研究指出，如果少數族裔學生未能融入學校、社區和社會成為其一份子，學生的學習和成長需求便未能進一步實現。 本研究將以社會建構和形象互動論的角度，探索香港少數族裔學生在學校、家庭及社會環境下對歸屬感的理解與經驗。學生在日常生活下的歸屬感，將會與形象互動論的前提一起進行深入探討。正如兩項研究（Willms, 2003; Kuang, 2015）均顯示少數族裔學生在學校和社區的融入程度較低。在平衡主流文化和少數族裔文化的差異之間，少數族裔學生的歸屬感因著個人的身分認同感（Anthias, 2001）、語言、社會經濟環境、社會概定歸類及權力（Yuval-Davis, 2011）等因素而建立。故此，這項研究計劃將探視少數族裔學生的歸屬感所受到的不同環境因素影響。 我們將會採用混合量化研究與質性研究的方法來探討少數族裔學生的歸屬感。我們會邀請四所學校的學生（樣本數量: 1200）來參與問卷調查（海明威問卷—青少年的聯結性）。根據問卷調查的平均分數，我們會挑選出兩所學校（最高平均分和最低平均分的學校）來進行更深入的質性研究，其中包括參與觀察、訪談和文本分析。計劃會邀請這兩所學校的學生參與訪談，並將他們對歸屬感的看法與老師和家長們的觀點作深入比較。計劃所使用的研究方法不但能以多角度檢視及查證研究數據，並能夠深入地剖析少數族裔學生的歸屬感問題（Phinney, 1992; Robert et al., 1999）。這項研究將會擴展香港少數族裔學生教育的視野，其結果將為有關文獻及目前的少數族裔學生教育作出新的啟示。

18607219.label: Realisation of objectives
18607219.value: Despite the unprecedented disruptions in school functioning due to the Covid-19 pandemic in the community throughout the lifetime of the project affecting the major millstones, the project team successfully achieved all the proposed objectives of the study. Nevertheless, with the suspension of face-to-face teaching in the schools as directed by the Education Bureau (EDB), the project team had to modify the project execution strategy by redefining the sample size and data collection methods without compromising the stated objectives and the quality of the investigation. The school closure for an indefinite time on various occasions during the project lifetime caused a significant workload on the project team. It resulted in unexpected delays both in communication with schools and data collection. Since data processing and analysis depend upon the availability of the data, the project team continues to work on the collected data, conduct a comprehensive analysis and explore additional milestones and outcomes of the research project even after the project's lifetime. As outlined in the research proposal, the research project was undertaken in two phases: quantitative and qualitative. Initially, the study was supposed to begin with the quantitative phase; however, the project team had to revise the actual plan due to the face-to-face teaching suspension and prolonged online teaching and learning strategy by schools. Consequently, the project team began the study with the qualitative phase first. Since it was impossible to conduct face-to-face interviews with students and teachers due to school closure because of the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic, the project team modified the data collection method. Students and teachers were interviewed online either on Zoom or skype. Similar to the modifications made in the data collection method in the qualitative phase, the mode of survey data collection for the pilot and main study was also modified. As it was impossible to administer the questionnaire physically in schools, the quantitative data was collected online and steps were taken to maintain the reliability and confidentiality of the students’ responses. With the support of the school leadership and teachers, survey questionnaires were distributed among the targeted students and gathered their responses online. Despite proper communication and planning with the schools, the sudden school closure due to the pandemic outbreak multiple times severely affected the quantitative data collection. The project team had to modify the data collection timeline several times, which resulted in several postponements in survey data collection. Although both the qualitative and quantitative phases of the study suffered severely from the Covid-19 pandemic, the project team achieved all the project objectives stated in the proposal. The project team has produced several journal publications and disseminated the research findings at some international conferences. Given the potential to produce additional publications from the collected data, the project team is committed to working on it even beyond the project lifetime. The project team hopes to have an encouraging effect of the research findings on the educational policy and practice in Hong Kong. It further aims to examine the available data at its optimum and contribute to the existing body of scholarship on the sense of belonging among immigrant/ethnic minority youth in multicultural contexts in the globalized world.

18607219.label: Major findings and research outcome
18607219.value: The survey questionnaire was completed by 403 secondary school students. The majority of the student participants agree that they have a stronger sense of belonging concerning school, home, and community. No significant differences were identified between Chinese and non-Chinese (NC) students. Nevertheless, there are variations across the groups of students with different ethnic backgrounds. For example, Indian students scored the highest among all the students, including Chinese, in academic, social, and family belonging. The student participants scored higher in the family belonging component than in social and academic belonging among the three socialisation contexts. Girls and boys expressed similar responses to family and social belonging, but girls exhibited a stronger sense of belonging to the school context than boys did. The interviews (Students: 15; Teachers: 9) confirm similar variations across the gender and ethnicity. The qualitative study findings underscore the critical role of socialisation contexts such as family, community, school, and the larger society that shape the determinants of belonging. The teachers' narratives and perspectives identify various interrelated and interdependent factors determining ethnic minority (EM) students’ sense of belonging to Hong Kong (HK). Accordingly, Chinese language proficiency plays an instrumental role in developing a sense of belonging. However, gaps in the Chinese language curriculum and pedagogy limit the acquisition of language proficiency, defining EM students’ everyday life trajectories in HK. Although various studies have already highlighted Chinese proficiency's instrumental role in NC students’ acculturation, researchers may need to explore other factors beyond focusing on a language deficit perspective. Both the qualitative and quantitative findings suggest that the development of a sense of belonging among EM people may depend on a variety of factors. In the present study, young secondary school students born and raised in HK and elsewhere make sense of it differently. Although the participants claim different degrees of belonging to HK, all appear to demonstrate similar behavioural and socialization practices in their everyday life. They all speak multiple languages, socialise mainly with co-ethnic and NC peers and friends, value their religious commitments, and express their sense of belonging differently. A comprehensive understanding of the sense of belonging among young EM people requires special consideration of the multiple dimensions of their acculturation and enculturation in HK. The participants’ multiple language learning practices and their intercultural engagement with NC peers and friends from diverse ethnic backgrounds also raise questions about the reliance of acculturation research on the stress and coping perspective.

18607219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18607219.value: The negative stereotypes based on race, culture, and religion perpetuate biased perceptions and behaviour towards NC, hindering the development of a stronger sense of belonging in HK. Different governmental departments and institutions may need to create conditions and structures for greater intercultural understanding at the societal level. Since HK lacks a multicultural education policy, educational institutions may need to ensure inclusive education for all. In an educational policy context of biliteracy and trilingualism, comparative research studies of English and Chinese language learning practices may help identify the diverse learning needs of students with diverse backgrounds. Furthermore, a critical examination of the broader social and educational conditions in which NC students struggle in learning Chinese might help schools and teachers in their professional engagement. Ensuring an appropriate curriculum for second language learners and culturally responsive and sustaining teaching practices may help them acquire the language proficiency needed to grow and prosper in HK. Lastly, preparing teachers to respond to the students' culturally diverse learning needs in their classroom settings may yield better academic and social outcomes and facilitate developing a stronger sense of belonging among young people with immigrant and ethnic minority backgrounds.

18607219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18607219.value: The research project explored the nature of a sense of belonging among non-Chinese students and examined the differences across ethnic and gender groups. Both the qualitative and quantitative findings confirm a significant variation across the sample groups. No significant differences were observed among the ethnic minority and Chinese students. However, there are variations among the non-Chinese students across ethnicities. No significant differences across gender were observed. Overall, the students show stronger family belonging than academic and social belonging. However, girls scored significantly higher in academic and social belonging. Similar differences prevail across the ethnic groups. Indian, Chinese and Nepali students scored considerably higher in academic belonging than others. As for social belonging, Indian and Pakistani students reflected a stronger sense of belonging than other ethnic groups, including the Chinese. Indian, Pakistani and Nepali students exhibited a stronger sense of family belonging than other non-Chinese and Chinese students. While Indian students showed a stronger sense of belonging, Indonesian students scored lower across the contexts of their socialization. Compared to non-Chinese students, the Chinese students scored higher in academic belonging than in social and family belonging.

18607519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18607519.value: 本項研究將會制定一個理論框架以釐清被中介調節 (mediated moderating, meMO) 的心理過程和被調節中介(moderated mediating, moME)的心理過程的差異。同時本項研究會開發驗測中介調節作用的統計分析程序和軟件。現有的文獻對於 meMO 和 moME 之間的分辨總是模糊不清 , 一方面有些研究指出 meMO 和 moME有著同樣的統計模型 , 另一方面其他的研究倡議 meMO 只是被定義為 交互作用項 (interaction term)的中介過程, 而交互作用項不帶有任何實質的意義, 所以 meMO 的研究並無意義。關於 meMO 意義的爭議性導致研究人員在應用研究中錯誤理解某些心理過程。本項研究將會解決這一爭議並會突破現有理論框架在區分 meMO 和 moME 的局限性。在這項研究中, 研究團隊將首先介紹一個分析 meMO 的新理論框架。其次, 我們會應用結構方程模型(structural equation modeling, SEM)提出一個在不同模型條件下(包括多組比較)研究 meMO 過程的統一分析程序。再者, 我們將進行一系列模擬研究以測試及比較新的統計方法與現有的方法在估算和驗測 meMO 作用 上的表現。最後，我們將開發 Variable System，一個在 R 統計分析系統中的附加軟件包 , 以幫助研究 人員應用 SEM 來實施所提出的統計程序。這項目的研究結果將為心理學家提供一個用以理解人類 對學習和社會行為的處理的重要且強大的統計範例。由於很多的心理過程都能透過 meMO 來詮釋，此硏究項目所提出的統計程序將對心理學研究作出重要的貢獻。

18607519.label: Realisation of objectives
18607519.value: Objective 1 “To enhance researchers' understanding of mediated moderation (meMO) by comparing the performances of different model specifications for estimating and testing the mediated moderation effect” was successfully accomplished. To address objective 1, we have designed a simulation study to compare different model specifications of meMO based on two different approaches, namely, the structural equation modeling (SEM) approach using the variable system (VS) analytical framework (Kwan & Chan, 2018) and the regression-based approach using the traditional analytical framework (Edwards & Lambert, 2007; Muller et al., 2005) for estimating and testing the meMO effects. The simulation study results suggested that the performance of different model specifications were comparable in term of the accuracy of parameter estimation, but the VS approach outperformed the traditional approach for testing meMO in terms of standard error estimates, statistical power, and coverage probability of 95% confidence interval (CI) in some conditions such as when the maximum likelihood with robust standard error (MLR) estimation and bootstrap method were used. However, the results of the simulation study suggested that all the model specifications failed to recover the total moderation effect, which was found in the simple moderation model, without controlling for the moderation effect of the mediator. We proposed that conservation of total moderation effect is an important principle in the analysis of meMO if the objective of the researchers is to decompose the moderation effect and explore the underlying mechanism of how the moderator changes the relationship between two variables. This important feature helps to differentiate the process of meMO from its counterpart, moderated mediation (moME) (Kwan et al., 2023). To address the limitation of the existing model specifications of meMO, we have refined the original VS approach and incorporated additional rules for transforming the conceptual model into the SEM working model in conditional path analysis. Specifically, the model specification of the new VS approach can take the conservation of effect in the effect decomposition process into account. We have re-run the simulation study to test the performance of the new model specification of meMO underlying the new VS approach for estimating the meMO effects. The simulation study results revealed that the new model specification of meMO showed satisfactory performance in testing the meMO effect. More importantly, only the new VS approach could completely recover the total moderation effect in the simulation study. The results of the simulation study supported the adequacy of the new VS approach for the analysis of meMO. In conclusion, the new VS approach can enhance the researchers’ understanding of meMO in at least three ways. First, the new approach illustrates the uniqueness and practical value of studying meMO effects by emphasizing the importance of conservation of total effect in the analysis of meMO. Second, it provides an alternative model specification of meMO, which is different from the statistical model of moME and helps researchers distinguish the differences in the analysis of meMO and moME. Finally, the simulation study results provide empirical evidences to support the adequacy of the VS approach for the analysis of meMO. Hence, objective 1 was successfully achieved. Objective 2 “To help applied researchers to address broader research questions about mediated moderation by proposing methods for comparing the mediated moderation effects across different groups” was well addressed. In this project, we have explored how the new VS approach can be applied for comparing the meMO effects across different groups under the multi-sample SEM framework. In particular, we have conducted a simulation study to compare two different methods for comparing the meMO effects across groups. The two methods are (i) the likelihood ratio test, in which the chi-square difference between the unconstrained model (i.e., without equality constraint imposed on the meMO effects across the groups) and the constrained model (i.e., equality constraint(s) are imposed on the meMO effects across the groups) is computed and tested for statistical significance; and (ii) the difference in coefficients test, in which the difference in the meMO effect(s) between the two groups is tested using the Wald test. The results of the simulation study suggested that both methods had sufficient power in detecting the differences between the groups when sample size was as large as 200 in all conditions except when the differences were trivial. In addition, both methods had good control in the Type I error rate when there was no difference in the meMO effect between the two groups. Taking into the consideration of the results of the simulation study and the fact that the difference in the coefficients test is only viable for two-group condition and the likelihood ratio test is more flexible for testing the group differences between two or more groups, we recommend researchers to use the likelihood ratio test to conduct an overall test for comparing the differences of all groups to avoid the inflation of Type I errors due to multiple tests and use the difference in coefficient test for pairwise comparison when the overall likelihood ratio test is statistically significant. Since we have proposed and examined the methods for comparing the meMO effects across different groups, objective 2 was well achieved. Objective 3 “To aid researchers to analyse mediated moderation by developing a new statistical package in R to support the implementation of the proposed methods for the analysis of mediated moderation and other conditional processes.” was successfully achieved. Based on the results of objectives 1 and 2, our project team has developed a new statistical package “VS” in the R system for statistical computing (R Core Team, 2023). As far as we know, the VS package is the first R package especially designed for the analysis of meMO although it can be used as a general statistical tool for handling conditional path models that integrate mediation and moderation such as moderated mediation and second-order moderation models as well. The VS package adapts the latest VS analytical framework as mentioned in objective 1 for conditional path analysis. Users of the VS package only need to specify the conceptual model using the R script and the package automatically run the SEM analysis using the lavaan package in R by using the VS approach. In addition, the VS package supports the following functions: (i) rescaling of data (mean-centered and standardized data); (ii) estimation method (maximum likelihood, maximum likelihood with robust standard error; and generalized least squares) (iii) bootstrapping; (iv) type of bootstrap confidence intervals (basic bootstrap method, bootstrap percentile method, and bias-corrected bootstrap method); (v) computing the index for evaluating a genuine moderated mediation effect in a dual stage moderated mediation model (Ng et al., 2023); (vi) multi-sample analysis; (vii) equality constraints on the conditional direct and indirect effects across groups; and (viii) likelihood ratio test for testing the equality of conditional direct and indirect effect across groups. Notably, the last three functions are necessary functions that support between-group comparisons of conditional direct and indirect effects such as the meMO effects as mentioned in objective 2. The VS package significantly reduces the workload of researchers in conducting conditional path analysis and helps them avoid the tedious and error-prone transformation involved in conditional path analysis by automating all the analytical steps. Hence, objective 3 was completely achieved.
