18611219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18611219.value: The Education Bureau encourages parents to engage in young children’s learning and advocates the use of a play-based, constructivist learning approach. Some parents, however, are not active or still use drill-and-practice to guide children to learn numeracy skills. Regretfully, there is no efficient research tool to assess the quality of home numeracy activities. This project therefore aims: (1) to develop and validate scales for measuring parents’ beliefs regarding numeracy learning and the frequency and quality of home numeracy activities; (2) to examine the relationships between parents’ beliefs, the frequency of home activities, and children’s skills and interest; (3) to investigate whether the links between parents’ perceived responsibility and home activities are subject to parents’ mathematics anxiety and numeracy learning belief; (4) to establish whether the links between home activities and children’s skills vary among families with different socioeconomic status; and (5) to consider whether parents from lower or higher socioeconomic status families engage their children in higher quality home activities, and whether these activities are more or less beneficial to children’ numeracy skills. The project will consist of three phases. In Phase 1, 30 parents engaging their children in four activities will be observed and they will be interviewed about their home practices. The collected data will then be used to construct items for scales on frequency and quality of home numeracy activities. In Phase 2, through distribution of questionnaires to 210 parents, administration of tests to their children, and observation of parent-child interactions in two activities, the scales developed in Phase 1 and an existing scale on numeracy learning belief will be validated. Upon finalizing the scales, in Phase 3, questionnaires will be distributed to 360 parents and tests will be administered to their children. The proposed model of the relationships between parents’ beliefs, home numeracy activities, and children’s numeracy skills and interest will then be tested. The project will end with deliverables of two simple yet valid scales to assess the frequency and quality of home numeracy learning activities. The project’s findings should contribute to our knowledge of the reasons why some parents recognize their responsibility but rarely engage children in home numeracy activities, as well as the types of home activities and style of interactions that are conducive to developing children’s numeracy skills and interest. These, in turn, should help educators and policymakers identify parents who would benefit from programs about how to support children’s numeracy learning. 教育局鼓勵家長參與幼兒的學習，並提倡運用遊戲為本及建構式的學習取向。可是，部份家長表現未見積極，又或沿用操練方式去指導幼兒學習數學。現時，學界仍然未有高效率的研究工具去測量家庭數學活動的質素。有見及此，是次研究旨在：（一）建構及驗證測量家長數學學習信念、家庭數學活動次數，以及家庭數學活動質素的量表；（二）探討家長信念、家庭活動次數與幼兒數學能力及興趣的關係；（三）探究家長知覺責任與家庭活動的關係，會否受自身的數學焦慮及數學學習信念所影響；（四）研究在不同社會經濟地位的家庭中，家庭活動與幼兒數學能力的關係會否有差異；（五）考量社會經濟地位較高抑或較低的家長，會安排較高質素的家庭活動給幼兒，並檢測有關活動對幼兒數學能力有否效益。 是次研究共分三個階段。在第一階段，30名家長將與幼兒進行四項親子活動。研究人員除了會觀察活動的進行過程，亦會在活動完成後訪問家長平日在家的活動情況。上述所得的資料，將用作建構測量家庭數學活動次數和質素的量表。在第二階段，研究人員將會向210名家長派發問卷、對其幼兒進行評估，並觀察家長與其幼兒在兩項親子活動中的互動情況，從而驗證在第一階段所建構的量表，以及現有的數學學習信念量表。在第三階段，研究人員將於制訂量表後，向360名家長派發問卷，並與其幼兒進行評估，從而探討家長信念、家庭數學活動，以及幼兒數學能力、興趣之間的關係。 是次研究完成後，將編製出兩份簡單而有效度的量表，以評估家庭數學學習活動的次數及質素。是次研究所得的結果，可讓我們了解為何有些家長明知道其責任，卻甚少與幼兒進行家庭數學活動，並知道哪類家庭活動及互動模式，有利幼兒數學能力及興趣發展。教育工作者及政策制定者亦可透過研究結果，辨識哪些家長需要參加支援計劃，以掌握引導幼兒學習數學的方法。

18611219.label: Realisation of objectives
18611219.value: This project has three objectives. To realize the objectives, data were collected in multiple ways. Specifically, semi-structured interviews were conducted individually with more than 30 parents of third-year kindergarten children in Hong Kong. Besides, more than 150 parents in Hong Kong were asked to engage their third-year kindergarten children in different numeracy activities, and the ways they interacted with their children during those activities were observed and analyzed. Finally, numeracy and cognitive tests were administered to more than 460 third-year kindergarten children in Hong Kong, and their parents were asked to complete a questionnaire regarding their beliefs, attitudes and practices, as well as their children’s learning behaviors. Initial findings were presented at international conferences, and we refined the data analysis based on the comments received. By the end of the project, all three project objectives were well achieved. In the following, details of how each project objective was achieved are described. The first objective of this project was to develop and validate scales for measuring Hong Kong parents’ constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning, the frequency of home numeracy activities and parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities. To achieve this objective, we conducted confirmatory factor analysis and reliability analysis on the parent questionnaire data, so as to examine the factor structure and internal consistency of the scale aiming to measure parents’ constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning. The goodness-of-fit indices and Cronbach’s alpha obtained indicated that the scale originally designed to assess pre-service teachers’ constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning could also be used to assess the beliefs held by parents of kindergarten children. Meanwhile, based on review of relevant literature (e.g., existing studies on the home mathematics environment and effective adult-child interaction strategies), as well as examination of our interview and observation data collected, we generated items for a new scale on the frequency of home numeracy activities and a new scale on parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities. We then performed exploratory factor analysis and confirmatory factor analysis to finalize the items of the two new scales. We also conducted reliability analysis to examine whether the two new scales had good internal consistency. To examine the construct validity of the two new scales, we conducted linear regression analysis to examine the antecedents and outcomes of the frequency of home numeracy activities and parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities. We also examined the correlations between parents’ self-reports of their use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities and the observed frequency of their use of sustained shared thinking strategies during joint numeracy activities with their children. The results showed that the two scales had good reliability. They also had high construct validity: the frequency of home numeracy activities and parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities had some significant correlations with children’s numeracy outcomes; parents’ educational level and endorsement of the constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning were positively associated with the use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities; there were some significant correlations between parents’ self-reported and observed use of sustained shared thinking strategies. From the above, it is evident that the first project objective was fully met, as this project yielded three reliable and valid scales to assess parents’ constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning, frequency of home numeracy activities, and parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities respectively. The second objective of the project was to examine the relationships between parents’ perceived responsibility in children’s numeracy learning, the frequency of home numeracy activities, and children’s numeracy skills and interest. To achieve this objective, we performed path analysis on the parent questionnaire and child test data, evaluated the goodness-of-fit of our proposed model of how parents’ perceived responsibility in children’s numeracy learning, the frequency of home numeracy activities, children’s numeracy skills and interest were linked, and tested all the paths in the model. We found that the goodness-of-fit of our model was satisfactory. Parents’ perceived responsibility in children’s numeracy learning was not significantly associated with their frequency of engaging children in home numeracy activities. The frequency of informal numeracy activities (such as number-related table games) was positively associated with children’s numeracy skills and interest. In contrast, the frequency of formal basic numeracy activities was negatively associated with children’s numeracy skills. In view of these findings, the second project objective was completely accomplished, as this project enhanced our understanding of the relations between parents’ perceived responsibility in children’s numeracy learning, the frequency of home numeracy activities, and children’s numeracy skills and interest. The third objective of the project was to examine the moderating roles of family socioeconomic status, parents’ mathematics anxiety and constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning, and the mediating role of parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities in the above relationships. To achieve this objective, we again conducted path analysis on the parent questionnaire and child test data. We found that parents’ mathematics anxiety did not moderate the relations of parents’ perceived responsibility in children’s numeracy learning to the frequency of formal and informal home numeracy activities. Parents’ constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning also did not moderate the relation between the relations of parents’ perceived responsibility in children’s numeracy learning to the frequency of informal home numeracy activities. The positive relation between informal home numeracy activities and children’s numeracy skills, and the negative relation between formal home numeracy activities tended to be stronger among families with lower socioeconomic status. Though parents from higher socioeconomic status families were more likely to adopt sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities, parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities did not mediate the moderating effects of family socioeconomic status. Instead, there were some positive correlations between parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies and children’s numeracy skills and interest. All the above indicated that the third project objective was fully attained.

18611219.label: Major findings and research outcome
18611219.value: This project produced numerous important findings and research outcomes. First, three scales were yielded to assess different aspects of the home numeracy environment. Specifically, a scale that was originally designed for measuring pre-service teachers’ constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning was shown to be a reliable and valid tool to assess parents’ beliefs. Moreover, based on literature review (see Cheung et al., 2021), parent interviews (Cheung & Li, 2021), and observations of how parents interacted with kindergarteners during numeracy activities (Cheung & Li, 2021), a new scale for measuring the frequency of different home numeracy activities and a new scale for measuring parents’ use of sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities were developed. These scales showed high internal consistency reliability and construct validity (Cheung et al., under preparation, under review), and thus represent useful tools for more in-depth investigations on how different aspects of the home numeracy environment jointly contribute to children’s numeracy outcomes, and how different factors lead to variations in different aspects of the home numeracy environment. Besides, this project provided insights into the relations between different parents’ characteristics, the frequency of different home numeracy activities, young children’s numeracy skills and interest. Specifically, we demonstrated that parents’ perceived responsibility in children’s numeracy learning did not have any significant correlations with the frequency of home numeracy activities, regardless of parents’ mathematics anxiety and constructivist beliefs about numeracy learning. The frequency of informal numeracy activities (e.g., number-related board games) had positive correlations with children’s numeracy skills and interest, whereas the frequency of formal basic numeracy activities was negatively correlated with children’s numeracy skills (Cheung et al., under preparation). Compared to higher socioeconomic families, the relations between home numeracy activities and children’s numeracy skills tended to be stronger among lower socioeconomic families. Meanwhile, parents from higher socioeconomic families used more sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities (Cheung et al., under review). Parents’ use of such strategies did not mediate the moderating effects of family socioeconomic status, but had positive correlations with some numeracy outcomes in children (Cheung et al., under review). These findings remind future researchers of the importance of assessing both the frequency and quality of home numeracy activities. They also shed light on how to support parents to create home environments conducive to early numeracy development.

18611219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18611219.value: Although this project yields three scales for assessing different aspects of the home numeracy environment, and shows that the frequency and quality of home numeracy activities have some significant correlations with children’s numeracy outcomes, various areas of the topic require further investigation. First, it remains unclear how the frequency and quality of home numeracy activities are associated with children’s numeracy outcomes over time, and researchers can further explore whether one of such dimensions has a stronger predictive power. Second, future studies can include both fathers and mothers as participants, examine whether they affect each other in shaping the home numeracy experiences they create for children, and investigate whether they play differential roles in the numeracy development of boys and girls. Third, future researchers can explore whether parents can be coached to adopt sustained shared thinking strategies during home numeracy activities and which form of parent coaching can yield more benefits on parents and children. Lastly, cross-cultural research can be conducted to examine the validity of our new scales in different cultural contexts, and investigate whether similar relations between different parents’ characteristics, home numeracy activities and children’s numeracy outcomes are found in other places.

18611219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18611219.value: Though parents play a vital role in early learning, there are limited simple yet valid research tools to assess the frequency and quality of home numeracy activities, especially for the local context. This project therefore created such scales, and investigated how different parents’ characteristics and home numeracy activities were associated with Hong Kong third-year kindergarten children’s numeracy skills and interest. The results revealed that parents who perceived themselves as responsible for children’s numeracy learning did not necessarily initiate more home numeracy activities. The more frequent informal numeracy activities (e.g., board games), the higher children’s numeracy skills and interest; the less frequent basic formal numeracy activities, the better children’s numeracy skills. The relations between home numeracy activities and children’s numeracy skills were stronger among lower socioeconomic families. Parents from higher socioeconomic families tended to adopt more interactive strategies that encouraged children’s self-construction of knowledge, and the use of such strategies were associated with some positive outcomes. This project yields useful research tools for further investigations on the home numeracy environment, and provides directions on how to support parents to guide children’s numeracy learning.

18611419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18611419.value: Sleep disturbance is a pandemic affecting almost half of the world’s population. Sleep has been proposed to be a core transdiagnostic process that underlies various psychological disorders. Beyond the disease model, evidence also suggests that sleep variables are associated with a wide array of human functioning, from physical health, neurocognitive affective functions, social relationships, to personality formation and character development. Given the prevalence and pervasiveness of sleep problems, it is of pivotal importance to investigate their long-term consequences. Previous studies reported the effects of sleep quality at a particular time point or its average across multiple time points; this proposal distinguishes itself by studying the effects of the path of change in sleep quality over time, namely the sleep quality trajectory, which is more meaningful and powerful as it captures intraindividual longitudinal development. We focused on emerging adulthood for the established significance of this developmental period for human growth and flourishing. To break through the constraints of previous research, we shall capitalize on an existing eight-year dataset, and bring it up to the next level to include objective measures of sleep and a comprehensive set of flourishing outcome variables, with some of which being objectively-measured. We shall collect two waves of survey data from the participant pool of emerging adults, of whom we have at least two previous waves of sleep quality data (n=1,277), among which 300 participants have also agreed to provide behavioral-experimental data. We shall analyze the longitudinal data with growth mixture models, to identify distinct classes of sleep quality trajectories. Logistic regression and ANOVA will be used to examine predictors and flourishing outcomes of the trajectories. We hypothesize that: (H1) there are distinct classes of trajectories of sleep quality change; (H2) these trajectories affect how someone flourishes in health, life satisfaction, meaning, virtues, relationships, and work; and (H3) the progression of poor sleep is related to some psychosocial contributors (optimism, neuroticism, religiosity, sense of community, and social support). This project will result in a 10-year, 10-wave dataset of a theoretically-driven and empirically-based list of biopsychosocial-spiritual variables, with the key variables of sleep and some flourishing outcomes measured both by a longitudinal survey as well as in-lab objective tests. This novel design will enable us to investigate the flourishing outcomes and psychosocial determinants of sleep trajectory in the critical period of emerging adulthood in a methodologically rigorous manner with potential for high theoretical and clinical significance. 睡眠障礙是一種流行病，並正影響著世界幾乎一半人口。有學者提出，睡眠障礙是心理障礙的其中一個跨診斷因素（transdiagnostic process）。除了此疾病模型之外，研究亦指出睡眠與多方面的人體功能有關，包括生理健康、神經認知情感功能、社會關係、人格形成和品格發展。基於睡眠問題的普遍性和廣泛性，研究其長期影響至關重要。過往有學者研究睡眠質量在單一時間點的影響，而本次研究將會集中探討睡眠質量變化軌跡。透過這項研究，我們將能總結出更有意義的長期個體發展。 為了突破過往研究的限制，我們將利用現有的八年數據庫，並加入一整套有關心理欣榮和睡眠質素的測量，為數據庫增加更豐富的資料。我們將與舊有參與者聯絡（1,277人），再收集兩次調查數據。其中300個參與者亦已同意參與新增的行為實驗部份。我們將以成長混合模型分析縱向數據，識別不同類別的睡眠質量變化軌跡，並使用邏輯迴歸分析和變異數分析找出能預測軌跡類別的因素和軌跡類別對心理欣榮的影響。 我們預測：（H1）睡眠質量變化軌跡存在不同的類別; （H2）這些軌跡類別會影響人在身心健康、生活滿意度、人生意義、美德、人際關係和工作方面的欣榮發展; （H3）睡眠質素的惡化與一些心理社會因素（如樂觀、神經質、宗教信仰、社區意識和社會支持）有關。 這項研究將總結出一個以理論與實證為依據的生理、心理、社會 、靈性的十年數據集，其中主要的變項,如睡眠質素及欣榮發展,更包含了客觀的評估。這創新的設計將使我們能夠以嚴謹的科學方法去研究睡眠質量變化軌跡的心理社會因素和對於欣榮發展方面的影響，具有重要的理論和臨床意義。

18611419.label: Realisation of objectives
18611419.value: All objectives were completed successfully, despite the immense challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic. We collected online survey data with over 1000 returning participants and over 2000 new participants, exceeding our planned sample size of 1166. Objective 1: To depict the trajectories of sleep quality over about 8-10 years (Output 1) We identified distinct classes of sleep quality trajectories by fitting growth mixture models on longitudinal data. We collected sleep quality data nine and eight times among our first (joined since 2009) and second (joined since 2010) cohorts of participants respectively. We modeled the trajectory of sleep quality—measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI)—as a function of participant’s age to examine intra-personal developmental changes. Our final growth mixture model included four classes of sleep trajectory. Figure 1 (refer to Annex for all figures) shows the trajectories of PSQI total score for the four identified classes/groups. The four sleep trajectory groups were(a) Stable and Good Sleepers who consistently reported a low PSQI score, (b) Improving Sleepers who had a decreasing trend in PSQI score, (c) Worsening Sleepers who had an increasing trend in PSQI score, and (d) Transitional Sleepers who experienced a worsening sleep quality in their mid-20’s but improved afterwards. Objective 2: To determine the flourishing outcomes of sleep quality trajectories (Output 1) Each participant was given a class label according to the aforementioned growth mixture modeling results. To address Objective 2, such class labels were used to longitudinally predict future flourishing outcomes—Secure Flourish Index, Depression Anxiety Stress Scale, Flourishing Scale, WHO Quality of Life, Relationship Assessment Scale, Utrecht Work Engagement Scale, Heartland Forgivingness Scale and State Hope Scale. Sleep trajectory classes significantly improved the predictive power of the regression models of all the tested flourishing outcomes beyond the two control predictors of gender and age. Figure 2 shows the standardized coefficients with bootstrap percentile confidence intervals in the regression models. (Output 2) Making use of our dataset and responding dynamically to the local and global situation during our data collection, which coincided with the first outbreak of the pandemic in Hong Kong, we incorporated some pandemic-related variables, specifically the stock of face masks and associated worries. As expected, we found that a low mask stock predicted negative emotions, driven by low hope and high worry about masks. Worry triggered negative emotions through insomnia, while good sleep quality acted as a protective factor against depression and stress caused by mask-related concerns. Individuals with greater hope or better sleep quality worried less and had better wellbeing, even after accounting for the effects of mask-stock. Importantly, sleep quality, but not mask-stock, predicted flourishing, even in such critical situations. Our findings underscore the importance of raising awareness of sleep health. During crises, a supply of material resources is critical; yet, boosting hope and promoting sleep quality also support quality of life and flourishing. (Output 3) Along similar lines, to examine the role of sleep quality in young people’s flourishing in the cyber-context, we built a statistical model and found that better sleep quality explained higher positive youth development (PYD), fewer cybervictimization, and better sleep quality also contributed to more cyberhelping via PYD. Objective 3: To identify the psychosocial predictors of sleep quality trajectories (Output 1) We used multinomial logistic regression to examine the psychosocial predictors of sleep trajectory classes. In the model, we included gender, age, circadian preference and caffeine consumption habits as control predictors, before testing the following psychosocial predictors: emotional stability, religiosity, spirituality, optimism and social support. Age, circadian preference, emotional stability and social support were found to be statistically significant predictors. Figure 3 shows how the probabilities of being classified into one of the four sleep trajectory groups change as the level of social support increases. (Output 4) To complement the identification of psychosocial predictors of sleep quality trajectories, we also continued to exploit our dataset to examine the predictors of sleep quality longitudinally. We demonstrated bidirectional associations between emotional stability and sleep quality. Interestingly, contrary to our hypothesis and despite correlations between social cynicism and sleep quality within and across waves, social cynicism did not have any association with sleep quality in either direction in our cross-lagged model testing. Further investigations are needed to further understand the associations between these two variables with other intervening factors and different time frames. (Output 5) As there were only a few studies on sleep quality trajectories with limited scope, we conducted a meta-analysis and systematic review using novel and rigorous methods, focusing on the trajectories of sleep duration, an important aspect of sleep quality. Our analysis revealed that studies with data collected at more time points (i.e., waves of data) reported more significant findings of the relationship between sleep duration trajectory groups and various outcomes of interest (i.e., health risk or mortality; mental health risk). Besides, our meta analyses included studies using group-based trajectory modeling revealed that the “rapidly decreasing group” demonstrated the strongest association with adverse health outcomes such as non-suicidal self-harm. Furthermore, we found significant differences in the proportions of individuals categorized as the shortest sleep duration group based on age range and sampling country, suggesting that age and cultural factors may influence sleep quality trajectories. (Output 6) Consistent with our goal to understand sleep quality in more sophisticated ways than measuring sleep quality, we adopted a person-centered approach with latent profile analysis to characterize the subtypes of sleepers with multiple sleep variables, including domains of sleep quality (i.e., sleep duration, subjective sleep quality, daytime disruptions, sleep latency, sleep efficiency) and other sleep health indexes, namely sleep variability, circadian preference, and insomnia symptoms. Our tentative analysis identified four distinctive sleep profiles: Good Sleepers (Profile 3, N = 1108), Poor Sleepers (Profile 4, N = 210), Unstable Sleepers (Profile 2, N = 699), and Self-perceived Poor Sleepers (Profile 1, N = 1244), with 6 domains of sleep quality shown in Figure 4 for illustration (Output 6). Compared to the other three profiles, Poor Sleepers (Profile 4) showed the worst outcomes in flourishing. With innovative methods of profiling sleep, our study demonstrated the differentiation of sleep patterns based on multiple measures, as well as the power of the profiles in predicting flourishing outcomes, above and beyond that of the sleep measures separately. Objective 4: To compare the power of sleep trajectories over multiple waves versus single time-points of sleep quality in predicting flourishing outcomes (Output 1) Conceptually, predicting future flourishing outcomes using sleep trajectory information addressed different research questions than predicting concurrent flourishing outcomes using sleep quality measured at the same time point. For the first time, we pioneered in examining the comparative strength of sleep trajectory information as a predictor of flourishing outcome by testing whether including sleep trajectory information could improve the prediction above and beyond concurrently measured sleep quality. Indeed we found consistent evidence that sleep trajectory classes improved the predictive power of the regression models of most flourishing outcomes (on 12 out of 15 measures). Figure 4 compares the standardized coefficients of Wave-9 PSQI score and those of the three trajectory class dummy predictors.

18611419.label: Major findings and research outcome
18611419.value: Our dataset with 9 waves of data spanning across 11 years revealed four distinct sleep quality classes, which predicted future flourishing outcomes measured comprehensively, above and beyond concurrently measured sleep quality (Output 1). The sleep trajectories were found to be predicted by age, circadian preference, emotional stability and social support (Outputs 1 & 4). We targeted the urgent needs of the society by reporting that good sleep quality acted as a protective factor against depression and stress caused by inadequate face-mask stock and the associated worries during the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic (Output 2 & Output A). Sleep quality was also found to be associated with youth’s flourishing through more positive youth development, less cybervictimization and more cyberhelping (Output 3). To provide new perspectives and methods in understanding sleep quality, we conducted three methodological studies dedicated to proposing and applying novel analyses. Our meta-analysis and systematic review (Output 5) demonstrated that studies with data collected at multiple time points reported more significant findings regarding the relationship between sleep duration trajectory groups and outcomes. Additionally, “rapidly decreasing group”, as defined by group-based trajectory modeling, exhibited the strongest association with negative health outcomes like self-harm; in our latent profile analysis (Output 6), we adopted an exploratory person-centered approach to identify four distinctive sleep profiles from combinations of sleep variables. Poor Sleepers (Profile 4), characterized by the largest sleep duration variability, evening circadian preference, and highest insomnia symptoms, in addition to worst scores in each sleep quality domain, showed the lowest income, and worst quality of life, mood states, and flourishing; our moderation analyses (Output 7), proposed a suitable way to estimate and report standardized moderation effects. The methods proposed in this paper can be used to test and report moderation effects in other papers in this and other projects. Manuscripts derived from the longitudinal dataset partially funded by the grant: Several manuscripts are under preparation, one of which has been published and showed that the presence of and search for meaning in life seem to work differently with respect to the relations between social axioms and negative emotions, with important implications for understanding the dynamics of social and personal beliefs in affecting flourishing in times of large-scale public crises.

18611419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18611419.value: Building on the successful completion of 9 waves of data collection spanning 11 years and based on the initial recommendations of the GRF Panel/reviewers, we applied for some internal funds to conduct a pilot study that collected wave 10 of the survey as well as some lab-based, objective sleep and cognitive data from more than 100 participants (not included in the approved proposal due to budget limitations). The extension study focused on attention, working memory and metacognitive performance in different sleep trajectory groups. We shall further explore if the novel methods we developed in analyzing sleep data (Output 1, Output 5-7) would afford us interesting and fruitful ways to model the associations between objective sleep quantity and quality and cognitive functions. Moving forward, we hope to secure further funding to increase the sample size for wave 10 survey with objective data, so that we have a truly comprehensive dataset that spans more than 10 years encompassing the pre- and post-COVID eras. The successful execution of this next phase promises to offer valuable contributions to both scientific advances and practical interventions for optimization of sleep and flourishing.

18611419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18611419.value: With over 1000 returning and 2000 new participants, this project successfully tracked sleep quality, flourishing outcomes, and psychosocial predictors in 9 waves of data collection spanning 11 years covering the pre- and post-COVID-19 periods. We discovered four different trajectory groups of people, whose sleep patterns varied or remained stable over time. The “Stable and Good Sleepers” thrived better in their flourishing outcomes, being happier, healthier mentally and physically, more purposeful and virtuous, with higher quality of life and better relationship quality, more engaged at work, and more forgiving and hopeful. On the other hand, age, morningness, emotional stability, and social support were found to predict the sleep trajectory groups. Lastly, we demonstrated the additional power of sleep trajectories in predicting flourishing outcomes beyond concurrently measured sleep quality. Uncovering the trajectories of sleep quality as well as their predictors and consequences is of significant value both theoretically and clinically, when it comes to understanding the psychological processes underlying the cause of sleep problems and the impact of sleep health on human flourishing. At the community level, health and mental health education strategies and public policies relevant to human flourishing can be formulated based on our findings regarding sleep health.

18611519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18611519.value: 近年來，在日本、韓國、新加坡、中國大陸和香港等亞洲許多國家和地區，學前機構的入學率均有增加。不僅如此，在過去幾年，每個國家和地區的平均幼兒教師數量也逐年增加。逐漸增大的學前機構規模改變了學校的組織結構。最值得注意的是，員工的組織結構已經從扁平化變為較為複雜的層級式結構。學校的組織結構中，新的層級在中層產生。這標誌幼兒教育的中層領導力的出現。 在香港，學前機構的規模（即平均每校教師的人數）從2011年的11.69增加到2017年的13.74。在政策議程中，政府將教育質素放在首要地位。隨著免費幼兒教育的實施，自2017年以來引入了一系列的教育質素改革措施：逐步將師生比例從1：15提高到1：11，為中層領導人員提供資源支持以加強人員結構，修訂《學前機構發展指標》來加強質素標準。這三個改革議程共同起到了塑造中層領導力發展的作用。然而，本地政府在下放學校領導力方面，主要是參考西方的教育改革模式。本研究項目對發展本地及亞洲中層領導力理論的觀點有重要的貢獻。 本研究項目旨在調查學前教育人員（包括校長、中層領導和前線教師）所認知的中層領導者的角色、權力和權威。本研究還會探討促進和阻礙中層領導力實施質素改進舉措的組織因素。為實現這一目標，我們將中層領導力的不同模型概念化為系統調查。本項目使用順序混合法，包括兩個階段：質化研究和量化研究。在第一階段，我們將有目的地選擇不同規模（小、中、大）、不同的課程時間（半日和全日）、不同的運營類型（獨立運營和非獨立運營）的學前機構。進行半結構式訪談。在第二階段，我們將使用分層隨機抽樣方法選取本地幼稚園進行問卷調查。定量分析將用於收集中層領導力的測量變量的總體模式。各種統計方法，包括平均值、標準差、項目總相關性、探索性因子分析和多級結構方程模型（SEM），將用於數據分析，以研究各種結構之間的潛在機制。

18611919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18611919.value: With over 40% of the territory of Hong Kong under statutory protection, the community is now shifting its focus on marine conservation. Although there are five marine parks and 1 marine reserve designated in Hong Kong, less than 1.5% of Hong Kong waters have been designated as marine protected areas. Marine parks play a significant role in preventing further marine environment destruction by pollution and development. However, human activities cannot be completely prohibited as these marine parks act as nature-based destinations to offer recreational activities for visitors. Inappropriate behavior of marine park visitors can impose adverse influences to the marine environment and organisms. Recreational diving is one of the popular activities for people visiting the marine protected areas of Hong Kong. Marine parks such as Tung Ping Chau Marine Parks and Hoi Ha Wan Marine Parks have been a popular destination for snorkeling or scuba diving activities. Understanding the environmental attitudes and ecologically responsible behavior of these recreational divers would be crucial for protecting coral communities and related benthic organisms. The objectives of our study are to: 1) study the recreational specialisation, environmental attitudes and ecologically responsible behaviours of the recreational divers; 2) explore the relationship between recreational specialisation, pro-environmental attitudes and ecologically responsible behavior of the recreational divers; 3) investigate the association between the socioeconomic factors and their environmental attitudes and behaviours of recreational divers, and; 4) provide assistance in the management of marine protected areas with reference to recreational divers. This research will be a pioneer one which combine three different data collection methods including questionnaire surveys, in-depth interview and underwater observation to allow a comprehensive investigation on divers’ behaviours. This research approach could complement the weaknesses of different data collection methods to come up with a more reliable results. Besides, using 360 degree underwater video recording will be a new approach for underwater observation. The video recorder can cover every angle to ensure all divers’ underwater diving behavior will be record. 18611919.label: Realisation of objectives

The association between socioeconomic variables, attitudes and behaviour have also been identified. Recreational specialization also indicates a significant association with divers’ attitudes and behaviours which advance the theoretical understanding of recreational divers’ attitudes and behaviour. Eventually, we can collect all data needed which are proposed in the research proposal. 18611919.label: Major findings and research outcome
18611919.value: 1. The results revealed that divers' sociodemographic status, particularly monthly salary, could affect their physical and biological preferences. Meanwhile, divers' diving experience was found to be a significant predictor in figuring out their biological preferences. However, no relationship between diving experience and physical preference was identified in this study. These results could inform management authorities in implementing ecological and environmental protection because biological conditions are considered the most attractive motivation for divers to dive in Hong Kong. Similarly, these results may help managers better understand divers' recreation needs based on different sociodemographic characteristics and diving experiences to create diverse recreation opportunities while enhancing their satisfaction by avoiding the negative impacts associated with identified preference attributes. 2. The results showed a statistically positive relationship between divers' recreational specialization and their attitudes, along with a statistically valid relationship between divers' recreational specialization and their marine-based conservation behaviour. However, divers' pro-environmental attitudes were not substantially associated with their marine-based conservation behaviour; thus, the discrepancy between current and previous studies was further discussed. In particular, our findings confirmed that recreational specialization could be a reliable predictor of divers' pro-environmental attitudes and marine-based conservation behaviour while serving as a pioneering model with which to fill the research gaps regarding scuba diving-based nature tourism in Hong Kong. Consequently, management implications and recommendations were presented in accordance with marine environmental conservation and scuba diving industrial sustainability in Hong Kong.

18611919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18611919.value: Recreational diving is one of the popular activities for people visiting the marine protected areas of Hong Kong. Marine parks such as Tung Ping Chau Marine Parks and Hoi Ha Wan Marine Parks have been popular destinations for snorkeling or scuba diving activities. Understanding the environmental attitudes and ecologically responsible behavior of these recreational divers would be crucial for protecting coral communities and related benthic organisms. The objectives of our study are to 1) study the recreational specialization, environmental attitudes, and ecologically responsible behaviours of the recreational divers; 2) explore the relationship between recreational specialization, pro-environmental attitudes, and ecologically responsible behavior of the recreational divers; 3) investigate the association between the socioeconomic factors and their environmental attitudes and behaviours of recreational divers, and; 4) provide assistance in the management of marine protected areas with reference to recreational divers. This research will be a pioneer one that combine three different data collection methods including questionnaire surveys, in-depth interview, and underwater observation to allow a comprehensive investigation of divers’ behaviours. This research approach could complement the weaknesses of different data collection methods to come up with a more reliable result. Besides, using 360-degree underwater video recording will be a new approach to underwater observation. The video recorder can cover every angle to ensure all divers’ underwater diving behavior will be recorded. With the new combination and adoption of the research methods, The findings of this study can help in the formulation of visitor management strategies of the marine protected areas in Hong Kong and provide a significant theoretical contribution to this field of study.

18612119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612119.value: Recent research has found that PhD students are suffering from psychological well-being problems at much higher rates than the general population. The alarming extent of these problems lead to much individual suffering and impose hefty economic, social, and intellectual costs. Despite increasing attention on doctoral well-being, there is a lack of a comprehensive understanding of the factors that underpin it. Most studies have been limited by focusing on one institution or disciplinary area. Moreover, almost all published studies have focused on PhD students in Western societies and there has been no large-scale systematic attempt to map out the psychological well-being of PhD students in Hong Kong, or elsewhere in Asia for that matter. To address these limitations, the proposed study will involve an empirical, mixed methods study of PhD students across all disciplines and across all public universities in Hong Kong. More specifically, this study aims to: (1) document the psychological well-being of PhD students in Hong Kong; (2) examine how the postgraduate research environment predicts PhD student psychological well-being; (3) compare the well-being of PhD students in Hong Kong with international comparison groups; and (4) provide feedback to the University Grants Committee and the Graduate Schools to improve policy and practice. The study has three phases. In Phase 1, a large-scale territory-wide survey will be administered to saturation to the more than 7,000 PhD students in Hong Kong’s eight publicly-funded universities. The survey will cover the postgraduate research environment, psychological well-being, and key personal background characteristics. A follow-up qualitative study using focus groups will flesh out the quantitative results. In Phase 2, the well-being data from Phase 1 will be compared with a key international dataset to help put the Hong Kong findings in context. Phase 3 will focus on providing feedback to the government and universities, with the goal of helping them formulate beneficial policies and practices, thereby maximizing impact. The proposed project moves the literature forward by examining the role of the postgraduate research environment in enabling or inhibiting well-being. The focus on environmental factors is theoretically rooted in a solid body of psychological research and is also solution-focused, because they are more malleable and amenable to policy and intervention efforts. By identifying the critical environmental factors most pertinent for well-being, it also yields actionable knowledge that can be used to craft effective policies and practices for optimizing doctoral well-being. 近期的研究發現，博士生的心理健康問題比率較一般人為高。這問題已到了令人擔心的程度，導致許多個人的痛苦外，亦帶來了沉重的經濟、社會和知識方面的代價。儘管越來越多人關注博士生的心理健康，但對於影響它的因素仍缺乏全面的了解。過往，大多數的研究都只局限於一個機構或學科領域。而幾乎所有已發表的研究，都集中在研究西方社會的博士生上。此外，一直沒有大規模而有系統地去嘗試詳細反映出香港或亞洲其他地方的博士生的心理健康狀況。 為解決這些局限，所提議的研究將以實證及混合的研究方法去研究所有學科和香港所有公立資助大學的博士生。更具體地說，本研究的目的是：（1）記錄香港博士生的心理健康狀況; （2）了解研究生的研究環境如何預測博士生的心理健康; （3）與國際比較香港博士生的心理健康; 並（4）向大學教育資助委員會和研究生院校提供反饋，以改善相關的政策和實踐。 本研究分為三個階段。在第一階段，將對香港八所公立資助大學的7,000多名博士生進行大規模的全港性調查。該調查將涵蓋研究生的研究環境、心理健康和關鍵的個人背景特徵。其後，會以質量的追蹤研究，利用焦點小組去呈現量化研究的結果。在第2階段，在第1階段所收集的數據，將與一個重要的國際資料數據進行比較，以助宏觀地理解香港的研究結果。第3階段將側重於向政府和各大學提供反饋，目的是幫助他們製定有用的政策和實踐方法，從而有效地利用本研究的結果。 所提議的項目，透過了解研究生的研究環境在促進或妨礙心理健康方面的作用，有助推動相關文獻的發展。以環境因素作為本研究的中心，其理論是建基於堅實的心理學研究。同時，本研究亦是以解決問題為重點，因為環境因素更易於受政策和干預努力所改變和修正。透過了解對心理健康最相關及重要的環境因素，它亦產生了可行動的知識，以製定有效的政策和實踐方法，去充分改善博士生的心理健康。

18612119.label: Major findings and research outcome
18612119.value: We allocated the major findings from this project into four perspectives. Each perspective has generated one journal article that has been listed in Part C respectively. First, this project identified the situation of PhD student well-being, and its antecedents (i.e., research environment) and consequences (i.e., performance and intentions to quit). Results indicated that different dimensions of the research environment such as supervision, research culture, and skills development showed distinct associations with positive and negative aspects of well-being. Well-being, in turn, was associated with performance and intentions to quit. Negative aspects of well-being showed the opposite relations. Furthermore, PhD students’ well-being significantly mediated the relationship between research environment on the one hand and performance and intentions to quit on the other. This manuscript is under review by Studies in Higher Education. Second, this project found that the research environment affects the well-being of PhD students through their motivation. Students’ autonomous and controlled motivation were posited as mechanisms linking the research environment to well-being. PhD students from eight Hong Kong government-funded universities reported that various dimensions of the research environment including process and assessment, culture, and skills development that had distinctive connections with students’ motivation and their well-being. Furthermore, students’ motivation significantly mediated the relationships between the research environment and their well-being. This manuscript is under review by Higher Education Research & Development. Third, this project aims identified the factors that influence PhD student well-being from a qualitative perspective and draws on the ecological systems theory as an overarching framework. The six main areas of the ecological systems theory were identiﬁed from a thematic analysis of participants’ responses. The study highlighted several salient influential factors of PhD student well-being such as coping strategies, social relations, and their living and cultural environment. An interactive effect among specific factors such as the Covid-19 pandemic and social movements was also identified. This manuscript is under review by The Asia-Pacific Education Researcher. Fourth, this project explored the classic types of PhD student-supervisor relationships using the model of interpersonal supervisor behaviour, and how these relationships influence PhD student well-being. We expect to find the perceptions of the eight types of relationships. They consist of Leadership, Helpful/friendly, Understanding, Student Responsibility/Freedom, Uncertain, Dissatisﬁed, Admonishing, and Strict. Moreover, the impact of these types of relationships of PhD student well-being will be also explored. This manuscript is under preparation and we plan to submit to Research in Higher Education.

18612119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612119.value: This project will support the research team to construct future research proposals on more specific topics and in a wider region for GRF and/or PPR applications. In terms of research foci, the research team plan to develop research proposals on the interventions to enhance PhD student well-being. The findings of this project identified the situation of PhD student well-being and the influential factors will provide sufficient information for research designs. In terms of research locations, the research team plan to extend the research locations into the Greater Bay Area (GBA). The GBA is one of the most vibrant, innovative areas of China and a major growth driver. Doctoral students constitute a critical human resource for the area and findings of this study could potentially inform policy-makers and educators in the GBA region. It can help the GBA establish an international reputation and leadership in providing quality well-being care for PhD students, thereby increasing its capacity to attract high caliber students who will contribute to building the GBA’s social, intellectual, and economic capital. The potential project will have a high potential to directly impact doctoral policy and practice and to benefit future students in the growing PhD market of the GBA.

18612119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612119.value: This project is an empirical, mixed methods study in nature to examine the situation of PhD student well-being, and its influential antecedents and consequences across all government-funded universities in Hong Kong. The achieved sample has accounted for around 50% of the total amount of PhD students in Hong Kong. This project identified research environment has influenced PhD student well-being mediated by their motivation. These relationships have also affected student performance and intentions to quit. Moreover, the different layers of influential factors have been also explored. The PhD student-supervisor relationship and its impact on student well-being have been also explored. This project can help provide PhD students with the right tools to remain healthy during their candidature which could ensure a seamless transition to cope with the rigor of professional academic roles, and subsequently, improve the sustainability of the higher education system. This project enables to offer broad baseline data for universities and policy makers in tracking the well-being of their PhD students. This project will offer vital knowledge and be of assistance to Hong Kong’s higher education institutions to assist them in deliberately focusing on their policies, programmes, and strategies for the encouragement and nurturing of their PhD student well-being.

18612619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612619.value: At the turn of the twentieth century technologies and media of sound recording entered music classrooms and became an integral part of music learning. What then existed was often called “the teaching of singing,” classrooms where students sung along to teacher- played piano accompaniment. What emerged was “music appreciation”—as teachers used recordings to teach great works like literature, shared music from distant places, and a variety of other ways to teach about music. Building on work in the field of sound studies, the present proposal will provide an historical account of the creation and emergence of music appreciation as pedagogy built around media of sound recording from approximately 1900-1950. This study addresses the understanding of how music learning is connected to various media of sound recording in ways that impact what is taught and how it is taught, working within theoretical approaches from the field of sound studies (Pinch & Bijsterveld, 2012; Sterne, 2012a). Sound studies is a newly emerged interdisciplinary approach to the study of sound in human contexts, typically combining disciplines such as history, philosophy, and science and technology studies. In particular, this study characterizes media not only as the gadgets, but as larger mediated networks of recurring relations between people, practices, institutions, and technologies that come to be understood as a medium through recurrent patterns of usage. For instance, the actual medium of radio is a network that includes producers, artists, technicians, broadcast standards, advertisers, and so on. Because the radio medium involves these various aspects, media theorists note plasticity as the medium evolves, and especially as a medium first emerges, just as radio now includes satellite and various connections through the internet. This project is comprised a set of case studies, each of which examines the ways that various media of sound recording were incorporated into the teaching and learning of music. Following previous research, particular attention will be paid to the emergence of specific pedagogic approaches that emerged in concert with media of sound recording. The cases will combine historical data, changing pedagogic practices, along with theoretical implications to establish the recurring patterns and interactions between people, practices, institutions and technologies as wants, needs, values and practices adapted to sound recordings. Cases will include changes to textbooks, the Music Memory competitions in the USA, and the NBC Music Appreciation Hour, along with the connections to the larger network of media and technology. 此項計劃將研究1900-1950年間音樂老師如何使用錄音方法，以及此項新方法如何對音樂教學帶來改變.

18612819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18612819.value: Since the return of Hong Kong’s sovereignty to China in 1997, Cantonese opera has been included in the SAR's school music curriculum. Recently, the People’s Government of Guangdong Province (2017) issued an ordinance to promote the transmission of the traditional music genre through all channels, including school education. Cantonese opera has been officially included in the policy agenda of both Hong Kong and mainland China, to preserve it and to promote cultural education in schools. Hong Kong people have been facing a challenge of identities. The initiative to develop Moral and National Education as compulsory subjects in schools in 2012 was opposed by younger generations. This was one of the reasons for the protest event “Occupy Central”. At present in the Hong Kong community, there appears to be conflict between younger generations striving for their “Hongkongese” identity, and another group that embraces and defends their Chinese national identity. A broad-based concept of national education has been proposed, which is a comprehensive model that should include national, political, social and cultural identity. As Cantonese opera is an art form replete with Chinese cultural elements, and thus suitable for promoting Chinese cultural identity, this study aims: 1) to investigate the current state regarding teaching and learning Cantonese opera in the schools of Hong Kong and Guangzhou, 2) to examine the extent to which variables such as teachers’ musical preference and teacher education in Hong Kong and Guangzhou may contribute to the teaching of Cantonese opera in music classes; and 3) to examine the extent to which learning Cantonese opera in schools may contribute to the development of Chinese cultural identity in students. Based on the Social Identity Theory, this study is in two phases employing a sequential explanatory mixed-method design. Phase I will be a questionnaire survey to investigate the current ways in which Cantonese opera is taught in schools. A hardcopy/online questionnaire will be designed and disseminated to all primary and secondary schools in Hong Kong and Guangzhou for music teachers. Phase II is a multiple-case study in which eight schools from both cities will be involved. Researchers will observe the classes over three months in each school and interview teachers and students for feedback and reflection on students’ development of Chinese cultural identity. This study will reflect the current situation in terms of teaching and learning of the genre, which will provide insights for future development. 自1997年香港回歸中國以來，粵劇已被納入香港學校音樂課程。 最近，廣東省人民政府（2017年）頒布了一項法令，通過各種渠道，包括學校教育，促進粵劇的傳播。 粵劇已被正式列入香港和中國大陸的政策議程，以保存傳統文化，並促進學校的文化教育。 香港人一直面臨著身份認同的挑戰。 2012年，學校將德育和國民教育作為必修科目的倡議遭到了年輕一代的反對。 這最終導致了一系列事件，包括“佔中”。 目前在香港社區，年輕一代正在爭取他們的“香港人”身份，而另一群人則擁抱和捍衛他們的中國人身份認同。 研究文獻已經提出了一個基礎廣泛的國民教育概念，這是一個應包括國家、政治、社會和文化特徵的綜合模式。由於粵劇是一種充滿中國文化元素的藝術形式，因此適合推廣中國文化認同。本研究旨在：1）調查香港和廣州學校粵劇教學現狀 ; 2）研究香港和廣州的教師音樂偏好和教師教育等音樂教師變數在多大程度上可以促進粵劇在音樂課堂上的教學 ; 3）研究在學校學習粵劇對學生中國文化認同發展的影響。建基於社會認同理論，本研究分兩個階段，採用順序解釋混合方法設計。第一階段將進行問卷調查，向音樂教師調查香港和廣州學校粵劇教學的現狀。第二階段是一個多案例研究，其中涉及兩個城市的八所學校。研究人員將在每個學校觀察三個月的課程，並採訪老師和學生，以反饋和反思學生對中國文化認同的發展。本研究將反映該類型的教學和學習方面的現狀，為未來的發展提供見解。

18612819.label: Realisation of objectives
18612819.value: The first and second objectives have been achieved by a survey to Hong Kong and Guangdong music teachers. Both hard copies by mail and a link to e-copies by email were sent to all primary and secondary schools in Hong Kong. The PI asked the Co-I, two university professors and one music inspector from Guangdong to help deliver the questionnaire through their personal contacts. A snowball sampling was also used to maximize the response rate. As a result, a total of 1,974 valid questionnaires were collected, of which 524 were from Hong Kong (319 primary schools and 205 secondary schools), and 1,450 from Guangdong schools (1,056 primary and 394 secondary schools). For the 3rd objective, it is achieved with limitations. I observed two primary schools in Hong Kong (School A and School B) and had one semi-structured interview with a teacher and four focus group interviews with five randomly selected students from School A. I went back to School A again three months later to observe their interdisciplinary week, an activity integrating different elements of Cantonese opera (e.g., designing Cantonese opera masks and creating scripts) through Chinese language, Visual arts and music lessons. I visited School A for a total of nine times. For School B, I had two interviews with a teacher and one focus group interview with five randomly selected students from School B. I visited School B five times. I observed two secondary schools (School C and School D) in Hong Kong. I visited School C for four times, during which I conducted one semi-structured interview with the music teacher and a tutor together and two focus group discussions with four randomly selected students. For School D, we interviewed two music teachers (of whom one was the music panel chair) together and I conducted a focus group interview with five randomly selected students in one visit. The Co-I, who worked in Guangdong, and five of her students conducted data collections in schools in Guangdong Province, China. They visited two primary schools and one junior secondary school. They visited those schools E for six times. All the interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed for analysis. However, many local schools refused the visits due to the pandemic, since all Hong Kong schools were closed for online teaching for a substantial period of time. Thus the data collection was limited. The original plan was that the PI would collaborate with the Co-I in visiting the schools, observe the classes and interview with the teachers and students. Due to the pandemic, the PI could not visit those schools in Guangzhou. Thus, the PI invited the Co-I to involve a few research students from her university to help with the school visits. Before the visits, the PI had briefed them on the techniques and methods of undertaking observation and semi-structured interviews. However, the data collected was insufficient due to their limited knowledge and skills in evidence-based research. On the other hand, school teachers and administration of the Guangdong schools tended to provide positive aspects only. This is another constraint for the investigation.

18612819.label: Major findings and research outcome
18612819.value: Findings reveal that 75% of Hong Kong respondents taught Cantonese opera while only 48% of Guangdong respondents did so. In terms of teaching time, in total, only about 8% of teaching time in both regions is contributed to teaching Cantonese opera; Hong Kong primary teachers (10%) taught more than secondary teachers (6%) while Guangdong secondary teachers (10%) taught more than primary teachers (7%). Teachers' age and teaching experience are not correlated to their allocation of teaching, while their education background is not a factor affecting the time allocation. However, teachers' musical background is influential; findings reveal that teachers with Chinese music background allocate more time significantly to teach the genre than those with Western music background. Their music background is related to their interest in Cantonese opera and their perception on their cultural identity. In general, all respondents tend to express a low level of knowledge of, interest in, and confidence about teaching Cantonese opera. In comparison, Guangdong teachers possess higher levels in knowledge, interest and confidence than Hong Kong teachers. Guangdong teachers are of higher interest and confidence in teaching the genre than Hong Kong counterparts. In general, it is found that in Hong Kong schools, music teachers tend to focus on teaching the knowledge and skills about Cantonese opera. They would teach tangible knowledge including the types of music and speeches, gong-che notation, the roles and singing types etc. Some teachers might involve students in singing but this is not common. Based on my observation, no music teachers would consider involving students in reflecting on Chinese culture and how Cantonese opera could contribute to nurturing students' cultural identity. In general, teachers do not consider nurturing students' cultural identity an important teaching objective.

18612819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
18612819.value: Music teachers in Hong Kong needs to learn about the ultimate goal of music education. Since they are music lovers, their only goal to teach music is to motivate students to love music with provision of music skills and knowledge. However, it is not the responsibility of school music education to generate musicians and music lovers. Instead, school music education should cultivate students in developing their national and cultural identity. Future research should be implemented on investigating what strategies in teaching Cantonese opera (and other Chinese music genres) should be developed in order to help nurturing students' national and cultural identities. On the other hand, we should also investigate if there are any effective strategies and policies adopted in overseas for our reference and comparison.

18612819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
18612819.value: This project aims to investigate the current situation of teaching Cantonese opera in Hong Kong and Guangdong schools, and to examine if students' Chinese cultural identity could be nurtured by teaching Cantonese opera. Findings suggest that both Hong Kong and Guangdong music teachers have allocated a modest amount of teaching time in teaching the genre. More importantly, the music background of music teachers are significant in affecting teachers' decision and extent in teaching Cantonese opera. Music teachers with Chinese music background tend to teach more Cantonese opera. This implies that the curricula in school education, tertiary education and teacher education are critically important in determining the decision of school music teachers. While most of the secondary graduates with Western music background enters into music programs of tertiary and teacher education, they will tend to focus on Western music. Consequently, university graduates may focus on Western music and they will do so in their school teaching. This will formulate a vicious circle, which is difficult to change. The value of this study reveals the shortfall of the music curriculum, music teachers' and teacher education institutions, which need to be improved. A balance between Western and Chinese music should be sought.

18613219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
18613219.value: A growing body of literature has demonstrated the importance of financial preparation for old age, especially in Hong Kong, where rates of poverty in old age are high and the population will age rapidly in the coming decades. Previous retirement preparation intervention studies suffer several major shortcomings in their design, such as lack of a control, non-representative samples, small sample size, invalid measures, short follow-up assessment, and lack of a theoretical basis. On the other hand, while a few recent studies have shown that personalized pension projection boosts workers’ retirement savings, the psychological outcomes, such as perceived savings adequacy, have not been assessed. Based on these lessons, this study seeks to examine the impact of the personalized projection of pension savings on retirement saving behavior, perceived savings adequacy, and financial preparation for old age among Hong Kong workers. Using a sample of 343 workers, we will develop a two-month intervention based on the interdisciplinary financial planning model and we will adopt a randomized experimental design with an active control group, identify a representative sample of workers by random sampling, use reliable and valid scales to measure outcomes including the amount of retirement savings, and administrate one-year and two-year follow-up assessments after the completion of the intervention. To strengthen the effect of this personalized information in magnitude and duration, we will also present participants with the discrepancy of the projected income and expenditure during retirement. Moreover, we will investigate whether the effect of this personalized information on our outcome measures is mediated through future time orientation, time discounting behavior, and retirement goal clarity. The proposed study is a 26-month randomized experiment in which the participants, working adults aged between 35 and 55 years, will be assigned within a three-arm design to receive either a personalized projected retirement savings intervention or a personalized projection of retirement savings with estimation of discrepancy replacement rate, or to active control condition. To assess the effectiveness of the intervention, we will measure the amount of voluntary contribution to the Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) and private retirement savings, perceived savings adequacy, and financial preparation for old age. The findings of this proposed study will not only make a strong contribution to the theoretical framework of financial preparation for old age, but also offer useful insights able to inform social policy and measures in Hong Kong by providing a cost-effective intervention to improve financial preparation for old age.

21100719.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21100719.value: 新出的羅非魚病毒（TiLV）遺傳決定因數的鑒定及預防工具的開發

21100719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21100719.value: 羅非魚是一種生長速度快的黑色淡水魚，它們在湖泊、池塘和河流等棲息地生長。由於羅非魚具有較高的營養價值並含有人體必需的蛋白質，因此它在水產養殖業和漁業中獲得了越來越多的關注。自2009年初以來，羅非魚的數量急劇減少。病毒類似病害（Virus-Like Diseases）似乎是引發高發病率的原因。該疾病主要的病變部位為眼睛、大腦和肝臟; 受感染的羅非魚表現出“合胞體肝炎”（Syncytial Hepatitis）的症狀。通過採用最新的分子鑒別診斷方法，導致該疾病的病原體被鑒定為“羅非魚湖病毒”（Tilapia Lake Virus，TiLV），這是一種正粘病毒樣病毒（Orthomyxovirus-Like Virus）。迄今為止，TiLV均有在非洲、亞洲和南美洲報告案例，由於死亡率很高，TiLV可能對全球的羅非魚產業帶來嚴重的威脅，並造成極大的經濟損失，這將嚴重危害養殖漁戶的利益。TiLV是一種新出現的病毒病原體，其相關研究處於高速發展。正粘病毒群（Orthomyxovirus Group），包括流感病毒（Influenza Virus），一直引起嚴重的公共衛生問題，因此從這個角度來看，儘管目前還沒有TiLV傳染人類病例的報導，但不能排除TiLV引起人畜共患病的可能性。有幾個研究團隊已經從遺傳學的角度將TiLV鑒定為具有10個片段的負鏈RNA病毒（Negative-Strand RNA Virus）。依據BLAST檢索和GenBank資料庫，在這些片段中，只有一種蛋白質的基因序列與C型流感病毒（Influenza C Virus）的PB1基因序列具有低水準的同源性，而其他的9個片段均與任何已知的基因序列不存在相似性。然而，從C型流感病毒（Influenza C Virus）的遺傳因素來分析，我們假設TiLV中含有免疫顯性的血凝素酯酶融合蛋白（Hemagglutinin Esterase Fusion Protein，HEF Protein），並且該蛋白在複製過程中將會高效表達，這對於病毒感染來說具有重要意義。為驗證上述假設，我們的研究計畫旨在（i）從陽性樣本中鑒別出TiLV基因組；（ii）將上文提及的10個病毒片段分別轉移到從甲病毒（Alphavirus）衍生出來的可自我複製的複製子平臺（Self-Replicating Replicon Platform）中，並在輔助基因組（Helper Genome）的協助下將構建的新序列逐一包裝起來（iii） 通過生物化學和免疫學試驗，並結合新合成抗體和新包裝的顆粒，來確定必需的靶蛋白。這種基於複製缺陷複製子（Replication-Deficient Replicon）的方法兼具了減毒活疫苗的效率以及滅活疫苗和亞單位疫苗的安全性，並且我們的長期目標是創建一個針對TiLV的有效的預防工具，以防止TiLV的進一步擴散，並減少相應的經濟損失。
