21200819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21200819.value: Cooling buildings consumes over 25% of Hong Kong’s total energy. Adsorption cooling systems (ACS) are an excellent replacement for vapor-compression refrigeration systems due to their environmental friendliness and energy-saving potential. Powered by renewable energy, they significantly reduce the dependence on fossil fuels. However, due to low cooling efficiency and bulky size, ACSs are not widely commercialized. Previous research focused on new adsorbents to enhance performance. Indeed, an energy-efficient evaporator together with an enhanced adsorbate is another research direction to improve efficiency. Here, a superhydrophilic wick-structured evaporator using hybrid-nanofluids as the adsorbate in ACSs is proposed. Because the capillary effect of wick-structures creates the orientation-independent property, increasing the heat transfer surface area in the evaporator, with the same cooling capacity, ACSs can be more compact. However, the evaporation rate of a wick-structured plate is lower than that of normal plates due to a larger contact angle on the wick-structure. Coating superhydrophilic patterns on the plate is one solution to address this issue since the superhydrophilic-coating increases the solid-liquid contact area. Our preliminary results show the evaporation rate of a superhydrophilic wick-structured plate using water improves by 430% and 450% compared to that of an untreated-plate and a wick-structured plate, respectively. Prior studies show that hybrid-nanofluids, dispersion of two types of nanoparticles in a base-fluid, exhibit better thermo-physical properties, i.e. higher effective thermal conductivity, than single-particle nanofluids, and much better than water. Therefore, the evaporation performance of the superhydrophilic wick-structured plate using hybrid-nanofluids can further be enhanced, substantially improving ACSs’ cooling performance and facilitating a more compact design. However, a number of academic challenges need addressing since hybrid-nanofluids heat transfer on superhydrophilic wick-structures has never been studied. This project will investigate and characterize thermo-physical properties of hybrid-nanofluids with different nanoparticle types and concentrations so that suitable adsorbates could be developed. Two mathematical models will be developed, with results being verified by experiments. One model will determine the effective thermal conductivity of hybrid-nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick-structured plate, while the other model will predict the evaporation rate of hybrid-nanofluids on a superhydrophilic wick-structured plate. Based on the models, a hybrid-nanofluids based superhydrophilic wick-structured evaporator will be designed, built and tested. Finally, the evaporator will be integrated into an ACS for performance evaluation. This research will reveal the impact of hybrid-nanoparticles deposition in porous media and the related heat transfer characteristics. The findings will enhance the thermo-physical knowledge of hybrid-nanofluids, and steer new development of ACSs. 在香港，超過百分之二十五的能源都被需要製冷的建築所消耗。環保的吸附式冷卻系統因其具備節約能源的潛力，從而成為蒸汽壓縮式製冷系統的絕佳替代品。在可再生能源的推動下，它們顯著降低了人們對化石燃料的依賴。然而，由於冷卻效率偏低和體積龐大，吸附式冷卻系統並未被廣泛商業化。過去關於它的研究，主要是集中在利用新型吸附劑來提高性能。實際上，把節能的蒸發器和加強型的吸附物結合起來，則會是另外一個有效提高系統性能的研究方向。在此，我們提出一種使用混合納米流體作為其吸附物的超親水毛細結構蒸發器。由於毛細結構中存在由毛細效應所產生的無方向性，因而能增大蒸發器中的傳熱面積。在製冷量不變的情況下，吸附式冷卻系統的設計可以更加緊湊。然而，毛細結構的疏水性會導致毛細板上的蒸發速率比普通平要低。對此的解決方案就是在板上旋塗超親水層，以增加固液接觸面積。我們的初步結果顯示，與未被處理的普通平板和毛細板相比，使用超親水毛細板的蒸發速率分別提高430％和450％。此外，過去的研究還表明，使用兩種納米顆粒分散在基礎流體中的混合納米流體，與使用單種顆粒的納米流體以及水相比，表現出更好的熱學物理性質，例如更高的有效導熱性等。因此，使用混合納米流體的超親水毛細結構板的蒸發性能可以進一步得到提高，從而顯著提高吸附式冷卻系統的冷卻性能，並使設計更加緊湊。然而，由於混合納米流體在超親水毛細結構上的傳熱從未被研究過，因此需要解決許多學術上的難題。此項目將研究和表徵具有不同納米顆粒類型和濃度的混合納米流體的熱物理性質，從而可以開發出合適的吸附物。當中會建立兩個數學模型，並通過實驗去驗證結果。一個模型將確定飽和混合納米流體的超親水毛細結構板的有效熱導率，而另一個模型將預測混合納米流體在超親水毛細結構板上的蒸發速率。我們將會基於這些模型，設計，搭建以及測試基於混合納米流體的超親水毛細結構蒸發器。最後，該蒸發器將會被集成到吸附式冷卻系統中以進行性能評估。本研究將揭示混合納米顆粒沉積在多孔介質中的影響以及相關的傳熱特性。此研究結果將會對混合納米流體的熱學物理知識進行補充，並引領出一個吸附式冷卻系統的全新發展方向。

21200819.label: Realisation of objectives
21200819.value: To achieve objective 1, we have investigated the thermophysical properties of hybrid nanofluids, namely the thermal conductivity, latent heat of vaporization, and surface tension. The thermal conductivities of the hybrid nanofluids under various mixing ratios and temperatures were measured using a thermal constant analyzer. The results indicated that the thermal conductivities of the hybrid nanofluids were higher than those of the base fluid and mono-nanofluids due to the synergistic effect of the interaction between the hybrid nanoparticles. The latent heat of vaporization of the hybrid nanofluids was obtained from thermogravimetric analysis/differential scanning calorimetry (TGA/DSC) tests. It was found that the latent heat of vaporization of the hybrid nanofluids was improved under low volume fraction (~0.1%). The thermal conductivities and latent heat of vaporization of the hybrid nanofluids were used in the following objectives for heat transfer and evaporation analysis. The surface tensions of the hybrid nanofluids at different temperatures were measured using a contact angle meter. The results showed that the surface tensions of the hybrid nanofluids were lower than those of the base fluid while the surface tension gradients of the hybrid nanofluids were higher than those of the base fluid. The surface tension was measured to investigate the evaporation behavior of the hybrid nanofluids in objective 3. For objective 2, the heat transfer performance of the hybrid-nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick-structured surface was investigated both experimentally and mathematically. The heat transfer coefficient of the hybrid nanofluids evaporated on the superhydrophilic wick-structured surface was determined by the heat flux of the copper heater and the temperature was measured at different distances apart from the evaporation surfaces. The morphology, wettability, surface free energy, roughness, and porosity of the evaporation surface were obtained for the heat transfer analysis. The results indicated that the heat transfer performance of the hybrid nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick-structured surface was almost three times higher than that saturated by water. Besides, increasing the volume fraction of the hybrid nanofluids could improve the heat transfer performance thanks to the enhancement of the thermal conductivity. However, when the volume fraction of the hybrid nanofluids exceeded a critical value, the surface properties (wettability and wicking effect), instead of the thermal conductivity of the hybrid nanofluids, dominated the heat transfer enhancement of the evaporation surface. This is because the high nanoparticle concentration on the evaporation surface, due to the high volume fraction, may obstruct the liquid entrainment across the superhydrophilic wick-structured surface, inhibiting the wetting of the evaporation surface. Moreover, the smaller pore size of the wick structure may facilitate the capillary flow of the fluid that kept the evaporation surface wet, improving the heat transfer performance of the evaporation surface, especially under high heat-flux conditions. Based on the heat transfer coefficient obtained from the experiment, a numerical simulation based on the mathematical model was also conducted using COMSOL Multiphysics to determine the temperature distribution of the evaporation surface. To achieve objective 3, an analytical heat transfer model was developed to estimate the instantaneous evaporation rate and analyze the evaporation mechanism of the hybrid nanofluids on the superhydrophilic wick-structured surface. The model was developed to study the effects of the contact angle, surface free energy, and surface roughness on the hybrid nanofluid evaporation. Experiments were also conducted in a controlled environment to measure the evaporation rate of the hybrid nanofluids. The results indicated that the evaporation rates increased with the quasi-equilibrium interface surface area and decayed with the quasi-equilibrium contact angle. Besides, improving the hybrid nanofluid’s spread ability and wettability on the evaporation surface could promote the evaporation performance. The liquid spreading could be improved by increasing the surface roughness and porosity of the wick-structured surface while the surface wettability could be enhanced by the surface free energy. Moreover, a numerical model was established to understand the internal convection effect (thermal Marangoni and natural convection effect) on the internal flow field and temperature distribution within the evaporating hybrid nanofluids. The numerical model was solved using COMSOL Multiphysics. The surface tension gradient was used as an input parameter to solve the thermal Marangoni convection in the model. The convection effect inside the hybrid nanofluids was investigated using the dynamic Bond number. Based on the calculated results, the Marangoni force was dominant in the evaporating hybrid nanofluids when compared to the buoyancy force. The enhanced thermal Marangoni convection of the hybrid nanofluids contributed toward the higher evaporation rate because of the improved heat exchange between the liquid-solid and liquid-air interfaces. To meet objective 4, a hybrid nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic-porous tank was designed and fabricated. The evaporation performance of the superhydrophilic-porous tank using the hybrid nanofluids with different mixing ratios and volume fractions was evaluated experimentally and mathematically. The evaporation enhancement was due to the increased heat transfer area from the deposited hybrid nanoparticles. Nevertheless, when the volume fraction of the hybrid nanofluids was further increased, the deposited nanoparticles accumulated to form a layer, resulting in additional thermal resistance on the evaporation surface. Thus, the evaporation rate of the hybrid nanofluid with a high volume fraction was reduced. When considering the mixing ratio, it was found that the thermal conductivity and stability of the hybrid nanofluid needed to be balanced to obtain the highest evaporation rate. Increasing the thermal conductivity of the hybrid nanofluid could facilitate the heat exchange between the heat source and liquid, while enhancing the stability of the hybrid nanofluid could facilitate the fluid spreading on the evaporation surface. A low spreading rate of the fluid could lead to a reduction in the evaporation. The heat transfer and evaporation performance of the hybrid nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick surface was also investigated using a one-dimensional heat transfer model. The evaporation performance of the surface was estimated according to the kinetic theory. The mathematical model well-matched the experimental results. For objective 5, to examine the feasibility of the adsorption cooling systems integrated with the developed evaporator, an adsorption cooling system prototype was developed and tested. A mathematical model was developed to optimize the cooling performance of the adsorption cooling systems by determining the optimal adsorption/desorption phase time. The model has been verified by the experimental results. The model considered the latent heat, specific heat capacity, heat transfer coefficient, and evaporation rate of the evaporator. During the adsorption-evaporation process, the working fluid in the evaporator evaporated when heated by the chiller water. The water vapor was then adsorbed by the composite adsorbent in the adsorber to retain a low-pressure environment in the evaporator for further evaporation. The adsorption heat was dissipated to the cooling water. The adsorption phase stopped when the adsorbent was saturated. During the desorption-condensation process, the adsorber was heated by hot water at a high pressure, and water vapor was desorbed from the adsorbent. Because of the pressure difference, the desorbed water vapor moved to the condenser for condensation. The released condensation heat was transferred to the cooling water. A minimum of two adsorbers with composite adsorbents were needed for a quasi-continuous cooling effect by switching between phase 1 and phase 2. Both the experimental and modeling results indicated that increasing the evaporation rate in the evaporator could improve both the cooling performance and the coefficient of performance of the system since the high evaporation increased the amount of water vapor entering the adsorber.

21200819.label: Major findings and research outcome
21200819.value: The thermal conductivity, latent heat of vaporization, and surface tension of the hybrid nanofluids were measured. The thermal conductivity of the hybrid nanofluids was higher than that of the base fluid (i.e., water) and mono-nanofluid due to the synergistic effect of the inter-particle interaction [item 6 in the table in Part C]. The heat transfer performance of the hybrid-nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick-structured surface was also studied experimentally and mathematically. It was found that the heat transfer performance of the evaporation surface was affected by not only the thermal conductivity of the hybrid nanofluids but also the wettability and wicking effect of the surface, depending on the volume fraction of the hybrid nanofluids. [item 7 in the table in Part C]. Next, the evaporation performances and the underlying mechanism of the hybrid-nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick-structured surface were analyzed. An analytical model was developed to investigate the evaporation mechanism based on the contact angle, contact area, surface energy, and porosity. The results indicated that the evaporation rate of the evaporation surface was improved by high contact area, low contact angle, high surface energy, high porosity, and high surface roughness. This is because improving the wettability of the evaporation surface could facilitate fluid spreading, resulting in greater heat transfer and evaporation performances [item 3 in the table in Part C]. Besides, a numerical model was adopted to analyze the evaporation based on the internal convection of the hybrid nanofluids on the evaporation surface. The results showed that the thermal Marangoni convection effect was dominant inside the hybrid nanofluid layer. The suspended hybrid nanoparticles could facilitate the heat transfer between the heated surface and the fluid layer, improving the evaporation rate [items 6 and 8 in the table in Part C]. After that, a hybrid nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick-structured evaporator was developed and tested. The experimental results indicated that the evaporation rate of the evaporator depended on the mixing ratio and volume fraction which alter the thermal conductivity, and spreading dynamic of the hybrid nanofluids [item 10 in the table in Part C]. Finally, an adsorption cooling system prototype was developed to analyze the cooling performance. A well-matched model was developed to optimize the performance of the adsorption cooling systems. The results indicated that improving the evaporation rate of the evaporator can enhance both the cooling power and efficiency of the system [item 2 in the table in Part C].

21200819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21200819.value: In this project, the performance and efficiency of the adsorption cooling systems were improved using hybrid nanofluids. To further improve the cooling performance of the adsorption cooling systems, hybrid nanoparticles can be implemented in the adsorber. It is expected that the hybrid nanoparticles with high thermal conductivity value can facilitate the heat transfer between the adsorbent and the heating/cooling source, thus improving the adsorption/desorption rate. As a result, the cooling power and efficiency of the system can be enhanced. Besides, to further reduce the energy consumption of the adsorption cooling systems, they can be integrated with passive radiative cooling technology. Passive radiative coolers can be used to pre-cool the cooling water of the system so as to improve the overall efficiency. By using the passive radiative coolers, the cooling energy of the system can be partly supplied by the passive radiative coolers, thus enhancing its cooling efficiency. However, the fundamental study of the hybrid nanofluids in the adsorbent for heat transfer enhancement and the feasibility of adopting the passive radiative coolers to meet the cooling requirement of the adsorption cooling systems have not been investigated comprehensively. Therefore, this can be the future direction for development of the adsorption cooling systems.

21200819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21200819.value: In this project, we have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of using a hybrid-nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick-structured evaporator in an adsorption cooling system. The results indicated that the evaporation rate enhancement of the evaporator promoted the cooling performance and the efficiency of the adsorption cooling systems. Fundamental studies have also been conducted to investigate the evaporation improvement mechanism of the hybrid nanofluids on the superhydrophilic wick-structured surface. The results revealed that both the thermal conductivity of the hybrid nanofluids and surface wettability were essential to enhance the evaporation rate. In addition, we have fabricated and tested a hybrid-nanofluids-saturated superhydrophilic wick-structured evaporator. By optimizing the mixing ratio and volume fraction of the hybrid nanofluids, the evaporation rate of the evaporator saturated by hybrid nanofluids can be 45% higher than that saturated by water. Overall, applying a hybrid nanofluid can boost vapor generation in the adsorption cooling systems, leading to cooling power and efficiency enhancement. Therefore, this project helps to explore new directions for improving the performance of the adsorption cooling systems, promoting commercialization ability and energy saving of the adsorption cooling systems.

21200919.value: 在冶金学中，将微量异质元素添加到纯金属中以形成金属合金是改善其机械性能和辐照性能的常用方法。以往的研究通常将只添加微量量合金元素，从而形成稀释合金。 这些稀释合金的性质强烈依赖于基体的性质，以这种方式人们开发了不同的合金系统，例如广泛研究的Ni基合金，Fe基合金和Mg基合金等。由于这些合金中的主要元素是固定的，因此通过引入微量组分来提高其性能也是很有限的。 与稀释合金相比，浓缩固溶体合金（CSAs，或者高熵合金，HEAs）则由多种主要元素组成，各组分均具有很高浓度。在CSA中，不同元素随机排列在一个简单的晶格之中，导致极端的化学无序和局部晶格畸变。由于其优异的力学性能、较强的耐辐照性和耐腐蚀性，CSA被认为是先进核系统中的候选结构材料之一。在CSA中，合金元素可以在较大的相空间中进行选择，从而提供了一个独特的平台来研究组成元素对合金性能的影响。研究表明，通过选择合适的元素组合形成CSA，可以实现优异的力学强度和抗辐照性能。由于CSA最重要的特征是不同元素随机排列而产生的内在无序状态，因此可以预期通过调节不同组成元素及其浓度可以进一步调控它们的性质。 结合稀释和浓缩合金的概念，本项目将通过向CSA添加少量掺杂元素来探索掺杂CSA的抗辐照性能。具体地，本项目将考虑一系列具有面心立方结构的3d过渡金属组成的CSA，包括NiFe、NiCoCr和NiCoFeCr，以及不同的掺杂元素，例如Al，Cu，Pd和Ti。由于CSA具有优异的抗辐照性，因此预计掺杂将是进一步改善其辐照性能的有效方法。本项目将采用多尺度计算模拟手段来深入了解不同杂质和不同CSA基底结合导致的不同的缺陷能量图谱。首先，通过基于密度泛函理论（DFT）的第一性原理计算，研究不同局部环境下的缺陷能量。计算得到的局部环境依赖的缺陷数据库，结合我们之前在等原子CSA中获得的结果，将用于构建机器学习（ML）模型，以便预测任何给定环境下的缺陷能量。该结果将用于原子动力学蒙特卡罗（AKMC）模拟，以研究长时间尺度上的缺陷演变。模拟获得的结果，包括不同掺杂元素在改变缺陷能量和组成元素的不同扩散系数方面的影响，将用于与实验上的透射电子显微镜（TEM）和原子探针扫描（APT）分析结果做对比。我们的合作者将对样品制备和辐照表征实验提供支持。这项多尺度研究的结果将加深我们对不同元素及其浓度在掺杂CSAs中所起作用的理解，并最终提供一种科学的方法来调整元素种类及其浓度以提高其辐照性能。

21200919.label: Realisation of objectives
21200919.value: Objective 1: Evaluate the effect of different dopants and their concentrations on defect energetics in different CSAs. This objective was achieved by performing extensive first-principles calculations on defect energetics in doped CSAs. Specifically, four different dopants, namely, Al, Cu, Ti, and Pd in CoCrFeNi were considered, which cover a variety of different dopants with different electronic structure properties and a multicomponent concentrated alloy with diverse local atomic environments, which are typical for such a class of complex alloys and has great implications for its subsystems. The defect energetics, including vacancy formation and migration energies, and interstitial formation and migration energies, were calculated. Besides, the influence of different doping concentrations on these defect energies was considered. The obtained defect energy distributions were compiled as a database and openly accessible. Objective 2: Establish a defect database using a certain machine learning model based on defect energies obtained by first-principles calculations. Based on the defect energy database in the binary, ternary, and quaternary alloys obtained from our extensive first-principles calculations, we built machine learning models to establish the relations between local chemical disorder and defect properties. Particularly, we studied FeNi, FeNiCr, and FeNiCoCr alloys and calculated their defect formation and migration energies. With the obtained data, we used machine learning models to describe the relations between the defect energies and the local atomic environments around the defect. For this purpose, the local atomic environments were used as descriptors as the input for the machine learning model, while the obtained defect energies were used as our output. The database contains around 2000 DFT data for each alloy. The machine learning model was built using artificial neural networks (ANN), and the performance was evaluated based on the 10-fold cross-validation method. The error from a well-trained model can be as low as 50 meV/defect, which is acceptable for fast evaluating defect properties under given local environments. Objective 3: Build an Atomistic Kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulation scheme based on a defect database from first-principles calculations and a machine learning model. We have combined atomistic kinetic Monte Carlo with the machine learning model to carry out long-time diffusion simulation for the concentrated alloys considered. The well-trained machine learning was used as the on-the-fly energy barrier calculator, and kinetic Monte Carlo was established to study defect diffusion under versatile local atomic environments. Thanks to the kMC algorithm, long-time simulations were achieved, which allowed us to pinpoint the dominant factors influencing defect diffusion in concentrated alloys, and further elucidate the role of short-range chemical ordering in the diffusion process. Objective 4: Validate our simulation scheme with state-of-art experimental techniques including TEM and APT regarding defect evolution and elemental segregation. This objective was achieved through our collaboration with experimentalists. In the experiment, a 0.2 molar ratio of Al/Cu/Ti was respectively added into the quaternary CoCrFeNi. The alloys were then irradiated by 2 MeV He ions at four temperatures from 673 to 973 K. After irradiation, He bubble behavior in specimens was investigated by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The results showed that bubbles in the minor alloying HEAs usually had a larger size, lower number density, and broader distribution range, comparing to their parent alloy. Such effects were more significant at a higher irradiation temperature and most pronounced by the addition of Ti. These results were understood based on our defect energies calculations, which revealed that the alloying addition could change the energy barrier for vacancy migration and formation in CoCrFeNi system, which thereby promotes He diffusion through the elemental replacement via the vacancy mechanism. Objective 5: Reveal the influence of different elements and their concentrations on the irradiation performance of doped-CSAs. Based on first-principles calculations and kMC simulations, the influence of minor doping elements on the properties of defect energies was evaluated. The effects of substitutional doping element species were investigated with Al, Cu, Pd, and Ti dopants and different doping concentrations were considered. It was found that doping elements located at the 1nn shell of the defect exerted a profound impact on defect energetics. Specifically, doping can decrease vacancy formation energies while enhancing migration energies at the same time. On the other hand, the energetics of interstitials were only slightly affected. Among the four elements, we discovered that Ti and Pd generally have more significant effects than Al and Cu in altering defect energies, which was attributed to the charge transfer and electronic interactions between the dopants and the constituent elements in HEAs. Increasing the doping concentration can further intensify the doping effects. Through kMC simulations with DFT energetics database, we show that doping can effectively tune atomic transport in HEAs. Therefore, tuning the electronic properties of constitutive elements in a HEA matrix through doping with minor impurities is an effective strategy to manipulate the defect energy landscape and improve irradiation resistance for HEAs. From experiments, we further verified that He bubbles in the minor alloy elements doped HEAs had a wider distribution range, larger size, and lower number density, compared to that of the parent alloy. Such effects were more significant at a higher irradiation temperature and more pronounced by the sequence of Ti-, Cu-, and Al-addition. These results are in good agreement with our theoretical analysis based on defect energies obtained on the basis of DFT.

21200919.label: Major findings and research outcome
21200919.value: Major findings: (1) Doping is an effective way to tune defect energies and irradiation performance of concentrated alloys. The formation and migration energies of vacancies are strongly influenced when a dopant is introduced at the first nearest neighbor shells around a vacancy. On the other hand, interstitial energetics are only slightly affected. Among different elements, Ti and Pd generally decrease vacancy formation energies and increase vacancy migration energies more significantly than Al and Cu. The doping effects become more pronounced when the concentration of the substitutional dopants increases. Furthermore, Ti and Pd can lower the tracer diffusivity in the considered HEAs and act as trapping sites, whereas Cu may enhance the atomic transport. (2) Machine learning is a powerful way to establish the unique relationship between versatile local atomic environments and defect energies. Due to the extreme chemical disorder, defect properties are highly variable depending on the local atomic arrangement. Such nonlinear relations cannot be described by a conventional method. Therefore, machine learning is an effective and viable option to establish the correspondence between chemical disorders and defect energetics. Our results show that an artificial neural network is a promising way for acting as the media to model such complex relations. It is expected that in the future, in combination with the latest development in machine learning techniques, further improvement of accuracy can be achieved for even more chemically complex alloys, such as high-entropy alloys with more than five components. (3) The combination of machine learning and kinetic Monte Carlo is an effective methodology for studying long-term defect evolution in chemically-complexed alloys. In these alloys, on the one hand, molecular dynamics simulations are difficult to perform due to the unavailability of suitable empirical potentials. On the other hand, defect kinetics becomes so slow that molecular dynamics methods are unable to probe the long-time dynamics. Therefore, building upon the defect database from DFT calculations is a viable way to study defect evolution in this class of complex alloys. Research outcome: Through GRF support, we have published 20 SCI papers, including those in first-rate journals, such as Acta Materialia, Journal of Alloys and Compounds, Journal of Nuclear Materials, etc. We also presented our work at several international and national conferences, including the TMS meeting before the pandemic.

21200919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21200919.value: In HEAs, extreme chemical disorder makes defect energies highly variable depending on local atomic environments. The complexity of the local atomic environments increases exponentially with the increase of alloying components, posing a great challenge to conventional machine learning techniques such as artificial neural networks as employed here. Future development will be required for employing advanced machine learning techniques to improve the accuracy and transferability of the machine learning model for describing defect energies in different HEAs.

21200919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21200919.value: In metallurgy, the addition of foreign elements into pure metals to form metallic alloys is a usual way to improve their mechanical properties and radiation performances. Traditionally, only a small amount of alloying element is added to a pure metal so that a dilute alloy is formed. The properties of these dilute alloys rely heavily on the matrix, and different alloy systems are developed in this way, such as extensively studied Ni-based alloys, Fe-based alloys and Mg-based alloys. Since the principal element in these alloys is fixed, the performance improvement by incorporating minor components is limited. In contrast to dilute alloys, concentrated solid-solution alloys (CSAs, or high entropy alloys, HEAs) are composed of multiple principal elements all at high concentrations. In CSAs, the random arrangement of different elements in a simple underlying crystal lattice results in extreme chemical disorder and local lattice distortions. Combining the concepts of dilute and concentrated alloys, we show that the performance of CSAs can be significantly improved and modified by adding a small concentration of doping elements to CSAs.

21201119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21201119.value: The building sector accounts for a large proportion of the total energy consumption in different regions. Thermal energy storage (TES) technologies play a significant role in building energy efficiency by balancing the mismatched timing and intensity between renewable energy supply and building energy demand. Compared to other existing TES technologies, the absorption TES (ATES) stands out due to its high energy storage density (ESD), low charging temperature, relatively high coefficient of performance (COP), and fast charging/discharging. These merits can facilitate much better utilization of renewable and waste energy for buildings. In addition, the low-grade thermal energy stored by ATES systems can be discharged in the form of cooling, heating, or dehumidification, offering a wider flexibility than current TES systems. Although the ATES technology has been increasingly studied, it still suffers from two critical shortcomings: (1) the crystallization risk of the conventional working fluids limits the ESD and system reliability; and (2) the charging temperature of the conventional ATES cycle (minimum of 80 °C) cannot be further decreased while maintaining an efficiency at satisfactory level. These two key problems seriously limit the wider adoption of the ATES technology. To maximize ATES’s contribution to energy saving and emission mitigation, a hybrid compression-assisted ATES (CATES) system using ionic liquids (ILs) as novel working fluids is proposed in this project. This hybrid CATES can be charged at temperatures as low as 50-60 °C with high COPs and be charged to more concentrated solutions (free of crystallization) with high ESDs. In this study, property models of various novel IL-based mixtures and dynamic thermodynamic models of the hybrid CATES cycle will be established for characterizing various cycle performance indices and charging/discharging behaviors. An experimental prototype of the hybrid CATES will be developed for performance measurement and model validation. Various groups of IL-based working fluids will be screened to identify their best performance and applicable domain for the hybrid CATES system. The compression ratio of the hybrid CATES system will be optimized for more efficient control under various conditions. A transient building energy simulation platform will be established to investigate the annual performance of the hybrid CATES to facilitate the design and operation in different buildings and climates. This project will motivate further progress in academia and industry, providing a promising approach towards sustainable buildings and societies by making the best of the natural resources in Hong Kong and all over the world. 建築能耗占不同地區總能耗的比例非常大。蓄熱技術在建築節能中具有重要的作用，因其可以平衡可再生能源供應和建築能源需求。與現有蓄熱技術相比，吸收式蓄熱技術具有較高的蓄能密度、較低的蓄能溫度、較高的蓄能效率以及較快的蓄能/釋能速率。這些優勢能夠有效促進可再生能源和廢熱在建築中的應用。此外，通過吸收式蓄熱系統存儲的低品位熱能可以非常靈活地釋放出來，用於供冷、供熱和除濕。盡管近年來有關吸收式蓄熱的研究日益增多，但仍存在兩個關鍵問題有待解決：（1）傳統吸收式工質對的結晶風險限制了蓄能密度和系統可靠性；（2）傳統吸收式蓄熱循環的最低蓄能溫度偏高（通常在80°C以上），需要在維持較高蓄能效率的前提下進壹步降低蓄能溫度。這兩個關鍵問題嚴重制約著吸收式蓄熱技術的推廣應用。 為了充分發揮吸收式蓄熱技術在節能減排中的貢獻，本項目提出壹種采用離子液體工質對的增壓輔助型復合吸收式蓄熱系統。該復合蓄熱系統能高效地蓄存 50-60 °C的低溫熱能，且能達到較高的溶液濃度而無結晶風險，從而具有較高的蓄能密度。本研究將建立不同離子液體工質對的物性模型和復合吸收式蓄熱系統的熱力循環模型，用於分析其循環整體性能和蓄能/釋能動態特征。將會研發復合吸收式蓄熱系統的試驗樣機，開展實驗測試及模型驗證。將會對比不同離子液體工質對，以遴選出性能較好的工質對，並分析其適用範圍。將會對復合循環的壓縮比進行優化，以實現更加高效的運行控制。此外，還會建立建築能耗動態模擬平臺，以分析復合吸收式蓄熱系統的全年運行性能，為該技術在不同氣候和不同建築中的設計和運行提供指導。本項目預期推動學術和技術進步，為香港和全球的可持續建築發展提供很有潛力的技術方案。

21201119.label: Realisation of objectives
21201119.value: We set five project objectives and carried out a lot of activities focused on these objectives. These activities can contribute to (1) development of a CATES technology; (2) performance characterization of the novel CATES under various operating parameters; (3) IL screening to maximize the performance; (4) optimization for more efficient controlling under various conditions; and (5) annual performance investigation to facilitate rational design and operation in different buildings and climates. All the project objectives have been successfully achieved as planned, with details summarized as follows. 1. To develop a CATES technology featuring high ESD, low charging temperature, high COP and fast charging/discharging. To realize the proposed concept of CATES, we design a hybrid energy storage cycle. In the charging process, the solution tank functions as a generator to produce vapor refrigerant with heat transferred from the external heat source to the solution, while the refrigerant tank functions as a condenser to liquify the refrigerant with condensation heat transferred from the refrigerant to the external heat sink. In the discharging process, the solution tank functions as an absorber for absorbing the incoming vapor refrigerant with absorption heat transferred from the solution to the external heat sink, while the refrigerant tank functions as an evaporator to vaporize the refrigerant with heat transferred from the external fluid to the refrigerant. Compared to the basic ATES cycle, the hybrid CATES cycle with compression decreases the generation pressure in the charging process and thus strengthen the vapor generation in the solution tank. In the discharging process, the compression increases the absorption pressure and thus strengthen the vapor absorption into the solution. In our design, either of the compression processes can be disabled to form different energy storage cycles through valve switching. The hybrid cycles include CATES with compression in both charging and discharging processes, CATES with compression in charging process only, CATES with compression in discharging process only. The structure design has been modified based on the established model. The prototype has been successfully manufactured for characterization and demonstration. 2. To characterize the cycle performance and dynamic behaviors of the novel CATES system under various operating parameters. The transient behaviors of the charging and discharging processes are modeled based on energy and mass conservation equations and heat transfer equations. The charging process and discharging process are modelled in a similar manner. Based on the above model of each component, the entire CATES cycle is modelled. The energy storage efficiency (ESE) of the CATES is the ratio of the cumulative discharged cooling capacity to the cumulative energy consumption. The ESEs without and with energy conversion are defined. The ESD (kWh/m3) of the CATES is the ratio of the cumulative discharged cooling capacity to the summed solution volume and liquid refrigerant volume. With the above mathematic equations, the dynamic behaviors and storage performance of the hybrid CATES are simulated following a proposed algorithm. The dynamic model is validated by comparing the simulated results with the experimental results. The transient heat duties of the generation, condensation, absorption, and evaporation processes are compared. The good agreement between the two data sets indicates that the model is of high accuracy. Using this model, the cycle performance and dynamic behaviors of the novel CATES system are investigated under various operating parameters (e.g., temperatures and flow rates). 3. To screen various groups of IL-based working fluids to maximize the performance of the hybrid CATES system. To identify well-performing ILs, the circulation ratio is used for the preliminary screening from a group of ILs. [EMIM][Ac], [EMIM][DEP], and [EMIM]EtSO4] yield the lowest circulation ratios in most conditions. [DMIM][DMP] yields the highest ESE of 0.722 while [EMIM][DEP] yields the lowest ESE of 0.603. [DMIM][DMP] shows the highest ESD of 94.1 kWh/m3 while [EMIM][DEP] shows the lowest ESD of 77.5 kWh/m3. The ESEs and ESDs of the ATES and CATES cycles under various generation temperatures are also studied. Compared with ATES, CATES can operate under lower charging temperatures. For the CATES, H2O/[DMIM][DMP] has the highest ESE and performs better than H2O/LiBr when Tg is above 86 °C. When Tg is below 75 °C, H2O/[EMIM][EtSO4] shows the highest ESE among all the working fluids. H2O/[EMIM][EtSO4] can operate under 70 °C, so that the CATES can be charged by lower-temperature thermal energy. The CATES yields much higher ESDs. The conventional H2O/LiBr suffers from crystallization when Tg is above 90 °C and has lower ESDs than H2O/[EMIM][EtSO4] when Tg is below 76 °C. Under Tg of 100 °C, the ESD is 65.9, 67.6, 55.8 and 55.6 kWh/m3 for H2O/[DMIM][DMP], H2O/[EMIM][Ac], H2O/[EMIM][DEP], and H2O/[EMIM][EtSO4], respectively. Under Tg of 80 °C, the ESD is 22.2, 30.0, 26.9, and 35.5 kWh/m3, respectively. H2O/[EMIM][Ac] shows the highest ESD when Tg is above 86 °C, while H2O/[EMIM][EtSO4] shows the highest ESD when Tg is below 86 °C. 4. To optimize the compression ratio of the hybrid CATES system for more efficient controlling under various conditions. We compare the energy storage performance of four cycles under various charging temperatures. When the charging temperature is lower than 80 °C, the energy storage performance gap between the basic ATES and hybrid CATES cycles is notable, and the gap becomes larger as the charging temperature decreases. The cycle performance under various pressure ratios is investigated. The overall trend is that the ESE first increases and then decreases as the pressure ratio increases. As for the ESD, it is 110.3 kWh/m3 for the basic ATES cycle (Pr=1.0) and enhanced to 135.9-199.2 kWh/m3 by the hybrid CATES cycle with Pr=1.2~2.0, significantly improved by 23.2~80.5%. Therefore, the pressure ratio is suggested to be no higher than 1.6. The highest ESE of CATES with discharging compression is 0.816 at Pr=1.6, while the highest ESE is 0.794 (Pr=1.2) for CATES with charging/discharging compression and 0.790 (Pr=1.0) for CATES with charging compression, respectively. As for the ESD, CATES with discharging compression is 1.6~4.3% lower than CATES with charging/discharging compression. However, compared to CATES with charging compression, CATES with discharging compression significantly enhanced the ESD by 11.4~52.0%. The CATES with discharging compression is comprehensively the best hybrid energy storage cycle, with both high ESDs and ESEs under low charging temperatures. 5. To investigate the annual performance of the hybrid CATES to facilitate the design and operation in different buildings and climates. The annual dynamic performance of solar-driven ATES is investigated and compared in four representative cities by simulation using an experimentally validated model, considering transient supply-demand matching. We further conduct comparative investigations among different absorption thermal battery cycles from a multi-criteria perspective, including energy storage efficiency, energy storage density, exergy efficiency, charging temperature, and initial cost. The effects of charging/discharging/cooling temperatures on the storage performance are analyzed in three scenarios, i.e., short-term cold storage, short-term heat storage, and long-term heat storage. Results indicate that the compression-assisted cycle and the double-stage cycle can improve the energy storage density and lower the charging temperatures (e.g., below 70 °C); the double-effect cycle can enhance the energy storage efficiency; the double-effect compression-assisted cycle can achieve improvements in energy storage efficiency and density simultaneously, with a maximum energy storage efficiency above 1.3 and energy storage density over 300 kWh/m3. This work aims to facilitate rational development of absorption thermal batteries towards carbon neutrality.

21201119.label: Major findings and research outcome
21201119.value: A novel hybrid compression-assisted absorption thermal battery is proposed. Three types of hybrid cycles are compared with the basic cycle. Dynamic characteristics and storage performance are studied. A maximum storage density of 282.8 kW/m3 is achieved. Better efficiency (0.66–0.71) is obtained with discharging process compression. Hybrid crystallization-free thermal batteries using H2O/[DMIM][DMP] is proposed. Effect of pressure ratio on transient performance is compared for various batteries. Storage density is greatly increased from 110.3 to 199.2 kWh/m3. Discharging compression outperforms charging compression by 52% in storage density. A novel double-effect absorption thermal energy storage cycle is proposed. Energy storage efficiency increased by up to 61.6% for cooling and 61.8% for heating. It is more suitable for charging temperatures above 160 °C. Optimization of solution mass distribution shows that equal-distribution is the best. A novel double-effect compression-assisted absorption thermal battery is proposed. Energy storage efficiency and density are significantly enhanced by 24% and 145%. The discharging rate is stabilized with the assistance of compression. A novel type II absorption thermal battery is proposed for temperature upgrading. A maximum storage density of 292.7 kWh/m3 is obtained. Temperature lifts of 10–55 ºC are achieved. There is a trade-off between the energy storage and heat transformer performance. A novel compression-assisted absorption energy storage heat transformer is proposed. The temperature lift is increased from 30 ºC to 65 ºC. The driving temperature is lowered from 60 ºC to 45 ºC. Various advanced cycles are compared for short-term and long-term storage. The compression-assisted cycle achieves a maximum storage efficiency of 1.53. The double-effect cycle obtains a maximum storage density of 365.4 kW/m3. The basic cycle yields a maximum exergy storage efficiency of 0.61. Energy storage efficiency and density are compared among different ionic liquids. The new technology avoids crystallization, lowers charging temperature, and improves energy storage performance. [EMIM][Ac] needs the longest charging time but shows the highest discharging rate. Novel computer-aided molecular design for H2O/ionic liquid used in absorption cycle. Eight machine learning algorithms are compared to predict the cycle performance. Relationship between cycle performance and molecular structures is well established. The best-performance ionic liquids identified under 18 typical operating conditions. Low-GWP refrigerants are studied for compression-assisted absorption cycles. Different hydrofluorocarbons and hydrofluoroolefins are paired with ionic liquid as alternative working fluids. Difluoromethane has the highest COPs while 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene has the lowest in most conditions. Compression ratios are optimized to be 1.9–3.4.

21201119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21201119.value: The proposed hybrid compression-assisted absorption thermal energy storage (CATES) or compression-assisted absorption thermal battery (CATB) technology has great potential to significantly save the building energy consumption. The results and findings of this project will motivate further research on advanced ATES systems with high ESDs and low charging temperatures for buildings. They will also provide a promising solution to engineering design and operation of sustainable energy systems. Wide commercialization and applications of this novel CATES technology will greatly cut the use of fossil fuels. It can also help the HKSAR Government realize the target to reduce the carbon intensity by 65-70% from the 2005 level by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2050. In 1-5 years, our research team will collaborate with relevant institutes and manufacturers to deepen the research and promote the development. In 5-10 years, our research team will collaborate with relevant enterprises and building users to promote better applications and further improve the energy saving effects. Over 10 years. our research team will collaborate with relevant governmental departments and NGOs to promote wider applications of this technology to maximize long-term energy saving and emission mitigation.

21201119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21201119.value: Thermal energy storage (TES) plays a significant role in building energy efficiency by addressing the supply-demand mismatch. Absorption TES (ATES) stands out due to its high energy storage density/efficiency and low charging temperature. Besides, the discharged energy can be flexible used for cooling, heating, or dehumidification. However, ATES suffers from two critical shortcomings: (1) the crystallization risk of conventional working fluids limits the energy storage density/reliability; and (2) the charging temperature of conventional ATES cycles (minimum of 80 °C) cannot be further decreased while maintaining a satisfactory efficiency. To solve these problems, a hybrid compression-assisted ATES (CATES) using ionic liquids (ILs) is proposed in this project. This hybrid CATES can be charged at temperatures as low as 50-60 °C with high efficiency and be charged to more concentrated solutions (crystallization free) with high density. The project objectives include (1) development of a CATES technology; (2) performance characterization of the novel CATES under various operating parameters; (3) IL screening to maximize the performance; (4) optimization for more efficient controlling under various conditions; and (5) annual performance investigation to facilitate rational design and operation in different buildings and climates. This project provides a promising approach towards sustainable buildings and societies.

21204819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21204819.value: 該項目的目的是研究新的多維網絡分析框架，以評估多式聯運交通系統的抵禦災害能力（resilience，或譯作‘韌性’ 、‘彈性’）。該框架的實用性將在香港公共交通的背景下展示，其包括了五種交通方式：地鐵軌道交通，公共大型巴士，公共小型巴士、電車和渡輪。城市公共交通作為最關鍵的基礎設施之壹，任何停運、中斷（即使是部分停運）都會對城市的健康、安全和經濟造成破壞性影響。香港公共交通負載了每天旅客出行人次總數的90%，其中斷可能對經濟和社會產生災難性的級聯影響。該問題引起了社會關註，尤其是考慮到氣候變化導致的極端天氣事件在增加時（就如最近遭遇的超強臺風Mangkhut）。這個為期3年的項目被分為三個目標： 1. 建立香港多式聯運公共交通的時空網絡模型。 2. 制定交通系統韌性的立方體方法，用於評估系統韌性循環的四個階段：準備，承受，恢復和適應。 3. 確定提高香港多式聯運公共交通系統韌性的方案，和其幹預點及優先級。 這種方法將用於計算香港公共交通系統韌性的各個維度。網絡拓撲和客流的數據將分別通過私人運輸公司和香港政府運輸部門獲得。該項目的結果將允許我們對投入設施升級的有限資金和其他資源進行優化分配。該項目的成功完成將提供空間和時間的特定規範性戰略，將支持香港交通規劃者和運營商的決策。

21204819.label: Realisation of objectives
21204819.value: The project objectives have been successfully achieved, as demonstrated by the publication of the research paper in Nature Communications. The paper, titled "Interconnectedness Enhances Network Resilience of Multimodal Public Transportation Systems for Safe-to-Fail Urban Mobility," addresses all three project objectives. Firstly, the paper creates a network model that integrates the five modes of public transportation in Hong Kong, thereby achieving the first objective. The model is designed to capture the interconnectedness of the different modes and their impact on the overall resilience of the transportation system. Secondly, the paper develops a multi-dimensional transportation resilience assessment composed of network measures of the four phases of the resilience cycle (prepare, withstand, recover, and adapt). This achievement addresses the project's second objective, which is to develop a comprehensive framework for assessing the resilience of multimodal public transportation systems. Lastly, the paper identifies points of intervention and prioritizes actions to support decision-making for a resilient multi-modal public transportation system in Hong Kong. This achievement aligns with the third objective of the project, which is to provide practical recommendations for improving the resilience of the transportation system. The publication of the paper in Nature Communications is a testament to the high quality and impact of the research. The paper has been cited in the policy report "Research and innovation in transport safety and resilience in Europe" from the Publications Office of the EU (Publications Office of the European Union, September 27, 2023). They cite the paper to emphasize the need for multimodal integration and modal shift to understand urban mobility resilience, indicating its relevance and usefulness to policymakers and the research community. Additionally, the paper has been shared on various social media platforms, increasing its visibility and outreach. In conclusion, the project objectives have been successfully achieved, and the research paper published in Nature Communications is a testament to the high quality and impact of the research. The project's achievements demonstrate the importance of interconnectedness in enhancing the resilience of multimodal public transportation systems, providing valuable insights for decision-makers and researchers in the field. 21204819.label: Major findings and research outcome
21204819.value: Overall, this proposal highlights the advantages of interconnectedness in the public transportation sector and provides insights for transportation planners to enhance the resilience of their systems. The findings suggest that interconnection can improve network robustness, interoperability, and efficiency, and address common vulnerabilities in public transportation networks. Specifically, this major findings of this proposal can be summarized as follows: Interconnectedness can enhance the resilience of public transportation systems by improving network robustness, interoperability, and efficiency. The integration of different transport modes within the public transportation sector can create a safe-to-fail system design, allowing for the redistribution of stranded flows in case of disruptions. The Hong Kong MPTN exhibits strong tolerance to minor disruptions and increased robustness when facing random disruptions and attacks on interchange stations and hubs. Interconnecting vulnerable systems can improve the overall network robustness, and intermodal edges provide an opportunity to adjust the network topology and address the source of vulnerability. Enhancing interconnection can address the common vulnerability of public transportation networks at their hubs and transfer stations. The examination of robustness at different intermodal transfer (IMT) distances reveals a concave-down relationship, suggesting that there can be considerable benefits to enhancing intermodal transfer in a transportation system with poor IMT accessibility. The Hong Kong MPTN exhibits significant interoperability in single disruption scenarios due to its densely placed stations, facilitating a safe-to-fail system design by redistributing stranded flows. The primary dataset utilized in this study adheres to the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) format, facilitating generalizability, validation, and replication of the analysis for future research.

21204819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21204819.value: The potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action are vast and diverse. The study's findings have significant implications for transportation systems in various cities, and the research's methodology and approach can be applied to other network-like infrastructures seeking to develop safe-to-fail designs. One possible direction for future research is to explore the application of the study's findings to other cities and regions, taking into account their unique characteristics and challenges. This could involve examining the interconnectedness of different transportation modes in various urban settings, identifying potential vulnerabilities and areas for improvement, and developing strategies for enhancing robustness and resilience. Another potential avenue for further research is to delve deeper into the development of standardized metrics and data collection approaches for transportation systems. The use of standardized formats like GTFS can facilitate the sharing and comparison of data across different cities and regions, enabling the development of more effective and efficient solutions. Additionally, future research could explore the integration of other factors and variables into the analysis, such as demands, capacity, and interdependencies between different transportation modes and sectors. This could provide a more comprehensive understanding of the complex interactions within transportation systems and inform the development of more holistic and effective strategies for enhancing resilience.

21204819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21204819.value: Cities around the globe, including Hong Kong, are fortifying their resilience to extreme weather events while simultaneously pushing forward with their sustainability and climate change mitigation targets. This requires a revamp of urban planning strategies and an overhaul of infrastructure systems to guarantee long-term sustainability and short-term resilience. The project aims to reduce the potential hazards of disruptions in Hong Kong's public transport system, a critical infrastructure that accommodates 90% of daily passenger trips. Any significant interruption could trigger cascading impacts on the city's economy, public health, and security. The research project provides valuable insights into the resilience of Hong Kong's public transportation system, highlighting its ability to adapt and recover from disruptions. It reveals that highly interconnected transportation networks can mitigate vulnerabilities and enhance tolerance against disruptions, while also improving post-disruption interoperability. Furthermore, the research offers a promising solution for bolstering the robustness of vulnerable systems by linking them together. Also, the findings have far-reaching implications and can serve as a guide for infrastructural improvements on a global scale. This research project is a significant step towards creating more resilient and sustainable transportation systems, ultimately contributing to the well-being and safety of Hong Kong, and other urban systems worldwide.

21205019.value: 基於物理和機理的Ti和Ti-6Al-4V合金塑性變形與斷裂預測模型

21205019.label: Project Objectives

21205019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21205019.value: Titanium (Ti) alloys are widely used in light weight, high strength and high resistance to corrosion applications. They have strategic importances in the aerospace, energy and biomedical industries. Despite their importances, the grain-scale defects, microstructures and their interactions in Ti are not well understood, even though they control material strengthening, hardening, fatigue and fracture. The proposed research aims to quantitatively establish the grain-scale materials science and mechanics of hexagonal close-packed (HCP) Ti and dual-phase HCP/body-centered cubic (BCC) Ti-6Al-4V (Ti64) alloy by (i) determining their defect properties and solute chemistry at the accuracy of quantum mechanics; (ii) developing accurate atomistic potentials capable of reproducing defect properties and solute chemistry; (iii) investigating the mechanisms of plastic deformation and fracture; and (iv) developing physics and mechanism-based, predictive models capturing the essential materials science and mechanics of Ti. The proposed research uses a sequential multiscale approach spanning quantum, atomistic and micro mechanics scales. First, fundamental defect properties and their interactions with Al and V solutes will be rigorously calculated using density functional theory, thereby forming the Material Genome of Ti. Secondly, based on the above Material Genome, accurate empirical/semi-empirical interatomic potentials will be developed using new formalisms of the Multistate Modified Embedded Atom Method and/or Neural Network potentials, thus overcoming limitations of all previous models. Success will enable realistic simulations of defects and microstructures in Ti and Ti64 at atomistic details, and thus represents significant advances in Ti science. Thirdly, the micromechanics of defects, including dislocations, twins, interfaces and their interactions, will be investigated in atomistic simulations using developed potentials. With that, the effects of temperature, stress and strain, microstructure and alloying on material plasticity and fracture will be quantitatively determined. Finally, mechanism-based predictive models will be developed to capture the essential materials science and mechanics obtained from the above quantum, atomistic and micromechanics scales. Such predictive models can guide designs of new Ti alloys and serve as inputs to mechanism-based, finite element models at engineering scales. The proposed research integrates state-of-the-art computational material models and theory, and leverages the latest breakthrough in HCP Mg alloys. Knowledge gained in each scale will advance both fundamental science and engineering designs of Ti alloys. The research program, combining quantum, atomistic and micro mechanics, thus enables the transformation of the empirically-driven, descriptive metallurgy to physics-based, predictive science.

21207019.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21207019.value: 规则区域上的加权逼近

21207019.label: Project Objectives
21207019.value: The first objective of this project is to investigate the convergence of Cesàro means associated with weighted orthogonal polynomials on spheres and related domains, where the weight functions are invariant under a finite reflection group. In such weighted setting, we shall determine critical indexes, for which Cesàro means is convergent in Lp norm for p≥1 and convergent almost everywhere. The second objective of this project is to study the error of Chebyshev-type cubature formulas for weighted Besov spaces on spheres and related domains. We expect to estimate the upper and lower bounds for this error in terms of the size of Chebyshev-type cubature formulas.

21207019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21207019.value: In mathematics, it is often desirable to approximate general functions on various compact domains by simpler functions. Then one naturally asks how good these approximations are, and what are the best rates that one can theoretically achieve for a given class of functions. For studying these problems, cubature formulas (CFs) and orthogonal polynomial expansions (OPEs) have been playing vital roles in dealing with various important topics, such as n-widths, spherical wavelet frames, distribution of points on spheres, covering and packing problems, coding theory and some aspects of convex geometry. Modern problems in CFs, OPEs are often formulated in several variables on various regular domains, such as spheres, cubes, balls, and simplexes, driven by applications in engineering, biology, medicine and quantum physics. At the current stage, however, in contrast to the situation in one variable, many fundamental problems have not been solved. The purpose of this project is to understand the qualitative and quantitative features of CFs and weighted OPEs (WOPEs) on regular domains with weights invariant under certain reflection group. Our topics will be focused on: Convergence of Cesáro means in weighted Lp spaces; Optimal Chebyshev-type cubature formulas in weighted Besov spaces. As long-term goals, we shall apply the expected results to challenges in quantitative approximation and other related areas, such as functional analysis, discrete geometry and convex geometry. 在數學中，人們通常需要用簡單的函數來近似定義在各種緊湊域上的一般函數。然後我們自然地會考慮這樣的近似效果有多好，對於特定的一類函數，理論上所能達到的最佳近似速率是多少？對於這些問題的研究，求積公式（CFs）和正交多項式展開（OPE）在用於處理各種重要課題發揮著至關重要的作用，例如：n寬度，球面小波框架，球體上的點分佈，覆蓋和打包問題，編碼理論和凸幾何。現今，在工程，生物學，醫學和量子物理髮展的驅動下，我們需要解決關於CFs 和 OPE在多變量框架下定義各種常規領域，如球體，立方體和單純形的課題。然而，在目前階段，相比於一個變量的情況，對於多變量的研究許多基本問題尚未解決。 該項目的目的是理解定義在加權常規域上CF和 OPE（WOPE）的定性和定量特徵。我們的研究課題將集中在：Cesaro 平均在加權Lp空間的收斂性質; 加權Besov空間中的最優Chebyshev型求積公式。作為長期目標，我們將把預期結果應用於解決定量逼近和其他相關領域的課題，例如定量分析，離散幾何和凸幾何。

21207019.label: Realisation of objectives
21207019.value: During the past 3 years, we have established a series of results in approximation theory on regular domains. In this paper “Isotropic positive definite functions on spheres”, we investigate the relationship between positive definite functions on unit spheres and on the Euclidean spaces. For the dimension to be odd, a new technique is developed to establish the inheritance of positive definite property from the Euclidean domain to unit spheres and the converse. For dimension to be two, we first proved the positive definiteness of a truncated function on the 3-dimensional unit sphere. Our results can verify a conjecture proposed by Beatson etc. and a sharp Pólya type criterion for positive definite functions on spheres. In the paper “Cesàro Means of Weighted Orthogonal Expansions on Regular Domains”, we investigate Cesàro means for the weighted orthogonal polynomial expansions on spheres with weights being invariant under a general finite reflection group on Rd. Our theorems extend previous results only for specific reflection groups. The upper estimates of the Cesàro kernels and Cesàro means are obtained and used to prove the convergence of the Cesàro (C, d) means in the weighted Lp space for d above the corresponding index. We also establish similar results for the corresponding estimates on the unit ball and the simplex. Based on approximation estimations we have developed, in the paper “Theory of deep convolutional neural networks II: Spherical analysis” and “” we considered a family of deep convolutional neural networks applied to approximate functions on the unit spheres. Our analysis presents rates of uniform and L_p approximation when the approximated function lies in the Sobolev space or takes an additive ridge form. Our result verifies theoretically the modeling and approximation ability of deep convolutional neural networks followed by downsampling and one fully connected layer or two. The key idea of our spherical analysis is to use the inner product form of the reproducing kernels of the spaces of spherical harmonics and efficient cubature formulae on spheres and other tools from approximation theory.

21207019.value: 1. In this project, we extend these results to the case of a general finite reflection group, using the standard theory of Dunkl operators and spherical h-harmonics. These kinds of estimates were previously known only for some particular reflection groups. Also, we establish similar results for the corresponding estimates on the unit ball and the simplex. The related outcome has been accepted for publication in Mathematics (ISSN 2227-7390). 2. We have constructed a family of positive definite kernels with respect to spherical distance. Such kernel will be utilized to construct interpolation approximation of functions on the unit sphere. And a long conjecture problem has been solved partly. It has been published in the Journal of Functional Analysis. 3. The PI also applied the spherical harmonic analysis and cubature formula to the approximation theory of deep neural networks. 21207019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21207019.value: We shall enrich the understanding of qualitative and quantitative features of our research findings and enhance the interactions among the fields of approximation theory and learning theory. Precisely, we plan to apply our research findings further to solving more practical problems from geodesic science, remote sensing, and some other related domains to develop large-scale research programs and promote interactions among various subjects, including approximation theory, machine learning, data science, and function spaces.

21207119.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21207119.value: 利用片上超連續譜產生的中紅外光譜顯微鏡

21207119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21207119.value: This project aims to develop a mid-infrared spectroscopic microscope capable of improved biomolecular identification and three-dimensional structural imaging. This microscope will be able to recognize many important biomolecules including protein, lipid, nucleic acid and carbohydrate through the characteristic molecular fingerprint spectral absorption in the mid-infrared wavelengths ranging between 2µm and 15µm. The traditional spectroscopic microscope faces challenges for practical implementation because of the prohibitively expensive broadband mid-infrared light, while in contrast, this project will deliver a chalcogenide-glass-based single chip with an on-chip mid-infrared light, delivering low-cost, portable, mass-producible high quality broadband mid-infrared light source for spectroscopic microscope applications in physiology, biology and medicine. The on-chip mid-infrared light is sourced from the recent success of broadband mid-infrared supercontinuum generation via integrated highly nonlinear chalcogenide waveguide. The chalcogenide glasses are a family of glasses containing one or more chalcogen elements which are of highly nonlinearity, negligible nonlinear absorption and excellent mid-infrared transparency. This project aims to further optimize the on-chip chalcogenide waveguide via comprehensive material study and advanced nano-fabrication, tailoring the performance of the mid-infrared supercontinuum generation toward to the practical applications on critical properties including spectral coverage, output power, brightness, stability and coherence. This project will deliver a cost-effective spectroscopic microscope with enhanced detection and imaging capabilities. For the first time, this will make high quality spectroscopic imaging accessible to a broad range of researchers and medical clinicians. The success of this project will also pave the way towards miniaturized on-chip spectroscopic microscope for wearable medical diagnosis at biomolecular level. The project will position Hong Kong at the forefront of this emerging field, with significant commercialization opportunities. 該項目旨在開發一種便攜式光譜顯微鏡以進行改進生物分子識別和三維結構成像。這個顯微鏡將能夠識別許多重要的生物分子，包括蛋白質，脂質，核酸和碳水化合物通過特徵分子指紋吸收中紅外波長。傳統的光譜顯微鏡面臨著挑戰實際實施是因為寬帶中紅外線非常昂貴相比之下，這個項目將提供一個帶有片上中紅外的單芯片輕便，提供低成本，便攜式，可批量生產的光譜顯微鏡適用於生理學，生物學和醫學。這種寬帶中紅外線光是通過一系列非線性現象的組合產生的，所謂的“超連續譜”。該項目旨在為解決主要挑戰提供解決方案超連續譜用於實際實施，例如研究激光穩健材料和優化的錐形耦合器可將輸出功率提高一到兩倍數量級;開發單模波導和超短中紅外泵浦激光器通過消除穩定，重複，高相干超連續光多模和噪聲引起的不穩定性。除了所述的優點光譜能力，中紅外超連續光也是有益的三維結構顯微鏡在軸向方面的臨界性能分辨率和生物組織穿透深度，因為它的超短一致性長度和散射衰減分別較小。這個項目的成功將會提供小型化，便攜式，低成本，中紅外光譜顯微鏡作為新一代成像工具，可同時進行分子和結構分析成像，在生理學，生物學和醫學中有重要應用。結果該項目還將承諾超出本項目範圍的各種潛力，例如：有毒或非法物質檢測，包括毒藥，殺蟲劑和爆炸物對公共安全至關重要。

21208219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21208219.value: 到2022年，移動通信設備所使用的數據量將占全球互聯網總流量的63%。為了滿足不斷增長的移動數據帶寬需求，通信頻率必將繼續向更高頻率的毫米波段（30-300 GHz）轉變。這一尚未大規模開發的波段將為5G與后5G時代通信提供前所未有的數據帶寬和相比于當前網絡成倍提高的數據傳輸速率。 然而，傳統電子元器件在毫米波頻段增益顯著下降，導線損耗增加，因而不僅價格昂貴，而且效率較低、功率損耗大。近年來，微波光子學已經成為解決未來毫米波信號傳輸與處理的重要平台。利用成熟的光纖基礎設施網絡，微波信號能夠以極低的損耗進行長距離傳輸。然而，傳統光學系統體積較大、且帶寬往往限制于35 GHz左右，無法直接與毫米波系統集成。 本項目將通過研發新型集成光子學平台為未來小型化、低成本的毫米波系統提供解決方案。其中的核心元件是一個集成毫米波電光調製器，該器件能將頻率高達300 GHz的毫米波信號高效且不失真地轉換為光學信號。器件由亞微米級鈮酸鋰薄膜構成，能夠提供遠超傳統器件的光學束縛和電光調製效率。項目負責人致力於集成鈮酸鋰光子學器件的研發，此前已實現基於該平台的高速、低功耗電光調製器，可望應用於下一代長距離光纖通信和數據中心通信系統。為了將調製器帶寬進一步提升以覆蓋整個毫米波段，本項目將創新性地在同一芯片上共同設計集成鈮酸鋰光器件和毫米波傳輸線。除了調製器這一核心器件，本項目還將研發一系列先進的光學和毫米波元件，包括線性化調製器和集成化毫米波接受天線等。項目負責人將與有超過30年的微波工程經驗的項目合作者緊密合作，并依靠城市大學先進的毫米波與光子學基礎設施，以實現項目目標。 本項目的成功實施將構建一個完整的小型化毫米波光學系統，可望應用於5G通信、醫學成像、機器視覺和遙感等領域，并推動香港和世界範圍內的學術研究和產業發展。

21208219.label: Realisation of objectives
21208219.value: Objective 1: Develop reliable fabrication process of low-loss LN photonic devices (100%) We have successfully completed Objective 1 in the mid-term progress report by developing reliable device fabrication process of low-loss lithium-niobate (LN) photonic devices, all based on in-house facilities at CityU. Currently we are able to create LN photonic waveguides with propagation losses < 0.3 dB/cm and microring resonators with Q factors greater than 1 million, which are well enough to support the devices needed for the proposed millimeter-wave (MMW) modulators. These results have been summarized as an invited paper at Chinese Optics Letters [1] (Item 2 in Part C, Section 8) and also a conference paper at IEEE TENCON 2022 [2] (Item 5 in Part C, Section 9). Objective 2: Optimization of MMW transmission line for efficient MMW-optic modulation (100%) &Objective 3: Realization and testing of integrated MMW modulators (100%) Objective 2&3 aims to optimize the MMW transmission line for efficient MMW-optic modulation, as well as to fabricate and test the MMW-optic modulators. We have performed a systematic investigation of the mmWave-optic modulation performances of thin-film lithium niobate modulators through theoretical modeling, electrical verifications, and electro-optic measurements at frequencies up to 325 GHz. Based on our experimentally verified model, we demonstrate thin-film lithium niobate mmWave-optic modulators with a measured 3-dB electro-optic bandwidth of 170 GHz and a 6-dB bandwidth of 295 GHz. The device also shows a low RF half-wave voltage of 7.3 V measured at an ultrahigh modulation frequency of 250 GHz. These results have been summarized as a journal paper at Photonics Research [3] (Item 6 in Part C, Section 8). Objective 4: Design of integrated, linearized modulators (100%) We have performed not only a detailed theoretical investigation of integrated linearized modulators based on the LN platform, but also have validated the design through actual device fabrication and testing. We demonstrate a monolithic integrated LN modulator with an ultra-high spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 120.04 dB·Hz4/5 at 1 GHz, using a ring-assisted Mach–Zehnder interferometer configuration. The excellent synergy between the intrinsically linear electro-optic response of LN and an optimized linearization strategy allows us to fully suppress the cubic terms of third-order intermodulation distortions (IMD3) without active feedback controls, leading to ∼20 dB improvement over previous results in the thin-film LN platform. These results have been summarized as a journal paper at Photonics Research and selected as “Editor’s pick” [4] (Item 5 in Part C, Section 8). References: [1] K. Zhang, Z.X. Chen, H.K. Feng, W.H. 21208219.label: Major findings and research outcome
21208219.value: 1. We have developed reliable wafer-scale device fabrication process of low-loss lithium-niobate (LN) photonic devices, all based on in-house facilities at CityU, with waveguide propagation losses < 0.3 dB/cm and microring resonators with Q factors greater than 1 million (Item 2 in Part C, Section 8 and Item 5 in Part C, Section 9). 2. We have developed the first erbium (Er)-doped photonic waveguide amplifiers on the thin-film LN platform, with net internal gain > 10 dB/cm (Item 1 in Part C, Section 8). 3. We have developed the first demonstration of polarization rotator-splitter on the thin-film LN platform (Item 3 in Part C, Section 8). 4. We have demonstrated a systematic investigation of the mmWave-optic modulation performances of thin-film LN modulators at frequencies up to 325 GHz, and realized thin-film lithium niobate mmWave-optic modulators with a measured 3-dB electro-optic bandwidth of 170 GHz and a 6-dB bandwidth of 295 GHz. (Item 6 in Part C, Section 8). 5. We demonstrate a monolithic integrated LN modulator with an record-high spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 120.04 dB·Hz4/5 at 1 GHz, using a ring-assisted Mach–Zehnder interferometer configuration. (Item 5 in Part C, Section 8).

21208219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21208219.value: The wafer-scale device fabrication process, theoretical and experimental investigation of LN modulators at ultrahigh frequencies, as well as the design and engineering of linearized modulators developed in this project, have laid important foundation for the continuous development of LN photonics in PI’s team. The device design and experimental knowhow have been adopted in the development of new photonic devices and circuits in a variety of application fields, including electro-optic frequency combs (Comm. Phys. 6, 2023; Adv. Mater. 2308840, 2024) and microwave photonics (Nature 678, 2024). The further development of the research toward the realization of an integrated millimeter-wave photonic phased array receiver system is currently underway with the support of a GRF fund (CityU 11204022)

21208219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21208219.value: The ever-growing bandwidth requirement of wireless networks are calling for shifting the communication channel frequencies towards higher-frequency, millimeter-wave bands (30-300 GHz). This largely unexplored spectrum could provide unprecedented data bandwidths for 5G and beyond, allowing for data rates orders of magnitude higher than current networks. In recent years, photonic approaches have emerged as a promising candidate for future millimeter-wave signal transmission and processing units because of the intrinsic low-loss nature of light and the availability of the mature telecommunication infrastructure. In this project, we have developed an integrated lithium niobate photonic-millimeter-wave platform that is ideally suited for future compact, low-cost millimeter-wave systems. We have developed an integrated millimeter-wave modulator that can efficiently convert millimeter-wave signals up to 300 GHz into optical domain, as well as a highly linear electro-optic modulator that could perform faithful conversion of analog signals into optics. We have also developed a wafer-scale fabrication technology that has substantially improved the cost-effectiveness and scalability of the integrated lithium niobate photonic platform. The successful accomplishment of this project has created an ultra-compact and high-performance MMW package that could enable a range of applications including 5G communications, medical imaging, machine vision and remote sensing.

21209119.label: Project Objectives
21209119.value: To design a uniform network structure applied to various single-restoration tasks, including denoising, deblurring, dehazing, inpainting, colorization, etc. This network structure, inspired by two fundamentals of signal analysis (residual and progressive), would unify the formulation and provide a better understanding of image restoration from the machine learning perspective. To develop the first network supporting training multiple image-restoration tasks with a single model by representing each task with a plugin to our uniform network backbone. Through this, different tasks can benefit from each other by joint training, and new tasks can be efficiently added by incremental training. To develop the first network that can restore images with mixed and unknown defects by learning the combination of pretrained basic tasks in an unsupervised manner. This can be applied in industries to solve complicated real-world restoration problems. To incorporate the above objectives into a practical system and make it user friendly and robust by adding two more functions. The first one is to support customizable restoration results by integrating exemplar guidance into our networks. The second one is the video extension by considering the temporal information and constraints.
