21209119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21209119.value: Image restoration is a classical but still active research topic in computer vision and image processing because it is fundamental to many applications such as photography, surveillance, and medical imaging. Image restoration is also a challenging ill-posed problem due to the information loss during the corruption procedure. Traditional methods define some priors to tackle each subproblem including denoising, deblurring, super resolution, inpainting, and colorization. Recently, with the success of deep learning, many different neural networks have been proposed to solve restoration tasks by utilizing large-scale training data. These networks are still designed for one specific task with a known corruption model. However, real-world corrupted images or videos, such as old photographs, historic artworks, or vintage movies, often simultaneously suffer from multiple artifacts caused by unknown and mixed corruption functions, which cannot be successfully restored using existing single-task methods. Therefore, we propose novel techniques for automatically restoring images from unknown and mixed defects and then extend them to videos. To achieve this, we have several targets. The first one is to design a uniform deep neural network structure that can be applied to different single-restoration tasks. This network is constructed by a pyramid of subnetworks with residual blocks, which progressively recover the target image residue in a coarse-to-fine way to get better quality. Our second target is to make this uniform network support joint training of multiple restoration tasks with one model; thus, different tasks can benefit from each other. This is realized by representing each task with a filter bank plugged into the shared uniform network structure. With the above two basics, our central target to restore images suffering from unknown and mixed real-world corruptions can be achieved by learning the combination of pretrained basic restoration tasks represented by filter banks in our network in an unsupervised manner. Moreover, we plan to add exemplar guidance into our networks, which enables simply feeding different references to customize results; and extend our method from image to video by imposing temporal constraints to generate temporally coherent results. The project is built on our previous works on deep-learning-based image/video processing and generation. Our preliminary experiments have already demonstrated both the feasibility and the quality of some building blocks in the proposed methodologies. Our proposal is the first attempt to tackle multiple, mixed, and unknown corruptions in images and videos, which will bring the state-of-the-art restoration techniques to the next level in solving real-world problems. 图像修复，作爲许多应用（包括摄影，监控和医学圖像等）的基础，是计算机视觉和图像处理中经典但仍然活跃的研究课题。圖像修復也是一個具有挑戰性的病態問題，因爲它要求恢復圖像在損壞過程已經丟失的很多信息。傳統方法通過定義一些先驗來解決單個問題，比如去噪，去模糊，超分辨率，缺失修補，上色等。近年來，隨著深度學習的成功，研究者提出了利用大規模數據集訓練深度神經網路的方法來解決圖像修復的問題。雖然多種不同的結構的圖像修復網絡相繼被提出，但它們仍然只針對具有已知損壞模型的特定單任務而設計。然而現實世界中損壞的圖像或視頻（如舊照片、歷史作品或老電影）通常同時受到未知和複合的損壞模型作用，產生多種瑕疵混合的效果，這些瑕疵無法使用現有的單任務方法所修復。鑒於此，我們提出從未知和混合瑕疵中自動修復圖像的方法，然後將此技術擴展到視頻中。 為了實現這一設想，我們有以下幾個目標。首先，我們設計一個統一的深度神經網路結構。它可應用於不同的單瑕疵的圖像修復任務。該網路由具有residual block的子網金字塔構建，以粗到細的方式逐步回歸目標圖像和輸入圖像的殘差，以獲得更好的修復質量。我們的第二個目標是使這種統一的網路支持聯合訓練多個圖像修復任務，從而不同的任務可以相互受益。每個任務由一組篩選器表示，再以插件的方式插入到共用的骨架網絡中來實現對應的任務。基於以上兩個目標的實現，我們可以通過訓練代表不同任務的篩選器的組合方式來修復真實世界中圖像的未知和複合的瑕疵。此外，我們計畫在我們的網路中添加範例指導，這樣用戶只需提供不同的參考圖像即可自定義修復結果;並且通過添加時間約束將我們的方法從圖像擴展到視頻。 該研究計劃基於我們以前在深度學習和圖像/視頻處理方面的工作。我們的初步實驗已經證明了研究計劃中一些構建基塊的可行性和品質。該研究計劃是首次嘗試解決圖像和視頻中的多重、混合和未知的瑕疵，這將使得圖像和視頻的修復技術在解決實際問題方面上升一個新臺階。

21209119.label: Realisation of objectives
21209119.value: All four major objectives have been fully achieved. Below, we list the realization of each objective. 1 Design a uniform network structure applied to various single-restoration tasks. For this objective, we propose an end-to-end gated context aggregation CNN that is generic for both deraining and dehazing tasks (output 9.4). In this network, we adopt the smoothed dilation technique to help remove the gridding artifacts caused by widely-used dilated convolution, with negligible extra parameters. We leverage a gated sub-network to fuse the features from different levels. We further improve the uniform image restoration network structure by considering two characteristics in image restoration: spatial variability and spatial correlation. Spatial variability indicates that the details of different areas of degraded images are distinct and should be recovered differently, while spatial correlation refers to the contextual awareness required for restoring local regions. By incorporating these ideas into the network design, we improve the uniform network structure and apply it to solve more image restoration tasks, including desmooth (output 9.1), inpainting (output 9.8, 9.10), JPEG compression restoration (output 8.13), and document rectification (output 8.2). 2 Develop the first network supporting training multiple image-restoration tasks with a single model. For this objective, we propose a new plugin module, the "Adaptive Filterbank Pyramid" (output 8.1), that can support multiple image restoration tasks and continuous parameter tuning when inserted into a backbone network. Our module represents one restoration task with one filterbank pyramid, and the weights of the filterbank pyramid are directly regressed by another sub-network for continuous parameter tuning. We applied the proposed module to a variety of image processing tasks, including smoothing, denoising, deblocking, enhancement, and neural style transfer, and experiments show that our method is generalized to different types of image processing tasks and different backbone network structures. Comparable to the per task model, our is significantly more efficient in both training and testing. 3 Developed the first network that can restore images with mixed and unknown defects. For this objective, we propose restoring old photos that suffer from mixed and unknown defects through a deep learning approach (output 8.22 & 9.2). Unlike conventional restoration tasks that can be solved through supervised learning, the degradation in real photos is complex, and the domain gap between synthetic images and real old photos makes the network fail to generalize. To address this, we use an unsupervised approach that trains two variational autoencoders to transform old and clean photos into two respective latent spaces and translate between them using synthetic paired data. We address multiple degradations using a global branch for structured defects and a local branch for unstructured defects, which are fused in the latent space for improved restoration capability. Our proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods in restoring old photos. 4 To incorporate the above objectives into a practical system and make it user friendly and robust. 4.1 Integrate exemplar guidance into restoration to support customizable restoration results. All image restoration tasks can be summarized as image-to-image translation, which involves the translation from degraded images into clean images. Therefore, we first explored some image-to-image (I2I) translation networks (output 8.3, 8.8, 8.9, 8.11, 8.14) as the basis for customizable restoration. We provide solutions to control the I2I translation network output based on semantically matched reference images. When applied to image restoration, we take a clean exemplar and a degraded input as input and perform semantic matching (output 8.7) between them, allowing the network to explicitly learn information from the exemplar for controlling restoration outcomes. We have successfully applied exemplar-based image-to-image translation networks to multiple image tasks domains, such as colorization (output 8.3), style restoration (output 8.6), and sketch restoration (output 8.16). 4.2 Extend restoration methods from images to videos. We have extended our restoration methods from the images to the videos by incorporating temporal information and constraints. First, we extended our method to remove contaminant artifacts for moving cameras (output 9.6), including dust, dirt, and moisture adhering to the camera lens, which can greatly affect the quality and clarity of the video. Our approach first detects attention maps indicating the regions to restore, hallucinate background flow to degraded attention regions, and restore frames using a recurrent technique and adjacent clean frames. Finally, a multi-frame processing stage is used to further process the entire video sequence to enforce temporal consistency. We have also extended our old photo restoration method to restore old films (output 9.13). We present a recurrent transformer network to restore heavily degraded old films. Instead of performing frame-by-frame restoration, our method is based on the hidden knowledge learned from adjacent frames that is beneficial for restoring challenging artifacts of each frame while ensuring temporal coherence. In addition, the same framework can effectively propagate the color from keyframes to the entire video, resulting in compelling restored films. 4.3 Extend restoration methods from images to 3D. We have extended our restoration methods from the image domain to the 3D domain by incorporating 3D constraints. Due to inevitable noise introduced during scanning and quantization, 3D reconstruction via RGB-D sensors suffers from errors in geometry and texture, resulting in artifacts such as camera drifting, mesh distortion, texture ghosting, and blurriness. To restore 3D models, we bridge the 3D and 2D space with a differentiable renderer. This allows us to apply our restoration methods on the rendered multi-view images, and the loss can be backpropagated to 3D models to restore the 3D model. We have leveraged this approach to restore both explicit mesh (output 8.21) & multiplane models (output 8.14), and implicit NeRF models (output 8.12).

21209119.label: Major findings and research outcome
21209119.value: In this project, we made the following major findings and research outcomes: 1 A uniformed CNN network with supervised learning can be designed for various single-restoration tasks, including deraining, denoising, deblurring, dehazing, desmooth, decompression, colorization, etc., as many image degradations share similar formulation. 2 Our designed plugin module, called "Adaptive Filterbank Pyramid" (output 8.1), supports multiple image restoration tasks within a single model by inserting it into the backbone network. Each restoration task can then be represented with one filterbank pyramid, and the weights are directly regressed by another sub-network for continuous parameter tuning. Training multiple image-restoration tasks with a single model using this plugin module is significantly more efficient compared to using a per task model. 3 We found that in real-world cases, such as old photos, image restoration is more complicated due to mixed and unknown defects. To address this problem, directly training a network with synthesized paired data may not be effective as the domain gap between synthetic images and real photos can cause the network to fail to generalize. Instead, we found that learning domain translation in the latent domain, rather than the pixel domain, is more generalizable and can alleviate this problem. 4 When extending image restoration to video and 3D, it is important to incorporate temporal and 3D consistency into the network design. Differentiable rendering can be a useful tool for imposing 3D constraints on images, while temporal attention is an effective approach for exploiting temporal coherence. 5 The restoration results can be diverse, and using exemplar guidance is an effective way to control the restoration outcome. The key is to establish correspondence between a high-quality exemplar and the low-quality image to be restored. To address this issue, we have proposed semantic matching methods that utilize deep learning features. The project has led to 22 journal publications in total, including papers published in top-venues in the field, such as IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, IEEE Transactions on Image Processing, IEEE Transactions on Multimedia, IEEE Transactions on Graphics and Visualization, ACM Transaction on Graphics, etc.

21209119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21209119.value: When extending image restoration to 3D, we found that the neural radiance field (NeRF) is the most suitable 3D representation due to its natural differentiability and compatibility with images, as it can be viewed as a multi-view image with continuous camera poses. Therefore, many existing image restoration methods can be extended to NeRF. Additionally, as NeRF has 3D information, many restoration tasks requiring 3D awareness, such as low light restoration, motion blur, or camera blur restoration, can benefit from it. We have successfully extended image deblur to NeRF deblur. In the future, we can further explore this direction, as NeRF reconstructed from images may also suffer from many degradations. Moreover, most image restoration methods are still trained in a supervised manner using synthesized paired data (before and after degradation). However, there is always a gap between synthesized data and real data, which limits their practical usage. In the future, we would like to explore unsupervised restoration methods to eliminate the need for data synthesis. The idea is to leverage the priors learned by pre-trained large-scale image models, such as transformer-based models like Dall-E and NUWA, or diffusion-based models like Imagen and Stable Diffusion.

21209119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21209119.value: This project provides methods for image, video, and 3D restoration to improve the quality of digital media. When digital media is captured, it can often suffer from various types of degradation, such as blurring, noise, or missing information. Our techniques aim to correct these issues and restore the media to its best possible quality. For example, image restoration can remove unwanted artifacts, such as scratches or dust, from photographs. Video restoration can reduce the noise and blur in footage, making it look clearer and smoother. 3D restoration can repair missing or distorted parts of 3D models, making them more accurate and lifelike. The significance of this research is that it can greatly enhance the quality of digital media, making it more visually appealing and informative. This can have important applications in fields such as medicine, where high-quality images and videos are essential for accurate diagnosis and treatment. It can also be used in the film and television industry to restore old footage or improve the overall visual quality of a production, leading to better audience engagement and critical acclaim.

21209419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21209419.value: Voice-based User Interfaces (VUI) have advanced rapidly with the recent development of Natural Language Processing (NLP). Using speech input allows users to write messages, memos or draft documents without occupying their hands typing and their eyes looking at a screen. It is particularly useful in situations where typing is not practical, or possibly due to impairment, or when written drafts need to be quickly generated. Current research on commercial VUI platforms, e.g., Alexa and Siri, focuses on understanding users’ intention and generating “smart” or human-like responses. There is also much work on improving speech recognition rate by analyzing people’s speech patterns, such as speech repair to address people’s natural stammers, repetitions and addition of filler words (eg., “em”, “ah”) [21, 20]. Existing dictation systems, such as Dragon and Google Doc Voice Typing, mainly transcribe users’ speech, then provide limited support for modifying the dictated text with the same modality. Moreover, existing work provides even less support for drafting a document such as structuring the spoken content and help ideation. In fact, generating textual content with speech is inherently different from typing [4]. To better design and implement future systems, we need an in-depth understanding of users’ natural behavior, expectation and responses while interacting with a voice-based system for this task. This is under-investigated in the existing literature. To fill this gaps, this project will investigate how to support users to generate textual content with speech, including tasks from composing, editing, structuring to ideating. We will invent and prototype new interaction techniques based on a conversational interface that enable users to generate and revise text with voice input and reduced visual engagement. For longer text, the interface can scaffold users’ speech for generating content with better structure and quality. What are the important design factors for these features that affect user experiences in terms of easiness to use, effectiveness and intrusiveness of the support? We will answer this question with user-centered iterative design and evaluation methods. In response to our preliminary studies of users’ natural behavior when performing writing tasks with speech, we will first develop prototypes of interaction techniques to support identified user strategies, and then evaluate their user experiences and performances with controlled user studies. The findings from this project will positively benefit the design and implementation of future commercial dictation systems and voice interfaces, and answer questions about how to better support the co-creation with machine intelligence. 随着语音识别技术的发展，语音界面在用户体验方面进展迅速，也有越来越多的应用。 用户可以不依赖屏幕和键盘来写信息，记笔记或是打草稿，方便在移动的或户外的场景中进行。此外，它对盲人的信息输入也有重大意义。现有的对语音界面的研究，例如Alexa和Siri, 主要致力于理解用户的意图和给出更拟人的回答。语音识别方面的研究致力于分析语音来提高识别率，比如如何过滤掉用户迟疑或停顿时的发音。而现有的听写系统主要是把用户的语音转变为文本，很少支持对这些口述内容的语音编辑，对语音文本创作的帮助较少。 已经有研究发现，用语音撰写文本和传统打字有根本性的区别，但对其用户行为的分析还有待加强。我们需要更深入的了解用户用语音界面来撰写文本时的行为，预期和反应，才能设计出更有效的界面。此项目针对这个问题展开，研究如何帮助用户用语音撰写文本，包括输入，编辑，以及创作和对文本结构的整理。 我们会采用以用户为中心的设计方法来设计新的交互方式，做出智能语音界面的系统原型，并通过用户实验来测试和选拔更优良的用户体验。研究成果将对未来的语音输入系统有指导意义，也会对如何更好的支持人与智能界面的合作给出一些答案。

21209419.label: Realisation of objectives
21209419.value: We realized 3 out of 4 project objectives. Objective 3 was not realized because we realized there were other more important problems to solve. Initially we thought auditory system feedback would be important for the speech-based text composition system because we attempted an eyes-free approach. As we continued the investigation, we realized eyes-free text composition via speech is challenging and is not required by the majority of our target user groups. Therefore we decided to design and develop graphical user interfaces instead, and conducted more research about the nature of speech input modality to inform how to build such interfaces that cater to the characteristics of speech-based text composition.

21209419.label: Major findings and research outcome
21209419.value: The goal of the research was to develop effective interfaces to support speech-based text composition and editing. We first developed Re-Dictation, a natural language method for text editing that allowing users to modify text by respeaking part of the text. The system automatically aligns the respoken text with the original text and identify editing operations, which include add, delete and replace. We evaluated this technique by comparing it against standard voice commands, found that it benefits especially compound editing operations, while voice commands are effective for simple operations such as deletion. Therefore we developed a system called VoiceRev, which incorporate both techniques without mode-switching. These research outcome is published in a ToCHI journal [1]. The Re-Dictation technique was also used in our related work EyEditor from the same collaborators with my participation as a co-author. The second phase of the research further explored how to support speech-based text composition, not only editing or words correction. We found that composition and editing are integrated tasks, hard to be separated when using speech as input. This led to a realization that speaking is fundamentally different from typing as an input modality - we need better understanding of its characteristics in order to develop effective interfaces. Multiple works were conducted to deepen our understanding about speech. First is Typist Experiment [2], a role-play experiment observing how one person writes long-form text by dictating to another person. This work generated a rich set of understanding that informs the design of future intelligent dictation interfaces. In addition, another outcome we had in exploring the design of intelligent interface is a collaboration platform [4] for helping researchers conduct wizard-of-oz studies. The second work in understanding speech surveys and summarizes literature in cognitive science and linguistics with the goal of identifying fundamental differences between speaking and writing. We found how speech is more spontaneous and leaves weaker verbatim memory than typing. Informed by both studies, we developed Rambler [6] and 1D Touch [5], supporting users to interact with text more at the gist-level. Rambler bridges the gap between speaking and writing by leveraging LLMs to smooth the raw transcript from speech and allowing users to easily merge, split and transform text for iteratively revising spoken text. 1D Touch injects NLP into a text selection text, supporting users to select text by chunks based on its semantic meanings.

21209419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21209419.value: Future research will continue developing gist-based interfaces that support the review and interaction with text by leveraging AI. We will also conduct diary study to further iterate and develop the Rambler dictation interface to cater to different user groups' writing needs.

21209419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21209419.value: This research advances speech-to-text interfaces for text composition. We developed ways for users to edit text via natural speech, such as by respeaking part of the text. For long-form text composition, we created new dictation interfaces that leverage AI to assist users to process the transcripts of their speech, which may involve disfluencies, errors and disorganization. Our solutions were shown to be effective and preferred by users compared to existing methods. Overall we mitigate some of the bottlenecks in user experiences when using dictation, in particular the difficulty of editing transcripts. As Speech Recognition accuracy continues to improve, we will see dictation become more widely adopted, improving users' input experience and productivity on mobile devices.

21210619.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21210619.value: 多種激勵環境下壓電能量採集技術

21210619.label: Project Objectives
21210619.value: To improve power output by developing new kinetic energy harvesters where energy associated with both periodic vibrations and strong shocks is harnessed. We will exploit the piezoelectric compressive mode, flexural force amplification mechanisms and impact methods to improve harvester performance as well as ensure a satisfactory reliability under strong excitations. To extend the operational bandwidth by exploiting nonlinear vibrations via geometric and magnetic nonlinearities and comprehend the interaction relationship between different nonlinear effects. The magnetic nonlinearity will be further explored to compensate the strong centrifugal force within high-speed rotations. To elucidate the stiffness and geometry effects of different layers of piezoelectric composites and develop high-efficiency piezoelectric composites for strain energy harvesting. Strategies also need to be developed to protect piezoelectric composites from overload and fatigue. To optimize the nonlinear effects and system parameters, and to demonstrate the ideas by implementing the developed hybrid harvesters within tires and achieving self-powered operation of tire sensors.

21210619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21210619.value: Energy harvesting is a promising renewable and long-lifespan power solution alternative to batteries for wireless devices. It has attracted much attention along with the booming of wearable devices and sensor networks. However, most existing harvesters cannot meet the power requirements from potential applications, owing to their low power-generation capability and poor environmental adaptability with narrow operational bandwidth. More seriously, most previous research is conducted in ideal laboratory environments with a single form of regular excitation, e.g., translational harmonic vibration. In contrast, the excitation sources in the real environment such as rolling tires and body motions are deformable and irregular. Usually combinations of various forms of excitations such as periodic vibrations, abrupt strong shocks and deformation exist simultaneously in the excitation bases, of which harsh environment can cause serious damage and performance deterioration. We believe it is very important to develop harvesters with the capability of working efficiently not only under one type of regular excitation, but also under the realistic multiple irregular excitations. This project is therefore aimed at exploring new methods for achieving high power-output and broad bandwidth for energy harvesting in environments where deformation, periodic vibration and shocks coexist. Based on our extensive research, we herein propose to develop a versatile vibration-impact-strain hybrid energy harvesting solution. Different from the existing research, both moderate periodic vibrations and strong abrupt acceleration changes will be captured via the unique compressive mode, force amplification mechanisms and the impact energy harvesting method to improve power output. Furthermore, highly-reliable multilayer piezoelectric composites will be developed to effectively harness strain energy associated with deformable excitation bases. To extend the operational bandwidth, geometric nonlinearity and magnetic nonlinearity will be introduced to energy harvesters and their interaction will be fully analyzed. Comprehensive theoretical analysis and systematic experiments will be performed to gain in-depth understanding of the effects of different parameters and nonlinear characteristics under different excitations, which provides guidelines for improving energy harvesting performances. For demonstration, we will at the end develop a self-powered tire condition monitoring system using the proposed harvesters and test it in running vehicles. To our best knowledge, this is the first research that combines kinetic and strain energy harvesting methods working with complex excitations. The new methods and knowledge generated from this project will greatly advance the research field of energy harvesting, nonlinear vibration and wireless sensors, which with no doubt will further promote the development of self-powered wireless devices significantly. 能量採集是替代無線設備中的電池實現長時間穩定電力供應的新興可再生能源技術。伴隨者可穿戴設備和物聯網的發展，能量採集技術吸引了越來越多的目光。然而，現有能量採集器不能夠滿足大部分潛在應用的用電需求，由於他們低下的能量輸出能力和極小的頻帶寬度。更為嚴重的是，能量採集器只能在實驗室理想單方向正弦激勵下工作。而環境中的激勵源如汽車輪胎，激勵包括振動和轉動而且有變形發生，現有能量採集器不能夠在這種複雜的實際環境中生存。 這個項目就是為了探索新方法實現在多種激勵環境下高能量輸出和寬頻帶能量採集。基於我們大量的前期研究，我們提出開發一種振動-衝擊-應變復合能量採集方式。現有技術相比，我們提出的方案將能夠同時俘獲強度適中的簡諧運動和高強度的衝擊能量。同時我們將採用多級力放大原理和多層壓電堆棧結構，提高能量輸出。為了擴展工作頻帶，我們將引入結構非線性和磁場非線性到系統中，通過振動分線性響應有效擴展頻寬，提高其環境適應性。我們將開展深入的理論分析和系統的實驗。為了展示，最後我們將開發一個基於此能力採集器的自供電車胎狀態監測系統，實現自發電、無線運行。這一項目的開展將極大的促進能量採集技術的發展，推動其走出實驗室，造福社會。

21210619.label: Realisation of objectives
21210619.value: Overall, this ECS project is to develop a new energy harvester that can harvest energy from different excitation sources and develop mathematical models for supporting the development of high-performance nonlinear vibration energy harvesters. Finite element methods and analytical methods were used to build theoretical models for analyzing the nonlinear electromechanical coupling energy harvesting systems. Harvester prototypes were fabricated, and systemically tested and optimized under multiple types of input excitations. The effect of geometric and material parameters on the harvester performance has been investigated theoretically and experimentally. All 4 designated objectives have been achieved. Technical details are disclosed in the attached published papers.

21211619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21211619.value: Mm-wave antennas are beginning to find marketplace applications in cutting-edge technological systems. The worldwide deployment of the 5G communications standard induces great need for mm-wave antennas both in cellular phones and in base stations. The smart car initiative requires high-performance radar sensing systems built from highly directive and steerable mm-wave antennas or antenna arrays. The proliferation of the Internet of Things greatly increases the need for small, lightweight and cost-effective antennas, which can be used on various wirelessly connected, mobile and/or wearable devices. Next generation mm-wave antennas can greatly benefit the aforementioned fields and many others. To a degree, the design of mm-wave antenna systems can be facilitated by upscaling established antenna system designs from lower frequencies. However, one faces challenges such as more stringent fabrication requirements and different material responses (in particular an increase in material loss) at higher frequencies. Traditional phased array antenna systems – which find great use in high-directivity and long distance communications – become expensive when they are scaled to mm-wave frequencies, because of the expansive cost for phase shifters at high frequencies, and because a very large number of phase shifters are needed for a mm-wave phased array. To alleviate many of the aforementioned difficulties, we propose to conduct research towards the design of mm-wave antenna systems enabled by passive and active metasurfaces. Recent works on the metasurface have demonstrated its merit as a highly flexible electromagnetic wave manipulation surface. Specifically, it can be lightweight, cost effective, and yet can be used to facilitated many antenna-related functions, like beam collimation, scanning, focusing and radiation to extreme angles. While the theoretical groundwork is largely laid, most prior works on metasurfaces have been at the microwave (low GHz) and optical frequencies, leaving the mm-wave regime, with its unique challenges and opportunities, relatively unexplored. In this regard, a recent work by the PI showed that an active metasurface can be tuned to generate an arbitrary waveform within an enclosed region of space. Preliminary results show that a minor modification can turn this device into a travelling-wave antenna which boasts a large beam steering range and a dramatic reduction in the amount of tuning elements required. The PIs’ expertise in metasurface and antenna design and the advanced fabrication and characterization facilities at the State Key Laboratory of Terahertz and Millimeter Waves at the City University of Hong Kong make this team uniquely positioned to succeed in the proposed research. 毫米波天線已開始在尖端技術系統中找到實質的市場應用。全球正在部署推出5G通信標準；這些項目中，無綫電話和基站中都非常需要毫米波天線。智能汽車的體現與普及也需要建立高性能的雷達傳感系統與及高度指向和可操縱的毫米波天線或天線陣列。物聯網的建立也大大增加了對新一代天綫的需求：這些天綫需是小巧輕便且具有成本效益，以便用於各種無線連接，移動和/或可穿戴設備。下一代毫米波天線具有極大潛力，能滿足上述領域和許多其他領域的需求。 在某種程度上，我們可以通過縮小較低頻率的天線系統來設計比較高頻的毫米波天線系統。然而，我們會面對一些挑戰，諸如更嚴格的製造要求，和電板材料在較高頻率下的響應（特別是電磁波損失的增加）。傳統相控陣天線系統在高方向性和長距離通信方面有很大的用途，但當它們縮放到毫米波時便變得昂貴，因為（i）高頻移相器的成本很高，（ii）毫米波相控陣需要非常多的移相器。為了緩解上述許多困難，我們建議研究如何設計由無源與有源超結構表面促成的毫米波天線系統。 最近關於超結構表面的研究已經證明其作為高度靈活的電磁波操縱表面的優點。具體而言，它可以是輕便的，高成本效益的，並且還可以用於促進許多與天線相關的功能，例如光束准直，掃描，聚焦和到極端角度的輻射。雖然理論基礎工作基本上已經奠定，但大多數先前關於超結構表面的工作一直處於微波（較低頻率）和光學頻率（極高頻率），使毫米波狀態具有其獨特的挑戰和機遇，相對未開發。在這方面，項目負責人最近的工作證明，通過調整有源結構表面，我們可以在封閉的空間區域內產生任意電磁波形。初步結果顯示，對上述裝置稍作修改即可製成行波天線，其具有大的波束轉向範圍並且所需的調諧元件的數量顯著減少。項目負責人在超結構表面和天線設計方面的專業知識，和其所屬香港城市大學的太赫茲和毫米波國家重點實驗室的先進製造和測量設施，為該團隊立在穩固的基礎上，能成功實現上述提議的研究項目。

21211619.label: Realisation of objectives
21211619.value: All of the revised objectives have been addressed. The following describes the achievement of each objective in order. Objective 1: The discretized Huygens’ metasurface was investigated and demonstrated as a way to construct efficient, wideband and wide-angle passive metasurfaces. Metasurfaces were designed which (i) performed anomalous reflection and transmission of electromagnetic waves, (ii) scattered the incoming wave and achieved significant RCS reduction, (iii) performed lensing/focusing of an incident plane wave and (iv) mimicked curved reflectors within a resonator antenna. Objective 2: We performed investigations on the active metasurface, where an RF wave drives current sources, in parallel or series formation, to achieve the desired surface currents leading to directive radiation. The active metasurface excites the Huygens’ box. The Huygens’ box concept was furthered developed into the Huygens’ box antenna, where a controlled wave emanates from a rectangular (or cylindrical) cavity as highly-directive radiation. The TEM HBA and the TM1 HBA were both demonstrated. One features a TEM cavity mode while the other features a TM1 cavity mode. Objective 3: For both the TEM HBA and the TM1 HBA, beam scanning in the azimuthal direction was demonstrated in simulation. For the TEM HBA scanning was also demonstrated in the elevation direction, as a function of the frequency and as a function of the effective refractive index inside the cavity. Objective 4: The construction and testing was done for the aforementioned metasurfaces, including (i) the anomalous reflection and transmission metasurfaces, (ii) the RCS reduction metasurface, (iii) chromatic and achromatic metalenses, (iv) the mimicked curved reflectors within a resonator cavity antenna, (v) the TEM Huygens’ box antenna. Discussion on Slight Underachievement While all objectives are addressed to a reasonable degree, parts of the project involving active metasurfaces and antennas have progressed slower than expected. The main reason was experimental complications due to the interoperability of a multitude of experimental parts. Notwithstanding this slight impediment we have successfully achieved experimental verification on all aspects of the objectives. However, the slow-down has affected our speed in disseminating full results on a small portion of our experimental works. We expect to have two more papers submitted for publication by Q2 of 2024, on our remaining works on active metasurface antennas arising from this project. Summary of Notable Works A. Anomalous Reflection and Transmission and Metalenses using Discretized Huygens’ Metasurfaces (Aligns with Objectives 1 and 4) We studied what happens when we intentionally discretize a metasurface aggressively, using unit cells with much larger sizes than conventionally reported in the literature. This is like forming an image with large pixels instead of fine pixels. We show that surprisingly, in some situations, aggressive discretization can actually improve the metasurface in terms of power efficiency, operation bandwidth and angular width. It can also relax the required tolerance size, opening the path to reliable metasurface operation at higher frequencies. A representative work is Paper #3 in Part C: Research Output, published in the IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation. In this work, we demonstrated a metasurface capable of bending a wave to an abnormal direction from input angles of {-45°,0°,45°} to output angles of {0°,45°,-45°}, respectively. For all three operation cases, a power efficiency above 80% was achieved over a bandwidth exceeding 10%. The relaxation of tolerance reported from the previous investigation was employed to demonstrate that one can make a Terahertz metasurface using conventional PCB fabrication technology. To this effect, we designed, simulated and fabricated two Terahertz metalenses which operated from 240 – 400 GHz. Both single-polarized and dual-polarized lenses have been fabricated and tested. The lenses’ numerical aperture of NA = 0.86 surpasses most lenses at this frequency range; near-diffraction-limited focal spots with sidelobes below 10dB were achieved. Being able to fabricate Terahertz metasurfaces (at around 300 GHz) from PCB technology represents a breakthrough that can dramatically reduce the deployment time and cost of such surfaces. The work, cited in Part C, Paper #5, is recently published online by Advanced Optical Materials and will be featured on the inside cover of its publication issue. B. Metasurface-Enabled Wideband RCAs (Aligns with Objectives 1 and 4) We also study how passive metasurfaces can serve as an enabling technology for microwave and millimeter wave antennas. In this regard, we investigated the usage of a true-time-delay metasurface to replace a curved mirror inside a cavity resonator antenna (RCA). Using filter technology, we design the metasurface to replicate the reflection phases of the curved plate over a wide frequency range of 25%, then we use it to replace a curved mirror inside a sub-wavelength cavity, allowing the wave to resonate and emanate from the said cavity. In doing so, we flatten the RCA, reduce its vertical profile and dramatically simplify its construction. Simulation and experiment show that the performance of the metasurface antenna approaches that of the original antenna with the curved metallic plate. This research, cited as Part C, Paper #6, is now published online by the IEEE Open Journal of Antennas and Propagation. C. Active Huygens’ Metasurfaces (Aligns with Objectives 2 and 4) We propose that active metasurfaces, which excite electric and magnetic currents across a boundary, can be synthesized to generate an electromagnetic field in free space with great flexibility. Accordingly, we investigated how to design such a metasurface with efficient feeding based on an iterative impedance matching design using the architecture of a sub-wavelength spaced serially-fed patch array. We show that wide-angle propagation beams (from -70° to 70°) can be achieved. Our results have been verified in experiment; a journal paper is under preparation on this topic. D. Huygens’ Boxes and Huygens’ Box Antennas (Aligns with Objectives 2, 3 4) By enclosing a region with an active Huygens’ metasurface, we show that one can invoke electromagnetic equivalence theory to generate an electromagnetic waveform inside the region with near arbitrary flexibility. We name this concept the Huygens’ box. Accordingly, we perform simulation and experiment to show the ability of this box to (i) synthesize arbitrary travelling waves in a metal box, (ii) generate a sub-diffraction focus from propagating waves, and (iii) Perform cloaking (hiding an object inside the box) and mimicking (making the object inside the box look like something else to observers outside the box). This work was published by the IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation and cited as Part C, Paper #7. We also propose and demonstrate that, by opening perforations on this box, one can obtain a leakage of radiation forming highly directive antenna. We call this the Huygens’ box antenna (HBA). An important advantage of the antenna is that it achieves near-unity aperture efficiency while the tunable elements reside only at the perimeter (not the area) of the aperture. This will represent a dramatic reduction in the number of active elements for high directivity antennas. Two types of HBA’s were proposed in a paper published in the IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters (Part C, Paper #1). One type was experimentally demonstrated. Preliminary results were disseminated in Part C, Conference paper #12. Full experimental results have since been obtained, and the journal paper is currently under preparation.

21211619.value: Major findings our outlined below, and explained in more detail in the "Realisation of Objectives" section above. A. Anomalous Reflection and Anomalous Transmission and Metalenses using Discretized Huygens’ Metasurfaces We exploit discretization to demonstrate metasurfaces that are simultaneously robust, power-efficient, broadband and wide-angle in operation. Prime example works include: A1. An anomalous transmission metasurface capable of bending a wave from input angles of {-45°,0°,45°} to anomalous output angles of {0°,45°,-45°}, respectively. For all three operation cases, a power efficiency above 80% was achieved over a bandwidth exceeding 10% (Part C, Paper #3). A2. A Terahertz metalens made from PCB technology. The metalens features a numerical aperture of 0.86 and near-diffraction-limited focal property. Being able to fabricate Terahertz metasurfaces (at around 300 GHz) from PCB technology represents a breakthrough that can dramatically reduce the deployment time and cost of such surfaces. (Part C, Paper #5). B. Metasurface-Enabled Wideband RCAs Using a true-time-delay metasurface (TTD-MS) to replace a curved metallic ground plane in a resonator cavity antenna (RCA), we flatten the RCA, reduce its vertical profile and dramatically simplify its construction. Our design achieves an overall gain of more than 15dB over a bandwidth of more than 20%, closely matching the original RCA with the curved reflector. (Part C, Paper #6) C. Active Huygens’ Metasurfaces We implemented a metasurface which generates driven effective electric and magnetic surfaces currents of an arbitrary profile, upon proper side-feeding. We show that wide-angle propagation beams (from -70° to 70°) can be achieved. Our results have been verified in experiment. (Journal paper under preparation) D. (Part C, Paper #7). We then open perforations on this box to obtain a leakage of radiation forming highly directive antenna, which we call the Huygens’ box antenna (HBA). An important advantage of the antenna is that it achieves near-unity aperture efficiency while the tunable elements reside only at the perimeter (not the area) of the aperture. (Part C, Paper #1 and Conference Paper #12).

21211619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21211619.value: We plan to continue research work trends to demonstrate: (a) Practical Terahertz metasurfaces made from PCB fabrication; (b) Metasurface-Enabled RCAs where the metasurface performs dispersion and phase management as the partially reflecting surface and/or a phase correcting surface; (c) Next-generation Huygens' box antennas with simple tuning that allows both azimuthal and elevation tuning of radiation (the present design only allows for straightforward azimuthal direction tuning).

21211619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21211619.value: Mm-waves and Terahertz waves are emerging as frequencies of choice in 5G communication and beyond. As the world becomes immersed in countless wireless connections, a major demand exists for smart technologies which allow one to shape mm-waves and Terahertz waves with high flexibility, high efficiency and low cost. In this project, we have developed passive and active metasurfaces at microwave, mm-wave and Terahertz frequencies, and advanced their status as ubiquitous manipulators of electromagnetic waves over these frequencies. We have developed wave redirection devices, delay-tunable metasurfaces, metalenses and metasurface-enabled antennas which allow one to redirect, advance or delay, focus or radiate electromagnetic waves according to need. Fundamental investigations allow us to learn more about how the metasurface interacts with waves, thus acquiring knowledge and intuition which leads to creative and successful designs. Practical metasurface applications have been shown, which flattens the form factor, reduces the size, cuts down the fabrication cost, improves the power efficiency, widens the frequency range of previous designs, and/or provides new functionalities. While the demonstrated metasurfaces are very useful on their own, they also illustrate the power to manipulate electromagnetic waves almost at will, benefitting communication, sensing and imaging among many other parts of our lives.

21212019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21212019.value: The development of underground structures (e.g., transportation tunnels and sewage treatment caverns) enhances land availability and reduces environmental impacts. In recent years, the demand for underground structures has rapidly increased in Hong Kong; however, due to significant uncertainties in ground conditions, planners for these projects frequently encounter cost overruns, schedule delays, and associated risks. To overcome these challenges, planners would obtain significant benefits (e.g., reduction of delays and their associated risks) from adapting stochastic programming and feedback control approaches. As a fundamental step, this proposed research focuses on implementing such approaches for hard rock tunnels under resource constraints. Formal implementation of such approaches requires planners to make two specific decisions: (1) schedules and (2) updating cycles of ground conditions. Although the repetitive and comprehensive generation and evaluation of schedules are necessary for the decision-making, existing methods have the following limitations: (1) existing construction process simulation methods cannot consider multiple activity allocation rules for different states (i.e., the excavation progress for each phase) and modify the rules as excavation progresses and (2) existing genetic algorithms are limited to reusing the outcomes for each state from previous learning. To address these gaps, this research proposes a framework that supports the formal adaptation of such approaches for excavation scheduling of hard rock tunnels under resource constraints. To consider uncertain ground conditions under the given equipment fleet, schedules are defined as optimal activity allocation rules for each state. This framework will consist of two methods: (1) a Q-learning-based schedule generation method that enhances the reusability of outcomes from previous learning and (2) an estimation method for durations resulting from schedules modified on the basis of the ground condition updating cycle, which allows for the application of multiple rules for different states. The schedule generation method will allow planners to rapidly identify optimal rules for specific states via the Q tables. In addition, the method for estimating durations will enable planners to rapidly and consistently estimate durations resulting from schedule modification based on the ground condition updating cycle. By conducting three case studies, the research team will identify how the adaptation of stochastic programming and feedback control impacts the reduction of excavation durations, which are also related to time-dependent costs, and their associated risks. In the long term, this research will be extended to complex underground structures and thus will support the development of a variety of underground structures in urban and adjacent fringe areas.

21212019.label: Realisation of objectives
21212019.value: The six objectives have been fully achieved. The research team formalized the ontology that allows users to consider comprehensive resource allocation policies for hard rock tunnel projects. In addition, the team formalized the methodology that enables construction planners (CPs) for hard rock tunnels to assess the duration of excavation schedules for hard rock tunnel projects considering comprehensive resource allocation policies under resource constraints. Moreover, the team formalized Q-learning methodology that supports CPs in finding optimal resource allocation policies for different excavation states considering uncertainties in ground conditions. Furthermore, the team has carried out case studies to validate the ontology and two methodologies in preconstruction and construction.

Formalize an estimation method for durations resulting from schedules modified on the ground condition updating cycle basis; and
Validate the consistency and speed of the estimation method.

21212019.label: Major findings and research outcome
21212019.value: Our research team has successfully developed a Q-learning-based schedule generation framework for excavating hard rock tunnels under resource constraints. First, the research team formalized the ontology, which can support the schedule assessment methodology and Q-learning-based schedule optimization methodology. The team submitted a conference paper based on the ontology. Second, the team proposed the methodology to assess the duration of excavation schedules for hard rock tunnel projects considering comprehensive resource allocation policies under resource constraints. The team carried out case studies and found that this methodology will allow construction planners (CPs) for hard rock tunnels to consider comprehensive resource allocation policies and identify the policy that minimize the excavation duration. Based on the methodology, the team submitted one conference paper and one journal paper. Third, the team formalized Q-learning methodology that will enable CPs to identify optimal resource allocation policies for different excavation states considering uncertainties in ground conditions in preconstruction and construction. The team carried out case studies and found that this Q-learning-based optimization methodology will help CPs reduce the excavation duration. Based on the methodology, the team submitted one conference paper and is preparing one journal paper.

21212019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21212019.value: Our research team will further develop the Q-learning-based methodology considering updated ground conditions during construction by using contextual bandits. This will help the construction planners (CPs) for hard rock tunnels identify more relevant scenarios of ground conditions as excavation progresses and CPs collect more information about ground conditions. Based on the relevant scenarios identified at specific points in time, the CPs will be able to apply the optimal resource allocation policy for the specific excavation state. The team will also collect the information about additional case studies and apply the methodology to validate the impact on schedule reduction.

21212019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21212019.value: In tunnel construction projects, uncertainties in the ground conditions often lead to higher costs and delays. Planners try to minimize costs by using limited resources like equipment efficiently. However, current methods do not fully support planners in finding the best resource allocation strategies before and during construction. This research proposes a framework to help planners assess how different resource allocation strategies affect the time it takes to excavate tunnels in hard rock areas with uncertain ground conditions. By doing so, it aims to help planners find the most efficient resource allocation policies for different stages of tunnel excavation, ultimately reducing construction time and costs.

21212419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21212419.value: In the big data era, recommender systems become fundamental to filter out content by exploring users' preferences and tastes, rather than explicitly searching for pre-specified content. The recommendation applications range from multimedia recommendations, such as movies, music, news, and ads, to product recommendations in e-commerce. On the other hand, a growing amount of Internet traffic is transmitted in wireless networks and mobile devices become a major tool for content access. More computation is being pushed to the edge devices (i.e., edge computing), such as sensors, industrial machines, and Wi-Fi hotspots. New challenges emerge for these wireless applications, such as limited bandwidth, broadcast features, distributed operations, and dynamic environments. Thus, it is natural to ask how to design recommender systems featuring wireless environments, or even more broadly, how to design machine learning algorithms over wireless. The main goal of this proposal is to develop a new learning framework for recommender systems that fits well in the wireless environment with high dynamics and uncertainty, limited bandwidth, and distributed storage and computing resources. Note that this project is NOT about how we apply recommendation techniques to recommend wireless channels, bandwidth, etc. This project is to design a recommendation framework that fits into the wireless. To tackle these problems, we leverage the contextual multi-armed bandit framework for recommendations, where the contextual information is used to capture the situational or environmental knowledge when making a recommendation, e.g., time, location, user profiles, browsing history. To capture the aforementioned wireless features, we propose three new wireless recommendation problems in this new learning framework for wireless recommendations and we will design and analyze the learning algorithms. 1) Group recommendations under bandwidth constraints. A recommender can recommend and broadcast items to a group of users, and we aim to learn the preference of users and optimize the content delivery at the same time given the limited bandwidth. 2) Federated recommendations for distributed operations. Each computing server has local data for making recommendations, and they can communicate and incorporate their recommendation models to make better decisions. Our goal is to make communication-efficient and robust recommendations. 3) Contextual recommendations with latent structures. Latent structures of items and contexts (latent structures mainly refer to some unobserved underlying structures, such as the clustering of items or contexts, due to the high dynamics of the wireless environments) are to be explored in order to facilitate the learning efficiency. 在大数据时代，通过学习用户的偏好，推荐系统已经成为基本的内容过滤工具。推荐应用包括了从多媒体推荐，比如电影、音乐、新闻和广告等，到电商的商品推荐。另一方面，越来越多的互联网流量在无线网络中传输，而移动终端已经成为主要的内容获取工具。大量的计算已经部署在边缘节点上（即边缘计算），比如传感器、工业机器以及Wi-Fi接入点等。这些新的无线应用也带来了诸多挑战，比如有限的带宽、广播特性以及多变的环境。因此，很自然的一个问题是如何设计无线环境下的推荐系统，或者更广泛的说，怎么设计面向无线环境的机器学习算法。 本项目的主要目的是构建一个新的推荐系统学习框架，使之能很好的适应多变的动态环境和不确定性、有限的带宽、以及分布式的存储和计算资源。值得澄清的一点是本项目并不是研究我们怎么样来利用已有的推荐技术进行无线信道和带宽的推荐。本项目研究的侧重点是如何面向无线环境设计行之有效的推荐系统。为了解决这些问题，我们针对背景感知的多臂赌博机框架下的推荐机制开展研究。这里背景信息是指进行推荐时的环境和情境信息，比如时间、地点、用户信息、浏览历史等。为了体现前面提到的无线特性，我们在新的框架下研究如下三项无线推荐系统的问题。1）带宽受限下的群组推荐。这里，推荐系统选择并且广播传输内容给一组用户。在无线带宽受限情况下，我们需要同时学习用户偏好并且优化内容分发策略。2）分布式计算下的联邦推荐。每一个服务器都有用来进行推荐的本地数据。这些服务器能够互相通信并交换学习的模型以便进行更有效的推荐。我们还希望推荐系统的通信也会更高效鲁棒。3）隐式结构下的背景感知推荐。这里隐式结构通常指推荐系统无法直接观测到的基础结构，比如由于多变的无线环境下物品或背景信息的聚类。我们将研究如何利用这些隐式结构来提升学习效率。

21212419.label: Realisation of objectives
21212419.value: Throughout the duration of this project, a series of research activities were undertaken to achieve the outlined objectives. Below are details of how each objective was addressed and the extent to which it was realized. 1) Objective 1. The primary objective of this project was to develop a new learning framework for recommender systems in wireless environments. This framework addresses various challenges, including limited bandwidth, federated recommendations with distributed servers, and dynamic and latent user contexts. We initiated the project by developing a federated multi-armed bandit (MAB) framework to address wireless recommendation problems, focusing on communication bottlenecks, broadcast features, and data privacy. Our approach involved designing privacy-preserving, communication-efficient algorithms to study the interactions between privacy, communication, and learning performance in terms of regret. We also explored wireless recommendations under computation and storage constraints, specifically in mobile edge caching (MEC) scenarios. We formulated a multi-objective caching problem as a Multi-agent Multi-objective Combinatorial Multi-Armed Bandit (MMC-MAB) problem. Our framework used adaptive federated learning for estimation and proposed methods for optimizing cache placement, yielding significant improvements in both cache hit rates and cache profit. Furthermore, we proposed a novel federated recommendation framework with personalized client models, addressing the performance limitations of homogeneous models caused by latent user context and item features. Our approach incorporated singular value decomposition to reduce communication costs and applied this framework to benchmark datasets, demonstrating significant improvements in accuracy and efficiency. 2) Objective 2. We investigated the impacts of various wireless factors on recommendation performance, focusing on the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) and wireless content delivery as case studies. IoV involves a distributed network of connected vehicles and infrastructure, where wireless recommendations play a crucial role. We explored key techniques and discussed the challenges and opportunities in deploying these recommendations within the IoV, emphasizing the importance of considering wireless factors in system design. In wireless content deliveries, various wireless servers will have different content popularity. The need to learn content popularity and adapt to wireless edge device resource constraints, such as limited computing, communication, and storage resources, has become challenging. To understand this research question well, we have theoretically and empirically studied the trade-offs among different wireless factors, such as communication bandwidth, computing, storage resources, privacy concerns, and recommendation performance. 3) Objective 3. Within the federated wireless recommendation framework, we devised algorithms for master-worker, decentralized, and hybrid structures, using differential privacy (DP) to protect data while minimizing communication costs. Theoretical and empirical results showed consistent trade-offs between regret, communication costs, and privacy concerns. In another study, we explored the benefits of coding techniques in wireless recommendation systems operating over channels with erasures. We identified scenarios where coded broadcasting could enhance user satisfaction at fixed channel utilization levels, particularly in cases of heterogeneous user preferences. Our findings provide insights into optimizing reward structures using coding techniques. 4) Objective 4. We focused on the trade-offs between communication costs and federated recommendation performance in distributed settings. Our research introduced the federated private bandits framework, which integrates differential privacy with communication-efficient multi-agent bandit learning. We analyzed the privacy and regret performance of this approach in both master-worker and fully decentralized environments, highlighting the trade-offs between privacy and performance. We have provided an adaptive quantization method to balance the tradeoff between communication cost and learning/recommendation performance in the distributed setting. We developed an adaptively compressed stochastic gradient descent (AC-SGD) strategy that adjusts quantization levels and sparsification sizes dynamically. This approach minimizes communication costs while maintaining model accuracy, outperforming existing gradient compression methods. This approach proved robust against client dropout rates, further enhancing communication efficiency in federated recommendation scenarios. In addition, we proposed a Risk-aware Computation Offloading (RCO) policy for Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) to balance risk management with service delay reduction under server-side attacks. By employing a Bayesian Stackelberg game, we modeled the relationship between the edge system and potential attackers, providing a robust solution for secure computation offloading in wireless environments. We also propose a general method that uses data encoding and error correction to combat Byzantine adversaries, achieving optimal tolerance levels while maintaining computational efficiency. We demonstrated a trade-off between adversary tolerance and resource requirements, proving the robustness of our approach in both streaming and offline settings. 5) Objective 5. Finally, we implemented the proposed algorithms using real datasets to validate their practicality. We proposed a Graph Neural Network-based Personalized Federated Recommendation (PerFedRec) framework. This framework effectively improved personalized recommendation performance by leveraging joint representation learning of latent user contexts and item features, user clustering to explore the latent features and model adaptation. Experiments on real-world datasets confirmed the superiority of our method over existing approaches. We also addressed the challenge of context-drifting in recommendations by developing the Hybrid Static and Adaptive Graph Embedding (HySAGE) network. HySAGE disentangles static user-item interactions from dynamic contextual features, providing a robust solution for context-sensitive recommendations. Extensive experiments demonstrated significant performance improvements, validating the effectiveness of our approach. In another practical implementation, we developed a proof-of-concept model for dialogue rewriting recommendations using semantic role labeling (SRL). Our experiments showed that incorporating SRL significantly improved the performance of a RoBERTa-based model, outperforming previous state-of-the-art systems. During the project, the primary challenges encountered included balancing the trade-offs between communication costs, privacy, and learning performance. These were addressed through the development of innovative algorithms and frameworks that provided theoretical and empirical insights into these trade-offs, ensuring the proposed solutions were both practical and effective. Overall, the project successfully realized its objectives by developing novel frameworks and algorithms that address the unique challenges of wireless recommender systems. The outcomes of this research provide valuable insights and tools for advancing the state of the art in machine learning over wireless networks, with broad implications for both academia and industry.

21212419.label: Major findings and research outcome
21212419.value: This project has yielded several major findings and research outcomes into the design of wireless recommender systems, particularly in the context of bandwidth-constrained environments with high dynamics and distributed local data. The key findings and outcomes are summarized as follows: 1) Build a federated multi-armed bandit (MAB) framework for wireless recommendations. As evidenced by our paper publications in IEEE JASC, TCCN, ISIT, and GlobeCom, we have developed a new federated MAB framework that integrates with limited bandwidth considerations (communication efficiency), privacy concerns, efficient content delivery and storage, multi-objectives over contextual information, allowing for more efficient recommendations under wireless constraints. This framework has proved effective in balancing recommendation accuracy with the limitations imposed by varying wireless network conditions. 2) Federated recommendation systems over wireless. We have published papers about federated recommendations and adaptive communication-efficient learning over wireless in ACM CIKM, IEEE JSAC, and ACM TIST to advance this research direction. The research extended traditional recommender systems to a federated setting, where data is distributed across multiple servers. This federated approach ensures that recommendations remain accurate and relevant, even when data is siloed across different locations. Several adaptive communication efficiency techniques are being developed to address the high dynamic issues in wireless settings. 3) Latent contextual bandit framework. We have publications in IEEE TIT, JSAC, IEEE TCCN, ACM CIKM, and IEEE GlobeCom to develop algorithms to handle and learn latent user contexts and item features, which often cause heterogeneity among users and servers. These algorithms learn the latent structures and user preferences over time, improving the personalization and relevance of recommendations. In addition, the project studied making the recommender systems robust to uncertainties and adversarial attacks, which are particularly relevant in distributed and wireless environments. 4) Several proof-of-concept experiments over real-world data have been conducted to verify the effectiveness of proposed frameworks. The research has advanced the state-of-the-art in wireless recommender systems. The successful integration of machine learning and information theory has resulted in frameworks that are both theoretically sound and practically viable. The findings and outcomes from this project have implications beyond recommender systems and can be applied to various domains, including real-time data analytics, edge computing, and sequential decision-making processes in dynamic environments. This broad applicability highlights the potential for further research and development based on the outcomes of this project.

21212419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21212419.value: This research sets the stage for expanding wireless recommender systems across broader machine-learning tasks and integrating machine learning with emerging wireless communication and networking technologies. Future development could enhance machine learning models over wireless, new large AI models over wireless, improve robustness against security threats, and apply these systems to new domains such as smart cities, wireless healthcare, and Artificial Intelligent of Things (AIoT). To advance these research directions, we propose the following actions: 1) Collaborative Research: Partner with our academic and industry collaborators to extend the application of our findings and explore new technologies, such as Large Language Models (LLMs). 2) Prototype Development: Create and test prototypes in real-world settings to refine the systems and assess practical challenges. Collect feedback to improve our framework further. 3) Outreach and Dissemination: Increase dissemination through publications, conferences, public talks, and industry engagements. Raise awareness among different domains. These steps will ensure the continued impact and relevance of the research in both academic and practical applications.

21212419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21212419.value: Recommender systems have become an integral component of modern information processing systems, enabling users to discover content based on their intent rather than explicitly searching for it. The applications of recommendation systems span various domains, including multimedia (e.g., movies, music, news), products, advertisements, tourism, transportation routes, and even healthcare diagnostics. With the majority of content now consumed on mobile devices and the growing trend of edge computing, the need to design recommender systems that are optimized for wireless environments has become increasingly urgent. The primary objective of this project was to develop a comprehensive theoretical and practical framework for designing wireless recommender systems. These systems need to account for bandwidth constraints that could affect user experience and the overall performance of the recommendations. Additionally, these systems also need to address challenges associated with federated recommendations, where data is stored locally across distributed servers, and the item features and user contexts are either latent (unobservable or partially observable) or time-varying.

21215319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21215319.value: The goal of monitoring social networks is to detect anomalies in a network as quickly as possible. Detection of such anomalies can be used to identify suspicious individuals or groups of individuals. In social network analysis aggregation over time is ubiquitous. Though this may be necessary for practical reasons, whenever data is aggregated (from timestamp to count in equal units of time) there is a loss of information. One example of such temporal aggregation is Sparks and Paris (2017) who collected tweet informatics in real time and aggregate the data to an hourly level. This so-called temporal aggregation is common practice in many research areas including monitoring. Zwetsloot and Woodall (2018) found that currently no detailed guidelines exist for selecting appropriate levels of temporal aggregation, also little research exists which studies the effect of temporal aggregation on the performance of monitoring tools. Therefore, in this project we focus on the use of temporal aggregation within the field of statistical process monitoring (SPM). This project will explore the effect of temporal aggregation with a focus on network data from social networks. The first objective of this project is to study the effect of aggregation on monitoring networks. I will illustrate the effect of temporal aggregation using well known case studies and simulation. In the second part guidelines and strategies are presented to select appropriate levels of temporal aggregation. For this new monitoring models will be developed. Schuh et al. (2013) showed that when monitoring univariate count data the detection speed increases as there is less temporal aggregation. They advise using time-between events models. Based on this result we hypothesize that lower levels of aggregation will increase the inspection speed for network monitoring as well. The third part of this project will explore how build a model for real time monitoring of network data based on the concept of time-between events models. 监测社交网络的目标是尽快检测出网络中的异常。检测出的异常可用来识别可疑的个体或群体。按时间聚合(temporal aggregation)在社交网络分析中是普遍存在的。数据聚合在实践中可能是必须的，但聚合的过程（从时间戳到相同时间内的计数）伴随着信息丢失。Sparks和Paris（2017）提供了一个时间聚合的例子，他们收集实时的推特数据并以小时为单位进行聚合。 上述的时间聚合常见于许多研究领域，包括监测。 Zwetsloot和Woodall（2018）发现目前没有选择合适的时间聚合水平的详细指导方针，也少有关于时间聚合对监测工具性能的影响的研究。因此在本项目中，我们关注时间聚合在统计过程监测（statistical process monitoring-SPM）中的使用。该项目将探讨时间聚合对来自社交网络的网络数据的作用。第一个目标是研究聚合对网络监测的影响。我将用案例研究和模拟来说明时间聚合的影响。在第二部分中，我们将介绍选择适当时间聚合水平的指南和策略，为此我们将开发新的监测模型。 Schuh 等（2013）研究发现，当监测单变量计数数据时，检测速度会随着时间聚合水平的降低而增加。他们建议使用事件间隔时间模型（time-between event models）。基于这一结果，我们假设较低的聚合水平会提高网络监测的检测速度。该项目的第三部分将探讨，如何基于事件间隔时间模型的概念去构建用于实时监测网络数据的模型。

21300219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21300219.value: 口山酮是一類基本分子式為C13H8O2的三環天然產物，廣泛分佈於微生物和植物中。該類化合物不僅具有豐富的結構多樣性，且大多具有廣泛的生物活性，同時也為藥物研發提供了許多重要的借鑒，因此其生物合成一直廣受關注。儘管在過去的幾十年中，有大量關於該類化合物的生物合成研究工作被報道，但其完整的生物合成途徑和內在機制仍未完全闡明。因此，通過進一步對口山酮的生物合成進行深入研究，不僅有助於我們闡釋該類化合物生物合成過程中的諸多未解之謎，也可為具有顯著生物活性的新型口山酮類化合物的合成生物學和代謝工程提供參考。 近期，項目申請人在新煙麴黴（Aspergillus novofumigatus）的基因組中發現了一條潛在的口山酮生物合成基因簇，通過基因敲除手段，我們證實該基因簇負責合成一個結構新穎的口山酮二聚體，neosartorin。目前我們已經部分闡明了該化合物的後期生物合成途徑，但尚存在諸多疑惑之處，例如該化合物骨架的形成和反應中涉及的關鍵酶具體是哪些仍然亟待解決。該項目旨在從分子水平上全面闡明neosartorin的生物合成的同時，並以該代謝途徑作為參考模式進行其類似物的生物合成研究，進而發現全新口山酮類化合物。 為了實現上述目標，申請人擬在前期研究基礎上，首先通過異源表達策略驗證和重構neosartorin的生物合成途徑。其次，通過體外酶促反應研究該化合物生物合成過程中所需關鍵酶的生物與化學功能，以深入了解neosartorin的生物合成。接下來，我們還將研究neosartorin類似物的生物合成，進而揭示口山酮結構多樣化與關鍵酶的關係。最後，本研究還將嘗試通過組合生物合成的策略研究來源於不同真菌口山酮的生物合成基因，以此來構建全新的口山酮合成代謝途徑，進而發現一系列全新的口山酮。 總之，本研究將首次闡明neosartorin的完整生物合成途徑並揭示其生物合成途徑過程中所需酶的功能，將是在基因/酶的水平上全面揭示口山酮生物合成合成途徑的第一個實例。此外本研究還將首次開發和構建一套該類化合物多樣性生物合成路徑的有效系統，以利用公共數據庫中海量的基因組數據來合成全新的口山酮生物活性分子。

21300219.label: Realisation of objectives
21300219.value: Objective 1: Understand the biosynthesis of chrysophanol that serves as the key precursor for the fungal xanthones. This objective has been completely realized. In this project, the biosynthetic pathway of chrysophanol was reconstituted in a heterologous fungus, Aspergillus oryzae, based on the predicted biosynthesis, successfully leading to the production of chrysophanol. The A. oryzae transformant created herein was then used as a host to investigate the functions of downstream biosynthetic enzymes. Objective 2: Elucidate the complete biosynthetic pathway of fungal xanthone heterodimer, neosartorin, to provide a first example in which the biosynthetic route of a fungal xanthone is fully revealed. This objective has been completely realized. Prior to this project, the biosynthetic mechanisms of blennolide A and blennolide C, which are biosynthetic precursors of neosartorin, remained enigmatic. Through in vivo and in vitro reconstitution of their biosynthesis, as well as structural biology study, key enzymes for their biosynthesis, have been identified and characterized. Objective 3: Perform biosynthetic studies on other fungal xanthones to identify the key enzymes that diversify the fungal xanthone pathways. This objective has been completely realized. In this project, the biosynthesis of secalonic acid D, another tetrahydroxanthone dimer, was investigated, and the key enzymes that are specifically required for secalonic acid D biosynthesis have been identified and characterized. Objective 4: Create new xanthone analogues by replacing selected biosynthetic genes with those from different pathways. This objective has been completely realized. Related to the point mentioned for Objective 3 above, several unnatural analogues were also successfully obtained through the heterologous production of secalonic acid D. Objective 5: Establish a new methodology that allows for the generation of diverse artificial metabolic pathways with a variety of genes from many different fungi. This objective has been mostly realized. Originally, this project aimed to establish a new fungal transformation method by utilizing the replication-cycle reaction (RCR) method. However, the RCR method did not work well for the construction of large fungal transformation plasmids. Therefore, as an alternative approach, we established a fungal transformation method that involves CRISPR-Cas9 guided homologous recombination, which works better than the conventional non-homologous recombination-based transformation. In addition, this method has been applied to introduce a large gene (approximately 30 kb) in a single transformation event. However, it is unfortunately still challenging to establish a method that allows for pathway diversification, and further consideration and investigation are needed. Objective 6: Apply the methodology established above to obtain many new xanthones. This objective has been realized to some extent. This project failed to obtain many new xanthones, but only a limited number of new analogues could be obtained. Nevertheless, the established method has been proven useful for biosynthetic investigation and engineering of diverse fungal natural products (including non-xanthone molecules). For example, this method was successfully applied to obtain analogues of variecolin, which harbors diverse potent biological activities. Objective 7: Evaluate the biological activities of the compounds obtained in this project. This objective has been realized to some extent. As mentioned above, only a limited number of xanthone analogues could be obtained in this project. However, the biological activity of other types of compounds obtained in relation to this project was evaluated. For example, one of the variecolin analogues has been found to possess a better anticancer activity than variecolin.
