21300219.label: Major findings and research outcome
21300219.value: This project first aimed to unravel the fungal strategy for tetrahydroxanthone (THX) biosynthesis and diversification, focusing on the key enzymes involved in this process. The novel isomerase NsrQ from Aspergillus novofumigatus was identified as a crucial enzyme in the biosynthesis of THXs, playing a significant role in the THX skeleton synthesis (Ref. 1). NsrQ was found to catalyze a two-step isomerization reaction, involving the isomerization of allylic alcohol and subsequent inversion of configuration at the methyl group. In addition, the crystal structure of NsrQ was obtained, and several key amino acid residues important for the reaction have been identified, providing the structural basis for the unusual reaction catalyzed by NsrQ (Ref. 3). Furthermore, attempts have been made to diversify the structures of THXs. To this end, the biosynthesis of the THX dimer, secalonic acid D, has been elucidated, and several unnatural analogues have been obtained (Ref. 2). Another major achievement in this study is the establishment of a new fungal transformation method. This method is based on the CRISPR-Cas9-guided homologous recombination, which allows the integration of target DNA to a specific chromosomal site with a smaller amount of substrate DNA compared with conventional transformation methods (Ref. 4–9). Importantly, multiple chromosomal sites can be targeted in a single transformation, enabling the efficient introduction of multiple genes. Furthermore, this method was found to be useful for the transformation with a large gene; a large gene, of which the size is approximately 30 kb, has been successfully introduced in a single transformation event (Ref. 8). Finally, the method was utilized for the structural derivatization of a natural scaffold to obtain an unnatural analogue with an improved biological activity (Ref. 9). In summary, this project has unveiled an intriguing biosynthetic mechanism in fungal THX biosynthesis, achieved structural diversification of THXs, and established an efficient fungal transformation method with wide applicability, which would facilitate future studies on fungal natural product biosynthesis and biosynthetic engineering.

21300219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21300219.value: Regarding the biosynthesis of fungal THXs, the PI’s group and some other research groups have identified and characterized several key biosynthesis enzymes, and therefore, their biosynthesis is now well understood. One thing that might need further investigation is the reason that secalonic acid D was not obtained as a major product in the heterologous host, which would facilitate the selective heterologous production of this medicinally important natural product. In terms of the fungal transformation method, further improvement is desired in order that heterologous expression of biosynthetic gene clusters can be more easily achieved and that biosynthetic genes from different sources can be readily combined in a heterologous host.

21300219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21300219.value: The research project aimed to understand how fungi produce certain compounds and develop a new method for modifying their genetic makeup. The first part of the project focused on a compound called tetrahydroxanthone (THX) and the enzymes involved in its production. We identified a key enzyme, NsrQ, and studied its role in the production of THX. We also determined the 3D structure of NsrQ, which is important for understanding how it works. Additionally, we were able to create new versions of THX, which could have different properties. The second part of the project involved developing a new method for changing the genetic makeup of fungi. This method, called CRISPR-Cas9-guided homologous recombination, allows us to make specific changes to fungal DNA more easily than before. This could be useful for making fungi produce new compounds that could be used in medicine or agriculture. In summary, this research project has uncovered new information about how fungi make important compounds, and has developed a new method for changing their genetic makeup. This could be useful for making new and useful compounds in the future.

21301319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21301319.value: Organic-inorganic metal halide perovskite solar cells (PVSCs) have attracted tremendous attention from various scientific communities due to their superb semiconducting properties. Very recently, the power conversion efficiency (PCE) has realized a certified value of 23.3%. Further improvement of the PCE has been greatly limited by the open-circuit voltage, since the reported short-circuit current density has reached over 90 % of the theoretical Shockley-Queisser (S-Q) limit while the open-circuit voltage only received much less than 90% of the limit. Various approaches have been carried out to reduce voltage loss. However, the deep understanding of the voltage loss and the in-depth mechanism are still lacking. In our project, we aim to address voltage loss originally through designing perovskite absorber and the adjacent interfaces. Integrated characterization of both materials and devices will be performed to deeply investigate the dependence of voltage loss on the compositions and interfaces, as well as provide a broad rule for the control of voltage loss.The PI has accumulated broad expertise of perovskite photovoltaics in the past 7 years’ research, including the crystallography of hybrid perovskites, material processing and interface engineering as well as advanced optoelectronic characterizations. To alleviate the voltage loss and unveil the relevant mechanism in optoelectronic devices, we proposed the following tasks: (1) from the perspective of materials, we will design novel perovskite materials through composition engineering and microstructure control; (2) from the perspective of interfaces, we will tune the interfacial properties by surface modifications and development of novel charge transport layers (CTLs); (3) by integrating perovskite and its interfaces, we will investigate and explore how the perovskite and perovskite/CTLs interfaces contribute to device performance and voltage loss, and establish the structure-properties-performance relationship. Our preliminary results have obtained a very low voltage loss of 420 mV in high-performance PVSCs, close to 370 mV of monocrystalline silicon photovoltaics, elucidating the high feasibility of our proposed work. We believe that the implementation of this proposal could not only explore and unveil the relationship between materials design/interfacial modification and optoelectronic performance, but also provide a new route to develop high quality perovskite absorber and CTLs to realize highly efficient and reliable PVSCs with extremely low voltage loss for mass production and commercialization. The technology developed through our comprehensive characterization and analysis in this project would also help establish more reliable characterization protocols in the photovoltaics field.

21301319.label: Realisation of objectives
21301319.value: Firstly, our approach focused on enhancing the stability and efficiency of inverted (p-i-n) perovskite solar cells (PVSCs) by addressing the stability issues of α-FAPbI3. We incorporated pseudo halide-based ionic liquids, specifically methylamine formate (MAFa), to regulate the residual strain within the perovskite structure. This strategy aimed to prevent the phase transition from α-FAPbI3 to δ-FAPbI3, crucial for maintaining the desired electronic properties of the perovskite layer. This method achieved a record power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 24.08% for inverted FAPbI3-based PVSCs, marking a substantial improvement and demonstrating the effectiveness of our engineering approach. Additionally, the devices exhibited remarkable stability, retaining over 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 hours in an ambient environment with relative humidity of 30 ± 5%. This level of stability is highly promising for practical applications (Adv. Energy Mater., 13: 2300700). Secondly, to further our objectives, we utilized an innovative approach by functionalizing multication and halide perovskite interfaces with an organometallic compound, ferrocenyl-bis-thiophene-2-carboxylate (FcTc2). This method aimed to simultaneously enhance both the efficiency and the stability of inverted PSCs. We achieved a PCE of 25.0%, positioning our results at the forefront of current inverted PSCs performance. The modified devices demonstrated outstanding stability, maintaining over 98% of their initial efficiency after 1500 hours of continuous operation under simulated AM1.5 illumination. Furthermore, these devices met the rigorous international standards for mature photovoltaics (IEC 61215:2016) and exhibited high stability under damp heat conditions (85°C and 85% relative humidity) (Science 376 (6591), 416-420). Lastly, we report a simple design strategy for polymer hole transport materials (HTMs) that can modulate wettability and promote anchoring by integrating pyridine units into the polyarylamine backbone. This design facilitates efficient and stable inverted PVSCs. The HTM properties were effectively modified by varying the linkage sites of pyridine units. Specifically, the 3,5-linked PTAA-P1 showed a more regulated molecular configuration, which interacted optimally with perovskites, leading to highly crystalline perovskite films with uniform back contact and reduced defect density. Dopant-free PTAA-P1-based inverted PVSCs achieved remarkable efficiencies of 24.89% (certified value: 24.50%) for small-area (0.08 cm²) and 23.12% for large-area (1 cm²) devices. Moreover, the unencapsulated device maintained over 93% of its initial efficiency after 800 hours of maximum power point tracking under simulated AM 1.5G illumination.(Adv. Mater. 2023, 35, 2208431)

21301319.label: Major findings and research outcome
21301319.value: Our research has made significant advancements in the field of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), addressing both performance enhancement and stability which are critical for commercialization. Below are the key findings and outcomes from our research: 1. Enhancement of Interface and Device Performance: We functionalized the interfaces of multication and halide perovskite with ferrocenyl-bis-thiophene-2-carboxylate (FcTc2), which led to a notable improvement in both the efficiency and stability of inverted PSCs. The treated devices achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.0% and maintained over 98% of their initial efficiency after 1500 hours of operation under simulated AM1.5 illumination. Additionally, these devices successfully passed the IEC61215:2016 international standards and demonstrated high stability under damp heat conditions (85°C and 85% relative humidity). 2.Development of Polymer Hole Transport Materials (HTMs): We introduced a novel design strategy for polymer HTMs by integrating pyridine units into the polyarylamine backbone, which improved the wettability and anchoring properties on perovskite surfaces. The modified HTMs, particularly the 3,5-linked PTAA-P1, facilitated highly crystalline perovskite films with uniform back contacts and reduced defect densities. This approach enabled the fabrication of inverted PVSCs with PCEs up to 24.89% for small-area devices and 23.12% for large-area devices. These devices also showed excellent durability, maintaining over 93% efficiency after 800 hours of continuous operation (refer to Part C for detailed experimental outcomes). 3. Simplification of Manufacturing Processes: We developed a one-step solution-coating process that simplifies the manufacturing of PSCs. This method involves the simultaneous formation of a robust self-assembled monolayer (SAM) and perovskite crystallization, significantly advancing manufacturability. Our devices achieved a PCE of 24.5% and retained more than 90% of their initial efficiency after 1200 hours of operation. This approach shows compatibility with various SAMs, perovskites, solvents, and processing techniques, enhancing its potential for diverse applications. 4 Thermal Stability Enhancement Using SAMs: We implemented a thermally robust hole-selective layer using nickel oxide (NiOx) nanoparticle films combined with a surface-anchored SAM. This configuration improved the energetic alignment at the NiOx/perovskite interface, reducing the voltage deficit and enhancing the thermal stability of the devices. The resultant PSCs reached a certified PCE of 25.6% and maintained over 90% efficiency after 1200 hours at 65 degrees Celsius under continuous illumination.

21301319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21301319.value: The research outlined demonstrates significant progress in enhancing the performance and stability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), a crucial step towards their commercialization. The functionalization of perovskite interfaces with organometallic compounds like ferrocenyl-bis-thiophene-2-carboxylate (FcTc2) has simultaneously improved efficiency and operational stability, with devices achieving over 25% power conversion efficiency and maintaining over 98% of initial performance after 1500 hours of continuous operation. This approach has also enabled devices to pass international standards for mature photovoltaic technologies. Further research could focus on scaling up this interface engineering strategy to larger device areas while maintaining high performance and stability. Evaluating the long-term durability under real-world environmental stresses would also be an important next step. The development of novel polymer hole transport materials (HTMs) with tailored molecular design is another promising direction. The reported PTAA-P1 polymer HTM enabled highly efficient and stable inverted PSCs, pointing to the potential of rationally designed HTMs to optimize perovskite film quality and interface properties. Exploring the compatibility of these HTMs with different perovskite compositions and device structures could lead to further performance improvements.

21301319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21301319.value: This research project described in the given content focuses on improving the performance and stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), which are a promising technology for harnessing solar energy. Perovskite solar cells have the potential to be more efficient and cost-effective than traditional silicon-based solar cells, but their commercialization has been hindered by challenges in maintaining high efficiency and long-term stability. The researchers have developed several strategies to address these challenges. Firstly, they have found that functionalization of the perovskite interface with an organometallic compound can simultaneously enhance the efficiency and stability of inverted PSCs, leading to devices with 25% power conversion efficiency that can maintain over 98% of their initial efficiency after 1,500 hours of continuous operation. Another approach involves designing a polymer-based hole-transporting material (HTM) that can modulate the wettability and promote the anchoring of the perovskite layer, resulting in highly crystalline perovskite films and efficient, stable inverted PSCs with certified efficiencies of up to 24.5% for small-area devices and 23.12% for large-area devices. Finally, the researchers have developed a one-step solution-coating procedure that simplifies the manufacturing of PSCs by allowing the hole-selective contact and perovskite light absorber to form simultaneously, addressing wettability issues and advancing the overall manufacturability of PSCs. These advancements in perovskite solar cell technology have the potential to significantly reduce the barriers to commercialization, paving the way for more widespread adoption of this renewable energy technology.

21301719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21301719.value: 改變納米微晶的暴露表面並由此控制其表面化學特性已被證實可以顯著的改變它們的催化性能。 CeO2催化劑由於具有多種酸鹼化學性質和快速可切換的Ce氧化態以儲存氧氣等特質使其應用比其他過渡/鑭係金屬氧化物更為多樣。然而，在高溫（特別是> 180℃）下，表面鈰的氧化還原可能隨後改變表面酸鹼性質，因此很難識別真正的催化活性位點。由於現今表面檢測工具的限制，過去幾十年來研究人員對CeO2晶面催化活性的解釋皆不同甚至存在分歧。拉曼和X射線光電子能譜（XPS）等檢測工具並非僅收集了最表面的信號，而是平均了從從表面到塊材的數據。而表徵最頂層表面的探針輔助紅外（IR）和溫度程序脫附（TPD）也有低分辨度的問題，通常無法區分不同CeO2晶面上的Ce陽離子。由此可知傳統的表面工具不足以檢測特定晶面上的物理化學性質的變化，因此嚴重阻礙了晶面催化活性的相關研究。 探針輔助核磁共振（NMR）可以通過給定化學探針的相應化學位移區分各種表面微環境的能力。我們成功使用此方法區分ZnO和TiO2不同晶面上金屬陽離子的化學狀態，並確認了相關反應中的真實活性位點。在此，我們將通過探針輔助核磁共振來研究Ce化學狀態的形貌依賴性，並藉此建立CeO2的晶面指紋。我們相信此建立的晶面指紋將有助於分析未來CeO2催化劑的表面Ce化學狀態分佈。更重要的是，藉由積分NMR峰面積可以很容易地獲得該Ce化學狀態的相應濃度。CeO2作為磷酸酶的潛在模擬物，在此我們將研究CeO2表面Ce化學狀態與濃度在去磷酸化中所扮演的腳色。我們相信"探針輔助核磁共振"不僅可以幫助闡明CeO2的反應機理，也將為未來高催化活性CeO2材料設計提供指導。

21301719.label: Realisation of objectives
21301719.value: The electron density (or Lewis acidity) of surface Ce, which influences the adsorption and activation energy of reactants on the surface, is anticipated to differ across different facets of CeO2. However, conventional surface analysis methods have been unable to distinguish or quantify these variations among facets, leading to disparate interpretations among researchers over the past few decades. To address this issue in this project, we employed probe-assisted 31P NMR for the surface study of CeO2 samples in the shapes of octahedron (octa.), rod, and cube enclosed by (111), (110), and (100) surfaces, respectively [ACS Catal. 2020, 10, 4003]. Trimethylphosphine (TMP), a Lewis base molecule, can coordinate with surface-coordinated unsaturated metal cations (Lewis acids, LA) and produce a wide range of δ31P values in 31P NMR (-20 to -60 ppm). The δ31P of TMP-LA adducts can differentiate cations with varying LA strengths on facets, with a stronger LA site leading to a positive shift in δ31P. Their concentration can be further approached by the peak area at a δ31P. This technique thus provides qualitative and quantitative insights into surface cations. The TMP-31P NMR results of CeO2 samples reveal a morphology-dependent distribution of the Ce chemical state, with decreasing δ 31P values: -33 ppm (octa.) > -47.5 ppm (rod) > -58 ppm (cube). With support from calculations, the electron density (or Lewis acidity) of surface Ce is thus demonstrated to be facet-dependent with 4+-like chemical state on the (111) facet and 3+-like on the (100) facet. The as-established fingerprint of CeO2 can report on the facet distribution/concentration of a given CeO2 sample. Trimethylphosphine oxide (TMPO) was further used as an alternative probe to confirm the results above. The TMPO-31P NMR spectra of CeO2 shapes show the same trend while in a different response region: 50.2 ppm (octa.) > 47.2 ppm (rod) > 45.1 ppm (cube). Despite this, the concentration of each kind of Ce sites was found to be comparable between these two probes. Objective 1 "To establish the 31P NMR fingerprints of three most stable CeO2 (111), (110) and (100) facets." and Objective 2 "To unravel the facet distribution on the surface of a given CeO2 morphology and the corresponding Ce concentration on each facet." was thus 100% achieved. The surface understanding of CeO2 catalysts in the first two objectives is a must for the study of Objective 3 "To determine the in-depth catalytic activity-facet relationships in the LA-catalyzed reactions". Using para-nitrophenyl phosphate (p-NPP) as the phosphorylated substrate, the concentration of surface Ce was shown to play a very minor role in catalytic dephosphorylation, while their acidity was found not only facet-dependent in the order of (111)>(110)>(100) but also the key factor for the activation of ester hydrolysis [Chem. Eur. J. 2020, 26, 1]. Advanced surface spectroscopic techniques suggested that Ce species on the octa. (111) surface can strongly chelate the phosphoryl oxygen (P=O) of substrates, enabling nucleophilic attack by water in this alkaline phosphatase (ALP)-like reaction. In stark contrast, their peroxidase (POD)-like activity was found to be in an opposite trend of (100)>(110)>(111). The high peroxidase-like activity of CeO2 cubes was attributed to the facilitated H2O2-to-OH radicals conversion by electron-rich Ce atoms on the (100) surface for the oxidation of tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) substrate. Fluorescent substrates such as 4-methylumbelliferyl phosphate (4-MUP) for the ALP-like reaction and o-phenylenediamine (OPD) for the POD-like reaction were further adopted recently for cellular imaging [Eur. J. Inorg. Chem. 2022, e202200202]. As expected, octa. CeO2 exhibited efficient promotion of the ALP-like reaction but hindered POD-like activity, while cube CeO2 showed no activity in the ALP-like reaction but displayed rapid catalysis in the POD-like reaction. We thus demonstrated in both works that surface area plays an important factor only if surface Ce could activate adsorbed molecules in these two reactions. In addition to CeO2, we also conducted an in-depth catalytic activity-facet relationship in the dephosphorylation of p-NPP over TiO2. It was found that the dephosphorylation of this molecule can only be catalyzed near room temperature by the (001) surface of TiO2 with fluorine modification [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 133, 16285]. As predicted by model analysis, the electronic withdrawing effect of fluorine imposed on TiO2-(001) surface strongly manipulates the electronic state of surrounding 5 coordinated Ti atoms by making them very acidic with 13 ppm shift in TMP-31P NMR. Those acidic Ti5C atoms on F modified-(001) surface were found to facilitate the bidentate adsorption of p-NPP and its later activation with an energy barrier of 60 kJ/mol, which is ~20 kJ/mol lower than that of pristine TiO2 (001) and (101) surfaces. This work further highlights the importance of unraveling the electronic effect imposed by surface pre-adsorbed species (e.g., surfactant) as it can significantly affect the physiochemical properties of active sites on catalysts’ surface and hence the observed activity.

21301719.label: Major findings and research outcome
21301719.value: 31P NMR spectroscopy was employed with surface probes, TMP and TMPO, to differentiate surface Ce species on various facets of CeO2 and the determination of their respective concentrations [ACS Catal. 2020, 10, 4003]. Both results indicate that the surface Ce acidity exhibits facet-dependent behavior, with a 4+-like state observed on the (111) facet and a 3+-like state on the (100) facet. By establishing the CeO2 fingerprint, valuable insights regarding facet distribution and concentration in given CeO2 samples can be obtained. Our later studies reveal that the strong Lewis acidity of the (111) facet can effectively catalyze the dephosphorylation reaction (i.e., ester hydrolysis) across various phosphorylated substrates [Chem. Eur. J. 2020, 26, 1; Eur. J. Inorg. Chem. 2022, e202200202] and even extend to the (001) surface of TiO2 upon fluorine modification [Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2021, 133, 16285]. A positive correlation was also observed between the Ce acidity and the activation of methanol in the synthesis of dimethyl carbonate from CO2 [Appl. Catal. B 2023, 336, 122914]. The surface understanding of CeO2 catalysts above allows us to explain the extreme H2O2 activation behavior in radical and peroxo pathways found on (111) and (100) surfaces [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2020, 11, 5390]. The radical pathway on (100) surface gives high peroxidase-like activity, making it suitable for H2O2 and glucose detection when combined with glucose oxidase [Chem. Commun. 2020, 56, 7897]. In contrast, The peroxo pathway on the (111) surface converts Br ions to HOBr, mimicking haloperoxidase (HPO) behavior for marine antifouling purposes [ACS nano 2023, 17, 17383]. Insights gained from these CeO2/H2O2 systems have also been applied to the study of cyclohexene oxidation over layered HNb3O8, where the Lewis and Brönsted acidity were found to affect H2O2 activation pathways and hence the product distribution [Appl. Catal. B 2022, 313, 121461]. Building upon the understanding of H2O2 activation above, we disclosed the origin of transition metal oxides as peroxidase mimetics in the field of nanozymes [ACS Appl. Mater. Interfaces 2022, 14, 22728]. The debate surrounding the peroxidase-like activity of Fe3O4 nanozymes compared to horseradish peroxidase was thus resolved [J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 2022, 13, 8872]. Metal atoms in cluster-form nanozymes with high electron density were further shown to promote the radical pathway of H2O2, resulting in optimal reactivity and active site utilization for peroxidase mimicking (cf, cationic single-atom nanozymes) [Small 2022, 18, 2104844].

21301719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21301719.value: The probe-assisted NMR investigation of CeO2 surfaces and their catalytic properties has yielded valuable insights into facet-dependent behavior and reaction activation. Further development of this research can be pursued in several directions. Firstly, the study can be expanded to examine the impact of surface modifications and doping on CeO2's catalytic activity. By introducing different dopants or functional groups on specific facets, the reactivity and selectivity of CeO2 catalysts can be tailored for specific reactions. Secondly, the knowledge gained from CeO2/H2O2 systems can be applied to explore the potential of surface-engineered CeO2 nanozymes in specific enzymatic reactions and their corresponding applications. For instance, our recent work demonstrated that by manipulating the shape of CeO2 nanozymes, the specificity of H2O2-associated enzymatic reactions can be regulated. Specifically, Ce sites enclosed by different coordination structures exhibited exclusive peroxidase-like activity for biomolecule detection and haloperoxidase-like activity for antifouling purposes [ACS nano 2023, 17, 17383]. These findings offer insights into surface control, even in pure materials, and guide the rational design of CeO2 nanozymes to achieve high activity and reaction specificity in targeted applications. This research should thus pave the way for diverse applications in biomedical and environmental remediation fields.

21301719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21301719.value: In this project, probe-assisted NMR was used to differentiate Ce sites enclosed by (111), (110), and (100) surfaces among CeO2 samples in the shapes of octahedron (octa.), rod, and cube. The established fingerprint can index the facet distribution of any CeO2 catalyst and provide qualitative/quantitative information on Ce sites. Several enzymatic reactions were then examined to highlight the importance of surface understanding of a given catalyst. The strong Lewis acidity of the (111) facet of CeO2 was found to effectively catalyze dephosphorylation reactions across various phosphorylated substrates. This catalytic behavior can even extend to the (001) surface of TiO2 with suitable modifications. We have also observed a positive relationship between the acidity of Ce and the activation of methanol in the synthesis of dimethyl carbonate from CO2. For H2O2 substrate, the cube (100) surface activates H2O2 through radical pathways, while the octa. (111) surface activates it through peroxo pathways. These findings have practical implications, such as using CeO2 cube for biomolecule detection and CeO2 octa. for antifouling purposes. We have also applied these insights to layered HNb3O8 and Fe3O4 nanozymes. Overall, our research enhances the understanding of CeO2 surfaces and opens up possibilities for developing efficient catalysts and nanozymes.

21304919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21304919.value: Atmospheric aerosols are of huge concern to policymakers worldwide due to their adverse environmental and health effects. Formulating air quality policies to reduce aerosol pollution based on current atmospheric models is challenging due to knowledge gaps on how the mass concentration and composition of aerosols evolve in the atmosphere. Aerosol acidity, which is described by the pH of an aqueous aerosol distribution, is an important property that regulates many atmospheric processes that transform aerosol mass concentration and composition. However, the effect of aerosol pH on atmospheric processes remain poorly constrained, which limits the capability of atmospheric models to explicitly consider aerosol acidity and assess its influence on aerosol mass concentration and composition. The proposed research aims to provide new insights into the contributions of emission sources to ambient aerosol acidity, and into the influence of aerosol acidity on various processes that transform aerosol mass concentrations and composition. We will first determine the pH of ambient aerosols in Hong Kong, and investigate the contributions of emission sources and their seasonal variations to aerosol pH. Aerosols will be collected on filters at City University of Hong Kong (CityU) during different seasons in a year-long study. Different analytical techniques will be used to identify and quantify major aerosol constituents. Ambient aerosol pH values will be determined using a thermodynamic model with the measured aerosol constituents and meteorological conditions as model inputs. Positive matrix factorization analysis will be performed on the measured aerosol constituents to identify and quantify the individual contributions of different sources. A comprehensive statistical analysis of these datasets will then be performed to quantify the contributions of different sources to ambient aerosol pH, and to determine how these source contributions to aerosol pH change with the season. We will also conduct additional ambient measurements at the same site and similar thermodynamic modeling studies to investigate the extent to which aerosol acidity promotes the water-solubility of different metals in ambient aerosols. Lastly, we will conduct laboratory aerosol oxidation experiments on collected ambient aerosol samples and laboratory-generated model aerosols to investigate the influence of aerosol acidity on the chemical transformation of aqueous organic aerosols through heterogeneous hydroxyl (OH) radical photooxidation. Overall, the successful implementation of this proposal will fill critical knowledge gaps on the role of aerosol acidity in atmospheric processes that transform aerosol mass concentration and composition, which is crucial for the improvement of atmospheric models used in air quality policy formulation. 由於對環境和健康的不利影響，大氣氣溶膠引起了各國決策者的巨大關注。因為對氣溶膠品質濃度和成分如何在大氣中演變的知識空白，基於當前大氣模型制定相應空氣品質政策以減少氣溶膠污染具有挑戰性。氣溶膠酸度由液態氣溶膠分佈的pH值來描述，它是調節許多大氣過程的一個重要特性，這些過程改變了氣溶膠的品質濃度和成分。然而，關於氣溶膠酸鹼度對大氣過程的影響人們仍然缺乏認識，這限制了大氣模型準確類比氣溶膠酸度並評估其對氣溶膠品質濃度和成分的影響的能力。 本項研究旨在對以下領域提供新的深入見解：排放源對環境氣溶膠酸度的貢獻，以及氣溶膠酸度對改變氣溶膠品質濃度和成分的各種過程的影響。我們將首先確定香港環境氣溶膠的pH值，並調查排放源及其季節變化對氣溶膠pH的影響。在為期一年的研究中，氣溶膠將依照不同的季節被收集在位於城市香港大學的篩檢程式裡。不同的分析技術將被運用於氣溶膠主要成分的定性和定量分析。環境氣溶膠的pH值將通過一種熱動力學模型來確定，所測定的氣溶膠成分和氣象條件將作為此模型的輸入值。正矩陣因數分解分析法將被運用於所測定的氣溶膠成分，以定性和定量不同排放源的單獨貢獻。然後通過對這些資料集進行綜合的統計分析，以量化不同排放源對環境氣溶膠pH的貢獻，並確定這些來源對氣溶膠pH的貢獻如何隨季節變化。我們還將在同一地點開展額外的環境測量和類似的熱動力學模型研究，以研究氣溶膠酸度在多大程度上促進不同金屬在環境氣溶膠中的水溶性。最後，我們將對收集到的環境氣溶膠樣品和實驗室生成的模型氣溶膠進行實驗室氣溶膠氧化實驗，以研究氣溶膠酸度對液相有機氣溶膠通過非均相羥基自由基（OH）光氧化的化學轉化的影響。總之，本提案的成功實施將填補有關氣溶膠酸度在大氣過程中的作用的關鍵知識空白，這些過程改變了氣溶膠品質濃度和成分，這對於改進空氣品質政策制定中所使用的大氣模型至關重要。

21304919.label: Realisation of objectives
21304919.value: Overall, all the proposed objectives in this study have been fully achieved. Six publications have resulted from this study. The goal of objective 1 was to characterize the pH of ambient aerosols during different seasons in Hong Kong through ambient measurements coupled with thermodynamic modeling, and then correlating the ambient aerosol pH with local emission sources and meteorological conditions. Given that different locations in Hong Kong have different dominant local emission sources, we chose different urban locations for this study, ranging from those with very high levels of vehicular traffic (Mongkok) to those with moderate levels of vehicular traffic but high levels of commercial, and/or residential, and/or industrial activities (Tsuen Wan, Yuen Long, and Kowloon Tong). We analyzed the composition of PM2.5 (specifically the water-soluble inorganic ions since they are key drivers of aerosol acidity) and measured the concentrations of gas-phase ammonia in these locations during different seasons. Using the aerosol composition, meteorological conditions (relative humidity (RH) and temperature), ambient gas-phase ammonia concentrations at these sites as model inputs in the thermodynamic model ISORROPIA-II, we were able to determine the pH of ambient aerosols at these locations. Regardless of the location, the PM2.5 was acidic, with clear and consistent seasonal oscillatory cycles. We performed comprehensive sensitivity analyses and showed that meteorological conditions played more important roles than local emission sources in influencing the PM2.5 pH in Hong Kong. The significance of this work is that it enabled us to gain a better understanding on the roles of aerosol composition in governing the pH of PM2.5 over different seasons in different locations in Hong Kong which will be useful for predicting how atmospheric processes that depend on aerosol acidity will evolve as air pollutant emissions change over time. The goal of objective 2 was to characterize the effect of aerosol pH on the water-solubility of various trace metals in ambient aerosols in Hong Kong. To complete this objective, we performed ambient gas-phase ammonia and size-fractionated aerosol measurements in Kowloon Tong. Kowloon Tong was chosen since it an urban location with many anthropogenic emission sources that can contribute substantial concentrations of trace metals. Measurements were performed for one month in each season of a year-long study. The key parameter that needs to be calculated for each metal of interest is the water-soluble mass fraction (i.e., water-soluble mass fraction of the metal = [water-soluble metal] / [total metal]). From the methodology point of view, protocols for the extraction of the total trace metals from aerosol filters and their subsequent analyses using inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry are scarce but we successfully established methodologies for both. We also analyzed the composition of the size-fractionated aerosols (specifically the water-soluble inorganic ions since they are key drivers of aerosol acidity) and measured the concentrations of gas-phase ammonia. Using the aerosol composition, meteorological conditions (RH and temperature), ambient gas-phase ammonia concentrations as model inputs in the thermodynamic model ISORROPIA-II, we were able to determine the pH of the size-fractionated aerosols. We then performed comprehensive correlation and statistical analyses on these datasets and determined that the trace metals’ fraction solubilities in PM2.5 were not governed by the aerosol pH even though sulfate-driven acid processing played an important role in the dissolution of the water-insoluble forms for most of the studied trace metals. The significance of this work is that it enabled us to gain a better understanding on the roles that sulfate plays in the acid dissolution of trace metals in PM2.5 in Hong Kong. In addition, our findings can be applied to other urban locations in South China, where sulfate is the dominant acidic and hygroscopic component in PM2.5. The goal of objective 3 was to provide new insights into the effect of aerosol acidity on the chemical transformation of aqueous organic aerosols during OH radical photooxidation. We decided on inorganic nitrate as the aqueous OH radical precursor since is it a ubiquitous component of atmospheric aqueous aerosols and it generates OH radicals and a suite of other atmospherically important reactive oxygen species and reactive nitrogen species upon exposure to solar radiation. As biomass burning is recognized to be an important global source of organic aerosols, we first chose to focus on phenolic compounds since they are prominent water-soluble organic compounds emitted during biomass burning. By performing systematic laboratory experiments using a variety of phenolic compounds with different chemical functionality, we were able to determine how the aerosol pH, amount of inorganic nitrate, and the molecular structure of the phenolic compound influence its reaction rates, products formed and light absorption properties. We next focused on various carboxylic acids since they are ubiquitous components of organic aerosols worldwide. By performing systematic laboratory experiments, we were able to determine how the aerosol pH, amount of inorganic nitrate, and the carboxylic acid’s dissociated vs. undissociated combine to influence the carboxylic acid’s overall reactivity. The significance of this work is that it enabled us to gain a better understanding on how aerosol pH can affect the reaction rates for different organic compounds that are commonly found in aqueous aerosols worldwide. Overall, the findings of this study have important environment implications, and the knowledge gained fill critical knowledge gaps on the role of aerosol acidity in atmospheric processes that transform aerosol mass concentration and composition, which is crucial for the improvement of atmospheric models used in air quality policy formulation. In addition to the research outcomes, we have trained a number of undergraduate students on atmospheric chemistry and environmental analytical techniques, and we have educated them on the importance of atmospheric chemistry.

21304919.label: Major findings and research outcome
21304919.value: The results from this project have been published in a number of high impact journals (Part C). The goal of objective 1 was to characterize the pH of ambient aerosols during different seasons in Hong Kong through ambient measurements coupled with thermodynamic modeling, and then correlating ambient aerosol pH with local emission sources and meteorological conditions. As reported by Nah et al. (2022) and Nah et al. (2023), clear and consistent seasonal oscillatory cycles were observed for both PM2.5 pH (2 to 5) and aerosol liquid water concentrations (5 to 40 µg/m3). While seasonality was a major factor in influencing PM2.5 pH and aerosol liquid water concentrations, local emission sources were minor factors. PM2.5 was the most acidic in the fall, and was the least acidic in winter. Aerosol liquid water concentrations were the lowest in summer, and the highest in winter/spring. Sensitivity tests revealed that chemical composition, especially particulate sulfate concentrations, plays a major role in driving the variations in aerosol pH and aerosol liquid water concentration during each season. However, the magnitudes to which aerosol pH and aerosol liquid water concentration respond to changes in chemical composition depend strongly on the meteorological conditions in each season. The goal of objective 2 was to characterize the effect of aerosol pH on the water-solubility of various trace metals in ambient aerosols in Hong Kong. As reported by Yang et al. (2023), the concentrations of total and water-soluble trace metals in fine and coarse aerosols were the highest during the winter and spring seasons due to the long-range transport of air masses by northly prevailing winds from emission sources located in continental areas north of Hong Kong. Particulate sulfate was strongly associated with both the concentrations of water-soluble Cr, Fe, Co, Cu, Pb, and Mn and their fractional solubilities in fine aerosols, which implied that sulfate-driven acid processing likely played an important role in the dissolution of the water-insoluble forms for these six trace metals. These strong associations were due to sulfate providing both the acidic environment and liquid water reaction medium needed for the acid dissolution process. The goal of objective 3 was to provide new insights into the effect of aerosol acidity on the chemical transformation of aqueous organic aerosols during OH radical photooxidation. We focused on organic compounds commonly found in aqueous aerosols worldwide (phenolic compounds and carboxylic acids). As reported by Yang et al. (2021) and Yang et al. (2023), the aerosol pH, amount of inorganic nitrate, and the molecular structure of the phenolic compound influenced the reaction rates of phenolic compounds, products formed and light absorption properties. As reported by Lyu et al. (2023), the aerosol pH, amount of inorganic nitrate, and the carboxylic acid’s dissociated vs. undissociated forms combined to influence the carboxylic acid’s overall reactivity. Overall, findings from this project enhanced our fundamental understanding on the role of aerosol acidity in atmospheric processes that transform aerosol mass concentration and composition, which is crucial for the improvement of atmospheric models used in air quality policy formulation in Hong Kong and globally.

21304919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21304919.value: The PI have established new collaborations to study the human health effects of water-soluble trace transition metals by investigating their abilities to generate harmful reactive oxygen species in the respiratory tract. In addition, even though our study showed that Cu is one of the most abundant water-soluble trace metals in PM2.5 in Hong Kong (and potentially the GBA) due to the large abundances of urban sources of water-soluble Cu and the ease at which water-insoluble Cu is converted to its water-soluble forms, insufficient attention has been given to the roles of soluble Cu (and trace transition metals other than Fe) in aqueous organic aerosol chemistry and thus they are mostly not considered in atmospheric and air quality models. Towards this end, the PI plans to conduct comprehensive investigations on the roles of soluble Cu in influencing aqueous organic aerosol chemistry to address the gaps of our fundamental knowledge in this area.

21304919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21304919.value: Atmospheric aerosols are of huge concern to policymakers worldwide due to their adverse environmental and health effects. Formulating air quality policies to reduce aerosol pollution based on current atmospheric models is challenging due to knowledge gaps on how the properties of aerosols influence the evolution of their mass concentrations and composition in the atmosphere. In this study, we studied the effect of aerosol acidity, an important aerosol property, on two important atmospheric processes (conversion of water-insoluble trace metals to water-soluble forms in aerosols and the OH radical photooxidation of aqueous organic aerosols) and characterized the PM2.5 acidity in different locations in Hong Kong during the seasons. We found that the PM2.5 in Hong Kong are acidic and have high water content irrespective of the season and location due to the high particulate sulfate concentrations and high humidity. The high aerosol acidity and water content combine to enhance various acid-catalyzed and acid-base aqueous aerosol reactions, which accelerate the transformation of aerosol mass concentration and composition. Overall, findings from this project enhanced our fundamental understanding on the role of aerosol acidity in atmospheric processes, which is crucial for the improvement of atmospheric models used in air quality policy formulation in Hong Kong and globally.

21307019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21307019.value: LiNixCoyMnzO2 (NCM, 0 ≤ x, y, z ≤ 1) has been considered to dominate the cathode technology of future automotive industry due to its high capacity and low cost. Despite the excellent prospects, however, severe capacity degradation of NCM cathodes during operation has prevented this promising material from further success. The mechanism of capacity fading in NCMs remains controversial, and might be attributed to the structural changes as follows: intermixing of Li/Ni ions, re-arrangements of transition metal (TM: Ni, Co and Mn) ions, anisotropic volumetric changes and complex phase transformations at high voltage. Therefore, an in-depth understanding of the coupling between structural changes and capacity fading mechanism is of critical importance to the improvement of NCM cathodes. However, precisely determining the structural dynamics of NCMs over cycling is still a challenging task to date. This is due to the difficulty in distinguishing light (Li) and nearby (Mn, Co and Ni) elements for the conventional X-rays method. Here, we propose to investigate a series of important NCM cathode materials with advanced time-resolved synchrotron and neutron scattering techniques such as in situ diffraction, in situ pair distribution function (PDF) of total scattering, etc. The characterization limitations of X-ray could be complementarily overcome by neutron, and the combination of diffraction and PDF analysis will provide both long-range and short-range structural information simultaneously. Specifically, we will precisely determine the fine structural dynamics in NCM compounds, including Li/Ni migration kinetics, transition metal arranging kinetics, anisotropic lattice evolutions and phase transition behaviors via in situ scattering techniques. It is expected that a comprehensive insight into the severe capacity degradation of NCM cathode materials will be provided from structural point of view, which could offer important guidance to the improvement of NCM cathodes and be in turn cooperated into the battery design especially for electrical vehicle (EV) industry. 三元層狀材料(NCMs, 0 ≤ x, y, z ≤ 1)因能量密度高和成本比較低廉，被認為是未來電動車的主要正極材料。然NCMs具有嚴重的容量衰減問題，限制其進壹步的發展和應用。從結構變化的角度來看，引起NCMs容量衰減的因素主要包括以下幾個方面：Li/Ni的混排，過渡金屬離子的重排，各向異性的晶體結構變化和高電壓區間復雜的相轉變等。因此，深入地理解NCMs在循環過程中的晶體結構演變對NCMs材料的發展至關重要。然而，由於不同的表征技術存在其本征的技術短板，精確地表征NCMs材料中過渡金屬的長程有序排布和短程局域畸變是壹大技術挑戰。對於原位研究電極材料動態過程中的晶體結構變化，同步輻射和中子衍射技術是非常有效的表征手段。其中同步輻射能夠實時追蹤電極材料在脫嵌鋰過程中晶胞參數的動態變化行為。而中子散射技術可以探測較輕的元素（如Li），可以通過不同的中子散射長度來區分原子序數接近的過渡金屬元素（如Ni，Co和Mn），因而可有效研究NCMs的Li/Ni混排以及過渡金屬重排現象。基於此，本項目擬將先進的同步輻射和中子技術相結合，原位檢測NCMs材料在循環過程中的結構演變，包括Li/Ni混排、過渡金屬元素重排、各向異性的晶格演變和相轉變過程；再通過結合材料的靜態和動態變化，從結構演變的角度深入地研究NCMs的容量衰減機制。我們相信，本研究將為NCMs材料在動力電池領域的廣泛應用提供新的設計思路和理論指導。

21307019.label: Major findings and research outcome
21307019.value: 1. We have developed the technology of in-situ (synchrotron) XRD to observe the structural evolution of NCM cathodes during the process of cycling. And we investigated the coupling between anisotropic lattice evolutions and capacity fading in a series of important NCM cathodes [2, 16]. 2. Based on the improvements to in-situ test device, we developed high rate in-situ test technology [17, 18]. 3. We have developed in-situ (synchrotron) XRD technology into other materials, such as Li-rich materials [8], P2-type layered oxide materials for sodium ion batteries [5], LiCoO2 materials [14]. 4. Through the analysis of the results of in-situ tests, we developed a series of methods to stabilized the structure during the processes of charging and discharging, further to improve the electrochemical performance [13]. 5. We have developed the in-situ synchrotron and ex situ neutron PDF devices, and successfully observed the short-range disorders of NCM cathodes [4]. Moreover, the influence of precursors on Li/Ni intermixing and TM-ion arranging kinetics was proposed [7]. 6. By studying the connections between the short-range disorders and long-term performance, we found that the valence state of TM-ion is one of the most important factors. So the advanced technology of in-situ XANES test was developed to continuously monitor the valence state of TM-ion [12,19]. 7. We have designed some experiments for local structural changes, and summarized the application of PDF [3,6]. 8. We have further applied PDF to Li-rich materials [1] and P2-type cathode for sodium ion batteries [11]. 9. We have trained 2 postdocs and 3 students, and they developed a unique understanding of this field and structural evolution [9,10,15].

21307019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21307019.value: Our finding of this project can effectively observe the subtle changes in crystal structure with high spatial resolution, thus reveal the capacity fading mechanism in NCM cathode materials. These in-situ technologies can be further developed toward the high temporal resolution. In particular, ultrafast in-situ XAS technology is underway and may reveal important insights on what happens inside the material at the moment when the ions are inserted or extracted. Moreover, further application of in-situ technologies on commercial battery system, such pouch cell, cylindrical battery, and so on should also be considered, as our preliminary results have found that the in-situ scattering offered new advantages than conventional methods, which can help us better understand the causes of battery failure and solve practical problems.

21307019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21307019.value: In this project, we developed several in-situ scattering technologies, which helped reveal the structural dynamics and capacity fading mechanism in cathode materials. We successfully observed the subtle changes in crystal structure during the processes of charge and discharge. We have extended these technologies to different materials. We studied the relationship between the local structural evolution and electrochemical performance of cathode materials. We developed a series of methods to stabilized the structure, and further to improve the electrochemical performance. Overall, the outcome of this project may be useful for experiments aiming to probe the atomic-scale structural dynamics in electrode materials.

21307819.label: Project Objectives
21307819.value: (i) Develop imaging and spectroscopy protocols to elucidate the Electrode-Electrolyte Interface reactions for Lithium/Sodium ion Batteries in order to provide scientific guidance of the future improvement. (ii) Do systematically investigation of lithium dendrite or sodium metal growth and solid electrolyte formation. Real-time monitoring of electrochemical process will help us solve the dendrite and SEI problem effectively and finally improve the batteries’ cycling performance. (iii) In-situ observation of lithium/sodium metal reaction. 21307819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21307819.value: The Solid Electrolyte Interphase (SEI) plays a vital role in determining the charge transfer and electrochemical kinetics, and thus the power density and stability of a battery. It is known that the SEI is electronically insulating and ionically conductive. Diffusion of cations through the SEI and spatial variation of ionic conductivity leads to non-uniform nucleation density and higher probability of dendrite formation. A uniform and compact SEI that passivates the alkali metal surface effectively prevents the exposure of fresh metal to the electrolyte; without the protective layer, the metal can react with the electrolyte leading to low coulombic efficiency. The SEI may also prevent non-uniform ionic flux induced dendritic growth. However, an unstable SEI may result in continuous “cracking” and “healing” of the layer with irreversible capacity loss. Other studies, to some extent, have revealed the composition of SEI, ion transport behavior through SEI and their dearly stages of nucleation and growth,8 but not fully understood. SEI on lithium/sodium has not been fully experimentally established and enough challenged, and fundamental understanding is still needed to definitively determine what and how species are formed on the surface, and how applied potential and cycling influence it. The development of synchrotron and in situ techniques should help find the missing pieces of the SEI puzzle. To elucidate the real growth behavior and composition of SEI, we are going to utilize three pathways to accomplish our goal, as shown in Figure 3. Pathway 1, In-situ Characterizations using 3-titanium electrodes electrochemical liquid cell; Pathway 2, Ex-situ Characterizations using 3- titanium electrodes electrochemical liquid cell; Pathway 3, Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) Characterization using Swagelok T-cell. After complementary characterizations through Pathway 1, Pathway 2 and Pathway 3, we will summarize the dynamic Li metal/ Na metal deposition behavior and SEI formation, the obtained composition, structure and chemical information, and the chemical diffusion coefficients. Combine with simulation and theoretical calculations, we will propose the SEI model with new insight and understanding, which will benefit to Li/Na metal batteries, Li-air/Na-air and Li-S/Na-S batteries. 固体电解质界面（SEI）在确定电荷转移和电化学动力学以及电池的功率密度和稳定性方面起着至关重要的作用。已知SEI是电绝缘的和离子导电的。阳离子通过SEI的扩散和离子电导率的空间变化导致不均匀的成核密度和更高的枝晶形成概率。均匀紧凑的SEI钝化碱金属表面有效地防止新鲜金属暴露于电解质中；在没有保护层的情况下，金属可以与电解质反应，导致低的库仑效率。 SEI还可以防止不均匀的离子通量诱导的枝晶生长。然而，不稳定的SEI可导致层的连续“开裂”和“愈合”，具有不可逆的容量损失。其他研究揭示了SEI的组成，通过SEI的离子传输行为及其成核和生长的成熟阶段。 关于锂/钠的SEI还没有完全通过实验确定，仍然需要基本的理解来明确地确定物种在表面上形成的物质和方式，以及应用的潜力和循环如何影响它。同步辐射和原位技术的发展应该有助于找到SEI谜底的缺失部分。为了阐明SEI的实际生长行为和组成，我们将利用三种途径来实现我们的目标，如图3所示。途径1，使用3-钛电极电化学液体池的原位表征；途径2，使用3-钛电极电化学液体池的非原位表征；途径3，使用世伟洛克T电池的电化学阻抗谱（EIS）表征。通过途径1，途径2和途径3进行互补表征后，我们将总结动态Li金属/ Na金属沉积行为和SEI形成，获得的组成，结构和化学信息以及化学扩散系数。结合模拟和理论计算，我们将提出具有新见解和理解的SEI模型，这将有利于Li / Na金属电池，Li-air / Na-air和Li-S / Na-S电池。

21307819.label: Realisation of objectives
21307819.value: Fundamentally understanding the complex electrochemical reactions that are associated with energy devices (e.g., rechargeable batteries, fuel cells and electrolyzers) has attracted worldwide attention. In situ liquid cell transmission electron microscopy (TEM) offers opportunities to directly observe and analyze in-liquid specimens without the need for freezing or drying, which opens up a door for visualizing these complex electrochemical reactions at the nano scale in real time. The key to the success of this technique lies in the design and fabrication of electrochemical liquid cells with thin but strong imaging windows. This protocol describes the detailed procedures of our established technique for the fabrication of such electrochemical liquid cells (~110 h). In addition, the protocol for the in situ TEM observation of electrochemical reactions by using the nanofabricated electrochemical liquid cell is also presented (2 h). We also show and analyze experimental results relating to the electrochemical reactions captured. We believe that this protocol will shed light on strategies for fabricating high-quality TEM liquid cells for probing dynamic electrochemical reactions in high resolution, providing a powerful research tool. This protocol requires access to a clean room equipped with specialized nanofabrication setups as well as TEM characterization equipment. The formation behaviors of LiF nanocrystals have been studied on anodes in Li-ion batteries; there is no research work reporting LiF crystal growth on cathodes. Here, we report a real-time LiF crystal formation on positively charged titanium (Ti) electrodes in an electrochemical liquid cell with 150-nm-thick Li hexafluorophosphate (LiPF6)/propylene carbonate (PC) liquid electrolyte loaded. The LiF nanocrystals show two-dimensional (2D) morphologies on the electrode surface, which can serve as a cathode electrolyte interface (CEI). Furthermore, the merging of LiF nanosheets was also observed, which may underlie the self-healing ability of LiF-based CEIs. Theoretical modeling indicates that there are two types of LiF formation paths on positive voltage-biased Ti electrodes. This work shows the remarkable morphing mobility and self-healing ability of LiF nanosheets and sheds light on strategies of modulating LiF nanocrystals and cathode surface chemistry for improving battery performance and cycle life. Na metal is an attractive anode material for rechargeable Na ion batteries, however, the dendritic growth of Na can cause serious safety issues. Along with modifications of solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI), engineering the electrode has been reported to be effective in suppressing Na dendritic growth, likely by reducing localized current density accumulation. However, fundamental understanding of Na growth at the nanoscale is still limited. Here, we report an in-situ study of Na electrodeposition in electrochemical liquid cells with the electrodes in different surface roughness, e.g., flat or sharp curvature. Real time observation using transmission electron microscopy (TEM) reveals the Na electrodeposition with remarkable details. Relatively large Na grains (in the micrometer scale) are achieved on the flat electrode surface. The local SEI thickness variations impact the growth rate, thus the morphology of individual grains. In contrast, small Na grains (in tens of nanometers) grow explosively on the electrode at the point with sharp curvature. The newly formed Na grains preferentially deposit at the base of existing grains close to the electrode. Further studies using continuum-based computational modeling suggest that the growth mode of an alkali metal (e.g. Na) is strongly influenced by the transport properties of SEI. Our direct observation of Na deposition in combination with the theoretical modeling provides insights for comprehensive understanding of electrode roughness and SEI effects on Na electrochemical deposition.

21307819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21307819.value: My research direction is designing advanced Electrochemical Liquid Cell on operando multimodal characterization of electrode electrolyte interfaces for next-generation energy applications. a) Based on my rich nanofabrication experiences of electrochemical liquid cell [Better TEM spatial resolution than commercial ones due to thinner liquid layer (150 nm vs 1000 nm), thinner SiNx imaging windows (35 nm vs 50 nm) than commercial products]3, we will further improve our electrochemical liquid cell design for revolutionary In-situ Liquid Phase TEM technique. b) Technical improvements: (i) 3-electrodes design instead of 2-electrodes design to provide a constant and defined potential; (ii) Graphene electrode fabrication instead of Ti & Au electrode to reduce the electron scattering and improve the special resolution; (iii) Indium spacer is removed to diminish side reactions from spacer; (iv) improved top & bottom cell assembly technique by using gel pack instead of water layer; (v) replace epoxy with UV glue to facilitate the bottom & top chip sealing manipulation; (vi) replace Cu cover with UV glue in reservoir area for improved liquid cell successful rates. c) Utilize in operando multimodal characterizations to elucidate the electrode-electrolyte interface reactions for battery, supercapacitor in order to provide scientific guidance for future improvement of energy storage.

21502219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21502219.value: Overqualification, a situation in which an individual’s qualifications, such as education,work experience, and skills, are beyond the requirements of the job (Erdogan & Bauer,2009; Maynard, Joseph, & Maynard, 2006), is prevalence in contemporary organizations. Our understanding of the outcomes of overqualification is inconclusive andbiased. Dominantly in the literature, overqualification has been considered as an undesirablephenomenon. Studies have shown that feelings of overqualification are negatively related to satisfaction with one’ job, commitment to the organization and positively associated with a desire to leave the company (for a review, see Harari, Manapragada, & Viswesvaran, 2017). Scholars, however, have begun to suggest although there are various drawbacks tooverqualification, overqualification may also provide positive outcomes foremployees and employers alike (e.g., Erdogan, Bauer, Peiro, & Truxillo, 2011). There isemerging evidence that feelings of overqualification may be linked to positiveconsequences such as proactive behaviors (Zhang, Law, & Lin, 2016), creativity (e.g.,Luksyte & Spitzmueller, 2016) and OCB (Lin, Law, & Zhou, 2017). Given the controversy in the existing literature, integrating capability-willingness-opportunity modeland minority influence model, we try to examine the implication of employeeoverqualification on extra-role behaviors, which will further affect employee careeroutcomes. We propose a novel, multilevel model that posits (1) employee perceived overqualification interacts with organizational identification to predict extra-role behaviors (i.e., helping and voice behavior); (2) leader humility works as a considerable cross-level moderator; (2) extra-role behaviors further contribute to employee career outcomes, including promotability and leader emergence. We will examine these issues through a series of multimethod studies, combiningexperiments and longitudinal field surveys, and field experiments. This research projecthighlights the moderating roles of employee organizational identification and leaderhumility in affecting the implication of employee overqualification on extra-role behaviorsand career development, thereby shedding light on organizations’ and employee’s effortsto reduce the adverse outcomes and harvest the bright side of overqualification. 員工資質過剩，或者說是員工個人的教育、技能、或工作經驗等資質超過了工作要求(Erdogan & Bauer, 2009; Maynard, Joseph, & Maynard, 2006)，在現當代企業組織中是很普遍的現象。我們對員工資質過剩所帶來的影響的認識還很有限並一定程度上是有所偏頗的。文獻中的主流思想是員工資質過剩是不好的，與之相對應地，一些研究結果表明員工資質過剩感與對工作的滿意度及對組織的承諾感負相關，且與離開組織的意願正相關(Harari, Manapragada, & Viswesvaran, 2017)。然而，也有學者提出，儘管可能有種種弊端，資質過剩亦可能為員工或僱主帶來積極的結果(例如，Erdogan, Bauer, Peiro, & Truxillo, 2011)。近年來一些研究證據顯示，資質過剩感可能會產生一些積極結果，如主動行為(Zhang, Law, & Lin, 2016)，創造力(e.g., Luksyte & Spitzmueller, 2016)，和組織公民行為(Lin, Law, & Zhou, 2017)。 鑒於現有文獻的爭議，我們試圖整合能力-意願-機會模型和少數派影響力模型以檢驗員工資質過剩對工作角色外行為的影響，並進一步如何影響員工的職業生涯結果。對此，我們提出了一個多水平模型，認為(1) 員工的資質過剩感與組織認同感交互影響角色外工作行為(助人行為和諫言行為); (2) 謙遜型領導是一個重要的調節因素; (3) 角色外工作行為進一步影響員工的職業生涯結果，包括可晉升性和非正式領導湧現。我們將通過結合現場實驗法與多輪問卷調查法來實證檢驗我們的研究模型。該研究突出了員工的組織認同感與領導者的謙遜型領導風格在員工資質過剩對角色外工作行為和職業發展的影響中所發揮的作用，從而進一步揭示了組織和員工如何減少資質過剩感帶來的不利影響而收穫可能的積極結果。

21504319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21504319.value: Social connections are an integral part of our lives. We constantly interact with close friends and family in real life and encounter reminders of them on social media (e.g., Facebook timeline) and marketing communications (e.g., “friends & family events”). Despite various benefits of social relationships, we explore the novel hypothesis that feeling socially connected decreases deliberation, or the amount of cognitive effort people invest in decision making. We base our hypothesis on prior works that show close relationships offer security (Bowlby, 1982), and argue that the sense of social connectedness can reduce cognitive vigilance, or alertness, leading people to reduce cognitive effort and deliberate less. Our project adds to the consumer research on social influence and cognitive functioning. It also offers implications on improving consumer decision quality in an increasingly connected world. 社交連結是我們生活中不可或缺的一部分。在現實生活中，我們會經常與親密的朋友及家人互動，而且在社交媒體（例如，Facebook Timeline）及行銷傳播平台（例如，「朋友及家人活動」）上亦會發現他們的最新狀態。社交關係會帶來諸多好處，不過我們研究了一種新的設想，即這樣的社交連結會讓人們不再那麼審慎，做決定時亦減少了在認知上的投入。我們的設想是根據過往的研究，即親密關係會帶來安全感（Bowlby，1982 年），社交連結可以降低認知警覺性或警惕性，從而使人們在認知上減少投入，不再那麼審慎。我們的項目新增了針對社會影響及認知功能的消費者研究。它亦可以在連結日益密切的世界中提高消費者決策水平。

21505519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21505519.value: Firms today collect an abundant amount of customer data from various sources, and use this data to target their customers with a high precision. Therefore, it is important that firms know how much, as well as which types, of customer data they should use for targeted advertising. In this research, we analyze a game-theoretic model to identify the value of customer data of different types, and thereby provide practical guidelines for firms’ optimal targeting strategy. We consider two types of customer data: category-preference and brand-preference information. These two distinct types of data have theoretically contrasting implications. The first type of data, such as a history of the search keyword laptop computers, indicates attractiveness of a consumer for all firms in a product category, and thus intensifies competition. On the other hand, the second type of data, such as the search keyword Lenovo laptop computers, reveals consumers’ preferred brand, and therefore softens competition. By analyzing the opposing competitive effects, we will uncover how firms should design their targeting strategy based on different types of customer data. Our firm-side analysis is complemented by the consumer-side analysis. In particular, we analyze a model of consumer search in which consumers can draw information from targeted advertising and consequently become interested in the product category even though they had no prior interests. Then, consumers can collect more information by searching other firms in the category and decide from which firm to make a purchase. This implies that there is an important tradeoff in each firm’s advertising efforts. On the one hand, a firm’s investment in advertising induces consumers’ interests in the product category from which the firm can benefit. On the other hand, it induces consumer search for other firms which can benefit other firms. We analyze this main tradeoff in advertising through the consumer-side in order to identify the equilibrium strategy of targeted advertising. This research will make significant theoretical and practical contributions. Theoretically, this research will improve upon the literature in targeted advertising by exploring “how much” as well as “which type” of information used in targeted advertising. Practically, the equilibrium advertising strategy, which accounts for the main competitive effects, will help firms thrive in competition through advertising. Lastly, the research will address concerns of regulators about data privacy. By separately identifying the value of different types of data in targeted advertising, we will discuss which data is more prone to data breach. 現今的企業會從不同的途徑來大量收集消費者的數據，並會運用這些數據以準確地定位他們的客人。因此，當使用目標式廣告，企業必需清楚知道他們要搜集多少和哪些類型顧客的數據。本研究將透過分析博奕理論模式來分辨不同類型客戶數據的價值，從而給予企業一些最佳目標市場策略的實用指引。 本研究考慮兩種類型的客戶數據：(i)種類偏好 (ii)品牌偏好。理論上，這兩種數據具有截然不同的的含意。第一類型的數據例如透過搜索關鍵字歷史筆記型電腦，來反映不同品牌在同一樣產品系列上對消費者的吸引力，從而加劇了競爭。另一方面，第二類型的數據例如輸入聯想筆記型電腦的搜索關鍵字，以反映顧客的品牌偏好，從而緩和了競爭。透過分析競争效應，我們便會發現企業如何根據不同類型的客戶數據去制定其定位策略。 公司方面的分析需靠消費者分析的補充，本研究分析了消費者的搜索關鍵字歷史。由於消費者通常透過目標式廣告獲取資訊，因此他們會對相關的產品種類產生興趣，即使消費者以前對該產品種類沒有興趣。然後，消費者可搜索其他品牌的相關產品種類，從而獲取更多資訊來決定光顧那個品牌。這意味着每間公司的廣告都有權衡關係。在一方面，企業希望透過投資廣告以引起消費者對產品種類的興趣，從而令企業得益。另一方面，廣告亦能促使消費者搜索其他公司的相關資訊，令其他企業得益。因此，本研究會從消費者角度分析企業廣告的主要權衡關係，從而分辨目標式廣告的均勢策略。 本研究將會作出重大的理論和實際貢獻。在理論上，本研究會透過探索目標廣告中使用“多少”和“哪種類型”的信息來增進目標式廣告中的文獻。在實際上，主要造成競爭效應的均衡廣告策略會協助企業透過廣告來提升競爭力。最後，研究將會解決監管機構對數據隱私的顧慮。是次研究亦會透過分析不同種類的數據對目標式廣告的價值，以討論那一種數據較容易引起數據外洩。

21505919.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21505919.value: 會計準則的均衡分析及有關經濟增長的監管執行

21505919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21505919.value: In this proposed study, I argue that an important difference between well-developed and less-developed economies is the efficiency of financial reporting standards in conjunction with regulatory enforcement. Financial reporting standards play a critical role in capital allocation across firms in an economy. Over time, an economy accumulates wealth, which can be reallocated to productive activities, thereby promoting economic growth and prosperity. As a result, economic activities affected by financial reporting standards in previous periods have a lingering effect on future periods. To capture this idea, I propose a dynamic general equilibrium model of accounting standards and regulatory enforcement. The presence of financial reporting manipulation interrupts efficient capital allocation across firms, thereby lowering contemporaneous economic activities and aggregate wealth in an economy. I will show that financial reporting manipulation in one period not only lowers the contemporary economic performance but also interferes with the course of the economic growth process from that point forward. The dynamic general equilibrium approach in this proposed study will make it possible to analyze the magnitude of macroeconomic consequences of investment, consumption, and welfare and thus better assess the impact of accounting policies. The main contributions of the proposed study are as follows. First, this study will contribute to the literature on accounting standards and enforcement by analyzing macroeconomic outcomes in a multi-firm setting. For policy-makers, a full assessment of accounting standards requires understanding aggregate outcomes and interactions among different stakeholders in an economy. The general equilibrium approach will allow me to analyze the macroeconomic consequences of accounting standards, thereby enabling the assessment and promotion of desirable accounting policies. Second, this study will also contribute to the earnings management literature by identifying a dynamic linkage between corporate fraud and future economic activities. In this proposed study, manipulated accounting reports bequeath a negative externality to subsequent generations by reducing accumulated wealth in an economy, which can lower economic activities (investment) from the next period onwards. That is, a corrupt economy accumulates less wealth and induces slower growth. Lastly, this proposed study has the potential to contribute to the literature on the role of accounting policies in economic growth. By analyzing the dynamic general equilibrium under different accounting policies, this study will highlight that financial reporting plays a critical role in the course of economic growth through capital allocation and accumulation over time.

21507119.label: Project Objectives

Publish the resulting paper in a top 3 finance journal

21507119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21507119.value: This project seeks to understand the role of labor separations, i.e., worker quits and firm fires, played in shaping asset prices. It is typically overlooked in the labor-asset pricing literature. For aggregate level studies, e.g., Merz and Yashiv (2007) and Petrosky-Nadeau, Zhang and Kuehn (2018), they assume that the labor separation rate is constant. For firm level studies, e.g., Belo, Lin, and Bazdresch (2014) and Kuehn, Simutin, and Wang (2014), they assume that the quit rate is constant. But in reality, the labor separation rate is time-varying: the quit rate is procyclical and the firing rate is countercyclical. In this project, I am among the first to document the empirical relationships between separation rates, i.e., the quit rate and the firing rate, and stock returns by running predictive regressions. Because the equity risk premium is countercyclical, I hypothesize that the quit rate negatively predicts stock returns, while the firing rate positively predict stock returns. Then I will build a business cycle model with on-the-job search in the labor market to rationalize the empirical relationships, while allowing the model to jointly account for labor market dynamics and asset prices. Importantly, I will highlight how the workers’ quitting decisions are informative about risk premium, which complements the focus of previous literature on the firms’ hiring decisions. Intuitively, the workers’ quitting decisions, like the firms’ hiring decisions, are forward-looking and respond to shocks to discount rates. When discount rates decrease, the marginal benefit of searching for a higher-wage job will be higher. Workers will search more intensively and the quit rate today will be higher. Therefore, the quit rate will be negatively associated with future stock returns. 該項目旨在了解勞動力分離，即工人辭職和公司解僱，在塑造資產價格方面發揮的作用。它通常在勞動力-資產定價文獻中被忽視。對經濟整體層面的研究而言，例如Merz和Yashiv（2007）以及Petrosky-Nadeau，Zhang和Kuehn（2018），他們假設勞動力分離率是恆定的。對公司層面的研究而言，例如Belo，Lin和Bazdresch（2014）以及Kuehn，Simutin和Wang（2014），他們假設辭職率是恆定的。但實際上，勞動力分離率是隨時間變化的：辭職率是順經濟週期的，而解僱率是逆經濟週期的。在這個項目中，我是第一個通過運用預測回歸分析來記錄分離率（即辭職率和解僱率）與股票收益之間的實證關係的人。由於股票風險溢價是逆週期的，我猜想辭職率負向預測股票收益率，而解僱率正向預測股票收益率。然後，我會建立一個包含允許在職工人尋找新工作的勞動力市場的商業周期模型，以使分離率與股票收益之間的實證關係合理化，同時允許模型解釋勞動力市場動態和資產價格。重要的是，我將重點介紹工人的辭職決策如何提供有關風險溢價的信息。這對以前文獻著重於公司的招聘決策是一個補充。直觀地說，工人的辭職決策，如同公司的招聘決策，具有前瞻性，會隨貼現率的變化而變化。當貼現率下降時，尋找高薪工作的邊際收益會更高。在職工人將更加努力地尋找新工作，今天的辭職率會更高。因此，辭職率與未來的股票收益率會負相關。

21507119.label: Realisation of objectives
21507119.value: Due to the intrinsic difficulty (both theoretically and computationally) to incorporate on-the-job search into business cycle models, we have simplified the model, abstracted away on-the-job search, and focused on job search decisions of unemployed workers. To be consistent with the model analysis, we have focused on the search intensity of unemployed workers for the empirical analysis. For objective 1, we find that unemployed workers' efforts to search for jobs (i.e., search intensity) negatively predict future stock returns across both short and long horizons in the empirical data, consistent with the intuition that lower search intensity is associated with higher discount rates. Notably, even after accounting for other labor-related return predictors such as unemployment, job vacancies, labor market tightness, and employment growth, search intensity remains a robust and significant predictor, especially in longer horizons. This result highlights the value of incorporating search intensity as an additional information source from the labor market, enhancing the predictive power of existing labor-related indicators in forecasting stock market returns. We have further investigated what drives job search decisions of unemployed workers through a variance decomposition. We take an asset pricing view of job search and decompose the variation in the dividend-price ratio of job search into a discount-rate component and a cash-flow component. We find that the variation in the dividend-price ratio of job search is mainly driven by discount rates, with little contribution from expected cash flows. In fact, discount rates more than 100% of the variation. We show that this is because discount rates and expected cash flows are positively correlated and the discount rate force dominates the cash flow force in the model. For objective 2, we augment the textbook Diamond-Mortensen-Pissarides (DMP) labor search model (Diamond (1982); Mortensen (1982); and Pissarides (1985)) with two key ingredients including variable search intensity, following Pissarides (2000) and recursive utility for the representative agent, as outlined in Petrosky-Nadeau, Zhang, and Kuehn (2018). We find that the model can jointly account for labor market dynamics and asset prices. We further investigate the quantitative impact of variable search intensity on output and consumption fluctuations, labor market volatilities, rare disaster risks, and asset prices. Our calibrated structural model indicates that variable search intensity amplifies the responses of quantities and asset prices to aggregate total factor productivity shock. We show that search intensity negatively predicts stock market returns in the model, aligned with the data.

21507119.label: Major findings and research outcome
21507119.value: 1. Theoretically Finding: Theoretically, we establish an equivalence result that equates the return of finding a job for an unemployed worker to the equity return of the firm that hires the same worker. 2. Quantitative Findings: We investigate the quantitative impact of variable search intensity on output and consumption fluctuations, labor market volatilities, rare disaster risks, and asset prices. Our calibrated structural model indicates that variable search intensity amplifies the responses of quantities and asset prices to aggregate total factor productivity shock. We show that search intensity negatively predicts stock market returns in the model, aligned with the data. In addition, through a variance decomposition, we show that the variation in the job search decisions of unemployed workers is mainly driven by discount rates, with little contribution from expected cash flows. 3. Empirical Findings: We show that search intensity negatively predicts future stock returns across both short and long horizons in both our baseline model and the empirical data. Notably, even after accounting for other labor-related return predictors such as unemployment, job vacancies, labor market tightness, and employment growth, search intensity remains a robust and significant predictor, especially in longer horizons. This result highlights the value of incorporating search intensity as an additional information source from the labor market, enhancing the predictive power of existing labor-related indicators in forecasting stock market returns. 4. Research Outcome We have written a working paper titled “search intensity and asset prices”. We have presented this paper in several international conferences. We will submit the paper to a top finance journal soon.

21507119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21507119.value: For future research, we can extend the model to allow for labor heterogeneities, such as high-skilled labor versus low-skilled labor. We can study how search intensities of different types of workers affect stock returns.

21507119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21507119.value: In this project, we study how unemployed workers' efforts to search for jobs (i.e., search intensity) are linked to stock returns. First, we show theoretically that the return of finding a job for an unemployed worker is the same as the stock return of the firm that hires the same worker. Second, we show that search intensity negatively predicts stock market returns in the data. We build a model to capture this empirical fact. Third, we show that search intensity provides additional information from the labor market for forecasting stock market returns. Our paper is the first to study the relationship between search intensity and stock returns and to establish the theoretical equivalence between the search return and the stock return. Our paper highlights that search intensity contains useful information for predicting stock market and financial markets in general. It is valuable for both academic researchers and financial practitioners.

21507519.label: Project Objectives
21507519.value: We will develop a multi-period dynamic general equilibrium model, which can address a wide range of asset pricing puzzles and which can also reproduce the formation and eventual burst of asset bubbles. After we calibrate the model to market data, we will assess whether and to what extent it can also address other asset pricing puzzles. We will also develop a Matlab program which will numerically solve our dynamic optimization problem. We will use this program to cross-check our analytical results. We will use market data to calibrate our model, thereby our project will also provide an estimate of the representative agent's aspiration level process and the strength of her preference for satisfying her aspiration. Eventually, we will write a paper with our results publishable in a top-tier journal in finance or economics.
