21507519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21507519.value: 在本研究項目中，我們分析一個具有願望水平效用的動態消費投資問題。代理人不僅從中間消費中獲得效用，而且能夠從實現預定的消費水平中獲得效用（我們將其稱為願望水平）。 該願望水平是內生確定的而且隨時間變化。我們的初步分析表示，最優性條件可以以封閉解的形式推導出來。其次，我們將框架擴展為一般均衡模型。此擴展使我們能夠根據市場數據校準模型，並研究願望水平型效用對資產定價的影響。 根據我們初步分析，本模型可以解釋幾個資產定價難題，並且解釋資產泡沫的形成和最終爆發。 首先，為了達到願望水平，代理人一般傾向減少投資（具風險的）證券。這將為股權溢價之謎提供解釋。 其次，即使代理人無條件遵循更保守的投資策略，其願意接受的風險水平仍然取決於時間和狀態。在某些狀態下，為了確保下一期有足夠的財富實現願望水平，“轉移至安全投資 “並減少投資證券是最佳選擇。在其他狀態下，代理人實現自己願望水平的唯一途徑是提高投資證券。這種最優投資組合的比例變化將導致更高的收益波動率，從而為過度波動難題提供解決方案。 最優投資策略的時間和狀態依賴性 不僅會增加收益波動率，還會導致時變的風險溢價。 反過來說, 也能夠解釋股票收益的可預測性 我們的模型不僅可以解決上述的資產定價難題，還展示資產泡沫的周期性內生形成及其最終破裂。當代理人提高願望水平時，她（他）需要承擔越來越多的風險。將導致資產價格越來越高。當代理人不能再為自己的高願望水平提供資金之後，她（他)會將大部分財富投入貨幣市場賬戶（轉移至安全投資）從而導致一次性的效用損失，導致 資產價格急劇下降（泡沫破裂）。然後，這個過程將會重新開始。

21507519.label: Realisation of objectives
21507519.value: We are glad to report that all of our project objectives have been successfully achieved. Furthermore, the Research Assistant whom we hired for the project, Bowen Du, has in the meantime successfully obtained his Ph.D. degree, and he has been hired as an Assistant Professor (tenure track) at Hunan University. Below, we address the above-listed five Project Objectives in more details. 1. As per the Project Objective No. 1, we have successfully developed a multi-period dynamic general equilibrium model. For the details of our model, please see Section 2 of our paper. For the general equilibrium implications of our model, please see Section 3 (Equilibrium asset prices). As the Project Objective mentions, our model can address a wide range of asset pricing puzzles and financial market phenomena, namely: equity premium puzzle, risk-free rate puzzle (including a time-varying but stable risk-free rate), excess volatility puzzle, return predictability (by the dividend-price ratio), weak negative autocorrelation of stock market returns, strong positive autocorrelation of the price-dividend ratio, highly volatile price-dividend ratio, stochastic stock market risk premium, stochastic volatility of the stock market return, occasional negative expected stock market excess return. For a demonstration that our model addresses these puzzles and financial market features, please see Table 3 and other parts of Section 5. 2. We successfully calibrated our model to market data. For details, please see Section 4 (Empirical analysis). We also managed to explain an additional asset pricing puzzle with our model beyond the ones which we originally had in mind. Namely, we found that our model not only generates a time-varying equity risk premium, but this model-implied equty risk premium is occasionally negative. This is an empirical fact which is documented in the literature, and our model can provide a theoretical foundation (explanation) for this. For details, please see the last part of Section 5.7 (Conditional expected excess returns). 3. As the Project Objective mentions, we successfully developed a MatLab program which solves our model numerically. Since submitting the Midterm Report, we managed to substantially improve the performance of our code mostly (but not exclusively) by applying a fixed-point iteration method to numerically determine the equilibrium price-dividend ratio function. For details on our numerical solution technique, please see Section 5.1 (Solution procedure). For examples on numerically determined price-dividend ratio functions under different aspiraton preference parameter values, please see Figure 1 (Model-implied price-dividend ratios). 4. As the Project Objective states, we calibrate our model to market data. For details on the market data, please see Section 4.1 (Data). The databases from which these data were obtained (CRSP and OptionMetrics) were provided by the PI’s institution (City University of Hong Kong, Department of Economics and Finance), no additional funding was required for this purpose. Furthermore, some of the data have been collected from sources which are available online for free (e.g., the 1-year Treasury Bill Secondary Market Rates were collected from the website of the St. Louis Fed). As the Project Objective states, we provide an estimate of the representative agent’s aspiration level process and the strength of her preference for satisfying her aspiration. For our aspiration preference process, please see equation (10) in Section 5.1. For the strength of the agent’s preference for satisfying her aspiration, we found a parameter value of α ̃= 0.45 provides the best match. We find that with the AR(1) specification of the aspiration level process (10) and with an aspiration preference parameter value of α ̃= 0.45 our model is able to explain several asset pricing puzzles and financial market features simultaneously. For the statistics implied by this aspiration level process specification and aspiration preference parameter value, please see the last column of Table 3. (For comparision, we provide the empirical statistics in the first column of the same table.) For comparisons of the effects of different aspiration parameter values, please see Tables 4-7 and Figures 1-6. For the interpretation of the aspiration preference parameter α ̃, please see Section 2, especially equation (3) and the connecting explanation. 5. Please find the paper attached. We have circulated it among our colleagues and we have collected feedback from them, which we have incorporated in the most recent version of the paper. Now, we plan to submit the paper to a top-tier journal in finance.

21507519.label: Major findings and research outcome
21507519.value: We develop a consumption-based asset pricing model with novel preferences. In our model, the representative agent derives utility not only from a consumption stream, but also directly from the performance of her financial portfolio. Our model can generate a highly volatile stock market return and excess return with stochastic mean and stochastic volatility, and a time-varying risk-free rate. The means and standard deviations of the returns and of the excess return implied by our model match closely their empirical counterparts. Our stock market return exhibits weak negative autocorrelation over the medium and long run, and it can be predicted by the dividend yield. Furthermore, our model-implied price-dividend ratio is highly volatile and exhibits strong positive autocorrelation.

21507519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21507519.value: As of now, we consider our project complete. We will now submit our paper to a top-tier journal, and if the referee(s) and/or the editor(s) request any further analysis, we will perform them accordingly.

21507519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21507519.value: Certain aspects of the beavior of financial markets cannot be explained by standard models. For example, the stock market return tends to be high when earlier the dividend-to-price ratio was high. Standard models do not explain why this is the case. There are many other features of financial markets for which standard models provide no explanations. In our research project, we challange the standard assumption that investors care only about their consumption. In our model, investors obtain utility not only from consumption, but also from the performance of their financial portfolio. For example, if their ambition is to achieve a 5% return on their financial portfolio and eventually they obtain only a 3% return, then they realize disutility. We find that the fact that investors care not only about their eventual consumption but also directly about the performance of their financial portfolio (for other reasons than consumption) can explain many features of financial markets. For example, besides the above-mentioned return predictability, it can explain why the risk-free interest rate changes from time to time, why sometimes the risk-free rate is higher than the expected stock market return, why certain times the stock market is more volatile than other times, and so on.

21603019.label: Realisation of objectives
21603019.value: I. The PI has managed to accomplish most of the intended research objectives despite a lot of challenges resulted from the Covid-19 pandemic. On Objective 1, with the help of a mainland-based assistant, the PI has collected over 30,000 pages of municipal government records between the 1920s and 1930s, maps and old photos of Canton from late 1800s to early 1900s, and Chinese and English newspaper articles. This part of the objective was completed as planned. The PI also took several field visits and conducted interviews to collect oral history. This part of the objective was less accomplished than planned. This was due to the traveling restriction for most of the proposed period of research (more details later). The PI also planned to explore other textual materials. However, due to the pandemic, the PI did not have enough time to finish this task. On Objective 2, the PI has finished the analysis of primary sources of the iron bridge project. The analysis was drafted as an article, first presented in an International Conference (see C9.1) that received good feedback and is currently under revision into a journal article to be submitted to a high-ranked peer-review journal (C8.4). The PI has also analysed the primary data of the tramline and cemetery conversion projects. Meanwhile, the PI has investigated the toilet reform project and developed two articles. Earlier drafts of one article (in collaboration with Dr. Santos) were presented as invited talks, and a journal article is under revision based on audience feedback (C8.7). The article (in collaboration with Dr. Ling) is under development. Its abstract has been included in a panel that has been submitted to an international conference (C8.6). This objective is accomplished as planned. On Objectives 3 and 4, the PI has explored how building infrastructure and constructing political power were intertwined, and examined how new political categories, rationalities and techniques regarding urban governance had emerged over time in Republican Canton in the above-mentioned infrastructural projects. On Objective 5, the PI has been developing the analytical framework for the study of social, political, and material transformation through the lens of infrastructural processes. Part of the deliberation were used in exploring infrastructural politics in articles not directly on Republican-period Canton (C8.1, 8.2 & 8.3). Meanwhile, the PI is conceiving a book manuscript on the formation of the urban in Canton. The part of the work has made satisfactory progress. On Objective 6, the PI has presented interim research results in one international conference specializing in mobility in 2023 (C9.1), and submitted the abstract of the toilet project to another international conference (AAS-in-Asia) in 2024 (C8.6). The PI is working on two articles (C8.7 and C9.1) that will be submitted to high-impact, peer-review journals, and is working on the outline of the book manuscript. The part of the work is slower than planned. II. Reasons for under-achievement. The ECS project was drafted in 2018. Research objectives, research design and activities were planned according to the research conditions in 2018. The project was granted the ECS fund in the summer of 2019. Research methodologies included primarily collecting archival data, supplemented by oral history collection, in the city of Guangzhou in Guangdong province, China. Research activities would be carried out between January 2020 and December 2022. When the funded project just started, the Covid-19 pandemic struck the world. Mainland China closed the national borders in early 2020, and such closure remained in place until the beginning of 2023. Meanwhile, Hong Kong government also carried out strict border control. In addition, the PI’s home institution, City University of Hong Kong also had regulations that restricted faculty’s moving across the borders. In 2020 and 2021, the PI had requested for work leave in order to carry out research work in Guangzhou. However, City University of Hong Kong rejected both requests. In 2022, while it was not impossible to enter mainland China from Hong Kong, there were quarantine requirements. The quarantine time for border-crossing outsiders was at least 21 days, with the risk of extended medical quarantine in case of the researcher infected with Covid-19 (subjected to daily testing). However, the PI had only 28 days of special leave to conduct research outside Hong Kong according to City University of Hong Kong’s regulations. As a result, the PI was not able to travel to mainland China for research work or to attend international conferences between 2020 and 2022 (except for the beginning of January 2020). During 2023 (the one-year extension of the project; more later), the PI was offered a visiting fellowship, funded by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research, Germany, for a three-month academic exchange. The PI spent three months of the summertime (from late May to late August) at the Universität Würzburg in Germany. While the PI benefited tremendously from the discussions with Sinologists in the host institute to develop the paper on the iron bridge and urbanization, the PI was not able to conduct archival research in person in Guangzhou in the summer when the PI did not have to teach; nor did the PI have enough time to examine the primary sources more thoroughly. Another unexpected challenge is that some of the senior interviewees, whom the PI knew from previous research, passed away during the pandemic, especially at the end of 2022 when the pandemic measures were suddenly removed in mainland China. The PI had to identify new interviewees, who have living experience in the first half of the twentieth century. In addition to collect archival data in mainland China, the PI had also tried to identify relevant sources online. However, the Canton government records are not accessible outside of China. On the other hand, mainland government’s tightened control of information on the Internet also made it difficult to search for information online. Some of the sources such as Guangzhou wenshi ziliao, which used to be easily searchable on the Internet and downable in Hong Kong, were no longer available. III. Efforts to overcome problems The PI has made substantial efforts to overcome the abovementioned problems. First, the PI had requested project extension for three times. A six-month extension was granted by City University of Hong Kong and another six months was granted by RGC. The third extension request was rejected. With the project extended until December 2023, the PI was able to take a few research trips, identifying primary sources, re-connecting with previous interviewers, and conducted a few oral history interviews. Second, a mainland-based research assistant was hired to help collect archival data. While the assistant’s work was often interrupted due to mobility control and testing during the pandemic period, the assistant has collected over 30,000 pages of government records and newspaper articles. The pandemic had greatly affected the deployment of this project. Nonetheless, the PI managed to accomplish most of the intended objective.

21603019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21603019.value: This project is about social, political and material transformation. By making sense of the efforts to rebuild the political system and to initiate social change through re-organizing space, this project seeks to unravel how social transformation is made tangible and durable. It does so by using an anthropological approach to study the historical development of urban governance in Canton (Guangzhou) in China in the early twentieth century (Republican period). In imperial China there was no urban administration despite the long history of walled cities. The Republican era witnessed a dramatic reconfiguration of the socio-political landscape including the rise of municipal governments. Yet, the process through which the language, rationality and techniques of urban governance took root and took shape, important as it is, has not been fully explored in the existing literature. Drawing on insights from the studies of governance and material power in the social sciences, this project develops an innovative approach to urban transformation in Republican China. With anthropological sensitivity to unravel a historical process, it will enrich our understanding of the complex entanglement between infrastructure, infrastructural power and political order, and contribute to develop an analytical framework for the study of social and urban transformation.

21603419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21603419.value: My project will examine a major company’s experimentation over several decades with the legal distinction between ‘employment’ and ‘independent contracting’. For about 30 years, the package delivery company FedEx litigated the issue of whether its drivers were ‘employees’, as the drivers claimed (and customers likely assumed), or ‘independent contractors’, as FedEx claimed. The distinction mattered, because the law affords important benefits only to ‘employees’, including the right to unionize. FedEx responded to adverse legal findings by making changes in the drivers’ work relationships to track the decisions. Judges responded by rejecting or validating FedEx’s changes as evidence of independent contracting. This project will advance our understanding of (1) legal notions of employment and independent contracting; and (2) ‘legal endogeneity’, or how law and organizational practice shape one another. Who counts as an employee is a pressing question in labour law and relevant to other regulatory fields, including competition law. FedEx had deep pockets and a commitment to perfecting its business model, making the litigation a strategic site for investigating changes in legal notions of employment, autonomy at work, and entrepreneurialism. The project will also illuminate debates over the labour law obligations of digital platforms, companies that use mobile applications or websites to connect customers with workers or sellers. The exceptionalism often imputed to digital technology does not explain the contours of these debates. FedEx prefigured many of the practices of digital platforms; its uniformed, ‘entrepreneurial’ delivery driver presaged today’s trope of the worker with a smartphone and car as an ‘entrepreneur’. I hypothesize that it is not only work relationships and technology that have changed, but also legal notions about what it means to be in business for oneself. The project will also further research on how organizations seek to shape the laws that govern them. Legal endogeneity theory suggests that judges look to organizational practices for cues about the meaning of vague legal standards and sometimes defer to those practices as evidence of compliance. I hypothesize that, through its construction and representation of workplace practices, FedEx subtly changed the meaning of legal concepts, like ‘property’, that regulated its relationship with drivers. The case-study method should advance our understanding of legal endogeneity by revealing judicial countermoves in addition to judicial deference. The subject of employment status also introduces a new dynamic into legal endogeneity research—company attempts to represent work relationships in contradictory ways to customers, workers, and legal decision makers.

21603719.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21603719.value: 信仰與利益之網：中日之間的佛教商人，838-1403

21603719.label: Project Objectives
21603719.value: To show the composition of Buddhist traders in Sino-Japanese trade and their changing roles over time. In particular, to demonstrate the importance of Buddhist traders in maritime East Asia, not only from commercial but also from cultural and diplomatic perspectives. To explore materials regarding Buddhist trade from many non-official records, including monastic records, correspondence between monks, pilgrim monks’ diaries, and collected works of Chinese literati who used to serve maritime positions. To investigate the mechanism of Buddhist trade, especially in forming partnerships, drawing contracts, and using credit; and to summarize the common terms and methods of phrasing used by the Buddhists to disguise the nature of their commercial activities. To fill the gap in studies of cross-cultural trade and trade between coreligionists by exploring the relationship between religion and commerce in East Asia, joining conversation with scholars whose work concentrates on Jewish and Muslim traders. To illustrate how religio-commercial networks took shape and to show how those networks could provide new understandings of Sino-Japanese relations. To show how commodities flowed and personal exchanges occurred via religio-commercial networks and to identify the characteristics of these networks. To use religio-commercial networks and an interdisciplinary method to reveal unrecorded maritime trade routes in East Asia, such as the trade routes connecting Japan, Korean peninsula, and the Kitan Liao dynasty in Northeast Asia in the eleventh century.

21603719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21603719.value: After the last Japanese embassy sailed to Tang dynasty China in 838, no official diplomats from Japan visited China until 1403, when the Ashikaga bakufu dispatched a delegation to the Ming dynasty to resume formal diplomatic relations. During this half millennium, monks and merchants from both China and Japan not only sustained but also furthered their communication across East Asian waters. Buddhist trade—the commercial exchange of objects for Buddhist uses, with monks and monasteries as participants—occupied a prominent position in Sino-Japanese trade between 838 and 1403. Previous scholarship has shown that the flows of commodities and personnel between China and Japan continued even after Japan had stopped paying tribute to China (Mori 1975; von Vershuer 2006; Enomoto 2007). However, why did the monks and monasteries participate in the trade? What advantages did Buddhist figures and institutions enjoy in the long-distance trade? To answer these questions, this study will focus on Buddhist traders, including monks, merchants (who were also lay Buddhists), and monasteries. During this diplomatically closed era, Buddhist traders used their religious resources as an asset to bring in trade partners and cut down transaction costs. Furthermore, these religious networks supported trade networks and facilitated commercial and cultural exchanges between the continent and the archipelago. In contrast with previous scholarship, this study pays close attention to the mechanisms of trade to show how religious networks and commercial networks gradually became integrated. Trust, credit, and contract are all important factors in long-distance trade and Buddhist traders transformed the trust embedded in religious networks to credit to facilitate transactions. Moreover, both textual evidence—The Record of Constructing the Tenryūji Monastery (1342)—and archaeological evidence—such as the Sinan shipwreck in South Korean waters—show that Japanese monasteries cooperated with merchants to trade with China and that they made agreements on how to divide their profits after the voyage. By integrating textual materials, transmitted images and objects, and archaeological discoveries, this project uses “religio-commercial networks” as a framework to re-examine the relationships between East Asian countries. Meanwhile, with a focus on the relationship between commerce and Buddhism, this project will provide a new dimension for investigation of trade between coreligionists and cross-cultural trade. It will also join a broader conversation with European historians who work on Jewish and Muslim traders. 在最後一批遣唐使於838年駛向中國之後，一直到1403年足利義滿向明朝遣使以恢復外交前，之間將近六個世紀都未有官方使節由日本前往中國。但在這段時期，中日雙方的僧侶和商人不僅僅維持，甚至進一步推進了東亞的海域交流。 佛教貿易--即以僧侶和寺院為參與者、或對用於佛教的物品進行的商業交換--在838至1403年間的中日貿易中佔據了顯要地位。現有研究已揭示出在日本停止向中國朝貢後，中日間的人員與物品往來並未間斷.(Mori 1975;von Vershuer 2006; Enomoto 2007). 但是，僧侶和寺院為何要參與進貿易中？他們在長距離貿易中享有何種優勢？為了回答這些問題，本研究將重點關注佛教商人，包括僧侶，皈依佛教的商人，以及寺院。在這段外交相對閉鎖的時期，佛教商人們運用他們的宗教資源來結交貿易夥伴、降低貿易成本。同時，這些宗教網絡支撐了商貿網絡並促進了中日之間的商業、文化交流。 與現有研究不同，本研究將特別著眼於貿易機制，以呈現宗教網絡與商業網絡逐漸相疊合的過程。信用機制、契約等都是長距離貿易中的重要因素。佛教商人就將宗教網絡中人與人之間的信任運用到了獲取貿易中的信用額度上。同時，文字記錄--如天龍寺造營記--和考古發現--如新安沉船，都體現出日本寺院與商人合作，以和中國進行貿易，並且在出航前已達成如何分配貿易利潤的協議。 通過整合利用文字資料、圖像資料，與考古發現，本研究以“宗教-商業網絡”作為一個框架，重新審視歷史上的東亞國際關係。同時，由於對佛教與商業的關係有特別關注，本研究將為跨文化貿易和同文化貿易的比較研究提供一個新的考察側面。

21603719.label: Realisation of objectives
21603719.value: Every objective of this project has been successfully achieved, and the research outcome has been presented in my published monograph Networks of Faith and Profit: Monks, Merchants, and Exchanges between China and Japan, 839 - 1403 CE (Cambridge University Press, 2023) and my other journal articles and book chapters. To complete this project and achieve all the objectives, I have collected textual and visual materials from China and Japan and engaged with English, Chinese, and Japanese scholarships. I was planning to go on multiple field trips to southeast China and Japan, but the plan was severely disrupted by the Covid-19 pandemic, which lasted throughout most of the duration of my project. But fortunately, I was able to travel to Fukuoka in Japan and Quanzhou in China before the outbreak of the pandemic, and I managed to collect all the key sources via database search or purchasing books and museum catalogs from overseas. By exploring a large variety of non-governmental sources, such as poems and letters written by monks and merchants, transmitted images and objects, and archaeological discoveries, my book presents a vivid and dynamic East Asian maritime world—a world where noninstitutional measures and nontraditional policymakers (such as monks and merchants) played a prominent role in overseas exchange and foreign affairs. By investigating the mechanisms of Buddhist trade—including mechanisms of trust, forming of partnerships, the use of contracts, and the many measures adopted to cope with accidents, my work provides many points of comparison to the studies on Mediterranean trade and offers a new dimension to the studies of cross-cultural trade and trade between coreligionists. My work also showcases new interpretations of many Buddhist records by explicating the commercial activities of monks and monasteries, which are described in opaque and euphemistic terms. In this way, my work offers a new understanding of the relationship between Buddhism and commerce and shows that Buddhist monks were actively engaged in trade. The importance of monks and merchants in Sino-Japanese exchanges and the formation of the religio-commercial network have been clearly elaborated on in my monograph. I have also published some significant case studies as journal articles and book chapters. Some case studies specifically showcase the mechanism of the religio-commercial network, such as the significance of trust, while some case study highlights the circulation of a particular commodity, such as the folding fans.

21603719.label: Major findings and research outcome
21603719.value: I have in total published one English monograph, three English articles, one Chinese article, and one Chinese book chapter as the research output of this project. I have also published a short blog on the website of the Cambridge University Press and gave a talk on the podcast New Books Network to further promote my research findings. The major research findings can also be seen in the above-completed objects. To summarize: 1. Contrary to what many historians have written, the tributary system was not the only vehicle for foreign trade in pre-modern China. By focusing on the period between 839 and 1403, when Japan and China suspended their tribute relations, this study shows how much trade occurred outside the framework of the tribute trade. 2. Proposes the religio-commercial network as a new framework for examining foreign relations in traditional China, highlighting the role of non-traditional policymakers, such as private traders and religious figures. 3. Sheds light on the usually undocumented role of monks in maritime trade and demonstrates their deep ties to merchants. 4. With a focus on the relationship between commerce and Buddhism, this study not only shows Buddhist figures and institutions actively engaged in trade and international affairs, but also provides a new dimension for the investigation of trade between coreligionists living in different societies.

21603719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21603719.value: While conducting research for this project, I have noticed that the "Buddhist diplomacy" of the Chinese Yuan and Ming dynasties is worth further investigation. The authorities in the Yuan and Ming essentially held different opinions toward Buddhism, but they nonetheless both used the strategy of sending monks as diplomats to Japan. I plan to focus on several representative Buddhist diplomats and the development of a monastery that functioned as an official bureau on multiple occasions in my future research. That project will discuss the Yuan-Ming transition from both local and transnational perspectives. I plan to apply for research grants from Hong Kong and Japan for that project.

21603719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21603719.value: Between 839 and 1403 CE, there was a six-century lapse in diplomatic relations between present-day China and Japan. This hiatus in what is known as the tribute system has led to an assumption that there was little contact between the two countries in this period. This project debunks this assumption, arguing instead that a vibrant Sino-Japanese trade network flourished in this period as Buddhist monks and merchants fostered connections across maritime East Asia. Based on a close examination of sources in multiple languages, including poems and letters, transmitted images and objects, and archaeological discoveries, this project presents a vivid and dynamic picture of the East Asian maritime world. It shows how this Buddhist trade network operated outside of the framework of the tribute system and, through novel interpretations of Buddhist records, provides a new understanding of the relationship between Buddhism and commerce.

21604719.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21604719.value: 從「自我實現」的角度重新審視人權理論及其對“殘疾人權利公約”的應用

21604719.label: Project Objectives
21604719.value: This is the first ever project to explore the concepts of self-fulfilment and human flourishing in the context of international human rights law, theory and practice in a systematic way. Through a distinctive mix of a theoretical examination of the foundations of international human rights law, systematic literature reviews and an interdisciplinary analysis of legal and disability studies, the proposed project will generate knowledge about whether the concept of self-fulfilment: • offers an adequate moral basis for protecting the rights to human flourishing and individual development • can be institutionalised in human rights law through international conventions, domestic legislation and the interpretive practices of courts, tribunals and international treaty monitoring bodies • effectively protects persons with disabilities whose rights to human flourishing and personal development are particularly vulnerable to being compromised by the inadequacies of human rights instruments based on the concept of dignity.
rows: This is the first ever project to explore the concepts of self-fulfilment and human flourishing in the context of international human rights law, theory and practice in a systematic way. Through a distinctive mix of a theoretical examination of the foundations of international human rights law, systematic literature reviews and an interdisciplinary analysis of legal and disability studies, the proposed project will generate knowledge about whether the concept of self-fulfilment: • offers an adequate moral basis for protecting the rights to human flourishing and individual development
• can be institutionalised in human rights law through international conventions, domestic legislation and the interpretive practices of courts, tribunals and international treaty monitoring bodies

• effectively protects persons with disabilities whose rights to human flourishing and personal development are particularly vulnerable to being compromised by the inadequacies of human rights instruments based on the concept of dignity.

21604719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21604719.value: The proposed research will use an interpretive philosophical analysis of human rights theory, literature and legal instruments to argue that the concept of human fulfillment should displace (take primacy over) human dignity from the foundational role that it plays in human rights discourse and legislation relating to economic, social and cultural rights. This project is important because the concept of dignity appears inadequate to secure the rights to ‘human flourishing’ and individual development (through, for example, cultural activities, sports and leisure) that international legal instruments such as the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) require states to protect and advance. In addition to exploring the significance of ‘self-fulfilment’ to human rights theory, the research will consider its utility in international human rights law. This aspect of the research will examine questions such as, which state obligations should ensue on the basis of the concept of self-fulfilment, and how should they be institutionalised? Findings from this part of the research will engage with claims that self-fulfilment as a normative concept plays an exceptionally prominent role when it comes to the rights of persons with disabilities and consider how the concept should inform the articulation of concrete rights and obligations enshrined in the CRPD. Through a distinctive mix of a theoretical examination of the foundations of international human rights law, systematic literature reviews and interdisciplinary analysis of legal and disability studies, the proposed project will generate knowledge about whether the concept of self-fulfilment: • offers an adequate moral basis for protecting the rights relating to individual development and human flourishing • can be institutionalised in human rights law through international conventions, domestic legislation and the interpretive practices of courts, tribunals and international treaty monitoring bodies • effectively protects persons with disabilities whose rights to human flourishing and personal development are particularly vulnerable to being compromised by the inadequacies of human rights instruments based on the concept of dignity. 這項研究將使用解釋性哲學分析探討”自我實現”的概念應如何補充或取代”人類尊嚴”在人權話語和有關經濟，社會及文化權利的相關立法中所擔任的角色。這是因為“人性尊嚴”的概念似乎不足以支持和解釋聯合國殘疾人權利公約(“公約”)就保護和推進個人發展（例如通過參與文化，體育和休閒活動）的權利，以致相關的權利一直被國際社會忽視。故此，這項研究除了探索“自我實現”對人權理論的重要性外，也會探討哪些公約中列出的國家義務應在"自我實現"這概念為基礎上重新理解。

21604719.label: Realisation of objectives
21604719.value: Challenges and difficulties The project started in January 2019, shortly before the social movement erupted. In 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic struck. These two major events seriously affected academic work. During the pandemic, conferences were canceled which led to the inability to submit to papers to/present at conferences. The planned visit to the Burton Blatt Institute in the US was canceled. In addition, the PI has experienced personal difficulties losing two grandparents during the fifth wave of the COVID-19 outbreak. In June 2022, the PI submitted his resignation to step down from his position. The PI and CityU agreed that the PI should stay on as an unpaid member of staff under 31 Jan 2023. Despite so, on 2 September 2022, the Research Office of CityU requested the PI to stop his research for the project. PI’s requests to access research funds – including to hire research assistants to help complete this project – were denied. With limited resources, on 22 October 2022, the PI submitted one article, based on existing material he has on hand, to the Oxford Journal of Legal Studies (attached together with this completion report). With regret, the PI is unable to produce further research output. Objectives 1 and 3 are fully complete, while objective 2 is partially achieved. This project explained how the concept of self-fulfilment offers an adequate moral basis for protecting the rights to human flourishing and individual development. Surveying the multitude of literature and treatise that addresses dignity in human rights law, it observed that the notion of dignity that is prevalent in the human rights discourse is mostly defined in relation to negative aspects of human experience ie as resistance to forms of oppression, subordination and humiliation (I referred this as negative dignity). This seriously restricted the theoretical potential of dignity and thus the development of human rights law. For the notion of dignity to attain its full theoretical potential, one must acknowledge an aspect of dignity that both demands that dignity is respected and provides for the conditions that enable a sense of self-worth to be developed and nurtured. This requires an acknowledgment that a person is only able to acquire a sense of self-worth by attaining basic levels of physical and psychological well-being and being given the opportunity to lead a self-fulfilling life. The justifications for the above findings can be found in Maslow’s theory of human motivation and Nussbaum’s capability theory. Maslow’s theory visualizes the fundamentals of human needs through a pyramid. At the bottom of the pyramid, the most basic of all needs, lie physiological needs (eg food, water, and rest) and safety needs (eg the security of the body, of health, and of property). On top of these lie psychological needs: the need for love and belonging (friendship, family, sexual intimacy) and the need for esteem (self-esteem, confidence, achievement, respect for others). At the very pinnacle of the hierarchy of needs lies the category of self-actualisation, which includes innate needs for creativity, practical reason and conscientiousness. Only when these needs are satisfied, are individuals able to acquire a sense of self-worth. Nussbaum’s capabilities approach also considers conceptions of dignity with reference to innate human potential. The capabilities approach argues that the freedom to pursue one’s well-being is of fundamental importance. In turn, this freedom should be understood in terms of a person’s capability or opportunity to realise their human functioning, thereby to achieve well-being. I call the aspect of dignity that relates deeply to a person’s freedom to develop their abilities, talents, capacities, character and sense of worth, positive dignity. Positive dignity redresses the deficits of negative dignity by defining rights in relation to how a sense of self-worth may be cultivated. The right of a child to schooling and education is an example of a right based on positive dignity as it is integral to nurturing a child’s senses, imagination and thought, and practical reason, providing an understanding of the world and of world values that is necessary to the development of their personality and the fostering of a sense of self-respect and worth. The right of everyone to have access to and take part in cultural life is crucial to the development of sensory or multisensory experience (of vision, audio, touch, etc.) and to the fostering of creativity and imagination. The right to participate in sports could also be considered a right based on positive dignity because it allows individuals to shape their personality and character (by instilling in their conceptions of mutual respect, perseverance, collaboration and teamwork) and promotes a sense of affiliation and belonging. Similarly, the right to play for children ought to be considered fundamental to positive dignity; as children learn through play, they learn how to communicate ideas, to understand others through social interaction, paving the way to build deeper understanding and more powerful relationships. The right of persons with disabilities to be included in the community is central to their capacity for affiliation (or their need for belongingness) and of esteem (ie of equal respect). The above is particularly important for persons with disabilities, especially persons with profound cognitive or intellectual disabilities. In essence, positive dignity acknowledges that persons with profound cognitive or intellectual disabilities and individuals with impairments of multiple sensory modalities may too lead fulfilling lives. Their human capacities are not precluded by their bodily impairments. For instance, persons with severe intellectual disabilities are able to develop deep, caring relationships with their caregivers and this brings profoundly valuable and meaningful experiences to both the person and the carer(s). To be able to cultivate such relationships with another is a core human capacity (the capacity to affiliate), the exercise of which brings meaning to life. They too have emotions (another valuable human capacity) and are able to express their love, desire and other feelings, positive or negative (eg happiness, excitement, discontentment and disgust), despite the fact that they express themselves primarily through behaviour rather than words. A positive notion of dignity requires that they will not be arbitrarily separated from their carers or the environment in which they exercise their capacity to affiliate. Conversely, their capacity to forge and develop bonding with others should be encouraged by state policies and programmes promoting social inclusiveness. While the project clearly articulated how the concept of self-fulfilment can be institutionalised in human rights law through international conventions - eg through the right to education (Article 13 ICESCR; Article 28 CRC; Article 10 CEDAW; Article 24 CRPD), the right to take part in cultural life (Article 15(1)(a) ICESCR; Article 31(2) CRC; Article 13 CEDAW; Article 30 CRPD), the right to leisure (Article 31 CRC; Article 30(5)(c) CRPD), the right (of the child) to play (Article 31 CRC, Article 30(5)(c) CRPD), the right (of persons with disabilities) to be included in community (Article 19 CRPD), and the right to be supported in the exercise of legal capacity (Article 12(3) CRPD) – and projected examples of how such rights may be violated (on grounds that an individual is deprived of his opportunity to lead self-fulfilling lives), the project has yet to survey whether such reasonings have been deployed in adjudicative settings. Nevertheless, this is going to be a very important future research direction.

21604719.label: Major findings and research outcome
21604719.value: The research yielded important findings. First, it found that the notion of dignity that is prevalent in human right discourse has been defined too narrowly, which explains why it is easy to comprehend issues such as torture and restrictions on liberty as forms of human rights violations, while difficult to appreciate why the rights of individuals are violated when they are not given the opportunity to individual development. Second, it successfully articulated a way to conceptualise self-fulfilment as an integral part of dignity, thereby positioning self-fulfilment as a core part of human rights. This is further done by (1) distinguishing two types of fulfilment, capacity and aspiration fulfilment, and clarifying that the notion of self-fulfilment that is to be advocated relates to the former and not the latter. Third, within the context of capacity fulfillment, it clarified that the concept of capacity is a matter of degree, ie it is not an all-of-nothing concept. This provided for the justification as to why persons with profound cognitive and/or intellectual disabilities too have rights to capacity fulfillment. Fourth, since capacity is a matter of degree, individuals are deemed to have capacities. From here, it developed a novel concept of residue capacity: one should not be deprived of the opportunity to exercise residue capacity, instead, the state should provide opportunities for one to develop capacity. Thus, eg for an adult person who suffers from dementia, his legal capacity should not be denied. Instead, resources should be invested to facilitate the exercise or development of his residue capacity, through forms of supported-decision making. Persons with intellectual disabilities too have residue capacities (such as affiliating and bonding with their caregivers) and thus their opportunity to do so should not be deprived (ie they should not be arbitrarily removed from the environment where they could foster their capacity to affiliate with others). On the contrary, resources should be given to facilitate the development of their capacity, by promoting inclusive environments. Lastly, it explained why the novel understanding further accommodates diverse forms of human flourishing that traditional conceptions of dignity are unable to secure. Eg it recognises that dignity through self-fulfilment is achieved often with the help of others and thus the important role that the community must sometimes play in providing the opportunity for individuals to thrive (a form of collective well-being). The above findings are contained in the article submitted (detailed in Part C).

21604719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21604719.value: The present research has much potential for further development. One research direction is to map and analyse how the notion of self-fulfillment is endorsed in domestic human rights decisions. For instance, in Whitney v California, 274 U.S. 357, 375 (1927), the Justice Louis Brandeis of the US Supreme Court once remarked ‘the final end of the state is to make men free to develop their faculties’. Another research direction is to examine how the notion of self-fulfillment and of ‘self-fulfilling rights’ may be applicable to articulating the rights of older persons. At the moment, the international community has been calling for an international human rights convention to be adopted addressing the rights of older persons, not least because of the aging global population. Articulating their right to self-fulfilment meant that they are not only entitled to rights not to be mistreated but that they also have the right to individual development which ought to be considered an important aspect of aging in dignity. A third research direction is to further the existing philosophical debate on dignity, including why persons with profound cognitive disabilities too have rights based on dignity despite that they may not have the capacity for moral reasoning.

21604719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21604719.value: Human rights offer emancipatory potential. However, this potential is restricted by a narrow construction of dignity upon which rights are often said to be based. The consequence is that human rights fail to deliver some of their express promises, including affording opportunities for individuals to develop their personality, character and talents to their fullest potential. This article offers a reconceptualisation of human rights based on the concept of positive dignity, arguing that individuals are entitled to ‘self-fulfilment’ rights, including the rights to education, culture, sports, (the rights of the child to) play, and (the rights of persons with disabilities to) supported-decision making and independent living. It argues that a person is only able to acquire dignity and a sense of self-worth by attaining basic levels of physical and psychological well-being and being given the opportunity to develop their human faculties.

21606219.label: Project Title(Chinese)
21606219.value: 大學寫作中心之讀寫實踐及學習

21606219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21606219.value: This research project investigates literacy as a social practice by focusing on an underresearched educational site: the university writing center. A writing center can play an important role in training and supporting university students in the development of their academic writing. The site of this study is a writing center at a university in Hong Kong whose goal is to help students become effective and independent writers in English. It offers students free one-to-one writing sessions. Students reserve a session in advance, and bring their writing assignments to the center at the appointed time. For 30 minutes, the student and a peer tutor work together on specific aspects of the student’s writing, using English as the medium of communication. For students for whom English is a second language (L2)—the vast majority of university students in Hong Kong in general, and the users of this writing center specifically—establishing understanding in the tutoring session itself may become a challenge. This raises an important question: How do the tutors and the students at the university writing center achieve mutual understanding when accomplishing their literacy tasks? Although many studies have investigated literacy practices in diverse institutions, there is a lack of empirical research that examines how L2 writing activities in a writing center evolve as social interaction, and how or whether the participants benefit from participating in them. To fill these gaps, this research project focuses on two key areas: (1) the interactional organization of the L2 writing consultations and the multimodal practices through which the participants accomplish the institutional agenda; and (2) the participants’ learning process during their involvement in the literacy events involved in the consultation, and changes in their practices over time. The project will use conversation analysis as an analytical approach. This analytic work will focus on what the participants say, how they say it, and what embodied or environmental resources they use in their achievement and maintenance of mutual understanding. By doing so, this study will result in a detailed description of how the participants engage in specific literacy practices while achieving the institutional agenda in an efficient and timely manner. The project will shed new light on literacy practices in educational institutions. The findings will be of use to students of English and their teachers around the world as well as for tutor training purposes at the center. 本研究從讀寫能力為一種約定俗成的社會實踐角度出發，來探討較少研究的教育地點：大學寫作中心。寫作中心可以在訓練及支援大學學生學術寫作的發展中扮演重要的角色。本研究位於香港一所大學之寫作中心；中心旨在透過提供學生免費的一對一寫作輔導課程，來幫助學生成為有效率且獨立的英語寫作者。學生事先預約輔導時間，並將他們的寫作帶至寫作中心。他們與一位同儕輔導在30分鐘裡利用英文來針對討論此學生的具體寫作方面。對於英語為第二語言的學生而言—包括絕大多數的香港大學學生，以及此寫作中心的使用者—在輔導過程中建立理解可能會是一大挑戰。此情形因而引發出一個重要的研究問題：同儕輔導與學生在大學寫作中心裡如何在完成讀寫任務中來達成相互理解的目標？即便許多研究已探討過不同機構裡的讀寫實務，實證性研究仍顯不足。此方面研究包括探究英語二語寫作活動在寫作中心裡如何演變為一種社會交流活動，以及參與者如何、或是否從參與的過程當中受益。本研究以補強研究不足的角度出發，著重於以下兩個關鍵領域：(1) 英語二語寫作輔導裡的互動結構，以及參與者用來完成機構議程所採用的多模式實踐。(2) 參與者在透過參與寫作輔導裡所包括的讀寫活動之學習過程、以及隨著時間所產生的讀寫實踐變化。 本研究將使用會話分析來作為分析方法。分析著重在參與者的談話內容、表達方式、以及他們在達到並維持相互理解所利用的具體或環境資源。本研究將詳細描述參與者如何在參與具體的讀寫實踐中同時完成機構議程。本研究將對於教育機構的讀寫實踐提供新的視角。研究結果將對於世界各地的英語學生與老師、以及寫作中心輔導人員培訓有所助益。

21609319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21609319.value: This project examines a key dilemma facing the developing world: How can governments enforce critical social and environmental policies, despite weak control over their bureaucracy? Traditionally, scholars have emphasized the need for rational, disciplined and meritocratic bureaucracies to overcome enforcement problems and prevent corruption (Bates 1981, Evans and Rauch 1999, Skocpol 1985). In recent years, China seems to be moving in the opposite direction, pursuing a combination of ad hoc campaigns, internal orders, and high-tech surveillance mechanisms to force through costly pollution control policies. This project assesses the impact of ad hoc governance on policy enforcement in China. Specifically, it explores the role of uncertainty as a method of bureaucratic control in weak institutional environments. Political scientists have long identified the use of uncertainty (in the form of unclear laws and unexplained arrests) as a low cost way for authoritarian regimes to scare citizens into self-policing (Crozier 1964, Scott 1990, O’Brien and Stern 2011). Based on recent interviews with local officials in China, I propose that the same strategy is being used within the Chinese state, to discipline bureaucrats into compliance. We see this in the rise of sudden campaigns (such as the anti-corruption campaign) or the use of impromptu commands (such the 2017 winter coal stove ban) to direct and control local bureaucrats’ behaviour. Focusing on recent pollution control campaigns, I will assess how “governance by uncertainty” has altered bureaucratic incentives to enforce environmental policies. Through a combination of interviews, case studies, and quantitative analysis of original data, I will evaluate whether the erosion of clear performance targets and stable reward mechanisms has strengthened or weakened local officials’ responsiveness to central leaders in China. Studies of Chinese politics have previously highlighted this flexible, ad hoc nature of party governance in China (Fewsmith 2011, Perry and Heilmann 2011, Zhi and Pearson 2017). However, these theories predict that ad hoc governance will make the regime more adaptable, because it encourages local officials to experiment with new tactics to accommodate limited institutional and fiscal resources. In contrast, this project builds on my earlier dissertation research to propose that uncertainty has made local officials more cautious, more conservative, and less capable of resolving China’s long-term policy challenges. Findings from this project will therefore contribute to broader scholarly debates on the limits of effective authoritarian governance, and may also challenge expectations that China’s party governance is becoming more routinized, law-based and resilient (Nathan 2003). 本項目探討在體制薄弱的環境下，不明確因素對監控官僚主義起的作用。政治學家早就發現利用涵義模糊的法規和特別監測是限制市民提出異議的低成本的措施。本研究查探中國中央領導是否在使用類似策略去解決政治體系內的委託代理問題 。就以近日突發的行動，如2016-2017年的全國全國環境保護督察，或特別專項政策方案推行，如2017年的《京津冀及周邊地區2017-2018年秋冬季大氣污染綜合治理攻堅行動方案》，屢見原先訂下的法治及績效指標遭受破壞的情況。本研究會以環境領域為主，编纂分析原有特別環境治理措施，並透過質性研究及訪談去剖析兩個研究問題：一】 為鼓勵官員去推行環境治理政策的明確健全獎勵制度，有否被削弱？二】 這些變化又如何改變了官僚機構對中央指令的反應？

21610019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21610019.value: In recent decades, many governments around the world have promoted voluntary environmental programs (VEPs) to encourage businesses to go beyond legal compliance and adopt progressive practices to minimize pollution emissions. In theory, VEPs complement the traditional mandatory regulations by reducing the administrative burden for regulators and allowing flexibility for regulatees. In reality, the effectiveness of VEPs can be hindered by inadequate monitoring and corporate opportunism. One central challenge is hence whether and how regulatees are interested in such policy endeavors and able to commit to the program obligations. Firms may be unwilling to enroll due to financial constraints, adopt the programs only symbolically, or exit because of programs’ ineffectiveness in improving environmental performance. Institutional complexities such as policy uncertainty and political turbulence can further undermine firm commitment. In China, where pollution control is now at the top of the government’s agenda, VEPs have a great potential to supplement the existing mandatory and market-based regulations. Nevertheless, we still know little about the determinants of regulatees’ interests and continual efforts in environmental self-regulation. The proposed project will address this gap by conducting a longitudinal and comparative investigation of firm exits from government-sponsored VEPs. It will apply the convergent insights of policy implementation and corporate environmental management to investigate the implementation of the Cleaner Production program—a flagship VEP in China. Specifically, the project will answer three important research questions: (1) How do organizational and industrial forces shape firm exits from government-sponsored VEPs? (2) How does regulatory and political complexity arise and moderate the organizational and industrial explanations of firm exits? (3) Under China’s decentralized policy implementation system, do regional and overtime variations in regulatory and political contexts affect the continuity of government-sponsored VEP? A mixed-method design will be adopted in the project. Archival data on policy implementation and firm participations will be collected in Guangdong province, with assistance from local environmental protection bureaus and the Cleaner Production Association. Semi-structured interviews with involved stakeholders in five major cities of the Pearl River Delta region will be conducted. This project will build on my earlier research on: (1) political commitment and policy uncertainty in China’s environmental governance, and (2) the diffusion of the Cleaner Production (CP) program in Guangzhou. By drawing on new and current data, the proposed research will provide significant insights into the theoretical development and practical implications of voluntary environmental governance. 近几十年来，世界各地的许多政府都推行了自愿性环境计划以鼓励企业超越环保法规的监管要求并积极采取措施以尽量减少污染排放。从理论上讲，自愿性环境计划可以通过减少监管机构的行政负担和加强监管的灵活性对传统强制性监管进行有效补充。但在实际操作中，监督不足和潜在的公司机会主义行为可能会阻碍其有效性。因此，自愿性环境计划的一个主要挑战在于被监管企业是否对此类政策感兴趣并且能够承担履行政策要求。考虑到成本等一系列因素，企业可能不愿意参与，或者只是像征性地采用这些计划，或者认为计划在改善环境绩效方面无效而退出。此外，政策不确定性和政治动荡等制度复杂性可能进一步削弱企业的参与。 在中国，污染控制现已成为政府议程的主要任务之一。自愿性环境计划对补充现有的强制性或以市场为出发点的环境监管体系有着巨大潜力。尽管如此，我们对于影响被监管企业的参与动力和持续努力的决定因素仍然知之甚少。本研究项目将通过对政府资助的自愿性环境计划中的企业退出行为进行纵向和比较研究来回答这一问题。基于政策实施和企业环境管理的理论整合，我将研究作为中国的一项最主要的自愿性环境计划“清洁生产计划”是如何实施的。具体而言，本项目旨在回答三个重要的研究问题：（1）组织和行业因素如何影响企业在政府赞助的自愿性环境计划中的退出行为？ （2）监管和政治复杂性如何产生并调节企业退出的组织和行业解释？3）在中国的分权政策实施体系下，监管和政治环境的区域差异是否会影响自愿性环境计划的连续性？在方法论上，本研究将采用混合方法设计。在当地环保局和清洁生产协会的协助下，我将在广东省收集一系列政策实施和企业参与的档案数据。此外，我计划对珠江三角洲地区五个主要城市的利益相关者进行半结构式访谈。该项目将建立在我早期的两项研究基础之上：其中一项旨在分析中国环境治理中的政治承诺和政策不确定性，另一项研究侧重于清洁生产项目在广州市的实施和扩散。通过整合分析已有的和新收集的数据，本研究将为自愿环境治理的理论发展和实际意义提供重要见解。

21610019.label: Realisation of objectives
21610019.value: The project objectives have been successfully achieved. We compiled three important datasets for analysis. First, in line with the objectives outlined in our grant proposal, we constructed a comprehensive dataset of firm exits from the Cleaner Production Partner (CPP) program at the city level. This was achieved by integrating various public databases and extracting detailed information from the official CPP program website, spanning 2009 to 2022. This dataset was complemented by several interviews conducted within Guangdong province with regulatory agencies, regulated firms, and service entities involved in the cleaner production initiative. Our second dataset was constructed to examine the implementation of the HK-Guangdong CPP program and how Hong Kong-based enterprises operating in the PRD region respond to this cross-border policy. This innovative dataset combines existing survey data on Hong Kong-based enterprises from 2014, with newly gathered data on voluntary participation in the CPP program from 2008 to the present. The final dataset has provided rich longitudinal insights. Our analysis reveals that institutional pressures from both the production sites and headquarters locations exert uneven influence on firms’ decisions to participate in cross-border environmental partnership initiatives. The third dataset significantly extends our original methodology, previously focused solely on Guangdong province and the Greater Bay Area. This dataset encompasses all CP industrial standards published by the Chinese government between 2003 and 2020. These standards, covering almost all manufacturing industries under environmental regulation in China, were collected from the National Standard Full-text Disclosure System (NDRC) website, and our review included the examination of the public comment process and other archival data such as news reports and speeches related to the drafting of these standards. With this dataset, we examine how stakeholder participation in rule drafting and public comments leads to high-quality voluntary environmental standards. Through the analysis of these comprehensive datasets, we refined our contingent model of firm exit from government-sponsored voluntary environmental programs (VEPs) (Objective 1) and explored the mechanisms behind firm exits (Objective 2). Our in-depth analysis of multi-dimensional and multi-source institutional pressures significantly enriched our understanding of the regulatory and political complexities of VEPs and their regional variations (Objective 3). Additionally, our investigation covered two flagship VEPs in Mainland China and Hong Kong, providing practical implications to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of voluntary environmental governance (Objective 4). High-quality publications were produced from this project, including two notable journal articles fully supported by the grant and three articles partially supported by the grant in RA recruitment and research collaborations.

21610019.label: Major findings and research outcome
21610019.value: The first major finding, centering on the role of third-party influences in VEPs, is derived from an in-depth analysis of the participation of regulatory entities in VEPs. Please refer to Liu (2021). Specifically, I introduced a novel component to the traditional conceptual framework that primarily addresses the regulator-regulated dyad. This study highlights the critical role of third-party influences in enhancing firm participation in VEPs, particularly under conditions of opacity and limited regulatory capacity. It demonstrates that firms inexperienced with voluntary programs are more likely to engage public intermediaries, especially when regulatory updates are anticipated frequently. This finding underscores the profound impact of regulatory complexity on the effectiveness of voluntary environmental governance. The second major insight addresses the complexities and dynamics of setting regulatory rules for VEP Standards. Please refer to Zhang, Liu, and Yuan (2024). We identified three pathways leading to high-quality voluntary environmental standards. Two of these pathways underscore the intricate nature of stakeholder participation in rule drafting, with the impact of firms highly contingent on the active involvement of other stakeholders, especially industry associations. The third identified pathway emphasizes the importance of public comments, particularly when stakeholder engagement in standard drafting is limited. The third major finding explores institutional explanations and contextual heterogeneity of cross-border VEP implementation. Our analysis reveals that while mimetic pressure from competitors in the same location increases a firm’s likelihood of participation, coercive pressures from both headquarters and production sites significantly enhance early involvement. Another working paper explores why firms exit VEPs despite apparent political and economic benefits. It highlights the critical role of local government actions and societal influence in maintaining firms' sustained participation in VEPs, affected significantly by the multiple cities they operate in, especially regarding government policy priorities, industrial emissions, and public opinion. Overall Implications Collectively, the findings from this project offer profound implications for both regulators and business managers involved in voluntary environmental governance in both Hong Kong and Mainland China. These insights range from understanding firms’ internal motivations to remain engaged with VEPs, firm responses to cross-border collaborative policies, the influence of third parties, to the complex contributions of stakeholders in effective VEP standard-making.

21610019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
21610019.value: We are now preparing two working papers for submission, targeting high-impact journals, which we believe will add novel insights to our findings and provide significant implications for both regulators and business managers in environmental governance. While our recent publications highlighted the role of stakeholder participation in VEP rule-setting, it was confined to one type of VEP. Expanding this research to encompass broader policy, institutional, and cultural contexts could provide insights into how complex rule-making processes affect various policy outcomes, which are prerequisites for satisfactory policy outcomes and sustainable industry participation in VEPs. Empirically, recent methodological advancements present opportunities to deepen both theoretical and empirical inquiries into VEPs. For instance, large language models could be trained to predict outcomes or simulate potential policy or stakeholder behavior changes under various voluntary program scenarios.

21610019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
21610019.value: Voluntary programs are increasingly recognized as crucial tools alongside traditional regulations in various policy areas. These programs encourage organizations to self-regulate, reducing the workload for regulators and providing flexibility to those being regulated. Particularly in environmental governance, voluntary programs are instrumental in reducing pollution and supporting the transition to greener practices. Our project collects comprehensive data to understand how effective VEP rule-making can be achieved through stakeholder engagement in China and local government policy efforts and business responses within flagship VEPs in the Greater Bay area. Using a cross-regional and cross-industrial approach, we integrated diverse data sources to provide an in-depth analysis. Our findings help delineate the design and implementation of VEPs through the lens of stakeholder engagement, collaborative governance, and regulatory compliance. Specifically, we unraveled (a) how institutional forces interact with organizational and industrial dynamics and (b) the variability at the firm, industry, and regional levels in utilizing and benefiting from these regulatory tools. This research not only enriches academic literature by shedding light on the complexities and dynamics of VEPs but also offers valuable insights for policymakers and business managers navigating the evolving landscape of sustainable development.

21614719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
21614719.value: East Asia is undergoing a progressive degradation of agricultural land on its fringes and in between megacities. In these peri-urban areas, the expansion of unregulated, urban-oriented activities produces contamination of soil and the pollution of water resources, threatening the health of local populations and ecosystems. While these regions are central in the global process of urbanization, and their populations are expected to grow by one hundred million people over the next decade, there are still no governmental plans or comprehensive strategies to halt environmental degradation and prevent associated threats to expanding populations. After undertaking several years of research and fieldwork I have hypothesized that in peri-urban areas: (1) top-down flood control schemes employing stream channelization cause significant degradation of both sociocultural and biophysical aspects of riparian agriculture creating favorable conditions for the expansion of unregulated urban-oriented activities; (2) and that stream renaturation can generate a partial recovery of riparian degraded landscapes, fostering bottom-up farming, land care, as well as reconstructing a sense of belonging to watercourses. Multimethod research is herein adopted with a focus on two cases located in Hong Kong’s New Territories, combining spatial and social analysis of the process of degradation and recovery of agriculture, while analyzing its dynamic association with hydrologic transformations. This proposed research will employ a quantitative analysis of land use change and morphological transformation of streams over the last five decades, using historical aerial photographs. Concurrently, the research will investigate the sociocultural aspects of the alteration of the hydrologic regimes through archival research and in-depth interviews with local farmers. Sources of secondary data are the Drainage Service Department and local archives. The proposed triangulation of methods aims both at a broader understanding of the phenomenon and cross verification. The proposed research will shed new light on the sociocultural and physical impacts of hydrologic modification. This study will contribute to the establishment of a more holistic approach to the management of water resources and stream renaturation through a higher integration of socially related factors. At the regional level, the proposal stresses the importance of establishing adaptive stormwater management frameworks, which enable a balanced rural-urban coexistence by preserving existing agroecosystems. At the local level, this research project will contribute to a better understanding of the causes of landscape degradation. 22103319.value: KIF9在腦膠質母細胞瘤進展和免疫治療中的作用

22103319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22103319.value: Glioblastoma is one of the most aggressive cancers that are highly malignant with limited surgical approaches due to its spread into surrounding areas of the brain diffusely. We have achieved highly promising preliminary data to believe that the protein KIF9 in the glioblastoma cells mediates the microglia enhanced glioblastoma cell invasion. Knockdown of this KIF9 protein in glioblastoma cells significantly slows down the disease progression of glioblastoma in vivo in multiple glioblastoma mouse models. Meantime, KIF9 has been reported to regulate macrophage activities, which suggests that KIF9 may also play a key role in regulating the macrophage-like microglia cells in the glioblastoma microenvironment. On the other hand, recent clinical trials have confirmed the effectiveness of immunotherapy, especially the immune checkpoint blockade therapy in treating glioblastoma. Thus, in this proposal, we will determine the role of KIF9 in remodeling the glioblastoma microenvironment including the tumor cells themselves and the microglia cells during the cytotoxic CD8+ T cell infiltration based immunotherapy. In detail, we will scrutinize the role of KIF9 in regulating glioblastoma cell spreading ex vivo and in vitro in our developed 3D spheroid cell co-culture and co-invasion system. We will also determine the role of KIF9 in regulating cell proliferation, cell-to-cell adhesion, inter-cell signaling, protein transport, etc. in both the tumor cells and the microglia cells (Objective 1). By employing multiple glioblastoma mouse models, we will further determine the role of KIF9 in glioblastoma invasion and proliferation and how it mediates the crosstalk between glioblastoma cells and microglia cells in vivo (Objective 2). Meanwhile, recent clinical trial results have reported very promising data on glioblastoma immunotherapy. Thus, to pave our way for the future “KIF9 blockade + immunotherapy” combo therapy to treat glioblastoma, we will further determine the role of KIF9 in regulating the glioblastoma microenvironment remodeling during immunotherapy in vivo, specifically the checkpoint blockade immunotherapy (Objective 3). The major goal of this study is to propose, evaluate and compare the Monotherapy of “KIF9 blockade” and the Combo therapy of “KIF9 blockade + immunotherapy” in treating glioblastoma.

22201419.value: Develop novel statistical model for IBD detection based on low allele frequency SNVs. The calculations for linkage disequilibrium and haplotype frequency for common variants are not appropriate to be applied to low allele frequency SNVs. The sequencing errors should be carefully considered due to their large impacts on the number of carriers of low allele frequency SNVs. Improve genetic studies by including disease manifestations from electronic health record (EHR). The information from HER is gold mine and could be used to refine the patients carrying the same IBD regions and better define the disease seed genes. Construct a computational framework to calculate disease-specific SNV pathogenicity score. A gap is left between gene function and disease pathology, previous algorithms only consider the impact of SNV to gene function, preventing their practical applications in clinical genetic testing. We aim to include both SNV pathogenicity score and gene functional similarities between variant altering and candidate genes. Build online system for geneticists and experts for genetic testing. A whole computational framework will be implemented in an online system, specialists can apply our model to their own projects with a click of a button.
