22201419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22201419.value: Many efforts have been made to investigate the role of single nucleotide variant (SNV) in human complex diseases. The identified disease susceptible common and rare SNVs can explain only a small proportion of disease heritability. Low allele frequency (LAF) SNV is another kind of variant that is not easy to be investigated because it requires a large sample size for association analysis or multiple families with similar manifestations for linkage analysis. The disease-associated LAF SNVs could be located in Identity-By-Descent (IBD) regions that are inherited from recent common ancestor and carried by sporadic patients. Extensive work has been done for IBD detection by common SNVs, losing the power from LAF SNVs to improve the sensitivity of detecting short IBD regions. In addition, previous tools only consider the effects of SNVs on gene functions rather than on particular diseases. Identifying which SNV in the IBD region is truly associated with the disease pose a substantial challenge. In this proposal, we plan to design a computational framework to prioritize disease-associated LAF SNVs from IBD regions. A novel statistical model is designed to detect IBD regions by making use of LAF SNVs from sporadic patients. For LAF SNVs, the calculation of haplotype frequency is influenced by sequencing errors substantially. Instead, the model assumes the haplotype is sampled from Bernoulli distribution and its parameter could be evaluated and updated by the observations from training and test sets. The model further finds a way to remove the influence of sequencing error in parameter estimation to avoid double counting of them. Our preliminary study proved the shared LAF SNVs were tended to be observed in IBD regions and hardly to be observed by random chance. The disease-specific impacts of LAF SNVs are evaluated by integrating gene functional weights and SNV pathogenicity scores. For each IBD region, we apply bi-clustering algorithm to identify the patients sharing the same disease manifestations, which are further used to calculate the susceptibilities of IBD regions by comparing with the number of carriers in controls. The disease seed genes are identified by examining patients’ manifestations and used to calculate gene functional weight, which is calculated by the functional similarities between SNV altering and disease seed genes. The gene functional weight is further integrated with SNV pathogenicity scores to calculate disease-specific SNV pathogenicity score. 近年來很多研究都在努力尋找與人類複雜疾病相關的單鹼基變異。但是先前研究中找到的常見和罕見基因組變異只能解釋复杂疾病中很小一部分遺傳度。除上述兩種變異之外，對另外一種可能與疾病相關的低頻變異則很少涉及，主要因為基於關聯分析的方法需要非常大的樣本量，而基於連鎖分析的方法則需要很多攜帶同一疾病表型的家系樣本。與疾病相關的低頻變異可能遺傳自同一祖先并存在於由病人共同攜帶的一段Identity-By-Descent (IBD)區域。針對這種情況很多研究都試圖利用常見變異尋找IBD區域，而忽略了低頻變異在檢測較短IBD區域中的貢獻。另外對於IBD區域中潛在的致病變異，之前的研究往往只檢測其對於基因功能的影響而忽略了基因與特定疾病表型的關係。如何在IBD區域中尋找與疾病表型關聯的低頻致病變異成為了巨大的挑戰。在本項目中，我們設計了一套計算模型用於在IBD區域中尋找低頻致病變異。對於低頻變異，測序錯誤會顯著影響單體型頻率的計算，為了解決這一問題我們假設單體型來自伯努利分佈，并設計統計模型從訓練集和測試集中學習參數並且該模型還可以進一步消除測序錯誤被重複計算的影響。前期實驗表明在IBD區域中會存在共有的低頻變異而這種情況很難在隨機狀況下出現。我們通過整合低頻變異對基因功能的影響以及該基因對疾病表型的影響來計算低頻變異對特定疾病表型的作用。對於每一個IBD區域，我們首先應用bi-clustering算法找到攜帶此IBD區域且具有相同疾病表型的病人，并通過與正常人中攜帶者數量對比找出顯著的IBD區域及攜帶者。然後根據疾病表型從數據庫中找出與此表型相關的“seed”基因并計算其與低頻變異所在基因的功能相似性作為權重。最後將該權重與低頻變異對基因功能的作用分數進行整合得到變異對特定疾病表型的影響分數。

22201419.label: Realisation of objectives
22201419.value: First, we implemented SILO a novel algorithm to detect long and short IBD segments by considering both common variants and LFVs (low-frequency variants). SILO employs an approach similar to that used by Parente2 to identify long IBD segments (e.g. lengths >= 2 cM) using common variants, but adapts the approach to detect short IBD segments using LFVs. SILO assumes that the probability of the presence of the minor allele of a LFV follows a Bernoulli distribution, with its parameter modeled by a Beta distribution. SILO implements a seed-and-extend algorithm to identify short IBD segments and implements a cleaning procedure to remove false positive IBD segments. SILO intrinsically considers the impacts of genotype errors. If the genotype error rates are high, SILO will put smaller weights on the observed genotypes and increase weights on other possible genotypes. We investigated the impacts of different genotype error rates on SILO. With a genotype error rate of 1%, SILO did not fully utilize the information from LFVs because there was a higher chance that the sharing of minor alleles of LFVs was attributed to genotype errors. Furthermore, it was observed that a genotype error rate of 0.1% could generally make SILO extract sufficient information from LFVs rather than regarding them as genotype errors and a genotype error rate of 0.001% was enough for SILO to fully utilize the information from LFVs. Second, we explored three categories of molecular biomarkers: 1. genomic variants (including SNVs [single nucleotide variants] and SVs [structural variants]), 2. cell-type composition, and 3. gut microbiota. These biomarkers are effective for categorizing patients and prioritizing genes that are likely to cause the disease. The polygenic risk score (PRS), which aggregates multiple risk alleles of SNVs of candidate diseases, has emerged as a standard approach for identifying high-risk individuals. We systematically validated and compared thirteen statistical methods, five machine learning models and two ensemble models using simulated data, twenty-two common diseases with internal training sets, four common diseases with external summary statistics and three common diseases for trans-ancestry studies in UK Biobank. For SVs, we developed Aquila_stLFR, an approach that resolves SVs through haplotype-based assembly of stLFR linked-reads. Aquila_stLFR partitions long fragment reads into two haplotype-specific blocks with the assistance of the high-quality reference genome, by taking advantage of the potential phasing ability of the linked-read itself. Each haplotype is then assembled independently, to achieve a complete diploid assembly to finally reconstruct the genome-wide SVs. AquilaDeepFilter is also developed to automatically filter false positive large deletions. It transforms sequencing data into an image and employs convolutional neural networks to enhance the classification of candidate deletions. To better explore cell-type composition from single-cell RNA-seq data (scRNA-seq), we have developed IGSimpute to impute missing values present in scRNA-seq data. IGSimpute recovers those missing values with an interpretable instance-wise gene selection layer. To optimize the algorithms used to decipher human gut microbiota, we developed Pangaea to improve metagenomic assembly on linked-reads, DeepMetaBin and METAMVGL to group assembly short contigs into metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and Deepurify to remove contaminations from the given MAGs. We developed Pangaea to improve metagenome assembly using short-reads with physical or virtual barcodes. It adopts a deep-learning-based binning algorithm to assemble the co-barcoded reads with similar sequence contexts and abundances to improve assemblies of high- and medium-abundance microbes. Pangaea also leverages a multi-thresholding reassembly strategy to refine assembly for low-abundance microbes. Moreover, DeepMetaBin is a contig binning method that combines short and long contigs using a graph-based Gaussian Mixture Variational Autoencoder (GMVAE). It begins by creating a k-nearest neighbor graph (k-NN) based on contig sequence composition features and removes noise nodes through clustering and label propagation. The refined k-NN incorporates edges as "must-links" to stabilize the embedding of short contigs in GMVAE. Contigs are then grouped into super clusters using a Gaussian Mixture Model in a low-dimensional space, and single-copy genes are used as "cannot-links" to aid in dividing these super clusters using constraint k-means. We also developed METAMVGL, a multi-view graph-based metagenomic contig binning algorithm by integrating both assembly and paired-end graphs. It could strikingly rescue the short contigs and correct the binning errors from dead ends. METAMVGL learns the two graphs’ weights automatically and predicts the contig labels in a uniform multi-view label propagation framework. We have introduced a novel decontamination approach named Deepurify, which utilizes a multi-modal deep language model employing contrastive learning to learn taxonomic similarities of genomic sequences. Deepurify utilizes inferred taxonomic lineages to guide the allocation of contigs into a MAG-separated tree and employs a tree traversal strategy for maximizing the total number of medium- and high-quality MAGs. Besides these molecular biomarkers, we have developed PRSIMD and Med-PRSIMD to integrate non-genetic factors to better stratify patients and define disease seed genes. We proposed a machine learning model called PRSIMD to integrate the genetic and non-genetic factors using posterior regularization for disease risk prediction. PRSIMD converts the PRS into posterior distribution using logistic regression and adopts log-linear model to aggregate non-genetic factors into prior knowledge distribution. PRSIMD employs Kullback-Leibler divergence as an additional loss to force the posterior distribution to approach the prior knowledge distribution in the training procedure. Additionally, we extended PRSIMD and proposed Med-PRSIMD, which exhibits robust scalability through the utilization of posterior regularization to integrate diverse data types, including genetic information, lifestyle factors, physical measurements, and medical history to predict disease risk scores. The causal language model pretraining module was adopted to train the transformer framework to generate potential event embeddings from medical history. Third, we developed DeepDRIM and dynDeepDRIM to prioritize SNV and genes based on the gene regulatory networks constructed from single-cell gene expression data. DeepDRIM is proposed to reconstruct cell-type-specific GRNs from scRNA-seq data with high precision and a low false positive rate. It converts joint gene expression of two genes into a two-dimensional histogram with 32 by 32 bins, indicating the number of cells falling within each bin. It then constructs 2n+2 neighbor images, where n refers to the number of genes, based on positive covariance with the two genes and self-images. Instead of using an augmented image, the neighbor images are organized as a tensor for improved performance. Two convolutional neural networks process the primary image and the neighbor image tensor. Network A follows VGGnet, while Network B is a siamese-like network designed for multiple neighbor images. These networks are trained using known TF-gene interactions from cell-type-specific ChIP-seq data and predict unknown interactions with confidence scores. We extended DeepDRIM and proposed dynDeepDRIM, a novel deep-learning model to reconstruct GRNs using time-course scRNA-seq data. It represents the joint expression of a gene pair as an image and utilizes the image of the target TF–gene pair and the ones of the potential neighbors to reconstruct GRNs from time-course scRNA-seq data. dynDeepDRIM can effectively remove the transitive TF–gene interactions by considering neighborhood context and model the gene expression dynamics using high-dimensional tensors. Fourth, we have shared the source codes of all algorithms we developed in github for this project. In addition, we have developed LRTK, a versatile toolkit for analyzing genomic data from both human genomes and metagenomes. It can be easily installed and utilized through simple commands, making it user-friendly for researchers and geneticists.

22201419.label: Major findings and research outcome
22201419.value: This project has made significant advancements in the field of identifying low-allele frequency genetic variants associated with human complex diseases. One notable achievement is the development of SILO, an algorithm capable of detecting both long and short IBD segments by considering common and low-frequency variants. In simulations, SILO outperformed other tools by achieving an F1 score 13 times higher for detecting short IBD segments ranging from 0.1 to 0.2 cM. Testing on real data from the 1000 Genomes Project revealed that SILO successfully identified short IBD segments that were previously overlooked. The project also explored the use of molecular biomarkers and non-genetic factors to predict disease risk, effectively distinguishing high-risk individuals within the general population. For SNVs, statistical methods demonstrated superiority in simulated data from additive models, while machine learning models showed advantages in handling genetic interactions. When it came to SVs, the combination of linked-read sequencing and deep learning models emerged as a cost-effective and accurate identification method, surpassing traditional short-read sequencing. Other innovations include the development of two deep learning models to fill in missing values in scRNA-seq data, enabling the discovery of molecular heterogeneity in complex diseases. The project also highlighted the significant variation in gut microbiota among patients. By employing a genome-based approach instead of gene-based methods, we develop three algorithms to improve microbial genome analysis and association studies in metagenome assembly and binning. The project also emphasized the importance of non-genetic factors such as lifestyles, lab tests, and medical histories in disease prediction and patient stratification. Additionally, the project developed DeepDRIM and dynDeepDRIM, two tools for reconstructing cell-type-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) using scRNA-seq data. By applying DeepDRIM to scRNA-seq data from B cells in patients with varying severities of COVID-19, the project discovered alterations in GRNs and identified transcription factor targets related to crucial processes like lysosome activity, apoptosis, and response to low oxygen levels, all of which are relevant to coronavirus infection. Furthermore, the project introduced LRTK, a versatile toolkit for analyzing genomic data from human genomes and metagenomes. LRTK is user-friendly, making it easily accessible for researchers and geneticists. The outcomes of this project have been published in 14 journal articles, including reputable journals like 'Microbiome' and 'Briefings in Bioinformatics.' Inspired by these findings, future research will delve deeper into the relationship between the human gut microbiome and complex diseases, with support from YCRG.

22201419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22201419.value: In the future, there is significant potential for advancing the precision of structural variant (SV) detection and further investigating the impact of human genomic variants on diseases. With the advent of the telomere-to-telomere human reference genomes, our comprehension of complex genomic regions has deepened. This advancement enables the detection of SVs in complex regions of the human genome, such as the highly polymorphic human HLA region and regions with segmental duplications. However, sequencing errors still present a substantial challenge in pinpointing the exact breakpoints of SVs on a population-wide scale. We plan to design an algorithm to construct a human pan-genome to enhance SV breakpoint refinement. Previous studies have demonstrated that genomic variations can influence the gene expression patterns and the composition of the human gut microbiota. More efforts could be directed toward analyzing spatial single-cell RNA sequencing data to unravel the spatial influence of genomic variants on cell type distributions. Furthermore, the dynamics between host genomic variants and the gut microbiota remain elusive. It is essential to conduct more in-depth research to understand this interplay and its implications for health and disease. Unraveling these complex interactions could provide new insights into personalized medicine and the development of targeted therapies.

22201419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22201419.value: In this project, we developed various algorithms to improve our understanding of genetic and non-genetic factors related to complex diseases. We developed an algorithm to detect identity-by-descent segments associated with diseases by considering both common and low-frequency genetic variants. It is designed to identify both short and long segments and takes into account the possibility of errors in genetic data. The project also explored different types of molecular biomarkers, including genomic variants, cell-type composition, and gut microbiota, which can help categorize patients and prioritize genes that may contribute to diseases. We validated and compared multiple statistical and machine learning methods to calculate polygenic risk scores. We developed a method that used linked-read sequencing to accurately identify structural variants. We developed tools to fill in missing data in single-cell RNA sequencing, to improve the analysis of gut microbiota, and to reconstruct gene regulatory networks from single-cell gene expression data. We also integrated genetic and non-genetic factors to better predict disease risks, and LRTK, a versatile toolkit for analyzing genomic data. This project has made significant advancements in understanding genetic factors associated with complex diseases and has provided valuable tools and algorithms for researchers and geneticists to further explore these areas.

22301719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22301719.value: RNA修飾影響細胞中的基因調節。最近發現了RNA修飾以促進癌症生長。例如，RNA修飾N6-甲基腺嘌呤（m6A）與膠質母細胞瘤（一種侵襲性腦癌）和急性髓性白血病（AML）的增殖有關。AML是一種快速發展的血癌。 當m6A去甲機酶FTO和ALKBH5的水平降低時，腫瘤進展顯示被抑制。這些發現為使用化學化合物來抑制ALKBH5和FTO開闢了抗癌治療的新機會。然而，我們目前沒有有效和有選擇性的抑製劑用於臨床研究。 我們假設用小分子抑製劑抑制m6A去甲機酶將實現抗癌作用。為了驗證我們的假設，我們提出了一種結合化學和結構生物學的跨學科方法來開發FTO和ALKBH5抑製劑。在我們的方法中，我們使用蛋白晶體學來闡明原子水平的抑製劑和蛋白的結合模式。然後，我們使用結構數據來指導下一代抑製劑的設計，然後在體外和體內進一步研究。 我們以前報導了第一個基於結構的FTO抑制研究，以及人類ALKBH5的新結構。根據報導的結果，我們在晶體結構的指導下設計了第二代FTO抑製劑。我們的初步數據顯示我們成功地（a）設計了具有改善效力的第二代FTO抑製劑，（b）通過晶體學確認其結合模式，和（c）在非目標細胞系中顯示低毒性。在這項提議的研究中，我們將使用經過測試的基於結構的方法進一步優化這些第二代抑製劑，以開發臨床相關的FTO和ALKBH5抑製劑。第三代抑製劑將在體外和體內驗證。 此擬議的研究為通過調節RNA修飾以治療癌症的新方法鋪路。該研究將有助於各種人類疾病的基礎健康研究和藥物開發，因為RNA修飾具有廣泛的生理效應，包括發育和病毒複製。

22301719.label: Realisation of objectives
22301719.value: Objective 1: We successfully designed and synthesized a total of 13 compounds. 7 of the compounds have higher potencies against FTO than the parent pyridinyl glycinamide compound (4). This work was performed in collaboration with Prof. Christopher Schofield’s group, University of Oxford. Our inhibitor design strategy was based on two crystal structures of FTO in complex with a pyridinyl glycinamide (4) and an anthraquinone rhein respectively. We designed a series of 4 inhibitors by aryl functionalisation of the C-6 of the pyridinyl ring, resulting in compounds that are predicted to bind across the 2-oxoglutarate (2OG) cosubstrate and m6A nucleobase substrate binding sites. Two of the compounds (13b containing a biphenyl at C6, and 13c containing a napthyl at C6) showed improved potencies when compared to the parent pyridinyl glycinamide compound. 13c was the most potent in the series. A crystal structure of FTO-13c complex was then determined (see objective 2) and used for subsequent rational inhibitor optimisation. We evaluated these inhibitors against 10 other 2OG oxygenases. The inhibitors showed general selectivity for FTO. Subsequently, we used the structure of FTO-13c to design a new series of inhibitors containing a heteroatom N between the pyridinyl ring and its C6-substituents. 9 compounds from this series were synthesized and majority of the compounds from the new series displayed enhanced potencies in vitro against FTO when compared with series 13. 14a, which contains a nitrophenyl group in its side chain was the most potent compound (IC50 = 80 nM). When tested against other 2OG oxygenases, this compound only weakly inhibited FIH and JmjC histone demethylases and possessed a 30-fold selectivity for FTO over PHD2. We also tested 14a against ALKBH5, another m6A demethylase. 14a showed a 900-fold selectivity for FTO over ALKBH5. Our efforts to design ALKBH5 inhibitors have been hampered by the lack of crystal structures of ALKBH5 in complex with inhibitor scaffolds (see Objective 2 for alternative developments on ALKBH5). We initiated docking studies of ALKBH5 using reported crystal structures of ALKBH5 to screen for potential inhibitors from compound databases (in collaboration with Prof. Guobo Li, Sichuan University). However, the top hits identified by computational studies did not show significant inhibition when tested in vitro using a MALDI-based single-point demethylation assay. Objective 2: We successfully determined two structures of FTO in complex with two most potent inhibitors, 13c and 14a respectively. We used the structures to confirm inhibitor binding modes, rationalise inhibitor strengths and design next generation inhibitors. We first determined a crystal structure of FTO in complex with 13c to 2.6 Å resolution. 13c binds in FTO by occupying both the 2OG and substrate binding sites. As designed, the pyridinyl glycinamide portion occupies the 2OG binding site, chelating the catalytic metal, while the 1-naphthyl side chain occupies the nucleobase substrate binding site. This structure was then used to rationally design series 14 inhibitors, of which 14a was discovered to be the most potent against FTO. We also successfully determined a crystal structure of FTO in complex with 14a (resolution 2.6 Å). 14a also binds across the 2OG and substrate binding sites. However, its nitrophenyl side chain does not positioned in between the sidechains of Tyr106 and Tyr108 as designed. Notably, the heteroatom N connecting the aryl side chain and pyridinyl ring can form a hydrogen bond with the side chain of Arg322, potentially explaining its increase in potency. 14a is also observed to displace the side chain of Glu234, which plays a role in substrate binding (Zhang et al. PNAS 2019). The two structures of FTO in complex with two different potent inhibitors from two different series were used to rationalise inhibitory strengths and selectivity of compounds in the two respective series. To perform structure-based ALKBH5 inhibitor design, we attempted to reproduce crystals of apo-ALKBH5 and ALKBH5 in complex with 2OG or generic inhibitor NOG based on reported conditions. However, these attempts were unsuccessful. In 2019, a crystal structure of an FTO variant in complex with a 6meA-containing ssDNA was reported. However, a structure of ALKBH5-substrate complex has not been determined despite structures of ALKBH5 without substrate being reported since 2014. To understand the difference in substrate binding between ALKBH5 and FTO, which could aid selective inhibitor design, we attempted to crystallise ALKBH5 in complex with an 8-mer m6A-containing ssRNA. What ensued was a significant alternative development of the project. We were able to obtain high quality crystals of the complexes of ALKBH5-m6A RNA, ALKBH5-2OG-m6A RNA, and ALKBH5-NOG-m6A RNA. We determined their structures by X-ray crystallography. These structures provided unprecedented insights into the mechanisms of substrate binding and m6A demethylation by ALKBH5, including 1) ssRNA binds in an opposite 5’-3’ direction, 2) ALKBH5 recognises G/Am6AC consensus motif, 3) ALKBH5 catalyses fragmentation of N6-hydroxymethyladenosine (hm6A) via a proton shuttle. These observations allowed us to understand the differences between ALKBH5 and FTO, especially why ALKBH5 only produces adenosine (A) as product while FTO produces A, hm6A, and N6-formyladenosine (f6A). These results also imply that FTO and ALKBH5 have different biological targets and are associated with different cancer profiles. Importantly, the discovered differences could aid future selective inhibitor design. Objective 3: We evaluated the biological activity of 14a and the methylester derivative of 14a (14aMe) in A573 melanoma and MDA-MB-31 breast cancer cell lines (in collaboration with Prof. Zhiling Yu, HKBU). 14aMe showed higher cytotoxicity against both cancer cell lines when compared to the acid form of 14a, suggesting that the methylester derivative aided in its cell activity. We next evaluated the antitumour effect by studying the cytotoxicity of 14aMe on selected cancer cell lines, as well as HEK293T non-cancer cells. Our results showed that 14aMe decreased cell viability to a varying degree depending on the cell lines, with the highest anti-tumour activity on U937 human myeloid leukemia cells (IC50 = 7.95 µM) while only marginal anti-tumour effects on THP1 and MCF7 cells (both with undetermined IC50). 14aMe also showed low cytotoxicity towards HEK293T cells (IC50 undetermined). We then determined the inhibition of m6A demethylase activity of 14aMe using a dot blot assay on U937 cells. Results from our dot blot assays showed that 14aMe resulted in initial increase in m6A levels in total RNA but the effects were short-lived. We further validated the anti-cancer effects of the methyl ester prodrug in mouse models. U937 human myeloid leukemia cells, which is the most sensitive cell line towards our inhibitor, were used in the animal study (2 groups with 4 mice in each). After 12 days’ intervention, the average tumor volume of the 5 mg/kg, 10 mg/kg or 15 mg/kg inhibitor groups were decreased by 53.28%, 70.27% and 54.81% respectively, compared to that of the control group. However, the average tumor weight of the inhibitor groups did not show significant difference compared to the control group. During the experimental period, no significant influence on weight gain nor abnormal behaviors were observed in all mice. Serum assay showed no significant obvious toxicity to the liver and kidney. The lack of dose-dependent anti-cancer effects of the inhibitor in vivo could be due to its poor solubility in aqueous or the short-lived m6A demethylase inhibitory effects in cells. Given the less than expected anti-tumour effects in vivo in this pilot studies, we did not conduct further animal experiments.

22301719.label: Major findings and research outcome
22301719.value: 1) We developed potent and selective inhibitors of FTO using structure-based inhibitor design (Shishodia et al., J. Med. Chem. 2021; Part C Publication No. 2). Using structure-based design, two series of inhibitors were developed to be inhibit FTO and are selective against other 2OG oxygenases. This research highlights a successful effort using structure-based inhibitor design whereby inhibitors that occupy both cosubstrate and prime substrate FTO binding sites showed generally higher potency and selectivity, compared to parent compounds. The most potent compound has an IC50 of 80 nM when evaluated in vitro. This compound also showed good selectivity for FTO relative to other 2OG oxygenases including PHD2, which previously shown to be challenging to distinguish in terms of inhibitor design, and to ALKBH5, another m6A demethylase. Our structural analyses using crystal structures of FTO-inhibitor complexes also showed that the aryl moieties of the compounds that overlap with the substrate binding site in FTO are potentially sterically hindered in the active site of other 2OG oxygenases, thus conferring selectivity for FTO. 2) We determined three crystal structures of ALKBH5 in complex with an m6A-containing RNA substrate and the structures provided crucial insights into the catalytic mechanisms of ALKBH5 (Kaur et al., Nuc. Acids. Res. 2022; Part C Publication No. 1). Importantly, the structural data distinguish ALKBH5 from the other m6A demethylase FTO, which has different product and disease profiles. Our structural data, supported by biochemical data, showed that ALKBH5 prefers the G/Am6AC consensus motif while FTO does not, implying the role of ALKBH5 as a demethylase of m6A within the DRACH motif. We also proposed a structure-based explanation for why ALKBH5 only produces A while FTO produces a mixture of products (hm6A, f6A, A) – a proton shuttle network in the ALKBH5 active site that allows for rapid fragmentation of hm6A into A; these conditions are not found in the FTO active site. The differences between these two enzymes have important biological consequences due to their association with different cancers types, thus could also be exploited for selective inhibitor design. 3) We developed an FTO inhibitor prodrug that showed anti-tumour properties in cells (Unpublished report; Part C Publication No. 3). However, its efficacy in vivo is not significant. We also showed that the methylester derivative of an FTO inhibitor showed better efficacy in cancer cells, verifying previous reports that a methylester prodrugs could be applied for this class of compounds for enhanced biological activities. We also discovered that the m6A demethylase inhibition effects of the methylester prodrug was transient in cells, potentially explaining its lack of significant in vivo anti-tumour activities.

22301719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22301719.value: We successfully used structure-based design to develop potent and selective FTO inhibitors and showed good efficacy in vitro and in cells. However, the methylester derivative of our most potent FTO inhibitor did not show good efficacy in vivo. One major issue is its solubility in water. For better in vivo efficacy of the inhibitors, improvement on their solubility would be the next hurdle to address. Secondly, its transient effects in inhibiting m6A demethylase activity in cells will also need more detailed studies to identify reasons behind these observations. Prolonging the effects of inhibitors in cells will enhance anti-cancer effects of the inhibitors. We successfully determined crystal structures of ALKBH5-RNA complexes. These structures that detail how m6A-containing RNA substrate binds to the active site of ALKBH5 could be a basis for the design of ALKBH5-selective inhibitors. The basis of m6A base binding that is flipped relative to that of FTO could be exploited for inhibitors that are substrate analogues.

22301719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22301719.value: RNA serves as transcripts of the DNA code in the cell. The RNA code can be further modified chemically to confer additional layer of regulation. N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is a modification that has wide-range of regulatory impact on gene expression and is linked to diseases such as cancer. m6A modification can be removed by two eraser enzymes called FTO and ALKBH5. Increase in levels of FTO and ALKBH5 is associated with cancers such as acute myeloid leukemia and glioblastoma. Targeting these enzymes for anti-cancer therapy is a new development. This project aimed to use 3-dimensional (3D) structures of FTO and ALKBH5 to design small molecule chemical compounds that can inhibit their enzymatic activities. In this study, we successfully developed small molecule inhibitors that can effectively reduce the activity of FTO and a prodrug of the most effective inhibitor was demonstrated to decrease viability of several cancer cell lines. We also determined 3D structures of ALKBH5-RNA complex that explain why ALKBH5 is biochemically different from FTO, hinting at why ALKBH5 has a different disease profile compared to FTO. These differences will also help in anti-cancer drug discovery in order to differentiate the two m6A eraser targets.

22502819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22502819.value: Governments and international organizations around the world have invested trillions of dollars in transportation and information and communications technology infrastructures. Various prominent models of trade maintain that reducing trade costs and information frictions promotes trade, thereby improving the welfare of the trading partners. Previous studies have found evidence that the expansion of the railroad network in 19th-century India and the connection of the transatlantic telegraph between New York and Liverpool in 1866 increased trade and better integrated the markets (Donaldson and Hornbeck, 2016; Donaldson, 2018; Steinwender, 2018). A broad literature suggests that trade (openness) could further facilitate technology diffusion across regions (Keller, 2004). However, little is known about whether infrastructure can stimulate more profound technology diffusion, and much less is known about whether different types of infrastructure are more effective at facilitating such diffusion. In this study, I propose to advance the literature on infrastructure, and on technology diffusion by examining the effect of the rapid expansion of railroad and telegraph networks in early 20th-century China (c. 1920s to 1930s) on the spread of high-quality American cotton to 786 rural Chinese counties. I will explore the question in two steps. First, I will estimate the effect of the expansion of railroad and telegraph networks on technology diffusion—specifically the adoption of U.S. cotton—using a differences-in-differences (DID) design to analyze county-level panel data on cotton cultivation. Next, I will examine the causal effect of infrastructure by using the potential railway and telegraph routes as an instrumental variable for the actual railway/telegraph network for a more robust estimation. Depending on the outcome of the above analysis, I will further examine the influence of two possible channels through which infrastructure could affect technology diffusion. The first channel is that, by reducing trade costs and/or information friction, infrastructure facilitates long-distance trade between remote rural counties and industrialized coastal ports, which gives peasants in these counties a strong incentive to sell lucrative American cotton to coastal textile factories (the "market integration" channel). I will digitalize domestic bilateral trade and price data to empirically test this channel using a county gravity model. The second potential channel is that an integrated market helps transmit the positive productivity shocks from the downstream industry to increasing demands for cotton from the upstream cotton farmers (the "supply chain" channel). I plan to construct a firm-level panel data set of the spinning and weaving industry to empirically test.

22502819.label: Realisation of objectives
22502819.value: In this section, we shall go over the four original project objectives one by one to discuss their realisation so far. The first objective was “To estimate the effect of the expansion of railroad and telegraph networks on technology diffusion—specifically the adoption of U.S. cotton—using a differences-in-differences design on a county-level panel data of cotton cultivation.” we have fulfilled it in the first output paper titled “Railways, Telegraph and Technology Adoption: The Introduction of American Cotton in Early 20th Century China”. We have confirmed a 12% and 6% effect of railway and telegraph access on the intensive margin of American cotton adoption, while 1.2 times and 52% increase of extensive margin measuring by the area of plantation using our baseline differences-in-differences model. The second objective is to use a more sophisticated IV approach to identify the causal impact of infrastructure, which we also fulfilled in the same paper. Leveraging on important historical facts, we use whether a county is located along a straight-line corridor between major cities covered by the railway network as an instrumental variable for railway access and whether it had a post office as an instrumental variable for telegraph connection. And we identified a consistent and positive impact of infrastructures on technology adoption in different IV specifications (including cross-sectional specification in years 1921, 1928, and 1937, and using panel data and IVCRC estimations to deal with the bias from heterogeneous treatment effects in IV estimation). The third objective has been partially realized. In the original objective, I proposed to explore two possible channels for the infrastructure effects, including both the transmission of positive productivity shock from the downstream industry and the market integration channel via the reduction of information friction and reduced trade cost. We have digitalized rich and detailed historical price data for the second channel and confirm that infrastructures did significantly promote market integration. And in the first draft of the working paper, we also confirm the supply chain channel using the textile factory data. However, one of the referees in our first submission suggested that we shall focus on making clear the channel for technological adoption within the industry first and leave the discussion on the spillover effect via the supply chain to a separate paper. We took this advice and devise a set of new mechanisms for technological adoption in the revised working paper and developed a separate project to particularly explore the supply chain effect. The last objective proposed to digitalize the prices and domestic bilateral trade data and use a county pair gravity model to empirically test the “market integration” channel. We constructed county-level price data between 1920 and 1936 for 102 counties and digitalized comprehensive domestic trade data from a commodity census conducted by the General Post Office of the Ministry of Transportation (Jiaotongbu Youzheng Zhongju) in 1934. These unique datasets help us to confirm the positive effect of infrastructures on bridging information friction in price (measured by the reduction of price spread of cotton) and reducing the trade cost for transportation which showed in the reduction in the average cotton price.

22502819.label: Major findings and research outcome
22502819.value: Three papers had been produced by this ECS project. The first one is the originally proposed study on how the development of infrastructure (both railway and telegraph) in early 20th century China facilitated the diffusion of one important agricultural innovation—the adaptation of American Cotton. For this paper, we first confirmed a quantitatively large positive effect of railway availability on the adoption of the new species on both the extensive and intensive margins, while telegraph accessibility only had a limited effect which was conditional on the railway. Secondly, guided by a heterogeneous agent model with trade and information frictions, we further explore the mechanisms, which we discover the railway and telegraph access significantly decreased the take-up thresholds measured by agricultural suitability and average farm size. Finally, incorporated the price data we digitalized uniquely for this project, we confirm a overall large—50% of—welfare gains from infrastructure availability was through the adoption of the new species. I further used the historical consumer price and economic data digitalized for the first paper to explore the introduction of another type of important infrastructure—the power plant in early industrialized China. In this second paper titled “Trade shocks, industrial growth, and electrification in early 20th-century China”, my co-authors and I find that the decreasing manufactured imports caused the expansion of power plant in the early 20th century China. We further exploit exogenous variations from tariff change and counties’ access to ports to confirm the causal effect. Finally, we propose the demand for electricity induced by domestic industrial growth is the likely channel for the observed effect. This paper has been accepted by the Journal of Comparative Economics for publication in February 2022. Finally, based on the findings of the second paper, we further quantify the impact of electrification on industrial development between 1875 and 1936 China in a third paper. In this paper, we first confirm a substantial positive effect of local (county’s) electrification on the entry of new industrial firms. And using detailed production data by the textile factories, we confirmed that after the supply of electricity had been guaranteed by the entry of power plants, textile factories increased their labor and capital inputs. And given the positive effect was concentrated on high-productivity (TFP) factories, it tended to increase the efficiency of resource allocation of the whole industry. This paper had been accepted by the top tier Chinese economic journal—經濟學（季刊）—for publication recently.

22502819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22502819.value: The main research output of the first paper, “Railways, Telegraph and Technology Adoption: The Introduction of American Cotton in Early 20th Century China” is still under review for publication. Our imminent goal is to publish it in an “A” journal. Apart from the three research papers, my co-authors and I are working on an extension project in which we are trying to study the impact of technology adoption via the case of American cotton on the development of the downstream textile industry development. Hanlon (2015) Econometrica paper finds that a positive effect of upstream supply shock affects the development of new technologies in the downstream textile sector using the case of the US Civil War as s source of exogenous supply shock of cotton to the British textile industry. Similarly, we hypothesize the upstream technological adoption shall also affect the downstream textile factories’ development via the reduction of the relative price of the input (high-quality cotton). We have digitalized the detailed textile factory production data in our second and third output papers for this project. We plan to use them for this new related project.

22502819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22502819.value: We provide historical evidence to prove the importance of infrastructure projects like the railway and telegraph in promoting the adoption of new farming technology. And the adoption of new farming technology, in turn, benefited the farmers by increasing their income. This not only helps us to understand an important episode of Chinese history—the early development of manufacturing production and corporation, it also sheds light on the important roles of infrastructure investment by the state and the private sector on the country’s economic development, which is an enlightening lesson for today’s policy-making as well. And since we confirm that the railway and telegraph benefited mainly by reducing the cost of transportation and by bridging the gap in information between different market participants. It provides strong justification to invest substantially in transportation as well as telecommunication infrastructures today to benefit the market, trade, and economic development in the same way.

22600319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22600319.value: This research project, “Transnational Identities of the Global South Asian Diaspora in Australia, Canada, Aotearoa New Zealand, and South Africa, 1900s-1940s,” will address a crucial issue in the modern world: How is identity formed by different populations living in communities distant from their original homelands? It will answer this question by analysing and comparing the historical forces that affected identity-formation of South Asian migrants in four diasporic communities under British rule. It will pose three main research questions: 1. Was the rhetoric about the equality of all British subjects adopted by South Asian migrants in the British Empire’s self-governing Dominions (Australia, Canada, Aoteatoa New Zealand, and South Africa) in the first half of the twentieth century? Building on the Principal Investigator’s previous research (Smith and Mann, 2016) and related scholarship on Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand, it will compare the experiences and the rhetoric in the four countries. 2. Did the experience of living in predominantly White countries encourage migrants from the Punjab and other regions in South Asia to adopt a common pan-South Asian identity? 3. To what extent did inter-ethnic and inter-faith relations in South Asia impact the South Asian diaspora in the self-governing British Dominions? The Principal Investigator’s previous comparative and transnational research has proven the efficacy of comparing national case studies in diasporic communities. If the rhetoric about the equality of all British subjects is demonstrated by the research, this would be highly significant, as it would illustrate that “Britishness” or a “Britannic Nationalism’ was not only an ethnic phenomenon, but also a civic one. Exploring the diversity of the South Asian diaspora, in terms of ethnicity, culture, and religion, will also be extremely enlightening, as the community was not a single monolithic bloc: even within the Punjabi community there were Sikhs, Hindus, and Muslims practicing different faiths. To answer these three questions, archival research into letters, newspapers, and other publications will be undertaken in the libraries holding materials relating to the four communities. The results of this research will be disseminated in the form of conference and seminar presentations, the publication of several articles and a monograph, and will engage the general public by establishing a website and a blog, giving those interested the opportunity to follow the progress of the research. 此研究項目名為「1900至1940年代澳洲、加拿大、新西蘭及南非的南亞僑民跨國身份認同」，而筆者主要關心的議題是：來自不同地方的族群，生活在遠離自己家園的社區時，是如何建構自身的身份認同？研究首先分析及比較四個英屬自治的離散社區，南亞僑民身份建構的歷史緣由與發展，並提出三個核心問題：1. 二十世紀上半葉的中南亞僑民在大英帝國的自治領地（澳洲、加拿大、新西蘭及南非）内，是否都認同在英國享有平等待遇的說法？本研究將在筆者 (Smith and Mann, 2016) 過去曾進行的考察及有關澳洲和新西蘭的學術研究基礎上，就以上四個國家的案例和論述進行比較。2. 在以白人為主的國家生活是否有助於鼓勵來自旁遮普和其他南亞地區的僑民建構一个共同的「跨南亞身份」(pan-South Asian identity)？3. 南亞族群和宗教之間的關係，在多大程度上影響了英國自治領地内南亞僑民的離散經驗？筆者曾多次比較離散社群與跨國僑民的經驗，並積累了可觀的案例分析。如果此次研究能證明所有英國主權底下的公民皆享有平等待遇的說法，這將有助於證明「英國性」及「不列顛民族主義」不僅是一種民族特色，更是一種公民特質。從種族、文化、宗教等多方面探索南亞僑民的多元性，是一項具啟發性的研究項目。同時我們必須意識到南亞社區不是鐵板一塊，單在旁遮普社區內就有錫克教、印度教及穆斯林等信奉不同信仰的社群。 針對本研究所提出的三個問題，筆者將到藏有四個相關社區及族群材料的圖書館展開研究工作，並收集信件、報紙和其他出版物等檔案材料進行分析。研究的成果將透過舉辦會議及研討會、出版著作等方式與學者進行交流，也會建立網頁及博客鼓勵公眾參與談論，讓有興趣的人士亦有機會了解此次研究。

22601019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22601019.value: This proposal is a technical study that explores how Qin Dynasty (221-207 BC) bureaucrats attained accuracy and precision in the production and utilization of measuring containers, through which an awareness of the Qin empire was cultivated among the populace. One of the salient achievements of the Qin empire was the so-called unification of measurement systems, including lengths, volumes, and weights. Yet measurement systems and the technological methods employed to achieve accuracy and precision in ancient China have scarcely been explored in English-language scholarship, despite their fundamental importance in changing how science and technology developed in early China. Past scholars have not investigated the production of these measures in detail, nor have they related the methods used to attain their accuracy and precision to a more comprehensive picture of the larger empire-building project of the Qin Dynasty. Even such renowned scholars of history of science as Joseph Needham and his successors have failed to place an adequate emphasis on the origins and development of accuracy and precision attainment in the Chinese historical context. Past scholars have instead focused primarily on the conversion of Qin volumetric units to modern-day metric units and the philological explanations of the edicts related to the unification of the measurement system, while ignoring the way in which these standard measures came into being. We hope to first investigate the meaning of accuracy and precision in the view of Qin producers and users by focusing primarily on the measuring containers themselves. Establishing standards of accuracy and precision was essential in all engineering and technological projects; this was extremely important for the success of all grand infrastructure, palace, and cemetery building projects in the Qin empire. We will examine the material features of the containers in detail and investigate the ways in which the producers may have attained them. Whether this was achieved by a calculation of the volume of each container or the rapid replication of their models and/or molds constitutes our initial query. The containers were also useful tools for the purpose of (indirectly) propagandizing the establishment of the Empire. We will further investigate the means by which Qin bureaucrats cultivated an awareness of the Empire by widely distributing the standard containers and displaying the royal edicts inscribed on them. In so doing, we will supply the field of Qin history with additional solid evidence with regard to how the Empire was established and strengthened. 此計劃旨在探討秦朝(公元前221-207年)官吏如何在量器的生產與使用上達致準繩與精度，透過這些方法他們嘗試在普羅大眾中建立秦帝國的意識。秦帝國的其中一項廣為人知的成就是「統一度量衡」。但是古代中國的度量衡制度與達致精準度的技術手段在英語學術界中卻極少談及，儘管它們在改變古代中國的科技層面上有如此重大的作用。過往的學者沒有細緻研究這些度量衡器的生產，他們也沒有把生產方法連繫到精準度的掌握，以及更廣闊的帝國建構層面上。著名學者如李約瑟及其繼承人等也沒有將古代中國人對精準度的掌握之起源與發展放在適當的位置上討論。過往的學者對於秦代量制也只是集中於單位的轉換，忽視了這些標準量器是如何生產的。 我們希望關注這些量器，從而探討秦代生產者與使用者對於精準度的掌握。精準度的標準確立是所有工程與技術的核心：這對於秦帝國的大型工程，如基建、宮殿、陵墓等都有着重要意義。我們會研究量器上的物質特徵、生產痕跡。我們初步的疑問是：每個量器的容量是通過計算達致的呢？還是透過複製量器的內核而達致的？這在青銅器鑄製史上有着極重要的指示意義。量器對於帝國建立、宣傳、意識型態的建立也是很有用的工具。我們會研究秦代官吏在廣泛傳發量器標準、宣傳統一度量衡的詔文的同時，如何建構帝國的意識。我們會為秦代歷史研究領域提供更多、更充實的研究證據。

22601019.label: Realisation of objectives
22601019.value: We have attained all objectives listed in the project proposal. Although there emerged many obstacles during the project execution period (2019-2022), such as the large-scale social chaos and the Covid-19 pandemic, we still managed to accomplish all goals. Achievements: We have generated innovative research results based on our close study of Qin dynasty containers. We have investigated how the containers showed the Qin container producers’ methods to attain accuracy and precision to maintain an empire-wise measurement system. This was an engineering and political achievement in early China. We have studied numerous containers cast in bronze and examined how they conveyed the messages of the Qin government. They display how the Qin government implanted the awareness of the empire among the populace. Our innovative method of using 3D scanning and modelling to experiment with the containers also proves that this is a new aspect of digital humanities that awaits further exploration. Objectives 1 and 2: The Qin Empire was famous for its unification schemes, one of which was the unification of the measurement systems, including length, volume, and weight. Our project focuses on the control of the volume system, which was how to produce and distribute the measuring containers. We proposed to study many Qin dynasty containers on site, handle and observe them in hand, and even 3D-scan them into 3D models for close study and experiments. We have been granted access to various museums and archaeological institutes to examine the measuring containers; most of them were made in bronze. We have found that most of the bronze containers were probably made in local foundries and the container production revealed some interesting facts. For one group of the containers, their shape and general size varied, but their volumetric shape, namely the cavity of the containers, is the same. This suggests that there might have been a blueprint indicating how to produce the containers, which provided a visual reference to local casters. But local casters might create containers of slightly different shape and size. The container as a whole was not to be replicated. We find out the volumetric shape might be replicated. Namely, the core for producing the cavity of the container might be replicated. We know that the most important part of a container is not its shape and general size; these could have varied. Producers who wanted to promote the measurement unification scheme would pay much more attention to containers with the same volumetric content (length x width x depth), and even the same volumetric shape. The core for casting would matter essentially. In this way, the casters could avoid problems such as frequently measuring and calculating the volumetric content of each new container. The core determined the volumetric shape, and thus the volumetric content of the final product, but not the general shape and size of the whole container. The producers could skip problems of complicated calculation and tedious imitation or replication skills. Instead, the central government only needed to distribute blueprints written or drawn on perishable materials such as silk or bamboo slips and clay cores to regional production centers. We validate this hypothesis with close measurement and observation results and 3D modelling. Close measurement and observation results have already shown that some containers share the same volumetric content but not the same general shape and size. This has already validated the hypothesis. We further validate it with 3D modelling results. We 3D-scanned some of the containers into 3D models and superimposed them together to determine how their volumetric shape overlap while their general shape does not. We have published these results in our paper on the Journal of Chinese History. We believe that the problem of whether inscriptions on the containers were cast or engraved awaits further exploration. On the well-known Shang Yang fangsheng, its inscription can be divided into three parts: the Qin Shihuangdi 221 BCE edict, the record about Shang Yang and the volume of the container, and the two place names. The 221 BCE edict seem to be cast and each character was carved on the clay model of the container by chiseling away the clay in carving out the strokes. This is why each stroke appears wide and smooth. The Shang Yang record seems to be engraved instead. This suggests that the fangsheng might have been cast during Qin Shihuangdi’s reign, in approximately 221 BC, with the edict cast on the fangsheng, while the record about Shang Yang and the volume was engraved at a later time. This conclusion has overthrown the current consensus about the dating of the famous Shang Yang fangsheng, and forces scholars to revisit the history of the development of inscription production in ancient China, and eventually the sequence of container production. Objectives 3: The 221 BCE edict, issued during the First Emperor’s reign, and the edict made by the Second Emperor, were to convey messages about the measurement system unification scheme to a wider audience. Our detailed examination of the containers has helped us discover the production relationship between the foundries and the government, which eventually shed light on the context of the implementation of the imperial policies. With the implementation and dissemination of the standard containers, the Qin bureaucrats were communicating with the populace in multiple ways. They were publicly propagandizing the new empire measurement policies, and euphemistically implanting the awareness of the new standards, and thus the new empire, among the users and witnesses of the containers. The containers were silent tools to nurture the awareness. Objectives 4: One of the obstacles in the development of art history and archaeology is that scholars cannot easily access the objects they want to study. Our research approach has demonstrated to the world how we can partially solve this problem. Our practice will help establish new research norms in the fields of art history and archaeology because we can validate the observation results. Containers that share very similar shapes may not be housed in the same museum. Instead, they are distributed extensively in museums in northern China. While we cannot take the containers out of the museums and compare them side by side, we can align their 3D models on the computer to determine whether they appear identical in shape and decoration. This is an innovative method to study objects that share very similar shape and decoration, whose significance will eventually be evident in the study of mass-produced objects in the rest of the world. Under-achievements and attempts to overcome problems: Under-achievements of the project are very few. But there are definitely areas in need of improvement. For example, our datasets are not comprehensive enough to represent the entire production industry of the measures in the Qin Empire. Our selected examples are still very few. Many containers are not archaeologically excavated items that do not bear any contextual information. In the future, we hope to travel to more museums and archaeological institutes to access more containers and other measures in order to generate a more comprehensive dataset. We also hope to examine more archaeologically excavated measures in order to gather more contextual information about the Qin measures.

22601019.label: Major findings and research outcome
22601019.value: We have generated new knowledge about the production and distribution network of the Qin standard containers, and eventually extended our study to the Qin standard weights and rulers. We have also introduced to scholars ways of combining evidence both from texts and materials, with an intellectual trajectory that will contribute to the study of ancient Chinese history as a whole. 1. “Attaining Accuracy and Precision of Measuring Containers during the Qin Dynasty”; and the forthcoming book. We have published most of our important findings in this journal article. The article explores how Qin Dynasty bureaucrats attained accuracy and precision in producing and designing measuring containers. The PI has examined the material features of the containers and reconstructed the production methods of how the clay models, molds, and cores of the containers were prepared before casting; while the book lays the historical foundation of how these methods were used. How the government distributed the containers and how it implanted the awareness of the Qin empire among the populace were also investigated. 2. “Decorated Model, Replication, and Assembly Line of the Bronze Industrial Production in 500 BCE China”. We have examined the origins of how the Qin containers were replicated. Approximately 300 years before the Qin dynasty, bronze casters knew how to use clay models, molds, and cores to replicate products efficiently. This laid the foundation for the production of Qin containers. 3. “Precious Stones and Bronzes in Jade Age and Bronze Age of China”. 4. “Emphasis on Visual and Tactile Experiences: Mechanical Treatments of Bronzes and Jades in Ancient China”. These two articles mainly examine the origins of engraving on hard materials, including bronzes and jades. Methods of casting and/or engraving inscriptions on Qin bronze containers stemmed from much earlier periods, such as the Jage Age and Early Bronze Age. 5. “Art History, Archaeology, and 3D Technology”, Kaiwu. This article offers insights into how 3D technology can be applied to the fields of art and archaeology, which will be an important digital humanities aspect. Conference papers 6. “Qindai liangqi de shengchan yu jingzhun kongzhi” This was meant to be published but the entire conference was cancelled and it ceased publication due to the political turmoil and the pandemic.

22601019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22601019.value: We conducted only a few research trips to collect related data about the Qin Dynasty containers. Hindrances are due to the outbreak of the social chaos and the pandemic. Many of our planned research travels ceased and this significantly impacted our research plan. However, we still managed to publish 1 book, 5 journal articles, which were all peer-reviewed. Another book specifically devoted to the study of Qin measures is in progress. We believe our research materials collected so far are adequate for further exploring the history of attaining accuracy and precision of measuring containers in the Qin Dynasty. If more travels are allowed in the future and grants permit, we will conduct more travels to locate more relevant containers and other measures.

22601019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22601019.value: This project has investigated how the Qin dynasty casters achieved accuracy and precision while producing one of the important measures for the empire, containers. We have examined how the models, molds, and the pour of metal of the containers were prepared and how they were processed in the foundries. We have shown that production relationship between the foundries and the government was very close, and foundries might have impact on the imperial policies. We have published a series of articles in international peer-reviewed journals and conducted numerous public lectures to conduct knowledge-transfer activities. The art historical and archaeological study of the Qin foundries and measurement system has been supplied with more solid evidence as we have renewed the factual basis of this field and provided new methodologies to guide future research directions.

22601119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22601119.value: Global public health guidelines recently moved from an isolated to an integrated approach for movement behaviors (sleep, physical activity and sedentary behavior) across a 24-hour period, recognizing that the whole day matters for optimal health for preschool children (3-5 years). In Hong Kong, much effort has been devoted to promoting healthy eating and active living for 3- to 6-year-olds since 2012. However, sleep has been overlooked in such campaign despite that all the movement behaviors interact and influence each other. Of particular concern is that local preschoolers have demonstrated the latest bedtimes compared with their counterparts in other countries. Studies examining interrelationships between sleep and daytime activity behaviors have provided mixed results and have primarily focused on sleep duration only. Consistent bedtimes and wake-up times are recommended in the new guidelines; however, weekday-weekend variations have been widely reported for preschoolers who are attending kindergartens worldwide. Social obligations such as school schedule may interfere with individual circadian preferences for bedtimes, known as chronotype. The discrepancy between biological clock and social obligation is described as “social jetlag”. Beyond sleep duration, social jetlag is associated with increased risk of obesity, metabolic disorders, and mental health problems. Research has indicated that feelings of tiredness induced by short sleep duration lead to lower physical activity level. The influence of social jetlag on daytime activity behaviors, however, has not been examined despite its significant impact on health for young children. The proposed study will follow up a group of 3- to 5-year-olds (approximately n=300) who were participants in an on-going cross-sectional study. It aims to investigate: (1) the temporal associations of social jetlag with physical activity and sedentary time the following day; (2) the longitudinal associations of social jetlag with activity behaviors over a two-year period. Data collected in the ongoing project that is relevant to purposes of the proposed study, including activPAL-assessed physical activity, sedentary time, bed hours, parent-reported screen time and socio-demographic factors, nap time in kindergartens will be used as baseline measures. Social jetlag is computed as the difference in the midpoint of sleep between school days and weekend days. Follow-up measurements will be taken at the similar time of year in 2020 (two years later after the baseline), comprising children’s chronotype, behavioral problems, TV in the child’s bedroom, and outdoor time reported primarily by parents. The findings will improve the understanding of the movement behaviors synergistically, which will better inform subsequent intervention strategies.

22601119.label: Realisation of objectives
22601119.value: In order to examine the changes of social jetlag among preschool-aged children (Objective 1) and the associations of social jetlag with physical activity and sedentary behavior (Objectives 2 and 3), we initially planned to follow up an existing cohort of young children who should enter K2 or K3 in academic year 2020-2021. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic induced social distancing and school closure, participants recruitment and data collection from 2020 to 2021 were dramatically disrupted. As a result, as reported in our mid-term progress report, we have to recruit another cohort of preschoolers. In addition to approach the kindergartens that participated in our previous project, we have proactively recruited the participants through the collaborative network and via snowball sampling. In addition, data collection was inevitably more time consuming than initially planned. Data collection for some participants was not fully completed until May 2022. Because of this, manuscript reporting the whole dataset has not yet been finished. However, partial data generated from this project have already been presented in several highly regarded international conferences and been submitted for publications in several journals. It should be noted that this study investigated circadian misalignment between biological clock and social obligation (e.g., school start time). Because of the disrupted schooling schedule during the pandemic, the findings may be unique to this specific period. Another challenge is to increase the compliance of wearing protocol of the accelerometer. Although we have rich experience in using the activPAL among local children, the compliance rate varies and some participants found difficulties in wearing the device for an extended period of time using a 3M Tegaderm transparent dressing (e.g. experiencing skin irritation). With the approved budget changes, we were able to improve the wearing experience by using a pouch sewn to an elastic cotton belt (details described in the mid-term progress report). The new method has been well received by children and parents. Eventually, we recruited a total of 431 children aged between 2.5 and 7.4 years (55% boys), 64% (n = 276) of whose parents agreed for their child to wear an activPAL accelerometer. These children were instructed to wear an activPAL in front of the thigh for eight consecutive days. Physical activity, sedentary time, and sleep parameters (sleep duration, midpoint of sleep, and social jetlag) were generated from the accelerometer data. Their parents responded to a questionnaire survey which assessed children’s chronotype (using Children’s ChronoType Questionnaire, CCTQ), and behavioral problems (using Strengthen and Difficulties Questionnaire, SDQ), parental physical activity and sedentary behavior (using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire, IPAQ short form), as well as the sociodemographic information (age, sex, body weight and height, educational attainment). A sample size of 276 is sufficient to detect a small effect size (f2 = 0.1) with a power of 0.90 under the conditions of an alpha level of 0.05, two tailed significant tests with 8 covariates in the regression model. For the remaining 155 children, only parental survey was conducted. In order to determine changes of social jetlag, the linear mixed models were performed while adjusting for children’s sex, age, and body mass index (BMI), and parental educational attainment. The changes were not significant (b = - 0.104, 95% CI: -0.463, 0.254, p = 0.567). Over half of the children (53.5%) was classified as evening type, while the others were neither morning nor evening type. No kids were classified as morning type. In order to assess the temporal associations between sleep parameters and physical activity/sedentary time (Objective 2), a dataset consisting of 5 repeated pairs of sleep → physical activity/sedentary time was created for each participant. Each pair included sleep parameters in the preceding night in minutes (Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday) and physical activity/sedentary time the next day (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday). Generalized linear models were performed to determine the temporal associations after adjustment of covariates including child’s age, sex, BMI, chronotype, and sleep duration in the preceding night, as well as parents’ educational attainment, Linear mixed models were performed to determine the longitudinal associations between changes in social jetlag and physical activity/sedentary time (Objective 3). Changes of social jetlag were regressed on physical activity or sedentary time, while adjusting for the above-mentioned covariates. Three conference abstracts reporting the preliminary findings of this study have been presented at the following international conferences: • “Parental role modelling on preschoolers’ movement behaviors during the COVID -19 pandemic” at the 2021 Annual Meeting of the American College of Sports Medicine. • “Parental perceived barriers and preschoolers' movement behaviours during COVID-19 pandemic” at the 2022 Annual Meeting of the International Society for Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity. • “Sociodemographic, individual, and parental predictors of change in sleep among preschoolers during the COVID-19 pandemic” at the 9th International Society for Physical Activity and Health Congress. Two manuscripts generated from this project, entitled “Associations of social jetlag with physical activity and sedentary behavior in children and adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis” and “Parental role modelling on 24-hour movement behaviors among preschoolers during the COVID-19 Pandemic” are currently under review. Data from this project also made contribution to a synthesis report of prevalence of underweight and its association with physical inactivity which is also under review (“Thinness as a risk factor for physical inactivity in children and youth”).

22601119.label: Major findings and research outcome
22601119.value: This study examined the changes of social jetlag and its associations with physical activity and sedentary behavior among preschool-aged children in Hong Kong. The major findings are summarized as follows: • The average midpoint of sleep was 3:31. The CCTQ chronotype score ranged from 27 to 38, with a mean score = 32.89 (SD: 2.51). Accordingly, 53.5% was classified as evening type, while the others were neither morning nor evening type. None of the children were morning-oriented. However, 10.2% of the parents considered their child to be “absolute morning type”. • After adjustment for children’s sex, age, and BMI, and parental educational attainment, linear mixed models indicated no significant changes in social jetlag (b = -0.104, 95% CI: -0.463, 0.254, p = 0.567) over 1-2 years. Furthermore, we found that sleep duration did not change during the pandemic among over 60% of the pre-schoolers (Part C, 9-3). However, parents played an important role in influencing their children’s behaviors including sleep. Children whose parents had shorter sleep duration and perceived more barriers to their child’s sleep were more likely to have a declined sleep duration (Part C, 8-2, 9-1, 9-2, and 9-3). • Temporal relationships between sleep parameters (sleep duration, midpoint of sleep, social jetlag) and physical activity/sedentary behavor were determined by generalized linear models adjusting for covariates and chronotype score. Social jetlag was positively associated with total physical activity (b=21.36, 95%CI: 4.76, 37.97), but not with moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (b=5.52, 95%CI: -0.93, 11.96) or sedentary time (b=0.24, 95%CI: -0.19, 0.67). A delayed midpoint of sleep in the preceding night was associated with a decrease in both physical activity and sedentary time the following day. Chronotype scores were not associated with physical activity or sedentary time. • The above findings regarding the relationship between social jetlag and physical activity/sedentary behavor were not fully consistent with the recently conducted meta-analysis by our team (Part C, 8-1). The possible reasons include different target age groups (preschoolers vs school-aged children and adolescents) and type of measurements (device-based vs objective measures). • It is not surprise that no relationships between changes in social jetlag and physical activity/sedentary time were observed because no significant changes were observed in social jetlag in our sample. However, social jetlag was positively associated with hyperactivity/inattention (r = -0.329, p < 0.01). • The findings should be interpreted with caution because of the impact of the COVID-19 induced disruption to school schedule from 2020 to 2022.

22601119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22601119.value: To the best of our knowledge, it is the first study examining the association of social jetlag or chronotype with physical activity and sedentary behavior among preschool-aged children in Hong Kong. As indicated in the recently conducted systematic review by our team, evidence in this age group is limited. Given that more than half of the preschoolers demonstrate evening-oriented chronotype, they are more likely to experience circadian misalignment and have unhealthy lifestyles. Build upon the success of the current study, we will further develop our research in two aspects: 1. We will compare social jetlag in pre-schoolers between pre-pandemic and during pandemic using data generated from our previous project (data collected in 2017-18) and the current study (both use activPAL to determine sleep and daytime activity behaviors). The findings will be helpful to understand whether or not sleep timing/patterns has been affected by the pandemic. 2. We aim to develop chronotype-specific experimental studies to promote an active lifestyle. Based on the findings of the current study and the above-mentioned systematic review, it is important to consider timing of physical activity/sedentary behavior interventions in order to make them more feasible and attractive to evening-oriented children.

22601119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22601119.value: It is important for children to have sufficient sleep and consistent sleep timing throughout the week. For children and adolescents attending schools which usually start early in the day, however, the interference of school schedules with the circadian rhythm regulating sleep-wake cycles have been widely reported. The misalignment between biological clock and social obligation is conceptualized as social jetlag. It is more profound among those with a late (evening) circadian preference, known as chronotype. This study examined whether or not having circadian misalignment was associated with a less healthy lifestyle. It was found that over half of the young children had an evening chronotype which means they have delayed bedtime and prefer getting up late in the morning. Children having circadian misalignment (social jetlag) were less physically active. The delayed midpoint of sleep (between bedtime and risetime) in the preceding night was associated with less physical activity in the following day. Social jetlag remained stable in the past two years, probably because of the pandemic disrupted schooling schedule. The findings suggest that there is a pressing need to consider children’s circadian preference when develop physical activity promotion strategies for young children, especially among evening-oriented individuals.

To apply the results to contemporary discussions on comparative religion and to promote interfaith dialogue.
