22603119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22603119.value: The Kalam Cosmological Argument (KCA) (which attempts to demonstrate that the universe has a First Cause) and the Teleological Argument (which attempts to demonstrate that the universe has a designer) are two of the most widely discussed arguments in contemporary scholarly discussions in philosophy of religion. This project aims to expose the weaknesses in recent assessments by their proponents and opponents, to offer a more compelling evaluation of alternative explanations, and to examine whether both arguments can be integrated in such a way that both are strengthened. Concerning the Teleological Argument, many scientists and philosophers have argued that the fact that the existence of life in the universe is delicately dependent on various of its fundamental characteristics is evidence for a Designer. Critics object that there could be alternative hypotheses which have yet to be considered. I plan to contribute to the discussion by making the argument more rigorous in its consideration of alternative hypotheses than current versions by Oxford philosopher Richard Swinburne and others. This is accomplished through devising an original deductive argument which demonstrates that the following are the only possible categories of hypotheses: (i) Chance, (ii) Regularity, (iii) Combinations of Regularity and Chance, (iv) Uncaused, and (v) Design. I shall collate a large variety of hypotheses in the literature and classify and evaluate them in accordance with their essential characteristics within the above mentioned categories. In particular, I shall compare and evaluate the hypotheses of an uncaused universe with that of an uncaused Designer by utilizing my previous monograph on KCA, and I shall examine the objections which have been raised since the publication of my monograph on this argument. I shall assess whether KCA can be used to strengthen the Teleological Argument by answering the question ‘Who designed the Designer’ through demonstrating that there is a beginningless and hence undesigned First Cause with free will. I shall also assess whether the Teleological Argument can be used to strengthen KCA by providing considerations for thinking that the First Cause brought about the first event intelligently rather than accidentally. In addition, I shall examine the usefulness of my approach for responding to David Hume’s classic objections to the Teleological Argument, and contemporary critics’ objections concerning the range of explanatory latitude. The project aims to produce two commissioned articles, one monograph, and a proposal for external research funding, and to promote interfaith dialogue and the dialogue between philosophers and scientists. 在宗教哲學中，「卡拉姆」式的宇宙論證（即嘗試證明宇宙有第一因）和目的論證（即嘗試證明宇宙有設計者）是當代學者討論最多的兩個論證。此研究項目旨在分析近年來反對者與支持者對這兩個論證所做評估的不足之處，從而提出對其他對立解釋更爲有說服力的評價，並探討兩個論證是否相輔相成，可以通過整合而得到加强。 就目的論而言，許多科學家與哲學家指出，宇宙中的生命微妙地依賴於宇宙的各種基本屬性 的微調，正是設計者存在的證據。但反對者認爲可能有一些尚未考慮到的其他對立解釋。我計劃對這一討論做出貢獻，通過提出比牛津哲學家理察·斯溫伯恩（Richard Swinburne）和其他学者更為嚴謹的回應其他對立解釋。我將提出一個原創的演繹論證來實現此計劃。這演繹論證將證明僅有五大可能的解釋：（1）機率（2）規律（3）機率與規律相結合（4）無因（5）設計。我將會整理當代討論中的各種解釋，依照其必要特徵，對它們進行分類和評價。藉助我之前有關「卡拉姆」宇宙論的專題著作，我會比較和評估‘無因宇宙’與‘無因設計者’這兩種解釋。同時，我也會分析與回應自我的「卡拉姆」宇宙論專題著作發表以來所收到的批評。我將會展示第一因無開始的特徵可以推論出第一因還應具有非被設計的和享有自由意志的特徵，從而進一步討論「卡拉姆」宇宙論證是否可以通過解決「誰設計了設計者」的問題來强化目的論證。另一方面，通過思考第一因是否是智慧地而非偶然的發起第一事件，我也會探討目的論證是否可以强化「卡拉姆」宇宙論。此外，我會評估我的論證方法是否能有效回應大衛·休谟針對目的論證所提出的傳統反駁和當代批評者所提出有關解釋範圍的反駁。這個項目計劃完成兩篇受委任的文章，一篇專題著作和一份外部研究經費申請計劃書，並促進不同宗教之間和哲學與科學界之間的對話。

22603119.label: Realisation of objectives
22603119.value: The project has contributed to contemporary scholarly debates in philosophy of religion concerning the nature of Ultimate Reality, by successfully formulating and developing novel arguments which address the problems concerning the consideration of alternative hypotheses and other objections to the Teleological Argument. The project has also successfully addressed problems concerning the issue of ultimate explanation and the nature of First Cause by combining recent work on the Cosmological and Teleological Arguments. The extent of success is indicated by the following glowing endorsements by world-leading experts on these topics for my forthcoming monograph The Teleological and Kalam Cosmological Arguments Revisited (Springer Nature, 2022), which is the fruit of this project. ‘An innovative examination and defence of the cosmological and teleological arguments – accessible to the non-expert but pushing the debate into new territory with great originality and verve.’ – philosopher T. J. Mawson, Oxford University, UK. ‘Andrew Loke's book provides an up-to-date assessment of the Teleological and Kalam Cosmological Arguments, including a thorough response to contemporary objections. It advances the discussion concerning the ultimate origin of the universe and makes a significant contribution to the field of philosophy of religion and the dialogue between science and religion.’-philosopher William Lane Craig, Biola University, USA; ‘This book provides an engaging guide to two important features of our universe – it seems to have had a beginning, and its ability to support life is remarkably rare – and their deeper implications. Up-to-date, wide-ranging and highly recommended.’- Cosmologist Luke Barnes, Western Sydney University, Australia. The above mentioned endorsements of my work is also an indication that this project has successfully demonstrate the relevance of philosophical arguments for answering the question of ultimate origins and promote the dialogue between philosophers and scientists. The application of the results to contemporary discussions on comparative religion and to promote interfaith dialogue was achieved during the online Global Philosophy of Religion conference hosted by University of Birmingham 2021, where I presented my research and had a fruitful interaction with scholars of various religions. In addition, I was invited by Islamic philosophers in the Iranian Institute of Philosophy (IRIP) to present a paper related to my research at their International conference on “Rationality, Theism and Atheism” (RTA 2021). The project has more than succeeded in achieving its objectives of producing two commissioned articles, two conference presentations, a monograph; in addition to these publications, it has also produced one other journal article and two other conference presentations. The results of this project have contributed to the discussion on philosophy of religion, and it will be used for a proposal to apply for external research funding from GRF in the area of philosophy of religion titled Artificial Intelligence: Philosophical and Theological Engagement in Asian Context. Another proposal will be submitted to the John Templeton Foundation at a later stage. It has also helped me win a grant as co-Investigator for a Hong Kong Research Grants Council General Research Fund (HKD 294,009): ‘A multi-disciplinary study of the multiverse hypothesis.’ Project number 18606721. September 2021 to August 2023. (Principal Investigator: Chan Man Ho). Concerning public seminar, I was invited to present my research on the Cosmological Argument at a seminar organized by The Veritas Forum on 15/1/2022, with more than 400 participants from China, HK and USA) In addition, I have been invited to participate in an interview by Closer to Truth, a well-known television series which features the world’s greatest thinkers exploring humanity’s deepest questions.

Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22603119.value: Throughout history, many have embarked on the quest to discover the answers to the fundamental mystery concerning the ultimate origins of the universe and the purpose of our existence. Some of the most brilliant thinkers in human history have contributed to this quest by formulating their answers to these Big Questions in the form of the Cosmological Argument—which attempts to demonstrate the existence of a Divine First Cause or Necessary Being—and the Teleological Argument—which attempts to demonstrate that our universe is the purposeful creation of a Divine Designer. This project has contributed to the discussion by successfully formulating and developing novel arguments which address the problems concerning the consideration of alternative hypotheses and other objections to the Teleological Argument, and the problems concerning the issue of ultimate explanation and the nature of First Cause by combining recent work on the Cosmological and Teleological Arguments. It has produced presentations and publications which have received glowing endorsements by world-leading experts on these topics, and contributed to comparative religion and interfaith dialogue.

22607619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22607619.value: Traditional consumer search literature assumes that the search cost occurs to a consumer when she visits a seller is independent of her search order. This assumption has broad application as for example, when consumers visit physical stores to purchase products, transportation cost and time is unavoidable and invariant of her search order. However, this assumption prevents economists to from studying an equally relevant environment where consumers incur search costs that are associated with her search order. Imagine that a consumer surfs on Amazon in order to purchase a digital camera. Distinct pages on Amazon may not induce different search costs since one only needs to click the page and browse around. Nevertheless, it is very likely that a consumer becomes increasingly exhausted after clicking and acquiring information from several product pages. One may wonder how consumers would determine their search order given that they know their pattern of search costs. Which seller should be assigned a lower search cost? Which seller will consumers visit first based on consumers’ assignment of search costs among the sellers? A key question in the literature has been to analyze how consumers decide the order of visiting the sellers and at which point they optimally stop. When search costs are independent of search order, consumers made their decisions based on each seller’s search cost and potential product value. When search costs are associated with each consumer’s own search order, consumers are the ones to decide which store bears how much search cost. More generally, one may wonder if there is a platform designer behind, who is free to pair sellers with search costs, how would he design the search environment to optimize consumers’ search process or other objectives such as to maximize consumers’ time spent on the site. Furthermore, a seller’s pricing decisions would be affected by such search design and in turn influence the optimal design. How the central comparative statics question in the search literature on the effect of search cost on prices might deliver a different answer as it is in the classical literature is also of interests. The objective of this project is to provide solution to this technical problem and derive concrete advice for consumers and online platform designers. I plan to document these results and implications in at least one international refereed journal article, and present these them in multiple conferences. 傳統的關於消費者搜索的文獻假設消費者拜訪每一個商家/商店的頁面時所付出的成本是與她拜訪這些商店的順序沒有關系的。這個假設固然有它的來由，例如，當消費者去拜訪實體商店的時候，所付出的交通費用與時間是不可避免的也是與拜訪的順序無關的。然而，這個假設阻止了經濟學家們去思考一個同樣可能的環境，就是當搜索的成本與拜訪的順序有直接的關系的環境。 想象一下這樣的場景：一個消費者在亞馬遜網站上試圖購買一個數碼相機。不同的商家的頁面不一定會對消費者產生不同的固定成本，因為消費者只需要在頁面上搜索自己所需要的信息。但很有可能發生的是，在搜索產品的過程中，消費者逐漸感到疲憊。使經濟學家們感到好奇的問題是，如果消費者知道自己會在搜索產品的過程中逐漸疲憊，她們會如何決定拜訪商家的順序？應該先去拜訪哪個商家？在消費者搜索的文獻中的一個經典的問題是消費者如何根據環境決定搜索的順序和決定何時停下搜索。當搜索成本與順序無關的時候，消費者會根據每個商家的搜索成本和產品價值分佈來計算出一個指數，根據指數的大小決定順序。而當搜索成本與順序有關的時候，按照指數排序的方法就不適用了。 比這個場景更為普適性的場景是，設想這整個搜索與購買過程的背後有一個平台的設計師，這個設計師有能力匹配商家和對應的搜索成本，那他要如何做出匹配，使得消費者在這個平台有愉快的購物體驗（最大化消費者剩餘）或者使得消費者在這個平台上逗留足夠長的時間？另外，每一個商家的定價也會受到整個平台的搜索設計的影響。在關於搜索的文獻中一個關鍵的問題是，當搜索成本發生變化，商家的定價會產生怎麼樣的影響？在這個框架中這個問題的答案如何發生變化也是值得探究的。 這個項目的目標是針對這個技術問題給予答案，也希望能夠給消費者和平台設計人員一些比較實用的建議。我計劃將這些結果和建議發表在一篇國際知名學術期刊上，並且參加幾個國際會議講述我的成果。

22608419.label: Project Title(Chinese)
22608419.value: 花園莊東地甲骨文語言研究

22608419.label: Project Objectives
22608419.value: This research plan is a continuation of the applicant’s book on the Huayuanzhuang East oracle bones, the manuscript completed in 2018 and to be published in July 2019 by De Gruyter in its series Library of Sinology. That book is primarily a translation of the oracle bone inscriptions, preceded by an introduction to the context in which the inscriptions must be viewed. It grew out of the author’s Univ. of Chicago Ph.D. dissertation of 2013. The present project is an extension of the previous book, this time focusing analytically on the language of the inscriptions. Apply a corpus-based and data-driven approach to write individual essays (or chapters) on aspects of the language found in these newly recovered oracle bone inscriptions. The topics include: a) the meaning and function of the technical term zhen 貞 “test”. b) divination codas, particularly kan 侃 “happy” and ruo 若 “favorable”. c) adverbs and particles, particularly the words yun 允 “really, indeed” and qi 迄 “arrive, finally”. d) verb forms, particularly verbs related to sacrifice like ce “register”, mao 卯 “split open”, and sui 歲 “to chop cut” > “sacrifice”; coordination of sui 歲 and guan 祼 “libation”. e) the language of prognostications and judgments. f) divination and scribal practice, especially as it concerns the abbreviating of divination statements in sets. Recognize ideas or problems in the interpretation of early epigraphic documents, and provide a methodology with solutions based on working with an intact body of materials like these. To demonstrate that these archaic Chinese texts are not highly peculiar and can be understood.

22608419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22608419.value: The Huayuanzhuang East oracle bone inscriptions, discovered in 1991 and published in six folio volumes in 2003, are a synchronically compact and unified corpus of 2452 individual divination accounts inscribed on 529 (345 completely intact) turtle shells and bovine scapulae. Produced during the late Shang period (ca. 1250-1045), China’s first historical dynasty, and sanctioned under the patronage of an adult male of the royal family, this recent discovery now stands as one of the most important epigraphic finds in the history of Early China studies. What the field of Early China has needed for quite some time is more intact oracle bone discoveries that leverage a corpus-based and data-driven approach to make a systematic and holistic study of the language of the inscriptions from the perspective of the experts who produced them. A clear model of what the inscriptions mean is required before proceeding to do other things with them. The ideal Shang oracle bones are those that have come to us unbroken and with their full context of other shells and pieces. Prior to this discovery such conditions have been rare. Although they had become disjointed and separated during their disposal, the majority of the inscriptions can be linked together in integral divination sets that lead to reconstructed timelines that span periods of weeks or months. The reorganized materials produce what is essentially China’s earliest daily planner. The divination accounts are remarkably linguistically transparent and well preserved, homogeneous in orthography and content, and published to an unprecedentedly high standard, which makes them ideal material for reading the epigraphic texts and explaining their language. Scholarship on the language and grammar of oracle bone divinations produced on behalf of royal family members, which comprises approximately five percent of the total inscriptional corpus and is the type to which the Huayuanzhuang East inscriptions belong, is understudied and can be woven neatly into well-established scholarship on the language of oracle bone divinations produced for the Shang kings. This project will enhance our knowledge of Shang oracle bone language, still very imperfectly understood, as well as to contribute in important ways to knowledge about Shang divination practices, the methods of scribes and diviners, and the daily life and concerns of the powerful patrons whose hopes and fears drove the divination process. 殷墟花園莊東地甲骨卜辭最初發現於1991年，2003年整理印行六大冊圖版及釋文，構成一組短時間內形成而內容相當統一的商代史料，計收529件帶刻辭的龜甲和牛肩胛（其中345件完整），合共2,452條單獨卜辭。花東卜辭形成於晚商時期（約前1250–1045年），主人是一位成年的男性王族成員；鑑於商朝為中國第一個毫無疑問的王朝，這宗新發現堪稱早期中國史研究裡最重要的古文字材料之一。多年以來，早期中國史領域缺乏一大宗相對完整的甲骨文發現，以供學者進行語料庫為本、數據主導的科研項目，從製作卜辭的專業貞人角度，對其語言做系統而全面的分析。顯然學者必須先對卜辭的意義體系有全盤認識，方能開展研究工作。 最理想的甲骨卜辭是完整無缺，並能夠與其他同時出土的甲骨完全對應起來，構成脈絡清晰的生成背景。這種發現在花東卜辭出來以前僅一二見。雖然部分花東卜辭在埋藏時經歷了斷裂和分散，大多數還是一組組繫聯在一起，讓學者得以重構數以週計、甚至月計的祭祀日程。經過重組的材料構成了中國第一部行事曆。難能可貴的是，貞卜記錄在語義上高度透明並保持完好，書體及內容統一，整理質量之高亦是前所未見，種種因素令它成為釋讀古文字文本、闡釋甲骨文語言的理想材料。花東卜辭可以歸入「王室卜辭」（為商朝王室成員製作的卜辭），全部約佔存世甲骨卜辭總數的百分之五；目前學界對（專門為商王所作的）「王卜辭」語言的研究早已碩果纍纍，相比之下對王室卜辭語言和語法的研究比較薄弱。可以預期，本研究所得將會與王卜辭語言相關的成果接軌，相得益彰。對於學界尚未充分把握的殷商甲骨文語言，本研究項目將會大大提高這方面的認識，並就各種不同的課題，例如商人貞卜的操作流程、刻手和貞人的作業方法、商代權貴的日常生活，以至這些受希望和恐懼驅使而作卜的卜辭主人憂心的事情，作出長足的貢獻。

The project was designed to apply a corpus-based and data-driven approach to write individual essays on aspects of the language found in the newly recovered Huayuanzhuang East oracle bone inscriptions. As detailed further below, I have gone on to publish, in both English and Chinese, three academic articles in top-tier publications on behalf of this project. The COVID pandemic greatly affected realizing certain designs to the project, for instance my research assistant needed to return to Mainland China and could not continue her work; I was unable to use any funds to hold a conference or advanced seminar; and I was unable to use funds for travel to present my research and to seek the valuable advice of specialists in the field. These under-achieving aspects of the project are understandable, and I intend to reapply for a GRF in the future to recover the funds returned and to better realize the project I originally planned. I hope I will have the RGC's full support, given the circumstances.

22608419.label: Major findings and research outcome
22608419.value: Major findings and research outcomes can be summarized as follows: Statistics drawn from the Shāng oracle bone inscriptions discovered in Pit H3 at Huāyuánzhuāng East challenge an assumption that all divination statements, or ‘charges’ mìng cí 命辭, be classified as zhēn cí 貞辭, and question an inflexible practice that systematically reads the prefatory word zhēn 貞 ‘test (the correctness of)’ into a divination account when it is absent. The restricted use of zhēn in this unified corpus of inscriptions implies that it had a particular and focused application in the process of decision-making. The Huāyuánzhuāng East inscriptions thus reveal a complex divination matrix that exemplifies the development of royal divination as an institution at Ānyáng more widely. A focus on the work habits and motives of the Shang recordkeepers who wrote the divination accounts discovered in 1991 in Pit 3 at Huayuanzhuang East. These scribes, who worked under the patronage of a head of one of the princely households, collaborated with diviners sanctioned under the same mandate and the two professional groups developed and employed technologies to micromanage their workloads economically and to do their jobs coherently and efficiently. The scribes who produced the divination accounts on this homogenous and unified collection of shells and bones demonstrated accurate divination recordkeeping and displayed a unique competency and innovation in how these specialized records were designed, written out, and formally presented. More crucially, the orientation of the divination accounts indicates a control of the materials, attests to scribal literacy, and implies that they were written to be read and consulted. Deciphering a sustained and collective use of the terms kan 侃 'happy' and ruo 若 'go well > favorable' in the Huayuanzhuang East oracle bone inscriptions, I was able to take a position that its efficacy in the process of divination was relatively high (more than 80%). This implies that when diviners applied it within a divinatory charge they anticipated a positive result. These findings greatly increase our understanding of the mentality of divination in the ancient world. Building off of this single rubric, I expanded my study to encompass the emotion of 'happiness' more specific to the patron whom the diviners served.

22608419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22608419.value: Research on oracle bone inscriptions rarely examine emotions. The article I published in Chinese, on behalf of this project, focused on what brought joy to a prince of the royal family in Henan circa 1200 BC. A concentrated focus on happiness by this previously unknown group of diviners is one of the representative features of their practice and contrasts with the limited usage of this word by other diviner groups who made divination at Anyang. More recently, and building off of the results of my research on happiness, I have written a paper, also in Chinese and to be published in 2024 in a Fudan University publication, on the negative emotion of anxiety and worry. There is a great potential for further development in innovative research on emotions at the beginning of China's historical period.

22611219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
22611219.value: 本研究計劃將探討移民和公民身份的道德規範如何與全球分配正義相互影響。 在當今世界，個人的居住或公民身份會對她的幸福，自由甚至生存產生深遠影響。顯而易見，全球不同國家的公民身份的價值相距甚遠。 大批身處貧窮國家的人渴望藉移民以逃避貧困或壓迫。 他們將不得不跨越一些戒備嚴密甚至軍事化的邊界。 與此同時，在許多富裕的西方社會中，反移民民粹主義運動正在崛起。 這些社會中的許多成員認為，由於移民增加，他們的經濟機會、社區生活和獨特的民族文化現在受到威脅。 關於移民的哲學和倫理辯論一直關注個人是否擁有遷移到其他國家的一般權利。 然而，移民限制實際上是高度選擇性的。 邊界通常只對那些因經濟，政治，文化或人口原因而被接收國視為「可取」的移民開放。 儘管如此，區分成員身份的界限不僅是地域性的，而且是政治性的 - 因為國家有權將某些個人歸類為公民。 例如，移民不會自動獲得其居住國的公民身份，但必須申請入籍。 部分國家更會對申請人的收入、良好品格、語言能力和公民知識等各方面有一定要求。 居留不是獲得公民身份的充分條件，但這是一個必要條件嗎？不少國家願意容忍雙重國籍，並允許移民將其公民身份傳給子女。 因此，「非居住」公民身份越來越普遍。 最後，政府也為破壞成員資格邊界做出了貢獻。 最近，各國傾向於撤銷其成員的公民身份，作為對某些行為的懲罰，例如參與恐怖主義。 本研究計劃旨在探討移民，長期居民和非居民公民的各自權利和義務， 並嘗試解答以下問題：（1）各國在什麼時候允許或限制移民？ （2）已移居外地的人對他們原來的國家有什麼義務？ （3）誰有權在特定國家獲得公民身份？ （4）國家在什麼條件下可以合理地撤銷公民身份？ （5）怎樣的公民身份分配是合乎正義？

22611219.label: Realisation of objectives
22611219.value: The research project set out to explore the moral and political issues of transnational migration. It started in January 2020, and then the COVID-19 hit the world. The Pandemic (and the Hong Kong Government’s policy responses) caused unforeseen disruptions and affected the achievement of some project objectives. However, I have been fairly productive in terms of research and I managed to attend 5 international conferences (virtually) to present research findings, published one book chapter and one journal article, and produced one working paper. The following statement is a brief description of the extent to which the project objectives have been achieved. Objective 1: To explore what justice requires with respect to migration and citizenship allocation In this research project, I have demonstrated that, as a matter of distributive justice, affluent states’ right to exclude potential migrants from poorer countries is conditioned and restricted by their obligations of global justice (and the extent to which such obligations have been fulfilled). Moreover, affluent states must not take advantage of the existing injustices in their immigration or citizenship policies. This has implications for the ethics of immigration control because affluent states routinely use immigration enforcement to protect their economic interests (by forcibly excluding unwanted migrants). Finally, I have shown that disproportionate immigration enforcement, which is routinely practiced by many affluent states, is unjust. In my research I have critically examined the normal justifications for states to inflict harms on individuals—collective self-defence, protecting property rights, and criminal punishment—and apply them to the context of immigration enforcement. My research found that these justifications have placed significant moral constraints on immigration enforcement. To sum up, my research has considered several problems migration and citizenship allocation as a matter of justice. I have fully achieved this objective in exploring justice requires with respect to migration and citizenship allocation. Objective 2: To discuss the moral implications of background global injustice for immigration and citizenship policies In this research project, I have identified and discussed several implications of background global injustices (and how the states have responded to such injustice) on immigration and citizenship policies. Three such implications were highlighted. First, background injustices could limit the state’s right to exclude prospective immigrants. This is the case even when the moral justification of the state’s right to exclude is grounded in their collective right to political self-determination. Second, background injustices could limit the way in which the state may permissibly enforce its right to exclude. It has been argued that a state’s right to exclude migrants is based on its territorial right as a kind of property right. However, the requirements of necessity and proportionality exclude the use of lethal force in defence of property, as there are effective remedies for property damage, whereas similar remedies are not available for personal injury or death. Third, states (especially affluent countries) are obligated not to take advantage of existing background injustices in their immigration and citizenship policies. To sum up, I have discussed the moral implications of background global injustice on immigration and citizenship policies from different perspectives. I believe I have fully achieved this objective. Objective 3: To determine the respective rights and duties of prospective migrants, long-term residents and non-resident citizens A number of prominent theorists in migration ethics have argued for a general right to immigrate (or freedom of international movement). Instead of following their paths, I have argued in this research that unjustly disadvantaged persons have a morally more urgent claim to migrate (and be admitted) as prospective migrants. Also, I have argued that migrants and long-term residents who have entered their host country without authorization should not be subject to criminal punishment for immigration violations if their legal rights are not generally being respected in that country. This objective has only been partially achieved because of its scope is so wide. For the project, I have focused on the immigration-related rights of prospective migrants and the long-term residents who have come to their country without proper authorization. Objective 4: To identify and defend the normative principles for acquisition, attribution and revocation of citizenship Many debates in migration ethics have been conducted in a highly abstract and idealized fashion. In this research project, I have defended the relevance of a state’s duty of global distributive justice to their right to exclude migrants in a non-ideal situation. Although I have not identified a set of normative principles as in ideal theorizing, my approach has contributed to the academic discussions of migration by exploring the moral implications of background injustice and highlighting the coercive nature of immigration enforcement as it is actually practiced. I have only partially achieved this objective in my research so far. This is partly due to my decision to focus more on the non-ideal side of migration and citizenship instead of taking a more idealized and abstract approach. My decision was inspired by some conversations I had with other scholars working in the same field during conferences or workshops. Objective 5: To consider the relationship between citizenship allocation and global distributive justice My research has analysed the relationship between citizenship allocation and global distributive justice from two distinct perspectives. The first perspective focused on whether the collective right to political self-determination gives the state, acting on behalf of its members, an unqualified right to decide citizenship allocation. I started with the thesis that political self-determination for all states was a fundamental principle in the existing international order, and then critically examined some contemporary theories defending the right to immigration control (which is essential to citizenship allocation) was integral to self-determination. I have invoked the idea of self-determination as a form of non-domination, arguing that, although non-domination can ground a collective right against colonization or settlement, it cannot ground a unilateral right to exclude outsiders in general. My contribution is to strike a delicate balance between a state’s right to control immigration based on the value of non-domination and the freedom of movement of potential migrants. The second perspective engaged with the question of immigration enforcement, which has tremendous impacts on citizenship allocation in the contemporary world. Background injustice at the global level serves to reduce the moral benefits of using force to guard membership goods in affluent states since it calls into the question the legitimacy of the distribution of goods and state members’ entitlement to their state’s current holdings. This claim does not offer a positive argument for a general right to immigrate. However, if the citizenship premium enjoyed by the members of affluent societies is partly the product of global background injustice, then we refute an important moral justification of states’ use of force to defend these benefits – namely, that only members are entitled to receive them. To sum up, my research for this project has emphasized that citizenship allocation has important implications for global distributive justice. This is linked to two factors: first, the world is characterized with staggering global social and economic inequalities; and, second, the affluent states regularly use their power to restrict migration. I believe this objective has been fully achieved.

22611219.label: Major findings and research outcome
22611219.value: In this research project, I have defended the following theses in the moral and political philosophy and international migration and citizenship: The collective right to political self-determination cannot provide an adequate justification for the state’s discretionary right to immigration control. Endorsing the presumptive right to restrict immigration does not settle the question of when or how it may permissibly inflict harms on individuals to enforce this right. Any immigration enforcement measure that involves lethal force or the infliction of severe bodily harm, which is routinely practiced by many states and considered legitimate, is morally impermissible; criminal sanctions for immigration violations are difficult to justify when their host countries does not extend the protection of law to irregular migrants. Background distributive injustice limits states’ right to exclude prospective migrants and how they might permissibly enforce such a right. Denationalization (or citizenship revocation), when properly constrained, is a justifiable response by liberal states to political wrongdoing, understood to be wrongs committed against the integrity of liberal democratic institutions or violations of others’ democratic rights with a wrongful intention.

22611219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
22611219.value: One question that stemmed from the research project is about the conditions under which liberal democracies exclude potential immigrants based on their political commitments. For instance, is it morally permissible for democratic states to exclude potential immigrants who do not accept democratic norms and values? Another question concerns the extent to which citizens or long-term residents have a duty to stay (not to emigrate). Political theorists debating the ethics of emigration (or the right to leave one’s country) have largely focused on the potential harmful impacts of brain drain on a country’s economic and social development. For instance, the emigration young and skilled workers (e.g. medical professionals) are likely to harm the social and economic development of the sending country (which is likely to be poor). What is missing from the current academic debates is the fact that emigration is also a political choice—that is, the potential emigrants are looking for more political freedom and democratic rights in their destination country.

22611219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
22611219.value: The proposed project investigates how the ethics of migration and citizenship would intersect with larger questions of global distributive justice. In today’s world, a person’s residency or citizenship can have a profound impact on her wellbeing, freedom, and even survival. There is clearly a global hierarchy of citizenship worth. Many in the Global South are desperately seeking to migrate in order to escape poverty or oppression. They would have to cross some heavily guarded and even militarized borders. At the same time, anti-immigration populist movements are on the rise in many affluent Western societies. Many members in these societies believe that their economic opportunities, communal life, and distinctive national culture are now under threat due to increased immigration. However, immigration restrictions are in fact highly selective. Borders are often only open to those migrants who are considered ‘desirable’ by the receiving state either for economic, political, cultural, or demographic reasons.

23500019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23500019.value: Previous research suggests that short-sale constraints on firm stocks can influence firms’ public disclosure incentives and practices (Karpoff & Lou 2010; Fang et al. 2015). Complementing these studies, this study examines whether short-sale constraints will influence market participants’ information acquisition activities, and consequently, the corporate information environment. In particular, the study will examine whether short-sale constraints affect market participants’ incentives to engage in access to management (AoM), which has long been recognized as a significant channel for outside investors to obtain firm-specific information (Soltes 2014). Edmans (2009) suggests that relaxation of short-sale constraints enhances investors’ incentives to gather firm-specific information because it provides investors with an additional channel to trade on the information. AoM allows market participants to obtain valuable corporate information through direct observation and assessment of various informational cues rather than passively relying on information offered by managers. As a result, AoM is likely to be an important information source for short sellers who are often sophisticated investors. Furthermore, the participation in AoM events is voluntary, which offers a testing ground to discern how the relaxation of short-sale constraints may affect investors’ underlying incentives to acquire information. To conduct the test, I will exploit the 2005 Regulation SHO pilot program in the U.S. as a shock to the short-sale constraints. The program imposes a relaxation of short-sale constraints on a subset of randomly chosen stocks (pilot stocks), but no change on the undesignated non-pilot stocks. Using a difference-in-difference approach, I will investigate whether the relaxation of short-sale constraints increases investors’ efforts in AoM (i.e. higher frequency and intensity of engaging in AoM). I will then examine whether AoM becomes more informative (causes a greater market reaction), and consequently, moves stock prices closer to firm fundamentals. Moreover, I will use transaction-level data to examine how short sellers trade around AoM and whether they obtain advantages and benefits from AoM. This project is important in several ways. First, while AoM has grown substantially, there is limited evidence concerning participants’ underlying incentives. This study identifies short-sale constraint as an important factor in shaping outsiders’ incentives to engage in AoM. Second, this study documents a specific channel (i.e. acquiring soft-information via AoM) through which short-sellers can obtain informational advantages. Lastly, this study shows that AoM can be an important means of improving market efficiency. The project calls for the simultaneous implementation of policies to promote corporate interactive communications and reduce short-sale constraints in financial markets. 摘要 之前的研究表明，公司股票的賣空限制可以影響公司的公開披露激勵和實踐（Karpoff＆Lou 2010; Fang et al.2015）。作為對這些研究的延申，本研究考察賣空限制是否會影響市場參與者的信息獲取活動，進而影響企業信息環境。特別地，該研究將審查賣空限制是否會影響市場參與者接觸公司管理層（AoM）的動機，AoM長期以來被認為是外部投資者獲取公司特定信息的重要渠道（Soltes 2014）。 Edmans（2009）認為，放鬆賣空限制可以增強投資者收集公司特定信息的動力，因為它為投資者提供了額外的信息交易渠道。 AoM允許市場參與者通過直接觀察和評估各種信息線索而不是被動地依賴管理者提供的信息來獲取有價值的公司信息。因此，對於是老練投資者的賣空者來說，AoM可能是一個重要的信息來源。此外，參與AoM活動是自願的，這為檢測放鬆賣空限制是如何影響投資者獲取信息的潛在動機提供了一個很好的試驗場。 為了進行測試，我將利用美國2005年的SHO試點計劃作為對賣空限制的衝擊。該計劃對隨機挑選的一部分股票(試點股票)放寬賣空限制，但對未指定的非試點股票不作任何改變。我將使用“差中之差”的方法來研究放寬賣空限制是否會增加投資者對AoM的努力投入(即更高的參與AoM的頻率和強度)。然後，我將研究AoM是否變得更有信息含量（引起更大的市場反應），從而使股票價格更接近公司的基本面。此外，我將使用交易級別的數據來研究賣空者是如何圍繞AoM進行交易的，以及他們是否從AoM獲得了優勢和利潤。 該項目的重要性體現在幾個方面。首先，雖然AoM已很普遍，但參與者進行此類活動的動機還不詳。本研究將賣空限制視為影響外部人參與AoM的重要因素。其次，該研究描繪了一個特定的渠道（即通過AoM獲取軟信息），通過該渠道，賣空者可以獲得信息優勢。最後，本研究表明，AoM可以成為提高市場效率的重要手段。該項目呼籲同時推進促進企業互動溝通以及減少金融市場的賣空限制的相關政策。

23500019.label: Realisation of objectives
23500019.value: To investigate our research questions and achieve the research objective, we identify exogenous shocks in short-sale constraints and study their impact on investors' information acquisition activities. Specifically, we exploit two quasi-natural experiments that relax short-sale constraints in the US and China, respectively. In the US, we examine the Regulation SHO pilot program of the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), which temporarily removed the uptick price test for a pilot group of stocks in 2015. In China, we examine the addition to, and deletion from a list of designated stocks for which the short ban was lifted and short selling was allowed. To measure investors’ information acquisition activities, for US stocks, we use the terabyte data of the Electronic Data Gathering, Analysis, and Retrieval (EDGAR) system’s search volumes to measure investors’ demand for SEC filings. In addition, we parse the text of the transcripts of earnings conference calls to count the numbers of participating analysts and questions asked by them. For Chinese stocks, we measure information acquisition using corporate site visits, a prevalent form of information acquisition by market participants in China. Based on these settings, we obtained results consistent with our expectation and achieved the proposed research objectives. The achievement of “1. Examine whether short-sale constraints affect investors’ incentives and efforts to engage in AoM.” We find that investors increase their information acquisition when the short-sale constraints are relaxed. Specifically, based on the US setting, we find that, compared to the control firms, the treated firms, whose price test constraint is removed (pilot stocks), experience an increase in EDGAR search volumes and numbers of questions and answers (Q&As) in the earnings conference calls during the pilot program period. In China, firms experience an increase (decrease) in corporate site visits when they are added to (deleted from) the designated stock list. The achievement of “2. Examine whether the relaxation of short-sale constraints improves the informativeness of AoM and eventually stock price efficiency.” 1) We find that, when short-sale constraints are reduced, new information is indeed incorporated into stock prices, which is essential for price discovery and market efficiency. Specifically, we find that the US market reacts more strongly to treated firms’ quarterly filings with higher EDGAR search volumes. Similarly, we find that market reaction to conference calls in the US and to corporate site visits in China are stronger for the treated firms compared to the control firms when analysts or investors ask more questions in those meetings. The results thus suggest that the relaxation of short-sale constraints allows investors to acquire value-relevant information and incorporate it into the stock prices during these corporate events. 2) We find that information acquisition induced by the reduction of short-sale constraints improves price efficiency. Specifically, we measure price efficiency using both high- and low-frequency variables, as in previous studies (e.g., Boehmer and Wu, 2013). Consistent with short selling enhancing price efficiency, we find that, relative to control firms, treated firms experience a decline in return autocorrelations and an increase in the speed of adjustment to market-wide information. Importantly, we find that the effects are concentrated among firms with higher EDGAR search volumes and are more pronounced among firms with more corporate site visits. The achievement of “3. Examine how short sellers trade around AoM and whether they obtain advantages and benefits from AoM.” We find evidence that short sellers trade around AoM and are compensated for their costly efforts of information acquisition. 1) We build on prior studies that show that short-selling activities are negatively related to subsequent stock returns (Asquith et al., 2005; Boehmer et al., 2008) and test how information acquisition affects the return predictability of short sales. We find that the negative relation between short volumes and future stock returns is concentrated among days when short positions are taken along with high EDGAR search volumes and corporate site visits, suggesting that investors indeed benefit from their information acquisition efforts. 2) Exploiting information on the opening and closing of short positions in the Chinese market, we further find that corporate site visits inform short sellers to increase (reduce) their short positions before stock price declines (increases). The results thus suggest that information acquisition benefits short sellers by improving their trading decisions. The achievement of “4. Examine how the effects of short-sale constraints on AoM vary with firms’ valuation uncertainty, governance strength, and the coverage of institutional investors, analysts, and news media.” We conduct various additional analyses to explore the heterogeneity of the effects of short-sale constraints on AoM: 1) We find that financial institutions (e.g., hedge funds) respond to the relaxation of short-sale constraints by increasing EDGAR searches more strongly than non-institutions (e.g., retail investors), consistent with sophisticated investors being often both information acquirer and short-sellers. 2) We conduct stacked regressions and propensity score matching analyses to strengthen the causal inference and find that adding to (dropping from) the pilot program in China increases (decreases) corporate site visits. 3) We find that investors’ information acquisition activities respond to the reduction in short-sale constraints more promptly in China than in the US. This result likely reflects two facts: a) the short-sale regulation in China lifts a short ban, whereas, in the US, it just removes the uptick price test, one of many constraints on shorting, and b) corporate transparency and stock price efficiency are generally lower in China than in the US. 4) Furthermore, we find that information acquisition in both markets gradually declines thereafter. This result suggests that the marginal benefits of information acquisition decrease as more information is traded on and incorporated into the market over time. 5) Lastly, we find that improved price discovery and market efficiency is concentrated among corporate events with negative market reactions in both markets. The result suggests that a reduction of short-sale constraints facilitates the acquisition of bad news. Overall, we obtained results that support our hypotheses, and address and achieve the four research objectives documented the proposal.

23500019.label: Major findings and research outcome
23500019.value: The funding of the project supports the development of two research papers. Paper#1: Su, Lixin (Nancy) and Wong, Sonia Man-Lai and Xue, Yuan and Zhao, Xiaofeng, Do Short-Sale Constraints Inhibit Information Acquisition? Evidence from the US and Chinese Markets (January 15, 2021). Available at SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3766616 or http://dx.doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3766616 Paper#2: Xue, S., Zhang, B. and Zhao, X., 2021. Brain drain: The impact of air pollution on firm performance. Journal of Environmental Economics and Management, 110, p.102546. Major findings of Paper#1: By exploiting two settings that relax short-sale constraints in the US and China, respectively, we find that the removal of short-sale constraints increases investors’ information acquisition in both markets, but the effect is more prompt in China. Investors acquire value-relevant information, especially bad news, and improve their short-selling decisions in both markets. Lastly, information acquisition induced by the removal of short-sale constraints improves price efficiency. Our evidence shows that a reduction in trading frictions promotes information acquisition and improves price efficiency. Major findings of Paper#2: We find that people exhibit an intention to look for jobs in less polluted areas when air pollution is high in their location. This suggests that individuals arrange their lives at least partially in response to air pollution. Consistent with this hypothesis, we find that the level of skilled executives and employees at a firm drops significantly when information on pollution in the firm's location is accessible in real time and when the pollution level in the firm's location increases, especially in locations where air pollution poses greater health concerns. Research outcomes: 1) Paper#1 is published in SSRN, which received 192 downloads and 957 abstract views as of December 13, 2023. Available at SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3766616 or http://dx.doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3766616 2) Paper#1 was presented in Asian Finance Association (AsianFA) Annual Conference and the department of Finance at Xi’an Jiaotong-Liverpool University. 3) Paper#1 is now under the status of “Revise and Resubmit” at the Journal of Financial Market (JFM). We are revising the paper and will resubmit the paper back to JFM by Apr 06, 2024. 4) Paper#2 is published in Journal of Environmental Economics and Management (ABS 3; the impact factor is 5.8).

23500019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23500019.value: We hand-collected and built up a database of transcripts of communication between investors and firms. Specifically, we parsed the text of the transcripts of earnings conference calls to count the numbers of participating analysts and questions asked by them in US. We also collected the transcripts of corporate site visits for firms listed in Shenzhen Stock Exchange and identified the number of participating investors and the number of questions asked by them in each site visit. The database provides a novel measure of information acquisition via private communications, which may benefit future research in related fields. One potential research area is to examine whether the introduction of ChatGPT has a significant impact on investors’ information acquisition. On one hand, ChatGPT empowers people to use various sources of information, potentially reducing the marginal benefits of acquiring information through traditional methods. This could lead to a decrease in information acquisition via EDGAR, conference calls, and site visits. On the other hand, ChatGPT lowers investors’ information processing costs, enhancing their ability to consume information. This might result in an increase in information acquisition. Therefore, the impact of ChatGPT on information acquisition remains an empirical question.

23500019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23500019.value: The research examines whether investors are more likely to gather information about a company when the company's stock is open to short-selling or when the restrictions on short-selling are relaxed. We found evidence supporting this idea in both the US and Chinese markets. Additionally, we discovered that investors with fewer short-selling constraints tend to acquire valuable information, particularly about negative news, which then helps them make better short-selling decisions. This behavior ultimately leads to improved stock price efficiency. The research provides evidence that easing short-sale constraints enhances price efficiency by motivating traders to collect information. It suggests that capital market regulators should be cautious when considering policies to ban short sales during crisis periods, as such bans could hinder the overall production of information and potentially exacerbate the crisis.

23601219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601219.value: 本項目采取語言景觀的視角深入研究轉型期中國的地方營造活動。在發展城市化，工業化和旅遊業的過程中，當代中國不同的社會成員運用各種形式的語言和符號資源來建構新的社會空間。由此而來，新的，舊的，新建的具備“歷史感”的地方空間，為人們帶來充滿差異的時間感 – 而這些差異也正在重新塑造人們的地方感。以語言景觀為研究對象，本項目旨在闡明當代中國社會多層面的社會變化。 基於其獨特的視覺交流的屬性和效果，漢字書寫系統迥異於其他字母和表音書寫系統。不僅如此，在中文書法實踐中，書寫是壹種具身的身體行為，並且高度反映書寫者的人格。此觀點在傳統中國山水文化中得到強化：各種書寫文本例如題字和碑刻常用來提升自然景觀的人文性，美學和道德維度。目前在社會語言學領域，還沒有研究涉及到中文書寫和語言景觀的文化歷史獨特性。 因此基於社會語言學，文化地理學， 和書法學的相關研究，本項目試圖制定新的適合研究中文語言景觀的理論框架。采用Järlehed 和 Jaworski 於 2015年提出的“字體景觀”概念，我將傳統書法字體和各種現代字體都歸於 “字體”之下。同時，我計劃在此框架中進壹步理論化中文書寫中共存的新舊字體形式以及它們風格各異的符號和象征意義。 此理論框架以及其他現存的研究方法將會應用於兩個地點的研究 （每個地點展示轉型期中國的壹個顯著特點）。 從城市變化和農村轉型兩個方面，這些個案研究旨在提供全面，具體的視角來視覺化當代中國的社會發展。兩個研究地點都采用了大量的中文符號資源。通過研究這些語言景觀，我意在深入調查以下問題：在今天的社會，人們越來越多的運用印刷和數碼科技進行中文書寫，中文書寫的意義有何變化？書寫和人格之間的聯系還存在嗎？轉型期的中國民眾建構並觀賞中文語言景觀，他們看到的是什麽，他們的地方感有何變化？於此之外，個案研究力求討論更廣層面的文化，社會和政治議題例如城市化和歷史空間建構，發展農村旅遊業以及新興中國消費社會的權力關系。

23601319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23601319.value: The interaction between politicians and firms is a central issue in an economy. Prior studies highlight that firms with connections to the government officials enjoy the preferential treatments, such as access to finance and government concessions. Yet, it is less understood that whether and to what extent the governing style of local top politicians shapes corporate policies and the underlying mechanisms. This project proposes a method to explicitly quantify the impact of the top local politicians on corporate behaviors. The method is based on the unique politician rotation system in China that generates a large variation in politician turnovers at different government levels (province, city, and county) and a census data of all above-scale manufacturing firms. A politician-firm matched panel data set is constructed to track a list of local politicians and corresponding firms governed by the politicians. Controlling for both observable and unobservable differences across firms, this study attempts to evaluate the similarity of corporate behaviors of firms operating in different regions but governed by the same politician at different time periods. This study will shed light on whether “politician fixed effects” matter for a wide range of corporate decisions, such as investments, employment, leverage, exporting, innovation and land transactions. For each corporate policy of interest, the model will generate a measure of the additional explanatory power of the “politician fixed effect” for each government-level of politicians. The project will dig into the underlying channels of the politician effects. First, by examining the heterogeneity of the politician effects among SEOs affiliated to different levels of government, private firms and foreign firms, this project attempts to uncover how politician affect the corporate behavior through sending commands to SOEs and the resulting spillover effects. Second, this study will identify the heterogeneous effects of politicians according to the quality of regional institution. The project will explore whether politician effects will be exaggerated by weak property right protection and severe government intervention. Last, this project will try to link the politician effects to the observable politician characteristics. The hand-collected dataset on the detailed demographics (birthplace, education etc.) of politicians facilitates an analysis on whether early-life experience (such as exposure to violence) and foreign education matter for governing style. Quantifying the magnitude of the politician effects on firm behavior, this proposed research uncovers the black box of the relationship between politicians and firms and has policy implications for the design of the political promotion system. 官員和企業之間的互動是經濟中的核心問題。之前的研究強調，與政府官員有聯系的公司享受優惠待遇，例如獲得融資和政府特許權。然而，人們不太了解當地政府官員的執政風格是否以及在多大程度上影響了公司政策和潛在機制。該項目提出了一種方法，可以明確量化當地官員對企業行為的影響。 該方法基於中國獨特的官員輪換制度，即在不同政府層面（省，市和縣）產生大量政治人員輪換變化，以及所有規模以上制造業公司的獨特普查數據。本研究建立一個官員-公司匹配的面板數據集來跟蹤當地政客所管理的相應公司的名單。本研究試圖控制不同地區的可觀察和不可觀察的差異，試圖評估在不同地區經營但在不同時期由同壹官員管理的公司的公司行為的相似性。這項研究將闡明 “官員固定效應” 是否對廣泛的公司決策很重要，例如投資，就業，杠桿，出口，創新和土地交易。對於每個重要的公司政策，該模型將為每個政府級別的官員產生 “固定效應” 的額外解釋力量。 該項目將挖掘官員影響的潛在渠道。首先，通過檢查隸屬於不同級別的政府，私營公司和外國公司的之間官員效應的異質性，該項目試圖通過向國有企業發送命令以及由此產生的溢出效應來揭示官員如何影響公司行為。其次，本研究將根據區域制度的質量來確定官員的異質性影響。該項目將探討是否會因產權保護薄弱和政府嚴厲幹預而擴大官員的影響。最後，該項目將嘗試將官員效應與可觀察的官員特征聯系起來。通過手工收集的關於官員的詳細個人數據（出生地，教育等）有助於分析早期生活經歷（如接觸暴力）和外國教育是否對治理方式有影響。 通過量化政府官員對公司行為影響的程度，這項研究揭示了官員與公司之間關系的黑匣子，並對政治晉升制度的設計具有政策含義。

23601319.label: Realisation of objectives
23601319.value: The objectives set in the proposal have been largely achieved. In the following, the details of the realization are provided. Firstly, the project examines the role of local politicians, or 'politician fixed effects,' and their influence on various business decisions. This includes how much companies invest, the number of people they employ, their financial tactics, export behavior, innovation efforts, and real estate interactions. Our research specifically finds that politicians heavily sway corporate actions associated with risky ventures, such as developing new technologies, taking on debt, and making large investments. These findings underscore the significant role politicians play in shaping local economic landscapes by pushing firms toward or away from risky but potentially rewarding activities. The direction of this influence can lead to two distinct outcomes: it can either foster a culture of boldness and innovation or create a more cautious and reserved business climate, depending on the politician's personal style and economic vision. Understanding this influence is key to grasping the different speeds and types of economic development across China. It points out that local economic outcomes are not just the result of broad national policies but are deeply affected by the risk tolerance and leadership approach of individual politicians. This insight sheds light on the varied economic progress seen across various Chinese regions, highlighting the importance of localized political leadership in influencing the vigor and direction of economic change. Secondly, the project explores how politician effects vary among different types of businesses, such as state-owned enterprises (SOEs), private firms, and multinationals. We find that SOEs, especially those tied to various government levels, are the most affected by politician effects. This is because SOEs are closely linked with political goals and are under the strong influence of local officials. SOEs rely on government resources like special contracts and financial support, but they also get non-financial help like favorable policies and regulatory backing, which are essential for their operations and growth. Moreover, SOEs are key to implementing government policies, serving as tools for local politicians to apply their influence and achieve wider economic and social goals. The relationship between politicians and SOEs stands out because these enterprises are at the crossroads of business and government mandates. While private and foreign companies do deal with political factors, SOEs are in a unique position where they benefit from government support and, in return, are expected to support the political and economic aims of the governing authorities. Our study here adds new insights to the existing research on SOEs by highlighting the deep ties between political leaders and these companies. By looking at this relationship, we offer a fresh perspective on how local politicians use SOEs to impact economic conditions, shape the competitive landscape, and push their strategic plans. Thirdly, the project will scrutinize the variations in politician effects across different regions, paying particular attention to how these effects are modulated by the strength of property rights enforcement and the extent of government intervention. Through our detailed analysis, we've observed pronounced interactions between local institutional frameworks and the influence exerted by politicians. In regions where institutions are robust and there is a greater openness to international influences and foreign cultures, the sway of local politicians appears to be less pronounced. This finding is particularly significant in areas that have made concerted efforts to establish strong legal systems and transparent governance practices, which in turn have cultivated an environment where private enterprise can flourish with less direct political interference. In contrast, regions with weaker institutional frameworks tend to exhibit stronger politician effects, as the local economy and business decisions are more susceptible to the whims of political influence. Moreover, in regions that are more globally integrated and receptive to foreign investment and cultural exchange, the local political impact seems to be buffered. Such regions may benefit from a diversity of ideas and practices that can dilute the concentration of political power and provide alternative pathways for economic and corporate development. The evidence we've gathered contributes to the political economy literature by emphasizing the critical role that institutions play in shaping the economic landscape. It suggests that strong institutions can serve as a check on political power and can help create an environment where businesses make decisions based on market dynamics and efficiency rather than political directives. Fourthly, the project endeavors to establish a connection between the distinct governing styles that emerge from politician effects and the personal histories of the politicians themselves. This includes their life experiences, particularly any impact felt from the Cultural Revolution, or influences from time spent abroad for education. To do this, we have meticulously curated the data to gauge the local exposure to the Cultural Revolution and investigate the varying effects of politicians who endured significant turmoil during that era. Our analysis goes a step further by examining how the enduring ethos of Confucian culture in China might shape a politician's approach to governance and their subsequent effect on economic activities. By exploring this, we aim to trace the roots of a politician's governing style back to their formative experiences or the historical legacy that they carry forward into their political careers. Specifically, we look at whether those with severe experiences during the Cultural Revolution exhibit distinctive patterns in their decision-making processes, potentially leading to more conservative or radical policy implementations. Similarly, the influence of an international education may introduce different perspectives and approaches to governance, possibly promoting more openness to global market practices and innovation. The trajectory from these early personal experiences to current governing styles is critical to understanding the diversity of politician effects across China. Lastly, the project is set to examine the influence of politicians' leadership styles on local business performance and efficiency and how these factors contribute to their professional trajectories within the political hierarchy. We aim to understand if and how the political system rewards leaders based on their ability to stimulate economic progress in their jurisdictions. On one hand, our findings support the notion of a 'tournament theory' within the Chinese political framework, where there is a systemic endorsement of politicians who actively champion local economic expansion. Such politicians often find themselves on a faster track for promotion, suggesting that the political system values and incentivizes immediate economic achievements. This promotion effect remains consistent, even when these politicians are reassigned to different regions, indicating that their reputation for fostering growth follows them throughout their careers. On the other hand, our study raises concerns about the prevalence of short-termism in policy-making among these upwardly mobile politicians. The pressure to deliver rapid economic results can lead to a focus on short-term gains at the expense of long-term prosperity and innovation. This approach can potentially stunt sustained economic development and discourage the adoption of forward-thinking initiatives, which are essential for long-term economic health and innovation. The tension between the desire for quick economic wins and the necessity for sustainable growth strategies presents a complex challenge within the political promotion system. Our project thus contributes to the dialogue on political economy, questioning the balance between immediate economic success and enduring economic strategy.

23601319.label: Major findings and research outcome
23601319.value: The project has successfully shown the strong influence that top local politicians have on business decisions within China. By tracking the movements of politicians and combining that with detailed data from manufacturing companies, we've found that the leadership styles of politicians can significantly shape corporate actions. We collected a lot of data to see how politicians and companies are connected. Our findings, which we call "politician fixed effects," suggest that the behavior of politicians can tell us a lot about company strategies. One key takeaway is that political influence doesn't affect all companies in the same way. State-owned, private, and foreign companies each respond differently to politicians' directions. When a politician gives orders to a state-owned company, it can end up influencing other businesses too. We also discovered that the strength of local laws and the level of government involvement can affect how much influence politicians have. In places where property rights are weak and the government is more involved, political influence seems stronger. The datasets we've built for this project are really valuable. They've not only supported the writing of two research papers but are also being used for more related studies. For instance, one paper studies the impact of politicians leaving company boards on the economy. Another project uses the data to look at how companies react to big challenges, like trade frictions between the US and China. Looking ahead, this newly created database will be a key resource for even more projects. It's poised to help researchers dive deeper into the complex relationship between political leadership and business operations in China, providing a rich source of information for future studies. This project has opened doors to a better understanding between politics and business in China and has laid the groundwork for others to build upon.

23601319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
23601319.value: The scope of this project extends beyond its initial findings, with several additional research angles poised for exploration. A key extension involves delving into the policymaking implications of the observed politician effect. We aim to conduct an in-depth analysis of the entire corpus of policy texts in China to discern whether individual politicians exhibit distinctive styles in championing specific agendas. This could include a propensity for security-oriented measures, indicative of a more protectionist approach, or policies leaning towards economic openness and liberalization. Furthermore, the project intends to investigate the divergent responses of various regions—be it cities or counties—to external economic pressures. A focal point of this analysis will be the regional variance in responses to the trade tensions between the United States and China. By examining how these regions adapt to such trade frictions, the research could uncover patterns of resilience or vulnerability linked to the governing styles of their local politicians. This extended analysis could provide valuable insights into the granular impact of political leadership on regional economic performance, especially under the strain of international trade disputes.

23601319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
23601319.value: The completed project has successfully quantified the significant impact of local top politicians on corporate behaviors within China's economy. Utilizing the country's distinctive politician rotation system and extensive manufacturing firm data, the research revealed that the governance style of politicians has measurable effects on a wide array of corporate decisions. The study constructed a detailed politician-firm matched dataset. The findings confirmed the existence of "politician fixed effects," demonstrating that these effects have substantial explanatory power over corporate policies. Key insights include the discovery that political influence varies among state-owned, private, and foreign firms, indicating that commands directed at SOEs can spill over and affect the broader corporate landscape. Furthermore, the project examined how regional institutional quality modulates these politician effects, with weaker property rights and greater government intervention intensifying the impact. The project generates a series of new datasets that are used in several related projects, including two published papers. For example, one paper uses the dataset on politician career path and examine the turnover of politicians from corporate boards and the economic impact. In another project, we examine the firm level effect of trade frictions using the datasets on region and firm level variables created in this funded project.

23605119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
23605119.value: This research project investigates popular culture and creative industries in Asia through a study of an important yet largely under-researched group of transnational creative subjects: diasporic Filipino musicians active in the recording and live music industries of Hong Kong and Singapore. It focuses on a pivotal period in recent popular culture history—the crucial postcolonial years between 1965 to 1989—to make the case that music-making in this region possesses a distinctly transpopular character. The term “transpopular” is proposed to describe the interconnectedness of musical practices, roles, styles, languages, conventions, and activities across spheres of leisure and labour (education, entertainment, paid work); industry sectors (live music, radio, TV, and film); audiences; and geographical registers (local/regional/global scales of culture and economy). Although relegated to the margins and footnotes of national histories of Asian popular music, existing research has shown that diasporic Filipino musicians were active facilitators and collaborators with local musicians in developing transpopular material that reflected the unique flavour and preferences of domestic and regional markets, notably through their capacities as intermediary performers in the “backstage” of industrialised popular music, and as “familiar strangers” who mediated creative relationships with local and other foreign musicians. As session/supporting musicians, music directors and coaches, producers, and arrangers in both recorded and live music contexts, these musicians translated creative content between the diverse functions, media, genres, and languages inherent in popular music production. The diasporic Filipino musician therefore represents the distinctly collaborative and transitive character of popular music in the region at a pivotal cultural, economic, and political period of Asian culture, characterised by the constant tension between adopting (whether closely imitating or loosely adapting) the “foreign” trends of Western Anglo-American music on the one hand; and on the other, crafting a musical form that reflected the particular and vernacular preferences of its target urban audiences. The stories and voices of the Filipino musicians to be featured in this project newly reveal this tension to have always been a productive and creative one from its postwar beginnings, using the performance practices of imitation, collaboration, and localisation to create a remarkably porous network of popular music consumption and production. By recovering a recent, pivotal history of popular music-making in the region from the perspective of its everyday workers, Transpopular Musics aims to offer fresh answers to the contemporary challenge of developing sustainable communities, practices, and policies of creativity within the uniquely global-local position of Asia. 跨流行音樂：在香港和新加坡的離散菲律賓音樂家（1960s-1980s） 本計畫通過研究一個重要卻受忽視的跨國創作群體——活躍在香港和新加坡現場音樂和唱片行業的離散菲律賓音樂家，來探討亞洲的流行文化和創意產業。本研究計畫聚焦于當代流行文化史上的一個關鍵時期，即1965年到1989年的殖民時期，來說明這一時期東南亞的音樂創作具有典型的“跨流行”特徵。“跨流行”主要描述不同音樂、角色、風格、語言和習俗與娛樂和工作活動（教育、娛樂和有償工作）、不同行業（現場音樂、廣播、電視和電影）、不同聽眾以及不同地域（地方/區域/全球的文化和經濟）的相互關聯。 儘管現有的研究把離散菲律賓音樂家降格為亞洲流行音樂的注腳，它們也說明了離散菲律賓音樂家是發展跨流行音樂——展現地方和區域市場的獨特風味和偏好——的積極推動者，這體現在他們能夠成為產業化流行文化背後的中間人，以及作為“熟悉的陌生人”來調解與當地和其他外國音樂家的關係。通過扮演不同的角色，比如錄音室樂手，音樂指揮家和指導，製片人，編曲家，這些音樂家在流行音樂生產的不同媒介、類別、功能和語言之間傳遞創意內容。 因此，菲律賓離散音樂家充分體現出了東南亞流行文化的合作和轉型兩大特點。此時，亞洲文化處於文化、政治和經濟的一個關鍵時期，這體現它在既想採納（不管是竭力模仿還是隨意改編）西方英美的“異域”潮流又想創作出能反映亞洲城市聽眾獨特偏好的音樂形式之間的衝突。本研究所探討的菲律賓音樂家的聲音和故事表明了這種衝突從戰後開始一直具有創造力且富有成效。 從普通音樂家的視角來重塑流行音樂產生的一段重要的當代史，跨流行音樂旨在對發展亞洲可持續的共同體和文化創意政策的當代挑戰提供新的答案。

24108519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24108519.value: Currently, there are approximately 300,000 hip fractures per year in the US with a mortality rate of 20% within 1 year. In Hong Kong, around 6,000 hip fractures occur yearly with costs approximately 52 million USD, and these numbers are projected to double by 2050. The treatment of osteoporotic fractures is a major challenge as bone healing is delayed due to the impaired healing properties with respect to bone formation, angiogenesis and mineralization. Failure to unite results in pain, weakness, reduced mobility and fixation failure, and these complications are most common in elderly patients. Enhancement of osteoporotic fracture healing even after surgical fixation is therefore critical as a major goal in modern fracture management. Low-magnitude high-frequency vibration (LMHFV) is a biophysical intervention that provides non-invasive, systemic mechanical stimulation and we are the first group to study its effect on fracture healing. Our previous animal studies have shown LMHFV to enhance healing from the early inflammation stage to the late phases of remodeling in osteoporotic diaphyseal fracture healing. Using our newly developed clinically relevant metaphyseal fracture model, we further proved the efficacy of LMHFV. Our results show LMHFV significantly enhanced fracture healing in both osteoporotic and normal rats radiologically by X-ray and micro-CT, histologically and biomechanically. To translate our pre-clinical data to clinical application, we conducted a pilot study of 40 trochanteric hip fracture patients. LMHFV enhanced fracture healing with X-rays showing earlier bone bridging at week 6 (p=0.04) and significantly higher relative radio-opacity at week 6 (0.73±0.13 vs. 0.56±0.09) (p=0.05) and week 12 (0.85±0.07 vs. 0.69±0.05) (p=0.05). Compliance was 95%. These findings provide convincing evidence to apply LMHFV to promote fracture healing in our hip fracture patients in this current study. Justified with our preclinical and clinical pilot studies, we hypothesize LMHFV can accelerate the time to fracture healing and enhance functional recovery. In this study, we propose to study the efficacy of LMHFV in trochanteric hip fracture healing by conducting a randomized double-blinded placebo-controlled clinical trial. Elderly patients aged 65 years or older of either gender, after surgical fixation, will be treated with LMHFV at 35Hz, 0.3g, 20 minutes/day, 5 days/week for 6 months. Results will be evaluated by clinical assessments, radiologically with X-rays, Computed Tomography (CT) and dynamic perfusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) for blood circulation evaluation, Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), functional outcomes, and mortality. Positive findings from the study would have huge impact and change clinical practice. 目前，美國每年約有300,000例髖部骨折，1年內死亡率為20％。在香港，每年約有6,000例髖部骨折個案，費用約為5200萬美元，預計這些數字到2050年將增加一倍。骨質疏鬆性骨折的治療是一項重大挑戰，因為癒合性能受損，包括骨形成，血管生成和礦化，導致癒合延遲。癒合失敗導致疼痛，虛弱，活動能力下降和骨折固定失敗，這些併發症在老年患者中最常見。因此，骨質疏鬆性骨折在手術固定後的癒合增強也是現代骨折管理的主要目標。低強度高頻振動（LMHFV）是一種生物物理干預，提供無創性，全身性機械刺激，我們是第一個研究其對骨折癒合的影響。我們以前的動物研究表明，LMHFV可以促進骨質疏鬆性骨幹骨折從早期炎症階段到重塑晚期的癒合。使用我們新開發的幹骺端骨折模型，我們進一步證明了LMHFV的功效。我們的研究結果表明，通過X線、微CT、組織學和生物力學測試，LMHFV顯著增強了骨質疏鬆和正常大鼠的骨折癒合。為了轉化為臨床應用，我們對40例轉子髖部骨折患者進行了初步研究。 LMHFV增強骨折癒合，X射線顯示第6週早期骨橋接（p = 0.04），在第6週（0.73±0.13 vs. 0.56±0.09）（p=0.05）和第12週（0.85±0.07)對0.69±0.05)（p = 0.05）的相對放射不透明度顯著提高。治療順應性為95％。這些結果為本研究中應用LMHFV促進髖部骨折患者骨折癒合提供了令人信服的證據。基於我們的臨床前和臨床試驗研究結果，我們假設LMHFV可以加速骨折癒合的時間並增強功能恢復。在這項研究中，我們建議通過進行隨機雙盲安慰劑對照臨床試驗來研究LMHFV在轉子間髖部骨折癒合中的療效。65歲或以上的任何性別的老年患者在手術固定後，將使用35HHz，0.3g，20分鐘/天，5天/週的LMHFV治療6個月。結果將通過臨床評估，放射學X射線，計算機斷層掃描（CT）和動態灌注磁共振成像（MRI）進行血液循環評估，雙能X射線吸收測定（DXA），功能和死亡率進行評估。該研究的結果將產生巨大影響並改變臨床實踐。

24108519.label: Realisation of objectives
24108519.value: 1. To investigate the efficacy of LMHFV in trochanteric hip fractures on the time to radiological healing by conducting a randomized double-blinded placebo-controlled clinical trial A randomised double-blinded placebo-controlled clinical trial was conducted with the primary outcome to assess the radiological healing in trochanteric hip fractures with low-magnitude high-frequency vibration. In order to assess this outcome, X-rays and CT scan were performed. The protocol for the duration of vibration therapy treatment was changed during the clinical trial, due to COVID-19, in which therapy was only conducted for 2 weeks instead of the original 6 months. In addition, although COVID-19 had affected the overall progress initially, we were still able to perform and achieve good publications during the project period (outcomes of hip fractures in the COVID-19 period; please refer to research output). Radiological healing assessments were found to be insignificant. All fractures in both groups healed at 3 months. Furthermore, CT scan is a gold standard in assessing fracture healing. At 6 weeks, where fracture healing usually occurs and is a good time-point to detect differences, we found that the osseous union was 61(+/-30.1)% for placebo group vs. 71.5(+/-19.4)% for the vibration group (p=0.484) with CT scan. Although there was a higher percentage osseous union rate observed, there was still an insignificant difference. This can be likely explained by the short duration of vibration therapy, and future investigations may be required whether a longer duration may lead to enhanced fracture healing. 2. To assess the effects of LMHFV in trochanteric hip fractures compared with control on clinical outcomes, densitometry, blood circulation, and mortality Regarding clinical outcomes, assessment time-points include baseline, 2 weeks, 6 weeks, 12 weeks and 26 weeks. There were several significant positive effects for the overall treatment of vibration therapy for pain, handgrip strength, quadriceps muscle strength, and balancing ability. For pain there was significant improvement for the vibration group compared to placebo group (p=0.034 for the overall treatment effect). For muscle performance, the maximum handgrip strength on the left hand was 11.7kg for placebo group and 14.2kg for vibration group at 26 weeks (p=0.000 for the overall treatment effect). For muscle performance, the maximum handgrip strength on the right hand was 13.2kg for placebo group and 15.1kg for vibration group at 26 weeks (p=0.000 for the overall treatment effect). For maximum quadriceps muscle strength on the affected lower limb, it was 5.41kg for placebo group and 8.8kg for vibration group at 26 weeks (p=0.004 for the overall treatment effect). For maximum quadriceps muscle strength on the unaffected lower limb, it was 7.1kg for placebo group and 11.7kg for vibration group at 26 weeks (p=0.004 for the overall treatment effect). For balancing ability, the overall stability index was 3.2 for placebo group and 1.6 for vibration group (p=0.033 for the overall treatment effect). There were no significant differences between the 2 groups in terms of other clinical outcomes including SF-36 and TUG test. There were also no significant differences between the 2 groups in terms of densitometry based on bone mineral density data, blood circulation based on dynamic perfusion MRI data, and mortality. There were no significant differences in terms of adverse events either signifying the safety of vibration therapy.
