24108519.label: Major findings and research outcome
24108519.value: Hip fractures are the most serious form of complications of osteoporosis and often leads to subsequent disability, pain, falls and fractures, and even complications from fracture healing. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to identify the effectiveness of exercises on falls and fracture prevention [1], as these often occurs after hip fractures. We found that exercise interventions, especially the combination of strength and balance training, were effective in preventing falls. Resistance exercises and jumping exercises were effective for fracture prevention. Effective exercises or biophysical interventions including vibration therapy can be incorporated and are potential interventions for hip fracture patients. Unfortunately, for hip fracture patients, regular exercise are often difficult due to poor adherence and feasibility, and therefore we assess the use of vibration therapy in this clinical trial. Our protocol for the randomized controlled trial was published, showing that the clinical trial methodology is recognized and would provide good evidence [2]. We additionally identified that for hip fracture patients, those that had outdoor unassisted and outdoor with aids ambulatory function before fracture had 3- and 1.5- times increased risk of mobility deterioration, respectively [3]. This signifies the importance of improving fracture healing, pain and muscle parameters. During the COVID-19 period, we had a delay in the clinical trial due to recruitment into the study. We found that patients with concomitant COVID-19 and hip fracture are at high risk of mortality and complications. Ct values and D-dimer levels have no prognostic roles for hip fracture outcomes. Early operative treatment is recommended as soon as patients are medically fit [4]. 24108519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24108519.value: Our previous study had shown that the prevalence of sarcopenia after fragility fracture reaches 95% in males and 64% in females [1]. Sarcopenia is the progressive and generalized skeletal muscle disorder that leads to accelerated loss of muscle mass and function. Despite aggressive intervention, 4.5 million people are disabled every year from hip fractures and it is currently ranked top 10 amongst global disabilities. Even for community-dwelling elderlies before the hip fracture, 80% require walking aids, 11% become bedbound and 16% require long-term institutionalization. In our study, there were positive outcome with vibration therapy for pain, handgrip strength, quadriceps muscle strength, and balancing ability for hip fracture patients. Given the significant improvement in the muscle parameters, further developments of research includes the use of vibration therapy in treatment for sarcopenia in hip fracture patients. The proposed next course of action is to perform a pilot study in using vibration therapy in treating sarcopenia in hip fracture patients as the primary outcome. If this is proven positive, we would plan to run a randomized controlled trial for this, which would potentially change clinical practice globally. References: [1]. Wong RMY, …, Cheung WH. Osteoporos Int. 2019 Mar;30(3):541-553.

24108519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24108519.value: Globally, 1.6 million hip fractures occurred worldwide in year 2000 and it is projected by 2050 this number will reach 6.3 million. Annual healthcare costs place a huge burden to societies and it is estimated that a single hip fracture costs approximately USD43,669 at 1 year for health, rehabilitation and social care. Hip fractures are the most serious form of complication from osteoporosis and often leads to subsequent disability, pain, falls and fractures, and even complications from fracture healing. In this randomized double-blinded placebo-controlled clinical trial, it was found that low-magnitude high-frequency vibration was effective in improving pain, and muscle performance including handgrip strength, quadriceps muscle strength, and balancing ability in hip fracture patients. These can potentially aid in the prevention of future falls and fractures of these patients. In the future, the use of vibration therapy can potentially be incorporated into the rehabilitation of hip fracture patients after operation.

24114519.label: Realisation of objectives
24114519.value: The study period of this randomized controlled trial (RCT) of Chinese calligraphy practice was initially scheduled from 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2021. However, the outbreak of COVID-19 in January 2020 led to the closure of elderly social centres, resulting in the suspension of our subject recruitment. With the COVID-19 pandemic gradually subsiding, and a 12-month extension granted by the RGC, we successfully recruited all 112 required subjects and completed the RCT by 31 December 2022. Our study sample comprised community-living Chinese individuals aged 55 to 75 years. These individuals had been practising Chinese calligraphy regularly (average practice time: 3.1 hours/week for 9.7 years) and screened positive for subjective cognitive decline (SCD), but negative for mild cognitive impairment or dementia. Participants were randomly assigned to either the intervention group or the control group. Over a period of 6 months, the intervention group doubled their weekly calligraphy practice time, while the control group maintained their usual practice routine. Cognitive functions were assessed using standardized, structured, locally validated neuropsychological tests by assessors blinded to the group assignments. Functional connectivities (FCs) within default mode network (DMN) were assessed using the resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) brain scans conducted at the university hospital. Pre-specified regions of interest included medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), inferior parietal lobe (IPL), hippocampal formation (HF), posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), and lateral temporal cortex (LTC). The cognitive changes (Objective 1) and FC changes (Objective 2) over 6 months were compared between groups using repeated measures analysis of variance. Associations between cognitive changes and FC changes (Objective 3) were computed with correlational analysis. Out of the 112 participants, 107 (95.5%) completed the follow-up cognitive assessments, and 96 (85.7%) completed the follow-up fMRI scan. No serious adverse effect was reported. By adopting the intention-to-treat principle in our analysis, we successfully achieved all three objectives.

24114519.label: Major findings and research outcome
24114519.value: Regarding Objective 1, we found that global cognition (as reflected by the ADAS-Cog total score) remained stable at 6 months in both groups. Among various cognitive domains, significant between-group differences were observed in the changes of working memory (intervention vs control = +0.20 vs -0.23; group difference = 0.43; p=0.01). These findings suggest that participating more in cognitive activities is useful for cognitive maintenance. In relation to Objective 2, we observed the control group exhibiting a decreasing trend in nearly all the FCs within DMN. In contrast, the intervention group showed either an increasing trend or a smaller decrease in FCs. Statistical significance was reached in the between-group differences of the following FC changes: mPFC and right LTC (intervention vs control = +0.08 vs -0.17; group difference=0.25; p=0.009), mPFC and right IPL (+0.07 vs -0.15; 0.23; p=0.007), left HF and right LTC (+0.08 vs -0.21; 0.28; p=0.04), and left HF and right IPL (+0.13 vs -0.21; 0.34; p=0.009). These findings suggest that greater participation in cognitive activities has a neuromodulatory effect on the brain circuitry. As for Objective 3, we found that changes in the z-score of ADAS-Cog total score correlated significantly with FC changes between mPFC and right LTC (r=-0.24, p=0.02), mPFC and right IPL (r=-0.22, p=0.03), and left HF and right LTC (r=-0.21, p=0.04). Improvement in the ADAS-Cog performance, as reflected by a lower score, is associated with strengthening of FC. These findings suggest that DMN FC changes represent a sensitive biomarker in detecting cognitive changes.

24114519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24114519.value: While increased participation in habitual cognitive activities may provide cognitive benefits to older adults, it remains to be determined whether the introduction of a new cognitive activity can yield similar benefits for those without prior experience or regular practice. Future research should consider conducting another RCT to investigate whether older adults who are not cognitively active could experience cognitive improvements and enhanced FCs through regular participation in cognitive activities. Investigating the differential effects of various types of cognitive activities would also be of interest. This could enhance our understanding of whether specific cognitive activities are more suitable for training certain cognitive domains, thereby enabling personalized intervention training for individual older adults.

24114519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24114519.value: Our results highlight the significance of engaging in more cognitively stimulating activities for maintaining cognitive functioning and a healthy functional brain network, particularly for individuals who have not yet developed mild cognitive impairment or dementia. Our findings challenge the commonly held belief that decline in cognition or deterioration in functional connectivities within the brain’s neural network in late life is irreversible. Our study emphasizes the importance of promoting and encouraging active participation in cognitive activities among older adults as a key component of a dementia prevention strategy.

24201219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24201219.value: Transoral Robotic Surgery (TORS) has been gaining popularity over open transcervical approach and traditional laryngoscopy for head and neck complications due to its precision, enhanced visualization, and increase in surgical site exposure. The da Vinci surgical robotic systems have been used in clinical and preclinical trials for various head and neck procedures. However, most TORS procedures have been applied only around the oropharyngeal space – surrounding the base of tongue. The oversized manipulators (holding the instruments), the lack of positioning flexibility of manipulators in the neck that presents challenging curvatures, and the limited distal dexterity in narrow space are major contributing factors behind the difficulty in accessing the lower neck region, including lower hypopharynx, lower larynx, and upper oesophageal sphincter. The goals of this project are to design a continuum manipulator with enhanced capability for TORS, investigate the kinematic model and hysteresis compensation in the control scheme, and evaluate its performance and design feasibility. The continuum manipulator will have a variable-length elbow segment based on shape memory alloy (SMA) wires to improve flexibility in instrument positioning and adaptability for different surgical conditions. It also allows shifting of the instrument pivoting point closer to the surgical site, reducing potential damage to the oral cavity. Besides, dexterity of the end effector instrument will be improved significantly through a miniature flexible wrist segment that has state-of-the-art bending curvature. The wrist will be in the form of a spring and fabricated through a new fabrication concept. SMA wires and cable-driven mechanism will be used as the driving systems for the elbow and wrist segments, respectively. A new kinematic model that considers the length variation property will be developed to study the expanded workspace and be implemented in the telemanipulation control system. Hysteresis due to the SMA actuation and cable-driven mechanism will be modelled and compensated to improve the control accuracy. The challenges in the project include miniaturization of a flexible elbow segment, implementation and modelling of the length variation property of the SMA wires, fabrication of a flexible wrist that is capable of high bending curvature, and implementation of hysteresis compensation. The evaluation will mainly focus on the performance and feasibility of new design features and its applicability in transoral surgery for anatomies in the lower neck. The continuum manipulator has a huge potential to be translated beyond the head and neck procedures to other anatomies that have high curvatures and narrow operation space.

24201219.label: Realisation of objectives
24201219.value: Objective 1: To design and develop a spring-based wrist segment capable of high bending curvature. A new compact 4-degree of freedom (DOF) wrist has been developed with an outer diameter (OD) of 4 mm. It consists of a yaw joint, a rolling joint, and a pair of grippers at the distal end. The two parts of the grippers can be controlled independently. The pitch motion is achieved by rotating the two parts of the grippers towards the same direction while the opening and closing of the grippers is achieved by rotating the two parts of the grippers in opposite directions. The rolling joint consists of a semi-circular annulus groove on which two actuation tendons for the rolling joint are routed. Two tendons can be actuated in two opposite directions to allow the wrist joint to roll in two directions. The yaw joint is essentially a pin joint located at the base of the rolling joint and at the distal end of the elbow bending segment. Objective 2: To design and develop a variable-length elbow segment consisting of an antagonistic pair of SMA wires and an adjustable disc. A novel bending actuator has been developed to be directly applied as the proposed variable length elbow segment for the surgical manipulator. The bending actuator, with the outermost diameter of 8mm, consists of a pair of SMA wires fixed between a distal disk and a proximal disk. There is a movable disk that is free to translate along the two SMA wires between the distal and proximal disks. Two electrical wires from the positive terminal of the power source are connected to the distal ends of the SMA wires at the distal disk, while another electrical wire from the negative (ground) terminal of the power source is connected to two copper sheets in the cavities of the movable disk for SMA wires, after passing through the lumen of the center tube. The two antagonistic SMA wires are connected to two different electrical circuits, which share the same ground terminal. The working principle of the bending actuator can be divided into two processes: bending length adjustment and bidirectional bending. The bending arc length of the actuator, l, is subject to Joule heating during the bending motion. This length is adjustable between 20mm and 40mm, depending on the location of the movable disk, which can be translated via a center tube. After the bending length is set, the actuator could be bent by completing one of the two aforementioned circuits using an electronic switch to heat one of the antagonistic SMA wires. Objective 3: To employ the twist-based approach to model the new kinematics of the manipulator that will take into account its variable-length property. The proposed robot is a 7-DOF manipulator, consisting of a 4-DOF wrist joint at the distal end, a 2-DOF elbow segment, and a base rotation. The base rotation is denoted by θ1. The translation of the movable disk from its home position leading to the variable length property is denoted by d2 while the elbow segment features a bending angle of θ3. The wrist joint has yaw motion θ4, distal roll θ5, and rotation of the two parts of grippers, θ6 and θ7. The kinematics analysis of the robot has been developed using the twist method based on the product of exponential mapping of the twists for all the joints stated above. The workspace of the variable-length elbow segment can be seen in Fig. 7 in Publication 2. It shows how the ability to vary the length of the elbow segment allows enhanced workspace coverage compared to typical bending joint with a fixed length. Objective 4: To characterize and model the hysteresis behaviour associated with the actuation mechanisms in the elbow and wrist segments, and develop the compensation model. To characterize the hysteresis behavior, a series of experiments were carried out. Since the tendon lengths in the wrist section is small compared to their total tendon lengths, tendons of the yaw joint (i.e., the most proximal joint in the wrist joint) are selected for calibration of actuation tendon hysteresis. The two tendons started from their home position (i.e., straight configuration of the yaw joint) were actuated for multiple cycles in a quasi-static way. After the motion of tendons were stable, the relationship between yaw angle and tendon displacement was plotted. It was found that the average hysteresis of the tendon displacement in the robot is 0.135 mm and was relatively repeatable throughout the motion cycles. A new modified Bouc-Wen (MBW) model was used to more accurately represent the relationship between actuation space and configuration space. A smooth function is defined in terms of the relative velocity to capture the hysteresis behavior. H(λ_1,λ_2,λ_3,n,β,γ) are the parameters that control the shapes of the hysteresis loops in both loading and unloading phases. In order to match the model output with the experimental bending angles, the genetic algorithm (GA) optimization was utilized to minimize the value of the fitting function. Objective 5: To evaluate the performance of the continuum manipulator and validate the feasibility of the manipulator for TORS in a phantom model and cadaver model. Each of the variable length elbow segment and the wrist segment was evaluated comprehensively. The robot workspace was evaluated at three typical angular positions of the rotational joints. The experimental results match the theoretical kinematics data well, with average root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 1.33 mm, 1.04 mm, and 0.38 mm for the variable length l = 40 mm, 30 mm, and 20 mm respectively. The larger error at l=40 mm is mainly due to twisting of the bending joint at large angle. The continuous variation of the bending length enables the stiffness and thus the output force to be adjusted in real-time during the surgical manipulation task. The largest force observed was 5.6 N at l =20 mm, which was nearly twice of that at l =40 mm. This distal force range is sufficiently large for most surgical procedures. The elbow segment was also commanded to track 2D trajectories at different amplitudes and 3D trajectories with different shapes, achieving tracking errors less than 1 mm. The wrist segment was mainly evaluated in terms of the effectiveness of hysteresis compensation. Under hysteresis compensation, the yaw joint was able to track the reference signal well without significant discrepancy. In contrast, without compensation, there is an evident lag in yaw motion. The average absolute error under compensation is 0.75o, nearly one-third of that without compensation, 2.14o. Finally, the entire robotic manipulator was evaluated in a phantom larynx model and a pig head cadaver model for feasibility evaluation, confirming that it offers the workspace and the bending capabilities that allow minimally invasive access to deep in the laryngeal region during TORS.

24201219.label: Major findings and research outcome
24201219.value: 1. A variable length elbow joint based on shape memory alloy (SMA) has been developed with diameter of 8 mm and a length adjustable between 20mm and 40mm. This work has resulted in two journal papers and one conference paper. Another journal paper is currently under preparation for submission to IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters. 2. A highly compact 4mm diameter wrist joint with 4 degrees of freedom (DOFs) has been developed based on smart integration of multiple pin joints and rolling joint. The integration of the distal rolling joint at 4mm scale is highly challenging and represent a significant advancement of wrist joint for minimally invasive surgery. A journal paper is currently under preparation for submission to IEEE/ASME Transactions on Mechatronics. 3. The hysteresis of the robotic manipulator has been characterized and compensated with satisfactory results, allowing more accurate trajectory tracking of the robot. 4. A manipulator consisting of a compact variable length elbow bending segment and high-DOF wrist segment provides dexterity and manipulability that have not been achieved using existing technologies. The variable length elbow segment, in particular, allows the robot to access different targets in the deep larynx region due to the different bending lengths available for deployment during the procedure.

24201219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24201219.value: 1. The shape memory alloy-actuated variable length elbow segment features limited actuation bandwidth, constrained by the rate of heat transfer during both heating and especially cooling. A compact, integrated cooling module can potentially be developed for the variable length bending joint to offer continuous bending motion with significantly enhanced actuation bandwidth. 2. The manipulator will be further miniaturized to under 5mm diameter to minimize the chances of collision between instruments and allow improved access to the lower neck region in larger patient pool. The diameter of the elbow segment at around 8mm is the bottleneck that limits further miniaturization of the entire manipulator, and it is required due to the stiffness required for the surgical procedure. A variable length bending joint with smaller diameter can be achieved by optimizing the heat treatment process of shape memory alloy wires to achieve high bending stiffness at a smaller diameter. 3. During TORS, it is ideal to have two manipulators for tissue manipulation and an endoscope for real-time visualization. Two of the proposed manipulators and a flexible endoscope will be integrated as a system to provide surgical control under the teleoperation and visual servoing manipulation modes.

24201219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24201219.value: Transoral Robotic Surgery (TORS) has been gaining popularity over open transcervical approach for head and neck complications due to its minimal invasiveness, enhanced visualization, and increase in surgical site exposure. However, most TORS procedures have been applied only around the oropharyngeal space – surrounding the base of tongue due to the challenging curvatures in the narrow laryngeal space, the oversized manipulators, and the limited distal dexterity of the instrument. This project introduces a continuum manipulator with two key innovations, including a flexible elbow segment that can vary its bending length to provide significantly improved access to navigate to different target lesion in the lower neck region and a multi-degree of freedom wrist joint that provides high dexterity to perform surgical manipulation of the target lesion. Specifically, the wrist joint provides the important distal rolling motion that facilitates surgical manipulation such as suturing and tissue retraction, as well as extremely high dexterity in a form factor of only 4 mm diameter. These innovations represent an advancement in the field of continuum robots towards higher dexterity and motion capabilities, allowing continuum robots to be adopted in various confined anatomical space for minimally invasive procedures.

24201919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24201919.value: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), via activation of its receptor tropomyosin-related kinase B (TrkB), plays a critical role in neuronal cell proliferation, differentiation, survival, and death. Alterations in BDNF/TrkB signaling have been linked to a variety of severe diseases that significantly change the lives of millions of people, including neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer’s disease, various cancers such as neuroblastoma, and mood disorders such as depression. Therapeutic strategies aiming to modulate BDNF/TrkB signaling have been pursued to treat these devastating diseases. Despite tremendous efforts, the development of BDNF/TrkB-related drugs has been impeded partly due to the incomplete understanding of the role of BDNF/TrkB signaling in these diseases as well as the lack of effective and efficient drug screening technologies. In this study, we propose to develop an optical strategy that aims to use light to activate TrkB signaling. With high specificity and spatiotemporal resolution, our method of light-mediated TrkB activation will greatly facilitate the investigation of the dynamic nature of TrkB signaling and its role in related diseases. Furthermore, using the optical activation of TrkB, we propose to develop all-optical platforms to screen small-molecule activators and inhibitors of TrkB. 24201919.label: Realisation of objectives
24201919.value: All the three objectives have been fully achieved. (1) For objective 1, 5 different optogenetic systems to activate TrkB have been constructed and tested. Among the five methods, the most effective one has been identified. (2) For objective 2, we have used different approaches to verify the efficient light-controlled activation of TrkB, showing that our method can not only effectively activate the downstream signaling of the pathway but also modulate neuronal differentiation. (3) For objective 3, we have showcased the feasibility of all-optical high-throughput drug screening platforms using our optogenetic tool. Using light as the input to activate TrkB signaling and light as the output to characterize the level of TrkB activations, we are able to identify the inhibitors of TrkB signaling and assess their inhibitive efficacy.

24201919.label: Major findings and research outcome
24201919.value: (1) We develop different optogenetic approaches that use light to activate TrkB signaling. Utilizing the photosensitive protein Arabidopsis thaliana cryptochrome 2, the light-inducible homo-interaction of the intracellular domain of TrkB in the cytosol or on the plasma membrane is able to induce the activation of downstream MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling as well as the neurite outgrowth of PC12 cells. Specifically, three strategies for activating TrkB with light are introduced: Opto-iTrkB, combining TrkB with CRY2 for cytoplasmic distribution; Lyn-Opto-iTrkB, adding a Lyn tag for membrane localization; and Opto-iTrkB + CIBN-CAAX, using CRY2/CIBN interaction for membrane recruitment and activation. All methods use light to trigger TrkB signaling. (2) Moreover, we prove that such strategies are generalizable to other optical homo-dimerizers by demonstrating the optical TrkB activation based on the light-oxygen-voltage domain of aureochrome 1 from Vaucheria frigida. The optical activation of all the above-mentioned methods were confirmed by live cell imaging method to check the translocation of the downstream MAPK/ERK and PI3K/Akt signaling reporters. Light exposure successfully activated TrkB-related pathways, as indicated by the movement of specialized reporters within the cell, validating the system's effectiveness in triggering TrkB signaling. (3) By comparing all the different strategies, we find that the cryptochrome 2-integrated approach to achieve light-induced cell membrane recruitment and homo-interaction of the intracellular domain of TrkB （Opto-iTrkB + CIBN-CAAX） is most efficient in activating TrkB signaling. This is assessed by the elevated levels of phosphorylated ERK (p-ERK) and AKT (p-AKT), and the neurite growth of PC12 cells. Opto-iTrkB + CIBN-CAAX shows the high levels of P-ERK and P-AKK, and induces the highest percentage of PC12 cell neurite growth. (4) To show the design of all-optical high-throughput drug screening platforms, we have shown treatment with U0126 (MEK inhibitor) or LY294002 (PI3K inhibitor) prior to blue light blocked the increase of p-ERK or p-AKT levels, respectively. U0126 treatment, instead of LY294002, suppressed the light-induced neurite growth which can be characterized by optical methods. This validates the design of the screening platform. Detailed results and related figures to show the data can be found in Peer-reviewed publication #1 in Part C.

24201919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24201919.value: Building on the success of using light to control TrkB activation, the next phase could explore the therapeutic implications of such precise control in living organisms, particularly in models of neurodegenerative diseases. By applying these optogenetic tools in animal models, we can seek new findings on how TrkB signaling affects disease progression and recovery and develop new therapeutic methods. To achieve this, Dr. Duan has acquired a Young Collaborative Research Grant (YCRG) “Light Protects Vision: Optogenetic Activation of Trk Signaling for Neuroprotection of Retinal Ganglion Cells in Ocular Diseases” , which is based on the data from this ECS project. We are collaborating with neurologists and eye doctors in this current project. Using optogenetic tools developed in this ECS project, we are constructing tools that can activate TrkB efficiently in the eyes and exploring the potential of a customizable and precision therapy for ocular diseases. On the other hand, results from this ECS project indicate new opportunities for the optogenetic application of other signaling pathways that are important for disease treatment, such as CNTF, GDNF, GP130, and PTEN signaling. We will seek other funding to develop novel optogenetics tools and apply them to disease studies.

24201919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24201919.value: The research focuses on a special protein, called TrkB, which is vital for the health and function of nerve cells in the brain. When TrkB works correctly, it helps these cells grow, mature, and survive, but when it doesn't, it can lead to brain diseases and cancer. It’s imperative to figure out how to activate TrkB in a controlled way so we can better understand its role and potentially treat related diseases. This project develops new tools that use light to activate the TrkB protein. A light-sensitive protein from a plant is used, which helps TrkB work only when exposed to light. This light switch can turn on important cell pathways and make certain cells grow outwards like branches. It is also shown that this method can work with different types of light-sensitive systems. The most effective tool found uses the plant protein to bring TrkB to the cell surface and make it work when hit by light. This research is exciting because it gives scientists a precise way to study how TrkB helps nerve cells, using just a light switch. This could lead to new ways to understand and treat neuronal diseases in the future.

24203419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24203419.value: Graph is a fundamental data structure to represent objects and their relationships, which can be used to represent social networks, email network, mobile call networks, transportation networks, and the World Wide Web, to name a few. An important category of graph queries is the random walk based queries, which find extensive applications in search engines, social recommendations, community detection, spam detections, and so on. In the era of big data, graphs are growing steadily and becoming massive. With the growth of the graphs, one big challenge is how to handle the random walk based queries efficiently since such queries are typically processed in large batches and in a regular manner by many IT companies, like Twitter, Pinterest, and Tencent. Therefore, reducing the overheads on such random walk based queries will help these IT companies reduce the computational costs, thus reducing monetary costs. Meanwhile, some new models of random walk based queries are recently proposed and are shown to provide more accurate results in many applications, e.g., in social recommendation and community detection. However, these solutions are still inapplicable to industry due to the prohibitive computational costs. If one can design novel algorithms that can significantly reduce the computational costs for these new models and make it applicable to existing IT companies, then these IT companies will benefit from the improved accuracy of those applications, improving the user experience and attracting more users to their applications. Motivated by this, the proposed project aims to devise more efficient solutions for random walk based queries by considering many aspects including developing new algorithms with improved time complexity, devising novel index structures with bounded space consumption, exploring new hardware or distributed computing, and considering new models of random walks for improved accuracy. As an outcome, the project is expected to develop new frameworks that can be used to facilitate the random walk based queries on massive graphs. 圖作為一種表示物體和它們相互關係的基本數據結構，被廣泛的應用于現實生活; 它可以用來表示社交網絡，郵件網絡，電話網絡， 交通網絡和萬維網等等。隨機遊走查詢是圖上面很重要的一類查詢， 並且被廣泛用於搜索引擎，社交推薦，社團檢測，垃圾郵件檢測等等。 在大數據時代，圖在不斷的增長並且變得十分龐大。現在很多互聯網公司，如Twitter，Pinterest，騰訊，都有很多龐大的圖。而在這些互聯網公司龐大的圖上，隨機遊走查詢被廣泛應用于它們的商業場景，並且需要被定期大批量的處理。 這給工業界帶來了一個重大的挑戰：如何高效快速的在大圖上處理隨機遊走查詢。解決這個問題能為這些公司顯著降低計算開銷，進而降低公司成本。 同時，最近有不少新的隨機遊走模型被提出來，並且在很多應用如社交推薦團體檢測中顯示能提供更準確的結果。但是這些方法因為昂貴的計算開銷卻還不能被廣泛應用到工業界。 如果能夠設計出新的算法來顯著降低這些模型的計算成本並且使得他們能被應用到工業界，那麼很多互聯網公司都能從中受益，例如能給用戶提供更準確的結果， 提高用戶體驗，從而留住並吸引更多用戶。 受此激勵，該項目旨在為隨機遊走查詢設計更高效的方法。項目會從許多方面出發來考慮如何提高隨機遊走查詢效率， 包括設計新的能降低計算理論複雜度的算法，構建新的可控存儲空間的索引機制，探索新的硬件和分佈式計算，考慮新的能提高準確度的高效隨機遊走模型。 作為成果，該項目希望能夠開發出一個新的模型來提高隨機遊走算法在大圖上的效率並希望能被用於工業界。

24203419.label: Realisation of objectives
24203419.value: Our project ambitiously aimed to advance the field of random walk-based queries through the development of innovative algorithms and techniques. We successfully achieved all four of our primary objectives, making substantial contributions to the efficiency and effectiveness of these queries. To accomplish our first objective, we achieved notable progress in several key research areas: (i) Randomized Backward Search (RBS): We developed a new randomized algorithm, Randomized Backward Search (RBS), which achieves optimal complexity for single-target personalized PageRank (PPR) queries, a renowned measure in random walk-based proximity. RBS has notably enhanced three key applications: heavy hitters PPR query, single-source SimRank computation, and scalable graph neural networks. This work was published and presented at SIGKDD 2020. (ii) Forward-Push with Incremental Random Walk Maintenance (FIRM): We have presented FIRM, an efficient index structure for personalized PageRank on dynamic graphs. Our proposed solution is based on a classic framework that combines the forward-push technique with a random walk index for approximate PPR queries. A standout feature of FIRM is its incremental updating scheme, maintaining indexed random walks in expected O(1) time post each graph update. This groundbreaking development, offering a substantial speed-up in update performance over existing dynamic schemes without compromising efficiency, was published and presented at SIGMOD 2023. In pursuit of our second objective, we successfully developed a distributed PPR (Personalized PageRank) computation framework. Addressing the limitations of existing state-of-the-art solutions for PPR computation in distributed settings, we developed an efficient framework for single-source and top-k PPR queries in distributed environments. It reduces the number of communication rounds while ensuring manageable load per executor. Our innovative approach combines a redesigned parallel push algorithm with the Monte-Carlo method for single-source PPR queries, leveraging pre-sampled random walks to minimize round numbers. We also introduced a new top-k algorithm optimized for distributed frameworks, significantly reducing the required number of rounds in practice. This work was showcased in PVLDB 2021. In addressing our third objective, we made considerable progress in developing advanced models for random walk-based queries. Our efforts in this area include: (i) Supervised Random Walk Framework: Initially, we explored high-order random walks to enhance the representational power of node embeddings. However, we found that the improvements were not substantial. Consequently, we shifted our focus to supervised random walks, where we learn the stopping probability at each step. This approach is particularly effective as it allows the random walk-based proximity measures to be tailored to specific tasks and datasets. To scale this solution for large graphs, we developed efficient sampling techniques and generalized push algorithms. This innovative work was published in SIGKDD 2021. (ii) Approximate Graph Propagation (AGP): We introduced AGP, a comprehensive randomized algorithm capable of computing a range of random walk-based proximity queries and Graph Neural Network (GNN) feature propagation. This includes transition probabilities, Personalized PageRank, heat kernel PageRank, supervised random walks, Katz, SGC, GDC, and APPNP. Notably, AGP provides a theoretical bounded error guarantee and operates with near-optimal time complexity. This significant advancement was published in SIGKDD 2021. (iii) Instant Graph Neural Network (InstantGNN): We developed InstantGNN, an incremental computation approach for dynamic graph representation matrices. This method bridges the gap between random walks and feature propagation, particularly for dynamic graphs under the edge-arrival model. It enables instant updates to the representation and predictions, efficiently handling both dynamic structures and attributes. InstantGNN also offers an adaptive training strategy, focusing on retraining at optimal moments for performance gains. This work, marking a major step forward in the field, was published in SIGKDD 2022. Our comprehensive experimental studies, conducted across a diverse range of applications, have consistently demonstrated the efficiency and effectiveness of our proposed solutions. This rigorous validation process successfully fulfills our fourth goal, emphatically highlighting the overall success of our project. Additionally, our outreach efforts included presentations at Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab and ICDM 2021, furthering the impact of our research on random walk-based query processing. Throughout the project, 6 PhD students were trained, each demonstrating exceptional academic excellence. One of these students has already graduated and is now continuing his research journey as a postdoctoral fellow at the National University of Singapore (NUS). One PhD student is on track to graduate in Spring 2024. Two PhD students are expected to graduate in the summer of 2024. Two PhD students are expected to graduate in Spring 2025. To conclude, this project has not only achieved but indeed surpassed its set objectives, making a significant contribution to the domain of random walk-based queries. Our findings have enhanced current understanding and capabilities in this field, laying a strong foundation for future exploration and innovation. An equally important aspect of this project has been its role in academic development and mentorship. The training and advancement of 6 PhD students underscore our commitment to fostering academic growth alongside scientific discovery. This dual impact, enhancing both scientific knowledge and academic careers, highlights the comprehensive success of our project.

24203419.label: Major findings and research outcome
24203419.value: The project achieved significant success in advancing random walk-based query processing, as evidenced by the publication of 23 papers in prestigious conferences and journals, including 6 in SIGMOD, 5 in VLDB, 6 in SIGKDD, 2 in ICDE, 1 in TODS, 2 in TKDE, and 1 in IJCAI. This impressive academic output underscores the project's scientific rigor and its substantial impact on the field. A key aspect of the project was its contribution to academic development, training 6 PhD students over four years, highlighting the project's dual focus on knowledge advancement and nurturing future researchers. In laying a solid foundation in random walk-based query processing, the project made significant advancements. For example, we demonstrated that existing index-based PPR computation frameworks can support efficient updates in expected O(1) time after each graph update, a notable improvement over the current best-known solution requiring O(m) update cost. Extensive experiments confirmed that our solution is orders of magnitude faster than existing ones. For distributed PPR computation, we presented a theoretical analysis under the Massively Parallel Computing (MPC) model, showing that our proposed solution can reduce the number of rounds asymptotically under the same load compared to existing solutions. This theoretical finding was further validated through extensive experimentation. Additionally, we introduced new models of random walks to enhance recommendation accuracies. For instance, we developed trainable random walks, learning the stopping probability at each step. This approach effectively tailors random walk-based proximity measures to specific tasks and datasets. To scale this solution for large graphs, we implemented efficient sampling techniques and generalized push algorithms. Overall, the project not only enhanced the efficiency and effectiveness of random walk-based queries but also set new benchmarks in the field. The integration of theoretical advancements with practical applications, coupled with the project's emphasis on academic development, demonstrates its comprehensive impact and success.

Our project's contributions, especially in new query types and processing techniques, have opened doors for further exploration. A critical direction for development is innovating diverse query types to meet the evolving data needs of today's world. Our advancements, like trainable random walks, have established a base for this exploration. The opportunity to create a variety of new queries could significantly enhance data processing efficiency and sophistication. Additionally, addressing theoretical challenges in this domain is crucial. Despite strides in optimizing computation times and efficiency, issues like suboptimal results and high computational demands persist in many sub-fields. Addressing these challenges involves refining theoretical frameworks and developing more efficient algorithms, benefiting both academic research and practical applications. In summary, the future of random walk-based query processing lies in the dual pursuit of developing novel query types and improving theoretical models, promising notable advancements in both academic study and real-world applications.

24204819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24204819.value: Developing an extended culture of hepatocyte in vitro is challenging because the conventional 2D cultures suffer from a rapid loss of cell viability and hepatic functions. Maintaining a long-term hepatocyte culture can have important applications in studying liver biology, drug testing, and developing bioartificial liver support system. The generation of 3D hepatocyte spheroids can maintain relatively long-term hepatic function. However, there are practical challenges associated with spheroid cultures, including the difficulty of forming and maintaining uniform-sized spheroids on a large scale and the lack of support for cell functions by extracellular matrix (ECM) cues (e.g. biochemical and mechanical). Given the heterogeneous distribution of various ECM components in the liver and the association of tissue stiffening with liver fibrosis, a platform that provides efficient spheroid fabrication and evaluation of the effect of various ECM cues will be essential to optimize hepatocyte culture. Microfluidic technology is able to manipulate tiny amounts of fluid/cells precisely. In our previous efforts, we developed a microfluidic double emulsion droplet platform that controllably produces hepatocyte spheroids entrapped in a microscale hydrogel (microgel). We also demonstrated an enhancement of spheroid functions in the presence of ECM cue (collagen type I). In this project, we propose to extend our platform to fabricate hepatocyte spheroids encapsulated in a combinatorial library of microgels containing different biochemical and mechanical ECM cues in order to determine an optimal culture configuration. The proposed research will be technically and conceptually novel. Technically, our microfluidic platform will be developed to integrate spheroid production with encapsulation in a combinatorial library of ECM microenvironments. Conceptually, this will be the first study that systematically optimizes ECM cues for hepatocyte spheroid culture. To fulfil Aim 1, we will first develop a microfluidic platform with multiple inlets and optimize the parameters to achieve the generation of spheroids encapsulated in a combinatorial hydrogel microenvironment. For Aims 2 and 3, we will investigate and optimize the effects of biochemical composition (collagen type I, collagen type IV, laminin and fibronectin) and mechanical stiffness on hepatocyte spheroid culture. The developed platform will be a powerful tool to advance liver research because many in vitro applications of hepatocyte culture depend on the extended hepatocyte maintenance. Our universal platform can also be applied to establish 3D culture of other cell types. Future iterations of the proposed work have the potential to enable the manufacturing of miniaturized tissues for personalized drug screening and regenerative medicine.

24206219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24206219.value: Recently deep generative networks (DGNs) such as Generative Adversarial Networks have shown impressive result in synthesizing photo-realistic images, such as the high-resolution living-room images and human face images. Despite the success of DGNs, many problems such as the instability of training and the lack of synthesis variation remain. Furthermore, the DGNs still work like a black box without much progress on why such photo-realistic images can be synthesized. To tackle these problems, it is essential to probe the internal representations of the DGNs for the better understanding of DGNs. For example, what attributes of the living-room does a DGN learn to draw a realistic living-room? Does it learn to draw certain objects such as televisions and sofas internally first before drawing the room layout? The objective of this project is to interpret and understand the internal representations of the Deep Generative Networks. Previous works have made initial progress in visualizing the representations of the deep neural networks trained for image classification. It is shown that the internal units of the representations detect visual concepts such as edges and textures at lower layers and objects and parts at upper layers. Thus the representations can be used to explain the predicted class, providing more interpretability to the black-box models. However, to visualize the internal representations of the DGNs, novel frameworks are needed due to the fundamental difference between the representations used for classification and the ones used for synthesis. For instance, to classify an image into a living-room, the internal representation of the classification network detect relevant informative objects, such as sofa and television inside the image; To synthesize an image of living-room, it is uncertain so far what representations are being used and how the attributes of living-room are encoded in the DGNs. Our work proposes a novel framework to interpret the internal representations of DGNs, as well as understand their inner working mechanism. The proposed framework identifies the groups of units specialized to synthesize visual concepts, by associating the internal representations with the semantics of the synthesized image regions. Training techniques are further developed to facilitate the DGNs towards more transparent and interpretable models. Based on the framework, questions on how the DGNs work will be addressed, the quality of synthesized images will be enhanced, and various applications including interactive image editing and manipulation will be implemented. 近年來深度生成網絡如GAN取得了突破性進展，可以合成高清的場景或者人臉圖片。然而在生成網絡成功的背後，也依然存在很多諸如訓練的穩定性以及合成圖片缺乏多樣性等問題。深度生成網絡依然以壹個黑箱模型的形式生成圖片，而缺乏解釋為什麽它可以生成這些逼真的圖片。為了解決以上這些問題，壹個關鍵研究問題是去分析深度生成網絡的內部表徵的可解釋性。比如說，是不是在生成客廳圖片的過程中深度生成網絡先學會了生成客廳的各項寓意特徵，以及是不是網絡內部先學會了如何畫如電視和沙發的物體。 這個項目研究的核心問題是解析和理解深度生成神經網絡的內部表徵。之前已有的工作主要集中在對深度分類網絡內部表徵的可視化。已有的工作分析出了深度分類網絡的低層主要含有邊緣以及紋理的檢測器，而高層主要含有物體和物體部分的檢測器。這樣這些具有語義檢測特徵的卷積單元可以用來解釋黑箱模型的預測結果。然而，因為深度生成網絡和深度分類網絡在結構上的不同，我們需要研究和開發全新的解析深度生成網絡的可解釋性框架。比如說，對於深度分類網絡來進行場景分類，網絡內部其實是在檢測於場景直接關聯的各種物體。而對於深度生成網絡，目前並不清楚到底內部是如何運作的。 通過這個研究項目，我們將提出壹個全新的解析深度生成網絡內部表徵以及理解內部運作機制的框架。這個框架將通過語義關聯性分析，來辨識出負責合成各種語義特徵的單元和單元組。我們也將設計壹些新的提升模型可解釋性的訓練方法。這個新的框架將幫助解釋深度生成網絡的內部表徵，基於這個框架的結果，我們也會進壹步設計交互式的圖片編輯框架等相關應用。

24206219.label: Realisation of objectives
24206219.value: InterFaceGAN framework for interpreting DGNs Despite the great success of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) in synthesizing images, there lacks enough understanding of how photo-realistic images are generated from the layer-wise stochastic latent codes introduced in recent GANs. In this work, we show that highly-structured semantic hierarchy emerges in the deep generative representations from the state-of-the-art GANs like StyleGAN and BigGAN, trained for scene synthesis. By probing the per-layer representation with a broad set of semantics at different abstraction levels, we manage to quantify the causality between the layer-wise activations and the semantics occurring in the output image. Such a quantification identifies the human-understandable variation factors that can be further used to steer the generation process, such as changing the lighting condition and varying the viewpoint of the scene. Extensive qualitative and quantitative results suggest that the generative representations learned by the GANs with layer-wise latent codes are specialized to synthesize various concepts in a hierarchical manner: the early layers tend to determine the spatial layout, the middle layers control the categorical objects, and the later layers render the scene attributes as well as the color scheme. Identifying such a set of steerable variation factors facilitates high-fidelity scene editing based on well-learned GAN models without any retraining. Improving the interpretability of DGNs. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) can synthesize more and more realistic images. However, one fundamental issue hinders their practical applications: the incapability of encoding real samples in the latent space. Many semantic image editing applications rely on inverting the given image into the latent space and then manipulating inverted code. One possible solution is to learn an encoder for GAN via Variational Auto-Encoder (VAE). However, the entanglement of the latent space poses a major challenge for learning the encoder. To tackle the challenge and enable inference in GANs, we propose a novel method named Latently Invertible Autoencoder (LIA). In LIA, an invertible network and its inverse mapping are symmetrically embedded in the latent space of an autoencoder. The decoder of LIA is first trained as a standard GAN with the invertible network, and then the encoder is learned from a disentangled autoencoder by detaching the invertible network from LIA. It thus avoids the entanglement problem caused by the latent space. Extensive experiments on the FFHQ face dataset and three LSUN datasets validate the effectiveness of LIA for the image inversion and its applications. New applications of the proposed framework. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have recently advanced image synthesis by learning the underlying distribution of the observed data. However, how the features learned from solving the task of image generation are applicable to other vision tasks remains seldom explored. In this work, we show that learning to synthesize images can bring remarkable hierarchical visual features that are generalizable across a wide range of applications. Specifically, we consider the pre-trained StyleGAN generator as a learned loss function and utilize its layer-wise representation to train a novel hierarchical encoder. The visual feature produced by our encoder, termed as Generative Hierarchical Feature (GH-Feat), has strong transferability to both generative and discriminative tasks, including image editing, image harmonization, image classification, face verification, landmark detection, and layout prediction. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experimental results demonstrate the appealing performance of GH-Feat.

24206219.label: Major findings and research outcome
24206219.value: Our research studies have shown that there is interpretable knowledge emerging inside the deep generative models trained for image synthesis. By discovering the hidden knowledge inside the learned representations of various deep generative models, we can steer and control image generation. Steerable image generation leads to a wide range of applications, such as facial attribute editing, image inpainting, and colorization. It also validates that the deep generative models are not black-box, where the internal representations have learned how to compose images in a semantically meaningful way. That makes huge progress for our deeper understanding of neural networks commonly used in computer vision. As research output, this project leads to several highly-impact publications: totally there are 3 journal publications, and 7 conference publications at top computer vision avenues. One of the publications already received more than 446 citations, which shows its high impact in the computer vision field. 2 PhD students are trained.

24206219.value: The latent manipulation properties of deep generative models can be incorporated into the image editing function for commercialization. There are future engineering developments for that.

24206219.value: This project pioneers our understanding of the deep generative models trained for image synthesis. We show that such models learn interpretable and disentangled representations. By discovering these interpretable representations we can steer and control the image generation process. This leads to a wide range of image editing applications. It also facilitates Human-AI content co-creation. The research output includes 3 journal papers published at IJCV, TPAMI, and 7 conference papers published at CVPR, ECCV, NeurIPS, which are all at top AI journals and conferences. One of the papers published in 2020 receives more than 446 citations so far, which is among the most cited papers in CVPR 2020. It clearly shows the impact of our research works.

24206919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24206919.value: The aim of this project is to maximize the dynamic performance of triboelectric nanogenerators (TENG) by conducting comprehensive studies using theoretical modeling, simulation and experiments. Given the rapid development of the Internet of Things, a significant number of interrelated devices will be required for sensing, actuation, and data transmission. Traditionally, these devices rely on batteries as an energy source; however, considering the limited lifetime and the difficulties in maintenance and replacement, it is necessary to find an alternative power solution. Energy harvesting technologies have been proposed to address this issue in a sustainable way by scavenging energy from the environment. Mechanical energy is available ubiquitously in various forms regardless of location, time, and weather. TENG is an emerging technology for harvesting mechanical energy, which has advantages of high output, low cost, and ease of fabrication. It has been predicted that there will be a US$480 million market of TENG-related applications in 2028. However, previous research about TENG only focus on the output energy. Improving the design of TENG units mandates considering both the input and output energies which are significant in practical settings, and still requires further investigation and refinement. This project is dedicated to developing such a design and will provide more robust information regarding the input and output energies of the TENG. We will conduct our research through four phases. First, theoretical research will be conducted to understand the dynamic performance of current TENG design. Next, we will develop and optimize the advanced design of TENG through multiple strategies. Then, the performance of the TENG with the advanced design will be systematic studied through theoretical modeling and simulations. Lastly, the theoretical results will be verified by experiments and demonstrations. The findings of this study will be of considerable value in terms of both fundamental studies and practical applications. This proposed research will represent the first study of its kind that systematically examines TENGs by modeling both input and output energies, which will greatly improve our understanding of dynamic performance, energy flow and efficiency. The study will also significantly contribute to the practical application of TENG units in related circumstances, with our findings being of interest to scholars in various research fields including energy harvesting, dynamics, and sensing. 本項目的目標是利用建模、模擬和實驗進行綜合研究，最大限度地提高摩擦納米發電機（TENG）的動態性能。 物聯網的快速發展需要相當數量的器件來進行傳感、驅動和數據傳輸。傳統上，這些器件依賴電池作為能源；然而，考慮到有限的使用壽命和維修更換的困難，有必要尋找替代電源解決方案。已被提出多年的能源收集技術通過從環境中收集能源，將以可持續的方式解決這一問題。在環境中機械能以各種形式無處不在，不論地點、時間和天氣。TENG是一種新興的機械能收集技術，具有輸出高、成本低、易於製造等優點。據預測，到2028年，與TENG相關的應用將有4.8億美元的市場。然而，以往對TENG的研究只關注其輸出能量。未來改善TENG的設計需要同時考慮輸入和輸出能量在實際應用中的重要作用，並進一步深入和細化研究。 本項目致力於開發這樣一种設計，並對TENG的輸入和輸出能量進行更扎實的研究。我們會將研究分為數個階段。首先，進行理論研究來瞭解當前TENG設計的動態性能。下一步，我們將開發多種策略優化TENG的設計，然後對優化設計的TENG進行系統性的理論建模模擬。最後，對理論結果進行實驗驗證。本研究的結果將具有重要的科學研究和實際應用價值。本研究將是首次對TENG輸入和輸出性能進行的系統性研究，這將大大提高我們對TENG動態性能、能量流和能量轉化效率的理解。本研究也將對TENG在相關情況下的實際應用做出重大貢獻。我們的研究結果值得能源收集、動力學和傳感等領域的學者關注。

24206919.label: Major findings and research outcome
24206919.value: 1, We have systematically investigated the dynamic characteristics of the original triboelectric nanogenerators (TENG). The theoretical electromechanical models were established, based on the original sliding freestanding triboelectric layer (SFT) TENG as a typical example. The transfer flow of the energy in the system was fully understood. 2, To improve the performance of TENG, we have developed two advanced structures based on SFT-TENG. One is a nonlinear oscillator-based grating TENG proposed based on the nonlinear oscillator, which is achieved by mounting springs perpendicular to the slider motion direction. The theoretical model containing both the dynamic response and transient electrostatic force is established. Through this model, we predicted that the enhanced power output can be achieved by the nonlinear property of the spring. The displacement, velocity of the slider in one vibration period, can be optimized under the same excitation frequency, and thus, the sweep/contact area in one period and the transferred charge are increased as well. The kinematic output performance of the nonlinear oscillator-based TENG is studied comprehensively, including the effects of the spring length, stiffness, excitation frequency, and external resistance. The experimental results indicate that the tested maximum output power of the nonlinear setup is 3 times enhanced compared to that of the traditional linear setup, and the power density approaches 244 W/m3, validating the established model. Compared with the traditional linear vibration system, this nonlinear oscillator TENG demonstrates advantages of the high-power density, broad bandwidth, and compact structure. (Ref. [13]) 3, Another structure is a nonlinear noncontact oscillator-based grating TENG achieved by the nonlinear restoring magnetic force. The theoretical model to capture the dynamic responses is established. Through this model, we predict that the power output can be enhanced by the nonlinear property of the magnetic force. In addition, the integrated EMG enabled by the magnetic force and coils demonstrates low-impedance output characteristics, which can serve as a supplement to the high-impedance TENG output to enable wider applications. The results show that compared with the linear system, this TENG can increase the peak current from 6.3 μA to 7.89 μA , with an increment of about 25%, increase the peak power from 650 μW to 977 μW , increasing by about 50%, and increase the bandwidth from 0.5 Hz to 7.75 Hz, increasing by about 1400%. (Ref. [23]) These studies may enable a new strategy to boost the bandwidth and output power of TENG toward various applications (Ref. [1-24]).

24206919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24206919.value: The developed non-linear and non-contact TENGs have the advantages of high-power output, wide bandwidth, and compact structure. Our existing studies may open a new trend with new methods to harvest broadband vibrational energy with high output performance to power multiple devices for the Internet of Things and other applications. For further development of this research, we can propose following actions: 1, Continue study about the advanced TENG-based energy harvesting systems. We can combine this structure with advanced triboelectric surfaces to generate high charge density, advanced dielectric materials with high energy density, and charge-self-excitation circuits. We may study the mechanisms and characteristics of this advanced energy harvesting system to maximize the output performance. 2, Develop the advanced TENG systems as a key component for self-powered systems. For example, we may use that in self-powered wireless sensing systems, human-machine interaction, wearable/implanted systems toward applications in energy harvesting, health monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, etc.

24206919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24206919.value: Powering the widely-distributed small devices required in the modern society through cables or batteries becomes a difficult task due to the limited lifetime of batteries, huge technical difficulties and costs. To utilize the mechanical energy and sustainably power electronics, triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) technology was proposed in 2012. However, the limited dynamic performance of TENGs limit its response to the wide frequency spectrum in ambient environments. This project systematically studied the dynamic performances of TENGs. The study starts from theoretical understandings on the dynamic models and energy flows of the existing TENG, as well as the proposed advanced TENGs. To enhance the output performance, we proposed an addition of nonlinear restoring forces applied to TENG to tune and broaden the resonance bandwidth. This restoring force can be applied by a non-linear oscillator made by springs, or permanent magnets at both sides of the slider and two external magnets. Compared with the traditional linear vibration system, the newly-proposed nonlinear TENGs have demonstrated the advantages of high-power output, wide bandwidth, and compact structure. This work may open a new method to harvest broadband vibrational energy with high output performance to power multiple devices for the Internet of Things and other applications.

24300619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24300619.value: The rapid emergence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) bacteria has become a serious global public health threat. Today, it is estimated that at least 700,000 people die every year from infections caused by the bacterial ‘superbugs’ with an associated healthcare cost of US$ 20 billion. Bacteriophage (Phage) therapy has recently been rediscovered as a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics in defeating MDR bacteria. However, it has achieved limited success for intracellular pathogens because phages are not able to get across mammalian cell membranes. Therefore, there is an urgent need for new formulations and delivery strategies to maximize the therapeutic effects of phages in our MDR battle. This timely project will produce inhalable liposome formulations of phages to target MDR bacteria that cause severe and persistence lower respiratory tract infections (pneumonia). In particular, we will focus on Acinetobacter baumannii and Staphylococcus aureus which can shelter within phagocytic, epithelial and endothelial cells in lungs. Recently, we have demonstrated that a microfluidic approach could offer excellent capability in preparing liposomal phage formulations warranting further studies on its potential. The proposed research will continue to refine the process parameters and formulation compositions to produce liposomal phage formulations suitable for pulmonary delivery. This route holds the greatest promise in achieving optimal liposomal phage concentration in lungs for efficient treatment compared with the current oral and intraperitoneal delivery strategies. The central hypothesizes of this research are that the liposome encapsulated bacteriophages can (1) be nebulized and delivered to the lower respiratory tract, (2) be internalized by targeted cells and (3) fuse with intracellular bacteria and subsequently lyse them. As S. aureus and A. baumannii can cause infections in extracellular environment, the efficacy of the encapsulated phages against extracellular bacteria is of equal importance. Accordingly, we have set the selection criteria for promising formulations: they need to have high encapsulation efficiencies (≥ 50%); low titer reduction during the encapsulation process (≤ 1 log); reasonable high cellular uptake (≥ 50%); excellent bactericidality (≥ 5 log reduction); appropriate size (ideally ≤ 1 µm); and good aerosol performance (fine particle fraction ≥ 50%) to ensure sufficient amount of encapsulated phage reaching the site of action. Ultimately, the research outcomes can lead to a cost-effective and efficient technology to produce liposomal phage formulations for novel treatment strategies of lower respiratory tract infections by inhalation. 多重耐藥（MDR）細菌的迅速出現已成為嚴重的全球公共衛生威脅。目前的統計數據顯示，全球每年約有70萬人死於耐藥“超級細菌”造成的感染，而相關醫療費用高達200億美元。因此噬菌體療法最近被重新引入作為抗生素的替代品，並證明有效擊敗MDR細菌。然而，因為噬菌體不能穿過細胞膜，它對細胞內病原體的成功有限。因此，积极研發新的製劑和遞送策略讓噬菌體在這場MDR戰鬥中有最大化的治療效果迫在眉睫。 本項目將產生可吸入的脂質體-噬菌體製劑，以靶向呼吸道的MDR細菌，特別是鮑曼不動桿菌和金黃色葡萄球菌。由於這些菌們能在吞噬細胞和上皮細胞內存活，所以它們能導致嚴重和持續的下呼吸道感染（肺炎）。最近，我們成功利用微流控技術將噬菌體包被到脂質體中，讓我們可以進一步研究這新製劑對治療胞内細菌感染的潛力。本項目將繼續改進微流控技術的工藝參數和配方輔料以生產適於肺部遞送的脂質體-噬菌體製劑。與目前口服和腹膜內遞送策略相比，把脂質體-噬菌體直接送入呼吸道更容易到達治療需要的濃度，获得更好的治疗效果。 本項研究的核心假設是生產的脂質體-噬菌體製劑可以（1）被霧化並遞送至下呼吸道，（2）被靶向的細胞內化和（3）與細胞內的細菌融合併隨後溶解它們。由於鮑氏不動桿菌和金黃色葡萄球菌也可在細胞外環境中引起感染，因此製劑對細胞外細菌的功效同樣重要。因此，我們設定了有效製劑的選擇標準：具有高的包被效率（≥ 50％）;生產過程中噬菌體的損失不大（≤ 1 log）;高的細胞攝取（≥ 50％）;優良的殺菌性（≥ 2 log）;適當的尺寸（≤ 1μm）;和良好的氣溶膠性能（細顆粒分數 ≥ 50％），以確保足夠量的包封噬菌體到達作用部位。 本研究的最終目的是研發出一種經濟有效的技術，用於生產脂質體-噬菌體製劑，為耐藥胞內細菌引起的下呼吸道感染提供新型的治療策略。

24300619.label: Realisation of objectives
24300619.value: Bacteriophage (phage) therapy using obligately lytic phage for therapeutic purposes or as an adjunct to antibiotics has been revitalized in the West to battle against MDR bacteria. However, phage therapy has been considered to be hence ineffective against intracellular bacteria because phages are incapable of penetrating across the mammalian cell membranes. The supported project is taking the advantage of the similarity of liposome and the mammalian cell membranes to harness it as a carrier to deliver phage into the cells and/or the sub-cellular compartments to target bacteria residing there. The three set project objectives have been realized and presented below. Objective 1: To encapsulate phage into liposomes using a microfluidic hydrodynamic focusing approach. Phage stored in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) was found to suffer from stability issues that the titer was decrease gradually with time. Therefore, we first prepared the studied phages (Phage K, vB_AbaM-IME-AB406, vB_AbaM-IME-AB2 and vB_AbaM-IME-AB9) into dry powder formulations using spray drying to extend their storage stability for the whole study period of this project. The compositions and storage conditions required to stabilize phage powders were optimized and exemplified with vB_AbaM-IME-AB406 phage and the related work was published in Pharmaceutics (https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics13081162). We first evaluated the suitability of the multi-inlet vortex mixer (MIVM) with an outlet channel diameter (~1000 µm) to prepare liposomes. Two key process parameters (aqueous/organic flow rate ratio (FRR) and total flow rate (TFR)) of the MIVM were identified to govern the size and polydispersidy (pdi) of prepared liposome preparation. Results showed that the size exponentially decreased from 600 nm with increasing FRR from 1:1 to 5:1 at which the size plateau at ~ 150 nm and slightly decreased with increasing TFR. In addition to the original MIVM design, two modified MIVMs, one with herringbone-patterned straight inlets and one with zigzag inlets, were designed to further improve the mixing efficiency to achieve better drug encapsulation. The zig-zag modified MIVM could achieve the best mixing performance. Overall, collected data confirmed that all MIVM devices are capable to generate liposomes of relatively uniform size over a wide range of flow conditions (https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics14061223). After confirming the suitability of MIVM in preparing liposomes, the formulation compositions and process parameters for the preparation of liposomal phage were optimized using a Box-Behnken Design approach. The optimized formulations had an encapsulation efficiency of ~62% and found to be comparable with those prepared with the conventional thin-film hydration followed by extrusion method in preparing liposomal phage. The advantages of the microfluidic approach are being one-step preparation process and can allow high throughput production. In summary, Objective 1 has been realized. Objective 2: To establish the validity and utility of the inhalable liposomal phage formulations characterization of their physicochemical and biological properties and nebulizability. As understanding of the interactions between phage and mammalian cells may hold the key for the successful development of phage therapy, we have first developed co-culture systems containing phage (using three A. baumannii phages as model phages), bacteria and human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) to evaluate the antibacterial efficiency in addition to the conventional in-vitro experimental settings containing phage and bacteria only. Our results demonstrated that the bactericidal effect of bacteriophage could be augmented and the emergence of phage resistance could be inhibited/delayed in the presence of non-mucus-producing epithelial cells (https://doi.org/10.36922/mi.3141). In the in-vitro co-culture model, phage K was also proved to effectively destroy the planktonic bacteria but limitedly resist S. aureus invasion to cancer cells. While the combination between phage K and Doxorubicin (a chemotherapeutics) could promote the killing of intracellular bacteria (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-36749-2), enhancement with the liposome formulation approach was demonstrated to be more effective ( https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijpharm.2024.124146). The intracellular bacterial killing was also found to be strongly depended on the lipids used to form the liposomes, where egg phosphatidylcholine (EPC)-phage exhibited the best killing performance with no relapsing. Phage K-EPC liposome nanocomplexes was also observed to manage the tissue infection in both 2D monolayer cell and 3D spheroid models more effectively than free phage K. A key contributor was the improved phage internalisation brought by the liposome carrier, from non-detectable phage titer to > 5 log phage inside the epithelial cells. Nebulization is an efficient administration approach for treating respiratory tract diseases. Currently, all reported phage therapies are administered via nebulization. However, ensuring the respirability of phage products is maintaining the stability of phage during nebulization remains a challenge as the mechanical stresses generated in the nebulization process can potentially damage the structural integrity of phages, resulting in reduction of phage viability and infectivity. Our results also confirm the destructive effect of the Aeroneb® Go vibrating mesh nebulizer on phage K, a 2 log titer reduction was noted. Positively, the complexation with liposomes showed a protection effect on phage K against the mechanical stresses upon the mesh nebulization process, resulting in less phage titer reduction, with the EPC-phage offered the best protection with only 0.8 log reduction. Also, the fine particle fraction, characterizing the amount of phage delivered with the lower respiratory tracts, of the EPC-phage formulation (~90%) was confirmed to be significantly higher than that of the free phage (~30%). The short-term storage of EPC-phage was also confirmed that no apparent phage loss was detected after storing the formulation under refrigeration. Overall, our work confirmed liposomal phage as a promising candidate to handle intracellularly-infected pathogens and the protective effect of liposomes on phage upon the nebulization process for respiratory infection treatment. In other words, Objective 2 have been realized. Objective 3: To study the in-vivo efficacy of inhaled liposomal phage formulations in infected animals - a proof of concept study. The in-vivo antibacterial effects of the EPC-phage K nanocomplex formulation were investigated in S. aureus-associate lung infection mice model. After 24 h of infection, bacteria were grown from ~6 log CFU/mL to around 8 log CFU/mL in the lungs of mice (control group). While treatment with phage or liposome-phage significantly reduced the bacterial load, where the numbers of bacteria still maintained at ~6 log CFU/mL after 24 h, implying that phage therapy could effectively inhibit the growth of bacteria in-vivo. Liposome-phage showed a comparable antibacterial effect with free phage, suggested that the presence of EPC liposomes did not interfere the bacterial lytic activity of phage K. Phage titer variations after 24 h of treatments in mice were also evaluated. Both free phage and liposome-phage increased their titers in vivo, from ~5 log PFU to ~7 log PFU/mL. This indicates that phage K can well propagate in the mouse lung with the presence of its hosts and the incorporation of EPC liposomes does not affect phage K proliferation. Taken together, phage K application showed remarkable effectiveness in the pulmonary bacterial infection management in-vivo, which can be a promising antibacterial option. Although no significant antibacterial difference was seen in vivo between phage K and EPC-phage K treatments (due to a limitation in the current intratracheal instillation method in mice), nevertheless, by virtual of liposome nanocarriers, EPC-phage K could be more efficiently delivered into the lungs via nebulization, which will provide more benefits and promises for the clinical usage. Collectively, Objective 3 is also largely realized, but an in-vivo model with chronic infection significantly affect by the intracellular bacteria may be more suitable to examine the full potential of liposomal phage formulations.
