24300619.label: Major findings and research outcome
24300619.value: Bacterial infections in the respiratory tract are considered a major challenge to the public health worldwide. The rapid emergence of multidrug resistance (MDR) bacteria has further limited the clinical options. In this project, we provided an overview on the development of emerging antibacterial therapeutics, including antimicrobial peptides, RNAi therapeutics, and bacteriophages, for managing lung bacterial infections (Output 4, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11095-022-03379-8). The current landscape of the development of inhaled phage therapy and the formulation strategies adopted to equip phage with the ability to target intracellular bacteria were summarized in a book chapter (Output 1, DOI: 10.5772/intechopen.96660) and a review article (Output 2, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.addr.2021.113864). These provided important insights in translating inhaled phage therapy to manage bacterial lung infections. Liquid phage formulations have often suffered from stability issues that the titer decrease gradually with time. We successfully developed stable dry powder formulations of the studied phages to ensure their storage stability (Output 3: https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics13081162). We also developed the microfluidic technology platform based on a multi-inlet vortex mixer (MIVM) to produce liposomal phage formulations. They were also found to have good storage stability with liposomes composed of suitable lipids, like egg phosphatidylcholine (EPC). The suitability of MIVM in preparing liposomes and encapsulating drugs into liposomes were confirmed in our published work (Output 7, https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics14061223). One major impediment for the clinical application of phage therapy is the lack of understanding of the phage, bacteria, and host body interactions. Therefore, we developed co-culture systems to investigate the dynamics between bacteria, phage, and mammalian bronchial epithelial cells. Our data demonstrated that the presence of epithelial cells could not only augmented the bactericidal effect of phage, but also the inhibited/delayed emergence of phage resistance (Output 8, https://doi.org/10.36922/mi.3141). Combine treatment with doxorubicin and incorporating phages with liposomes were also demonstrated to have superior performance in managing intracellular infections compared with free phage treatment (Output 5, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-023-36749-2 and Output 6, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijpharm.2024.124146). The phage-liposome nanocomplexes also demonstrated to have protective effect to phage against the mechanical stresses upon the nebulization process to yield higher in-vitro lung dose. No improved in-vivo efficacy was noted in phage K-liposome nanocomplexes compared with the free phage K in a mice lung infection model. We attributed this to the short period between bacteria introduction and phage administration, limiting the capacity of bacteria invading into host cells. More suitable animal models to investigate the efficacy of liposomal phage in controlling intracellular lung infections are needed.

24300619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24300619.value: Despite progress made in this project, some limitations exist and accordingly, some prospective studies should be considered in the further investigations, which are described below. The stability of the liposomal phage formulation is a very vital parameter in the practical application and for the regulation of phages as pharmaceuticals. If phages loss their viability and complexation with liposomes, the performance of the formulation, such as the nebulization efficiency and the antibacterial efficacy, may undergo significant alterations, compromising the therapeutic outcomes or posing threats to patients’ health. In this manner, it is desirable to perform long-term stability test for the liposomal phage formulations to estimate the shelf-life of the liposomal phage products. In the in-vivo mice lung infection model assessing the antibacterial efficacy of liposomal phage, insignificant improvement was noted over the free phage formulation. This could be due to the short time frame between the initiation of bacterial infection and phage formulation administration, which was not sufficient for bacteria to invade into host cells. Animal model with established intracellular infection should be used to further evaluate the benefit brought by liposomal phage in the future.

24300619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24300619.value: The rapid emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria has become a serious global public health threat. Phage therapy has become a promising solution to combat bacterial infections. However, it has achieved limited success for intracellular pathogens. While many major respiratory pathogens have recently been found to survive within host cells, contributing to their persistence and relapse of lung infections. Therefore, further strategies are required to phage with the ability in targeting intracellular bacteria. This timely project developed a microfluidic technology platform to produce inhalable liposome formulations of phages to equip them with the capability of targeting bacteria surviving within host cells. The research not only maximize the therapeutic potential of phage therapy, but also offer develop novel phage treatment for life-threatening lung infections. Further investigation should be warranted to facilitate the translation of the developed technology and treatment strategy.

24301419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24301419.value: 最近單細胞測序實驗技術的進步使我們對基因組學特徵的分析達到前所未有的精準。如今，我們不僅可以測量單細胞中的基因表達，也可以測量其它基因組學特徵，包括蛋白質結合，甲基化和染色質開放性。因為實驗限制，單細胞基因組學的數據非常稀疏，部分原因是由於實驗材料較少造成的數據缺失。單細胞基因組學的數據還容易出現批次效應。單細胞數據的這些特點為數據分析帶來挑戰。單細胞基因組學的一個主要目標是識別並描述新的細胞類型。為實現這一目標，人們通常先進行聚類，然後再進行變量選擇。基於模型的聚類方法可以為聚類結果提供統計學推斷，但這方面研究相對較少。 在這個項目中，我們將開發一個統一的統計學框架來對單細胞染色質開放和單細胞基因表達數據進行統計建模和聚類。我們考慮一種越來越常見的“耦合聚類”的情況：對於來自相同細胞群體的不同細胞，我們獲得了兩種數據類型，而我們的目標是聚類和匹配不同數據中的相同細胞類型。我們提出了一種新的隱變量模型來對單細胞基因組學中的數據缺失以及跨數據類型的隨機性進行建模。基於ENCODE，Roadmap以及仿真數據的初步研究，我們提出的方法實現了更好的聚類效果，並且能夠更好地處理批次效應。在此基礎之上，我們還提出了基於這個隱變量模型的推廣，包括引入稀疏性限制來提高模型的可解釋性，以及整合基因組構象數據，以進一步提高聚類的效果。對於統計學推斷，我們還開發了一種高效的蒙特卡羅算法。 在單細胞基因組學中，這是第一個基於概率模型的聯合聚類多種數據類型的統計方法。通過整合多種數據類型，我們可以提高對不同細胞類型的識別，在此基礎上可以深入影響下遊的生物醫學研究。我們提出的統計框架具有很好的擴展性，並且可以有效利用其它可用的基因組學數據。對於處於分化中間狀態的細胞，我們方法中的統計推斷將能夠提供更多有用信息。我們提出的模型中的組件，包括如何對實驗中的數據缺失以及不同數據類型的隨機性進行建模，具備一定的普適性，可以應用於數據科學中的其它問題。

24301419.label: Realisation of objectives
24301419.value: We have developed a novel model-based approach designed to cluster single-cell chromatin accessibility and single-cell gene expression data concurrently. Our innovative approach is characterized by several distinctive features. Firstly, our model is unique in that it does not rely on training data to create a connection between the two data types. This is a significant departure from traditional models, which often depend on pre-existing datasets for training. By eliminating this requirement, our model offers a fresh perspective on how single-cell chromatin accessibility and single-cell gene expression data can be clustered. Secondly, our approach takes into consideration the inherent noisiness present in single-cell experiments. We have addressed this issue by explicitly modeling the loss of biological signals. This feature ensures that the model can accurately interpret the data despite the noise, thereby improving the reliability and robustness of the results. Thirdly, our model has the ability to adaptively infer how well the two data types, single-cell chromatin accessibility and single-cell gene expression data, are matched. This adaptive inference is based on the data itself, which allows for a more accurate and dynamic understanding of the correlation between the two data types. Fourthly, our model allows for statistical inference of the cluster assignment. This feature not only provides a robust statistical foundation for the clustering process but also enhances the interpretability and reproducibility of the results. Finally, we have developed an efficient Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that incorporates collapsing and auxiliary variables. This algorithm not only enhances the computational efficiency of our model but also ensures its scalability to larger datasets. In summary, our model-based approach to jointly cluster single-cell chromatin accessibility and single-cell gene expression data introduces a unique combination of features that collectively enhance the accuracy, reliability, and interpretability of the results. This approach represents a significant step forward in the analysis of single-cell data. The software packages for our methods are available on GitHub.

24301419.label: Major findings and research outcome
24301419.value: Unsupervised methods, such as dimension reduction and clustering, are integral to the analysis of single-cell genomic data, primarily because cell types are usually unknown and need to be inferred. Model-based clustering methods, which can quantify the uncertainty in cluster assignments, are under-explored in the area of single-cell genomics. However, combining information across different types of genomic features can yield rich biological insight and lead to better separation of cell types. To this end, we have developed a model-based framework specifically designed for single-cell genomic data. This approach can jointly cluster single-cell chromatin accessibility, gene expression, and even methylation data. Our modeling framework provides statistical inference of cluster assignments, achieving superior cell type separation by combining biological information across different types of genomic features.

24301419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24301419.value: The potential for further development of this research is substantial, given the increasing importance of single-cell genomic data in biological and medical research. Our method has shown promising results in clustering single-cell chromatin accessibility, gene expression, and methylation data. However, there is a clear need for additional research to extend its capabilities and improve its performance. One proposed course of action is to adapt our approach for use with other types of single-cell genomic data, beyond the types we have already tested. This could involve the development of new algorithms or the modification of existing ones, to handle different types of data distributions. We also propose conducting more extensive real-world testing of our approach, including its application to larger and more diverse datasets. This would allow us to further evaluate the performance of our approach and identify any potential areas for improvement. Finally, it may be beneficial to explore the integration of scAMACE with other computational tools used in single-cell genomics. This could lead to the development of a comprehensive software package for single-cell genomic data analysis, enhancing the usability and accessibility of these powerful computational methods.

24301419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24301419.value: We've created a new method to group data about individual cells, specifically looking at how accessible certain parts of the cell's DNA are and how much each gene is active. Unlike previous methods, ours doesn't need any prior data to make connections between these two types of information. This is a big change and gives us a new way to understand this data. Our method also takes into account that data from single-cell studies can be quite messy and can lose some biological signals. We've made sure our method can still make sense of the data even with this noise, making our results more reliable. Our method can also figure out how well matched the two types of data are, based on the data itself. This gives us a more accurate understanding of how the two are related. Additionally, our method uses statistical inference to assign cells to clusters, making our results easier to interpret and reproduce. We've also developed a new algorithm to make our method more efficient and scalable. In simple terms, our method offers a better, more reliable way to understand individual cell data. We've made the software for our methods available online.

24306919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24306919.value: 現代統計推斷不再遵循簡單的兩階段結構：「上帝生成數據，分析師分析數據」。由於可能存在插補的缺失數據，合成機密數據和不兼容的順序工作，統計推斷變得更為複雜。這些問題是經常遇到，甚至有時在實踐中是不可避免的。我們將這種情況形式化為：數據生成（G）、刪除（D）、插補（I）和分析（A）的四個階段。假設上帝在階段G創造數據；「魔鬼」在階段D中刪除的部分數據；插補師在在階段I中通過多重插補（MI）填充缺失數據；並由分析師在階段A中進行推理。由於上帝、魔鬼、插補師和分析師可能是不同的參與者，他們的模型或程序可能是不相容的。解決階段D、I、A中兩個不兼容問題是本計劃書的研究目標。 第一層不兼容性是指階段D和A之間的分歧。由於數據缺失，分析師估值的精確度有所下降。因為缺少數據對不同的估值有著不同的影響，所以不同的估值之精確度會有著不相等的百分比下降。但是，大多數現有的MI測試假設等百分比下降。它導致了缺失數據機制與分析師程序之間的不兼容。 第二層不兼容性是指階段I和A之間的衝突，部分原因是知名的分析師模型及插補師模型之間的不兼容性。處理此問題的現有方法要麼犧牲統計效率，要麼要求分析師及插補師之間進行（不可行的）信息交換。實際上，不兼容性不只是源於兩個模型的不兼容性。由於插補程序和分析師的MI程序是高度依賴相方之假設，如果分析師沒有被告知、不了解或沒有接受過插補程序的培訓，則會導致程序不合適。 我們提出了兩種稱為Sieve MI（SMI）和Laminated MI（LMI）的程序，分別用於解決第一層和第二層不相容性問題。 SMI過濾掉MI數據集中包含的不需要的信息，以便巧妙地解開導致第一層不相容性的複雜鏈接。我們推測確實存在兩類缺失：缺失數據及缺失插補師模型，其中第二類缺失是第二層不兼容性的起源。 LMI同時處理兩層缺失。有趣的是，我們在估算方差時將缺失數據問題轉換為時間序列問題。

24306919.label: Realisation of objectives
24306919.value: The objectives of the proposal have been fully achieved. The proposed methodologies, outlined in the proposal, have been adequately generalized and polished to handle various types of inference problems, as stated in Objectives 1 and 2. These two objectives have been realized in one published article entitled "Multiple Improvements of Multiple Imputation Likelihood Ratio Tests" (Publication #1 in Part C). Additionally, we have extended the methods stated in Objective 2 to other related missing-data or incomplete-data problems, resulting in the submission of three articles that are currently under review. These articles are Publications #6, #7, and #8 in Part C. The detailed theoretical properties, including asymptotic distribution, representation, and validity, as well as the computational properties such as parameter tuning, computational efficiency, and algorithm, were also studied as stated in Objective 3. This objective has been realized in one publication in the Annals of Statistics entitled "General and Feasible Tests with Multiply-Imputed Datasets" (Publication #4 in Part C). This article was presented in international conferences and various departmental seminars in overseas universities. An R package called "SMI" has been developed to implement the proposal, as stated in Objective 4. This R package is a part of Publication #4 in Part C. Additionally, we have developed a variance estimator that is helpful for analyzing one of the proposed tools, as stated in the proposal. The laminated version of MI requires a special type of variance estimator for tuning as mentioned in Objective 3. This part is realized in one publication entitled "Mean-structure and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix Estimation" (Publication #3 in Part C). Furthermore, the proposed methods have been applied to two real-data studies as mentioned in Objective 5. These real-data studies involve uniportal video-assisted thoracic surgery and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. In both studies, the datasets consist of various percentages of missing data. The proposed methodologies were successfully applied to analyze these problems and achieve reliable statistical inference results. Two publications entitled "Uniportal video-assisted thoracic surgery for major lung resection is associated with fewer immunochemokine disturbances than the multiportal approach" and "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs Reduce Pleural Adhesion in Humans: Evidence from Redo Surgery" (Publications #2 and #5 in Part C) have been produced.

24306919.label: Major findings and research outcome
24306919.value: The proposal aimed to develop new methodologies for multiple imputation (MI) and yielded six major findings. First, we compared existing methods for combining likelihood ratio tests (LRTs) in MI inference. We identified several defects in the existing method, including negative combined F-test statistics, lack of invariance, non-monotonic power, and the need for nontrivial access to the LRT statistic; see Publication #1 in Part C. Second, we found a new principle to combine imputed datasets via stacking. This method only requires users to conveniently stack the imputed datasets without the need to write non-trivial functions. This leads to a novel MI test. Upon assuming equal odds of missing information (EOMI), we proved that it can be implemented efficiently; see Publications #1 and #4 in Part C. Third, another notable finding is that FMI (Fraction of Missing Information) can be estimated using an LRT statistic computed based on multiple imputed datasets that are stacked differently. It allows us to derive a new MI test that bypasses the assumption of EOMI; see Publication #4 in Part C. We showed theoretically that the proposed test resolves the aforementioned issues, and demonstrated empirically that it can control the type-I error rate accurately. Fourth, this study offers a unified algorithm for performing Wald's tests, likelihood ratio tests, and Rao's tests in MI inference; see Publication #4 in Part C. We have built an R package for implementing it. Practitioners can apply it as a black box. Besides, a laminated version of the MI test requires us to use the variance estimator developed in Publication #3 in Part C. Fifth, the tests have been applied to various clinical problems that consist of missing data. We found that using uniportal video-assisted thoracic surgery for major lung resection is associated with fewer immunochemokine disturbances than the multiportal approach, and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs reduce pleural adhesion in humans; see Publications #2 and #5 in Part C. Sixth, we successfully derived some results for handling data that are missing not at random and for handling coarsened time series; see Publications #6 and #7 in Part C. We also found a related application in causal inference as it naturally appears as a missing data problem; see Publication #8 in Part C. Remark: Publications #1 and #3 were submitted before the project commencement. However, they have undergone substantial revisions during the manuscript revision stage and were supported by the grant during this period.

24306919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24306919.value: Although all objectives of the proposal have been achieved, several directions can be further developed to improve the proposed methodologies. First, in the big data era, the proportion of missing data may be very large. Examples include datasets in recommender systems and network datasets. Traditional results and the proposed results may not work well in this situation. Second, it is also worthwhile to develop results for selecting covariates (or selecting models) based on multiply imputed datasets. The selected covariates based on different multiply imputed datasets may not be the same; hence, it poses a challenge on how to combine different selected covariates across imputation. The proposed multiple imputation likelihood ratio test may be helpful, but it is important to develop a more sophisticated method that is specialized for covariate selection in, for example, regression models. Third, it is of interest to derive a deep-learning algorithm for performing multiple imputation. The resulting multiply imputed datasets could possibly be fully nonparametric and better reflect the true distribution of the data generating mechanism and missing data mechanism.

24306919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24306919.value: Missing-data problems are ubiquitous in practice and naturally appear in many real-life datasets. To handle them, multiple imputation (MI) has been a preferred method by many practitioners, especially those who are ill-equipped to handle missingness on their own. However, the existing method for performing MI likelihood ratio tests (LRTs) has multiple defects. The major goal of this proposal is to derive a very handy MI test that is free of those defects. The new MI test is developed based on a novel yet simple stacking principle. A general, unified, and feasible MI test without requiring a strong assumption on the missing structure is proposed. The proposed MI tests control type-I error substantially better than all existing methods. Additionally, users can perform a valid incomplete-data test by solely applying a standard complete-data testing function on the imputed datasets. Hence, the proposed method is very user-friendly. Furthermore, we have also built a computer code for implementing the incomplete-data test straightforwardly and as simply as performing a complete-data test. The proposed MI test has been successfully applied to two real clinical problems and has helped doctors identify better ways to perform surgeries and treat patients. Insightful results were obtained.

24501519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24501519.value: Do investors only care about financial returns in their investment decision making? This question is essential for asset managers. Due to the growing social responsible investing (SRI or ESG investing), it is not obvious if asset managers need to simply provide the best financial returns to their investors or to consider the changing investor preferences towards ESG investments. Given this background, natural questions are: How do investors evaluate asset managers when they consider both sustainability performance and financial performance? How do asset managers respond? In March 2016, Morningstar introduced the Sustainability Rating for most mutual funds in the US. Such an exogenous release of the sustainability performance of funds provides a natural experiment to explore the aforementioned research questions. Using a difference-in-differences (DID) approach, this proposal studies the impact of sustainability rating on the flow-performance sensitivity for active open-end mutual funds and managers’ response to such an effect. Theoretically, how funds’ sustainability performance affects the flow-performance sensitivity is ambiguous. There can be at least two competing hypotheses. First, funds’ sustainability performance is a substitute for financial performance and investors put less weight on their financial returns (Riedl and Smeets, 2017). Therefore, the flow-performance sensitivity is lower (higher) for poorly performing funds with high (low) sustainability rating. Second, investors react to extreme ratings (five-star and one-star) (Hartzmark and Sussman, 2018). Consequently, there should be more attention to the extreme performance, and a possibly higher sensitivity for both high and low sustainability funds. Fund managers’ incentive will also change. First, managers of poorly performing funds may choose to invest in ESG stocks to mitigate the outflows from investors. Second, perhaps more egregious one, is that managers may engage in window dressing their disclosed portfolios by investing in ESG stocks prior to quarter ends to appear socially responsible. The contribution of the proposed project is two-fold. First, this is the first study on the causal effects of sustainability on flow-performance sensitivity. The heterogeneity in sustainability performance does not occur randomly. Neither does the investment decision in a certain fund. Due to such endogenous nature, there is inclusive evidence from the extant literature. The exogenous release of sustainability rating from Morningstar, addresses the endogeneity concerns. Secondly, our study deepens our understanding about fund managers’ behavior and strategies as the taste and demands of the clients change. As financial returns are no longer the single benchmark, managers’ incentives should also change. 投資者是否只關心投資決策中的財務回報？這個問題對資產管理者至關重要。由於不斷增長的社會責任投資（SRI或ESG投資），資產管理者是否只需要簡單地向投資者提供最佳財務回報， 還是需要考慮投資者對社會責任投資的偏好變化？ 這個問題的答案並不確定。在此背景下，我們提出兩個問題：投資者在考慮社會責任投資績效和財務績效時如何評估投資經理？投資經理又如何回應？ 2016年3月，晨星公司推出了基金的社會責任投資評級，囊括了美國大多數共同基金。這個外生性事件，為探索上述研究問題提供了一個自然實驗平台。通過使用雙重差分法（DID），此提案研究了對於的開放式的主動基金，社會責任投資評級是否會影響基金流量對於績效的敏感性，並且進一步分析投資經理的回應。從理論上講，基金的社會責任投資績效如何影響基金流量對於績效的敏感性是模棱兩可的。至少存在兩個不同可能的假設。首先，基金的社會責任投資績效取代了財務業績，投資者對其財務回報的重視程度降低（Riedl和Smeets, 2017）。因此，對於具有高（低）社會責任投資評級基金，投資者對於財務業績的敏感度降低（升高）。其次，投資者對極端評級（最高評級和最低評級）會有更強烈的反應（Hartzmark和Sussman, 2018）。因此，投資者應該可能會更關注極端評級，對最高社會責任投資評級和最低社會責任投資評級的基金表現出更高的敏感性。在此情況下，基金經理的投資決策也會發生變化。首先，財務表現不佳的基金經理可能會選擇投資社會責任好的股票以延緩投資者的資金流出。其次，也許更加令人震驚的是，基金經理對要披露的資產組合進行”粉飾櫥窗”, 通過在季度結束之前投資社會責任好的股票以彰顯出對社會負責，進而吸引投資者的資金流入。此研究項目的貢獻是雙重的。首先，這是關於社會責任投資對資金流動敏感性的因果影響的第一項研究。社會責任投資績效的異質性以及基金的投資決策都不是隨機發生的。由於這種內生性質，現存文獻中也並沒有統一的結論。晨星公司對社會責任投資評級評級的發佈可以解決此內生性問題。其次，隨著客戶的品味和需求的變化，我們的研究加深了對基金經理行為和策略的理解。由於財務回報不再是單一基準，管理者的激勵措施也需要作出調整。

24501519.label: Realisation of objectives
24501519.value: We explore most of our proposed objectives in our working paper “ESG Preference, Institutional Trading, and Stock Return Patterns”, which has been conditionally accepted by the Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis. Objective 1. We first define socially responsible institutions according to their holding information. Using MSCI ESG STATS database, which reveals the corporate social responsibility performance along different dimensions of firms each year, we calculate the net ESG performance (number of strengths minus the number of concerns) for each firm each year. Then using value-weighted average of the ESG scores of all the stocks in an institution’s portfolio, we define socially responsible institutions. To serve the other objectives, we study all of our objective 1-4 at stock level. Therefore, to measure the impact of socially responsible institutions on a stock, we further construct socially responsible ownership and other institutions’ ownership. We explore our first objective by examining the ownership (number) change of socially responsible institutions compared with that of other institutions when there are clear signals of trading, i.e. mispricing signals. We measure mispricing signals by the SYY scores in Stambaugh, Yu, and Yuan (2015) and the unexpected earnings surprise (SUE). We do find that socially responsible institutions trade differently in comparison with other institutions. Facing mispricing signals, the change in socially responsible institution ownership (or the number of such institutions) is much smaller than that of other institutions, indicating that socially responsible institutions are less responsive to the trading signals. It is very likely that these institutions are constrained by their focus on ESG performances and could not respond sufficiently to salient mispricing signals. We have fully achieved this objective in our proposal. Objective 2& 3. To understand how socially responsible institutions affect the firms, we first study the stock return patterns given mispricing signals and the presence of socially responsible institutions. Each month, we independently divide all sample stocks into two groups based on their previous quarter’s socially responsible institutional ownership, and into five groups based on the most recent SUE score within previous three months or the SYY score of last month. Using value-weighted portfolios and after adjusting for risk exposure, we find the mispricing signals predict the stock returns much better when the socially responsible ownership is higher. This is consistent with the under-reaction evidence we have documented in the first objective. When there are many institutions with an agenda of focusing on ESG perspectives of a firm, these institutions under-react to mispricing signals, leading to a delay in mispricing correction and a much stronger return predictability by the mispricing signals. For example, the SYY scores only significantly predict stock returns when there is high socially responsible institutional ownership. The difference between the return spreads is as high as 0.55% per month. To further demonstrate these results are because of the growing impacts of socially responsible institutions, we split our sample into an earlier and a later period., i.e. 1996-2003 vs. 2004-2016. We find that our aforementioned results are concentrated in the later period. The impacts of socially responsible institutions are absent in the earlier period when investors are less aware of the ESG issues, and climate changes. Therefore, Objective 3 of the proposal has been fully achieved. As our return results demonstrate that it takes longer for the mispricing correction in firms with higher socially responsible institutions, a natural question would be how that affects the corporate behaviours. Overpricing, to a certain extent, favours the firm and managers by lowering down the cost of capital. Therefore, we examine whether firms with higher socially responsible institutional ownership are more likely to increase their ESG performance to keep these institutions and lower cost of equity. Our panel regressions with change in ESG performances as dependent variable and lagged socially responsible institutions as independent variables confirm such hypothesis. Therefore, we confirm that socially responsible ownership could increase ESG performance of the holding firms. Objective 2 has been fully achieved. However, we decide to keep these results for our own information, given our paper focuses on the stock return patterns. Objective 4&5. Empirically, we do not find evidence of higher direct costs associated with shorting stocks with higher socially responsible institutional ownership. For example, among overpriced stocks, there are even more lendable shares for stocks with high socially responsible institutional ownership. The lending fees are also comparable among stocks with high and low socially responsible institutional ownership. Such results indicate that from the supply side, there are no traditional short sell constraints. We further examine the demand side, i.e. from the short seller’s perspective. Do short seller face more social pressure when they publicly short a firm with high socially responsible institutional ownership? We find supporting evidence. We first use data from Ljungqvist and Qian (2016) to identify major short sellers and then collect data on short-sale positions by these short sellers reported on hedge fund websites and the SeekingAlpha website between 2004 and 2020. In total, we have identified 170 publicly disclosed short-sale campaigns with socially responsible institutional ownership measure available. We find that there are more public short-sale campaigns for the low SR_IO group than the high SR_IO group (96 vs. 74), which suggests that hedge funds do tend to target stocks with high SR_IO somewhat less. To measure the social pressure that a short seller may take when it reveals a bearish view towards the target, we manually read each of the 7,326 comments associated with the 170 short sale campaigns, we assign an AGREEMENT_SCORE, which is equal to -1 if the comment is against the short-sale activity, +1 if the comment is supportive for the short-sale activity, and 0 if it is neutral. We use the public attitude towards the campaign (AGREEMENT_SCORE) as dependent variable, and socially responsible institutions as the independent variable in our panel regressions. We find supporting evidence that when a short seller publicly reveals a bearish view towards firms with higher socially responsible institutional ownership, there are more negative views from the public. Therefore, social pressure is a valid channel that affects short sellers’ trading behaviour. In another working paper “ESG and short selling”, we explore objective 4&5 in a more detailed way. Specifically, we identify a negative relationship between firm’s ESG performance and short selling activities among overpriced stocks. short selling overpriced stocks with high ESG scores is subject to a higher 1) synchronization risk—the shareholders of “the long side” are reluctant to sell the high ESG stocks; 2) ESG sentiment risk—high ESG stocks may experience sentiment-driven price jumps when public attention on ESG issues spikes; and 3) ESG reputation risk—short sellers who accumulate large positions on high ESG stocks may have bad ESG reputation. Therefore, objective 4&5 have been fully achieved.

24501519.label: Major findings and research outcome
24501519.value: Cao, Titman, Zhan, and Zhang (2021) document that socially responsible (SR) institutions tend to focus more on the ESG performance and less on quantitative signals of value. Consistent with this difference in focus, the study finds that SR institutions react less to quantitative mispricing signals. The evidence suggests that the increased focus on ESG may have influenced stock return patterns. Specifically, abnormal returns associated with these mispricing signals are greater for stocks held more by SR institutions. The link between SR ownership and the efficacy of mispricing signals only emerges in recent years with the rise of ESG investing and is significant only when there are arbitrage-related funding constraints. Cao, Titman, Zhan, and Zhang (2021) also explores the cost of shorting these stocks with high socially responsible institutional ownership. The study finds in terms of traditional short selling costs, firms with high and low SR institutional ownership are comparable. By manually collecting comments associated with short sale campaigns, the study finds short sellers take much higher social pressure when they short firms with high SR ownership. Zhan and Zhang (2022) document negative relationship between firm’s ESG performance and short selling activities among overpriced stocks. The study finds short selling overpriced stocks with high ESG scores is subject to a higher 1) synchronization risk—the shareholders of “the long side” are reluctant to sell the high ESG stocks; 2) ESG sentiment risk—high ESG stocks may experience sentiment-driven price jumps when public attention on ESG issues spikes; and 3) ESG reputation risk—short sellers who accumulate large positions on high ESG stocks may have bad ESG reputation thus potential fund outflow. Cao, Li, Zhan, Zhang, and Zhou (2022) extend the research agenda to the corporate bond markets and find bond mutual funds also have concerns when the issuer of a bond has very bad carbon performance. Such trading behaviour leads to a deteriorating liquidity condition of these bonds and worse stability of the corporate bond market. We have completed one published paper and two working papers: Cao, Jie, Sheridan Titman, Xintong Zhan, and Weiming Zhang, 2022, ESG Preference, Institutional Trading, and Stock Return Patterns, conditionally accepted at Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis Zhan, Xintong, and Weiming Zhang, 2022, ESG and Short Selling, Working Paper Cao, Jie, Yi Li, Xintong Zhan, Weiming Zhang, and Linyu Zhou, 2022, Carbon Emissions, Institutional Trading, and the Liquidity of Corporate Bonds, Working Paper

24501519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24501519.value: 1. We plan to extend our study to an international sample of stocks. It is known that different countries have different attitudes towards socially responsible investing. We expect that our main findings would be more pronounced in countries with higher levels of ESG awareness. 2. We plan to study the incentives of different institutions. Mutual funds are concerned with a firm’s ESG performance as they face redemption risks from the end investors. It is not clear about other institutions such as insurance companies and hedge funds. We would like to explore the footprint of these institutions to understand their mindset and trading behaviour.

24501519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24501519.value: The rise in sustainable investing brings with its pitfalls. The greater the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) credentials of a company, the less likely its shares are to reflect the company’s underlying value. Fundamental analysis of the stock market will yield signals that a company’s shares are either overpriced, suggesting investors should sell, or underpriced, suggesting investors should buy. But these signals are not heeded by investors seeking strong ESG holdings. That leads to inefficiencies in trading. Ignoring trading signals does not necessarily mean that the performance of the shares is better or worse. It simply means that their trading price is less volatile, more predictable, and at times not as efficient at reflecting the underlying fundamentals of the company. The popularity and rising prevalence of ESG investing therefore introduces new characteristics to the broader stock market. The more socially responsible investors that own a stock, the greater the inefficiency. That also means the predictability of the ESG-favourable stock is greater, too, almost triple the predictability of a stock that doesn’t classify as an ESG company.

24503519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24503519.value: Can you get information from your enemies without punishing, rewarding, or tricking them? It feels unlikely, but we show that you can, and moreover we investigate why. Suppose a decision maker DM faces a choice between two options. DM does not know which option is better, but his enemies, who wish DM to make the wrong choice, do. More specifically, each enemy has a piece of partial information about which option is better. We ask whether DM can extract these pieces of information from his enemies and make an informed choice benefiting him and hence harming them. In particular, we ask whether this can be done with a ''mechanism'', technically a contract between DM and the enemies stipulating which option DM has to choose given the information he gathers. Note that a mechanism disallows additional punishments or rewards. We surprisingly find that information extraction is possible in general. In addition, we find that: 1. If the mechanism has to be "ex post incentive compatible'', i.e. under the mechanism each enemy wishes to truthfully reveal his information even if he knew the information held by the other enemies, then information extraction is possible. 2. If the mechanism has to be "strategy-proof'', that is, under the mechanism each enemy wishes to truthfully reveal his information regardless of whether the other enemies are truthful or not, then information extraction is not possible. We will further the project by analyzing when can a "Bayesian incentive compatible'' mechanism extract information. Under such a mechanism, each enemy wishes to truthfully reveal his information as long as he believes that the other enemies are also truthful. We will look for an economically interpretable characterization of situations where information extraction is possible using a Bayesian incentive compatible mechanism. We will also apply the finding to discuss the robustness of voting mechanisms. 博弈中, 我方如何不用威逼利诱而获敌方机密？为求解答，本研究分析如下模型：某人(称DM) 需从L与R两项中选一。DM不明两项孰优, 反而, 有数个对家分别部分知晓两项孰优，他们却希望DM选错。我们发现： 1. DM可能巧妙设计信息披露机制使对家自愿（服从ex post 激励相容条件）披露机密。 2. 如果披露机制的激励相容条件加强为 strategy-proof , 则DM不可能从对家获得机密。 如果披露机制的激励相容条件减弱为 Bayesian incentive compatibility, 则DM更容易从对家获得机密。特别的，该结论可用来分析投票选举机制的设计。

24503519.label: Major findings and research outcome
24503519.value: A decision maker DM faces a binary choice. DM does not know which alternative is better, but a group of experts do. However, the experts would like DM to make the wrong choice. Given the hostility, is it still possible for DM to extract useful information from the experts using mechanism design? We answer “Yes”: There are mechanisms where truth-telling is a Bayesian or even ex post equilibrium, even though the information leak benefits DM and hurts the expert. On the other hand, if truth-telling is required to be an interim or ex post dominant strategy, then no mechanism extracts information in favor of DM. We also discuss two extensions. In the first extension, we show that DM can extract information even if his commitment to a mechanism is limited. In the second extension, we show that if DM can first Blackwell-garble the experts’ information, then information extraction becomes much easier. A paper is being prepared to present the research outcome. Spin-off project has also been completed and has led to the publication of a paper: "The limits of ex post implementation without transfers", with Tangren Feng and Axel Niemeyer (Theoretical Economics forthcoming).

24503519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24503519.value: In this study we have carefully examined a number of solution concepts, one of which is interim strategy-proofness. It turns out that this solution concept is understudied in literature and is particularly useful when it comes to designing mechanisms that are easy to use and robust. We have started exploring implications of this solution concept to mechanism design, and will push it further in the future.

24503519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24503519.value: This project studies if it is possible for someone to cleverly elicit useful information from other people---his ``enemies''---whose interests severely conflict his. We find that it indeed is possible, even if this person does not use reward or punishment to induce information revelation. Voluntary information revelation is made possible by driving a wedge between the enemies so that their interests, initially aligned, become diverged. This study helps us understand how information transmission may be possible even in adverse environments.

24603119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24603119.value: Today, China occupies a position of ever-increasing importance in the global economy, transnational policy, and international institutions. As a result, there is lively debate in academic and political circles as to whether China will prove to be a “status quo” power, which endorses the existing international system, or a “revisionist” one, which seeks to transform that system. However, existing discourse tends to focus solely on China’s experience and behavior in the course of its economic rise following the start of the “Reform and Opening-Up” era in 1979. This is particularly true in the case of the relatively few works analyzing China’s relationship with public international law, which often portray it as a kind of recent newcomer (and potential disruptor) to a preexisting Western international legal system. This project challenges that prevailing model, proposing instead that a longer view of the international legal system, and the global governance networks in which it is embedded, reveals that China has long exercised extensive theoretical and practical influence on their development. More specifically, it uses analysis of legal documents, diplomatic communications, and archival sources to clarify: 1) how different conceptions of sovereignty have historically developed in China, and how these have exerted impact on its domestic and international legal activities; 2) how China’s theorization and practice of sovereign power have affected the key transformations of modern positive international law from the early 17th century through today; and 3) the ways that China’s unique international role has historically contributed to the development of specific concepts such as border sovereignty, substantive obligations in international treaties, individual responsibility in international criminal law, and ethnic self-determination. As the project will show, China’s history of diplomatic and legal engagement with outside states features many existing and potential contributions to the understanding of state sovereignty and international order. China’s influence today, via its multilateral initiatives such as the One Belt, One Road (OBOR) project, Asian International Investment Bank (AIIB), and Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), similarly carry broader implications for the role of sovereign states in an interconnected world. Rather than a “newcomer” to public international law, China is best seen as a longtime active participant in the latter’s historical development and current operation. This carries implications not only for how China’s international role can be better understood, but also for developing a more nuanced theoretical account of “international law” itself, as an inherently multipolar system based on pluralistic influences. 今天的中國在全球經濟，全球治理，和國際組織等領域都處在一個越來越重要的地位。這一趨勢引起了許多學者的討論：中國是否將偏向於“保持常態”的國際角色，還是要“修整”已經存在的國際制度。不過這些討論大多數都是默認的把中國視為1979年以來以西方為中心的國際法制度的“新會員國。” 這項研究項目將試圖以更廣闊的歷史視角來證明中國早就對現有的國際公法理論與實踐的發展起到了重要的影響。主要通過法律文件，外交通訊等現存的歷史文獻進行研究，這個研究項目旨在研究：1）中國歷來對主權概念的不同了解和表現形式，以及其對其法律體系和對外關係的影響；2）中國所提倡的主權概念與現代的實在國際法的互相影響與演變過程 ；3）中國獨特的國際角色與歷史是怎麼對現有的國際公法概念，包括邊界主權，國際條約所規定的國家責任，國際刑事法的個人責任，民族自決等規範起了重要的影響。 中國與外國的外交與法律方面的交流歷史可以讓我們對今天的國家主權與國際制度有更深的了解。中國最近以來的國際影響，比如說一帶一路，亞投行，区域全面经济伙伴关系協定，上海合作组织等多邊的交流與合作平台也可以被看作是中國對其主權與國際公法歷史的繼承表現。最好不應該把中國看成一個國際公法的“新會員國，”而應該視其為現有國際公法的建立國家之一。按照這個歷史發展的視角，對中國在國際公法中扮演的角色的認識以及對國際公法本身的理論建構的了解都將有所改變。尤其是中國的國際公法史可以表明國際公法本身不應該脫離其多邊主義與多元化的思想根基。

24603119.label: Realisation of objectives
24603119.value: This project successfully accomplished the five listed objectives that were noted by the PI as the goals of the research to be conducted. The following summary is intended to indicate the ways in which the research project, as well as the resulting publications, realised the primary aims that the PI set out to achieve. First, with regards to the objective of "provid[ing] the first comprehensive analysis of Chinese conceptions of sovereignty and international order in comparison with the primary Western theoretical models", this project did indeed carry out a comprehensive comparison of Chinese discourses of sovereignty and how these were informed by, and at times diverged from, those prevalent in the West. The PI's archival research in Qing Dynasty and Republican Era archival materials, especially those of the Zongli Yamen (the Qing foreign affairs ministry), were invaluable in turning up new discourses of the concept of sovereignty and its ramifications that had been hitherto unexplored in scholarly literature. These discussions of sovereignty, such as those by leading Qing officials of the Xianfeng, Tongzhi, and Guangxu Emperors' respective courts, were often highly illuminating with respect to Chinese incorporation of the Western lexicon of state sovereignty during important historical episodes. Especially illuminating in this regard were findings regarding the way in which aspects of imperial China's state system, such as the acceptability of dispersed management of state personnel with regards to some border issues, differed from Western understandings of the unitary authority of the sovereign state. The process by which such understandings shifted over time were explored in detail in the publications resulting from this project, especially the monograph "Recentering the World: China and the Transformation of International Law" as well as the Asian Journal of International Law article "China’s Participation in the Second Hague Conference and the Concept of Equal Sovereignty in International Law." Later, Chinese views on the importance of state sovereignty converged much more closely with those of Western states, however even during these periods (e.g., during the interwar era and during and after the Second World War) Chinese officials and scholars tended to have different focuses and understandings of issues of sovereignty, often being especially concerned with the imposition of limitations on the use of force as well as the legalisation of interstate relations through the mediation of international courts and arbitration. These factors were also thoroughly explored in the research project and featured in the resulting publications. Meanwhile, more recent divergences such as the Chinese focus on promoting a more state-centric conception of human rights, as opposed to one emphasising individual civil and political rights, were also explored in the course of the research project and reflected in the resulting publication in the American University International Law Review article "The Emerging Chinese Doctrine of Statist Human Rights." Second, the research project effectively "made use of historical legal documents and archival materials to demonstrate the significant role that Chinese thought and practice played in the history of international law." It accomplished this objective through the PI and research staff's thorough exploration of archives including those of various Chinese foreign ministries and related bodies, as well as a great degree of archival and database materials regarding legal interactions such as the important treaty-negotiation conferences in which the Qing Dynasty, Republic of China, and People's Republic of China were involved. The conclusions reached upon the basis of this research, meanwhile, did indeed relate not only to Chinese views and positions on sovereignty and international law, but also to the impacts that these views and interactions had upon the practice of other states as well as shifts in international norms. While not attempting to make an excessively bold claim that Chinese influences were primarily responsible for shaping international legal norms or institutions that had global origins, this project did reveal important aspects of Chinese influence that had previously been unknown or underemphasised. The role of Chinese lawyers and diplomats in proposing limitations on the use of force during the League of Nations era, for example, was a particularly important topic in the research conducted, and the PI's conclusion that Chinese figures were among the pioneers in this regard with respect to the global international law profession was a significant one. Third, and relatedly, the PI effectively helped to "further the theoretical understanding of sovereignty as a transcultural phenomenon, rather than one whose intellectual content is derived solely from Western influences." The research project was ideally geared towards achieving this aim because its inherent focus was the reception of and impact upon sovereignty of China, a major non-Western state. However, the PI also proactively sought to ensure that the topic of diverse and non-Western intellectual influences upon the development of international law, including as well as going beyond China itself, was also addressed at various points while conducting the research and publishing its results. Thus, for example, the author devoted considerable time to exploring discussions of sovereignty and international law not only in China or by Chinese individuals, but also among China's Global South partners in Asia, Latin America, and Africa. Aspects of these findings were introduced into the resulting publications in order to help contextualise Chinese contributions and to put the "China - West" relationship into a more globalised and detailed frame of analysis. Fourth, the project did result in "providing the first ever translations into English of [some] key Chinese primary sources embodying historical and current discourse trends regarding state sovereignty." Naturally, many important primary sources regarding these issues have already previously been translated, anthologised, or otherwise made available in English. However, the PI identified a number of key materials, often in highly bureaucratic Classical Chinese or other relatively challenging written styles, that had never previously been translated into English but were highly relevant to the research project. Many excerpts of such sources, and a few in their entirety (such as the important 1871 Okubo Memorandum regarding Sino-Japanese confrontations over the law of territorial sovereignty) were newly translated into English by the PI, making them available as resources for future scholarly research conducted in English. Fifth, the research project did result in a "book-length report specifically regarding Chinese conceptions of sovereignty and international order, to serve as a useful academic reference for others working in this area and related fields." The resulting publication "Recentering the World: China and the Transformation of International Law", published by Cambridge University Press, is an original monograph-length scholarly exploration of the above themes that focuses, to a greater degree than any other academic monograph published in English to date, on explicating the relationship between Chinese conceptions of sovereignty, international law, and international order, and on the ways that such conceptions have impacted global developments with respect to these concepts. It contrasts with other works to date that have been more specifically focused on historical accounts of the Chinese state or, when focusing on the intellectual history of sovereignty and/or international law, have not paired this with a sustained analysis of Chinese participation in and interactions with international organisations or specific norms of positive international law. The monograph thus has made a highly unique contribution that spans the disciplines of international law doctrine, legal history, and modern Chinese history.

24603119.label: Major findings and research outcome
24603119.value: The major findings of the research conducted include the identification of a number of important legal scholars and academics in China from the period of 1850-2000, especially the early part of this range, whose contributions to modern Chinese conceptions of sovereignty and international law were previously unknown or poorly understood. In addition, the research involved the identification and investigation of new materials in important diplomatic archives and other sources with relevant information about the history of international legal thought and practice in China. A particular focus was the exploration of the diplomatic archives of multiple states with regards to Chinese participation in and contributions to major, sovereignty-limiting international law conferences such as The Hague Conferences of 1899 and 1907, as well as the Paris Peace Conference of 1919 and the San Francisco Conference that led to the founding of the United Nations. Each of these episodes, as well as several others of similar importance, was developed on the basis of the above-mentioned newly-identified primary sources into a detailed historical account, which sheds new light on the importance of the diplomatic/legal interactions in question, their impacts upon the development of core international norms and institutions, and especially their relationship with concepts of state sovereignty. Particularly significant was the identification of the contributions of particular legal scholars and diplomats, such as the longtime Chinese representative to the League of Nations Zhou Wei, who have been largely left out of many subsequent historical narratives in both English and Chinese. These more obscure individuals are, for the first time, developed into major figures in modern Chinese legal history in my book Recentering the World: China and the Transformation of International Law (which resulted from this project). Meanwhile, much more well-known figures such as Wellington Koo, W.A.P. Martin, or Wang Chonghui, about whom extensive historical material already exists, are also explored in new detail in this book, with major contributions such as Wang's role in the planning of the International Court of Justice, for example, being put in connection with his earlier experiences as a lawyer and diplomat during the League of Nations era. Given the fundamental importance of legal concepts such as human rights and the equality of states to the concept of sovereignty, these issues and the exploration of their connection with shifting Chinese views on sovereignty were the focus of additional article publications that arose out of the project.

24603119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24603119.value: This research might be further developed in the future through several pathways, including via additional studies of historical episodes in which Chinese views on sovereignty impacted directly upon either official or public reactions to major issues in international law and relations. Such episodes, some of which were not fully explored in the course of this research project, include Chinese interactions with Western states with respect to the Korean and Vietnam Wars, the Suez Crisis, and other important Cold War episodes during which official Chinese state representatives as well as lawyers and academics in civil society made written and spoken contributions to public discourse, domestically and internationally. While the overall picture of how sovereignty was conceptualised during the early to mid Cold War period was conveyed through the study conducted in the course of this research project, many further nuances might be profitably explored, such as the ways in which doctrines on the use of force (i.e., interventions against sovereignty understood as territorial integrity) were highly malleable during the periods of the Sino-Soviet split in international relations. Additional archival resources, in China and in other jurisdictions (especially regionally), might help to shed more light upon such issues.

24603119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24603119.value: This research project helped to develop a new, more detailed understanding of how Chinese officials, lawyers, and citizens came to think of their country as a "sovereign state", and how they envisioned and interacted with a world order established upon the basis of state sovereignty. It relied on the exploration of sources including diplomatic archives, other government ministry records, archival holdings of international organisations, biographical materials, as well as periodicals and scholarly publications, all of which contained significant information regarding individuals' and organisations' claims about the concept of sovereignty and the authority of the sovereign Chinese state during various historical episodes. The long-term value of the research project lies primarily in making possible more nuanced conversations and analysis regarding China's positions on issues of sovereignty and international law. Sovereign rights are among the most important topics within the field of international legal discourse, as they are often treated as defining the limitations of the application of international norms. In many legal and diplomatic interactions, sovereignty comes into play, often as a concept that is being invoked by both sides of a disagreement. This project helps to clarify how some such debates have their origins in a long historical process.

24604619.label: Project Objectives
24604619.value: To contribute to the historiography of Hong Kong cinema by studying the history of an important but relatively neglected genre, the crime film. To bring genre theory to Hong Kong cinema studies, and to explore how Hong Kong cinema can contribute to global genre studies. To propose the crime film as a productive category in our understanding of Hong Kong cinema, by highlighting its ability to uncover hitherto neglected connections between various subgenres. To rethink the genre-society relationship that is often assumed in studies of specific film genres by taking a “theoretically cubist” approach and treating the crime film in relationship to, rather than as a reflection of, the wider contextual culture. To explore how the crime film—by staging particular affective encounters and otherwise—engages Hong Kong society’s conflicting attitudes towards ideas of justice, the rule of law, and the authorities.

24604619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24604619.value: Crime movies are undoubtedly one of Hong Kong cinema’s most famous exports. However, while the territory’s martial arts cinema has been the subject of multiple books, the Hong Kong crime film and its history have not yet been the subject of a dedicated monograph. This project proposes to change this state of affairs, by tracing the history of the genre since the late 1940s. By adopting a multidimensional theoretical approach that moves beyond treating the crime film as a collection of texts to be analyzed and instead also considers the constitution of the category itself in its various discursive contexts, it aims to produce a comprehensive historical account of this important Hong Kong genre. This approach will enable a reconsideration of the local crime film as intertwined with international and regional cinematic trends, the local socio-economic and political environment, the colonial government’s censorship policies, as well as critical and scholarly discourse on the genre and its subgenres’ existence. By focusing on films dealing with crime and related social problems, the project will also contribute to our understanding of the contemporaneous and conflicting social attitudes towards issues of law, justice and governmental authority. These concerns are common to modernizing and urbanizing societies around the world, but they have their own unique inflections and import in the Hong Kong context. Building on years of preparatory research, the project will make use of and expand a database of Hong Kong crime films since 1947 as well as hundreds of notes and synopses of relevant films. It will further draw on primary sources such as documents related to film censorship from government archives in London and Hong Kong, as well as film magazines, promotion materials and newspaper articles available at the Hong Kong Film Archive. The goal is to make a significant contribution not only to the historiography of Hong Kong cinema, but also to the way film genre in general is studied and understood. Although the Hong Kong film industry has experienced a steady decline since the mid-1990s, the crime film and its accumulated conventions continue to influence filmmaking today, not only in Hong Kong, but also in the rest of the world, and especially in mainland China. A study of the genre’s past will therefore also shed light on its more recent reincarnations in China’s rapidly rising film industry.

24604619.label: Realisation of objectives
24604619.value: The main deliverable promised for this two-year ECS project was the preparation of a book manuscript on the history of the Hong Kong crime film. After a three month extension of the project, I am almost finished putting the full manuscript through several rounds of revision and am starting to approach publishers to gauge interest. My goal is to secure a contract with a reputable academic press by the end of the year at the latest, so that the book can come out in 2023-24. The below indicates to which degree the manuscript achieves the original objectives. Objective 1: To contribute to the historiography of Hong Kong cinema by studying the history of an important but relatively neglected genre, the crime film. This project significantly changed shape in the course of research and writing. After writing the first few chapters, I realised the manuscript was becoming too long for any publisher to even consider. I had originally planned to write a history of the Hong Kong crime film from the 1940s to the present, but as I struggled with the expanding size of the manuscript, I found that I could easily turn this project into two stand-alone books, each with their own distinctive arguments. What I have now competed is the first of those books, which is basically a “pre-history” of the Hong Kong crime film, before the genre became locally and internationally prominent following the success of John Woo’s "A Better Tomorrow" (Yingxiong bense, 1986). It thus covers the period from the 1930s to the mid-1980s. As I discuss below, this altered the other original objectives somewhat, but in terms of this first objective—contributing to Hong Kong film historiography—it surpasses what was originally planned, as the period covered is woefully understudied. The manuscript for the first time presents a comprehensive overview of the crime film from the 1940s to the 1960s, and breaks new ground by considering the changes in the crime film through the lens of colonial censorship and various social issues from the late 1960s to the early 1980s. Objective 2: To bring genre theory to Hong Kong cinema studies, and to explore how Hong Kong cinema can contribute to global genre studies. In the early stages of this project, I attempted to directly bring in film genre theory to construct the central argument of the book. This turned out somewhat dissatisfactory, as the importation of Hollywood-centred genre theory felt somewhat sterile and I could achieve no real breakthrough. While I still engage genre theory in the finished manuscript and the book as a whole is still unabashedly a genre study, I eventually shifted the focus away from genre theory somewhat and instead proposed the concept of “criminal realism” as crucial to our understanding of the Hong Kong crime film from the 1930s to the 1980s. Criminal realism refers both to the colonial censorship that to varying degrees criminalised explorations of local realities during this period, and to the critically contested nature of the realism of crime films locally. Rather than a sterile application of existing genre theories, I believe the manuscript in this way makes its own theoretical contribution to Hong Kong film studies—one that should also be relevant to scholars working on genre, the crime film and realism in other contexts. Objective 3: To propose the crime film as a productive category in our understanding of Hong Kong cinema, by highlighting its ability to uncover hitherto neglected connections between various sub-genres. The manuscript illustrates the usefulness of the crime film as a lens through which to study local film history. The boundary between various crime sub-genres such as the detective film, suspense thriller, gangster film, etc. is always blurry in any case, and focusing on the crime film as a whole has facilitated the tracing of film censorship’s impact on local filmmaking, as well as the establishing of connections between contentious social issues and the way these influenced particular sub-genres. An awareness of the various sub-genres that the broader frame of the crime film facilitates for instance reveals the importance of Kuei Chih-hung’s "The Teahouse" (Chengji chalou, 1974), a hit film that combined in embryonic form many of the sub-genres and figures that would come to define the Hong Kong crime film in later years, such as the figure of the vigilante, the triad society with its particular culture, the immigrant gangster, and even the undercover cop. While some previous commentators have noted the importance of Kuei’s film based on its general subject matter and its box-office success, attention to issues of genre can more carefully pinpoint its actual significance. Objective 4: To rethink the genre-society relationship that is often assumed in studies of specific film genres by taking a “theoretically cubist” approach and treating the crime film in relationship to, rather than as a reflection of, the wider contextual culture. While I have largely abandoned the explicit “theoretically cubist” approach mentioned in the original objective as part of my general move away from a too mechanical application of Hollywood-centred genre theory, the genre-society relationship has remained central to the project. I have taken a historicist approach, looking at how the crime film was shaped by and itself shaped a moral panic around (youth) crime in the 1960s and 1970s, while also interacting with film censorship and influential foreign films. To stay with the example of "The Teahouse", which Kuei claimed was inspired by the Charles Bronson vehicle "Death Wish" (1974), a consideration of the film in terms of its encounter with colonial censorship and its reference to various social problems and debates of the time (such as the panic around juvenile delinquency and the discussions surrounding the death penalty) both deepen the understanding of the film itself and vividly bring to life the social context of the mid-1970s. Placing this film then next to contemporary films that took a much less critical view of the authorities further shows how films participate in a kind of public discussion: they both reflect and shape the society that produced them. Objective 5: To explore how the crime film—by staging particular affective encounters and otherwise—engages Hong Kong society’s conflicting attitudes towards ideas of justice, the rule of law, and the authorities. In my original conceptualisation of the project, this final objective would have been pursued more in the later chapters of the book dealing with the history of the crime film since the 1980s. It will certainly be a key theme in the follow-up book I hope to write on the Hong Kong crime film: in the one chapter I have already written for this book, these concerns take central stage. Still, the interest in how crime films engage society’s attitudes towards the rule of law, justice and the authorities is present in the background of the currently completed manuscript as well. In the first two chapters, for instance, I consider the subtly negative depiction of police officers in 1950s and 1960s films, as well as their perhaps even more telling absence from most crime stories at the time.

24604619.label: Major findings and research outcome
24604619.value: The main outcome of this project is a ca. 85,000-word book manuscript with the proposed title “Criminal Realism: Hong Kong Crime Cinema, Censorship, and Society”. As a genre history, it uncovers a number of nearly forgotten films and presents a pathbreaking historical account. Some of the manuscript's main contributions are: - It traces back the local crime film’s history to the 1930s, and it sheds light on the genre’s many links to pre-1949 Shanghai popular culture. - It looks at the remarkable local impact of Alfred Hitchcock’s suspense thrillers, exploring the numerous local remakes of his films. - It systematically looks at the impact of film censorship on Hong Kong film genres, and highlights several films that influenced censorship, especially during the transitional period from the late 1960s to the early 1980s. - It historically contextualises a large number of crime films, situating them in relation to contemporary social debates as well as local and international cinematic trends. - It challenges the conventional dismissal of the Shaw Brothers output of the 1970s as out of touch with local realities, arguing that in the middle of the decade Shaw Brothers actually produced several pioneering crime films. - It provides a different perspective on the otherwise much-studied Hong Kong New Wave filmmakers, who, it is often overlooked, made their cinematic debuts overwhelmingly in the crime genre. The original project proposal planned for presentations at three international conferences. Due to COVID-19 making conference travel impossible during the entire duration of the grant, I have only been able to join four conferences as an online participant: I gave presentations based on different chapters of the book in September 2020 (AAS-in-Asia conference), May 2021 (Nottingham-Ningbo conference), June 2021 (Society for Hong Kong Studies conference) and March 2022 (AAS conference). As a result, the grant money set aside for conference expenses has barely been used.

24604619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24604619.value: The original goal of this project was to write the history of the Hong Kong crime film up to the present. For reasons outlined above, the book manuscript only deals with the period from the 1930s to the 1980s. A logical further development of this research is to write a second book that brings the historical narrative up to the present. One chapter that could go into this next book has already been written, and I have last Fall submitted a GRF proposal to fund this research (result pending). The research on the history of Hong Kong film censorship that I engaged in for this book could also be developed into a separate project. In this respect, I am considering organising a conference that may lead to an edited volume on the history of film censorship in East and Southeast Asia.

24604619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24604619.value: This project has resulted in a book manuscript that looks at the history of the Hong Kong crime film from the 1930s to the 1980s. When published, it will be the first book in any language to systematically study this subject. The book’s major contribution lies in its putting forward and developing the concept of “criminal realism” as the defining characteristic of the Hong Kong crime film during the period under study. This concept refers both to the role of colonial censorship that basically made the depiction of certain aspects of local reality off-limits, and to the contested realism of crime films. Drawing on extensive archival research, the book breaks new ground in its close study of the impact of censorship on local filmmaking and provides an unprecedented close analysis of the genre’s evolution before it reached local and international prominence. Paying close attention not only to the impact of censorship, but also to the influence of foreign films, contemporary social issues and literary works, the book treats crime films as both reflecting and shaping the society that produced them.

24604819.label: Project Title(Chinese)
24604819.value: 晚清到當代上海的方言書寫與身份形成

24604819.label: Project Objectives
24604819.value: To represent the history of dialect literature in Shanghai in relation to broader economic, political, demographic and cultural transformations in China. To analyze narratological devices, aesthetic styles, and marketing strategies of dialect writing in Shanghai using examples of serialized novels, short stories, folk songs, and poetry as well as study the history of their reception, adaptation, translation, and canonization. To re-evaluate the role and status of dialect writing in the New Culture Movement and the formation of literary modernity in China. To develop a theoretical framework for understanding dialect literature beyond the national literature model. To offer informed recommendations for language policy makers and education departments on dialect learning. To provide comparable suggestions for handling the tension between promoting Mandarin and preserving local dialects in other dialect-speaking regions such as Guangdong, Fujian, Hong Kong, and Macau.

24604819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24604819.value: 本課題研究晚清到當代在上海產生的吳方言書寫的歷史變遷及其文化意涵。明清至民國初期不斷發展的各地區方言為新國語提供了重要的語料資源。在各方言區中，吳方言區擁有豐富的口頭文學傳統，藉由印刷出版業在上海的興起與發展，以報章雜誌等形式接觸廣大讀者。隨著國語運動與普通話推廣等一系列語言文字改革的推行，方言書寫的地位雖漸趨邊緣，但吳方言仍在上海及海外華人文學文化中佔據一席之地。本課題關注晚清上海小說中的吳方言書寫，民國初期新文化運動對方言文學的經典化，四十年代左翼作家倡導方言文學的運動，新中國成立之後方言文學的式微，以及八十年代以來方言文學及其影視改編在上海及海外上海移民群體中的復甦。通過文化研究，翻譯研究，媒體與聲音研究等方法，本課題將方言書寫置於國家語言政策，印刷出版業及讀者消費模式，跨媒介傳播，以及上海人在港台，東南亞地區，及北美地區的移民歷史的發展變遷中。通過追溯上海的吳方言連載小說，短篇故事，民歌民謠等體裁的作品的發展歷史，本課題聚焦晚清到現當代的口頭文學對地方文學史以及地方身份形成的重要影響，並為理解方言與國語在中國以及華語世界中錯綜複雜的歷史關係提供新的理論學習方法。

24604819.label: Realisation of objectives
24604819.value: With the help of ECS grant, the PI has realized the objectives proposed in the revised proposal from the following perspectives. 1. Despite the travel restriction imposed by different regions the PI proposed to visit and conduct archival research, the PI has obtained archival materials through a local researcher, and expanded the database of Wu-dialect literature and culture produced during the Republican era and the first seventeen years of PRC history. In the past, this time period is always missing in official history about Shanghai literature written in dialect. An important discovery of this period is the local newspaper and magazine that carried bits and pieces of dialect writing. In addition, local opera and other performative arts also contain dialect elements in its scripts. This finding will significantly enlarge the database for researchers who are working on similar topics. 2. With the discovery of the aforementioned archival materials, the PI is expected to analyze the narratological devices, aesthetic styles, and marketing strategies of these works. However, due to COVID-19, the PI was not able to visit the archives personally, and the local libraries and archives opened limited seats each day to visitors. Each day, the local researcher had to compete with other visitors for the limited seats via the online reservation system. To minimize physical contact, the libraries and archives also restricted the visitors from the browsing room, and only allowed them to request one stack of newspaper and magazines per visit. The researcher then had to scan the materials to be sent to the PI. This has seriously delayed the progress of this project. Fortunately, through the visits to the libraries and archives over 2 months, the PI found useful materials through the scanned documents by the researcher. Hence, in the following months, the PI will be able to analyze the materials and complete this objective according to the ECS proposal. With the lifting of travel restrictions, the PI can finally visit these locations personally during the summer 2023 and further conduct archival research. 3. With the newly discovered materials, the PI is able to re-evaluate the role and status of dialect writing in the New Culture Movement and the formation of literary modernity in China. The potential theoretical framework will draw upon Sinophone studies theory, folk culture studies, and sound studies. The most important contribution of this project will be to contextualize Shanghai literature in the global flow of words and ideas, and treat Shanghai literature not solely as a regional literature of China, but rather viewing it from a global perspective. Drawing upon narrative strategies from other Sinophone communities, Shanghai dialect literature serves as a good example of world literature in the age of globalization. 4. The project aims at offering informed recommendations for language policy makers and education departments on dialect learning. One major suggestion for policy makers generated through the research findings of this project is, that dialect literature should not be considered as the opposite of Mandarin writing, as something that deviates from the agenda of promoting national identity. Rather, it fosters a stronger attachment and sentiment towards the local while at the same time conforms with and even stresses Chineseness in a more inclusive way. Hence, the government and educational system should utilize dialect literature as a good way of enhancing cultural identity.
