24615919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24615919.value: Competence in early mathematics is crucial for later school success. Although research indicates that a spatial and hands-on approach to learning improves student engagement and mathematics skills for young learners, such approach has been difficult to implement in mathematics education, especially in Hong Kong, partly due to the culture of drilling and recalling procedures by manipulation of abstract symbols on paper. In contrast, Making draws upon the innately human desire to make things with our hands. One important application of Making in education is a spatial and hands-on approach to learning which also has implications for meeting the global needs for expertise in the Science-Technology-Engineering-Mathematics (STEM) disciplines. Despite its significance, few research has examined the effects of Making in education, including how Making may effectively support technology-enhanced mathematics and/or STEM learning. This study builds on the PI’s previously developed notion of ‘learning as Making’ (LaM) to examine mathematics learning in a highly transformative and technological Making environment; it involves the use of 3D Printing Pens which enables 3D models to be created instantly via one’s moving hand. Within this particular LaM environment, students are engaged in inquiry-based learning through hands-on production of 3D-printed artefacts, which serve as both diagrams (processes) and products of learning. LaM aligns with emerging theoretical developments on gestures, embodiment and materialist perspectives of thinking and learning. The PI has conducted relevant empirical studies, pointing towards the rich mathematics learning with LaM in primary schools. This design-based research explores the effect of a LaM pedagogy in mathematics education through designing and implementing twelve teaching experiments in six Hong Kong primary schools. In this mix-method study, (1) students’ development of visualisation, generalisation, and problem solving in mathematics will be analysed statistically using pre- and post-test measures, and (2) students’ inquiry-based Making during the lessons and post-lesson interviews will be captured via video-recording, after which discourse and micro-genetic analyses will examine students’ learning and sense-making processes with 3D Printing Pens. This study fills the research gap with regard to the changing nature of knowledge, learning and pedagogy in the digital age, in that it will advance the educational potential of 3D printing technology and LaM in school mathematics in particular and STEM education in general. Its findings will contribute to teaching and learning abstract mathematical and/or STEM concepts in hands-on, technological, and innovation-oriented environments. More broadly, it will contribute to speculation on the future potential of emergent technologies in education and LaM curricula. 早期數學基礎對於成就以後學習至關重要。儘管研究指出，空間感訓練以及實踐式學習有助於年幼學生的數學參與度和數學技能的培養，但這些學習方法在數學教育中很難實施，特別是在香港。部分原因在於香港數學教育文化偏向重視以抽象化的數學符號進行反覆練習和運算。相比之下，「造」則迎合人類以雙手創新的天性和對製造的好奇。尤其在教學中，「造」強調空間感訓練以及實踐式學習，這同時迎合到國際間對科學（Science）、技術（Technology）、工程（Engineering）及數學（簡稱STEM）學科專業知識的需求。儘管其意義重大，但少有研究考察過「造」對教育的影響，例如「造」能如何有效支援數學及STEM的科技增進學習。 是次研究建基於研究員先前研發的「造中學」（Learning as Making）概念，以探討在創新、製造、和技術化的環境中學習數學。這其中涉及3D打印筆的應用，讓參與者能即時創建3D模型並進行探究式學習。「造中學」與手勢學、具身化認知、新物質主義等新興理論保持一致。研究員曾進行相關的實驗研究，顯示「造中學」能豐富小學數學學習。 此設計本位研究將在香港六所小學中設計並實行十二個教學實驗，從而探討「造中學」教學法對數學教育的影響。本次的混合研究中，數據的收集和分析包括：學生在數學中形象化、歸納和解難方面的發展，學生在課堂中探究「造」的過程，以及課後訪談，並從對話及微觀發生法的分析中探討學生用3D打印筆時的學習和意義建構過程。 這項研究增加了對數碼時代中日新月異的知識、學習和教學的研究，從而提升3D打印技術和「造中學」兩者在學校中，特別是數學，以至是STEM教育中的教育潛力。其研究結果將有助於在實踐式學習、技術和創新導向的環境中數學及STEM相關概念的教育和學習。更廣泛而論，研究結果將有助預測未來新興科技在教學和「造中學」課程中的潛力。

24615919.label: Realisation of objectives
24615919.value: Overall, the study has fully met the project objectives set out as planned. The four project objectives were realized in the form of 9 research outputs (7 published journal articles and 2 accepted book chapters). In what follows, the PI provides a summary of project objectives achieved, followed by a more specific account of how each objective was achieved. Upon completion of the project, the research team has gathered quantitative evidence (Project Objective 1) and qualitative evidence (Project Objectives 2 and 3) of the effect of implementing a "Learning as Making (LaM) pedagogy" through inquiry-based Making with 3D Printing Pens, on primary students' geometry learning. Also under Research Objective 2, the research team generated findings regarding primary school teachers’ professional development by investigating their discourse change during and after Maker-centered mathematics lessons for inquiry-based geometry teaching. Regarding the fourth objective, the research team developed empirically-grounded theoretical accounts about LaM pedagogy and designed technology-enhanced learning tasks that promote productive mathematics/STEM learning, as well as engaging the PI’s research findings with the academic and professional communities to increase the research and social impact of this project. For example, a list of seven research outputs in the form of research and professional seminars have been generated as a result of the project (see Part C, Section 12). Research Objective 1. This objective was achieved and documented in Ng et al. (2021) and Ng and Ye (2022). In particular, Ng et al. (2021) reports the effects of two classroom-based technology-enhanced teaching interventions, conducted in two schools in sixth (age 11–12) grade. In one school, the intervention involves the use of a class set of 3D Printing Pens, and in another school the use of dynamic geometry environments, for inquiry-based learning of the relations among the number of vertices, edges, and faces of prisms and pyramids. A pretest-posttest-delayed posttest design was used to assess students’ prior knowledge before the intervention started, the learning outcomes obtained immediately after intervention, and the retention of knowledge after the interventions had been completed for a sustained period of time. The purpose of this study is to explore differences in geometry learning outcomes in two technology-enhanced environments, one that involves dynamic, visual representations of geometry and another that involves embodied actions of constructing physical 3D solids. Among the results, it was observed that students with the aid of 3D Pens demonstrated better retention of the properties of 3D solids than their dynamic geometry counterparts. Namely, the results from the ANCOVA suggest that the retention effect was more significant with 3D Pens. This study has established evidence that the digital instructions produced strong but relatively temporary geometry learning outcomes, while 3D Pen instructions as a form of embodied learning can help solidify that knowledge. Likewise, Ng and Ye (2022) used a mixed-methods design, with quantitative results showing that the designed learning activities with 3D Printing Pens greatly supported student learning on all questions related to working with vertices (0D), edges (1D), and faces (2D). The results of these studies further shed light on the effect of visual and sensory-motor experiences on school mathematics learning and corroborate previous work showing that the effects of gesture are particularly good at promoting long-lasting learning. Research Objective 2. The PI achieved this dual objective of observing teachers’ and students’ mathematical discourse in the following studies: Ng & Ye (2022); Ng & Chan (2021); Ng & Park (2021); and Ng et al. (accepted). For example, in Ng and Ye (accepted), the researchers observed that the students produced hand movements and language that were conducive to learning the properties of 3D solids while they interacted with 3D Printing Pens. In this study, two significant findings were reported. First, constructions with 3D Pens supported students’ composition of 3D solids by their 0D, 1D, and 2D parts, as well as improved students’ visualization of the relationships of these parts in embodied ways. Second, constructions with 3D Pens gave rise to gestures conducive to learning the properties of 3D solids. This study draws attention to the unity of mind–body and body–tool interactions in the act of making something (i.e., mathematics learning as embodied making). In Ng and Park (2021) as well as Ng and Chan (2021), the researchers focused on in-service and pre-service teachers’ discourse respectively when learning to use the technology of 3D Pens in classroom teaching. For the former study, it was observed that pre-service teachers developed expertise by reflecting on the coordination of using 3D Pens towards achieving curricular goals. Importantly, their discourse showed that they did not only realize the impact of 3D Pen instruction but also compared it with the use of traditional teaching aids to enhance student learning. In Ng and Chan (2021), the researchers analyzed four in-service mathematics teachers’ noticing upon watching video episodes showing an actual mathematics lesson that implemented 3D Printing Pens for teaching and learning shape and space. Analysis included what the teachers identified as important or noteworthy in the video, and thematically accounting for the teachers’ interpretations and decisions in relation to using 3D Pens for teaching and learning mathematics. Findings suggest that the teachers underwent a discourse change by realizing the affordances of 3D printing as novel-to-them technologies. Research Objective 3. This objective was exemplified in Ng and Ye (accepted), in which the researchers adopted the theoretical approach of inclusive materialism, which sheds light on the ontologies of the body and mathematics in the teaching and learning activities with 3D printing technologies. Based on the linguistic expressions and gestures of students using 3D Pens for inquiry-based learning, the authors conclude that 3D Pens can support students’ understanding and construction of 3D solids. Theoretically, the adoption of a materialist perspective was helpful for exploring the unique prospect of using 3D Pens in mathematical activities, as embodied diagramming/gesturing during material creation which engenders new possibilities for encounters with mathematical concepts. Research Objective 4. The PI achieved this objective by providing an empirically grounded account of student learning and teacher professional development throughout the project, through actively engaging in classroom-based interventions with school mathematics teachers to develop a technology-enhanced constructionist pedagogy, termed ‘learning as making’. In Ng (2020), the PI shares one of these experiences of working with teachers on developing constructionist learning activities with 3D Pens, in particular, providing an account of collaborating with local primary school teachers on planning a lesson for properties of triangles. In Ng and Tsang (2020), the researchers further developed a three-fold characterization of constructionist learning in mathematics education, drawing upon examples from the project and the innate human desire to make things with our hands. The authors argued that two important elements of constructionist learning—technology literacy and engineering design—have implications for meeting the global need for expertise in the STEM disciplines. To date, the practice of teaching and learning mathematics remains to be dominated by manipulation of symbols with the paper-and-pencil medium. In response, the authors discuss how constructionist learning can play an important role in teaching and learning school mathematics via a transdisciplinary STEM education. Two examples of the authors’ empirical research on constructionist learning in school mathematics classrooms with 3D printing are illustrated. Findings suggest that the 3D printing played an active role in the construction of artifact (physically) and mathematical meaning (cognitively).

24615919.label: Major findings and research outcome
24615919.value: The project’s major findings are four-fold. 1. There exists significant retention effect of 3D Pen instruction for geometry learning. It was observed that students with the aid of 3D Pens demonstrated strong retention of the properties of 3D solids. Namely, the results from the ANCOVA suggest that the retention effect was significant with 3D Pens. Moreover, the project has established evidence that the digital instructions produced strong but relatively temporary geometry learning outcomes, while 3D Pen instructions as a form of embodied learning can help solidify that knowledge. 2. Students’ cognition in the dimension of measure, shape and space benefitted from constructionist and inquiry-based learning with 3D Printing technology. As revealed in the students’ discourse (verbal and gestural), 3D Printing Pens played an active role in the students’ construction of artifact (physically) and mathematical meaning (cognitively). Specifically, constructions with 3D Pens supported students’ composition of 3D solids by their 0D, 1D, and 2D parts, as well as improved students’ visualization of the relationships of these parts in embodied ways. Finally, constructions with 3D Pens gave rise to gestures conducive to learning the properties of 3D solids. 3. Teachers developed expertise in lesson design and technology-rich pedagogy with 3D printing over the course of the study. The teacher participants used the videos collected in this study to anticipate their future teaching in 3D Pen-rich mathematics classrooms. Their discourse was multimodal, as they often re-enacted their imagined drawing process with 3D Pens, either through gesturing or diagramming on paper. Moreover, they attended to students’ nuanced actions of 3D drawing, which ranged from the hand movements with 3D Pens to the size and orientation of the final product. Methodologically, the video episodes captured the dynamic processes of students’ constructionist practices with 3D Pens rather than merely their final products statically–this facilitated the teachers’ reflections about the evolution of students’ mathematical thinking. 4. Development of design-based constructionist learning trajectory and pedagogical principles with 3D Pens The findings characterized constructionist mathematics learning as hands-on and goal-oriented, allowing learners to construct knowledge actively rather than receive information passively; it aligns with transdisciplinary STEM learning because the 3D, tangible, and technologically enhanced nature of artifact constructions makes them applicable to real-world problems and projects, thereby helping to shape the learning experience of STE(A)M. Finally, low-floor, high-ceiling learning opportunities are afforded for students to engage with mathematical ideas and invent new ways to do mathematics without the constraints of paper-and-pencil.

24615919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24615919.value: This project's future extensions include conceptualizing constructionist learning with 3D printing from the perspective of realistic mathematics education, which views learning mathematics as a human activity connected to the reality. As argued by realistic mathematics education, much opportunities should be given to children to reinvent mathematics through hands-on and informal experiences, which is in line with our developed conception of 'learning as making'. Therefore, future research may consider how students make connections and reinvent meanings of 3D-printed (mathematical) object, such as a 3D printed triangle, in real-world contexts, and how their mathematical discourse evolve before and after their creation and interactions with the 3D printed models. These research directions should contribute toward providing a basis for further research into the role of 3D materiality in mathematical cognition. Regarding the results shedding light on what teachers identified as important and noteworthy in a 3D Pen-enabled lesson and how they realized certain pedagogical affordances of the 3D Pens through video-aided reflections, the PI plans to examine the use of videos as a boundary object, serving purposes from the perspectives of both school teachers and researchers for pedagogical and curricular design with new forms of technology, including but not limited to 3D printing.

24615919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24615919.value: In recent years, a body of research has addressed mathematical cognition as situated not only in mental processes but also in physical actions, where providing rich perceptual, tactile, and kinesthetic experiences can greatly support learning mathematical concepts. In this connection, this study has been one of the first attempts to examine the relationship among gestures, embodiment, and mathematical thinking by highlighting the role of 3D printing in mathematics education. The empirical investigations point to the potential changes in thinking, learning, and doing that may result from the use of 3D printing technology, which enable mathematics to be performed in the third dimension and thereby helping to make certain mathematical concepts tangible through touch and moving one's hands. Specifically, by comparing pre- and post-test results, as well as examining students' linguistic expressions and hand movements during classroom-based interventions, this study reveals that 3D printing supported students' investigations, visualizations, and learning about geometric relationships in significant ways. Furthermore, through pedagogical reasoning in the context of video-aided reflections, this study conclude that teachers can learn to be responsive to students' diverse ways of construction with 3D Printing Pens and to facilitate meaningful classroom conversations with students in their classrooms.

24617019.label: Realisation of objectives
24617019.value: Four project objectives have been fully achieved. The 1st objective have been attained by following research activities: 1. Development of the Protocol 1.1 Literature Review and Writing Up the Protocol – The protocol draft was written and proofread in May 2020. 1.2 Panel Review – Three sessions of panel reviews were implemented in June 2020. Feedback and comments from the seven panel members working on the protocol draft were collected and the protocol content was fine-tuned according to their comments. 1.3 Preparation of Instructional Materials and Props – Visual strategies are effective learning tools for people with intellectual disabilities. Therefore, videos, visual cues and props were produced from June to September 2020 for use in the group intervention. 2. Implementation of the Pilot Study 2.1 Training for the Practitioners – Three sessions of training workshops were conducted in early September 2020 by the PI for the practitioners of the pilot study. The aim was to equip the practitioners with the rationale, theoretical knowledge, protocol content and practical skills required for the group intervention. 2.2 Implementation of the Pilot Study – All group intervention sessions were carried out from October 2020 to May 2021. 3. Finalizing the protocol After two practitioners finished the pilot group intervention, my research team finalized the protocol with the feedback gathered from the practitioners and our observation through playing back videos taped during the pilot study. The 2nd to 4th objectives have been attained by the following research activities: 4. Participants Recruitment and Randomisation Exercise 4.1 Five non-governmental organizations (NGOs) serving people with intellectual disabilities were invited to be the collaborators in May 2021. 4.2 The collaborating NGOs recruited the participants and the randomisation exercise was completed in June 2021. In total, 106 participants confirmed to participate in the intervention. 4.3 At the same time, in total 16 practitioners were assigned by the collaborating NGOs who would implement the group intervention. 5. Pre-intervention (T1) Data Collection 5.1 Interviewers were recruited and the research team provided the interviewers training in June 2021. 5.2 The pre-intervention data was collected from July to August 2021. 6. Training for the Practitioners 6.1 Training for the Practitioners – Four sessions of training workshops were conducted in July 2021 by the PI for the practitioners of the intervention. The aim was to equip the practitioners with the rationale, theoretical knowledge, protocol content and practical skills required for the group intervention. 6.2 Review Sessions – The PI and research team conducted 3 review sessions for the practitioners during the intervention from August to October 2021. The aims was to render the supports to the practitioners. 7. Implementation of the Intervention In total, 10 intervention groups and 5 comparison groups were conducted in August to October 2021. 8. Post-intervention (T2) Data Collection The post-intervention data was collected in November 2021. 9. Fidelity Review 9.1 Invitation of and Training for Fidelity Reviewers – 5 experienced social workers who have worked with people with intellectual disability for more than 15 years were invited to be the reviewers and they attended the training in December 2021. 9.2 Implementation of Fidelity Review – The reviewers were assigned to watch back the videos of the group intervention and completed the fidelity assessments in December 2021 to January 2022. 10. Data Analysis Data analysis has conducted since February 2022 till June 2022.

24617019.label: Major findings and research outcome
24617019.value: This study is the first attempt to develop the curriculum of a group-based intervention for Chinese adults with ID. While we recognized that sustainable opportunities are important to persons with ID people with ID for maintaining and enhancing self-determined actions, the intervention group was designed to facilitate participants in exercising various self-determination component elements under the adulthood context. The RCT results show that the 10-session intervention group has positive influence on both the self-determination and personal well-being of persons with ID. Participants’ self-report competencies and feelings of self-determination were enhanced, and their self-perceived personal well-being were increased. The result of process outcome measure also reflected that participants learn different self-determination skills and are able apply them in different situations.

24617019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24617019.value: This study is the first such attempt in the Asia-Pacific region. The curriculum developed is ready to use by NGOs to support the enhancement of SD for people with ID and can be further developed for special schools to adopt in their life-planning education and in adulthood transition services. Further studies are recommended to assess its effectiveness when adopting to other service settings. Since stronger positive outcomes were found for ID participants in the parent-involved SD-PLUS group, we also recommend further research into the effects of such intervention on the parents and parent-child relationships to better understand how to more effectively promote self-determination for people with ID.

24617019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24617019.value: Self-determination (SD) is an intrinsic need in all human beings. Its importance is universal, across different cultures, though the ways of satisfying it may vary. In the past two decades, the construct of SD has developed extensively in the international intellectual disability (ID) field. However, very little research has been done in Chinese societies. Self-determination is regarded as an adult outcome for people with ID. Students with ID in western countries learn SD knowledge and skills through the systematic curriculum in schools. However, the curriculum for adults with ID is still underdeveloped in the West. In Hong Kong, the SD curriculum is rarely available in any setting. This study aimed to develop a culturally-tailored SD enhancement group intervention for adults with ID and to evaluate its effectiveness. The research results show that the curriculum developed has positive impacts on both the self-determination and personal well-being of people with ID. The curriculum is also ready to use by the local NGOs and other Chinese societies.

24621319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
24621319.value: This three-year project aims at writing a monograph on Paul’s economic ethics and teaching concerning various economic relationships. Paul has used many household relationships as a metaphor in his teachings and also addressed some of these relationships or values responsible. However, scholars so far have not systematically analysed the nature of the household and relationships in it among its members from an economic perspective. These ethics and teachings are crucial to our 21st capitalist society, where relationships are mainly driven by economic concerns and values. My goal in this project is to fill this gap by offering a cross-disciplinary approach, which brings conversation with literatures, inscriptions, archaeological findings and biblical text. There are three main sections in this project. The first part of the project will focus on the economic analysis of the existing literary, iconographical, epigraphical, archaeological and legal evidence to reconstruct the institutional functions of the household. According to NIE, a new form of institutions is required, at the beginning of the expansion of an empire, to facilitate its expansion and new form of economic activities. Furthermore, scholars realised that the composition and relationships within a household were extremely complicated and tensional. It did not simply function as a production or a family in modern sense; however, no study has been conducted to investigate the institutional aspect of households. The first part of this involves fill this gap by elucidating the institutional need of the Roman economy and the institutional function of a household. Post clarifying the institutional function of household, the Roman economy establishment and sustenance, in light of the NIE framework, will be investigated – namely the formal and informal institutions. This is a methodological extension of PI’s previously published research in using NIE framework to analyse the formal and informal institutions of Roman slavery and the resulting economic relationships between the master and the slave. I will argue in this part how both formal and informal institutions cooperated in facilitating the household to achieve its institutional function. The final aspect of this project will focus on generating the resulting economic relationships among members of the household from the above findings. Then, the Socio-Rhetorical Interpretation will be used as a platform to explore the Roman economic texture, including the institutional functions, underlying values and resulting economic relationships within the household, and investigate Paul’s ethics and teachings and its implication in our 21st capitalist society. 這研究計劃主要有三個階段，首先透過新制度經濟理論的框架研究從考古發挖出來的碑文、石刻圖像、其他文獻及法律有關文件，從而找出在羅馬經濟中Household 的經濟角色及在household 中不同角色經濟關係。第二，研究會進一步f透過研究其formal and informal institutions 來分析 Household所發揮的經濟功能。最後，會利用社會修辭學釋經理論來研究保羅如何回應相關的經濟關係與背後的價值。這研究盼望把研究成果集結成一專書。

24621319.label: Realisation of objectives
24621319.value: Introduction to the whole project: In this research project, we embarked on a journey to bridge the gap between contemporary economic theory and the ancient world, particularly within the context of New Testament studies. Our primary objective was to demonstrate the relevance of Douglass North's New Institutional Economics (NIE) framework in shedding light on various aspects of the New Testament, while also constructing a practical model for fellow scholars in this field. We initiated this exploration by dissecting how the NIE framework could be aptly applied to New Testament studies, resolving the long-standing debate regarding the applicability of modern economic theories to ancient economies. Our endeavor extended beyond theoretical discourse, substantiating our argument with tangible examples drawn from Roman literature, material culture, laws, and customs. Our research unfolded in a series of chapters, each tackling specific themes and questions relevant to New Testament studies. We meticulously examined the dynamics of wealth, poverty, and ownership as presented in the Gospel of Luke, employing the NIE model to decipher the underlying economic relationships. This examination provided a solid foundation for understanding the ethical teachings of figures like Paul and their implications within the ancient Roman context. Moreover, we delved into the complexities of Roman households, scrutinizing the intricate web of formal and informal institutions governing relationships such as slave and master, father and son, and patron and client. By juxtaposing these relationships with the ideals of love advocated by figures like Paul, we uncovered ethical implications for slave owners and other members of the household. Our research also extended its reach to investigate the broader economic landscape of the Roman Empire. We probed into the historical factors that contributed to the dominance of the elite class in politics and scrutinized the formal and informal institutions driving wealth distribution in the first century. This analysis allowed us to gain insights into how these institutions shaped the belief systems of the wealthy, ultimately shedding new light on the ethical teachings found in the Gospel of Luke. In summary, our research not only exemplifies the application of contemporary economic theory to the ancient world but also highlights the significance of the institutional layer beneath human interactions and biblical texts. By meticulously analyzing formal and informal institutions within the Roman economy, we have paved the way for interdisciplinary dialogue and a deeper understanding of the multifaceted relationship between institutions, belief systems, and human behavior in the ancient world. Realization of Objective based on the main research output the contracted Monograph to be published in 2024: Fulfilment of Objectives 1 to 3: In the first three chapters of the book, it first clarified how Douglass North’s New Institutional Economics framework could be relevant to New Testament studies. Then I construct a model for New Testament scholars to be able to apply it in their research. Then, I make use of a detailed examination of the Roman literature, material culture, and laws, to investigate three main topics related to New Testament studies including the rich-poor and wealth possession in the Gospel of Luke, the material culture of Greek agora and the conflicting Christian-slavery relationship. In this project, I use the model constructed in the first two chapters to investigate and show various relationships within a Roman household in light of the formal and informal institutions related to them, including the slave-master relationship, father-son and patron-client. The outcome is promising as the findings provide a more concrete foundation to compare the loving relationship suggested by Paul. Secondly, the project provides a complete explanation for a long debate concerning whether one can apply contemporary economic theory to ancient economy. This project provides a comprehensive analysis and a concrete model arguing why the NIE is the answer. The project does not only argue from the theological perspective but uses examples to show how the model constructed can be applied to analyse the material culture, literature, laws and cultures. Thirdly, the framework constructed based on the NIE framework provides a platform for interdisciplinary dialogue. The key contribution of the model is that it demonstrated that there is an institutional layer underneath the human interaction and the biblical text. Building on top of North’s contribution to the relationship between institutions and the belief system of individuals, we can develop an institutional layer to explain the relationships among the Roman law (Formal institution), Roman culture and values (Informal institution), people’s related belief system. This institutional layer has to be revealed through a close investigation of the formal and informal institutions of the Roman Economy. Fulfilment of objectives 4 to 7: Concerning the institutional role and function of the Roman household, a chapter has specifically discussed the Roman household and the economic relationships within a household. In this chapter, I applied the NIE model to analyse the formal and informal institutions to generate the economic relationships between slave and master. Then, I compare it with the loving relationship advocated by Paul to derive the ethical implications for slave masters to treat their slaves. The research also extends to investigate the problem of rich, poor and wealthy possessions in the Roman economy. Again, it applies the NIE model to investigate the historical reasons leading to the elite-dominated political situation. Then, the research analyses the formal and informal institutions leading to the wealth distribution in first century and discuss how these institutions will affect the belief system of the rich. The final ethical section will discuss the teaching for the rich in the Gospel of Luke which will shed new light on people living in 21st century.

24621319.label: Major findings and research outcome
24621319.value: 1. Applying NIE Model to Ancient Economy: The study addresses the age-old question of whether economic models, such as NIE, can be applied to ancient economies. The works of scholars like Moses Finley and Peter Temin have fueled this debate. By using North's NIE model, we aim to provide a fresh perspective on this issue, demonstrating the applicability of economic theories to ancient societies. 2. Introducing the Institutional Layer Concept: A significant contribution of this research is the introduction of the "institutional layer" concept. This concept accounts for the intricate relationship between institutions, belief systems, and human behavior in ancient societies. This analytical framework offers new avenues for understanding how institutions influenced the socio-economic aspects of ancient communities. 3. Analyzing Wealth Disparity in the Roman Empire: The study employs the NIE model to analyze the distribution of wealth and possessions in the Roman Empire, providing a contextual backdrop for understanding the ethical teachings found in the Gospel of Luke. This approach enables us to uncover the economic realities that shaped the moral and ethical principles presented in the New Testament. 4. Utilizing NIE to Examine Material Culture: The research demonstrates how the NIE model can be effectively employed to analyze material culture from the ancient world. This approach enhances our ability to extract valuable insights for interpreting New Testament texts. By examining artifacts and material remains, we gain a deeper understanding of the economic and social dynamics of the era. A book chapter was published (2023) based on this research titled The Institutional Function of the Agora and its Relevance to New Testament Studies A New Institutional Economics Approach to the Athenian Agora and the New Testament 5. Contrasting Roman Household Relationships with Paul's Ethical Teachings: Another application of the NIE model is the analysis of Roman household relationships, revealing contradictions with Paul's ethical teachings based on love. This comparative study offers a nuanced perspective on the socio-economic influences that shaped ethical frameworks in the New Testament era. Conclusion: This research showcases the applicability of Douglass North's NIE model to ancient economies and its utility for New Testament scholars. By introducing the "institutional layer" concept and applying it to various aspects of the ancient world, we gain valuable insights into the relationship between institutions, belief systems, and human behavior. This approach enriches our understanding of both the economic realities and ethical teachings of the past, bridging the gap between economic theory and ancient history.

24621319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
24621319.value: 1. Extending the Model to the Entire New Testament: To advance the research, consider extending the New Institutional Economics model to encompass the entire New Testament, including the Book of Revelation and the Letter of James. Begin by conducting a comprehensive literature review to identify relevant passages and themes related to economics and ethics. Collect historical and archaeological data specific to the contexts of these texts. Apply the NIE model to analyze how economic factors, institutional structures, and belief systems intersect in these texts. Compare the findings across different New Testament texts to reveal commonalities and differences in early Christian economic and ethical dimensions. 2. Generating In-Depth Roman Archaeological Insights: To enhance the research's applicability, collaborate with Roman archaeologists and historians to conduct targeted excavations and studies at archaeological sites with economic significance. Integrate the archaeological findings into the NIE framework to refine and validate the model's predictions regarding economic institutions. Publish the combined archaeological and economic analysis to benefit scholars and researchers in understanding the economic complexities of the ancient world. These steps will contribute significantly to our understanding of how economics, institutions, beliefs, and behaviors intersected in ancient societies and offer valuable insights for both New Testament interpretation.

24621319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
24621319.value: Imagine going back in time to ancient times when the Bible was written. Have you ever wondered how economics, money, and beliefs influenced the people of that era? This research helps us understand this. First, it uses a special model to study how ancient economies worked. This is a big deal because some people have argued that modern economic ideas can't be applied to ancient times. But this research shows that we can use a model called "New Institutional Economics" to understand ancient economies, like those in the Bible. The research also introduces a concept called the "institutional layer." Think of it as the way rules, beliefs, and how people behave are all connected. This helps us see how institutions, like rules or traditions, affected how people lived in the past. The study explore things like why some people were rich and others were poor in ancient Rome. It also looks at material things like old objects and buildings to learn more about the past. Finally, it compares what the Bible teaches with how people really lived in those days. Sometimes, there were differences between what the Bible said and how people acted, and this research helps us understand why.

25100219.label: Project Objectives
25100219.value: The proposed research has two primary objectives. The first objective is to understand the effects of priming stimulation timing of the left DLPFC using fNIRS at rest. The time window between priming cTBS and test iTBS will be either 0, 10, or 20 minutes. We hypothesize that 0 minutes will eliminate the effect of the test iTBS, whereas 10 minutes will potentiate it; 20 minutes will have no effect (i.e., result in no difference, relative to sham priming). The second objective is to evaluate the effects of priming stimulation in the context of facial emotion processing in subclinical depression. Previous evidence indicates that DLPFC stimulation modulates affective processing on the neural and behavioral level [15]. We hypothesize that optimal priming stimulation will affect reaction times in an emotion-specific way and will reduce the negative bias observed in subclinical depression [10].

25100219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25100219.value: Priming stimulation is a highly promising tool to boost the beneficial effects of therapeutic repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in psychiatry. The potentiating effects of priming stimulation, however, depend on the time interval between the priming and the test stimulation. Although it is known that too short and too long intervals have no effects, systematic studies that identify the time needed to maximize efficacy have not yet been done. Thus, there is a need for studies to investigate the effects of priming stimulation in order to fully utilize the potential benefits and advantages of this promising new rTMS protocol. Here we propose a research program that will systematically investigate the neuromodulatory process underlying priming stimulation to enhance metaplasticity in the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) – one of the main targets for therapeutic rTMS – in individuals with subclinical depression. The brain is a highly plastic organ and its activity can be influenced using rTMS. At the same time, the brain also has a mechanism – called homeostatic metaplasticity – which counteracts extreme plastic changes. Homeostatic metaplasticity therefore can limit the beneficial effects of brain stimulation interventions. However, priming stimulation protocols that include both a priming and a test stimulation session may utilize homeostatic metaplasticity to increase the beneficial effects of brain stimulation, although the optimal treatment parameters for priming are not known. Moreover, little is known about homeostatic metaplasticity in the DLPFC, an area that is particularly relevant for psychiatric conditions given its role in the top-down control of emotions. Here, we will systematically study metaplasticity using priming theta-burst stimulation (TBS), a potent form of rTMS in the left DLPFC. Changes in blood oxygenation that signal brain activity changes will be assessed using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) at rest and during engagement in an emotion discrimination task (EDT). The findings from this study will (1) elucidate the optimal time interval between priming and test stimulation; (2) elucidate the influence of priming TBS on emotion discrimination and its underlying brain activity in subclinical depression; and (3) validate homeostatic metaplasticity in the left DLPFC. Subclinical depression has serious consequences for the quality of life and is associated with considerable economic costs but adequate treatments are poorly explored. Therefore, by systematically testing priming stimulation and investigating its underlying neural processes, this study will pave the way towards developing adequate antidepressant treatments that will reduce personal suffering, reduce costs and occupational disability. 啟動式刺激是一個非常有前景的方法，它可以增強重複經顱磁刺激（rTMS）在精神病學領域中的治療效果。然而，啟動式刺激的增強作用取決於啟動刺激和實驗刺激之間的時間間隔。雖然已知太短和太長的間隔都會導致啟動刺激沒有啟動的效果，但尚未有系統的研究來調查多長的時間間隔可以最大化啟動刺激的效果。因此，我們需要一個研究來探討啟動刺激的效果，以便充分利用這種有前景的新的重複經顱磁刺激（rTMS）方案的潛在益處和優點。本研究將系統地研究在亞臨床抑鬱症患者中，啟動刺激增強左側背外側前額葉（DLPFC）皮層突觸再可塑性的神經調節過程。這是治療性重複經顱磁刺激的主要作用之一 。 大腦是一種高度可塑的器官, rTMS可以影響其活動。與此同時，大腦也有一種機制 - 稱為穩態化突觸再塑性 – 即抵消極端的塑性變化。因此，穩態化突觸再塑性可以限制腦刺激幹預的有益效果。但是，包括啟動刺激和實驗刺激的啟動式刺激方案可以利用穩態化突觸再塑性來增加腦刺激的有益效果，儘管啟動刺激的最佳治療參數是未知的。此外，人們對DLPFC的穩態化突觸再塑性知之甚少。因為DLPFC在自上而下的情緒控制中發揮作用，所以它與精神疾病特別相關。在這裡，我們將使用啟動式θ-節律刺激（TBS），一種有效的rTMS形式，刺激左側DLPFC來系統地研究突觸再可塑性。我們通過功能性近紅外光譜儀檢測休息期間和情緒識別任務期間（EDT）期間大腦血氧信號的變化，繼而反映大腦活動的變化。本研究的結果將（1）闡明啟動刺激和實驗刺激之間的最佳時間間隔; （2）闡明啟動式TBS對亞臨床抑鬱症患者情緒識別的影響及其潛在的大腦活動; （3）驗證左側DLPFC的穩態化突觸再塑性。 亞臨床抑鬱症對生活質量產生嚴重影響，患者在這上邊花費巨大，但是相關的治療方法的研究卻很少。因此，通過系統地調查啟動刺激的影響並研究其潛在的神經過程，該研究將為開發適當的抗抑鬱治療鋪平道路，這將減少個人痛苦，降低成本和職業殘疾。

25100219.label: Realisation of objectives
25100219.value: The project objectives have been fully achieved. One hundred and sixty subjects were involved in this study. The priming TBS protocol comprised a priming cTBS followed by a subsequent iTBS. The experimental conditions included real or sham cTBS immediately followed by iTBS, real cTBS followed by iTBS after a 10-minute and 20-minute delay. TBS was delivered to the left DLPFC at the intensity of 70% of their individual resting motor threshold. Brain activity of the left DLPFC was assessed using functional near-infrared spectroscopy before and after stimulation. Behavioral effects were evaluated using verbal fluency task (VFT) and emotion recognition accuracy (ERA) task. Pertaining to objective one, results revealed a significant decrease of ∆HbO after all priming stimulation conditions. Notably, this effect was significantly more pronounced and robust in the 10-min interval priming TBS condition compared to other conditions. Pertaining to objective two, there were no differences in VFT performance across the different priming TBS groups, as all groups showed improved performance. No significant differences were found regarding the ERA performance. However, subgroup analysis demonstrated significantly faster responses in the ERA task in subclinical depression compared to controls. In conclusion, our findings suggest that a 10-minute interval between cTBS and iTBS may be the optimal timing to alter the hemodynamic effects of iTBS by leveraging metaplasticity mechanisms. However, these differences do not translate into measurable behavioral differences, at least not for the tasks under investigation. These results highlight the potential of priming TBS protocols to enhance the efficacy of rTMS treatments for depression and other neurological disorders by optimizing stimulation timing and leveraging metaplasticity.

25100219.label: Major findings and research outcome
25100219.value: This ECS project is embedded in a larger research program of the PI focused on therapeutic brain stimulation with TMS. Therefore, the project delivered results beyond the two project objectives stated above. The project provided results on a number of other research questions, as detailed below: For example, in a study published in ‘Frontiers in Psychiatry’ in 2022, we investigated the impact of varying iTBS intensity on the left DLPFC in healthy adults. Twenty participants received iTBS at 50%, 70%, and 100% of their resting motor threshold (RMT) in separate sessions. The results indicated that 70% RMT is the most effective stimulation intensity and was therefore used in the main study. In a study published in ‘Brain Stimulation’ 2021, we explored how stimulating different brain areas with iTBS affects associative learning in 75 healthy participants. We demonstrated that stimulating the DLPFC and the lateral parietal cortex produced distinct effects on brain activity patterns and associative learning. In another study published in ‘Brain Stimulation’ 2022, we investigated the relationship between TBS-induced electric field characteristics and antidepressant effects in patients with treatment-resistant depression. We found that the normal component of the electric field was significantly associated with symptom relief, providing insights into the neurobiological mechanisms underlying TMS efficacy in depression. In another study published in ‘Brain Stimulation’ 2023, we identified several intra-and interindividual moderators of TMS-induced prefrontal excitability. In a series of experiments published in ‘Asian Journal of Psychiatry’ in 2024, we demonstrated biological sex differences in prefrontal oxygenation, that these differences are amplified by the stimulation and that they are modulated by stimulation intensity. Furthermore, we found evidence for TMS effects on elevating serum serotonin levels, a finding published in ‘International Journal of Molecular Sciences’ 2022. In a meta-analysis published in ‘Translational Psychiatry’ 2020, we found that rTMS of the right DLPFC can significantly reduce core symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder. In a meta-analysis published in ‘Therapeutic Advances in Chronic Disease’ 2022, we found that tDCS reduces fatigue and rTMS reduces muscle spasticity in patients with multiple sclerosis. Finally, in a large cross-diagnostic meta-analysis published in ‘The Lancet Psychiatry’ 2023, we provide a novel framework for assessing target or efficacy and interactions of rTMS. The RGC and the project is acknowledged in all named publications.

25100219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25100219.value: Leveraging the insights from this study, future research should prioritize two main areas: customized, state-dependent TMS protocols, and individualized electric field modeling for optimal stimulation. The aim of priming TBS was to modulate brain activity to a lower state before using metaplasticity to enhance subsequent stimulation effects. However, recent studies show that the impact of TMS on brain networks is influenced not just by recent brain state history but also by ongoing oscillatory and cognitive brain states. These states are essential for determining TMS's immediate effects and are directly related to "target engagement" in TMS therapy. The principal investigator's future research will include cognitive tasks during TMS to explore state-dependent effects. Additionally, using EEG-informed or EEG-triggered closed-loop TMS protocols, which stimulate at specific amplitudes or phases of simultaneously recorded EEG oscillations, might also enhance treatment outcomes.

25100219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25100219.value: This study investigated a modern treatment protocol for psychiatric disorders in which magnetic fields are passed through the brain in order to change the activity of distinct brain regions. The type of brain stimulation we used is called priming theta burst stimulation (TBS) and the study looked at how timing affects the brain's response to the application of a continuous TBS (cTBS) followed by intermittent TBS (iTBS) on the left side of the brain. We tested different timings: iTBS immediately, after 10 minutes, or after 20 minutes of cTBS. We measured brain activity using a special brain scan called functional near infrared spectroscopy and tested behaviour using a verbal fluency task. The results showed that waiting 10 minutes between the two types of stimulation worked best for changing brain activity. However, these changes did not lead to noticeable improvements in behavior. This suggests that timing can enhance the effects of priming TBS by making use of the brain's natural ability to adapt, called metaplasticity.

25103719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25103719.value: Regardless of advanced therapeutic techniques are invented, Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM) remains so deadly due to its location and malignancies. Recurrence and therapy resistance are the nightmares for all the GBM patients, given that the surgical resection often obscures by the critical brain tissues. The proposed study initiates from the mechanism of MSI1-AGO2-mediated RNA fate decision under hypoxia through the protein-protein interaction (PPI), to the enhancement of radioresistance in GBM cells. The concepts of this study fit the scope of tumor microenvironment concerning non-cellular constituents and the clues for a novel therapeutic strategy. Musashi-1 (MSI1), an RNA-binding protein, is known for the abundance in neural stem cells and is reported to regulate translation process. MSI1 was found to prevent apoptosis and to create a tumor-friendly environment in many cancers, but the mechanism are still unclear. Our preliminary results indicated that hypoxic GBM expressed condensed MSI1 which interacts with AGO2, a core component of RNA-induced silencing complex (RISC). Knockdown of MSI1 or disengagement of hypoxia both relieved the binding and the release of target genes. Therefore, we hypothesize that the MSI1-AGO2 coordination forms a complex during hypoxia, and selectively regulate targets to gain oncogenic features in GBM. The objectives of this study are: 1) to illustrate the mechanisms of MSI1-AGO2 protein-protein interaction responding to hypoxia. We will investigate the interacting machinery between MSI1 and AGO2 and the subsequent RNA fate decision after binding. Thus, we will determine the stability, half-life and translation activity of those RNAs, to elucidate how MSI1/AGO2 regulate the translation and expression of these binding targets. 2) To determine the actin cytoskeleton homeostasis and the associated DNA damage repair efficiency. We identified cytoskeleton-associated genes are bound in the MSI1-AGO2 complex using next-generation sequencing, and we also found cytoskeleton homeostasis is closely related to radiosensitivity. The causal effect of MSI1 and AGO2 will be dissected in response to ionizing radiation through DNA damage repair, apoptotic, and proliferation events. 3) To develop a novel therapeutic strategy targeting abrogation of MSI1-AGO2 interaction. Decoy peptides will be designed to disrupt the interaction between MSI1 and AGO2. An imaging platform will be built to real-time and quantitatively reflect the events of MSI1 and AGO2 PPI. Overall, the results of this 3-year project will not only provide important information for investigating the MSI1-AGO2-driven tumor progression in GBM but also develop novel strategies for treating malignant and therapeutic resistant tumors. 即使新式的治療技術推陳出新，多形性神經膠質母細胞瘤(GBM)仍舊因其生長位置與惡性程度而十足致命。復發與治療抗性一直是所有GBM病患的夢靨，尤其手術切除仍受到保全腦組織及功能的種種限制。本研究旨在探究缺氧環境誘發MSI1-AGO2機制所介導的RNA調控，進而導致輻射耐受度上升的因果關係。主要概念在於闡述腫瘤微環境變化進而尋找嶄新治療策略。 Musashi-1 (MSI1)是一種富含於神經幹細胞，主導調控轉譯機制的RNA結合蛋白。MSI1在許多癌症中被證實具有防止細胞凋亡以及優化腫瘤生長環境等功能，但實際機制仍然不明。我們的前期研究指出，缺氧的GBM細胞具有高度的MSI1表現，並且與RNA介導基因沉默系統(RISC)中關鍵的AGO2蛋白交互作用。MSI1表現量的抑低或解除缺氧雙雙都能解除前述的基因調控以及蛋白結合。因此，我們假定MSI1-AGO2於缺氧環境下產生的聚合與基因表現調控將主導GBM癌症的惡化。本研究主要目標如下：1) 解開於缺氧環境下MSI1-AGO2蛋白蛋白交互作用的機制。我們將探討MSI1與AGO2結合後，影響已結合之RNA存續命運。針對被結合RNA的穩定度、半衰期以及轉譯活性等進行探討與量化分析。2) 探討細胞骨幹動態平衡與相應的DNA修復效率。先期成果使用RNA測序已經發現MSI1-AGO2複合體會鎖定結合一系列細胞骨幹相關RNA；同時，細胞骨幹在DNA修復功能中扮演舉足輕重的角色。因此我們將探討前述細胞骨幹動態平衡受到MSI1-AGO2影響下，與輻射敏感度之間的關聯。3) 針對MSI1-AGO2交互作用開發新式治療策略。先期成果中已經嘗試設計短肽鏈來阻絕MSI1與AGO2蛋白的交互作用，於此同時我們建立一個影像系統用以定量並定性蛋白交互作用之效用，進一步地，我們在細胞層級驗證潛在的治療效果。 總結來說，此三年期之研究成果可望解釋MSI1-AGO2調控GBM腫瘤生長與惡化的機制，並從而開發一項新的藥物與治療策略，盼能用於緩解GBM在復發與耐藥性等。

25103719.label: Realisation of objectives
25103719.value: Throughout the project period, most of the objectives were properly addressed with sufficient evidence and trials. Despite the hypothesis and objectives being made according to plenty of preliminary data, a few of them resulted in unexpected trends, so alternative measures were considered. Generally, this study aims to decipher the molecular functions of an oncogenic RNA-binding protein, Musashi-1 (MSI1), which was preliminarily identified to regulate various critical tumor-associated genes, such as CCND1, p21, p53, etc. To screen the associated genetic networks, high-throughput next-generation sequencing and the consequent bioinformatics were performed. We successfully identified many cancer-associated regulatory circuits involved, such as cell cycle regulation, DNA double-strand break repair, and cytoskeleton organization. In this connection, we started our study by treating different types of stresses, including hypoxia, radiation, chemotherapy, and reactive oxygen species, to unravel the potential underlying mechanisms that eventually lead to therapeutic resistance of the cancers. Given the known protein-protein interaction (PPI) between MSI1 and AGO2, we questioned whether this PPI is related to the oncogenic features. We then introduced decoy peptides and RNA pull-down assay to see if there were any unknown modifications on MSI1. Surprisingly, we identified a novel phosphorylation site on Serine-347 via a frame-shifting site mutation assay. In the absence of S347 phosphorylation, the oncogenic effects, as well as the aforementioned pathways found in Bioinformatics studies, were affirmed. We conducted LC-MS/MS and Phos-Tag to carefully validate the novel phosphorylation site on serine-347, followed by a series of point mutations to mimic the active and inactive format of MSI1. We then tested the PPI between MSI1 and AGO2 using different strategies. We used a co-IP pull-down assay to confirm the PPI between MSI1 and AGO2, and it turned out that there was no significant change in the interaction despite the serine-347 being within one of the proposed binding motifs between MSI1 and AGO2. The next question is: does MSI1 and AGO2 interaction come from an RNA-mediated manner, considering both proteins bind RNAs for the respective functions? We performed transcriptome sequencing again, comparing the wild-type and loss-of-function mutant MSI1 to identify if there are significantly affected pathways. Intriguingly, we spotted a microRNA family, let-7, impactfully increased in the absence of Serine-347 phosphorylation, again showing the pro-cancerous function of MSI1. It is known that let-7 biogenesis is associated with LIN28, a core member in the RNA interference system. MSI1 was reported to have physical interactions with LIN28 on the intrinsically disordered C-terminus, which coincidentally overlapped with AGO2 binding domains and the newly found phosphorylation site on MSI1. Further, we introduced a decoy peptide to quickly test whether the masking of the MSI1/AGO2 binding motif and the serine-347 site can affect oncogenic phenotypes, such as growth rate, sensitivity to treatments, cell cycle, and cytoskeletal regulations. Although we found no particular changes in the growth rate and the drug resistance against Carmustine (BCNU), it is well noted that the cell cycle and cytoskeleton were found to be dramatically dysregulated. CDKN1A (p21) was found to be significantly down-regulated, followed by an obvious morphological change in the brain tumor cell lines. With abundant reference, CDKN1A is one of the most cited targets of MSI1, and we also confirmed the physical binding by RNA binding protein-immunoprecipitation (RBP-IP) and quantitative PCR. However, it is surprising that we found no changes in RBP-IP qPCR but a significant change in protein level, suggesting a post-translational modification in response to the phosphorylation level change. To further validate the RNA fate change, we conducted a domain stepping assay to explore the potential binding site shift between different MSI1 phosphorylation statuses. Interestingly, we noticed that the binding site of MSI1 on CDKN1A mRNA has migrated from the distal part of 3’UTR to the proximal side, which we suspected the influence on the RNA fate control despite the RNA binding to CDKN1A remained. To this extent, we have partially addressed the objectives 1-3, 6, and 7. To further address the regulatory mechanism, we looked into the causal effects of MSI1 phosphorylation-associated cell cycle and cytoskeleton controls. Due to the inhibitory role of MSI1 on CDKN1A, it is consistent that the cell cycle was affected when compared to the wild-type and S347A mutant MSI1. Both the restoration of CDKN1A and the knockdown of MSI1 led to a similar outcome of cell cycle distribution assessed by flow cytometry. Given that the let-7 miRNA family was found to be regulated by MSI1 in a potentially LIN28-mediated way, we further investigated the impact of Let-7 in the brain tumor cell morphological changes. With respective let-7 sponges, we identified let-7i, the most affected let-7 family member, is responsible for the cytoskeletal remodeling control. Both MSI1-S347A and let-7 restored GBM cell lines, and we noticed a dramatic decrease in cytoskeletal rigidity and filopodia formation, according to the phalloidin staining. Cells became smaller and were prone to detach from the dish, indicating a significant behavioral change. In summary, we illustrated the oncogenic function of MSI1 via the activation of Serine-347 phosphorylation. The Phospho-MSI1 can decide the fate of bound RNAs, such as CDKN1A, and affect LIN28-associated miRNA biogenesis, such as the Let-7 family. Both effects from MSI1 phosphorylation led to the enhancement of oncogenic functions of brain tumor cells, and this study has successfully addressed objectives 1-6. Lastly, we sought the possibility of using decoy peptide or other surrogates to counteract the phosphorylation of MSI1 on serine-347. By the introduction of decoy peptide with a length of 20 amino acids, we noticed a temporary function of inhibitory effect to MSI1 phosphorylation; however, the inhibition did not last long enough to make any phenotypic changes. The introduction of the MSI1 C-terminus showed promising results, such as that a competing sponge might be a strategy for MSI1 inhibition, but it is not practical to make it happen in clinical situations. Therefore, we screened again using the MSI1 co-IP followed by LC-MS/MS to identify any physical interacting kinase that might be responsible for MSI1 serine-347 phosphorylation. Eventually, we noticed a DNA damage repair protein, DNApkCS, might be highly related. Although we eventually narrowed down our scope to exploring the responsible kinase, we were unable to identify or validate the relationship between a specific kinase targeting the phosphorylation status of MSI1 and the subsequent oncogenic function. Nevertheless, we have indeed provided sufficient supporting data to objectives 1-7, although a few of them were eventually found not a null hypothesis according to our evidence.

25103719.label: Major findings and research outcome
25103719.value: Glioblastoma Multiforme (GBM) is an extremely aggressive type of brain cancer characterized by its resistance to treatments that inhibit cell growth and its tendency to recur. The recurrence of GBM is often associated with increased cell invasion and the ability of the cancer to rebuild itself, a process that involves changes to the cell's internal framework. A key player in GBM's aggressive behavior is Musashi-1 (MSI1), an RNA-binding protein that is overexpressed in various cancers, including GBM. MSI1's role in GBM's resistance to treatment and its recurrence is not fully understood, but it is a critical area of study for developing new treatments. Recent research has shown a strong link between MSI1 and the pathways that control the cell's internal structure and the promotion of cell growth in GBM. In our study, a form of MSI1 that has undergone a chemical change known as phosphorylation at site S347 is associated with the initiation and growth of GBM tumors. This phosphorylation changes the cell's internal structure, making it more likely to form tumors. Our results confirmed that pMSI1(S347) increases the ability of GBM cells to form colonies and tumors. All in all, this research reinforced the oncogenic function of MSI1 in glioblastoma, and provided a potentially feasible therapeutic solution. Despite much research indicating the role of MSI1 in various cancers, little is known about the underlying function of MSI1 regarding molecular control or bound RNA fate decisions. Although multiple reports revealed the consensus sequences of MSI1’s RNA binding function, the fate of the bound mRNAs was unclear. This study unravels the first time that MSI1 may shift its consensus sequence and subsequently change the aftermath of the translation of the mRNA. The discovery of the MSI1 activation switch, the serine-347 phosphorylation site, is also one of the most critical findings in this study. This finding allows the targeting of MSI1 to become a new therapeutic strategy for glioblastoma treatment.

25103719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25103719.value: This study is the first report to reveal the molecular mechanism of MSI1 in regulating the oncogenic functions of Glioblastoma. The novel phosphorylation switch can help search drugs targeting Glioblastoma selectively and provide an additional choice for suffering patients. We have narrowed down the scope of drug searching to kinases that target serine or threonine residues to control protein behaviors chemically. There are many available kinase libraries that can be used for future drug screening; in the meantime, we plan to build an image-based, high-throughput drug screening platform for targeting MSI1. A dual reporter system with MSI1 binding motif tandem repeats will be introduced to magnify the signals from MSI1 inhibitory effects. We believe the identification of new drugs can be essentially meaningful to glioblastoma patients, families, and the entire society.

25103719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25103719.value: A brain tumor is one of the most deadly diseases in the world, and Glioblastoma (GBM) is one of the most aggressive subtypes that usually leads to a pessimistic outcome for the patients. The GBM cells are usually resistant to therapies and difficult to be removed surgically without side effects. Eventually, a better target will always be desired to benefit the suffering cohort. Musashi-1 (MSI1) was reported to be a bad protein that drives many pro-tumoral functions. However, it is almost impossible to silence a protein for therapeutic purposes. This present research discovered a critical switch on MSI1 that can regulate its bad behaviors, also known as the Serine-347 phosphorylation. This finding opens a new gate for drug development and ignites a new hope for patients if a specific agent can turn the switch off. Taken together, we illustrate a new path to treat GBM and highlight the critical regulator that can be a novel therapeutic target to benefit patients.

25202719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25202719.value: 多主元中/高熵合金是一種具有優異力學性能的新型金屬材料，應用前景十分廣闊。近年來，納米結構的中/高熵合金因兼具中/高熵效應和納米組織的優勢，有望獲得獨特的力學和物理性能而備受關注。 納米結構中/高熵合金具有較快的擴散動力學，可以克服粗晶中/高熵合金的動力學限制，而表現出與粗晶中/高熵合金不同的相穩定性。目前，儘管納米結構中/高熵合金的研究已取得長足發展，但仍有一些基本科學問題尚未解決，比如納米中/高熵合金的低溫穩定結構是面心立方，還是密排六方？控制納米中/高熵合金中溫相穩定性和晶粒長大的機理是什麼？納米中/高熵合金的變形機制是何種？晶粒尺寸和溫度如何影響其變形行為？針對這些基礎科學問題，本項目擬利用理論計算（熱力學和第一性原理計算）和實驗表徵（原位透射電鏡和三維原子探針）相結合，系統研究溫度和晶粒尺寸對納米結構中/高熵合金的相穩定性、結構轉變、成分演化、力學性能和變形機理的影響，旨在揭示控制納米中/高熵合金的中低溫相穩定性機理，探索溫度和晶粒尺寸對納米中/高熵合金變形機制的影響規律，以期獲得具有優異強塑性的納米結構材料。 本項目的開展將有助於深入理解納米中/高熵合金的中低溫相穩定性和變形機理，為開發具有良好穩定性和優異力學性能的新型中/高熵合金提供科學依據。

25202719.label: Realisation of objectives
25202719.value: (1) Objective 1: the mechanisms controlling phase stability and mechanical behavior of fcc-base M/HEAs at low temperatures were investigated through a combination of first-principles calculations and experimental techniques. The Gibbs free energies of the Co‒Cr‒Ni MEAs were calculated within the adiabatic approximation. The calculation results show that the energy difference between the hcp and fcc structures of the equiatomic or near-equiatomic CoCrNi alloys is negative, indicating that the hcp structure is more stable than the fcc structure at 0 K. Moreover, increasing the Ni concentration enhances the stability of the fcc structure, whereas increasing the Co concentration contributes to the phase stability of the hcp structure. The effects of alloying additions on the phase stability of fcc-base Co‒Cr‒Ni‒X (X = Al, Ti, Mo, and W) M/HEAs were also evaluated using first-principles calculations. It was found that Al, Ti and W act as fcc stabilizers, while Mo acts as an hcp stabilizer. To understand the deformation behaviors of the Co‒Cr‒Ni‒X M/HEAs, intrinsic stacking fault energy (ISFE) and unstable stacking fault energy (USFE) were calculated, and the ratio of the ISFE to slip energy barrier at low temperatures were evaluated. It was found that Mo enhances the formation of stacking faults, whereas Al favors the occurrence of both dislocation slip and stacking faults. In addition, this project studied the mechanical properties and deformation behavior of ordered fcc alloys. It was found that the elastic moduli and ideal shear strength increase with increasing average electron density. The electron localization function analysis reveals that the Co–X bonds have a strong covalent character, which plays an important role in the strengthening of the alloys. Regarding the deformation behavior, we found that the ratio of superlattice intrinsic stacking fault to antiphase boundary energy decreases with increasing atomic number of alloying elements, which tends to change the deformation mode from the antiphase boundary-favored to superlattice intrinsic stacking fault-favored ones. In addition to the theoretical calculations, the phase relationship and deformation behavior of the Co–Cr–Ni and Fe–Cr–Ni M/HEAs at different temperatures were experimentally evaluated. A series of Co–Cr–Ni alloys were fabricated by arc-melting and sever plastic deformation. High densities of dislocations and grain boundaries were introduced, which enhance the diffusion kinetics of the alloys at low temperatures. The annealing treatments were performed at 400 and 500 °C. It was found that the phase structure can be fcc, fcc + hcp, or fcc + bcc, depending on the alloy composition. Specifically, the equiatomic CoCrNi alloy exhibits a single phase fcc structure. Co, Cr, and Ni enhance the stability of the hcp, bcc, and fcc structures, respectively. The volume fractions of hcp and bcc phases increase with increased annealing time and temperature. At 400 °C, the type of phases does not show significant changes, but the volume fractions of hcp and bcc phases decrease. Therefore, the phase transformation is diffusional and time- and temperature-dependent. For the equiatomic Fe–Cr–Ni M/HEAs, a single fcc phase can be observed at both 293 and 15 K. Upon plastic deformation, dislocation movement and multiplication are the dominant hardening mechanism at both temperatures, whereas twinning and phase transformation are not prevalent, which is likely due to the high stacking fault energy of the Fe–Cr–Ni M/HEAs. (2) Objective 2: the thermal stability of fcc-base M/HEAs against phase decomposition and grain growth at intermediate temperatures were studied by various experimental techniques, including TEM, APT, EBSD, SEM, and XRD. A series of Co–Cr–Ni-based MEAs and Co–Cr–Ni–Fe-based HEAs were fabricated, and their thermal stability at 600–900 °C were critically evaluated. The equiatomic CoCrNi and CoNiCrFe alloy exhibit an fcc single phase solid solution in this temperature range. A small amount of Al and Ti results in a notable phase decomposition into ordered L12 and disordered fcc nanostructures. The L12 nanoprecipitates are formed through two competitive modes, i.e., discontinuous precipitation at grain boundaries and continuous precipitation in grain interiors. At intermediate temperatures, both continuous and discontinuous precipitation occur simultaneously and compete. Grain refinement was found to promote the discontinuous precipitation reaction by providing more nucleation sites and faster diffusion paths. The effect of pre-strain on the phase decomposition of fcc-base M/HEAs is a complex phenomenon depending on the amount of pre-strain. At low pre-strains, the plastic deformation increases the dislocation density without significantly affecting the grain structure, which accelerates the continuous precipitation reaction by promoting the nucleation and growth. At high pre-strains, the server plastic deformation induces the formation of a high density of deformation bands and sub-grains, the boundaries of which provide preferred nucleation sites for the discontinuous precipitation reaction. In addition, the high stored energy induced by the cold deformation enhances the grain boundary migration, which promotes the growth of discontinuous precipitation and concurrent recrystallization. With this understanding, this project proposed a strategy to control the phase decomposition and precipitation of M/HEAs. We found that an appropriate amount of Nb additions can induce grain boundary segregation, which substantially inhibits the grain boundary precipitation and migration due to the reduction of grain boundary energy and solute drag effect, thereby suppressing the discontinuous precipitation at grain boundaries. The phase decomposition of nanostructured fcc-base HEAs was found to be sensitive to alloy composition and temperature. Nanostructured HEAs with coherent nano-lamellar architectures were developed through sever plastic deformation and subsequent annealing at 600 °C, which led to the formation of nano-lamellar structures within ultrafine grains. APT reveals that Co, Cr, and Fe partition to the fcc nano-lamellae, whereas Ni, Al, and Ti partition to the L12 nano-lamellae. Using HR-TEM, we observed a coherent interface with continuous crystal lattices, where the crystal lattice of the ordered L12 phase is very close to that of the disordered fcc phase, which effectively stabilizes the coherent nano-lamellar structure without significant heterogeneous coarsening. The new HEAs exhibits a combination of over 2 GPa yield strength and 16% uniform tensile ductility. The ultrahigh strength originates mainly from the lamellar boundary strengthening, whereas the large ductility correlates to a progressive work-hardening mechanism regulated by the unique nano-lamellar architecture. The coherent lamellar boundaries facilitate the dislocation transmission, which eliminates the stress concentrations at the boundaries. Meanwhile, deformation-induced hierarchical stacking-fault networks and associated high-density Lomer-Cottrell locks enhance the work hardening response, leading to unusually large tensile ductilities. Furthermore, we found that the high-entropy effect in multicomponent nanocrystalline composites significantly reduces the Gibbs free energy and promotes the formation of an amorphous structure and compositional inter-diffusion at the interface. The contribution of entropy effect to the reduction of the energy for forming nanocrystalline multicomponent composites is more than three times that of binary systems.

25202719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25202719.value: Understanding of phase stability and deformation mechanisms of nanostructured M/HEAs is crucial for the design of novel alloys with superior structural stability and mechanical properties. This project focuses on the understanding of the mechanisms controlling phase stability and thermal stability of M/HEAs at low and intermediate temperatures. Future work can be placed on the understanding of deformation mechanisms of M/HEAs at low and intermediate temperatures. First, the phase stability of M/HEAs at low temperatures is sensitive to the stacking fault energy of the alloys, which can affect the generation of various types of crystalline defects during deformation, such as stacking faults, deformation twins, and dislocations. The precise manipulation of multiple deformation mechanisms may lead to the development of advanced alloys for cryogenic applications. Second, mechanical properties and deformation behavior of M/HEAs at intermediate temperatures are highly dependent on the type, morphology, size, and volume fraction of second phases, which in turn are related to their thermal stability against phase decomposition and grain growth. Therefore, it is proposed to further study the mechanism of the effect of the type, morphology, size, and volume fraction of second phases on mechanical properties and deformation behavior of M/HEAs at intermediate temperatures.

25202719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25202719.value: Medium- and high-entropy alloys (M/HEAs), also referred to as multi-principal element alloys, have emerged as a new type of metallic materials that show great potential for engineering applications because of their excellent mechanical properties. However, it is a scientific puzzle whether an fcc or hcp phase is the stable structure for fcc-base M/HEAs at low temperatures, and their intermediate-temperature stability against phase decomposition and grain growth is complicated and not well understood. This project systematically studied the phase stability of nanostructured fcc-base M/HEAs at low temperatures and their thermal stability against phase decomposition and grain growth at intermediate temperatures through a combination of theoretical and experimental investigations. Specifically, the effects of alloy composition, grain size, temperature, and pre-strain on the microstructure and stability of M/HEAs were clarified, and new nanostructured HEAs with a combination of over 2 GPa yield strength and 16% uniform tensile ductility were developed. The findings not only shed light on the fundamental understanding of phase stability of fcc-base M/HEAs but also provide useful guidelines for the design of advanced M/HEAs with superior mechanical properties for technological applications.
