25202919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25202919.value: As an energy and cost efficient strategy, passive capillary flow in fibrous porous materials has been used for liquid delivery in many applications including functional clothing, evaporative cooling devices, solar steam generators, microfluidic chips, and water-oil separators. However, the advancement of these applications has been hindered by insufficient liquid transport and lack of direction control of capillary flow. Regulating the speed and direction of such capillary flow is incontrovertibly significant but is also a great challenge, considering the intrinsic limitations that the fluid movement slows as more liquid is driven into a fibrous system and the fluid flow tends to be bidirectional or radial without any preferred direction. With this motivation, a unified mechanistic framework will be developed to facilitate fast and tunable liquid transport in fibrous structures without external pressures. Fundamental investigations will be carried out to quantitatively correlate the transport properties with the microstructures of fibrous materials, incorporating the significant effect of evaporation loss. Furthermore, this model-driven framework will retrofit capillary flow behaviors in fibrous media, based on the optimized heterogeneity of localized microstructures for adaptive interplay between capillary driving pressure and resistant pressures along the flow direction, introducing unusual features: (1) fast and programmably, the capillary flow will be formulated at high but controllable speeds with consideration of evaporation loss; (2) unidirectionally, the fluid will be regulated to flow in the preferred direction and will be blocked from the opposite direction. Experiments will be implemented to corroborate the model development and to validate the proposed framework. Preliminary results have shown that flow speed can be enhanced by 30% in a simplified dual-layer fibrous system with different pore sizes, and unidirectional liquid transport can be facilitated in a water-friendly fluid-diode fabric with asymmetric pores, providing an important basis and startup for this project. From fundamental research to application-oriented implementation, the success of this project will inspire an innovative liquid management framework beyond conventional properties and, most importantly, will advance understanding of interfacial transport phenomena in porous media. Furthermore, the framework will serve as a powerful guide for engineering fluid-regulation fibrous structures with many high-performance applications. To demonstrate the potential applications, a prototype of clothing fabric will be developed that prompts rapid and unidirectional transfer of excessive sweat from the skin side to the fabric’s outer surface for evaporation, keeping the skin dry and promoting comfortable well-being, while preventing undesired penetration of external liquids such as rain. 基於毛細作用且快速可控的液體輸運纖維結構可廣泛應用於功能服裝，蒸發冷卻，太陽能蒸汽發生，微流控和油水分離等領域。然而，有效控制和調節在具有複雜結構的纖維多孔材料中，無外加動力驅動的毛細流動是一項重大挑戰。本項目將研究和表徵多種纖維結構的毛細流動規律，在此基礎上對纖維系統局部微結構非均質優化，探索液體輸運過程速度和方向的有效調控。本項目將建立一個基於纖維結構的新型液體管理輸運框架，促進多孔材料液體流動規律的發展，並為眾多亟需液體流動調控的應用提供理論指導和優化方案。

25202919.label: Realisation of objectives
25202919.value: 1. Develop and optimize fibrous structures for fast, controllable liquid transport properties. In contrast to existing passive fluid transport that tends to be slow and poorly regulated, the liquid transport in the optimized fibrous systems will exhibit the greatest speed and controlled flow rates while taking into account evaporation loss. Achieving fast and controllable capillary flow in fibrous structures is highly desired for various applications, including functional clothing, evaporative cooling devices, solar steam generators, microfluidic chips, and water-oil separators. Nevertheless, passively controlling and regulating liquid transport in fibrous structures presents considerable challenges. In response to these challenges, we investigated mechanistic models to comprehensively and accurately characterize the capillary flow process in fibrous structures, taking into account the significant effect of evaporation loss. Furthermore, we optimize these fibrous structures, which are heterogeneously engineered, to achieve maximum speed and controllable flow rates. The flow process have been characterized with consideration of the balance between the driving capillary pressure and the resistant pressures. The viscous pressure within a fibrous medium correlates proportionally with the height of the occupied fluid, h. This pressure also varies with the fluid velocity (dh/dt), fiber radius r, porosity ε, and the fluid viscosity coefficient, μ. In the procedure of in-plane capillary flow, the impact of evaporation loss will be particularly addressed as it becomes increasingly influential over a longer duration. Upholding the law of conservation of mass, the flow rate at the distance, l, is calculated as the sum of the flow rate at the distance, h, and the evaporation loss occurring on the surface between l and h. An optimum pore radius, R, can be determined that would give a minimum flow time or the maximum speed, under constraints of global volume and length. Furthermore, when liquid advance ceases (dh/dt=0), the maximum evaporation area will be determined by reverse-calculating the microstructures with minimized thickness for lower thermal resistance. We have developed theoretical models that factor in significant parameters, including fiber radius, porosity, evaporation coefficient, and contact angles. Through this modeling and optimization, we have identified the optimal structures required to achieve the fastest and most regulated flows. The research studies are going smoothly and consistent with the original plan. 2. Investigate new design strategies that facilitate unidirectional, diode-like liquid transport in heterogeneously structured hydrophilic fibrous structures, overcoming the existing weakness of multi-directional capillary spreading that has limited the performance and functionality of fibrous materials. Humans naturally sweat as a method for cooling down and dissipating heat in a variety of indoor and outdoor settings. This is achieved as the process of liquid sweat evaporation absorbs body heat, thus reducing skin temperature. However, once sweat production is excessive or when the wearer becomes drenched due to external liquids such as rain, even the most effective moisture-wicking fabrics can become soaked and saturated. This results in a fabric that is unbreathable, heavy, clingy, and drastically reduces wearer comfort and performance. To address this, we've developed an innovative moisture management fabric that actively transfers liquid, encompassing excess sweat from the skin, towards the fabric's outer surface. Meanwhile, it blocks external liquids. We have accomplished unidirectional liquid transport by creating a heterogeneously structured fabric that enables programmable Laplace pressure. This fabric with regulated liquid movement offers broad potential for various applications, including sportswear, worker uniforms, casual wear, protective clothing, firefighter apparel, and military clothing. Moreover, it supports building energy conservation by ensuring moisture and thermal comfort while adapting to an expanded temperature range of the air-conditioning system. Specifically, we have quantified the effects of local contact angles (θ) and water path angle (α) on liquid movement as represented by the advancement angle (A). The wall angle (α) demonstrates the changes in the flow path between fibers, with negative values for narrowing and positive for expanding. The advancement angle (A) is derived as (90°-θ-α), with negative values for continuous liquid advance and positive for reverse flow. Guided by this model, we have developed a fabric that enables directional liquid transport. It's significant to note that the proposed model is effective for both hydrophilic and hydrophobic materials. Although our focus is on hydrophilic fabrics, we have proposed models for fibrous layers with gradient wettability, taking into consideration variables like contact angle, fiber size, and inter-fiber distance. 3. Investigate the fundamental mechanisms of capillary-driven liquid transport in realistic fibrous porous structures. Elucidate the dependence of fluid speed and direction on geometric parameters. The mechanisms have been investigated in realization of Objectives 1 and 2. 4. Validate the proposed theoretical framework. Building on our theoretical model, we have successfully developed hydrophilic fabrics utilizing knitting methods and chemical treatment. We have observed asymmetric liquid transport from different flow directions, which can be attributed to the heterogeneously designed yarns with a gradient in pore size and the corresponding Laplace pressures. We have also explored various fabrication techniques, such as laminating and weaving, in order to develop fibrous structures with the desired heterogeneous properties.

25202919.label: Major findings and research outcome
25202919.value: Major findings: Motivated by the need to facilitate fast and tunable liquid transport in fibrous structures without external pressures, we have developed a unified mechanistic framework. We have carried out fundamental investigations to quantitatively correlate the transport properties with the microstructures of fibrous materials, factoring in the significant effect of evaporation loss. This model-driven framework has been successful in retrofitting capillary flow behaviors in fibrous media. To optimize heterogeneity of localized microstructures for adaptive interplay between capillary driving pressure and resistive pressures along the flow direction, we introduced two unusual features: (1) the fast and programmable capillary flow which formulated high yet controllable speeds, considering the evaporation loss; (2) the unidirectional fluid flow that was regulated to move in the preferred direction and was blocked from the opposite direction. To confirm the model development and to validate the proposed framework, we carried out extensive experimentation. We were also successful in facilitating unidirectional liquid transport in a fabric diode. The research outcome is summarized as follows: 1. A comprehensive review of tunable liquid transport in fibrous structures and discussion of the fundamental mechanisms of capillary-driven liquid transport in realistic fibrous porous structures: No 6 2. A review of thermal management fibrous systems that includes the critical effect of optimized liquid transport on wear and thermal comfort: No 7 3. Modeling and optimization of fibrous structures for fast, controllable liquid transport properties, and investigation of the fundamental mechanisms of capillary-driven liquid transport in realistic fibrous porous structures.: No 7 4. Development of directional liquid transport in heterogeneously structured hydrophilic fibrous structures based on knitting method, and validation of the theoretical framework: No 4 and Patents Awarded 5. Development of directional liquid transport in heterogeneously structured hydrophilic fibrous structures based on chemical treatment, and validation of the theoretical framework: No 1, No 2, Recognized International Conference, Students Trained, and Patents Awarded 6. Asymmetric vapor transport for enhanced evaporation and drying based on the developed Janus fibrous structures: No 3.

25202919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25202919.value: The ongoing research aimed at enhancing the capillary flow of liquids through fibrous materials shows immense potential for further development. This technology holds promise in a wide range of applications from clothing fabrics and cooling devices to water filters. Specifically, it could lead to substantial improvements in sportswear design by providing more efficient sweat management solutions, thereby increasing wear and thermal comfort. Moreover, the technology could be further explored in extended sectors like liquid-based energy conversion systems, where optimal cooling and heat management are essential. The next steps for the project are: 1. Further Optimization: There will be ongoing refinement of the developed technology to ensure efficient, rapid, and directed fluid flow within various practical fibrous materials such as complex functional knitted and woven fabrics. 2. Testing for Commercial Implementation: Once the technology has been optimized and diversified, it will be tested in practical, real-world commercial product applications. 3. Comprehensive Modeling: The research will also place emphasis on considering other main modes of heat and mass transfer such as thermal convection, conduction, and radiation in real-world applications.

25202919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25202919.value: This project focuses on enhancing the flow of liquids through fibrous materials utilizing passive capillary action. Such materials have wide-ranging applications, which include clothing fabrics, cooling devices, and water filters. Current technologies often face challenges controlling the speed and direction of liquid movement, leading to potential inefficiencies. Our objective is to create a fibrous system that facilitates rapid and directed fluid flow within these materials. Implementing this technology could significantly improve various products such as sportswear by ensuring efficient transfer of sweat away from the skin, contributing to wear and thermal comfort. Additionally, it could optimize the functioning of numerous cooling devices by controlling the distribution and movement of liquids. The implications of this novel technology extend beyond enhancing our understanding of liquid movement through porous structures.

25203419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25203419.value: 共享經濟是一種全球範式的轉變，其通過新的形式提供資源使用，如Airbnb，Uber和Yunmanman（中國的頂級優步卡車），逐漸對生活的方方面面產生著重要的影響。共享提高了資源利用效率，使得城市居民和環境受益。有關共享的優化和度量方法，已經開發出來一系列新的指標。其中用戶滿意度很大程度上影響人們是否願意分享。然而，在大多數現有的共享研究中，用戶滿意度被過度簡化（甚至在某種程度上被忽略），這可能導致用戶不願意分享和分享效率低下。作為城市移動性的一部分，像人類出行和駕車類似，貨運是城市交通不可或缺的一部分，有助於提高城市生活質量。貨運共享允許人們在卡車中共享貨物運輸空間以提高運輸效率，但在用戶滿意度和分享意願方面與乘客的乘車共享可能會有所不同。隨著共享經濟的快速發展，迫切需要開發一套分析解決方案，以便更好地了解影響貨運共享的因素。 該項目的主要目標是開發基於用戶滿意度的貨運共享模型，使用眾包大數據和機器學習來衡量和優化貨運共享。該項目將利用GoGoVan提供的超過一千萬份貨運訂單數據。GoGoVan是香港最大的優步貨運公司，擁有超過20, 000輛註冊車輛，占據80％的市場份額。當用戶通過設備在發出貨運交付訂單，司機通過車輛上的GoGoVan位置感知設備接受系統派發的訂單時，貨運數據的信息被眾包並存儲，例如從（原點）運送到哪裏（目的地）（OD），運送的時間，價格和車輛的信息等。訂單OD之間的車輛軌跡被記錄為數據庫中的一系列連續GPS點。 除了這些時空數據之外，用戶對貨運共享的偏好將通過態度調查獲得，該態度調查將與貨運大數據相結合以模擬用戶滿意度並使用機器學習優化貨運共享。該項目旨在實現以下三個目標：a）提出基於用戶滿意度的貨運共享識別模型; b）開發基於深度學習的訂單調度優化模型; c）評估貨運共享的成本效益，以改善運費共享服務。這項研究的結果將為貨運分享提供新的見解，並對相關領域有用，例如城市規劃和政策。世衛組織（2015年）的預測表明，到2050年，世界人口的70％將實現城市化。因此，該項目將在世界範圍內產生有意義的影響。

25203419.label: Realisation of objectives
25203419.value: The project planned to achieve three objectives, including (1) proposing a user satisfaction-based freight-sharing identification model; (2) developing a deep learning-based order dispatch optimization model; and (3) evaluating the cost-efficiency of freight sharing. In the original plan, these three objectives were scheduled to be achieved one by one in a time order, i.e., they were named as stage one, stage two, and stage three. In the first stage, we established a virtual database that is linked to the GoGoX Company. This database is designed to extract relevant data from the company’s operations. We utilized this extracted data to construct data models that allow us to perform in-depth analysis. This process involved data cleaning, transformation, and integration to ensure the accuracy of our data in the experiment. In addition, we employed an open-source map-matching algorithm to develop a map service. This service visualizes GoGoX orders, providing a clear and comprehensive view of the company’s order distribution. This visualization tool allows us to gain insights into various aspects of GoGoX’s operations, such as hotspot regions for orders and peak order times. In the second stage, we delved into a comprehensive analysis of various algorithms to investigate mobility patterns. These algorithms were meticulously examined and tested to ensure their effectiveness in identifying and predicting mobility patterns. The algorithms analyzed encompass a wide range of techniques, from traditional statistical methods to advanced network analysis. They were used to process and analyze the large-scale trajectory data, revealing valuable insights into the mobility patterns within urban environments. This includes understanding peak travel times, popular routes, and common destinations, among other aspects. The findings from these works are of significant value. They not only provide a deeper understanding of urban mobility patterns but also contribute substantially to the design of freight-sharing methods. By understanding these mobility patterns, we can optimize the allocation of resources, improve route planning, and enhance the efficiency of freight-sharing operations. Furthermore, these insights can also inform the development of sustainable urban planning strategies and contribute to the reduction of carbon emissions by optimizing freight routes. In the context of urban mobility, this could lead to more efficient transportation systems, reduced traffic congestion, and improved air quality. We believe that our work will have a significant impact on the future of urban mobility and freight sharing. For the third stage, we have planned to conduct the investigation using a questionnaire for user satisfaction and preference, however, the epidemic lasted far longer than we expected, especially in 2022, the second half of the project. Therefore, we have no conditions to complete these face-to-face investigations. Besides, influenced by the epidemic and unstable human travel behaviors, the planned investigation is not typical to reveal the people’s freight perceptions in a normal period, even if the questionnaire had been implemented. Alternatively, we respectively explored the freight-related urban characters, urban dynamics, and crowdsourcing by multiple modes of transport, which aided as a preparation for future freight studies. Here are some details about these studies: (1) The freight-related urban characters play as a background to support urban freight. However, some situations were neglected by previous researchers, e.g., in a scene of night activities. Based on that, we proposed some new indicators to measure urban diversity and urban vitality, which were highly associated with urban economic operations and freight. (2) Urban is not stationary. Understanding the urban or freight needs a dynamic perspective. It is inevitable to consider the interactions between multiple traffic modes. We studied some traditional traffic tools’ interaction patterns using multi-layer networks to extract the graph clusters, which can potentially be transferred to freight situations in future work. (3) In terms of sharing effectiveness, except for uber-like freight sharing, some novel shared freight functions need to be considered, e.g., crowdsourcing, that is, goods can accompany the movement of people to complete the freight. Those mainstream traffic hubs in human mobility, e.g., metro stations, need extra attention. Through research, we further understand the activities in metro function zones and some related factors, beneficial to crowdsourcing freight arrangement algorithms. Moreover, novel traffic models are another loader for crowdsourcing, e.g., e-scooters. Understanding the characteristics of e-scooter usage varying from different cities can prompt the effectiveness of knowledge transferring from other cities to Hong Kong. We studied the conflict between novel modes and mainstream modes, e.g., excessive competition. The conflict increases public expenditure and brings uncertainty for crowdsourcing planning, which needs to be investigated before the shared freight is implemented.

25203419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25203419.value: This project aimed to create a smart system that makes sharing freight space in trucks as satisfying as possible for the people sending the goods. First, the project came up with a way to figure out how happy people are with sharing deliveries. Then, it used advanced computing capacity (machine learning) to make sure that orders are sent out most efficiently, considering what customers like. It also checked if sharing deliveries saves money. To do this, the team cleaned up and organized big sets of data about past deliveries. They looked closely at the routes trucks take and matched them up with what customers want, like quick delivery or discounts. Then, they tried to ask people what they think about sharing deliveries and use this info to make a “smart map” of shared delivery happiness. Third, they used machine learning to predict which orders drivers are likely to take. This project could make shipping goods cheaper and more efficient for everyone.

Based on the findings of Objectives 1-4, the standard of the fire-safe battery can be improved to guide future research and the development of safer battery technologies using Li-ion and other new chemistries, which can balance safety with power performance.

25205519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25205519.value: Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries offer the advantages of being small, light, of high-energy density and quick charging. They play a significant role in the modern information and energy technologies, and will continue to do so. However, the fire hazard of these high-energy batteries has become an emerging issue in smartphones and electric vehicles. Recently, because of the battery fire risk, Samsung Galaxy Note 7 was banned by most airlines, and was eventually recalled, resulting in an economic loss of more than $10 billion. Most past fire researches focused on batteries under extreme operational conditions, including short-circuits and over-charging, or under external thermal or mechanical impact. Although extreme operational conditions or external impacts do increase the risk of fire, they are not necessary conditions. Many catastrophic fire accidents occurred with non-operational batteries during manufacture, storage, and transportation. For example, in 2010 a UPS Boeing 744 crashed at Dubai because a large quantity of batteries in the cargo caught fire. It was suspected that self-heating of the batteries initiated the fire, but the phenomenon is not well understood. The purpose of this research is to understand the fundamental mechanism of self-heating and ignition in the non-operational Li-ion battery. Through small-scale laboratory experiments, the critical environmental conditions for the self-ignition of the battery can be identified under various states of charge and packing configurations. Through theoretical analysis, experimental results can be scaled up to predict the fire risk of large battery packs in the warehouse and during transportation. Through numerical simulations, the underlying chemical reactions and heat transport processes which are responsible for self-ignition can be quantified. The developed model can be further applied to optimization of the design and management of a fire-safe battery in special applications such as in low-pressure aircraft and microgravity spacecraft. This research will benefit the scientific community and human society in the following respects: (1) Advancing scientific understanding of the self-heating process and the fire risk of high-energy batteries which are not in operation or subject to external impact; (2) Understanding the influence of self-heating on batteries, and improving the long-term battery safety in electronic devices and electric vehicles for billions of global users; (3) Optimizing the safety management for batteries during manufacture, storage, transportation, and disposal, and helping to improve safety standards in the handling of Li-ion batteries; (4) Guiding future research and the development of safer battery technologies which use Li-ion or other new chemistries. 鋰離子電池具有體型小、輕便、高能量密度和快速充放電等優點，是當代資訊和能源技術的重要組成。但是這些高能電池的火災風險也成了智慧手機和電動車的重要安全隱患。如近些年發生在三星Galaxy Note 7智慧手機的電池火災事故，導致其被大多數航空公司禁運，並最終被召回，造成超過100億美元的經濟損失。 大多數電池安全的研究集中在短路和過充等極端工作條件下或由外部機械和熱衝擊導致的火災。雖然極端工作條件或者外部衝擊可以導致電池的火災，但這些因素不是必要條件。事實上，大量的火災發生在非工作中的電池，如在生產、儲存和運輸過程中。2010年UPS的一架波音747運輸機因貨運電池起火在迪拜附近墜毀，引發火災的原因可能是貨艙中大量鋰離子電池的自加熱，具體火災現象依然不明。 本項研究的目標是理解非工作中的鋰離子電池發生自加熱和自燃點火的機理。首先，項目將開展小尺度的實驗研究，確定電池組自燃的特徵環境和電池排列參數。然後，進行理論分析來拓展實驗結果，預測倉庫存儲和運輸過程中大尺度電池組的火災風險。最後，通過數值計算，確定導致電池熱自燃的關鍵化學反應和傳熱過程；進一步優化模型可用于設計更安全的電池組，並降低包括在低壓機艙和微重力太空艙等特殊環境中的電池火災風險。 本項研究將在以下方面促進學術界和社會的發展： 1. 科學揭示非工作中的高能電池的自加熱過程和火災風險； 2. 理解自加熱對電池的影響，並提高數十億使用者的電子設備和電動車電池的長期的安全性； 3. 優化電池在生產、儲存、運輸和廢棄過程中的安全管理，提高鋰離子電池的安全標準； 4. 為未來新型電池的研發提供安全指導。

25205519.label: Realisation of objectives
25205519.value: Realisation of Objective 1: Inspired by classical self-heating ignition tests for conventional hydrocarbon fuels, we conducted lab-scale experiments to investigate the self-heating ignition process of LIBs and determine the critical conditions for “thermal runaway”. Specifically, the pouch and cylindrical LIB piles were tested in classical hot-plate experiments, whereas the cylindrical LIB piles were employed in classical hot-oven experiments. Results indicated that the self-heating ignition process could be divided into three stages: pre-heating, self-heating, and thermal runaway. Thermal runaway of battery pile is accompanied by the release of toxic gas, jet flames, and even explosion. Furthermore, the state of charge (SOC) has an important impact on the self-heating ignition of LIBs. The higher SOC level means an enormous fire risk. Moreover, the critical ambient temperature for self-heating ignition decreased as the cylindrical battery pile size increased in hot-oven tests, which satisfied the classical self-ignition theory. However, the critical boundary temperature for the self-ignition was insensitive to the battery pile size in hot-plate tests, against the expected results. This different phenomenon could be ascribed as the discrete nature of battery cells, swell effect, and chemical impact. The experimental study for pouch LIB piles was accepted as an oral presentation by the 13th International Symposium on Fire Safety Science and published in an international and peer-reviewed journal, Fire Safety Journal [1]. The hot-plate tests result for cylindrical LIB piles was accepted as an oral presentation by the 2nd National Symposium on Thermal Safety Science and Technology. Realisation of Objective 2: Based on the experimental data in hot-oven tests, the classical thermal explosion theory, Frank-Kamenetskii (F-K) theory, has been applied in this project to analyse the characteristics of self-ignition and determine the effective kinetics and thermal properties of battery piles. Then, the lab-scale results were extrapolated to predict the maximum safe ambient temperature for large-scale LIB pile in storage and transport. The theoretical analysis predicts the self-ignition ambient temperature could be lower to 30 ℃ for large battery piles with multiple tightly packed layers, such as those in the shipping container and warehouse. Nevertheless, creating gaps and providing effective cooling between each battery layer could effectively lower the first risk by increasing the self-ignition ambient temperature above 125 ℃. To create a database for different ignition scenarios, future study will investigate the influence of the battery type, insulation between cells (or packing method), and atmospheric pressure on the self-ignition limit. This theoretical extrapolation work has been published in Journal of Energy Storage [2] and Renewable Energy [3]. Realisation of Objective 3: To understand the key thermochemical and electrochemistry for the self-heating ignition of Li-ion batteries, a detailed numerical model of small-scale battery packs has been developed. This model can describe exothermic chemical reactions inside the battery, the heat accumulation within the battery pack, and the cooling mechanism by the environment. The model focuses on the interaction between batteries and between the battery pack and environment, so it is different from most of the models in the literature. It is constructed in commercial code of COMSOL to simulate the hot-oven test of the small-scale battery pack, where each battery includes its major components (e.g., anode, cathode, and electrolyte). The electrochemical kinetic parameters of each component, obtained from the hot-oven experiments and F-K analysis, are input to the model. Detailed heat transfer processes between battery components, between batteries, and between battery and environment will be simulated. This work is in collaboration with Imperial college London and is now under review in Journal of Power Sources. Realisation of Objective 4: During the air transport, most freighters’ cabin has a sub-atmospheric pressure (e.g., 26 kPa at 10,000 cruising altitude). In order to investigate the self-heating ignition and explosion characteristics of LIBs under low pressure, a novel low-pressure experimental platform was established. This platform can provide a well-controlled environment with ambient pressure ranging from 0 kPa to 100 kPa. Therefore, experimental study and numerical simulation will be employed to study the self-heating ignition behaviour of LIBs to provide safer management strategies and standards in air transport. Two papers have been published to quantify the self-ignition and fire hazards of battery pack in low-pressure environment [4,5]. Due to high energy density and long cycle life, LIBs have gradually replaced traditional cadmium-nickel and hydrogen-nickel batteries and are widely used in satellites and other space vehicles. However, the safety of LIBs is of great concern compared to conventional batteries employed for space power sources. In the microgravity spacecraft environment, the LIB fire may perform different fire behaviours due to alteration of air convection, such as a higher concentration of black smoke, faster fire spread, and unconfined jet flame. Therefore, we reviewed the thermal runaway mechanism of LIBs and proposed a research framework to improve the fire safety of LIBs in spacecraft environment. This framework includes the potential ground-based microgravity experiments and extensive numerical simulations on LIB fire, which can provide scientific guidelines to help design the thermal management system of LIBs and the corresponding fire protection strategies for the space station. This work has been published in a Chinese and peer-reviewed journal of Fire Safety Science. Realisation of Objective 5: With the dramatically increased number of EVs, concerns are also rising that relate to the fire risk of LIBs. Therefore, we reviewed the battery fires in LIB EVs, hybrid EVs, and electric buses to provide a qualitative understanding of the fire risk and hazards associated with battery-powered EVs. Based on the test data in the literature, the important thermal-runaway characteristics of the operating LIBs involved in various EV fire scenarios and the corresponding fire hazards were comprehensively analysed and assessed. The empirical correlation between peak heat release rate of EV fires and energy capacity of LIBs crossing different scales was delivered. Moreover, the fire-suppression strategy for EV was discussed and outlooked. The above research findings can advance the understanding of EV fires and attract future research and development on improving the overall safety of future EVs. This work was published in an international and peer-reviewed journal of Fire Technology [6], which has been cited more than 700 times in Google scholar so far. 25205519.label: Major findings and research outcome
25205519.value: The experimental data on the self-heating ignition of non-operational Li-ion batteries reveal the critical conditions (e.g., minimum battery pack volume and ambient temperature) that can trigger the self-ignition process and thermal runaway. This demonstrates the potential fire risk of batteries even when there is no external impact. This research also develops a theoretical model to predict the criteria for the self-ignition of a larger battery pack, such as the environmental temperature, the state of charge, and the size and shape of the battery pack. We have also developed a detailed numerical model for a small-scale battery pack to explain the experimental results, including those ignition tests under a low-pressure environment. Using this model, the key materials and chemical reactions that are responsible for self-heating and the dominant heat transfer mechanism have been identified. This model has the flexibility to predict the self-ignition risk of batteries under complex packing configurations and low-pressure airplane environmental conditions. It can quickly provide vital information to guide the safe management of batteries in storage and transportation. These research outcomes have been continuously published in multiple journals and presented at local and international conferences as milestones to demonstrate the progress of this project. One master’s dissertation and one PhD thesis have also been produced on the proposed project.

25205519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25205519.value: Because of the complex nature of battery fire, many battery parameters (e.g. kinetic and thermophysical parameters) and environmental conditions (e.g. transient temperature and wind) have not been tested in this research to determine their effect on the risk of self-ignition. In future, a random selection and combination of these parameters in their possible ranges will be modelled. If a large number of simulations are conducted, the number of successful self-ignition can be determined. Then, together with the latest AI tools, the probability of self-ignition fire can be estimated. Based on the probability of fire, a safety factor will further be derived with machine learning methods based on the maximum storage size and the required environmental conditions for the safe handling of a large quantity of Li-ion batteries. The proposed modelling tool and fire-risk analysis can also provide vital safety information for untested new batteries with different chemistry and newly designed battery packs. By estimating the risk of fire, reliable thermal-management design and fire-protection systems can be provided. Eventually, better fire regulations can be applied to improve safety in the manufacture of batteries and prevent battery fires in warehouses and transportation.

25205519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25205519.value: This research has advanced our understanding of the self-heating mechanism of Li-ion batteries and the dynamics of initiating a battery fire. The research outcomes reveal why battery fire can be self-ignited during storage and transportation even if the battery is distant from any extreme thermal, electric or mechanical impact. This project also develops experimental and computational tools to quantify the critical self-ignition conditions for batteries. Hong Kong is a leading maritime capital situated near the world’s largest Li-ion battery manufacturing centre, the Pearl River Delta. Millions of Li-ion batteries and electronic devices are exported to or in transit in Hong Kong daily. Therefore, this research directly benefits Hong Kong by improving fire safety standards during transportation and in the storage of batteries. Also, the research outcomes are relevant globally for all major markets of portable electronic devices, electric vehicles and energy storage facilities using Li-ion batteries. A safer battery technology will promote new technologies of information and transportation that rely on batteries, thus offering a great opportunity for researchers, industries, and markets.

25207319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25207319.value: The advance of electric vehicle technology and the rising of sharing economy are reshaping the future mobility. A prominent example is the increasing popularity of electric carsharing services around the world including Hong Kong. Despite the friendly environment towards the development of this new mobility service, many carsharing operators are confronted with vehicle imbalance problem, i.e., the supply of vehicles/parking spots at some stations cannot well match the dynamic customer demand. Relocating vehicles between stations in a real-time fashion is believed to be an inevitable approach to correct the imbalance. Regrettably, in practice the decision-making of carsharing operators for real-time vehicle relocation is often complicated by the uncertainty of customer demand, i.e., some customer orders arrive randomly over time and space, and their information can only be known on a request by request basis. The limited driving range and complicated charging process of electric vehicle cause additional management problems in the carsharing systems. To offer an efficient and robust mobility service, the carsharing operator has to well address the vehicle relocation problem while considering the demand uncertainty and characteristics of electric vehicle. We therefore propose to develop a dynamic algorithmic framework to support the real-time decision-making of carsharing operators in pursuit of cost minimization regarding vehicle relocation and vehicle charging with demand uncertainty. Within the framework, optimization models and customized efficient algorithms will be developed to make sure that the vehicles are properly relocated and charged, and new demand information is promptly responded to. Extensive numerical experiments and case studies will be conducted to evaluate the proposed decision-making tool and to explore the impact of demand uncertainty and other influential factors on the performance of electric carsharing services. Suggestions of guidelines and measures of improvement will be furnished to relevant stakeholders. This study will contribute to both theory and practice, and the achievements will be of tremendous value in promoting the sustainability of transportation and shared mobility. 電動汽車技術的發展和共享經濟的提出正在重塑人們的出行方式，其中以包括香港在內的全球範圍內日益興起的共享電動汽車為代表。儘管共享電動汽車市場前景被一度看好，運營商卻不可避免地面臨服務站點間的需求不對稱問題。例如，在動態需求下，用戶在使用共享汽車的過程中常常面臨“無車可租”和“有車難還”的窘迫。對此多數運營商採用在站點間調配車輛的方法緩解需求不對稱問題。遺憾的是，在實踐運營中，用戶訂單存在時間和空間的不確定性，詳細的訂單信息也只有在用戶下單時候才能獲取，這種需求的動態性和不確定性使得車輛調配員難以有效地進行實時調度。此外，電動汽車有限的續航里程和復雜的充電過程導致給共享電動汽車的運營決策帶來額外挑戰。為了給用戶提供高效且穩定的出行方式，共享汽車運營商在設計車輛調配方案時需充分考慮用戶需求的不確定性和電動汽車有別於傳統燃油汽車的特性。本項目擬針對以上問題為共享電動汽車運營商開發一套動態決策工具，通過構建優化模型並設計高效定制的求解算法獲取實時車輛調度和充電方案，為運營商降低運營成本，提高管理能力和服務水平提供堅實的理論基礎。本項目也將通過大量的數值實驗和案例分析對開發的模型和算法進行評估， 並探索需求的不確定性和其他因素對共享電動汽車服務系統的影響，從而為共享電動汽車運營商的設計和運營提供指導意見。本項目的開展具有深遠的理論研究和實踐應用價值，其實現將極大的促進綠色交通和共享出行的推廣和發展。

25207319.label: Realisation of objectives
25207319.value: Objective 1: Establish a dynamic algorithmic framework based on a rolling time horizon for the real-time decision-making of electric carsharing systems considering demand uncertainty and dynamism Research activities: We have established a rolling time framework with details of the start and stop epoch of each sub-horizon, the computation time limit, the implementation epoch, and the implementation period of the solution to the problem for each sub-horizon for the dynamic decision-making of electric carsharing systems. Specifically, to cope with the demand uncertainty and dynamics, we have developed a dynamic algorithmic framework for the real-time vehicle routing and charging scheduling problem (RT-VR&CS) based on a rolling time horizon. The entire planning horizon was discretized into a sequence of K sub-horizons. The breakpoints might not be evenly spaced in time. The solution to the problem was obtained by successively solving a series of static problems defined over these sub-horizons. At each time point, the static problem defined over the sub-horizon was solved to optimize the vehicle relocation and charging strategy to cover unserved existing orders, with all the information known up to this point of time. Unlike an offline static problem where time constraint was not a major concern, the online environment of the RT-VR&CS problem required a timely response to the change of demand information. Therefore, we imposed the computational time limit for each static problem. By the next time epoch, a solution to the kth S-VR&CS problem had been obtained for implementation. The solution was then implemented over the concerned time interval. We have illustrated the proposed dynamic algorithmic framework, including the start time point and end time point, the computation time limit, the implementation time point, and the implementation period of the solution to the kth static problem for each sub-horizon. Objective 2: Develop optimization models and customized algorithms to determine the incumbent optimal vehicle relocation and charging strategy over each sub-horizon within the dynamic algorithmic framework Research activities: We have developed optimization models and algorithms to determine the incumbent optimal vehicle relocation and charging strategy for each sub-horizon within the dynamic algorithmic framework. Specifically, a concurrent-scheduler-based algorithm has been proposed to solve the optimization models. We showed the flowchart for the action determination at the kth decision epoch under the concurrent-scheduler-based policy. Take the action determination at the kth decision epoch as an example. To determine the activity trajectory implemented by an EV and the trip chain performed by a staff member at the kth decision epoch, we picked the orders one by one in ascending order of their departure time. For a picked order, we first decided which EV should be relocated by which staff member to the pick-up station of the order so that the order could be served. To achieve this, for each combination of an EV and a staff member, we checked its feasibility for serving the order in terms of travel time and electricity consumption and calculated the incremental profit if feasible. An identified feasible combination associated with the highest and positive incremental profit to carsharing operators, namely, v* and f*, would be the final decision for serving the order. Given v* and f*, we first determined the charging scheduling of the EV v* for serving the order. Then we assigned the order to the EV v* and the corresponding relocation task, if necessary, to the staff member f*. Objective 3: Evaluate the performance of the proposed model and method, and derive managerial insights through numerical experiments Research activities: We have developed a test instance generator to randomly create test problems and confirmed the case study for the evaluation of proposed algorithms. These test problems mainly differed in system configuration and customer demand pattern. We have assessed the performance of the proposed algorithm and the benchmark approaches and explored the managerial insights into the operations and management of electric sharing mobility services. Specifically, we built up a transportation network in an Euclidean plane such that the travel distance between any two grid points in the network was the Euclidean distance between them. A pre-specified number of stations were uniformly chosen from the Euclidean plane. The pick-up and drop-off station of each customer order as well as the initial station location of each EV before the planning horizon were randomly generated from the chosen stations. For the comparison between the proposed policy and the benchmark policy, the results showed that the numbers of satisfied orders obtained by the proposed policy were higher than those achieved by the benchmark policy in most instances. Besides, the proposed policy could on average serve as high as 18.1 orders more than the benchmark policy. As for the profitability, all the profits produced by the proposed policy were larger than those obtained by the benchmark policy and the largest relative gap in profit reached 47.5%. Overall, the results demonstrated that the proposed policy outperforms the benchmark policy in solving our problem. Some interesting results and findings were obtained from impact analysis. For example, as the staff number increased while the fleet size was fixed, more relocation operations were performed and accordingly more orders were served, leading to a decreasing number of satisfied orders and a growing profit. It was interesting to find that when fleet size increased under a constant number of staff members, the number of satisfied orders rose, whereas the profit ratio (with respect to the case without considering staff rebalancing) generally declined. This implied that vehicle fleet expansion should be implemented jointly with manpower increase to achieve a higher profit by serving more orders. We could also conclude from these results that staff rebalancing played an important role in improving the service level and profitability, and ignoring it in the decision-making of vehicle relocation could cause the overestimation of service level and profitability.

25207319.label: Major findings and research outcome
25207319.value: The research project aimed to optimize the decision-making process for electric carsharing systems, considering demand uncertainty and dynamism. The project had three main objectives: establishing a dynamic algorithmic framework, developing optimization models and algorithms, and evaluating the performance of the proposed model and method. For the first objective, a dynamic algorithmic framework was developed based on a rolling time horizon. This framework was designed to cope with demand uncertainty and dynamics in electric carsharing systems. The planning horizon was divided into a sequence of sub-horizons, and the solution to the problem was obtained by solving a series of static problems defined over these sub-horizons. A computational time limit was imposed for each static problem to ensure a timely response to changes in demand information. The second objective involved developing optimization models and algorithms to determine the optimal vehicle relocation and charging strategy for each sub-horizon within the dynamic algorithmic framework. A concurrent-scheduler-based algorithm was proposed to solve the optimization models. The action determination at each decision epoch was made based on the feasibility of serving the order in terms of travel time and electricity consumption, and the incremental profit if feasible. The third objective was to evaluate the performance of the proposed model and method and derive managerial insights through numerical experiments. A test instance generator was developed to randomly create test problems for the evaluation of proposed algorithms. The performance of the proposed algorithm was assessed and compared with benchmark approaches. The results showed that the proposed policy outperformed the benchmark policy in most combinations of station, electric vehicle (EV), and staff numbers. The proposed policy also produced larger profits than the benchmark policy, with the largest relative gap in profit reaching 47.5%. The research also revealed that increasing the number of staff members while keeping the fleet size constant could lead to more orders being served and higher profits. Conversely, expanding the fleet size without increasing the number of staff members could lead to a decline in the profit ratio. These findings suggest that decision-making in vehicle relocation should take into account staff rebalancing to avoid overestimating service level and profitability. The outcomes of the project have been published or accepted by influential journals including Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies, IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems, International Journal of Production Research, Transport Policy, and Networks & Spatial Economics.

25207319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25207319.value: The research project has significant potential for further development considering the emerging autonomous vehicle (AV) technology. The current model and method can be extended to incorporate the unique characteristics of AVs in carsharing systems. In an autonomous carsharing system, vehicles can self-relocate, eliminating the need for staff rebalancing. This could significantly improve the efficiency and profitability of the system. However, new challenges may arise, such as the optimal routing of AVs and the coordination between AVs to avoid conflicts. Therefore, the next step in the research could be to develop new optimization models and algorithms for the real-time decision-making of autonomous electric carsharing systems. These models and algorithms should consider not only the demand uncertainty and dynamism but also the autonomous driving capabilities of the vehicles. The performance of the proposed models and algorithms should be evaluated through numerical experiments and real-world applications. This research could contribute to the advancement of autonomous carsharing systems and promote their adoption in the transportation industry.

25207319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25207319.value: This research project focuses on optimizing the operations of electric car-sharing services. We have developed a dynamic algorithm that makes real-time decisions on vehicle allocation and charging, considering fluctuating demand. This system breaks down the planning period into smaller segments, making decisions for each based on current information. We have also formulated models to determine the optimal strategy for vehicle relocation and charging within each time frame. The system decides which shared vehicle should be moved by which staff member to meet a customer's request, considering factors like travel time and electricity consumption. The project's significance lies in its potential to enhance the efficiency and profitability of car-sharing services. The system was tested using simulated scenarios and outperformed other methods, serving more customers and generating more profit. The research also highlighted the importance of staff in improving service quality and profitability. This project holds immense value as it can help car-sharing companies operate more efficiently, serve more customers, and increase profits. Additionally, it contributes to the broader goal of promoting electric vehicles, thereby aiding in reducing carbon emissions.

25209819.label: Project Objectives
25209819.value: To synthesize, functionalize, and characterize a library of nanomaterials (graphene oxide, carbon nanotube, and nano-silver particles) with varied physical and chemical structures/properties (e.g., size, oxygenated functional groups) that are desired for nanocomposite membrane applications. To develop an aerosol-assisted deposition approach to incorporating these functional nanomaterials, in-situ during membrane surface (re-)formation, and to produce mechanically stable nanocomposite membranes with uniform and high surface coverage of nanomaterials. To fundamentally characterize structure and evaluate performance of the as-synthesized nanocomposite membranes for water and wastewater treatment applications, and to reveal the underlying synthesis-structure-performance relationships in a quantitative way, e.g., relationship between nanomaterial functional groups/densities, membrane surface hydrophilicity, and water flux, among other important ones.

25209819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25209819.value: The world is facing a challenge of sustainable water supply in terms of both quantity and quality, driven by growing population, environmental pollution, and accelerated climate change. Efficient yet affordable technologies are needed to create new water sources such as desalinated seawater and reclaimed water from advanced wastewater treatment, in which membrane technologies will play a more important role than ever before. However, current polymeric membranes have important flaws including imperfect selectivity and easy fouling. The adoption of engineered nanomaterials (ENMs) in water treatment membranes has a potential to fundamentally resolve these problems as demonstrated by some recent developments. Nevertheless, current approaches of making nanocomposite membranes (i.e., impregnation or surface coating) resulted in low surface coverage and a lack of precisely controlled distribution/location of nanomaterials. These shortcomings have greatly compromised the benefits of using ENMs in membranes. This proposal is aimed at developing a novel aerosol-assisted (spray-assisted) fabrication approach for synthesizing nanocomposite membranes. Followed by a library of ENMs desired for membrane applications (carbon nanotube, graphene oxide and Ag), this aerosol-assisted fabrication approach will be optimized to achieve high and uniform surface coverage of ENMs. The as-synthesized nanocomposite membranes will be fully characterized with regard to structures/properties and then their performance will be evaluated for water/wastewater treatment applications. They are expected to have similar (if not increased) permeability and selectivity, but with much enhanced anti-fouling properties compared to un-modified membranes. Furthermore, with unprecedented structural information, this project is also aimed at establishing (quantitative) links among synthesis, structure, and performance. Successful outcomes from this project will create a new paradigm of nanocomposite membrane, and gain the required knowledge to support the (re)design of the molecular-scale transport phenomena that underlie future advanced water separation membranes. 可持續供給清潔水資源是當今世界的重大挑戰之一。高效且具有經濟性的技術是創造新水源（如海水化淡和再生水等）的核心。其中，膜分離技術將扮演前所未有的重要角色。然而現有的高分子膜都有一定的技術缺陷如較差選擇性和膜污染等。最新的研究表明在水處理膜中應用功能納米材料可望從根本上解決上述缺陷。本項目旨在利用氣溶膠途徑合成一種新範式的納米複合水處理膜；該種複合膜表面將具有高密度且均勻分佈的功能納米材料，其將在飲用水深度處理和污水回用中得以應用。同時，全新的結構信息將用於構建納米複合膜的“合成-結構-功能”關係，繼而為重新設計水處理膜分子層面的傳輸機制提供知識基礎。

25209819.label: Realisation of objectives
25209819.value: All three research objectives have been achieved. Regarding Objective 1, a library of graphene oxide (GO), carbon nanotube (CNT), and nano-silver (Ag NP) particles have been either synthesized in-house or purchased from commercial outlets. Firstly, we performed a thorough summary of graphene oxide properties and their impacts on the separation functions of graphene oxide membranes. Then, we conducted a thorough investigation into property-aggregation relationships of common carbon nanomaterials (namely, GO and CNT), which are important to their solution processing and aerosol deposition. We employed a meta-analytic approach to synthesize the data from 46 individual studies reporting the critical coagulation concentration (CCC) of GO and CNT. The correlations between CCC and material physicochemical properties (i.e., size, ζ-potential, and surface functionalities) were examined and compared to the theoretical predictions (i.e., Derjaguin-Landau-Verwey-Overbeek (DLVO) theory). Our findings rationalized the inconsistency between experimental observation and theoretical prediction and provided essential insights into the aggregation behavior of nanomaterials in water, which could facilitate their rational design. These fundamental insights laid a foundation for us to design and apply carbon nanomaterials with specific physicochemical properties as nanofillers in polymeric membranes. In relation to Objective 2, the project has first conducted a thorough study of the impacts of nanomaterials as fillers in polymeric ultrafiltration (UF) membranes on their formation and performance. We utilized CNT and GO as two representative nanofiller materials. The results of the solvent-based (blending) approach provided mechanistic insights into the effects of nanofiller on membrane structure and performance, in particular with regard to rejection mechanism(s). In general, the combined effect of increased (surface) pore size (i.e., to decrease rejection), enhanced hydrophilicity (i.e., to increase negatively charged molecules), and varied properties of solutes determines effective interaction(s) between solute and membrane (surface/pores), and thus (the change of) rejection after nanofiller addition. Further, we have prepared and characterized polysulfone (PSF) UF membranes via nonsolvent-induced phase separation (NIPS) which incorporated oxidized fullerenes (fullerols). Fullerol addition, at relatively low loadings (≤1.5 wt%), has a significant impact on the structure, permeability, anti-fouling, and mechanical properties of the resulting membranes. The addition of fullerol works in the same way to influence the membrane formation kinetics and thermodynamics as CNT and GO do. Our project then demonstrated a new approach via (electro)spray-printing to modify or synthesize new types of composite membranes. Our as-developed approach was able to solve a few key technical issues associated with conventional NIPS approaches to incorporating functional nanomaterials, such as low material efficiency, long processing time/tedious processes, and/or no precise control of nanomaterial distribution/location. In this approach, microdroplets containing Ag NPs, PSF, and N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) were uniformly deposited on commercial polyethersulfone (PES) membrane surface. The residual NMP induced fusion bonding of contacted polymers and subsequent integration of the deposited Ag-PSF microbeads. This new approach acts as a technical platform for the synthesis of novel nanocomposite membranes with diverse structures and multiple functions. Further, its scalability using multi-jet electrospray systems sheds light on its potential commercial applications in advancing water treatment and industrial separation membranes. Furthermore, we have developed a single-step spray-assisted NIPS approach that achieves ultra-high loading of carboxylic CNTs (c-CNTs) into the polyvinyl chloride (PVC) membrane surface layer. The incorporation of a high density of functional nanomaterials into the surface layer of UF membranes led to their improved structure and performance. The spray was characterized using advanced techniques (laser Doppler velocimetry (LDV) and laser diffraction particle size analyzer (LDPSA)), which aided in selecting the two solvents used in spray (dimethylformamide (DMF)) and NIPS (TamiSolve® NxG). The utilization of the selected solvents ensured the incorporation of deposited c-CNTs into the surface layer of the cast wet film without causing significant damage. The introduction of c-CNTs in the surface layer overall acted as a barrier for solvent-nonsolvent exchange, which contributed to even higher kinetic hindrance compared to that in conventional NIPS. The as-prepared membrane structure and performance coincided well with the proposed membrane formation mechanisms. As a result of structural incorporation, no c-CNTs leached out from the membranes. Our study highlights the potential application of spray-assisted NIPS in large-scale nanocomposite UF membrane preparation. In addition to the above aerosol-assisted functionalization of the membrane surface, the project has also demonstrated a magnetic field-assisted stabilization approach. A Fe3O4-hybridized GO (GOF) membrane, assembled via vacuum filtration, was shown to be ultra-stabilized in a tuned magnetic field. This simple, scalable method that physically stabilizes functional engineered nanomaterials on a surface opens new opportunities for developing nano-enabled water treatment membranes, among many other applications. In connection to Objective 3, we performed a meta-analysis regarding preparation-structure-performance relationships of nanocomposite membranes. The effects of nanofiller addition on UF membrane performance in a total of 121 papers from the literature were analyzed. Cross-comparison of membrane performance was conducted between different types of nanofiller-enhanced membranes. Key membrane structure parameters were determined by the Spearman analysis. Among all nanofiller modification methods, polymer grafting was likely prefered to further improve filtration performance. Based on these analyses, research gaps and future opportunities were discussed and identified. This study provides timely information to fully exploit the potential of nanomaterials as a unique filler for the improvement of polymeric UF membranes. Lastly, we applied the membranes in advanced wastewater treatment. As a proof-of-concept, we developed a hollow fiber membrane chemical reactor with high and sustainable catalytic reactivity, enabled by novel confinement of the catalysts. The membrane chemical reactor can achieve wide-spectrum decontamination, removing contaminants ranging from large-size nanoplastics to endocrine disrupting molecules, which is beyond the reach of current approaches.

25209819.label: Major findings and research outcome
25209819.value: This project unraveled preparation-structure-performance relationships of nanofiller-incorporated membranes through experimental and meta-analysis studies, and developed two simple yet robust aerosol-assisted membrane surface nanoengineering approaches. This project has performed a thorough summary of graphene oxide properties and their impacts on the separation functions of graphene oxide membranes (Publication 7). Then, this project has conducted a thorough meta-analytical investigation into property-aggregation relationships of common carbon nanomaterials (Publication 2). Results showed the relationships are overall qualitatively consistent with the prediction of the DLVO theory, but with certain size/surface charge threshold limitations. Based on the above understandings, this project has successfully prepared/modified two carbon nanofillers (i.e., graphene oxide (GO) and carboxylic carbon nanotube (c-CNT)) and applied them as nanofillers in polymeric ultrafiltration (UF) membranes (Publication 1). The study revealed that the morphological factor, as a result of nanoparticle properties, is an important factor to consider during membrane preparation (i.e., nonsolvent-induced phase separation (NIPS)). Further, this project has prepared and characterized polysulfone (PSF) UF membranes via NIPS which incorporate oxidized fullerenes (Publication 5). The research results revealed that the addition of fullerol works in the same way to influence the membrane formation kinetics and thermodynamics as CNT and GO do. To localize nanomaterials on the membrane surface, this project has developed a rapid surface nanoengineering approach that combined electrospray and polymeric solvent bonding (Publication 3; Patent ZL202110272172.4). Successful stabilization of Ag NPs via interfacial polymeric bonding occured under the conditions of large material contact area, high material compatibility, and proper temperature (22 °C) and polymer-to-solvent ratio (3-5%). The resultant membrane showed markedly improved catalytic and antimicrobial (anti-biofouling) performance and maintained rejection. The surface nanoengineering approach was further modified to incorporate c-CNTs of ultra-high loadings into the membrane surface layer during spray-assisted NIPS (Publication 8). Membrane formation was influenced by thermodynamic, kinetic, and morphological factors. The as-prepared membrane structure and performance coincided well with the proposed membrane formation mechanisms. Through optimization, membranes with the highest c-CNT loading (11%) were prepared. The project has also demonstrated a magnetic field-stabilization approach, through which a Fe3O4-hybridized GO (GOF) membrane was shown to be ultra-stabilized in a tuned magnetic field (Publication 4). A meta-analysis of data from 121 publications was further conducted to reveal the preparation-structure-performance relationships. The results showed 1D or 2D nanofillers (e.g., CNT, SBA-15, or GO) usually have lower optimum mass loadings than 3D nanofillers (e.g., TiO2, SiO2, and ZnO), and high nanofiller hydrophilicity and concentration of nanofillers into the membrane surface layer improve both membrane separation and antifouling performance. This project has also developed a hollow fiber membrane chemical reactor that can achieve wide-spectrum decontamination (Publication 6).

25209819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25209819.value: (1) The role of nanofiller in UF membrane formation requires further theoretical delineation, and future studies can further identify desired nanofiller properties and verify them via experiments. The relationships between the nanofiller properties (e.g., shape, size, surface functional groups, and material nature) and NIPS need to be quantitatively constructed. Identification of desired nanofiller properties for membrane performance enhancement needs further investigation. More efforts shall also be made to fully utilize the unique functionalities that nanomaterials can bring to the enhancement of filtration and antifouling performance, in addition to the mechanical strength of nanofiller-incorporated membranes. (2) Future work can focus on optimizing the two aerosol-assisted engineering approaches to prepare uniform nanocomposite membranes with diverse structures and enhanced performance in a large scale. One or more ENMs can be incorporated via the addition of relevant ENMs in the spraying/electrospraying solution(s). Both approaches may also be expanded to other polymeric membrane types (e.g., ultrafiltration and nanofiltration) and configurations (e.g., hollow fiber membranes). Both approaches are scalable with the application of multiple spray/electrospray jets. (3) New avenues for applications of novel types of nanocomposite membranes with ultra-high nanomaterial loading shall be explored, for example, photothermal membrane distillation, among others.

25209819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25209819.value: The world is facing a challenge of sustainable water supply in terms of both quantity and quality. Membrane technologies will play an essential role in addressing the ever increasing water challenge. The adoption of engineered nanomaterials (ENMs) in water treatment membranes has a potential to fundamentally address limitations of current polymeric membranes such as low separation efficiency and fouling issues. This project has first synthesized a library of ENMs, including carbon nanotube, graphene oxide, and Ag nanoparticles, and has systematically studied their property-aggregation relationships. Understanding their aggregation and the method to prevent it laid a foundation for their solution processing and aerosol deposition. This project has then revealed the roles of nanomaterials as functional fillers in polymeric filtration membranes, which is a long-standing knowledge gap that has hindered the proper design of ENMs for use in polymeric membranes. Furthermore, this project has developed two innovative aerosol-assisted (spray-assisted) fabrication approaches that enable fast, continuous, and scaled-up manufacturing of advanced nanocomposite ultrafiltration membranes. These membranes have shown increased separation performance, along with enhanced anti-fouling, mechanical and catalytic properties, which underpin their potential widespread applications in various advanced water and wastewater treatment.

25210419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25210419.value: Poor aircraft cabin environments have drawn public attention as air travel gets increasingly popular. Current cabins contain airborne contaminants, and are often not thermally comfortable. To maintain a viable cabin environment, commercial aircraft use a mixing air distribution system which, unfortunately, increases the risk of infection to airborne diseases because of its low ventilation effectiveness. Supplementing the mixing ventilation system, a system of gaspers provides a measure of personalized ventilation control. Normally, one gasper is situated on the ceiling above each passenger, enabling adjustable air supply velocity and direction. The gasper system allows passengers to improve their individual thermal comfort level, but it has a mixed impact on air quality. An innovative personalized displacement ventilation system could be applied to maintain thermal comfort and, importantly, reduce airborne contaminant transport in airliner cabins. However, few if any studies on the performance of the personalized displacement ventilation system with the concurrent operation of gaspers have been reported. Without a full understanding of the impact of gaspers, assessment of the performance of the personalized displacement ventilation system cannot be properly made. In this project, therefore, the personalized displacement ventilation system will be investigated with the concurrent operation of gaspers, as a step towards reducing airborne disease transmission in commercial airliners. This project will first start with the laboratory experiments on the air distribution and source dispersion characteristics in index passenger’s breathing zone in an aircraft cabin mockup when the personalized displacement ventilation system is in use. Based on the experimental data and CFD calculations, this proposed project will investigate the influence of the index passenger’s gasper on the near-source contaminant transport. Further experiments will be carried out to investigate how gaspers influence the receptors’ contaminant exposure, considering different seat locations, gasper flow rates, and flow directions. This study will then identify the optimal gasper operating strategy for one single passenger. Finally, a method to obtain optimal gasper settings will be obtained, verified by an experimental investigation of the performance of the personalized displacement ventilation system in a seven-row cabin mockup. The proposed project will enhance our understanding of source dispersion in aircraft cabins, and how the use of gaspers affects contaminant transport. The findings will provide guidance for the use of gaspers in commercial airliners, and help the development of the innovative personalized displacement ventilation system to reduce airborne contaminant transport while maintaining cabin thermal comfort. 隨著搭乘飛機越來越普遍，公眾開始關注飛機客艙內的空氣質量。目前，機艙內存在大量可通過空氣傳播的污染物。此外，機艙內的熱舒適並非總是令人滿意。當前絕大多數客機機艙採用混合通風系統，然而由於其較低的通風效率，機艙內的空氣傳染病傳播仍然存在較大的風險。為了滿足個性化的熱舒適要求，通常在每個乘客的頭頂還會加配可調節送風速度和方向的風口。總的來說，可調節風口可以提高乘客的熱舒適，但是對空氣質量不一定有正面的影響。為了同時滿足熱舒適和空氣質量的要求，我們可以採用一種新的個性化置換通風系統。那麼，可調節風口會如何影響個性化置換通風系統對於空氣傳染疾病的控制呢？這就是本項目的研究目的。 本項目首先通過實驗測量，研究個性化置換通風下機艙內的氣流分佈和污染源擴散特性。基於實驗和計算流體力學模擬的數據，本項目將研究源乘客的可調節風口對於近污染源區域污染物傳播的影響。此外，本項目還會研究其他乘客的可調節風口，在不同在座位、送風量、和送風方向下，對每個乘客的污染物暴露的影響。基於模擬的數據，本研究會找出對於每一個乘客的最佳可調節風口的調節策略。最後，本項目將提出一種最優的可調節空口的全局設置方法，並通過在七排模擬機艙內的實驗來驗證此方法。 本項目將會提升我們對於機艙內污染源擴散的理解，並且提出如何有效的使用可調節風口以控制空氣傳染病的傳播。研究的結果將可以為我們提供客機機艙內使用可調節風口的指導意見，還可以有助於個性化置換通風的發展，降低機艙內的空氣傳染病傳播，且同時滿足熱舒適要求。

25210419.label: Realisation of objectives
25210419.value: All of the 7 objectives have been achieved. This project constructed a three-row, single-aisle, economy-class aircraft cabin mockup with 18 personalized displacement ventilation diffusers at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University. An adjustable circular jet vent was installed to model the gasper system. The project experimentally investigated the influence of the gasper-induced jet flow on the near-source contaminant transport, and on receptor's exposure to exhaled contaminants using SF6 as tracer gas. Due to the limited lab space, the three-row aircraft cabin mockup could not represent the air distribution in an actual aircraft cabin. Therefore, the obtained experimental data was used as benchmark for numerical simulations in the following objectives. Therefore, objective 1 'to experimentally and numerically investigate the influence of gasper-induced airflow on the near-source contaminant transport in an aircraft cabin with personalized displacement ventilation' has been partially achieved and objective 3 'to experimentally investigate the influence of gasper-induced airflow on the receptors' exposure to exhaled contaminants in an aircraft cabin with personalized displacement ventilation' has been fully achieved. Numerical calculations were conducted in a seven-row, single-aisle, fully occupied, economy-class aircraft cabin with the computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation method. We also simulated the air distribution in a 25-row section of an aircraft cabin to provide momentum and thermal data for the front and rear surfaces of the seven-row section model to achieve a more realistic simulation. To investigate the impact of gaspers on near-source transmission, we considered three source locations according to symmetry: the source passenger seated at window seat), middle seat, and aisle seat. The other passengers' gaspers were assumed to be closed. For the source passenger's gasper, the flow rates of half-open and fully-open were considered, and turning the gasper off was used as a benchmark. Three directions were considered for the source passenger's gasper direction: to the head, to the mouth, and to the abdomen. A total of 21 cases were calculated. We first analyzed the airflow pattern and exposure index of the receptors when the source passenger was in different seat locations with all gaspers off as the benchmark. We then compared the exposure index under different source gasper settings, including directions and flow rates. Finally, we assessed the performance of different gasper settings in reducing overall exposure to obtain the optimal gasper setting for source passengers. Therefore, objective 1 'to experimentally and numerically investigate the influence of gasper-induced airflow on the near-source contaminant transport in an aircraft cabin with personalized displacement ventilation' has been fully achieved. For a source passenger's gasper, the direction and flow rate of the gasper flow either increased or decreased the air contaminant transmission to other passengers. Directing the source gasper to the abdomen with a medium flow rate significantly mitigated the overall exposure, as this approach minimized the contaminant circulation in the aircraft cabin. This setting was recommended for the source passenger, and could reduce the mean exposure index by at least 45% compared to the benchmark. Therefore, objective 2 'to identify the optimal gasper operating strategy for the source passenger for minimizing the average background exhaled contaminant concentrations' has been fully achieved. To evaluate the effectiveness of gaspers in protecting receptors, we first identified the most at-risk receptor with the highest exposure for each seat location as the target receptors. For each considered receptor's gasper, the flow rates of half-open and fully-open, and three directions were considered, and the gaspers of other receptors were assumed to be closed. We then compared the exposure index of a given target receptor under different receptor gasper directions and flow rates to quantify the impact of the receptor's gasper settings. Furthermore, we analysed the airflow pattern and the contaminant concentration distribution to characterize the working mechanism of the gasper. Turning on a receptor passenger's gasper could be an effective strategy to protect the receptor, and the working mechanism was revealed. The gasper-induced jet flow entrained the surrounding air into the jet region, and the protective effect was related to the contaminant concentration at ceiling level. With a suitable gasper direction and flow rate, the gasper jet formed a virtual barrier between the source passenger and the receptor. When the contaminants were transported upwards to a receptor's breathing zone, turning on the receptor's gasper reduced the contaminant concentration, since the downward gasper jet altered the airflow pattern in front of the receptor. Therefore, objective 4 'to develop a model for determining the optimal gasper operating strategy for each receptor to reduce the contaminant concentration in the breathing zone' has been fully achieved. The calculated exposure index of all the receptors could be used to determine the optimal gasper operating strategy for source passengers, and directing the source gasper to the abdomen with a medium flow rate was the recommended setting. The calculated exposure index of each at-risk receptor could be used to determine the optimal gasper operating strategy for receptor passengers. As one at-most risk receptor passenger was determined for each seat type. Therefore, objective 5 'to develop a method to determine the optimal gasper operating strategy for both the source and receptor passengers in a seven-row, single aisle aircraft cabin mockup with personalized displacement ventilation' has been fully achieved. The determined seat-type dependent gasper operating strategy was numerically implemented in a seven-row, single-aisle, fully occupied, economy-class aircraft cabin for the concurrent operation of all gaspers. The corresponding exposure index was compared with that with all gaspers turned off as a benchmark. The results showed that operating the source gasper as the recommended setting could reduce the overall exposure index. However for receptors, as the air distribution is altered by the operation of other gaspers, the performance of the identified seat-type dependent gasper operating strategy could not be ensured. Therefore, objective 6 'to numerically verify the proposed optimal gasper operating strategy for the whole seven-row, single aisle aircraft cabin' has been fully achieved. This project developed a Bayesian optimization method based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD). A seven-row, single-aisle, fully occupied, economy-class aircraft cabin was used for the numerical investigation. First, the open ratios of all the gaspers were optimized by the CFD-based Bayesian optimization method with only 20 trials. With the optimal open ratios of all the gaspers, the number of relatively high-risk passengers (exposure index over 0.95) was effectively reduced by at least 86% when compared with the results with all gaspers turned off. Next, the optimal open ratios and flow directions of the gaspers near the index passenger were also determined by the proposed method. With the optimized operations of gaspers, the number of relatively high-risk passengers was effectively reduced by at least 67%. Therefore, objective 7 'to numerically assess the performance of the personalized displacement ventilation system with the proposed method to determine the optimal gasper setting in commercial airliners' has been fully achieved.
