25210419.label: Major findings and research outcome
25210419.value: Major findings: 1. For a source passenger's gasper, the direction and flow rate of the gasper flow either increased or decreased the air contaminant transmission to other passengers. Directing the source gasper to the abdomen with a medium flow rate significantly mitigated the overall exposure, as this approach minimized the contaminant circulation in the aircraft cabin. This setting was recommended for the source passenger, and could reduce the mean exposure index by at least 45% compared to the benchmark. 2. For a receptor's gasper, turning on the gasper with an appropriate setting could be an effective strategy to protect the receptor. The working mechanism of a receptor's gasper can be summarized as follows: (1) The gasper-induced jet flow entrained the surrounding air into the jet region, leading to either a positive or negative impact on the receptor's exposure. The protective effect depended on the contaminant concentration at ceiling level. (2) With a suitable gasper direction and flow rate, the gasper jet formed a virtual barrier between the source passenger and the receptor. This mechanism reduced the contaminant transmission to the receptor's breathing zone. (3) When the contaminants were transported upwards to the receptor's breathing zone, turning on the receptor's gasper reduced the contaminant concentration, since the downward gasper jet altered the airflow pattern in front of the receptor. 3. For implementing the identified seat-type dependent optimal gasper setting in commercial airliners for the concurrent operation of all gaspers, operating the source gasper as the recommended setting could reduce the overall exposure index. However for receptors, as the air distribution is altered by the operation of other gaspers, the performance of the identified seat-type dependent gasper operating strategy could not be ensured. 4. The open ratios of all the gaspers optimized by the CFD-based Bayesian optimization method could reduce the number of relatively high-risk passengers by at least 86% when compared with the results with all gaspers turned off for a seven-row, single-aisle, fully occupied, economy-class aircraft cabin with personalized displacement ventilation. Research outcome: This project has led to 6 journal publications in Building and Environment, Indoor Environments, Indoor Air, and Measurement Science and Technology. Another journal paper is under preparation. The research results were disseminated in Indoor Air 2020, COBEE 2022, and twice in Indoor Air 2024.

25210419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25210419.value: Optimizing the operation of gaspers can reduce passengers' exposure risks, offering a secondary function of the gasper system beyond its primary role in personal thermal comfort. However, few studies in the literature have systematically explored the potential of the gasper system in this regard. It is potential to further develop a self-adaptive operation strategy for gaspers to reduce airborne infectious disease transmission in commercial airliners while maintaining passengers' thermal comfort. First, a simulation-based optimization method will be developed to identify the optimal operation of gaspers for minimizing passengers' exposure risks in a seven-row aircraft cabin. The mechanisms by which optimized gasper operation affects air distribution and reduces passengers' exposure risks will be systematically investigated. A database of optimal gasper operations will then be established using the simulation-based optimization method for scenarios in which some passengers manually adjust their gaspers to achieve thermal comfort. Based on the obtained database, a machine learning model for advanced gasper operation that adapts to passengers' thermal comfort needs when some gaspers are manually adjusted will be developed. Finally, the effectiveness of the self-adaptive gasper operation strategy in reducing passengers' exposure will be experimentally assessed in an aircraft cabin mockup.

25210419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25210419.value: As air travel grows, concerns about cabin environments have risen due to airborne contaminants and thermal discomfort. Current mixing air distribution systems in aircrafts can increase the risk of disease transmission because of low ventilation effectiveness. Gasper vents offer personalized control over air supply, improving thermal comfort but with mixed effects on air quality. A personalized displacement ventilation system could enhance comfort and reduce contaminants, but its performance with gaspers is not well-studied. This project investigates this system with gaspers to reduce disease transmission. Laboratory experiments were conducted to examine air distribution and contaminant dispersion in a cabin mockup. Using experimental data and CFD calculations, the project assessed how gaspers affect contaminant transport and exposure. This study identified optimal gasper settings for passengers and verify these in a seven-row cabin mockup. Results show that directing a source passenger's gasper to the abdomen with a medium flow rate can reduce exposure by at least 45%. For receptors, appropriate gasper settings could offer protection, and the working mechanism was revealed. This research enhances understanding of contaminant transport and guide gasper use to improve air quality and comfort.

25211319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25211319.value: Degradation of engineering structures often begins with initiation of microscopic fatigue cracks which progressively worsen to become significant damages that would compromise structural integrity and lead to failure. For both safety and cost-saving consideration, it is of unquestionable importance to be able to monitor progression of fatigue cracks, preferably using in situ means as well so that normal operation of test structures would not be interrupted. Fatigue cracks are hardly perceivable by conventional damage detection techniques that depend on damage-induced linear macroscopic changes in diagnostic signals. Rather, it has been shown that this type of cracks result in nonlinear modulation of ultrasonic waves, and such physical phenomenon forms the basis of nonlinear ultrasonic damage detection techniques. In this project, by exploiting the nonlinearity of ultrasonic guided waves (UGW), a novel in situ technique for monitoring growth of fatigue cracks in plate-like structures will be introduced. Phased array scanning (PAS) that employs focused UGW will be carried out by permanently installed piezoelectric transducers. Differences between the diffuse fields that are generated by sequential and parallel transmission based total focusing will be parameterized to quantify damage-induced nonlinearity. Development of the proposed technique will build upon a number of fundamental investigations: (1) configuration of piezoelectric transducer arrays based on mathematical analysis of focusing of UGW by phased arrays, (2) tuning of diagnostic signals via analytical modelling of excitation of UGW by piezoelectric transducers, and (3) determination of imaging parameters through numerical simulation of propagation of UGW and statistical assessment of acoustic diffusivity. Results of PAS will be presented as pixelated images, from which quantitative characterization of cracks will be attained by advanced image processing. Experimental validation of the proposed technique will be conducted extensively using structures that contain fatigue cracks with various characteristics. Compared to detection by sparse arrays, imaging by phased arrays is deterministic in nature and possesses a superior resolution, enabling visualization of finer details such as shapes of cracks and co-existence of multiple cracks. By wisely manipulating differences between the energies that are experienced by focal points in real time during sequential and parallel beam-focusing, high-energy excitation of piezoelectric transducers will no longer be necessary, eliminating the need for high-power amplifiers which has been a major hindrance to real-world applications of detection of fatigue damages using the nonlinearity of ultrasonic waves. Automated and continuous quantitative evaluation of fatigue cracks, starting from their embryonic stages, will provide vital information to structural integrity assessment. 工程結構的退化往往始於微小疲勞裂紋的出現。這些裂紋會逐漸演變為可危及結構完整性并導致結構失效的損傷。出於安全性以及經濟性的考慮，針對疲勞裂紋發展過程的監控至關重要。如果可以採用原位的方法進行監控，則被檢對象的正常使用将不會被影響。疲勞裂紋几乎不可能被傳統的、依賴於由損傷導致的線性信號變化的探傷方法檢測到。相反，這類裂紋已經被證實可以導致信號的非線性變化。此物理現象為非線性超聲無損檢測方法提供了理論基礎。本項目將立足于超聲導波的非線性，通過對一系列基礎科學問題的探究，建立一種新型的、可用於原位監測板材中的疲勞裂紋的生長過程的超聲導波相控陣技术。

25211319.label: Realisation of objectives
25211319.value: This project has been successfully completed with all of its objectives satisfactorily achieved. The research methods adopted in this project embody theoretical analysis, analytical and numerical modelling, and physical experimentation. At first, we investigated, via Huygens-Fresnel principle, the effects of the dimension and central frequency of a piezoelectric transducer on the amplitude and geometry of the ultrasonic wave field that the piezoelectric transducer would generate. Using the finite element method, we then established the relationships between the parameters of a piezoelectric phased array (i.e., the number of piezoelectric transducers and the relative positions of the transducers) and the amplitude and coverage of the total ultrasonic wave field that the piezoelectric phased array would generate. We further formulated a high-fidelity analytical-numerical modelling framework that can vividly simulate the excitation and reception of ultrasonic waves by piezoelectric transducer arrays, and the propagation of ultrasonic waves in solid structures. The modelling framework was used to aid the development of an imaging technique that can quantitatively reconstruct the locations and dimensions of microscopic defects from the time-of-arrival’s and amplitudes of defect-modulated ultrasonic waves. Finally, we performed a variety of corrosion experiments, during which corrosion defects on steel substrates were tracked, in order to validate the feasibility and performance of the imaging technique.

25211319.label: Major findings and research outcome
25211319.value: (1) We resorted to several different approaches to accelerate the computation of the modulation of ultrasonic waves by microscopic defects in solid structures. All of these approaches have been shown to be capable of significantly reducing computational expenses in terms of computational time and number of degree-of-freedom’s. The resultant mathematical models served as the basis for the development of the proposed ultrasonic defect monitoring technique. (2) We introduced an in situ ultrasonic technique that makes use of permanently installed piezoelectric transducer arrays to monitor, in real time, the initiation and growth of microscopic defects in solid structures. Via physical experimentation, the technique has been shown to possess a measurement accuracy that’s comparable to that of high-resolution white light interferometry, and an ultra-high measurement resolution of 100 nm. (3) Two PhD students, one MSc student and one undergraduate student have been trained under this project. (4) Five SCI journal publications have been generated in total. Four of the five publications were for disseminating the research results, and one was produced by an undergraduate student who participated in the education programme associated with this project.

25211319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25211319.value: The ultimate goal is to transfer the proposed ultrasonic defect monitoring technique to industry. Through this project, the theoretical foundation of the technique has been comprehensively built up. Currently, we are working on improving the performance stability and manufacturability of the technique, two aspects that are crucial to real-world applications. Once we have devised a stable and easy-to-manufacture prototype, we will seek other suitable funding to carry out further commercialization-related research.

25211319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25211319.value: Throughout the service life of a loading-bearing structure, defects inevitably accumulate, leading to damages which gradually deteriorate the structure to failure. While structures are always designed with due consideration for defects, factors such as excessive material imperfections and unexpected operating conditions often cause accelerated degradation. Numerous defect-induced structural failures have occurred in the past, resulting in devasting societal, environmental and financial impact. In this project, we have developed an ultrasonic technique that can continuously assess, in real time, the severity of defects while structures are in service and even in operation. With such capability, it is expected that defects will be identified in a much prompter manner, significantly reducing the chance of happening of more severe consequences. The proposed technique, the theoretical foundation of which has been furnished through this project, is currently being developed into a field-implementable technology.

25211819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25211819.value: Nowadays, advanced remote-sensing techniques provide high-fidelity observations of terrestrial ecosystems from different perspectives, dimensions, and granularity. Especially, the combined application of airborne LiDAR and digital cameras provides multispectral point clouds and permits volumetric measurement and characterization of vegetation. Individual tree-based methods using advanced computer vision and machine learning algorithms can directly provide various interesting attributes at a tree-object level, including location, species, volume, and vitality, making it more applicable to widespread high-resolution data. Based on extensive experience obtained through our former study on LiDAR-based forest inventory over a long period of time, the aim of the proposed project is to address the bottleneck in 3D vegetation mapping for precise ecosystem assessment. The idea is to advance an individual tree-labeling strategy for 3D aerial forest inventory to segment and classify tree objects (tree species and vitality conditions) simultaneously in multispectral point clouds. This study will be innovative in the development of graph-based semantic segmentation for multispectral point clouds of a heterogeneous forest by embedding image domain knowledge learned in a weakly supervised manner because the image/scene-level labels can be used as comparable priors for tree categorization and can be obtained in a much easier and cheaper way than is possible with field data. Finally, we plan to jointly validate and analyze tree characterization results with respect to detection and classification accuracy. This project's holistic approach will provide key insights into the role played by weakly supervised graph segmentation within the framework of multispectral point cloud analysis for tree characterization. The project outcomes will contribute to LiDAR-based forest inventory by combining tree segmentation and classification in one solution by not only increasing the tree segmentation accuracy but also reducing the dependency on field data. The results would also help characterize multi-dimensional fine structures of a heterogeneous ecosystem in a more comprehensive way. 如今，先进的遥感技术可以从不同的角度，尺寸和粒度提供对陆地生态系统的高保真度观测。特别是，机载激光雷达和数码相机的组合应用提供了多光谱点云，并允许对植被进行体积测量和表征。使用高级计算机视觉和机器学习算法的基于树的单独方法可以直接在树 - 对象级别提供各种有趣的属性，包括位置，种类，体积和活力，使其更适用于广泛的高分辨率数据。基于我们之前对基于LiDAR的森林资源清查长期研究所获得的丰富经验，该项意图解决三维植被制图的瓶颈问题，以进行精确的生态系统评估。其目的是推进3D空中森林库存的单树标记策略，以便在多光谱点云中同时对树木对象（树种和活力条件）进行分割和分类。本研究将通过嵌入以弱监督方式学习的图像领域知识，开发基于图形的异构森林多光谱点云语义分割，因为图像/场景级标签可用作树类分类的可比较先验并且可以比现场数据更容易和低成本的方式获得。 最后，我们计划在检测和分类准确性方面联合验证和分析树木特征结果。该项目的整体方法将提供关于弱监督图分割在树木表征的多光谱点云分析框架内所起作用的关键见解。通过在一个解决方案中结合树分割和分类，项目结果将有助于基于LiDAR的森林调查，不仅提高树分割精度，还减少对现场数据的依赖。该结果还有助于以更全面的方式表征异构生态系统的多维精细结构。

25211819.label: Realisation of objectives
25211819.value: The recent development of multi-modality remote-sensing technology ( aerial multispectral image and LiDAR) has contributed a lot to a revolution in 3D vegetation mapping by generating integrated semantic and volumetric tree models for a heterogenous ecosystem. Such measurements can be efficiently used and modeled using phenological theory to obtain the source parameters for interaction between climate and the ecosystem. However, creating fully supervised tree annotations (e.g. species and vitality) via field work is costly and time-consuming because it still relies on providing the ground truth of object boundaries and locations for training. Thus, the applicability of the aforementioned approaches is limited to small-sized datasets. I therefore proposed to do a new study of single-tree characterization by graph semantic segmentation of aerial multispectral point clouds based on weakly supervised learning, which requires only image/scene-level weak labels. The proposed work is built on my existing skills by adding a significant suite of techniques that will diversify competences. The two objectives have been fully realized via following developed approaches: 1. proposed a pseudo-label-assisted ALS point cloud segmentation method with very few sparsely sampled labels that are normally randomly selected for each class. An adaptive thresholding strategy was proposed to generate a pseudo-label based on the prediction probability. Pseudo-label learning is an iterative process, and pseudo labels were updated solely on ground-truth weak labels as the model converged to improve the training efficiency. 2. developed a framework for segmenting multiple tree stem objects of a common dead tree type from aerial imagery using a collection of evolving active contours, unified under an aggregate energy functional encompassing various aspects of the segmentation quality.

25211819.label: Major findings and research outcome
25211819.value: The current study is based on a new trend in 3D vegetation mapping solutions using multispectral aerial image and point cloud data. Such data can be generated by airborne multispectral LiDAR directly or by geometrically co-registering airborne waveform LiDAR point clouds with multispectral aerial images. More importantly, this study sheds light on weakly supervised learning and its role within the graph-based semantic instance segmentation framework for individual tree labeling in aerial images and point clouds. The proposed study has direct implications for the revealing of vegetation carbon dynamics in high fidelity and for scaling semantic segmentation for 3D forest inventory applications to larger datasets. The overall project concept has not been tested before, but it is desirable for research attempts with a high-gain potential that leads to new knowledge. The project outcomes contributes to aerial image and LiDAR-based forest inventory by combining tree segmentation and classification in one solution by not only increasing the tree segmentation accuracy of various types but also tremendously reducing the dependency of the leaning model on field data. The results would also help characterize multi-dimensional fine structures of a heterogeneous ecosystem in a more comprehensive, precise and efficient way.

25211819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25211819.value: Advanced remote-sensing techniques provide high-fidelity observations of terrestrial ecosystems from different perspectives and granularity. The aim of the further proposed study could address the bottleneck in vegetation mapping for precise ecosystem assessment. The idea is to advance an individual tree-labeling strategy for 3D forest inventory to segment and classify tree objects (tree species and vitality conditions) simultaneously in multispectral image and point clouds. The study will be innovative in the development of graph-based semantic segmentation for multispectral aerial data of a heterogeneous forest by embedding image domain knowledge learned in a weakly supervised manner because the image-level labels can be used as comparable priors for tree categorization and can be obtained in a much easier and cheaper way than is possible with field data. Another issue to be addressed in future work is associated with objects split by shadows or occlusions in the probability image, leading to fragmentations of stems into disjoint parts. For large scenes with hundreds or thousands of objects, it would be computationally intractable to jointly consider all high-probability image regions within one optimization problem. Instead, a more feasible strategy seems to perform merging of the detected polygons as a post-processing step, e.g. using a graph-cut approach.

25211819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25211819.value: Plants and vegetation can help mitigate elevated temperatures by providing shade and increasing evaporative cooling, although the resulting increase in humidity may negatively affect thermal comfort. Street trees and forest parks offer particular potential for cooling microclimates and provide important ecosystem services and values. However, so far, we still have little quantitative information about the role of such trees in providing regulating ecosystem services. The large spatial and temporal variations in a heterogenous ecosystem require multi-modality remote-sensing techniques with observation of both high spatial and temporal resolution from various perspectives and dimensions. Other than area-based approaches, the proposed project helps assess terrestrial ecosystem by characterizing vegetation structures and ecological budgets based on individual trees. The limitation of former approaches is apparent with respect to information retrieval from LiDAR and imagery data. To improve the synergistic capacity of sensor-specific models for tree characterization, an explicit understanding of the cross-modality linkage between spectral and geometric signatures toward mapping ecological indices is developed.

25215519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25215519.value: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a highly prevalent neurodevelopmental condition that results in considerable lifetime costs. Early identification of ASD is critical, in order to implement early interventions to enhance treatment effectiveness and reduce personal and family burdens. Because the medical diagnosis of ASD relies on detecting behavioral, social, and communication deficits, the first diagnosis is usually made when the patient is between 3-5 years old. Emerging evidence suggests that individuals with ASD exhibit early motor development and neuromotor deficits, even before one year of age. Among these deficits, preliminary findings suggest that aberrant fidgety movements presented between 8-20 weeks of postterm age predict future development of ASD. However, these preliminary findings have been challenged by small study sample sizes (i.e., n≤20) and the use of heterogeneous samples (e.g., inclusions of children with risk factors for ASD). In addition, information about the sensitivity and specificity of early aberrant fidgety movements as predictors of ASD is lacking. Conventionally, the assessment of fidgety movements requires trained clinical practitioners. Leveraging the improved capacity of video-based motion analysis, fidgety movements could also be assessed using videos recorded by ordinary cameras or smartphones. However, information, such as differences in the fidgety movement kinematics (e.g., range of motion, velocity, acceleration, and smoothness) between children with ASD and typically developing children, is needed before the video-based technology can be applied. Moreover, with the advancement of computational algorithm (e.g., machine-learning), conventional fidgety movement assessment could potentially be enhanced in infants with confirmed medical diagnosis of ASD. The trained algorithm would likely demonstrate better predictability of ASD than the conventional clinical method. In view of these knowledge gaps, we propose to collect retrospective videos recorded between 10-16 weeks of post-term age from 28 children with confirmed diagnosis of ASD and 28 children with typical development. The videos will be analyzed by a trained and experienced clinician who is blind to the children’s condition; we will examine the sensitivity and specificity of rater’s assessment of fidgety movements for ASD prediction. The same batch of video clips will be processed by a state-of-the-art video motion analysis algorithm. We will compare the selected kinematics parameters between children with and without ASD. Based on the results of the kinematics differences, we will establish a prediction model using machine-learning techniques, aiming to improve the prediction of ASD by fidgety movement analysis. Similar to the clinical method, we will examine the predictability of the model.

To enhance the digital coaching system taking uncertainty considerations into account to guarantee a near real-time re-planning on motion guidance against dynamic training scenarios. Simulated training experiments will be conducted based on the actual site information to validate the effectiveness of the proposed coaching system. 25221519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25221519.value: Cranes are critical construction site resources. Accidents do occur and safe crane operation is a critically important goal. Most crane accidents are due to careless operation, no doubt often due to inadequate training and insufficient knowledge. This project will develop a digital crane coaching system, for training purposes, a system which has experienced crane operator knowledge embedded within it. The system will be capable of displaying and teaching a large number of crane lifting scenario. The trainee will be able learn passively as various lifting operations are simulated on the screen, and teaching comments are made simultaneously. The trainee will also be able to learn actively by carrying out virtual lifts, receiving advice on the mistakes made and, if requested, guidance on the next step. A facility will also exist whereby trainee lifting solutions can be compared with system generated preferred solutions. The research will address a significant gap, in that although current virtual crane training practice is feasible for preliminary rehearsals, it fails to reflect the knowledge and experience of the practiced crane operator, including the concerns and uncertainties which arise naturally for such an operator when faced with a new lift in a specific environment. To date, little research has been conducted on developing such a ‘digital coach’ one including automatic guidance to trainees in the manner proposed here. The project team will identify, assemble and model those factors related to crane operation, including safety considerations, perception limitations, and control features, so as to generate close to authentic automatic crane motion patterns. Knowledge formulae relating to crane operations will be established, and mechanisms to embed operational factors into the automation design will be developed. A sampling-based motion planning approach will be improved upon. In order to validate the practicability of the proposed coaching approach, experimental comparisons will be made with conventional training processes. The coaching approach to be developed and studied is expected to support effective virtual crane training, with graduate trainees able to propose practical, safe and efficient operational lifting plans. The automatic motion planning deliverable will enable assessment criteria to be derived and used during the training process. The intended research contributions to knowledge and understanding will be in the link made between known heuristics and operator enhanced awareness. New discovery will be made regarding how to effectively transfer heuristic used by experts to enhance the awareness and performance of novices in the field.

25222319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25222319.value: Projecting future changes in hydroclimatic regimes (e.g., precipitation, temperature, relative humidity, evapotranspiration, streamflow, etc.) at a high spatial resolution (≤ 4 km) plays a crucial role in improving urban sustainability and resilience to climate-induced extreme events, such as floods, droughts, heat waves, and storm surges. The combination of climate and hydrologic models is recognized as a powerful means to predict hydroclimatic changes driven by future anthropogenic and natural forcings. There are many climate and hydrologic models available for generating hydroclimatic projections. Since every model has a unique mathematical structure that may accurately represent certain hydroclimatic processes but overlook the others, no single best model can be applied to accurately and reliably predict future changes in hydroclimatic regimes. Thus, there is a strong consensus in the hydroclimate science community that forecasts from multiple models with different structures are superior to single-model forecasts. However, a tremendous computational cost is often required to combine multi-model ensemble forecasts, thereby resulting in a significant challenge to the applicability of multi-model techniques. Previous studies have suggested that the high-resolution (≤ 4 km) hydroclimatic projections are particularly useful for providing a realistic representation of small-scale hydroclimate dynamics that are important for areas with heterogeneous land surfaces (e.g., mountainous, coastal, urban regions, etc.). However, such high-resolution projections are often generated using single models (i.e. the combination of a single regional climate model and a single hydrologic model). Few studies have been conducted to utilize multi-model ensemble projections of future fine-scale hydroclimatic changes. Therefore, the challenge is to develop a multi-model ensemble framework for taking advantage of different combinations of multiple climate and hydrologic models in order to improve the accuracy and reliability of high-resolution hydroclimatic projections. It is also necessary to develop a computationally efficient approach for improving the effectiveness and efficiency of multi-model ensemble techniques. The proposed project aims to develop a new multi-model ensemble framework for projecting future changes in hydroclimatic regimes over China’s Greater Bay Area. The new ensemble framework will be implemented using Bayesian model averaging with multivariate copula functions (BMA-MCF). In addition, factorial-polynomial-chaos-based surrogate models will be developed to reduce the computational cost of Bayesian multi-model combinations. Such a surrogate-based BMA-MCF approach will enable the generation of multi-model ensemble projections in a computationally efficient manner. The projected changes in hydroclimatic regimes will provide meaningful insights into climate change related risks, opportunities, and adaptation actions to ensure a resilient future for China’s Greater Bay Area. 利用高分辨率區域氣候模式對未來極端水文氣候事件（如洪水、乾旱、熱浪等）進行預估對加強城市可持續性發展起著至關重要的作用。水文模型和氣候模式被認為是預測未來水文氣候變化的有力工具，由於每個模型都有一個獨特的數學結構，可以準確地表徵某些水文氣候過程而忽略了一些其他過程，因此沒有一個最優模型可以準確可靠地預測未來的水文氣候變化。在水文氣候科學界有一個強烈的共識，即來自具有不同數學結構的多模型集合預報優於單模型預報。然而，多模型集合預報通常會產生巨大的計算成本，從而導致多模型技術在適用性方面面臨著重大挑戰。過去研究表明，高分辨率水文氣候預報能夠更加真實地表徵小尺度的水文氣候過程，對於地貌比較複雜的區域（如山區、海岸線、城市等）特別重要。然而，過去研究通常使用單一模型進行高分辨率的預報，利用多模型技術進行高分辨率水文氣候集合預報的研究還很少。因此，本研究擬開發一個多模型集合預報系統，利用多個氣候模式和水文模型，通過使用貝葉斯模型平均法和copula函數，以提高高分辨率水文氣候預報的準確性和可靠性，並在此基礎上開發一種新方法來提高多模型集合預報的計算效率。擬開發的多模型集合預報系統將用於預測粵港澳大灣區未來水文氣候變化，為粵港澳大灣區製定應對氣候變化戰略和政策提供科學依據，以實現可持續性發展目標。

25222319.label: Realisation of objectives
25222319.value: The three objectives of this project have been fully achieved. Specifically, we have developed the multi-decadal convection-permitting climate projections with horizontal grid spacing of 4 km for China’s Greater Bay Area (GBA) and surroundings (Qing and Wang, 2021), using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model based on an ensemble of 10 Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 5 (CMIP5) GCMs. Our findings demonstrate the added value of the convection-permitting WRF model with the spatial resolution of 4 km for simulating the spring and summertime precipitation as well as extreme heavy rainfall events with daily amounts larger than 30 mm over China’s GBA, in comparison with 12 km and 36 km simulations. Future changes in precipitation, temperature and their extremes have also been projected for the period of 2074–2099 relative to the reference period of 1980–2005 under different scenarios of Representative Concentration Pathways (RCPs) 4.5 and 8.5. According to the proposed dissemination plan, we have developed a web-based China’s Greater Bay Area Climate Data Portal (GBAcdp), http://www.gbacdp.cn/, to disseminate future projected climate change information derived from convection-permitting climate simulations and to support extreme weather and climate research. The GBAcdp enables both technical and nontechnical users to have easy access to high-resolution climate data. Users can freely explore the interactive maps with more than 30,000 grids over China’s GBA. Based on the high-resolution projections of climate variables, we have used two physically based hydrologic models, including the Variable Infiltration Capacity (VIC) and the Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) models, to assess hydrologic regimes in response to climate change over the Dongjiang River Basin which is located in the east of the Pearl River Basin, South China. Such a multi-model ensemble approach is able to address model structural uncertainty in high-resolution hydroclimatic projections; however, it requires an extremely high computational cost. Consequently, we have developed the factorial polynomial chaos expansions (PCEs) as surrogate models of VIC and SWAT to improve the computational efficiency of multi-model ensemble hydroclimatic projections (Zhang et al., 2022). The PCE coefficients are time-variant and are estimated based on hydrologic observations, indicating that the coefficients are not available for future periods without observations and thus the PCE model fails to predict the future hydrologic regimes. To address this issue, the time-variant PCE coefficients are assumed to be related to the meteorological forcing variables (e.g., precipitation and temperature), and such a relationship can be characterized by deep neural networks (DNNs) and remain valid in the future. The input and output of DNNs are meteorological variables and PCE coefficients, respectively. Such an assumption enables efficient PCE-based hydrologic predictions by using well-calibrated DNNs to predict PCE coefficients for future periods without observations. The DNN-based PCE models have been successfully applied to predict daily discharges of the Longchuan and Boluo gauging stations, respectively, located in the Dongjiang River Basin. Our findings indicate that the DNN-based PCE models achieve comparable performance to the physically based hydrologic predictions with an extremely low computational cost. As a single DNN-based PCE model is inadequate for reliable hydrologic predictions due to model structural uncertainty, we have developed a vine copula multi-model ensemble approach to combine the outputs from multiple DNN-based PCE models to address the uncertainty in model structures, thereby improving the reliability of hydrologic predictions (Zhang et al., 2022a). Such a surrogate-based vine copula multi-model ensemble framework has been used to project future changes in hydrologic regimes over China’s GBA. We have also used the ANOVA-based variance decomposition method to estimate the contribution of model parameter and structure to the overall uncertainty in projected changes of hydrologic regimes. In addition, the vine copula multi-model ensemble approach has been applied to project future changes in precipitation intensity–duration–frequency (IDF) curves, with a multi-model ensemble of five regional climate simulations (Zhang et al., 2022b). The IDF curves play a crucial role in the design and planning of urban infrastructure to reduce the risk of urban flooding and rainfall-triggered landslides. Our findings reveal that the vine copula multi-model ensemble approach achieves higher reliability and accuracy in reproducing the climate-model-based precipitation IDF curves compared to the ensemble mean simulation. Our results suggest that the current urban infrastructure in China would be inadequate to prevent losses and damages caused by rainfall-triggered hazards under a high emission scenario (RCP8.5) if designed solely based on historical precipitation observations. A web-based data platform has been developed for China’s Urban Precipitation IDF Curves Considering Climate Change Impacts (http://chinaidf.com). To explicitly address model structural uncertainty in high-resolution hydroclimatic projections, we have developed a Bayesian model averaging (BMA) framework, which merges five regional climate model simulations, to project future changes in hydroclimatic regimes over China under two representative emission scenarios (RCP4.5 and RCP8.5). We have also developed a Bayesian copula approach to uncover underlying interactions of drought characteristics and associated uncertainties (Zhang et al., 2021a), thereby improving the multidimensional drought risk assessment. Our findings reveal that the variations in drought characteristics are generally underestimated by the ensemble mean simulation. The Bayesian framework improves the reliability and accuracy of hydroclimate simulations and better reproduces the drought regimes compared to the ensemble mean simulation. The drought duration and severity are projected to substantially increase for most areas of China. The estimated joint risk from drought duration and severity is expected to increase under both emission scenarios. The likelihood of extreme droughts is also projected to increase as the radiative forcing increases. Furthermore, we have developed a Bayesian vine copula approach to explicitly address the multidimensional dependence of flood characteristics (i.e., flood peak, volume, and duration) and underlying uncertainties (Zhang et al., 2021b). The Bayesian vine copula framework has also been applied to the probabilistic prediction of extreme storm surges induced by tropical cyclones in Hong Kong (Zhang and Wang, 2021). In addition to methodological development, we have applied novel multi-model frameworks to address the emerging risk of hydroclimatic extremes in this project. Specifically, we have performed a comprehensive assessment of the onset development of flash droughts and the underlying mechanisms based on an ensemble of global climate model simulations and bivariate copulas (Qing et al., 2022). Our findings suggest that Hong Kong and other southern parts of China have become more vulnerable to flash droughts that develop in a shorter time amid climate change. Atmospheric aridity creates perfect conditions for the occurrence of flash droughts, and the joint influence of soil moisture depletion and atmospheric aridity further enhances the rapid onset of flash droughts. We have also explored the spatiotemporal characteristics and dynamic evolution of dry and wet extremes in China (Chen et al., 2020, 2023), based on an ensemble of regional climate model simulations. Our findings provide scientific evidence and new insights into the development of climate adaptation and resilience policies for achieving sustainable development.

25222319.label: Major findings and research outcome
25222319.value: We have developed a multi-model ensemble framework by merging the strengths of Bayesian model averaging (BMA) and multivariate copula functions to project future changes in hydroclimatic regimes (Zhang et al., 2022a & 2022b). This framework can explicitly address model structural uncertainty, thereby enhancing the accuracy and reliability of hydroclimatic projections over China’s GBA. In comparison, our new multi-model ensemble framework outperforms the widely used BMA techniques in combining multiple model outputs in terms of reliability, sharpness, and accuracy. To improve the computational efficiency of multi-model ensemble hydrologic predictions, we have also developed DNN-based PCEs as surrogate models of VIC and SWAT used to predict daily discharges in the Dongjiang River Basin. Our findings indicate that the DNN-based PCE models achieve comparable performance to the physically based models but are more than 4,000 times faster. Based on the multi-decadal convection-permitting climate projections using the WRF model (Qing and Wang, 2021), we have also developed a web-based China’s Greater Bay Area Climate Data Portal (GBAcdp), http://www.gbacdp.cn/, to disseminate simulated climate change information for impact studies. With the aid of the multi-model ensemble framework and copulas, we have revealed the spatiotemporal dynamics and physical mechanisms of hydroclimatic extremes, including storm surges (Zhang and Wang, 2021), droughts (Qing et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2022) and floods (Zhang et al., 2021), as well as their interactions (Chen et al., 2020 & 2023). Our findings provide scientific evidence and new insights into the development of climate adaptation and resilience policies for achieving sustainable development. In recognition of our outstanding accomplishments in hydroclimatic extremes research using China's Tianhe-2 supercomputer, we won the “2023 Tianhe Star Award” for excellent application. We also successfully organized a special issue titled "Hydroclimatic Extremes and Impacts in a Changing Environment: Observations, Mechanisms, and Projections". This special issue is a timely collection of 50 high-quality articles that cover a variety of topics in the field of hydroclimatic extremes. In addition, one PhD student, three MSc students, and six undergraduate students have been trained to work on relevant research during this project. The PhD student, Boen Zhang, is now working as a postdoc fellow at the University of Oxford's School of Geography and the Environment. The MSc student, Tong Man Po Bowie, received the 2022 HKIS Dissertation Award for Postgraduate Students. The undergraduate student, Chue Cheuk Ying Cherry, received the 2020 HKIS Outstanding Final Year Dissertation Award.

25222319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25222319.value: Compound weather and climate events, which consist of two or more hazards or drivers, have received widespread attention in recent years from researchers, practitioners, and policymakers. The impacts of compound events can be greater than the sum effects of individual events. The Bayesian vine copula framework we developed in this project is applicable to the study of compound events by explicitly uncovering the multidimensional dependence and interaction between multiple hazards or drivers, advancing our understanding of the underlying mechanisms of compound events. The multi-model ensemble framework can also be used directly to combine the outputs of multiple models used to simulate various hazards, thereby enhancing the reliability of predicting compound events. In addition, we will further investigate the climate change impacts on the spatiotemporal dynamics of compound events based on the high-resolution hydroclimatic projections over China’s GBA, facilitating the implementation of regional multi-hazard early warning systems. The research outcomes lay a solid foundation for future investigation of compound events in a changing climate.

25222319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25222319.value: Projecting future changes in hydroclimatic regimes plays a crucial role in improving urban sustainability and resilience to climate-induced extreme events, such as droughts, floods, and storm surges. This project developed a new multi-model ensemble framework to improve the reliability and efficiency of high-resolution hydroclimatic projections. Based on these high-resolution projections of climate variables, we developed a web-based China’s Greater Bay Area Climate Data Portal (GBAcdp) to disseminate projected climate change information and to support extreme weather and climate research. In recognition of our outstanding contribution to extreme weather and climate research using China's Tianhe-2 supercomputer, we won the “2023 Tianhe Star Award” for excellent application. In addition, our research on hydroclimatic extremes has been published in high-impact journals, such as Nature Communications and Water Resources Research. Our research has received widespread international and local media coverage and has also been selected as ‘Research Highlight’ in Nature. Our major findings and research outcomes provide meaningful insights into climate change-related risks, opportunities, and adaptation actions to ensure a climate-resilient future for China’s Greater Bay Area.

25223119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25223119.value: This paper proposes post-earthquake optimization for inspection routing and restoration scheduling (OIRRS) for highway bridges networks, with the aim of facilitating post-disaster relief, including the networks’ response and recovery capabilities. OIRRS for highway networks in the response phase is complex, comprised of real-time interaction between simultaneous inspection and restoration for damaged bridges. On the one hand, optimal restoration scheduling is enhanced by real-time data on bridges’ damage status obtained by inspection; but on the other, optimal inspection routing can benefit from knowledge of moment-to-moment data on changes in network functionality resulting from restoration. Therefore, understanding the complex interactive impacts of real-time interaction and its impacts on OIRRS is necessary to identify and implement practical OIRRS for its management and use. However, current methods for post-disaster restoration scheduling in the response phase do not consider real-time bridges’ damage information, while methods for post-disaster inspection routing in the same phase are currently lacking. Additionally, these methods are too optimistic to facilitate optimal scheduling in reality: the system functionality is assumed to increase monotonically, ignoring the degradation in the functionality that can occur when a network component such as a bridge is taken out of commission while being restored. Understanding the impacts of such network-element downtime due to restoration on network functionality is necessary to the estimation of the network’s resilience (a measurement of network’s recovery capability). Therefore, we also propose a novel resilience-quantification model that can improve practical appraisal of highway networks’ post-disaster recovery capability by investigating the impacts of network-element downtime due to restoration on network functionality. By incorporating the proposed resilience-quantification model, this project aims to develop novel post-earthquake OIRRS model for highway networks while accounting for the impacts of the real-time inspection-restoration interaction on the networks’ functionality with special consideration for maximizing the networks’ resilience, thereby improving post-earthquake response and recovery. The main phase of this research effort will consist of the development of mathematical tools to support real-time decision making for efficient OIRRS, with the assumption that multiple inspection and repair teams will be operating simultaneously, which will involve complex, real-time interaction problems that will be modeled using mixed-integer programming techniques. This research will contribute to both practice and theory. The results of this study can provide support for decision makers in drafting post-earthquake OIRRS strategy for highway networks. Additionally, the proposed resilience quantification model can expand the capabilities of current theoretical resilience models of highway networks. 地震发生后，具有良好地震韧性的公路交通网络可在较少影响其通行功能的情况下快速恢复到震前交通通行能力的水平。公路交通网络的地震韧性决定了灾后应急响应及灾后恢复活动是否可以顺利进行。桥梁是公路网络中地震易损性最高的结构组件，桥梁的受损状态往往决定了公路网络的交通通行能力，因此快速检测桥梁损伤状态并优先修复公路网络中重要的受损桥梁对于提高公路网络的地震韧性具有重要意义。首先，本研究通过对过往文献的分析，结合公路交通网络地震韧性的概念与灾后应急管理的措施，提出交通网络地震韧性的新型计算方法。其次，以桥梁损伤程度最高，桥梁重要性最高和桥梁检测路线时间最短为目标，介绍了震后桥梁损伤检测动态路线优化的理论模型，通过考虑桥梁检测过程中不断更新的灾区受损信息来持续修正桥梁检测路线，达到实际检测路线最优的目的。然后，基于桥梁检测的结果，以桥梁维修过程中交通网络地震韧性最高为目标来优化桥梁维修顺序。最后，通过案例分析来模拟本方法在实际救灾过程中的应用，验证了本研究对提高交通网络的地震韧性和加快灾害应急响应和应急恢复进程的实际价值。另外，本研究对遗传算法加以改进来加快模型优化速度，以提高本模型的信息处理能力和实时决策能力。尽管在本研究是以地震救灾为背景，本模型未来可拓展至其他灾害的应急响应和应急恢复，从而制定具有一般性的基于韧性的公路交通网络灾害应急管理策略。

25223119.label: Major findings and research outcome
25223119.value: This project has developed a post-earthquake optimization model for inspection routing and restoration scheduling (OIRRS) model for highway networks while accounting for the impacts of the real-time inspection-restoration interaction on the networks’ functionality for maximizing the networks’ resilience, thereby improving post-earthquake response and recovery. The main phase of this research effort consists of the development of mathematical tools to support real-time decision making for efficient OIRRS, with a focus that multiple inspection and repair teams can be operating simultaneously. Such complex, real-time interaction problems that have been successfully modeled using mixed-integer programming algorithm proposed by the principal investigator. This research contributes to both practice and theory. The results of this study can provide support for decision makers in drafting post-earthquake OIRRS strategy for highway networks. Additionally, the proposed resilience quantification model can expand the capabilities of current theoretical resilience models of highway networks.

25223119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25223119.value: Though it is hoped that the present study will serve as a basis for further research on dynamic emergency inspection routing and restoration scheduling for post-disaster highway–bridge systems, it has some limitations that should be acknowledged. First, it utilized a deterministic optimization program; however, in support of more comprehensive recovery decision-making, a stochastic program could be used instead, to address the uncertainty associated with certain parameters (e.g., inspection and restoration times). Second, resilience of networks depends very much on their topology, and the results of the present case study were derived from a single selected network; thus, the proposed methodology could be tested using various other network topologies. Third, to save enormous calculating time, a deterministic method was used for the calculation of the probability mass function of degree of dynamism the present study; however, simulation methods, such as Monte Carlo Simulation, could be used to examine the probability distribution of network resilience under different levels and their associated probability mass function of degree of dynamism. Finally, given that the proposed hybrid GA may not be able to obtain a global optimum solution, and that the deviation from the exact solution was thus unknown, as well as that the computation time could significantly increase when larger sizes of networks are applied, more advanced solution methods that can lead to higher computational accuracy and efficiency should ideally be devised.

25223119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25223119.value: The significance and value of the proposed work are as follows. 1. Highway-network disaster recovery: The proposed resilience-quantification model will improve practical appraisal of highway networks’ post-disaster recovery capability by investigating the impacts of network-element downtime and city isolation on network functionality. Although travel time will be used as a proxy for network functionality in this model, other functionality-performance measurements can be substituted to facilitate analysis of other infrastructure networks. 2. Highway-network disaster response: The proposed real-time optimization model for post-disaster inspection routing will capture the effects of real-time damage information on the post-disaster inspection-routing problems for highway networks. Because the overall damage situation is revealed gradually over time as inspections proceed, we model optimal inspection routing based on emergency-response needs on a rolling basis. The results are then used to help generate optimal restoration scheduling. Although bridges that are directly connected with cities subjected to severe casualties are given priority for inspection and restoration in the response phase, longer-term urgent priorities such as the efficient transportation of rescue teams and humanitarian supplies can also be included in this model to facilitate comprehensive multi-objective decision-making. Lastly, although highway vehicles will be used for inspections in the proposed study, the model could equally well be tailored to inspection via high-resolution satellite imagery or unmanned aerial vehicles, if weather conditions allow. 3. Real-time interaction problems: The proposed OIRRS model will help understand optimization for real-time interaction problems of simultaneous inspection and restoration in response phase: on the one hand, optimal restoration scheduling is enhanced by real-time data on the network’s damage status; but on the other, optimal inspection routing can benefit from knowledge of moment-to-moment data on changes in network functionality resulting from restoration. This phase of our research can also be applied to other types of infrastructure networks.

25301819.label: Realisation of objectives
25301819.value: This is the completion report for project 25301819. Despite the challenges posed by COVID-19 since early 2020, we have diligently conducted research activities from 1 January 2020 to 31 December 2022. The objectives were the development and synthesis of a new series of simple, highly tunable heterocyclic-based ligands, and addressing challenging substrate transformations. Throughout this period, we explored straightforward pathways to construct diverse phosphine ligands. We developed new types of easily accessible phenylpyrazole phosphine ligands, examined in palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling of alkenyl pivalates using organomagnesium reagents (Asian J. Org. Chem. 2021, 10, 776−779), featured in a special collection for early career researchers. Additionally, we developed alkyl-pyrazole-based phosphine ligands, distinguished by a pyrazole core and cyclohexyl groups at the C3 and C5 positions, facilitating the first palladium-catalyzed chemoselective amination of chloro(hetero)aryl triflates via C¬Cl bond activation (Adv. Synth. Catal. 2023, accepted). Chinese patents were filed for these ligand types (Application nos.: 202110175011.3 and 202211730999.6) to protect the technology. For other challenging transformations, we utilized aryl and heteroaryl sulfonates as electrophilic partners in palladium-catalyzed direct α-arylation of arylacetonitriles (Eur. J. Org. Chem. 2020, 1912–1916). We also employed enol carbamates, advantageous in atom economy and thermal stability, in Kumada and Negishi coupling reactions (Org. Lett. 2020, 22, 3879−3883). The synthesis of highly sterically congested compounds was accomplished. In addition, our new ligands enabled the first ligand-controlled site-selective α- and γ-arylations of α,β-unsaturated ketones with (hetero)aryl halides, with a detailed mechanistic study revealing the effects of various phosphine ligands on selectivity (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2020, 59, 23438−23444). Remarkably, this paper was also highlighted as on the cover of the journal and as a “HOT” paper. We were also invited to contribute a Synfacts article in Synlett (Synlett, 2022, 33, 805-814). In selective coupling reactions, we achieved palladium-catalyzed chemoselective Suzuki-Myaura reaction of polyhalogenated aryl triflates (ACS Catal. 2021, 11, 7820−7827), with insights from experimental and computational studies highlighting the role of methine hydrogen and steric hindrance. Additionally, we accomplished chiral ligand synthesis using chiral HPLC resolution and studied enantioselective cross-coupling reactions. Overall, despite continuous challenges due to COVID-19, we successfully achieved our proposed objectives. Furthermore, one M.Phil. student was trained during this project period.

25301819.label: Major findings and research outcome
25301819.value: The major findings and research outcomes of this project are described as follows: During this project period, we developed new types of easily accessible phenylpyrazole phosphine ligands. These ligands were tested in palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling of alkenyl pivalates with organomagnesium reagents. This reaction encompassed a wide range of alkenyl carboxylates under mild conditions, offering a practical alternative for synthesizing multi-substituted alkenes. A communication paper on this topic was featured in the Asian Journal of Organic Chemistry, dedicated to early career researchers (AJOC 2021, 10, 776–779). We also developed a novel alkyl-pyrazole-based phosphine ligand, characterized by a pyrazole core and cyclohexyl groups at the C3 and C5 positions. This ligand enabled the first palladium-catalyzed chemoselective amination of chloro(hetero)aryl triflates via C-Cl bond activation (ASC 2023, accepted). We filed Chinese patents for these two types of ligands (Application no.: 202110175011.3 and 202211730999.6) to protect the technology. For other unexplored cross-coupling reactions, we utilized aryl and heteroaryl sulfonates as electrophilic coupling partners in palladium-catalyzed direct α-arylation of arylacetonitriles. This discovery was published in the European Journal of Organic Chemistry (EJOC 2020, 1912–1916). Additionally, we employed enol carbamates, noted for their higher atom economy and thermal stability compared to other enol electrophiles, in Kumada and Negishi coupling reactions. This research was published in Organic Letters (OL 2020, 22, 3879−3883). In terms of site-selective cross-coupling reactions, our newly developed ligands facilitated the first ligand-controlled site-selective α- and γ-arylations of α,β-unsaturated ketones with (hetero)aryl halides. This contribution was published in Angewandte Chemie, International Edition (ACIE 2020, 59, 23438–23444) and highlighted as a “HOT” paper, with an invitation to contribute a Synfacts article in Synlett (Synlett, 2022, 33, 805-814). Moreover, we achieved palladium-catalyzed chemoselective Suzuki-Miyaura reaction of polyhalogenated aryl triflates, showcasing a reactivity order of C–Cl > C–OTf. We developed a new phosphine ligand that exhibited high chemoselectivity towards the C–Cl bond, published in ACS Catalysis (ACS Catal. 2021, 11, 7820−7827).

25301819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25301819.value: The research outcomes of this project hold significant potential as foundational work for the further development of new catalyst systems. These systems can promote carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bond-forming coupling reactions. With the appropriate catalysts, we can enhance the success of these reactions and provide access to a wider range of reaction partners, both academically and industrially significant. This advancement could even provide the way for new applications in medicine and materials science.

25301819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25301819.value: This project is centered on the design and development of novel ligands to enable versatile substrate transformations. We have successfully established new catalyst systems and achieved challenging cross-coupling processes. These processes are beneficial for synthesizing potential pharmaceutical molecules, natural products, and functional materials. This discovery should serve as a fundamental model for developing new catalysts suitable for other challenging reactions.

25503919.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25503919.value: 圍墻中的安全感：天花板高度與本體性安全對于零售消費者之影響

25503919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25503919.value: Retail researchers have long focused on influencing consumer decisions. For instance, retail managers maneuver store atmospherics (music, design, lighting, ambience, smell, etc. see Baker et al., 2002) to influence consumers’ perception of the store and their corresponding behavior. While sensory elements (visual, olfactory, auditory, etc.) of retail research has been well-established, the same level of attention has not been given to factors relating to retail architecture (i.e., ceiling, flooring, walls). In this proposed study, we propose to investigate the effects of retail ceiling height on store intimacy and variety-seeking behavior. Meyers-Levy and Zhu (2007) demonstrated that high (vs. low) ceiling environments provide greater perceived freedom (vs. confinement) and orient people to process information relationally. Since then, much of this belief popularized the development of high-ceiling stores. Hence, retailers have long touted the benefits of building high-ceiling stores, which developed from the adage that building open-concept stores provide consumers with greater freedom to shop and explore. In this research program, we query whether the assumption regarding the high-ceiling effect is misguided. Despite the previously established association between high-ceiling and freedom, such construction of a retail store may not always be beneficial for consumers. Typically, consumers are predisposed to desiring control over their consumption environment (e.g., Proshansky et al., 1974; Harvey, 1976). Indeed, people have a fundamental need for ontological security; it is the concept in which people feel that their surrounding is secure and predictable (i.e., similar to how one would experience in their own home). Similar to a home, people can develop ontological security to familiar retail stores that yields comfort, safety, and trust. Here, we contend that consumers who experience loss of control may find a high-ceiling store less intimate, thus leading them to experience lower ontological security. This in turn may lead to greater variety-seeking behavior as a compensatory response. In contrast, we predict consumers in low-ceiling environments will not show the same mechanism. Findings of the research will provide a systematic understanding of the effect of ceiling height on consumers contributing to both academia and retail practitioners. We believe our findings will inform retailers on how they can better utilize their retail space to influence their customer-base. 零售研究者一直致力於影響消費者的決策。例如，零售經理通過佈置商場環境（音樂，設計，燈光，氛圍，香味等等，參見Baker et al., 2002）來影響消費者對零售商場的感知以及相關的消費行爲。雖然對于感官相關元素 （視覺，嗅覺，聽覺等）的零售研究已經取得較大進展，但零售環境中與建築物有關的因素（即天花板，地面，墻壁）卻未得到研究者的重視。在本研究中，我們將探索零售商場天花板高度對消費者的商場親近性及求變行爲的影響。Meyers-Levy與Zhu （2007）的研究指出，高天花板（vs.低天花板）的環境能夠導致更強的感知自由性（vs.保密性），並引導人們對信息進行關聯性處理。此後，這一觀念推動了高天花板商場的建設與普及。零售經營者們也對高天花板設計的好處進行吹捧，認爲營造開放概念的零售商場能夠給予消費者在購買及探索過程中更高的自由度。 在本研究項目中，我們將調查有關高天花板效應的假定是否存在誤導性。儘管先前的研究發現高天花板與自由性存在關聯，但建設高天花板並不總是對消費者有益。消費者一般都會傾向於對其所處的消費環境具有控制力。事實上，人們都具有對本體性安全的基本需求，也就是説人們總希望周邊環境是安全和確定的（即是說，和在家裏的感受一樣）。人們能夠對熟悉的零售商場產生本體性安全感，從而提升舒適性，安全性以及信任度。我們認爲，對周遭環境失去控制力的消費者會認爲高天花板的商場難以親近，從而導致他們產生較低的本體性安全感。這將進一步導致消費者的求變行爲。相反地，我們預計消費者在低天花板環境中不會產生這一結果。本研究的結論將對天花板高度對消費行爲的影響提供一個系統性的解釋，對學術研究及零售實踐都具有重要貢獻。我們的研究結論將有助於零售經營者們瞭解如何能夠更好地利用其零售空間影響目標顧客群體。

25504319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25504319.value: Loneliness is running through all segments of society including all ages and socioeconomic statuses across the world. It is not just an unpleasant feeling; it is associated with negative health consequences, and even a reduction in lifespan similar to that caused by smoking fifteen cigarettes a day. Considering the pervasiveness of loneliness and its severe negative impacts, a better understanding of how people could confront this challenge and take action to address loneliness is needed. In the current research, we raise a new possibility about tackling this epidemic: Can used products, those products that have been owned previously by other consumers, help reduce loneliness? We propose that such products can. Used products symbolically connect the consumers with previous users, that is, increase consumers’ feeling of social connection, and thus can effectively alleviate loneliness. We have found initial support for this effect with a pilot study, and will further test this proposed effect, the underlying mechanism and boundary conditions through a series of field, lab and online studies. By offering a comprehensive examination of the proposed effect, we expect to find a way to kill two birds with one stone. That is, we can on one hand find an easy-to-implement method to combat loneliness effectively, and on the other hand, increase a purchase practice that benefits the environment by saving resources and reducing waste. The current research is expected to contribute to both the loneliness literature and research on reuse consumption, and to have significant implications for society. 孤獨正在擴散到社會的各個部分，包括世界範圍內的各年齡和社會經濟階層。孤獨並非只是一種不愉快的感覺；它會對健康產生不良後果，對壽命的危害甚至相當於每天吸十五支煙。考慮到孤獨的普遍性和其負面影響，人們如何採取行動應對這一挑戰是亟待解決的問題。本研究提出一種可能的新策略來應對不斷蔓延的孤獨：二手產品（也就是曾被其他消費者使用過的產品）能否幫助減少孤獨感？我們認為這是可行的。因為二手產品象徵性地將消費者與曾經的使用者連結起來，令消費者感覺到更多的社會聯繫，因此有效地減輕孤獨。對此，我們會通過一系列的各類實驗（包括實地，實驗室，和在線實驗）來研究這一策略，以及其內在機制和邊界條件。通過一系列綜合檢驗，我們期待能達到「一石二鳥」的效果。也就是說，一方面找到一種易於實行的方法以有效對抗孤獨，另一方面可以增加對環境有益的消費，節約能源並減少浪費。我們期待本研究可以對關於孤獨感和二手消費的研究領域都做出貢獻，並且對解決相關的社會問題有所啟示。

25504319.label: Realisation of objectives
25504319.value: The three objectives of this project have been successfully achieved. Related to objective 1, we identified that consumption of used products has the potential to symbolically connect present and previous users of these products, something that may appeal to lonely consumers (“Feeling Lonely Increases Interest in Previously Owned Products,” published in the Journal of Marketing Research). We conducted seven studies using diverse sample to demonstrate the effect. Our studies operationalized loneliness in naturalistic settings (e.g., being alone in Studies 1 and 2, without a date on Valentine’s Day in Study 3, or a result of the pandemic in Study 4a) as well as in controlled settings (Studies 5–7), and we measured interest in used products across a variety of categories (e.g., books, furniture, jewelry). Related to objective 2, as we showed that used products attract consumers with the feelings of loneliness, the project contributes to the research about the value of reuse consumption. While previous research has found that givers of used products care about symbolically connecting with receivers of the products, our project demonstrated that receivers are similarly attentive to this bond and thus has implications for the marketing of used products. In another paper (“From Second-Hand to Third-Hand: Reuse and Resale Cycle,” 2nd round revision at the Journal of Consumer Research), we took a further step and found the initial purchase of a used product prompts a consumer to resell the item in the future, potentially leading to more rounds of reuse and resale behaviors by the next consumers—a phenomenon we call a “reuse and resale cycle.” Taken together, those findings provide more comprehensive understanding of reuse consumption. Related to objective 3, we tested theoretically relevant and practically important moderators. For example, we found the effect of loneliness on consumption of used products is moderated by social connection as well as by the framing of used products as given versus discarded. We also found the “reuse and resale cycle” diminishes when an intervention of undermining connection with the products is introduced, or among consumers who chronically have a high tendency to link themselves with their possessions.

25504319.label: Major findings and research outcome
25504319.value: In this project, we examined the relationship between loneliness and used products. We also provided comprehensive understanding of reuse consumption. Specifically, in the first paper (“Feeling Lonely Increases Interest in Previously Owned Products,” published in the Journal of Marketing Research), we found that consumption of used products has the potential to symbolically connect present and previous users of these products, something that may appeal to lonely consumers. Accordingly, across seven studies, feeling lonely increased consumers’ preference for previously owned products. For example, the proportion of lone shoppers was higher in a used versus a regular bookstore, lone individuals (vs. those sitting in pairs) were more likely to select a used over a new product, people without (vs. with) a date on Valentine’s Day expressed stronger preference for used products, and individual differences in loneliness during the COVID-19 pandemic predicted interest in used products. Other studies documented that the desire to symbolically connect underlies the effect of loneliness on consumption. At a time when loneliness is on the rise, the findings have significant implications for the marketing of used products and how loneliness might motivate consumers to reduce waste. In the second paper (“From Second-Hand to Third-Hand: Reuse and Resale Cycle,” 2nd round revision at the Journal of Consumer Research), we found a “reuse and resale cycle,” whereby consumers are more willing to resell products originally obtained second hand, compared to products obtained brand new. One potential mechanism that accounts for this effect is that consumers feel weakly attached to second-hand items they own. Six studies confirmed this effect across various product categories. Study 1 tracked consumers’ actual resale of the possessions they owned in real life. Subsequent studies provided further empirical evidence for the proposed effect, uncovered the underlying mechanism, and explored whether the effect diminished among consumers who chronically have a high tendency to link themselves with their possessions. The findings advance the understanding of reuse consumption, with implications for society to achieve sustainability in the long run.

25504319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25504319.value: Our project opens doors to more in-depth study of reuse consumption, which is an important topic for achieving sustainability. For example, in the current research, we focused on used products—products others passed on for direct reuse. Another type of products—postconsumer recycled products—may be influenced by loneliness in a similar way. Future research could further test this question. Another direction for future research could be testing whether and how previous owners’ characteristics (e.g., identity) and the number of previous owners (e.g., a single owner vs. multiple owners) of the used products matter to lonely consumers. Finally, this project reminds us of a more fundamental question: what can be done to promote second-hand market? Although governments around the world put effort into motivating reuse and resale, the growth of second-hand markets has nevertheless been limited. Besides the findings in the current project, other methods to stimulate the second-hand market could also carry great meaning for future research to explore.

25504319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25504319.value: Product reuse is a common environmental action that has received significant societal attention. Here, we identify one factor—loneliness—that increases interest in previously owned products. The reason is that used products symbolically connect present consumers with past ones. Considering the rise of loneliness in the recent years, and specifically over the COVID-19 pandemic, this research points out one silver lining. Feelings of loneliness may motivate environmentally conscious action via increased preference for used products. Moreover, the initial purchase of a used product prompts a consumer to resell the item in the future, potentially leading to more rounds of reuse and resale behaviors by the next consumers—a phenomenon we call a “reuse and resale cycle.” The research thus has implications for society’s sustainability in the long run.

25507519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25507519.value: On July 24, 2014, the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) published the International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) 9 for financial instruments. Effective from January 1, 2018, IFRS 9 sets a new accounting standard for the impairment of financial assets by introducing the expected credit loss (ECL) model to replace the incurred credit loss (ICL) model that has been used over 40 years. The implementation of ECL model is considered as “the biggest change ever to bank accounting” (American Bankers Association, 2016). This project is motivated by the potential significant real effect of IFRS 9 on bank behavior. According to the simulations conducted by certain banks before 2018, 60% of participating banks anticipate that the IFRS 9 would have a material impact on bank lending activities, but the direction of the impact is “difficult to determine ex-ante” (European Banking Authority, 2016). The impacts of IFRS 9 on bank lending reflect the real effects of a new standard or regulation, i.e., how an entity changes its own behaviors (e.g. decision making, investment or consumption) due to the standard or regulation change. De George, Li, and Shivakumar (2016) point out that research into the real effects of IFRS adoptions is still “in its infancy,” and Leuz and Wysocki (2016) call for more research on the real effects of financial reporting regulations. Nevertheless, because of the recentness of its initiation, there is still no evidence of the consequences of the IFRS 9 adoption. By employing a difference in differences (DiD) method, I will study the real effects of IFRS 9 on bank lending behavior in this project. Specifically, first, I will investigate the effects of the IFRS 9 adoption on loan issuing. Then I will examine the relationship between the IFRS 9 adoption and bank loan contracting items using a sample of granted loans. I will also explore the impact of the IFRS 9 on bank loan syndication structure. Last, I will test whether the above effect is contingent on two factors: the timeliness of LLR in the pre-adoption period and the strength of a jurisdiction’s legal enforcement This project shall shed light on the role of the accounting standards in bank lending behaviors. This study will also contribute to a growing literature about the real effects of IFRS adoption. This project will have policy and practical implications for worldwide accounting standard-setters, bank regulators, and practitioners. 2019年7月24日，国际会计准则委员会发布了第9号国际会计准则-金融工具。该准则于2018年1月1日正式生效，并且该准则对于金融资产首次采用了预期损失模型替代了已沿用40余年的已发生损失模型。这一变化被认为是银行会计中迄今为止最为重大的变化。（美国银行家协会，2016） 根据欧洲银行管理局的估计，60%的参与调查的银行表示，第九号准则会对银行借款行为产生重大影响，但该影响的方向性不确定的（欧洲银行管理局，2016）。对于银行借款行为的影响反映了准则变化的“真实效应”。 De George, Li, and Shivakumar (2016) 指出，对于国际准则的“真实效应”的研究依然偏少。Leuz and Wysocki (2016) 也指出需要更多的关于会计报告管制的“真实效应”方面的研究。但是，迄今为止，由于第九号准则刚生效不就，现在的相关研究仍然几近空白。 本研究应用双重差分法来研究第9号准则对于银行借款行为的影响。更具体地，首先，本项目将检验第9号准则对于贷款发放的影响。其次，本项目将研究该准则对于贷款条款的影响。再次，本项目将研究该准则对于银团借款结构的影响。最后，本项目将考察以下两种因素对于上述关系的影响：准则应用前的贷款损失确认的及时性，和银行所在地区的法律执行力。 本项目有助于厘清会计准则在银行借款中的作用。本研究还丰富了现有的关于国际会计准则“真实效应”的文献。本项目对于会计准则制定者和银行监管当局具有一定的政策启示和实践意义。
