25508819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25508819.value: The importance of online user opinions has been widely acknowledged in both business and social events. An emerging literature examines how the opinions are generated with the argument that people tend to adjust own ideas based on others’ opinions in the surroundings. However, most of the existing studies utilized the aggregated measures of prior information and replied only on structured data. The sequential pattern in online opinion generation by taking advantage of unstructured data remains unexplored. The project aims to address this gap. I focus on online discussion communities where users interact with each other by initiating or replying to a common interested topic. Moreover, the sequence of replies is highlighted such that the latter repliers will read the former ones before they add new opinions. The unique features of online discussion communities call for a deeper analysis by taking the sequential effect of prior replies into account. In this project, I extract the textual information of user replies and aim to uncover the sequential pattern in reply generation in an online discussion community. I believe that the sequential pattern takes effect beyond the aggregated measures. Deep learning techniques will be adopted for analyses. In data preprocessing, I apply text mining to quantify the reply of each topic. The reply information is measured in three aspects, i.e., sentiment, information relevance to topic, and length. The textual measures will then be analyzed by two studies. In study 1, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks will be trained to predict next reply over sequence. The model will be evaluated by test data. Moreover, the best look-back step will be selected based on the prediction performance, which will feed in study 2 to build econometric models. In study 2, I will further examine the underlying relationships among prior replies and the subsequent one. This project contributes to the literature by investigating the propagation of online user opinions from a sequential perspective, going beyond the aggregated information. The text mining analyses enrich our understanding of online user opinions. Moreover, the combination of deep leaning and classical econometric methods enables us to identify the best look-back information over sequence and further uncover the mechanisms. This project sheds new light on the user opinions in the context of online discussion communities. It informs whether the online discussion is growing as expected or out of prediction and provides the guidelines for firm managers and political officers to design campaigns. 網絡用戶論點的產生及傳播已經在商業和社會各領域中被廣泛地認可。現有的文獻提出，網絡論點的產生是基於在網絡環境中已有用戶的論點對新用戶的影響。然而，大部分的現有文獻使用了結構化數據，並且採用整合測量的方法來量化用戶論點。並沒有對非結構化數據以及非結構化數據中的序列關係進行深入研究。本項目將重點解決這個問題。 我將重點研究網絡論壇社區。用戶可以在論壇上對共同感興趣的話題提出問題或給與答復。在網絡論壇環境中，用戶的發言順序是一個重要特征。即，後來的用戶基於前面的討論給出自己的論點。這項特征使得研究在網絡論壇中用戶論點的順序相關性尤為重要。在本項目中，我會選取網絡論壇社區中用戶發言的文本數據，分析順序對用戶論點產生的影響。這種序列作用存在並且超過一般的整合測量。 我將使用深度學習技術來分析這個問題。在數據預處理階段，我會使用文本分析技術來量化每一條用戶發言。主要從三方面量化文本信息：情感度，主題相關性，和長度。文本分析結果將被用來做進一步研究。在研究一中，將應用Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)神經網絡模型預測下一條的用戶發言指標。同時，基於模型預測表現，估算出最佳預測長度。這項結果將被用於研究二中，進一步分析檢測已有發言對後續發言的潛在關係和作用。 本項目從序列的角度研究網絡用戶論點的繁衍。文本分析可以幫助我們更深入地了解用戶的論點。本研究將兼顧深度學習技術和經典計量經濟學模型優勢，在預測用戶論點的序列關係的同時，進一步分析其內在的因果關係和影響機制。本項研究將會對我們了解用戶在網絡論壇上論點的產生和傳播提供更多的理論知識和實際資訊。

25508819.label: Realisation of objectives
25508819.value: The key objective of this project is to detect the sequential pattern of online user behaviors in digital contexts, based on deep learning and text mining techniques. In my original research proposal, I mainly focused on the online user-generated content and aim to uncover and predict the sequential pattern in user opinions. Furthermore, I have extended this idea to a broader application, where I attempt to model online users’ dynamic behavioral patterns in digital content consumption. I have fulfilled the project objectives through two studies. In the first study, I and my co-authors developed a novel attention-based deep learning approach to capture the sequential patterns of online user behaviors. We empirically evaluated the model performance in a digital content consumption context, where we modeled user behaviors in digital game-play and purchase and predicted how the previous behaviors affect users’ subsequent engagement. Leveraging individual-level parameter estimates, we further demonstrated our model’s utility for conducting segmentation analysis and evaluating the impact of past behaviors on users’ future engagement. This study has addressed the first (i.e., to uncover the sequential patterns in online user behaviors by deep learning methods) and the third (i.e., to predict the subsequent online user behaviors based on the sequential pattern and examine the mechanisms) objectives. In this second study, I and my co-authors examined the dynamic pattern with a focus on online user-generated content. We used text mining techniques to quantify the information congruency along the sequence of user posts. In specific, we calculated the content similarity between adjacent user posts and further aggregated the values based on an exponential decay weight. Moreover, we evaluated how the dynamic patterns of previous user posts affect the subsequent discussions, and tried to explain the underlying mechanisms of those relationships. This study has addressed the second (i.e., to quantify dynamic pattern in user-generated content by text mining techniques) and the third (i.e., to predict the subsequent online user behaviors based on the sequential pattern and examine the mechanisms) objectives.

25508819.label: Major findings and research outcome
25508819.value: The major findings of the first study demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method (i.e., attention-based neural point process approach) in examining user behavioral dynamics. In this study, we have modeled the dynamic patterns of multiple user behaviors which may occur concurrently in digital contexts. The model was evaluated in the empirical context of a sports video game, showing its superior predictive performance over a wide range of baseline methods. Moreover, we discussed its application and generalizability to other digital content consumption contexts with similar characteristics of user behaviors, namely multi-faceted and concurrent behaviors, dynamically interacting, and susceptible to external influence. This paper provides managers and practitioners with a powerful tool for developing more effective and targeted marketing strategies and gaining insights into user behavioral dynamics. The research output, titled "Modeling Behavioral Dynamics in Digital Content Consumption: An Attention-Based Neural Point Process Approach with Applications in Video Games", has been accepted at Marketing Science. The major findings of the second study reveal the dynamic patterns of online user posts. Using the empirical data from a popular online automobile forum in China, the results demonstrate that higher information congruency among online user posts motivates shorter response intervals, more positive sentiment, and increased post volume in subsequent user engagement. In addition, we examined various mechanisms to illuminate these relationships. Our exploration of contingent factors further reveals that the effects of information congruency are more pronounced when the discussion thread comprises a higher proportion of inquiries. Moreover, the effects of information congruency vary across different phases of the discussion process. This study underscores the importance of information content and display sequence of user posts, offering valuable implications for platform designers, marketing managers, and thread creators seeking to boost trending topics in online discussions. The initial version of this paper, titled "How does Content and Sentiment Coherence Influence Online Discussion", has been published on ICIS proceedings. The full paper is currently under review at a UTD journal.

25508819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25508819.value: The first study's attention-based neural point process model, currently applied to sports video games, holds potential for expansion into other digital content consumption contexts such as streaming services and social media. This approach, coupled with real-time data integration, could enable dynamic marketing strategies and user engagement tactics. Customizable modules within the model could also allow for adaptation to various digital contexts. This expansion requires collaborative partnerships with digital content providers as well as advanced model refinement. The second study on online user posts could benefit from advanced sentiment analysis tools and cross-platform user behavior analysis, enhancing the understanding of engagement dynamics. The development of algorithms predicting and monitoring discussion threads in real-time would be a valuable asset for platform moderators and marketers, and would help broaden the impact of the research, providing deeper insights and more effective tools for understanding and influencing digital user behaviors.

25508819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25508819.value: The research project utilizes deep learning and text mining to analyze and predict sequential patterns in online user behaviors within digital environments. The primary goal is to understand how users interact with digital content dynamically in different contexts, and to forecast future behaviors based on these interactions. In the first study, a novel attention-based deep learning model was developed to predict future user engagement based on past sequential information. This approach allows for effective segmentation and targeted marketing by understanding individual behavior patterns over time. The second study applied text mining to analyze user-generated content, specifically looking at the similarity between consecutive posts. By assessing how these similarities influence subsequent discussions, the study provides insights into the dynamics of information spread and user engagement. Together, these studies enhance our ability to predict user behaviors over time, offering valuable strategies for improving user engagement and personalization in digital platforms.

25602119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25602119.value: Globally, the Internet has become an integral part of many people’s lives, especially for young people, who are the main Internet users. Cyberbullying is becoming a serious form of misbehavior among juveniles and it is a social problem of growing concern for researchers and practitioners alike (e.g., educators and social workers). Although the negative outcomes of cyberbullying have been well documented, there is a lack of research of how cyberbullying develops and of its underlying developmental mechanisms. Although a positive association between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying has been uncovered, its causal relationship is still unclear. Moreover, the mediating or moderating mechanisms of cyberbullying by individuals after being cyber-victimized are unknown. Individual values, such as moral disengagement (MD) and normative beliefs about aggression (NOBAG), are found to predict cyberbullying, while their mediating function in the cyber-victimization and cyberbullying link is lacking. School is a socialization agency for children but few researchers have investigated the protective roles of school environments (e.g., teacher-student relationships (TSR), peer supports, and school engagement) in cyberbullying prevention. Consequently, it is of theoretical and practical importance to assess how positive and conducive school environments can help children to distance themselves from the continuum of being cyberbullied and then cyberbullying others, and buffer the negative impacts caused by individual non-normative values. In addition, although young children are increasingly becoming active Internet users, most research on cyberbullying has focused on adolescents and has ignored this important younger cohort. To address these research gaps, the proposed three-wave longitudinal study aims to explore the dynamic development of primary school children's cyberbullying after being cyber-victimized. This is the first study on cyberbullying of primary school students in Hong Kong. Specifically, this study plans to explore the causal relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying. It will also examine the mediating roles of individual values (e.g., MD and NOBAG) in the cyber-victimization and cyberbullying link. Finally, it will further investigate whether these mediating processes and the impacts of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying will be moderated by school environments (e.g., TSR, peer supports, and school engagement). This study's findings will potentially contribute to our understanding of cyberbullying development in school-aged children and it will also assess the cross-cultural generalizability of existing empirical findings from Western contexts. Moreover, this study's findings could direct both future research and intervention programs aimed at protecting children in the cyber world, in which they reside.

25602119.label: Realisation of objectives
25602119.value: Globally, the internet has become an integral part of people’s lives, especially young people, who are the main internet users. Cyberbullying is recognized as a global social problem in today’s digital age, described as a type of repetitive, intentional, and aggressive behavior occurring on information technology platforms. Based on the social information processing (SIP) model, victimization experiences may lead children to feel less in control of certain situations and that their positive efforts are futile, and thus become more inclined to respond with aggression (van Reemst et al., 2014). While previous studies have verified a robust relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying, few have focused on the mechanism underlying the longitudinal relationship between cyber-victimization and eventual cyberbullying, integrating individual values (i.e., moral disengagement [MD] and normative beliefs of aggression [NOBAG]) and school contextual factors (i.e., teacher–student relationship [TSR], peer supports, and school engagement). As such, this study aimed to investigate the relationships between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying using a three-wave longitudinal design among Hong Kong children. Using random sampling from all primary schools in Hong Kong, 16 schools were invited to participate in the project, which exceeded the eight schools projected in the proposal. Consent forms were collected from schools, parents, and students, achieving a total of 1,252 Grade 4 students (age 9.38 ± 0.57 years, 711 boys and 541 girls) who completed the Time 1 (T1) paper-and-pencil questionnaire in a classroom setting in the 2020–2021 academic year, although we had proposed collecting data from only 1,011 students in T1. Despite the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic during our investigation caused the suspension of face-to-face teaching in nearly all schools in Hong Kong, the 16 schools were strongly committed to continuing their participation in subsequent surveys. A total of 1,181 Grade 5 students (age 10.54 ± 0.60 years, 661 boys and 519 girls) completed the T2 questionnaire between November 2021 and May 2022 in classroom settings. For Time 3 (T3) data collection, 1,144 students (age 11.43 ± 0.61 years, 634 boys and 503 girls) completed questionnaires between November 2022 and May 2023 in classroom settings. For each school, the time interval between two consecutive assessments was about one year. After matching the three-wave data, 988 students (age 9.38 ± 0.56 years at T1, 550 boys and 438 girls) had filled out the questionnaires at all three time points, which exceeded the number in the proposal (n = 930). To achieve Objective 1, we first performed correlational analyses to examine the concurrent associations between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying. Cyber-victimization correlated positively and significantly with cyberbullying in T1, T2, and T3. T1 cyber-victimization was also significantly and positively related to T3 cyberbullying (r = 0.16, p < 0.001). Moreover, a cross-lagged panel analysis further revealed the longitudinal association of cyber-victimization with cyberbullying. Our findings demonstrated a reciprocal longitudinal relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying, suggesting that cyber-victimization may be a risk factor for future cyberbullying. For Objective 2, the mediating effects of individual values (i.e., MD and NOBAG) on cyber-victimization–cyberbullying association were validated in each assessment. In cross-sectional data, cyber-victimization significantly and positively affected cyberbullying through MD (bT1 = 0.06, 95% CI = [0.034, 0.081]; bT2 = 0.06, 95% CI = [0.033, 0.083]; bT3 = 0.05, 95% CI = [0.028, 0.077]) and NOBAG (bT1 = 0.03, 95% CI = [0.020, 0.046]; bT2 = 0.07, 95% CI = [0.043, 0.098]; bT3 = 0.06, 95% CI = [0.032, 0.089]). Additionally, a longitudinal parallel mediation analysis showed that T1 cyber-victimization increased T2 MD (b = 0.15, p < 0.001), which further increased T3 cyberbullying (b = 0.10, p < 0.01); and T1 cyber-victimization increased T2 NOBAG (b = 0.15, p < 0.001), which further increased T3 cyberbullying (b = 0.25, p < 0.001). With regard to Objective 3, we found that the school environments including TSR (i.e., satisfaction with the relationships with teachers, instrumental help, and conflicts with teachers) and school engagement (i.e., behavioral, cognitive, and emotional engagement) significantly moderate the association between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying. Regarding cross-sectional data, the indirect effect of T1 cyber-victimization on T1 cyberbullying was moderated by T1 behavioral school engagement (b = –0.20, p < 0.001), indicating that behavioral school engagement helped reduce the risk of cyber-victimization. Meanwhile, teacher–student conflicts reinforced the association between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying (b = 0.28, p < 0.001). Notably, peer support strengthened the relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying (b = 0.05, p < 0.05). At T2, as behavioral (b = –0.17, p < 0.001) and cognitive school engagement (b = –0.04, p < 0.05) increased, the relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying weakened. Overall school engagement also reduced the effects of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying (b = –0.09, p < 0.001). Satisfaction with the relationships with teachers significantly buffered the link between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying (b = –0.12, p < 0.001). In contrast, conflicts with teachers increased the risk of cyber-victimization (b = 0.26, p < 0.001). Additionally, the relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying was strengthened by peer support (b = 0.05, p < 0.01). At T3, behavioral school engagement moderated the relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying (b = –0.11, p < 0.001). Overall school engagement buffered the negative effects of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying (b = –0.04, p < 0.05). Conflicts with teachers increased the effects of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying (b = 0.09, p < 0.001). Unexpectedly, peer support strengthened the positive effects of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying (b = 0.08, p < 0.001). Regarding the longitudinal data, T3 cognitive school engagement and T3 conflicts with teachers moderated the longitudinal relationship between T1 cyber-victimization and T3 cyberbullying. Specifically, the direct relation between T1 cyber-victimization and T3 cyberbullying was lower for children with higher levels of T3 cognitive school engagement (b = –0.08, p < 0.01). Furthermore, the interaction between T1 cyber-victimization and T3 conflicts with teachers was significantly negative on cyberbullying (b = –0.06, p < 0.05), and the effects of conflicts with teachers were significantly positive (b = 0.07, p < 0.05), indicating that there is a clear substitution relationship between teacher–student conflicts and cyber-victimization. In general, school environments play a positive protective role in buffering the development of cyberbullying, while teacher–student conflicts can exacerbate the negative effects of cyber-victimization, thus fostering the occurrence of cyberbullying. However, T3 peer support did not moderate the longitudinal relationship between T1 cyber-victimization and T3 cyberbullying (b = –0.03, p > 0.05). Therefore, how peer support influences cyber-victimization and cyberbullying needs to be investigated in the future. This study is the first to identify the mediating effects of MD and NOBAG on the relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying based on the SIP model, highlighting the cognitive factors that lead to cyber victims’ propensity to perpetrate cyberbullying in Hong Kong. By uncovering the mechanisms behind the overlap between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying, our results equip schools, families, and society with constructive recommendations toward minimizing the adverse consequences of cyberbullying and suppressing the transition from cyber-victimization to cyber perpetration. Prevention programs, including moral education and courses should be conducted and encouraged in primary schools to reduce moral disengagement of children and promote their ethical beliefs.

25602119.label: Major findings and research outcome
25602119.value: This project examined the relationships and underlying mechanisms of cyber-victimization and cyberbullying among children in Hong Kong. First, cyber-victimization had a significantly positive relationship with cyberbullying in each time point (r = 0.47–0.63), and there was a significantly positive relationship between cyber-victimization at T1 and cyberbullying at T3 (r = 0.16, p < 0.001). Second, the parallel mediating impact of moral disengagement (MD) and normative beliefs about aggression (NOBAG) exacerbated the impact of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying at every time point. The longitudinal relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying was mediated by both MD and NOBAG (indirect effect of MD: 0.02, 95% CI = [0.004, 0.031]; indirect effect of NOBAG: 0.04, 95% CI = [0.018, 0.070]). Cyber-victimization significantly predicted MD (b = 0.15, p < 0.001) and NOBAG (b = 0.15, p < 0.001). Cyberbullying was predicted by MD (b = 0.10, p < 0.01) and NOBAG (b = 0.25, p < 0.001), and the direct effect of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying was significant (b = 0.10, p < 0.01). Thus, children experiencing cyber-victimization were more likely to have higher levels of MD and NOBAG, and in turn, participate in cyberbullying. Finally, at each assessment, school engagement and teacher-student relationships can have moderating effects on the relationship between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying. Further longitudinal moderated mediation analysis showed that cognitive school engagement (b = –0.08, p < 0.01) and conflicts with teachers (b = –0.06, p < 0.05) moderated the direct effects of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying. We shared these research findings in our annual school report with all the 16 participating schools to point out their students’ development situations. We also have regular annual meetings with school principals and teachers to share our insights and recommendations for further improvement of students’ internet use and the school education and environment. In addition, we delivered two talks related to cyberbullying prevention for parents and children during the three years. Moreover, the findings were presented or will be presented at three international conferences—ؙRotterdam in August 2023, Shanghai in November 2023, and Prague in July 2024—and a public seminar for local school principals and teachers in Hong Kong in May 2024. Moreover, two research articles have been published in top-tier journals (e.g., Psychological Assessment), and two are under review. In sum, this study promotes the future development of cyberbullying research.

25602119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25602119.value: This study provides important insights into the underlying causes of cyberbullying among Hong Kong’s school-aged children by considering the mediating mechanism of individual values and the moderating mechanism of school environments. Therefore, the findings of this study provide a deeper understanding and practical suggestions for practitioners to help them develop culturally sensitive and tailored prevention and early intervention programs to break the continuum of being cyberbullied to cyberbullying among school-aged children in Hong Kong. Specifically, moral and normative beliefs education may be introduced into school curricula to nurture the moral engagement and normative beliefs of school-aged children. Meanwhile, creating a harmonious school environment with good teachers, supportive peers, and active engagement can protect students from the negative effects of cyber-victimization and help them avoid reacting by participating in cyberbullying. Future studies on the development of cyberbullying are essential to reduce the adverse effects of cyberbullying on children with different types of victimization. The Principal Investigator was awarded by the General Research Fund to conduct a research project entitled “Cyberbullying among Children with Victimization Experiences: The Role of Emotional Risk Factors and Social-Ecological Protective Factors” in 2023–2024, which is considered a continuation of cyberbullying research.

25602119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25602119.value: Cyberbullying is becoming a serious form of misbehavior among children, drawing widespread attention from educators and social workers, but there is a lack of research on how cyberbullying develops and its underlying developmental mechanisms. This study employed a three-wave longitudinal design to examine the relationships between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying among 998 primary school aged children in Hong Kong. The findings indicate that cyber-victimization positively predicted cyberbullying. Moral disengagement (MD) and normative beliefs about aggression (NOBAG) had mediating effects on the cross-sectional and longitudinal relationships between cyber-victimization and cyberbullying. Moreover, moderated mediation analyses indicated that the indirect effect of cyber-victimization on cyberbullying was moderated by school engagement and teacher–student relationships. Specifically, a higher level of cognitive school engagement can help children with cyber-victimization experiences and reduce the likelihood of their engagement in cyberbullying, while teacher–student conflicts have a negative impact on children’s growth and development, which can exacerbate the negative effects of cyber-victimization, thus fostering the occurrence of cyberbullying behaviors. The study is pioneering in the existing cyberbullying literature and contributes to understanding the long-term impacts of cyber-victimization and the development of cyberbullying. These findings provide practical implications for interventions that incorporate individual values and school environmental factors.

25604919.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25604919.value: 中國海外工廠之當地勞工管理：以柬埔寨和加納作研究案例

25604919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25604919.value: This project studies the challenges and limitations of human resources management (HRM) practices in terms of job creation, remuneration provisions and skill transfers, of Chinese firms in developing nations. Particularly in Africa, debate surrounding Chinese foreign investment and local development has focused on whether Chinese companies are socially responsible employers, instead of explaining the rationale of, and the constraints that Chinese overseas firms face in their business operations, including HRM practices that play an essential role in shaping their local development impact. From the initiation of China’s Going-Out Strategy in the early 2000s, to the latest Belt and Road initiative, attention on the impact of Chinese foreign investment on local societies has expanded from Africa to other regions’ developing countries. This project identifies what factors influence the HRM practices of Chinese manufacturing companies in Cambodia (Southeast Asia) and Ghana (Africa), and how this manifests. It examines to what extent Chinese HRM practices are endogenously driven – how much they are predominantly influenced by the economic, social and cultural backgrounds of Chinese companies, as well as their Chinese management and expatriates, regardless of their globalisation destination – and how these practices are exogenously specific to the social and cultural embeddedness of the host society, as well as how and why these practices change over time. The project findings will contribute to our understanding of the local social impact of Chinese foreign investment in developing societies, where employment opportunities and professional development are of ultimate importance for their relatively young populations; will help illuminate the intensifying connections between China and developing nations, and will fill a gap in our knowledge of the changing landscape of the global economy. 這項目硏究中國企業在發展中國家的人力資源管理實施情況，以及所遇到的挑戰及局限，包括了創造就業，薪酬待遇及技能轉移方面。圍繞中國海外投資的爭議，特別於非洲國家，一直集中於中國公司對當地社會發展是否正面以及有否履行社會責任，但討論並沒有先去真正理解中國公司在發展中國家營運的情況，包括在當地勞工管理上遇到的挑戰，要對此有深入的理解才能更好地判斷中國海外公司對當地發展所扮演的角色，以及提供有效建議。從21世紀初中國的“走出去戰略”開始到最新的“一帶一路”倡議，關注中國對外投資對當地社會的影響已從非洲擴展到其他地區的發展中國家。此項目會深入了解有哪些因素影響中國海外工廠在柬埔寨（東南亞）和加納（非洲）的當地勞工管理手法，以及如何及為何隨時間改變。這些因素一方面包括中國公司自身的經濟、社會文化背景以及其派往當地的中國管理人員之跨文化管理經驗，另一方面，當地政治社會文化因素。發展中國家的人口相對年輕，就業機會及專業發展是當地社會發展的要素，此項目調查結果將有助於我們了解中國海外投資對發展中國家實質的影響，同時亦有助於闡明中國與發展中國家之間日益緊密的聯繫，並將加深我們對全球經濟不斷變化之景觀的認識。

25607719.label: Project Title(Chinese)
25607719.value: 渉及簡要正念為本治療(MBI)對雙相/兩極情緒(BD)患者個人復元的效果機制

25607719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25607719.value: 隨著復元運動在精神健康上的興起，一個人本主義的範式轉移正在發生，當中會將焦點由功能或臨床復元（即症狀減輕或增加身體功能）轉移到個人復元上（即希望，身份和生命意義）。然而，迄今為止，很少有社會心理干預措施可以促進個人復元。在復元旅程中，患有雙相/兩極情緒（BD）的人正掙扎如何應對抑鬱和躁狂之間反復出現的情緒波動。此外，他們也試圖應對由於這些波動引起的日常生活限制。正念為本治療(MBI) 有著對改善個人復元的潛力。 因此，此研究將評估簡要MBI之有效性和機制，以幫助BD患者的個人復元。 研究將假設BD患者若隨機分配到簡要MBI，其個人復元的測量值會比分配到等候控制組的人有更大改善。此外，研究也假設簡要MBI對個人復元的益處將通過情緒意識，情緒調節和疾病接受度的改善來調節。再者，BD的特定階段也會被假設在簡要MBI的有益效果上有緩和作用，即是BD的早期階段將會於情緒意識和情緒調節上獲得更多益處，而BD的晚期階段則會在疾病接受度上帶來更多的優勢。 這個研究項目將從醫院和社區環境中招募154名BD成年人。 本研究將採用混合方法設計。研究將進行一項隨機對照試驗，以比較簡要MBI組（總共四節療程）和等候控制組。評估將在基線（T1），干預後（T2）和六個月跟進（T3）進行。此外，研究將採用名為Photovoice的質性和參與性研究方法，以進一步了解在個人復元過程中接受簡要MBI的參與者之經歷。如果研究假設得到支持，此研究結果將為一個非傳統的治療提供實證支持。此外，通過確定簡要MBI的有益效果之機制，研究結果將突顯過程中的可變因素，這些因素可以特定地讓MBI治療在BD群組中發揮更大效用。

25608919.label: Project Objectives
25608919.value: Objective 1: To evaluate the effectiveness of the dual-task (CIBT- experimental) training compared with single task (conventional intensive balance, coordination and cognitive- active control) training on functional balance and number of falls. Hypothesis 1: Both dual-task and single-task training will improve functional balance, however, the dual-task training will be more effective in reducing the number of falls. Objective 2: To identify the mechanism underlying the effectiveness of the dual-task training on functional balance and the number of falls; that is, to evaluate the extent to which treatment-related changes in the functional balance and dual-task cost of balance and cognitive performance mediate the reduction in the number of falls. Hypothesis 2: Improvement in functional balance resulting in the reduction of number of falls will be mediated by the reduction in the dual-task cost of balance and cognitive performances. Objective 3: Compare the cost-effectiveness of the dual-task and single-task training for preventing falls. Hypothesis 3: Dual-task training will be superior in terms of cost-effectiveness than the single-task training from a health-care perspective of Hong Kong.

25608919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25608919.value: Combining cognitive training with physical training to improve balance is a new approach for reducing the risk of falls in patient populations who are at risk for falls. Dual-task refers to the simultaneous performance of two tasks; that is, activities that combine cognitive demand and physical task. Dual-tasks are complex due to the great demand for motor and cognitive resources. People with brain pathology including cerebellar ataxia (CA) have difficulty in performing dual-tasks. Deficiency in dual-task performance relative to single-task performance referred to as dual-task cost is high in CA. Due to the high demands on cognitive resources, people with CA have higher falls rates during activities that involve dual tasking. Tai-Chi involves both cognition and physical movements making it a dual-tasking activity. However, our previous study on the effects of 12-weeks of 8-form Tai-Chi did not demonstrate that it had beneficial effects in reducing falls among CA population. This null finding could potentially be due to (1) the lower levels of cognitive demands of Tai-Chi exercise, (2) the intervention not being intensive enough, or (3) the intervention may not have targeted the specific symptoms of CA. To determine if adding structured cognitive demands to conventional balance and coordination training (i.e., addressing all three possibilities for our previous null findings), we conducted a pilot study (n=5) to evaluate the feasibility, safety and benefits of a Cognitive-coupled Intensive Balance Training (CIBT) program. We found that the more intensive and focused CIBT intervention reduced dual-task cost, improved balance, and reduced the number of falls in a sample of individuals with CA. Important next steps in our research program are to (1) evaluate the efficacy of the CIBT in a fully powered clinical trial, (2) understand the mechanisms underlying the benefits of CIBT training, and (3) determine the cost-benefits of this intervention. Based on the results of our pilot study we hypothesize that (1) CIBT will improve balance and reduce falls; (2) reduction in dual-task cost of balance and cognitive performance will mediate a reduction in the number of falls in CA and (3) CIBT will be a cost-effective treatment option for improving balance and reduce falls. To test these hypotheses, a randomized controlled trial (RCT) with economic evaluation will be conducted over a period of two years to evaluate the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of dual-task (CIBT) training compared with single-task (conventional balance: active control) training in individuals with CA.

25609819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
25609819.value: Abstract Hong Kong is facing ageing crisis and it sees a large number of stroke patients, accounting for about 5% of the bed use in local hospitals. Post-stroke medical problems include physical, sensory, cognitive, emotional, and communicative deficits. Research showed that about 22-60% of stroke patients suffered a dysarthria, which is a speech production deficits often include weakness, spasticity, incoordination, involuntary movement or excessive, reduced or variable muscle tone. Traditionally, behavioral management aims at restoring or compensating for affected aspects of speech such as breathing, articulation, rate or loudness. These methods could be time-consuming and costly because speech therapy are often needed for a long period of time. However, limited treatment efficacy has been reported. Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) of the brain has shown enhancement effect on motor behavior and cognitive functions in both normal and brain-damaged individuals. Previous tDCS studies have revealed its positive and promising effect in enhancing motor cortex excitability in a non-invasive, reversible, and focal way. The proposed study aims to determine if tDCS can enhance the effect of speech therapy in post-stroke patients with dysarthria. A total of 60 Cantonese-speaking post-stroke patients who are suffering from dysarthria will be recruited and randomly divided into real tDCS and sham groups. All the participants will receive individualized speech therapy based on the results of their speech assessment. For the real tDCS group, an anodal high-definition tDCS of 2 mA lasting for 20 minutes will be delivered to the orofacial area of the primary motor cortex (SM1) during speech therapy. For the sham tDCS group, stimulation given during speech therapy will only last for 30 seconds in order to cause similar sensation on the scalp as the real stimulation group. There will be a total of 10 daily sessions during a 2-week period. The primary outcome measures will focus on functional change in speech intelligibility before and after stimulation, including participant-report on communication effectiveness. Other outcome measures include acoustic and kinematic measurement, as well as self-perception quality of life. It is anticipated that post-stroke dysarthric patients will see improvement in their speech intelligibility after stimulation. The results will have high clinical value as it may contribute to the reformation of current intervention regime for dysarthria post-stroke by using tDCS as a supplementary therapeutic intervention. The result will provide important insights into the role of tDCS on functional reorganization of articulatory movement in individuals with dysarthria post-stroke.

25609819.label: Realisation of objectives
25609819.value: This was a randomized, placebo-controlled double-blinded control study investigated the effectiveness of increased cortical excitability in the orofacial area of primary motor cortex of the affected hemisphere, as facilitated by transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), in enhancing the effects of traditional speech therapy to improve speech intelligibility and speech related physiological functions in stroke patients who suffered a dysarthria. A total of 30 participants were recruited. However, many of them did not fulfil the inclusion criteria, due to personal history of epilepsy or seizures (2 people), moderate to severe aphasia and/or apraxia of speech (13 people), and very mild dysarthria (2 people). One participant who fulfilled the inclusion criteria withdrew from the study due to safety concern. Assessment for dysarthria was performed using the Frenchay Dysarthria Assessment- Second Edition (FDA-2). Screening for aphasia and AOS were also conducted. Twelve post-stroke participants with dysarthria (mean age of 58.6 ± 8.15 years) were randomly assigned by a research assistant either to the stimulation or the sham group. Both the clinicians and participants were blinded to the allocations. All participants attended ten days of treatment sessions in a 2-week period. Each session lasted for 20 minutes. In the stimulation group, individualised speech therapy was delivered along with 2mA anodal tDCS stimulation delivered to the participant’s left inferior primary motor cortex. In the sham group, 30s of stimulation was delivered under the same settings while the individualised speech therapy lasted for 20 minutes. The individualized speech therapy was tailored-made for each participant targeting their dominant phonological process and/or coordination difficulties as identified from the pre-treatment baseline data and also their primarily affected dimensions of speech (i.e., articulation, respiration, prosody, resonance and phonation). All participants completed the treatment, and one participant did not complete the second post-treatment outcome measures. The outcome measures were conducted on three separate days. For pre-treatment baseline, data were obtained within one week prior to the commencement of treatment. Post-treatment data were collected after the tenth treatment session, and one-month post-treatment to examine potential maintenance effects. The outcome measures included (1) perceptual analysis of single words, passage reading and overall speech quality, (2) acoustic analysis of a sustained vowel, and (3) kinematic analysis of rapid syllable repetitions and syllable production in sentence, (4) self-ratings on the Communicative Effectiveness Index (CETI-M) and the Quality of Life of the Dysarthric Speaker (QOL-DyS), conducted before and after the treatment. Perceptual analysis results showed that both the stimulation and sham groups had increased percentage of syllable correct and percentage of initial consonant correct, improved syllable repetition rates, and reduced short rushes of speech post-treatment, but no significant differences were found between the stimulation and sham groups. However, acoustic analysis showed that the stimulation group had significantly reduced voice pertubation post-treatment. Kinematic analysis also showed that the stimulation group had significantly improved articulatory kinematics during rapid syllable repetition. Improvement in self-ratings of communicative effectiveness and quality of life was also noted. Additionally, maintenance effect was observed in articulatory kinematic in the stimulation group but not in the sham group. Overall, the findings suggested beneficial effects of anodal tDCS over the primary motor cortex on speech production and combined tDCS and speech therapy may promote recovery from post-stroke dysarthria. Despite very strong efforts in participant recruitment through the hospitals, speech therapy unit, and different relevant community settings, the project was unable to recruit a total of 60 participants as proposed. The main reasons included 1) majority of the post-stroke participants also had some degree of aphasia (a language disorder) and/or apraxia of speech (another speech disorder), in addition to having dysarthria, and 2) the project started around the outspread of COVID-19 pandemic, which also affected the willingness of potential participants to take part in the study due to safety concern as the participants need to have their mask-off for treatment and data collection. In an effort to make the most of the study, some of the participants who were excluded from this study due to aphasia and apraxia of speech (with or without dysarthria) were invited to participate in a new side project to examine their tone-vowel interaction and coarticulation. The preliminary results showed that Cantonese participants with aphasia and apraxia of speech had difficulty in producing distinctive vowels and tones. They also showed large within-speaker variation in vowel production but reduced tone contrast, especially at the final positions. The disrupted anticipatory co-articulation between vowels as well as between tones further suggested that the speakers with AOS could not sequence segments and suprasegments simultaneously. In order to further understand the neuromodulatory effects of non-invasive brain stimulation, including tDCS, on speech motor control in dysarthric speakers, a review study was also conducted. Fourteen out of 9242 studies involving 192 participants which evaluated the therapeutic potential of non-invasive brain stimulation matched the inclusion criteria. Twelve out of fourteen (85.71%) studies suggest that noninvasive brain stimulation techniques can partially resolve the symptoms of dysarthria. However, the pooled effect size for data collected from three studies suggested limited effect of non-invasive brain stimulation techniques. Thus, non-invasive brain stimulation might be a useful tool in resolving dysarthria symptoms to a limited extent. Overall, the objectives of this project have been achieved.

25609819.label: Major findings and research outcome
25609819.value: Perceptual analyses results showed that both the stimulation and sham groups had improved performance in speech articulation and rates, although no significant differences were found between the stimulation and sham groups. However, acoustic and kinematic analyses showed that the stimulation group had significantly reduced voice pertubation and improved articulatory kinematics during rapid syllable repetition production, respectively, post-treatment. Improvement in self-ratings of communicative effectiveness and quality of life was also noted. Additionally, maintenance effect was observed in articulatory kinematic in the stimulation group but not in the sham group. Overall, the findings suggested beneficial effects of anodal tDCS over the primary motor cortex on speech production and combined tDCS and speech therapy may promote recovery from post-stroke dysarthria. The findings of the relevant pilot study are published in PLoS ONE. A manuscript reporting the final results is being prepared and will be submitted for publication in near future. The development of assessment materials for the project, including a sentence intelligibility task and a novel reading passage, were presented at the 18th Conference of the International Clinical Linguistics and Phonetics Association and the Asia Pacific Society of Speech, Language and Hearing (APSSLH) Conference 2023, respectively. The preliminary findings on people with aphasia and apraxia of speech (with or without dysarthria, excluded from the main study) documented large within-speaker variation in vowel production, reduced tone contrast, and disrupted anticipatory co-articulation between vowels as well as between tones. The speakers with AOS are suggested to have difficulty in simultaneous sequencing of segments and suprasegments. The findings of this study were presented at the 32nd World Congress of the International Association of Logopedics and Phoniatrics and is accepted for publication in Aphasiology. The review study on the therapeutic effects of non-invasive brain stimulation found that twelve out of fourteen included studies suggested that noninvasive brain stimulation techniques can partially resolve the symptoms of dysarthria. However, the pooled effect size for data collected from three studies suggested limited effect of non-invasive brain stimulation techniques. Thus, non-invasive brain stimulation might be a useful tool in resolving dysarthria symptoms to a limited extent. The relevant findings were presented at the 5th International Brain Stimulation Conference. A manuscript is being revised and will be submitted for journal publication in near future.

25609819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
25609819.value: This study has provided evidence, though limited, on the beneficial effects of anodal tDCS over the primary motor cortex on speech production and support that combined tDCS and speech therapy may promote recovery from post-stroke dysarthria. The great difficulty encountered in recruiting post-stroke participants with pure dysarthria only (without aphasia and/or apraxia of speech) may reflects the true demographic of the post-stroke population. Hence, in the future study, we will recruite post-stroke participants with different characteristics, for example, dysarthric only vs dysarthria and aphasia only vs dysarthria and aphasia and apraxia of speech vs aphasia and apraxia of speech only, to further examine the effects of tDCS over the primary motor cortex on speech and/or language production, and promotion of speech and/or language recovery post-stroke.

25609819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
25609819.value: Hong Kong faces an aging crisis, with a significant number of stroke patients occupying hospital beds. Post-stroke complications include various deficits, with 22-60% of patients suffering from dysarthria, a speech production disorder. Traditional speech therapy methods can be time-consuming, costly, and have limited efficacy. This study explores the potential of transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) to enhance speech therapy outcomes in post-stroke dysarthria patients. Despite challenges in participant recruitment, 12 individuals were randomly assigned to receive either tDCS or sham stimulation alongside individualized speech therapy. The results showed improvements in both groups, but the tDCS group demonstrated additional benefits in voice quality and articulatory kinematics. Maintenance effects were also observed in the tDCS group. These findings suggest that combining tDCS with speech therapy may promote recovery from post-stroke dysarthria. A review study on non-invasive brain stimulation for dysarthria also found limited but promising effects. Overall, this research highlights the potential of tDCS as a complementary tool to enhance speech therapy outcomes and provides valuable insights into the speech production challenges faced by individuals with post-stroke dysarthria. The findings contribute to the development of more effective treatment strategies for this population, ultimately improving their communication abilities and quality of life.

26101919.value: 精子细胞中钙信号的研究

26101919.label: Project Objectives
26101919.value: Recombinant expression and purification of the CatSper complex. Although single particle cryo-EM does not require the formation of crystals, a smaller amount of protein sample with good behavior in solution is still necessary. Since the first subunit of the CatSper complex, CatSper1, was identified in 2001, the successful heterologous expression of this complex has not been reported, perhaps because unidentified proteins are needed to assemble the functional complex or chaperone proteins are required to assist with complex folding. I will combine biochemical and biophysical methods to obtain a functional complex with high purity for structural determination using single particle cryo-EM. The first aim of the proposed project will be to obtain a sufficient, well-behaved functional sample for structure studies. A purified sample will also make in vitro functional assays possible for further mechanistic studies. Determining the CatSper complex structure using single particle cryo-EM. Unlike other ion channels, the CatSper complex is formed by at least seven subunits, in which the asymmetric pore comprises four different alpha subunits, CatSper 1-4 (Figure 1). This unique assembly feature makes CatSper intriguing and complicated, especially in the asymmetrical ion passing pore region and regulatory subunits. Compared with the whole complex, identification of the minimal functional complex may make structural studies easier. The second aim of the proposed project will be to use the single-particle cryo-EM method to determine the structure of the CatSper complex at atomic resolution, with the minimal functional complex of the CatSper ion channel determined first, followed by the whole complex. Identifying key residues responsible for ion selectivity and channel gating. Based on information provided by the CatSper structure at atomic resolution, we will be able to study pore-lining residues to identify the key residues related to ion selectivity and/or channel gating. Identification of these residues will help us understand the working mechanism of the CatSper ion channel. We can also localize disease-related mutants in the3D structure and explore how these mutants cause malfunctions in the CatSper ion channel. The linkage between these mutants and detailed structural information will help us understand the pathogenesis of male infertility and provide some hints for treatment. Gating mechanism of the CatSper ion channel. To pass the ions, the pore region of the ion channel undergoes conformational change from a closed state to an open state. According to information from the ion channel with known structures, the closed states are more stable conformations, and are usually are the first state to be captured. We will also try to stabilize protein in an open conformation, either by mutagenesis or generation of antibody that can specifically bind to an open channel, and determine the structure following a similar approach. Comparing the closed and open channels, together with biochemical and electrophysiological studies, will help us understand the gating mechanism of CatSper.

26101919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26101919.value: The influx of calcium ions into sperm cells plays an important role in regulating the hyperactivated motility of sperm, which is essential for fertilization. Calcium signaling in the sperm cell is orchestrated by the cation channel of sperm (CatSper) family proteins. CatSper is a calcium-selective and pH-sensitive ion channel that is specifically expressed in sperm. Unlike other ion channels, CatSper is a heterotetrameric channel formed by four distinct alpha subunits: CatSper1-4. In addition to these four pore-forming subunits, there are three auxiliary subunits: beta, gamma and delta (Kirichok and Lishko, 2011). All of the subunits are required for the proper functioning of the channel, although the role of each subunit is still unclear. Importantly, only mutations or knockout in the CatSper channel, not in the other reported sperm ion channels, result in male infertility in mice. Although CatSper plays a pivotal role in normal sperm function, many questions remain to be answered, including how CatSper mediates and controls calcium ion permeation, how calcium signaling is activated and regulated. And how each subunit of the CatSper complex communicates and works to fulfill its physiological functions. I would like to unveil the molecular mechanism of calcium signaling in sperm dominated by the CatSper complex and focus on the aforementioned questions. The related methods will be a combination of neural science, biophysics, and structural biology, including x-ray crystallography and single-particle cryo-EM. 发生在精子细胞中的钙离子内流，在调控精子超活化运动过程发挥着重要的作用，而精子的超活化运动则是完成受精的必要条件。精子细胞中钙信号受精子阳离子通道家族蛋白CatSper的调控。CatSper特异性表达在精子细胞中，是一个具有钙离子选择性和对pH敏感型的离子通道。和其他离子通道不同，CatSper由四个不同的alpha亚基CatSper1-4组成异源四聚体通道。除了这四个组成通道的亚基外，还有至少三个辅助亚基beta，gama，delta一起形成CatSper复合体。虽然每个亚基的具体功能未知，但他们对于维持通道正常功能是必需的。更重要地是，只有发生在CatSper通道，而不是其他已报道的位于精子上的通道蛋白发生突变或被敲除，才会导致雄性小鼠不育。虽然CatSper在精子正常功能中发挥着至关重要的作用，但是仍有很多问题不是很清楚，包括：CatSper如何介导和调控钙离子转运，钙信号如何被激活和调控，以及每一个CatSper复合体中的亚基是如何组装并且履行其重要的生理功能。我期望利用包括神经科学，生物物理，以及结构生物学（包括X-射线晶体学和单颗粒冷冻电镜）在内的多种方法研究精子细胞中钙信号的分子机制，并回答上述亟待解释的问题。

26101919.label: Realisation of objectives
26101919.value: Realisation of objective 1: We have successfully expressed CatSper1-4, pore forming subunits of CatSper complex and optimized purification conditions to obtain well behaved protein for structural studies. Meanwhile, we have obtained well behaved protein of CatSper-zeta and EFCAB9 proteins for structural studies. In addition, using CatSper-zeta as a bait, we have performed pull-down assay to purify endogenous CatSper complex from mouse sperm, and confirmed by western blotting. These results indicate that sub-complex of CatSper ion channel could be purified using recombinant system for subsequent structural and functional analysis. Realisation of objective 2: On the basis of reported cryo-EM structure of CatSper complex, we have focused our efforts on in-situ structural determination of CatSper ion channel in its native context. We have applied two strategies to pursue the near-atomic in-situ structure with details following: In the first approach, we applied cryo-ET study of Sea Urchin sperm. To clearly understand the function-structural relationship at molecular level, study the in-situ structure of axoneme without disturbing its native architectures including every piece of its components is fundamental. Under this scenario, cryo-ET is rather useful to present a larger view of the specimen in its near native condition or other conditions under physiological stimulates. The cryo-sample is prepared using isolated sperm from Sea Urchin, then loaded to 300 kV microscope for data collection. In total, 311 tilting stacks were collected under a total exposure of about 116 electrons, using dose symmetric scheme at a tilting range of ±60 degree, with 3 degree as the tilting step. 193 tilting stacks were aligned and used to generate bin4 tomograms using IMOD. The filament models were drawn out of 84 tomograms using DYNAMO on the bin4 non-anisotropic diffusion filtered tomograms. The ones that with no good specimen or with poor alignment (e.g., fiducial values which are larger than 1.4) were discarded. The 3D volumes used for sub-tomogram average were cropped from bin2 tomograms with box size of 288. The average result contains 5559 particles. From the aligned tomograms, the variation in width of each sperm axoneme is commonly observed. About 5500 particles were cropped, averaged, and contributed to the sub-tomogram average results. Particles with different width were removed step-by-step during classification. The wider particles contribute to the final volume. In the averaged results, it seems to show a 9+2 doublet microtubules arrangement. While the other particles which didn’t contribute to the final volume indicates a clear difference exist from acrosome to the tail in width and it may suggest the doublet microtubules (DMT) arrangement within axoneme from mid-tail to the very-end changes. Several different DMT arrangements are expected apart from the classic 9+2 model. These aligned particles were further processed from the unbinned tomograms, Figure 3d, with a symmetry applied on the DMT region, with a cylinder mask out the inner region. The resolution with and without applying symmetry is different, 25 Å and 8 Å respectively. In this small concept-proof case, applying symmetry didn’t work out nicely, as the intrinsic variation of the axoneme in width and DMT arrangement. The better option is to collect more tilting stacks, adding more identical particles would be the way to improve resolution. These results demonstrated the study of sperm cell structure, e.g., the axoneme, using cryo-ET and subtomogram averaging is possible. Higher resolution could be achieved by using subtomogram averaging or combined 3D single particle analysis. In the second approach, we performed single-particle cryo-EM study of Sea Urchin sperm. At the same time, we aimed to elucidate the in-situ structure of CatSper localized on the membrane of sea urchin sperm, by employing single-particle cryo-EM techniques. Freshly extracted sea urchin sperm samples were prepared on grids. From the collected movies, we could observe two distinct states: intact sperm tails with membranes and sperm flagellar doublet microtubules devoid of membranes. We hypothesized that the membrane damage observed may have occurred during the cryo-sample preparation. Owing to the regular arrangement of the CatSper channel, we decided to employ single-particle analysis to investigate the in-situ organization. Data acquisition was carried out using a Titan Krios 300 kV transmission electron microscope (TEM), with a total exposure of approximately 80 e-/Å2 per movie. The collected movies were subjected to motion correction and contrast transfer function (CTF) estimation. Initial attempts to employ automatic particle picking methods, such as blob picker and template picker in cryoSPARC, yielded suboptimal results due to the limited distribution of target particles and strong noise signals contributed by sperm tubulin within the micrographs. Therefore, we utilized GisSPA for CatSper particle picking and manually identified particles located on the sperm membrane. Following particle extraction, 2D classification was performed, revealing clear densities of protrusions from the membrane that were consistent with the expected in-situ CatSper distribution. However, due to severe interference from other proteins and low signal-to-noise ratio, it is challenging to obtain feasible results from 2D classification. Subsequent 3D classification and reconstruction were carried out based on the particle coordinates from GisSPA using a reference map, which combined a previously determined mouse CatSper density map with the sperm membrane density derived from our data (Figure Y). The atomic model of mouse CatSper was docked into the determined density map, exhibiting a high degree of congruence. Our ongoing efforts focus on enhancing the resolution of our map to provide greater insight into the structural details of in situ CatSper. Currently, we are optimizing parameters used in the data processing to further improve the resolution. Meanwhile, we are preparing manuscripts to report our findings in the in-situ structural studies of Sea Urchin sperm, which will uncover the details of sperm in the native context and refresh our understanding in this field. The manuscript will be submitted for peer review in the next couple months. Realisation of objective 3: We generated structures of individual components of CatSper complex by using AlphaFOLD and performed a comprehensive structural analysis. By docking the predicated model into the density map we obtained in objective 2, we found some very interesting results, which had not been observed in the previous study. We revealed several key residues mediating interaction between CatSper zeta and EFCAB9, and also key residues that important for channel activity and selectivity, with assistance from sequence alignment and structural comparison with other calcium ion channels. This information guided us to design biochemical assay for a comprehensive understanding of the molecular mechanisms of CatSper ion channel complex. Realisation of objective 4: To understand the gating mechanism of CatSper ion channel, we performed molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The MD analysis provided us with some clues to understand how CatSper ion channel undergoes conformational changes to facilitate ion passing. Through this way, we identified key elements that may govern conformational switching of CatSper ion channel. In summary, we have addressed all of our objectives utilizing cryo-EM, cryo-ET, biochemical and computing approaches, which facilitated our understanding of calcium signaling in sperm cells.

26101919.label: Major findings and research outcome
26101919.value: 1.We have successfully isolated Sea Urchin sperm and identified optimal conditions for cryo-sample preparation, which are prerequisites for in-situ structural determination of sperm using both cryo-ET and single-particle analysis. 2.We have obtained high-quality cryo-ET datasets and reconstructed the axoneme at medium resolution. Differences in DMT arrangements are observed along the sperm tail, indicating functional relevance with different segments of the sperm. 3.We have collected high-quality cryo-EM micrographs of Sea Urchin sperm for single-particle analysis and identified optimal strategies for data processing. The resulting medium-resolution cryo-EM map aligns well with the model, further confirming the feasibility of achieving a near-atomic resolution structure of CatSper in its native state. 4.During the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, we contributed to the development of a local platform for vaccine identification and optimization. We have elucidated the molecular mechanisms of several neutralizing antibodies that interact with the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2, providing valuable information for further optimization and potential vaccine development against a broad range of SARS-CoV-2 variants. 5.We have developed a method by applying MSBP in cryo-sample preparation to improve particle distribution and orientation. Our data shows MSBP preotects a majority of particles from the air-water interface and mitigates preferred orientation, as confirmed by analyzing various sample proteins. The use of MSBP is a simple method to improve particle distribution for cryo-EM structure determination. 6.We have made significant achievements by determining protein machineries in the DNA replication field. We have captured the structure of the human pre-replication complex, which reveals an unprecedented open state with melted DNA bound in the central channel. This work unravels an intrinsic mechanism that couples DH formation with initial DNA melting to license replication initiation in human cells. Additionally, we have revealed the dynamics of the yeast replisome by determining a series of structures at different states. Our study elucidates a mechanism inherent to the replisome that coordinates the activities of CMG and Polε to overcome obstacles such as DNA damage and epigenetic marks encountered during translocation along replication forks. 7.We have successfully determined the structure of TMEM63C, exhibiting structural differences compared to the plant orthologs OSCAs. We have also demonstrated the important roles of the coupling of TM0 and TM6 in channel activity. Furthermore, we have confirmed that TMEM63C primarily exists as a monomer under physiological conditions, while TMEM63B is a mix of monomer and dimer in cells, suggesting that oligomerization serves as a novel regulatory mechanism for TMEM63 proteins.

26101919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26101919.value: The protocol established in this proposal has yielded promising results in revealing the in-situ structure of the CatSper ion channel in Sea Urchin sperm. With further optimization, obtaining the high-resolution structure of the CatSper ion channel in its native context will provide valuable insights into the assembly of its unique arrangement and its association with microtubules in sperm tails, crucial for initiating hyperactivated motility and successful fertilization. Moreover, the strategy developed in this study can be applied to investigate other protein machineries in their native environments, which may differ from studies conducted using in vivo systems. The MSBP method we developed offers an alternative approach for cryo-sample optimization. We have proposed several working mechanisms to explain how MSBP protects protein particles from the air-water interface, but the exact mechanism remains unclear. On one hand, we are optimizing the conditions to broaden the application of MSBP for addressing other challenges in the field of cryo-EM. On the other hand, we are conducting cryo-ET and cryo-EM analyses to explore the underlying mechanism of MSBP.

26101919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26101919.value: This proposal aims to understand calcium signaling primarily mediated by the CatSper ion channel in sperm cells. In this study, we successfully isolated high-quality sperm samples from Sea Urchin and established a comprehensive workflow for studying the in-situ structure. During cryo-ET analysis, we observed a variety of axonemes in diameter along the sperm tail, which may be relevant to the functional differences of individual segments. Single-particle cryo-EM analysis revealed a medium-resolution structure of the CatSper ion channel, which fit well with the model and demonstrated the feasibility of achieving a high-resolution in-situ structure of CatSper using our strategy. Additionally, to address recurring problems in cryo-EM, we developed a novel method to improve particle behavior in cryo-samples by applying MSBP. The results demonstrated that the application of MSBP could protect protein particles from the air-water interface, thereby providing an improved distribution for high-resolution structure determination. The methods we reported here will facilitate in-situ structural determination of biological macromolecules and offer an alternative strategy for optimizing cryo-EM samples for high-resolution single-particle cryo-EM studies, ultimately benefiting the entire cryo-EM community.

26102719.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26102719.value: 腫瘤的發病率和預後在不同人群中存在差異。了解這些差異可以揭示腫瘤發生和發展的機制，從而確定人群特異的療法。腦膠質瘤是成人顱內最常見的惡性腫瘤，對比東亞人種與高加索白種人，東亞人種具有較低的發病率、更長的存活率和對標準療法的不同反應。流行病學研究表明，這種現象在移民人群中依舊存在，表明遺傳因素很可能是這些巨大差異的基礎。目前，相關分子水平研究很少。 我們最近的數據顯示，高級別膠質母細胞瘤中，MET擴增在東亞人群人（10.5％）中比在白種人中更常見（2.6％），而EGFR變異在白種人（21.3％）中比在東亞洲人中更常見（11.0％）。此外，我們鑑別了導致MET受體酪氨酸激酶癌基因中外顯子14缺失的致癌突變METex14，並與醫院合作進行了MET靶向臨床試驗，在兩例高級別繼發性膠質母細胞瘤患者中實現了部分緩解（Cell 2018）。這項研究充分表明，種群特異性變體的鑑定可以促進種群特異性靶向療法的開發。 我們假設種群特異性功能性體細胞和種系變異將影響腫瘤的轉錄程序，並且還將影響疾病的臨床過程。為了識別亞洲特異性膠質瘤分子標誌物，我們將計算研究亞洲膠質瘤的基因組和轉錄組。為此，我們將收集來自七家亞洲醫院的1000多個東亞膠質瘤的測序數據和臨床信息。其中，RNA測序信息將用來識別體細胞和種系變體的相關轉錄途徑。同時，我們將在先前報導的體細胞突變基因和表達基因組中的常見種系變體中鑑定與特定體細胞變體相關的等位基因特異性表達和轉錄失調。為此，我們具體實現一下幾個目標： •開發基於RNA-Seq數據識別功能性體細胞變異的計算策略（SYNAPSE）; •確定與種族特異性膠質瘤轉錄程序相關的常見種系變異（> 1％）; •將體細胞（目標1）和種系（目標2）變體與臨床數據（性別，存活率，級別，年齡，對治療的反應）聯繫起來。將通過在神經膠質瘤細胞系中引入選擇的變體來進行實驗驗證。 這項工作將識別與人種相關的膠質瘤決定因素，為理解發病機理和制定更合理的治療方案提供理論基礎。

26102719.label: Realisation of objectives
26102719.value: 1. Aim 1 has been fully achieved. We developed several computational methods to identify functional mutations from not only RNA-seq data but also other multi-omics data. These methods, including CNAPE and CELLO2, were either computational pipelines or machine learning methods, prioritizing several mutations in the context of adult diffuse gliomas. These methods were used in the study of cerebral cavernous malformation, recurrent gliomas, and other intracranial disorders, leading to some high-impact findings related to disease etiology and patient prognosis. 2. Aim 2 has been fully achieved. We revealed the overall profile of clinical and genomic differences between East Asian glioma and Caucasian glioma and reported that East Asian patients are in general younger and have longer survival (CBM 2022). More importantly, we identified the enrichment of the risk allele of rs55705857 in the European gliomas but extremely rare in the East Asian population. Instead, more somatic MYC gains in East Asian glioma than that in Caucasian glioma were observed (Sci Transl Med 2023). 3. Aim 3 has been fully achieved. We used somatic and germline variants to predict patient prognosis (CELLO2), and selected MYC as a key driver for the experimental study. In our study, we conducted chronic temozolomide-induction experiments on glioma cell lines and isogenic patient-derived gliomaspheres. The results clearly showed that MYC plays a significant role in driving temozolomide resistance by promoting hypermutation. Our investigation into the underlying mechanisms revealed that c-MYC, through its binding to open chromatin and transcriptionally active genomic regions, heightens the susceptibility of crucial mismatch repair genes to mutagenesis triggered by treatment. As a consequence, hypermutation is triggered. This research not only uncovers early indicators of cancer evolution during therapy but also serves as a valuable resource for precision oncology, enabling targeted interventions for managing cancer dynamics in diffuse gliomas.

26102719.label: Major findings and research outcome
26102719.value: The project led to the development of computational methods for functional somatic variant identification and prioritization, which includes CNAPE (IEEE TCBB 2019) and CELLO2 (Sci Transl Med 2023). We also revealed the overall profile of clinical and genomic differences between East Asian glioma and Caucasian glioma and reported that East Asian patients are in general younger and have longer survival (CBM 2022). More importantly, we identified and established the role of MGMT translocation in GBM drug resistance (Nat Commun 2020) and identified the enrichment of somatic MYC gain in East Asian glioma than that in Caucasian glioma (Sci Transl Med 2023). Regarding the germline-level difference, we found that the risk allele of rs55705857 reported to drive MYC pathway activity in the European gliomas was extremely rare in the East Asian population, implying different mechanisms of gliomagenesis in the two populations. To investigate the association between germline and somatic mutations, we established a website named MGSA to summarize the findings from our statistical analyses (Cancer Res, provisionally accepted for publication).

26102719.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26102719.value: Based on the current results, we will work on the following directions: 1. Investigate the role of HLA in the predisposition of somatic mutation and disease subtypes; 2. Investigate the molecular mechanisms of the associations identified by our study.

26102719.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26102719.value: We worked on a project that focused on finding and prioritizing important genetic changes in certain diseases. We developed computer methods called CNAPE and CELLO2, which help identify these genetic changes. We also studied the differences between glioma (a type of brain tumor) in East Asian and Caucasian patients. We found that East Asian patients are generally younger and have longer survival rates. We discovered that a specific genetic change called MGMT translocation is responsible for making glioma more resistant to drugs. We also found that a genetic change called somatic MYC gain is more common in East Asian glioma compared to Caucasian glioma. In addition to studying genetic changes, we also looked at differences in the genes people are born with (germline differences). We found that a particular gene variant associated with the MYC pathway, which is important in glioma development, is very rare in the East Asian population compared to the European population. This suggests that there are different ways glioma develops in these two populations. To understand the link between germline and genetic changes, we created a website called MGSA. This website summarizes our research findings and statistical analyses related to glioma. Overall, our project aimed to better understand the genetic factors involved in glioma development and treatment, particularly in different populations.
