26202019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26202019.value: This proposed project will aim to investigate the photo-alignment and polarized emission properties of cadmium (Cd) free or low Cd quantum rods (QRs) and their applications in modern liquid crystal displays (LCDs) to improve their efficiency and meet modern requirements. In the current state of the art, the LCD/OLED display efficiencies are limited to the range of 3-6%, while LCDs equipped with quantum rod enhancement film (QREF) can achieve ~8%. The down converting QRs, with their core-shell structure, emit partially polarized light upon being irradiated by the unpolarized light that can be used to reduce the polarization losses of displays. However, large-scale QR alignment is challenging. In 2015, we showed that the photo-alignment technique has a clear advantage over other techniques and offers high-quality QR alignment (order-parameter ~0.87), and recently we showed that QREFs can improve the optical efficiency of modern LCDs from 4.8% to 8%, which is a significant improvement. However, the presence of Cd because of its toxicity has come under public scrutiny. Currently, the concentration of Cd in displays is restricted to 0.2 micrograms/mm2, by the EU, and this concentration can be reduced further due to its adverse effect on humans and the environment. Therefore, it is important to find a solution that is Cd-free or that contains less Cd in QRs. The crux of this Cd-free/Low-Cd based QREF is the high quality of both QRs and their alignment in the polymer films. The new QRs should have sufficiently high quantum yield (QY) to minimize down-conversion energy losses, and high fluorescent anisotropy (FA) to secure highly polarized emission. Recently, we found that the excess of Zn in QRs shows both high QY and sufficiently high FA. Furthermore, it is essential to find maximum compatibility between the ligands attached to QRs and the polymer matrix to secure high film homogeneity; otherwise, the system shows serious QR aggregation and PL quenching. Recently, we have also demonstrated that the use of dendritic ligands can improve film quality but aligns QRs in an orthogonal direction to the photo-alignment easy axis, and further investigations are required to align QRs in the same direction as the photo-alignment easy axis. This proposed project will investigate both of these issues and explore their applicability to modern LCD backlights. The LCD backlight market size was ~US$ 45 billion in 2017, and thus the success of this project can have a significant economic impact and benefit Hong Kong.

26202019.label: Realisation of objectives
26202019.value: The InP NRs were studied in first report for the Cd-free NR option. Zinc telluride is one of the potential candidates for the cd-free NRs as one of the few potential candidates due to its suitable bandgap, we made the ZnTe rods, and TEM confirmed the elongated (rod-like) nanoparticle shape with an average length of ~17 nm, though the shape is not uniform. No photoluminescence was detected for this material in accordance with previous reports. As the photoluminescence quenching can be a result of a large number of surface defects, we tried to grow a wider semiconductor shell on top of the synthesized ZnTe nanoparticles. Considering the crystal lattice mismatch for the corresponding hexagonal (wurtzite) crystallites, the most suitable materials for this would be CdSe (~1.4% mismatch) or CdS (~4.1% mismatch); however, as our target is to avoid Cd in the system, we explored ZnSe for this purpose. The expected mismatch for w-ZnSe on top of w-ZnTe was ~6%. However, we did not achieve any enhancement of PL after several attempts to grow the shell. Moreover, separate nucleation of ZnSe nanoparticles was observed during the synthesis. Further deeper study is required to optimize the shape of ZnTe and the subsequent shell growth to secure the final material PL properties. Thus, for now, we need to resort to the Low Cd solution for the applications and keep exploring the possibilities of the Cd-free NR. Currently, we are able to reduce the Cd content below 0.18 micrograms in the device, which is smaller than the RHoS limits. In the second objective, we try to align NRs parallel to the photo-alignment easy axis. We found that the diluted T-shape ligands and the LCM-ligand interaction work significantly better. The T-shape ligands on the NR surface cannot efficiently align along the LCM easy axis. The mutually parallel alignment of the T-shape ligands modified nanorods and liquid crystal monomer, enables the fabrication of hybrid films with a nanorods concentration up to 10-20 wt.%, simultaneously retaining high brightness and polarization property. The results are published in Nano Research (J4). In the objective, we promised to develop the QREF for LCD backlight applications. The QREF with green/red emitters should be fabricated by means of ink-jet printing. In the midterm report, we demonstrated that using customized slew rate and pumping waveforms, we can print the QR with low viscosity without any problems. The proposed approach is very robust, and we were able to print QR film of various sizes with repeated optical quality in terms of uniformity and degree of polarization. In 4th objective, we have been able to make the display with color saturation of 96% BT2020 and the paper is under review. Thus, the proposed photoaligned ink-jet printed QRs with the T-shape ligands are the most qualified candidate for QREF, which can be applied in the modern LCDs. We have been able to fabricate uniform emitting film with a large QR concentration of up to 20 wt.% using multilayer printing. LCM used here works not only as the alignment agent but also, after UV-polymerization, protects the emitting material from oxygen and humidity. To demonstrate further advantages of our NRs, we printed six-inch red and green QREFs on the flexible substrates. Afterward, we assembled a display backlight unit using the QREF, and later we deployed it to a conventional LCD panel. The total (white) film thickness was ~48μm, and the brightness of the designed QR-BLU, before LCD, was ~7000 nits and ~550 nits (CCT  7657 K) after the panel, which is perfectly suitable for modern displays. Our QR-backlight covers an extended color gamut of 121% of the NTSC color triangle on the CIE1931 color space and optical-efficiency of the LCDs to 7.9%. The power efficacy of the QR-BLU-equipped display is 103 nits/W. In 5th objective, we tried to align the NRs in the patterns using the re-writable photo-alignment process using AZO dye SD-1. We have successfully demonstrated multidomain alignment of NRs and demonstrated a multi-fold security element. Later, we also aligned the NRs in continuous alignment using the holographic projection. A manuscript is submitted to the journal of Semiconductors. Later, we applied apply large electric field on these aligned NR films that breaks and show burning marks. The dielectric breakdown can be attributed to this phenomenon. The more interesting point of observation is the burning patterns. For the native ligands, the burning patterns are perpendicular to the alignment direction of the liquid crystal monomer, whereas for the TL, the burning patterns are parallel to the alignment of the liquid crystal monomer. This confirms that the alignment of NR is the driving force behind this burning effect. In other words, a great heat is generated along the c-axis of the NRs. The second observation is the burning threshold electric field is higher in the case of the TL, which can be explained using the insulating nature of the native phosphonic acid ligands. However, the insulating medium of the LC monomer is the same, thus further study required to understand the process. Later, we tried to study the heating effect for the NR material only without alignment and aligning medium. In this case, we wanted to understand how the temperature increases and how it affects the emission properties of the NRLEDs. The experimental steps are as follows. First, we drop cast the NR material on the top of the glass chip and then place this glass chip on the top of high-power LEDs. The high-power pumping LED (λmax = 456nm), which can produce a light flux of 16W, and at the same time, the junction temperature can reach 150 C. On applying current to the LED, the junction temperature increases, and so the emission wavelength changes with the time that can be described using the Varshni equation- E_g=E_g (0)-αT^2/(β+T) Here, E (0) is the energy gap at 0 K, α represents the temperature coefficient while β represents Debye temperature. The value of α for thin CdS shell NRs is 3.9×10^(-4) eV/K, for Zn modified NRs is 5.15×10^(-4) eV/K. The fitted value of β is 178 and 196K, respectively. We tried to study the change in the emission wavelength as a function of the time at various current for both native and T-Shape ligands. The emission wavelength increases with time and saturates to a certain value. Furthermore, NR with Native ligands start to break apart for the current higher than 300 mA, but T-shape-equipped NRs can sustain higher current. In fact, the NR with T-shape ligand can sustain temperature 162C at 500 mA, but these NRs also break down on applying 800mA of current. Multiple observations, first the conventional increase in the band gap, but local temperature is higher than the LED junction temperature. Moreover, the heating rate for longer rods is higher than the smaller rods, however, overall increase in the temperature is less for the longer rods, that might be due to heat radiating properties related to the same. Thus, we can conclude that the material shows anisotropic conductivity and quantitative study needs to define it. We are developing new experimental setups to study these properties and will also apply for another research grant to perform these studies.

26202019.label: Major findings and research outcome
26202019.value: We found that we can improve the alignment quality of the Quantum rods (QR) films in the liquid crystal polymer matrix using the anisotropic ligands and also increases the acceptable material load in the liquid crystal polymer matrix. It is essential for these QRs, which can now be used in the display. The second important outcome of the project is quantum rods in the full visible range. We also found that the Zn doping process works well for the CdS/CdSe-based QRs and can produce repeatable Quantum rods in the visible spectrum with wurtzite crystals lattice. The wurtzite crystals lattice is essential for the polarized emission. We showed the QRs in the full visible range with sufficiently high PL quantum yield. Later, we aligned these quantum rods using ink-jet printing on the photoaligned PET substrate with good optical quality and a high degree of polarization. We made quantum rod enhancement films and deployed them on the LCD. These LCDs show significant enhancement in LCD optical efficiency that increased by twofold. In the last segment of the project, we studied the micropatterning of the quantum rod alignment. We successfully demonstrated the binary and continuous alignment of quantum rods equipped with specially designed anisotropic ligands. We have also studied the thermal conductivity of the aligned quantum rod films and confirmed, though qualitative, that the aligned quantum rod films show anisotropic thermal conductivity. We further found some local heating effect in these quantum rods, which strongly depends on the ligands, material composition, and size of the quantum rods. We need to study this phenomenon further. The project has been successfully completed, producing 33 publications (Invited talks-10, Journal Papers- 10, and Conference paper-15) and three awards. Additionally, some of the new results were patented, and later we started a startup company to commercialize the achieved results. Two students were primarily trained during the project. One of the two trained students is joining the startup company to commercialize his learning from the project. The second student is joining a big firm in Sep 2023. Another student who has been partially trained during the project will contribute to work on the thermal properties of the aligned quantum rod films.

26202019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26202019.value: We aligned the QRs in the pattern in both binary and continuous alignment and also studied the anisotropic nature of the thermal conductivity. We confirmed that the thermal conductivity shows anisotropic behavior; however, we observed multiple processes. First, the conventional increase in the band gap, but the local temperature is higher than the LED junction temperature. Moreover, the heating rate for longer rods is higher than the smaller rods. However, the overall increase in the temperature is less for the longer rods, which might be due to heat-radiating properties related to shape and size. This behavior indicates that the thermal properties are showing more complex phenomena that strongly depend on material composition, shape, ligands, and quantum rod orientation. Thus, we can conclude that the material shows anisotropic thermal conductivity, but more study is needed to quantitively study the anisotropy of the thermal properties of these QRs. We are developing new experimental setups to study these properties and will also apply for another research grant to perform these studies.

26202019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26202019.value: Moder display efficiency ranges between 3-5 % depending on the resolution and drops below 2% for the high pixel density displays. Both LCD and OLED use polarizers that incur more than 50% loss of optical energy. The nanorods emit polarized light; therefore, the aligned nanorods emit films can reduce the polarisation losses and improve the Display efficiency. The outcome of the project established the fact that aligned nanorods can double the efficiency of the display. The project outcome illustrates the method of nanorod alignment, new nanomaterial, and device. The project also elaborates on new strategies to pattern-align nanorods in an innovative way using the holographic project, which we can use for security applications.

26202319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26202319.value: Urban areas experience higher temperatures than the rural areas that surround them. This is known as the urban heat island effect and has adverse implications for energy demand, air quality, and resident health in cities. Waste heat emissions from vehicles comprise a substantial portion of the human-induced urban heat, and they are the dominating factor in forming heat islands over compact built-up areas with high vehicular flows. The higher energy efficiency of electric vehicles (EVs) than internal combustion engine vehicles (ICEVs) offers a potential strategy for urban heat mitigation. Generous government subsidies in recent years have boosted the global EV market from 0.3 million in 2012 to 3.1 million in 2017. This massive increase in the number of EVs can significantly alter the urban thermal environment, as transportation activities are concentrated in cities. The potential benefits of EVs for urban thermal environment include decreased temperature, enhanced pedestrian thermal comfort and reduced building cooling demand. In addition, the shift to EVs facilitates the advance of automated driving and vehicle sharing systems, which brings further benefits if saved parking spaces are to be converted into green infrastructure. Although the aforementioned benefits are crucial for urban developments, the majority of EV studies focuses on hardware technologies, life-cycle carbon emissions, and policy options. The proposed project will be the first attempt to quantify the potential benefits of EV adoptions on the urban thermal environment. First, we will study the modifications made by EVs and ICEVs to mass and heat transport in the complex urban environment. Second, we will integrate vehicle impacts into urban climate modeling. Combined with high-resolution traffic data, the new model will be capable of realistically assessing the impact of vehicle heat at the city scale. Third, we will quantify the effects of EVs on urban ambient temperature, pedestrian thermal comfort and building energy consumption. In particular, the conversion of unused parking lots to green spaces will be investigated as one potential co-benefit of EV adoptions. Hong Kong is one of the most densely built cities with large traffic volumes and strong urban heat islands. We will use Hong Kong as an example to demonstrate how EVs can assist the development of a sustainable urban thermal environment. In the proposed project, we will integrate environmental science, atmospheric science, and engineering technology in an interdisciplinary manner. The results will provide insight into human-environment interactions along the development of cities. 城市熱島效應是指城市區域氣溫顯著高於其週邊郊區的現象，此現象會對城市的能源需求、空氣質量和居民健康產生不利影響。其中，機動車排放的廢熱在城市人為熱排放中佔有很大比例，是車流量大的緊湊建築群區域中形成熱島效應的主要因素。因此，高能效的電動汽車相比於傳統的內燃機汽車為城市熱島提供了潛在的緩解策略。在近年來政府的大力補貼下，全球電動汽車市場從2012年的30萬增加至2017年的310萬。由於交通運輸活動集中在城市區域，電動汽車數量的大幅增漲可顯著改變城市的熱環境。電動汽車對城市熱環境的潛在效益包括降低氣溫，提高行人的熱感舒適度以及減少建築製冷需求。此外，內燃機汽車向電動汽車的轉變將促進自動駕駛和共享汽車行業的發展。在此基礎上如果將節省的停車位轉變為綠色基礎設施，可為城市熱環境帶來更大的效益。上述電動汽車的益處對城市發展至關重要，然而迄今為止大多數與電動汽車相關的研究都側重於硬件技術，生命週期碳排放和政策選擇。 本項目擬首次量化電動汽車對城市熱環境的潛在效益。首先，本項目將研究電動汽車和內燃機汽車對複雜的城市環境中物質和熱量傳輸的影響。其次，不同汽車的影響將被整合嵌入到城市氣候模型中。結合高分辨率的交通資料，新模型將能夠真實地評估在城市尺度下車輛熱排放的影響。最後，本項目將量化電動汽車對城市環境溫度，行人熱感舒適度和建築能耗的影響。值得注意的是，本項目將未使用的停車場轉換為綠化空間視為電動汽車的潛在效益之一。香港作為交通最為繁忙、建築最為密集的城市之一，它的熱島效應非常顯著。因此，本項目將以香港為案例，論證電動汽車如何協助構建可持續發展的城市熱環境。此項目的跨學科式研究包括環境科學，大氣科學和工程技術，其研究成果將對城市發展中人與環境交互作用提供更加深入的瞭解。

26202319.label: Realisation of objectives
26202319.value: The proposed project objectives have been achieved. As a result, the project team has published five top journal articles and three conference presentations. One PhD student developed her PhD thesis from this project and graduated in 2023. Objective 1. Simulate the dispersion of waste heat emissions from vehicles in the urban environment, and analyze its variability with respect to canyon geometry and vehicle density. We have successfully set up a guidance for simulating the dispersion of waste heat and pollution released from vehicles in street canyons using Fluent. The CFD simulation results with the incorporation of vehicles have been systematically evaluated against wind-tunnel measurements. Two-lane traffic moving in the opposite direction insignificantly affects the mean pollutant concentration and heat dispersion inside the canyon, and traffic moving in the same direction has a strong influence. With one-way traffic at the density of 20 vehicles/min and 30 vehicles/min, the net flow rate towards the outside of the street canyon is observed at the lateral opening downstream of the traffic direction. When the density of one-way traffic reduces to 15 vehicles/min, the net flow rate at the lateral opening downstream of the traffic direction is towards the inside of the street canyon, owing to the weak traffic motion. Objective 2. Integrate vehicle impacts into urban climate models, and estimate the influence of vehicle-released waste heat at the city scale. We have successfully implemented fine-resolution vehicle waste heat data into urban climate simulations at the city scale over Hong Kong. Results show a strong temporal variation of the vehicle heat impact at daily, weekly, and seasonal scales: 1) the warmth of urban canyon air temperature is stronger and more consistent at night than in daytime, 2) temperature increments are more pronounced during weekdays than weekends, 3) temperature change in winter is larger than that in summer. Mean 2-m urban air temperature increases by 0.35 °C in winter and by 0.32 °C in summer over the vehicle heat emission area. Increased air temperature over the land area by vehicle heat correlates with urban area fraction and building height positively, and dominates in low urbanized areas with highways and circulation roads. Objective 3. Quantify the potential benefits of electric vehicles on urban ambient temperature, pedestrian thermal comfort and building energy consumption. We have successfully developed scenarios of electric vehicle adoption in Hong Kong and its impact on parking spaces if incorporated with the automated driving technology. Under the future climate, the urban air temperature will increase by 0.90 °C in January and 1.47 °C in July by 2050 in Hong Kong. In winter, EV adoption can offset 25.5% of the global warming signal at the city scale, and the benefit is most distinct during the evening. However, EV adoption provides less cooling in summer when the global warming signal is more evident. By saving parking spaces and converting them into outdoor green spaces, the carsharing system can provide additional cooling benefits only during the evening rush period in winter.

26202319.label: Major findings and research outcome
26202319.value: We first developed a numerical setup guidance for computational fluid dynamics (CFD) studies considering moving traffics in the urban environment (Zheng and Yang, 2021). Then we investigated the impact of traffic direction, traffic density, and background wind speed on the mechanism of heat and pollutant dispersion in an urban street canyon (Zheng and Yang, 2022). Only traffic moving in the same direction strongly modify the wind flow and subsequently heat and pollutant dispersion, especially under a low approaching wind speed. Utilizing the vehicle heat (VH) data derived from the Transport Department of Hong Kong, we quantified the spatiotemporal impact of VH at a fine resolution under the current climate (Chen et al., 2021). Results suggest that increased air temperature over the land area by VH has a positive correlation with urban area fraction and building height. Vehicle heat plays a dominative role in warming low urbanized areas with highways and circulation roads. In the end, we examined the cooling benefit of EV adoption and its combination with the carsharing system under future climates using numerical weather simulations (Chen and Yang, 2022). We found that over Hong Kong, EV adoption can offset 0.23 °C of future warming in January at the city scale, but provides negligible benefits during the summer. The spatial extent of the EV benefit is also larger in winter than in summer. We also investigated the modification of urban road network design on residents’ exposure to traffic pollutants (Zheng and Yang, 2023). All reserach output are listed in Part C.

26202319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26202319.value: The scientific knowledge and modelling techniques obtained from this project has infused new insights into the influence of anthropogenic activities on urban microclimate over complex terrains. The findings have contributed to the development of a new project that focuses on the vertical profile of meteorological variables in typical urban neighbourhoods, which is funded by NSFC.

26202319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26202319.value: Heat emission by traditional vehicles with internal combustion engines is one major component of the anthropogenic heat release in the urban environment. With high efficiency electric motors, electric vehicles (EVs) can substantially reduce the waste heat emission from traffic in cities. This project is the first study that quantifies the potential benefits of EV adoptions on the urban thermal environment, using Hong Kong as a testbed. Under the current climate, the vehicle-induced warmth of urban canyon air temperature is stronger and more consistent at night, during weekdays, and in wintertime. Dispersion of vehicle heat in the urban environment will be strongly affected by traffic moving in the same direction, especially under a low wind speed. Under the future climate, EV adoption can offset about 25% of the global warming signal in Hong Kong during wintertime, but provides much less cooling in summer. Meanwhile, EV adoptions allow the conversion of unused parking lots to outdoor green spaces, which can provide additional cooling benefits only during the evening rush period in winter.

26203619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26203619.value: Three-dimensional (3D) whole-organ imaging with microscopic resolution is an ideal tool to analyze disease-induced structural changes as features can be interpreted across different length scales, from organelles to organs. However, the fundamental trade-off between spatial resolution and imaging depth causes difficulty in implementing this ideal imaging tool. In recent years, the integration of mechanical sectioning or chemical tissue clearing with optical microscopy has provided a solution to this problem. Yet, the majority of previously reported 3D imaging techniques require lengthy and specialized sample preparations and staining to visualize an entire organ, hindering the applicability of these techniques in medicine and the life sciences. For example, the diffusion staining of a whole brain is an extremely slow process due to the scant extracellular space in the central nervous system. Any label-free imaging technology that can provide a superior imaging contrast of different biomolecules will address this critical need. To this end, we developed a 3D whole-organ imaging device, a microtomy-assisted photoacoustic microscopy (mPAM) system (recently reported in Nature Communications). The mPAM system takes advantage of the intrinsic optical absorption contrast of different biomolecules, enabling high-contrast subcellular imaging of a whole organ. By integrating with a microtome, the mPAM system images an entire organ at subcellular resolution. To further improve the imaging specificity and sectioning quality, mPAM can be upgraded in two ways: by chemically removing the “background” signals (e.g., lipids) and by using a vibratome, which is ideal for soft tissue. The upgraded system has been named clearing and vibratomy-assisted photoacoustic microscopy (cvPAM). Because light can penetrate more deeply due to tissue clearing, cvPAM requires less tissue sectioning, hence shortening the data acquisition time. The cvPAM system will provide 100% specific endogenous natural staining, enable high-speed and high-quality whole-organ imaging, and potentially identify novel cells or features of an organ. The proposed project will develop the next generation of mPAM (i.e., cvPAM) for high-speed, high-quality, and high-specificity whole-organ imaging. The first step is to implement the cvPAM system with a vibratome. cvPAM will then be used to scan organs with and without tissue clearing. The two sets of images will be compared. The “cleared” whole-organ volumetric image could potentially provide new insights into organ features. At the later stages of the project, the organs with different diseases will be scanned by our cvPAM system to analyze disease-induced structural changes, such as those seen in Alzheimer’s disease. 具有微觀分辨率的三維（3D）全器官成像是分析疾病誘發的結構變化的理想工具，因為特徵可以在不同長度範圍內解釋 - 從細胞到器官水平。然而，空間分辨率和成像深度之間的基本權衡導致難以實現這種理想的成像工具。近年來，機械切片或化學組織清除與光學顯微鏡的整合為這種科學追求提供了解決方案。然而，大多數先前報導的3D成像技術需要冗長且特殊的樣品製備和染色以使整個器官可視化，妨礙它們在醫學和生命科學中的應用性。例如，由於中樞神經系統中的細胞外空間不足，全腦的擴散染色是非常緩慢的過程。 顯然，任何能夠提供不同生物分子的卓越成像對比度的無標記成像技術都將滿足這一關鍵需求。為此，我的小組去年在<<自然·通訊>>報導了一種稱為微切片輔助的光聲顯微鏡（mPAM）的3D全器官成像裝置。 mPAM利用不同生物分子的固有光學吸收對比度的優勢，實現整個器官的高對比度細胞成像。 mPAM與切片機結合，使我們能夠以細胞分辨率成像整個器官。為了進一步提高成像特異性和切片質量，mPAM可以在兩個方面進行升級 - 化學去除“背景”信號（脂質），並使用振動切片機（適用於軟組織）實施mPAM。升級的mPAM被命為清除和振動輔助光聲顯微鏡（cvPAM）。由於組織清除導致光線更深，cvPAM需要更少的組織切片，因此縮短了數據採集時間。 cvPAM將定位於（1）提供100％特異性內源性自然染色，（2）實現高速和高質量的全器官成像，和（3）潛在地識別器官中的新細胞/特徵。 擬議的項目將開發下一代mPAM（即cvPAM），用於高速，高質量和高特異性的全器官成像。第一步是使用振動切片機實現cvPAM系統。然後將cvPAM用於掃描沒有和有組織清除的器官。將比較兩組圖像。 “清除的”全器官體積圖像可能為我們提供有關器官特徵的新見解。在後期階段，我們的cvPAM系統將掃描具有不同疾病的器官，以分析一些疾病誘發的結構變化（例如，阿爾茨海默病）。

26203619.label: Realisation of objectives
26203619.value: [Objective 1]: For the proposed clearing and vibratomy-assisted photoacoustic microscopy (cvPAM) imaging system, we have used a diode-pumped Q-switched ultraviolet (UV) laser (WHF-266nm, Bright Solutions, 20 kHz pulse repetition rate) to predominantly excite DNA/RNA in the tissue by generating pulses at a wavelength of 266 nm. The laser beam is first spatially filtered by a pair of lenses and a pinhole and illuminates an organ from the top after passing through a ring-shaped focused ultrasonic transducer which is the detector of the generated PA waves. An organ (e.g., a mouse brain) that is either formalin-fixed or fresh, paraffin- or agarose-embedded, and with or without tissue clearing can be mounted on an organ holder immersed in water. The tissue is then automatically imaged under computer control. The 3-axis motorized stage controls both the scanning for imaging and the tissue sectioning by a vibratome which ensures high-quality soft tissue sectioning. The cvPAM system automatically records and displays the cross-sectional images (e.g., coronal sections of a mouse brain) in real-time during data acquisition. The exposed top tissue surface is imaged, then a thin layer will be shaved off, and the new surface will be imaged. This sequence will be repeated to obtain the 3D image. Tissue clearing allows the laser beam to travel deeper into the tissue (e.g., up to 60 μm), shortening the data acquisition time for multilayered scanning. The cvPAM’s lateral resolution is ~0.8 μm, which is more than sufficient to image individual cell nuclei without labeling. [Objective 2]: One common problem in PAM is its low specificity. UV light at 266 nm is absorbed by many biomolecules, including DNA/RNA, hemoglobin, and lipids. In particular, there are two ways to tackle this problem, either by optical or chemical approaches. In this project, we have focused on solving this problem with a chemical approach, namely tissue clearing. As there are numerous tissue-clearing approaches, we have tried several of them, e.g., (i) immunolabeling-enabled three-dimensional imaging of solvent-cleared organs (iDISCO), (ii) clear, unobstructed brain imaging cocktails and computational analysis (CUBIC), etc. Note that these two mentioned approaches have demonstrated high efficiency in washing out lipids while retaining the integrity of the tissue. To test the effect of tissue clearing, two similar types of organs with and without clearing have been imaged. The two sets of images have been compared to validate the effectiveness of the tissue-clearing approach for cvPAM. According to our results, CUBIC is the best option. First of all, CUBIC is able to wash out lipids effectively, hence, improving the imaging contrast and specificity with cvPAM. Second, with CUBIC tissue clearing, the tissue is still soft and suitable for sectioning with vibratome, whereas, with iDISCO and many other tissue clearing methods, the tissue becomes fragile and cannot be cut with vibratome or microtome. As a result, only CUBIC allows whole-organ imaging using cvPAM. Third, CUBIC greatly improves tissue transparency, thus, allowing us to image deeper into the tissue and multilayered tissue imaging. In short, we successfully benefit from both advantages simultaneously with tissue clearing: (i) deep tissue imaging and (ii) high-specificity subcellular whole-organ imaging. [Objective 3]: We have compared two sets of images, taken before and after tissue clearing, which have been validated with mouse brain, kidney, and heart tissues. A tissue slice without tissue clearing is first imaged using the proposed cvPAM system. Then, the tissue slice was optically cleared using the aforementioned approaches (e.g., iDISCO or CUBIC), and subsequently imaged again with cvPAM. Afterward, the two sets of images were compared both qualitatively and quantitatively. As expected, because of the background signal removal (i.e., removal of lipids), cvPAM successfully revealed cell nuclei that cannot be visualized originally without tissue clearing (e.g., for kidney and heart tissues). Also, according to our results, we found that the contrast-to-noise ratios (CNRs) of cell nuclei are improved by 3–5 times, depending on the tissue types, which is highly encouraging and greatly improves the specificity of PAM. [Objective 4]: We have optimized the parameters for the system design and tissue-clearing approach for the cvPAM system. We have applied it to image different biological tissues with or without tissue clearing. According to our results, the cvPAM could potentially be a powerful universal 3D whole-organ imaging tool. We have used cvPAM to image several types of tissues, including the brain, kidney, and heart. With optical clearing, cvPAM consistently provides a much higher quality of cellular imaging for different types of tissues. Surprisingly, the use of optical clearing with kidney tissues is probably the best as we could reveal the cells that are originally invisible under PAM imaging, which are then clearly identified with cvPAM and closely resemble histologically stained images in clinical practice. This image similarity enables our images to be easily understood by medical professionals and can bring insights to biomedical applications (e.g., for the study of diseases).

26203619.label: Major findings and research outcome
26203619.value: There are multiple important findings and research outcomes in this proposal, which are listed below: 1. We successfully implemented a high-speed photoacoustic imaging system (references 1 and 3). We have shown that it is possible to image a biological tissue with a size of 5 mm × 5 mm (a typical size of a tissue biopsy) within 15 minutes. 2. We tested that it is possible to use deep-learning algorithms to transform 2D unstained/ stained images to histological style, which can then be easily interpreted by medical professionals (references 4–6 and 9). We have shown that our virtually stained images can closely resemble the histologically stained images that medical professionals are used to, ensuring that our images can be used easily. 3. We designed a high-quality imaging and sectioning system with full automation (reference 7). We have shown that it is possible to image the entire 3D tissues with fully automated imaging and sectioning capability. The imaging resolution is ~1 μm. The sectioning thicknesses can be a few μm for microtome sectioning, and about 50 μm for vibratome sectioning. 4. Two review papers are written and published in this related direction (references 2 and 8).

26203619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26203619.value: In this project, we have successfully demonstrated that the proposed clearing and vibratomy-assisted photoacoustic microscopy (cvPAM) imaging technique can generate high-quality PAM images (in terms of imaging contrast, specificity, and resolution) of unlabeled biological tissues. The organs that we used in this project are mainly the brain, kidney, and heart tissues. This research project outcome can be further expanded to other types of organs or disease models to enable us to better understand the complex connections and disease-induced structural changes of an organ. In addition, the label-free imaging property will ensure that all the biomolecules can be probed with their intrinsic fingerprints, avoiding situations where biomolecules are not labeled effectively with dyes. As a result, all the 3D whole-organ images from cvPAM will be of high fidelity, potentially allowing us to find out new connections in an organ.

26203619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26203619.value: To better understand the complex connections and disease-induced structural changes of an organ, visualizing the three-dimensional (3D) anatomical structure of an entire organ with high resolution is vitally important. Conventional 3D whole-organ imaging in clinical settings can be obtained only by registering images of all sectioned and thin histology slices, which individually can only provide information about a single-layered tissue (~7 µm). However, despite considerable rectification efforts in the field, each registration step is subjected to a different level of inaccuracy, preventing us to understand the organ in 3D with high accuracy. In addition, sectioning before imaging can also cause undesired tissue ruptures in each thin slice, further reducing the quality of registered images. Here, we proposed a new imaging approach with tissue clearing, terms clearing and vibratomy-assisted photoacoustic microscopy (cvPAM), which can address the aforementioned issues, while providing high-specificity, high-speed, and high-quality whole-organ imaging. Our results show that the label-free imaging contrast and quality can be significantly improved after tissue clearing. With the cleared tissue, multilayers of cell nuclei can also be extracted from the PA signals with a single raster scan, hence, providing rich 3D information about complex connections and disease-induced structural changes of organs in a time-efficient manner.

26206419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26206419.value: To ease analysis for complicated service queueing systems that involve a large amount of stochasticity, it is customary in the queueing literature to assume that the system's primitives (such as the arrival processes, service times, patience of different customers, etc.) are independent of one another and of the system’s dynamics and state. In many practical settings, however, dependencies across different primitive processes, or between a primitive process and the state of the system, should clearly hold. For example, it stands to reason that, in service systems such as call centers, hospitals and restaurants, customers’ service requirements should depend on that their patience, or on the time that they spend waiting in a queue for service, or on their valuation for the service. It is then natural to ask, to what extent do these types of dependencies affect the performance, control, pricing and optimal design of a service system? Answering this question is crucial for the optimal planning of the service sector, which is the most dominant sector in Hong Kong, having contributed to 92.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2016. In the health sector, with a reported expenditure worth of 137 billion HKD in 2014, these dependencies are observed in various locations in hospitals. For example, it has been shown that patients’ length of stay in intensive care units (ICU) increases with the delays they experience before admission to the ICUs. Similar dependencies are reported in the food service industry, where sales hit a record 128 billion HKD in 2014. In restaurants, it has been that the dining times may depend on the amount of time diners spend waiting to be given a table. Despite such evidence of dependencies in the service sector, it is unclear how these dependencies affect the performance of service systems. The purpose of this research is to develop queueing models that are faithful to reality, while keeping the analysis simple enough to allow easy use in practice. As will be demonstrated in this research, these dependencies can have considerable impacts on key performance measures, and therefore on the optimal staffing, control, and design of a system. In particular, even a moderate dependence may render quantitative results from “standard” models (with no such dependence) highly inaccurate. Further, qualitative analysis and insights from standard models do not necessarily carry over to systems with dependence. Therefore, the proposed research will have profound impacts on the service industry. 现实生活中的排队系统往往非常复杂，并且伴随着很大程度的不确定性。为了简化分析，排队论的文献通常假设构成这些排队系统的关键部分（比如顾客的到达过程，顾客的服务时间，顾客在排队等候过程中的耐心程度等等）都是相互独立的，而且不依赖于系统的现实状态。然而，在很多现实场景中，排队系统的各个部分往往是相互关联的，而且依赖于系统的现实状态。比如，在电话客服系统，在医院，在餐馆等等，顾客的耐心程度很有可能与顾客预计需要的服务时间相关，而顾客的实际服务时间又跟他们排队等候的时间相关。那么，在这种情况下，这些可能存在的相关性会怎么影响服务排队系统的具体表现和最优设计呢？ 回答上述问题对香港服务业的顶层设计至关重要。服务业是香港最重要的支柱产业，2016年92.2%的生产总值来源于此。在这其中，医疗产业贡献了1370亿港元的支出，而医院里多处场景都观测到排队系统的相关性。比如，有研究表明，重症监护室病人的治疗时间与他们转至重症监护室接受治疗之前的等候时间有正相关性。餐饮业是另一大产业，2014年的营业额达到了历史性的1280亿港元。餐饮业也观测到类似相关性，有研究表明，顾客的用膳时间与顾客排队等候的时间有负相关性。 尽管实证研究验证了不同行业的排队系统中都存在不同程度的相关性，刻画这些相关性如何影响系统表现的研究却是少之又少。这个项目即是通过建立与现实相符的模型来研究这些相关性，同时确保研究成果具有可行性。初步结果表明，系统中的相关性可以对系统的关键指标（比如队长，顾客的等候时间）有显著影响，进而影响系统的最优设计（比如雇人多少，如何区别顾客进行分类服务）。这意味着，即使程度适中的相关性，也足以使得常用的标准模型（没有相关性）的预测结果高度失真，使得标准模型得到的管理经验不再适用。因此，这个项目的成果将对服务业的排队系统影响深远。

26206419.label: Realisation of objectives
26206419.value: 1. To demonstrate that dependencies in service systems can have substantial impacts on relevant performance measures and therefore, on the management of service systems. This objective is fully achieved. The PI has rigorously demonstrated in his research that dependencies in service systems can have significant impacts on key performance measures such as the system’s expected throughput and queue length, as well as on management of service systems such as staffing, scheduling, and pricing. In the research output “When Service Times Depend on Customers’ Delays: A Relationship Between Two Models of Dependence” (J1), the PI shows that treating the stochastic processes in service systems as being independent when they are indeed dependent can lead to substantial errors in estimations and predictions of the system’s expected queue length and throughput, as well as substantial losses in profits when staffing levels are to be optimized. In the research output “Optimally Scheduling Heterogeneous Impatient Customers” (J2), the PI characterizes the optimal scheduling policy for multi-class service systems with intra-class dependencies between customers’ service and patience times. This work suggests a substantial loss in cost objectives if the system manager devises scheduling policies by considering the within-class primitives to be independent when they are indeed dependent. 2. To develop effective, accurate and analytically-tractable models, approximations and methodologies to analyze service systems with dependencies. This objective is fully achieved. In the research output “When Service Times Depend on Customers’ Delays: A Relationship Between Two Models of Dependence” (J1), the PI provides a unified characterization of system dynamics under two dependence mechanisms, and builds on this characterization to demonstrate an important relationship between these two dependence mechanisms. The latter relationship further facilitates statistical estimations considerably which are practically important because identifying the source of dependence from observed data is often hard because both the service times and patience times are censored due to customer abandonment. In the research output “Optimally Scheduling Heterogeneous Impatient Customers” (J2), the PI studies the optimal scheduling policy (how to route idle servers to waiting customers) for multi-class service systems with intra-class dependencies. Noting the analytical intractability of an exact solution for large systems, the PI undertakes a fluid approach by utilizing an intimate relationship between the fluid model and the original queueing system. Specifically, in the fluid version of a scheduling policy, the decision of which class to allocate an idle server to becomes equivalent to computing the fraction of capacity allocated to each class. The decision of which customer within a class to allocate the server to can be solved by splitting the class into multiple subclasses and processing each subclass under the First Come First Served (FCFS) policy. These two decisions are inherently linked and the PI develops a full analysis of this linkage in the fluid optimization problem. The fluid analysis further provides guidance for developing scheduling policies for stochastic queueing system, and based on the fluid solution, the PI proposes two scheduling policies applicable to stochastic queueing systems: a mostly-FCFS policy that maintains within-class FCFS for all but at most one class, and an mTIQ policy that differentiates customers of all classes based on their current time in queue. The effectiveness of these two scheduling policies is demonstrated via simulations. 3. To perform an empirical study of systems in which customers’ service times depend on their patience or delay, and develop efficient methods to address (censored) data. This objective is fully achieved. The research output “When Service Times Depend on Customers’ Delays: A Relationship Between Two Models of Dependence” (J1) was motivated by the empirical observations in various service contexts such as restaurants, call centers, and intensive care units, that customers’ service times are related to the delay they experience in queue. The PI proposed two dependence mechanisms to drive such phenomenon: First, the service requirement of a customer may evolve while waiting in queue, in which case the service time of each customer is endogenously determined by the system’s dynamics. Second, customers may arrive (exogenously) to the system with a service and patience time that are stochastically dependent, so that the service-time distribution of the customers that end up in service is different than that of the entire customer population. The PI refers to the former type of dependence as endogenous and to the latter as exogenous. Identifying the source of dependence from observed data, however, is hard because both the service times and patience times are censored due to customer abandonment. Further, even if the dependence is known to be exogenous, there remains the difficult problem of fitting a joint service-patience times distribution to the censored data. The PI provides a unified solution to these two statistical challenges by proving that both problems can be avoided. It is shown that, for any exogenous dependence, there exists a corresponding endogenous dependence, such that the queuing dynamics under either dependence have the same law. It is also proven that there exist endogenous dependencies for which no equivalent exogenous dependence exists. In other words, the endogenous dependence can be considered as a generalization of the exogenous dependence. Thus, whenever dependence is observed in data, one can always consider the system as having an endogenous dependence, regardless of the true underlying dependence mechanism. Because estimating the structure of an endogenous dependence is substantially easier than estimating a joint service-patience distribution from censored data, this approach facilitates statistical estimations considerably and the PI proposes an easy-to-implement estimation procedure for the generalized endogenous dependence. To demonstrate the effectiveness of this estimation procedure, the PI generates synthetic data using simulations of a system with an exogenous dependence, and then follows this procedure to estimate the equivalent endogenous dependence, and shows that the resulting estimations can perform very well in capturing system dynamics when the system condition changes, as opposed to an estimation procedure that ignores the dependence but has very poor prediction power in response to changes in system parameters. 4. To identify optimal management schemes (control, staffing, pricing, etc.) for service systems with various dependencies. This objective is fully achieved. In the research output “When Service Times Depend on Customers’ Delays: A Relationship Between Two Models of Dependence” (J1), the PI proposes an easy-to-implement procedure to estimate the generalized endogenous dependence in service systems with customer abandonment, and shows that this procedure, despite its simplicity, is very effective in capturing system dynamics when the system condition changes, and very accurate in prescribing the optimal staffing level when it is to be optimized. In the research output “Optimally Scheduling Heterogeneous Impatient Customers” (J2), the PI characterizes the optimal scheduling policy for multi-class systems with intra-class dependencies between customers’ service and patience times. The PI shows that the scheduling policy for systems with intra-class dependencies can differ significantly from those for systems without dependencies, and thus, considering the within-class primitives to be independent when they are indeed dependent can lead to substantial losses in cost objectives. In the research output “Managing Customer Search via Bundling” (J3), the PI studies how monopoly firms should use pricing and bundling tactics to manage customers’ search behaviors when they have uncertain but correlated valuations for multiple services. The PI identifies an intimate relationship between customers’ search behaviors and the correlation structure. Thus, achieving good profitability requires closely tailoring prices and bundling tactics to the underlying correlations.

26206419.label: Major findings and research outcome
26206419.value: Our works contribute to both the theoretical and empirical research on managing service systems with customer-driven dependencies. Specially, the research output “When Service Times Depend on Customers’ Delays: A Relationship Between Two Models of Dependence” (J1) builds on the empirical observation in service systems that customers’ service times are related to the delay they experience in queue. The PI develops a unified solution to two empirical challenges in this context that arise from censoring due to customer abandonment. The PI shows that whenever dependence between customers’ service and waiting times is observed in data, one can always model and analyze such systems by considering a generalized endogenous dependence. This finding facilitates statistical estimations considerably, and the PI proposes an easy-to-implement estimation procedure for the generalized endogenous dependence and demonstrates its effectiveness in estimations and optimal staffing via simulations. The research output “Optimally Scheduling Heterogeneous Impatient Customers” (J2) characterizes the optimal scheduling policy for multi-class systems with intra-class dependencies between customers’ service and patience times. The PI undertakes a fluid approach to solve the policy optimization problem and shows that the optimal fluid policy splits at most one customer class into two subclasses (each corresponding to a different offered wait), and processes all other classes under the First Come First Served (FCFS) policy. Based on this fluid solution, the PI proposes two policies, mostly-FCFS and mTIQ, for stochastic queueing systems. The PI further shows that considering the within-class primitives to be independent when they are indeed dependent can lead to significant losses in cost objectives when implementing these policies. The research output “Managing Customer Search via Bundling” (J3) studies monopoly firms’ optimal pricing and bundling decisions when customers actively search to discover their uncertain but correlated valuations for multiple service. The PI develops a non-obligatory search framework to study two market scenarios: a market of one mature and one new services, and a market of two new services. The PI shows that bundling cultivates customer search in a market of one mature and one new service, but inhibits search in a market of two new services. The PI also studies mixed bundling and shows that its economic benefits only carry through when customers’ search cost is not too large. In this case, mixed bundling can lead to considerable revenue improvement in a market of one mature and one new services, but only tiny revenue improvement in a market of two new services.

26206419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26206419.value: Customer-driven dependencies are fundamental in service systems, and as demonstrated in this project, they can have substantial impacts on systems’ key performance measures and on the management of service systems. The PI pursues several directions in this project, such as scheduling, pricing, and statistical estimations. Despite these efforts, the PI believes that customer-driven dependencies in service systems should be studied further as the understanding of this fundamental component in service systems is not yet complete. Potential directions include unravelling underlying mechanisms that drive customer-oriented dependencies through experimental studies, extending single-station analysis to complex queueing networks, and providing a holistic view of system management that integrates various operational levers such as staffing, scheduling, and pricing in the presence of customer-driven dependencies. The PI hopes the completion of this project could invite more investigations into this exciting strand of research.

26206419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26206419.value: Customer-driven dependencies are fundamental in service systems, and they can have substantial impacts on systems’ key performance measures and on the management of service systems. The objectives of this project are thus to provide an effective, accurate, and analytically-tractable framework to model and analyze customer-driven dependencies in service systems, and to propose operational schemes to manage such dependencies. The PI undertakes this task from both a theoretical and empirical perspective, and demonstrates through a rigorous analysis that ignoring these dependencies can be detrimental, and that operational schemes such as scheduling and pricing can be effective in managing these dependencies. The framework developed is easy to understand, and policies proposed easy to apply, both allowing the analysis and outcomes of this project to have a broad and grounded impact.

26209319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26209319.value: The goal of the proposed project is to help advance the current state of the art in robotic dexterous manipulation, which enables robots to skillfully manipulate objects and interact with the environment. Achieving human-level dexterity and versatility is one of the grand challenges in robotics. In typical object manipulation and transportation scenarios, robots must be able to get a good hold (or “grasp”) on objects, transfer objects between secure grasps, and interact deliberately with the environment. Such seemingly simple tasks are still very difficult for robots today, as their dexterity and versatility are far below human levels. However, even special-purpose end-effectors (in essence, robotic “hands”) with little dexterity are often the most expensive part of a robotic system. This presents a barrier to the wider adoption of robots. We aim to fill a major gap in the theory and practice of robotic dexterous manipulation at present. Our technical approach will bridge effector design, models of mechanics, and manipulation planning/control. Our main objective is to devise (1) novel design, planning, and control tools for composing various dexterous manipulation primitives that exploit resources both intrinsic and extrinsic to the robot, which will complement the traditional approach to robotic dexterity relying mainly on the fine motor skills of high-mobility robot hands, and (2) a systematic framework for integrating these manipulation primitives, which advances from the conventional manual, ad hoc approaches to robotic task fulfillment as can be seen in the DARPA Robotics Challenge for example. The proposed systematic integration of various dexterous manipulation techniques will greatly scale up the range of dexterity tasks that robots can perform in an autonomous manner. While our proposed tools and integration framework are expected to be task-agnostic and applicable to a wide range of robot platforms, both minimalist and sophisticated, they will be demonstrated through concrete challenge tasks and hardware systems. For example, the conventional combination of a two-fingered gripper and a six-axis robot arm will be used to perform dexterous part insertion or precision placement tasks beyond the platform’s major application to routine grasp-lift-and-carry tasks. By introducing a systematic methodology for enhancing robotic dexterity that can be implemented on a wide range of robot platforms, our results will render dexterous robotic manipulation more adaptable and affordable in many important application areas including transporting goods in warehouses, manipulating parts in factories, and handling everyday objects to serve people directly. 本項目的目標是提高當前機器人靈巧操作的技術水平，使機器人能夠熟練地操作物體並與環境交互。實現人類水平的靈活性和多功能性是機器人領域面臨的巨大挑戰之一。在典型的物體操縱和運輸場景中，機器人必須能夠很好地抓取物體、轉移物體，並有意與環境交互。對於今天的機器人來說，這些看似簡單的任務仍然非常困難，因為它們的靈活性和多功能性遠低於人類水平。然而，即使是不太靈巧的專用末端執行器（即機器人的“手”）也常常是機器人系統中最昂貴的部分。這給機器人的廣泛應用帶來了障礙。 我們的目的是填補目前機器人靈巧操作理論和實踐中的一大空白。我們的技術方法將結合末端執行器設計、力學模型以及操作規劃與控制。我們的主要目標是設計：（1）一個新穎的設計、規劃和控制工具，用於設計各種靈巧的操作原語，這些原語利用機器人的內在和外在資源，彌補傳統的依靠高機動性機械手的精細運動技能為主的實現機器人靈巧操作的方法；以及（2）集成這些操作原語的系統框架，該框架是從傳統的手動、專門的設計方法發展而來，來完成如美國國防高等研究計劃署機器人挑戰賽中的任務。我們提出的對各種靈巧操作技術的系統集成將大大擴展機器人可自動執行的靈巧任務的範圍。 儘管我們提出的工具和集成框架是希望完成各種任務、適用於任何機器人操作平台，但無論是最簡單的還是複雜的，它們將通過具體的有挑戰性的任務和硬件系統進行演示。例如，二指爪和六軸機械臂的傳統組合將用於執行靈巧的零件插入動作或精準放置任務，這超出了此平台在常規的抓取、提升、搬運任務中的應用範圍。通過引入一種可以在多種機器人平台上實現的提高機器人靈活性的系統的方法，我們的研究結果將使靈巧的機器人操作在很多重要的應用領域具有更強的適應性和經濟性，例如倉庫貨物運輸、工廠操縱零件以及處理日常物品直接為人們服務等。

26302019.value: 大维低秩矩阵模型的统计检验及置信区间

26302019.label: Project Objectives
26302019.value: Design a novel estimator for noisy matrix completion by which data-dependent entry-wise confidence interval is constructed in the undersampling scheme. Prove the central limit theorem of singular vectors for the matrix perturbation model where data-dependent confidence regions of singular vectors are constructed. 26302019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26302019.value: Low-rank statistical models describe structured matrix signals planted inside high-dimensional noisy data. In the past decade, tremendous efforts have been made to efficiently estimate high-dimensional and low-rank statistical models. The aim of the proposed project is to evaluate the uncertainty of these reported estimates and it will focus on the statistical inference for various popular low-rank models. In particular, we aim to construct confidence regions and confidence intervals for several important low-rank related parameters. Confidence regions are conventionally used to evaluate uncertainty of point estimates. They play a fundamental role in statistical inference. We plan to begin by revisiting the renowned noisy matrix completion problem. By sophisticatedly integrating the de-biasing technique and spectral projection, we will propose a novel low-rank estimator. In addition, we will prove the central limit theorem for entries of the proposed estimator, which will allow the entry-wise confidence interval to be constructed in the undersampling scheme when the sample size is much smaller than the ambient dimension. Consequently, the explicit sample size requirement will be derived. We will then investigate the matrix perturbation model and develop asymptotic normality theory for the empirical singular vectors. We will also investigate the signal-to-noise ratio which is fundamental to ensure such asymptotic normality. Based on data-dependent centering and normalizing quantities, we will propose data-driven confidence regions for singular vectors in the matrix perturbation model. Our methods will be further extended to the low-rank multivariate regression model, so that relevant confidence regions can be constructed. Finally, the matrix sensing model will be considered. After imposing sparsity assumption on the inverse covariance of measurement matrices, we will propose effective procedures to construct data-dependent confidence intervals for a single matrix entry and linear functions of matrix entries. 低秩统计模型描述有噪音的矩阵信息。基于近些年已经提出来的高效的低秩矩阵估计方法，我们的这个项目致力于低秩模型的统计推断。 具体的目标包括建立几种低秩统计模型的置信区间和置信区域。作为最传统的统计推断方法，置信区间可以刻画统计估计的不确定性。 我们首先回顾噪音下的矩阵还原问题。借鉴成熟的消偏方法和谱投影，我们提出在矩阵还原问题下新的低秩估计量并证明每个元素的中心极限定理，以及建立每个元素的置信区间。然后我们会研究矩阵扰动模型并证明关于特征向量的中心极限定理，以及研究特定的信噪比条件。基于这些中心极限定理，我们可以建立特征向量的置信区间。然后我们会研究低秩多元回归模型并建立相应的置信区间。最后我们研究高斯测量下的低秩回归模型，并研究相关的置信区间，当测量矩阵具有特殊稀疏性的前提下。

26302019.label: Realisation of objectives
26302019.value: The first objective has been perfectly achieved. In the article titled "Statistical Inferences of Linear Forms for Noisy Matrix Completion," published in the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society - Series B, the PI and his collaborator introduced a double-debiasing method. This method constructs a nearly unbiased estimator for noisy matrix completion, exceeding the original goal of creating an asymptotically normal estimator for each entry of the underlying low-rank matrix. The PI's method goes beyond, establishing a normal approximation theory for a general linear form of the underlying low-rank matrix. This is particularly beneficial in practice since statistical inference of a linear form aids in comparing different entries of the underlying low-rank matrix. The methodology and theory developed are universal, resolving a long-standing problem in noisy matrix completion. The second objective has been successfully accomplished as planned by the PI. The results of this objective have been published in an article titled "Normal Approximation and Confidence Region of Singular Subspaces" in the Electronic Journal of Statistics. In this paper, the PI introduced a novel spectral representation tool for matrix perturbation. This tool provides a deterministic formula for singular vectors or eigenvectors under any perturbation, as long as the magnitude of the perturbation is smaller than the signal strength. Leveraging this tool, the PI examined the matrix denoising model, where a low-rank matrix is randomly perturbed by Gaussian noise. The focus was on studying the normal approximation of the distance between the empirical spectral projector and the population spectral projector. The results generated the first non-asymptotic normal approximation theories of the empirical spectral projector under the matrix denoising model. The non-asymptotic theory is notably flexible as it permits arbitrary relationships of matrix dimensions, allowing the rank to grow in relation to the matrix dimension. The original goal of the third objective was to explore low-rank multivariate regression and develop corresponding statistical inference methodology and theory. However, the PI and collaborators identified more ambitious and practically useful objectives that also had fundamental implications for statistical methodologies and theory. In the manuscript titled "Semiparametric Tensor Factor Analysis by Iteratively Projected SVD", currently under minor revision in the Journal of the Royal Statistical Society - Series B, the PI and collaborators developed a comprehensive framework for semiparametric tensor factor analysis. This framework focuses on the methodology and theory of low-rank tensor decomposition with auxiliary covariates, covering multivariate regression as a special case. A novel estimating procedure based on iterative projected power iterations was proposed. The efficacy of this new method was demonstrated both in theory and through real data experiments. In a related work titled "Higher-Order Accurate Two-Sample Network Inference and Network Hashing," currently under revision in the Journal of the American Statistical Association, the PI and collaborators developed a new methodology for the statistical inference of two-sample networks. Considering networks as special cases of matrix-valued data, the developed methodology and theory were tailored for a general network graphon model, which includes the low-rank model as a special case. This work represents the first result concerning a higher-order accurate inference method for two-sample network comparison. The original goal of the fourth objective was to explore sparsity in the low-rank matrix regression model, which could primarily be of interest for theoretical purposes. However, the PI and collaborators have pursued more ambitious and practically relevant objectives -- exploring sparsity in tensor methods and their applications. In the article titled "Effective Tensor Sketching via Sparsification," published in the IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, the PI and collaborators developed a new statistical sampling method for compressing large tensors, with matrix regression included as a special case. Essentially, this innovative method enables the storage of only a tiny proportion of any given tensor while still preserving substantial information. In a related manuscript titled "Community Detection for Hypergraph Networks via Regularized Tensor Power Iteration," the PI and collaborators explored sparsity in developing new statistical methods for analyzing hypergraph networks. The developed method accommodates extremely sparse observed networks and can consistently recover the node community memberships. A novel tensor incoherence norm leveraging extreme sparsity serves as the key technical contribution.

26302019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26302019.value: The technical tools developed in this project are universal and can be applied to a wide range of low-rank problems, particularly when the primary objectives are statistical inference and uncertainty quantification. Matrix-valued data also feature prominently in many unsupervised learning problems such as clustering. Exploring the statistical limit of clustering matrix-valued observations is a fundamental yet challenging task. The spectral representation formula developed in this project is a critical tool for studying matrix-variate clustering problems. A combination of K-means clustering and low-rank approximation can be employed to investigate these clustering problems. The main challenge in the theoretical analysis of the algorithm's performance lies in the low-rank approximation, where the spectral representation formula plays a pivotal role.

26302019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26302019.value: Matrix-valued data with embedded structures commonly appear in numerous fields of scientific study today. The information of scientific value often lies in the hidden low-dimensional structure, such as a low-rank signal matrix. Over the past few decades, an ever-growing body of literature has focused on developing statistical methodologies and theories for estimating this hidden low-dimensional structure. However, these estimation procedures often lack valid statistical inference guarantees intended to quantify the uncertainty of the developed estimators. In this project, the PI and collaborators have developed a series of potent technical tools and methodologies that empower statisticians and practitioners to construct estimators for the hidden low-dimensional structure in matrix-valued data, which exhibit asymptotic normality. These advancements offer substantial value in analyzing and interpreting complex matrix-valued data structures across various scientific domains.

26302219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26302219.value: In quantum materials, interactions of electronic, spin, orbital and lattice degrees of freedom (DOFs) have proven to be a fertile source of emergent quantum phenomena that range from high-Tc superconductivity, colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) to quantum spin liquids. The details of the interacting DOFs and how such interactions foster emergent quantum states are far from understood but are of fundamental importance in modern condensed matter physics. This field bears exciting opportunities for scientific discoveries and new-generation functional materials for technological advancement. Much effort has been made to manipulate the emergent phases in quantum materials by means of static tuning, including direct carrier doping and the application of external pressure, magnetic field, hydrostatic pressure and strain-engineering. Despite their great success, these control methods are relatively primitive and slow, and hence have limitations (see also the next section for details of the key issues and problems being addressed). These static tuning methods often indirectly interact with crucial elementary excitations, and hence make it more challenging to unambiguously understand the rich yet complex physics of quantum materials. We propose to use state-of-the-art all-table-top THz pump-probe spectroscopy to directly and selectively manipulate specific elementary excitations—phonons, magnons and amplitude mode of condensate states—at their fundamental energy- and time-scale (meV to eV, and femtosecond to picosecond). This will be done by means of light-matter interaction in the nonlinear regime offered by a strong-field (multi)-THz drive with field strength in the kV/cm to MV/cm range. The non-equilibrium dynamics on ultrafast time-scales, initiated by the intensive (multi)-THz drive, will be subsequently probed by our ultra-broadband THz probe pulse, emitted by laser-induced air-plasma, to simultaneously investigate individual elementary excitations (electronic, phononic and magnetic) and their interaction, enabled by the unique octaves-spanning air-plasma THz source, which covers 0.2 to 25 THz. In particular, we will conduct the aforementioned intensive THz/multi-THz pump- ultrabroadband THz probe spectroscopy at cryogenic temperatures to identify, investigate and then ultimately manipulate the fundamental interactions of elementary excitations in intriguing quantum materials, including (i) heavy fermion compounds with strongly correlated Coulomb interaction among electrons and magnetic interaction as the leading contributing factors, and (ii) more complex strongly correlated transition metal oxides involving many other, if not all, degrees of freedom.

26302219.label: Realisation of objectives
26302219.value: Objective 1: Implement a tunable narrowband intense THz (0.3 to 2 THz) and multi-THz (4 to 18 THz) pump, capable of providing on/off-resonant drive in quantum materials. The work on implementing intense THz excitation may splits into two parts, generation of THz pump beam in the standard THz and the multi-THz regime. (1). In the standard THz regime, we used the tilted-pulse-front technique to generate in the LiNbO3 crystal (ambient housing) for single-cycle strong THz pulse with the peak field up to 300 kV/cm. The peak field is further enhanced to exceed the level of 1 MV/cm with the addition of a cryogenic enclosure (77 K housing) with the customized optical cryostat. Peak fields rendered by either configuration are sufficient for access physics governed by nonlinear THz response in most materials, e.g., quantum materials, semiconductors and even dielectric materials. (2). In the multi-THz regime, we employ the configuration of difference frequency generation by mixing two near-infrared beams of distinct center wavelength, for instance, 1.3 µm and 1.55 µm beams from an optical parametric amplifier. The active medium for the wave-mixing (DFG) process to take place are DSMTS organic crystal for the 5-20 THz range and GaSe crystal for 15 -70 THz, with an exemplary tuning spectrum shown in the last annual progress report. At the excitation wavelength of 30 THz, the excitation fluence is as high as 50 mJ/cm2, approximately corresponding to a peak electric field of 20 MV/cm. Furthermore, after incorporating a stretcher module to manage chirp of the input pulse for the DFG process, the Mid-IR output acquires the versality to switch between broadband and narrowband mode to fit for experiments of different kinds, depending on whether strong peak field or well-defined driving frequency is the more favorable character. Objective 2: Implement an ultra-broadband THz probe for linear spectroscopy (0.5 to 20 THz, 15–600 µm) with sub-ps temporal resolution. The ultra-broadband THz probe pulses can now be routinely generate using two-color-field laser-induced air-plasma filament. To be specific, the intense fundamental pulse of the Ti:sapphire laser amplifier with the standard characteristics (center wavelength 800 nm, pulse duration 35 fs, pulse energy 3 mJ) and its second harmonic pulse (center wavelength 400 nm) are temporally and spatially combined to synthesize the two-color field with a broken inversion symmetry. The two-color field is subsequently focused in the ambient to create the air-plasma filament that emits pulsed single-cycle THz field spanning 0.5-20 THz frequency range. To read out the time-domain waveform of the THz pulse, we used the electro-optic sampling technique to respectively cover the low frequency range (0.5-8 THz) with GaP detection crystal and the high-frequency range (8-20 THz) with GaSe crystal. The associated pulse duration approximately reads a value equal or less than 200 fs (0.2 ps), favorable for probing sub-ps dynamics. Combined with the strong-field excitation pulse of outstanding tunability both in center frequency and bandwidth, we therefore completes the instrumentation work for ultrafast spectroscopic dynamics study in various material systems, on which details are provided in content related to Objective 4 as well as in the research output. Objective 3: Implement a compact platform for broadband THz spectroscopy at cryogenic temperatures. Upon completing the abovementioned implementation of the tunable pump beam as well as the ultrabroadband probe beam, we augmented the home-made THz pump-probe spectrometer with an optical cryostat–switchable between closed-cycle helium cooled and liquid-He continuous flow modes–for capabilities to measure either thin film samples in transmission mode or single crystal samples in reflection mode. The system is capable to operate in the the range from 5 – 350 K (78-500 K in other configuration) at the sample position, more than sufficient for dynamic study of a wealth material systems from quantum materials to photonic functional materials. Objective 4: Perform nonlinear THz/multi-THz pump–broadband THz probe spectroscopy of correlated materials for the study of non-equilibrium dynamics and the search for “hidden” phases. Taking the cryogenic nonlinear THz spectroscopy, we have investigated a considerable amount of materials systems from those described in the original proposal (CMR manganite, titanium oxide and Kondo insulator SmB6) to those beyond (Weyl semimetal WTe2, the 3D Kane fermion system Huygens’ metasurface). In the colossal magnetoresitant La2/3Ca1/3MnO3 thin film, we observed a novel photo-induced transient metastable states, which onsets at a characteristic temperature of 200 K and gives rise to a nonlinear THz emission signal. We attribute the remarkable observation to launching and breaking the coherent state of the phonon-dressed charged carriers, coherent polaron. It is a state that were only hinted at by multiple static state measurements, but has not yet been experimentally verified and examined in a serious way, albeit it may bear the answers to secrets of the still-elusive colossal magnetoresistant materials, of which the physics is of fundamental importance and shared by the high-Tc superconductivity, one of the most perplexing and prominent enigmas in physics. Due to the novelty of our discovery, publication in a high-quality journal is expected and the manuscript is to be submitted in the coming months. In Weyl semimetal WTe2 thin film, of which the topological aspect depends on lattice symmetry, we use the near-IR excitation to transiently modify electron occupancy so as to induce a metastable state, featuring a structural change. However, it remains elusive whether Weyl-point-related topological phase transition indeed takes place and in what manner it would proceed. Probing the free-carrier dynamics with the THz pulse, we secured the first evidence of the electronic phase transition that has been assumed by others. Most importantly, we found that the electronic phase transition is percolative; that is a real space dynamic competition between the topological trivial and nontrivial states. Such percolation dynamics shows a complete independence from both excitation fluence and the temperature. Hence, it features a universal scaling behavior in the pump-probe traces, leading to a striking dynamic isosbestic point. To reach the full potential of the set-up, we expanded into the new line of research on the time-boundary effect in metasurface. A free-standing Huygens’ metasurface has been designed and fabricated in a way that the electric and magnetic resonances of the constituent silicon disks become degenerate and are of exceptionally high quality factor. Upon carrier-injecting photoexcitation, the sudden change in dielectric function prompts a time boundary and consequently occasion the removal of two-fold degeneracy. With the time-boundary-imposed suppression on coherent local oscillating fields, we demonstrate and observe for the first time the THz energy gain effect, as evidenced by the the above-unity transmission spectra. Note on spending deviation: Over the course of project, large portion of the budget for Research Staff and Conferences has been shifted to expense on the equipment part on account that: (1) The proposed budget on equipment reflects only the ideal case. In practice, owing to the explorative nature of our research activity, redundancy is necessary in terms of optics and key equipment so as to offset the impact from uncertainties; (2) Due to the COVID pandemic, most items have costed considerably more than expected, and traveling out of Hong Kong for conferences have been impossible for many years. We, therefore, have overspent on the Equipment for the best use of the fund and outcome of the project.
