26302219.label: Major findings and research outcome
26302219.value: In output 1, we presented a novel strategy named interferometry-type frequency-resolved optical gating (FROG) for extending time-domain spectroscopy with sub-cycle temporal resolution into the challenging visible regime enabled by a new phase-locking mechanism. The methodology may serve as a generic way for ultrafast-compatible measurement on complex optical dielectric function of materials. Specifically, we proposed an interferometric FROG to eliminate ambiguities of time direction, zero-order absolute phase and first-order translational phase, which are rampant in conventional single-pulse FROG measurement. This extension of phase sensitivity to the lowest possible order is established by resorting to properly synthesized double-pulse train that activates a remarkable phase-locking mechanism. In output 2, the work furnishes an innovative route of generating both CEP-controllable and center-frequency-tunable narrowband THz radiation from laser-induced air plasma. It not only proves the feasibility of coherent control of the narrowband THz radiation from air plasma, but also demonstrates a straightforward solution to the phase stabilization of the air-plasma THz source, a favourable attribute for advanced spectroscopy. It reported a new method for taming the two-color air-plasma THz source by devising an interferometry-based scheme for coherent manipulation of the driving field. Relevant to the laser-plasma based THz source, a US patent has been granted and a China patent application is under review. In output 3, the PI has been invited to write a "News & Perspective" on the photo-induced superconductivity in the fullerene (K3C60) in the journal Nature Physics. In output 4, through dynamic spectroscopic investigation in the THz regime, we identified electronic signature of the topological phase transition, as the evidential confirmation of the photo-induced metastable phase in WTe2. Our discovery of the universality-embodying dynamic isosbestic point may set the standard for identification of ultrafast percolative transition without recourse to real-space imaging methods for the leading evidence. Our findings and methods, as a whole, may inspire and facilitate future exploration into critical phenomena on the fundamental scale, i.e., in the adiabatic limit, especially in case of light-induced transitions in diverse material systems beyond those just hosting competing topological phases. In output 5, in the context of time-boundary engineering, this work demonstrates the long-quested wave amplification and instances the potency of Huygens’ metasurfaces in facilitating novel optical functionalities. The work at THz frequencies opened the door to experimental confirmation on and insights into the microscopic dynamics of time-boundary-engineered media, in general. Although only proven working at THz frequencies, the presented method is readily applicable for extension to mid-IR and even visible wavelengths. It brings forth the exciting possibility of parametric amplification, should even more sophisticated level of control be available.

26302219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26302219.value: The ADI-FROG spectroscopy was a methodology that works in principle and is at present under experimental verification for a proof-of-principle demonstration. If successful, the method and pertinent set-up may be turned into a push-button system for time-domain spectroscopy that delivers exhaustive spectroscopic information (magnitude and phase) at ultrahigh temporal resolution. The narrowband generation of tunable and phase-stabilized THz pulse is a topic of interest in terms of both fundamental science and application. A full understanding of the complex nonlinear interaction of strong laser field and gaseous medium requires a comprehensive investigation of the microscopic dynamics and can occasion THz source of unprecedentedly broad tuning range in the strong-field regime, favorable for coherent control of advanced materials and THz frequency devices. As for the Weyl semimetal, our work addresses the curious question on how a topological state, evading Landau paradigm of phase transitions but coupled to lattice, annihilates into a trivial state, and vice versa. The switching threshold provides a gateway toward on-off control over Weyl-point-related functionalities. The ultrafast universal scaling and isosbestic point may have set a new benchmark in identification of ultrafast critical phenomenon, particularly in the adiabatic limit, in diverse systems beyond topological materials.

26302219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26302219.value: Over the course of the project, our group has implemented a state-of-the-art THz and multi-THz spectroscopy system that provides access to novel physics in the strong-field limit. A wealth of material system from gaseous media to quantum materials and metamaterials can well fit into the scope of the machinery. To showcase its capability, we have demonstrated tunable narrowband THz radiation from strong-laser-field-induced plasma filament, amplification of THz waves in the Huygens’ metasurface and ultrafast on-off-switch of topological states in the Weyl semimetal. The spirit of time-domain spectroscopy has been successfully extended into the challenging visible frequency range and a new technique (ADI-FROG) for an ambiguity-free reconstruction of femtosecond laser field towards broadband and ultrafast spectroscopy at an unprecedented level.

26303319.label: Realisation of objectives
26303319.value: Several results on the project objectives have been realized. Objective (1): Together with G. Schrader and A. Shapiro, we studied the Peter-Weyl type theorem of the harmonic analysis for the regular representations of the split real quantum group U_q(sl(n,R)) in type A on the Hilbert space L2(SL_q+(n,R)) from the Gelfand-Naimark-Segal (GNS) construction in C*-algebra, using the techniques developed in the P.I.'s previous work in rank 2. The manuscript is almost complete, but we would like to include an extra construction using canonical functionals, which will be more in line with the Fock-Goncharov approach using the quantum geometry of moduli spaces and strengthen the research results. The collaboration has been interrupted by the pandemic, and the question about tensor product decomposition is not fully addressed, although it seems to be a consensus that the question is deemed too difficult in Lie types other than type A. Objective (2): In the preprint (arXiv:2008.08589) we constructed a new family of irreducible representations of U_q(g_R) and its modular double by quantizing the classical parabolic induction corresponding to arbitrary parabolic subgroups, such that the generators of U_q(g_R) act by positive self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space. We gave a new construction of the evaluation modules of the affine quantum group U_q(sl_{n+1}^) modeled over this minimal positive representation of type A_n. In the preprint with Ryuichi Man (arXiv:2203.14828), a new class of degenerate positive representations corresponding to Zero Casimirs was constructed, which generalize the notion of a complementary series. The project proposal originally expect just a construction to the maximal parabolic case only, so these results provide a big leap to the project goal. Objective (3) Using the technique of virtual highest weight developed by the P.I.'s previous work, we studied the tensor product decomposition of the split real quantum group U_q(sl(2,R)) from the perspective of finite dimensional representation theory of compact quantum groups. We proved that one can derive the corresponding Hilbert space decomposition, given explicitly by quantum dilogarithm transformations, from the Clebsch--Gordan coefficients of the tensor product decomposition of finite dimensional representations of the compact quantum group U_q(sl_2) by solving certain functional equations arising from analytic continuation and using normalization arising from tensor products of canonical basis. The research results have been published in Lett. Math. Phys., 111:39, (2021). Finally, a combinatorial study of quantum group embedding is also carried out in the preprint (arXiv:2211.09601) by proposing a new quantized version of Lusztig’s Injectivity Lemma in the language of quantum cluster algebra, verifying the independence of the Coxeter moves on positive representations.

26303319.label: Major findings and research outcome
26303319.value: (With G. Schrader and A. Shapiro) the Peter Weyl type theorem has been generalized to higher rank in type A. New families of positive representations have been constructed. This includes the reduction to parabolic subgroups (arXiv:2008.08589), and (with Ryuichi Man) the positive representations with degeneracy to zero Casimirs (arXiv:2203.14828), as well as their modular double counterparts. The tensor product decomposition in rank 2 was studied combinatorially from the perspective of compact quantum groups (Lett. Math. Phys., 111:39). A new quantized version of Lusztig’s Injectivity Lemma was introduced in the language of quantum cluster algebra, and we verify the independence of the Coxeter moves on positive representations (arXiv:2211.09601).

26303319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26303319.value: The tensor product decomposition in Objective 1 is not fully addressed yet if the Lie type is not type A, and still requires further development. The construction for Objective 2 was done algebraically by generators and relations. It is natural to study them from the geometric point of view in line with Fock--Goncharov's approach. In particular, the construction of parabolic positive representations is closely related to quantum Hamiltonian reduction. Finally, the combinatorial description of the quantum group embedding also required further refinement, potentially using techniques arising from dimer models and canonical basis.

26303319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26303319.value: The research project continued to explore the newly developed theory of positive representations of split real quantum groups. We deepened our understanding of the split-real quantum version of the classical Peter Weyl theorem. We also construct new families of positive representations through several methods of reduction and study them by combinatorial means. The project builds new connections between representation theory and quantum geometry via cluster algebras.

26308419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26308419.value: Differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) inevitably produces inappropriate or even tumorigenic cells. Efficient cell type isolation after iPSC differentiation allows creditable disease modeling in the laboratory and safe transplantation in clinical setting. Moreover, accurate cell type monitoring during the differentiation process can better clarify the molecular mechanisms of differentiation. At present, the most prevalent cell type identifications methods are antibody-based, that are not applicable to cells that lack unique surface markers. Other approaches, such as methods based on lectin-conjugates or toxin-regulating gene circuits, have limitations in sensitivity or side effect on non-target cells. To address these limitations, here we propose a novel high-performance cell selection strategy free of toxin and surface-marker. Combining synthetic mRNA circuit with functional molecular self-assemblies, the targeted cells will be selected with high sensitivity and low side effect. The proposed strategy senses cell-specific marker microRNA, leveraging microRNA mediated expressional suppression of mRNA. The engineered protein expressed from the mRNA forms functional molecular self-assemblies only in cells lacking the marker microRNA to enable cell type selection. We recently discovered that certain naturally existing RNA base modifications could substantially enhance the microRNA sensitivity of synthetic mRNA circuit. With this finding, our proposed circuit could overcome the low-sensitivity issue of the existing microRNA-sensing synthetic RNA for iPSC targeting reported in our previous work. Moreover, our previous reports on molecular self-assemblies for eliminating iPSCs or cancer cells both demonstrated that the use of functional molecular assemblies formed by non-functional monomers prevented toxic side effect on non-target cells. Because molecular self-assemblies only forms above a threshold concentration, leaky expression of the non-functional monomer would remain below this threshold and thus caused no toxic side effect. Our previous findings and experience uniquely enable us to combine these two areas and to deliver a high-performance approach for cell-type selection. The proposed strategy will sense microRNA and selectively produce fluorescent molecular self-assemblies for cell type identification, or apoptosis inducing ones for cell type elimination. The proposed strategy is highly tunable. Synthetic mRNA can be easily tuned to target single or multiple microRNAs to enable simultaneous identification of single or multiple types of cells. The encoded molecular self-assemblies can also be engineered to fit for different down-stream needs. The proposed research will yield a novel high-performance cell type selection approach that will substantially promote the research and application of iPSC technologies. 人工誘導多能幹細胞（iPSC）的分化不可避免的會產生不合適甚至有腫瘤傾向的細胞。高效的細胞純化技術可提供準確的由iPSC分化的細胞以用於構建可信的疾病模型以及安全的細胞植入手術。目前的細胞純化技術基本依賴於免疫標記 ，這些方法不僅成本昂貴，需要在特殊環境中進行，而且無法有效的辨別缺乏表面抗原的細胞種類。其他利用選擇性毒性蛋白表達的方法則受限於洩露表達的副作用。為了解決細胞純化的技術瓶頸，本項目提出一種基於人工RNA控制迴路，不改變細胞培養環境的情況（原位）的，高能效低副作用的細胞純化方法。 這些人工RNA控制迴路由三個主要部分組成。近年來先進的測序技術發現每種細胞都擁有其特異性表達的小分子核糖核酸（microRNA）。microRNA天然的功能在於調控其他種類RNA的活性，因此本項目中控制迴路的感應元件可以識別這些細胞特異性microRNA的人工RNA控制迴路來達到對於細胞種類的鑒別。在識別了細胞種類後，這些控制迴路的表達元件會選擇性的表達人工設計的蛋白分子單體。只有非目標細胞中累積了足夠多的蛋白分子單體時，這些單體才會在人工RNA控制迴路輸出元件的指引下有序的形成功能性自組裝體，自動的達到對細胞種類的螢光分析報告或者對目標細胞的純化。由於蛋白分子單體本身沒有活性，因此這種方法避免了洩露表達帶來的副作用。 這種全新的細胞純化方法綜合了核糖核酸與蛋白的功能性設計，是對合成生物學的一種新的綜合應用。由於iPSC在醫藥開發和臨床治療方面不可估量的前景，這種方法的成熟將有望解開iPSC細胞技術瓶頸，推動iPSC技術的廣泛應用，對公共健康事業做出貢獻。

26308419.label: Realisation of objectives
26308419.value: 1. Achievements in synthetic mRNA circuit development Synthetic mRNA circuits are designed to sense cellular molecules or traits (input) and modulate the expression level of encoded proteins, thereby generating output signals for monitoring or manipulating target cells. Because of their high biocompatibility, biodegradability and no interfere with the genomes, synthetic mRNA circuits promise safe cell-based solutions for biomedical applications, such as cellular therapeutics, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. However, the advancement of synthetic mRNA circuits is hindered by their poor cell fate manipulation performance. One of the issues is the non-covalent binding between the input and mRNA, leading to unavoidable leaky expression that generates high signal noise in non-target cells. This leaky expression also limits the design of complex circuits to amplify input sensing, resulting in a restricted level of cell manipulation in target cells. Another issue is that the current control modules of synthetic mRNA circuits mostly operate in a simple binary mode (referred to as synthetic mRNA switches), lacking precise control over output protein production in cells. The use of N1-methylpseudouridine (m1Ψ) that we discovered to enhance the binding of synthetic mRNA with microRNA and protein is an enabling technology that has allowed us to design various high-performance circuits. In our work to overcome leak expression-induced signal noise, we fully substituted uridine with m1Ψ, which enhanced the stability of the RNA aptamer structure, ensuring strong binding between the inactive output protein, produced by the mRNA switch, and the aptamer array located on the UTR of the same mRNA switch. The aptamer array serves as a scaffold, bringing the inactive proteins into close proximity and guiding their self-assembly into functional assemblies. Only when the concentration of the inactive proteins is sufficient to saturate the array can functional protein assemblies form, creating a concentration threshold for signal generation. This module effectively blocks the low amount of protein expression leakage that produces a signal. The controlled self-assembly of inactive proteins using the aptamer array serves as a readout control module to address the issue of output signal leakage in synthetic mRNA switches. This design helped establish the first mRNA tool capable of determining the spatial organization of its own product protein. Therefore, in addition to proposing a novel functional element for the synthetic mRNA toolkit, this study highlights a promising engineering direction to achieve guided spatial enrichment and protein self-assembly, which can facilitate the advancement of spatial protein assembly in synthetic biology applications. This achievement complete all three aims of the proposal. 2. Achievements in synthetic mRNA engineering Poly(A) tail plays multiple key roles in mRNA biology. Besides cooperating with the cap structure to initiate translation, the poly(A) tail also takes part in the initiation of the principal mRNA degradation pathway used in both yeast and higher eukaryotes. The removal of the poly(A) tail by the deadenylation protein complex triggers downstream decapping and degradation of mRNAs. While other parts of the mRNA have been extensively engineered to enhance protein production efficacy, the tail has largely been overlooked. Generally, researchers tend to use a poly(A) sequence containing 40 to 120 As, as it is sufficient for translation initiation. Segmented tail sequences, such as 10 nt of random sequence inserted into the A sequences (i.e., A30LA70), were used in mRNA vaccines for COVID-19. However, the segmentation is mainly to reduce the recombination rate during the DNA template plasmid production in E. coli. Several studies that introduced artificial bonds or structures to the 3' end of the tail to block mRNA degradation also failed to show significant protein production enhancement, likely due to the complete blockage of tail removal triggering other mRNA decay pathways. While traditionally considered as a long chain of adenosine, recent advancements in sequencing have revealed that many mammalian mRNAs carry non-adenosine nucleotides in the tail. However, the impact of such non-adenosine nucleotides in the tail on mRNA degradation and the consequent protein production remains largely unknown. In this work, we discovered that synthetic mRNAs with cytidine (C) placed close to the 3' end of the tail exhibited substantially higher protein production rates and longer production durations in cells and on mice. The optimal enhancement of synthetic mRNAs was achieved with around 20% C substitution near the end of the tail. We found that the C-containing tails can slow down Ccr4-Not (CNOT) complex-mediated tail removal, as two of the four catalytic proteins on the CNOT complex disfavor the removal of C-containing tails. We believe that such a difference is due to the structural difference between C and A bases. As a result, the C-containing tails prolong the intracellular half-life of synthetic mRNAs, allowing for a longer duration of protein production inside the cells. Importantly, the C-containing tails are generally applicable, being cell-type independent, transcript-independent, and transfection reaction-independent. Moreover, the use of C-containing tails requires no additional cost in the production and manufacture of synthetic mRNA and can be used with artificial cap molecules and modified nucleotides. Thus, such C-containing tails can be broadly used to directly promote the protein production efficacy of current and future synthetic mRNAs. The work presented here showcases the first systematic sequence optimization to enhance the basal protein production of synthetic mRNAs.

26308419.label: Major findings and research outcome
26308419.value: 1. Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) switches are powerful synthetic biological tools that can sense cellular molecules to manipulate cell fate. Because the input-switch binding is based only on weak noncovalent bonds, the limited input- switch binding affinities yield poor output performance, especially high signal noise due to leaky output expression in the presence of input. Harnessing the principles of supramolecular chemistry, we engineered a readout control module to circumvent the output signal leakage issue of synthetic mRNA switches. The synthetic mRNA switches with the readout control modules all exhibited substantially enhanced output performance, featured with the near-complete sequestering of output signal noise, stronger input sensitivity, and a wider output operation range (e.g., 90% in signal level on the miR-21-sensing switch). We believe that the advanced synthetic mRNA switch with readout control module enables efficient and accurate cell fate manipulation, thereby promising the biomedical applications of synthetic mRNA switches for clinical purposes. See Journal paper 1: Lu Q.; Hu Y.; Li C. Y., Kuang Y.* “Aptamer-Array-Guided Protein Assembly Enhances Synthetic mRNA Switch Performance” Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2022, e202207319. 2. The poly(A) tail is a hallmark of mature eukaryotic mRNA, impacting from the nucleus-to-cytosol transportation to the degradation of mRNA. Echoing the recent reports that discovered that non-A nucle- otides existed in mouse and human mRNAs, we examined the cellular performance of synthetic mRNAs with tails that contain different non-A nucleotides and furthermore demonstrated the functional roles of non-A nucleotides in mRNA regulation. Our study showcased the power of systematic evaluation of the impact of sequence alteration in the tail to influence protein production and analyte sensitivity from various synthetic mRNAs in vitro and in vivo. This work provides prominent C-containing tail se- quences that can be readily and generally applied for promoting the performance of a broad spectrum of synthetic mRNAs in vitro and in vivo. The study highlights the role of C substitution in the rear part of the tail that can shield mRNA from CNOT complex-mediated mRNA degradation and suggests the non-A nucleotides in the tail place versatile roles in the regulation of natural mRNAs. See Journal paper 2: Li, C.; Liang, Z.; Hu, Y.; Zhang, H.; Setiasabda, K. D.; Li, J.; Ma, S.; Xia, X.; Kuang, Y.* “Cytidine-Containing Tails Robustly Enhance And Prolong Protein Production Of Synthetic mRNA In Cell And In Vivo” Mol. Ther. Nucleic Acid, 2022, 30:300-310.

26308419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26308419.value: In addition to the manuscript detailing the discovery of C-containing tails, we have also applied patent for this technology due to its high translational value in mRNA therapeutics and vaccines. In 2022, a press release introducing this technology was hosted by HKUST, and it attracted coverage in various news media and newspapers in and outside Hong Kong. Apart from the first patent focused on tail optimization to enhance protein production of linear mRNAs, we have extended the technology for a broader scope of applications. Since we are the first group to optimize tail sequences using cytidine insertion, we hold independent intellectual property rights for this technology and are actively working on its translation.

26308419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26308419.value: The emergency authorizations of using mRNA vaccines to fight with the COVID-19 pandemic largely sped up the development of synthetic mRNAs. However, despite these improvements in synthetic mRNAs, there are significant challenges remain, such as limited protein production and lack of targeted protein expression. We pioneered the tail sequence optimization of synthetic mRNAs so that they can produce protein in substantially higher amount, increasing the drug efficacy of synthetic mRNAs. We also new types of synthetic mRNA circuits that control peptide self-assembly to achieve accurate targeted cell fate control.

26310119.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26310119.value: Digital microfluidics (DMF) is a droplet-based technology, a variation of conventional microfluidics that works via a series of electrical potentials applied onto microelectrodes covered by hydrophobic surfaces. These surfaces may be manipulated with respect to their wetting properties by the application of electrical fields. Compared with currently established analytical tools, DMF systems display significant advantages, such as extremely small reaction volumes, rapid heat transfer, and suitability for highly parallel screening. Moreover, different from conventional microfluidic platforms, fluid flow in DMF can proceed autonomously without assistance of microchannels, pumps, valves, or mixers. Thus, multistep integrated systems can be manipulated on a simple and versatile chip with significant potential to benefit routine analytical workflows. The method has been demonstrated for various applications but is still at an early stage of development. Integrated monitoring capabilities in DMF would significantly enhance their capabilities and methods are needed to establish these. Fluorescent or luminescent sensors are thin films with nanometer to micrometer thickness that contain a probe responsive for an analyte or process parameter such as pH, dissolved oxygen (DO) or temperature in an embedding polymeric matrix. In this work, we aim to integrate these fluorescent or luminescent thin film sensors into functional DMF devices using microfabrication techniques. First, we want to create single sensors for spatially resolved temperature measurement, and then produce single and dual sensors for pH and oxygen. The target application areas for demonstration are: 1) DMF-based single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) screening via melting curve analysis, 2) Photothermal optical absorbance detection and its use in an immunoassay for pesticides and 3) Microbioreactors for multiparameter toxicity screening of seawater contaminants Each of these areas make use of the advantages of these types of sensors, in that they are non-invasive, non-irritant and can measure spatially-resolved, in a different way. Together these application areas can serve to explore scope, properties, analytical parameters and possibly the limitations of these sensors in DMF. It is foreseen that these devices can impact the miniaturization and automation of highly-sensitive biological and toxicological product assays in molecular biology research, the drug discovery area, environmental monitoring and clinical practice only to name a few fields. Such platforms could enable highly-automated massive parallel assays with much lower personnel and reagent cost than what is available on the market currently. These devices also promise a greater sustainability and potential to be used in self-learning algorithms and other forms of highly integrated systems. 數字化微流體是壹種基於液滴操縱的新型科學技術，是傳統微流體的壹種變體，其通過改變施加到由疏水表面覆蓋的微電極上的壹系列電勢來操控位於微電極陣列上的液滴接觸角變化，也稱之為介電潤濕現象。與目前建立的分析工具相比，DMF系統具有顯著的優勢，例如極小的反應體積，快速的熱傳遞並且適用於高通量平行篩選。此外，與傳統的微流體平臺不同，DMF中的流體流動可以在沒有微通道，泵，閥門或混合器的幫助下自主地進行。因此，多步驟整合系統可以在簡單且通用的芯片上進行操作，具有使常規分析工作流程受益的巨大潛力。該方法已經在多種實際應用中進行展示，但仍處於開發的早期階段。DMF中的集成監控功能將顯著增強其功能，並且需要建立合適的方法來實現這些功能。 熒光或發光傳感器是厚度從納米至微米的薄膜，在聚合物基體中包含有對單種分析物或其他參數，如pH，溶解氧（DO）或溫度具備響應的探針。在這項工作中，我們的目標是使用微加工技術將這些熒光或發光薄膜傳感器集成到功能性數字化微流控設備中。首先，我們準備構建用於空間分辨溫度測量的單壹傳感器，然後發展用於檢測pH和氧氣的單壹及雙重傳感器。 目標應用領域是： 1. 基於DMF系統通過熔解曲線分析來進行單核苷酸多態性（SNP）篩選； 2. 光熱吸收光譜檢測及其在農藥免疫分析中的應用； 3. 微生物反應器用於海水汙染物的多參數毒性篩選 每項應用都都合理利用了光學傳感器的優點，因為它們可以以不同的方式在空間分辨範圍內進行非侵入性，無刺激性測量。這些應用領域可以共同探索DMF中這些傳感器的應用範圍，特性，分析參數和可能存在的限制因素。 可以預見，這些裝置可以影響分子生物學研究，藥物發現領域，環境監測和臨床實踐中的高靈敏度生物和毒理學產品分析的小型化和自動化研究進程。這樣的平臺可以實現高度自動化的大規模平行測定，其人員和試劑成本比目前市場上的低得多。這些設備還具有可持續性發展潛質，並且有巨大的潛力被用於自學算法領域和其他形式的高度集成系統。

26310119.label: Realisation of objectives
26310119.value: All main objectives of this project could be achieved, in particular digital microfluidic (DMF) platforms could be equipped with temperature, oxygen and pH sensors and each of the sensors could be well characterized and investigated. Protocols suitable for multisensors could also be developed but not fully implemented, and some of the applications had to be a bit modified based on the project results. Generally speaking, the project proposal did maybe not fully account enough for the fact that after devising suitable microfabrication protocols and construction of single sensors, as well as their characterization and calibration (objectives 1, 2 and 4), in order to publish these advances in a good journal, important for the students who were working on that, at least simple applications for these single sensors also had to be developed. Because of that, and specific results found within the project, the latter objectives (5, 6 and 7) were modified a little bit and could not be 100% performed as originally planned within the project period but also yielded a lot of advances and useful results. Also, it should be mentioned briefly that it was a most challenging period to carry out this project, as the relevant time frame in Hong Kong was characterized by many disruptions related to social unrest and later multiple outbreaks of Covid-19, leading to lab closures, difficulties to get chemicals and other materials, students and the PI at times being stuck outside HK or in quarantine, inability to use central facilities, and other hindrances. Nevertheless, the project yielded a wealth of results and all objectives could be fully or to a high degree achieved, and even when there were problems, they provided useful findings for further research and development. Below is a brief breakdown by objective. Objective 1: Exploration and identification of suitable microfabrication protocols to create multilayer microdevices that possess functionalities of both digital microfluidics and fluorescent or luminescent chemical sensors This objective was fully achieved, and various microfabrication protocols could be established allowing for the integration of these sensors in DMF platforms and also allowing variations, modifications and other further developments. The protocols could also be adapted to introduce different kind of sensors or other functions into DMF as we could also demonstrate. Objective 2: Construction of single sensors for dissolved oxygen, pH and temperature in digital microfluidic devices This objective was also fully achieved, and sensors for each of these compounds could be realized and published, also some variations of these sensors could also be described and explored. Objective 3: Creation of multisensors for both dissolved oxygen and pH using hydrophilic sites within hydrophobic spots in digital microfluidic assemblies. This objective could be realized almost fully, we described oxygen and pH sensors and one way how to create hydrophilic sites in a hydrophobic environment and also attached multisensors to these surfaces in the form of an oxygen sensor in hyflon and a polydopamine-silver-polydopamine nanocomposite, that could and was verified as a functional SERS sensor but was used mainly for its antibacterial property. We extended this part a little bit because of the expertise of the student who was working on that project at the time. So we created a multisensor, but not exactly for these parameters, but to switch the silver-based sensor with a suitable pH sensor has been performed and is straightforward as the microfabrication and sensor chemistry are almost identical, but still needs a little optimization, which is subject of current efforts (see also discussion to obj. 7) Objective 4: Characterization and calibration of the integrated sensors for optical, electrical and mechanical properties Again, this objective was fully achieved and much data about that can be found in the mentioned publications in part C and their supporting informations. Objective 5: Application of temperature sensors in the monitoring of DMF nucleic acid amplification techniques This objective was mostly achieved, but based on the project results some modifications are suggested that are subject of current work. The problems were mainly in the following areas. A) The temperature sensors tested, as well generally most of the temperature sensors of the luminescent variety, are not well-suited to the high temperatures of common PCR protocols. This could be solved with different temperature probes. Related to that, B) As originally planned there is still a separate optical label needed for the DNA/RNA which requires some modification of the optical setup, which could only partially be performed during the project. But to finish this appears to be not the best option at this point. During the project period, we have discovered, while working on another project in collaboration with Prof. PPH Cheung, CUHK, that nucleic acid amplification reactions, in particular LAMP, can be conveniently monitored using microfluidics-integrated pH sensors in minimally buffered solutions. The latter method is very sensitive and using an almost identical pH sensor to the one employed in DMF in this project. And in contrast to the original plan, it requires no label for the DNA/RNA, so it is a label-free method (G.D. Suarez, S. Bayer, Y.Y.K. Tang, D.A. Suarez, P.P.H. Cheung, S. Nagl, Lab Chip, in press, DOI: 10.1039/D3LC00391D; G.D. Suarez, Y.Y.K. Tang, S. Bayer, D.A. Suarez, P.P.H. Cheung, S. Nagl, submitted). In the cited works, we used a centrifugal microfluidics platform, but we are currently working on adapting this to a DMF platform. Objective 6: Application of temperature sensors in the monitoring of DMF nucleic acid amplification techniques This objective was also concerned with the application of temperature sensors and faced some of the same problems as objective 5, in particular, the multispectral setup needed for the application could not be fully realized within the project. Also some of the results of objectives 2 and 4, in particular the high temperature changes during DMF operations, caused problems in the design of this application as it is difficult to detect relatively small temperature changes when they are overlaid by a much bigger effect. Also some difficulties arose because, in contrast to an earlier work that was based on continuous-flow microfluidics, (S.A. Pfeiffer, S. Nagl, Anal. Chem. 2017, 89, 9400-9406), the mostly stationary nature of the droplets in DMF caused multiple problems and effects in operation and detection when illuminated with very high power laser light as required for the method. But it is still a promising development and under further development. Objective 7: Employing integrated dual DO/pH sensors for digital cell culture in a multiparameter toxicity assay. Similar to objective 3, this objective could be realized almost fully. We described optical pH and oxygen sensor, we realized a suitable layout for a multisensor, we implemented an antimicrobial susceptibility test based on an integrated oxygen sensor and we could show that the metabolism of various types of cells could be followed with a DMF-based integrated pH sensor. But there are still some optimizations needed before the platform can be routinely operated and the results published

26310119.label: Major findings and research outcome
26310119.value: Within this project the chemistry and microfabrication techniques to realize three different types of optical sensors were devised, temperature, oxygen and pH sensors. The approaches that were found to work differ in the type of sensors. However good results could be achieved with amorphous fluoropolymers in fluorinated hydrocarbon as solvents. We identified Hyflon AD60 as a polymer that exhibited a good combination of compatibility with digital microfluidics as well as favourable sensor physics and chemistry and used it both for temperature and oxygen sensors but in principle other fluoropolymers also showed promising results. The temperature sensor was realized using CsPbBr3 quantum dots in Hyflon AD60 (part C publ. 1), the oxygen sensor was a perfluorinated platinum porphyrin in HyflonAD60 (part C publ. 2). Regarding the pH sensor the main challenge was to create hydrophilic spots on the digital microfluidic surface, which was realized using a tape shielding method. The sensor then used a fluorescein derivative covalently bound to poly-2-hydroxyethylmethacrylate (part C publ. 3). All sensor microfabrication techniques are suitable or can be modified to include different probes and sensor chemistry. A sensor surface within digital microfluidics covered mostly with hydrophobic oxygen sensor was introduced hydrophilic spots of polydopamine-silver-polydopamine to allow for mammalian cell culture (part C publ. 4), This surface fulfils all the requirements for a dual pH-oxygen or pH-temperature sensor. Regarding the application, the temperature sensor was used for investigation of the temperature effects of many digital microfluidic operations (part C publ. 1) and could reveal temperature changes of up to 18 K in common digital microfluidic steps with implications for many digital microfluidic procedures. The oxygen sensor was used to construct a miniaturized and automated antimicrobial susceptibility assay, and may be used to test a variety of antibiotics or other classes of compounds for the cell-toxic effects. (part C, publ. 2). The pH sensor was employed to investigate the extracellular pH of cell cultures depending on the type of cell and metabolic conditions. It could show a number of findings, e.g. cancer and non-cancer cells could be differentiated, and the effect of anti-cancer drugs and other common metabolites such as glucose tracked (part C, publ. 3). The dual functional surface described in part C, publ. 4 has been demonstrated in an antimicrobial susceptibility assay and a growth inhibition assay and its main use is in the selective growth of mammalian cells with no contamination of bacterial cells.

26310119.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26310119.value: Having established sensors for three different parameters within this project, further action can be taken in the following directions. A) Integration of sensors for different analytes. For example various cation or anion sensors could be integrated using the protocol for the pH sensor as a template. The chemistry and microfabrication of oxygen and temperature sensors could be modified e.g. for a carbon dioxide sensor. B) Different applications for the integrated sensors. Whereas the project was limited mostly to cell-based techniques, other bioanalytical or biomedical applications could be pursued or in entirely different fields such as environmental or materials analysis. C) Application or combination of the developed techniques for multisensors or other functional surfaces in digital microfluidics. The proposed course of action is to use the digital microfluidics integrated sensors in follow-up projects. Our recently granted general research fund project aiming at the combination of digital microfluidics with machine learning is a good example for that as it employs the signal of the integrated sensors as the source which artificial intelligence will use to learn, and, among other goals, AI is planned to be used to improve the sensors with respect to sensitivity, selectivity, versatility, and robustness.

26310119.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26310119.value: Within this project the technique of digital microfluidics was further developed and refined to include optical sensors for temperature, oxygen and pH. These sensors are thin films or spots of suitable molecular or nanostructural probes in polymer matrices. They could be integrated into digital microfluidics using multistep fabrication protocols. For temperature and oxygen sensors suitable probes could be integrated into hydrophobic fluoropolymers and brought onto the microchips using spin coating or blade coating. pH sensor spots could be realized by shielding small areas on microchips using wafer dicing tape during deposition of the inner layer. The tape was then removed and suitable precursor solutions deposited and dried. Applications of these platforms could be demonstrated in antimicrobial susceptibility tests, growth inhibition assays and extracellular pH monitoring. The temperature sensor could also be employed for fundamental investigations into the effect of digital microfluidic commands, in particular employed voltages for droplet movements on the local temperature and significant temperature effects could be found. These results will hopefully aid the further development of digital microfluidics which due to its miniaturization and automation capabilities is a promising and green, sustainable testing and analysis technique.

26500019.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26500019.value: With 3.5 billion searches every day on Google alone, there is an increasingly important global trend for practitioners to shift more expenditure from traditional channels such as television to search advertising. For example, just within Hong Kong, total advertising spending is expected to reach USD8 billion in 2021 and the TV share of advertising spending is expected to be overtaken by the internet share by 20%. This gives rise to another important trend for coordinating search advertising with TV advertising, for more effective marketing strategies. For example, when viewers see a TV ad for pizza, many will be hungry and look to order take-out food. The ad spurs them to think about the advertised brand, with the goal of prompting an online search for the product. In this type of strategy, companies should adjust their bidding strategies immediately (e.g. for keywords, bids, targeting demographics and ad copy design), to secure or steal the expected online traffic and potential sales triggered within the few minutes of the TV commercial. However, advertisers constantly struggle with their spending and coordination strategies and Google admits that advertisers wasted their money on more than half of internet ads. Most existing studies just focus on the relationship between increased TV advertising expenditure and online search volume, mainly due to the complexity of this problem or/and the challenge of getting high-quality cross-channel advertising data. Therefore, there is a great need to understand more deeply the impact of TV advertising on search and on the effectiveness of search campaigns. In this research, we aim to fill this gap by collaborating with the Microsoft Bing search engine and by leveraging real-world experiments in two U.S. industries, wireless and fast food. In each industry, our focal company systematically turned off its TV advertising for a long time, which gives us unique opportunities to understand and measure the impact of the focal brand’s TV advertising on the effectiveness of the search advertising across competing brands and in several dimensions, such as keyword types, search device, search location and time. Ultimately, the results of our research will help advertisers optimize their advertising expenditure across different channels and potentially save billions of dollars. 随着仅谷歌每天35亿的搜索量，全世界的广告商都逐渐地将他们的预算从传统的电视广告转投入搜索广告。比如仅香港，总广告开支预计将于2021年达到80亿美元，而同时互联网电子广告的预算将超出电视广告20%。为了设计更为有效市场营销策略，这种趋势推动了协调搜索广告和电视广告的需要。比如说，当消费者收看到一则关于某披萨品牌的电视广告，许多观众会觉得饥饿然后想定外卖。这则广告使消费者想起了这个品牌的披萨，进而促使消费者去上网搜索这个品牌的信息。在这种情况下，广告商应该立刻调整他们对搜索广告竞标的策略（例如关键词的选择，价格，广告文本），以获得这些电视广告在接下来的几分钟内引起的网上搜索高峰以及其潜在的销售额。然而，如何协调多渠道广告策略对广告上来说仍是个未结的问题，并且谷歌也承认广告商多余一半的网上广告投资是完全的浪费。由于多渠道广告研究的复杂性和相关高质量数据的缺失，目前已有的学术研究只探索了增长的电视广告支出和在线搜索量的关系。因此，学术界和业界需要更多地理解电视广告对搜索广告的影响。 在这个科研项目里，我们通过和微软的Bing搜索引擎合作来填补这方面的空白。具体地说，我们利用两个在美国不同行业（通讯和快餐）在现实世界的实验来回答这个问题。在每一个实验中，我们关注的公司长时间地系统性地取消了在电视上的所有广告。这给了我们很好的机会来理解和测量电视广告对搜索广告的影响，分别从打广告的品牌和其竞争品牌的角度来看。我们还会研究这个关系如何会随着下面这些因素的影响：搜索关键字，搜索平台，搜索的时间和地点。最终，我们的研究结果将会帮助广告商优化他们在不同渠道的广告预算，并因此帮助广告商节省很多资金。

26500019.label: Realisation of objectives
26500019.value: All of the research objectives have been accomplished through one publication in Marketing Science and one working paper that is currently under the second round of review at the Journal of Marketing. Both are listed below. [1] Liu, Jia, and Shawndra Hill (2021), “Frontiers: Moment Marketing: Measuring Dynamics in Cross-channel Ad Effectiveness.” Marketing Science, 40 (1), 13-22. [2] Liu, Jia, Shawndra Hill, and David Rothschild (2023), “The Dynamic Impact of Temporally Turning off TV Ad on Search: Evidence from the U.S. Telecom Industry.” under 2nd round review at the Journal of Marketing First, the objective of “develop synthetic control method to measure the impact of turning off TV advertising on brand’s search traffic and conversations (for both the advertised brands and their competitors)” is completed in both papers [1] and [2] using slightly different techniques and data contexts. Specifically, paper [1] uses regression methods to study the U.S. pizza (fast food) industry, and paper [2] applies the generalized synthetic control method in studying the U.S. wireless telecom industry. Second, the objective of “quantify how such impact varies across factors like keyword groups, search device, and geographic location” is completed in both papers [1] and [2]. Specifically, paper [1] examines the treatment heterogeneity across keyword groups, search device, and geographic location, while paper [2] only focuses on keyword group. Both papers show significant heterogeneous treatment effects across these factors. Third, the objective of “from the advertised (focal) brand’s perspective, understand the relationship between its TV advertising and search advertising. In particular, answer: (a) when, where and what types of keywords an advertiser should bid for corresponding to its own TV commercials; (b) whether a focal brand’s present or past long-term TV advertising can improve the click-through rate and conversation rate of its search results; and (c) whether the above effect is different for organic and sponsored results” is completed in paper [1]. Our main finding is that advertisers can increase cross-channel ad effectiveness by implementing search advertising when the TV advertising expenditure is higher. The effect is particularly stronger for the sponsored results, compared with the organic results. Fourth, the objective of “from the perspective of competitors of the advertised (focal) brand, understand the relationship between the focal brand’s TV advertising and search advertising by its competitors. In particular, answer: (a) whether and when a focal brand’s TV advertising may help improve the effectiveness of search advertising by its competitors; (b) whether small advertisers should free-ride on TV advertising by big competitors by stealing their online traffic through search advertising; (c) how competitors' (present or past long-term) TV advertising affect the click volume, click-through rate and conversation rate of the focal brand’s search results” is mostly completed in paper [2]. We find significant evidence that competitors can also benefit by poaching each other’s online search traffic by bidding on competitors’ branded keywords when the competitors’ TV advertising expenditure is high. Fifth, the objective of “understand how the information that consumers acquire influence their online behaviour, including what search keywords to use, which products to browse, which products to purchase’’ is completed in the paper [2]. By examining the content of the TV advertising, we observe how the keyword usage is changed in online search behavior. In completing this objective, we also collected data through running incentivized online experiments. This incurs additional expenditure that is covered by the “outsourcing” category. The “outsourcing” category was not used for the initial claimed purpose because due to the pandemic, I didn’t travel at all to companies to acquire the required information or data. I instead used the funding to conduct another form of research that could help complete my research objectives.

26500019.label: Major findings and research outcome
26500019.value: This research project involves two papers: one is already published and the other is a working paper (in the review process). I summarize their findings separately. In the first paper, we study moment marketing which is a new strategy that entails the ability to synchronize online advertising (e.g., sponsored search) in real time with relevant offline events such as TV ads. We take advantage of a unique opportunity for causal estimation in this research area by leveraging large exogenous variation in TV advertising expenditure over a long period, while at the same time having access to granular consumer search data under relatively stable sponsored search advertising strategies. Utilizing this novel setup, we provide the first empirical evidence that TV-moment-based search advertising could be effective for optimizing sponsored search advertising for both TV-advertised brands and their competitors. We also document the mechanisms driving such cross-channel advertising effects. Specifically, TV advertising can change the quality of online search traffic (e.g., who searches, where they search, and how they search) in the moments following a TV ad, so that an average searcher responds differently to subsequent search results. In the working paper, we measure the effects of major TV advertisers’ temporary discontinuation of TV advertising on consumer keyword search over time, by leveraging a large-scaled quasi-experiment in the U.S. wireless telecom industry in which the focal brand stopped its TV advertising for one randomly chosen week. The causal identification challenge of this event study, involving continuous treatment variables, lies in having appropriate control groups for eliminating unobserved confounding factors. We address this challenge by applying the generalized synthetic control estimator (GSC) to debiase interfering “treated” and “control” units when conducting counterfactual analysis. We find that the focal brand’s intervention resulted in a significant 5% reduction of its daily search volume. This effect initially occurred after two days, but once regular TV advertising was resumed, it took two weeks for search volume to return to the prior level. In addition, we find large treatment heterogeneity across topical search categories. For instance, while search traffic was more likely to be reduced (up to 30% per day) for searches that are relevant to the content of TV ads (e.g., promotion and plan), this effect wore off quickly. Lastly, we find a positive spillover effect of the intervention on the focal brand’s competitors, which, however, is usually very short-lived.

26500019.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26500019.value: For the second paper, it is currently under review for the second round at the Journal of Marketing. We hope to go through this process and make the paper published eventually.

26500019.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26500019.value: “Moment Marketing’’ refers to a new strategy that entails the ability to synchronize online advertising (e.g., sponsored search) in real time with relevant offline events such as TV ads. Our research examines whether and how “moment marketing” is effective as a cross-channel advertising strategy, by leveraging a quasi-experimental data set. We found out that ads on TV can influence how and what people search for online right after seeing the TV ad. This means advertisers could use TV moments to optimize their cross-channel ad effectiveness. In another study, we examine the effects of temporally shutting down TV ads for major advertisers’ online search traffic, by leveraging a quasi-experimental data set. We find that for the focal brand involved in our study, there was a 5% drop in how much people searched for the brand online. It took two weeks for search volume to bounce back after TV ads started again. We also saw that the drop in searches depended on what the TV ads were about. For example, ads about promotions led to a bigger drop in searches. In simple terms, our research shows that TV ads are more important than we thought—they don't just make people aware of products but also lead them to look for different types of information online. This can give businesses new ways to plan their advertising across different channels.

26501519.label: Project Title(Chinese)
26501519.value: 求职者与受雇者视角下企业社会责任问题研究

26501519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26501519.value: Despite a growing body of research showing that most people perceive an organization’s corporate social responsibility (CSR) positively (Rupp & Mallory, 2015), what remains relatively unknown are the conditions under which some people are turned off by or indifferent to an organization’s CSR activities. Using attribution theory as an overarching framework (Heider, 1958; Kelley, 1967; Shaver, 1985), I propose that individuals will view an organization that engages in CSR activities focusing on external stakeholders (i.e., external CSR) as inauthentic when the organization does not also engage in activities that benefit its own employees (i.e., internal CSR). In other words, individuals will perceive an organization that is engaging in external CSR to be authentic only if it also engages in internal CSR. Furthermore, perceptions of an organization’s authenticity potentially affect two groups of individuals – job seekers and current employees. First, job seekers who view a potential employer as inauthentic will be less attracted to that organization. Second, employees who view their current employer as inauthentic will display less organizational commitment, which might further harm their in-role performance and organizational citizenship behavior. Three complementary studies are proposed to test the proposed theoretical model. Study 1 is an archival data study of the Fortune 500 companies, and examines how their actual CSR practices relate to how job seekers evaluate them (i.e., company rank on Global LinkedIn Top Companies list, which is based on 500 millions of LinkedIn users’ searches and page views), as well as how employees evaluate them (i.e., company evaluation on Glassdoor.com, a website where employees anonymously review companies and their management). Study 2 is an experimental study which examines the causal relationships and mechanisms proposed in the theoretical model using individuals’ evaluations of a company after reviewing its online profile. Finally, Study 3 is a multi-source field survey study across a variety of organizations and industries, involving employees and their respective supervisors. Employees will evaluate their company’s CSR activities as well as their attitudes toward their organization. Supervisors will evaluate their employees’ work behaviors. Findings from the proposed research are expected to make theoretical contributions to the literatures on micro approaches to CSR, human resource management, and authenticity in organizations. The proposed research also offers practical advice for organizations on when their external CSR activities may be perceived negatively, and thus, how they should strategically present their CSR activities to avoid such negative effects. 尽管越来越多的研究成果表明大多数人对企业社会责任有着积极的认识，但在何种情况下人们会改变想法甚至变得漠不关心尚未明晰。我认为，当企业仅参与针对外部利益相关者的企业社会责任活动(即外部企业社会责任)，而不重视有利于内部员工的企业社会责任活动时(即内部企业社会责任)，人们往往会认为它是不可信的。换言之，只有企业同时参与内部和外部企业社会责任活动，其行为才会被认为是真实的。此外，对企业真实性的看法对求职者和受雇者都将产生潜在的影响。首先，求职者不会被不可信的潜在雇主吸引。其次，认为雇主不可信的受雇者的组织承诺将降低，这可能进一步影响其工作绩效和组织公民行为。因此本研究将为企业说明他们的外部企业社会责任活动何时可能产生消极影响，并提供实操性建议以帮助企业合理地展示其企业社会责任并避免产生负面影响。

26502519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26502519.value: When a CEO says “we are confident about future product sales”, does he really mean it? A vocal cue is a sound of the voice used to send a message. Vocal cues play a significant role in nonverbal communication, as the cues either affirm or discredit the message. Nowadays, firm executive communication with investors and analysts goes far beyond financial statements and numbers. Executives communicate information not only verbally through press releases and SEC filings, but also nonverbally through investor meetings and earnings conference calls. This project will examine the information role played in financial markets by nonverbal communication, voice. To study the information role of voice in financial markets, we look at firm quarterly earnings call. Earnings call is an important channel for executives to communicate information to investors and analysts. A burgeoning body of research has adopted text analysis framework to study the executives’ verbal cues (such as language used) in earnings calls, and it has shown that the verbal language used by executives can predict firm fundamentals and stock returns. However, as we know that vocal cues in nonverbal communication can either affirm or discredit verbal language, this project aims to ask the following research question: controlling for the language used by executives during earnings calls, can vocal cues create additional information that adds to or otherwise affects the firm information dissemination and assimilation? In this project, I will obtain earnings call audio recordings and textual transcripts for S&P 1500 companies in recent five years. Using speech recognition models built by deep learning algorithms, I will align sentences spoken by CEOs with corresponding audio clips. I will then extract vocal cue features from audio clips, and examine whether CEO’s vocal cues change as he answers analyst questions, especially whether the topic of questions is the stimulus for the vocal cues change. I will also examine the relationship between vocal cue changes and firm fundamentals, controlling for firm financial numbers and CEO verbal language. This study will strengthen our understanding of how the information contained in nonverbal communication affects financial markets. It answers a call for the study of unstructured multimedia data to explore for rich insights, and tackles the formidable methodological challenges entailed in analyzing unstructured multimedia data. It also answers a recent call for research of innovating the financial industry through emerging information technologies. The outcome of this research will have practical implications for analysts, investors and regulators. 當CEO說到"我們對未來產品銷售充滿信心",他是否言不由衷? 人聲音的音頻特征(如語氣語調)會傳遞出信息並且在交流對話中扮演著重要的作用.日常經驗告訴我們不僅僅說話內容,說話方式可以更好的幫助我們判斷信息的可靠程度.如今公司的高層們和投資者分析師的交流已經遠遠超過了書面上的財報數字和文本.這些交流場合包括了投資者會議和財務電話會議.這個研究項目旨在分析公司高管在財務電話會議中的聲音在金融市場中傳遞的信息作用. 上市公司的財務電話會議是壹個非常重要的和投資者以及分析師溝通的渠道.大量的研究使用了文本分析方法去研究公司高管的在財務電話會議中所說的文本內容, 並且發現高管使用的語言詞匯可以預測公司的基本表現和股票收益.因此,我們想通過這個研究回答以下問題:財報會議中高管的說話方式是否可以對投資者和分析師提供相對於說話內容的額外信息? 在研究中,我會獲得過去幾年美國S&P1500上市公司財務電話會議的記錄文本和音頻錄音.使用最新的深度學習算法,我可以從音頻中抽取和文本對應的音頻特征信息,並且去分析CEO的說話方式是否在回答分析師提問時有變化.這樣的變化是否和問題內容有關.這樣細微的說話方式變化是否和金融市場的反應和公司的表現相關.通過這個研究,我們可以加深了解非文字信息對金融市場影響.在大數據的今天,我們相信對多媒體數據的研究(文本,音頻),可以幫助我們更好的利用信息科技來從事金融市場活動.該研究對金融監管機構同樣有現實意義.

26502519.label: Realisation of objectives
26502519.value: This proposed research seeks to explore the informative role of voice in financial markets. Alternative data, such as text and audio, offers unprecedented opportunities for actionable decision-making within the financial industry, especially in areas like portfolio and risk management. However, due to significant methodological challenges, the anticipated business value from unstructured alternative data remains unrealized. Hence, this research proposal holds direct significance for both academia and market professionals. To achieve the research goals, I tackle research and methodological challenges through the following steps: First, I gathered a unique dataset comprising both textual transcripts and audio recordings of 6,047 earnings conference call samples. I selected constituent firms from the S&P 500 index for the sample because of their prominence and manageability. To our knowledge, this dataset is the first to encompass both textual and audio recordings of earnings calls. Second, given that an earnings call can be lengthy, often extending up to an hour, it presents considerable challenges for subsequent analyses. To counter this, I employed a text-audio alignment algorithm to pinpoint the exact start and end audio markers of each sentence. This enables analysis of managers' vocal/verbal cues on a more detailed, sentence-by-sentence basis. I utilized Praat, an open-source software, to extract vocal features. Third, viewing the earnings conference call as a series of spoken sentences with their respective vocal recordings, I utilized a deep learning algorithm – a long-short term memory (LSTM) neural network. This LSTM algorithm captures the sequential nuances of managers' vocal cues and integrates them with verbal cues. This innovative approach of incorporating textual and audio data for predictive tasks serves as a notable contribution to the field. These three foundational steps drive the primary aim of the research – understanding the value of voice in financial markets. To investigate the informative role of voice in predicting firms’ financial market outcomes, we selected financial risk as our primary research variable. Financial risk is defined as the standard deviation of a firm’s stock returns over a specified period. Rather than directly forecasting stock returns, it's generally believed that the risk associated with a stock can be forecasted using publicly available information. Financial risk is pivotal in numerous tasks associated with financial markets, including investment portfolio management and risk assessment. It's also a fundamental element in many established option pricing models, and accurate risk forecasting is essential for derivatives trading. The derivatives markets constitute significant segments of global capital markets. For instance, trading in equity options alone reached 7.5 trillion U.S. dollars in the first half of 2021. Hence, the capacity to predict the financial risk of publicly listed firms should be of considerable importance to practitioners, scholars, and regulators. To examine the information role of vocal cues in predicting financial risks, I considered the following hypotheses. H1: Incorporating managers’ vocal cues will improve the accuracy of financial risk prediction, compared to existing methods that use firm fundamentals, historical risks, and managers’ verbal cues. H2: A two-stage LSTM model is a better design for the sequential pattern learning of vocal cues and vocal-verbal integrations and will improve the accuracy of financial risk prediction compared to existing machine learning models. H3: Using basic vocal cues will improve the accuracy of financial risk prediction compared to using high-level vocal constructs. I designed DeepVoice, a system for examining the information role of vocal cues in predicting financial risks. In the experiment, I demonstrated that by incorporating managers’ vocal cues, we can achieve a more accurate financial risk prediction than with existing methods that rely on firm fundamentals, historical risks, and managers’ verbal cues. Specifically, DeepVoice's performance surpasses the market benchmark prediction by 7.31%, 8.34%, 4.28%, 2.26%, and 7.45% for 3-day, 5-day, 10-day, 30-day, and 60-day forecast horizons, respectively, in out-of-sample tests. This result sheds light on the first research objective: to investigate whether a manager’s tone of voice can provide insights into a firm's market reactions. Additionally, I conducted a cross-sectional analysis to assess how DeepVoice's enhancements vary based on different firm characteristics. I discovered that DeepVoice exhibits superior predictive capabilities for firms that show higher fluctuations in their financial fundamentals. In other words, for firms experiencing notable material shifts, the managers' vocal information during earnings conference calls offers supplementary insights beyond the quantitative data found in the financial statements. This insight further enriches our initial research objective. This finding further contributes to the first research objective. I also investigated how a manager’s vocal cues change during an earnings conference call. Using the earnings conference calls from Advanced Micro Devices, Inc (AMD) in the first and second quarters of 2017 as a case study, I observed that the CEO’s vocal cues underwent more noticeable shifts during the question-and-answer sections, especially when she was being questioned by financial analysts. This finding further contributes to the second research objective. Additionally, I explored the potential of managers' vocal cues to predict firm misreporting, essentially looking at managerial deception. However, my experimental results did not yield positive findings. Managers' vocal cues didn't enhance the predictive accuracy for firm misreporting in out-of-sample tests. A plausible reason might be that financial misreporting is exceptionally challenging to detect, especially when relying on alternative data sources like the spoken words and vocal tones of managers. I aim to delve deeper into this research question in my future studies. This finding concludes the third research objective. Regarding the fourth research objective, which seeks to "pin down the informational role of nonverbal communication in financial markets," the developed DeepVoice system provides a robust foundation for this aim. By adopting a design science and predictive analytics methodology, DeepVoice capably quantifies the significance of vocal cues in the financial realm. Beyond fulfilling the proposed research objectives, I also explored a new dimension: the economic significance of vocal cues in financial markets. Specifically, I employed a long-short straddle strategy for option trading. Here's how my strategy functioned: from the forecast model, I extracted data indicating whether the volatility over the next horizon (60 days) would rise or fall. I then ranked the change in volatility (forecasted volatility minus current volatility) in our out-of-sample data and used this ranking to signal buying or selling for a straddle. I took long positions for top-ranked stocks (those anticipated to experience the most significant increases in volatility) and short positions for the bottom-ranked ones (those expected to see the largest decreases in volatility). The portfolio return was computed as the aggregate of the straddle returns. Simulation results indicate that DeepVoice yields a return of 8.89%, marking a significant 91.2% enhancement compared to the market model's return of 4.65%. This experiment underscores that the predictive potency of vocal cues can indeed be leveraged for tangible economic benefits.

26502519.label: Major findings and research outcome
26502519.value: This research introduces a system named DeepVoice that utilizes managers' tone of voice during earnings conference calls to predict a company's financial market risks. Our primary findings include: 1. DeepVoice significantly enhances risk forecasting accuracy compared to existing models that rely solely on managers' verbal information. 2. The accuracy improvement can lead to substantial economic benefits in options trading. 3. We discovered that managers' vocal information during earnings conference calls offers added more predictive value for firms with greater uncertainty in their financial fundamentals. 4. We also observed variations in managers' vocal cues in the question-and-answer segment when they respond to analysts' queries. The outcomes of this research have been rewarding. Our findings were published in an MIS Quarterly paper titled "Unlocking the Power of Voice for Financial Risk Prediction: A Theory-Driven Deep Learning Design Approach." MIS Quarterly is a leading journal in the field of management information systems. The prototype of the DeepVoice system can analyze and predict a company's financial risk in real-time during an earnings conference call, showcasing great potential for adoption by industry practitioners.

26502519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26502519.value: Building on the progress of the current research, this project can delve deeper into the following questions: 1. While the present research primarily focuses on the risk aspect of financial decision-making, it would be intriguing to determine whether the multi-dimensional vocal cues can be transformed into a singular "vocal factor" and then assess this factor's effectiveness in empirical asset pricing models. 2. Our research has determined that vocal information provides enhanced predictive power for firms with higher uncertainties in their financial fundamentals. It would be valuable to investigate how the predictive strength of this vocal information correlates with other specific firm characteristics in a cross-sectional analysis, such as firm size, value, or quality. 3. The research currently uses a sample of S&P 500 firms. It would be informative to see if similar findings apply to relatively smaller firms, like those in the S&P 1500.

26502519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26502519.value: This research examines how to utilize alternative data, such as voice recordings and texts, to enhance financial and investment decisions. Although there's significant potential in using voice recordings, texts, and other alternative data for investment risk management, extracting valuable insights has been challenging due to methodological hurdles. In this study, we developed "DeepVoice," a system that doesn't just focus on what a company's managers say during their earnings conference calls, but also on how they say it. DeepVoice predicts financial risks with greater accuracy. We designed DeepVoice using a novel two-step deep learning algorithm that blends managers' spoken words with their tone of voice. We tested DeepVoice on over 6,000 recorded calls from large U.S. public firms spanning four years. It outperformed existing systems in predicting a firm’s financial market risks. This suggests that investors can make more informed decisions and better understand their investment risks. In essence, this research underscores that not only the content but also the manner in which managers speak is crucial, especially in the financial domain.

26502619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26502619.value: 客户资本 - 客户对公司的品牌忠诚度 - 是公司最重要的无形资产之一，因为它通过为公司创造大量进入壁垒和持久优势来决定稳定需求流的能力。发展和维持客户资本对于公司的生存，增长和盈利至关重要。 在这个项目中，我们计划研究公司之间的对客户资本的竞争对企业债券估值的影响。公司通过设定较低的产品价格去吸引更多的客户。在公司不相互合作的情况下，固定的总客户群会激发公司间掠夺性定价行为，因为一家公司的客户群的增长必然意味着另一家公司客户群的损失。这种针对客户群的定价竞争会促进公司间相互合作，通过协商维持高价格以实现更高的利润率。然而，公司间相互合作的激励会随着总体经济状况的变化而变化。当总需求低时，公司间的协作更难进行，因此在经济衰退期间公司间更容易放弃协作定价而导致价格战。这种内生的顺周期加价会导致公司承担更大的系统性风险，因为公司的现金流会产生更高波动性，从而增加公司债券的违约风险。因此，我们的理论提供了一个新的角度来解释公司的信用利差和低杠杆。 该项目的执行包括三个主要步骤。首先，我们编写一个简单博弈论模型，以阐明企业内生形成协同定价均衡，以及这种协同定价的激励如何随总体经济状况的变化而变化。其次，我们通过将动态随机博弈理论嵌入到结构动态企业模型中来开发一个新的定量模型。第三，我们使用信用和价格的微观数据来估计模型，从而研究模型对产品价格和违约风险的预测。我们将检查模型的预测是否与我们在数据中观察到现象一致。 该项目的最终目标是开发一种新的定量模型，以进一步了解产品市场与金融市场之间的联系，并帮助我们思考对如何对两个市场进行相辅相成的政策干预。在标准的公司模型中（例如Leland 1994），现金流是外生假设的。这种模型无法分析产品市场和金融市场之间的相互作用。因此，这种模型也很难被用于分析产品市场政策（如反垄断法）对金融市场中公司违约和信贷利差等的影响，反之亦然。

26502619.label: Realisation of objectives
26502619.value: Explanations for expenditure: Our actual expenditure on research staff is 546,641.54, which is higher than the approved expenditure (351,240.00). As a result, we had less expenditure in other categories (general expenses and conferences). We spent more on research staff because we hired 12 undergraduate RAs to help us manually check the matching of firms across different datasets for roughly six months. The manual check was conducted to improve the accuracy of firm-matching based on a fuzzy-matching algorithm. This was not expected when we initially wrote the proposal. I am sorry for overusing the budget on research staff. We have achieved the following objectives: 1.We developed two models. In both models, firms cash flows are micro-founded by firms' strategic pricing and competition for customer capital. The first model is analytically tractable and it combines the Merton model of credit risk (Merton, 1974) with a repeated-game model that allows for tacit collusion (e.g., Fudenberg and Maskin, 1986; Rotemberg and Saloner, 1986). The second model is a full-fledged quantitative model that generalizes the first model across several dimensions. This quantitative model is solved numerically with the following objectives. First, we aim to validate that the primary economic mechanisms and their implications from the simple model remain robust under more general and more realistic specifications. Second, by aligning parameters with data moments, we aim to gauge the quantitative strength of the mechanism and evaluate its empirical relevance within the context of this quantitative model. Finally, this quantitative model enables us to study important theoretical implications that are beyond the capacity of the simple model, like the effect of entry barriers on predatory pricing behaviors. 2. Our first model clearly illustrates the interaction between financial leverage decisions and product market competition, which in turn endogenously determines a firm’s profitability and its risk of financial distress. This illustration sheds light on the key insights of both the competition-distress feedback loop and the financial contagion effect. Our second model takes these mechanisms to data and quantitatively evaluate their empirical relevance. 3. We provide three sets of empirical results in Online Appendix to support the main theoretical implications in this paper. First, for evidence of the feedback effect, we find that industry-level profit margins load negatively on the discount rate and more so in industries where firms are closer to their default boundaries. This finding is consistent with our model’s prediction that higher discount rates reduce firms’ collusion capacity, and that the competition-distress feedback effect is stronger when firms’ distances to default are lower. Second, we provide evidence of the financial contagion effect. By sorting the top six firms (ranked by sales) within each industry into three groups based on their distances to default, we find that adverse idiosyncratic shocks to the financially distressed group diminish the profit margins of the financially healthy group. Furthermore, we find that the within-industry spillover effect is more pronounced in the industries facing lower entry threats (i.e., higher entry barriers) as predicted by our quantitative model. Third, we provide evidence of the model’s implications for the profitability-leverage relationship. Specifically, we show in the data that industries with lower profit margins or higher idiosyncratic left-tail risk are associated with higher leverage ratios. Moreover, the negative profitability-leverage relationship across industries becomes insignificant after controlling for idiosyncratic left-tail risk.

26502619.label: Major findings and research outcome
26502619.value: We demonstrate that the interplay between tactical competition and the threat of financial distress engenders a distressed competition mechanism, leading to a competition-distress feedback loop and a novel form of financial contagion. These feedback and contagion effects will influence a firm’s credit risk and the overall financial stability of the industry. Furthermore, by introducing strategic market competition into the tradeoff theory of capital structure, our model helps resolve the longstanding “profitability-leverage puzzle.”

26502619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26502619.value: We are currently extending the model with time-varying discount rates and industry hetergeneity to shed light on industry-level distress anomaly.

26502619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26502619.value: The competition-distress feedback loop proposed in this research project yields two important implications about capital structure. First, it diminishes firms’ incentives to increase leverage, as higher leverage curtails their ability to collude and reduces profitability. This effect introduces a novel source of financial distress costs. Second, the feedback loop provides an explanation for the profitability-leverage puzzle at the industry level. Profitability is negatively associated with leverage across both firms and industries, a robust empirical pattern that is at odds with the traditional tradeoff theory of capital structure Our model can account for this negative relationship by endogenously connecting profitability with financial leverage. Specifically, industries with higher profitability tend to be those in which firms enjoy higher capacity for tacit collusion. This capacity is particularly vulnerable to the financial distress risk. As a result, to preserve their collusion capacity, firms in these more profitable industries opt for lower leverage.
