26503919.label: Realisation of objectives
26503919.value: All the objectives of the project have been successfully achieved. Objective 1 aims “to generalize the literature on private meetings between institutional investors to the international setting.” This project accomplished this objective by compiling a novel large sample of international corporate access events where managers can meet with institutional investors for private information. Unlike prior literature that focuses on one-country studies, it presents empirical evidence of the market reactions to these information events for both U.S. and non-U.S. firms. In addition, prior literature studies the immediate consequences of corporate access events in isolation. By focusing on conferences as prominent corporate access events in the global market, this project identifies firms’ overall voluntary disclosure strategies around conference meetings as an important determinant of the economic impact of these information events. Objective 2 aims “to examine how the informativeness of private meetings varies with country-level characteristics such as investor protection, audit enforcement, mandatory disclosure requirement, and media penetration.”. This project empirically investigates the association between market reactions to corporate access events and country-level characteristics that may potentially affect the informativeness of corporate access events. This includes factors such as investor protection (captured by the rule of law from the World Bank), audit enforcement (measured by the audit enforcement index from Brown et al., 2014), media penetration (measured by the internet infrastructure data from the World Bank), and mandatory disclosure requirements (disclosure requirement index from La Porta et al., 2006). Objective 3 aims “to provide important inputs for regulators working to curb selective disclosure with consideration of the local institutional infrastructure.” This project generalizes prior literature to the international setting and presents large-sample evidence that investors indeed gain private information from meeting with managers on corporate access events in the global market, which raises fairness concerns for regulators. In addition, it shows that managers strategically time their voluntary disclosures around conference meetings to maximize the informational benefits. These documented empirical patterns are also significantly related to local country-level institutional characteristics, such as the strength of the rule of law and information infrastructure. These findings should provide useful insights for regulators. In summary, all three objectives have been fully addressed in this project, contributing to the literature on international corporate access events that allow institutional investors to have private access to managers and the role of country-level characteristics, and providing valuable inputs for regulators.

26503919.label: Major findings and research outcome
26503919.value: This project documents that corporate access events, which enable institutional investors to potentially gain private information from meeting managers, are associated with significant market reactions, measured by short window abnormal stock returns and share turnovers. As expected, the significant market reactions to corporate access events are prevalent in both U.S. and non-U.S. firms. In addition, it finds that the informativeness of corporate access events is significantly positive in countries with stronger rule of law (a proxy of overall investor protection) and with better information infrastructure (as a measure of media development). However, there is no systematic evidence that the informativeness of these information events is associated with country-level measures of audit enforcement and mandatory disclosure requirements. By focusing on conferences as the most prominent corporate access events in global investor relation programs, this project finds that managers strategically provide more disclosures of positive news before conference meetings to increase the informational benefits of conferences. The coordination of voluntary disclosures is found to be an important determinant that affects the informativeness of conferences where institutional investors gain an information advantage by meeting with managers. Firms with greater shareholder pressures, lower visibility, and less concentrated ownership are more likely to strategically provide voluntary disclosures around conferences. Similarly, the strategic disclosure strategy is also significantly positive in country-level characteristics, including the strength of investor protection, capital market development, and information infrastructure. Based on discussions with senior experts in this area, presentation feedback, and the comments from the journal review process, the related paper gradually evolved to focus more on conferences as the preeminent corporate access events and disclosures around conferences as an important determinant to increase the information benefits of conferences. The culmination of these findings is reflected in the latest version of the paper, titled "Strategically Timed Voluntary Disclosures before Conferences: Global Evidence." This paper is currently under the status of revise and resubmit at the Journal of International Accounting Research.

26503919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26503919.value: The current project focuses on the institutional characteristics of firms' home countries. To extend this research, we can explore how the economic consequences of corporate access events are affected by pair-wise institutional characteristics (i.e., the geographical, legal, cultural, and linguistic distance between investors and firms). This can help us get a deeper understanding of how managers overcome various frictions to mitigate information asymmetries through corporate access events. In addition, the findings of the project on international corporate access events in general can be repackaged.

26503919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26503919.value: Managers around the world attend various corporate access events to communicate with investors. This project documents that investors find these corporate access events informative for both U.S. and non-U.S. firms. The informativeness of the events is greater in countries with stronger investor protection and better information infrastructure. Specifically for conferences, one of the most prominent corporate access events, managers strategically provide more voluntary disclosure of good news before conference meetings to increase the informational benefits of conferences. This coordination of disclosure strategies is also more significant in countries with stronger investor protection and financial institutions.

26504219.label: Project Objectives
26504219.value: From a theoretical perspective, we aim to develop a parsimonious model that captures the spillover and carryover effects in the online advertising ecosystem, and leverage it to design optimal budget allocation strategies to maximize the effectiveness of a multi-channel ad campaign given a finite budget. In preceding studies in marketing, heuristic allocation strategies are suggested. However, their performance is evaluated only numerically for particular datasets, so it is difficult to obtain structural insights in general instances. In contrast, our innovative solution approach allows us to analyze theoretically the structural properties of optimal strategies, and the insights gained from this analysis apply in a wide range of practical situations. From a practical perspective, we aim to show the effectiveness of our proposed strategy in the real world. To this end, we will perform extensive numerical experiments based on the data provided by our industry collaborator. Armed with this backing, we will continue to work with our industry partner to conduct a field experiment to test the effectiveness of our proposed strategy in the actual market.

26504219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504219.value: This research investigates the budget allocation problem of a marketing agency operating multi-channel online ad campaigns, motivated by operations of our industry collaborator in South Korea. Our work considers two salient features of multi-channel ad campaigns, the spillover and carryover effects: The spillover occurs since a customer is exposed to multiple channels of ads, and therefore, the money spent on a particular channel may affect the effectiveness of other channels. The carryover occurs since a customer is exposed to the ads several times over the campaign. The goal of the marketing agency is to maximize the total expected number of clicks or conversions in the presence of the spillover and carryover effects. Despite ever-increasing spending on online ads worldwide, this problem has been recognized as a difficult problem to solve and relatively under-explored in either academia or the industry. In our research, we aim to provide theoretical and practical contributions. From a theoretical perspective, one of the main difficulties is the curse of dimensionality in the associated dynamic programming problem. We use an innovative approach using a so-called fluid approximation and derive key structural insights, which are leveraged to design implementable, near-optimal budget allocation strategies. In addition to our theoretical results, we aim to verify the effectiveness of the proposed strategies via simulation as well as via a field experiment with our industry collaborator. Using the data collected by our industry partner, we show that the strategy used by the firm is significantly suboptimal. Motivated by this, we will continue to work with the firm to test our proposed strategy in the actual market, ultimately to quantify the value gained by judiciously regulating the spillover and carryover effects. 受位于韩国的合作公司运营的启发，本项目研究营销机构运营多渠道在线广告活动的预算分配问题。我们的工作考虑了多渠道广告活动的两个显着特征，即溢出效应和延续效应：溢出效应是由于客户接触多个广告渠道，因此在特定渠道上花费的资金可能会影响其他渠道的有效性。延续效应则是由于客户在活动期间会多次接触到该广告 。营销机构的目标是在溢出效应和延续效应下最大化预期的总点击次数或转化次数。 尽管全球在线广告的支出不断增加，但此问题已经被公认为一个难以解决的问题，并且在学术界或行业中的探讨都相对不足。我们研究的目标是提供理论和实践贡献。从理论的角度来看，主要困难之一是动态规划问题中的维数灾难。我们使用流体近似的创新方法，获得了最优解结构的关键洞察，并利用这些洞察来设计可实施的，接近最优的预算分配策略。此外，我们致力于通过计算机模拟以及与行业合作者的现场实验来验证所提出的策略的有效性。使用行业合作伙伴收集的数据，我们证明该公司使用的策略非常不理想。受此激励，我们将继续与公司合作，在实际市场中测试所提出的策略，最终量化通过明智地管理溢出效应和延续效应所获得的收益。

26504219.label: Realisation of objectives
26504219.value: Objective 1. Theoretical results. First, we construct a tractable model that captures key elements of the multichannel marketing environment. Our departure point will be a prototypical single-channel dynamic model introduced and formalized by Vidale and Wolfe (1957) and Nerlove and Arrow (1962), where customers’ response to advertising is manifested by an ordinary differential equation. In the field of oper- ations, researchers have developed optimal advertising policies for single-channel ad campaigns based on these parsimonious models (e.g., Sethi 1977). Building on this modeling framework, we construct a multichannel dynamic model that captures key elements of multichannel ad campaigns in contemporary environments. Specifically, our model captures the following interactions: an ad exposure can make customers aware and attentive about the product; repeated ads exposures in- crease the so-called advertising adstock (Broadbent 1979), thereby making consumers more likely to purchase, possibly through other marketing channels; however, adstock may decay to a negligi- ble level without further exposures. In contrast with existing multichannel models, our model is tractable to analyze optimal budget allocation strategies in a rigorous mathematical manner. Second, we rigorously quantify the “price of misattribution” when marketing agencies are blind to the interaction across marketing channels. Motivated by the common practice based on the last-touch (also referred to as “last-interaction” or “last-click”) attribution method, we consider a reduced model that does not explicitly take into account the spillover and carryover effects. Suppose that a marketing agency estimates the model and then optimizes the budget allocation for multiple channels; combining further data, the model is re-estimated, and so on. In this process, one might intuit that spillover and carryover effects can be reflected when model parameters are repeatedly estimated using data, thereby achieving the optimal budget allocation in the long run. In contrast to this intuition, our analysis indicates that when cross-channel interactions exist, be it large or small, budget allocation based on the reduced model converges to a suboptimal point in the long run. Specifically, suppose, for example, that the agency decreases the budget on a channel based on past low conversions, neglecting the fact that the ads from that channel greatly increased customers’ awareness and thus induced conversions through other channels. Consequently, the agency will observe lower conversions, thereby further decreasing the budget on that channel. We show that this pattern continues, eventually leading to suboptimal performance in the long run. In other words, the price of misattribution is significant: marketing agencies that ignore cross-channel interactions might lose a positive fraction of the maximum attainable revenue from each consumer. See Theorem 1 of our paper attached to this report. Third, we characterize structural properties of optimal budget allocation policies. As indicated earlier, the cross-channel interactions due to spillover and carryover effects significantly complicate the study of optimal budget allocation policies. Using a fluid approximation, we characterize a sufficiently tractable solution to the budget allocation problem. In particular, we show that optimal budget allocation policies exhibit the so-called turnpike properties; in particular, there exist three distinctive phases over the ad campaign: bump-up, stationary, and exploitation phases. From a practical standpoint, this property is important because it provides a guideline for practitioners in designing budget allocation strategies. However, in the extant literature, the turnpike property has been studied exclusively in the context of single-channel ad campaigns. Our paper is the first to extend this important result to multichannel ad campaigns. Furthermore, when the ad campaign is sufficiently long, we show that the bump-up and exploitation phases become negligible, and consequently, a static budget allocation is near-optimal. The latter result provides a theoretical justification for common practices. Due to operational restrictions, marketing agencies cannot adjust their budget allocation in real-time; our analysis suggests that near-optimal budget allocation strategies need not be dynamic as long as the ad campaign is sufficiently long. Objective 2. Empirical results. We use a panel dataset obtained from our industry partner that operates the ad campaign on behalf of a leading online fashion retailer. The dataset includes daily observations from two marketing channels, where the campaign period is from January 2020 to June 2020. Each observation record contains the budget expenditure (in South Korean won), the number of impressions, the number of clicks, and the number of purchases. The campaign operates two categories of ads: Channel 1 operates display ads via social media platforms such as Facebook and Instagram; and Channel 2 operates retargeting ad via commerce media platforms such as Criteo and Mobion. In this paper, we use the number of final purchases as the conversion measurement. Based on this dataset, our empirical findings are two-fold. First, we present empirical evidence that marketing agencies do not internalize cross-channel effects in their budget allocation decisions. Specifically, we find that the marketing agency allocates the budget in proportion to the magnitude of the marginal benefit (i.e., the additional conversion from a one-unit increase in the budget), which violates the optimality condition. This empirical finding is consistent with our market research interviews which reveal that 70% of marketing agencies rely on last-touch attribution methods, which gives all of the credit for a conversion to the last touch point in customers’ journey, thereby ignoring cross-channel effects. Second, we perform counterfactual analysis to quantify how much one can improve the performance by correctly internalizing cross- channel effects. Using our calibrated model, we find that the conversion rate can increase by 30%, which indicates that there exist a lot of room to improve in multichannel ad markets. For future research, we plan to conduct a field experiment with our industry partner. Our theoretical and numerical results indicate that our proposed methodology is implementable and would work reasonably well in practice. Although we did not conduct a field experiment due to time constraint, there is no doubt that a significant contribution can be made by quantifying the impact of our method in real-world multichannel ad campaigns.

26504219.label: Major findings and research outcome
26504219.value: First, we rigorously quantify the price of misattribution when marketing agencies are blind to the interaction across marketing channels. Specifically, motivated by common practice, we examine a class of budget allocation policies that repeatedly allocate the budget based on the observed conversion rates from the recent past. We show that, although the observed conversion rates reflect the cross-channel interactions, the resulting budget allocation can be significantly suboptimal in the long run. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result that theoretically demonstrate possible consequences when the cross-channel interactions are not properly managed in the process of budget allocation. Furthermore, this negative result motivates the study of optimal budget allocation strategies that properly internalize the cross-channel interactions. Second, we derive a fluid approximation to consumer dynamics across multiple channels, which lends itself to characterizing structural properties of optimal dynamic budget allocation policies that internalize the cross-channel interactions. To facilitate implementation, we propose a fixed budget allocation policy that is not only tractable in practice but also near-optimal when the campaign period is sufficiently long. Third, we use a data augmentation method to estimate the model in the absence of individual-level data. Moreover, we show via counterfactual analysis that our proposed strategy performs well compared with a benchmark policy that are oblivious to the spillover and carryover effects. Our counterfactual analysis shows that our proposed method can improve the performance of the said benchmark by 20%.

26504219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26504219.value: Our work makes significant theoretical contributions to the literature by characterizing the poor performance of the methodology that is quite common in practice. Furthermore, our small-scale numerical experiment clearly indicates that there is a lot of room to improve with our proposed method. In the future, we plan to continue our collaboration with the industry partner and pursue a field experiment to test our method in the actual market.

26504219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26504219.value: We study how a marketing agency can allocate advertising budget across multiple channels. When customers are exposed to multiple channels, an ad from one channel may affect that the efficiency of an ad from another channel, which is commonly referred to as cross-channel interactions. First, we show that cross-channel interactions, if not properly managed, can lead to suboptimal performance; thus, the most of common practices based on last-click attribution methods is not suitable in the multichannel environment. Second, we derive a fluid approximation to consumer dynamics across multiple channels, which lends itself to key structural properties of optimal budget allocation strategies. Furthermore, we propose a tractable budget allocation strategy that is near-optimal when the campaign period is sufficiently long. From a numerical perspective, we use a data augmentation method to estimate the model in the absence of individual-level data. Moreover, we show via counterfactual analysis that our proposed strategy performs well compared with benchmark policies that are oblivious to cross-channel interactions.

26504319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504319.value: 在本提案中，我计划分析国际会计准则与银行监管趋同的共同作用。自1988年《巴塞尔协议》首次发布以来，已有100多个国家自愿通过。同时，我们也看到徐国国家主动采用一套单一的会计标准，例如国际财务报告标准。尽管许多论文分别研究了银行监管全球化的经济后果（例如Acharya, 2003; Dell’Ariccia and Marquez, 2006; Holthausen and Rønde, 2004）和会计准则全球化的影响（例如Armstrong, Barth, Jagolinzer and Riedl, 2010; DeFond, Hu, Hung and Li, 201; De George, Li and Shivakumar, 2015; Gao, Jiang and Zhang, 2018），目前还没有太多的研究分析它们的综合效应。我计划在本项目中填补这一空白。为了研究这个问题，我建议使用一个两个经济体的简单模型。每个经济体都由一家代表性银行、一系列风险中性投资者和一家银行监管机构组成。银行筹集外部资本并决定进行高风险投资，这可以被认为是商业贷款或抵押贷款。由于统一的银行规章制度，银行可以进入国外市场，因此投资者可以投资国内银行和外国银行。会计信息在此模型中将帮助投资者理解银行的资产质量以决定是否投资。然而，如果两个经济体使用不同的会计准则，外国投资者将无法解读这一信号。因此，会计准则的趋同将影响投资者、银行业、监管机构的行为，最终影响社会福利。我推测，与Acharya(2003)类似，由于一个自利的银行监管机构没有将其外部性内部化，两个经济体可能无法协调，从而减少总盈余。如果这两个经济体采用相同的会计准则，这种低效率可能会得到缓解。

26504319.label: Realisation of objectives
26504319.value: All the objectives have been achieved. 1. Regarding Objective 1, we show that the harmonization of accounting standards could hurt social welfare in the presence of investment beauty-contest. Therefore, mandating a high level of accounting standards harmonization in banks may not be desirable because they are prone to runs and thus feature greater investment externalities. 2. We also find that mandatory adoption of harmonized standards can be necessary, as firms, when left to their own, will not voluntarily choose to do so. This result provides a justification for the recent mandatory adoption of more harmonized accounting standards, such as IFR. These results can address Objective 2. 3. Lastly, regarding Objective 3, our findings have rich implications about the cost and benefits of converging towards harmonized standards. For example, our results imply that the adoption of harmonized accounting standards would be best decided at an industry-by-industry or country-by-country level, as different countries and industries exhibit different degrees of investment externalities. Our results also predict that when an entire country (region) adopts uniform accounting standards (e.g., the European Union's adoption of IFRS), industries in the adopting country (countries in the adopting region) that exhibit higher degrees of beauty-contest motive would benefit less from such adoption than the ones that exhibit lower degrees of beauty-contest motives.

26504319.label: Major findings and research outcome
26504319.value: Based on the proposal, I have completed two research projects. The first paper is titled “Harmonized Accounting Standards and Investment Beauty Contests,” coauthored with Xu Jiang (Duke) and Gaoqing Zhang (Minnesota). The main message of this paper is that while more harmonized accounting standards have ambiguous effects on the reports' informativeness in representing firms' underlying fundamentals, they always reduce their usefulness in forecasting aggregate investments. Therefore, the stronger the beauty-contest features (e.g., in banks), the more important the forecasts about the aggregate investment, thus calling for less harmonized accounting standards. This paper has been accepted for publication at the Accounting Review, a top journal in accounting. The second paper is titled “Uniform Standards, Information Quality, and Capital Flows,” coauthored with Lin Nan (Purdue). We examine the impact of uniform standards from an economy's perspective in the presence of capital crunches. Our analysis indicates that converting to uniform standards brings a positive effect on each economy by facilitating capital flows across economies and improving investment efficiency. On the other hand, it also changes the amount of foreign capital an economy obtains, contingent on the severity of the capital crunch and information quality. We show that these effects jointly determine whether converting to uniform standards increases or decreases an economy's expected output. This paper has been accepted for publication at the European Accounting Review, a well-recognized journal in accounting. In Part C, I will provide more details about these two projects.

26504319.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26504319.value: This project develops a tractable framework to study the impact of accounting standards harmonization in the presence of investment complementarity. The work can be extended in a couple of dimensions. First, the modeling of harmonized accounting standards only incorporates one aspect, i.e., how such convergence affects the reporting noise across firms. There are several other important aspects, for example, how the convergence of accounting standards affects investors' processing of accounting reports and financial statement comparability. An explicit formulation of the connections among these different aspects towards a unified framework is an interesting avenue for future research. Second, from a practical standpoint, the beauty-contest feature is especially salient in the financial sector. Our analysis thus implies that the switch to harmonized accounting standards is particularly relevant to financial institutions/banks. Future work can explicitly model institutional features of banks (e.g., the mismatch between assets and liabilities and the liquidity needs of depositors) to shed light on how accounting standards harmonization affects the banking sector, and in particular, systemic bank runs.

26504319.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26504319.value: This project examines the economic consequences of accounting standards harmonization. We show that more harmonized accounting standards make it more difficult for investors to forecast others' behaviors and thus may impair welfare. Our results imply that the adoption of harmonized accounting standards would be best decided at an industry-by-industry or country-by-country level. These results can generate rich implications for empirical research, accounting standard-setting, and regulations.

26504419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504419.value: Economists have long considered the consequences of political favoritism in the allocation of government resources. In the proposed project, we will examine how political ties distort the allocation of central-to-local fiscal transfers across regions and the resulting general equilibrium welfare loss. In a country with a vertical fiscal system like China, transfer from the central government constitutes a significant share of local government income. In 2016, the share of provincial government spending that came from the central governments was over 40%. Not surprisingly, the allocation of intergovernmental transfers across regions and sectors has always been marked by corruption and cronyism. There have been many anecdotal accounts of local government officials trading favors with ministers seeking earmarked fiscal transfers, a practice coined as “pao bu, qian jin”, which literally means “run forward,” but can also be translated as “go to the Ministry and get money.” Despite mounting anecdotal evidence, there is surprisingly little empirical or quantitative evidence on the consequences of political ties in the allocation of fiscal resources. How do they affect the distribution of population and income across space? What is their impact on productivity and welfare at the national level? Are they closing or widening regional disparities? To shed light on these important questions, we will first present reduced-form evidence linking provincial leader-ministry official connections to central-to-provincial fiscal transfers, with identification coming from official turnover. We will then set up and quantify a general equilibrium model that embeds a canonical local public finance environment (Fajgelbaum et al. 2018) with many regions, several factors of production, and costly trade and migration across regions. A spatial model is essential for this the research because the overall welfare effect depends to a large extent on whether or not fiscal transfers affected by political ties are concentrated in regions with lower capacity to use them and makes a limited contribution to the aggregate economy because of excessive trade and migration frictions. Because of the redistributive nature of fiscal transfers, we will conduct counterfactual analyses of (1) Removing the effects of political connections in intergovernmental transfer allocation; (2) Adopting a fiscal transfer rule specified by the recent reform on both aggregate welfare and regional inequality. 中央到地方的财政转移支付是地方经济发展的重要助推力量，中央财政转移支付在地区之间的分配对中国经济整体的效率和地区间均衡发展都起到了重要的作用。本文通过建立一个地区间的一般均衡模型，分析不同的地方转移支付分配方案对中国经济总效率和地区间不平衡发展的影响，并且考察由于部委和省市之间官员的政治联系带来的可能的资源错配现象。

26504419.label: Realisation of objectives
26504419.value: 5.3 Realization of Objectives Objective 1: Collect a data set on the connections of provincial leaders with ministry officials and provide rigorous empirical evidence on the relationship between political connections and intergovernmental transfers. We have collected a comprehensive dataset on the connections between provincial leaders and ministry officials. Our data collection process, made possible by a highly efficient team of research assistants, involved sourcing career data of Chinese officials from ChinaVitae, a website that compiles the curricula vitae of Chinese Communist Party and government officials. This data provided us with information on officials' birth years, provinces of origin, colleges attended, and most importantly, previous positions held in the party or government. Using this data, we constructed indicators to measure political connections between ministers and provincial leaders. We focused on the connections between ministers and the top provincial leaders, specifically the provincial Party secretary and governor. We created three measures of ties: workplace connections (whether they worked in the same branch), alumni connections (whether they attended the same university), and hometown connections (whether they were born in the same province). To establish causal evidence, we control for the official (provincial party secretary-governor pair) fixed effects in the panel regression of log transfers on connection dummies). which effectively controls for all omitted variables associated with city leadership. Hence, the identification of the political connection effects comes from the rotation of ministers. Specifically, the political connections obtained by a provincial official come from whether during the term period in the province, one or more of his past colleagues or alumni become ministers, which is largely uncertain and exogenous. Our baseline results show that workplace connections between provincial leaders and ministers significantly influenced the allocation of fiscal resources, resulting in a 6% increase in fiscal transfers to the connected province. While alumni ties had an impact on transfers for ministers-governors, hometown ties did not show a significant effect. Heterogeneity analyses between key ministries (ministries with greater authority over the distribution of fiscal transfers) and less important ones (ministries unlikely to have a strong say in fiscal transfers, including the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of National Defense, and the Ministry of Justice) in the central-to-local fiscal transfers show that the effects only exist for the connections with the former but not with the latter. The data includes information on their affiliations, interactions, and other relevant factors. Through rigorous empirical analysis, we have examined the relationship between political connections and intergovernmental transfers. Our findings provide substantial evidence on how these connections influence the allocation of fiscal resources between regions. Objective 2: Construct a spatial general equilibrium model that embeds a canonical local public finance environment with many regions, several factors of production, and costly trade and migration across regions. We have developed a sophisticated spatial general equilibrium model that incorporates a canonical local public finance framework. Previous theoretical work has shown that which demonstrated that the free market spatial allocation without transfers is inefficient with compensating differentials for consumption across regions and externalities that make amenities or output per person functions of population. To illustrate the intuition, we start with a simplified analytical model that abstracts away from firm heterogeneity, input-output linkages, and spatial frictions. We show that the optimal government spending should enhance the dispersion of appeals among areas, attracting more people to places with high productivity, better amenities, and a plentiful supply of land. To further quantify the impact of these channels, we constructed a multi-region, multi-sector quantitative spatial model that incorporates various elements: the local public finance environment, the central-to-local transfer formula (in which political connections played a role), heterogeneity in productivity, amenities, and endowments across regions, trade and migration costs, and input-output linkages across sectors. We carefully calibrated the model to match China's economic geography in 2012, allowing us to conduct a counterfactual analysis of alternative fiscal transfer schemes, including one that entirely eliminated the influence of political connections on transfer allocation. Objective 3: Conduct a counterfactual analysis of alternative ways of allocating fiscal transfers (removing the role of political connections, following the formula used in allocating central government funds in the US, following the rules specified in a recently proposed fiscal transfer reform, etc.) on (1) Overall welfare; (2) Regional inequality. Guided by the quantitative model, we have conducted a counterfactual analysis to examine different scenarios for allocating fiscal transfers, such as removing the influence of political connections and considering alternative allocation formulas, such as those used in the US or proposed in recent fiscal transfer reform discussions. Surprisingly, we find that when the influence of political connections on fiscal transfer distribution is eliminated, real GDP experiences a decline of 0.22 percent, and aggregate welfare decreases by 0.58 percent. This indicates that the allocation of fiscal transfers driven by political connections has a positive impact on both economic development and welfare. This outcome is the result of the interaction between two institutional features in China. Firstly, fiscal transfers in China aim to reduce regional disparities, leading to greater transfers to poorer regions. This approach promotes regional equalization but can come at the expense of overall welfare. Secondly, political connections are positively associated with local fundamentals. Officials who are promoted to wealthier provinces are more likely to have political connections, as they often share elite backgrounds and career paths with ministers, particularly those heading key ministries. This positive connection-fundamental relationship undermines the redistributive function of fiscal transfers and aligns them with economic fundamentals. In fact, our analysis reveals that the removal of political connections reduces regional inequality by 0.76 percent. We also consider several alternative arrangements, such as following the transfer formulas of Germany and the U.S. Removing all transfers leads to an 18\% increase in aggregate welfare and a 15% increase in real GDP, but a staggering 116% increase in inequality, which highlights the important role of transfers in balancing regional economies. Finally, when calibrating the dependence of fiscal transfers to key regional outcomes such as GDP per capita and past tax revenue to German or U.S. levels, we find that the current Chinese fiscal transfer scheme entails more fiscal equalization across regions than the U.S. system and less fiscal equalization than the German system, with the counterfactual allocation following the U.S. formula delivering higher aggregate output and inequality, and the counterfactual allocation following the German rule resulting in lower aggregate output and inequality. In conclusion, we have largely achieved the project objectives. We collected a comprehensive dataset, provided rigorous empirical evidence, constructed a comprehensive spatial general equilibrium model, and conducted counterfactual analyses based on model estimation. Despite challenges encountered, our team's perseverance and collaborative efforts enabled us to overcome obstacles and successfully advance the project. We would like to address the concerns regarding the deviations in spending between the approved budget and actual expenses in staff. We note that a significant portion of the funds was allocated towards supporting students from both the Economics and Environmental Science departments. By providing financial support to these students, we aimed to enhance their research capabilities and contribute to their professional development. We believe that this allocation of funds towards student support aligns with the broader objectives of the project and contributes to the overall success and impact of the research.

26504419.label: Major findings and research outcome
26504419.value: Our empirical results demonstrate that workplace connections between provincial leaders and ministers have a significant impact on the allocation of fiscal resources. Specifically, we find that such connections lead to a 6% increase in fiscal transfers to the connected province. While alumni ties influence transfers for ministers-governors, hometown ties do not show a significant effect. Further analysis reveals that these effects primarily exist for key ministries responsible for fiscal transfers, such as the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, the Ministry of Education, the National Health Commission, the Ministry of Finance, and the National Development and Reform Commission. Less important ministries, such as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of National Defense, and the Ministry of Justice, do not exhibit a similar influence. Using a general equilibrium spatial model, we find that removing the influence of political connections on fiscal transfer distribution results in a 0.22% decline in real GDP and a 0.58% decrease in aggregate welfare. This outcome arises from the interaction of two institutional features in China. Firstly, fiscal transfers aim to reduce regional disparities and promote equalization, which can come at the expense of overall welfare. Secondly, political connections are associated with local economic fundamentals. Officials promoted to wealthier provinces are more likely to have political connections due to shared elite backgrounds and career paths with ministers, particularly those heading key ministries. This positive relationship undermines the redistributive function of fiscal transfers and aligns them with economic fundamentals. Removing political connections reduces regional inequality by 0.76%. We also explore alternative arrangements, such as adopting transfer formulas from Germany and the United States. Eliminating all transfers increases aggregate welfare by 18% and real GDP by 15%, but inequality rises by 116%, highlighting the crucial role of transfers in balancing regional economies. Calibrating fiscal transfers based on regional indicators to German or U.S. levels, we find that the current Chinese fiscal transfer scheme achieves more fiscal equalization than the U.S. system, but less than the German system. Counterfactual allocations following the U.S. formula result in higher output and inequality, while those following the German rule lead to lower output and inequality. The research outcome is culminated in our paper "Political Connections and Fiscal Transfers in the Regional Economy: Evidence from China", finished in August, 2022. We hold high expectations for this paper and have made diligent attempts to submit it to esteemed economic journals. In September 2022, we submitted the paper to the American Economic Review, and in January 2023, we submitted it to the Review of Economics Studies. Although we received positive feedback from editors and referees at both journals, our submissions were not successful due to the high standards of these two journals. As of now, we have not yet achieved any publications due to the time-consuming nature of the submission process and the considerable time we have invested in revising our paper based on the valuable comments provided by editors and referees. In light of the editors recommendation, we have subsequently submitted our paper to the Review of Economics and Statistics and the paper is still under review.

26504419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26504419.value: To further advance this research, we can explore several avenues. Firstly, we can examine the effectiveness of various policies aimed at reducing discretion in fiscal transfer allocation. This includes investigating the impact of initiatives such as the State Council's efforts to decrease the proportion of earmarked grants and promote a more transparent, rule-based allocation system. Additionally, we can consider the effects of closing "regional liaison offices" in Beijing to address lobbying activities. Furthermore, we can utilize our dataset on connections between ministry officials and provincial leaders to delve into other aspects and outcomes. For example, we can explore how these connections influence collaboration between ministers and provincial officials in achieving specific central-to-local policy objectives, such as environmental regulations or industrial policies.

26504419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26504419.value: China, like many other countries, implements fiscal transfers to address economic disparities between regions. However, the allocation process of these transfers is often opaque. It is widely observed that local governments in China engage in favor exchanges with ministry officials to secure additional fiscal transfers. Our research paper aims to shed light on the effects of political connections, measured through shared hometowns, educational backgrounds, and work experiences, between provincial officials and ministers responsible for allocating fiscal resources. We find that a shared past working experience between officials and ministers leads to a significant 6% increase in fiscal transfers allocated to the connected province. To assess the overall welfare implications of these politically influenced fiscal allocation patterns, we employ a general equilibrium spatial model. Surprisingly, our findings indicate that removing the influence of political connections on fiscal transfers would actually result in an increase in aggregate GDP. This counterintuitive outcome stems from the fact that more developed provinces, which contribute significantly to the national economy, tend to have leaders with stronger political connections, thereby receiving a larger share of fiscal resources. However, this approach exacerbates regional disparities, contradicting the primary objective of fiscal transfers to promote balanced regional development.

26504919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
26504919.value: The Chair of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) endures high pressure while facing scrutinizing questions from the media during the scheduled press conferences after each meeting. Unwilling or reluctant to disclose information, they may resort to vague answers that create higher macroeconomic risk in the stock market that is compensated with excess returns. We develop a measure based on artificial intelligence (AI) to quantify the degree of vagueness from the FOMC chair's responses during the question and answer session (Q&A) of the press conferences. Using the data of FOMC press conferences from 2011 to 2018, we plan to test the stock market’s reaction to press conferences by examining the risk premium and market beta. This study aims to contribute to the emerging field of fintech by proposing and evaluating a novel, AI-powered measure of the Fed’s behavior, and outlines the importance of macroeconomic risk on asset prices. 聯邦公開市場委員會主席在每次新聞發布會上，都面臨媒體提問的壓力。當他們不願意披露信息時，可能會採用含糊不清的答案並表現出不同的行為信號。這樣的不確定性會在股票市場中產生更高的宏觀經濟風險，並引致更高的風險補償。我們提出了一項基於人工智能（AI）的算法，以量化聯儲主席在新聞發布會的問答環節（Q＆A）中的回應及行為表現。利用2011年至2018年聯儲新聞發布會的數據，我們計劃檢驗股市對新聞發布會中的這些行為的反應。本研究旨在通過提出和評估新穎的人工智能測度來刻畫對應答的迴避和不自信，為新興的金融科技領域做出貢獻，並證實宏觀經濟風險對資產價格的重要性。

26504919.label: Realisation of objectives
26504919.value: Our study addresses all the revised research objectives. Here is how the point-by-point summary of how each objective is achieved. 1. Measuring the FOMC Chair’s Behavioral Hints and Visual Cues: We develop two main visual cues: the chairperson's appearance proportion and their gaze shift frequency during Q&A sessions. These cues are quantified using image analysis and computer vision technologies, including Face++ for facial recognition and OpenFace for detecting gaze movement frequency. 2. Measuring Monetary Policies from Fed Statements: We measure the Fed committee’s statement content by 1) the federal discount rate, which is the interest rate set by the Fed on loans extended by the central bank to commercial banks or other depository institutions; 2) The decision regarding the change of the federal funds rate’s target range (labeled as “easing” if the target range is lowered, otherwise “tightening”. 3. Analyzing Sentiment of the FOMC Press Conference: The study uses a finance-specific dictionary (Loughran and McDonald 2011) to assess the communication tone during press conferences. The Loughran and McDonald finance dictionary is a widely recognized tool in financial sentiment analysis, particularly for its effectiveness in identifying finance-specific sentiment in texts. For the purpose of this study, we identify finance-specific negative words during the answer period of the press conferences. By employing this dictionary, the study aims to capture the nuances of financial communication that might be missed by general sentiment analysis tools. 4. Investigating Monetary Policy Uncertainties and Visual Hints: We find that both higher appearance proportion and more frequent gaze shifting by the chairperson are associated with reduced monetary policy uncertainty, as reflected in financial market reactions. 5. Examining Monetary Policy Surprises and Visual Hints: We find that a higher appearance proportion and more frequent gaze shifts are associated with higher monetary policy surprises, indicating these visual cues play a significant role in shaping investors’ expectations regarding monetary policy surprises. In summary, we have addressed the role of visual cues in influencing investor perceptions of monetary policy, particularly focusing on the FOMC chairperson’s appearance proportion and gaze shifting behaviors during press conferences and how these cues relate to monetary policy surprises and uncertainties. All the five research objectives are fully addressed as detailed above.

26504919.label: Major findings and research outcome
26504919.value: Our study delves into the impact that visual cues during the QA segments of FOMC press conferences have on investors' expectations regarding monetary policy. We introduce two innovative nonverbal metrics designed to capture the essence of messages from the central bank, and we assess their effect on the volatility of asset prices on a minute-by-minute basis. By leveraging artificial intelligence with capabilities in computer vision, such as facial recognition and tracking eye movements, our findings are twofold: firstly, when investors perceive a higher screen presence of the chairperson, they tend to associate it with greater surprise in monetary policy announcements and reduced uncertainty. Secondly, a more frequent gaze shift by the chairperson is also perceived as an indicator of significant policy announcements and diminished uncertainty. Additional analysis confirms that both a greater presence and more frequent gaze shifting correlate with a reduction in uncertain terms within the transcripts of the responses, suggesting a higher degree of information relayed to investors. In sum, our research underscores the significant informational value that visual elements in FOMC press conferences hold for investors. A journal submission of the paper is under preparation.

26504919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
26504919.value: Investigating the nuanced, non-quantitative information presented during press conferences can provide investors with a clearer insight into the Committee's decisions. The implementation of press conferences marks a significant reform, promoting an open dialogue about the Committee's approach to shaping future policy. Looking ahead to future research avenues, integrating the two suggested indicators with both textual and vocal analyses may provide more insights. By aligning specific themes or subjects with the identified behavioral patterns, we can gain a more profound comprehension of the chairperson's nonverbal cues. Additionally, exploring whether there are other types of objective and reproducible nonverbal metrics that could effectively measure the subtle information conveyed during monetary policy press conferences is also a fruitful direction.

26504919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
26504919.value: The project discusses how the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) press conferences, introduced in 2011 to help the public understand policy decisions, offer valuable information not just through what is said, but also through nonverbal cues. The research takes a new approach by focusing on the nonverbal signals from the FOMC chairperson, like how much screen time they get and how often they shift their gaze while answering questions. These visual hints could give away additional insights into monetary policy decisions. The findings suggest that when the chairperson is seen more on camera, or when they look around more, investors seem to pick up on unexpected news and feel more certain about the economic outlook. This study introduces innovative methods for measuring these visual cues using computer vision and psychology theories. It also combines what the chairperson does and says to give a fuller picture of how their behavior affects investor decisions. The article argues that these insights are useful for market players and suggests that the FOMC should continue to offer clear and informative communication to the public.

27104219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27104219.value: The proposed research aims at understanding how microtubule (MT) stability is regulated during neuronal outgrowth and axonal regeneration. In order to circumvent the extreme complexity of the mammalian nervous system, we will use the well-characterized mechanosensory Touch Receptor Neurons (TRNs) in the nematode C. elegans as an in vivo model system to study neurite formation and regeneration. Specifically, we will address three questions regarding MT regulations. First, we will study how post-translational modifications (phosphorylation and polyglutamylation) of tubulin isotypes affect MT stability and TRN morphogenesis and axonal regeneration. Second, we will study how the F-box and WD40 repeats-containing protein MEC-15 and ubiquitination and protein degradation regulate MT structure and neuronal outgrowth. We will identify the MEC-15 target protein, whose abnormal accumulation possibly leads to unstable MTs. Among the candidates are several HSP90 co-chaperones, whose mutation can rescue the loss of MEC-15. This detrimental effects of the HSP90 chaperone machinery on MT stability would potentially challenge the prevailing view for a protective role of molecular chaperones in development. Third, we will investigate how the RNA binding protein MBL-1, which regulates alternative pre-mRNA splicing, affects MT structure, axonal growth, and regeneration. We will identify the target gene of MBL-1 and provide one of the first examples for the role of alternative splicing in neuronal differentiation and regeneration. This project is built on a body of previous work using a similar system. All three research directions are supported by strong preliminary data and the proposed methodologies are well-established in the fields of genetics and cell biology. We expect to identify several novel regulators of MT stability and discover new mechanisms for the regulation of neuronal outgrowth and axonal regeneration. Given the orthology between C. elegans and mammalian genes, the mechanisms found in C. elegans TRNs is likely to be conserved in humans. Therefore, our research could provide insights into the development of complex nervous systems and possibly help identify therapeutic targets for neurodevelopmental diseases. One particular group of diseases is tubulinopathies, which are caused by mutations in tubulin genes that lead to dysregulated MT dynamics and severe defects in neuronal migration and axonal outgrowth. Understanding the regulation of MTs can help develop therapies. Moreover, the in vivo laser axotomy system we will build can serve as a discovery platform to identify molecules whose activities would affect axonal regeneration. 27104219.value: 1. Through CRISPR/Cas9-mediated editing of endogenous tubulin loci, we have analyzed the effects of several tubulin PTMs on axonal outgrowth and regeneration, including beta-tubulin S172 phosphorylation, alpha-tubulin K40 acetylation, beta-tubulin K252 acetylation, alpha-tubulin detyrosination, and alpha/beta-tubulin polyglutamylation. This part of the work not only achieved the original objectives (mostly restricted to S172 phosphorylation and polyglutamylation) but also extended the analyses to more tubulin PTMs, thus expanding the original research scope. Our analyses led to the discovery of a strong microtubule-destabilizing effect of S172 phosphorylation on axonal growth and found that an optimal level of S172 phosphorylation is needed for effective regeneration. Polyglutamylation works in a more subtle way and modifies MT stability by altering the interaction with the MT-destabilizing kinesin-13 family protein KLP-7. We also showed that K40 acetylation has very little effect on axonal growth and regeneration. In the meantime, we characterized a large list of over 100 tubulin mutations for their effects on neurite growth; many of these mutations are found in human neurodevelopmental disorders. Our work also clarified the role of a tubulin gene tba-7, which was previously thought to have microtubule-destabilizing effects; we found that the previous phenotype was caused by a background mutation and not tba-7 itself. 2. We have elucidated the interaction between the ubiquitin-proteosome system (UPS) and the molecular chaperone system in regulating neurite growth. We found that the UPS and the chaperones do not regulate each other; instead, they act antagonistically to regulate the common substrate. UPS promotes the degradation of the substrate, whereas chaperones stabilize the substrate. This tug-of-war keeps the common substrates at the optimal level, which is crucial for a range of neurodevelopmental processes, including microtubule formation, axonal growth, synaptic development, and neuronal functions in several neuron types. We identified key components of each system. UPS contains the F-box protein MEC-15 and ubiquitination machinery, which promotes microtubule stability, whereas the molecular chaperone system contains the chaperones HSP-90 and HSP-110, as well as the cochaperones, protein phosphatase 5 (PPH-5) and the Hsp90 cochaperone (STI-1), p23 protein (DAF-41), and CDC-37/Cdc37, which appears to promote microtubule destabilization. 3. We have identified and characterized at least one common substrate of UPS and chaperones to be the dual-leucine zipper kinase (DLK-1). We found that DLK-1 is degraded by the UPS and stabilized by the HSP90 chaperones. DLK-1 physically interacts with HSP-90. Moreover, DLK-1 level is increased in mec-15 and ubiquitin-activating enzyme mutants and reduced in the chaperone mutants. Overexpression of DLK-1 destabilizes the microtubules, suppressed neurite growth, and canceled out the stabilizing effects of removing the chaperones, suggesting that DLK-1 is one of the essential downstream targets of UPS and chaperones. We have also characterized another potential downstream target, the Microtubule-associated protein MAPH-1.3. Loss of MAPH-1.3 and its paralogs did not cause apparent defects in neurite growth, but gain-of-function mutations in MAPH-1.3 have MT-stabilizing effects downstream of mec-15(-) mutations. MAPH-1.3 does not seem to interact with HSP90 but may provide additional regulation on microtubule stability downstream of the UPS. We are close to finishing up the analysis on MAPH-1.3.

27104219.label: Major findings and research outcome
27104219.value: Using the C. elegans touch receptor neurons as a model, we identified two new mechanisms of regulating microtubule stability during axonal growth and regeneration. First, we studied the effects of a range of tubulin posttranslational modifications (PTMs), including tubulin S172 phosphorylation, K40 acetylation, K252 acetylation, detyrosination, and polyglutamylation, on neurite development and regeneration. We discovered that beta-tubulin S172 phosphorylation by CDK1 plays an important role in promoting microtubule dynamics and controlling neurite growth and axonal regeneration. We also found that tubulin polyglutamylation modulates microtubule stability by controlling the interaction with the microtubule-destabilizing kinesin-13 family protein KLP-7 and thus promoting dynamic instability (Lu et al., under review). Second, we uncovered an antagonism between the Hsp70/Hsp90 chaperone machinery and the ubiquitin-proteosome system (UPS) involving an F-box protein MEC-15 on neuronal differentiation (Zheng et al., Development, 2020). We found an unexpected negative regulation of neuronal morphogenesis and function by chaperones. mec-15(-) mutants showed defects in microtubule formation, neurite growth, synaptic development, and neuronal functions; these defects can be rescued by the loss of Hsp70/Hsp90 chaperones and co-chaperones. MEC-15 and UPS degrade the dual-leucine kinase DLK-1, which is an Hsp90 client protein stabilized by the chaperones. The abundance of DLK-1 is fine-tuned by the antagonism between MEC-15 and the chaperones, which tightly controls neuronal differentiation. In addition, we characterized a large number (> 100) of tubulin missense mutations for their effects on axonal development and mechanosensory function (Lee et al., Mol Biol Cell, 2021). Many of these mutations were found in human neurological disorders, such as cortical malformation, thus highlighting the utilities of our system in modeling disease-causing mutations. In fact, we could engineer human mutations into C. elegans tubulin genes through gene editing to test their effects on neuronal development at the single-cell level and to connect cellular phenotypes with clinical symptoms. We also examined the role of tubulin gene tba-7, which was previously thought to be a microtubule-destabilizing tubulin. Our analysis using knockout alleles generated by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing challenged that view and found that the previous phenotype was associated with a background mutation. The incorporation of TBA-7 does not directly destabilize microtubules (Lu and Zheng, Mol Biol Cell, 2021). Finally, we did a comprehensive analysis of tubulin gene expression and function in the entire organism of C. elegans using newly generated single-cell transcriptome data and a systematic literature review (Lu and Zheng, Front Cell Dev Biol, 2022).

27104219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27104219.value: Our systematic study of a series of tubulin PTMs for their effects on neuronal development used CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing to install PTM-inactivating or -mimicking mutations in the endogenous tubulin genes, which allowed the direct comparison of the effects of different PTMs in the same system. Going forward, we will combine the genetic manipulation of various PTMs to evaluate their potential synergistic or antagonistic effects, allowing further testing of the “tubulin code” hypothesis. Moreover, our genetic analysis characterized the biological effects of tubulin PTMs on axonal growth and regeneration but the biophysical basis for such effects is not entirely understood. The next step is to collaborate with biophysicists to understand how such PTMs alter microtubule structure, stability, and interaction with other proteins. Combined in vivo and in vitro analyses can help better elucidate the effects of the tubulin PTMs. Finally, we can use our platform to evaluate tubulin mutations associated with human disease. Moreover, the finding that molecular chaperones could negatively regulate neuronal morphogenesis by stabilizing negative regulators of microtubule stability opens a new research direction. In addition to DLK-1, we will use advanced proteomics to identify more HSP90 interactors, which will become candidates for important microtubule regulators for future studies.

27104219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27104219.value: Neurons that make up our brain have special structures with long cellular processes (or neurites) called axons and dendrites. The development and regeneration of these neurites depends on the cytoskeleton, such as microtubules, which provides structural support for neuronal outgrowth and tracks for intracellular transport. In this project, we found two new mechanisms of controlling neuronal morphogenesis by regulating microtubule stability. The first is through chemical modification of the tubulin, which is the building block of microtubules. Specifically, adding a phosphate group at the serine 172 of beta-tubulin or adding a chain of glutamate residues to the C-terminal tail of the tubulins would change the properties of the microtubules and thus affect neurite growth and regeneration. The second mechanism is the fine-tuned control of the abundance of certain proteins through the tug-of-war between protein degradation and stabilization machineries. The level of these proteins plays a critical role in regulating microtubule stability and neurite development. Our research provides critical insights into understanding how the shape and morphology of neurons are formed and regenerated, thus helping the investigation of many neurological diseases that result from impaired microtubule stability and malformed neuronal structures.

27106419.label: Realisation of objectives
27106419.value: In this project we aimed to identify the genes and potential regulatory elements underlying melanin- and carotenoid-based plumage color development to elucidate the genetic basis of sexually and seasonally dimorphic plumage color in the American goldfinch (Spinus tristis). Multiple tissue samples were collected during the breeding and non-breeding seasons for both male and female goldfinches, including feather follicles in different body regions, skin, liver, and duodenum. Specifically, feather follicles were collected from the forehead, back, chest, and vent regions. Feathers of the males in the back and chest regions were yellow during breeding season but olive during non-breeding season, while the feathers in the forehead is black during breeding season but olive during non-breeding season. Feathers in the vent region is white in both seasons. The feathers in the front head, back, and chest regions are all olive in color during both breeding and non-breeding seasons. This allows a comparison of feathers from different seasons, sexes, and regions to identify the genes and potential regulatory elements underlying plumage color development, by analyzing the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility. Before the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility analyses, the genome of American goldfinch was sequenced and de novo genome assembly were performed using Supernova2. The genome assembly was annotated using MAKER2 and gene identities were assigned by performing BLAST against the Swiss-Prot section of the UniProt KnowledgeBase (UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot). The annotated genome was used for later analyses. Total RNA was extracted from the collected tissues for transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq). STAR was used to align the transcriptome sequencing reads to the goldfinch genome assembly. Expression level of genes was estimated using RSEM. Differential expression analysis was performed using edgeR. Gene ontology (GO) term enrichment analysis was performed using clusterProfiler. The transcriptomes of the feather follicles showed a difference between seasons, sexes, and body regions. To identify genes underlying carotenoid-based coloration, differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between breeding males and non-breeding males, between breeding males and breeding females, and between yellow and non-yellow body regions of breeding males were examined. Genes with functions related to carotenoid metabolism and carotenoid uptake were overexpressed in yellow feathers of breeding males compared to non-yellow feathers in breeding males, breeding females, and non-breeding males. Some of those genes were shown to be responsible for feather coloration by functional test. To identify genes underlying melanin-based coloration, DEGs between breeding males and non-breeding males, between breeding males and breeding females, and between black and non-black body regions of breeding males were examined. Multiple genes that play a role in melanin production were overexpressed or underexpressed in black feathers of breeding males compared to non-black feathers in breeding males, breeding females, and non-breeding males. Many of those identified genes are well known for their functional roles in melanin production. Biological pathways (GO terms) related to pigment production were enriched. GO terms that were significantly enriched included pigmentation, melanosome, pigment granule, pigment metabolic process, pigment cell differentiation, melanin biosynthetic process, and melanocyte differentiation. To examine chromatin accessibility, libraries were prepared from developing feather follicle samples for Assay for Transposase-Accessible Chromatin using sequencing (ATAC-seq). ATAC-seq libraries were prepared from feathers from different body regions from breeding males, breeding females, and non-breeding males, which included yellow and non-yellow feathers and black and non-black feathers. Adapter of the ATAC-seq data were first removed using NGmerge. The sequencing reads were then mapped to the American goldfinch genome assembly using Bowtie2. ATAC-seq peak calling was performed using Genrich. Peak merging and counting were performed using bedtools. Differential accessibility analysis was performed using Diffbind. Peak annotation was performed using ChiPseeker to assign peak to the nearest gene. Motif enrichment analysis was perform using HOMER. Genomic regions of differential accessibility were identified when comparing yellow and non-yellow feathers, suggesting candidate regulatory regions that control the expression of genes relevant for carotenoid-based coloration. Genomic regions of differential accessibility were also identified when comparing black and non-black feathers, suggesting candidate regulatory regions that control the expression of genes relevant for melanin-based coloration. While most of the peaks were located in intergenic regions, more than 10% of the peaks was located in promoter regions, which could be the regions regulating the differential gene expression between different feather types. The finding of genes underlying carotenoid-based and melanin-based feather color in the American goldfinch is a significant and valuable contribution to our knowledge of the genetic basis of avian plumage color. Identification of candidate genomic regions regulating the expression of feather color is a key pioneering step to unravel the development and evolution of avian plumage color diversity. The knowledge on the mechanism of sexual and seasonal dichromatism of birds is very limited, and this project has laid an important foundation for future studies. The manuscript generated from this project is in preparation and will be ready for submission to a 4* journal in 2024. A presentation on this project will be given in the 3rd Joint Congress on Evolutionary Biology in July 2024 in Montreal, Canada.

27106419.label: Major findings and research outcome
27106419.value: The major findings in this project are the identification of genes and candidate regulatory regions underlying carotenoid-based coloration (i.e. yellow feathers) and melanin-based coloration (i.e. black feathers) in the American goldfinch. The knowledge of the genetic basis of sexual dichromatism and seasonal dichromatism in birds is very limited, and we have identified genes that were differentially expressed between males and females and between males in the breeding season and non-breeding season, advancing the understanding in this area. Many of these genes were shared between the comparisons of the sexes and seasons, indicating that the underlying mechanisms of sexual dichromatism and seasonal dichromatism are similar. Compared to the more well understood melanogenesis pathway and the genes that play a role in melanin-based body coloration, we just started to gain knowledge on the carotenoid-based coloration in birds in the recent few years. Most of those studies were based on mutants arose in captivity. In this project, we studied natural plumage color variation and discovered that the development of carotenoid-based coloration involved genes that play a role in carotenoid metabolism and carotenoid uptake. We also found that to develop the melanin-based coloration, many genes that are well known for their functional roles in melanin production were involved. Some of the identified genes have been shown to play a role in body coloration in other birds and non-avian vertebrates, demonstrating a convergence in the genetic basis of body coloration development. This is an important piece of work in our understanding of the genetic basis of avian plumage coloration. The research outcomes include a publication and conference presentation: a manuscript is in preparation and will be ready for submission to a 4* journal in 2024; and an oral presentation will be given in the 3rd Joint Congress on Evolutionary Biology in July 2024 in Montreal, Canada.

27106419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27106419.value: We just started to understand the genetic basis of sexual and seasonal dichromatism in birds, and this project is a pioneering piece of work on this topic. Studying other sexually and/or seasonally dichromatic birds to investigate how universal is the genetic basis, i.e. whether the genes and candidate regulatory regions are shared between birds from different clades, is a fruitful area for future projects. The knowledge on the genetic basis of carotenoid-based coloration is still very limited, especially on yellow plumage. Future studies can investigate other birds with yellow plumage to determine if same genes are involved in the development of yellow feathers. The approach that we used in this project, i.e. combining transcriptomics and epigenomics and including samples from different sexes, seasons, and body regions, is very powerful to identify the genetic basis of coloration development. Future studies can use similar approach to investigate the same topic in other species. In vivo experiment to knock down genes in developing feathers can be carried out to validate the function of genes in future projects.

27106419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27106419.value: Birds are some of the most color-diverse animals in nature. However, our knowledge of the genetic basis of plumage color and pattern is still very limited. We know very little about how the same individual develops different colors on different body parts using the same genotype, and why the plumage color and pattern are different between males and females or between seasons in some species. In this project we identified genes and candidate regulatory regions underlying carotenoid-based coloration (i.e. yellow feathers) and melanin-based coloration (i.e. black feathers) in the American goldfinch. We have identified genes that were differentially expressed between males and females and between males in the breeding season and non-breeding season, advancing the knowledge of genetic basis of sexual dichromatism and seasonal dichromatism in birds. We discovered that the development of carotenoid-based coloration involved genes that play a role in carotenoid metabolism and carotenoid uptake. We also found that many genes that are well known for their functional roles in melanin production were involved in developing the melanin-based coloration. This project has laid an important foundation for our understanding of the genetic basis of avian plumage coloration.
