27107919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27107919.value: Ecosystems are dynamic systems determined by environmental factors and a multitude of beneficial and harmful interactions both within and between species. Many of these interactions are essential for the health of the ecosystem, yet we understand very little about their molecular basis or how these interactions are controlled at the molecular level in the brain. A very promising model to study the molecular processes in the brain underlying social interactions is the cleaner fish, a small reef fish. Cleaner fish survive by cleaning parasites off other fish species (clients), including large predatory fish. This social behaviour occurs at specialized "cleaner stations" which demonstrates a behaviourally complex, mutualistic relationship that is of great importance to the health of the coral reef ecosystem. To feed, the cleaner fish makes a variety of behavioural choices while interacting with its client fish. For instance, in addition to removing parasites, cleaner fish also engage in apparent beneficial behaviours such as tactile stimulation similar to a massage as well as harmful behaviours such as biting the client. In the absence of cleaner fish, coral reefs loose half of their fish diversity and a similar reduction in the number of young fish which demonstrates their significant ecological importance. To understand the molecular basis and the influence of environment on this vital interaction, I plan to study specific brain regions of cleaner and client fish by measuring gene expression. By understanding the genes involved in this complex behaviour, we can determine the neural basis of social interactions between two individuals. Alarmingly, in recent years we have seen that many marine organisms, including the cleaner fish, exhibit behavioural impairments when subjected to ocean warming and acidification conditions predicted for the end of this century. To understand the possible impact on this vital behaviour, we will evaluate the impact of environmental change on cleaner fish interactions. In one large experiment, we will observe the behaviour and measure brain gene expression of interacting cleaner and client fish. A fraction of the fish will be subjected to ocean warming and/or acidification to assess the impact of future climate change on these fundamental species interactions. This study will help us understand the important pathways and functions used in different regions of the brain of two interaction organisms as well as evaluate if there is a change in these fundamental interactions with climate change. 生態是個受環境因素及物種之間的互動影響而不斷改變的系統。縱使物種互動是決定生態系統健康的重要一環，現今我們仍缺乏了解這些互動背後的分子基礎或大腦如何在分子結構上控制這些互動。而醫生魚，這種細小的珊瑚魚能為針對大腦在生態互動中控制分子結構過程的研究提供一個可靠的模型。醫生魚會在指定的「清潔站」依靠清理其他魚類（客戶），包括大型捕食性魚類上的寄生蟲為生，展現出複雜的行為及共生關係，是整個生態系統的重要部分。醫生魚為了進食，會作出一系列多元化的行為與客戶互動。例如除了移除寄生蟲外，醫生魚亦會花時間作出對客戶有益的行為如類似按摩的觸覺刺激，但也會作出不利的行為例如咬客戶。如缺乏醫生魚，珊瑚礁將會失去大概一半的魚類物種及幼魚數量，証明了醫生魚在生態中擔當了重要的角色。為了解當中的分子基礎及環境因素在這重要生態互動中的影響，我計劃去量度醫生魚及客戶魚腦袋其中一部分的基因表達。找出與複雜行為有關既基因後，我們便可以決定神經系統在兩個不同個體之間互動中扮演的角色。令人擔憂地，我們近年發現很多海洋生物，包括醫生魚，在已預計本世紀末全球暖化及海洋酸化的程度下會出現行為上的障礙。因此，為了解行為上的潛在轉變，我們將會評估環境改變對醫生魚互動的影響。在一個大型實驗中，我們會觀察醫生魚與客戶魚之間的互動行為及量度兩者大腦中的基因表達。實驗中一部分的魚類亦會放於模擬海洋暖化及/或海洋酸化的環境中以量度未來氣候變化對物種互動的影響。這份研究將可幫助我們找出兩個不同個體互動時大腦會使用到的重要途徑及功能，亦能評估氣候變化能否改變這些根本的互動。

27107919.label: Realisation of objectives
27107919.value: Both objectives have been fully achieved. Objective 1: We performed an experiment in which we allowed cleaner wrasse to interact for 40minutes and this interaction was filmed. Other fish were left alone without interaction. Directly after the behavioural assay was performed the fish was euthanized three brain regions dissected out: The fore-, mid- and hindbrain and snap frozen with liquid nitrogen and in the -80 until further processing. The video were analyzed by several methods, including BORIS but also a costum developed supervised machine learning pipeline. The brain samples were then processed in the molecular lab for total RNA extractions and then sequenced on an Illumina platform. The obtained raw sequences were then bioinformatically processed to remove low quality reads and then two de novo transcriptome assemblies were produced as a first reference for both species (the cleaner and the client). The high quality reads were the mapped against the reference and the expression levels counted. Finally differential expression analysis was performed. We would that it was mainly the fore- and hindbrain involved in the interaction behaviour and identified key molecular pathways differentially regulated when these fish interact. Namely, immediate early gene alteration, dopaminergic and glutamatergic pathways, the expression of neurohormones (such as isotocin) and steroids (e.g. progesterone and estrogen). This study was published in 2022. Objective2: The same experiment was performed for the interacting fish, but this time with different environmental factors to understand the impacts of climate change on the fish interactions and the underlying mechanisms. One control (current day temperature and CO2 conditions) were provided and then compared with fish which were exposed to: elevated temperature, elevated CO2 and the combined treatment of elevated CO2 and temperature. Each of these environmental conditions resulted in behavioural disruptions concerning the motivation to interact and the quality of interaction. The associated functions under warming were linked to stress, heat shock proteins, hypoxia, and behaviour. In contrast, elevated CO2 exposure affected a range of functions associated with GABA, behaviour, visual perception, and circadian rhythm. Interestingly, in the combined Warming & High CO2 condition, we did not observe any expression changes of behaviour. However, we did find signs of endoplasmic reticulum stress and apoptosis, suggesting not only an additive effect of the environmental conditions but also a trade-off between physiological performance and behaviour in the cleaner wrasse. We suggest that impending environmental shifts can affect the behaviour and molecular processes that sustain mutualistic interactions between L. dimidiatus and its clients, which could have a cascading effect on their adaptation potential and possibly cause large-scale impacts on coral reef ecosystems.

27107919.label: Major findings and research outcome
27107919.value: Marine mutualisms are key to fitness and survival and allow species to develop complex networks of interspecific relationships. The cleaning interaction between a cleaner wrasse and its client is not only fascinating, owing to the cleaners’ immense cognitive capabilities including self-recognition but is also a key process in maintaining reef fish biodiversity. Environmental changes, such as climate change, however, are affecting these crucial behaviours, but we have yet to understand the drivers that lead to this potential mutualism breakdown. Here we evaluated what happens in the brain of these fishes when they interact and evaluate the impacts of predicted near-future environmental scenarios on behaviour and the underlying neurological mechanisms with fine-scale transcriptional patterns across three brain regions in Labroides dimidiatus and its client species Acanthurus leucosternon. Most of the transcriptional response in both species was regulated in the Hindbrain and Forebrain regions and interacting behaviour of L. dimidiatus involved immediate early gene alteration, dopaminergic and glutamatergic pathways, the expression of neurohormones (such as isotocin) and steroids (e.g. progesterone and estrogen). During ocean acidification and warming conditions, we exhibit significant changes in the interaction behaviour and transcriptional reprogramming, with functions related to stress, hypoxia, behaviour, GABAergic neurotransmission, visual perception, and circadian rhythm. We also highlight possible cascading effects on adaptation potential due to future environmental changes that include the combination of both future acidification and warming. We demonstrate that near-future predicted environmental changes can impact crucial ecological interactions by disrupting cognitive abilities and potentially resulting in mutualism breakdown.

27107919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27107919.value: Larger scientific project have come out from this funded grant with the information obtained now used to further understand the complex brain of the cleaner wrasse. We are now starting various project to elucidate more on how the brain control very important behaviours of the cleaner wrasse and get to the bottom of where exactly in the brain these signals are seen and what neuronal cells may be responsible. Furthermore, this project also lead to creating a reference genome for the cleaner wrasse species (currently in press).

27107919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27107919.value: All species need to interact in the wild as it is necessary for their survival and reproduction. However, we know little about how the brain contributes or even controls these key interactions. Here we use an interesting fish, called the cleaner wrasse, to study what happens in the brain when it interacts with a so-called client, as the cleaner in fact cleans parasites off other fishes. We revealed that it is specific brain regions facilitating this interaction now know how they were regulating this interaction. However, when the cleaner and its client live in the future (with warmer and more acidic waters due to climate change) these fish interact less and in fact their brains show signs of stress which is most likely the reason why many of the behaviours are changed. This could have large impact on coral reefs and fish biodiversity as the cleaner is a key player in keeping other fishes healthy by removing the parasites.

27110519.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27110519.value: Dementia is a highly disabling syndrome that is often devastating for persons suffering from it and for their families. Over 47 million people worldwide are reported as being affected by dementia. With no curable treatment, extensive effort is needed to ensure risk reduction, timely diagnosis, and early intervention. The development of data-informed decision-making strategies that use electronic health records to efficiently identify individuals at high risk of dementia, is essential to facilitate large scale prevention and early intervention. Pathways that lead to dementia are complicated. A recently proposed concept of cognitive footprint suggests that a person's cognition will be affected by a range of activities, i.e. footprints, throughout the life course. Genetic and environmental factors may interact across the lifespan. The timing and duration of exposure to certain risk factors may also play a significant role in the risk of dementia in later life. Based on the cognitive footprint of medical history, this population-based case-control study aims to develop and validate a clinical algorithm for predicting dementia using machine learning techniques. Using territory-wide electronic health records from the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS) in Hong Kong from 2001 to 2018, exposure to potential protective/risk factors, such as infectious diseases and medication, in combination with the period of exposure, can be modelled holistically. CDARS currently holds more than 9 million records, including 70,000 records of dementia diagnoses from 2001. With reliable information about prescription, pharmacy dispensing, diagnosis, laboratory test results, the CDARS offers a unique opportunity for hypothesis testing of existing theories and generating new hypotheses. Using a subsample of 2000 patients, we will explore the added value of neuroimaging data in reducing the prediction error by linking clinical data from CDARS with Magnetic Resonance Imaging scans from a research cohort. The direct product of this study is a clinical tool for categorizing an individual's dementia risk. The tool can be used for supporting early prevention and early diagnosis. The application of flexible machine learning techniques allows the generation of novel hypotheses. The algorithm, which is derived from real-world data, can be easily embedded into the current health information system in an automated fashion. Patients with a high risk or likelihood of dementia can be efficiently identified to allow primary intervention, without the extra costs involved in undertaking assessment. This study may also contribute to a broader discussion regarding the value of electronic records in promoting better health care. 認知障礙症是一種嚴重失能的綜合征，常會給患者和家庭造成毀滅性的影響。目前，全球有超過四千七百萬人患有認知障礙症。由於沒有可治癒的治療手段，故需在降低患病風險、及時診斷和早期干預方面做更多的努力。為實現大規模預防和早期干預策略，制定基於數據的決策策略至關重要，這包括使用電子檔案中的診斷、症狀或主訴特徵，以有效確認出具有認知障礙症高風險的個體。 導致認知障礙症的路徑很複雜。最近提出的認知足跡概念認為，個體的認知功能會受到生命歷程中一系列活動（即足跡）的影響。遺傳因素和環境因素可能在整個生命週期中相互作用。暴露於某些風險的時點和持續時間也可能對晚年認知障礙症的患病風險產生顯著的作用。 本項基於人群的病例對照研究旨在使用病史中所記錄的認知足跡，開發和驗證應用機器學習預測認知障礙症的臨床算法。使用香港臨床數據分析與報告系統（CDARS）中2001至2018年全港的電子健康記錄，將潛在的保護/風險因素（例如傳染病和用藥）結合其暴露時間整體建模。憑藉可靠的處方、藥房配發、診斷、實驗室檢測結果信息以及自2001年起七萬例以上的認知障礙症診斷，CDARS為對現有理論的假設檢驗和產生新的假設提供了特有的契機。 本研究的直接產出是用於對個體認知障礙症風險分級的臨床工具。該工具可以用於支持認知障礙症的早期預防和早期診斷。應用靈活的機器學習技術有助於創新性假設的產生。用於對實際工作數據的計算程序可被簡單地嵌入現有的健康信息系統中自動應用。具有高風險和高患病可能性的患者，無需花費額外的資源進行評估，即可接受初級干預。本研究還將促進對有效利用電子記錄以提高保健水平的更廣泛討論。

27110519.label: Realisation of objectives
27110519.value: We have successfully retrieved electronic medical records of 159,920 individuals aged 65 and above, both with and without dementia, between 2000 and 2018 from the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System in Hong Kong. We included individuals with incident diagnosis of dementia between 2010 and 2018, as well as their 1:1 matched controls. Medical records prior to 2010 were examined to determine mid- and late-life exposures to risk factors before the index date. The achievement of each objective is reported below. Please refer to the manuscript submitted in Part C 8.2 for all tables and figures mentioned in the text below. 1. Identify important patient characteristics (predictors) before their first diagnosis of dementia. Completed. We identified 51 features, including exposures to established and exploratory risk factors before and after the age of 65, from January 1, 2000, to the first diagnosis of dementia. The established factors included diabetes mellitus, hypertension, obesity, depression, head injuries, hearing loss, and lower education levels. Based on the theory of cognitive footprint, the exploratory risk factors included vascular diseases, infectious diseases, toxicity, nutritional deficiencies, and medication use. Toxicity included poisoning by drugs, medicines, and biological substances, as well as the toxic effects of substances mainly from non-medicinal sources. The diagnosis of diseases was determined by ICD-9-CM. The sample characteristics of the case and control groups are available in Table 1 of the manuscript uploaded in Part C 8.2. 2. Evaluate existing risk scores, developed from research cohorts, in terms of their predictive power of future dementia in a clinical population in Hong Kong. Completed. The reference model, which included only established risk factors, had an AUC of 0.689 (95% CI: 0.684, 0.694) for the total sample. 3. Test the theory of cognitive footprint by including relevant predictors from previous medical records and their interactions with the time dimension in the predictive model. Completed. The predictive model, which included both established and exploratory factors, showed a significantly improved AUC of 0.774 (95% CI: 0.770, 0.778). 4. Develop a more flexible predictive model using machine learning techniques to further improve the predictive accuracy of risk scores developed from conventional parametric models. Completed. The prediction accuracies of seven machine learning models, including LASSO, Random Forest, Multilayer perceptron, gradient boosting, XGBoost, LightGBM and categorical Naïve Bayes, were compared with logistic regression model for dementia risk, in the total sample and subgroups stratified by age. We found that Machine learning models that included the 15 selected factors showed comparable performance with the logistic model with all factors, with AUCs ranging between 0.767 for LASSO and 0.778 for MLP. Figure 1 shows the calibration plot of each machine learning model. Both XGBoost and MLP models were well-calibrated with an intercept near 0 (XGBoost: 0.107; MLP: 0.098) and slope near 1 (XGBoost: 0.891; MLP: 0.883). The LightGBM (Intercept: 0.159, Slope: 0.816) and Gradient Boosting (Intercept: 0.182, Slope: 0.794) models were calibrated slightly worse. Subgroup analyses stratified by sex and sensitivity analyses showed similar results to the model for overall population (Supplementary Table S6-S9). The SHAP plot showed the contribution of each variable to the MLP model, the model with the highest AUC (Figure 3). 5. Explore the contribution of neuroimaging data in improving the perdition accuracy using a subsample of stroke patients with Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans available from a research cohort. We obtained data from 1003 stroke patients who underwent MRI scans between 2000 and 2018. The dataset comprised of premorbid and post-event data, clinical variables during stroke presentation, medication, blood parameters, and MRI markers. The MRI markers included markers of Small Vessel Disease (SVD) such as microbleeds, White Matter Hyperintensities (WMH), Lacune, Enlarged perivascular spaces, and total SVD score, large artery atherosclerosis, Diffusion-Weighted Imaging (DWI), and lesion. Initially, we applied machine learning algorithms to a baseline model that only included clinical variables. We then compared this baseline model with models that additionally included MRI markers. During the study period, only 55 patients developed dementia. The reference model using XGBoost had an AUC of 0.65, while the models that included MRI had an AUC of 0.70. This provided initial evidence that MRI data can improve the prediction accuracy of dementia. However, since the incidence of dementia was low in this cohort, the overall prediction accuracy was suboptimal. We are currently collecting follow-up data on this cohort of stroke patients, as more dementia diagnoses may have been recorded between 2019 and 2023.

27110519.label: Major findings and research outcome
27110519.value: Using population-based electronic health records of 159,920 individuals from public hospitals in Hong Kong, this study developed general and age-specific clinical algorithms for predicting dementia. The mean age at dementia diagnosis was 83.97 (SD = 7.38); 40.5% of participants were male. Dementia patients had a higher prevalence of comorbidities (except ischemic heart diseases, heart failure and cardiac valve diseases), and prescribing rate of medications. The missing value rate was high in education, particularly for controls (92.5% in controls vs. 62.6% in cases). Various prediction models, including traditional logistics regression and seven state-of-the-art machine learning models, were experimented based on the cognitive footprint theory. Comparably satisfactory performances were observed between models, with the best AUC of 0.778 observed in the general population and 0.815 among people younger than 80. Exploratory risk factors such as antipsychotic medications, antidepressants, vascular diseases, polypharmacy, nutrition, and dyslipidemia were identified as important predictors. Additionally, selected important predictors varied in age-specific models with cardiovascular diseases and infectious diseases becoming prominent as age increased, implying the need for implementing age-specific models to improve prediction accuracy. The prediction models developed in this study can serve as an early screening tool for identifying individuals at increased risk of dementia or already with undiagnosed dementia. These prediction models can be integrated into current information system to facilitate clinical decision-making in a cost-effective manner without collecting additional information. Important predictors identified from our models may enhance the current understanding of modifiable risk factors of dementia that are potentially unique to the Chinese population, which allows the generation of novel hypotheses.

27110519.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27110519.value: • Limited by the case-control design, where cases and controls were matched by sex and age, these two crucial demographic variables were not included in the prediction model. With further funding support, we aim to apply a cohort design to enhance the prediction model, which will offer more direct insights into dementia prevention. • The significantly higher accuracies in predicting dementia at a younger age highlight the importance of mid-life risk factors. However, due to the duration of the study period, information on risk factor exposure during younger age is unavailable for individuals diagnosed at an older age. We plan to continue the follow-up to extend the observation time.

27110519.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27110519.value: Dementia is a highly disabling syndrome that has devastating effects on individuals and their families. Developing data-informed decision-making strategies to efficiently identify individuals at high risk of dementia is essential for large-scale prevention and early intervention initiatives. This case-control study aimed to develop a clinical algorithm for predicting dementia using machine learning, based on the cognitive footprint of medical history. The study utilized territory-wide electronic health records from the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS) in Hong Kong. A total of 159,920 individuals were included. Compared to the model that only considered established risk factors (area under the curve [AUC] 0.689, 95% CI [0.684, 0.690]), the predictive accuracy substantially improved for models that included exploratory factors (0.774, [0.770, 0.778]). Machine learning models and logistic regression performed similarly well, with AUC ranging from 0.767 for LASSO to 0.778 for MLP. Age-specific models identified different sets of important features, with neurological or psychological diseases and medication being more important in younger ages, while cardiovascular and infectious diseases became prominent in older ages. The models developed in this study demonstrated satisfactory predictive power for diagnosing dementia. These algorithms can be utilized in clinical practice to enable precise and timely primary interventions cost-effectively.

27117419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27117419.value: Human enterovirus EV-A71 is one of several Enterovirus serotypes that cause hand-foot-and-mouth disease, which can produce life-threatening neurological complications. Severe outbreaks caused by different enteroviruses, including EV-A71 and CV-A16, have been reported periodically throughout the world. Nevertheless, neither an effective vaccine nor an anti-enteroviral drug is available. Our recent work has identified a novel interferon inducible EV-A71 entry factor, a host-produced tryptophanyl tRNA synthetase (hWARS), which is not only essential for translation but also upregulated for effective enterovirus infection. More importantly, we demonstrated that interferon gamma (IFNg) stimulation increased the infectivity of EV-A71 in human neuronal cells through the upregulation of the surface expression of hWARS. The results are highly relevant to the elevated level of IFNg in patients with severe EV-A71 infection. With the new understanding that a tRNA synthetase functions in virus attachment, the next important step is to study the interaction between the hWARS and EV-A71 and the regulation of hWARS, which could shed light on EV-A71 pathogenesis and future development of anti-EV-A71 drugs. Therefore, in the proposed work, we will first identify the interaction region(s) of hWARS and surface protein of EV-A71 by using in vitro pull-down assay. In addition, we will make use of the recent structural advances in cryoelectron microscopy, which allows us to further study their protein structure interaction. The functional importance of the interaction region(s) will be verified by generating hWARS mutants followed by performing infection and virus attachment assays. Notably, our preliminary results obtained so far are encouraging. Firstly, we have already showed that the N-terminus of hWARS is essential for effective EV-A71 infection. Secondly, mass spectrometry analysis has confirmed that hWARS is heavily post-translationally modified, suggesting that its expression is tightly regulated. Given the versatile roles of post-translational modifications (PTMs) in regulating various steps of virus replication as shown in previous studies, the importance of PTMs on the cell entry role of hWARS during EV-A71 infection will be investigated using site-directed mutagenesis approach. Lastly, we will generate an EV-A71-susceptible mouse cell line by genome-editing mouse WARS sequence using CRISPR/Cas9 technology. The identification of the EV-A71 interaction region and the cell entry regulatory PTMs of hWARS could greatly facilitate future development of anti-viral entry blocker peptides and anti-EV-A71 drugs. Also, the knowledge of generating an EV-A71-susceptible mouse cell line could be transferred to the generation of a new mouse model for studying EV-A71 pathogenesis and drug testing in the future. 人類腸道病毒A71型（EV-A71）是眾多腸道病毒血清型之壹，EV-A71病毒感染可導致手足口病及嚴重者出現危及生命的中樞神經系統癥狀。全世界範圍內腸道病毒感染病例呈周期性爆發，其中就包括常見的EV-A71型和柯薩奇病毒A16型（CV-A16）。然而目前仍無有效的疫苗以及抗腸道病毒藥物進行防治。我們最近研究發現壹種新型幹擾素誘導型EV-A71入侵因子-色氨酰-tRNA合成酶（hWARS），由宿主生成的hWARS不僅在蛋白質生物合成方面起重要作用，更能通過上調表達而促進腸道病毒的感染。尤為重要的是我們證明幹擾素-gamma（IFN）可誘導人類神經細胞膜表面hWARS的過度表達從而增加EV-A71的感染性，上述研究結果與臨床EV-A71感染重癥患者體內上調的IFN水平高度吻合。鑒於目前研究發現hWARS在EV-A71病毒附著方面的作用，下壹步重點研究hWARS同EV-A71之間相互作用以及hWARS的調節機制，此項研究將有助於闡釋EV-A71感染的病理機制及後期抗EV-A71病毒藥物的研發。因此，本次科研計劃申請中我們將首先通過體外蛋白拉下實驗鑒定hWARS和EV-A71病毒表面蛋白的結合位點。並且借助冷凍電子顯微鏡術在蛋白質結構學中的研究優勢，深入研究hWARS與病毒蛋白間的結合區域。通過合成hWARS突變蛋白檢驗EV-A71感染性及病毒附著實驗來進壹步驗證其功能性結合區域。值得關註的是我們前期實驗結果令人振奮，首先我們已經證明hWARS N-端在EV-A71感染中起著關鍵作用。其次質譜分析結果發現hWARS蛋白存在大量翻譯後修飾，這也暗示hWARS蛋白的表達受到精密調控。基於前期蛋白質翻譯後修飾在病毒復制過程中多樣性調控作用的研究文章，通過點突變實驗論證hWARS在EV-A71感染過程中的蛋白質翻譯後修飾功能將極其關鍵。最後我們將通過CRISPR/Cas9基因組編輯技術改變小鼠WARS基因序列從而構建EV-A71易感性小鼠細胞模型。EV-A71病毒結合區域以及hWARS蛋白翻譯後修飾作用的研究將極大促進後期抗病毒侵入的多肽以及抗EV-A71病毒藥物的研發。除此之外，構建EV-A71易感性小鼠細胞模型的實驗技術將應用到後期EV-A71病毒感染機制研究和相關藥物測試方面。

27200419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27200419.value: This research project is motivated by the PI's experience of managing operations in multiple hospital units. Through the collaborations with the hospitals, the PI has observed that the coordination among different units, even within the same hospital, is challenging. One of the fundamental problems is that key performance indicators (KPIs) are measured on an individual department basis. Owing to the existing heavy workloads imposed on the individual units, there is a lack of incentives for them to put the essential joint efforts into optimizing the overall efficiency of the hospital. The PI will leverage his experience of managing emergency department (ED) patient flows and inpatient ward (IW) operations to investigate a coordination mechanism between the two units. This proposed research aims to address two key questions: why and how shall the two units coordinate their operations? This project will deliver a complete coordination mechanism consisting of three core components -- (i) system visibility, (ii) coordinated decisions, and (iii) coordination incentives -- all of which have been proven successful in facilitating coordination in a supply chain context. However, the existing coordination mechanisms in a supply chain setting are not applicable to healthcare units because of the substantial differences between the two systems and the non-transferable and conflicting KPIs among hospital units. Thus, an in-depth study is imperative to establish an appropriate coordination mechanism. The novelty of this proposed research is threefold. First, we study how real-time and future information shared between ED and IW will benefit the ED boarding operations. Second, we establish a coordination mechanism with the utilization of such information for integrated and responsive decisions between the two units. Third, KPI improvements for the individual units are demonstrated for creating coordination incentives. Look-ahead stochastic and integer programming models are developed to achieve the goals. For an independent and unbiased performance assessment, the optimization models will be solved in a rolling-horizon framework to guide continuous decision-making under a dynamic simulation environment to evaluate the benefits of the coordination scheme. To translate research into practice, managerial insights derived from this research project will be shared with the PI's long-time collaborating hospitals for policy recommendations. 此研究項目建基於項目主持人於不同醫院部門協助運營管理之經驗。透過與醫院之間合作，項目主持人觀察到即使在同一醫院內，不同單位之間的協調也具挑戰性。其中一個基本問題是關鍵績效指標（KPI）是按個別部門衡量。基於各單位現有繁重工作量，部門缺乏動力引領他們共同努力優化醫院的整體效率。項目主持人將利用他於管理急症室（ED）和住院病房（IW）的經驗研究兩個部門之間的協調機制。這項研究旨在解決兩個關鍵問題：兩個不同部門為何以及如何協調其運作？此項目將提供一個完整的協調機制，此機制包括三個核心組成部分:（i）系統可視性、（ii）決策協調、以及（iii）協調激勵。此三要素都已被證明成功促進供應鏈協調。然而，因為供應鏈和醫療系統之間存在實質性差異及醫院單位之間存在不可轉移和互相矛盾的KPI，現有供應鏈協調機制並不適用於醫療系統。因此，必須進行深入研究，以建立適當的協調機制。這項研究共帶來三項創新點。首先，我們研究ED和IW之間共享實時和未來信息將如何有利於ED病人進院運作。其次，我們建立了一個協調機制，利用這些信息，為兩個單位之間作統一及快速決策。第三，證明各個單位的關鍵績效指標改進，以創建協調激勵措施。項目開發隨機整數規劃模型以實現目標。項目將作獨立效能評估，優化模型將在滾動範圍框架中求解，以帶領在動態模擬環境下的連續決策，以評估協調方案的效能。項目將研究轉化為實踐，將與項目主持人的長期合作醫院分享來自研究項目的管理見解，以獲取政策建議。

27200419.label: Realisation of objectives
27200419.value: For Objective 1 (To investigate how real-time and future information shared between the ED and IW can be utilized for coordination): Under this objective, we have worked with the HKU Department of Emergency Medicine and HKU-Shenzhen Hospital on patient boarding from Emergency Departments (EDs) to Inpatient Wards (IWs). With their help and support, we gained access to the Clinical Data Analysis and Reporting System (CDARS) database containing ED, IW, and patient boarding records. We conducted a case study in Hong Kong and analyzed the data (with machine learning) to understand the relationship between ED and IW operations during COVID-19. We identified factors associated with hospital boarding during the Omicron surge in HK. We conducted a retrospective cohort study including all ED visits and inpatient (IP) ward admissions from January 1st to March 31st, 2022. Vector Autoregression model evaluated the effects of a single variable on the targeted hospital boarding variables. Our statistical analysis suggested that the number of confirmed COVID-19 cases was not the sole significant contributor, while occupancy of medical wards was still a critical factor associated with patient boarding. The resulting paper was published in the Journal of Medical Systems (Wu et al., 2023). Regarding the future information sharing mechanism, our proposed framework considers a patient streaming strategy and develops a coordination mechanism between ED and IW. With our proposed system visibility, both the system status and information about the operations are shared between the two units. The required framework has been established and evaluated in Wang et al. (2024). For Objectives 2 (To establish an optimization framework to determine the joint decisions of ED and IW for ED boarding), 3 (To demonstrate coordination incentives by evaluating the KPI improvements for individual units), 4 (To develop efficient computational algorithms for real-time and integrated solutions): Collaborating with CUHK Accident and Emergency Medicine Academic Unit and Prince of Wales Hospital, we established an optimization framework to solve the integrated problem of ED and IW operations and address ED boarding issues, evaluated the key performance indicators (KPIs) in ED and IW by considering coordination incentives, and developed computationally efficient algorithms to provide real-time and integrated solutions. Mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models are developed, and our proposed methodology is shown to be effective in improving computational efficiency. Coordination effects are evaluated with numerical experiments. The main results are presented in Wang et al. (2024). Additionally, tasks related to the development of computationally efficient algorithms in ED operations are presented in Thiago Alves de Queiroz et al. (2021, 2023). In Thiago Alves de Queiroz et al. (2021, 2023), we optimized ED patient scheduling for doctors by minimizing total weighted tardiness. We introduced a re-optimization heuristic that utilizes multiple queues categorized by urgency levels. We then combined this with an effective variable neighborhood search. Additionally, we proposed a scenario-based planning approach that uses sampled scenarios to anticipate future events and further optimize scheduling using the variable neighborhood search. We also addressed a problem variant where the emergency department receives advanced information on some patients' arrival times and urgency levels. We conducted a comprehensive computational study on realistic instances from Hong Kong SAR of China and Italy. Our results validate the performance of our proposed methods, highlighting the benefits of having more doctors and receiving early information. Finally, further research on optimization frameworks and computational algorithms for home health care (Nasir and Kuo, 2020) and coordination incentives design (Wang et al., 2022) was also conducted. For Objective 5 (To assess the performance of the proposed coordination mechanism under a dynamic simulation environment): We developed a dynamic simulation environment for the integrated ED and IW environment and deployed the proposed coordination mechanism in such an environment. From our numerical experiments, patients’ waiting and boarding times in ED could achieve 43% and 49% reductions, respectively. Our results suggest that the coordination mechanism can significantly improve the efficiency of both units in terms of patient waiting time, boarding time, and length of stay. Lastly, we extend it to more complex scenarios and find that the coordination mechanism continues to perform well when service durations are uncertain and streaming accuracy varies. The impacts of various factors are also investigated to derive managerial insights. The details of the simulation model and the performance of the proposed coordination mechanism are presented in Wang et al. (2024). Publications: - de Queiroz, T. A., Iori, M., Kramer, A., & Kuo, Y. 27200419.label: Major findings and research outcome
27200419.value: Regarding ED and IW demand and capacity modeling and prediction, we conducted a case study in Hong Kong to analyze the relationship between ED and IW operations during COVID-19, through the collaboration with HKU Department of Emergency Medicine and HKU-Shenzhen Hospital. Using the CDARS database, we identified factors associated with hospital boarding during the Omicron surge and concluded that occupancy of medical wards was a critical factor associated with patient boarding (Wu et al., 2023). We also established an optimization framework to solve the integrated problem of ED and IW operations and address ED boarding issues. We evaluated the KPIs in ED and IW by considering coordination incentives and developed computationally efficient algorithms to provide real-time and integrated solutions. The proposed coordination mechanism was effective in improving the efficiency of both units in terms of patient waiting time, boarding time, and length of stay. Patients’ waiting and boarding times in ED could achieve 43% and 49% reductions, respectively. The impacts of various factors were investigated to derive managerial insights. The research outcomes were presented in Wang et al. (2024). We proposed a re-optimization heuristic that utilizes multiple queues categorized by urgency levels and a scenario-based planning approach that uses sampled scenarios to anticipate future events. They also addressed a problem variant where the ED receives advanced information on some patients' arrival times and urgency levels. The proposed methods were validated through a comprehensive computational study on realistic instances from Hong Kong SAR of China and Italy. The results highlighted the benefits of having more doctors and receiving early information (Thiago Alves de Queiroz et al., 2021, 2023). The research resulted in several publications, including papers in the Production and Operations Management, Decision Support Systems, European Journal of Operational Research, Journal of Medical Systems, and Lecture Notes of Computer Science. The proposed coordination mechanism was also submitted for review at Production and Operations Management. The research outcomes have significant implications for healthcare organizations and policymakers. The proposed optimization framework and coordination mechanism could be utilized to improve the efficiency of ED and IW operations and address ED boarding issues. This is expected to lead to better patient outcomes, reduced hospital crowding, and lower healthcare costs. The proposed methods can also be extended to other healthcare settings and can be adapted to handle different types of emergencies (Wang et al., 2024).

27202219.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202219.value: 小型自主無人機（UAV）的激增是過去十年中機器人行業最顯著的趨勢之一。受益於計算、通信和傳感技術的快速發展，無人機具有前所未有的便攜性和成本優勢，為各行業帶來了巨大的機遇。例如，無人機大大降低了航空攝影的成本，徹底消除了基礎設施檢查中工人的安全問題，並大大提高了測量、三維測繪和包裹投遞的效率。巨大的潛力驅使著各行業公司積極投入到無人機開發中。大疆創新（DJI）開辟並塑造了小型消費無人機的消費市場。高通（Qualcomm）、英特爾（Intel）和亞馬遜（Amazon）也積極投入無人機開發，並大力推廣用於工業用途的無人機技術。 但是，在工業環境中採用無人機仍然面臨著根本性的挑戰。 其中包括如何生成大機動的飛行策略使無人機能在擁擠環境中操作。該任務的困難主要來自於兩方面：（1）有限的機載計算資源限制了可以使用的算法；（2）高度非線性的飛行動力學極大地復雜化了軌跡跟蹤控制器的設計、分析和穩定性驗証。實際的UAV操作還要求軌跡生成和控制算法對模型內部不確定性和外部干擾有足夠的魯棒性。 該項目的目標是系統地研究一類具有非線性空氣動力學和廣飛行包絡線的無人機，即尾座式垂直起降（VTOL）無人機，的軌跡生成和跟蹤控制。我們將開發一套完整的框架來設計、分析和驗証該類無人機的軌跡生成和控制算法， 尤其是在復雜環境中的大機動飛行。該框架將包括（1）一套統一的算法框架用於生成尾座式無人機全包絡線下的飛行軌跡，（2）一套理論可証明穩定性和魯棒性的在線軌跡跟蹤控制算法。我們將開發所提出的算法，並在模擬器和實際無人機上做充分的驗証。這些工作的成功實施將推動無人機技術的理論和實踐，並最終為其在工業中的廣泛應用鋪平道路。

27202219.label: Realisation of objectives
27202219.value: 1. We investigate the full-envelope tail-sitter dynamics and parameter uncertainties, and thoroughly prove the differential flatness in the coordinated flight condition. We consider the entire airframe as a rigid body and model the translational and rotational dynamics using Newton–Euler equations. The aerodynamics are represented by a classic aerodynamic model following the conventional fixed-wing aircraft. Choosing the vehicle position as flat output, we show that the full 12-dimensional system states (i.e., position, velocity, attitude, body velocity) and inputs (thrust and control moment) can be expressed by functions of the flat output and its derivatives. The key to this problem is that we specify the UAV to perform coordinated flight where it has no side force, and thus formulate the flatness function of the angle of attack into a one-dimensional root-finding problem, which can be solved efficiently by numerical methods. Subsequently, we divide the system model into two levels to practically reduce the control complexity and efficiency -- a low-level system isolates the angular velocity control and attenuates the Coriolis term, aerodynamic moment, and model uncertainties including actuator dynamics, flexible modes, propeller vibrations, and delays, -- a high-level system considers the rest rigid motion, reducing the computational complexity in trajectory generation. Details of the implementation can be referred to [2] (Item 2 of Part C-8). 2. Based on the differential flatness of the tail-sitter, we develop a trajectory optimization that generates aggressive flight maneuvers while taking into account obstacle avoidance, actuator constraints, flight time, dynamical feasibility, and singularity conditions in coordinated flight. Furthermore, since the proposed trajectory optimization is a constrained nonlinear problem that is hard to solve efficiently and reliably, we develop an efficient, feasibility-first nonlinear programming (NLP) solver based on penalty method and sequential quadratic programming (SQP), enabling real-time planning via only onboard computation. Details of the implementation can be referred to [2] (Item 2 of Part C-8) and [3] (Item 3 of Part C-8). 3. We propose a two-stage control architecture for high-accuracy trajectory tracking control, even in the presence of wind gusts in outdoor environments. The first stage transforms the planned flat-output trajectory into a state–input trajectory while compensating for wind effect and treating singularities. The second stage is a real-time state trajectory tracking controller, which consists of a low-level controller for tracking angular velocity command in high bandwidth, and a high-level controller for tracking state trajectories (i.e., position, velocity, and attitude trajectories) throughout the entire flight envelope. Specifically, the low-level controller employs loop-shaping techniques (i.e., proportional–-integral–derivative (PID) controller and additional Notch filters for flexible modes attenuation), to enhance the robustness to model uncertainties. The high-level controller is an advanced on-manifold model predictive controller (MPC) that linearizes system states by mapping them to local coordinates on the state manifold around each point along the reference trajectory, resulting in a minimal-parameterization, singularity-free, global control within the entire flight envelope. Details of the implementation can be referred to [1] (Item 1 of Part C-8) and [2] (Item 2 of Part C-8). 4. We conduct extensive simulations and real-world flight experiments to validate the proposed algorithms. We compare the proposed tracking controller and trajectory optimization with existing methods, both showing superior performance in simulations. We further implement these algorithms on a tail-sitter prototype, demonstrating elaborate flight experiments in both indoor and outdoor environments, including agile SE(3) flight through consecutive narrow windows requiring specific attitude and with speed up to 10 m/s, typical tail-sitter maneuvers (transition, level flight, and loiter) with speed up to 20 m/ s, and extremely aggressive aerobatic maneuvers (Wingover, Loop, Vertical Eight, and Cuban Eight) with acceleration up to 2.5 g. Moreover, we also develop a fully autonomous tail-sitter UAV equipped with a LiDAR sensor, capable of high-speed navigation with obstacle avoidance in unknown, cluttered environments using only onboard sensors and computation. Details of the implementation can be referred to [2] (Item 2 of Part C-8) and [3] (Item 3 of Part C-8). [1] Guozheng Lu, Wei Xu, and Fu Zhang, "On-Manifold Model Predictive Control for Trajectory Tracking on Robotic Systems," IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics , vol. 70, no. 9, pp. 9192-9202, 2022. [2] Guozheng Lu, Yixi Cai, Nan Chen, Fanze Kong, Yunfan Ren, and Fu Zhang, "Trajectory Generation and Tracking Control for Aggressive Tail-Sitter Flights," The International Journal of Robotics Research, 2023, doi:10.1177/02783649231 207655, (In Press). [3] Guozheng Lu*, Yunfan Ren*, Fangcheng Zhu, Haotian Li, Ruize Zhu, Yixi Cai, Ximin Lyu, and Fu Zhang, "Autonomous Tail-Sitter Flights in Unknown Environments," IEEE Transactions on Robotics, 2023 (In submission, preprint available at https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OtWoTwjggEegNQ0I_Je2sJjfFRkAT2lf/view?usp=sharing).

27202219.label: Major findings and research outcome
27202219.value: We address the theoretical and practical problems related to the trajectory generation and tracking control of tail-sitter UAVs. Theoretically, we focus on the differential flatness property with full exploitation of actual UAV aerodynamic models, We have found that a tail-sitter is differentially flat with accurate (not simplified) aerodynamic models within the entire flight envelope, by specifying coordinate flight conditions and choosing the vehicle position as the flat output. This fundamental property allows us to fully exploit high-fidelity aerodynamic models in trajectory planning and tracking control to achieve accurate tail-sitter flights. Particularly, an optimization-based trajectory planner for tail-sitters is proposed to design high-quality, smooth trajectories with consideration of kino-dynamic constraints, singularity-free constraints, actuator saturation, and obstacle avoidance. We also develop an efficient, feasibility-first solver to resolve this constrained non-linear trajectory optimization in real-time. The planned trajectory of flat output is transformed into a state trajectory in real-time with optional consideration of wind in environments. To track the state trajectory, a global, singularity-free, and minimally parameterized on-manifold MPC is developed, which fully leverages the accurate aerodynamic model to achieve high-accuracy trajectory tracking within the whole flight envelope. The proposed algorithms are all validated in real-world flight experiments. We develop a fully autonomous tail-sitter UAV capable of high-speed flights in unknown, cluttered, real-world environments via only onboard sensors and computation.

27202219.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27202219.value: Our proposed framework is a model-based approach. Higher tracking accuracy requires a more precise dynamic model, especially the aerodynamic model. However, identifying a high-fidelity aerodynamic model generally requires high-cost and time-consuming wind tunnel tests. The cost and time escalate for tail-sitter UAVs where the envelope of the angle of attack is large. In this paper, we leveraged the wind tunnel test data. For general tail-sitter UAVs, such an aerodynamic model could be identified from onboard sensor data collected in real flights, which would be a promising future research to pursue. The tracking accuracy can be further improved by augmenting a low-level controller to the thrust acceleration. In the present implementation, we directly mapped the thrust acceleration command to the collective throttle of the four motors. However, the actual propeller thrust is also affected by various other factors, such as the propeller inflow and motor internal dynamics. These factors have caused significant errors between the actual and commanded thrust acceleration as shown in our experiment results. This issue could be mitigated by tracking the thrust acceleration command aT with a low-level controller based on accelerometer measurements.

27202219.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27202219.value: Our research provides a thorough theoretical analysis of trajectory generation and tracking control for tail-sitter UAVs, and successfully implements the proposed algorithms on prototypes demonstrating aggressive flights and autonomous navigation in real-world environments.

27202419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202419.value: Coastal cities worldwide are vulnerable to flooding caused by storm surges, intense rainfall or both, resulting in severe property damage, disruption to daily life and socioeconomic losses. It is widely recognised that the risks associated with flooding will increase in coming decades owing to continuing urbanisation, economic growth and climate change, which is leading to rising sea levels. Hong Kong, subject to frequent tropical cyclones, typhoons and intense rainstorms, is no exception, and flooding is a significant threat. Although the construction of improved drainage systems has greatly alleviated urban floods, it is not uncommon for storm surges combined with intense rainstorms to result in severe flooding in low-lying coastal areas. However, current models, forecasts, warnings and management strategies for such flooding in low-lying areas with a high concentration of infrastructure remain inadequate. The imminent and worsening risk requires improvements in scientific understanding, prediction and management. The aim of the proposed project is therefore to improve the understanding and prediction of coastal flooding in low-lying urbanised areas by performing real-time in-situ observations, delivering a step change in robust modelling capability and developing novel impact assessments for storm surge-induced flooding in combination with intense rainstorms, thereby moving beyond existing research on such flooding from storm surge and overland flow. The applicant will first perform real-time field monitoring during coastal flooding by exploiting wireless sensor networks in combination with the crowdsourcing approach in a selected flood-prone site in Hong Kong. A novel robust modelling framework and parameterisation capable of accurately and efficiently predicting coastal inundation and its interaction with buildings and infrastructure will then be developed. The aforementioned field dataset will be used to develop physical understanding and to verify the numerical model and correct its parameterisation in real time. Model capability will be improved by providing better predictions and more dynamic information on the spatial and temporal variability of coastal flooding in urban areas. Based on real-time measurement and modelling, the project will develop a generic hazard impact model for use in coastal flooding decision-making under various current and future scenarios, leading to generic approaches that can be used in coastal cities worldwide to manage coastal flooding caused by storm surges and overland flow. 世界各地的沿海城市都容易受到風暴潮、強降雨或兩者誘發的洪水的影響，導致嚴重的社會經濟損失。人們普遍認識到，由於持續的城市化，經濟增長和氣候變化，未來幾十年與洪水相關的風險將會增加。香港受頻繁的熱帶氣旋，颱風和強暴雨影響，洪水是一個具有重大威脅的自然災害。雖然目前排水系統的改善已大大緩解了城市洪水，但風暴潮加上強烈暴雨導致低窪沿海地區嚴重水災的情況並不少見。然而，目前在基礎設施高度集中的低窪地區發生洪水的模型，預報，警告和管理策略仍然不足。 因此，擬議項目的目的是通過洪水數據收集和高性能城市洪水數值模型開發改進對低窪城市化地區風暴潮與強降雨誘發的海岸洪水的預測，並揭示洪水在低窪沿海城區的形成與影響機理。申請人將首先在沿海洪水易發區利用公眾參與的方法收集實時洪水數據。然後開發一種新穎的穩健洪水數值模型方法，能夠準確有效地預測沿海洪水及其與建築物和基礎設施的相互作用。通過提供關於城區海岸洪水的空間和時間變化的更好預測和更多動態信息，改進模型搭建和參數化方法，提高模型預測精度。基於洪水監測和建模，該項目將開發一個通用的災害影響模型，用於各種當前和未來情景下的沿海洪水決策，從而提出可用於全球沿海城市管理風暴潮和陸強降雨誘發的海岸洪水的通用方法。

27202419.label: Realisation of objectives
27202419.value: The project has identified four objectives, and all of them have been fully achieved. To be specific. Objective 1: Gather flood data in low-lying urban area during flooding by exploiting the crowdsourcing approach. The finding for this objective was published in International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction (Q1). To achieve this objective, we have developed a data gathering approach to collect public social media data during a flood event. We used 2020 Chengdu rainstorm as a case study and social media including Weibo and Tiktok were used for data collection. Spatio-temporal patterns of public responses towards urban flooding and flood impacts were analysed. Temporal evolution of social media activities was also investigated to track the flood process and further compared with observed precipitation data. Moreover, major flood impacts were assessed through frequency analysis of impact-related keywords. Finally, spatial information was extracted and the typical hotspots are selected for detailed analysis. And the data collected via social media can be further used for validating flood modelling. Objective 2: Develop a novel high performance full hydrodynamic model for flooding from storm surges in combination with intense rainstorms that includes critical urban features and land use. The finding for objective 2 led to two journal publications, one in Hydrology and Earth System Science (HESS)(Q1), and one in Journal of Hydrology(Q1). To achieve this objective, we first did a comprehensive review on urban flood models (the publication in HESS), and concluded that full hydrodynamic flood model has the robust capability of simulating urban flooding and the associated dynamic processes. Therefore, we develop a spatially distributed hydrodynamic model framework incorporating both hydrological and hydraulic processes of surface and subsurface drainage processes during urban flooding (the publication in Journal of Hydrology). The model is built upon 2D full shallow water equations solved by a Godunov-type finite volume method with robust treatments of the bed source term. To properly involve drainage flow effects, we present three methods to quantify the drainage flow discharge and its delay time which affect both urban hydrology and surface inundation. Besides, a simple OpenMPI-based parallel algorithm is applied to accelerate the model and ensure computational efficiency when applied to real-world events. The model framework is justified through the validations with five benchmark cases. Benchmark results indicate that the well-balanced treatment of bed source term ensures the model applicability in irregular urban surfaces, the model can predict both urban surface inundation and flood hydrograph, and the proposed drainage flow treatments can well reproduce drainage flow hydrograph. The model framework is successfully applied to simulate rainstorm-induced flood events in a rural–urban catchment, the upper Shenzhen River catchment. Results further demonstrate the robust capability of the model in the quantification of flow exchange between surface and subsurface systems to some extent even in the absence of drainage information. Our framework provides a practical solution for urban flood simulation even when pipe data are scarce. Objective 3: Investigate physical and model complexities to improve coastal flooding prediction in low-lying urbanized areas. The finding from this objective was published in Journal of Hydrology (Q1) With increasing urban flood risk due to urbanisation and climate change, flood hazard prediction is ever more crucial for flood risk management and emergency response. However, when sufficient high-quality data are lacking, a standard flood inundation modelling approach has significant uncertainties. Therefore, this study develops a bottom-up approach for urban flood hazard mapping at multiple levels (grid-kilometre-district), built upon the integration of grid-based flood modelling with data acquisition from open sources. This reduces the adverse effects of data scarcity and quality on hazard modelling. In the paper, we first set out an integrated approach for gridded inundation mapping in an urban basin using a hydrodynamic model supported by crowd-sourced social media data. Then, applying the model to flooding in Chengdu in August 2020, we articulate how input data bias and parameter uncertainty both affect urban inundation modelling. The results show that the choice of terrain data and the quantification of urban drainage flows significantly influence the modelled urban inundation extent, depth and duration. This indicates the potential for large variation when using urban inundation mapping merely relying on a single-scale flood hydrodynamic modelling even when supported by crowd-sourced data. The multilevel hazard mapping approach developed here presents multi-layered and comprehensive inundation mapping; thus the effects of data bias or availability are reduced and the coarser hazard mapping shows less sensitivity to the data input quality and model uncertainty, indicating relatively higher reliability at this higher spatial scale. The grid-kilometre-district three level approach provides more reliable flood hazard mapping, which can support rainstorm-induced flood management in data scarce cities. Objective 4: better understand the dynamic processes of the spatial and temporal variability of coastal flooding. We have investigated the flood dynamics processes from multiple viewpoints, including flood and underground space interaction, surface water flood drainage over runway sufaces etc. The finding on flood dynamics led to more than two Q1 journal publications (e.g., Tunnelling and Underground Space Technology, Construction and Buildin Materials).

27202419.label: Major findings and research outcome
27202419.value: 1. To develop a crawler-algorithm to extract and filter the social media flood data from the commonly used social platforms, namely Weibo (static data) and Tiktok (dynamic data). Based on the spatiotemporal analysis of the extracted flood data, we found that, social media activities and precipitation are temporally correlated in a significant and positive way. The temporal evolution analysis of social media topics reveals the process of flooding and enables quick determination of severely affected areas. Spatially, social media data can provide spatial flood information and social media activities are typically connected with user demographics. 2. To develop a spatially distributed hydrodynamic model framework incorporating both hydrological and hydraulic processes of surface and subsurface drainage processes during urban flooding. Results demonstrate the robust capability of the model in the quantification of flow exchange between surface and subsurface systems to some extent even in the absence of drainage information. Our framework provides a practical solution for urban flood simulation even when pipe data are scarce. 3. To develop a bottom-up approach for urban flood hazard mapping at multiple levels (grid-kilometre-district), built upon the integration of grid-based flood modelling with data acquisition from open sources. The research outcomes reveal that the choice of terrain data and the quantification of urban drainage flows significantly influence the modelled urban inundation extent, depth and duration. This indicates the potential for large variation when using urban inundation mapping merely relying on a single-scale flood hydrodynamic modelling even when supported by crowd-sourced data. The multilevel hazard mapping approach developed here presents multi-layered and comprehensive inundation mapping; thus the effects of data bias or availability are reduced and the coarser hazard mapping shows less sensitivity to the data input quality and model uncertainty, indicating relatively higher reliability at this higher spatial scale. The grid-kilometre-district three level approach provides more reliable flood hazard mapping, which can support rainstorm-induced flood management in data scarce cities. 4. To examine flood dynamics on underground staircases and its relationship with staircase characteristics through a series of numerical experiments using a two-dimensional (2D) hydrodynamic model. The study also uncovers how staircase design influences flood hazard levels.

27202419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27202419.value: Further research could focus on applying the developed model and approach to investigate flood impact on critical infrastructures (e.g., subway system) under an uncertain climate. To this, a proposal is being planned for seeking further funding support.

27202419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27202419.value: Urban flooding is becoming more frequent and severe due to urban development and climate change and it may cause significant damage and socio-economic impact. To address urban flood challenges, this research project develops a method to extract open sourced flood data, advanced numerical model to simulate flood dynamic processes, and multi-level hazard mapping technique to predict urban flood impact. Our models and frameworks provides practical and more reliable solutions for urban flood simulation and hazard mapping, which can support rainstorm-induced flood management.

27202919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27202919.value: 人類目前面臨許多挑戰，如威脅生命的疾病，包括癌症和神經退行性疾病。在解決此類疾病方面，我們需要有效的生物傳感技術，以便在分子水平上進行精確測量，早期診斷和優化治療。小型化生物傳感器的尺寸以提高其空間分辨率和靈敏度是應對這些挑戰的一種策略。因此，非常期望開發新的成像方法以及开发可時空分辨的代謝分析量化探針。 在過去幾十年中，熒光成像在生物醫學研究方面取得了非凡的進步，但迄今為止尚未解決的主要挑戰之一是熒光素的穩定性差。相比之下，具有生物相容性的納米金剛石顆粒中的氮-空位色心（光致發光缺陷）顯示出無限的光穩定性。這些原子缺陷的依賴於電子自旋態的光致發光可以促進量子感測，即用作光學磁力計，在室溫下具有前所未有的靈敏度和精度。不幸的是，它們相應的生物學應用受到許多由非磁性信號支配的生物醫學過程的阻礙。在這裡，我們的創新方法是將納米金剛石（有前景的量子平台）與新興的自旋交叉複合物（可切換的分子磁體）結合起來，以實現各種生化信號的光學讀出。潛在的機制涉及這些分子致動器在外部刺激（例如溫度，壓力，光照射等）下從反磁性（低自旋S = 0）到順磁（高自旋S = 2）狀態的可逆切換。 該研究旨在開發先進的量子納米傳感器，其原則上能夠檢測局部生物事件，目的是可視化亞細胞組織和動力學過程。我們將通過靜電相互作用將納米金剛石與鐵基自旋交叉分子（包圍在配位絡合物中的生物相關離子）接枝來構建量子納米傳感器。通過開發優化的傳感方案，我們可以響應局部環境實現自旋狀態轉換的可靠光學測量。作為概念驗證演示，我們將研究開發的納米傳感器在單個納米粒子水平（例如，在單個激光光斑的照射下）的溫度依賴性轉變行為，這對於在納米尺度實現自旋交叉複合物的全部潛力是至關重要的。 該項目將引領下一代量子工程和測量技術。成功完成這項研究將創造一個強大的工具（特別是在量子計量學中），以精細細節揭示和理解單細胞的奧秘，從長遠來看，有望帶來生物醫學研究的突破。

27202919.label: Realisation of objectives
27202919.value: We have conducted a number of investigations targeting the project objectives and have almost completed all objectives as originally proposed in the project. Specifically, we have systematically studied the literature about bio-orientated quantum sensing and its exploration in bio-membranes, and summarized our understanding in a review article [ACS Sensors, 6, 2077-2107 (2021); Membranes, 12, 957 (2022)]. We have constructed nanodiamond-based hybrid nanosensors, and explored their practical applications [Biomaterials Science, 9, 5127-5135 (2021); Journal of Materials Chemistry C, 10, 13734-13740 (2022); Nano Lett., 22, 7714-7723 (2022); The Journal of Physical Chemistry C, 127, 3013-3019 (2023); Nature Communications, 14, 2507 (2023)]. We have found the ways to pattern those nanosensors for our planned experiments [Advanced Science, 9, 2103598, 2022], and investigated the cellular behaviors of neuron cells [Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology, 8, 621777 (2020) and Journal of The Royal Society Interface, 17, 20200331 (2020)]. We have achieved quantitative imaging of magnetic labelled cells in culture using optimized NV relaxation sensing scheme, and managed to monitor the dynamic changes of spin labels using our development (published in a conference proceeding in Quantum Information and Measurement VI 2021). The above results on objectives 1-4 have been published in 15 journal papers as attached. Two Ph.D. graduate students were trained and involved in this project, and one of them successfully pass his PhD defense this August. In addition, one research assistant and one postdoctoral researcher were partially supported by this project.

27202919.label: Major findings and research outcome
27202919.value: The major findings and research outcome from this project are in several aspects: publications, local/international conferences, patents, researchers training and collaborations with academia and beyond. A total of at least 15 published journal articles have been produced from this project. We have explored the deployment of micro/nanodiamond particles in bio-orientated applications. We have found ways to achieve controlled patterning of diamond nanosensors on arbitrary substrates. We have investigated the magnetic imaging of cells using quantum diamond microscope through spin relaxometry. By carrying out this research project, we have established strong collaborations with international partners including both academic and industrial experts. Based on the developed wide-field quantum diamond microscope, we have been working with Prof. Qiang Wei (College of Polymer Science & Engineering, Sichuan University), and Dr. Cheng-han Yu (School of Biomedical Sciences, The University of Hong Kong) to develop diamond molecular tension microscopy for studying cellular traction forces (successfully awarded on RGC-NSFC JRS project). In addition, we have also been working together with local industrial partner, Master Dynamic (a major high-tech company especially in precision diamond manufacturer) to apply quantum sensing for authenticity of diamond jewellery (successfully awarded one ITF project). Except journal papers, a few patents (US, PCT, CN) have also been filed as detailed in report.

27202919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27202919.value: The demonstrated bio-applications in current project remains in an early stage, and we will continue with the direction of applying quantum sensing techniques for investigating the corresponding biomedical applications. In addition, we noticed that the performance of our developed quantum sensing microscope could be improved in terms of spatial and temporal resolution. For instance, it is possible to improve the resolution by introducing some proper super-resolution technique, or some new sensing protocols enhanced with AI technologies.

27202919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27202919.value: Humanity is currently faced with numerous challenges, including life-threatening diseases like cancer and neurodegeneration. To effectively address these diseases, we require advanced biosensing technologies that enable precise, molecular-level measurements for early diagnosis and optimized therapeutics. Our team is working on a cutting-edge project to develop tiny, intelligent sensors that can detect and analyze biological events within cells. These sensors combine stable, glowing particles called nanodiamonds with special molecules that change their magnetic properties in response to factors like temperature or pressure. By creating sensors that can "read" these changes, we aim to visualize the inner workings of cells in high detail, potentially leading to breakthroughs in diagnosing and treating diseases like cancer and neurodegeneration.

27203319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27203319.value: 地下建築的開發費用遠遠高於地上建築。據有關機構統計，地下項目（如地下停車場和地下交通系統）的開發費用一般是地上開發項目的1.3到6倍。事實上，如果在地下建築設施的設計階段沒有充分考慮用戶在後續使用中的健康風險，國家的醫療經濟負擔將會更高。據英國國家醫療服務體系（國民健康服務）給出的數據，英國每年花費約1.4億英鎊於治療建築環境引起的健康疾病。為了保障和提升地下用戶健康，以人為本的設施管理便是關鍵。然而，現有的設施管理文獻大多僅僅停留在地上建築的層面，只有少數是跟地下或密閉環境有關。這些設施管理研究內容或是過時，或是缺少實證研究支持。在極少數有實證型的研究中，它們大部份均局局於某一設施上（例如虛擬窗戶和空間形狀設計），嚴重忽略了現實中各種設施均在互動中影響用戶。這是目前在學術研究和業界實踐的局限性。有鑑於此，本課題致力於通過實証研究和虛擬實驗來建立全面的地下設施管理 - 健康模型，以提升地下用戶的健康水平。

27203319.label: Realisation of objectives
27203319.value: OBJ 1-2 - To identify FM (facilities management) components in underground developments and H (health) indicators of underground users Based on an extensive literature review covering research in the areas of underground space development and human health in the built environment, an FM-H conceptual framework was developed for underground space users. The framework comprised 3 main categories of FM components, namely space management (e.g., connectivity, wayfinding), building services (e.g., thermal comfort, indoor air quality, ventilation, acoustic comfort, visual comfort, etc.) and supporting elements (e.g., greenery, anti-epidemic measures, etc.), and various health indicators, including physical (e.g., building-related symptoms, insomnia, etc.) and psychological health (e.g., burnout, emotional exhaustion, depersonalisation, claustrophobia, etc.). These underground FM components and health indicators were further validated by a series of empirical data. OBJ 3 – To develop an integrated FM-H structural equation model (SEM) To achieve this aim, twelve underground sites and twelve corresponding aboveground sites in Hong Kong were selected for a large-scale questionnaire survey, resulting in 651 survey samples. The survey covered post-occupancy evaluation of health (physical and psychosocial), underground environmental quality (visual, thermal, acoustic comfort, indoor air quality, ventilation), space design, and greenery. Independent-samples T-test, Pearson correlation, multiple regression modelling, and SEM were used to investigate whether significant differences existed between the health of underground and aboveground users, and to develop an underground environment-health model for unveiling the significant associations between underground environment factors and users' health. The SEM results provided empirical evidence that: i) the health of underground users was significantly poorer than that of their aboveground counterparts; ii) underground development users' health was significantly affected by space design, greenery, and environmental quality in terms of thermal comfort, indoor air quality, ventilation, and acoustic comfort, but not visual comfort; and iii) among the various identified factors, space design had the strongest predicting effects on human health. OBJ 4 – To fine-tune the model with a field measurement study To cross-validate the questionnaire survey results, an objective field measurement study was further conducted at six underground sites, including underground subway stations, shopping malls, and offices. The field study echoed the survey findings and further unveiled the relationships between different environmental factors and human health. The underground IEQ factors were measured objectively. By mapping the on-site measurement results with users' physical and psychological health levels, the relationships between different underground environment indicators and health were unveiled. The results indicated that increased levels of temperature, relative humidity, CO2, HCHO, and noise were associated with lower levels of physical and psychosocial health. Conversely, the higher the degrees of greenery and space design, the better the users' physical and psychosocial health. However, no obvious pattern was shown for light level, which echoed the survey results. Both the questionnaire survey and field measurement study results highlighted the importance of distinguishing between underground developments and above-ground ones in various guidelines and standards, especially those related to space management. OBJ 5 – To verify the model using a virtual FM-H experiment (VR) To achieve this objective, a series of Virtual Reality (VR) models were initially developed with different connection designs, wayfinding systems, green density, noise level, etc. Participants were randomly assigned to the various scenes for the experiments. In the experiment, the participants' psychophysiological states, including stress level, mental workload, alertness, and mental fatigue, were measured using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals, salivary cortisol, and a questionnaire survey. A series of tests, including Wilcoxon signed-rank and Kruskal-Wallis tests, were performed. In addition to cross-validating the survey and field measurement studies, the virtual experiment study further unveiled the mechanisms of underground FM and users' health, such as: i) Physical connection to the outside environments had no significant impact on the psychophysiological states of underground space occupants under stress. ii) While visual connection had no significant impact on occupants' mental workload and fatigue, it buffered the increase in their alertness levels under stressful situations. Low alertness levels were associated with creativity and novelty. iii) Green density did not influence the wayfinding performance of underground occupants, regardless of noise levels. iv) In low noise underground spaces, all green density levels mitigated the negative effects of stress on occupants' intuition, attention, and relaxation, with a medium green density level further significantly enhancing relaxation. v) In medium noise underground spaces, all green density levels mitigated the negative effects of stress on occupants' attention and relaxation, although the stress impact on intuition was only mitigated by a medium green density level. OBJ 6 – To develop a set of FM guidelines for enhancing underground users’ health This research provides empirically supported references for better harnessing underground space by considering various health-related underground FM elements, including but not limited to the followings: i) Physical connection to the outside environments had no impact on the psychophysiological state of underground space occupants in stressful situations. ii) Visual connection to the outside environments had no impact on the mental workload or fatigue of underground occupants. Therefore, for underground spaces designed for work requiring a high level of attention (associated with α brainwave), such as clerical and technical work, visual connection does not make a difference in occupants' mental workload and fatigue. iii) Visual connection to the outside environments has a buffering effect on the increase in alertness of underground space occupants under stressful situations. A low level of alertness (indicated by a decrease in β brainwave power and an increase in θ brainwave power) is associated with individuals' creativity and novelty. Therefore, visual connection to the outside environments (e.g., glass ceiling or designs featuring visual outside elements) is recommended for underground spaces designed for artistic and creative purposes, such as art studios, creative media production, museums, and exhibitions. iv) A medium level of green density is crucial for maintaining individuals' intuition in medium-noise underground environments. Intuition plays a vital role in human decision-making processes, particularly in situations where rational analysis may be insufficient, and instinct is required, such as personnel management and leadership roles. In medium-noise underground spaces designed for individuals in these roles, such as management offices in subway stations, a medium level of green density is recommended to prevent a significant reduction in intuition levels during stressful situations. v) A medium level of green density is essential for promoting relaxation in low-noise underground environments. It is becoming increasingly common to find designated art corners in quieter areas of subway stations, where there are fewer passengers. A relaxed state enables individuals to connect emotionally with the art and be more creative in discovering interpretations. In these areas, a medium level of greenery is crucial for enhancing individuals' relaxation levels and fostering creativity. vi) Greenery at all levels of density can maintain individuals' attention levels in underground environments with either low- or medium-noise levels. Attention levels are crucial for ensuring accuracy and precision in complex tasks, such as those carried out by subway system operators and maintenance professionals. While underground spaces designed for these purposes may have varied noise levels, greenery at all levels, even a low level of greenery, is recommended for inclusion in these areas to maintain users' attention levels and prevent them from being reduced by stressful situations.
