27618619.label: Realisation of objectives
27618619.value: A qualitative study to understand strategies that Hong Kong mothers used to maintain breastfeeding and cues to action We conducted a qualitative study following a phenomenological framework to explore the experiences of mothers who had been “successful” in breastfeeding maintenance. Informants were Hong Kong mothers who were aged 18 years or above, had maintained any breastfeeding for at least 4 months, and were able to communicate in Cantonese. Informants should not have stopped breastfeeding for more than 12 months before the interview to reduce recall bias. More details about the inclusion and exclusion criteria can be referred to our publication (Liao et al., 2023). Eligible informants were identified and recruited through advertisements distributed by the Hong Kong Breastfeeding Mothers’ Association, campus bulk emails, and Facebook. Purposive sampling was used to recruit informants with diverse backgrounds including age, educational attainment, income, employment status, number of children, and breastfeeding duration. Semi-structured in-depth interviews were conducted for data collection. The first 18 interviews were conducted face to face between September 2019 and January 2020. Thereafter, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the interviews were suspended to avoid data collection during a period when people were emotionally overwhelming by the pandemic. We resumed data collection in September 2020 to avoid further delay the project progress. However, the interviews were changed to be telephone-based to address participants’ concerns about the pandemic. A total of 30 in-depth interviews were finally completed. The interviews asked participants about the challenges they encountered when breastfeeding was initiated, new challenges as breastfeeding continued and how they overcame those challenges as well as the cues (values, goals and perceived benefits of breastfeeding) that help them to maintain breastfeeding. All interviews were transcribed verbatim and analysed in NVivo 12.0. Development and evaluation of the intervention materials Following the completion of the qualitative study part, we developed and evaluated the intervention materials using the findings from the qualitative interviews. We finally designed 40 short messages of goal-related cues and 40 short messages of norm-related cues as our intervention materials. Specifically, the goal-related cues were specific words (e.g., smart child, good digestion, convenience and saving money) relating to breastfeeding-related values, benefits and goals that were mentioned by the participants in the qualitative study. Each cue was accompanied with a picture showing the desirable goal. The pictures were purchased online from a registered photography provider that maintains around 200 million royalty-free stock photos. The norm-related cues were the adapted narrative statements derived from participants’ statements in the qualitative study about how a mother behave in specific decision context. Each narrative statement was short but addressed a specific challenge experienced by breastfeeding mothers in specific decision context. Each message, either the goal-related cue or the norm-related cue, was designed as a breastfeeding encouragement card for mothers. Each intervention message was modified to adapt to the smartphone format. All messages were evaluated using one-by-one cognitive interviews covering 10 postpartum mothers who are breastfeeding their infant to ensure clarity, comprehensibility and without evoking any feeling of discomfort. Feedbacks from each cognitive interview were reviewed by the research team to make further editions on the intervention materials. We did not encounter specific difficulties in this stage. The randomized control trial (RCT) This was a three-arm randomized control trial. We recruited first-time mothers from the postnatal wards within the first 72 hours following childbirths following a list of inclusion criteria: (i) being ≥18 years, (ii) being Chinese ethnicity and Hong Kong residents, (iii) without any serious medial or obstetric complications, (iv) having a full-term (i.e. gestational age ≥37 weeks) healthy infant with normal birthweight (≥2,500 grams), and (v) expressing an intention to breastfeed post-discharge and stay in Hong Kong for at least six months postpartum. We started our subject recruitment for the RCT in Queen Marry Hospital in July 2021. Eligible subjects were first identified by a nurse through screening the daily ward logbooks and approached by our project assistant to further confirm the subject’s eligibility. Then, the eligible subjects were invited by our research assistant to complete an electronic questionnaire by scanning a QR quote in the postnatal ward for baseline assessment. The initial subject recruitment was smooth with around 10 subjects being successfully recruited every week. However, we observed that the birth rate was lower in the later months of 2021, with only ~5 subjects/week being able to be successfully recruited since November 2021, which was confirmed by our collaborator in QM hospital, possibly because mothers changed to opt for delivering their babies in private hospitals during the COVID-19 pandemic. To accelerate the progress of subject recruitment, we contacted the Department of Obstetric and Gynaecology, PYNEH and seek their approval as one additional subject recruitment site. We obtained IRB approval for recruiting subjects from PYNEH and started subject recruitment in PYNEH in January 2022. However, due to the resurgence of COVID-19 pandemic—the most severe omicron outbreak in Hong Kong occurred in February-May 2022, subject recruitment was suspended during this period. We attempted to recruit subjects from Facebook groups that were run by non-Government organizations during the omicron outbreak but since most of these mothers had participated in various breastfeeding promotion programmes (Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, most studies had moved to be online) and they were not available for our study. By the end of our extended project end date, we were able to recruit a total of 252 eligible participants for the RCT who successfully completed the baseline assessment. The sample size did not meet the original goal. The participants who had completed the baseline assessment were randomized to three groups: the control group who received short standard textual information (general information about breastfeeding), the goal-cueing group who received goal-related cue messages, and the norm-cueing group who received norm-related cue messages. The messages were delivered to each participant within one week after childbirth via WhatsApp, once per day and five days per week. References Liao, Q., Yuan, J., Lok, K. Y. W., Ngu, S. F., Chen, Y., & Lam, W. W. T. (2023). Learning from mothers' success in breastfeeding maintenance: coping strategies and cues to action. Frontiers in Psychology, 14. Retrieved from https://www.frontiersin.org/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1167272

27618619.label: Major findings and research outcome
27618619.value: Our qualitative study revealed the major strategies and cues that helped mothers to maintain breastfeeding. We found that almost all participants had experienced an initial adjustment period. During this period, a social support network, personal perseverance in “trying” breastfeeding and “pumping,” and adjusting expectations for breastfeeding to relieve themselves from the pressure of exclusive breastfeeding were important coping strategies. All participants then entered a stage of getting more attuned when breastfeeding was easier. During this period, seeking support from the online mother groups, deliberating medication that might affects breastfeeding, adjusting to accommodate breastfeeding and lives, and managing breastfeeding in public were the main strategies. For working mothers, despite workplace and employers’ support, proactive adjustment for using the facilities and lactation breaks for breastmilk expression was essential for breastfeeding continuation after returning to work. Throughout the whole journey, positive cues identified from their breastfeeding experiences that helped breastfeeding maintenance included enjoying breastfeeding, breastfeeding as a personal achievement, a healthy and thriving child, positive social feedback, bodily response, the convenience of breastfeeding, and breastfeeding as a motherhood commitment. The RCT found that breastfeeding rates declined over time, with any breastfeeding declining from over 80% by one month postpartum to less than around 40% by six months postpartum. Exclusive breastfeeding rates were low across the three groups, being around 20-30% by one month postpartum and lower than 10% by six months postpartum. Our interventions were not significantly associated with any and exclusive breastfeeding rates and breastfeeding duration without considering the modification effect of perceived self-efficacy in breastfeeding. However, after accounting for the interaction between perceived self-efficacy in breastfeeding and the interventions, we found that goal-related cues significantly increased the duration of any breastfeeding, with the effect being more favourable for participants with low perceived self-efficacy in breastfeeding. In addition, our survival analysis found that higher educational attainment of mothers, intention to breastfeed for at least six months, and a higher score in rational thinking were associated with longer breastfeeding duration.

27618619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27618619.value: Although the small sample size of the RCT may have limited the statistical power to detect the effects of our interventions. Our study indicates that further interventions for promoting breastfeeding maintenance should be tailored by perceived self-efficacy in breastfeeding in mothers. While low perceived self-efficacy in breastfeeding has been consistently shown to be a barrier for breastfeeding initiation and maintenance, our study found that the goal-cueing messages can be an effective intervention to encourage mothers to maintain breastfeeding. Our qualitative study also reveals the dual processes of breastfeeding maintenance—the cognitive process help overcome challenges in breastfeeding while the affective process help cue breastfeeding maintenance, indicating that those goal-related cues should be incorporated into existing psychosocial interventions for promoting breastfeeding maintenance. Furthermore, our study demonstrates a process of developing person-centred interventions through conducting qualitative interviews with the target group, intervention evaluation and testing the effects of interventions. Such process can be applied to other intervention development.

27618619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27618619.value: This study focus on how to design, evaluate and test interventions for promoting breastfeeding maintenance. Specifically, we developed two interventions using results from a qualitative study. The two interventions are messages of breastfeeding goals such as health child, better body shape, and close parent-child relationship, and messages of norms, that is, messages about how other parents cope with breastfeeding-related difficulties. We tested the effects of the two interventions for promoting breastfeeding maintenance. The specific messages were delivered to postpartum women, once per day, five days per week. Our study found that, for mothers with low confidence in successful breastfeeding, messages of breastfeeding goals can significantly increase their breastfeeding duration. However, the messages of norms had no effect on changing breastfeeding rate or breastfeeding duration compared with the control.

27618919.value: “侵入家室：兒童、政權、性别與美國現代保守主義之起源 (1852至1933年)”

27618919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27618919.value: This project will explore how the rise of the modern liberal state in the United States challenged male rule in the family as the state increasingly assumed direct responsibility for the governance of children’s lives in the late-nineteenth and early-twentieth centuries. Since colonial times, the state had governed through the head of the household who was vested with the authority and discretion to control his dependents in what William Blackstone famously dubbed the “empire of the father.” Between 1852 and 1933, as this project will detail, every state in the U.S. introduced laws, including compulsory schooling laws, child-labor regulations and mandatory vaccination requirements, that set minimum standards for all children. Using legislative debates, legal cases, and the records of reformers, the first purpose of this project is to account for the array of state-builders in the late-nineteenth century who found common cause in education, health, and labor campaigns, and championed the “rights of the child” as synonymous with the needs of the state. It will trace the emergence of national reform movements in the early-twentieth century that proposed extending the states’ powers over children to the federal government as well. Despite the labyrinth of state-level laws regulating children’s lives by the 1930s, however, reformers’ efforts to grant the federal government powers over children’s education, health and labor all failed. The second purpose of this project is to explain the limits of the state’s powers over children by tracing the emergence of a gendered, anti-statist politics rooted in defending the sovereignty of the white, male-headed home. The project will explore how resistance to local and state-level laws in the nineteenth century ultimately gave rise to national anti-statist campaigns in the early-twentieth century that used the paternal rights of men as a rallying cry across class and faith lines to galvanize opposition to the expansion of state power. As a whole, the project will make two historiographical interventions by revealing how the expansion of state power and the development of anti-statist politics both grew out of a contest over paternal power. The project’s primary objective is to produce a book proposal and full draft of a book-length monograph that offers the first comprehensive treatment of the changing relationship among children, men and the state in the period under study. The project will also yield two academic articles contributing to the fields of legal, political and, women and gender history. 本研究計劃將探索現代自由主義政府在美國的崛起如何挑戰男性在家庭的主導權。在十九世紀末至二十世紀初，政府負起更多直接管理兒童生活的責任。自殖民時期，在這個威廉·布萊克斯通(William Blackstone)稱為「父親的帝國」的地方，政府一直透過掌有控制受養人權力的一家之主去管治社會。本研究將詳述於1852至1933年間，美國各個州份定立義務教育法、童工管制、疫苗接種規定等法例，為所有兒童設下最低標準的經過。 本研究將參考法例資料庫、法庭個案及改革先驅的紀錄，旨在闡明在十九世紀末不同州份建設者如何在改革教育、公共衛生及勞工運動中爭取共同目標。他們提倡兒童權利，並將其與國家需要視為一體。研究亦會探討在二十世紀初倡議將州政府管理兒童的權力延伸至聯邦政府的國家改革運動的冒起。 儘管在1930年代已有縱橫交錯的州法律去規管兒童生活，改革者卻未能成功擴大聯邦政府管理兒童教育、衛生及勞工的權力。本研究的另一目的是要通過追溯一種源於保衛白人男性的家庭主導權的反國家及性别偏好的政治主張，解釋政府管理兒童的權力限制。研究將探索十九世紀末民眾對地方及全國性法律的反抗如何造就二十世紀初的反國家主義運動。後者利用父權作跨階層及信仰的號召，激起民眾對政府權力擴張的反對。總括而言，本研究將透過指出政府權力擴張及反國家主義均源自父權之爭，改寫兩段歷史。 本研究的主要目標是撰寫一部專著的計劃書及完整草稿。此專著將是首部詳盡研究該時期兒童、男性及政府三者關係轉變的書籍。本計劃亦會出版兩份學術文獻，豐富法律史、政治史、女性史及性別史的研究。

27620419.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27620419.value: The recent philosophical study of the mind and knowledge has grown increasingly interdisciplinary, as philosophers and scientists have together debated the theoretical implications of empirical research on neural processing for fundamental questions concerning the nature of perception and consciousness: What does it mean to perceptually represent objects in the world, and what sorts of objects in the world can we perceive? How can perception be distinguished from other mental processes like imagination and cognition? Do these processes interact, and how might that interaction enhance or diminish our ability to know the world? Finally, what is the nature of consciousness? When and how in the perceptual process do we become conscious of what we see? The significance of these questions extends from the metaphysical and moral, from shaping our understanding of the relation between mind and matter, to determining the ethical status of coma patients and non-human animals. However, because prior philosophical assumptions inevitably constrain our interpretations of scientific findings, this project broadens these assumptions by employing theoretical insights from an underexplored source, namely classical and early modern Indian philosophy. Many central subjects of current philosophical research on perceptual consciousness were anticipated in centuries-old debates between rival traditions of Buddhism, Vedānta, and Nyāya. This project focuses on a diverse set of arguments regarding the existence of non-conceptual perception and reflexive self-awareness. These two issues have been enduring topics of debate in both classical Indian and modern Western philosophies because they stand at the intersection of several deep questions about the relation between mind and world. They remain pertinent to current investigations into the perception/cognition border, perceptual error, the range of possible perceptual contents, and the structure of phenomenal consciousness. While there has been renewed interest in these subjects among modern scholars of Indian philosophies of mind, this scholarship has not yet considered the full breadth and depth of relevant sources, particularly in the early modern tradition of Navya Nyāya. More importantly, there have been few discussions of these sources which combine close textual analysis with contemporary theoretical and empirical research, especially with respect to how Indian philosophers understood the roles of attention and memory in structuring conscious perceptual experience. Through a series of four essays and the preparation of a book proposal, this project reconstructs Indian accounts of non-conceptual perception and self-awareness in naturalistic terms, in order to demonstrate how the unique resources of Indian traditions can address contemporary philosophical and scientific concerns. 最近, 有關心靈和知識的哲學研究愈來愈跨學科化, 因為哲學家和科學家們辯論 了神經處理的實證研究的理論意義, 就著感知和意識本質的根本問題: 感知地表 象世界的對象, 是甚麼意思? 我們又可以感知到甚麼對象? 感知與其他心理過程 諸如想像和認知等, 是如何能夠區分開來的? 這些過程會否相互作用? 這些相互 作用如何提高或削弱我們了解世界的能力? 最後, 意識的本質是甚麼? 在感知的 過程中, 我們何時和如何意識到我們所看見的? 這些問題的重要性, 從形而上和 道德, 從建構我們對心與物關係的理解, 延伸至確定昏迷者以及非人類動物的倫 理地位。 然而, 以前的哲學假定無可避免地限制了我們對科學發現的詮釋。此研究項目透 過參考未曾充分探索的理論資源——古印度和早期現代哲學的理論洞見, 來擴展 這些假定。目前許多關於感知意識的哲學研究的核心課題, 都在持續了數百年之 久的佛教、吠檀多派和正理學派的爭論中有所預示。此研究項目集中探討關於 非概念感知和自我認知的存在的各種論證。這兩個問題一直都是古印度哲學和 現代西方哲學的課題, 因為它們正是許多有關心與物的關係的深入問題的交叉點 。它們仍然跟目前對感知邊界、感知錯亂、可感知內容的範圍以及現象意識的 研究密切相關。 雖然現代的印度哲學學者對這些主題有了新的興趣, 但其學術研究還沒有考慮到 相關材料的廣度和深度, 特別是新正理學派的早期現代傳統。更重要的是, 對這 些材料的討論, 很少會把文本分析跟當代理論和實證研究結合起來, 特別是在印 度哲學家如何理解注意力和記憶在建構有意識的感知經驗的角色這一點上。透 過一系列的四篇論文以及書籍提案的準備, 此研究項目重構印度哲學對非概念感 知和自我認知的說明, 以展示印度哲學的獨特資源, 如何能夠回應當代哲學和科 學的關切。

27620419.label: Realisation of objectives
27620419.value: This project made significant progress in achieving its main objective, namely, to reconstruct Nyāya and Buddhist philosophies of mind in a way that reveals their contributions to debates in the contemporary philosophy of mind. I published three out of the four proposed essays at top-ranked generalist journals in philosophy, which have more visibility within the profession (and hold more weight for tenure purposes) than the specialist journals I had initially targeted. I also showcased my research through several invited lectures and peer-reviewed presentations at international conferences. Over the course of the project, my research focus shifted toward Yogācāra Buddhism and away from Nyāya philosophy of mind, which meant that my published essays were based on topics related to my work on Yogācāra texts. I did manage to conduct some of the promised manuscript research that would be used for my proposed essay on Gaṅgeśa and Nyāya theories of consciousness. I received copies of two Navya Nyāya manuscripts from libraries in Tamil Nadu, and was able to pay a researcher to transliterate the manuscripts into Devanāgarī script. Given the time constraints posed by my upcoming tenure application, I will have to postpone textual analysis of these manuscripts in order to focus on more immediate writing projects. (I was also unable to access two of the manuscripts most relevant to my work on Navya Nyāya -- one on the unintrospectability of non-conceptual perception, and the other a discussion of non-conceptual perception by Bhavānanda (17th cent.)) (I published a 2020 article in Journal of Indian Philosophy that was adjacent to my proposed essay on Gaṅgeśa's theory of consciousness, but was the output of research conducted prior to the grant period.) Another objective of the project was to prepare new translations of Sanskrit philosophical texts. In the course of my research, I've composed extensive translations of passages from both Nyāya and Buddhist texts. One issue I've faced in publishing translations along with my journal articles are the word constraints of generalist philosophy journals. There is no venue for publishing straightforward translation work that would directly benefit my tenure application. Hence, my translations particularly of Yogācāra Buddhist texts have not yet been published. Nonetheless, the translations produced during the grant period -- specifically of works by Vasubandhu, Sthiramati, Dharmakīrti, and Ratnakīrti -- will be vital to my future research on Indian and Buddhist philosophy, and I will have more luxury to work on translation projects should I be awarded tenure. One such project that has followed from my grant research is an annotated translation and commentary on Ratnakīrti's "Citrādvaitaprakāśavāda" titled, "The Phenomenal Unity of Consciousness: Ratnakīrti's 'Theory of Manifold Nondual Manifestation'" (co-authored with Patrick McAllister). We plan to complete our manuscript and secure a book contract in the next year. This text will introduce non-specialist readers to a Yogācāra theory of phenomenal holism, or the view that the phenomenal character of individual conscious states depends upon the total phenomenal experience to which those states belong. This view, which has been recently defended by philosophers like Elijah Chudnoff and Sebastian Watzl, is clearly anticipated by Ratnakīrti and earlier Yogācāra thinkers who argue that conscious awareness is unitary and yet phenomenally manifold. Using the lens of phenomenal holism to reconstruct these arguments will help uncover the views and insights of Yogācāra thinkers vis a vis contemporary analytic debates. As a result of the essays and translation research produced during the grant period, I have revised my idea for a single-authored monograph proposal. Rather than writing a general introduction to classical Indian philosophies of perception and consciousness, I intend to synthesize my research on non-conceptual perception and self-awareness into a monograph on Yogācāra philosophy of mind and the history of its development. This future monograph will build upon the philosophical research and philological analysis undertaken during this grant project, while also requiring additional studies of contemporary philosophical debates and classical Yogācāra texts. The work undertaken during my Early Career Scheme grant has therefore been crucial to my future research trajectory.

27620419.label: Major findings and research outcome
27620419.value: The major findings of my published outputs are explained below: 1. It is a commonly held intuition that the mental states belonging to a subject are conscious only if the subject has an inner awareness of them. Some philosophers further claim that this inner awareness is ubiquitous and reflexive. I make the novel argument that the most plausible case for this further claim can be developed from Sebastian Watzl's account of attention as the structuring of consciousness into an experiential center and periphery. I show how, through a subject's ubiquitous awareness of its active and passive attentional activity, the subject would gain a reflexive inner awareness of its own conscious states as they are being structured into relations of phenomenal priority. I demonstrate further how this attention-based account improves upon other contemporary models of ubiquitous inner awareness. 2. The 7th century Sautrāntika-Yogācāra philosopher Dharmakīrti defended the essentially non-conceptual nature of perception in ways that strikingly anticipate many of the central strategies adopted by contemporary non-conceptualists. Not only that -- Dharmakīrti's account in certain respects improves upon several modern arguments for non-conceptualism. In particular, I show how Dharmakīrti's account coheres with empirical research on the cognitive encapsulation of sensory processing. Moreover, I give a new interpretation of Dharmakīrti as advocating for the essentially iconic nature of perceptual representations. The essay thus concludes that Dharmakīrti's comprehensive account of essentialist non-conceptualism could serve as a theoretical starting-point for the modern non-conceptual content debate that could move it beyond its recent terminological impasse. 3. Despite their evidently idealist claim that "consciousness only" exists, the 5th-6th century Yogācāra philosophers Vasubandhu and Sthiramati actually appear to be illusionists about phenomenal consciousness. I provide the most thorough account in recent scholarship of how Vasubandhu and Sthiramati converge with contemporary illlusionists in taking an unconscious causal basis of cognitive/linguistic processes to be responsible for generating the illusion that mental states have phenomenal appearances through which they represent intentional objects. My as-yet unpublished research findings: 4. The Navya Nyāya philosopher Gaṅgeśa suggests a theory of consciousness according to which the conscious character of perception is tied to the conceptual structure of its intentional content. 5. The 11th-century Yogācāra philosopher Ratnakīrti defends the holistic unity of phenomenal consciousness.

27620419.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
27620419.value: Aside from completing two planned essays on Nyāya theories of perception and consciousness, in future work I will develop my grant research on Yogācāra philosophy of mind. This will take the form of new translations of Yogācāra texts, and a single-authored manuscript on Yogācāra philosophy of mind. This monograph will examine how Yogācāra philosophers understood cognitive mechanisms like memory, attention, and inner speech to be operative in all ordinary conscious perception, and how this claim may be made plausible in light of empirical studies on the role these mechanisms play in structuring conscious experience and the sense of self. The monograph will show how understanding the activity of these cognitive mechanisms further allows us to reframe Yogācāra accounts of non-dual consciousness in naturalistic terms. By reshaping the cognitively modulated activity of memory and attention in structuring experience and its contents, one could thereby reshape one's sense of being a conscious subject that undergoes contentful experience. Clarifying the philosophical and scientific plausibility of non-dual awareness promises to shed light on the notions of phenomenality and subjectivity as such.

27620419.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
27620419.value: This project contributes to the philosophical and scientific study of basic questions concerning the nature of perception and consciousness: specifically, how do we consciously experience what we perceive, and is our perceptual experience shaped by our past knowledge and concepts? Because our theoretical assumptions constrain our interpretations of empirical research on these questions, this project attempts to broaden these assumptions by reconstructing relevant debates in classical Indian and Buddhist philosophy. The significance of these questions concerns our understanding of how conscious minds relate to the external world, as well as the ethical implications of the influence that cognitive biases may have on our perception of and responses to the world. This project shows that classical Indian philosophers offered novel insights into fundamental issues in the philosophy of perception and consciousness, and demonstrates the relevance of cross-cultural approaches for studying the nature of the mind.

27621619.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27621619.value: The composition of early medieval English law codes has not received sufficient scholarly attention. At the centre of this field of study are approximately 55 legal codes, edicts, and treatises written wholly or partly in Old English and produced before the Conquest in 1066. These English-language legal texts survive in 33 manuscripts: most are available to modern audiences only in outdated nineteenth-century editions, and only a fraction has been translated into Modern English. Yet this material from the cradle of English law is rich in its diversity, quantity and language range, and immensely suggestive of both the legal and administrative systems that produced and preserved it, and the variety of compositional impulses that helped shape its final form. With the law codes of the English kings from Æthelberht of Kent (c. 602) to Cnut (c. 1020) as its focus, my project has three broad aims: to examine how the fields of early medieval law and early medieval literature come together in early law-writing; to uncover the intellectual, emotional and social dimensions of law-code production across the earliest period of English history; and to derive from this work new insights into our understanding of what it means to compose law. It is in the early efforts of Anglo-Saxon law-makers that the aesthetic fictions of literary production and the practical and social urgencies of legal frameworks first combine to create what was to become a uniquely English approach to the writing of law. In the development of increasingly sophisticated preambles and legal codes across the Anglo-Saxon period, their authors can be seen to confront and seek solutions to questions which continue to challenge modern framers of statutes and constitutions. How is legal authority to be performed and legitimised? How might legal text exploit or shape understandings of social and cultural identity? For whom were these texts composed? How does the language and rhetoric of written law function to create textual authority and establish a shared expectation of compliance? My focus on the literary and legal aspects of early English law-writing aims to enrich as well as modify current understandings of the legal and social history of legislative composition. It will offer a new way of understanding statutory production: as a phenomenon whose roots can be traced to an early English conspiracy of literature and law. 中世纪前期英格兰法典的撰写，一直是一个未受广泛重视的研究领域。这一领域主要囊括了在1066年诺曼人征服英格兰之前，全部或者部分以古英文写成的约55部法典、法令和专著。这些英文的法律文本保存于33个手稿中。其中绝大部分，现代读者只能找到其19世纪的整理版本，只有一小部分文本被翻译成了现代英文。虽然如此，这些见证英格兰法律起源的素材还是数量可观，涵盖不同的语言，颇具多样性 。它们可以在很大程度上揭示促使其产生和得以维系的法律和行政体系，以及推动其最后成型的文学性因素。 此项目主要研究从肯特国王埃塞尔伯特 （约602年）到克努特大帝（约1020年）统治期间英格兰国王发布的法典。此项目有三个主要的研究目标：第一是审视中世纪早期的法律撰写中，法律和文学这两个领域如何共同发挥作用；第二是揭示英格兰的早期历史中，法典制定所涉及的学术、情感和社会这三个维度；第三是从中汲取新的见解来深入理解法律制定的内涵。 盎格鲁-撒克逊的法律制定者最先将文学中的语言的美感和叙事的技巧同亟需的法律框架相结合，创造了独特的英格兰法律的撰写方法。在不断的完善和细化法律序言和具体法典的过程中，这些法律的制定者面临并解决了诸多问题，这些问题对于现代的法令和宪法的编纂者仍有巨大的借鉴意义。法律的权威该如何展现和确立？法律文本该如何利用或影响社会身份和文化认同？法律语言和其表达方式如何能赋予法律文本权威并且建立起服从法律的共识？ 此项目对早期英格兰法律制定中文学及法律学方面的关注，旨在于丰富和修正目前人们对于法律撰写史的认知，更是提供了一个全新的视角来看待法律的制定。法律的制定不止事关法律领域，更是和文学领域密不可分，它的根由可以追溯至早期英格兰法律制定者对于文本和法律两方面的操控。

28300619.label: Major findings and research outcome
28300619.value: The concentrations of arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), mercury (Hg) lead (Pb), Zinc (Zn) and dichlorodiphenytrichloroethanes (DDTs) in commercial fish feed (Tongwei®) and spent coffee grounds-based biochar (SCGB) were tested. Zinc (90.3 ± 9.07 mg kg-1d.w.) was the highest concentration among all seven pollutants. On the other hand, the concentrations of As, Cd, Pb, Hg and DDTs in commercial fish feed were also low except Zn (303 ± 20.8 mg kg-1) and Cr (58.0 ± 1.00 mg kg-1). In the sorption experiment, the highest removal rates by SCGB were observed at 88.2% for Pb(II) ions and 45.2% for Zn(II) ions. In general, the fish group that received SCGB-based diets exhibited comparable growth performance to the control group (34.0 ± 6.66g (1% SCGB-based diet); 34.2 ± 4.38g (5% SCGB-based diet); and 33.2 ± 3.25g (control)). Zinc (74.3 ± 4.04 mg kg-1) ranked top among As, Cd, Cr, Hg, Pb, Zn and DDTs in the fish fed with a commercial diet (control), aligned with the observation in fish fed by fish feed supplemented with 1% and 5% SCG-biochar (Zn: 30.3±3.21 and 18.3±2.28 mg kg-1). The result indicated that fish fed with SCGB-based diets had significantly lower Zn and DDTs levels in fish meat than the commercial diet counterpart (p<0.05). For the health risk assessment, no potential health risk (As, Cd, Cr, Hg, Pb and DDTs) was posed to humans via consuming fish fed by 1 and 5 % SCGB-based and control feed. In spite of the relatively high concentration of Zn in fish, there was no non-cancer risk of Zn posed on human health risk when bioaccessible fraction was applied in the calculation. In addition, the microbial diversity of the fish gut showed that the significant phylum of bacteria was Proteobacteria, Actinobacteria, Bacteroidetes, Fusobacteria and Firmicutes, respectively. The fish fed with 1% and 5% SCG-biochar fish feed has a higher percentage of Bacteroidetes (3.67% and 5.67%) and Firmicutes (15.91% and 20.23%) than those fish fed with control feed (Bacteroidetes (2.52%) and Firmicutes (12.64%)). Bacteroidetes and Firmicutes may facilitate the restriction of pollutants, namely Zn and DDTs, in the fish gut to fish meat. This study provides fundamental data on using biochar to reduce pollutant uptake in fish.

28300619.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28300619.value: The spent coffee grounds-based biochar (SCGB) contained low concentrations of As, Cd, Cr, Hg, Pb, Zn and DDTs, and the sorption tests indicated that promising removal rates were observed at 88.2% for Pb(II) ions, 45.2% for Zn(II) ions. The fish fed with the SCGB diet also demonstrated a similar growth rate with lower Zn and DDTs concentrations than fish fed with control fed. There were no potential health risks of fish fed with SCGB-based diet based on the As, Cd, Cr, Hg, Pb, Zn, and DDTs levels in fish, especially the bioaccessible portion of metalloid/metals used to estimate the health risk. In addition, a higher % of bactericidal activity was observed in fish fed with the SCGB diet than in the control diet, indicating that SCGB may improve the fish's health. In particular, Bacteroidetes and Firmicutee may facilitate the restriction of pollutants, namely Zn and DDTs in the fish gut to fish meat. The results are encouraging and can be used as fundamental support to further studies such as developing other food waste/food processing waste materials-based biochar for further reduce the uptake of persistent toxic substance in fish.

28300619.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28300619.value: Biochar is a charcoal produced by a process known as pyrolysis, which can be derived from different types of biomass feedstock such as wood, crop wastes, and spent coffee ground (SCG). Using biochar for agricultural and aquacultural applications can provide multiple benefits, such as retaining nutrients and pollutants (heavy metals and organic contaminants) in soil and wastewater. There are limited studies concerning biochar used as a fish feed supplement. This study uses bioresource, SCG, to produce biochar and SCG biochar-supplemented fish feed for lowering the concentration of pollutants (metalloid/metals: arsenic (As), cadmium (Cd), chromium (Cr), mercury (Hg), lead (Pb), zinc (Zn) dichloro-diphenyl-trichloroethanes (DDTs)) in growing freshwater fish (Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)). The potential role of gut microbiota pollutants uptake in fish was also studied. Fish are one of the primary dietary protein sources for humans: The current global consumption, per capita, has reached 20.5 kilogrammes per year. The outcome of this study provides essential information on the production of safe and high-quality freshwater fish fed with SCG-based biochar with fewer pollutants

28600919.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28600919.value: Private tutoring has become a widespread phenomenon particularly in places where high-stakes testing and competition for higher education prevail. In Hong Kong, English language has the highest enrolment rate because of its importance for studies and future career. The rise of English private tutoring (EPT) has transformed students’ language learning experiences both inside and outside school, making their language learning more complex and diverse with potential influences on their agency and learning effectiveness. Despite its worldwide prevalence and significant impact on students’ learning experiences, EPT has remained under-researched. The recent “social turn” in second language (L2) research has called for an investigation in learner agency and started paying attention to its dynamic nature by taking timescales and contexts into account. Learner agency is perceived as an individual’s will and capacity to make choices and act on those choices to facilitate his/her learning. It plays a key role in students’ learning experiences. Agency and context are inter-related. Learners exercise their agency to shape the environment into one that is conducive to their learning, but their agency can also be empowered or constrained by contextual factors. Through the lens of complexity theory, this project aims to understand the agency of learners in a complex educational context where mainstream schooling and EPT coexist. Through narrative inquiry, this study will investigate the experiences of 12 senior secondary students (Form 4 to Form 6) enrolled in EPT for one year. Participants will be selected in three cram schools from a range of backgrounds (e.g., beliefs and behaviours of learning English and reasons for attending EPT courses). Data will be collected through three rounds of individual interview and three pieces of learner reflective writing, supplemented by field observations in the tutorial schools and informal conversations with different stakeholders such as schoolteachers, tutors and parents. The multiple sources of data will be compiled as narratives of learner experiences for analysis. This project will paint a comprehensive picture of language learners’ narrative experiences both inside and outside school and how they exercise their agency in the language learning process. It will add to our understanding of learner agency in current L2 research and frame a new direction for qualitative research on shadow education. In practice, the findings will yield insights into the complex relationship between private tutoring and mainstream schooling and how schoolteachers and tutors can support students to be agentic in regulating their learning. 補習已經成為一種普遍的現象，尤其是在盛行高風險考試和高等教育競爭激烈的地方。在香港，因為英語對學業和未來就業很重要，所以英文科的補習報讀率最高。英文補習的興起改變了學生在校內與校外的語言學習經歷，使他們的語言學習更加複雜多樣，對他們的學習能動性和學習效果產生了潛在的影響。儘管英文補習在世界各地廣泛存在並且對學生的學習經歷有著重大影響，但它仍未得到充分研究。最近在第二語言研究中的「社會轉向」呼籲對學習者能動性進行研究，並開始考慮時序和背景以關注其動態性質。學習者能動性能理解為個人做出選擇並根據這些選擇採取行動以促進其學習的意願和能力。它在學生的學習經歷中起著關鍵作用。能動性和背景是互相關聯的。學習者運用他們的能動性將環境塑造成有利於他們學習的環境，但他們的能動性也可以受到背景因素而強化或約束。透過複雜性理論的視角，本研究旨在了解主流學校教育和英文補習共存的複雜教育環境中學習者的能動性。透過敘事研究，本研究將調查12名高中生（中四至中六）參與英文補習一年的經歷。不同背景（例如學習英語的信念和行為以及參加英文補習課程的原因）的參與者會從三間補習社中被選出。本研究會透過三次個人訪談和三篇學習者反思寫作收集數據，並以補習社的實地考察及與不同持份者（如教師、導師和家長）的非正式對話作補充。多種數據來源會被收集為學習者經歷的敘述以供分析。本研究將全面描繪語言學習者在校內與校外的敘事經歷，以及他們如何在語言學習過程中運用自己的能動性。它會增加我們對當前第二語言研究中學習者能動性的理解，為影子教育的質性研究奠定新的方向。在實踐方面，研究結果會加深對補習與主流教育之間複雜關係的了解，以及學校老師和補習導師如何教導學生有能動性地管理自己的學習。

28600919.label: Realisation of objectives
28600919.value: This project aimed to understand Hong Kong senior secondary students' narrative experiences of English language learning within and across shadow education and mainstream schooling, examine their sense of agency, identify factors that facilitate and inhibit their exercise of agency, and generate practical implications for improving their English learning experiences. All the project objectives have been achieved within the project period, as elaborated below. Objective 1: Understanding Students' Narrative Experiences The first objective aimed to understand 23 senior secondary students’ narrative experiences of English language learning within and across shadow education and mainstream schooling. This was achieved through a year-long longitudinal narrative inquiry, which involved three rounds of individual interviews, two pieces of learner reflective writing, and supplementary artefacts such as language learning materials and interviews with tutors, schoolteachers, and parents. By compiling these multiple sources of data collected over one year into narratives, the study provided rich insights into how the 23 student participants navigated their English learning experiences both in mainstream schooling and EPT courses. The findings revealed the complex and dynamic interplay between these two contexts and highlighted the participants' preference for EPT resources over school-provided materials due to perceived helpfulness and financial investment. What added to the structural complexity was the intermittent suspension of face-to-face teaching in both mainstream and tutorial schools during Covid-19, leading to the transcendence of online (synchronous and asynchronous) and offline learning environments. This dimension has, unexpectedly, enriched the findings regarding the complex nature of students’ private tutoring experience and agency. Objective 2: Examining Students' Sense of Agency The second objective aimed to examine the sense of agency of senior secondary students enrolled in EPT and how they exercise their agency to learn English. By adopting a Complex Dynamic Systems Theory (CDST) perspective, this study successfully illustrated the complex nature of learner agency as it emerged through the participants' experiences. The findings demonstrated how the students exercised their agency both within and outside of EPT courses, with examples such as their enrolment in EPT, engagement with learning materials, adaptation to online learning, and seeking feedback from tutors. Furthermore, the study showcased the spatiality, multidimensionality, and sustainability of the participants' agency, as they continued to engage in self-directed learning even after leaving EPT courses. Objective 3: Identifying Factors Facilitating and Inhibiting Agency The third objective aimed to identify factors that facilitate and inhibit senior secondary students’ exercise of agency in the English learning process. This objective was achieved by examining the contextual, relational, and cultural factors that shaped the participants' experiences. For instance, the study identified the financial investment in EPT courses, the perceived helpfulness of tutors, and the asynchronous nature of online lessons as factors that facilitated the learners' agency. On the other hand, cultural preferences for passive learning among many Asian students and the limited tutor-tutee interaction in asynchronous online EPT lessons were found to inhibit the participants' agency. By considering the complex agency-structure interplay, the study highlighted the importance of understanding the factors shaping learners' agency to better support their English learning experiences. Objective 4: Generating Practical Implications The fourth objective aimed to generate practical implications on how to improve the quality of students’ English learning experiences in the context where mainstream schooling and private tutoring coexist. Based on the findings, several implications can be drawn for educators, policymakers, and stakeholders in both mainstream schooling and shadow education. These include: 1. Recognising the importance of learner agency in language learning and fostering a supportive environment that enables learners to exercise their agency effectively. 2. Encouraging interaction and communication between learners and tutors, regardless of the mode of delivery (online or face-to-face), to enhance the learning experience and facilitate the development of agency. 3. Acknowledging the role of cultural and contextual factors in shaping learners' agency and adapting teaching strategies accordingly to meet the diverse needs of students. 4. Collaborating between mainstream schools and private tutoring institutions to share resources, best practices, and feedback, ensuring a more comprehensive and cohesive approach to English language learning. 5. Encouraging learners to take ownership of their learning and fostering a growth mindset that values the process of learning and self-improvement. By achieving these objectives, this project contributes to the understanding of learner agency in a complex educational context where mainstream schooling and private tutoring coexist and offers valuable insights that can inform practice and policy to better support and enhance students' English learning experiences.

28600919.label: Major findings and research outcome
28600919.value: This project adopted the Complex Dynamic Systems Theory (CDST) to explore the agency of 23 participants in their English learning process through English Private Tutoring (EPT) courses. The findings reveal that participants demonstrated a high degree of agency in their learning experiences. The participants' enrolment in EPT courses shows their agency in seeking supplementary English learning opportunities to achieve personal goals, such as exam preparation or future careers. This finding supports previous research on the role of possible future L2 selves in motivating language learners, especially in high-stakes exam contexts. Throughout the study, participants exercised their agency by engaging with EPT resources, making choices about learning materials, completing assigned tasks selectively, and utilising feedback from tutors. They appeared to value EPT resources more than school-provided materials, possibly due to financial investment in EPT courses and perceived helpfulness of tutors. The transition to online EPT courses during Covid-19 presented both challenges and opportunities for participants' agency. While the online mode saved travel time, it required learners to create conducive learning environments. In response, the participants exercised their agency by adjusting their surroundings to create conducive learning environments and controlling the pace of their learning in asynchronous online lessons, reflecting the multidimensionality of agency in CDST. Despite limited tutor-tutee interaction in asynchronous online EPT lessons, participants found ways to communicate with tutors and influence their learning experiences, demonstrating "structure-agency complementarity". However, this study also highlights cultural preferences for passive learning among many Asian students, which could limit their autonomy and interaction with tutors. Finally, participants exhibited sustainable agency, as they continued to engage in self-directed learning even after leaving EPT courses. For instance, they revised EPT materials, sought feedback from others, and identified areas for improvement. This demonstrates the dynamic and evolving nature of agency in CDST, which requires reflexivity and self-organising interaction of both internal and external factors. Overall, this study emphasises the significant role of agency in English language learning through EPT courses and the complex interplay of contextual, relational, and cultural factors that shape learners' experiences. The findings contribute to the understanding of language learners' agency from a CDST perspective and offer valuable insights for educators and policymakers to support and enhance students' learning experiences both inside and outside the classroom.

28600919.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28600919.value: The findings from this study open up several avenues for further development of the research with respect to understanding the role of learner agency in English language learning in complex educational contexts. As the transition to online learning has become more prevalent, it would be valuable to explore how technology such as generative artificial intelligence (AI) can facilitate or hinder the development of learner agency. Research could examine the effectiveness of various digital tools and platforms in promoting agency and autonomy, as well as the challenges and opportunities that arise from the integration of technology in language learning. In addition, research, educators and policymakers can design interventions and strategies aimed at fostering learner agency within both mainstream schooling and shadow education settings. Examples include creating opportunities for self-directed learning, promoting learner autonomy, and providing guidance on goal-setting and self-assessment, particularly in the online environment. Moreover, this study highlights the importance of a cohesive approach to English language learning across different educational contexts. To facilitate this, future research could explore the potential for collaboration between mainstream schools and private tutoring institutions to share resources, best practices, and feedback, ultimately enhancing the overall quality of learners' English learning experiences.

28600919.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28600919.value: This project explored how senior secondary school students learn English in a complex educational environment, where they attend both mainstream schools and private tutoring. The study specifically focused on understanding the students' own role in their language learning journey. Through a wide range of research instruments including interviews and narratives of students' learning experiences, the project found that the learners actively made choices and took control of their English learning process in both mainstream schooling and private tutoring. The research also identified factors that supported or hindered the students' ability to take charge of their learning, such as the quality of teaching resources, cultural preferences, and the nature of online lessons. The findings are significant because they show the importance of considering students' active role in their language learning experiences and the factors that influence their ability to regulate their learning. The research highlights opportunities for collaboration between mainstream schools and private tutoring institutions to provide a cohesive and supportive learning environment. This project provides insights into how students navigate their English learning journey, offering practical implications for educators, policymakers, and stakeholders to enhance the quality of English language education and better support students in their learning process.

28601819.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28601819.value: Theory of mind refers to the ability to represent one’s own and others’ mental states such as intention, desire, emotion, and belief (Premack & Woodruff, 1978). Individual differences in theory of mind have mostly been attributed to language ability and verbal interaction (Milligan, Astington, & Dack, 2007; Harris, de Rosnay, & Pons, 2005). Hence the existing theory-of-mind training is largely language-based. Building on the embodied notion of cognition, here I propose that simulating another person’s visuospatial experience can also facilitate our representation of that person’s mind. I design two training studies to test this thesis. Study 1 first determines if training in visuospatial perspective-taking improves emotion and mind understandings. I recruit 80 typically-developing 4.5-year-olds and randomly assign them to engage in either altercentric block building or egocentric block building. In the altercentric training I specifically train children to be visuospatial perspective-takers by asking them to imagine how a model figure looks for another person and to build a figure that looks the same as this mental representation. In contrast, children in the egocentric training are asked to reproduce the model figure according to their own visual frame; no visuospatial perspective-taking is involved. I expect that children who receive the altercentric training would improve more than those from the egocentric group on emotion understanding and theory of mind, and that the enhanced emotion and mind understandings can be attributed to the visuospatial perspective-taking training. Study 2 goes on to compare the relative importance of visuospatial perspective-taking and verbal interaction in developing mental state understandings. A total of 120 4.5-year-olds are randomly assigned to participate in either (a) socialised altercentric block building (both visuospatial perspective-taking and verbal interaction), (b) parallel altercentric block building (visuospatial perspective-taking only), or (c) paired dialogic reading (verbal interaction only). The findings would show whether simulating others’ visuospatial experiences in the absence of verbal communication is sufficient to promote emotion and mind understandings, or whether verbal interaction is necessary to support children’s developing ability to represent mind states. Theoretically speaking, the potential causal link between visuospatial perspective-taking and theory of mind may cast new light on what underlies the emergence of mental state understandings. This research also has direct practical implications. If visuospatial perspective-taking training in the form of block building is found effective, we can popularise it to enrich the conventional language-based theory-of-mind training. 是項硏究旨在設計砌磚活動，訓練幼兒的視覺空間換位思考，從而提升其情緒理解及心智理論能力。

28601819.label: Realisation of objectives
28601819.value: 1. To examine preschoolers’ abilities to adopt other’s frame of reference in doing visuospatial judgement (i.e., visuospatial perspective-taking) Preschoolers’ abilities to adopt other’s frame of reference in doing visuospatial judgement appear to transcend cultural boundaries. The participants from the present training studies were typically developing Cantonese-Chinese children aged 4.5 years. This study makes a significant contribution to the field of developmental psychology by introducing much-needed diversity and improving the generalizability of findings in the literature. This is important because the field has traditionally relied heavily on samples from industrialized Western countries (Nielsen at al., 2017). Notably, our research deviates from the usual practice of using only Western samples, therefore providing a more representative and comprehensive view of developmental processes. Moreover, our results indicate that this training paradigm enhanced children’s performance in visuospatial perspective-taking. This gives credence to the notion that individual differences in visuospatial perspective-taking can be influenced by social-environmental input, such as block-building activities, rather than solely determined by developmental processes. 2. To determine whether preschoolers’ visuospatial perspective-taking correlates with their psychological perspective-taking (i.e., emotion understanding and theory of mind) The correlations between visuospatial and psychological perspective-taking were not consistently found across the two studies. In Study 1, visuospatial perspective-taking was found to be associated with their emotion understanding (p = .05) but not theory of mind, whereas in Study 2, visuospatial perspective-taking was found to be associated with their theory of mind (p < .05) but emotion understanding. Based on the assumption that visuospatial and psychological perspective-taking may share common functional similarities (Erle & Funk, 2022; Erle &Topolinski, 2017), there is one reason why these results might have occurred in this study. The first reason is that there may be a connection between the visuospatial and psychological perspective-taking. However, this connection cannot be accurately captured by a simple correlation coefficient because there is another variable that hinders the correlation. Indeed, past studies have emphasized that the relationship between different kinds of perspective-taking may be heavily influenced by the involvement of embodied self-other engagements (Erle & Topolinski, 2015; Erle &Topolinski, 2017). In both studies, children who underwent six weeks of visuospatial-based training showed a significant enhancement in visuospatial perspective-taking and psychological perspective-taking abilities, indicating that the involvement of visuospatial perspective-taking activities results in psychological perspective-taking enhancements. Therefore, the inconsistent correlation between visuospatial and psychological perspective-taking does not indicate that they lack commonalities or are unrelated. Alternatively, it implies that their relationship is multifaceted and could be affected by additional variables. Therefore, further studies are needed to elucidate the underlying mechanism of different kinds of perspective-taking. 3. To examine the extent to which preschoolers’ visuospatial perspective-taking is trainable through block-building activities The initial study found that the visuospatial-based block-building training paradigm influenced children's ability to adopt visuospatial perspectives (F(1, 103) = 15.41, p < .001, ηp2 = 0.12). This result aligns with previous research indicating the connections between visuospatial ability and structured block-building activities (Ramani et al., 2014; Verdine et al., 2014). In the intervention group, children were instructed to use egocentric transformation to simulate their play partner's visual frame from a first-person perspective. They were then tasked to mentally rotate a block figurine from the perspective of their play partner. The training sessions ensured that children continuously manipulated the visuospatial connections between the blocks and the perspective of their play partner in their minds. Consequently, the findings demonstrated that young children who received training in adopting the visual perspectives of others during block-building activities had enhanced visuospatial perspective-taking and emotion understanding compared to the children in the control group. This indicated that the visuospatial-based training led to an enhancement in children's visuospatial perspective-taking ability. 4. To test whether block-building training improves preschoolers’ emotion understanding and theory of mind through enhanced visuospatial perspective-taking Study 1 demonstrated that children trained in the intervention group had better emotion understanding than the children in the trained control group at the post-test (ηp2 = 0.05). In Study 2, improvements were observed in both emotion understanding and theory of mind abilities in the refined visuospatial-based group. The findings of our study challenge the assumption of historical separation between visuospatial perspective-taking and psychological (emotion understanding and theory of mind) perspective-taking and indicate that these two kinds of perspective-taking might co-vary under the same embodied-based training approach. In the training regime, children were directed to inhibit their egocentric perspectives and to engage with another person’s perspectives when imagining how the block figure appeared. This activity displays functional similarities with the process of understanding emotions, in which comprehending another person's feelings requires overcoming one's own current emotional states and amplifying the mental representations of the other person (Davis, 1994). In essence, perspective-taking, whether visuospatial or affective, involves the fundamental characteristics of temporarily suppressing one's own perspective and actively examining another person's viewpoint. 5. To compare the effects of visuospatial perspective-taking versus general verbal interaction training in improving preschoolers’ emotion understanding and theory of mind Study 2 demonstrated that the refined visuospatial-based approach is comparable to the conventional language-based approach’s training effects on emotion understanding and theory-of-mind. The findings revealed that children who engaged in block-building activities, which involved repeatedly manipulating the visuospatial relationships between the blocks and the play partner’s viewpoint in their minds, improved their ability to understand emotions and theory-of-mind. The outcomes from the visuospatial-based training regime are coherent with previous findings and support the view that the foundation of psychological perspective-taking may stem from the process of simulating the visual and spatial experiences of others, as psychological perspective-taking involves mentally placing oneself in the actual position of another individual (Erle & Funk, 2022; Erle & Topolinski, 2015; 2017). The results indicated no significant differences in emotion understanding between the visuospatial-based group and the language-based group after controlling the pre-test scores (F(1, 75) = 0.79, p = .38, ηp2 = 0.010). Further analysis using a paired-sample t-test showed that both the visuospatial-based group (p = .003) and the language-based group (p = .007) significantly improved emotion understanding after the training. Next, a one-way ANOVA showed no significant group differences between the two training groups on children’s theory of mind after controlling the pre-test scores (F(1, 75) = 0.11, p = .75, ηp2 = 0.001). Follow-up analysis with paired-sample t-test revealed that both visuospatial-based (p < .001) and language-based groups (p = .01) have significantly enhanced children’s theory-of-mind after the training. Since the children in both training groups showed significant improvements in their emotion understanding and theory-of-mind abilities, the current results suggested that the visuospatial-based approach is comparable to the conventional language-based approach in training children’s emotion understanding and theory of mind.

28601819.label: Major findings and research outcome
28601819.value: In Study 1, we developed a novel visuospatial-based training paradigm and tested its effectiveness in enhancing emotion understanding and theory-of-mind in 4.5-year-old children by drawing on the embodiment literature. We obtained two main findings. First, children who participated in the embodied visuospatial-based training paradigm for six weeks performed significantly better in visuospatial perspective-taking and emotion understanding post-training than the control children. Second, a two-wave mediation model was found to be significant, including the post-test visuospatial perspective-taking-emotion-understanding relation, with visuospatial perspective-taking and emotion understanding at the pre-test as covariates. These results support a link between visuospatial perspective-taking and psychological perspective-taking in young children and show that embodied-based training has a transfer effect on promoting children’s emotion understanding. Study 2 was conducted to replicate the findings in Study 1, to refine the newly designed visuospatial-based block-building training, and to test the effectiveness of the novel training regimen over traditional language-based training in promoting children’s socio-cognitive development in terms of emotional understanding and theory-of-mind. The findings contributing to the profound comparison of different prompting modalities and training approaches were expected to provide insights into the underlying mechanisms through which language and visuospatial perspective-taking influence social-cognitive abilities. Two primary results were obtained. First, children who underwent the visuospatial-based training for six weeks showed a significant enhancement in visuospatial perspective-taking and social-cognitive abilities. Among the two prompting modalities investigated, the training approach in the block-building group with visual-verbal cues was better for visuospatial perspective-taking and improving children’s emotion understanding and theory-of-mind than a comparable training with verbal cues only. Importantly, the visuospatial-based and language-based approaches were comparable in their effects on children’s emotion understanding and theory-of-mind. The results of this study provide empirical evidence for the potential relationship between visuospatial and psychological perspective-taking, highlighting the feasibility and effectiveness of the embodied-based approach in promoting children’s emotion understanding and theory of mind.

28601819.label: Potential for further development of the research and the proposed course of action
28601819.value: First, cross-cultural research has indicated that culture has a significant influence on the social-cognitive development of children (Fujita et al., 2022; Doan & Wang, 2018). In order to determine the extent to which the present novel training method can be used in the broader population, future studies should involve a diverse sample of children from various cultural backgrounds. Second, given that the enhancements in emotion understanding and theory-of-mind were solely detected immediately after training, it is uncertain whether these effects can be maintained in the long term. Future research ought to broaden the follow-up period to determine if the observed effect of training in the studies is sustained over time after its completion. Third, the absence of a control group in Study 2 hinders the capacity to control the potential confounding variables that could impact the intervention outcomes. Consequently, the study's internal validity may be undermined since it is challenging to conclusively attribute any observed differences in performance or outcomes simply to the differences in training methods. Future research should include a control group to provide a baseline for comparison and improve the validity of the findings on the effectiveness of different training methods.

28601819.label: Layman's Summary ofCompletion Report
28601819.value: When children learn about the world around them, they are required to be good at understanding how others are feeling and thinking. In the first study, 4.5-year-old children from Hong Kong were split into an intervention group and a control group. We found that playing with blocks helped the children better understand others’ emotions, but not directly. When children were figuring out how to see things from different perspectives while playing with blocks, they were practicing how to understand other people's feelings. In the second study, 4.5-year-old children from Hong Kong were split into a block-building group with verbal cues (same as the intervention group in Study 1), a block-building group with visual-verbal cues (the refined block-building training), and a storytelling group. After training, the children in the block-building groups who received visual and verbal feedback performed better in seeing things from different angles, understanding emotions, and understanding thoughts. This block-building training worked just as well as the traditional way of teaching children with stories. So, playing with blocks in a certain way can be a fun and effective way to help young children get better at reading emotions and thoughts and relating them to behaviour.

28602319.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28602319.value: Psychological stress-induced mental health problems such as depression have a strong negative impact on socio-economic burdens. Yet, not everyone who is under high stress would develop psychological disorders. Those who are more resistant to the development of psychological disorders are known as resilient people. Psychological resilience (hereafter named as resilience) is defined as the ability to rebound from adverse events. Cultivation of resilience is, therefore, believed to prevent the development of psychological disorders. There are increasing numbers of resilience research that attempt to prove the potential beneficial effect of resilience on the mental well-being in different populations. Despite the obvious potential, implementation of resilience training and monitoring programs remains difficult, which is mainly due to the absence of reliable and objective methodology to assess resilience. To date, subjective reports remain the most commonly used tool to assess resilience in research. Although this approach has value, self-report bias is inevitable with this method. An alternative is the application of standardized and validated biomarkers in describing and predicting resilience. These measures are less prone to subject manipulation; thus, improvement of assessment accuracy can be achieved. For instance, baseline heart rate variability (HRV), cardiovascular recovery, cortisol to dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) ratio and cytokine responses measured after stress, have been suggested to be reliable biomarkers in predicting resilience. Although the two methods have complementarity, the combination of these methods is rarely applied to explain and predict resilience. This proposed study aims to evaluate the predictive power of the combination of the above biomarkers together with self-report measures in predicting resilience in healthy adults. Perceived stress, subjective resilience level, resilience components and mental health status will be assessed using self-reported questionnaires on the experiment day, followed by HRV assessment and saliva sampling at baseline. Participants will then go through a laboratory stress task with their heart rate being monitored throughout the task. Saliva sampling will be performed again immediately, and at 5, 10 and 20 minutes after the task for the measurement of cortisol, DHEA and cytokines levels. The association of the level of subjective resilience with putative biomarkers of resilience and self-reported resilience components will be examined. Subjects will be followed up for a year. Their mental health status, perceived stress and self-reported resilience level will be assessed again at the 3rd, 6th, 9th and 12th month after the experiment. Results from this study will provide insight into the development of comprehensive assessments of resilience. 一直以來，因心理壓力引起的抑鬱等心理健康問題對社會經濟負擔帶來很強的負面影響。然而，並非每個處於高壓力之下的人都會發展出心理障礙。那些較少機會發展出心理障礙的人被稱為有抗逆力的人。 心理抗逆力（以下稱為抗逆力）被定義為能從嚴重事件中反彈的能力。因此，人們認為培養抗逆力可以預防心理障礙的發展。越來越多研究試圖在不同的人群中證明抗逆力對心理健康有潛在益處。儘管有明顯的潛力，實施抗逆力訓練和監測訓練方案的成效仍然很困難，這主要是由於沒有可靠和客觀的方法來評估抗逆力。目前，自我評估報告仍然是量度抗逆力的最常用的研究工具。雖然這種方法具有價值，但這種方法難免存在偏見。另一種方法是利用標準化和已被驗證的生物標誌物來描述和預測抗逆力。這些標誌物不容易受到主觀因素影響 ; 因此，可以提高評估的準確性。舉例來說，過往的研究指出基線的心率變異性（Heartrate variability, HRV），心血管恢復，受壓後的皮質醇與脫氫表雄酮（DHEA）比值和細胞因子反應等，可作為預測抗逆力的可靠生物標誌物。雖然自我評估報告和生物標誌物在預測抗逆力中具有互補性，但這些方法很少被結合起來用於評核和預測抗逆力的研究上。 這項擬議的研究旨在評估結合生物標誌物和自我評估報告在預測一般成年人的抗逆力的準確性。在實驗當天，研究員會以問卷方式評估受試者的感知壓力，主觀抗逆力水平，抗逆力的構成要素和心理健康狀況，然後在基線進行HRV評估和唾液採樣。受試者接著會進行一項壓力任務，在整個過程中他們的心率會被監測。壓力任務完成後將立即進行第二次唾液取樣，並在任務後第5,10和20分鐘後再次取樣。唾液樣本將用作測量皮質醇，DHEA和細胞因子的水平。自我評估報告的結果和生物標誌物水平之間的關聯性將會被分析。受試者需接受為期一年的追縱研究。他們的心理健康狀況，感知壓力和主觀抗逆力水平將會在實驗後的第3個月，第6個月，第9個月和第12個月以問卷方式再次被評估。這項研究的結果將有助建立全面綜合化評估抗逆力的方法。
